I thought that was a nice touch.Be aware that they actually offer you the choice of still, sparkling or tap, but our server conveniently left it off the options when he asked and only the chef asked us if we wanted tap.The appetizer was a type of mousse quinoa salad, and it was very nicely done. There were crunchy pieces mixed within and the texture of the mousse paired quite beautifully with it.The next dish was the lobster which was the highlight of the night. The lobster had a nice, almost tomato like sauce on top of it and was paired with a lobster emulsion and potatoes underneath. This dish was beautifully made, though I thought the potatoes were a bit too salted in certain parts. Still, a top notch dish.The dish after was the truffles and it was alright. It came with brioche covered in truffle oil and that was a bit too overpowering. On the dish the egg and the spices end up covering up a lot of the taste of the truffle which was quite mild in comparison. It had the nice nutty and mushroom taste of a truffle but lacked that smell so characteristic of a good truffle.The next dish was halibut and fennel and that was probably the most disappointing dish of the night. The halibut tasted rather plain, although it was cooked well and had a nice crunchy texture at the bottom, with a taste reminiscent of a pecan pie. The fennel was alright, it was covered with a sauce that tasted like one of those ones from the Japanese curry boxes.The final main course was the duck, and while it was relatively simple, it was beautifully executed and tasted excellent. The textures were on point, the seasoning complimented the dish and really brought out the flavors of the duck, overall really well made.Things wrapped up with a dulce de leche dessert, which was delicious albeit very rich and sweet given the amount of dulce de leche. It had a nice crunchy piece on top, then a nice whipped cream followed by the dulce de leche and hazelnut spread and ice cream on the side. I enjoyed it though it can be very sweet so if you like dulce de leche and Nutella you'll probably love this.Overall a great meal, but outside of the lobster nothing really blew me away.

Mighty Bowl's on my regular weekday lunch rotation in Midtown. It's a bowl fast-casual restaurant that specializes in Asian-fusion flavors. I've only picked from their Classic bowls, but you can also build your own (base, protein, veggies, sauce). Personal favoritesSeoul - grilled steak, scallions, Chinese broccoli, mushrooms, and 5 spice sauce Shanghai - grilled steak, kimchi, scallions, bonito, bean sprouts, cucumber salad, and gochujang sauce. I always order extras such as poached egg, mangos, kimchi, and extra proteinIf you go for weekday lunch, you can also opt for garlic fried rice (+$1) as your base

Super cute Italian restaurant in the UES! I came here with family but it would be a great date spot as well. Our waiter was really friendly and we didn't feel rushed at all. Food was delicious!! We ordered a few appetizers and I got the pasta with eggplant which I really enjoyed. Highly suggest the key lime pie for dessert which tasted amazing. Definitely on the pricier side but the food and ambiance are definitely worth it for a special occasion!

Nice concept! Ramen and beer! They have a really decent selection of beer on tap as well as stuff in the fridge. You can just walk up and grab something you like and they give you a glass no corkage fee. They also have wine. I had the classic ramen and really liked it. Very flavorful and good portion. I like that you can also add veggies or other stuff if you want. The Mac and cheese is really good also. Cheesy, gooey, nice flavors and comes piping hot. The place is spacious and bright, service was great. Will come again.

Title: A Decade of Satisfaction at La Mela

My unwavering loyalty to La Mela as my top Italian dining destination in NYC spans over a decade, a testament to its consistent gastronomic excellence in a city brimming with choices. La Mela's allure is twofold: the authenticity of its scrumptious offerings and the generous portions that make it perfect for dining duos, especially when indulging in their family-style three-course feast.

From the outset, the ambience transports you to a classic Italian eatery reminiscent of the '50s and '60s, complete with a warm welcome from the friendly waitstaff. It's charmingly retro with a touch of that old-school, mobster-film vibe.

The culinary journey commences with a no-frills, yet sublime caprese salad—thick slices of mozzarella and fresh tomatoes, accented with basil, olive oil, salt, and pepper. It's pure, unadulterated simplicity at its best.

But it's the hot antipasto that truly captivates. A medley of asparagus, peppers, and onions marinate in a symphony of savory juices, accompanied by divine stuffed mushrooms. The showstopper, though, is their innovative mozzarella dish: pasta transformed into a cheesy delight that's oven-baked rather than fried—a truly unique and mouthwatering twist.

The feast culminates with a trio of pasta perfection. The straightforward yet delectable rigatoni with red sauce, gnocchi al Sorrentina with succulent baked mozzarella, and the flavorful tortellini in a creamy pink sauce with peas—each dish competes for your affection while harmonizing beautifully together.

La Mela is a place where bread isn't merely a side; it's an integral partner, sopping up the myriad of delectable flavors and leaving no room for anything but contented sighs. This establishment doesn't just serve food, it creates an experience—a must-visit for anyone seeking the heart and soul of Italian cuisine in the heart of New York City. Bon appétit!

Pretty good rice roll place and fairy reasonable price since everything in Chinatown has been increasing quite steadily. The service is quick too! I got congee and pork rice roll wrap and  they were perfect for a cold rainy day. I can see why they get incredibly busy by the locals and tourists during all times of the day. So be prepared to wait a while if it's already full here, worst case order take away!Only issue they are cash only...

Title: A Special Birthday Dinner to Remember

My boyfriend's birthday celebration took us to a charming spot within The Kitano Hotel, where we were immediately taken by the cultural ambiance as waitresses in elegant kimonos greeted us. Despite not booking the private room, the layout offered secluded sections that provided a sense of intimacy.

The culinary journey began with the Sushi okonomi kaiseki and the special kaiseki menus, each dish arriving as a visual masterpiece coupled with exquisite flavors. The selection included an impressive sake range that complemented our meal beautifully. From the small appetizers to the generous sushi offerings and succulent wagyu beef, each bite was a testament to the restaurant's culinary excellence.

Dessert was an adventure in itself, featuring black sesame ice cream, coffee jello with cream, and mochi. The unexpected touch of a complimentary chocolate mousse cake, along with a keepsake handkerchief from the hotel, made the birthday dinner all the more memorable.

In summary, the evening was an outstanding experience, providing exceptional food and service that justified the expense for such a special occasion.

On a stormy Manhattan night, my friends and I found warm refuge in a favorite NYC eatery. The hostess greeted us with prompt seating as we awaited our party, setting the stage for what was to become an unforgettable dining experience. The table consensus was unanimous: the pasta entrees, complemented by a fine selection of wines and sumptuous desserts, were culinary triumphs. I indulged in the "Sinfonia di Paste" - a trio of daily pasta preparations at $25.95 - and as always, it did not disappoint. Each dish was cooked to perfection, both delectable and generous in portion. An exceptional meal that easily keeps this spot high on my list of must-visit restaurants.

A friend of mine wanted to give this place a try and being a love of all things chicken nuggets and sandwiches, it didn't take much for me to get here.For those that like choices, you'll have an abundance of different sauce options or specialties concoctions to dip or lather onto your nuggets or chicken sandwiches. We went the 6 piece 'reg nugs' and a spicy chicken sandwich.For $9 for 6 pieces, the value seems a bit off. The nuggets aren't massive, two small bites finishes one nugget. Why I didn't enjoy it as much was because the batter overpowered the chicken. Most of the flavor was flour and the chicken wasn't moist. Luckily the sauces save it, especially the truffle mayo. The spicy chicken sandwich was around $10, and the patty size was pretty big. The spice was light and barely there. Chicken was cooked a bit better here, and the buffalo and truffle mayo took it to another level. Overall, if you are feeling chicken nuggets or a sandwich and in the area, it'll check the box. In an era where the chicken sandwich game is way strong, I think there's some room for improvement here.

Title: Delightful Eats with a Side of Jazz – Minor Service Hiccups

I recently dined at a charming spot that doubles as a haven for live jazz enthusiasts and those with an appetite for dancing. The ambiance truly comes alive with the rhythmic beats and energetic performances, making it a unique dinner experience.

The culinary offerings are impressive, particularly the fish dishes which were remarkable enough to leave me eager to return for their meat selections. For those with a sweet tooth, the pre-fixe 3-course meal is a steal at $49, especially when capped off with a delectable dessert.

However, my evening hit a sour note due to a misunderstanding with the staff regarding the cover charge for the live music sessions. Initially told by the manager that my $20 admission covered both sessions, I was later asked by a waiter to pay an additional fee during the intermission. Although the issue was eventually resolved by the manager, allowing me to stay for the second set, the situation was uncomfortable and could have been handled with more grace.

From a cost perspective, the $80 spent (including tax and tip) felt steep for a single hour of entertainment, especially given the minimum spend requirement on food and drinks. On my first visit, the female bartenders were welcoming, contrasting with the less hospitable male servers on this occasion. I left feeling undervalued as a customer, especially on a quiet Wednesday night.

In summary, while the food and music are worth the applause, the service missteps and pressure to spend more cast a shadow on what could have been a flawless evening. Would I recommend it? If you're there for the band and the bites, absolutely – just be clear on the charges upfront to avoid any discord.

This gem of a dive-in ramen spot continues to impress with its swift service and generous portions. The prices are a steal for the hearty bowls of goodness you receive. My go-to miso ramen has been consistently stellar across visits—a reliable choice for a satisfying meal. Highly recommend for any ramen enthusiast looking for quality without breaking the bank.

Ravioli and spaghetti is what we ordered while at II Buco. This little Italian restaurant was seriously packed to the brim. We couldn't get a table so we decided to have our dinner on the bar. It's a little bit on the tighter side but it still was pretty comfortable. Our bartender and server was pretty nice and recommended some things to us. We also drank a few glasses of wine with our meal. Overall the spaghetti to me was a tad bit saltier than I would want. But hey maybe this is the style, I'm not too sure. My favorite thing was the ravioli which tasted pretty rich as well but I liked how the flavor blended well together for this dish. We also ordered this cheese toast which is not melted but I assumed it would be. People were ordering this dish left and right so we did too. But it wasn't something that I thought was good. The salad was typical as well, overall the experience was just alright. I did enjoy having the bartender ask us if we needed refills on our drinks and was pretty attentive. But food wise I would say it's just an average Italian restaurant.

Title: A Neighborhood Gem That's Worth Every Calorie

Living within walking distance of Sylvia's is both a blessing for my taste buds and a playful curse on my waistline. From the moment I sat down, the warmth of the staff made me feel right at home. Kicking off the meal, the cornbread set a high standard, arriving as a delightful prelude to the main act.

The star of the show was undoubtedly the chicken and waffles. The chicken's seasoning was a masterclass in flavor, hitting all the right notes, while the waffles provided a comforting, sweet canvas for the savory masterpiece. It's crystal clear why Sylvia's has become an essential thread in Harlem's culinary fabric.

Not only was the food memorable, but the atmosphere was equally inviting. As I said to the waitress—and I meant every word—"it's my first time here, but definitely won't be my last!" Sylvia's, you've earned a loyal patron.

Title: Affordable Eats in Midtown with a Side of Inconsistency

Nestled in the bustling heart of midtown, this restaurant offers a surprisingly affordable culinary escape from the urban rush. My recent visit, however, was a tale of two experiences. Upon arrival, my friend and I were met with a noticeable lack of hospitality; no greetings, no guidance – a silent treatment from staff members more engaged in conversation with each other than with customers. It was a self-service venture to find a seat.

Once settled, the majority of the staff continued to seem indifferent, but a shining exception was a waitress with short blonde hair whose attentiveness salvaged our dining experience. She checked on us mid-meal and ensured our comfort throughout.

As for the menu, it's quite the delight. The mushroom malatang I sampled was hearty and satisfying, brimming with an assortment of fresh vegetables like lotus root and broccoli that made for a comforting meal on a chilly evening. The heat enthusiasts will revel in their "highest spicy level" - it's a legitimate scorcher that lives up to its fiery promise.

Value is where this spot truly shines. With lunch specials priced at $10.10 from Monday to Friday and generously portioned offerings like my $12.95 mushroom malatang, your wallet will leave as full and content as your stomach.

In summary, if you can navigate past the initial indifference and seek out the kind-hearted servers, you'll find this spot to be a gem for your taste buds and budget alike. Just remember to bring your spice tolerance and patience.

As someone initially skeptical about the wonders of vegan fare, my dining experience at by CHLOE was a delightful revelation. The taco quinoa salad, a crowd favorite, did not disappoint. Its generous portions and a vibrant mix of flavors captured my palate and lingered in my memory long after my visit to New York – a true testament to its culinary prowess. While the prices lean towards the higher end, the quality and taste justify the expenditure. Additionally, the inventive vegan mac & cheese, with its creamy sweet potato sauce and shiitake "bacon," was a standout. It's a genuine wish of mine to see by CHLOE expand to the SF Bay Area, where it would, no doubt, be a resounding success.

Thursday night I finally went out to dinner & I'm so glad I did! I have wanted to try this place for a while and my expectations were high! For starters we ordered the rock shrimp and tuna tartare spring rolls. The rock shrimp was spicy (but delicious) and the tuna was good! I ordered the lamb chops (medium rare) and my friend ordered the sea bass. Both were delicious. You have to get a side since none of the dishes come with anything - we tried the Asian green stir fry. It was good, cooked perfectly and pine nuts were a nice touch!We also tried 2 desserts, the chocolate pistachio cremoso (best I have had in a very long time!!!) sweet, crunchy, little salty- this was too good! We also ordered the three treasures! This is their take on sticky toffee pudding with toasted rice ice cream- so good!

This is my favorite neighborhood UES Italian restaurant for all occasions. A hidden gem located between 2nd and 3rd (closer to 3rd) on 84th st. Great service and food. Cute inside atmosphere. I recommend the Penne Bosco e Mare ($19.95).

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Emmy Squared

From the moment we walked into Emmy Squared on a bustling Sunday evening, I knew we were in for a treat. Despite not having reservations, we snagged a high top and watched as the place quickly filled up—an obvious testament to its popularity.

Our taste buds were tantalized with the Colony and Margherita pizzas, each boasting its own unique allure. The Margherita was a standout—adorned with creamy burrata and fresh basil, it elevated the pizza experience to new heights. The tomato sauce was a flavor masterpiece, striking the perfect balance between sweetness and salinity.

The Colony wasn't far behind; the combination of pepperoni and hot honey delivered a delightful fusion of sweet and spicy notes that danced on the palate. The pepperoni itself was notably succulent, its thickness capturing just the right amount of indulgent greasiness.

However, the real hero of the meal was the crust. I've met few grandma crusts that excite me, but Emmy Squared has rewritten the script. Their crust offers a divine crunch around the edges, while maintaining a fluffy and satisfyingly dense interior.

Emmy Squared isn't just recommended, it's a must-visit for any pizza aficionado. Prepare to be amazed.

My partner and I stayed at a nearby hotel, and we were looking for a restaurant that was still open and decent. We stumbled by Donburiya and decided "why not?"It's not a big restaurant, but it does have the traditional Japanese restaurant vibe to it. The service is straight business. There is no playing around, which isn't bad because it gets the job done efficiently. The food is quite yummy, but the portions are a little small considering the prices for them. Everything was going good until we decided to get the bill and leave. As we were checking the receipt over, we saw the chef take a spoonful of food from a dish and eat it, and then he put the plate out onto the platform for one of the waiters to take it to the table. I'm not sure if the spoon was clean or not, but it was really unprofessional. I'm hoping he didn't do the same to our dishes.

This place is pretty small and if you plan to sit you'll be smashed up next to strangers. Besides that they have a semi open kitchen where you can see them making noodles. The dumplings are so good and served with this savory sauce. The Peking duck buns are the best things on the menu. The bread part is light and fluffy and the duck is to tender and flavorful. The scallion pancakes with beef does not taste as good as regular scallion pancakes but it's worth a try. The waiters were friendly and knowledgeable but too pushy. I'd love to come back to try more of the menu.

The thing that shines at this place is the service. Who says that New Yorkers are rude?! I think this place proves that it's actually the opposite. They obviously care about the customer. I got the trio sampler which had half a sandwich of the lobster roll, crab roll, and shrimp roll. I also ordered the lobster bisque with the meal. I can say that EVERYTHING tasted wonderful! Now, my only gripe is with the obvious that this is a pricey meal for what you actually get. All lobster rolls in general are super expensive, I know this. However, I can say that with all the lobster rolls I've had in my life, this was the smallest I've had (I'm judging this based off of my friend's full lobster roll size). I get that this establishment serves lobster (which is already expensive) and that they're operating in one of the most expensive cities in the world. However, I've had many lobster rolls all over the city and this one is still the smallest portion at the highest price. Again, this is only a small gripe. I would come back mainly for the convenience and the service.

I recently visited a chain restaurant close to my downtown office and had a pleasantly efficient experience through Ritual. I opted for a customized Thai Chicken Crunch Salad during a non-busy hour and was delighted by the prompt service upon arrival.

My tweaks included roasted turkey, shaved parmesan, and substituting kale for the standard romaine. The proteins were diced finely and, despite being indistinguishable, they generously peppered each forkful of fresh veggies. The well-mixed, slightly spicy dressing perfectly complemented the ingredients, enhancing the salad's overall flavor.

I thoroughly enjoyed this delightful mix and am looking forward to exploring more of their offerings in the future.

I went with the wasabi and super spicy Xiao Long Bao. Both were equally terrible. I thought wasabi one will be a bit weird. But the wasabi flavor was so strong I could not eat more than two. The strength with which wasabi burned my nose, I thought it was vaporize from my face. Unless you are wasabi fanatic, avoid it. Generally shops add chili oil to dumpling and call it spicy dumpling. But their super spicy dumpling is not that. They added some super spicy chili powder to make those dumplings. I eat a lot of hot and spicy food. Even I could not eat more that two of those dumplings. So it's best to avoid this as well. The dumpling skin was thin and there was enough soup in it. If I went for Kung Fu or crab it would have been ok. Finally their chocolate dumpling was really good. It was a dumpling filled with banana and Nutella.

This was an amazing experience. My friend wanted to bring me here to try them out before they blow up. I can definitely see this place becoming a spot where you have to reserve quite far in advance so definitely try then out soon. I initially walked right past the restaurant because it is so inconspicuous and from the outside, resembles the windows into one's home. They have a very modest dining area with only, maybe 30 seats and very few of those are actual tables. Although, the real treat is sitting at the chef's counter, where you're able to see, firsthand, how each dish is intricately plated and you can awe at the well-oiled machine that is the kitchen staff. It really makes you appreciate each dish that is presented before you.They offer a five-course tasting menu in the dining room and an extended version at the chef's counter. We were happily seated at the chef's counter and had front row seats. As of now, they are BYOB but there are no short supply of stores in the area that will have just what you're looking for, when it comes to a bottle of vino that will pair well with your meal. I opted for a bottle of Malbec which was an excellent choice.We started off with an amuse-bouche, a perfect one-bite of the day of butternut squash, kohlrabi, crispy lentil comes together in one fantastic taste. I loved the flavour.Next, was the fermented pineapple which became a completely different texture! Almost tasted like a pineapple gelatin. Sooo good! Then, their mussels were great. I want a stick of that nuoc cham butter to keep in my refrigerator.The spice raw beef was wonderful. Espelette was so tasty and the lumpfish roe added a salty element that was favorable to the dish.The next dish had such a boastful flavour of corn. The textures made the dish.The extra dish that we added to the courses had Uni. Periodddtt!The sweetbreads dish was different than I've ever had. I loved the sour passion fruit puree and the cauliflower puree because they brought a great balance.The Eastside breakfast was the bomb! Green eggs and NOT ham! Sooo good. The seasoned egg yolk and everything bagel seasoning are to die for. On point course.The hake was wonderful. The salty umami from the nori and the pumpkin seed brought the dish together.The flat iron dish we received was soooo good! Burnt onion and lingonberry gave conflicting, yet complimentary flavours to the meal. Amazeballs!Finally, the rice ice-cream dish was so good with its raspberry "snow" and mango lassi flavour. I loved this. Perfect ending. The supporting staff was awesome! I wish I remembered everyone's names but we shared a bottle of red and by the end of dinner, I was three sheets to the wind. I was in stitches from the beginning to the end of our meal. Everything and everyone was phenomenal. I've had the pleasure of eating food prepared by chefs, Nahid Ahmed and Arjuna Bull, many years ago so I could only imagine what they had in store this night and I was not disappointed. They have an imaginative whimsy when it comes to their food concepts and plating. It's amazing to watch and satisfying to eat. Make a reservation ASAP!

From the moment I stepped into Thai Villa, I was captivated by its stunning interior, which set the stage for a memorable dining experience. The ambiance radiated warmth and authenticity, inviting guests into a serene culinary oasis. 

Visiting on the weekend, I found the restaurant brimming with life—a testament to its popularity. It's wise to leverage Yelp's waitlist feature to secure a spot in advance, given its bustling nature.

The highlight of my meal was the Massaman curry. Having sampled this dish across Queens and even in Thailand, I can confidently say that Thai Villa's rendition is unparalleled. The complexity of flavors and perfectly tender meat left a lasting impression.

Not to be overshadowed, the Khao Soy with chicken thigh was another standout, combining succulent poultry with a rich, aromatic broth—truly terrific.

Thai Villa has etched a stellar mark on my culinary map, with dishes that not only satisfy the palate but also the soul.

Title: A Celiac-Friendly Homecoming Feast at Zia Maria – Chelsea, NY

My much-anticipated return to New York City from the sun-soaked climes of California brought me to the welcoming doors of Zia Maria in the vibrant Chelsea neighborhood. Dining out can be a Russian roulette for someone with Celiac, longing for the nostalgic indulgence of the city's myriad cuisines, but Zia Maria’s gluten-free options assured a safe and delicious reunion with my old stomping ground. 

The star of the evening was unquestionably the gluten-free Margherita pizza – a fabulous pie that harmonized the classic simplicity of fresh mozzarella, tomatoes, and basil with the culinary mastery of a perfectly crispy crust. Amidst the spacious and comfortable ambiance that Zia Maria offers, this pizza was a slice of heaven for a gluten-intolerant patron.

What’s more, the reasonable prices provided a welcome respite from the often exorbitant cost of dining out in the Big Apple. As we gathered around the table, each of us – from the gluten-free to the gluten-full – savored our meal with evident pleasure. Zia Maria served as an impeccable kickoff to what promises to be a splendid New York vacation.

Tucked away on the west side is a charming tapas gem that's certainly worth a visit. With limited seating, it's wise to book ahead to secure a spot. The menu delights with mouth-watering options; the gambas al ajillo and patatas bravas didn't disappoint, while the torrijas offered a sweet contrast. However, the star of the show was the bocata de lomo adobado – a must-try. Pair your meal with their refreshing frozen watermelon tequila drink for a perfect accompaniment. Service was prompt, enhancing the overall positive atmosphere. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Last Saturday night, my visit to this hidden gem in NYC proved to be a delightful culinary escapade. With space at a premium in the city, the entranceway to the restaurant was both easy to overlook and charmingly unexpected. Despite arriving ahead of our reservation time, the hostess graciously accommodated us at the bar until our full party arrived.

Opting to dine family style—befitting the Italian ambiance—we ordered an array of appetizers, pastas, and sides to share. Each dish was delectably prepared, with the Foie Tortellini, Beef Ragu Pasta, and Crispy Potatoes standing out as particularly memorable. A pro tip for future diners: don't hesitate to dip your bread into the rich, savory broth of the tortellini for an added treat. All in all, the food was exceptional—a sentiment echoed by the entire group.

Morimoto omakase* 150. per person "chef's choice" a multi course tasting menu designed to allow you to experience the essence of morimoto's cuisine. we recommend ordering omakase for your entire table.* sommelier selected wine and sake pairing  85. per personfirst coursetoro tartaresecond courseseasonal sashimithird coursesashimi saladfourth coursechawanmushififth course5 pieces chefs choice seasonal nigirifresh wasabi 12.intermezzoyuzu sherbetsixth coursefresh codseventh courseamerican wagyu strip steakjapanese A5 40. per 2ozeighth courseyuzu, black sesame & beni imohanabi dama 10seasonal wagashiDINNER. SERVICE AND PRESENTATION OF ALL ABOVE WERE OUTSTANDING. TWO BOTTLES OF HIJINJU SAKE .. OUTRAGEOUSLY DELICIOUS. WE ADDED ALL THE UPGRADES AND IT WAS WELL WOTH IT ... BEAUTIFUL RESTAURANT!!!

my friends and I came here with great expectations because of how hype the reviews are and so many people (even our own friends) who rave about it. the place does feels very authentic and was convincing. it was one hot summer night and I don't think their AC works but we didn't mind. the waiter was very friendly and service was awesome!we were told that the spicy miso is good so we ordered that. the broth looks intimidatingly red but it's barely spicy at all so don't worry. on the first bite, it was amazing. pork texture was good, bamboo shoot was delicious, the noodle has just the right firmness, but the broth was just okay. however the more we eat the more the magic disappears. in fact I'm sad to say that the overall experience felt very flat. plus it felt very heavy and oily after a while. at the end it also leaves some after taste that doesn't suit my palate so I wasn't very pleased with the food. it was quite toward the expensive side, and the think is I feel like there are a lot of other ramen places that tastes far better with either the same price or even less. so for a one time experience it was okay, but to be honest I will think twice to come back

This is a new bakery place in the midtown area and I checked in to see what they offered. I didn't have the appetite to try out a lot, so settled for a Silky milk bun alone. The shop looked clean and spotless.The bakery items were well stacked and easy to follow for purchasing. I took one of the buns and kept it near the register for the attendant to check out. But the lady at the count picked up my milky bun and added it to the order of another lady whom she was checking out.When I informed her that it was mine, she realized and called out another employee to do a reversal. It took them some time to figure out how to fix it and send us our ways. The milky bun was very soft and  delicious, but the whole shopping experience for just a single bun was so lengthy that seemed as if I went out on a weekly grocery shopping.P.S: I've updated my review from a 2 to 4 star rating, considering their genuine care to reach out a dissatisfied customer and compensate with a complement. I declined to take up the complementary offer, but felt their intention should not go unnoticed.

Title: Hearty Feast at Little Sheep: A Hotpot to Remember

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Little Sheep on a Wednesday night, seizing their unbeatable "all you can meat" special at just $16.95, available from Monday to Thursday. Delighted by the trio of broth choices, I chose to indulge in a blend of the spicy and regular milky bone broths, which outshone any hotpot base I've encountered before with their rich, savory depth.

The special featured an endless supply of proteins including chicken breast, fatty beef, lamb shoulder, white fish, lamb tripe, pork, and a unique lamb bone delicacy. Despite the variety, the white fish captivated my palate, and the addition of fresh noodles was a revelation – they maintained a perfect bite while soaking up the flavorful essence of the hotpot.

Although the special was comprehensive, the full menu remained at my disposal. I complemented my meal with a selection of fresh vegetables, mushrooms, and extra meats, finding each to be a worthy enhancement.

Little Sheep delivered one of the most satisfying hotpot experiences I've had to date. The combination of the rich, customizable broth, extensive meat selection, and perfectly executed noodles left me eager to return. If you're a hotpot enthusiast, Little Sheep is a must-visit.

They are a tapas style Korean restaurant, and you can order a la carte or go for the tasting menu. Because it was our first time, we opted for the tasting menu for 3 people.The outstanding dish was the Danji braised black angus short rib. The meat really melts in your mouth and the flavor is outstanding. I still dream about the dish from time to time. This is a must-have when you come here.One item I would skip is the tofu with ginger scallion  dressing. The skin had a mochi-like texture which is not what I normally expect from tofu. I felt a little nauseous after eating it. The k.f.c. has a great sauce but the meat itself was a little too fatty. The other items on the tasting menu were good but wouldn't make a special trip to have them. The exceptional short rib is what will keep drawing me back though.

Title: A Szechuan Delight Worth the Spice

Last week's visit to this Szechuan spot was a revelation for my boyfriend and I. A delight for spice lovers, the restaurant's authenticity and hospitality set the tone for an amazing experience.

We skipped the renowned grilled fish, evidently a crowd favorite, and dived straight into the spicy beef and tripe. Though the serving size could have been larger, the dish itself was a fiery wonder, packing a symphony of spice and flavor that we relished. 

For mains, the name of the chicken dish escapes me, but it was reminiscent of a saltier Taiwanese popcorn chicken – a hit for my boyfriend, albeit too salty for my taste. The beef hot pot, however, was a showstopper with its generous portions of tender beef and vegetables.

A piece of advice: complement the meat-heavy offerings with some vegetable dishes for a balanced meal. Also, don't skip the rice – it's included and it perfectly complements the rich dishes.

What truly elevates the dining experience is the family history behind it. Lisa's insights into her family's commitment to Szechuan culture added depth to an already charming environment.

While prices may be a tad high, the cost is well justified by the genuine, attentive service and the culturally rich atmosphere. Eagerly anticipating our next visit!

Ratings:
Food: 5/5
Ambience: 5/5
Service: 5/5

Title: A Cozy Tuesday Evening with Sizzling Clay Pots

My recent Tuesday night visit to this bustling restaurant was memorable. Despite the crowd, we were seated instantly. The highlight of our meal was the clay pots; I chose double shrimp, while my boyfriend opted for a mix of chicken and beef. These pots, served searing hot, made the rice at the bottom sinfully crispy—a texture lover's dream! The server's drizzle of sweet soy sauce added an indulgent finishing touch. The tableside ginger-scallion condiment was irresistible, making it worth a return visit alone. I'm already planning a future outing to sample their appetizers alongside another delightful clay pot!

Title: A Warm Experience with Tasty Comfort Food

I recently dined at [Restaurant's Name] on an exceptionally hot day, and while the AC struggled to provide relief, the food made up for any discomfort. My friend and I indulged in a shared feast, starting with the chicken and sweet potato pancakes, which unfortunately didn't quite hit the mark for my taste. 

However, the baked Mac and cheese was a delightful comfort, creamy and satisfying. But the star of the meal was undoubtedly the po' boy, a delicious creation that stood out as the best dish on our table. 

Though the service had its slow moments, it was all forgotten with each flavorful bite we took. In summary, if you're looking for hearty and delicious fare, this spot is worth a visit—just perhaps on a cooler day.

Not bad not bad. Service is a bit slow compared to other take out dumpling place. Other places have you in and out in 30 seconds but this place everybody on line waited 5-10 minutes for their orders.My friends and I tried the boiled and fried dumplings, peanut noodles, hot and sour soup and sesame pancake. Dumplings were solid - a bit pricey. Loved the hot and sour soup. Pancake... eh - definitely been sitting out for awhile. Peanut noodles... eh. Not enough flavor or sauce. Would go back but wouldn't be on my recommendation list

They delivered lunch to my job today and my goodness!!! I had the chicken kabob w/rice, green salad, and baklava! The chicken was so juicy and flavorful; rice came with grilled onion, tomato, and lemon; salad was refreshing; and the baklava--ugh to die for! Everything was nicely packed and it was so scrumptious!

Visited this bustling eatery for brunch and wasn't disappointed. To avoid the rush, it's wise to arrive early and snag a table. The brunch offerings are satisfying and come at reasonable prices. Definitely worth a visit for a solid morning meal.

I had friends come in from out of town and wanted to show them the NY Italian experience. Piccola Cucina Osteria has been on my list of to-try Italian places so I brought them here. The service here was fine, although I did find it a bit unnerving that one of the waiters kept on standing by my friend to check out his hair in the mirror.We ordered the squid ink pasta, risotto, bolognese and lobster linguine. The pastas were good, but there was no particular standout dish from what we had. I feel with all of the good pasta in New York, I probably would not revisit this establishment but it seems like a fine choice if you are craving a quick bite near Soho of decent quality.

Title: A Gastronomic Delight Surpassing High Expectations

As someone who has spent the better part of a decade indulging in the finest dining this city has to offer, it takes something truly exceptional to distinguish itself as a favorite. This restaurant has done just that, soaring beyond my already lofty expectations set forth by a friend's glowing recommendation.

The culinary journey here was nothing short of spectacular, particularly for someone who typically shies away from cooked fish – yet every dish was a revelation. Of the four fish dishes sampled, the wild sea bass with its caviar and succulent buttery cream was sublime. The cod was memorable, though it was the accompanying rice that stole the show, rather uniquely. Moving on from fin to shell, the langoustine was a delight, presenting a skillful contrast in textures between claw and tail meat, all bathed in a zesty lemon cream sauce.

However, the pièce de résistance was unequivocally the Hokkaido uni. Served atop a crisp brioche with a hint of black truffle, it left me yearning for more—so much so that I found myself wishing for an à la carte option just for an extra taste.

While predominantly seafood-focused, the menu also made room for meat with a quail dish and a melt-in-your-mouth wagyu course that was the epitome of indulgence. The wagyu's fattiness was perfectly balanced and, despite my boyfriend's preference for a touch more salt, I found it faultless.

Spanning 13 courses, the meal culminated in three dessert acts that, while somewhat overshadowed by the preceding savories, were a welcome lightness. The melon palate cleanser, strawberries in syrup, and a playful shaved ice soufflé gave a refreshing end to a sumptuous feast, with the strawberries emerging as a classic favorite.

Service was impeccable throughout, and contrary to Chef Ramirez's controversial history, we witnessed a hospitality staff that was both diverse and gracious. And for those who like to capture their dining experiences, photography is encouraged—just hold off on the video.

In conclusion, this restaurant has earned a spot at the top of my list, and I am already planning a return—perhaps to celebrate a special occasion. It's not just a meal; it's a benchmark for culinary excellence.

I don't understand, in most instances I feel like New Yorkers are too generous with their yelp stars in my opinion. So why does this wonderful restaurant have a three star average?The space here is generous and the top floor is GORGEOUS. Definitely request to sit on the top floor as it is a big improvement on the second. Service was friendly, precise, and fast. Here's what we had:Burrata: holy shit this cheese is like butterrrr. Like if you think a ball of mozzarella cheese is a ball of mozzarella. Nope. This is amazing. Don't miss it. 5 stars. Arugula salad: this was like a mountain of arugula with two cherry tomatoes and some shaved Parmesan on it. I was expecting more seeing at it costs $3 to make this at home but it was good as it could be considering. The dressing was good.Farfalle Al Limoncello  ommmmmgggg this was heavily! Great flavor, you could really taste the lemon but it was not sour. Fantastic though the portion is small (though prob not smaller than normal NY portions).Margarita Pizza: considering how good everything else was I was expecting much more from this. It was whatevs. Overall though the food here is great and you should definitely give it a try as I think it is the full 4.5 star package!!! Yummmm!!!

Love this cozy Indian spot, their newest location tucked into the Theatre District. The must-gets:- the masala chai: oh my gosh, glorious, sweet, spicy, piping hot, THE BEST chai I've ever had - the channa saag: the chickpeas have this great roasted taste, simmered in their spinach that's not too creamy or salty, so deliciously made- the chaat appetizer: crispy rice puffs dressed in sweet and savory sauces, refreshing, light, such a great start to the meal- the roti: the flatter, whole-wheat cousin to naan totally won me over! Served hot and just the right amount of doughiness and sweetness 5 stars!!!!

Everything looked beautiful and tasted amazing!We were a group of 8 for Saturday night dinner, so we were able to order a lot of different things,  share appetizers,  share desserts,  and try each other's entrees. The wait staff and bartender were great and very nice.  We were there about 3 hours.  It's a relaxed and enjoyable meal in a lovely space. My favorites:EscargotFried calamariMoules frites (mussels with a side of fries)Pasta aragostagoat's milk cheesecakeApple tart

I was expecting fast casual food from the pictures I've seen of the iPad menus, but this place was far from it. It was a nice casual Mediterranean restaurant that just uses iPads to show their menu, which was interesting... I guess it saves paper.I shared the shawarma and Moroccan laffes with my friend. Super juicy and flavorful, and the wrapping provided enough support to make for clean eating. We also shared hummus and tabbouleh which were also really good!

To start, I had researched this restaurant well in advance of visiting NYC. I love love love Italian food, especially family recipe style true Italian. It is so awesome that Lady Gaga and her family wanted to share this amazing cuisine with the rest of the world.    Me and a friend wanted to dine here for dinner and made reservations in advance because they do fill up for dinner, it isn't a very big restaurant at all. You could honestly kiss it if you weren't searching for it nestled between buildings. It does have a cute outdoor terrace area for a back patio dining experience as well. Being December, we ate in the main dining room which was cozy and well decorated for Xmas!    The food was nothing short of spectacular, we started off with some Italian style dinner bread and oil for dipping. The bread was very tasty and fresh.     Finally came our delicious looking entrees! We both got the White Truffle Alfredo! Hands down the best fettuccine Alfredo dish ever! So well seasoned and the perfect temperature. Topped with grated Parmesan & sautéed mushrooms! The truffle infused cream was very unique and satisfying as well.      It was so filling although didn't look like much food. No room for dessert although I'm sure that wouldn't have disappointed. Would def return the next time I'm in NYC, worth the wait and transport to it! It was amazing! The atmosphere inside was very inviting and comfortable yet upscale. The tables and holiday decor added an element of intimacy and elegance too. The family did this place right, everything seemed very well thought out and the food still has me wanting to return! My only slight concern was the lack in exceptional service, with everything else being so perfect, the staff seemed a bit lackluster or overwhelmed idk which. Would definitely return and recommend to any Italian lovers or Gaga fans for a unique and memorable dining experience. LOVED THE FOOD SO MUCH!! Mmmm

Title: A Fresh Taste of Innovation in Midtown

Just stepped into a new spot on 45th in Midtown, and it's worth the chatter. Straying from the predictable, I ditched the familiar Kellari Tavern and took a leap of faith (cue the soundtrack to my shower concerts featuring Steve Winwood's "Valerie") to this eclectic eatery that's stirring up the local lunch scene.

The establishment boasts a sleek bar with a scenic backdrop—bottles poised against a towering window pane, an aesthetic tease for the appetite (picture it here: bit.ly/2FQNcZt). The menu? A tasteful mosaic of options, from the avant-garde smoked crispy duck wings to the comforting embrace of beef cheek steamed buns, burgers, flatbreads, and salads.

I indulged in the Roasted Beets & Wild Arugula Salad, a symphony of whipped goat cheese, wheat berries, candied pecans, and pomegranate vinaigrette, topped with a perfectly grilled salmon (feast your eyes: bit.ly/2AZUu9X). The dish was a harmonic blend; each ingredient sang but none outshone the others. The colleagues I dined with gave a nod of approval to their own choices, hinting at future visits—much earlier than my eventual return.

This Midtown newcomer hits the right notes: FOOD at a glowing 4 stars for its creatively satisfying fare, AMBIANCE a comfortable 3.5 stars for its chic yet inviting vibe, and SERVICE at 3.5 stars with an enthusiasm that borders on overzealous. Overall, a harmonious 4-star experience, bolstered by its culinary prowess and prime location.

In the bustling symphony of New York City dining, this place adds a refreshing melody. Still humming, "Valerie, call on me," I'm calling you to give this place a try. Looking for more NYC dining spots? Check out my collection of reviews here: bit.ly/2sGleaS.

Title: A Szechuan Twist to Seafood Boils in Chinatown

My friends and I ventured into a bustling seafood boil spot in the heart of Chinatown, lured by the promise of Szechuan-infused flavors. The concept was as intriguing as it sounds: a traditional seafood boil meeting the fiery zest of Szechuan cuisine.

We dived into a culinary sharing spree, sampling an array of dishes that circulated our large table. Notably, the Fried Diced Popcorn Chicken with Spicy Chili lived up to the spicy hype, delivering an intense kick that set our taste buds ablaze.

As for my main course, I settled on the Combo C, immersed in the supposed 'Ghost Street' sauce. Unfortunately, the sauce missed the mark on the Szechuan reputation for heat, leaning more towards sweet and oily rather than the anticipated tongue-tingling spiciness.

However, the experience wasn't marred by this. The rest of the meal was enjoyable, with various dishes (whose names elude me) satisfying our seafood cravings. The attentive staff deserves a shoutout for their vigilance in maintaining a clean table and for the charming surprise of donning bibs on us pre-feast - a delightful touch.

In summary, while I hope for an amped-up Szechuan spice level in future visits, the overall atmosphere and service made for a solid dining experience. Here's to more heat next time!

I recently visited this restaurant for a friend's birthday dinner on a Tuesday when it was delightfully quiet, providing us with a private dining experience. The menu selection we chose was excellent and included nan bread, samosa, a flavorful lamb curry, a perfectly seasoned chicken curry, aromatic basmati rice, a mouth-watering chicken biryani, stuffed naan bread, delectable fried chicken, and a sizzling meat platter. Among these, the fried chicken and chicken tandoori stood out as my personal favorites, though the curries also impressed with their well-balanced heat. The service was satisfactory, complementing an overall enjoyable meal.

Title: Takeout Triumphs at Noodle Lounge

My experiences at Noodle Lounge have led me to a simple conclusion: takeout is the way to go. The in-house service is notoriously slow, having tested my patience on multiple lunchtime visits. Despite escalating wait times on each occasion, prompting a last-minute grab-and-go during my final dine-in, the food quality never wavers.

The culinary highlight is undeniably their Pineapple Fried Rice and Drunken Noodles, especially with shrimp— a standout choice over the somewhat lackluster chicken and beef options. Other must-tries include the vibrant papaya salad, the crispy fried dumplings, and the indulgent crab rangoon.

Price-wise, the lunch specials hit the sweet spot offering great value for money. And should you find the time to dine in without clock-watching, treat yourself to their refreshing sangrias or the delightful lychee martini.

In summary, Noodle Lounge serves up delectable dishes that are best enjoyed from the comfort of your own home or office. Their takeout service is efficient, ensuring you get to savor their flavors without the wait.

My friend and I came to Gotham Bar and Grill for a weekday lunch. We had a 1 pm reservation and I was seated promptly. The restaurant was busy but not every table was full nor was it crazy. I was offered a drink menu and I started with a glass of wine, before it arrived at the table my friend showed up. She placed her drink order which was delivered as we began to mull over the menu. The waiter never checked in on us nor did he reappear. We saw staff with a bread basket handing out warm rolls so we asked for one, and the server obliged. It was an extraordinary amount of time until our server came to take our food order. We both ordered from the Lunch 3 Course $48 menu: - The Seafood Salad- The Bucatini Cacio E Pepe- (2) Miso Marinated Black Cod with bok choy, shiitake mushrooms, sticky rice, soy lemongrass- Gotham Chocolate Cake- Assorted SorbetWe had decided to split the appetizer, first course, and desserts which we had mentioned to the waiter. The food came out very slow, it was delicious and precise. Perfectly presented and no need for accoutrements.  As we eagerly awaited each next course we also eagerly awaited ordering another drink. The surrounding tables came and went and we didn't finish dining until after 4 when we had arrived at 1pm. Thankfully we weren't in a rush but this seemed extreme. The lack of attention from our original server who eventually left for the day in the middle of our meal was replaced with someone friendly and more attentive. This experience was disappointing especially considering with food and drink this meal for 2 was close to $300. The food itself is to die for (except the bland sorbet). If it wasn't for the lackluster service this review would be 5 stars.

Tucked away in the bustling Lower East Side, a delightful new family-run eatery has recently opened its doors, offering a refreshing alternative to the usual dining scene. Specializing in wholesome and satisfying purple rice bowls and rolls, the restaurant is a haven for those seeking nutritious yet hearty options.

Despite its burgeoning popularity, this gem remains highly affordable, a welcome surprise in an area often known for pricier establishments. Both the chicken and pork rice rolls I sampled were exceptional, demonstrating a commitment to quality without overcomplicating the flavors. Now, venturing into their rice bowl, the same level of freshness and simplicity has left a lasting impression.

The no-frills approach to good food shines through with every bite, and I fervently recommend a visit for a meal that feels both down-to-earth and gratifying. Before you leave the area, don't miss the chance to indulge in Sam's fried ice cream just around the corner — a perfect sweet ending to a delightful dining experience.

Title: A Refreshing Culinary Experience at [Restaurant Name]

Upon entering [Restaurant Name], the distinct difference from its village counterpart was immediately apparent; the bright, airy ambiance set by the expansive skylight instantly lifted our spirits. The menu boasted a delightful selection of dishes, and we indulged in the vibrant Mango Tango, Osaka Tower, and Tokyo Sunset – each a testament to the restaurant's culinary creativity.

Our choice of the Meat Lover's set menu, accompanied by Lady M's exquisite green tea crepe, showcased a well-rounded offering, including soup, salad, and an array of meats, culminating in a gratifying dessert. The standout dishes for me were the robustly flavored bistro hanger steak and the playful s'mores dessert, a perfect ending to the meal. The meat's quality shone through in every bite, complemented by sauces that truly acted as the perfect finishing touches.

An insider's tip: don't miss the happy hour before 6pm for amazing deals, and take note of the late happy hour after 9:30pm for those night owl cravings. Whether you're dining as a cozy duo or a bustling group, [Restaurant Name] caters effortlessly to all party sizes.

In conclusion, [Restaurant Name] earns a spot on your must-try list when in the city – a beacon of taste and value, any time of day.

Title: A Bite of Italy in the Heart of NYC

I recently discovered an Italian gem in NYC that can stand toe-to-toe with my beloved Little Nonna's in Philly, especially when it comes to the perfectly chewy and consistent pasta. During restaurant week, my friend and I indulged in a fantastic deal—$26 for two entrées, an absolute steal.

The meal kicked off with decent bread, nothing out of the ordinary, but paired with a fantastic bean dip that set a high bar for what was to come. The first course, penne, was a culinary delight. It earned a solid 5/5 for its impeccable consistency and taste that left me yearning for another bite. The second course didn't disappoint either; the rigatoni maintained the high standard with another well-deserved 5/5 rating. Although I had a moment of menu envy eyeing the thinly cut wagyu beef at another table, the pasta proved to be completely satisfying.

The experience was wonderful, and I'm already planning my return visit. Ironically, the restaurant seemed to have a humorous way of making guests linger—a little ornament on the stairs took a souvenir from my attire by snagging my pants and tearing a hole. A small misadventure that will make for an amusing story on my next visit!

My family and I took a trip up to New York City for my brother's birthday. We had just gotten back from the matinee showing of Hamilton. My family was now hungry. We knew there was an Italian restaurant nearby because we had reservations for this place on our first night in town. We didn't make those reservations. We decided to try again to eat at this establishment. The restaurant was conveniently located across from the Wagner hotel in which we were staying. We still had to GPS the place. It's easy to miss. It looks like a hole in the wall of this staircase at Wagner Park. When my dad pointed out the sign on the door, I said "No dad that's graffiti" and I almost kept walking. Luckily, my dad has better vision than I do and could see the sign read Gigino's. We walked in and were immediately greeted and seated. It was about 7pm on a Sunday. There were a few seats inside. Outside is where it's at though. They have lots of seating outside and the view is amazing. It's right on the battery with an excellent view of the Statue of Liberty. The sun was setting over the river and the skyline. It was beautiful. This place is an Italian restaurant. Not like Olive Garden. The menu is mostly words I don't know, probably in Italian. They give good descriptions of each dish in English, however. I ordered the Capellini Sirenetta. It was angel hair pasta with shrimp and tomato sauce. Oh yea and arugula. It was delicious. It had a little bit of a spicy kick to it. There were some small chunks of tomatoes, which I don't care for. The tomatoes were easy to eat around. I finished most of my meal despite the tomato chunks. Overall, this place was a great choice. I loved watching the sun set over the water and the city. The food was excellent. This place is a little hard to find, but definitely worth looking for.

Tucked away in the West Village, this Vietnamese eatery offers a refreshingly straightforward menu spotlighting bun, com, and pho, without the frills of modern twists. With seating for around 20, the cozy interior boasts a warm wooden ambience.

I opted for the beef and brisket pho, noodle-free to accommodate my temporary keto diet, and was pleased to find the kitchen willing to swap in a generous serving of sprouts. These sprouts soaked up the soup's flavors beautifully, though the broth itself verged on the salty side. The beef was tender, adequately portioned, and cooked nicely in the broth.

My dining companion's catfish rice fell short of expectations. One could tell the catfish wasn't fresh; it sported a chewy and thick crust indicative of being fried too far in advance, rendering the fish dry and lackluster. The dish suffered further from a meager serving size, with just a small bowl of rice, a couple of vegetable pieces, and few bites of the disappointing catfish.

While I'd give the place another chance, perhaps sticking to their pho, I'd be hesitant about reordering the catfish unless it's guaranteed to be freshly fried. If not, I'd recommend exploring other protein options on the menu.

I visited this eatery with high hopes for a gratifying Mexican meal but was left yearning for more zest in my dining experience. The steak taco and steak quesadilla, my choices for the evening, while decently prepared, were noticeably lacking in robust flavor. The tomatoes, intended to add a fresh burst, instead contributed nothing but texture due to their blandness. Additionally, the green sauce served alongside was disappointingly dilute, detracting from the overall taste rather than enhancing it. In conclusion, the restaurant is passable for a casual meal, but it might not satisfy those in search of a truly vibrant and rich culinary adventure.

Friends and I came here for brunch because our original brunch plans didn't work out and this was nearby with plenty of open tables. I had the frittata, but it was dry, bland, and disappointing. Their $30 entree with unlimited drinks deal during brunch was such a great deal though, so I can totally see myself coming back and would just choose a different brunch entree. There was a choice of four classic cocktails. I tried one of each! So worth the $30 total. Even though I did not enjoy my frittata (my friends enjoyed their food though!), I would still definitely recommend this place for their entree plus all-you-can-drink deal. Taste | 3Atmosphere | 3.5Presentation | 3.5Service | 3OVERALL | 3

Title: Serene Sushi Sanctuary in Midtown's Hustle

Last-minute plans led my friend and I to discover a midtown gem for our sushi cravings. Opening its doors at 5pm, the restaurant exudes a sense of cleanliness with a no-frills interior, providing a tranquil escape from the city's chaos.

The staff extended a warm welcome, going above and beyond by accommodating my friend's travel luggage with a smile. Prompt service complemented our experience as we delved into the culinary delights, notably the eel donburi with its flawlessly seasoned and cooked rice.

Perfect for a catch-up, the attentive yet unobtrusive service cultivated an ambiance where the restaurant's presence faded into the background, allowing for an uninterrupted evening of conversation and superb sushi. A true midtown find that should not be overlooked.

Title: A Nostalgic Bite of Heaven at New Chinatown Gem

As Mother's Day approached, I found myself scouring Yelp for the perfect luncheon spot when an image of familiar rice rolls appeared before me. They were reminiscent of South Wind's famous specialty that I hadn't savored in 14 years. Deciding to explore this new find in Chinatown was a spontaneous decision that did not disappoint.

The shop was minuscule, just roomy enough for a handful of patrons, but it pulsated with memories and conversations about the iconic rice rolls. The anticipation built up as I waited to take a bite of what I hoped would be a taste of my childhood.

The rice rolls were an aromatic delight – oily in the best way, with a generous stuffing of dried shrimp, scallions, sesame seeds, and tender pork. The first bite was a flood of nostalgia; they were the embodiment of my fondest memories, perfectly recreated.

If you're unacquainted with these rolls, consider it your culinary duty to try them. Be swift though; they're popular and sell out quickly – and missing out may just spark a public display of disappointment. Next visit, I'm definitely grabbing half a dozen. The folks running the place couldn't be more gracious, contributing to an overall heartwarming experience.

Title: Best Bang for Your Buck Pizza!

If you're craving pizza without breaking the bank, this spot is your go-to. Recently, they've sweetened the deal; slices are $1.50 each, with a combo of 2 slices and a soda for just $3.

Open round the clock, a slice of classic cheese pizza is always at the ready for just a dollar. And when nothing but the freshest will do, a mere 10-minute wait will reward you with a piping hot pie straight out of the oven. For a convenient, quick, and affordable meal, it's hard to beat this pizzeria's offerings.

Title: Authentic Slice of Naples in the Heart of the City - Song E Napule

I recently ventured into Song E Napule after being captivated by its high praise on Yelp. This unassuming gem surprised me with its authentic Italian vibe; I honestly felt transported to Naples the moment I set foot inside. Despite its modest size, the place charmed me with its unique decor, complete with a washing line hanging from the ceiling that added to the authentic ambiance.

The staff, clearly passionate about their craft, injected the dining experience with warmth, and the presence of Italian-speaking patrons only deepened the immersive feel. While the iPad menus were modern and sleek, their functionality puzzled us as we couldn't place orders through them, which felt like a missed opportunity for innovative dining.

We settled on a calzone and a small pizza, both of which arrived in good time. The pizza was hands-down the best I've had in New York, with impeccably balanced dough that struck the perfect chord between softness and crispness. The calzone, though not the best in the city, was delicious in its own right.

Rounding out an already delightful experience was the exceptional service and the unexpected treat of a complimentary chocolate panna cotta—a sweet ending to a memorable meal. Song E Napule is a must-visit for pizza aficionados seeking a slice of authenticity without leaving the city.

I had a delightful dining experience at this ramen spot. The flavors were robust and satisfying, truly tantalizing to the taste buds. The service was commendable, with a waitress who was exceptionally kind and attentive. It's a fantastic place for ramen enthusiasts. My only gripe is the serving of just half an egg in each bowl, which was a bit disappointing. Nonetheless, the food quality makes it a place worth visiting.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Charming Greek Spot

I stopped by this Greek restaurant for lunch with high hopes as a picky eater on a health kick. The menu looked promising with genuine options, and I went for a bowl with mixed greens, a feta-free Greek salad, flavorful broccoli, and lemon chicken, all complemented by hummus. The chicken was pleasingly unmarinated and not overly salty, which suited my palate, and the broccoli packed a punch taste-wise – a delight for my clean eating regime. However, despite the initial deliciousness, my experience was marred as I felt unwell an hour post-meal, leading me to an unfortunate bout of hydration frenzy. My sensitive constitution may have reacted to something in the meal, which was a letdown.

On a positive note, the service was commendable with very friendly staff tending the counter. The ambiance matched the service in quality – it's a cute establishment perfect for a quick bite, offering a variety of Greek staples like gyros and tempting baked goods, alongside convenient upstairs seating.

Overall, while the food at this restaurant hit some high notes on initial taste, my subsequent discomfort makes me hesitant to return. I'd give the food a 3 out of 5, with service and ambiance both earning a solid 4 out of 5.

Title: A Slice Above the Rest at a DDD Alum

I recently visited my 40th restaurant featured on Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives, and it did not disappoint. The frittatine was a delightful starter, but the real star was the pizza. The Montanara Starita Signature Pizza was delicious, but the Montanara Genovese truly stole the show – easily one of the best pizzas I've ever enjoyed. The Bellini paired nicely with the meal, and the service was remarkably swift. While the bill came to $70 including tip, which isn't exactly budget-friendly, the quality and experience were in line with New York City's prices. Definitely worth a visit for any pizza aficionado.

Title: A Hipster Twist on Traditional Banh Mi - Xe May Sandwich Shop

I've been a frequent patron of Xe May Sandwich Shop in the Village, with visits spanning across the spring months. With a couple of visits each in March and April, and three in May, it's safe to say Xe May has become a bit of a habit - and for good reason. While the coffee here is passable, it's truly their Banh Mi sandwiches that shine, possibly deserving of the same adoration some give to their Boba tea.

Xe May's take on the Vietnamese classic may stir some controversy, with whispers of 'hipsterfication' of a beloved staple. However, I find these murmurs of dissent only partly justified. These sandwiches retain the heart of the traditional Banh Mi with well-executed bread, fresh veggies, and succulent meats, setting a high bar for authenticity.

Admittedly, the price point does stir some debate. While hovering below the $10 mark, a number that I'm personally thankful for, it does make me hesitate in awarding a perfect score. The famed lime soda left me underwhelmed, nudging me further toward a four-star rating.

That being said, the potential is undeniable. Should my next venture, armed with Vietnamese coffee and a new sandwich selection, blow me away, I won't hesitate to bump Xe May up to a five-star delight. Price aside, the sandwiches here flirt dangerously close to perfection. Xe May, you just may have won my heart. 

Rating: 4 stars (with room to grow)

Title: A Delightful Surprise at Vic's

I stumbled into Vic's alongside a colleague, aiming for another spot that proved too chaotic and cramped. Vic's welcomed us with the comfort of a spacious booth and a promise of reprieve from the bustle. And what a serendipitous turn it turned out to be!

I must emphasize: while Vic's may be a haven for pizza lovers, don't pigeonhole this gem of a restaurant. The Gem Salad is aptly named – a substantial offering that dazzles with its harmonious blend of acid and texture. The brussels sprouts, reimagined salad-style and served crispy, had us marveling at the sheer deliciousness that the kitchen sent out. 

Admittedly, the fish dish didn't quite soar to the same heights, but the minor misstep was more than made up for by the attentive and seamless service we received. If you're looking for a great lunch spot where the offerings extend far beyond the expected, Vic's should be your go-to. Remember, it's not all about pizza here – give their diverse menu a chance to impress.

We were the 3 of us and bravely decided to do a walk-in for brunch at a few places on LES, on a beautiful sunny Saturday. Off all the places, Sweet Chick was relatively empty and we were hoping to be seated right away. We were put on the waiting list and were told to wait for 40 minutes. It took exactly 40 minutes for us to get our table.Once seated, we ordered a bottle of champagne (St. Vincent @ $40). For food, I got the Kale BLT Salad ($13), and others on got the Shrimp & Grits ($19). Shrimp & Grits was really good and was very flavorful. The Kale Salad on the other hand was not that great and I did not enjoy the house cured Bacon at all.Service was slightly slow to our liking and the staff wasn't that attentive. Although, we did get a pretty good seat - so thanks to our hostess for moving us to the seating we requested!

Last week's team lunch at this spot truly impressed with its upscale yet comfortable modern atmosphere. The restaurant served us generous portions that allowed for a delightful sharing experience. We enjoyed a variety of dishes, including a fresh sushi platter, crispy spring rolls, perfectly grilled asparagus, earthy wild mushrooms, and nicely seasoned roasted potatoes. My personal choice of filet mignon, paired with a glass of red wine, was the highlight—deliciously flavorful and cooked to perfection. Highly recommend for both the food and ambiance.

Title: Charming Bite with Generous Portions

My recent visit to this charming little restaurant offered a cozy dining experience with a bit more elbow room than your typical NYC eatery. Opting for the 3-course tasting menu, my taste buds were taken on an adventure with a well-rounded selection, including appetizers, entrees, naan, dessert, and the bonus of rice and lentils.

The Mango Cod and Banana Leaf Chicken were the highlights of the meal - each dish bursting with flavor and cooked to perfection. The generous portions meant leaving with a satisfied belly.

However, the dessert course fell flat for us. The tart and chocolate mousse came with odd flavor combinations that might not cater to everyone's palate - certainly not ours. 

Service-wise, while pleasant, could use a bit of a nudge in attentiveness; having to flag down for water, dessert menus, and the check slightly dampened the experience.

Overall, a quaint spot that shines with its main courses but could improve on dessert offerings and service attentiveness.

I recently visited Sprinkles on a Sunday morning and indulged in a dozen cupcakes, opting for a split of their Games of Thrones and Strawberry Shortcake Bar specials. To no surprise, both selections were exceptional. True to form, the staff at Sprinkles maintained their reputation for being incredibly friendly and helpful, making the experience all the more delightful. Highly recommend for a sweet treat and top-notch service!

This is honestly my favorite brunch spot in harlem! Staff is super attentive and food is flavor full! Angels of harlem offers and unlimited brunch for 1.5 hrs. They quickly refill your glass when you are running low. Aside from drinks the food iis unparalleled. The shimp and grits is my favorite.

Jiang Diner is a Northwestern Chinese spot in East Village with a focus on noodles and large format dishes.That last part is crucial-- this is far better pick for a group of friends than a date. Portions won't overwhelm you (my boyfriend and I split an entree and an app and were just fine) but your dollar goes further with upsizing and sharing. The large big tray chicken is double the size of the small, and at $26 vs $18, that's a real deal.Almost equally as crucial is that they're one of few BYOB options in this neck of the woods (and I can safely say they have Panna II Garden, or BYOB Christmas Lights Indian Place, beat on the food front). So come with a six pack and dive into some big plates with friends.Your focus here should be large big tray chicken without bones-- $2 is a small price to pay given the amount of labor it took us to debone. It's more spiced than spicy and the chicken is tender. Spicy Village's version is more flavorful but I think the meat quality is better here. It comes with hand cut noodles, which are chewy and absorb the sauce well. The potatoes are the secret stars.I have yet to explore the entire menu, but I can report that the lamb shumai (more like soup dumplings) are great. We also tried sauteed rice noodles from the Northern Wheaten section which were fine but uninteresting.The interior is cheerful, with exposed brick, generic art, and pops of red. Service is fine. Generally no wait on weeknights. If you come in a group, you can keep your tab under $20 a person, which is unusually good for this part of town.

amazing experience, sat in the upper level the terrace area which was so gorgeous. great wine and cocktail selection (must try the serafina champagne cocktail.) got a margherita pie to start (duh) and the tagliatelle paglia & fieno. get that exact order and you won't regret it lol

Upon a friend's zealous recommendation for having the best tots in town, I decided to give this restaurant a try. The tots turned out to be fine, although they didn't quite live up to the hype. However, the silver lining was their really impressive beer selection, which offered a range of choices for connoisseurs and casual drinkers alike.

Found this spot on yelp just casually searching. The ambiance of this place is amazing and def a cute little date spot. I came with a friend and ordered the dan dan noodles ($12) and It was super flavorful and had just enough spice. She got the green peppers in sweet and sour sauce which were really just shishito peppers in sweet and sour sauce but they were PERFECT. ($6) I also got the seafood pancake ($6) which was a little bit too doughy for my liking. I'm used to scallion pancakes which have a nice crispy texture and are very light, these were made a little different. I'll def be returning and trying out other noodle options soon!

Good food, good service, fairly priced. Need I say more? Definitely recommend the noodle set if you're feeling some curry noodles. The shrimp tempura and work were very delicious! A word of advice - the spicy levels should not be taken lightly, my friend got a level two (highest is level 4 and lowest is level 0) and it was pretty darn spicy!

My boyfriend and I popped into this spot for a breakfast bite and were hit by a wave of heat upon entering. Originally, we requested our sandwiches to go, finding the temperature due to the December heat unwelcoming. However, after expressing my discomfort, the staff kindly adjusted the heat, and we decided to dine in.

We ordered the Hamilton Classic with a fried egg on an everything bagel, and the B Train Sandwich scrambled egg style, sharing both. Each sandwich was satisfying, but the B Train stood out as our favorite. The prices didn't break the bank, making the experience worthwhile despite the initial sauna-like setting.

I needed something quick as most New Yorkers do because we're always on the go. This place was just average on their efficiency rating. I mean the waiter never came to check up on me and I had to keep calling him over. Anyways, I was craving pho and after reading all the reviews I decided to eat here. I usually go to my regular spot in Queens, but decided to venture out and try a new spot since I was in the Midtown area. I gave it 3 stars as it's JUST average and nothing more nor less. The service was average, the price of the pho was a bit much, and the taste of the summer rolls + the pho was average. They gave a large bowl of noodles with a little bit of meat inside. I'm not sure why the price on the menu and the price on the receipt was different. I decided not to make a scene about it and made a choice not to return again. I can get cheaper and tastier pho elsewhere.

This is our second time here for their lunch buffet. I was so disappointed with the food this time. I had butter chicken special and my friend got the biryani special. Got a plate with butter chicken gravy which was bad, chicken was rubbery and not fresh. Two other curries were cabbage and  Gujarati kadi, bowl of rice, yogurt, Jamun and naan. And my friends biryani was soggy and not very flavorful. We only liked the soft naan and nothing else. Surely not going back!

The Smith is a New York brunch classic and for good reason. Their brunch menu is truthful the perfect breakfast + lunch fusion. No matter what you walk in with the taste for, at least three or four options on the menu are going to catch your eye. Make sure you call ahead and make a reservation-  despite the restaurant being x10 the size of every other boozy brunch venue in New York, you will be hard pressed to find a seat. The line pours into the sidewalk and with good reason. If weather permits, try to grab a window seat and enjoy the sunshine in the Upper East Side. Not the place to be if you're balling on a budget, but definitely perfect for your treat yourself moment.

Again.... on Sundays we brunch!!Came to B2 Harlem with a friend for just that. My friend and I fumbled our meet up time resulting in us needing to push back our reservation by 2 hours. The staff at B2 were very accommodating. Once I arrived we were both seated. Our waitress came over introduced herself and gave us menus. I immediately noticed the menu given is not the menu on their website. Unlimited mimosa is no longer offered *one of the reasons I chose the restaurant*, and the steak & eggs I was sold on isn't offered either. Disappointed my friend and I went with a carafe of mimosa instead. For my meal I had the Lobster Hash which was very tasty, full of flavor and the perfect portion. My friend and I both enjoyed the mimosa, so much that we ordered another carafe this time trying the Bellini which was also good. Great balance of champagne & juice.  The restaurant is very intimate, the owner Adriane makes her way around the room making sure everyone is taken care of. I enjoyed my time here and look forward to bringing my mom back for dinner.

Title: A Safe Haven for Taco Lovers During Social Distancing

I popped by the local taco joint on Friday to check their social distancing protocol and was pleasantly surprised. The restaurant has smartly moved to a no-indoor guest policy, efficiently handling all orders at the door. Payment is seamless, with both cash and card accepted, and your food is safely delivered curb-side using your name — a truly contactless experience.

Despite the typically lengthy queues, the current situation meant I got to savor their flavors without the wait — a silver lining indeed. Preparing the order took a tad longer, but patience paid off, as the food was exponentially better than during my last visit.

For anyone craving tacos in these precarious times, this spot is a must-try. It's not just about the food; it's also about staying healthy and safe. Highly recommended for a responsible, yet satisfying, culinary escape.

Title: Jeepney: A Taste of Filipino Comfort in the East Village
