If you're on a quest for heartwarming Filipino cuisine in the East Village, look no further than Jeepney. This gem caters to every scenario, be it a lively gathering with friends or a cozy dinner with a special someone, promising a tropical ambiance that warms the soul.

The menu is a parade of delightful dishes, generous in portion and rich in flavor. The mussels and fries come highly recommended, yet rest assured, there doesn't seem to be a single disappointment in the offering. While sometimes there's a wait, it's a small price to pay for the quality you're served. Summer brings the added bonus of garden seating—perfect for those balmy evenings.

Don't leave without trying the tiki drinks; they're as much a staple here as the food. Complementing the vibrant dining experience is the warm and amiable service that makes you feel right at home.

Jeepney isn't just a restaurant; it's a destination. Whether it's a casual night out or a celebration, it's a spot that deserves a place on your go-to list for a reliably delicious and comforting meal.

I was brought here by a buddy from work who is a pizza FANATIC. This is his favorite pizza in NYC and it might be mine as well. The pizza isn't your typical NYC pizza although just as thin, it is very very crispy. The classic, vodka, and shrimp scampi are outstanding. To be honest, I haven't had any of the other flavors, but will keep coming back to try them all! This pizza joint ranks up there with the best of them.

Lovely new Filipino restaurant addition to the Lower East Side. If you want to come here to gossip with friends, this is the place to do it as tsismis means gossip. When you enter the restaurant, you are greeted by a great restaurant crew and a hostess that will seat you to your table. There is a lot on the menu for every eater - whether you are a vegan, vegetarian, seafood lover, meat eater, etc. There is a lot to choose from - the Beefsteak Tagalog, the Pritong Isda (fried milkfish), or the Pancit Bihon are some of the many dishes that are offered. I tried the appetizers with a friend and was glad to see that there were specials for happy hour. Babylou's vegetable lumpia, was fried to perfection. It was filled with a nice array of vegetables and served with vinegar to compliment the taste. Chef Jappy's wings were a happy hour special and was served with a nice mango salsa. The wings were seasoned well. The Kale Laing special stole the show. It was a great happy hour special that was served with a glass of white wine- Galerna Verdejo from Spain. In the Philippines, Laing is usually made with taro leaves, but the chef creatively transformed the dish into something even more delicious and healthy. To end out our meal, we had Sylvanas, which were cute meringue mini cookies with light buttercream. It was great to try these dishes from Tsismis. Can't wait to be back for more.

Came here for brunch on a Saturday, decided upon the 1k+ reviews it has already received. We were seated in the back of the restaurant as the front was the bar area. They have a pretty cool set up with wooden tables and chairs with a long table in the middle.Upon being seated, we were given a bag of complementary mini chocolate muffins which appears to be fresh as they were warm. Definitely unique than giving out bread and butter. I got the IPA Fried Chicken and Waffles while my gf got the Eggs Benedict, which they mentioned is their best seller. I definitely loved my Chicken and Waffles meal which came with two over easy eggs. Tasted wonderful and was a filling meal. The Eggs Benedict came with home fries and they're cooked more on the crispy side which is what I like.I didn't come here for drinks, but they look like they have some awesome drink specials, happy hour deals, especially the pitcher deals for 25$ if I recall correctly. Count me in next time someone wants to have brunch here!

Title: Patient Service Ups the Ante at Champion Pizza

Last Saturday night, my boyfriend and I stumbled into Champion Pizza for a take-home pie, and it's fair to say that while the pizza scored a modest 3.5 out of 5, the accommodating service we received nudged it up to a solid 4.

In the throes of indecision, we bickered over toppings and styles, presenting a challenge to the pizzaman with our half-and-half request – a regular cheese pie and a chicken pesto pie. The styles typically demand different bases, but he was a champ, providing price quotes and even altering the pesto pie to our liking, all with a patience that deserves applause. 

Our custom pie, ringing up at $24, was ready in about 10 minutes. While I appreciate the quick turnaround, a couple more minutes in the oven might have done our pie some good. We looked forward to a crispy crust but were met with soft doughiness instead. The chicken topping, regretfully, was on the soggy side due to heavy breading. 

Champion Pizza epitomizes the classic, no-frills NYC pizza joint – affordable and straightforward. Our experience wasn't dazzling and the pizza itself was somewhat hit or miss. Despite its flaws, I'd choose it again over a fancier option for its sheer simplicity and stellar service.

Average sandwich. The parts of it that had the sauce had great flavor, but then other bites lacked much flavor. Additionally, I had ordered it online and it was not ready by the time it said it would be, so I had to wait a little while.

Title: A Mixed Experience with a Highlight on Cheese and Spinach Naan

I recently visited a local restaurant and had a somewhat mixed dining experience. The highlight was undoubtedly the cheese and spinach naan, which was delicious and I highly recommend. The other naans, rosemary and chili & garlic, were hit or miss with the latter packing a gradual punch and the former being partially burnt.

My main course, chili chicken ordered through Mealpal, was decent but not as spicy or as generous in portion as a street cart version I fondly remember. It came with a lot of white basmati rice that, while filling, lacked flavor.

The staff were commendable – very friendly and accommodating, adding a positive note to the visit. However, the chatpati lasooni gobi appetizer fell short, with the cauliflower being undercooked and difficult to eat, even though the sauce was just fine.

Given the reasonable prices and delightful cheese and spinach naan, I'm willing to give this place another shot in the future.

I recently dined at a local restaurant on a Tuesday night, taking advantage of a Pulsd deal. The ambiance upon arrival was slightly off-putting with the absence of music in an empty venue, but the atmosphere improved with a busier crowd and tunes later in the evening. However, the temperature inside was uncomfortably warm, to the point of perspiration, which detracted from the overall experience.

The deal included a choice between three red and three white wines, which was satisfactory, and a selection of tapas. We tried the spicy tuna taco and crab caviar taco, super white tuna tataki, filet mignon tataki, and the rainbow sashimi roll. Flavor-wise the dishes were pleasing, particularly the filet mignon tataki and the trio of meatballs we added from the regular menu, which were highlights. Portion sizes were rather small, necessitating additional orders to reach a modest level of satiety.

The most disappointing dish was the rainbow sashimi roll, which was challenging to eat due to its tendency to fall apart and the imbalance of too much cucumber to fish.

While the meal was decent, the combination of the sweltering heat and the less-than-satisfying quantity leaves me without a strong desire to return.

I recently visited this restaurant with four friends, and we were all delighted with the culinary experience. The meat dishes, particularly the Bo Liu and Vietnamese Steak, were the stars of the evening, boasting an authentic Vietnamese taste that reflected perfect marination techniques. Each bite was succulent, oozing with rich flavors that transported us to Southeast Asia.

Although the prices were on the higher side, they were justified given the "bbq" style experience. Additionally, the fried garlic rice is a must-try, adding a fragrant touch to the meal. However, there was a slight timing mismatch as the rice arrived too soon and had cooled down by the time the meat was ready. Ideally, I'd prefer hot rice served alongside freshly cooked meat.

Despite this minor hiccup, the overall dining experience was superb, and I would gladly recommend this restaurant to those in search of exquisite Vietnamese barbecue.

Sooo I gave 4 stars mostly because my waiter was amazing and attentive. I ordered the catfish. It was cool. Nothing spectacular . The Mac n cheese was ok. Everything was just 'good'. I would go back because the menu is interesting and I would want to try other things that may make me come back and give another star. I hope. PS. The watermelon marg wasn't the best . Again everything was just 'OK'

Title: A Dreamy Culinary Stop Near Color Factory

My recent visit to this charming eatery just a stone's throw from Color Factory was an experience that turned our dreams into delectable reality. Arriving 5 minutes before the 11 AM opening on a Sunday may seem like a short wait, but for a Gen Z'er, it's an eternity. Thankfully, the anticipation was worth it.

The space, while not expansive, offers a cozy upstairs seating area, with additional room downstairs for larger groups. A welcoming bar greets you by the entrance, amidst a handful of booths and several tables.

Our culinary adventure was led by my friend's simple request for a cheeseburger, and to our delight, 'The All-American Burger' hit the mark. With its prime burger patty, fresh lettuce, ripe tomato, tangy pickles, melted American cheese, and a secret sauce, this burger was a star. To top it off, we indulged in the "crazy milkshake" - a towering cookies and cream delight that's as Instagram-worthy as it is delicious. The waitress graciously offered us the choice to receive our orders as they were ready or wait for everything at once, and we wisely chose the former.

Fair warning: try not to fill up on the milkshake, however tempting it may be after you've snapped your wide-eyed, mouth-dropped, big silly grins for the 'gram. The shake, adorned with a giant Oreo, whipped cream, and crushed cookies, is a dessert meal in itself.

When the cheeseburger landed on our table, accompanied by a generous serving of crispy fries, it was clear that we had our work cut out for us. Despite our best efforts, not all the fries and shake could be finished, but what we did manage was a feast for both the palate and the memory.

For those in need of refreshment, the restaurant offers a single, spacious, and clean restroom for females.

In conclusion, if you're ever in the area for a celebration or just in search of a sweet treat that guarantees a joyous expression, make a stop here for the milkshake. It's an indulgence that's decidedly worth it. Enjoy your visit!

If you're wandering near Madison Square Garden searching for an authentic and robust meal, allow yourself the pleasure of experiencing the Signature Combination Beef Pho at Chef Trung's cozy establishment. This Northern rendition of Pho breaks away from its sweeter Southern counterpart, delivering a rich and savory broth that has been lovingly simmered with beef and pork bones. Its aromatic essence is a prelude to the satisfaction you'll find in each mouthful.

The dish comes generously portioned with thick rice noodles, a hearty serving of meat, and is garnished with just the right amount of green onions and cilantro. The absence of the usual Pho accouterments like hoisin, sriracha, and fresh herbs is hardly felt, as the broth's complexity stands firmly on its own. A splash of vinegar from the table can amplify the flavors even further, should you desire.

A side of the Crab Meat Spring Rolls is non-negotiable. These crisp parcels, brimming with succulent crab meat, and accompanied by a tangy fish sauce infused with carrots and daikon, make for an irresistible combination.

The restaurant's minimalist menu - focusing on spring rolls, pho, and beverages - allows for a dedication to excellence, which is evident in every bite. Opting for a medium bowl proves to be ample, satisfying even the hungriest of patrons.

Despite its modest size, the spot conveniently located by Penn Station boasts a clean (albeit dim) bathroom and an intimate array of tables plus bar seating. The staff's attentive and friendly demeanor only enhances the dining experience.

In summary, this little gem offers a delightful culinary journey with its well-executed traditional fare, proving to be a must-visit for both pho aficionados and novices alike.

Title: Hits and Misses with Potential for a Second Chance

Rating: ★★★½☆

Our visit to the restaurant started with a bit of a hiccup as we arrived on time only to be caught up in a confusing wait due to some seating mix-ups. However, the swift turnover of tables worked in our favor, and we were seated relatively quickly. 

The menu, with its wide array of options, promised something for every taste, raising our expectations. Sadly, the food did not quite meet the mark; while it was presented attractively, it failed to deliver on robust flavors. The tartare and fried chicken stood out positively, offering a glimmer of what the kitchen is capable of. Conversely, the deconstructed eggs Benedict lacked excitement, and the breakfast sandwich suffered from dryness. Another table's feedback on the donut tree suggested that we perhaps weren't alone in our disappointment.

Despite the underwhelming experience, the restaurant shows promise, and it feels only fair to give it another shot once the dining scene returns to normal post-quarantine. Here's to hoping that a second visit will reveal a more consistent and flavorful experience.

Title: Cozy Lobster Haven by Lady Liberty

After a delightful visit to the Statue of Liberty, we stumbled upon Luke's, a cozy nook for lobster lovers. Despite its petite size that seats about 20, the ambience was comfortable and not overcrowded.

Service was a high point, with attentive and courteous staff making our meal a pleasure. We dove into the seafood theme with my boyfriend choosing the lobster roll priced at $16 – a tasty but slightly smaller portion than anticipated. I opted for the lobster grilled cheese at $13, which was generously filled and utterly scrumptious.

To complement our main dishes, we shared a large Lobster Corn Chowder for $10, which proved perfect for the nippy weather and paired wonderfully as a dip for my grilled cheese.

While the lobster roll could benefit from a side to round out the meal, the grilled cheese and chowder duo left us content and warmed. Luke's is definitely worth the visit for any lobster enthusiast, especially for the grilled cheese that I'd gladly recommend!

Went to flame last night and had a reunion of sorts with two of my close friends. This was my first time here but I've heard great things from friends, co-workers, and fellow Elites, so I really looking forward to it. They did not disappoint at all! We walked in without a reservation at about 8pm but were seating immediately! I had an old fashioned or two before arrive so I was pretty hungry. I ordered the skirt steak platter and we all shared soup dumplings. I love the fact that each of the soup dumplings came individually placed on their own soup spoon, which completely solves the issue of them potentially tearing/leaking. I literally tore through my meal and left no crumb behind. I even looked up a few times to see my coworkers staring and laughing in amusement. What can I say... the meal was delicious. The white rice was cooked perfectly (note to self: get a rice cooker!); the steak was cooked medium rare and was soft, tender, and juicy; the vegetables seasoned well and hat a bit of a spicy kick; the shrimp, while only a few, were large, plump, and seared with a crisp.

My dining experience at this restaurant offered a delightful mix of tasty food, speedy service, and affordability. Surprisingly, on a Saturday at 1:30 pm, the place wasn't crowded at all – we were the only patrons. Our bill came to a reasonable $27.12, covering both a starter and a main course, tip included. I tried the Bakso, which was flavorful; however, the beef balls were disappointingly chewy, bordering on rubbery. Despite this, the restaurant is a commendable option for a quick, budget-friendly meal.

If you're craving Mexican cuisine on the Upper East Side, Toloache should be at the top of your list. My brunch experience there was outstanding. The queso appetizer was a mouthwatering start, oozing with freshness and packed with flavor. The highlight, surprisingly, was their burger, which was expertly cooked and equally delicious. To wash it down, their sangria was nothing short of amazing. I highly recommend Toloache for a flavorsome brunch.

Been meaning to try this place for a long time and even walked by it a couple of times, but I finally got myself some soup. This place was made famous by the sitcom Seinfeld as the inspiration for the Soup Nazi. Service here was friendly and my soup was pretty good. Each soup comes with a piece of bread, a Lindtz chocolate, and a fruit (I got a banana). Eat the chocolate right away or it melt into a mess. I had the jambalaya soup, which was a first for me so I have nothing to compare against. It was slightly spice and very hardy with a lot of meat and rice. It was very good and pretty filling. Note that this is just an open store front with no seating. Grab your soup to enjoy at home, your hotel, or bring it to nearby Columbus Circle/Central Park.

Title: A Relaxing New Spot with a Touch of Class

I recently dined at this fairly new restaurant and was immediately taken by its low key and chill ambiance. On my visit, GM Chris extended a warm welcome and ensured our evening was perfect.

The food here didn't disappoint. Their promotion of 50% off selected bottles of wine on Mondays (though I'm not certain if this will be a long-term deal) was a pleasant surprise. My friend's pork chops were tender and flawlessly cooked, while my hanger steak was elevated by a delicious herb butter, and the brussel sprouts on the side were the perfect complement.

Their happy hour boasts impressive specials like $5 wines, which I'm eager to come back for. To cap the night, their tiramisu pie was an absolute delight, balancing the savoriness of our meals.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit, particularly to enjoy their happy hour once again.

In terms of its identity, Legends is a relatively standard Irish sports bar. However, there are a couple things that set it apart from the others. For one, it is huge. This place can easily accommodate a huge group in the first floor space alone, and it evens have a second floor too. Secondly, you will find TVs everywhere with each one dedicated to any kind of sport here: NBA, basketball, baseball, college basketball, NFL, college football, etc. They even show international soccer games like Premier League and La Liga. Other places will usually be missing some sports - not so at Legends.Food and drinks are average priced too, which is not bad for a place right next to the Empire State Building.

TLDR: Michelin-starred Korean noodle shop near Greenwich Village. Ramen bowls with unique Korean broths, super good.When I still worked near here, I was fortunate to grab a reservation as a last minute dinner idea. JeJu had not yet received their star but nonetheless - we had an awesome meal.It was a weekday so we didn't go too crazy. We did get the JeJu Chicken Wings which were great. It was crispy, that spicy mayo-ish concoction coated the crust with this creamy richness. Excellent.We got the Gochu Ramyun and So Ramyun. The Gochu broth was this rich pork broth, it had spice, it had depth and was just so different. Very unique compared to most ramens you'll have int he city. The So Ramyun I liked a lot too but just a heads up - it is on the heavier side. The broth is a veal bone broth, incredibly creamy and very heartwarming. Especially since we went in the winter time.I've heard great things about the tasting menu here. Unfortunately we haven't been able to come back since but definitely will. Great to see they're doing well.

Title: A Sunday Brunch to Remember at Cesca

My recent visit to Cesca for Sunday brunch was nothing short of a full-blown epicurean escapade. Invited by my best friend who snagged a fantastic deal on Pulsd, the experience was first-class from the outset. I arrived to find him sipping a scrumptious bellini, which I promptly decided to mimic.

Cesca's ambience exudes elegance without pretension, striking a perfect balance between sophistication and comfort. The service was impeccable; our attentive waiter ensured our glasses never saw the bottom, thanks to the generous two-hour bottomless deal included in our voucher.

Though the brunch menu was selectively curated, it showcased an array of farm-to-table dishes. The standout for me was the salmon served over a unique mix of cubed beets and peaches – a dish whose flavors still dance in my memory.

We capped off the meal with a raspberry and cream sorbet that transported me back to my first gelato experience in Florence – simply divine.

Cesca has secured its place as a top contender in my list of favorites. I'm eager to return, particularly if they partake in restaurant week. I wholeheartedly recommend Cesca for anyone looking for an exquisite brunch spot – do try that sorbet!

Title: A Delightful Discovery Near Central Park – Mei Jin Ramen

I recently visited Mei Jin Ramen, nestled conveniently near the museums and Central Park, and came away thoroughly impressed. The restaurant, a hidden gem devoid of the typical tourist traps, lived up to its stellar Yelp reputation.

On a dreary, rainy day, the Mei Jin Miso Ramen was exactly what the weather ordered. Its rich, flavorful broth, tender meat, and perfectly cooked noodles provided a comforting embrace, complemented by the right mix of bamboo shoots and corn, all served in a generously deep bowl.

My companions explored the diverse menu with gusto. One savored the colorful, pescatarian-friendly poke bowl on purple rice, while another enjoyed the omelette on rice. Thanks to a brunch special with 50% off, we were tempted to sample the breadth of their offerings.

The beverage selection didn't disappoint either. I indulged in a self-poured Japanese iced milk tea, followed by a light and refreshing lychee mojito adorned with an actual lychee. The complimentary hibiscus fruity drinks, complete with candied flowers, were a delightful touch and a testament to Mei Jin Ramen's hospitality.

Speaking of hospitality, the service was exceptional. The staff were attentive, patient, and created a welcoming atmosphere that encouraged us to linger over our meal. They weren't just servers; they were the embodiment of warmth and friendliness, especially with their unexpected drink offerings.

The ambiance contributed to the overall charm of Mei Jin Ramen. An abundance of natural light, an opportunity for people-watching from our bar seats, and an eclectic music selection that resonated with me, created an enjoyable dining atmosphere.

Even the restrooms deserve a mention for their cleanliness and quirky one-way mirror design – another indicator of Mei Jin Ramen's attention to detail.

In conclusion, Mei Jin Ramen has earned a return customer in me. The meal was a parade of flavors, the service was stellar, and the ambiance was simply delightful. Their brunch menu deal is a steal, and the surprise complimentary drinks were the proverbial cherry on top. Thank you, Mei Jin Ramen, for a memorable meal!

At Humble Fish, the authenticity of their poke bowls shines through, offering a taste of Hawaii on the mainland. The Classic bowl, with its traditional mix of tuna, sesame oil, onions, and seaweed, transports you straight to the islands - it's a nostalgic bite for anyone missing home. I was equally impressed with the Sincerely, Salmon bowl, a delightful blend of vinegar, sweetness, and salmon, completed with a generous serving of ikura. The only place where Humble Fish could elevate their game is by sourcing genuine ogo limu from Hawaii, which would lend their bowls that distinctive, crunchy seaweed texture. Considering it's affordable at $1/lb, this seems like a feasible enhancement. Overall, a strong contender for those seeking a Hawaiian poke experience.

This place is a trek from where I live and after such a journey for this pizza, I can say this place certainly lives up to the hype it's gotten. Mama's Too good to be kept a secret.When I heard about this place, I've had it on my list of places to visit since many people I know posted about the pepperoni squares and that crust. I mean I love a good pepperoni cup especially when its all crispy and there's a ton of it. There was a line outside the door and ended up waiting with my brother for about 20 minutes for fresh roni squares.The Verdict? That crust was crunchtastic because I enjoy a crispy crust and the toppings were aplenty. Getting two can more than fill you up. There were other options I ended up not trying for the sake of repeat visits. They all looked great and if the standard is as good as the ones I've already had, then Mama's Too has a delicious future.Happy eating and remember: Don't deny, satisfy!

Amazing food here but the service could be better.We made the reservation (a must) for a Friday at 6:30pm. Our table was given away when we showed up 5 mins late, meanwhile, another couple that showed up on time did not get their table either.As such, we waited another 30 mins for a table to clear up. The restaurant was super small so it was an art to even stand strategically while waiting.Once we were seated, it took the server couple tries to bring us water, take our order, and bring us a corkscrew for our wine. For a while, we had the wine opened but no wine glasses to drink from. When the manager (or owner) showed up to assist..she was embarrassed to find out that I opened the wine bottle myself and gave us some bread on the house.Onto the food, the three of us shared beef umka puff pies (delicious), Lagman soup (perfect for winter and they divided into 2 bowls for us), Uzbek Plov (I can eat this everyday), and kazan kebab.The portions were perfect and the dishes were very delicious. Yes it was worth the wait but could be better if the servers were a bit more efficient.

Title: Brunch at Balthazar: A One-Time Experience

After years of anticipation, we finally brunched at Balthazar, a New York City staple. Although we were swiftly seated thanks to advanced reservations, the cacophony inside was startling; the noise level was so intense that the bustling streets of NYC felt tranquil in comparison.

Our waiter promptly attended to us, taking our orders efficiently. I opted for a Rosè and Petit steak with frites and greens. While the meal arrived quickly, it was unremarkable and failed to leave a lasting impression.

In summary, while I'm pleased to have experienced Balthazar, the overwhelming noise and average fare have led me to the decision that a return visit is not in the cards.

Went for after work cocktails which were good. You can always get a Texas style Pineapple Crush with an extra shot.Always alot of people in there and very nosey but that's what you expect when you go. We had the steak and shrimp and the bbq beef ribs which I can say is on point. If you looking to get a decent meal and a good quality drink BBQs on 23rd and 8th is a good place to start.

I came in on a whim to see Steve Earl in the Barrel Room, who is apparently a country music legend that moved to NYC many years ago. I had no idea what I was about to experience.Tickets were about $50 (they have a small surcharge applied to credit transactions - meh). They also serve food, I ordered deviled eggs and a meat plate. Skip the rubbery deviled eggs; the meat plate was good and came with a spicy horseradish spread, cornichons, and olives. I had what I think may have been the best seat in the house, with a direct line of sight to the stage. It was hard getting a servers attention on my floor, but I found a way to manage it. There really is no bad seat in terms of stage view, but I felt like Steve Earl was singing right at me and I'm not ashamed to say I teared up a few times. If you have a chance to see him it's an amazing show, he has a lot of heart and it was both raw and uplifting. Bathrooms (down a beautiful curved staircase) are clean, stylish, and spacious. Staff was helpful and polite. The whole venue is large, great for groups or dates or whatever.I had a very different experience at the Loft, a performance space of theirs three doors down. Tickets here were cheaper, about $25 with fees. I came to see a New Orleans brass band. The Loft stays closed until 30 minutes to showtime and is up a flight of stairs. There is not an official coat check like in the Barrel Room, there are unattended racks to hang your stuff from instead. There is a dance floor in the center, with tables around it. If you had a table you could order food and drinks from the waitstaff, though I did see some people with seats approach the bar too. Two stalls in the ladies room, garbage was overflowing before the show was over, toilet paper on the floor. The bar situation was awful, one of the worst I've seen at any venue or event. Two people behind a very small bar, one handling table orders and the other servicing everyone else. They were tripping all over each other, conversing a lot, staring at cards and receipts and spending too much time not hustling. The guy handling table orders couldn't see the receipts the orders were printed on, and was squinting in the low light and spilling drinks on them. The bartender handling the standing crowd seemed new, either that or completely overwhelmed. He moved painfully slow, was dropping stuff, had no concept of how to keep a record in his head of who was there first and often took people out of order, and seemed to be struggling with his POS system (lots of frustrated hand gestures while staring at the screen for 2-3 mins per order while more people waited impatiently for him to get on with it). His till did not have proper cash before the show started, and he had to give out singles instead of fives and tens. They had a very small beer selection, but at the beginning of the night had already run out of one of their options. It was like no one told them there was going to be a show that night! Their bar area was messy and chaotic, and they ended up losing some poor guy from Alabama's credit card. It took about 15 minutes to get a drink and in 2.5 hours I managed to order one beer because the process was so poorly organized and aggravating (I did score a free beer from some nice guys standing at the bar - the bartender mistakenly gave them an extra one. For real). My first experience in the Barrel Room was so good that I'm sticking with 4 stars, and I hope the Loft works out its kinks!

Title: Mixed Feelings at By Chloe - New York Location

I'm a fan of By Chloe, but my latest experience at the New York branch left me with mixed feelings. Usually, a visit to By Chloe is a delicious respite from overindulgence, but this time, things didn't quite hit the mark. My order consisted of two taco salads, lemonades, and a cookie, totaling about $40 - not exactly a bargain for a supposedly lighter meal.

The taco salads were disappointing, dominated by an abundance of lettuce, which felt skimpy compared to what I've received at other locations. The seasonal mandarin lemonades were a letdown, tasting akin to canned juice, and the cookie was unfortunately dry and crumbly.

Thankfully, the lemon vinaigrette dressing on the taco salad was a highlight, giving enough flavor to carry me through the meal. On a practical note, the restaurant offers a single unisex bathroom, which is something to consider if you're planning a visit.

In summary, I give this specific By Chloe location 3 stars. While I love the brand, this particular experience didn't quite live up to my expectations.

Title: A Worthwhile Slice at Upside Pizza

If you find yourself in New York with a pizza craving, Upside Pizza offers a satisfying fix. This no-frills spot serves up pizzas that are ready to be picked from a display and quickly re-heated to perfection in their pizza oven. While it might not take the trophy for the best pizza ever, the slices here are more than decent. The combination of speed, affordability, and tasty pizza makes it a solid choice for anyone looking for a quick bite in the city.

Came here on a Wednesday night for my husbands birthday. We absolutely love Marc Forgione restaurant in TriBeCa, and wanted to try his steakhouses, he has two. The restaurant is absolutely beautiful! A stunning place to look at. It's dark, romantic, elegant, and a great place to have a date night. The chair are so nice & big, very cozy! There is no rush to leave...which I love! Because when you're spending hundreds on dinner, you want to make a night of it. The service was great, our waiter was extremely attentive & personable. The bread that they brought out was absolutely delicious, it was hard to not ask for another order! It basically melts in your mouth, and the butter makes it even better. For appetizers we had the crab cake, and my husband had Marc Forgione lobster chili, which he loves! Unfortunately I can't enjoy it because it's too spicy, but I must admit I do get jealous everything my husband has it, because it smells, and looks amazing! The crab cake was good also, the sauce on the plate went perfect with the crab. Now on to the steak, we both enjoyed the dry aged NY strip, which was absolutely delicious! I loved how the outside was so crispy but the inside was like butter! The steak was cooked to perfection, the flavors that bursted after each bite was amazing. I will definitely be back for the steak, it was probably the best steak I've had in a long time, my husband & I are huge steakhouse people, so to truly impress us takes a lot, I must say we were lost for words! The side I was impressed by, they were good, but didn't blow me away. But we weren't there for sides anyway. Of course we were extremely full but I still had to surprise my husband with a chocolate dessert, we tried to eat as much of it as possible, it was very rich, and delicious. The waiter was nice enough to give us complimentary dessert because it was my husbands birthday. Lastly the drinks are STRONG! But good!!! They might be pricey but so worth it. Overall it was a great night, definitely a place to celebrate a special occasion.

Title: A Disappointing Experience at Bubba Gump's NY

Having been to the Bubba Gump in Orlando, I had high expectations for the New York location. Unfortunately, the experience was subpar. Upon entering, the unique "run Forrest run/stop Forrest stop-signs" concept was poorly explained by the indifferent staff. 

Service was frustratingly slow – I found myself repeatedly asking for silverware as my meal cooled on the table. Unlike the friendly and efficient service in Orlando, the staff here seemed disinterested, with only a handful offering a smile.

While the food was decent, it hardly made up for the overall lackluster experience. New York is a city brimming with dining options that outshine this place in service and enthusiasm. Regrettably, a revamp seems necessary to compete. Two stars – solely for the edible meal.

I came here before the lunch rush at around 11:35am and there was already a crowd of people. Tacos are about $4. I ordered 1 carne asada and 1 pastore and 1 carne asada quesadilla. The quesadilla is just a slightly larger taco with cheese on the bottom. I was expecting it to be different. I thought it was a tad pricey per taco...until I had a bite. These are the best tacos that I've eaten on the east coast thus far. The flavors in the meat are incredible and perfectly seasoned. The toppings were generous and fresh. I opted for the corn tortillas and they were so filling. They make their tortillas fresh in house which I love.Even though the price is higher than I'd like, I am a fan and will def return! Their horchata is also really good. Not overly sweet.

Title: A Bridal Brunch to Remember

I recently hosted a bridal brunch at this charming spot, and despite an initial hiccup with my reservation date, the staff went above and beyond to accommodate my party of nine. A few kitchen mix-ups occurred, notably with the French toast, but these were swiftly resolved to our satisfaction.

Our waitress deserves special mention for her patience and exceptional service, truly enhancing our dining experience. While you should note the $25 cake cutting fee for outside desserts, it’s a minor detail considering the overall quality of the visit.

The food was generally pleasing, with the red velvet pancakes being the only letdown due to their dryness. My choice of French toast and fried chicken was delightful, and feedback on the shrimp and grits, as well as the salmon croquettes and grits, was positive.

All things considered, the brunch was a success with no significant issues, ensuring a smooth and enjoyable celebration for all attendees.

Came here because I heard the fried chicken was amazing.Obviously got the chicken and waffles and then also got the ricotta pancakes.The fried chicken was indeed good and you are allowed to add extra pieces for a little extra cost. The legs were so much better than the breast, so even this place still struggles in making every piece delicious. I loved the breading here as it wasn't too thick, but also a generous amount still. Normally I like to compare against Popeyes, and yes this is better than Popeyes.The pancakes were surprisingly good. Loved the ricotta with the pancakes, kind of feels like butter, but so much more rich.Don't think this place has too much variety though and idk how often I'd come back here, but it's good enough for me to recommend to friends if they said they wanted some fried chicken.

Okay vibes, but not sure I would visit again. The restaurant is located inside a hotel. Upon arriving, I was seated right away. I took a bit of time to review the menu because everything sounded so enticing. I ended up ordering a flight of sake, fried oysters and the spicy pork belly ramen.The sake flight was just ok, and I was severely unimpressed. This was my first time trying sake, and I'm not sure what the hype is about. Perhaps it was the kind that I tasted, but I was not impressed. The fried oysters were tasty and fried perfectly - extra points for it not being oily. However, who serves fried oysters with barbecue sauce? This was not a great combination. I didn't finish the appetizer because of the barbecue sauce. The star of the evening was the spicy pork belly ramen. The broth was hearty and had a hint of spice - nothing too overwhelming. The noodles were cooked perfectly and were not soggy.In terms of service, the waiter was not attentive. She checked in maybe one time? When I asked for a straw, she brought it back with her bare heads. This is important because the straws are unwrapped. When she noticed that I didn't put it in my drink, she brought over a wrapped straw.Overall, Shinka was just ok for me. I wouldn't visit again.

My best friend and I, both ardent aficionados of Middle Eastern cuisine, recently dined at this chic new spot in Nolita, where the setting is as you'd expect: marble tables, low lighting, and a vibe amplified by lounge music. Be warned, the prices are on the steep side - but that's Nolita for you.

The standout star of the night was, quite unexpectedly, the humble homemade PITA. Served fluffy and warm with the Arayes, this simple pleasure was the highlight and, amusingly, the most pocket-friendly item on the menu. Coupled with the TAHINI, also part of the Arayes dish, you're in for their top culinary experiences by ordering just one appetizer.

The rest of our journey through the menu was a solid four-star affair. Falafel latkes were presented with a delightful pomegranate salad, though the falafel itself didn't rise above the ordinary. As for the Arayes, I wasn't as enthused about the meat filling, but the ensemble of charred pita, tahini, and grilled tomatoes was sublime. The lamb hummus brought to mind a sort of lamb stew with carrots nestled within, surrounded by a rather dry hummus – tasty but not spectacular.

In summary, for a taste of the best this place has to offer, stick to the pita and tahini – and maybe set your budget expectations a bit higher before walking in.

Title: A Missed Goal at [Restaurant Name]

Walking into [Restaurant Name], I anticipated the usual decent pizza joint experience, but the reality was a mishmash of hits and misses. There's a palpable Italian vibe, intensified by the live projection of Italian soccer games and the authentic enthusiasm of the Italian staff and regulars, which sets the stage for an immersive dining escapade.

However, the excitement of the match seemed to sideline the service significantly. Getting the attention of the servers was a drawn-out affair, taking much gesturing and patience. When I finally managed to order, the execution fumbled. Not only did they get the order wrong, omitting a pizza, but there was also an unsettling misrepresentation.

We tasted the Parma, Ciliegino, and a mysterious red pizza dressed with mushrooms, the latter recommended as 'the most popular' choice. Yet, this particular pizza isn't listed on any menu or mentioned in reviews online, suggesting that the staff might have been playing their own game of make-believe.

While the atmosphere promises an authentic Italian experience, the slow service and questionable honesty of the staff left a bitter aftertaste that no slice of pizza could mask. [Restaurant Name] has the potential to score big, but this visit felt more like an own goal.

Came here since it seemed to be a hot spot for brunch. My extreme brunch/breakfast at Norma's (NYC Parker Meridien), only managed to get 1/4 of it down, it was so sweet.  The Chocolate Decadence French Toast, covered in Strawberries, caramel, Pistachios and Valrhona Chocolate. It was rich and sweet and made my tooth ache from the intensity of sweetness from every bite of this. It's maybe something better shared as a brunch dessert and with more than 2 people to distribute the sweetness overload. My friend got the lox & lox and bagel, piles of salmon, surrounded by cucumbers and topped with caviar. He enjoyed it, but he enjoys most any foods, even thinks Olga's is good.

I recently had the opportunity to escape the sweltering summer heat and duck into a bustling New York eatery favored by the locals. As a first-timer, the welcoming vibe was immediately palpable. Swift and proficient, the service matched the city's famous pace, ensuring a seamless experience without breaking the bank.

While my visit was brief and limited to a refreshing round of drinks, the surrounding buzz about the food left a lasting impression. Patrons praised their meals with the kind of enthusiasm that can only come from genuine satisfaction. A quick glance at the menu hinted at a promising return visit. If you find yourself yearning for a cool pause from the city's hustle, this gem is worth dropping by.

Absolutely love the food here. Carne asada burrito is where its at. Same concept like the other burrito establishments, tacos or burrito, meat, beans rice and all the fixings. The meas was well marinated, grilled to perfection, tasted so good. Guacamole was another highlight of the dinner. Seemed like it was made fresh, tasted very good. If i had to nitpick would be the price. I know its nyc. However when you have the competitors a few blocks down at slightly less, makes you kinda think about it a bit. Also seating, is extremely limited.  Its all outdoor seating. Only a small handful of people can be seated at a time.  Other than that. Place is great. Food is better.

My friend wanted to bring me here because it was an udon place instead of the usual trend of ramen. We got there for an early dinner and I was glad we did because the place is pretty small and it's obviously very popular. Udon isn't as rich as ramen so I wanted to try to get something substantial so I decided on the shrimp tempura udon. My friend also suggested the chawanmushi as a starter. I had something else in mind entirely but the mix of proteins and the pine nuts and veggies in eggs were delicious. I imagine a flan like texture but it wasn't quite as thick.My tempura udon was light, with the noodles being chewy and semi-firm. I went with the my friend's suggestion and got a poached egg which helped to add to the richness of the broth. Service is quick and attentive, I think it's team style because there was a mix of folks who came by to check on us, efficient.

Following a chilly evening stroll from a King Kong Broadway show, my brother and I stumbled upon a Japanese Ramen spot that warmed and lifted our spirits. Despite the unexpected detour, it proved to be a stroke of good fortune.

My brother, a self-proclaimed ramen aficionado, praised the authenticity of the dish, equating it to the revered bowls he'd sampled in Tokyo. The restaurant's ambiance embraced tradition, offering private ICHIRAN-style cubicles for a focused dining experience akin to those in Japan.

I opted for the large bowl to honor the traditional eating method, and while the price point was on the higher side—justifiable by its Times Square vicinity and the high-grade ingredients—the quality stood undisputed.

The service was impeccable, with servers interjecting polite Japanese phrases that augmented the authentic vibe. The experience left an impression, and I'd readily recommend this establishment to those seeking a genuine taste of Japan. Arigato Gosaymasu (thank you very much) for an unexpected culinary highlight in the heart of New York City.

Title: A Gem Amidst the Times Square Bustle

I recently dined just a stone's throw from Times Square and was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the meal at this bustling hotspot. The brief wait time of under ten minutes was a welcome start to our evening.

Our culinary journey began with beef short ribs that, while on the leaner and saltier side, were passable. However, the side salad's freshness paired with an outstanding sesame oil dressing quickly lifted the experience. The homemade gyozas stood out with their delectable flavors, and the miso soup was notably well-balanced, not falling prey to the common pitfall of over-salting.

The chicken karaage was a highlight, arriving piping hot and highlighting the succulence of the chicken thighs, complemented by a delightful spicy mayo. But the star of the show was the salmon kama – grilled flawlessly and seasoned with expertise. Additionally, the Alaska roll showcased the freshest salmon sashimi with perfectly portioned rice and roll size.

The staff provided excellent service, contributing to a seamless dining experience. At approximately $48 per person after taxes and gratuity, this restaurant offers a satisfying meal with great value, considering its prime location.

I recently visited this restaurant for a Mealpal lunch and was impressed with the efficiency of the service - my pickup was seamless and quick. The day's special included Vegetable Jalfrezi and Palak Paneer over rice. Both dishes were exceptionally flavourful, with the vegetables offering a perfect blend of spices and a desirable level of heat. The Palak Paneer was equally delightful, creamy and packed with taste. For anyone seeking a satisfying lunch, these dishes come highly recommended. Additionally, their standard choose-2 lunch deal, ranging from $9.20 to $11.04, provides great value and includes choices like roti, naan, or garlic naan. With its delicious variety, this restaurant is well worth a visit for lunch.

Title: Great Sushi, Steep Prices, and Some Concerns at Nami Nori

My recent dining experience at Nami Nori was a mixed bag. While the quality of the handrolls is undeniable, with fresh fish that sings with natural flavor, the high price point was a significant downside. Despite my love for sushi, I expect to leave a restaurant feeling satisfied, not hungry, especially after a bill exceeding $140. Unfortunately, my husband and I did not find this value here.

Pros: The California aka snow crab roll, the XO scallop, and the innovative salmon with tomato and cream onions + chives were standouts, showcasing the potential of this establishment.

Cons: However, the enjoyment was marred by inconsistent execution, such as handrolls overwhelming with wasabi and a seabass drowned in hot sauce. The lack of subtlety in these dishes detracted from the overall experience.

A point of concern was the hygiene practices, especially amid heightened health awareness. Observing staff potentially reuse handroll holders without washing them is worrying and should be addressed immediately to ensure patron safety.

In conclusion, while Nami Nori serves up some quality handrolls, the combination of high prices, a less-than-satisfying quantity, and potential hygiene issues means I'll be exploring other handroll venues in NYC that promise both quality and value.

Plaza Food Hall stands out as the premier dining destination in the vicinity, offering a plethora of options that cater to every palate. The service is remarkably swift, ensuring a minimal wait time before diving into a scrumptious meal, all while keeping your wallet at ease with its affordable pricing.

The standout for me has been Luke's Lobster where the quality of the food never falters. It's as if the freshness of the sea is wrapped in each bite, maintaining remarkable consistency in both taste and quality – a testament to their dedication to serving nothing but the finest.

However, the popularity of this place can sometimes lead to a minor inconvenience; finding a seat can be a bit of a challenge during peak hours. But this slight downside does little to detract from the overall exceptional dining experience at Plaza Food Hall.

At Chef Daniel Boulud's Boulud Sud, the essence of Mediterranean cuisine is masterfully presented, celebrating flavors from Turkey to Morocco and beyond. The dining area, with its classical decorations and soaring ceilings, provides a warm backdrop, while the semi-open kitchen adds a dash of culinary theatre.

Our recent visit was a journey of taste, starting with the tender Octopus À La Plancha and the succulent Gambas Al Ajillo. The main courses - a perfectly Seared Mediterranean Sea Bass and the exotic Egyptian Lamb Cleopatra - were rich in flavor and cooked to perfection. And for dessert, the Grapefruit Givré and Chocolate Zuppa Inglese were sublime finales.

Special commendation to Harold, our server, whose outstanding service greatly enhanced our dining experience. Boulud Sud not only excels in its culinary offerings but also shines with impeccable service.

I was pleasantly surprised by this vibrant brunch spot tucked away in Tribeca. The staff's warmth added to the welcoming atmosphere. Although the menu was concise, it didn't disappoint in delivering well-prepared dishes. My bagel topped with salmon, smashed avocado, and cream cheese was exceptionally flavorful. Meanwhile, my husband thoroughly enjoyed his burger. We also appreciated the selection of delicious craft beer. This place is a definite must-visit for a delightful brunch experience.

Title: A Succulent Feast at Ssam Bar

My boyfriend and I, along with another couple, all self-proclaimed food enthusiasts, recently visited Ssam Bar for a double date. We were all eager to sample their much-talked-about pork shoulder, which we wisely reserved in advance.

The pork shoulder did not disappoint. It was the epitome of tenderness, clearly benefiting from an overnight cure. Each bite offered the delightful contrast of sweet, salty crust against the decadent melt-in-your-mouth fat. Accompanying the meat was a variety of condiments and sides including fresh lettuce wraps, briny oysters, zesty kimchi, and a flavorful blend of scallion in garlic oil, all tied together with their signature ssam sauce. We embraced the full Ssam Bar experience by combining these elements into flavorful lettuce wraps, which were substantially sized enough to satisfy a party of six.

To finish, we indulged in the cornbread sour cream ice cream dessert. It was an interesting choice, though it left us neither overwhelmed with excitement nor underwhelmed with disappointment.

In summary, Ssam Bar delivered a meal that was worth every bite—at least where the main course was concerned—and we would heartily recommend the pork shoulder experience to any fellow culinary adventurers.

I honestly never knew there was a korean spot in Chinatown until I came upon this place.. the place was tidy and clean. The staff was very welcoming and attentive. And most importantly, the food was delicioussssssss, we wanted to try everything on the menu... Definitely recommend this place 8/10... !

Absolutely divine experience at this gem of a restaurant! The pork loin cutlet paired with prawns was a dance-inducing delight. Miso soup outshone the seafood variant, and the generous shrimp ratio was a pleasant surprise, flipping the usual batter-to-meat script. The pork cutlet's tender interior and crispy exterior, alongside a chilled Asahi, made a perfect combo. While the boyfriend enjoyed his Berkshire pork cutlet with curry, the standout was the free refills on rice and salad, ensuring a satisfying meal. Generous portions promise a return visit for those mouthwatering bites. A fantastic find that nails it on flavor and value.

I have had Pepper Lunch bookmarked for the longest time and finally got a chance to go!  There are two locations in NYC, but apparently, there are over 460 locations in 16 Countries!  Wow, who knew?!?!Pepper Lunch is a Japanese franchise, which offers a quick meal; a couple notches above fast food. Prices are a little high for this type of dining but they do not accept tips, so that helps. There is no waiter service; you peruse the menu at the register, place your order and pay for your order.  Then you are given a number on a stand to put on a table.  Seat yourself; when your food is ready, it will be brought to you.  Service is super fast since you are basically cooking your own food. There are lots of condiments on your table to choose from: soy sauce, sweet garlic soy, garlic soy, garlic, wasabi, smokey hot sauce, and salt n pepper. There are also all the utensils you may possibly need: chopsticks, forks, knives, and spoons.  Talk about thorough!  You will want for nothing!  Also, they will bring free tap water in a glass for you. On our visit, someone came quite often to refill our water glasses and to check on how we were doing.  What great service!Food: two of us dined today and we both ordered the Sambar Beef Pepper Lunch (one classic size and another Jumbo size). This is a great option if you want something spicy; albeit it really wasn't THAT spicy (hint: add some delicious smoky hot sauce). There was a significant difference in the amount of meat you get between the classic and jumbo size. So if you're really hungry, definitely go for the jumbo size. You will also want to use some of the afore mentioned condiments that are on your table. You're basically looking your own meal, so cook it to your own preference. The food will be pretty bland if you don't add "something".Warning: be careful of the sizzling hot plate that your meal comes on! There is a reason there is protective paper wrapped around the plate!All in all, this was a great, quick meal!  Service was friendly and efficient. Again, no tipping.  I look forward to a return visit to try other menu items!One last note: with your purchase, you get a scratch off ticket!  I won a free curry sauce topping to use on my next visit before 1/31/20!  Happy 2020 y'all!!

Weekends are made for brunch. Jane is a classic staple brunch spot located in Greenwich Village.  This place always seems to be packed during brunch hours so expect wait and make a reservation ahead of time. FOOD I RECOMMEND:* Jane Benedict - Very unique and delicious. Instead of using muffins, they use crab cakes.* Vanilla Bean French Toast - Phenomenal. So tender and creamy inside. Love it!* Tuna Tartare Tacos - It's sooo good and the tuna is so fresh.DRINKS:* Champagne - So refreshing. They were the first things our waiter brought to our table when we were seated, and said they're complementary after having us wait longer than expected.* Passion Fruit Screwdriver - It was flavorful and not that strong.* Caffe Latte - No complaints. It was well crafted.Overall, I had a good time here and our waiter was very efficient.

I discovered Tre back in 2013 when I stayed at a hotel on East Houston. The following year by some sort of fluke, the Air BnB I booked was next door! Needless to say I was thrilled. I love their 5-7 Happy Hour with small plates & $6 champagne (wine, beer etc). I've only been able to visit once a year & each time have had a different bar tender, but everyone has been nice & you meet interesting people sitting at their small bar which is just inside the door. The front opens to the street & yesterday it was quite warm so doors were open. I had my standard calamari happy app which is always delicious & a bit spicy. I had 2 glasses of their house champagne & then ordered their spaghetti carbonara which is to die for. They have dining tables in the back & an outdoor garden which I've never actually seen. They also do a Sunday brunch which I've heard good things about. So if you're on the Lower East Side & want a cute little Italian joint with good food & decent prices & a fab happy hour, I recommend TreMay 2019: Made it back again this year. Tre never disappoints. This time I stopped in with a local friend for Saturday happy hour. Even though the menu says happy hour starts at 5, they have us happy hour menu & prices at 4pm. I noticed the prices went up a bit from my last visit, but I was glad to have champagne & their delicious calamari again. My friend had champagne & their fried artichokes, also wonderful. We enjoyed the nice weather & open door to people watch and relax. Hope to be back next year (or before).

Title: A Slice of New York Heaven at a Bargain

If you're scouring New York City for a quintessential pizza experience, do yourself a favor and stop by this local pizza joint. Renowned for its high-quality, yet straightforward ingredients, the eatery lives up to its reputation as a city staple.

The standout for me was a classic cheese pizza – perfection in its simplicity. The dough strikes an ideal balance of texture, neither too chewy nor too crispy, practically made to be folded and devoured in true New York style. And at $3-4 per slice, it’s a steal that leaves both your stomach and wallet full.

Be warned, the lines during peak hours can stretch out the door, but don't let that deter you. The staff churn out orders with such speed and efficiency that you'll hardly notice the wait. Seating inside is sparse, so consider taking your slice to go, or better yet, grab a whole pie for your crew – it's guaranteed to delight.

In short, for an authentic taste of New York pizza without the frills or fuss, this spot is a must-visit.

I felt almost all their dishes were exceptional.  This is a very well thought take on Peruvian-Japanese Nikkei cuisine. The only miss was the aged duck nigiri which was over powered by the addition of unnecessary banana. Hamachi Tiradito with uni, coconut, matcha - fragrant and piquant, maybe my most favorite ceviche. The flavor balance is perfect!Japanese eggplant, pine nut, huacatay, fresh cheese, grape - tender with textures from smooth cheese, crisp sweet grapes, and leafy micro greensCabbage, miso, nori, anchovy, quinoa furikake, mizuna - this was lovely- they cooked the cabbage to the point it was tender but still had a bite and charred it to add smoke and complexity. It was complemented by a smooth, rich miso cream based sauce that completed the dish.  The lobster, beef heart, rice, aju panka dish featured perfectly cooked lobster and bold meaty heart. The beef heart was slightly over shadowed by the spicy dressing. It did take some of the iron-y properties provided by the offal yet was not without its own charm.Miso Banana, Oxapampa honey & white sesame dessert was ok, it took too long to reach us and was akin to banana pudding but perfectly edible.Portions were decent sized but I think we could have had one more dish between the two of us.  We chose a Chilean red wine that was minerally, dry and complex. Staff were very pleasant and service was good. Solid restaurant, we visited just a day after it opened and were impressed. Given time I can only imagine it will get even better.

Title: Delicious Eats with a Side of Service Hiccups

I recently dined at this hotspot on a bustling Saturday night with a friend. Right off the bat, the crowded scene indicated this place was in high demand. Unfortunately, the service initially mirrored the chaos—unattended at the entrance and left hanging without a wait-time estimate, we opted for the bar rather than gamble on a table.

The saving grace was, without a doubt, the food and drinks. Both were exceptional—flavorful dishes and well-crafted beverages did not disappoint. The portion sizes were generous, ensuring a bang for your buck.

A word to the wise, though—always check your to-go orders before leaving. A simple request for rice and beans on the side was overlooked, only discovered upon my return home.

While the culinary experience was a solid 4-star affair, the service missteps necessitate a notch down to 3 stars. A little more attention to diners and detail could easily elevate this experience to perfection.

Title: A Slice of France in the Meatpacking District - Pastis Review

Pastis, the reincarnation of the old favorite under the meticulous attention of restaurateur Keith McNally, is a triumph in the trendy Meatpacking District. With a vibe that effortlessly transports you to France, this brasserie excels in creating a dining experience that's hard to forget.

Service is front and center, with commendable nods to Ahn, our personable waiter whose recommendations and attentive care added to the evening's success. From the moment we started with a perfectly chilled glass of Taittinger's to the final bite of our decadent ice cream profiteroles, each detail was curated to enhance the dining experience.

The array of appetizers - from pristine oysters to a lush crabmeat and avocado salad, down to a meticulously assembled cheese plate - set a high bar that the main courses met with ease. The Trout Amandine was a study in balance, with its flaky flesh and sweetly caramelized almonds. Meanwhile, the lobster special, drenched in garlic butter and accompanied by crisp pomme frites, was the epitome of indulgence.

Even with the bustling ambiance and challenges in securing a reservation, the evening was a leisurely three-hour sojourn worth every minute and penny. Pastis is a must-visit that guarantees an exceptional meal in an atmospheric setting. Highly recommended for those seeking a quintessential French brasserie experience with all the trimmings of stellar service, ambiance, and cuisine. Dress to impress and come ready to be wowed.

Atmosphere: The Kunjip is very welcoming and seems to have enough seating available. However, the tables are pretty close together so you can hear other guests' conversations easily. Service: Staff was friendly, and our food came out in a reasonable amount of time.Food: We ordered the LA galbi and naengmyun lunch combo special. The galbi was pretty good; it was marinated well and not too chewy. The naengmyun was standard taste but was refreshing.Overall: Pretty solid Korean food at The Kunjip, but we wouldn't say that it's worth the price. We'd probably go somewhere else in KTown for Korean food.

Sustainable chic, but make it fancy and French. There you've got Le Jardinier, one of three new venues in the gorgeous 610 Lexington space. While Shun upstairs is considered the "fine dining" arm of the trio, Le Jardinier is still quite upscale, as far as Manhattan restaurants go. The space is bright and airy, with lush plants galavanting around in every direction. And yeah, I'm one of those plants-obsessed millennials, so you can bet your ass I was getting jacked up on those photosynthesis vibes, y'all. The food is delightfully consistently with the vibe here--everything is impossibly fresh, light and healthy. Though French-inspired, don't expect heavy-handedness on the butters/cheeses. You'll leave feeling uplifted and nourished, though perhaps wishing you didn't spend quite that much money. Still, Le Jardinier is an excellent, inspired addition to the Midtown East scene, excellent for a business meal or dinner with generous parents. Came here with the bf at 8:30 on a Saturday night. I virtually never dine in Midtown because a) I hate Midtown, b) Midtown restaurants tend to be overpriced and c) patrons of Midtown (especially Midtown East) restaurants are the type of folks who sit Center Court for the entirety of the US Open. In other words: I cannot relate to them nor do I particularly want to. But hey, it's nice to experience from variety sometimes and I live uptown so the trip down was an easy one. And as I mentioned, the space itself is beautiful--sleek and healthy, and only a teeny tiny bit pretentious. Le Jardinier has a big name attached to it--Alain Verzeroli, a major partner of the late Joel Robuchon. To come here is to expect top-notch technique with French flair. Robuchon was meant to be more involved with this project, but Verzeroli has carried on the legacy well. The menu is fresh, veggie-forward as the name implies, and notably gives the diner a choice between a la carte and tasting. If you're looking for a more formal Robuchon tasting menu, check out Shun upstairs. The adjectives I'm most called to use in this review are "fresh" and "clean", not just because I've been brainwashed by Outkast. The flavors are just that, and sophisticated in their construction. I'd expect nothing less.A note about drinks: we mostly stuck with cocktails for the night, but the drink menu isn't up on the Le Jardinier website. That said, if you'd like to get an idea of the mixology program, check out the Shun website and go to the menu for Bar Shun, which features many of the cocktails you'll see on the Le Jardinier menu. Standouts are the Mata Hari (Pierre Ferrand 1840 Cognac, Chai infuse Sweet Vermouth, Lemon, Rose), a vodka/watermelon spritz-style drink, and a shaken, bourbon/pink peppercorn drink. Bright and creative, excellent technique, and yes, very expensive.Before I get down to the details, two notes. One, the amuse bouche here is a turmeric/citrus drink that does its job and more. Savor it. Two, all of the bread is gluten-free (praise!). Eats, below:Summer Squash, Montauk Fluke, Lemon Verbena: A+Our palettes successfully awakened, this first dish was a beauty. Gorgeous presentation and as fresh as could be. Delicate flavors, subtle enough as to not overpower the fish. Though squash is listed as the first ingredient, this a basic crudo preparation, so don't be deceived by the order. Melon, Burrata, Figs, Maracona Almonds: AOne of the heavier appetizers (relatively). As far as burrata dishes go, this is easily the lightest one I've ever tried. We expected something richer. Still, the flavors were delightful and as expected at this point, the produce was as fresh as it gets. And honestly, I'm grateful it didn't weigh us down, as we still needed to prepare for our larger plates. Make sure to get a complete bite with a piece of fresh fig. Doesn't get much more decadent than that.Zucchini, Chanterelles, Romesco Coulis, Almonds: AAnother stunner on the plate, and equally tasty. The bf was blown away after popping a teensy tomato half in his mouth. Thoughtful in design, concept, execution. The romesco coulis was just perfect, dolloped with razor-sharp precision.Ora King Salmon, Ginger, Walla Walla Onions, Mushroom Bouillon: A-/AWe were so excited by our trio of starters that the salmon seemed a bit boring in comparison. Yet I still can't really complain about this dish. The salmon was cooked perfectly and the broth was both light and rich, adding some umami to the flavor profile. Though there were only a few, the onions were just outstanding. Don't think outstanding is an adjective appropriately applied to onions? Try these.Bavette Au Jus, Turnip, Horseradish, Broccolini: A+Though pricey for the amount of food you're getting here, the flavors are impeccable. A sophisticated, elegant, masterful steak preparation. Go with the medium rare recommendation. The turnip puree and horseradish seemed obvious accompaniments, providing earthiness and complexity to the dish, rounding it out perfectly.

Seamore's is okay; not a place I would return to unless I simply wanted the oysters happy hour. While the food was nothing special, I actually really love the set up, the space, and the overall vibe of the place. It's warm and fun, and is the perfectttt lunch spot (again, only if the food was better!) Seating is a bit tight, but we're in NYC, so I'm probably going to be more shocked if I can actually stand up without knocking over someone's utensils on my way out.Oysters: fresshhhhhhhClams Linguine: not much flavor? I liked the clams and the garnishes, but didn't taste how this dish could be set apart from another restaurant. Smallish portion, not suitable for sharingReel Deal: presentation wise, didn't look very appetizing (especially the sauce) but the fish was very moist. Again, not much flavor

Relatively famous dumpling spot with a hole in the wall vibe. Came here early around 9:30 am (Yelp's hours are correct but google's are not). Service was super fast and the food was made right in front of us quickly. There's a $15 minimum for credit card and the Atm machine outside didn't work for me so we ended up ordering a bunch of food. Got two orders of their pork dumplings in soup (one with cabbage and one with chives). Both are supe good. We also got the shrimp boiled dumplings on a plate (no soup) and they were still super moist and delicious. Soup itself is delicious too (has bok Choy in it). Prices can't be beat (we were struggling just to reach the $15 minimum)! Definitely would come back for a quick bite :)

Title: A Culinary Cornucopia at the Local Market

If you're in the mood for a gastronomic adventure, look no further than this bustling market that's a treasure trove for food enthusiasts. With an impressive array of stands, you can indulge in an eclectic mix of flavors, from enormous pans of savory paella to the freshest fish and seafood.

Treat your taste buds to a variety of sandwiches, fine cured meats, artisanal cheeses, and freshly baked bread. Satisfy your sweet tooth with a selection of pastries, empanadas, and crisp churros or cool down with some artisanal ice cream. For those craving something hearty, the market offers perfectly spicy patatas bravas, delightful flatbreads, and a tapas bar brimming with small plate wonders.

To wash it all down, there are two cocktail bars and a sophisticated wine bar, ensuring that you find the perfect pairing for your meal. When you want to elevate your experience, choose from one of the three sit-down restaurants, each offering a unique and relaxed dining ambiance.

Beyond food, the market features a charming gift shop, floral delights, and a retail shop to browse through. This is more than just a place to eat; it's a vibrant spot to wander, sample, and savor the best of local cuisine. Whether you're a seasoned foodie or just looking for an enjoyable outing, this market is a must-visit. Don't miss the chance to dive into this culinary wonderland!

Title: Mixed Feelings at STK During NYC Restaurant Week

I ventured into STK for a taste of the NYC Restaurant Week offerings, hoping for an exceptional dining experience. Despite running late, my party was accommodated fairly quickly, within 15 minutes of my arrival. The evening started off on a less than pleasant note with a sneeze-related mishap involving the hostess and my punctual dining companion. 

We dove into the $42 dinner special, adding the $29 wine and champagne pairing to elevate the meal. The initial garlic and chive bread was unremarkable, not particularly to my liking. My choice of ribs as an appetizer was a highlight, but the main event, a steak, fell short of expectations at a place with STK's namesake. The meat was tougher than preferred, and even a requested steak sauce to rescue the dish had a surprising $2 charge attached.

The shared mac and cheese side was just average, hardly justifying its price tag, and the warm cookie dessert was regrettably neither warm nor indulgent. On the positive side, the staff was attentive and the ambiance energetic, though the volume of the music made it less suitable for intimate conversations.

In summary, while I'm glad to have seized the opportunity to partake in Restaurant Week, I'm not enticed to return to STK for seconds. The quality of the food didn't match up with the cost, and although the service was commendable, it simply wasn't enough to offset the culinary disappointments.

I would like to try this place one more time to write a proper nice review. We actually went with a group of 10 people so didn't get much detail idea on the vegetarian dry pot. The spice levels were on point and if they aren't then with chili oil it does hit the right spot! We ordered 3 pots with 12 ingredients between 10 people. The vegetarian pot had I think everything vegetarian from the menu and was delicious. We ordered bok choy, tofu, noodles, zucchini, lotus root, mushrooms and more but I don't remember everything. Also they do have an option for white rice or purple rice. I loved the purple rice and would definitely try white rice next time!

Sunday brunch!Pros:Great food, great ambiance, great service! And great olive oil. They way they serve the bread is brilliant. The olive oil and fresh herb leaves makes a piece of art. For starters, I highly recommend the grilled octopus. Doesn't get better than that! For main, I recommend the lamb chop. Perfectly cooked: Crispy on the outside yet tender and juicy inside. I also recommend trying their fish as well. Be aware that they serve the whole fish, with fish head. It's totally fine with me but you may want to think twice, in case this is out of your comfort zone.Cons:I wish there are some greens coming with the lamb chop instead of fries. The fries are ok but not blowing me away or anything.

I tried this place out today, the hot soup hit the spot on a cold day. I ordered pork belly bun and lamb noodle soup. The broth was very tasty, it had a slight flavor of chinese 5 spice. The lamb was pretty good, nice and tender and they were generous with the noodles. The pork belly bun was nice and tender and juicy with a yummy peanut flavor and a slight flavor of cilantro. If am in the area i will go again.

I ate three-quarters of a small pie just​ minutes before around the corner at Rubirosa. I was full. When I turned the corner​ and saw the line in front of Prince Street Pizza, I knew I had to experience the much-hyped, and highly lauded "Spicy Spring" their take on sheet pan pepperoni pizza.Damn, that mother jumper of a slice was freaking delicious​. This is how pepperoni pizza is done, ​people.There so much pepperoni piled onto the thing it's impossible to eat without pepperoni slices falling on your lap (lean over when you eat it and spread your legs if you're not sitting at a table to prevent a greasy mess on your lap.) Many of those slightly charred and cupped pepperoni slices have a little pool of tasty fat in them, and they're pleasantly chewy, and just a little spicy.The slice is thick, but it's light, it's not heavy, and the bottom and end crusts are crisp. It has just enough cheese and sauce.I've never had a better pepperoni slice. Pepperoni lovers rejoice, the Spicy Spring is your jam.EDIT: Okay, it's not pepperoni, but is supposedly spicy soppressata. It doesn't​ matter, that's semantics.

Wow. First time ever having deep dish and this exceeded every expectation I had. This is a quaint little pizza place with very old school vibes. The bar tender was really good too! We got the pineapple and ham deep dish pizza which was delicious. We're only here for the weekend so I doubt we'll be back anytime soon but we will be sure to stop by here any time we are in NYC.

What a homey place!The staff was two workers but they were extremely kind and welcomed us warmly. Despite being a weekday and the store being located pretty far away from other food places, the tiny store was semi packed! I ordered the dry Tofu Rice Noodle ($11) and my friend ordered the Cold Chicken Rice Noodle ($11). You pay upfront. The water is self serve.My dish came all beautifully presented. After being informed by the worker that the messier, the better, I mixed those noodles real good! With all the flavors of the sauce and minced meat and chives in that dish absorbing into the noodle, you best believe those noodles were delicious! The noodles alone were also soft and bouncy! Everything was super flavorful, but after eating for a while, the dish soon got too salty for me. I think my friend had better luck with her sour but less salty cold chicken dish. Great friendly place! We chilled there for pretty long after our meal and did not feel rushed to leave. I loved the vibes here and would love to go back next time I crave noodles again!

I had the pleasure of trying the eggplant and string bean lunch special at this charming eatery. The dish, delightfully coated in a basil garlic sauce with a teriyaki twist, was delectable. Accompanied by nutty brown rice, a crispy spring roll, a sweet pumpkin wedge, and a fresh green salad with a savory miso dressing, the meal was an absolute triumph. Everything was superb and I can't recommend it enough.

This place is pretty good. It is a little expensive for what it is. The food is okay. It is pretty generic brunch food that doesn't blow your mind, but it's decent. The flavors are relatively average, nothing is spiced super fantastically or use some cheese that really gives makes the dish go the extra mile. Their bottomless deal is a little on the pricer side, but they really do mean bottomless. They are really good about making sure that the carafe at your table is never empty. The staff is really great. I came here with my suitcase right before flying out and they were super nice about it and helped me figure out the best place to store it. The atmosphere is great. It is loud but not too loud. The decor of the restaurant is chic but not trying too hard. They also didn't have nearly the wait that some of the other places had which was a huge plus especially when you are on a time schedule.

Tucked away in the bustling city, this eatery proves to be a delightful spot for a lunch break. Although the menu may not boast an extensive list of options, the quality of their offerings more than compensates for the variety. The chicken quesadillas stood out, with a perfectly crisp tortilla embracing well-seasoned chicken, though the accompanying salsa might startle those sensitive to a strong lime presence. The guacamole, however, was a sheer delight. The Kobe beef sliders also deserve a mention for their juicy goodness, cooked to a lovely degree of doneness.
