Service was a highlight, with our waiter's friendliness adding to the positive experience. An ideal venue for sipping on drinks and nibbling on satisfying finger foods.

I recently visited an amazing restaurant that serves authentic Chinese cuisine, complemented by friendly service. Despite the chill of a freezing Saturday night, the warmth of the venue was undeniable. Opting for the big plate chicken, noodle, and cucumber salad, the two of us found the portions generous and satisfying. The standout was undeniably the big plate chicken – a mouthwatering combination of braised chicken, potatoes, peppers, and noodles, all brought together by a rich, flavorful sauce.

The restaurant had a good number of patrons, yet it wasn't overcrowded, creating a cozy atmosphere. The serving staff were not just efficient but exceptionally cordial, adding to the overall positive experience. The cherry on top was the 20% off Yelp check-in deal – a steal that only heightened my satisfaction.

Eager to explore more of their menu, particularly the barbecue, I am already planning my next visit. This place is a must-try for anyone seeking a taste of authentic Chinese food with ample portions and at great value.

I came here for dinner completely last minute. I always thought of this place as being a little too bro-y (which it is), but the food made it worth it. GET THE BUFFALO CHICKEN MAC. YOU WONT REGRET IT. I was so stuffed after sharing it as an appetizer I could barely eat the other food we ordered. The fried chicken is really good. You get two large pieces and both bbq sauce and ranch for dipping. The Caesar salad was okay and the salmon I added to it was fresh and delicious. Also, the shrimp were good and I loved the toasted bread it came with for dipping. Surprisingly a really good food spot!

I came here for the Under 30 lunch and it was one of the best meals I've ever had. I believe you can email the restaurant to be notified the next time they have this event (would highly recommend). Seating: You have the choice between sitting in the main dining room and lounge. We sat in the lounge but the seating was a bit low for my 6'0+ boyfriend and I noticed someone at the other table also hunched over his meal, so I would only recommend it if you're not too tall. That being said, we had perfect lounge seats right in front of a large window. ***Vegetarian ReviewI'm a particularly picky eater, but I enjoyed everything that I had during the lunch. Everything was flavored perfectly and had such a unique taste. It seems like a lot of money to pay for courses of vegetables, but I've never tasted vegetarian food like this elsewhere. I actually enjoyed the food here more than the vegetarian courses at EMP since I found that you could really taste all the individual ingredients here. The courses were refreshing and light so I managed to finish almost everything, even though I was struggling at the end. My boyfriend was just as full so I think there would be plenty of food for most. The usual tasting menu also comes with more courses if this is a concern.The service was amazing as would be expected from a restaurant of this caliber. The water cups were never empty and everything was served promptly. Thomas Keller himself also came around to greet each of the tables. We unfortunately weren't able to get a picture since everyone in the restaurant was trying to take a picture with him.I would definitely recommend visiting Per Se, especially emailing the restaurant to get notified for the next Under 30 lunch. I found myself nonstop smiling after the meal. Next stop, the French Laundry!

The wait at Pho Bar was too long so my friends and I decided to come here instead.Service was quick but I felt that the dishes were overpriced. I got the "Little Pot" which was chicken broth with noodles and minced pork. There was barely any meat and zero veggies, yet it was $14..almost the same price as a huge bowl of pho with a huge short rib bone and meat elsewhere. We also asked for tea which they didn't serve. We tried a few small dishes, the cold wood ear and crispy pork, both were fine, but nothing to brag about. There are so many places around here so I don't think I had a compelling enough experience to come back.

Looking for a top-notch late-night bite, my friends and I hit up this spot around 12:30 AM on a Saturday and were not disappointed. With an extensive pizza selection and a decent array of beer, it catered perfectly to our diverse tastes. Despite the limited seating, we managed to snag a spot to enjoy our feast. I sampled a variety of slices thanks to my pals, each more delicious than the last, without breaking the bank. The service was surprisingly quick, making it an even better experience. Definitely recommended for that late-night pizza craving!

Title: Cozy Atmosphere, Average Fare – An Office Sendoff at [Restaurant Name]

My colleagues and I chose [Restaurant Name] for a Tuesday dinner sendoff, and our experience was a mix of hits and misses. We managed to secure a table for five without a prior reservation, which was a pleasant surprise.

Ambiance-wise, the restaurant delivers. It's a pretty spot with a welcoming vibe, perfect for catching up with friends or saying farewell to a coworker. As we settled in, we shared a bottle of wine, which, while enjoyable, seemed overpriced for what it was. The quality did not quite match up to its cost.

For the main course, I opted for the hand-cut rigatoni with meat sauce and octopus. The dish was satisfactory but lacked that exceptional quality one hopes for when dining out, especially considering the menu's higher price point.

In summary, if you're after a venue with a lovely atmosphere for social occasions, [Restaurant Name] fits the bill. But if your priority is culinary excellence that leaves a lasting impression, you might want to explore other options.

This is an awesome place to go out with friends for drinks and food. The ambiance is great and there's a live DJ so if you're looking for something quiet this isn't the place to be. My friends and I had the chipotle guacamole which was great and the portion was good enough for 4 people. The Asada tacos were okay, but they could've used more flavor. We got there at around 5:30 on a Thursday and there weren't many people at first but it was packed by 6:30. Drinks are $8 during happy hour but must be purchased at the bar to get the deal.

Mao's Bao are pretty and colorful. The pork baos were my favorite. The balance of skin to meat ratio was good. They were great with the hot sauce. I liked that they were small and I could try four for $10. It was surprisingly filling. The girls working were very friendly and helpful.

I absolutely adore this gem in Manhattan Chinatown – a haven for dim sum enthusiasts seeking authenticity. Enormous in size, Jing Fong impresses with its high-quality, delectable offerings that are kind on the wallet too. A paradise for the famished, embarking on a dim sum feast here is best enjoyed with a crowd, allowing you to indulge in a wider selection. For solo diners or parties of three or fewer, expect communal seating, which might just lead to new friendships. A bonus for the curious and food lovers, Jing Fong's Instagram provides a tantalizing peek into the kitchen, where master chefs craft dumplings with mesmerizing speed and skill. It's a visual feast not to be missed.

Small spot for Mediterranean tapas. A couple of complimentary breads, but none were amazing. They came with butter and great jelly however. I got the hummus and chicken. The chicken (and especially the yogurt that came with it) was great, but the hummus was only fair. Great service. My GF and I sat by the door and it was very cold.  7.75/10

Title: A Seafood Gem in NY

I recently savored an exceptional dining experience at one of New York's premier seafood destinations. The restaurant boasts quality food matched with equally impressive service, making it a standout eatery. The protected outdoor seating is a delightful choice at any hour.

Though oysters aren't typically to my liking, I sampled one from their extensive selection and found it incredibly fresh. Appetizer highlights included the cod and crab cakes, both of which disappeared swiftly from our table due to their delectable taste. Additionally, the warm octopus salad was a tasty and healthier alternative to fried options.

The miso-glazed sea bass stood out among entrées, striking a beautiful balance with its seasoning, although I would have preferred more string beans in place of the kimchi. The truffle crusted cod was a symphony of flavors, especially with the hen of the woods mushroom, though an extra ravioli wouldn't have gone amiss.

Dessert was a triumph, particularly the caramelized mango tart, with its blend of mascarpone and macadamia ice cream. For those favoring coconut, the coconut pannacotta was a flavor bomb, and the warm apple tart remained a comforting classic.

In summary, this is a restaurant that leaves you yearning for just one more bite of its culinary excellence.

Title: A Refreshing Twist on Brunch at a Health-Conscious Haven 

My recent brunch experience at this charming Upper West Side gem offered a delightful departure from my usual indulgent weekend fare. The restaurant prides itself on crafting delicious, healthy options, and it certainly delivered.

We started with coffee, which was rich and aromatic, setting the tone for the meal ahead. My companion chose the avocado toast—a visually stunning and tasteful dish that seemed to please both the palate and the eyes. My order of shakshuka arrived in an artistically heavy bowl, enhancing the overall enjoyment of the dish. The flavors were spot-on, suggesting that wholesome ingredients can indeed lead to a satisfying meal.

While my cravings typically lean towards the classic, heavier brunch choices, this experience was a welcome change. It's a spot worth revisiting with the expectation of savoring well-prepared food that nourishes the body and soul. Just remember, if you're in the mood for traditional greasy spoon fare, adjust your expectations and prepare to be pleasantly surprised by the lighter, yet equally tantalizing, offerings.

Good and relaxing place to enjoy some good food and drinks, the two young ladies who attended to my orders were very professional, nice and greeted me with a warm smile. I almost lost track of time, as I just enjoyed being there, sipping on my Ketel One Vodka and devouring the food. Also, while being there, I discovered that Ketel One has botanical flavors now  Shows that I'm not much of an astute drinker...lol. I tries the cucumber mint, grapefruit and peach (separately of course). Funny thing, both the young ladies working there were surprised that I drink my vodka with pineapple juice, had them giggling and smiling as their eyes lit up in amazement. One of them said that she would actually give it a try, to see if she likes it. Again great place, staff, food and atmosphere. Highly recommended

I visited this restaurant for a weekday lunch with a reservation in hand, intrigued by their variety of Thali offerings. The menu cleverly categorized Thalis into Vegi, Chicken, and Goat Lamb, with ample selections within each. The concept is straightforward: pick your main entrée and enjoy a predetermined set of accompaniments.

I sampled two Thalis – the Non-veg featuring a Goat Lamb curry, and the Vegi with Malai Kofta. Both dishes were, regrettably, quite mundane. Accompanying items such as Dal, Saag, Potato curry, and a dessert of Kheer mirrored the entrees in their mediocrity – traditional flavors that failed to transcend the ordinary.

The restaurant strikes me as a decent spot for those seeking the comfort of a no-frills, homestyle Indian meal, yet it's not a place I'd recommend for culinary adventurers. A solid 3-star experience for its execution of the basics, but it falls short in leaving a memorable impression.

Sugarfish undeniably offers one of the best omakase options in NYC. Not only do you get great value/quality for the price you pay, gratuity is also included in the price advertised on the menu. There are 4 different omakase options ranging from $33-$63. I personally think the $45 Nokzawa is the perfect amount and selection. Each plate is served as soon as it's prepared and the rice that's served on the sushi is always loosely packed and always served warm. I believe all these little things paired with fair prices is what makes SUGARFISH very popular.  With that said, reservations are not an option and wait times cant be up to 2 hours long. I highly advise to come during off hours. (Bet lunch and dinner).Beer, sake, and wine are available. I highly recommend the nigori (unfiltered sake) for those that enjoy sweet/chilled milky sake. Cheers!EXTRA EXTRA:*Free street parking available after 7pm. *Servers politely decline any requests for additional sauces, rice, or salt.

Came to the soho Boqueria after going to the one in UES. Overall, I think it's a great tapas option, and I liked this location a little bit better.We can here as a large group (10+ people) for the unlimited brunch ($39 bottomless). They give the table a sheet of paper where everyone collectively decided what to order, and they portion out enough for everyone. They were super accommodating of vegetarians when I went, and gave us the option to pick a few veggie items to replace the meat ones and adjusted the portions for everything accordingly.Their brunch paella is amazing (albeit a little on the dry side). We got the churro ice cream for dessert, which was a riot! I had the red wine sangria, and they were very attentive on refilling everyone's drinks / making sure our group of 10+ were comfortableOverall: would recommend for a group (as tapas should be eaten), and would certainly recommend for a birthday celebration

Title: Lovely Brunch Experience at Balthazar

I recently enjoyed a delightful brunch with a group of seven friends at the iconic Balthazar. Thanks to our advance reservation, we were seated promptly upon arrival. The service was commendable throughout our meal, attending to our large group with efficiency and care.

I indulged in the cheeseburger, priced at $23, which was substantial in size and accompanied by a serving of fries. Our table also shared the well-known bread basket for $24, an assortment of delectable breads and pastries that included the likes of monkey bread, a flaky croissant, and a rich pain au chocolat.

While the prices were on the higher side, the overall experience of brunch at Balthazar was thoroughly enjoyable and met the expectations for such a reputable establishment.

Title: Packed with Flavor and Fun Even on a Rainy Night!

My Friday night at this bustling spot was nothing short of awesome, despite the weather trying to dampen the mood. The foresight to have a waitlist that texts you when your table is ready is a godsend, allowing some nearby bar-hopping while waiting. Once seated, I dove straight into the kimchi udon – a dish that hit all the right notes, although I wished for more than the scant two pieces of shrimp it came with.

We didn't stop there, indulging in some scrumptious takoyaki and a flavorful omu soba, both of which were delightful. To top it all off, the frozen beer added a cool twist to the meal. Amidst the packed venue, the service shone bright with efficiency, and our food arrived surprisingly quickly. I definitely recommend checking this place out for a vibrant dining experience that doesn’t compromise on service or taste!

Title: Hidden Gem on the Upper West Side

During a recent day trip to NYC, my wife and I, hungry and wandering the Upper West Side, discovered a delightful culinary retreat nestled among a row of eateries. Opting for convenience over a trek to Chinatown, we were enticed by the extensive offerings of this Asian fusion restaurant, boasting everything from cold dishes and hot pots to sushi – all reasonably priced, with most items ranging from $15-$18.

I indulged in the duck nebeyaki udon, a harmony of udon noodles, fresh scallions, and a medley of vegetables in a savory broth that was nothing short of delicious. My wife’s choice, the soba noodle hot pot with duck, struck an exquisite balance with its side of cold noodles, providing a welcome contrast to the warmth of the broth.

The intimate setting with thoughtful table arrangements for couples and groups complemented the dining experience. The staff's welcoming greeting upon arrival, though indecipherable to us, was a charming touch that added to the hospitable ambiance.

Stumbling upon this establishment was a stroke of luck. Given the quality of our meals and the overall experience, this restaurant is a must-visit on the Upper West Side. We're already looking forward to our next visit to explore more of their culinary delights. Highly recommended!

Title: Disappointing Experience Despite Friendly Hostess

I had high hopes for this restaurant, especially on a festive day like Christmas, but was met with disappointment. Our reservation for 10 was honored, which was a relief given our plans to attend the noon show of the Big Apple Circus. The hostess greeted us with a warmth that promised a delightful meal, but that's where the positives ended.

The service system seemed straightforward—order with the waiter, food is brought by runners—but the execution was flawed. After being seated, we never received our initial order of coffee, juice, and egg creams; it appeared the staff had a strict division of tasks, and no one but our waiter could fulfill our drink request.

Our "friendly" waiter was, regrettably, neither attentive nor efficient. We received our food and drinks an hour later at 11 am, and while the pancakes, omelets, and bagel were quite good, the service dampened the experience. We repeatedly had to ask for basic condiments and refills, which proved to be a challenge each time.

In summary, despite a warm welcome, the service was a letdown. The staff's rigid adherence to their roles over customer service was baffling. Regrettably, this is a place I would not revisit.

Started out at the bar for happy hour, there's not a ton of space, and it took forever to get the attention of the bartender (poor guy was overwhelmed) whenever we were ready for another round, but the cocktails were sweet and delicious. Note that you do need to close out your tab before moving on to dinner.1-Thyme: Soju, St. Germaine, thyme-infused syrup, grapefruit juice - may be showing my age, but is this a nod to the old school hip hop group 1TYM? If so, I'm a fan. This was sweet and fruity, and didn't taste alcoholic at all, but remember - soju creeps up on you.Dinner service was much better. I had made a reservation, so to the joy of one of my girlfriend's, she got to spin the wheel and won us an order of  free croquettes.Truffle fries - I will never say no to fries, these were hot crispy, but light on the truffle flavor. croquettes - pretty standard, but perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery inside - also something I never say no to.tteok & cheese: rice gnocchi, sweet corn, quinoa, fontina, cheddar,parmesan cheese, truffle essence, garlic bruschetta - it's sort of a fusion of italian/korean/murica, like a delicious fancy mac & cheese, but with pillowy nuggets of gnocchi.tuna mayo tartare: tuna, pickled radish, chives, mayonnaise,sesame oil, garlic bruschetta with honey drizzle - this was a sleeper hit, initially my companions were not impressed with the appearance, but soon they were fighting for the last biteUni Bibim Paella: rice on a sizzling hot stone plate topped with uni,cured shrimp, capelin roe, pickled radish, kimchi,quinoa, egg and seaweed puree - this is DELICIOUS! the texture variations! the contrast between creamy uni and tart kimchi - if only the dish was larger.We also had garlic shrimp tacos, bulgogi steamed buns and duck steamed buns - all on point and satisfactory.The only disappointment was the Chef Jin's Egg Souffle: egg, topped with quinoa, chive, 3 different types of roe, which wasn't bad by any means, it just wasn't at all memorable. This is a decent place for catch up dinners over korean tapas, and they also do korean bbq, but I'd probably skip the happy hour next time. Reservations are easy to make and the tables upstairs do give you ample space to chat with your friends. Solid choice for casual dinners.

Came here a Friday night with my man we were coming from Johnny Utah and didn't want to go home yet. Place has a dark decor, we were greeted & seated quickly. We only stated for an hour and enjoyed the hookah.They have some hookah special only for happy hour I guess. The regular hookah is expensive! But everything in New York is smh. We have a good time, id def come back.

Title: A Slice of New York Perfection at Prince Street Pizza

If you're on the hunt for an authentic New York pizza experience, Prince Street Pizza is a must-visit. Their pepperoni slice is legendary, with a distinct quality that sets it apart from the rest – a true hallmark of pizza artistry. The margherita slice, which I sampled with an additional request for extra sauce, was equally impressive and stood out without the alteration; it simply didn't need any tweaks to shine. Beyond the fantastic food, the locale itself is nestled in a picturesque neighborhood that's perfect for tourists or locals in search of a leisurely shopping day. Prince Street Pizza doesn't just serve pizza; it delivers an experience steeped in New York charm.

Title: Farewell to Joe's on St. Marks

I typically reserve my restaurant reviews for operational eateries, but after Joe's abrupt closure, I felt compelled to share my thoughts. The culinary prelude to my disappointment began with an unexpected shuttering on my first visit, an omen for the closure that would follow just six months post-opening.

While some critics have noted the rolls were underwhelming in taste, I found the $4 price point to be the silver lining, making up for any lack of inherent flavor. A liberal dose of soy sauce and chili paste was all it took for Joe's to satisfy my rice roll cravings at their conveniently situated St. Marks spot.

In the end, it's trust issues I'm grappling with, having been let down twice by Joe's closed doors. It's a shame their journey was so fleeting.

I recently visited the new dim sum restaurant across from Golden Unicorn, and I must say, it was a delightful experience without the usually long wait. They serve all the classic dim sum favorites – from siu mai to steamed buns, to a comforting bowl of congee – at reasonable prices. The service was attentive with the cart ladies coming around often, and the wait staff were diligent in keeping our tea and iced water full. The food was executed beautifully, and I left with no complaints whatsoever. Highly recommend for a no-fuss, delicious dim sum meal.

Ok There is a reason there is a line out the door!Dam good pizza is waiting for you.We hit this place on Sunday at about 1pmLine was to the shop Nextdoor (electric motorcycle)That was about 30 minute to get our pizza.So do t worry about the wait it is worth it!I would highly recommend this place.

In the city? After hours? Super late after the club? Go here. It's just Chinese food but it's good. They're always open and it's right by soho. I almost ALWAYS stop here if I'm out late in the city before going home. My friends and I love this place. Go for it go for it

I took my mom and sister here during their visit to Manhattan as we were craving some Taiwanese beef noodle soup and were already in the area.  My friend had actually mentioned this place a few times, and I was excited to try it.  It's tucked away on a small side street, pedestrian only, and has that same typical small Chinatown feel - don't expect fancy.  Things we tried included:Stuffed lotus root (slightly sweet) AppetizerPROS:- good for sharing between two to three people, just for a taste- not ridiculously sweet but definitely on the sweeter end for an appetizer- lotus root was relatively crunchy, not overcookedCONS:- somewhat simple, not necessarily a bad thing but not what I expectedSeaweed and preserved tofu (appetizer):PROS: - shareable between two people, would need more than one for 3+- not overly powerful (I have a feeling five-spice was used which can be overwhelming if too much is used)- comes out COLD (just an FYI, not a pro)CONS:- none: it's a very typical standard cold dish appetizer.  I feel that if you're Asian, most likely you've had something similar.  If not, it can be an interesting experience.  I can't even describe it as a "cooked salad" which would be the closest thing.  A non-sour but pickled appetizer?Beef Noodle SoupPROS:- definitely shareable between two or more people if other dishes are ordered- came out hotCONS:- not my favorite in terms of other places I've had this in the city.- meat was not tender, very chewy- slightly on the saltier end for the broth- imbalance: way too much noodle compared to the rest of the other ingredients.Shaved Ice (Customized): herbal jelly, corn, and aiyu jellyPROS:- customizable!- I love jelly so this really made my day- not too sweet!CONS:- not too much of a con but if the ice-shaver would make fine shaved ice, that would really take it up a notch.I'd still come back though to try the porkchop fried rice.  Somehow fried things always seem to go down a little better.  We did also have tea-eggs and those were pretty spot on.  It wasn't terrible, but it wasn't that great either.  Will re-review if I get a better meal with different food next time!

Way back when, a friend of mine said that he didn't understand why anyone would want to return to a restaurant when there are so many (newer, and not even necessarily better) choices in NYC. I concurred at the time as I was relatively new to the City, but since then I've come to realize that a handful of restaurants, with one or two dishes having made a lasting impression, relentlessly tempt me go to back. And I do end up giving in to the temptation! Tuome is the kind of restaurant that I'd happily return to despite the endless options in NYC. I've been here 2-3 times in the past year and it has delivered consistently. My favorites are the chicken liver, octopus, and snow crab. Normally I wouldn't order chicken liver because of the chalky texture but Tuome's smooth, silky mousse is irresistable. I always order octopus when it's offered as an appetizer whilst dining out, but never have I ever had it served with xo sauce, an asian element to this dish that I highly appreciated. The snow crab noodle with dashi butter is relatively heavy but simply too delicious to resist. For some reason it always reminds me of carbonara but far superior. Beignet was the one dish that I underestimated. When it was first presented to me I chuckled and said, "Oh, mantou, prolly not as good as my mom's." I was wrong (sorry mom). It's perfectly crispy on the outside and tender but not too moist on the inside.I was very happy to see that it was awarded a Michelin star this year. Totally called it.

Despite its limited menu, this establishment truly excels at every dish they serve. My recent experience was delightful, with the exception of their pho missing a key ingredient - jalapeño peppers, which I find essential for that extra kick. While the chef does accommodate requests for super-hot Thai chilis, it's not quite the same and seems to be provided somewhat reluctantly. The quality of the food has tempted me to try nearly the entire menu, save for the tomahawk steak priced at $120. It's difficult to justify such an expense for a steak in a casual setting lacking the ambiance of a traditional steakhouse, complete with tablecloths and an extensive wine list. Perhaps it's my own bias, but that level of investment demands a more refined dining environment.

Was skeptical about an outpost of the amazing original West Village location, but was craving it and liked the expanded menu. The burger came out perfect, just like downtown. The loaded tots were also great. Best part was the great service. Incredibly welcoming and accommodating. Very different vibe than downtown where you wait on line and sort of get what you get...

If there's a whole building full of Job Advisors, then it's a Korea House. This is not that. This is just a stall in a market that makes f***ing good food.I had the soft tofu soup about two weeks after they first opened on the first trip that I made here. I've since been back three or four times but haven't eaten at this stand since then - even though I enjoyed it a lot the first time.I'll definitely be eating here again soon though. It's a little high in the price department which is why I don't give it five stars and it wasn't the best I've ever had - but it was pretty damn good. I just wish that it was under $10 like a lot of the stands inside the H Mart and whatever - but it's still a fantastic food court and I like all the stands in here and they're mostly Korean and stuff.

Tucked away in the upper west side of New York, this little gem offers a taste of authentic Mexican cuisine at an affordable price. It's a regular spot for me, largely due to the Chile toreados, a must-try for spicy food aficionados. The drinks, be it Margaritas or Mescalitas, are generous and bursting with flavor. The ambiance is casual, with a friendly vibe that may just have you chatting with your neighboring diners. Highly recommended for a delightful dining experience.

Arrived for a late lunch in the middle of the afternoon and the place was pretty quiet. We were seated quickly and our server came over and introduced herself pretty quickly and was attentive throughout our lunch.The menu is pretty unique and extensive with a great range of comfort foods and some pretty amazing looking milkshakes. We got cheese curds to start which were delicious and came with a nicely spiced dipping sauce, a Veggie burger with amazing crunchy curly fries and a Breakfast Pancake Burrito, which was eggs, cheese and bacon wrapped in pancakes and covered in maple syrup...WOW!On top of the amazing food and milkshakes, they have a great list of local and domestic beers.Will definitely be coming back here the next time I'm in town!

Hunan Slurp is just one of the many somewhat overpriced, trendy Chinese spots to have popped up in the city (especially the East Village/St Marks area). Part of me thinks it's weird to be paying $20+ for the same dish I've had sitting on a stool in a hole-in-the-wall in actual Hunan province for $3, but the other part of me is happy that Chinese regional cuisines are finally breaking out of the stereotype of being a lesser Asian cuisine (i.e. how Chinese cuisine is "supposed" to be cheap to be authentic but the same isn't applied to Japanese, etc.)That being said, Hunan Slurp is a very cute place for a casual dinner between friends or for a chill date night. The dishes are a little on the pricier side and some dishes are more generously portioned than others. I was hoping to try the stir-fried frog legs, but they had run out that day (went around 7pm on a Saturday, had reservations). My fiancé and I shared the Hometown Lu Fen (one of their signature dishes), Hunan Charcuterie (beef shank, tripe, pig's ear, and pig's tongue), and Hunan Salad. The lu fen was pretty good, but nothing that special. I would definitely want to try one of the other entrees next time. The "charcuterie" was very tasty and perfectly málà, and the portion size was much larger than expected for an app. This can be easily shared between 4 people so we had plenty of leftovers. The surprising standout, however, was the Hunan Salad! It was much smaller than I imagined (just four small sections of eggplant stuffed with thousand year egg and other yummy mush) but the flavor was amazing!Given the price, I'm not sure how soon I will be back but I definitely recommend it if you're looking for tasty Chinese food in a very aesthetically pleasing setting.

Good value on the New Yorker breakfast which includes fresh squeezed orange juice and coffee, other dishes may be quite expensive like $18 for pancakes. Waitress allowed me to substitute the bacons and they serve egg whites with a variety of choices for the toast selection. Service was extremely fast. Request for a booth seating inside or else they will direct you to the front cafe dining area which is not as nice and no window view of the building/city. Across from the grand central terminal, a convenient place to meet up.

I recently visited a local Italian eatery with an appetite for something hearty and was pleased to find their prices quite reasonable. My choice was a classic chicken parm paired with rigatoni in a vodka sauce. The portion size was satisfying, though the chicken, while smothered in sauce and perfectly melted cheese, lacked juiciness, and the breading had lost its crisp. The rigatoni was on the thicker side, yet the vodka sauce brought it to life. The mozzarella sticks, unfortunately, fell short of expectations, missing the quintessential cheese pull. However, they did redeem themselves with the side of broccoli rabe; despite being a touch too salty, it was generously served and boldly flavored with garlic. Their garlic knots were a notable highlight. On the whole, the experience was quite positive, and yes, I would order from here again for a fulfilling Italian meal.

I loved brunching here when I lived a few blocks away! My favorite was the truffle grilled cheese with asparagus, with the unctuous truffly cheese in perfectly toasted bread. I've tried the chicken and challah- which is also quite nice on a good day. There were several occasions the fried chicken was a little inconsistent (sometimes too oily or very dry, or the fried bits are coming off the chicken). The challah French toast is always lovely. The shrimp and grits are great too, the "secret oils" add a kick. They have a mean Bloody Mary called the Bloodier- with a piece of bacon in it.

I visited this restaurant in the afternoon for a meal with my girlfriend and was quite pleased with the experience. The food we had was really good, though the lunch menu options were somewhat limited. I'm intrigued to see what their dinner menu has to offer and will certainly be back to explore more of their culinary delights.

This spot is very low key and professional. For my drink I ordered a hot sake lychee "fantasy" drink and It was so good. For my meal I did get a Miso Tonkatsu, it came out sizzling and was very tasty. The food selections seem to be really high in sodium as for ingredients used so if you are watching your sodium intake I would not say come here. The vibes were great and though the grade is pending and online it's a C rating I would have at least given them an A if I didn't know. The staff here are nice great and care about allergies as they did ask me if I had any restrictions.

As the saying goes, "Rice to meet you!" And it definitely was "Rice" to come here. Went with a +1 for a late night treat at 8pm on a Thursday and Clay Pot NYC didn't fail to impress. We were given a tasting invitation by the owner, Alex Yip, and the restaurant wasn't too packed so we were immediately seated. We both got the claypot with two toppings ($13 each normally), and I had mine with pork belly and Chinese sausage, she had hers with pork belly and eel. The restaurant also gave us complimentary salt crusted quail eggs! Clay pot includes vegetables and corn and tofu in the mix as well.Disclaimer: Invited here by the owner, so the claypot was complimentary along with the salted quail eggs.AMBIANCE:I definitely like the openness vibe here compared to the East Village spot! This definitely feels less cramped and spacious, even though its still a relatively small restaurant. PROS:Pork belly was delicious! Very succulent, fragrant and literally melts in your mouth. I must say the pork belly can compare with the chashu you get in any of New York's famous ramen restaurants. Chinese sausage was sweet and you can never go wrong. On top of that you can adjust the saltiness, sweetness, and heat with their provided soy sauces. I really like the crispy rice on the edges of the clay pot bowl - definitely adds an added crunch and texture to the whole dish! Oh did I mention that there's a vat of ginger garlic on your table? I certainly abused it. Quail eggs were a unique touch! They are simply boiled and poached, and served with salt. Can't go wrong with that. Absolutely love the hospitality of service we got tonight. Big shout-out to Eric who was taking care of my table during the night! Three toppings Clay Pot rice was also 14 dollars if you wanted to get that. Could've opted for the special clay pot where you get six different types of protein (including seafood) for 16 dollars. Fyi rather small portion size, if you're a big guy like me you might need to order another one. Otherwise solid choice for a delicious Cantonese inspired food getaway!OVERALL:Come here for a more spacious, delicious clay pot experience you'd get compared to the OG East Village spot. Definitely the clay pot here did not fail to impress!

It's your standard NYC pizza place. It's gets crowded because of the location. But overall, it's not worth the price. Size is ok, and it does well. But I wouldn't make this a go to place. Try it out for sure, but don't close your mind to other places.

If you want to relive your southeast Asia trip, this is the place to be. Everything was very flavorful and had a good mix of meats/veggies on the side for a taste of freshness. The ginger quail was tasty, tender, and slid right off the bone.The coconut crunchy rice was very crispy and had a great combination of sweet/sour/savory flavors mixed in. The chilli prawn was also good, but I probably wouldnt get it again at $34 for 3-4 prawns and some bread. Not a big fan of prawn and bread pairing. The pork curry noodle was greasy but worth it for the taste if youre a fan of laksa. I'd also recommend getting the crispy pig face if it's still on the special menu. It came with a lot of garnishes, sticky rice wrappers, and a sweet peanut sauce which went really well with the crispy pork wraps we made.

Title: A Slice Above the Rest at Joe's Pizza

I recently visited Joe's Pizza and was pleasantly surprised by the quality of their pies. One of the best aspects is their late hours, perfect for those with late-night cravings or adjusting from travel.

The pizza here is thin and crispy, making for a lighter meal that doesn't skimp on flavor. I sampled several slices:

- Supreme: This was by far my favorite. Every bite was packed with toppings and bursting with flavor.
- Special (white and spinach): An interesting combination that was decent but didn't quite hit the mark for me.
- Pepperoni: A classic choice that was satisfactory, though not remarkable.
- Cheese: A simple slice that was pretty good, but not the standout of the night.

When I return to Joe's (and I definitely plan to), I'll be ordering 2-3 slices of the Supreme without hesitation. If you're looking for a great pizza spot, Joe's is definitely worth the visit.

Title: A Cozy Spot with Delectable Eats – Crispo Delivers

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Crispo with my best friend who was visiting from out of town, and I must say, the experience was nothing short of perfect. Keen to share a memorable meal, I found Crispo to be the ideal blend of a charming atmosphere paired with exceptional food.

The service shone with attentiveness and sincerity, with our servers displaying a commendable understanding and accommodation of my celiac condition. They crafted a bespoke dish for me – a riff on bucatini pomodoro transformed into a gluten-free penne delight, generously topped with creamy burrata (an extra $11, but well worth it).

My friend indulged in the carbonara, a dish she proclaimed as "to die for", and judging by the empty plates we both ended with, the flavor profiles were spot-on.

Crispo's environment was just as pleasing as its cuisine – a vibe that compels you to return. This gem has secured a spot on my go-to list for impressing guests. Whether you're a local foodie or just passing through, Crispo is a must-visit for anyone in search of a culinary treat.

The hype for this place is real. The lines are always out the door, but their food is a solid 3/5 in my opinion. We got their shrimp with beef rice roll, as well as their shrimp with pork rice roll, and they tasted exactly the same. After a while we couldn't pick up which ones we were eating anymore. Don't get me wrong the meat inside the rolls were very smooth and tender, but there wasn't a big difference between the two dishes. We also got their thousand year egg with pork congee, maybe it's me, but I enjoyed that more than their rice roll. The place is brand new and very clean. Service is quick. Prices are very expensive for rice rolls though, I've never seen rice rolls priced at $7 in other similar establishments before. This place is worth a try, at least once.

Came here with a couple of folks and got to try a good variety.For appetizers had the calamari, fried tofu, veggie spring rolls. None of these were that special....and calamari was prob my favorite, but it was just your standard breaded calamari.I myself got the spicy red snapper in tamarind sauce and I tried the same fish in mango sauce. Be warned, this place is spicy. If you're usually the mr tough guy for spices, be cautious of here. When they say thai spice level, they mean it. The fish itself was good, breaded and a very significant portion. Almost couldn't finish it.Overall, the meal was decent, environment felt like a bit upscale, but the food didn't match. Too expensive for what it is.

Title: A Delightful Bao Experience at Baohaus

As a fan of Eddie Huang, my anticipation to try Baohaus was sky-high, and finally, the stars aligned. Tucked away near Union Square, I seized the opportunity for a late dinner at this famed eatery.

From the get-go, the welcoming vibe was undeniable. The staff was incredibly friendly, ready to assist as soon as I stepped through the door. Despite the cozy space—maxing out at around ten diners—the atmosphere was perfect for a quick, casual bite with the added luxury of seating to truly savor the experience.

The menu boasted a variety of tempting options, but the Birdhaus Bao, with its promise of fried chicken enveloped in a soft, fluffy bao, was irresistible. My partner opted for the Spiceland Bao, a fiery rendition that certainly delivered on its heat. Both were served promptly, piping hot, and living up to their flavorful descriptions.

Admittedly, at $5-6 per bao, the price is slightly above what you might find in Queens, but the convenience and taste justify the Manhattan mark-up. The Birdhaus delighted with its well-seasoned crunch, while the accidental spill of Spiceland's sauce onto mine added an unexpected, searing kick—definitely not for the faint-hearted.

Side glances at neighboring diners revealed tantalizing rice bowls, hinting at another must-try for future visits. Baohaus provided an enjoyable, albeit brief, culinary adventure. Whether you're a heat seeker or prefer milder tastes, Baohaus has a bao waiting to take your breath away.

Visited this restaurant for brunch after purchasing a Pulsd deal and was semi-skeptical at first. If you read prior reviews you'll see that some reviewers had issues with what the deal and what it entitled them too, as well as what they were charged after the fact. I made sure to make my worries known when booking the reservation and the restaurant assured me that they had resolved the issues they were having with Pulsd and that I'd only be paying for the additional tip and tax. Suffice to say we had a great experience after this was addressed!We arrived at 11:30 and were seated promptly. I'm happy we decided on this time because about 30 minutes later the restaurant was packed! It's a beautifully designed space adjacent to a hotel. When you walk in you're taken back by the dim lighting and modern atmosphere. This space seems more suitable for a nice dinner or late night drinks, but they still manage to make it fun for their early brunch crowd.Our pulsd deal entitled us to two entrees and 90 minutes of bottomless prosecco with mixtures. I ended up ordering a breakfast frittata with bacon, chicken sausage, and tomato. It also came with a side of garlic roasted potatoes. Definitely a filling dish and I'd recommend it if you're coming here with an appetite! Overall it was a great brunch experience! They seem to have everything squared away with pulsd and their staff is on point with service. Come here for a low key brunch party atmosphere with good food.

I recently visited a charming restaurant that transported me straight back to my childhood with its authentic, fresh, and truly delectable dishes. The flavors were spot on, reminiscent of heirloom recipes, and for those who adore a good kick in their meal, the spice levels here can be thrillingly intense—mouth-numbing, even. However, a word of caution for those with a delicate palate: tread lightly on the spices. Seating is somewhat limited, with just a few bar-type spots available against the walls, so I suggest opting for takeout or being prepared for a wait. Nonetheless, the food is entirely worth it.

Sandwiches are awesome here. They are expensive but huge! I was able to have one sandwich for two meals. I have tried New York, Trento, and Pisillo. I think I liked the Trento the most, which had truffle oil.

Title: A Sizzling Feast with a Side of Convenience

I recently dined at a K-BBQ-inspired restaurant with a unique twist - the cooking is a spectacle performed by the waitstaff right at your table. They delivered a variety of raw meats including octopus, steak, and shrimp, and then expertly grilled, sauced, and served them on our plates. The convenience factor was off the charts!

The value was impressive, especially considering it's an all-you-can-eat setup. For a hearty meal that included two beers each, our bill was a mere $86. Terrific spot for groups and birthday celebrations – they even offer a free meal on your birthday, or up to three days after.

While the restaurant buzzes with energy, perfect for festive occasions, I did take note that, in line with other Saint Marks establishments, a bump-up in cleanliness would be welcome. Overall, a 4-star experience that successfully marries fun, flavor, and convenience.

Title: A Mazemen Revelation at Niche

I recently discovered the Steak Mazemen at Niche and it has quickly skyrocketed to the top of my favorites list. Mazemen might be broth-less ramen, but don't let that fool you – the flavors in this dish are out of this world. At first, I was doubtful; I mean, who likes dry noodles? But the dual saucing of a delicious pork blend on the steak and a separate one for the noodles kicked any doubts to the curb.

Let's talk about the steak – juicy, tender, and cooked flawlessly, it was the star of the dish. Even though the ramen was "dry," the sauces ensured every bite was moist and bursting with flavor. It was a delightful surprise that I now prefer over traditional ramen.

We also indulged in the uni toast, which is a must-try for sea urchin lovers. This small appetizer packed a punch and perfectly complemented our main course.

All things considered, Niche delivered an exceptional dining experience. Whether you're new to mazemen or a seasoned enthusiast, head over to Niche for their Steak Mazemen. Trust me, it's an encounter you don't want to miss.

I've tried Balade Your Way and really liked it, so figured I needed to try Balade proper. Ordered delivery for dinner one weeknight and the food came super fast. My boyfriend and I shared the Fattoush salad, meat shawarma sandwich (my fave thing that we ordered), hearty lentil soup (also amazing) and baklava for dessert. Definitely recommended!

They are back in business!After a long closure during the winter break, Joe's back! Not really sure why they closed since they didn't let any notice. However, they did some slight renovation with the seating. The kitchen area still looks very much undone. They also now allow you to customize your order and introduced jianbiang. It's still a pricey plate of rice noodles but I still maintain it's a good addition and provides variety to the types of food in the area.

This restaurant is great. We didn't have a reservation, but they were still able to seat us even though they were very busy. The service was great and the food was also great. My husband started with the poached lobster appetizer and loved it. He said the sauce that came with it was amazing. I got the Burrata and prosciutto appetizer and it was also amazing. The portion was a good size and the flavors were great. My husband then got the Dover sole for his entree and it was very good. However, it was pretty small for the price. I got the 30 egg yolk spaghetti with tomato sauce. I like this dish but I wish the sauce was a bit creamier. I think I would try something different the next time (the eggplant parm appetizer looked great). The espresso martinis were also amazing. I would definitely come back.

This was a place that I stopped at before going to the cloisters on one of my NYC adventures. I'll essentially eat anything so I was glad that we were able to try something authentic. Manolo seems like it's plucked right out of Spain and set down in NYC. The service was great! Prompt and not overbearing, which is what I love.True to tapas form we decided to order drinks which were tasty gin and tonics and then we ordered several small plates to share.Fresh muscles in a light white wine sauce, which were delicious and came out of the shell easily with a fork, it also came with a good crusty bread that you could soak up the sauce with.We also had Piquillo Relleno de Cordero Asado which was delicious and savory, the patatas bravas also delicious. For desert we had Un Canto a Kiara chocolate truffle with raspberry sorbet in a vanilla as raspberry sauce. All around an awesome experience and I would go again.

Title: A Noodle Haven in the Heart of Chinatown

If you're in the mood to satisfy your noodle cravings, this Chinatown gem is the place to be. Their hand-pulled noodles have been my go-to for years, and for good reason. I gravitate towards the lo mein every time - it's simply unbeatable. However, the noodle soup is a strong contender, and both the steamed and fried dumplings shouldn't be missed. While the service and seating don't always hit the mark, and it's a cash-only establishment, the culinary experience is worth any minor inconvenience. For those keen on avoiding dining hiccups, the takeout service is fast and efficient. This spot continues to be a staple for its unrivaled flavors and quality dishes.

Title: A Delightful Brunch Experience for Foodies and Michigan Alums Alike

I recently visited a brunch spot recommended by a friend, and it turned out to be a delightful experience. As a Michigan alum with a taste for fun, delicious meals, my expectations were high, and I'm pleased to say they were met.

Our wait time was around half an hour, which flew by as we chatted away. The ordering process was unique; we received a bandana color to identify our table, which added a quirky touch. The brunch options were solid, boasting a tasty array of foods that satisfied. They also serve alcoholic beverages for those looking to kickstart their day.

The only hiccup in an otherwise perfect meal was the failed attempt at the signature paw print on my Grey Dog latte – a slight disappointment for someone hoping for that Instagram-worthy moment.

The location proved to be exceptional for us tourists, nestled conveniently for a post-brunch stroll through Chelsea Market and the scenic High Line. If you're in the area and searching for a spot that promises a combination of good food and good times, this is it.

Came here and got some traditional dim sum like the chicken feet, sticky rice wrapped in lotus leaves, shrimp rolls , pork wrapped in bean curd as well as some more different ones like duck dumplings and shrimp roll with mango.Things here...just didn't hit the spot. The best items were the duck dumplings and the fried shrimp wrapped in mango. The texture was really nice for the duck dumplings and there was no gamey taste at all. Not like a super juicy dumpling, but it was different and good.The other items, are seriously offensive to serve imo. They had no levels in the taste or texture. It was all just plain. Idk how it's ranked as a bib gourmand.

Besides the wait, this place never really disappoints. The food is very good and the service is very professional. You can always get more side dishes and cheese corn. The meat quality is very good and the dipping sauce is delicious!! The grill is a little different from other places so you can cook cheese corn and eggs while you're cooking meat. Super yummy!!

Title: A Seafood Delight That Feels Like Home

Since my last visit during the soft opening, I'd been eager to return to this bustling neighborhood gem. Booking a week in advance secured us a cozy table for four at 6:30 pm, right in the midst of their delightful Happy Hour with appetizers priced at a mere $8.

We began with the fried calamari, which arrived promptly, allowing us to tuck in before our friends arrived. The restaurant graciously didn't mind us sitting and starting our meal early – a nice touch of customer service. Squeezing lemon over the calamari and dipping it into the spicy marinara sauce, we were reminded of the culinary care this place takes.

For our main course, we unanimously opted for the Fisherman's combo, a decision influenced by previous tantalizing experiences. Ditching the informal plastic bag presentation, our seafood feast was now elegantly displayed on a platter, artfully arranging the corn, rice cake, potatoes, crab, and shrimp. Sharing the platter between two was challenging yet satisfyingly ample.

A small hiccup with oversized gloves turned into a positive note when our attentive waiter provided perfectly fitting rubber gloves, a testament to the restaurant's exceptional service ethos. Special thanks to Kevin, whose hospitality never fails to make us feel at home.

In summary, this restaurant remains a recommendation I would joyously extend time and time again for anyone craving a taste of the sea coupled with a warm, welcoming atmosphere.

Title: Mixed Feelings at the Italian Eatery

I recently dined at this restaurant with friends and had a rather mixed experience. The rose sangria caught our eye, and while it was delightful, opting for single glasses rather than a pitcher would be both economical and more satisfying.

We kicked things off with the family-size Burrata, which presented us with a twist; it leaned more towards a ricotta-like consistency, departing from the traditional Burrata texture some may prefer. Caution to those who are particular about their cheese textures!

For my main, I chose the homemade cavatelli pasta coated in an exquisite alla vodka sauce. The sauce lived up to expectations, yet the pasta's al dente bite was not to my liking, leaving me to expect more from a supposedly fresh pasta. The rigatoni, on the other hand, was a better experience, and the fettuccine I sampled from a friend's plate was notably superior. My advice for pasta lovers – the fettuccine might just be your safest bet here.

While the outdoor seating is a definite recommendation for a lovely ambiance, overall, I find myself inclined to explore other dining options rather than making a return visit to this establishment.

If you're in Central Park this is a great spot to have some food with a great view of the park and the city. On the weekends they have a good brunch that goes on until 4. It's a la cart and I surprisingly found it a great price compared to other places in the tourist areas of the city. I was expecting it to be much more expensive. We had the oysters they were great, the Mac and cheese was also very good and cheesy. I had the quiche which was very good but my friend had the fish and chips and it was probably my favorite. Another friend had the French toast and it was huge! You could not go wrong with any of the meals. The best part is the view while it's cold outside you're nice and warm inside surrounded by windows watching the sunset start over Central Park.

Enjoy the comforts of amazing authentic and traditional Korean Food without ever having to leave the East Village. This small and cozy spot has amazing fried chicken, and I absolutely loved the kale and mackerel fish fish. Excellent cocktails and driink menu as well. A very minimalism vibe that boast amazing flavors!

The pho broth was fragrant and tasted pretty decent. The noodles were not my favorite and they still had a bite to them. Typically, pho noodles are soft and the noodle strands are smaller. These were much wider but perhaps it's their preference. This place was also very tiny. If you have a big group and want to eat during busy hours, there will be waiting. We got lucky with four people during lunch hours on a Tuesday. If it was up to me, next time I'm in NYC I would try something else when it comes to pho.

Kenka presents an impressive array of affordably priced Japanese delights with a quality that punches well above its weight. Be prepared for some bustling crowds, particularly in the evenings—if you swing by around 8pm on a weekday, you might find yourself waiting for a half hour. However, the wait is a small price to pay for the rapid service and attentive staff that greet you upon entry.

The menu is vast, encouraging a pick-and-mix dining adventure. A standout for me was the Gyudon; a hearty bowl of succulent beef mingled with rice, onions, and a burst of garlic, all for a mere $5.50. Although it's tempting to reorder on the next visit, the sheer variety on offer would make it a missed opportunity to explore.

Less impressive, however, were the Onigiri. These rice balls came off as a rather bland staple—an easy skip for next time, considering the overlap with rice in other dishes.

While the food scores high, the seating arrangement may not be to everyone's comfort, with tables designed as box-like structures that can challenge your knees and seating posture.

Overall, Kenka is a wallet-friendly jaunt into Japanese cuisine that doesn't skimp on portion or taste. 

Ratings:
- Price: 5/5
- Quality: 4/5
- Quantity: 5/5
- Service: 4/5
- Atmosphere: 3/5

Tucked away in midtown, this gem of a restaurant offers an unbeatable lunch special: buy three and you're treated to a fourth one on the house. At just $12 each, these specials are a steal. Dining solo or in the mood for a culinary challenge? Dive into the numbing fish fillets. This dish is a daring symphony of flavor, featuring a spicy broth peppered with actual peppercorns and complemented by crunchy lotus root slices. To top it off, service here is notably attentive. A must-visit for any foodie in the area!

Tucked into a bustling neighborhood, this gem offers an incredible lunch special that can't be beat for the price. The star of the show, the Margherita with prosciutto, is an absolute delight – the embodiment of a pizza 'OMG' moment. Served in an ideal personal size, it makes for a perfect solo lunch indulgence. Plus, for those seeking a more balanced meal, there's the option to add a side salad conveniently available through various ordering apps. Whenever the pizza-for-one mood strikes, this is unequivocally my go-to spot.

I approached this dining experience with high hopes, particularly for their eggplant parmigiana, which unfortunately fell short of expectations. The eggplant lacked the coveted crispiness and, to my disappointment, leaned towards the chewy side. The tomato sauce accompanying it was notably tart, veering away from the classic flavor profile I anticipated. On a brighter note, the table bread emerged as the culinary highlight of the meal – deliciously fresh and well-prepared. Having had a positive experience with the pizza at their Brooklyn outpost, I was left pondering whether this was an off day for this particular location or a larger inconsistency issue. Despite my underwhelming meal, the past enjoyment at the other venue leaves me on the fence about a return visit.

After a brief stroll from my hotel, I ventured into this restaurant with high hopes, only to face a letdown. Despite it being a Monday evening, our server was swamped, leading to a service that felt neglected; requests for refills and drinks had to be repeated.

The cost of the drinks was a punch to the wallet, and their potency did nothing to offset the subpar taste—a bitter disappointment. On a brighter note, the mussels were delightful, and the yuca fries were a genuine highlight. However, the brussel sprouts were drowned in sauce to the point of being nearly inedible, and the bacon's overcooked, chewy texture was another misstep. 

Regrettably, the negatives outweighed the positives, steering me away from a return visit.

Title: Elegant Tastes with a Side of Rush

I booked a table through OpenTable at a highly rated restaurant, enticed by the exceptional reviews on both Yelp and OpenTable itself. Expectations were high, given its sterling reputation. The evening unfolded with a rush, as the staff seemed eager to move us along, especially when I inquired about the dessert tasting menu. This led to an unexpected relocation to the bar, which could have been better communicated from the start to avoid an uncomfortable situation.

The food, however, was a redeeming feature - both a feast for the eyes and a delight to the palate. We indulged in the seasonal tasting menu, where the craftsmanship of each dish was evident. Unfortunately, there's an emerging trend among Michelin-starred establishments to incorporate common elements like foie gras and truffles, which, although exquisite, are becoming rather predictable.

Standout dishes included the succulent black cod, the flavorful duck, the refreshing Omija Korean wild berry drink, and a whimsically crafted white chocolate shaped like a banana. While these dishes were memorable, I couldn't help but long for the unique wow factor that is expected of such distinguished venues.

In conclusion, despite the culinary highlights and the overall enjoyment of the meal, the steep prices paired with the lack of originality in the menu might deter me from a return visit.

Title: A Convivial Feast at Carmine's UES

Carmine's on the Upper East Side lives up to its reputation as a New York City Italian staple by serving up generous family-style dishes perfect for sharing. Despite its popularity—which means you'll need to book in advance—the bustling atmosphere, complete with celebrations of all sizes, adds to the charm, though be prepared to raise your voice over the chatter.

The service was attentive, maneuvering a vast menu filled with tempting options from chicken to seafood. We dove into the complimentary bread, a tasty preamble to our main course. Our party of four settled on the chicken parm and lasagna, both of which were delightful and hearty. Note the steep $4.25 per person soda price, though.

Heads up: the portions are substantial, so arrive hungry. Regrettably, we had no room left for dessert, but those, too, are served family-style. A return visit is in order, perhaps next time with a sweet ending.

Final Thought: Carmine's is a go-to for robust Italian meals that promise both flavor and festivity. Mangia!

I came here for lunch on a Tuesday.  The place was larger than I expected.  There was a good amount of seating if you want to eat there. It's basically like Chipotle but for Korean rice bowl (bibimbap), salad, or burrito.  I ordered a rice bowl: spicy chicken over fried rice with carrots, lettuce, garlic butter corn, kimchi, spinach, and gochujang (Korean red pepper paste) sauce.  The portion was larger than I expected.  The spicy chicken was juicy and tasty.  However, the veggies (carrots, kimchi, spinach) tasted a bit old.  I also didn't like the fried rice.  The rice was mushy and not fried at all.  The staff were friendly and helpful.  It was an okay place to try, I would not go out of my way to come here.  I would rather go to Koreatown and get a better bibimbap.

Title: A Hearty Feast at a Cozy Spot

If you've been saving your appetite for something truly indulgent, this is the place to let loose. I ventured in post-work, my stomach rumbling in anticipation of their sandwich lineup. The 'Italian Combo' immediately caught my eye, but the 'Chicken Parm' and 'Eggplant Parm' presented a tantalizing dilemma. 

My decision? The Chicken Parm and the Italian Combo. The Chicken Parm was a solid choice with its perfectly breaded chicken lavished in the right balance of sauce and cheese, though a crisper hero bread would have made it exceptional. However, it was the Italian Combo that stole the show and my taste buds, bursting with bold and satisfying flavors.

Their mixed drinks, the Old Fashioned and Parm Manhattan, complemented the meal with a robust kick that should not be underestimated.

Be prepared for a snug ambiance – it's the only minor quibble I had, leading to a well-deserved 4-star rating. The warm service and mouthwatering fare are compelling enough reasons for a return visit, particularly for another round with that Italian Combo!

Title: A Slice of Classic NYC at a Top Pizza Spot

I finally had the chance to visit what's touted as one of the city's premier pizza joints, and it didn't disappoint. My family and I arrived just ahead of the dinner rush around 5:30 PM on a Thursday and were seated immediately, avoiding any wait—a plus in busy NYC.

A heads-up for future diners: the place is cash-only and has a single bathroom, but the air conditioning is a relief.

We ordered a small Margherita pie for $22. It lived up to the hype with a perfectly thin crust, a tantalizing char, a robust marinara sauce, fresh basil, and rich mozzarella. Indeed, it was the quintessential NYC pizza experience.

This spot claims the title of the city's first pizzeria—an impressive heritage, and the pie we had was a testament to their lasting quality.

A couple of oddities: water was served in plastic cups, contrasting with the lemons that came in glass. They promptly refilled our water, although there was a questionable $1 charge per small jug of tap water. It might have been tax, but that wasn't clear.

Overall, it's a venue I'm glad to have experienced at least once. The pizza is authentically satisfying, and the place holds onto its classic charm.

Jean-Georges has done it again, I love everything on this menu! Absolutely fantastic food, you don't even realize its vegan. The restaurant itself is lovely and has the most beautiful art pieces everywhere. The food is absolutely delicious, you feel healthy coming out of this restaurant. @traveleen_gurl

Wow! This place is close to where I usually stay which is super convenient, especially because I plan on being a regular here! I came here on a Friday night with my partner. We walked in and the ambiance was quiet for conversation, chill, and somewhat cozy with the lighting.We walked in and were seated in the middle of the second room. We were immediately brought out menus and prawn crackers with peanut sauce. The prawn crackers were crunchy and splendidly crackly when dipped in the sauce, much like a chemistry experiment. We ordered the spicy pho, a pork lemongrass banh mi to share as an appetizer, and chicken lemongrass vermicelli noodle.The waitstaff was very kind, patient, and accommodating to all of our requests, as well as our nut and soy allergy (which is not easy to do in Asian cuisine). Our food came out at a reasonable time and arrived hot. My partner's spicy beef pho was amazing. He loved it and kept eating past being full. He described it as having lots depth to the flavor and broth, having a lot of meat, and not being overwhelmingly spicy. I loved my vermicelli! The meat was delicious and wonderfully seasoned and came with cucumber and carrots. I would have preferred more vegetables in the dish but it was a good amount to not be overwhelming. I poured the fish sauce that came with it over my dish and that added more intense flavor and complementary depth to my dish. The Banh Mi had the perfect amount of spicy mayo (most places overdo it), the pickled carrots were briney and paired well with the salty and savory pork.Overall, very delicious food with great ambiance and service. As I said before, will be back to order more!

Title: Hidden Gem in Midtown - Kati Shop Review

Nestled in the heart of Midtown, Kati Shop is a delightful fast-casual Thai spot that's set up akin to a Chipotle, promising a feast that won't weigh you down. On my visit, I opted for the lemongrass chicken curry paired with their house curry sauce, fragrant jasmine rice, sweet potatoes, and a cucumber and tomato salad. 

The chicken was succulent and well-seasoned, while the rice could've stood as a star on its own with its aromatic flavor. The salad was simple yet elevated with a light dressing that made it a refreshing side, and the sweet potatoes were a winner. However, the curry sauce wasn't to my liking, overpowering my meal as it smothered both protein and rice. In the future, I'll request it on the side.

Their daily in-house made Thai tea was middling and forgettable, so I'd likely skip it on a return visit. Despite this, Kati Shop shines with its bright and clean ambiance, friendly staff, and cozy seating. I'll be back to savor their culinary offerings, just with a slight tweak to my order. It's a stellar addition to the area, and I hope it maintains its high standards as more diners discover its charm.

I've been going to both locations of Flor De Mayo since my college days, and the food is always just as good as I remember. It's one of my favorite spots for a quick, casual meal and the prices are very reasonable. I always get the Pollo a la Brasa half chicken with either their yellow rice or their green plantains for $12.50, and it's enough to bring home leftovers for your next day's lunch.The chicken is incredibly juicy. The seasoning on the crispy skin almost reminds me of Peking duck, but once you dip it in the acidic, tomato-based sauce, it goes from Chinese to Peruvian.I always make a point of stopping by here whenever I find myself in the neighborhood. It gets a little crowded during weekend dinners, so if you want to avoid any wait time, check it out during lunch hours!

Visited Hou Yi with my wife around 4:00 PM on a Saturday. It wasn't busy and they just opened.We ordered half mild beef spicy hot and half herb w/ pork as our soup. We also ordered various items such as pork belly, cabbage, fish tofu, etc. Everything tasted good. No complaints about food.Here's why I'm giving this place two stars. We were one of four groups to be seated. We observed two people manning the restaurant. On multiple occasions, we had to walk to the back to grab someone for another menu to order more items. When the third round of food was brought out, the waiter brought the check as well. We didn't ask for the check. As far as we were concerned, we were allowed to stay for up to an hour and 40 mins. It was only an hour at this point. Additionally, the plates that were brought out did not include everything we asked for.Overall it was a bad experience. Hopefully the other location is a little better.

This spot is amazing! My coworker told me about it so I decided to go one night before I had to work a performance (I work at Lincoln Center so this is a perfect spot that's not too pricey and is very quick to hit before a ballet performance or opera etc.) We went in as a party of 3 at 615 on a Tuesday and we got a table right away and were out of there by 7.  We got the pork soup dumplings, scallion pancakes, chicken lomein & steamed vegetable dumplings to split between 3 people. Was definitely a good amount of food. The soup dumplings were excellent. The veggie dumplings were also great. The scallion pancakes I loved- weren't covered in grease like other ones I've had and the sauce they gave us to dip it in was so tasty. I personally liked the lomein. My mom did not lol. It had Bok Choy in it too which I'm currently obsessing over. I will say though that for the lomein being the most expensive item we ordered- I felt the serving size could have been a bit bigger. My boyfriend got an unsweetened iced tea as well. The service was excellent, our waitress fixed our wobbly table without us even asking and she brought our food out very quickly. The atmosphere was lovely and the decor was really nice. Total for everything (without tip) came out to be $47. For 3 people, right by Lincoln Center? Incredible deal. So happy to have found this place! It's excellent!!!! The service is fantastic, and the price is unbeatable. Will definitely definitely be coming back!

During my recent visit to this restaurant, I was eager to delve into their assortment of dim sum offerings. The Peking Duck Spring Roll, however, was disappointing as it lacked the signature flavor of the dish it's named after; it failed to deliver on the expected rich and savory taste of the duck. 

On the more positive side, the Sticky Rice with Chicken in Lotus Leaf was a delight. It struck the perfect balance in moisture and had uniformly distributed flavors, easily becoming my favorite item on the menu. The Chicken Feet were also enjoyable, though they were drenched a tad too liberally in sauce for my liking.

I found the Taro something clear dumpling to have room for improvement, with the skin being unappealingly thick and the filling somewhat arid.

Despite some letdowns, I am intrigued by the extensive menu. While the prices are steeper than your average dim sum haunt, the quality and diversity on offer hold promise. I'm inclined to return and discover more of what the kitchen can do.

Title: Great Food and Exceptional Service at Local Gem

Last Saturday, my party of four enjoyed a delightful dinner experience around 7:30 PM. We were immediately seated upon arrival in the spacious setting that boasted communal share tables, adding to the convivial atmosphere.

Our server, Allen, was exceptional from the start, enhancing our evening with attentive and thoughtful service. The drinks, comprised of spicy margaritas and beers, were top-notch. We savored a variety of shared dishes, including nachos, wings, quesadillas, a kale salad, and fries. Each item was delicious, leaving us with no room for complaints—it was the epitome of satisfying bar food.

The night was made extra special due to it being a celebration for one of our birthdays. After a stealthy chat with Allen, he orchestrated a perfect surprise. Despite the restaurant's bustling environment, he discreetly coordinated the presentation of a dessert with a candle, much to the birthday girl's delight.

In summary, the combination of great food and Allen's stellar service resulted in a memorable evening. We'll definitely return, and a huge shoutout to Allen for going above and beyond!

Stopped in for dinner after 6, and found an empty restaurant with 2 other customers.  The good, Chicken Drunken Noddles ($12) . The bad, Beef Holy Basil Ka  Praw ($12) .  I don't know why, but this dish was overly salty.   I think they poured on the Soy Sauce for this dish and that's where the sodium comes from .    The Drunken noodles were good and not salty by any means.  Everything was seasoned properly.

Title: Delightful Soba Experience

I recently visited this restaurant for lunch and was pleasantly surprised by their variety of specials. Opting for the bento box, which included soba, I decided to have my noodles cold with dipping sauce. The dish did not disappoint. The soba was cooked to perfection and complemented by a rich, flavorful sauce. A highlight was the braised vegetables served on the side, which added a delightful dimension to the meal with their unique seasoning. Overall, a very satisfying experience for any soba enthusiast!

Beautiful, open and airy space. So much space for eating and socializing I wish it was closer to where I lived so I could park it with my lap top. The staff is very energetic and helpful and the food came very fast. I got the golden cauliflower salad with a small chicken and there was a lot given in the 'small' portion. The bread was very fresh crunchy and flavorful! I loved the plants and decoration. Very modern feels. Definitely recommend.

Title: A Hearty Meal with a Side of Speedy Service

I popped into this eatery with my sister on a bustling Thursday evening, pleasantly surprised by the ample seating. The menu boasted staples like noodles, jianbing, and baos, all ordered at the cashier with the convenience of table service.

Our shared meal consisted of pork belly and duck baos, alongside a generous bowl of wonton noodle soup. The soup impressed, featuring a hearty portion with perfectly cooked noodles and delightfully homemade wontons. It was the highlight of the night for me.

The baos were a mixed bag. While the duck bao's fresh veggies added a welcomed crunch, both suffered slightly from baos that didn't seem as fresh as I would have liked. Price-wise, the meal was reasonable, and the portion sizes exceeded our expectations.

Friendly and efficient service rounded off the dining experience, ensuring I'll be making a return trip to sample their jianbing and other noodle varietals.

Cute restaurant and good service but the food was just ok. This was my first time trying a seafood boil and I wish I could say I was impressed. While the food wasn't terrible, it certainly could have been better.We came in without a reservation so we had to sit at the bar and wait for about 30 mins. During that time we got a few drinks (the Mango Mojito was great!), and a Battered Shrimp Basket with Cajun fries to share which was a little greasy but tasty nonetheless. Once seated in our table we ordered 1lb of the Snow Crab Legs in Envie Sauce and another combo of Snow Crab Legs + Shrimp in Shaking Sauce. I really liked that they give you the option to get the shrimp headless, and the shrimp itself was good. The sauces on the other hand were very mid and neither had the spice it claimed. If I had to choose a favorite though it would be the Envie one. Some of the crab legs had very little meat which was disappointing, but the ones that had were delish. For sides we got an order of Cajun fries, and two of the garlic mac & cheese which was just ok as I didn't taste much of the garlic or cheese.Would I try Shaking Crab again? Maybe, maybe not. If the former I'd probably check out their Brooklyn location.

My Valentine's Day outing to Max Brenner was a delightful surprise, having never heard of the chocolatier before. The buzz at the door hinted at the need for reservations, a move my companion prudently made. Initially, its aesthetic gave off a Cheesecake Factory vibe, leading me to anticipate a more generic dining experience.

The menu was a haven for those with a sweet tooth, resembling a dessert catalog more than a traditional restaurant offering, with even cocktails doubling as sugary treats. We indulged in a Valentine's Day waffle, intended for sharing. While the presentation was impressive, the taste was comparable to a homemade waffle, leaving something to be desired. Their dessert drinks and fondue platters, on the other hand, seem worth revisiting.

I tried the Strawberry Dream, which was visually enticing but fell short on flavor and lacked the expected kick of vodka, reminding me more of a standard strawberry smoothie. This visit taught me that Max Brenner, being a chain, sticks to a script, ensuring consistency at the expense of individual culinary flair.
