Title: A Slice of Japan with Impeccable Service

As a sashimi enthusiast freshly back from Japan, finding a stateside spot that satisfies my cravings has been a challenge—until I discovered this gem. The authenticity is spot-on, with fish directly flown in from Japan, ensuring that freshness is never in question. The Wokuni-Don lunch special, priced at an incredibly reasonable $24, is a sashimi lover's dream: a generous assortment of the finest cuts accompanies the perfect miso soup, flawlessly cooked rice, and crispy tempura.

Choosing to visit at 12:15 pm on a holiday proved wise, as we enjoyed a quieter venue and immediate seating. The service here deserves a special mention; from the thoughtful complimentary tea that warmed us on a chilly day to the welcoming hostess who genuinely considered my seating needs due to wheelchair accessibility. The restroom facilities maintained this considerate trend, being fully accessible and equipped with all necessary features.

This restaurant isn't just a meal; it's an experience that I'll undoubtedly be reliving soon. Highly recommended for the food, value, and especially the service.

Tucked into a charming corner, this quaint Shanghai-style eatery offered a delightful dining experience. I opted for the stir-fry thick noodles, which hit the perfect balance of flavor — substantial yet far from overpowering, ideal for a satisfying lunch. My companion went for the fried dumplings. After snagging a taste, I was impressed by the unique dipping sauce that amplified the dumplings' taste, elevating a simple dish to something memorably delicious.

This is such a fave. I've been coming here for so many years and have never once had a bad time. Brunch and dinner are totally different experiences and both are epic - we've prob been for brunch more times than dinner, but I legit love both. Atmosphere: so great. Small, cozy, booth seating, cool art on the walls and a pretty glass ceiling to let the light in. Music: SO good. This place never feels like too much of a "vibe" - you can go and relax and not feel like you're at a brunch spot that turns clubby, but they play great music that always puts me in a good mood. Service: amazing. Shout out to the waitress who brought me a virgin Bloody Mary when she saw I was prego and couldn't have the real deal!FOOD: BOMB. Love everything. Steak and eggs, mushroom omelette, salad with the lot, Australian coffee, bloody Mary's, snack menu for HH... it's all good. OMG and the pavlova - just order it. Most of the time I'll go with just 1 or 2 other people, but I also threw a birthday brunch here for a friend which was affordable and so fun. If you live in UWS and have never been, what the hell is wrong with you? If you don't live in UWS, it's worth the trip.

Got lunch here again today.  Tried two new dishes and they were both had super tasty sauce.  L15. Kung Pao Shrimp with Peanut Lunch SpecialL18. Beef with Fried Tofu Lunch SpecialThe Kung Pao was a slightly sweeter sauce.  Not spicy at all.  I wish it had more kick to it.  It came with a bunch of peanuts, peppers, onions, and a few other accouterments in addition to about 6 or 7 pieces of medium-sized shrimp.The Beef dish was definitely a must get next time. Super tasty sauce and chuck full of beef, fried tofu, and edamame.This place never disappoints.

I went here on a Friday night around 9 pm and had to wait about 30-40 minutes for a party of 2 off of the yelp waitlist.We got the soy garlic wings appetizer, fries, and a bulgogi hot stone pot. All were tasty. Price is a little expensive for my liking so I'll usually share when I go here.The union square location is definitely more comfortable, and accommodating for larger groups. This location is not really a comfortable setting, tables are very close for comfort. Best to come here with a small group.Service was good, was able to get the attention of my waiter promptly each time. Overall, I like the food but I think there are better places in the area with similar food.

I've been here twice and ordered 4 dishes in total. Every single one of them has turned out to be great. I especially recommend the Argentinian skirt steak. Really big portion sizes in general. Service was attentive. Space is quite small and crowded. Not much of an ambiance. But the food makes this place worth a visit.

I'd give this place a solid 3.5. Came here after roaming around Chinatown, and was craving their fried dumplings. No one else makes it better than this place. It's called something else in Chinese, but their menu has a picture of it. It's just the plumpest fried dumplings I've ever had, and the sauce that comes with it, compliments this dish so well, I literally dream about it. The sauce is the perfect balance between sweet and savory, and I am guilty of always drowning my food in it. Everything else is pretty standard. This place is great for the price, and the space is huge. It's good for large groups, but expect a wait if you're going to dine here at a typical lunch hour. I came around 2pm, and it wasn't as busy.

Title: A Cozy Bistro Delight for a Special Celebration

My girlfriend and I chose this charming restaurant for an early Chinese New Year/Valentine's celebration, and it was a splendid choice. The ambiance immediately set a romantic tone with decor that transported us to a Parisian bistro, complete with soft French melodies.

Seated promptly for our 7pm reservation, I indulged in the restaurant week menu featuring a perfectly seasoned Steak Tartare with a delightful quail egg, a Duck Confit with crispy skin complemented by zesty orange sauce, and an exquisite chocolate mousse that boasted high-quality dark chocolate. Each dish was a culinary triumph, especially the Duck Confit resting on tasty brussel sprouts— a dish I'll certainly crave again.

My partner's choice, the bone in NY strip with truffle-topped steak frites, presented a generous portion of fries with an unmistakable taste of truffle. While the steak frites were satisfying, the NY strip, unfortunately, missed the mark being somewhat overcooked and underseasoned, save for the accompanying herb butter.

Despite the minor disappointment with the steak, our overall experience was delightful with an inviting ambiance, mouthwatering dishes, and reasonable prices – about $80 for an enchanting evening. This restaurant is indeed a fantastic spot for a date or celebration, and I eagerly anticipate our next visit.

Pride in the city was so much fun. We popped in here for some pre-pride shenanigans, and even though they weren't fully open they were more than happy to make us some drinks. They were ready and decked out with rainbow flags! We had a few spicy cheladas that were delicious and were on our way! The service was so great, I'd definitely give them another try when in the area.

Found myself on the westside in Chelsea and decided to come here for dinner.ATMOSPHERE: The inside is supposed to mimic street carts in Chengdu. So depending on what you order, the "cook" goes to that "cart" and makes the food and then serves it to you from that cart.  They have 2 large tables and then high seating and I've never seen it that crowded so it's good for larger groups.FOOD: They specialize in Chengdu style Chinese food which means lots of Sichuan peppercorns etc.  They have dumplings, soup noodles, these meat sandwich items and more.  They have items for vegetarians and vegans. It's fast casual where you pay upfront and then sit down.DU BRAISED BEEF NOODLE SOUP - a lot of people liked this when they ordered it.  It's kind of like their version of Taiwanese beef noodle soup but spicier.  My husband can handle spicy and even he said it was pretty spicy.  The noodles are rice noodles and it comes with beef cubes and bok choy.  Overall, pretty good.SPICY AND SWEET WATER NOODLES - these are thick, udon looking noodles tossed in a chili oil Sichuan sauce.  The noodles are more doughy than chewy, they are slightly hard with a bite to it than any chew or soft-ness.  They are a bit cold and the oil is doused.  It's spicy and has lots of the Sichuan peppercorn so my mouth was tingly and drinking water made it worse and tasted salty.  It's more salty than sweet but I did taste the sweetness.  This is the vegan option, it's not bad but it looked better than it tasted.FRIES - we got the fries and had to return them because they were cold and not like fries, more like potatoes that were undercooked. Overall, there are lots of options for food here and if you like Sichuan food it's worth trying.  They don't really "cook" the food to order as far as I could tell so some of it may be cold or taste a bit pre-cooked.

Title: A Must-Visit Brunch Haven for Aesthetic Aficionados

If you're a brunch enthusiast with a keen eye for Instagram-worthy locales, you simply must pencil in a visit to this charming establishment. My experience, which unfolded on a tranquil Monday, was nothing short of delightful due to the lack of crowds.

Stepping inside, I was immediately taken by the decor. Admittedly, I wouldn't have pegged it for a brunch spot at first glance, but I'm thrilled it defies expectations. The menu tempted us with the Pulled Pork Benny and the Salmon Eggs — both choices did not disappoint. The Pulled Pork Benny stood out to me with its robust flavors, while my companion was taken by the ultra-fresh, expertly smoked Salmon Eggs. Naturally, our meal was accompanied by the quintessential brunch beverage: mimosas.

This place isn't just about appearances; it's a full-on sensory delight that echoes California cool. It's not just a photogenic backdrop but a culinary hotspot that exceeded my expectations. So, here's a tip for NYC visitors: carve out time in your schedule for this spot. You won't regret it.

Maybe we came on an off day or we didn't order the right item but thought my shrimp pho was very very average? Came here in the late afternoon on a Friday wanting to try the beef pho however was informed by the cashier that they already ran out. The shrimp pho was very light. There was not much flavor to the soup besides the spice and salt. Portion was ok for the price. Thought the whole thing was just meh  Definitely want to come back and try their beef pho. Small place with a few seats only

Came here at 4pm when they open for the day at the back of the cafe to try the Quiet Storm. You have to order  at the same register where cafe customers order at and get a order number. The broth was flavorful, and does not have as much of a fishy taste as the Dirty, which is expected due to the paste. The noodles had a nice texture and the ajitama soft boiled egg was worth the money to complete the ramen. I chose pork instead of chicken, but one piece was not as soft as I wanted it to be -- it was dry and thick, while the other was thinner and softer. I am not sure if there is complementary water since I brought my own. Other restaurants that serve ramen would provide water to quench your thirst and cleanse your palate automatically when you sit down, but not here -- perhaps it was because the purchasing process is like eating at a food court or Mitsuwa. There were waiters/waitresses who brought and cleaned up the dishes though.

Hao Noodles is a boujee noodle joint with modern decor and calm environment​ that attracts young professionals who is willing to pay $20+ for a bowel of noodles. It's definitely not your Asian parents' noodle shop, where loudness and crowdedness​ reign supreme! The interior​ is open, filled with plants and ample of open light, giving off a refine and natural vibe​. Having its name literally translates to "Good" noodles, it is obligatory to try their noodles. I ordered the signature Hot Pot Beef Noodle. The verdict: the noodles themselves were good .... above average, certainly had better noodles for a ​better price. What carried the dish was the flavor and the aroma of the broth. The spice level was mild enough for me to appreciate all the flavor of the herbs. The addition of cilantro also provided the freshness to contrast the smokiness​ of the broth. The beef was tender but the cut was not ideal. I got plenty of tendons, though there weren't tough to bite through. ​We also ordered the cabbage vermicelli​. It came wrapped in parchment paper to pack all that flavor within, especially the strong flavor of the old Chinese cooking wine. The service was great! The staff were very welcoming and accommodating​. Overall, I enjoyed ​it. I can see how it can justify having its price tag​. In my opinion,​ it was smart of them to name it "good" noodles and not "best" noodles.

I remain steadfast in my belief that this spot serves up the best non-fancy tacos in New York, a title they've held in my book for some time. On my latest visit, I ventured beyond my usual order to try the quesadilla especial with pork, and it was a revelation. The flavor-packed quesadilla rivals, if not surpasses, the excellence of their tacos. It was really an incredible addition to an already stellar lineup. Highly recommended for anyone in search of authentic, top-notch Mexican fare.

Title: A Hearty Feast at Amy Ruth's

If you're planning a visit to Amy Ruth's, brace yourself for a bit of a wait – a testament to how worth it this soul food haven truly is. With two bustling floors, the vibes are as lively as the flavors.

The bar may be small, but it packs a punch with offerings like the shareable mimosa carafe and the perfectly light Harlem Renaissance Wit Beer, both excellent partners to the feast that awaits. Speaking of which, resist the temptation to fill up on the heavenly cornbread – especially if you dare to add butter – because the main courses deserve your full appetite.

Take the Ruby Dee, for example. Whether you opt for it fried or baked, the catfish is a showstopper that'll have your heart singing with joy. And it's part of the Daily Entree menu, so you're in for a treat with two sides. Pair it with their creamy Mac N Cheese and crispy French fries for the ultimate comfort meal.

Here, hot sauce reigns, ready on most tables for an immediate kick to your chicken or fish. And do not underestimate their portions; the photos simply cannot capture the generosity on each plate. Come hungry to Amy Ruth's and leave delighted, your craving for soulful indulgence thoroughly satisfied.

Title: Unbeatable Flavor Worth Every Transit Stop

Review:

Don't let distance deter you from dining at the Spice Grill; it's a culinary trek I'm happy to make time and again. Once a convenient stroll from my old office in midtown, I now navigate two trains for a taste of their exceptional Bhel Poori. This unique dish is a delightful muddle of crunchy, snack-like delight, tossed with potatoes, red onions, and parsley — an unbeatable blend for someone who enjoys milder spices like me. Paired with a salad, the Bhel Poori brings a crescendo of flavor that transforms a simple lunch into an extraordinary one. Distance aside, Spice Grill remains my go-to for an amazing meal, proving that some flavors are truly worth travelling for.

Title: Noodle Abundance at a Cantonese-American Fusion Spot

I recently dined at a Cantonese eatery that promises an abundant serving with every dish. The menu, extensive as it is, might overwhelm at first, but it's part of the restaurant's charm.

Their star offering, hand-pulled noodles, may have received mixed reviews from noodle aficionados. Personally, I found them quite delightful, albeit not the best I've ever had. They were plentiful—almost enough to share with a small crowd—indicating the restaurant's generous nature.

The cuisine is a harmonious blend of traditional Cantonese fare with subtle American twists. It's clear they've mastered the classics, serving them up in hearty portions that are easy on the wallet—a much-appreciated trait in Manhattan's dining scene.

While this place may not top my list of Chinese culinary experiences in Chinatown, their good standard of food and service makes them a contender worth revisiting for a casual meal out.

Title: A New Culinary Love Affair at Bocca

From the moment I stepped into Bocca, I knew it wouldn't be my last visit. They say the first encounter sets the tone, and Bocca certainly charmed me with a promise of a blossoming culinary romance.

We originally came in for drinks post-work but couldn't resist the allure of their menu. The Lamb Carpaccio was a revelation, adorned with crispy snap peas and pickled onions – an absolute delight. Meanwhile, the complimentary bread served with a sun-dried tomato paste was an award-worthy starter on its own.

At the persuasive recommendation of our bartender, Eric, we opted for the grilled octopus paired with a spicy sausage spread. It was a dish that transported me straight to the heart of Italian cuisine. But the true star was the pasta with Romano cheese, perfectly al dente, creating a symphony of flavors in every bite.

Eric, the epitome of professionalism and charm, guided us expertly through the menu. His recommendations ensured a memorable dining experience.

In summary, if you're an aficionado of Italian cuisine, Bocca delivers an exceptional affair for the senses. My first visit was a definite hit, and I'm already looking forward to the next.

Made reservations for 2 on a Saturday at 1145 am for brunch. Arrived when they opened at 11 and they accommodated us for wanting to change the reservation to 11 so right off the bat the experience was pretty positive. Sat down and began browsing the menu, I chose the unlimited mimosas for my brunch drinks of choice while my brother went with the unlimited beer. The waiter was quick to refill my drinks because I drink like a fish and would finish my mimosas in 12 seconds lol. For my entree I went with the steak eggs and a side of longonisa. The steak was cooked perfectly as were the eggs. The side of longonisa was also amazing. The sauce that it came with was super delicious. My brother got the sizzling pork head with an egg which I tried, that was also very very good. The fact that I liked this place even more was the music selection. A lot of hip hop to make the brunch a complete enjoyable experience for us.

Wow! Completely unexpected that some of the best ramen in the city was so close to home! The ramen here is top notch and way better than most of the popular spots in the Manhattan.Let's get it out of the way first, the toppings kind ofsuck here. The egg is a little plain a bit overcooked and the pork was rather flavorless. But it's like that for a reason, the ramen broth is just so flavorful thst having more flavor would poorly compliment it.I got the spicy shoyu and the stars of the show were the ramen broth and the ramen. The broth was thick and rich, a decadent tori paitan style that was beautifully made. The ramen noodles were amazingly made and cooked and complimented this broth perfectly.So obviously with this combination it makes sense that the toppings can be flavorless. They also give  you a lot of green onions to break through the fattiness of the broth, which brought an excellent balance to the ramen.Delicious!

Title: A Satisfying Lunch Experience

I recently visited this restaurant for lunch and was pleased to find they offer an excellent selection of lunch specials. I opted for the panini, which featured pastrami, portobello mushroom, and Swiss cheese. It came with a side of soup and fries. The fries were well-seasoned and deliciously crispy. The panini itself was grilled to perfection, maintaining its moisture and flavor.

Additionally, I tried the bacon beef burger which, although not part of the lunch special, was noteworthy. Topped with portobello mushroom, grilled onions, bacon, spinach greens, tomato, and cheddar, the burger was so generously stacked that I had to resort to using a knife and fork. Nevertheless, it was a burger worth the effort.

The service matched the quality of the food – efficient and attentive, ensuring a pleasant dining experience. Overall, the meal was thoroughly enjoyable, from the savory main dishes to the satisfying sides.

I've been to Sofritos many times in the past and one thing is for sure they have one of the best sceneries! It's absolutely gorgeous especially as the sunsets. The music playing was pretty good. The chicken empanadas are good and i enjoyed the sweet dipping sauce that it comes with. I ordered a glass of rose' to start off the meal.I ordered the salmon with sweet plantains and my S.O got the chicken breast with spinach. The salmon was cooked well but could have used a bit more seasoning and the plantains were on poking. Chicken was well seasoned but the spinach was a bit plain. Food was pretty average.The one thing that we were disappointed with the most was the service time. My SO had to ask numerous times for a refill of his water and we asked for the bill and waited about 20 mins to get it. They may have been short staffed but they should consider that it will impact the customers overall experience. It might be a while before I revisit...

This is the place to go for lunch !Stopped in to try their signature Ramen and some Gyoza and I was pleasantly surprised.Gyoza was fried fresh but that's not why you're here.Their signature Ramen was quite good the broth was light and tasty. And everything that accompanied it with it was pretty good. The char Sui tender and tasty ,  and the egg was well seasoned but a little overcooked.Overall if you're looking for a backstreet style Tokyo Ramen shop this is it ! I will be returning!Follow me on Facebook Instagram yelp Twitter as I travel the world in search of the perfect bowl of noodle soup@noodlesoupr

I had a pretty unique Japanese dining experience due to our order of the tuna ribs. It was so so delicious! My friends and I were all in shock when the server brought out the ribs since we weren't expecting it to be so huge. We spent a while scooping out the meat from the bones, which we then paired with a seaweed sheet and scallions. It was such a fun experience! If you have a large party, definitely try the tuna ribs out and call in advance. Aside from the tuna ribs, we ordered a sushi for 3 and two sushi for 2s. It came with a variety of sushi and sashimi pieces such as tuna, salmon, California rolls, spicy tuna rolls, uni, and more. I was stuffed by the end of my meal! The sushi was high quality and yummy! This place is on the pricier end of a typical dinner but definitely worth checking out if you want to splurge again!

I'm not sure how long the Skylight Diner has been around but I'm confident it will be around for a long time to come. My friend and I decided to garb a pre-movie night dinner. Truth be told, I didn't want to have to pay through the nose at the movies and so the next best thing was to go grab something non fried and fresh. I had the Cobb salad and it was absolutely fabulous.The Skyline Diner has a great staff and the customer service is top-notch. If your in the neighborhood or headed to the movies in the area, I would highly recommend the Skyline Diner.

Title: A Delightful Indonesian-French Fusion Experience

My recent dining experience at this gem of an Indonesian-French restaurant in NYC was nothing short of magnificent. Despite an unexpected delay due to a subway incident that made us 40 minutes late—resulting in the loss of our dining room table—we were promptly accommodated at the bar tables which turned out to be a blessing in disguise, thanks to our super cool bartender, Connor.

The food and beverages were of top-notch quality, with every sharing plate bringing a new delight to our taste buds. From the crispy veg spring rolls to the flavorful clams cooked Jimbaran style, to the rich oxtail soup and steamed black pepes, each dish was a testament to the culinary prowess in the kitchen. The fried rice was perfectly seasoned, and our meal topped off with the cooling shave ice and the sweet pandan custard was simply divine.

As for the drinks, the Batavia punch and Summer Kelapa were refreshingly unique, and the red wine selection was impressive. This establishment truly brings an authentic Indonesian flair combined with French sophistication to the heart of New York City. The mood and ambiance hark back to the fine dining experiences of Bali, which, as an Indonesian, I found incredibly nostalgic and heartwarming.

I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for an exceptional culinary journey that blends Indonesian warmth with French elegance. It's a feast for the senses that's not to be missed.

The wait is not worth it! We waited in line for about an hour to be seated for brunch and it was a waste of time. Friend of a Farmer offers a cute farm to table ambiance with decor including raw fruits and vegetables in baskets throughout the restaurant, farmhouse style wall paper, etc. Unfortunately, the food and service require a bit of work. We had the farmers market omelette and gramercy omelette. Both were served on a skillet along with some home fries and were incredibly underwhelming... could have made the same omelette with the same presentation at home or picked it up at my local corner store deli. For beverages, we ordered the French press coffee. I inquired about almond or soy milk for the coffee, which the restaurant did not have... only whole milk. Our waitress was nowhere to be found for the majority of our brunch... we had to flag her down to order, ask for ketchup, and then the check.

My friend and I came here for dinner. We really wanted to like it but multiple items that we got were subpar. Ribs: You know the expression "fall off the bone?" well this was the opposite of that. While the flavor of the dry rub was good, can't say the ribs were easy to eat. Sliders: The meat was dry but oddly crispy because it was so dry. Not the worse thing on the plate. Homemade sausage and Pastrami were by far the best thing we had on the plate.Cornbread: That cupcake cornbread is not cornbread. Both my friend and I agreed it wasn't cornbread. Did not taste like cornbread. Baked Beans: Eh. Happy Hour $10 for 2 well drinks. Tiny baby glasses with mostly ice. Not a good deal.

Title: A New Benchmark in Penang Curry at The Villa

I’ve long been a staunch advocate for Thai Market's Penang curry, but The Villa has redefined excellence with their take on this classic dish. Their ingenious addition of sweet potato slices to the already rich and condensed curry introduces a captivating, almost caramelized sweetness that simply astounds the palate. Equally impressive is their rendition of mango with sticky rice. Though initially skeptical of the unconventional purple hue, the dish proved to be an irresistible indulgence, coaxing me into savoring every last grain of the perfectly prepared rice. Beware, it's so good you might find yourself skipping your next meal just to balance out the day's caloric indulgence.

Title: Wings to Remember at Cozy Thai Spot

From a converted skeptic of Thai cuisine, let me just say, the chicken wings at this place will change your mind! I stumbled into this restaurant with friends on a whim and left a big fan. Though I'm typically indifferent to Thai food, their wings were nothing short of spectacular.

The restaurant atmosphere struck me as particularly charming, making it a prime spot for date night with its cute and cozy setting. While I gave their popular drink a try, it turns out I'm not fond of the particular fruit they use, but that's just a matter of taste.

One word of caution: their rice dishes pack some heat, so if spicy isn't your thing, you might want to steer clear of that menu item. Despite that, I'm already planning my next visit and would recommend this spot to anyone in search of a tranquil environment with delicious eats.

Title: A Blend of Tradition and Trend at Cho Dang Gol

I recently ventured into Cho Dang Gol, part of the Hands Hospitality family, where I've enjoyed dining at their various concepts like Her Name is Han and Izakaya Mew. This visit, I was delighted by an invitation to sample the offerings at Cho Dang Gol, and it did not disappoint.

At first glance, Cho Dang Gol strikes a balance between traditional charm and modern finesse. Inside, it's a trendy haven that honors the authentic flavors of Korean cuisine. The staff were congenial, regularly replenishing our banchan, with a standout being the miniature seafood pancake.

Every dish I tasted was a testament to their culinary prowess. From the kabocha and potato pancake to the standout cod roe omelet—fluffy and brimming with texture—each bite was a delight. The baby octopus was tender, and the grilled bulgogi was richly marinated and cooked to perfection.

Cho Dang Gol isn't just another Korean restaurant; it's a place where the essence of traditional tastes is not only preserved but celebrated in a trendy and inviting setting. I wholeheartedly recommend this spot to anyone looking for a truly savory and authentic experience.

Title: A Delightful Lunch Haven for Solo and Time-Conscious Diners

I recently enjoyed an excellent lunch at a stunning and welcoming restaurant that truly understands the essence of a cozy ambiance. As a solo diner, I felt right at home, surrounded by an inviting vibe that radiated warmth.

The staff deserves high praise for their seamless teamwork and efficiency, ensuring that even the busiest professionals can savor a meal within the confines of a lunch hour. The offered lunch special, reasonably priced at $14, began with a fresh salad dressed just right, setting a refreshing tone for the meal.

While the chicken and shrimp dumplings seemed to lack a homemade touch, possibly prefabricated and reheated, they were still satisfactory. The highlight was undoubtedly the Pad Kea Mow. Though my request for an extra spicy kick seemed to have been missed or ignored, the dish still impressed me greatly. The noodles were cooked to perfection, with a generous serving of chicken and a vibrant mix of veggies, creating a harmony of flavors that truly resonated with my palate.

This restaurant has not only won my appetite but also my anticipation for a future visit—next time, hopefully, accompanied by a date.

This was a really cute find. My friend and I had exhausted our LES hang out spot and wanted to try somewhere new. Bar Belly came up in a Yelp search and a colleague confirmed it was a good choice. It's a super cute, dimly lit cocktail bar. The Happy Hour specials are incredibly, reasonably priced. I had the penicillin and an old fashioned. The Belly fries were delicious, but more importantly the spicy, chipotle sauce they come with. We lucked out and got serenaded with live jazz and had the perfect evening catch up sesh. When life resumes to some form of normalcy and restaurants reopen, we'll be here.

Title: A New York Slice on a Dime

Last night, my intro to the Big Apple included the mandatory dollar pizza experience, and it did not disappoint. Weary from our travels, my craving for a no-fuss, quick bite led me to a bustling spot where I snagged two cheese slices and water for a mere $2.75. The service was as impressive as it was swift, thanks to the notably efficient and amicable staff member manning the oven.

Sure, this isn't a contender for the 'best pizza ever' title, but its warmth and taste were exactly what I needed on a chilly New York evening. For those looking for a satisfying snack that's kind on your wallet, don't pass this place by. It's a simple pleasure that you'll be glad you didn't miss.

Last Thursday, my group of six arrived at this trendy spot at 8 PM and had to endure a bit of an organizational hiccup: a 30-minute wait despite receiving a notification that our table was ready. Once seated, service picked up and we eagerly ordered intriguing dishes like Pig Ear in Chili Oil and shared three dry pots with varying heat levels.

The pig ear was an unexpectedly delightful departure from the usual, with its unique jelly-like texture, while the dry pots, albeit a touch smaller than anticipated, were packed with flavor. Each customizable with a range of ingredients, from short ribs to tofu noodles, these pots, however, can quickly become costly as everything is priced à la carte.

At $30 per person — for what we ordered — the value is debatable, especially considering larger portion sizes can be found elsewhere in Brooklyn and Queens. The spiciness, too, was not as intense as expected, with the 'very spicy' pot barely hitting the mark.

In summary, for those with an immediate craving for something unique and aren't deterred by the price, this place could be a worthy adventure. However, those seeking better value and generous portions might want to explore other neighborhoods.

I recently ordered the trio combo for delivery from a local seafood establishment, a selection that promised a taste of the ocean with its crab roll, shrimp roll, and lobster roll, accompanied by a drink and chips. My experience was satisfactory, if not exactly remarkable.

The shrimp roll stood out with its flavor, hinting at the potential of the dish. However, the lobster roll was a missed opportunity to indulge in richness; a dab of butter or an extra pinch of seasoning could have transformed it. As for the crab roll, it was disappointingly bland, screaming for the simple yet transformative touch of butter to enhance its taste.

Additionally, the choice of chips as a side felt mismatched for the delicate seafood rolls. A side of crispy fries would have complemented the meal more aptly, contributing both texture and substance. In conclusion, while the combo was decent, it left room for improvement on several fronts.

Not a huge fan of the famous lamb burger here but the Caesar salad is definitely one of the best salads I've had. The lamb burger was cooked a bit rare for us when we ordered medium. The cheese on top was feta cheese which I'm not a fan on a burger and the bun was hard. The fries came with spicy cumin sauce which was good. We went around Christmas time and the restaurant is very Christmasy - with decorations and caroling! The drinks are sweet but pretty good but I would give the food here a 3.5 star. The service was good and attentive. Definitely a cool British pub vibe in here so the ambiance is different from other restaurants in the city. A little bit pricy for the food but worth the decor I guess.

Title: A Refreshing Twist on the Classic NYC Brunch at Green Kitchen

Upon first glance, Green Kitchen stands out from the quintessential bustling diners. Its exterior suggests a serene dining experience that bridges the gap between casual and upscale. Stepping inside, I was greeted with an extensive menu that caters to all palates—from conservative to adventurous eaters.

Service was attentive and efficient despite the usual swarm of patrons, including families, friends, and couples, finding their brunch bliss. The atmosphere was a welcome departure from the frenzied NYC brunch spots.

Portion sizes didn't disappoint, though prices edged towards the higher side. Nonetheless, for those looking for a quality brunch without succumbing to the trendier eateries, Green Kitchen delivers a solid experience. It's an ideal locale for families searching for that 'nice NYC brunch' vibe without the fuss.

Randomly walked by this cute Japanese spot in the East Village and decided to check out their lunch set don buri. You won't miss the place, there's several barrels of sake outside. I ordered the tsukimi tori don and my girlfriend got the una tama don. They both come with either miso soup or a salad. The tsukimi tori is basically fried pieces of popcorn chicken with a poached eggs with noodles and mushrooms. The una tama is grilled eel with a soft scrambled egg topping. Both were quite delicious and filling. The service is very friendly and the bathroom is super clean. This place gets an all around A. And a perfect spot for a quick hearty bite.

Title: A Satisfying Visit to a Bustling by Chloe Location

I recently dined at by Chloe during a busy lunch period and found that the bustling atmosphere could be overwhelming. To enjoy a more relaxed experience, I recommend visiting around dinner time. The restaurant is spacious, making it a comfortable spot once you secure a table.

The food, as always, arrived nicely packaged, with my Quinoa Taco Salad standing out for its burst of flavors. Despite the restaurant's size, they do struggle slightly with organization, which may lead to extended waiting times, particularly for larger parties.

However, they managed our substantial order without any hiccups, and everything was correct and accounted for, which is commendable during peak times. In summary, by Chloe delivered a satisfying meal, even amidst the holiday rush, proving why it remains a popular choice.

My mom and I decided to come here because their location in Chinatown was so highly reviewed and I wanted her to try soup dumplings. We had a great dinner, we were seated promptly and service was great. The restaurant is rather small, but that was fine, as they turned over tables fairly quickly. The pork soup dumplings were delicious and so flavorful, and the beef lo mien was good (nothing crazy). We also got the shredded beef with string beans and that was really good, very tender and the green beans were cooked perfectly. I honestly never would have come here tonight based off of this locations yelp reviews, but because the one in Chinatown was so highly rated, we decided to try it and I'm glad we did. I would definitely return, and really, if anyone is near Rockefeller center or Broadway, this place is a very quick walk and the soup dumplings alone are worth it!!

Ummm I love abiko curry! I love how clean the curry taste and the spicy is spicy. I tried the basic curry  with chicken cutlet and my sister got the udon curry with pork cutlet. Both were really good. The pork cutlet was better.They have 4 levels of spiciness. 4 is the spiciest. I got level 3 and my sister got level  2. Idk but I really like it and it's popular for a reason. I think it would be better if the cheese was inside and not outside the cutlet

This is my favorite Indian Fusion restaurant in the city and trust me there are several that are awesome .There is one person in particular that makes this place so welcoming and friendly that the excellent food is just a bonus and his name is Prasad. He's not just behind the bar and make you any concoction but he is all over from taking reservations to making sure you receive great service.I recently hosted my family for dinner after making  reservations  with Prada's. Manager owner Monica wasn't there but everything was smooth the entire eveningWe had the following and I can recommend all of it:Bhatti Murg ki ChampLasuni GobiHabanero TikkaKasundi PrawnsCorn PadduLamb ChopsGhost Chili KababChicken tikka masalaLamb biryaniGarlic naanChicken KulchaFor dessert Guava mango fluteHazelnut chocolate A very satisfying dinner and can't wait to return to New York

Interesting and more than just sushi.  Full bar.  Tables are close together so not a lot of privacy.  Everything we ordered was amazing.  The grilled shrimp was huge.  Prices were NYC.  I'd go back.  This is only location outside of Japan.  Enjoy!!

Title: Late-Night Bites at a Bright Spot

On a recent Friday night quest to quell my post-celebration cravings, I found refuge at this locale with its clean and bright atmosphere, perfect for winding down. The menu, a simple affair posted on the right wall, offered just what I needed.

Eschewing the typical burger route, I opted for the Chicken Sandwich ($8.50) and indulged in a Chocolate Chip Cookie Shake ($6.75). The pricing was reasonable, especially for a late-night spot, and service was brisk, with my order arriving swiftly.

The shake was a hefty, rich concoction that delivered on chocolate, though the promised cookie essence played hide and seek. As for the chicken sandwich, it was a bit of a letdown – the chicken was sadly overdone. While the sandwich fixings couldn't quite salvage the poultry, it was nothing a little ketchup couldn't handle.

While it hit the spot for a late-night fill, next time I'll likely heed the whispers of the patty and go for the burger instead.

I recently visited a new restaurant with my girlfriend, aiming to indulge in some warming noodle soup. Arriving just after opening, we were met with a near-empty venue and standard service. The bilingual waitress was a plus, ensuring no language barriers for both Chinese and English speakers.

We started with a shared appetizer of crispy fried pork, which was truly enjoyable – tender on the inside and perfectly crispy on the outside. For the main course, I opted for the Little Pot with a no-spicy request. However, it still packed a mild kick, which was unexpected, but the dish overall lacked depth, perhaps due to my non-spicy choice. The noodles particularly were quite bland.

Despite the highlights of the appetizer, the lackluster main course makes it unlikely for me to return.

If you're in the mood for a decadent treat, this restaurant doesn't disappoint. The highlight for me was the chicken waffle sandwich – savory, satisfying, and perfectly cooked. The communal experience of digging into the chocolate fondue with friends added to the fun, with a delightful variety of white, dark, and milk chocolates. Be warned, though, this place is a hotspot and tends to get crowded, so a little patience may be required. But trust me, the wait is worth it for the desserts alone.
I came here for lunch. Ordered farm salad w salmon. It was so delicious. Salad was very small portion though, so I would recommend you ordering at least one protein.

Title: New Go-To Spot for Happy Hour

I recently decided to check out a new spot for a spontaneous happy hour and it surpassed all expectations! The service was impeccable, creating a welcoming vibe from the get-go. The pub-style ambiance, complete with a standout illuminated bull statue, set the perfect tone for a relaxed evening.

The menu did not disappoint – especially the boneless buffalo wings ordered by my companion. As someone who typically steers clear of wings, I was impressed by these delectably seasoned strips of white meat that hit the ideal balance between flavor and spice.

Affordability is another plus at this joint, with reasonable prices and drink specials that extend beyond the typical happy hour window. Based on this delightful experience, it's safe to say this place has secured its spot on my list of after-work hangouts.

Cons: We came pretty early at 11am to beat the crowd. Unfortunately, a 30-45min becomes 1.15 hour wait for us. It's prob because there's 6 of us.  (-1 star) Once you gave your number, you are better off going somewhere till you are called.Our party consisted of 5 adult and 1 baby. We were charged 20% for a large party even though the baby didn't eat anything. That's pretty silly cause it's charged per body. (-1star)Pros: the chicken and waffles were pretty good. Portion was bigger than what most reviews mentioned. The waffles were crunchy and were accompanied with tasty butters. Bloody Mary was pretty tasty as well.

Title: Fair Prices, but Unremarkable Omakase Experience

Review:
While the omakase pricing at this establishment offers good value—$48, $60, and $85 options for a sizeable assortment of nigiri and a handroll—my experience was underwhelming when it came to the flavor profile. The sushi, though competently prepared, failed to leave a lasting impression on both myself and my date, and did not distinguish itself from other omakase experiences we've had in a similar price range. However, a delightful touch was the inclusion of tamago to conclude the meal, a personal favorite of mine. In summary, while the meal didn't soar to culinary heights, it didn't fall short in terms of value.

Great happy hour spot, it does end pretty early at 6 pm. 2 for 1 margaritas and beers are a great deal. Margaritas are frozen and strong. The food is also good, had nachos and chimichanga. Been here a few times and will compite to come back when I'm in the area.  The bar area is pretty small and gets super crowded! Not a place to go to if you're trying to have a conversation, better as a pregame spot with some friends.

Title: Italian Cuisine Delight with a Side of Hubbub

I recently visited an Italian eatery that left my taste buds reveling in delight, but the experience wasn't without its imperfections. The pizza and pasta dishes were nothing short of sublime. "Amazing" hardly does justice to the thin-crust pizza, which boasted the perfect crunch, and the pasta was cooked to absolute perfection, each bite better than the last. 

The staff, with the exception of the hostess who seemed overwhelmed and inattentive, were phenomenal, contributing positively to the dining experience. 

Be prepared for a boisterous atmosphere—this place is loud and always bustling with patrons, which I took as a testament to the quality of the food. Despite the noise and a less than welcoming entry, the delicious offerings make the wait decidedly worthwhile.

Overall, I'd rate it a well-deserved four out of five stars, docking a point solely for the hostess's indifferent demeanor. If you can handle a lively ambiance and a potential initial overlook, you're in for an exceptional Italian meal.

I absolutely adore this hidden gem nestled in the bustling heart of Times Square. The DIY burger concept is a major draw, offering a plethora of free veggies and fruits to stack on your patty. Embracing the opportunity, I craft a towering masterpiece that stands 5-10 inches tall—a true marvel in both flavor and presentation. Despite its tourist-heavy location, the quality of food and service is impeccable. Having already returned five times, I’ve played host to out-of-town friends, each of whom has left with nothing but praise for this delightful eatery. A must-visit for any burger enthusiast in the city!

For restaurant week 2019 I finally made it to Delmonico's for a solo dinner. I was about 15 minutes late but the staff still accommodated me, which was nice. There were two floors which calls for segregation from the restaurant week people and their high end regular clients. My waiter was awesome and knowledgeable about the menu items. I reviewed the menu for restaurant week and the appetizers were different variations of their regular menu appetizers. So I settled for the burrata with arugula, beets and poached pear, which was tasty with the Portuguese white wine. For the entree, I settled for the miso butternut squash glazed bass, which was part of their regular menu was beautifully presented. The skin was crispy, and the meat combined with the squash and the leeks plus the white wine was perfect, and I felt sad when I finished the plate. But, the highlight of my three course meal was the baked alaska, which I paid $8 more because it's their classic recipe. The dessert presentation was amazing, the walnut cake, banana gelato, and lemon meringue plus carmelization smokiness was to die for. This would be a great special occasion restaurant or for a date night for two.

Came opening day to Urbanspace W52 and on my list to checkout was Eisenberg's for there Egg Cream.Well they offer the standard chocolate and vanilla and I am a vanilla guy.  So I got my vanilla egg cream and it has more body and less foam than some of the other's that I had lately namely Gen Spa or Ray's. But it had the same taste because the legit shops all use Fox's U-Bet as the syrup.Now Eisenberg's was not the best on my list but it's good enough to not take a subway ride to the village or Brooklyn when I need my fix.  But the main complaint here is that real Egg Creams supposed to be foamy.Now if they can't do Egg Creams right do you want to try and the Pastrami, Reuben, or Tuna Melts sandwiches and what about Matzo Ball Soup ?

Title: A Cheesy Haven in the LES

From the moment I tasted their offerings at the grand opening—spicy tomato soup and a classic grilled cheese sandwich—I was hooked. Each visit to this Lower East Side gem reaffirms my love for their comforting fare. Their garden Mac and cheese bursts with fresh flavors, while the buffalo chicken grilled cheese provides a delightful kick.

Do not miss out on their homemade lemonade, a refreshing companion to the cheesiness. The location is convenient, a stone's throw from the F train and multiple bus routes, making it a perfect chill spot to satisfy your cheese cravings.

Pro tip: personalize your meal! I love swapping beef for chicken in the nachos and adding goat cheese to the tomato soup for an extra layer of flavor. Highly recommended!

Cute little gem in the area! I love the vibe here, and the staff are so friendly. Great spot for a date or nice dinner out with friends!For a table of 3, we ordered the calamari to start which was delicious. The squid was fresh and perfectly seared, paired well with the potatoes and seasonings. We also shared Linguine alle Vongole and 2 Margheritas (one regular and one with GF crust). The linguine was tasty, but came with barely any mussels. Next time, I'll probably try a different pasta on the menu. The pizzas were great! We all preferred the GF - worth a try if you stop by this place :)

While better than dollar pizza, this spot doesn't live up to my beloved neighborhood pizzeria. The Large Cheese Pizza offered an impressive cheese pull but was let down by its inauthentically thick and slightly undercooked dough (3/5). The Eggplant Parm Hero disappointed with a disproportionate bread-to-vegetable ratio, featuring a thick ciabatta that overwhelmed the scant eggplant layers (3/5). The Garlic Knots, although well-formed, skimped on the garlic and were overly oily, leaving my fingers greasy (3/5). In summary, the offerings here fall short of the mark, especially when compared to my usual haunt, even at a similar price point.

Here for a business trip and was craving for some Korean food. Came across this Korean tapas place and let me tell you, this place is LEGIT. I'm from Southern CA where Koreatown and Korean food is synonymous to the dining scene, the offerings here at Barn Joo is amazing. I ordered the bulgogi veggie wrap set and the chicken wings soy garlic with gochuchang on the side. The bulgogi was very tender and flavorful. I loved the smoky char flavor on their bulgogi. It came with green leaves and jalapeño and red onion. It's was so delicious. The chicken wings were crunch on the outside with the right amount of sweetness and a hint of heat. I was so pleased with my dinner. And they offer a shot of their soju cocktail for doing your Yelp check in. Will definitely be back here when I visit NY again.

Callie's take out service is a hidden treasure right now located in the middle of Harlem on the famous Malcolm X Boulevard. Rum punch and Margaritas go for 7 bucks each. Happy Hour is from 3-7..Monday through Friday and every order comes with a mandatory food item unfortunately. The bartender was beautiful and very polite. This place seems to thrive on a heavy crowd and can't wait to have restrictions lifted to operate at full capacity. Check it out if your in the area and see for yourself.

Dining at Tuome is a fabulous experience.We ordered:Chicken Liver Mousse - Fellow liver mousse lovers, you must order this when visiting Tuome. The mousse is light in texture and rich in flavor with a variety of textural accompaniments to round out the dish. Loved this.Octopus - The octopus was perfectly cooked and plated in a cool way. Would definitely try again.Pig Out for two - The star of the show, we LOVED the pig out. The pork was crispy, tender, fatty, meaty, savory, and sweet. It basically encompassed all of the food adjectives. It came with a fantastic sauce, salad and peanut noodles. I wish the peanut noodle bowl had been endless.Beignets - Flaky, crunchy on the outside, soft on this inside with a lovely caramel sauce. Just yum.The ambiance is romantic and cozy. Perfect location for a date or an intimate dinner with a small group friends. Our server was attentive and was very knowledgeable about the menu which was helpful in our decision making. Would definitely come back.

Title: Pricey Decadence Meets Imperfect Warmth at Prova

In the heart of Midtown, where inflated prices are the norm, Prova's $7 four-cheese Sicilian slice may prompt a double-take. The cost is ambitious, stretching the wallet in a way that might make one reconsider their lunch options.

Despite the price tag, the slice itself is a cheesy indulgence that soothes the palate with its rich flavors. While it's no traditional New York slice, the bready crust has its own charm when expectations are appropriately set. Taste-wise, the slice delivers.

However, Prova needs to fine-tune its reheating game. The experience of a warm, crispy edge giving way to a disappointingly tepid center is a letdown. Ensuring a uniformly heated slice would significantly elevate the dining experience.

Although I wouldn't recommend a special journey to Prova, if proximity and a pressing hunger are factors, and the line is mercifully brief, it's a viable spot to quell the cravings with a slice that's flavorful, albeit steeply priced.

Came here on a Sunday night. Ambience is sort of classy/casual so it could be a fun place to go eith friends or with a date. Heard good stuff about the dan dan noodles so had to order those and was not disappointed! They were incredibly flavorful and tasty. Got the dumplings in chili sauce which were also pretty good. For the entree, got the dry pepper style, which was crispy and delicious. All this food for two people was bit of an overkill; I think we could've done without the dumplings. Either way, leftovers are never a bad idea! Service was excellent and our waiter kept checking in on us to make sure everything was going well. Definitely will be back and definitely recommend!

I'm from Boston and truly was expecting this to taste somewhat similar to Bonchon. It was good but definitely had too much salt. I felt as though the sauce on the chicken was not enough as well. I had ordered the soy garlic and sweet n spicy. The soy garlic was just alright and the sweet n spicy was too sweet for me. I also had the fried rice with an egg they added too much black pepper. Overall the food was ok.Food: 3Customer service: 3

Title: A Fair Feast with a Few Surprises

After hearing rave reviews, my boyfriend and I decided to give Waylay a try, particularly intrigued by their chef's table. The unique experience of watching the chefs at work added a layer of entertainment, although the space was cramped and awkwardly positioned in a walkway, limiting our comfort and the number of dishes we could sample simultaneously.

Our culinary journey began with the chicken satay, which was tasty but not exceptional, bearing resemblance to what one might find in a local Chinatown. The clams, unfortunately, were disappointingly over-spiced. The lobster noodles, while overly salty, stood out from the menu and hinted at the potential of the dishes here.

The nasi goreng fell into the category of a well-executed classic but didn't quite excite our taste buds beyond the realm of good fried rice. The true standout of the evening was the oxtail stew – a dish so remarkable that it alone justifies a return visit to Waylay. The passionfruit pandan dessert, although slightly overpowered by vanilla, was delightful, especially with the added touch of passionfruit seeds. It's a must-try for dessert aficionados like myself.

Rounding out the experience were the robust and well-crafted drinks that did not disappoint in strength or flavor.

In summary, while the hype set a high bar that not all dishes could match, Waylay's oxtail stew and passionfruit pandan dessert did leave a memorable mark, ensuring that this wouldn't be our last visit.

French food done RIGHT ... and for a reasonable price at that. I came here for a group reservation dinner on a Saturday evening at 6pm and the experience could not have gone any better. We were seated promptly at our timeslot, but the restaurant never got extremely crowded, which was actually great and a nice change for a good restaurant. Most of the restaurant was occupied, but there were moments where a few tables were empty here and there, which gave us breathing room. In addition, we didn't have to scream across our table to talk to each other since the noise level was relatively low.Since we were there for an early dinner, the Prix Fixe Early Dinner menu (5-6:30pm) was available to us, with a choice of a starter, entree and dessert for just $29.95! Woohoo! And, shockingly, almost everything sounded really good. A few of us went for the Prix Fixe, while the others went for the regular menu. Here's a quick run-through of some of the items we ordered:ESCARGOTS - Part of the regular starter menu and it was refreshing. Glistening in garlic herb butter and flavors coming out of every angle of the escargot. If you're into escargot, get it!FRENCH ONION SOUP (+$2) - THE starter to order if you're ordering from the Prix Fixe. It was hot, cheesy and delicious. For a prix fixe French Onion Soup, it was damn good.WILD MUSHROOM RISOTTO, PARMESAN & BLACK TRUFFLE - My entree from the Prix Fixe menu and it was everything I hoped it would be. The truffle and mushroom permeated through the dish and the risotto was almost perfectly cooked, maybe a little al dente, but it was very, very slight. I'm a bit biased towards risotto because I love it and if you're a fan of risottos, this would be the choice from the Prix Fixe.PAN-SEARED LOUP DE MER, PALM HEARTS, WHITE WINE SAUCE - My wife's entree from the Prix Fixe menu. Nicely plated, but the bass wasn't exactly what she thought it'd be as it was lacking some flavor. There was sauce on top and on the bottom, but something about it was just a little off.STEAK FRITES, HANGER STEAK & POMMES FRITES - This was a friend's entree from the Prix Fixe menu. I didn't get to try a whole lot of it, but it was a huge order. There was a ton of frites on the plate and the steak portion was generous. I had one piece of her medium steak and it was perfect - Juicy, tender and portioned well for each slice.ASSORTED SORBET & ICE CREAM - Our table shared in the sorbet and ice cream. If you order the sorbet or ice cream, you're allowed up to 3 scoops from 4 different flavors. Honestly, I don't remember all of the flavors, but we basically devoured it all quickly.Besides the fantastic food, our waitress couldn't have been friendly. She was very patient throughout the evening as we took our time eating and dining. The atmosphere was also very casual, with some people dressed nicely, while others were on the casual side in t-shirts. If you're looking to have a group gathering or just want to have a quiet, relaxing, delicious dinner, Le Midi checks all of those boxes.

Title: A Vietnamese Culinary Delight in East Village

My recent visit to this Vietnamese gem nestled in the East Village was a delightful experience that I must share. Reservations are a must for parties of six or more, which makes it convenient to avoid the queues—a plus in my book.

Upon arrival, we were promptly seated within a mere 15 minutes of our set time. The house beer proved to be a perfect companion to our meal, reasonably priced at $6, and is a must-try.

We indulged in a variety of appetizers, including crispy spring rolls, summer rolls, and a uniquely surprising papaya & pig ear salad. The latter was the star, transforming what might sound unusual into a delectable treat.

My friends raved about their shellfish curry, hearty and visually appealing, while I found solace in a bowl of beef pho priced at $16. The broth was rich, though a bit more meat wouldn't have gone amiss. Accompanied by a crispy breadstick, a simple addition that elevated the dish, it made for a memorable meal.

The ambiance was cozy and relaxed, making it an excellent spot for an intimate dining experience without the overwhelming noise.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit to this culinary oasis. Highly recommended!

I recently ordered delivery from this restaurant, and I was pleased with the prompt service and accurate order. The Cobb Salad, priced at $15, was a delightful surprise with its generous portion and exceptionally fresh ingredients, including perfectly cooked bacon, flavorful grilled chicken, ripe avocado, hard-boiled egg, red onion, crumbled bleu cheese, and tomatoes. It was, quite simply, delicious and a meal in itself.

The Sliced Filet Mignon, at $11, was unfortunately a bit of a letdown. Although it arrived hot, by the time I was ready to eat, the meat had become dry and was less tender than what I've experienced in the past. The accompanying toasted garlic English muffin, designed to soak up the meat juices, was just okay, and I ended up discarding it. However, the horseradish crème provided a nice touch, albeit not particularly spicy.

Overall, the star of the meal was the Cobb salad, which I would wholeheartedly recommend and order again. The filet mignon, while reasonably priced, might not make it into my cart for a second round.

After a long day, feeling too weary to face the hotel's room service menu, I turned to GrubHub and found a gem that delivered right to my door. My choice was spot-on: a succulent salmon atop a bed of crisp mixed cabbage, drenched in a transcendent panang curry that had just a whisper of coconut-infused spice. It was a harmony of flavors I yearned to revisit immediately.

The green beans, still vibrant and with a hint of garlic, were a crunchy delight, while the sriracha zucchini, despite lacking the anticipated heat and being slightly mushy (perhaps a casualty of my late order), was enjoyable. The real surprise was the larb mushrooms—a side that truly elevated the meal.

With my order completed by two bottles of Evian water, the entire experience was seamless and swift—a mere 20 minutes from order to arrival. This effortless feast was the perfect cap to an exhausting day.

Charming little spot that I follow on Instagram. I have been dying to try so we Popped in for a cocktail and dessert. We found seating at the bar. The bartender was engaging and informative. He recommended the hummingbird cake. We were served a big slice of cake. The frosting was light and the cake very light. It was fabulous. He also offered us a taste of Italian Amaro after dinner drink which we had never had. We watched several entries being served. The French dip looks Devine. Great experience all around.  We will def be back.

Title: A Sweet Spot with a Festive Flair

My recent dining experience at this charming establishment proved to be as delightful as it was visually pleasing. The restaurant, with its colorful decor, exudes a cool and cute vibe that's matched by a menu of fancy desserts that are as much a feast for the eyes as they are for the palate.

The staff's demeanor, while adequate, lacked the warmth and inviting nature you'd expect from such a vibrant place. However, the prices are reasonable for the city, and the ambiance more than compensates—with lively Christmas music enhancing the already cheerful atmosphere.

A standout was the licheeade—a delicious and whimsically presented beverage that, along with the desserts, comes highly recommended. These sweet offerings are not to be missed and will leave you planning your next visit.

On a Sunday outing, my companions and I were pleased to find a bustling crowd yet no wait time for a table, which was an unexpected bonus. The festive spirit didn't stop at the music; however, be cautioned that the gifts and roses onsite, while tempting, are notably pricey.

I'm already looking forward to returning and sharing this gem with my mom, as I'm confident she'll be enamored with the experience just as much as I was. If you're in the area and looking to indulge your sweet tooth or enjoy a refreshing drink, this spot is a must-try. You won't regret it.

Title: A Wallet-Scorching Experience with Perfect Meat at [Restaurant Name]

If your wallet's feeling heat, that's because [Restaurant Name] has prices that might set it ablaze. Although the cost may singe your funds, the quality of the meat is undeniable—it's cooked to absolute perfection. The catch, however, is the portion size. Ideal for a small gathering of 4-6, but a large group will likely leave yearning for more.

The dining experience here is interactive, with servers grilling the meat right at your table to your liking. Remember, don't just focus on the meat—embrace the side dishes to create a fulfilling wrap and balance your meal.

While the meats are a culinary delight, it's a fine line between worth and want. For a small, meat-loving company, it could be just right. Larger parties, be warned, your hunger may not be satiated.

A word to the wise, the aromatic embrace of your meal will linger lovingly on your clothes well after your visit—so maybe skip the dry-clean only attire and opt for something cozy and washable.
Worth the wait! Get there early if you can. I loved the uni on beef sashimi, shiso and nori dish!

Recently, I had the pleasure of dining at a restaurant that's been on my bookmark list for a while, and I'm delighted to report it lived up to my expectations. As part of the esteemed group that brought us Trademark, this establishment offers the same high standards in dining.

The service was exceptional—warm and attentive without being intrusive. The ambiance strikes a perfect balance with its charming interior. Guests have the choice between enjoying the lively atmosphere of the patio or opting for a more tranquil experience by the bar.

The menu didn't disappoint. I indulged in a chopped salad with beets and chicken, which was a revelation in flavor. The broccoli tacos followed suit, showcasing both creativity and culinary skill. Each dish was a marvel in presentation and portion size, proving that quality does indeed beat quantity.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit when I'm back in Chelsea. This restaurant has certainly earned a spot on my go-to list for future dining experiences.

If you're trying to decide between this and Ben's Pizzeria across the street, I'll save you the trouble - Ben's is terrible and Artistic is great.Sure, Artistic is tiny, but their pies are fresh, the owner is the nicest dude, and they have pretty inventive pies (including vegan options).I got a plain and asked what their specialty was. And that's how I ended up with a plain and a chicken ranch slice. Both were pretty damn good! And cheap!This will definitely become one of my go-to drunken Greenwich Village late night stops.

Title: A Flavorsome Korean Curry Experience in KTown

My girlfriend and I decided to try out a Korean curry spot in KTown this past Sunday night. To our delight, there was no wait at around 7 pm, and we were seated promptly upon arrival. I opted for the Pork Cutlet Set priced at $18.99, while she chose the pork curry rice for $12.99.

Pros: The curry itself was a standout — distinctly Korean with its thinner consistency and packed with flavorful chicken and scallions. My pork cutlets were fried to perfection, crispy without being overly greasy.

Cons: When it comes to value, the Pork Cutlet Set seemed a bit steep, particularly when other spots like Go Go Curry offer more generous portions. It was also surprising that the "pork curry rice" did not include a pork katsu, necessitating an additional purchase for a complete experience.

Overall: This restaurant offers a delectable Korean twist on curry that's well worth trying out. Despite a couple of drawbacks, I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a savory curry fix in KTown.

This is a hidden gem in terms of a great Happy Hour. I'm not speaking about energy here more in terms of prices. The staff was kind of personable - the bartender was somewhat nice, but also borderline rude if that makes any sense. Glows:-Great happy hour even on the weekends (Fri-Sun 12-8 pm)- Food looks yummy and fresh -When ordering pitchers are probably your best bet Grows:-Some drinks on the menu can't really be altered because they are premade or so I was told-If you're prone to getting acid indigestion I would suggest sticking to beer. Most of the drinks that I tried seemed like the person making them added too much sour mix which can mess up any good drink. -Bartender could have been friendlier. -Next door is karaoke and also another spot across the street - always fun. Might stop by again if I'm in the area.

Title: A Mixed First Impression at The Soho Diner

My inaugural visit to The Soho Diner within the chic confines of the Soho Grand had its highs and lows. Expecting the sophistication synonymous with 'upmarket,' the absence of a turkey burger option seemed like a menu misstep, yet the no-substitution policy felt needlessly rigid. Initial service could best be described as 'confused,' with staff members still finding their rhythm, though one notable exception shone through the hiccups.

The interior boasts sleek, trendy booths that hint at the professionalism behind the establishment, yet this image is cheekily undercut by what appears to be toy-like silverware – a whimsical choice that doesn't suit the otherwise grown-up vibe. Also, the lavatories echoed the compactness of a train's, which might be charming for some, but not for all.

Culinary redemption came in the form of a richly flavored $12 roasted tomato soup and a perfectly executed $26 king salmon plate, elevating the dining experience. However, the necessity of requesting bread to accompany an already pricey soup felt slightly off-key.

The menu itself is expansive with 75 items, though the lack of flexibility is something to keep in mind. While breakfast and dinner offerings present a more appealing value proposition, and the food is undoubtedly delicious, one can only hope that, with time, the diner will upgrade its flatware to match the quality on the plate. A second visit is on the cards, but it's the cuisine, not the cutlery, that'll be the draw.

Title: A Sunday Delight at Dutch Freds

My impromptu visit to Dutch Freds on a Sunday afternoon turned out to be a remarkable experience. Greeted by the lively strum of live music, which we learned is a weekend staple from 11-2, the atmosphere was instantly welcoming.

Perched at the bar, the service was nothing short of excellent, with the bartender dishing out both drinks and charm in generous portions. I experimented with the Happy Feet, a zesty non-alcoholic cocktail which I spiked with vodka, and it did not disappoint – flavorful and thirst-quenching. Meanwhile, my mom's dirty martini received high praise, living up to the standards of any discerning aficionado.

The spinach and chicken salad was another highlight. The chicken was succulent, nestled among a bounty of fresh veggies, making for a satisfying meal.

For a spot nestled within the hustle and bustle of NYC's tourist pathways, Dutch Freds offers surprisingly reasonable prices and a slice of tranquility. This establishment has etched its way onto my go-to list for future visits.

Have been here twice and had favorable experiences each time. Our first visit was spent at the bar only and we were impressed by the extensive cocktail list as well as the friendly and attentive bartenders. We tried the white lady cocktail which was incredible and actually brought us brought a second time. On our following visit, we were impressed by our window table with a great view of Columbus Circle and also by the great service once again. I highly recommend the burrata which was uniquely served with pears and hazelnuts but not the traditional bread accompaniment. The truffle tagliatelle was also good but did lack flavor although some salt and pepper did the trick. I also loved the decor- very hip, colorful and fun. Props to the stylish and well dressed maitre d was very welcoming and made us feel at home.

Title: A Dazzling Culinary Experience at Manhatta

If it were possible to award six stars, Manhatta would unquestionably deserve them. The epitome of fine dining, my recent visit there has been the highlight of my year. Despite the price jump to $94—a notable increase from $78 last year, and even the $88 I paid in May—the experience justifies every penny.

The unparalleled views of the Brooklyn Bridge set the stage for a dinner prix fixe that tantalizes the senses. The lobster quenelle, a dish so remarkable that I remain hopeful for its return to their seasonal menu, ensured that Manhatta left an indelible mark on my palate. Accompanied by a scotch nail, exquisite wagyu, tender duck, warm date cake, and a delightful soufflé, each course was an ode to culinary excellence.

Service here stands out, with a personable server who strikes the perfect balance, devoid of the pretentiousness that often plagues upscale eateries. Elegantly relaxed, my evening stretched into three hours of dining bliss, punctuated by a stunning sunset beside the Brooklyn Bridge.

Manhatta is more than just a restaurant; it's a destination for celebration. Be prepared to reserve a table a month ahead - a commitment that is absolutely warranted for such a memorable night.

I recently visited the Chelsea location of a restaurant I had enjoyed at Bryant Park, seeking a spot for a business meeting with the added bonus of a happy hour. This location didn’t disappoint—it was indeed more relaxed, making it an ideal setting for combining work and pleasure.

Upon arrival, the hostess promptly seated us once my party assembled. We took advantage of their happy hour, which ran until 7pm, featuring both drinks and food specials. Our appetizers included wings and oxtail croquettes which, though tasty, were modest in size—the wings arrived in a serving of five, and there were three croquettes to share.

My beverage choice, a mojito priced at $8 for happy hour, was perfectly balanced and set the tone for the meal to come. For my main course, I opted for the Char Sui Pork accompanied by a sweet potato purée, a dish that was exceptionally flavorful and beautifully presented.

The ambiance was conducive to our business needs, with background music quiet enough to allow easy conversation, well-sized tables that accommodated our notes, and lighting that was bright enough for comfortable reading. All said, it proved to be a superb venue for a business meeting, with the added delight of great food and drink specials.

this place is kind of far for me but I'd say it was worth the travel. came here to meet up with a friend and for the first time in forever I just know what I want right away (usually I'm the most indecisive person when it comes to choosing what to order). went for the vegan platter because it's exactly the kind of dish that I love.food takes time to come out but this place has a very nice ambience and atmosphere so it's perfect to just chill, talk, and catch up as we wait. service was amazing! the waitress was so polite, attentive, has great vibe, and make sure everything goes alright. and when the food comes, I'm so satisfied with how it turned out. decent portion, and plus it looks really pretty too. the vegan platter contains: tabouli, greens, beet salad, spicy eggplant salad, roasted eggplant salad, hummus, and pita bread.everything tasted great and fresh but the winner has got to be the spicy eggplant salad. it was eye-opening good! i really enjoyed the dish!also tried the lamb kofta and the sauce on the side is so good! the kofta was tender, flavorful, and fragrant! it was amazing.price is average. overall it was a great experience!

Title: A Roast Duck Noodle Delight in Chinatown

I recently visited a cozy little spot in Chinatown and had an experience that left a memorable taste in my mouth—the roast duck pan-fried hand-pulled noodles were nothing short of divine. Perfectly balanced in flavor, these noodles were just the right amount of sweet without being overly salty, and the duck was tender, easy to eat, and packed with taste. It's a dish I'm already planning to have again on my next visit.

While the fried pork dumplings and beef soup didn't quite hit the same high note, they were still satisfyingly good. We arrived at a bustling 1:30pm on a Saturday and snagged the last available table, thankfully avoiding a wait. The restaurant, true to Chinatown form, is quite compact, offering an additional basement seating area that I didn't explore.

Heads up—this place is a cash-only establishment and prices are a tad higher than neighboring noodle joints (though still a bargain relative to NYC standards). Despite this, the roast duck noodles are a draw that can't be ignored. For that dish alone, I'll be back.
The staff here was so helpful and informative! Just Salads as a company no longer chops their salads unfortunately.

Title: A Bite of Paris in NYC: La Sirene Review

I recently had the pleasure of dining at La Sirene, a delightful French bistro that has captured my taste buds not once, but twice. Upon entering, you're greeted by the authentic French-speaking staff, which adds to the charm and authenticity of the experience.

The French Onion Soup here is a must-try and stands out as one of the best in NYC. It's rich and packed with onions, topped with the perfect amount of melted cheese. Another appetizer, the Goat Cheese Tart, set a high standard with its delectable flavors.

For main courses, La Sirene shines with both the buttery Pan Seared Hanger Steak and the Braised Rabbit Dijon a la Creme from their Restaurant Week menu. Each dish was expertly cooked, the steak so tender it nearly dissolved on the tongue, and the rabbit moist and beautifully complemented by the creamy white wine sauce. A side of assorted vegetables for two accompanied the entrees, and my steak came with a slice of perfectly layered potato gratin.

Though I don't frequent this neighborhood often, La Sirene gives me the perfect excuse to return for an exceptional French dining experience. A reminder of Paris on the streets of New York, this restaurant is an absolute gem.

For someone who loves steak, Ikinari is one of my guilty pleasures. Lets be real here, for $25, you're not getting the best 10 oz ribeye out there. However, is the steak still fatty and juicy? Yes. Does the sizzling pan make me happy? Yes. Are all the condiments fun to occasionally dab onto my steak? Yes.It's a little gimmicky, but I enjoy the experience each time. Eating a tiny bit of wasabi with my steak and downing it all with beer just doesn't seem to get old for me. Whenever I'm craving a decent steak that won't break the bank, I know I'll probably still head for Ikinari.

I recently visited the final location of the renowned artichoke pizza chain, which proved to be a bit of a hidden gem, tucked away inside a supermarket. Despite the initial challenge in locating the place, the helpful staff within the building quickly pointed me in the right direction.

The purchasing process was unique – you pick up your food along with any groceries and pay at the supermarket's main cashier. Consistency is key here, as the pizza maintained the creamy artichoke goodness I've come to expect from their other outlets.

They offer enticing lunch and dinner specials depending on when you drop by. Seating is limited to a small area resembling a diminutive cafeteria, so be prepared for a cozy dining experience.

A word of advice: resist the urge to fold your slice, Brooklyn-style. My friend attempted it, only to have the cream topple out, inadvertently turning the pizza into a makeshift dip. However, this mishap did result in an unintentionally delightful concentration of flavors with each bite.

Title: A Consistent Delight: Stone Bridge Pizzeria

I've been a regular at Stone Bridge since its grand opening and it has never failed to impress.
