Perfect for a quick lunch break or a relaxed dinner post-work, this place offers ample seating to accommodate crowds. The commitment to fresh ingredients is evident in every dish, catering to a variety of dietary needs with options like gluten-free crusts. The selection of sodas is refreshingly unique.

I'm a fan of the 'build-your-own' pizza that allows for personalized creations, though I must tip my hat to their mushroom pizza - a must-try for fungus aficionados. However, I'd suggest skipping the salads; they're just average and you'd find better at a place specializing in greens.

Stone Bridge is a gem I confidently recommend, having received two thumbs up from everyone I've introduced to its culinary charms.

Title: A Hidden Gem Near MOMA

Having stumbled upon this delightful restaurant in close proximity to MOMA, my experience was nothing short of wonderful. The food and service both deserve top marks, impressing with their quality and attentiveness. A serene upstairs dining area offers a scenic view of the museum, providing a tranquil escape amidst the bustling city. Although the prices are on the higher side, the overall experience was so enjoyable that I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit. This spot is certainly a must-visit for museum-goers seeking culinary excellence.

Came here thinking it was another place, which turned out to be right around the corner. I had made a reservation through Open Table, and when I was seated by the host, they asked if we wanted to be in the bar for Happy Hour menu or the main dinning area for the full menu. We chose the Happy Hour menu, but then they wouldn't verify my reservation for the points, which was kinda wonky tbh. The Happy Hour was fine prices for the neighborhood. It's an upscale taco place. Definitely splurge on the chips and salsas. The three kinds are truly delicious and they'll bring you more chips at no additional charge, which was a fortunate surprise. I got the pollo taco, which was good, not amazing, but pretty tasty. We also got the duck confit app which was super small for the price, but also tasty, so toss up on value there. It didn't get very busy on a Tuesday night. There are tables in the bar area for Happy Hour along with plenty of bar seating, and a large dining area for the full menu. I would recommend if you are interested in trying many different kinds of tacos that you do the Happy Hour where you pay per single taco and can mix and match, instead of on the full menu where you get two tacos per order and cannot mix and match those two.

I had an amazing experience at this restaurant, particularly with their artichoke pizza. For just $6 per slice, the portions were unexpectedly generous, easily satisfying two people. In fact, the slice was so large it required two plates!

The pizza itself struck a perfect balance with a crust that was both soft and subtly crunchy. The cheese was plentiful without being excessive, allowing the flavors to shine through. As my introduction to NY pizza, this place set the bar high, and I eagerly look forward to my next visit. Highly recommended for anyone looking to share a delicious, oversized slice of pizza heaven.

I recently dined at this well-patronized spot with my mother and grandmother and found the reservation process to be quite tight; only very early or late slots were open two weeks out. Upon arrival, the insistence on waiting for my full party before seating was a bit of a cold welcome, considering the half-empty dining room. A request for brighter lighting due to dimness-induced discomfort was also declined.

Service-wise, a highlight was our waiter's proficiency in handling my garlic/onion intolerance with utmost care, going as far as to deconstruct dishes to accommodate my dietary needs.

Our meal started with the kale Caesar, priced at $14.95, which regrettably lacked in heartiness and paled in comparison to similar offerings at places like Sweetgreen. The General Jane's honey fried chicken, at $19.95 for six pieces, was a win – even without the sauce, the chicken boasted a perfect crispy exterior. The double cheeseburger, enhanced with an egg for an extra $2.95, was praised by my dining companions for its high-quality meat.

A minor hiccup occurred when a wood shard was discovered in the burger. Our waiter handled the situation with grace, promptly addressing the issue and offering adequate compensation.

In summary, despite some initial setbacks and one disappointing dish, the establishment redeemed itself with its meat-centric entrees and commendable service recovery. Stick to the meats for the best experience.

The ambience is a YES. The staff is a YES. The food is an ABSOLUTE YES!The decor is fab at Wayan and makes it a go-to spot for that special date or small group gathering. The food here is delicious & on par with flavor. Presentation is on point. And the representation of Balinese culture is on point with a fancy flair.DO get the lobster noodles - wavy noodles immersed in spicy lobster sauce, then topped with buttery poached lobster & a tidbit of basil. DO get the clams - baked with just a hint of coconut & perfect notes of sweet and savory, soft and crunchy all in one bite! DO get the pandan pudding - creamy vanilla & pandan pudding topped with crunchy passion fruit seeds.I loved the intimate atmosphere but I just came with one of my girls ;) Perfect for small celebrations but my home girl & I just wanted girls night out, haha.

New spot that opened up next to my house. Exotic and loud decor with fast and friendly service. I had the fried rice and it was good. My friend ordered the curry and liked it as well. Not show stopping, but solid spot.

Service here was horrible. Lots of staff running around in all different directions. How about one if you jumping in and helping out!? Table next to us sat down, then got up and left with 3 minutes of seating. Food was eh. Lots of the same stuff served different ways. Really needs pics on a menu at a place like this. Didn't know what anything was or what to expect. I ordered the appetizer gazpacho soup that was like a shot glass of soup. It was good but it wasn't chunky like I expected. It was tomato broth with a few diced pieces of tomato. Tasty but tinyyyyy.  We had the tomato bread appetizer which was good. Not great. Toasted bread brushed with tomato juice. For lack of anything else to chose from, my husband ordered the pressed ham and cheese sandwich. It was very, very thin with not much too it. Minimal filling. He was starving!  The wine is served in a small, stemless glass container. Doesn't look like much. I won't be back.

Title: A Mixed Bag Experience at a Yelp Elite-Recommended Spot

After a previously organized event piqued my interest, I ventured to this restaurant to delve deeper into its offerings. The experience kicked off on a precarious note with wines from Vino – two surprisingly small pours set me back $30, which seemed excessive. I'd recommend buying a bottle elsewhere to enjoy here instead.

Service throughout was underwhelmingly slow, detracting from the experience and making the high price tag for beverages feel even less justified. However, the culinary journey redeemed itself with the ham and cheese sandwich from Bocatas & Empanadas, delivering a delicious buttery and perfectly toasted treat at a more reasonable price ($12-$13).

Moving on to La Barra, the seating system was confusing, requiring a hostess for guidance. The beer served was refreshingly cold and pleasing, a contrast to the scanty croquette dish that featured a mere two pieces – tasty, but not satisfying. The spicy chorizo wrapped in potato chips added a nice kick, while the chicken skewers served with delightful bread were the culinary highlight.

The market-like setup of the restaurant didn't quite meet expectations, with an air of chaos and steep prices that didn't match the value received. Its best feature is undoubtedly the location – nestled in a vibrant area ideal for exploration and adjacent to high-end shopping.

In summary, the restaurant isn't a complete letdown if you're in the area and looking to pass the time, but don't set your hopes too high – especially when it comes to your wallet.

Title: A Gem on the UES Serving Healthy Asian Delights

I recently stumbled upon an extraordinary spot just steps from my Upper East Side apartment. Craving wholesome Asian cuisine, my brother and I ventured in for a Saturday lunch and were not disappointed. I opted for the poke bowl with salmon, served over brown rice and adorned with seaweed, carrots, scallions, daikon radishes, and a sweet soy sauce that brought the dish to life. The freshness of the salmon was unequivocal, and the portion generous.

My brother's choice, the Shanghai Bowl, with its tender, perfectly seasoned beef on a bed of brown rice, was a meat lover’s delight. Each bite was savory and satisfying, with a sweet sauce enhancing the already robust flavors.

At around $22 for two bowls, the value was excellent, especially for the quality and quantity of food we received. Service was swift, our meals arriving within five minutes of ordering—impressive!

In summary, this place is a must-visit for anyone seeking a quick, nutritious, and delectable meal that won’t strain your wallet. High marks and highly recommended!

Title: Oasis Above the City - A Review of the Third-Floor Bar

My visit to the bar on the third floor was a mixed bag, but with some notable highlights. The prospect of a two-hour wait for the coveted indoor rooftop seats is daunting, especially when the alternative is braving the sweltering New York summer without the relief of air conditioning.

Despite seating challenges, the drink offerings showed promise. The RH Bellini was a standout, offering a refreshing and delicious escape from the heat, accompanied by a surprisingly generous pour. The Spanish Rose, however, fell short, its sour notes not quite hitting the mark for my palate.

The highlight, undeniably, were the expansive white pillow couches that beckoned with the promise of comfort—and they delivered. It's not every day you find a bar that also sells furniture, adding a unique twist to the ambiance.

Post-visit, I was impressed by the attentiveness of the management. Their effort to reach out for feedback speaks volumes about their dedication to customer service.

Overall, I recommend this spot as a stylish retreat from the heat, perfect for lounging in luxury with a delectable Bellini in hand.

I visited this restaurant drawn by their attractive happy hour wine specials, which, I must admit, were quite decent. However, the food didn't match up to the same level. The menu items were overpriced, and the flavors failed to impress, leaving much to be desired in terms of taste and quality.

Okay I've been to No 1 Tacos pretty much every trip to NYC....I wish I would've know about this hidden gem all those times. The fish taco is  soooo yummy. Some of the best I have had. And the homemade corn tortilla makes all the difference. Don't waste your time on the shrimp taco tho...it's all about the fish!

Had a really great dinner here. I had an 8:30PM reservation for Wednesday night but came at 7:30 hoping to get seated earlier. The restaurant was poppin so I couldn't get seated until 8. Also the place was really loud so it was hard to have a conversation, but come for the food.The Khao Soi was not my favorite because the noodles were al dente & there were way more fried wonton noodles than my friend and I would've liked. Get the Pork Belly Adobo! It paired really well with the coconut rice. The sauce + poached egg + rice + pork belly combo made for a delicious bite every time.Lastly we got the halo halo for dessert. It was pretty filling in and of itself and had a good coconut-y flavor. I'm so glad this place exists. Thai + Filipino food in one place = great meal. I would come back to try all the other dishes I didn't get to eat in this visit. This place is family style so bring lots of friends if you can and split everything!

Title: Decent Pizzas, Not The NYC Classic

We swung by this pizzeria just minutes after doors opened, which was a smart move considering the throngs that flocked in later. Venturing off the beaten path, we opted for the hot honey pizza and a burrata pizza. While topped with quality ingredients, the pies had a density that deviated from the typical NY-style slice. They weren't disappointing, but they lacked that 'wow' factor you'd expect from a city like this. My suggestion? Go with the crowd-pleaser - The Grandma pizza, which is this spot's claim to fame.

Cute little romantic, candle lit date spot. Had sushi here. We ordered some tuna and salmon dishes (the crispy rice tuna was amazing) to share. We then had a layered green tea dessert which was delicious with tea. Must have is the lychee martini. Very nice and different.

Came here the other week and had a truly phenomenal experience. Got the eggplant caponata, and it was the perfect balance of savory and sweet. The truffle focaccia was also a great appetizer. For entrees, got the cavatelli with mushroom ragu, which was super tasty. But my favorite was the fusilli Alla Napoletana. It was seriously one of the best pasta dishes that I've had in a while. Also don't forget a side of Brussels sprouts, so delish! For dessert, we got the lemon ricotta bomboloni with Nutella cream and holy yum! I could've eaten a dozen. Highly recommend this WV spot!

HB burger is an authentic American restaurant, serving comfort food and is located close to Times Square. The ambiance was causal and waiters were friendly but not attentive. The food was decent but not outstanding with reasonable price compared to other restaurant in the neighborhood. We tried their Chopped Caesar Salad, Burger Royale and Southern Fried Chicken Sandwich. The Burger Royale which made with ground beef, bacon and fried onion ring was the best; the patty was juicy, well cooked and well balanced with cheddar cheese and aioli sauce. The veggies in salad were not fresh and dry with too much dressing.

Came here after a long stroll at the Brooklyn bridge. Me and my friend were craving pizza so bad so... (PSFP)Place: it's a pretty big place compared to the other pizza places I've been in the city. Service: the guys weren't very friendly but they were quick to do their job so I'm okay with thatFood: the pizza was ummm. It wasn't bad but it wasn't anything special too. I've been to better placesPrice: I guess the price isn't so bad after all since the portion is bigFor short, if you're REALLY hungry and want pizza this place is great portion wise. But if you're looking for NY pizza that will blow your mind. This isn't it.

This place is pretty awesome. The food was very good and the women working there were friendly and efficient. You line up cafeteria-style and choose your food and you can then either dine in or get it to go. The dining space is not fancy but it is a decent size kept clean as I saw them cleaning the tables pretty quickly. We chose to eat a little there and buy to go as well.The star here is surely the food. If you've never tried west African food you are in for a treat. My husband is Nigerian and we devoured the jollof rice and wished we had bought more. This is our second time here and I'm certain we will return.

I read about this place being legit on ny.eater.com, so I figured I'd give this place a try today after having my favorite zest sechuan down the street.I got the L08 Kung Pao Chicken lunch special, which on the delivery.com website said it was tingly, etc.  It was not overly sweet like some others on here said, but I was disappointed by the spice level and had to add my own Ning Chi chili oil to get it where I wanted it.  It did have a very slight numbing, but hardly noticeable for more than a second for a few times.The Hot & Sour Szechuan Soup was better than Z-Szechuan IMHO.  More soupy and less syrupy.Rice was perfect, as it should be.I will come back and try a few other lunch specials before making a final verdict on whether I just stick with Zest Szechuan.

Yes it's a bit pricey (but not THAT pricey), but the food is so good, so I definitely think it was worth it!!! Eggplant salad - not actually a salad, but was super good. It's really just 4 small pieces of eggplant filled with some minced meat (I think), and was really good - probably my favorite dish here! Ground pork noodles - very flavorful! I really liked it. I would recommend that if you also get the hometown lu fen to finish the ground pork noodles first (so as to not overpower the mild but delicious taste of the ground pork noodles)Hometown lu fen - has a touch of spice that's really good. At first I didn't like it was much as the ground pork noodles, but the more I ate the more I liked it! Winter melon - very good. My husband's favorite dish! Was slightly sweet, very flavorful. Supreme tofu - was very good in my opinion. It was a very soothing meal.

Title: A Charming Lunch Break at Up Thai

My recent lunch at Up Thai was a delightful experience from the moment I stepped inside its charming interior. The attentive servers ensured a refreshing glass of water was always at hand, adding to the welcoming atmosphere.

My friend and I opted for the lunch specials, a wise choice considering the affordability. I enjoyed a crisp salad while she savored a warming soup. Our shared appetizers included tasty dumplings and a unique chive pancake, which offered an unexpected twist on the traditional.

My main dish, the Pad See-Ew, struck the perfect balance of flavor and texture, truly "yummy" in every sense. My friend's pork entrée also impressed with its remarkable taste, making our lunch selection a hit.

Up Thai's lunch offerings provide exceptional value, and though I anticipate higher dinner prices, the quality and service would likely make it worth the cost. An easy recommendation for anyone seeking a cozy spot with delicious Thai cuisine.

I recently visited this spot for a taste of their pizza and was pleasantly impressed with both their regular and Sicilian slices. The pizza boasted a thick, generous layer of cheese and a hearty helping of sauce, all served up in satisfyingly large portions that pay homage to classic old school New York style. The flavors were spot on, exactly to my liking. If I had to point out a flaw, it would be the size of the crust, which bordered on being overly substantial and lent a slightly too bready texture to the slices. Nonetheless, it's a minor quibble in what was otherwise a delightful pizza experience.

We popped into this cozy spot for a casual Friday night of snacks and sips. While we snagged seats swiftly, there was a bit of a wait for our drinks. The Riesling was as refreshing as hoped, but the kitchen's heavy hand on the fryer left the gyoza a bit overdone for my taste, and the grilled edamame's char was overpowering. Despite the missteps in my small plates, the welcoming vibe was a plus. It seems like a place better suited for sushi lovers, so I might pass on a return visit for snacks.

My boyfriend and I came here during Valentines weekend on our vacation, I felt like the maze is more of a lounge thing if you want to get drunk and just grab appetizers with friends. I think overall the experience was pretty fun. The service was quick, we ordered a bottle of wine and Soju. I also got the kimchi pasta and tacos. I would definitely recommend the kimchi pasta tho, 10/10!!! I would probably be back next time I come to NYC. The lounges decor was really nice for pictures!

Came here during happy hour on a Thursday evening to enjoy a quick bite and a brew. Modern interior with a bunch of table seating as well as bar seating.Happy hour menu consists of several small plates as well as basic drink options. Opted for the Lettuce Wrap ($5) and Duck Wings ($6) from the HH menu and a Matcha IPA ($11) from the regular menu. Lettuce wrap is okay, doesn't hold up well in your hand, though the meat is seasoned well (maybe too much mint). Duck wings are tender and glazed nicely. While my beer was expensive (as are a lot of other beer choices here), the brew was different and interesting pairing. Service can be a bit slow here, as there was only one person taking orders for the entire place (until later in the night). Pricing can be wonky here, especially for beers, but the food is enticing.

I continue to adore this gem of a restaurant. The value for money here remains unbeatable, especially considering the exorbitant prices at a place just two blocks away that offers far less food. Bonus tip: Check in on Yelp during your visit for a complimentary scoop of ice cream! A visit here is always worthwhile.

I typically steer clear of deli buffets, yet I found myself pleasantly surprised by this gem. The selection of well-seasoned, health-conscious dishes truly stands out. For those mindful of their waistlines, it delivers excellent value. The maki sushi rolls deserve a special mention, with their fresh, quality cuts of tuna and salmon. The roasted salmon is cooked to perfection, avoiding the all-too-common pitfall of being overdone. The shrimp salad is another highlight, featuring succulent medium-sized shrimp packed with flavor. And for a light touch, the fresh baby arugula is crisp and delightful. Highly recommended for a satisfying, guilt-free meal.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience at [Restaurant Name]

My dining experience at [Restaurant Name] last Friday evening was absolutely delightful. With a reservation in hand, my party was promptly seated upon arrival. The menu offered tantalizing choices, and we indulged in a meat and cheese platter followed by a well-done steak, delectable spinach, and succulent octopus. Each dish did not just meet but exceeded our expectations in flavor.

The ambiance of the restaurant added an extra layer of pleasure to our meal. The spacious interior afforded a view of the kitchen's bustle, enhancing the dining experience. Whether planning a romantic evening or a casual catch-up with a friend, the setting proved to be perfect. The low lighting, chic bar, and unique ceiling design contributed to the inviting atmosphere.

Service was generally amiable, although there were moments when summoning a server proved challenging. Nonetheless, the upkeep of the restaurant, including the cleanliness of the restrooms, remained beyond reproach.

In summary, [Restaurant Name] presents a fusion of delicious cuisine, a welcoming ambiance, and service with a personal touch, albeit occasionally distracted. It's a dining destination I would recommend and revisit.

Title: Convenient Location with Mixed Experiences

I recently visited a restaurant just across from the Brooklyn Bridge Park water play area, which made it an ideal spot for a post-playtime lunch. Opening at 11am, we were able to head straight there after a morning of fun. The establishment boasts a spacious outdoor seating area complete with shaded umbrellas, perfect for a breezy day. Though there's mention of a rooftop space, we stayed on the ground level due to the heat.

Seeking respite from the sun, we chose to sit indoors. The space, unfortunately, lacks air conditioning, but open windows and a couple of fans helped alleviate the heat slightly. The menu was diverse, with options ranging from pizzas and sandwiches to pastas, catering to various tastes.

The ambiance was somewhat marred by the loud music containing explicit lyrics, which was not suitable for my children. While I requested a volume reduction, the staff complied minimally and with apparent reluctance. While the location and food variety were positives, the indoor comfort and music choice left something to be desired on this occasion.

Title: Cozy Spot with a Few Hiccups

My dining experience at this place was a mixed bag. The restaurant felt a bit congested, especially at the back tables. It’s not ideal when constant foot traffic disrupts your meal or when you're unexpectedly sharing a six-seater with strangers.

On the menu, the Turmeric Latte and Cafe Au Lait fell short of expectations, but the kitchen redeemed itself with the Shakshouka and Early Lunch, both of which were flavorful and satisfying. The Zaatar Scone was decent but not remarkable. However, the complimentary pita bread was an absolute standout – the softest and tastiest I've ever had.

Despite the seating snags, the ambiance was pleasing and the service competent. In essence, come for the amazing food, but you might want to avoid the back tables.

Title: A Disappointing Pizza Experience

I ventured into this pizza spot hoping for a slice reminiscent of my beloved New York or New Haven styles, but regrettably, I came away unsatisfied. The balance between cheese and sauce was unsettlingly skewed – an abundance of cheese overshadowed the nearly absent tomato sauce. Halfway through the slice, I decided to discard the remainder; a bitter decision considering the $4.75 price tag.

My brother's experience echoed my sentiment, as his Sicilian slice bore more semblance to a cheese sandwich than a traditional pizza – it too found its way into the waste bin.

The sole redeeming quality of our visit was the staff's politeness, which shone through their excellent customer service. Sadly, even that wasn't enough to save the overall disappointment. One can only hope the pizza dough is better matched with its toppings in the future.

After a family visit to Shanghai Heping Restaurant, a spot highly regarded by our discerning auntie with a particular taste for Shanghai cuisine, I'm left with mixed feelings. The restaurant's culinary offerings, particularly the spicy beef tendon, certainly met expectations—both flavorful and generous in portion, presenting a solid value for the price point.

However, our dining experience was overshadowed by service and cleanliness issues, prompting a modest three-star rating. Staff interactions were marred by discourteous behavior and communication challenges, detracting significantly from the overall ambiance. Additionally, the restaurant's standards of cleanliness fell noticeably short of expectations, lagging behind what is typically acceptable, even within the bustling environment of Chinatown’s dining scene.

Feel like this place is like a hidden gem, I felt like this place would be a fufu Thai place. I actually came here twice during my business trip to NY. I guess that means something right? First time I came with friends who live in NY, they have a wide variety of options and items I've never tried before. I liked how they had many vegetarian options, try the spring rolls and vegetable dumpling. They also give you a little butternut squash soup for a taster. Their pad Thai and pad sew ew were my favorites! Their drinks are very yummy! I forgot what I got but it's a must try!

Walked by couple of times and saw this was a very popular restaurant, so I made a note to try it. Came in on a Tuesday night at 6:30pm with my friend, and the place wasn't too crowded yet but had several tables dining. We sat down and I noticed the variety of seafood displayed by the kitchen. There was also a nice bar where you can grab and drinks and wait for your party to arrive. When I looked at the menu, I was surprised to see this is mainly a seafood place and the prices were $25-$40 an entree which was a bit more than what I planned to spend that night but we already sat down so we were committed. Trying to strategize and try a bit of everything, we ordered one small salad, one appetizer, and one entree to share between the two of us. I think it was plenty because the entree came with a lot of fish!Very friendly staff, good food, and we got a complimentary dessert which was a nice surprise. Would come back and visit just to eat the app, it was a very very good dip.

On a quest for a delightful lunch, my friend and I discovered a hidden gem on a quiet Thursday afternoon. We timed our arrival perfectly at noon, just before the lunch rush that poured in around 12:30. Early birds definitely get a serene start here, so take note.

The moment we stepped inside, we were wrapped in the warmth of its stunning interior—a cozy embrace highlighted by soft lighting and a romantic, dark red color theme. It's easy to envision couples basking in the amorous atmosphere come evening.

Our table was a smorgasbord of flavors: the kumquat and passionfruit green teas were refreshing, albeit with an average syrup quality (3/5). The Dan Dan Noodles, however, were exceptional (5/5)—chewy, just spicy enough to tease the palate, and utterly satisfying. The mapo tofu (5/5) arrived in a generous portion, its smooth and savory goodness a delight. The standout, surprisingly, was the Chicken Herbal Soup (5/5)—priced at a mere $10, it felt like a restorative elixir for the soul.

Kudos to Frank, the manager, whose kindness and attention to our experience didn't go unnoticed. The staff mirrored his hospitality with their own pleasant demeanor. For an overall excellent dining experience, I recommend this restaurant wholeheartedly.

Absolutely make a trip to this gem for the milkshakes – they're a marvel. The Valentine's Day shake indulged us with its strawberry decadence, adorned by a rim of icing and sprinkles, and crowned with a generous slab of red velvet cake. The Midnight Madness was an ode to chocolate lovers, its rich shake embraced by a chocolate icing and chip-encrusted rim, all topped with twin fudge brownies and a layer of whipped cream. The shakes are not just drinks but desserts in their own right. Don't hesitate, treat yourself to these renowned concoctions.

I stumbled upon Miss Lily's quite by accident. I was headed to Jane's to meet friends and since my name is Lily and I was a half hour early, I decided to pop in for a drink. I sat at the bar and I was just loving the vibe. The reggae music and the staff were so friendly and chill. I spied the guy's grilled salmon and it looked beautifully cooked! LOL. I ordered a homemade Ginger Beer and it was delicious!! The best ginger beer I ever had. The guy with the salmon said he comes to Miss Lily's whenever he's in NY and he said was very authentic and comfort food for him. The guy to my left looked like a young Snoop. I called an audible and asked if the rest of my friends would mind changing venues. They were able to accommodate a party of five and I was so happy we did. Like LA Guy said, "You can get food like Jane's anywhere. I guarantee this food will be way more flavorful".  It was a good call and we love absolutely everything we ate. We got the Crab Boil which is only served on Tuesday nights. Lucky us! The Crab Boil has corn, potatoes, two kinds of crab, Cole slaw and something else I can't remember. It doesn't matter. It was awesome. We also ordered the vegetable lo mein. Ooh that packed some heat. Again, yummy. The oxtail stew was sumptuous. I wanted more. My friend ordered the Curry Shrimp. I don't eat curry but he said it packed a lot of flavor and he's very fussy. Even the side of rice was tasty, flavored with coconut. That was not my mama's rice but it tasted so good with the oxtail sauce from the stew. I was a very happy camper and a little relieved that everyone else liked it too. Considering I changed plans 20 minutes before we were supposed to be at another restaurant. Sorry Jane!The service was great, especially considering how crowded it was getting. We were in the back room with a huge party of 22. And we had a nice circular booth, which always makes for a much better experience in my opinion. I took one star away because it was so hot. Granted it was like a heat wave outside but it was really hot even with the a/c going full blast. It was a bit of a drag to be so uncomfortable while eating outstanding food. I also wish the serving sizes on the lo mein and oxtail were bigger. Really just nitpicking but I can't give it a perfect score unless everything was perfect but on food, value and service. For food, ambience and service, I give Miss Lily's an 8 out of five stars. I will come back again. If you're looking for delicious, flavorful, perfectly executed food and you want to have a good time with great music and an Island feel, Miss Lily's is the place. It's my new favorite restaurant. I'll be back on a cooler day. I love it when an impromptu change of plans falls into place. Thank you Miss Lily, the bartender, Snoop and Mr LA.  It was definitely the right call to switch restaurants!

Came here not expecting much after dinner. But was pleasantly surprised with the marinara sauce they have. Their pizza and just about everything was really good. The meatballs were weird. They were like falling apart and the taste was not great. But everything else I loved. I've even craving to come back here.

Unfortunately, my dining experience at this particular establishment was far from impressive. The ambiance was hindered by a cramped setting, where patrons were expected to seat at dated kitchenette tables, accompanied by an overbearing volume of Caribbean music.

The quality of the food did not help to salvage the evening. I opted for the curry shrimp, which was a letdown due to an excessive amount of sauce that overwhelmed the flavor of the shrimp, which, to add insult to injury, was overcooked.

Service did little to alleviate the underwhelming meal. The waitress appeared hurried and displayed irritation when we inquired about the menu options, contributing to an unwelcoming atmosphere. It's safe to say that I won't be recommending this establishment based on this experience.

Venturing into Paris Baguette instead of my regular Starbucks across the street turned out to be a delightful surprise, thanks to my dad's suggestion. The moment I stepped in, the intoxicating aroma of fresh bread was undeniable and set the tone for a wonderful experience.

The visual feast of sandwiches and pastries was almost overwhelming. I indulged in the croque monsieur, a sophisticated twist on the classic ham and cheese sandwich. It was masterfully toasted, with a perfect contrast between the robust crust and the soft, warm center. My father opted for the turkey mozzarella focaccia, which was elevated by a seasoning that tantalized our taste buds.

Though tempted by the extensive array of desserts, we refrained, but I am determined to explore the cakes on a future visit to the corner of 52nd and Lexington.

Seating at Paris Baguette is limited, but we snagged a spot with ease. The space seems to cater more to the grab-and-go crowd, which makes sense given the bustling city location.

In conclusion, Paris Baguette is a gem for anyone with a penchant for carbs and quality quick bites. I'll definitely be back for more.

Last weekend, post-Andy Warhol exhibit at the Whitney, my partner and I stumbled into the Chelsea Market chaos. Hunger nudging, we aimed for snacks but found a culinary treasure at mokbar—a haven amidst the packed corridors. With serendipity guiding us to the last two counter seats, service kicked off promptly as our eager waiter navigated our order with grace.

Our palate piqued at K-Town Fries ($5), an Asian-inspired mountain eclipsing any fast-food expectations (not that I'd admit to frequenting those, of course). Laden with kimchi, nori, and gochujang, they were the crispiest of delights—far from mere "snacks."

The K-Pop Chicken and Waffle ($9) delivered a twist—a blue corn waffle cone cradling succulent fried chicken. While the chicken and rice cakes hit high notes, the cone fell flat, a novelty better suited for dessert rather than a main act.

Curry Chicken Katsu ($12) rounded out our feast. Generous in portion, its breaded chicken harmoniously married with the robust curry flavor. A less soupy take on ramen, it was more than sufficient for two. Accompanied by an excellent green tea ($3 or $4), the meal hit all the right marks.

For about $30, contentment was achieved, despite the nuisance of close-quarters dining amongst a sea of queued patrons—just a minor gripe. My advice? Seek out a quieter time or visit mokbar's Brooklyn outpost for an equally satisfying but more tranquil experience.

Came here for an event having a typical Chinese banquet of ten dishes. Had come here for dinner upstairs which has its separate staircase. The main level can accommodate about 15 tables of 10 people each. There are TV monitors throughout the restaurant.Loved the first course which was the standard jellyfish, octopus, seaweed salad, spareribs and crispy fish. Other main courses included soup, prawn with broccoli, Peking duck, beef cubes (pretty tender), tofu with mushrooms, fried fish with greens (delicious), lobster (fried with eggs, yummy), fried rice, noodles and of course red bean soup to end the meal. Everyone was so full by the time the fifth dish came. And you can image there were lots of takeout boxes. Service was attentive. Food was not bad. Restrooms are located in the basement (not the best ones though).

My friend and I decided to dine in at a local restaurant known for its variety, and we were not disappointed. The highlight of our meal was undoubtedly the lamb noodles, which were absolutely delicious - rich in flavor and perfectly seasoned. While the chicken special was just okay and didn't quite meet our expectations, it didn't dampen our overall dining experience. The Xiao Long Bao (xlb) we started with were a delightful beginning, offering a good balance of taste and texture. Adding to the pleasant experience was the very nice staff who were attentive and cordial throughout our visit. I'd return for those lamb noodles in a heartbeat and recommend giving them a try!

Wow! Right off the bat this place is beautiful! The décor and menu was during the spring season, and my friend and I opted for the $32 brunch special where we got a pasty, appetizer, and entree. Beet Pesto Salad: Sooooo flavorful! The pesto was bursting with flavor, and the beets were complemented it perfectly. This came with a side of toasted baguette, and served as a perfect savory appetizer.Burrata Salad: This salad came with a side of salad with a light citrus vinegrette and strawberries. This was my favorite dish of the day! Highly recommend it if you see it on the menu! Pineapple French Toast: This was VERY sweet. It served more as a dessert than an entre. A slice of toaste was soaked in batter and ended up tasting more like a bread pudding than a French toast. On top was a caramel-tasting sauce, and all topped with grilled pineapple. Only get if you have an extreme sweet tooth!Everything crusted Branzino: Two slices of branzino, coated with almonds with pickled onions on top and a fresh cream sauce beneath. Highly recommend this dish! The onions and sauce cut any kind of overt fishy-taste, and it was just delightful!! Fried Chicken Sandwich: A solid chicken sandwich, nothing stands out. Chicken was flavorful and juicy, and was placed between two brioche-type buns with coleslaw, which was on the drier side. Definitely will seek out this restaurant when I'm back in the area. Such a great place to hang out, have any kind of get-together, and the food is always solid and delicious. Each dish had a combination of unique flavors I have never tried before, and I felt feeling....more educated in terms of my palate! amazing!

Title: A Delightful Lunch at Uncle Boons

We stumbled upon fortune last Friday noon, easily settling our group of seven at Uncle Boons with a mere five-minute wait. Although a tad cramped, the coziness did not deter from the culinary adventure that awaited us.

The Tom Yum soup, though startlingly small at $5 a cup, was an explosion of flavors, arguably the best I've ever savored, chock-full of fresh ingredients. The Thai tea babka French toast presented a subtle twist to a classic, a pleasant albeit not standout appetizer.

Our palette was further intrigued by the Kanom Krok; these coconut bites were pleasant, though they didn't quite leave a lasting impression. The Khao Phat Rot Fai, on the other hand, was a revelation. This fried rice dish boasted a perfect serving size and the freshness of each ingredient sang through with every bite.

Sampling the crab cakes and stuffed cabbage rounded out the meal nicely, confirming that Uncle Boons has an array of great options to choose from.

In essence, Uncle Boons delivered a satisfying experience with some dishes truly shining through. We left ready for a return visit - the hallmark of a successful dining escapade.

We came here for breakfast with our mom and we had a great time. It was pretty empty when we came in on Tuesday morning. We were seated immediately. I ordered the challah french toast with a cappuccino. My mom ordered the herbed eggs with tea and my twin ordered the Israeli breakfast with regular coffee. We don't have any complaints about anything. The food was really good. Our waiter was attentive. I'd come back.

I pass by this place all the time, but never went inside. I was craving pizza the other night and tried it for the first time. I was not disappointed although I prefer the margherita pizza over the mushroom one, just because the truffle oil was a bit heavy. The cheese on the margherita was so perfectly dispersed. The sauce wasn't too overpowering since I'm usually not a fan of tomato sauces. Would cone back again to get a quick and delicious lunch.

It actually took me some time to find this location because from the outside it looks like a pawn shop. Once you go past the back door of the pawn shop, you'll find yourself in this very grand magnificent restaurant that's decorated with peacock feathers and chandeliers and a sky facing window that looks like the top of a greenhouse. We came for brunch and I got the lemon blackberry ricotta pancakes! They were super delicious and incredibly filling. We also got their burger which was also very flavorful too and a good compliment to the pancakes. Overall it was an amazing experience.
Very flavorful ramen Specialty Tokyo miso was quite good Spicy komo miso was nice in flavor Great value No atmosphere Ok service Solid 3.5*

I met a friend here for lunch and arrived right when they opened. We had a nice table in a corner. The decor is sleek with some retro touches. It's a good spot for a date spot or power lunch.Our waiter, Jackson, was attentive and also good at reading the table, as he noticed we were deep in conversation and not quite ready to order. He also replaced my water after noticing himself that something was in it. Also, I appreciated his mentioning that the juice wasn't fresh squeezed and really just for the bar.My burger was medium, though a little unevenly cooked ($19). But it was juicy, and the bacon and jalapeño were great touches. I appreciated the side salad, as well.Maybe a tad more expensive than my average lunch, but it was a nice treat.

Came here for dinner on a Thursday night around 7:30 with a group of friends. We were seated immediately. The dishes were all so delicious. I had the sriracha noodles with shrimp. The noodles were soo flavorful and the shrimp was amazing! Texture was perfect and had a great amount of flavor. My friend got the pad Thai with shrimp was really interesting. It was a bit sweet and tangy which made for a really good combination. Another friend got the green curry with shrimp and it was soo good! It was the perfect amount of spicy (my friends and I love spice, but some may find it too spicy) and flavorful. I got the Thai tea which was the perfect amount of sweet and it was delicious. Although, I would ask to go easy on the ice next time. The glass is very thin so it gets watered down rather quickly

I recently visited a restaurant that boasted a pleasant atmosphere conducive to relaxation. While the service was laid-back, the food unfortunately did not leave a lasting impression – it was passable but lacked flair. It's not a restaurant I'd go out of my way to visit again, yet I wouldn't mind popping in for a drink if I happened to be nearby. Overall, my experience lacked excitement upon departure.

I find myself In Little Italy annually for the San Gennaro festival. This year, my friend and I split a deliciously sweet and cheesy arepa before venturing into Aunt Jake's. I was drawn here based on the many reviews on Yelp, but we should've looked at the lunch menu before sitting down as the lunch menu was as expensive as the dinner menu! It was double the price compared to other lunch options around. There were also no drink specials, which was surprising for a Sunday afternoon. We asked for the complimentary garlic breadsticks, which were really good! My friend got the Chicken Parmesan which was about 22-23 dollars for 2 pieces of chicken. The portion was huge for lunch, but what we expected for the price. There was an option for pasta with it for another 6 dollars. For the pasta dishes, you can choose the style for a base price and depending on what sauce you add to it, there's an additional fee. I got the tagatielle with carbonara. It was tasty, but nothing extraordinary. I would probably come here again for dinner. If i could, i would give it a 3.5 star.

Knew this wasnt going to be a groundbreaking meal the minute I walked in. This has average written all over it. What  I didn't expect was the type of service we received. We will touch on that later. This italian american food was as standard as you can get and one thing I will never understand is how pricey it is for a piece of chicken parm or chicken piccata. It was not bad food but it wasnt top notch. You can set your watch to this italian food. Wont blow you away but you wont be disappointed. Now for the service... here is the situation... while ordering our lunch I didnt like that the server didnt tell us the sides were extra. She simply asked if we want spinach or broccoli with our main meals.  Usually italian dishes come with a pasta or side of vegetables so she never clarified that. She never once mentioned it wasn't part of the meal because she made it sound like it was. What servers don't realize is when you upsell you have to be honest because you arent fooling anyone. The extra few bucks she made on tip by ripping us off doesnt help the integrity of the place. This place would have received 3 stars if it wasnt for us feeling like we got ripped off. Honesty is always the best policy in my book.

Visited the restaurant at 2pm and encountered all employees gathered at a table, engaging in a loud conversation. This continued until we requested they quiet down. While the food impressed us, the service and ambiance left much to be desired.

I came here to try their vegan desserts.  They had a pretty large selection: cupcakes, cakes, cookies, rice cereal marshmallow squares, cinnamon rolls, brownies, and pies.  They also have CBD infused brownies, cookies, rice cereal marshmallow squares, and cupcakes now too.  My friend and I shared a pumpkin pie.  It was cold so we asked if they could warm it up but they said they couldn't.  Most bakeries, even Starbucks, would warm items up for you.  The flavor of pumpkin filling was tasty and I liked the marshmallows on top.  It wasn't that sweet.  The crust was thick but it wasn't flakey (probably since it didn't have butter).  The desserts were pretty, colorful, and taste great for being vegan.  I just wish they would warm up the items if a customer requested it.

I recently visited a local restaurant for lunch and decided to try their chicken curry over rice accompanied by a Thai iced tea. Unfortunately, the curry was disappointingly salty, detracting from the overall flavor. Additionally, the dish utilized ground chicken, which lacked a distinct quality and texture. I found myself wishing for real, substantial pieces of chicken instead. The Thai iced tea, however, was a pleasant complement to the meal. Despite the beverage, I would hesitate to recommend the curry based on this experience.

Went with a group of friends to this spot , my first time trying Vietnamese cuisine . It's a small spot in Murray Hill , but they were able to cater a group of 8. From the sign outside they claim to have the best PHO, and it actually was really good . We good few appetizers and also decided to try their Special Tomahawk. That's what I was really excited for. It was actually cooked to perfection and was paired with bore marrow. Overall the food was great . It was a great experience!!Ambiance- 8/10WiFi - Not Sure Service - 10/10Reservation- Yes Large Parties - Call to Ask Parking - Good Luck

We came here as a group of 4 for a lovely dinner while visiting some friends in NYC. We made a reservation ahead of time, but the restaurant had a lot of empty tables anyway. Overall, it was a great experience with with the small portion sizes being the only drawback.What we ordered:Mushroom pizza: amazing! Very light and delicious.Scrambled eggs: unexpected for dinner but very yummy!Brussels sprouts: lowkey my favorite vegetable ever, but Gato served it well with pomegranate Bread pudding: tasted a bit like tiramisu, but overall very yummyOlive oil cake: I liked this dessert a little less, but it was still goodAmbiance 5/5: Gato is romantically dark. There is enough light to see you companions, but not too much. It's a lovely space with beautiful decor.Service 4/5: pretty standard, but our food came out very quickly which is a major benefit.
The soba noodles for which Azuma is known were delicious and the sesame ice cream is a nice way to finish lunch. The $18 set is expensive for soba plus 3 pieces of salmon and sides.

If you're down to try dry hotpot and don't mind spice, this is the perfect place for you. I've been to the East Village location as well, and I like both locations. I came around noon on a Friday for lunch with no reservation, and it was poppin'. Thankfully there were seats at the bar, so we were seated right away! (+ there was A/C next to us and the bar stools were so comfy). They do individual lunch sets for $13 but you can also just order one pot with as many toppings as you want (which we ended up doing). We got "mild" but it was still pretty spicy! And we added pork belly (so good), eye of round, rice cakes (also delicious), broccoli, lotus roots, and bok choy. The portion was more than enough for just us two, so I got the rest boxed up to take home (just need to make more white rice to pair with it)! Would definitely recommend trying this place out for lunch or dinner, but try to make a reservation as it's pretty popular!

The hospitality is keen here.My friend discovered this restaurant through Instagram and realized it was part of the works of Hand Hospitality which also created "Her Name Is Han" along with seven other restaurants around Koreatown. We attended its opening night back in February. My friend reserved a table for 4 at 6:15 p.m through its website. There was no wait time. Once we arrived we were seated immediately. The meal, service, and food made the experience wonderful. For a table of 4, the meal was reasonably priced. ~~ 9.0/10 Hospitality: Throughout the course of the evening, our waitress came by often to answer our questions, explain the concept of the restaurant, provide suggestions, explain the cooking procedure, and ask us about our preference. Menu: The menu is particularly interesting and well organized. Displayed is a key to tell you if the dish is gluten-free, vegetarian, chili, hot & spicy, or if it has seeds, tree nuts, peanut butter, egg, shellfish, Mollusca, and/or dairy. It also includes noodle choices, ingredients in each dish, and price per serving size. Before appetizers arrived, we were served the complimentary banchan (the amuse bouche portion). We were also given options for different sauces if we were interested in them. Each person received his/her/their own set of 3 small banchan dishes to try. The first was a gray, cloudy dish that had a pasty consistency, the second was a small tomato pastry, and the third had a nutty taste. For appetizers, we ordered the Pine Nut Espuma Shrimp Salad and the Grilled Short Rib Patty. The Pine Nut Espuma Shrimp Salad is a light, healthy version of the Chinese walnut shrimp dish with broccoli. It was light and fluffy. The Grilled Short Rib Patty dish was well-cooked light beef patties. It was incredibly tender, delicate, and light. The glass noodles under these beef patties remind me tiny pieces of shrimp chips in the Chinese crispy chicken with shrimp chips dish that you typically see at banquets. The complimentary dishes we were given were the pickled cauliflower and spicy clams. The pickle dish is expected in many Korean banchan dishes. The spicy clams were incredibly fresh and had a good mix of flavor. The complimentary dishes are subject to change. For the "Pot" section. The "Pot" dish is the primary focus of this restaurant - Korean style hot pot. The first portion of this section comes in either Shiitake & Oyster Mushroom Rice or Seasonal Vegetable Rice. We decided on the Shiitake & Oyster Mushroom Rice. The rice cooked while we ate our appetizers. The mushroom rice was soft. For my taste, it was well-cooked. You also get a choice between stuffed eggplant or chicken tofu ball. We decided on Chicken Tofu Ball which was also cooking while we ate the appetizers. Each person got one chicken tofu ball which was thoroughly steamed and delicately formed. Now to the actual "Pot" section. We ordered Bulgogi with Burdock. They began cooking these parts of the dish while we were eating our rice and chicken tofu ball. For a table of 4, we ordered the large size of the "Pot". The Bulgogi includes Strip Loin Prime Beef, Burdock, Shishito Peppers, Oyster Mushrooms, Scallion, and Onions along with our preference of rice noodles. The soup is savory with nicely cut, tender pieces of beef. While you get your first bowl of noodle soup, the pot continues to cook until you are done eating so they can add more soup base and receive your refill. For dessert, we ordered both the Pear Shaved Ice and the Yakgwa Mille-feuille. The Pear Shaved Ice was a great way to end the meal with something icy cold, refreshing, and slightly sweet. I'm told the "Yakgwa Mille-feuille" is a traditional Korean dessert. It was a very well-made flaky puff pastry with chestnut mousse on the side. After eating, the waitress asked which dish we preferred more and all of 4 of us pointed straight for the Pear Shaved Ice which had to do with the fact that we love fruits.

I wanted to give 5 stars UNTIL I ordered delivery.  Both times there were no sauces. There is no live customer service!!! If you call you receive a recording suggesting you send an email. I had issues with both of my delivery orders and no way to rectify them. I do not trust restaurants where there is no live person answering the phone to help rectify an issue or answer questions.  The voice recording directs you to email customer service... it's been 3 weeks since my last email, and I never received an email reply. My review for non-delivery:The food is great. The store is small and takeout only, lines can be long and wait can be long. Order ahead if you can. Double-check your order is correct before you leave the restaurant.

Title: A Memorable First Sushi Experience at Beyond Sushi

I ventured into Beyond Sushi with the hopes of discovering the allure of sushi for the first time, and I wasn't disappointed. This gem in NYC has earned the top spot as my favorite sushi destination. The moment I stepped in, the attentive service was commendable. The waiter, sensing my novice status, offered a variety of suggestions, each of which hit the mark with their impeccable taste and presentation.

Notably, the Mango Tango roll was a revelation – a must-have for anyone visiting. The fusion of flavors captivated my palate and ensured my newfound love for sushi. Additionally, the Badge dumplings were a delightful treat, perfectly crafted and full of flavor. The Sunny Side rolls also deserve a special mention, boasting a unique taste that left me wanting more.

In summary, Beyond Sushi offers an exceptional experience for both sushi enthusiasts and first-timers seeking quality, variety, and fantastic service. It’s a place I’ll certainly be revisiting.

Title: A Cozy Culinary Gem: Las Laps

From the comfortable ambiance to the exquisite flavors, Las Laps has truly outdone itself. I've frequented this spot several times but only recently indulged in their culinary offerings. On my last visit, the lobster arepas stole the show with their ideal blend of sweetness and freshness, setting the bar high for what comfort food can be.

The jerk chicken spring rolls struck a harmonious balance with their seasoning - not too overpowering, yet tantalizingly present. Similarly, the sweet chili wings delivered a delightful kick, aligning with the restaurant's evident commitment to flavor precision.

The timing of the dishes was impeccable, allowing for a relaxed and savored dining experience. Complementing the meal, the inventively named "Love Thy Enemy" cocktail provided the perfect, satisfying buzz.

The staff's amiability added to the welcoming, homey atmosphere Las Laps is known for. Although I missed out on dessert this time, it's a compelling excuse to return. For anyone in the area, don't miss the chance to experience this unique establishment – it's an absolute treat.

I recently dined at Dim Sum Go Go and found myself underwhelmed by the experience. Despite the restaurant's name suggesting a quick meal, our service was anything but rapid. We waited over half an hour for a simple order, which is too long considering the food was just average. The highlight was their homemade green ginger sauce—it truly stood out and partially redeemed the meal. However, the staff's unwelcoming demeanor didn't help matters, especially since the place was nearly empty. Given the plethora of options in Chinatown, I'm inclined to explore elsewhere next time. Dim Sum Go Go didn't leave a lasting impression that would warrant a return visit.

My recent dining experience at the local Szechuan spot was a delightful immersion into authentic Chinese cuisine. The Soy Sauce Fried Rice, Lo Mein Chicken, and Ma Po Tofu each presented a symphony of flavors that truly satisfied my palate. Despite the dishes being slightly on the saltier side, the overall taste was not diminished. This restaurant is a must-visit for anyone in search of genuine Szechuan taste.

Very reasonably priced dumplings and nice staff. They seemed to cook up the dumplings as you order them so you have to wait a bit, but the tradeoff is you get piping hot dumplings. They do not have any hot chili oil only Sriracha and soy. Also, didn't like styrofoam used for everything, but I'm sure that's part of the reason they keep everything so cheap.CASH ONLY (but so inexpensive) and they stop taking order about 15 minutes before they close.

Came in on Father's Day at around 1 pm for lunch and it was pretty busy. The restaurant is pretty big and there were a few parties waiting. Luckily, we we didn't have to wait for a party of five. We decided to order a bunch of dishes to share. We probably ordered a little too much for five people, but at least we had lunch for the next day. Roti canai - a must-have. So light and fluffy! Perfect way to start the mealRoti prata - a flattened condensed version of roti canai. It tastes pretty similar but is a bit cleaner to eatSatay tofu - one of my go to apps - I love the peanut sauce that it comes topped with. We ordered two of theseBeef rendang - I don't really like stewed beef because it can be chewy, but I loved the sauce. I used it on top of the noodles, which sounds weird, but it was a good combo. My only complaint is that it doesn't come with riceSalted fish fried rice - not the best but not the worst. I probably wouldn't order this againHainanese chicken (whole) - can't go wrong with this, especially with a side of the chicken broth rice, and the special hot sauce the chicken is served withChow Kueh Teow - this one is a classic, so if you're looking for non-spicy stir-fried noodles, this is a good option. The menu says that it's spicy but I didn't taste it at allCrispy chicken salad - skip this. The chicken is SO dry and pretty bland. The only good thing was the crispy skin. Even so, you're better off ordering extra Hainanese chickenSalted fish with eggplant - this was pretty terrible. It was unbelievably salty - it would have been impossible to eat if you didn't have any rice to go with itMalaysian iced coffee - I was afraid this would be all sugar/condensed milk and no coffee, but the coffee flavor was actually really strong so I really enjoyed this.I've been here before a long time ago, but I guess I had forgotten how good it was (certain items. Will be coming back to try some new dishes!

Title: Pleasant Surprise at a Vintage Diner

Despite the slew of negative reviews, my curiosity got the better of me, prompting a breakfast visit with friends to this local diner. Against all odds, the experience defied my low expectations.

First impressions were delightful – the diner exuded a charming, vintage retro vibe that felt lifted from classic movie scenes. It was undeniably cute and welcoming, setting a positive tone for our meal.

The menu didn’t aim to surprise; it provided exactly what one might expect from classic diner fare. I opted for the French toast with an additional scrambled egg, while my companions went for the classic and chocolate chip pancakes. One quirk to note: maple syrup incurred an extra charge, which seemed a tad unreasonable to us.

My French toast arrived fragrant with cinnamon and struck a pleasant balance of sweetness, proving to be a satisfactory portion. The pancakes proved too generous for my friends, leaving me to tackle the leftovers, which were decent though unremarkable. However, I found the chocolate chip pancake overly dense, but that’s a matter of personal taste.

Service deserves a mention; the staff were amicable and attentive, with water glasses kept brimming. One friend sampled a milkshake that, while overly sweet for my taste, seemed to hit the spot for them.

In summary, this diner isn’t about to win culinary awards, but for a cozy atmosphere, friendly service, and decent food, it’s a solid choice. I'd rate it a pleasant 3.5 out of 5 for an enjoyable breakfast experience.

Mighty Catch has been on my radar since it first opened last month. I LOVE seafood and I finally had a chance to try this place out yesterday for my birthday dinner.  The restaurant's overall décor is nautical with a lot of exposed brick, shiplap, wooden tables and floors.  The restaurant isn't that big but there are plenty of seating and long tables that are good for large groups. For appetizers we got the Bang, Bang Shrimp and the Lobster roll.  The Bang, Bang Shrimp was nice and crispy and tossed in their house chili sauce.  This was by far my favorite item throughout the whole meal.  The shrimps were huge, and the chili sauce was perfect with the pieces of pineapple and lettuce.  We loved the sauce so much we asked for more on the side and used this as a dipping sauce for other items.  The Lobster Roll was also very good.  This was appetizer sized so smaller than what you normally would get.  It had warm buttered lobster with a little bit of mayo and chives, and it came with fries.  This dish was very filling for an appetizer.For our entrees, we got the Fishermen Combo and the Fried Seafood Platter.  For the Fishermen Combo, we asked for garlic butter sauce with mild spice.  The mild sauce was very garlicy (which was great) but a little bit too mild, and we wished we had gotten the medium or spicy level instead.  The combo has boiled snow crab legs, shrimp, red potatoes, and Cajun corn.  I like the way they presented this dish.  It was brought to our table in a clear plastic boil bag which was blown up from the heat and steam.  Then they opened it for us and the steam and fragrance coming from it made us "ohh" and "ahh".  Super cool. The Fried Seafood Platter has fried shrimp, catfish, lobster tail and sweet potato fries.  It came with a small cup of tartar sauce, Cole slaw and ketchup.  Everything was delicious.  The portions were surprisingly big, and we took home leftovers-win! Finally, I must note the service here was exceptional.  The staff working the night we went were very attentive and accommodating.  Manager even came over to chat with us a couple of times.  We had a wonderful meal and will definitely be revisiting.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Hyped Ramen Spot

My recent visit to this ramen joint was a rollercoaster of highs and lows. Anticipate a lengthy wait if you decide to dine here—planning ahead is crucial, especially for those prone to hanger. A heads-up for the wait area: it’s exposed, with the entrance set in a downward stairway, making it cramped and uncomfortable.

As an Oregonian with ramen experience, I couldn't help but feel underwhelmed by the broth. It was overly salty with a buttery, oily undertone, which was off-putting. On a positive note, the noodles were spot on, boasting an ideal texture that complemented the well-prepared meat and egg.

The pork bun deserves a shout-out for its deliciousness, easily a highlight of the meal. A notable service quirk here involves taking your order while you're in line. This speeds up the process, ensuring that food arrives swiftly after seating—a clever touch for a quicker turnover.

In essence, even though the wait system is efficient and certain items impressed, the place seems to ride more on hype than distinctiveness in the ramen scene. It was worth a try, but it wouldn’t be my first recommendation for those seeking an extraordinary noodle fix.

Stumbled upon a buzzing taco spot right by our hotel in NYC, Los Tacos No. 1, and it was a revelation – a slice of San Diego in the Big Apple. Being from Chula Vista, it takes a lot to impress my taco palate, but these guys knocked it out of the park. They're serving up the real deal: authentic Mexican street tacos that could rival any back home.

Despite the daunting line, the service was lightning fast – they've got their system down to an art. The choice was simple yet satisfying: tacos or quesadillas, with a range of fillings from Asada to Nopal. And their "Con Todo" option? A dream – loaded with fresh onions, cilantro, salsa, and guacamole. The chips and guac? Don't even get me started – perfection.

Wash it all down with a creamy Horchata, and you'll be planning your next visit before the last bite. Just remember the golden rule: no ticket, no taco. So clutch onto that little piece of paper like your meal depends on it – because it does.

Los Tacos No. 1 is already a hit in Times Square and Chelsea Market, and with Grand Central and Tribeca on the horizon, they're taking NYC by storm. Here's to hoping they bring this taco magic to Honolulu – the lines would be insane. If you find yourself in the city, do your taste buds a favor and drop by. Trust me, you won't regret it.

I came here for a date night on Valentines Day weekend. I was able to make a reservation easily off Yelp. They sent a few reminders beforehand for the reservation which I appreciated.When we walked in, the place was a bit small and tables are pretty close together. The waiter seated us right away. The lady told us all of the specials of the day such as duck breast, etc. HIGHLIGHTS: French Onion Soup & Bistrot Steak Frites with Grilled Shallots in a red wine thyme sauce. French Onion Soup: It was good enough for 2 of us as an appetizer. There was a huge layer of melted cheese on top and soup tasted savory. They also gave us bread on the side with butter.  Bistrot Steak Frites with Grilled Shallots: Steak with fries, grilled shallots, and a salad. I would come back here and get this again!! The steak was cooked perfectly medium rare and they cut the steak for you beforehand. The grilled caramelized shallots and thyme on top of the steak made it extremely flavorful. Fries were crispy and salad was refreshing after the steak. I usually don't finish all my fries but it was so good NOT to finish it. They give you a big portion so we were super full afterwards.The service was a 5/5! They kept coming to fill up our water when our cup was just half empty and asked if we needed anything, Next time, I will be trying the escargot. Love love love this place.

Great spot for a date night but definitely overpriced. The reservation was easy to get--I booked a Saturday dinner for 2 within the same week. The spot comes with a bouncer to make sure you have an actual reservation, because the restaurant itself is tiny (maybe seats 9-10 along the booths, and 4 more along a tiny counter) and there's definitely no space for walk-ins. The service is a bit slow because there's only one guy running the front of house for the 5-6 parties. The food was pretty solid, but not crazy memorable.Between the two of us, we each got a drink and split:- uni toast (served on pretzel bread with a bit of mustard, I believe? I've never had the taste combo before and it was awesome)- tuna toast (delicious but tasted like normal tuna tartare)- trout roe toast (my favorite of the night, served with a sprinkle of truffle on top)- tuna carpaccio (I preferred this one out of the two carpaccios just because the foie gras made a delicious spread and the razor clams added a nice texture)- beef carpaccio (under-seasoned, needed some salt)

Title: A Ramen Revelation

I've stumbled upon a culinary gem that had me wondering, "Where has this place been all my life?" After numerous visits—five in the last three months, to be exact—I can confidently say this restaurant serves up consistently outstanding ramen. Their chicken katsu ramen is a personal favorite: the broth brims with layers of flavor, complemented by fresh veggies and perfectly crispy, strip-cut chicken katsu. For a more veggie-heavy option, I indulge in the vegetable ramen, which never disappoints, especially when I add an egg with its delightfully creamy center. Pro tip: immerse the chicken katsu in the broth for a bit to infuse it with even more depth. Each spoonful, a medley of toppings and broth, guarantees a happy mouth. Portion sizes are generous, ensuring either a fulfilling meal for my boyfriend to finish or leftovers to savor later. This place definitely deserves a shout-out for keeping my ramen cravings thoroughly satisfied.

Gyu-kaku  has two locations in Manhattan. We were at the Times Square site. My Yelp app would not let me post a review because it said I was too far away. One of the servers got me on track and here it is. Great place and very authentic. The Happy Hour prices are insane. What a bargain for the money. We  ordered two beers: Asahi mug and Kiein Mega Mug which was so big I could hardly pick it up and almost finished it. Three apps and all were delicious: Chili Shrimp Shumai creamy with a bite, Fried Pork Gyoza crispy and tasty, and Veggie Spring Rolls fresh and hot. Got out of there under $30. Lots to choose from and the dinner for two looks amazing so will def to back. Service is super with lots of help and no push...a super place to chill in the summer heat.

Upon visiting this popular eatery, my patience was tested with an unexpectedly lengthy 45-minute wait from order to pick-up, intensifying my hunger to the point of frustration. It didn't help to see phone orders being prioritized over in-person customers.

Price-wise, the establishment hits the mark, offering value for money. When it finally came to the food, the rice rolls impressed with their authentic texture, allowing for the discernment of each delicate layer. The cilantro scallion filling delighted my palate, marrying well with the perfectly steamed rice rolls. However, the curry fish ball variety fell short, lacking the robust flavor I had anticipated.

Would I consider this place for a future meal? The deliciousness of the cilantro scallion rice roll tempts me, but the decision hinges on whether I can bypass the queue. If there's no line, I might give it another go.

Solid restaurant that serves pho in Chinatown!I'm originally from Northern Virginia and there are tons of pho restaurants where I'm from. All of them are similar in that they are authentic.When I entered Nha Trang One, I knew I would have a good experience because I overheard some employees talking in Vietnamese!I ordered a dish of Cha Gio and a bowl of Pho Bo Vien. The Cha Gio was crispy, hot, and flavorful. The broth of the pho reminded me of my hometown in Northern Virginia and the meatballs were cooked perfectly. The reason why I'm not giving this restaurant a perfect five star rating is because the pho noodles could have been better. They could have been a little softer. Despite this, still a solid restaurant and I'll definitely be back!
I was supposed to get "Sichuan Spicy Chicken"" they ended up giving me which looks and tastes like ordinary chinese takeout Chicken With Broccoli.  Lame.

Food: We ordered the Kari Kari Chicken, Lamb Burger, and Beef Burger. The chicken was nicely breaded and fried, and actually had a decent chunks of chicken. Glad it wasn't mostly fried bits with a small piece of meat. We actually came specifically for the burgers after seeing on a burger show that they used this sick cast iron skillet with spikes to cook the patties and smoked the entire burger prior to serving. We asked them to split the burger in half so we could try them both. The Lamb Burger was amazing...the patty was not crumbly like a meatloaf or other burgers I've had and was super tender and juicy - not gamey either. The Beef Burger had a strong meaty flavor and was similarly tender and juicy. I was actually a bit disappointed that the burgers were not served on a pretzel bun, which is how we saw it on the show and from others' pictures. The fries that came with it were actually similar to McD fries and had a few pieces of bacon on top. We also added the "deluxe", which was basically giving us tray of lettuce, onions, pickles, and sauces on the side. The veggies were whatever but there was this red sauce (I later found out it was ancho chilies) that was dope.Experience: We went on a Monday around 5 pm for their "Burger Monday" special. The rest of the restaurant wasn't open then but you can sit at the bar/high tops. The service was great and the restaurant set up was super cool - def a fan of the vibe. Value: The "Burger Monday" special is $25 for a burger (lamb or beef), fries, and a drink. We thought it was a sweet deal, since the burger is usually priced at $24 (lamb) and $23 (beef). The Kari Kari Chicken was $7 off the HH menu. Overall, we thought the meal was worth but would probably only eat the burgers with the Monday deal.

Popped in for a dinner after a matinee show because they have an award winning fish & chips and lots of plant based options for hubs.   The decor is really cool and food was good.  Started to get busy after we arrived a lot of young "wall street" types it looked like.   Food was good, I think I've had better fish and chips but it was still good.   The fries were actually hand cut which was a delightful surprise!

I got the chirashi cold noodle soba! Absolutely delicious. I love cold soba with a cold dip on a hot summer night for dinner with friends. It's a small, cozy little place which sets a super casual, comfortable vibe. Along with good food, you can't go wrong here. Highly recommend with friends or just a casual date.

I was pleasantly surprised by the beautiful decor of the restaurant, especially considering the quiet mid-week lunch hour. The warmth of immediate seating and a nice pot of tea was a welcome respite from the cold, windy day outside. The service did not disappoint, with the waiter being attentive without being intrusive. As for the food, it hit the mark on flavor and portion size, offering good value for money. I'm already looking forward to my next visit, if only to indulge in the tea service once again.

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Prince St. Pizza

As a Brooklyn-bred pizza aficionado, losing the old corner pizzerias of my youth left a gaping hole in my quest for the perfect slice. Price hikes aside, my heart always seeks that ideal balance of tangy sauce atop a crust that's perfectly crusty on the outside and pillowy soft within. Following a hot tip, I found myself navigating to Prince St. Pizza, a literal hole in the wall that delivers big on the pizza experience.

With just enough space to order and run, this is the epitome of grab-and-go pizza culture. The line was manageable upon arrival, but by the time I savored the last morsel of my pepperoni square, a crowd had amassed, signifying that I wasn't alone in my verdict.

That pepperoni square was a revelation. The ratio of meat to dough hit the sweet spot, and the sauce? Divine. Sure, it was a bit greasy, but that's just part of the charm—this is indulgence at its best, and every bite was worth it. Prince St. Pizza may be small, but the flavors are massive. For anyone with a serious pizza craving, this spot is a must-visit. Trust me; it's the bomb.

I love the convenience and service at this place. It's a pretty welcoming diner that is perfect if you're craving diner food and nearby. Some friends and I came during the polar vortex of 2019 lol since it was nearby and the staff were extremely nice. The food is pretty standard diner food.. but I liked how the staff gave us a free plate of fruit and was pretty attentive. It seemed like there are a lot of frequent diners here which I'm not surprised about since the diner has a pretty warm vibe.Overall would recommend this place if you're in the area and looking for a filling diner meal.

This is a tiny little place and unless you come at an off time there will likely be a wait but it is worth it. The pizza here is sooooo good. I've come here twice now and both times got the killer bee pizza- it has honey on it which sounds weird but it is incredible.  I've also tried the Italian stallion and the you got a lot a balls which were equally good. Very quick and friendly service. Will be back frequently!

If there's one thing that K-Town Chicken does right, it's their KFC and I'm so blessed that they're in business. Their wings are always thick and juicy as hell. Both of their ktown & spicy flavors are on point. I've tried some other things on the menu but their wings are where it's at. They're open pretty late so there really is no reason to not try this spot.

I recently visited a local ramen spot where I opted for their classic ramen noodles. The broth was a standout – robust, and brimming with flavor. The noodles, while expertly prepared, lacked a bit in taste and I hoped the salty pork would provide that missing punch. Unfortunately, the pork's strong flavor clashed with the already seasoned broth, tipping the balance too far into the salty spectrum. Despite this, the overall experience was enjoyable, and I'm eager to return to try a different dish that could hit that perfect savory harmony.

Best pizza on the UES (at least). This location is tiny, but there are outdoor tables when it is warm. The pizza uses fresh ingredients from Italy. I recommend asking for olive oil to drizzle on the crust. Speaking of the crust, it's super thin and crispy- delicious! I had their burrata special with eggplant and zucchini. It was truly the best eggplant I've ever had! Too bad it's not on their regular menu. Pizzas are about $20 each and so worth it! They also have a really good rosé that is available by the glass. Definitely check it out! I need to stop by their bigger location that has entrees.

Prepare to have your dessert expectations forever transformed at this gem of a restaurant, where the union of gelato and waffles forms a symphony of sweetness that is nothing short of divine.
