Gelato here is not just lovingly scooped but also artfully perched atop warm, fluffy waffles, with an array of flavors that promise to tantalize every palate. Drizzle your choice of sauce for an added touch of indulgence. A glance at the attached picture speaks a thousand words, but the experience itself is indescribable. Trust me, visit and you'll be singing praises long after the last bite. Thank me later!

Title: Monday Night Delight at a NYC Pizza Gem

I ventured into this pizza spot on a Monday evening and was pleasantly surprised by the lack of a queue. Service was swift; in under 20 minutes, I was diving into my Spicy Spring slice and Fancy Spring slice. The Spicy Spring, a zesty square pepperoni piece, was exceptional with its generous cheese topping, perfect crust, and full-bodied flavor. The Fancy Spring, their take on Margherita, was satisfying, though not as thrilling, and a great vegetarian option.

While nibbling on my pizza, I enjoyed the walls adorned with photos of famous patrons, mostly accomplished male athletes, adding to the restaurant's unique charm. The real shocker? Walking out satisfied with a New York pizza experience at just $11. For pizza aficionados in NYC, this place is an absolute must-try.

I recently visited Yoon in New York, a sibling to the famed Haeundae Somunnan Amso Galbi in Busan, Korea, and it did not disappoint. Although the bustling atmosphere of the original location could not be replicated, the quality of the Korean barbecue here was remarkable and quite affordable. Their marinated galbi remains a must-try, and the unique noodles provided a delightful end to the meat-centric feast.

The menu at Yoon surprisingly offers more variety than its Busan counterpart. Standout appetizers included the flavorful galbi dumplings and a perfectly crisp seafood pancake. Service was attentive and efficient, adding to the overall positive experience. For anyone craving authentic Korean barbecue in New York, Yoon is a go-to spot. Of course, if you find yourself in Busan, the original Haeundae Somunnan Amso Galbi is an essential stop. Five stars for both establishments!

3.5 stars. I didn't hate it but I didn't love it. It was okay but  good to try. I had the original broth which was around $10 and I added the pork and fish balls which was another $3. The service was pretty quick. It was a deconstructed bowl of noodles. You add the noodles and ingredients into the bowl of hot soup. You add the meat first to cook longer and then the rest of the ingredients. I never had Yunnan noodles before and it was an interesting concept. The broth was milky and tasted decent. The vermicelli noodles and the rest of the toppings were okay. They give you a little plate of corn, a slice of spam, a quail egg, a shrimp, some chopped black fungus mushrooms, tofu skin, one fried fish tofu, and some garnish. I felt the ingredients were pretty simple and just okay. With the exception of the soup, I think I could have bought the toppings and made this at home. I don't think I'm going to crave this again but it was worth a try.

I don't think this place offers the authentic rice noodle, but nonetheless it was a very yum and fun experience.For just $9.99 you can choose from most of the soup base options on the menu. All come with a plate a rice noodles and a beautifully assorted toppings tray with 11 different toppings! They serve the soup to you boiling hot, and it's then up to you to add in the noodles and toppings. Since the toppings include raw pork slices, you should definitely put that in the soup first as soon as you receive it. The porks slices are super thin so you shouldn't have any worry of undercooking it. After that, feel free to add in the rest of the toppings and finally the noodles.I got the shredded pork and pickled cabbage soup base. The broth was very flavorful and has the perfect hint of sourness from the pickled cabbage. My friend got the tomato soup base, which to me was not a traditional chinese noodle soup base choice, but I gave it a try and loved it immediately. It was rich but not overpowering due to the sourness of the tomato; would definitely have to get it myself next time. Despite the already amazing value you'll receive from just $10, I was very surprised to find out that they also offer a free rice noodle refill. So definitely don't worry about leaving with an empty stomach!(BONUS: they serve their water with reusable plastic straw; that gets an upvote from me!)

I recently visited this spot for lunch and was pleasantly surprised by the variety on their lunch special menu. The sushi was not only affordable but also quite tasty. It's an ideal venue for a group lunch as the servings are conducive to sharing, though you could just as easily savor a meal on your own. If you're nearby or work in the vicinity, this place is a great choice for a quick, wallet-friendly meal. Highly recommended for a midday food stop!

Really glad that I hit this spot before the shut down in K Town. Where this place stands above the rest when it comes to KBBQ is the quality of the meats, the service, and the ambience. This is a little more high end of a spot and it shows in their meat quality. Their pork belly is SO GOOD! I could eat about 20 servings. They're very attentive and make sure you have plenty of rice and banchan as it's hard to not just stuff your face with all of it. Their hanger steak is also a bright spot on this menu as well. Price wise, it's pretty along the lines of most other places in the area, but where it really shines is that it doesnt feel like a steamy grease bath. Some times, that's exactly what you want, but this has excellent ventilation and great view on the middle level for people watching. Can't wait until they open again!

On has been on my list for a while since i like their sister store: take 31 and her name is han. The service is attentive and ambience is nice where you can bring dates or friends. My biggest disappointment is the snapper pot which i had high hopes in. The broth is just sub par. It is very cute to look at: all the pretty colors in a pot but it is so easy to assemble without any secret ingredients. The soup just tastes like lettuce with fish, which is not a good  soup combination flavorwise. They do provide soy sauce on the side but other than that no seasoning at all.Everything else is good. I adore jalapeño fried chicken. The coating is different. Mochi gives it a light, crunchy yet tender taste. On wants to westnize the dish. There is no traditional ingredients like daikon or kimchi, which is the soul of korean cuisine. The only twist i really like is mochi coating, which comes from asia. There is nothing that smell pungent or asian. Not hating... just wish i did not order that snapper pot.

This diner is in the New Yorker hotel where we were staying. We ate 2 breakfasts and 1 dinner here. First for the dinner we had. Our waiter was okay. Not to friendly or helpful. He did not know what "au jus"was.   I was ordering the steak sandwich and wanted some on the side. He got kinda snotty and said they did not have anything liquid or gravy like to offer. I decided to order the burger instead. It was just okay.  Nothing special.   We came back the next morning because I saw chicken and waffles on the menu.  I have always wanted to order this. And heard it was a NY thing. It was chicken tenders on the waffles and I love maple syrup in chicken. We came back the last morning because it was convenient since we were staying at the hotel. This Waiter was super friendly and efficient this time. I had eggs Benedict. It was good.  Lots of comfort food on the menu.  Basic cafe cooking. Good for a quick simple meal.  No frills or whistles.  Just food

Title: Unparalleled Thai Cuisine at [Restaurant Name]

For anyone searching for the epitome of Thai flavors, [Restaurant Name] is a culinary gem that consistently exceeds expectations. Their renowned "Royal Pad Thai" lives up to its regal moniker and easily snags the title of the best in the city, a testament to the authentic and scrumptious dishes they serve.

On our return visit, we delved into appetizers like the aromatic chicken wrapped in leaves and crispy fried fish cakes, each a delightful prelude to the main course. To accompany our meal, a draft Singha beer provided that refreshing zest, complementing the symphony of flavors.

The main courses, a savory chicken basil stir-fry and the signature Royal Pad Thai, were nothing short of spectacular, showcasing the perfect balance of spice and freshness. The service matched the quality of the food, with the waiter adding a dash of warmth to our experience.

In summary, our culinary journey at [Restaurant Name] was memorable from start to finish. This establishment is a must-visit for Thai cuisine aficionados. We eagerly look forward to our next meal here.

In the pizza-saturated landscape of NYC, Farinella offers an experience that stands out, though not necessarily for topping the charts. Their take on the classic New York slice tilts towards the complex, differing from the city's celebrated simple-yet-sublime pizza archetype. The flavors were satisfactory, but not exceptional, especially considering the premium price point. While it's a viable option for those sudden cravings when options are scarce, Farinella doesn't capture the quintessence of New York pizza. Give it a go if you're nearby, but keep in mind that this spot shouldn't be the benchmark for all that NY pizza has to offer.

I recently had the pleasure of enjoying an exceptional brunch experience. The standout dish was the Southwest tots - a delightful skillet brimming with crispy tater tots, spicy chili, gooey melted cheddar, and a dollop of cool sour cream. Every bite was pure comfort food bliss.

The chicken and toast were just as satisfying, with a generous portion of perfectly breaded chicken and delectable French toast. The French dip hash browns were another triumph, featuring a crispy potato latke topped with succulent roast beef and a perfectly fried egg.

While the breakfast sandwich had potential, it fell short due to the unmelted cheese; I’d suggest passing on this one in favor of the other tantalizing options. Overall, this brunch spot is a gem, and I'd definitely recommend a visit for anyone looking to indulge in a hearty and delicious morning meal.

My go to burger place has great salads. They have the impossible burger, which is a good choice. Their onion rings and fries are a great option. They have a brussel sprout side with Thai sauce. Drink options include la croix. Join their rewards program on Facebook and the thanx app.

Title: A Hot Pot Haven in NYC

Despite initial reservations about their unconventional seating and booking process, I feel compelled to dub this the reigning hot pot champion of NYC. Don't let the logistics deter you; the value for money considering the generous portions, exemplary quality, remarkable variety, and mouthwatering flavors is second to none.

Celebrating my friend's birthday here was a delightful experience. They honored the occasion with a complimentary meal for the birthday boy, accompanied by the unexpected entertainment of a dancing monkey. The staff's accommodation for our own celebratory cake was an appreciated touch.

The service deserves special commendation for its promptness. Connoisseurs of meat will revel in the succulent cuts offered, while our vegetarian companion left equally satisfied. A personal tip: opt for the kimchi base for a pot where each ingredient is a pleasure to devour.

Make your way here for a cozy winter repast, a festive birthday, or lively Lunar New Year festivities. This hot pot spot is not just a meal; it's an experience.
Busy little spot for a cold beer break. Service is not fast but acceptable. Has good channels for sports. Good times for a happy hour!

what we ordered: spicy tuna crunch roll, pork chop bento, and chirashi. what i loved: it's a deal!! compared to all its $$$ neighbors, you're getting a bang for your buck. portions are good, and fish is fresh. yes, some people are complaining about the service but honestly how often do you actually need your servers to do anything but refill your water/tea ?? the chirashi came in cute little separate bowls - nice presentation. spicy tuna was a good amount of spicy and portion of the bento was perfect for dinner. good place to get your lunch/dinner fix with good food but without the annoying waiter who checks if you're still alive every 5 minutes.

The Tetsu Burger, that's what we were here for. Like what prior reviewers stated, Tetsu was featured on First We Feast, Worth It, etc, so we made it a priority to check this place out. This place gets packed up, so definitely make reservations.We were promptly seated on the second level mezzanine; it overlooks the kitchen. During the winter months, it does get a bit hot where we were seated, but nothing too uncomfortable. My companions and I thoroughly enjoyed our meal. Portions were good. The Tetsu Burger lived up to its name; we had both beef and lamb. The TB was a simple, no frills burger, but was one of the most delicate burgers I've ever had. Cocktails were refreshing. Their Foie Gras special was solid as well.They had closed 2/7/2020. Glad we got to check it out.

Walk in your typical New York pizza joint: small, narrow and a bit stuffy. One thing is for sure though, there is nothing typical about their pizza! If you're in the Washington Heights area- I believe this maybe Inwood, I definitely recommend you stop here. I recommend the Chicken pizza the topping will leave you speechless. I bit my whole cheek! Stays open til 1am.

I had a delightful dining experience at this restaurant where the food was brimming with flavor and cooked to perfection. The staff went above and beyond in terms of friendliness, offering me a chance to sample all three curry sauces since it was not busy during my visit. The sides did not disappoint, with the sweet potato side dressed in coconut being a standout. I highly recommend it for a flavorful and welcoming meal.

Came for lunch and ordered the lunch special for $18.  You also get your first margherita for $1 too bad we weren't drinking!  So for lunch special you can choose an appetizer and main meal. I ordered the beet salad for my app and it was not good.  Tasted like straight vinegar which overtook the whole dish. It was not good at all. For my main meal I ordered The fish tacos which were better but still not up to par with the top taco's I have had. The fish had a good crunch to it but there was a lot of mayo sauce on it which made it taste more like the sauce than anything.  You also only get 2 tacos in the order which makes it not really worth the price. I would pay for quality over quantity but the quality wasn't there.  I expected more from this meal honestly. The restaurant is beautifully decorated and the service was pretty solid. I am sure if I order other things on the menu I may have a different opinion but yet to be seen if I make it back here.

Title: A Friday Feast at Uncle Boon's

After hearing endless raves about Uncle Boon's from two friends, I succumbed to my curiosity and headed there on a Friday evening at 5:30pm, luckily just ahead of the crowd. Do note, they have a full-party policy before seating, which caused a slight hiccup when a friend ran late.

Pro-tip: Arrive early to dodge the two-hour waits that can build up later in the evening.

Between the three of us, we ventured into an array of dishes including the green mango salad, a tantalizing chicken salad, and the standout bone marrow, which I claimed. While the cabbage dish received lackluster feedback compared to someone's "best thing they had ever eaten" review, the rest of our selections were culinary triumphs.

Not only was the food exceptional, but the service was remarkably swift. We went from menu perusal to payment in a brisk 45 minutes, without the meal feeling hurried.

The restaurant's ambiance is well-curated, though the dim lighting slightly detracted from the experience for me, making menu reading strenuous and food photography challenging.

Despite these minor quibbles, Uncle Boon's deserves a resounding 5 stars. I’m eager to return and introduce more friends to this culinary gem.

I recently visited a local restaurant and was pleasantly surprised by the culinary experience. The star of the meal was the Seafood Cobb, which packed a flavorful punch and was quite generous in portion. The service was efficient and courteous, contributing positively to the overall dining experience. Although the ambience didn't quite dazzle, the quality and taste of the food more than compensated for the lack of atmosphere. It's a solid choice for those seeking a casual dining spot in the area. I'd definitely recommend giving it a try!

Excellent food. The ramen is well cooked. The broth is delicious. The ingredients are fresh. The service speed is quite fast. The server attention to details are great. The only minus is that it took almost an hour of wait time at the front in a bit of a cold. Everything else is wonderful!

Title: A Must-Visit for Ramen Enthusiasts: Ichiran Review

Ichiran turned out to be a fantastic dining experience, surpassing all my expectations. If you're a fan of tonkotsu ramen like me, this Japanese chain serves up a singular focus that really hits the spot. Opting for the recommended set at $25, I was eager to indulge in their culinary craft.

Adding the pork loin for an extra $9 was a decision I'll never regret – it's an exclusive offering at their New York location and it elevated the meal tremendously. Although there's usually a queue, their proficient system makes the wait bearable and ensures a quick turnover without feeling rushed.

I appreciated the DIY aspect of the meal – toppings are served on the side and you even peel your own egg. However, next time I'll skip the spice blend as it overpowered the delicate flavors I prefer in my ramen.

Culminating the meal with the only dessert on the menu, the matcha pudding was a delightful palate cleanser – light and not overly sweet. It's a breath of fresh air in the dessert world often dominated by sugar.

In conclusion, don't hesitate to visit Ichiran. Just make sure to arrive early, and when you do, the pork loin is an absolute must-try. It's a game-changer for ramen lovers.

I had the pleasure of enjoying the classic ramen at this quaint spot and it was nothing short of delicious. The serving size was generous and assuredly satisfying. Opting for a poached egg as an add-on was a wise decision; it introduced a delightful creaminess that enhanced the dish perfectly. If you're looking for a great place to grab a fulfilling lunch, this simple yet impressive restaurant is a fantastic choice.

Great Food and service !! It's a small restaurant that opens around Noon and pretty much first come first serve. Don't think they take reservations but people were waiting at reception for it open and then at Noon they seated groups in order they came. Coming to food, everything was as you would expect from a $$$ Japanese restaurant. Fresh, flavorful meal!! Prompt and responsive service. Will surely visit again.

Wow! They enlarged the space in here and turned it from a little quick counter and stool wing spot to a restaurant where you can actually eat-in! They even have 4 TVs throughout; one was playing a Halloween movie, the others were the News, ESPN, and NBC. This is awesome! I was happy that the staff allowed me to taste a variety of their sauce before making a purchase. The INSANE was too hot for me. I got the inferno and smokey-bourbon instead. It was $14.99 for 10 traditional wings. I love the inferno. It was delicious. The smokey-bourbon was sweet and smokey. But the inferno was exciting and addicting and mouth-burning. I wish I ordered more of it. My only complain is I wish I had more wings and less drum sticks. And maybe also that I didn't like their blue cheese, it was too sour. I used my own bottle of Roquefort blue cheese instead. Other reviews said their wings had too much sauce. Guess they've already made the change because mine didn't have enough sauce. Overall, I love the Inferno wings here and I'm already craving for more!-------------------------------------------Update: Came back the next day to order 10 traditional Inferno wings. I asked for wings only, no drumsticks. I got 4 drumsticks. The lady staff  explained that she put in Flat Heavy for me and that means I'm going to get very few drumsticks... I was thinking 2, but 4/10 is almost half of my order! Yesterday I ordered 10 wings and got 2 sauces on the side, today 10 wings gave me 1 sauce on the side somehow. Same restaurant, different experience everyday.

Great addition to the Village - both in terms of the food and atmosphere. Came here on a Friday night hoping to snag two seats at the bar. We ended up waiting 30 min and two seats at the chefs counter opened up which added to the overall experience. Got two vegetables - carrots/cauliflower. Both were good but not great. After debatin between the pasta and chicken we defaulted to the chicken as it seemed to be their thing. I'm glad we made that choice as it was fantastic, with or without the  accompanying dipping sauces. Will be back for sure.

My fiancé loves their warm bowls. I on the other hand.. I'll pass. No matter which bowl I get ( I've had at least 4 different ones) the taste just doesn't change. Hard to understand how one could possibly mess up a salad, but it's possible. Furthermore, 27 bucks for two salads is rather expensive if you ask me. You'd think I was eating seafood for that price! And did I mention that they charge for ALL extras. Yup, even croutons. Am I being crazy? Keep the free bread and give me an extra tablespoon of croutons, please.

Came here for a work holiday party and it was so pretty! The food was amazing and the decore super cute. Very festive rooftop which overlooks Bryant Park market and ice skating ring. Had such a romantic feel to it. Will be coming back for dinner and enjoy the romantic atmosphere when that time comes.

During a recent weekend visit to NYC, my party of five, despite a reservation made a week prior, experienced a 25-minute wait at a bustling restaurant with an appealing aesthetic. The food, a standard fare of overpriced brunch offerings, fell short of expectations. My Egg + Sausage Sandwich, misrepresented as a hash-focused dish, turned out to be a soggy burger-like disappointment. My boyfriend's Huevos Rancheros, though recommended, resembled a simplistic concoction of tortilla chips and salsa with an egg. Similarly, the dishes ordered by my friends—Poached Eggs, Simple Oven Baked Eggs, and Falafel—failed to impress. Even the side of Hash for the table was unremarkable. While the Caesars were visually appealing, they did not redeem the overall dining experience. My advice: explore other NYC brunch offerings and skip this underwhelming establishment.

Best tonkotsu ramen in nyc especially if you like the heavy thick and rich broth. I had the warm ramen as an entree and fried chicken skin as an appetizer and they were both so amazing. I loved the thick noodle in the ramen. Their thick noodle is thicker than any other ramen restaurant's. Yes they were heavy and they are not the type of food I would normally crave but on a cold day, this is perfect. The atmosphere is also very warm and cozy. I would definitely go back.

Was driving through Manhattan and wanted a Sicilian slice. The nearest location for pizza with a high rating was My Pie Pizzeria Romana. We went around closing time, so there weren't many choices left to choose from. There's a poster outside for truffle mushroom pizza, which sounds so good, but wasn't a choice unless you order a large pie. I got a slice with artichoke and a slice with tomato. The slices are pretty big. I had leftovers. Their flour is from Italy! The slice was perfectly crisp on the bottom. The AC was blasting. We didn't get an attitude from the cashier despite it being near closing time. Good food and good service. Outlets available as well.

WowWowWwwooooooowwwwwww..OBSESSED!!This place is one of my new FAVORITES!To start, we got the Scorched Broccoli and Cauliflower, and Fun Guy and The Badge Dumplings. The cauliflower honestly wasn't anything special, I was expecting them to be charred, like super roasted, but they were basically just cooked and a little bland. The dumplings tho!!!! Those were amazing! Usually I prefer dumplings to be crispy like potstickers, and these were more doughy, but the flavors were soooo amazing. I could've eaten 100 of each!Then, we got rolls for entrees: the Mighty Mushroom, Chic Pea, and Spicy Mang. Wow. I can't even explain how good they were or even why they were so good. The flavors were somehow delicate but also completely enveloped my tastebuds. Highly, highly recommend these rolls. Dessert we got the Cinnamon Roll...OBVIOUSLY, and a takeaway treat that was a coconut chocolate ball. The cinnamon roll was incredible, but I was most pleasantly surprised by the chocolate coconut ball thing. When I got it, it was hard as a rock. I wondered how I would even bite it. But when I opened the plastic and took a bite it was actually so fudgy and rich and dense! I took bites throughout the whole rest of the night and was so sad when it was gone. Highly recommend grabbing a couple for late night snacks!!Overall, I can't wait to come back here ASAP and try some new things and some favorites. The wait staff was friendly and accommodating, the space was clean and open, and the food came quickly. Overall 6/5 stars amazing!!

*Disclaimer: Boucheie invited me for a complimentary dinner. This review is for what we tried for that dinner* I love all the Boucheries across town but they're a more of a special occasion dinner for me, given the average entree price. So I was so happy to see Petit Boucherie pop up, a tiny, cozy spot in West village with scaled back menu and prices. We had dinner for two on a weekday night and even though the place. The atmosphere is elegant, but not stuffy. Candlelit tables and an ancient intricate wooden door, colorful Parisian prints on the walls. The service was warm, fast, and accommodating. The drink menu rivals the other Boucheries, which inventive cocktails and several champagne and sparkling wine options. For appetizers, we tried the steak tartare and squid ink linguini. The tartare comes with a quail egg on top, fresh greens, and two slices of crusty bread. The taste was light but good. The linguini comes with a cream sauce and a few shrimp and crab. The squid ink pasta was al dente and wonderful. The sauce and seafood were well made and flavorful, but I prefer the version at the other Boucheries with red sauce and rock shrimp. For mains, we had the Steak Frites and Truffle Wagyu Burger. Boucherie always delivers on meat and these were delicious! The truffle slices on top of the burger were a generous size and made the meal more special. As always, the fries are a major highlight of the meal. Perfectly golden - crispy on the outside and tender and dense on the inside. Love the little pickles that came with the burger. For dessert we had the tarte tartin which came in an interesting shape with caramel swirls underneath. The ice cream that came with was a perfect complement. We had a magical night at Petite Boucherie which I'm looking forward to returning too more often for casual and special dinners! I prefer the appetizers at the main Boucheries slightly more, but overall, Petit Boucherie embodies the best of the Boucheries in a cute, tiny package.

Excellent Food!.... very Spanish, very authentic.I literally felt i was having tapas in Spain.The decor is super nice and cozy, tue ambience is very business like and serious but Casual still, service friendly and Food is "on point"We had the very expensive Jamon Iberico which was scarce but delicious, we tried the octopus, Bacalao which was done exactly right and the camarones al ajillo mmm those where a delight... on top of it we had the cordero pinchos, lamb skewers... amazing.This is a great tapas place which you gotta

Title: Lucky Cat's Okonomiyaki Hits the Spot

After an energy-draining marathon, I visited the much-talked-about Lucky Cat to sate my intense hunger. The star of the show was undoubtedly the pork okonomiyaki, priced reasonably at $11. This Japanese pancake brimming with pork, cabbage, and egg, and served hot on a sizzling skillet, met every expectation—hot, sweet, and utterly satisfying.

Regrettably, the chicken kara-age didn't live up to the okonomiyaki's standard. It lacked the depth of flavor that I've come to love from the marinade-rich versions at more down-to-earth spots like Omusubi Gombei. The chicken was somewhat bland, only salvageable by salt, pepper, and a lemon slice that unfortunately reminded me more of fried fish than poultry.

Service slipped into the slow lane, with an oversight on our okonomiyaki that required our intervention. Despite the hiccup, the allure of Lucky Cat remains—it's a haven for okonomiyaki enthusiasts. Just be prepared for a potential wait and a few service snags.

Next on the agenda, attempting to snag seats at Tomi Jazz. Wish me luck!

I recently visited this gem for a business lunch and was thoroughly impressed. The lunch special, priced at $11.95, started with a delightfully savory lentil soup, setting a promising tone for the main course. I opted for the shrimp quesadilla, which was flawless. The shrimp was cooked just right, complemented by the perfect melting cheese, and the option to switch the standard rice for fries or salad was much appreciated—I chose the salad, which was fresh and paired well with the meal. However, what truly elevated the experience was the attentive service; our waiter, exuding warmth and hospitality, graciously offered a sample of the fries, which did not disappoint. Including the soup, my entire meal came to a reasonable $14.95. This place nails it in both cuisine and customer care. Highly recommended for a satisfying lunch with prompt and personable service.

Great service from our waitress. The food arrived very fast. Definitely get the pull apart French bread for an appetizer. Restaurant is very clean. My husband got the fish and chips but subbed with sweet potato fries and  I got the falafel burger  with fries. BBoth  of our fries were seasoned well.  The falafel burger made of chic peas was crunchy on the outside and cooked well on the inside. It did taste great.  There is a full bar with two tvs set on different channels and they have low and high seated tables. Cushion chairs and cloth napkins. I'd say kids would be fine here  as well as handicap seating. It's my first time eating at Macy's restaurants and I enjoyed our meal. The price for two was $58

I recently dined at a charming Italian spot that really hit the mark. The menu boasts a delightful array of pastas and pizzas, with generous portions that ensure you won't leave hungry. Their rigatoni funghi e salsiccia stood out – a satisfying blend of al dente pasta, savory mushrooms, and hearty sausage, all enveloped in a tasty pink sauce. While a few pasta pieces were a touch firm, the overall experience was a palatable one, with the pasta capturing the sauce beautifully. Additionally, their complimentary bread, fluffy and perfect for dipping into the provided olive oil and balsamic vinegar, was a noteworthy opener to the meal. I wholeheartedly suggest giving this establishment a try for a fulfilling Italian feast.

This place was recommended to me by the manager of my nearby abode the East Village Hotel, as a local place with lots of history and good Eastern European food - it's in the heart of the Ukraine Community that borders East Village. On this particular morning I decided to walk the two miles from EV to Midtown - partially because I needed the exercise and partially to take in NYC from the streets - I think to really get the feel of a city you need to explore by walking.Veselka is on the corner of 2nd Ave and 9th St so about a block away for me and in the right general direction of my walk so I decided to drop in for breakfast. The exterior is brightly lit with red and yellow panels surrounding the exterior seating. The interior is what you would expect from a cafe or diner from the era - tall ceilings and plenty of history to look at on the walls - they've been serving food since the mid-50's. I sat by myself at the counter after being greeted by a young man with what sounded like a Slavic accent (to my ear it sounded Russian but what do I know?). The menu was pretty diverse with the both the usual breakfast diner options and several choice Ukraine/Russian/Eastern European selections - from experience recently in Belarus the sausages, fried potato cakes and borscht would all be interesting and should be fairly authentic. I really wanted to hit some of those but for my walk decided on something simple, an egg sandwich with coffee.Once I ordered I got a cup of coffee and a small juice (guess that's part of the service?). It's funny how simple breakfast items can tell you a lot about a restaurant - my sandwich was on a toasted roll with bacon. The egg was appropriately runny and the bacon very crisp - everything about the sandwich was about perfect. My coffee was typical diner coffee - fairly neutral in roast and acidity. It did take a minute to flag my server down for the check but I think I was in-and-out in about 20 minutes. I do like quick meals like this - it's no nonsense, filling and you leave satisfied. I hope to order more of the other offerings the next time I'm in the neighborhood (seems about once a month with this client).

We were lucky enough to get tickets for both their pre-opening lunch and dinner (the pictures are from dinner only).For lunch, we were given a free bowl of our choice while they trained their servers on the line. You start out by choosing white or forbidden rice as the base. The rest of setup was kind of confusing since they separate their cooked (chicken, pork, beef, salmon) vs. raw proteins (poke) on the line. Obviously it was their first day, but you get to choose 1 cooked OR raw protein (I was told at first one cooked and one raw). Then you get to choose up to 5 toppings, including kimchi, bok choy, broccoli, and your typical poke toppings (crab/seaweed salad, masago, pickled ginger, jalapenos, etc). The rice was kind of soggy and the rest of the plate was just mediocre, but I won't dock them any stars for now. What they will lose 1 star for is the price - with the extra protein the plate would have come out to $21-$22 after tax, and $17 without (steak and tuna). I wouldn't consider this place significantly better than a Dig Inn or Cava, but the price seems significantly higher.For dinner, we were able to choose 3 plates. All of their mocktails and appetizers are incredible - both in looks (as the servers walked by) and taste. The octopus we ordered was extremely tender, a good portion size, and the potatoes, pineapples, and Japanese mayo it came with was a great combination. Not to mention all the shareables and mocktails are 50% off during happy hour (4-7pm) which makes them an awesome value (octopus would have been $8)! Similar to lunch, both the entree Bulgolgi plate and miso ramen were passable. In fact, the miso ramen tasted like instant chicken ramen. For desert, we got their special, which is a bowl of matcha ice cream and vanilla cream puffs covered with a chocolate cage lid, which would melt when the warm chocolate sauce is poured over. Though the cream puffs tasted a bit stale, our major complain was that the ice cream immediately melted to a puddle as the warm chocolate was poured in. Overall, we still had a terrific experience (the service was awesome, super attentive, and receptive to our post meal feedback), so I'll be back to try again in the future when their operations are more intact.

Loved this place!Super unexpected because it looks like another small japanese shop. One in a million in New York, but the bowls are decently sized and really fills you up. Seating is a little tight (there are about 4 tables), but people tend to eat quickly so the wait isn't terrible.I got a brown rice, steak with sesame sauce. The steak was amazing! Charred nicely and sweet. The sesame sauce went on the greens that come on top of your base so that was a nice touch of salad. I also got some pork gyoza which were crispy on the outside and soft on the inside like they should be. The price isn't terrible for New York, but I do feel like it is a little pricey for some teriyaki. Great for a quick, delicious bite that will really satisfy your teriyaki craving.

Title: Unbeatable Lunch Special in Little Italy!

I recently had the pleasure of experiencing the lunch special at a local gem in Little Italy, and I must say, it deserves a full five stars. For the unbeatable price of $10, I enjoyed the most delectable garlic bread, a hearty soup, and a large portion of my favorite Italian dishes, including spaghetti and chicken parm. The service added to the charm, with warm and friendly staff that let you choose your own seating. The food arrived quickly, and the homemade quality was evident with every bite. If you're looking for an excellent meal that won't break the bank, this is the place to go. Loved every moment and every mouthful!

You DEFINITELY have to check out 886 for a meal! 886 has cool vibes and great food. The restaurant is also located on the same street as a few yummy dessert places that you could stop by after your meal. There are three dishes on 886's menu that you have to try. The first is their Lo Ba Beng, which is a rice dish with pork and bamboo, it also comes with white radish as a side dish. The second is their beef noodle soup, the soup is a little on the saltier side, but it was very flavorful. Then, my third recommendation is their popcorn chicken. The chicken is glazed with a sweet, delicious sauce and is very tender on the inside while crispy on the outside. I definitely recommend ordering a few dishes and sharing with your friends so that you can try a little bit of everything. Overall, my experience at 886 was amazing! When my friends outside the city ask me for a restaurant recommendation, 886 is one of the first ones that comes to my mind, I highly, highly recommend it. I am definitely coming back for more good times and yummy meals.

Title: Unexpected Culinary Delight at Trattoria Dell'Arte

I stumbled upon Trattoria Dell'Arte during a hunger-fueled search for dinner, and what a delightful accident it turned out to be. The restaurant, with its inviting outdoor seating, drew me in and a glass of chianti set the stage for a pleasant evening. The wine was smooth and dry – a perfect start.

My main course was the supreme salumi pizza. Despite a disappointingly thin and brittle crust, the toppings were a savory celebration of cold cuts that more than made up for it. Each slice of salami, pepperoni, sausage, and prosciutto was a nod to Italian authenticity. I convinced myself that the lighter crust meant fewer carbs and therefore less guilt.

On the waiter's recommendation, I indulged in cannoli for dessert. They were beautifully presented with a blueberry sauce and sugared almond slices. The cannoli were delightful, though the filling was a tad too sweet for me. Thankfully, the sauce balanced it out.

Located opposite Carnegie Hall and a stone's throw from Central Park, the restaurant's atmosphere is reminiscent of a traditional Italian trattoria, buzzing with energy and full of attentive service. It's great for families and couples alike due to its ample seating. However, the constant rotation of different waiters attending to various tasks was a slight drawback, disrupting the dining experience.

The menu is on the pricey side – $30 for a pizza and $13 for a glass of wine – but given the quality and location, it may be worth the splurge for some. A solid four-star experience for those willing to overlook the service hiccups and price point.

Title: Birthday Boozy Brunch Bonanza at Boqueria

Looking for the ultimate brunch spot for a large group that promises a lively atmosphere and flowing drinks? I celebrated my birthday at Boqueria with 14 friends and was blown away by the experience. For a reasonable $42 per person, you'll be treated to an array of entrées, appetizers, and desserts that will exceed your party's appetite. Their sharing format ensures that no one leaves hungry, piling more than enough delectable dishes on the table.

The drink situation is particularly impressive; whether you're a mimosa lover or sangria enthusiast, the staff keeps the glasses topped up to the brink of debauchery. It’s a delightful challenge trying to keep track of how many you've had!

While the Spanish Tortilla didn't quite transport me to Spain, it was the only minor blip in an otherwise sumptuous spread. Everything else was top-notch, and the generous portions call for a crowd that knows how to put away a good meal. Boqueria is the place to be for a brunch that guarantees good times and great food.
Everything here was perfect , especially the service. We didn't mind waiting for 30 mins... add  eggs for $2.00 for every ramen. The bu s, cucumber , short ribs and noodles ... yummy!

Tucked away in Chelsea's bustling hub is a cozy culinary gem with a vibrant interior adorned by lively red walls and intriguing artwork. Although space is limited and elongated, the atmosphere remains warm and inviting.

Upon arrival, we were greeted with complimentary corn nuts – a crunchy treat that leaned toward the salty and dry side. For the main course, my companion and I indulged in the Bistec a lo Pobre, priced reasonably at $18. The dish was a feast for both the eyes and the palate: a hearty assembly of well-seasoned steak, crisp fries, sweet maduros (plantains), a savory hot dog, and a perfectly fried egg over rice, sans beans per my request.

The steak's tenderness coupled with the flavorful hot dog and the maduros' subtle sweetness made for a harmonious blend of tastes and textures. Each bite brought a delightful crunch from the fries and a satisfying richness from the egg.

Service was swift and attentive, a much-appreciated effort as time was not a luxury I had that evening.

With a promise of more tantalizing menu items yet to explore, we vowed to return post-pandemic closures. This vibrant spot not only offers a taste of culinary abundance but does so with friendly service and prices that defy its central location. A definite must-visit for a flavorful experience that doesn't break the bank.

Not very tasty - just one of the many subpar Shanghainese restaurants that have sprouted up to take advantage of the newfound craze for XLB.We started with veg steamed dumplings - the filling was fine, but the texture was a little doughy, perhaps from being steamed too long. The dough also had a strange slightly sweet flavor that I didn't  love.The  pan fried noodles were a very small portion and almost flavorless. Felt like a thrown-together dish without care.Probably a place best avoided.

If you find yourself with time to kill due to waits at neighboring Korean spots, consider a detour to this gem for their renowned yogurt drinks. We sampled the black sesame and strawberry and cream flavors, and each was a delightful treat. Highly recommend for a refreshing and tasty experience!
Good vibes. Great interior. Easy music. Friendly service. Spicy cocktails! Handsome date. Happy to be here.

They have a good lunch special deal! I have not found too much information on yelp, so I figured the I could writeskemthjnh to be helpful. Lunch special is anytime before 3pm Monday through Friday for $11.95. A really good deal for a cold weather especially if you are around the area. First of all, I like the little sheep broth a lot, it's quite flavored and with a lot of herbs inside. Also, the spicy one is good especially after it could for about 20 mins, when the spiciness reach it's peak! You can choose one protein, but aside you get several different vegetables, mushroom, noodle, quail egg, fish ball, and fish tofu. You can basically try everything and see what you like. I ordered the lamb shoulder, which is not too fatty. You can also order additional dish is you are still hungry. I ordered an extra lamb shoulder, which kick the me to $20. I walked out the restaurant super full! Worth the price. If you would like to take advantage of lunch special, this is definitely a good choice.

We had a great lunch!  The ambience was fantastic and the food as well.Everything we ordered was delicious.  Even the presentation was awesome!We had a delightful lunch and our Server was very helpful.After 2-3 years - and they consistently keep the place well and their menu great!

Loving this place! They have wine flights for $12 and pretty decent pours. Staff is friendly and accommodating. There's a variety of appetizers to choose from on their happy hour menu and there's a separate menu for cheese. It's a cozy place and can get quiet crowded. I'd be more than happy to visit again either for date night or girls night. Definitely worth visiting on the west side. Outdoor seating available but limited.

We had a fun time tonight!  The restaurant week meal was surprisingly good and exceeded  our expectations.  I definitely would come back for the fish or stew again. He steak was good too.   The only disappointing part were the  desserts.  We expected everything to be richer.   The mousse was flat.  The crepe brûlée was a little bit runny.

Recently, I visited an Italian restaurant in the bustling neighborhood of Tribeca to celebrate a friend's birthday. The establishment presented itself charmingly with decor that transported us to a quintessential Italian ristorante, complete with pristine white tablecloths.

Our dining experience kicked off with a variety of appetizers, each tantalizing our taste buds more than the last. The highlight of my own meal, the Gnocchi della casa, was satisfactory, though it didn't ignite culinary fireworks.

The restaurant shines with good quality food and surprisingly reasonable prices for its prime location. Even though I'm enticed to return, it hasn't quite topped my list of favorite Italian spots in New York.

This place is a party. You walk in and it's a crowd early(ish) on a Friday night. I wouldn't call this a speak-easy; but it has similar vibes.Super hip and fun, but also cozy. The interior is exactly my style- comfy but ready to party.Come with a group or just yourself, they treat you the same. This place has everything; good food, dancing on the weekends and nice staff. I need to try some more of their drinks as well as the brunch menu to better calculate my opinions on them. This is definitely a fun place to go to and I look forward to coming here more in the future.

I went to the smith yesterday and it's a lovely place . I had reservations for 5pm and got seated at 4:44 which was excellent . I got the butternut squash bucatini and also the mushroom empanadas . Everything was absolutely delicious . The bucatini was so fresh that the noodles just melted in your mouth. I could have cried it was so good and the amount they gave you was plentiful . The empanadas were good but what made them great was the jalapeño crema . It was the most delicious thing I ever tasted. I also had the pear cider which was pretty tasty. My only con would be that the sitting areas we too close to the point I could barely get out until I moved the table . I'm a curvy woman so work on that but the food was wonderful ! I'll be back for brunch !

Cool little bistro. Not a bad sized place and at lunch it wasn't too busy. The exterior didn't give a clue to the meat interior.     Food was pretty good, slightly towards the pricey side for what you got.     I went with a croque monsieur. The bread was the standout. The sandwich itself tasted good, but it really skipped on the ham and cheese filling. There was also a bechamel sauce, but the odd part was it wasn't warm/saucy. It was kind of cooled and spread over the top of the sandwich like butter. (See in the pic) With only a side of potato chips, it was a little pricey for what you got.
They DO NOT accept PULSD. When we tried to pay with the voucher they would not accept it. The voucher was for $29 for dinner for two. Instead I had to pay $75 for two bowls of soup! Not worth it.

Title: Festive Office Dinner with Room for Improvement

I attended an office Christmas dinner at this establishment on December 18th and had a mixed experience. The service was a highlight, with our waiter displaying exceptional enthusiasm and attentiveness, although the restaurant appeared understaffed as clearing the table took longer than expected.

The sampler platter, featuring notably tasty ribs, was a strong start to our meal. My Patron drink was refreshing, and I opted for the customizable meal option, which allowed me to try the taquitos, a fish taco, and another item. While the taquitos were passable, the fish taco fell short and could definitely use some refinement.

Among my colleagues, the salmon received a positive review. Despite the fish taco's letdown, I see potential in this eatery and would consider returning, perhaps during happy hour for a more casual experience.

This place is the favorite pizza spot of two close friends and their recommendation was spot on! Try and make a reservation or come right when it opens! My bf is super picky about his NY slices, and he loved this place!We got a split pizza. While I liked the supreme, the tie-dye pizza is where it's at! The dye pizza, vodka sauce with swirls of pesto! Omg the vodka sauce was so flavorful and the fresh bites of pesto really elevated this amazing pizza!!! We also got the meatballs, a perfect blend of beef, pork and veal. It's like the perfect meal!

Title: A Gastronomic Delight at DaDong New York

Nestled in the vibrant Bryant Park, DaDong New York is more than just a dining spot—it's a three-story marvel of chic design and culinary excellence. Opt for a window seat if you can; the view complements the ambience beautifully as you ascend via one of the majestic elevators.

From the get-go, the Cherry Foie Gras appetizer tricks and treats the palate, with real cherries mingling alongside foie gras masquerading as their lighter twin. Seafood lovers would appreciate the fresh selection of raw oysters and clams, a briny prelude to the main event.

Speaking of mains, the star—the DaDong Roast Duck is a must-try, and the Baked Black Cod and Sautéed Pencil Asparagus don't lag far behind in quality. But let's talk about the Wagyu Beef Fried Rice. This dish, seemingly simple, captivates with every spoonful, setting the bar impossibly high for fried rice everywhere. A clear favorite.

Desserts were a roller coaster of highs with the DaDong 'Nata' Custards leading the pack - a sensorial explosion of creamy bliss that frankly deserves its own shop. The Crispy Chocolate Rice Pudding paled a bit in comparison but was enjoyed nonetheless.

The personal touch for my son's 17th birthday, a complimentary bowl of noodles from the chef, was a thoughtful gesture reflecting the restaurant's dedication to customer delight.

Service? Impeccable throughout our visit—absolutely five stars.

In conclusion, DaDong New York delivers an unforgettable experience where the food not only meets aesthetic standards but also surpasses taste expectations. It's a resounding testament to the art of fine dining.

Title: A Gem for Italian Fare - Perfect for Date Night

If you're on the hunt for an authentic Italian dining experience, this charming little restaurant is the spot to be. It's a quaint place, perfect for a romantic evening, with about ten cozy tables indoors and a delightful option to dine outside when the weather permits.

Operated by Italians who bring their homeland charm right to your table, the warmth of the staff is palpable, with Ciro, the friendly owner, often present to ensure everything runs smoothly. My boyfriend and I have made this place a staple for our date nights, though be warned, its popularity may mean a wait at times.

The menu boasts scrumptious Neapolitan pizzas – you can't go wrong with any choice – as well as calzones, panuozzo sandwiches, salads, and a handful of appetizers. The arugula salad is a must-try, it's simplicity perfected, and the meatballs will leave you wanting more. While I haven't tried their pasta, the selection seems to be concise but tempting.

A note of caution: don't mix this up with San Matteo Pizzeria e Cucina located ten blocks south. Although similar in name, they are distinct entities – the latter accepts reservations, unlike our little no-reservation gem on 90th.

Title: Kenka: A Staple of St. Mark's for the Izakaya Ambience

Review:

If it's a genuine izakaya vibe you're after, Kenka on St. Mark's is your go-to spot. This place is less about the culinary finesse and more about soaking in the atmosphere and enjoying a casual evening with friends. Steeped in nostalgia from my high school days, I'm always thrilled to find its prices still pleasantly low, solidifying its status as a neighborhood landmark.

Bear in mind, Kenka shuns reservations for a more spontaneous waitlist system. Be prepared for a bit of a stand-around outside—no phone holds here. For our duo on a bustling Saturday at 8pm, a table took a 90-minute wait, but the lively queue adds to the buzz of the experience.

Inside, space isn't an issue. The layout affords ample breathing room between parties. I dove into the Modan yaki, a hearty, saucy okonomiyaki with noodles. Perfect for late-night cravings, it's admittedly on the greasier side. The spicy raw tuna egg salad followed suit: enjoyable but standard. As for the Russian roulette takoyaki, it regrettably mirrored the taste of frozen aisle fare.

The prices are the real winner here; they make up for the culinary rollercoaster. But a note of caution: at the time of my visit, Kenka was sporting a 'C' grade in food safety, a critical detail for diners to consider. All in all, come to Kenka for affordable bites, a convivial setting, and an authentic izakaya hangout, but set your gourmet expectations aside.

Title: A Refreshing Find for a Post-Church Meal

After a Sunday service near Union Square, my boyfriend and I were in search of a light yet different dining experience and stumbled upon this quaint spot we found on Yelp. The cozy setting, with a welcoming capacity of about 25, offered both intimacy and comfort with a mix of seating arrangements. Arriving at noon, we beat the rush and settled into a quiet table at the rear of the restaurant.

The service immediately impressed us—our waitress was the epitome of friendliness, enhancing our experience with her warmth. The complimentary chips provided a promising start, teasing our appetites with their tastiness.

My choice was the rice bowl with quinoa and grilled steak, a dish that perfectly matched my craving for a healthy yet protein-packed option. While reminiscent of Chipotle's bowls, this version stood out with a boldly flavored side sauce. My partner's Huevos Rancheros disappeared in a testament to its flavor and heartiness, suggesting it's a dish worth returning for.

Regretfully, the Mexican Hot Chocolate caught my eye only on our way out, leaving me with a tantalizing reason to revisit. I'm eager to explore more of what this delightful eatery has to offer on our next trip.

In short, if you're in the area and on the hunt for a meal that satisfies the desire for something wholesome without sacrificing taste, this little gem near Union Square is well worth a visit.

Title: No-Frills Dining with a Quick Service

I recently dined at a no-frills restaurant known for serving up inexpensive, speedy meals. My visit on a bustling Saturday evening around 6 PM was just in time to snag the last available table. Opting for the salt and pepper chicken over rice with a side of pork chops, I was pleased to see that despite the crowd, our food was swiftly served.

The star of the meal was undoubtedly the salt and pepper chicken; it was juicy, well-seasoned, and the accompanying rice and pickled veggies created a harmonious blend of flavors. The portions were generous, especially considering the affordable cost.

Unfortunately, the restaurant's famous pork chop failed to hit the mark. Overpowered by excessive grease and an overwhelming saltiness, the chop, while tender, proved to be a challenge to enjoy.

Priced around $10, the experience didn't leave me regretful. With a diverse menu on offer, I'm open to returning, perhaps to sample other dishes and give their desserts a chance.

Title: Unmatched Vibes and Views at TriBeCa's Gem

Nestled in the heart of TriBeCa, this classic New York City haunt exudes excellence with its superb drinks, top-notch service, and an energetic crowd that complements the urban vibe. The bartenders, especially Antonio and Rafael, elevate the experience with their friendly, attentive, and professional manner.

The rooftop patio is a must-visit, offering breathtaking panoramic views of downtown and the Freedom Tower—don't miss out on snapping some stunning photographs here. Even the restroom experience is noteworthy, reminiscent of the stylish facilities at the Standard, complete with impressive city vistas.

For anyone seeking a quintessential NYC outing with a view, this spot is an undeniable winner.

Title: A Dissonant Dining Experience

Upon entering the restaurant, one might be mistaken for thinking it's a casual airport eatery, setting an expectation misaligned with both menu offerings and pricing. My guest and I indulged in a meal costing $92 before taxes, which included two glasses of wine, an appetizer, and a shared rice dish.

The starter, Gambas al estilo de elBulli 1996, presented shrimp artistically flattened with a savory paste evocative of shrimp heads, an intriguing choice for seafood lovers. The accompanying bread, while crisp, could benefit from a slight softness for improved palatability.

Our main, the arroz negro cremoso con calamares, promised a feast for two but delivered a visual illusion. Arriving in a vast, deep bowl, it teased with generous squid pieces, yet the rice underneath was a mere shallow layer, leaving us wanting and a little deceived.

The flavors shone through, the calamari cooked to perfection, and the rice decadently flavorful. However, for a restaurant with high-end prices, one expects a certain generosity that matches the cost, both in portion size and the dining environment.

My rating hovers at a 2.5, nudged slightly upward by the quality taste. Yet, the dissonance between ambiance, portion presentation, and price leaves a lingering sense of dissatisfaction. Advice to potential diners: be cognizant of the restaurant’s incongruities and perhaps eat a little beforehand.

This is really a 3 1/2 star review. The hubby and I had movie date night last night, and it happened to be across the street from Wagamama. We decided to grab a quick bite there before the film. I was hesitant to go given my last experience, where I was treated with total disregard because the wait staff had some misguided judgments and assumptions. But, the hubby talked me into giving this place a second chance since I had a healthy conversation with management, and felt that my concerns were heard.Anyone who knows me knows that service to me is as important as the food, if not more so. Because bad service will ruin a meal faster than anything. And, on that alone, the Wag hit out of the ballpark. Though we were wondering if the waiter knew I was the outraged customer since he claimed to be the manager during that hullabaloo.Kahlid was our server, and he was great. He was welcoming, and he clearly has the kind of personality that's made for hospitality.Kahlid also managed to do something that seems to be a forgotten thing in New York City, and that's check on customers to see how they're enjoying their meal, after they've gotten their food. I'm not quite sure why so many servers at New York restaurants fail to check back on tables after the food came out. We always notice when it does too. It makes a big difference.The food was mostly good this time too. We started off with the bang bang cauliflower. That's always been a hit here.My ramen wasn't the best, and it wasn't the worst. I had the chili chicken ramen, spicy. The chicken was cooked perfect (last time I was there the meat was so over cooked it tasted like burnt rubber) and it definitely hit the spot. I'm much more of a soup broth person than a noodle person, so I asked for an extra side of broth. I wish I had taken Kahlid up on his offer to get me the spicy broth rather than the regular. Jayson had appetizers. He had the salad and then the chicken karaage, which is Japanese fried chicken. This was a huge miss for us. I don't know if it was overcooked, or just not the way we're used to, but it wasn't our favorite. The sauce was awesome.What helped to really make the difference tonight was Kahlid let us know after we ordered that because the food it cooked to order, sometimes dishes will come out at different times. I wish someone had told us that on any of our dozens of visits to Wagamama. That's been a huge irritation in the past. But, having the server let us known that our meals might come out a few minutes apart from one another made a huge difference. Our expectations shifted, in a positive way, and we were like, "Okay, no problem."It turned out to be a really great choice to grab a bite, and definite improvement over the last two times at this Wagamama. Will we be back? If we go to a movie at the theater across the street, it's possible. But I don't know if I'd go out of my way for this.  Again, it says a lot that corporate took my concerns to heart, because that was such a bad experience. But also, sometimes a customer who had a rather unpleasant experience simply wants their feelings and concerns addressed and heard. In this case, the latter got the former, and it turned out to be a good thing.

Title: A Quinoa Bao Bun Revelation

If you're on the hunt for a healthy lunch spot with a flair for flavor, look no further. This gem of a restaurant takes a leaf out of Dig Inn's book but turns the page with its standout dish: quinoa bao buns. An absolute must-try, these buns steal the show with their warm, soft embrace, housing a burst of savory delight that outshines their bowl counterparts.

While the bowls are commendable – the shrimp bowl boasting crispy coconut shreds that playfully contrast with smooth green curry, and the braised beef bowl offering a hearty mix with beans – it's the slightly mushy rice in the shrimp bowl that may distract from its overall appeal. Nonetheless, the beef is tender, and the curry is expertly spiced.

But let's circle back to the main attraction: the quinoa bao buns are so satisfyingly packed with flavor that they alone warrant a return visit. Pairing them with a side could easily round out a meal, leaving you full and content. Healthy eating rarely tastes this good!

This place was such a random find but nonetheless it was an amazing find. From the moment I walked in til the moment I left, I can honestly say I had an amazing experience! The food was amazing, the service provided was exceptional & the ambiance was beautiful with my favorite Spanish songs playing. Its such a lively & friendly environment, you just don't want to leave! Best part about brunch was getting the small pitcher that comes with the food!-STEAK AL CARBON AND EGGS - Flame Grilled New York Strip Steak Cooked to a Temperature of your Choosing, Served with two Eggs any Style and Home Fried Potatoes- BRUNCH BURRITOS - Scrambled Eggs, Cheddar Cheese, Chorizo or Bacon, Beans, and Mexican Rice, Guacamole, and Pico De Gallo. Topped with Salsa Rojo and Cotija Cheese-Small pitcher of mimosa Its a great place to grab a bite, a few drinks or even have a qcelebration with 2 floors & 3 bars to choose from!

I came here on a Friday night for happy hour. It does get pretty loud and rowdy as it is a sports bar so keep that in mind if you're looking for a more low key spot. With that being said the music and the ambiance was great. The food was delicious but my only gripe was with the drinks. I tried their "Seasonal sangria" first and it tasted mostly watered down with no real flavor. I then tried the "Grapefruit crush" which was a little better but lacking in flavor as well. Should have just stuck with wine or beer. I tried their famous "Raise burger" which was very filling with a lot of fries, cooked perfectly crispy. I actually finished the whole burger (which is rare) and I didn't feel overly full after. They also have a deal where you can get 3 small plates for $29. There's a section upstairs as well that you can rent for private events. I would definitely recommend making a reservation during the weekend because most of the tables around us I saw were reserved. This is a solid choice if you're in the area looking for a place to eat/drink/hang out.

I recently dined at an Italian restaurant conveniently located next door to the theater showcasing "Book of Mormon," making it an accessible spot for a pre-show meal. The establishment offers typical midtown fare with prices ranging from $20-$30 per dish. With seating available both downstairs and upstairs, each area provided its own bar setting.

Upon visiting with a party of four at 5pm, we found our reservation unnecessary as the place was quite empty. Despite the lack of patrons, we experienced a 30-minute wait for our food. Service could have been more attentive, particularly regarding drink refills and the timely filling of water glasses, as our bartender also took on the role of waitress.

As for the meal itself, it was average – satisfactory yet unremarkable Italian cuisine. The portion sizes seemed disproportionately small relative to the cost. Considering the overall experience and value, I would suggest looking for alternative dining options in the area.

Tucked away in Kips Bay, Sachi Asian Bistro is a gastronomic delight that serves up an array of scrumptious dishes. The lunchtime bustle is testament to its popularity, with the Bento box lunch special standing out as a particularly satisfying choice. Both the sushi and Pad Thai come highly recommended, bursting with authentic flavors. It's clear that at Sachi, any selection from the menu is a surefire path to a delightful meal.

Title: A Delightful Discovery of Congee and Rice Noodle Rolls!

I recently had the pleasure of trying congee and rice noodle rolls at this restaurant, and I must say, I was thoroughly impressed. The cravings that followed are a testament to how delicious the meal was. When it comes to value, the portions are generous, particularly the congee which offers a hearty meal at a great price.

For fellow South Asians unfamiliar with congee, imagine a comforting bowl of Haleem but with a distinct ginger zing - it's mouthwateringly good. Although, if you're not a fan of ginger, you might find the flavor quite prominent.

My experience was so positive that a return visit is unquestionably on the cards. An additional pleasant surprise was their offering of hot water, a habit I've since adopted; it really does feel better than the room-temperature alternative. Highly recommended!

I haven't had a drink there, I've only had their food each time, I've been and it's always super yummy. I usually get the vegetarian chili( awesome) and the nachos( delicious). I'm surprised how yummy their food is. The place is always packed and the servers are attentive. Once you step place in this bar, it's easy to forget that you are in New York City.

Title: Cozy Dinner with Standout Dishes at The Beekman Gem

Last week, a friend and I enjoyed a delightful weeknight dinner at a restaurant nestled within the stunning Beekman hotel. For starters, we shared the innovative beet "linzer" appetizer, a savory twist on the traditional tart that was simply remarkable. 

We also indulged in a creamy winter squash side, a juicy burger, and the perfectly al dente Cavatelli with a rich lamb sauce. Each dish was prepared with care, but the linzer, burger, and a light yet flavorful soufflé, complemented by a tart lingonberry jam, were the true showstoppers of the evening.

While service occasionally lacked that attentive edge, it didn't detract significantly from our overall experience. The Beekman's grandeur, particularly its bar/library and atrium, added a dash of elegance to our dining adventure.

Eager to return, I've got my eye on the steak frites for the next visit. The restaurant hits the mark with its culinary creativity and charming ambiance, making it a spot worth recommending.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Casa Mono

Despite a friend's high regard for Casa Mono, my skepticism lingered due to a past uninspiring experience at its sibling, Bar Jamon. When a visiting friend craved Spanish cuisine, I gave it a chance.

Upon arrival, my reservation was honored promptly, but the seating arrangement was cramped, compromising privacy and comfort as we were wedged close to our dining neighbors in the restaurant's quest to maximize space.

Service was marred by a pushy approach, with staff steering us towards pricier menu items and wines, which I found off-putting. They advocated for more dishes than necessary, resulting in an overabundance of food for our party.

Our meal commenced with a charcuterie board and mussels, neither living up to their steep prices. Luckily, the subsequent servings of octopus, duck, and steak were savory delights, though the high cost for small portions left us wanting more value for our money.

Conclusively, while some dishes were a hit, the overall experience did not justify the expense nor the service. My return to Casa Mono seems unlikely.

Auntie's Kimbap. I so wanted some kimbap tonight and walked from 45th and 3rd to get some. I really wanted to try the jalapeño and spicy tuna kimbap, but was utterly deflated and so bummed to find they only accept cash. Really? I don't generally carry cash ever and didn't feel like searching for my bank to get out money for a roll or two. I will try to make it back when I have some paper dough or if they ever decide to accept credit card in the near future, I am hoping for the latter. The kimbap roll pics looks so yummy I could have eaten the paper pictures even. Cash only bites big time. It keeps out a lot of patrons I feel.

We came later on a Friday night and somehow managed to grab a seat without waiting. Started with some appetizersMouthwatering chicken - Mala spicyCucumber salad - refreshing Beef rice noodle soup - extremely flavorful yet salty broth. Beef was tender. Not much spice even with spicy level 2. The rice noodles were pretty soft and didn't retain much flavor, left me wanting for more. Pay at the front.

Alize was our server And after going there for two days in a row I can effectively say I have tried the entire menu. Every time I come here I just grab a seat in the lounge area which is well illuminated has great music and typically awesome service. My favorite part is perhaps the comfortable sitting in the Ready availability of a one Michelin star restaurant experience. It's perfect for a girls night a date or even a corporate event. The only reason I Docked one star is because the first night I went there I made the mistake of ordering the halibut and the Seabass. I will say even just their popcorn with the hint of black pepper in it is something to experience. I don't drink so I have had the range of their mocktails and the bartender is a genius With taking my preferences in the account and customizing healthy refreshing beverages that complement the entrées. This review really is a shout out to my server on the second night-Alize.More food specific comments to come

After a late night comedy show on Canal street my friend and I were looking for an spot where we could get some staple Chinese dishes in a comfortable setting. Given the time (around 10 PM) we were worried nothing would be open but then I remembered hearing about the late night spot "Wo Hop". I had never been and asked my friend if she'd be down to try a new spot. She accepted and I'm convinced it was the best decision I made that entire week.The entrance for the spot is a little inconspicuous, we almost walked past it twice! When we found our way though we were pleasantly surprised. The space itself is on the smaller side but has several booths and stand alone tables inside. However, what really got me was the decor. Pictures of patrons and celebrities who've dined there literally adorn the every inch on the walls, along with a few dollar bills with notes for the restaurant inscribed on them. I liked this because it was different, it really added to the experience.When it came time to order we were taken back by the vast amount of options they had. He asked for the hot and sour soup ($4) to start, followed by an order of steamed dumplings ($4.85), chicken fried rice ($5.10), and beef lo mein ($5.60). They also served complimentary hot tea with our dishes. Overall the quality of the food was alright. A little greasy, but the plates were flavorful and filling. Not all Chinese restaurants can say that...The service was surprisingly good as well! The restaurant is staffed by older Chinese men with ESL, but they answered any questions we had and quickly brought out our dishes after we ordered. Overall a decent late night spot in Chinatown to get any Chinese dish you could imagine. We were lucky it wasn't busy, but I definitely could see it getting filled fast during peak hours. Try to go late night for that super authentic experience.

Lovely atmosphere and really spacious!Came for lunch and the burger ordered is seriously ginormous. Just look at it! Very juicy and flavorful, presented beautifully, with the nicest and fluffiest looking top bun. I like my fries a little more thicker but these were good too. Calamari was a bust - wished the marina was served on the side and not on top, because those pieces were super soggy when eaten since the sauce has soaked in for too long. Calamari also wasn't the crispiest either

Title: A Veggie Haven in NY: Superiority Burger Review

If ever a name captured the essence of a dining experience, it's Superiority Burger – a vegetarian sanctuary that's also a vegan's delight. Nestled in the heart of New York, this spot has swiftly climbed the ranks to become one of my absolute favorite veggie joints.

My visits to Superiority Burger are frequent and fervent. The allure was so strong that I even made a special trip for Rizo's renowned San Antonio Tex-Mex pop-up, only to find that I'd missed the boat, with everything sold out except the candy cane gelato. Trust me, even amidst winter's chill, that gelato was a scoop of heaven.

Talking about delightful surprises, the breakfast tacos and conchas remain unchecked on my list, but I'm determined to try them. On my latest pilgrimage, I couldn't resist snagging a Seth Bogart-designed t-shirt – a super cool marriage of fashion and food. The blue-on-white "scribbles" are as iconic as the flavors here.

And the food? Oh, the food. The veggie burger, especially with cheese, is a revelation. Then there's the broccoli – transformative, enough to convert any skeptic to the "dark, chlorophyll side". It's not your average supermarket fare; it's Superiority's magic on a plate.

Excitingly, there's a cookbook now – definitely penned on my Christmas wishlist – promising the secrets to those classic Superiority recipes, along with a sprinkle of NY charm. The inclusion of local favorites like the Cast family is a personal touch that speaks volumes about the community this place nurtures.

Be forewarned, the physical space of Superiority Burger is as modest as their broccoli is bold. Seating is a game of musical chairs, but the menu's ever-changing seasonal offerings make it worth the dance.

Superiority Burger doesn't just serve food; it curates an experience for the soul – and it's one worth savoring bite by bite.

iang doesn't like being chewed, so I don't recommend you Go Chew iang, but if you really want to, that's your prerogative.One of the awesome and awesomely priced Korean stands inside the excellent Korean food Hall on 32nd Street (Food Gallery 32, what an imaginative name), which is actually one of the highlights of all of Manhattan - so come here and check it out and maybe eat at all the different stalls because they're all actually pretty awesome in my opinion.

If you haven't already seen them on Instagram, than this spot is a little hidden gem on Christopher street in the west village. It's a small narrow spot with a few tables and the front counter where you order.  I got the pleasure of meeting the owner, David, and he was super nice and down to earth, loved that! It was nice to hear where Flip'n Toss came about and what not.  Ok. Back to the food.  Wow.  I got the Mac n cheese burger and the lobster Mac and cheese. Plan to share that crazy Mac n cheese burger with a few ppl because it is ABSURDLY large (and delicious) and you have to eat through the Mac to get to the burger! So yum. It's a double patty burger with lettuce and tomato and stuff.  Lobster Mac and cheese was also really good. The lobster tasted fresh and it was not skimpy on the lobster meat. Can't wait to go back and try some more of their cheesy goodness options

Went here late night and ordered some food in their patio area. Perfect for the munchies after going to happy hour! Service was great, food came out promptly. It was a little chilly in the back patio area, but I could see the patio being perfect for summer. We started off with a plate of roasted peanuts which they brought out straight away. The peanuts were good, but pretty spicy, definitely strong  really strong lemongrass and kaffir flavor. We then ordered the fried chicken which was excellent, we totally devoured it. The pineapple chutney and curry leaves gave it a unique flavor profile. The half Hainanese duck was also really good and the duck fat rice was amazing! My only minor complaint was that the small pieces of duck on the side of the large duck breast came with a ton of fat on them. The sauce was excellent. The Khao Soi noodles dish was awesome, so much flavor! These Thai noodle dishes are becoming my favorite thing ever. I love the the hot, soft noodle pairing with the crispy strips of top. We could barely get a table at 10:30 pm (Friday evening), so I imagine this place gets super packed during peak time.

Oh how I love this place! Luckily, I found this place online and the view caught my eye. The view was something I have never been to in my life. I been to a lot of restaurants with sky views! The view looked so dreamy that I knew this place is the place where my birthday should be celebrated at. As I tried to book a reservation, I only had an opening for lunch time so I took it! I liked how you are also able to ask for any accommodations or let them know about any celebrations. Being in New York the first time coming from California, we wanted to be there on time for the reservation. We called Lyft and then got stuck in traffic. There was a marathon going on that blocked the streets. My boyfriend and I, thanks to the Lyft driver's advice, to walk around the marathon to call another ride! We did and running in heels was an experience! The whole point of the story was that I called Manhatta and they were understanding to hold my reservation!
