I was so thankful!Once we got there, the view was just what I pictured and we sat in the area I wished for. The service was great! Our server explained the menu and the taste of the food very well! I went with his recommendations of what would taste best and I wasn't disappointed! I had the Chardonnay and my entrees were: 1st Entree:Red Snapper Crudo (Kumquats, Beets& creme fraiche)It was so good and very light taste! It reminded me of ceviche. I also tried my bf's Foie Gras Reuben (Tete de Veau, Dijon, Garlic Pickles &Brioche) which had a strong rich taste.2nd Entree:Striped Bass (Fingerling Potatoes, Trout Roe &Vin Blanc)Delicious!3rd Entree:Marcona Almond Creme Brûlée (Roasted Apples &Cider Caramel) My favorite! I'm glad I saw this on the menu!Birthday Dessert: The black and white dessert was delicious! It was a very sweet touch to end the meal.

I recently attended a trivia event at this gem of a restaurant, where the highlight, amidst the brain-racking questions, was undoubtedly the food. A notable shoutout to the curly fries – a deliciously crisp, golden delight that warranted an order per person at our table. Their crab cake appetizer deserves a special mention as well; it was so scrumptious that I almost enacted a scene to secure my last piece from being prematurely cleared away. The waitress was a joy, engaging with our shared enthusiasm for the curly fries with a warmth that added to the overall experience. I'm already planning my next visit for more of their tasty offerings!

Title: A Delightful Feast at Perry St for Restaurant Week

As a newcomer to New York's Restaurant Week in the summer of 2019, I couldn't have asked for a better introduction than a visit to Perry St, a hidden gem on the waterfront and a pride of Jean-Georges’ culinary empire. From the moment we were seated by the welcoming hostesses, the experience at Perry St was one for the books.

The Restaurant Week menu beckoned with enticing options, though the regular summer offerings – like the poached lobster – nearly swayed me for a future visit. The ginger margarita was a zesty preamble, perfect for nursing a sore throat and equally enjoyable for its flavor punch. Rye bread, thick and fresh, served with creamy butter, set the stage for an exciting meal.

My eggplant toast with ricotta was generous and honored the vegetable's natural taste, providing a delightful crunch despite its sturdy texture. The salmon sashimi appetizer sampled from my friend’s plate melted like butter, a testament to its freshness.

The main course presented a substantial parmesan-crusted chicken – a delicious deviation from the expected small portions of fine dining. While succulent and flawlessly cooked with a cheesy crust, the accompanying crunchy corn did stir a bit of confusion over its texture. A glass of pinot grigio complemented the dish nicely.

The meal reached its crescendo with the legendary chocolate molten lava cake, a balance of decadence and subtle bitterness that fully lived up to its hype. It was the perfect sweet note to round out a superb dining experience.

Overall, Perry St offered a delightful blend of fantastic food, attentive service, and a stylish yet unpretentious atmosphere. I eagerly anticipate my next visit to this laudable establishment.

Decent Ramen. I was walking by this store front with my boyfriend and we were actually looking for a pho place around the corner, but we were starving so we decided to stop in. We ordered green tea to start because it was chilly outside. Absolutely delicious!We also ordered salted edamame as an appetizer to share. This was yummy and fresh. My boyfriend ordered some pot stickers for himself and said they were good. Of course we had to try the ramen for our main entree and I ordered the only veggie option on the menu. The ramen was tasty, but super basic. Seriously just one piece of broccoli, two baby carrots straight out the bag and some corn? Really?I enjoyed the dish but would not come here again. My boyfriend enjoyed his ramen with meat, but also agreed my veggie option looked quite sad.

Had a seat out front on a beautiful afternoon. Started with a couple of pints of the Paulaner which is fantastic and crisp then I had the Sausage Platter, 3 different types of tubed deliciousness with potato salad, red cabbage and sauerkraut. Could not have been any better. Large portion perfectly priced. Service was also very kind and attentive.

Marta is one of the best things about NYC! And the staff and happy hour are two more reasons to love it like your mother. So, do you really need another pizza place in your phone?When it comes to Marta, in a word - yes! Marta is best known for it's delicious, gourmet pizzas. You can find them 50% off Sun-Sat between 3pm-6pm. My favorite is the mushroom and plain Margherita. But pizzas are not the only thing you will salivate over here.You will find delicious Italian favorites from branzino to clams to chicken with Italian salad. The menu rotates through the seasons with daily specials.But the dessert? That's where the moon hits your eye and it's amore! The ice cream pops? In a word - the greatest thing you will find in the Flatiron besides gossip on your ex! If this is not enough. How about the wonderful beers from Jack's Abbey to $18 champagne at happy hour. Or the late night happy hour with a free pizza for each bottle of wine you purchase. Go! Manga! Enjoy.

Tucked away in a cozy nook, The Wilson charms with its hip vibe and eclectic tunes—a hidden gem I'm thrilled to have discovered. On a recent visit for lunch, I indulged in their pre-fixe two-course menu, which to my delight included vegetarian options. The chia and chickpea burger impressed with its hearty flavor and classic veggie burger consistency, making it a satisfying choice.

We kicked off our meal with shared appetizers: the carrot hummus outshone expectations, its smoky taste wonderfully paired with chickpeas and aioli, while the avocado fries were a crispy delight served with a piquant, smoky aioli. Despite the restaurant's quiet atmosphere, I imagined a livelier happy hour or dinner scene soon to unfold.

Service was friendly though leisurely, which could be chalked up to the lead-up to a potentially busier evening. Regardless, The Wilson earns my recommendation for a memorable lunch and has me eager to return for their dinner or brunch offerings.

Came here right after seeing Oklahoma across the street at the Circle in the Square Theater. We wanted Japanese and Yelped it and this seems like a good choice.  No line when we walked in and it has a good crowd but was seated right away.  We lucked out with the NYC Restaurant Week menu, otherwise it is pretty pricey. The food was good and fresh but I think the service can be a little better.  Not sure if because the server we had dealt with tourists all day or what but she was not bad but do not have a lot of patience when I asked about the dish.  Not very forthcoming I should say.  I had to drag the answer out of her so I guess she is not one of the actors waiting tables to pay her rent lol.  I liked everything I ordered and didn't feel rushed but everything came out on time so for those who wants to eat before the show this is a good place for that:  I am not sure if i would come back if it wasn't for the restaurant week.  Nice ambiance and the host by the reception was a very friendly gentleman.

Title: A Slice of Sicilian Heaven in New York

If you're looking for an unforgettable pizza experience in the Big Apple, look no further. The Sicilian Pepperoni square is a true testament to the city's culinary prowess. Every bite sends you into a blissful state, with the pepperoni achieving the perfect balance of crispiness and seasoning. It elevates the slice to new heights, creating a symphony of flavors that dances on the palate. This isn't just another pizza; it's a love affair with food. Missing out on this would be a crime for any pizza aficionado. A must-visit indeed!

After hitting the books, I decided to take a lunch break. I considered my many options nearby, and came across this place.I decided to keep it simple, and order chicken with broccoli, with a side of rice. I was hoping for some decent tasting food, but unfortunately, the food came out rather bland.What stuck out most about this meal is the overuse of salt, which left me feeling lethargic for a few hours after the meal.The food did not sit well with me, and I tossed the leftovers rather than use them to cook a future meal.They need to work on their taste. And stop using so much salt... it is no substitute for good cooking.

I was told by a friend that these tacos rival the ones in San Diego. I know the original founders/owners come from that area so I was really excited to check it out.I ordered two adobada taco ($3.75), one carne asada taco ($3.95), and one pollo asada taco ($3.75). For the adobada, I felt like I got a lot of the small burnt bits that I couldn't taste much adobada at all. The pollo asada was a little dry and I was not a fan. My favorite of the three was the carne asada. I kinda wish they added more of the salsa and guacamole because I think that took away from the flavor of all the tacos.I'm not sure if it was the high expectations or if the tacos that I happened to eat were a fluke but I wasn't as impressed as I would've liked.
Go. Seriously just do it. Amazing food and service. They even helped with my reservations.

Title: A Scrumptious Shrimp Roll Experience at Luke's Lobster

I had the pleasure of dining at Luke's Lobster for the first time via MealPal, having enjoyed their famed lobster rolls at other branches. This visit introduced me to their shrimp roll - a delicious ensemble of bountiful shrimp packed into a buttered roll, complemented by mayo, a tang of lemon butter, and seasoning. The balance of shrimp to bun was just right, making for a satisfying bite.

While tasty, the meal's portion leaned towards the smaller side, so pairing it with a soup or salad might be ideal for those with a larger appetite. A heads-up for eager eaters: as you near the end of the roll, the shrimp may play a game of escape, but using the provided box as a tray should save you from losing any of that delightful seafood.

Navigating the short, table-lined hallway to the counter was a breeze, and my meal was promptly served. Efficiency is clearly on the menu here. I'm already looking forward to my next visit for a taste of their signature lobster roll.

I'll preface this by saying that I haven't tried a lot of NYC's Sichuan food, though down in H-town we have a multitude of excellent options - as an example, the chef at our Mala Sichuan was a James Beard finalist. Trust me when I say I know what Sichuan food should taste like.My cousin and I met up at Szechuan Mountain House for an early dinner on Monday night, but by 6 pm the place was completely packed - we snagged the last table for 2 and watched as people filled up the entryway, both inside and outside. I went to go wash my hands and discovered that the men's bathroom HAD NO FAUCET. It was literally a dry sink. (Please, dear God if there is one, let there be a separate employee bathroom...)The menu is beautiful and enticing, so despite the fact it was just 2 of us we ended up ordering 5 dishes: the mouth-watering chicken (口水鸡), conch in chili oil, fried pork intestines, lotus root with carrots and fungus, and spicy fried eel. The fragrant tea served with our meal and the pickled cabbage whet our appetite before the brisk arrival of our first orders.In order of how I liked the dishes:Mouth-watering chicken (口水鸡) (4/5) - This was a great appetizer because the flavors were spot-on and the texture of the chicken was soft and moist, not stringy. I would have liked this to be spicier, but I'm guessing they've turned down the heat for the general palate.Lotus root with carrots and fungus (4/5) - Pretty standard but prepared well. The lotus root is cut super thin but it's still cooked to a nice crispness. A good vegetarian option!Conch in chili oil (3.5/5) - A very textural dish, but lacking flavor. A good choice if you know you like the springiness of conch, but I wouldn't order it again. Not spicy enough and also a little under-seasoned.Fried pork intestines (3/5) - This is a really classic Sichuan dish and could be seen as the "exotic" option compared to the spicy fried chicken (辣子鸡). But there wasn't a good integration of the ma (numbing) and la (spicy) flavor base with the crisply fried pork intestines, which was a shame. A minute or two more of wok action would have drastically improved this dish.Spicy fried eel (2/5) - This was the only one of our dishes that was oversalted - in hindsight I should have mixed this one with the fried pork intestines. You can't really taste the eel, but it does earn a few points for having been fried well.Service is quite attentive, with waiters delivering fresh plates every so often and keeping the teapot topped off. But NYC - is this really the best Sichuan you've got? Maybe the one out in Flushing is more up to par, but given the crazy wait here it's unlikely I'd visit again.

Title: Sticky's Spot Hits the Spot

Despite the long line upon arrival, the service at this bustling location was surprisingly swift and delightful. The staff demonstrated remarkable patience and were incredibly helpful in tailoring orders to personal tastes—a plus in my book!

The restaurant's prime location near a park offered the perfect perch to enjoy my meal amidst a scenic backdrop. The venue's cleanliness was impressive given its high traffic, and the ability to dine al fresco added to the charm.

Now, let's talk about the food. As a self-proclaimed Chinese food connoisseur, the General Tso's medium poppers were an absolute delight, living up to my expectations with an option to have the sauce on the side or poured over the top. And the fries? A dream come true for any fry enthusiast.

Sticky's is a gem for anyone looking for a great meal in proximity to Penn and the Flatiron area. Whether you're a chicken aficionado or just in the mood for some tasty bites, this is the spot to settle in and indulge.

I came here with one of my buddies because I was craving for unlimited tacos! The first thing that came up in my mind was the Taco Shop.  Reservation is effortless since you can do it on yelp or their official website.  Their unlimited brunch for tacos or drinks is on the weekends only.  It was $24.00 for unlimited tacos and $18.00 for unlimited drinks for 1.5 hours.  1 taco here is about $4.00 usually.Food: I had about 12 tacos in total, and I was in love with the Baja Fish tacos and the pork belly tacos.  The Baja Fish is very soft, and it's delicious if you enjoy eating fish/seafood.  The pork belly tends to melt in my mouth, and it was so good.  I was not hungry the whole day after this bottomless brunch!Overall: I would come here when I have a craving for tacos.  But I would not come here daily.

Nice crispy crust, super tasty cheese and pepperoni. Upside pizza is definitely a nice step up from dollar pizza (which are more than a dollar for anything other than cheese anyway). At $4, I think the pepperoni slice is a reasonable deal. $2.50 for a small soda without refills was more than I was willing to pay though.Location was convenient for me from the theater district. Definitely not destination dining.

Title: A Cheesy Delight at The Melt Shop

I stumbled upon The Melt Shop and what a delightful surprise it turned out to be! Far from your average eatery, it elevates comfort food to a new level. I was treated to an indulgence of cheesy goodness, with each bite packed full of flavor. The Nutella and buffalo chicken grilled cheese sandwich is a must-try; it's an unexpected but perfect marriage of flavors.

Sipping on their luscious milkshake, I found it hard to believe how something so simple could taste so divine. However, be warned, the space is cozy—typical for NYC—and might require a bit of a wait during peak hours. But, with swift service and a line that moves quickly, you'll find the wait worthwhile.

This isn't the destination for those seeking a light bite. But if your taste buds are craving something decadent, The Melt Shop is your go-to for an unforgettable cheat day treat or a heavenly milkshake that'll leave you smiling long after the last sip.

Title: A Hidden Gem with a Lamb Specialty

Upon entering the restaurant, I was immediately taken by the sophisticated decor and the deceivingly spacious interior, thanks to the clever split-level design. The top floor, in particular, struck me as the perfect spot for a group celebration or special event.

Our lunch choice included the lamb sandwiches and the chicken with avocado and tomato. Both selections were a delight—expertly plated, bursting with flavor, and exuding a touch of elegance. It's rare to find a place that serves lamb so well, and this restaurant lived up to its reputation, which was the main draw for our visit.

However, I find myself withholding that one star due to the dinner menu prices, which seemed steep. Additionally, the lack of a dedicated kids' menu could be a drawback for family outings, although the kitchen's flexibility with a simple pasta and butter dish saved the day for my child.

Overall, the restaurant delivers an exceptional culinary experience, especially for lamb aficionados, in a charming and spacious setting.

Title: Unwavering Excellence in Soup Dumplings

Having revisited one of my favorite spots for soup dumplings, I'm delighted to report that they remain among the best I've ever savored. Despite a change in management, the restaurant continues to impress with exceptional service; the staff is remarkably attentive, ensuring a pleasant dining experience with swift food arrival. The portions are generous, perfectly suited for family-style sharing without compromising on quality. In summary, this eatery holds its ground as a top destination for dumpling aficionados.

I first heard of the Meatball Shop while watching Chopped where co-owner Michael Chernow was a guest judge. The name and concept stuck with me, but I never really made an effort to try it out. Flash forward to the other day when I was making dinner plans - I thought this would be a nice, casual spot to grab a bite so off we went. There are a few Meatball Shops throughout the city - most are in Manhattan and one is in Brooklyn; additionally, they're planning on opening their newest location in Westport, CT. They have a small space outside to eat as well as a pretty large, open dining space inside. The decor was modern but not too flashy, similar to other trendy spots I've been to. I noticed out of the corner of my eye a stairwell that went down to a place called Underballs - I'm not sure if this is a speakeasy or private event space or whatnot, but I was intrigued. Meatballs are the star of the menu as I expected, though they do have a nice selection of starters, sides, and salads. They also have "baller plates" where they incorporate meatballs into other dishes. Since we just wanted straight balls, we browsed the "build your own" section. They have a number of proteins to choose from for the meatballs, as well as sauces to pair them with. We went with two varieties - the classic meatballs with classic tomato sauce and the spicy pork with parmesan cream sauce. Each plate came with four meatballs as well as a little focaccia. The meatballs are good - growing up in an Italian household nothing can personally beat my mother's, but these are some of the best I've had from a restaurant. The tomato sauce was good and the parmesan cream was surprisingly light - also I was pleasantly surprised at the nice amount of heat in the spicy pork. We also ordered two sides - roasted broccoli and rigatoni with tomato sauce. These were both good - the broccoli was paired with chilis and garlic which gave it great flavor, and the rigatoni was served al dente with their tomato sauce.Service was great, everyone was really friendly and the food came out at a good pace. Overall, I was impressed with The Meatball Shop. While I'm not sure when I'll be back, this is a solid go-to option and it's nice to know I can get decent meatballs when dining out.

A surprisingly calm corner in Grand Central Station. Located in a corner on the main level of the station, the spacious restaurant is an oasis. The lunch menu is limited  , but the dishes are tasty and well presented. The prices are reasonable and they accept reservations.

Title: A Mixed Experience During Restaurant Week

I recently dined here for restaurant week and had a decent experience. For $42, the all-you-can-eat salad bar, along with a variety of meats and sides, offers good value. The servers, true to the Brazilian style, brought different meats directly to the table. The garlic steak was a highlight, perfectly cooked, while some other options were unfortunately dry. Service was quick, and a special nod goes to the fried banana side, which was a standout.

However, there were a few letdowns. Not being presented with the wine menu was disappointing, and despite having a reservation, we were handed a buzzer and had to wait—an approach to timing that I found less than ideal.

While the quality of the meats varied, possibly due to the set restaurant week menu, it left me wanting more of the premium cuts. Considering the fierce competition among New York's steak houses, especially in this price range, I'm on the fence about a return visit. My experience lands at a rating of 3 to 3.5 stars.

On my way back to Penn Station my friends and I  decided to stop in and order some appetizers and drinks at the bar. There was time to kill while waiting for our train back to Jersey. I'm so happy I stopped in. I saw lots and lots of people with Ranger Jerseys on. They were all here to watch the game and cheer on their team. There was so much team spirit, it was infectious!I arrived at a good time, and was able to get some of the last available seats at the bar. One my friends ordered HARRY'S MARTINI- Elder Natural Flower Liqueur, Russian Standard Vodka, Lavender Syrup, Lemon Juice, Lemon Twist Garnish. He really enjoyed this. My friend Lisa had been here before and suggested we try their appetizers. I really wasn't hungry because I just came from a Restaurant Convention at the Javits Center where I sampled lots of new food dishes, but I figured a couple bites here and there wouldn't hurt and I shared everything with my friends. Our Two bartenders were originally from Ireland and they couldn't of been nicer. They had a lovely Irish accent and were so polite. I knew they couldn't have been in NY that long because they were super friendly and not hardened yet.Mustang Harry's had a great assortment of spirits, some I've never even seen or heard of. The drinks were properly made and served with a smile.There were several flat screens for watching different team sports, golf, or the news.This place itself is long and somewhat narrow. In the front part of the restaurant as you walk in there are booths along the wall and some tables in the back. The decor is rustic and warm. The long bar is the centerpiece of this establishment. The bartenders even lit colored candles and placed them all around the top of the bar. Which added to the ambiance.I wanted something to nibble on so I chose the DEVILED EGGS and Double Smoke Bacon. These were so tasty I could've eaten a dozen of them. Anything topped with bacon is amazing!The second thing that I tried was the LETTUCE WRAPS K-TOWN STYLE. These wraps were so good. It was like a burst of flavor in your mouth.Hanger steak, pepper slaw, sriracha Aioli served on lettuce. There was a nice spice to them and again I could've eaten plates full. I didn't stay too long because I had to catch a train.When I come back into the city I will definitely make sure I return here.

Almond croissant and chocolate almond croissant are big and have good amount of fillings. The croissant is moist, not crunchy not too sweet.Eclairs have smooth fillings and icingFlourless chocolate cake is dense and has perfect sweetness.All of the pastries are very enticing and pretty. Fast service and helpful staff

5 Napkins Burgers has it all. It's obvious by the name, you will be able to enjoy some of their delicious burgers but they have so much more. The original plan was to hit up another spot but I'm glad my bestie decided on 5 Napkins. This happen because he happened to be at said location with a friend for their late evening happy hour. Who knew? This is one of the only places that has a midday and evening happy hour. You can't beat that. As I mentioned, I was having a late bottomless brunch with friends and boy did they deliver. The staff, particularly our waiter was awesome. Although we waited a bit for our meals, it was so so worth the wait. Two of us had the grilled chicken sandwich and my other friend had the burger. Everything was cooked to perfection. The drinks kept flowing and our waiter made sure we had a great experience. 5 Napkins will officially be in my rotation. I highly recommend going with friends, the vibe and food is so worth the time.

I was initially hesitant about dining at this hotel restaurant, but its positive reviews convinced me to give it a try. My dining companions and I started with the hummus and octopus appetizers, both of which set a promising tone for the meal. For the main courses, we chose a mix of fish and pasta dishes, complemented by a selection of drinks.

The quality of the food was impressive, leaving everyone in our party quite satisfied. There were minor inconveniences, such as having to visit another floor to access the restrooms, and a slight wait before our waiter approached us. However, once we were in his care, the service was attentive and helpful.

In conclusion, the dining experience was quite pleasant and exceeded my reservations about hotel restaurants.

Title: A Bowl of Excellence at This Local Ramen Shop

My dining experience at this incredible Ramen shop has left me utterly impressed. From the very first slurp, the Ramen proved itself to be excellent. I indulged in the standard bowl, while my son tackled the spicy variant, both of us relishing every mouthful. The side dishes didn't disappoint either - the Truffle sweet potato fries achieved a level of perfection I hadn't known was possible, and the pork buns were delightful. This wonderful Ramen shop isn't just a meal; it's a culinary highlight. Highly recommended for anyone craving authentic flavors and quality dishes.

Very very friendly staff which always makes my experience better. The original location is in Florence. The panini's are good, but not stuffed to the max. the are kind of flat/ not a hefty fully loaded sandwich. Nonetheless, it was still a very good sandwich. I ordered the #4 and the #13.4= Stuffed chicken with prosciutto cotto & mortadella, mushrooms, fresh mozzarella, rosé sauce.13= Marinated Eggplant, roasted onions, artichokes, sun dried tomatoes, olive spread, and pesto.The guy working there also gave me a sample of the soup and it was delicious. There are a few seats to sit and eat there or you can take it to go. I think i liked the 13 more than the 4 but both were sooo good. Would definitely return if in the area.

Title: A Top-Tier Grab n' Go Sushi Experience

If you're on the hunt for exceptional sushi on the go, look no further. This sushi spot stands out with its fresh, flavorful offerings, boasting an impressive array of rolls – including unique combinations that are sure to surprise even the most seasoned sushi enthusiasts. The compact venue may have limited seating at a communal table, but it more than makes up for it with its immaculate and welcoming interior. The friendly staff ensures a swift and pleasant service, making it a must-visit for anyone craving a quick sushi fix. Added bonus: it's certified kosher, which is definitely a draw for those with dietary considerations. Highly recommended for a fast, delicious sushi experience!

One of my most favorite meals ever! Absolutely outstanding food. Everything I had was delicious. Definitely get the Stuffed Garlic Bread and the Stracchino Gnocchi, absolutely divine!!Upate-I went to Don Angie again recently for my birthday and had the most wonderful meal and time! We got here early and snagged two seats at the bar. There is a month long wait to get a table reservation, but if you show up around 5:30pm, then you might get lucky and get a seat at the bar. Damien was our server (at the end of the meal we found out he was actually the GM!) for the night and he was fantastic! He took such great care of us and we were absolutely blown away by his hospitality. He made the best recommendations for us and since I'm a vegetarian he made sure that all the necessary adjustments were made in the kitchen.Hands down one of the best meals I've had. This is my absolute favorite place to get Italian cuisine. All the pasta is made in house and everything is super fresh. IG- @traveleen_gurl

had  a  perfect girls night out  after checking out a local gallery and some random shopping we ventured off to find a weekend happy hour and I'm sooo glad to have found Verlaine. Honestly this place was super sexy in decor . We arrived thinking happy hour was over at 7pm so we quickly placed an order for lychee martinis,  five spiced calamari, garlic wings, hot chips, and coconut curry shrimp.  The  lychee martinis were amazing!!!the food had potential, but my god I think I had to pour a bottle of salt to every dish, thank good each dish was accompanied by a dipping sauce because it gave the dish some flavor. After our first round of drinks we realized  the happy hour ended at 10pm, this was a complete game changer !!!  We ordered red sangrias, gin and tonics and. Some more lychee Martinis. The red sangrias were bomb, every drink literally had just the right amount of alcohol. Our server she was great but sad to say I couldn't remember her name from the amount of alcohol consumed but she was a doll. I will definitely be back for another girls night out.

I came here with 4 African American males, and we were asked to leave the outdoor patio, so we went to the inside. Once we were inside, we were asked what were we here for uh drink perhaps since it is a night club/ restaurant?! You're unable to come here with a party of African Americans. Management will turn you away and make you feel uncomfortable. You know how these places do.... They also have the BLACK security (set up as a decoy) come tell you. Don't bring your black dollars here. Management doesn't appreciate its black patrons! 11/30. Food is great but why waste your time on a place that doesn't want to accept black patrons ? CATCH will never get a dollar from me:-)

I've been waiting a while to try Areppas since I have heard good things about it. I ordered take out and the food arrived well packaged. I tried the "queen" arepa and the Cachapa. The "Queen" arepa was not my favorite. In my opinion it had too much avocado or mayo. Not sure. The Cachapa was good and big enough to share as an appetizer. Even though I was not very satisfied with my order I will still give it a second try in person.

Title: Hooters by MSG – A Wing Haven Amidst the City Bustle

After a 20-year hiatus, I revisited Hooters, lured by recent claims of their exceptional chicken wings. Opting for the location opposite Madison Square Garden, the restaurant offers an enviable view of the city bustle from its wrap-around windows, particularly impressive from the second floor.

The interior's layout, with multiple TVs and dual levels, creates a sports-friendly ambiance without sacrificing sightlines. However, my focus was squarely on the supposed fresh, never-frozen wings. Skeptical but curious, I ordered a 10-piece of the original Hooters wings alongside the Blackened Dry Rub variant, complemented by curly fries, tater tots, and a Hooters salad.

The wings lived up to the hype. Their texture bore no hallmarks of prior freezing, confirming the menu's claim. Both the traditional and dry rub wings had a delightful crunch, the former reveling in its unexpected buttery twist on Buffalo, while the latter brought a peppery kick that would please fans of a more subdued, sauce-free wing. Surprisingly, the drumettes' size suggested drumstick lineage, yet maintained a succulent juiciness.

The sides, however, left something to be desired. The tater tots disappointingly soaked up excess grease, perhaps due to suboptimal frying temperatures, and the curly fries were unremarkably dry. The Hooters salad was overwhelmingly rich, packed with proteins like bacon bits and cheese, overshadowing the sparse greens.

Service was efficient and pleasantly understated, offering a family-friendly vibe without the strain of overzealous friendliness. Considering its prime location, prices were reasonable, and the wings alone warrant a return visit. All in all, for a wing enthusiast or anyone looking for a casual dining spot in the heart of Manhattan, Hooters by MSG stands out for its commendable wing fare.

Their website is full of Clickbait-And-Hook, and you might find some underage girls in here (Jailbait And Hook), so be careful.Could there possibly be a Philadelphia Eagles bar in New York City? Hell yes there is.It could only really be in Manhattan where they get away with that, where a lot of New Yorkers don't actually live. It's a hell of a bar on game day and gets pretty loud. Louder than a lot of Giants bars for that matter. And Jets. If you want to see the Eagles playing, then this is the Eagles place to come. If you want to meet a bunch of expatriates from Philadelphia, this is the place to come. It's not cheap but they neither is Barbie.

came on a Saturday around 12:30 and had to wait about 20 minutes for 2 seats at the bar. The bartender was super pleasant! I ordered the chicken chilaquiles from the brunch menu. Overall great flavor but not a huge fan of how it was played. The "fried tortillas" (aka chips) laid under the chicken which was mixed w salsa made the chips super soggy. Could have put it to the side or maybe served it faster, or maybe left the salsa on the side? Flavor overall was ok and speed of service was good for the busy brunch rush.

Yelp reviews lead me to this place.  The yelp nation loves it so you know I had to validate that.  Walking in it looks like your typical pub. It even has that typical pub smell which I am not the biggest fan of.  The bar area had some people but the tables were empty.  Don't think it is a hotspot for lunch so maybe dinner is better.  The service was pretty good even though there was only one person serving for lunch.  The guy made the experience nice for us. The menu is pretty straightforward. I have never had buffalo cheese curds though and they were the perfect snack. So good. The chicken sandwich had a lot of bread compared to chicken but it was still good. I went with the grilled fish tacos and I enjoyed them.  Everything was solid but it was still bar food. Nothing really elevated about it but doesn't mean the dishes weren't executed well.  In the end, the reviews aren't necessarily off.  It is a solid place with good food and on point service. Don't come if you want to be wow'd but if you are looking for a drink and a meal come through.  I have this at a 3.5 but bumped it up because I am feeling nice!

An amazing meal! We each got an entree and did some add ons to our meal. The biscuits were perfect cooked and crumbly. I had their signature sandwich with pepper bacon and a perfectly fried egg. The best part of the meal though was the fried chicken, I would go back and just get that. Also tip, look them up on yelp and put your name on the waitlist before you go. This place is small and you shouldn't expect to just walk in and get a spot.

Ikinari Steak House once again proves why it's a go-to spot for steak enthusiasts. The steak served sizzling on a hot skillet is a culinary delight, hitting just the right notes of flavor and texture—especially when ordered rare, allowing the residual heat to continue the cooking process to perfection. The service at this location stands out for its excellence; the staff are not only friendly, but also eagerly assistive, ready to tackle any queries with a smile. Highly recommended for a top-notch steak experience!

TLDR: A sushi restaurant of two worlds. The front is great for high quality casual sushi and the back houses the Michelin-starred sushi bar that serves a top tier omakase. Good for a special occasion or if you're just looking to satisfy your sushi craving. I love Kanoyama. If you're eating in the main restaurant, ask for the maguro nakochi or tuna rib.I've been eating at Kanoyama for many years but only recently had the pleasure of dining at the rear counter. The rear counter is in the back dining room so it can get a bit loud, especially on a weekend night. However, you're so busy watching chef prepare each piece that you kind of forgot about your surroundings.Chef Noboyuki Shikanai is laser-focused when he serves that back counter. It was mesmerizing to watch him move, slice and form each piece. I didn't take many photos here because the omakase started when he appeared out of nowhere. Nigiri in his palm and simply said "fluke" then waited for me to take it. Each piece he described the fish and how it was dressed. His pace is good because you're not waiting endlessly for the next piece. There was nothing he served I didn't like and.. I got the fried botan ebi head too! Dessert also came with the meal which was a monaka (rice cracker) ice cream sandwhich with mochi and red bean. So good.If you're eating here for casual sushi, you absolutely must get the maguro nakochi or tuna rib. It's around $50 to $60 depending on the weight. The tuna rib is presented with a stack of nori, wasabi, scallion and spoons to scoop the tuna off. Here's a tip, order a side of sushi rice and have yourself a hand roll party. When you're done getting the easy meat off, they'll take it in the back and grill the rest of it. It's a twofer!Their standard rolls though are pretty great. Kanoyama is one of those restaurants that you do for literally any occasion. An excellent spot in the East Village.

Title: A Slice of History with Mixed Feelings at NYC's First Pizzeria

Review:

I ventured into NYC's first pizzeria, a must-visit for any pizza enthusiast, on Christmas Eve at 7pm. Surprisingly, our 15-minute wait was brief, considering the holiday crowd. A slight delay with our wine at the bar was promptly eclipsed by the charm of being escorted through the bustling kitchen to our quaint top-room table, with its small, brick-walled ambiance and very New York alley view.

We opted to share a small six-slice pizza and ordered a calzone. The pizza boasted a thin crust and a decent topping spread, but the flavor didn't leave a strong impression. The calzone's arrival was delayed due to a mix-up with the ingredients, but the staff swiftly corrected the mistake. Although tasty, the service missteps continued. The calzone's to-go box and our second round of wine were slow to arrive, with neighboring patrons voicing similar concerns.

Eventually, we found ourselves seeking out our waiter to settle the bill, and after realizing the forgotten to-go box wasn't coming, we reluctantly departed.

The overall experience was a rollercoaster—subpar service, yet the allure of the pizzeria's history and a satisfactory calzone earned them 3 stars.

Really cute brunch spot. Food was very good, nice atmosphere. Service was a little slow but overall had a great brunch experience. It's a small place so make a reservation if you can, but they have a self seating bar area. Definitely recommend & would come back.

Pretty above-average Vietnamese food. We came here on a Tuesday afternoon around 3PM so it was pretty empty in the restaurant. At least because of this, service was quick. I ended up getting a banh mi which helped fulfill my cravings for Vietnamese food, although I wished it had the pate. A little pricey overall, but it's about average for New York Vietnamese food.

This was the place that a family friend has been raving about their hot stone rice bowl (aka rice casserole).Finally got a chance to try this place after the original restaurant choice was rejected by some members of the group.On a Wednesday evening, we met up and the place was packed.  This place was more suitable for 4 people or less groups.  Otherwise you might wait a while to be seated for groups of 5+ which was what happened to us.We were promised a table and another group with a smaller number of people jumped ahead of us.  The entrance was narrow and not suitable for larger number of waiting customers, we were hovering over the patrons seated near the walkway which was never comfortable for customers eating nor waiting.The space between the tables were narrowed so it's best not to have a lot of items since there wasn't a lot of space to put your items and eat comfortably.Food-wise some dishes are awesome; others are okay.Congee: we got 2 dishes- Seafood -- which was the typical dish- Special which was good -- forgot the name.Rice Noodle Rolls/Crepes: we got 3 dishes- Scallions and Dried Shrimps dish was great; - Roast Pork was chopping up into smaller pieces which is good though you lift the rice noodles roll, it falls apart which I wasn't crazy about.- Fried Fritter (Dough): this was great.Rice Casserole: we got 4 dishes.- salted fish with minced meat -- this was great!- taro with preserved meat -- this was great!- preserved meat -- was ok.- chicken - was ok.The floor was a bit slippery while walking to the bathroom.  The bathroom is a single toilet and it's clean.Good for small groups, tight space, good for if you need a quick meal.

Text to friend (who is 8 months prego): Where do you want to eat?  What kind of cravings do you have?Friend's reply: My husband likes steak.*Wow, that's sacrifice.  8 months pregnant, you can only eat steak well done, and you are still contemplating dining options based on your husband's preferences.  You deserve to be nominated for the wife of the year award.  We came here for RW dinner.  The three of us ordered:- Calamari: A-ok 3/5- Steak tartare: Kind of bland, actually 3/5 - Carrot soup: Tasty 4/5- Hangar steak: Perfectly cooked medium rare and flavorful 4.5/5- Filet mignon: Perfectly cooked medium rare and tender 4.5/5- Salmon: The skin was over-salted.  The fish itself was ok.  3/5- Sides: mashed potatoes, creamed spinach, mac n cheese: Great! 5/5- Cheesecake: Eh 3/5- Profiteroles: Good 3.75/5- Tiramisu: Good 3.75/5Our server had a strange sense of humor/attitude, but got the job done.  Their strengths here are definitely their meats and sides.  Everything else I could have done without.  Overall, a 3.5.  If I come back, I will order the entrees a la carte and leave it at that.------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------*Argh, hubby didn't even make it to dinner...

Title: A Fiery Delight at Jaiya – An Authentic Thai Experience

My long-awaited dinner at Jaiya certainly didn't disappoint! After being enticed by their captivating commercials, my husband and I decided to celebrate our anniversary at their Upper East Side location. Pro tip: double-check their hours before you go; they've caught me off-guard a couple of times by being closed!

Upon arrival, the stunning decor that I'd admired on TV surrounded us. It was equally impressive in person, adding a special touch to our celebration. Although we started off close to a rather enthusiastic fellow diner, the staff was accommodating when we asked to move to a quieter spot.

The highlight of the evening was the food and drinks, which were as visually appealing as they were delicious. I indulged in a drink with a literal flame – a feast for the eyes and tastebuds. Our waiter, Win, was the perfect guide through the menu, recommending dishes and the not-to-be-missed spicy margarita. He was right; it was outstanding!

Our meal arrived promptly and was served piping hot. Jaiya's commitment to quality and the vibrant atmosphere has ensured that it's now on my list for future outings, especially when friends visit the city.

For anyone in NYC craving authentic Thai cuisine with a dash of flair, Jaiya is the place to go. No disappointments – just pure culinary bliss.

Despite my long-standing obsession with Xi'an's culinary offerings, my recent visit to one of its franchise locations left me with mixed feelings. Before I dive into the experience, let me share an unrestrained expression of my Xi'an infatuation through a rap that's as passionate as it is cheeky:

"If I was a Beatle I'd be JOHN,
If I was an Eagle I'd be DON,
But here at XI'AN, you best believe I'll get the N1."

Now, onto the review.

Ambiance: The restaurant swaps the beloved basement vibes of Queens for a more Americanized decor. While still inviting, it lacks the authentic Far East Asian atmosphere.

Service: This particular visit was marred by a less-than-welcoming staff. A certain employee seemed particularly irritable, making for a less pleasant experience.

Food: Despite the aforementioned drawbacks, the star of the show remains the N1 lamb cumin dish. While it hasn't quite maintained its basement-brewed perfection, it's a culinary masterpiece that keeps me returning.

Final Thoughts: The franchise may not fully capture the soul of Xi'an's basement origins, and the staff could use a lesson in hospitality, but the love for the N1 secures a hard-earned 5 stars. If you find yourself in New York and have only one meal to spare, make it Xi'an.

Title: A Plant-Based Palate Pleaser!

I've recently embarked on an exploration of plant-based cuisine and, on the high recommendation of friends and colleagues, visited this charming restaurant. My first impression was of a spotlessly clean and inviting space.

Deciding what to order was a challenge, but I settled on the quinoa taco salad and a small mac and cheese. The salad was not only a feast for the eyes but also generous in size. The seitan chorizo was particularly noteworthy for its perfect seasoning and freshness. The mac and cheese was unexpectedly delightful, with a creamy sauce that defied its dairy-free nature and an intriguing addition of shiitake bacon.

My companions enjoyed the pesto pasta, spicy Thai salad, and classic burger—all of which I can attest were delicious. The chicky chicky was the only dish that didn't quite hit the mark for me, feeling a touch too oily for my taste. A highlight was the condiments, especially the beet ketchup and aioli, available in copious amounts.

The grand finale was a chocolate dairy-free ice cream that was nothing short of a revelation, especially for someone with dairy sensitivities like myself. The secret to its creaminess is apparently a blend of coconut, cashew, almond, and hazelnut, which achieves a smooth texture without an overpowering coconut aftertaste.

This restaurant has won me over, and I eagerly anticipate my next visit to delve further into their menu.

On weekends they serve brunch until 4 pm. The lunch/dinner items are available ONLY after 4 pm. I stopped by on a Saturday to have a dinner. I went with lamb tagine with green sauce (charmoulla). Lamb was good. One complaint I have is that the sauce was a lot milder that the one I had from another Moroccan place. But if you like mild taste, you will like it. Bastilla was a good concept - chicken stuffed in a crispy pastry. That was also mild for me. I liked tagine better than bastilla though.

Good place to eat in the village.If there were half stars this would have been 4.5.Cool ambiance.  Not too loud.  A little cramped (to be expected in winter with all the coats).  Inviting staff.  Relaxed feeling.Good menu.  Vegan/Allergy friendly.  Good brunch options as well with non-vegan choices.Good options for all and a well above average American restaurant.  Food was very good - would definitely go back again!

My boyfriend and I decided to try this spot for lunch and were pleasantly surprised by the additional offerings with their donburis — a side salad, pickles, and sweet beans, which aren't available during dinner. I opted for the Unagi and Egg Don, which was a delightful meld of flavors. The eel was cooked to perfection, the egg was just right, and the dashi brought it all together harmoniously. The accompanying pickles and side dishes were also tasty and complemented the main dish well. I even had a chance to taste the Oyako Don from my boyfriend's plate, and it was equally scrumptious. A great lunch experience overall!

Title: Cozy Evening at Veselka – A Mixed Bag but Worth Another Visit

My recent dinner at Veselka turned out to be a pleasantly surprising experience with only a minor hiccup. The Ukrainian Pierogi Bowl, commemorating the restaurant's 65th anniversary, was an enticing centerpiece of the meal. This hearty dish came with a variety of pierogi – potato, meat, and sauerkraut – though there was a mix-up that led to an extra serving of meat instead of sauerkraut. I opted for the fried version, anticipating a pan-fried texture, but they arrived deep-fried, which was somewhat disappointing. Nevertheless, the bowl was flavorful, especially with the addition of slab bacon, grilled kielbasa, and sweet caramelized onions.

Balancing out the meal, the borscht was exceptional – a must-try that radiates authentic Ukrainian flair. As for the beverages, the beer and coffee on offer complemented the food nicely.

Service at Veselka was efficient and friendly, adding to the overall positive experience. The ambiance of the place was inviting and contributed to an enjoyable dining atmosphere.

Despite the slight misstep with the pierogi, I'm inclined to return to Veselka. Next time, I'll be sure to clarify my preference for how I'd like them cooked. Overall, I would recommend giving this spot a try, especially for those looking for a taste of Ukraine in the heart of the city.

I've always wanted to try Xi-an Famous Foods and was finally able to try it the other day. I came around 5pm on a weekday and it was fairly empty. Cashier was very helpful with the menu and was friendly from start to end. This location is very small with limited seating. Hospitality is included.As for the noodles, I got [N2] which is the spicy & tingly beef hand-ripped noodles. I chose their mild spicy but I'll probably get their regular spicy next time. I really enjoyed their thick, chewy noodles. Even though the beef was cooked to perfection and literally melts in your mouth, it was a tad salty for me so couldn't finish the meat. Overall, Xi-an is conveniently located everywhere in the city. I would highly recommend to anyone who wants quick and quality food.

Title: Underwhelming Experience Despite Appealing Presentation

I recently dined at a restaurant that, while promising an enticing visual feast, fell short on flavor. The udon noodles with shrimp tempura soup appeared delectable at first glance but proved disappointingly bland. Although the dish wasn't terrible, it lacked the culinary excitement I anticipated. Suffice it to say, I finished my meal without much enthusiasm and wouldn't return for a second helping. However, it's worth noting that the service was impeccable, with a staff that was both attentive and pleasant. If you're curious about this spot, feel free to give it a shot, but in my opinion, your taste buds might prefer you pass.

Came here once during restaurant week. The service was extremely slow to start the night. They took about 10 minutes to serve us the complimentary bread and then maybe another 5-10 to take our order.As part of the resturant week special, I ordered the meatballs, branzino (sea bass) with zucchini and tiaramasu for dessert. All three dishes were pretty good but there are definitely better Italian spots in the city.

Title: An Elevated Journey Through Korean Gastronomy at Atomix

Dining at Atomix isn't just a meal; it's an immersive experience into the artistry of Korean cuisine. As a novice to Korean omakase, my $500 meal opened my eyes to the intricacies of flavor and presentation that this culinary style embodies.

With 10-12 meticulously curated courses, each plate was a revelation of thoughtful consideration. The accompanying cards detailing the dishes' origins enriched the meal with stories, transforming the evening into a cultural sojourn within a cozy, homelike ambiance. The cards also make a charming memento of the night.

Before the feast begins, selecting personal chopsticks from an array of beautifully crafted options offers a touch of interactivity and appreciation for detail. Similarly, the provision of a tiny chair for handbags exemplifies the establishment's commitment to guest comfort and luxury.

Atomix masterfully melds Korean culinary staples, such as chojang and red bean paste, with Western elements like buttermilk cheese and caviar, showcasing the chefs' passion and ingenuity.

Upon arrival, the seamless service begins. A skilled waiter at the bar presents an inventive cocktail menu, like the sharply delightful Samioko. As you transition to the chef's counter, the attentive staff and sommelier ensure a seamless flow to the dining experience, which is, in every sense, flawless—save for perhaps the dessert options, which may cater more to an Eastern palate.

One word of caution: secure an early reservation to avoid a midnight departure. Moreover, be wary of the truffle upsell, an unnecessary extravagance that adds little to the already exceptional flavors.

In summary, Atomix delivers an exceptional journey through Korean gastronomy, carefully balancing tradition with a modern touch, though it's not without its pitfalls. It's a top-notch experience that leaves a lasting impression and a deeper appreciation for the craft of fine dining.

Title: Unforgettable Flavors Await at Mama's Too!

I've realized that sometimes I overlook sharing my thoughts on the absolute gems I frequent, and Mama's Too is the epitome of such places. This pizzeria has become my go-to spot for pizza cravings and the answer I excitedly give when friends ask for recommendations.

Having discovered Mama's Too shortly after its inception in February 2018, I've witnessed the buzz grow exponentially, especially post their New York Times review acclaim. Frank, the maestro behind the counter, crafts square pies that are nothing short of legendary, and his house round pie—an equal showstopper.

While their pepperoni slice garners the most social media fame, I can't stress enough that any selection from their menu guarantees satisfaction. Yes, even if that means a 30-minute wait for a fresh-out-of-the-oven House Round Pie—it's a slice of heaven worth every minute.

The eatery itself is a cozy nook, not designed for the throngs it now attracts daily. My advice? Embrace the wait. The bustling atmosphere is part of the charm, and your patience is rewarded with some of the finest pizza this city has to offer.

Stopped here for lunch during a work trip. I had the blackened salmon tacos and the table had the cauliflower and crab dip. All were DELICIOUS. Great setup. Great location. My only complaint is water was slightly warmer than room temp lol. The windows all along the side give an immaculate view and let in the most beautiful sunshine.

Tucked away in the East Village, this small and cozy gem of a restaurant serves up absolutely heavenly udon. With a nice variety of appetizers to choose from, it's a great destination for both lunch and dinner, and particularly charming for a date spot. The beef udon, featuring a deliciously rich broth, is not to be missed. Although there's usually a wait, the line moves quickly, so don't be deterred. This place is truly worth the visit.

I recently visited Little Rascal for a weekend brunch and was thoroughly impressed by the experience. The ambiance is casual and inviting, setting the stage for a delightful meal. The menu offerings were truly exceptional, capturing the essence of a radical culinary adventure with authentic dishes that tantalize the taste buds. The service was outstanding, with a hospitable waiter/bartender who ensured our experience was nothing short of perfect. And for coffee aficionados, the Turkish coffee is a must-try – it was nothing less than stellar. Little Rascal comes highly recommended for anyone looking for a captivating brunch spot.

Title: A Brunch Haven That Won't Break the Bank

If you're scouring the area for the ultimate brunch spot, look no further. This gem offers an impressive menu at prices that feel like a steal. Ideal for a laid-back weekend feast, the dishes here are simply sublime. Eggs come perfectly baked, with the Italian sausage variety standing out, and for the cheese lovers, the creamy spinach is a dream.

For those dining in a pack, tackle the sweet menu and share the joy. The banana walnut pancakes deserve a special shout-out — absolutely divine. Just a heads up: the popularity of this place means there's a likely wait during weekends, so early birds get a seat faster. Inside can buzz with chatter and feel a bit tight, so seize the opportunity for outdoor seating if you can. This spot is a must-visit for brunch aficionados.

Pretty decent Irish pub. Family and I had a really long day sightseeing and just got off the miss Ellis Island ferry. We were haaaangry and stumbled upon this place. Thank goodness for Irish pubs.  Dark but pleasant atmosphere. Good variety menu and they even made my aunt a frozen margarita. I ordered a veggie burger which was sort of weird with small pieces of vegetarian "meat" but the brioche bun was warm and toasted, skinny fries were mealy and hot. Also ordered soft pretzels (baked) but the ends were hard (maybe overbaked). They were large bread sticks and they had cheese dip sauce. Ok I'll forgive the hard ends because I have had a hankering for cheese sauce and it was darn good. I don't care if it was even velveeta or whatever they used, that's exactly what I wanted. Service was very good and we were all happy, so this place is a win for us!

Title: A Night at the Speakeasy

The ambiance of the bar area immediately sets a striking tone with its alluring red lights, creating a vibrant yet overwhelmingly crowded space. Our work dinner transcended the ordinary when we discovered a hidden staircase leading to a former speakeasy, which served as our dining haven.

The culinary highlights of the evening included an impeccable calamari, a sumptuous cheesecake, and a tiramisu that was nothing short of perfection. Unfortunately, the salad was unremarkable. A misstep occurred with the steak; it's worth noting for future guests that preferring it well done might be the way to go, as my less-than-well-done order fell short of expectations.

All in all, the venue's history and select dishes left a lasting impression, making it a worthwhile experience for those who appreciate a touch of the past intertwined with their dining.

Title: A Delightful Evening at [Restaurant Name]

My teenager, who shares my love for dining out, and I enjoyed a wonderful Saturday dinner at [Restaurant Name], a place I had previously visited for their excellent oysters. Our experience was nothing short of delightful.

We began with a lobster salad, artfully split onto two plates with generous portions of lobster. The combination of avocado, beets, and mesclun greens dressed in champagne vinaigrette was a hit.

The bread selection was a carb-lover's dream, featuring a unique corn bread stick and an onion focaccia that was bursting with flavor.

My entree, the scallops paired with a sumptuous crab risotto, was a savory masterpiece, subtly echoing the essence of a lobster bisque with sherry. The inclusion of sugar snap peas added a satisfying crunch.

My child opted for the truffle cod served alongside mushroom ravioli. I snagged a taste and can confirm it was equally impressive.

We capped off our meal with a coconut panna cotta draped in tropical fruit and passion fruit sauce, delivering a vibrant endnote. Some complimentary cookies concluded our evening on a sweet note.

[Restaurant Name] once again proved itself as a top-notch dining destination. Each dish was a testament to their commitment to flavor and presentation. Highly recommend for a special night out.

Had a late dinner at Uncle Boons on Saturday night. And despite the long and aggravating wait, the highs of the meal, especially the Khao Soi Kaa Kai, made it worth it.Quality: By the time we sat down at Uncle Boons, it was late and we were starving. The first dish we ordered was the Laab Neuh Gah, a spicy chopped lamb salad. It is extremely spicy, but so many flavors shined through. It is ground lamb, which was not the most pleasing, but still a dish I would order again. Next out was the Mee Krob, sweetbreads with a crispy noodle salad. Everything about the dish was excellent. Even the texture of the sweetbreads, which I usually find off-putting was solid. The Pla Muuk, grilled baby octopus was the worst dish of the evening. They overdid it on the grill and the octopus tasted only of charcoal. I would be afraid the other charcoal grilled goodies are the same. Luckily, the Kaduuk, roasted bone marrow avoided it, minus the brioche. But the rich and decadent bite overcame the bread issue. Finally we had the Khao Soi Kaa Kai, northern style golden curry with egg noodles and chicken leg. It was by far the best dish of the night. The flavors of the curry, the tender meat, and the texture of the other ingredients were all spectacular. A perfect dish.Quantity: Even the small plates are large and filling. With our order we took an additional meal home with us.Value: $18 for the Laab Neuh Gah. $16 for the Mee Krob. $18 for the Pla Muuk. $18 for the Kaduuk. $25 for the Khao Soi Kaa Kai.Ambiance: Uncle Boons is located in Lower Manhattan. When you enter you must go down a few steps into a semi-basement space. They have a few tables near the entrance and a small bar at the far end of this room. As you move further in they have a separated dining area with additional tables along the wall and a few more tables in the very back. Wall to wall the place is covered in artwork and pictures and each lighting fixture hanging from the ceiling is different. In the background hip-hop music played, but it wasn't until I was in the bathroom that I realized it was Thai hip-hop.Crowd: Two hour wait on Saturday night. They do offer limited reservations and ignore the fact that they advertise most of the tables as available for walk-ins, a reservation is a must.Service: Once you sit down in the restaurant everything is fine. However, they skipped us on the wait list and had we not showed up curious of where we were, we may have never received a text to come back.Parking: Minimal street parking nearby.

Title: Authentic Delights at A Great Value

My recent visit to this restaurant, a spot I'd been eagerly tracking on Instagram, exceeded all expectations. The authenticity of the cuisine is a standout feature, and the value is exceptional – a lavish spread for three cost us just $60. The lamb shumai is a revelation, transforming even lamb skeptics with its soup dumpling-like succulence.

Another must-try is the large plate chicken, a dish that'll have you planning your next visit before you've even finished. Despite its popularity, I was seated immediately on a busy Friday at 8 pm, though the place filled up quickly. For a smooth experience, I recommend using their convenient online waitlist. Don't miss out on this culinary gem!

Delightful brasserie lunch in Tribeca.   Did a walk in because Resy is so annoying and said they had nothing available.   Take your chances.We did the prix fixe lunch that included either duck confit w/ verre du vin and chocolate mousse, or the lamb daube with semolina cake and leeks w/ gribiche.Fantastic duck confit and sublime melted leeks w/ that delicious French eggy mayo sauce (gribiche).  The lamb also was delicious with Moroccan spices, prunes and apricots.  Why not 5 stars?The potatoes were not cooked, still on the raw side.....and the wine that came with the duck prix fixe lunch was undrinkable....a strange Italian red poured out of a cask.   We did the a la carte menu for wine.....yikes.....We will definitely be back for dinner.  Service very kind and friendly.

Stopped by with a friend for brunch. We ordered the mac n cheese, hash brown, vegan pancake and the giving tree pressed juice. This is bar far  the best vegan mac n cheese I've ever had! Theres the sweet potato cashew cheese sauce with the shiitake mushroom bacon on top. The hash brown was surprisingly good with its tofu sour cream and smoke paprika. Loved the variety of food items here. I'll definitely be back to try their spin on other dishes.

My manager took me here to celebrate getting lots of work done after a heavy week (woohoo!). Oh my, did I get HOOKED on their happy hour!(FYI Hama Happy Hour is from 5pm-7pm).This location is about 2 blocks and half an avenue away from where I currently work in the Rockefeller Plaza. They have a vast happy hour menu that ranges from $5 sushi rolls to $7 Japanese-style cocktails. If you're looking for beer, wine, or sake, those drinks are $5. The decent prices keep me coming back; it's my new favorite place to bring coworkers! I think it happens to be one of my manager's favorite places too as I bumped into her as we were meeting different coworkers for happy hour :) The quality is consistently good, and the sweet, salty, and umami flavors you'd expect to be from Japanese cuisine are present. Don't expect 5-star sushi, but rather sushi to fill you up if you're hungry for a satisfying dinner. My favorite drink I've ordered so far was the Sakura - it's super yummy if you like sweet drinks, and it's very presentable. Some great sharing options if you're sharing with friends/family/coworkers are the following:-Edamame (5/5): A classic, can't go wrong-Shishito peppers (3.5/5): This was my first time trying them here. They could be better, but if you like mild-medium spicy, this is for you. Watch out as some can be really spicy, but most of the time they are mild-medium-Grilled Miso Salmon Rolls (5/5): A twist on salmon tempura rolls, this pick was very tastyCurrently writing this as the COVID-19 situation shut down most of NYC. Will definitely be back once offices open up again. Until then, I will be dreaming about well-deserved happy hours after a long work day/week...

Title: A Vegan Sushi Revelation

As a skeptic of vegan sushi, I was pleasantly surprised by the culinary adventure this restaurant offers. Their dishes prove to be deliciously crafted, emphasizing the natural flavors of fresh, clean ingredients. Rather than relying on mock fish, this restaurant excels in highlighting the ‘awesome’ in every vegetable and seasoning, all while remaining affordable.

With an expanded menu featuring more than just sushi, diners can now enjoy hearty entrees that are both satisfying and health-conscious. Although their gunkan sushi has been retired from the offerings, much to my slight disappointment, the spicy mang roll remains my steadfast favorite, perfectly paired with a mushroom noodle salad or a summer roll. Their soups are yet another testament to their flavorful fare.

Not only is the food note-worthy, but the restaurant's atmosphere is equally commendable – bright and inviting. Accompanied by the warm hospitality of the staff, it's a welcoming dining experience, enhanced by the convenience of their delivery service.

In short, this vegan sushi spot is an unmissable gem for both taste and value.

Visited this gem where the appeal of unlimited toppings on a perfectly crispy thin crust won me over instantly – all for a reasonable $13! The pizza was baked to perfection, delivering an explosion of flavors that had me saying "So yum!!" While I would have preferred my salad to be freshly made rather than pulled from a fridge, I was impressed by the restaurant's dedication to eco-friendliness. Coupled with excellent service, this place exudes charm. It's a definite must-return for me!

I recently visited this local pizzeria with my mom and was pleasantly surprised by the quality of their pizza. The ingredients used were noticeably fresh and contributed to the overall delicious taste. The option to add feta to my pizza was a welcome touch that enhanced my dining experience. The wood-fired cooking method added a delightful smokiness to the crust that I thoroughly enjoyed. While it may not top my list of pizza places, its commitment to freshness makes it a spot I'd happily return to when in the area.

Trendy hipster place with overpriced food and drinks.  Nonetheless, they get four stars because everything was delicious! The service was attentive but also felt a bit annoying as they were too quick to want to clean up plates before we were done.  That's typical in most of the US.  They need to be in tuned when a party is trying to spend a relaxed dining experience.  Having said that, I still absolutely recommend this place especially for date night.

I recently ordered a margarita pizza pie from a local spot in the Financial District, and I was thoroughly impressed. The pizza was notably large, with ample, generous toppings that didn't skimp on flavor—truly embodying the essence of a great-tasting New York pizza. Additionally, the delivery service in the FiDi area was top-notch, making it a great option for those craving a delicious pizza without the hassle of going out. Highly recommended for anyone in the mood for authentic NY pizza!

What a fun atmosphere!  Now we expected some characters but assumed the food would be just mediocre, well were we wrong!  The food was sooo tasty and presented in a cool Tim Burtonesque style.  We tried so many of the drinks between all four of us that I hope I get the names right.  The first drink we started with was the Sparks's Minty Margarita and The Beetle's Juice, both very good.  The beetle's juice was a bit sweeter than the margarita.  Second round I had the coco skellington and my husband had the Glen or Glenda again went down quick.  I think our friends had the Barnabis Collins and one of the martinis but by this time we were all feeling good so no one's certain.  We started our pre fixed 40 dollar meals with the baby beetle juice salad, Jacks Jambalaya Risotto and the Oogie boogies braised bacon.  The were all delicate but the stand out was the bacon, highly recommend.  Our mains were the Sweeney beef, Edward burger hands and the Blooms big fish.  All the dishes were excellent.  I would have liked my salmon a little less overdone but the potatoes and pickled corn salsa made it a winner dish.  The actor who played Beetle Juice throughout our dinner was hysterical and was FULL of energy.  So much like the actual character with his mannerisms and jokes, we loved it!  Lydia was great too!  We ended with a birthday sorbet and were on our way to see the new Beetle Juice Broadway show!  So great!  We'll be back to visit again soon!

Pa Pa Thai is amazing!! Quaint little place, not fancy at all with just a few tables. The service and the food is fantastic so what else do you need!? I got the spicy noodles and boy were they SPICY. I love spicy, i couldn't stop eating! The server had to refill my water glass probably 15 times, but she did it with a smile every time lol. Highly recommend PaPa Thai for a low key night out!

I stumbled upon this place whilst looking for a decent bar for after work drinks. Their food was to my surprise so good that I made a dinner reservation to come back for a full meal. The ambience is lively and the key menu items that are solid include: the African chicken, dumplings, fried rice, and charred octopus.

During our recent trip to NYC, my husband, a stickler for a solid breakfast, reluctantly tried The Ritz after a less satisfying experience elsewhere. He couldn't stop raving about it, prompting me to visit too. Nestled just a short walk from our hotel, The Ritz is a quintessential diner that strikes all the right chords. 

Perched by the window, I was immersed in the city's vibrant energy while enjoying impeccable service. The culinary team was a joy to watch, masters at work. My breakfast plate was a home run: flawlessly cooked eggs, succulent sausages, and freshly-made home fries, all for a mere $9.60 pre-tip. For a taste of NYC that won't disappoint or break the bank, The Ritz is a definite winner.

I am a digger for good Mediterranean food in general, especially Lebanese food. This one honestly has my mind blown. I ordered the Beef Kafta Burger via MealPal and it was AMAZING! In each bite, I could taste every element of the dish. The onions, the rich hummus, tender beef, the garlic and fries on the side - all came together beautifully. Loved their space and service too. Super delighted and will return for sure. - Christine@sugarcoatedmasala

Title: Perfect Spot for Penn State Games

I've visited this gem twice to catch Penn State games, and it's quickly become my go-to spot. What I appreciate most is the refreshingly low-key vibe, which is a rare find during big game nights. No elbowing your way through a crowd here; there's a comfortable space to enjoy the game and still soak in the collective enthusiasm.

The staff deserves a shoutout for their friendly and attentive service, making sure that our experience was nothing short of fantastic. The drinks won't break the bank, and they don't skimp on the pour either—a win-win in my book.

Food-wise, I've sampled only a handful of dishes, but the baked mac and cheese is a standout. Served in an adorable cast iron skillet, it's the kind of comfort food that perfectly complements the game-day atmosphere. And those crazy appetizers on the menu have already caught my eye for a future visit.

In short, if you're looking for an enjoyable place to watch the game without the usual sports bar frenzy, this spot is a touchdown.

After a recent streak of underwhelming dumplings elsewhere, I find myself compelled to amend my rating for Vanessa's. The dumplings here stand out for their consistent quality and flavorful profiles. The chicken and basil, alongside the pork and chive, are personal highlights. This establishment certainly earns an extra star for maintaining high standards and delivering tastiness in every bite.

Title: A Hidden Gem of Authentic Szechuan at Dekalb Market

I've strolled by this spot at Dekalb Market on numerous occasions, never giving it a second glance, skeptical of its authenticity. Consider me corrected - dining here today was an eye-opener. The dry pot pork and pepper fish we ordered were nothing short of phenomenal, each bite bursting with genuine Szechuan flavor. The beef tripe in chili oil was a bold, cold appetizer that complemented the meal excellently.

The experience was akin to the cherished flavors of Spicy & Tasty in Flushing, which speaks volumes about its authenticity and quality. To top off the experience, there's a full bar available, making it not just a meal, but an event. This place has earned a rightful spot on my go-to list for true Chinese cuisine.

Excellent fried chicken and sides all day and all night! We loved the bucket of chicken. So crispy while still juicy. Brussels sprouts were great. The octopus with the citrusy cream sauce wowed up. The octopus was done well with a nice crunch to it.

Unfortunately, my latest visit to the once beloved dumpling spot proved disappointing. The dumplings, a former favorite, have transformed into thick, greasy, and unpleasantly doughy morsels that pale in comparison to their past iterations. This drastic change in quality has me doubting a return visit. Additionally, the restaurant itself is in dire need of an update; its worn and unclean ambiance detracts significantly from the dining experience. On a positive note, the prices remain affordable, but the cost savings hardly compensate for the decline in both the food and the atmosphere.

Average drinks mixed by a pretentious bartender, served by a great staff.I've been passing by this place for a couple months, and decided to pop in after every other bar in the area was full. The host was an adorable young man that gave me a seat at the end of the bar but reassure me that the couple next to me was leaving soon.When the ordered another round, he was very sweet and let me sit at a table. I grabbed a table and ordered the Capri. I asked the waitress if I could have it with gin instead of vodka. She hesitated and said she would ask. Kind of a yellow flag, because it's such an easy swap out.The bartender looks down from her high perch (Literally, the bar is higher than the seats, which is pretty nifty tbh) and gives the waitress a stern look. They discuss for a while and the poor waitress is literally pleading with the bartender to make this swap. The bartender gives her a huff and shrugs.The waitress comes back and says the bartender will do the swap but she's not sure it will taste good. Of course it will taste good. It's fucking gin, aperol, lime and passionfruit like ????  Don't be an asshole.The Capri with gin was good of course -- but 75% ice. Come on it's 2019 aren't we over the ice scam?Probably won't be back. I can understand all of the complaints of mediocrity.

At first glance TabeTomo is charming. The all wood aesthetics has the mind drifting to images of a Japan of old. A view of an open table sure looks alluring to hungry travelers, unwilling to endure the unjustified wait of the nearby Momofuku Ramen Bar. But just like the literal and verbal mouthful, Tonkotsu Chashu Tsukemen Ramen, that I ordered, the gleaming first impressions did not hold up. An AC unit running full blast on a fall evening, and a table so wobbly, that it was rendered unusable are all forgettable inconveniences, but a ramen joint serving just mediocre ramen is unfortunate. Like everything else, the first sip of the Tonkotsu Chashu Tsukemen Ramen has you smiling. The pork broth is rich and fully flavored. The pork is tender and nearly melts on the tongue. The ramen is thick, springy, and absorbs the soup flavors. Unfortunately, the elation doesn't hold up half way through. You begin by wondering about the out of place lump of wilted spinach at the corner of the bowl. Then you wonder if all that bean sprout do anything for the taste of the soup. Finally, once the toppings and ramen begin to disappear, you'll wonder what all those bits are that are teaming in your bowl. It's garlic, and lots of it. I'd estimate a number of cloves best counted by the dozens made their way into my bowl. What tasted so good at first, unfortunately turns overbearing.

Tucked away in a cozy corner of town, this restaurant is a real gem for those seeking authentic Chinese cuisine. The highlight undoubtedly has to be the delectable dumplings – each bite is an ode to traditional flavors and culinary craftsmanship. However, it's worth noting that while their pan-fried noodles boast a robust flavor profile, they are somewhat marred by an excess of oil. If they dialed back on the grease, these noodles could easily match the high standard set by their other dishes. Despite this slight hiccup, the restaurant's offerings are a flavor-packed journey worth taking for any Chinese food enthusiast.

Title: A Decent Spot for Cuban Cuisine

I recently visited this Cuban eatery and found it to be a satisfactory option for a casual lunch. The Cuban sandwich I ordered was passable, though not the best I've had in the area. However, the accompanying soup was a delightful addition, especially appreciated during the chilly season.
