One of the restaurant's strengths is its ample seating, even during busy hours, so you can expect to find a spot without much wait. Additionally, the service was attentive, with a server readily available to take orders.

While the food quality and taste are just fine, there are superior Cuban restaurants nearby that tend to be more crowded. This makes this place a solid choice for those seeking a less hectic dining experience. Overall, it's a good spot to enjoy a Cuban meal when you're looking to avoid the crowds.

Tucked within a stone's throw of Times Square, Manting may initially surprise with its pricing, especially for those accustomed to budget-friendly Chinese takeout spots. Yet, this isn't just another generic joint. Manting delivers a robust culinary experience, one that justifies each dollar spent.

The portions served are generous, satisfying even the heartiest of appetites, and the varied menu ensures a dish to suit every palate. For those yearning for authenticity that transcends the usual suspects, Manting's General Tso's chicken packs a punch with its genuine spiciness.

Having sampled an array of their offerings, I can vouch for the consistency in quality and taste—Manting doesn't miss a beat. Do remember to hit the ATM before your visit as it's cash only. Whether you choose to soak in the modest ambiance on site or grab a meal on the go, Manting is a solid pick for delightful Chinese fare.

I recently dined at a local steakhouse that offered a fun, yet pleasantly quiet atmosphere, setting itself apart from the typical noisy NYC steak scene. The highlight of my meal was the grilled bacon, which was nothing short of awesome. The grilled wedge salad caught my attention with its unique taste and stunning presentation — a delightful twist to a classic dish.

Though I'm not typically swayed by filet mignon, I couldn't help but admire the tempting presentation of their filet — it's definitely on my list for the next visit. I opted for the Strip steak instead, which was cooked to perfection in terms of temperature, although it was slightly tougher than I expected. The bone-in ribeye our table shared, on the other hand, was delectably tasty and cooked to perfection.

The side of au gratin potatoes was a stand-out, boasting a unique flavor profile and a comforting texture, thanks to a slow 6-hour roast. All in all, this steakhouse is doing a lot right, especially if you're in the mood for some grilled goodness without the usual cacophony of the city.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at Lunch

I stopped by this restaurant on a whim for lunch and was pleasantly surprised by the affordability of their lunch specials. I opted for the chicken with garlic sauce, which was served with a side of hot and sour soup and spicy cold noodles. Although the soup didn't quite hit the mark for me, the noodles were deliciously spicy, and I appreciated the generous portion of veggies in the chicken dish.

The shumai also caught my attention with their impressive presentation and size, not to mention the delightful taste that had me savoring each bite. 

What truly elevated the experience from average to memorable was the staff's handling of a customer issue while I was there. A woman had an online ordering mishap, and the staff were incredibly accommodating, showing genuine concern and patience to resolve the situation. Witnessing such a positive customer service interaction certainly left a good taste in my mouth.

Overall, my visit was leaning towards a solid 3.5, but the commendable service tipped the scales. I'd recommend this place not just for the food, but for the refreshing customer experience as well.

I'm not vegan, but I've been ordering from here on occasion recently and I've been pretty impressed. The place itself is really cute - fast casual but has plenty of seating, bright, decorated well, very clean. The menu is big and there are a lot of choices both healthy and not-so-healthy. Portion sizes are good - not huge, but most items are in the $10-$12 range so it's definitely not going to break the bank. They do a good job with pickup orders through Seamless; packaged well, on time, nothing forgotten.The bulgogi bowl, with cauliflower mash, pickled veggies, and Brussels sprouts, is fantastic. The fake meat, whatever it is, is really convincing and has a great flavor. The taco salad, with corn, chorizo, avocado, etc is a little bit more filling in my opinion and is always dressed perfectly, although the "chorizo" is not going to fool any meat eaters. I've heard great things about the Nashville hot chicken sandwich as well. The baked goods are great - really like the oatmeal raisin cookie. The food isn't phenomenal, but when you take everything into account this place is a real tour de force in the vegan space. Comparable to byChloe but I actually like it better. Not as good as jajaja but cheaper. Great experience overall. Will return.

The red cooked beef broth is great and the meat is tender and flavorful. The wide noodles were the right amount of chewiness. The only complaint I have is that they don't have any pickled mustard green as a side or condiment. I also ordered a side of tendon to try but it was way chewier/crunchy than I am used to. The spice level was also on point.

I was really excited to try the new Au Cheval in NYC since I've wanted to try Chicago's location for a few years now. I jumped at the chance to snag a reservation.I got the single cheeseburger with egg, and also got chicken wings as an appetizer. It was decent burger but I didn't feel like it quite lived up to the hype. If I'm going to shell out this much $$ for a burger, I'll be getting that burger fix at Minetta Tavern.Overall decent taste, great service, and cool interior design.

I recently dined at a pleasant eatery nestled in the Hudson Yard Mall, just a stone's throw from The Vessel and the Javits Center. The restaurant boasts a chic, modern decor that's on the darker side, but the tables are well-lit, striking a cozy ambiance.

The menu includes both a selection of raw bar items and hearty entrees. For my late lunch, I started with a delightful shrimp tempura roll, followed by a steak salad. While the steak was perfectly cooked to my liking, the salad was slightly marred by an overly generous application of dressing.

I also sampled "The Vessel," a cocktail that's a must-try for gin aficionados. Service-wise, the staff was on point – attentive and quick to rectify an initially mistaken order with efficiency and grace.

Overall, the restaurant delivers a solid dining experience, worthy of a visit when you're in the area.

Title: A Sizable Celebration with a Few Hiccups

I recently attended a post-wedding dinner with a party of about 20 at this establishment, and while the experience was generally positive, there were aspects that could have been refined. The service stumbled slightly as appetizers and entrees were served concurrently, leading to a congested table and a somewhat rushed dining experience. Despite the service hiccup, the food itself was commendable.

The chicken quesadilla was tasty, hitting the mark with a balanced cheese-to-chicken ratio and complemented by a notably fresh picadillo. As for the black angus skirt steak fajitas, they were a standout with succulent, thick, fat-free meat slices. However, I found the accompanying tortillas overly large - a smaller size akin to what's typically served at Mexican eateries would make for more effortless consumption. Although I didn't fully savor the red snapper myself, my dining companion was quite pleased with it.

It's plausible that the simultaneous arrival of starters and mains was due to our large group size or a specific request, which I am willing to overlook. The food quality shines through enough to warrant a recommendation for this restaurant.

My family and I were just walking around looking for a restaurant to grab dinner at on a Friday night around 7 PM and we randomly decided to stop into this restaurant. But I'm so glad we did because it turned out to be a great decision. When we arrived, I saw that there are two parts of the restaurant. As soon as you walk through the door you arrive in the bar and are then taken past that and brought to the dining area on the other side. As soon as I walked in, I was impressed by the decor. It was clean, modern but also true to its culture. The setting of each table was also lovely. Service was very professional. Everything was very efficient and well thought out. My only complaint is that the servers all did not have any sort of smiles of their faces which was a bit weird to see in a restaurant. They were polite just not very friendly. After we sat down they brought over some water and complimentary starters and chutney. Flavors were great and really opened my appetite for the rest of the meal. Afterwards for an appetizer we ordered the ratlami proha kabab  which was a croquette and was really delicious, a bit dry and heavy in terms of flavor but was a great order. As for the main course, we got the goa shrimp curry (nice flavor with large, jumbo shrimp) and chicken tikka masala (good flavor). Both dishes were surprisingly filling and really good portions. The complimentary side of rice was also very delicious and just worked so well with the curries. We also ordered the regular naan to go along with our meal which was very fragrant and so yummy. Finally for dessert we got the gulab jamun creme brûlée. Surprisingly this was the most disappointing dish from our meal. The creme brûlée's flavor was great; however the dough ball soaked in syrup was not very good and just felt like it pulled down the flavor of the rest of the dessert. Also the chocolate drizzle had a strange aftertaste as well and was just not needed.All in all, even though there was a couple of hiccups during the dinner it was truly a great experience with generally great dishes. I will definitely try to make my way over the next time I am craving Indian food!

A generous 4 starsWhen you have so many reviews and your rating is dismal, you are doing something wrong, maybe many somethings wrong.  For our early dinner visit yesterday, the food was very good, the service not so much.My granddaughter and I watched a Columbus Day parade along 5th Ave, across the street from Friday's.  It was a long parade, my granddaughter loved it, and when it was over we headed across the street.  There did not seem to be a rush to Friday's, but they may have had a spike in business, so I'll cut them some slack.It took too long for our server to arrive, but she did, and we placed our order.  I had their Signature Whiskey-Glazed Burger.  My granddaughter's food arrived first, and the food runner seemed surprised I expected food too.  Our server explained they try to get kid's food out quickly, kids being less patient and all.  I agree, but her food took about 12 minutes - not very fast.  Mine arrived several minutes later.After a confusing interaction with that food runner, it was time for me to eat.  The burger was very good.  The glaze comes in a separate container and it is difficult to keep the slippery burger together, but I managed the best I could.  Paying was another opportunity for service to suffer, but after too long of a wait we got that done and headed out to explore more of NYC.

Wow this place is so cute!! I went in on a Tuesday (Christmas Eve) early afternoon and they had many tables opened -- we got there just in time though because people were lining up to get seated just after we did. The hostesses were welcoming, and our server greeted us immediately. Our server was a young man with a cute accent who was very accommodating. He first took our drink orders (grapefruit juice and peach iced tea) then took our food orders (shrimp pasta, big breakfast, crab linguine, and truffle fries). The food came out after a good amount of time and they were all very delicious. I would definitely recommend sharing a bowl of truffle fries amongst your group because they are amazingggg! I got the shrimp pasta myself and enjoyed it very much, and my friends also enjoyed theirs as well. Although a very small restaurant, the interior is very cute and all their staff are very accommodating and friendly which I appreciated greatly. Especially since it was Christmas Eve, it was a nice addition to my day :) I would definitely come back and try their other locations as well. 10/10 would recommend!

Title: Lackluster Bottomless Brunch Experience at [Restaurant Name]

My visit to [Restaurant Name] for their $49 bottomless brunch was a mixed bag. While the concept of unlimited tapas and drinks is enticing, the execution fell short. The tapas reminded me of average buffet fare, lacking the freshness I hoped for. We tried several items - the Angry Zengo roll started us off on the wrong foot with a dirty plate and was just passable in taste. The Asian pear salad missed the mark entirely, leading to its untimely return to the kitchen. Peking duck and scrambled egg steamed buns were overwhelmed by sauce, masking all other flavors, and the buns themselves seemed stale.

There were a couple of positives: crispy potatoes that lived up to their name and the Mexican chocolate waffles that my husband found delightful. The drinks provided a pleasant respite from the otherwise mediocre meal. However, these few highlights couldn't salvage the overall experience. If you're seeking a noteworthy brunch, I suggest looking elsewhere as [Restaurant Name] didn't quite satisfy our tastes.

I recently had the pleasure to enjoy a meal from Beyond Burger, which included sampling three different sushi rolls. I found the unique packaging of the sauce particularly delightful as it was separate from the sushi, allowing me to "inject" the sauce directly onto the sushi, adding a fun twist to the dining experience.

This was my second visit to this location and my first time ordering through Grubhub for takeout. The whole process was seamless, and the food quality was just as impressive as dining in. The experience certainly lived up to my expectations, leaving me eager to return and explore more flavors on their menu. Highly recommend for any sushi aficionado looking for something new!

Title: A Hidden Gem for Hearty Eats

My latest culinary adventure brought me to a humble spot that's a true steal for the wallet-savvy foodie. At a mere $5 for a small portion or $7 for a large, this eatery doesn't skimp on their servings. Each container brims with a generous heap of meat, rice, and cabbage, smothered in a sauce that transforms the dish into a mouthwatering delight.

The menu offers a trio of meats – duck, pork, and chicken. While none reached peak tenderness, with some pieces being on the drier side, the sauce generously ladled on top compensated beautifully. Among the meats, the chicken was notably the most tender, but it was the bbq pork that truly won my palate.

Speaking of the sauce, it deserves a shout-out. It's what pulls the entire meal together, creating a symphony of flavors that seeps into the rice and meat, ensuring each bite is as satisfying as the last.

Bear in mind that this spot is no-frills – there's no seating and it's cash only. Despite often facing a queue, the line moves quickly, a testament to the efficiency of the place. If you're after a tasty, filling meal that won't hurt your budget, this is the spot to hit.

Title: A Culinary Home Run at Nick + Stef's Steakhouse

I recently enjoyed an exceptional dining experience at Nick + Stef's Steakhouse, located conveniently near Madison Square Garden. Opting for a Saturday night visit during a Rangers game proved to be a strategic choice, as the restaurant was delightfully uncrowded, and the service was both attentive and personalized.

Our server, Greg, was particularly helpful, providing knowledgeable insights into the menu and sharing his personal recommendations. Among the standouts were the swordfish special, seasoned with robust Cajun spices, and the petite filet, both exquisitely prepared and thoughtfully portioned for sharing. The sides did not disappoint either, with the charred brussel sprouts adorned with thick bacon slices stealing the spotlight.

Dessert was a crowning touch, with the fresh, in-house-made NY cheesecake leaving a lasting impression with its perfect balance of creaminess and a cherry compote that offered a just-right tart counterpoint. The generously sized servings may appear deceptive at first glance, but rest assured, they are more than sufficient to satisfy your hunger.

The wine and cocktail list was impressive, and my glass of Malbec was an excellent accompaniment to the meal.

A word to the wise: Due to nearby construction, first-timers might find the restaurant a bit challenging to locate, but a quick call to the helpful staff at Nick + Stef's will set you on the right path.

For anyone in the area for a show, concert, or sporting event, Nick + Stef's Steakhouse is an absolute must-visit for an unforgettable meal.

Toloache, Toloache, Toloache! Now you say it 3 times fast. Came here for my birthday and had a fabulous time my friends. I sat at the bar for a Prickly Pear margarita while I waited for my friends. The bartender and bar crowd we're all super friendly. It just happened to be Mexican Independence Day and the bartender gave us a little history lessen.We sat in the middle of the restaurant which was a little busy and right next to the kitchen, but luckily no one bumped into us. Great decor and the food really speaks for itself. I had the one of the platos fuertes...The JM Carne Asada (Grilled skirt steak, potato gratin, guacamole, Mole-cheese enchilada). I switched my sauce to a green sauce which was also excellent, and I liked the idea of potatoes instead of rice.We did not save room for dessert. Their popcorn flan looked amazing. Unfortunately, I could not have it because it's not gluten free, however, they do have many gluten free options  @ Toloache. Excited to go back. Not cheap but definitely good, quality food.

Title: A Homey Haven with Hearty Helpings

Upon entering the quaint eatery, we were instantly wrapped in a charming and cozy atmosphere, a perfect setting for a leisurely Sunday breakfast. Greeted by super friendly staff, their warmth was as palpable as the aroma of coffee that promised a delightful start. As first-timers, we found the counter-ordering system novel, but the staff was exceptionally patient, guiding us through their process with a smile.

The food, oh the food! Fresh, homemade, and served in generous portions that justify the slightly higher prices. My smoked salmon toast was an artfully crafted dish with dual layers of delectable smoked salmon on robust bread, complemented by a zesty cream cheese, dill, and scallions. The side of crispy, spiced home fries was a perfect accompaniment. My daughter’s pancakes were fluffy and ample, adorned with a unique berry butter and the classic touch of maple syrup.

The free coffee refills were a bonus, especially given the brew's high quality that kept us sipping happily. By the time we finished our meal, a line had formed, a testament to the place's popularity.

The colorful and eccentric staff added to the experience, ensuring we were content and feeling at home from the moment we walked in. It's not just a meal at this restaurant; it's a heartwarming experience. We'll certainly be back soon!

Spot Dessert has been my go-to sweet haven multiple times, standing out with favorites like The Harvest—a delightful mix of chocolate crumbles, layered cake, and raspberry sorbet—and the indulgent Golden Toast, oozing with honey butter atop thick toast paired with whipped cream, condensed milk ice cream, and strawberries. Simply irresistible.

The menu has pleasantly expanded beyond their dessert tapas and macarons to embrace an array of drinks and cookies. The Matcha Lava cookie, while earnest in its matcha bitterness, tips the scales too far on sweetness for my taste, lacking a harmonious flavor balance. The Oreo Chocolate Chip cookie is generously studded with Oreos and chocolate chips, though it might benefit from a bit more dough to mitigate the intense sweetness. However, the Caramel Miso cookie was an absolute hit with its perfect blend of flavors, despite its mildly messy caramel.

Pricing has seen an uptick over the years, with dessert tapas now at $11.95 each. Although there's a bundled discount for multiple tapas, it's odd that it can't be combined with other promotions. It's essentially the same as the discount I would've gotten with my 10% off coupon.

A gentle reminder for dessert enthusiasts—don’t overlook the stamp card like I did; it's a bummer to miss out on those sweet rewards!

St Tropez is a cute little place in the Village that serves French inspired food and has an extensive wine list. It's tiny - maybe 8/10 bar seats and 8/10 tables. You will get to know your fellow man/woman because everything is smushed together. So make a reservation especially on weekends. I ended up at the bar and will say their stools are super uncomfortable. I started with a rose - they had three choices by the glass and I appreciated being told that my first choice was a sweet rose so I could pick something else instead. Glasses range in the $12-18 range so about average for the location. Food wise I decided to nibble and had a cheese/charcuterie board. 3 options was $19 and it was a good amount on the board - definitely nice to share with a few people. I especially liked the pate which was fresh and garlicky. Service was efficient but not especially warm or welcoming. This would be a great date night spot.

Title: A Mediocre Experience at The Meatball Shop

I recently visited The Meatball Shop to see if it lived up to its hype, especially since I consider myself something of a meatball connoisseur. The ambiance was what you'd expect from a city eatery—cramped but quaint. I opted for the spicy pork meatballs with rigatoni and butternut squash in a creamy Parmesan sauce, which cost $22. Frankly, it wasn't worth the price. The dish was disappointing, with a scant serving of aldente pasta and meatballs that barely registered on the heat scale, their spiciness seemingly reliant on the presence of bell peppers.

My partner's choice, the classic meatballs with spaghetti, was marginally better, boasting more flavor and a pleasing texture. However, neither dish stood out in the crowded Lower East Side culinary scene. In summary, The Meatball Shop didn't meet my expectations, leading me to lament spending both my money and appetite there.

The competition is steep for upscale Mexican in NYC, and Bodega Negra offers some unique touches to enter in this race The food is good here, it's just not spectacular. You rarely cant go wrong with tacos/enchiladas/fajitas, but you can with the price you pay for them. To start- the tuna ceviche was excellent. In terms of tacos, I tried the fried fish and steak. Both were pretty good, but nothing amazing.The chicken and chorizo fajitas were presented on a spit over a bed of queso and seared vegetables. The display was impressive, and although the chicken wasn't as tasty, the vegetables and queso were delicious. Overall, the price was pretty expensive for trendy Mexican food. The drinks were also not terribly impressive. So overall, enjoyed the food, but this would probably not be the first place I'd be running back if I have a taco craving.

- Quick, convenient, cooked in front of you- Stopped by after an evening performance nearby- Super convenient spot near the theater district- Got the classic beef- You order at the front, get a number, and they bring the food to you when they're ready- I've tried this chain in China and Hong Kong and I guess there are still some differences- The meat was ok- Try their house sauces- The concept of this place is the meat is raw and comes on an electromagnetic cooker. You mix the ingredients yourself and determine how you want your meat to be cooked- Plenty of seating available

Is this the best Pizza in NYC? Probably not - but that being said any pizza in NYC is going to be better than most you'll find elsewhere. Mike's is a local by-the-slice place close to the Marcel Hotel (where I was staying during this visit) - I needed a couple of slices because, well, you can't go to NYC without getting at least one slice. They had a deluxe and a regular cheese - I like to try them unadulterated - I think that's the true test. Both were delicious and had a nice amount of mailardization to the ingredients with a bit of sweetness and a super crisp crust - these guys know what they're doing for sure.Service was fast and good - the place usually has a line. It could probably use a good cleaning, but as pizza goes this is top-notch. The people behind the counter were a bit short on words but otherwise friendly - both times I ate the slices at tables inside.

Title: Hidden Gem in the Heart of the Big Apple

On our initial evening in New York City, fate led us to a charming family-owned gem that immediately captivated us with its warmth and authenticity. Opting for the daily specials, I commenced my culinary journey with a divine burrata, tomato, and basil salad. The burrata's creaminess coupled with the sweet balsamic drizzle was a dance of flavors I'll remember fondly.

The star of the evening was the house-crafted pappardelle pasta, lavished with a velvety mushroom sauce and crowned with succulent jumbo shrimps – a dish that truly exemplified the kitchen's prowess.

My companions explored other corners of the menu – from clam linguini to the house lasagna and a classic pizza – all of which met our table's collective approval. We capped the meal with a duo of desserts, the standout being a sumptuous chocolate soufflé. Though it strayed from traditional lightness, its warm, rich density made each spoonful a celebration of chocolate.

The second treat, an ice cream cloaked in a chocolate shell with a surprise maraschino cherry core, brought a smile to my husband's face. In summary, this delightful eatery not only satisfied our appetites but also provided a memorable start to our NYC adventure.

Came here for a conference work lunch so had low expectations but I really enjoyed the meal here!  Service was friendly and efficient.  There were at least 40 people at my table and the staff handled us like champs.Bread basket was excellent.  The octopus salad was the stuff dreams are made of!  It was so well done....I've never had anything like it.  Wow..just wow!For my entree, I had the linguine nera.  It was so light and the seafood tasted very fresh.  The sauce was delicious.  I loved it.Unfortunately I had to run back to the conference prior to getting to sample the cannoli and the tiramisu but it looked great.Would love to come back here for a regular meal.

Food 3.5/5 Service 5/5Overwhelming nice staffs and waiter. This place is fairly new so they're still training people but wow the service was really amazing. We split  a pasta for appetizer and shared two main dishes. We ordered spaghetti ala vongole to start and it was delicious! They split the pasta for us and served on two plates. All of their pastas are freshly made by the chef. Then we had the branzino and their special lamb shank. The branzino was quite a show because they flamed it and broke the salt next to our table. Once it got to the plate, it was only lukewarm so I think this could improve. The seasoning was not enough and it tasted a little bland. The lamb shank was really good and it was covered in some kind of tomato based sauce. The chef said it was slow cooked for 4-5 hours. The ambiance is very quiet and nice. It should be a perfect place for a date. It was kinda empty at prime time on a Thursday night.

Not the best sushi I've had in the city, but it gets the job done.  The restaurant is located below street level and would be easy to miss in the dark if it weren't for the bright neon sign, which is the only thing that detracts from the feel of this place.  Once inside, it feels quaint, cozy, and a little like you've been transported to small town Japan.To start, we ordered a bottle of Forgotten Japanese Spirit junmai off their substantial sake menu.  Delicious.For food, we got the Early Bird Dinner Special w/Salmon Oyako Don (a bento box meal with your choice of main dish available only before 6pm, $31) and the Sushi Regular (8-pieces of sushi & your choice of roll, $30).  Note that if you choose the futomaki roll for the Sushi Regular, you only get half a roll, which is still a lot of food.  Both items were a feast for the eyes; beautiful colors and variety of food.  Everything tasted good, if just a bit underwhelming.  The taste of the fish did not pop and the knife work was subpar as evidenced by uneven slices of fish.  Nothing was bad, but just a little unimpressive.

Title: A Hearty Brunch with Mixed Impressions

I visited this restaurant for a Saturday brunch with friends, greeted by friendly staff and an inviting ambiance. The place boasted space and comfort, setting the stage for what I hoped to be a delightful meal.

Ordering a much-anticipated mac & cheese burger, priced at $20 with a $7 bacon and truffle oil add-on, expectations were high. The presentation did not disappoint, the burger's size was striking upon arrival. Yet, the appearance was the peak of the experience.

The burger presented a challenge to traditional consumption; its enormity required deconstruction with utensils, detracting from the "burger" experience. While cheesy, with a notable fried mac and cheese patty that my friend enjoyed, the burger's flavor lacked complexity, yearning for a spicy or tangy element to cut through the one-dimensional cheese profile.

Despite the service hiccup regarding a separate check and asynchronous meal delivery, the staff was efficient. The included truffle fries were a pleasant side, though the truffle essence didn't translate to the burger itself.

In sum, while the concept of a mac & cheese burger intrigues, this version could benefit from a balance of flavors and a more manageable size. While it's potentially shareable or suitable for leftovers, those seeking a nuanced and juicy burger might find this one falls short.

Title: Mind-Blowing Sushi Burritos!

Body: From the very first bite, it's clear that this restaurant serves up a sushi burrito that is nothing short of divine. Pairing freshness with flavor, their bowls are delightful, but the burrito is an absolute game-changer, bursting with a cornucopia of customizable toppings that ensure each visit can be a new experience. The eel sauce, rich and umami-packed, is a standout, providing the perfect complement to the meal. And for a revitalizing finish, don't miss out on their juice drinks—they're a blast of refreshment on any warm day. A trip here is a must for any sushi aficionado seeking a twist on the traditional.

The food here was very enjoyable. I love the dips here. They were all fresh and light.I liked the octopus but didn't love it paired with the artichoke hearts and mashed potato concoction.The gyro sliders were the preferred dish between my mom and I. The side of feta truffle fries was good but the fries were not fresh.

I recently dined at a charming establishment steeped in history, originally a speakeasy during the Prohibition era. The facade is unassuming, but the interior is beautifully appointed with an aviation theme and rustic picnic tables, creating a delightful contrast.

Starting with appetizers, the goat cheese ravioli, bursting with flavor, was a highlight, while the Caesar salad didn't leave as strong an impression. The main courses were a mix; the Berkshire pork loin was satisfying, yet the coq au vin suffered from dryness. The side of truffle Mac and cheese was delicious, though the cost seemed steep at an additional $14.

We indulged in all three dessert options; the Panna cotta's lightness and the rich classic cheesecake were enjoyable, but the chocolate tart's dryness detracted from its flavor.

While the Restaurant Week experience was enjoyable and provided value, I'm hesitant about a return visit at full prices, given that the food was enjoyable but didn't quite hit the mark of exceptional.

Dined at this gem where the Uni Don takes center stage. Surprisingly, the menu doesn't list the price for this delicacy, which rings up at $68 a serving – a detail that could use transparency. That said, the investment is worthwhile; the sea urchin is sublime, melting effortlessly upon tasting, and is complemented exquisitely by the roe and seaweed pairing. While my boyfriend opted for the chicken on stone, I found it couldn't match the glory of their seafood offerings – the roasted and grilled items simply don't shine as brightly. A must-visit for sea urchin aficionados, but steer clear of the poultry if you're in search of culinary perfection.

I love this local place.  They have an excellent very reasonable lunch menu that you must try.  Mine was with Mutahmarah.They make this. Rey well.  It is made with red sweet peppers and walnuts.  Makes a good spread on bread.For lunch I chose the zucchini pancakes.  I highly recommend it.  Light and crispy on top.

During a recent visit to the nearby complex, I stumbled upon this gem of a restaurant. Intrigued by the buzz, I grabbed the avocado chirashi and shiso onigiri to go. The onigiri was fairly standard—tasty but nothing out of the ordinary. However, the avocado chirashi truly shone; it was a dish that I later wished I had savored on-site. Additionally, the house sauce was a revelation—its mysterious blend of flavors left me eager to purchase a jar for $10 on my inevitable return. This spot is a must-visit for anyone in the area.

I stopped by La Diagonal for a couple of drinks. I was not blown away by my margarita, but it was not the worst that I had. I will say that the staff was very nice and friendly, especially the bartender. La Diagonal has a very cool, open interior design with some limited outdoor seating. Most of the tables outside can accommodate 1 to 2 people. Perhaps during my next visit, I will try some of the food options.

I approached TomoTomo with cautious optimism, hoping it would overturn my belief that ramen and tsukemen are strictly dine-in fare. Unfortunately, my experience only solidified that sentiment. On the positive side, the take-away noodles maintained a commendable chewiness. However, the broth fell short, presenting an overbearing saltiness without the complexity one craves in a good ramen broth, worsened by its lack of warmth upon arrival. The seafood tsukemen included a generous portion of pork belly, though it was disappointingly fatty, and the scant bamboo did little to make up for it. While extra toppings like an egg are available, they come at an additional cost. TomoTomo may satisfy a quick noodle fix, but for a truly fulfilling experience, I'll stick to sitting down at a ramen shop.

Man oh man. I remember coming here years ago in my. Went with some friends to nyc to celebrating a bday. We had the frozen margaritas #moscatomama (so great!!), and wayyy to much food. The waiter could have at least told us and explained to us how big the freaking chicken wings are- def shot up with steroids. But the sticky wings are the best, Hennessy wings not so great. 2 of my friends ordered chicken and waffles (THE RESTAURANT DOES NOT HAVE SYRUP- They want you to use the chicken sauce- ew). Also the birthday song there loll- I literally laughed the whole time  the waiter comes out singing the bday and brings Hershey kisses and the check. Terrible! What happen to ice cream or dessert lol. Overall def a place to go in nyc, hush don't order a lot of food. SHARE with who you came with the waiters wont tell you to share though. 3 stars for the Hennessy wings, the drink, but the waiter could have been more reliable, and don't celebrate your bday here.
This place has the most delicious ramen! (The complimentary extra not comes in handy, too.. )

I loved the atmosphere here and the menu looked so appealing, but the tempura cauliflower dish I tried wasn't as flavorful as I had hoped for. The bartender said it was the most popular dish on the menu so I figured I picked a winner, but I ended up thinking it was just so-so. That being said, I was impressed that it stood alone as a meal. I figured I'd have to order an app or two to satiate my hunger, but the cauliflower was enough!

This was my first time having Cambodian food and it did not disappoint! The restaurant has a warm atmosphere and is nicely decorated. The seats are very comfy and our waitress was very helpful in helping us select dishes. She recommended pure Cambodian dishes that you can't find elsewhere. We were a large group, but the service was quick. The food was delicious, but a bit expensive. I highly recommend the nem nuong, yellow curry, and kuythiew cha. They also have frog legs! I tried the following:-Summer roll: Prawns and vermicelli wrapped in rice paper. It was just ok. I've never been a fan of summer rolls. There are better appetizers to choose over this one.-Khmer fish cake: Spicy fish cake. It was very flavorful!-Nem nuong: Skewered barbecue pork meatballs. My favorite of the appetizers I tried! The meat was very tender and flavorful. The sauce went great with it.-Mango salad: Green mango salad. It was sour tasting, but in a good way. Very refreshing.-Yellow curry: One of my favorites! It's so colorful looking, not heavy tasting, and not too spicy!-Phnom penh roast duck: Boneless duck. It was perfectly tender and not overly fatty. Very good!-Baked amok: Cambodia's national dish. It comes in a basket with fish baked with prawns, scallops and eggs, rice, and vegetables in curry sauce. The baked fish was so smooth (almost like a custard) and very good. Very unique dish!-Shrimp and scallop: Also good, but it didn't stand out much.-Loc Lac: Stir-fried beef with a sour lime, black pepper dipping sauce. Tasty, but I found it a bit too sour with the sauce. Meat was nicely cooked and not tough.-Kuythiew cha: My favorite of the night! Vermicelli noodles with shrimp and eggs. The noodles was cooked perfectly and soaked up the flavor!-Old fashioned pudding: Sweet sticky rice pudding with coconut milk and corn. Mildly sweet and light.-Cha dau: Similar to old fashioned pudding but with black eyed peas instead of corn. Both were good, but I preferred this one better. There was slightly more flavor in this one.

Title: Unfortunate Turn of Events at Lunch

My experience at this restaurant took a rapid turn for the worse today. Initially set on awarding three stars for a seemingly decent lunch option, I was horrified to find a dead fly in my takeout. This unsettling discovery came as I was about to mix rice into my bowl of General Tso's chicken. Although I had heard murmurs of dissatisfaction from colleagues, I hadn't encountered any issues until now.

Despite never facing such an incident at any restaurant before, I must commend the staff for their prompt customer service. Upon contacting them, they remembered my order and courteously offered a replacement meal or a refund. However, given the gravity of my experience, I am unable to bring myself to patronize the establishment again.

Additionally, the wonton soup that I ordered failed to meet expectations and did not contribute positively to the meal. After the incident, I felt compelled to return everything to the restaurant. Regrettably, this visit has firmly deterred me from revisiting.

service is slow and confusing. The day we went they were out of pitchers and snacks. Second, our IDs were taken away and held onto for like 5 minutes. One of the waiters asked for our IDs and left with them... and then gave them to some other server who was already busy with other customers to check our IDs. Um.. why ask for our IDs then in the first place if you're going to ask someone else to do it? Usually takes a few seconds just to look at our date of births. The drinks were absolutely the worst. You might as well change the word "cocktails" to "mocktails." Not only did they take forever to come, but were served in a plastic cup (understandable) and chipped ice. For highballs, Moscow mules.. I get it. but for a Manhattan?! it literally looked like rum and coke or any other well drink. In addition, it tasted like Robitusson. It was all bitters and vermouth. I stopped drinking after a few sips. Definitely not worth your time or money or service. Either that, just stick to beer.

Title: Truffle Grilled Cheese Heaven at Local Spot

If you adore a classic grilled cheese sandwich, brace yourself for a delightful experience at this gem of a shop that has mastered the art. On a brisk day, my choice of the truffle grilled cheese sandwich truly did not disappoint. This wasn't just any ordinary grilled cheese; it came with a twist of greens tucked inside, lending an unexpectedly fresh and flavorful lift to the comfort food staple. The bread was perfectly crisped with a buttery crunch, while the cheese inside was melt-in-your-mouth, stretchy goodness. Holding the warm sandwich was not only a treat for the taste buds but also a cozy respite for our chilly fingers. In essence, it's hard to mess up a grilled cheese unless you forget the essential - the melt, which they've got down to an art here. Rest assured, there's little chance of disappointment at this grilled cheese haven.

Most people dine at fancy restaurants in NYC, but my bf and I like to try the low key spots. We came here a few days before Christmas because this spot was only a 5 min walking distance from our hotel, and we were starving. First and foremost, they have a daily happy hour from 3-10 pm which was incredible! I ordered a white peach sangria which was delicious. For dinner, I ordered an avocado roll + sweet potato roll and both were super tasty! The sushi was inexpensive, and the place got packed about 30 mins after we got there. I would definitely recommend!

Title: A Creamy Encore at the Artichoke Pizza in Chelsea

During my initial visit to Artichoke Basille's Pizza, I was mentally awarding it five stars for their artichoke slice – a delectable surprise that left me enamored, although I never got around to writing a review. Upon my recent return to their Chelsea location, I felt compelled to share my thoughts.

The artichoke slice still reigns supreme in my eyes, making it an undeniable go-to choice on the menu. Despite my prior indifference to artichokes, the combination of artichoke hearts and spinach nestled atop the pizza has now irreversibly captured my palate's affection. Each bite is a testament to the pizzeria's culinary bravery, embedding a love for a previously disregarded ingredient.

However, I must note a slight adjustment to my initial rating, bringing it down to a solid four stars. The reason? The cream. It's a generous, rich addition that initially feels like a luxurious indulgence, yet its opulence can prove overwhelming. The decadent blanket of cream surpasses sumptuousness after several bites, teetering towards excess.

To counterbalance this creamy onslaught, I recommend a tactical approach: alternate bites with the crust's crisp relief or take intermittent sips of beer to cleanse the palate and restore gustatory harmony.

Would I recommend Artichoke Basille's Pizza? Absolutely – with the caveat that patrons prepare for the cream's bounty. Will I return? Without a doubt. The artichoke slice has secured its spot as my number one pick, with a side note to self: always order a beverage for flavor equilibrium.

Came here for Christmas Eve dinner without a reservation and was seated right away. Conveniently located close to grand central station and lots of seating inside the restaurant. If you check in on yelp, Buy $30 worth and you get a free standard cocktail. If you're a party of 2 and both check and spend $60+, you get 2 standard cocktails free. We got the pisco sour and the Manhattan and both were delicious. The chirashi bowl was just as yummy as beautiful to look at. I love the sushi rice at the bottom! My sister said Japanese-Peruvian fusions are best because of the sauces and she's not wrong! The Sexy sana had this white sauce at the bottom of the plate that was especially delicious. The Nikkei potato salad was also pretty delicious for an appetizer. The smoothness of the potatoes mixed with the crunch of the cucumber made for a pleasant bite. All the fish tasted fresh to us too. For dessert we got the waffle and the chocolate tiramisu with green tea ice cream -- I would recommend both. It's hard to choose once since they were both very different so it depends on your taste preference. The tiramisu didn't really have any espresso notes, but the chocolate was almost like a ganache. The waffle came out slightly crispy which was delicious. Both had these crunchy mini balls which gave the dish much more dimension - loved it.

A very casual food court alternative to the various famous Korean Fried Chicken restaurants nearby.  Perfect for when they aren't open or the wait is too long.  Despite the setting, it's not that much cheaper, maybe because it is made-to-order and the quality is still high.Honey Garlic Chicken Wings: A very thick sauce.  Also, very honey intensive, which is a nice change compared to "honey"-flavored sauces that taste nothing like it.  Kinda messy since sauce gets all over, but quite tasty.  The crispy wings definitely stand up to this sauce without getting soggy.Pelicana Spicy Chicken Wings: My favorite of the two sauces.  I got the in-between spicy, which wasn't that spicy at all.  Reminded me more of the Bonchon-style in terms of sauce thickness.  Loved the tenderness and crispiness of the wings.Frozen Strawberry Ade: Strawberry soda with frozen lemonade on top.  Thought this would have more natural fruit given the price point.Frozen Mango Ade: Like the other one, but with mango soda.  Decent, but probably not worth the $7.
Yum! Pasta was so fresh and the sauce was great! Staff were so nice! I got the weekly special, which was mushroom and sausages.

Title: A Blossoming Dining Experience for Veggie Lovers and Beyond

If you're on the hunt for a vegetarian or vegan dining haven, Blossom should top your list. Even my non-veg friends leave raving about the flavors. The service shines with friendliness and efficiency, a true feat considering the large groups (10+) I've been part of.

The menu is a parade of hits, especially the fries with truffle aioli – a crowd-pleaser we demolish every time. Pasta lovers, rejoice with the rigatoni and gnocchi – my go-to dishes that never disappoint. While the fried artichokes didn't quite captivate my taste buds, the overall array of entrées impresses, with the "chicken" marsala winning over my omnivorous companions.

Don't skip dessert; the chocolate ganache is divinely rich (best shared) and the tiramisu earns top marks in my book.

Blossom delivers a delightful culinary experience whether you're all-in on plants or just veg-curious.

The Greek salad and the chicken platter with basmati rice were great. The chicken was so juicy and the Greek salad so refreshing and perfectly dressed and chopped and crisp.However, the babaganoush and hummus were seriously lacking, which stinks because I'd love to order a sandwich with one of those spreads. The babaganoush has this strange sweet, almost plastic-y taste to it, while the hummus has OD'ed on cumin, which tastes like an armpit. I'd definitely come back for the salad and the chicken.

My recent visit to the restaurant before catching a movie was underwhelming due to the excessively long wait time. While I found the majority of the dishes to be quite average and unremarkable, a notable exception was the truffle fries, which were exceptionally tasty. However, the slow service could have easily caused us to miss our movie if we were solely relying on this meal.

Underwhelming....Not sure about where this best French onion soup in the city said came from? Very water down, lack of flavor, barely have onion inside, barely have bread inside. It was sad.Mussel was pretty good and fresh but the portion is obviously smaller compare to other restaurants. Blame that it's in tourist location?Fried Gnocchi with pesto sauce, not bad but definitely on the heavy side. They should said it's pesto (30%) + creme (70%) sauce more correct...
Food is like an absolute 5 out of 5.  But the service...? I literally had to ask 4 times for refill my water. It was for my friends birthday. Not sure if I wanna bring her here again :(.

Title: Disappointing Dining Experience on 8th

After my latest visit to a new spot on 8th Avenue, my quest for culinary excellence hit a snag. A Thursday night outing with friends led us here, where we encountered service that was passable but inconsistent in pace.

Our order comprised a reasonably priced bottle of white wine, which was a highlight with its wallet-friendly selection. The bread and olive oil served as an appetizer were average, nothing to write home about.

We had a pepperoni pizza, boasting a burnt crust that detracted from the experience rather than adding the sought-after charred flavor. The spicy salami was similarly overdone, and the overly sweet sauce only compounded the pizza's faults -- it was a struggle to eat, and we left most of it untouched. Even at $16, it fell short of even the humblest dollar slice in quality.

The Beef Agnolotti, priced at $18, offered perfectly al dente pasta, but the beef filling was underwhelming. The rich sauce didn't quite justify the small portion, leaving the dish feeling somewhat overpriced.

Thankfully, the olive oil gelato - priced between $8 to $10 - was a delightful surprise. Its unique blend of sweet and savory managed to redeem the meal slightly. The use of high-quality olive oil, in contrast to what accompanied the bread, was evident and appreciated.

Despite the reasonable wine and exceptional gelato, the rest of the experience was a letdown. For an enoteca in such a competitive gastronomic neighborhood, it was remarkably underwhelming. With other establishments offering more value, better service, and superior culinary executions, this place sadly ranks at the bottom. My final rating: a generous 1.3/5, rounded down for the disappointment it delivered.

So when they say quintessential slice of Pizza in NY, it's not exaggeration by any stretch. If you have a chance to dig into 'any' one  of their slices, you'll agree. We tried a slice of almost all variations and they were close to perfection. Thin slices with lightly crispy bottom and topped with cheese and toppings loaded with flavor. Droool....Service - 4/5Food - 4/5Ambience - 4/5

I visited this restaurant for a lunchtime treat and decided on the chirashi lunch special - a choice I didn't regret. Served in a generously sized bowl, the selection of fresh fish slices was impressive. Although the price point is a bit higher, it's justified by both the quality and the upscale ambiance of the establishment. The portion was satisfactorily hearty, leaving me contentedly full. An unexpected delight was the inclusion of two or three varieties of Japanese pickles, adding a pleasant tang to the overall experience. Highly recommend for those seeking an indulgent lunch option.

After running the New Jersey Marathon, I knew without a doubt that I wanted to treat myself to pizza at some point while I was in New York. I spent the Monday after the race in Manhattan with my sister and my husband. We (mostly me) decided to go here for lunch and so glad we did.     There are a couple high tables but otherwise no seating. There were people at all the tables but a table opened up by the time we were ready to eat. We walked right up and ordered, Between the 3 of us, we ordered 2 pizzas- the classic and the pepperoni. The deal they have on the classic is very reasonable. For all this pizza, we paid a little over $25. Not bad for 3 people to eat lunch and walk out satisfied.     The pizza itself was ready quickly. They had tons of different pizzas. They had one with broccoli that looked really good. There was another one with mushrooms that I almost got. The pizza was delicious. The crust was perfect- crispy on the outside/ edges but soft in the middle. There was garlic powder and red pepper flakes available. The pizzas are rectangles cut into 4 slices which I like, and made it easier to share (not that you would want to!)     Overall great pizza. I definitely recommend this place.

Title: A Soulful Brunch Experience at Sylvia's

My quest for genuine soul food led me to the bustling Sylvia's, and the experience was every bit as authentic as I had hoped. For their renowned Sunday gospel brunch, it's crucial to arrive early; I found myself amongst a gathering crowd before doors opened at 11 am and was fortunate to be among the last seated immediately.

The ambience was buzzing, though I must mention that the soul-stirring gospel music didn't commence until 12:30 pm, something for early birds to consider. The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the fried chicken paired with hearty home-style fries - a sublime treat that left me craving more despite its generous filling nature.

While the prices might reflect a premium for the ambiance and experience rather than just the meal, it felt well worth it for the authenticity and quality served up. I'm already eager for my next visit - Sylvia's waffles are next on my list!

Title: A Culinary Gem: Sushi Ishikawa

Review:

Dining at Sushi Ishikawa is an experience that's not to be missed. It's no surprise why this bustling high-end sushi spot in NYC is always packed – the food is simply mind-blowing. While the decor is modest, scoring a 7, it does little to detract from the overall excellence of the restaurant.

Chef Don's innovative approach to sushi takes you on a gastronomic journey that is far from traditional yet leaves a lasting impression. Having followed his culinary evolution for over 15 years, from Geisha to Geisha Table, I can attest to his humble nature and relentless dedication to his craft.

The $155 omakase is one of the best sushi deals in the city, giving you a taste of premium items worth every penny. Each piece served is a work of art, causing an almost communal sense of jubilation among diners. From the rich flavors of Nodoguro and Tairagi to the sublime pairing of Miyazaki A5 Wagyu with Foie Gras, each bite is a testament to Chef Don's brilliance.

Notably, the blend of Southeast Asian flavors with Japanese techniques only enhances the experience. The restaurant offers a perfect 10 in both cuisine and overall impression, with service close behind at a 9. Whether you're a sushi purist or open to inventive culinary fusions, Sushi Ishikawa promises a truly memorable meal. Don't hesitate - make your reservation now and prepare to be amazed.

I recently visited this spot for a quick bite with a friend, and it turned out to be a mixed experience. First up, the ambiance is energetic to the point of being excessively loud post-5:00pm, so conversation seekers, beware. The happy hour perks are exclusive to the bar, which wasn't a shocker.

On to the food - the menu did impress. We opted for the risotto croquettes ($6), which were a standout for sure, alongside the tasty yet slightly meager shrimp flatbread ($17). The spinach salad, surprisingly, might have stolen the show for me. Service-wise, everything was peachy until the bill arrived. There was an extra $15 tacked on, which the waiter chalked up to an accidental addition of someone else's drink to our tab. Apologies were made, but it was still a disappointing glitch in an otherwise pleasant visit.

Bottom line, I'd swing by again, but probably just stick to the drinks at the bar.

Title: Cozy Noodles with a Side of Chills

I've dined at this spot on a couple of occasions and found it to be fairly satisfactory. On my initial visit, we were relocated near the entrance to accommodate a larger group, which resulted in an uncomfortable draft each time the door opened, somewhat dampening the experience of my hot soup.

During my second visit, I tried the pork kimchi dip soba, enhancing it with chicken meatballs, which turned out to be rather unremarkable. Next time, I'll stick to just pork. The broth was on the saltier side, a sentiment echoed by other patrons, though the restaurant thoughtfully offers additional base broth to fine-tune the flavor to your liking.

If you're in the mood for some noodle soup, this place will hit the spot with its tasty offerings. Just be mindful of where you sit if you'd rather not pair your meal with a breeze.

Title: A Cozy Post-Show Dining Experience with a Side of Sticker Shock

After enjoying the delightful Broadway play "The Prom," my wife and I found ourselves wandering into a charming restaurant en route to Grand Central Terminal. Despite the absence of a formal greeting by a hostess, a kindly bar patron directed us further into the establishment where we were soon tended to by a waiter.

The interior was captivating, adorned with a beautiful mural and various posters that contributed to a very lovely atmosphere. The menu, although not extensive, offered a special print-out with additional choices, striking a balance between variety and focus.

We kicked off our meal with appetizers – the fried calamari was a highlight, perfectly cooked with a delightfully light breading, while my wife's avocado salad was equally impressive. For the main course, my linguine with white clam sauce, featuring fresh Long Island clams, was a hit despite the pasta being vermicelli rather than linguine. My wife's chicken cacciatore was equally enjoyable, served off the bone with tender chicken breast.

Service was where the restaurant truly shone. Our waiter went above and beyond to ensure a pleasant dining experience, while the bus staff kept our area tidy and our drinks flowing. The manager's check-in was a thoughtful touch.

Breaking our usual habit, we indulged in a cannoli for dessert, shared between us, which was fresh and full of flavor. My double espresso was generously more akin to a triple, and a complimentary almond liqueur from the house was a welcome surprise.

However, the evening's splendor was somewhat dimmed by the bill. At $215 for two, inclusive of tax, drinks, and a deservedly good tip, the expense surpassed the $$ expectation set by Yelp and firmly placed the experience in the $$$$ category. It's with this note on value that my initial 4-star impression has been adjusted to a 3-star review.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Hide Chan Ramen

My husband, an avid ramen enthusiast, and I were brimming with anticipation to try the renowned Hide Chan Ramen, famed for their authentic HAKATA-style noodles. Their specialty, Tonkatsu ramen, promised a rich experience; indeed, the creamy, pork-infused broth did not disappoint with its depth and robust flavors, lovingly simmered for hours.

However, our excitement was dampened by the pricing and serving sizes. Despite indulging in two bowls each, we were left wanting, as the portions felt meager relative to the cost, and the accompaniments were sparse. True satisfaction eluded us this visit—Hide Chan Ramen delivered on taste but fell short on value and generosity.

Came here for restaurant week with some coworkers and got the mixed greens salad and the salmon. The salmon was good but the greens were not all that fresh unfortunately. I feel like we should have had a little bit more food on the main plate. I've been once before and ordered off the lunch menu then which was a much better experience. I would avoid restaurant week here again.

I ordered the stir fry thick rice noodles. It was delicious!! The portions was also very large. I love spicy food, and zest was great. Service was good, the food was authentic, and I would definitely come here again.

Title: A Medley of Hits and Misses at This NYC Soba Noodle House

My recent dining experience at a New York soba noodle house was a mixed bowl. On the upside, the house-made soba noodles themselves were a delight: light, refreshing, and perfectly embodying the essence of what a soba dish should be. The broth—a critical component—was well-balanced; it was fair and subtle, avoiding the pitfall of overpowering the delicate noodles.

Unfortunately, the restaurant dropped a few noodles in terms of service and logistics. The wait staff seemed disengaged, which detracted from the dining experience. Additionally, the ordering process came across as unnecessarily confusing, making it a somewhat frustrating task to even get to the meal.

Compounding these issues was the seating arrangement. The tight quarters and suboptimal layout left much to be desired, especially in a city where space is at a premium but smart design can make even the smallest venue welcoming.

In the end, I would give the food a commendable 3-star rating, but the service and atmosphere only muster a 2.5-star rating. Considering the vast sea of Japanese specialty options in New York City, I'm uncertain about a return visit to this particular establishment.

My recent visit to this restaurant left me quite disappointed, particularly with the Pad Thai. Unfortunately, the noodles were a sticky mess, lacking in both flavor and temperature. Although there were plenty of shrimp, they too were lacking in seasoning and weren't served hot. The highlight of the meal was the Singha beer, which was a safe and reliable choice. Service was passable, and we opted to sit at the bar due to a line and our lack of reservation. I'm left with the certainty that there must be a better Pad Thai to be found elsewhere in the city.

I recently dined at this two-story restaurant for lunch and was greeted with the option to sit and watch the kitchen on the second floor. The atmosphere was complemented by a bar downstairs. Starting with the calamari, it was served Shanghai-style with a sweet and spicy sauce, accompanied by peanuts—a tasty, albeit non-traditional, take on the dish with its breading. 

The cheesesteak eggrolls were another inventive choice, sliced and topped with cheese. However, my dining companions from Philadelphia found them to be a departure from their hometown standard. The prime beef short rib stroganoff featured pappardelle egg noodles that were slightly underdone, paired with sour cream and crispy onions. The short rib itself was a bit of a letdown, being tough and dry instead of tender and succulent. 

Service was competent, with staff ensuring our meal was expedited upon request due to our time constraint. Overall, the experience was acceptable, but there's room for improvement in both food execution and flavor authenticity.

La Pecora Bianca has some great fresh tastes and ingredients. I shared the local burrata, tagliatelle (beef and pork bolognese) and toscano salad. The local burrata cheese was fresh and paired nicely with the figs. The toast was a little too toasted and burnt for my taste but I really liked the burrata. The toscano salad was so fresh and I absolutely loved the fun colored carrots. The salad came together really nicely with the lemon vinaigrette and the dressing was just enough to cover the usual bitterness of kale but not too overwhelming. When the tagliatelle came out, I was already a bit stuffed (the portions are nice), and the pasta did not disappoint! The pasta was so hot and freshly made. I really liked this pasta because usually bolognese can be very heavy but the pasta didn't feel like this at all.The ambiance here was really great. Would recommend making a reservation and getting here early. It gets crowded really quick with both people who do and do not have reservations.

I recently made what might just be the best food decision since I moved to the city, and it came from a gem in Chinatown. For just $6.50, I enjoyed a mouthwatering dish of large roasted pork and duck over rice. Each bite was a delight of juicy, authentic flavors that married beautifully with the side of rice and cabbage. The generous portions were substantial enough to stretch over two or possibly even three meals, offering incredible value.

While some might say the vegetables were a bit on the sparse side, I personally found the meat-to-veggie ratio to be perfect, tipping the scales towards a meat lover's dream. All things considered, this spot delivered a satisfying meal that's not only a treat to the palate but also to the wallet. A definite must-visit in Chinatown!

I stopped by this gem during their happy hour and was immediately struck by the stylish decor and warm service. The happy hour deals are too good to pass up, especially the piña colada which was a tropical delight. While I didn't sample the food this time, the menu tantalized with promising options. Cleanliness is clearly a priority here; even the bathroom was spotless. To top it off, their vintage photo booth added a fun twist to the experience. This spot is absolutely worth a visit!

Despite its weekday buzz, this bustling spot rewards patience with its culinary offerings. A seemingly simple salad impresses upon taste, while the pasta dishes highlight an appreciation for al dente texture and fresh ingredients. The pizza shines with its delightfully thin crust, and generous portion sizes ensure a satisfying meal. While the food doesn't quite hit the heights of astonishment, the overall quality makes dining here worthwhile—provided the queue isn't dauntingly extensive.

Really prefer the noodles at Momofuku compared to Ippudo! This is a great spot to grab a meal in the Columbus Circle area, but make sure you have a reservation (otherwise you could face a long wait). Note it closes between lunch and dinner (4-5pm). The restaurant is pretty brightly lit and spacious--you can sit at the bar or tables. I've been at both, and I will say it's pretty interesting to watch them assemble the dishes at the bar. Mad props to the line cook. Onto the food! The Garlic Chicken Ramen is my go to dish. I love pairing the chicken with the Ssäm sauce, and I think the broth is delicious (usually I can't finish the broth at other restaurants since it's too salty). A single bowl of ramen isn't enough to fill me, so I'll get one side dish. The pork buns are good (they're off the menu but you can still order it) although they are a little better at Ippudo, and I like the Fried Japanese Potatoes dish to share as well. If you're a fan of ramen, you'll have to try Momofuku!

It's not too big inside and doesn't look good for big groups. Waited about 30m for brunch but the waiting area was heated and not crowded. Our waitress was very friendly. I had the grilled chicken sandwich which was delicious. The mimosas were also $6 that day.

Title: A Delightful Brunch Experience at Sall's

I recently had the pleasure of visiting Sall's for their unlimited brunch, and it was an absolute delight. Arriving at 11:30am meant we avoided any wait time, which was perfect as my friends and I had a show to catch later.

The restaurant's interior is simple yet sophisticated, especially the bar area. The lively Latino music set a fantastic ambiance throughout our stay. At approximately $20 for the unlimited brunch, the value is outstanding. It includes one hearty entree plus endless mimosas—three of which were enough to get pleasantly tipsy.

I indulged in the lobster mac & cheese, which was a treat, although the chicken & waffles were quite tempting. The mimosas with "experimental" rim spices provided by the friendly bartender added a unique touch to our meal.

The staff's personable nature and attentiveness to our time constraints contributed to the overall excellent service. Sall's brunch is a lovely affair and I recommend an early visit for the best experience.

As a lover of soba, Cocoron has been on my eye for a while.Coming here on a cold winter day, I opted for one of their popular dip sobas.  I decided on the large Stamina Dip Soba ($15.5).  The soup had various meats inside, mushrooms, and scallions.  There was a rich and full flavor, and the soba paired with it nicely.  For dip soba, the soba comes cold on the side, and you dip it into the hot soup to eat together.  It's a fun way to eat, and it keeps the noodles fresh and chewy.  I enjoyed how they keep the soup hot with a small fire underneath the bowl.  I also like how they give you broth after you finish your soba so you can drink the rest of your soup. I definitely recommend the large if you're eating a full meal, and the small if you're just having a small meal or a snack.  If you're a soba lover, Cocoron is definitely a great place for you!

On my first trip to NYC for work, I was looking for a place to get some food on a weekday evening. I settled on Nittis and the bar. It was around 8PM when I arrived and the restaurant/bar was fairly empty.I sat at the bar. The bartender was immediately attentive. I indicated I would be eating dinner and was presented with a placemat and silverware. Based on bartender recommendation I have the Papparedelle Bolognese. It was a huge portion, served with bread and two infused butters. Very tasty food. While sitting, I met the owner who offered me a glass of wine while I finished. Overall a great experience. I found the staff to be friendly and attentive.

I recently dined at a local Thai restaurant and couldn't resist trying their lunch special. As a fan of Thai cuisine, I opted for my favorite, the massaman curry, paired with white rice. Priced under $10, the deal also included a choice between soup or two mini spring rolls. Despite a slight deviation from the traditional recipe, as the curry lacked peanuts, the flavors and spices were nevertheless excellent, delivering an authentic and satisfying experience. Highly recommended for those seeking a flavorful and affordable lunch option.

Ive tried many curry spots, but this one is the best in Nyc so far. The curry packs a punch and the flavor is amazing. I dont usually finish this much rice, but this is my first time cleaning a plate with mostly rice on it. I would give this place a 5 star but I notice the service is extra slow. There was like 4 customers. I waited about 30min for 2 plain curry with  cutlets on top. By the time I got my food the place was packed.Overall the curry was amazing. I would reccomend friends and family and come again.

Title: A Hit and Miss Experience at the Noodle House

I recently dined at the Noodle House, enticed by their promising Asian cuisine. The scallion pancake with beef was the highlight of the meal, easily deserving a 4 to 5-star rating. It had a comforting similarity to duck buns, thanks to the savory sauce and crisp raw scallions—a delightful fusion of flavors.

The soup dumplings, while flavorful, couldn't quite match my expectations set by recent travels in Shanghai. The skins were on the thicker side, which was a bit of a letdown, keeping the dish at a steady 3 stars.

I also tried the house special cut noodles. The texture was peculiar, with a noticeable uneven chewiness that made me question if it was a deliberate choice. However, the beef served with the noodles was succulent, with the right amount of fat and tendon to enrich the dish.

Title: A Delectable Soho Experience at RAWBAR

If you find yourself meandering through the vibrant Soho neighborhood with a craving for exquisite sushi and seafood, DOMODOMO's spin-off, RAWBAR, is an absolute must-visit. Nestled right next door to its renowned sibling, this upscale sushi bar has created quite a buzz for itself, and I had the pleasure of finding out why on a bustling summer Friday night.

With a minimal wait time of mere ten minutes, my anticipation was well rewarded. The sight of fashionably attired patrons along Houston Street added to the lively ambiance. Settling into comfortable padded chairs at a low bar, designed more for lounging than perching, the interior struck a refined balance between a traditional blond-wood Japanese eatery and a chic, subway-tiled oyster bar. The clientele was an elegant mix of well-dressed couples and NYU students splurging on quality dining.

The oyster selection, leaning towards East Coast varieties, was modest yet satisfying, with an unbeatable offering of $1.50 "happy hour" oysters available at all times. Each succulent variety received an instant upgrade thanks to the innovative wasabi-lime sorbet—an accompaniment that delivered a welcome punch of cool zest.

Handrolls are another highlight here, rivaling the likes of Kazunori. While the craftsmanship may not be flawless, the quality of the salmon, toro, and unagi filled rolls left no room for complaint. But the true star of my meal was the uni pasta—its creamy, rich dashi sauce bore a remarkable resemblance to a sophisticated take on mac-and-cheese, captivating my palate and leaving me longing for more.

To complement the meal, I explored the sake menu, which was impressively curated, although wine and beer were also available. While prices may tip towards the higher end, the exceptional quality and service provided justify every penny.

In summary, RAWBAR delivers an experience where each component—be it the fresh oysters, the handrolls, or the meticulously prepared cooked dishes—shines on its own. But it's the combination of these elements, all conveniently housed under one roof, that makes dining here a triumph. A resounding success, RAWBAR is undoubtedly greater than just the sum of its parts.

Debating whether to give 2 or 3 stars but since I am writing a review on my dine in experience and the food, I will be honest. It started out great, I was seated within 5 minutes because only two other tables had patrons and the kind server asked us what we wanted to drink then waited a few moments to let us read the menu. Tres leches was great but everything went down hill from there. There may have been a shift switch so the new servers never checked in on us, never refilled our waters for half an hr. Not sure what other patrons are eating but the lomo saltado was tasteless this time and the crispness of the jalea was ruined by juices from the onions. If I wanted my "fried" yuca wet, then I would have just ordered steamed yuca. The jalea I had did not include fried crab that was in other pictures, but it could have been the price difference between small and large. When we asked for a to-go box and the check, they said the sauces cost extra so I was fine with that. I went home and the sauces were not in my to-go box. Their website online offers 10% off all dine in at the Chelsea location but that was a lie. The check never came even though there were 4 servers standing around, talking to each other, playing with music selection, standing in the bar area, and not attentive to the three tables that were supposed to be served. I would recommend taking $50 to eat at home for delivery with their subpar food or really go elsewhere in Midtown where there are better selections to choose from. If you want delicious Peruvian chicken and green sauce there are options on 34th Street a few blocks away

I recently dined at this BBQ spot for their $29 all-you-can-eat lunch and was pleasantly surprised by the decent selection on the menu. The assortment included tasty options like ribeye, bulgogi, a variety of pork cuts including belly and shoulder, as well as spicy variations, sausage, tiger shrimp, calamari (both regular and spicy), marinated chicken, mushrooms, shishito peppers, and the usual sides of rice, egg soufflé, vegetables, pickles, and an array of sauces. 

While the menu wasn't extensive, the quality of the food was impressive, with everything served very fresh. The restaurant wasn't completely full at the time of my visit, but service suffered due to only one waiter attending to the entire second floor, making it challenging to get his attention and resulting in longer wait times for service.

A noticeable downside was the lack of a range hood over the grill, which made the dining area quite smoky. Overall, if you're not in a hurry and don't mind a bit of smoke, the food here is worth a try.

Title: A Yuzu Haven with Generous Nori Portions

I recently visited this spot with a serious craving for yuzu and wasn't disappointed. Their yuzu dashi was a delight, perfectly capturing the citrus's essence - a must-try for fellow yuzu aficionados. The option to add an ajitama egg and nori was a welcome touch, especially given the generous portion of nori, a rare find in most establishments.

My companions opted for the shaki shaki and XO miso, both boasting unique and memorable flavors. It's the sort of place that leaves you planning your next visit before you've even finished your meal.

However, diners be warned: the lack of a bathroom could be a deal-breaker for some. Regardless, for those willing to overlook this inconvenience, a culinary treat awaits.

I enjoyed my dining experience here, I still remember my first visit it was quiet, the room was dim light, busy but not crowded we were seated at the room were We can enjoy our conversation and at the same time people watched. I adore their ceiling restaurant decor it was stunning. The service was great, we were allowed to enjoy our wine and food. Oh and the food we ordered the famous copied version of the Peter Luger's Porter house dry aged steak for two, creamed spinach and the sautéed mushrooms. Our steak was cooked to our liking medium rare. It was juicy and melts in your mouth. I love going to Peter Luger in Williamsburg for my Porterhouse dry aged steak, but whenever reservations are full, Wolfgang's is always my back up. People who can't get reservations from Peter Luger should come to Wolfgang's to experience a much more friendly service, an expansive restaurant menu that has something for everyone, a decor' that you will admire and it's in Manhattan.

Title: A Delectable Greek Feast at TY Taverna

I recently had the pleasure of dining at TY Taverna for an early Saturday lunch and was swept away by the authenticity and freshness of their Greek cuisine. This charming, quaint spot may be small in size but is colossal in flavor and generosity.

My family and I indulged in a variety of dishes including a crisp traditional Greek salad, succulent calamari, perfectly grilled octopus, the robust kyclades seafood special, along with both chicken kebab and grilled chicken platters. Each dish was exceptionally fresh, expertly seasoned, and evocative of true Grecian flair. The calamari, grilled octopus, and kyclades special, in particular, were the stars of our Mediterranean feast.

Be warned, the portion sizes at TY Taverna are remarkably generous! It's a wise strategy to share among your table to experience a wider range of their offerings without reaching the brink of overindulgence—a lesson I'll remember for my next visit.

The experience was further enhanced by the thoughtful touches of complimentary bread to start and a dessert to finish. It's those little things that elevate the dining experience from good to unforgettable.

In summary, TY Taverna is a gem worthy of visiting where the robust flavors and ample portions will leave your taste buds delighted and your belly full. Just be prepared to leave with a couple of extra pounds as a souvenir!

Love this place! Wish it was a bit closer - like walking distance. But 15-20 minutes on the subway + walking isn't too bad for legit hand pulled noodles. My wife and I came for lunch one weekday and had the herbal beef soup with knife cut noodles and the beef stir fry with shanghai noodles. I mostly devoured the stir fry and the shanghai noodles were wonderfully bouncy and chewy. The sauce was also very good - next time I'll take it up a level and try spicy. My wife's herbal soup was great as well but a totally different flavor profile than my stir fry. We shared some fried pork and chive dumplings. They were top notch!
