The filling tasted home made and the dumpling skins were resilient and crispy on the outside - yet also chewy.This is a great all around spot for hand pulled noodles uptown!

I was excited to see a new Makimaki location, of course i popped in for two rolls. Service as usual is excellent, and this location of the biggest ive seen. Plenty of room to sit and clean.Pricey rolls but it's the city, no surprise here! The one thing i was looking for in this location was the juices in a can, but it looked like this location only had carbonated options for the most part.

I stopped by this spot on a Friday evening for a casual drink and bite to eat, arriving shortly before the happy hour at 5pm. Lucky enough to nab seats at the bar, we opted for Shiner Bock on tap at a reasonable $7. When it came time to eat, I grabbed wings directly from the counter—mistakenly incurring a nearly $10 surplus on the bill compared to bar pricing. The staff, however, swiftly rectified this upon being informed. The wings themselves were a highlight: smoky, substantial, and satisfying, with three pieces proving more than enough to satiate. Overall, a pleasant experience punctuated by attentive service and hearty fare.

They also have chili oil sitting out which is amazing.Even without those two spectacular additions, some of the best dumplings I've had. Perfect, inexpensive. Title: Quaint Charm with Rapid Service in Chinatown

My recent visit to this cash-only establishment in the heart of Chinatown revealed a bustling hotspot that belies its archaic payment policy. Despite its traditional Asian restaurant facade, the interior exudes an unexpected classy air, shadowed yet inviting.

A Friday night is predictably crowded, but the efficiency of the staff had us seated in a prime window spot within 20 minutes – a delightful surprise given the packed waiting area. The service, almost too prompt, had us juggling with multiple servers ready to take our order before we could even settle on our choices.

The menu, while hit-and-miss, offered some standout dishes. The ginger duck soup was a highlight with its succulent meat and comforting noodles. The rendang boasted tender meat as well, though it could benefit from a bolder flavor profile. In contrast, the roti was underwhelming, more suited for children's palates, and the spicy squid might be an acquired taste, with its crispy texture and intense fishiness.

Overall, there's a reason to return, armed with the knowledge of which dishes to embrace and which to avoid. Just remember to hit the ATM beforehand.

Title: Respectable Ramen at Nakamura, but Lacks the Magic Touch

I recently dined at Nakamura for a ramen fix while in the area, and the experience was solid, though it didn't quite set my culinary world on fire. The ramen is good – let's be clear on that. If you're looking for a decent bowl of noodles, Nakamura's offerings, with their satisfying chew and snap paired with a creamy, umami-rich tonkotsu broth, will meet your expectations.

The Jidori Mazemen was a standout, providing a twist on the traditional with its unique chili granola. It's worth a try if you're after something that breaks away from the norm.

However, as much as the ramen is competently executed, it lacks that indefinable allure – the 'x factor' that incites cravings and culinary obsessions. Nakamura might be what I'd describe as "the thinking man's ramen," where creativity and intellect meet noodle soup, but it failed to resonate with my more impulsive, emotion-driven appetite for the dish.

The sides, like the gyoza, were perfectly enjoyable – nice and crispy. Service was friendly and efficient, contributing to a pleasant dining experience.

Tucked away next to a bridge, Nakamura is a spot I'd revisit if I happened to be nearby and hungered for ramen, but it's not a place I'd go out of my way for. It's good, it's interesting, but not unforgettable.

Title: A Brunch of Mixed Emotions at a NY Eatery

During a recent brunch experience in New York, the Burekas plate offered a delightful taste of Israeli cuisine, albeit at a premium price of $17. The dish boasted perfectly scrambled eggs, a fresh tomato-cucumber salad, and indulgent flaky pastries filled with olive and feta. Accompanied by high-quality yogurt drizzled with olive oil and spices, as well as a mild green tahini sauce, the flavors and textures were a celebration on the plate.

While the meal itself was impressive, the ambiance and service left something to be desired. Despite the availability of plenty of indoor seating, there was a wait to be seated, which led us to opt for a spot near the open windows to escape the dimly lit interior. My dining companion's choice of crispy fried dough was a smaller portion but pleasantly savory.

The service, however, was less than attentive, and a small mishap involving a piece of string found in the salad was overlooked due to their lack of presence. To our dismay, a side order of pancakes for takeaway, costing $12 with an additional charge for "fresh" berries, turned out to be a disappointment. The pancakes were dry and unremarkable, reminiscent of a boxed mix, and the berries were not fresh, with one showing signs of mold.

While some elements of the brunch shone brightly, the overall experience was tarnished by service missteps and subpar takeaway options that didn't justify their high cost.

I visited a local Upper East Side Chinese restaurant for lunch today and found the experience to be a step above your typical takeout in terms of price. Despite the higher cost, I was impressed by two standout dishes: the hot black bean pork and the house chicken, both of which were very flavorful and well-prepared. The egg rolls didn't quite match up to the standard set by China Taste, though they were still satisfactory. As for the fried rice, it was decent — a basic offering that rounded out the meal.

5 Star experience for sure! We dined here Valentine's Day weekend for my hubby's birthday. Reservations were easy to make in advance via Resy, but were limited due to the popularity (and holiday weekend) of the restaurant. Everything is top notch-- from the decor, to the food, to the outstanding service. There are a few set menus to choose from, including a vegetarian option. If needed, they can accommodate a swap from one menu to another (just ask). The highlights of the night were the Brussel Sprout salad (not on the menu, complimentary with the progression), absolutely delicious rolls with goat cheese whipped butter (to die for!) and the Baklava ice cream dessert. Honestly, everything was really good, but these are the dishes that left me wanting more! I added in the Resy notes that we were celebrating my hubby's bday and they brought out a delicious coconut meringue cake with candle and birthday message-- definitely made our night and the cake was amazing! They even sent us with a to-go treat of banana chocolate chip coffee cake for the next day. I would definitely return if in the city again!

The food is so good! We ordered salmon sashimi, eel sashimi, the tuna crispy rice, and the northern lights roll. Everything was delicious - I'd definitely recommend the tuna crispy rice and the northern lights roll. We arrived about 15 minutes before our reservation and they seated us early, which we appreciated! However, our waiter was really unfriendly. It didn't put a damper on the meal too much but he wasn't attentive. Definitely make a reservation in advance! We had one, but there was a lot of people waiting for a table in the lobby (this was on Saturday night).

I recently made my second visit to this gem of a restaurant, and it was just as splendid as the first. The must-try dish is the Cheesy Pork Cutlet, which is as tender and crispy as they come, with an outstanding cheesy pull that elevates it to a whole new level. I also had the Vegetable Curry Rice, a delightful twist on the classic, brimming with fresh broccoli, onions, potatoes, and carrots.

My dining companion opted for the Creamy Noodles, but in my opinion, the rice pairs far better with the cutlet. I’ve been raving about this place to friends and have every intention of returning.

A word to the wise: the spice levels here are not to be underestimated. Even self-proclaimed spice aficionados should proceed with caution, as my friends and I learned firsthand, battling through the sweat at level 1 spice. If you’re sensitive to heat, don't hesitate to ask for a milder experience.

Title: Cozy Corner for Comforting Thai Classics in Hell's Kitchen

Nestled in the bustling streets of Hell's Kitchen, this gem offers a culinary retreat for both the solo diner and groups seeking a heartwarming meal. Their oxtail soup is a star on the menu; a hearty concoction with a beefy punch and an abundance of herbs, best enjoyed with sticky rice as a delightful alternative to the regular serving. The staff's warmth only adds to the restaurant's charm, a trait that has cemented its status in the neighborhood.

The Tom yum noodle soup is solid, with the squid salad standing out as a personal favorite—both generous in size, making them perfect for sharing. Their latest addition, the beef and beef ball noodle soup, is a revelation with its mouthwatering tender beef so soft it nearly falls apart at the touch. Paired with egg noodles—or other noodles of your choice at no extra cost—and some chili vinegar and chili sauce, it's an experience not to be missed.

Affordability is the cherry on top here, with prices noticeably lower than other local Thai spots, especially for the rare finds like their beef ball noodle soup. Whether you're seeking the simplicity of a solo meal or the jovial spirit of shared dining, this unassuming corner restaurant is a treasure to be savored.

I recently had the pleasure of visiting this delightful lobster truck, and I must say, their Maine lobster roll was a revelation. Served in a super soft, perfectly toasted bun, the roll let the star ingredient shine. Instead of being smothered in an array of fillings, the succulent lobster pieces were sweet and tender, allowed to bask in their own glory with just the right touch of butter. The butter sauce was rich and generous without overpowering the delicate seafood. While the lobster pieces were on the smaller side, the quality and flavor were unbeatable. For those seeking a pure and satisfying lobster experience, this truck is a must-try. It's no wonder I found it comparable, if not superior, to my usual go-to lobster roll. Highly recommended for any lobster aficionado!

Title: Authentic Italian Gem in the Heart of New York

Review:
I've found an Italian oasis in New York that I consider an all-time favorite. With three charming locations, this restaurant excels in creating a cozy ambiance reminiscent of a quaint eatery in Italy. The staff's sweetness and friendliness enhance the dining experience, ensuring every visit is delightful. 

The pasta here is a standout, always tasting as if it's been made from scratch with the utmost care, and their wine selection is thoughtfully curated, accommodating the most discerning of palates. Freshness is a theme, extending to their seafood offerings that are consistently impeccable. 

This spot is flawless in my eyes, and I'm always eager to bring friends and family to share in the experience. Word to the wise: it's a popular place, so be sure to book a reservation in advance.

SalaThai is a double-edged sword. On one hand, their bold, punchy spices redefine everything you've ever understood about flavor. The downside is that you likely won't be able to enjoy anything for at least 24 hours--anything you ingest afterwards will be far too bland in comparison. Still, I could think of no better way to break what had been a month-long hiatus from Thai.Thai crepe dumplings (5/5): If you're looking for an app to impress, look no further. These violet-tinged beauties are an explosion of sweet, salty, nutty, crunchy and tangy thanks to the minced chicken, water chestnut, peanut,and tamarind mixture tucked within. They're also gluten-free and 100% all-natural! Don't believe me? The slippery soft skins are rice-based and naturally dyed with the extract of butterfly pea tea which give them their purple hue! Pla Muk Yang (5/5): The charred octopus was an equally strong contender for an impressive app. The color on the octopus was perfection. Each skewer bore 3 succulent pieces of tender tentacle flavored with a salty-tangy fish sauce mixture. Khao Soi (4/5): Albeit being a tad too acidic for me thanks to the generous topping of pickled veggies and lime, there was no denying the heartiness of this curry noodle soup. In addition to the pickled greens, the bowl was topped with my choice of protein (beef), soybean sprouts, red onion, dried chiles, scallion and fried garlic. Pad Ped Hoy Darb (5/5): This entree was just as much of a stunner as the appetizers. I was skeptical of SalaThai's portion sizes at first, but was convinced otherwise as soon as this dish hit the table. There were tons of razor clams, hidden between the shells--don't let the number of shells fool you! Moreover, the basil-infused curry sauce it was sautéed with was unforgettable. The sauce probably could have been diluted with a few extra cups of water and the dish would still be tasty. Medium spicy brought plenty of heat. If we hadn't already stuffed ourselves full of apps, we probably would have inhaled a few extra bowls of rice drowned in that addicting curry sauce. Thai Medley (5/5): To soothe our chili-stung tongues, we ordered their housemade pandan and coconut ice cream.  This dessert was served in a coconut shell along with sweetened red bean, young coconut strips and jackfruit. It was a delight to admire and to eat! Thai Iced Tea (5/5): Creamy, sweet, strong. A classic must-try drink at any Thai establishment. SalaThai is a must if you're in the area. Put down this review and make your dinner reservation now!

When I tell y'all THE BEST fish tacos are birthed here. Believe it! Authentic deliciousness. I tried the shrimp and did not realize they come battered (I'd prefer they not) and they were just okay to me. The fish however... is the reason ill return. This was a Taco Tuesday success.

I think I've liked everything I've ordered every time I'm here! Great place for brunch, lunch, or dinner so basically any meal any time of the day. I highly recommend the mac and cheese (cheese pull goals ofc), braised short rib pasta, smores jar, toffee pudding, and birthday cake. The desserts here are so decadent and perfect for any occasion (birthdays, anniversaries, or if you're having a bad day and want a pick-me-up). Give this place a try!

Title: A Hidden Gem Worth the Detour

Having dined at this charming spot twice, I've become quite taken with its allure. Nestled down a shady alley, do not be deterred by its unassuming exterior, as inside awaits a cozy and inviting atmosphere with just the right amount of low lighting to set the perfect tone for a romantic date.

Their cocktail menu shines, especially the Dirty Martini adorned with blue cheese olives—a must-try for enthusiasts. But the true star of the show is undoubtedly the burger, ranking high as one of the city's finest. Amp it up with bacon and you'll understand why it's a non-negotiable for any visit here. However, take my advice and skip the fries; the burger itself is ample.

To round off the meal, indulge in the salted caramel gelato for a sublime finish. And a word to the wise—booking a reservation is key to bypassing the wait and diving straight into this delightful dining experience.

That damn Jack better appreciate Freda because that food was fuqn delicious, clean and satisfying. Real talk I wanted to order another of something else but was on my way to cycle under water (that's a different review) so I felt I should be good. I loved seeing everyone gather to break bread and toast each other up. It was a page out of modern day "Sex and the City ".... oooh oooh...I'm blaque Samantha. LMFAO.

Title: Satisfying Weekday Lunch at Spacious Eatery

I stopped by this restaurant for a lunch date on a non-busy Monday at noon. The vast interior, including a second floor and outdoor seating, almost guarantees a seat even during a lunch rush, though I'd wager it sees more action during happy hours.

The lunch menu boasts an array of specials ranging from $10-$13, pleasing for both wallet and palate. I savored a Double Cheeseburger with delectably crisp, house-cut fries, cooked to a near-perfect medium without prompting. My wife enjoyed a moist Grilled Chicken Sandwich complemented by a flavorful Tomato Soup.

Service was decent but somewhat slow considering the sparse crowd. We wrapped up in under an hour, which was ideal.

Rating this place at 3.5 stars for a good meal and plenty of space—worth a visit for those midday hunger pangs.

We went to spoon this am and it was SO GOOD. It was a bit hard to find. They don't have visible outdoor signage, so we thought it didnt exist.  At 10:30am on a Sunday we were able to score a high top without a reservation. Needless to say, they absolutely shine for brunch. I ordered the fried chicken and waffles (sans gravy), my boyfriend ordered the biscuits and gravy skillet. Solid 10/10 for both. Mimosa carafe was a great deal, and nice way to top off such a delicious meal. I highly recommend coming here for brunch, and I personally cant wait to return.
This place has delicious food! I ordered on grub hub so I can't commit on the actual facility but our delivery was fast and accurate!

Tucked away near Chinatown, my Saturday brunch at Au Cheval Diner was a delightful discovery. The highlight was their 'single' cheeseburger, which, contrary to its name, featured a double helping of succulent patties. Elevating the experience, I opted for an indulgent addition of bacon and egg – a decision I'd recommend to any diner. Accompanying my burger with a side of crispy fries and aioli was a wise choice, as they aren't included but are quite the savory treat.

It's no wonder the burger reigns supreme here; glance around, and you'll find it gracing almost every table, just like the tantalizing nachos that caught my eye for a future visit. The staff's warmth added to the charm, though their busyness meant a bit of effort was required to catch their attention for orders or the bill.

Despite this minor hiccup, Au Cheval's allure is undeniable. I'm already planning to return with friends. For a standout burger and more, this diner gets my hearty recommendation.

Jin Ramen is a restaurant known mostly for its different types of ramen, ranging from traditional styles like shoyu to more adventurous styles like Thai curry. There are plenty of options for one to choose and the prices are not really unreasonable, as they may be slightly higher than your typical ramen place in NYC depending on where you go. Having many options is great for someone who has tried plenty of traditional ramen and would like something new. Otherwise, for a ramen newcomer, it might be better to go for a traditional ramen like shoyu or tonkotsu to venture into the food genre.I got the miso ramen, which uses a chicken broth with a miso base. The toppings included chopped chashu, chicken sausage, corn, bean sprouts, bok choy, and a soft boiled egg. The broth was quite savory and not too salty while still providing a slight spicy kick. Although the menu says there are two chili pepper signs, I'd say it's not that spicy for someone with an average spice tolerance like myself, as the spice is not overbearing to the point where one may need more water. Overall, the ramen was quite good, though I would like more noodles that would capture the broth better. Maybe thicker noodles would help as well, so that I can enjoy the taste of the broth with the noodles. With the ingredients used in the miso ramen, it was hard to eat everything with just my chopsticks and it required using the large soup spoon (which I do think should be used in other ramen places) to fish out the bits of chashu, chicken sausage, and corn hiding in the broth somewhere. However, despite how tedious the task of using my spoon continuously may be, the ramen itself was enjoyable and left me content.Jin Ramen is a solid option if you have a ramen craving, especially if you're in the area, considering a lot of the more well known ramen places are in midtown or below. They have a lot of variety and are good at what they do.

Title: A Late-Night Culinary Delight at Au Cheval

Despite the hiccup of a late 10:30pm reservation and no way to directly contact the restaurant, Au Cheval completely won us over with a seamless and scrumptious dining experience.

Upon arrival, we were promptly seated, even a few minutes ahead of schedule. Eager to dive into the menu, we opted for a shared Kale Caesar for starters and their renowned Cheeseburger with an extra slice of Thick Cut Bacon. A frothy root beer on draft kicked off the meal.

It's worth mentioning that the "Single Cheeseburger" deceives with its double patty richness, while the "Double" is quite the triple threat. The burger was a standout, masterfully cooked and seasoned, and while the bacon was a nice touch, it proved unnecessary — the burger alone commanded the spotlight.

Set in a modern, trendy ambiance with prices hovering around $18-$20 for a burger, Au Cheval is an excellent choice for a date night or a casual outing with friends. Coupled with attentive service, this spot is a must-visit for burger aficionados. I'm already planning my next visit.

I recently visited this restaurant for the Super Bowl, and while the space was accommodating for our large reserved table, the service left much to be desired. Despite the expected Super Bowl crowd, the restaurant seemed understaffed, and it was difficult to flag down one of the few servers on hand.

The nachos I ordered were quite tasty, a highlight of the evening. However, my experience at the bar was disappointing. The bartender was unfamiliar with a vodka gimlet, and despite my instructions, what I received bore little resemblance to the classic cocktail, proving to be watery and improperly mixed.

While my friends had chosen this venue for the event, I was underwhelmed by the level of preparation for such a busy night, particularly at the bar. Unfortunately, I don't see myself returning, especially if I'm in the mood for a well-crafted drink.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Ramen Delights in NYC

As a seasoned ramen enthusiast, I've slurped my way through numerous bowls across New York City and recently found myself at a new spot that caught my attention. The service here immediately set a positive tone—friendly waiters and complimentary water were a pleasant start, and the swift arrival of my ramen was impressive.

Diving into the miso ramen, however, left my taste buds yearning for more. The broth lacked the depth and 'spark' that I've relished in other establishments, and the oddly flavored bamboo shoots were a misstep. The absence of mushrooms in my bowl was also a letdown.

But not all was lost; the saving graces of the meal shone through. The pork was exceptionally tender and the egg was cooked to a delightful consistency. Yet, it was the garlic oil provided on the side that truly transformed my experience. This remarkable condiment, when drizzled into the broth, elevated each spoonful into a flavorsome journey.

While the ramen itself was merely decent, the allure of that garlic oil is enough to beckon me back for a future visit. Perhaps next time, the rest of the bowl will rise to meet the high bar it sets.

Upon initially dining at this restaurant, my expectations for their much-hyped pizza were met with disappointment; the crust's excessive thickness evoked the heft of a bread bowl rather than the traditional pizza foundation I had anticipated. Despite my initial misgivings, the pizza's flavor profile was undeniably well-balanced, providing a harmonious blend of ingredients that lingered pleasantly in my memory. Even now, the thought of that pizza with its unique characteristics tempts my palate, hinting that perhaps it was not so overrated after all.

Tucked away just around the corner from my place, the buzz around this local eatery had reached my ears through enthusiastic friends and colleagues. Expecting much, I decided to drop by and was met with an experience that was both surprising and slightly underwhelming.

Where they truly shine is in their beverage offerings – their tea selection is nothing short of impressive, featuring an array of choices including a delightful vanilla chai that quickly became my favorite. When it comes to food, the scone specials stand out, especially with inclusive options like the vegan, gluten-free banana, and the indulgent caramel pecan, though I must admit, the quality does vary.

The egg white omelette with its unique side of pears and asparagus is a testament to their creativity, and their pancakes are next on my list to try. That said, if you're pressed for time, this might not be your best option; service can be a tad slow, certainly not helped by the cozy confines of the place that seems to prolong the dining experience unexpectedly.

Despite the desire for a more expansive menu and faster service, this spot is a solid find in the heart of New York City. It's a place that beckons for repeat visits – just make sure you're not in a hurry. Highly recommended for those seeking quality food and a vast tea selection.

This was my first time seeing a bar tucked inside a department store! With views of the Vessel across the street, Bar Stanley was definitely a cool spot for drinks. Came here with four friends for a drink on a Saturday after climbing the Vessel. The bar was a little hard to find, but we eventually found our way with some help from employees. They had a great drinks menu! I had the "Good Buy" (Belvedere, cucumber, butterfly flower extract, lemon, aquavit, sparkling water) and it was fantastic! It was a light and sweet drink, and it was definitely strong. I also had a sip of my friend's "Mrs. Malaprop" and really loved the taste of it and how unique it was. They also served some bar snacks, which we definitely appreciated because it was almost dinner time and we were starting to get hungry.  Taste | 4.5Atmosphere | 4Presentation | 4.5Service | 4OVERALL | 4.5

Title: Disappointing Portions and Lackluster Flavors

I swung by this spot with high hopes after seeing glowing reviews, but sadly my experience fell flat. First off, the wonton soup was a letdown; at $8, I expected more than what barely filled a cup - and only discovering this after I got home due to the staples sealing the to-go bag added salt to the wound.

The XLB (soup dumplings) I tried cost over $8 for six pieces, which seemed steep considering they lacked the signature brothiness. They had decent dough and meat, but failed to wow my taste buds. The highlight, though, was the unique dipping sauce - a sweet soy variety that was a pleasant departure from the usual vinegar.

While the staff was amiable and the service quick, the requirement to spend $20 just to pay with card felt excessive. In sum, if you're after value and authentic flavors, you might want to skip this place and hunt down a more unassuming eatery that delivers on both counts.

I was really looking forward to this place because of the reviews but unfortunately I was disappointed. The breakfast options were lacking (only maybe 6-8 different options) and the service was subpar. There were no real heathy options besides the açaí bowl so someone ordered the buffet for $25 for just the oatmeal. We needed to get the attention of one of the waiters to order after we sat there for too long and he also told us he'd bring milk for the coffee but never did. The food was decent and the presentation was good, however.

I came here last night with a group of friends and I will say I was very disappointed this time around. I usually go here on a week day and whenever I come my experience is relatively good. However, last night was my first time going on a Saturday night so even though I was anticipating it'll be busy, I was not expecting it to be so disorganized. So the first thing I will say that's frustrating about this place, is that they don't take reservations, if this place gets really packed during a Friday or Saturday night and a large party wants to come, it would make sense to offer the option to reserve a table. So it was going to be eight of us and my friend was the first one to arrive so she put her name down and asked how long the wait would be for eight people. One of the hostess said it would depend on the time everyone in the party shows up. So the first half of us were there and then we waited 45 minutes for our other friends to arrive. After everyone was there, they then told us we had to wait two more hours in addition to the 45 minutes we were already waiting. So I asked the one of the hostesses what is the point of taking people's names down just to tell them they have to wait the same time if they weren't here. She gave me some BS answer. I also didn't appreciate the other hostess' the blonde one's attitude either, it sucked. So to my frustration I told her to take our name off the wait list, which she already did before I even told her to. We left and decided to go to somewhere better and less crowded. The reason why I'm leaving 3 stars and not 2 is because I like the food and usually my other dining experiences here have been more positive, but this was very off-putting. I hope they either eventually start taking reservations or create a better system when it comes to sitting people during a busy nights.

Needed a good tasting homemade soup. One that would be useful for a person getting over the flu. Ordered the cauliflower soup (soup of the day) and it was a HOME RUN. Very flavor and fresh. You could taste the spices and everything was well balanced. Definitely not a disappointment. I've eaten here and ordered from here many times and I can't say I've had a disappointing meal from here. Very reliable and satisfying

Basic Chinese bakery with no frills service and lots of tasty treats, from taro and red bean buns to bbq pork buns steamed. Self service on most,  and cash only business. Bubble tea and coffee available,  too. They also do cakes,  less sweet than the French or American versions.

Title: A Sangria Worth the Reunion!

If you find yourself wandering through the bustling market on a sizzling summer day, do your friendships a favor and lead them to Mercado Little Spain after your tour, just as my long-lost friends and I did. With the anticipation of our Vessel visit ticking away, we sought refuge inside the mall and stumbled upon this hidden Spanish gem – though you'll need a keen eye, as signage is sparse. Hint: if you're coming from the Vessel side, swing a right, dodge the store distractions, and descend the stairs to your oasis.

Our serendipitous find was crowned with a pitcher of Sangria de Cava Zahara that carried a hefty $60 tag – a price that initially had our eyes wide. But let me tell you, as we clinked glasses and rekindled stories of old, the cost faded into insignificance. It wasn't just a pitcher of sangria; it was an elixir of nostalgia, laughter, and the perfect antidote to our sun-drenched fatigue.

In every effervescent sip, laced with the perfect balance of fruit and sparkle, there was consensus: it was worth every cent. Whether you're reconnecting with old pals or just need a lavish liquid escape, this sangria won't just quench your thirst – it'll be a highlight of your day. Cheers to that!

During a recent trip to NYC, I decided to drop by Ahhh Wah Fung, a spot I discovered on 'subtle asian traits.' To my delight, the eatery wasn't crowded, and we scored our food in under five minutes.

Our large group was a test for the lone hustling worker, who gracefully handled our continual orders, even as we sprung new requests just when he thought he was done. His patience didn't waver, even as I timidly practiced my Cantonese while ordering.

We ambitiously sampled nearly everything on the menu, opting for various portion sizes. My personal highlight was splitting a BBQ pork, chicken, and duck combo with a friend. At $7 total, this was a bargain feast for two. The BBQ mirrored the high quality of similar spots in the San Gabriel Valley, yet the prices were unbeatably low.

The only hiccup was navigating through the loose bones in the duck. However, the BBQ pork was exceptional – lean yet bursting with flavor. A pro tip for anyone visiting: the BBQ pork rice in a small portion is the perfect pick for a satisfying snack or light meal. At under $10, you could even double up with another dish and leave full without breaking the bank.

I was looking for a new place to try near union square and stumbled upon this place while looking online. Excited to try Singaporean food!If this was just based on the food, it would be 4 stars no issues, but service knocked it down a bit.I made a reservation for 2 at 8:15PM on a Friday night. We arrived on time and saw a huge crowd waiting. We made our way to the table and no hostess was sighted. The place appeared understaffed. About 10 minutes later, someone came back to the table. I let them know I had a reservation for 8:15 but was told they'll get to me as soon as they seat this other party. This person didn't even ask for my name to see if I actually had one. I then proceeded to ask another person who actually checked me in. There was another 15 minute wait before we actually got seated.Once we sat down, we looked at the menu. We ordered Singapore lesak, chicken satay and hainanese chicken.The chicken satay came out 10 minutes later and boy was it delicious! The chicken was juicy and chunky, and the peanut sauce on it was great with a slight kick to it. Almost made me want to get a few more orders.The Singapore lesak came out next. The noodles was splendid on a cold Friday night. The chicken and soup had a good spice to it that warmed you up. Definitely something to warm you up if you're chilly!The hainanese chicken came out last and was a disappointment. The chicken was slightly bland and didn't have much flavor. The rice that it came with was better than the chicken. Honestly think I wasted $22 on this dish.The food overall was good, but combined with terrible service made for a worser experience than it should've been. I would try this place again just to see if there's any changes.

Chicken Yunnan Crossing Bridge with Tomato Soup ($20): The crossing bridge noodle with tomato soup is a new flavor aside from their signature crossing bridge noodle soup, so I decided to give it a try and I ABSOLUTELY LOVED the tomato soup. It was so flavorful with just the perfect amount of sweetness. It was so smooth and kind of creamy that I think this is one of the best tomato soup based noodles I've ever had. It also came with an assortment of fish, shrimp, squid, fried pork, and chicken meat along with veggies, eggs, and rice noodles, which were mixed in altogether by the waiter who served the dish. It felt like I was eating a really good tomato soup based hot pot with fluffy rice noodles! I also appreciated how they brought out the toppings in small dishes separated from the pot of soup and then poured each one into the pot to demonstrate the traditional origin of the crossing bridge noodle from Yunnan province. Dry Tofu Pudding Rice Noodle ($14): The dry tofu pudding rice noodle was very unique yet delicious. The tofu pudding mixed with minced pork along  with veggies was sooo yummy. It tasted similar to dan dan noodles but softer texture and less spicy. The noodle had sooo much meat but it felt very light because of the tofu pudding. I recommend this if you want to try something new! Crispy Fried Pork ($8): Fried pork belly was crispy and seasoned well with black pepper and garlic powder that it tasted kind of similar to popcorn chicken. I was hesitant to try the ketchup based sauce on the side, but it was actually pretty good as it added a sweet and sour kick to it. Braised Pig Feet ($7): The sauce was thick and flavorful while the meat was chewy. It met my expectations for this classic side dish! Milky Rice ($6): Tried this one as the waiter recommended it as a traditional Yunnan dessert. It tasted like rice porridge but with a smoothie texture, and had a hint of sweetness from the milk. I never had anything like this before but I actually enjoyed it. Even though the crossing bridge noodle soup is slightly pricey, the portion was huge for both noodle dishes. They give you a lot of veggies, meat, and rice noodles that I think one noodle dish will definitely make one person very full. Food also came out very quickly and staffs were very friendly. Inside is pretty spacious with many tables and there are some bar tables that accommodate solo visitors as well. I would definitely make another trip here to try more traditional Yunnan dishes! TIP: check-in on Yelp for one free dessert!

I have mixed feelings about this place.  We came for a celebratory lunch and decided on the AYCE BBQ... (not worth it) - don't expect Ktown KBBQ, you will surely be disappointed by 1000%. Barn Joo took over, what I think was the old "Heartland Brewery"... the decor is nice and spacious with 2 floors.  Relatively empty for lunch hour... and we found out why.  The service... what service?!? Took forever to get water, refill, sparkling water, extra ban-chans, Kim Chi, scallion mix, extra meat... so basically everything.   Our waiter was sooooo absent, at one point we got up and grabbed a new bottle of water ourselves. The food is decent, we liked the spicy wings and fried dumplings. For AYCE, we ordered: Ribeye, Pork Belly and Kalbi patty (1st round), ribeye & pork belly is ok, not the best quality of meat.. but the kalbi patty was like eating a regular hamburger. It was gross.  2nd round, ribeye, shrimp and bulgogi.  Do Not Get the Bulgogi!! What's a sloppy mess of destroyed beef. It was not visually appealing. The shrimp was dry (as expected). 3rd round, ribeye, pork belly and pork shoulder. Honestly, by the time we got our meat refill, we were 90% full because we sat and waited like 20 mins in-between rounds.  Because our waiter is absentminded, didn't give a shit or perhaps that's their "AYCE strategy" - make you full with air.  For AYCE - order Ribeye & pork belly. Decent. I think we might give it another try but probably just the a-la-cart menu. Really iffy by this experience but perhaps it will be different for regular dining.

I knew I was going to love this restaurant as soon as I saw the cute terrace that you could eat outside on. Walking in, it does feel like you're transported to the 1920s. I absolutely loved the neighborhood this restaurant is in as well as the decor. The restaurant is surprisingly spacious. As mentioned, there's an outside eating area, a long bar, and then several tables inside. I was pleasantly surprised by how extensive the menu was. We ordered the crab and pork xiao long bao (soup dumplings), drunken chicken, fried buns, fish, and two bowls of rice for three people. Every dish sounded delicious (especially the appetizers), and we had a hard time deciding what to order, so our server gave us his recommendations. Speaking of the service, it was incredible. Our dishes came out so quickly, and I appreciated that they provided new plates for us before the entree. I saw in other reviews that the portions are small, but I thought the appetizers were average-size, and our one main entree (Fish Blossom) was more than enough to feed three people. I would absolutely come back to try more dishes!

Regrettably, my experience at this much-raved-about dessert spot was underwhelming. Marketed as a chocolate lover's paradise, it fell short with its mediocre offerings that came with a hefty price tag. Service was disappointingly sluggish; our server seemed to have misplaced her sense of urgency, particularly as we were seated upstairs and appeared to slip from her attention. Adding to the frustration, there was a puzzling sequence where our food arrived prior to our beverages. My hot chocolate, a supposed specialty, was served lukewarm and tipped the scales on sweetness, throwing balance out the window. This establishment is a classic tourist trap, and I'm unable to recommend it to those seeking a delightful dessert experience.

Place was really cool. Cool entrance and the lobsters on the first floor are cool to see. For a place that yelp lists as family friendly they had a Very limited menu and for sure nothing specifically for the kids. Would only recommend for adults. Concept is cool and food is delicious. We got oysters for an app, and then the lobster po boy and a burger. Both were phenomenal. Our waiter was just okay - seemed to be in a rush to flip the table. Neat concept - would recommend.

Wow. After eye balling this place for a couple of days I finally had the pleasure of having dim sum at the " Dim Sum Palace". And yes, it lived up to the hype. The dim sum here is phenomenal. Never have I ever been so satisfied with dim sum.We ordered shu mai , seafood shu Mai, har gow (shrimp), Chinese broccoli , crispy garlic spareribs and fried squid. Everything was soo good . That dipping sauce was life. We literally kept asking our waiter to refill the chili paste because we like it with a little kick. Definitely a go to if you're in the mood for some good dim sum. Can't go wrong with anything in the menu since everything we ordered was delicious !

Boka is such a great addition to Chinatown ! Just between the busy streets Boka serves up amazing korean chicken! Soy garlic wings are a  must to get  here, delicious and so crispy. The food comes out fast and hot. Pair it with a cold beer which they have many on tap and to offer. I also highly recommend getting the tofu soup. Especially after a cold day outside, the spicy soup warms you from within Service and interior was amazing. Staff was extremely nice and attentive. And interior was nicely decorated. Love the seating arrangements near the window, can definitely fit larger groups in this restaurant!Definitely will be returning to try their watermelon soju. A bit on the expensive side so it is great to  share with a group!

Title: A Delightful Omakase Date Night

My girlfriend and I chose this spot for our Friday dinner date, eager to indulge in their omakase experience. The presentation did not disappoint – an enticing array of sushi served simultaneously, with instructions to enjoy from left to right. The journey through each piece was like a symphony of flavors, leaving us both savoring every bite until the very last.

We did notice that service lagged slightly, which could be attributed to the restaurant's spacious layout. Despite this, the quality of the food and the inviting ambiance made up for the wait.

Overall, if you're looking for a romantic evening with exquisite sushi, this restaurant is a solid choice. The omakase offering won't disappoint, and the experience is well-suited for a special date night. Highly recommended for couples seeking to relish a culinary adventure together.

I had just finished my driving lessons in the neighborhood and was STARVING. On my way home, I walked by a little Thai restaurant that seemed new and was eager to give it a try. The moment I stepped in, I felt fantastic! The fast restaurant was bright, spacious, clean, and simple. Just my type. It's minimalistic, yet comforting and welcoming at the same time.The two women working there were kind, attentive, eager to answer any questions I had, and made the process simple and quick. I was in and out in ~5 minutes. I got the three entree lunchbox with purple sticky rice (+ $1), pork jerky, broccoli/zucchini/brussel sprouts, and chicken curry. All of which were VERY delicious. Even my boyfriend (Thai food fanatic) approved.The only thing that I'm iffy about with the whole thing was the price tag. It was $15.19 for the lunch box, which I would say should have been $11 - $12 max. Definitely stop by for some quick and delicious Thai food if you're in the neighborhood, though!

Title: Mazete: A Fresh and Flavorful Twist to Flatiron's Quick-Serve Scene

In the wake of minigrow's exit from the NYC quick-serve noodle scene, Mazete slides into the Flatiron district with a proposition that hits all the right notes for the health-conscious and flavor-seeking diner. Its bowl-centric menu brims with enticing protein options, such as curried egg salad and crispy shrimp tempura, catering to a variety of tastes and dietary preferences.

The choice to mix and match—going full noodle, half salad and half noodles, or all greens—is a welcome nod to carb counters without sacrificing the rich, Asian-inspired taste profiles. The egg ramen noodles, served al dente, provide a satisfying chew, though beware, you might find yourself yearning for an extra dash of sauce to evenly coat each strand.

Opting for tofu stew as the base protein, supplemented with hearty toppings like curried egg and tempura, results in a protein-packed bowl that doesn't skimp on flavor—or spice, thanks to the zesty kick from the spicy nuts.

While you might need to allot a little extra time to navigate the line, the plush seating ensures a comfortable spot to dive into your customized noodle creation. The only misstep? An absence of on-the-side condiments—a splash of hot sauce would elevate the experience, ensuring every bite is as robust as the last in this otherwise delicious addition to the local fast-casual dining landscape.

Title: A Mixed Experience at Ippudo

My latest visit to Ippudo was a journey of hits and misses. As a seasoned Ippudo patron, my expectations were high, but the miso akamaru ramen fell short. This special seasonal offering missed the mark with its overly salty broth lacking the usual depth I relish at Ippudo. On the flip side, the pork baos shined bright; their perfectly tender filling wrapped in buttery, irresistibly soft buns.

Despite the ramen setback, the service was swift and efficient, a testament to the staff's skill at navigating the bustling weekend dinner crowd. The ambiance, as always, was a delight. I'd definitely give Ippudo another chance, eager to pick a different bowl from their usually stellar menu.

Title: Pleasant Brunch Experience with Great Drink Deals

I finally visited this well-talked-about brunch spot with a couple of friends, and the experience was quite pleasant. We strolled in around 1pm, and to our delight, there was no wait for a table—a definite plus in the bustling city.

Our server was extremely cordial, though a tad forgetful, which was easily overlooked given her kind demeanor. The food was satisfactory; while it didn't top my list of brunch favorites in the city, it was enjoyable nonetheless. However, the Bloody Mary shined as a standout, boasting a flavor profile that justified its $9 price tag.

What truly caught my eye was the bottomless brunch offering—for a mere $20, one can indulge in endless mimosas or Bloody Marys, a deal I'm eager to return for. Additionally, the prospect of food happy hour specials is enticing, especially since the French fries I spotted at another table seemed scrumptious.

I'm already planning a future visit to delve into the drink specials and nibble on those promising fries.

Was looking for some good eats before a show and wasn't willing to wait 4 hours to get into Rubirosa. Lucked out and snagged a Resy here and happy I did. The place was great, service was prompt and helpful and the vibe of the place was very cute and fun. My girlfriend and i shared the escargot, the tartare, and the Branzino and all were fantastic. The tartare was up there with some of the best I've had. We enjoyed two bottles of wine as assisted by our server who was fun and friendly. I highly recommend!

Title: An Intriguing Tasting Experience at Day One of Restaurant Week

I recently had the opportunity to dine during the first day of restaurant week at an establishment with a concept as intriguing as it is confusing. The menu is tiered, akin to the style of an afternoon tea, allowing patrons to sample a variety of the restaurant's culinary offerings. While the format took a moment to wrap one's head around, the food itself did not disappoint; each dish was flavorful and evidently crafted with care.

Before sitting down to this unique dining experience, I visited the bar. Note to prospective diners: the bar requires payment upfront, even for signature drinks that are part of a promotional discount. The cocktail prices are on the steep side, with most at $28, but a selection from the special menu will save you $8.

As for the ambiance, it was nothing short of beautiful—a perfect setting for a special occasion. However, be prepared for a sizable bill; my meal came to $42, and unfortunately, the portions were on the smaller side, leaving me slightly hungry afterward.

In summary, if you're looking to sample exquisitely prepared food in a stunning setting and don't mind spending a bit for the experience, this restaurant certainly delivers. Just remember it may be more suitable for a lighter meal or special outing rather than your go-to for a hearty dinner.

Title: A Cheesy Delight at Flip'n Toss

My cravings led me to Flip'n Toss, lured in by their mouthwatering Instagram posts in search of the ultimate Mac n cheese. Their version perfectly hits the spot – the cheese was ideally sharp and seasoned, with just the right consistency.

I indulged in the build-your-own concept, adding lobster and shrimp to my Mac n cheese. The shrimp, bathed in garlic butter, was a highlight and generously portioned. The lobster, however, fell short in both quantity and value; next time, I'd skip it for another topping adventure instead.

Aside from Mac n cheese, they have burgers that caught my eye for a future visit. The space is cozy, so it's best enjoyed in a small group or solo. With a welcoming service, delicious food, and fair prices, Flip'n Toss has earned itself a spot on my go-back-to list.

Pretty good Korean restaurant in KTOWN NY.  They do serve brown rice but I was a little disappointed that they only have spicy Galbitung instead of the traditional ones in the stone pot.  Good side dishes, on the third floor and the restaurant is on the quiet side, probably a pretty good place for chit chat or dates.

Came here without too much expectation other than knowing that this is a place I wanted to try. Came in to get the Japanese curry noodle and the volcano tonkatsu ramen.The japanese curry ramen, was meh. It wasn't anything special in either direction. What was really good was the tonkatsu ramen. Wow, I really loved the noodles there. (They use two different noodles between the two dishes). The noodles were were not too firm, but still soft enough to slurp down. I was really pleasantly surprised. The broth had a ton of flavor and there was a circular mount of spice in the ramen so you could help control when and how much spice. The pork was ok in it, but the noodles and broth were just so good.I'd come back here for the ramen no question. One of my favorite spots in the city

A group of my colleagues and I had a wonderful meal at Per Se! You truly feel like you're dining in New York's finest. The food was incredible, especially the Oysters and Pearls course. Our only real complaint was that the waiter kept accidentally pouring both still and sparkling water in our glasses.That aside, it was a fabulous meal. The wait staff was incredibly attentive and knowledgeable about Thomas Keller and his empire!

I recently visited a nearby restaurant and was thoroughly impressed by the experience. The food was delectable across the board. The servers and the bartender exuded warmth and friendliness, enhancing the overall ambiance. The highlight for me was the Dan Dan Mian noodles, which boasted a remarkable harmony of flavor and spice. Surprisingly, the dumplings were served in generous portions, a pleasant departure from the norm. Although the prices were a bit steep compared with nearby Chinatown options, the quality and service make a strong case for a return visit.

This place was totally cool and my part and I had a blast. Our server was super nice and accommodating- truly the best. She was all alone and was taking care of all of the tables for a while which wasn't her fault, but it did put a damper on things. The bartender was also a little slow - we were a party of about 6 and we all received our drinks in dribs and drabs. For all six drinks to come out it was probably about 20 minutes. Again not her fault, but seems to be more of a management piece. In addition to the service being super slow due to a lack of people serving tables, they only had 4 glasses for a party of 6. At one point couples were all sharing glasses until they were able to get us another two glasses. Glows:-Experience/Characters -Food was decently priced compared to what you got. -Drinks were strong, but comparable to the price of the drinks ($14 and up). -Friendly Staff-Food was hot although slow to come out. Grows:-Super small - I'm not sure how to fix this, but I guess relocate lol-Service was very slow and food/drinks didn't come out all at once which stinks because people go out to dinner and for drinks to have them with their party.  I would recommend coming here for the experience. Just know you may be sacrificing service for experience.

If you're on the hunt for authentic New York-style pizza, look no further than NY Pizza Suprema. Conveniently situated near Madison Square Garden, this pizzeria is the ideal spot for a quick bite of both classic and innovative pizza options. Be aware that it's a cash-only establishment, but with an ATM available at the start of the frequently formed line, you won't be inconvenienced.

While some may find the $4-6 price tag for a slice a tad on the higher side, the quality and taste justify the expense, making it a worthwhile culinary experience. My companion and I indulged in four different slices – the delectable Hot Honey, hearty Sicilian, timeless Cheese, and the savory White Garlic. Each slice was a testament to why NY Pizza Suprema has earned its stellar reputation. In summary, for a slice of the city's best, this is your go-to spot.

I loved everything about this place!! Definitely a must when in Manhattan. the atmosphere, seating, FOOD, and service were all amazing.I liked that the Jeju Chicken Wings ($14) came with pickles and a dip. 4.5/5I tried my friend's ramens: So Ramyun ($19), Gochu Ramyun ($18), and Truffle Kong Gook Su ($38). Each soup base had such a distinct, bold taste. The cold truffle noodles was nothing like I've ever had; light, yet creamy, truffle-y. 5/5

Gorgeous and sophisticated interior decor with a high ceiling, dazzling from top to bottom. I came here for a couple of my birthday dinners and the foods and desserts are well presented and mostly authentic. The portions are well sized and their drinks are excellent. Their menu is large and they have wide selection of food ranging from authentic street foods to northern Thai dishes such as my favorite Khao Soi to royal Thai cuisines and more. However their menu does change from time to time. They also have the popular Mango Sticky Rice and it is spot on.This place does get packed, including their bar seating, so reservations should be made ahead of time. However, if you come right after they open around 5pm to 6:30ish pm on the weekdays, there're plenty of seats available so it's pretty much a walk-in with no reservations required. Unfortunately, the hostess would not seat you unless all members of your party have arrived. Their restrooms are also very clean and well designed, giving off a nice villa vibe. The waitstaff and hostess are very friendly and efficient. Will definitely be back again.

Firstly, this restaurant appears to illegally charge a 4% surcharge to all customers opting to pay by credit card ("No seller in any sales transaction may impose a surcharge on a holder who elects to use a credit card in lieu of payment by cash, check, or similar means." N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law, Section 518). Make note, if you come here, you better pay in cash.Came here for the chicken soup dumplings. I like soup dumplings, but traditionally they're made with pork, which I do not eat. All of the dumplings we had here were pretty good, but I think the rest of the food was not all that spectacular. The sesame chicken was way too sweet, and the spicy dishes were not really spicy at all.Disappointed, probably will not return.

This is a new bar that just opened up on a great lively stretch of Bowery. They also happen to have a full menu of some great food that is definitely worth stopping in to try even if you don't drink.They just opened tonight and I stopped in to try a couple things. Start with the Guacamole ($10), which comes with Duros, these really great wheat flour crackers I've never actually seen in a restaurant before but always see all over Queens in huge bags hanging off street vendor carts.I also had the Story Burger ($18), Impossible style, which was really excellent and comes with perfectly crispy fries, and the Tlayuda ($18), a really great take on a Oaxacan style "pizza". I'll definitely be back to try the rest of the food and the brunch menu too.

**Restaurant Review: RW Summer 2016 Dining Experience**

**Rating: 3.5/5**

I wish there were half-star ratings to give a more nuanced review of my dining experience at the RW this summer. However, I'll round up my overall impression to a solid 3.5 stars.

**Venue:**
The ambiance of the RW is outstanding, with a striking staircase and luxurious tufted chairs set against the backdrop of an impressive chandelier. The glass-encased wine storage and electric fireplace contribute to the chic yet classic modern decor that surely catches one's eye.

**Service:**
Our experience began on a high note with a friendly waiter promptly taking our orders in the stunning dining hall. Despite being the sole diners initially, the service retained its warmth. However, our steaks required multiple redos to reach the desired doneness, which was a slight tarnish on the service's record. That said, the staff handled our requests professionally and without any hint of negativity.

**Food:**
The RW's food quality merits praise, particularly the bacon appetizer, which was thick, juicy, and delectable. The sides of broccoli and mashed potatoes were also commendable. Yet, when it comes to their steaks - the heart of a high-end steakhouse - they fell short in thickness and precision cooking. Our ribeye underwent two errors before arriving at a satisfactory medium doneness. While the flavors were enjoyable, it's worth noting that both the ribeye and filet mignon were unexpectedly thin. The dessert had its merits but left something to be desired in its presentation.

**Conclusion:**
Despite areas for improvement, particularly in attentive details and consistency, the RW provides a decent quality of food and service for the price, even during Restaurant Week. Restaurants should remember that this week often serves as a trial run for new customers, making meticulous care all the more critical. Thank you for reading this review.

I recently dined at a pleasant restaurant conveniently located within walking distance from nearby subway stations. The establishment offered ample seating, contributing to a comfortable dining experience. The menu featured enjoyable options, including delicious takoyaki, while the rice dishes were satisfactory. Complimentary water was a welcome touch.

Service was cordial, with staff members exuding a good attitude and maintaining a well-organized environment. Cleanliness was evident, and the provision of a restroom was appreciated. However, it's worth noting that meals are not rushed, so this may not be the ideal choice for a quick bite.

The ambiance suggests a place of comfort food, yet while the experience was agreeable, it lacked a distinctive edge to render it remarkable. Overall, a nice spot for a casual meal, albeit without the wow factor that commands a return visit.

Upon my recent visit to a moderately-sized local eatery, I took advantage of a discount through the Crave App – a nice perk though exclusive of other deals like Yelp check-ins or lunch specials. Speaking of which, the latter featured a duo of an appetizer and a main, from a somewhat narrow array of choices.

Opting instead for a regular menu item, I selected the green curry. The dish's volume didn't quite match the price, being heavily skewed towards bamboo shoots over scant chicken and eggplant. It did arrive with complimentary jasmine rice, a comforting addition. Flavor-wise, it leaned towards a sweeter, spicier profile.

However, the experience soured when witnessing the waitress's handling of a customer presenting a promotion – far from professional. My departure was swift post-meal, with the resolve that this dining experience would be my last at this establishment.

Title: A Deep-Dish Delight: First Impressions

As a first-timer venturing into the realm of Chicago-style deep dish pizza, my anticipation was met with sheer joy upon tasting the vegetarian pie adorned with green peppers and onions at this bustling yet cozy eatery. The luscious layers and robust flavors have truly set a new pizza precedent in my heart – a playful jest, as my New York pizza loyalty remains unwavering. The service mirrored the quality of the meal; attentive and pleasant. Do prepare for a brief wait as the no-reservations policy may require a 10-15 minute patience test, but rest assured, the experience is well worth it. Eagerly awaiting my next visit!

I recently dined at Au Cheval for the second time and unfortunately, I came away disappointed. The reservation process was frustrating, as my party had to wait 15 minutes past our booking time to be seated, despite other incomplete parties getting preference.

Service was lackluster; we struggled to get our waitress's attention for water, and her response felt dismissive, citing a "full restaurant" despite visible empty booths. The interaction was off-putting and set a negative tone for the meal.

As for the food, I had high hopes for the cheeseburger given my love for the sister restaurant's famed burger, but it fell short on both visits. The first encounter involved an oversalted patty and undercooked egg, while the second suffered from a severely underseasoned patty. The bun's propane-like odor was particularly off-putting, leading me to leave part of the burger untouched – a first for me.

The side of crispy potato hash with duck heart gravy was decent but not enough to salvage the overall experience. With a price tag over $40 for a meal that lacked in both service and substantial quality, I cannot recommend Au Cheval and will not be returning. My overall rating is 2.5/5.

Come for the menswear, stay for the refreshments and glorious service by Asa, Alfonzo & Paddy's whole fabulous team!!This delightful, upscale spot is located in the far west side of the men's department inside Neiman Marcus Hudson Yards.  There's plenty of seating between the bar area and two intimate nooks to the north and south of the space, as well as a handful of tables to the west that have a spectacular view of the vessel. There's another half dozen tables on the opposite side. Table and bar service available.The customized cocktails made in house are delicious and well worth the approximately $18 cost each.  Drinks come with a small assortment of specialty cocktail mix - , three distinct different flavors in a melded three-portion service.It's a delight to have adult beverages and service far away from the maddening, pedestrian crowds.What is unexpected in this swanky cocktail space is the delicious barfood. The guacamole is phenomenal as are the tacos. Shishito peppers are quite tasty as well!The service, the food, the beverages and atmosphere are all swanky without being pretentious. If you come appropriately attired and with an upscale, pleasant attitude, you'll fit right into this haven.  TL/dr: Upscale, hidden swanky drinks retreat.

Title: A Serendipitous Find at Flor De Mayo

Review:
Stumbling upon this bustling Flor De Mayo location instead of its Broadway sister was a delightful accident. Smaller and evidently more popular, the place thrummed with energy from the waiting crowd, but luckily, our party of two was swiftly seated.

Immediately, a busboy served us warm bread, a baguette to my delight, quelling the pangs of hunger. Swift service continued with our attentive waiter taking our orders promptly. I indulged in the pollo alla brasa, which lived up to my fond memories, offering tender, well-seasoned chicken that didn't disappoint. A generous taste of the lomo saltado from my dining companion's plate was revelatory; the steak's rich flavors melded perfectly with the grease-kissed fries, and the rice shared a delightful similarity to savory Chinese fried rice, accentuating the fusion vibe of the restaurant.

To wash it down, a glass of Rioja Spanish wine was a lovely complement, striking a balance of flavor without overwhelming dryness. As much as the offered flan tempted us, our satisfyingly full bellies necessitated a polite decline. This unexpected gem earns itself a spot on my list for a guaranteed revisit.

Tucked away in a quiet corner of the Upper East Side, this charming little Thai haven is an absolute delight. Despite its unassuming exterior, the fare here is nothing short of remarkable. Regular visits have introduced me to a parade of mouthwatering dishes, with the green curry chicken topping my list of favorites. The summer rolls are refreshing, but it's the basil ground chicken with a perfectly runny fried egg that has captured my heart—and taste buds—during my recent forays. The blend of savory basil and rich egg creates a flavor profile that's simply unforgettable. For anyone seeking a quick, satisfying Thai meal that promises fresh, quality ingredients and robust flavors, this spot is not to be missed. It's a culinary gem that consistently impresses.

Ahh, the hustle and bustle of NY at it's finest.  Located right off of Time Square this list one room store was packed!  If you have never felt like you were packed in a can of sardines before get ready.  I actually liked the setup.  It was authentic, true to the core.  Even when the guy dropped a couple of the doughs on the floor and didn't change his gloves!  I mean do you want authentic NY pizza or not!  You probably think I'm crazy for giving this place five stars after saying that, but honestly I do not care.  The pizza was absolutely delicious, and for a whole pie and 4 drinks it was right at $20.  Now tell me where you can get that with YUGE NY style slices hot hot hot.  As they say in the Bronx's, get outta here.  Cash is preferred and there is a minimum requirement if you want to use your card.  I think it was $20 actually.  Evidently everyone in NY does not want to pay the CC processing fee.  Who knew.  I added some photos!  Even though we just had the pepperoni, sometimes it's best to stick to the simple things, they had a wide variety of pizzas.  I really wanted to try the buffalo chicken, but I guess that is for another day!

I recently enjoyed a lunch at this spot on a quiet Monday and was pleased to find that seating was readily available. Our meal kicked off with buffalo wings that stood out for their desirable crispiness, alongside a fairly standard spinach and artichoke dip, slightly marred by an abundance of broken chips.

The highlight was the Big Cat burger - an impressive upgrade from their renowned Fat Cat, featuring extras like pulled pork, BBQ bacon, and a fried egg that complemented the already tasty ensemble of caramelized onions, American cheese, special sauce, lettuce, tomato, pickle, all sandwiched in an English muffin. This burger delivered on flavor and was expertly crafted.

The service matched the quality of the food, rounding out a satisfying dining experience.

Best.Food. Ever.Service is the only thing that was disappointing. Not the people who were bringing out the food or waiting on tables but the women who were seating us. They were very mechanical but lacked genuinity I thought. Cold. That's Sad because everything else was so perfect. Lychee mist and BELLE DE JOUR comes highly recommended.The spicy beef salad was extremely refreshing. It was spicy while being absolutely flavorful. The beef was the right texture with all the greens. Lemon addition was perfect.The ravioli was basically like a steamed spring roll. The filling was a tad less on seasoning and flavor but the minute you hit the dip that dish is magical. I like when flavor adds up and takes into account all the different parts of a dish. The shaking beef was tender and juicy and great. There not too many ingredients and that worked best for this dish. The ginger and scallion were the right additions.Ok so we don't like chicken esp in restaurants but we thought since this was a fancy establishment we would give it a try. The Saigon chicken was so good. The lemongrass hits all the right notes. That chicken is damn good and comes highly recommended. We had the lemon tart that is extremely tart (if you know what I mean) and it is perfect. The crust is thin and flaky and just right. The sorbets were good but I'm not a sorbet person so won't hold it against it.

Tucked away in the bustling heart of Korea town, I stumbled upon this Korean BBQ gem without the typical wait time, which was a pleasant surprise. The restaurant's layout spans two floors, with a dedicated sushi and entrees section on the ground level and the coveted BBQ grills upstairs, where we were seated.

The experience kicked off with a tasty miso soup followed by the main event, where we ordered bulgogi and another meat for the grill—a rule of two meats minimum in play. Portion sizes were generous, leaving us satisfyingly full.

What stood out was the service; unlike many places in New York, here the staff expertly cooks the meat for you, juggling between multiple tables with efficiency. As someone with Korean heritage who knows her BBQ, I must say, the flavors were top-notch—the best bulgogi I've ever had.

Side dishes were plentiful, though not my all-time favorites, they were still delicious and refillable. To cap off the meal, a slice of watermelon was served, a refreshing end to a gratifying dining experience. Overall, this spot holds its own amidst a sea of Korean BBQ options, and I'm definitely returning.

Title: A Disappointing Departure from the Hype

As an ardent fan of Korean cuisine, the discovery of a Korean restaurant nestled in the heart of Chinatown piqued my curiosity, especially with the rave online reviews it had garnered. However, my recent dining experience left me perplexed and at odds with the overwhelmingly positive feedback.

Despite the promise of an authentic Korean meal, our early weekday dinner was a letdown. The restaurant itself was notably quiet, a potential red flag. My choice of beef soon doo boo with the expectation of a spicy kick turned out to be a watery disappointment, lacking in both spice and flavor. Additionally, the shared kimchi pajun was reminiscent of dry cardboard rather than the usual savory pancake I've enjoyed elsewhere.

Furthermore, the banchan, normally a vibrant assortment of side dishes, was bland and forgettable. This was not the quality I anticipated; it was akin to subpar food court offerings masquerading as genuine Korean cuisine.

In an attempt to be fair, I've settled on a two-star rating rather than one, an acknowledgment of the ample portion sizes and the pleasant demeanor of the restaurant's host and hostess. Regretfully, this establishment falls short of a culinary delight, and I'm left to conclude that it is far from the four and a half star experience others have claimed it to be.

Title: Good Food, Service Could Improve

I visited this eatery on a bustling Saturday night with my fiancée and a friend. Despite the crowd, our reservation secured us immediate seating after grabbing the host's attention. There was a noticeable wait before we could order; we opted for a shared salad, pizza, and pasta. Unfortunately, all dishes arrived simultaneously after a lengthy wait, which was disappointing given that we intended the salad as a starter.

Culinary-wise, the fare was enjoyable. The four cheese pizza was tasty, albeit lacking a bit in gorgonzola for my liking. The service, while friendly, seemed stretched thin, impacting our overall experience. In a different company, the service gaps might have been more irksome. We had a pleasant evening, but the service issues nudged my rating to 4 stars.

Had an outstanding experience at Union Bar, largely thanks to Evyn, our impeccable waitress. Her warmth and attentiveness heightened our comfort and joy during the visit. Combined with the exquisite food, Union Bar's service is truly exceptional. Their efforts made my best friend's birthday celebration unforgettable. We're already looking forward to returning. Both the cuisine and service at Union Bar are remarkable and deserve high praise.

Title: A Gem of Culinary Delight

Walking into this restaurant, one is immediately struck by the impeccable aesthetics that are a prelude to the culinary excellence that awaits. The attention to detail is evident in every dish, each small in portion but crafted with such care it's difficult to choose a standout. The thoughtful twists on traditional presentations add a touch of excitement to the dining experience, making familiar flavors feel new and invigorating.

If I must recommend one must-try dish, it would be the snow mountain BBQ pork buns—these are simply divine. Be mindful that the prices are on the higher side, so it's best to visit with a group to enjoy a wider variety of dishes while sharing the cost. This restaurant is a true testament to the love of food and is not to be missed by those who appreciate culinary artistry.

Title: A Meatball Lover's Paradise on 9th!

My family and I stumbled upon this gem when we accidentally walked into the wrong location—yes, there are two on 9th, so pay attention to your reservation. Despite the mix-up, the staff was incredibly accommodating, seating us immediately with a warm welcome.

The restaurant's concept is truly unique, focusing entirely on meatballs. This specialization means that this spot is a dream for meatball enthusiasts but might not be the best choice for those who don't share the same affection for these savory spheres.

Our party sampled a variety of dishes, each centered around—you guessed it—meatballs. I'm pleased to report that everyone at the table found something to their liking, and not a single person left disappointed.

If meatballs are your thing, you can't go wrong with a visit to this cozy spot on 9th. Just make sure you're at the right one!

You know the saying "If you can't handle the heat, get out of the fire!" I'm a spicy fiend and I haven't found many places in my area that have legit spicy foods. Sigiri is the most unsuspecting place in the East Village. My friend recommended this place and I would have never though that this place was legit. I've been had Sri Lankan food so I was really excited.The space is small with one man serving the restaurant. My friend has been here before so I let him order. Our first dish was the Pork Black Curry. I love spicy and when my friend said to get this medium, I was shook! He said to trust him and i'm glad I did. At first bite, It wasn't spicy but it builds up. My mouth was on fire after a few more bites. Don't get me wrong, I enjoyed the burn and the curry was really tasty. If you can't handle spicy, say mild so you can actually taste the food. Our vegetable curry dish was also really good and spicy. The whole grain rice was just okay in my opinion but my friend is pre diabetic and can't eat white rice.The portions are a little on the small side and the two dishes were barely enough for the two of us. The service is real slow and the server was not attentive. Other than that, my first taste of Sri Lankan food was good. If you love spice, Sigiri is the way to go!

Title: Weeknight Surprises at the After-Work Hotspot

I ventured into what seemed like a typical Monday evening rendezvous with a friend, expecting a quiet spot for a bite and a sip. To my astonishment, I landed in a full-blown club atmosphere reminiscent of a vibrant Saturday night. Navigating through the crowd at around 6:30 PM, I faced a 10-minute queue just to enter – this place was buzzing to the brim.

The throngs inside were dense, yet surprisingly, the mood was congenial; not a single bump or shove met with a frown. Patrons, still in their work attire, contributed to the genuine after-work aura.

Admittedly, the drinks came without happy hour grace, a tad heavy on the wallet. My order of Hennessy and a Corona totaled $22, a price that might cause a double-take. But the famous frozen rum punch, setting me back another $10, did pack a delightful punch, its potency belying its frosty facade.

Amidst the revelry, dining took a backseat – the energy was just too magnetic to focus on food. Hence, my review pauses at three stars; a revisit is due for a full experience. For those yearning to unwind post-office hours in a spirited, grown-up crowd, this spot ticks all the boxes.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this local gem and it's safe to say that the Chinese cuisine here is unparalleled. The hot and sour soup, a standout starter, was a delightful surprise with its perfect balance of flavors without the usual heaviness. The chicken lettuce wraps, my main course, were a revelation – fresh, flavorful, and just the right amount of seasoning. Service was friendly and attentive, contributing to the pleasant ambiance with comfortably spaced tables. Highly recommended for an exceptional culinary experience.

Finally got to check this off the bucket list after living in NYC for 7 years, and I was not disappointed by the ambience/the food/the tea. I did, however, expect a little more in terms of the service (took a while to be seated despite having a reservation, and would have loved for our server to check in on us more during the meal). I made a reservation several weeks in advance on OpenTable, and they called to confirm a few days before. When we arrived, it was definitely very busy, and we had to wait an additional ten minutes for our table. I am glad that we had a separate table for two--some parties of two were sat close to other parties (shared the same bench). We went with the New Yorker Tea, and selected Thé Des Amants and Rooibos des Vahinés teas. The menu of teas is extensive, and you get a large pot that sustains YOU throughout out your meal, so take time to consider which one appeals to you! I enjoyed both teas--the former being more cinnamon heavy (perfect for autumn)  and the latter being sweeter. I absolutely loved all the food. It may not look like much, but you will definitely walk away full. It took us about an hour and a half to finish everything, and we worked our way up, starting with the scones (otherwise we def would not have had room). My favorites were the scones (the lemon and butter spreads were delicious), deviled organic egg salad sandwich, smoked salmon sandwich, roasted beef rib eye sandwich, chocolate and passion fruit cake, and cheesecake. Since I went for a birthday, they also surprised us with a dish that said happy birthday with candles and four macarons--so sweet! We also saw a father treating his little daughter to tea for her birthday, and she looked like Eloise! Would def recommend treating yourself to afternoon tea here.
