They have happy hour from 5-8pm. 3 glasses of sangria for 20 bucks and they are not shy with the wine. Came here with two friends and I really enjoyed the music. The vibe was quite eclectic with so many things that didn't seem to go together in the same place. It was interesting. The waitress was nice but her voice was too quiet and she started talking about the specials before I even got to put my coat down and sit. She was quite attentive though.I got the Terra burger and the buns were plantains. It came with Yukon potatoes, which were neatly stacked and a pickle. The patty was quite thick but a little dry. It was a decent burger. My friend tried the corn croquet and I thought it was pretty good. There wasn't much of a theme to the menu so be prepared for any type of food. Decent place to come with friends as there are lots of tables and a bar.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Greek Eatery

My dining experience at this restaurant left me conflicted. The culinary aspect was nothing short of amazing - the flavors of the typical Greek dishes danced on the palate, and each dish, from the appetizer to the dessert, was fresh and brimming with flavor. Accompanied by a lovely bottle of wine, my friend and I enjoyed what should have been a delightful meal.

However, our enjoyment was significantly marred by the lackluster service. Our waiter seemed disinterested, failing to check in on us or offer even the basic courtesies such as providing pita bread or ensuring our satisfaction with the meal. It appeared that the included 20% tip might have diminished his motivation to provide good service.

The restaurant's interior added a touch of charm to the experience, but notwithstanding the exceptional food, the poor service has left me uncertain about returning. In the competitive world of dining, service is as crucial as the cuisine, and unfortunately, this establishment fell short of expectation.

Title: Happy Hour Haven with a Slight Timing Twist

I stopped by this spot for happy hour on a Thursday and was pleasantly surprised to find the deals extending until 7 PM—though keep in mind, it's an hour earlier on Friday/Saturday. The fries were a standout; they nailed the perfect fry. The oysters, on the other hand, left a little to be desired in freshness. Service was commendable, especially considering one of the bartenders was new, yet both were exceptionally amiable and efficient, especially as we were seated at the bar.

We indulged in a peach soju, a standard selection but fairly priced at $10. While the happy hour offerings were impressive, the varying end times (7 PM on Thursdays, 6 PM on weekends, and a 5 PM cutoff for bar bites) were a tad confusing. Make sure to double-check the schedule (see my uploaded photo for reference). All said, this place is quite the catch for happy hour—just watch the clock! Solid 4 stars.

Title: A Surprisingly Satisfying Lunch at Cozumel Tortilla

I walked into Cozumel Tortilla with moderate expectations and left thoroughly impressed. The fajita lunch special, priced reasonably at $10 plus tax, was a generous serving that hit the spot. Accompanied by rice, beans, pico de gallo, guacamole, and the choice of a soda or soup, it made for a complete and satisfying meal. The homemade tortilla chips, served with a punchy spicy salsa, were a delightful start. The standout, however, was the garlic chicken—expertly flavored and cooked to perfection. My experience at Cozumel Tortilla was a positive one, and it’s added to my list for those days when a lunch splurge is on the cards.

Small restaurant with bar style seatingIntimate dining experience Came here for the wine and food pairing tasting menu and really loved the bespoke experience that evening. Each entree came with its own specific wine; we learned about the history behind each wine and how the region where the grapes are grown cultivates the taste of the wine. Their kitchen is quite small and I'm actually impressed with how they're able to prepare such delicious food in such a tiny space.Tasting menu:Ikaria Fall SaladGarlic Gulf shrimp souvlakiOctopus a la planchaSeared day boat sea scallopThrace meatballsI'd would definitely recommend this tasting experience for a date or to celebrate a special occasion. You'll be fed enough food and wine to leave in a happier mood than when you came in. If you have a party of 10 (maximum diners allowed) to experience the tasting menu, you can essentially have the entire restaurant to yourself.IG: @eatingwithbeebs

In summary: Great cocktails and yummy food but definitely overpriced for what you get. Came here for dinner on Tuesday and sat at a high top since we didn't make a reservation. The ambiance of the restaurant feels trendy and fun! I ordered the gin and shrub cocktail which was delicious ($19) and my friend and I split 3 tapas (each around $30 for a small amount aka two tacos). Like I mentioned above all of the food was delicious I just wish it was a little cheaper. Our waitress recommended 6 tapas to share but that definitely would have been too much. 3-4 for two people is fine!! It seemed like they were trying to over sell. All of the staff was friendly and had good recommendations!  I'm really happy I tried it but definitely would only come back for an occasion since it was on the pricy side.

I was initially hesitant to try this spot due to mixed reviews, but I'm glad I took the plunge. The value for money here is impressive; my shrimp Lo Mein coupled with crab Rangoon came in at a mere $11 including tip. The crab Rangoon, arguably the best I've sampled locally, leaned on the sweeter side, earning a solid 3.5/5 from me—I'm still on the hunt for my perfect match. The Lo Mein was flavorful, though the shrimp were on the smaller side. Delivery was swift, arriving within 20-25 minutes. For a budget-friendly and quick meal, this place will see me as a return customer.

Title: Exquisite Lychee Martini - A Must-Try!

Walking into this establishment, one might not expect to encounter the finest lychee martini in the vicinity, but that's precisely what awaits. The drink menu does boast a variety of impressive beverages, but the lychee martini steals the spotlight. Expertly mixed, it offers a balance of sweet and potent — a must-have for any visitor. However, a word of caution: these martinis are deceptively strong. To make the most of your visit, aim for happy hour, when you can enjoy these delightful concoctions at their most tempting prices.

Really enjoyed this restaurant for brunch. I had the skirt steak and everything including the service was excellent. It was a little pricey for the portion sizes but other than that I had no complaints.

Title: A Refreshing Change from the Usual Indian Fare

My visit to this charming restaurant was a delight for the senses. The decor sets a welcoming tone right from the outset, providing a hint that this isn't your average Indian eatery.

The culinary offerings here are good, with the standout being the succulent goat meat that was rich in flavor and expertly prepared. However, it's worth noting that ordering a la carte can make your bill climb – the dishes, while delicious, do come with a steeper price tag. To really get the most out of your dining experience, I would recommend opting for the fixed-price menu. It's a bounty of value, including a choice of appetizer, main dish, dessert, and the added bonus of daal, rice, naan, and a delightful amuse bouche to kick off your meal.

This restaurant does not dabble in fusion cuisine, nor does it offer the standard fare found in the overwhelming majority of Indian restaurants. It's a refreshing deviation that invites diners to explore less common dishes with authentic flavors.

In summary, if you're looking for a nice-looking spot with good food and are ready to spend a little extra or choose the fixed-price option for a full meal, this restaurant should be on your list, especially if you're eager to try some truly excellent goat meat.

We visited Tender prior to seeing a Broadway show. I have to give high marks due to the service. They were lightening fast and very receptive to the fact we were seeing a Broadway show. This was one of the few restaurants we encountered to not be frazzled at all by the Broadway crowd. They are a well-oiled machine in their kitchen but don't sacrifice quality.We had an excellent sushi roll and filet mignon. All the items are a la carte, so plan to get a few side items. They take reservations on OpenTable which I so appreciated, because it made for a seamless night. The inside has a dark, bold color palette and is a great choice if you need a date night spot near Broadway. We would definitely return if we needed another dinner spot nearby Broadway!

I came here on NYE and they had their regular menu which I definitely appreciate. The wagyu steak was delicious and all the sauces that came with it were really tasty as well as the mushrooms and peppers that come on the side. The caramel apple kakigori also stood out as being quite good, I loved the combo of the apple flavored ice with the creamy caramel on top.

FiDi doesn't have enough good Chinese food, and Chubby Princess helps solve this problem! Delicious food served in a cute, clean setting with VERY quick and friendly service. We enjoyed all the dishes, especially the scallion pancakes which are thin and crispy without being too oily. Pickled greens/pork/rice dish was spicier than expected, but everything else was perfect. The pork potstickers came out piping hot and flavorful. Appreciated that there are several vegetarian options! Prices are extremely reasonable, all the seating is small tables for 2, and the food came out in minutes, so this restaurant is ideal for a quick bite!

Came during Happy Hour: Tom yum Noodle soup is light sweet and spicy. The noodles are light and absorbs the spicyness of the soup. The Sa thorn Spicy seafood noodle soup has a medium thickness and spicy and has hints of coconut. The egg noddle is springy when you bite into them which a pleasant feeling on any given day. The only issue I had was that the fish tempura in the seafood noodle tasted a little hard and seems a bit old but other than that the bean sprouts are light spicy and fresh with a nice crunch to it. The karrage is juicy but the sauce was a bit thin and would be better thicker. Order the lycee martini and Coconut colada. The drinks are sweet and juicy so the alcohol flavors aren't too strong if that's your thing.

Last minute choice. Love how informal and open this little place was. All of the pastas we had were excellent, six of us had six different dishes. The texture on the house made pasta was very satisfying. Pecorino garlic cream sauce the best in my opinion. For apps had an excellent carpaccio, perfectly cut, light crust on edges and a very light truffle mayo.The Calamari also excellent.Will return on our next trip to NYC.

Jajangmyeon and tangsuyuk ( + ) is literally my favorite combination in the whole entire world. And the only thing I like more than jajangmyeon is spicy jajangmyeon  It's really rare to find a place that does spicy jajangmyeon well, but Shanghai Mong does it so well. DVSN's "Do It Well" should be dedicated to this place hehe. It's only $12 for a large spicy jajangmyeon, and $10 for a large regular jajangmyeon. Both were delicious, but the spicy jajangmyeon was really the star of the show. It was savory, slightly sweet, and flavorfully spicy. Even though I ordered take-out, the noodles were still chewy and they weren't soggy at all. The  was deliciously crispy, although I do wish the sauce was a bit more flavorful. Overall though, the food was cheap and delicious. If you're in the area, you should definitely check it out! Or better yet, order takeout and watch K-Town LA on YouTube, which is the Korean Jersey Shore you never knew you needed.

With the exception of feeling extremely rushed through our entire meal (ie: maybe allowing us to finish our appetizers before cramming 500 other dishes on to our table of 2), everything was delectable. This duck they have down to a science!
Food was SO GOOD. Quaint little spot, but very friendly staff. Kind of loud, but nice. Will be back next time I'm in the city.

Title: A Mediterranean Gem That Goes Beyond the Ordinary

From the moment my friend and I stepped into this restaurant for happy hour, we knew we were in for a treat. The food here is not just good, it's incredible—a truly unique take on Mediterranean cuisine.

A highlight was definitely the sangria. It was refreshingly authentic, focusing on the wine itself without an overabundance of fruit, suggesting it had been expertly infused for an extensive period of time.

We began with tzatziki and pita, which set the stage for the culinary excellence to follow. For the main course, the lamb buns were a delightful surprise, tender and packed with flavor. Equally impressive was the Mac and cheese, elevated with shredded lamb that provided a rich and decadent twist to a classic dish.

If you're eager to explore Mediterranean flavors with a creative spin, I couldn't recommend this restaurant more. It's perfect for those in search of a culinary adventure that's a little out of the ordinary.

During a serendipitous visit to The Cupping Room in NYC, we experienced exceptional hospitality that truly stood out. The manager, overhearing that we were celebrating a friend's birthday, generously treated our party of eight to complimentary rounds and shots. The festive atmosphere was further elevated by a live band performing a special rendition of "Happy Birthday." To our delight, they even extended the happy hour, which was a welcome treat after our 6-mile bike ride around Central Park. The friendly staff, attentive service, and convivial vibe made our visit memorable. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a great time with a touch of unexpected kindness.

After years of hearing negative feedback about this restaurant's service and pickup issues, I cautiously ordered a lunch special pad see ew with shrimp. Upon arrival, my disappointment was immediate. The portion was shockingly small, reminiscent of leftovers, with a mere four shrimps. Moreover, the shrimp had a questionable taste, hinting at its frozen and slightly undercooked origins. To compound the issue, the noodles were excessively oily and salty - ironically, the small serving size became a twisted blessing. In contrast, my coworker's chicken pad see ew was substantially better, both in portion and appearance, with no signs of the oiliness that marred mine. Despite the chance that my experience was a stroke of bad luck, I am disinclined to give this establishment another chance.

I had a great time at this spot. It is beautiful inside, the food is great and it's pretty easy to access. Public transportation isn't very far ,however, my friend and I cabbed it's from Brooklyn and the traffic was terrible. We had two other friends meeting us that were already at the restaurant, they wouldn't seat them until we arrived. Although we had reservations for 8pm, with traffic we arrived at 8:30. They seated us quickly even though we were late - most places in the city will not do this especially when there is no availability The waitstaff were very kind and knew everything that was on the menu, they were able to make recommendations as well. We ended up getting the "fiesta suprema" and thought we would order more food but we were actually full with the large share plate that we got! To end the night, we ordered a "Don Huevo" which is a must have if you go. One thing you should do once you settle in is find out how to get to the restroom. It's not so near to where you eat and is a bit of a detour but it was a beautiful detour, possible because they're a part of Dream hotel.

I was so excited to try this place out, and it didn't disappoint (mostly). The line was huuuuge but I had my mind made up so I waited. The menu board was hard to see until you were up to the counter, at which point you were rushed to order and pushed down the line to watch your meal be made. The whole process is a little confusing, but I'll chalk it up to being a tourist and not a regular. I ordered the tamarind tea and the girl behind the counter suggested I try something else? Not sure why, but I declined and went with my first choice and was plenty happy, as tamarind is a personal favorite of mine. I ordered two tacos along with my tea and was able to customize the toppings and meat to fit my preference. Both were hot and delicious. I devoured them quick and went on my way. There isn't abundant seating available nearby so I ended up standing and eating, which didn't bother me any but if you were trying to chat with someone over lunch it'd be a little challenging to find a place to do that. Everything was fairly priced and worth the cost for sure.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Hyped Ichiran

I visited Ichiran with high expectations, intrigued by the buzz it generated during my travels in Japan. The food quality earns a solid 4 stars; it was good, but not groundbreaking, especially considering the prices are steep compared to other ramen places. The basic bowl starts at $18, which is a jolt, and the recommended set runs $24.

Opting for the recommended set, I corrected my initial custom order with the waitress, who confirmed the change. Despite this, my order arrived with extra items, including an unnecessary second egg, which was rectified. However, later I found an additional unrequested seaweed topping that cost an extra $1.5, which they wouldn't remove from my bill as it was already mixed in my ramen. My total came to an unjustifiable $27-28.

While the ramen was tasty, the value for money and the staff's refusal to acknowledge their oversight on a minor charge left a sour taste. For a renowned establishment like Ichiran, it's disappointing to see such service flaws overshadowing their culinary efforts.

Title: A Mixed Bag at a Family-Friendly Eatery

I finally satisfied my curiosity about the much-talked-about local restaurant this past humid Saturday. Despite the anticipation, my experience was a mixed one, leading me to rate it 4 stars mainly because of the service issues.

Arriving at 5pm, the place seemed understaffed, contributing to a painfully slow service that didn't match the number of guests present. Due to previous online booking frustrations, the emptier-than-expected dining room was puzzling. A pressing engagement meant we anxiously waited 15 minutes just to receive our check, after several requests—certainly a damper on the evening.

The setting, both inside and out, was more casual than anticipated, teeming with families and babies—a delight for those dining with little ones. Outdoor seating allowed us to enjoy the last of the warm weather, which was a highlight.

Culinary-wise, the potato monkey bread lived up to its Yelp fame, though the portion size seemed less generous compared to what I expected. The savory bar steak, economically priced during early dining hours, and the hanger steak, both with a side of curly fries, were delectable surprises. The bavette's juiciness won over the marginally larger hanger.

Dessert brought a colossal salty toffee cake, shared due to its sweetness. While fluffy and warm, inconsistent toffee distribution and a stingy sprinkle of pecans diminished the indulgence. The latte, light on the coffee, was an unexpected treat for a non-coffee drinker like myself, though it might disappoint those who prefer a stronger brew.

Overall, there's potential for a great dining experience if not for the underwhelming service. I'd be willing to return, perhaps to try the other desserts, on a less pressing evening.

A little disappointed with our experience. First off they should mention that the breakfast is not served outside. I specifically requested a table outside when I made my reservation and upon arrival was told they don't start serving food outside until brunch. Food was underwhelming for the price point. Our reservation was for 10 AM and we watched them set up for brunch when they brought out the nice flowers and tableware and put out Chef Daniel's book on display. I felt like a second class citizen just having breakfast there.  I wanted to celebrate my husband's promotion with a fancy breakfast( which I also mentioned when I made the reservation) but was disappointed and felt out of place. Coffee was very good.

Title: Long Lines but Mixed Feelings at Lombardi's

My visit to Lombardi's was accompanied by the typical long queue indicative of a culinary gem, especially noteworthy in winter's chill. Joining the wait at 2:30 pm on a Saturday, we were teased with a 20-minute anticipation for what we hoped would be an extraordinary meal.

The star of our table was the clam pizza, boasting a bountiful helping of clams paired with delectable flavors, earning a solid 4 out of 5. Unfortunately, the dough's cardboard-like texture pulled us back from a full-fledged rave.

Be prepared for New York prices—the $32 price tag for the pizza felt steep, especially considering the bustling atmosphere which delayed our ordering process even at the off-peak hour of 3 pm.

In summary, Lombardi's offers some tasty choices, but the combination of wait times and high prices means my return isn't guaranteed. If faced with a similar wait in the future, I might just explore other eateries nearby.

Ok...full disclosure....we didn't go here for the food. We went as it is the diner location for Seinfeld. We were not expecting much and was overall pleased with our experience. Being a huge Seinfeld fan, I was simply excited with the cool paraphernalia on the walls and experience itself. It is a casual old time diner with a few booths and bar seating. It is clean and in a safe area. The food was pretty good. I ordered the eggs and corn beef hash. My husband ordered the Greek lasagna. Both of us were happy. I ordered a bagel as well and was REALLY happy with it. The reason I didn't give the 5th Star was due to the "gruff" waitress. I noticed it wasn't just ours, but three of them were generally snippy and ready to get us in and out quickly. I was also made fun of as I was taking photos and my waitress rolled her eyes and said loudly.."oh boy another Seinfeld fan". I laughed and stated I'm sure they appreciated the business that comes in just for the experience and she was not a fan of that opinion lol She wasn't rude, but we are used to wait staff checking on us and being super nice even when they aren't in the mood to. Otherwise it was a great meal and experience and we would recommend others to try it out as well.

Just WOW. Fresh fish and very delicious combinations. For drinks we had the creme rosette which was phenomenal. Super refreshing and just the right amount of sweet. Presentations of everything was beautiful and service was very attentive. The tuna tarts are as amazing as everyone says, even better. ORDER THEM!! Alaska crab crispy rice, salmon tartar and yellowtail sashimi were also great. Great ambience, perfect for date night!

Still amazing! Just wanted to add some photos of the amazing food. The somtum is the best in Manhattan for sure and their tomsabb soup is super spicy and authentic!! Order the basil fried rice and you won't regret it!

Title: A Sumptuous Sunday Brunch to Remember

Our Sunday brunch experience at this restaurant was nothing short of outstanding. From the moment we zipped up in the express elevator, the excitement was high. The restaurant offers immediate seating, although I suggest snagging an early reservation since it fills up by 11:30 am.

The array of food stations had something for every palate – the cold station boasted an impressive selection including pastries, salads, smoked salmon, and charcuterie boards. The hot station was a delight, especially the parmesan gnocchi, while the breakfast offerings like made-to-order omelettes, pancakes, and waffles with all the possible toppings were irresistible.

Service was impeccable, thanks to our server, Colette, who was the epitome of friendly and attentive, ensuring our bottomless mimosas were never empty.

However, there’s some room for improvement. The price point was steep compared to other brunch buffets, making it suitable perhaps for occasional splurges. Additionally, while the urban view was decent, it didn’t add any wow factor to the experience.

Despite these minor drawbacks, the overall experience was fantastic, and I would definitely recommend this place for those special brunch outings.

A bowl of pho cost about $9.75 and the portion is so generous that it can be shared between 2. Great price, big portion, tasty food, definitely filling, clean bathrooms, what more can you ask for? Thai Son is a great place for a quick bite of Vietnamese that will fill you up for a low price! Check it out if you're around the area

Title: A Gem for Vietnamese Cuisine Lovers

My recent visit to this Vietnamese spot in Chinatown left a delightful impression, thanks to their famous meticulously-crafted broth. Opting for their regular Saigon Pho, I was treated to a steaming bowl filled with perfectly thin slices of beef, tender meatballs, and succulent brisket. Accompanying this was the aromatic lemongrass chicken vermicelli, which proved equally pleasing. 

The prompt service meant both dishes arrived quickly, but it was the Pho's richness that showcased the hours spent perfecting the broth. The establishment prides itself on cleanliness, and it shows—from the well-furnished dining area to the exceptionally clean restroom facilities. Efficient and courteous staff add to the overall positive experience. 

For anyone craving authentic Vietnamese flavors in a welcoming atmosphere, this restaurant is unquestionably worth a visit.

Title: A Gem Uncovered at Sumela

Following a friend's suggestion, we ventured to Sumela for lunch and were met with an unexpectedly delightful experience. Nestled in the Upper East Side, this establishment greeted us with immediate service as they opened their doors.

The meal commenced with warm Turkish bread, perfectly complemented by an exceptionally smooth and creamy side of hummus, priced reasonably at $8. I opted for a Greek salad, enhanced with chicken for an additional $5, and found the portion both hearty and fresh, with a light dressing that accentuated rather than overwhelmed.

My companions enjoyed the whole branzino, a dish that showcased the kitchen's skill with its impeccably deboned and grilled presentation, complete with crispy skin and tender flaky meat, all for $27.

Ending on a high note, we indulged in the baklava, which struck a fine balance with its pistachio-rich, flaky layers, thankfully avoiding the pitfall of excessive sweetness.

Despite UES-standard pricing, Sumela stands out with its unwavering commitment to quality cuisine and meticulous service, fully justifying the expense for a truly memorable dining experience.

Title: A Taste of Cuba in the Heart of the City

On a spontaneous Thursday night stroll towards Times Square, my curiosity and hunger led me to a vibrant Cuban restaurant pulsing with the rhythm of a live band. The animated crowd's energy was infectious, and the warm welcome by the staff who seated us promptly only added to the lively ambiance.

Eager to dive into the Cuban experience, we started with the must-try Ultimate Mojito and Brazil's National cocktail, the Caipirinha—both expertly mixed and the perfect kick-off to our culinary adventure. The Cuban garlic bread arrived next, paired with a cheesy spinach dip that set a high bar for the courses to follow.

The pineapple pork chops were the star of the show, served on a bed of yuca with a tantalizing side of burnt rice—every bite a delightful testament to Cuban flavors. The stuffed peppers, however, fell short of expectation but did not detract from the overall experience.

To conclude, the tres leches was a creamy dream, ending the meal on an unquestionably high note.

In summary, this Cuban gem offers an immersive experience with great food and an energetic atmosphere. A 10/10 recommendation for anyone looking for a slice of Cuba in the city. I'm already planning my next visit!
A must at Stop when in NYC.   Love the small local feel of this place and the food is great.    Never had a bad meal.    If you are near Hell's Kitchen check this place out.

Title: Disappointing Experience at a Former Favorite

I'm reluctantly revising my rating from a solid five to a mere three after a disheartening experience at what used to be one of our top dining destinations. As Brooklyn residents, we've been loyal patrons, often venturing out to this spot, but our latest visit to catch the UFC fight left a bitter taste.

In all my numerous visits, I've never felt compelled to leave a negative review – until now. While the service here typically shines, it faltered significantly last night. Our waitress repeatedly mixed up orders and carried a less-than-pleasant demeanor, though not without a few redeeming moments.

The real issue that soured the night came when, after settling a nearly $300 tab, we were asked to vacate our seats for another party. Their selective approach to seat turnover was clear, as the table beside us wasn't approached with the same request. Despite the inconvenience, we chose to stay and finish watching the fight, as well as the drinks and shots we had just ordered.

The incident left me questioning future visits. There's a slim chance we’ll return with the same frequency, if at all, after such a letdown. Disappointed is an understatement.

Title: A Soulful Experience at Harlem's Culinary Gem

Harlem really stakes its claim as the premier destination for southern-style soul food, and my recent dining experience did not disappoint. The restaurant offers a laid-back atmosphere where casual attire is perfectly acceptable, allowing diners to relax and enjoy their meal in a creative setting. The interior is adorned with murals that pay homage to black history, providing not only visual delight but also a cultural journey that adds depth to the dining experience.

The menu presents an enticing selection of dishes with a celebrity twist, piquing interest from the moment you glance at it. The fried chicken, sautéed greens, cheesy grits, and catfish were exceptional in flavor and authenticity, truly living up to the restaurant's reputation. To top it off, the service was flawless, contributing to an overall enjoyable experience. Harlem proves to be a spot where both your palate and your spirit are nourished, with no shortcomings to speak of.

Patsy's reputation as one of the best pies in the city certainly held up. I went for a late lunch with a group of friends and we were seated immediately even though it was a Saturday. I just moved to the neighborhood, but would say it's definitely worth the trip up to East Harlem for the original Instead of going to another one of its locations in the city.

Really good vegetable dumplings and ramen.  My only complaint is that I ordered chicken Katsu ramen expecting to get white meat chicken and it came with dark meat that didn't seem to be great quality.  I'd order from her again but would get only vegetarian options.  Probably the steamed vegetable dumplings and veggie ramen.  Ordered delivery and the ramen came piping hot.  really appreciated the way that everything was packaged to ensure that it came in optimal shape -- the chicken cake separately from the soup and they even punched a little hole in the chicken container so that the heat didn't stay in and make the chicken breading wet and less crunchy.  Only the pan seared dumplings didn't transport very well.

I recently dined at a local spot known for its Filipino cuisine and it was definitely a mixed bag of delicious and just shy of perfect. Starting with the sisig, it was on the fattier side compared to others I've tried. The fat was chunky, and although the flavor profile was impressive, a finer chop could improve the balance in each bite—it didn't quite match up to the delight of Pig & Khao's offering, though it did surpass Maharlika in terms of being less salty.

Moving on to the Crispy Pata, the portion was generous, easily feeding 2-3 people as stated on the menu. It reminded me of a Cantonese roast pig with its comparable crunchiness, and I was pleased to find it well-marinated, tender, and moist inside.

The garlic rice fell short, needing a stronger garlic punch, but it was still enjoyable. What stood out to me was the overall restraint on salt—a welcome departure from the typically salt-heavy Filipino dishes I've experienced elsewhere.

Service was top-notch, leaving a positive impression and a desire to return. I have my eyes set on exploring their beef and seafood offerings next time.

The "Once Bitten" sandwich at this gem of a restaurant is a true culinary delight. The garlic sauce adds a delectable kick that beautifully complements the perfectly marinated veggies. When ensconced in a fresh wrap and combined with the tang of goat cheese, the flavors meld seamlessly. Despite being a tad messy to handle, the explosion of taste makes it a must-try. Absolutely delicious!

The service here is good.  The food is good.  The value?  Poor.A friend and I had lunch here where he ordered a congee, cruller, and two rice noodle dishes manly for himself as he was hungry and I actually already ate.  The thousand year old egg congee was good but does not rival against a any other restaurants nearby.  The cruller was the worse seeing the picture on the menu, you see the typical double tube of delicious fried dough.  Instead, it $3 for 6 small and thin pieces from a single tube.The rice rolls themselves are ok.  The beef and shrimp one which appears to be their signature is good though shrimp wasn't spread out evenly as we cut through it to share.Perhaps the big crowd is just first timers or they are loyalists from a particular region of China, but speaking from and American Born Chinese person who lived in Chinatown for 30+ years, there's a lot better options.

I recently revisited this restaurant with my best friends for a pre-dancing dinner and drinks. I must say, the Mediterranean flatbread was a delight, and my friend thoroughly enjoyed her buffalo flatbread and hamburger, noting the portions were generous. We sampled the froze, which was outstandingly refreshing. Although the Black Pearl cocktail proved a bit too potent for one of us, it's a minor hiccup in an otherwise splendid experience. The abundance of outlets was a thoughtful touch, ensuring our devices were charged for the night ahead. Cleanliness of the premises, including the restrooms, was impeccable, and the vibe struck a perfect balance between tranquility and vibrance. We couldn't have asked for a better start to our evening.

Title: Another Bite at Umami Burger at Brookfield Place

On a recent jaunt to Brookfield Place with an appetite for burgers, my husband and I gave Umami Burger another chance to impress us. This time, we split the hefty original Impossible Burger, which featured a double stack of Impossible patties and an enticing mix of toppings including grilled onions, American cheese, and miso mustard. Though tastier than previous visits, it still hasn't topped my list of favorite burgers.

We also indulged in the 'manly fries,' which were a decadent heap of beer-cheddar, bacon, and other bold flavors. Despite being a hit to our taste buds, they were rivaled by the dirty frites from neighboring Mighty Quinn's, which ultimately won our preference.

In conclusion, Umami Burger provided a satisfactory meal that hit the spot but didn't outshine its competitors. If you're in Brookfield Place with a burger craving, it's a solid option, but not a destination in its own right.

Whoa !!!  What an amazing surprise!!Decided to visit the park today in a rare 65 degree day in January!!   Stopped by Saiguette for the first time and tried the Lemon Grass roast pork banh mi. Saiguettes sandwich (Banh Mi)Grilled lemon grass pork shoulder ($11)What a fabulous sandwich ! First it was huge and well worth the $11 price.  The porks was tender and savory and took two hands to eat this monster.  Every bite was crisp and flavorful, then I hit the jalapeños and BAMM. !!!   I need to come back to this little corner dine and you should too !!!! Sorry no picture of this sandwich, but I ate it just down the trees at this waterfall....

Finally got to try this location. It's always busy during lunch hours but the line is fast. It's nicely lit and bright against the white walls. There are no seats but there are places to stand and eat. To order, you go by the cashier. They give you a ticket and you present it to the next part of the line. Fairly efficient. Ordered the carne asada and carnitas adobodas and it was delicious! It includes guac so no extra. Lime and additional sauce you get on your own. It was quick meal.

My dining experience at this establishment was thoroughly enjoyable from start to finish. The meal commenced with a refreshing glass of Prosecco, setting the stage for the classic starters that followed. The crispness of the iceberg wedge was a delightful prelude to the rich, savory depth of the French onion soup, which was masterfully prepared.

The main event, however, was the porterhouse for two, cooked to a perfect medium rare. This succulent cut was complemented by creamy mashed potatoes and perfectly cooked asparagus, creating a symphony of flavors that was both comforting and indulgent. My dining companions echoed my sentiments, each savoring their respective cuts with evident pleasure.

To accompany our meal, we selected two bottles of red wine, which proved to be an excellent choice, enhancing the dining experience with their robust flavors.

In conclusion, this restaurant delivered an impressive combination of quality dishes and superb service, leaving no doubt that it is a destination for any lover of fine steaks and complementary pairings.

We came around 2 pm and were sat immediately. My friends and I all ordered cappuccinos. The appearance was cute with the foam art, however, 2/3 were cold. The best part of the brunch were the excellent poached eggs, perfectly cooked - 5/5 stars. The bacon on the other hand was so incredibly salty that it was difficult for me to eat. My friend requested salt for her poached eggs and 10 minutes later, the waitress apologized for completely forgetting. Overall, alright brunch spot that I wouldn't necessarily recommend.

Our first meal of the trip and it didn't disappoint. For dinner, they have 2 prie fixe options: 7- or 4- course meal. Glad we asked the waiter on which option would be the better--we went with the 4-course and tried out 8 different dishes between the two of us. Best one is definitely the bison but everything pictured was absolutely amazing. The cod was a bit underwhelming compared to the rest of the dishes we got; but still good. Would definitely do the same dishes when we come back, maybe sub in something else for the cod.

Churrascaria Plataforma is an all you can eat Brazilian steakhouse. The price is a bit expensive, but it was a fun experience to try at least once. I went during restaurant week for $42 per person (it's a bit less expensive than the normal price but not all the meats are offered). You can stay up to 2 hours and there is no additional charge if you can't finish your plate. There is a salad bar which has different types of cold appetizers such as roast beef, salads, sushi, stuffed grape leaves. The sushi wasn't the best quality or the freshest but it was satisfying. At the table you can check off which sides you want (mashed potatoes, french fries, fried polenta, etc). I tried the Brazilian cheese bread (pao de queijo) and the mashed potatoes. The pao de queijo wasn't the freshest, but it was decent. The mashed potato was very creamy and smooth but was a little bland. Just don't fill up on the buffet or the sides, save room for the meats! Each person has a token with green on one side and red on the other to indicate if you would like more meat. The servers bring the meats on spits around the restaurant and carves a slice in front of you. Be sure to flip your card over to red if you need a break. They come out fast! I found the meat pretty good, but some were slightly too salty. The chicken was my least favorite. Dessert is also included, but I was not impressed by the chocolate mousse. Service was excellent and very friendly!

The Strawberry and Nutella Crepe is absolutely delicious! It fits everything I look for in a crepe where each bite was a perfect fruit, crepe, cream, and Nutella ratio. The order came out super quick and fresh. The place is a bit cramped on the inside but there are spaces to rest the plate while you enjoy your crepe.
We got the West 4th and Macdougal! I think I liked the Macdougal better because of the added falafel flavor and texture. But otherwise, good portions, lots of flavor, reasonable price! I'd go back.

Affordable and tastes good. What else to ask for?It's easy to miss, not because it's a small store, but because there's nothing from the store front that makes it stand out on the block. My friend raved about this place before so I thought I should definitely give this place a try. And it's as good as I've heard. I choose the stir friend knife cut noodles with shredded chicken. It didn't look like there was much in the dish but it certainly was very filling. The knife cut noodles were very bouncy and chewy and short.Even though I was super stuffed from the noodles, I shared a plate of fried dumplings with a friend. And wow, they were so juicy! One bite and I see all the soup juice in the dumpling still! Definitely recommend to get.Don't expect kind smiles for the service but don't let this turn you away either. They give you the most basic service needed. Also make to have CASH!

New and seemingly tucked away in NYC. There's a little heated patio in the back with additional seating that's cute in its own way. Has plastic shrubbery surrounding the area to give that outside vibe. For appetizers we ordered the calamari and shrimp and the baby arugula salad. Calamari was delicious, light outside crispy layer with a spicy tomato sauce and a thicker tartar sauce. I like the twist with shrimp, but the plate was lacking the tentacle octopus calamari pieces which are my favorite! It was also unique that they serve the calamari in what looks like a crispy tortilla bowl. The baby arugula salad was alright -- light and refreshing. Could have done with the cheese shaved or largely grated than the slices we got on top. For entrees, we of course had to get the pasta. We ordered the tagliatelle mare Monte and the saffron fettuccine with pesto and shrimp. Both were delicious. I enjoyed the creaminess of both sauces. The pastas were on the softer side (which I liked!) and were homemade. Shrimp is always a great pairing with pasta and it was cooked very nicely in both dishes. The saffron was mild in flavor and could probably be heavier on the pesto. Overall, it was a good visit, but I was amazed by anything that makes my urging to come back.

This place never has a line compared to everything that surrounds it. Very overpriced for skimpy, small slices on extremely thin (often overcooked) crust. Though I do appreciate the natural, fresh ingredients they use. Anything with red sauce has been lackluster. I highly recommend the arugula or mushroom pies. Arugula had so much parmesan mixed within, light balsamic glaze, fresh cherry tomatoes, and a hearty fresh mozzarella glob. Everything paired so nicely that I was sad to be done. Mushroom is cheesy and white based, also yum. Overall average--not your standard NY pizza slice, so don't expect that here!

Title: Cozy Evening with Soju and Korean Comfort Food

Last Friday night's visit to this vibrant spot was a steal, especially during happy hour when a bottle of flavorful soju was just $14. Despite the packed bar, it didn't take long to get seated for our party of three. Right off the bat, the sight of crispy fried chicken was irresistible. Without hesitation, we ordered soju to kick things off, followed by a superb deal on the fried chicken - only $4 for 4 pieces. To complement our meal, we opted for the sumptuous Korean army stew and cheesy rice cakes, which did not disappoint. Each dish was not just delicious but provided the perfect comfort for a chilly evening. Highly recommended for those looking to indulge in great food and drinks at even better prices!

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this restaurant to those in search of a satisfying Mexican meal. Upon visiting with my family, the immediate red flag was the notably slow service. Our waiter vanished after taking our order, leaving us without the chance to voice our concerns about the food. The guacamole lacked flavor, and although my enchiladas were passable, they did not impress. The rest of my family's dining experience paralleled the lackluster guacamole, with meals that did not meet our expectations. The lack of attentive service sealed our decision that we wouldn't be returning.

UPDATE: I got the negitoro don which was alright. For $24.99 I was expecting to get more bluefin tuna but I did so I'm sad now. My girlfriend also got the gonna shoyu tuna which was pretty good but I definitely still like the Sichuan chili salmon the most. Stay tuned as I will try all of these bowls at least once to see which one is the best.

Title: A Luxurious Bite in a Historic Setting

If you're looking for an upscale dining experience that caters to those special occasions, then this might just be your spot. Admittedly, the pricing is steep – dining here could set you back a pretty penny, especially during their large events, which often support noble causes but are unfortunately out of reach for regular visits on an average budget.

That said, for those less extravagant days, I find myself gravitating towards their small bites section – a perfect compromise without missing out on the ambiance. Speaking of which, the historic boathouse charms with its timeless allure, offering a romantic fireside retreat in the winter and stunning outdoor scenery year-round.

It's the kind of place I proudly include in my Central Park tour for out-of-town guests. A visit here, particularly with well-heeled relatives, turns a simple lunch into a fashionable affair. Trust me, even my cousin Robert never passes up a chance to drop by. In summary, this restaurant is a must-see, whether you're a local or just passing through.

One, two... Tierra & Mar is coming for you! HAHAHA! No, for real though... Tierra & Mar is taking business away from every restaurant in the area!I have had Tierra & Mar a few times, and it never disappoints! No matter what time of the day it is, you can count on Tierra & Mar to have a variety of fresh choices! The food is fresh because they continuously have to bring more out, as it gets pretty busy in there!

Celebrating the Chinese new year with a couple of my friends. I wanted to try some dim sum for the first time. This was pretty close to our job so we walked over after work. Got there around 5pm on a Friday and it was actually pretty empty. We order steamed shrimp dumpling, an assortment of pan fried dumpling, fried crispy spare ribs and broccoli cooked in garlic sauce. We also had some sake to end the night. Really great service and the food was impeccable.

For a diverse a city as New York is, good authentic Mexican food is hard to find. Most places you go to always get something wrong but not Los Tacos No. 1. This place makes makes me feel like I'm back in the mercado in Mexico. Not only does the stand have that mercado feel and look to it, but the tacos, Jesus the tacos are really good. The hand made tortillas, the correct sauces, al pastor meat that you see the taquero carve off the spit, make for a cosmic explosion of goodness in your mouth.This is the only spot in NYC that you should be eating tacos from

I expected and that is the problem... I ate it with gusto as I was full of tequila and beer, but I've had far superior pizza in San Diego. I will continue the search for the best pizza until my dying day.I'm similar to Don Quixote seeking the lost treasure of El Dorado, hopefully I don't lose myself on the journey.

Came here to do a pickup (I think most people do pickup from the looks of the store...and the fact that no one was in the store when we ordered).Got the pork and chicken katsu (both with curry). Honestly, you couldn't really tell the difference between the two, so just get whichever meat you like better or maybe chicken since it's healthier. I thought it was well done and very homey. They give you a cup of curry and at first I was worried that it wasn't enough, but it was definitely enough. Very thick, but doesn't feel too fatty, don't feel that bad for finishing all of it. The katsu itself and the sauce it comes with, they seemed more on the meh side, like getting a burger at McDonalds. It definitely tastes like Tonkatsu, but it doesn't really make you say wow or anything. It just satisfies that craving of eating tonkatsu.This is basically fast food tonkatsu and as long as that's what you have in mind, this will be great.

Title: Community Gem Shines Through Uncertain Times

I recently had the pleasure of dining at The Grey Lady, and it was a heartwarming experience. Amidst these challenging times, it's inspiring to see the staff and owners stepping up to support the community. Their goodwill resonates with every interaction, and I encourage those who can to leave cash tips as a token of gratitude.

During my visit, I savored the potato leek soup, which was nothing short of delicious. It left me eagerly anticipating the day I can return to enjoy their full menu. Here's to hoping The Grey Lady resumes normal operations soon, as I'm confident that the rest of their offerings will be just as delightful. Hats off to this local treasure!

First timers here ..  we walked into this restaurant from a busy street and crowded places in NY and surprisingly saw so much room inside .. lots of seats .. they also had 2nd floor .. look and feel of the restaurant was great .. loved the service too . They always smiled and served us .. Cocktails and drinks were awesome ..  they didn't have much options for beer but just had a local one .. spring rolls were good but chicken wings weren't that good . It was different to what we normally have . Was dry . Overall a good experience and good restaurant in a busy street ..

Came here with a group on a Tuesday night - the place was pretty dead but I imagine it's busier on the weekends. The restaurant itself is two levels with a fishing tank running through the middle of the space. We were seated upstairs which was a fun vantage point to observe other people fishing. Our waitress was helpful explaining the menu choices and she was attentive throughout the meal.If you decide to go fishing, you have a number of options based on price point and type of fish. We opted to go for the cheapest fish (rainbow trout). But be warned - the fish come in 3 sizes and if you catch a big one then you pay the highest price. Once you decide which fish you want to catch, the staff give you a poncho and a fishing rod with bait and help you set up. We spent a solid 30 minutes fishing - those darn fish did not want to bite! For people who are over it, you can always ditch the fishing rod and grab a net and pull one out. It was super fun once we caught one. The staff have a fun ritual involving hitting a drum and chanting. The best part is once you've got your fish, you get to choose among 13 different styles of cooking. And pro tip: you can do your fish half and half if you want to try different styles.We ended up choosing to get our fish two ways: grilled and simmered and soy sauce. I think the grilled fish could have used a little more salt/flavor, but the soy sauce simmered version was quite good. We also ordered a number of additional dishes including the vegetable tempura, the uni and fatty tuna handrolls, the spicy salmon roll, and the matcha tiramisu for dessert. To be honest, none of these dishes were really standouts, but they were fine. They're also pretty small so you end up needing to order quite a few dishes to feel full. We also split two carafes of sake to accompany our meal. In the end, the bill was about $55pp which isn't crazy but not the cheapest either. Overall, you're going to this restaurant for a unique, hands-on fishing experience. This would be great for a family or even a date activity. I wouldn't expect the most mindblowing food, but that's not what you're going for anyway. Would recommend!

Title: Quaint Charm and Tantalizing Tastes at a Local Hideaway

My impromptu Saturday night at this charming eatery was a pleasant surprise, beginning with the ease of snagging a last-minute 8:30 pm reservation. Navigating through the somewhat misleading main entrance—an apartment building facade—led me to a bustling atmosphere teeming with diners.

Promptly greeted by a delightful hostess, our early arrival was accommodated with grace, and we were escorted to a serene upstairs seating area, away from the hubbub. The residential roots of the building lent a cozy, unique vibe that I found quite endearing.

The service was prompt; the server was attentive, providing us with the evening's specials and enough time to peruse the menu. Our culinary journey started with the Chef's Tasting Plate—fig bruschetta and seaweed caviar canapés stood out and left me longing for more.

Moving on to the greens, the kale salad was fresh but underwhelming in flavor. Main dishes were a mixed bag: a lasagna that was hearty but heavy on the seitan, a bitterish trumpet mushroom scallops I'd pass on in the future, and a comforting butternut squash soup.

Despite nearing satiety, dessert was a must—cashew ice cream in three delightful flavors was the perfect finale to our meal. With a reasonable tally of $165, accounting for a couple of wines and service, I'm keen to return for brunch and further menu explorations. The great service also warrants a repeat visit.

During my recent visit to the local ramen joint, I had the pleasure of trying their Mentaiko ramen. The dish was notably saucy, which added a unique and bold flavor. However, I found myself yearning for an option to pair the Mentaiko with spaghetti pasta, believing it would complement the sauce beautifully. Additionally, I sampled the katsu sandwich, which was quite delectable, although it would have been perfect if the meat were served a bit thicker. Overall, the restaurant offers a solid dining experience with room for some minor improvements.

Title: A Quiet Evening with Phenomenal Food

I've been meaning to share my thoughts on this gem of a restaurant since a memorable visit back in October 2019. My partner and I were in pursuit of a lovely dinner, and this place did not disappoint. The braised short rib with mashed potatoes stole the show—meat so tender it slipped effortlessly off the bone, paired with the creamiest, most flavorful mashed potatoes I've had in a long time.

The ambiance was unusually tranquil, given it was a slow night with just a handful of other diners, which made for a very personalized experience. Service was swift and efficient, with our order taken promptly and the food arriving in just 10 to 15 minutes. Although the quietude was pleasant, I'm curious about the restaurant's vibe on a busier evening.

In sum, the food was exceptional, and I'm eager to return, perhaps on a livelier night to fully experience the restaurant's atmosphere.

After watching a YouTube video about the backstory of 2 Brothers Pizza, I was compelled to experience it myself. Their famed $1 cheese slice is a wonder amid the bustling Manhattan landscape— a commendable feat considering the soaring costs and fierce competition in the area. True to their word, the cost did not disappoint.

The pizza exceeded my dollar's expectations with its simple yet satisfying fare, characterized by a perfectly thin crust. It's a no-frills delight for the price point. Service was impressively swift, making the visit swift and efficient. For an affordable and quick bite, particularly during the late hours, 2 Brothers is a definite go-to. I'm rooting for them to persist with their budget-friendly offerings.

Title: A Lunch Special That Hits the Spot!

I recently enjoyed an exemplary pre-fixe lunch menu that has set a new standard for my midday dining experiences. The choice was tantalizingly simple: succulent Chicken Tikka Masala or creamy Saag Paneer. Opting for the Chicken Tikka, I was off to an indulgent start.

But the culinary journey didn't end there. The second entrée selection boasted an impressive array of options. My eye was initially drawn to the Butter Salmon, but on the waiter's sage advice, I pivoted to the Curry Salmon. What a delightful twist it was – perfectly flavored without being overly spicy, but with the option to dial up the heat for those who prefer it.

The final decision was a classic one: rice or naan? If you're accompanied, I advise splitting the two because who would want to forego either the comfort of freshly baked naan or the perfect pairing of rice with Chicken Tikka Masala?

Although our large group faced a bit of initial disorganization even with our reservation, the staff quickly regained their footing, and we enjoyed seamless service thereafter.

My advice? Don't walk, run to this restaurant for the lunch special, and remember – they offer a dinner special too!

I had a wonderful dining experience at this restaurant. The highlight was undoubtedly the tantan ramen, which featured uniquely wide noodles with an ideal al dente texture, all swimming in a delectably spicy broth that tantalized the taste buds. While the katsu curry offered a mixed bag with its slightly chewy pork, the curry sauce itself was a savory triumph. Considering the variety on the menu still left to explore, I am eagerly looking forward to my next visit.

Ehhhhh meh. Honestly  - - "my pie" you were just A-OKAY.We were expecting something a lot different when we came in based on the high rated fellow yelp reviews.Visiting from Boston we were excited to try some authentic New York style pizza, however we kinda missed the ball on this one.My man got the margarita slice and I opted for the arugula parm slice. Both were again, not really what we were expecting for New York style pizza. From what we remember I don't think they even had a plain slice of just cheese pizza. All slices are mastered with different kinds of toppings and cheeses making this place extra pizza fancy.Pros: Fresh ingredients, cute spot, and the slices were visually appetizing.Cons:Not bad, not great. Where's the basic slices for us basic people?!

I recently dined at a charming restaurant that embraces the classic Chinese style of sharing, and I must say, the experience was delightful. Each dish we ordered burst with flavor, leaving us satisfyingly stuffed without burning a hole in our wallets.

The attention to detail in the decor complemented the elegant presentation of the food, served in exquisite bowls and dishes that enhanced the overall dining experience. This spot is definitely on my list for a return visit, preferably with a group of friends to partake in the joy of sharing these amazing dishes. Highly recommend for anyone looking to indulge in authentic and scrumptious Chinese cuisine!

I came here for a birthday dinner with a group of 6 people on a Friday night.  We ordered the special group combo for $99 (3 appetizers, crayfish, Dungeness crab, big head shrimp, sausage, corn, potatoes), the blue crab with salted egg yolk, and the big head shrimp noodles.  They gave us the cajun fries appetizer on the house which was nice.  We got the Chongqing popcorn chicken, fried calamari, and chicken wings appetizers.  We got the seafood boil with Spicy Cajun sauce.  The portions were large enough to share with everyone.  I really enjoyed the salted egg yolk crab the most since it's wasn't too salty but still tasty.  The best appetizer was the Chongqing popcorn chicken, very spicy and crispy.  The seafood boil was delicious and full of garlicky sauce.  The big head shrimp noodles were great also.  Service was very fast and attentive.  I would definitely come back to try other dishes.  FYI - You can get a free can of soda with Yelp check-in.

Popped in on a weekday evening. I really wanted to like this place but was let down. Unfortunately,  the Bad service will not lead me back to this establishment. Management is a complete moron and not Up to par with the guests and location. Staff needs to adapt better communication, attention to detail and perhaps some compassion for its customers. Myself and my party were treated poorly.Other tables near us were complaining due to lack of service and lack of attention.One table sat and left after waiting to be served and not being attended to. Another couple sat for quite a while and almost left after not being greeted.Floor manager tried assisting as well but he was pretty clueless and rude to the tables.Our group ordered hand rolls, various appetizers, drinks, salads and additional special items.Food was good but not out of this world and a bit overpriced for the servings. The rolls were the tiniest rolls I have ever seen. -good taste and fresh but tiny! Will NOT be returning.

Tucked away in a quaint, albeit compact location, this poke spot shines with its cleanliness and inviting ambiance. Navigating through NYC's poke scene can be a gamble, with starkly contrasting reviews often causing hesitation. However, after vetting the online opinions, which showed more positives than red flags, I decided to take the plunge.

To my delight, the salmon was remarkably fresh, falling just a hair short of the best I've had in the city, hence the four-star rating. The true standout was the generous array of complimentary toppings that allowed for a symphony of flavors in each bite. While one cautionary review about the spicy fish options was noted, my experience with the raw selections was wholly satisfactory.

Value for money is an understatement here – a substantial large bowl brimming with salmon set me back less than $15, a stark contrast to other reviews calling it overpriced. It's not every day you find yourself struggling to finish such a hearty portion.

My visit was during a quieter time, so I can't attest to the service during the hustle and bustle that some have found less than pleasant. However, based on my tranquil and tasty experience, this is a place I'd readily recommend for a poke fix in the city.

Title: A Mixed Bag at a Bustling Bistro

Last Friday night, I ventured into a bustling little restaurant that quickly revealed why its 8 tables are in such high demand – popularity doesn't necessarily mean availability. The place was swarming, and patience was essential, but the staff kept their cool, ensuring that, despite the wait, the service remained a high point of the evening.

The mixed feelings began when our drinks arrived. The mojitos, generously sugared but stingy on spirit, left me underwhelmed with a disappointing 2-star impression. As for the food, it was a rollercoaster of sorts. The noodles boasted a comforting yum factor, earning them a hearty 3.5 stars. However, the shrimp spring rolls, though tempting in description, were a letdown in both size and temperature. The steak salad initially impressed but eventually drowned in its own enthusiasm, begging for a sauce moderation that turned my taste buds off by the final forkful.

Awarding the service a well-deserved 4.5 stars, I acknowledge the restaurant staff's effort to keep the evening flowing smoothly. Although my review might come off as critical - perhaps a reflection of an overeager appetite - I believe in second chances. This eatery has earned itself a revisit, though next time, I'll be steering clear of the cocktail menu.

Great vegan restaurant with the most delicious food ever! We ordered the beet hummus which was delicious and came with a wide variety of vegetables to dip with it and we got the lentil chips because they were able to make it gluten free. I had the falafel platter for dinner which consisted of probably the best and freshest falafels I've ever had! We also got blackberry Mojitos which were so refreshing and tasty. For dessert we got the chocolate cake which tasted like a brownie and it came with a side of lavender ice creams which was the strangest ice cream ever but good! The staff was extremely attentive and constantly refilling our water cups which I appreciate. It was clean and romantic atmosphere. I can't wait to go back!

Title: A Tasty Surprise at Antico Noe

I recently ventured into Antico Noe, an Italian sandwich haven on 53rd St. just shy of 3rd Ave, lured by a tempting 50% off through Lunchspread. As someone who usually bypasses sandwiches for wraps, I was pleasantly surprised. The spot was clean and welcoming, with a delightfully short wait time at a prime lunch hour of 12:05 PM on a Thursday.

The staff, cheerful and familiar with their regulars, welcomed everyone with a hearty "Buon Giorno!" I took a chance on the #23, eager for the brie, but word to the wise: let them know if you want your panini halved when ordering. Post-order, the place quickly filled, affirming its popularity, but my panini arrived in just 5 minutes, piping hot and well-prepared.

Though delicious, the #23’s heat overshadowed the brie, but the variety on the menu means I'll return to taste my way through the other offerings. Seating is scarce, hinting at its to-go nature, but this doesn't detract from the quality. Antico Noe is a gem for anyone seeking a swift, savory bite.

$5.90 for an almond milk latte, but it was a stellar latte. On-point in terms of Australian style and quality, that's for sure. It was bigger than I expected, too, but I finished it in fewer than five minutes, because it was that good. The bitterness was just right. Two Hands is very sophisticated and modern inside. It feels open, relaxed, bright, and airy. Dreaming of Byron Bay white sands and sun? Pop in here for avocado toast (duh) and Melbourne-style coffee (what else) to satisfy that craving. Yeah, you're close to Little Italy and it feels sacrilegious to get a latte at an Australian place, but Two Hands makes it worth it. I'd love to return for a proper brunch one day, as they have pastries, sandwiches, and breakfast bites.

07.08.2019This place is located in a small food hall called "City Kitchen". Our first day here in NYC brought us here with my brother, bro-in-law and my family after dropping our luggage off at the hotel. We love food halls or food courts because we all want to eat something different so it's a perfect solution. I ordered the lobster combo with a clam chowder side and a blueberry lemonade. The lobster roll was the perfect size and I didn't even eat the entire thing. Hubby ate about half of it. The lobster was fresh, dressed well and lightly. Nothing over powered the taste of the fresh lobster.  The clam chowder was yummy and had pieces of potatoes and clams. The flavor was light and mild. Not too fishy tasting and also not too creamy--just a little of both. The blueberry lemonade was yummy!  I loved the slight sweetness of the blueberry with the tart lemonade.Price is a bit steep for such small portions but I wouldn't mind coming back to taste the lobster bisque.

During a recent visit to a local dining establishment, I opted to enjoy the ambiance on a particularly fine day. While the atmosphere was enjoyable, I'm afraid the same could not be said for the fare. I selected the chicken club from the menu and was met with disappointment. The chicken was not only lackluster in flavor, but it also had the unmistakable character of a frozen patty. This was particularly disheartening considering the price point, which could only be described as steep for the quality presented. I also perused the cocktail menu, which seemed creative and engaging; however, the excitement was dampened by the exorbitant costs attached to each concoction.

Disappointed mostly with the value.  Food was okay but coming from SoCal, the sushi here is nothing to write home about.  Service was solid, taste was okay but the value was a 1/5.  The rolls were comprised of 6 bite sized pieces for $12 - there are other spots in HK/UWS that either offer almost double the portion or 1/3 less the price.  The decor and ambiance here is cool so I assume people come here more for that than the food.  Save your money and head elsewhere.

Love the decor and music. Very rustic and warm feeling. I ordered the 1/4 chicken, avocado salad, and a side of tostones. The first bite of chicken was SOOOOOO juicy!! Despite the chicken being well cooked/juicy it was a little on the salty side. I enjoyed the salad as well but not worth $9. As for the tostones, they give you a good portion (about 5 or 6) for $4. I was satisfied with my meal and didn't feel gross or heavy afterwards. This is somewhere I'd be willing to come to once a week.

Shanghai Asian Cuisine serves solid food with reasonable prices! The vegetarian mock duck was great; I really enjoyed the smoothness/slight stretchiness of the mock duck with the chewy mushrooms, and the mushrooms were really flavorful and not mushroom-y in the typical way (which is high praise coming from someone who doesn't love mushrooms). As it's a cold dish, it came within a minute of ordering and was super refreshing!The xiao long bao were also really good today. The dumpling wrapper is as thin as can be, the soup inside is clear, and the meat isn't fatty, making for pretty light (but tasty!) bites.I dined at Shanghai Asian Cuisine last winter and was disappointed to find the meat in the xiao long bao a bit dry. There is perhaps a bit of inconsistency in the dumplings here, as some of the xiao long bao today were juicier than others. However, the staff were really nice, and I would recommend stopping by if you're in the area!
Love indikitch!! It's like fast food version of Indian food. Love that u get a bit of everything. Tasty and priced well. One of my fave spot

Last night, an unforeseen Midtown blackout disrupted our plans to dine at the Modern, but the staff's proactive efforts secured us a last-minute reservation at Manhatta, another gem in the Danny Meyer collection. As a personal favorite, I relished the opportunity to revisit, finding the menu had been thoughtfully updated—a practice that continues to pique my interest.

The meal commenced with market vegetables, a seemingly simple dish elevated by pristine freshness and a delightful gribiche. The butter poached lobster that followed was nothing short of exquisite, boasting a velvety butter sauce and a lavish portion of succulent lobster meat. To conclude, the chocolate mousse was an absolute pleasure and a must-try for any chocolate aficionado.

As a courteous touch, post-meal sweets were provided on the house, alongside a glass of dessert wine as an apologetic gesture for the earlier inconvenience. Although the wine veered towards the sweeter side for my palate, I valued the considerate act.

Anticipation for my next dining experience at Manhatta is already mounting, a testament to the lasting impression left by both the cuisine and the service.

Came here for a lunch special and saved money. It was a nice meal after Washington Square Park. Rasa is one of the relatively few Malaysian restaurants in New York. Even though it's easy to find Asian restaurants, this particular country isn't as represented here. The cuisine is pretty similar to Thai, with rice and often being spicy. After taking a nice walk around the park and arch, my new acquaintance and I headed over here. It was lunch and we got there in time to get the lunch special menu. This is a money saver. It has a number of menu items at pretty good prices. There's a lot that come with rice. It's not surprising because that ingredient is very cheap. Whatever though because the curries are very good on rice. I had the Green Curry. It's about $10 with tofu at lunch. This is made with bamboo, basil, coconut milk, eggplant, onions, and peppers. She had the Malaysian Curry. This is made with eggplant, okra, onions, peppers, and potatoes. I could return for lunch again. It's the best time to come. The specials are large and a good price.

Title: Secretive Spot with Style, But Unremarkable Bites

I ventured into this burger joint on a weeknight, lured by the buzz around its concealed entrance and cinematic ambiance. True to the whispers, the thrill of discovery was the highlight. Decked out with nostalgic movie posters, rustic wooden tables, and the glow of a vintage CRT TV, the decor charmed with its dive-y authenticity.

The burger, while a central piece of the experience, was unfortunately a bit of a letdown – the patty arrived slightly cold and leaned towards the dryer side, even if the sauce tried to make up for it. As for the fries, despite the hype, they struck me as pretty standard fare.

In summary, while the hideaway vibe tickles the fancy, the culinary performance won’t steal the show. It’s a place perhaps worth the detour for the novelty factor with visitors, but when it comes to the food, there're juicier, more satisfying options out there.

It's been a while since I last came to this place... I happen to be in the area w some friends & this was one of the only things opened late.  We came in & stayed in the front area by the bar. Drinks stuck to beer hard to go wrong. The pace itself wasn't too bad not jammed packed since it was later but decent enough. Decent mix of music playing, ok crowd .. service was good , decent place for drinks.

Title: A Spellbinding Cocktail Experience at a Chic Hotspot

If you're searching for a cocktail paradise with an enchanting twist, this is your destination. The vibe strikes the perfect balance between rustic charm and modern elegance, thanks to its exposed brick walls and contemporary furnishings.

The cocktail selection is nothing short of impressive, with a creative menu that pays homage to beloved movies - a treat for both mixology enthusiasts and film buffs alike. The famous Hogwarts Express is a crowd-pleaser, but the diverse concoctions ensure there's a spirited masterpiece for all.

A personal favorite is the Red is The New Black - a refined blend of Bombay Sapphire, St. Germain, and a symphony of raspberry, lavender, honey, and egg whites. It's as delicious as it is beautifully crafted.

Given its popularity, securing a spot via Open Table is wise. This place isn't just a bar; it's an experience. Cheers to an establishment that truly understands the art of a great drink!

Decided to stop by for a quick lunch and was glad I did! Ambiance: Cutest little spot! There's an "instagrammable" area where they have lights and a cute chair to sit in. Definitely could take some cute pics there. The colors and vibes keep you awake. I also saw a lady with a laptop there so you can sit and relax while enjoying a good meal. Food: My sister and I were stumped on what to order because everything sounded soooo good. We decided to try the pesto meatball sub, mac and cheese and chicken tenders. We love, love, LOVED the pesto meatball sub. The pesto was packed with flavor and sitting on that potato sub roll? To die for. The mac and cheese was okay, not my fave. I did like the shiitake bacon bits on top as it gave the mac and cheese a little more flavor. The chicken tenders tasted the same as every other vegan tender i've tried, not saying that this is a bad thing! I did like that they had different dipping sauces to choose from as well. Even though the food was good, I think next time i'm going to try a salad since everyone kept ordering one! They also have a wide range of vegan desserts to so I need to try those as well.Price: All 3 items were $26. I thought the food was a bit cheaper than usual for it being vegan and in NYC.Parking: There's some street parking but I took the train into the city so it wasn't a bad walk.Service: Fast and to the point, again, this isn't a bad thing!Try the pesto meatball sub everyone!

I came here for brunch and really enjoyed my meal.  A couple days after I decided try out their dinner menu. The layout/decor is simple and contemporary. The food here is amazing. You can tell they use fresh ingredients and puts a modern Mediterranean twist to traditional Italian cooking. Great wine list and creative cocktails kept me ordering drinks all night. If you are around NoMad and want to grab some fresh pasta, I highly recommended La Pecora. Enjoy! MUST TRY-Burrata-Gramigna (slightly spicy)-Meatballs-Nutella Tart (for 2)

Title: Royalty Regalia at Prince Street Pizza

From the first tantalizing bite, Prince Street Pizza ascends to the throne, claiming its rightful crown as pizza royalty. It's not just pizza; it's a revelation, a taste bud revolution that topples all former monarchs - sorry Joe's, you've been dethroned.

The spicy pepperoni forms a tangy aristocracy, the mozzarella stretches like the luxurious trains of royal gowns, and the hearty dough lays the foundation of this flavor palace. Each slice is an eruption of celestial delight, towing my senses into a whirlwind of flavor and sheer happiness.

Forewarning, the loyal subjects queue extensively on weekends, but for the indulgence of Prince Street Pizza's regal feast, patience is a small price to pay. Believe the hype, for when that first piece dissolves on your tongue, you too will feel the coronation of a new pizza sovereign. All hail Prince Street Pizza - a pie that guarantees love at first bite.

Title: A Carnivore's Delight at [Restaurant Name]

My partner and I celebrated our anniversary at [Restaurant Name], and it was nothing short of a carnivorous fantasy. The mantra here could easily be "eat meat until you're delightfully defeated," and it's a paradise for meat-lovers. Still, there's a nod to inclusivity with a salad bar—a palatable palette cleanser amidst the protein parade.

Service was exceptional—attentive waiters played along with photo ops and were keen on customizing meat thickness to our preference. They even caught on to our craving for beef ribs and promptly satisfied it. 

The showstopper? Their cheese bread. An addictive blend of stretchy, cheesy goodness that could rival the meats in consumption. Speaking of the meats, the beef rib reigned supreme with its succulent tenderness, followed closely by the impeccably seasoned and grilled lamb chops that made a lamb lover out of me.

Our experience at [Restaurant Name] was indulgent and memorable. I'd recommend it to anyone with a hearty appetite for quality meats—and suggest elastic waistbands for the aftermath. We'll be back after a brief veggie detox, and that's saying something.

pizza of my NY heart1.  This place was my brother's recommendation.  I'm glad I listened to him and bookmarked on my yelp account.2.  Many varieties of pizza to choose from.  Thankfully, it wasn't that busy we arrived; we were there between 300-500pm.  Since there were no crowds, my friend and I took our time perusing the selections.  I finally chose a slice of the surprema, while my friend (if memory serves correctly) chose a slice of the white pizza.  3.  The verdict:  The pizza is incredibly delicious!  Do stop by if you're visiting NYC!4.  Seating available.BOTTOM LINE:I've left a pizza of my heart in NYC.  Thank you NY Pizza Suprema!  I'll absolute return on a future trip.

I recently had a delightful brunch experience at a conveniently located restaurant just a stone's throw from Central Park.
