This place is fantastic for larger groups, offering a variety of seating options from tables to booths without the overwhelm of noise – conversation flowed easily among us. I didn't need my reservation, as the place wasn't packed even at 11 am on a Saturday.

I savored the Huevos Rancheros, which were quite tasty, and everyone in my group was pleased with their meals. Yes, the prices are a tad on the higher side, but that's New York for you. If you're in the city and looking for a pleasant brunch spot that facilitates group dining and a peaceful atmosphere, this could be your go-to, especially with the allure of a post-brunch stroll through Central Park.

I recently visited a Korean restaurant with my co-workers for a change of pace from the bustling Koreatown scene. The experience overall was enjoyable, especially given the generous array of side dishes that accompanied our meal, with the steamed egg dish standing out as a delightful favorite.

The variety was impressive and appreciated; however, I encountered a significant issue with my main dish, the Octopus Dolsot Bibimbap. Unfortunately, it was excessively salty, to the point where it detracted from the enjoyment of the meal and caused discomfort to my palate. Additionally, a better balance of ingredients could be achieved with an increase in the amount of rice, which would have mitigated the overpowering saltiness.

Despite this setback, the quality of the side dishes and the pleasant atmosphere leave the door open for a return visit. I'd be willing to give this restaurant another chance, especially if they take the feedback to heart and make an effort to reduce the salt in their dishes.

If you're hunting for the supreme pizza experience in New York, look no further. I've found a place that can only be described as 'the bomb dot com' when it comes to crafting the perfect pie. Not only is their pizza outstanding, but they also serve up excellent beer and pasta – a trifecta of Italian delights.

Seeing your pizza made fresh right before your eyes is part of the magic, and it lives up to the hype – it's truly AMAZING. Whether you're a local or just passing through, make it a point to stop by for a pie or a slice. This spot is a game-changer, and I guarantee you'll be back for seconds. Trust me, this is THE BEST PIZZA IN NY, bar none.

Really wanted to like this place because all of the great reviews and the Instagram posts of the decor. We joined the waitlist ahead of time and were seated 15 minutes after the estimated time. We were seated upstairs instead of the main floor with all the lights. The upstairs didn't have the same decor as downstairs, but it felt cozy.Our waitress was really nice. We ordered two drinks (forgot the names but they were tasty - not strong though). We got fried calamari and wings for the appetizer - both of which were great.For main entrees is where I was really disappointed. We got the pad kee mao and pad see ew with crispy half duck ($24 each). Half way through eating my dish I found a long hair in it and almost wanted to throw up. Our waitress was nice enough to offer to remake my dish, but I really did not want anything to do with this place.

Title: Cornerstone Cafe: The Gem of the Lower East Side

I'm rounding up to give Cornerstone Cafe a resounding 5-star review because it deserves every bit of praise. This eatery has mastered the art of delivering high-quality food at unbeatable values—case in point, their $8 Penne Vodka. It’s a delight to find a restaurant that doesn’t inflate prices for a dish that’s inexpensive to make, a refreshing change from the standard $16+ you'd begrudgingly shell out at other places.

But it's not just about the price here; the quality is remarkable. The goat cheese in their dishes? Creamy perfection. Plus, the Penne Vodka isn't just a lonely pasta—it comes with a side salad and bread, making it a full, satisfying meal.

The service holds up as well, contributing to the overall exceptional experience. Despite always being packed—which speaks volumes about their popularity—Cornerstone Cafe is a beacon of goodwill in the lower east side. Their commitment to quality ingredients, reasonable prices, and stellar service places them in my permanent recommendation list. Keep it up, Cornerstone Cafe; your fans, myself included, notice and appreciate what you stand for.

Tucked away in the bustling heart of Times Square, NYC, this burger gem stands out from the limited selection in the area. Despite its cozy confines, the turnover is quick—a boon for the hungry crowds. The highlight is the customizable burger experience, a delightful prospect for any aficionado looking to craft their perfect bite. The menu also offers ready-made options for those less inclined to design their meal.

The shoestring fries are a personal triumph, hitting all the right notes of crunchy and savory. To wash it down, a selection of milkshakes, sodas, and beers provides ample choice for pairing. Be warned, its popularity means you might encounter a queue and a high decibel level inside, but the reward is a burger that's charred and juicy in all the right places. If you're in Times Square with a burger craving, this spot is a must-try. Just hope for a shorter line and prepare for a treat. Enjoy!

I love ramen and I love that the noodles here are slightly different than the noodles at other ramen joints. The noodles here are a bit thicker which I really enjoy with the thick broth they serve. I got the eak ramen which I really liked. Also got the asian fries which were delicious with the mentai dipping sauce. Would also recommend the berry soju drink. Service was a bit slow but the food made up for it.

Waffle cones with maple syrup.   I'm down with that.Spicy buffalo chicken bites.  Sign me up.Cajun fries.  Absolutely.When you put all the pieces together, you can't go wrong with Chick'nCone.  The two times I've been there, service has been fast and friendly.    This place is dangerously close to my apartment so I have to resist the magnetic pull of the chicken or else I'd be eating there every day.One thing I like about getting it in the cone is that the cone has some sweetness to it and against the spiciness of the chicken, it's heaven on earth.  I am now advocating for more cone-based foods.

Title: A Gem for Vegans and Dog Lovers Alike!

Review:

On my second visit to this delightful vegan pizzeria, I must reaffirm its well-deserved 5-star rating. The staff remained exceptional; the hostess and our waitress went above and beyond, reserving our table generously even as we ventured nearby for a pre-dinner drink (and vegan appetizer at the adjacent Mexican spot!).

Bringing my dog along turned out to be a breeze, thanks to the spacious outdoor seating and the attentive service that included a refreshing cup of water for my furry companion. This welcoming atmosphere extended to the clientele, who engaged in friendly banter, drawn in by the charm of my four-legged icebreaker.

The restaurant itself impresses with beautiful decor and a prime location that makes for an airy, uncramped dining experience. But let's talk about the star of the show – the food. Skeptics in my party were converted; one, in particular, devoured her vegan pizza with the gusto of a true believer, erasing any doubts that dairy-free could achieve pizza perfection. We indulged in individual pizzas and shared a cacio e pepe that left us scrapping every last bit of the savory sauce.

This establishment stands as a testament to excellent service, convivial surroundings, and plant-based culinary excellence. I eagerly anticipate my next visit, and I'll be sure to bring along more friends and family to enjoy this wonderful find.

Tucked away in the bustling Hell's Kitchen area, this casual yet delightful spot consistently impresses with its culinary offerings. The menu is a testament to the use of fresh ingredients, ensuring each meal is as tantalizing as the last. Not to mention, their margaritas pack a punch, perfect for those who appreciate a well-crafted cocktail.

Upon arrival, guests are greeted with complimentary chips and salsa, a savory precursor to any meal. The staff here are not only easy on the eyes but provide top-notch service, enhancing the dining experience.

For the social media savvy, the lighting is particularly photo-friendly, ensuring your food snaps look as good as they taste. In all honesty, this restaurant doesn't miss a beat. It's a must-visit for anyone looking for a fuss-free, satisfying dining experience in Hell's Kitchen.

On a Friday night, this place was packed but they were able to accommodate my large party of about 12-15 people. The ambiance was loud yet nicely decorated, and we had enough space for our group.The food was decent, I got the 3 tacos, each $5 each: the al pastor, pescado, and carnitas. Some of the tacos felt too spicy, but they were filled with a lot of meat / fish and toppings. I thought that the pork in the carnitas taco was too tough to bite through, had to use a knife just to get bite sized pieces to chew, which I wasn't a fan of. They were very filling, however.This restaurant was OK overall ... the service was a little slow for the chips and guac our table got - we had to consistently ask for more chips among the 7 of us at one end of the table.

Nestled in a bustling city corner, Obao serves up a trendy fusion of Thai and Vietnamese cuisine within its compact, yet stylish bi-level space, bathed in mood-setting dim lighting. A bustling atmosphere greeted me for my 6 pm weekday reservation, with the restaurant already abuzz at 75% capacity.

Service at Obao proved impressive; the host and staff exuded warmth and efficiency, a notch above the standard. The attentive care was particularly noteworthy on the typically slower-paced second floor, yet here, no drop in service quality was evident. Waitstaff were commendably diligent, ensuring water glasses remained full and dishes arrived promptly.

I ventured to taste the Khao Soi, which while hearty and boasting perfectly springy egg noodles, fell somewhat short of my expectations. It leaned into a sweetness that hinted at a tailored experience for the American palate, somewhat distant from the authentic Thai flavors I sought. While the dish was enjoyable, it may disappoint purists.

However, Obao does not falter in presenting a pleasing dining experience, complete with the allure of beautiful hanging lamps that add an enchanting touch to the ambiance. For those open to a Western twist on Thai cuisine, Obao is a worthy consideration.

This pizza haven in midtown is a find! Offering two specialty slices with a fountain drink for under $10, it's a steal. The service is quick, perfect for a rapid in-and-out dining experience. Although I pass by daily, resisting the temptation to indulge in their delectable offerings is a daily challenge. While not every specialty slice hits the mark, choosing from the freshest pies usually guarantees satisfaction. A solid pick for anyone around Penn or perhaps post-fur coat shopping spree.

Oof, this was a letdown. Started with the Tropical Cup cocktail, then shared:+ Small mussels+ L'italien fries+ Agnolotti+ Meat & cheese board + Sticky toffee pudding Everything was just...fine. The meat and cheese board was heavy on the meats, with a combo of liver toasts and (mostly) hard cheeses, none of which I really loved. Mussels were yummy but could have been served hotter. The pasta and fries were tasty but not memorable. Dessert was good. Nothing too inspired happening here so I probably won't be back.

When you think of SoHo, you think: trendy, fashionable and edgy. This hotel encapsulated what this neighborhood is most known for.  This is a super friendly, clean and hip hotel. They have valet parking for $55 per 24 hours. They're located next to the trendy SOHO neighborhood where you'll find museums and tons of restaurants.  The hotel itself has a bar on the rooftop and cool lounge courtyard space with two cute little wooden cabins. The lobby has a candy shop and a restaurant called Harold's. Most of the bedrooms face inward and you can see into other people's beds if you don't have the blinds down. The rooms are on the smaller side but aren't cramped. The bathroom has a rain shower head with a modern sink. I liked that the TVs had Chrome cast so I could connect my iPad to the TV and watch movies. I also liked that you could control the entire room's light with the light switches by the headboard so you didn't have to get up out of bed to turn the lights out at night. Everything was very carefully thought out. The gentleman at the front desk was very smily, friendly, and calm. The entire front staff greeted us with perky smiles when we entered each time. The hotel key is also the access card to get up in the elevator so there is that added level of security. The rooms were very peaceful and quiet. The  hallways are a bit narrow and are dim but are clean, quiet, and have really cushiony carpets. The rooms came with two complimentary fancy water bottles in the hotel mini fridge. They don't have a fitness center. The room we were in wouldn't be great for folks who aren't intimate/close with each other because even when the sliding glass bathroom door was closed, there was a large crack/open space where one could see a person on the toilet. I loved the floating toilet seat and buttons to flush it. The entire design of the spaces were really modern and clean.

Tucked away in Chelsea Market, this culinary treasure next to Los Tacos is not to be missed. A straightforward menu with standout dishes like the superbly fresh fish ceviche, served generously with avocado on a tostada, is worth the visit alone. At $4.50, it's a steal for the quality and portion size. While the fish taco, at $3.75, is also great, the ceviche truly shines.

The drink selection impresses, especially their Clamato – a spicy michelada with a tamarind stick twist. For $12, it's the best I've had: rich in flavor, yet not overpowering. Accompanying your meal, you'll find an array of hot sauces, including a unique homemade peanut variety, encouraging a custom spice level.

Efficient and warm staff manage the quick-moving line, making the experience even better. Seating is limited but adequate, with a few tables and bar spots, plus ample standing room.

Overall, this place is a definitive five-star experience in New York's dining scene. Highly affordable for the quality offered, I can't wait to return.

I recently dined at this charming spot and have to say, it's quite a find! Their offerings are a delightful fusion of flavor and creativity. The standout for me was the kale Caesar salad, a harmonious blend of vegan Parmesan, robust Caesar dressing, and ingenious additions like maple croutons and shiitake bacon - even as a kale skeptic, I was thoroughly impressed.

The air fries are another must-try, perfectly crispy and served with two unique sauces - the aioli being my top choice over the beet ketchup due to texture preferences, though both were tasty. The taco salad, with its seitan "beet" and crisp tortillas, packs a punch of flavor and is surprisingly filling at just over 500 calories, even if the spiciness was a bit much for my palate.

The one miss for me was the soba noodles, which unfortunately didn't live up to the rest of the menu when they substituted my original choice. It lacked the exciting flavor profile found in their other dishes.

The convenience of ordering via an app for a quick pick-up is a major plus, and the ambience of the place adds to the overall positive experience with its cozy and inviting vibe, complete with swing chairs.

I'd recommend this restaurant not only to vegans and vegetarians but to anyone looking for a satisfying meal that doesn't skimp on taste or imagination.

Stumbled upon this place looking for food and drinks and Juraka is solid!! The drinks here were all phenomenal. I love that the cocktails are all so unique and tasty. They also offer excellent happy hour deals here and if you check in on yelp, you can get a free app for the table. In terms of food, I'd recommend the yakiniku, the beef was super flavorful and and the dressing over their salad was really good! The skewers were tiny but the chicken one was super juicy. Really dig their gingertini - it's not what you expect in terms of flavor but it packs a good punch. Servers were great, the place is super chill - they even make their own stickers on instagram so make sure to check those out too!!

Went here for my cousins birthday and it was an amazing time. Server was nice and even though she prepped me for what I was about to have,  I still was not ready. Since we were in a large group, we did a pre fix menu which was $65 per person. But wow, the food was amazing. Between the whiskey wings, chicken, truffle pizza, truffle fries, steak and salad...needles to say that I was more than full by the time I left the restaurant. Went on a Saturday night and they had a DJ there that was good. Drinks were also good, but after my meal, I could barely fit anything else. I would definitely come back to this place as I had an amazing time.

As a huge fan of roasted pork and duck, I love this place so much. I always get a mix of roasted pork and duck over rice and it's so delicious. It tastes so authentic and the price is unbeatable. There's always a long line, but it gets short pretty quickly so don't just walk away because of the line! It's a take out place and there's no seats inside, so I usually take it home and even if I eat some leftovers the next day by using the microwave, it's still sooo good!

Cute little brunch spot! As you wind your way towards what you think is the back of the restaurant, you find yourself squeezing through a corridor to get to another dining room. Great ambiance, very accommodating for our group of 12 with attentive and straight forward service. The drinks came quickly and the 3 for 1, $13 brunch drink special is a total steal! We found the brunch menu to be a bit overwhelming in terms of options and description, but we all seemed to find something that worked. The food was definitely a different take on brunch which I always appreciate the attempt, execution wasn't the tastiest I've ever had. But overall, this was a fun spot with a good vibe and we walked away happy! Just a note to diners - it's cash only so make sure to come prepared.

Spoonfed had an awesome, cozy atmosphere on a Friday night (loved the live music!). Be sure to make a reservation if you're coming on a weekend. The fried chicken with the "darker the berry" sauce was incredible. Totally decadent, but worth it. I really liked that they gave you a mix of bone-in and boneless chicken pieces (two of each). The highlight of the meal for me was the homemade biscuit though - I'm not usually a huge biscuit lover, but theirs was SO fresh. I topped it with a piece of the boneless fried chicken and a generous pour of the berry sauce, and I was in heaven. Thumbs up to the mashed potatoes as well. They also brought out some pears with a balsamic glaze as a complimentary snack while we waited for our meal - I love little extra touches like that. The side of cornbread that we ordered was OK (probably my least favorite item, but not bad by any means). I was a little bummed that they mentioned they were out of the cider that was on their menu, but the red wine that I chose was a worthy replacement.Definitely plan at least 90 minutes for your meal - our attempt to get in and out in about an hour was probably unrealistic from the start (and I take full responsibility for that). Our server was great though, and was willing to bring us the check while we finished up our entrees, so that we could get out of the restaurant in plenty of time to make our show. This place is worth a visit if you're in the area for sure.

Title: A Manhattan Gem for Steak Lovers

I recently dined at what has now become my favorite steakhouse in Manhattan, and I must say, the experience was nothing short of stellar. From the attentive waitstaff who struck the perfect balance between presence and privacy to the thoughtful guidance to the restroom, each detail was handled with care.

The highlight of my visit was the surf and turf - a culinary masterclass featuring a succulent filet mignon paired with a delicate arrangement of lobster, king crab, and shrimp. The steak was a revelation, flawlessly cooked and seasoned to perfection. It's no overstatement to say that it ranks as one of the finest steaks I've ever had the pleasure of tasting. This restaurant truly sets the standard for a premium dining experience.

Title: A Culinary Gem with Hit-or-Miss Service

My recent dinner experience at this establishment was a blend of delights and disappointments. While securing a reservation was a challenge, resulting in a late 9pm slot for date night, the culinary journey was stellar enough to garner a 5-star rating on the food alone.

The complimentary puff pastry starter was unexpectedly delightful, a creative mix resembling a scallion pancake crossed with a cream cheese spread. The fluke dish presented a visual and gustatory spectacle with its yuzu coconut pairing, a raw yet unrecognizably smooth treat. The octopus entrée was a textural triumph, so irresistible that it vanished before a photo could be taken, but left me longing for more than a single piece.

The snow crab noodles left a lasting impression, with the truffle variant enhancing the dish's depth. The dual order, one with and one without truffle, revealed a preference for the earthy fungus's addition. However, a more generous helping of snow crab would be appreciated.

To conclude, the beignets suggested by the waitstaff to be converted into ice cream sandwiches were a novel and delectable innovation, their heat indicative of a freshly-made dessert, the goat milk caramel sauce balancing sweetness without overpowering.

However, the service was disproportionately underwhelming. Initially, our waiter was adequate but not exceptional. As the evening progressed and a shift change occurred around 10:15pm, the new waiter's attention shifted noticeably towards tables with all female clientele, leaving us feeling somewhat neglected.

Ultimately, I would return for the food's allure with aspirations for a service that rises to meet the high bar set by the cuisine.

Title: A Delightful First-Time Hotpot Experience at Dalongyi

As a newcomer to the world of Chinese hotpot, my visit to Dalongyi provided a delightful and memorable dining experience. I opted for the restaurant's signature three-way pot, featuring a comforting tomato base, a savory mushroom soup, and the fiery Dalongyi oil chilli broth. Although the chilli broth proved too spicy for my taste with its abundance of peppercorn, the other two broths were nothing short of delicious.

The ingredients, ranging from meats to vegetables, were impressively fresh, often served on ice to maintain their crispness. The freshness of these components truly elevated the meal, making each bite a testament to Dalongyi's commitment to quality.

While I thoroughly enjoyed the food and overall atmosphere of the restaurant, it's worth noting that the experience comes with a higher price tag. A meal for two reached $180, so it's something I'll be keeping in mind for future visits. Despite the cost, I highly recommend Dalongyi for anyone looking to indulge in an authentic and satisfying hotpot meal.

Title: Bustling NYC Gem with Delectable Fare

My recent culinary adventure at this bustling local hotspot in NYC proved to be worth the buzz, especially since a mere 10-minute wait with a reservation led to a delightful dining experience.

The fried chicken dumplings, resembling empanadas, were a savory start, with juicy chicken complemented by a lightly sweet sauce. While I didn't sample the seafood ramen, my companion's satisfied silence spoke volumes about its quality.

The bulgogi hot stone dish was a standout, with well-done yet tender beef mingling with brown rice in a heated bowl, all enhanced by a mild, slightly sweet orange-red sauce. The slight timing misstep of our pork buns arriving mid-entree was easily forgiven, thanks to their spongy texture and succulent, melt-in-your-mouth pork.

A pleasant surprise included a free shot of a lichi-flavored house cocktail for checking in on Yelp, an enticing concoction hinting at a tipsy treat if it were a full glass. Despite the crowd, the hostess maintained composure, and our slightly timid but attentive server ensured our order was precise.

Without a doubt, this place is a culinary jewel worth visiting. The only note for improvement would be the sequencing of dishes, but it's hardly a deal-breaker. Overall, a great dining experience that I would recommend to anyone seeking a taste of local NYC flavor.

Title: A Pleasant Return After Years

After a lengthy hiatus of 15 years, I revisited this Vietnamese gem situated conveniently near a subway station, an obvious draw for tourists. The bustling vibe didn't disappoint; the place has maintained its charm.

The cuisine was delightful, reminiscent of the dishes I savored on a recent trip to Vietnam. Service was notably sharp and courteous. Though the prices edged slightly above the neighborhood's norm, the experience was worth that extra bit.

A light-hearted chat with the owner, who amused me in Cantonese, added a personal touch to the meal. They considerately seated us in a quiet corner to accommodate my daughter's nap—a gesture I appreciated, especially when a large tourist group arrived, yet she remained undisturbed.

While my nostalgia was briefly interrupted by the stark price difference compared to Vietnam, it didn't detract from the overall satisfaction. My verdict? A solid 3.5 out of 5, as there are other favorites in Chinatown that hold a slightly higher place in my heart.

Instagram: @Danyoizme

Title: Casual Midtown Pub Experience

Dined with friends at a typical midtown pub for a casual dinner and despite a hiccup with our reservation which they couldn't find, we were promptly seated without issue at 6pm on a Friday. The ambiance in the downstairs back area was suitable for our group's laid-back gathering.

Service was a mixed bag -- our server was personable and attentive, yet had a habit of dashing off before our table could place full requests. While the overall food quality was acceptable, the establishment's rendition of a "veggie burger" fell short, consisting of a fried green tomato and mozzarella on a bun, a tasty combination but a stretch to call a burger.

In summary, this pub offers a decent spot for a no-fuss meal among friends despite some service quirks and a somewhat misleading menu item.

Title: Mixed Feelings at La Loteria's Happy Hour

I popped into La Loteria aiming to indulge in their touted margarita variety during happy hour. Despite having a reservation, the place was notably uncrowded with a good 40% of seats vacant. A quick heads-up for fellow happy hour enthusiasts: you'll need to park yourself in the bar area to snag those special prices.

The margarita lineup didn't disappoint – we tried the blackberry, guava, and a classic. The guava margarita hit a sweet note, perhaps too sweet for some, while the rest were quite enjoyable. To pair with our drinks, we went for the guacamole and chips combo. While the margaritas made a good impression, the food, unfortunately, didn't follow suit. The guacamole and chips were just passable – not the burst of flavor you'd expect for a $20 combo.

We chose not to explore the menu further based on our initial sampling. Even though the food was underwhelming, La Loteria did score points with its charming interior and an inviting outdoor patio. A decent spot if you're here for the drinks and ambiance, but perhaps look elsewhere if you're craving a memorable meal.

Upon visiting this charming eatery, I was treated to a grilled cheese sandwich that was nothing short of amazing. The bread was toasted to perfection, creating a delightful crunch that yielded to a cascade of gooey, melted cheese. Additionally, the service was notably friendly, enhancing the dining experience. A pleasant surprise was the complimentary water, a simple touch that didn't go unnoticed. This restaurant comes highly recommended for a satisfying meal that is sure to leave you impressed.

I've been to some clubhouses in NY. Recently I went to a Harmonie Club for an alumni event. They booked a good size room for about 75 attendees. I love events because they try to serve good (if not great) hors d'oeuvres. This time it was a great one. We had a panel discussion followed by a networking event. The interior of the clubhouse is peaceful and cozy. The lobby's quiet and quite small and the logo can be found all over the clubhouse. It's a clubhouse and not a hotel, so you don't always see people. "I see dead people!" I'm kidding! I'm kidding! The service was of course excellent because professionalism is their utmost importance. My friends and I enjoyed the hors d'oeuvres although I didn't get to take the photos due to my hands being occupied with a plate and a drink, sorry! But I enjoyed the hors d'oeuvres.

Ventured into a cozy brunch spot today and I must rave about their Strawberry Pistachio Morning Bun - it’s a slice of heaven that's perfect for sharing. While indulging in its flaky, sweet layers, I did find myself longing for a wider selection of vegetarian choices. More veggie-centric dishes would certainly tempt me to return with greater frequency. Here's hoping they'll expand their menu to charm herbivores like myself. Hats off, @traveleen_gurl for the recommendation!

The best, of the best, of the best!!! Cannot go wrong here, especially with Fadil Morina! Had laughs the whole entire night! Absolutely delicious food, absolutely delicous drinks, and the service??? Absolutely phenomenal!!! Best visit here for a first time! Definitely recommend, definitely will come back again!

Large, clean, bright space. Friendly, attentive service. I had the teriyaki shrimp bowl-it came with 5 large shrimp-very tasty, and a 5 pieces of steamed broccoli over rice. For it to be worth $20 I would add maybe 2-3 more pieces of shrimp and 2-3 more pieces broccoli. The steamed broccoli had no teriyaki sauce, nothing on it, no flavor. I asked for a little dish of extra sauce which they happily provided.The shrimp was bursting with flavor. My husband had the tonkotsu ramen which he enjoyed. We judge ramen based on how perfectly cooked the egg is...and it was pretty darn close. It looked definitely marinated at least 1-2 days. He will review separately. They also gave us complimentary ice cream scoop which was very nice. Green tea is no charge, but you need to ask for it.

Title: Hidden Gem in Chinatown - Au Cheval

Nestled in an unassuming alley of Chinatown, Au Cheval is a stark contrast to its gritty exterior with a chic and modern interior adorned with dark wood furnishings. My friend and I popped in for lunch and were met with both exceptional food and attentive service.

Pros:
- The Bone Marrow, accentuated by a rich and balancing cheek sauce, was a standout dish. Its flavorful yet heavy nature makes it an ideal choice for a party of four. [4.5 STARS]
- Their signature Cheeseburger, enhanced by a perfectly runny egg and delectable bacon, is a must-try for first-timers. While the added toppings elevate the experience, repeat visitors might find the burger stellar on its own. [4 STARS]
- Service was a high point, with our server displaying a warm and diligent approach, ensuring our experience was nothing short of satisfactory.

The Okay:
- Although the General Jane's Honey-Fried Chicken boasted a crispy coat with a tantalizing honey glaze, it teetered on the edge of being excessively salty. Best enjoyed in smaller servings. [3 STARS]
- The Mille Feuille's airy vanilla cream and flaky crust were delightful, but the overall sweetness was a bit overpowering. The pastry might remind some of Taipan's Napolean cake. [3.5 STARS]

In conclusion, Au Cheval offers a dining experience that's as surprising as it is fulfilling, with a couple of dishes that might cater to specific palates. It's a venue where quality and care in service are as evident as in their culinary creations.

When we arrived the place was crowded, but we were seated quickly since one of our party made a reservation. The bar and wine list are quite extensive, but we chose to be non-alcoholic and ordered iced tea and coffee. Perusing the menu I noticed that they were proud they smoked and cured their meats. One of our party ordered the chicken sausage and eggs and I ordered pastrami and eggs. The outer edge of the pastrami was delicious with that pepper and spice crust, but the flavor got lost as you moved away from the edge, unlike you would have at a deli. I also thought the dish could have used more than two slices of pastrami. The chicken sausage, on the other hand, was delicious with a little bit of heat in the mixture. I had to lower the rating seeing as our server kept passing my empty cup of coffee and never asked if I wanted more and I finally had to request one.

Title: A Soulful Delight at Sylvia's in Harlem

My girlfriend and I found ourselves ravenous in Harlem and, after some research, Sylvia's Soul Food emerged as the beacon of our cravings. It was immediately apparent that this was an establishment with roots as deep as the flavors promised by its menu. Despite a sizable crowd, the typical NYC wait time of 30 minutes did little to dampen our spirits.

The anticipation was sweetened by a serving of warm cornbread, setting the stage for what was to come. The main event did not disappoint - the fried chicken was the epitome of crispy perfection, while the sides of mac and cheese and collard greens were nothing short of soul-warming triumphs. At around $40 for two, the experience was a steal.

In short, should you find yourself in Harlem with an appetite, Sylvia's is the place to feed your soul. The food, ambiance, and value are a recipe for satisfaction. Trust me, disappointment isn't on the menu here.

Title: Midnight Ramen Fix with a Twist

If you find yourself with an insatiable craving for ramen at 1:30 AM, this hole-in-the-wall spot might just be your savior. Keep in mind it's a cash-only establishment, though there's no need to panic as there's an ATM conveniently located across the street.

Our experience kicked off on a positive note with some delectable gyoza, which set a high expectation for the main event. However, while the ramen broths were unanimously praised for their variety and robust flavors, the noodle substitute was a bit of a letdown. Out of the four of us, only one actually received the traditional ramen noodles, with the rest of our bowls curiously sporting angel hair pasta. This was a rather unusual choice that was tasty enough but admittedly dampened the authentic ramen experience we were after.

In summary, while the dishes were enjoyable on the whole, the unconventional pasta swap was enough to leave us slightly off-kilter. Therefore, I'd give this late-night spot a solid 3 out of 5 stars. It's great for a quick ramen fix, but it might leave purists yearning for the real deal.

Always a fan of Indian fusion restaurant and when you get mexican and Indian food at one place, then its a bonus. So this place have tacos(made of Indian bread - Naans/Rotis) with indian curries. I have tried Chicken Malai kabab naan taco,chicken tikka masala roti taco and lamb curry roti taco. Although this is a very small shop with limited seating inside but they have outdoor seating of 5-6 tables as well.They also have vegetable tacos which include Naan/Roti tacos with any vegetable curry(Chickpeas, Lentils). Service is quick and interior looks clean. They have hand sanitizers on end of each table. Their kitchen is very small, I guess they prepare the food before and when order comes, then they start making it accordingly.Chicken malai kabab -5/5It was a huge naan with chicken malai kababs, white sauce on the top and was garnished with red cabbage and some greens. Overall it was a great dish, taste of the soft naan with sauce and chicken kababs was delicious. The chicken kababs were flavorful as well.Chicken Tikka Masala Roti Taco - 5/5If you dont want to eat heavy then this is the best option, it is a roti(Indian round bread) rolled with chicken tikka masala and salad. The taste was amazing. I wish roti to be big enough for atleast 4-5 bites. I finished it in 2 bites only(:D)Lamb Curry Roti Taco - 4/5It was same like above but with Lamb curry. Lamb was soft and again great taste. The spices were to the level in both tacos.I highly recommend this place if you want to eat Indian food with fusion.

Title: Lacking the Mediterranean Magic

Saturday brunch at this highly talked-about spot fell short of expectations, leaving us mostly underwhelmed. The menu initially seemed promising, but the execution didn't hit the mark. Our kickoff with mimosas was uneventful, but the subsequent dishes didn't deliver the Mediterranean zest we had anticipated, particularly the flavorless paprika hummus.

The disappointment seeped into our main courses as well. The shakshuka was a letdown—simple, overly sweet, and undercooked. Similarly, the menemen eggs suffered from the same sweetness and lack of proper cooking, necessitating extra seasoning just to meet our palate preferences. Thankfully, the steak was the saving grace, pleasing at least one of our party.

Our experience concluded with us seeking satisfaction elsewhere at Thelewala with their nizami rolls. Perhaps this establishment shines brighter with its dinner offerings, but as for brunch, it's a no-go unless they step up their game.

New addition to the village. Love the concept of layering with the texture and flavor, esp the wafer crunch. I had the small Gem Bing with pork floss. I thought the soybean sauce did not fit in, for the entire thing, or possibly just for the pork floss. The sauce they have now is close to what we eat with Beking Duck (only) I think they would need the more traditional (maybe sweet oyster sauce kind) that would be more balanced?

A great neighborhood spot, not pretentious at all, and very comfortable.  Wooden tables, a small bar with an efficient, friendly bartender, and usually some interesting selections on the dinner specials menu.  Staff is helpful and the cocktails are well done!

I had been eyeing this restaurant ever since sampling their breakfast offerings at my workplace. Excited to dive into their lunch menu, I opted for the spicy Thai salad, priced at $11.50. Expecting a flavor-packed bowl, I was greeted by greens, quinoa, crispy wontons, glazed tempeh, and a peanut dressing. Unfortunately, the salad underwhelmed me, being too sweet and quite basic for my taste. Despite this, I'm not writing them off just yet; the burger options caught my eye and I’m eager to give them a try.

The true star of my visit was the banana bread – a steal at just $3.45. It was a superb treat: super soft, perfectly balanced sweetness, and altogether delectable. It alone earns the restaurant four stars from me. I'm already planning my next visit, with the banana bread on my mind and the burgers in my sights, not to mention the tempting cupcakes!

Came here with a few of my friends for a casual dinner. Food was fantastic! Service was good, drinks were amazing! I got to practice my French I learned while visiting Paris this past summer lol.Very cozy and intimate, would love to see what this brunch is all about!

This is a solid find in Lower Manhattan for lunch or an easy dinner. I always get the same thing, the Bueno Bowl - Mojo thigh, brown rice, black beans, guacamole, pico de gallo, maple chipotle sauce. I love that they do huge globs of guac and the chicken is marinated really good! (as the name would imply).

Title: Chic Ambiance Meets Mixed Service at Trendy Eatery

My dining experience at this up-and-coming hotspot proved to be a bit of a roller coaster. The restaurant's interior design is striking and elevated the overall cool atmosphere, though the seating arrangements at the high tables could benefit from an ergonomic tweak to enhance comfort.

The service kicked off on a high note - friendly and efficient. However, as the place filled up, the promptness waned, and the odd change of servers mid-meal, despite the original waiter's presence, was puzzling.

The drink menu was a highlight. My 'Sleeveless Hoodie' cocktail was impressive, and my friend's '90s-inspired beverage didn't disappoint. Kudos to the bus staff for keeping us hydrated on a hot day.

Pasta dishes were the stars of the show. My black fettuccine with seafood hit all the right notes with its richly flavored sauce. Everyone at the table seemed pleased with their choices.

However, the moment for sweets turned sour as we were neglected when it came time for dessert and another round of drinks. Attempting to flag down a server became a sport we hadn't anticipated playing. In the end, we opted for the check over a delayed dessert.

This restaurant has the potential for greatness, with its excellent drinks and delicious food. If they could iron out the service kinks, I'd have no reservations about returning for a second helping.

Title: Udon Deserves the Spotlight at Raku

Raku in NYC is a minimalist haven for udon enthusiasts, offering a fresh alternative to the ubiquitous ramen scene. The decor’s stark contrasts allow diners to focus on their slurping, though the lack of a proper entrance can let in a chill during cold weather, a slight setback in comfort for the sake of aesthetics.

The drink selection includes the premium Sapporo Reserve, elevating the usual beer experience. The Chicken Tatsuta-age, while crispy, falls short on tenderness and flavor despite its marination, but the Ankimo is a star: a creamy monkfish liver delicacy that comes in a rich but portion-conscious serving.

The udon dishes are where Raku truly shines. The Niku Udon, with its incredibly tender tripe and succulent short rib, combines with a lightly flavorful broth and perfectly al-dente noodles for a heartwarming meal. The Kamonan udon's duck breast, however, suffers from chewiness, and its shoyu broth leans toward the ordinary.

Service is sharp and attentive, a small wonder given the surplus of staff for such a cozy space. Note: it’s cash only, which can be inconvenient. Although I hover between 3.5 and 4 stars, the drafty dining experience nudges me to a 3-star rating. Raku’s udon bowls are worth braving the cold blast at the door, proving that udon deserves its share of the spotlight.

Really a great and peaceful time here.I bookmarked this a while back and was surprised to find out it's on the same block as my boyfriend's apartment. I've been passing by it for months and only realized!The front of the restaurant is very nondescript and also says "SUSHI" in green letters. (They don't serve sushi.)On our anniversary, we decided to pull the trigger and head in on a cold Sunday evening. The place was mostly empty and playing soft j-pop.We grabbed a seat in the front and ordered three apps and a katsudon to share.The waitress was nice, left us to our own devices and wasn't judgemental at all. I was so ready to have a bad experience based on these reviews. It was a great time.The katsudon was great. (More pretty than delicious.) The real show stopper was the tomato soup. I had never had anything like it before. Definitely a real treat.It was around 45~ for the two of us. Average for comfort food.Well yes, I can go across the street and make a katsudon cheaper and the same quality. But the atmosphere is calming and I'm interested in the other dons.I will be back. It's great to find quality Japanese food on the UES.

In the bustling metropolis of NYC, finding an exceptional udon spot can be a challenge, yet this gem truly sets itself apart. Their niku udon (beef) is a showstopper – the noodles are perfectly chewy and swim in a rich, savory broth that's absolutely divine. Starting off with the age tofu appetizer primes the palate with its delightful flavor and texture. A sweet, refreshing touch awaits at the end of the meal with a couple of frozen grapes, a simple yet ingenious treat. Despite its modest size, this place is worth any potential wait for a table. Count me in for a return visit – this noodle haven is not to be missed!

I recently dined at Bodhi in Chinatown and was thoroughly impressed with the quality of their vegan offerings. Best known for their dim sum, Bodhi's menu is entirely vegetarian, with plant-based versions of meat that are convincingly similar to the real thing. Amidst an area bustling with fusion eateries and dwindling authentic spots, Bodhi stands out for its authentic flavor profile and an extensive vegetarian selection.

The ambiance of the restaurant added to the experience, as my friend and I enjoyed our meal with a charming view of Mulberry Street from our front table. I savored a Vegetarian Beef Noodle Soup, priced reasonably at $9 for a generous portion. The 'beef' was a step up from the usual tofu fare in both texture and taste, and the mushroom broth was a flavorful base for the variety of vegetables within. My friend delighted in the Vegetarian Chicken Fried Rice, equally content with her choice.

Though we didn’t indulge in dessert, the tofu cheesecake—lauded as vegan—caught my eye for a future visit. Bodhi proves that vegetarian cuisine can be both affordable and delectable without compromising on authenticity. It’s a gem for vegetarians and food enthusiasts alike; we're already looking forward to exploring more of the menu.

Knockdown 5 star place in the West Village. This is one of the more unique concepts you will find. It is a furniture store but on the rooftop it is a bar/restaurant. There is also a bar on the 3rd floor if you want to grab a drink you can and you can hang out in the showrooms while you wait for your reservation. Now they don't take reservations at the Rooftop so come early and put your name down or else you will be waiting. It is such a cool vibe here. They have the restaurant but also outdoor seating where you can get a drink and chill. Problem is they dont have table service for the outdoor seating area. You have to go to the 3rd floor to get a drink. A little surprising but whatever.As for the food, I loved the burger with fries. Burger was perfectly cooked and fries were fresh and crispy. I didnt expect much from the food honestly because you never know if a rooftop is all novelty and no substance. It wasnt the case here. We also ordered the cheese board and it was good but I would skip it next time only because cheese boards are consistently underwhelming to me. The drink selection is also on point. This place isnt cheap so come ready to spend some dough.Based on the full experience this is the definition of a 5 star place. The service was awesome too. They dont rush you out and they let you enjoy the experience. I would recommend to anyone visiting nyc or wanting a cool unique experience.

I met up with a group of friends. It didn't take long to get our table. Just had to have all the party present. This place is clearly popular but it is huge and was packed with people. Our server Shon, was friendly and helpful about questions with menu items. I ordered the sticky chicken fingers and yellow rice. That rice was looking so good on other's plates in the restaurant. My friends who ordered appetizers or salad got their food first which was fine. Then shortly after all the other food came out. It was a lot of food. I loved the flavor to the sticky fingers and the rice was good without adding anything to it Sorry that I didn't take a photoS of my food. The food was good just check it out. I would definitely explore the menu more next time in town. My only drawback was the check situation. We all had so many things on the order and one check so we had to break it up so many ways to pay. I will go back to visit soon.

Title: A Slice of New York Excellence

Walking into this pizzeria, one is instantly struck by the promise of authentic New York-style pizza—and it delivers. The bill may come as a bit of a surprise, it's true, but so will the quality of your meal. The pizza here is simply some of the best I've ever had; a testament to why New York's reputation for pizza is well-earned.

While the prices are higher than your average pizzeria, your taste buds will thank you for the splurge. With a wide array of toppings available, customization is at your fingertips, ensuring that your pizza is exactly to your liking. And as if the pizza itself wasn't enough, the full bar is the proverbial cherry on top, making this not just a meal, but an experience.

Do not hesitate to visit this place if you're ready to pay for premium taste. Chances are, you'll find that it's worth every penny.

Not sure if I made stellar order choices (heh heh) or if everything happens to be super good!!! I came here with my boyfriend and we ordered the soup dumplings, scallion pancakes, sweet and sour ribs, and chicken dry pot. Baodega really surprised me -it was a pleasant experience from the food to the nice decor and calming music. I can't decide which dish I loved most:*the pork soup dumpling had pretty great flavor, not too much or too little soup, and I loved the texture of the wrapper (soft but not thin)*the sweet and sour pork ribs were fantastic -succulent, great serving size, and packed with flavor*the chicken fry pot was fiery -literally. Great presentation and filled with a good mix of veggies and really moist and well marinated chicken cubes. Also, there's a cool craft coffee area in the front of the shop that also serves matcha.Give this place and go and definitely order at least one of the above! You'll love your experience. Plus, prices are fair and the people are nice

Title: A Festive Evening with Exemplary Service!

From the moment our party of 12 was seated, our experience at the restaurant was nothing short of fantastic. Kudos to my friend's sister for securing a reservation and arranging a personalized menu in celebration of the bride-to-be. Each cocktail, especially the Oaxaca Express, was expertly mixed and utterly addictive. For those with dietary restrictions, the staff is commendably knowledgeable; they ensured my fish tacos were pan-fried to gluten-free perfection. The chicken poblano main course lived up to the high standard set by the starter. In a true test of service, the staff demonstrated honesty and care when I left my phone behind. They safeguarded it and returned it before closing. For both their culinary prowess and outstanding service, this restaurant earns a solid A+.

I went in with low expectations, considering the reviews and thinking that pickle flavored soft serve was a gimmick. It's pretty good! I neither love nor hate pickles, but was curious to try it out. I expected a briny, sour taste and instead was pleasantly surprised to find it tasted slightly tart, kind of like the original pinkberry flavor. The pickle flavor was very mild and gave it a light savory flavor. I love a good balance of savory and sweet and I think this hit the right note.I also tried the pumpkin flavor, which is seasonal in the Fall. The pumpkin flavor was also subtle, and I think it would pair deliciously with a Pumking beer. You're welcome.The only savory food item I've had here is their cold sesame noodle dish, and it's not bad. I'm not sure I'd return, but I'm glad I tried it once.

This is my go to cheap eat in the east village! They have both broth noodle soups (good for winter) and dry noodle dishes (good for summer). The place is relatively small but you could get a group of 8 in there if you combine all the tables.What I love about Yunnan Rice Noodles is the texture - it is so silky and light! I've tried the tofu rice noodle with pork, cold rice noodle with chicken, little pot rice noodle, mouthwatering chicken & cucumber salad...they were all delicious! They also have tons of vegetarian options too.I will definitely return soon to try the Kunming Tender Beef Rice Noodle.

I recently dined at Madame Pho and sampled their signature dish, the classic Madame Pho. While the broth was adequately clear, the dish failed to justify its nearly $30 price tag, offering an average experience. For those seeking a truly memorable pho, I suggest trying Hanoi House just down the block.

Title: Tacos Fall Short at Local Eatery

I ventured in hoping for a satisfying taco experience, however, I found myself disappointed. Ordering was a struggle; the cashier repeatedly misunderstood my request to dine in, resulting in a takeout mix-up. The service was painfully slow and unprofessional, with staff using coarse language within earshot.

Once I finally received my $12 taco order, the quality left much to be desired. The tortillas were stale, and the meager filling was a letdown. On a brighter note, the $6 extra for chips and guac was the meal's saving grace—generous in portion, although the chips lacked seasoning.

My advice? Drop in for the chips and guac if you must, but skip the tacos to avoid frustration and wasted energy.

this place is crazy crowded when we got here but service was really quick and we got seats in less than 5 mins. service was awesome! everybody is so attentive and helpful! we love it! we ordered the galbi platter, the pork platter, and sundubu jjigae (tofu soup)! they have extensive choice of banchan (complimentary side dishes) - spring onion salad, kimchi, kimchi jjigae, gyeran mari (steamed egg), and many more. even the banchan tastes great. they cook the meat for us and you can eat it right away but I usually make some sort of wrap: use 1 lettce leaf, fill it with meat, a little bit of kimchi and little but of spring onion salad (or anything you like), wrap it into tiny package and stuff the whole thing in your mouth. this way there will a burst of flavor once you bite into it. but even without that, the meat in itself has great texture. need sauce to have more flavor though. for a price i think it's a little bit too much but well it's pretty good

It's not Chinatown,but if you're smack in the middle of the theater district, and are looking for soup dumplings, and don't want a drawn-out, overpriced white tablecloth experience, then Kung Fu Little Steamed Buns is the place to go on 8th Avenue. Most tables are communal. Service is fast and efficient. Dumplings are fresh, flavorful, and filling. I wish they stayed open past 10:30pm, because this would be a great late night option.

Top Thai's food and staff are amazing! The sauces are sweet without being icky sweet. The portions are generous so go hungry. Everything was cooked wonderfully, juicy and crispy! The waitresses are very kind, attentive and helpful. All of their dishes come with ample amount of meat and they give a lot of food for the price. They have drinks for $1 which most restaurants would charge at least $5 for. The appetizer platter is a killer so make sure to order!

Title: High Hopes Dashed by High Prices and Mediocre Fare

I ventured into this establishment with great expectations, only to leave underwhelmed. The service shone brilliantly amidst the experience, with attentive staff that couldn't be faulted. However, the excessive pricing was a jarring contrast to the quality of the cuisine. At a staggering $16 for 8 dumplings, one expects a culinary revelation, but I found myself reminiscing about far superior dumplings mere blocks away that would barely dent one's wallet.

The noodle soup epitomized blandness, and the noodles succumbed to a sogginess that defied the grasp of chopsticks. While the eatery prides itself on using organic ingredients like chicken meatballs, it's not enough of a redeeming factor. Organic does not necessarily equate to flavorful.

In sum, despite the care evident in their food preparation, there's no balancing act that can reconcile the taste with the inflated prices. Regrettably, I must say this was my first and last visit.

Title: A Birthday Brunch at Sons of Essex: Hits and Misses

I recently chose Sons of Essex for my 30th birthday brunch celebration. The restaurant exudes charm right from the entrance, with its prominent and inviting bar. For those looking to dine amidst a lively atmosphere, I recommend snagging a reservation post-noon when the ambiance truly comes alive with energizing music.

However, my experience was not without its drawbacks. Despite not opting for the birthday package, my party of four was allotted a two-hour seating window, which is understandable for turnover purposes. Yet, the dining experience was marred by the overzealousness of the bussing staff, whose frequent attempts to clear our table made for a rushed and somewhat uncomfortable meal.

Despite this hiccup, Sons of Essex showed potential as a festive brunch spot. I’m willing to give them another chance in hopes that my next visit strikes a more leisurely pace.

From the chef: "Today may be a special day for some, maybe just an ordinary day for others. But as we have prepared this meal for you - we hope that we have enriched your day and have turned even the most ordinary of days into an extraordinary one."Atomix is nothing short of extraordinary both times I've dined here. The entire experience from end to end is flawless - service, food, atmosphere. Every dish has a meaningful story behind it from the chefs - from childhood, travel, and adulthood - and has its deep roots in Korean heritage and culture. Atomix has elevated the Korean food experience without losing the every day essence of love and life... of everything it means to be a Korean. Atomix has my heart for my favorite meal in NYC. Couldn't recommend it more highly.

Recently, I found myself venturing into a hidden gem on the edge of Chinatown, a spot my new acquaintance tipped me off about. It's a sister venue to a Chicago favorite, which was news to me. To reach it, brace yourself for a walk down a dimly lit alley that, despite its darkness, feels safe due to its proximity to bustling streets.

Stepping inside, I was thrust into what could only be described as a classic movie set masquerading as a diner, so authentic I half-expected to be handed a script. Standing there with no femme fatale to meet, I quickly regained my senses and opted for their burger paired with a "Pink Vodka Lemonade"—a combination that did not disappoint.

In short: The ambiance is a knockout, the food hits the spot, and the experience is unique enough to warrant a second visit. If you're feeling adventurous, don your detective hat, navigate the alley, and discover this cinematic eatery for yourself.

Title: A Serendipitous Brunch at an Upscale Hideaway

On a recent whirlwind trip to New York, with time ticking before my departure back to Boston, I experienced an unexpected delight. Initially set on Parker & Quinn for a farewell brunch, the crush of reservations nudged us upstairs to its lesser-known sibling restaurant perched on the 13th floor.

The ambiance exuded a cozy charm, straddling the line between indoor comfort and al fresco dining with clever coverings that allowed for both experiences. Despite lacking a reservation, we were promptly seated—a relief given our tight schedule.

Our brunch selections arrived posthaste, much to our contentment. I indulged in the Deluxe Egg Sandwich, a butter-rich creation with lavishly oily bacon paired with crispy potatoes—delightfully satisfying, though a finer chop would have perfected their crispness. Sampling the Lamb Merguez Hash, I reveled in its robust flavors, and my husband concurred with enthusiasm.

In a city brimming with brunch spots, this establishment proved to be a serendipitous find, blending a lounge-worthy setting with efficient service for those in a time crunch. Grateful for the twist of fate, this venue has earned a warm recommendation from a traveler sated and pleased.

Hop Shing, one of the few "original" classic dim sum tea parlors left in Chinatown. This place has been here since I can remember (70's). But my parents tell me it's even older than that. It's appeal is clearly their food and pricing but it's reputation is an institution in itself, where labor men and working class folk meet to dine and swap stories and the latest current events.  The casual low key vibes keeps the regulars coming back.Feeling nostalgic and missing my father (RIP), I came here to dine alone and reminisce about my days with the family eating dim sum.  I was also people watching and sipping my hot tea. Ahh!  Since it was a weekday, my fellow diners were mainly retired peeps and bankers on a coffee break.Onto the food, best thing here as everyone knows, the famous Baked Roast Pork Bun (I even left with three to go)! A thin sweet layer of glaze atop this gorgeous dome shaped bun. The filing is sweet and savory at the same time -- roast pork pieces with soft onions and their signature sauce. A perfect blend of meat and onions, not skimpy by any means.  I recall from my childhood days, my family and friends would buy these by the dozen to share. Still as good as it was in the 70's. This recipe never changed. I think that's what iove that about them.For those that prefer the white steamed pork bun, they make that too. The barbeque like sauce is savory and delicious. There's also the "big bun", which has a meatball inside with greens and some egg, saltier, not sweet.  It's not as well known but still just as good!  They have dim sum carts circling around from table to table or if you don't want to wait, just order it with the waiter. Depending on the dish, they will likely just grab it for you.  Prices are still very reasonable and the food is just classic.  Not sure what to order? No problem, there's a dim sum menu or just point. Fond memories of this place. I was happy to dine in even though I hate eating alone.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Bustling Burger Spot

I recently dined at a local eatery with high hopes for a laid-back experience, especially given its inviting bar and enticing happy hour specials. The restaurant certainly had its perks, offering a range of burger options to suit various dietary preferences, including bison, chicken, and vegetarian choices on wholesome sprouted bread rolls—points for variety and health-conscious offerings.

However, the dining experience didn't quite hit the mark. One couldn't shake the feeling of being subtly rushed by the staff, as if there was an invisible timer nudging us along to free up the table. This pressure, coupled with an awkward layout where staff constantly maneuvered through diners to access the bar and restrooms, disrupted what could have otherwise been a smooth flow.

As for the burger that should have been the highlight, it fell short of expectations. Ordered medium well, it arrived with an uneven cook, pink on one side, which frankly, I left untouched. The overall quality of the food was just okay, lacking that special something to make the meal memorable.

In summary, while this spot has the potential to be a great haunt with its cocktail and burger options, the lack of ambiance and an underwhelming main course might have you pondering if the good outweighs the not-so-good.

Title: Patience Pays Off for Piping Hot Pepperoni Perfection!

If you've ever wandered down to this pizzeria around dinner time, you're no stranger to the bustling crowd and the inevitably lengthy queue, with waits to enter stretching upward of 15 minutes. Take my advice: a post-8pm visit somehow makes the line more bearable. My latest visit at 5:30 pm proved to be the usual – an additional wait inside to get my hands on that mouthwatering pizza.

Once you're assigned a number, anticipate another 15-20 minutes of foot-tapping anticipation as you join the scattered bunch on the sidewalk. But let me tell you, the moment you sink your teeth into that doughy, pepperoni-laden marvel, all memories of the wait vanish into thin air. It's a symphony of pepperoni, folks – they don't skimp on toppings here! Each piping hot slice is a meal in itself, though who would stop at one?

Sure, seating is a no-go. But who needs chairs when you've got prime sidewalk real estate? I'm a weekly patron and despite the dance of patience I perform each visit, my verdict remains: zero complaints. The pizza doesn't just satisfy; it triumphs.

Title: Seasonal Charm with a View at [Restaurant Name]

I've had the pleasure of visiting [Restaurant Name] during both the summer and winter months and can attest to its delightful seasonal ambience. What sets this place apart is the rooftop experience – it's perfect for soaking up the summer sun or enjoying the stunning New York skyline from a cozy vantage point when it's chilly out.

The drinks menu, while not extensive in its beer offerings, includes a few noteworthy selections. I do find myself longing for a wheat beer on tap, but there's enough variety to keep each visit refreshing.

As a vegetarian, I'm particularly impressed with the small bites available. The options are flavorful and cater to diverse palates, ensuring that anyone can find a tasty nibble regardless of dietary preferences. Overall, [Restaurant Name] is a fantastic spot for a picturesque outing with satisfying sips and eats.

Title: A Mixed Bag at the Start of MDW

My dining experience at the local go-to spot started with a slight change in plans, as my friend and I opted for the indoor space due to the unexpected bustling and noisy outdoor crowd, likely spurred by MDW celebrations. Nevertheless, the indoor ambiance offered a quieter refuge.

We decided on a shared margherita pizza which, despite an initial disappointment over its salty and somewhat watery taste, improved with every slice. The complimentary bread, doughy and superior to many, was a carb-heavy partner to the pizza, which might not suit everyone's taste.

My cocktail choice, the Hennylicious, was a delightful mix and a highlight of the meal.

Service, on the other hand, was overzealous. The attentiveness of the waitstaff bordered on intrusive as they seemed eager to clear dishes prematurely and frequently checked in, making us feel pressured despite visibly continuing our meal – all in all, an unnecessary rush with no queue in sight.

Despite these irritations, the allure of their famous square pies beckons for a future visit, preferably at a quieter time. The potential for a more relaxed experience is there, and I'm willing to give it another chance.

This place is pretty new and it's worth a visit!As of now, they are still BYOB.Compared to the other location in Greenwich Village, this location is much much bigger.The red snapper is a must get!! We got the basil sauce with mild spicy and it's just soo good!

Title: A Cozy Culinary Gem with Minor Winter Woes

Having dined at another location in New York, I anticipated the delights of the familiar menu when visiting this outpost. The beer selection did not disappoint and served as a refreshing counterpart to the rich fare. Their mac and cheese remains a personal favorite, the alchemy of transforming mushrooms into bacon is impressive every time. 

The spinach dip, accompanied by an overly generous serving of chips, repeated the usual predicament of running out of dip far too soon. Venturing into new territory, I sampled a burger and it was an unexpectedly satisfying experience, even for a non-vegan like me who must navigate dining choices due to lactose intolerance.

However, a visit on a bone-chilling Sunday evening in January exposed a flaw in the restaurant's atmosphere: the double door entryway failed to stave off the piercing drafts that accompanied each arriving guest. Despite the warm ambiance inside, this issue with the chilly entrance detracted from the otherwise cozy experience. A reevaluation of their setup may be in order to truly make winter dining as comfortable as the food is comforting.

Obvi came here because hello it's "Lombardi's" pretty cool experience. Interior was awesome, there was a little wait time and when we were seated it was upstairs. Not as comfortable as I would like but I wasn't sure about the whole vibe if it was suppose to be like that or not. I'm not a New Yorker lolPizza was good, not something I thought was extraordinary but I'm glad I came to visit and try

Best Waiter ever!! My boss took the team for our holiday outing to Marta as she raves about the pizza. We went at around one pm and was seated promptly as we had a reservation. Our waiter greeted us and let us know wow all the specials going on and recommended things to try. We were given the menus to look over and honestly everything seemed mouthwatering. We each got pizza or salad. The waiter was superb, always coming back to answer any questions we had checked in frequently on how we were with our meal and suggested the best dessert options all with a constant smile on his face. He made my first time experience worthwhile here and all his suggestions were on point. It's hard to find great staff who enjoy their job at restaurants in nyc but I can tell this guy loved his job.

Title: A Sweet Affair at Spot Dessert Bar

If you're a dessert aficionado, Spot Dessert Bar is a must-try. Despite commonly finding a queue, the fast-paced service more than makes up for it. The staff may rush you to order, but the upside is that decadent treats land on your table in record time.

Among a universally tempting menu, the matcha lava cake is a showstopper – a harmonious blend of molten chocolate and matcha, complemented by creamy matcha ice cream. It's a lava cake that will capture the heart of any connoisseur. The coconut monkeybread, a seasonal delight, also shines with its delectable texture, although the coconut ice cream isn't everyone's cup of tea.

Portions might seem small for the $12 price tag, but they're perfectly sized to indulge without overdoing it. Spot Dessert Bar is indeed the sweet spot you don't want to miss.

From what I recalled, the nacho used to be in this large tray when dining in. Even ordering take out, they were in this big aluminum catering tray. Ordered for take out today and noticed that there is 1-person option and 2-people options, which I do not see on the menu at the restaurant. When I picked it up, it's a much smaller portion than it used to be. Was happy that they put guac which I don't recall they usually do, but disappointed about the size.

Great lunch spot for Middle Eastern.  Recommend the chicken shawarma in the pita or in the pan.  The pita makes all the difference as it tastes like its straight from the oven.  The pan version is a large platter filled with rice, veggies, velvety hummus, and well seasoned chicken.  All the ingredients are fresh and flavorful.  Also enjoyed the classic falafel and the sweet potato falafel pita sandwiches. Like how they have kiosks for ordering and service is fairly quick.  The place has the new restaurant feels and has plenty of seating.   They have made it on my regular lunch rotation.

Title: Nikko Hibachi - A Harlem Gem That Outshines the Competition

If you've got a hankering for hibachi but don't want to venture into the city, Nikko in Harlem is your spot. Dare I say, it's even better than Benihana. From the accommodating waiting area to the lively hibachi table that seats around ten, the atmosphere is perfect for any occasion.

The evening began with the house salad and miso soup, which while slightly below expectations (watery dressing and lukewarm soup), were just the prelude to a mouthwatering main course. I went for the filet mignon and lobster tail hibachi, a generous portion at $40 that included the works. They're not shy about ensuring your steak is just how you like it—though take it from me, order a touch rarer than usual to hit the sweet spot.

As for entertainment, the hibachi chefs put on a spectacular show, complete with fiery theatrics and playful vegetable tossing. A slight hiccup with my steak being a tad overcooked and the inclusion of mushrooms, which I'm not fond of, didn't detract from the overall experience.

In true fashion, my party and I took our time savoring our meal, and the staff graciously offered us a regular table to linger longer without pressure. And hey, if hibachi's not your thing, their full menu of Japanese delights is sure to entice.

Nikko has firmly planted itself as my top pick for hibachi in Harlem. Next time, I may just delve into their sushi offerings, but one thing's for sure—I won't be dining elsewhere for hibachi anytime soon.

This review is for last April 9, Tuesday at around 10:00pm. Sad to say that I wasn't very satisfied with this place. The only reason I am giving two stars is for the Buffalo Wings which are just okay. The service was so slow too given that they only have few tables and couple of servers working that time. I was so excited with their bbq ribs but were very disappointed when I received it.

Title: A Bustling Hub of Creativity and Culinary Delights

My recent visit to this restaurant left a lasting impression thanks to its imaginative interior and exterior design. However, more outdoor seating would alleviate the congestion in front of neighboring businesses and enhance the experience.

The establishment is a magnet for college students, which means it can get particularly crowded on Fridays, Saturdays, and during holiday breaks. Despite the bustling atmosphere, the affordability of the extensive menu is a pleasant surprise. The food quality exceeds expectations considering the reasonable prices, and their drink selection is equally commendable.

There were a couple of hiccups with our order, but I'm inclined to overlook these given the restaurant's busy nature. Our fried tofu was unfortunately a letdown, seeming undercooked and gooey on the outside. On a brighter note, the Taiwan ramen and rice bowl were both delectable triumphs.

These minor issues aside, the restaurant has won me over, and I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit.

I recently dined at a fantastic sushi spot in midtown, renowned for its impeccable sit-down ambiance. The sushi is invariably fresh, the menu options are creatively executed, and service is impressively swift. Particularly notable is their lunch special, which is generous in portion. Highly recommend for an exquisite sushi experience!

I love the concept and what a fun menu! Pick your ball type and sauce. They also have small plates, pasta, and sliders. We tried the Mini Buffalo Balls ($9) as well as a couple of the make your owns ($9 for 3 meatballs and a chosen sauce).Kind of pricey for the portions but the balls were fresh and tasty, lol. Lots of pun jokes to be made here. Casual setting with a good amount of seating.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Korean BBQ Aficionados

If you find yourself craving authentic Korean BBQ, this excellent hideaway is a must-visit. Tucked away from the street view, keep an eye out for its unassuming sign. My experience began on a busy Friday at 5 pm, and to my delight, we were promptly seated. Take note, post-5 pm diners should anticipate a wait, as the restaurant was bustling by 6:30 pm, with a queue forming in the lobby.

Our choice for the evening was the beef platter, priced at $87.99. It boasted an array of premium cuts – kalbi, prime ribeye, beef thin skirt, and beef brisket. The meat's quality was so exceptional that it stood out without the need for marinade, although marinated options might cater to other palates. 

In comparison to its Koreatown peers, this restaurant offers reasonable prices, especially given the quality on offer. The ambiance is particularly noteworthy, with booth-style seating thoughtfully arranged to transport you to a bustling Korean town, making it a versatile spot suitable for any event. Whether you're a seasoned Korean BBQ enthusiast or a curious first-timer, this restaurant promises an experience that's hard to beat.

This is a huge venue, very classic dim sum decor. We got seated right in the front and definitely ate with our eyes, grabbing 10 dishes before we even sat down since we were so hungry. I love how they cook the food right in the front of the venue as well. There's a whole row of grills and heated trays of food. That way instead of waiting for the carts to come to your table, you can just go to the front and have them serve it piping hot for you. But we made a mistake and got the turnip cakes too early just as she placed them down on the grill and served them anyways when they're weren't completely cooked yet. It would have tasted much better if they were cooked more and crispy on the outside. Looks are deceiving, the other dishes were cold and lukewarm. Some dishes tasted better than others but overall I wasn't blown away with the quality of the food. Everything was just ok, I've had better dim sum in Vancouver. The plus side is that they do give generous portions.

I visited Sabai with high hopes for a delightful Thai meal. While the ambiance was pleasant and the staff attentive, the Pad Thai unfortunately fell flat. Despite my love for Thai cuisine, my dish, served with tofu and no egg, was surprisingly bland and simply mediocre. It seems the kitchen may need to revisit their flavor profiles. The overall experience was underwhelming as the food did not live up to expectations.

We came in for drinks after work. The ambiance, the design is impeccable. The restroom itself is an experience so be sure not to miss it.The bar selection, especially of whisky, including Japanese, scotch is impressive, tho owners should make it easier for the bartenders to reach. The knowledge of the bartender was also impressive.We had one roll of such and two orders of sashimi to accompany our drinks. It looked so beautiful. The prices tho, was overly so. $14 for a roll of buttered shrimp and $7-8 for a slice, yes, one sashimi piece. If it was fatty salmon or some exotic fish, I could understand. But it was simply tuna and salmon sashimi and I didn't die and went to some sashimi heaven. So that was disappointing Drinks prices was actually acceptable for Manhattan.

Title: A Genuine Delight at Hanoi House

Hanoi House might just challenge the notion that certain Asian dishes resist the so-called "elevation" to fine dining. They seem to effortlessly prove otherwise with their clever use of luxurious ingredients like bone marrow and uni, which, coincidentally, are favorites of mine.

Despite its somewhat dim lighting, which wasn't entirely to my taste, Hanoi House boasts an aesthetic interior that, coupled with its vibrant atmosphere, was impressively lively for a weekday evening.

The standout starter was the papaya and pig ear salad - an unusual but captivating choice. The pig ears, surprisingly one of my preferred indulgences, were fried to a mouthwatering crisp, and the sweet soy sauce dressing complemented them perfectly.

The main course, shaking beef, paired with charred filet mignon and roasted bone marrow, took me by pleasant surprise. The generous portion of bone marrow was a heavenly addition, elevating each bite of the impeccably cooked beef.

The pho, served with a thoughtful touch that involved splitting it into two bowls, each with a chunk of bone marrow, was an aromatic revelation. The broth's depth of flavor was unmistakable, and the suggested crispy breadstick was an excellent accompaniment.

Hanoi House delivers an exceptional experience, balancing the authenticity of Asian cuisine with upmarket flair. And don't be deterred by a predominantly non-Asian clientele; the flavors here are universally appealing. Highly recommended for a foray into upscale yet genuine Asian dining.
