This is a chain restaurant established in Japan. I've tried one in Tokyo, which was okay. This one.. hmm, it was arranged for the US audience, but not quite in a right way (3 star, 8/10/2019). We ordered ohitashi, seaweed salad, salmon ikura noodle, four pieces of their special rolls, chawanmushi. We skipped a "fishing" experience as it was 20 min before their last call and we just wanted to eat. It was sad to see that many of their menu items emphasize fancy ingredients of uni, ikura, toro and salmon. Their special rolls definitely needed some additional/different ingredients to avoid merely fatty, creamy and melting flavors. I wish they didn't follow the general rules of successful Japanese restaurants, but would stay as unique as their fishing policy. Ohitashi was okay. I'd say all other items need a bit more adjustments and twist to survive this tough NYC market.

had high hopes for this place as it always seemed packed when i walked by and everyone raves about the fish tacos.service is 5 stars+ - super attentive servers and very friendly.the tacos themselves were just mediocre - the pieces were too large that they dont even fit in the taco so it's a really awkward meal to try to have civilly. great crunchy exterior, but the breading was a bit thick for my liking. accompanying rice and beans were nicely cooked and the beans had good flavor.i'm interesting in their other dishes, but would probably visit for dinner next time and not for brunch

I usually don't eat steak and it's actually rare that I do so. I've had this bookmarked for a while and I'm glad I finally came here. At this place you have to go to the back and choose what you want and how many ounces you'd like and then of course how you'd like it cooked which was new to me but it wasn't strange at all. It's you going up to them instead of them coming to you which isn't a big deal and was actually fun to do. The wait wasn't long and I had some bomb steak. It comes with onions and you get to choose one side. Any extra side is $1 which is fair. It'd be nice if rice was added as a side or maybe more vegetable options but it was good. I'm gonna be back here for sure and when you enter is smells amazing. Coming around lunch time is a good time to go since there aren't many people there.

"Summit of Manhattan" created by Australian artist, Todd Stuart. is presented at the front of Summit New York, a new luxury 43 story rental building in Midtown East in the Murry Hill section of Manhattan.Crafted from high grade stainless steel polished to a mirror finish, "Summit of Manhattan" reimagines the infinity symbol and hovers above a reflecting pool, where it can be admired by residents and passersby.

Went back for the third time. Still great ambience and laid back and consistent yummy food. Fish Cakes are highly recommended (that lemongrass is mwah) and the pork steamed dumplings too. We tried the steamed mussels too (I missed bread with my mussels tbh). I obviously ordered the Baked amok and it so delicious. The fish is perfectly cooked and has flavors complimenting the meat in the dish. The tricky part about curries is salt. Angkor is on point with that. We also had the roast duck dish (sorry had with names). DELICIOUS. This is now my must order here. The duck is tender with skin on so a tad crispy too. The veggies pair perfectly well with the dish. We tried the Banh Chao and that filling is so yummy. Crepe was burnt at places but I did not mind. Overall this place has not disappointed so far. ....This is my second time here. Both times I have received excellent food, service, and ambience. The veg dumplings, chicken skewer, and fish cakes are yummy. The baked amok and all their noodles (yes we needed up ordering one of each kind) was amazing. The baked amok comes with veggies and rice and is soft and flavorful. They explain their dishes very nicely if you ask them. They also suggest good wine pairs. I never had place for desert either times because the food is so good you tend to overeat. I highly recommend this place and I might come again :)

I finally managed to visit a much-anticipated spot for a friend's birthday dinner at 9pm, finding it bustling with patrons. Initially underwhelmed by the scant menu, we made selections that turned out to be satisfactory, though lacking in novelty. The desserts, however, were a delightful highlight. While I'm open to a return, there's no immediate rush for a repeat. Service was a mixed bag, with our waiter shining in attentiveness amidst an otherwise indifferent staff.

Because this place is usually so packed, I sort of took it off my radar as I'm usually too impatient to wait for a table. So glad I thought of it last night, though, because I was having a late dinner date and there was plenty of seating when we got there at around 8:30. I've been to the location in the village once before and absolutely loved it, and here we have another awesome place with a nice array of delicious vegan options! I had the vegan quesadilla which was huge, filling, and delicious. Our server was just that right balance of always available but never intrusive. He was happy to talk with us about the menu and he knew ever detail about the ingredients. He also kept us supplied with chips and salsa, something I really miss from my years in Texas where chips and salsa flow like manna from heaven. When Omni restaurants offer vegan options, they can feel like an afterthought, and are often poorly thought out and unimaginative. Not so at Blockheads where there is clearly a chef on board who knows their way around a vegan kitchen. I often refer to midtown Manhattan as a vegan wasteland, but that's only because I forget about places like this where there are plentiful options, good service, and casual vibes, just like I like them. I can't wait to go back!

Title: A Late Night Greek Delight at [Restaurant Name]

Craving a taste of Greece after my travels, I found myself at [Restaurant Name], enticed by its renown and a tempting $49 late-night prix-fixe menu. Despite a Friday night buzz and a post-reservation wait at the bar, the expansive dining space promised a comfortable experience.

Seated by the windows, we had to prompt our waiter for the special menu. A standout was the exquisitely prepared grilled octopus atop a smooth yellow split pea fava—my dish of the night. The family-style Greek salad was a generous and refreshing accompaniment, although the sea bream, while beautifully presented, fell short with its slightly overcooked texture. My friend's lamb chops, however, hinted at culinary excellence I plan to indulge in on a future visit.

A glass of Assyrtiko wine complemented the feast well. The walnut cake concluded the meal on an unremarkable note, but the honey lavender ice cream left a delightful, lingering freshness.

While the service did have its lapses—a forgotten salad order and a somewhat inattentive waiter—the overall experience left me satiated and eager to return. Lunchtime beckons for a second helping, and the late-night prix-fixe remains a recommendable choice for the night owls seeking authentic Greek flavors.

Title: A Slice of Heaven with a Side of Attitude

Upon my friend's glowing recommendation, I ventured into this tiny, bustling pizza haven expecting something extraordinary. True to her word, the Spicy Spring pizza, ordered extra crispy as per her sage advice, did not disappoint. Crisping up those pepperonis took the flavor to new heights, with each bite delivering a delightful crunch that married well with the heat of the spices.

Our group also sampled a trifecta of NY-style slices, each sporting a different topping, and while these were enjoyable, they paled in comparison to that standout Spicy Spring.

Be warned, this popularity means patience is necessary; the wait was bordering on the absurd. Once our pizza treasures were in hand, the lack of seating sent us to the streets, dining al fresco on the sidewalk. 

It's worth noting that the service could use a sprinkle of cheer, as the staff's demeanor was less than welcoming, giving off a vibe that customer interaction was a chore rather than a pleasure. However, the exceptional pizza meant that even their sour moods couldn't detract from the overall experience, and I'll refrain from docking any stars for it.

In summary, if you can withstand a lengthy wait and indifferent service, your taste buds will thank you for a slice of this pizza paradise.

So I took my friend here because I heard so much about Artichoke pizza here in NYC, especially near Chelsea, so I thought why not take him here for the "New York" experience. There weren't many people here...we were probably the fourth party there. We were seated right away and the atmosphere was nice. The staff was very sweet but not as attentive as we would have wanted. The pizza took a lot longer than we thought it and the staff apologized to us by giving us two extra slices which was super nice of them. I personally couldn't eat the pizza while it was hot because I had to run to make my train; but my friend said it was really good so I'm glad he was able to enjoy it! When I took the leftovers home, my mom also said that it was really good pizza so I guess since that's TWO people who said it was good, that makes it pretty good pizza haha. Would definitely love to go back and experience the full dining experience. 3 different slices of pizza is $18 so it's pricier than any other pizza parlor but they are pretty big pizza slices so I would say it's good to split between two people so it's not that bad!

I've always seen this place packed for dinner (definitely need to make reservations) but a couple friends and I were finally able to walk in for lunch on a Monday. This spot is a lot bigger than I thought - nothing too notable about the decor.As for the pizza though - delicious !! Super thin crust pizza with sweeter tomato sauce base. What's great about this spot is that you can choose between two sizes and do half-and-half. We got one large pizza, half Tie Dye and half Rubirosa Supreme. So so so good! I prefer the Tie Dye for its simplicity but the meat combo on the Rubirosa Supreme should not be completely overlooked. We also ordered the Tajarin allá Carbonara which was fantastic. I usually don't go for carbonara but this one hit the spot - creamy base but not too heavy. Would definitely recommend this spot if you're able to grab a table or make reservations!

Title: A Steep Bill for Comfort Food at Cho Dang Gol

My dining companion and I recently visited Cho Dang Gol with expectations of warming our souls with some classic Korean comfort food. To kick things off, we shared the japchae appetizer, which certainly pleased with its peppery zing. While a solid start to our meal, the $18.99 price tag seemed excessive for a dish that is traditionally more modest in both preparation and cost.

The main event, the spicy army stew, unfortunately did not march to the bold flavors I've encountered in Ktown's myriad of options. Although the stew was satisfactory, it faded into the background, particularly given its nearly $40 cost—a price point hard to reconcile for something I know from experience can be made simply and affordably at home.

In all honesty, the meal was well-prepared and the food was tasty enough to earn a respectable 4 stars. However, the value for money simply wasn't there. Next time, I'll be taking my appetite and my wallet to a place like Her Name is Han, where the army stew lives up to its higher-quality promise.

Title: A Haven of Fun, Flavors, and Fabulous Decor!

If you're looking for a dining spot that packs a punch in both ambiance and flavor, look no further! This eclectic gem has been serving up joy and jollification for over two decades, and my latest visit confirmed it hasn't lost its touch.

The decor is an extravagant feast for the eyes – delightfully over the top and buzzing with energy. It's the perfect backdrop for both large celebrations and cozy gatherings. On this visit, the warmth of the venue shined brighter with a complimentary serving of Banana Fritters that set our taste buds alight – a massive, mouthwatering treat that was both enormous in size and flavor.

But, the true star of the show was the Lamb Kurma. Bathed in a heavenly blend of almonds, raisins, and sweet spices, all swimming in a sumptuous cream sauce, it's a dish that beckons your return before you've even left. While paired perfectly with rice, the naan bread served alongside was a delightful companion, scooping up every last drop.

To wash it all down, the Mango Lassi was a sweet revelation with just the right hint of cardamom – a refreshing foil to the rich feast. And for a sweet finale, my daughter was charmed by the complimentary chocolate ice cream, a gesture that left us all beaming with satisfaction.

A note to fellow patrons, do mind the stairs leading up to its welcoming doors, and be prepared for a cash-only exchange. The energetic buzz is softer during daylight hours, with evenings bringing a crowded and lively throng. And while current times have paused the festivities (temporarily closed due to Covid), there's no doubt the good vibes and times will return. A must-visit for anyone yearning for spirited surroundings and delectable dining.

My recent visit to this restaurant was a delightful experience, primarily due to their good fresh pasta. I indulged in a plate of spaghetti with a rich and flavorful vodka sauce, while my boyfriend enjoyed the rotini bathed in a creamy herb sauce. Both dishes proved to be delicious and satisfying. Additionally, the garlic sticks deserve a special mention for their softness and freshness. I am already looking forward to returning and sampling more of their culinary offerings.

Unlike LA's Ktown BCD tofu house, this place is not 24 hours, but during Friday and Saturday, it is open for 20 hours which is not too shabby. We arrived at 3AM after clubbing at Maru and it was still quite packed, but we did not need to wait even with a large group. We just decided to squeeze into a small table and get 2 items, in which the waitress complained that we should get 1 item per person. If we are not taking a large table and we just want to give some money to the business, it is of best interest to not even mention that. Eventually, the waitress was fine with it. We got the beef soondubu and tteok bok ki, which was pretty average to be honest. I don't really know why, but I think that at such late hours, everyone does not care about the food quality, so the food quality is butchered. I have tried BCD in other cities before, but they are not as mediocre as this place. The tofu soup here is quite bland and the amount of tofu is rather low. The tteok bok ki is more mushy than chewy, implying that it was a bit overcooked.

Recently, I had the pleasure of visiting Fieldtrip during a Yelp Elite event and it's safe to say this Harlem eatery has quickly climbed to the top of my NYC favorites list. Nestled near the A, B, C, D, and red express trains, it's a breeze to get to.

The menu here packs a punch. I dove into the Shrimp Bowl and Quinoa Bao Buns, washing it down with an invigorating Dragonfruit Lemonade. My friend Brit mirrored my drink and side choice but went green with the Veggie Bowl. Both our palates were thrilled as the food not only met but soared beyond our expectations with its generous portions and vibrant flavors.

Fieldtrip isn't just about the food though; the staff's stellar service, highlighted by Krys's hospitality, elevates the dining experience. The inclusive vibe extends to their gender-neutral bathroom. Plus, the free WiFi and a soundtrack that echoes the heart of Harlem itself only add to the ambiance.

While I'm from Brooklyn, the trek to Fieldtrip is a no-brainer for me. It's the epitome of a week well started and even better finished – just remember to plan around their Monday closure. Fieldtrip, see you again very soon!

Title: Seafood Satisfaction with a Side of Confusion

Entering the establishment for a much-anticipated seafood boil presented its initial confusion; the lack of a reception area left me awkwardly loitering until acknowledged by the staff. The unconventional welcome, coupled with a 15-minute wait, started the experience on an uncertain note.

However, the dining tale took a positive turn once seated. The culinary highlight was undisputedly the Cajun sauce draping the succulent snow crab legs and shrimp - a triumph in flavor that would lure any seafood aficionado back. Opting for medium spice, the balance of heat and seasoning was impeccable, complementing the accompanying potatoes, corn, and a bonus choice between french fries or garlic noodles. The latter proved to be a delectable companion to the seafood feast.

Navigating the menu's pricing structure did cause a momentary hiccup, as the cost wasn't outlined clearly as per-pound or set-portion, leading to a slight disappointment in the inability to order in lesser quantities than the standard offering.

Beverage-wise, the Mr. Rich cocktail, a spirited fusion of vodka, lychee, and pineapple juice, packed a punch both in strength and taste. Sampling the Madam Berry offered a similarly enjoyable palate pleaser.

The meal concluded with a decadent note in the form of funnel cake fries crowned with vanilla ice cream - a sweet finale to an overall delicious experience.

Ambiance-wise, the space could benefit from a more cohesive layout and clear customer flow. On a quirky note, the restrooms offered mouthwash and lemons for those eager to freshen up post-feast, a detail indicating the establishment's consideration for its seafood-loving patrons.

Despite the initial mix-up and seating challenge, the culinary offerings etched a positive impression. A return visit is on the horizon, with hopes that the front-of-house experience will match the kitchen's prowess.

4 stars: 5 stars for their peppercorn fish dish which is really good, 3-3.5 stars for a lot of other dishes.I've been to this place lots of times and the experience has been uneven depending on what we ordered.  The peppercorn fish dish is really great if you like spicy greasy numbing Sichuan food and your seafood fresh.  The fish is REALLY thinly sliced which I haven't seen at other places.  (Message me if you know another place that does this well.). This usually says 1) the fish is fresh, 2) chef has mad knifework skillz. Other stuff is hit and miss.  I also enjoy the seafood asparagus soup sometimes.The menu has pictures which is a plus.Don't expect much from the ambiance.  It's a Sichuan resto in Times Square...

Not your typical Gyu-Kaku location! Love how this is on the 2nd floor of a building -- that extra leverage gives a nice view. We had a group of 6 and they sat us in the area that you have to take your shoes off. Super clean and interesting experience. SERVICE: Great! Attentive waiters who also gave recommendations. DEALS: it's almost always happy hour here - some drinks are $5 and many menu options are a couple dollars discount. For drinks we opted for a large carafe or hot house sake for $7 per carafe. MEAT: honestly, consistent across all gyu-kaku locations I have visited and I have been to several. My personal fav everywhere I go is the bistro hanger steak! Appetizers: my favorite is the spicy tuna volcano. It's spicy tuna filling on top of a block of crispy rice that was formed to be sort of like a block shape. Amazing play on textures and def different! Also love their seared salmon sashimi -- a refreshing contrast to all the meat

Stepping into this charming old-fashioned diner with its quaint soda fountain vibe instantly takes you back in time. The food here is enjoyable, offering that comforting nostalgia on a plate. However, the prices are on the steep side given that most menu items come à la carte, which can add up quickly. Expect a bustling atmosphere on weekends, as this spot's cute appeal is no well-kept secret. Overall, it's a lovely experience for those willing to splurge a bit on a trip down memory lane.

Absolute hidden gem in Midtown Manhattan. I call it "hidden gem" because its under scaffolding at the moment, but is rather large inside. Everything on the menu is amazing! The pizzas are delicious (they even have pizza with cauliflower base if you want to cut out some carbs). Everything is made fresh to order, including the salads. @traveleen_gurl

I visited cafeteria on a Saturday evening with some family and friends for dinner. We sat downstairs in the lounge area. The restaurant appeared quite popular. There were a number of people occupying the patio and upstairs spaces. We visited after a recommendation of a friend. I had the Turkey burger and truffle Parmesan fries. The burger was cooked and season very well. The horseradish with the avocado was very good. Probably one of the best restaurant turkey burgers I've ever had. The truffle fries were not good. If I was to ever return, I would try a different side. The Parmesan wasn't melted and was just sprinkled on the fries. They weren't anything superior whatsoever. We also had both the calamari and devil eggs as appetizers. The devil eggs were nothing amazing. As a southern, I've definitely had better. The chicken skin on top of the eggs was the best part of them and were very much the thing that drew our attention to them. The calamari was cooked perfectly. It came with some house made tartar sauce. A chipotle sauce of some sort would have definitely heightened the experience. The calamari was cooked very well. Cindy was our server. She was very helpful. She answered all of our questions. If she didn't know a question we asked, she asked and gave us a timely response. Notable mentions: the Oktoberfest beer with two orange slices and their house made old fashion are highly recommended drinks. The biscuits were fantastic!

Came here with a party of 6. You're greeted as soon as you walk in which is nice. When we got seated, we saw the table was already set up with the side dishes. Since we had a big group, we opted for the large beef and large pork combo. The server cooks your food but there seemed to be a barrier of sorts because he never bothered to let us know if the meats were ready to eat or not. We'd watch him flip and cut the meats. Then he'd walk away. We had to ask several times what type of meat he was cooking and if it was ready to eat or not. Once, he walked away when the meat was still red. We sat there looking at each other, wondering if it was still being cooked or if we could eat it. When we asked, he said it's rib eye and it's ok to eat med rare since it's not pork. Would've been nice to know that before he walked away and we let it sit there cooking an additional 5 min! He couldn't be bothered to volunteer any information! The side dishes were ok. But we didn't get much refills. Would've been nice to get more than two pieces of kimchi when asking for more, especially for a table of 6 people where 4 of them are hungry teenage boys. We paid for our meals and the food didn't sit right so I went to the restroom and it was FILTHY! Toilet paper strewn about everywhere, the toilet was clogged and full of piss and poop from past patrons. With the large amount of toilet paper in the toilet, it looked as though multiple people used it and just left it there. But how can you blame them? The toilet did not flush! Try to tell an employee and again, thru just couldn't be bothered. I don't see how a restaurant that charges so much for its food ends up with a bathroom that filthy. Makes me wonder how their kitchen looks - no wonder the food didn't sit right in my stomach.

Title: A Late-Night Seafood Delight at Burger & Lobster

After a tiring show and with appetites in tow, we stumbled into Burger & Lobster well past the dinner hour. Guided by my trusty Yelp app and a craving for seafood, the decision to dine here was a no-brainer. Despite the late hour and a bustling crowd, service was prompt, and our eclectic selection of oysters, lobster mac and cheese, and lobster bites arrived quickly.

The seafood shone brightly – the oysters were the epitome of ocean freshness with just the right hint of brine, and the lobster bites were heavenly morsels that simply dissolved in our mouths. The lobster mac and cheese was a decadent, creamy affair that cosseted our late-night hunger.

But the real star of the evening was Darius, our server. He was engaging and personable, a genuine gem who made our weary group feel right at home in the heart of NYC. His warmth and hospitality were an unexpected highlight and surely made him the nicest encounter on our trip.

The ambiance, set in a chic refurbished building with lofty ceilings, expansive bay windows, and striking blue uplighting, added another layer of enjoyment to our visit.

For anyone in search of exceptional seafood and a touch of late-night comfort, Burger & Lobster is a must-visit. It's a place where the food and staff, especially Darius, will ensure your dining experience leaves you feeling like a "happy camper" from any state – Ohioan or otherwise.

Detroit-style pizza aficionados, take note: Lions & Tigers & Squares is a must-visit! Despite never having been to Detroit myself, I can vouch that this spot does justice to the city's famed pizza. Finding this iconic style on the East Coast is a rarity, but this quaint establishment hits the mark.

With a compact space that offers a few stand-up dining options, it's the perfect spot for a quick bite. Don't be fooled by the pizza's smaller size; they pack a mighty punch. The decor is charming and the tunes, spot-on.

The pizza itself? Thick, crunchy crust, top-notch ingredients. The pepperoni square pizza, with its abundant mini curling pepperonis, shines brightly among the options. Plus, every pizza is cut into four, guaranteeing that sought-after corner piece every time. At $5 for a classic cheese, it's a steal.

In summary, Lions & Tigers & Squares is a delightful gem. I can find no fault here—just pure pizza pleasure. Go forth and indulge!

Ordered a quick lunch from here. I went with the lamb pita. It was small but filling. There is a lot going on here in terme of flavors. It has both a mediterrean and middle eastern taste to it.  Although the flavors were complex it still hit the spot. The lamb was cooked well and the pita was the perect vessel for it. We picked it up to go and ate it in a nearby park. I didnt try anything else but was pleased with the lamb pita. Will definitely keep it in mind for lunch in the future.

Pretty awful experience. Came here because every other place was full on a Friday night. After perusing the takeout menu converted into a restaurant menu and viewing the multiple empty seats, I knew this dinner was not going to turn out well. I was not mistaken. We ordered the unagi don and the spicy roll combo. The freshwater eel was not long and wide like I'm used to. Instead, small pieces of unagi were placed on top of rice, failing to give me the satisfaction I would normally get from my fork separating a thick buttery fish. The cucumber on the unagi don plate was extremely bitter and the avocado and seaweed were added to just fill up the plate.The spicy roll combo, however, was worse. The salmon and tuna didn't have any flavor, but they weren't as bad as the spicy yellowtail roll, which straight up tasted foul. The fish tasted so spoiled that we couldn't have more than one piece of the roll. When we informed our server that the yellowtail did not taste fresh, he indicated that he asked the kitchen to ensure it is and told us he would give us a $5 discount because we left half of our meal on the plate. Not that we would have expected to be compensated for that dish, but getting $5 taken off from our bill like it was some promotion looked silly to me. The prices are reasonable and almost cheap in the West 4th area. I had mixed feelings about the customer service due to our experience, but at least the servers did bring the dishes and the check quickly. Sushi, though, needs some work. I won't be coming back.

The short: super impressed by how quickly, safely, deliciously and effectively SUGARFISH pulled off its to-go operations.The longer: I ordered by telephone for pickup during the coronavirus pandemic. I called on the earlier side (5pm) but had no problem getting through. Pickup was perfectly on time and organized. There's tape on the ground and tables for contactless pickup. Whole pickup experience took five minutes. The FOOD. Omg. The sushi was on-point. We had a trust me nozawa box and added the lobster hand cut and toro hand cut, plus large scallop and salmon sushi. Everything was so fresh, and the rice is so much softer than sushi you'd normally get to go. The winners: lobster roll, salmon, large scallop and sea bream. Loved the whole experience! Highly recommend.

Although I didn't try their food, their drinks were exceptional. I was visibly New York and my friend recommended that I try this frog top bar. It's great for pictures lol. I Loved all the decor and staff was very pleasant.

Title: A Delightful Evening at an Upscale Italian Gem on 2nd Avenue

My sister-in-law's graduation celebration brought us to this exquisite Italian haven in the heart of the city, and it did not disappoint. Despite the crowd and a short wait at the bar, the ambiance was lively, providing an up-close glimpse into New York's elite—rumor has it, celebrities frequent this spot too.

The hospitality was as authentic as the olive oil, imported directly from Italy, which set the stage for a culinary delight. The calamari appetizer was a showstopper, possibly the best I've ever savored. My entree, the spaghetti with meat sauce, was a robust symphony of flavors. My wife's chicken parmigiana, though not the pinnacle of her dining experiences, was certainly of high quality.

The wine list, while inclined towards the pricier side, complemented the meal beautifully. The decor struck a cozy note, which along with the overall experience, positions this restaurant as a must-visit when in New York City.

Title: A Solo Dissenter Among Praises

As a self-proclaimed foodie eager to savor the renowned fusion of East Asian and Latin American cuisines, I approached my dining experience without preconceived notions, aiming purely to delight in the flavors before me. Despite the restaurant's high ratings and my anticipation, my palate was left searching for excitement in the ambitiously crafted dishes.

The evening's menu featured an array of intricate creations: Japanese eggplant with pine nut and huacatay, cabbage with miso and anchovy, and a curious aged duck breast nigiri with banana. Each plate was meticulously presented, showcasing the undeniable quality of the ingredients and the kitchen's attention to detail. However, the flavor combinations failed to transport my taste buds on the journey I had hoped for.

It was the simpler concoction of octopus, crab, egg, and jasmine rice in a dashi and soy broth that emerged as my lone favorite, a beacon of satisfaction in a sea of unfulfilled expectations. The subsequent dessert provided a unique and light coda to the meal, a welcome shift from the savory courses.

Though the setting was modern and the service pleasant, overall, the dishes I sampled that evening did not live up to the anticipation set by their descriptions and the restaurant's acclaim. I remain optimistic that my experience was an outlier and hope future visits will align more closely with the raves of fellow diners.

I recently visited this restaurant for a friend's birthday celebration and it was a delightful experience. The ambiance is wonderfully serene, partly thanks to the tastefully dimmed lighting. Our meal was absolutely delicious, impressing both of us with its flavors. Adding to the pleasant atmosphere was our server, who stood out with their friendliness and helpful dish recommendations. The service truly enhanced our dining experience. This is definitely a place I plan to return to. Highly recommended!

Hummus Kitchen is an adorable brightly lit restaurant with hearty healthy food. The service was great, and the ambience was casual.K and I saw the Endgame Avengers, then went here for brunch.The place was filled with families and their children. Kids were laughing, and devouring the food; groups of girls were brunching; couples sitting outside in the sun were laughing and talking. It was great.We ordered the Shakshuka Senya (which comes with tiny tapas style of all the apps, The Kitchen Benedict (salmon benedict), and the Kitchen Kadif (dessert). The Shakshuka Senya was excellent: it was hearty, with sauteed beef and cumin in a tomato savory based stew with perfectly poached eggs. The best part? The fluffy day-baked local pita bread. It was so gorgeous!The Kitchen benedict was good, I just wished for more salmon. Or that I ordered another shakshuka. The apps were very refreshing and good. The best app was the thin slice of the Gravlax Salmon and the savory rich roasted cauliflower. Kitchen Kadif (dessert) was this amazingly beautiful Halva (nutty sweet dense cake) parfait on in a sweet phyllo dough nest topped with halva & silan (date honey). It was very sweet and very unique. So many layers of textures and types of sweetness. Our waitress was so sweet and friendly! She was dancing and singing while serving. She also helped us pour for our videos! Thank you so much!Brunch was very affordable and surprisingly great for the UES! I can't wait to return to try their shawarma and other shakshuka!

Title: A Love Letter to Thai Culinary Excellence!

If a picture is worth a thousand words, then the gallery I've amassed of the delectable dishes from this gem of a restaurant should be enough to drive any food lover wild. My latest visit, as always, was graced by the ever-charming waitress who has become a familiar face, deserving of a selfie next time, for her consistent, outstanding service.

The star of the show, without any shadow of a doubt, is their kow pad gra prow. Imagine chicken basil fried rice so authentic and flavorful, it transports you straight to the bustling streets of Bangkok with every bite. The curry puffs are nothing short of a flavor explosion, while the chicken sate skewers have me debating whether it's acceptable to lick the plate in public.

The bustling crowd is a testament to the culinary mastery housed within; patience is a small price to pay for such divine indulgences. A slight hiccup comes in the form of their spring rolls, which, while tasty, don't quite reach the high bar set by the rest of the menu. But this is a mere whisper in the thunderous ovation I'd give this establishment.

It's with a full heart and even fuller stomach that I extol my love not just for this restaurant, but for the very essence of Thai cuisine as represented by their gifted chefs. Consider this a resounding nomination for the BEST Thai Cuisine and BEST Thai Chef awards within the NYC-NJ axis. Take my advice: go, eat, and let the love affair begin.

Title: A New York Pizza Heaven with a Spinach Twist

Any trip to New York isn't complete without a pizza pit stop, and this place is a must-visit for its plethora of pie choices. On a quest for a quick bite, I stumbled upon this gem and was immediately drawn in by the extensive menu. 

The spinach dip pizza grabbed my attention and did not disappoint; each bite had a perfect cheese pull accompanied by robust flavor, all resting on a fragile, paper-thin crust. The slice size? Colossal. 

Compelled to return, I sampled more options, and each visit reaffirmed my love for the spinach variety, which reigned supreme. White sauce options truly shone here, capturing my taste buds with their creamy goodness.

The only slice that left me wanting was the chicken parmigiana pizza. Despite being fried to a golden hue, the chicken lacked moisture and fell flat on taste.

For those wary of payment options, take note: there’s a $10 credit card minimum. But that's hardly an issue — you'll want at least two slices anyway, both for your stomach's and your wallet's sake. Trust me, one is never enough. 

In short, this spot is a slice above the rest (minus the chicken parm). Whether you're a pizza aficionado or just in for a casual munch, you’ll want to make room for their spinach masterpiece in your New York itinerary.

Title: A Midtown Gem for Affordable, Quick Bites

If you're navigating the pricey landscape of midtown Manhattan in search of an affordable lunch that isn't fast food, Stick To My Pot Potsticker is a refreshing outlier. This spot hits the sweet spot of being wallet-friendly without compromising on quality. The service is impressively quick, ideal for a grab-and-go situation, though a few high tops are available if you fancy a rapid sit-down.

My usual order – 1 pork bao bun and a choice of 4 or 6 savory dumplings – sets me back less than $12. An unbeatable deal for tastiness in this neck of the woods. Plus, their vegan options mean nobody's left out. Stick To My Pot is truly a boon for the budget-conscious, discerning foodies in midtown.

Solid thai place in LES! Dropped by for their lunch special (which i think runs til 3? On weekdays). Its $9/$10 (depeneding on which meat) for an entree and you also get a small appetizer. I got the pad thai with chicken -- was pretty good and flavorful. I also tried the green curry and that was very tasty as well.They said pad kee mao & pad see ew wasnt available when i went - not sure how commin of an occurrence this is though. I think they probably didnt have one of the ingredients on stock. I would say the portion size is a weee bit on the small side - but i might have been really hungry lol. Nevertheless, definitely reasonable for the pricetag.

We made a reservation for a late lunch (12 people).  They had our table ready and waiting.  Our service was super direct and to-the-point (some might say rude, but I appreciated her "no nonsense" attitude).  We had the onion rings for an app.  The server recommended different sauces which were super yummy.  I had a regular ole burger with cheese and bacon, and I think I needed only three napkins :-).  The cooks grilled it to a perfect medium, so it was quite juicy and delicious.

Title: A Birthday Treat to Remember at a Noodle Lover's Paradise

I had the pleasure of celebrating my birthday at this noodle haven, thanks to a dear friend's recommendation. The restaurant strikes the perfect balance between cozy and modern, with its spacious layout and beautiful decorations. Cleanliness is clearly a priority here, which is evident from the moment you walk by the spotless kitchen on your way to the back.

The skylight room, where we were seated, is an absolute delight and seems ideal for larger gatherings, boasting a grand communal table at its center. Despite the potential for a busy and bustling atmosphere, the service was outstanding—attentive and friendly without being intrusive.

Now, let's talk about the food. It arrived with impressive speed, which initially made me skeptical about the quality. However, to my amazement, every dish was executed flawlessly. This place has set a new standard for what quick service and exceptional cuisine should look like.

I'm eager to plan my next visit to this amazing noodle spot, and I'm positive it won't be long before I do. If you're a noodle enthusiast like myself, do yourself a favor and drop by—you won't be disappointed.

I recently tried a Japanese-Peruvian fusion gem in midtown New York and it was an absolute delight. Right off the bat, the menu proudly states that the staff are paid above minimum wage, making it a non-tipping establishment, which is both refreshing and conscientious.

The must-try items are a testament to the harmonious blend of cultures. The Japanese-Peruvian salad bursts with distinctive flavors from both cuisines, offering a truly unique taste experience. Additionally, the steamed egg is flawlessly executed, and the seafood dish is a standout with its generous portion and unparalleled taste.

As for the ambiance, the decor strikes a perfect balance between modern and inviting. The stylish interior is enhanced by cozy seating and charming wood accents, creating an atmosphere that is both chic and comfortable. This spot is more than a dining experience; it's a feast for the senses. Highly recommended for an innovative culinary adventure!

Title: A Flavorful Journey at BaoHaus - A Must Visit in NY

I had the pleasure of visiting BaoHaus' original location in New York twice, and it was a culinary revelation. The Chairman Bao was the star of the show, with its rich, fatty, and incredibly flavorful pork belly – easily one of the best I've had. The accompanying spicy oil sauce added a delightful kick that perfectly complemented the bao.

Not to be outshone, the fried chicken bao was another hit, showcasing a piece of succulent Taiwanese fried chicken that was simply delicious. These baos are a testament to the remarkable flavors BaoHaus has to offer.

On the flip side, the customer service didn't match the warmth of their bao. Service felt mechanical and lacked the welcoming touch that could elevate the dining experience. Despite this, the outstanding quality of the food overshadowed this aspect.

Eager to continue my bao journey, I'm looking forward to trying out their LA location, with their spicy chicken option in my sights. Here's hoping it lives up to the high bar set by the NY bao!

My recent lunch at Calle Dao proved to be a delightful culinary experience overall. Despite our arrival at the bustling hour of 2 PM on a Thursday, the restaurant's popularity was a good omen that was indeed fulfilled.

We started our meal with the oxtail croquettas – savory and meaty morsels paired expertly with aioli, although the portion size of three for $12 seemed slightly pricey. Our other appetizer, the shiitake mushroom rolls, unfortunately, fell short; they were bland and dry, and the accompanying sauce failed to elevate the dish.

The highlight of our meal was the lechon asado. This simple, yet expertly executed dish, offered a generous portion ideal for sharing. At an effective price of $10 each, considering the size, it was an absolute bargain. The escabache accentuated the pork splendidly, making it a dish I'd revisit.

Calle Dao struck me as a gem nestled in the heart of Midtown, with offerings that promise to beckon you back for more.

On a recent visit to the Food Gallery, my family and I decided to branch out from our usual spot upstairs. We arrived at an opportune time with no lines and ample seating. In pursuit of a more affordable option to Korean BBQ, we opted for the BBQ rice bowls. Both my sister and I were impressed with the generous amount of well-marinated bulgogi in our servings. The portion overall was satisfying, although the accompanying soup was underwhelming. At $15, the price was on the higher side, but the quality and quantity of bulgogi left us content, suggesting it might have been an especially good day at the Gallery.

I looked up this place on Yelp because I was craving dumplings and I was already in the Union Square area. My friend and I went to this place an hour before closing so it was pretty empty. We ordered the shrimp, chive, and pork dumplings and the sweet rice cake. We got our food pretty fast and I was immediately intrigued by the flakey cake that was placed on top of the dumplings. I ate it with the dumpling and it added a nice crunch to the soft and steamed dumplings with such flavorful filling! I got the 8 piece dumplings and it was enough to fill me up for the night.The sesame rice cake also had the consistency of mochi but softer and more jelly like. It had a nice sweet flavor and was delightfully chewy. I was given four pieces and split it with my friend. I don't usually get rice cake because it's usually bland or not sweet enough, but this rice cake was scrumptious and tasteful. All of this for around $12! Couldn't have asked for a better late night dinner.Will definitely come back here to try the noodles!

I regret not heeding the advice of prior reviews. The portion sizes at this establishment border on ridiculous - imagine paying $12 for a mere pint of wonton soup. On a positive note, the tea was beautifully presented. However, the lack of sauce for both the scallion pancakes and duck spring rolls was a significant oversight. For a bill nearing $90, I expected more than a collection of meager appetizers.

I'm not the biggest fan of Pho, but the madame pho is not only a really big bowl of Pho, but the broth is pretty rich. I'd recommend sharing with a friend if you're not starving.I've gotten the Tet Noodles every time I've visited because this dish is even better than the Pho. The noodles are stir-fried to perfection with garlic and fish sauce. If only there was more crab meat, it's been inconsistent. The first time there was a good amount, then the second time there was significantly less. The flavors of the stir fry are amazing though, would definitely recommend trying it even if you're leaning towards a pho. Alternatively, you could convince a friend to order it so you can try some too, haha.The salt toasted soft shell crab is incredible, super crunchy and delicious. It's exactly the way soft shell crab should be everywhere. This dish was devoured in about 5 minutes.

I wanted to love this place. I only have a week in NYC and wanted to make it count for each and every meal. I researched online and on Yelp to find best hot pot place. The decor is nice. First off, there were no customers but one sad table with two ladies. The place is pretty big and empty. They seated us next to restroom and kitchen, with wait staff literally hovering over our table. The breeze from AC brought smell of bathroom and kitchen (directly spoons and plates were right there for me to stare at. There were way better tables as it was all empty. The employees don't seem to know the menu or food well as they couldn't answer basic questions. The white broth was good. The spicy broth was not very flavorful. It was just oily. The rib eye was cut super huge and hard to eat. The meat quality did not taste very good. I came here because reviews said their meat was good. It was not and certainly not worth the high prices. Based on price and quality, I would not recommend this place. The food is okay but not for the price they are charging. The prices for veggies and drinks were fine. The meat prices were crazy expensive and not very good. The meat was not cut right. For a "nice" restaurant trying to be modern and trendy, their choice in music is weird. It was hardcore rap from the late 90s and clubbing music from early 2000s. While the service was okay (they refilled my water often), nobody smiled.

Title: A Hidden Gem in Greenwich - Balaboosta Shines Bright

From the moment you step into the charming enclave of Greenwich to find Balaboosta, you know you're in for a treat. This place truly lives up to its rave reviews with a culinary prowess that's hard to disregard.

Our party of three was greeted with the Hummus Basar - a luxurious blend of hummus topped with a generous portion of beef. It's not an overstatement to call it phenomenal, especially when scooped up with the light yet perfectly crispy pita served alongside.

We ventured further into the menu, sampling the octopus, which easily ranked as one of the finest I've ever enjoyed; the brick chicken, which impressed us with its succulence; and the lamb shank, a rich and flavorsome feast for the senses.

The ambiance of Balaboosta adds to the dining experience, making our meal not just satisfying but thoroughly enjoyable. Safe to say, my taste buds were very happy campers here.

I'm absolutely obsessed with this gem of a restaurant! Not only does its motto resonate with the dining experience, but the food truly steals the show. The truffle mac and cheese is divine, and do not even get me started on the edamame gyoza – a must-try! Be warned, snagging a table can be a challenge since this hotspot fills up quickly; they have a strict policy of seating only when your full party arrives. But trust me, it's worth any wait. And for an extra treat, order one of their signature light-up soju drinks. It's not just a meal; it's an experience. Do yourself a favor and plan your visit soon!

Title: Breathtaking Views and Comfort at Marriott Marquis Lounge

I recently visited the lounge on the 8th floor of the Marriott Marquis and was instantly mesmerized by the incredible views. Easily accessible and family-friendly, this rooftop-ish gem is not to be missed. Initially, navigating the elevators was a bit of a puzzle, but the small effort was well worth it.

Upon arrival, we were greeted with an array of open seating options, but we struck gold with window-side seats that offered an unparalleled perspective of the cityscape. The ambiance was perfect for enjoying a selection of appetizers and beverages.

Price-wise, the drinks are on par with typical Manhattan rates, yet the vista alone justifies every penny spent. My 16-year-old was just as enamored with the experience, proving it's a hit for all ages.

Without a doubt, this lounge has earned a spot on my list of must-returns, and I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone seeking a blend of comfort, a delightful atmosphere, and a feast for the eyes.

I was in the mood for dumplings & was recommended by yelp to try out this spot. Such a great decision! This month's special was the Thanksgiving Dumplings. I couldn't believe it! When I saw this on the menu at, I just had to try it & I am sooo glad I did!! Hands down one of the best dumplings I have had thus far!! The flavor was on point & all the ingredients went to well together, I just wanted more & more  Worth every bite!.Thanksgiving dinner dumplings made with local turkey, house made gravy, cranberry sage stuffing served with a side of hose made cranberry sauce. It's only for the month of November but I hope the bring it back in the near future!. The place itself it cute & clean. Love the vibe & the bright light setting! Great for photos :)

Stopped by at 12 on a Tuesday and there was a line out the door. Luckily, we got inside after only about ten minutes of waiting. Not bad, considering the place is new and it was prime lunch time. Once you're inside, the line moves even quicker. So it's best to look up the menu ahead of time and decide what you want. You order at the register and pay, then bring the ticket to the next counter and will ask you if you want corn or tortilla for the tacos (we did one of each and I preferred the corn), and what toppings you want. All items come with guacamole, onions, cilantro, and salsa, unless otherwise specified. There's also a self-serve say s station where you can get pico de gallo, salsa verde, and hot salsa (all were great).There were a bunch of things on the menu that my cousin and I wanted to try so we decided to order a bunch of things to share. This wasn't the best idea because it was very difficult to split everything since they don't have plastic knives. So we did our best with a plastic forks and worked with what we were given. Here is everything we ordered:Carne asada quesadilla - this was the best one. The steak was great. Also, it's not really the typical quesadilla you'd think of. I would think two tortillas with melted cheese and some protein. But the quesadillas here are more like tacos. Same size too. Not really sure what the difference between the two at Los Tacos is, to be honest. Especial quesadilla (added chicken for $2) - this is a fried quesadilla. I'm really glad we shared this one because it was pretty oily and would have been a bit much for one person. Adobada taco - this was a pork taco. My friend had mentioned this one wasn't great but I really wanted to try it so I ordered it anyway. Maybe she just had a bad batch? But I didn't think it was bad at all. Not the best pork taco, but not the worst either.Pollo asado taco - we had thought we ordered the nopales (cactus) taco but either we ordered it wrong or it was rung up wrong. Either way, it was still a good taco. The chicken here is chunks of chicken, instead of shredded so it was nice, because it wasn't dry.I'd definitely come back if I want some good tacos, especially since it's pretty close to my office. But next time, I won't be sharing. I had also see someone post a picture of a special cheese taco shell they had, which I didn't see. So hopefully next time, they'll have it.Tip - standing room only

What a surprise In NYC !Found this lil gem via Seated, and a gem it is. Who knew Chicken Pho could be this good. Yes Chicken Pho !First to hit the table was the crispy fried spring rolls. Delicious grilled pork with wood ear mushrooms, Ming bean, taro, carrot, onions and a homemade spicy fish oil sauce. The rolls were crispy and flavorful. And well paired with its tangy, and spicy oil sauce.Also to hit the table were pork summer rolls. Grilled pork with lettuce, herbs, mango and a fried wonton, wrapped in the traditional noodle skin. The first bite had me ! The crunch, flavors and crispiness of the veggies and crispy wonton made me wanting more! This will be on my table again... complimented with Hosin and peanuts on the side.And finally what we came for the chicken pho !This pho is chicken-based bone broth with shredded tender chicken, a chicken egg, veggies, herbs and rice noodles with a chicken ginger oil dipping sauce. At first without the sauce the pho was lightly seasoned, but once adding the ginger oil sauce, this made the pho POP ! Spicy chicken noodle flavors, YUM....I did the lunch specials (pho+roll+drink $15) well worth the price.Follow me on Instagram, Facebook, Yelp, and YouTube as I travel the world, in search of the perfect bowl of noodle soup..#noodlesoupreview #noodlesoupr

Title: A Sweet Catch at Sugarfish

Rating: ★★★★★

Review:
Do believe the buzz around Sugarfish; it’s a catch. Arriving early at 5:30 PM on a Saturday paid off, sliding just ahead of the inevitable queue. The staff at the front desk exuded warmth, and despite the hour-long wait projection for two, it was a pleasant surprise when it was cut down to 45 minutes. Their system kept us in the loop via text.

My partner and I opted for different set meals - the Trust Me and Nozawa Trust Me (minus the raw scallop special on this occasion). We indulged in extra rolls of unagi and sweet shrimp. A minor setback, the uni was unavailable, but this did little to dampen the spirit of the meal.

The quality of fish could spar with the city’s finest omakases. A standout feature was the sushi rice - unexpectedly warm and a perfect companion to the seafood. Choosing favorites is tough, but if pressed, the toro hand roll, albacore, and unagi rolls stole the show. The sets are a smart choice over a la carte.

The staff deserves applause; they were affable and unhurried, a true testament to guest care. Sugarfish is already on my “can’t wait to return” list. Highly recommended.

After spending a lengthy day at conferences, I finally visited a spot that came recommended for late-night gatherings by my friends. I settled on the shrimp and vegetable tempura udon, which was fairly standard fare—nothing particularly noteworthy. I started with the Tako Wasabi and Potato Croquette, only to find them passable but not remarkable.

The standout of the meal was the grilled duck, which was quite enjoyable and worth mentioning. A dining companion opted for the Sukiyaki Udon and regrettably found it overwhelmingly salty. It's a flavor profile some may prefer, but it's prudent to approach with caution if you’re sensitive to salt.

The establishment seems better suited for its 3 AM sake than its culinary offerings. Given the late hours, I understand the appeal for my friends in search of a nightcap. An added convenience is the tip-included pricing, sparing diners the usual post-meal calculus.

In short, if you're in for the late-night drinks, it's your spot. Come for the food, and you might find it a hit or miss.

Title: A Sauce to Remember

If there's one thing you must do when in Little Italy, it's to pop into this quaint gem and give your taste buds the treat of a lifetime. The star of the show? Their heavenly sauce. A unanimous decision among the four of us, it's the best we've ever savored—infusing just the right balance of vinegar, spice, sweetness, and that ever-elusive umami. This delightful concoction had us pleading for a bottled version to take back to Arizona. And let's not overlook the dumplings—utterly scrumptious! During a gastronomic odyssey through NYC, this spot easily took the crown for the best bite in town. Do yourself a favor and make it a must-visit. Your palate will thank you!

I recently dined at Sai Gon Dep and was blown away by the experience. Not only does this restaurant offer fantastic food, but it can comfortably accommodate large groups without a hitch. The service was top-notch – attentive and efficient throughout our visit. Most impressive was the value for the price, with generous portions and high-quality dishes at reasonable rates. This place is a gem and definitely worth checking out. Don't just take my word for it, see more rave reviews here: yelp.com/biz/sai-gon-dep.

Met a friend here as I was in the area. A small and cosy restaurant with great service. The restaurant fits about 20-25 people and we were lucky enough to get a table for 5 with no prior reservation. We tried out a couple of mains from their menu - burger, huevos rancheros, their daily chorizo special and a side of Brussels Sprouts with chorizo. All were delicious and we finished it all. The chorizo was so nice and spicy, I would definitely order it again. The food took awhile to come out however the restaurant was basically almost full when we were there.I also tried their coconut mojito. A little bit on the sweet side but it was nice and enjoyable. Three mains, a side and 4 drinks came at $140 for the table which wasn't too bad.The place might not be stroller friendly unless you have one of those collapsible ones as space is a bit tight.

I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant during a lunch break to celebrate a coworker's birthday. Despite our tight schedule, the service was admirably efficient. Our waiters, though a tad awkward, were genuinely kind and provided insights on the menu that guided our meal choices effectively. I opted for the chicken sandwich; it was nothing short of incredible — substantial in size, I took half of it home. It proved to be a satisfying meal that offered great value for the price. Additionally, this location outshines its Upper East Side counterpart by miles. I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

Recently had this delivered. My normal go-to was still delicious. (Spicy coconut lemongrass soup.)HOWEVER, being the adventurous eater that I am, I also added on a new item I saw on their menu, a pan-fried chive cake dumpling.  I do not recommend this. It was way too gelatinous in texture, barely edible and weird flavor. Avoid this menu item.Still get the spicy coconut lemongrass soup. That's still a 10/10 in my book. 4.5/5

Title: Warm Service and Tasty Treats at Cozy Eatery

I recently dined at a local restaurant that truly understands the meaning of hospitality. Despite our staggered arrivals for a party of seven, the staff maintained their sweetness and professionalism, keeping our table ready amidst numerous other inquiries—a testament to their accommodating nature.

My choice of a Thai iced tea was a delightful refreshment, and it came complimentary, though a tip for fellow diners: present the check-in offer before ordering to ensure the deal. My main course, duck basil udon, was a mix of hits and misses. While the udon noodles were cooked to perfection, the duck, unfortunately, fell short of expectations, being somewhat dry and lacking in tenderness.

To end our meal on a high note, the restaurant surprised us with a complimentary dessert that was nothing short of delicious. For those curious about the visual culinary journey, their Instagram account @phothegram is a feast for the eyes.

In conclusion, while there was a slight hiccup with the duck, the exceptional service and the delectable dessert left us walking away with smiles. Definitely a spot to consider when you're craving a warm welcome and a satisfying meal.

Title: A Brunch with Potential at Havana Central

Havana Central boasts a vibrant atmosphere that's ideal for brunch enthusiasts. As you step in and are welcomed with the lively strums and beats of live music, you're instantly transported to the streets of Havana, immersed in a rich, cultural setting.

A standout feature of my experience was the exceptional service by Abinael, whose professionalism and charisma could very well crown him the best waiter in New York. His ability to elevate the dining experience is a compelling reason to revisit.

While the ambiance and service hit high notes, the brunch menu's performance was less stellar. The offerings felt repetitive, and my breakfast burrito arrived somewhat tepid, requiring a dash of extra seasoning for that needed zing. However, the drinks were the redeeming act – the rum punches were brilliantly concocted, delivering a delightful and memorable impact.

Havana Central is on the cusp of great with a few tweaks to their brunch menu. A broader selection would no doubt complement their already impressive drink lineup and service, making it a must-visit spot for a truly fulfilling brunch experience.

Food: Just okay. Feels like Japanese / American bar food. We started off with some pretzels, popcorn and cucumbers. First course was scallops. Second, oysters with kimchi. Third, tuna with fried rice balls. Fourth, shisito peppers. Fifth, salmon. 6th, yuzu / blueberry shaved ice (pretty bad). Last, pizza. The food was just average and nothing memorable. I'm happy I tried the place out but would never go back again for the food.Ambience: great! You have a beautifully set up restaurant where you get to choose a record. If the food only matched the ambience this place would be a slam dunk. One con was that the record player was a little janky throughout the night.The service was okay. Nothing spectacular nor horrible to note.

Title: A Stellar Vegetarian Experience at Nix

From the moment I made my reservation at Nix, I knew I was in for a treat, but nothing could quite prepare me for the sensory delight that awaited me. As someone who typically gravitates towards lighter vegan fare, the prospect of dining at a vegetarian restaurant with a Michelin star was tantalizing.

The experience was top-notch right from the get-go. Celebrating my move to the city, I was touched by the thoughtful welcome – a special card and complimentary rosé, courtesy of Nix. Such personal gestures added an extra layer of charm to an already promising evening.

The culinary journey was nothing short of spectacular. Each dish was a discovery, starting with the heavenly tandoor bread accompanied by a smoky eggplant dip that set my taste buds dancing. The winter-summer roll and the white carrot tabbouleh were notable highlights, showcasing the kitchen's ability to elevate simple ingredients into complex flavor profiles. The spicy tofu and cauliflower tempura continued the trend, with heat and texture in perfect harmony.

My drink, the "in pink" cocktail, was a refreshing accompaniment, artfully crafted and delicious. To cap off the meal, the ginger cake was a revelation – the zing of ginger weaving through each moist, decadent forkful.

The service was impeccable throughout, with our server guiding us skillfully through the menu and ensuring our evening was flawless. Nix has certainly set a high bar for my Michelin star adventures in the city, and I'm eager to return for another round of their culinary delights.

We came here for restaurant week dinner and everything was amazing!! The decor of the restaurant is romantic and RED! The walls are literally painted red which is very unusual for a steakhouse. All the apps are very good I would recommend getting the Caesar salad and the bacon. They were super delicious. For main, we got the filet mignon which was cooked perfectly to medium rare. The sides are very good. I would recommend the creams spinach and Max and cheese or fries- depending on your mood. The tiramisu as our dessert is out of the world. The service was fast and casual. Very comfortable setting and place for a bottle of good wine and delicious dinner!

99 Favor Taste beats Hometown.Both hotpot experiences were within one month of each other, so I can easily say that if I go to hotpot again, it would be at 99. Same great selection of sauces, and slightly more hotpot options than at Hometown. In particular, there's this fish roe dumpling/ball that I love here! I've never had it before until the birthday girl ordered it, but one bite, and the stuff was popping, oozing hot into my mouth and I was sold.I love that this establishment recognizes that no one wants go to the dry cleaners with their outerwear after two hours of bbq/hotpot here, so the first thing they do is help your party stuff your jackets into a big plastic bag. You can wash everything else yourself, but odds are, you're not gonna be able to wash your down jacket, so this is awesome.Our party of four originally wanted to do bbq until we realized how little meat options there were for bbq...so we switched to hotpot. Got the pork bone broth, which they legit put one huge piece of pork bone into. YES.Food was served almost immediately, and while they did forget some orders at the end, they were very willing to agree to two plates of the same meat at once! We were there for definitely more than two hours, but they didn't rush us to leave at all. Skip the carrot juice unless you absolutely love carrots. There was so much pulp/foam at the top, that I barely drank any actual juice. Not worth the price.

Fantastic Chef's tasting menu.  Sancerre and Italian beer to kick things off.  Primi were the burrata and mushroom truffle tortellini.  Both very delicious. We had the pork chop and the duck.  They were prepared perfectly and very satisfying.  Loved the cheesecake and chocolate mousse desserts.  Pretty space and attentive service.

When I was here I ordered roti, chicken satay, and ultimate curry laksa. All of them were very very good! Would definitely recommend the laksa, I tried it because I saw it on buzzfeeds worth it video. It was very expensive to me though, at $18. But it was delicious!! I loved the vibes this place had too, like the decorations and signs on the wall.

Mille Nonne has stolen the title of my favorite Italian spot with its heartfelt homemade offerings in the bright and airy spaces of the new Essex Market. Service is counter-style with meals enjoyed in a sunlit dining area, thanks to the floor-to-ceiling windows.

The meal was a sharing affair with standout dishes like the pesto gnocchi, boasting a perfect chew complemented by high-quality olive oil and pine nuts. The spinach lasagna was deceptive in its simplicity, with a béchamel that elevated creamed spinach to new heights, all harmonizing with a luscious red sauce. The turkey quinoa meatballs were another highlight, surprising with their light yet satisfying texture and flavor.

For dessert, the macerated berry panna cotta was a triumph—berries adding a tart contrast to the velvety custard. The ricotta mousse dazzled with its blend of dark chocolate, orange peel, and a hint of olive oil, making for an unforgettable finale.

Mille Nonne not only satisfied our palates but also showed true kindness in service. Every dish mentioned is certainly on my reorder list. A heartfelt thank you to the team for such a memorable dining experience.

This place was very good. The hari mirch tikka and chili shrimp balchao appetizers were excellent. The chicken curry (we went off of the waiter's recommendation) was good as well. My only point of contention is that it was a bit expensive. But if you don't mind that, I would recommend trying this place out!

During my visit to the restaurant, the prices felt quite steep considering the offerings. While the Lobster roll was tasty, its 'jumbo' size was misleadingly small. The Lobster brisket, though branded as 'large', was underwhelming with an abundance of potatoes and corn and scant lobster meat. Price-wise, $35 for the roll and brisket alone seemed excessive. Factoring in tax and a soda, my modest lunch totaled an eye-watering $50. When I think that elsewhere in Manhattan I could indulge in a 1 1/2 lb. grilled lobster with butter, fries, and salad for $30 or savor a selection of three rolls for $25, the value proposition here just doesn't hold water.

Wow! Such flavor-packed wafels and the dinges made it all spectacular. We ordered a double decker build your own to share. Prices are high: $17 for ours with 2 waffles and 4 toppings (1st topping free). Service is slow. But the taste is really great. We will enjoy this treat again.

If you are looking for authentic arepas, this is not for you. Areppas offer set arepas or you can customize and make your own. I had the downtown arepa. They are generous with the toppings especially the cheese, but it wasn't satisfying for me especially for the price. The arepa is a bit hard and it could use some sauce but it wasn't bad tasting.

A bottle of Chardonnay, table by the window and a dozen fresh clams.  Patrick's selection of clams from both east and west coast is perfect.  To top it off order Fish & Chips, simply delicious.A table by the window is a must, great people watching.  They also have very nice private rooms if you wanna have a little party.

I came across the Yelp page for Prince Street Pizza and notice many of main Elite NY, NJ Yelpers that I know have reviewed them with one major discrepancy, and that was that my face wasn't among them. Well I have rectified that issue and here is my review.I got the two main slices from here,  the Spicy Pepperoni Square, and the Margherita  slice, There was standing space in the shop to eat it there if I wanted too and it I only took about 5 minutes or so from the time I got there to the time I was out the door.And the verdict ?Well the Pepperoni Square was covered edge to edge with median slice spicy pepperoni that the spiciness was in the middle of the scale. Well if I was a pepperoni guy then this would have been the bomb with all that pepperoni, but I like sausage more than pepperoni so judging on just taste then this had nothing else going for it other than a thick crust.  The Margherita slice was better tasting with a thing crust and not oily. I found it better tasting than the pepperoni slice. But I have had pizza in NY and in NJ that was better than both of these slices. And these where and  main event from what I see in other reviews so Prince is more of a Duke in my royal book.So I am giving Prince a generous 4 stars instead of 3 only because they got enough going for them with other Yelpers to make me come there for a slice of pizza.

I brought my sister here for the Restaurant Fest at Eataly. Diners had a choice of two courses for $18 and a bottle of wine for $25. I made reservations, luckily, because the wait was kind of crazy and it was apparent that many people did not reserve ahead of time. My suggestion is that if you plan on visiting, make reservations ahead, especially on a weekend.I asked for accommodation since I would have a stroller with me and the ladies in at host podium were very helpful in that they sat us where I would have enough space to park my stroller next to our table. They also offer high chairs so don't worry about bringing the kiddos. The restaurant is very tightly packed with tables and very busy so be prepared.Our server was attentive, despite it being a bit of a frenzy that particular day. We ordered some fresh spring salads that were really good, my sister had the spaghetti for her main and I chose the ravioli. Had it not been for the bread we received at the beginning of the meal, we likely would have been hungry still.I also ordered a couple of pizzas for my boys at home. The prices were kind of ridiculous considering how the pizzas tasted. They were "ok" but not worth the $20+ price tags. All in all, the food tasted good and I was satisfied by the end of our meal but I doubt I'd return.

Sometimes you get hangry and have to eat by yourself. Luckily at ramen joints, there are bar seats and it feels less awks. Ramen is also quick and easy. Nakaura is around the block from my apartment and I decided to have a solo dinz. The small restaurant wasn't too packed for a Saturday night and I was able to get a seat at the counter. I always opt for a Tonkotsu broth - their rich and creamy pork broth with chashu pork, bamboo shoots, spinach, scallion, and red cabbage. I was expecting a quick meal, but it took a terribly long time for my bowl to come out. As mentioned below, the restaurant wasn't even packed. I also ordered a side of their ajutama egg, but they had forgotten it. The soup was barely hot as well. If you're hungry, I would order extra noodles. The (210g) of noodles as listed on their menu is kid portioned. The broth was thick and somewhat flavorful. It comes with one piece of meat which wasn't the most tender.The restaurant was so small and yet it took forever for them to acknowledge me to get the bill.  For $20 a bowl (+2$ for an egg), you can get better ramen elsewhere. I left borderline satisfied and could have used an extra order of noodz.

You live in or costing Manhattan and want some place to watch Game of Thrones with a crowd?   Well this is the place!  The Stone Creek Ale is one good beer.  The grilled chicken sandwich on brioche is yummy and comes with crinkled fires.  The Caesar salad is crispy and tasty.  The nachos weren't that great though... needs more cheese. The good news is the cheese is real, not that Velveeta stuff.  And the service is good too. I guess they show GoT here every Sunday night.  Pretty crowded so get there at least an hour early.  Lots of fun and chit chat.... till the show starts. Then you don't talk. You watch.  Seriously.  But if you're a GoT fan, it's really fun.  Why not five stars?  Well the food isn't THAT good and it's a little pricey.

Went with two colleagues who were extremely hungry. We were seated quickly. I just had water and no appetizers. The server was a young woman and friendly. It was a small spot but stayed full. I decided on the BUTTERMILK FRIED CHICKEN with arugula & chipotle mayo, no avocado on a portuguese muffin and truffle fries. So the sandwich was good overall. Maybe the avocado is what sets it off. The fries were already the battered fries so I would have eaten without the truffle. Overall, the service was good. The food was just okay for me personally. I did like the chicken sandwich but not so much the fries. I would consider going back to try a different menu item as well as just the regular fries.

Right when I walked into omakase room by masser, I was not overcome with the smell of fresh, delicious fish, but of a very strong, potent floor cleaner smell. By all means, I'm glad that may mean the establishment is clean, but my gosh was it overpowering.Overall, not impressed by the quality of the omakase. Besides the quantity being adequate for the price, I wouldn't return or come back again with others. The fish to rice ratio was not proportional. The rice kept falling apart. The sushi chefs were not knowledgeable about the fish. They would hesitate when we asked them where a piece was from and then say the same city of Japan every time (who knew if it was true or not). When we were given the Hotaru ika with the mysterious white creamy sauce on top, we asked the chef what the sauce was and they couldn't provide us an answer. Our sushi chef who was serving us looked at the sushi chef next to him and he told us to "just eat it". Of course we ate it. It was tasty. But thanks dude. Guess we'll just call it a 'mysterious crack mayo sauce'.One star only given to the fact that each server made sure I knew it was BYOB once walking through the door. They said if I wanted to go purchase a bottle at the wine store nearby, I'm welcome to. There are no limits to the number of bottles which is great. We really needed the alcohol to wash down all the fish which came from the same city in Japan and topped with 'mysterious crack mayo sauce'.

I have been here twice now for dinner, and I genuinely want to like it but I can't stand the ambience. I would recommend maybe ordering to pick up or coming for lunch because their food is reasonably priced (generally $15 per meal), but I no longer want to come and sit down.Food: Delicious. I tried something new every time, and haven't been disappointed. The Kow Soy had a light sweet milky taste, not too heavy and the crunchy noodles added a great texture. So much food, I had trouble finishing it! The Khao Moo Palo's pork was savory and juicy, paired nicely with the cooked vegetables. Would recommend both.Ambience: Can't stand it! I can't hear myself speak, or if I do it's because I'm yelling and going hoarse. The restaurant becomes a popular spot at night for couples or groups of friends to hang out and drink at the bar, and the sound carries over so easily that the place sounds like a high school cafeteria. In addition, at around 8pm the place is so packed on a weekend that you can't enjoy the company of your friends; you get asked to leave right after you pay the bill to make room for the next guests. Not blaming the staff of course, but if you plan to have a leisurely catch-up with friends this is not the place for you.

Came here for dinner on a Tuesday night around 8 and we were able to be seated right away. The menu was a little confusing with the one two three system, one was pretty clearly appetizers but from the pictures online a lot of the options in 2 didn't look to be enough for a full entree (I'm a very hungry person). Our server said the items there weren't too big or too small, but they do recommend people order more than one item. I decided to go for the sausage and kale pizza after seeing how popular it was in reviews and I completely understand why that's the case! The sausage had a nice smoky flavor that went really well with the parmigiano and both of those strong flavors balanced out nicely with the kale. The pizza was big enough that I could imagine 2 people splitting that and a small appetizer and being more than satisfied. I will usually skip the bread to not waste space/calories, but the free bread here is worth making an exception. It's super soft and lightly salted, brought me back to the best soft pretzels of childhood.

Walked right in, no line but we took long to decide what to order  ended up with the 7oz lobster roll combo - chips and bottled drink.  Super delicious lobster roll and I had half a crab roll which was also delicious!  We met one of founders, Ben and had a little conversation about best places to eat in New York!  Awesome service and yummy seafood rolls!

Came here because I'm a vegetarian and I saw this as one of the best veggie burgers from Buzzfeed. I wanted to see what the hype was about and whether it lived up to expectations. I ordered the Megamouth considering that I was more hungry than usual and it was the larger sized superiority burger.The inside can barely seat more than 5 people. It was extremely small, so we ordered the burgers to go and ended up sitting in the park nearby.The burger wasn't amazing - I felt that it was just a typical veggie burger and it didn't surprise me or anything. For a $9 burger, I'd say it was fairly average in taste and size.I was somewhat disappointed, but I'm happy to say that I did give it a try as a fellow vegetarian.
