Came here for restaurant week. The place is inside Perrine Hotel and and near Central Park. I was surprised that it was fairly empty when I arrived for a Friday 7pm dinner. The food was pretty good, the two appetizers: tuna tartare and heirloom tomato salad was really good. Tuna was fresh and nicely paired with the sauce. Tomato salad was also refreshing however, wish there was more burrata. The two main course, beef short ribs and swordfish; short rib was nicely paired with the sauce but the swordfish could use a little work; maybe it was the wrong sauce pairing. The desserts were good! Loved the creme brûlée from here, it had a little bit of a citrus taste! The warm chocolate cake was pretty good, warm and chocolaty but can get a bit overwhelming when you eat too much since it's heavy. I would go back to try their lamb chop and other dishes if I'm around the area.

Having read rave reviews about this unique establishment, my curiosity got the best of me, and I ventured in to sample their signature dish: the surf and turf pho. At $25, it's the priciest pho I've encountered, but the lavish inclusion of a substantial beef rib and a hearty half lobster justified the cost. True to its acclaim, the pho base was robust and satisfying, with no aspect amiss.

The beef rib was a highlight, tender enough to effortlessly part from the bone, while the lobster was a testament to skilled preparation – succulent and flawlessly cooked. To elevate the meal, the spicy pig knuckles were an unforgettable delight that demand a taste.

Overall, the experience was well worth the visit. This restaurant has secured a spot on my go-to list, and I'll certainly be back for more.

Title: A Delicious Thai Delight at Uncle Boon's

I recently celebrated my friend's birthday at Uncle Boon's, a restaurant high on her culinary bucket list. Our Thursday 6pm arrival was met with a bustling scene – the place was swarming with diners, signaling a wait time of over an hour. Opting for the bar, we snagged seats in a mere 10 minutes, the tantalizing aromas already promising a delightful meal.

The menu presented a welcome challenge with an array of enticing options, making selection a delightful dilemma. The drinks did not disappoint; my choice of Mr. Rambutan, adorned with the actual fruit, was as tasty as it was visually stunning.

Our shared plates journey began with fried pig ears, which were a revelation in seasoning and texture, erasing any past disappointments I had with this dish. The frog legs, although a touch too salty for my taste, were nicely complemented with noodles. The crab fried rice was a highlight, generously laden with succulent crab meat – an exemplary dish despite the green sauce's overpowering nature when combined.

Dessert was a dual affair: an ice cream sundae that paired the crunch of candied peanuts with the soft sweetness of coconut flakes, and the squash custard, a mild and unique choice for those desiring a less adventurous sweet ending.

Ratings tell the story of an almost flawless dining experience: Taste at a hearty 4 to 4.5, Atmosphere and Presentation impressing at 4.5, with Service deserving a perfect 5, bringing the Overall experience to a commendable 4 to 4.5. Uncle Boon's certainly delivers on its promise of a memorable Thai meal.

Title: A Birthday Dinner to Remember

Review:
Our recent visit to this gem for a birthday celebration left us as enamored as ever. Despite a slightly revamped menu, the quality hasn't waned in the slightest. Opting for the day's special, the steak was cooked to perfection, highlighting the chef's continued commitment to excellence. The service was as commendable as my fond memories, contributing to a dining experience that ensured everyone left with smiles. A seamless blend of the familiar and the novel, this restaurant remains a top choice for special occasions. Highly recommended!

Venturing out for restaurant week, I had the opportunity to experience a venue quite distinct from my regular NYC haunts. Catering to an older demographic, the establishment hummed with energy even as it neared closing time. The decor was eclectic, with an array of "toys" adorning the ceiling, though it was hard to discern a unifying theme.

The restaurant week menu was lacking in vegetarian options, prompting me to opt for sides - a Caesar salad, truffle mash, and roasted vegetables from the regular entrees - to complement the meal, while my partner enjoyed the meat dishes. The truffle mash was a highlight, but overall, the meal failed to make a lasting impression. The desserts, however, did offer a more memorable finish.

Though the ambiance felt a bit dated and the clientèle somewhat staid, the staff was personable and attentive. While my visit left me feeling rather indifferent towards the culinary experience, it might be worth a try for those curious about this old-school establishment.

The place reminds me Johnny Rockets.  It has all the colorful aspects of it, including the tables and seats.  Left a concert at the Gramercy theater and it was about 11pm.  I was originally looking for Les Halles down the block but my guest and i decided to get some basic comfort food.  The place has a feel for a diner which it is. The music they were playing were 80's type and brought back some memories for my guest who dined with me. It was a late nite and the close at midnight i believe. Had the sliders which were not bad at all. The burgers were cooked almost well done, the chocolate shake was enormously generous.  It was a decent shake and i did enjoy it. You can tell the people were wiped out and looking to go home. Even the manager seemed to have a sour face. My guest had the tater tots smothered in gravy and cheese.  You could say it was an alcohol absorbing meal.  The place is not bad and good for late night if you are in the area. I am sure they fill up during the day because of the confort food they serve.

Wonderful Turkish food and service!Have been here several times, and saw the restaurant transform wonderfully from its earlier days - with improved and inviting colors, paintings  and artwork.  Food is always fantastic. My favorite's are the manti and sultan delight which are incredible.Service.  Servers are attentive and friendly, and the owner we met one visit was also very friendly.Attracts a little bit of everyone. Various ages, couples, families, and friends. We were there once when a fun, talented and entertaining belly dancer made an appearance while we ate dinner. She engaged a few people and even motioned for a few audience members dance with and even adorned a tray full of candles on her head for part of her 15 minute so dance.  Everyone from children to couples around us enjoyed the experience.Definitely recommend for friends, date or a family outing for fantastic food, service and an upbeat vibe.

When I first arrived, the waiter asked if I had a reservation. Although there were many seats available, he looked around and thought real hard before putting me at a table with poor lighting. When someone else entered after without reservations, I noticed him do the same. So if you care about getting the better seats in the place, I suppose reservations are the way to go. Now onto the food. My friend ordered their shashuka with added tonkatsu and a side of bacon. I tried some of the shashuka and it mostly reminds me of tomato sauce. Meanwhile, I opted for their yuzu clams vongole. While my friend found his meal filling, my clams vongole did not fill me up at all. I felt pretty hungry after finishing even though it was $21. That price really can't be justified and honestly I kept choking on the panko that was in the pasta. If you inhale as you eat, you might have the same problem as me. As for the taste, I thought it was more on the bland side.At the end of the meal, I tried getting the waiter's attention. He motioned one second and greeted people who came in. Afterwards, he seemed to have forgotten and just walked around. He poured water for a table beside us and I had to get his attention again. Aside from that, the service was decent, but I'm really disappointed in the portion size.

A quick place to grab an Indian meal. Opted for the chicken tikka Kati roll, which was pretty flavorful. It was the perfect amount of heat. I wanted to try the paneer but they do not let you mix the orders. The service was quick around 830pm. The interior was spacious with plenty of seating. A good place for a quick bite.

Title: Tater Tots Triumph at Cozy Sandwich Spot

I recently visited a charming eatery renowned for its sandwiches, and I must say, the experience exceeded my expectations. The loaded tater tots were a standout, adorned with a velvety cheese sauce, crispy bacon, and a kick of jalapeños – each bite was a crunchy delight. Not to be overshadowed, the brisket sandwich was a culinary masterpiece; the bread’s perfect crunch paired with a mouthwatering sauce and filling left me impressed. To complement my meal, I sipped on a Babe Rosé, a bubbly choice that harmonized beautifully with the flavors. It's a winning combination for anyone who fancies a casual dining spot with top-notch fare.

Not sure if we came on an off day, but the two of us found our three shared dishes a bit disappointing. The dan-dan-mixian ($20!) was bland and gummy. Half the pork wontons were soggy and exploded. And most upsetting of all was the scallop crudo, which was presented beautifully but sadly seemed like everything had been pre-cut & marinating for far too long so the flavors & textures were muddled and bloated; however if they added another scallop and cleaned up the presentation a lot, they could easily charge three times as much and I would not complain one bit, because the concept is banging. I'd been wanting to come here forever, and have seen & heard many great things about it from friends, but I just cannot see myself returning until they sort out the unfortunate preparation pitfalls...

After an evening at the Vessel in Hudson Yards, the Spanish culinary delights at this gem of a spot were a much-anticipated treat. Boasting an array of sit-down restaurants and kiosks, options abound from churros to jamon, satisfying a variety of cravings. My dining companion and I indulged in the Valencia paella, a generous portion priced reasonably at $16, brimming with hearty chunks of meat and pleasantly crispy bites. The half dozen freshly prepared churros, paired with a delicate chocolate dipping sauce, were a steal for $8. In terms of ambiance, this place edges out Eataly with its spacious, less crowded setting and superior decor. The experience was a resounding success and I'm eager to explore more of their offerings on my next visit.

Title: A Warming Taste of Vietnam in the Heart of Chinatown

If your taste buds are yearning for Vietnamese cuisine, consider making your way to this authentic gem nestled in bustling Chinatown. With manageable wait times outside the dinner rush, seating is relatively prompt, though larger groups should aim for an early arrival owing to the no-reservation policy.

The pho is a must-try, particularly comforting on chilly days, paired perfectly with the warmth of hot tea. The grilled pork chops and fresh spring rolls are excellent for sharing, adding variety to your meal. However, the chicken fried rice falls short, lacking the distinct zest one might expect.

Service here is notable; staff are attentive, ensuring that your food arrives swiftly. Should you prefer the comforts of your home, take-out is an efficient option.

A word of caution: the floors can be treacherously slippery when wet, so tread with care, especially during inclement weather. Facilities, including a single restroom for each gender, can be found at the back of the restaurant, mirroring the familiar layout found in its local counterparts.

In sum, this establishment offers a solid Vietnamese dining experience, with a few standout dishes and quick service. Just keep an eye on the floor, and you're in for a treat.

This is a sweet place for dining, but we were a little disappointed in the food and service. There is a great drink selection, and the desserts were terrific. But the salads and entrées, and even bread, were just sort of average. There was a consensus in our group about this. Not bad, but we had expected more.

I had previously been recommended to try Tacombi so I decided to try it with a friend on a Tuesday night around 7 PM. When we arrived the restaurant was packed but thankfully there were still a few tables available so we were seated right away. Our server came over immediately to take our orders and bring over a bottle of water. My friend and I got a little bit ambitious with our order since we assumed that the tacos would be smaller than they actually were. But our order ended up to be: -CORN ESQUITES : Flavor of the dish was delicious! Absolutely a much get and they went very well with the chips we got as well-TOTOPOS FUNDIDOS: I've never had totopos until I got it at Tacombi but they are a very interesting flavor - very similar to Fritos chips. The combination of the chips with the toppings and cheese was delicious and definitely was a great starter. -CHIPS AND GUACAMOLE : The totopos made another appearance with the guacamole. The guacamole itself was just ok - not as much flavor as I was hoping there would be so honestly if you're looking for a solid starter I would just stick with the corn esquites and totopos fundidos instead. -AL PASTOR TACO: The al pastor flavor was delicious. I also really liked how the pineapple was sliced very thinly so it gave a hint of the citrus sweetness to help balance out the sauce. -BAJA CRISPY FISH TACO: the fish was very well fried and the sauce it came with was delicious - another great option!  -CHILE RELLANOS TACO: These tacos were very disappointing especially as someone who loves chile rellanos and was looking forward to the dish. The chili was good however the combination of what appears to be butternut squash among other things with it just did not bode well with me both in taste and in texture. -VEGETARIAN QUESADILLAS: They were pretty good - the mushrooms were a little bit on the sourer side but it did come with a nice layer of cheese . All in all, a great light atmosphere with awesome food I will definitely check this place out again the next time I'm craving some Mexican food!

Returning to this local gem after several years, I am pleased to find it thriving. Despite a slight uptick in prices, the value remains commendable. The pork tostada stands out as a delectably messy highlight, maintaining the quality that likely contributes to the eatery's longevity. Space is at a premium, with now four tables tucked inside, reflecting its cozy charm. It may not clinch the title for the best Mexican cuisine across the Five Boroughs, but it certainly holds its own as a reliable neighborhood haunt.

Title: Fusion Delight with a Side of Wait

My boyfriend and I stumbled upon a neighborhood gem on a bustling Saturday evening. The vibrant atmosphere at this packed eatery set high expectations, as did the seemingly scrumptious menu. Boasting a grand selection of sushi rolls and mouth-watering appetizers complemented by attractive happy hour specials, it was difficult not to be enticed.

The culinary highlight was the daring infusion of Latin American flavors into traditional sushi. The result? An exquisite sushi roll with creamy avocado inside and a dollop of guacamole on top, not to mention the surprising crunch of fried cheese. This cross-cultural concoction was nothing short of mind-blowing, and the potent sangria added to the delight, hinting at a future happy hour revisit.

Alas, the service did not match the food's excellence. The wait for our meal stretched to an agonizing 30-40 minutes, a letdown for a spot that should be adept at handling the Saturday night rush. While patience is a virtue, acknowledgment or a small courtesy for the delay would have been appreciated.

Despite the frustrating service, the innovative cuisine and convivial vibe earn this place a solid four stars. It's a restaurant that promises a good time with phenomenal food—if you're prepared to wait.

My birthday dinner at this restaurant was unexpectedly disappointing. The quality of the food has taken a nosedive since my last visit. My go-to sellongtang, priced at $14, was spoiled by pre-mixed rice and a scant amount of soup, which was a terrible letdown. The bossam, costing $30, was served in such meager portions that it hardly justified the price. To make matters worse, the service was painstakingly slow. Regrettably, I won't be returning.

Title: A Slurp of Satisfaction at Xi'an Noodle Haven

I was utterly captivated by the Spicy & Tangy Lamb Noodle Soup at this gem of a spot in NY. Every spoonful was a harmonious blend of flavor without overwhelming spices—a bowl that perfectly sates noodle cravings. So irresistible, in fact, I found myself returning not once, but twice during my trip. If you're in the area, this eatery is a must-try. The lamb noodle soup alone is worth the visit. Highly recommended!

I visited this restaurant for their lunch specials and was not disappointed by the array of offerings. We ordered the BBQ short ribs combo priced at $24.99, which was cooked to perfection, and both the oyster tofu soup and curry tofu soup at $14.99 and $12.99, respectively. Each dish was flavorful and well-portioned. As expected with Korean cuisine, we were treated to complimentary appetizers which, much to our delight, included an extra serving of fried fish. Overall, the quality of the food was decent and the prices felt reasonable for the value received.

Have passed The Palm Too many times and finally dropped in for Saturday night dinner. Nice casual nostalgic vibe with many spacious booths along the wall, glad we got one as the place was loud and I like a bit of privacy. Started off with Sin City and Blackberry Bramble cocktails, potent and delish, also a great deal @ under $15 per. Shared burrata app (special), a creamy fresh glob of buffala with heftyy slices of tangy prosciutto to set it off. I've had burrata in many places and this was the best yet! For mains I got prime rib (need to reserve a piece in advance) and hubbie chose bone-in ribeye. Prime rib was so-so, kinda tough actually but a big piece. Hub's ribeye was juicy and tender. Shared the half and half, a humongous dish of onion fries and chips.Thought we'd add a healthy side so ordered brussell sprouts, which I usually dislike but Palm Too's version is palatable. Finished this feast with cheesecake and fresh whipped cream, very good but served too cold, needed time for it to defrost. Our server Carlo was friendly and attentive despite the busy conditions. We're big eaters and still have enough food left over for another full dinner tonight. We'll be back again but will choose a less busy time for the next visit.

Title: A Delightful Encounter with Scallion Ginger Noodles

I recently dined at a charming spot in New York City and was thoroughly impressed by their Scallion Ginger Noodle entrée. It was a flawless fusion of crisp vegetables and scallions intertwined with exquisitely seasoned noodles; a true "clean bowl" meal that left nothing to be desired for a refreshing lunch.

However, I do feel the restaurant could enhance its appeal by expanding the vegetarian options, as the current selection was somewhat limited for those with plant-based preferences.

The ambiance of the restaurant was perfectly suited for lunchtime, with a comfortable noise level that allowed for a pleasant dining experience. The service was commendable as well, with a server who was both friendly and well-informed about the menu options.

In summary, while I would encourage a broader variety of vegetarian dishes, I left satisfied and would like to extend my gratitude for a memorable meal.

I stopped by this restaurant on a whim and decided to try their ravioli. The dish was exceptionally delicious; however, the portion size left me wanting more. I'm already looking forward to my next visit with plans to sample their pizza.

Growing pains perhaps.  Got a seafood pancake and a small beef combo.  The pancake stood out with good seafood.  The hanger steak was delightfully beefy.  The marinated rib was too sweet.  The bulgogi was overcooked.  The lettuce was artfully presented in a cocktail cup.  I should say, even the beef platter was beautifully arranged, with assorted vegetables adding color.  Portion sizes were adequate.  The kimchi stew was pleasantly sour and bright.  So why 2 stars?  If I'm spending the amount of money for 2 with drinks, then I really don't want to be rushed out of the restaurant in under an hour, especially since the place wasn't busy.  Unless I'm mistaken and they were going for a fast casual restaurant.  Why did the servers grill multiple meats at once?   Why did they continue grilling everything else if they just plated the meat that was just cooked, when we still had the first 2 servings of meat sitting and cooling off, especially when I asked them to hold off the last portion?  The servers are attentive to the point of being overbearing.  I was interrupted mid flight a few times, trying to spoon some soup or sauce my pancake.  It seems like management runs a tight ship but the service needs to be calibrated.  We had at least 6 different people come by the table for different things, not counting the staff that had to move past us for other tables.  It's chaos. The food was fine, the decor and platings were very polished, but the overall experience was lacking due to the staff's behavior.  Leaves a bad taste in your mouth if it feels like all they're trying to do is turn over the table...

After a splendid evening at "Phantom of the Opera," we stumbled upon this vivacious fusion restaurant that catered perfectly to late-night cravings with a last call at 10:30 pm. The service mirrored the hour—swift and efficient.

Our culinary journey commenced with the chicken wings. An exemplary take on texture, they were double-crisped on the exterior, encasing the succulent meat within. Though the soy ginger variation was slightly underwhelming in flavor, it leaves the promise of a spicier adventure for future visits.

The truffle rice cakes draped in an assortment of molten cheeses were a triumph, creating a harmonious blend of gooey and crispy that tantalized the palate.

The bulgogi, a veritable mountain of smoky, savory meat, did not disappoint, although a side of rice would have perfectly complemented the hearty dish.

Our venture took a misstep with the spicy charred chicken, an overzealous attempt at heat without the depth of flavor, which proved overwhelming for some of my companions.

In excess, our order was ambitious for a trio, but the surplus made for a delightful encore at home.

The restaurant's atmosphere was undeniably hip, accented by the cool glow of a moonlight feature, contributing to the overall allure.

This spot comes highly recommended for its atmospheric charm and a menu that excites the senses, albeit with a note of caution for the spice-adverse.

I recently visited a gem of a spot that's perfect for a laid-back meet-up with friends. The ambiance is all about relaxation and ease, setting a chill tone as soon as you step in.

Ordering is straightforward: grab your food at the counter and take a numbered bottle to your table where a server will bring your meal to you. I went for the #2 combo, which included a generous serving of chicken, beef, and shroom tacos, accompanied by chips and guacamole. While flavorful and satisfying, the portion was more than I could handle, so I had the beef taco packed up for later enjoyment.

Kudos to the team for a fantastic experience; the service was top-notch, and the food didn't disappoint. Would recommend for anyone looking for a casual spot with great vibes and tasty eats.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Beetle House

As a seasoned Yelp reviewer, it pains me to write negative reviews, but honesty is key in sharing my experience at Beetle House, which unfortunately earns a dismal zero stars from me.

My visit on a Saturday night started on the wrong foot with the absence of a host to provide a warm welcome or guidance. The feeling of neglect was palpable, much like the ignored pigeons in that well-known airline commercial. 

My attempt to secure a table was met with an abrupt and rude response from an employee, informing me that tables were strictly reserved for clients who had made bookings via Yelp or their website. This crucial information was nowhere to be found in their online presence, nor was it disclosed in their operating hours, which indicated they were open until 2 a.m.

The decor may be enticing, but it does nothing to compensate for the lack of hospitality or clear communication. I ended up dining at Dallas BBQ, where immediate seating starkly contrasted with my experience at Beetle House.

With all due respect to other reviewers who've had positive experiences, based on my visit, I cannot recommend this establishment. The search for good service and a pleasant night out led me elsewhere, and I suggest future patrons consider this before choosing Beetle House for their evening plans.

Title: Fantastic Find for Mexican Fare!

I recently had the pleasure of dining again at my favorite local spot, which has undergone a splendid renovation. The ambiance now is as inviting as their menu, with beautiful new décor that enhances the fun and affordable dining experience.

Their Taco Tuesday is unbeatable – both the chicken and beef tacos are just $2 each and are a must-try. The happy hour offerings are equally tempting with great discounts on drinks.

Weekend brunch here is another highlight. The huevos rancheros, eggs Benedict, and hot chicken have all been exceptional. Each dish was well-prepared, flavorful, and left me thoroughly satisfied.

This restaurant is, without a doubt, my top choice for Mexican cuisine. Whether you're there for a casual meal or a festive brunch, it will not disappoint. Highly recommended!

Steeped in history, Fanelli's isn't just a restaurant; it's a New York institution. Perched on the same Soho corner since 1847, this venerable spot has witnessed the district's transformation from upscale retail hub to manufacturing powerhouse, into the notorious Hell's Hundred Acres, and finally into the chic, artsy enclave we know today.

Fanelli's essence is as authentic as it gets — a place that has satisfied appetites and slaked thirsts through every imaginable era, including the clandestine tippling of the Prohibition period. The ambiance evokes the true spirit of New York: unyielding, eclectic, and drenched in the patina of countless yesterdays.

A visit to Fanelli's is more than a meal — it's a tantalizing taste of the city's rich tapestry, woven into every bite and sip. It's a must-go for anyone craving a genuine slice of the Big Apple.

Title: A Lifelong Affair with Dallas BBQ

I've been a Dallas BBQ loyalist since my earliest memories, finding comfort in their smoky flavors for every conceivable occasion. This spot is my go-to for life's peaks and pits, and the food has never disappointed. Top of my favorites list are the baby back ribs, which I rate an unparalleled 20/10, setting the standard for all ribs I've ever tasted. Close on the ribs' heels are the divine spicy chicken wings, drenched in sauce that's nothing short of celestial, alongside the equally irresistible sticky wings, whose sauce I'd gladly sip by the liter. Don't even get me started on the onion loaf—an unsung hero often overlooked, yet incredibly delicious.

While those are my die-hard favorites, the steak, shrimp, and yellow rice also deserve an honorable mention for their consistent tastiness. And let's not forget the drinks; strong, well-priced, with the peach margarita standing out as a fruity concoction that never fails to delight.

In short, if you're ever in the mood for comfort food that hits the spot every time, Dallas BBQ should be at the top of your list.

It's Saturday night, the seventeen of us went to Bubo for after dinner drinks.  Loving it here so, we stayed till the wee hours of the morning.Sophisticated is the interior of this bar at Murray Hill. Creative are their cocktails.  Attentive is the service. Cozy is their "library" semi-private room.At this writing, I cannot attest to their food. Instead, I will treasure this gem of memorable sweet sips with my peeps of then and for years to come.CHEERS!

This pizza spot was only a block away from my hotel and after a week of walking by multiple times smelling the delicious pizza, I finally decided to go get a slice for dinner tonight! Super quick/efficient. Lots of choices/topping variations. It's an indoor/outdoor corner walk-up style spot. I got a veggie slice for $3 and it was perfect for dinner (I don't think you'll need 2 slices unless you're starving). There are also cheaper slices for less toppings.Veggie $3 slices came with broccoli, red pepper, mushrooms, cheese, olives, etc. I'll definitely go back if I'm passing by and hungry in the future! I'd like to check it out when it's not rush hour to see if they have any seating in the back or where they're hiding the Parmesan / red pepper flakes

We recently dined at a restaurant where the wait was thankfully short. The ambiance was pleasant, albeit unremarkable. Our meal consisted of a 6-Hand Roll set and salmon sashimi, which left us content but not particularly impressed. We appreciated that the gratuity was included in the price, eliminating the need for additional tips. A standout feature, surprisingly, was the well-designed bathroom which offered two types of soap: unscented for before eating and scented for afterwards – a thoughtful touch that didn’t go unnoticed. It's often the small details that enhance the dining experience.

**Title: A Culinary Adventure at Gotham**

**Rating: 4/5**

Last month's visit to Gotham, a one Michelin-starred establishment that recently underwent a chef change and was lauded with a three-star New York Times review by Pete Wells, proved to be a gastronomic delight. Opting for the a la carte menu, my group and I sampled a broad range of offerings.

**Appetizers:**
- **Terrine (3/5):** A meaty starter with a predominantly ham hock composition. Accompanied by toasted whole wheat sourdough bread, it unfortunately erred on the dry side and felt a tad heavy for an appetizer.
- **Scallops (5/5):** A new addition to the menu, the scallops, and uni were the stars of the evening—light and exquisitely delicate.
- **Beef Tartare (5/5):** The highlight among starters, boasting a tender texture that could rival fine sashimi. The prawn crackers, though slightly oily, didn't detract from the overall finesse of the dish.

**Entrees:**
- **Lamb Shoulder (4/5):** Served with tomato sauce and vegetables, this might be the best lamb I've experienced, with a flawless preparation that only stumbled with a sliver of pure fat.
- **Braised Rabbit Leg:** Although I didn't try this dish myself, it came highly recommended by my peers.
- **Spaghetti Neri (3/5):** Despite perfectly cooked octopus and an al dente texture, this squid ink pasta fell into the category of being just standard fare.

**Desserts:**
- **Dark Chocolate with Hojicha Ice Cream (4/5):** The balance skewed towards a more robust chocolate presence, which was finely cut by the hojicha. Ideal for those who revel in the intensity of dark chocolate.
- **Pear Soufflé with Yogurt Ice Cream (3/5):** Overpoweringly tart and sweet, yet the texture was a marvel of culinary finesse.
- **Hazelnut Ice Cream (3/5):** A familiar flavor that failed to impress my table.

The restaurant sports a very traditional interior, complete with cream-colored bedsheet-like drapery. While the atmosphere leans towards a more conventional clientele, the culinary expressions are anything but dated. An additional quirky note: each bathroom stall houses a sink, which struck me as unusual.

Gotham stands out

During my recent visit to the restaurant, I found that the seafood clearly stood out, while the accompaniments left much to be desired. The fried shrimp was a highlight, showcasing a succulent taste with a perfect breadcrumb coating and fry. In stark contrast, the onion rings were disappointingly reminiscent of a fast food experience, coming across as a pre-packaged afterthought rather than freshly prepared.

The service, however, was commendable, with a highly attentive staff ensuring a continual flow of water and readily available condiments, like mustard, which is a nice touch.

I also had the opportunity to sample the fried tuna, which did not disappoint and lived up to the standard set by the shrimp.

I would consider dining here again for the seafood alone, but would certainly steer clear of the onion rings next time.

When you walk cross the gangplank, you're in for a treatJust be sure to keep stable and sturdy on feetThe cocktails are tasty and chock full of colorDrink em through metal straws, some sweeter, some duller But the food is the headliner, select your choice well!Or just share with your friends! I swear I won't tell. The French toast, on raisin bread, is crisp and delicious And the blueberry topping.... is also delicious Avocado toast is surely not to be missedWith a poached egg atop, you'll be super-a-blissed!Go to pilot! It's a boat with oh-so-good eatsIt is wickeds. And awesomes. And tasties. And neats!

Came here for brunch! Very tight space with rickety everythingTried:- brioche french toast 7/10: nothing too special, the bread was really soft, almost doughy. Generous amount of nutella on top and your standard fruits (strawberry, blueberry, bananas)- brussel sprouts 9/10: i like my brussel sprouts really crispy on the outside and this was exactly that! Some sort of peanuts (?) sprinkled on top & was a tad too salty- eggs scandinavian 7/10: was pretty badic, the bread was a little softer than im used to. The smoked salmon wasn't very "smoky". It was just averageThree stars bc everything was just average, nothing i'd want to come back for. Maybe their dinner menus is different?

This is a long overdue review. We discovered this place 3 years ago and haven't been back until yesterday. They changed the whole staffs and they are very accommodating. The thing we learned from this Izakaya is GET THE CABBAGE! Yes it is addictive and yes you will want to order more than one!! The point of this tiny tiny hole in a wall restaurant is to drink. They offer a variety of sakes and beers. Their food is supposed to be tapas like and small dishes. It's more like they serve snacks to go with your huge bottle of sakes. This place is definitely a fun place to visit. We ordered the cabbage, agedashi tofu, croquettes, and fried chicken nanban to start. The cabbage is marinated in salt, sesame oil, seaweed, and sesame seeds. It was just so delicious that you're willing to pay 6 dollars for some pieces of cabbage! The croquettes are made of potatoes and corn served with spicy mayo. The agedashi tofu was perfectly made. The chicken omg the chicken!!! It's probably one of the best fried chicken very juicy and delicious! For the main course we had the clams ramen, the curry and the sukiyaki. The curry used to be way better with rice served separately but now they put the curry on top of rice in a clay pot and added cheese to it. We didn't like it as much. The clams ramen is amazing. It reminded me of spaghetti vongole but with a twist of saffron and chili peppers in it. It was delicious! The sukiyaki was also amazing. We really enjoyed the food here!!

Beautiful ambiance, great location close to Flatiron and Union Square and excellent service. Food was good, but nothing extraordinary. I have been to many Thai places in Manhattan, and found Thai Villa's food good in comparison. We had Thai iced tea to drink, curry puffs ($10) and steamed dumplings ($10) to start, and the royal pad Thai ($21) and pad see ew as the main course. Both appetizers were good. The royal pad Thai had a wonderful presentation and the noodles were really good; however, the shrimp in the pad Thai were a little tasteless. The pad see ew was probably the best out of what we ordered. Overall good experience, very attentive and great service, and fair prices for Thai in New York City.

1. I should have my Bronx Card revoked because it took me 41 years to have Mofongo. 2. I'm kicking my own ass because some damn good Mofongo is just blocks away from me. I'm an idiot. Don't be like me. If you like porky goodness, get you some Mofongo De Chicharron De Cerdo, stat! So good. And such a big serving I had some for the next day when it tastes even better. Or you can be a savage like my friend and eat it with no utensils in your hotel room. No names because I'm discreet like that. Like with most Spanish food I've had, it comes with a side salad that gives you the barest ability to say you ate something green. It also comes with 2 nuggets of even more pork on the side. From what I'm to understand, the sauce is key and this one is proper and plentiful. The place has a diner look and feel. They do breakfast as well. Nothing fancy. But I never care about the decor when the food has my entire attention. Our server was friendly and our food came out quickly. I posted about losing my mofongo virginity on all my social media. Yup. I'm an idiot. But I'm a mofongo eating idiot!

Title: A Delightful Vegetarian Fine Dining Experience

My recent visit to this restaurant was nothing short of amazing! The fine dining ambiance set the stage for a memorable evening. The Mushroom Crepe and Seitan Picatta I ordered were delectable, with portions generous enough to satisfy even non-vegetarians.

The staff's hospitality enhanced the experience; servers were courteous while the bartender added a personal touch, engaging us in conversation and adeptly guiding us through the menu. Despite a slip on our part by not making a reservation, the attentive service staff swiftly accommodated us at a comfortable table.

Overall, the combination of sumptuous food, congenial service, and a welcoming atmosphere ensures my return to this gem of a restaurant. Just a friendly reminder to future patrons: reservations are a must to secure your spot in this culinary haven!

Came here on a chilly, busy Friday night. Place was packed as expected but many other places were full so it seems you can count on the place because of capacity? Overall the food was alright but overpriced.Let's start with the fried asparagus. I believe we got 5. This is when appetizers become a pet peeve. $10 is a bit much for what it is, but NYC. Why give an odd number if the appetizer is meant to be shareable? The next app was the Nacho Belly - pork belly, soy bean paste, tortilla chips and some other things that were pretty much garnish. Better than the asparagus and a more fair price, still I wasn't overly impressed but nice presentation. Again questionable share-ability if more than two people.My main entrée were the NY Bites. Strange name compared to some of the other offerings. Not bad. I don't get the hub bub with everything being truffled though. The entrée was very meaty and I didn't feel cheated here so this gets a thumbs up. Had cocktail which also was pretty good, but more impressed with presentation than the drink.Overall though with high NYC prices for just passable entrees makes feel like I'm playing tourist coming to a place like this. I'm sure there are more fitting Korean spots. I'd probably come back for the same circumstances - other venues full, out with friends and I'm real hungry but that's about it.

Like a not so very smart person, I ordered the pork slouvaki platter rather than the pork gyro player that I had had my eyes on. But no biggie because the pork was absolutely fantastic!! So flavorful!I got it with brown rice which was unfortunately very basic with minimal flavor and. The pita bread was absurdly delicious and dipped in the taziki, yum! Will get the gyro platter next time!!

I came in to get 1/4 of a chicken so I could shred the meat for my dogs food. I am in the area on weekends only and forgot my spoiled dogs food. Well, the place is not very appealing, and staff speaks limited English, but they are very friendly. This was my third visit here over the past year to get the chicken, and my next visit will be to get food for me not Chichi. While waiting I can't help but notice how nicely the meals are plated and look so yummy. I can't wait to try for myself, so next weekend I will post an update.

Title: A Cozy Spot for Brunch and Mimosas with a Caveat

I recently visited a brunch spot renowned for its bottomless mimosas and I have to say, it's quite decent. If you're planning to go, either arrive early or book ahead to avoid the inevitable wait. The cozy size of the restaurant doesn't lend itself well to large parties, but if the weather permits, their outdoor seating is a delightful option.

The mimosas pack a punch, though you might have to be a little proactive to get refills due to the infrequent table visits from the staff. Speaking of service, don't expect frequent check-ins – the place is bustling, which can spread the staff thin.

On the flip side, the food selection is impressive and satisfying, adding to the charm of this establishment. And if you're a chai latte aficionado, theirs is a must-try. Despite the drawbacks, the experience is generally pleasant, especially if you're willing to assert a little to get your glass topped up.

Two stars is for the friendly service,outside of that..I think my fellow Yelpers hit the nail on the head with the so/so reviews.My friend had gotten great news at the hospital around the block and we wanted to grab a bite before the ride home.When we arrived there was a line and it moved rather quickly,plus the cashier was very polite.We seated oursekves and waited for our food.The cranberry surprise which we were told had pineapple snd another special ingredient that I couldn't taste nor can I recall was okay(make it more like a compote..surprise!).The sweet potatoes were very loose and had strings,not such good flavor either.The potato salad,the tatoes were cubed way too large and it was a rather bland side.I am not a fan of bbq beans but I do cook them and my friend said they tasted straight out the can. The green beans almondine were okay..As for the sliced brisket(check out the pics) we were straight annoyed: no smoke ring no flavor just sad and steamed looking.The broasted chicken breast was very tasty and cooked well..how the wing had ping meat,do not ask me and I was too dissapointed with my meal to complain.Cornbread muffin..I passed to my friend and didn't ask,they looked nice.The prices were fair for the area and that is about it.I wouldn't turn down that breast but I also would not go out of my way..

Ok, dumpling fix is satisfied. Went with braised pork meatballs noodle soup (yey, didn't need the assorted vegetables which resembled something from a microwave bag). Noodles were great, and broth was delivered in a plastic bag wrapped around a plastic container. Pan fried baos were great too, kinda doughy, would have liked some more pan fry on them, but all good, and I'm not the connoisseur.  The soup dumplings were really good, and I'm still picking on the leftovers I ordered too much of. Used door dash, ordered as quoted and the food traveled well across town. The place is just shy of four stars, accurately rated here on yelp.

Let me start that I've never get to sit down and have a real dinner in this place , so I cannon judge that par. But I love happy hours here ! I've been here 2 times and never got disappointed. They offer 1/2 price on a draft beer and have super delicious fried oysters 1 $ apiece, 1$ shrimp and a bunch of other finger food for a very reasonable price.  Definitely, one back, here again, not only because of the convenient location closed to my work but also because they have a good selection of draft beer and great happy hour specials

Tucked away near my workplace, the bar-style eatery proved convenient for our office holiday party and a recent coworker's farewell gathering. The menu, while somewhat uninspiring and pricey, does feature a standout crab and rock shrimp burger priced at $18—worth every penny and served with satisfying cut fries. Despite a slightly chilly interior, the hearty burger provided ample warmth. Ideal for happy hour, it's a spot I'd recommend for a casual drink rather than a full dining experience, but make sure to try the burger if you're in for a bite.

This place intrigued me when it opened but I didn't quite understand what it was until I came.  It's essentially hot pot - without the pot and cooking it yourself.ATMOSPHERE: Came on a Saturday night around 6:30 pm and there was no one inside.  The inside is a bit small with only 4 tables that fit 2 and then a counter that probably fits 4-5 people.  They have hooks for jackets and you see them cooking.  You will also slightly smell of hot pot when you come out because of the cooking that is done in there.FOOD: It's a build your own bowl type of place but if you check in on yelp or follow them on instagram you get free noodles, which is like a $2.50 benefit! On the sheet of paper you mark what you want in your bowl.  Don't be fooled because the way I quickly read it meant that you get 2 meats, 2 veggies and 1 noodle base.  However, each item costs money so if you prefer all veggies or all meat with no noodles you can modify it however you want.  I believe the meats were $3.50 each and the veggies, noodles etc. were $2.50 each.  If you get the 2, 2, and 1 with the check in combo it's about $12.  They basically put everything into one big pot and cook it for you and then serve it in a bowl with a bit of the soup at the bottom (but it's not soupy).  MEAT - The sliced beef is like the thinly sliced meat you would get at a hot pot place which I liked the best.  The pork belly was tasty with a good amount of fat but the meat itself is a bit tough.  VEGGIES - napa cabbage is always a good option and the broccoli was also pretty good.  Next time I would get mushrooms.NOODLES - my husband got the prince noodle and I got the thick glass noodle. The thick glass noodle is like the potato noodle you get at hot pot places. Very chewy and delicious! They give you a healthy portion.  The prince noodles are like these flour, thin noodles that had a good chew to them.SAUCE - you don't really need sauce but if you want it there is a sauce making station with homemade soy sauce, garlic, chili and cilantro.One complaint is it's a bit hard to eat because it's mostly noodles on the bottom and then the meat and veggies sort of in layers but because the bowl (it's more of a long cup) is narrow it's hard to mix everything. Overall though, I loved the concept of it being like hot pot but without you having to cook and fish for things and everything tasted good!

Absolutely delicious. I loved that they had so many locations across the city. We ended going to the closest one to our hotel and grabbed dinner there. We didn't realize how big the portions were before we ordered so we weren't able to finish everything. The service was quick and for each order you place you get one free tea. Everything we ordered was so good. My favorite thing had to be the lamb dumplings. This is now on my must visit list for food when I go back to New york.

Title: A Satisfying Soba Fix at Soba Azuma

My brother and I stumbled upon Soba Azuma in midtown on a Saturday, looking to satiate a soba craving. The seating was abundant, with immediate accommodation upon arrival—a contrast, I'd guess, to the weekday bustle.

Our appetizer, the karaage, was a pleasing start despite my tongue's hasty encounter with its heat. While the chicken could've boasted a crisper skin, the underlying salad and a spritz of lemon lifted the dish to a commendable starter.

The soba experience itself was a tale of two parts: the Ten Sashi Gozen platter, an array of soba, tempura, sashimi, and rice, was paired with an additional order of plain soba to ensure sufficient sustenance. The platter's components, especially the fresh sashimi and crispy tempura, were well-executed, yet lacked a distinctive flair that would etch the meal into memory. The soba's lightness was its triumph, with condiments like radish, wasabi, and scallions enhancing the noodle's subtle charm.

A unique aspect of Soba Azuma is the customizable portion control, offering soba sizes from 100g to 300g at a uniform price—ideal for tailoring your meal to your appetite.

In sum, while Soba Azuma may not dazzle the palate with surprises, it offers a solid and satisfying soba experience, perfect for a light, refreshing meal that leaves you contentedly full.
A quick bite to eat before going to the movies. I had the Tontoro within amazingly creamy broth. So good.

Good food and good vibes. I needed dinner before getting on the bus back to Philadelphia. The good ole Yelp app steered me in the right direction. Yep right across the street from The Lincoln Center after a ballet performance. I quickly made a reservation 10 minutes later I was pleasantly greeted then off to my seat immediately. Then I was given a big hello by the wonderful Lindsey! She was a ball of energy. very pleasant and highly efficient! Before placing my order Lindsey went over drink favorites and dinner specials. I went with sea bass and it was DELICIOUS!! Smok'em if you got 'em was my cocktail choice and a good one at that it helped to calm the chill I had from the night rain.The decor reminded me of a French style cafe with an American flair. The only negative although this is NYC the dinner options were pricey for the portions. But I found the staff very helpful and timely. Because the restaurant, food and staff was memorable I will return.

Went here for a company event at the outside garden. Summer is over but it's hot af. The garden was buried between all the tall buildings so no breeze/cool air whatsoever. I'm wearing a blazer and it was unbearable. My friend was literally dripping. I'm not sure about the price because it was on the party host's tab but looking at the 4 dollar signs on yelp, I'm pretty sure it's waaaaaay over priced because I had a cocktail with full glass of ice. It taste nothing like an alcoholic drink and my friend said his drink need 3x the lime to makeup for the taste. The food was served by the server on a tray in a finger food form. It was nothing special. Just fried egg roll and dumplings that I can get same if not better quality in some cheap Chinatown bakery. The one dish that caught my eyes was the chicken wings. It looks like those salt and pepper fried drums but it's full of chilly so I wasn't dare to try. Plus it was a professional event, I don't feel comfortable eating wings, especially it's so hot and crowded and we were all standing awkwardly. Other then those I've mentioned, the staff was really nice. The servers are sweating more than us but they had to put up with the crowd and squeeze between us so everyone get food. The bartender was nice, he never ignore me. He listened to my order and prepared it very promptly.

Finally had a chance to come here!! Highly recommend making a reservation, especially if youre coming during weekend brunch hours. We tried:- bloody mary (8/10): was ok, i personally would have preferred more tomato and less spicy- farmhouse popover (10/10): this was excellent!!!!! The eggs were so fluffy and delightful and paired perfectly with the bread. The salad was also very fresh and refreshing- mushroom omelette (7/10): it was a pretty standard omelette, nothing fancy or special aka worth $20. The potatoes that came with were also average- brussel sprouts (9/10): very crispy and very delicious, not too oily

Title: A Tasty Bite at the Hartford Riverfront Truck Festival

At the bustling 2019 Hartford Riverfront Truck Festival, one truck stood out from the rest with a constant crowd gathered around. Curiosity piqued, I decided to see what the fuss was about. The menu was straightforward, offering both Maine and Connecticut-style lobster rolls. Being a fan of buttery goodness, I opted for the Connecticut roll, even treating myself to extra meat.

The lobster meat was succulent and flavorful, a real highlight of the meal. However, it's worth noting that the portions seemed a bit modest, even with the extra serving. To pair with the roll, I scooped up some clam chowder, which was quite satisfying. The only slight disappointment came from the accompanying crackers, which had lost their crunch to sogginess.

Despite the minor setbacks, the truck delivered a memorable lobster roll that lived up to its reputation. Worth a stop if you're in the mood for some classic New England fare on the go!

Title: A Satisfying Evening at Vietnaam

I can never resist pronouncing "Vietnaam" with an exaggerated drawl, and my recent visit on a bustling Saturday night did not disappoint. Despite the 7:30 PM crowd, our party of four was quickly seated within five minutes—though a reservation is recommended.

We indulged in a feast for the senses, starting with a vegetarian papaya salad, a crunchy symphony of flavors with its peanut and taro toppings. The grilled chicken summer rolls were a fresh delight, especially when swirled in the zesty nuoc-cham sauce.

The star of the evening was the spicy pho, a warming embrace on a chilly night. With pink slices of beef transforming in the hot broth, it was both a visual and gustatory delight that outshone the other noodle dishes we sampled.

On a whim, we tried the basil eggplant, which proved to be a tender and aromatic vegetarian surprise. Service was impeccable amidst the full house, with attentive water refills and expedited bill handling upon request.

Vietnaam certainly earned its stripes in the Upper East Side for a return visit.

Fantastic brunch spot. Picked this place last minute for brunch with a group of friends. From the start our waiter was super friendly and energetic. We requested to have seating in the back because we felt a bit more cozier and he accommodated us no problem. Cocktails to start were GREAT! The "do it for the gram" was such a treat- tasty and playful yet very strong. It smelled like pine which I really don't know how they pulled off. Food was soo good! I came in with the dilemma of not knowing whether to pick savory or sweet, and ironically enough the special was chicken and waffles with a maple glaze. I got hollandaise sauce to put on top because I'm weird, but it was fantastic! I would highly recommend this place for brunch in midtown. Will definitely be back!

It's a cute food hall but kind of overpriced. I left hungry. [CONEY SHACK]I got the short rib hotdog - the flavors were good but it was REALLY messy so make sure to grab a fork/spoon, and a ton of napkins in advance. It wasn't the flavor I was personally expecting, but still good. I paid about $14 for the hotdog that didn't really even fill me up which annoyed me. My friend got one of their roti wraps which was maybe $12? and it looked like the $1 quesadilla from taco bell - it was pathetically small. Decent tasting but very small. Seating is kind of nice and open but also a bit awkward. Hoping to come back soon to try more and take it to go.

I ordered from here once weekend evening, after a long bout of studying. I was in the mood for Mexican food, and I wanted to try out a new place. Burritos y Mas showed up on my UberEats app, so I decided to order from here.I ordered a beef burrito on a wheat tortilla. After waiting 30 minutes for the delivery guy, I was ready to devour my food.The burrito was not as great as I expected. The beef portions were lacking, and the quality of beef was mediocre. The put way too much sour cream, in spite of me requesting less of it. I was not impressed by this place. Maybe that was just a bad first impression. But first impressions matter a lot. I will not be ordering from here anymore, but I hope they do improve their meal prep.

I went here for brunch with two of my friends on a cold winter's Sunday at noon and we were luckily able to be seated immediately at the bar. We ordered the hummus, shoo shoo breakfast, smoothie bowl, and shoo shoo burger. While our server was very nice, it took nearly 40 minutes from ordering for our main dishes to come out. The server noticed at 25 minutes that we had been sitting there for a while without our food, and we started to notice that people who had come way after us were getting their dishes even though we had not gotten ours yet. As we had done a workout class before, we were ravenous, and were eating the hummus without pita bread as we were only served one for the group. The waiter asked us if we wanted more, and we obliged. When we finally got our meals, we did not receive an apology for the long wait time. My  Israeli breakfast was ok but nothing special and as I had filled up with bread and hummus by the time it was served, I wasn't able to finish it.To add insult to injury, we were charged for the extra pita bread the waiter had brought out for us because we had been waiting so long. I feel this should have been waived as we had been sitting there so long without food. It's only 1 dollar but still! The food certainly wasn't bad but I don't think I would be back after this experience. It's a shame, because it has a very cute vibe and I had been looking forward to coming here.

So this place lets you pick your steak cut, how much you want and how you want it cooked all to order! They also have wagyu cuts! It was so delicious! I think also considering the quality the prices are fair!

Really great udon!Kani Salad- This was a sad, yet tasty salad. It was mostly leafy salad with a very small amount of kani. Pretty disappointing, especially for the price. ($16)Chicken Tatsuta-age- Good, but not great. (10 for $12)Nabeyaki- I wasn't expecting such a generous portion, it was huge and super filling. The consistency of the udon and taste of the soup base were perfect. What really stole the show was the shiitake mushroom in the soup. I've never had such flavorful mushroom in my life, words can't describe how delicious it was! I wasn't too fond of the chicken, and the shrimp tempura contained such small shrimp, but everything else was amazing. ($25)I would definitely recommend any hot udon and shiitake mushroom. You won't be disappointed!

Title: Disappointing Experience at Indikitch/Deep

I revisited Indikitch/Deep recently after a lackluster first impression a few years back, hoping for improvement based on friends' recommendations. Regrettably, my experience was still subpar.

I ordered Paneer Kati Rolls sans onions for pickup; the 20-minute wait coincided with my arrival. The dimly lit interior and awkward service at the counter—waiting awkwardly while my food sat in sight—set a negative tone.

The kati rolls themselves were a letdown: soggy, improperly wrapped, and mistakenly included onions despite my clear instructions. The thick, naan-like paratha lacked the tidy, convenient structure of a traditional kati roll, transforming what should have been a simple meal into an untidy affair.

On a positive note, the accompanying raita was satisfactory, and the portion size was generous. However, the unpleasant service, the disregard for my dietary preference, and the ensuing digestive discomfort lead me to advise against dining here—unless a side of raita is all you seek. Overall, I rate Indikitch/Deep 2 stars, mostly for mismanaging a staple dish and poor customer service.

The sleek and modernly decorated Hakkasan features a menu jam packed with awesome dim sum choices and other Cantonese traditional dishes. Originally I was going to feature their perfectly crispy and seasoned Peking Duck dish but I'm not sure if it'll be featured on their Restaurant Week 2019 menu so instead I'll highlight their amazing "Hakka Steamed Dim Sum Platter" which is always on their Restaurant Week menu. There truly aren't enough words to describe how beautifully prepared every dish is and also how artsy and aesthically pleasing they are. Highly recommend making a reservation to take advantage of the minimal cost for such a decadent meal.

Celebrating my aunt's birthday, we decided to escape to the nearby Cuban-Asian fusion oasis, Calle Dao (Chelsea), for a relaxed 1pm lunch. Having experienced its Bryant Park sibling a couple of years back, I was eager to compare. This venue exudes a distinct, easygoing ambiance that felt perfectly welcoming.

The lunch menu, while different from the evening offerings, maintains comparable pricing with surprisingly generous portions. My beef and broccoli - reimagined with a ramen twist - was a culinary highlight I'd readily return for.

The happy hour drinks beckon early, and my subtly sweet mojito proved a delightful lunchtime indulgence. The decor transported me straight to Havana's heart from the cigars at the reception to the Cuban beats and nostalgic interiors.

Staff, from the hostess to our waiter, added a personalized touch to our meal. Without fanfare, they treated my aunt to a slice of tres leches, a sweet birthday gesture attuned to our desire for subtlety.

Charmed by the atmosphere, the hearty meals, and the staff's kindness, I look forward to a dinner return - and yes, for more mojitos.

Yes you need to know someone to even get into here.  It also looks abandoned, especially at night.   Luckily I had a friend in NYC with some clout.  :)But honestly, it's an interesting approach to owning a restaurant, almost like some kind of secret club you need to be part of.  It certainly drives interest, as I notice other people asking for referrals just to dine here.The inside is quaint and looks more like a living room with a bar in it.  It's not quite a comfortable living room where you kick off your shoes and watch the game while sinking into a couch, eating buffalo wings.  It's the kind of living room where you're at your boss's house and you're worried about your posture or spilling wine on the sofa, and you sit almost in a pose you can stand for a prolonged period.PROS:   The food was really good.  The poke bowl was perhaps my favorite, followed by the sliders.  I was least excited about the sliders having read a review where they were dry...BUT, mine came medium-rare and I could have eaten 4 of them by myself.  You must get them!  Order 2 orders and get 4.  I would!  :)The assorted sushi was so good, but at $40 for 6 pieces, it seemed a little high.  Figure that's $20 per person for 3 pieces.  I ended up at a nice sushi tasting place for $58 the next day, and it was 12 courses.   So although the 3 pieces were good, not worth the price for me.I found the raw beef ok, and the desserts were maybe a 3 star affair at best.Cocktails were on point, with the bartender muddling fresh fruit and mint.  Waitress as welcoming and helpful.  I think her suggestion of 4-5 dishes for 2 people was spot on.  Although there were 3 'large' dishes on the menu, which I avoided, but ask them, because it sounded like you only needed 1 of those per person.CONS:   The price was a bit high, but you're paying for the exclusive, small feel of this place.   OVERALL:  It's probably 4.5 stars, so it's worth investigating.  I'd suggest the sliders and poke for sure.

Small spot but good spot for soup dumplings. 6 in an order and I always get the pork one along with a crabmeat one. They also have truffle soup dumplings here if you wanted to enhance the taste which I like but it's a once in a whileeeee thing. I love the kau fu which is basically a cold dish that tastes like spongy mushroom without the fungi taste. The wine chicken is really good too and it's also a cold appetizer. Not much meat. I also got the beef slice scallion pancake which is a must get here! Crunchy scallion pancake with hoisin sauce inside along with cucumbers and beef. Yummy!! The soup dumplings were pretty good here except the skin was like stuck to the wrapping paper or stuck to another soup dumpling buddy so I had 2 dumplings that ended up with a stab wound leaking out the precious soup dumpling broth essence. Also the only credit card they take is AMEX but they take cash too.

Absolutely delighted with my dining experience! The karaage chicken was the star of the show – the crispiest, most tender, and juiciest I've ever had the pleasure of tasting. A solid 10/10 for Yum Yum Yum – I'm already planning my next visit to sample more delights!

Of course we came for the burger as almost every patron does. Stopped by around 530pm on a weeknight and we were seated immediately. We ordered a burger (medium rare) for each of us and it took a while for it to come out. Luckily we weren't super hungry and it gave us time to catch up. Burger is super tender and topped off with blue cheese. That's it. I'm a lover of all cheeses so it worked for me. I also love my salt, but this burger definitely went a tiny bit overboard on my standards. Just be warned if you have high blood pressure. The shoestring fries are also great. They give you a mountain of it. Wasn't quite sure if I should eat it a few strands at a time or shovel it in my mouth with a fork. Seating is a bit tight so come early to enjoy the space before it fills up.

In the Chelsea area, at the late lunch hour, stumbled onto Jun-Men and discovered an excellent lunch spot.Stepped inside this small Ramen Bar and we were greeted and immediately seated. Water was brought and I ordered a Junmai sake.Started with an order of the Chicken Wings.4 pieces of double fried chicken wings glazed with jun-men sauce. Excellent. Wings were salty & crispy, but that glaze added sweetness. Jun-Men Fried Rice. Chinese sausage, kimchi, fried egg, tobiko, micro basil. I loved this fried rice. Inhaled.Pork Bone Ramen.Chashu, kikurage, menma, egg, scallion, black oil.I was a fan of the Ramen, too! Alternating bites between the fried rice and ramen.Service was friendly and efficient. Food exceeded my expectations and wish I could have ordered more food, but alas, was too full.

I recently dined at this lovely upscale diner for lunch, and it was an absolutely fantastic choice. The servers were the epitome of courtesy, attentive and efficient, making sure my dining experience was nothing short of delightful. Their handling of various customer personalities was impressive – they truly deserve a raise for their exceptional service!

As for the meal, the shrimp wrap was simply scrumptious and exactly what I needed to hit the spot. The consistent check-ins from the staff were much appreciated, ensuring a seamless meal from start to finish.

This place is a must-visit for anyone in the area, and I'm definitely planning to return on my next visit. A round of applause to the management for maintaining such high standards in both cuisine and service!

I recently visited a highly talked-about pizza spot that turned out to be a disappointment. Branded as a must-visit eatery, it felt more like a tourist trap. After enduring a lengthy wait, my anticipation for a remarkable slice was met with a reality that fell short of the hype. The pizza was unbearably oily; so much so that the grease soaked through the plate and several napkins, which was simply unappetizing. It's one thing to expect a bit of oil on a pizza, but another to see it pouring off the slice upon lifting it. My advice? Skip the lines at this overrated place and find somewhere less tourist-centric for a better pizza experience.

Title: Cozy Spot with Quick Service and Tasty Eats

My friends and I had a solid dining experience at this restaurant last night. Despite the weekend rush, the seating was prompt, although be mindful that the layout includes communal tables which means you may share your dining space with others.

The service was speedy, and the food didn't disappoint. The pork soup dumplings were the star of the evening, receiving high praise from my companions. The scallion pancakes are also a must-try. As a vegetarian, the options were limited; however, the staff was accommodating, customizing the Singapore chow mei fun with egg and veggies for me, and it was delicious.

Whether you're considering dining in or taking out, this restaurant is definitely worth a visit.

Title: A Fusion Delight Outshining a Michelin Star

If you're tired of the usual brunch monotony, this Indian fusion eatery is a breath of fresh culinary air. Known for its creative take on Indian cuisine, the restaurant offers a plethora of tasteful vegetarian and pescatarian options, perfect for the health-conscious foodies or those simply seeking variety.

Portion sizes are generous, making the dishes ideal for sharing among a group of 4-5 people. The ambiance strikes a balance between trendy and cozy, complemented by attentive service that enhances the dining experience.

During my visit for brunch, I was pleasantly surprised to find no waiting lines, which is quite the rarity compared to other city spots. Opting for their prix fixe menu was a solid choice, allowing us to sample a broader range of flavors. Each dish was not only delicious and unique but also a feast for the eyes with its beautiful presentation. 

The only minor drawback was the small serving size of the chai and coffee. Also, the rice noodles dessert fell a tad short of the otherwise high bar set by the rest of the meal. Despite this, the cocktail selection caught my eye and is something I'm looking forward to trying on a future visit.

Price-wise, the restaurant is unexpectedly reasonable, especially given the quality on offer. While this spot's performance has outshined the Michelin-starred Junoon in my books, it remains a hidden gem awaiting discovery by more discerning diners.

I'm keen on returning for brunch, and possibly dinner, to explore what other delectable dishes they have in store.

Title: A Worthwhile Walk for a Whopping Sandwich

Upon the recommendation of a colleague, I ventured to this local spot and was not disappointed. Opting for 'The Palermo' on sfilatino bread—a hearty assembly of sopressata, creamy fresh mozzarella, zesty hot peppers, and crisp arugula, enhanced with a drizzle of truffle oil—proved a wise choice. At over $16, it's a splurge for a sandwich, but justified by its impressive size; it's so large that half is enough to satisfy, leaving the rest for another meal.

The flavors were robust and well-balanced, from the truffle's aromatic allure to the arugula's fresh bite and the sopressata's peppery kick. This place is a gem for those seeking a genuine taste of Italy packed between slices of bread. If you're an enthusiast of Italian cuisine and generous portions, add this spot to your must-visit list.

I enjoyed The Smith. The food was good, it is a basic enough menu that everyone can find something they'd like, they were able to accommodate my party of 6 (we made reservations a few days in advanced of course). It just wasn't very special. My food was good, eggs and toast a little over done but still fine, but for $33 (that was for an entree and an iced coffee) I would want it to really stick out. It did not. Not a bad experience for sure, but not one I would actively push for again when there are so many unique options in New York.

Ordered the lamb kebab pita which came with in house made potato chips! If you don't mind gamey meat, I would recommend it. The pita was delicious, soft yet dense enough to hold everything. It came with two large lamb kebab balls, tons of chopped tomatoes and salad, tahini and grilled creamy eggplant. I loved that you could actually taste the eggplant among all the other delicious herbs and flavors.  The whole meal was satisfying and filling. Great casual lunch spot!

Title: A Taste of Hong Kong in the Heart of the City

If you're seeking an authentic Hong Kong culinary experience, this no-frills spot delivers with gusto. Upon being served a steaming hot cup of Hong Kong milk tea, I was instantly transported to the vibrant streets of HK. This isn't your typical upscale eatery; think of it more like a lively cafeteria buzzing with unapologetic energy.

The setting is perfect for those who appreciate a bit of commotion. Conversing at increased volumes isn't just tolerated, it's practically the norm — a boon for my conversations with my hard-of-hearing father. The absence of decorum means there's no shushing here, as patrons chatter on FaceTime or catch up on TV shows openly.

Casual run-ins with friends and locals are common in this Chinatown gem — making it an ideal spot for some impromptu socializing over a delicious order of fishballs and that aromatic HK tea. While the clamor of to-go orders and loud exchanges with the chef may resonate with the essence of NYC, it adds to the charm rather than detracting.

That said, this isn't the retreat for quiet contemplation or working remotely. But for those who enjoy the city's din and yearn for a slice of Hong Kong life, this spot is a definite winner. I'm already looking forward to my next visit, with noodle dishes and breakfast combos on my must-try list.

Had the original plate and it was amazing! The soup looks plain but is incredibly flavorful. The three sauces were all great. I wish I could buy them. In order of taste - ginger/garlic sauce, the green cilantro sauce, and the dark soy sauce. Mix them all up. And go at it with the chicken and chicken riceZ best version of this I've had in a long time.

If you like spicy ramen, this is the place to go! They have a really spicy one. They have 2 options, an average spicy and then a really spicy one. I definitely was drinking my water for this meal. I enjoyed the kick as well as the broth. The ingredients were fresh and plenty of protein. The prices were also fair.I also ordered the pork buns and this is where it was a bit disappointing and why they do not get 5 stars. Their pork buns came out cold and their pork was not tender and very hard to bite into. It was also very bland and they didn't do much to elevate their dish. They charged a lot for this small app and I was super disappointed with the quality.Will be back for the spicy ramen, but not for the pork buns.

My group of eight visited the restaurant on a bustling Thursday evening and were met with pleasant service and satisfying dishes from appetizers through to desserts. While nothing on the menu particularly stood out, the generous portions provided a solid dining experience. This eatery is a commendable choice for a casual night out with friends.

Truly excellent Mediterranean (strong Greek/Israeli overtones) newly opened in TriBeCa. Food and service are excellent. Wonderful, house made mezze with other excellent apps. The drinks and service are great as well. The Israeli movie playing on the wall is a bit odd, but does not detract from the ambiance or the vibe. The Greek Mac 'n Cheese is awesome. The desserts are good as well. We will be back, often!

If you have the money to splurge then come here for the tasting menu. On my visit the place was packed so that tells you something. The food is really good. As with all high end restaurants the service is over the top. They take good care of you. They also have a seperate dining room which is less pricey and just as busy.

Every Seinfeld fan needs to eat here once of you're in NYC. Seinfeld memorabilia decorates the wall.  If you sit at the actual diner in corner you can take a selfie with Kramer  The staff attend well to the guests.  They serve typical American diner food that is average.  I ordered a pastrami sandwich that was a little disappointing because I paid just as much as I would have for a pastrami sandwich at the Sarge's etc. but there was very little pastrami on my sandwich. I give Tom's a four start rating for service but only three stars for their food and prices.
The crust is so thin that you literally roll it up. He ce, Rollio! :)We ordered the Big Bang, and the ItalianSausage Pick (i forgot the name)... both were very tasty and ingredients seem fresh!

I recently dined at a restaurant that boasted a stunningly simplistic and elegant ambiance, making it a perfect spot for a romantic date, a catch-up with a friend, or even a group outing. We indulged in two entrees and a small dish to share, which proved to be the right amount of food. The portions were generous, and each dish was bursting with flavor and interesting textures, satisfying our palates. While the drinks were somewhat overpriced and lacked originality, the culinary experience was not diminished. The food quality alone is a compelling reason to return, especially with the allure of an ever-changing menu. I'm eager to come back and explore more of what they have to offer.

Title: Upscale Family Dining with Room for Improvement

My family and I had the pleasure of dining at a local upscale restaurant renowned for its modern vibe and spacious setting. The ambiance certainly sets the stage for a delightful family gathering, with an atmosphere that buzzes with a subtle sophistication.

When it comes to the cuisine, the experience was pleasant, though not particularly extraordinary. The dishes were competently prepared, but none stood out as a signature item that would beckon a swift return. The food, while enjoyable, lacked that memorable punch that would elevate the dining experience from good to exceptional.

A word of caution for those with a sweet tooth: the Holy Cannoli may not be the divine dessert its name suggests. Despite its grandeur and steep price, it's an overwhelming concoction that could easily serve a small army with its overpowering sweetness. This dessert would be best shared among a large group, with most patrons likely to tap out after a few bites.

Regrettably, I missed the opportunity to try their hot chocolate dessert, which I suspect may have been more to my liking. In conclusion, while the restaurant is a solid choice for families looking to dine in a refined environment, there are areas, especially in the dessert section, where a recalibration of the sweetness scale could lead to sweeter success.

Man I love this bar! I came in to see some live music during the Christmas season and they have their cozy ambiance right. It was cold, windy, with that oh-so-fun "wintry mix" hitting me in the face as I walked along the hulking shadow of the Brooklyn Bridge. And shining in the night with a warm glow was Cowgirl Seahorse.You know that feeling of being well insulated from the whipping elements while you sit in a cozy place full of smiling people sharing the experience? It's special and it was exactly what I was looking for. My bartender Gail is a lovely person who took care of me all night and she chatted with me whenever she could in-between slinging drinks. They do live music weekly so it's worth checking out. The food was just OK - it's perfect for munching on something at the bar. There seems to be a few nods to New Orleans cuisine - po boys and such. I ordered the deviled eggs which I thought needed more mayo and come with some odd slices of lemon and lime, and the shrimp basket with fries. Fries were perfect, salty and crispy. The batter on the shrimp kept falling off, but the shrimp themselves were solid. Clean bathrooms, friendly customers, unpretentious and welcoming. It's perfect.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at Hula Poke

As a discerning and health-minded diner, I'm always on the lookout for food that meets my high standards. To my delight, Hula Poke has managed to exceed my expectations with their Samurai Poke. The combination of succulent salmon scoops perfectly paired with brown rice and crisp vegetables provided a satisfying and flavorful experience.
