The dressing was a revelation, adding a zesty kick to the dish. Hula Poke has earned a spot on my shortlist for when I crave a light yet delectable meal. Poke has certainly made a lasting impression, and I'm eager to return.

I ventured out to Spicy Village and it was well worth the journey. This cozy gem requires mingling at communal tables—a nod to its authentic hole-in-the-wall vibe. Aim for off-peak hours to avoid the bustling crowds.

The first visit introduced me to their beef brisket soup with yam noodles; a delightful dance of herbaceous flavors with perfectly chewy noodles. Though the beef leaned toward overcooked, the overall experience wasn't tarnished.

A return trip, this time with my sister, featured their big tray chicken—ample for two and satisfying, yet the spice level left something to be desired. As a note to self, I'll opt for an extra kick of heat on my next visit.

Spicy Village hits the mark when it comes to flavor. It's a definite go-to spot for those willing to venture off the beaten path for an authentic culinary experience.

Such a great restaurant with amazing food and service. My boyfriend kept commenting throughout our meal here how this was the best food we'd had in a long time. SETTING: came for a dinner reservation for two people on a Friday night for 8:45pm. When we arrived, the restaurant was busy with every table was taken. I live nearby and there always seems to be a crowd waiting outside.It's a beautiful & cozy restaurant with a bar in the front, smaller booths and tables towards the back and a second floor that looks out onto the first floor like a loft space / balcony. There are ~five or so tables up there, with doors opening out onto a patio space with more tables. The outdoor space was closed that night due to the weather). FOOD: the food was excellent. We ordered the Thai style mussels and French onion soup for our appetizers. The sauce they used for the mussels was incredible- creamy, rich, savory and the perfect amount of spice. Soaked our bread in it and basically lapped it up with a spoon. Delicious! The French onion soup was the best I've ever had. The broth was so perfectly savory with just the right amount of cheese / soaked bread. Would highly recommend, this is a must! For our entrees we ordered the special for the night, which was veal served with mashed potatoes. We also ordered the cheese ravioli. Again, for both dishes- we both agreed (1) best mashed potatoes we've ever had (2) best ravioli we've ever had. We don't say that easily.... which I think speaks to how amazing the food is here. Not exaggerating! The veal was also really delicious and fatty, perfectly cooked and seasoned. SERVICE: our waiter was really great and told us when we wanted to order another appetizer that we had gotten enough food. Thank god because it was a struggle towards the end to finish all that food. VERDICT: so happy to have found this place- it will be my l new favorite neighborhood spot for dinner. I will definitely be back and hope to become a regular here ! Highly recommend you this place, because you will be very happy!

Went here on a Saturday evening so I expected it to be busy! My friend's dad recommended it to us for trying New York style pizza. We checked in with the host and put our name on the list it was about a one hour wait. Which I expected being a weekend evening. After about an hour I got a text for our table. We were seated in the space near the restroom area. It was a quaint space with very nostalgic decor. We ordered a pizza (broccoli and mushroom), the vodka sauce penne, and eggplant parmigiana. The food was all pretty good and had good sized portions. Each dish ranged from i'd say $15-$30 depending on what you ordered. For me the pizza was not that great but I think it's because I would have preferred pepperoni or sausage on it. My friend is a vegetarian so we respected her by not getting any meat added to it. The penne was my favorite dish, the vodka sauce went well with it. The eggplant parmigiana was ok in my opinion. It was just very soggy and I expected it to be crispier. The food overall was pretty average but what really gave me a negative experience was the service. Our server was rude and not attentive at all. It took forever to place our order, get our food, and even ask for the check at the end. I understand it is a busy place and everything but he was clearly nicer to other tables. He also basically disappeared from existence and we had to try and flag down someone to pay our bill. Our server only took our ordered, served the food, and nothing else. The one thing that stood out to me was the way they sing Happy Birthday to the customers. I think it was super charming and definitely left everyone in a good mood to see the staff singing joyfully.

I'll start off by saying I don't even like Korean food, but Oiji changes the game. It's simply one of the few restaurants that has made me reconsider whether I like Korean food or not. I've basically tried everything on the menu based on the spring & summer menus since I went several times in 2019. They recommend about 2-3 small plates and 1 large plate per person. The menu is broken out with the left side being small plates and the large plates on the right side. My friend and I ordered 6 dishes each and ignored the portion recommendations since the menu itself is rather small. The only dishes that I didn't care for too much were the red snapper and the beef shank, everything else blew me away. I'm not going to talk about every dish in my review, just the ones that stood out even though I provided pictures of everything.Mushroom salad: is amazing with a variety of mushrooms, the flash-fried texture of the mushrooms even though they were not the least bit greasy was shocking yet delicious. They made it clear that the mushrooms were the star of the dish, the salad itself was as expected.Baby Octopus: was my favorite dish on the menu and it doesn't seem to rotate off seasonally. The sauce that pairs with the octopus is so delicious and goes well with the texture and flavor of the octopus. It's a touch of spicy, almost a little sweet and slightly savory all at once. You'll have to try it for yourself.Scallops: were incredibly fresh, I'd never had raw scallops before this dish, but I was sold right after the first slice. It's a nice way to start out your meal and prep your taste buds for the rest of your journey at Oiji.Fried chicken: was deep-fried with a very light batter, possibly just corn starch. You're supposed to dip the chicken into the serrano soy sauce before eating each piece with the lettuce and not let the dish sit for too long. Overall, it was an excellent take on fried chicken that is different than normal. Long Island duckling: was tender and juicy, but for me it was all about that kimchi fried rice under the duck. I liked that more than duck itself which is hard to believe considering I don't like kimchi. Oiji bowl: is very small in size(comparable to adult human palm). The bowl is filled with seaweed rice with uni and sweet shrimp on top (half uni half shrimp). Over-priced for its portion and the taste was unique but not exceptional. The shrimp needed to be uni instead and it might have been priced more appropriately. I would recommend trying this dish if it's your first visit, I feel like different taste buds may like it more than others, but objectively I liked it, wished it had more uni.Oxtail: has a great soup base even though it's not a soup dish. The oxtail has a good mix of meat and tendon; slow-cooked so that it was easy to chew, nearly falls off the bone and rich in flavor.

I revisited the restaurant to sample their winter 2019 menu and was pleased to see that while their shabu shabu selection remains a comforting constant, the appetizers have been slightly updated to add a touch of novelty. The service continues to impress with its attentiveness, and Mayu, along with her staff, exudes friendliness that enhances the dining experience. The quality of the food remains exceptional, with evident care and thoughtfulness put into the menu choices. An amazing experience overall.

Title: A Visit to Antoni Porowski's The Village Den

My recent brunch at The Village Den, a spot beloved by fans of Antoni Porowski from "Queer Eye," was a mix of excitement and mild contentment. Tucked away in the charming Greenwich Village, we arrived on a bustling Sunday just before noon and were greeted with the trendy vibes of the restaurant that still had a few tables spare.

For my meal, I opted for the Almond Pancakes with a side scotch egg, as traditional breakfast meats were notably absent from the menu. The pancakes themselves were satisfactory, especially when paired with the delectable roasted mashed banana, which stood out as the highlight of the dish. However, the scotch egg didn't quite hit the spot as a pancake accompaniment, leaving something to be desired in the realm of a breakfast side.

My daughter chose the Poached Salmon, which she found enjoyable—a sentiment I shared regarding the dish's value compared to the pancakes.

The Village Den operates on counter service, which was efficient enough, though not particularly noteworthy. The restaurant's atmosphere was enhanced by its stylish design and an eye-catching wall mural. Still, the prevalence of students lingering on laptops did pose a challenge for those hoping to find seating quickly.

Pricing felt steep, with the pancakes marked at $11 and the scotch egg at $6.50, which I didn't find justified. The poached salmon bowl seemed a better deal at $15.

Overall, while my daughter’s affinity for Antoni made the visit worthwhile, The Village Den might not see us returning. The experience was adequate, yet with the abundance of dining options available, it’s likely we’ll venture elsewhere in the future.

I recently visited a pleasant new restaurant that's a great addition to the neighborhood for those seeking healthier dining options. The establishment features an inviting open-air space, perfect for a relaxing meal. While the prices lean towards the higher end, they're not unreasonable considering the quality of the food.

I tried the cauliflower dish and was pleasantly surprised by how satisfying it was, both in flavor and portion size. However, the Caesar Salad with Avocado didn't quite hit the mark. The serving size was disappointing, with just a few leaves of lettuce that left me wanting more. Additionally, the avocado was charred to an extent that seemed excessive, bordering on unappetizing.

Overall, the restaurant has potential with its focus on healthy cuisine, but I hope they can adjust the portions and preparation methods to improve the dining experience.

Recently discovered this place close to work & I was glad I did since it's close enough to the office that I can get my ramen fix for lunch if u wanted too. First time around I did  come in for lunch gave the Teppen Shoyu ramen a try wow this was very goodgreat tasting broth really liked the garlic taste, noodles & egg comes with the pork, pork was ok for me could do with out. Second time around went with the Teppen Shio ramen now I do love me some noodles so I opted for extra noodles & egg no pork this time good broth not as tasty as the shoyu but not bad at all great noodles but in the end way too much for me I was definitely eating with my eyes. Also gave the Pork dumplings a try not bad nice taste with the soy sauce. Small location , good quick service CASH ONLY a bit of a nuisance the cash only since u can forget they of course have an ATM available if need be. Good place, will for sure keep visiting from time to time.

Was craving Filipino food so my friend and I decided on this joint. It's small but cozy and the workers are really hospitable. We ordered the sisig, laing, lumpia, and dinuguan.Everything was good but nothing compared to my favorite Filipino places in Queens. That's where it's really at. However, for the city, Grill 21 does well too.

As opposed to trying out our default place around Astor place, my fiancé and I decided to give Bowllin' a shot! We came in on a Sunday afternoon around 3PM, so it was understandably vacant. There are about 3 large tabels, so Bowllin' looks more like a grab and go type of restaurant. I ended up ordering the salmon poke bowl without the beans/replaced with an extra helping of seaweed salad!Although the bowl was around $13, I definitely got my bang for my buck with this bowl! It was the largest poke bowl I have had, and I ended up saving two-thirds of it for later meals! The sauce was both spicy and creamy. The salmon was both tasty and plentiful! There were heaps of crab salad and seaweed salad as well! I am so glad we came to Bowllin', and I will definitely come back here!

What's there not to like about this shop? NOTHING! This is one of THE best gelato shops I've ever been to. First, the vibe: the inside is bright and very welcoming. When you walk in, the gelato and sorbet cases are on the right and there are about 8-ish tables in the shop. Most of the tables seat 2-3 people, but a lot of people just take out their gelato anyways. The gelato and sorbet: it's AMAZING. The presentation is just so cute! If you get your gelato in a cone, they'll make it in a rose shape and you can add a macaron on top. You can even get three different flavors! I got organic chocolate sorbet, coffee gelato, and coconut gelato with a vanilla macaron for mine and all flavors were unique and flavorful. They aren't too overpoweringly sweet either. I love this place :D

During every trip to NYC, I make it a point to dine at this gem of a restaurant. The food and ambiance consistently impress, and the service is exceptional. The 12" Margherita Pizza, adorned with fresh basil, is a personal favorite, alongside their divine Stuffed Shells. Highly recommended for an unforgettable dining experience.

Title: A Flavorful Thai Feast Awaits in the East Village

I recently dined at a delightful Thai spot in the East Village and was pleasantly surprised by the minimal wait time, opting for a cozy seat at the counter. The culinary experience was a hit, starting with the larb, which was a fantastic explosion of authentic Thai flavors, unabashed in its spicy kick. The papaya salad followed suit, delivering a thoroughly enjoyable blend of taste and heat.

While the fried chicken was satisfactory, it didn't quite reach the same heights as the other dishes. Although it comes recommended, I'd suggest exploring other options on the menu next time. As for the sides, the sticky rice was a personal favorite, complementing the mains better than the coconut rice, though the latter did prove useful in soothing the fire of the spices.

The service was as delightful as the food, contributing to an overall fantastic dining experience. If you find yourself craving Thai in the East Village, this eatery is a must-visit.

I was honestly skeptical at first, for how gimmicky this sounded, but absolutely enjoyed the ranch chicken and waffle cone I ended up getting.  The waffle cone was actually very good itself, which I believe helped tie the whole thing together because that was the area I was most concerned about.  The ranch and chicken were also great and definitely left me wanting more.  They had a few flavors to choose from too, ranging in hotness, so everyone should be able to get a flavor they like and they also have Cajun fries, which looked pretty good too.  My only complaint is that it is a little bit of a small portion for the overall price you could pay for the chicken and cone, fries, and drink, but it's New York, so you're never going to find a bargain.  Overall, solid place and would absolutely recommend.

Tucked away with its comical name, NB Wing Wong is a gem serving classic Cantonese cuisine that far surpasses expectations. The roast duck and pork are perfectly executed, delivering savory satisfaction with every bite. For those who appreciate tender, flavorful dishes, the stewed beef tendon was a standout, providing a robust and delightful experience.

Equally impressive were the crispy fried noodles – a dish that often falls victim to greasiness, yet here, they were anything but; instead, they were a crunchy delight with spot-on taste. Even the smaller portions, such as the roast duck noodle, packed a flavorful punch that belied their size.

In a city where food courts, like those in Flushing, can often promise more than they deliver, NB Wing Wong stands out as a beacon of culinary excellence downtown. This is definitely a spot worth returning to for anyone seeking authentic and scrumptious Cantonese fare.

Got a plain slice of cheese pizza for 2.75. It has a crispy bottom and it's not soggy. It tastes like a regular pizza - oily and fresh. The seating is really awkward - they have two chairs placed outside, but facing inward.The interior is typical of any pizza place. There's no air conditioning - only fans. It's a good pizza place to just grab and go, not to sit down and enjoy the slice.Would I come here again? Sure if I'm nearby, but there's nothing special. I'd go to another place and checkout there pizza since there are so many in this area.

Title: A Mixed Bag at Sylvia's in Harlem

I eagerly trekked from Times Square to Harlem on 10/26/2019 after my niece recommended Sylvia's for breakfast, a place she treasured from her girls' trip. Despite the expectation of a warm Southern welcome, we were greeted with a delay—a perplexing 15-minute wait before being acknowledged by the hostess. With ample space in an adjacent room, the decision to split our party of five into 2 and 3 in the main dining area added a twinge of disappointment.

Seating came at 10:14 am. The time between sitting and receiving our breakfast was 40 minutes, a wait exacerbated by struggles to procure basic necessities such as utensils and drinks, turning what should have been a seamless experience into an ordeal. Thankfully, my iPhone XS Max chronicled every moment of the lackluster service, which contrasted starkly with the establishment's storied history and celebrity patronage.

The saving grace of Sylvia's is undoubtedly the cuisine—scrumptious and thoroughly satisfying, living up to its reputation. However, the service left a sour taste that even the best of grits couldn't wash away. I'm torn; despite the excellent food, I'm hesitant to allot more than 3 stars due to the service snafus. Would I give Sylvia's another chance? Yes, but with the hope that they'll align their service with the high standard of their dishes.

Happy Eats, but with a side of patience.

Title: Stunning Views, Underwhelming Flavors at Manhatta

I visited Manhatta several months back for a special birthday dinner for my girlfriend, drawn in by its renowned panoramic views of the New York City skyline. The setting didn't disappoint, offering a breathtaking reminder of the city's architectural marvels.

Opting for the prix fixe menu, we were eager to embark on a culinary journey. The meal began on a tentative note, with dishes tipping the scales towards the salty side. This issue escalated with the main course; the wagyu was accompanied by over-salted vegetables, rendering the spinach beside it inedible. Although our server asked about our experience, my feedback on the issue seemed to be met with indifference, leaving a sour taste.

Dessert was a mix of highs and lows. The date-focused sweet was delightful, though the initially promising souffle succumbed to an overpowering deluge of syrup, leading to an unfinished end.

Overall, despite the impressive locale, the food experience at Manhatta was underwhelming. With a city like New York teeming with dining options, there aren't enough reasons for a return visit to Manhatta, where the flavors failed to match the grandeur of the views.

I was pretty excited to come here with my friend and his wife who is originally from Sichuan. I arrived at 11:50 to get us a table but because they didn't arrive until 12:10, we had to wait until 12:40 for the first round of patrons to leave to be seated.We ordered a variety of dishes including the pork belly, pepper chicken, bamboo shoots with eel, tomato beef stew, pickled fish stew, and eggplant. There were not any stand out dishes and everything ordered was expensive. The tomato beef stew didn't taste like Chinese food and my friend's wife remarked she had never had anything like it in Sichuan. The bamboo shoot with eel lacked flavor and was difficult to eat.Perhaps we ordered the wrong dishes but considering the  the price point of this restaurant and long wait, I do not think I would bother to return.

Grabbed a couple of slices here while waiting for my Amtrak train. As I was about to take my seat a homeless man asked me for change. Not out of line for NYC, but still not a good look for the pizza shop. I had 2 slices of pepperoni pizza. They were typical NYC thin slices. Good taste, with the foldable crust. But it may have been the cause of my stomach rumbling a bit on the train afterwards. It wont exactly be my first stop next time I'm in Penn Station.

Title: A Vegetarian Delight in a Trendy Haven

My friend and I decided to dine here on a Saturday afternoon, lured in by its reputation for beautiful decor and vegetarian-friendly menu. It didn't disappoint. The restaurant embraces a trendy, airy atmosphere that immediately sets a relaxed tone. Despite its appealing ambiance, I was pleasantly surprised to find it less crowded than anticipated.

The service was prompt and attentive, making the dining experience even more enjoyable. As for the food, it was nothing short of fantastic. Seasoned to perfection and presented with care, the dishes clearly showcased the kitchen's commitment to flavor and quality.

This gem has been on my must-visit list for a while, and it certainly lived up to my expectations. I'm already eager to return and delve deeper into their varied menu. Whether you're a vegetarian or simply a lover of excellent food, this restaurant is a must-try!

Sooooo glad we decided to Brunch here! We made reservations a week in advance and reached a little early, but they were happy to accommodate. Seated immediately and we were offered coffee. They serve all day breakfast and lunch #amazing! Since we were a group 8! We got a lot of the items in the menu. I got the Peri Peri chicken wings- oh. my. GOD! The best wings ever and they have a homemade hot sauce, which I honestly think they should sell in bottles! The Rosewater waffles were amazing, chicken sandwich was perfect served with fries and a green sauce (maybe avocado) sooooo good! Tried the chicken kebabs as well and the Mediterranean breakfast. Do yourself a favor go to Jack's wife Frieda! Food is 5/5Service 5/5 Ambience 5/5

If you're in the mood for sushi but don't want to break the bank, this is the spot for you. The combo special, featuring eight pieces of maki and a generously filled temaki, is the standout deal. Opt in with MealPal and you'll snag this delicious duo for a mere $7, though the regular $10 lunch offer is still a steal. I've sampled both the tuna and salmon, and each has been consistently fresh and flavorful. The packaging is also worth noting – the temaki comes in a nifty tearaway sleeve, making it perfect for those on the move. Plus, for MealPal users, they ensure your order is prepped and ready for a swift pick-up. A great deal all around for tasty sushi on the fly.

We visited Vinatería for brunch over a month ago. The inside was actually a bit smaller than I thought it would be. Still, spacious and very bright with loads of natural light coming through from the large windows. Their brunch menu includes complimentary coffee, tea, mimosa, or bloody mary, which is great! Their coffee was strong, real-deal coffee! We had Baked Eggs and Applewood Smoked Bacon Cheeseburger. The Baked Eggs & Pomodoro was nice, eggs perfectly poached, and the tomato sauce flavor was tasty. Cheeseburger comes with fries or salad, but I substituted them with Truffle Fries for extra $4. The fries were soft and potato-y, just the way I like it. Great aroma and flavor or truffle. The burger was really big! The buns were fluffy, but very dry, which was disappointing. Bacon was meaty, almost crunchy. Patty was super juicy! Other than the super dried out buns, which made it difficult to eat, it was a good burger. I just left the buns on the plate...Service was nice and polite, they don't rush you. A nice spot for a brunch, good portion at affordable prices.

A hidden restaurant that is location underground. With huge name of the restaurant on the outside but nowhere to be seem until looking down and noticed it was in the basement. Walking down the stair as well as passing through two doors, finally inside the restaurant. The waitress took us to a reserved table since I made a reservation. By checking in on yelp, you will receive a small Thai tea with purchase of an appetizer. We order two appetizers so they gave us two Thai teas. The Thai tea was good just a bit too sweet. One very important thing or special about this restaurant is the call ringer. You can press it for the services instead of calling the waiter or waitress. It was very convenient.We ordered original roti that came with curry sauce and popcorn chicken(recommended snack/appetizer). Roti is a street food that mean most people use their hand to eat, if you don't like the messiness of using hand then I don't recommended. Popcorn chicken was really disappointing and that is the reason I drop one star. It was freshly made but lack of flavor and the chicken was in tiny little pieces. Those tiny pieces of chicken was over cook and dry. This is not a recommended appetizer especially popcorn chicken originated from Taiwanese. For the main dish, we got Kl Hokkian Char Mee noodle and White Curry noodle. The Kl Hokkian Char Mee noodle was stir fry in dark sauce(like soy sauce) with meat and seafood. It didn't taste salty as it's look. It is really good. The white curry noodle came with shrimp and meat and that was okay. It is the traditional food with strong coconut cream and curry flavor(similar to Thai's green curry just less condensed). Reasonable price for the portion just a bit hard to find. Other than that it was pretty good.

Thai Villa stands out as an extraordinarily adorned dining establishment, offering an all-encompassing sensory experience that is not soon forgotten. The interior, complete with shimmering golden tree leaves, creates an ambiance that's both captivating and warm.

Unfortunately, the popularity of Thai Villa means that weekend tables are highly coveted, and with no reservation option available, large parties should anticipate an early dinner around 5 pm to ensure seating.

The menu, while reflective of classic Thai cuisine, does offer standout dishes such as the puff pastry with salmon—tasty, though diners might crave just a bit more. The tofu and vegetables in ginger sauce delivered on flavor, despite a somewhat untidy presentation. The unanimous favorite was an off-menu dessert, a unique concoction blending sticky rice, condensed milk, red beans, coconut ice cream (notably firm), jackfruit, and toast. This peculiar mix surprisingly emerged as the highlight of our gastronomic journey.

In sum, Thai Villa may serve up standard Thai fare, but it's their ability to surprise and delight with unexpected delights like their dessert that truly makes a meal here memorable.

My wife and I were in New York for a couple of days on business.After business was done ,we decided to stop over at Bait and Hook New York.My wife and I frequent Bait and Hook in Cokato Mn.So it was a must we try this location while visiting New York.We got the same great food,friendly service and welcoming atmosphere!!I must say the food is quality food at a great price! I ordered the fish and chips.It was $18 for a nice size portion.Im a big man and I left the place feeling full.The cod was fried to perfection.Not greasy at all! When I was done with my food I did not have that sick feeling that one can get after eating fish that has not been fried well.Hats off to the Chef!!My wife ordered the Baja Style Chicken Tacos.Four tacos for $12.These street style tacos were the bomb!!!The corn tortillas were fresh.The chicken moist and seasoned well.The veggies(shredded cabbage and mango salsa was a marriage made in heaven.The homemade aioli could have been eaten by the buckets it was that good!This is our go to place.Be it small town Minnesota or The Big Apple New York City!!If you want great food...seafood and drinks!!! Bait and Hook is your place!

Food: 2.5/5Moderate food overall. Some dishes were better than others. Ordered chicken shoyu ramen, soba meshi, crunchy nori tacos, and the karagge. This place is supposedly known for their chicken broth ramen but the ramen (2/5) was underwhelming. The temperature of the broth was lukewarm and the broth itself didn't have much flavor. The noodles were cooked well but overall, it wasn't memorable. The soba meshi (2.5/5) was ok. It was seasoned well with brown sauce (I think soy sauce and something else) and came with an egg but it had soba and rice sort of mixed together. The dish was more of a soba stir fry and had to be eaten with a spoon. The crunchy nori tacos (4/5) were tasty. Came over a bed of fried seaweed with rice, salmon, tuna and avocado. The sauce was similar to spicy mayo. Tasty and crunchy! The karagge (4/5) was perfectly friend and super juicy! 4 stars, not 5 because it wasn't boneless.Service: 4/5Great service overall. Very friendly waiters and very accommodating.Ambiance: 4/5Very cute and modern establishment. Very small and inconvenient bathrooms .

During my vacation to NYC I was on my way to eat sushi when I saw this place, was so beautiful that I had to go in, best decision ever! Started with a bottle of wine. We tried pasta carbonara, risotto fungi and pizza nostrana. Definitely our plates were empt at the end! Such a great food and atmosphere. The Torta all' Olio di Oliva was the perfect ending!!

From the moment we stumbled upon Banter for a late Saturday brunch at 4pm, the Australian touch on our dining experience was unmistakably delightful. Nestled into a cozy corner, we were pleasantly surprised to find ourselves in the midst of their daily Happy Hour, running from 2-5pm. A well-crafted Aperol Spritz was a steal at $8, down from its usual $13.

I opted for the innovative mushroom toast and, with the indulgent addition of a poached egg for $3, I found myself wondering why this isn't a staple alongside avocado toast everywhere. The mushrooms were perfectly savory, supported by a generous layer of creamy burrata and a tangy sundried tomato pesto that provided a welcome flavor pop.

Across from me, my boyfriend enjoyed the aesthetically pleasing golden folded eggs, which he enhanced with fresh salmon for an extra $2. The combination of mushrooms, avocado, and kale made the dish not only visually striking but also 'one of the best brunches' he's had in ages.

Banter has rightfully earned our agreement on that point — their brunch is a standout in both taste and value.

Title: A Letdown Brunch Experience

I recently visited a popular brunch spot, booking through Open Table for a Sunday meal. The necessity of reservations became apparent upon arrival; the restaurant's cozy dimensions would certainly struggle to accommodate walk-ins. Upon entry, our reservation ensured we were seated without delay—a silver lining to start.

Opting out of beverages, I observed my companion enjoy both a Bellini and a mimosa, each met with approval. My choice, the scrambled egg with cured salmon, regrettably fell short of expectations. A lackluster dish, it was undermined by an absence of flavor. The accompanying fries and side salad were passable, but nothing to write home about.

My friend's Croque Monsieur, on the brighter side, received a favorable verdict. However, the meal concluded on a sour note with our shared dessert, the Apple Tarte Tatin. It was a unanimous disappointment, with both texture and taste missing the mark so entirely that we abandoned it after a single bite each.

In conclusion, my brunch experience was unsatisfying. Despite the smooth seating process and a well-received beverage, the food failed to impress, casting a shadow over the entire meal.

After going to Spain this year, I have been searching for something close to the delicious Iberian ham I had there. I think this will be the closest thing to it! We started with some cured meats, the beef and ham. For $22, it actually was a decent amount of meat. The beef was okay, but the ham definitely hit the spot and satisfied some of my craving. For our entree, we both decided to share a paella. The portion was huge and definitely could feed more than 2 people. It was a bit bland, but had SO much seafood in it compared to other places I've tried in the city. I think for $65, it's pretty reasonably priced. Will definitely be back.

Title: An Affordable Chinese Gem by the MoMA

If you're scouring the city for top-notch Chinese cuisine that won't break the bank, look no further than this conveniently situated eatery just across from the MoMA. The restaurant distinguishes itself with ample seating – a refreshing contrast to its busier counterparts – ensuring you can snag a spot without the usual hustle.

During my visit, I opted for the lamb burger paired with a soothing chamomile iced tea, both of which exceeded expectations at an impressively low cost. The flavors were spot-on, making it clear why this chain is renowned for delivering some of the best Chinese dishes around.

Another plus is the accessibility of an individual restroom, making your dining experience that much more comfortable. Trust me when I say, a meal at this venue is a decision you'll savor. Do yourself a favor and drop by.

Title: Great Food Marred by Subpar Service

I recently visited a restaurant where the culinary experience was excellent, but the service left much to be desired. Upon arrival with a reservation confirmation in hand, the hostess inexplicably failed to honor our booking — a frustrating start, especially given the near-empty dining room. The standoff continued until the manager intervened to seat us.

As we settled in, the attitude of the staff did not improve, with servers who seemed unfriendly and overly eager to rush us through our meal.

On to the food itself: The tapas were the highlight of our evening. We indulged in the grilled octopus, which was exceptionally tender despite a slight fishiness. The laffa taco, with its savory chicken shawarma, was a table favorite, truly outstanding. The roasted cauliflower, elevated by a zesty lemon tahini dressing, and perfectly crispy Brussels sprouts also left us impressed. The freshly baked bread provided a warm welcome to the culinary delights that followed.

Despite the culinary delights, the prices were on the higher side. It's unfortunate that such delightful dishes were overshadowed by the lackluster welcome and service, casting a shadow over an otherwise enjoyable meal. Reluctantly, given the treatment we received, a return visit is questionable.

Found this location walking in the city. Stopped in impromptu.  Great decision.  Drinks were good. The price is right. Wings were great. JJ the bartender was great. Customer service on point,  attentive and welcoming. I will be coming back

Delicious, clean yet tiny Thai restaurant in Chelsea. We had pad see ew, chicken satay and papaya salad. Everything was soooo delicious and authentic (even for someone that has travelled to Thailand multiple times ;)). The servers are also very friendly and attentive throughout our meal.The restaurant is very small, as there are less than 10 tables. However, it is beautifully decorated and is very clean. Glur also does delivery on all major delivery websites (seamless, ubereats, etc). I would love to come back to try the soup and curries.Ps, if you reserve on seated, you get 15% cash back (shameless plug seated promo code VANESSA390 for $15 cash back)

New York Pizza !  Hands down a great pizza pie! I had a slice of white pizza - which was excellent! And took a slice of chicken ranch pizza to go! The slices are HUGE!  I think I ate 3-4 bites and was full!  Even cold it was delicious!  I did not end up eating the other slice ... I was done with pizza by then.  However the verdict was good!  Good pizza for sure!  Price .... a bit high IMO two slices and a bottled water $17But hey it's NYC!Customer Service~ Hummm could have been better honestly ...1) said their CC machine was down and the ATM was down too and that it needed to be cash.I walked over input my card into ATM - BAM money in hand!  Yep I was a little frustrated due to the fee attached!  So I said hey!!!! Oh let me try your card and what do you know ... it worked !  Epic fail ! No tip given... 2) They were busy for sure but in my opinion busy or not you give friendly and excellent service always ... fail3) Crowded seating ... yeah yeah I know it's NYC Pricey... $$$Low customer service ... Good pizza  3 Stars  due to flavor of pizza / crust only!

Title: A Cozy Spot for Szechuan Near Rockefeller - Wu Liang Ye

Located just across from the bustling Rockefeller Center, Wu Liang Ye offers an authentic Szechuan dining experience that we've enjoyed countless times. The restaurant, set in what seems to be a former row house, boasts fireplaces and sparkling crystal chandeliers, though it must be said that the charm is slightly dimmed by decor that feels dated and in need of a refresh.

On our latest visit, we opted for a lighter meal, starting with the chilled spicy noodles and potstickers, both of which were delightful and lived up to our expectations. The main course, General Tso's chicken, was a standout with its generous portions of white meat, flawlessly battered and mixed into a robust General Tso's sauce that ranks highly amongst its East Coast rivals.

In sum, Wu Liang Ye remains a solid choice for those seeking quality Chinese fare for either lunch or dinner in the heart of midtown.

Tucked away near the lively theatre district and the pulse of Times Square, this spacious Italian gem is ideal for group gatherings. Our dining experience kicked off with a unique touch - wine served in elegant engraved glasses that added to the charm. The appetizers set the bar high; the fried mozzarella sticks were a delightful dance of crispy and gooey textures, while the mussels bathed in a sublime white wine and tomato sauce became the perfect companion for bread-dipping.

The entrees maintained this high standard, with the veal marsala impressing us with its tender and rich flavor profile. However, the true spectacle was the pasta flambeed with Hennessy in a cheese wheel. The tableside preparation wasn't just theatrical; it was a flavor journey crowned with parmesan that proved to be both entertaining and delectable.

Despite a full belly, dessert was irresistible. The molten lava cake was a decadent, warm chocolate indulgence, yet it was the tiramisu shake that stole my heart – a brilliant twist on a classic, offering the essence of tiramisu in a creamy, sippable form.

In a nutshell, this restaurant offers an outstanding Italian feast paired with an enjoyable ambiance and inventive presentations. It's a place I'd definitely recommend and eagerly return to.

Title: Curry Heaven at Ktown's Cozy Gem

I'm a regular at this delightful spot in Ktown, having returned multiple times, most recently twice in the span of three weeks—a testament to its allure. My go-to dishes include the udon curry set and the curry chicken set, both generously accented with tasty chicken and shrimp. 

For those contemplating the spice level, take heed; it's robust—perhaps a level up from what you might anticipate. I opted for a spice level slightly above mild (a 2, I believe), which to me was the perfect heat, especially in the soup where it's more pronounced. If you find it too spicy, the accompanying rice acts as a perfect fire extinguisher.

Portion sizes are generous, ensuring you leave satisfied. The katsu is a standout, sporting the ideal amount of crunch, and while the curry carries a distinct flavor profile compared to others, like GogoCurry, it's uniquely satisfying, albeit pricier.

The ambiance is charming, especially the quirky placement of utensils tucked under the tables—an endearing touch. Service is generally good, although there may be moments of miscommunication that can come across as terse.

Overall, this spot is a must-visit for anyone craving curry in a quaint setting, with ample food to satiate late-night cravings.

This Thai restaurant ticks all the right boxes for an authentic dining experience. The food served is exceptional across the board, leaving nothing to be desired. A standout was their Thai iced tea with milk – a flawless blend that is not to be missed. The beauty of this place extends beyond the plate; its interior design is notably charming and even extends to the small detail of a well-maintained bathroom. Highly recommended for anyone craving a taste of Thailand.

This place is right next to my office, and it is a go-to for the local power lunch. The food is actually pretty good, and the presentation is thoughtful.I also love that there is a huge selection for the lunch special, think 12 dishes to choose from for appetizers and another 12 for entrées, and a small dessert as well for under $30.There's a wide selection of fish in keeping with the Greek theme, and certain things on the menu definitely brought me back to a recent trip to Greece.My lunch companion and I both ordered the fish of the day, which was a white fish that was thoughtfully prepared. It was well cooked, and we both enjoyed it. I got the octopus appetizer, which had a small supplement price, but was worth every penny. The grilled octopus was delicious and juicy, and the bed of onions it was served on was wonderful.I'm giving this three stars off because the service was flat-out rude. I hadn't finished my salad when they tried to plate my fish course. It was too small of a table, so they tried to take the salad away while I was mid-bite. There was still quite a bit on the plate. I thought about letting it go, but I instead told the waiter that I needed more time to finish my salad. He hovered over me while holding my entrée plate. It was super awkward for everybody, but I wasn't going to get bullied into not finishing the salad! It was really good!Anyway, after 30 seconds of hovering, I finished the salad and he plopped down my fish. Uncool!

I had a pretty pleasant experience here. Service and food were both nice/fine, but I generally have very high expectations for Italian food in the city given how.many.italian.restaurants.there.are. Fine just doesn't cut it for Italian for me anymore.I actually quite liked the bruschetta spread and the bolognese. I ordered my bolognese without truffle oil, but my friend said she couldn't really taste it in hers, even though she had my extra portion in hers in addition to the normal portion. Huge negative is the door - it's such a small restaurant that anytime anyone steps in or out of the restaurant in the middle of winter, you get a giant gust of wind.Not your typical below-average Little Italy Italian restaurant, but nothing to rave home about either. Service was spot on though!

Located in the lobby of a hotel, this place can look a bit deceiving and possibly not the most authentic. But don't be fooled because their ramen is AMAZING.The bone marrow ramen is delicious. The broth is creamy in the best way possible. I normally don't like to drink the entire bowl of soup while eating but my friend and I both finished all our noodles including the broth. The meat was also tender and melts in your mouth.There's a good selection of sake and other happy hour items as well.

Ok to start off, this place is located in the 24th floor of Equinox. The address is 33 hudson yards, right opposite to 30 hudson yards which is where all the shops are. When you find Equinox go to revolving door in the middle of the building, not to the left corner. If you do end up in the left corner of the building, the extremely tall doorman will direct to the middle. I'm just giving you directions incase you end up like me lost and hungryI came here for brunch and had the warm.black bean crepe, it was different and delicious. The avocado and cilantro have it a tangy taste and the eggs made the crepe soft. I also had coffee here which was good. Our waitress was sweet and attentive. Another person in our table got an iced latte which was white in color, and she told me it tasted like milk and there was no coffee but she didnt mention to the waitress. The waitress however noticed it and she came over and asked her if she could get her another latte because she felt like her glass didnt look right. That was really sweet and good service! Our waitress didnt add the latte to the bill either.Apart from the service and unique food options, the ambience and the view is lovely.

I enjoy this place, went for a quick happy hour and the bartending staff is out of this world. Very kind, respectful and sparked great conversation. One recommended me to come for brunch. She rocked.Here's where they lost me. They added  gratuity. What is the reason behind that? The bartenders are doing an exceptional job and they should be rewarded why put a pebble in my boot by adding a mandatory tip. Nonetheless I am consumed by the hype and will come back.

When here for a quick post workout meal with my friends. The decor is rustic, the food and ingredients seem fresh, The hummus is exceptionally good, and the chef signature sweet potato falafel is definitely worth a try. We were pleasantly surprised by the lightly sweetened freshly brewed tea beverages in peach and hibiscus. An interesting twist was the vermicelli noodles if you order a pan. They're basically an eggbased noodle shaped and cut and cooked as yellow rice. Definitely worth a shot for a hole in the wall.

During my recent visit to Mart, hidden within the bustling shops of Hudson Yards, I had the opportunity to sample the much-talked-about black and white sando. The shop, although small and offering a mix of snacks, ramen, and sandwiches, felt slightly overpriced compared to other markets—perhaps not the best choice for a regular workday lunch. Fortunately, on the Saturday I dropped by, the mart was well-stocked and not crowded, which allowed for a quick grab-and-go experience.

The sando in question featured bread reminiscent of those found in Asian bakeries, though it was on the dry side for my taste. While the black sesame filling was notably underwhelming—bearing a faint nuttiness more akin to peanut butter than the rich flavor I anticipated—the cream added little to the overall experience. While it was an interesting novelty to try once, it lacked the compelling qualities that would invite a repeat purchase.

Title: A Classic Meal at a Veteran Korean Eatery

Nestled on a street bustling with culinary contenders, this long-standing Korean restaurant serves up a familiar menu that promises a pleasant dining experience. While the street is lined with similar offerings, I found myself unexpectedly charmed by the non-BBQ items on the menu.

The eatery, steeped in history as one of Korea's oldest, delivers a satisfactory meal, though it lacks that extraordinary touch one might anticipate from such an establishment. The highlight for me was the egg soufflé, a standout item not included in the traditional banchan. I opted for a topping of spicy cod roe, an enjoyable addition despite wishing for a more generous portion to amplify the flavor.

On to the Korean BBQ - the presentation of the meats was visually appealing, especially the kalbi, which never disappoints. The bulgogi, while succulent, became a tad messy as it bathed in its own juices. As for the banchan, I stuck to my staples, indulging in favorites like steamed egg, pancakes, dumplings, and fried chicken - all of which were pleasing.

Regrettably, service was more reserved than I had hoped. The waitress, conservative in her recommendations, left me navigating the menu on my own, a task I'm familiar with but one that didn't allow me to explore the menu's full potential.

Despite a lack of gastronomic surprises, the overall quality keeps me intrigued. It's a place I'm willing to revisit, with the intention of delving deeper into their offerings, many of which seem to promise much more than what I sampled.

Title: Satisfying Squares at Prince Street Pizza – 3.5/5 Stars

During a quintessential NY pizza adventure, I decided to check out the bustling Prince Street Pizza. Its infamous lines lived up to their reputation, but fortunately, the efficient staff kept things moving at a brisk pace.

The pizzeria's interior is quite compact, with just enough counter space to balance your prized slices – a true grab-and-go atmosphere, complemented by walls adorned with celebrity endorsements.

I opted for their signature square pepperoni alongside a classic cheese slice. The pepperoni, unfortunately, was overdone to a rubbery texture, detracting from the overall taste. However, the crisp crust was a highlight, providing a perfect textural contrast despite the slightly excessive doughiness of the thick-cut squares. The sauce was flavorful and robust, a real standout, though a more generous cheese topping would've been appreciated.

Value-wise, the slices were reasonably priced and didn't skimp on size. Cash is king at this establishment, but there's an ATM onsite for convenience.

While Prince Street Pizza's offerings didn't quite surpass my established favorites, they still served up a solid pizza experience. It's a place I'd be willing to revisit for a second taste when in New York again.

Prince Street Pizza is a super popular pizza store in New York. This was my first time trying it out and on the night it was actually pretty chilly and the line wasn't existent. I ordered two slices of pepperoni and their pizza is a little unique. It is shaped as square and a little thicker than most New York pizza slices. I enjoyed the slice of pizza and wish I had ordered another! But hey there is always a next time when I'm out in that area. The inside is small and it is only standing so if you want you can take it to go and walk around! That's what I did and I totally enjoyed myself around the area. It's in a location where there are plenty of stores to shop around and browse. Try this pizza out and you might be surprised at how much you like it.

Title: A Delightful Happy Hour Experience at a Charming Spot

I recently dropped by this gem of a spot during their happy hour from 4-7pm and was thoroughly impressed with both the drink deals and the atmosphere. The $8 cocktail selection included some wonderfully infused spirits; both the English Breakfast and the Apple Bourbon on the rocks were standout choices. Complementing our drinks, the truffle fries were a revelation – simply amazing.

While the bartender was undeniably friendly, I did notice the absence of a water service. This didn’t detract much from the experience, though, as the mature crowd (mostly 35+) contributed to a sophisticated yet warm vibe, further accentuated by guests greeting the host like old friends.

The restaurant's section exuded elegance with its beautiful decor and pristine white tablecloths, perfect for a special dinner or impressing the parents. However, be prepared for a bit of a squeeze at the bar area, as space is at a premium.

Overall, the experience left me excited to return and delve into their main menu. A delightful spot that promises not just good food and drinks, but also an inviting feeling of community.

Dining at this establishment proved to be a delightful experience. The broth served was truly amazing, teeming with depth and flavor. Complementing the broth, the noodles were unmistakably fresh, adding a perfect texture to each bite. The restaurant's set up may be unconventional, but it only added to the charm, making the overall experience a positively good one. Highly recommended for those in search of an exceptional and interesting culinary adventure.

The Dumpling Room is a small cozy room with wide wood planks on the ceiling, the walls and floor.  Chairs are metal in a variety of colors.  Tables are a 50's throwback with formica tops.  My weekday lunch was really good and that's saying something because I'm a tough critic, especially when it comes to Chinese food, my favorite cuisine.  Green beans arrived hot and blistered but still crisp and a bit salty which paired well with the moist rice and freshly made fried pork dumplings.  I'll go back to try more even though it's in a rather remote part of the UWS.

Title: A Hidden Gem in New York City

Review:

This restaurant quickly became one of my favorites in New York City, despite the bit of travel required to reach it. From the moment you step through its unique entryway, you are transported into one of the city's most beautiful lounges, buzzing with attractive employees and guests alike.

Just going for a drink is an experience in itself; the mixology is exceptional and the atmosphere is simply top-notch. I highly recommend lounging at the bar, enjoying a casual bite, and soaking in the vibrant ambiance.

Although my visit was just before dinner elsewhere, I couldn't resist trying the tomato soup with cheese dumplings cake – a dish fervently recommended by a regular. It was a culinary revelation: generously portioned, creatively crafted, and truly scrumptious. Bonus for vegetarians: they'll happily omit the bacon upon request.

Don't miss out on a visit to the ladies' room, where a complimentary glass of sparkling rosé awaits – an indulgent touch that could turn any bad date around. As someone from Houston, I'm envious we don't have an equivalent spot to escape to. This restaurant is not just a meal; it's a delightful escape that I absolutely adore.

Title: Exquisite A5 Wagyu at New Upscale Korean BBQ

If you're a fan of premium beef, the A5 wagyu at this new upscale Korean BBQ joint is an absolute must-try. The meat's quality rivaled the famed Kobe beef in Japan, offering a melt-in-your-mouth experience that's hard to come by. Although the regular price of $120 for eight petite slices may cause a bit of sticker shock, the grand opening special of 50% off made it more palatable, albeit still a splurge. Remember, though, you're investing in exceptional quality that is truly phenomenal. The restaurant itself boasts an elegant decor that creates a romantic ambiance fit for couples seeking a special dining experience. Despite the hefty price tag, the indulgence in such fine meat is a worthwhile treat for those who appreciate the finer things in life.

I am absolutely thrilled to recommend this restaurant to any Korean cuisine enthusiast. Although the prices lean towards the expensive side, the exquisite presentation and intricate preparation process of each dish justify every penny. The dishes are not only visually stunning but also boast exceptional flavors that are sure to delight the palate. Furthermore, the service is commendable; our server demonstrated impressive knowledge, guiding us through the experience of combining ingredients to craft the perfect mouthful. A visit here is a must for a truly memorable dining experience.

Stoped in to this cute little restaurant in East Village for a Margarita with family.I had the Jalapeño, my daughter had the Prickly Pear and my husband had the Traditional. All were really good, pricey( not unexpected for NYC), and I would recommend them all. The food looked fantastic- confirmed by my daughter-but we were too full from dinner. Bartender was friendly and attentive.  Will come back to try their food next time!

Service is horrible during the night hours. They don't care about you. They take long to come take your order and they take long to pick up the check. They give you cold food... how does boil pierogis, come out cold...it should be boiled hot... isn't that obvious. I wish they were more consistent because their prices are high and it's a amazing concept for this restaurant

There's honestly not much to say. Came on a Tuesday on my birthday before dinner. That's right, before dinner, I had to get some Prince Street for an appetizer. The pepperoni slices are the best anywhere you go. Love when they curl up on edges, makes all that tasty oil. It's just something you need to try when in NYC. One of the best in town.

The first thing that gets your attention about this restaurant is the decor and aesthetic. There are 2 large neon signs on the main wall that have a vintage vibe to them. There are also some worn looking posters plastered on the pillars. This place is made to look like you're actually in Cuba.We ordered drinks and appetizers off the happy hour menu. I got the margarita and my boyfriend got the mojito. They were both very very delicious. I would come again for the drinks alone.We ordered the sesame wings, yucca fries and the lechon on tostone. The lechon was delicious and not too dry. The sesame wings were well seasoned and juicy. The yucca fries were crispy and they provided with a house made ketchup, which had more vinegar than regular ketchup to give it more of a kick. The other sauce, the House Mojo, which was pretty buttery and had a hint of basil. I really enjoyed both.We ordered the Cuban fried rice to share. Nothing too special about this. It was good but it didn't stand out to me. If I were to come back, I would try something else off their entree menu.Overall, this place is a great place to go after work for happy hour. If you don't feel like eating a full meal, definitely come here for the drinks!

Honestly, one of the best experiences in my life. Not even joking. I ordered one of everything and it was all sensational. I love cheese and that's definitely a prerequisite to the visit, but wow is it worth tThe Mac and cheese is gold (just like a few reviews suggested)The Mediterranean Raclette is also incredible for a vegetarian option!The fig tartine was the table favorite, it's a MUST.The burger was phenomenal. Everyone needs to go to Raclette, I'm a firm believer of its magic.

My friend found this cozy French restaurant for a get together dinner. The restaurant has two levels. The first level is the bar, so it's quite noisy and cold during the winter. The second level is much quieter with dim lighting.I ordered the homemade potato gnocchi that came with cremini & maitake mushrooms in a porcini-cognac cream. I wasn't expecting to have such good gnocchi here. The texture was very soft and pillowy. I liked the extra crunch from the fried cremini mushrooms. I wish they gave more maitaki mushrooms though. For the group we shared some fries, which could have been more crisp, and a plum tarte du jour. The waiter kept on saying the tart was too small to share for our group of five, but when it came out the slice was huge and easily shareable. Although I had more than my share of bites because the crust was so tasty. I would come back just for the gnocchi and plum tarte.

I recently dined for lunch where I splurged for the prime ribeye ssam add-on at an extra $42. The toro ssam bap, a divine concoction of fatty tuna and scrambled egg wrapped in seaweed, was the highlight of the meal; it was mouthwateringly unforgettable. The rest of the offerings were satisfactory but didn't quite elevate the experience to exceptional. A notable letdown was the gochu ramen, specifically the meat, which was regrettably overcooked to the point of being inedible, a stark contrast to the flavorful broth. Despite these mixed impressions, I appreciate having sampled the menu but my previous experiences at establishments like ON and nonono have set a high bar that wasn't surpassed here. It was worth the visit, but a return is unlikely.

I love bao buns, and I'm normally pretty picky but I loveddddd these. We got the chairman (classic pork) and the tofu and I couldn't decide which one I loved more. They were also extremely filling which was great. I was satisfied and full after two but they were so good I wanted to keep eating! I definitely recommend going if you enjoy bao buns.

Title: A New York Gem for Quick and Tasty Eats

For the second time while on a work trip in New York, I found myself back at this unassuming spot near my hotel for a late-night meal. My previous visit left a good impression with a well-made burger, so I had to return. Tonight's decision, a grilled chicken with cheese, sans bun, and a side of fries, was a delightful surprise. The chicken breast was expertly seasoned, easily ranking as one of the tastiest I've ever enjoyed, especially for the unbelievable price of under $15—quite the steal in NYC.

The service was another highlight. Not only was the staff member who took my order incredibly warm and welcoming, but despite the bustling environment with about six other parties dining in, the service remained impressively swift without a hitch.

Admittedly, the decor could use a refresh, but the cleanliness and prominent A health rating provide ample reassurance. Ultimately, this place checks all the right boxes: delicious food, speedy and friendly service, and exceptional value. Surely, it's a five-star experience for anyone looking for a quick and satisfying meal in New York without breaking the bank.

Food here is truly delicious. So good that it doesn't get 3 stars for all the negatives but no 5 stars because of the negatives. This trendy share style place really has a lot to offer and delicious menu filled with all sorts of amazing food. The basil fired chicken was particularly delicious and noodles were very good. However, the price, the portion size and lack of air conditioning really drags this place. For 1/2 the price and double the food, my cohorts and I went up the block right afterwards because of how small these portions were. Definitely try the food here because it is very good, but unless you want to drop serious money, expect to get a second meal afterwards.

Title: A Pleasant Halal Surprise at Top Thai

I recently dined at Top Thai with my in-laws, aiming to satisfy their craving for halal Thai cuisine. To my delight, I discovered upon arrival that the restaurant now offers a fully halal menu, an upgrade from what I thought to be a partial one.

The menu selection was impressive, and collectively we indulged in a variety of dishes. The standout for us was the tamarind duck—it broke the mold of typical Thai offerings with its unique blend of crispy, tender meat complemented by a slightly tangy tamarind sauce.

Despite the culinary highs, I find myself giving Top Thai four stars due to the dinner prices, which seem steep relative to the portion sizes. However, a pro tip for fellow diners seeking value: take advantage of their lunch specials for a more economical yet equally delicious experience.

Title: A Delightful Vietnamese Culinary Adventure

I recently dined at a restaurant that came highly recommended by a food influencer I follow on Instagram. Photos don't do this place justice; it exceeded expectations, prompting me to visit with a couple of friends.

We skipped the popular 'Meat-7-Ways' due to its overwhelming portion size, instead opting for variety. The 'Ban Hoi Platter,' a do-it-yourself Viet spring-roll kit, was a standout, allowing for a playful and interactive dining experience.

The Short Rib Egg Roll was a hit, with just the right balance of flavor and a crispy, non-greasy exterior that wasn’t merely filler. The Oxtail Congee was hearty and satisfying, albeit slightly greasier than expected. The Short-rib with spring onion was impeccable—tender and well-marinated without overpowering seasonings.

Surprisingly, the Five-spice Beef Tongue managed to deliver subtlety with this often-dominant spice, and the assistance of the server in grilling allowed us to savor the meal unfettered.

Finally, the Vietnamese Steak with bone marrow butter was rich and perfectly cooked, though not quite on par with a high-end steakhouse—it stands on its own merits.

Would I return? Without a doubt, especially to share this gem when friends are in town.

Title: A Slurp-worthy First Encounter with Ippudo

My inaugural visit to Ippudo left me thoroughly impressed with both its ambiance and exceptional service. The interior boasted an inviting aesthetic, and our interaction with the staff was characterized by their warm and efficient manner.

As a trio, we opted to blend in with the communal vibe, sharing a table with fellow diners. Our culinary adventure began with the pork buns—fluffy morsels enveloping succulent, sweet pork—that set our taste buds dancing in mere minutes. The truffle poutine fries followed, striking a savory note with their slightly salty profile balanced by the rich meat and gravy.

The star of the show, however, was the Akamaru ramen, elevated by an irresistible egg addition. This bowl of ramen was a revelation—the broth an elixir of depth, the noodles boasting that delightful chewy resistance. Sharing, it turned out, was my only regret as I craved more of that umami symphony.

A shoutout to the attentive servers is in order. My water glass never dipped below the halfway mark, a refreshing detail discreetly managed without intrusion.

I left already planning a return—a rendezvous with the Yuzu ramen awaits. For any ramen aficionado or newcomer, Ippudo is a must-try that promises a delectable escape into noodle nirvana.

This place is an awesome hang out joint, let it be for lunch or for happy hour! They are known for their massive beer hall and Brew pub located in New York City's West Village. Serving an exclusive selection of craft beers and specialty cocktails with a great amount of space! .After attempting to come here twice to try their burgers, but finding them closed For a private event, the third time was a charm! I got to try their: Burger & Fries - Custom-Blend Angus Beef, Choice of Aged Cheddar, Gruyere or Bleu Cheese on a Toasted Potato Roll with Lettuce, Tomato and Fresh Cut Idaho Fries.My husband raves about them so much! & it was a hit! Loved the simplicity & of course the beer garden atmosphere

I had a fabulous birthday celebration here. The food was amazing and we danced after. They have a fun boomerang photo booth too, and the jewelry is nice! Favorite dishes include: the grilled cheese dumplings in tomato soup sauce, eggplant pizzetta, shishito peppers, spaghettini, philly style mac and cheese, and the empanadas. I would order all of them again exactly the same. We had a group of 6 and a good booth for that. The dancing was fun afterward upstairs, and we enjoyed the cocktails. I will definitely come back here. It's a great spot especially for celebratory occasions!

Upon visiting the NoMad Chikarashi, the size of the restaurant took me by surprise, which was notably smaller than the Canal St store featured on their Yelp page. The practical use of space includes convenient hooks under bar seating and additional bench seating, though the establishment seems primed for takeout or delivery.

My selection, the Goma Shoyu Tuna, priced at $16, delivered a modest serving of bluefin tuna, infused with a flavorful sesame oil, soy, and mirin sauce. Accompaniments included wakame, nori, onions, a slice of avocado, and garlic chips. Chikarashi's offerings are reminiscent of an elevated chirashi experience and cater to diverse palates with both cooked and vegetarian choices. A delightful bonus to the meal was the scrumptious Dole whip – a refreshing end to an overall pleasing dining experience.

A good burger spot. Service is quick. Burgers are good but could use a higher fat content. Shakes are very thick. Decor and layout is pretty sparse, not really a place you would stay and linger. Overall good value and nice apt for a quick in and out of meal.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Scampi's – Instagram Fame vs. Reality

Scampi's marketing prowess had me eager to dive into their celebrated scampi malfadini pasta, a dish that’s become quite legendary online. Despite high expectations set by the countless rave reviews and impeccable images, my experience was a tad underwhelming, though it did help to demystify the Instagram hype.

Arriving early for our reservation, I was impressed by Scampi's accommodating nature, as they seated us ahead of time—a rare occurrence in the bustling New York dining scene. This initial delight, however, was dampened by the unexpectedly long wait for our entrees, which took over an hour to arrive.

The meal commenced with mixed signals. Our starters appeared swiftly, with the brussels sprouts proving to be an unexpected raw variation that left me regretful for not scrutinizing the menu. The red snapper ceviche, on the other hand, was a delightful mix of fresh fish, tomatoes, and a kick of chili peppers.

The acclaimed scampi malfadini unfortunately missed the mark for me. Its lemon zest overshadowed the dish, and while I enjoyed the al dente pasta, it lacked depth in flavor. The presentation couldn't salvage my anticipation for a culinary revelation that never arrived.

Scampi’s ambiance provided a beautiful backdrop to our evening, and despite the delay in service, the experience was pleasant. For those looking to sample Scampi’s offerings, I’d suggest their $23 lunch special as a more economical choice without the dent to your wallet that dinner might incur.

What can I say, we always end up here as it has great food and great service. They are always fast and friendly. It is clean and big space with lots of table. It is next to the road and walk up. The prices are okay but they have varieties of food.

Title: A Touch of Shanghai Charm in Manhattan

During a family visit to New York, we stumbled upon China Blue in Manhattan and decided to give it a try. As a Californian from the 626, my standards for Chinese cuisine are high, and I entered with modest expectations.

The service was unremarkable, typical of Chinese eateries, and the restaurant itself was small but not crowded. The interior, however, was a delightful surprise – a nostalgic nod to 1930s and 1940s China with its vintage décor, from the old lamps to the typewriters and telephones, and a room that harkened back to traditional Chinese tea houses. The ambiance truly enriched the dining experience.

While we passed on their extensive alcohol menu, it's worth noting for those interested in spirited offerings. The dim sum menu deviated from what I'm used to, offering made-to-order items as opposed to the push-cart service I'm familiar with.

Our selections included Crystal Shrimp Dumplings, Baby Cucumbers, Pan Fried Pork Dumplings, Shanghai Shumai, and Shanghai Spring Rolls. Unfortunately, the Spring Rolls were a letdown, resembling common Chinese egg rolls rather than the lighter, rice paper-wrapped variety I anticipated.

However, the standout dish was their Pan Fried Pork Dumplings (or Buns), which were expertly crafted, juicy, and wonderfully seasoned - a true culinary highlight. Paired with hot tea and crispy cucumbers, these dumplings elevated our meal and left us satisfied.

In summary, while China Blue may not revolutionize your culinary world, it offers a pleasant dining experience with a few standouts and an atmosphere that transports you to a bygone era.

Title: Speedy Service and Exquisite Eats at Bustling Bistro

My recent visit to this bustling eatery solidified its reputation in my book: delightful, delicious, and impressively speedy. Giving the place a second chance after its opening phase, I was not disappointed.

Upon arriving at a chaotic front area, dual receptionists swiftly tackled the crowd with iPads in hand. Despite the lunchtime rush, we were seated at the bar within five minutes—no small feat, given my mix-up with the reservation date.

The bar seating proved advantageous, offering a prime view of the day's specials and on-demand server attention. The portobello mushroom bao—my ultimate food wish—lived up to its dreamy standards. The day's special, a poached egg and hollandaise concoction, topped with shredded truffle and nestled in a bun, was nothing short of a taste explosion.

My dining companion enjoyed a savory noodle soup with chicken, while the special eggplant curry, though too spicy for me, was a hit thanks to its light, fluffy panko-crusted eggplant.

Regretfully, we skipped dessert and the tempting frozen slushies, but the rapid dining experience—just 45 minutes—was perfect for a workday lunch break.

To sum it up: go for the bao, stay for the tantalizing flavors, and expect to be served swiftly and with enthusiasm. I'm already planning my next visit.

Its not easy to find good authentic thai food in NYC. But i finally found it. So many mouth watering selection from salad, appetizer, main dish to dessert. We had couple of appetizer the one that really stood up was the curry puff. Got tilapia fish green curry that super delish. Mango sticky rice is a must and dont forget the thai ice coffee. Service was attentive and our server patiently explain the menu

Title: A Solid Choice for Authentic Korean Lunch Specials

I recently visited this restaurant for their lunch special and found it quite satisfying. For $10, the Seolleongtang was a warming and delightful dish, while the kalbi with spicy tofu soup at $20 offered a generous portion and a pleasing kick of heat. Their ban chan selection varies with each visit; sometimes it's exceptional, including favorites like kimchi, spicy tofu, and the occasional squid, but other times it falls a bit short.

The service here deserves a mention – it's quick and efficient, ensuring a smooth dining experience. However, the inconsistency in flavor, particularly with dishes like the beef noodles and ban chan, prevents me from giving a full five-star rating. When they get it right, it's truly delicious and rich, but on off days, the food can taste somewhat bland.

Despite this, the pricing and portion sizes make it a great deal. With some improvement in maintaining the quality of their meals across the board, this restaurant has the potential to be a top-notch destination for Korean cuisine enthusiasts.

Title: A Pricey Yet Pleasing Culinary Experience

My dining experience at this restaurant was nothing short of exceptional, despite the initially daunting prices. The service shone with excellence, as the staff exuded friendliness and a warm welcome. The ambience struck a cozy and inviting note, creating a delightful backdrop to our meal.

Our table indulged in an array of dishes, starting with the orechiette—where spinach, tomato, Italian sausage, and mozzarella mingled in perfect harmony—and the trenette, a comforting mesh of rib ragu, peas, and carrot. Each pasta dish impressed with its perfectly al dente texture and well-balanced flavors.

The special sandwich of the day, a soft shell crab creation accented with red pepper aioli, avocado, and heirloom tomato, was served alongside fries that were a standout in their own right: freshly cut, impeccably crispy, and utterly addictive.

The pièce de résistance, however, was the shaved truffle pizza. Its aroma was so intoxicating that it captivated the attention of passersby, who couldn't help but comment on its richness.

In summary, this restaurant delivered an indulgent food experience that justified every penny. It's a gem for those looking for quality cuisine combined with heartwarming service and a pleasant atmosphere.

Title: A Slice of Naples in the Heart of the City

If you're craving the authenticity of Neapolitan pizza without boarding a plane, look no further. This cozy gem serves up a slice of Italy with immense flavors that belie its modest size. During my visit, I sampled both the Diavola and Quattro Formaggi pizzas – and each was a revelation. The Diavola was a fiery delight, while the four cheese was a masterclass in balance, rich yet not overwhelming. The secret seems to be in the freshness; the tomato sauce sang with the notes of just-picked tomatoes, and the cheeses tasted like they were sourced straight from a local farm.

But it's not just the food that impresses; service here is prompt and attentive, making for an all-around stellar dining experience. The pizzas arrived at our table with impressive speed, yet there was no compromise on taste. This spot has undoubtedly earned a return visit from me, and next time, I'm diving into their pasta dishes. For anyone in search of genuine Italian cuisine that's crafted with care, this restaurant is an absolute must-visit.

Im glad they opened a location in Midtown. This restaurant chain started in Flatiron and they had a very simple premise: burger and lobster. Those used to be the only items you could order. Now they have expanded their menu and offer a variety of burger and lobster inspired items. Like the lobster mac n cheese. Hint: it's delicious!I dived into their non-traditional menu and ordered The Beast. It's a Pat La Frieda patty burger with lobster, swiss cheese and truffle mayo. This monstrosity is not for the faint of heart. It kinda works, but the lobster temp was noticeably colder than the rest of the burger (which makes sense). The result is a weird hot and cold thing going on in your mouth. There is no doubting that the flavors work well together though. Overall this place is a more turbo charged version of the original NYC location. Beautifully decorated and great ambiance.

Was introduced to this place because of a friend's birthday dinner and liked it so much that it's now a delivery favorite as well. I've tried many of the pastas and pizzas, and my favorites include the spaghetti limone (strikes the perfect balance between acidic, cheesy, and salty), the calamari, and the mashed potatoes (sounds strange but they're really so hearty and comforting). The pizzas are also done very well, though this is less of a standout due to the many competing pizzerias in the city. The staff is so nice too -- they were very accommodating during my friend's birthday dinner and during every delivery. Once, I placed a Seamless order and it hadn't arrived within the allotted time frame given. When I called to inquire, the owner explained that their system had shut down and apologized profusely, offering both to comp my meal and to send along a free dessert for my next delivery. So nice.10/10!

Last evening, my friend and I dined at this charming little spot. I was intrigued by the Early Bird Dinner Special, reasonably priced at $22. It was an appealing set, consisting of various vegetable sides, a pair of shrimp tempura, inari, refreshing soba with a dipping sauce, and a classic vanilla ice cream to finish. A unique touch was the addition of a pour-in for the leftover dipping sauce, transforming it into a drinkable broth - a pleasant end to the meal.

On the other hand, my friend's choice was the Sake Yuan Yaki, a disappointingly small portion given its $13.50 cost. He also tried the Ten Zaru Noodle Large for $27, which was a more substantial offering that included additional noodles and tempura compared to mine.

Despite the quantity that seemed ample at first glance, I was left feeling unsatisfied, my hunger not entirely quelled. Taste-wise, the meals were passable but failed to justify their prices. In summary, the experience was a mixed bag: cute ambiance, unique dining touches, but ultimately underwhelming in both portion size and flavor for the cost.

The pasta was pretty good. If you like al dente pasta, this is a spot for you. All the pasta dishes - the pasta had a bite to them. Service was rather slow here.
