We had to wait a bit between the appetizer and the meal. We also would have to solicit service for drink orders Cauliflower was all cut up into very small pieces unlike the photos on yelp. I wouldn't get it again for the price as it wasn't anything special. Tartare was decently sized and had good amount of fishThe octopus was cooked well - not too chewy and not too hard.

Wasn't a huge fan of this place. I think this was partially due to the fact that I'd seen a video of Joshua Tree on a social media platform, and they'd advertised all the games they had (eg, beer pong, pool) which you could play all day long. But when we got here, we walked in and saw that games were nowhere - a waitress told us they were downstairs, but they weren't open that day. But this was a Saturday afternoon and I expected this to be a popular time when people would come to play games! So that was pretty disappointing. The place also felt dirty since the floor was sticky. We all ordered drinks and appetizers - calamari and nachos. I couldn't eat the nachos but the calamari wasn't bad! It didn't taste super fresh but that's what I was expecting. I would just come here for the ambiance, lots of sports on TV and the lighting is nice for big groups.

When I'm in the mood for IHOP this is my go to location. There is usually never a wait, and most times you'll be seated right away. For the most part, it's never usually crowded. This location is 24 hours on the weekends, so it's perfect for a late night treat!

We had a great brunch on Sunday. Place was empty, but we couldn't get a booth as server said that all were booked. Ok.We ordered cace e pepe, kale salad and French toast. All was tasty. Service was good.Convenient location for us, so plan on coming back with reservations.

While wandering in the area with a friend, we stumbled upon this gem and were lured in by their $14 pre fixe lunch special. We indulged in fried spring rolls, a succulent pork belly vermicelli bowl, a savory pork belly sandwich, and a refreshing Thai iced tea. Each bite was a revelation, with the pork belly stealing the show with its tender and flavorful profile. This place delivers on taste and value, making it a must-visit again should our paths cross with this delightful area.

Title: A Weekend Brunch Turned Weekly Indulgence

I ventured into this restaurant one weekend for brunch and found myself delightfully surprised by the quinoa avocado spinach salad; the dressing was perfectly balanced, elevating the dish beyond its humble description. The spinach artichoke dip, served with a choice of pita or tortilla chips, was nothing short of phenomenal—a must-try appetizer in my book.

Captivated by the big screen's advertisement, I couldn't resist returning for their Wednesday wing night. I opted for the 20 wings deal, a mix of buffalo and BBQ. While most were delicious, a few wings did fall prey to overcooking, but that was a minor hiccup in an otherwise flavorful experience.

Unable to resist the siren call of the French onion soup, I took a gamble that paid off with a cheesy, satisfying pull. But the true star was the Mac n cheese over tater tots; an indulgent, carb-laden dream that I firmly believe everyone should treat themselves to at least once.

This restaurant turned a single visit into a series of cravings satisfied—one plate at a time.

I recently visited a capacious restaurant on a quiet Sunday afternoon that wasn't bustling with the usual lunch crowd. The establishment presents its menu family-style, with generous portions that are meant to be shared. We were three at the table, and the bread basket that arrived was ample, featuring a variety of breads that were tasty, though they might have been even more delightful if served warm.

For starters, the stuffed mushrooms were the standout dish – absolutely the highlight of our dining experience. We also shared a pasta dish amongst us, which was robust in flavor, although it tipped slightly towards the saltier side. This is a spot worth checking for those who appreciate a leisurely meal in a spacious setting with food intended for communal dining.

Straight forward and right to the point kind of place - But in a good way! - you order your ramen (food) you pick up at counter when ready and you have restaurant-like sitting to choose from. Very clean and very well organized.The food is YUMMY!!!! Comes with a side of gelato or tea (of course gelato for me please) especially after burning my tongue with a miso ramen - pork so tender and delicious it melted in my mouth - spicy? YES!!! Very - but I love spicy so it was right up my alley. They always have specials or discounts - it's a win win!

Title: A Birthday Celebration to Remember

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this gem of a restaurant for my mother's birthday, and the experience was nothing short of exceptional. From the moment we stepped in, the staff went above and beyond to ensure my mother felt celebrated, infusing warmth and personalized attention into every detail of our visit.

The meal commenced with delightful complimentary offerings from the chef, setting a high bar for what was to come. Our appetizers and main courses lived up to this promise, with the kitchen accommodating my vegetarian preferences without missing a beat. The flavors were exquisite, proving that fine dining and dietary restrictions can indeed go hand in hand.

But it was the dessert that truly stole the show—an otherworldly creation that had us savoring every bite. Its inventiveness and execution left an indelible mark on our taste buds.

I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to anyone in search of a fine dining experience that combines culinary excellence with heartfelt service. Whether it's a special occasion or a treat for the senses, this place is sure to impress.

Title: A Slice of Spain in SoHo - Boqueria Shines

My experience at The Boqueria in SoHo was a delightful escapade into Spanish cuisine, rivaling the tapas of Spain itself. Securing a reservation is a must, as its popularity is evident in the bustling atmosphere that persists throughout the evening.

Our host, Giselle, expertly recommended the Chef's Menu at $49, setting the stage for a culinary journey. The evening commenced with a bottle of effervescent Cava, leading into an appetizing spread of Serrano ham, Manchego cheese, grapes, an assortment of peppers, olives, and bread - a promising start.

The tapas soon followed, each pairing seamlessly with our Cava. From the bruschetta topped with a perfect egg, to the sweetness of dates wrapped in bacon, and onto the creamy mushroom and ham croquettes alongside shishito peppers - each bite was a testament to classic Spanish flavors.

The culinary crescendo peaked with savory lamb meatballs and a captivating Paella de Mariscos that married seafood with saffron-infused rice perfectly.

Dessert did not disappoint, with churros in both Nutella and chocolate - a decadent finish to an exquisite meal.

Service was impeccable, with dishes arriving in a symphony of timing. The gesture of a complimentary premium tapas coupon upon departure by Giselle was the cherry on top of an already fantastic evening.

Boqueria in SoHo has captured my palate and my heart; it is unquestionably a spot I'll be returning to, eager for another taste of Spain.

During a nostalgic visit to a spot my husband used to treasure in New York, we found ourselves dining near Times Square at a place soon to shutter its doors come January. In pursuit of times past, we opted for T-bone steaks, accompanied by garlic bread, baked potatoes, and salad. The meal was passable, though it didn't live up to my husband's cherished memories. The inside revealed a dated decor with a touch of neglect, which, in light of the imminent closure, suggested a fading rather than a flourish. It was a poignant reminder that some experiences are best left as sweet recollections.

Title: Stepping Back in Time for a Delightful Date Night

My wife and I recently enjoyed a splendid date night at a restaurant that may seem modest at first glance, but once inside, it transforms into a nostalgic New York City haven. The ambiance is rich with history, featuring beautiful woodwork, leather sofas, and evocative old photographs, truly reminiscent of old NYC.

The cocktail selection was impressive. I savored a robust Highland Park concoction, while my wife's mezcal-based cocktail was a perfect balance of refreshing and smoky – both expertly mixed.

For our main course, my wife chose the "86'd Burger," and it was nothing short of sensational. The combination of bone marrow and crispy shallots elevated the burger to an unprecedented level of flavor; it was sinfully delicious. Meanwhile, my Lamb Wellington, despite being tender and encased in a perfect crust, fell slightly short due to its overseasoning.

In conclusion, the restaurant offered a charming escape to a bygone era, complemented by a memorable meal. While my dish had room for improvement, the overall experience was exceptional. This unique spot comes highly recommended for anyone seeking to indulge in the historical vibe of NYC dining.

Upon visiting this local noodle establishment, the nuances between rice noodle quality became strikingly apparent. Unfortunately, the noodles I experienced were on the overly fresh side, causing them to disintegrate rather than allowing for a delightful forkful. This lack of firmness was a letdown, particularly when one seeks that perfect balance of silkiness with a hint of al dente resistance.

Additionally, while the quantity of shrimp tucked within my rice roll was generous, the freshness was underwhelming, which is unacceptable, especially considering the premium price point this restaurant commands – easily twice that of neighboring noodle spots. Given these factors, the overall quality failed to justify the cost, leaving much to be desired from the meal.

Love this Italian spot around the corner from us. It's not OMG I'VE GOTTA GO food, but when you're in the mood for something comforting, rich, with great sauces, fresh bread and a homey feel, come here. Came in at 6pm on a Saturday to no wait. You've gotta get the buttery, hot garlic bread and any pasta with their marinara sauce. We got the meatball spaghetti special which was great, but I'd forgo the meatballs next time - it didn't even need them! - and try the simpler penne alla Norma next.We also had their famed carbonara, but I'm not a fan. It tastes very "piggy" to me. Even the spaghetti without a piece of ham in it tastes like ham. Too much. Heard the desserts were just mediocre so skipped that and hopped over to City Cakes nearby on 18th Street for the greatest chocolate-chip cookie in New York.

This is one of the best brunches I've had in New York so far! The waffles were amazing- a perfect balance of the sweet cinnamon and zesty orange. I was also able to sneak a bite of my friend's amazing Mac and cheese which I totally regret not getting for myself. The staff was nice and we were seated for our reservation right away. They kept our glasses full throughout the meal and the food came out quickly. Highly recommend! (Bonus- in terms of New York pricing, this place wasn't so bad! Under $20 for my meal)

I recently visited this gem during restaurant week and had an exceptional culinary experience. The complimentary bread set a high bar, tantalizing my taste buds with its deliciousness. The beet hummus was a flavorful starter, laying the groundwork for the main courses. The salmon poke bowl and chicken kabob were masterfully prepared, offering a symphony of flavors with each bite. The lamb tagine was equally impressive, with its tender meat and rich, aromatic sauce.

While the main courses were a delight, the dessert, unfortunately, missed the mark. The flavors clashed, leaving a confusing aftertaste that did not complement the meal.

Despite the dessert hiccup, the overall experience was top-notch. The restaurant's decor added to the ambiance, making for a beautiful dining environment. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit to this exquisite establishment.

Title: A Flavorful Discovery near Broadway

My dining experience at this mid-town gem caught me pleasantly off-guard with its robust flavors. Stepping in at 5:30 PM on a sun-soaked Saturday, the eatery, despite its proximity to the theater district, was only a third full, possibly due to the allure of the first nice weekend in ages. By 7 PM, the place buzzed with more life, filling to about two-thirds capacity.

The staff showed a warm, accommodating spirit towards our party, which included a toddler, ensuring a smooth and enjoyable dining experience. Service was timely with appetizers arriving promptly and mains following suit.

Our table sampled an array of dishes:
- Agedashi Tofu: The crispness of the fried skin contrasted beautifully with the silky interior and tender eggplant.
- Kara-age Chicken: A delightful crunch and fresh-from-the-fryer heat.
- Gyoza: Standard fare with a satisfying crispy bottom.
- Calamari-age: A solid choice.
- Nippori Ramen: The coconut-soy broth offered an intriguing twist on typical ramen flavors.
- Garlic Ramen: The seasonal special was the unanimous highlight of the meal, with its tantalizing garlic sauce and perfectly paired toppings.
- Beef Gyuu Ramen: A comforting bowl, though somewhat reminiscent of a home-cooked meal.
- Tan Tan Ramen: The sesame-infused broth provided a fragrant and enjoyable experience.

The only drawback of our culinary venture was the saltiness of the ramen broths; a reduction by a third would let the natural flavors shine without compromising taste.

In summary, I would eagerly return for another round of the delightful ramen offerings, hopeful for a less heavy-handed salt approach.

I recently dined here during restaurant week, drawn by its proximity to the theater showing "The Book of Mormon." The restaurant offers a choice between their regular offering of 20 types of meat and the restaurant week menu, which includes 7. Opting for the latter, as the former seemed excessive, my experience was lackluster. The interior felt outdated, and the meats largely failed to impress—with the exception of the garlic steak, which was occasionally available in my preferred medium rare. Fortunately, the restaurant week pricing spared me the disappointment of feeling overcharged. Highlights included the excellent bread and tasty fried bananas, but the rest was forgettable. In hindsight, a steakhouse might suit those who prefer their steak cooked to specific preferences, though if it's variety you're after and you have an appetite for an extensive meat selection, this place may appeal to you.

Came for the gigantic cannoli, stayed for the bruschetta!A friend and I saw the massive cannoli recently and decided to plan a trip to NYC just for it. However, we decided that just dessert wouldn't cut it and ordered some small appetitzers. We chose the truffled honey and burrata bruschettas ($12 each) and a small charcuterie board ($22). Everything was soooo good - that truffled honey bruschetta was absolutely AMAZING.Now on to the cocoa cannoli, the piece de resistance. That thing is so monstrous that our server literally wished us luck when we dug in.It was $25, but oh-so-good! It's got 2 different fillings on either end, some hot chocolate in cookie shot cups, and a small brownie. There's also a crab mallet thing to smash it, y'know to facilitate the eating process.As great as the food and the service was, prices are a bit steep. However, I'd love to come back and try some other plates on the menu!Tl;dr: slightly high prices, yummy  bruschetta, yummy cannoli

Rip off for vegetarians and vegans . They serve generous amount of meat protein depending on what u order; salmon, chicken, turkey meat balls for $13-$14 however when you order a vegeterian bowl, which is basically potato patties and mushrooms they significantly reduce the size of your serving.Bowl with quinoa, greens and one lame piece of potato patty and few mushrooms..Like one single piece??Like seriously how much does one piece of mashed potato cost u guys over 3 pieces of turkey meat balls or one filet of salmon??I ordered an extra potato patty n landed up paying $15.50 for a single bowl.. don't get me even started on the taste... the patties were bland and undercooked, you get taste of half cooked potatoes with  every bite. The guy preparing my bowl was least interested in what add ons I wanted. He was itching to get done with me asap to attend the next meat eating customers. I'm saying this with conviction coz I have ordered meat bowls from this place before and have had good experiences. It's like they are intolerant to vegeterianism.What a downfall from being one of my favorite lunch places in fidi to me never wanting to visit it again.

Title: Hidden Gem with Room for Service Improvement

I finally visited this local taco spot on a friend's recommendation and kicked myself for not discovering it sooner. The exterior deceives with its modest appearance, but step inside, and you're greeted by a surprisingly spacious venue bathed in natural light from a grand skylight, creating an almost open-air dining experience.

The taco selection is a highlight, with street-style portions that encourage sampling multiple varieties. My choices included a perfectly crispy fish taco and a succulent carnitas taco, both bursting with authentic flavor. Paired with a classic side of rice and beans, it was a fulfilling meal.

While the ambiance impresses, the service left something to be desired. Despite our waitress's friendly demeanor, the odd requirement for our three distinct groups to order off a single menu card was cumbersome. Additionally, our attempts to order more or even settle the bill were met with delays, as our server seemed to vanish when needed.

If the restaurant could refine its service to match the quality of its fare, it would easily earn a five-star rating. For now, it remains a must-visit for taco enthusiasts who can navigate a little service stumble with patience.

Kenka in the East Village delivers a delightful dive into the vibrant atmosphere of a traditional Japanese izakaya. While it may not cater to those seeking an upscale dining experience, its charm lies in a different kind of appeal. With an extensive menu that promises an adventure through Japanese comfort food — think succulent yakitori, hearty ramens, and flavorful curries — there's a flavor for every palate.

The place buzzes with an energetic vibe, complemented by an impressive array of Japanese beers and sakes, all reasonably priced. Couples can revel in a full dining experience without breaking the bank, with a feast and drinks likely under $50. Service is swift, ensuring that even if there's a wait to get in, your hunger won't be prolonged.

However, note that the décor includes mature-themed artwork, which might not be suitable for a younger audience. If you're looking for a budget-friendly, fun night out with a dash of eclectic flair, Kenka is a top pick for a casual and rapid dining affair.

3.5/5I'll give credit where credit is due. The Tori Kurozu was slapping--taste-wise. The fried chicken was juicy, and the vegetables, ranging from eggplant to carrots to zucchini, all of which worked well with the sauce. My issue is that the portions are ridiculously small for the price. No rice or soup included, a mini salad, and only a few pieces of chicken. And guess what? It's $23 here, but $21 at Ootoya Chelsea. Additionally, maybe it's because my table was beside the door--which was so heavy I needed 2 hands to pry it open--but I felt quite cold in the restaurant and had to keep my jacket on the entire time.At least the food came fast, and the staff are a nice bunch, who seated me before my reservation time even though the other person hadn't arrived yet.

Title: A Dip in Culinary Standards But Service Remains Strong

As a frequent visitor to the city, I've often looked forward to dining at this establishment, recalling the excellent service and quality meals of the past. Regrettably, my latest experience fell short on the culinary front. The once-memorable burrito dinner seemed hastily prepared, possibly pre-made and reheated, as it arrived suspiciously fast—less than five minutes after ordering. Although the dish was served on a plate hot enough to suggest recent cooking, the meal itself lacked its former freshness and flair.

The accompanying chips and salsa were disappointing, with the chips tasting stale and the salsa resembling watery. The burrito, while adequate, did not live up to my past experiences; the ranchero sauce in particular had lost its homemade charm, hinting at a canned origin. The chicken inside the burrito was moderately seasoned but failed to elevate the overall bland taste.

Despite the disheartening food quality, the service maintained its impeccable standard, with attentive and swift staff that seemed to uphold the restaurant's reputation for excellence in hospitality. It's a true shame that the vibrant flavors I once savored here did not match the still outstanding service. Here's hoping for a return to form in the kitchen to match the high bar set by the front-of-house team.

Amazing restaurant! I fInally got to try it on a weeknight and yes I did wait around an hr and a half  to 2 hours, but the food and drinks made up for it. I mean the decor already was fabulous. The mango sunrise drink is sooooo good. The menu is thick but it's very cute with their logo on front. I got the panang curry and I tried their wings and calamari. All were really good. The friends I came with also thought the restaurant was beautiful and can't wait to go back!

Ichiran was fine. The service was great - very friendly employees - and I liked the small menu. Booths are also fun. Unfortunately, the ramen was just not that great, and it's definitely pricey. Don't think I'll be back.

Title: A Flavorful Feast at Empellón 

Dining at Empellón's Midtown location is always a treat, so we were eager to sample the fare at this other location – and it did not disappoint. A must-try for any visitor is the All Seven Salsas; the variety of spicy salsas sets the stage for an adventurous meal.

For entrees, we indulged in the Pork Tongue Tacos and the Carnitas plate, both of which were exceptional. The carnitas, in particular, was a standout – the meat was succulent and perfectly tender, easily pulling apart and pairing excellently with the provided tortillas. It's a generous dish meant to be shared, and it certainly was the star of our meal.

While we missed the Avocado dessert we've come to love at the Midtown outpost, we left the restaurant more than satisfied, and pleasantly surprised by the reasonable total bill. Empellón once again proved that it's not just about a single location, but a consistently delightful dining experience across the board.

Thai Market's lunch specials are a steal, running from 11:45 am to 3:30 pm at just $9.95 for an appetizer and a main course—a delight for those of us nearby.

I indulged in their Curry Puff and Pad Thai Noodle. The curry puff impressed with its flaky exterior and robust filling, and the accompanying sauce was a standout, enhancing every bite with its complex flavors. The Pad Thai, however, was a touch underwhelming. It lacked the depth of flavor I was hoping for, and although my boyfriend suggested it might've been an off day for the dish, it didn't quite hit the mark for me.

Nonetheless, considering the generous portions and wallet-friendly price, the experience offers solid value. With prompt service and satisfactory fare, Thai Market is worth another visit to explore more of their menu.

Came here on a Wednesday night for quick drinks with friends. Relatively easy to get a table around 6pm'ish. Drinks were on happy hour - they were making these apple cocktails for $8 which was absolutely delish. There are loads of other happy hour specials with food as well and it changes depending which day you go. Great selection of beers too! Check in into yelp to get free 5oz beer - small but better than nothing!

I recently had an opportunity to try out a midtown spot for pho, a place I stumbled upon after a recommendation from Robert Sietsema of Eater. Despite the nostalgia for the pho of my Maryland days, this restaurant provided a convenient and promising pre-game meal before heading to a Rangers matchup.

While the pho, specifically the Just Combination Pho, didn’t top my all-time list, it was a welcome discovery in the area. The establishment was buzzing with patrons upon my arrival, usually a good omen for any eatery. The service matched the vibrant atmosphere - attentive and efficient.

The meal took an unexpected turn when I inadvertently sampled all the varieties of their Nem, or spring rolls. Among the crab, pork, and veggie offerings, the veggie spring rolls stood out, elevated by its superior dipping sauce. The crab and pork versions, however, left me reaching for the jars of pickled garlic to inject additional zest into the flavors.

While this outing hasn't deterred me from exploring other Vietnamese haunts in NYC like Madame Vo, the hunt for the perfect bowl of Pho continues. Perhaps the local take on Ho Chi Minh style simply isn't to my taste.

(4.5 stars) Tucked away in the culinary mosaic of Hell's Kitchen, this unassuming Thai gem truly shines where it matters—flavor authenticity and quality ingredients. Their Pad See Ew is a masterclass in balance, each mouthful rich and savory without the greasiness often encountered elsewhere. Portion sizes hit the sweet spot for a satisfying lunch that doesn't overwhelm. The standout beef option, featuring actual steak cuts, elevates their offerings far above the standard fare, making lunchtime here an experience that's not to be missed.

I recently dined at Bassanova Ramen and was underwhelmed by the experience. The appetizers were a mixed bag; the fried chicken was decent but overpriced given its size, while both the dumplings and pork buns were disappointingly too salty and lacked sufficient meat.

Moving on to the main course, we tried their popular black pepper and lemon ramen and green curry ramen. Unfortunately, the wait for our ramen was excessively long at about 30 minutes, which dampened the overall experience. When considering the steep prices, it becomes difficult to justify the value of the meal.

Having tried other ramen spots in the city, I regret to say that Bassanova Ramen does not live up to the competition. It's unlikely I'll return for another meal.

Having eagerly ventured into one of the few local establishments specializing in distinct dishes, my experience was met with a blend of anticipation and mild disappointment. The Mount Qi beef noodles, amid high hopes, emerged as underwhelming with nondescript noodles and an unremarkable broth. Similarly, the hot sesame noodles fell short, lacking the depth of sesame and peanut flavor I'd expected, evoking a muted echo of spiceless dan dan noodles.

The Taiwanese stewed pork, while typical in its generous rice-to-topping ratio, didn't stand out. Yet, the stew pork burger offered a flavorful bite, just shy of perfection due to its need for additional sauce—a gap easily filled with a touch of chili sauce.

Amidst these middling impressions, the Sichuan-style dumplings shone through as the highlight: a delightful mix of spicy and sweet that danced on the palate. It is noteworthy, however, that this spot does not provide complimentary water, an omission that might stand out for some diners.

Title: A Feast for the Senses Without Breaking the Bank

After hearing numerous praises for this dining spot, I was eager to experience it for myself, and it certainly lived up to its reputation. The happy hour deal for two at $30 per person is a rare gem in NYC, offering incredible value. The meat was notably fresh, enhancing the joy of cooking it ourselves. Complementing the meal, the drinks were crafted to perfection. However, a word to the wise: arrive with an appetite. The generous portions ensure you leave feeling more than satisfied. A gastronomic delight that's kind to your wallet!

I don't give 5 stars to a restaurant that easily but this place was absolutely amazing. We were actually supposed to go to the ramen place nearby but because of long queue, we came here.The waitress was extremely gracious throughout our meal. Food was delicious!! Service was great. Chef came out for a break and had a little chat with many tables. Would definitely recommend this delightful place

Tator tots on FLEEK!The tots come packed with Bacon, Aged Cheddar & Chives, let me warn you however they pack a nice kick to them and these came out of the kitchen very hot almost burning the tongue. For me to give them five stars and almost causing me bodily harm you know they are out of this world!Ordered the Pastrami Reuben Spring rolls which were suprisely light and absolutely delciious accompanied with great sauces including a hot mustard sauce which will send you to the moon and back.Four chicken wings that were okay at 16 bucks I would pass on next time but the spot is a great find with a wide array of flavorful beers and a good vibe. There was a party going on while we were there relatively early on a Saturday around 1:30pm and they were definitely enjoying themselves. This is a great spot to come for a football game no doubt if you want to stray away from the typical bar food and want to class it up a notch.

Tried the vegan chicken bowl. It was very filling and flavorful but I don't think it paired well with brown rice - wish u could sub with couscous or quinoa. Overall nice options if you're tired of salads!

Delicious place! I came here for a dinner special, including a chicken samosa, beef dhanshak (described as a spicy Persian spinach/lentil dish), and mango ice cream for $17-loved it! The decor is festive, happy, and florescent. Perfect since with the door open it felt like an open-air restaurant!

I came here on Portale's first night open and you would have thought they had been open for months. On night one this place ran a tight ship and only continued to get better each visit. I've been here twice now just for drinks and finally ate dinner here on my third visit. The staff, the service, the drinks, and the food are all amazing. Portale does a great job of being a nice restaurant that is also welcoming.The staff treats everyone here so well and the bartenders are both fun and great at what they do. I've had vodka martinis, Old Fashioneds, several Don Verdes and after dinner drinks and have loved everything. Food wise I have had the Burrata and the Bistecca which were great. Others have ordered the Fritto Misto and the Spaghetti Ai Frutti Di Mare and loved those as well. I would highly recommend trying out Portale for both drinks at the bar and dinner. Personally I would sit at the bar to get the fun experience of chatting with the bartenders and watching them work their magic. I will definitely be back here for the Don Verdes and to try more items on the menu.

Title: A Second Helping of Excellence at The Boil

Review:

The Boil's new spot utterly matches the high bar set by its LES original, serving up the same stellar culinary delights in a more spacious setting. While my heart remains with the location where my love affair with The Boil began, it's hard to fault this venue's vibrant atmosphere.

Dining here is an experience, starting with the fun of donning bibs – a necessary accessory for the gloriously messy feast that awaits. Their 'Special Sauce' is a must-try, a thick concoction bursting with flavor that elevates their generous servings of top-tier seafood, especially their notably hefty shrimp.

Accompanying the feast-worthy combo bags, the soft shell crab appetizer is a textural delight, while the Cajun fries add a perfect spicy crunch. If you're expecting ordinary with their mac and cheese, think again – it's a comfort dish with a gourmet twist. Round off your sides with some extra corn and potatoes, and do not skip the papaya salad. It's a refreshing counterpoint with its unique, irresistible twist.

Set to the backdrop of classic Trap and Biggie, it's the kind of place where you'll lose track of time and simply revel in the good vibes. So go ahead and treat yourself to The Boil's latest venue – it's a decision you'll celebrate long after the last morsel. And when you do, you'll know who to thank.

Stepping into this East Village gem is like being whisked away to Greece, thanks to its exquisite decor and authentic ambiance. The culinary experience matches the setting, with Greek dishes that are, simply put, unparalleled. The Branzino evening special, flawlessly cooked and complemented by a zesty lemon herb sauce, is a revelation in flavor. The Horiatiki salad is the epitome of freshness and strikes a delightful balance in its ingredients. And the Tzatziki? It’s transformative - you haven’t truly experienced this classic until you’ve tasted theirs. Make sure to indulge in the Galaktobourekakia for dessert; it’s a must. For a spectacular Greek feast, this restaurant is a must-visit.

Taco Tuesday deal, $0.99 bottomless salsa, happy hour margaritas, and a nice casual vibe..what more do you need! Came with my gf on a Tuesday night and it was relatively full but no wait. We went for happy hour and the server told us they had $3/any taco all night on Tuesdays which was even better! We ordered: 2 Pacific Battered Fish, 2 Sriracha Shrimp, 2 Mango-jerked Chicken. They were out of the Al Pastor by 6:30pm so I didn't get to try it. Must be good though. The tacos came out fast. Shrimp wasn't as sriracha flavored as I expected it to be but I like my shrimp more light and clean tasting anyway. I've had better shrimp tacos but they do a not bad job. Liked the mango-jerk chicken! Margaritas were pretty standard..next time I visit I'll try the other flavors and try out all their tacos. We both were pretty full after having 3 tacos each. I'll definitely be back!

Very cute and trendy restaurant with great food to boot! My favorites were the eggplant carpaccio and the Jaffa souvlaki. I felt the portion sizes were quite big and we were recommended to order one dish too many for my party so perhaps order a little less than you think you need and order later if you are still hungry.

Viv has a pretty interesting and vibrant ambiance that makes it feel more like a lounge than a restaurant. There's a huge dragon on the ceiling that greats you as soon as you enter the restaurant, and it pretty much travels to the back of the restaurant. Plus, the restaurant gets pretty packed during the weekend adding to the lounge vibe. The food at Viv is fine if you are in the area, but I would not travel from another part of town just to dine here. It's more or less on par with the other multiple Thai places in Hell's Kitchen. If there is a wait for more than 30 min, I probably would check out another place rather than waiting around. Service was pretty good and efficient.

The most "Thailicious" food in the LES by far. Definitely date spot vibes with their attention to detail and design. They serve all your favorite fried rices to noodle dishes along with authentic entrees. The ribs were heavenly and the Pad See Ew is as good as it gets. Leave room for dessert and try their fried banana spring rolls. Expect this spot to get really popular come summer time when word spreads!

Good but not great NYC pizza. Decided to stop in with a friend on a random Sunday...place was empty. Waiter and chef spoke Italian...I mean off the boat broken English, Italian. Menu is simple...lets not over complicate things. Calzone - the smoked mozz and spicy salami were delicious...the actual dough was crispy and very hallow inside...I mean for the price you are charging, add some more ingredients.Pizza - small, pricey and dough was average. They are skimpy with the toppings. It's not the worse pizza I have had nor the best. They offer bottled beer and a limited wine list by the glass, I really wanted to love this place but it's average. With so many great options, doubt I would return here...

Heading to Food Gallery is like a nostalgic trip back to the high school cafeteria minus the dread. Among its plethora of Korean culinary offerings, tucked away behind a staircase on the first floor, you’ll find Noona Noodles. This hidden gem serves up an array of noodles that can only be described as a delightful overload.

On my visit, the choice was the Jjampong noodle—a fiery seafood concoction. The payment process was seamless with a credit card, and I was handed a beeper to alert me when the dish was ready. Despite a momentary delay caused by an indecisive customer, the server's patience and cheerfulness shone through, adding a positive note to the experience.

The Jjampong portion was astonishingly generous. Imagine a bowl so large it could rival the span of your arm from elbow to wrist. It’s a feast for the eyes and stomach, generously topped with head-on shrimps, clams, mussels, and more. The flavors lived up to the memories of my Korea trip, transporting my taste buds back with every spoonful.

Priced at $11.99, this dish is a steal, either for sharing between two or for satisfying the hunger of a solo diner with a formidable appetite. Noona Noodles earns a glowing recommendation from me, and the Jjampong has set a high bar for the other noodle dishes, which I am eager to return and explore.

I went on a weekday morning and didn't have to wait.  Apparently there's usually a line starting around 11am. It's eat-in only, no take-out which kind of sucks that they're turning away a huge base of customers. I had the cha siu rice roll which I thought was pretty good.  The rice roll is thin and silky smooth.  There's nice chunks of thinly sliced tender cha siu which is quite satisfying.  I like how the rice roll is all drenched in soy sauce which was just the right amount of flavor, not too salty/sweet.  The rice roll is definitely better quality than a lot of the chinatown places, but is it worth almost twice the price?  I'm not so sure about that. This won't be my go-to place but I'll come back to indulge myself once in a while.  I hope they do take-out soon!

Meh, I think there is much better Chinese food around. First of all, the service is laughably rude. They literally roll their eyes or walk away as you're talking with them. Second, the food wasn't great: the half-duck was mainly skin and bones, and the actual meat was lukewarm. We had to ask them to warm it up. The bok choy was so oily. And the beef stew was mainly cartilage and very little actual beef. And third, the seating is so tight and uncomfortable. I'd skip and find another spot.

only okay curry (butter chicken). their garlic naan is good. we initially ordered 2 butter chicken curry, but the waiter only put an order for 1. we asked for another curry, but he only brought 1 curry with no rice... and told us to share the rice we got already. ummm that's not how it works man. Also their drinks are meh... drinks came with a silver foil on top and waiter did not even know what it was. he said ummm maybe sweet stuff.. huh? it looks like a gum cover. waiter was not attentive. I had a good experience a few years ago, but I am not sure if i will be back.

Title: A Whimsical Evening at The Maze

Last night, my girlfriends and I finally experienced The Maze, a spot I've had my eye on for a while. I'd booked us a table for our get-together dinner two weeks in advance, but upon arrival, we found the initial seating uncomfortable. Thankfully, the accommodating staff promptly moved us to a more agreeable table.

We arrived just in time for Happy Hour, which offers a delightful price drop on various items and is a steal for early birds. Although we had to endure the minor inconvenience of a snug elevator ride to the third floor, it was well worth it once we began to explore their menu.

The gastronomic journey kicked off with Fried Calamari, a standard fare that was decent but didn't dazzle. The Maze Chicken Wings, which promised a burst of soy garlic flavor, fell short of our expectations, unable to dethrone my local favorite KFC.

However, the Kimchi Cream Pasta proved to be a slurp-worthy delight, requiring some skill to enjoy without any wardrobe casualties. The Mussel Clam Bisque was a hit, even for a meat lover like myself, though the stinginess with the accompanying baguette and the steep charge for extra bread left a slight dent in the experience.

The Bulgogi Dupbap was the star of the show, impressing us with its savory depth and leaving me eager to return and delve further into the menu.

An unexpected twist to the evening was the appearance of a promoter offering prizes for an alcohol brand. While we weren't imbibing and had to settle for facial masks rather than the more exciting rewards going to the boozier tables, it was a fun addition to our night.

In summary, while some dishes were hit-and-miss, The Maze holds promise. With its quirky charm and Happy Hour incentives (be sure to catch it before it ends at 7 pm!), it's a venue that warrants a second visit. The Maze has certainly left its mark on us, and I'm looking forward to my next culinary adventure here.

Try: Tonkotsu Chashu Pork Ramen and Crispy Fried Meatballs!Why: Tonkotsu Chashu Pork Ramen was really good and full of flavor. The pork was large and fatty. Variety of veggies adding some crunch, texture, and flavor in each bite. Yes, I enjoyed all the soup to the bottom of the bowl! The Crispy Fried Meatballs were a great appetizer. It has pork, water chestnut, ginger and scallions, and you dip it in a sweet & sour sauce. Notes: I ordered Delivery and everything was packed well. I enjoyed a Ramune (Japanese soda) with the meal. I also tried the one piece of the Sweet Buns for dessert and it was good, but I was too full to really enjoy. I'd like to try their other Ramen, Banmen, Dalumen, and Purple Yam Pies next time!

This is one of my proud yelp moments. Found this gem on yelp, blindly trusted it, LOVED it, going back soon.1. Their live wait option is fantastic. We also got lucky and did not have to wait because they had a bar seat ready. 2. Bar tender was v pleasant. I ordered a lycheetini which was pure yumminess in a fancy glass. 3. The decor is so ornate and beautiful you want to wait next time to get one of the cute booths. It's cosy, not too large, and very decorative (including the restroom basins)4. We got the fried chicken in pandan leaves for appetizers. Very tender chicken nicely marinated and fried. Came with a thick sauce that went well.5. My basil eggplant lemongrass onions and peppers with crispy duck was absolutely delicious. I want to reorder when I'm there next time but I'm intrigued how other stuff on their menu is too. Do order their green chili in some vinegary thing. You will not regret :) Overall, great experience.

The bar tender Danny was awesome! He kept conversation going and kept the bat running! He told us about some interesting things places here in NY and was an awesome bar tender! Really enjoyed sitting here drinking at this local bar down the street from our hotel The Pearl! The signature drink was Raspbreeze very good! Had a great time here!

On a leisurely summer Saturday, Dan and I were in search of a casual dining spot and stumbled upon a delightful restaurant with inviting outdoor seating. The weather was ideal for enjoying margaritas under the sun, which we eagerly did. To complement our drinks, we opted for the cheesy nachos and they did not disappoint - absolutely delicious!

Title: Contemporary Charm with Room for Culinary Improvement

Located on the bustling second floor in Koreatown, this modern establishment buzzes with energy, particularly on a Friday night. Despite the crowd, the seating process was prompt—a welcome start to the evening.

Our culinary journey began with Seolleong Tang, which, while traditional in essence, was unfortunately lackluster in taste, necessitating a request for seasonings to enhance its flavor profile. The Spicy Samgyupsal fared better; the meat was enjoyable, yet it fell short of justifying the steep price point.

What the restaurant lacked in flavor, it made up for somewhat in service. The waitstaff were genuinely cordial, and the attentive manager shone with his efforts to ensure our comfort—a redeeming aspect of our dining experience.

I recently had the pleasure of brunching at B2 and I'm already planning my next visit. The mimosas? Absolutely perfect. The ambiance is just as delightful – cozy and inviting. But the real star is the food, with each dish artfully presented, turning a meal into an experience. Don't pass up on the catfish appetizer; it's a must-try. B2 has risen splendidly from the legacy of Billie's Black, and it's now a spot I'll frequent without hesitation. A truly gratifying discovery for anyone who appreciates culinary artistry combined with a warm atmosphere.

A new welcome to the dimsum restaurants in Chiantown. The dimsum is freshly made, hot and served to your table - instead of being carted around. One of my favorite dishes there is their Japanese tofu with mushrooms (vegetarian friendly!)The best part, is Julia herself! Very sweet and personable, extremely accommodating to make sure you have the best experience possible. Definitely recommend if you're in the area!

Title: Contemporary Vibes with a Side of Disappointing Service

I recently dined at this spot, and while the food earned a solid four stars for its tastiness, the service lagged behind at three stars. The restaurant's contemporary design offers a comfortable dining experience, coupled with acoustics that pleasantly surprised me, allowing for easy conversation. 

Cocktail enthusiasts might find the list a bit too concise; however, what they lack in variety they make up for in presentation and flavor. Be prepared to pay a premium for your meal, as the prices are a touch steep for the portions provided.

The downside of the experience was the service. Attention from our server seemed scarce, only arriving at our table when we managed to catch their eye—definitely an area in need of improvement.

Overall, a spot worth trying for the food and ambiance, but set your expectations accordingly for the service.

Barnacho met expectations. Reasonable pricing, decent options and tasty food. They even have a handful of tables for outdoor seating.One of the employees was pouring a chemical product into the street, which was not a pleasurable dining smell. No complaints about the house margarita or veggie quesadilla. The squash inside seemed fresh and the portion was big. The chips and salsa was a nice touch, although I haven't had similar salads before and can't really describe it. This wouldn't be a five star place, but had four star potential as a neighborhood Mexican joint.

Title: Charming Hudson River Experience at North River Lobster Company

Tucked away on the Hudson River, North River Lobster Company is a delightful little gem that offers a unique dining experience in New York City. Although it's lost a bit of its local allure since introducing a $10 entry fee, the concept remains charming—enjoy a serene boat ride for about an hour while mingling with friends.

The setting is particularly enjoyable for those over 21, thanks to a happy hour special that complements the scenic backdrop nicely. Onboard, the menu features seafood staples like savory lobster rolls, comforting mac and cheese, and classic fish and chips, alongside a selection of small plates. While the food doesn't necessarily steal the show, it's the tranquility of gliding on the Hudson that truly defines the outing.

It’s a refreshing change of pace from the usual city buzz, with the rare sight of kayakers dotting the river adding to the picturesque environment. It's worth noting that the boat docks hourly, making it quite convenient to plan a visit as part of a broader exploration of the area, perhaps including a stop at the nearby Vessel.

In conclusion, if you're in the vicinity, the North River Lobster Company is certainly worth a visit, especially during the balmy summer months for a touch of nautical novelty in the heart of the city.

Title: A Fiery Delight at Silky Kitchen

If you're in the mood for a meal that packs a punch, Silky Kitchen is the place to be. The service is commendably swift and the staff exudes friendliness. I decided to try their Hunan Beef coupled with dry mix noodles, elevating it with an extra coddled egg, and opted for a medium spice level.

Be warned, their Hunan spice is a force to be reckoned with. Each bite delivers an intense heat that even a seasoned spice aficionado might find challenging – I found myself reaching for my water glass more than four times! Despite the fire, the dish was undeniably delectable. The noodles were expertly prepared, the beef was succulent, and the egg added a delicate richness to the fiery symphony of flavors.

In summary, Silky Kitchen delivers on its promise of authenticity and taste. Just be sure to brace yourself if you dare to venture into the spicier side of their menu – it's a true testament to Hunan cuisine's bold character.

What a wonderful find in the flatiron district. Laut Singapore is a sister restaurant to Laut in the Union Square/borderline flatiron area - they're just a few blocks away from each other. Owner/chef Salil brings his A game from the kitchen to your table. We enjoyed four of the savory dishes recommended by our server:Salty Egg Prawns: crispy jumbo prawns in salted duck egg sauce infused with curry leaves and egg floss. This dish is luxurious and so tasty. It comes with 4 pieces and is adorned with a large flat (and edible) shrimp chip. Calamari Singapura: crispy rice, sambal, curry leaves cooked to perfection. This dish is basically a fried calamari dish with a spicy chili sauce (as opposed to sweet chili sauce) and topped with a aromatic mix of crispy rice puffs and herbs.Nasi Goreng: Shrimp sambal umami rice - this is a fried rice with shrimp paste dish topped with a fried egg. We stuck with the seafood theme and got this with shrimp.Singapore Chili Crab: Crab cooked in signature sweet and spicy chili sauce and velvety egg, served with Chinese bun. We opted for the Dungeness crab and steamed buns. The dish arrives to the table partially cracked with the top shell removed but assembled on the dish for display. You'll get claw crackers and hand wipes to get dirty and enjoy the meat. The steamed buns were great for dipping into the signature sauce. For an additional cost, you can get additional buns. For desserts, we tried the Tisu, which is a crispy roti tower served with condensed milk. You can crush or rip the top of the roti. Basically you want to break it down to get to the ice cream (thai tea flavor) inside at the base of the tower. We also tried the kaya dessert, which is a pandan coconut jam served atop sticky rice. Other desserts we tried whose names I don't know include: a nut-filled roti pancake served with condensed milk on the side for dipping; plus another filling stuffed crepe whose shell is crunchy and is served with ice cream.The interior setting here is beautiful. You walk in to see a beautiful mural on the side wall and teal upholstered seats and tufted benches along the brick wall in the back. The bar is eye-catching as well with the red lighting and gold chandeliers. My favorite bites here are from the savory section of the menu. There seems to be treasure hidden in the kitchen and I'be only discovered a sliver. A lot is offered here that pulls from the cuisines of Southeast Asia but, at least from my first visit with the four dishes, the food is executed well and transports you to Singapore. Experience its cuisine with influences you might recognize from China, Indonesia, and Malaysia. Learn and appreciate how to eat these dishes and you'll understand a little more about its culture. What a wonderful addition to the Asian food scene in Manhattan!
Love this placeOyster HHDRINK HHAPPETIZER HHFood, staff, people, and the bartenders!!!

I think Famous Ben's Pizza has seen better days..  the pizza is pretty good, large, New York style slices..  but the place is kinda dirty, the tables are always dirty. I just wish they'd keep the dining area cleaner..
Had a japchae today and well while it was good i found it very expensive. $20+tax... I feel this is a better place for lunch specials

Title: A Taste of LA's Tatsu in NYC's East Village

Tatsu Ramen has successfully transported its LA charm to the bustling streets of the East Village, making it a must-visit for any ramen enthusiast. As a connoisseur of NYC's ramen scene, having sampled over 30 different shops, I can confidently place Tatsu's BOLD ramen at the pinnacle of my preferences.

On a serene Saturday evening at 5:30 PM, my brother and I found ourselves comfortably seated without delay. The spacious interior, a notable improvement from its LA counterpart, offers a variety of seating arrangements from counter tops to bar seating.

Ordering via iPads enhances the experience, mirroring the modernity of Sawtelle Blvd yet keeping the cozy authenticity of Tatsu's. The ability to grab unlimited nori and garlic is a welcomed carryover, and while customization isn't as intricate as some competitors, the essentials are all there—from protein choices to scallion portions.

The standout is undoubtedly the Tonkotsu broth: a rich, silky concoction that perfectly enlaces the noodles, which carry just the right amount of spice. The three succulent pieces of chasiu and flawlessly runny soft-boiled egg complete the masterpiece. The Cheeky ramen, with its exemplary chicken-based broth, doesn't fall far behind, marking another favorite in my book.

In summary, whether you're reminiscing about LA's Tatsu or discovering it anew, this East Village gem earns a hearty recommendation for a soul-satisfying ramen journey.

Title: Yet Another Delightful Dinner at The Rag Trader

I recently enjoyed my third visit to The Rag Trader, and it continues to impress. The cauliflower fritters stand out as an essential start to the meal; served in a perfectly portioned set of six, they were ideal for our group of six to share.

The service was outstanding, contributing to the overall enjoyable experience. Each of us savored our individual dishes, with the consensus firmly landing on an all-around culinary triumph.

While the evening was a success, we found the Bo Peep lounge downstairs a bit too popular for our taste, making the post-dinner drink plan a challenge due to the crowded and noisy environment.

Nevertheless, the superb dinner experience, combined with the restaurant's convenience to Penn Station and other subway lines, solidified The Rag Trader as a reliable choice for an excellent meal in the city.

Came here on Thurs night with 2 friends--we had a 7pm reservation and boy was it PACKED! I guess a lot of people were there already for happy hour (which sadly we missed) and with the tables so close together it felt a bit claustrophobic. Very noisy, so it was hard to catch up, and we were all rather hoarse by the time we left. However, it is a very cute space--all the decor and the little lights made the space cheery & cozy. Our waiter was friendly and happily answered our questions/recommendation requests. We all enjoyed our drinks--I had the "Revolucion" and my friends both got the "Opium" cocktail. Apps--we got free yucca fries with Yelp check-in (thanks Yelp!) which were good though we didn't like the accompanying sauces; we also got the "Cuban spring rolls" (tasty but very small portion) and the ceviche. The ceviche (a dish I generally love) I have to say was the worst I've ever tasted; you couldn't taste any citrus and it was full of cilantro (blech) and the seafood just tasted off. I could only take a bite of that. Luckily our entrees were good. I had the popular Lechon Asada fried rice (which was tasty though the pork was a bit dry) but my friends both got the black rice seafood paella which the waiter recommended, and when I tasted a bit of that I wish I got that as well! The black rice even had a nice creaminess to it and they got a good quantity of mussels & shrimp. They both enjoyed it, and portion size was good so we all had to take food home. When we split the bill it was a bit over $60 each before tax & tip, so not exactly cheap but not too terrible. Overall a good experience and I would go back. Maybe sometime I can make it there in time for happy hour!

Discovering an authentic Ramen spot in my old stomping grounds of Washington Heights, Manhattan, has been a delightful surprise. Despite its modest size, the restaurant boasts a welcoming mix of indoor, bar-side, and outdoor seating. My choice of ginger beef ramen, paired with an iced Matcha tea, proved to be an exquisite meal. The broth's richness and the harmonious blend of ingredients were noteworthy, even though the ginger was overpowering for my taste. Nevertheless, I relished every spoonful, leaving my bowl spotless. The cozy ambiance and the lively scene of cooks crafting ramen only enhanced the dining experience. I'm already looking forward to my next visit when I'm back in New York.

I gave this place three stars b/c it's not a classic NY pizza place as far as taste.  It however makes up for being a quiet spot in the middle of manhattan to sit down when u don't feel like searching for another spot and just to relax and enjoy your food. Pros - nice specials (see pics) $2 slice of cheese pizza. This is a place for a quick bite to eat spot and to take a quick seat before your on the go again.  This place has about 7 stools it's small but that's more than enough seats unless it's super busy. The pizza was nice and cheesy. The place is super quiet and peaceful given it's 3pm on a sunny spring day in NY. Cons- although the pizza is cheesy this is not your classic NY slice as the ratio or sauce and cheese is not accurate. You can not taste the sauce, it's more cheese and bread.

My husband and I recently decided to try a new burger joint in our neighborhood, looking forward to exploring more local dining options. Sadly, the experience proved to be disappointing with service inconsistencies apparent from the outset. Upon our 6pm arrival, it seemed under-staffed with only two workers present, and one of them was being trained.

The food itself was underwhelming. We ordered the "Envy" and "Temptation" burgers along with chicken & waffles, expecting freshly cooked and hot meals. Instead, we received lukewarm dishes; the burgers were disproportionately small and soaked in condiments, resulting in a soggy texture rather than the intended messiness. The chicken lacked any seasoning, not even a sprinkle of salt, and the waffles were a mix of overdone on top and undercooked and soggy on the bottom.

Hygiene was also a concern, as we observed an untrained staff member handle our fries with bare hands after dropping them. Thankfully, we chose to dine in rather than take out, heeding the advice of a fellow customer, which saved us from what would likely have been an even soggier meal. Overall, the visit was far from the culinary adventure we hoped for and does not inspire a return visit.

Wild Shroom wrapBadge dumplings Spicy Mang rollSweet Tree rollFlower Top dumplings Cucumber-mint lemonadeBlueberry lemonade CHEFs Cookie Almuerzo picante.. this is my next submission to answering the ultimate question....42 is already taken....and I must admit a repeat of the "spicy Mang"  it goes everywhere with everything....today the perfect level of spice that gives accent to the food without stealing the flavor....wow!Also ...the spicy sauce from the "fun-guy" dumplings etc... goes  GREAT with with flower top dumplings...(my opinion only)...we ordered a side and oooo sooo goood!I must close with the Chefs Cookie....ordered it twice in two days....I believe it may be my "42."

Last night's impromptu dinner at this newly opened gem did not disappoint. After falling in love with Gaijin, I was eager to experience this sister establishment, and it lived up to my high expectations. Opting for the omakase at $180 per person felt entirely reasonable given the exceptional quality and flavor profiles that tantalized my palate. While my enjoyment was somewhat hampered by allergies, the attentive service ensured I could still savor each offering. This spot definitely merits a recommendation, and I'm counting down the days until I can return at full health for the complete experience.

After being enticed by an Eater video to visit Factory Tamal, I'm pleased to report that the experience lived up to the hype. The tamales were of outstanding quality, each one bursting with flavor. The store itself exuded charm with its cozy size, limited but welcoming seating, and vibrant decor that contributed to an enjoyable atmosphere.

Out of the three tamales we sampled, the bacon + cheese tamale was a standout – a deliciously memorable combination that has me eagerly planning my next visit. And while I didn't get a chance to try the mole this time, it's certainly on my list for when I return. Factory Tamal has more to explore, and I am looking forward to indulging in more items from their delightful menu.

I recently discovered an absolute gem of a restaurant that excels in serving up delicious buns. The variety on offer is commendable, ensuring that there's something for every palate. Even more impressive are the reasonable prices, making this spot a must-visit for anyone in search of quality food that won't break the bank. Highly recommended!

Small cozy little restaurant with only about 10 tables. Probably not the best place for groups or if you are claustrophobic. You are pretty much dining with the person next to you but it is nyc and that is kind of normal. We came for lunch and noticed that the lunch special is a good price. When you order be read because the food comes out fast. The appetizer and lunch meal came out at the same time.  You get a small appetizer and a main meal. I got a spring roll and the chicken pad thai. I thought the pad thai was a little bland but I did eat it all.  If you are in need of a quick lunch at a good price come here. This isn't top level food but it does the job. 3 star all the way.

This is the best burger place ever. whenever I'm in NYC, I go... at least once. And maybe twice, even if I'm only there for a few days. - I always build my own turkey burger with a sprouted bun, avocado, caramelized onion, and mushrooms. Sometimes I add other veggies. There's so many options, definitely something for everyone.They also have an entire vegan menu with multiple patty options (impossible AND beyond meat as well as others like sweet potato, black bean, and quinoa patties).- The Brussels sprouts are AMAZING!!! They are so crispy, oily, and the vegan cheese is amazing. Adds a perfect saltiness as well. These are outstanding - a must. - Sweet potato fries are just average. Skip them. Not quite crisp enough, We found them to be a bit soggy.- DO NOT SKIP THE VEGAN MILKSHAKES!!! Star of the dinner. I have tried the velvis (a peanut butter, chocolate, and banana concoction) and a chocolate mint one. Both were amazing, but I preferred the pb chocolate one. They are so thick and creamy and very decadent. we always split them but I could probably finish one myself. Please open a location in chicago!!! Love love love bare burger because the burgers are insanely well-cooked, organic, great ingredients, high-quality, and flexible for different diets!!!

Pre show dinner at this cute little chic cave in the basement reminds me of an old speak Easy. Waiters and staff very professional and helpful. Food just didn't hold up to the rest of the restaurant   Had the burratta special and it was just ok. Cheese wasn't that good and the arugula salad they had on side wasn't dressed. They say there pizza is Great but wow what a disappointment. I ordered veal saltimbocca veal was tender but tiny and sauce way over salted. Side of mash potatoes that reminded me of the potato u get in a TV dinner.  We also had the chicken piccata which was a good dish but tiny with the same potatoes.  Also ordered orechietti with sausage and always wIth broccoli rabe but it came out with steamed no taste broccoli.  Tried the chocolate cake and it was good.  All In all its a cute fun little place for pre theater dinner just be careful what you order. Prices not bad.

I had the pleasure of stumbling upon the Cousins Maine Lobster truck in Astoria and it was an incredible find. Their lobster roll was a delight, generously stuffed with succulent lobster, and enclosed in a perfectly delicious bun. My son sampled the lobster grilled cheese and gave it his seal of approval for its tastiness. The menu is a treasure trove of comforting favorites, all enhanced with lobster's luxurious touch. I'm eager to reunite with this culinary gem soon!

The atmosphere was great and the burger was legit.We came in on a Sunday evening and were able to get a table for 3 right away. Our waitress was a little slow, but otherwise the experience was good. I am always swayed by ambiance, and this place was lovely. I think in general Restoration Hardware with it's comfy couches and bar would be an excellent date spot.The menu is not extensive, so I picked from the options available. I had heard good things about the burger.  Yes the burger was expensive. I've had au cheval (both here in NYC and in Chicago) and the burger here is legit. It was moist and flavorful. Fries were good but I wish just a little more crispy. And the food came out just as fast as the drinks somehow! Impressive!This place delivered what I was expecting and I will come back!

When it comes to pho, sometimes I just want a satisfying warm bowl with all the essentials - without all the unnecessary extra frills a lot of NYC joints provide as an excuse for an upcharge. (I'm thinking of those over-priced hipster joints in East Village where a bowl of pho costs $16-25)After trying out a dozen places in NYC, I think I have finally found a good pho hole-in-the-wall! It's so refreshing to see prices below $12 for once!!! Very reasonable, given the central location. They specialize in Hanoi-style pho. Reviewers who say this is not traditional/authentic pho should go on a cultural journey (or even just wikipedia) and learn that there are many regions in Vietnam with their own region-specific styles of food.Taste-wise it was good! Maybe not Southern California-level good, but I've been so sick of overpaying for pho in NYC that this is a much-needed addition to my rotation of pho spots.Note #1: I LOVE the wide pho rice noodles!! You have no idea how long I've waited to find a pho restaurant that serves these (the thinner ones are more widely used because they cook faster). I am discombobulated by how some of the reviewers are objecting so strongly to these noodles. Note #2: It seems like the owner has reached out to some reviewers on here in an aggressive manner (I personally have not had this issue) - to me it seems like there is a cultural disconnect, but I would strongly recommend that the owner do not engage reviewers that way and just focus on delivering good food - then the reviews will speak for themselves, and people will gradually become more familiar with this style of pho that has been around longer than the Saigon style which is widespread in the US.Note #3: I just came in again on 11/17. The noodles were fresher and the spring rolls crispier (albeit smaller). However, the broth was notably watered down (which was not the case on my prior visit), and the service was not as good. I guess this place can be a hit or miss!

Title: A Brunch Affair to Remember

I recently visited a charming brunch spot with a delightful French flair. Their brasserie-style menu is a dream for any Francophile, brimming with classics like crepes, omelets, French toast, and divine oeufs preparations. The salmon and goat cheese omelet I ordered was nothing short of luscious – perfectly cooked, fluffy, and packed with flavor. Moreover, when I requested a side of bacon, I was pleasantly surprised to receive a generous bowl full – a true highlight for bacon lovers!

Across the table, the beet salad caught my eye, especially after adding goat cheese. It's a fresh option for those seeking something lighter. My daughter's enjoyment of her crepes confirmed that this isn't just an adult's paradise; it's a place for all ages.

The restaurant exudes a welcoming ambiance, complemented by attentive service that makes you feel at home. Overall, it's hard to fault this delightful establishment. I highly recommend checking it out for a brunch experience that satisfies on all fronts.

After an exhaustive 9-mile trek through the city, my weary feet and I found respite with a spontaneous visit to NB Wing Wong, a spot I remembered for its crispy duck from a previous year's quest. This time, my appetite guided me, and I opted for a swift culinary pick-me-up. Service was prompt—within a mere 10 minutes, a feast of succulent shrimp and pork dumplings, accompanied by a flavorful shrimp fried rice, was before me. The meal was hastily devoured, a testament to its delightful taste and the urgency of my hunger. In brief, NB Wing Wong delivered quick and satisfying nourishment, hitting the spot perfectly.

So good! Ordered in and got the babaganoush (comes with warm bread) and the shepherds salad, and they even gave us a free rice pudding with a smiley face on the container. So sweet! Everything was delicious. The babaganoush is thick and so well balanced and hearty, especially when you dip the huge slabs of fresh bread in it. The shepherds salad was huge, even when I got a size small, so be prepared to have a lot that might be leftover. The rice pudding is indulgent and so good, slightly baked on the top. 5 stars!!!!

Wow!!! I absolutely love this place!  The Petrossian Boutique is located at 911 7th Avenue and features Petrossian's renowned caviar, foie gras, and smoked fish. They also offer pastries and tarts. They also have table service for breakfast, lunch or a quick bite. It's a shame their restaurant next door closed--they had the most decadent and opulent interior and incredible food!  The building that houses (and housed) their 2 locations is s Rococco-gone-wild building that has to be seen to be believed.

I recently visited a tapas restaurant where the set menu offering included a bottle of wine and four tapas choices—it did not disappoint. The service was impressively swift and attentive, especially our waitress, whose proactive approach to keeping our glasses full displayed a commitment to hospitality that I deeply appreciated.

The culinary experience was nothing short of exquisite. Our selections comprised the flavorful Filet Mignon Tataki, the substantial Super White Tuna Tataki, wonderfully spiced Spicy Crab and Tuna Tacos, and a unique Cucumber Rainbow Sashimi Roll. Additionally, we indulged in the renowned tri-meatball selection, which was outstanding—potentially threatening to fast-food chains with their sheer quality.

Despite the high praises, I have to note a few details that kept the meal from perfection. The Filet Mignon Tataki could have benefitted from a thicker cut, the Spicy Crab Taco's garnish slightly overpowered the main ingredient, and the Cucumber Rainbow Roll, while inventive, lacked the structural integrity that makes traditional rolls so satisfying.

Overall, the meal was fulfilling and the restaurant's quality to value ratio is commendable. I would heartily recommend it to anyone in search of a top-notch tapas experience without any cuisine-specific limitation. The service alone could persuade me to return. The only reason I withhold a perfect score is due to the few tweaks that could elevate the dining experience even further. A solid 4 stars from me.

What a magnificent place! We came for drinks only before heading to dinner but this would be a fabulous location for bites, dinner or tea. The bar area is wonderful, beautiful and smells amazing. Our server was fantastic and friendly. Of course this is NYC and the Plaza after all, so everything is expensive. But still worth it!They have a beautiful wine and cocktail list. I opted for the Hemingway daiquiri and it was delicious and refreshing. Loved it!

I've been here twice with my family and loved it both times! Their pizza is amazing but pricey- a staggering $15.95-16.95 for a personal sized pie but worth every bite. They have one of the best pizzas I've ever tasted. The crust and dough have a nice bite and crisp to it. The sauce is delicious and plentiful. The cheese is generous and melty and ooey-gooey. I've tried their cannoli which has a crisp shell that cracks and breaks upon bite. It tastes fresh and pairs well with their cannoli cream which is rich and decadent. My favorite dessert there is the mixed berry tart though. It's layers of raspberries, red berries with cream and a crust. They always give you bread which is hot and crunchy. The service is good and friendly. I always make an extra effort to come here whenever I'm in Little Italy!

Honestly I had very high expectations after hearing from friends that Jongro had really good KBBQ, but in my opinion it was overpriced and tiny portions. I would much rather go to a place that has All-you-can-eat. The meat quality was good, but nothing spectacular. One thing I did like a lot was the decorations inside which looked like a little village.

UES thai spot with lunch special 7 days a week! Restaurant has a rustic feel - wooden walls, vines, and stained glass lanterns from the ceiling. You feel hidden from the city once you walk in. We came in on a Sunday at noon and we did not have to wait but a line had started to form. $11 lunch special which includes appetizer and a main course from a limited menu. I went with the steamed dumplings (shu mai) and chicken pad kee mao. I like how they have duck here for only $2 more - maybe I will try next time.Food came out quickly and was nicely presented on huge white plates. Good portions. I appreciated how many vegetables there were and that it was not just mostly noodles with a couple pieces of meat.Service was not super quick but understandable as it was a packed restaurant at that time. Great quality thai food for an unbeatable price.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Busan Delights at [Restaurant Name]

During a recent lunch at [Restaurant Name], my companions and I embarked on a culinary adventure, sampling a variety of appetizers that brought the flavors of Busan to our table. The standout was undoubtedly the Galbi Dumpling, plump and brimming with succulent short rib, perfectly accentuated by the chef's special marinade. Equally intriguing was the Busan Neighborhood Pancake, a delightful concoction of scallion, bulgogi, and shrimp in a gochugaru batter that proved to be both unique and satisfying.

While the Galbi Patty with its hand-chopped short rib and rice cake was decent, it failed to meet my expectations. Even less impressive was the Beef Ji Ji Me, which seemed to focus more on the egg batter than the promised sirloin filling, leaving much to be desired.

On the individual meal front, my friend's Beef Spicy Noodle had a comforting heat for the cold day, yet skimped on the brisket, while my Silken Tofu Stew was enjoyable with its rich tofu and short ribs, though the balance of flavors and consistency weren't quite up to par for a stew.

The dishes were a hit or miss, though the novelty of the Busan-style offerings was a plus for us. It's worth noting that we were left with an unusual level of thirst post-meal, sparking some curiosity about the ingredients used.

The restaurant's ambiance is modern and welcoming, providing a spacious and comfortable environment for a casual lunch. Service was notably efficient, ensuring a swift and easy dining experience. Despite being a Korean BBQ spot, I missed out on the BBQ meats, leaving room for curiosity to bring me back.

In summary, [Restaurant Name] offers an interesting array of Korean dishes that might not have fully hit the mark for us, but the experience was intriguing enough to warrant a return visit, perhaps next time for the BBQ.

Loved my first lunch here today- used the Ritual app to order and everything was fresh and delicious! I tried the Salmon and added crab, the bowl came up with a choice of brown or white rice or veggie noodles (I did a combo of veggie noodles and brown rice) it came with pineapple, edamame, and seaweed salad. Everything was fresh and the serving was good. It also came with a side of sauce, I tried spicy mayo. They were quick and efficient - highly recommend! They also have some seating which was nice but be warned lunch time 12-1 it was pretty busy!

We tried to go to Osteria as a weekend lunch walk-in, but they were full. They did point us towards this sister establishment around the corner which we were able to get in without reservations. Started off with fresh bread with tomato and olive oil. I couldn't get enough of either. Fresh bread came warm and the tomato olive oil was a nice change from the usual olive oil and vinegar. We ordered the tagliatella carpacio and spaghetti lobster pasta.Spaghetti lobster was amazing. Spaghetti is so soft and the red sauce is incredibly flavorful. Noodles came piping hot, it was actually incredibly difficult to eat right away. For having half a lobster, this was reasonably priced at $26.50. Lobster tasted slightly mushy but still great flavor and not overcooked. Tagliatelle carpaccio was lighter in flavor since there wasn't any tomato sauce. Carpaccio tastes fresh. Noodles came out fresh from the kitchen and they ring a bell every time it's ready. Loved the experience overall and the food was amazing.

Title: Hooked on Japanese Curry Bliss

I approached Japanese Curry with an adventurer's curiosity and emerged a devotee. My recent infatuation is with the Seafood Set, a generous offering of two crispy fried shrimp atop fluffy white rice, all smothered in a divine brown curry sauce teeming with succulent shrimp and tender squid. This dish isn't just a meal; it's an indulgence that leaves you satisfyingly full.

Previously, I savored the chicken set, which was equally impressive, proving that this eatery doesn't play favorites with its flavors. Each set, replete with miso soup and a drink, feels like a cozy embrace on a plate, making it perfect for those chillier days when soup alone won't cut it.

At $17, the sets might appear pricier, yet the ample portions justify every penny. For the budget-conscious, the lunch special mirrors the set's allure at a modest $10. It's a steal for a slightly smaller but equally delicious version.

For groups, this spot is unexpectedly accommodating; just be strategic and beat the noon rush. My advice – arrive pre-11:30 to secure a serene dining experience. Whether you're a party of many or a duo seeking a culinary escapade, this restaurant's Japanese Curry will ensnare your senses and leave you planning your next visit before you've even left the table.

Title: A Slice of Tokyo in NYC - Ikinari Steak Experience

My adventure at Ikinari in New York City was an authentic excursion into Japanese steak culture, right in the heart of the Big Apple. The concept is hands-on and exciting: select your preferred cut and size on the menu, then watch the butcher expertly slice it for you at the butcher window. It's an engaging process that heightens your anticipation for the meal to come.
