The chef takes over from there, cooking your steak perfectly to order, paired with vegetables of your choosing – though the corn and white onions are a solid default. As you sit back at your table, the waiter is ready to take drink orders and handle any extra sides you might crave.

Wearing the provided paper bib is a must, especially if you're donned in white, as the steak arrives on a sizzling hot plate, ready to tantalize your senses. The table boasts a variety of condiments, but the standout is a dark brown sauce served in a glass jar, providing the ideal balance of saltiness to complement the unseasoned steak and amplify its rich flavors.

In addition to the au jus, there are condiments like garlic sauce, salt, pepper, and an American chipotle sauce to suit every palate. Ikinari Steak perfectly captures the essence of its Tokyo origins, offering a stellar Japanese steak experience that's well worth a visit for any carnivorous connoisseur.

Title: A Dim Sum Disappointment in the Heart of NYC

My recent visit to this dim sum restaurant, nestled in the bustling theatre district of NYC, was underwhelming. With its prime location steps away from Times Square, it's clear that the high prices are more for the address than the fare offered.

The ambiance is cozy, seating roughly 55 people between the main area and the elongated back room. Service was efficient—orders are placed by marking a paper menu, ensuring a quick turnaround.

Unfortunately, the food couldn't live up to the speedy service. The dumplings were a letdown, with the rice wrappers tearing easily, which is a sign of over-steaming. The cha-siu buns were only average, and the turnip cake skimped on the star ingredient. The Szechuan dumplings lacked the signature heat that should tickle the taste buds, though the vegetable dumplings had a savory filling, marred again by over-steaming. The fried rib pieces stood out with their flavor, and the spring rolls encased in rice noodles were a novel twist, yet these moments of enjoyment were sparse.

The bill left a sour taste, coming in at 25% more than what you'd pay in Chinatown, compounded by the surprising $8 charge for a pot of tea, which is usually complimentary elsewhere.

While the restaurant's extended hours and all-day dim sum service might appeal to some, the overall experience doesn't justify the premium. For a truly memorable dim sum, consider a short trip to Chinatown where your palate and wallet will find better satisfaction.

Title: Mixed Impressions on Tasting Tuesday

My companion and I ventured out on a snowy Tuesday to take part in the restaurant's Tasting Tuesday event. Nestled in the bar area, we were intrigued by the $25 wine flight promotion that promised a complimentary order of dumplings. Of course, our appetites demanded more, so we eagerly added fish and mushroom dumplings, wings, house special shrimp, and an assortment of soup dumplings and spicy wontons to our order.

The culinary experience was, overall, a bit underwhelming. Service hovered around average, requiring us to actively seek attention for any requests. The standout dish was the fish dumplings—exquisitely executed and brimming with flavor. Unfortunately, the rest of the menu items fell into the realm of the ordinary. We had high hopes for the chicken and pork soup dumplings, but they were notably bland. The wings disappointingly lacked finesse, sticky and unimpressive, compounded by a shortage of napkins. Shrimp with palatable seasoning was marred by inconsistent preparation, while the mushroom dumplings were overpowered by truffle oil.

The spicy wontons, draped in the so-called "house crack sauce," managed to redeem the starters somewhat, although they lacked the promised heat and came with scant sauce. We found ourselves requesting extra to fully appreciate their potential.

On the brighter side, the wine flight, a selection of rosés, was a highlight. Each glass arrived with a thoughtful description, adding a touch of sophistication to the evening. The atmosphere was cozy with a backdrop of nostalgic '90s hip hop that lent a cool vibe to the setting.

In summary, while the rosé flight and music selection made for a pleasant ambiance, the food and service left room for improvement. The restaurant nails the concept but needs to refine the execution for a truly memorable Tasting Tuesday experience.

Title: Authentic Delights at 2nd Ave Deli

Review:
Stepping into 2nd Ave Deli is like entering a cherished chapter of New York history. This kosher Jewish deli stands as one of the rare gems in the city, offering a nostalgic feast that harks back to the storied delis of yore. From the thick-cut pastrami sandwiches to the warm, savory knishes, the menu is a parade of classics done right.

As someone raised on Brooklyn deli fare, specifically the likes of Edelman's on 13th Avenue, I can attest to the authenticity and quality 2nd Ave Deli presents. Their pastrami sandwich competes with the best I've ever tasted, a sentiment that holds weight coming from a non-kosher, non-Jewish native who knows his deli.

2nd Ave Deli isn't merely serving food; it's preserving a slice of culture. Whether you're craving blintzes, a hot dog, or a slice of nostalgia, this institution delivers with aplomb. I may be gushing, but when a place is this good, it's hard not to share the joy. 2nd Ave Deli is true to its roots and a must-visit for anyone seeking the heart and soul of New York's deli scene.

Cute place, not sure why it felt sort of unexpected in this area. Overall there was a good selection of both healthy and more indulgent menu items. I liked how much natural light there was. Comfortable seating options, both low top tables and bar area. There is a chess top table for those inclined to play chess! I enjoyed the Israeli scotch egg with tahini. This place didn't wow me enough to make the trek back for it, but it's a good option if you happen to be in the neighborhood.
We just go here just for desserts, but you can't beat all of that chocolate! Great service every time. Make a reservation so you don't have to wait on a long line.

Title: A Stellar Birthday Celebration

My friends and I chose this gem of a restaurant to celebrate a birthday last Tuesday, and we couldn't have been more pleased. The ambience was lively with a full house, yet the dress code remained comfortably business casual.

Our waiter was the epitome of professionalism, juggling detailed specials and wine service with a finesse that's rare to encounter these days. His memory for detail was nothing short of impressive.

The menu did not disappoint. My salmon dish was cooked to perfection, and a sample of the homemade pasta with red sauce convinced me I’d have to return—simply the best. Although the details of the sides and appetizers elude me, their deliciousness lingers in my memory.

This restaurant is a safe bet for anyone looking for exceptional food and service. It set the stage for a perfect birthday celebration, earning every bit of the five stars I've awarded.

Restaurant Review:

Food: 3/5 - My experience with the food was mixed; while the California omelet exceeded my expectations, the sausage, egg, and cheese croissant sandwich fell short due to its oiliness. The Parmesan toast was satisfactory, and the vegetable omelet was decent but not remarkable. A note for improvement would be to serve the omelets' accompanying toast and French fries separately to maintain their crispness.

Service: 2/5 - The delivery arrived earlier than expected, which is a plus. However, communication was a significant issue. When I needed to clarify my order, the restaurant’s staff spoke to me in Spanish, which I did not understand. My request to communicate in English was met with them hanging up, which was quite frustrating, especially since I am not a native English speaker myself.

Overall: 3/5 - For those in a hurry and not particular about the quality or taste, this spot could be suitable due to its swift delivery service. However, be prepared for potential language barrier issues when ordering.

Based on a glowing recommendation from a fellow Yelper, I decided to try out Momosan, conveniently located just across the street from my office—and to my delight, it’s owned by the renowned Iron Chef Morimoto.

After convincing my VP and Director to join me for Happy Hour, we ventured into Momosan where I indulged in the tsukemen. The experience was on par with the acclaimed Tsujita, featuring delectable dipping noodles. I appreciated the flexibility to swap pork chashu for a well-marinated, juicy, and tender chicken alternative. The menma added a satisfying crunch and depth of flavor, while the sweet soy aji-tama was a luxurious touch with its custard-like yolk. The broth, lighter and less fatty than other venues, was more to my taste, allowing for a richer enjoyment of the dish. I enjoyed watching my VP get the hang of eating tsukemen just before savoring my own.

We also tried the sake sangria carafe, a sweet mix of sake, plum wine, and seasonal fruits that I found a tad too sugary, though still pleasantly crafted.

My time at Momosan was exceptional, providing a deeply satisfying end to a long workday. The place is a sure hit for anyone seeking quality Japanese cuisine with a masterful touch.

I heard a ton about BobWhite, and heard about they set up outposts at Urbanspace Vanderbuilt (and now the other Urbanspace location too!), so I've been meaning to hit em up! I noticed they had a deal on Ritual for their Fried Chicken Sandwich, so now I was completely out of excuses!So the deal was 50% for a sandwich plus choice of side.  Given that it was still pretty close to 'resolution' season (i.e., Jan. 2-3), I opted for the collard greens (and forwent the other dainty sides, like the mac n cheese or slaw). The sandwich was composed of a decent-sided piece of chicken on an appropriately sided, toasted (yes!!!!) potato bun, topped with bread and butter pickles.  Simple, but pretty damn delicious. Tender juicy chicken, nice bite of the pickles, and a buttery-toasted bun that held up well with some added crunch.  The chicken was really tasty, though I wish it was a tad bit more crispy, but still...yum. Sauce options at the stand seemed to be Sweet Baby Rays, ranch, and hot sauce.  I had to go with Sweet Baby and some hot.The collard greens provided a healthier contrast to the sammich, and were pretty okay. Not bursting with flavor, but...then again, it wasn't very bland and...wasn't loaded with bacon bits / accomplished the 'get your greens in' objective.In terms of a smash-n-grab Ritual pick-up, service at the booth was just fine - polite and prompt.Given this intro to BobWhite, I'd definitely be interested in trying some of their full-blown plate-dishes or taking a trip to the mothership.

Title: Mixed Experience at a Popular Gamecock Hangout

Last night, our school group of 20-30 people had a reservation at a well-known Gamecock Club, lauded for its vibrant atmosphere and alumni gatherings. Upon arrival at 7:30 pm, the reservation was promptly honored; however, the staff seemed ill-prepared for our large group, with only two waiters and a bartender available during a bustling evening.

As expected with large groups, our party members arrived sporadically, which had an impact on the service. The staff’s insistence on serving all meals simultaneously led to a protracted wait, with some guests not receiving their food until 9:30 pm, a full two hours after being seated. This approach was impractical for our large party and resulted in noticeable delays.

Customer service suffered due to the lack of staff. Waitstaff were seldom seen, and patrons were better served by going directly to the bar for additional drinks and requests. Clearly, more planning is necessary to accommodate events of this size.

On a positive note, the food, when it did arrive, was a delight. My fried chicken was perfectly seasoned, paired beautifully with smooth mashed potatoes and a heavenly gravy that left me craving more. The mac and cheese was a comforting addition to the meal. The MJ Lemonade, requested without mint, provided a refreshing counterpoint to the evening's frustrations.

In summary, while the venue is an exciting spot for sports, music, and local camaraderie, the dining experience for larger parties can be significantly improved with better staffing and more strategic meal service. Nonetheless, the culinary offerings once they arrived on the table were a highlight of the evening.

Possibly the best dining experience for the price in NYC. I've been meaning to come to Atoboy for so long, and I'm mad at myself for holding out. From the decor, to the service, to the execution of the dishes... everything was perfect.They have a selection of Soju cocktails (I love soju) and I really enjoyed my fruity/spicy Jalapeño Rosso.For $46 a person, you make a selection three dishes - all packed with amazing options like hamachi, octopus, and galbi. Every single dish was executed perfectly.We tried the...1. YellowtailOff menu saladCrab2. SunchokePork and shrimpLobster3. GalbiDuckWe also got the fried chicken, and opted for the seasonal sweet potato rice rather than white rice. Everything was exceptional, and I wouldn't change a thing we ordered. Standouts for me was the pork and shrimp, the sunchokes, and lobster.This is a great restaurant to bring out of towners with New Yorky vibes and a reasonable price point. Can't wait to be back!

Happy that there's another food option to eat in Chinatown!Came right before their lunch rush started so my friend and I didn't have to wait before we were seated. As a brand new establishment the interior was nice and clean. To place your order, you simply indicate the items that you would like by marking it on the the menu. There's a good variety of broths on the menu but it's not too extensive. I opted for the Original Rice Noddle Soup ($9.49) which was perfect for a cold winter day.The staffs were attentive and we got our food relatively quick. I absolutely love the deconstructed concept of the noodle soup. The toppings come out on separate dishes and you add in the toppings and the noodles into the piping hot broth. They give a good portion size of noodles which makes the dish pretty filling already but there's the option of getting a free refill on noodles (I just couldn't resist!) The noodles were tasty and didn't get soggy in the broth. The original broth was hearty and I would definitely recommend it if you're unsure of what to get.Affordable prices for a great value, would definitely come back again!

We recently celebrated my cousin's birthday at this unique dining spot, and it was an outstanding experience! The restaurant features an intriguing seating arrangement where you step down into your seats. While this added a distinctive touch to our evening, it did pose a slight challenge for maneuvering in and out, especially with a larger group. The interactive dining experience allowed us to cook a variety of dishes right at our table, to our personal tastes. I must say, everything turned out to be absolutely delicious! Highly recommended for a fun and flavorful evening.

Title: A Hyped Haven That Delivers

From its television shout-out in "Billions" to a personal recommendation by my bartender at the Edition, my expectations for this restaurant were sky-high—and I’m pleased to report they were met in every delectable way. Diving into the creamy depths of the lobster bisque, followed by a masterfully cooked prime New York sirloin, each bite confirmed this place's well-deserved reputation.

While there was a minor hiccup as I momentarily longed for my bread, the attentive bar staff noticed the oversight and promptly rectified the situation, showcasing their dedication to service. The atmosphere buzzed with a lively vibe that complemented the meal, making for an all-around outstanding dining experience. Highly recommended for those seeking culinary excellence!

Great place to come for cheap drinks & good Thai food. Well drinks are $7 beer is $5, they have a bar + TVs showing sports, a great going vibe with a nice mix of people. Wasn't to crowded, they staff let us take our time & everything was tasty. Recommend coming here to get your night started or just to hangout & have a few drinks without breaking with your wallet.

Came here because the menu at the rooftop was not exciting. Staff was friendly and efficient I had the tagliatelle- which was good  . Friend had the swordfish and loved it . We also shared a dozen oysters which were good

Awesome 24/7 spot in Chinatown! It's pretty nice inside since it's so new. Fast service and tasty food. You choose which broth you want (all comes with those toppings and a few slices of meat). I got the original which was clear and tasty, but my friend got the shredded pork broth, which was definitely more flavorful. Since the noodles are pretty light, I think a heavier broth is okay. Free cup of soda and extra noods is always great.

Tucked a few blocks away from the heart of Koreatown, Yoon Haeundae Galbi distinguishes itself as a refined Korean BBQ establishment on 36th Street. The atmosphere is notably less hectic than its 32nd Street counterparts, promoting a more relaxed dining experience. With reservations accepted and honored, it offers a convenience seldom found in the area.

The service is impeccable, with attentive staff ensuring a seamless meal from start to finish. We began with a fresh hamachi salad, a delightful combination of raw yellowtail, mild kochujang dressing, and crisp vegetables. The mung bean pancake and steamed mandu, although filling, were somewhat unremarkable in flavor. Conversely, the array of banchan presented an excellent prelude to the main course, with each small dish prepared to perfection.

The seafood tofu jigae stood out, brimming with shrimp, blue crab, and clams, and pairs wonderfully with the recommended brown rice. The BBQ selection shone brightest with their prime package; American wagyu beef in various cuts took center stage. Each meat, from the wafer-thin beef tongue to the succulent wagyu ribeye, was cooked to perfection, with the wagyu short rib being a standout for its buttery tenderness.

To conclude, we indulged in noodles, stir-fried in the rich pan juices, rounding off what was undeniably a premium offering of beef and an experience that justifies the higher price. Yoon Haeundae Galbi is a gem for those seeking top-notch Korean BBQ with a side of serenity.
Our go-to neighborhood gem never disappoints! We highly recommend saving room for dessert — it's a must!

Our party of three consisted of two omnivores and one vegan, and we all left extremely happy and satisfied.We shared the nachos with guac, and echoing many previous reviews, it was extremely delicious and definitely a must-get. Whether it's pricey or not really depends on how you look at it: If you compare it with the typical cheesy, heavy, and salty sports-bar nachos, then sure, it's kinda pricey. However, if you value not feeling miserable after having thoroughly pleased your taste buds, then it's absolutely worth it. I got the Chorizo Burrito as my main and it was five stars in terms of taste, portion, and presentation. We also shared the flan and it was good. I've never been to their other locations but this one was pretty spacious with tables, booths, and bar seats. The downstairs unisex bathroom stalls were clean. Service was friendly and attentive. I concur with a previous reviewer that their menu oddly doesn't list out all the ingredients that goes into a dish. They do check with you if you have any allergies when taking your order but what if there's something that you simply don't like? Hope they can be more transparent with their menu.

Upon arriving, I was like oh great ANOTHER Thai place in Hell's Kitchen. But, I gotta say that I'm glad that we stopped by this place for dinner. First, the restaurant is decorated very beautifully compared to the other Thai joints in Hell's Kitchen. Next, the restaurant has a pretty awesome dinner prix fix menu. For $26, you get a soup (three options) a salad, an appetizer (five options), and an entire (five separate noddle and rice options). The shrimp tom yum soup was perfect spiced/seasoned for my tastes, which may be too spicy for other folks. Also, the peanut sauce used for the salad had a nice kick to it. The portion size for each course was generous for the price, and you will be stuffed after your meal. For now (Jan. 2020), the restaurant has a happy hour that lasts all day and all night. If memory serves me correctly, beers are around $5. During out meal, I could not have asked for better service from the restaurant's great staff. Since I tend to let my hair down in Hell's Kitchen, I have a felling that I will be back.

This was our second time at Le Coq Rico. We came here first in July for the Restaurant Week and we were amazed both by the food and the staff so we decided to come back again. The food was great this time too, however the first time it definitely tasted better and I found that not only they served slightly bigger portions before but also the effort they put into the dishes was greater last year. The Cauliflower Veloute was only okay, the chicken liver pate was excellent and the bread they served it with was phenomenal. The main course was Coq Au Vin and Butternut Squash Risotto and, although I find the risotto tasty, it was a super small portion size and except for the cheese "chips" on top I didn't find it extraordinary. My husband's dish wasn't warm enough, and the sauce was too watery. The l'ile flottante was good. Also, what I found super annoying is that we had to sit right next to the aisle where the staff was going up and down continuously, therefore not only we heard everything they talked about, but it was also impossible to keep up our private conversation as somebody would come to our table every few minutes to ask something (whether we would like more drinks, is everything ok, etc.), interrupting our convo.All in all it was a good experience but not as exceptional and as pleasant as for the first time.

I have walked past Acme several times and finally decided to visit the restaurant. As a group we ordered the beef tartare, spicy meatballs, cacio e pepe, Duck ragu. These dishes did not disappoint at all. For the entree I got the duck dish. The duck was delicious, juicy and full of flavor. The waiter staff was excellent was attentive to the tables needs with having an over bearing presence. After the meal, Acme has a basement bar where you can party and get a couple drinks. Did not know this before coming to the restaurant. It was a very pleasant surprise. Will definitely return again to try all the other food options.

BEST PLACE FOR BRUNCH WE'VE BEEN TO. We loved everything about this place. The service was really good, decor is top notch, all the items in the menu are made fresh and tastes DELICIOUS!1. Truffle Egg Toast - This is the best option for everyone who loves to eat eggs. It was a 10/10 from us and we highly recommend it.2. French Toast - OMG, this was probably one of the best French Toasts we've ever had. We loved every bite of it. It was made to perfection.3. Rosemary Focaccia bread - This was super buttery and just the perfect amount of salt in it. It was really good. We highly recommend to pair the focaccia bread with your drinks. 4. Linguine Pasta - It's a good option for those who loves cheesy and lemony pasta. It was a perfect mix of Parmigiano and Lemon in a bowl of pasta5. Fusilli Alla Napoletana - This was our personal favourite Pasta. It's a red sauce fusilli pasta. Loved it! Overall, absolutely loved our experience here and we're definitely looking forward to their dinner menu here. We highly recommend this place to each and everyone. It's a must visit place!

I recently dined at a Mexican restaurant that boasts a pretty decent selection of authentic fare. Visitors should set their expectations for a homey atmosphere rather than a polished New York City dining experience. On the day I visited, the kitchen was unfortunately missing several menu items, which was a bit disappointing.

I ordered the spicy enchilada taco and the huarache. While both dishes were flavorful, the huarache seemed to lack the traditional garnish of lettuce and tomatoes, leaving it feeling somewhat incomplete. The pricing was very reasonable and the portions were generous.

Despite the value, there were some service issues that might deter me from a repeat visit. All in all, though, it's worth trying out for those looking for a no-frills spot to enjoy some Mexican cuisine.

Snarky hostess that states they don't allow walk ins. Perhaps that's the case but seems strange sincr the restaurant was half empty. Restaurant is in the basement. Quality of the food is good but an expensive night out.

I wouldn't necessarily call this authentic Lao food but nice try. After growing up eating Lao food from the kitchen of friends' moms and grandmas and countless Lao temple trips, I'm more inclined to call past experiences authentic, not this place. The restaurant can be summed up in one word - sweet. Everything we ordered (except the pigs face) was sweeter than I'm used to. Papaya salad was too sweet. The beef jerky was super sweet. And Nam Khao (crispy rice) was drenched in a sweet chili sauce. We were given free mango sorbet at the end of our meal which was a nice touch and greatly appreciated. The sorbet tasted like ripe mangoes - it was the star of our meal. I took off two stars for the food being too sweet and not authentic as advertised but mostly because of the pigs face - lack of help from the wait staff and only a small portion of it was edible. We ordered it at the waitress' suggestion and didn't realize it was literally half a pig's face. I'm a pretty adventurous eater and I'm game to try almost anything once, but this caught me off guard. We sat at the table staring at each other, unsure of what to do. They placed the pigs face on the table with a knife stabbed in the side and walked away. I made eye contact with several servers and I swear they smirked but no one offered to help. How exactly do you cut a pigs face? With no other choice, I started cutting what I could. The flavor of the pork skin was amazing! The fat was rendered nicely so you're left with a crispy salty bite. The problem is that not all of the pigs face was like this, only a portion of it. The other portion was rock hard and inedible. If you look closely at the picture i posted, you can see tiny bubbles around the pig's cheek which is the perfect crispy part but as you get closer to the nostril, there aren't any tiny bubbles and that's where the skin was inedible. That took away from the great parts of the dish. You pay $40 for only 1/4th of the dish that's edible. Once we did what we could, we turned the pigs face over and saw a row of teeth. My adventurous side ended right then and there!

Incredibly delicious.  Greek fare with a fresh market to choose your fish. Impeccable 5 service from greeting to final goodbye. Try to get a seat near the window and enjoy the views of #Vessel and the water. Cocktails are crafty especially the hot Baklava. Great greek wine selection as well. Get the Labraki fish grilled and the potatoes on the side. Perfect seviche and oysters on the raw.

Title: Lukewarm Experience at Brasserie 812's Brunch

I recently visited Brasserie 812 for their much-anticipated Sunday brunch with four friends. The initial descent into the brasserie set a promising ambiance with a visually pleasing interior that immediately caught our attention.

The brunch operates as a self-serve buffet, which in theory should offer convenience and variety. The diverse menu offerings, which can be previewed at brasserie812.com/menu#Su, unfortunately did not translate into an equally satisfying dining experience.

My primary concern was the buffet's food temperature. It seemed the establishment did not take the necessary measures to keep the dishes warm. With a less than bustling brunch crowd, this oversight led to cold, unappetizing plates. Despite ample portions, food quality suffered visibly over time, especially at the carving station where roast beef, leg of lamb, and turkey dried out before our eyes.

Even the crepe station, a staple in French cuisine, was not adequately highlighted, causing confusion amongst diners looking forward to this classic dish. On a more positive note, the waitstaff provided commendable service, and the shrimp cocktail section did not disappoint. Additionally, the desserts were well-received by my party, overshadowing the main courses.

However, given the premium price point, I cannot in good faith recommend Brasserie 812's brunch. The dining experience fell short of expectations, leaving us hashtag disappointed.

Title: A Worthy Wait for Remarkable Ramen at Columbus Circle

Last Thursday, amidst the patter of rain and the anticipation of a long-overdue college reunion, my friend and I ventured to a bustling ramen spot nestled on the third floor of a local mall. Despite previous visits, the restaurant's tucked-away location required some guidance to find.

Arriving at 7:30 pm, we were met with a 45-minute wait that stretched into a full 65 minutes. Tip for future patrons: aim for off-peak times to dodge the lengthy queue. A nearby bakery offers a comfortable waiting spot for those who find themselves with time to spare.

Once seated, service lagged slightly, a testament to the restaurant's overwhelming popularity rather than a lack of effort from the diligent staff. Patience, however, paid off handsomely.

The menu tantalized with offerings like daily specials—charred octopus and pork stew—that we’ll have to return for. We kicked off with the spicy rice cake appetizer, a fiery prelude that demands caution with each bite.

For the main course, my choice of spicy beef ramen delivered a symphony of flavors, boasting a unique broth that was perfectly heated, complemented by fall-apart tender beef. The accompanying spinach and green onions lent a refreshing crunch to the dish. Meanwhile, the ginger scallion noodle savored by my friend surely did not disappoint either.

A silver lining to our experience was the owner's personal attention to feedback, with a mention of potential reservations, showcasing a commendable dedication to customer care.

In summation, if your travels bring you near Columbus Circle and a steaming bowl of ramen beckons, this spot, despite the wait, promises a delightful culinary encounter.

East Village local, and I've been here a few times. Sometimes for dinner and drinks, other times for late night happy hours. I have had some good servers here, and some who leave food and run away. For the price, the food is good. I like the ambiance. But my favorite has to be the late night appetizer special. Nothing beats it in the area. Drinks are on the pricey side--but hey, it's New York.

Title: Delightful Feast at a Charming Spot

Our party of 13 was treated to a generous tasting event at this charming eatery, where big portions call for sharing or a take-home box. The adorable décor, with a pink wall adorned by wooden piggies full of compliments, sets a fun, calming tone for the dining experience, although the pig figurines in the dimly lit bathroom might surprise you.

Service was impeccable; our large group never felt neglected. As a first-timer to authentic Chinese cuisine, I found the spice levels a bit challenging, but the well-seasoned dishes were mostly enjoyable and the extensive menu accommodates even the pickiest of eaters.

Standouts included the soup dumplings—delicately wrapped, juicy, and perfect for a chilly evening—as well as the deep-fried Brussels sprouts, which were light, non-greasy, and packed with flavor. Unexpectedly, the hand-made Sichuan cold noodles with sesame sauce won me over despite my usual aversion to noodles.

The popcorn shrimp appetizer in sweet sauce was another highlight, best enjoyed warm for its delicate texture. While I couldn't try every main dish, the famous BBQ ribs were, regrettably, a letdown for me.

Overall, I'm eager to revisit for more soup dumplings and to explore the pork dishes. A gem worth checking out!

This place is a hidden gem just outside of Chinatown. We ordered the cheapest and biggest dumplings New York has to offer. You won't be disappointed by the quality and size of the food as it is a perfect size/$ ratio. You could feed a small family for $20 worth of dumplings. The only reason why I rated this a 4 was that my order took a while to receive and that the place is overly crowded because there are so many people and no organized seating

Title: A Delightful Second Serving of a Favorite

Rating: ★★★★★

Having been a fan of their original Elmhurst location, I was thrilled to find they've expanded closer to me. Despite the inevitable lunchtime lines, the queue is swift, with the option of ordering from a personable cashier or via an efficient kiosk system. The establishment boasts a two-tiered seating arrangement, though I've never had to venture to the second level as the ground floor usually has ample space.

Their menu is a delightful mix of signature dishes and customizable options, allowing for personal preference with every ingredient interchangeable. A standout must-try is the beef bulgogi and caramel pork topped with a perfectly runny egg—just thinking about it makes me hungry! Don't miss out on the crispy spring rolls and the delectably seasoned fries. To wash it all down, there's an impressively authentic Thai iced tea.

With 2020 ahead, I've set a tasty goal: to come back and savor every other tempting item on their menu. Highly recommend a visit!

Upon our visit to the namesake restaurant, the culinary experience was notably impressive. The centerpiece dishes, a burger and a lobster po'boy, lived up to our high expectations. The lobster was the epitome of tenderness, carefully fried to avoid any toughness, and nestled within a perfectly toasted roll complemented by a flavorful remoulade sauce. Similarly, the burger was a testament to skilled seasoning and cooking, delivering satisfaction in every bite.

The accompanying sides did not fall short, either. The fries were a delightful play on textures, thin and crispy as desired. The salad was a refreshing counterpart, with impeccably fresh greens lightly adorned with a tangy balsamic dressing.

The sole caveat to an otherwise stellar dining experience was the unexpected wait time; despite our reservation, we were asked to linger for 20 minutes before being seated. This small hiccup kept the restaurant from achieving a flawless five-star review. Nonetheless, the food alone warrants a strong recommendation for those seeking excellently prepared comfort cuisine.

At this no-frills establishment, a single dollar nets you a hot slice of cheese pizza that defies expectation. The simplicity of the transaction is matched only by the surprising quality of the pie. An excellent choice for a quick, budget-friendly bite.

During my NYC visit, I had breakfast at a restaurant situated within the Stewart Hotel, conveniently close to NY Penn Station. The fare was fairly standard—nothing noteworthy or unique, but adequate. The kitchen was efficient with little delay in serving the meal. The staff was commendable for their friendliness and attentive service. Overall, a satisfactory yet unremarkable dining experience.

Great if you're in the area. I like this place, randomly saw it while walking and walked in. It's a little bit crowded but from 11am - 5pm the lunch special is amazing for the price. I'm a fat@$$ and this filled me up! Great portions and THE TAKE CARD!!  :)Honestly for lunch special this is worth it if you're in the area.

I like Ted's Corner Tavern. Well, -ish. We went there on before catching a movie. Granted, the draw of going was their happy hour oyster special. But, it looked like an awesome place and had all the fixings to make it on to the short list of our go-to's for movie date night. Unfortunately, it didn't quite hit the mark.I was a bit put off that their website touts their oysters, almost making them sound like they are a connoisseur of what is undoubtedly my obsession. So, I was very excited. They claim to "locally sourced the waters of British Columbia, Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, Rhode Island and Virginia ...  hand selected and intensely groomed, providing optimal body, pillow-like softness and clean flavor." So, one would expect as least two choices. No, just the one. And, when I inquired about the oysters, I was pretty much told it's usually the same, which would be fine, had they not had a separate page on their site devoted to oysters, and made it sound like they'd have a wide selection on the lines of Crave or Cull & Pistol.I was very annoyed by that. We still would have come if they had been more honest. I wouldn't have had such a high expectation.That said, the oysters they had were very good, mostly because of the chef's unique way of serving them with a slice jalapenos on top and both lime and blood orange segments on the side. They were delicious; dare I say, yummy. That little extra jalapeno oomph was a pleasant surprise, and mellowed my annoyance a little. Well, until the rest of the meal arrived. But I'll get to that moment. Before we go down the reasons we were less than happy, let's first talk about the things that TCT really shined with .. We got there early, around 5 p.m., before the happy hour crowd. We were the only ones there when we arrived. (The place was packed when we were done and on our way out 45 minutes/an hour later.) So, we really got to have a good look at the decor. The place itself is absolutely adorable. Charming. Quaint. It's extremely welcoming. I absolutely love the irreverent humor that went into putting up photos of Teds of all kinds from Roosevelt to Knight to Bundy. That's my kind of off-kilter humor that shows a place not taking it all so seriously, and I mean that with the highest compliment.And the service was stellar. The bartender was our hostess with the mostess at the start. Then our waitress arrived and picked up. Both were delightful, attentive and very friendly. Flawless, in fact.The problem is that the appetizers we ordered beyond the oysters really fell flat, and that's being kind. We had the spicy cauliflower. They were neither spicy, nor cooked very well. And, I LOVE cauliflower. That's my other obsession, behind oysters.The truffle flatbread tasted like something you'd buy in the frozen section and make in the microwave. Actually, that's being a little bit kind. It was like the poor man's flatbread, from your college days, where you'd buy rolls for a $0.50 at the market and try to make it yourself for under $1 and pretend it's gourmet. We couldn't even eat it. And it's almost deceiving to call whatever was on top "mushrooms" "cheese" or "truffle oil." Really, I'd expect this at some tiny hole in the wall in Queens. That really crushed the meal. We just paid and left. I would go back for the oysters, but, I doubt my husband would. And, really, when I start to think back to the appetizers, there's nothing special enough about the oysters to make a return trip worth it ... even if it's just a few blocks from the movie theater.

I recently visited this restaurant for the first time for lunch and was smart to reserve a table ahead of time, as it's always bustling. Upon arrival, I noticed 'reserved' signs on all tables, but curiously, even after an hour, those tables remained unoccupied, suggesting the signs may just be for show.

Despite this oddity, my dining experience was quite positive. The staff was notably friendly and attentive, ensuring a pleasant atmosphere from the get-go. The service was prompt, with drinks arriving quickly and meals following suit. The food itself was impressive - served hot and delicious, living up to my expectations.

Overall, the quality of the food and service outweighed the minor confusion caused by the reservation signs. I certainly plan to return for another lunch soon.

A quick stop here after a long day (3.5 star, 8/10/2019). Im not sure how crowded this place usually is. However, there was no line at 8:30pm on Sat. We got brewed ice tea, lemonade and one red velvet. Every item was reasonably priced even though many places in this neighborhood usually are. I loved non-sweetened ice tea which doesn't give a typical after taste. Lemonade was unique, and not too sweet (that's how I prefer). A red velvet cake was very dense and heavy. The cake was unfortunately not my favorite. I'd come back here though if there's no wait!

Ever since I was little, I've always loved mixian and was craving for Yunnan crossing the bridge noodle to be in NYC. This place definitely is a gem!They have the small plates of veggies and meat that you can pour into the hot noodle soup yourself and I enjoyed the process every single time!The set is fresh and delicious and did i mention that they also have unlimited noodle addition?! We added noodle 3 times and they are still very nice about it!Needless to say, COME HERE!

Title: Tasty Bites with Iconic Views at NYC Café

We were graced with perfect weather for our NYC adventure, which included a delightful boat ride to the Statue of Liberty, complemented by a meal at a charming café on the island. I savored a mouthwatering grilled vegetable sandwich while my husband indulged in a juicy burger accompanied by crispy onion rings. Admittedly, the prices were a bit steep, but considering the location, it was no surprise. Despite the cost, the food was delectable and added to our memorable day. I'd definitely recommend grabbing a meal here during your visit to Lady Liberty.

The best of the best! It's been a few years since living in Brooklyn. Forgot how amazing the pies are. Was happy to be reunited after two years, yesterday, with two doughy, delicious pies. The proceeds of the one (Kuala Colada) even went towards the devastation in Australia. Happy to eat a yummy pie for a good cause. The only complaint is the cramp-ness. Wish it was a slightly more spacious spot, but it's of course in high demand, so I get it. Plus, for once, we had no wait! Even on a beautiful Sunday afternoon.

Title: Authentic Malaysian Delights in the USA

As a Malaysian expatriate in the USA searching for a taste of home, this restaurant is an absolute gem. The menu transported me back to the streets of Malaysia with its authentic flavors. The hokkien noodles were a standout, boasting the perfect texture - firm yet tender. The hainanese chicken rice, with its fragrant yellow rice, was a comforting reminder of the familiar. The Assam laksa, a Penang specialty thanks to the owner's roots, was a spicy indulgence that was delicious despite the heat.

The dishes were fresh, the portions generous, and the prices reasonable, making this eatery a must-visit for anyone craving Malaysian cuisine. Whether you're Malaysian or simply a food enthusiast eager to explore rich, authentic flavors, this restaurant is not to be missed.

My mother taught me when you think about a restaurant, 3 things are important. Food, service and decor. Remember this, you can't eat the decor. It it should at least be pleasant. K Rico decor was good. No problem there. Service- despite our large party of 16, service was spot on. No problem there.Now the most important, the food. We ordered a 22oz rib eye. Well, I know you need some fat grizzle for flavor but our cut had about 20% fat. (See picture) This the loss of 2 stars.The other 17.2 ounces of steak were just ok. World class prices for a sub world class piece of meat. The Brussels Sprouts were to oily and greasy overpowering the vegetable.We won't be coming back. Too many choices in New York.

Super authentic French food. Actually ate here once like 4 years back and finally tracked it back down-- food is just as good as I remember which says something for its consistency. I've eaten the best snails of my life here; the escargot are cooked in this garlic butter sauce that is simply delicious and goes great with the complimentary bread. Also ordered the mussels with chorizo, which was also very good. Think it might be better if it came with bread for dipping instead of fries but it's quite good as is. Desserts are great, especially their creme brûlée, which had the perfect ratio of caramelized sugar to custard. Owners are super nice and for a French restaurant, it's not too expensive, especially given the quality.

There are some instances where restaurants live up to your expectations, and other instances where they exceed them. Le coucou falls into the latter category. I came here with a friend on a cold Sunday evening. We had a 5:30 reservation, and were seated immediately, at a table in front of the open kitchen. The service was impeccable, and we were taken care of from start to finish. The dining We decided on two appetizers, and two entrees each. Each dish was presented fairly quickly after ordering. My friend had the sweetbreads, while I had the foie gras. The foie gras was served in a novel way, baked into a pastry-like concoction, and garnished with a slightly sweet pineapple sauce that complemented the rich foie gras. The sweetbreads were cooked well, with that quintessential chewy texture that only innards can possess. After finishing our dishes, our mains were again served quickly. My friend had the rabbit, while I had the catalan style pigeon. Both entrees were on the larger side for a restaurant of this calibre. My pigeon was rich and succulent, accompanied with a sweet-tasting sauce that brought out its flavor. My friend said her rabbit was very good, which I agreed on, but was somewhat confused by the serving style of broth and meat separately. Though she liked it, she said it wasn't a dish she would have ordered again, would she come back.The positioning of our seats towards the open kitchen meant that we could see everything that was going on. As I like to watch chefs at their craft, I was watching the goings on of the evening, and engaged in an awkward game of eye contact with the host and head chef all evening. Either way, still an excellent dinner that we enjoyed tremendously. With appetizers going up to $28, and most entrees priced over $40, this is not a cheap meal, but an affordable extravagance, and one that is well worth it. I would probably say this place is now my favorite French restaurant in the city. Thanks for an excellent dinner!

Title: A Unique Ramen Experience at ICHIRAN Manhattan

Having heard a great deal about ICHIRAN, I was intrigued to try the new Manhattan location, which opened its doors on March 28, 2019. Arriving at 6pm, the restaurant was surprisingly not bustling, though the policy of not seating incomplete parties was a minor setback.

The layout, with its booth sections, felt private and well-organized, and I was tickled by the green-lit board indicating available seating. The no-tipping system is a plus, making the ramen experience more wallet-friendly.

ICHIRAN's customizable ramen is a highlight, allowing diners to tailor everything from garlic and oil levels to noodle texture. Note that extra noodles cost $3.9, or $2.9 for a half portion, but the firm ones—particularly chewy—are worth a try, especially since the first half order can be free with an app download.

Service was amicable, though self-service water was a bit unconventional. As for the ramen, it was decent, though having to assemble ingredients, including peeling your own egg, was unexpected. While the soup had a potent salty flavor and an unexpected spicy zing despite ordering "mild," the matcha pudding dessert stole the show—creamy and flavorful, albeit small and steeply priced at $8.

In comparison to whispers of the Brooklyn location's superiority, the Manhattan branch holds its own with its unique dining experience, but there's room for improvement in the ramen's balance of flavors.

I like this location and my local location the same. I don't know if they are affiliated with each other, but I can tell you that they both have good food and okay service. I mean both location could work on being a lil friendly when it comes to the service, I don't know if it's a language barrier, but I like when my server communicates with me I feel like they just take your order, bring you your food, and then that's it, you don't see them again until you are calling them for your bill, or something else. Anyway I would recommend this place for some good Latin food, and it does have a nice vibe to the place, also I think for some of the items, they can be a bit pricey but I can't complain because its worth its weight in volume. So on that note, I prefer this Spanish spot along with my location one of the better Latin cuisine places to eat.

The question I always have about Dos Caminos is if the experience lives up to the name.  I hear about Dos Caminos as a cool trendy place to hang out but wasn't sure if the dining experience was all novelty. I came for a business lunch with some colleagues on a weekday. We walked right in and were seated in the back corner area of the restaurant. It is a spacious restaurant with a long bar. We weren't drinking but it looks like a cool place to get a drink.The lunch menu had all the heavy hitters.  We had to start with guacamole but it comes already done so not sure how fresh it is but it tasted good. The three salsa's that came when the guacamole came out were also pretty delicious. I don't know if it was part of the meal or part of the guacamole appetizer. The salsa I loved the most was the mild one. Great flavor. For lunch, I went with the chile rellenos. I really enjoyed it. There isn't a ton of heat to it but the flavors work. There is a lot going on with the dish but the combination of chile to filling worked. It is a hearty dish so don't come expecting to watch your calories but they were well worth it.  My friend orderd the burger well done but it was still pink. I know chefs hate when people order meat well done but the customer is always right!In the end Dos Caminos lived up its name. It was not just a novelty but a place you can get some good food. I don't know how authentic the food is but who cares it is still good. Will definitely be back.

Sai Gon Dep is Viet restaurant in Murray hill. The creative dishes were superb and such high quality for a pho restaurant. The service was excellent. The music was fun and had great beats. The space is small, so call ahead if you're coming with a big group.We had dinner with a group of friends there during a weeknight. We shared the following: Crispy Fried Spring Rolls- ground pork with wood ear, mung bean noodles, carrot, onions with hoisin peanut sauce. This was a solid classic spring roll. Pork Summer Rolls- grilled pork with mango, carrots, lettuce and cucumber. I loved the mango and the blend of textures. There was a rolled wonton skin that was deep fried; it was stuck inside the roll to offer a crunch to contrast the crisp vegetables and mango. I loved the textures of this summer roll!Beets and mango summer roll (vegan roll)- beets, mango,, lettuce, mint roll. I loved the textures of this roll. It was so refreshing! It was so pretty and was really tasty.Beef Pho- This was wonderful! I loved the beefy clear broth. The pho comes with bean sprouts, mint, sauces, rice noodles. The star of the show: 60 day dry aged tomahawk steak with beef pho. It was soft medium rare juicy semi fatty tomahawk steak. I loved it! It accompanied the beef pho so well. Beef with beef.The tomahawk steak comes with two bone marrows and sauce. I loved spreading the bone marrow on the crullers, then dipping into the sauce. Everyone oohed and aahed over the steak. It was so decadent to eat in a pho shop. Off menu items:Fried soft shell crab salad- this was amazing! The crab was crispy, the watercress and tomato salad was dressed with fish sauce and vinaigrette that was so refreshing! One of my friends liked the salad more than the crab! I loved both! Mussels- this was served with a coconut curry sauce and topped with Youtiao (Chinese Cruller). This was one of my favorite dishes! I loved the spicy sweet savory sauce with the mussels. And dipping the fried cruller into the mussel sauce was heavenly! Banh Mi with steak with beef broth dip- The beef broth was the same soup base for the pho. It was the best Banh Mi that I've ever had! The beef sandwich was savory, spicy on crispy baguette. The beef broth was perfect! It was better than the Chicago Italian dip sandwiches that we've had. This was a crowd pleaser! I would def return for the Bahn Mi, Mussels, Beef Pho and Crab salad!

In the city for a concert and craving Seafood, we settled on this restaurant in Grand Central Station. Our experience was mixed; our initial server was terse and dismissive, almost rude but at the end of the meal he must have gone off shift and we were assigned a charming and friendly replacement. The place itself is an interesting mix of Grand ceiling and lighting, in keeping with its location, and trashy grocery store salt and pepper containers and cheap tablecloths, cutlery and dish-ware. The inflated prices (at least $10 per plate more than each dish is worth, we paid less at Bobby Flay's gourmet restaurant for top of the line everything!) lead you to believe you're getting class, but there are contradictions everywhere. The food was 3 star worthy, the pasta was cooked ok but the pesto was low on flavor (definitely needed more garlic) but was very fishy flavored which was unpleasant; most of it remained on the plate at the end of the meal. The asparagus was crisp and tender and the seafood up to par. The highlight of the meal was the "grilled" - it was actually pan fried with butter so be aware if you have dietary restrictions - salmon. It was perfectly cooked, juicy on the inside and crisp on the inside! The accompanying vegetables were perfectly cooked and the flavors so good (after adding salt and pepper!!) that I forgot about the side of hollandaise sauce. For close to $100 with only soft drinks and no appetizers or desserts it was way overpriced, even for NY and I wouldn't return. With all the restaurants in the city we have too many choices for a mediocre experience!

During my second visit to Little Italy in New York, my friend and I dined at a local restaurant. We were enticed by a complimentary first glass of wine, which proved to be delicious—the Moscato and dry red were particular highlights.

Unfortunately, our experience was marred by inconsistent service. While one waiter was attentive and caring, the other was overly flirtatious and made us feel uncomfortable with his constant Spanish and inquiries about our origins. Compounding this issue was a mix-up with two waiters unknowingly doubling up on their service, adding to the confusion.

The food was a mixed bag. We had to request the house bread, which, disappointingly, arrived hard and stale. However, the bruschetta offered an intriguing and tasty twist on the traditional recipe. The eggplant dish was well-prepared with a pleasing texture and a Marinara sauce that enhanced its flavors. On the other hand, the seafood salad was a letdown, as the mix of seafood with pesto did not marry well.

Overall, considering the steep prices, the service inconsistencies, and the hit-or-miss dishes, the dining experience left much to be desired.

Title: Cozy Haven for Gluten-Free Delights

Review:

Tucked away in a quaint corner, the restaurant may be small, but it's big on charm with an ambiance that exudes a cozy, homey vibe. The menu isn't sprawling, yet its dedicated gluten-free offerings are a breath of fresh air, especially for the two members in our party with Celiac – a worry-free dining experience indeed!

The complimentary gluten-free bread set a welcoming tone. My choice, the mushroom and spinach quiche, was delightfully fluffy, paired with a fresh arugula salad and scrumptious breakfast potatoes that boasted a perfect crisp and an aromatic surprise of whole garlic cloves. Although tasty, the quiche portion left me desiring just a bit more. 

My companions' dishes – the prosciutto arugula pizza, tuna sandwich, and french toast – appeared deceptively 'normal,' hiding their gluten-free nature well. The pizza was a standout, with plentiful, crisp prosciutto, though a balsamic drizzle would have made it stellar.

Admittedly, prices lean towards the higher end, ranging from $15 to $20, but given the gluten-free specialty, the value is justifiable. We eyed the pastries, all displayed like edible artwork, with regretful appetites too sated to indulge – a tempting reason to return.

In a nutshell, this little gem is well worth a visit, especially for those in search of scrumptious, worry-free gluten-free dining.

Title: A Delightful Discovery in Soho

I've been strolling past this gem in Soho for years, but today I finally decided to step into the culinary oasis at around 4 pm. The decision couldn't have been better. Greeted by the beam of sunshine that is Bailey, her warmth and expertise shone through as she effortlessly guided this first-timer through the menu.

Taking her advice, I indulged in the curry chicken paired with rice and a tantalizing cilantro chutney. The dish was an excellent showcase of Indo-American fusion, with the Indian flavors having my taste buds in an absolute frenzy of delight. The cilantro chutney was nothing short of a revelation, perfectly complementing the curry.

The experience was a gratifying escape into the flavors of India during my lunch break. I left already planning my next visit – the dosas and soup are calling my name. Kudos to the team; Bailey is indeed a gem. Can't wait to return!

Having frequented Chirp roughly seven or eight times following my initial review, it's with regret that I report a lack of improvement in service. An aspect that stands out is their miserly approach to the beloved green sauce (aji sauce), notable by its limitation to a half-filled small container, regardless of whether you order a quarter or half chicken. Requesting additional sauce incurs a charge of $0.50 each, which feels petty considering the meal cost of $12-15.

Despite the chicken's flavor, this nickel-and-diming, coupled with the service, dampens the dining experience. For context, during my first visit, a confusing encounter with the server, "Karla M.," highlighted disorganization in service early on. While some may overlook such grievances for outstanding cuisine, the chicken at Chirp, though decent, lacks the depth of spice found in other city establishments like Pio Pio, especially within the sauce.

In conclusion, Chirp's tasty chicken isn't enough to compensate for the persistent service issues and the frustrating sauce policy. It is unlikely that I will return.

Title: A Redeeming Encore at Seamore's

Last night's encore visit to Seamore's, prefacing a show, washed away any residue of past misgivings. Courtesy of an invite from Matt, we found ourselves enveloped in a gustatory do-over that truly hit the mark.

The initial salvo of a dozen oysters set a briny yet balanced stage—impeccably fresh and conscientiously devoid of overpowering sea. The guacamole that followed was nothing short of a crowd-pleaser at $12, perfectly tuned with its companions—tomato, onion, cilantro—and a signature touch of salted blue corn chips.

The Maryland Crab Dip, however, stole the show. At $22, it was a decadent dance of sharp cheddar, parmesan, and sizable chunks of crab, melding into a gooey delight. A nibble more heat would've been the cherry on top, but it stood out regardless.

Segueing to the Tuna Poke for $20, we were greeted with what can only be described as the epitome of freshness. Generous avocado portions wading in a light, tangy ponzu sauce left our tastebuds singing.

Regretfully, the s'mores dessert remained a dream deferred, as we hit the satiety ceiling. But it leaves us with an alluring reason to return.

A hearty thanks to Seamore's for the culinary encore that turned skeptics into fans. You've not only righted a past wrong, but you've earned yourselves a pair of devoted patrons. Cheers to many more meals!

Decided to try this restaurant out with a few friends on a Monday night. Reservation was done via Seated app and it was pretty straightforward. Waiter was attentive and helpful in figuring out orders for the night. We all decided to order a number of appetisers to share for the night so we ended up with few house specials. Some to mention:- Grilled octopus: pretty fresh and well grilled. Enough to share between 4 people- Tuna tartare: did not taste as well expected. The only item we did not polish offIn addition to some of the dishes above, we decided to go crazy on the desserts:- Flourless chocolate cake: nice and chocolatey, served with some custard, fruit and cream on the side - Tiramisu: can't go wrong with a tiramisu. Tasted like a standard tiramisu, nothing to write home about- Cheesecake: my least favorite dessert. It didn't taste like a standard cheesecake rather it was more custard like. Service was good, toilets were nice and clean. We missed their happy hour but I think there is happy hour from 5-7pm. Also book via Seated app for extra perks!

Cute sports bar with a fantastic tap list and interesting atmosphere.I came here just for the beer while my wife did a bunch of fabric shopping in the garment district, having seen friends check in to really good beer on Untappd before. The tap list did not disappoint with lots of beers over 4.1 on Untappd and mostly local beers. Better yet, they'll do 4 oz pours for everything, so you can actually try all the beers you want without getting hammered and then still probably have a full pour of your favorite.I could have done without the giant TVs everywhere showing sporting events. I've never really lived in a house with a TV on in the background, so I have trouble tuning them out.Otherwise, the place had a cool, refined, upscale-british-bar ambiance with leather or dark wood everywhere and library card catalog style labels for the taps.

As an omnivore I can appreciate a solid vegetarian meal as it is on trend but I also approach all these health fads with caution.I mean look, is your vegan meal really good for you if it's still a burger and fries? Consider that first. I also got one of the original nutritional science degrees back in the day and I don't think that science has improved much despite it being several years later.  There's too much money in the food business.Enough of my rant, this place serves a good bowl and salad options. And they might actually be healthy. I really liked the Sonoran bowl I had here. Less the taco salad but the sprouts were too sprout-y for me then.

Title: A Casual Spot That Packs a Flavorful Punch

My recent visit to this fast casual gem was a delightful surprise. Though unassuming at first glance, the eatery offers an impressive selection of dishes that punch well above their weight in taste. The food quality is exceptional, particularly noted in the rich and aromatic Thai basil noodles and the savory Singapore noodles that my friend enjoyed. Admittedly, the prices are a tad steep for a casual dining experience, yet they align with the local standard and are justified by the flavors offered. Since my visit, cravings for their robust noodle dishes have been a frequent occurrence. I wholeheartedly recommend this spot for anyone looking for a quick yet satisfying meal.

I had the pleasure of experiencing the omakase by the renowned Box, and it did not disappoint. The sushi was exceptional, each piece a testament to the chef's expertise. The evening was not only a culinary delight but also thoroughly entertaining. Highly recommend for an unforgettable sushi adventure.

Title: Game Night Delights with a Side of Missteps at Woodpecker

This past Monday, my friend and I descended upon Woodpecker to revel in their new promotion, an all-day happy hour coupled with game night. Initial confusion by the bartender over the promotion was professionally resolved by the GM – much appreciated.

With appetites in tow, we embarked on a culinary journey through the entire bar food menu, each item a modest $7. The offerings were diminutive versions of their full-sized counterparts, but not in flavor. Standouts included a juicy burger and succulent calamari. The fries, however, were inconsistent – a mix of perfectly crispy and disappointingly limp. The pizza was passable, though unremarkable, but it's the burger that would beckon me back.

Dessert was where excitement waned; the cinnamon panna cotta failed to deliver, lacking both flavor and a pleasing texture – a far cry from the lush versions I've savored elsewhere. Its blandness had me longing for their apple tart, which I now hold in higher esteem.

Woodpecker offers a spot I'd return to if I found myself nearby, with a brunch visit at the forefront of my mind.

Title: A Sichuan Gem in New York

After returning from Richmond, BC, I was yearning for an authentic Sichuan culinary experience in New York, and I've found my favorite spot! This establishment truly delivers an explosion of flavors that restored my enthusiasm for the New York food scene.

The 晾衣白肉, a classic Sichuan dish, has earned its place as a permanent feature on my dining table – it's an absolute must-have. The shuizhu fish maintains its high standard with the perfect balance of spice and tenderness. As for the Chongqing fried chicken, its authenticity took me straight back to the buzzing street food markets of China.

It's not just the main attractions that shine here; even the vegetables are a delight, fresh and full of flavor. My only quibble is the portion size. Although on the smaller side, six dishes accompanied by some perfectly steamed rice proved to be a satisfying meal for our party of four.

A word to the wise: the wait can be lengthy, as experienced on a bustling Thursday evening, so I recommend arriving early to secure a spot. Despite the wait, this restaurant has cemented itself as my go-to Sichuan haven in the city.

I recently visited a restaurant that truly impressed me with its delicious fare and vibrant atmosphere. The tacos stood out with their mouthwatering flavors, clearly made with top-notch ingredients. Complementing the meal was the guacamole, which was notably fresh and added a burst of zesty taste. The ambiance of the place was decidedly hip, with an added touch of whimsy from the hanging egg chairs that provided a fun and unique dining experience. As for the value, the prices were quite reasonable for the quality of food and experience provided. This spot is definitely on my list for a return visit!

Title: "Affordable and Strong Drinks Reign at 212"

If you're on the hunt for potent, yet reasonably priced drinks in NYC, look no further than 212. On my recent Saturday visit, I was pleasantly surprised by the change in ambiance. The previously overpowering loud music has been swapped out for calmer, elevator-style melodies that set a perfect backdrop for an evening out.

The margarita remains my go-to choice; their generous pours never disappoint. To complement your drink, I highly recommend adding an order of crispy calamari and fries to the mix. Trust me, it's a winning combination.

In short, 212 offers the best value for your money when it comes to enjoying a drink or two in the city. Without a doubt, it's my top pick for a budget-friendly night out with a side of serenity.

Title: A Brunch Delight with Spirited Service

My recent brunch experience at this restaurant was an absolute pleasure, defined by a great ambiance, high-quality food, and top-notch service. Although the seating arrangement was a bit chaotic for larger groups, it's a minor hiccup in an otherwise delightful dining experience.

The service truly shined; we were treated with care by our wonderful waiter who was not only friendly but attentive, ensuring our basket of chips was never empty and seasoning our meal with good humor.

We indulged in a variety of dishes:
- The smooth Rosie's Margaritas are a must-try, especially by the pitcher. (5/5)
- Flavorful Carne asada plato and Torta chorizo, both satisfying choices for meat lovers.
- The Chips and guac offered a generous portion, complemented by delightful guac and salsas that weren't too spicy. (4.5/5)
- The Bistec steak taco was memorable for its juicy, well-seasoned goodness. (5/5)
- While the Pescado was the lighter fare, it was perfectly crispy, though it could use a flavor boost. (4.5/5)

In conclusion, this restaurant is a brilliant choice for those who appreciate friendly service and great food. Despite a slight seating struggle, the experience left us more than content and eager to return.

Took my dad here when he came into the city to visit this past weekend because his name is Jake too ha. When we walked in (around 1PM on a Saturday) it was pretty dead. Just a few people at the bar and that's it, we thought they were closed. We sat wherever we wanted and the bartender shouted to us from across the bar asking us what we wanted to drink. (Honestly, I liked this haha. Very cool vibe to someone just yelling to you from across the room.) She then came over to take our orders, I got the turkey burger with no bun and French fries. When I received my meal they gave me tater tots instead (whatever, that's fine.) The turkey burger was fine, really nothing exciting about it though- and the pickle on the side literally just tasted like a cucumber. They bring the food in from a place next door where they make it, but it was still warm upon arrival to our table. The waitress was very nice and attentive. Honestly, I feel like this is just a place to come for drinks not so much the food. The food is probably just good for drunk people to have while they're there, but I wouldn't choose this as a dinner destination.  They had beer pong cups and a table set up in the back where a group of younger people were playing and seemingly having a good time (very cool!) And a sign on the wall that said they'll make you a spiked coffee (BYOC- bring your own coffee) which I think is such a cool idea! They didn't have the Yankee game on which I think is strange considering it's a bar in NYC. All in all this place was fine. I think I'd come here for the happy hour if I wanted a drink or just for a little pre going out pit stop in my evening for something cheap and good. Definitely seemed like a "locals" bar of people that are there all the time and know each other. Don't come here for the food, plenty of other places around to choose from.

Out of all the restaurants I dined at in my 7 nights in New York, I was least impressed with Lattanzi. It was recommended to me by a friend who has introduced me to some great restaurants in the Chicagoland area, so I was expecting much more than I received. The restaurant itself is a nice space and with a garden dining area in the back which we were shown to for dinner. Our server never introduced himself, which is a pet peeve of mine. He was not engaging and had very little interaction with us other than the basic. We ordered a bottle of wine, and received the bread service. After Gato and Saju Bistro, the bread basket was underwhelming for an Italian restaurant, diner quality.  I shared the mozzarella pomodoro with my husband. That was the best thing we ate here. The cheese was so fresh and tasted homemade. For dinner, my husband had the lasagna and I had the salmon with fennel. I requested no potatoes and extra veggies with my salmon - that didn't happen. Our server was not checking back with us so I never said anything and just ate the salmon and left the potatoes on my plate. Our entrees were not bad at all, typical fare. Overall, I wouldn't recommend Lattanzi as it was #7 out of the seven restaurants we dined at for dinner.

Title: Fresh Flavors Hit the Spot at Local Gem

On a recent visit with my dad, we stumbled upon this quaint spot, a stone's throw from our hotel. Eager to satiate our craving for good bread, which was left unfulfilled by a previous dining experience, we decided to give their offerings a go. This place serves up breakfast through dinner, catering to those with a penchant for fresh, light bites.

Our choice, the smoked salmon tartine, proved to be a revelation. The salad was dressed to impress, and the golden, toasted bread base a crunchy pedestal for the impeccably balanced flavors above. Creamy creme fraiche perfectly complemented the salmon's brininess, with an egg on top to round off the dish.

Dessert was equally divine. I opted for a duo of macarons - the strawberry bursting with fruity zest, while my dad favored the classic vanilla. In short, this eatery delivered a meal that was nothing short of delightful.

Title: A Brunch Worth Waiting For at The Foragers Table

I recently had the pleasure of visiting The Foragers Table for brunch, and it was a delightful experience. Although the wait time was a bit lengthy for our party of five on a busy weekend, the adjacent mini Mart offered a pleasant distraction.

The restaurant's interior captivated us with its natural light pouring in from large windows, complemented by high-top tables and stools that provide a perfectly balanced aesthetic of rustic charm and industrial chic. Service was commendably attentive without being intrusive, striking just the right note of hospitality.

The highlight of our meal had to be the pancakes we decided to share. These fluffy treats, with just a hint of citrus tang, achieved a sublime level of mellow sweetness – and for those with a sweeter tooth, a drizzle of honey is available. Accompanying my meal, the latte was expertly crafted, and the salad was notably fresh, featuring poached eggs cooked to perfection.

For a visual taste of our experience, check out the Instagram snapshot at @phothegram. If you're in search of a satisfying brunch with a cozy ambiance, The Foragers Table should be at the top of your list.

Title: A Slice of Spain in Hudson Yards - Mercado Little Spain

I recently discovered a gem in Hudson Yards Mall, an unexpected delight on the basement floor. Mercado Little Spain is a vibrant Spanish enclave teeming with market stalls, sit-down eateries, and tapas bars, reminiscent of a bustling Little Italy but with an Iberian twist.

Despite a substantial wait time for a table at the sit-down restaurant - ranging from half an hour to 45 minutes - my dining partner and I opted for one of the more casual food kiosks. Initially perched at a bistro-style stand-up table, we soon snagged a more comfortable spot to enjoy our meal.

Our choice for the evening was a classic Spanish seafood paella, which did not disappoint. Paired with a refreshing Spanish sparkling wine, it was a delectable experience at a premium price point. We rounded off our meal with some exquisite Spanish pastries and robust coffee.

The atmosphere of Mercado Little Spain is dynamic and joyful, with decor, music, and an ebullient crowd that collectively transport diners straight to Spain. It's a perfect culinary prelude to my upcoming tour of the country.

Having sampled other restaurants in Hudson Yards on previous visits, Mercado Little Spain stands out for its casual yet immersive Spanish ambiance. Open daily from 5 pm until 11 pm, it's a must-visit for anyone looking to indulge in a little Spanish escapism in the heart of New York City.

Great authentic reasonably-priced food. I regularly visit the one at the Empire State Building. You can tell that this location is new. Everything is very neat and clean. Very spacious as well. I only wish that there were combos or deals that include (3 tacos for ??). I also don't know if there is a happy hour there. That would also be appreciated.

Title: A Cozy Thanksgiving Feast at The Clockwork Bistro

My girlfriend and I decided to spend our Thanksgiving evening indulging in the prix fixe dinner at The Clockwork Bistro, an establishment with an entrance that evokes the grandeur of its namesake. Admittedly, I had expected more horological decor inside, yet found myself admiring mere pictures rather than actual clocks.

Nevertheless, the dining experience was nothing short of delightful. The standout dish for me was the perfectly seared scallops, followed by a succulent New York Strip steak, which did require an additional $20 but was well worth the splurge. We both reveled in the complimentary bread served at the start of our meal—springy, piping hot, and a perfect match for the delectable homemade butter.

Service at The Clockwork Bistro was commendable—attentive without being intrusive, delivering both quick and efficient attention to our dining needs.

In sum, the experience left us curious and excited to return for a taste of their regular menu. The Clockwork Bistro has certainly etched a memorable spot in our hearts for holiday dining.

My recent visit to this new neighborhood gem certainly satisfied my culinary cravings. The menu offered a tantalizing fusion of flavors, and we dove into dishes like lobster noodles and avocado gado gado, both of which were outstanding and highly recommendable. The corn fritters were a delightful bite, crisp and flavorful.

While the oxtail soup's tender meat hit the mark, the broth's overpowering aroma detracted from the overall enjoyment. However, the true star of our evening was the shared passionfruit pandan custard dessert. Its perfect balance of sweet and tart had us scraping the plate clean—a must-try that would easily lure me back.

The service matched the quality of the food—attentive but not intrusive. Wayan brings a refreshing twist to Indonesian cuisine, and it's a spot I'd urge food lovers to check out.

I came here with some of my old co-workers and the new interns and we all enjoyed our experience. There is the Smith & Wollensky side of the restaurant, which I believe is a bit more classy, and there is the Wollensky Grill which has more of a bar vibe. We made a last minute reservation, but the servers were very nice and made a table just for us to sit. Although they were dressed to the T, they were a lot of fun and nice. Order:- English cut prime rib (4/5)- Filet mignon (5/5)- House-made wollensky burger (5/5)- Roast beef hash (5/5)- Side: Asparagus (4/5)- Side: Hashed browns (5/5)- Side: Creamed spinach (4/5)- Side: Macaroni & cheese (4/5)- Dessert: Chocolate ganache cake (4/5)- Dessert: Coconut layer cake (4/5)- Dessert: Sticky toffee pudding (5/5)Pros:- Great tasting food - Great service - Good options to choose from Cons:- Expensive - Not the best prime rib I've had - Very loud restaurant Overall:- A very good restaurant to go to. If you're looking for a more intimate experience, I'd recommend going next door to Smith & Wollensky

This place has a really great a lunch deal. You get an appetizer, mint lemonade and bowl of pho for $15! Best deal in NYC! For the appetizer, I had the crispy spring rolls which were pretty typical. My hubby had the pork summer roll which was way better-we go excited when we saw it had a spam like slice of ham/pork-delicious! They apparently make the sauce that goes with it. So yummy! We both ordered the chicken pho because well, the sign outside said it was the best in NYC. Plus, we never had it before. Honesty, it is quite bland for our tastes. We spiced it up with their special sauce and that made it much better. Nevertheless, we were happy that we tried it! Great service too. The mint lemonade was also delicious! We were stuffed when we left! Thank you!

For starters, this is not a sushi place but a Japanese restaurant focused on "Katsu" which is meat that has been pounded thin and then breaded with Japanese panko.
