You can find a variety of katsu and sashimi in this place. Everything we had was amazing, very flavorful and well prepared and presented. One thing that caught my attention was that there were a few Japanese costumers really enjoying the place, so I guess this is closer to the real thing.

Title: Valentine's Disappointment at The Sea Grill

We had looked forward to celebrating Valentine's Day at The Sea Grill, a restaurant that holds a special place in our hearts. Sadly, our annual tradition was marred by a confusing and costly experience.

Despite making our reservation via OpenTable with no mention of a special prix-fixe menu, we were unknowingly opted into one priced at $95 per person. Our server did not clarify this until after we received a shockingly high bill. We thought we had ordered moderately - a Seafood Platter ($18) we were quoted turned out to be $38, and Crab Cakes ($12) - on top of the prefixed steak and salmon ($95 each) that we initially didn't realize we were committed to.

The staff seemed more interested in upselling than in ensuring a pleasant dining experience, and our request for the check was met with a push for additional dessert or coffee purchases.

When we reached out to management the next day, they acknowledged the lack of clear communication but only offered complimentary desserts on a future visit, which falls short of addressing the principle of the matter. Their inability to rectify their mistake in a more significant manner has left us with a sour taste, and now "our restaurant" is associated with feelings of frustration and disappointment.

This Valentine's experience was unforgettable for all the wrong reasons, and it's with regret that we'll remember The Sea Grill not for the love and celebration but for the dissatisfaction and unresolved issues.

This restaurant consistently delivers an exceptional dining experience. Every visit is a delight with quality food, inviting ambiance, and top-notch service. It's a place you can count on to exceed expectations time and time again. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a reliable spot that never lets you down.

I recently visited this spot for a to-go Nutella milkshake on a late Saturday afternoon and was pleasantly surprised by the quick service. The milkshake itself was delightfully thick, just how I like it. However, be warned, the restaurant's current situation amidst building construction makes it a bit challenging to find. The scaffolding almost caused me to miss it, so keep a sharp lookout when you head over.

Title: A Taste of Guangzhou in the Heart of NYC

Last week, I had the pleasure of visiting the newly opened Guangzhou-style steamed rice rolled noodle chain in New York City. Despite its fame, I was pleasantly surprised to find the wait time was a manageable 20 minutes, a testament to its popularity.

What's intriguing is that this establishment doesn't offer takeout or delivery yet, though they permit to-go orders while dining in-house. It's a clever tactic that might be aimed at managing the initial rush.

The food itself is a comforting embrace of traditional Guangzhou cuisine. The congees and you tiao (crispy fried dough) combo was the standout for me, delivering that soul-warming satisfaction. The restaurant's focus is evidently on the fillings, with generous amounts of well-marinated meats that overshadow the rice noodles—a stark and welcome contrast to Joe's @steamriceroll, which may have silkier noodles but can't compete with the generous and cost-effective stuffings here.

Value-wise, this spot is a clear winner, offering three times the stuffing for half the price compared to their competitors. Service was also remarkably efficient for a quick-service eatery that's still finding its feet.

For first-timers, I highly recommend their preserved egg congee, Lai wan style congee, beef rice roll, and the you tiao. And don't miss out on the hk curry fish balls—they are simply divine. If you're in NYC and craving authentic Guangzhou flavors, this is a must-visit destination.

I came here for brunch on a Sunday at noon. Curiously enough, there was only one other party in the restaurant before my friend and I arrived. The garden area was so pretty- it's a nice surprise to see this in the middle of Hells Kitchen. It doesn't seem like a very touristy spot at all. I feel that this place deserves closer to a 3.5. I ordered the poached eggs with jumbo lump crab cake and hollandaise sauce. I also got one mimosa (they do have an interesting deal where you can get unlimited mimosas, bellinis, or bloody Mary's for 2 hours at just $18. If I weren't so hungover I would have wanted that). While there wasn't anything particularly wrong with the food (eggs were runny, salad was dressed, temperature was ok) I didn't think that there was anything particularly special. The crab cake could have more crab chunks, the slice of not crispy toast below the eggs added little value. It kinda needed something else to give it some oomph. Not dying to return anytime soon.

A solid brunch spot in the heart of one of the touristy spots in New York- right next to Penn Station.The close location to Penn reflects how touristy this place can get- however it still executes and provides a good brunch spot at a central location if meeting up with people coming from different locations.Got the steak and eggs, comes with fries and a jalapeño sour cream- overall very solid and was happy with my dish.

I was strolling around SoHo at lunch time on a Monday & chose this place due to their $10 lunch special sign out front, prior YELP reviews & the fact that it was small & open air on a beautiful sunny day. I started with a glass of chilled Prosecco and the octopus salad & then ordered the orecchiette with shrimp which was only $10 at lunch. It was a massive portion with spicy sauce served in a huge metal sauce pan with a handle. After my appetizer this portion would have been enough to split with two other people (and I can eat lot). I ate half & unfortunately did not have a refrigerator in my hotel room so I could not take home the leftovers. Service was friendly. Water refilled often. Definitely worth a lunch stop.

Came here with a few friends last night for my birthday dinner! This is an old school steakhouse, very cool exterior which has pipes signed by famous bankers throughout the years.We all ended up ordering various cuts of steaks and  2 sides, creamed spinach and the Yukon gold mashed potatoes.To drink, we each got a glass of red wine, and the pour was very generous!The steaks were okay, they came out as we ordered.  The portions were larger then I thought, so we ended up taking most of it home.For dessert we ended up getting the better scotch and hot fudge sundaes.The service was fantastic and the food was great!

Honestly went in with low expectations but my wife simply loves Ukrainian and Russian style cuisine. The potato pancake was ridiculously good and went well with the apple sauce. Stuffed cabbage roll was pretty good and had great red cabbage on the side. The beef stroganoff flavor was good but the texture of the beef could have been better, it was not that tender. Overall though good service for a diner and they're open 24/7.4.5/5 stars

Opening night Wednesday.sleek and sexy spot from Denver restauranteurs, on Greenwich Ave next to Rosemary's is live! Love the name which represents the small but feisty.owmer and vibe. The flavors are upscale Southwestern with a carefully curated menu.Ate:Mussels EscebecheHake with turnipsTotal $37House made mussels are a rich treat with buttery bread and hake is absolutely heavenly in a beurre blanc sauce. I am excited to try more! The lovely dishes are from Gowanus (note pics) and playing is lovely. Welcome to the nabe Banty Rooster. You are petite but mighty in flavor. Owner Dolores from Denver and server from Harlem Jamilla are awesome!I was there opening night(note photos) actually  at the restaurant eating and experiencing and truly the first to review!

Title: A Slice of Heaven in the West Village - Artistic Pizza

After a bustling day of city adventures, we stumbled upon the quaint gem that is Artistic, nestled in the West Village. This pint-sized pizzeria, with its cozy seating for four, was a serendipitous find. It caters marvelously to both vegan and omnivore palates alike, striking the perfect harmony in price, size, and taste.

Although we had eyed Screamers in Brooklyn for its famed vegan slices, the lengthy commute dissuaded us. Fortuitously, Artistic emerged on our route home, boasting an impressive vegan selection. The experience exceeded every expectation—staff were welcoming, the ambiance exuded cool, and the food was exceptional.

For anyone seeking an inclusive pizza haven with a laid-back vibe, Artistic is a stellar choice. Definitely put it on your list—a resounding 100% recommendation from this happy couple!

Laut Singapura, the sibling establishment to the acclaimed Michelin-starred Laut, impresses with its charm and casual ambience that mirrors the vibrant dining scenes of Singapore. The restaurant strikes a delightful balance, offering a beautifully designed space without sacrificing the authentic feel of a typical Singaporean eatery.

The culinary offerings are nothing short of excellent, evoking a true sense of nostalgia for those familiar with Singaporean flavors. Each dish is a testament to the expressive yet balanced taste profiles characteristic of the region's cuisine.

As of my visit, the restaurant was still in anticipation of its liquor license. The absence of a beverage menu is a temporary shortcoming that, once addressed, will undoubtedly enhance the dining experience.

Service-wise, the staff brings a level of warmth and amiability to the table. Although they haven't quite perfected their efficiency, their pleasant demeanor contributes positively to the overall atmosphere.

In summary, Laut Singapura is a commendable destination for anyone seeking to indulge in authentic Singaporean dishes in a setting that exudes a relaxed yet refined vibe. With time, and with its anticipated full beverage service, it promises to evolve into an even more enticing dining spot.

Beautiful restaurant with a limited menu and ok service. I visited with a few work colleagues and my boss for a quick lunch, and it certainly could have been better. The menu was very diverse but small. After much debating I - along with 3 others - decided to go with the Lobster Tortellini ($25). They had a lunch special for Pasta which included a glass of wine for $22.  Initially my boss asked if we could do the special without the wine but the waiter was not giving in. I ended up having a glass of Pinot Noir which was good. While waiting we received some delicious complimentary bread with olive oil - we ended up ordering seconds later on. Once we got our entrees however, I was a bit disappointed. Although tasty, the food was hardly lukewarm and it did not seem a substantial portion for the price. I had noted that they serve pizza in some of the reviews but I guess that is only during dinner. Service was nothing special, I actually felt it was a bit slow considering the restaurant was nearly empty. Not sure I'd come back.

Came here before a Broadway play for dinner. A Saturday around 6pm. We were seated downstairs which was great because it was less crowded but service was still quick and we didn't want to miss our play which started at 8pm. We left here at around 7:30. With no feeling of being rushed or delayed. We had more than enough time to walk to the theater which was great. My favorite part of the entire meal was the grilled lamb chops. The Camarón a ajillo was bland, the pulpo a la gallega was meh with chunks sliced too thick and the tortilla was just ok. Ive had better elsewhere. Hubs had the arroz con pollo and left most of it. The rice seemed parboiled and not made from scratch at all. Most of the meals were subpar. We both shared the chops and ate it all. The Sangria was decent as was the service. The waiter was attentive and quick. I wont ever be back though. It wasn't a memorable experience.

What a delightful restaurant experience we enjoyed here. Island has an attractive, rather intimate dining room with a little space for sidewalk tables, and the theme is sort of yacht-like without going overboard about it (keep in mind the restaurant's name). And the eclectic menu offers some appealing seafood dishes without slipping into Red Lobster mode. For instance, you can find some delicious crispy calamari, a tasty lobster quesadilla, Maryland crab cake sliders and a moist and lightly crusted yellowfin tuna burger if you are so inclined. We did and relished all but the crab cakes, which weren't bad at all but lacked the bursting crab meat flavor we've found at a few other restaurants (looking at you Guppy's in Florida). We also, however, tried the Kobe beef hot dog, an item we have never seen anywhere before this. When served, it looked almost like the Oscar Meyer weinermobile, neatly curved over a bun and packed with lots of sauerkraut. The verdict? Gimme' more. We didn't try any of the desserts though our server said we would be missing something good. No doubt. The wait staff seemed attentive and friendly though not obtrusive. In general, the atmosphere is not quite laid back but spiffy and focused as you might hope the staff on your yacht would be. As we said, a good experience, and given it's location not far from a family member's home, we'll certainly return.

I don't know why all the negative reviews.  So let me just set the scene, we were at the Waitress show across the street and during intermission I start to Yelp surrounding restaurant in the area to eat after the show.  I want something quick and some place that opens late and also not something that's totally horrible.  Ok now I am a foodie, check my other reviews so I am not a tourist from Iowa ( nothing against you Iowa) but I have a sophisticated palate and that being said I also know what I should be expecting when it comes to type of restaurant and it's food.  I know this is a sports bar type of place, a chain corporate restaurant.  So I expect the food to be consistent and also bar food.  Now comes the review of 5 stars, it is 5 stars because I expected the wings to be good since it is the name of the place ( I have never been in any other BWW) and I know it will be loud and with tons of TV.  It all lived up to the expectation of being a bar restaurant, the wings were good and the chicken tacos were great and fried pickles were awesome.  I didn't come here for a 5 star Michelin tasting menu like Eleven Madison ( which by the way sucked) but I expected bar food and served fast.  It all delivered and as for the service? I thought our waitress was wonderful she made great suggestions of different types of sauces and it was all good,  the food came fast so it satisfied what I needed so this 5 stars is just as equivalent as my other fancy restaurant reviews.

Came here for the Akamura ramen and Bao Buns and they were excellent. Both items were really, really good. You can't go wrong with either. Service was a little slow this afternoon but the food was totally worth it.

Came for dinner with a party of 3 on a Friday night during happy hour. Unfortunately, the happy hour menu was only available for bar seating. We ordered the truffle fries, crab guac, classic white wine mussels and bisque mussels. They definitely didn't skimp on the guac- the guac to chip ratio was like 2:1!!!! We ended up not finishing the guac because we didn't have enough chips. We all preferred the bisque mussels because it was just a bit more flavorful! Their complimentary bread was so soft and warm on the inside and crispy on the outside. The truffle fries were pretty standard I guess. We opted for 4 of their doughnuts for dessert. We agreed our favorite actually ended up being the plain cinnamon sugar dipped in the vanilla icing on the side. Coming here definitely satisfies a seafood/mussel craving!

Title: A Trendy Twist on Chinese Cuisine in the Heart of NYC

Upon entering this modern-meets-grunge Chinese eatery, the vibrant ambience of New York City is unmistakable. The restaurant thrives with an exciting decor that sets the stage for a casual yet funky dining experience.

The menu, albeit slightly Americanized, offers dishes that satisfy a craving for Chinese flavors. The standout is undoubtedly the innovative pork belly with cotton candy; an adventurous blend of savory and sweet, even if the sugary garnish falls short of enhancing the meat's natural richness.

The chicken wings, dusted with a lightly sweet dry rub, may disappoint those in search of a kick, as the heat is notably absent. In contrast, the fried rice delivers comfort in every bite and is executed quite well.

A slight letdown comes from the shrimp dumplings and soup dumplings, whose fillings are generous but are encased in a skin just a tad too thick for connoisseurs of delicate wrappers.

The drink selection errs on the side of sweetness, a pattern in this establishment, yet these concoctions are undeniably refreshing.

This spot shines as a destination for groups seeking a hip setting and dishes that hit the spot for a night out. While it won't pacify purists in search of authentic Chinese cuisine, it does offer an enjoyable, if not entirely traditional, culinary experience.

Title: Authentic Hand-Pulled Noodles with Room for Improvement

Located in the heart of Chinatown, this restaurant offers a decent experience for those craving hand-pulled noodles. After multiple visits, their consistency is notable, albeit not outstanding. The service and decor are rather basic, so set your expectations accordingly.

A pleasant surprise, the dumplings here arguably outshine the main attraction – they are a must-try. As for the beef noodle soup, the beef itself is wonderfully tendinous, offering an enjoyable chew. However, the broth falls short as it arrived lukewarm, and the noodles, while hand-pulled, were disappointingly on the tougher side.

A word of caution for the cleanliness-conscious: the tables and shared sauces might leave you somewhat concerned. Overall, this place is an acceptable option for a quick noodle fix, but there's definitely room for improvement, particularly in the warmth of the soup, noodle texture, and cleanliness standards.

It was fall in NYC and our group was down for some ramen. My group of 8 arrived just before 12pm and were seated immediately. Space is small, but accommodated us comfortably. The name and the decor are inspired by Dragon Ball Z. There's even a neon light image of the character, Goku on the wall.I tried the Takoyaki $8 and the Spicy Tonkotsu Ramen $15. The takoyaki app came with four perfectly fried octopus balls. They were tasty and had a nice drizzle on top. The spicy tonkotsu was delicious! The broth was rich, creamy, and flavorful. It had a nice kick, but I didn't think it was that spicy. The pork was tender. Solid meal overall and service was fast.

Title: Cozy Brunch Haven with Tasty Fare

My recent brunch at this spot was a delightful experience. Despite my tardy arrival, the staff was accommodating, seating us promptly. We savored the gravy and biscuit skillet, which struck the perfect balance of heartiness without being overwhelming. The lox bagel platter, a simple yet satisfying assembly-your-own dish, also pleased our palates. The hot spiked mulled apple cider provided a soothing remedy for my sore throat, an indulgent touch albeit not the healthiest choice. The ambiance added to the charm, featuring comfy and quaint interior seating. Service efficiency was the cherry on top. Would wholeheartedly urge anyone to visit for an enjoyable brunch.

Title: A Tasty Experience at Clay Pot with Room for Toppings

I recently had the pleasure of accepting an invitation from owner Alex to dine at the new West Village location of Clay Pot. Accompanied by a friend, we were promptly seated at 7 PM on a Friday, just before a line began to form, hinting at the restaurant's popularity.

Service was swift and attentive, with our server exuding warmth and efficiency. I opted for the two topping clay pot featuring eel and pork belly. Presentation wise, the pot appeared generous, but the reality was a bit unbalanced: a substantial amount of rice overshadowed the four slices of pork belly and two pieces of eel, supplemented by a modest assortment of vegetables (two broccoli florets, a small tofu piece, and a spoonful of corn), along with half an egg.

The flavors were exceptional, yet I couldn't help feeling a hint of disappointment at the topping-to-rice ratio, especially given the $13 price tag per pot. Despite this, the overall dining experience was positive, and the restaurant's cleanliness and the inclusion of a restroom are commendable.

Clay Pot offers a delightful culinary journey, though a more equitable toppings distribution could enhance the experience. Still, I’m grateful for the opportunity to sample their fare and recommend timing your visit to avoid the rush.

I recently visited Mariachi's for a Meal Pal lunch and was so impressed that I'm eager to return for dinner. The meal exceeded my expectations; it was delicious and perfectly cooked. Prepared fresh upon my arrival, the dish was completed with a satisfying serving of rice and beans. As someone from the Southwest, I have high standards for Mexican cuisine, and Mariachi's met them with ease. I highly recommend this establishment for an authentic and delectable dining experience. Awesome meal, indeed!

Let's start off with we have a high standard for sushi. There are just too many good omakase places but this place beats many of our expectations. They offer a 9 piece omakase with one hand roll for the price of 45 dollars! What a great deal! You can always add on pieces of uni, botan ebi, chuntoro and other things they have that day. The pieces were delicious and fresh. my favorite was the tuna with truffle tofu! The sushi rice was made to the perfect taste. The chef was friendly and made us two pieces of crispy rice spicy tuna that we were looking at when another table ordered it. They have a small selection of sakes but you can do a sake flight for 35 dollars which has 3 glasses of tasting sakes. They were all yummy and served in wine glasses. Definitely a new got spot for sushi. The rolls all look amazing and we look forward to try more rolls here next time. There are only 4 sushi omakase spots on the sushi bar so be sure to book in advance. They're not on opentable yet but you can book on the yelp app.

I have always been a fan of Maison Pickle, frequenting it for the last two years, but my most recent visit was deeply disappointing and has me questioning a return. Despite a reservation and arriving early, we endured a nearly hour-long wait while others were promptly seated. Our small party size didn't justify the oversight, particularly in a nearly empty restaurant with vacant tables. The hostess, more absorbed by her phone than guest concerns, only responded after being directly confronted. Regrettably, this experience turned a once beloved spot into a complete letdown.

Not a place for vegetarians and vegan peeps. We were told everything entree had fish sauce and there were only 2 options for us on the menu for entrees. They were ok..we got spring rolls and dumplings too. Spring rolls were good but dumplings were bland and dry.Place was good looking though. I wouldn't go back.

After enduring a 40-minute wait at Jack's Wife Freda, I was apprehensive about the dining experience ahead. The menu, a bit peculiar with its limited selections, initially left me doubtful. However, I was pleasantly surprised when I took a bite of the Madame Freda. This dish, a creative rendition of the classic croque madame, was an unexpected delight – a perfectly harmonious blend of arugula, onion, duck bacon, and cheese. It was exactly what I craved without even knowing it. My companions were equally pleased with their choices: Jack's Breakfast and shakshuka. While the service could have been warmer, it was efficient. Overall, Jack's Wife Freda deserves its 4.5-star acclaim.

Good food and cheap for the area. The chicken teriyaki with mushrooms was delicious and flavorful. It comes with rice, a couple of pieces of sweet carrots, and a sauce that tastes a bit like thousand island salad dressing. Mix your food with the sauce for creaminess and even more flavor!

Quality sushi and great service, but prices seemed to be very high and the environment felt a little cramped.They have a very wide selection of cold Sake, highly recommend getting a bottle, although it will cost you around $75 for the average bottle.Keep in mind that what you see on the menu is not everything that's available. You can mix and match usual sushi and roll combinations, and there's also a "secret" sushi menu for more interesting one pieces. The fatty tuna cost $7 a piece when we were there.Whole dinner cost about $400 for 4 people including tip with one bottle of Sake. It's a good spot, but just seems to be very expensive. There were no "showstoppers" or visual effects like putting anything on fire etc. They didn't have crispy rice or even a vegetable gyoza. They should work on appealing more to the vegan and kosher crowd.

Title: Boka – A Lively Spot with Room for Culinary Improvement

Tucked away in a less-traveled alley and shrouded by a dreary rainfall, Boka stands as a bustling beacon of energy on a bustling Friday night. The ambiance is immediately welcoming, buoyed by the remarkably friendly and attentive wait staff who are not shy to steer spice enthusiasts away from potential overestimation of their tolerance. Heed their advice and you may find enjoyment in their recommended Medium Wings & Drums Combo or perhaps the Seafood Pancake – though, manage expectations accordingly.

Pro tip upon arrival: check in for a complimentary shot of soju, a pleasant touch considering the absence of cocktail offerings that their St Marks sibling boasts. Speaking of beverages, if you're yearning for a summer refreshment, the promise of watermelon soju may be a redeeming reason for a seasonal visit.

However, culinary speaking, Boka's dishes leave the palate wanting. The Soy Garlic wings were too ambitious with salt while the Seafood Pancake, regrettably, fell apart in a soggy defeat instead of presenting itself with that desirable crisp edge.

Despite the flawless service, picking up dishes and refilling glasses with a nearly telepathic sense of timing, the food itself struggles to match up. And a word to the wise: pack your cash, as plastic won't pass here.

In summary, Boka offers warmth and welcome in staff spirit but has yet to find its footing in perfecting its plates. It's a place I'm willing to revisit, if not for the cuisine, then for the novelty of a watermelon soju on a hot summer's day.

Title: A Gem for Hand Roll Enthusiasts

If a six-star rating was possible, this culinary gem would be its first recipient. The concept is deceptively simple - sit at the bar and feast on hand rolls crafted before your very eyes, each taking merely a heartbeat to create. Yet, the execution is nothing short of extraordinary.

The hand rolls are divine; each one bursts with high-quality fish paired with perfectly warm rice. The set menu offers an exceptional value, with a 6-piece set that will tantalize your taste buds without draining your wallet. We couldn't resist indulging in a few more, including a lavish $16 specialty roll. Even then, the total bill for an ample meal for two was a reasonable $68.

This was more than a meal; it was an experience that left us in awe. The value is unbeatable, the food unforgettable. We are already planning our next visit. This place isn't just good; it's "wow" good.

Oh my goodness!!! The dim sum here is SO GOOD!!! I was in the area for medical appointments at NYU Langone, and craving dim sum. I am so glad I found this place. It's a little difficult to find as the sign is not clear. The word FLAME is prominently on the door, another sign says Hibachi, then underneath that, is the word Dynasty Dim Sum. The place is modern. Not a typical dim sum joint so I was pleasantly surprised the dim sum dishes were SO GOOD!!! I got the spareribs fried, rice rolls with shrimp, lobster dumplings and of course...hello kitty buns. The flavors were authentic, not westernized. The shrimps were individually wrapped in rice rolls. I loved everything and the best part was the friendly and attentive service! This place's location to NYU makes me actually look forward to my medical appointments now.

Title: A Happy Hour Surprise and a Meal to Remember

My visit to this gem of a restaurant left me absolutely delighted! Stumbling upon their happy hour, which I was pleasantly surprised to discover runs until 7pm on Thursdays, was just the beginning. The atmosphere was welcoming as we transitioned from the bar to a cozy table for dinner.

Having teased my appetite by scrolling through their Instagram feed, the expectations for their food were high – and rightfully so. The loaded tots were indulgent, the surf and turf sliders were the perfect marriage of land and sea, and the tacos, oh the tacos, were a flavor fiesta. Each dish was so divinely delicious that our plates were left spotless.

Yes, the menu isn't the most extensive, focusing instead on delivering a variety of twists on a select few items. But when the food is this good, simplicity is a virtue. To top it all off, the warmth of the staff – with a shout-out to the owner or manager – made our night as they joined us for celebratory shots.

In short, if you're looking for great vibes and even better food, this is the spot you shouldn't miss!

Not the best but pretty good!We got the little hot pot + beef + enoki mushrooms + fish cakes and the bam bam noodles. They're pretty to look at but I do think there could have been a bit more depth in flavor, especially in the broth. Service was great and the interior is cute! I'd probably go again.

This is definitely my family and I's favorite dim sum place in Chinatown! We've come here so many times for weekend dim sum and will definitely keep coming again. They get super busy on the weekends and past 11:30 am, you'll probably have to wait for seating.They do the pushcart dim sum and the dim sum cart ladies are super nice. They always help us look for a specific dish when we ask for it and even go out of their way to look around for us. I always like to get the Spare Ribs Rice Noodles, Durian Pastries, and the Tripe. It's sooo good. If you like durian, definitely go for the pastries. Very few places serve durian pastries and I love it when it's fresh and hot. The tripe is always a good texture and I love the soup/sauce taste. The rice noodles are usually good but sometimes they're just ok because of the texture of the noodles. But I still order it every time because it's one of my favorite dishes.I'd highly recommend all three of these dishes, and I'm honestly salivating as I'm writing this review. Can't wait to go again!

Fast service, lots of menu options. It gets crowded all the time on the weekend! Great for group (many sitting options) and their yakidori is always on point with reasonable price. The service was great! They were very nice

I recently dined at a charming restaurant that exudes cuteness and coziness, making for a comfortable dining atmosphere. Although the service could have been more attentive, the culinary experience was delightful. The flavors and quality of the food were impressive enough to overshadow the service shortcomings. I would definitely recommend giving this place a try; the dishes are worth it.

Title: A Delightful Greek Feast at Milos

I recently visited Milos for a delightful lunch with my family, indulging in their $32 fixed price menu. Each course, from starters to entrees, offered generous proportions and exquisite taste.

The Greek salad I started with was a refreshing medley of ripe tomatoes, crisp cucumbers, sharp onions, and vibrant peppers, tied together with some of the most flavorful feta cheese I've tasted. The freshness of the vegetables was noteworthy. My family enjoyed a varied dip sampler, which surprisingly included a palatable fish egg dip alongside the classic tzatziki and a red pepper one, each dip proving to be as delectable as the last.

For mains, we sampled a range from a savory tuna burger to a perfectly cooked white fish, and a mouthwatering chicken dish from the lunch menu. All the entrees were packed with flavor and served in satisfying portions.

Beyond the food, the service at Milos was exceptional. The servers were attentive and went above and beyond to meet our needs, including charging a phone and providing hot water for my nephew.

Milos is a must-visit for anyone in search of authentic Greek cuisine paired with a warm atmosphere and top-notch service. I eagerly anticipate my next visit.

The Mercer Kitchen was a solid place to venture out for Restaurant Week. I had high expectations since it was a Jean-Georges restaurant, and while the ambiance was modern and hip, most of the food wasn't extraordinary.AppetizersTruffle Pizza - By far my favorite dish of the night. It's listed as an appetizer, but the personal pan would be more than enough as an entree. The pizza is a crunchy thin crust with a generous layer of fontina cheese, scattered truffle bits, and topped with greens. Would legitimately consider coming back just for this. Burrata - I'm lactose intolerant so I only had a small taste of this, which actually means I had about a quarter because this was tiny. The surrounding citrus basil salad added a sweet but slightly bitter kick.EntreesChicken Milanese - aka fancy schnitzel. I did like that the chicken wasn't too tough, which I found to be a common fault with thinly fried meats. Grilled Shrimp - This entree also suffered from unwanted tiny portion size. (There were only 5 jumbo shrimp pieces). Thankfully, this isn't on the standard menu so you won't have to fall prey to ordering this. The chimichurri sauce was tasty on its own, and I actually dipped into it with the complimentary bread. DessertMolten Chocolate Cake - Why do these restaurants always have the tiniest desserts. The one thing I enjoyed about this dessert was that the warmth of the cake complemented with the cool vanilla ice cream. The caramel brittle had a nice crunchy texture that differed from the otherwise soft dish. Lemon Eclair and Sherbert - Nothing worth writing home about. The sherbert also brought a cooling effect to the warm, lemony eclair. Service was prompt, though I wasn't surprised because they probably mass-prepared all of these dishes for Restaurant Week.

Title: A Classic NYC Burger Experience Worth the Wait

My boyfriend and I braved the bustling atmosphere of this cash-only gem on a Saturday night, and it didn't disappoint. Despite a 30-minute wait, which we pleasantly passed with drinks at the over-crowded bar, anticipation built up for what was to come. True to the no-reservation policy, early or odd-hour visits may save you some time.

Our orders – hamburger, cheeseburger, fries, and chili – were served up surprisingly fast given the crowd. The burgers, priced reasonably at $11.75 and $12.50 respectively, were simply divine. Arguably one of the best in NYC, they boasted flawless cooking and the bacon added a sublime touch. Complemented by the nostalgic decor, the dining experience oozed old-school charm.

In a nutshell, fantastic food, fair prices, and a vibrant atmosphere have secured our future return. Would highly recommend for a taste of authentic New York burger culture.

Title: A Rustic Gem with Unique Flavors near Hilton Times Square

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a charming restaurant just a stone's throw from the Hilton Times Square during my NYC visit. Despite its popularity, I was seated immediately upon arrival at 11:45 am, thanks to the efficient waitlist system on Yelp - a step I'd suggest future patrons take given the limited seating.

The rustic interior sets the scene for a menu filled with unique and tempting options. My choice, the Shakshuka with added feta cheese, over-medium fried egg, and a side of smoked salmon, was a flavor revelation. Served piping hot in a skillet with pita bites, the dish struck a perfect balance between the sweet tomatoes, aromatic garlic, and onion against the salty feta. The smoked salmon leveled up the dish, infusing it with an irresistibly umami essence.

For anyone looking for a standout meal near Times Square, this spot is a must-visit. I'm already planning my next meal here on my future NYC escapades. An absolute high recommendation!

Title: A Golden Experience at Thai Villa

I recently dined at Thai Villa, a Thai restaurant that truly deserves its 4.5-star rating for its stunning golden aesthetics reminiscent of the grandeur of the "Beauty and the Beast" ballroom. The interior is absolutely breathtaking, and the ambiance sets the stage for a unique dining experience.

A friend, a repeat patron, encouraged my visit post our Thailand trip, leaving me skeptical at first. However, Thai Villa's culinary offerings quickly dispelled my doubts. The menu, particularly the lunch specials, is reasonably priced between $13-$17, depending on the protein choice, and includes a soup or salad plus an appetizer.

I opted for the Green Curry with Tofu and Veggies, priced at $13. The dish carried an authentic taste and a formidable two-star spice level that is not for the faint of heart. My companions enjoyed the Red Curry, Panang Curry, and Pad Thai, each expressing satisfaction with their choices albeit a cautionary note on the spice levels.

Portions align more with traditional Thai standards than American ones, which some may find small, yet they were satisfactory for us. A Thai Iced Tea at $5 seemed steep in comparison to memories of 30 baht counterparts in Thailand, but it was undeniably pleasant.

Service at Thai Villa was nothing short of spectacular. Attentive servers frequently checked on us, ensuring an experience where our glasses remained full and our preferences catered to without feeling rushed, even as we lingered post-meal.

In conclusion, Thai Villa offers an affordable slice of luxury. While you do pay a premium for the splendid surroundings, the lunch specials provide a wallet-friendly gateway to a rich dining experience. I foresee many more visits to this Thai haven in the future.

Title: A Cozy Feast at the Local Izakaya

If you're a fan of authentic Japanese snack-sized dining, this izakaya will not disappoint. The variety is splendid, especially for yakitori enthusiasts. We indulged in an array of skewers including beef tongue, liver, cartilage, bacon-wrapped emoji, chicken meatballs, and gizzard, complemented by a grilled mackerel and a savory mussel soup.

The standout was, without a doubt, the liver—perfectly cooked and seasoned. Don’t miss the chicken meatballs; they come with a raw egg yolk dip that’s simply divine.

The only drawback was the ventilation. It struggled to clear out the smoky air, so expect your clothes and hair to carry a souvenir of your meal. Nevertheless, for a true izakaya experience with an extensive selection, this place hits the spot.

I recently dined at a pristine gem of a restaurant that truly stood out. The modern décor, complemented by clever lighting, immediately sets a welcoming tone, complete with a charming patio that's perfect for basking in warm weather. The curated playlists were a delightful backdrop, enhancing the Spanish ambiance so much so that I saved them to my Shazam.

The service was notably friendly and efficient, with staff members who were both agile and accommodating, ensuring a seamless dining experience. The vegan Mexican cuisine served here is nothing short of delectable. Despite the portions appearing modest, they were surprisingly satisfying.

From the appetizer to the dessert, each dish was packed with flavor. The drinks were not only crafty but also visually stunning, showcasing mixology at its finest. This place is a must-visit for anyone looking to indulge in vegan Mexican fare. I am already looking forward to coming back.

Decent neighborhood spot for ramen. The main vegetarian ramen option is the "veggie veggie ramen" which comes topped with tasty tofu skins. The second time I went, there was a seasonal "spicy creamy veggie ramen" which was pretty good although it could have been spicier and it could have been creamier. It unfortunately does not come with the tofu skins, though it does come with arugula, cherry tomatoes, mushrooms, and corn. The spicy edamame are tasty but covered in butter/oil to the point that I had to wash my hands afterward. The vegetarian gyoza are good but not worth getting again. Overall, I really don't have any complaints about the food/ambience/service at Mei Jin, but it just isn't the to-die-for ramen experience I'm looking for.

Tucked away on 46th Street, this gem of a restaurant may require a sharp eye to locate, but it's well worth the search. Bustling with patrons during lunch, the atmosphere is a testament to its popularity. Patrons will find the menu prices quite reasonable, a pleasant surprise for the wallet. Service is not only swift but also attentive, ensuring a delightful dining experience. The food impresses with its tastiness, and the drinks are exceptional, truly elevating the meal. I've fallen for this spot and highly recommend it to anyone looking for great food at a great value amidst the hustle of the city.

This place is a little pricey, but the food quality it 5 stars and it's a great place to chill with small groups or wow a first date. I have the 10 course omakase here and it was NOT disappointing.  Drink the Wasabi Mule for a light drink that makes the evening. The space is large and multilevel. Come here for the food and ambiance.

Retroactive to January 2018:Very much comparable to Chipotle. Better in some ways, inferior in others. Loved the Chipotle Crema. Strong portion of guac (see: Chipotle) but the actual guac was good, not great.In my opinion you've got a wider selection here but Chipotle has always stressed and prioritizedquality over quantity. Nonetheless, Blue Maiz is delicious.

Based on some of the experiences others had, I was a little apprehensive bringing a large group here. But on paper, it sounded like a perfect location for a friend's birthday (meat, meat, and some veggies for the less meat inclined eaters, with good cocktails and a speakeasy vibe). Rolled the dice, and lucked out, we had a great experience that wasn't at all lukewarm (the reviews about lukewarm food had me the most concerned)."Birthday Boy" and "Former New Yorker" arrived a little early and started on some snacks and drinks. By the time I arrived with some more of the party, they were happily perched at the bar. The hostess then guided us to our "Foxy's Lair" large booth. With 9, we were a little tight in the space, but we made it work.  Our server Shawn brought over limoncello compliments of the bartender to celebrate "Birthday Boy" and then started telling us his favorites off the menu. We didn't have anything that was bad, everything was decent, but some stood out more than others.Grand National Cocktail: Koch Mezcal, Blumen ApricotLime, Pineapple, Ginger - "Former New Yorker" and I quite enjoyed the slightly tart spicy cocktail to temper the flavorful dinner we had.Decent: Winter Citrus salad - it was a tad too much fennel for our preferences, but still very enjoyable; the sweetness of the pistachios and chili honey were a lovely contrast with the citrus, and is a great way to start a meat-centric mealCharred Broccoli - enjoyable, but overshadowed by the excellent brussel sproutsBone-in Ribeye - decent, but I've had many that were better, that tallo potato though? Someone please explain what that is to me, that was amazing and should be a dish on it's own! Where can I try more of this?!Steak au poivre - not my favorite cut of meat in general, but did enjoy the maitake mushrooms paired with it.French Fries - perfectly decent thin crispy fries, but if you have to pick one potato dish, stick with the crispy potatoes.Would skip next time: Croquettes - a little to dry for our likingSmoked Cabbage - not bad, just not memorableDelicious:Beef Tartare - we loved spooning this on pieces of the giant chipBone In Pork Belly: crunchy, spicy, sweet, toothsome - we enjoyed the contrasts so much we had three servings of this; definitely the stand out of the night.Beef Rib: cooked well, flavorful - there's a reason why so many are raving about thisHouse smoked sausage - I actually quite enjoyed the flavor of this, though they might have minced just a touch more than I usually prefer.Crispy Potatoes: with the mustard aioli, we started to fight over this before we gave up and just ordered moremac & cheese: I'm going to go against the majority of yelpers about this dish, our party enjoyed it. I don't know if we were just lucky that night, but ours were rich in flavor, al dente, and perfectly creamy.Brussel Sprouts - lovely texture and love the unique pairing with the blueberryThe desserts were all decent, but the black and blonde won over the pudding and sundae by a landslideBlack and Blonde: blondie bar, toasted meringue, hazelnutDulce caramel pudding, coffee crumble and bruleed bananasSadly I was unable to take any pictures of the food as our booth was in the red light zone, and I'm adamantly against using the flash feature. All in all, fun place to start off with a drink or to and then move onto an entirely satisfactory dinner as long as you stick to the best dishes.

Just like any place in Mexico authentic and delicious  We call it a whole in the wall here at home in NYC but this are the best places for this kind of food Mexican, Chinese, Indian or any minority cuisine no need to be fancy just good and this is just the way I like it. Sopes, Tortas, huaraches, chilaquiles, tostadas snd all the good street food all in one place I been coming here for 25 years or more and I'll keep coming here

We were having a relatively good day and this took our day up to a whole 'nother level. We got the pot of dirt looking dessert and the cornflakes, ice cream and banana dessert. They were both delish (pot of dirt one was slightly better). But we would definitely Italy return to try the other 2 desserts that piqued our interest (matcha lava cake and the money bread). We got seated right away but I think we were lucky and the staff was friendly enough.

I recently visited this cozy spot that truly shines with its drink selection, especially during happy hour. The outdoor seating adds a lovely ambiance perfect for a relaxed evening. Inside, the space is limited, but the cleanliness and attentive service more than make up for it. Definitely a place to consider for a laid-back drink with friends.

Had a great, relaxing dinner for my babe's birthday. It was my first time watching a jazz band with a singer and it was enthralling. We got a round table near the stage. The food was nothing special (the portions were not bad) but the drinks that they make are great! They were very unique, fresh and they make an array of them, as well has having an impressive selection of liquor.The service did not hover-which I love. The Flatiron Room is definitely a place to sit back and enjoy some good music and cocktails and would be a wonderful idea for date night.

Tucked away in a unique space that intriguingly straddles the basement and street level, this compact food hall transports diners straight to Spain with its array of vendors serving authentic Spanish dishes that reignited fond memories of my time in Madrid. There is ample seating available, but be forewarned: it's a popular spot that can quickly become crowded with tourists and the local lunch crowd.

Title: Perfect Casual Dinner at a Local Pizzeria

After a full day of sightseeing, we found a convenient spot for dinner just a stone's throw from our hotel. The ordering process at this no-frills pizzeria was straightforward - pick your slices, watch them warm up in the oven, and pay at the register. The best part? The affordability. We spent less than $25 to satisfy our family's appetite, which included four hearty slices of pizza, a set of garlic knots, and a bottle of soda.

My partner and I enjoyed the white pizza with spinach - simple yet savory. As for the kids, they devoured the pepperoni, supreme, and cheese slices with gusto, noting that the portion sizes were generous. The garlic knots were the only average note of the meal - slightly overdone for my taste, but still a decent complement to our slices.

All in all, this place was a fantastic choice for a relaxed dinner back in our hotel room.

Title: A Charming Spot with Tasty Bites and Happy Hour Delights

My recent visit to this adorable eatery was a delightful experience. The highlight was their generous happy hour from 3-7 PM, offering a variety of drinks and food options perfect for any palate. Whether you prefer cozying up at the bar or grabbing a table, comfort is guaranteed.

Despite it being a Monday evening, the atmosphere was lively yet not overcrowded, striking a perfect balance for a relaxed meal. The service staff made a great impression with their welcoming demeanor, enhancing the overall vibe of the place.

On to the food: The fish taco I ordered was a pleasant surprise with its meaty fillings and fresh, uncomplicated taste. The coconut ice cream stole the show with its rich, creamy texture, loaded with authentic coconut flavor in every spoonful—a generous serving adorned with playful sprinkles.

Our shared chips and guac were a hit in terms of portion size—ample enough for four, not just two. The guacamole was heaped on, much to our delight, although the chips themselves could have used a bit more salt to enhance their thick, crunchy bite.

Affordability isn't an issue here, and the clean, laid-back atmosphere makes it a place I'd gladly revisit or recommend checking out their other locations. A great spot for a casual bite that won't break the bank.

I recently found my new go-to spot for kicking off the weekend – and it might just be the best place to savor a margarita in town! Their Spicy Watermelon Margarita, crafted with Espolón silver tequila, triple sec, juicy watermelon, fiery serrano pepper slivers, sweet agave, and a rim dusted with chili-lime salt, is a masterpiece of flavors. It's the perfect balance of sweet and spicy – so good that stopping at one is not an option.

But this place isn't just about the drinks; the food stands on its own. The mixed appetizer platter paired wonderfully with the impeccably seasoned steak tacos, making the meal thoroughly satisfying.

The cherry on top is the adorable ambiance, decked out with charming fall decorations that make every corner 'Instagrammable.' If you're in the mood for great drinks, scrumptious eats, and a cozy atmosphere, don't miss out on this gem!

It's an amazing Mediterranean place. My bf and I got the selection of six tastings and two appetizers - falafel and cauliflower. I heard many good things about the Spicy feta. In addition, I love the Taramousalata (fish roe, a bit too salty though) and green Tahani. The cauliflower is flavored very well but almost too oily. The inside decoration was cute too.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Professor Thom's

My latest visit to Professor Thom's was a rollercoaster of highs and lows. The prospect of 50-cent wings on Wednesdays had been the main draw for my frequent patronage over the past 6 months, especially during sports nights like the NBA finals.

Pros: The original flavor wings, when served without sauce, are usually a stand-out.

Cons: However, this Wednesday, the excitement fizzled out when we were informed that the wings were full-priced, contrary to the usual deal. For 10 wings, I shelled out $14, which was a disappointment and a deviation from what we had come to expect.

Adding to the frustration, my attempts to confirm the weekly specials over the phone proved futile as calls went unanswered amidst a confusing automated menu.

Staff turnover also seems to be an issue, with new faces every visit hinting at deeper management problems.

The wings themselves this time felt like they'd been sitting around a tad too long - not quite stale, but not fresh either.

Overall Impression: Despite these setbacks, I'm rating Professor Thom's at 3.5 stars. The previous good times will bring me back, but the inconsistency with the special pricing and the less-than-fresh wings have tainted my view of this establishment.

My friend who was yesterday's birthday celebrant wanted Cuban for our celebration so I booked it here. We were given the table by the entrance al fresco style so that was appreciated.From a price standpoint, we paid $360++ for a group of 6. Not the cheapest and that's alright but we didn't appreciate the attitude of the guys bringing our food out and serving it like we're the ones who owe them a favor by being customers.They have a $25+ deal if you order entrees, that gets you unlimited drinks for 90 minutes. Champagne is included and I tried that but it's honestly like watered down with cerveza. I had it exchanged for a bellini and it was decent. I only had 2 despite what I paid for the Unlimited deal, it was that 'enjoyable'. My friends to be fair enjoyed and maximized the various different drinks that can be switched within the timed 90 mins.As for the food, I ordered the skirt steak and not only was it not cooked medium rare as requested, it was bland, needed seasoning. The only thing that stood out was the Beef Broccoli dish with noodles. The beef was tender and delicious. They did a nice little touch in coming out with a small custard with a birthday candle for the dessert. The dessert was just okay, overpowered by a citrusy taste.Careful when paying, we almost added a separate 'suggested' gratuity when 20% was actually already added.

Had a group brunch here on Sunday funday and it was so pleasant! I never get salmon for brunch, but the pictures online looked so appetizing I had to try it! The salmon Benedict was delicious and I tried some of Dan's poached egg spinach and potatoes and that was just as amazing. We got outdoor seating and it was the perfect weather to enjoy a nice meal with friends.

Title: Cozy Space with Fresh Offerings, Hit-or-Miss Flavors

I recently visited Kilo for a weekend dinner with three friends, having booked a table in advance. On arrival, I was struck by the restaurant's small size, which was emphasized by the bustling crowd. A tad disappointing was our seating arrangement—a cramped table ill-suited for our party size and the array of dishes we would order.

The menu boasts seasonal fare, indicating a promise of freshness. My taste buds, however, were left searching for that wow factor, as the majority of the food was quite ordinary in flavor. A standout was the octopus—cooked to perfection and a delight in texture. For plant-based diners, I recommend the mushroom tacos, a savory vegan option that didn't disappoint. The Basa catfish was passable, but it was the Fingerlakes grass-fed ribeye that captured my meaty cravings with its rich taste. Unfortunately, the burrata fell flat, missing the mark entirely for me.

In reflection, Kilo seems better suited to smaller groups, given the spatial constraints and table sizes. While the fresh ingredients are commendable, the overall culinary experience was a mixed bag.

Title: Authentic Italian Bliss in NY

I had the pleasure of dining at this charming Italian gem where the experience was nothing short of fantastic. Promptly seated after our 6 PM arrival, the service impressed with its swiftness. Our server was attentive, inquiring about our night and efficiently taking both drink and dinner orders.

The culinary highlight was undoubtedly the authentic Italian fare. The chicken Parmesan was superb, but the vodka sauce pasta adorned with shrimp stole the show—utterly amazing. Adding to the ambiance, a roving guitarist serenaded us as we savored our meals, enhancing the dining experience.

Despite the high quality, the prices were incredibly reasonable, ranging from $12-$15 for a delightful meal. This place is a must-visit while in NY; it truly lives up to the praise. I eagerly anticipate my next visit. Take my word for it—you won't be disappointed.

Title: A Celiac Foodie's Dream: Del Posto Delivers

From my very first visit to Del Posto for a special event years ago, the exceptional service made a lasting impression. Their thoughtful gesture of providing extra gluten-free dessert bites because, as they said, "those who are gluten free/celiac always get items subtracted from their meal - not added," won me over completely. Returning for lunch this week solidified my admiration, confirming that an outstanding review is well-deserved.

Del Posto has not wavered in their commitment to providing a safe dining experience for those of us with gluten sensitivities. They served my bread first and separately, ensuring no cross contamination, and mirrored the same dishes and pastas as my dining companions, a touch that resonates deeply with me as a foodie with celiac disease.

Let's talk about the star of the show—the food. Opting for the tasting menu, each dish was more memorable than the last, particularly the rabbit pillow pasta, striking a harmonious balance between rich and mild flavors. The gluten-free donut holes were nothing short of heavenly—so much so that I consider making them my sole dessert in the future. The ragu pasta followed closely in delight, with the branzino and beef seconds also leaving a mark for their divine flavors. However, the pastas reign supreme, and for good reason—they're stunning.

Matching the high caliber of the dishes, the service at Del Posto is impeccable. The staff are attentive, contributing to the already special experience. The ambiance exudes an understated elegance and coziness that adds to the charm without feeling pretentious.

Its proximity to Chelsea Market and the Highline only enhances the allure, offering a scenic approach to this culinary haven.

In summary, Del Posto is a consistent joy for the palate and a haven for those with dietary restrictions, promising a treat with each visit. I eagerly anticipate my next meal there.

Title: A True Taste of Turkey in the Neighborhood

I stumbled upon a delightful neighborhood gem last Saturday and had to share the experience. We arrived for lunch at noon and were immediately seated, a pleasant surprise given it was the weekend.

The ambiance transports you straight to a Turkish bazaar—dark cord, intricate art, and all. It felt like a piece of Istanbul, which was charming and nostalgic for me.

Our order included lamb and chicken Adana, striped bass, and a salad, tallying up to a reasonable $75 with tax and tip. The Adanas were the highlight; seasoned to perfection, generous in size, and accompanied by the most aromatic, milky rice that paired beautifully with the sour cabbage and onions. The freshly baked bread, served complimentary, was a memorable touch.

However, the meal wasn't without its flaws. The salad failed to impress—simply put, it was bland. The striped bass, albeit flavorful, was marred by an overabundance of tiny bones that made for a painstaking meal.

In sum, for an authentic and affordable Turkish dining experience, this spot is a must-try. While you might skip the salad and be cautious with the fish, don't miss out on their exquisite Adanas—they're the true stars here.

Title: A Valentine's Dream Dinner Experience

My partner and I celebrated Valentine's Day at this gem of a restaurant and were swept off our feet by the romantic ambiance. The staff was the epitome of friendly and attentive, ensuring our evening was special.

Our taste buds were tantalized starting with the handcrafted cocktails, 'The CP' and 'Strawberry 54'. The calamari appetizer set a high standard, striking a delicate balance between tender and crisp, complemented by a divine sauce.

Entrees were a delightful journey for our palates. The pasta with clams bathed in a white sauce with fresh herbs, and the fettuccine mingling artichokes, tomatoes, and shrimp in a white wine sauce were exquisite. The side of beets in pomegranate vinaigrette was a vibrant burst of flavor alongside our mains.

Ending on a sweet note, the ricotta cheesecake was pure indulgence, rounding off a flawless dining experience. The thoughtful touch of a complimentary rose encapsulated the thoughtfulness of our evening.

We left with smiles, full hearts, and the promise to ourselves to return. A heartfelt thank you to the team for crafting our perfect Valentine's Day dinner!

Overall food was ok but meh, it's a good place to come as a large groupWe were a group of 12 people, so we had:Appetizers (2 order of each to share)- bread with 3 dips (one straciatella, one dices tomatoes and yhe 3 a greasy sauce that I don't know what was but was quite gross. Streaciatella fine and tomatos were micely marinated- Bacon -- that was awesome and the beat of the night- Mozzarella with prosciutto saladMy main course was mar e monti pasta. 3 shrimps, few mushrooms and the tagliatelle. Pasta was cooked al dente but overall it lacked flavour butteryFor dessert we had 2 orders of churros: nice presentation but not good. Everyone knows that churroa are deep fried so are oily. That was excessive, churros were like 10 times fried or so or they used old oil. We had 3 bottles of wine, few beers and ended up paying $74/pers- expensive for what you get given that main courses were pizzas and pastasNice that they didn't rush us with the check and to leave.

Title: A Flavor Bomb in Every Bite at Pisillo Sandwiches

If you're on the hunt for a sandwich that will consistently knock your socks off, look no further than Pisillo Sandwiches. Each delectable bite is a mystery of perfection, with a taste that's off the charts. It's hard to pinpoint what makes these sandwiches so irresistible, but whether it's the balance of salty and savory in their perfectly sliced meats, their lush tuna, or the satisfying vegetarian options, Pisillo doesn't miss.

The staff exudes warmth, always ready with a friendly recommendation to guide you through their mouth-watering selections. Be warned, these sandwiches are colossal—they're a marathon meal that could easily stretch over a couple of sittings or generously shared.

For those with a penchant for a fiery kick, the hot pepper spread is an absolute must-try. Just remember, Pisillo is a cash-only establishment, so hit the ATM before you treat yourself to one (or several) of their sandwich masterpieces. Trust me, your taste buds will thank you.

Title: A Satisfactory Hotpot Experience at Tang Hotpot

Last Wednesday night turned out to be a delightful experience at Tang Hotpot, thanks to a group outing fueled by a Puls'd voucher deal that offered dinner for two with an alcoholic beverage each for a reasonable $78.

Standing out with its unique atmosphere, meticulous presentation, and distinctive flatware, Tang Hotpot sets itself apart from the usual hotpot spots. The highlight of the meal was the high-quality meats and fresh seafood, complemented perfectly by the lychee rose cocktail, which was as delightful to the palate as it was to the eyes.

Service didn’t lag behind, with attentive staff ensuring a pleasant dining experience, and I was pleased to find the restroom maintained in a spotless condition. The only downside was the lingering scent of hotpot on my coat post-dinner, a minor inconvenience that could have been solved with the thoughtful provision of plastic bags, a practice adopted by some other establishments.

In conclusion, my friends and I enjoyed a great night out. With the voucher, the meal was quite a catch, summing up to $50 per person, inclusive of tip and service—a worthwhile treat for anyone looking for an elevated hotpot experience.

Title: Pleasant Outdoor Dining Experience

I recently visited a restaurant with a tempting happy hour deal, but take note - it's exclusive to the bar area. Despite this, we opted for outdoor seating and were delighted by the ambiance. The patio was exceptionally pleasant, making for a lovely dining setting. Our table ordered the chorizo flatbread and chicken taquitos. The flatbread was quite flavorful and a highlight of our meal. However, the chicken taquitos were somewhat underwhelming and lacked distinction. While the taquitos left more to be desired, the overall experience was enjoyable, especially due to the charming outdoor atmosphere.

This place gets mad props for a variety of reasons.I've passed by here countless times but never realized just how good it was until I finally give this a try.  Their signature T-bone steak was 100% top notch.  The way they cook it was more Keen's than Peter Luger, however I definitely thought the T-bone here was better than what I had at Keen's.  The flavor, sear, texture and even grease level was just right.  Not too heavy and plenty of natural flavor.  I can see why many people seem to like this place as their dark horse steak joint.It helps that they also include 2 sides - in my case a very generous helping of mashed potatoes and creamed spinach.  The former was excellent and actually pairs very well with their exceptionally delicious home made steak house.  The latter was a bit too creamy for my preference but maybe others might enjoy a thicker cream spinach.I also had their popular French Onion soup and I can see why it's quite well liked.  The cheese was baked perfectly, the soup was flavorful but not too salty and all in all it was just savory in the best of ways.  Last but not least I gave the chocolate souflee a try.   It was a very rich and devilish concoction that was well worth the extra toll it took on my stomach.  All in all a perfect way to end what was a very delicious meal.The ambiance of the entire place was extremely old school with its wood paneling and overall warm atmosphere.  It was packed to the gills at 6pm on a Friday night, and for good reason.  Our server was very attentive and friendly.  This restaurant really nails it in terms of the overall experience - from the service to the food to the overall memorable ambiance.  It's like a slice of old New York that I'm very glad is still in existence and a part of the fabric of the neighborhood.  I'll definitely be back.

Title: Great Food Marred by Hostess Mishap

I had high hopes for what seemed to be a well-regarded restaurant, but the experience fell flat from the outset due to a disorganized hostess. Despite checking in upon arrival and being assured we were next in line, we languished for over half an hour, as the hostess continually failed to recognize us, making for a frustrating start.

Once seated, however, the food redeemed the evening. The fried chicken and cheddar waffle with chicken chilaquiles were both delectable, especially when the spicy sauce was ingeniously mixed with syrup for a perfect sweet and spicy blend.

In short, the cuisine shines, but the service at the front door could use a serious overhaul to match the quality at the table.
Perfectly fine HH place with really well-fried (not greasy; hot; well-seasoned, not overly salty) breaded apps! Wonderful service and incredibly meticulous holiday decor.

Located on the Upper East Side, this restaurant is an excellent choice for those seeking flavorful Indian cuisine coupled with great value, particularly during lunch hours. The butter chicken and sag paneer are standout dishes, beautifully complemented by the light, doughy naan bread. However, a word of caution: visiting the bathroom involves an awkward journey through the kitchen followed by a descent to the basement. Despite this minor inconvenience, I wouldn't hesitate to return for the delectable fare.

As a regular customer who works across the street, I often order lunch from this spot. The convenience of ordering through Ritual or their own Beyond Sushi app, which offers a $5 discount for new users, is a plus. While I find the portions a bit on the small side given the price, and a lunch special often leaves me wanting more, there's no denying the superb taste and inventive ingredient pairings. I've sampled a variety of their rolls and dumplings and have yet to be disappointed. Everything is simply delicious.

Little Italy is a place I never really go to when I'm in New York; however, I was with a coworker who really wanted to visit, and that's how I ended up at Sal's.  Even the locals in the area recommended this place so I just knew it was going to be good.  Sadly, Sal's fell short of my expectations.Our waitress was really friendly and made sure to check up on us throughout our meal.  I ordered the chicken parmesan w/ spaghetti, which left me unimpressed.  The chicken was a tad overcooked, and the sauce was bland. Chicken parmesan is my favorite Italian dish, so when it doesn't hit right it makes me sad. Lastly, while walking out, I saw a sign that said "Special, Chicken Parmesan, side salad, and a glass of wine for $25." I rolled my eyes so hard that I could see the back of my head.  If a restaurant has specials it should be up to the waitress to relay them to diners before they order.  I mean, damn, she could have even told me about the special when I ordered the chicken parmesan just by itself because I ended up dropping $25 anyway.  I felt scammed. No shade, but the next time I'm in Little Italy, I'm going to have to skip Sal's.

I recently dined at a local restaurant that left me with mixed feelings. The highlight of my experience was the tuna dishes I ordered. However, the flavors failed to leave a lasting impression, as I struggle to recall the specifics of what I ate. An attempt to enhance my meal with mango was met with disappointment due to the minuscule portion provided, despite the additional charge. When considering value, the $17 price tag felt steep for the quantity received. Overall, my visit was underwhelming, with the cuisine lacking the memorable punch one would hope for at this price point.

Title: A Classic Bite at Joe's Pizza – New York at its Finest

There's no denying that NYC is a pizza paradise, and among the myriad options for a good slice, Joe's Pizza stands out as a beacon of traditional New York-style pizza excellence. Their slice hits all the right notes with balanced cheese-to-sauce ratios and a sauce that strikes the perfect balance between tangy and sweet. Unlike some of its contemporaries, Joe's steers clear of the divisive cornmeal-dusted crust, opting instead for a chewy, crispy base that can only be described as delightful.

The space itself is cozy to say the least, conducive more to a grab-and-go experience than a sit-down meal. Still, for those lucky enough to snag one of the few stools, it's a prime spot for indulging in a classic New York bite. If not, there's always the outdoor public space just across the street – an ideal locale for enjoying your slice and engaging in some quintessential people-watching.

A note to diners: prepare to pay with cash, as plastic isn't accepted here. And while Joe's serves up whole pies that are worth every penny, make sure to plan ahead as there's no public restroom on site. Bottle sodas and water are available to wash down what is arguably one of the best slices in the city. Joe's Pizza doesn't just serve pizza; they serve a slice of New York life.

Review from a Californian - because trust, people in NY don't know what a good taco taste like.Okay, honestly, this would be more of a 3 stars in SF, but hey, on the east coast, good tacos are hard to come by. This is the best I have had since moving here. They have fresh adobada (marinated pork) spinning on the rotisserie which I love. I didn't even bother to try the other meats. They are decently priced at $3.75 a taco. The ordering system is weird. You place your order at the cashier and then hand the receipt to one of the cooks. There's no line so people are just gathered around them. The salsa bar and other condiments are on the same area where you wait for the food. It's not an efficient system at all. There's also no tables to eat your taco so you might have to walk around and eat it on a bench. My tacos were got a little cold when I finally found a place to eat. Welps.My tacos, although warm, were pretty bomb. The meat was flavorful and the salsa was on point. Their horchata is also pretty bomb too. If you are craving some legit tacos, Los Tacos No.1 is the place to go.

Had some expectations based on the nyt review but should have believed the yelp reviews.. it was the definition of a tourist trap and even worse than eataly -- at least at eataly although the food is expensive its quite good and sufficient. Our group of four got so many dishes but still left unsatisfied with quite a significant spend. My 3stars are reserved for places i didnt care for but would go if someone really wanted to, but this was a place i would actively discourage someone to go to if they wanted to.

Title: Hidden Gem with Exceptional Seafood and Service

I stumbled upon a fantastic bar that immediately felt like my kind of place. The bartenders here are not only talented but also personable, effortlessly remembering your name and preferred drink—a touch of personal service that's hard to come by.

The local flavor shines through in their seafood offerings, with the halibut and Montauk Swordfish standing out as particularly excellent choices. Both dishes were cooked to perfection, offering a taste that's hard to forget.

The highlight for me, though, has to be their happy hour special. It's arguably the best-kept secret around: $1.50 oysters every day! And these aren't just any oysters—they're consistently fresh and make for an unbeatable treat.

In short, this bar is a must-visit for anyone looking for quality seafood, a friendly atmosphere, and some of the best deals in town. Don't pass up the opportunity to make this spot your next dining destination.

Title: A Delightful Discovery Near the Football Frenzy

My experience at this gem of a restaurant, found with a simple Apple Maps search, was nothing short of delightful. Just a short walk from the local football viewing spot, the entryway set the stage with a fascinating display of lobsters ready for the picking.

Seated immediately upon arrival, the service was prompt with drinks and appetizers arriving quickly. The lobster bisque, shared with my boyfriend, was exceptional in flavor. For the main course, we indulged in the original lobster roll and Combo #1, which paired a burger with a 1lb lobster. Both dishes were satisfying and flavorful, if not earth-shattering.

For fans of coastal eats, especially burgers and lobster, this place hits the mark. It’s earned a return visit from us the next time we're in town.

It's not my first time and I live to gone back. Their food is mostly vegan (some dishes have dairy and it's marked in the menu), and it still had the good old Chinese flavors. My favorite plate is the chickn lo mein, and everything else that we took was also delicious. Their sushi is not the best, but after all it's a Chinese restaurant, not Japanese:)

Title: A Hyped Spot with Lackluster Flavors Off Canal Street

Having heard rave reviews about its Chicago counterpart, I ventured with high expectations to this off-beat location nestled in an unassuming part of Chinatown, a stone's throw from Canal Street. Despite its peculiar setting down a rather dubious byway, the restaurant greeted me with a modern and inviting ambiance, seemingly perfect for a trendy gathering spot.

The menu beckoned, and I heeded the call starting with their Single Cheeseburger. It promised much but delivered an experience that was just passable – flavorful, yes, but it lost points for being unexpectedly dry despite a medium cook. The texture echoed a Shake Shack patty, but it was too salty and lacked a robust beefy richness.

My adventurous side was piqued by the Crispy Potato Hash with Duck Heart Gravy, a dish I anticipated would sing. However, it hit a flat note, over-seasoned and overwhelmingly heavy, with the duck heart's contribution indistinct amongst what seemed like a standard sausage gravy affair.

Then came the Fried House-Made Bologna Sandwich, an Eater-recommended dish that left my palate underwhelmed. Hopes of a thick-cut, artisanal bologna were dashed by the reality of thin, griddle-fried deli slices, again too salt-laden, sandwiched within a brioche bun.

A saving grace, the Bread and Butter Pickles offered a much-needed palate cleanser. Their slight sweetness and pleasing flavor provided a brief respite from the meal's previously over-salted offerings.

While the setting hits the mark for potential popularity, the food lacks the punch and finesse one would expect from such a revered establishment. Overall, a mediocre culinary adventure in a spot that buzzes with unfulfilled potential.

Title: High Hopes Dashed at a Renowned Eatery

As a food enthusiast, I was eager to try the famous beef noodle soup at this well-known restaurant. Unfortunately, my experience fell short of the hype. The ordering process is straightforward, with diners placing their order at the counter and then finding a seat at the communal cafeteria-style tables. Be prepared to cozy up with strangers during busy hours and juggle your winter attire, as the backless chairs offer no support for personal belongings.

The menu, visually displayed on the wall, sets expectations high which weren't met by the actual meal. At $12 for a small bowl, I expected a rich and flavorful broth, but instead encountered a disappointingly watery base. The noodles, though unique in their chunky shape, contributed little to the dish's overall appeal. More disappointing was the beef, which lacked the tenderness one anticipates in a soup that carries its name.

In summary, the fame of this eatery might draw you in, but be prepared for an underwhelming meal that doesn't quite justify the price or the popularity.

I recently opted for a delivery from Sugarfish via Postmates for my Monday dinner and couldn't have been more delighted with the experience. The order arrived in a swift 20 minutes, and the quality was exceptional. The fish was remarkedly fresh, with no hint of fishiness, coupled with perfectly cooked rice. The packaging was meticulous, preserving the delicate sushi, and the inclusion of three kinds of seasonings complemented the meal beautifully. Opting for the 'Trust Me Lite,' I found it to be an ample portion. Sugarfish certainly lived up to its reputation, even when enjoyed from the comfort of home.

Cute alley with lots of options! We ate outside in the middle of the street. We shared the small antipasto, which was still big with lots of meat, veggie and cheese/olive options. It came with thicker baguette style bread. We shared the Romana- prosciutto and arugula pizza and margarita preferred the romana. Overall, we had too much food for 4 people, but enjoyed it all!

Great pre-theater spot. Went here before heading over to New World Stages for an evening show. The service, food, and atmosphere did not disappoint. For starters we ordered steamed dumplings, pork belly, coconut soup, and spring rolls. Everything was very flavorful. It was so much food we could hardly get to our mains.The mains included shrimp pad Thai, skirt steak bowl, and fish fillet. My favorite was the pad Thai. Absolutely delicious. They also have a lobster version I wouldn't mind trying. My favorite part was the drinks. It was happy hour so all of the drinks were discounted before 6pm on a Friday.
