I ordered a raspberry mojito and a lychee martini. Definitely worth a try! I recommend this place.

Tuesday dinner for 2.Came here on a date with my love to try a place we have heard about for a while. Once we got inside from the early winter chill, we felt so warm (except for the occasional draft from the door opening and closing). We waited maybe 15 minutes to be seated. Loved the vibe of the place especially as a 24-hour establishment. Noticed some cute illustrations on the wall - "Velska is Love" kind of a nod to Wes Anderson style. Let me tell you, the borscht was amazing. We also ordered the deluxe meat plate including: dumplings, stuffed cabbage. We added the pancakes as well. The winner was definitely the borscht - hearty, with potatoes and meat. I've had homemade borscht and love it but this one was a little extra, like New York. The bread with butter dipped in was so on point on a cold November night. We also ordered the banana cream pie but it was a little top heavy for what we wanted. I may try the cheesecake or chocolate mousse next time. Highly recommend. Especially on a night out in EV.

Title: A Twilight Delight at PalmCourt

PalmCourt certainly has a particular ambiance - be prepared for a touch of pretense and a crowd that's a mix of fashionable elites and families creating memories. Yet, during Restaurant Week, such considerations become secondary to their offering: the Twilight Tea Service.

Indulgence was the theme of my latest visit. My companion and I didn't hold back, opting for the full tea service with all the trimmings - think caviar and a tasting tour of the cocktail menu, all four concoctions.

The experience was lavish and satisfying, a feast not only for the palate but for the eyes. Each course was a testament to PalmCourt's commitment to excellence, and the extra macarons at the conclusion were a sweet finale that sealed the deal. Whether you're there for the vibe or the victuals, the Twilight Tea Service doesn't disappoint.

Title: A Delightful Taste of Uzbekistan in the Heart of the City

Walking into this charming Uzbek restaurant felt like a serendipitous encounter, a surprising slice of my hometown brought to life in an unexpected corner. The menu, a delightful assortment of traditional dishes, did not disappoint.

The manti were a standout, perfectly seasoned and wrapped in a delicate dough that melted in the mouth. Meanwhile, the lagman sang with flavors, although the portion left me wishing for just a bit more. The plov, a hearty Uzbek staple, was exactly as I craved — though it was amusingly skewed with an abundance of tender meat overshadowing the rice.

The lamb kababs were another highlight, skewered in a traditional fashion that surpassed the usual ground meat varieties found throughout NYC. While they could have embraced a touch more spice, their simplicity allowed the quality of the lamb to shine, which I appreciated greatly.

The ambiance added to the experience, with the exotic decor transporting me further east and waitresses adorned in traditional attire contributing to the authenticity. Service was attentive and unobtrusive, rounding out a solid dining experience.

For those yearning for a culinary adventure or a taste of Central Asia, this restaurant is a gem well-worth exploring. I wholeheartedly recommend it for an experience that satisfies both nostalgia and the pursuit of new flavors.

During my early January stay at the Redbury NY, I had the absolute pleasure of indulging in their pizza. Not only did the decor and service at this establishment capture the essence of fine dining, but the convenience of room service truly enhanced my experience. The pizza itself, a thin crust masterpiece, was a testament to the mastery of oven-baking – each bite conveyed the perfect texture and taste that one expects from a quintessential New York slice. A culinary delight indeed, and a noteworthy highlight of my stay.

I had been wanting to come here for brunch for the longest time and finally had a chance to do so about a month ago. The place is essentially a bar with tables in the back area. It was dark, loud and bustling. I waited at the bar because they do not seat incomplete parties. As soon as my friend arrived, we were given a table. I was disappointed because the Steak and Eggs were no longer part of the brunch offerings even though it was listed online. For this reason, it took me even longer than usual to decide what to order. I narrowed it down to the bacon, egg and cheese sandwich and the falafel burger with waffle fries. Our waitress, who was also the hostess, really knew the menu well and described both food items in detail. After I let her know I was leaning toward something lunch-y, she suggested getting the falafel burger with pita instead of bread so that it wouldn't be as heavy. I decided to follow her advice. The falafel was a nice, hearty size and between warm pita bread, served with tomato, purple onion and lettuce, along with a pickle on top. The falafel was quite thick with a satisfying crispness and packed with delicious seasoning. It worked well with the tasty pita and the fresh vegetables added a lightness to the sandwich which was helpful because the falafel was a bit overpowering. I enjoyed the waffle fries which were slightly seasoned and were delightfully crunchy. Service was just okay. The place was pretty busy and the hostess / waitress also turned into a bartender as time went on. There were several times when it took awhile for our waitress to attend to us. I definitely would not return.

Title: Authentic Northwestern Chinese Flavors in the East Village

Last Wednesday evening, a party of ten, myself included, descended upon Jiang Diner in the vibrant heart of the East Village. With a reservation in hand, we were greeted by a reserved space just for our group—a welcoming touch that set the stage for a memorable dining experience.

The restaurant buzzed with a comforting hum of activity, yet was far from overcrowded, allowing us to revel in the small, casual ambiance. The decor was charming, reflecting the authenticity that was further endorsed by the predominantly Mainland Chinese clientele.

As for the meal, it was a family-style feast of Northwestern Chinese cuisine, a delectable journey through bold cumin, tender lamb, and aromatic dry spices. Standouts included the Da Pan Ji—savor the boneless version for an easier yet equally succulent treat. The portion was generous, to say the least.

The Spicy Diced Chicken lived up to its name with an enjoyable heat that tingled the palate, though the bitty bones scattered throughout were a slight setback. Lamb ribs were another triumph, seasoned impeccably with cumin, the meat so tender it nearly fell off the bone.

Shumai dumplings, offered in beef and lamb, were a delightful twist on the traditional, with the lamb variety edging out as the favorite for its distinctive flavor.

In summary, Jiang Diner presents an authentic and thoroughly satisfying foray into Northwestern Chinese cuisine. The lamb dishes, in particular, come with high praise and a strong recommendation. For anyone in search of a genuine taste of China in the East Village, look no further than Jiang Diner.

Title: Late Night Bite at Hyped Pizza Spot

Stopped by this eatery at 1:30 AM on a Friday, and was pleasantly surprised to find no queue. We opted for a slice of their square pepperoni pizza, which seems to have quite the reputation. While the pizza was decent, with notably crispy pepperoni, it leaned towards the salty and oily side. It's a solid choice if you're in the area and craving a quick slice, but I wouldn't recommend waiting an hour for it. Don't forget to grab some napkins on your way out – you'll need them.

I came to this place because another location had a crazy wait time and we had to get lunch quick. This used to be a sit-down type of Thai restaurant but now it's a casual, on-the-go or order and sit down type of place. I don't think I accurately described that but you'll see when you walk in. I decided to get food off their lunch special selection instead of the menu. The menu is better for fresh, hot food made in the kitchen. The lunch special is pick-your-own style as you see it. It's cheaper and has less wait. For $10 you get to pick a rice, protein, two vegetables and free water/soda. I picked jasmine rice, crispy chicken, broccoli, green beans and the fresh ginger sauce. The rice was a little hard to my liking but made up for it with the fresh ginger sauce that's drizzled all over it. The crispy chicken was good. Smaller portion but good. My friend's grilled chicken had some bones in it so be cautious. The vegetables were fine. Overall, it's alright. Good for a quick meal and if you don't care about flavor and just wolfing down your food. I do like that it comes with a beverage. Sit down, eat, bring your tray to the disposable area and you'll be on your way.

Nothing bad to say about TGA. Came from brunch early Saturday morning where there wasn't a soul to our left or right. Just how I like it. There wasn't any waiter/waitress around, but there was the bar tender tending the bar and the outside tables. Not the smartest move, but I guess payroll is tight? What we got:-Coffee (pretty good for brunch) -Watermelon Spritzer (vodka drink that was VERY tasty. Lots of vodka too) Food we got and recommend:-Brunch Burger (Very messy but worth it!)-Avocado Toast (Interesting take on avocado toast with thinly sliced cucumber on top) -Short Rib Grilled Cheese (More of a short rib sandwich that a grilled cheese; short rib a little dry) Prices are a tab bit expensive for Herald Sq., but I can see us coming back for a special day. Would love to try some of their other cocktails.

A solid spot for both spicy/non-spicy Japanese curry lovers. I do believe it's a Korean/Japanese fusion, however. I tried Abiko both for dinner and lunch and I'd recommend going for lunch. It's on the pricier side, so their lunch specials seem a lot more worthwhile. Their lunch special options are basic curry udon with fried shrimp and basic curry rice with pork katsu for only $9.99. I went for the latter and chose the level two spice which is the "spicy" (scale is from 0-4). I love spicy food but be warned, they do not joke around with their spice. My tongue was able to handle the spice, but my stomach was burning a bit for the next few hours. The dish, however, was really good - both the curry and katsu components. I'll definitely be back!

Food is great. The steak with Ikinari sauce was everything but service is lacking. My boyfriend's steak was over cooked and he waited almost 30 mins for a new rare 18oz steak. My garlic pepper rice did not come out with my steak I waited 30 mins after my steak was served. The waiters were polite and apologetic but they definitely need to work on service.

Even ordering it via delivery, the hearty, plant based big leap quinoa burger was unforgettable Quantum leap comes up if you search lists of best veggie burgers in the city, so it's been on my list for a while. While stuck at home, they're thankfully taking orders via Uber eats and I finally decided to give them a try.The big leap burger is absolutely delectable. Unexpectedly, the bun is whole grain and provides nice stability to a jam packed burger. The patty itself is made of beans, veggies, and grains. No one ingredient stands out. It's well integrated and it's got a fulfilling, savory flavor. All the toppings are on point, especially the perfectly crispy onion ring. My boyfriend was very happy with his salmon in fresh herb dish, but he took a bite of my veggie burger and said he would definitely get it next time. We agreed that the buffalo wings were a bit small portioned, 3 pcs, and not outstanding. We definitely prefer buffalo cauliflower but we're wary to order that for takeout. When I dine out, I want to eat something delicious that I couldn't easily make at home. Check and check. I'll be back for another Quantum Leap burger!

This was a great lunch spot!  The prices are rock bottom and the dumplings were amazing. The menu is very small, but that did not matter. We ordered two types of dumplings and they were ready within minutes. A plate of 8 dumplings was a very filling lunch - for less than $5!  The pork and cabbage were traditionally delicious and the chicken and mushroom were savory and so yummy. Highly recommend.

Title: Cozy Saturday Night at a KBBQ Gem

We stumbled upon a delightful culinary experience last Saturday evening with no wait time, a surprise for our party. Our seating in the upstairs area immediately piqued our interest with the allure of Korean BBQ.

The popcorn chicken was passable, though not the highlight of our meal. However, the Yuk-Gae-Jang ramyun captured our palates with its rich and robust flavors - a definite must-try.

While the uni in the bibimbap was sparse, the dish itself did not disappoint in taste. The egg souffle was a unanimous crowd-pleaser, light and fluffy, making it an effortless indulgence.

The beef large combo was impressive, boasting a generous variety of cuts that were perfect for our KBBQ cravings.

Our venture into the seafood pancake territory yielded a more mundane experience, landing on the average side of the scale. An additional order of the souffle egg, unlike the version that came with the beef combo, missed the mark with an overpowering riddle taste that clashed with our taste buds.

The service, nevertheless, remained attentive and commendable throughout our dining experience, ensuring a pleasant atmosphere. Despite the few hiccups, the evening was largely enjoyable, and the restaurant's offerings are well worth a visit.

Small clean Japanese fast food takeout sit down joint. Only had some sashimi and green tea and fried dumplings all good for the price which was average. Place is definitely worth trying for a quick munch. I'll be back to try other things for a better review.

Love this place. Been twice so far. Servers are so so nice &accommodating. Have ordered regular cocktails (Bay Breeze) & ALSO the Hogwarts Express one and the Working Class Hero. I will say I'm not the biggest fan of egg whites with my drinks but it was an experience none the less. The Working Class Hero however was amazing. The whiskey was smooth and tasted remarkable. Food also is good. A little pricier than I'd like but still a nice treat out to have when in the city. Definitely would come back.

Title: A Brunch Delight in the Heart of Manhattan

My Sunday brunch experience at this bustling eatery in Manhattan was marked by attentive service and appetizing dishes. Despite the busy atmosphere, our waitress was on point, keeping our glasses filled and ensuring a smooth dining experience.

The California Benedict, my choice for brunch, was a delightful surprise. Opting out of the smoked salmon addition, I found the portion satisfying and well-balanced with a light, healthy side salad. For those with a heartier appetite, the smashed potato side is a must-try.

The ambiance is casual and inviting, perfect for a laid-back gathering with friends. However, be prepared for the limited space—typical of Manhattan—which can feel cramped and loud, possibly deterring any hopes for a quiet, romantic date.

While most of the menu impressed, the breakfast burrito special fell short, being somewhat on the dry side. Yet, this minor setback wouldn't deter me from returning for another round of their enjoyable brunch offerings.

Title: A Hearty Feast for the Hungry Crowd!

My visit to this restaurant was a delightful surprise with its incredible portions and mouth-watering flavors. It's a paradise for anyone with a ravenous appetite, as each dish could easily satisfy two or three diners. Our large group couldn't stop raving about their meals, from the succulent wings that were a hit with the kids to the unexpectedly hefty spinach and quinoa salad that I thoroughly enjoyed despite my smaller appetite. The salad's dressing was a standout, and the fried onion appetizer was a close second favorite.

Although the place buzzed with energy and was quite loud, it added to the lively atmosphere that even our boisterous party enjoyed. The lack of desserts on the menu was peculiar, but not a deal-breaker. Parents can rest assured that the vibrant ambiance doesn't compromise the restaurant's kid-friendliness. A word of caution to expecting mothers: the women's bathroom is snug, with very small stalls that may test your maneuvering skills.

Overall, we had a fantastic experience with great food and a warm, if boisterous, environment. Just be prepared for a crowd and a bit of noise.

Great place for Mexican food if you're in the area! The interior felt like a diner, with the black and white tiled floor and red seats. There's a waiter who greets you at the door and another lovely waiter who would take your order. You order by writing down the number of items you want on one menu paper. The guac and chips can determine the quality of the food, and it's safe to say, the guac and chips here are great! Their chips here are thicker than other chips and tasted amazing with the generous guac they gave! I ordered the Pollo Yucateco and Carnitas Taco for around $8 in total, which is typical Midtown price. Luckily, they tasted pretty good, or else I would be complaining. I prefer the Pollo taco over the Carnitas. I don't even know what type of veggies were on the taco but they tasted great with the meat and pinch of lime! I'm normally picky with my tacos but this place was decently good! I would go back if I want Mexican for lunch again!

Stumbled across this place after the AIDS Walk and thought it was cool and tasty. Great vibe on a Sunday. I felt like I was in Cali somewhere Prices are awesome for the upper west side Brunch drinks weren't great but if we had to choose between the mimosa, sangria or cactus pear Bellini we would definitely choose their version of the Sangria. The other drinks need some more character.I have to come back to try the Margaritas during the week. Staff is okay not as friendly as other places in the upper west side. The wait on a Sunday for 3 people was about 20 minutes which wasn't too bad. The food is tasty I really liked my burrito and the idea of make your own guacamole. But it could use more flavor for sure. For dessert they literally have a churro ice cream sandwich which was delicious but could use a drizzle of caramel or something on top to make it easier to eat and a more complete dish.

I recently satisfied my ramen cravings with delivery from this local gem. Opting for the spicy tonkatsu ramen, I was met with a delectable and well-seasoned broth. The pork chasu was generous and flawlessly fatty, a carnivore's dream. Accompaniments like corn, green onions, and the perfectly runny egg melded with the dish, while the springy noodles had that sought-after chew. My only minor quibble was the broth quantity, but as a takeaway order, it was understandable. Eager to explore more of their offerings, this spot has earned my hearty recommendation as a new favorite.

High end korean bbq with A5 wagyu beef. The beef was top notch, and they had diff type of salt and sauce for the beef. We sat in the private nook area, which was cozy and private. Service was great, and they grilled at our table over the iron plates. Loved the traditional bronze silverware, decor was clean simple traditional yet modern asian/korean theme. Unlike the traditional korean bbq place, they do not have a lot of side dishes (ban-Chan). Attention to details, the experience and ambiance was sophisticated.

After hearing about this oldest and most famous pizza place, i decided to go for dinner. I ordered half original and half white pizza as we wanted to try both these options. White pizza was decent but the original pizza wasn't great , definitely not as we had expected. There are such good places in Brooklyn and around that area that have better pizzas. Surely wasn't up to the hype and serves mediocre slices and it was $20. Also, there was no wait line and almost all tables were filled.

Title: Disappointing Experience in Greenwich Village

My recent dining experience at a Greenwich Village eatery was underwhelming. We chose the restaurant for its indoor seating to escape the heat, but the accommodating environment ended there. The staff's unwelcoming demeanor made it clear that our presence was more of a bother than a business.

The menu, though straightforward, did not translate to satisfactory meals. My boyfriend's Mighty Bowl featured an unpleasant surprise—an ice-cold sweet potato and unappetizingly mushy, bagged avocado. It was a missed opportunity to showcase fresh ingredients.

My spicy chicken sandwich was a mixed bag; while the chicken itself was tasty, the application of refrigerator-cold hot sauce was a puzzling misstep. Additionally, an oversight at the ordering station led to a frustrating encounter at the register, where I felt like an inconvenience for requesting a side of burnt end baked beans—which, regrettably, did not live up to their cost or potential.

The ambiance was marred by loud and explicit rap music, an unexpected and unwelcome soundtrack for a lunchtime setting, compounded by the startling screech of the front door. This restaurant could greatly improve by addressing its hospitality, food temperature issues, and overall dining atmosphere.

Title: A Mixed Bag at a Quaint Spot

I recently visited this charming restaurant for a family lunch and found myself in a beautiful space that was surprisingly empty. Despite this, the hostess seemed less than thrilled to receive us, which was a downer. However, the remaining staff were delightful and provided stellar service, saving the day.

The menu had some real gems like the Zia Maria Chicken and the perfectly stuffed cheese ravioli, which were the highlights of our meal. Regrettably, the eggplant parm did not live up to expectations – it was a rather uninspired rendition with a single layer of eggplant.

Price-wise, the restaurant is quite reasonable. It's a shame the food and service aren't on par with their other location in Little Italy, which I've found to be superior. This spot would be incredibly convenient for me if it were up to the same standard, but for now, it seems like a work in progress. Overall, the food won us over, but there's definitely room for improvement in service and certainly some dishes.

I met with a friend for a double date and he told me he was practically a regular. I can definitely see why. Great service, delicious and satisfying portions. I really enjoyed their Duck hash. The interior consisted of a rustic but cozy decor. It was raining and it was helpful that there was not just a coat rack but also section to put your umbrellas.

This is a niche place in this neighborhood where the closest restaurant that you can see from its windows is called "chicken and burger". No this is no chicken or burger, this is quality Japanese food sourced specially by the owner and made with love. I love eating food made with care.The restaurant itself is a very intimate experience so if you don't like lots of people that may be good but also you may be sitting pretty close to someone at the long table they have. The couch seating is pretty comfy. The music always sets a certain mood...I think there is a Sade pic in the washroom.The food is really the star here. It's fresh, clean tasting, and flavorful without being too extra (those sushi places that make rolls so big and crammed with stuff this is NOT). I had a really good spicy tuna don bowl the last time I went. I've tried the onigiri which is decent. I'm also a big fan of mochidoki and they serve these for dessert.You are going to pay typical NYC prices for Japanese food (not high end elite but not cheap-o) but it's worth the experience.

Title: A Bibimbap Haven in Koreatown

If you're a bibimbap aficionado like myself, your search for perfection ends at this gem in Koreatown. Their dolsot bibimbap is a culinary triumph, served in a stone pot so hot it could melt the coldest of hearts. Watching the staff masterfully mix the vibrant ingredients is a prelude to the symphony of flavors in every bite. Paired with their irresistibly crispy fried dumplings, which pack more flavor than their steamed counterparts, this meal is a testament to the simple joy of well-crafted Korean comfort food. A definite must-visit for a soul-warming dining experience.

We noticed a sign for the beyond burger outside the hotel.  There was also a menu posted.  The prices overall weren't to bad and the price of the beyond burger was $14 which is comparable to other restaurants where we have ordered the beyond or impossible burger.  We walked in and walked up to an employee that was talking to another employee about going out.  We were not acknowledged, even though we were seen, because when we walked up we were standing next to the employee she was engaging in dialogue with about partying and what she would look good in. My fiancé interrupted her (the person that took our order) and asked her about the beyond burger.  She said it is the the same as the impossible burger which I knew this was not correct.  One is made of soy and the other pea protein.  We placed our order, to include their happy hour special which was the classic margarita, paid and waited for our food.  We were both surprised when our food arrived.  The burger was a slider!  We paid $14 for a slider.  We thought their prices were comparable but there is no comparison between a slider and a burger.  Other than that the food was good, the French fries were shoe string fries which we both enjoyed....haven't had them in ages.  My margarita was very strong, it wasn't good but strong. After paying $14 for a slider, I felt that a strong drink was needed.Restaurant is located in the Dream hotel. The restroom is located on a different floor in the hotel area.  There is an elevator and staircase.  The hotel is beautiful, well maintained and upscale.  The decor is very beautiful, definitely worth a walk to.     Parking......there is a parking garage not to far away, rate is around $10 an hour.  We arrived in the area via the transit line.

I love this place!! Came here during restaurant week for dinner and also got lucky with the generous pour wine event the restaurant was running. The restaurant is huge with plenty of seating and a bar at the front as well. We had a reservation and ended waiting approx. 10 minutes for our table as we had another person joining and boy, it was worth it as we were seated in the mezzanine level, in our own private room like space. We ordered the seafood tower and the $42 restaurant week menu. I ordered the NY strip cut for dinner which was served with beans and mash. I asked for medium and it was a little bit over cooked but I still enjoyed it anyhow. The generous pour was definitely generous and made our dinner far more enjoyable. The seafood tower was also nice - it comprised of lobster, oysters, shrimps and crab meat. Needless to say we polished it off. Service was great. Our waiter was very pleasant and attentive and ensured we were having a great dinner. Would definitely come back here again, especially when there is a restaurant week offer!

This restaurant was recommended by a friend.  I went and had a reservation and we were seated immediately.  The restaurant is very beautiful.  We had the bread, burrata and snap peas to start.  They were all great.  I had the cacio e pepe and my friend had another pasta dish.  We then had the passion fruit tart for dessert.  The sommelier recommended a great bottle of red wine that went with all the food.  It is a more expensive restaurant.

First, they don't take reservations (maybe for two only). Second, when you walk in, all parties must be present in order to get the table, otherwise you have to wait, no matter how hungry you are. So yes if one of your parties is late, blame him/her!My friend introduced this place to me so I decided to join her for dinner when she said let's go here. Unfortunately, she was late, so I was feeling hungry for almost 45 mins with the food aroma and all the delicious smells in the background, I thought I would kill myself. We had a nice Asian male waiter. He was pretty busy handling many tables but he didn't forget us. We both ordered appetizers, mussels and steamed vegetable dumpling. My dumpling was in purple!!! How cool is that? I was looking at purple dumpling while eating it. The mussels plate was the best! Then we both had the green curry but my friend had it with vegetables and I had it with shrimp. I liked my dishes but the green curry wasn't very authentic. It was very good. We both enjoyed the drinks too. They got plenty on the menu, colors, non-colors, all kind of crazy names that I can't remember. Overall the mussels moved me! Order this for the sake of humanity!The place is beautiful from the entrance to the back, and upstairs looks great as well. Would I be back? Sure! Maybe I'll try something different next time. My friend said she ordered the red curry before and that was so much better than the green curry. So, let's see!

I recently had the pleasure of trying Joe's Pizza for the first time when my company catered an assortment of their delicious pies, ranging from classic Cheese to Veggie to my personal favorite, Meat Lovers. As a self-proclaimed carnivore, the Meat Lovers pizza was a delectable feast worthy of mention with its generous toppings and savory flavor that sent my taste buds into a frenzy of delight.

The pizzas arrived with individual bottles of soda, a thoughtful touch since they don't offer large bottles. Even the pizza cutters were provided in charming packaging that added to the overall experience. The thin crust of the pizzas was notably yummy, striking the perfect balance between crispness and chewiness, making each bite more enjoyable than the last.

Two slices in and I was already feeling quite full, a testament to the satisfying nature of their pies. But the pizza was so tempting, I considered going for a third slice. Joe's Pizza definitely understands how to please a hungry crowd with quality toppings and perfectly executed crust. If you consider yourself a fan of good pizza, Joe's is not to be missed – especially if you're in the mood to indulge your inner carnivore!

Venturing into Little Italy for a lunchtime treat proved a challenge with the abundance of tantalizing Italian eateries. Our decision was swayed by Sal's, courtesy of their tempting pizza by the slice deal that initially caught our eye, though we ultimately settled for a sit-down meal in the back dining room. While it lacked a noteworthy view or ambiance, it provided a serene spot for an undisturbed chat.

I opted for the pepperoni calzone, intriguingly offered either fried or baked. On the server's recommendation, I went for the fried version, although I later pondered if baking would have been the more authentic choice. My dining partner selected a plain personal pizza. Both dishes were devoured, as much due to their delightful taste as our ravenous appetites from wandering the neighborhood.

A basket of lukewarm, uninspiring white bread served with tiny tubs of butter arrived oddly late and went untouched. The bathroom facilities, conveniently sited near the dining room, were commendably clean. Despite some quirks, Sal's served up a satisfying meal that hit the spot, with service that was warm and appreciated.

review solely based on food as service was a-ok but note worth noting in this review.went as a party of 2 on a sunday evening at 745pm. the bar area when you first walk into the establishment was nearly empty and kind of ssullunghae (i dont even know how to translate this to english) but the dining room was pretty busy. clean lines and minimal decor - but who cares, let's move on to the food.we ordered the insalate, spaghetti, and bistecca all to share.highly recommend the spaghetti frutti di mare, which was a nearly perfect dish. Tomato sauce was full of flavor and had notes of sweetness from the basil and the seafood in the dish was perfectly cooked. i especially enjoyed the bites of octopus which were plump and had a good amount of chew. bistecca cooked to a perfect medium rare and was served on top of a really nice jus that complemented the beefy steak. the potatoes that came with the dish were excellent, really crispy on the outside but fluffy interiors. wish there were more than two leaves of brussels sprouts, but oh well.salad was fine (not that memorable, hence no pic).minus a star as i think for the price, the quantity wasn't quite there for the primi dish. and i get it, it's a primi, but for the amount it costs, i figured it could still be a serving that would pass as a meal,but this would definitely leave you hungry. however, the quality of the dishes is excellent and definitely worth a trek to chelsea

If you are looking for an Instagrammable experience this is the place to be! My fav was the glitter matcha. I also really liked their waffle icecream bouquet, it was a piece of art. Do your homework before you go and look up pictures of what you want.

I recently tried a delivery from the local build-your-own bowl spot and was thoroughly impressed. Opting for the comfort of our own place, the delivery was surprisingly swift, despite the restaurant's distance from our home. My boyfriend fell for the yeero bowl, while the veggie bowl was an absolute delight for me. The Greek salad and lentil toppings deserve a special shout-out for their exceptional flavor. We'll certainly be ordering again!

I've been to the other location which is more casual than the Times Square location.  The ambiance is definitely more on the dating side which also implies it's nicer also.  Ordered the lobster bites for an app which were very good and always love a Thai chili sauce.  Entree I had ordered the beast and it was a bit messy to eat but I guess I could have used a knife and fork...it just tasted so good as it was lobster and Swiss on a burger with truffle mayo.  Fries and salad as the included sides were standard nothing very special.  service was very attentive as well.  Overall a good experience and would come back to try other items as well.

We came here for restaurant week with the 10 of us but looking at the price. It was not worth it to order from the restaurant week menu we ended up just ordering from the normal menu. We got 100 oz steak, crab cake, the tartare. Everything was really good. It was a good choice. Will definitely come back here

Ordered here twice hoping second time would be better. I used to live in Astoria and love my Greek food. Both times meat was super fatty and over cooked. I got the Greek salad with chicken the second time and I could barely eat the chicken it was so dry. Fries were good though. Pretty bummed as this place is across from my apartment and the reviews on yelp seemed so good. Will have to go to look elsewhere.

New spot for a quick lunch option in the area. Small space with some stool seating available, but really no one inside on a Monday afternoon.Menu is brightly colored and a bit all over the place, but finally settled on my order after a few minutes. Decided on the Slammin' Saag with Beef ($12) and an Iced Chai ($4.50). Food was made to order while the chai was pre-bottled (did not know that). Got my food after 8 minutes which was place in a pretty nice to-go bag. The saag frankie is hefty, with loads of spinach, beef, and paneer barely keeping inside the wrap. Intense flavor and not too spicy. Only qualms was that the I didn't taste much, if any, of the mango pickle marination on the beef (which in itself was a bit tough). Chai is solid despite being pre-bottled, not too sweet and an even amount of cardamom.Rounded up from 3.5 stars since it's something different from the usual sandwich or salad options.

TLDR: Such a fun bar! I'd definitely recommend checking this place out and getting their watermelon soju or yogurt soju.Drinks: 7/10I LOVE Korean drinks! The sugar in the drinks really is a little dangerous, but the drinks taste so good. I'd recommend either the watermelon soju or yogurt soju. If you get the watermelon soju, however, I've heard rumors that they reuse the watermelon...Price & Portion: 6/10I can't remember exactly how much we paid, but it wasn't anymore than a normal night out.Service: 7/10Really exceptional service! We were seated right away and the staff checked in with us frequently. We also saw 2 birthdays being celebrated while we were there, which the staff handled with so much enthusiasm!Ambience: 8/10It's absolutely beautiful in here! They have moody lighting with the string lights. There's also a bunch of soju caps hung around the room, which makes it perfect for playing some casual drinking games.

After hearing endless praises from colleagues, I ventured to a popular local eatery keen to experience its offerings for myself. Arriving just before the noon rush, I was met with a modest queue of five and was promptly greeted by a staff member who handled my initial order of a protein choice. I opted for the ground beef kebab, intrigued by the diverse selection process.

The subsequent steps involved a personalized approach to the meal: I selected beans and fried Brussels sprouts for my vegetables, though the sprouts were slightly overdone and dry. A fresh kale salad complemented the dish, and I couldn't resist adding an assortment of three dips, along with pickles—all of which added a flavorful dimension.

For good measure, I sampled the steak and chicken ordered by my colleagues. Each protein held its own, leaving no room for disappointment. It's worth mentioning that some items include nuts, a potential concern for allergy-sufferers, but the staff was diligent in making these details clear.

Pricewise, the meal was reasonable. A full spread of three different proteins rounded up to $42 with tax. In all, the experience lived up to the hype, and despite a minor setback with the sprouts, the restaurant delivered a satisfying and varied lunch option.

Service at this place is pretty straight forward. Even though it's a pizza joint you get the Mexican hospitality of the guys who work here which make it even better. The food here is totally worth the price as well not too cheap and not too expensive. This joint is very clean as well.

I don't like writing bad reviews, because generally we're all trying our best, right? But this place was dismal for ramen. I didn't try the sushi but let me talk about this ramen. There were barely any noodles in here! They dumped so much spicy flavoring in here but that's it. I am always full after ramen but this time I felt like I barely ate anything. The egg was sickly looking and not good at all. Broth was mediocre. They put no pork slices in there. I should one star this but service was pretty quick and they got me out of there in no time so I guess that counts for something.

Needing a quick and warm lunch, my fiancé and I go to Ippudo in Manhattan! Luckily we were seated immediately, despite the business of Thursday lunchtime! We were seated next to people/shared a large table, which we don't mind, but it's good to know just in case some people do mind. We ordered the shiromaru hakata classic (ramen with dashi) as well as a small bowl of tuna and rice.It was my first time having dashi, so I loved the fishy and saltier essence of the broth! Sometimes having pork broth can get monotonous, so it's nice having a change of broth flavors! The noodles were somewhat al dente, although a little bit closer to the firmer side. A delicious dish! While my fiancé and I were almost done with our respective entrees, we were still waiting for the tuna and rice. When someone asked if we were waiting on anything else, we asked about the tuna and rice. He looked surprised it wasn't out yet considering our entrees were almost complete. He told someone in the kitchen, and then 10 minutes later, the tuna and rice came out. Seems like they forgot about our dish, little yikes. The tuna and rice were delicious, and they tasted even better with the spicy mayo sauce drizzled over the dish. At only $3 (when ordered with a bowl of ramen), I couldn't complain too much about this dish.Overall great place to go to! My only hiccup was when they forgot about our side dish.

Title: A Vietnamese Delight Awaits at [Restaurant Name]

My experience at [Restaurant Name] deserves high praise for its irresistible Vietnamese fare, stretching from the comfort of Pho to the succulent pork chops. This gem offers all the beloved classics while daring to spin some unique twists that elevate it beyond the typical fare. Although I've only begun to explore their menu, the dishes gracing not just my table but also those around me appeared mouthwateringly delectable. I'm definitely returning to continue this culinary adventure.

Title: A Soontofu Sanctuary with a Side of Mediocrity

If you find yourself at this establishment, zero in on the soontofu—it's the star of the show. The beef soontofu I ordered arrived straight from the kitchen, bubbling with a heat that promised flavor and comfort. As it settled on the table, a fresh egg was cracked and gently submerged into the stew, cooking delicately amidst the simmering tofu. The spice levels cater to various palates, but as an aficionado of fiery dishes, the 'hot' hit the spot for me without overpowering the senses. Beware of venturing into 'danger' territory unless you're purely in it for the thrill.

I also sampled the bibimbap, which unfortunately fell flat, proving to be quite typical and lacking the pizzazz of its soupy counterpart. Complimentary small plates are a bonus, with an option for refills, though the fried fish included might not be to everyone's taste due to its bony texture—I certainly didn't care to finish mine.

In essence, the soontofu is the main act worth the visit; skip the filler and stick with this restaurant's fiery forte.
Wow!  Another great Chef Bouley property.  Am not going to ruin the surprise.  You need to go.  Will be one of those great life experiences.

Title: Flavor Fusion and Fantastic Margaritas at Buddha Taco Bar!

My recent visit to Buddha Taco Bar was an absolute delight, especially for a tequila enthusiast like me. Their Passionfruit Margarita stands out as a top contender in my extensive margarita tasting experiences. With plans to return for their house-made infused tequilas and tantalizing cocktail lineup, Buddha Taco Bar has quickly become a favorite.

The menu offers a creative blend of Mexican and Korean flavors that tantalize the taste buds. The taquitos are a classic must-try: crispy, cheesy, and perfectly filled with shredded meat. When it comes to tacos, there's something for every palate. Heat-seekers should dive into the kimchi pulled pork—its tenderness and homemade kimchi pack a punch. The pork belly taco is a delightful twist on the traditional, while their fish tacos offer a lighter, yet equally flavorful option. The star of the show, however, was the shrimp taco, seasoned to perfection with evidently fresh shrimp.

In summary, Buddha Taco Bar impressed with their combination of mouth-watering tacos, fair prices, and exceptional service. And for those who appreciate a good happy hour, the drinks here are a must. Cheers to a spot that checks all the boxes for a fun and flavorful dining experience!

Title: A Cozy Retreat from the Rain at The Irish Pub

On a drizzly day, The Irish Pub proved to be a serendipitous find right off the subway, offering a snug haven while I waited for a ballet performance. In search of a quick snack and drink, I opted for their house Irish Pub Amber Ale paired with Loaded Potato Skins. The ale was a delightful match for the gloomy weather, boasting a robust flavor and just the right body to lift my spirits. However, the Potato Skins, although a promising choice, fell short of expectations – they were somewhat bland and lacked the anticipated crispiness, arriving with a softer texture than preferred.

The ambiance was enhanced by the array of TV screens peppered around, allowing patrons to keep an eye on sports games while enjoying their meal. Reflecting on a past visit, I can attest to the quality of their burgers, which were a hit among my friends and me. The Irish Pub offers a mix of comfort and conviviality, ideal for both casual solo visits and relaxed outings with companions.

I'm not sure how I didn't know about Kubeh. It has been around for two years in the Greenwich Village area. It was a suggestion my friend made for dinner and a first for both of us.Their cuisine is Middle Eastern with flavors from Syria, Iran and Israel.We didn't have a reservation (mistake so keep that in mind especially on a Friday night) but there was an available table for the duration of 90 minutes. Worked for us.The décor was lovely, cozy and inviting. Happy hour ends at 6 p.m. but since we arrived at 6:02, they allowed us to select wine from their HH menu--I chose a crisp Rose from France and my friend selected a Pinot Noir--both delicious.The menu was diverse and it was difficult to choose. Kubeh, the traditional dish that bears its name, was a popular choice (soup containing meat or vegetable filled dumplings) but we ultimately decided on the Persian Lime Chicken. Twin meals. We were informed it was a hearty selection for the unseasonably cold weather. It arrived not long after we placed our order. Indeed, it was a large bowl that included rice, potatoes, veggies and a pretty big chicken leg (thigh and drumstick). Unfortunately, there was no option to have the breast or white meat which was my only nitpick but the meal was flavorful and delicious. My friend and I both devoured it leaving not a morsel behind.And just like Cinderella's coach turned into a pumpkin at the end of the fairytale, we had to give up our table at the designated time. Luckily, we were too full to order dessert. As we left, the entire restaurant, including bar area was nearly filled. Kubeh is a keeper and I'm going to return (hopefully soon) to try their traditional dish, Kubeh and brunch. The food was delicious, atmosphere was cozy and staff were very hospitable.Really good!

Title: My Go-To Spot for the Ultimate Steak Sandwiches

There's something about this place that keeps me coming back, especially when work brings me to the area. Their chimichurri steak sandwich is a masterpiece that I can't resist ordering for myself and my crew. The option to choose your bread is a nice touch, but it's the generous layers of juicy steak, melted cheese, and a medley of onions, mushrooms, jalapeños, and crispy onion rings, all drenched in a flavorful chimichurri sauce, that takes the sando experience to a whole new level. It might not be a menu mainstay, but the staff never fails to whip it up upon request.

Don't skip their soups either—opt for a creamy one if you can. The salmon chowder I had was simply sublime. And for those looking for something lighter, the salad bar is a fresh delight. You pick the ingredients, they do the chopping, and voilà: a fresh, personalized salad.

Just a heads up—payment and departure might require a bit of patience during peak hours due to the crowds. But trust me, the flavors you'll discover here are well worth any minor inconvenience.

I had the unexpected pleasure of visiting this spot for a late night pizza run and was thoroughly impressed. For just $4, the margherita pizza offered a satisfying balance of cheese, sauce, and basil on a crust that struck the perfect note between too thin and just right. It's definitely worth stopping by if you find yourself in the neighborhood with a pizza craving. Recommended!

On a bustling Tuesday evening, our dining experience kicked off on a high note with a warm welcome and immediate seating due to our reservation. However, we soon found ourselves crammed into our booth, a tad too close for comfort to our neighbors.

Our server, friendly but clearly overwhelmed, took our order promptly but then vanished into the abyss of busy tables. The tapas trickle out at a snail's pace, testing our patience. When they did arrive, the "Salteado de Setas" and "Patatas Bravas" were delectable, and the "Pulpo a la Plancha" was beautifully tender. Yet the "Gambas al Ajillo" disappointed with its unexpected cool temperature, and the "Albóndigas" were underwhelming, vanishing from memory as quickly as they did from the table.

Despite the slower service and a mixed bag of hits and misses, the vibrant atmosphere carried us through a pleasant evening of camaraderie. Unwilling to gamble on additional waiting times, we opted to cap off the night elsewhere with dessert and drinks. Cheers to the delights and letdowns of gastronomic adventures!

What a great stop to stop and dine while you sit on the patio and watch North Broadway come to life (I think we were north, we were at the top of Broadway regardless). Just a few blocks from the theater district this had a large selection of food to choose from. I especially enjoyed the gentleman who greeted us when we came up to Applejacks tired and a little sweaty (we hoofed it from the Met). He was quite friendly and welcoming and we were excited to be able to sit outside and people-watch. I ran off to the Theater district to collect Playbills with my daughter and my son and hubby held down the table. They were so accommodating while we were on our scavenger hunt. The Long Islands were delightful and the servings were large! Come hungry!

Food is great but the food takes forever to come out. Service is hit and miss depending on the day. Sometimes the staff is awesome and other times they are just average. The truffle Mac and cheese is so worth the money!!! It's a must order.

Great place for a special occasion at a reasonable price (and in an incredible space). I managed to get off the waiting list for a reservation when another party cancelled last minute. The interior is beautiful and great for a date night. There are only a handful of tables, so the ambiance is intimate and quiet, but the low dining chairs and interior garden still make it feel relaxed and not at all stuffy. The service and drinks were both great, and each dish was delicious! I recommend skipping the fixed price menu and ordering a la carte instead.My favorites were the uni croquettes and the beef short rib sashimi. As for my drink, I really enjoyed the Indian Cooler (citrusy chai).

We got here a little after 5pm since reservations are mostly walk in and were seated right away.  Score!  However, because we got there so friggin' early, I wasn't the slightest bit hungry.  I told my man to order whatever he wanted since I was just gonna nibble.  We got our eats and I gobbled up more than half of our order!Jeju chicken wings:  These have got to be the crispiest chicken wings I've ever had.  I don't know how they do it, but BRAVO!!  The inside was nice and juicy too.  The accompanying crudités were very tasty as well.  Loved the dipping sauce.  5/5Pyunche salad: I love my condiments and the chimichurri and spicy yang yum jang were delish paired with the Amberjack and greens.  4.5/5So Ramyun:  OMG this was so good.  The veal broth was bursting with flavor, the brisket was tender, the noodles had the perfect bite, and the fried garlic atop was a winner.  Add the banksuk egg!  5/5Excellent service too.  Can't wait to come back!

I ordered the beef chow fun and it came in a pretty big portion. It was a little disappointing that the food was dry and did not have much flavor. The chow fun was quite bland. I was expecting it to be more juicy. However, the Thai iced tea was really good.

Title: A Neighborhood Gem with Flavors That Impress

I recently stumbled upon a new spot just around the corner from my apartment and decided to give it a try when hunger struck on a casual stroll. The experience from start to finish was nothing short of delightful. Despite the minor hiccup with their credit card terminal being down, the cashier's warm smile and accommodating nature ensured I didn't have to wait unnecessarily for my meal.

Taking a quick dash to the ATM to pay in cash, I returned to find my order ready and steaming. The food was superb, packed with an explosion of flavors that had me relishing every bite. It's rare to find such delicious sheish that leaves a memorable impression.

I've since returned multiple times and each visit reaffirms that I'll definitely be back whenever I'm in New York. This place isn't just convenient; it's a culinary treasure for anyone in search of a flavor-packed meal served with a genuine smile.

The whole fam bam was in Chinatown, and after deciding Vietnamese was the way to go I gave yelp a quick search and Thai Son popped up. I really love Vietnamese grilled meat with all the veggies wraps and fermented carrots/radishes... and Thai son has a combo for you that could feed a village and then some (just kidding we managed with 4 people). For $30~ it comes with grilled pork (so so so good), fried spring rolls, grilled shrimp/seafood meat ball, beef wrapped in grape leaves, and everything else that someone as indecisive as me wants. This was def a winner for all of us, so if you're coming with a big crowd this is the dish.. or rather platter, to get. My other favorite Vietnamese dish is banh xeo (crispy egg crepe filled with savory stuff). Thai son served me a pretty big banh xeo, but fillings were a bit lacking. Felt like they weren't really trying and it was just 90% bean sprouts. As if we didn't already have a lot of food we also got a bowl of pho and seafood over crispy egg noodles. The noodle dish was also pretty gigantic. I love getting the crispy bits but also the softer/chewier texture as it soaks up the gravy sauce. Overall, good viet spot and you def get your money's worth!

Nestled away just off its listed address, this gem of a restaurant may take a moment to find, but your efforts will be richly rewarded. The expansive interior offers ample space, ensuring a comfortable dining experience without the usual crammed-in feel. An ambitious menu tempted us to indulge in virtually every offering; standout dishes included a sublime Paella, luxurious Foie Gras, and a tender, perfectly cooked Octopus. We accompanied our meal with both white and red sangrias, each one a delightful complement to the array of flavors. Every sip and bite was a testament to the establishment's commitment to culinary excellence. Highly recommended for an unforgettable dining experience.

I love lobster. I enjoy watching Shark Tank. So, when the opportunity to eat lobster at Cousins Maine Lobster came up while in NYC, we decided to give it a shot. The verdict: Very tasty, and very pricey for fast casual (but it is lobster so kind of expected to an extent). We tried the Connecticut Lobster Roll (warm) and the Maine Lobster Roll (cold) as well as the lobster tots. My daughter who doesn't like lobster got a salad with chicken. We drank tap water. 4 lunch meals and $88 later, we sat down and ate. We enjoyed the lobster rolls a lot, especially the Connecticut version. The grilled bun paired with the warm lobster pieces was a treat. The tots were great though we wish more lobster was inside. My taste buds hope we get one in Michigan, but my wallet isn't as interested. In any case, I'll be surprised if this actual location sticks around because it was empty, at a peek lunch time. I'm guessing they'll find a different location to open in NYC where they get more traction. I'll have to check back to see if I'm right.

Title: A Chinatown Gem for Jianbing Lovers

I can't help but share my love for this Chinatown culinary staple. It stands out as a go-to spot I find myself returning to time and again without a hint of disappointment. Their jianbing is a must-try, boasting generous portions at a price that undercuts the competition elsewhere in the city. Whether it's the sausage, fish, or beef option, you're in for a treat, though the beef remains my personal champion.

Don't miss out on their noodles; they're equally delightful. But it's not just the food that makes this place shine. The service adds to the charm, with attentive staff ensuring a cozy dining experience even when the place is bustling. Be aware that restroom access requires a brief excursion outside and down to the basement, a small quirk in an otherwise seamless dining experience.

Came here with a friend for a fancy Sunday brunch. The decor and ambiance is pretty upscale, so a perfect excuse to dress up a little!We had the $32 3-course lunch menu, which was a very good deal for both the quality and amount of food you get! I also thoroughly enjoyed the bread they provided to start, accompanied by olive oils and fresh herbs. For my appetizer, I had the Greek meze plate, which in itself could've been a full meal! I really liked all 3 of the dips, although my favorite was probably the taramosalata. I also requested extra pita bread, which came warm and freshly baked! For my entree, I had the dorade royal - come hungry for this one, since it's a full fish! Simply cooked but very fresh, and great with some of the leftover dips from my meze appetizer. Finally, for dessert, I had the Greek yogurt - I'm a sucker for any Greek yogurt, but the crumbled baklava really made this one! Would probably come back just for the Greek yogurt alone! Had a great experience here - would definitely consider coming back again to try more dishes!

Decor and entrance is just beautiful. Good and symbolic way to represents lobster. If you're curious check it out for yourself Lobster bites - fresh lobster and shrimp wrapped in a pastry shell with cheese and pickles. 4 small bites. I wasn't sure what to make of it. It was interesting but I was confused. Is this supposed to resemble a Vietnamese egg roll? The lobster and shrimp... it didn't really complement each other well but I appreciated the whole chunks of lobster!Combo for 1 - A 6oz burger and a whole 1lb lobster with fries and salad. We see other people order this combo for just themselves to eat. My mom and I were like, nuh uh, were gonna share! We ordered medium rare for the burger and grilled for the lobster. Surprisingly, I really liked the burger! The bun was crispy and bronze with sesame seeds on top. The beef patty was perfectly rare with juices gushing out with each bite. The pickles were lovely.However, I didn't seem to appreciate the lobster as much. I expected more. I think it may have been a tad over cooked. BUT the buttery hollandaise sauce that came with the lobster to dip in was very goodLobster Mac n cheese. This was just okay. For $14, they gave enough lobster chunks but the quality and cheesiness of the Mac n cheese wasn't quite there. It just wasn't great. Disappointed.Pros:-can make reservations on yelp-cute decor Cons:

Tucked in for a Saturday brunch at this local spot and dove into their specials menu. I started with the house bread—it's serviceable, if forgettable. The salad, a standard affair, hit the mark for a house offering. However, the standout was truly the veggie pizza. With a perfectly baked crust, generous melt of cheese, and vibrant, fresh toppings, it was a dish to remember—and generously portioned, easily shared between two.

Service was attentive, though the dining experience was dampened slightly by the cramped seating arrangement. Navigating the tight space made for a bit of discomfort, as the wait staff—through no fault of their own—necessitated frequent shuffling in an already congested area. Worth a visit for the pizza, but be prepared for close quarters.

I guess I may have accidentally impregnated someone when I was in Thailand, I'm not sure. I didn't even know which gender I was messing around with and didn't care. But now this girl named Billie Jean from Bangkok is saying this kid is mine, and I'm like.SHE SAYS I AM THE ONEBUT THE KID IS NOT MY THAI SONReally adorable Thai restaurant which was one of my first Thai meals ever in New York City. It's not a city that has a massive amount of Thai, and there are some real things mixed in with the not so real. But I like this. Back at the time I didn't really know what authentic food was so I can't speak to the authenticity. It was about three years ago.We tried to go here recently but ended up being late. I'm looking forward to updating my experience here but I wanted to review it before I forgot all about it because I am on a mission to make sure I review everything that I've ever eaten at.

After a manageable wait for a table—a time investment I highly recommend—my taste buds were rewarded with the "Spicy Spring" pepperoni pizza. The flavors were nothing short of amazing, confirming that the culinary queue was time well-spent. My friends might have had fashion on their agenda across the street at Everlane, but my priority was well-placed on this delicious pizza. Do yourself a favor: wait it out and order the spicy spring. You won't regret it.

Went there on a Sunday morning. Had a wait time of 5 mins and service was excellent. We got promptly seated. Ordered a English breakfast, got an earl grey tea bag already in my water so did not say anything. Also because I love both teas. Ordered the nova Benny. Poached eggs- perfectly done Which Im Not going to take for granted just because it's a good place. Smoked salmon- beautiful :) I was a tad disappointed with the potato pancakes which were hard and seemed old and re-heated. Bummer because I was really looking forward to them.Also disappointed with the cappuccino :( In a nutshell did have good food not great and don't think I going to go back though.

One of our favorite spot for Cantonese food.The price is very reasonable.And somehow I don't need to wait every time I went there. Their curry beef stew with rice noodles is the must, I ordered this everything I go.Also the salty fried pork is the best! I highly recommend everyone should order this plate.

Excellent pizza! I don't know why it's so hard to find deep dish pizza in NYC. I mean, I get it, we aren't Chicago but for a city that has food from 8000 miles away, I think we'd at least have some more national options in the city.Anyway, I am a huge fan of deep dish and have been wanting to go to Emmett's for a while. Finally went this past weekend and it was just like the deep dish in Chicago really. So freaking cheesy and thick. A medium pie can definitely fill three moderate appetites. You chose your pie and toppings making it completely customized which is great. However, the veggie toppings are a bit on the pricey side...It's a small space with few tables but decent bar seating and no outdoor seating. The pizza here is worth your time, come have a bite!

Came here with friends since it was close and open.  Just needed a place to sit and talk.  Got a ice coffee it was huge.  Friends got chocolate pudding and rice pudding.  The puddings came in a pint container.  Big and each is less than 5.00.  Two bites in, friend said rice pudding taste weird.  We smelled it and it was spoiled.  Won't be coming back in the future.

Not gonna lie, the dish that lured me in was the hanging sliced pork belly. It didn't disappoint! The sauce was to die for! We also got a fish soup, a vegetable dish & a chicken dish. All were so flavorful and surprisingly not too spicy. Generally, I find that Szechuan food is really salty but it wasn't too bad. It did leave me really bloated the next day though. The restaurant is pretty big and spacious for a restaurant in Flushing. The service is actually pretty good too! They always made sure we had ample tea and change of plates. Definitely my new favorite Szechuan spot!

I stopped by this spot for their $5 happy hour drinks at the bar and was pleasantly surprised. The temptation from the menu was too much to resist, so I also tried the pão de queijo and churrasco de boi. The food was decent, delivering flavors that satisfied the craving for a hearty meal with the steak and garlic sauce combination hitting the spot. To top it off, the service was good – attentive without being overbearing. Overall, you can't go wrong with $5 happy hour drinks and a solid menu to complement them.

This place was pretty decent. Came in after walking for literally miles around NYC looking at Christmas window displays and lights and worked up a good craving for some fatty food. This restaurant was mobbed! So they must be popular. When we went to give our name, they said the wait would be a little over an hour.... but we had no choice but to stay and hoped it would be quicker than what they told us. To our surprise, we only waited about ten minutes before our little hand held device started lighting up. Sweet! We Were seated downstairs by the bar area and I was ready to just order something and get grubbing. We ended up getting a ranch hand burger which was a cheese burger with bacon served on a pretzel bun! It was so juicy and delish. We also had a chicken quesadilla and they were just okay to me--- I was loving the burger too much- but we shared. The burger came with fries and were seasoned perfectly. My friend ordered a rum and coke and the first one he had he could barely taste the rum, but the second one, was mostly all rum and no coke, but he was happy, and I was laughing as he got a little tipsy from his drink. I'm glad we came here because we both left with happy stomachs and surprisingly filled from the food although we shared. I would come back again if in this area.

The roll was great and it had a good filling of lobster. The fries were also well cooked and extremely well seasoned. My favorite part was definitely dipping the fries into the mayo. I think this place is great, but their serving of lobster isn't as heavy as Luke's Lobster from what I have experienced

I recently visited a restaurant with a unique concept that thoroughly impressed me. Upon arrival, you purchase a pre-loaded card with your desired spending amount. Return the card before leaving, and you're rewarded with a $1 refund. For cash loyalists, handing over $20 gets you a $25 value on the card—a neat little perk.

The real novelty lies in their dual walls fitted with various beer taps, each accompanied by a helpful description that includes the name, origin, alcohol content, and price per ounce. With a simple card tap, you have 10 seconds to pour and sample as you please, controlling both the quantity and cost of your drink. The system offers an excellent variety of beers to cater to different tastes and preferences.

The ambiance is perfect for sports enthusiasts, with plentiful seating and TVs in every corner to ensure you don't miss a game. As for the food, the wings were simply outstanding, complementing the beer selection wonderfully.

Whether it's a date, a casual meet-up with friends, or just enjoying a game, this spot ticks all the boxes. I had a great time and I'm already planning my next visit. Highly recommended.

Title: A Pleasant First Brunch-Dinner Experience

My friends and I had our inaugural dining experience here during the transition from brunch to dinner hours. We kicked off our waiting period by delving into the "cheese and meats" selection, enjoying a generous and tasty tabla de queso y embutidos, which comfortably served our party of four. However, the sangrias we ordered, priced nearly at $50 each, didn't quite hit the mark in terms of value for money.

Once dinner commenced, the dishes on the table included pulpo a la plancha and pollo rustido, both of which my friends devoured happily. The star of the show was the large paella, which, despite its slightly overdone bottom, stole my heart and comes highly recommended.

We concluded with churros, where the dulce de leche-filled ones stood out as a must-have. Despite the enjoyable food and excellent service, the restaurant didn't leave me with a strong urge to return soon, but those churros might tempt me back someday.

Working in Soho this week and came across this restaurant on Yelp. Tried it with a friend and the food was yummm. The Crispy artichokes are a must - don't you love when you don't have to work to each your artichoke. My favorite dish was the Cacio e pepe, probably one of the best I've had including a trip to Italy. The complimentary chips and dip appetizer was also a cool addition. The dip is different for sure but I was a fan.It was pretty easy to get a last minute reservation for two. The bar was lively and music kept it interesting. The food came out quick. There's not a lot on their menu but every dish we had was good. Not sure why this place isn't rated higher I enjoyed myself and servers were very attentive.

Title: A Flavorful Feast at a Fair Price

If you're searching for authentic flavors, this is the spot. On our visit, we delved into the R1, R2, R5, and the standout shredded pork and preserved egg congee – a heartwarming classic. The portion sizes were perfect for our group of four. We especially enjoyed the rice rolls, which were tender yet sturdy enough to embrace the filling effectively – and at $6-7, they're a steal given their generous size.

The congee is a star dish and an absolute must-try. Be warned, though: this place is popular, so you might encounter long lines. However, their extending operating hours offer flexible options outside the peak meal times. Service-wise, we felt well-attended, with regular check-ins and constant drink refills. This joint is a delightful find that doesn't disappoint.

I visited this restaurant on a less crowded Saturday night and took advantage of the complimentary naan with a Yelp check-in. My Tandoori chicken, served with rice, arrived swiftly. Although I requested spicy, the dish lacked the expected heat, and while some chicken pieces were succulent, others were dry. The flavor was mediocre, and the accompanying rice, though fluffy, didn't have the distinct basmati taste I've savored elsewhere. The naan was passable but unremarkable. Overall, the dining experience was decent, yet nothing truly exceptional to note.

Title: A Satisfying Bite at Lenwich - 82nd and Columbus

During a hurried morning dash to work, I decided to try out Lenwich for a quick sandwich fix. The chain was new to me, but their extensive menu boasted an array of enticing options. The shop's spacious, sunlit interior on 82nd and Columbus welcomed me with ample seating.

Ordering was a straightforward affair: select at the back, pay at the front, and await your meal. Opting for the chicken parm on ciabatta, which set me back $11.92, I found the 10-minute wait reasonable. They announced my order for pickup, presenting a sandwich that justified the cost with its quality. 

Lenwich delivered a typical modern deli experience—variety-rich menu, custom salads, beverages, desserts, and all. The staff exuded friendliness, the environment boasted cleanliness, and the sandwich hit the spot. Lenwich ticks all the boxes for a quick, reliable eatery.

Authentic delicious cuisine, the staff are very eager to please. We were attending a 7pm show on Broadway and they were honest about the time it would it would take to prepare so suggested certain items to order that would take the shoertest amount of tIme to prepare (we arrived at the restaurant just after 6pm).We ordered a quesadilla, the freshly made guacamole and three tacos after they suggested that these take the shortest amount of time to make.  They don't have their liquor license yet, but they advised that we could BYOB next time.Overall very good authentic Mexican with and eager to please with an eager to please attitude.

Title: A Spirited Spring Fling Event at a Ping Pong Haven

I had the delight of ticking off a long-standing bookmark during our company's Spring Fling Event held at this venue that's a stone's throw from our office and the 6 train station. The ease of access made for a smooth start to an event-filled afternoon.

Descending into the venue, we were promptly wrist-banded by a colleague, marking us ready for the festivities. Our reserved space boasted four ping pong tables nestled between plush leather chairs and an additional cozy seating area. It had been ages since I last played ping pong, and despite being a bit rusty (I can't deny my competitive streak, possibly inherited from my dad who played in tournaments back in Shanghai), I eagerly dove into doubles matches. Let's just say my serves were enthusiastic enough to send balls flying in unexpected directions!

Transitioning from beer to sparkling rosé, the latter was a refreshing switch that paired delightfully with the eclectic selection of nibbles. The Hop Pop Chicken and Beef Sliders were spot-on in flavor, while the Mac n Cheese Bites were a comforting indulgence. The Shrimp Ceviche's heavy cilantro presence was not to my taste, but that was quickly remedied by the sweet finale of macarons from a tantalizing dessert spread.

This place isn't just a restaurant; it's an experience melding sport, sips, and savories. I'm left with no doubt that I'll be returning – it was an unequivocally FUN event!

Title: A Slice of Authenticity in the Heart of NYC

As a devoted food lover, I eagerly stepped into this New York City gem for a taste of Indian/Pakistani cuisine. True to the city's character, the restaurant is unassuming – a modest hole in the wall with nothing more than a counter for seating that is overshadowed by the constant bustle. Visitors may find themselves sidestepping to allow access to the cramped restroom, all part of the authentic NYC cabbie atmosphere.

The culinary highlight was undoubtedly the stewed chicken, paired with a hearty side of cauliflower and potatoes, which I found to be exceptional. The flavors were rich and the chicken fell apart tenderly with each bite. Conversely, the samosa topped with chickpea stew failed to impress. The dish's execution – a samosa drowned in chickpeas – was unexpected and not to my preference.

For those seeking the plush comforts of a fine-dining establishment, this spot won't be your destination. However, if it's an adventure for your palate and a no-frills experience you're after, this restaurant delivers. The food resonates with genuine flavor and the place pulses with the city's relentless energy. Worth a visit for anyone looking to savor an unpretentious bite of NYC's diverse culinary offerings.

I recently visited this eatery for a lunch special and was pleasantly surprised by the Spicy Eggplant with Garlic Sauce. Despite its name, the dish wasn't particularly spicy, which actually worked in its favor, allowing the flavors of the sumptuous garlic sauce to shine. Pricing was quite fair, at around $9, and the portion size served was just right—not too little, not too much, but perfect for a satisfying midday meal.

From the moment we entered, the enticing aroma assured us of a savory experience ahead. The service was commendable, attentive without being intrusive. The restaurant offers a versatile dining approach with both tapas and larger dish options. I indulged in the complimentary Yelp check-in shot followed by a zesty jalapeño margarita, which set the tone for the evening.

Our table reveled in a shared feast that included crispy popcorn chicken, succulent pork dumplings, perfectly roasted vegetables, and a flavorful tiger roll. Each dish arrived swiftly, brimming with taste and artfully presented, leaving no room for disappointment.

The portions were generous, ensuring that we departed with contented stomachs and the kind of satisfaction that comes from a meal well-enjoyed. This restaurant has earned a spot on my list of go-to places—I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Really good Cantonese food in the heart of Chinatown. The food is excellent quality and well prepared. While service is a bit gruff, it is relatively fast and efficient. The noodles, soups and dim sum are all great. August Gatherings has a liquor license with a good selection of wine and spirits. With a lot of good spots to choose from, August Gatherings stands out and we keep going out. Please note that it is cash only.

How CUTE is this place! It's got to be the best Thai in Hell's Kitchen and the cutest restaurant in the neighborhood as well! The staff is so friendly and gives great recommendations! Favorite dishes were the Honey Tamarind Duck and the grilled Pork Chops with honey garlic sauce (I guess I love honey!). The lighting is great for Instagram pictures and you definitely should try the mango sticky rice for dessert. I love love LOVED it here and will be back (probably once a month lol)! I know there is a billion other Thai places within blocks but go here first! You won't be mad

Title: A Group Feast on St. Marks - The Bao

If you're navigating the culinary landscape of St. Marks, The Bao stands out as an essential group dining destination. The diverse menu practically begs for a communal, family-style meal, giving everyone at the table a chance to dive into a variety of flavors. While it may not be a dumpling heavyweight in a city brimming with dim sum options, it more than makes up for it with standout items. Reservations are a wise move here – the long lines speak to the restaurant's popularity.

Don't miss out on the fiery delight of the super spicy xiao long Bao or the unique texture of the lotus root dumplings. For those who favor the heat, the Szechuan chili fried chicken is a must. My strategy of trying something new on each visit keeps the experience fresh and exciting. The Bao is definitely a spot I'd urge any food enthusiast to check out!

I recently stumbled upon El Centro during a busy day of errands and was immediately thankful for the find. The eatery was quiet, a welcome oasis for a quick lunch break. My coworker and I entered on a whim, and our serendipitous decision was well rewarded.

We were greeted by warm service — something I particularly appreciated when a thoughtful waitress steered me away from empanadas cooked in pork fat due to my dietary preferences. Instead, I savored the mahi mahi tacos which were a delightful mix of juicy fish with the perfect balance of spice and tang. My coworker's shrimp enchiladas were also tasty, but I'd opt for the tacos on a return visit without a second thought.

El Centro didn't revolutionize my dining experiences, but it did exactly what I needed: it provided delicious food with considerate service, leaving me satisfied and refueled for the remainder of my day.

I'm surprised I've never gotten around to posting a review here - the best South Indian restaurant in Manhattan is thankfully open for take-out during COVID, and fulfilled my craving for a dosa and filter coffee breakfast. I'll go back soon to fulfill my twin craving for a poori and coffee, just like I would have every morning in Bangalore.

Food is average, the pescatore linguini didn't excite me. Mozzarella appetizer is on the salty side. Chocolate cake is too sweet. Place is quiet and cozy. Good for meeting and conversation over drinks. Staff are attentive. Won't come back for awhile.

I recently visited Field Good Chicken for a meal that proved to be mostly delightful. The main attraction, a well-seasoned and perfectly cooked half chicken, did not disappoint. It was both satisfying and gave the impression of a healthier dining choice. Accompanying the chicken was a generous helping of mac and cheese and broccoli. Unfortunately, the mac and cheese fell short, lacking the cheesy punch one craves in such a dish. The broccoli was decent, rounding out the meal fine. The cornbread was a pleasant surprise, boasting just the right balance of sweetness without being overly crumbly. Portion sizes won't leave you hungry, and with a variety of sides to choose from, there's something for everyone.
