Despite a minor hiccup with one of the sides, I would recommend Field Good Chicken for anyone looking for a hearty and seemingly health-conscious option.

This place is not bad if you want something spicy to eat. Personally for me, the food was alittle too spicy though. I took one bite of my taco and my eyes begun to water and my stomach begun to burn. . I'm sure I can deffinatly find something on the menue that isn't that spicy the next time I decide to come in , but for now.. It is what it is. The staff was actually really friendly about the whole scenario and offered to replace the dish but my stomach was just shot afterwards. The place was cute and lively and I will be back to try again some day. I've added this place to my bucket list. It did have a great atmosphere and that friendly service. I really do want to try other things on the menue when I return! The guac actually looked amazing. It will be on my list of things to try for the next time I'm in nyc.

I recently visited Taqueria Emilio for lunch and was thoroughly impressed with their offerings. I opted for the lunch special at just $8, which included three tacos and a soda; a fantastic deal. My choices were the tacos al pastor, along with a tamarind Jarritos, and couldn't resist adding a chipotle chicken taco to meet the credit card minimum.

Before the main event, we were treated to a basket of chips accompanied by two contrasting salsas – one mild green and one spicy reddish-orange. The chips were a perfect crunchy prelude and set the stage for the salsas, with the fiery option winning my preference.

The arrival of the tacos was a sight to behold – a plate brimming with generously topped offerings, each adorned with a swirl of sour cream and a sprinkle of queso fresco. The taste was even more remarkable than the presentation; the al pastor was delightfully sweet with pineapple, melting in my mouth, while the chipotle chicken brought tears of joy with its flavor. Despite feeling full after the four tacos, my palate yearned for more of these exceptional creations. Taqueria Emilio now holds the title of having the best tacos I've enjoyed in recent memory.

Title: A Flavorsome Experience with a Side of Slow Service

I recently visited a local eatery and my taste buds were in for a treat! The sour pickle and fish rice noodle soup I ordered had a robust flavor that was quite heavy, yet I found myself enjoying every spoonful. I also indulged in the spring special - a fried egg with Chinese chives and shrimp. While the dish nailed the authentic taste, the portion of shrimp was a tad disappointing for the $20 price tag, offering just five to six pieces.

The pineapple grilled pork belly and BBQ shrimp didn't disappoint, either. It was a delightful fusion of Eastern and Western seasonings, and the meats were exceptionally tender. However, service could use a step up in speed, and be prepared to cozy up with strangers since communal tables are the norm here. All in all, the food certainly made up for the minor hiccups.

Small crowded dining room. You will share your table with other guests but you may get lucky like we did and sit with interesting people. We got the sausage plater to share and an order of spaetzles. Both were decent. Too bad they're closing down after about 20 years.

I was so excited to try this place after hearing about their win in the ramen fest. My friend and I ordered one pork belly bun each for an appetizer. It was only $3 for the happy hour so we couldn't resist. They were extremely messy but a joy to eat. Melted in our mouths, as they should. It was a more chinese style of pork belly but I don't really mind since I love chinese pork belly. Unfortunately I think I striked out with my ramen by ordering their less known dish - tonkotsu ramen. The pork belly was really delicious, a nice sweet, glazed flavor. The noodles were pretty decent as well. However, I was disappointed that for a $15 dish, I had to pay an extra $2 for a runny egg. I can't imagine that to not be a norm for a ramen dish at that price point but oh well. I was also a little disappointed with the broth, it was relatively flavorful but not the punch that I was looking for in a broth. The service, however, was the the best part. Our waiter was extremely attentive and would refill our water constantly and remove plates right as well finished them. He also checked in often with our table to see how we were doing. Granted, it was a Thursday at 6 PM, so they weren't that busy, but I really appreciated the care. We also stayed for an extra hour after finishing our meal to talk, even after paying the bill and were not rushed out at all. It was a very nice and chill vibe, and allowed me to feel comfortable.

I remember trying poke for the first time as a teen in Cali, the Asian food capital of the United States. "These lucky Californians" I thought to myself. "Why can't New York have poke like this?" Yes I know poke is Hawaiian, but its creation was influenced by Japanese workers arriving to HI in the 1800s right? Doesn't it just taste like deconstructed sushi in a bowl? I think it's the bees knees.Fast forward a decade and it is an absolute boom time for poke in NY. In this area alone there's Maui Onion, Snowfox, Chikarashi, heck, Little Beet has a poke bowl. Sweetcatch is pricey, but it's good. Notable here is the marinated kale, it tastes so much better than the flavorless greens you get at other places. The fish itself is marinated too, and tastes great. I always experience mild sticker shock at the end though, regularly spending about $18 here. Those toppings add up.

Downtown Yummy (永泰海鲜酒楼; Yongtai Seafood Restaurant, possibly named for the county in Fujian Province, China) is a pretty decent alternative to the slightly more expensive Golden Unicorn, right across the street, for dim-sum. Golden Unicorn seems to have a wider variety of dim-sum, but the food at Downtown Yummy is almost, if not just as good; and the value at Downtown Yummy seems to be better.Food: Average to Better Than Average (3.5 of 5). For me, there are a couple of bellwethers for food quality at a dim sum restaurant: the rice noodle rolls and the shrimp dumplings. The Beef Rice Noodle Rolls (牛粉; Ngau Cheung) here are pretty good, with a better than average "smoothness" (the Cantonese term is "waat"; 滑) but the Shrimp Dumplings (蝦餃; Ha Gow) were meh, perhaps a limitation of the restaurant's inexpensive prices.Everything else we tried was pretty good -- including the Milk Custard Buns (奶黄包; Lai Wong Bao), Pork & Shrimp King Dumplings (燒賣王; Siu Mai Wong), Deep-Fried Sesame Seed Balls (煎堆; Jin Deui), etc. Downtown Yummy offers a few rarities for New York City dim sum restaurants. If you have a chance, do try the Goji Berry Osmanthus Jelly (杞子桂花糕; Gei Ji Gwai Fa Gou), a lightly-sweet traditional dessert, and the Crispy Fried Taro Shrimp Patties (炸芋蝦; Zha Wu Ha). Both are pretty good!As with another Yelper, I was surprised that Downtown Yummy does not offer chrysanthemum tea. Also, the chili oil, normally a great condiment for nearly any dish, is very weak here. Chili oil is available from the dim-sum cart that serves stewed beef offal (牛雜; Ngau Zaap). Service: Very Good (4 of 5). The wait staff are quick to remove empty dishes, and refill empty tea pots. Tea pots with hot water instead of tea are available upon request. You're free to take your dim-sum ticket and rove about to the dim-sum carts if they don't come quickly enough to your table. If it isn't too crowded, the dim-sum cart ladies may deliver your request to your table.Atmosphere: Good (3.5 of 5). The restaurant is brightly lit, and seating is comfortable. There are separate men's and women's bathrooms that are adequately maintained but are without ADA grab bars.Value: Great (5 of 5). Dim sum is priced per plate. We spent about $85 for 8 people; your experience may vary.

I tried to come here for dinner once before but was quoted over a 2 hour wait. Fast forward, a few years later, I came here again but this time for brunch and I was seated immediately. I guess the hype with the place went away over time.Maybe I waited too long to finally try this place, but I thought that all of the food was underwhelming. I tried the drunken deviled eggs, sweet tea brined fried chicken, cheddar waffles and the lavender lemonade. The presentation, plating and quickness was on point. However the food fell short of my expectations. The hint of lavender in the lemonade was very subtle. You can barely taste it in the drink. For the sweet brined fried chicken, I was able to request all dark meat with my order. It came with two thighs and two drumsticks. The drumsticks were not crispy at all. I peered into the kitchen and it looks like the fried chicken is pre-made and kept warm instead of being made to order. Also, the cheddar on the waffles didn't seem to go well with the meal. I ended up peeling off all the cheese. I am glad I was finally able to try this place but I probably won't return.

Come visit Nowon for a Korean American gastropub experience that will leave your taste buds reeling.Though their menu may be small, their dishes that feature interesting combos of ingredients you never would have guessed would work well together.Their honey butter tater tots are a great starter. You might expect tater tots to be overly greasy, but these were not. The crispy and soft tots garnished with bits of nori and sesame tasted even better when dipped into the garlic butter at the bottom of the plate.My friends and I also shared the Octopus Spam Fried Rice and the Chopped Cheese Rice Cakes. One small caveat is that it was so dark that it was hard to make out the ingredients within each dish. Maybe the lack of visual stimulation honed our taste buds even more and helped us appreciate the different flavors. The octopus fried rice had a unique flavor unlike any other Asian fried rice dish I've ever had, probably due to the blend of bone marrow butter, dill, and lemon juice. It's like a more buttery version of spam fried rice. I loved every dish we tried, but my favorite were the Chopped Cheese Rice Cakes. These dubboki were covered in a yummy cheesy sauce instead of the usual stringy melted cheese. The beef bits tasted amazing and the pickled japanenos add a nice kick for spice lovers.The prices here may be on the steeper side given the small portion size, but it was definitely worth it given the quality of the food and the unique style of the dishes. Your experience here will definitely be memorable

Upon a recent visit to Holi Mole, fueled by a burrito craving, I found the experience to be underwhelming. I ordered the Bistec/Ribeye burrito for $10.89, which turned out to be a hefty portion dominated by bland rice – roughly 75% of the filling – with a meager 5% of ribeye that didn't pack the flavorful punch I was hoping for.

While the eatery itself maintained a high level of cleanliness, which I appreciated, I questioned the value of their offerings, particularly after noticing that a side of guacamole cost an exorbitant $5. Disappointingly, the guacamole lacked the expected zing, especially since there were no jalapeños as some reviewers mentioned, only minced green scallions.

Giving Holi Mole another shot, I opted for a ribeye taco instead of a quesadilla on a following visit, influenced by the numerous taco images from other diners. Alongside, I ordered chips and guacamole for $6. The taco was just passable, and the chips were flavorless, making the price seem unjustified for the uninspiring taste and portion size.

I'm left curious about what Holi Mole is truly famous for, given that my experiences have not lived up to the hype.
Good, standard Thai. Delivery can be a while 50 minutes sometimes and I live very close. Even pickup I waited a while. Staff is very nice so it's okay.

This is a pretty spacious restaurant with a sizeable menu, so I'd recommend if you're in the area! For pho though, I'd vote for Saigon Shack or Pho Bar over Saigon Market, although this restaurant is much better for larger parties. There's a nice list of lunch specials on the back page of the menu book with several different options. The Pho Bo is what I usually gravitate towards, although the portion isn't that big... The Xao Bun is delicious if you like Pad Thai. The most recent time I went, I tried the Bun with a meat spring roll (rice vermicelli with veggies and Nuoc Cham sauce on the side). It was super filling and still tasted good as leftovers the next day!

Came here with a reservation via OpenTable (very easy to get) and was extremely happy! This is probably one of my top brunch spots in NYC, and in the LES.There is light everywhere. It is an open / rustic vibe with lots of windows / mason jars, etc. They also have a lot of longer tables, so it could be great for groups (especially a birthday party).I was pretty impressed with their vegetarian brunch options. Their eggplant benedict was amazing. I also highly, highly recommend their fries - they were perfect. Overall, would highly recommend for a cute-sy date brunch, catching up with a friend, or a large group.

Title: Rustic Charm with Room for Noodle Improvement

Upon entering this spot, the cleanliness and rustic decor immediately set a welcoming ambiance, despite the bustling crowd. With a price point of $11 per bowl, one must take into account the notorious Manhattan-inflation when dining here. The broth served is decent, marrying flavor with warmth, and the duck spring rolls are a noteworthy highlight, adding a nice crunch to the meal.

However, not everything hits the mark. Traditionalists may be disappointed by the absence of Dac Biet on the menu. The noodles, a cornerstone of any good bowl, were unfortunately a tad too firm for my liking. Additionally, the side veggies were scant, leaving one yearning for more freshness and texture with their meal. The meat options, while adequate, stuck to the basics, lacking the variety some patrons might be seeking.

In short, while there are areas ripe for improvement, particularly with the noodles and accompaniments, this restaurant offers a generally pleasant dining experience for those in the heart of Manhattan.

What a fun, new experience! This is a great place to eat solo - as in you literally don't have to talk to anyone or feel self-conscious. You get placed in an individual station, order with a little paper order form, slide it into the window, and receive your meal out of that same window. The broth here is also some of the best I've had.

Still traumatized by the fact that our order came 2 hours late because the delivery person ran away with our food but well, the restaurant was good enough to expedite making the order when they were informed the food went missing.Regarding the food, it's not bad for its taste but at the same time, nothing stands out. I ordered yangzhou fried rice and it was not too salty or greasy and the food is good portion and a good balance of veggies and meat. The egg drop soup looks kind of scary because I dont know what kind of coloring they used and the soup was like a bright orangy yellow. The taste is decent though.Overall not a bad choice for lunch.

Title: A Haven for Fresh Veggie Lovers in NYC

I recently stopped by this well-recommended eatery during a work trip in New York, and it certainly lived up to its reputation. The restaurant offers ample vegetarian choices – I'd rate the variety at a solid 4 out of 5. I had the opportunity to dig into their market plate and was impressed by how fresh and flavorful the vegetables were.

While I relished the fresh produce, the veggie hot dog didn't quite hit the mark for me. It seemed to be a standard frozen variety when I was hoping for something more akin to the creativity of house-made or Impossible "meat" alternatives. That said, it wasn't a letdown taste-wise.

Overall, the food quality was commendable. If you're ever in a rush, craving something wholesome, or trying to accommodate a range of preferences with friends, this spot is a reliable choice in the bustling city.

Title: A Pasta Lover's Delight

My dining experience at this restaurant was largely impressive, thanks in part to its beautiful ambiance and the attentive, friendly service that made us feel well-taken care of from the moment we stepped in.

The culinary journey started on a high note with a delightful olive oil paste accompanied by fresh, aromatic bread – an excellent precursor to the main event. The pasta offerings were the real showstoppers; the Busiate with Pesto was an aromatic twist on the classic, with almonds adding a wonderful crunch to the dish, and the Braised Oxtail Ragú left me savoring every bite of its rich, meaty goodness. The Seafood Lasagna Special proved to be another triumph, boasting perfectly cooked pasta layers and a generous portion that helped justify the prices, which are admittedly on the higher side.

However, not everything hit the mark. The Fritture appetizers were a letdown. The Funghetti, Polpette, and Melanzane were all victims of over-frying, resulting in greasy, flavorless bites that were heavy rather than indulgent. The meatballs, especially, were a sore point, being both diminutive and tough.

In conclusion, while I'd pass on the fried starters, the pastas alone are worth a visit to this restaurant. They showcase true culinary craft and are sure to delight any pasta enthusiast.

One of my favorite Chinese spots in the city! We came here for dinner through an easily made reservation. Our server, Jin, was friendly and attentive. He chatted amicably with us and provided wonderful service. We ordered three noodle bowls to share and the pork soup dumpling between the two of us. The noodles were hot and tasty, but definitely make sure you can handle your spice if you go with something spicy!Highly recommend this chic, clean, comfortable spot in Chelsea. The staff is so friendly and the food is amazing!

Came here on some last min plans with my friends. It was a party of 3 and the beautiful young lady in the front told us it will be a little wait. Along cane this young man who stepped in and got us seated right away to our surprise. He was just a burst of energy and so nice. This was my 1st at this location so the menu was different. Our waitress was so nice and patient with us because we were sure on what drinks to order. She gave us great recommendations and she also explained the oyster menu to us. And thanks to us we found an error on their menu lol. She called over the young man who helped get seated and we just laughed at the mistake. Every one of us enjoyed our drinks and food. My mussels were sooooo good (my mouth is watering just thinking about it lol ). I recommend this place to many ppl bc the food and drinks are amazing. We were sad we missed the happy hour ( they have the best margaritas )

I'm a frequent customer of Hao Noodle on West 4th  so I thought I'd try the Chelsea location with my friends. Upon entering, the vibe is more Japanese and French cuisine. Dark atmosphere with pinhole lights; the only bright and airy lighting coming from the tables in the back and the chefs that cook across from the high tables.For a table of 4 we reserved ahead of time and were promptly seated. Our first dish was a fried tofu appetizer. I normally don't eat fried tofu and thought it was going to be bland. The skin however  was fused with spices and the tofu was incredibly soft..! It was sooo good. I ordered the Chicken and Shiitake noodle for my main meal, a classic that I always get! It's delicious :)  we also ordered the lamb skewers but they weren't as tasty and are kinda dry. I wasn't able to try the dessert since it's made with soy but I've been told it's ok!Overall 4 stars because there's not much seating in this location and while the foods are good it's not something I'd come here for often! I only ever get their chicken and shiitake noodles since it's a classic but I wouldn't eat it everyday!

I recently dined at this local Indian restaurant and while the overall experience was satisfactory, it didn't quite hit the mark for memorable dining. The food and service were both competent, yet they failed to stand out from other Indian cuisine I've had in the past. The compact nature of the establishment, with closely-packed two-person tables, detracted from the intimacy one might seek in a dining experience. This became particularly noticeable around 7 PM when the place filled up, amplifying the noise level and further impacting the ambiance. For those considering a visit, I recommend securing a reservation to ensure seating, as the restaurant does get busy during peak hours.

Service was extremely amazing, the arepa and guacamole with a side of banana chips was off the hook as well. This place is interesting the only thing I didn't like was the crowd. It's not the type of people I like to be around. Last but not least they have pretty yummy margaritas.

This is by far one of my favorite restaurants in NY. Every time I visit the city, I have to go here as well as Joe's Pizza (which is walkable distance); yes, I go to both in one day ;).The beef short rib, beef shoulder, and garlic rib eye were all really tender and flavorful but my choice would be the garlic rib eye. I am a huge fan of garlic and the way that this meat was marinated, was a perfect pairing. Now, onto THE GO-TO DISH that I would have unlimited orders of if I could (afford it, tummy and wallet wise), is the Kobe beef/uni seaweed and perilla leaf wrap. This is just 100%; I cannot explain into words what this combination of flavor produces in your mouth, except that it is so enjoyable in every way possible and makes me utterly happy with every bite. Sadly, 1 order is only 4 pieces so when you share with someone (I do not know why I decided to do such a thing), you only get 2 pieces to yourself. . . * cries * They have a waitlist where you put down your phone # upon arrival and then they call you when your table is ready. See why I make a stop at Joe's in between? Our wait was a little over an hour but it was really worth it. I mean it! Restaurant is small and it gets smokey in there from all the grilling, but the restaurant staff is nice enough to store your coats for you in another smoke-free room. Ugh, I miss this place already and can't  wait to go back at my next visit to NYC!

Still have people going in at 10.45pm on a Sunday. This place is really delicious. They used to be a small hole in the wall restaurant and it used to be very dirty. This is a huge upgrade for them! The price is a little higher now and it averages 10 dollars per boodle bowl. They have delicious dumplings and very good hand pulled noodle soup and knife cut noodle soup. Definitely a great place when you have cravings for noods.

Title: A Delightful Find for Arabic Vegan/Vegetarian Cuisine

I stumbled upon this gem of a restaurant during a casual search for nearby food options and was intrigued by its unique Arabic vegan/vegetarian menu. The pictures and glowing reviews drew me in, and after a brief walk, I arrived with a growing appetite.

For falafel enthusiasts, the combination platter is a must-try according to the buzz. However, as someone who isn't keen on falafel, I opted for the cauliflower with tahini - a dish I had savored before. This restaurant did not disappoint; the flavors were spot on, and the dish was a delight. It's worth noting, especially for fellow falafel skeptics. The offering of falafel-free and onion-less dishes makes this a versatile spot for varied tastes.

Overall, I highly recommend the cauliflower with tahini. If you're in search of a healthy and flavorful dining experience, this restaurant is a standout choice.

I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant, and I was blown away by the culinary experience. The standout dishes for me were the soup dumplings, which were a delightful burst of flavor, the crispy pepper chicken that had just the right kick, and the scallion pancakes, which were the perfect balance of crispy and chewy. The use of Szechuan peppers added an exciting fizz to the palate, an effect that was delightfully enhanced by sipping on carbonated drinks. Overall, the meal was an unforgettable experience—one that I would rate 10/10 without hesitation. I am eagerly looking forward to my next visit.

Title: A Delightful Plan B at [Restaurant Name]

I'll admit my rookie mistake upfront—I missed out on the much-raved-about burger that's exclusively available at the bar. Nevertheless, my experience at [Restaurant Name] didn't suffer one bit. I pivoted to the steak au poivre, a dish that paid homage to the elusive burger with its peppercorn crust and decadent sauce - every bite was a revelation. My boyfriend's choice, the roast chicken, was equally impressive, especially with the creative twist of jambalaya risotto adding a punch of flavor.

We capped off our meal with the profiteroles, and oh, were they a triumph! The pairing of intense dark chocolate with the classic vanilla ice cream and delicate pastry was nothing short of perfection. Missed burgers aside, [Restaurant Name] certainly lived up to its glowing reputation. Highly recommended!

I recently dined at this establishment on a warm and windy evening, opting for the outdoor seating, which was delightful and deserving of a full five stars. Upon being seated, we were served bread and butter that was quite satisfying, meriting four stars. The French onion soup followed, teeming with cheese and rosemary, a pleasing combination that also earned four stars.

However, the meal took a turn with the mushroom and gruyere crepe. While the ingredients promise a gourmet experience, the excessive use of rosemary overwhelmed the dish, leading me to give it a middling three stars. Similarly, the risotto with chicken and green beans was a letdown. It lacked the creaminess one expects from a good risotto, feeling more like a hearty, chunky casserole, hence another three-star rating.

In summary, the restaurant boasts some strong points, particularly the ambiance and starters, but the main courses struggled to impress. It was a passable dining experience, though not compelling enough to warrant a return visit.

Super chill spot with some really cool employees. We got the "Chairman Bao" and it was a bit on the smaller side than I expected for $5.5. But it included a thick, fatty slice of pork belly slice that was flavorfully braised and cooked till soft. The peanut crusts was a really pleasant addition to the bun as it gave it a crunch as well as an additional layer of flavor. I do hope the bun part could be slightly bigger so the pork belly doesn't hang out too much, just so I can enjoy the bun and pork together in every bite.

If you're looking for cheap eats in NYC and don't mind eating in a place that looks like a basement of a church, Streecha is for you!Good:-  prices, in comparison to everything in the city, it's cheap!  $9/12 pierogies and they were DELICIOUS!  Soo pillowy soft and def not from the freezer aisle-  as per the above, food was DELICIOUSMeh:-  limited menu, only a handful of items-  plastic utensils, not the best for the planet-  limited hours of operation, closed Monday/Tuesday!  And it doesn't open lateStaff seemed pleasant.  I'd definitely go back!  Where are these "daily specials" as pictured??!!

Title: A Hotspot for Hotpot Lovers

If you're a fan of dry hotpot and find yourself in a prime location looking for a satisfying meal, this place is a gem. It boasts ample seating, making it a fantastic spot for groups - you won't struggle to find a table here.

The unique thing about this restaurant is the pricing structure: meat is charged by the pound, and veggies come by the basket - a clever invitation to veggie lovers to load up. For a duo, expect to spend a reasonable $30-$35, a fair price for the quality and quantity offered.

The variety of meat options is impressive, ensuring there's something for everyone. Plus, the ability to choose your own spice level means you can customize your pot to perfection. The ordering process is reminiscent of Chipotle's DIY style, but there's also a menu of set dishes for those who prefer a more straightforward choice.

Service here is a highlight; the wait staff are amiable and attentive, enhancing the overall dining experience. And the convenience doesn't stop there - you pay after you've enjoyed your meal, which adds to the relaxed atmosphere.

I've visited this dry pot haven multiple times and have yet to be disappointed. It's a resounding yes from me, and I will definitely be back for more.

A friend told me she heard good things about this spot, and now I see why! This is a great spot if you're craving noodles on a cold night or if you're just in the mood to share a few Chinese dishes. I love that they have a coat rack at the front--makes it so much nicer than having to crumple your coat next to you when you sit down. The ambience is also nice and cozy--there's not a ton of seating but there are seats at the bar which is nice, especially if you just want to come in for a solo meal. I ordered the Oxtail Beef Noodle Soup, and the noodles and broth were delicious!!! The portion size was great, and it came with a lot of oxtail bones. For dessert, we got lychee ice cream which was honestly so good I could've finished a pint in one sitting. I would love to come back and try some other shared dishes, but their other noodles looked good as well. Would recommend checking this place out!

Although I could not enjoy the spicy lemongrass soup I ordered so it's more like 2 stars for me because of how ridiculously spicy it was, I don't think it accurately reflects the overall rating of the store. My friend enjoyed her vermicelli bowl which was quite stuffed with the ingredients.I really can't handle spicy so when the waiter told me they could not decrease the spiciness of the soup and asked if I can handle spicy, I should have changed my mind on ordering it. But no, I blindly took it on as if any cell of my body can withstand what was to come next and I really wish someone would have slap some sense into me right at that moment. I even ordered a Large cause I thought it wouldn't be enough but boy, it was more than I could ever handle. I saw somebody order a small sizeof the pho and it's definitely enough for one so do not fret if you are a normal-appetite sized eater. I ended up only being able to finish about close to half of it because there was no way to avoid the spicy soup flavor. The sliced eye rounds were pretty good btw.If I was to come back, I know to definitely steer away from the SPICY Lemongrass soup.

Title: Stylish Locale, Sullied by Service

Perched atop Lincoln Center with a unique grassy rooftop, the restaurant sets the stage with its captivating locale. The elegance and modernity strike as you step inside, the stunning interior decor immediately demanding attention. Seated comfortably at a plush round table, the ambience promised an upscale dining experience.

Restaurant week lured us in, and we embraced the chance to sample the uova appetizer. It was pleasant, albeit lacking the wow factor one might expect from such a reputable establishment. The mains – salmon, carbonara, and chicken cutlet – were satisfactory; solid, but not spectacular, reinforcing the notion that the venue's acclaim perhaps rides on the back of its renowned name more than its culinary prowess.

Regrettably, the evening's letdown was our waiter's dismissive demeanor. His passive-aggressive tone, from questioning our understanding of food allergies to mocking our ordering process, chipped away at the experience. Etiquette and grace are expected at such an establishment, but his condescending approach felt uninviting and left us with a sour taste that no dish could mask.

Final Rating: 3/5 – While the setting and decor were impressive, the food did not live up to the hype, and the service severely lacked the refinement expected, overshadowing the more positive aspects of our visit.

Don't aspect a grand entrance. The interior is small and outdated, and will not review interior but the customer service and food. We mainly order take out from the establishment and normally have the lunch specials.  Their food always fresh and tasty.  For all the years our take out orders are good.  The food is tasty and pricing very well.  The customer service are friendly and courteous.

Came here for lunch with a group of three. We were seated immediately. We couldn't resist ordering Thai iced teas, which came incredibly quickly. The service was on point throughout our whole meal and I get the sense that the staff truly enjoy working there. Their smiles, their cheerful banter while working, and the snug nature of the restaurant will make you radiate good vibes. The food itself was pretty solid. I had the fried rice with lump crab meat. It was good but I felt like it could use a bit more flavor. It felt like it was missing something but I'm not sure what exactly. I liked the chicken satay a lot more than my entree, especially the coconut sauce. The other menu dishes sound enticing as well.

Review for 12/31/192nd stop for my birthday festivities.  Everything was great!  Our server was engaging and made convincing suggestions.Look how huge the Shrimp, how juicy the Libations, how thick those Macaroni noodles.  The author of the menu deserves props for making all dishes read as irresistible. We further enjoy the crowd and ambiance at the bar for a few more rounds.  The bartenders were an excitement to watch in action.We will be returning for sure!

I recently visited one of the chain’s outlets located a stone's throw away from the bustling tourist hotspots. The experience was a solid, middle-of-the-road affair. If you have a hankering for some fusion Vietnamese cuisine, this place offers an adequate selection that neither disappoints nor wows. Service followed suit: efficient but unmemorable.

The menu's greatest letdown was the Banh mi, served on bread that fell short of expectations—slightly dry and tough. It's evident that the prices here are a reflection of the restaurant’s prime locations rather than the quality of the food itself. My advice: If you’re tight on dining options or stomach space, it may be worth exploring other eateries in the area.

My husband and I came here for our 5 yr anniversary dinner (before hitting up a show a few blocks away). The location is ideal for people heading to a show. They knew we had a tight schedule for the show and tended to our needs very quickly. The wait staff was attentive and took our drink and food orders immediately after being seated. We ordered the oysters Rockefeller and the porterhouse for 2 (medium rare). The oysters were delicious. The steak (filet side) was delicious. Part of it was too rare for my husband so I ate it and it was absolutely buttery. The other part started off ok but then found that part of the steak was more medium than medium rare so I felt it was a bit more chewy than I would have liked. Since we hams a tight fit with the show we didn't bother saying anything.  The decor was very old school with the dark wood and dark lighting which was kind of cool. I think I would probably come back to try their key menu items and when we have more time to spend

The food was good overall but overpriced, even with a Yelp coupon. The snow buns are solid tho but nothing was amazing for the price. I feel like you're just paying for the nice decor that you're eating in which isn't what I want but for some it's what they want to pay for so make your choice

Stepping into this NYC eatery, you're immediately transported to the sun-soaked shores of California thanks to its surfer-themed decor. A welcome oasis in the urban jungle, the restaurant offers ample space, ensuring a table without the typical lunchtime rush. The blend of indoor and outdoor seating is a thoughtful touch, and the centrally located bar buzzes with activity, even in the afternoon.

The menu boasts coastal favorites, and my colleague's tortilla soup was a hit—both visually and on the taste buds. I indulged in a mix of tacos and the "Kaleifornia" salad. While the tacos were a flavorful journey, the salad, though generous with kale, fell a bit flat—salvaged only by a dash of hot sauce.

Service was attentive until an untimely bill presentation suggested an unnecessary rush—a small but significant misstep in hospitality. However, the overall experience remained positive. With a cool theme and solid food, this spot is worth a visit for those looking to catch a wave of California charm in the heart of New York City.

Really enjoyed this place. Cute ambiance, perfect for a date, and won't break the bank.The grilled haloumi was great and so was the sweet potato falafel (which didn't really taste like falafel). Only thing I would NOT recommend is the beet salad - the beet and horseradish were good, but the bitter radicchio really took over and ruined the salad.The sea bass was very nicely cooked and flavorful, but it is a whole fish and difficult to filet. Also it's a very large portion.Drinks were great, but wish they were stronger and also wish they had more manly type (bourbon based) drinks

I recently tried the shawarma bowl from a local restaurant via MealPal, and it was a delightful experience. Upon arrival, my order was promptly ready, showing excellent service. The bowl brimmed with flavorful chicken shawarma, perfectly cooked couscous, savory Spanish eggplant, fresh tomato, crisp cucumber, and crunchy red cabbage, all drizzled with a smooth tahini sauce. The side of warm pita bread and creamy hummus complemented the bowl well. The portion size was generous, leaving me satisfied and full. Overall, the meal was thoroughly enjoyable, and I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a hearty and tasty food option.

One of the better Italian restaurants I have been to in NYC. A gem of a restaurant located in Greenwich village. For dinner we ordered the Cozze in padella: mussels in a white wine, garlic, lemon broth, prosciutto di parma, fusilli e manzo - pasta with Parmesan cheese and braised beef. Everything had so much flavor - I was tempted to order seconds just to experience more. The service was fast and efficient as well. As soon as we were seated the waiters attended the tables and did not have us waiting to order drinks, appetizers or the entrees. Will definitely be back in the near future.

On the hunt for a bustling spot to enjoy tacos and margaritas, we landed at this restaurant after a Yelp find. We braved the Saturday night crowds and a significant wait, ending up seated by the entrance. The complimentary chips and salsa were a welcome starter, although the service was lackluster, with noticeable delays in attention and delivery. Our server's offer of extra chips—albeit reminiscent of refrigerated store-bought salsa—was a small consolation.

My choice of two chicken tacos and one steak taco was average. The tortillas lacked the fresh, homemade touch, and while the meat was tender, it could have used a more robust seasoning. However, the portions were hearty and filled us up. The margaritas struck a nice balance at $12 for a generous serving, not too potent and well-priced for the city.

In sum, this eatery is a solid choice when in the mood for a filling meal, though not a standout culinary adventure.

Title: A Delightful Lunch at Soba Totto

My wife and I had the pleasure of dining at Soba Totto for their lunch special and were thoroughly charmed by our experience. Arriving at 11:30 am on a Friday, we were the first to partake in the coveted offer available to the first 20 patrons. 

The meal commenced with a salad that boasted a satisfying crunch, a delectable dressing, and fresh, invigorating greens. This was followed by the star of the meal: hot soba noodles that were nothing short of amazing. But, the dish that truly captured my heart was the rice bowl. It featured impeccably cooked rice paired with the freshest salmon and tuna - an absolute delight.

As for customer service, it was exemplary. From the warm reception at the door to our informed and professional waitress who made our first visit unforgettable, every interaction was marked by friendliness and efficiency.

In summary, Soba Totto provided us with a STELLAR dining experience, and it's a place I would recommend to anyone in search of top-notch Japanese cuisine.

Really cool Asian restaurant. Inside there is a courtyard in the back with lots of plants. It feels very tropical inside. The food is soo good. They have great dim sum as well as other dishes. Everything is family style so I would recommend bringing lots of people to share all the dishes. Be warned though that if they say a dish is spicy, it's super spicy!! Make sure to get the tea as it really complements the meal.

Vino E Grano is located inside of the Eatly Complex which is located in Building 4 of the New World Trade Center.  Eatly had a number of dining areas and options.  Vino E Grano has a casual atmosphere and a wide selection of Italian dishes; pastas, pizza, meat plates.  Everything was very well prepared.  The pizza was a thick crust style and very tasty.  With beer and wine, it is a bit of an expensive lunch but overall recommended.

I recently visited this restaurant during restaurant week and found the fixed menu fairly satisfactory, especially since it included sides of broccoli and mashed potatoes. The Caesar salad starter was unremarkable yet acceptable. As for the main course, the petit filet mignon portion was reasonable; mine was cooked to a perfect medium, though my wife's was underdone, leaning towards rare, which she couldn't finish. Dessert was a bit disappointing – the carrot cake was merely a thin sliver, and the chocolate mousse was average, both unnecessarily accompanied by a dollop of whipped cream. The ambiance matched that of a typical nice steakhouse but lacked any distinctive flair. Overall, a decent experience but not particularly memorable.

Title: A True NYC Burger Haven on 2nd Ave

As a longtime New Yorker, I'm almost embarrassed to admit that I only recently discovered a burger joint on 2nd Ave that can only be described as a culinary revelation. The moment you step into this quintessential NYC establishment, you know you're in for a treat – a promise fulfilled by their spectacular burgers, generous portions, and heavenly milkshakes.

My choice was the bacon cheeseburger adorned with grilled onions, and let me tell you, it was nothing short of a masterpiece. Opting for medium over medium-rare was the move as it retained all the juiciness without sacrificing the burger's integrity. It's rare to find a place that truly lives up to the hype, but this spot exceeds it. These burgers aren't just good; they're mind-blowing. Do yourself a favor and make your next meal here – you won't regret it.

Title: Cozy Spot for Taiwanese Eats with Hits and Misses

Last Sunday night, my group of nine arrived at this quaint little restaurant, armed with a reservation. A slight hiccup occurred when we were initially asked to wait for everyone before being seated, but a compromise allowed us to order in advance for the absent members and settle down.

The beef noodle soup boasted a generous serving of noodles, albeit in a broth a tad too salty for my liking, but undeniably rich in flavor. The three cup chicken, however, was a letdown with its oversized chunks and scant sauce failing to deliver the anticipated punch. Similarly, the pineapple shrimp, recommended by our server, didn't justify its price tag with its lackluster taste and presentation.

The popcorn chicken, in contrast, was a revelation at 5/5 – the perfect blend of sweetness from honey and a satisfying crunch, elevated by aromatic basil. The oyster omelette was a nostalgic touch, reminiscent of Taipei night markets, though I wished for a more generous drizzle of the accompanying red sauce.

"Danza Mian" introduced me to an extremely savory broth unique to the dish, and the "la ba beng" with its luscious pork and well-seasoned bamboo rice didn't disappoint either. The Taiwanese sausage fried rice was a nostalgic delight, delivering that classic comfort food satisfaction. The "sausage party" won points for presentation and flavor but didn't quite make a lasting impression.

Unfortunately, the drunken clam was another miss, drowned in garlic with the clams playing second fiddle.

Despite a few forgettable dishes, the restaurant overall left a positive mark, especially with its offering of a Taiwanese breakfast – a detail that has already earned a spot in my future dining plans. It's a gem for Taiwanese cuisine enthusiasts, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Restaurant Review: Sorry Doe

Regrettably, I cannot endorse Sorry Doe after a recent visit that left much to be desired. My party of three entered with tempered expectations, only to find ourselves mired in a series of service missteps that began with a puzzling disregard for the "please wait to be seated" sign by other patrons, and was compounded by inattention from staff who seated and served others who arrived after us.

When it came to our meal, the truffle fries were disappointingly oily and inedible, ending up in the trash. The avocado toast was misleading, more salad than the expected item, though the toast itself was praised. Mozzarella sticks failed to deliver on both texture and flavor, arriving lukewarm and bland. The shining exception to our culinary mishaps were the nachos – a generous portion adorned with ground meat and a tasty addition of red peppers.

Our beverage experience offered some redemption; despite the spicy margarita lacking heat, it was enjoyable, and the pumpkin beer was a seasonal delight with its true pumpkin taste.

In summary, while the nachos and select beverages were commendable, the overall experience was tarnished by service issues and several disappointing dishes. Sorry Doe might be a bustling spot, but it failed to live up to our hopeful anticipations.

Title: A Tale of Two Visits at [Restaurant Name]

I approached my second visit to [Restaurant Name] with fond memories of an amazing brunch a year prior. Unfortunately, this experience fell short due to poor service. Our initial waiter displayed unprofessional behavior - he was noticeably irritated when we requested water and blatantly ignored us when we attempted to order. His brusque manner, particularly when we placed our entrée orders, left us feeling unwelcome.

Compelled by the waiter's rudeness, I spoke with the manager and we were assigned a new server, Delaney, whose patience and kindness salvaged our visit. Culinary-wise, the flatbread was the highlight, while the Mac and Cheese disappointed with its lack of creaminess and dry texture.

Desserts are the establishment's forte, though service issues persisted as only one of our multiple orders arrived. Despite the allure of the desserts, the overall experience was marred by the initial service. Price points are reasonable and reservation is advisable given the restaurant's popularity. Thanks to Delaney, the visit ended on a brighter note, but a consistent level of professional service is crucial for future visits.

Adorable little spot in the Greenwich area. For a Thai spot in the city, it's pretty affordable and standard in price. All the workers here are SUPER friendly and sweet. They make you feel right at home and work together to give you the best service. I had the pad see ew and no complaints! Flavorful and great portion.

What's better than having a place to sit down and munch on something after doing some shopping? I love the location because you're still in the department store, looking at all the beautiful things while eating. It's not the cleanest restaurant/café but the service was amazing! Our server was very patient and explained the menu to us, and surprisingly the cookie that we ordered was so good!

Title: A Delightful Encounter with Thai Flavors at Thailicious

I recently dined at Thailicious with an old friend and had a truly enjoyable experience. Upon my early arrival, the coziness of the restaurant was complemented by the warm reception from the staff. The friendly lady at the register not only seated me promptly but also took the time to address my queries about the menu.

Our meal started with the side of roti, which was a delightful beginning, thanks to its warm, flaky texture. The mango curry with tofu, a vegetarian option, was a standout dish, brimming with hearty tofu and veggies without being overly sweet. The highlight of the curry's versatility was its taste the following day, remaining just as tantalizing after a night in the fridge.

Although I personally couldn't indulge in the Pad Thai due to its fish sauce content, my friend was quite pleased with it. However, the limitation of not being able to customize the Pad Thai and Pad See Ew to be vegetarian-friendly led to a slight deduction in my overall rating, giving Thailicious 4 out of 5 stars for vegetarians, but a solid 5 for non-vegetarians.

Nevertheless, the flavors and hospitality have made a lasting impression. I am already looking forward to my next visit to Thailicious and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to friends, with a note to fellow vegetarians about the sauce inclusion in certain dishes.

Title: Underwhelming Experience Amidst Local Hype

I recently visited a much-talked-about restaurant with friends post a museum excursion, only to encounter a dampener, quite literally. The venue accepts cash only, which can be a bit of a snag if you're unprepared. Amidst the patter of rain, we were fortunate to quickly snag a table in the cramped quarters of this bustling eatery.

However, fortune was short-lived as our seating was compromised by a leaky roof. Droplets made their way into my ramen, prompting an abrupt seat change and a spoiled appetite. To compound the discomfort, what little I consumed led to an unsettling stomach experience that lingered for over a day.

Despite the local rave reviews, my visit was marred by the lackluster ambiance and a need for better customer service. A word to the wise: avoid peak hours to circumvent the inevitable lines, as the restaurant struggles to accommodate its popularity comfortably. My reluctance to return stems from a first impression that was less than stellar.

I enjoyed the ambience a lot more than the food quality. The restaurant has dim lightening and comfy seating.The food was overall decent but I don't know if I would come back. We ordered the sashimi deluxe, pan fried sea bass, fried oyster, uni , and fried ice cream.. overall 6/10

In the words of Chef Hugh, co-founder of Mighty Quinn's, "the brisket is what built the house, but the bronto rib is what broke the internet." Personally, I would recommend sticking to just the latter. The bronto rib was quite expensive although worth the high price point. It's a huge slab of meat, so you'll definitely end up leaving satisfied. The brisket, although fatty, was not very moist. I also got to try the sausage, which was likewise underwhelming.

High-quality XLB and dumpling soup. Okay xiao yang pan fried dumpling (生煎). I really like how bright and clean this place is and its convenient location right in the middle of Chelsea. I will definitely come back to try its lunch specials

Title: Cozy Evening at Jasmine Restaurant

Nestled just a few blocks from our hotel, Jasmine Restaurant was an inviting stop for soup dumplings on a surprisingly serene Saturday evening. The immediate seating and small bar, where we kicked things off with whisky and TsingTao beer, set a positive tone.

Our culinary adventure began with an unconventional choice – Steamed Gluten. While the spongy texture was unique, the combination of gluten cubes with fungus and peanuts turned out to be a delightful surprise. The highlight, of course, was the soup dumplings, brimming with a warm, savory broth that did not disappoint.

The Sticky Rice Shumai and steamed shrimp dumplings, however, fell into the realm of the ordinary, and the Tossed Noodle with Shrimp lacked the punch of flavor we craved. But the meal's charm was reinstated by the sweet bun dessert, whimsically shaped like a pig.

Service throughout was efficient and friendly, with the staff providing insightful recommendations in the restaurant's clean and snug setting. With its relaxing vibe and privacy between tables, the atmosphere allowed for an enjoyable dining experience.

In terms of value, we found the dim sum selection well-priced, contributing to one of the more economical dining experiences we've had in Manhattan.

Overall, Jasmine Restaurant served up a decent and speedy meal that was both affordable and enjoyable. While we barely scratched the surface of their extensive menu, the dumplings alone make a return visit enticing to explore their signature offerings.

I had a delightful experience at this restaurant, particularly with their avocado toast - a harmonious blend of flavors accompanied by perfectly cooked eggs. Service was notably swift, leaving me quite pleased with our decision to dine here. Highly recommended for a quick, tasty meal.

Tucked away in the tranquil streets of Alphabet City lies an unexpected culinary marvel that has rightfully earned a one Michelin star accolade for its novel twist on Chinese-American cuisine. This tapas-style establishment invites diners to indulge in a multitude of small plates, with 4-5 dishes providing a satisfying feast for a couple.

Kicking off the experience was an artful octopus appetizer, served with a theatrical pour of brown butter from an icing dispenser, an undeniable visual and gastronomic delight. The cauliflower with blue cheese miso, grapes, and herbs followed, delivering a surprising and delectable combination of flavors that awakened the palate with each bite.

The pièce de résistance, the "Pig Out" for two, was a generous main course accompanied by sumptuous garlic QQ noodles – a perfect companion to the candy-crusted fried pork. The accompanying arugula salad was a standout, adorned with a sweet lychee dressing, candied walnuts, and succulent lychees, elevating a simple salad to an exquisite level.

An unintended yet fortunate side order of sticky rice wrapped in banana leaves with Chinese sausage and duck fat was a decadent addition, rich and bursting with deep flavors.

This hidden gem is a must-visit for an exceptional dining experience. My anticipation to return is high, and I heartily recommend this spot to all seeking culinary innovation and satisfaction.

Title: A Delightful Surprise in the Heart of the City

Last Saturday, my quest for culinary adventure led me to an exceptional American food gem tucked away in the bustling streets of the city. From the moment we stepped in, our experience was nothing short of fantastic.

The food significantly exceeded our expectations. The meatballs and tuna tartar set an impressive stage with their rich flavors, while the main courses—the perfectly grilled chicken and succulent braised short ribs—were a testament to the kitchen's prowess.

Adding to the enjoyable meal was the exceptional service. Our waiter was the epitome of hospitality—welcoming and attentive without being intrusive. The ambiance of the restaurant struck a perfect balance, offering a cozy and down-to-earth atmosphere that made us feel right at home.

In short, this establishment is definitely one to visit for anyone looking for delicious American cuisine served with a side of warmth and comfort.

Title: Mixed Impressions at the New Buzzworthy Eatery

After bracing myself for the long waits I'd heard about, my Tuesday early evening visit to this new hotspot came as a pleasant surprise with only a thirty-minute wait. The staff's warmth set a welcoming tone early on. Despite a peculiar instruction to wait in an initially vacant downstairs bar, the confusion was soon sweetened by a complimentary drink and the upbeat ambiance.

The good: The bartenders exuded friendliness and expertise, picking up on my preference for non-sweet drinks. The music and overall feel of the place contributed to a pleasant experience. When it comes to food, I can't stop raving about their fries with a sumptuously savory duck breast gravy – a harmonious blend of bacon, egg, and 'magical' ingredients. Furthermore, their farmhouse beer is a must-try.

The disappointments: A major letdown was the restaurant's famous single cheeseburger, which was alarmingly over-salted to the point of detracting from its inherent flavors. An unfortunate hair incident also marred the experience (though, to be fair, it could have been my own). The rushed service, while friendly, led to an almost-empty plate of delicious fries being prematurely cleared, a small but notable detractor.

The chocolate martini for dessert was satisfactory but failed to impress. While the experience wasn't entirely negative, it wasn't compelling enough to warrant a dedicated return visit. Although I faced issues, especially with the burger's saltiness, I'd hesitate to dissuade others from trying this place out – you might just have better luck!

Overall Rating: 3/5 Stars

Poketeria is my favorite poke spot. Their portions are always great and they don't charge extra for toppings like other places (premium toppings, yes, but you can do unlimited regular toppings). Love that they do a punch card system.. once you have a fully punched card, you get a free bowl! Note you can only use punch card when you order in store, cant use it for pick up or delivery orders. Their fish is always fresh... I've never felt iffy about the fish here. love the seaweed salad and the mango and the premium topping of shiitake mushrooms. You can choose a base of zucchini noodles, white rice, brown rice, quinoa, or lettuce. Can mix and match also. I always do half tuna half salmon. Plenty of sauces to choose from also. They also have a water cooler with cups, sesame oil, and soy sauce, at the end when you leave if you'd like. This will continue to be my go-to spot.

Great restaurant.  Started with a refreshing glass of prosecco.  Then into the most delicious and fresh truffle pasta with shaved truffle upon ordering.  Also had the gnocchi with meat ragu and the lemon sole.  The fish was just ok a bit dry.  Nice complimentary zucchini.  Very original pistachio tartine for dessert, ask for chocolate ice cream on the side.  All pastas are housemade!

Title: Crusty Delight with a Veggie Twist

Venturing into the bustling culinary scene of NYC, my quest for exceptional banh mi led me to a quaint eatery that promises a crusty rendition of this Vietnamese classic. The highlight? Their baguettes have an unrivaled crunch that adds a delightful texture to each bite.

For the veggie lovers, rejoice! The banh mi here is generously packed with a verdant array of vegetables, offering a refreshing crunch in every bite. However, purists beware – the "classic" banh mi strays from tradition with a sparing smear of pate and a bolder emphasis on veggies.

While the delivery service is reliable in fulfilling orders, punctuality can be hit-or-miss. Expect your meal to arrive late on occasion, with a minor chance of significant delays.

Despite the unconventional take on the classic and the roulette of delivery times, this place is a must-visit for those craving a crusty, veggie-packed banh mi in the heart of New York City.

Title: A Charming Evening at Blue Ribbon

From the moment we stepped into Blue Ribbon, the service was impeccable. The staff was exceptionally attentive, ensuring even the smallest details were addressed, such as the proper orientation of the embossed plates. The waiter-to-table ratio was generous, ensuring prompt and precise service. Our waiter was the epitome of attentiveness, and the busboys performed their duties with a smooth grace, respectfully waiting until we had both finished our meals before clearing the table—a rarity and much appreciated.

Blue Ribbon's decor is best described as understated elegance. Despite the bustling crowd on a Sunday night, the ambiance remained tranquil, allowing for easy conversation. The lighting strategy, with its minimal electric fixtures complemented by the warm glow of real candles at each table, created an inviting and serene setting, ideal for a romantic dinner.

The culinary experience was outstanding. The Greek salads, bounteous and topped with exceptionally fresh Feta cheese, hinted at an almost farm-to-table freshness. The main courses, a succulent hanger steak and a flavorful salmon, seemed as though they were sourced straight from the ranch and the sea respectively, each dish cooked to sheer perfection.

In summary, Blue Ribbon is an exquisite addition to New York City's dining scene, ideal for those special occasions as evidenced by the thoughtful touch of complimentary champagne and warm wishes for our anniversary. It is a must-visit establishment where I look forward to dining again.

Interesting combination of the mix of Cuban and Chinese, but it works! We came here for a late lunch and got the Cubano sandwich and mushroom and broccoli lo mein noodles. Both were very flavorful. The Cubano was good, but I think my favorite was the noodles. I love the variety of mushrooms they used; it tasted so good with the broth. If you get these dishes, you should dip the sandwich into the noodle broth! I know Cubano's don't normally come with a dipping sauce, but it tasted really good! Overall good, would be interested in trying some of their items from the dinner menu.

When in NY you have to hit Los Tacos 1 on 43rd. It was packed at 3pm , but the line moved quickly. These taco builders moved like surgeons building some bomb tacos. I tried the carne and adobada aka al pastor. The carne was respectable and came with a guacamole salsa, salsa but the adobaba was so delicious coming with pineapple. I'm ready for 6 more. $3.75 a taco might be a bit on the high side but probably in line with NY prices. Delicious!My top 5 places to eat tacos for sure!

Title: Southern Comfort Meets Eastern Savory in NYC

From the moment we walked into this gem of a New York eatery, the warmth of the staff's southern-level hospitality was evident and unwavering. In a bustling city known for its brusque service, this restaurant stood out with its exceptional accommodation, displaying patience and thoughtfulness that felt reminiscent of my Houston roots. Our modest needs were met with grace, including the simple request for a high chair and a spacious seating arrangement.

The culinary experience matched the high bar set by the service. The lentils served were the epitome of creamy and tender, achieving a balance that rivaled some of the better establishments back in Texas. The naan bread, infused with garlic, struck a perfect chord between flavor and subtlety, while the samosas delivered the anticipated crisp and gentle heat. 

The tempura vegetables were an unexpected delight, masterfully combining a crispy exterior with a tender interior that burst with flavor. While the menu left me anticipating a broader array of fusion dishes, the offerings we sampled were satisfying and left little room for complaint.

In conclusion, for those seeking a dining experience where friendly service is as prioritized as a flavorful meal, this restaurant is a must-visit in New York City. Whether you're a local or a visitor longing for that touch of Southern hospitality, you're in for a flavorful treat that feels just like home.

Had a wonderful dinner here on a Saturday. This place was easy to book for a table on a Saturday night. The cocktails are amazing and the food was delicious. This was my first time trying Laotian food and I think it's very similar to thai food. The staff brought out the sticky rice as soon as we ordered food. That's like their equivalent of giving you bread in Italian restaurant. We ordered the papaya salad, the quail, and the crispy rice. I think the quail was by far my favorite. Then we split the salmon with green curry. Everything was very yummy!!

Cool neighborhood bar.  We were walking around looking for a place to grab lunch.   Saluggis was a block away and had good reviews.   We popped in to grab a bite.   Really enjoyed our visit here and would recommend this spot.  I had the Meatball Sub.   I can say that the portions are pretty huge.   I did finish it but struggled a bit.   The food was quality but just a tad dry.  I wish that they would have added a little more sauce.   Really liked the atmosphere of the bar.  Just a cool neighborhood place to hang out.  Service was good as they checked on us frequently.

This was an awesome bar that had happy hour all day on Monday which had great deals. The oyesters were $1.25 each and came in all shapes and sizes. If you could I would recommend making reservations  instead of walking in- my friends and I walked in and had to wait about an hour on a Monday for a table. Even all the bar stools were taken at the bar- we had to a stool as soon as someone left because there were so many people waiting. I would recommend getting the avacado and shrimp slider- tastes delicious! As well as the salmon tartar.

Title: Lovely Brunch Experience Post-Art Gazing

Following our visit to the Whitney, we ventured into a nearby establishment for Sunday brunch. Despite being a group of five, we were seated promptly, which allowed us to immediately soak in the establishment's dynamic vibe. The atmosphere buzzed with energetic conversations and music, although some might find it leans on the louder side.

The culinary journey began with a matzo ball soup that tasted authentically homemade—a comforting start to our meal. Sharing a grilled cheese with apple and caramelized onions proved to be an excellent choice; the flavors were paired to perfection. We capped off the meal with slices of banana and peanut butter pies—while both were delectable, the banana pie, with its harmonious crust-to-filling ratio, was the standout dessert for me.

The star of the show, however, was not just the food, but our waitress, Clare. Her stunning visage is truly remarkable—she's a gem that any cosmetics brand would be lucky to discover. Beyond her striking appearance, Clare provided attentive and delightful service, adding a personal touch to our enjoyable brunch experience.

Atlas Chinese restaurant is a refreshing addition to the dining options around Columbia University, contributing to the area's burgeoning reputation for quality Chinese cuisine. While my parents remain skeptical, primarily due to their aversion to the higher price point, I believe the food justifies the cost. 

The menu is an inspired blend of classic Chinese American selections alongside standout Szechuan dishes. Highlights included the fiery and crisp spicy chicken and the flavorful special eggplant, though the pork guobarou was unremarkable in comparison. 

Portion prices range from $15 to $20, which is reasonable given the quality. The service was efficient and the ambiance of the dining area was bright and inviting. While it may not surpass the authenticity of Chinatown or Flushing establishments, Atlas certainly holds its own—with a little imagination, you might just forget you're not there. A definite thumbs up from me.

This restaurant serves a very specific clientele that kind of makes sense with its exorbitant pricing of food and eccentric art decor on one side of the restaurant countered by the typical European construction in the rest of the establishment. Personally, my friends and I felt a bit out of place eating there, but anywho! On with the review.When I went with a group of 5 about 1.5 years ago, I remember the art was nice to look at while I waited to be seated. Once seated, I found that it was difficult to find something on the menu that wouldn't hurt my wallet and thus, settled on a $15 sandwich. Many others either went for sandwiches or Eggs Benedict for $19. One of my friends was allergic to gluten, so she just chose the market fruit.The sandwich was fine, honestly, but I kept thinking about I could've gotten the same thing in a cafe for nearly half the price (after tip and tax). Now, the bowl of market fruit was a complete JOKE. It consisted of literally several  blueberries and raspberries for $14 (plus tip and tax). One could put that together from Trader Joe's for literallY $3. One other friend also got a small pot of black coffee that was $6?? Let me tell you; I am willing to pay more if the dish is very high quality, unique or made with some level of difficulty and time, but these two things were not worth it at all.

This place looks small as you go in but as you walked down a semi long corridor with several seats, you can spot a whole new floor downstairs with lots of open space and more seating. We arrived on a Saturday night at 10:30 pm and the place was pretty packed but there were a few tables open, lucky us! It's not very lit inside but the food options make your stomach most certainly light up! I ordered the anticuchos with papa a la huancaina and chicha morada to drink. Normally Peruvian restaurants serve canchita to snack while you wait but they didn't have that here. The drink was a bit bitter but it was drinkable. The anticuchos were very tasty, juicy and cooked well. The papa a la huancaina had the best sauce, I just wished the potatoes were peeled but either way I ate everything and left nothing on my plate. The waiter was very nice and brought some hot green sauce (my favorite!) but didn't come often to check if we needed water. I guess he may have been busy but next time, I hope the waiter I get is a little more attentive, given the fact I love hot sauce and my tongue will love some cold water to get the feeling back. One con I did see was that the prices were raised by $2.00 on certain things. Lucky me, my dishes were more than what the menu stated. Hope they fix it by my next visit!

Title: Takoyaki Letdown at a Laid-Back Local Spot

I ventured into a well-rated takoyaki joint, lured in by a tantalizing 4.5-star Yelp score, only to find that stars may be deceiving. The ambiance is certainly casual and ideal for lounging with pals, though the bathroom's size might leave you chuckling - it's minuscule!

Staff were pleasant enough, albeit the chef appeared a tad too eager to serve up the takoyaki, possibly due to the 15-minute wait that preceded the cooking. Unfortunately, it seemed that haste made (undercooked) waste. The balls of octopus were too soft, collapsing at the slightest touch. Flavor-wise, they were passable, drenched in sauce but lacking any noteworthy zest.

Despite the rave reviews online, my experience was underwhelming. It crossed my mind that I might've hit an off day, or should try other menu items, yet the first impression was soggy enough to dampen any return visits.

Sapori D'Italia may appear touristy, but it is not. It's an authentic Italian restaurant and store in the heart of Little Italy steps from Chinatown. The space is small, but they have tables inside and outside maximizing the space. The service is on point and the food even more so. I am not much of a red sauce guy so I ordered the spaghetti aglio and it was perfect. It tastes light but flavorful. Some of the best pasta I've had. Their wine list is also stellar!

Out of this world Thai food in the lower east side. The pad kee mao was some of the best I've ever had, not too oily or spicy, perfect flavors. Also the crispy duck and Khao Soi are must try indeed!!!

Pretty solid but nothing extraordinary. Enjoyed the Peking duck and snow pea shoots. My date loved the crab tofu but I personally thought it was just okay - the grainy crab bits in the sauce were a bit off putting to me.

Tucked away on the Upper East Side lies a culinary treasure that has long been my sanctuary for comfort food, especially for a steaming bowl of pho on those chilly days when nothing but soup will do. Their spicy pho, customized with rice noodles upon request, never fails to delight with its bold flavors and soothing warmth.

The vermicelli noodle pork chops are a standout, arguably amongst the best I've encountered stateside. Perfectly marinated meat that's tender without being chewy, paired with vermicelli, creates a symphony of sweet, savory, and subtly citrus flavors that dance on the palate.

No visit is complete without indulging in the summer rolls and shrimp satay appetizers, both of which are consistently impressive. I've returned countless times and will continue to do so. This gem truly stands out for its exceptional dishes that hit the spot every time.

Coming here feels like you are being transported to a bistro in Paris. It has a bistro-esque decor with windows all around that I assume open in the summer time.  It has a modern feel with all the fixings of a good lunch spot. The waiter was very helpful always checking on us to make sure we were ok. This is a higher price point for the area so I wanted to see if the price met the quality. The burger jumped out at me because if I see a burger on the menu I usually have to try. This one had a lot of funky ingredients to it. It was hard to eat since it was messy. All the condiments that come on it sort of overpower the burger. It is not bad and the meat tasted fresh but it did not eat well. The fries that come with it were decent. They are thicker fries and they were seasoned well. I am more of a thin frie guy but I won't hold that against them. My friend got the butternut squash agnolli. It is a smaller portion than I would expect for the price but she said it was good. Another positive here is that they had good wifi. I love places that have good wifi and they didn't rush us out. We enjoyed our meal and did some work on top of that. I am torn between 3 or 4 stars here. You can see they put effort into making the restaurant top notch but I don't know if it hit the mark food wise. It wouldn't be my first recommendation in this area but if you need some lunch give it a try.

Finally visited the place which I repeatedly bookmarked on Yelp. We came to Maison Pickle for dinner but I have heard their breakfast is great! We also got the balcony seats from where, we could see the entire dining area and bar! More than the ambience I was in love with the food! A must visit for all those who want quality and quantity (the portions are huge!)We got the Pull-apart bread & butter for appetizer (a must order!), Chicken Parm(huge dish with 3-4 fried chicken breasts) and the Classique Mac & Cheese which was super cheesy and generous size! Highly recommend this place!

Title: A Fiery Find - Great for Groups and Pets Allowed!

My recent visit to this vibrant spot was nothing short of delightful. The cocktail star of the night was the 'Inferno', a dangerously delicious concoction that had us all on our toes! The tacos on the menu were decent, with a special shoutout to the fish taco, though they didn't stand out from the usual fare you'd find elsewhere.

The main dish I chose was the short rib, which was tender and cooked nicely, but could have used an extra pinch of seasoning to bring out its full potential. However, the accompanying potatoes were a hit – perfectly executed. Another dish that packed a punch was the spicy shrimp enchilada, which I would highly recommend to those who enjoy a spicy edge to their meal.

Hosting our group of 12 was a breeze in their spacious back room area, and they could've easily accommodated a couple more. The service was notably exceptional – swift, flexible, and delivered with genuine smiles – a rare gem in NYC. Plus, this place gets extra kudos for being pet-friendly! I'd definitely suggest it for anyone looking to dine out with a large party (furry friends included).

Solid 5 all across the board.  This is my new favorite place for a quick bite.  This place gets all the high marks.  Friendly staff.  You can sample anything if you ask.  The ingredients are the highest quality.  The presentation of the food is fantastic.  The space itself is beautiful.  They sell organic wines and beer, however, the beer is not on draft but in a can which I wasn't  crazy about.  The place looks like a cafe in Paris but has a pharmacy theme with servers wearing lab coats.  Their slogan is "Let the food be the medicine" and the word "menu" is replaced with "prescriptions"My wife and I split the 3 bowls for $30 to share where you can select any 3 entrees.  Others in my party opted for doing the soup and half entree portion of the pasta which was a generous serving of both.  The soup, which we sampled and loved was a butternut squash soup with pistachio nuts.  The three bowls we tried were the spicy chili, vegetable tajine, and Tibetan mama.  All were out of this world good bursting with flavors.Oh and it's all plant based and organic so you get a delicious healthy meal.  We were scratching our heads as to why there weren't a lot of people eating there because this place is phenomenal!  I can't wait to go back!

Title: Middle-of-the-Road Dining Experience at Local Eatery

My recent visit to this restaurant, prompted by a cousin's invitation, was a study in mediocrity. Greeted by prompt seating at 7 pm, we hoped for a meal that would match the efficiency of our welcome. Unfortunately, expectations started to falter with the appetizers. The Bruschetta was forgettable: a mere three pieces lacking any unique flair. The Beef Carpaccio followed suit, skimping on flavor and leaving much to be desired.

Our main course comprised a shared trio of dishes. The Gnocchi with Vodka sauce emerged as the night's winner, with a sauce that undoubtedly stole the show. The Truffle Pappardelle with Sausage and Mushroom was a competent dish, elevated slightly by the smoky notes of the sausage. Regrettably, the Homemade Ravioli failed to leave any impression, unanimously deemed unworthy of a mention.

The evening's finale was a petite green tea tiramisu, whose saving grace was its lightness and balanced sweetness. However, its size was underwhelming, better suited for an individual than to share.

Service was erratic; the staff seemed undertrained, contributing to a feeling of disarray. Our small table was constantly cluttered, as our waitresses seldom cleared finished plates to make room for new ones. The restaurant's atmosphere teetered on the edge of cozy and uncomfortable, the space needing a breath of fresh air—literally.

Reflecting on the experience, there's little to lure me back. With a plethora of dining options available, it's unlikely I'll choose to return to a place that settles for "good enough" rather than striving for exceptional.

Title: A Night to Remember at a Woodland Culinary Retreat

From the moment I secured a last-minute reservation at this exceptional restaurant, I knew I was in for a treat. Upon entering, the dining room welcomed me with its lodge-like charm, complete with high ceilings, exposed wood beams, and tasteful art. The layout was spacious, boasting an open kitchen view that added to the immersive experience.

The bar, though quiet during my visit, felt inviting, distinctly separate from the dining area yet equally elegant. The staff's enthusiasm and excellence in service shone through, making the evening even more enjoyable.

The culinary journey began with Bretzels, an intriguing hybrid of breadsticks and pretzels. Their Tarte flambee, laden with bacon, onion, and creme fraiche, was a savory delight, hinting at even larger versions available at the bar.

Next came the Foie Gras terrine, a dish I typically avoid, but here, it was transformed. Accompanied by the sweetness of jack fruit and mango purée, along with a delightful crunch of nuts, it was a pleasant surprise.
