The highlight for my palate, however, was the Citrus cured tuna, bursting with bright flavors complemented by wasabi tobiko’s subtle heat and texture. The accompanying caviar on cornbread paled slightly in comparison but was enjoyable nonetheless.

Hearty yet balanced, the Trout on a cedar plank alongside the inventive corn gaspacho proved cozy and complex, a testament to well-executed comfort cuisine.

While the Japanese black fish with red pepper emulsion was good, it was overshadowed by the previous fish dish's success. Still, the emulsion indeed added a lovely depth of flavor.

The Braised rabbit fleischnacka presented a whimsical take on pasta, and the Porklette's crispy skin was simply ‘wowza,’ although I could have skipped the accompanying cut fruit.

Approaching my limit, the selection of cheeses maintained the high standard, but it was the two-bite, pre-dessert plum that was the embodiment of light, refreshing satisfaction.

Concluding with an intricate chocolate creation featuring passion fruit and hazelnut nuances, and a delightful like frappe, I was thoroughly impressed.

I left this establishment full, not just of expertly crafted food, but of joy and the anticipation of recommending this gem to friends and family. The experience was a parade of culinary hits, a must-visit for anyone looking to celebrate a special occasion or simply indulge in a remarkable dining experience.

In a city full of high spots, low spots, dive bars, gourmet restaurants, comfort food, French poodle food, grease trucks, and everything in between, it's usually clear what we're getting into when my husband and I go out to eat. As NYC food veterans, I wouldn't consider us snobs so much as particular in our understanding of what to expect. The level of preparation and price points so dictates how good we expect the service and meal to be. It's a sliding scale. Having a burrito from a taco truck in Spanish Harlem will not get the same scrutiny as etouffee in the Village. That said, we were totally unprepared for this restaurant. *** you can skip to the bottom of this review if you want the executive brief.***Located downtown in an amalgamation of restaurants, bars, and historic landmarks, this one is easy to miss. There's the downstairs which is exquisitely decorated with a blend of modern & trendy with old fashioned "high society" sprinkled on top. There's an upstairs which is taken to the next level (figuratively and literally) with scenic Hell's Kitchen as the background to your meal. Oddly enough they seem to operate as two separate restaurants. The menu is detailed with just the right mix of variety and specialty so you don't get analysis paralysis flipping through diner-sized menus. Our server (who really doubles as a concierge) Jessica was knowledgeable on the drink menu, funny, and attentive. The describing food is always difficult because you can't properly communicate a taste in the way that captures the breathtaking melody of flavors so I'll leave it at this: Very rarely do you find a restaurant that does everything well from the welcome to the exit. This is one of them. The ambiance, the music, the service, the drinks, the 8 items we ordered in total were all incredible. This is an experience that we will go back for seconds (pun intended). As a fan of food or someone interested in a special date, this is the crown jewel of downtown Manhattan. ***Executive Summary**** Environment: Excellent* Service: Outstanding (Jessica is the one to seem)* Food: Singularly Amazing * Expensive: Yes       - Worth it? : Every Penny. * Verdict: A special experience you won't forget.

Came here randomly after moving into the neighborhood. The owner was super friendly and great with the recommendations. We ordered the mac and cheese, the cumin cauliflower, oxtail stew, meatloaf, and bread pudding. We shared everything and they were all pretty on point. The only thing I would comment on is that the meatloaf was a bit dry and it's what's really keeping this from a 5 star review. The mac was great and I definitely recommend it. Again, the staff is great here so it'll definitely be of my neighborhood go to's as I start to settle in. Happy to be part of your neighborhood.

I recently visited a local restaurant renowned for its pierogis and was thoroughly impressed. The highlight was the option to mix and match, so I sampled 2 meat, 2 cheese, 2 potato, and 2 sauerkraut pierogis. The meat and cheese varieties stood out as my favorites, boasting savory flavors that satisfied my palate. Additionally, the service was commendable - quick, friendly, and attentive. A delightful dining experience that I would recommend to any pierogi enthusiast!

I found myself at the Gem Saloon on a Tuesday night to catch up with a friend I hadn't seen for a while. I usually don't trek to the east side for a variety of reasons (distance from my west side apartment being the main one) but I'm actually happy to have gotten the chance to discover this spot.Located on the corner of 27th and 3rd the Gem Saloon is a quick three block walk from the 6 train on 28th. When I arrived at the spot I was surprised to see how big it actually was. They have a main bar space in the middle with booths, as well as s separate area for dining directly behind the bar. At 6 on a Tuesday it was pretty dead but as the night progressed it got more and more busy. Regardless, this space is so big you definitely shouldn't have trouble finding space to sit.Their happy hour specials are what convinced my friend and I to try this spot out. They had half off their entire beer selection from 4 to 8 PM. I stuck with their Goose Island IPA ($7) while my friend ordered a few mixed drinks. We also got a plate of their classic nachos ($14) to share. A nice portion with a generous amount of toppings!The service here was also on point. From the moment we sat down we were given menus and were able to ask any questions we had about items they served. All the bartenders were extremely hospitable and efficient. I 100% recommend this spot if you're looking for a cozy place to grab drinks after work or to catch up with a friend on the east side of the city.

Title: Tamarind – Elevating the Indian Dining Experience in NYC

My latest culinary adventure took me to Tamarind, a restaurant that claims to be the "Finest Indian Restaurant in NYC," and in many ways, they lived up to the title. The ambiance of the restaurant is immediately noteworthy, as its meticulously curated interior, from elegant furniture to gleaming tableware, sets the stage for a fine dining experience.

The starter, a complimentary Amuse-Bouche of a savory potato patty atop a spicy mint chutney, hinted at the innovative flavors to come. Throughout the meal, the service remained impeccable, with staff consistently attentive, readily topping up curries, a rarity in many Indian restaurants.

The menu offered a fusion of traditional and unique flavors. On the flavor front, while Tamarind does stand out in the American Indian culinary scene, it slightly missed the mark in comparison to the homely, intricate balance of spices I grew up with. The complexity of flavors was there, but lacked the precise harmony of traditional recipes. That said, the cocktails served were a delightful complement to the meal.

A minor letdown was the somewhat unwelcoming reception by the front house staff during our visit for a more casual Saturday lunch. Despite our less formal attire, my group was there for the experience and our bill reflected our enthusiasm for the offerings.

In conclusion, Tamarind offers a discernably refined dining experience with an Indian twist that deserves recognition. The service overshadows minor hiccups in welcoming and flavor authenticity. I'm intrigued enough by the quality and presentation to return, particularly to try a Prix Fixe menu that might showcase the best of Tamarind's culinary prowess.

Manhattan and the Midtown area is quite devoid of good authentic Sichuan restaurants. I am so glad to have found this spot just a few blocks from Times Square! Came here on a Wednesday dinner at 7pm with a reservation for eight friends, we were given a table upstairs for our group. We ordered the following (definitely missing a few since we feasted like Queens and Kings of old): chili beef tendons 夫妻肺片，cucumbers salad (黃瓜） as our appetizers. For main, we got Chongqing spciy chicken (重慶辣子雞），Chongqing grilled fish （重慶烤魚）， chongqing hotpot beef (重慶火鍋牛）， Lamb with cumin (孜然羊）， shrimp with egg yolk, Mapo tofu （麻婆豆腐），Stir fried snow peas (蒜蓉豆苗）Disclaimer: we were invited by the owner for a summer invitational tasting event, so the meal was gratis.AMBIANCE:I love the ambiance here. It's not going to be your go to fancy restaurant, but you know it be popping when on a Wednesday night the entire floor is packed with patrons!  Casual spot to hang out, bring friends, and enjoy a hearty Sichuan meal. PROS:Portion sizes are quite massive here. Come here with an empty stomach!Let's start with favorites. Cumin lamb and the salty egg yolk shrimp were BOMB. Cumin lamb was fresh, seasoned aggressively, and that cumin taste you can never go wrong with it. The numbing effect that cumin and peppercorns can have go really well with the lamb, and it was stir fried with a bunch of onions and peppers which were flavorful and aromatic! The salted egg yolk shrimp was DELICIOUS. I love the egg yolk crust on the shrimp as it adds a new depth of flavor, and the shrimp wasn't too greasy.  Next favorites would be the hot pot beef. I didn't expect it to have a tomato broth in it, but boy was that flavorful. It comes in this ridiculous looking chinese porcelain bowl that according to the owner, was once served to the emperors during the Qing dynasty (not the actual bowl, but a replica). Boy did we feel like royalty when that dish came out. The sliced beef works really well in the broth, and loved the addition of tomatoes in it to really bring out the flavors in it. Chongqing spicy chicken was great as well. Reminded me of a cooler version of a Kung Pao Chicken, albeit less saucy and definitely more spicy. Think hipster and a turnt up fiery version of KP chicken.Shanghai Dou Miao was perfect - love the balance of the garlic in it, flavors were on point, and it wasn't too greasy. So was the cucumber salad and the beef tendons in chili oil. Last dish was the Chongqing grilled fish. REALLY cool concept! What they do is they first fry a massive whole tilapia, then grill it, and then douse it with their Chongqing style sauce/broth. At first I was concerned that it was going to be oily, but it turned out to be just right! Flavors were on point, the fish was fresh, and the fish was massive and seasoned really well. Level of heat was good, although personally I would love to see the option of customizing how spicy you want the dish to be so that I can maximize the amount of chili's in it. Overall, great dish, and I can see why its such a seller here!MISC:Service was great, and our waiters were really friendly and attentive. Lisa, who manages the restaurant, was super friendly and we ended up talking more about the history of the restaurant, what directions that their team wanted to take the restaurants, and some cool experimental dishes that they're rolling out soon. Definitely was really inspiring to meet such a hardworking and entrepreneurial person! Looking forward to see where she takes the restaurant in the future!OVERALL:Sign me up as a regular here, because I'm sold that this spot is good for legit Sichuan food!

Title: Brunch with Hits and Misses

I recently visited this establishment for brunch and was pleasantly greeted with no wait time. The overall experience was satisfactory, earning a modest 3.5 stars.

Service was commendable, with attentive and friendly staff. The fresh orange juice offered a refreshing kick, albeit a tad too sour for my liking. A standout was the Hangover Hash; the fennel sausage mingled delectably with the hash, making for a delicious combination. Sadly, the poached eggs paired with it were a letdown, cooked to an unfortunate hard yolk.

The Steak and Eggs entree delivered a robust smokiness, which was a bit overpowering, causing me to cough. Once again, the poached eggs missed the mark with overdone yolks. On the side, the bacon was competently prepared, yet it also leaned heavily into smokiness, which isn't my preference.

In summary, while the service and certain elements like the hash shone brightly, the kitchen's heavy-handed approach to smoky flavors and the consistent mishap with overcooked poached eggs left room for improvement.

Tucked away next to Union St. in NYC, this cozy Ramen spot is a delightful find. We indulged in their Tonkotsu Ramen, a savory miso garlic base with pork bone, alongside the Spicy Miso Ramen - an ox bone and bone marrow broth concoction with a spicy kick, balanced by the freshness of bean sprouts and roasted corn. Each sip of the broth was a plunge into deep, rich flavors that satisfy.

The service was efficient, ensuring a pleasant dining experience without unwanted waiting. Portion sizes are generous, leaving diners satiated. The inclusion of pork, chicken, and vegetarian broth options shows a thoughtful consideration for varying dietary preferences.

Price-wise, it's a fair deal for the heart of NYC. One small hiccup - my order was missing the extra egg I paid for, likely a simple oversight. Despite this, if you're in the Union Square vicinity, this place is a must-visit for an authentic and flavorful ramen fix.

I won't make this review too long. All you need to know is that Atomix is worth all of the hype, praise, and accolades that it received ever since opening. Yes, it's a bit frustrating how difficult it is to get a reservation, but it's all worth it in the end.Every dish is meticulously thought out and executed flawlessly. It's definitely a modern, fusion take on Korean food but the meal absolutely pays a lot of respect to Korean cooking technique and flavors. And unlike some other high end restaurants I've been to, they are not afraid to be very flavor forward.The tasting menu is heavily seafood focused. Some highlights for me: Sugar snap peas and caviar over blue fin tuna, Langoustine, and Wagyu with truffles (as a supplement). But honestly, there were no misses at all.Service was top notch. Attentive without feeling claustrophobic. All questions were thoughtfully answered. The somm was fantastic and recommended some incredible wines to pair with our meal as we did not do pairings. I also appreciated nice touches like being able to choose your own chopsticks and having each course come with a menu card describing the origin/concept of the dish. They of course save each one and wrap it for you to take home with you.They change menus every season, and you bet that I'll be there every time!

Let's start with the good. The sweet potato falafel on a pita was delicious. The sauce, the falafel, the salad IN it. Good to the last bite. I would totally grab one to go in the future. That's it. Tried a few things here with my sister who accompanied me. We were greatly disappointed. Hummus. Ordered it with sweet potato falafel in it and sweet potato fries on the side (which I paid an extra dollar to be seasoned.) The hummus was not the worst my sister had ever had, but she couldn't actually think of WHEN she had a worst one. She couldn't even finish it. The sweet potato fries were tasteless. I think I paid $1 extra for them to sprinkle sparingly some parmesan cheese on the top. Maybe 1 teaspoon. It didn't help and wasn't worth the $1. The hummus WAS saved by the sweet potato falafels that were in it.My sweet potato falafel pita came with a side of potato chips and I ordered a side of cauliflower. The potato chips were stale and the cauliflower was over cooked BUT well seasoned. So I'm putting it in the win column. All in all, not worth the price or the time in Union Square where there are so many other places you can grab a bite at various price points.

Upon spotting an intriguing photo, curiosity led me to try this local eatery. I opted for the lunch combo, featuring a nutty buddy wrap and a sunny side up roll. The wrap, though tasty, suffered from a monotonous texture that lacked a satisfying crunch. Meanwhile, the sunny side up roll was commendably innovative, though it fell short of its potential. The rice, deviating from the expected sushi standard, was disappointingly sticky. On a brighter note, the butternut squash and tomato were delightful. However, the braised fennel's tough texture was jarring, clashing with the other components of the dish. Overall, while there are flashes of creativity, the restaurant has ample room for refinement in texture and balance.

I really enjoyed the experience at this establishment. Although there was a wait at 5pm, it flew by. We had some great drinks at the bar and time fled by without a notice.The service was polite and on point. The bathrooms, though, were very crammed (and this is a guy complaining about it; I cannot begin to imagine the lady's room).The food was decent, though not spectacular. We had just gone on in from the first part of the Harry Potter play, so I had wanted to come here afterwards since I had been to this place many years before and loved it! I still enjoyed it, though it did feel... old. Still, they're like a well oiled engine; runs without a snag. Nevertheless, I kind of hoped that they had kept up with the times and improved on the "feel;" yet I don't quite feel like I'm at a classy restaurant. Maybe it's the volume..., I don't know.All the same, if you are in a pinch, this place will kick butt. The taste is there and so is the service.

I'm amazed at this place called Raoul's. I've never had such an amazing, tasty  burger before. Let's just talk a little about how exclusive this burger is. First off if you are not going on the weekend you'll have to fight the crowd to order it and each day they only make 12, yes 12 burgers. But a good tip is that if you want to make a reservation and secure your spot for brunch, you'll be able to order it during the weekend. It was my first time coming to this place and my friend that lives in New York made a reservation for us to have it during brunch for her birthday. We ordered one burger and also a quiche because this is a French restaurant and we wanted to split everything. The overall burger was super tasty and the fries were cooked well too! The quiche has a side of salad and that made it seem pretty healthy to us and the dressing was nice and light. Full of flavors and goodness we totally enjoyed the experience and I'm so glad that we ordered "the burger". If you ever have a chance don't miss out on this because it truly is a pretty good burger.

Title: Pasta Perfection at Aunt Jakes

My love for pasta drew me to Aunt Jakes, and it certainly did not disappoint. They've mastered the art of combining homemade pastas and sauces, offering a delightful mix-and-match experience. I indulged in the rich, creamy goodness of cavatelli with garlic cream sauce, which was an absolute hit. Each order also comes with a couple of bread slices, but don't miss out on requesting the garlic bread—it's a must.

Portions are generous, almost guaranteeing leftovers for later enjoyment. Service was a highlight too, with our waiter providing attentive and friendly care throughout the meal. While I stuck with water, I noticed they offer a creative 'make your own cocktail' option that added a lively twist to the dining experience.

Aunt Jakes also boasts a super cute interior, enhancing the overall ambiance. It’s a good, fun spot for pasta lovers and anyone looking for an enjoyable meal out.

Golden Unicorn has become a frequent stop for me in Chinatown, particularly commendable for its dim sum offerings. Despite its popularity, I've been pleasantly surprised to never wait over 30 minutes to be seated. A remarkable aspect of this eatery is their consistent availability of a wide array of dishes, even late into the afternoon.

My top picks include the succulent shrimp balls, the delicate har gao, flavorful pork ribs, and the delightful shrimp paired with walnuts and broccoli. However, I'd recommend skipping the siu mai, as it doesn't quite meet the standard set by the rest of their menu.

For any dim sum lover in NYC, Golden Unicorn is unabatedly a must-visit spot. My friends visiting from out of town have been unanimous in their enjoyment, ensuring its place on my recommended list for a true taste of Chinatown's offerings.

During my recent visit to Avra, I found the culinary experience to be quite delightful. Admittedly, it's on the pricier side, but the quality of the dishes justifies the expense. For those looking to dine here, I highly recommend going for the classic options. The Rack of Lamb was cooked to perfection, the Greek Salad was remarkably fresh, and the swordfish was truly memorable. Additionally, the AVRA chips should not be missed; they were a standout for me.

On the flip side, I found the Grilled Octopus rather lackluster, and the Grilled Tuna fell short of expectations – neither dish made a strong impression, so I wouldn't order them again. However, if you concentrate on their foundational offerings, Avra is sure to leave you content with your dining choice.

Brasserie Saint Marc is a delightful addition to the East Village dining scene, offering a French culinary experience that ranges from good to excellent. My companion and I visited on a Saturday evening and found the service to be outstanding and the atmosphere romantically inviting.

We started with the Charred Octopus, which was a generous serving of tender, chargrilled tentacles over fresh greens and soft baby potatoes — a notable highlight. The Beef Tartare, albeit lacking the typical bright red appearance, was unexpectedly pleasant with its rich flavors complemented by onions, capers, and cornichons.

The Escargot de Bourgogne, sans shells, were delicate and savory, with the garlic and parsley butter providing a perfect accompaniment for the accompanying crispy baguette. The Coq au Vin impressed with its succulent, wine-braised chicken, while the Steak Au Poivre was a standout with its perfectly cooked medium-rare Angus strip and indulgent creamy pepper sauce.

Our choice of beverages, a Chenin Blanc Vouvray and Goose Island beer, were well-matched with our meal, particularly the crisp and slightly sweet wine. Desserts were a delightful end to our meal, with the Creme Brulee presenting a textbook example of a sublime crust, and the less visually appealing Poached Pear proving to be deliciously honeyed.

I'm eager to revisit Brasserie Saint Marc for the charred octopus, escargots, steak, poached pear, and to savor that Chenin Blanc once again. This charming spot is a welcome addition for anyone seeking a touch of French flair in their dining repertoire.

Can anyone say pretty in pink? Located in a basement setting, this cute restaurant is fit for a cute date, or celebration! We came to celebrate our one year wedding anniversary and were treated so well. Their pastas are freshly made and they have several creative, festive drinks! The food was 3 to 3.5 stars, but the service and cute insta-worthy photo ops bump it up to a 4 star restaurant!

Place is still great. Delicious wings, great ambiance, friendly staff and cheap beer. My only complaint is that they've been playing a lot of hip hop and similar music and this isn't the Down the Hatch essence. We want 80s, 90s, Bon Jovis and all those fun songs please?

Title: Hidden Gem Serving Mind-Blowing Eats

In my multiple visits over the past two months, this unassuming hole-in-the-wall restaurant has consistently impressed me with its culinary prowess. The chili dumplings are nothing short of phenomenal, bursting with flavor at each bite. And the beef noodles? They absolutely blow my mind with their rich and savory depth. Every dish here seems to unleash an adventure for your taste buds, making each visit an exciting experience. Despite its inconspicuous facade, this place truly throws down when it comes to delicious food. Eagerly anticipating my 4th visit, I can wholeheartedly recommend this spot to any flavor chaser out there!

I finally decided to try the Chinese restaurant I often walk past, opting for beef and broccoli with white rice to take back to the office. Initially, the generous portion seemed promising - it looked decent and had a tempting aroma. However, my experience took a disturbing turn when I discovered a small worm in my meal, which was thoroughly off-putting. This incident indicated a concerning lack of cleanliness in their vegetable preparation. Regrettably, what I had hoped might become my new favorite takeout spot is now a place I'll never visit again.

The restaurant location was also known as Raise New York which might cause a little confusion when you tried to search online. We wanted to grab a quick bite before movie at the nearby Kips Bay AMC. It was a rainy Thursday evening so it wasn't packed when we got there. The restaurant has many flat TVs and mostly high tables. Unfortunately there were no hooks on the walls for umbrellas and bags so we had to put our stuff on the floor. Not biggie but it would be nice if they would install some. Food was absolutely amazing! The chipotle chicken wrap was very tasty and the tots were very crunchy.  I had the house base burger which was good too and the fries were hard to resist. Service was quick and staff was friendly. Would definitely come back again when we are in the area.
Had a togo order. Personally love the Pieorgi in Sweet Potato stuffing. Stuffed Cabbage at $17 just feel too overpriced, also was just fine for me.

I recently revisited Pinto at their new location, moving on from their Christopher Street roots. The upgrade is noticeable, boasting more space and an inviting outdoor patio perfect for al fresco dining. On a Wednesday afternoon, the place was unexpectedly quiet, lending an air of private dining to my lunch experience.

Opting for something light, I chose their Chicken Wings, priced at $10, alongside a $14 glass of wine. The wings arrived - nine in total - perfectly crisp, bathed in a delightful balance of sweet and spicy Thai sauce. Though small, they were tender and satisfying, complementing the generous serving of wine.

Service was swift, no doubt aided by the lack of other patrons. I left Pinto considering a future visit to explore their lunch specials, as the quality and value have certainly whet my appetite for more.

Title: Healthy Joe's - A Delightful Keto-Friendly Surprise

I visited Healthy Joe's today and had the pleasure of trying their Keto Bowl with an added portion of chicken. I must say, the bowl was a fantastic alternative to my usual Chipotle pick, especially with my current goal of shedding a few pounds. The blend of cauliflower rice, tender broccoli, a perfectly cooked egg, ripe avocado, and a single slice of bacon for a touch of smokiness, provided a satisfying and flavorful meal. Although I did enhance it with my own Frank's Hot Sauce, the natural flavors truly impressed me.

On a separate note, I took advantage of an offer received via email (a nice marketing touch using the previous Muscle Maker Grill's mailing list) and got myself a free Buffalo Schroom sandwich with my drink purchase. A mishap with the iced tea spilling in the bag did lead to a soggy bread experience, but the sandwich fillings were undeniably tasty. The side of oven crisped broccoli deserves a shoutout for its excellence, and the peach iced tea, partly enjoyed, was refreshingly good. Also, the ice from their ice maker reminded me fondly of Sonic's.

Overall, Healthy Joe's has made a great impression and is a welcome addition to our neighborhood, offering wholesome and delightful dining options.

My boyfriend and I had a remarkable dining experience at this restaurant during Valentine's Day. To mark our made-up anniversary, we opted for a fancy dinner, and the venue didn't disappoint. Upon seating, I was pleasantly surprised with a rose, setting a romantic tone for the evening. I started with a house Cabernet that was delightful.

For our meal, we indulged in a shrimp appetizer and savored the rich flavors of the lobster bisque soup. The highlight was the steak for two, which was absolutely amazing - cooked to perfection and bursting with flavor. The server deserves a special mention for their attentiveness and friendliness, enhancing our dining experience.

The interior decor of the restaurant complemented the upscale vibe perfectly. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone craving a good steak and a touch of elegance.

Tucked away in the bustling streets of New York City is a gem of consistency and reliability known as Lui's Thai Restaurant. Their charming BYOB policy is the cherry on top of an already delightful dining experience. A visit to Lui's isn't complete without kicking things off with their zesty papaya salad. Following this fresh start, diving into their savory curries and mouthwatering noodle dishes always hits the spot. Lui's steadfastly delivers on flavor and satisfaction, never failing to impress.

You know that good feeling you get when a place lives up to your expectations?  Well that summarizes my experience with Claudette.Who hasn't wanted to dine here over the years.  Lovely outdoor seating on 5th Avenue.  Charming interior and a cozy French bar if that's what you prefer.   Today, even though it was overcast and chilly, I wanted to maintain my persona of a hard core NY'er and decided to sit outside.I opted for the lunch Prix fix at $28 and it included Pumpkin falafel that was amazing and included some hot peppers and raspberry preserves. The flavors came together nicely.The chicken BLT included a small slice of avocado on a small french baguette.  Small side of fries.  Together to two plates filled me for lunch, and I was very satisfied.  Service was excellent.   I'd love to make lunch here a monthly event.  Maybe try it for brunch someday soon.

Title: A Feast of Korean Delights

My experience at the restaurant was truly excellent. Our party of four dived into a delightful variety of dishes, from the tangy kimchi & banchan to the sizzling half and half fried chicken. We also savored the spicy rice cake, the luxurious wagyu beef, the refreshing cold noodles in beef broth, the robust fresh noodles in black bean sauce, and the indulgent kimchi fried rice.

The standout dishes for us were the spicy rice cakes, the garlic fried chicken, the succulent wagyu beef, and the flavorful noodles smothered in black bean sauce—each a definite highlight and worthy of a future re-order. While we might have over-ordered, the variety allowed us to explore an array of tastes and textures.

Although I have a slight preference for Her Name Is Han and Kawi based on my recent Korean dining experiences, this restaurant easily stands out as a strong contender in its own right. I would gladly return for another round of their delectable offerings.

Title: The Perfect Nacho Fix at Happy Hour

I've been a loyal patron of this local gem for quite some time, mainly enticed by their enticing happy hour offerings that run from 4 to 8 pm. The menu shines with a variety of drinks, but let's talk about the star of the show: the nachos. At only $10 during happy hour, these are a must-try, especially with a hearty recommendation from my supervisor. While you can add meat for an extra charge, they stand out on their own.

Don't miss the Roasted BBQ cauliflower, which has recently been revamped with a healthier, saucier flair while retaining its deliciousness. Conveniently located next to my workplace, this spot has become my go-to whenever the nacho cravings hit. With great food and a fantastic happy hour, it's definitely worth a visit.

I think my favorite thing about Community is the ambience. Everyone is talking and laughing and the staff are so friendly and upbeat that it's no wonder why people always want to come here for brunch on the weekends. Today, I got the truffled egg? It was a fried egg on a bed of sautéed greens, mushrooms and bacon with a truffle sauce. Tasty, but a bit heavy. Also got the hibiscus flavored soda. Yum! Tried my I was here around noon on a Friday for lunch and got seated within 10 minutes. I've been here once before for brunch on a Sunday and we waited almost 40 minutes so plan wisely.

I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant and it exceeded my expectations on all fronts. The drinks were perfectly mixed, refreshing and complemented the meal wonderfully. Service was top-notch; attentive and courteous, making the dining experience smooth and enjoyable.

Now, let's talk about the pizza - it was a culinary delight with a perfectly crisp crust, delicious sauce, and high-quality toppings. Not to be overshadowed, the rest of the food was equally tantalizing, with an evident attention to flavor and presentation.

Adding to the charm was the breathtaking view that this restaurant offered, providing the perfect backdrop for a memorable meal.

While the prices were on the higher side, the quality of the food, service, and overall experience made it worth every penny. My visit here was thoroughly enjoyable, and I'm already looking forward to going back.

Title: A Calzone to Remember at Loring

I recently visited Loring, a gem I discovered on "The Best Thing I Ever Ate," eager to try their famed Calzone. Despite the Saturday night bustle around 9 PM, I ordered ahead and smoothly picked up my meal at the bar.

Loring's Calzone is truly a masterpiece, setting the bar for inventive takes on Italian classics. Stuffed with a divine blend of ricotta, mozzarella, and sausage, the Calzone is wrapped with a Spicy Soppresata that's having its well-deserved moment in the culinary spotlight. The result? A harmonious balance of flavors that elevate this dish to the top of my list. It's not only the most unique Calzone I've ever savored but quite possibly the best.

Beyond the food, Loring boasts an inviting atmosphere that calls for a dine-in experience. I'll be back, next time to enjoy the ambiance as much as the cuisine.

These people take their avocado toast seriously.But truly, though. I'm pretty sure there was more avocado than toast, which was delicious, but not ultimately the light breakfast I'd been aiming for. This isn't a complaint, simply a surprise, since I know the darn things have been going up in price lately and plenty of restaurants cut corners a little bit. The coffee was solid, the salad that went with my avocado toast was well-dressed and actually in bite-sized pieces [so many people miss that mark] and my friend's meal was good enough she refused to share, so there's that.The staff is also very sweet and the bartender, oddly enough, turned out to be a local from -our- hometown transplanted to New York, so there was a lot of chatter and reminiscing before we headed out again.

We went on Saturday 12pm and we were part of the 5 people in that seating, so service was very attentive. We were a few minutes late to the reservation but it was chill because given the number of people, we had one chef dedicated to serving us delicious, fresh pieces of nigiri at well-timed intervals. We never felt rushed at all nor did we feel like we had to wait long for each piece. Everything is so fresh, tender, and flavorful, as each piece is served with no garnishments (for the original flavor) or with garnishments (to enhance the flavor). Even sea urchin and oysters, which I generally don't like when I order in a typical restaurant, are amazing! Since this place is still relatively new, you can do BYOB, so we got a nice bottle of sake. They gave us sake cups to pour into that is prefrozen, which is a very nice gesture. Also, since this place is relatively new, I'm not surprised if this place is going to be popular really fast because of the price to quality ratio of this place! 17 piece omakase after tax and tip is like $150 which is a really good deal especially in New York.

We visited the restaurant with high hopes, but unfortunately, it fell short of expectations. The prices didn't match the modest portion sizes, leaving us feeling the value just wasn't there. Service could have been warmer; the staff came across as distant and not particularly welcoming. Space was at a premium, making the dining experience a bit cramped. While the food was flavorful, it erred on the side of being overly spicy, which was a challenge for those with milder palates. Additionally, vegan options were sparse, which was a notable downside for those seeking plant-based meals. Although bread is usually a staple at a table, here, we had to request it, which was a minor inconvenience. On the plus side, we were seated swiftly upon arrival, and the ambiance did carry a certain posh charm. In sum, our experience was just okay – not terrible, but not outstanding either.

Treadwell is fantastic, and we're so lucky to have it in our neighborhood. A true gem on the upper east side, they've got a bunch of activities like ping pong, board games and pinball machines. Beer selection is top notch, and the menu is constantly changing. Service is great, and they've got TVs all over the place showing obscure sporting events. You can't go wrong with any entree, and the portions are large. For a fun casual vibe, you won't go wrong with Treadwell!

I recently had the pleasure of brunching at a high-end Greek restaurant that surpassed my expectations. The culinary excellence was undeniable, presenting an array of delectable flavors that transported my taste buds to the Mediterranean. The ambiance of the establishment only enhanced the experience, its stunning decor eliciting the sensation of a European escape. To top it off, the service was commendable, attentive and warm. Highly recommend for anyone looking to indulge in a sophisticated brunch affair. Kudos to the team! - @traveleen_gurl

Very cool spot with a relaxed vibe. We visited this place for a much needed "cool off" beer during a hot afternoon. For the most part, the place was pretty empty aside from a few tourists. We stopped in around 4:30 pm, so maybe most of the clientele were still working. The beer selection seemed pretty vast; there was a bit of something for everyone. My lemon weisse sour ale did not disappoint, but the bar ran out of it. :( That said, the bartender did have a few nice recommendations. The bar has a general happy hour deal - if you purchase a 20 oz beer, then you'll be charged for a 16 oz. The two bartenders seemed pretty nice and laid back. I do not if I would visit the place unless I was in the neighborhood, but it was a great random find for us.

Super authentic!!! It currently has 15 locations. I can see this concept grow to easily over 100 locations. Liang Pi is amazing and their spicy cumin lamb noodles is hot and savory. Look forward to meeting the owner soon to talk about expansion plans!!

Pretty average ramen and sushi place. Got the spicy ajisen ramen and the sexy girl sushi. Ramen broth was super bland. All I could taste was how spicy it was. No depth of flavor. The soup didn't attach to any of the noodles, so the noodles just tasted plain. I do have to warn y'all: the spicy ajisen is SPICY.  The sushi was very ordinary. Not much flavor at all. Wasn't bad though. Wasn't great. It was $12 for each dish. Waiters/waitresses never refilled my water. Probably should've just gotten the ramen.Overall, wouldn't recommend because there are better ramen places in NY that are around similar prices. However, this place is cheaper than most ramen places for having $12/bowl as many ramen places are around $16/bowl.

Title: Misleading Advertising Overshadows Potential

I recently visited a restaurant that caught my eye with its appealing lunch menu poster. Despite the allure, I was greeted with disappointment as the experience was marred by misleading advertisement.

We walked in at 2pm, enticed by both the lunch and brunch menus displayed at the entrance. To our surprise, the restaurant was eerily empty. When we inquired about the lunch options, the waitress informed us that the advertised menu was only available on weekdays—a detail conveniently omitted from the outdoor signage.

Pointing out the discrepancy, we hoped for the restaurant to honor the posted deal, considering we were the only patrons at that time. Regrettably, our request was declined. Faced with higher prices for the same dishes, we felt compelled to leave.

It's disheartening to see a business fail to accommodate or adapt, especially during slow hours. My advice to the restaurant: align your advertising with your actual offerings or be flexible enough to honor posted deals for the few customers who do come in, or at the very least, clearly state the days when special menus are available. Honesty in advertising is the cornerstone of customer trust and satisfaction.

Rating: ★☆☆☆☆

Title: Cozy KTown Gem for Late Night Bites

I recently ventured into KTown for a late-night meal and stumbled upon this wonderful spot. Opting for the Beef Bulgogi and Soondubu combo special, I was delighted by the generous portions and how it hit the spot, providing the perfect comfort to stave off the NYC chill. We also shared rice cakes and Korean pancakes, both of which were tantalizing additions to our table.

The prices are incredibly reasonable, especially considering the prime KTown location. Service was a standout, with attentive and pleasant staff enhancing the dining experience. The restaurant's ambiance is relaxed and low key, making it an ideal setting for unwinding after a long day.

I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant for anyone craving satisfying late-night eats or seeking respite from the cold with some hearty Korean fare.

Went to lunch here on New Years Day with friends. Seating was quick and the place was festive and lively. A beautiful Christmas tree was centered in the middle of the space, which was a nice touch. Our waitress was friendly and our food arrived quickly.Chinese Salad - ordered without chicken, but the salad was still outstanding! The salad wasn't overcrowded with too many ingredients or dressing and it was crunchy, healthy and light My only gripe would be the pricing on my salad and other items on the menu seemed a bit steep considering there weren't many vegetables included in my salad. However, the ambiance and food was great, and I can definitely see myself returning!

My visit to this restaurant on Thanksgiving for hot pot was a mixed experience. The wait time of 30 minutes was manageable, but I found the seating arrangement unusual as we shared a large table with another couple. The ambiance was quite disconcerting—white walls doubling as projector screens displayed graphics that were almost blindingly invasive, coupled with loud dance music reminiscent of a nightclub rather than a dining venue.

As for the meal, the hot pot was as expected— it's hard to go wrong with such a dish, so there were no issues on the taste front. However, it's worth mentioning that this establishment does not offer an all-you-can-eat option and charges are per item. In summary, while the food met expectations, the overall dining experience left something to be desired due to the disorienting atmosphere.

Title: A Fusion Feast at NYC's Cajun-Chinese Gem

If you're craving the zesty kick of Cajun coupled with an innovative Chinese twist, this spot in NYC is a culinary adventure you won't want to miss. Our group of ten spontaneously popped in on a busy Wednesday night at 7 PM, and the accommodating staff swiftly merged tables to seat us comfortably. While calling ahead is advisable for large parties, the restaurant's fresh decor and welcoming ambiance made for an immediate thumbs-up.

We indulged in the $99 group sharing combo, perfect for a trio, which offered a generous starter and a hearty seafood boil bag. The standout popcorn chicken, a delightfully crispy treat bursting with flavor, was a universal hit. Adding to the feast was an array of seafood boil flavors, ranging from the classic Cajun to the daringly spicy "Flaming Ghost Street," reminiscent of Beijing's famed heat—a nostalgic nod for someone hailing from the city.

While the potato chunks in the boil were tad underdone and the provided cracking tools a bit inefficient, the bounty of crab, crawfish, and sausage more than made up for these minor hiccups. For the adventurous, the salted egg yolk Dungeness crab is a must-try—a decadent dish unfamiliar to American palates. Other notable mentions include the spicy crawfish over rice, akin to a piquant take on jambalaya, and the soothing sour fish soup, which provides a tangy relief from the spice frenzy.

Service was attentive, with the staff going the extra mile to ensure our comfort with bibs and gloves for an immersive, hands-on dining experience. Though prices are on the higher side, the restaurant justifies it with ample portions ideal for sharing. Located conveniently in Chinatown, it's an excellent choice for a cozy yet fiery meal on a cold winter's night. Highly recommended for those seeking to explore an intriguing blend of Cajun and Chinese flavors in a convivial group setting.

Actually wildly impressed with my experience at MSG's rehabed restaurant under the new name The Grill Room (formerly Club Bar & Grill). I was invited to a soft opening lunch to try their new & improved menu that featured perfect steak house options. The ambience & decor are very alluring, quite a classy and pleasant vibe to the place with a great soundtrack. Onto the food... as a party of 4 we got to try a few apps, entrees & sides. The allstar of the apps was the slab pecan crusted bacon -- really incredibly cooked with that gorgeous crust. The fried artichokes were delicious and didn't taste super heavy for a fried food. Every entree that hit our table was beautiful, from seared scallops (4 in an entree), to the steaks, to my winner of an entree, presentation was spot on. Scallops were cooked perfectly. Steaks come with your choice of housemade sauces (that were delish. the one with gorgonzola was amazing). My entree was the short rib and it was as massive as it was absolutely delicious. The perfect amount of fat to meat ratio, amazing sauce, crispy edges, no like literally I mean this was a perfect entree. Oh and it was bigger than my head. Alllll in all, I highly recommend this spot for a family dinner, business meal & date night it can really be any occasion warranting a delicious meal

Another week, another ginger stir fry type dish. Laut Singapura is a brand new restaurant in Flatiron and it exceeded all expectations. From our first step inside we were blown away by the details put into every inch of this place. The walls, decor, chairs, tables, even gold forks were something to ogle. We were a group of about 8 that got there around 11:30 and had no trouble all getting a table together. They have a pretty big menu and a very decently sized lunch special section. Although a little confusingly arranged, we managed. I ended up getting the Ginger Scallion with mixed seafood (you have a choice between chicken, veggies and tofu, shrimp, mixed seafood or beef). The mixed seafood was shrimp and squid and, what I later learned were fish balls. All delicious and the ginger sauce was perfect. The lunch specials all came with two little spring rolls, miso soup and a side salad. The spring rolls were crunch and delicious, the soup was a perfect little starter to get warmed up, but I didn't love the salad. It was still a nice starter, but I personally wasn't a big fan of the peanut dressing. But to each their own! It also came with a big heap of jasmine rice. It was a generous serving of food, especially since I wasn't expecting any of the soup/salad/spring rolls. They also did not skimp even a little with the seafood, and all for $18, it was well worth it. Before going, I did a little searching around on Yelp and saw photos of the Iced Malaysian White Coffee and was super curious. I couldn't resist not getting a glass. It was the perfect balance of coffee and milk, not too heavy at all, like a Thai iced tea can be (I still love Thai iced tea). I definitely recommend a glass. Infact, I recommend this entire place. Go for the lunch special!

Title: Unassuming Excellence with a BYOB Twist at Local Omakase Gem

Last evening's omakase experience at this understated sushi haven was nothing short of remarkable. Despite a presentation that leans more towards simplicity than sophistication, each piece of sushi was an explosion of authentic flavors, with the quality of the fish taking center stage - a welcome deviation from the sauce-heavy creations often encountered elsewhere.

Every bite was crafted with meticulous care, fully satisfying my palate without exception. The ability to pair the meal with a bottle of our preferred sake, thanks to their BYOB policy, only amplified the pleasure.

A glance at the menu on the wall reveals an array of exotic options beyond the typical omakase fare, tempting patrons with unique selections not found in your average sushi joint. 

The two-store layout of the restaurant can fill up quickly, especially around the sushi bar. To enhance your experience, securing a corner seat upon reservation would be a strategic move. 

In summary, this establishment delivers an omakase that is as delicious as it is authentic, enriched by the cozy charm of a BYOB setup.

Title: A Long-Awaited Brunch Paradise

After years of anticipation, my husband and I finally visited this gem for a Saturday brunch, and it did not disappoint. Our appetizer of oysters was phenomenal, setting the bar high for the mains. My avocado toast with eggs was a blissful encounter; the toast was the ideal crunch, and the fresh avocado paired with a flawlessly poached egg was a delight. Meanwhile, my husband was won over by the crispy chicken sandwich, which he devoured with approval. The Pumpkin beer we opted for was the perfect accompaniment to our meal, encapsulating the essence of brunch. Coupled with the attentive service, our experience was second to none. Rest assured, we'll be returning before long – this time, much sooner.

I frequent this place and you cant beat their happy hour prices in the area. They have great margaritas and appetizers. The service at the bar is better than the tables. The guacamole is terrific and made to order, you can choose from mild to spicy.

I recently visited this restaurant for brunch and was left underwhelmed. Despite an early arrival at 11am, avoiding a wait for a table, the service was excruciatingly slow, likely due to the growing crowd by 12:30 pm. Opting out of the acai bowl after a discouraging review, I chose the pulled chicken bowl. Priced at a steep $18, the dish was merely average and certainly not reflective of its dinner-entree cost. The cramped space further diminished the experience, making it less than ideal for group outings or relaxed chats. My final bill came to $27 after adding a coffee, which felt excessively expensive. Overall, this place didn't live up to expectations.

Title: A Reliable UWS Spot for Group Dining

I recently dined at this neighborhood staple on the Upper West Side, where we met up with friends, both kids and adults. It's wise to book ahead, as this place tends to fill up quickly—no surprise given its years of popularity in the area.

The menu is quite versatile, with options ranging from sushi to burgers to fish. While the food was good, it wasn't remarkable, but it does the job for a diverse group. We were seated by the windows, which accommodated our gathering comfortably.

This restaurant seems to be one of those places people stumble upon and end up liking a lot. Personally, I'm partial to eateries with a bit more flair, so while I appreciate the spot, I'm not totally enamored by it. In short, it's a solid choice, especially for groups, but don't expect culinary fireworks.

Title: Mixed Impressions at Vendome Bistro – A Birthday Dining Experience

My initial hesitation about Vendome Bistro, chosen for a birthday celebration, was partly quelled by a stranger's high praise before we entered the elegant two-floored venue. The dinner menu hadn't sparked excitement, but I found solace in ordering the scallop risotto at $32. It was a delectable dish rivaling my favorite from Upstate, with fresh, perfectly seared scallops, though the risotto bordered on too salty. 

A companion's fish soup, priced at $15, was a misstep; its overpowering fishiness was off-putting, and a little ginger could have balanced it out. On the brighter side, the fries ($8) avoided mediocrity and were quite enjoyable. Meanwhile, the additional side salad accompanying the mussels was a letdown, overpriced at $8 for a disappointingly meager portion that offered nothing special.

Desserts redeemed the culinary roller coaster. Their apple tart, served with a scoop of ice cream, converted me despite my usual ambivalence towards apple desserts. The profiteroles were irresistible, the perfect blend of cream puffs, ice cream, and chocolate sauce. The thoughtful touch of a birthday candle in the apple tart by our waitress was a sweet gesture.

In summary, Vendome Bistro offers an elegant backdrop for special occasions with a hit-or-miss dining experience that shines in select dishes, particularly at dessert.

After much anticipation, I finally visited this Indian restaurant renowned for its healthy, daily fixed menu—a concept perfect for my indecisive nature and love for Indian, vegan, and vegetarian cuisine. Despite the considerable distance from home, my excitement was unmatched, and rightfully so.

Upon arrival, the service was impeccable; a friendly lady quickly seated us and provided the day's options—brown or white rice—making the decision easy as I have a penchant for brown rice.

The meal was a delightful array of two types of veggie curries—one with zucchini and another with an intriguing mix of beans and mushrooms—a perfectly spiced yellow dhal, a refreshing salad, fluffy rice, and warm roti. The substantial portions were matched by their authenticity and flavor, and when offered a refill, I couldn't resist a second helping of the dhal.

The meal concluded with a sweet note of Kheer, a rice pudding dessert I adore, sealing an immensely satisfying dining experience. This restaurant is truly a gem for those seeking flavorful, health-conscious Indian fare without the stress of choosing from an extensive menu.

Great lunch special! $14.95 for garlic bread, soup/salad and a main course. The service was quick and the food was tasty (we got the fettuccini alfredo and the lasagna). Nice ambiance for a casual dining experience, polite wait staff and most importantly, everything came quickly! Wouldn't say it's a go-to Italian spot in Manhattan, but for having walked around looking at some other options in Little Italy, we found this place really fit the bill for two hungry people who wanted a quick and simple Italian meal.

Great experience! Thanks to YELP, we jointed the waitlist while we shopping. When we get there, they helped us seated without waiting! The curry  is so good. We order regular spicy for red curry and mild spicy for  free curry. If you can't handle  spicy food, don't order the regular just ask for mild like us lolll  one  bowl of rice is totally not enough, coz the sauce is soo good. We finished every single drop The Thai pad is a little bit too sweet for usThe service is really good, the waiters are nice. When we seated, they bring us the pre drink, we still don't know the name of the drink, he said this is on house, to keep us warm( it was freezing outside))We loved the decorations. The smell and the food. We feel like we are in Thailand having dinner  in a local restaurant! !

Title: A Delightful Brunch at Friedman's

My friends and I dropped by Friedman's for a quick brunch and were pleasantly surprised by the spacious setting, which proved perfect for lingering conversations post-meal, even during typically crowded hours. Although I found the pancakes to have an unusual aftertaste, and the syrup served cold with no option to heat it was a letdown, the rest of my group thoroughly enjoyed their dishes. The prices at Friedman's are reasonable for the city, and the ability to call ahead helped us secure a table without the hassle of waiting in line. Overall, despite the minor hiccup with the pancakes, it was a lovely experience.

This place came highly recommended from a friend, so I brought my boyfriend here for his birthday. We opted for the January 2019 tasting menu and an a la carte order of the miso black cod as well. Farmer's Fresh Vegetable Fondue: The cream cheese sauce was absolutely amazing and all the veggies that came with it were fresh and crisp. Uni Croquette: The croquette was delicious, though nothing too special. Both of us received uni that was not fresh and left a bad taste in our mouths.Washu-Beef Short Rib Sashimi: This was the best thing that came on the tasting menu. The beef was incredibly tender and melted right in your mouth. Pan Roasted Branzino: For me, the branzino was just alright. The roasted veggies that came in the dish were the highlight, especially the brussel sprouts with sardines. Bohemian Washu Mini Burger: Honestly disgusting. I wouldn't even order this if it was a dollar. It was incredibly salty and had no other flavor. Avoid getting this if you can.Sashimi Rice Bowl: I have had better rice bowls at any other poke place in the city. The fish here was not fresh and there was a pool of very sour sauce at the bottom. Miso Black Cod: This was cooked perfectly, and melted in your mouth like butter. The skin was crispy and full of flavor. We ended with Morganstern's ice cream, which was pretty good.It was a nice experience, but for $275 for 2 people, I expect fresh ingredients. I probably wouldn't be back. There are other places in the city at a similar price point with better tasting menus.

Service here was 6/5 stars. I loved our server, Maddy! We came on a Sunday for brunch, and thankfully we beat the crowd so we were seated immediately. Right away, we got water, and this might be minor, but I really appreciate that they gave us two vials of water as opposed to one and extra napkins. Maddy even noticed when one of us dropped a fork and got us a replacement right away. We ordered the truffle fries to share and then I got the Southwestern Bowl (one of the specials). We had asked that the truffle fries be brought out first, and since they actually came out only like 2 minutes before our food, it was given to us for free. How amazing is that??Food-wise, the fries were great and the avocado and poached eggs in the bowl were delicious, but to be honest, the rice and bacon was a little... hard? Honestly though, the service was so above and beyond I would definitely come back.

Title: A Dumpling Delight for Korean Cuisine Lovers

I had a fantastic lunch experience at this restaurant, where the shrimp dumplings stood out as a highlight. Expertly prepared with authentic Korean flavors, they hit the mark for anyone craving Korean-style dumplings. The lunch special was a feast, complete with savory japchae, tangy kimchi, and perfectly cooked rice. The menu caters to a range of tastes with its Korean/Asian fusion offerings, including vegetarian options. For fellow dumpling enthusiasts or anyone keen on Korean fare, this spot is a must-try. Eagerly anticipating my next visit!

Title: A Fiery Staple with Some Misses - NYC's Szechuan Go-To

I frequent this Szechuan standout in NYC, a testament to its popularity with now multiple locations easing the once inevitable lines. The Dekalb food hall outpost shines with its nifty takeout window, perfect for quick cravings. However, consistency is not their strong suit. On a visit to the East Village branch, the usually delectable dan dan noodles were disappointingly dry, leading us to swear off that location.

Yet, the fiery allure of the spicy tofu fish keeps me returning. Served at a daring spice level of 10, it still woos even those timid with heat, thanks to the impeccably cooked fish and silky tofu - a true delight, especially with the bonus of free rice refills for the broth. The wontons in chili oil strike a perfect balance of sweet and spice, firmly placed on my favorites list along with the piquant mapo tofu and the double cooked fried chicken.

Steer clear of the fried rice, which sadly lacks the same punch. But don't overlook the complimentary hot tea; it's a comforting end to the bold flavors. Despite the occasional misstep, the hits make it worth the visit for those seeking a spicy kick.

Rubirosa's pizza crust might just set a new benchmark for thin-crust aficionados - it's astonishingly paper-thin, almost challenging the very definition of pizza. At $28 for a large half-and-half pie, I had the pleasure of sampling the Tie-Dye and Vodka varieties, each with sauce so memorable that it's a toss-up which one won my heart. While the crust's cracker-like delicacy may border on excessive for some, it's undeniably a unique culinary experience. Just a note - due to its richness and an earlier pizza adventure at nearby Prince Street, we savored only two slices. For those who relish the crunch of a thin crust, Rubirosa is not to be missed.

Unbelievable shakes. We got the peanut butter shake and the birthday cake shake which were crazy. Also the burgers and salad are excellent as well. Convenient location close to the 1, C, E subway stations. We will definitely be back.

Title: A Redemption Dinner at Blue Fin

After a previous letdown at Blue Fin, we skeptically ventured back and were pleasantly surprised by the turnaround in our dining experience. From the moment we entered and were greeted by a friendly young man, the evening took a turn for the better. We were seated downstairs, which provided a cozy and tranquil setting, a stark contrast to the bustling upper level.

Our server Nihil was attentive from the outset, offering us a choice of water and briefing us on the evening's specials without delay. Refreshingly, he showed no change in demeanor when we mentioned we don't drink alcohol – a courtesy that made us feel valued, unlike our last visit.

The culinary journey was nothing short of exceptional. We indulged in a half dozen oysters, the special tuna tartare, the beet salad, and crispy cauliflower, each dish proving to be a must-try. The freshness of the tartare paired with a delightful avocado sauce was a highlight, while the consistency of the menu offerings like the burrata and beet salad reassured us of the kitchen's prowess.

Regretfully, our schedule didn't allow for dessert, as we had a show to attend, but it's on our list for next time. Kudos to Blue Fin for a complete dining transformation and to Nihil, whose inclusive service made a lasting impression. It’s gratifying to see a restaurant that treats non-drinking customers with equal attention and respect. Bravo indeed!

I recently had brunch at this charming spot and was thoroughly impressed. The standout dish was the fried chicken and waffles, priced at $23. The chicken was perfectly fried to golden perfection, and it paired exquisitely with the unique Tabasco syrup, which amplified the flavors. To top it off, the bill was reasonable, enhancing the overall dining experience. Highly recommended!

I stopped by to grab a slice of the much-talked-about mozzarella pizza. The slice was satisfactory, with the mozzarella standing out as a highlight worth sampling. The tomato sauce was used sparingly and had a lighter, somewhat watery texture which surprisingly worked well for my palate. While the pizza didn't knock my socks off, the crust deserves a shout-out; it was wonderfully crispy, lending itself perfectly to the classic New York fold-and-bite. Overall, a decent option if you're in the mood for a no-fuss slice.

Believe the hype. It's delicious even when it's leftover. I've been wanting to try this for a while but am never in the area - but I made the trek and it was 100% worth it. Craftfully and meticulously created - you can tell that they're consistent and put love into it. The vodka slice - it was a pillow of dough with delicious vodka sauce. Everything I imagined it to be.The pepperoni slice - did not disappoint. Crispy pepperonis covering your whole slice with juicy flavors. The grandma with both ricotta and original are great thin slices, an ode to a classic. They're also doing custom deliveries for the boroughs during quarantine and takeout is super simple!

I stopped by this bustling spot solely for drinks and dessert after dining elsewhere, and I must say, the "Hit Me" cake alone merits a perfect 10/10 rating. Despite the overwhelming crowd and the seemingly endless waitlist, the vibrant atmosphere made the wait more than bearable. It's clear this place is a hit for good reason.

Title: Disappointing Fare at Sagaponack Despite the Charm

I've tried to love Sagaponack for its ambiance and convenient location, not to mention the tempting happy hour specials, but the food disappoints every time. My latest visit, intended as a final chance, unfortunately confirmed my previous experiences.

The seafood, which should be the star at a place like this, was underwhelming. The clams on the half shell were watery, likely from sitting on melted ice, and the oysters were overshadowed by subpar condiments. The horseradish lacked freshness and punch, the cocktail sauce was akin to plain ketchup, and the mignonette was oddly adulterated with what seemed to be pickles.

Recalling the overpriced and under-filled lobster roll from my last visit, I regretfully advise against this spot for a seafood fix. You'll get more for your money and tastier options elsewhere, like the more affordable and generous offerings at Luke's Lobster.

To add insult to injury, an uncomfortable encounter with a bartender over an honest review I had written left me feeling unwelcome. While service was commendable until that point, this final interaction sealed my decision not to return. It's a shame when a restaurant's potential is overshadowed by repeated culinary missteps and a single moment of poor customer relations.

Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3/5 stars)

This place is known for its cocktails for good reason! They are inventive and tasty combinations. The kiss kiss bang bang makes this person who doesn't necessary like gin want to have another and the Willy Wonka is a great dessert cocktail from a place that doesn't offer a dessert menu. As for the food ordered, everything was delicious. We had the carne Asada tacos which features tender meat. The cauliflower fritters which were luscious and perfectly balanced. The highlight was the zucchini chips with the honey dipped sauce which were fried perfectly. And of course, the truffle Parm fries which turned my friend who is never had truffle before into a lover. I will definitely be back for brunch and cocktails!

During Restaurant Week, my visit to this elegant eatery was an absolute delight. Beginning with earthy truffles and fresh bread gracing our table, the stage was set for an evening of culinary finesse. The pork shoulder stood out, tender to the fork and bursting with juiciness, although the filet mignon left me yearning for a splash more of seasoning.

The service, however, was impeccable – attentive and warm, ensuring we were cared for throughout the meal. Adding to the ambiance was the stunning decor, which would serve as a perfect backdrop for a photographic memoir of a special night out.

This spot is ideal for celebrating milestones, cozy dates, or simply a night of indulgence with friends or family. With the promise of a seasonal menu rotation, I'm already planning my next three visits to experience the fresh flavors this restaurant surely has to offer.

Title: A Taco Haven with Unbeatable Vibes

If you're looking for a fantastic spot to dig into some Mexican cuisine, especially tacos, this place is a gem. The ambiance channels the coolness of "The Smith" but with a Mexican twist, making it uniquely inviting. 

The menu varieties I've tried have all been top-notch. Tacos are priced fairly, and it's not just your average filling wrapped in a tortilla; each one comes with its own signature slaw and sauce, elevating the flavors to new heights. My tip? Gather a group of friends, come with an appetite, and indulge in the smaller dishes. You'll want to pass on the larger items like burritos to fully enjoy the spread.

Even when opting for takeout, there is no sacrifice in quality. This spot is versatile - great for solo outings, company events, a romantic date, or a casual taco night with pals. Whatever the occasion, this place won't disappoint.

I never had Lombardi's before and when we were in the area, we had a craving for pizza. It was a Saturday night so I was expecting a long wait but thankfully it turned out to be only a 10 minute short wait. We got breadsticks with sauce to share and it was alright..nothing special. The margarita pizza was delicious. It was thin, crispy and the right amount of sauce and cheese ratio. The crust was a bit too chewy and hard for me but overall I enjoyed the pizza. I wouldn't say this was the best pizza I have ever tasted but if I'm in the area and wanted some pizza, I'd definitely come around.

Luckily we came at the right time to where we didn't have to wait-now our table was a little rickety but hey, we didn't have to wait. I started with a margarita which was super strong and didn't taste the best (just bc the drink is strong doesn't mean it's going to be good). The portion size was huge, of course I had to get the fried chicken with macaroni & cheese and green beans. The chicken was good and juicy but my green beans were bland; they weren't seasoned/buttered and honestly I expected some bacon in them considering this was a soul food restaurant. The macaroni and cheese was super cheesy to the point to where the taste was lost (if that makes sense). Overall, we went here bc the tour bus we were on recommended it but wish we would have tried somewhere else that the locals would have recommended.

This is one of the most diverse sports bars I've been to in Ktown. Krush is on the 4th floor of a building, and it can get extremely crowded by 11 pm. One side of the space reminds me of a college frat party with 4 tables for beer pong, while the other side has the bar and tables for sit-down groups. It can get very loud (not sure how anyone in the building sleeps) and it took a while for bartenders to take our orders. Drinks were reasonably priced, and we got a mix of fruity cocktails to Corona beers. The kimchi fries were delicious, perfect for late night drunk food. It also comes with mozzarella cheese, ketchup, and an aioli. Overall, I can see the appeal of going to Krush, but I'd prefer to go to other nearby Ktown watering holes.

This place looks a lot fancier from the outside than from the inside. They had a sushi bar to your left where you can sit and enjoy a meal.sushi mixed special, not enough food. Average food at best. Sushi special wasn't much of a special. It comes with 2 small sides that sucked. Service was bad too. The best way to describe this place is that it sucked.

Title: A Slice of NY Perfection at Joey's Pizza

If you're on the hunt for authentic New York pizza, look no further than Joey's Pizza. This gem truly deserves the top spot on your NYC pizza bucket list, with Bleecker Street Pizza coming in as a close second.

Food: 5/5
Joey's takes their craft seriously, from the first bite to the last crumb. Unlike the all-too-common bland crusts that most pizzerias offer, Joey's dough is seasoned to perfection. Even their crusts are irresistible, leaving you savoring every bite without the urge to discard those final doughy edges. 

The variety, while not extensive, strikes all the right notes with options like the classic NY slice, the gooey mozzarella cheese pizza, and the hearty Sicilian style. Each variant is a testament to the pizzeria's dedication to quality and flavor.

Ambiance: The place channels a quintessential New York vibe that adds to the overall experience. 

Tip: Be prepared to queue for these coveted slices, although you might find shorter lines on a Monday when it's less crowded. But rest assured, the wait is worth it. Joey's Pizza is not just a meal; it's a highlight in the city's culinary landscape.

Title: A Unique and Enjoyable Fishing-to-Table Dining Experience

My dining adventure at this one-of-a-kind eatery was an absolute delight! From the moment we were handed raincoats and fishing licenses, the excitement was palpable. The opportunity to catch our dinner from the restaurant's "pond" was not only novel but incredibly engaging—even for those less skilled in angling, thanks to the handy scoop option.

My friend and I successfully reeled in a rainbow trout and opted for it to be prepared as tempura and soy sauce simmered, both of which were mouthwatering choices. Although the edible portions were on the smaller side, the flavor was unparalleled and thoroughly savored.

Aside from fishing, the appetizers on the menu did not disappoint. However, I would pass on the sea bream over rice in the future, as it was a bit too fishy for my taste. But the matcha tiramisu? A flawless fusion of aesthetics and taste.

Service-wise, our waitress was the epitome of friendliness and helpfulness, further enhancing the overall extraordinary experience. This dining concept is not just about the food; it's about the joy of the catch and the feast that follows. I'll definitely be returning for the fun atmosphere and the deliciously unique experience. Highly recommended for a fun and interactive meal out!

Other than the view I was greatly disappointed with this restaurant. First off if you are not staying at the hotel it's $8 charge per person. Why? No reason, if I had to go back I wouldn't pay unless I'm staying there and even then there are lots of other places to eat there. The view is nice, the restaurant slowly rotates which is cool. The tables for 2 are up at the edge and then other tables are scattered around further away from the glass. You have two options. One is the buffet, the other is a small menu with mostly appetizer plates. We ordered the Mediterranean platter. It came with hummus, bruschetta, and spinach and artichoke dip with pita chips. The bruschetta had capers. They don't work well together. That is not bruschetta and was my least favorite. I had one taste and no more. The hummus was next. I've had good hummus, this one seemed so bla. I had a little since I didn't want to waste it. Actually the spinach and artichoke surprised me. It was my favorite. It is grinded down very fine compared to what you'd normally have as a spinach dip but I liked it. The spinach wasn't overpowering and went well with the pita chips. It was the only thing of the platter I liked. Very overpriced for $23. I will give them props on the drinks. Their signature view drink was delicious. You could taste the alcohol, but it wasn't overpowering. Service was spotty, I had to ask out waiter for more water several times and for the check. He was attentive when we sat down and to take our order, but after that our server disappeared. I expected more being one of Marriotts prime hotels and being so expensive. I guess you're paying for not staying at the Marriott and for the view.

Went to Totto Ramen Next Door (the difference is they make their broth with pork at this location and not chicken.) we opted to go here because there was no wait as opposed to the other which had a very long wait. It was a Friday night around 8PM. I ordered the appetizer dumplings because I wasn't too hungry. The waiter brought over some sort of curry dish which was definitely not what I ordered. But it only took him a few minutes to bring out the right order once I corrected him. My siblings and friends all got ramen, honestly they smelled gross. Very fishy scent to them, which might have been the seaweed but either way it made me lose my appetite. The bathroom is behind the kitchen so you have to walk thru the kitchen to get to it which is strange BUT I like the fact that there's a bathroom to use regardless. At the end of our meal (we had just finished,) the waiter came up to us and asked us to leave so other people could come sit and eat which- is kind of rude. I mean I understand you want to be able to fit as many people in as you can but I've hosted and waitresses before and I would never ask paying customers to leave (unless we had a reservation coming in soon OR if they had just been sitting there for hours, wasting a table.) But we weren't, we had been sitting for an extra maybe ten minutes after we paid. It was kind of rude. My siblings and friends didn't have great reviews for the ramen. I didn't try it though so I can't really say. Probably would choose Momofuku which is a little farther from this location.

Perhaps the best Peruvian chicken I've ever had.I grabbed a few items for dinner from here including a half chicken, arroz chauffa and some really interesting item called saltipapa. It took about 15 minutes for the food to be ready.The chicken itself was half shire and half dark meat but the skin and meat were super flavorful and juicy. Far more flavorful than other Peruvian chicken places I've been. It didn't need the green sauce it came with so I used that on the other dishes.The chicken and soy sauce in rice were good. Lots of chicken in the rice.The saltipapa is just a bunch of hot dogs cut up and mixed with French fries. I've never had it before but this was good. The fries were on the soggier side and the hot dogs tasted similar to the Hebrew national brand.All in all I'd come back here for the chicken itself and maybe a few sides.

After Le Coucou first opened mid-2016, they were excluded from Michelin's 2017 and 2018 list, but made it on the 2019 list. I typically find the most value and surprises in one-star Michelins but this restaurant met expectations given its pricier menu and hype. The interior design and decor was wonderfully executed by Roman and Williams. If you love the atmosphere of Le Coucou don't miss La Mercerie, also done by Roman and Williams. Le Coucou has a lovely soft, quiet and intimate ambiance. I would suggest grabbing a drink at their aesthetic bar (see photo) if you're waiting on other guests. The bartender made me a refreshing champagne cocktail (I told him flavors I like, not on menu). I came here for lunch with visiting friends. They offer the two course pre-fixe lunch for $58 per person. I had the oysters then the chicken and foie gras. Both were good but not outstanding. I uploaded photos of the courses and entrance bar as well. Service did leave something to be desired, nothing flagrantly wrong but definitely cold. While lunch overall was enjoyable and I'm glad I went for the experience, I do not think I would return. As Michelin describes its one-star rating, it's worth a stop.

After much anticipation, I recently dined at ABC Cocina for brunch and the experience did not disappoint. From the moment I set foot in the restaurant, the attention to detail was evident. The decor was stunning, creating a welcoming ambiance that complimented the meal.

Even though I arrived ahead of my friends, the staff graciously seated me early. As I browsed the menu, each option seemed more tempting than the last, a testament to its thoughtful design. Our servers were a delight, striking the perfect balance of attentiveness and efficiency.

To start, we sipped on a mezcal mango drink and a passionfruit margarita, both of which lived up to our high expectations.
