The food arrived swiftly, and we indulged in an array of dishes including guacamole, beef empanadas, mushroom tacos, chicken tacos, patatas bravas, and churros to cap off the meal. The guacamole and mushroom tacos stood out as extraordinary, while the other dishes were enjoyable but not remarkable.

In conclusion, my visit to ABC Cocina was a memorable one. The overall ambiance, coupled with the swift service and delectable flavors, left me eager to explore the rest of the ABC culinary family.

Having a Burger in Box (BIB) just a block away from work in Midtown is a game-changer! Their burgers never fail to impress—they're my go-to in the area. True to form, this location didn't disappoint, conveniently situated near R Café. Each burger is made to order, guaranteeing freshness that you can taste. The horseradish sauce adds a bold, zesty kick to their classic burgers that I absolutely adore. I'm already eyeing the chicken sandwich for my next visit!

Title: Great Views, Average Eats at Waterside Bistro

During a recent visit to the Waterside Bistro, I found that while the food was good, it didn't quite knock my socks off. The restaurant boasts a picturesque location, perched by the water with stunning views of the city skyline and passing boats. The option to dine al fresco is a definite plus, allowing guests to soak up the atmosphere, weather permitting. However, indoor seating is also available for those seeking shelter from the elements.

My meal of choice was the Cadillac Burger, which unfortunately arrived more well-done than the requested medium. Thankfully, the burger retained its juiciness, and the fresh tomato, lettuce, and cheese helped balance the dryness. Though satisfactory, the bacon on the burger was a touch overdone for my taste.

Each burger is substantial in size and accompanied by a generous serving of crispy fries, ensuring no one departs with an empty stomach. However, the pricing felt steep considering the overall quality of the meal. In summary, while the setting might be idyllic, the culinary experience doesn't fully measure up to the high prices.

Japanese noodle destination with solid variety of soba, udon and more offered.Across the ubiquitous Japanese restaurants in NYC, Soba AZUMA is one of the few places where I have seen a majority of Japanese local and visiting going for affordable and authentic Japanese food.DecorThe two person tables are tight in their design as you enter but the table dimensions are relatively large for your average midtown restaurant. It is a comfortable atmosphere with booth seating and accommodating large groups and solo diners a like.FoodWith a few recent visits, I am consistently happy with the quality and portions of the meals. The Pork Kimich Nabeyaki Udon is a true star which I have eaten twice and it is a solid cold weather option. It has the spicy kimichi flavor with the little bowl to slow enjoy. The Fried Chicken Curry Soba was tasty with the fried chicken but the curry was a little thinner than your average Japanese curry. The fried yuca fries with mental mayo is a winner for the flavor. The crab cream croquette are also a good option. For dessert, there are a lot of ice creams from ice cream with sesame and green tea flavors, green tea tiramasu, and black sesame Mont Blanc. I like the Mont Blanc and I was surprised by the size.ServiceAll the staff spoke some Japanese which was nice even. I think that they did not rush anyone on the meals. The menu is big so it can feel overwhelming but we were treated well and efficiently.OverallI like this location and their Fort Lee location too. I will come back next time that I am nearby.

My college friend decided to try this spot. This casual hangout spot is know for their Cal Tex-Mex street food.  The tacos were definitely deceivingly filling but I ended up ordering the appetizers as the main entree. The food I ordered was pretty good with leftovers to take home.I ordered the sangria, which was really good with the tot-chos with the chili and grilled Mexican corn. I also requested to take the corn out of the cob. Food, drinks and service were solid. I would recommend this spot.

Our destination stop every Sunday after Church.Sometimes, we take out.They have a  variety of pastries, from meat and eggs breakfast products ones to sweet mini tarts. We tried the Mini Hot Dogs, Egg Toast, Chocolate Croissant, Fruit Tarts, Raisins Twists, Almond Croissant. There is also a refrigerated area with Sandwiches, Salads.Cakes are available to go.Coffee, Tea, Hot Chocolate, Juices, Cold Drinks, are available

Friend and I mad a reservation for after a midweek show.  We were seated immediately upon arrival by the friendly bartender.  There were a few occupied tables and they sat is at a nice quiet table. We didn't realize it was restaurant week when we booked and were pleasantly surprised by the large selection of items on the list. I opted for the lobster bisque, seafood crepe and bread pudding.  My friend ordered the mussels, beef bourgiunon and apple tart.  The mussels were tasty, prepared more like a stuffed calm with breadcrumbs and parmesean cheese.  The soup was tasty but very watery, not like any bisque I have ever had and was lacking seafood.  My friend enjoyed the Bourguignon and I enjoyed the crepe even though the only seafood I could detect was bay scallops. However, the béchamel sauce was delicious. Dessert is where this meal fell short.  As a French restaurant we both had high hopes for a delicious sweet treat.  Unfortunately the bread pudding was literally like a slice of bread with a creamy sauce, very strange and not like any other bread pudding I've had.  Once again sauce was the shining star of the dish.  The apple tart was served ice cold with a large amount of raspberry puree.  Unappealing on multiple levels.   Initially our waiter was very attentive and friendly, but soon after we ordered he was difficult to locate for additional drinks, asked if we wanted coffee/tea after our desserts were served ( and left mostly uneaten) and never asked how we enjoyed our meal when he left the check.  I will give this place another try because it started off well and I am not sure how many tables the waiter was handling, plus the sauces were good and the apps were tasty.  Perhaps it was due to restaurant week that the place fell short, but I did still have a nice meal and enjoyed myself, just not to my level of expectation. Next time I will try the onion burger everyone raves about!

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Renowned Ramen Spot

I arrived at the restaurant with pretty high expectations, only to leave somewhat underwhelmed. The shoyu ramen, which I usually relish, was a letdown at a mere 5/10. The broth lacked depth and left a peculiar bitter aftertaste, while the noodles failed to make an impression. The pork was merely passable, noticeably tougher than what I've savored at other establishments.

On a more positive note, the mapo ramen scored an 8/10 for its innovative twist. Though the dish boasted a rich sauce and a generous mixture of tofu and meat, it still fell short of remarkable, leaving me with no compelling urge to return.

As for the extras, the fried chicken add-on, also receiving an 8/10, delighted the taste buds but offered scant value at $4 for two small pieces. The gyoza, a 7/10, was another story of mediocrity with its unremarkable filling and skin, leading me to question its worthiness as a $3 addition.

In short, while this restaurant presents some creative dishes, it struggles with consistency and value, which sadly mars the dining experience.

Title: A Brunch Haven with Room for Improvement at Upper West Side Kosher Dairy

I recently visited a kosher dairy gem on the Upper West Side, ideal for brunch enthusiasts. The star of the menu has to be the paninis, thanks to their spectacular sesame bread. For those leaning towards a heartier choice, the tuna steak is an infallible option, striking the perfect balance between a charred exterior and a juicy core.

The Haloumi salad, with its delightful fried cheese morsels, is a crowd-pleaser, whereas the pizza, preferably thin crust, does satisfy despite a tendency to be on the greasier side. The Israeli salad is consistently fresh and delightful.

However, the restaurant could improve its game in a few areas. A note to the chefs: keep wraps and salads separate to avoid a soggy disaster! While the broccoli side was tasty, discerning palettes can tell it's likely from the freezer, not the garden.

Service shines here but can stumble, particularly when requests stray from the standard — like half-and-half pizza toppings, which seemed to puzzle our waiter. The absence of avocados or any side sauces is a curious gap, and with craft beer's popularity in the neighborhood, expanding their selection could be a wise move.

In summary, this spot is worth a visit for its dairy delights, especially if you make it in time for brunch. A few tweaks could transform this from a good to a great dining experience.

Reliable neighborhood Asian cuisine. Menu spans from Japanese and Chinese to Thai and Vietnamese. We went the Japanese route and ordered miso soup, kani salad, salmon tartar and several sushi rolls. Everything was fresh and tasty and made exactly to order. Prices were also incredibly reasonable. Ozen will definitely be our new UWS casual Asian food spot!

After a year of anticipation (when we were in NY last year, the restaurant was closed for maintenance/remodeling), we were so disappointed with the quality of the food. Everything we ordered (Mango Salad, Mee Goreng, and Basil Fried Rice) was so sweet and have no taste. How can you mess up with such simple dishes? The mango salad was filled with iceberg lettuce and big chunks of pineapples and cucumbers to look like there were a lot of mangos. I also asked the server why the fried rice was especially sweet. She said it was because of the special sauce that they used and I should have ordered spicy instead. We asked them to remake it spicy and it still came out sweet. Very disappointed that Rasa did not serve authentic Malaysian food. At least my wife's hot milk tea and the service were good, so I gave them two stars for that.

A mix of various Asian cuisine without fusion. Here you can find various Thai, Japanese, and Chinese options. Thus it is a perfect place to have a gathering of people with different (Asian cuisine) tastes.

Title: Hip Hangout with Hits and Misses

I've turned into a regular at this vibrant spot that's perfect for a gathering of friends. Happy hour is the best time to indulge in their drink specials, love the $5 lychee martinis, and dive into some tasty bar food. The dry-aged sliders and Cajun waffle fries are standouts - absolutely delicious.

On Tuesdays and Thursdays, they have a tempting taco deal where you can pick any three tacos for $12. Their selection, including bulgogi, tempura shrimp, tempura fish, and banh mi chicken, offers a nice variety. Although my favorite taco pick varies with each visit due to some inconsistency in preparation, the bulgogi was notably succulent last time, although the shrimp did fall a bit short on filling.

The charbroiled oysters are generally a treat, though on my last visit, they were somewhat sandy. Despite these minor hiccups, the overall experience is generally great. I'm giving this place a solid 4 stars. It's certainly worth a try, especially on taco nights, but be prepared for some variability in the quality of the dishes.

My colleagues and I often frequent Pera Soho for happy hour, and a recent visit reaffirmed why it's our favorite spot. Despite a brief mix-up upon arrival, the staff seated us promptly with the understanding that we had 1.5 hours – ample time for our plans.

The Apricot Margarita continues to reign as my top pick from their Happy Hour offerings, which impressively run every day of the week. My cousin sampled the rose sangria and found it exceptionally light and refreshing, perfect for winding down. 

Pera Soho's service didn't disappoint; the staff was attentive, ensuring our short visit for drinks and snacks was enjoyable. It's no wonder this place remains a staple for our after-work outings.

Title: Innovative Service, but Sushi Lost Its Essence

I recently dined at a contemporary restaurant that put a unique spin on the sushi experience. The service was nothing short of amazing, earning a well-deserved five stars. Our waiter particularly shone, going above and beyond to surprise my friend with an outstanding birthday dessert.

While the food was generally good, I found the sushi to be overly adorned, with large pieces of truffle and other ingredients that overwhelmed the delicate flavor of the fish. Purists be warned: this is not your conventional sushi joint. The sushi's journey to our table, routed through the kitchen rather than directly from the chef's hands, struck me as unusual and detracted slightly from the authenticity of the experience.

Overall, if you're seeking exemplary service with an open mind for a modern take on sushi, you might find this place a delight. Traditional sushi aficionados, however, may want to look elsewhere.

Title: A Flavorful Vegan Experience with Room for Service Improvement

After much anticipation, I finally dined at Seasoned Vegan, and the name truly reflects the culinary delights on offer. The vegan fare is impressive, the Nori Rolls being a standout surprise with their delectable mystery, and the “chicken” so masterfully smothered that even omnivores would not pine for meat. While the pizza quesadillas might cater to the less adventurous, the sweet potatoes burst with flavor, and despite the Mac & "cheese" needing a bit more zest, it was satisfying.

However, the service did not parallel the quality of the food. One might expect smoother operations from a well-established spot, especially during the rush of unreserved diners. The host seemed overwhelmed despite the restaurant's longevity.

Closing on a high note, the Raisin cupcake was nothing short of awesome, capping the meal beautifully. Seasoned Vegan stands out with its bold vegan stance. Despite service hiccups, the experience was positive, proving that a completely vegan menu can be both exciting and fulfilling.

Walking into the restaurant immediately conjured images of a dimly lit club, with Snoop Dogg's music setting an oddly vibrant backdrop to the Chinese lantern-adorned dining area. Despite the confusing atmosphere, the staff's friendliness shone through as they efficiently served up our meal.

Our culinary journey started with a shared chicken pho that boasted a broth of supreme quality—arguably one of the finest I've savored. While the other pho components were satisfactory, it was the broth that left a lasting impression, earning a solid B+.

For the main course, the spicy eggplant tofu was presented with modest portions. The well-prepared tofu was enlivened by just the right texture of eggplant, and the spice level, albeit higher than anticipated, was enjoyable, warranting an A-.

In summary, the cuisine is a compelling reason to revisit, but the discordant club-like vibe is a deterrent. A softer soundtrack could bridge the gap between the ambiance and the wonderful flavors on offer.

Title: Delightful Dining with a View at Hudson Yards

My dining experience at the Hudson Yards restaurant offered a lovely meal complemented by the stunning backdrop of the Vessel and Hudson River. Despite our late arrival for the 5:45pm reservation, the staff graciously honored their 15-minute grace period, promptly seating us by 6pm and accommodating my belongings with complimentary coat check services.

As I awaited my companion, I was treated to a glass of Pernod Absinthe, a delightful surprise to find on their menu. The appetizers were a highlight with the octopus and dim sum platter standing out for their flavor and quality, though the fried sea bass fell short, seeming overbreaded with little meat.

An unfortunate moment occurred when my dinner partner was inconvenienced by crumbs from our waiter, but this did not overshadow our evening. We engaged in lively conversation, relishing the good food and company in a truly beautiful environment. Despite the small mishap, I would recommend this dining venue for its overall pleasant atmosphere and attentive service.

I recently visited a local restaurant for lunch and opted for their lunch special, which boasted a great price and generous portion size. The meal was also visually appealing, adding to the overall dining experience. I chose the tomato fried with eggs set, which came with a tomato egg soup—amusingly doubling my tomato and egg intake for the day.

The egg component was slightly on the dry side, reminiscent more of crispy fried egg skins than a traditional moist scramble. However, this texture added an interesting dimension to the flavor profile of the dish. As a side note, I sampled their black fungus, which packed a serious punch in terms of heat. A word of caution for those who prefer milder dishes: the black fungus is incredibly spicy. Overall, the meal was enjoyable—a few surprising elements but definitely worth a try for the adventurous palate.

First restaurant week experience and OMG, is it because I'm inexperienced or just that I was BLOWN AWAY by everything?!?! Only time will tell, but I absolutely loved everything.My boyfriend and I made reservations for a Thursday evening and took part in their restaurant week deal, which is actually really worth it for the price. For less than $50, you are served really delicious American-French fusion, with a gorgeous presentation and spectacular service (Nicole was amazing!). Upon seating, you get to choose from a basket of breads. It smelled so good and I settled for the sourdough while my boyfriend got the rye.For the entree, I ordered the duck breast (medium rare) and my boyfriend ordered the Filet Mignon and added a lobster on the side for $12. The duck skin was seared perfectly and my boyfriend said his was equally delicious. It was cooked perfectly, with a warm pink center, which we requested. Also, shoutout to the Peach Melba, which I literally inhaled in 10 seconds.  Overall, a beautiful beautiful dinner place with wonderful food and people. I definitely want to go back, when the wallet permits...

It's a nice place to eat if you feel like everywhere is too crowded at the Chelsea Market. Loved the interior, super Parisian! Food is a hit or miss though!  I ordered two appetizers (Mac 'n' Cheese & Fries) and absolutely loved it! It got me so excited to try the main (Steamed Mussels) but it wasn't that good. You just have so much more better options at Chelsea Market.

Title: Comfort Food Heaven at Five Napkin Burger

If your taste buds are screaming for an indulgent 'cheat day' or your soul is aching for some crispy, carby solace, Five Napkin Burger is your sanctuary. Visiting NYC for work with my omnivorous boss and coworker, we stumbled upon this gem in search of late-night comfort food that could cater to my vegan needs while pleasing meat-lovers too.

Charm oozes from every corner of this adorable eatery, with an inviting atmosphere that's matched by a much-appreciated full bar. We kicked things off with their towering onion rings, a crispy dream with that perfect oniony center, accompanied by a symphony of dipping sauces.

The star for me was their vegan burger, paired with sweet potato fries. I devoured every morsel with gusto – not a crumb survived. It was so good that despite a short stay in the city, a repeat visit was all I could think about. Five Napkin Burger deserves a resounding five stars for making everyone at the table exceedingly happy.

Hate to give this one a bad review due to the hype and reputation of this restaurant from Italy, but I really thought this place was average especially for the long line required to enter in the restaurant.  First of all, they officially open at 12pm. I started waiting on line at 11am and didn't get in until 12:30pm. 1.5 hour long wait was not worth the panini. It was good/average and would be something I would consider getting if the queue wasn't this long. First of all, the bread is tasteless imo. It has a nice layer of olive oil on top, but the bread itself lacked flavor. That's okay right ? You would assume that the inside ingredients of the sandwich would make it more flavorful right ? Wrong. La summer is a very light sandwich with prosciutto, mozzarella, tomato, and balsamic vinegar, so in some ways, the ingredients itself taste on the lighter side. Some may like it since it's refreshing. (My boyfriend actually preferred this sandwich to Le boss) but I personally felt it could have used a bit more balsamic vinegar to bring out more flavor. The Le boss was another sandwich we ordered. This one was much more flavorful due to the truffle cream. The truffle flavor was quite pungent. The sandwich itself looked sad compared to La summer  since it's super flat, but I liked this one much more than La summer. This place is somewhere I'd consider getting a quick lunch at if there's no long queues. However the workers there were very enthusiastic when making the sandwich and were overall very nice.

Came here to have a fancy tea party with my friends on a random Sunday. Reservations are recommended, but didn't seem necessary. We were late to our reservations, but the host and waiter were very accommodating.Each floral tea set comes with your own pot of tea (which you choose from a large selection/list), and preset finger sandwiches and dessert for $80 not including tax and tip.The tea selections we each got were the grand lapsang souchong, chocolate, and bai mu dan.Overall, the ambience was beautiful and very fancy (added bonus having a huge chandelier at the center of the room)! The finger foods were good, but not really worth the $80. Tea was phenomenal. The Grand Lapsang Souchong had a nice smoky smell/taste, reminded me of a campfire. Wouldn't come back, unless for a very special occasion.

Title: Cozy Spot with Stellar Ramen, But Bring Your Patience (and a Flashlight)

My recent visit to the local ramen joint left my palate sated yet my comfort a bit compromised. The Kuu Chili Ramen was the star of the night—its broth was rich and flavorsome, a perfect symphony of spices. However, the noodles, while tasty, were on the thinner side; a heartier thickness would've elevated the dish even further.

The ambiance, unfortunately, dimmed my enthusiasm. With lighting so low, the struggle to appreciate the meal's visual appeal was real. Arriving at peak dinner hour, 7:30 pm on a Friday, meant enduring a brief wait—in a place that feels more like a sardine can than a dining room. The scant seating—a mere three tables and a couple of bar areas—made for an uncomfortably close dining experience.

Mind the time of your visit, and maybe your wallet too; at $18 for a bowl, it's not the most budget-friendly. In summary, the ramen may beckon me back, but it'll be during the off-peak hours for sure.

3.5/5Stopped by on a Tuesday evening for dinner. There were open tables so we were seated immediately. We ordered:Chicken wings - crispy and fresh. You can choose from soy garlic, original, and spicy. Bulgogi tacos - on the dry side, but they were pretty loaded with meat. Comes with sour cream and lime. Cheese tteokbokki and chicken katsu - would have liked more cheese on the dish, it felt like the cheese was more of an after thought. The katsu was crispy but on the thin side.Marinated Ribs with corn cheese - meat was tender and flavorful. The cheese is on the sweeter side, but needs to be eaten right away - as it solidifies pretty fast. Comes with rice, which was on the dry side. They have happy hour deals from 5 to 8pm with $2 off some of their beer, soju and cocktail selection. Service was good and food comes out fast. Great ambience and decor. Definitely doesn't compare to the restaurants in ktown but does the job.
Cool , hipster inspired Mexican joint with a causal feel . Good drinks . Limited beers and solid chips n salsa . The steak quesadilla was excellent ! Wu definitely come back for more !!!

Title: Cozy Evening with Flavorful Bites

My dining experience on a bustling Thursday night around 7pm at this local eatery started with a longer-than-anticipated wait, which surpassed the 30 minutes we were initially quoted. Nevertheless, the delay was made more pleasant by the bar's offerings, where I particularly enjoyed the "happy soda" – a delightful mix of condensed milk, rose syrup, and soda that really allowed the rose's fragrance to shine.

Once seated, the food proved to be quite satisfying, albeit the portions were somewhat small for my liking. Our table shared a variety of dishes including chicken satay skewers, chicken wings, beef rendang, and a noodle dish. The standout for me were the chicken wings – perfectly seasoned and packed with flavor. Each dish brought its own spice profile to the table, making the meal an overall savory adventure.

Rating: 3.5/5 – Great flavors, but be prepared for a wait and modest servings.

I recently discovered a fantastic Thai food spot that's perfect for the New York City pace. The service was outstanding, with super friendly staff who delivered our meals with impressive speed. They offer a happy hour on weekdays at 7:30 PM featuring $5 beers, which is a great deal.

We ordered the papaya salad, tom yum soup, and grilled steak. While the papaya salad was a tad too sweet for my taste, the grilled steak was a standout dish, and the tom yum noodles brimming with seafood were simply divine. If you're looking for quick, delectable Thai cuisine and efficient service, this gem of a place is certainly worth a visit. I'm already looking forward to my next meal here!

Hung out at Blind Tiger Ale House on Thursday afternoon. The bar has an excellent selection of beers, but the space is tight and the prices are high.Quality: With 28 beers on draft you are bound to find something you like at Blind Tiger Ale House. They had a good mix of styles and at least one beer on nitro. There was a clear emphasis on local and New York beers, but they also had some other craft brews from across the country.Quantity: The size of the pour is listed on the board, but they were still smaller than I expected.Value: $7-$11 for the listed Draft Beers.Ambiance: Blind Tiger Ale House is a dive bar located in Greenwich Village. With a clear emphasis on high quality beer, this is not exactly the hole in the wall dive bar you may expect. In a space that is reminiscent of an old English pub, the bar is a relaxed and cozy space for a drink, and on a cold day, somewhere you can sit by a fire. A single television sits in the corner and conversation overwhelms any music that may play in the background.Crowd: When we arrived the place was packed. It is not a big space, so it fills up quick. Lots of people were watching the baseball game and enjoying the day off.Service: Very animated bartender who seemed to get along with all the guests.Parking: No easy street parking nearby.

Title: Unmet Expectations on a Heartfelt Visit

As a loyal patron of Del Posto, making my fourth visit, I brought my parents along, eager to share my favorite culinary gem in the city. Previously, I'd leave counting the days until my next visit, singing praises of the unforgettable courses. However, this time, the experience fell flat. The excitement for the truffle-infused chicken was met with disappointment – a promised burst of flavor that never materialized. With every bite, my anticipation for the familiar thrill of their cooking waned, replaced by the realization that the dishes were merely ordinary. Reluctantly, I have to admit that Del Posto, once a deserving contender for Michelin's 3 stars in my book, now feels more akin to a one-star experience. Despite the evident care in preparation, it pains me not to rate the food any lower than three stars. My earnest hope is for Del Posto to rekindle the culinary magic I know they're capable of. I miss my favorite restaurant, and wish for nothing more than to fall in love with it all over again.

My recent visit to this restaurant in pursuit of their 'Box of Dreams' was an absolute delight. Typically not a sashimi enthusiast, I found myself thoroughly impressed by the array of offerings. The presentation was stunning, and each sampler in the box surpassed my expectations with its freshness and superb taste. What stood out was the branded egg – a unique touch that spoke to the thoughtful branding of the establishment. Coupled with great service, this dining experience was top-notch from start to finish. Highly recommended for both aficionados and newcomers to the delicacies of sashimi and beyond.

Title: A Satisfying Post-Happy Hour Feast

Following a lively happy hour nearby, my companions and I swung by this eatery on a bustling Friday night seeking edible solace to temper the evening's libations. The culinary highlight were the pork buns—so mouthwatering that I nearly succumbed to the temptation of a second helping for the journey home. Accompanying this was the eel don, another dish that did not disappoint with its rich flavors.

Service here shines with a friendly and efficient staff that keeps the dining experience smooth and enjoyable. Prices are reasonable and competitive for the area, aligning with what you'd expect from similar 9th Avenue Asian spots.

While the cocktail enthusiast in me was a bit let down by their discontinued mixed drinks (an artifact still teased on their current menu), the selection of beer and wine proved to be a sufficient consolation. This minor hiccup won't deter me; I'm eager to return and delve deeper into their menu offerings.

B Side is a great pizza spot not too far from Times Square, which is A) a food wasteland, as we know and B) unfortunately where my office is. Two friends and I shared the Roasted pear salad, Killer bee pizza and Spicoli pizza. Our waiter sort of went away halfway through, which was annoying, but the food was awesome.

Title: A Ramen Oasis in the Bustling Heart of New York

Tucked away in the energetic streets of New York, this cozy ramen joint is the perfect escape for a quick, delectable bite. Don't let the frequent line out the door deter you; their revered ramen is worth the wait. The ambiance is quaint and unassuming, ensuring the focus remains on the flavors that await.

Operated as a cash-only eatery with a refreshingly concise one-page menu, the culinary simplicity is part of its charm. Purists will appreciate the authentic selection of ramen, complemented by traditional appetizers like edamame and tofu. Though options for vegetarians are limited, the generously portioned bowls – priced between $13 and $18 – are packed with aromatic broth and spices that promise to satisfy.

With a welcoming team of ramen chefs, service is as smooth as the broth, allowing for a swift dining experience should you wish. And for those finding themselves craving just a bit more, a nominal fee buys you a comforting refill of broth to savor. This spot is an absolute gem, offering a taste of authenticity that's bound to have you contemplating seconds.

This was our first stop after we got into NYC for the weekend. There was an all afternoon happy hour so they had 8 dollar cocktails. I had the Pickled Jane: vodka, honey, pickled tomato juice, served on the rocks. It was very good and sort of like a Bloody Mary, but sweeter and not tomato based. I had the special of the day sandwich- caprese with pesto. It was very good and I liked the pesto. It came with rosemary fries, which were OK but a bit over cooked. The service was not great, but it seemed they were understaffed.

After anticipating a visit to this much-talked-about eatery, I finally had the chance to dine there. The experience was pleasant, with dishes that were as delightful to taste as they were to look at. However, with prices starting at a steep $11, it feels like a place to experience just once before seeking out more budget-friendly options.

Title: A Letdown at the Noodle Spot

I recently dined at this establishment with high hopes for a comforting bowl of ramen, but left feeling somewhat underwhelmed. Personally, I'm not a fan of thick broths and noodles, so the heavy consistency wasn't to my liking. However, this boils down to personal preference and might delight those who enjoy a heartier soup base.

The most disappointing aspect for me was the chashu. A highlight of any ramen dish, the pork was unfortunately dry and lacked the juicy succulence I anticipated. This significantly detracted from the overall experience, considering how essential chashu is to the dish.

An additional hiccup came with the kaedama, or extra noodles, that I had ordered on the side to prevent them from becoming soggy. Due to a mix-up, they were served directly in the broth, despite my efforts to avoid this very issue. Although I informed the waitress and chose not to have it corrected, it resulted in a less enjoyable texture than I prefer.

In summary, while the meal wasn't wholly negative, it did not live up to my expectations, particularly with the execution of the chashu and noodles.

Solid, comfy neighborhood thai food spot. Really good service despite how late it was and how busy they were. Food arrived quickly and was fresh and flavorful.  Lights are super bright and much of the decor is shiny white so bring your shades if you are light sensitive or hungover.

During my highly anticipated return to this exquisite restaurant, the culinary journey was nothing short of phenomenal. Our appetizer, the leeks, which I previously criticized, astonished me with an improved flavor profile that resonated deeply this visit. The lobster and scallop-stuffed cabbage were delectable, but with the myriad of intriguing options, they might not make our list next time.

The main course, a roasted duckling shared between two, was a revelation. While the duck breast garners much adoration, it’s the succulent leg that truly captured our taste buds and left a lasting impression as one of the finest new dishes I've savored recently.

Our dining experience reached a sweet crescendo with a magnificent trio of cheeses, enhanced by sublime honey, and a decadent chocolate mousse paired with white coffee ice cream. While the dessert was sheer bliss, cheese connoisseurs might consider swapping for a second sweet treat.

In summary, the entire meal was a testament to the restaurant's consistency and culinary excellence. It's clear we'll be returning for more unforgettable dining experiences.

Very loud bar and Korean restaurant known for their fried chicken. More of a place to pre-game than a place to go for dinner. Play Korean music, and have screens in the back of the restaurant streaming their music videos. When I went the waitress was not familiar with the menu and could not make any recommendations. They also forgot one of our dishes. We ended up ordering a scallion pancake, honey lemon fried chicken, and a chicken bimbimbop. You choose a size of order for the fried chicken (S-XL), the type of chicken (wings, thigh, breast, etc) and the flavor. We got a medium size boneless breast with honey lemon flavor, and it was HUGE! Their were 12 pieces. It was not high quality though, and was just like chicken fingers from McDonalds. The bimbimbop and scallion pancake were not any good either.The drinks are absurdly expensive. One beer was 10$15% tip is added to the tip3/10

This is a 2 story steak house. We went around 6 pm on a Friday and made a reservation in advance. I don't think you would need a reservation around this time; there were not many people inside until about 7 pm. Before we were seated, we were told it is mandatory to coat check, but later saw multiple tables with there coats on their chair, which was annoying. We ordered the Traditional Caesar Salad ($17) as an appetizer. For the entree, we ordered the 15oz Cold Water Lobster Tail ($59) and the Filet Mignon 10oz ($51). The lobster tail was good, and we asked for it steamed instead of baked. The Filet was okay, could've had more seasoning. Overall, the restaurant is exceptionally overpriced for an okay meal.

I recently dined at this establishment with a friend during a relatively quiet period, but despite the lack of crowdedness, we experienced quite slow service. The visibly understaffed situation, with only one waiter tending to all customers, could explain the delay. While our waiter came across as amiable and hard-working, we had to actively seek his attention to place our order. Fortunately, once ordered, the food arrived in a timely manner.

However, a minor hiccup occurred when the waiter offered parmesan, which we accepted but he never returned with, leading us to enjoy our meal without it. As for the dish itself, we opted for the Paccheri alla Norma. The sauce was rich and flavorful, which was a highlight, but unfortunately, the pasta's texture was too al dente for my preference.

My friend and I came to Yoon Haeundae Galbi at 5:30pm on a Friday.  My friend made a reservation via the app Seated.  The restaurant was moderately busy when we arrived and picked up by the time we left around 7pm.  The vibe here is more upscale than other K-town restaurants and is reflected in the prices.Yelpers, if you check in you can get a free draft beer (we got Asahi).  We ordered the beef jijimi appetizer ($13), a soondubu jjigae ($17), a wok fried mushroom ($16) with rice ($2), and 1 Kloud beer ($6 - happy hour).  Overall, we thought the food was average and overpriced.  I would not recommend the beef jijimi.  It was very bland and definitely not worth $13.  The jjigae had heat to it and it was fine, but I've had better for cheaper in the NYC K-town area.  Normally, this would be a three-star review, but service is outstanding.  The staff really make you feel special and welcomed.  There were multiple check-backs, our waters were refilled, and the food came out in a timely fashion.  A man who seemed like the manager also checked in with us and seemed to genuinely care.  We felt very appreciated here!  My friend got great deals from using Seated at YHG, so I would recommend using the app if you have an iPhone.

During quarantine, I swung by Prince St Pizza and met with the expected line, though it moved swiftly due to the prevalence of delivery service agents. Admirably, the establishment enforced safety measures: a two-customer limit, mandatory takeout, and a protective plexiglass at the register.

Taste-wise, the pizza slices earned a respectable 7/10. The sauce was robust, the crunch satisfactory, albeit not exceptional, and the slices were commendably light on grease. I particularly enjoyed the margherita slice over the Sicilian.

Despite the quality, I wouldn’t advise waiting in a lengthy queue during normal circumstances, especially considering New York City's plethora of excellent pizza spots. Additionally, the price point of $9.50 for two slices is a tad steep for the experience offered.

Marinara stands out as one of the top three pizza joints in the area, boasting fair prices for the quality of flavor on offer. The ingredients typically taste fresh, which is a significant plus for their menu selections. Beyond their pizza, the mozzarella sticks are noteworthy, and the Pepperoni wheel certainly deserves a mention for being moreish. However, inconsistency slightly tarnishes the experience; there are occasions where the pepperoni wheel disappointingly contains only a couple of slices of pepperoni. Despite this, the overall satisfaction is high, making it a recommended spot for a good slice. Solid 4/5 stars.

While staying at a hotel nearby I was looking for a place to get fried chicken for national friend chicken day. I noticed that the Melt Shop had a fried chicken melt so I decided to give it a try. I made the perfect choice to celebrate national fried chicken day. I had the best fried chicken sandwich ever! A perfectly cooked piece of fried chicken on toasted country white bread, with pepper jack cheese, red cabbage slaw, and melt sauce. The proportions of every ingredient were right on the money. I'm looking forward to going back and trying more of the menu next time I'm in NYC.

Title: A Portobello Masterpiece at Our Local Gem

I recently had the pleasure of indulging in the special portobello mushroom burger at a neighborhood favorite, and it was nothing short of spectacular. This hefty burger came adorned with juicy portobello mushrooms, caramelized onions, and a secret sauce that tied every bite together in a deliciously dangerous dance of flavors. It's a dish that I've raved about to friends, who have since sampled and attested to its addictive quality.

While my son has tried the basic burger and found it to be merely good -- not quite the pinnacle of burgerdom I proclaim the portobello to be -- it's clear that the magic truly lies in the unique portobello topping blend that elevates it to a five-star experience.

As if the burger wasn’t enough to keep us coming back, the fried pickles and fries also scored high on our list of tasty treats. To top off the convenience, they offer delivery, ensuring that the next craving for this mouthwatering burger can be satisfied from the comfort of home.

Title: A Lackluster Experience at Extended Happy Hour

I recently visited a restaurant for their extended happy hour and was left underwhelmed by the experience. While the prices were affordable, it is clear that you get what you pay for – and in this case, it wasn't much.

I had high hopes for the sushi, but both rolls I tried, the Twin Roll (3/5) and the Spicy Girl Roll (3.5/5), were just passable. The sushi, particularly the Salmon Toro (2/5) and King Salmon Nigiri (2/5), was tough and lacked freshness, making them impossible to enjoy. The pricing on the menu should have been a red flag; premium items like toro should command "market price," not a suspiciously low fixed cost.

The sole highlight of the meal was the Karaage Chicken, which deservedly earns a 4.5/5 for being the only dish that met my expectations. As for the Sparkling Sake (3/5), it reminded me more of Sprite than a refined beverage.

In conclusion, I left disappointed and with no intention of returning. The mediocre food simply does not justify another visit.

An update since my review 1year ago....Upland is still awesome, delicious and for dinner they hit the ball out of the park.You still need a reservation, but at 5:15pm it's certainly not as crowded.The four of us shared:-Crispy Duck Wings ($20) 3 to an order, adding 4thWe shared these entrees:-Bucatini Cacio e Pepe ($20)-Roasted Lamb Shoulder ($36)-Roasted Bronzino for Two ($72)For dessert:-Labneh Cheesecake ($14)-Apple pie sundae ($14)Not worth scoring each individually again because everything was 5 stars, just like the service.

Title: A Blissful Vegan Experience at XYST

Nestled in a cozy corner, XYST presents itself as a vegan haven, boasting a menu that tantalizes with its clean, healthful, and utterly delectable offerings. The moment you step into its quaint and inviting dining space, you feel the warmth of a homey embrace, with the option to sit at the bar enhancing the friendly, attentive service one receives.

The Muhammara, although straying from its traditional roots, emerges as a delightful twist on the classic—with roasted red pepper taking center stage over the usual walnut and pomegranate molasses. The surprising addition of grapes injects a playful burst of sweetness and texture. 

The artistry of the Smoked Hummus is not just in its taste but also its presentation, surrounded by a ring of pita and vibrant vegetable crudités. It's a feast for the eyes as much as the palate.

A standout is the Grilled Eggplant with smoked eggplant spread, serving as a hearty, smokey entree that leaves you satisfied yet eager for the next visit. The babaganoush further elevates the smokiness, creating a harmonious symphony of flavor.

Be warned: the generous portions of the appetizer spreads might well suffice, so consider diversifying with another less spread-focused appetizer.

Eagerly anticipating my next visit, XYST has set the bar high for vegan cuisine that doesn't just satisfy but also excites. It's a culinary gem that beckons you back for more.

This is my FAVORITE Italian restaurant in NYC!!! This place is such a gem. The restaurant itself is extremely homey and the staff is so kind. They have a wide range of pasta and any dish with seafood has a GENEROUS amount of seafood on it. I love coming here when I'm craving Italian food or if I'm looking for a nicer place to eat with friends visiting from out of town. I highly recommend !!!

Tucked away in an unsuspecting corner, Buddha Taco stood desolately during the usual lunchtime rush, which may raise eyebrows for potential diners. However, bustling with delivery orders, it appears the eatery does have a clientele, perhaps dissuaded from dining in by an ambiguous name that leaves the cuisine a bit of a mystery.

Opting to give it a chance, we sampled the cauliflower and baja tacos. The latter emitted a fishy odor that permeated the establishment, a less than appetizing welcome. Despite that, the culinary experience was a roller coaster, with the baja taco best avoided, while the cauliflower variant proved itself a satisfying choice. Their homemade chips were the highlight, boasting an addictive crunch that somewhat mitigated the sting of the somewhat overpriced, albeit tasty, guacamole.

In essence, Buddha Taco delivers a middling dining experience. While there's room for improvement, particularly if the fish tacos are revamped, this place has the potential for redemption through its solid offerings like the delectable chips. Whether or not Buddha Taco can allure the lunch crowd to its tables remains to be seen, but I'm rooting for their success.

By far the best sushi on the East Coast! Once I had Sugarfish, it ruined any other sushi restaurants for me. They do not take reservations, but you can order a drink (wine/beer/sake only) and sit upstairs in their lounge. Usually, we will put our name in and go down the street to a bar. When you are nearing the top of the list, the restaurant will text you so you know when to head back over. On a Saturday night, be prepared to wait 1-2 hours for your table- BUT do not let that turn you away...it's worth the wait! I typically order the trust me lite, and it's more than enough food for me. My husband usually orders a la carte. The chef recommends you to eat the food as soon as it comes out - especially anything with seaweed. My favorites on the trust me lite menu, are the albacore sushi and the toro hand roll. Usually my husband and I will order an extra toro roll to split, because it is that amazing and fresh. We are big sushi fans, and this is actually our favorite restaurant. The sushi is prepared perfectly and is extremely fresh.If you are wanting to try this restaurant but not willing to do the wait, one of the slowest times that I have seen is a Sunday afternoon during football season. We have gotten in several times with minimal wait (maybe 15 mins). Just to note- they will not seat you until your entire party has arrived.

This is my grandma's favorite Vietnamese restaurant in Chinatown. I came with my grandma and mom the other day; they each got a pork chop noodle soup ($9.25), I got a grilled chicken over cold vermicelli ($9.25), and we shared a small Vietnamese spring rolls ($6.25). Meat portions are very plentiful and everything is flavorful. The grilling is not very consistent; sometimes the meat needs to be grilled more. They also give a lot of noodles. The spring rolls were hot and crunchy. Service is very normal here, which is honestly a win for Chinatown establishments. Would come back!

This was my first time at one of David Chang's restaurants. I have seen Mind of a Chef, Ugly Delicious, and episodes of other shows with him and finally got around to trying his food. Finally got to taste the genius that is David Chang. The cocktails were unique, delicious and beautiful. We had monkey fizzness (gin, beets) and the matcha cocktail. Then came the buns...melt in your mouth pork belly bun, special egg and truffle bun, and chicken and caviar bun with creme fraiche. I was blown away by the chicken and caviar bun.I had to try the smokey pork ramen because the broth is prepared with Benton's hickory smoked bacon from Tennesee (the best tasting bacon I have ever eaten). I could drink this broth. It came with a big chunk of pork belly, bamboo, egg yolk and a nice textured noodle.We also tried the fermented chickpea and miso ice cream with rice krispies. Sounds weird but tasted like malted milk balls!Our server Stephen was attentive, friendly and knowledgeable. We arrived around 6:45pm and it was busy but still a few seats left. Overall one of my top overall restaurant experiences!

Title: A Mixed Bag of Surprises at Momofuku Noodle Bar in Time Warner Center

I returned to Momofuku Noodle Bar with a hint of reluctance, given its location in the bustling Time Warner Center, fearing a loss of charm that the East Village spot emanates. To my delight, the venue retained the unique David Chang flair, comfortably nestling itself amidst the commercial vibe.

We were seated promptly at the bar, although we soon discovered the charm of the rotating specials board wore thin quickly due to its distracting noise. Our bartender, while informative, teetered on the edge of intrusive with his frequent interjections.

The El Dragon cocktail, steep at $16, defied my watermelon skepticism, delivering a punch of flavor thanks to the dragoncello herb. Shishito Peppers, charred to perfection, met their match with a tangy romesco sauce – a painful inhale of pepper flake the only hiccup.

Celebrating the original Noodle Bar's 15th anniversary, the Chilled Spicy Noodles hit an off-the-charts heat level, the sauce stealthily cloaking the inferno about to ensue. The standout components, sausage and candied cashews, couldn't cool the fiery dish.

A saving grace, the Ginger Scallion Noodles introduced a refreshing, brothless take on ramen, accented by pickled shiitakes and cucumber – a dish that will likely lure me back for another visit.

The Passion Fruit Cheesecake, while competently made, failed to excite, and its diminutive size left our sweet tooth wanting.

Tallying up to $63 post-tax and split two ways, the Noodle Bar experience was an eclectic mix of hits and misses. While certain annoyances might deter some, the pull of those Ginger Scallion Noodles might be too strong to resist a future revisit.

I've long been eager to dine at Uncle Boons each time I'm in NYC, but snagging a reservation was like grasping at straws—both online and over the phone. On my last visit, we tried our luck walking in and after a 45-minute wait, we were in. The place may be small, but it's brimming with character—cozy and dimly lit, with an energetic, warm staff.

Our server was a standout, friendly and efficient amidst the bustling atmosphere. Onto the highlight: the food, which was simply unforgettable. The bone marrow with bread started us off with a rich, indulgent bang. Then came the snails—without exaggeration, the best I've had, better even than in France. Served in a zesty green chili Asian sauce, they were a revelation, especially when scooped up with the accompanying paratha. Rounding out the meal, the ceviche and noodles were both exemplary.

Uncle Boons left an indelible impression, and I'm already looking forward to my next meal there. It's a gem truly worth the wait.

Title: Quaint Spot with Hearty Burgers and Friendly Service

I stumbled upon this charming little restaurant, boasting just a handful of seats and an inviting counter space that we had all to ourselves—a pleasant surprise given its cozy capacity. The ambiance was warm, enhanced by the cook's friendliness and impressive ability to manage the entire show solo. Service was swift, making for a satisfying experience.

However, the burger presentation did give me pause. The bun, comically oversized, dwarfed the patty it was meant to complement. While the burger itself was flavorsome and benefited from fresh, abundant produce, the sauce was disappointingly bland and too runny, leading to a soggier-than-desired bun. My advice? Skip the sauce.

The accompanying onion rings were lackluster, lacking any memorable seasoning and paired with an indistinct sauce—possibly marinara— that didn't hit the mark for me.

Despite these hiccups, the menu's variety, from burgers to chicken options, warrants a return visit. Plus, their late hours are a definite bonus for any night owl with a burger craving.

Title: A Hidden Gem Serving Delightful Dip Soba

If you haven't tried dip soba yet, do yourself a favor and head to this remarkable spot. Their meri meri dip soba is a revelation – perfect for warding off the chill of winter. The broth is rich and hearty, requiring just a quick dip to impart its deep flavors into the perfectly cooked noodles.

Word to the wise: they don't accept reservations, so timing is key – early birds get the noodles! Locating the restaurant can be a mini-adventure since it's missing a marked awning, but the hunt is part of the charm.

Don't overlook the cucumber appetizer; it's a refreshing preamble to the main event. Plus, vegans and vegetarians have a place at the table with plant-based dip soba options.

In summary, this place is a find. It's not just a meal; it's an experience that calls for repeat visits. I know I'll be back.

I visited Beyond Sushi on a Thursday evening after coming across the restaurant on Yelp. I went with one other person, and although we didn't make a reservation, the restaurant wasn't packed so we were seated immediately. After skimming over the menu, I decided to go with an order of dumplings, the mighty mushroom roll, and the spicy mango roll. We were very hungry at the time so thankfully, the food came out in under ten minutes.I can't remember the name of the dumplings I ordered but it was the best thing that I ordered! If I were to visit again, it would solely be to get more dumplings. They were delicious and quite succulent, and I found myself quite sad when I finished them. I enjoyed the sushi, but I wouldn't go out of my way to come to this restaurant for sushi. I'm quite the sushi enthusiast, so I love all things sushi, but neither of my two rolls really did it for me. Yes, I enjoyed the food, but I feel like I could've made similar tasting rolls at home.Overall, this place is worth trying if you're in the area and have a deep craving for sushi, but I honestly wouldn't go out of my way to eat it, nor would I recommend it to others.

Lovely outdoor seating but it was raining so we sat indoors. Since it was a Monday, the happy hour was for all night. I tried most of the happy hour appetizers, but a lot of them were mediocre with maybe two hit items. Mini New England clam chowder $3 - I personally like it thicker so I wasn't a fan. Also it was crazy tiny like five spoonfuls tiny or even less lol. Cute but not worth.Salmon tartare $5 - I didn't touch it but my friends had a hard time finishing it because they didn't like it. Mini mermaid fish taco $5 for one - everyone in my party got one. Came with hard shell, It was ok, a little spicy. Crab and spinach dip $8 - came with packaged crackers which I thought was really odd because it didn't win me over presentation-wise. Unfortunately, the taste was just average. Not the best I've had but still able to finish it. Fried calamari $7.50 - you can almost never go wrong with calamari but the ones here were so bland. We had to season it with the salt and pepper shakers and only then did it taste better. Grilled shrimp and avocado $7.50 each- this was by far my favorite. It was soo tasty and flavorful. I actually didn't care about it - until I tried it. Hacienda cocktail - very fruity I would recommend. Lobster knuckles escargot style $15- this was from the regular appetizer menu. It came with toast to have with the lobster. But omg the toast was so burnt, couldn't have it with the lobster. There was complimentary dessert and fortune fish teller

Title: Unbeatable Lunch Deal at Sardine-Sized Gem

If you're on the hunt for an incredible lunch value, look no further than this bustling little spot where the prix fixe lunch menu is the star attraction. For just under $15, I savored a delightful Chicken Tikka Masala paired with the creamy Saag Paneer – a tough choice given the tantalizing options. You're also faced with the Sophie's choice between fragrant rice or a generous portion of pillowy naan – I say, why not splurge an extra $2 for the veggie samosa?

While the dishes arrived a tad cooler than expected, the flavors were on point – bold and satisfying. But let's talk about the papadum: these toasty, nutty, perfectly crisped pre-meal snacks were nothing short of addictive. Truly, don't skip on the 'pap.'

Be advised, the cozy quarters mean it's not ideal for large groups – takeout might be your best bet if you're rolling deep. However, the servers navigate the tight space with grace and utmost politeness.

In summary, if you're a fan of incredible deals and tasty Indian fare, this spot deserves a visit. Just remember, the lunch prix fixe is the real winner here.

I recently visited a nearby ramen spot, lured in by my boyfriend's claims of their ramen's acclaim. Eagerly, we ordered their premium bowl. At first glance, the presentation was underwhelming, but I held out hope that taste would triumph over aesthetics. However, I was met with disappointment. The broth was overwhelmingly salty and lacked the depth of flavor found in other ramen joints. Additionally, the scant two pieces of pork were thinly sliced, doing little to add substance. The noodles themselves were a letdown, with a mushy texture that did not justify the $15 price tag. Despite my best efforts, I couldn't finish my bowl, and my boyfriend graciously suggested I stop trying. While I'd like to give them the benefit of the doubt and consider a second chance, this visit was sadly forgettable.

Title: Tasty Falafel, Steep Prices

Rating: ★★★☆☆

The falafel platter at this joint is a flavorful yet pricy affair, costing around $14 for a meal that pales in portion to the more generous, budget-friendly street cart offerings. While the falafel itself is a delightful, crispy-on-the-outside, soft-on-the-inside treat, the accompanying mezze, consisting of a salad, some couscous, pickled veggies, and a pita, is merely average and does little to justify the steep cost.

Service for pickup orders tends to miss the mark timewise, though the staff is quick to expedite when you're physically present. Despite the shortcomings and pricing quibbles, the quality of the falafel might see me returning, largely due to the restaurant's convenient location—albeit with a grudge. If you're not nearby, don't bother making the trip.

Title: A Delightful Discovery at the New Noodle Nook

I recently dined at a new establishment that took over a beloved ramen spot, and I must say, it was a pleasant experience. Opting for the spicy miso ramen, I was treated to a delectable bowl with the perfect hint of heat — spicy, yet not overwhelming. However, the chicken served in the ramen did come across as dry. I'm optimistic, though, that this may have been an isolated issue and not indicative of their usual quality.

Taking advantage of their lunch special proved to be both economical and satisfying, even though it left me feeling quite stuffed. Despite the minor hiccup with the chicken, the overall meal was enjoyable, and I'm looking forward to returning to give them another chance to truly impress.

This place is awesome! The soba noodles are fantastic and super delicious and fulfilling. Be prepared to wait a bit as this place is very popular during peak hours! Highly recommend the tempura (get the large, trust me it's worth it)

I like this place a lot.  Came here for my Jinny's birthday. Combination of bbq and hotpot is $34.99 and just hotpot is $23.99. Perfect for cold weather. And service is great.    We had combo bbq and hotpot.  Bbq sticks were yummy and hotpot as well.  We will definitely come back. Oh if you celebrate birthday. Show your I'd, you get a discount.

Title: Lively Ambience but Unremarkable Fare at Hudson Yards

My visit to this buzzing restaurant in Hudson Yards was met with the expected Saturday afternoon hustle. I'd stress the importance of making reservations to avoid disappointment due to its popularity. Despite the raucous atmosphere at 3:45 PM, the service managed to be attentive and prompt.

The sangria I started with was a highlight, hitting all the right fruit-infused notes. As for the tapas, the SELECCIÓN DE QUESOS paired with fig jelly was pleasant though not memorable. Similarly, the pan con tomate was a decent rendition of the classic, yet it failed to leave a lasting impression. 

It was the churros that stole the show, ending the meal on a sweet and satisfying note. Nevertheless, given the vast culinary options available in the area, I would likely explore other dining venues at Hudson Yards on my next visit rather than returning.

Come here for roast pork. This deal is so cheap. Roast pork + rice + cabbage all for like 5 bucks. What???The roast pork is really tender and fatty with just enough sauce. It's nothing sticky and is a little more subtle and they drip a lot of sauce in your container so if you wanted it more saucy, you can.Also got the roast duck. That was nothing special and I wouldn't get that again.

I recently visited this restaurant for my 25th birthday celebration with friends. Despite their somewhat odd reservation policy (which required a potentially steep no-show fee), the experience was worth the hassle. We had a bit of a hiccup initially as we arrived to a just-opened and seemingly disorganized venue, compounded by a rather rude hostess. 

Thankfully, the atmosphere quickly made up for the rocky start. The food and drinks were both delightful and reasonably priced. The in-house DJ provided an energetic vibe that truly brought the brunch to life, reminiscent of the famed Woodland brunch scene.

This is definitely a hotspot if you're looking to celebrate a special occasion like a birthday, but keep in mind that space is limited—so those festive balloons may have to stay behind. A word to the wise: the restaurant could improve the experience by managing reservations more efficiently, fine-tuning their organization, and training a friendlier front-of-house staff.

Title: Disappointing Hype at Saltbae Burger

My visit to Saltbae Burger was a letdown. The restaurant had an air of "upscale trashy" with an odd imbalance of too many staff members and too few patrons. Service was slow off the mark, and once we got the menus, there was an unexpected perk: the veggie burger was complimentary for all guests, a welcome change from a previous ladies-only offer.

Yet, the experience nosedived from there. The server seemed more interested in up-selling a $4.50 bottle of Voss water than providing good service. We stuck to the free veggie burger that was accompanied by fries and black gloves – presumably for a clean-handed Salt Bae impersonation.

Eating a burger with gloves on was peculiar, though it did keep the grease at bay. The burger itself was lackluster, with the patty dwarfing the bun and a single piece of wilted lettuce doing little to excite. The fries were the meal's saving grace.

Overall, if you're considering Saltbae Burger for the hype, it's best to reconsider and spend your money elsewhere.

Title: A Mixed Bag at By Chloe's New Lex Location

I recently visited the new By Chloe on Lexington, eager to include their fast casual, vegan options into my lunch routine. As a non-vegan who enjoys their Guac Burger and Quinoa Taco Salad, I had high expectations based on my experiences at their other venues.

This Lex spot is notably smaller than the one at Rockefeller, tucked behind Hale & Hearty, with no seating options and operating as a card-only establishment. The setup features several self-service kiosks and a large pick-up shelf for mobile orders.

I give this location a solid 3.5 stars. The Guac Burger stayed true to its tasty reputation, but the air-baked fries were a letdown—best to avoid unless lukewarm, overcooked potatoes are your thing. Service was slower than anticipated, which was surprising given the number of staff present, especially with a crowd waiting.

Overall, despite some hiccups, By Chloe is definitely worth a try for those looking to explore comforting vegan cuisine. Just remember to order ahead to save time.

This was my first time here at this restaurant and overall I would say that it was a pretty decent experience. If it was possible I would've rated this experience a 3.72. So technically  it was closer to four stars than three stars.  We were seated pretty quickly. The aura in the spot was very chill and serene.  It's the perfect date spot for you and your partner to stop by on a nice Friday night.  Nice and cozy with dim lights. The drink was amazing as well. However, when it comes to the food when comparing to other Thai food places it isn't quite as good. It's very possible that I would also just choose something that was not as great ! This is also pretty common with vegetarian options. The portion size was definitely worth it.

I'm rating this restaurant 3 stars as my expectations for the grilled meat fell short. It lacked the charred quality I was anticipating and appeared to be broiled, suggesting the grill wasn't adequately heated. While I've had superior Korean BBQ experiences elsewhere, my friends who ordered hotpot were pleased with their choice.

Churutto proves to be a delightful destination for ramen connoisseurs, offering an affordable culinary adventure. Nestled in a chic setting with warm wooden furnishings and tasteful decor, this eatery strikes a perfect balance between casual dining and refined atmosphere. The service is commendable, with staff members exuding friendliness and efficiency.

The ramen selection, although succinct, provides ample variety to cater to different palates. I indulged in the spicy ramen, which was a fiery treat, while my companions savored the classic variations. Each bowl was a harmonious blend of savory broth, perfectly chewy noodles, a succulent runny half-boiled egg, and delectable char siu. With prices ranging from $11 to $16, Churutto stands out as a go-to spot for those seeking a delectable ramen experience without breaking the bank. Cozy and stylish, Churutto is undoubtedly a must-visit for a satisfying meal.

Wanted to like Nakamura more; I found the food to be good rather than great. They were out of one of the appetizers we wanted so we started with the Matsutake tempura instead, which was my favorite thing we ate. Mapo tofu and gyoza followed, both tasty. I had the Torigaro ramen and it was decent. Overall I didn't think there was anything that sets this ramen spot aside from others. 3.5 stars.

I recently visited a spot that served up some delectable sheng jian baos – an absolute must-try! Perfectly crisp on the bottom with delightfully fluffy sides, these pan-fried buns were bursting with hot, juicy meat. They were so good, I almost preferred them to the soup dumplings, which is saying something.

Speaking of soup dumplings, while they used to be my favorite, another place in Queens has since eclipsed them. Regardless, these still rank in my Top 10, easily second-best in the neighborhood, next to Noodle Village. The wrapper is commendably thin, though a bit more broth wouldn't hurt.

The noodle soup with pork chop was a miss for me; the broth lacked depth of flavor and the noodles had an unusual starchy texture I didn't care for. Additionally, the pork chop was disappointingly dry.

As for the pork and bean curd soup, despite not recalling the exact name, it stood out with its rich, satisfying taste – a real comfort food hit.

In summary, a mixed bag, but the sheng jian baos and certain soups are definitely worth a visit.

Good taste but too expensive for a "taco". The roti ones are about $5 while the naan ones are about $10. If you're eating this for an actual meal you cant get full from just one of these.. you need to order at least 2 or even 3 if you're getting the roti ones. That's $15-30 total which is way too much for a quick casual lunch. I got the lamb curry roti. It's literally just curry on top of a roti... i wish it was more of a fusion of Indian and traditional taco flavors. The actual flavor of the curry was great.. I liked how they added chutney on top. I'm not sure if I'd go back.. seems more catered to non-Indian population.

I am rating this place higher mainly because of the interior. And their margaritas. Everything else was questionable. I was starstruck walking in to the beautiful decor they had decorated for Christmas. It shows how much they care about the ambiance and keeping things seasonal! For a dinner at 6PM on a weekend, the place was packed. Luckily, they had a "waiting lounge" at the back, where we chilled. It would have been nice, if we weren't chilling there for around a hour. When we were finally seated, we ordered 3 orders of Tacos (Chicken, Fish, Al Pastor) for around $15-16 each. We also had Guac and Chips ($8), Steak Quesadilla ($16) and their $5 Frozen Margaritas. I regret ordering so many tacos without knowing if they were good. Their tacos were actually the kind I don't like, with two tough grainy shells each taco. There also wasn't too much filling. The Chicken was dry, and the Fish was too bland. I guess you can say Al Pastor was the best out of the 3 but it wasn't that great tasting either. The Quesadilla was bomb though. Luckily, it was conveniently cut into 3 slices for our party of 3. The steak was chewy and tasted amazing with the cheese and sauces. The Margaritas saved the show for me. Not only were they just $5 but they were delicious! I had the Mango was it tasted just like how I imagined it to be. Strong yet mango flavor! I would go back for the beautiful decor and margaritas!

Title: A Gem for Generous Portions and Friendly Service

I recently visited a local eatery that nailed the dining experience with flying colors. From the moment we entered, a mere half hour before closing time, the hospitality was palpable. The man at the counter greeted us with a warm smile and outstanding service, going the extra mile to accommodate special requests like adding chickpea salad to our already sealed bowls.

Speaking of the food, we chose the 'create your own bowls' option, generously topped with extra tzatziki, and a side of pita chips with a delightful dip – all for a very reasonable $30. The portions were incredibly hearty; each bowl was so packed it felt like lifting a brick – a true testament to their generosity.

The ambiance of the restaurant was pleasant, with ample seating, self-service soda fountains, and convenient grab n' go selections for those in a rush. Their commitment to customer satisfaction shone brightly, ensuring that this won't be my last visit. In fact, I'm already looking forward to my next bowl from this fantastic establishment. Highly recommended for anyone with a hearty appetite and a preference for courteous service.

Title: A Cozy Culinary Gem in the Heart of New York

As frequent visitors to NYC with family in the city, we've found our go-to spot just a stone's throw away from their place. The establishment is a bustling hub of deliciousness that miraculously seems to always have a table for us, even during peak hours.

Making a selection from their extensive menu is a delightful challenge, with each dish more tempting than the last. The chicken with smashed potatoes and a zesty lemon aioli is my personal favorite—nothing short of AMAZING. But the fish and chips? They're a close contender and absolutely do not disappoint.

On Sunday evenings, the restaurant transforms with Music Trivia night—a surprisingly captivating event that'll have you hooked. With a few drinks, some collaborative brainpower, and a colossal ice cream sundae to sweeten the deal, you're in for a memorable night. We landed in third place, but the fun was definitely in the journey.

This place boasts a welcoming ambiance, a well-stocked bar, and a menu that keeps on giving. It's the perfect spot for a guaranteed good meal, particularly on a Sunday. Can't wait to come back!

I am usually not a huge fan of ramen, but this restaurant has converted me into a ramen lover! I have been here twice and both times have been great. The service is quick and very efficient.  Not only is their food great, but I highly recommend their happy hour! From 5:30-7 on weekdays, they have half priced drinks and most of their appetizers are on a happy hour price. We got edamame for $4 and I had an alcoholic drink for only $2.50! Honestly the best happy hour I have found in midtown yet.The shrimp ramen was super flavorful. You can get it with wavy or straight noodles and I personally loved the wavy noodles. It was not super spicy and overall a delicious and filling meal. If you're looking for good and affordable ramen in the city, check this place out!
Thought the menu looked good and love the bar setting, but food was very mediocre. I feel like there's many more better options at Chelsea Market.

I popped in here by myself before catching a show on Broadway and I am so glad I did. The food here was TO DIE FOR. The atmosphere is very casual, which was perfect for me, but if you have a party larger than two, then this might not be the place for you as most of the seating is "bar seating" style. The noodles are absolutely perfect and the meat is so tender. I love the balance of spices and the prices are fantastic. Next time I'm in NY, I'll definitely be stopping in here!

Title: Solid Eats and Treats for Dinner and Brunch

My experiences dining at this spot for both dinner and brunch have been quite enjoyable, albeit with a few hiccups. For any weekend diners, be prepared for a bit of a wait during dinner time; my dining partner and I endured a 25-minute queue for a cozy table for two. On the flip side, our brunch visit at 1 PM on a Sunday was delightfully prompt, with no waiting involved.

The dinner menu, though slightly pricey, offers a decent range of affordable choices. Their signature margaritas are enormous and can be easily shared—so consider halving one with a companion. When it comes to appetizers, the nachos can't be missed; they're generously topped with extra melty cheese and delectable chorizo. The guacamole, prepared fresh to order, adds a perfect touch.

While the service may lag a tad during the busier evening hours, dining al fresco is a pleasant experience thanks to their ample outdoor seating. Transitioning to their brunch offering, the value is commendable: two cocktails paired with an entrée. Despite the brunch menu's limited selection, there's enough to satisfy. I tried the breakfast bowl, which essentially felt like a Chipotle bowl but with the welcome addition of eggs—though it could have benefited from more eggs and less lettuce. Each brunch dish is accompanied by sweet potato hash, which is a nice complement.

The cocktail options included in the brunch deal are varied and pleasing to the palate. Overall, while there's room for improvement in the service speed and balance of ingredients, the dining experience here is quite solid, especially if you're able to enjoy their outdoor space.

The best part is the shrimp with head-on! Oh yea! Gimme all you got! So ok, I went downtown to meet my old supervisor and a friend who worked at the same office many years ago (across from the World Trade Center). She gave me a few suggestions and we picked this one. The manager (or he could be the owner) was a friendly gentleman who likes to joke, also a nice fellow.Juliana was our waitress. She's friendly and attentive. We ordered calamari to share. The calamari app includes some fish. Then I had the black linguini with shrimp. My friend had salmon special and that looked super neat and fresh. My dish was unbelievable! The shrimp came with the heads on. I'm glad they didn't cut the head because I like the head. Did I mention that I eat fish head a lot too? Most people want to know the secret of my good memory. Fish head! That's the answer! You'll be thanking me for the rest of your life for making you remember everything that you try to forget! My pasta was delicious, I won't forget that. The sauce was very good. My friend liked her salmon dish. She said she's been here before and liked the food the last time she was here too. Good to know they're consistent. We both finished our meals. The restaurant's pretty big with a high ceiling and we sat by the booth. I got a pretty good view of the whole restaurant. I definitely enjoyed dining here. I hope you do too!

Title: A Stellar Encore at a NYC Gem

On our final evening in the Big Apple, we returned to a beloved spot and it did not disappoint. Despite the quiet ambiance caused by the pandemic, the quality of food and service remained top-notch. Our server was attentive, enhancing an already enjoyable experience.

Beer enthusiasts will rejoice at their selection—particularly IPA lovers like us who reveled in the unique options not found back home. The food was exceptional, with the octopus and potato croquettes being so delectable we ordered seconds. The cheese board, Brussels sprouts, and mushroom flatbread all deserve praise for their flavor.

Beyond the culinary delights, the staff's consideration was noteworthy; a prompt call about a forgotten item by one of my children showcased their exceptional care.

This place is a testament to NYC's resilient spirit. Amazing people, food, and atmosphere make it a must-visit establishment.

There's really not much to say about pizza other than if it's good or not. And I can attest - this place is GOOD. If you're into vodka pizza and/or square pizza, this is the place for you. The vodka square pizza is amazing. It has glorious crust (gooey on the inside, crispy on the outside) and of course amazing sauce with a great ratio of sauce to crust (see pic for proof). The pizza is sold by the personal pie or very large slice depending on how you look at it. The personal pie is $10 and can be cut into four slices. If you're super hungry you could probably eat the entire thing by yourself. If you're just normal hungry, I'd recommend splitting this.

Solid spot for ramen in Midtown. We came around 9 PM on a Sunday night and were seated almost immediately. The booths are for parties of 3 or more so expect bar seating if you're a party of 2. The service was quick and the food was pretty good.I had the Spicy Tan Tan (they can remove the ground pork) and my boyfriend ordered the Tonkotsu ramen. I thought that the Spicy Tan Tan was unique because it tasted more like khao soi (Thai curry with noodles) than your typical ramen. The Tonkotsu was good but not as rich as I would have liked. They have a wide range of condiments to help flavor your ramen. As for service, after ordering, the food surprisingly came out in like 5 minutes. Since we were at the bar, our water was constantly being refilled.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at an Indian restaurant in NY, and I must say, it truly surpassed all my expectations. From the attentive and exceptional service of the wait staff to the exquisite flavors of the dishes, everything was remarkable.

During my first visit with my sister and friends, we indulged in the lamb roganjosh, tandoori chicken paired with haricot verts, and the butter chicken.
