Each dish was a burst of authentic, well-crafted flavors that even made the plain rice seem extraordinary. But the highlight was undoubtedly the dessert - a rum ball so delectable that it deserves a special mention.

On my second visit, I opted for the gajar halwa and was once again astonished by the culinary excellence. The richness and depth of taste in that traditional dessert left my mind truly blown.

If you find yourself craving for Indian cuisine, this is the place to go. I cannot recommend this restaurant enough; it is evidently a jewel within NY's dining scene.

Tucked away near the campus, this restaurant is a gem for a Sunday brunch scene. It boasts a beautiful setting conducive to a relaxed meal. The prices are quite reasonable, making it accessible without compromising on quality. To ensure a seamless experience, I highly recommend making a reservation to bypass any potential wait time. Overall, an excellent choice for weekend dining.

Welcome to the upper west side, Pizza Collective! It's no easy feat to open in the middle of a pandemic, but if you are properly equipped with PPE (none of that mask halfway down nonsense) and around the area, come grab a slice!I was quite happy with my mushroom slice, the olive oil flavor is strong and the mushrooms are delicious. The crust is a little thicker than the slices I've had in Rome (mm La Renella in Trastevere), with big air bubbles and edges so crisp you hear a satisfying crunch on each bite. I love crispy things, so getting the corner slice was a plus!

Typical old school NYC diner that gets the job done. Located steps away from Penn Station if you are looking to sit down for a bite before catching a train and don't want to be subjected to the fast food crap located there.Always a pleasure to be able to order up hot breakfast foods later in the evening after working late. Service was fast and friendly. Food came out hot and just as ordered. Having the choice to get sweet potato fries with my omelet was very nice indeed. The place is clean and well organized. Fairly priced. Nothing to rave about or wow you, but it feels cozy and homey. A-OK by me. I'd go back again if in the area and craving a late night breakfast.

Title: A Refreshing Change of Pace at The Smith

I recently veered from my go-to Mac n' cheese and brunch offerings at The Smith, second ave location, to explore their dinner options – quite a delight! Opting for the pot of mussels partnered with the "oysters of the day" (likely from Cape Cod), I was impressed by the sheer freshness of the seafood. Each mussel, so succulent, had me reaching for more until I hit the 40 mark!

The side of French fries didn't disappoint either – perfectly crispy and flavorful. Despite the bustling crowd, the service at The Smith was top-notch; my dishes arrived promptly, leaving no room for impatience. This experience has elevated the second ave location to a frontrunner among my favorite Smith spots.

Title: A Gastronomic Delight During Restaurant Week

I recently dined at an exceptional spot during Restaurant Week 2019 and was blown away by the dinner offerings. The appetizer of beef tartare accompanied by bone marrow glazed with miso was simply out of this world, easily earning a spot on my list of top dishes ever. My friend was equally impressed with their tender and delectably sauced roasted duck breast.

For the main course, my uni risotto with truffle was a winner, marrying two of my favorite flavors into a rich and fulfilling experience. Meanwhile, my friend enjoyed the variety in the omakase selection, featuring four pieces each of sushi and sashimi, all beautifully curated with distinct tastes.

Dessert was a matcha cheesecake; it was pleasant, though not quite as standout as the previous courses. Given the excellence of each dish, I'm tempted to make this spot a regular haunt, though the special $42 Restaurant Week price point is particularly alluring.

Service topped off the experience, with servers demonstrating both attentive and friendly qualities. Not to be overlooked, the umeshu mojito was a delightful blend of sweet umeshu and mint, adding a unique touch to the meal.

Count me in for next year's Restaurant Week – it's an amazing deal for such high-quality fare.

Title: A Stellar Dining Experience to Remember

I ventured into this restaurant for the first time yesterday and was immediately taken with the beautiful decor and the warm ambiance that greeted me. The service was nothing short of exceptional, with servers who were genuinely nice and attentive.

Visiting during restaurant week, I was eager to try what this place had to offer, and it surpassed my expectations. Celebrating my friend's upcoming graduation, we indulged in a feast that included steak tartare, a classic Caesar salad, a succulent 10 oz filet mignon, and a flavorful 12 oz hanger steak. Both steaks were cooked to medium rare perfection, making the filet mignon one of the best I've had in New York.

The side dishes, mac & cheese, and creamed spinach, were equally delightful, complementing the main courses nicely. We topped off our meal with some homemade tiramisu and New York cheesecake, which were the perfect endnotes to our celebration.

The restaurant wasn't crowded, which added to the relaxed experience. This place has certainly made an impression on me, and I am keen to return. If you're looking for a top-notch steakhouse experience, look no further—this establishment is a must-visit.

Overall a really great experience food and service wise. My friends and I (a party of 3) got here around 9:10pm and it was packed. We were quoted on the wait list for about 20 minutes. After we got the text to come back to the restaurant, we still had to wait 15 minutes for people to clear their check and clean the table. We ended up getting seated at the bar. My friends and I ordered the Tonkotsu Jiro Ramen, Tonkotsu Chashu Jiro Ramen, and the Tonkotsu Tusukemen. I asked for the Tusukemen to be spicy which I shouldn't have; not because it was too spicy, but the spice ended up ruining the flavor of the broth. The broth is actually amazing here. It's not watery and there is a body to it. Also very garlicky. The Chashu was cooked great and wasn't too fat. The portions are very filling. Considering the tsukemen is $14 and you leave with a full stomach, that's a steal in terms of Manhattan prices. My only complaint would be the lack of staff here (or maybe someone called out that night). As a former waitress it hurts me to see one guy breaking his back trying to take orders and bus like 7 tables at once.

During my recent visit to the restaurant, I ordered the chicken rice which, unfortunately, fell short of expectations. The dish was mostly rice with a noticeably scant portion of chicken, a significant change from previous visits where the balance was more satisfactory. Additionally, the accompaniment consisted solely of lettuce which had an unusual pink hue. The quality has evidently declined, and I was left disappointed by the dish's composition and presentation.

Title: BONDST: Style Over Substance?

TLDR: BONDST, an upscale Japanese restaurant in NoHo, certainly impresses with its stunning decor and is a prime spot to wow a guest or client. However, the culinary experience may not justify the steep prices for some. A bit reminiscent of Tao or Nobu's chic but somewhat pretentious vibe.

During my long-anticipated visit, the menu prices were a slight shock—$9 for miso soup seemed steep. I indulged in the Big Eye Tuna Tarts, an appetizer that truly shined with its delicate balance of truffle and perfectly cut tuna on a razor-thin tart; a highlight I'd return for.

The sushi, adorned with luxurious ingredients as expected, was part of the chef's omakase. Although it was finely prepared, nothing particularly wowed me. It felt like an experience geared more towards the aesthetics of dining rather than an authentic culinary journey.

Bottom line: If you're after a standout omakase or celebrating a special occasion, other venues might offer more bang for your buck. BONDST seems better suited for occasions that call for impressive visuals and ambiance over an exceptional food adventure.

This is a pretty unique taco joint... #POSITIVEVIBES The space is very fun and inviting - it's large and has a classy, relaxing, tropical vibe going on with cool pink lighting and wicker decor. I did not expect to see a place like this in the Theater District! It felt so beachy even though it was the middle of December. I almost felt like I was at a resort. There are a handful of Taco Dumbo locations throughout the city but I'm not sure if they all have this type of decor. My friend and I stumbled in here on Christmas Eve en route to Rockefeller Center. We sat at the bar and each ordered the combo deal which includes two tacos and a side. Even though there were not many people sitting at the bar, the service was slow. The slow bar service was the only downside to this cool joint - the staff was friendly, the drinks were strong, restaurant was clean, the food came out quickly and was delicious at a reasonable price. I ordered the Rotisserie Chicken Tinga Taco and Truffled Shroom on Crunchy Shell with guac and chips and my friend got the Beef Short Rib and Rotisserie Chicken Tinga with the street corn. Definitely recommend the chicken and beef short rib. Also there was a big difference between the quantity you get for guac and chips versus corn, I got way more food with the guac and chips than my friend did with the corn. There were also some cool tunes playing. My favorite  part was definitely the ambience. I would come back here for a quick bite!

This is a very popular place filled with Asians so you can tell the food is quite legit and authentic. The chicken dishes (Satay Chicken & Hainanese Chicken) were especially nice - very tender and juicy!! Definitely the place to be if you're craving for Malaysian food!

I had a fantastic lunch experience at this Chipotle-style eatery! Arriving post-lunch rush meant a relaxed atmosphere without the crowds. The customizable bowl concept here truly elevates the game - it's a cut above the rest. Fresh, healthy ingredients made for a deliciously satisfying meal. Count me in as a return customer!

Title: Navigating the Seas of Flavor at Capt Loui

I recently revisited the restaurant formerly known as Loui Loui, now rebranded as Capt Loui, and I'm pleased to report a delightful turnaround. The happy hour menu is particularly impressive, offering tantalizing appetizers like the crispy fried calamari and well-seasoned cajun fries. Although they were served with just ketchup, lacking any special dipping sauces, the quality spoke for itself. The to-go fried shrimp also did not disappoint, although it's worth noting the happy hour portions are smaller than the regular servings.

The atmosphere at Capt Loui has been enlivened by the addition of a liquor license, enhancing the dining experience with an excellent selection of drinks. However, not all dishes cast the same spell upon me— the garlic noodles continue to disappoint, resembling plain thin spaghetti rather than a garlicky delight.

While the corn and potato sides were flavorful, the portion size left something to be desired, especially considering the prices. It's a slight improvement from the past, but their sauce, though better, hasn't completely won me over.

Despite a few missteps, Capt Loui has charted its way into my top 10 local spots for a convivial atmosphere and delectable seafood. Its proximity is an added bonus, making it a convenient choice for a casual outing.

Title: "Unremarkable Evening at a Modest Eatery"

My recent dining experience was a textbook example of an average evening out. The service provided was efficient, with a notably attentive waiter whose name escaped me, yet his eagerness to please was evident. The ambiance was understated, fostering a tranquil environment, though it failed to leave a lasting impression.

The meal commenced with a Caesar Salad that was rather uninspiring – a sparse array of lettuce and cheese lightly tossed in a dressing that could have benefitted from a bit more zest. Moving on to the main course, the seafood stew boasted a quartet each of shrimp, mussels, and clams, but was dominated by an excessive helping of calamari swimming in what was an unfortunately insipid tomato purée. The flounder, however, served in a delicate lemon sauce, was the highlight of the dinner, meriting a solid 3.5 out of 5.

Dessert was a Crème Brûlée that managed to match the flounder's score, but even that sweet note wasn't enticing enough to ensure a return visit. All in all, I'm left with little impetus to revisit.

Great pizza !We really liked the pizza here although they offered a lot more.  The pizza was in a wood fires grill.  Nice.  Lots of sports on if you are in to that.  The margarita pizza was especially good.  Pretty quick too because we were on the clock.  We would come here again.

Took my dad here the other night and had an incredible experience. Both the host, Jose, and our server were incredibly welcoming and helpful. we started with the tomato-burrata tart, which was wonderfully crispy and was the perfect balance of tangy and creamy. My dad ordered the Sunday special Sole Muniere, and was blown away. I got the crispy salmon and paired with sautéed spinach, I was also impressed. We also tried the tuna tartare (highly recommended) and the risotto was incredible too. For dessert, we got the chocolate cake and OH MY GOODNESS YUM. We'll be back again soon!

This is like an Epcot Center food court in Manhattan. By which I mean, highest quality authentic food in a beautifully thought-out but ultimately upscale theme park setting.You can tell a lot of money was invested in this food court. The food is displayed beautifully to make your mouth water. It's almost like a VR ad experience of the foods of Spain.When we came on a Friday night around 8pm it was insanely crowded. It seemed like every Spanish tourist in NYC was here. Plus every other tourist. And everyone on a tinder date.My friend and I spend a few minutes browsing the shelves and making fun of how high the prices were. In truth, a few thing were affordable and others laughably expensive. You could really drop some serious cash and impress your date at the wine bar.I was hungry, but overwhelmed by the choices and the lines. We ended up sharing a huge sandwich that had fried chicken and mayo. It was named after a football(soccer) team I think. It was delicious and very unhealthy.Then we had a dessert topped with pork bits. That's how Spanish people roll. Sorry my vegan friends. We just had to try it and it was delicious, too.

Title: A Brunch Haven on the Upper West Side

I recently visited a spacious brunch spot on the Upper West Side, keen to dive into their extensive selection of morning favorites. What caught my eye was the breakfast pot pie ($19) – a creative twist marrying my love for breakfast fares and the comfort of pot pies. It was an intriguing dish, topped with two perfectly sunny side up eggs that added a delightful creaminess to each mouthful. Breaking through the biscuit crust, I was immersed in a pool of gravy, sausage, bacon, and potatoes that was so flavorful, I scarcely remembered to pause for a sip of water.

Despite the delectable flavors, I found the pot pie's interior a tad too soup-like compared to the hearty filling of a traditional chicken pot pie, reflecting in my four-star rating. Nonetheless, the overall dining experience was exceptional. On a busy Sunday post-church rush, our party of three was promptly seated—outdoors on a beautiful Spring day, no less—with the bonus of complimentary sparkling water. Prices were reasonable, with dishes under $20 including a variety of eggs, waffles, pancakes, and sandwiches.

While I'd suggest opting for something other than the breakfast pot pie if you're after a classic potpie experience, this Upper West Side gem still comes highly recommended for a delightful brunch outing.

My husband and I celebrated a special occasion at Gabriel Kreuther when it boasted one Michelin star, marking my inaugural journey into the Michelin dining experience. Opting for the comprehensive 13-course tasting menu, this establishment provided an unforgettable introduction that I wholeheartedly recommend.

We arrived an hour before our reservation, and given the absence of a crowd, were promptly seated, welcomed by excellent service and a serene atmosphere. While the price point was steep, meriting a four-star rating, the culinary offerings were nothing short of incredible.

The essence of French cuisine came alive with each sauce-laden course, leading me to a newfound appreciation for the art of plating. I realized that aesthetic presentation significantly enhances the dining experience by enticing the palate visually.

Notable highlights included the hamachi intertwined with black truffle and foie gras pate, a harmonious blend of French and Japanese mastery, and a scallop dish that embodied the freshness of spring. We did find the two dessert courses overwhelming after such an extensive meal but enjoyed every other dish.

If your palate leans towards French and Japanese flavors, Gabriel Kreuther is a destination worth traveling for. A resounding culinary triumph, this restaurant skillfully bridges taste and presentation, leaving you with an enriched appreciation for fine dining.

Title: A Showstopper Meal at Ellen's

If you're looking for a side of pizzazz with your dinner, Ellen's in New York delivers with a standing ovation. Despite our large party of 17, we only waited 30 minutes for seating—a pleasant surprise. The menu boasts a plentiful selection, satisfying everyone with its quality.

But the real star of Ellen's is undoubtedly the singing waitstaff. These talented individuals serve up your favorite show tunes and current chart-toppers with passion and flair. Don't be startled if your server takes a brief interlude for a solo performance—they'll seamlessly transition back to refilling your water glass without missing a beat.

Ellen's offers a unique combo of delightful eats and engaging entertainment, making for an unforgettable dining experience. Whether you're a Broadway aficionado or just in for the novelty, this place is a hit.

Ate here a few nights ago with my roommate. We used a pulsd gift certificate for my birthday. We ordered 4 tapas items and a bottle of wine off a limited menu. The food is delicious! One drawback is that they didn't realize we were there for the limited menu at first and gave us the full menu. I saw a few things on there I would've loved to try. All in all, delicious meal, we ordered filet mignon and tuna tataki, 2 rolls and chicken and shrimp dumplings. The filet mignon literally melts in your mouth. Modern interior as well, definitely a good date spot.

I revisited this charming restaurant for the second time in two weeks, a testament to its allure. The lobster tartlet was a delight, but the standout dish was undoubtedly the chicken waffle. Tender and juicy, the chicken paired with a perfectly cooked sunny side up egg was a combination that exceeded my expectations. I strongly recommend giving this dish a try - it’s a clear winner on the menu!

After discovering this gem on YouTube, the anticipation was high, and thankfully, it did not disappoint. The tuna sashimi was a revelation, boasting incredible flavors paired exquisitely with pear. The bibimbap followed suit, impressing with perfectly sautéed, flavorful vegetables. However, the star of the show was the visually stunning sesame ice cream dessert, a masterful blend of flavors that even included dried strawberries, a particular hit with my wife. This place is undoubtedly recommendable for a memorable culinary experience!

I recently visited Sweet Chicks for brunch and had a delightful experience. Following online recommendations, I arrived at opening time (10:30am) and was seated without delay. The tantalizing aroma set high expectations right away.

Service was a highlight – the staff were quick and attentive, effortlessly managing the early crowd. My choice, a bacon, egg, and cheese biscuit with home fries and a side of Carolina cheese grits, did not disappoint. The sandwich maintained its integrity bite after delicious bite, and the home fries boasted a perfect crispness that needed no extra seasoning. The grits were thick and cheesy, precisely how I prefer them.

Overall, Sweet Chicks provided a leisurely and satisfying brunch. My advice? Get there early to fully savor your meal without any rush.

Title: Perfect Pre-Show Dining with Happy Hour Perks

My experience at this restaurant was a delightful prelude to an evening show. The ambiance was immediately welcoming with tasteful decor that set a pleasant tone for our early dinner.

The staff earns praise for their affable nature, contributing to the overall warm atmosphere. An added bonus was the happy hour special, available from 4-7pm, offering a chance to enjoy discounted treats.

Our appetizers, shishito peppers and gyoza, were hits at the table. The peppers packed a flavorful punch, although they were a tad oilier than preferred. Moving on to main courses, the Hot udon with shrimp tempura was a standout, boasting a clear, savory broth that complemented the crispy tempura perfectly.

The Samurai ramen, with its rich tonkotsu broth, was heavier and oilier but still managed to be satisfying. It’s important to note that the ramen deviated from traditional Japanese styles, featuring noodles that were softer and longer cooked than the expected curvy wavy variety. While not the classic ramen texture, it was nonetheless comforting and fulfilled a craving for a hearty bowl of noodles.

In summary, for those looking to indulge in a satisfying meal before catching a show, this restaurant hits the mark with its friendly service, enjoyable happy hour, and a menu that's sure to cater to your pre-theater appetite.

I recently celebrated a friend's promotion at a fantastic restaurant that proved to be perfect for our group of eight. Our waiter, Erin (or Aron?), showed remarkable patience and helpfulness throughout our meal. We were comfortably seated at a series of connected tables near the entrance.

The meal kicked off with drinks and freshly baked, hot bread salted to perfection, paired with olive oil for dipping. I indulged in the spaghetti noir – an intriguing dish blackened by squid ink and enlivened with bread crumbs, red peppers, crab, and a hint of lemon. The sauce was an excellent balance of sweet and savory, truly enhancing the fresh crab within.

Another standout was the risotto, a creamy delight infused with squash and topped with pine nuts, which our vegetarian companion thoroughly enjoyed. They were also impressed with the lemon custard dessert, and I noted that dairy-free sorbet options were available.

The baked chicken was a masterclass in texture – crispy on the outside while remaining succulent inside. The restaurant's ambiance added to the experience, with warm lighting and a charming terra-cotta theme that even extended to the restrooms. This place left a mark on me, and I'm eager to return.

Great place in Greenwich village for some Chinese dishes. The food was excellent and not overly priced. My lovely date had the Spicy cauliflower with pork belly. I had the tea smoked duck. The soup dumplings we had were average. The spicy cauliflower was very good and it goes well with white rice but it didn't have as much pork belly as advertised. My tea smoked duck is definitely 5 stars. It packed a great Smokey punch and the fried rice had that lovely wok flavor. Definitely one of the better Chinese places in Manhattan.

Title: Village Square Pizza - A Slice of Heaven!

I've had the pleasure of visiting Village Square Pizza twice, and each time I've been blown away by their mouth-watering pizzas. On my first visit, I indulged in the white slice, and on the second, I savored the pepperoni square - both priced reasonably at $4.50. What stands out is the impeccable balance between the generous layers of cheese and the flavorful sauce. I especially appreciate the ample pepperoni, a true testament to not cutting corners on quality.

The texture of the pizza is a foodie's dream: a crunchy crust complemented by chewy, fluffy dough that enhances each bite. Consistency is key, and Village Square Pizza nails it every time, paired with warm and welcoming service.

Though the space may be on the smaller side, it's cozy and inviting with an abundance of natural light and enough seating to enjoy your pizza on the spot. The rustic charm of the exposed brick and the modern flair of neon signs create an appealing ambiance.

At a fair price point for such high-quality pizza, this eatery is a worthy local spot. Conveniently located near Tompkins Square Park, it’s ideal for a quick grab-and-go to enjoy outdoors. Village Square Pizza is a stellar addition to the neighborhood, and I can't recommend it enough for a slice (or two) of perfection.

Title: A Ramen Respite Near Rockefeller

I recently discovered a gem of a spot just a stone's throw from Rockefeller Center. The new location of this ramen haven is perfectly placed for a warm bowl of comfort after city wandering. Despite a bustling crowd, as a solo diner, I was whisked to a seat without a moment's delay.

The interior exudes contemporary charm, with an abundance of cozy booths that beckon you to settle in. Service was swift, a delight for any hungry patron, and my ramen arrived with an impressive promptness, without compromising on quality. The flavors were rich, the noodles perfectly chewy, and the presentation in the new Jubako box was a treat for the eyes that heightened the entire dining experience.

The staff at this establishment deserve their own round of applause; their friendliness and attentiveness added an extra layer of warmth to my meal.

For anyone planning their visit, here's a tip: download the Ichiran app to earn points with your purchase. I will undoubtedly be returning to this location for another round of their exquisite ramen.

Title: Family-Friendly Brunch Haven in Chelsea

My family and I discovered a brunch gem in Chelsea – Cookshop. Despite its popularity, we were seated immediately on a bustling Saturday morning. The expansive interior is matched by an inviting outdoor patio, perfect for those sunny days.

Service at Cookshop stands out, especially for families. Our toddler was welcomed with a high chair and entertained with a charming farm-themed coloring book, making the experience enjoyable for all.

As for the food, it's a hit. I indulged in the egg and sausage biscuit, featuring housemade sausage, accompanied by flawlessly seasoned potatoes – a testament to the quality of Cookshop's fare.

In short, if you're looking for a relaxed yet delightful brunch spot in Manhattan, Cookshop should be at the top of your list.

Wowwww. It's been 4 days and I'm still thinking about that pizza. Where have I been all my life!! This is slightly embarrassing but I've lived in NY for 25 years and I just had Joe's for the first time on Saturday. But I can also say... I've lived in NY for 25 years and can be really picky about my pizza. The pizza here meets & exceeds all expectations of a quintessential NY slice. We got the fresh mozz, pepperoni and white slice w/ spinach - all PERFECT. Perfectly thin, crispy and tasty. The white one had such a delicious garlic flavor to it ugggghhhhh just take me back already!* Edit: Just returned last night and had the white w/ spinach again as well as the caprese. Still 10/10 perfection.

Ventured into this spot on a sushi craving whim, conveniently located by my workplace. To my delight, the experience was top-notch. The sushi tasted remarkably fresh, each bite harmonizing with zesty dressings and sauces that added the perfect amount of heat. The Samurai roll was a standout, and the pork belly skewers were equally impressive, packed with flavor. Prices were reasonable, not causing a wince when the bill arrived. A friendly tip for fellow diners – complement your rolls with an appetizer, as they come in sets of five. I'd confidently recommend this place for a satisfying sushi fix.

I have been collecting Hard Rock Cafe tumblers from every city. With that in mind, this restaurant is on our top list on where to eat in NYC. Plus, we were kind of tired and hungry from all the walking, so we really needed a place to sit.At 10 pm, there was a 45 minute wait. We were'n't complaining cos like I said, my sister and I were mostly tired than hungry. I didn't notice any chairs on the waiting area, so waiting to be seated was not comfortable. We pretty much sat on the floor, but we didn't care at all. Our server was really nice and seat. She was the reason why we enjoyed our dinner so much. She was helpful and is different from the other servers. She also accommodated me when I asked for overcooked green beans.For our meal, we started off with the spicy shrimp, I forgot it's name, but it is really good. We enjoyed it so much. If the serving was not small for this appetizer, I would probably order this as my entree. My sister order the ribs and I ordered the steak. If you've been any other Hard Rocks, the taste is still the same, so there's really nothing special about it. The mashed pototes were good and I loved my overcooked green beans. We weren't going to order a dessert, but those Hot Fudge brownies from the other tables looked so good. I was glad that we ordered it because it was really delicious.Like any other Hard Rock, I always recommend  this place. It was enjoyable and they're food are really great. We will definitely be back

In the passage of my travels hunger pangs strike as the time was 2 pm and I came across this noodle cafe.  The Yelp reviews do not disappoint.  It was somewhat empty on a holiday for President's Day.  I decided on the shrimp hand-pulled noodle soup $9.95 which was served piping hot.  The noodles were solid and abundant.  The shrimp was good portion and came with Chinese veggies and scallions.  Service is attentive.  Condiments and utensils are located on each table for self-service.  There is sufficient electric wall outlets for charging tech gadgets.  Yes, tap water is available.

Title: A Fresh Mexican Delight in the Neighborhood

I recently enjoyed dinner at a vibrant new eatery that's a wonderful break from the usual chain options. The space is bright and inviting, with a welcoming atmosphere set the moment you're greeted by the cheerful staff at the register.

My meal consisted of an assortment of tacos – the chicken ones were flavorful, but the carnitas taco stole the show, packed with succulence that every taco enthusiast dreams of. Complementing the meal were three unique sauces available, each adding a delightful kick to the tacos.

This place is a fantastic addition to the local dining scene, offering a much-needed authentic Mexican flair contrasted against the familiar background of Dos Toros and Chipotle. It's a relief to have a delicious, independent option right in our neighborhood.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this restaurant where I sampled the spicy cumin lamb noodles and the spicy cumin lamb burger. Both dishes were outstanding. The spice level hit the sweet spot - present but not overwhelming. The lamb was exceptionally juicy and tender, a testament to the kitchen's expertise.

The burger's bread deserves a special mention; perfectly toasted on the outside, while the inside served as an excellent sponge for the lamb's rich juices. As for the noodles, they were the right amount of chewy, pairing nicely with the sauce and ensuring each bite was flavorful. Generous portions of meat in both dishes rounded off a truly satisfying meal. Highly recommended for spice and lamb aficionados!

I visited this restaurant for the first time yesterday and was pleasantly surprised by the ease of parking on a Sunday. Opting for the bottomless brunch special, my girlfriend and I delved into the menu. I savored the jerk chicken roti sandwich which was bursting with flavor—especially the jerk sauce—and thoroughly enjoyed the perfectly cooked chicken, paired with delicious rice and beans. While the rum punch was a bit on the sweet side, its strength was undeniable and paired nicely with our meal. The ambiance was a highlight, featuring a laid-back atmosphere complemented by great music. Although we were seated at the front, the back of the restaurant boasted a charming decor with records and a shiny disco ball, inviting a future visit. My girlfriend's fish sandwich fell short due to excessive batter, but the addictive fries made up for it. Eager to return, I'm looking forward to exploring more of the menu and experiencing dinner here.

Title: Hit-and-Miss Dining Experience at New Expansion Spot

Upon stepping into the new restaurant extension, the vibe initially struck me as reminiscent of a bustling mall food court due to its expansive layout. My cousin and I received a lukewarm welcome and were left to seat ourselves among several open tables, indicating a need for improved staff training.

Service was prompt in taking our order, and we waited a reasonable ten minutes for our food – a highlight in an otherwise mediocre experience. The atmosphere was marred by an inexplicable increase in music volume, which transitioned the setting from a casual eatery to a borderline club scene, much to our confusion.

Regrettably, the service and drinks only managed an average rating, but it was the food that truly underwhelmed. I ventured to try "el Dominicano" sushi, allured by the fusion of Dominican salami, fried cheese, and sweet plantain. Yet, the dish fell short: the plantain was notably undercooked, an off-putting discovery mid-meal, and the accompanying sauces did not redeem the situation.

In contrast, my cousin's choice of tacos was a success; she found them to be delicious and satisfying. As for drinks to accompany our meal, we opted for Long Island iced teas, which were competently made but peculiarly served in piña colada glasses.

In summary, while there are glimmers of potential in this new establishment, consistency in quality and service needs addressing. If I find myself in the area again, I'll come armed with alternative dining options.

I recently visited this charming three-floor restaurant with my girlfriends to indulge in their restaurant week dinner menu and it was quite the delightful experience. The ambiance of the place is perfect for various occasions, whether a romantic date on the ground level, a casual meal in the dining room, or drinks with friends on the second floor.

Starting off with happy hour, I tried their Traditional Caipirinha with strawberry puree — a tad sweet for my liking, hinting at a calorie splurge, but nonetheless delicious. Service at the bar was a tad slow due to the bartender being the sole attendant for a bustling crowd.

Dinner was a mixed bag. Seated near the entrance, the continual door opening brought in a chill, which was a bit uncomfortable. However, the service was lifted by our waiter's good humor. The short rib empanadas were decent, though not outstanding. My main course, a hanger steak, unfortunately didn't hit the mark. It was chewy and not quite cooked to my preference, but the accompanying sauce was a savory highlight with its Thai red curry reminiscence. Dessert ended on a high note with a scrumptious chocolate and coffee bomb — it's hard to go wrong with chocolate for me.

All in all, despite a few hiccups, the evening was enjoyable and the food satisfactory. I'm open to giving this spot another try in the future.

This place probably has one of the most appealing/interesting appetizers out of all of the ramen places i've been to (ofc next to umai ramen back in Brooklyn). It didn't seem like there was a lot of seats/ space but my party of 3 got a table in less than a minute. Mind you, it was around 12 pm lunch time. There were single traditional seats but also tables for groups (sorry if that didn't make sense LOL). There is one restroom all the way in the back and to the left. I ordered the katsu sando and the sweet potato croquettes since they sounded the most interesting. It's not everyday that I find those at a ramen place. The katsu sando came in four slices and had passionfruit jam, which I could taste hints of. My hate for mayonnaise overpowered the fruitiness since it tasted like the fruit jam was mixed with mayo. I don't recall seeing mayo listed as an ingredient so maybe it was just my taste buds playing with me. I would still get the katsu sando again though. The sweet potato croquette was also delicious. It came in three and I could taste both the sweet potato and the cheese. The taste and smell kind of reminded me of fried mantou with condensed milk. I would definitely get it again. I ordered the kimchi ramen since it said it had peanut butter in it. I love to try unique things but I didn't taste any peanut butter flavor. On the contrary, my friend did. It was apparently strong. Despite that slight personal disappointment, it was still good. There were mushrooms, beansprouts, boiled egg, minced meat, one piece of meat, and cabbage in it. Overall, I would definitely recommend this place for ramen lovers or just people who love to try new things. Their menu is great and there is a happy hour special at 3pm for appetizers and drinks. Lunch ramen is priced at $9.99, which is cheaper than it usually is. How budget friendly!

I recently stumbled upon a charming little gem of a restaurant that deserves every bit of praise. This cozy, quaint hole in the wall served up some of the most delightful dishes I've had in a while. Each menu item we tried outdid the last, from the delectable roasted carrot salad to the perfectly crafted pasta. But let me tell you, the meatballs were the true stars of the show – an absolute must-try. If you're looking for an amazing culinary experience in a snug and enchanting setting, add this spot to your list.

Quick, easy, fresh, busy and tasty are some of the instant adjectives that come to my mind when I think of Los Tacos No. 1! You feel like you are in a different country when you enter here - it gives me In-n-Out vibes in terms of decor and how the staff uniforms with Hispanic music playing and it's bustling with people. There is always meat on the grill and always quick service, especially good when you are in a rush (like I was). The guacamole is made with fresh avocados and tastes homemade in a good way! The salsa is yummy with a hint of garlic which I love! The tacos are soft and delicious without it being extra. And I like that they have a simple menu and everything for everyone. It's an overall a fast and great taco experience near Times Square.

Title: A Bittersweet Birthday Dinner at Gran Tivoli

I recently celebrated my birthday at Gran Tivoli, a new Italian eatery with a French bistro vibe, thanks to my brother's thoughtful gift. Despite its trendy atmosphere, the restaurant's layout left much to be desired; our corner table was cramped, forcing us to juggle our personal items and deal with constant bumps from passersby.

Service was underwhelming, but I was pleased with my Aperol Spritz, expertly mixed and a refreshing standout amidst my recent samplings. We started with two appetizers: the Calabrian Salt-Baked Baby Beet Salad, which surprised with an earthy balance rather than expected sweetness, and the "Marche's Lumaconi Gigante," featuring melt-in-your-mouth lamb ragu that showcased high-quality meat without a gamey aftertaste.

Compelled by modest portion sizes, we opted for The Gran Bread Basket. Although diverse, it was a letdown except for the delicious grape tomato focaccia rolls. The rest, from the dry malt sourdough to the bland seeded rolls, missed the mark.

Entrees took an unusually long time to arrive, and when they did, they were a disappointment. My Faroe Islands Organic Salmon was underseasoned and undercooked, saved only by its accompanying sides. My brother's Steamed King Whiting "Cartoccio" was slightly more palatable with its turmeric-fish bone broth, though still lackluster.

Our server comped our drinks to apologize for the wait, but it wasn't enough to lift the sense of dissatisfaction. While Gran Tivoli may be new and in need of time to refine its offerings, I'm not inclined to return. Here's to hoping they can work out the kinks for future diners.

If you're Korean in Flushing and sometime you get that little crave for mak-chang (rectum) gop-chang (intestine), there's really no choice around here. My friends and I had a crave and decided to give this place a try, I gotta say.. unless they kick it up some notches.. we probably won't be coming back.. 1. 3 "Dweji-kalbi" The marinated pork rib: yes, I enjoyed gnawing on the pork ribs.. I usually don't eat marinated meat because I prefer natural flavors seldom topped with housemade sauces, but my friends recommended it. It was ok.2. 1 "Gop-chang" The small intestine: Don't freak out. It usually comes out pre-cooked. They're not giving you left over at some other tables. But it's usually under cooked, so cook some more. When we tried it, the skin was very tough, we rrreeeaalllyy overworked our jaws today.3. 1 "Dae-chang" The large intestine: Looks more appetizing, but skin was even tougher. At this point we were just disappointed. What.. how we're supposed to eat this! We had to ask for sizzors to cut it thinner. It didn't help much.4. 1 "Mak-chang" The rectum: I believe the menu had another word for it, but most accurate term is rectum. It's supposed to be the lost chewy of all intestines. It was pretty good! But no other restaurants can really bring out Seoul style. Why is that? So sad.5. "Dwen-jang Jji-gye" Soybean paste soup: Aiyaa.. I get that salt is free, but.. shouldn't it be optional. It's free, but it's salty.6. "Gye-ran Jjim" Steamed egg: can't go wrong. It's good. Also free.7. "Kimchee Juhn" Korean Kimchee pancake: can be more crunchy, but here it's served a bit soggy. It's midiocre.With everything single order except the marinated pork ribs (3 orders), with 18% tip, the dinner came out to $226 for 5 people. Kind of crazy. But yeah, one of the good thing is that they have their own parking space you can turn into, which is pretty rare in Flushing Murray Hill. It's usually circling around for several minutes for street parking. Star for that!But come on, accept the new trends and kick up some notches! Let's change for the good!

TLDR: In the back of Mercado lies Mar, a restaurant worth going to. Seafood-forward small plates. Petite portions, expensive prices but then again; this is Hudson Yards. Go splurge and discover something else besides gambas al ajillo.We had almost given up at Mercado but figured we'd try Mar. I wish we had just eaten here only but it's probably good we went through the rest of the space first. We'd have probably spent 3x as much if we only ate here.The portions I expected to be small but everything tasted really great. The Atun Rojo Balfego was good, very refreshing this wonderful balance of acidity. We also tried the Bienmesabe Canario con Mojo Rojo, they were these lovely petite fish cakes almost. The little dab of pimenton aioli was perfect.The star for me though was the Albondigas con Sepia y Gamba Roja. Meatballs made with cuttlefish? That was super unique. The sauce was incredibly shrimpy in a good way, it's no surprise they give you that crusty slice of bread to mop up all those flavors.I'd like to come back here for the pre fixe lunch or the tasting menu.

Honestly, I felt like this was a spiritual experience. I was around the corner for an event have never been to Uncle Boons. I figured I couldn't pass up my close proximity to the "sister" location, and popped in to pickup some takeout. Call me basic, but I love Pad Thai. It's one of my favorite things to order, and I can proudly say I've eaten a decent amount out and about NYC. With that being said.... this was BY FAR the most delicious Pad Thai I've ever had. I didn't know Pad Thai could be so delicious. It was perfectly balanced with sweet, savory, and spicy. The chicken was soft, moist, and perfect. The noodles were chewy and firm. And throughout, there were crunchy veggies and (fried chicken skin?) that I loved.I'm so thankful I discovered Uncle Boons Sister and cant wait to go to Uncle Boons himself!

We came here during the lunch rush and man, this place was packed! We waited about 5 minutes and got seated on one side of this alley with a bar on either side. It was CRAMPED. Luckily they have a coat hanger for coats, or else I don't think we would have been able to squeeze in with our jackets. We both ordered the Spicy Ginger Stamina ramen. They give you two pieces of karaage chicken or a salad as an appetizer with your ramen, and we both went for the chicken, which was delicious. When the ramen arrived, it looked amazing. So many toppings, chili oil, soft boiled egg, the works. The ramen noodles were perfectly chewy, but the broth fell a little short for me. It tasted just average, not the amazingness I was expecting. Also, it was not really spicy, and they charge you $1 extra to change the spice level of any dish, which is kind of lame. The staff here are super nice though and it's definitely a solid choice for a bowl of ramen in the area!

Came here with a group of friends for their unlimited wine dinner! Super cute seasonal decor - they've just rolled out their autumn menu, as well! We were seated pretty quickly, and also appreciated having a round table for the group. I don't normally expect food at "unlimited" wine joints to be good, but wow, I'd come to this place with or without the wine! It's also a nice touch how the server pairs different wines with each course - I had at least one white, red, rose, and Prosecco through the night (and several glasses, at that)! They first came out with pumpkin bread and what I can best describe as a warm apple on a stick - which was much tastier than my subpar description sounds, I promise! The pumpkin bread was also some of the best I've tasted!To start, I had the gnocchi Parisienne - they were able to serve it without pork, for all those flexitarians out there! The sauce on this dish was amazing - I'd probably come back just for this! For my entree, I had the Viking village scallops, also without the pork - probably not as memorable as the gnocchi, but very well-cooked as well!I was pretty stuffed at this point between all the wine and food, but I made room for the cinnamon s'mores sundae dessert - a bit on the sweet side, but a great way to end the meal. Wish I had more of an appetite to eat more of it!All in all, a great experience - would come back to try the other seasonal menus, too!

A decent eatery albeit overpriced. I went today prior to Slava's Snowshow performance. The food was decent, service was very nice, but the prices were a bit outrageous. The drinks were good. 1) 18$ for a small "king crab" leg- not very tasty and very small2) Lobster Mac & cheese and burger bites were great3) 20-25$ lobster rolls with an unimpressive salad and a side or fries- felt very underwhelming 4) lobster salad hardly had any lobster or anything else except lettuce in it It was convenient and the food ok enough- but I can't recommend it.

The food is pretty good and the price fair. I appreciate that they give a good portion of noodles and veggies. I left very full. I'd say the flavor and quality is very similar to other places. Free tea and free water. Loved the service too. Very friendly.

We recently tried out a bustling eatery in Koreatown, drawn in by its short wait time amidst the neighborhood's usually crowded dining scene. The queue moved briskly, thanks to their efficient system of taking orders while you're in line, ensuring that our meals were ready almost the moment we sat down. The interactive aspect of cooking at our table added to the experience, and the attentive staff made certain we had a delightful time. The food was quite satisfying, offering authentic flavors that didn't disappoint. The only drawback was the cramped space, which made the dining area feel a bit congested. Nonetheless, for a quick and tasty Korean meal, this place certainly hit the spot.

Title: Pre-Theater Dinner Delight

Last night, my friend and I had the pleasure of dining at this spot before catching a show. Right off the bat, the service was impeccable, catering to our tight schedule without missing a beat.

For starters, the frisbee salad was a hit – a perfect harmony of crispy bacon and parmesan that sang the right tune of deliciousness. As for the main course, I opted for the fish special, a branzino. I appreciated the theatre of being shown the whole fish before the skilled filleting at the kitchen's hands. While the fish was expertly cooked, it could've done with a sprinkle more zest to truly make it shine. Meanwhile, my companion's risotto of the day was met with a satisfying nod of approval.

Dessert was a race against the clock, but the staff delivered. The shared apple tart accompanied by ice cream was a delightful final act, swiftly served and thoroughly enjoyed.

Admittedly, the prices are steep, but considering the overall quality and stellar service, I'd certainly return for an encore.

KazuNori is a sushi enthusiast's dream for those on the go, offering a unique twist with separate dine-in and take-out menus. My recent visit involved sampling from both. The dine-in experience was simple yet satisfying; I indulged in their salmon hand roll, priced at $5.75, which didn't disappoint. My friends enjoyed a sequential serving of their 3-hand roll sets, adding an element of anticipation to each bite. Price-wise, it leans towards the higher end, but the convenience of a tip-included policy softens the blow.

Transitioning to take-out, I opted for the 16-piece set at $18, which featured an eclectic mix of toro, bay scallop, cucumber, and crab. Each roll was fresh and flavorful, with the cucumber roll being an unexpected delight. Payment is hassle-free, completed at the cashier after dining.

In summary, KazuNori delivers on quality and convenience. It's a must-try for hand roll aficionados. I'm already planning a return visit to re-experience the salmon hand roll and delve into other menu items.

This place has a cool vibe. I was staying at the hotel that it was connected to so it made dining very convenient.I went on a Wednesday night and it seemed like there were lots of people there doing the happy hour. I walked in at 7:30 no problem and sat down to order. It was like I snapped my fingers and when I looked up my food was there. I ordered the Blue Crab Carbonara. It was good, I think I expected it to have a more oil...vinagar-y base rather than the cream. The portion size was decent....the plate was $29 and I was afraid the portion was going to be overwhelming but it wasn't I am a big eater to I managed to eat it all. Im excited to try out breakfast. I really really like their decor and vibe. This is going to be an excellent place for the summer.

I recently visited this restaurant for a date night and encountered a mixed experience. Securing a reservation was hassle-free, even for a Saturday at 8pm, and the place was bustling. We sampled a few appetizers, like the conventional chips with guacamole and salsa, and chose from a menu that seemed a tad limited, notably for vegetarians.

Our waitress, who was quite amiable, promptly delivered our drinks—a frozen margarita and a mojito. One highlight was the comfortable ambiance that allowed for conversation. However, the staff appeared thinly spread, causing a delay when ordering. The Chile Relleno was the main vegetarian option, while other appetizers and exotic taco choices, such as the chapulin, rounded the starters.

The entrees were served promptly and portions were generous, yet the food quality didn't quite hit the mark compared to other local Mexican eateries. A sweet end to the meal was the complimentary second dessert—a chocolate cake with pop rocks, which paired nicely with our churros. Despite this gesture, the food seemed to lack the freshness I hoped for, and the overall service could improve.

Given the abundance of Mexican restaurants in Hell's Kitchen, it's unlikely I'll opt for a second visit.

This is definitely the best pizza I've had in the city. I regret only eating one slice here. Greats like Anthony Bourdain and Andrew Zimmern have dined here and I can see why. The pizza is delicious, crust is the perfect thickness and has the right amount of crunch. The pizza overall is not too oily or greasy and that tomato sauce has the right level of tartness and acidity. All this basically equals a perfect slice. I will definitely come back for multiple slices in the near future.

What a wonderful little bar.  Having lived in Japan for a couple of years, it was a reminder of home in a way - just like what you'd find there, but through a NYC prism.  The bar itself was Tiny, and everyone was more or less chatting with each other, while enjoying tasty food and drink.  Also, the night I was there, there was a really, really good DJ.  I can't wait to go back here.  Cannot recommend enough.

Title: Disappointment at Spice's New Portion Sizes

Having been loyal patrons of Spice since their days at East End, and continuing to support them throughout their tenure on Lexington Ave for a decade, our latest experience left us deeply disappointed. Upon ordering our usual favorites, including various pad thais and General Tso’s, we were taken aback to find that the portion sizes had been reduced to half of what they once were, while prices remained unchanged.

Feeling confused, we reached out to the restaurant for clarification, only to be met with a dismissive response from the manager who implied that this reduction had been the norm for years, a claim that contradicted our long history with Spice. We would have appreciated and respected a straightforward notification about any change in lunch special portions. However, the lack of communication with customers about this significant change, coupled with the manager’s handling of our concerns, has tarnished our view of a once-favorite dining spot.

Title: Mixed Feelings on Takeout Experience

I recently decided to give a local restaurant a try by ordering delivery for my family. While my family seemed content with their meals, my personal experience left much to be desired. I opted for the small fried chicken with fries, which unfortunately turned out to be excessively salty and lacking in meat, paired with disappointingly soggy fries. 

I did sample the half chicken and rice from my brother's plate, which was decent, though it could have benefited from a touch more seasoning. The chicken salad my mom ordered was passable but didn't stand out. It's worth noting that the portion sizes were generous, and the pita bread was a highlight for me. 

However, considering the premium pricing, I expected higher quality. Given my underwhelming experience, I'm not eager to make this restaurant my go-to option for future meals.

Dubu Maru is a gem for those who prioritize a healthy menu with a delightful Korean twist. As the name suggests, tofu is a highlight here, featured prominently in a variety of appetizers. However, it's the Hot stone pot of rice that steals the show, offering a comforting choice for both meat lovers and veggie enthusiasts. 

Our group sampled an array of dishes, starting with the Stie fried tofu & eggplant, a well-balanced dish priced at $14. The Steamed/fried tofu with vegetables ($18) was another crowd-pleaser, offering a great texture contrast. For those with a penchant for something meaty, the Spicy pork with kimchi ($20) delivered a good kick of flavor. A unique must-try is the Stone pot rice with spicy pork, kimchi & cheese ($20), a fusion that's as indulgent as it is satisfying. And for a hearty option, the Spicy beef short rib soup ($20) doesn't disappoint, rich and full of depth. 

My friends, particularly the vegans, were impressed by the variety and quality of the plant-based offerings. If health-focused, Korean cuisine is what you crave, Dubu Maru is worth a visit.

Title: A Love Affair with Korean BBQ

From the moment we entered the restaurant, it was clear that we were in for a treat. We were warmly greeted by what seemed to be the manager, who promptly seated us—a touch of personal care that set the tone for the evening.

The menu was a carnivore's dream, mirroring the typical Korean BBQ offerings with an extensive selection of meats. However, it wasn't just the choices that impressed us; it was the VIP treatment that transformed the meal into an extraordinary experience. The meats were cooked to absolute perfection, each bite succulent and flavorful, enhanced by impeccably matched sauces that elevated the entire culinary journey.

There's hardly a negative comment to make about our dining experience. It's worth mentioning that a lot hinges on the quality of the service, and our wait staff was nothing short of magnificent, ensuring our night was memorable.

In summary, this restaurant isn't just a place to eat; it's a place to fall in love with food all over again.

Title: A True Italian Delight in NYC

As a newcomer from the Pacific Northwest on my inaugural full day in NYC, I stumbled upon an Italian haven just outside Chinatown. The charming lure came from a manager with a catchy invitation, "Are you hungry?" in a playful Italian accent. His effective pitch led us to bask in the sun at an outdoor table without bothering to glance at reviews.

Service was stellar, with the manager's attention ensuring all patrons, including my partner and me, were cared for posthaste. We kicked off with drinks—the Gennaro Fresh for him and a Gennaro Lemon Martini for me—both delighting despite modest presentations.

The main dishes, however, were the showstoppers: Cheese Ravioli in a delectable creamy red sauce for me and Cannelloni Ripieni Amalfitana for him. Both dishes soared beyond any Italian fare we've tasted, setting a new standard and making chain restaurants a thing of our past.

We rounded off our meal with a shared dessert, despite my usual aversion to custard. The Creme Brûlée, accompanied by an Espresso, was a revelation in texture and portion—utter perfection.

Admittedly, prices are a bit steep, but the experience and cuisine are unequivocally worth it. Our future plans already include a return with our girls and recommendations to any family and friends bound for NYC. This spot isn't just a meal; it's a culinary experience that's not to be missed.

It was raining and this place was a few blocks away from the hotel so I made a run for it. I stopped in for three toasted bagels. They only had 3 types left at 11am so I grabbed the raisins. Seems like a lot of people get their sandwiches and salads here on their lunch breaks. It took about 15 minutes for them to put some cheese and toast my bagels for me. Total was just under ten bucks I believe. I grabbed it to go and ate breakfast back at the hotel with the family. Bagel was just ok, nothing special.

Nestled in Manhattan's vibrant Koreatown, Abiko Curry is a gem for those who appreciate the art of Japanese curry without the fuss. Its straightforward menu invites diners to customize their meal: choose a base (rice or noodles), a protein, and, for the brave, one of four escalating spice levels. A fair warning: the third tier is fiery enough to challenge even the most seasoned spice aficionados. 

Abiko masters the delicate balance of flavors in its curries—a harmonious blend of sweetness and saltiness, with a gradual spicy crescendo. The udon noodles are a highlight, providing a satisfying chewiness to complement the exquisitely seasoned broth. Crispy tofu and fresh scallions add a delightful crunch, while a side of pickled radish serves as a palate cleanser, preparing you for the next mouthwatering bite.

Although curry is the star, do not overlook their other offerings, like the flavorful chicken donburi bowl. Abiko dispels the myth that curries are heavy, proving it can be a light and enjoyable dish. However, heed this tip: opt for the second spice level to savor your meal without regret. Abiko Curry stands out as a must-visit for a truly authentic Japanese curry experience.

I recently tried the La Mancha mac 'n' cheese from a local eatery. Opting for the nosh size with an added touch of garlic, the dish was delicious. The inclusion of fennel and onions lent a unique and savory twist to the classic comfort food. Portion-wise, the nosh size was just right for a single serving, though it did feel a tad expensive for the quantity provided. Overall, a tasty experience with a note on value to consider.

At Veselka, the promise of a rainbow palette of flavors was met with a selection of tasty dishes, albeit with a price tag that could dampen the spirits. As someone eager to savor the tastes of Ukraine, this rarity was a must-try, especially with a Ukrainian connection at home.

While the brunch menu flirted with American classics and fusion items, I found solace in the traditional offerings. The homemade Ukrainian dumplings (varenyky) stuffed with corned beef hash were a delightful blend of textures, especially when coupled with perfectly cooked over-medium eggs and a fresh bite of green onions. The accompanying fresh-pressed orange juice was a pure and refreshing complement.

The borscht stood out with its authenticity, warming my palate with its rich, beetroot goodness. The combination meat plate was an indulgent journey through the heartier side of Ukrainian cuisine, with perfectly paired sides enhancing the experience.

While the menu ventured into more familiar territories with salads, sandwiches, and burgers, the offering of fruit pierogies retained a touch of Ukrainian charm. My one lament is the scant selection of Ukrainian-style cakes or desserts, which would have made the meal feel more complete. Nevertheless, Veselka proved to be a vibrant culinary experience, even if the wallet felt a little lighter upon departure.

The popular Upper West Side staple for brunch-goers certainly lives up to its reputation: be prepared for a wait, but your patience will be rewarded. While it may not top my list of all-time favorite brunches, the varied menu is sure to please any palate, and the attentive service is a delightful bonus. A special nod goes to the strawberry butter accompanying the waffles – it's a standout hit that's not to be missed!

I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant on a Wednesday night, perfectly timed for their happy hour from 4pm to 6pm. Despite the bustling scene, I was seated promptly—an excellent start. The happy hour here is a steal, with all drinks at half price, allowing me to indulge in a pitcher of sangria for a mere $13.50.

Compelled by the cozy and inviting ambiance, I transitioned to dinner, and the experience only got better. From appetizers and main courses to desserts, every dish was delightful. A standout was the kitchen Kadif, a divine Halva parfait with shredded filo dough, artfully presented as an egg nestled in a bird's nest. The rich sweetness of Halva paired with the crunchy texture of the dough was a culinary revelation.

Moreover, the presence of Israeli wines on the menu caught my eye, a unique offering that I am eager to explore on my next visit. This place is definitely on my list for a return, and I'd highly recommend it to anyone looking for great deals on drinks and a stellar dining experience.

La Bergamote's bakery side is still open and the pastries are as amazing as ever! On a recent visit I got a peach danish and linzer tart - both incredible. Next time: I need to finally try the chocolate almond croissant!

Title: A Toast to Edward's: A Delight in Every Bite

Last Tuesday evening, my girlfriend and I stumbled upon Edward's restaurant, a gem we found online. To our surprise, despite not having a reservation at the bustling 6:30 PM time slot, we were welcomed to choose our table without a wait.

Although the heat was palpable both indoors and out, the staff promptly ushered us to a cooler spot in the back. Michael, who multitasked as our gracious host, server, and bartender, was a standout star, ensuring our experience was nothing short of exceptional.

In the spirit of celebration for my girlfriend's upcoming nuptials, I savored a perfectly tailored martini, while her Aperol spritz fell victim to a pesky mosquito. Undeterred, we both indulged in the seared ahi tuna— a delectable and evidently healthy choice—accompanied by a medley of fresh vegetables and rice, arriving in a timely 20-minute fashion.

Upon sharing the happy news with Michael, he generously offered complimentary Prosecco, adding a sparkling touch to our festivities. His thoughtful offer to capture the moment with photos was the cherry on top, leaving us with adorable memories of the evening.

With remarkably fair pricing, our meal—complete with two cocktails and two tuna entrées—came to a pleasant total of $70. A slight hiccup with the payment was the only blur in an otherwise flawless encounter, but it was quickly overlooked in light of the overall experience.

In conclusion, Edward's restaurant is a find with outstanding service, excellent location, and reasonable prices. The enticing happy hour and specials are a bonus, and the quality of both food and drinks makes it a must-return spot on my list.

I think this is one of the tastiest burgers I've ever eaten. They cook the meat perfectly to your liking. The fat to meat ratio made the patty super juicy and all the fixings compliment it perfectly. It's the kind of burger where you take one bite, blink, then you're already finished. Conveniently in the gansevoort market with many other great vendors. Way less crowded than chelsea market but way better vendors

Have been wanting to try this place for the longest since my boyfriend lives close by. Honestly it wasn't the best experience I've had for brunch but it wasn't bad either. We walked in on a Sunday after where there were many people already at the bar drinking and having a good time. The place is set up with a bar area as soon as you walk in and a sit in dining area further into the restaurant. Although the dining area was very empty it took a while for the server who was also our waitress to attend us. Our waitress was very nice and after the first initial wait time she was very quick and attentive during our meal. For brunch you are allowed one complimentary drink. You can choose between a mimosa, screwdriver or a Bloody Mary if I remember correctly. I chose to drink their mimosa and ate the Vanilla bourbon French toast and my boyfriend had a screwdriver with the Avocado toast with fried eggs and French fries. Both meals were good; smaller in portion than we both expected but they both had good flavor. My French toast was on the burnt side but I didn't mind all that much. Overall, I don't think we will be revisiting but I'm glad we finally got to check out The Spotted Dog.

Title: A Hidden Gem in the Heart of NYC - Ikinari Steak

Review:

My long-awaited visit to Ikinari Steak did not disappoint. Amidst the buzz of potential closures reported by Eater, I was eager to check it off my bucket list before it was too late—and what a decision that was!

On a hectic Saturday night, as neighboring eateries boasted lengthy queues, Ikinari stood out like a beacon of hope, welcoming us in without a delay. The staff was notably amiable, easing us into the Ikinari way: drinks and starters via waitstaff, and a unique, interactive experience of selecting and weighing our steak at the cutting station. The novelty of this process, though perhaps unconventional in the American dining scene, was a highlight and speaks volumes to Ikinari's commitment to a distinctive dining experience.

The steak itself? Sublime. Served on a sizzling skillet with a side of our choice, it rivaled pricier steakhouse offerings both in taste and presentation. Paired with a bottle of Sake—of which, in hindsight, a glass would have sufficed—we savored every bite.

Ikinari offers a novel twist on the steakhouse archetype, merging quality and affordability in a casual yet chic environment. It's an experience I'd recommend to any food enthusiast willing to step outside the traditional. Here's hoping this concept thrives; it's indeed a treat for those adventurous enough to embrace it.

Title: Convenient Pre-Show Dining at Cha Pa's

My dining experience at Cha Pa's Noodle and Grill was punctually scheduled before catching the delightful production of 'Puffs' nearby. The restaurant, which was only a third occupied upon our 6:30 PM arrival, offered a serene dining environment that gradually livened.

A strict seating policy kept my friend waiting for a brief moment until I arrived, despite the visibly available tables. However, once settled, we delved into the menu with anticipation. My choice, the Chicken Curry, priced fairly at $11, presented a harmonious blend of flavors, tender chicken without overwhelming spice. Equally palatable was my companion's Grilled Pork Vermicelli Bowl, also $11, complemented by a crisp Cha Gio Roll for an additional $3. The bowl's composition of rice noodles, fresh vegetables, and garnishes created a satisfying meal.

While the culinary delights at Cha Pa's may not break new grounds, they certainly hit the mark on taste and value—attributes of note in this bustling neighborhood. Service was adept, with attentive check-backs and water refills.

In conclusion, for a casual, pre-theater meal, Cha Pa's is worth repeating. Its combination of good food, reasonable prices, and decent service makes for an easy choice when in the area for entertainment.

After a coworker's recommendation and some online research, I decided to give this much-hyped restaurant a try on a quiet midweek evening. The location is conveniently accessible, mere steps from the train station, and upon entry, the ambiance and friendly staff set a promising stage. However, despite the well-maintained bathrooms and the overall positive vibe, the dining experience itself left much to be desired.

The much-lauded paella, which seemed to have a fan following, was a letdown as it bore little resemblance to the traditional Spanish dish, aside from being served in a frying pan. The Brussels sprouts seemed overpriced for what has become a trendy vegetable, and the tenderloin was unremarkable.

A glimmer of hope came in the form of delicious fritters, but the joy was short-lived due to the meager serving size. We opted to skip dessert at the restaurant, finding more value and satisfaction with a sweet treat at a nearby spot.

In summary, while the restaurant may be riding on the reputation of a notable name, the culinary experience failed to live up to expectations, proving to be quite ordinary. My dining companion summed it up perfectly: we might have been better off sticking with Thai food.

I love eating rice rolls! It's one of my favorite things to eat for Chinese food and I found a great one in NYC!  The prices are very cheap and you can get full without breaking your wallet.  Each roll is less than 2 bucks and so I get a few and barely spent anything.  The texture was great and rolls come out quickly.  They also offer sauces at the counter for you to pour into your rolls before you're off.  They also have frozen dumplings for a cheap price too! Such a great find in Chinatown NYC!

When I have heard of Capital Grille it seems synonymous with high end service and food. Ifoe an appetizer I had the tuna tartare with avocado and crisp bread. Delicious with the only exception of mentioning mango in the description with only a small bit in the sauce. I was expecting more to layer the flavors. For the main course I had the dry aged steak au poivre which was perfectly encrusted with an absolutely deliciously buttery sauce that was wonderful to savor. Brussel sprouts perfectly cooked and wonderfully charred. And I was too full for dessert. And brought home enough for a second meal. My only disappointment was that our drink glasses were dirty when wine was poured in. They were replaced and comped.  And also our orders got mixed up and the guest of honor did not get what she ordered. Again this was perfectly corrected with the expected apologizing. The atmosphere is reminded me of someplace I would go to after a fox hunt  with a few dead animal heads on the walls. As the evening went on and the light started to fade the lighting got darker. Almost a bit too dark for a business dinner. Price is what I would expect at a high end steak house  if I could give half stars this would be four and a half.

Title: A Tasty Treat with a Slight Wait

I visited this gem during restaurant week and was not disappointed by the culinary offerings. The menu boasted of their famous chicken satay and oxtail bao buns, both of which lived up to the hype on my maiden visit. Despite having reservations and being seated immediately, a 15-minute wait for service initiation was a hiccup in an otherwise delightful experience.

The highlights included succulent appetizers and a creme brûlée that set the gold standard for desserts – easily the most impeccable rendition I’ve savored to date. With the bonus of restaurant week pricing, it was an affordable indulgence.

This establishment is a versatile venue suitable for anything from group gatherings to a cozy date night. The wait time for service could improve, but the food is a guaranteed crowd-pleaser. Solid 4 stars.

Title: Authentic Japanese Noodles Worth the Wait

Recommended by a friend, my expectations for this noodle house were high, and I was not disappointed. Despite the 45-minute wait (pro tip: use Yelp to get on the waitlist), which underscored the popularity of this cash-only establishment, the experience was worth it.

From the appetizing edamame and bacon to the kamaage and shrimp tempura hot udon, each dish was a testament to their commitment to authenticity, especially their imported Japanese noodles which stood out in both texture and taste. The service was exceptionally efficient, with attentive staff clearing plates and checking in regularly.

In summary, despite the wait time, this eatery delivered on both food and service, ensuring my return on my next NYC escapade.

We ended up stumbling into Angela's on an early Saturday afternoon. We planned to spend some time in the park and thought it wise to pick up something quick to enjoy once we were inside. We were feeling sandwiches and saw this spot on the way and decided to give it a try.The shop itself is pretty narrow and has the majority of it's seating in the back. When we walked in we looked at their large menu which is directly over the cashier in the front. They've got a pretty wide selection of both hot and cold sandwich options, as well as the means to customize a sandwich for you.I ended up ordering the cold Vietnamese sandwich which was comprised of pork, an "asian sauce", carrot, and cucumber. The sandwich itself was pretty massive which made me feel like I got my $$$ worth, but that was even more solidified after I took my first bite. It was exactly what I never knew I needed! All the ingredients came together perfectly. Try it for yourself to see how good it is!

Stepping into this charming local ramen joint, you're immediately greeted by a cozy interior and the warm smiles of an amicable staff. The ramen bowls here sing with authentic flavors, showcasing a delightful medley of rich broths and perfectly cooked noodles, while the rice bowls are a satisfying homage to traditional Japanese fare. A neighborhood gem, this spot has won over locals with its culinary prowess. To top it off, a curated selection of Japanese craft beers provides the perfect accompaniment to an already splendid meal. An easy favorite, it's a must-visit for anyone craving a taste of Japan.

Came here for lunch on a weekday and was seated right away. I've always passed by this place and figured I'd give it a shot since I've been a NY noodletown loyalist...Had to get the roast pork wonton noodle soup (Cha siu won ton mein). Wontons and noodles were good but the roast pork was ok. I think I got a bunch of end bits...Soup could have been tastier but not bad. I was kind of surprised how expensive it was for lunch, ended up paying $13 ( $10.35+tip ), so that's why I'm giving 3 stars. Definitely cheaper alternatives for better wonton noodle soup elsewhere.

After several visits, it’s about time I share my thoughts on this local gem. The wait staff consistently delivers friendly service, enhancing the dining experience. The food here truly hits the mark for tastiness; the mussels stand out with their savory taste and delectable broth. As for the linguine Bolognese, it’s a hearty dish bursting with rich flavor that doesn’t disappoint. Adding a side of meatballs was a wise choice; they were nothing short of delightful. Given its proximity and quality, it’s become a go-to spot for me. I’m already looking forward to my next meal here.

Title: Chic Ambiance with a Side of Patience

My recent visit to this stylish eatery left me thoroughly impressed. The decor strikes the perfect balance between chic and hip, creating an inviting atmosphere that’s ideal for a night out with friends or a cozy date.

While the service was on the slower side, anticipation only heightened the eventual delight of the meal. The much-touted burrata pizza, while a tad underseasoned, still met my high expectations with its fresh and creamy topping. I'd suggest a pinch more seasoning to elevate it further.

In contrast, the truffle mac and cheese was a flavor explosion, expertly balanced and satisfying my craving for something rich and indulgent.

The staff deserves a mention for their friendliness and helpfulness, adding warmth to the overall experience.

The menu, brimming with unique offerings, has several dishes calling me back for more. This spot isn't just a treat for the taste buds but also a feast for the eyes perfect for a social media shout-out. I'm already planning my next visit!

Just got my noodle pulled here, and I could not be happier. I got the dry rub which left a little bit of a burn from the heavy hand with the cumin. This is a great place for a quickie or take something exotic home to spice up your evening.

Decent food, good prices. Came here for happy hour but didn't really get any happy hour drinks and got a cocktail off the menu.  Their list of signature cocktails seemed a little outdated and had more of a fall/winter theme to it since it included a hot toddy, cider drinks, etc.  Our server was pleasant and came to check on us a few times. For food, ordered the chicken mozzarella sandwich which wasnt warm and left much to be desired.  Just a cold chicken sandwich. Fries were excellent though. Overall a decent spot in the area.

Great Restaurant!  My boss recommended this restaurant. I made a reservation but you don't need one. It was Friday at 8:00 pm and it was full but it was a couple of tables available.   We waited like 5 minutes for them to acknowledged we were there waiting for a table. A really nice guy came and guide us to our table. The Restaurant is not big but has his charm.  The hostess brought the menu, Huge menu!!! We waited like 10 minutes for a server. When the server came I was ready to order everything ! but he left after I ordered the drinks lol... The drinks came pretty fast and then we ordered. Great food! and the quantity is very good!
