Food !* Scarparelli ( for one) - not ! this is not true! you can share this plate! is huge !!!   The sausage is spicy , the filet mignon was very soft and the chicken was very juicy. 5 of 5!!!! * Shrimp Scampi alla forlini -  the sauce is to die for!! excellent !!! we even used this sauce for the spaghettis ! 10 of 10 !! the shrimp were excellent !!!Drinks!*Sangria Forlinis - 5 of 5 ! excellent !!!  Overall, this restaurant is very good , they need to get better on the service ! that is why I gave them 4 stars !Extremely recommended !

Title: Charming Spot for a Girls' Night Out

I recently visited this stunning restaurant for a girls' night out, and it was an absolute delight. The decor set a lovely ambiance, and the service was nothing short of exceptional.

We hit a minor hiccup with the bone marrow dish, which unfortunately arrived devoid of marrow on the first try, and undercooked on the second. However, the third attempt was spot-on, showcasing the kitchen's commitment to rectifying the issue. The staff handled the situation with grace, ensuring we felt valued as patrons.

The scallops were a highlight—cooked to perfection and incredibly delicious. We indulged in several dishes, each proving to be quite satisfying. To top off the evening, a sparkling dessert was brought out, adding a festive touch to our celebration.

I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant for its remarkable atmosphere and attentive service. It's an ideal choice whether you're planning a girls' night, a brunch, or a romantic date.

This place was on my list for a while now. I got the pepperoni square pizza and had to wait for about 30 minutes because there was a long line. The pizza was ok not the best. I wonder what the hype is all about. The slice is 4$ and it is fun to try it once.

Came here for birthday dinner.  My reservation was at 6:15pm.  Arrived at 6pm.  Went up to the host, told her I have a reservation at 6:15pm for party of 4.  But she couldn't find my reservation, Lucky I took a screen shot right after I make a reservation and I show it to her.  She went to her I believe either a manager or someone that's higher up.  She look it up and said she don't see my reservation, but my name is in the system.  I don't get that.  But she said she will show me to my table.  I said ok.Anyway, once we sat down, our waitress came and took our order.  For appetizers we order Crispy Calamari, Lump Crab Cakes, Crispy Sweet & Spicy Chicken Wings.  Entree we order, Blackened Scottish Salmon, Grilled 10 Oz. Filet Mignon, Baked Lobster Tail With Crabmeat & Penne Pasta With Jumbo Shrimp.  While we're having our appetizers, I notices there's no bread, but we saw other tables have bread.  So we ask our waitress, and she said oh you want bread?  Shouldn't it comes with as complimentary?  Since I saw every table got bread except us.  Then our entrees came, still no bread.  When we are almost finish our entrees then the bread came. Shouldn't the serve once we order?  Dessert we order Chocolate Mousse Cake & Nutella ice cream with Chantilly and valrhona.  Overall, beside the bread issue that we have to ask for it.  Other than that.  The food is really good.  All the appetizers have good flavors.  Salmon and Losbter is not over cook.  The steak is cook perfectly and really tender..  Overall, I would come back again.

Tucked away in the heart of Chinatown, this Korean gem defied my initial skepticism—it's the real deal, authentically Korean-run and every bit as satisfying as what you'd find in Ktown. Despite the Monday evening bustle, the space was welcoming with plenty of seating. The banchan here is a highlight, offering an excellent variety, including a memorable seaweed and a delightful steamed egg served in generous portions.

For starters, the kimchi pancake was a solid choice, though the mixed tofu soup was the standout for me—rich and flavorful without being overwhelming, though I’d recommend sticking with the 'medium' spice level. The army soup (budejigae) was satisfactory and filled with all the essentials, but I'd say the tofu soup outshone it.

The bossam didn't disappoint, delivering that succulent pork belly goodness. As for the eel stone pot, it's worthy of a try based on my single bite. If you find yourself craving Korean in Chinatown, this place is a sure bet—no need to trek all the way to Ktown.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Penn Station Eatery

My visit to the Mexican restaurant in Penn Station was underwhelming and marred by poor service and lackluster food. Despite hopeful reviews, the staff's evident unhappiness translated into outright hostility towards patrons. 

Jayson's tacos were unremarkable, and while my burrito junior was sizable, it did little to make up for the overall experience. The complimentary chips and salsa, a potential redeeming feature, were compromised by stale chips and what seemed like unsanitary conditions at the salsa station.

In a city brimming with excellent and affordable Mexican cuisine, I recommend bypassing this establishment and seeking out one of the many other options available.
I ordered the Avocado Ranch burger and signature hand cut fries. The burger was pretty good, and the fries were good too. This place has a lot of seating and wasn't very busy around lunch time.

This is our go to in Korea Town when we want to meet for a quick dinner by Penn Station. The food is consistently delicious. I usually opt for the spicy squid bibimbap but the last time I had a beef soup because it was super cold outside. The broth was fab and the meet was tender and filling. They are also able to accommodate our vegan family members so we meet there often. Sometimes the service can be a little rushed and lacking but the food is great.

Title: A Cinco de Mayo Fiesta to Remember

Celebrating Cinco de Mayo at this bar was a fantastic experience. The cocktail menu was exceptional, featuring not only classic margaritas but also innovative twists like the zesty Paloma and the refreshing 'stealth margarita' with its unique blend of cucumber and elderflower liquor—all expertly mixed to the perfect strength.

The food did not disappoint either. The nachos topped with mole chicken may not have been the epitome of authenticity, but they were undeniably scrumptious. Coupled with the warm and welcoming staff, the atmosphere was vibrant.

And the cherry on top? A live donkey mingling with the guests! This bar is a must-visit spot for a memorable, fun-filled outing.

Title: Generous Portions and Speedy Service!

I recently dropped by this no-frills eatery on my sister's recommendation and was pleasantly surprised by the value for money. We went for the Ma La Tang - I chose beef while she opted for the beef brisket. The servings were hearty, though I would have preferred more, thinner slices of beef rather than a few thick ones.

Service here is self-serve, aligning with the quick-stop vibe. The food comes out hot and fast, perfect for a rapid lunch or dinner. Despite a less fiery kick than expected, the Ma La Tang was rich in flavor, brimming with fresh vegetables and my beloved thin clear noodles.

Payment is as straightforward as the dining experience - eat, then take your ticket to the front desk to settle the bill. My only gripe? The AC. A cooler interior would make the hot noodle soup far more enjoyable, especially during the sweltering summer months.

I'm already planning my next visit, enticed by the tasty offerings and snappy service. A solid choice for a satisfying meal on the go!

If you find yourself with a spare $10 and a craving for empanadas, this is the spot for you. The spinach and cheese empanada stands out, packed with flavorful cheese and perfectly fried. The seating area is ample with the convenience of two bathrooms, a water station, and an abundant supply of delicious green sauce. This place lets you enjoy a satisfying meal without straining your wallet. Highly recommended for a comfortable and tasty dining experience.

I recently discovered Tacombi in Flatiron, and I'm admittedly miffed that this gem remained a secret from me for so long. Our party of eight arrived at 11:45, yet we easily found ample seating - a testament to the establishment's thoughtful layout prioritizing comfort over cramming in extra tables.

The interior exudes charm with its engaging decor, but let's talk food: the ordering process is streamlined with a shared slip of paper, which I found refreshingly efficient. We kicked off with two generous orders of chips and guacamole, more than sufficient for our group.

On to the main event, the shrimp taco was a miss for me due to an unusual taste, but the beef taco? A revelation. Tender, flavorful meat paired with veggies and a delectable sauce, transformed into my idea of the PERFECT taco with the addition of leftover guacamole.

A glass of cool pineapple juice provided the perfect accompaniment to the meal. Considering the reasonable prices, fantastic food, and amiable staff, Tacombi is now high on my list for a repeat visit.

Title: A Delightful Brunch at Jane

My recent brunch at Jane was nothing short of delightful. We enjoyed the ease of being seated immediately upon arrival, thanks to our reservation. The staff's warmth and welcoming smiles set a positive tone for our experience.

The restaurant's interior struck a balance between cleanliness and chic elegance, creating a comfortable ambiance for dining. As a vegetarian who abstains from eggs, I appreciated the thoughtful, albeit limited, options available to me. My choice, an avocado sandwich, was not only a feast for the eyes but also for the taste buds. The stunning presentation captivated my attention before I indulged in the delicious flavors.

The latte I ordered complemented my meal perfectly, serving as a testament to Jane's commitment to quality in both food and drink. The environment allowed for easy conversation without the distraction of a noisy background, enhancing the overall dining experience.

In summary, Jane impressed us with their service, ambiance, and delectable cuisine. We left satisfied and are already looking forward to our next visit.

I recently dined at this restaurant and was left quite dissatisfied. The ravioli I ordered was a letdown; the filling was both dry and lacking in taste. Moreover, the prices did not reflect the quality of the food. To add to the disappointment, the service was sluggish—it took an excessive 30 minutes just to get the server's attention for the check. Unfortunately, I can't say the experience was worth the expense.

We made reservation on a Sunday afternoon and the place was absolutely packed. Ordered the grapefruit and orange juice which was really expensive, almost $10?! Chips and guacamole with crab - actual crab! This was goodLoaded tots with bacon - surprisingly good even though the tots were made from chickpea and not potatoesBeef short rib - this was fine, nothing to really write about. Eggs, salmon, and cream cheese - interesting taste with the cream cheese. it wasn't really mixed cleanly into the egg, it was more like lumps. I liked that the entrees were a bit different than your normal brunch offerings for variety especially the appetizers.

Title: A Delightful Experience at KazuNori

I recently enjoyed my inaugural visit to KazuNori with a friend, and it was nothing short of delightful. Arriving shortly after opening on a Saturday, we were promptly seated at the counter amidst a welcoming early crowd. As we finished our meal before 1pm, a queue had formed, which seemed to move swiftly due to the quick dining experience.

Opting for the three roll set, priced at an affordable $15, we savored the fresh flavors of salmon, scallop, and crab. The scallop emerged as my personal favorite, leaving a memorable impression, while the crab ranked last on my list. We noticed others inquiring about substitutions, though it was unclear if these incurred additional costs. Individual rolls are available for those looking to customize their meal or add to their set.

To my surprise, the three rolls proved quite filling, attributed to the generous portion of rice. Overall, KazuNori impressed with its fresh offerings and efficient service—a must-visit for sushi enthusiasts.

Title: Worth the Wait at This Hotspot - Book Ahead!

If you're planning a visit to this gem, heed my advice: book a table via Yelp well in advance – at least two hours before you intend to dine. I learned the hard way with a staggering 94-minute wait upon a walk-in attempt, which found me desperately hungry by my eventual 9:00 PM seating.

Parking is a nightmare, so come prepared for that challenge. The dimly lit entrance does little to prepare you for the enchantment inside where a stunning Buddha water mural sets the tone for the dining experience ahead.

Seating is a mixed bag: parties of two might find themselves rather cozy with neighbors in the tightly packed center, while groups of three or more revel in spacious, tent-like periphery tables offering comfort and exclusivity. There's also an upper level that caught my eye for next time.

The food, albeit a tad pricey, is where this establishment truly shines. We indulged in a divinely spicy Green Curry with Vegetables ($15) and the perfectly savory Krapraw Gai Sub ($17), accompanied by an intriguing blue Sencha tea. Each dish was a delight, though portions could be more generous.

Service, while friendly, can be on the slower side – a small price to pay for the high demand and quality of the food.

In summary, despite the initial hunger pangs and the wait, the food and ambiance make a return visit irresistible. Just remember to plan ahead!

I dropped by this quaint spot for some takeout and was pleasantly surprised. Despite not being much of a lobster enthusiast, I opted for the crab roll paired with a side of clam chowder, which was nothing short of spectacular – rich in flavor and perfectly seasoned without being overly salty. Though modest in size, the chowder was surprisingly filling.

Moving on to the main event, the jumbo crab roll might have appeared small at first glance, but it was generously stuffed with fresh crab meat. While the roll was delicious, a tad more seasoning could elevate it to the next level. The bread was satisfactory, though it didn't particularly stand out.

On a side note, this place does offer a happy hour that seems worth checking out, especially given the size of the venue, which was quite bustling during my lunchtime visit. Overall, it's a solid choice for seafood lovers.

Title: Hearty Flavors with a Dash of Chaos

I popped into this spot for a Friday lunch with a friend and was pleasantly satiated by their Southeast Asian offerings. We indulged in the roti appetizer, whose curry sauce boasted a potent kick that primed our palates for what was to come. The Hainanese chicken didn't just meet expectations - it was remarkably juicy, paired with a rice so rich in flavor from the chicken stock, it could stand on its own. 

However, the Malaysian pork chop's sweetness overstepped my taste preference, teetering on the edge of being cloying. Service did dip into the chaotic - our Hainanese chicken was momentarily forgotten - but that's a quirk one quickly learns to navigate in Chinatown eateries.

Value for money was evident, with lunch deals offering generous portions. And a pro tip worth noting: it's a cash-only establishment, but a check-in on Yelp sweetens the deal with a complimentary Thai iced tea. I'm eager to return and delve deeper into their menu.

Ehhhhh, overhyped? Lots of celeb sightings posted on walls, elbow or elbow even at midnight, well-loved in reviews, kinda grimy/dirty/rude and no real seating. A disappointing slice of thin greasy pizza to us.... pepperoni for sure was NOT the thing to get.  Would definitely try ANOTHER, different place for a "slice of pie" NY style

Title: A Vietnamese Gem Beyond Chinatown

I recently visited a Vietnamese eatery that's quickly become my go-to spot for authentic cuisine outside of Chinatown. Every visit is a delightful venture into new tastes, and I've yet to be disappointed. What I particularly appreciate is the punctuality with reservations—they honor your time slot to the dot, which is incredibly convenient!

On my latest trip, we opted for the appetizer plate, which turned out to be a generous spread, almost too generous for our group of three. The portions were so substantial that we struggled to make room for the main course. As a pho enthusiast, I was a tad disappointed that I couldn't indulge in a bowl due to the appetizer takeover. Next time, the strategy is simple: order less from the starter menu to save space for the main attractions, like their aromatic pho and a variety of rice and noodle dishes.

Lunch-time on a Monday afternoon, walked over to this spot as it's one of the few nicer sit down restaurants around Brookfield. Fairly packed inside due to the holidays, yet managed to get a couple seats at the bar.Definitely a pricier place for lunch, with entrees and sandwiches averaging around $20. Decided on the Lump Crab Cake Entree ($24) instead of the sandwich version which was $2 more. After taking our order, the bartender/waiter asked to hold on to a card (an odd thing when not ordering drinks). Food comes out 15 minutes later, and they bring out a sandwich instead of the entree I asked for. They quickly correct the mistake three minutes later with just the crab cake entree (it looks like they removed it from the sandwich and placed it on the plate).Meal overall was unappetizing - the crab did not taste fresh, and the cole slaw was an afterthought. Absolutely not worth the money - was better off spending the extra dough on the bun and fries.

Title: Superb Takeout Experience at Caffe Buon Gusto

I recently opted for takeout from Caffe Buon Gusto and was thoroughly impressed with the value for money. The capellini alla vodka cost me just $12, and the portion size was generous, outdoing what you'd get for $20-$25 at other establishments. The pasta itself was delicious!

However, I had to dock a star, making it a 4-star review, because the additional toppings were on the pricier side, each costing between $4-$5. While I would've enjoyed customizing my dish with broccoli and mushrooms, the cost deterred me.

Despite this, the quality and affordability of the main dishes ensure that I'll be a repeat customer.

Title: Authentic Flavors at Jiang Diner – A Mixed Bag for Xinjiang Cuisine Enthusiasts

If you're craving the robust flavors of Northwestern China's Xinjiang cuisine, Jiang Diner is a commendable choice with a diverse menu worth exploring. Begin your culinary adventure with appetizers such as the delightfully spicy hot and sour cucumbers or the tangy wood ear mushrooms dressed in vinegar, chili oil, and mustard. Though the spicy baked buns may disappoint if you're expecting a meaty filling, they're nonetheless a flavorful bread option.

For those anticipating tantalizing dumplings, the steamed lamb shumai might fall short, offering a too-firm filling and somewhat inconsistent dough. However, the sautéed rice cakes with an assortment of pickled vegetables steal the show, each bite enriched with a savory sauce that beautifully complements the chewy texture of the rice cakes.

The hand-rolled noodles present a unique twist on the traditional, but it's the rice cakes that truly shine in the entrée section. The big plate chicken, a staple in Xinjiang cuisine, has room for improvement, particularly in noodle texture, but still holds its own in flavor. Unfortunately, the sautéed crispy baked buns with lamb and cumin don't live up to expectations, with an overly firm, crouton-like texture.

One word of caution: bell pepper and onion are common ingredients here, so those averse to these vegetables should specify their preferences when ordering. Overall, Jiang Diner offers a genuine taste of Xinjiang cuisine with a few hits and misses along the way.

Today, my friend and I had the pleasure of lunching at this local gem while in the area, and I must say, it was an absolute delight. The ambiance struck the perfect balance of chill and comfort, allowing us to unwind as we dove into the menu. Each dish—from the savory ramen and succulent dumplings to the fresh sushi—was a hit on our taste buds. To top it off, I sampled sake for the first time, and it was truly exceptional. The experience was flawless. No complaints, just pure culinary joy.

This is a hidden gem. I have tried other Thai places in New York and it's hard to find one that's consistent and good. I thought I found a food go or Thai place till  I ate here! The food is so good, they have vegan choices that taste like meat  and their cocktails are so good tooo!  I highly recommend the assorted appetizer and their spicy lychee martini. Def my go to Thai place and a great dinner spot after work

Title: A Quick Bite with a Side of Tacos at Taco Dumbo

I've stopped by Taco Dumbo several times since its opening for a post-work nosh and have, for the most part, relished the experience. Geared towards the bustling Broadway scene and local after-work revelers, this spot understands its clientele well.

The taco selection is a strong draw, with offerings that satisfy most palates. I've ventured through nearly the entire taco menu, with the impossible taco winning top honors in my book. It's the highlight for me—a must-try. However, I'd suggest steering clear of the nori tacos if you're a taco traditionalist; they miss the mark on the expected taco experience.

Expect a crowd, especially with the extended happy hour margaritas that outlast neighboring establishments. Seating is a challenge in the compact space dominated by the bar, but there are some standing spots available if you don't mind eating on your feet.

For vegans and vegetarians, this place is a gem, offering a substantial array of choices, including the celebrated impossible tacos. My vegan colleagues gave their seal of approval, despite finding some options a tad pretentious.

On the downside, the pricing is steep for the portion sizes—plan to spend $10-$15 for a satisfying amount. While not the go-to for a full sit-down meal, Taco Dumbo is perfect for a quick, casual bite.

To sum it up, Taco Dumbo is a commendable choice for those seeking a fast, casual vegan-friendly spot. It's not quite fast food, but it's an excellent place to grab a frozen margarita and a taco or two.

I frequent La Vela alot. It's close to my job so when I'm not in the mood to cook dinner, I stop by on my way home because it's usually quiet around 5ish/6.While they make a delicious pasta & clam dish, I only gave this spot three stars because it is overpriced. I spend an easy $50 on a glass of wine, one entree and tip. No dessert or apps included. If I didn't enjoy their one entree so much and the location wasn't convenient, I'd probably never go, tbh.

Vibes: small, simple, modern with counter and small table seating Tasting notes (weekend breakfast):-Mee Jiang (peanut milk), hot: smooth, not too creamy or thick; on the sweeter side -Egg Bing with Pork Floss: fluffy egg; love the large egg to bing ratio and the presence of scallions in both components; bing is very thin with the most subtle chew; creamy accompanying sauce adds a nice savoriness; a modest amount of pork floss that filled each cross section and made for neater eating-Turnip Cake: served with oyster sauce; scallions on top add flavor and color; very lightly crispy on the outside; interior is starchy, tender to the bite with very small ham and turnip bits-Pork Belly over Rice (breakfast special): generous cilantro on top; appreciate the surprisingly large bits of meat; umami rich with a hint of sweetness; once mixed with short-grain rice, adds oiliness to the rice that is not overwhelming; pickles are a nice palate cleanserOther thoughts:-Waited about 15 minutes on a Sunday morning a little past noon for two people-Beef noodle soup only at dinner on the weekend, so will have to come back!

Came to this place after seeing it featured on Buzzfeed's Worth It! The ambience was super nice and romantic (bring a date here! Haha). We got seated at the bar first while our table got prepared so we were able to get popcorn shrimp for their happy hour ($7). It was delicious and fresh. The crunch was super crispy as well.The masa toro roll came after and this was the highlight of our meal! At a steep price of $35, it came with a lot of expectations and thankfully it was met! The tuna was so fresh and it felt like it can melt in your mouth. It paired well with the sliced up scallions in the roll. We also ordered the lamb burger and beef burger. The beef burger was delicious and juicy! It had a lot of flavor to it. We got the $5 deluxe (lettuce, tomatoes, pickles and onions) and the toppings were enough for both burgers. I didn't like the lamb burger that much because of the after taste of lamb  but that was a personal preference. I would recommend this place especially for its romantic ambience and the masa toro roll! I would come back to try their other sushi items.

We popped into this spot for brunch and were immediately seated, thanks to it not being crowded. The staff greeted us with open arms, a warm touch that set the tone for our meal. The brunch menu offered fantastic value - for roughly $18 each, we enjoyed hearty entrees along with a complimentary drink, which felt like a steal. Both dishes we tried hit the mark on flavor and satisfaction. And to top it off, the live jazz serenading us throughout our brunch elevated the whole experience. A delightful visit, indeed!

A nice spot for an Italian brunch.I loved the focaccia they served. The steak tartara was the highlight of the meal.The spaghetti was just okay and the tripe with eggs was definitely good, but not something I'd order by itself.Overall, a great meal.

This trendy NYC eatery offers a cool and energetic atmosphere for a classy dining experience. Their Italian-American cuisine is delicious, albeit pricey, but well worth it for those looking to indulge. The cocktail menu is impressive and, while expensive, provides great pairings for the meal. The complimentary bread was a standout, an appreciated touch of hospitality. All in all, it’s your quintessential high-end New York City spot that doesn't disappoint.

Title: A Local Gem with Authentic Flair

I finally decided to try the bustling local favorite around the corner from my home, and it did not disappoint. With a lively atmosphere and outdoor seating that's always in demand, this spot exudes a casual, relaxing vibe perfect for a lunch with friends.

The highlight of the meal had to be the short rib tacos – an absolute delight with their perfectly cooked corn tortillas and irresistibly fresh sour cream. It was a nostalgic throwback to the amazing tacos I savored on a recent trip to Mexico City, capturing that authentic flavor I've been craving.

Service was prompt, enhancing the experience with complimentary chips and salsa that tasted fresh and house-made. Each bite was packed with flavor, ensuring this restaurant has earned its place on my go-to list for future lunches.

I was there for a birthday celebration back in June and ordered the dinning room tasting menu. It was nice that they customized your menu with a "happy birthday" sign, but my experience was just average.The whole experience took me about 3 hours. I received an email few days before the dinner and I told them I have dietary restrictions to follow. However, they didn't make any adjustments on my menu beforehand. They offered to choose a dish from the vegetarian menu which I did. I was disappointed. I was expecting more than just getting a random dish given that I notified them few days in advance and they should have sufficient time to replace a dish based on my liking. The food were nothing to write home about. Pearl and Oyster is their signature dish but it didn't give me a wow. I have tasted similar flavor in Le Coucou which is relatively cheaper. The best part was probably the dessert. It was full of varieties but they were slightly over-sweetened. My servers are friendly and recommended a glass of delicious red wine. I received a box of cookies and chocolate and a signed menu by Chef Keller as a little gift at the end of my meal.I went to Per Se before The World's Best 50 Restaurants announced the 2019 list. I'm not surprised that Per Se has dropped from 81 in 2018 to 115 in 2019. I don't think their food quality justifies the prices I paid for.

Came in on a Monday night around 7PM after failing to snag seats at Rubirosa - we were craving pizza!We didn't need a reservation and were seated quickly because there's plenty of space. The area downstairs would probably be nice for a work happy hour or birthday event. Overall, it's clean, spacious and nicely lit.We ordered the Burrata Bruschetta and the Quattro Formaggi Pizza with Brussels Sprouts on the side. Everything hit the spot. The burrata was very smooth blending with the balsamic dressing and grape tomatoes. It comes in quarter pieces, cut easily to be eaten. The Quattro Formaggi is worth the hype especially if you like goat cheese and figs - it's the perfect balance between savory and slightly sweet. The crust is thin and crisp with a fluffy crust and not too much dough. It comes in six slices perfect to share. Lastly, the Brussels sprouts were great with the honey glaze and ricotta cheese sprinkled but the only turnoff might be the excessive oil. However, the service was great: food came about all together and warm, the water service is constantly running! We ended up drinking a lot of water because of how flavorful everything was. Unfortunately, we had no room for dessert.I'd definitely come back during the spring and summer (the space opens up) to share other pizzas!

Came here for brunch with some friends and wasn't blown away with what we ate. The flavor soju was good though.This is what we ordered to share:PaJeon (seafood pancake) - Decent but the seafood filling was very littleKorean Fried Chicken Wings - we got the soy garlic and it was pretty bland. The flavor was just not there but at least it wasn't dry.Hot & Crispy Baby Back Ribs - pretty good. Flavorful but too spicy for meBiBimBap - it was ok. Again, a little on the bland side. I know you eat it with the gochujang sauce but the dish wasn't even fragrant. BuDae JjiGae - pretty good. very flavorful and not too spicy.L.A. GalBi - this was bad. It tasted like it was boiled and we can actually taste the cow as in the meat didn't taste fresh. (ugh)Overall, I didn't think the food was bad but it just wasn't good enough where I want to tell my friends to come and try. The service was friendly and quick and the food came out piping hot.

Title: A Love-Hate Relationship with Times Square's Olive Garden

My experiences at the Times Square Olive Garden could best be described as a consistent dive into the depths of mediocrity, yet somehow, I'm drawn back time and time again. Vegan options are minimal, but they manage to scrape by with a passable pasta and marinara sauce combo, a simple salad, and a generous helping of breadsticks - all unremarkable yet strangely comforting in their predictability. A recent venture into their minestrone soup, also vegan, revealed a surprisingly flavorful addition to my usual order.

Despite its perpetual state of being crowded and an inexplicably persistent funky odor that seems ingrained in the establishment, there's a unique charm to the place. Perhaps it's the cheerful staff who seem genuinely happy to serve, or the delight of my partner that makes the culinary mediocrity somewhat endearing. The food isn't noteworthy, especially for those on a vegan diet, but it's steady, and in a city with a myriad of superior vegan options, Olive Garden's consistency has its own merit. A future inclusion of a vegan sausage option like Beyond Sausage could elevate the experience.

Olive Garden in Times Square isn't a culinary destination, but in a pinch, it's a safe bet for a vegan meal where the servers are savvy about your dietary needs, and you'll leave full, if nothing else.

After noticing the long line at Joe's earlier in the evening, curiosity led us back post-show to see if the hype was justified. Despite the crowded space, which had us eating standing up, the experience was worthwhile. I indulged in a white slice and a supreme slice, both of which were truly delightful. Joe's seems to be a popular spot for good reason – the pizza is a must-try.

Cosme, spearheaded by renowned Chef Enrique Olvera of Pujol and Chef's Table fame, brings an upscale slice of contemporary Mexican cuisine to the heart of Flatiron. Although since its lauded opening, prices have surged, it's a price point that may lead some diners, myself included, to hesitate, particularly when it comes to brunch—costs that aren't transparently shared on their website.

Venturing in on a Saturday for brunch, Cosme's space impressed with its sleek, industrial charm and comfortably spaced seating. As daylight cast a glow over minimalist glassware and furniture, the ambiance remained somewhat reserved, with the restaurant at just a third of its capacity.

The drinks, like the $17ish margarita, though served with a flair on chunky ice and a striking half-salt rim, didn't break the mold. The starters, including an arctic char tostada and burrata with veracruzana and quelites, shone for their fresh ingredients and especially for the irresistible tortillas, albeit at prices ($23ish and $18ish, respectively) that felt steep for the portions.

The main event, a lamb barbacoa at around $70, was where Cosme truly dazzled. The generous portion of succulent, slow-cooked meat and veggies, transforming into a delightful DIY taco affair, could satisfy anywhere from two ravenous to four moderate appetites. This dish alone would draw me back to Cosme.

Dessert kept to the classics, with a whimsical churro and deep chocolate dip for about $12, perfectly accompanied by a cappuccino. Service throughout the meal was polished and smooth, with reservations surprisingly easy to snag during the day.

Cosme is a must-visit for those unperturbed by price or on the hunt for unparalleled, luxurious Mexican fare in NYC. Yet for those watching their wallets, Cosme's sister locale, Atla, offers a more affordable glimpse into Olvera's culinary vision.
My favorite healthy counter service place in nyc! All of the bowls and tartines are delicious and balanced healthy meals that make you feel good! You have to try the cashew cheese, it is amazing.

I came here during "the early bourbon" (12pm-6pm daily).I love the bar area and the countertop looks really cool. It's a chill place with a nice laidback atmosphere. The bartenders don't pry and let you do your own thing while they're doing their own thing (my bartender was reading a book when no one needed to be helped).My first drink was the old fashioned ($8) which was okay. It was a bit too bitter and it seems like they used a ton of bitters when watching them make it. It was like four dashes of two different types of bitters. My second drink was the noreaster ($8) which tasted like a Kentucky mule. It was tasty and refreshing. They don't have a lot of cocktail options for their early bourbon menu but the drinks were not bad.Bourbon is my favorite spirit so I would love to come back and try some of their other bourbon drinks.

Title: Casual Spot with Vibrant Vibes and Friendly Bartenders

Review:
I recently visited this super casual bar during my one-night stay in NYC, and the vibes couldn't have been better! As we checked in, we were treated to complimentary shots, enhancing the welcoming atmosphere. One bartender, celebrating her birthday, was exceptionally friendly, sharing birthday shots and engaging with our group. Her warmth and helpful recommendations on where to go next were a highlight, making us feel right at home.

The reason for my 4-star rating is the mixed experience with the staff. While we adored one bartender, another gave off less than stellar vibes – nothing deal-breaking, just a noticeable contrast. Additionally, the bathroom was quite small and could have been cleaner, though it was manageable.

Despite these minor points, for anyone coming into the city and looking to dive into the nightlife with helpful, local tips, this spot is definitely worth a visit!

I'm caught somewhere between a 3-star and a 4-star review. Cafe Cluny was good. It was fine. The food was fresh and well prepared. I wasn't blown away by anything in particular though. I suppose this is an upscale neighborhood restaurant, but not a dining destination as it once was in its hay-day. Cafe Cluny is a shoe box of a restaurant. My friend and I were sat up front where tables were more or less crammed together. People kept bumping into our chairs and reaching over us. I may have jostled the light fixture with my arm while I was putting my coat on. Even on a Thursday night, the restaurant was quite crowded, making it a little too loud for my liking. The service was excellent. It was efficient and the waitress knew the menu like the back of her hand, especially when we asked questions about ingredients in certain dishes [my friend has a peanut allergy]. Hamachi Tartare [$19]: The hamachi tartare was beautifully presented. Albeit, I'm not sure what the foam and edible flowers were about. The dish was light and delicate. I was under the impression, however, that wasabi and ginger were ingredients in this dish and I don't think that came through at all. Both the green peas and fish roe popped in your mouth, like a nice little burst of springHousemade Ravioli [$29]: I love when a restaurant makes their own pasta dough. There's just something about freshly made pasta.I enjoyed the yam filling which was particularly light. The spinach cream sauce was really nice. And the hazelnuts provided a nice texture contrast to the smoothness of the rest of the dish. Supposedly, there's suppose to be a kick of wasabi, but I didn't taste that either. Apple Tart Tartine [$10]: This apple tart tartine is one that would make Paul Hollywood proud. You can see the layers of flakey dough when you cut into the pastry. You could hear the crunch too. The salted caramel ice cream on top was good, but I've definitely had better [like at any artisanal ice cream shop]. The apples were soft enough, they were fine.I also had a glass of pinto gris [$13].I paid $86 after tax and tip. I don't know that I need to come back to Cafe Cluny. It's definitely expensive for what it is. If you live in the neighborhood, by all means, go.

It's such a shame this place closed!!! Dan and I went here when he used to live nearby in Harlem. It was the perfect spot for some good frozen margaritas and yummy Mexican food. They had a great happy hour too! I got a quesadilla and Dan got a burrito.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Lombardi's

I ventured into Lombardi's, the renowned first pizzeria in America, with high expectations. While I personally found the pizza's taste and texture more appealing than Joe's – a sentiment not shared by my dining companion – the experience didn't quite justify the hype for me.

The price tag felt steep at approximately $30 for a pizza that struggled to satisfy two appetites. We opted for the popular double pepperoni red pie, which was decent but didn't wow us. The intrigue remains whether a different choice, such as the white pie, might have elevated the meal.

It's also worth noting that Lombardi's is a cash-only establishment, and should you need it, the ATM will set you back an extra $3.25. The silver lining was the service: friendly and attentive, which was a plus on a busy Saturday without any wait.

In summary, Lombardi's offers semi-decent pizza with a side of history. If you're in the area and curious about the first pizzeria in the U.S., it could be worth a stop, but I wouldn't recommend going out of your way for it.

Don't know why there isn't higher stars! The place is great and so friendly/accommodating! Went there for happy hour, they have a great menu especially the food. Had the potstickers, which were flavorful and the chicken (boneless) wings. Loved the seasoning on the wings. Kudos for the great service!

After months of anticipation, I finally seized the opportunity to dine at the renowned sushi spot, slipping in just before the post-5pm rush. Opting for the 6 roll set, I was not disappointed. The lobster, scallop, and crab were delightful, but it was the fish hand rolls that truly stole the show - the salmon, tuna, and hamachi were exceptional. A special nod to the restaurant's no-tip policy which underscores their commitment to ethical service practices. Count me in for a return visit, with a note to self for a fish-focused order next time!

Average Korean food experience that got ruined after noticing a large cockroach on the wall. When we saw the cockroach, we immediately informed the server, who was too scared to kill it herself (can't say I blame her). She informed the kitchen and that was the end of the story. Nobody bothered to take care of the cockroach and everyone went about their day. After a while, the cockroach dropped from the wall and disappeared into god knows what hole. During this turn of events, our appetites transitioned from hungry to nonexistent. Thankfully we were halfway through our meal, so at least this review won't be all about the roach. We got the Korean Fried Chicken wings as an appetizer. Despite asking for very hot wings, we got  them non-spicy. The wings not only had no heat to them, but were in fact sweet. They were crispy and had a good chunk of meat in them though, so if you are not a fan of spicy food, this appetizer is perfect for you.We got the Spicy Pork Bulgogi, Galbi, Beef Bulgogi, and Kimchi Jigae as our mains, ordered from most to least favorite. At this point it is no surprise to  you that the Spicy Pork Bulgogi was anything but spicy. However, I'll admit, it was packed with flavor. The galbi was also tasty, but galbi always is: all you do is grill beef short ribs, which is truly hard to mess up. The beef bulgogi unfortunately felt too shredded rather than sliced, which is how it should have been. Finally, the kimchi jigae. There were two pieces of tiny meat in that dish, and the rest was all kimchi. Normally I wouldn't even mind this since I love kimchi, but the flavors were just not there. At each spoonful I was forcing my tastebuds to like something with no avail.We did get some soju for the table and that helped us take the cockroach incident lightly. The prices ain't cheap, but they are nowhere near the sucking-your-wallet-dry Ktown prices, which is one positive.

I walked into this restaurant for a team lunch totally unaware of its star chef owned background. So let's say I had 0 expectations or opinions as I walked in. The restaurant to my surprise was on the basement and we had to take the stairs to get down from the ground level. The place looked classy and the interior decor is something that a lot of restaurants can take cue of.We came here unplanned and the restaurant manager still let us (group of 5) in after a bit of thought. As we walked in, the restaurant offered more visual delight with how it was designed and I was just 'Wow'ed. This only made me set my expectation bar higher by the time we ordered the food.We were greeted warmly by the service person  who informed us of the 'Restaurant Week' and what options they offer for the current day. Even the person who was filling/refilling the water everytime  it was getting lower seemed nice.The menu, true to NYC standards was pricier and I ordered a Cavatappi pasta without the spicy lamb most of my team went for the Restaurant week menu. We were offered a sample taster cake as a starter. It was too good and I knew we were going to be set up for a great meal, right away.Alas, the wait game started and people were pouring in. The restaurant was growing louder with every passing minute and the crowd strength resounded throughout the place. With every passing bowl and plate, we started wishing if that would be ours but they were not.Finally after almost a 35-40 minute wait, appeared our Angel who brought in a large bowl of pasta that looked straight out of heaven. I frantically mixed the  grated cheese on the pasta and took a plunge straight into it.Then I realized it was indeed a plunge. Yes, all the expectations that skyrocketed me, plummeted and came spiraling down as if I took a Sky dive from an airplane without a parachute. I mixed the pasta further more, hoping that I had probably missed the trick and to my disappointment, the more I tasted the more I was disappointed.The pasta was cold mostly and was undercooked in a lot of places giving a hard time biting through. I convinced myself that I was probably unlucky like a kid who probably chose wrongly, the only candy he could pick from the shop and hoping others would still be great. I got rest of my food boxed, thanked and returned to work, Hungry.

After working late, I turned to Riko for a late-night meal delivery. They impressed with their promptness, yet the food itself was a mixed bag. I ordered the chicken combination that came with white rice, beans, and maduros. Unfortunately, the chicken's dryness detracted from what I anticipate in a flavorsome Peruvian dish—it lacked the juicy tenderness that typically makes it a pleasure to eat. The maduros fell short as well; they were tough when I was anticipating a soft, melt-in-your-mouth experience. The rice and beans were standard, but they didn't compensate for the other elements' shortcomings. While I might consider giving Riko another chance by dining in, I'm hesitant to opt for delivery again.

Title: A Staple in Chinatown with Authentic Bites

After frequenting this spot for two decades, I've come to terms with the service—it's not the cheeriest, but it's what you'd expect from a traditional Chinese restaurant in Chinatown. The value is unbeatable (#cheapeats), and I find myself constantly craving their sesame chicken and egg fried rice, which always tastes best on-site.

My wife's perennial favorite is the curry beef stew, characterized by its generous portions that are perfect for sharing with just an extra side of rice. The noodles warrant a special mention for their exceptional quality, with my personal favorite being the fish ball noodle soup with egg noodles, sadly not pictured.

Sadly, a recent incident involving a hair found in the siu mai deducts a star from this review. In terms of rating:
- Food: 3 stars
- Taste: 4 stars
- Service: 3 stars
- Hygiene (due to hair in food): 1 star

Overall, this is a spot that's endured the test of time for us, balancing familiarity with hearty and satisfying meals.

Listen you certainly do not have to be a vegetarian or vegan to love this place. It's almost wizardry because the menu to me isn't super appealing but the final product is.The recommendation from our server was 4-6 dishes for 2 people and we shared 4 + 1 dessert and that was plenty.We tried...1. Avocado Lettuce Cups $16 (2 to an order)Sounds and looks super simple but it was insanely good, complex & I can understand why people order multiple of these.2. Half Roasted Cauliflower $16Our least favorite because I feel like I could technically make a variation of this at home 3. Pine Nut Lemon Spaghetti $26The most filling of dishes, creamy (without cream for you lactose intolerant peeps) and the stand out dish is the night 4. Dosa: Smokey Eggplant $20Basically a wrap made from rice batter, with eggplant inside with a tomato chutney, coconut yogurt and cilantro sauce. Yum5. Dessert: Carrot Soft Serve $16Bits of carrot cake, black sugar syrup with rum raisin & candies ginger. Outstanding & taste like a carrot cake in liquid from. Pretty large & so filling we didn't finish it shockingly.From the decor to food to lovely service, this place is easily one of my favorite restaurants and I'll be returning to (over ABC Kitchen too:)

I came here before a theater show. I will say that the service and food turnaround is really quick, without making you feel like they want you out of the table as soon as possible. The wait staff was helpful in making recommendations and offering advice on food choices. This place is CASH ONLY. they have an ATM for you to use. It's pretty spacious and has seating for larger groups, they also are portioned to let themselves out for private events if you choose. I do like the decor, lots of wood and they have some spanish themed pieces on the wall, looks like a little restaurant in spain as you travel the roads between cities. While they have larger plates, we chose the hot tapas- we had  the dates, the chorizo in wine sauce, the shrimp and the steak on bread slices. I highly recommend the dates and the shrimp, the sauce for the latter was fantastic. The other dishes were great as well, they rounded out the meal, I would say everything was really flavorful and uniquely prepared. I also got the honey ice cream crepes for dessert which were delish and they come with preserves. total bill was $50

Delicious and affordable jumbo meal during the covid-19 pandemic.  You order through a pick up/service window (or pick up from an online order) so there is minimal contact with others.  The staff is always super friendly; the woman who took my order sounded genuinely sorry when she said that they ran out of all meats except for the curry fish the first time I tried to order one night (about thirty minutes before they were going to close at 9pm).  I came by another day (earlier, around 7pm) and ordered the jumbo meal, which comes with three meats and three sides for $30 (though the price may be higher if you order online as opposed to ordering when you get to the window). Wait time to receive the food was about ten minutes.Got the jerk chicken, curry goat, and oxtail for the meats and mac n cheese, rasta pasta, and mixed veggies for the sides.  Everything was so full of flavor! How did they make the jerk chicken and rasta pasta have a kick without any visible pepper sauce?  Must have been the dry rub seasoning-- either way, so satisfying.  Even the mixed veggies (steamed cabbage, green beans, carrots) are tasty.  Would definitely recommend for take out, mon!

I've been here on two separate Saturday afternoons. The space has a coffee shop at the front, with more formal table service at the back. There are two large communal tables (at the front by the Koni coffee) that also offer Baodega table service, and usually have a few people working on their laptops. The staff are all wonderful, and on both occasions, I've seen the same lady single handedly constructing fresh soup dumplings/xiao long bao behind the window. I've ordered the Dan dan noodles ($10) and the beef stew noodle soup ($18), both of which were well-portioned and flavorful. I will certainly be back!

Title: A Gem of a Find for a Local Bar Experience

My partner and I absolutely adored this local bar located conveniently close to our hotel. While the Tito's on the rocks I ordered was decent, though not exceptionally generous for the standard $10 price tag in the area, it didn't detract from the overall experience.

The establishment presented itself as a clean and inviting space, definitely scoring points for its upscale vibes in comparison to your typical neighborhood watering hole. The unique touch of our bartender pulling double duty as a DJ was truly the highlight of our night. The mix of Top 50, Latin, and lively dance tunes created an irresistibly energetic atmosphere.

The crowd was amicable, contributing to a great vibe, and the staff were welcoming, save for the door guy who played up the 'tough guy' act but was completely harmless. We thoroughly enjoyed our evening and have made a mental note to return on our next trip to the area.

Dining at this establishment proved to be a sublime experience with a culinary finesse that justifies the slightly steep prices. The chef's commitment to gastronomic excellence is evident in each dish, masterfully crafted with an array of sauces and floral elements that enhance without overwhelming. The proteins and mains were executed flawlessly, reflecting a patient and skilled kitchen. The standout dish, Oysters in Bone Marrow, was a sumptuous affair of buttery richness that should not be missed.

Title: Elevated Dim Sum Delights in Chinatown

Tucked away in the bustling streets of Chinatown, NY, lies a dim sum haven that requires an elevator ascent. With spacious seating, my group of four arrived early at 10:30 am to outsmart the crowds that this place rightfully attracts.

Positioned right by the kitchen, we witnessed the magic of freshly prepared dim sum as it rolled out. The staff orchestrates the cart service with efficiency, ensuring a steady flow of steaming baskets to our table. The dumplings were notably plump, and the meats succulent. Although the variety wasn't the widest I've encountered, the offerings were more than sufficient to satisfy our cravings.

A standout for both taste and Instagram-worthiness were the custard piggy buns. After indulging in a diverse spread of 10 different items, the check was pleasantly modest – a mere $17, inclusive of tax and tip. For a genuine dim sum experience without the frills, this spot hits the mark.

Title: A Tasty Twist on Tacos at This Unique Eatery

I recently visited this charming little spot that puts an inventive spin on traditional tacos, and I must say, it’s a delightful culinary detour. While it's hard to classify their offerings as standard tacos, they've mastered the art of fusion with their scrumptious chicken tikka roti, akin to a kati roll, which I found absolutely delicious.

The concept is brilliant, and since their grand opening, they’ve expanded the menu substantially. Out of the new additions, the chicken tikka naan is a showstopper for me. It strikes the perfect balance in size, unlike the smaller roti options that are reminiscent of street tacos.

For those with a penchant for something more robust, the lamb will not disappoint—it’s yummy indeed! Plus, they accommodate cravings for an extra kick of flavor by offering garlic naan for an additional charge.

The staff exudes friendliness, contributing to the welcoming atmosphere. Be mindful that the eatery itself is quite compact, with only outdoor seating available. But if you’re in the mood for something uniquely tasty and don’t mind dining al fresco, this is the spot to try!

Restaurant Review:

I recently dined at a charming spot I'd been eyeing since catching a glimpse of its photogenic dishes on social media. Admittedly, the entrance can be a bit elusive since the restaurant nestles below street level, but the welcoming presence of staff outside is a helpful touch.

Immediately, the service left an impression. Andres, our waiter, was the epitome of patience and warmth, enhancing our experience from start to finish. This place boasts house-made pasta where diners mix and match shapes and sauces to their liking. I went for the Tagliatelle Carbonara at $19, while my boyfriend tried the Cavatelli with Broken Meatball for $20.

The ambience struck a cozy balance between dim lighting and a subtle romantic vibe, further sweetened by candlelight and adorable heart-shaped bread accompanying our meals. Be warned—the portions here are generous, and we almost succumbed to a carb-induced slumber.

Both pasta dishes were meticulously al dente, though the Cavatelli proved a bit unwieldy. Sauces were flavorful, although mine had an unusual aftertaste that didn't quite hit the mark. It's a pleasant spot to satisfy Italian cravings with a touch of cuteness, but it lacks the wow factor that compels a quick return. That said, I'm intrigued by the idea of dining beneath their window roofs in the future.

Title: A Class Above: Il Mulino Prime Stands Out

In a city where the name Il Mulino sparks images of classic Italian fare, there's a unique twist to the tale on a bustling Soho street corner. While its siblings across town are synonymous with heartwarming pastas and traditional Italian-American dishes, Il Mulino Prime carves out a distinct niche as a high-end steakhouse.

Il Mulino Prime retains the charm of the original on West 3rd Street, yet sets itself apart with a meat-centric menu. Their pièce de résistance: prime cuts of beef, dry-aged to perfection for 30 days, offering a symphony of flavors that both meat aficionados and Italian cuisine lovers can appreciate.

The sumptuous steaks harmonize with the restaurant's stellar pasta offerings, ensuring that the essence of Il Mulino's heritage is well represented. Service here is impeccable – attentive without intruding, efficient yet warm.

Whether you're in search of a superb steak or a delightful Italian meal, Il Mulino Prime in Soho marries the best of both worlds under one roof, making it a standout in the family of Il Mulino eateries.

Title: A Delightful Vegetarian Experience at Live and Dine

My recent visit to Live and Dine offered an impressive foray into the vegetarian culinary scene. The atmosphere immediately set a cool and inviting tone, creating a comfortable ambiance perfect for casual dining. Live and Dine exceeded my expectations with its array of delectable vegetarian options. Each dish I sampled was a testament to their commitment to flavor, particularly the Brussels sprouts, which were prepared to perfection.

However, the highlight of my meal was the spicy veggie sliders. As a newcomer to this dish, I was pleasantly surprised by the bold flavors and satisfying heat that made these sliders stand out. They're a must-try for anyone who appreciates a spicy kick to their meal.

Live and Dine has solidified its spot on my list of top dining spots. For those seeking a vibrant atmosphere and scrumptious vegetarian cuisine, I wholeheartedly recommend giving this franchise a visit. 

- Sha

I've become a regular at this spot for its fantastic happy hour scene, where the live polka band and an excellent selection of beer create an irresistibly festive atmosphere that I've enjoyed countless times with friends and colleagues. The service at the bar is top-notch, with staff that earn an easy A+ for friendliness and efficiency. However, there's a stark contrast when it comes to the table service – the waitresses and hostesses have consistently displayed an off-putting attitude over the years. It's disappointing, as it detracts from the otherwise vibrant and welcoming vibe of the restaurant. It seems as if this behavior is ingrained in the service culture, which is a real shame and something I hope management will address.

I recently visited a charming little nook perfect for a brisk luncheon, boasting an array of vegetarian and vegan delights. On a quest for something wholesome, I opted for the Gado Gado—a vibrant cornucopia of tofu, tempeh, and a medley of vegetables doused in peanut sauce. While the tempeh's meaty guise was intriguing, I found the dish's flavors not to my liking, leaving me unable to finish. However, my companion's satisfaction with her flavorful Dabu Dabu has me eager to return and explore more of the menu.

Really solid taco spot in a location that you wouldn't really expect it in. I'm a sucker for corn tortillas, and these were great. We got six tacos (two shrimp, two cheeseburger, the short rib, and the chicken), an al pastor quesadilla, and guac. We liked all the tacos, with the cheeseburger being our favorite, and we'd get all of them again, minus the chicken maybe. The guac was good, but the highlight of the dish was the oversized chips that came with it. We were (very surprisingly) not that into the quesadilla -- I'd love to try the other quesadillas/tostadas next time, though.Overall, very good food for a decent price in an area of the city that could really use it.

Title: Great Food in a Less-Than-Great Setting

I arrived at the restaurant with high hopes, fueled by the waves of Instagram praise and widespread acclaim. Thankfully, the food lived up to the hype; it was nothing short of excellent. The butternut squash appetizer, $10 glasses of wine, a hearty chicken parm, and a savory Bianca pizza amounted to a reasonable $82 bill. Despite the food's triumph, the experience was marred by the restaurant's cramped interior, which turned uncomfortably hot and claustrophobic.

The reservation system also fell short. Despite a near-punctual arrival for a 7:30 reservation, we were seated a half-hour late, which seemed to defeat the purpose of booking in advance. Once seated, the proximity to neighboring diners stifled conversation and exacerbated the crowded atmosphere.

Service was a mixed bag; our waitress was pleasant but lacked attentiveness. Furthermore, the restaurant's cash-only policy was a minor inconvenience, compounded by the awkward placement of their ATM amidst clutter and traffic.

Ultimately, while the cuisine was a delight, the environment detracted significantly from the overall experience. It's unlikely I'll dine in again, though I might consider takeout for another taste of their delectable offerings.

Title: A Convenient but Mixed Experience by the Water

Location: ★★★★★
Convenience reigns at this eatery, situated directly across from Brooklyn Bridge Park's water play space. The 11am opening time is perfect for families looking to grab lunch post-play.

Ambiance & Comfort: ★★☆☆☆
The restaurant boasts ample outdoor seating with shaded umbrellas—a savior on sunny days—as well as an indoor option. Yet, the latter disappointed during our visit; with no air conditioning and only two fans providing relief on a sweltering day, the indoor climate was less than ideal.

Menu Variety: ★★★★☆
From pizzas and sandwiches to pastas, the menu caters to a range of tastes. A solid selection for a quick bite.

Service & Atmosphere: ★★☆☆☆
Unfortunately, the atmosphere was marred by loud, explicit music played by the staff, which persisted despite a request to lower the volume. It wasn't the family-friendly environment I'd hoped for.

Overall, a mixed bag: Great location and menu options, but the comfort and music choices could use some reconsideration for a better family dining experience.

Dropped by a quintessential local Irish pub after work and was immediately charmed by its festive atmosphere, complete with a pair of well-maintained pool tables that seemed to be a draw for enthusiasts, judging by the regulars with their own cues. Service was prompt and friendly. The beer selection was what you'd expect from an authentic pub, with a decent range of choices. Opted for a pint of Smithwick's Ale, which was perfectly poured and hit the spot. Would recommend for a casual evening out with friends or unwinding after the day's work.

I have been coming here for the last five years and I have thoroughly enjoyed it. I tend to go for the lunch special where you get your protein, rice and soup for $12. It is so filling I usually take some home for dinner. The general tso chicken here is also one of my favorite. You can also call ahead for pick up, just give them 10-20 mins heads up.

Title: Cozy Spot for Authentic Italian - Penne Vodka Delight

I recently savored the penne with vodka sauce from this local gem as part of their $10 lunch special. Although the portion was on the smaller side, the value was undeniable. Using the Ritual app, ordering and pick-up were seamless and efficient—perfect for a workday lunch.

Over time, the penne vodka has emerged as a crowd-pleaser among my colleagues and me. This restaurant remains a top choice for anyone in search of genuine Italian cuisine. Despite its compact size, the place is lively and bustling, particularly during peak hours, adding to its charm. A reliable spot for a satisfying Italian meal!

Great new spot in the east village. The waitress was an absolute sweetheart and she had the chef come over and explain how the pizza was made and all of the different types of dough and types of pizza (multi grain, regular, tonda, etc.). Very cute and cozy and the pizza was delicious. Currently they are BYOB Because they are still waiting for their liquor license but there are nearby wine shops you can head to to grab a bottle. The restaurant currently charges a fee of $7 to open for you so keep that in mind if you do buy a bottle from somewhere. Will definitely be back again for more delicious pizza!

It's hard to find a good pho place in NYC, oddly enough. I would highly recommend that you try the pho here with the short rib ($16 +$6). The broth itself is extremely delicate, which I love. The bowl is huge, i know it doesn't look like it in my first photo but I did a comparison of the bone to my forearm in the second. It is huge! The grilled pork chop and fried egg on rice were delicious as well ($16+$3). I can get this dish closer to home for under $10. Of course the service was great, it's NYC.All in all, it's a bit pricey but the experience of the pho was worth it.

Title: Authentic Italian Bliss in the LES

If you're in search of that home-cooked Italian warmth in the Lower East Side, look no further. Nestled among the bustling streets is this gem of a cafe that's far from average. Their culinary prowess is evident, as they offer a tantalizing new menu every day – a feature that tempts you to become a daily fixture here.

The pastas are the star of the show; each bite leaves you yearning for more, and you'll find yourself eagerly sopping up every last drop of sauce with your bread. Firm favorites include their rich, layered lasagna and the variety of hearty paninis. True to authentic Italian roots, don't expect Americanized meatball pasta here. Instead, delight in their succulent meatballs served alongside perfectly roasted potatoes.

Portion control tends to go out the window, as it's nearly impossible to resist over-ordering. And for the perfect end to a sumptuous meal, indulge in their divine tiramisu coupled with a robust Ily coffee. This cafe is not just a meal; it's a slice of Italy right in the heart of the LES.

My friend and I stopped by here to check out the happy hour $1.50 Oyster special.  We sat at the bar right in front of the oysters.  There were a few listed on the board, but the ones included in the happy hour special were not listed there.    Both were from the east coast and not briny at all. The cherry? (I think, it was about 2 months ago, so not quite sure of the name) had a crisp type of finish, but otherwise not much flavor.  This was a good base to add the toppings which were standard.  The hot sauce was quite spicy.  The other oyster Chappequa? had a bit more character and could be enjoyed with a touch of lemon juice.  Service was average.  The oyster bar is located in the Roxy hotel along with a theater and coffee shop.  The easiest way to a access it was through the coffee shop entrance.

I recently visited Mad Dog for their Taco Tuesday deal and have mixed feelings about the experience. The offer of unlimited tacos for just $20, complemented by a frozen margarita, is unbeatable and a fantastic value. However, the service left a lot to be desired. Our server was inattentive, making something as simple as refilling water or providing extra napkins a prolonged ordeal despite multiple requests. Due to the service issues, I can only rate Mad Dog 3 stars, although the food and drinks were a hit.

Title: A Cozy Spot for Asian Delights

Upon entering the establishment, patrons have a clear choice: to the left, a lively bar with high-top seating, or to the right, a more traditional dining area with backless chairs and tables. The menu, though concise, covers a range of Asian appetizers, from edamame to a selection of flavourful ramen and crispy curry rice dishes.

I opted for the beef base ramen with miso, shredded pork in pork broth, and the chicken katsu curry. Each meat dish impressed with its tenderness and depth of flavor, the soup bases were robust and warming, and the ramen eggs, whilst slightly sweeter than my preference, had yolks cooked to perfection.

Service was commendable for their attentiveness, although the ambience was slightly marred by occasional flies, a result of the restaurant's open-door policy.

In summary, this is a destination for anyone craving a comforting bowl of ramen or a hearty curry dish served in a welcoming atmosphere with high-quality ingredients. Just be prepared for a minor disturbance from the occasional winged visitor.

Bareburger has the best vegan burger! The Original Impossible burger is 100% vegan but tastes and bleeds like meat. I usually am picky with veggie burgers and am not a fan of the grainy, rice/bean-based veggie burgers that most burger places serve. However, I couldn't believe that the Original Impossible burger was not meat! It was juicy and tender and just as good as a regular burger. If you don't eat meat, I highly highly recommend trying the Original Impossible burger.

Ocean Prime is an upscale steakhouse/seafood restaurant located in the heart of midtown. I decided to check it out during Restaurant Week and was really impressed by the food, ambience and service. The restaurant has outdoor seating available outside for warm summer nights, and inside has a bustling front bar area and a larger dining area in the back. The space is very elegant with modern, dim lighting and dark finishes. We were seated in the dining room and the service from beginning to end was impeccable. Our waiter checked on us frequently, keeping our wine glasses full, and bringing the courses at a perfect pace where we didn't feel rushed. They have an interesting cocktail menu (there was one with dry ice smoke!) and a full wine menu. Our waiter helped advise our choices and we ended up splitting a bottle of wine we quite enjoyed. From the restaurant week menu, we both ordered the caesar salad, 8 oz filet mignon with cauliflower pureé, kale and mushroom medley, and the 5 layer carrot cake. We were started off with a warm bread basket with assorted rolls. The filet mignon was perfection! It was incredibly tender and the seasoning was on point. The accompanying sauce was also delicious. I would love to come back to try some of their other steaks if this was any indicator of the quality of their meat! The 5 layer carrot cake was a perfect finish to the meal. It had a rich buttercream and a great carroty kick.I see on their regular menu they have a 13 layer carrot cake that is probably even more impressive.Overall, I had a great experience at Ocean Prime - ambience, service, and food were superb. I would recommend this place for a date you are trying to impress or for a celebration. Hope to be back soon!

Title: A Hidden Gem in NYC: Tavola Delights

After a half-hour stroll through the bustling streets of New York City, my husband and I were lured into Tavola by the high praise of a departing couple. The recommendation was a gift in itself, but the offer of their cozy window seat was the cherry on top, especially since the interior was dimly lit.

Our culinary adventure began with a shared margherita pizza and eggplant pesto pasta. The pizza was a triumph of textures, with a crust that managed to be both crisp and airy, though a tad more mozzarella would've been welcomed to balance the vibrant sauce. As someone who seldom opts for pasta, the eggplant dish was a delightful surprise – scant on sauce but each bite packed with flavor.

A mid-meal mishap saw me accidentally shatter a glass cup, but the staff handled the incident with grace and understanding, leaving us to revel in the wonderful dining experience. Tavola, with its friendly atmosphere and delectable offerings, has earned itself two more fans. It's a must-visit for any food lover in NYC.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Local Eatery

I recently dined at this restaurant with high hopes, only to find myself navigating a menu of hits and misses. The meal overall was a tad disappointing due to the overly heavy dishes that seemed to tip the scales away from authenticity.

The highlights were few but notable. The Sausage Party was a delightful surprise, reminiscent of flavors from back home, while the Beef Noodle Soup stood out as one of the top contenders in the city—a rich, flavorful broth paired with tender beef, though I yearn for thicker noodles to complete the dish.

On the less impressive side, the Water Spinach failed to impress, succumbing to the common pitfall of being too salty. The Clams were passable, nothing to write home about, and the Black Pepper Steak, while decent, did not live up to its Taiwanese-inspired potential.

The biggest letdown of the night was the LO BA BENG, which was overwhelmingly greasy, leaving an unpleasant heaviness that lingered long after the meal ended.

In summary, the restaurant has the potential to wow with a couple of standout dishes but needs to address the balance and authenticity of its offerings to truly shine.

Title: A Smoky Delight at Hill Country BBQ

I finally had the chance to taste the offerings at Hill Country BBQ, and it certainly lived up to the hype with truly exceptional smoked meats. The server recommended the smoked turkey, claiming it was a hot seller. Skeptical at first, I was convinced after a sample - it had an uncanny pork-bacon flavor, but I stayed true to my BBQ quest.

I went for a combo platter featuring smoked pulled pork and BBQ brisket, along with bourbon sweet potato mash and slaw, topped off with a cornbread biscuit. The meats were impeccably smoked - tender, juicy, and enhanced with a bit of extra sauce.

The bourbon sweet potato mash was a standout, arguably the best I've ever tasted – I'd love to know the bourbon they use. However, the slaw fell a bit flat and could use a kick, perhaps a pinch of smoked paprika for an inventive twist.

The moist cornbread was the perfect finisher, balancing the textures nicely. Ample portions meant a second meal to enjoy later, adding value to an already satisfying experience.

Hill Country BBQ earns a solid 4 stars from me. Don't hesitate to stop by for your smoked BBQ fix!

I recently visited this restaurant for a business lunch and opted for the warm lobster Cobb salad. The salad was delightful, featuring generous portions of succulent lobster tails and claws. However, the lettuce serving was disappointingly small, making the salad seem more like a side dish rather than an entrée. Aside from this, the experience was very pleasant. The restaurant offers great outdoor seating, enhancing the dining atmosphere, and the service was attentive and efficient. Overall, a recommended spot with just a minor tweak needed on the salad front.

One of my fave restaurants in Harlem! They never disappoint! Decided to grab lunch midday on Saturday. It was pretty packed but we were seated immediately.For starters we went for the veal meatballs and garlic bread which was DELICIOUS! I wish the portion sizes were a bit bigger but it was still worth  it. Picked the arugula salad with pears, walnuts and grilled chicken for my entree. It was a nice size and i couldn't finish the entire thing. Definitely enjoyed it. Was reminded why this is one of my fave places to grab a bite in the area

Great food!They have set brunch, with either coffee or bloody marry. There is a variety of food to choose from, and all the ones we ordered were good!The French roasts came with fresh fruits, and the one without Nutella tasted better in my opinion, as it was not overly-sweet. The Benedict was good, with nice salad dressing. The baked potatoes were also very flavorful.Portion was huge, and sharing is better if you cannot eat a lot. Great and polite service!A little noisy, and cash only.

Title: A Decent Dip into Tsukemen in NYC

I ventured into this Manhattan spot with high hopes for tsukemen, a dipping ramen popularized by a favorite YouTube blogger of mine. The Sunday afternoon timing meant no crowds and swift service. We kicked off with a white yuzu beer, which was refreshing, though more yuzu flavor would've been welcome. The karage was generous but didn't quite hit the mark for me - Hide-chan's version remains my go-to.

My partner opted for the spicy miso ramen - a solid choice, though it failed to impress. On the other hand, the spicy Saba tsukemen I ordered delivered with its thick, slightly fishy broth that I found quite pleasing. Both of our dishes featured melt-in-the-mouth charsu and the perfect chew of wavy yellow noodles.

In the end, the visit was pleasant, but after the revelation that was Ichiran, it's clear that not all ramen experiences are created equal.

I recently dined at this local gem where I indulged in their Steak Mazemen, and it left me thoroughly impressed. Though there was a slight unusual scent at first, the dish's taste was exceptional, making it easy to overlook. The steak was cooked to perfection, bursting with flavor, and the hint of smokiness infused in the mazemen from the steak truly elevated the experience. The ambiance and service were equally commendable, contributing to a delightful visit. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next meal here and would highly recommend it to anyone in search of a mouthwatering feast.

Title: A Heavenly Revolving Experience at [Restaurant Name]!

My visit to [Restaurant Name] on October 25th for a special anniversary dinner with my boyfriend was nothing short of spectacular. For food enthusiasts like me, don't forget to peek at my Instagram (@angel.eatsny) for more delicious ventures.

From the get-go, the service was top-notch, setting a phenomenal tone for the evening. Opting for the Prix Fixe menu over the buffet was a pricey but rewarding decision. My Crab Cake starter was the finest I've ever indulged in, while the char-grilled octopus my partner had was uniquely delightful.

The main course saw me savoring a sumptuous Salmon en Croute, perfect in portion and taste. Meanwhile, my boyfriend's surf and turf was an extra indulgence, featuring a succulent filet mignon and luxurious lobster (worth the additional $23). We added three sides, including an unforgettable Lobster Mac and Cheese with its rich Alfredo-like sauce and succulent lobster chunks.

While my boyfriend's Red Currant dessert was quite good, my cheesecake was the true showstopper. Its sweet strawberries and unexpected but successful hints of lime and cucumber shavings were a delight.

Our experience was amplified by the warmth and hospitality of the staff. I couldn't recommend [Restaurant Name] more for anyone seeking a memorable dining experience with a view that's as breathtaking as the food. Worth every penny and more!

I tried this restaurant after seeing it in a Bobby Flay show where  he and his daughter enjoyed an awesome breakfast.  I went here with my daughter and son and my former assistant (who now lives and work  in NYC) joined us.  This restaurant is located in the Meatpacking District right across the street from the entry point to the High Line park.  While we were waiting for my assistant to finish work, my kids and I enjoyed the Nachos $12 appetizer.  It was made with tortilla chips, cheddar cheese, black beans, guacamole, sour cream and salsa.  It was pretty good and a great value for Manhattan.  Lol.
