We also started on a bottle of 75 Cab $42.  I was thirsty after a day of walking 13 miles in Manhattan.  I ordered the Meatloaf with mashed potatoes and chicken gravy topped with onion rings $20.  It was stick to your ribs comfort food.  My daughter had the Grain Bowl $17.  It had a bunch of things that I've never hear of before, but she enjoyed it very much.  She's an old soul when it comes to her diet.  My son decided to go big or go home.  He ordered the Bubby's Burger with cheddar and fries $22.  Now THAT'S more like Manhattan... a $22 burger!  I guess he enjoyed it as he inhaled it in no time.  My former assistant ordered the Caesar Salad with chicken breast $23.  I have no clue about parking as We took the subway and then walked the Highline.  Service (Jasmine A) was awesome.  If I go back to NYC I'd like to come back here for brunch.  Cool place!  Try it.

Speedy Romeo had long been on my radar, and it finally had its turn. The size of the venue struck me upon arrival; it's larger than anticipated. Despite a busy Friday night, seating was swift, which was a pleasant surprise.

We started with the much-talked-about chicken wings, receiving a portion generous in size. They were big and succulent, with a hint of celery and a shy spice kick - satisfactory, but they didn't steal the show.

Pizza is the heart of Speedy Romeo, so we followed the waitress's advice and settled on the Dangerfield and St. Louie. The Dangerfield was a delightful white pie with meatballs and a creamy béchamel, yearning for a hint more sauce.

The arrival of the St. Louie boasted an array of toppings I usually adore, including soppressata and Provel cheese. However, its salt level was a misstep, even for someone like me who tends to overindulge in salt. To mitigate this, I found myself alternating with bites from the Dangerfield.

While the toppings left me divided, I must commend the crust's char and texture. Although I'd return to explore other pies, when it comes to the tastebud satisfaction, I'd score Speedy Romeo a modest 4 out of 8 slices.

I really love pierogi and read about Veselka online. We came in the afternoon in the time between lunch and dinner and it wasn't very crowded. I tried the anniversary bowl because it included everything I was craving: different kinds of pierogi and sausage. It was delicioius and filling. I appreciated the opportunity to try each type of pierogi. We also ordered the chili con carne, which was uneventful, but the best part of it were they raw onions that came on top. Their water comes big and filled with ice.The interior is filled with things to look at and really sets the mood for the history of Veselka. I really liked the food and the vibe and I look forward to coming back the next time I'm in New York for delicious, no fuss Ukrainian food.

3.5/5 Definitely very pricey as far as Korean food goes, and you're probably better off going to K-town, but I still loved my experience and appreciate the presence of Korean food in this part of town. I came with 3 friends on a Friday night with a reservation and got seated immediately, as it was pretty empty. The restaurant itself is pretty and the tables are very spaced out. I started the meal off with a cocktail. All of their cocktails were all on the very high end side of cocktail prices in NY (~$18), and if they're anything like the one I tried, they definitely aren't worth it. You're better off sharing a bottle of soju.Here's an overview of the dishes we tried:-Vegetarian jap chae ($16): I loved it and thought it tasted better than most jap chaes I've had-Dduk bokki (rice cakes, $14): I absolutely love Korean rice cakes in general and thought this was well done. Not too spicy, but just right to be enjoyable for the average person-Kimchi Pa Jun (kimchi pancake, $17): standard but good, extremely overpriced for what it is-Korean BBQ items: all of them were really delicious and well marinated. Three of us were going to share the Korean Barbecue Platter, but our waiter said you're honestly better off getting the items a la carte. You get 1/2 the a la carte sizes for the 4 items, so it's not better value to get the platter. I really appreciated the waiter's honesty! Just a heads up that they offered no guidance with cooking items, so hopefully you have some experience with Korean BBQ/are somewhat adept at cooking in general     -Bulgogi ($36)     -Kal bi (boneles beef short rib, $38)     -Samgyupsal (lean pork belly, $28)

Friend of a Farmer on Irving Street is a charming choice for brunch aficionados. Having not visited for some years, on a recent trip to the area, I decided to stop by for a drink, recalling their delightful little bar setup perfect for a cocktail. Their happy hour is notable, both for its great deals and the unique feature of a cheese wheel. Regularly priced drinks, however, such as the $13 glass of rosé and cocktails from $16-$18, seem steep for the setting, despite the quality of the beverages and the warmth of the bartender. If you find yourself near Caffe Panna with a thirst for a well-mixed drink, swinging by during happy hour at this cozy spot might be your best bet.

Franny's doesn't disappoint when it comes to fast casual dining with an Italian twist. Whether you're indulging in pasta, zoodles with a touch of zucchini, or diving into their pizzas, the experience is delightful. Not to be overlooked are their salads and what I consider the best tomato soup in town. The atmosphere buzzes with friendliness, and the value you get for what you spend is truly unbeatable. Highly recommended for a quick, delicious bite.

The newest location just opened in the Upper East Side, half a block away from PQR, which has been a little off lately, so this is a nice addition to the neighborhood for a reliably great classic NY slice. It's also nice that it replaced Two Boots, which hasn't been good for many many years, if ever.The grandma is also excellent, especially with some Roni Cups added.

Title: A Culinary Gem in Chinatown - Unbeatable Flavors!

If you're on the prowl for outstanding Chinese cuisine in Chinatown, look no further! This place is a treasure I just can't stop frequenting - everything on the menu is a must-try.

Service-wise, brace yourself for a bit of a language barrier - the staff are cordial but limited in English. Patience is key, but the food more than makes up for it.

The menu is a parade of stars, but let's talk highlights. The Japanese Style Dumpling is a revelation - fresh, made in-house, and my top pick. XO Rice Noodle is akin to an Asian twist on spaghetti - intriguing and scrumptious. For meat lovers, the spareribs are bite-sized perfection, while the Korean Style Short Rib will steal your heart with its tender, melt-in-your-mouth goodness. Don't overlook the Chicken Feet and Fried Dough Rice Noodle, both unique and flavorful. Seafood enthusiasts? The Seafood Pan Fried Noodle brims with oceanic delights. Beef Chow Fun outshines Pad See Ew any day, and while the Hot and Sour Lamb Casserole was just satisfactory, it's the only dish that didn't dazzle.

Price-wise, it's a steal - a 4 out of 10 on the cost scale with generous portions. My returning visits testify to the consistent quality. Tip: Do not miss out on the Japanese Fried Dumpling. It's the culinary bomb!

In conclusion, this place is a no-brainer for Chinese food lovers. Prepare for a taste bud fiesta, and remember - order liberally!

During my recent visit to the restaurant, the experience was a mixed bag. On the one hand, the ambiance was quite lovely with its deep wood decor and crisp white table linens, contributing to a spacious and open feel. The steak served was divine – cooked to perfection, flavorful, and well worth the investment. Also, the baked potato was impressively large and maintained its heat throughout the meal.

However, there were significant downsides to the visit. My server's lack of hygiene, notably digging into his backside before walking away from the table, was off-putting, to say the least. Thankfully, another staff member delivered my meal. Additionally, being seated next to the server's station meant an onslaught of noise and overheard complaining, which detracted from the dining experience. Despite checking on us often, service was slow, and small touches like offering cracked black pepper were missed.

In conclusion, while the food quality may draw me back, it would only be under the condition of a better seat and a different server, one who understands basic hygiene etiquette.

I recently dined at a local restaurant and was left with mixed feelings about the experience. The food overall merited a 3/5; while some dishes were decent, I was especially disappointed by the hunker begendi—sadly, it was the worst rendition I've had in NYC. On a positive note, the rice pudding dessert was delightful, a true saving grace of the meal. Service-wise, the staff performed admirably, earning a solid 4/5 for their friendliness and attentiveness. The ambiance was the highlight of the evening, boasting a cozy, busy, and artsy vibe, which fully deserves a 5/5. While not everything hit the mark, certain aspects of the restaurant made the visit worthwhile.

Very trendy restaurant with great service and solid ramen! I wanted to try their special of the day, which was a duck ramen, but it was sold out. I went with the Tonkotsu ramen instead. My friends and I also shared a bottle of the Junmai sake, which was served with shot glasses overflowing into a masu. Our waiter explained that the overflow is supposed to signify good fortune. It was nice to learn more about Japanese culture over dinner.

Title: Spicy Delights at a Cozy Birthday Lunch

I recently celebrated my birthday at a charming spot arranged by my BFF, and I must say, the cozy atmosphere complemented the cute interior perfectly. The lunch deal at $16 for a two-dish combination offered both variety and value. My selection of Green Curry paired with Chili Calamari hit the spot with its bold flavors and just-right spiciness – the chili sauce was love at first taste! My friend's choice of Pad Prik King Pork and Spicy Crab Meat also garnered praise for their zest and flavor. Each dish, accompanied by wholesome grain rice, was a decent portion size, bursting with fresh ingredients. If your palate yearns for something that packs a punch, the green curry and the 'grilled caramel' (presumably a typo for 'chili calamari') are must-tries. I left the restaurant not just satisfied, but thoroughly delighted with the entire meal.

Stopped in quickly to try a few baos as this place is highly regarded and we wanted to try the chocolate baos.The chicken dumplings were okay but rather plain. They needed the sour soy sauce to add some flavor.I love spicy food and tried the super spicy XLB. They were just moderately spicy and would not really recommend them for those who want truly spicy dishes. The chocolate dumplings were interesting. It was filled with I think chocolate covered banana. Very interesting though I'm not sure the value was great compared to all the other desserts in the area.Overall I'd come back to try some other items recommended here on yelp. It was rather busy even around 9pm on a Wednesday. Service was good and the food came fast.

Last night at Kyma was a revelation—a perfect blend of atmosphere, taste, and warmth that photos simply can't capture. The space itself is a chameleon, perfectly suited for anything from a romantic date to a lively family dinner or a casual meal post-work. What really sets Kyma apart is the impeccable service. The hostess led us to a cozy corner booth, and then we were in the capable hands of Jimmy, with expert wine guidance from sommelier William.

We began with a light and fruity Greek assyrtiko wine that set the tone for the meal. The tomato salad was a standout, bursting with freshness, while the tuna tartare was as visually stunning as it was delicious. The table also featured warm, irresistible pita and hummus. For the main course, the whole pink swordfish was the star—cooked to perfection, it transported us straight to the Greek islands.

Dessert was a unique and satisfying custard creation, complemented by the most delectable scoop of pistachio gelato. A final glass of Samos dessert wine was the ideal end to the culinary journey. Kyma has earned its place as my new favorite Greek haven—I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

My recent visit to this dim sum restaurant on a Saturday was a mixed bag. Despite our party of eight having a reservation, the place wasn't busy, with many empty tables suggesting walk-ins would be fine. The pricing is a tad steep compared to Chinatown's fare, averaging $5-6 per dish with no significant leap in quality.

The shrimp dumplings were disappointing, featuring not-quite-right shrimp encased in overly thick skins. However, the seafood peashoot dumpling fared better, delivering on flavor despite a slightly sticky and fragile wrapper. BBQ pork buns were standard, albeit with less filling than usual. I particularly enjoyed the minimalist and small sticky rice, although it may not satisfy those looking for ample fillings.

I'd advise against the xiao long bao; ours were deflated, and the flavors seemed off—a reminder that dim sum and XLB hail from different Chinese cuisine traditions. The pan-fried shrimp & chives dumplings were satisfyingly juicy, if a bit greasy, and the shrimp rice noodle rolls were decent but marred by less-than-fresh shrimp.

Service was unremarkable but adequate. Our meal totaled $150 before tax and tip, which feels high for the experience delivered. The tieguanyin tea, disappointingly lukewarm and bland, added $8 to our bill. On the plus side, seating was comfortable and well-spaced. Overall, this spot might not be the best value for dim sum enthusiasts, especially given the quality to price ratio.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Local Ramen Spot

After frequently passing by this quaint ramen joint, I finally decided to give it a go with my ramen-loving mother in tow. Expectations were high, especially with their tantalizing online menu boasting a plethora of broths, proteins, and toppings. 

Unfortunately, the reality was a menu much more limited in scope, with a mere three broth choices and an exclusively pork-centric protein selection. As someone with a palate geared towards chicken and fish, this was a disappointment, only exacerbated by their lack of flexibility in altering cooking methods to suit dietary preferences.

On a positive note, I can't sing enough praises for the service. The staff was exceptional, with our server exemplifying attentiveness and efficiency, ensuring our comfort and hydration throughout our meal. 

The ramen itself was satisfactory but didn't quite hit the high notes I've experienced at other specialty establishments. My mother shared this sentiment, leaving us with a lukewarm impression of the culinary experience.

In summary, a solid three stars for the food, primarily due to the limited options not matching expectations set by the online menu. However, the impeccable service is deserving of five stars, making it a place perhaps more suited for the less selective ramen enthusiast.

Chumley's offers an alluring speakeasy ambiance paired with what could easily be considered one of the city's top burgers. Though the once-raved-about Dungeness crab pot pie is no longer on the menu, the culinary adventure is still worth the trip. 

The signature off-menu burger, although served at room temperature on this visit, did not disappoint with its juicy medium-rare patty and luxurious bone marrow topping, albeit a bit overwhelming for those who appreciate a simpler burger. The beef fat fries, at a premium price, delivered on the promised aged beef flavor. Starter highlights included veal tartare and an imaginative foie gras and chicken liver mousse cannoli, while Hemingway's chili provided a symphony of flavors, perfectly countered by a dollop of creme fraiche.

Despite a few hiccups, Chumley's stands out as a prime destination for those seeking a blend of casual elegance and indulgent cuisine. It's an ideal spot for a date night that promises to impress with its culinary offerings.

Giano is known for its homemade pasta, so I came with that in mind and ordered the ravioli. It's a bowl of about ten small, spinach ricotta pieces that were the most buttery ravioli squares I've ever had. It's cooked perfectly, and the sauce is ever so slightly creamy, which helped the flavor evenly coat every bite. My friend got the salmon, which was on another level. It's a huge filet that was maybe the best restaurant salmon I've ever had. It was so warm and tender. It comes with peas and fava beans, which were also delicious. No lie, it was a spectacular dish.We also shared the meatballs appetizer, which was so impressive to me. The sauce was so fresh and tasty, and the meatballs were huge. Loved every bite. The restaurant itself is homey, romantic, and rustic. There's really lovely decoration along with exposed brick walls. The service was so genial and welcoming. The waiter/boss man was right out of Italy - I just loved watching him talk with his hands while telling us the night's specials. Overall, major neighborhood gem vibes. Recommend for date night or pasta night at a contemporary Italian restaurant.

I didn't know here until last night. It was late night I was hungry but kind late after10:30. Usually I stayed Chinatown I gave up food after 11:00 because most are closed but I found out before 11 many Italian restaurant opens! After broadway Show will be more easy !! Any way this pizza place no seat place give us tasty pizza after 10:30!! Thank god. Crust is skinny but little chewy. Sauce is very authentic with some garlic slice! My recommend is margarita! It just $3 ! Cheap! And again tasty ! I really come back again when I stay in Chinatown!!

Beware: they only accept cash, mastercard, amex or discover. NO VISA (reason being too many charge backs have hapIt's probably the best buddae jiggae (army stew) in NYC, with a close second being Bangia. This place is great to eat at early on your night (dinner) or after a night of drinking.First time?- Watermelon Soju (32.99)- Buddae Jigae (32.99)- Corn Cheese- Seafood Pancake- Soy Garlic WingsTotal is around $150Easily can feed five with this.Fairly quick wait despite a Friday night as well and good service. Just a little more on the expensive side.

Title: A Vegetarian-Friendly Vietnamese Delight with Irresistible Happy Hour Deals

I recently visited a charming Vietnamese eatery that truly captured my heart with its warm ambiance and delectable cuisine. With a variety of vegetarian options on the menu, this place is a haven for those who prefer plant-based dishes.

The service was notable for its friendliness and efficiency, ensuring a pleasant dining experience right from the start. An added bonus was the happy hour – an absolute steal with $4 beers and $5 house sake.

We kicked things off with vegetarian dumplings, which were simply scrumptious, setting a high bar for what was to follow. The vegetarian Ban Mi sandwich didn't disappoint either; packed with fresh veggies and encased in perfectly crisp bread, it was a flavorful journey in every bite. The Vegetarian Pho, brimming with noodles and veggies, was yet another dish that warmed our souls.

Our friends echoed our sentiments, thoroughly enjoying their meals. All in all, this spot is a gem for anyone craving Vietnamese flavors – I can't recommend it enough!

Environment: it looks like they transform a garage into a restaurant which very interesting. Nice place to take a date to. Its little small because the table was so close to each other but that is normal for the space they have. If it winter highly recommended stay away from the door because wind does get to u.  Food: their good was great. Strong favor which surprising because most of the time we have to go to place that cook real asian food to get that taste. This place seem to run by American and still give me the taste of real Asian taste. The cheese cake was like home make. It so good even though I'm not a big fan of cheese cake. Great decorations on the food. I wouldn't order bone marrow cause it barely have anything on it. The coconut noodle soup was great, they give strong favor of coconut in it. Not like other place said coconut and barely any taste of coconut. They also give us a bottle of favor which has mint, cucumber, orange,...  it a nice decorations and natural favor water. I love it. Service: they are so nice and yes they seem to be all Male. The good thing they did that I rarely find in other place is a smile and I mean everytime they come they also  come with a smile and they are so friendly. They offer us whatever we need. I would give 10/10 for service. Its not because they male and I give it. Other places also have nice looking waiter but they never smile and dont seem to be friendly at all. This place has nice looking waiter, they are smiling and friendly to every customer. That is the service each restaurant  need. Highly recommended to come here try out the food and great services.

If you're in search of a quick, affordable meal without the frills, [Restaurant Name] is worth a stop. The smaller, yet satisfying portions of their rolls make for perfect snacks or a light lunch. Our group sampled the goat, lamb, beef, and chicken options, with the unanimous favorite being the flavor-packed chicken tikka.

Be warned, the naan wraps can be oily, so come prepared with an appetite for extra napkins. Seating is scarce in this cozy eatery, so snagging a table might feel like a mini-victory.

While the wraps are reasonably priced at $7, the lassi is somewhat steep at $5 for a small bottle. However, they are utterly delightful — the strawberry mirrors a fresh smoothie, and the mango is equally delectable. Though the honeydew was unavailable, having both wraps and lassis left me content and full. It's a spot where the costs can accumulate, but the satisfaction from the meal justifies the expenditure.

I absolutely love this place. They serve some pretty authentic chinese dishes at reasonable prices. I'm a fan of their drunken noodles because the soup is so flavorful and tasty, especially with the fried ground pork and fried garlic in it. The thick noodles are also chewy and perfectly cooked! I always get this whenever I'm here and I highly recommend this dish to anyone! This time I also got their fried turnip cake as an appetizer and it was so delicious. The fried skin was thin but crispy and mixed really well with the sauce drizzled on the top! Would recommend here to anyone who's looking for some solid noodle dishes at good price.

Title: A Hidden Gem That Truly Lives Up to Its Name

My dining experience at this particular restaurant was long overdue, but it certainly did not disappoint—earning my wholehearted recommendation for anyone in search of top-notch cuisine.

Upon entering, my friends and I opted to forgo the fare at the neighboring Ace Hotel's eatery, a decision we wouldn't regret. We kicked things off with a generous kale chicken salad and a delightfully fresh Crab & Avocado roll, both of which were perfect for sharing among the three of us.

The true star of the evening, however, was the filet mignon. This dish commanded attention not only with its presentation but also with a taste that outshone even well-known steakhouses. It was so impressive that I am already planning a return visit for my husband's birthday—he's a serious carnivore, and I'm confident that this restaurant will impress.

The name of this establishment aligns beautifully with the experience they offer, where the quality extends beyond the plate to include attentive and engaging service. If the food is the heart of this restaurant, the service is certainly the soul. It's a rare find that genuinely excels in all aspects, making every visit memorable.

Title: Consistently Satisfying with a Minor Hiccup

I recently dined at one of my go-to chain restaurants, XFF, and was delighted to find one during my shopping trip last Thursday. My boyfriend, an avid fan, insisted we stop for dinner, and we weren't disappointed. We indulged in some of our staples: the Liang Pi Cold Skin Noodles ($6.98) for me, and the Spicy & Tingly Beef Hand-Ripped Noodles in Soup ($11.11) for him, both delivering the familiar punch of flavor we've come to love. The cold noodles were the perfect balance of refreshing and spicy, a delightful contradiction for the palate.

Our beverage choices, the Chrysanthemum Tea and the Sour Hawberry Tea, were refreshing, though we're curious about the refill policy for the self-pour machines – a potential bonus for future visits.

The Stewed Pork Burger ($4.68) fell a tad short this time, coming across as drier than usual but was redeemed after being dipped in the cold noodle sauce. The casual dining experience near the front door was quite comfortable, with ample space available. This location seems to have more seating than others in the chain, which is a definite advantage.

Overall, despite the minor misstep with the pork burger, XFF remains a favorite for a satisfying and budget-friendly meal.

Came for dinner and drinks with a couple of friends.  Decor is nice.  It was very crowded in a Tuesday but perhaps that's to be expected in New York.  I ordered a glass of rose and a glass of Sauvignon blanc later on.  Both weren't great.  My friends liked their drinks one had a watermelon cocktail and the other a glass of Champaign.  We had a kale artichoke dip with chips for an app.  It was really good.  Then for dinner I had a salad that was supposed to have chicken and quinoa but they easily switched it to salmon for me.  It was really delicious.  The salmon was cooked perfectly and I liked that it was cut and seared into bite sized pieces.  Everything in the salad was very fresh and tasty.  I would definitely return for that salad again.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at what can only be described as a culinary haven amidst the energetic buzz of New York City. This restaurant isn't just fabulous; it's an over-the-top symphony of tastes, sights, and hospitality.

From the moment we walked in, the staff greeted us with a warmth that felt both premium and personal. The views provided a stunning backdrop, showcasing the quintessential NYC skyline. It's the kind of panorama that transforms a meal into an unforgettable event.

Speaking of meals, the food was nothing short of a masterpiece. Each bite of the Scotch Escargot was a revelation, and the mushroom risotto with its earthy morels was a testament to the chef's mastery. Momma K's choice, the wagyu beef, was an exercise in pure indulgence. And the cheese selection for dessert? Sublime.

A word to wine enthusiasts: you will be in awe of the extensive, carefully curated wine list, featuring selections that span the globe. Yes, the prices reflect the restaurant's caliber and location, but the experience justifies every penny.

My recommendation? Aim for a sunset reservation to elevate the already stellar experience.

In conclusion, this place isn't one to simply read about. It demands to be experienced firsthand. From its culinary prowess to its impressive service and the breathtaking views, it's a resounding love letter to fine dining. Highly recommended.

4 and a half stars but rating down because it took a LIL too long for my delivery to come, and the burger was slightly over cooked. Ordered the classic cheeseburger and the Breakroom fries. My total with tax and tip came to a little over $20 which I thought was totally reasonable for what I was getting. I'm also pretty sure it's cash only in the actual restaurant so it's dope that you can order online. Ordered my burger medium rare and while it was realistically medium well it was still strangely juicy and flavorful for being like an $8 burger. The bun was really tasty and the fixins (lettuce, tomato, onion) were fresh. The real star, unsurprisingly, were the fries. A combo of fries and tater tots with cheese, jalapeños, a fried egg, etc that clogs the arteries in the best way. Jalapeños were fresh instead of pickled and I'd probably order without them next time, but YUM. Wasn't sure how I'd feel about the fried egg but it was perfectly cooked. These are fatty fries done to perfection.Would for sure order again.

This place came highly recommended to me by other fellow foodies! true square deep detroit style pizza complete with pepperoni cups the red pizza are fantastic and the pink too... i ordered the colony with no pickled jalapeños because i felt like that would be too spicy lol still pretty delicious

I recently dined at Pro Thai and had a generally positive experience with their solid Thai cuisine offerings. The standout for me was the chicken pineapple fried rice, a dish I would highly recommend for its balance of flavors and delightful combination. The cashew chicken and pad Thai were also satisfying, and the papaya salad paired perfectly with the richer dishes. While the egg rolls were good, they were somewhat overshadowed by the sauce's intensity.

However, not everything hit the mark. I found the side salad with mustard dressing somewhat out of place with the rest of the flavors, and the curry puff didn't quite live up to expectations. Additionally, the eggplant appetizer was a bit too heavily dressed for my taste.

While Pro Thai might not top my list of Thai restaurants, its strengths, particularly the chicken pineapple fried rice, make it worth revisiting. I'm inclined to order from here again, sticking to the highlights like the fried rice and cashew chicken.

Title: A Birthday Feast at a Bustling Taco Spot

As a birthday treat to myself, I finally made it to this much-raved-about taco joint, and it did not disappoint. Despite the crowd, the service was swift, with a line that moved surprisingly fast. Each bite was a delight—the blend of succulent meat, fresh tortillas, and zesty salsas was a culinary trifecta, leaving me devouring my meal in record time.

This isn't your leisurely sit-down restaurant; it's all about the high-top standing tables that complement the quick-eat atmosphere. The staff was friendly and the ambiance inviting, making the dining experience pleasant and efficient.

I'm already planning my next visit to what has quickly become my top taco destination in New York. If you're looking for flavors that pop and a place that understands the value of both time and taste, this is the spot you can't miss.

This is a first: going from a 5-star dining experience to a 1-star dreadful dinner. Since I was so happy with some of the food I ordered 7 months ago, this time I had clear in mind what to get: boneless steak, pork belly and mussels. The first round went fine. Except for the fact that we were served less than half of the meat we ordered, the rest went ok. The waiter grilled our meat. The quality of the meat was good. The service was responsive. The trouble started later on. We ordered more of the same, and after waiting for a while (hungry), the dude showed up with very little meat, again. He put it on the grill and disappeared. We got there before 5p, so the place was half empty... He had no reason to go MIA. We decided to take the meat out but it was too late: overcooked. The mussels continued to cook until they were burned and inedible. We could have taken them out but he was supposed to cook them with a sauce (which btw was nothing like the sauce we had 7 months ago). There was a woman - prob the floor manager - who at times would show up, but didn't do anything. After the disaster in the second round (we ate the meat anyway), I made it clear in the third round of what happened and ordered more meat. After another 10-minute wait, another guy came with the meat (again, very little) and dumped it on the table. We ended up grilling it ourselves. The fourth round went pretty much the same way. The quality of the meat decreased at each round. At some point, the boneless steak was so chewy we could barely eat it. Not only it tasted different... it also looked different (!). It was light years from what we were served at the very beginning. With each round the service would get more and more absent, careless, almost confrontational... like they hated us because we didn't get full after just a couple of pieces of meat. It was clear to us that they were avoiding us like the plague. Wow. Bottom line. If you're so cheap and stingy that you serve only a fraction of the food ordered and keep your customers at the table forever bc they need to keep ordering until they're full... that's a horrible business decision on your side, because you could serve twice as many people and make twice the amount of money. If you keep serving worse and worse quality meat the more orders customers make so you can save money... that's a dishonest strategy on your side, and you won't get my money ever again. If you disappear and force customers to cook their own food without even caring about their dining experience... that's a dumb choice on your side, because those people won't ever come back. I know you could care less about my opinion... clearly, you have enough customers lined up every day to really be bothered about my review. However, if this is the way you treat your customers, it won't take long until New Yorkers start turning their back on you. We were there for 2 hours and ended up leaving really disappointed with the quality of the meat and annoyed with the service. I have no reasons to ever go back. Note. If you're the owner, if I'm not mistaken, you own Nyonya as well. That place is awesome. I wish Hometown were managed the same way.

Title: A Memorable Celebration at a Charming Venue

I visited this restaurant for a combined Mother's Day and birthday celebration and was thoroughly impressed. Our reservation was promptly honored, and we were comfortably seated on the quieter second floor amid the restaurant's captivating decor. 

The service was swift, our drinks arrived quickly, and the staff was attentive—demonstrated when they promptly replaced my sister's Thai iced tea, which had unfortunately toppled due to a slightly tilted table, at no extra charge. 

We relished a variety of appetizers, with the shrimp roll standing out so deliciously that we couldn't resist ordering a second. Each dish we tried was bursting with freshness and had us all delighted with our individual meal choices. My mother had a particularly great time.

The restaurant nailed every aspect of the dining experience, making our special occasion both enjoyable and memorable.

Came here for a company dinner. Large space but it wasnt super busy. It was a Tuesday night. Got an assortment of dim sum and duck.The duck was very nicely done. The sauce for it reminded me of Korean bbq.I felt the dim sum was generally good. The turnip cakes were great. The shrimp balls were too. The shrimp rice noodle was only alright. Drink selection was larger than expected. Some decent craft like hitachino and also an okay wine selection.Service was decent. If given the choice, I'd go to golden unicorn instead.

My husband brought me here for our anniversary and it did not disappoint! The ambiance is laid back and casual which we both enjoyed and we sat in the area overlooking the chefs which is always a cool experience!Here are a few dishes we sampled and we loved everything!!-chicken satay- well cooked and super tasty. I mean who doesn't love peanut butter sauce with some crushed peanuts on chicken? We gobbled it up!-clam- tiny little suckers but loaded with flavor. Had a spicy kick which we both never mind :)-pork ribs- they were beautiful (please refer to my photos) with edible flowers and other garnishes and just tasted delicious! Perfectly cooked and seasoned and great for sharing-lobster pasta- oh my this was so yummy as well! A lovely taste explosion and ample amounts of lobster which was not over cooked by the pasta-salted caramel chocolate- excellent mix of salty and sweet. We of course gobbled it up!!I'm beyond happy my husband found this place and let me just add so affordable! Def head on over and give this place a try :)

Amazing Cuban food with the ambiance to match! Delicious food and a tropical feel. Great mojitos and incomparable cuisine, with satisfying taste and matching presentation. What more can I say? This was our second visit to Havana and they've secured a third. If you know good Cuban food then you will definitely enjoy Havana. The venue is clean and decorated fittingly. They have a great selection of tropical drinks, tempting appetizers and fulfilling entrees. Don't forget dessert! You've got to try it!

Dope spot with *delicious* trapizzinos. Ordered the chicken, oxtail and eggplant. All were great but the chicken and oxtail were exceptionally tasty. The chicken was so tender, juicy and perfectly seasoned. The oxtail ragú was hearty and filled with flavor. The sourdough bread that the trapizzinos come in is also out of this world - crunchy on the outside yet soft and fluffy on the inside. Each one is ~$8 so totally worth it! We also ordered the classic supplí but the trapizzinos are where it's at. Still dreaming about them now...

Title: Charming Diner with Top-Notch Cuisine

I recently visited a delightful little spot that's earned a solid spot in my gastronomic heart. Food-wise, it's a home run – five stars for the jerk chicken, which tantalized my taste buds with its perfect blend of spices. The side of mac and cheese? Absolutely scrumptious. However, keep in mind that while the dishes are superb, you might find the portions not quite matching the price tag.

The ambiance is unapologetically pure diner. This hole-in-the-wall experience adds a unique charm, but it's something to be aware of if you're expecting a more upscale environment. Drink options are somewhat limited with a modest selection of wine and beer. Cocktail lovers might be a tad disappointed as it seems they work around a full liquor license with malt beverage concoctions.

Even with these considerations, my overall experience was overwhelmingly positive, and I’m eager to return. If you appreciate quality food and a bit of quirky charm, this is a place you won't want to miss.

Cheap Chinese take out place with lunch specials for about $8.75. The service here is a bit gruff, but that's the norm with Chinese takeout restaurants. After looking at all the reviews, I was hesitant to try them out but it's not as bad as some people make them out to be.I had the BBQ boneless spare pork ribs which comes with a soda. There was so much meat and the taste wasn't bad. Don't except it to be like America BBQ. Chinese BBQ sauce is more on the sweet side. I would have liked a couple of pieces of vegetables to make the meal less meat heavy. There was enough for two meals. The pieces were cut pretty big and some were quite fatty. Otherwise not a bad lunch option.

A friend of mine told me that this was a NYC bucket list sort of place, and so we checked it out on a recent Friday night. Despite concerns that there would be a line out the door, it was actually pretty quiet. The line moves quick and the portion size is solid.  The pork-noodle combo that I got was essentially big chunks of pork and gi-normous strands of thick noodles. So much so that I had to use a knife to separate chunks of the noodles (I enjoyed this part).  I thought it was flavorful, and they have spicer options available. I'd go back for a quick bite or order take out for sure.

Tucked away in midtown lies a charming Spanish tapas restaurant that's a perfect kick-off or capstone to your evening, whether it's a romantic date or a night out with the girls. Surrounded by an array of excellent wine bars, this cozy spot entices with its ambiance and a delightful menu. Don't miss their standout veggie paella, which is a flavorful nod to traditional Spanish cuisine, the delectable pan con tomate, and the perfectly seasoned patatas bravas. Of course, no visit is complete without indulging in their refreshing sangria. This place is a must-visit for a slice of Spain in the heart of the city.

Title: A Stellar Evening by Bryant Park!

From the moment I stepped into this gem right off Bryant Park, I was enveloped in its dazzling atmosphere. The service was nothing short of exemplary, with attentive staff that made the dining experience seamless.

The decor was stunning, creating an inviting and sophisticated ambiance that perfectly complemented the unique and delightful food offerings. The crispy rice with spicy tuna and the edamame dumplings truly stood out, each bite a testament to the culinary creativity and flavor mastery of the chef.

No evening would be complete without a good cocktail, and this establishment did not disappoint. Their cocktail selection was impressive, and each sip was as great as the last.

I left with a sense of true dining satisfaction and with gratitude for such a stellar evening. This restaurant has earned itself a repeat customer, and I eagerly look forward to my next visit. Thank you for an unforgettable experience!

Title: A Gem for Japanese Cuisine Enthusiasts

Upon entering this high-end Japanese sake and skewer haven, one is immediately enveloped in an atmosphere of sophistication, with ambient lighting and plush seating enhancing the dining experience. The level of service is impressive, characterized by attentiveness and efficiency that adds to the overall enjoyment.

A minor disappointment surfaced when the famed Yamazaki 18 was unavailable due to the holiday season, but the alternative, Ichiro's blended malt & grain whiskey, did not disappoint with its robust maltiness and smooth finish. The plum wines also come highly recommended and should not be overlooked.

The culinary journey commenced with an exquisite sashimi combo featuring succulent salmon, tuna, and melt-in-your-mouth yellowtail, followed by an assorted tempura that struck an ideal balance between a crispy exterior and a light interior, avoiding any sense of doughiness. The skewer variety was a highlight, with offerings such as Washu Wagyu, beef tongue, and salmon decked with fish eggs delighting the palate with their impeccable preparation.

In summary, this establishment has swiftly ascended to the top of my list for unparalleled Japanese gastronomy in New York City, providing a memorable experience that beckons diners to return.

Walked passed Bill's Bar and Burger and decided to stop in for lunch. The restaurant was much bigger than it looks from the outside. Although busy, we were seated right away. Our waitress was lovely and seemed to really care that we have a good dining experience. Very reasonable prices and the food was excellent.

Title: A Charming Establishment with a Personal Touch

My latest visit to this beloved neighborhood gem reaffirms why we've been regulars since its inception. Admittedly, the prices have climbed, with certain dishes now exceeding the $20 mark, a change that's hard to ignore. Yet, the charm of customizing our meals remains undiminished. The choice of meatballs paired with a sauce and served over pasta, rice, veggies, a crisp salad, or tucked into a sandwich still delights.

The bar area, a social hub, never disappoints. This evening was no exception, as we mingled with an international patron from Gouda and a fellow American from Huntsville. The highlight, however, was our bartender, Zachary, whose charisma and knack for storytelling transformed our night into an extraordinary experience. The personal interactions here are as much a draw as the food itself.

Can't go to NYC and not get late night pizza! After drinking around ktown, we trekked over here for some late night pizza and we were not disappointed! The staff was also really friendly even though it was close to closing time. My favorite was the hot honey pizza and the chicken bacon ranch. Although sweet, the honey surprisingly went really well with the ricotta cheese. Personally I think ranch tastes good with pizza so I was excited to get the chicken bacon ranch. They give a lot of chicken on it! I normally don't like eating crusts on pizza but I did really enjoy the crust here.
Amazing pizza, drinks and service! Not too casual and not too fancy. Just right. Thank you, Patzeria, for a wonderful night!

Last night's omakase dining experience for a mere $50 post-4pm was remarkable for the value, with well-sized portions. Locating the restaurant was a bit of a challenge with its hidden locale and a walk-in policy. Amidst a flurry of delivery orders, only a handful of diners occupied the space, allowing for quick and attentive service. My meal unfolded swiftly within an hour, starting with a standard yet comforting miso soup. While the sushi's freshness was questionable by sight, the flavors were surprisingly pleasing, particularly when paired with the sharpness of ginger, the warmth of sake, and the sweet finale of lychee mochi ice cream. Standouts included the buttery toro, rich salmon, savory eel, and classic shrimp. However, the uni and tobiko fell short of my expectations.

We came here for a friend's birthday as a whimsical dinner; the diner theme is pretty fun, and the milkshakes are great. It's probably that we had a large group of 13 people, but the service was a bit slow. I was surprised that we were sitting at a diner for over 2 hours (which was okay since it was a birthday) when I normally associate diner with fast food. That said, the service was pretty great; when one of our friends said that her drink didn't taste like it had much vodka in it, a server appeared out of nowhere and straight up poured vodka into her glass. The portions were all pretty large; each entrée could easily feed two people. The food itself was pretty decent, and the milkshakes were straight up decadent - most people could only drink a few sips of their milkshakes and they were done. Ultimately, I think I'm not really into diner food; I'd rather get a good chicken and waffles somewhere else. For people who love diner food, though, I can see how this would be a great choice.

I recently visited a restaurant where the cauliflower dish truly impressed me - it was "bomb" as they say, and I'd certainly suggest giving it a try. However, when it came to the main courses, both the black bass and the roasted chicken fell into the realm of mediocrity. My recommendation would be to frequent this spot for its vibrant drinks and tantalizing appetizers rather than a full dinner experience.

Title: A Satisfying Blend of Hits and Misses

My dining experience at this establishment is deserving of a solid 3.5 stars—a testament to its enjoyable yet slightly inconsistent offerings. The beef carpaccio was a standout appetizer, tender and flavorful, worth ordering again. On special, the burrata paired with prosciutto didn't disappoint either, its creaminess complementing the well-chosen sides.

While the grilled polenta was delightful, its accompanying mushrooms lacked the depth of flavor one would hope for. The mussels were a hit with my husband, though I found the sauce to be a timid version of a marinara, craving more seasoning.

Pasta lovers would appreciate the lightness of the mushroom ravioli, though the sauce could benefit from a bit more zest. The meal ended on a high note with a fluffy and impressive tiramisu.

For those nearby, it's worth dropping by to sample some of their tastier dishes.

Had been to the restaurant and loved the food, but hated the noise.  It is LOUD!  Cool space, though.  Now on to the food.  Favorite was the cheesecake.  Wow - delicious!  And a really nice portion. Also enjoyed an arugula salad,  and the chicken satay which came with some grilled pineapple.  I was disappointed with the onion soup and the skirt steak, which was a bit too fatty for my taste.

Love this place!I came here for dinner. One of my friends highly recommended it and we were in the area. I'm so glad I stopped by here!The food was amazingly fresh and delicious!I had the bacon, waffles, chicken and salad. Everything I tried had incredible flavors. I was so glad that I decided to come here.The bacon was thick and juicy. I loved it! I would definitely come back here again!

Title: A Solid Choice for Chinese Cuisine

I've frequented this local spot enough to say their food hits the mark on both taste and value. The bustle around lunchtime is testament to its popularity, so I've learned to ring ahead to dodge the packed setting—and the inevitable eau de fryer that clings to my clothes post-visit. Service-wise, I haven't hit a snag. All told, it's a reliable pick for Chinese fare in the area.

I just had this for dinner and it was a good deal for seamless. I got gyoza, a california roll, and a spicy crunchy roll. I thought the gyoza was 5/5, california was 4/5, and spicy crunchy roll was 3/5. I got a good amount of food and it was pretty tasty. Satisfied with my experience.

Title: A Symphony of Spices and Flavors at Spice Symphony

Review:

My recent dinner at Spice Symphony was a culinary delight. We opted for Indo-Chinese fare, indulging in Hakka noodles, Manchurian, and chilli chicken, all of which were savory and satisfactorily spiced.

The standout experience, however, was the soups. With the chill of the night setting in, both the coriander and the manchow soup provided a warm and tasty reprieve that tantalized our taste buds.

Dessert was a journey through sweetness that should not be missed. The malai kulfi, gajar halwa, gulab jamun, and the coconut caramel custard were each exceptionally delightful, earning the moniker bomb.com without question.

Service at Spice Symphony was top-notch. The individual who attended to us, potentially the manager, was not only courteous but also insightful with recommendations that enhanced our dining experience. Overall, Spice Symphony is a must-visit for those seeking authentic Indo-Chinese flavors with service that boasts meticulous attention to detail.

It's been a while since I've had good duck, chicken and/or pork over rice. My sister recommended this place. It was 6.50 for 2 meats over rice with some bok choy and came with a very salty melon soup. As you can see in the photos, the meats were all very good pieces without too much fat and/or bone. We asked for an extra scoop of the special soy sauce over the rice, which was a questionable choice as it made the rice so tasty that I finished it all. I would definitely come again when I'm craving this, but will also come back to try their clay pot rice options!

This place is great! We had frequently attended the Ramen spot formerly at this location, so it was a nice surprise to see such a similar restaurant open up in its place. I had the spicy miso ramen. It was delicious and had a nice kick without being too spicy. Unfortunately the chicken was very dry but I am hoping it is a one off, it won't stop me from coming back and giving it another try. We had the lunch special which was a great deal, although I was extremely full by the time we headed out.

Um, no.I know I self-deprecatingly identify as millennial trash who is obsessed with brunch, but even I have to draw the line somewhere. And honestly, I didn't expect it to be in the middle of a meal at Jane. But the greatest thing about living in New York is that nothing fazes you anymore... right?Seriously, even though there are 3000+ seemingly positive reviews, go somewhere else. Because with in a city with so many better brunch options, there's no reason why you should wait for a table in a packed, sterile-looking website and pay an obscenely exorbitant amount for bland food.I'm still recovering from the flavorless disaster they have labeled as the $21 vanilla bean french toast on their menu, though I have nothing negative to say about the maple syrup and fruit, even if it couldn't salvage the dish.

Title: A Cozy Breakfast Spot with Standout Paninis

My husband and I recently visited this delightful little restaurant for a quick breakfast before an appointment at MSK. To our delight, we discovered a lovely selection of breakfast paninis on the menu. We both opted for the #26 – a delectable combination of scrambled eggs, crispy pancetta, shaved parmesan, and a flavorful pesto sauce. It was, without exaggeration, delicious.

Accompanying our meal with coffee, we found both the beverage and the food to be of excellent quality. While the space is compact and seating is limited, it contributed to the cozy ambiance. The staff at the counter were exceptionally kind, adding to the positive experience. This place may be small, but it's a gem worth visiting for its superb paninis and coffee.

Title: A Culinary Revelation at Bucket List Dining Gem

From a self-proclaimed fine dining skeptic to a renewed gourmet enthusiast, my experience at this much-talked-about restaurant was nothing short of transformative. Though my visit began with a minor hiccup, as a waiter accidentally spilled something on the table, the swift recovery with a fresh white napkin was a prelude to the impeccable service that followed.

Course after exquisite course left me in awe, but the dish that truly captured my palate was the uni. As someone who previously steered clear of sea urchin, the preparation here made me an instant convert, or as I’d like to call it, an "uni-believer." Equally memorable was the frozen corn soufflé, a marvel of texture that conjured visions of indulgent, frosty cotton candy, but with an invigorating depth of flavor.

For those who prefer their fine dining sans alcohol, the restaurant's non-alcoholic beverage selection did not disappoint, offering a spectrum of refined and satisfying options.

While my quest to explore new culinary destinations might delay my return, this restaurant has earned a rare accolade from me: it's a place I’d gladly dine at daily. A must-visit for anyone whose passion for fine dining needs a spark.

They're not joking--this restaurant has the best ramen probably in the whole world (subjective opinion, I know). It comes in a classy, traditional ramen box that keeps all the flavour locked in til you open it up. The whole restaurant is a unique experience with single booths to "block out" distractions to let you concentrate as you indulge in the ramen. They don't take tips, but then again the ramen is pricier compared to other spots in NYC. However, you can't beat the quality of this spot. Definitely a must try!

Upon my recent visit to this charming Thai restaurant, my palate was thoroughly impressed by the authentic flavors each dish presented. The Pad Thai was an absolute delight, with just the right balance of sweet, sour, and savory, while the BBQ pork chops were succulent, tender, and perfectly charred. Portion sizes were generous, making both dishes well-suited for sharing between two. An added perk was the offer of a complimentary Thai tea or coffee simply for providing a review—a refreshing finish to a satisfying meal. Highly recommended for a genuine taste of Thailand.

Came here for a birthday brunch with a group of 10 on a Saturday. A few of us were late so unfortunately the ones who arrived earlier had to wait for everyone to start the bottomless.We sat upstairs and the place was really cute but small, we felt a little smushed...but after the second drink we forgot. A lot, of options for drinks so if you're not a mimosa person don't worry. The drinks were strong but very sweet so prepare for a headache.  A lot of options for brunch, everything from your typical brunch food to traditional Cuban dishes. With so much variety I was a little worried about the quality everything would be. Everyone loved what we got from the apps to main courses. The presentation and service was also really good. So food was definitely great, only con were super sweet drinks.

Stepping into this New York legend, I immediately felt transported to a true Italian eatery, the kind you might imagine in a classic gangster film. The staff welcomed my family with open arms, providing service that was both friendly and helpful.

Now let's talk about the pizza – it was nothing short of remarkable. The crust had the perfect amount of crispness, supporting a pizza so light, it seemed to defy gravity. The sauce was a standout with so much twang, it sang with each bite, perfectly complementing the superior quality cheese.

For those seeking an authentic Italian experience in the Big Apple, this restaurant is an absolute must-try.

My last visit here was last summer. The boathouse is such a charming restaurant-Particularly when you're able to sit on patio and take in the sun setting on the water or the rowers rowing away on the lake. I actually came here after rowing for an hour, which was also a fun and picturesque experience. The menu is not extensive, however it's appropriate, considering the endearing ambiance. The crab cake was lukewarm and flavorful. It was lightly breaded and accompanied by a cucumber salad. The ahi tuna came with a significant amount of ahi surprisingly and had a mild coconut flavor with coconut shavings. The lobster tostado did not quite live up to my expectations. It was a bit on the bland side. The Seafood Pasta was incredible. Rich with spices and the right amount of shrimp and scallops. I absolutely loved it!!!! Clay was our waiter and he was FANTASTIC !!! He was engaging, informative and fabulous. He made the experience even more special and he is a asset to the restaurant. I will definitely return before the season is over.

Left my wallet at home and did not set up Apple Pay..had my husband order for me to pick up...when I walked in there..first red flag was that it was empty..but it was also raining...$18 for my "everything" poke without rice$4.50 for edamame $2 for can of green teaIt left me yearning for more...Pros: quick-but no one was thereEdamame was hot even after I brought it back to my office. Ingredients were fresh Lady working there put my poke bowl salad in the refrigerator before I got there to pick it up-I really appreciate that she tried to keep it fresh for mePlace looks clean Con: Flavors were bland, even my spicy salmon was bland...not sure how that can happen...I tasted the pickled ginger and a hint of soy sauce...it just did not come together...Maybe it was a bad day for them or maybe the ingredients I picked just weren't their specialty or didn't belong together ...I would probably not come back simply because there's so many options to choose from...

Title: Burger Monday Bliss at Tetsu

I recently visited Tetsu on their famed Burger Monday, and it did not disappoint. The expansive, lively space offers a prime view of the kitchen's hustle and a communal vibe that's perfect for dining with friends. My buddy and I, on our quest to conquer New York's best burgers, both opted for the beef burger, cooked to a succulent medium rare. 

The burger, a simple yet sublime combination of meat and cheese on a toasted bun, paired with fries, was a culinary delight. The experience was akin to savouring beef tartare, a testament to the quality and preparation of the patty. We tossed in a masa roll, which, despite its simplicity, was delectably noteworthy, although the $35 price tag was a bit of a splurge.

In conclusion, Tetsu's burgers are pure perfection and worth the visit for those special occasions or when you feel like indulging in a fine dining burger experience.

If you're on the hunt for a Happy Hour haven, this spot should be at the top of your list thanks to its great deals. The interior is pleasantly roomy, though I suggest arriving early as seating can get a bit haphazard with groups leaving awkward gaps of unused chairs. Aim for the coveted swinging chairs by the windows for prime people-watching – but be warned, they're a hot commodity, as I noticed a pair of midtown uniform-clad patrons snagging them pre-HH.

Onto the food, the Impossible Taco is a must-try; it's a plant-based revelation. The Nachos, loaded with the same impossible taco meat, are a crowd-pleaser worth digging into. Don't miss out on their Guac & Chips – simple, fresh, and the perfect accompaniment to their discounted beverages. All in all, it's a solid choice for after-work unwinding.

I recently visited a local gem that served up an excellent plate of fish and chips - crisp, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Pairing splendidly with the meal, their house beer was not only delicious but also reasonably priced for the area. An added bonus was the complimentary matches provided. Overall, a delightful dining experience worth recommending.

I recently visited Egg Shop, a place I once held in high regard, but my latest experience was disheartening due to an encounter with a particularly rude hostess. From my initial attempt to simply put my name down for a table, I was met with unnecessary attitude from the hostess with curly blonde hair. Her customer service was disappointingly lacking.

Upon the arrival of my full party, her response was no more helpful, offering a curt reply with no updates or estimated waiting time. Such treatment is unacceptable, and it promptly led us to leave the establishment in search of a more welcoming dining environment.

This incident was a stark contrast to my previous visits to Egg Shop, which had been pleasant. It's a shame that one staff member's behavior can so drastically affect the overall experience. Proper training or personnel changes are needed to prevent future patrons from being similarly turned away.

Awesome AYCE sushi spot in the Manhattan Chinatown alleyway! I say this because the restaurant is probably not the easiest to find, and I only found it because I was eating at the Malaysian restaurant next door (which is also very delicious). The entrance alley is right next to jing fong btw peeps.Came here on a Saturday afternoon with couple of friends. You can choose the AYCE or not, up to your party. We did opt for the AYCE menu and got to order off the tablet (pretty fancy). So you just select what you want on the tablet and the server will come and confirm your order for you. Our food also didn't take too long to come. The portions were generous and we ate till we could not eat another bite. The only other AYCE sushi place I experienced was in Brooklyn and it was awesome. So it's nice to have something as satisfying in the city. Very friendly staff as well, everyone should go check it out.

If you're looking for southern food this is the place to be. Everything I had was so delicious and the portions we very generous. Price point was also on point. I had the honey chicken meal with the macaroni and cheese and I would have swore my mother was back in the kitchen cooking the food herself. Chicken was seasoned very well. The honey was not over bearing and just the right amount of crunch. The Mac and cheese was also good. I love a good baked Mac and cheese. Usually at a place like this they don't give you that much Mac and cheese, but not here, they have a good amount for me not to want anymore. The cabbage I had was also delicious. It was the right amount and cooked to perfection. My waiter was very friendly and honest about telling us what she liked on the menu. Doing this allowed us to make some really good food choices. Will be def coming back here.

Tucked away in the Lower East Side lies a gem serving up authentic Spanish cuisine that truly captures the essence of a classic neighborhood eatery. Their quarter chicken with rice and beans—part of a lunch special costing a mere $8—is a steal that could easily satisfy two appetites, though I guiltlessly indulged solo. The value and quality are undeniable. I'm already planning my return to explore the variety of proteins on their menu. A reliable spot for anyone craving a taste of Spain.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Dumpling Enthusiasts - Chi Dumpling House

Tucked away by Grand St station, Chi Dumpling House may not catch your eye immediately, especially with the popular Wah Fung No 1 nearby, but this modest eatery holds its own with unbeatable value. For under $10, my feast included ten pan-fried pork and chive dumplings that delivered on flavor, especially when savored fresh and crispy. Those craving a smaller bite can opt for the five-piece serving at just $1.50.

I also tried the steamed chicken and cabbage dumplings; while the skins were a tad thick, the filling itself was quite satisfying. The hot and sour soup didn't hit the mark, leaning too much on soy sauce, but the portion size was generous for the price. As for the flat egg noodles with peanut butter sauce, they were unfortunately lackluster when compared to local street cart offerings.

Despite its less inviting facade and reliance on disposable cutlery, Chi Dumpling House boasts an 'A' Health Department rating and a bilingual service which makes ordering a breeze. While certain items may fall short, I'd still recommend this spot for anyone on the hunt for a dumpling haven that's easy on the wallet.

I've been meaning to come here but I have been so busy lately.  I realized it's almost July 13th so I better get here now! I've been to the place in Florence so I was excited to try it here.  I should've came here earlier since the people in the front of the line came at 11am when it opens at 12pm.  I got there at 12pm and it was about an hour wait.  There were 6 sandwiches available.  I ordered the L'Inferno which had porchetta, 'nduja (spicy salami spread), grilled eggplant, and arugula.  I wanted to order the La Summer (prosciutto, mozzarella, arugula, basil, tomatoes, oil, balsamic) initially and decided to try something new that I couldn't get in NYC.  The staff were very friendly and offered bread samples while you wait on line.  The sandwich was as delicious as I remembered.  The bread and ingredients were fresh and tasty.  I wish they would open a permanent location in NYC.  I'm glad I got to try it before it closes.

Title: Klong: Happy Hour Heaven and Thai Delights

I've been a regular at Klong for two years, mainly because their happy hour is unparalleled. They're not shy about pouring drinks, and the $3 margaritas are unbeatable. When it comes to food, the pad thai tops my list with its impeccably tangy flavor and flawlessly cooked noodles. The pad sew, brimming with unique flavors, is a fantastic comfort dish that I crave after a busy day. The prices are fair, making the choice to dine here even easier.

Klong attracts a vibrant crowd of young professionals looking to unwind post-work. With its dimly lit atmosphere, the place promises a fun and laid-back evening. If you're in search of quality Thai cuisine and a lively happy hour, Klong is your go-to spot.

Some of the best nachos I've had in a long time.Came here with a few friends for some drinks and eats. I ordered the white wine sangria pitcher which was fruity and delicious.We were enjoying some salsa and guacamole to start- the salsa had a good flavor and was very fresh. The guac was quite basic, there wasn't much added to it aside from avocados so we threw the salsa in to jazz it up.The main star of the night though was the nachos. The cheese was perfectly melted over the full plate, with plenty to go around. All of the chips were well covered. The steak was in nice sized pieces and a cooked medium which I appreciated. Would come back for the nachos 100%

Title: Unmet Expectations at Local Persian Eatery

I ventured to a recommended Persian restaurant, lured by its reputation as one of the best budget-friendly spots in the city. Anticipation was high, but unfortunately, the experience was underwhelming. Despite its cozy, shared space with a pizza counter, the charm didn't extend to the food.

The $13.95 combo platter offered a selection of two mains. The cranberry walnut chicken presented an imbalance in flavor, being overly sweet and sour with a lack of savory notes, which made it difficult to finish. The split pea beef showed some improvement, but the meat's dryness overshadowed the dish, saved only slightly by the accompanying peas and interestingly topped with potato chips.

Overall, the portions and culinary execution did not justify the price. With a hopeful palate, I believe the quest for exceptional Persian cuisine in New York City continues.

I can't stress enough just how good 2nd Avenue Deli is. Don't let the price tag next to some of the items scare you away, I personally think this is the best Jewish deli on the Isle of Manhattan. I definitely recommend doing the half sandwich and soup special. I also highly recommend the matzo ball soup, it's really fantastic, especially on a cold day. I personally had the hot double: hot corned beef and hot pastrami on rolls and I just had to get mac salad. The corned beef is excellent, perfect pairing with the coleslaw they give you with pickles and hot mustard. The pastrami is my favorite meat here. I love it on the half sandwich, I love it on the roll, I even love it in eggs! Its perfectly seasoned, sliced perfectly, and a true NYC delicacy. While not an every week restaurant and my current financial situation, certainly a treat when I do come in here.

This is a great spot for soup on a cold winter day. I was impressed by the amount of noodle dishes they have! The story behind the Crossing Bridge noodles is so sweet (it's on the first page of the menu). I also love that they serve you hot water. Our server was a friendly woman who was very attentive throughout our meal. I was excited by the idea of the Crossing Bridge noodles, since the ingredients come separately and then they help you put everything into the broth so it can all cook together. The noodle soup stayed hot throughout the meal, so if you don't like it when your soup gets lukewarm, this is great. About the meal itself however, I wasn't a big fan of the broth. There was an ingredient in it that made it spicy, but not *hot* spicy--a bit hard to explain. I would love to try the other broths, but again, not a big fan of my beef bone broth. Don't forget to check in on Yelp to get a free dessert of your choice! You can also get it by adding the restaurant on WeChat or posting photos on Yelp. I got the Milky Rice which was delicious, along with the Taro Tapioca Pudding.

While the experience at this place didn't start off the best (there was a line of around 30 people I had to wait in), it was WELL worth the wait. The line moved extremely quick and the staff moved efficiently to take orders and make the food.The food wasn't too expensive and all the options on the menu were great! I had two tacos (one pork, one beef) and a pork quesadilla and they all tasted so good. I ate them so quickly I was tempted to get another order!The meat tasted so fresh and juicy, plus the toppings it had all were distinct and added something to the flavor. Even the tortillas tasted nice!Though the line can be intimidating it moves extremely quickly and the food is well worth the wait!

I arrived at this establishment with my two girlfriends after having a very disappointing experience at one of the establishments located in the basement....directly under this building. We arrived on a Friday night around 8:45pm and the place was packed wall to wall.....the atmosphere is very divey......just like the waitstaff the patrons were very laid back. Since there was not available seating for my friends and I we installed ourselves at the bar...right where you are only supposed to pick up drinks and keep it moving. However the bartender was very accommodating.....she let us chill there for a while.....we ordered the Absolute Lemonade....and it was absolutely amazing and needed after a long day. The bartender poured our drinks in front of us and she did not skimp out on the liquor. After awhile the bartender noticed a free spot in the "bleecher" section and my party and I went to be seated and waited for our food to come out.We ordered wings and waffle fries with an assortment of dipping sauces.....the wings are a nice organic sized split in half. They were fried to perfection and evenly coated in wing sauce.....the dipping sauces made the fries that much better....we even ordered another basket of fries...I recommend everyone try the Jalapeño Aioli dipping sauce.So a few things to know .....the bathrooms are located to in the very back are unisex and plagued in a graffiti decor.....they are environmental friendly and they do not have plastic straws....however they have metal ones they sell you for a dollar and are yours to keep.....you must order your food at the bar and you will be given a number to sit on your table and it will be taken out to you...they have huge sport water coolers and small colorful kid like plastic cups around bar ...were patrons serve theirselves water. For a great night out for 3 ladies....a double order of wings and fries.....2 rounds of drinks plus shots...our tab was ONLY $80.73 before tipping....you cant beat that...Oh I forgot to mention.....they have a super cool photobooth in the front corner...shout out to the kick ass bartender Bianca.....hands down the BEST....great personality....and the only sucky part about this spot was the bouncer outside who cards you..he was a little rude because we had to dig our ID out our purse and did not have in hand already...he was a hideous rendition of the Westly Snips character Blade...who held a resting bitxh face and spoke like robo cop....but his blue/grey eye contacts made it even harder to take him seriously...But with all that being said I most absolutely will be going back.

Staying around the corner at the Renwick so we head over to Momosan for a ramen fix at lunch. Sunday at 11:45 and the line is forming. We are second in line so are assured a table but the place is packed within 20 minutes of opening. Waiter is nice and goes over the menu and his recommendations. We order the Tonkotsu Ramen, the Salmon Zuke Don, Peking Duck taco and pork belly bao.  Eveything is very good. The tonkotsu broth is very flavorful and we really enjoyed it. Food is top notch but we wouldn't expect any less from an Iron Chef. One suggestion- the busboy/other waiter continually picks up empty plates and bowls while you are eating your meal making it inconvenient to enjoy your main course as he is reaching over your shoulder and motioning for you to help him retrieve the empties. Pretty annoying. Better to wait till folks are done so we are not passing dishes around. I get it they need to turn tables over but, hey, let me enjoy my ramen!Besides that we enjoyed our meal.

I've been here maybe 10 times - it's a solid choice for an everyday dinner - good food at reasonable prices, and lots of seating (including outdoor seating when the weather is warm).  The food isn't anything amazing - I wouldn't come here as a destination - but if you're in the area and want to grab a solid, casual dinner, then this is your place.  My favorite dishes have been the salmon and the salad with grilled chicken.  Usually the starter bread is warm and good.  I'm not a fan of the mezze platter - I don't find their hummus to be that good.  We had a spinach/cheese pie special which was quite good.  I recommend this place for groups not looking to spend a ton.  They did not have high chairs.

Before catching a show at Bowery Ballroom, my companion and I visited One Mile House for a bite. The establishment boasts a cozy, modern pub ambiance, albeit on the smaller and dimmer side. Our server provided excellent service, making sure to inform us of the day's specials.

Deciding to share appetizers, we ordered the wings in chili Asian sauce and the poutine adorned with pork confit. Both dishes were surprisingly generous in size and utterly delicious. If you find yourself in the vicinity, One Mile House is definitely worth the detour for a satisfying pre-show meal.

Title: Mixed Feelings at L'Accolade

I had high hopes for L'Accolade, but my experience fell short of expectations. The happy hour special featured a $10 glass of Chilean red wine which failed to impress. Opting for a $80 bottle of red from Périgord provided a decent, albeit overpriced, alternative considering its 2016 vintage.

The evening's real test was the food, which showed promise in flavor but was marred by slow service; we waited 90 minutes for three of our four appetizers, and the fourth one seemingly vanished into thin air. The bread and butter provided a tasty respite from the long wait.

In an attempt to end on a high note, we switched to desserts, which thankfully did not disappoint. However, with a bill totaling $200 after tax and tip, the evening was quite the investment. We capped off our night with an indulgent treat from Big Gay Ice Cream nearby.

Title: A Truffle Lover's Paradise

I recently dined at a restaurant that has won over my pasta-loving heart. The standout of the evening was an exceptional cappelletti, recommended by our knowledgeable waiter. Infused with just the right amount of truffle, it brought a sublime earthiness to the dish without overwhelming the palate. For truffle enthusiasts, this place is a dream, as their special off-menu truffle risotto also proved to be exemplary.

The burrata appetizer was another delight, pairing the creamy cheese with the unexpected sweetness of strawberries and a drizzle of balsamic vinaigrette. This combination exemplified the thoughtfulness put into each dish.

While it's true the prices are on the steeper side for the portion sizes, the culinary experience is worth it. I'm already looking forward to returning for their Monday night pasta specials – a must-try for fellow pasta aficionados.

Really enjoyed my trip to chef's table and I think it is deserving of all of the hype. As a tip - the restaurant is at the back of a little market (you'll see a hostess stand). They're pretty strict on dinner timings, so be aware of that.We had a little trouble getting a reservation, but were lucky to get a spot after trying for weeks. The tasting menu is really great - my favorites of our 6+ courses were the sea urchin and the fluke. We sat at the bar and it was great to see everyone prepare everything.Overall, amazing (but pricy) experience. If you ever have the chance to go, would recommend.

Solid performance by Lido. Reservation was made, reservation was change and there was no fuss. Gave us a table in the middle, and then moved us to a more cozy spot. Can't complain about the service whatsoever. Drinks were flowing and the waiter knew his way around a wine cellar. Very impressive. Also, this joint was packed for a late Thursday dinner. Very impressed with how they keep up with the demand. What we got:-Mozzarella -Fried calamari -Side salad -Bourbon old fashion What I got for dinner:-Gnocchi dish with cream sauce, bacon, and a bunch of other stuff. Could sap this up with bread the sauce was SO good. Overall, very neat spot. Highly recommend for anyone north or south of 117th. Fresh pasta, great service, and good booze. Can't go wrong. Heard they have a great brunch too? Could be back for that in the next few weeks!

I really wanted to love the place, but I just couldn't :(I made a last minute reservation for Saturday night and did not have any issues. The restaurant is very, very tiny and cramped. You will be seated inches away from another party..They first start off with a complimentary bite sized fried puff served with something like an everything bagel seasoning cream cheese. It was nice and crunchy... pretty good..Snow Crab Noodles... $34.00... it tasted fine - pasta was cooked well and texture was good. the dish has a very light flavor but still feels heavy, so we shared this as an appetizer. This is something I would eat again if offered, but it was nothing phenomenal. I overheard the waiter saying how much he loved this dish and how it's the best dish ever, but I didn't understand the hype.
