Pig Out for Two - $61.0010 cubes of stringy pork belly with crispy skin - definitely not as tender as I expected, a little on the drier side.I was extremely disappointed with this dish because there's nothing I tasted that could justify the price I paid for this. I would have much preferred the standard pork they serve at Chinese restaurants..The side of peanut noodles this dish comes with is good though, even better than the noodles from the crab dish.Overall, I just think that this restaurant was over hyped and pricey. Nothing was bad about any of the dishes, but nothing (not even the signature dishes) was mind-blowing or amazing either.

Came for lunch during Restaurant Week and thought it was a great deal, if not the absolute best food ever. I ordered the calamari, tuna burger with zucchini fries and walnut cake for dessert. My boyfriend had the Meze dips and sea bream. The calamari was just okay, but the dips were great the entrees were delicious. Fish was perfectly cooked and the portion was huge. Tuna burger was tasty and I especially loved the zucchini fries. Service was good until the end, when it took forever for our waiter to bring our check. Overall it was a good experience.

I love clay pot so much.The neighborhood where I live has clay pot as well. I eat it almost once a week!We got 2 of 2 topping clay pot- beef and Chinese sausage- eel and pork bellyFlavor was really good, love sweet soy sauce (the must) and they also offer spicy soy sauce and ginger paste. Very good with the rice together.Our favorite topping is eel, we didn't see those topping before, it's quit fit with the pot.The beef and pork belly taste pretty good but we feel they should cut it in little smaller, so is easy to mix and eat with rice.Definitely worth to try if you never had clay pot before!

I've visited this restaurant multiple times for both lunch and dinner, and I'm consistently impressed by the delicious food. Each visit has been outstanding. The prime seating is near the front window, where you'll be treated to a stunning view of the Empire State Building, particularly captivating in the evening when it's beautifully illuminated. Highly recommend a meal here for the food and the view!

I came here for brunch with my girlfriend hoping for a nice, chill meal where we could catch up. Unfortunately, this is more of a party spot for brunch so we found ourselves sitting at an uncomfortable table, surrounded by a loud dining room.My girlfriend had the Shrimp and Grits and I had the Ackee and Saltfish with a side of turkey bacon. My girlfriend enjoyed her dish but I had serious reservations about mine. The quality certainly did not justify the price. It was very watery and lacking greatly, something that could stand by the fish and ackee. All it was served with were a couple of pieces of fried sweet plantain and not a dumpling in sight.I probably won't be back here as it's just not my cup of tea.

Title: A Fresh Take on Dimsum in Chinatown

If you find yourself wandering through Chinatown with a craving for dimsum, the latest addition to the scene will satisfy your appetite with a delightful twist. Unlike the traditional cart service, this gem serves freshly made dimsum hot and direct to your table, ensuring each bite is as steamy and succulent as possible.

The menu caters to a variety of tastes, and one standout is the Japanese tofu with mushrooms – a delectable option that will even have meat-lovers eyeing the vegetarian section. But the real heart of the experience is Julia, whose warm and personal touch elevates the dining ambiance. With her utmost attention to hospitality, you're guaranteed an impeccable meal.

For those in the vicinity, this spot is a must-try. It's not just a meal; it's an exceptional culinary encounter led by a host who truly cares about your experience.

Title: A Hidden Gem Serving Authentic Chinese Cuisine

Back in October, my quest for authentic Chinese fare led me to a delightful hole-in-the-wall restaurant that instantly transported me to the vibrant streets of LA's Chinatown. Despite having already eaten dinner, I couldn't resist indulging in a large bowl brimming with succulent pork, perfectly steamed rice, and tender cabbage – all for the modest sum of $5.50.

For those seeking a genuine taste of Chinese cooking without breaking the bank, this spot is a must-visit. They don't skimp on portions either, ensuring a satisfying meal that leaves both your belly and wallet content. My first-time foray into New York's culinary landscape was made all the more memorable thanks to this tasty find.

I recently had the chance to visit Chubby Princess, the newly rebranded eatery that took over from the much-loved Tomorrow. This fresh venture maintains a resemblance to its predecessor's offerings but has elevated the dining experience from fast casual to a more composed sit-down atmosphere. One orders at the front before selecting a table, subtly shifting the service dynamic.

On my initial visit, I indulged in the Mapo Tofu with Rice, priced at an agreeable $10. The dish proved to be a delightful and fulfilling experience, ensuring great value for the cost. The flavors were spot-on, promising a return trip on my calendar. I'm eager to explore more of their menu to see how Chubby Princess has redefined its culinary identity.

During a bustling day exploring New York on foot, my boyfriend and I stumbled upon a hidden gem of a pizza spot luring us with an irresistible sign boasting a $3 pizza and soda combo. While the special was limited to a cheese pizza and soft drink, we still snagged an excellent deal on our selections.

Served piping hot – just the way I love it – the pizza was a slice of heaven, offering a perfect pit stop to refuel. For those looking for a quick, delicious, and wallet-friendly bite in the heart of the Big Apple, I'd heartily recommend dropping by this place. It's an especially great find for avid walkers in need of a tasty pick-me-up!

Title: A Sichuan Twist on Seafood Boils

After much anticipation, I visited a restaurant that sets itself apart from The Boil and similar establishments with its unique Sichuan flair. The menu presents an array of choices, but the standouts are definitely the skewers and boils—not to be overshadowed by the also available hot pot.

Embrace yourself for a spice adventure, as the dishes here carry the hallmark Sichuan heat. If your taste buds are faint of heart, it's wise to request a milder experience. The signature numbing spice, a result of Sichuan peppercorns, allows the more daring diners to withstand the escalating heat.

The culinary journey was a hit, particularly the chicken gizzard skewers, which were expertly flavored. The seafood boils, including shrimp and crab legs bathed in a spicy 13-herb blend, were a delight. And the flaming drunken shrimps? A fiery spectacle not to be missed.

In summary, the restaurant impresses with its bold flavors and Sichuan twist on seafood. I'm already looking forward to my next visit, especially with the incentive of a 10% cash payment discount.

Title: A Mediterranean Gem Offering Authentic Greek Elegance

Review:

My recent visit to this upscale Greek restaurant was a delightful odyssey of Mediterranean flavors. The highlight of the experience was undoubtedly the lunch pre fixe menu, an absolute steal at $32. 

The ambiance transports you straight to Greece with its al fresco vibe, complemented by fresh produce and fish displays that make the setting all the more authentic. The food is exceptional, ranking high on my list of Mediterranean cuisine – it's a well-deserved 5/5. Selections ranged from succulent grilled octopus to fresh oysters and a classic Greek salad to kick things off. For mains, the dorade, cooked simply with olive oil and salt, was a revelation in its tenderness and flavor, while the lamb chops were worth the extra supplement. Concluding the meal with a walnut cake or fresh seasonal fruits left my palate completely satisfied.

Portions were bountiful, ensuring you leave feeling content. The freshly grilled bread paired with olive oil and herbs, snipped at the table from a live plant, added a unique touch to the meal.

Service shone at a 4.8/5—attentive and personal, though there were brief moments of delay when the restaurant became busier. It did little to dampen the overall experience, which was a solid 5/5. This restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving a taste of Greece in a beautiful setting.

Welcome to Dig Inn's fancier sister restaurant. If you're familiar with Dig Inn's menu, the food is healthier yet tasty and a bit on the vegetable heavy side. That said, as a self proclaimed meat lover, I did not miss the meat at all in this meal. The hummus with homemade pita was divine. Some of the best pitas I've ever had the brussel sprouts and carrots were good. The tagliatelle with Jonas crab was amazing. The flavor is absolutely on point. The lasagna had an amazing bechemel sauce and was quite sizable. It is also very rich so I recommend sharing this dish. Very good overall. A few things to note. They don't seem to have a full bar yet so the cocktails are made with liqueurs. They do have wine and beer though. I feel like they're a bit understaffed on the waitstaff but that's easily rectified. The kitchen is open and they gave an amazing open pit grill. The one really weird thing that I've never seen before in a professional kitchen is that the guys cooking the chicken kept using the meat thermometer like they were not confident. The same piece of chicken was stuck numerous times by 2 different chefs. Weird. Be more confident! Also one of the chefs seemed to have been doing nothing while all the others hauled ass.Overall the food was tasty and I'll be back again. Hopefully the few issues will be resolved by then as well as a full bar.

i have wanted to try this place for a long time and haven't got the chance until finally i went to see the F.R.I.E.N.D.S apartment and this place happened to be really near so we went to grab a quick bite. the place was pretty clean. the service was decent, a little bit nonchalant but okay. i asked the guy which one is the most recommended and he said Nonna Marie. everyone on the internet seems to say that too so I went for that. great call. it was a generous slice of fresh, beautiful perfectly baked dough that has nice crust on the edges but not dry or burnt, topped with fresh tomatoes, mozarella, and basil. i don't even usually like cheese all that much but this pizza is good. and it's only $3.50 per slice! plus i have how they have seatings outside and it feels nice to enjoy the pizza while sitting outside and enjoy the cute neighborhood

I spent a day in New York with my sister just walking all throughout the city. We promised ourselves to have at least one authentic slice of New York pizza and decided to have it here. Totally unplanned, we ended up by Joe's pizza (I recognized the name from the all the food videos I watch on YouTube) and decided to get our slices here. We got lucky the line was really short when we got ours but moves super fast. Be ready to have your order and cash ready by the time you get to the front of the line. We were in and out in under 5 mins. The pizza's good, especially for the price (considering fame and all). For the amount of ooey gooey cheese on this pizza and the pepperoni, it is surprisingly not that greasy as well. But personally, I have had better but it's a good iconic pizza to try. Buy a slice for a snack but you'd probably need 2 slices to fill you up.

Title: A Lukewarm Experience at Artichoke Pizza

My quest for the perfect slice led me to one of the original Artichoke Pizza locations alongside my Buffalo comrade, a die-hard fan. While I've frequented various establishments since, my experience here was notably mixed.

Upon arrival, the promise of late-night indulgence is a clear advantage. Artichoke Pizza caters to the after-hours crowd, providing a rare beacon of cheesy sustenance when options dwindle. This, however, does not entirely compensate for the less-than-warm welcome received from the staff, an issue that seems consistent across their venues, especially the one amidst the Meatpacking district's pulsing nightlife.

The menu touts an artichoke specialty slice that's bound to thrill artichoke enthusiasts. Sadly, for the price, the pizza fails to impress. The slices, noticeably overpriced, arrive lukewarm with an overwhelming cheese-to-sauce ratio and a tendency toward undercooking.

While Artichoke Pizza might win some points for uniqueness and being an after-dark haven, it's hard to ignore superior nearby alternatives like Joe's and Bleecker St, not to mention the more artistically inclined Artistic Pizza. The scale tips unfavorably — Artichoke is overrated, overpriced, and doesn't quite hit the mark for me. A touch more friendliness might sway me to round up to four stars, but as it stands, I find it hard to fully embrace their take on the New York slice.

I dined here tonight with my wonderful kids and it was lovely! We had an attentive waitress and a great table next to the kitchen. We ordered gluten free fried calamari which was so good . I ordered the albacore, my daughter ordered the chicken  and my son ordered the lobster pasta. It was all pretty darn good! I would totally go back!!

I visited Almond with a few friends on Saturday and LOVED it - The restaurant is so chic & the wait-staff was amazing, along with the food! The price tag is a bit hefty, but the dining experience is worth it.We made reservations beforehand and no trouble getting a table - We were seated immediately. We ordered a few glasses of wine & picked a few entrees off the menu. I got the Saturday special (which was supposed to be Rack if Lamb), but instead we were informed of a slight menu change; lamb shank with some fresh homemade gnocchi. I decided to give it a try and I was happy I did - The meat was so tender and melted off the bone, and the gnocchi were delicious. Other dishes that were ordered were the sea scallops & roasted duck, roast chicken, and skirt steak. We also ordered the le grande Mac & cheese to share, which was the right choice - So creamy & truffley, definitely fed my soul!The meal was great, but my friend's steak was a bit tough, so she told the waiter. He quickly brought us out 3 desserts on the house to compensate! The sticky coffee date cake was my favorite. He also brought out a piece of the lemon tart and the chocolate pot de creme. All the desserts were sweet & hit the spot. We really appreciated Almond's generosity and care for their guests! I will definitely be back!

Title: Missed the Mark on Authenticity and Value

I had high hopes for a Korean feast when I visited this spot, but what I found was more 'Korean-inspired' than truly Korean. The lack of traditional dishes like kimchi jjigae was disappointing. I settled for 'spicy' rice cakes, which turned out to be a misnomer. While the texture achieved a mild crispiness, the rice cakes were predominantly gummy and the sauce lacked the advertised heat. To make matters worse, shelling out an extra $3 only added two lonely shrimp to the mix.

The stinginess extended to the portions as well; I was left hungry after my meal. Topping off my experience was the steep price tag—$24 for the dish and a soda, a questionable value for what was on offer.

In summary, if you're craving genuine Korean cuisine, this isn't the place. The food here is as Korean as General Tso's is Chinese, and with the unfulfilling portions and hefty prices, I won't be returning.

Popped in as an alternative for a light Brunch before the Opera. Brunch was being served and that was ideal for a lighter meal.Mimosas were ordered. Yogurt Parfait full of Fresh Fruit, Granola was a perfect starter.Eggs Benefit & Jambon Beurre Sandwich as main Entrees.The dishes were delicious, the ideal light fare dishes.Ambiance was nice. Service attentive. Our coats checked in. A nice place for a quick bite.Pricey though.

I recently embarked on a Netflix-promoted treasure hunt in Little Italy, coinciding with "The Irishman" release, and stumbled upon an uncharted gem for my first stop. Expectations were undefined, but the buzz in the queue piqued my interest. This inconspicuous pizzeria was a shot in the dark for me, yet it turned out to be a delightful surprise.

At my turn, I uttered the code phrase "tell 'em Jimmy sent you," promptly rewarded with a slice straight from the oven. This wasn't just any slice; it was an impeccable balance of organic tomato sauce and cheese, nestled on a flawless thin crust, piping hot and fresh. 

A heartfelt nod to Manero's Pizzeria and Netflix for this slice of heaven. It's clear to me now—when the craving hits, this is the spot for my pizza fix.

Visited a noodle spot in Hudson Eats on a Thursday afternoon, placing a Ritual order for convenience. Tucked away at the food hall's end, the eatery offers swift servings of noodle and rice dishes. I opted for the Beef Noodle Soup, priced at $14.50. Prepared within 15 minutes, albeit a slight delay attributed to engaged staff, the dish was a hearty portion with abundant beef cuts but could have benefited from more noodles. While satisfyingly ample, the broth lacked the expected kick, tilting towards oily rather than richly flavored. While not an exceptional dining episode, it still stands out in Hudson Eats, next to Tartinery and Fuku.

Ordered Tartinery for lunch- this is like thr 3rd or 4th time I've ordered from it.This time i got turkey cheese toast with spinach and tomatoes and lentil salad. They are gorgeous to look at and pleasant to eat as well. I have to say every time I order from Tartinery I am always surprised by how good the crust of the toast is- maybe thats why it keeps driving me back!I was surprised to see how big the lentil salad is and as usual, wasnt able to finish all the food.Will definitely come back again!

Used to come here a lot with friends for brunch while I was in grad school. Haven't been in a few years but with my aunt and sister in town for the Lunar New Year i wanted to have a fun NYC brunch experience planned for them.  When we arrived we were seated promptly. One thing that struck me was that the usual brunch crowd wasn't there. Usually there's a decent line (we arrived around 10am) but the place was mostly empty. After we were seated, our waiter (forgot his name) took our order and promptly never returned. He just left us there and we had to wave down someone else for ketchup/hot sauce/more water, etc. We saw our waiter continually stopping by the bar to chat and socialize with his fellow coworkers but never could catch his eye or attention for service. Eventually another waiter named Johnathan started helping us and continued to do so. We thought it was weird that if we were being passed on to another waiter, why our original waiter didn't inform us or introduce us to whoever would be taking over our service. It was just rude and  disappointing and it wasn't even by busy by any standard of weekend brunch in NYC on a Saturday. We tipped 18% anyway because I have a roommate who works in the restaurant industry and I know how much they depend on tips. We wanted Johnathan to have the tip alone and not have to share it with our original waiter, but he said it all goes into one pot and is divided up at the end of the day. Food was meeehh. I ordered the salmon Benedict and the eggs were almost cooked all the way through... none of the runny yolk characteristic of a good eggs benny. My sister got the chicken sandwich, which was all bread with a small scrawny  piece of chicken compared to how large and thick the bread was. My aunt ordered the egg white omelette with spinach and it was so wet and oily. Like the eggs were pretty much inedible. It looked like it was cooked in a lot of oil then dunked in sink water before being plated. My husband got the BECA (bacon, eggs, cheese and avocado) which he liked but said it was a little greasy. The side salad we ordered was wilted and not very appetizing. Outside of Johnathan, who could tell we were being ignored and decided to serve us... everyone else basically ignored us. All in all, I feel like this service, the food and the atmosphere was very poor. Also, I think our original waiter didn't even bother to write down our order correctly because my husband first was given an egg white omelette... it was corrected to the BECA when we told them of their mistake. I always appreciate the restaurant staff and try to tip even if the service was bad... but this really rankled because no one noticed or cared or apologized for the crappy service and food. I would NOT eat here again and I would definitely discourage anyone from eating here. NYC has such a high number of excellent brunch spots that no one has to suffer through such bad food and service... I guess there's a reason why there's no longer a long line waiting outside Jane to eat. RUNNNNN!

I love Bettibar! It is the bar on the second floor of Hourglass and has killer happy hour deals seven days a week from 5-10pm. You can also get full food service up there. On happy hour they have $5 red sangria. It was such a great deal and tasted delicious! I would definitely order it again.We also ordered food, which was the real star of the evening. I had the chicken alfredo which was out of this world amazing! The blackened chicken on top adds the perfect level of spice to the creamy alfredo fettuccine underneath. I am honestly not even a fan of fettuccine alfredo and I order this every time I am here.  I would come here just for this pasta dish... that's how incredible it is! Definitely check out Bettibar for not only the great happy hour deals, but the food as well! I just wish there was a little more seating because sometimes it is hard to find a few seats together and hard to grab one of the few tables. Other than that, a perfect bar experience!

Title: A Sparkling Gem Before Times Square's New Year's Festivities

My New Year's Eve in NYC turned delightfully delicious when my party and I stumbled upon this cozy restaurant en route to the Times Square ball drop. Braving the pouring rain, we were met with the serendipitous fortune of immediately snagging a table for four in the bustling yet efficient eatery.

The staff had the customer turnover down to an art, whisking us to our table and serving up our meals with New York haste, yet without scrimping on quality. The Paneer Tikka appetizer was a standout, thoughtfully prepared to let the cheese's natural flavor shine amidst a subtle spice blend. Their bread basket, boasting fluffy Naan and hearty Tandoori Rotis, was testament to their authentic Tandoor oven mastery.

While the Veg Biryani had room to make its mark, the Malai Kofta was a showstopper, rightfully earning its "signature dish" status. Note that the entrees don't automatically come with rice, but the accommodating staff readily provided a side of aromatic pilaf.

Capping off the meal were complimentary servings of Kheer, a sweet note of traditional dessert bliss. Amid the New Year's frenzy, this restaurant was a culinary oasis, especially for those who appreciate the fine balance of swift service and high-quality Indian cuisine.

Ahh this place brings back old memories when I use to hang around Chinatown...I remember lining up for their Hk milk tea because they were one of the few places that made it resembling HK...Visiting again shocked me as I noticed the place has not change, I was even more shocked that they didn't raise their price as their neighbors has changed many times...I ordered the usual: milk tea, shark fin soup, yunan noodles, and house special French toast. Everything was delicious except for the over drenched French toast. Overall still very satisfy as every taste brought back the years of happiness

Our office cane here for  lunch to celebrate our President's birthday.  We were sat in the back room which would have been nice if it hadn't been so quiet you could hear a pin drop. One of my coworkers asked  if they could turn on music in the room and they said no. Our waiter also left a lot to be desired. It took him 3 or 4 times of someone saying what they wanted before he understood. We then sat at our table for more than 30 minutes before an appetizer or salad came out. I ordered the Lasagna Bolognese and it was delicious and filling once I finally got it. When we ordered dessert at the end, the person sitting next to me asked if they had any fruit we could get for the Pres. as his dessert and he outright said no. A few minutes later, not knowing my coworker had asked, the Pres. asked the exact same question of the waiter and he said sure no problem and brought out a fruit plate. It was a very strange experience.

Since we had wonderful dining al fresco a week ago, we decided to go back to Greenwich Village and do just that again.Enter Fukurou since we were craving for either Japanese tapas or izakaya, the reviews mentioned that it gets busier at around 7pm so we showed up at 6:30pm and were seated outside. The place is arguably small with few tables inside and out, it was also an open kitchen so you get to see what they're doing with your dishes.We started with 360ml of Sake and the first tapa to come out was the tuna and avocado carpaccio, then were intrigued with Omu Yakisoba, it's pan fried noodles wrapped in Japanese pancake with cabbage, it was delicious. They then served the deep fried baby horse Mackerel and grilled salmonFollowed by deep fried octopus and squid and spicy pepper drumsticks. We thought that among the plates the spicy fried chicken and the Omu Yakisoba stood out. While the rest were perhaps a little lacking in both flavors and presentation.All in all, although there were some dishes that did not live up to expectations, we would certainly still consider to come back and try some of the other small plates, the service staff are commendable!

It's mid-morning and I need a quick pick-me-up. This bar was open. Everything from coffee to beer to food to Red Bull. Fun and chill decor. Friendly and attentive staff. Fun crowd. And surprisingly pretty crowded (but not too crowded) for a mid-morning weekday. Definitely a spot I'd hit up again and again. Great spot to chill and drink and grab a bite to eat.

Title: A Mediterranean Gem with Minor Hiccups

If you're on the quest for an upscale Mediterranean dining experience, your search might very well end at this delightful spot. From the moment you walk through the door, the ambiance envelops you with a warm welcome, thanks in part to a super sweet hostess—regrettably, her name escaped me.

While waiting for our party to gather, the bar was a cozy layover with the discovery of the "Mediterranean mule." A concoction so divine, I'm now on a mission to find fig vodka to recreate this masterpiece.

With an appetite sharpened by excellent drinks, we delved into the menu. Our waiter's expertise was invaluable in navigating the array of "Limani Specialties." We feasted as a group of seven, embarking on a culinary adventure. The Kolokitni was simply off the charts, a unanimous 20 out of 10! Greek Meze came in strong with an 8.5, the Ktipiti a standout. However, the Calamari fell short at a 5.5, as it was over-fried and lacked the punch of flavor one would expect.

Main courses were a mixed bag. The lobster pasta, ordered by four of us (one with a scallop substitute), didn't hit the mark, needing just a bit more seasoning to truly shine. The others enjoyed their Organic salmon, filet mignon, and halibut—no complaints on those fronts. Paired with two bottles of wine, we capped the night with the irresistible BAKLAVA—an absolute crowd-pleaser.

All in all, while the pasta and calamari might not see a re-order from us, the allure of that sublime Kolokitni and other dishes calls for a return visit. This Mediterranean restaurant holds promise, and with a few tweaks, it could rise to perfection.

This place is 5 STARS FASHO! I came here for my birthday and the creamy kimchi udon is to die for. Literally I could take a bath in that sauce. Ambience is fun in an underground basement type vibe with twinkly lights. The izakaya mew roll was also delicious. Frozen beer was cool, but not for me.

We had a delightful dining experience at the restaurant, thanks in large part to our wonderful waitress, Jenny. She was attentive and informative, expertly walking us through the day's specials with persuasive recommendations. The nachos were nothing short of amazing, and the wings did not disappoint either, being really good. Complementing the meal was the $5 Goose Island beer, which was a perfect touch. I'm looking forward to my next visit.

After an unexpected delay due to traffic that pushed my NYC arrival to 9 p.m., I found solace in a Yelp-recommended eatery. Despite missing a planned dinner with a friend, the Spicy ramen and karaage chicken I ordered did not disappoint. The ramen's broth was delightful, and the noodles boasted a satisfying texture, hitting the right spot after my prolonged bus ordeal. At a precise $20 pre-tip, the meal was reasonably priced. I'd certainly recommend this spot for a comforting bite in the city.

During Restaurant Week, my anticipation was high to try out a participating local favorite. The experience mostly lived up to the hype, with the pre-fix menu showcasing some standout dishes. The highlight for me was the lychee martini; a refreshing twist on the classic, boasting a perfect blend of citrus without being overly sweet.

The meal commenced with the best crunchy spring rolls I've ever had, accompanied by an exquisite orange Thai sauce. Wrapped in lettuce, they offered a harmonious mix of texture and flavor. Another starter, the "ravioli" of chopped chicken, shrimp, and veggies in rice paper, was a delightful twist on the traditional.

For mains, the spicy chicken, which was pleasantly mild, and the perfectly cooked salmon topped my list, both served with their respective rice. Though the white sticky rice was somewhat plain, the jasmine rice had a more robust presentation that leaned towards a fried rice look.

Dessert was the only underwhelming part of the meal, with a basic sorbet and a decent tart, which admittedly isn't to my taste.

The evening took an odd turn when we found an unidentifiable grey substance on our lettuce. Alerting the waiter resulted in an apology but no further explanation, which was disappointing.

Setting aside that hiccup, dining in a hotspot frequented by celebrities like Tory Burch and Cindy Crawford added to the allure. Despite the small mishap, the restaurant delivered a memorable Restaurant Week experience.

Title: A Consistently Delectable Lobster Roll at Luke’s

Review:

Luke's has solidified its spot as my go-to for a spectacular lobster roll experience. The rolls are unfailingly buttery, with perfectly toasted buns and a precise meat-to-sauce ratio, even in the smaller serving. Priced under $20, it's a steal, and you can upgrade to a jumbo for just $6 more. Sure, it's pricier than your average takeout, but we're talking lobster here, so it's absolutely worth it.

Luke's isn't just about lobster rolls though; their menu also features tasty crab and shrimp rolls, and the option to indulge in combos. While you'll find Luke's in various locations throughout the city, the one I frequent offers a spacious dining area, a pleasant upgrade from some of the more cramped spots. All in all, for a satisfying seafood roll, Luke's never fails to hit the mark.
Excellent bibimbap. You can't go wrong with either the bulgogi or the spicy pork ones. Japchae is also very good. Steamed mandu were good too.

Title: A Delicious Find in KTown - Samwon

Upon entering Samwon, the prices might give you pause—especially for the Korean BBQ options. However, delve a little deeper into the menu, and you'll find the pricing aligns with other eateries in KTown. In fact, the quality, taste, and generous portion sizes here surpass what you'd typically expect.

One must-try is the Chadol Kimchi Bokkeum Bap. This dish is a delightful mix of flavors, hitting the perfect note of spiciness. The rice crisps beautifully and is interspersed with hearty chunks of meat, creating a satisfying texture and taste. It's quite shareable, too—ideal for 3-4 people.

To complement your meal, the peach makgeolli is an absolute standout. This drink is refreshingly light and captures the essence of peach in a fizzy, soda-like concoction. It's as delightful to the palate as it is unique.

In summary, Samwon offers a culinary experience that's worth every penny, especially once you venture beyond the barbecue. Highly recommended!

We got here between 2-3p, hoping there'd be no wait, but we were wrong.  We waited 20-30 minutes.  Unless your party is more than 2, you'll most likely be at the communal table.  The restaurant is loud.  I had the Akamaru New York Ramen; hubby chose Shiromaru New York Ramen (vegetarian).  Both were pretty good.  Mine is more interesting.  Portion is light.  Perhaps I'm used to the more generous portion in Los Angeles.   I'd think there are many comparable ramen shops.  I have to say that it has a cool vibe.

Kosaka's reputation as a sophisticated omakase destination with a Michelin star is well-deserved, underscored by its warm and helpful staff, as well as its unique distinction of having a female sushi chef—a refreshing sight that seems uncommon in both San Francisco and Japan. Their sake program impresses, adding to the allure of the dining experience.

Nevertheless, despite these promising attributes, a few missteps during our visit were difficult to overlook. Most notably, the kitchen running out of tamago, a fundamental element of an omakase meal, was perplexing, particularly given our standard 8:15 PM reservation time. This was compounded by the absence of an alternative dessert course. Further disappointment came with the unavailability of any variety of uni for their signature dishes, which was a crushing blow to our anticipation.

Scrutinizing the food itself, the artistry on display did not meet expectations. The sushi, though fresh, suffered from imprecision in cuts and assembly. Additionally, some nigiri pieces had overly moist rice that compromised their integrity, causing them to fall apart—an inconsistency unbecoming of a restaurant of this caliber and price point.

In summary, while Kosaka has many of the right ingredients for an exemplary dining experience, our visit was marred by a few avoidable shortcomings that left us feeling underwhelmed.

Tucked away as a Lower Manhattan classic, The Odeon stands out as an all-day dining gem—a true cafeteria, as its sign proudly claims. Whether you're yearning for a hearty breakfast, a leisurely brunch, a casual lunch, an afternoon tea escape, post-work libations, a satisfying dinner, or a late-night treat, The Odeon delivers with aplomb. Unlike jack-of-all-trades eateries that falter, this establishment excels across the board. Though its days as an '80s hot spot might be a glimmer in the past, The Odeon's longevity and resilience, especially through the trials of 9/11, speak volumes. It's a beacon of culinary reliability and comfort, and one can only hope that it remains a steadfast fixture for generations to savor.

I recently visited Russian Samovar with a friend well-versed in Russian cuisine, and it was a delightful culinary adventure. For starters, we indulged in the Russian trio salad, a tasting plate of Olivier, vinegret, and shuba. The creamy Olivier was my favorite, likely due to its comforting mayonnaise and potato combination. While the vinegret acquired taste, the shuba found a happy medium. Sampling all three was a wise decision.

The vareniki, pan-fried potato dumplings accompanied by mushrooms and onions, were a highlight. Their flavor was elevated when paired with the accompanying sour cream. As for the main courses, my duck a la russe was satisfactory but unremarkable. However, my friend's tabaka seemed to be a better choice, reflecting authentically Russian flavors.

Dessert was the showstopper: the medovik, a heavenly layered honey cake, was exceptional and generously portioned for sharing. My friend, fresh from a Russian visit, confirmed its authenticity.

Lastly, for a bit of fun, don't miss out on the free vodka shot offered with Yelp check-in; the cucumber selection was refreshingly smooth. Russian Samovar stands out as a solid choice for traditional Russian fare.

I could boast and brag about Los Tacos No. 1 for pages and pages but in simpler terms, they're just fantastic! The line is sometimes longer than you'd like but the food is worth the wait. I absolutely love their Adobada tacos! Delicious, fresh and full of flavor is what comes to mind when I think of them. 3 isn't nearly enough but self control. I'll be coming back and bringing all my friends and family.

This place randomly popped up on my Yelp app and I was so excited to show my mom/grandparents - they're Hakka and frequented South Wind years ago. I'm also a huge fan of all types of cherng fun (rice rolls) so we all had to try it ASAP.The tiny hole in the wall is the perfect place for pick up / takeout. We brought the Hak Rolls and stuffed tofu back home to enjoy and it brought back a lot of nostalgic feels for my family. The rice rolls were a little too oily for me but still soo good. The meat stuffing in the tofu however had a weird texture to it that we didn't like. I'd come back for just the rice rolls and maybe to try the dumplings.My mom also confirmed that they have no relation to the original South Wind owners, but they're friendly / know of each other.

There's no better endorsement than when multiple people are inside already finishing having stuffed their faces before NOON. I would soon follow in their footsteps, and I would not regret going out of my way to drop in at the highly regarded Sauce.Given the early time of day, only half of the counter was filled with pies, but each looked outstanding. I flirted with the idea of ordering the Sausage, Vodka, and Al Pastor slices. But the Cheese and Upside Down caught my eye.I asked the guy behind the counter which was better and he said both are incredibly popular and it depends on the person. He added that the cheese includes fresh basil while the upside down has oregano and pecorino; I ordered both.On a 1-10 scale, the Cheese gets an 8.8 and the Upside Down an 8.1. The sweet sauce from the cheese and slightly burnt crust made each bite better than the next. Very much my style slice (some prefer a more garlicky sauce). Thin, rich, vibrant, light. One of the best slices I've had in NYC. I could see people coming to Sauce solely for the Upside Down slice but I prefer the classic cheese. That pecorino on top was DAMN good though.The two slices came with Sauce's "signature tomato gravy" which was incredible. Reminded me of a tomato soup in the best way possible. I didn't think it was necessary at first but it was perfect for dipping the crust in. A nice touch adding this to orders and a great complement to my slices.And the cherry on top: I asked for a cup for water but was told the cup delivery hadn't arrived yet. The guy went to the back and grabbed me a bottle of water and offered it free of charge. Upper echelon pizza and excellent service.

Title: A Hearty Slice in the Heart of the City

If you find yourself craving a good, substantial piece of pizza, this spot has got you covered with slices so hefty, one pepperoni will suffice. These slices tip the scale on the greasier end, yet they pack a satisfying punch with their thick, chewy dough – a fulfilling experience for those with big appetites.

Be prepared for a bit of a wait; the popularity of this place is evident in the line. Service might feel rushed here; we had a slight hiccup understanding the server when ordering our slices – their speedy delivery in this fast-paced city is something to adapt to.

All things considered, this pizza joint is a must-visit for those looking for a slice that's truly a meal in itself. Just make sure you're ready for a swift transaction!

Upon visiting this restaurant, impressed by its cleanliness and open layout, I encountered a notable inconvenience—low stool seating, which posed an initial challenge for my octogenarian father. However, driven by hunger, we decided to stay, and thankfully, the seating was manageable.

My anticipation for their cuisine had been stoked by a Food Channel feature on their dishes. Yet, the reality at this specific branch fell short of my high expectations. The hand ripped noodles with oxtail, especially the spicy variant I chose, disappointed me. The noodles seemed like thick, greasy dough swatches, and the spices were unpleasantly grainy, detracting from the overall experience. While my sister found some enjoyment in the meal, she noted the price was steep, and my father deemed it just passable.

Despite this, the restaurant seemed to have a much-lauded burger, judging by the number of patrons opting for this item, especially as a takeaway option. Should I give this place another try, the burger will be my choice in hopes of a more satisfying experience.
Just a dumpy English pub. But we had an Irish waitress who was sweet. The whisky pours were generous and the chips were crispy. So it was near the hotel. What more could you want, had fun!!

Boy is this place busy. We had gotten facials right next door and decided to grab a bit here to eat. We asked how long the wait was and the guy told us two hours but was joking. It was 5-10 minutes so we put our name in. We waited way longer than 10 minutes. Once we got called my mom who had a hard time doing stairs (but can still do them) asked if there was an elevator. That took even longer. The host insisted as he called into his walkie for an elevator assist. The elevator is located behind a door in the back. We finally got assisted to go up and told us to wait here. So we basically had to get back in line and we're the last people in the group even though we were the first ones called. That was a bummer and a bit annoying. We should have been the first ones seated. We finally got seated and our server was nice. Told us about the signs again. We ordered the New England clam chowder, shrimp po boy and accidental fish and shrimp. My mom received a dirty spoon with her soup so she asked for a new spoon. Food was good. Pricey because it is time square. Overall, service was fine (she was nice), food was fine, but the whole process prior was longer than we were told.

When Au Cheval came to New York, I immediately wanted to try it.  After seeing their three hours lines looping around the block, I decided to (somewhat impatiently) wait a few weeks to see if the crowds died down.  I'm glad I did.  While I was OK with a half hour late the other night, I would have been seriously enraged to wait three hours for what we ended up with.After eating at Au Cheval, I sat there and wondered about myself.  If everyone loves this place, what's wrong with me?  I was just overall not very impressed, especially for the price point.  I went into work the next day and asked some colleagues if they had been yet, and they all felt similarly.  Then, I saw the Eater and Grub Street articles about Au Cheval, and I felt completely understood.It's not that the food here is bad.  It certainly is not.  However, for $18 for a burger and $9 for fries, I would rather go to Minetta Tavern.  This meal is not worth $27.  We got the single burger which was, as mentioned, good but not great. We also got the honey fried chicken for $24 which was a large portion but again, seemed just OK.  Believe it or not, our favorite dish was the crispy potato hash for $9.  The portion was small but the hash was crispy and flavorful. Our server was helpful and knowledgeable about the menu.  All in all though, we felt like our meal was very overpriced.  I would eat this food again but the price / quality ratio is way off.

Came here on a Tuesday night and it was pretty packed with a wait of about ~40 minutes if you didn't have a reservation, so I recommend making reservations beforehand. Staff was very attentive and quick with our orders. My party ordered the kakuni, bacon mochi skewer, beef tongue, teriyaki ika, okonomoyaki with bacon, and the hamachi tamaki. I enjoyed all of these dishes, I highly recommend the hamachi tamaki as it was my favorite among all. The hamachi was seared perfectly and almost melted in your mouth. The yuzu sauce wasn't overpowering but complemented it very well! The bacon mochi skewer was unique and I do recommend this as well, because it also worked perfectly together with flavor and texture. The teriyaki ika was good and the squid has a bounce to it, but not the excessively rubbery over cooked kind of bounce to it. The okonomoyaki comes with a seafood or bacon option and I believe it's additional to add cheese. I recommend adding cheese because cheese makes everything great. Still the okonomoyaki was nice, fluffy and enjoyable to eat, but it was on the heavier side for me. Overall, I recommend coming here for a casual dinner with some pals over food and drinks. Super relaxed ambiance here and I thoroughly enjoyed my experience here!

I won't hesitate to say that this is my favorite empanada joint. It's the only place I've had empanadas that were completely stuffed. My favorite one to get is the Reggaeton!! I add a little green sauce and I'm in heaven. It's unfortunate that I could only eat three hahahaha they have a big menu and so far everything I've had is good. You can tell this place takes pride in their food. Most places I've gone to leave half the empanada empty. So you're basically just eating flour. Not Empanada Mama!! Im guessing the owners are part Colombian because they offer a lot of Colombian foodies. I love their mora (blackberry) juice. I would say the only bad thing about this place is this Arepas. But seeing that I only go there for empanadas. I could careless if their arepas suck. If you're looking for good empanadas, with flavor, variety and good dipping sauce. Empanada mamas is the place to go!!

Had my birthday brunch here, Simone is excellent to work with. Made everything very easy and flawless. We had a group of 20 and pricing was great for the amount of food we got. Apps: Escalivada (eggplant dis) was unique and filling, the patata brava are potatoes wjth a garlic aioli, croquetas de seta are mushroom croquettes to die for. Honestly could eat these for dayyys. The pan con tomato was aweosme, bread with garlicky tomato sauce and a slice of menchego cheese. Too good. Entree: Torrija (french toast) with everything you'd want, and the huevos Benedict was really tasty. I asked for the poached egg to be cooked well and they were able to accommodate. Dessert: churros sundae (noms). Unlimited drinks were gin based red sangria, vodka based white sangria, and tequila based rosé. Overall, I'd go back for the food, but space is small so it was difficult to take pictures with each other etc if you're meeting for a bday or friends after a long time and want to do that. And there's no pop music so it's more of a eat breakfast vibe rather than a let's celebrate vibe.

Love this place for dim sum!Got steamed ribs, black pepper short ribs, shrimp dumplings, pineapple buns, vegetables and so on.Everything was fresh and delicious! Have to say the taste is very authentic, though having the sweet soy sauce would make it better. Their pineapple buns actually got pineapple inside! Such a nice surprise!Large portions and good service. No complaints at all!

Title: Quick Lunch Respite at Xe May Sandwich Shop

On what felt like one of New York's hottest days, I found sanctuary in a little subterranean spot called Xe May. Craving a quick and satisfying meal, I opted for what I consider the ultimate solo lunch delight: a Banh Mi.

The shop keeps a low profile, nestled downstairs of a nondescript building, and while the menu tempts with various fusion offerings, I'm a classic kind of diner. I ordered the traditional Banh Mi, a delectable assembly of BBQ pork, headcheese, pork roll, and a slick of pate. Xe May nails the personalized experience with an option to select your spice level, so I took a cautious route and picked "spicy."

Unfortunately, the day's jalapeños packed less punch than expected, prompting a side request for extra heat. Regardless, the sandwich didn't disappoint. The bread was toasted to perfection, creating a satisfying crunch, and the chili mayo was nothing short of divine.

Complementing the hearty Banh Mi was the basil limeade—a choice as refreshing as it was palate-cleansing. It's a must-try for anyone looking to beat the heat.

Service at Xe May was another highlight, with a super friendly cashier who wasn't shy about recommending other items on the menu. Her enthusiasm has me considering a return visit to explore beyond my usual pick—perhaps a foray into their fusion tacos.

In summary, Xe May is an excellent spot for a quick, delicious, and no-fuss meal, complete with friendly service and a menu that promises more culinary adventures.

Title: A Slice of Japan and Taiwan Right Here!

After a long stint of disappointing delivery sushi, I decided to switch things up and ordered pickup from this gem of a restaurant — what a revelation! Each bite transported me back to my travels through Japan and Taiwan, where the sushi is nothing short of an art form. While prices here are notably higher, they're entirely justified by the superior quality of the fish. I'm already planning my next order and look forward to the day I can enjoy the full dine-in experience post-pandemic. Highly recommend for any sushi connoisseur!

really wanted to come here to compare it to ichiran. i waited for about 30 minutes for a table for 3 on a sunday night for dinner around 730 pm. as we were waiting, we looked through the menu to see what we wanted to order. we had a pretty high expectation because of all the yelp reviews.i ordered three of the akamaru modern with eggs in all of them. we were all left pretty disappointed after we mixed in the chili paste. it was SO salty and none of us drank the broth. if you get this, take the paste off and try the broth or else it gets real salty. broth:too salty, couldn't eat it with the ramendon't put all the chili sauce in because it ruins the brothnoodles: too firm, even letting it sit was not good enoughnothing special about their thin noodles, not special or something i would get againchashu: slices were a good portion (2 slices) bigger slices than ichiranegg: delicious egg! better than ichiran in this sense pork belly buns $9 for 2 pieces: they should shred the lettucethe sauce was all in the center and not distributed in the bites, some bites were really heavy in sauce while others had no sauce pork belly was not tender at allsuper chewy and presentation was not that greatwould not get it again. overall -egg was the best part of the meal, everything else was definitely not the move. maybe the hakata classic ramens broth would have been better.. many people rave about their broth but this tasted like salt water to us. not sure what happened to our broth. super disappointed and would definitely pay the difference to eat at ichiran. cute date spot though!! dark inside for dinner.note: it is easy to miss due to the construction and the japanese letters. service - super friendly people !!

Always amazing. The flavor truly permeated through into the noodles, and the lamb was the perfect amount of tender and chewy. I ordered N1, the cumin lamb noodles. Definitely a favorite. Also ordered N10, which is the oxtail noodles, and the meat was also amazing. The spice was strong, but it wasn't overpowering. The space is quite tight, but the meal was definitely worth it every single time I go. I could eat this every single day not going to lie

Ahhhhh Manhatta. I've been waiting so long to try this place and it did not disappoint. A solid $78 pre-fixe menu with unreal views?! That's pretty difficult to find in NYC.A few key notes:- Look for the Manhatta sign! Don't get lost like I did and enter through the main building. Manhatta has a separate entrance on Liberty Street.- Come in time for the sunset. Go to the Bayview room for before/after dinner drinks to fully enjoy the views. - The food menu has been updated recently and oftentimes does NOT match the photos on Yelp. Ask your waiter/waitress questions to make smart decisions about courses 1, 2, and 3. - The cocktail menu is pretty limited but the wine list is extensive. For the food, the scotch snails with the table bread were SPOT ON - flavorful and amazing. So good. I really enjoyed my duck and my friends enjoyed their lobster and fish dishes. The desserts were YUMMMM. The whiskey cake, olive oil cake, and strawberry dish were all so delicious. Overall, we had great service, and a great ambience. And of course, incredible food! It's a romantic spot - perfect place for a date or a night out with close friends. I'd highly recommend Manhatta for visitors and locals alike. 4.5/5 stars.

On a recent Sunday evening, my dining experience at this local eatery was delightful. The service was prompt as we were seated immediately. The star of the meal was undoubtedly the ramen—its broth rich and savory, hitting all the right notes of flavor. Both the price and portion size left us satisfied, offering great value for money. I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone in the vicinity. An overall rating of 8/10 seems fitting for such a gratifying dining experience.

Great location near so much, with quite the Sushi menu.After catching an early comedy show near by decided to catch some dinner before walking down to Rockefeller center to see the tree!Thinking out of the box decided I wanted to go for something different. So I opted to go with their name sake the Natsumi roll. You can totally see the love of the Sushi rolling art in their designed presentation. My dish and every other barside with me were like perfect presents. The taste was so fresh, for once I was able to finish it all.All tasted so good I was able to convince my guest to try the Red Bean Ice Cream. Always so good, and should be tried by all. It doesn't taste like beans at all so don't freak. ;) I call it the perfect palette cleanser at a location like this. My guest was pleasantly surprised by it and enjoyed. The only disadvantage there is less for me.Nevertheless, if you are in this area don't get memorized by the familiar. Check in for some tapas...Natsumi tapas, as the plates are bigger than you think and its totally worth every bite!

Title: Disappointment with a View

I've visited this restaurant for both brunch and dinner, and despite the beautiful view, I've been left underwhelmed by both the food and service. The chickpea noodle dish was overwhelmingly salty, lacking any notable texture. It was a struggle to consume despite my thirst from the salt overload. The 'somewhat simple salad' lived up to its name; it was an uninspiring mix of vegetables with no apparent effort to impress. On a positive note, the polenta fries were the solo highlight, offering an intriguing flavor that hinted at this restaurant's untapped potential.

Service was equally disappointing. Getting a waiter's attention felt like an exercise in patience; it took excessive waving and waiting for every interaction, from ordering to the simple request for water, and finally, to settle the bill. Speaking of the bill, an alarming overcharge—$30 more than the actual total—was only corrected because we caught the error on the spot. No apology was offered for this glaring mistake, which is unacceptable for an establishment that markets itself as high-end. Sadly, the restaurant falls flat, saved only by its scenic location.

Ok ok. This was really good. A restaurant specializing in gnocchi? Sign me up!I'm a huge fan of gnocchi, so I've been wanting to try Gnoccheria for a while now. I came in last night with decent expectations, but also didn't expect too much because you just never know with gnocchi. It can either be very ok or fabulous. But wow! I must say it was fabulous! We ordered the gnocchi trio for two. It comes with their sorrentina (red sauce + mozzarella), pesto and three cheese sauces. They were all spectacular! I think my favorite was the three cheese sauce. It was so delicious... and it's hard to go wrong with cheese! The red sauce was absolutely amazing as well. I wasn't expecting much since it seemed like a normal marinara, but it's much more than that! The pesto was good as well, but we both agreed it was our least favorite. I think the trio is the way to go because you get to try a few different sauces. A whole plate of one sauce might be a bit much. I thought the portion size was good for two people and reasonably priced ($28). I would probably also get an app as well next time. The gnocchi themselves were so puffy and delicious. The reason I give 4 stars is because of the service. Not very attentive and kind of rude and a bit slow. Otherwise, a great experience!I do recommend making reservations as it does get crowded!

I recently visited a local spot for a bowl of Old Skool Ramen, priced at $16. While the ramen offered a generous helping of wood ear mushrooms, which I thoroughly enjoyed, it fell short on meat, providing a scant two slices of pork. For the cost, I expected a more substantial serving. Additionally, the absence of an included egg was a disappointment, requiring an additional $3 outlay to complete the dish – bringing the tally to $19 per bowl.

On a more experimental note, I sampled the ramen burger. As an alternative to a traditional burger bun, its crunchiness was a welcome twist and, being relatively inexpensive, it's a novelty I'd opt for again.

One downside to note was the unexpectedly long wait for our food to be served. Overall, the experience was a mixed bag, with room for improvement in both value and service.

I recently visited this restaurant for brunch and was taken aback to find their menu identical for lunch, brunch, and dinner, lacking the usual twist. As part of the same group as Union Square Cafe, it maintains similar pricing, but unfortunately, the food doesn't match up in delicacy, nor does the dining experience linger in memory. The ambiance leans more towards efficiency than leisurely enjoyment.

Their Brussels sprouts were a highlight in flavor but not in portion size, especially at the $11 price point. The pasta stood out with its Asian fusion touch and was a pleasant aspect of the meal. The focaccia paired with grilled chicken was satisfactory, yet the chicken was overly salty, dampening the enjoyment.

A positive note was the unexpected 5% discount for Whitney Museum members, a small but welcome surprise. Overall, the experience was passable but not exceptional.

This place is decent. Nothing to write home about. My friends and I decided to try this place out since I've never been. It's surrounded by other Viet places so I was curious to see what this place delivers in comparison to their rivals.Very average pho. Very salty broth that left me thirsty for hours after. I tasted the broth on its own and it's definitely not my favorite. Couldn't taste the meaty goodness that makes pho delicious. Pho Bang is still my favorite in Chinatown. Also dock a star for the staff giving my friend a hard time about swapping out porkchop for chicken in one of their platter. They wanted to charge him $4 extra. No.

Good Japanese restaurant located on West 50th Street.  Restaurant week so price fix menu of $42 per person for appetizer, entree and dessert.  Good selection to choose from.Filet mignon was excellent as was the dumplings.Tight seating inside.  Bar is separated from restaurant by corridor. Would go back.

My visit to RH Roof was an absolute delight from the moment we walked in right when they opened at 10am on a Friday. The early timing meant we were seated immediately, avoiding the weekend rush that I've been warned about. 

We started with a delectable plate of prosciutto paired with fruit and cheese, setting the stage for a scrumptious meal. This was followed by a hearty scramble and a perfectly prepared avocado toast, both of which boasted generous portions and were exceptionally tasty. 

The ambiance of the place was nothing short of incredible, making it hard to leave. Given that RH Roof is a fairly new gem, celebrating a year come September 2019, I highly recommend visiting before it's swamped by tourists. It's a place that not only meets but exceeds expectations.

Came here on a Saturday for lunch. I got the shoyu ramen (I think), it was tasty but very salty. I remember seeing a sign on the wall that said it was savory, not salty, which I found funny. There wasn't anything too special about the ramen in particular, but I liked it.

Stopped in on a Saturday afternoon with my boyfriend to come grab a drink and was not disappointed. Upon walking in we were greeted by a friendly bartender and sat by the bar area. They do have tables throughout the bar if you don't want to sit at the actual bar. This is a cute sports bar. All the tables had candles lit on them and the lighting was perfectly dim. The aesthetic of the bar was very laid-back and chill. They have big screen TVs throughout the place so you won't miss a thing. They have a well stocked bar area. I mean,cmon, they have frozen rose! What more can you want?! Overall, if you're looking for a laid-back casual sports bar then this is your spot!

Title: Mixed Feelings on Margarita Spot

I've visited this Mexican restaurant multiple times, drawn in by convenience, pricing, and friends' curiosity. The highlight is undoubtedly their Happy Hour—running all day from Sunday to Wednesday and 12-8 PM Thursday to Saturday with $5 margarita specials. If you want a flavor boost, it's $7 more, though standard house margaritas are priced at $8. They also feature a Patron Happy Hour daily until 7 PM.

However, beware of the crowd noise on weekends; it can get overwhelmingly loud. Seating is cramped, so personal space can be an issue. Food-wise, don't expect to be blown away—it's decent, but you might find it overpriced for what you get. As for the drinks, they're flavorful, but if you prefer a stronger cocktail, you might be disappointed unless you stick to the specials.

Service is inconsistent, with pleasant experiences at tables contrasted by occasional neglect at the bar. The place has a bouncer and does fill up, signaling its popularity despite its shortcomings.

In summary, if you're nearby and the Happy Hour aligns, it's worth a try for the drink deals. However, there are better options in the area if you're after top-notch Mexican cuisine and strong margaritas.

Title: Mixed Experience with Italian Comfort

I recently opted for delivery from a local Italian spot. The food quality was solid, though not exceptional. I sampled two pasta dishes and a marinara pizza. Unfortunately, the pizza suffered during delivery, arriving with a dishearteningly soggy center which rendered it unsuitable for my toddler, as the toppings slid off readily.

The ingredients showed promise, notably the high-quality mozzarella and the freshness of the dough, but the final product didn't hit the mark due to consistency issues. On a brighter note, the gnocchi was delightful with its flavorful sauce making it the highlight of the meal. The Bolognese, paired with fresh pasta, was acceptable but the sauce and meat didn't stand out.

I'm open to giving the pizza another try under better circumstances and would certainly reorder the gnocchi. The meal was pleasantly accompanied by complimentary bread, a tasty bonus. Overall, potential seen in some dishes but there's room for improvement in others.

Got food from here before for delivery and now I went in person. I came here on a Saturday afternoon around 2pm with my boyfriend and enjoyed the simplicity of this small restaurant. We both got lunch specials, him the bento box and myself the 2 rolls for $12. I got the shrimp tempura and spicy tuna. I liked the shrimp tempura, I just thought there were a lot of lettuce in it and the spicy tuna was not really good - was too mushy and didn't really taste too fresh. However, the miso soup and salad that came with the lunch deal was surprisingly so delicious on a fall day!Overall, the food was a great price and the waitress/server/only worker in the restaurant made the experience enjoyable. Not sure if I would come again, but it was nice to try this sushi restaurant in the UES.

I recently ordered takeout from a local spot keen on delivering a flavor adventure. The standout for me was the jerk chicken, which packed a more fiery punch than I've found elsewhere - a delight for those who favor the heat. Alongside it, I sampled an array of sauces: potato leaf, cassava leaf, okra, and peanut. Each was flavorful, though noticeably rich with oil. The spicy rice lived up to its name with a hot kick that added an extra oomph to the meal. Overall, a tasty experience for those with a palate for spice.

If you have the time and patience to wait for happy hour or lunch, do it!! Their happy hour menu (ends at 7pm) has $10 drinks, tacos, and plates to share like quesadillas, nachos and queso. La Contenta has solid drinks that are well mixed - not too sweet like many other places offering mojitos and margaritas. I had the Mayan and the paloma and enjoyed both. But the happy hour food is even better. Get a big bowl of guacamole (they even stick in the chips for you) and it was more than enough to share for the four of us. The fried fish tacos were SO juicy and I was pretty full from the two big pieces. I wish it was a bit bigger - there's a row of 5-6 tables on the right and bar seats. Not a big space and the bathroom is petite too. Waiters are attentive and quick and didn't rush us to finish our drinks. Definitely coming back again next time we're in the LES!

Title: Casual Hangout Spot with Room for Improvement

Located conveniently near the A, C, E, and L trains and within walking distance to several bus stops, this laid-back eatery offers a cozy spot for friends to unwind. The ambiance is relatively calm on weekday evenings, with a manageable level of noise that occasionally spikes but doesn't disrupt conversation.

The menu is pretty standard; the food is adequate but won't leave a lasting impression. The portion sizes are generous, though, and the drink selection covers the basics from beers to a few ciders, with the potential for a simple cocktail upon request.

Service is exceedingly friendly, adding a personal touch to the experience. However, be prepared for a leisurely meal as the kitchen pace can be unhurried, which might not suit those in a hurry or with a big appetite right off the bat.

The venue is tidy and well-maintained, including a pair of clean restrooms. Price-wise, it won't break the bank, making it a reasonable choice for a casual meet-up. 

While it may not become my staple haunt, the overall agreeable atmosphere and kind staff make it a place I'd consider revisiting when time is no object.

Title: A Gem on Governors Island with a View to Dine For

I recently ventured to a restaurant featured on New York Live, eager to finally explore Governors Island, a spot I'd overlooked despite my lifelong New York residency. The journey began with an affordable and pleasant ferry ride from 10th South Street, clocking in at just seven minutes.

Upon disembarking, the restaurant greeted me to the right, and I was promptly seated. It's worth noting that there isn't a bad seat in the house—the panoramic views of Manhattan's skyline, the serene Hudson, and the distant New Jersey shores are simply spectacular. The shimmering sunlight dancing on the water, coupled with the sight of the Statue of Liberty, added a touch of emotional majesty to the setting.

True to the rave reviews, the oysters were a highlight, offering both traditional and an intriguing sweet and sour take—I found both to be delightfully satisfying. The lobster roll was another triumph, packed with flavor and skillfully prepared. Unfortunately, the fish tacos didn't hit the same mark, suffering from over-fried fish that proved tough to chew.

Despite the minor letdown of the tacos, the overall experience was delightful, and I am eager to return before the season concludes. It's a charming waterfront destination that marries culinary prowess with iconic views—a true New York City treasure.

As an *older* person I'm usually in the mood for a not packed-like-sardines-music-is-too-damn-loud kind of experience when I go out and Excuse My French offers exactly that. I came here for an after work meeting with a friend and the first thing that piqued my curiosity was the layout. It's essentially a long rectangular mid-basement bar aka, all of the restaurant is bar seating, so don't come here with a really large group. We ordered the burrata salad, brussel sprouts, and croque monsieur. The croque monsieur bites came with cute little French flags in them and were the highlight of the menu, so cheesy and savory. The service left a little to be desired. As mentioned by other reviewers, upon entering we were greeted with some blank stares, which weren't very welcoming, but overall the wait staff was fast and accommodating.

Solid Italian restaurant in the East Village.  It's authentic (I exchanged a few words in Italian with the host) and has the right blend of formality and comfort.  We were fortunate enough to sit in the enclosed garden area, which was neat.  The margherita pizza was excellent as an appetizer, as was the antipasto (especially the bread that came with it).  Our pastas were delicious (broccoli and sausage rigatoni) and just the right portion size.  The service was above-average. Only minor complaint was that the wine list was short on inexpensive options.  Otherwise, I'd definitely go back.

Title: A New York Gem for Burger Enthusiasts

If you're willing to splurge a bit for quality, this bustling plaza hotspot is a must-try for burger aficionados. The aroma lured my husband and me into choosing this joint, and we were far from disappointed. We indulged in their signature burger—a mouthwatering masterpiece where the perfectly cooked meat and their unique sauce truly set it apart. Be warned, the portion of fries is generous to a fault; even together, we couldn't conquer the mountain of crispy potatoes.

The seating arrangement encourages diners to mingle, which led us to a friendly chat with a couple from our neck of the woods. It's worth noting, New Yorkers might not be the chattiest, but the atmosphere here brings people together. 

Heartily recommended for anyone seeking a standout burger experience in New York.

Tucked conveniently beside the path, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone journeying from Jersey. The ambiance strikes the perfect balance of comfort and elegance, matched by rapid and proficient service that doesn't miss a beat. Among the culinary highlights, the tuna gaga, spicy salmon, and spicy sea scallops rolls stand out with their fresh, bold flavors that are sure to delight any sushi enthusiast. In summary, this place is a delightful find, offering a splendid dining experience for locals and travelers alike.

I recently discovered a gem in the heart of Times Square: Patrick's. Unlike typical tourist spots, Patrick's is a spacious Irish pub that caters well to both sports fans and casual diners with its dual bar areas and plentiful seating. Booking a table for a bustling Friday night was a breeze, and our choice to sit by the window proved perfect for a quieter meal with a view.

The service was standout. Our waitress was attentive, ensuring our experience was top-notch throughout the evening. The oyster selection set the bar high, with the East Coast's saltiness contrasting nicely with the West Coast's sweeter counterparts, and both were notably fresh.

The Tony Chicken parm didn't disappoint—tasty and generously portioned—and the salads, particularly the Lobster Cobb and Shrimp Avocado, were satisfying without compromising on flavor. A side of sweet potato fries was irresistibly good, and I admit to indulging more than intended.

In summary, Patrick's offers great company, attentive service, and delectable dishes—a rare find in Times Square that's worth a repeat visit.

On a recent Thursday evening, I revisited a familiar haunt in Midtown East with a party of six. It had been some time since my days of working nearby, but I couldn't resist ordering a nostalgic favorite, the spicy miso ramen, accompanied by my beloved fireball for that extra kick. The dish didn't disappoint; the broth was as rich as I remembered, and the noodles maintained their perfect chewiness. Service remained commendable – prompt and alert, even when a minor hiccup occurred with my friends' lucky cat ramen orders, lacking nori, which was swiftly rectified. Although my visits to this area are sporadic, this experience affirmed that a return is guaranteed whenever I find myself back in Midtown East.

Mama's Too serves up square slices that ingeniously fuse Detroit and Roman pizza al taglio traditions. Their slices boast an airy crumb, generously slathered with sauce and toppings, without compromising on that miraculous lift. A notable feature is the frico crust—a crunchy, cheesy delight with a crisply cooked bottom, tipping its hat to Detroit style.

Their well-fermented, high-hydration dough results in a crust that's light yet crisp, indicative of Roman influence. The caramelized onion and mushroom slice is particularly noteworthy, striking a harmonious balance between sweet and savory; the mushrooms soften to accentuate the signature crispy cheese edge.

With a rotating menu, every visit promises something new. The value for money is excellent too, at $5 for square slices and $4 for their equally delectable house slice. Don't miss out on these masterfully crafted pizzas that are both innovative and delicious.

I recently visited this spot for a bottomless birthday brunch and was thoroughly impressed with the service. Our waiter was the epitome of attentiveness, ensuring our needs were promptly met and our glasses were never empty. While the drinks were decent—not the tastiest I've had, they were certainly satisfactory for a bottomless affair. The food complemented our celebration perfectly, hitting the right spot in terms of quality and taste. Would recommend for a casual, fun brunch event.

Title: Mixed Impressions at a Lincoln Center Locale

On a particularly dreary Friday afternoon, the need for a comforting meal led my companion and me to a restaurant close to Lincoln Center, despite its less-than-stellar reviews. Our experience was a mixed bag; while the customer service was commendable for its attentiveness and friendliness, allowing us to comfortably linger for conversation in the uncrowded dining area, the food left much to be desired.

The menu, which indeed requires a serious revamp, featured a Creamy Tomato Soup that struck me as quite average, served with an uninspiringly small piece of cheddar toast. The Falafel Burger, though edible, was disappointingly dry and seemed to lack the promised Tzatziki sauce, prompting us to order an additional side of fries to fulfill our hunger.

As for the Country Chicken Pot Pie, it was a letdown with its thin broth, scant vegetables, and overly large, dry chunks of chicken that proved difficult to swallow, although the presentation of the pie was somewhat appealing.

The saving grace of the meal was the Gamay Reine from Loire Valley—a dry red wine with a smooth finish and pleasant texture, priced at $15.

The establishment is ADA accessible, though currently obscured by scaffolding. As we left, I noted the business cards and postcards available, though I doubt I would return for another meal. This spot could be a decent choice for a quiet conversation over wine, but as far as the culinary experience goes, it desperately needs a new chef and a refreshed menu to live up to its prime location.

This was the top of my list for places to get pizza when in New York!Came here after 1pm and even though there was a line out the door, the wait was not terrible. (There were other occasions we passed by and the line was soooo much longer). My boyfriend and I both ordered a square pizza each and we understand why it's so hyped and you guys, it deserves the hype. Each slice looks super oily because the pepperoni slices look like small cups of oil, but the pizza holds a nice crunch and bite to it while having the right amount of cheese.Each slice was about $5. You MUST come for a square while you're here!

My husband and I were thoroughly impressed during our first visit to Atlantic City, where we dined for my birthday dinner. We indulged in the sampler and the mini slider burgers, complemented by a delightful chicken sandwich. Each dish was exquisite, culminating in a complimentary birthday sundae that was simply delicious, complete with a cheerful round of singing from the staff. The service was outstanding, with waiters who were exceptionally attentive and professional. This experience definitely warrants a high recommendation - the food and service are both phenomenal!

One of my favourite by Chloe locations to stop by for lunch. Their salads are really good, reasonably priced ($10.50) and delicious! My favourite is their Kale Caesar Salad with mushroom "bacon". My only complaint is that their mushroom "bacon" is extremely salty and their sweet potato fries (even though they say are air baked, could be less oily. However, these sweet potato fries are delicious- even though they taste deep fried. Another great dish is their Spicy Thai Salad. Would definitely come back.

It's been a little while since I've been here but I've gone a few times when I'm in the area. The ramen is good, not the best I've had but it's tasty and I've always been satisfied. Only one I'm not a fan of is the Mt Fuji ramen. Too much going on there for me but my friend enjoyed it. It's a small place with not much room to put anything if you're carrying bags and whatnot. Gyoza are good. And the Okonomiyaki was pretty yummy too. Service is nice. Interior is pretty cool looking. Prices are good as well. All in all I def like to visit this spot when I'm in the are

Title: A LES Brunch Gem During Restaurant Week

My latest brunch experience in the Lower East Side has landed a new spot on my list of favorites. Venturing out during the last day of NYC Restaurant Week, I was enticed by their prix fixe brunch menu, a first-time treat for me.

We kicked off the meal with Grandma Daisy's angel biscuits and drunken deviled eggs. The eggs were a standout, with the root chips offering a satisfying crunch. The biscuits lived up to their heavenly name—flaky and buttery to perfection.

For the main course, the chicken & waffles were a hit, with the dark meat combination delivering succulent flavors enhanced by the accompanying sauces. The biscuits & gravy continued our biscuit streak and did not disappoint. Accompanying sides of mac & cheese and home fries were standard fare but complemented the meal well.

Value-wise, the quality and quantity were well worth it, and we joyfully had leftovers to take home. The only downside? Space—or the lack thereof. The cozy venue means close quarters dining, so a reservation is a wise choice to avoid the quick-to-form crowds.

Title: New Year's Eve Delight at Cozy Culinary Gem

I'm tempted to give 5 stars purely based on the exquisite food at this charming eatery where I spent my New Year's Eve dinner.
