Despite a slight hiccup with a 10-minute wait even with our 8:15 pm reservation, the waiting area's allure eased the delay, and soon we were seated, albeit unexpectedly, in the adjacent hotel's lobby. The unconventional setting surprisingly contributed to the cozy atmosphere.

The meal kicked off with the BURRATA & KNOTS, which were a revelation, especially the fresh burrata and perfectly garlicky 'garlic bread'. The CHARRED OCTOPUS was an unexpected triumph, blending tender octopus with Korean BBQ sauce, balanced by refreshing smashed cucumbers. The CRISPY CALAMARI, steering away from traditional preparation, was a textural marvel with a softer breading that maintained its crunch, pairing splendidly with rice beans. The SPAGHETTI & CLAMS fell short due to overcooked pasta, a minor disappointment in an otherwise stellar lineup. Redemption came with the BRICK CHICKEN, impressively moist and boosted by the zing of cherry peppers.

Service was less attentive than desired, understandable on a bustling NYE, but not detracting from the overall experience. A post-visit, personalized email from the GM was the cherry on top, reflecting the care put into the establishment. Will I return? Without a doubt, as my taste buds are already calling for an encore.

Title: A Flavorful Experience with a Side of Patience at [Restaurant Name]

I recently dined at [Restaurant Name], and I'm still craving the Sweet Tree roll – it's an absolute must-try for anyone who enjoys the creamy comfort of sweet potatoes with a delicious savory twist. Priced at $9.50, it's worth every penny. My friend opted for the Mighty Mushroom roll, which, despite my usual aversion to mushrooms, surprised me with its depth of flavor and seamless integration into the roll – it's a well-executed dish also at $9.50.

We added the Za'atar Hummus and Rosemary Garlic Planter Bread to our meal for $15. Although aesthetically pleasing (perfect for the 'gram!), it fell short in delivering the shareable, satisfying experience we hoped for. Next time, I'd rather get an extra roll instead.

While the food was delightful, service lagged slightly; we were seated for 10 minutes before getting water, and overall the meal pace was unhurried even with several empty tables. However, the staff was cordial when tending to us.

In summary, if you're in no rush and want to savor some innovative rolls, [Restaurant Name] delivers on taste but may test your time.

I recently re-discovered the joys of mazemen at this diminutive ramen joint.  Mazemen is generally overlooked by most ramen joints and it's difficult to find, compared to the more popular soupy tonkotsu ramen bowl.  But this brothless ramen, when done right, is every bit as satisfying, and even revelatory, especially on hot and sultry evenings. Nakamura, and its casual mazemen specialty outpost situated next to it, definitely does mazemen  right.  I ordered a jidori mazemen, which featured generous cubes of smoky, tender chicken thigh, batons of menma (bamboo shoots), spinach, handful of sprouts, some tare (sauce) and a very softly poached egg. Once mixed vigorously, the sauce resembled the texture of carbonara, and coated the noodle strands perfectly.  And on this hot and sticky evening, this mazemen bowl was the perfect meal for me.The chicken wings are also highly recommended.  Salty, sticky, a little garlicky, they are highly addictive, and a perfect companion for your frosty beer.

Restaurant Week Winter 2019 Review.With RW starting on a holiday/MLK Day, I thought it'd be a great day to dine out - despite the blistering cold temperatures outside, and Danji seemed like a equidistant place from me and a friend I was meeting. Armed with my massive parka, I braved the elements...and my heart sort of sank when I arrived to see that the staff and many patrons were still wearing their coats...inside the restaurant.Yup...heating issues. But we were already there, already 7:30, and already hungry and cold.  The service was fairly attentive, but not super helpful when it came to suggestions or recommendations. We ended up choosing:Apps:spicy 'k.f.c' korean fire chicken wings (d'artagnan organic chicken, peanuts,  cilantro & pickled daikon) - the tang/spice was alright, and I liked the peanut-sprinkling, but the wings are pretty heavy on the breading and a wee bit light on the meat/size. bulgogi beef slider w spicy pickled cucumber & scallion salsa - the flavor was there, but again, wished there was a bit more substances on the beef front to justify the size of the slider bun. But tasty.Mains:kimchi bacon wet fried rice with soft scrambled egg, bossam gravy - my friend got this...and, well, it seemed a bit underwhelming. bits of bacon in rice with some kimchi and some egg on top. Oh, and this was brought out about 4 mins before my dish was due to appear. Not awkward...spicy soft tofu stew w. seafood 'busan bouillabaise' - I was freezing (and a little schvitzy from the wings, so then doubly cold), so I had to go for this. It was served up hot (thank god) and hearty - good amount of tofu with a moderate amount of seafood (primarily shrimp).Dessert:Ice Cream! ...lol, I sh*t you not. The only option. That said, I did sample some of the black sesame, because...when ice cream is in front of me...primal instincts take over.  It was fine...but really not the evening to really enjoy it.Do I think I could have like Danji more if I wasn't freezing most of the time? Perhaps. Some of the food was rather tasty, but there were several misses too and left just feeling cheated.

My friend and I finally got the chance to try out this spot after all the hype died down. We had reservations for 2 P.M. but I arrived 15 minutes late and they still honored our reservation. Turns out that they do walk-ins too. The venue was pretty hipster. There was wood and exposed brick wall everywhere. The large windows gave me the reason to believe that this venue was a former warehouse. My friend and I both had the single cheeseburger with a runny egg and bacon. A single cheeseburger comes with 2 patties and a double comes with 3 FYI. The burgers did take a while to come, but when it did, we were ready to dig-in. The burger was extremely juicy and the sweet bacon really stood out to me. Overall, the burger was pretty well seasoned and prepared. This was one of the best burgers I've had in the city, but not THE best. Still worth trying though!

Title: A Tantalizing Yet Pricey Experience

I ventured into this restaurant with high hopes and left with a palate pleased but pockets notably lighter. The culinary journey began with their shin ramen chicken wings, an inventive dish scoring an 8/10, thanks to the chef's clever use of the entire ramen packet. However, at $15 for a mere trio of wings, the value proposition was questionable - a novelty unlikely to warrant a repeat order.

Next, we sampled the octopus & spam rice, also meriting an 8/10. The high-quality ingredients shone through in every flavorful bite, but once more, the price tag caused a double-take. At $24, the modest serving size hardly seemed justifiable.

The restaurant redeemed itself slightly with their cheeseburger, a masterpiece deserving of a 10/10 and no longer confined to the "happy hour" specials. The flawless melding of the cheese with the meat, cradled by the perfect bun, compelled us to indulge in a second serving. Alas, our decision was tinged with the knowledge that the enticing flavors could not compensate for the small portion sizes and the unlikely prospect of returning soon due to the cost.

In conclusion, while the food tantalizes the taste buds, the prices and portion sizes leave a bittersweet aftertaste.

You know if Guy Fieri says this is the best thing he ever had in a bowl, you just have to try this place out. Yes, the restaurant is tiny. You drink in paper cups. But the service here is FAST. We ordered and minutes later, the lady plopped our bowls down. I ordered the Roast Duck Noodle Soup ($9.50? I think) with Small Wide Noodles. There is a variety of noodle types to choose from, which was neat. And oh my god, let me just say that broth was delish. All of the flavors of the roast duck had submerged into the broth, that I didn't even want to ruin it at first by adding in chili oil and vinegar. The noodles did need a lot of breaking apart since it seemed like they just dumped a frozen batch in, but all good! On a cold winter day, I was craving something soupy and delicious, and this fit the bill and taste! I don't know if it really is the best thing I ever had in a bowl, but I would definitely go back to try their other foods!

Title: Transparency Issues Overshadow Brunch Plans

I was quite disappointed during my recent visit to a West Village eatery, where I had anticipated enjoying a leisurely brunch. Upon my arrival, as I perused the menu at the side entrance, I was surprised to discover a 'Grade Pending' notice concealed behind a large plant, well away from immediate view. This intentional obscuring of their health inspection rating by the management raised serious concerns about their transparency and business ethics. Such deception leaves a negative impression and undermines customer trust. Consequently, I decided to forgo my meal and seek out a more forthcoming establishment in the area. Patrons deserve to make informed dining choices, and this restaurant failed to provide that opportunity.

Title: Decent Dining Experience Before a Show

Last evening, before attending a show nearby, my sisters and I decided to try our luck for dinner at this bustling restaurant. Despite a predicted 30-minute wait, the staff was right on the mark, seating us precisely on time, an appreciated display of honesty regarding wait times.

Opting for the outdoor seating, which I usually find delightful, was somewhat marred on this occasion by a boisterous neighboring table. Their lack of decorum was a slight damper on the ambiance, but such is the gamble with al fresco dining, and I don't fault the restaurant for the patrons' behavior.

Our server, despite being evidently overwhelmed, managed to provide attentive service. Drinks were served promptly, refills offered without prompting, and our dishes arrived with little delay—a testament to the efficiency and friendliness of the staff under pressure.

On to the meal: the chips were notably salty, yet the guacamole was a standout, fresh and flavorful. The burrito was substantial, if not the most extraordinary I've had, it held its own in terms of size and fillings.

While the experience wasn't such that I'd make a special journey back, the restaurant offers a solid dining option if you're already in the vicinity and looking for a reliable meal.

This place embodies greenwich district. It takes traditional food, creates a hip environment, serves nice cocktails, and then makes food twice what it normally should be by focusing on presentation.Having said that, I enjoyed this place. Got the Pork Soup Dumplings (XLB), Peking Duck, black bean clams, and pork lotus wrap. I thought the XLB were some of the best I've had in the city. Really good balance of soup, meat, and skin. Wish I got more than one order of it.The black bean clams were good and I got it because I remembered eating this reallyyyy good one in some other Chinese restaurant and this didn't hit that spot. The pork lotus wrap had some really soft and fatty pork and it was like a decomposed lotus wrap. You could tell they used better ingredients here than normal other Chinatown stores. Expensive, but delicious.Tip about the duck! It's about 100 bucks, feeds 4, and you have to order in advance supposedly (we were able to order without doing so ‍) The Star was the duck. It was Peking Duck and it came with dan dan noodles. The noodles was a nice touch and it helps make sure you will be full. It's nothing special. The duck was really good. Crispy skin, fatty duck, with all the appropriate condiments. Haven't been to enough duck places yet, but so far this is going to set the bar. If money no concern, this is a great choice.

Having savored the delights at several of their venues in Tokyo, Osaka, and Brooklyn, this ramen haven never disappoints. Until 2020, they're generously offering a complimentary kae-dama – that much-appreciated extra portion of noodles for those of us craving just a bit more of their delectable ramen. 

Parents will be overjoyed to hear that kids eat for free, adding tremendous value to an already worthwhile experience. In my opinion, their ramen surpasses that of Ippudo, especially considering the customization options that cater to every palate. 

Strategically located at prime spots both in Japan and NYC, convenience is part of the package. At $24 for a full set, it's an irresistible proposition that guarantees satisfaction without breaking the bank. A must-visit for ramen enthusiasts and casual noodle lovers alike.

It was our second time in the restaurant. We usually do not go to the same place twice but this happened by accident. Place is pretty decent. Food is very good but service is very bad. You wait 10 minutes for a menu and it is Monday 7:30 pm. You wait very long for guacamole, like 30-40 minutes. After we finished our main courses, we waited like 30 minutes with dirty plates on the table. And again it was Monday. Food was pretty good that is why 4 stars. They had specials for dinner, pretty good salmon and blue crab enchilada. Tres leches cake was great as well. So not a single complaint about the food, it was pretty good. The problem is slow and inattentive service.

I ordered the shrimp with udon noodles in coconut curry sauce. It was absolutely delicious. They give you some hot sauce on the side but I didn't even need it since it had some kick! It was a pretty large portion too. It was nice and hot when I was ready to pick up. Will definitely come back to this convenient spot!

Char Sue certainly defies initial expectations, blossoming from a pork-centric eatery to a diverse culinary destination. Undoubtedly, one must indulge in the miso cod bowl—a dish that lingers in memory with its smoky, tender cod and profound umami from the miso sauce, harmonized with delicate sushi rice and a vibrant slaw.

The menu variety doesn't end there; the wild salmon sashimi and the unexpectedly scrumptious miso eggplant appetizers are noteworthy choices. While my companion's chili daikon soy fried chicken and chicken paitan ramen were enjoyable, a touch more salt might have perfected the latter.

To wash it all down, the beer selection is commendable and the happy hour simply sweetens the deal. Char Sue stands out as a solid, well-rounded dining experience.

Pretty mediocre Chinese food, at best, especially for being in NYC. Food was pretty bland but not too greasy (sesame chicken).The scallion pancake was a bit well done and way too oily.Egg drop soup was par for the course.Just ok and nothing special, i would only go back if craving Chinese take out since it is a nearby option for pickup. Food was prepared fast rhou

Update 7/25/2019 - we stopped in here with my friends on a Friday evening due to the cute outdoor patio. It was nice to sit outside. My friends were hungry and ordered some bar bites. I'm still bitter you can't get some of the breakfast/brunch items at dinner time - they look so good! A few of my friends ordered the "Capri sun" looking drinks and would not stop raving about them! They compared them to Christmas punch. On a positive note, it did not smell this time we went, and the "patio" was nice. I got the cookie with ice cream. It was dry and generally not good. Just barely warm. Not recommended. I had a similar feeling as last time. Was nice to stop in with a group - but the food is just meh. If you are looking for fun and cool drinks - per my friends, the ones in the bags are recommended!---------------------------------------This place has amazing coasters! And fried candy bars! But on the day we went, it smelled like poop. Literally.When we first arrived it smelled a little like sewer, so we asked to be seated upstairs. Unfortunately it still smelled bad up there. Was a bit overwhelming. We got nachos. They were okay. The Brussels were not crispy enough.Fried candy bar was good. We all shared it. It was smaller than we thought it would be though.I likely wouldn't come back. The smell was off putting. I hope they resolve the sewer situation. I do love the coasters though

Tasty is an understatement because these noodles are heavenly and divine. The texture and pull, the chewiness, the flavor, these noodles really have it all and it blows my mind. I came here with some friends and I ordered the duck stir-fried noodles and was not disappointed. We decided to throw in some dumplings and they were pretty good nothing too crazy but of course, the star of the show was the stir-fried noodles. I already went on about the texture but the flavor was great and I recommend the duck because the noodle really takes in the duck fat making it even tastier! The duck itself was pretty standard but that is not a bad thing at all considering the noodles were the main point of this dish. We went around 12 PM on the weekend and fortunately, there was no wait. They also have a yelp waitlist so make sure to use that! The place is a bit tight and a bit gritty but that is probably a sign that it is good. It is cash only so make sure to be ready! I highly recommend this place and will for sure be coming back soon.

Title: A Refreshing Departure from the Usual Indulgences - Vegetarian Sushi Delight

After a week of rich indulgences in San Francisco's classic offerings of burgers, pizza, cookies, and Mexican fare while celebrating with family, I approached the vegetarian sushi at this eatery with a mix of guilt and gastronomic fatigue. It proved to be a place one might consider a sanctuary for the repentant weekend sinner.

As I settled into the meal, the moral compass within me celebrated a day free from meat, cheese, and baked goods. The seasonal dumplings and Swiss chard sushi greeted me with a distinctly grassy, earthy flavor, which, while commendable for its "earthier-than-thou" essence, wasn't quite to my personal taste.

However, the meal took a delightful turn with the Sweet Tree roll, featuring sweet potato and an ambrosial orange sauce, alongside the Mighty Mushroom in its savory tan sauce. Both creations were an absolute revelation, marrying the concept of clean eating with explosive flavors.

Although the Spicy Mang roll proved to be a firecracker beyond my spice tolerance, it was the only minor misstep in an otherwise standout meal. I would gladly return for another round of the Sweet Tree and Mighty Mushroom rolls.

In summary, the culinary craft of the sauces here deserves a resounding five stars, with the Sweet Tree and Mighty Mushroom rolls earning a solid four stars. The other offerings, while good, settle at a respectable three stars. For anyone looking to ease their dietary conscience or simply to enjoy a lighter, flavor-packed meal, this vegetarian sushi place is a must-visit.

Title: Fresh and Satisfying Poke at a Fair Price

I'm a regular at this spot for their 'pick your own poke' bowls. My go-to is a hearty serving of kale noodles topped with fresh salmon and shrimp, all perfectly complemented by the house Oki classic sauce. The poke here never disappoints in freshness and flavor. You definitely get your money's worth with the generous portions offered. While I'm not overly impressed with their Ramen, the poke bowls are a different story. They’ve won me over, and I’ll definitely return for a poke fix whenever the craving strikes.

Came here for restaurant week for lunch-$26 for an appetizer and entree; you can add  $3 for the desert which I highly recommend-absolutely adorable restaurant. Had a reservation for 4 and was seated almost immediately on arrival. I ordered the no ssam bun- the pork belly buns were delicious. One of my friends ordered the jap chae which was very filling according to her and tasted healthy- she got the vegetarian portion. The Mandu dumplings were also delicious- probably the best tasting out of all three of the appetizers. As for the entree's three of us got the korean BBQ which was beautifully prepared. The pork belly seemed to have more pieces than the shrimp FYI, so I would keep that in mind when ordering. Also with the KBBQ- the pork belly has to be cooked by yourself where as the rest of the proteins can be cooked in the kitchen. If you are a desert fan- would get the banana sabayon! Great custard with sesame seed dipping cookies. Overall great meal and loved that I came here during restaurant week so I could try the food do or a great price.

**Hortus: A Gem of Asian Fusion**

Hortus swiftly secured a spot on my list of top new restaurants, mastering the art of Asian fusion with finesse. Behind it are chefs with glittering Michelin-starred backgrounds, bringing to life a harmonious blend of Chinese, Korean, and Thai flavors that steer clear of confusion and kitsch.

The dual nature of Hortus is captivating – a laid-back lunch scene encircles the bar and open kitchen, where customizable lunch sets brim with delights like crispy tempura and tangy pickles. The star? The grilled mackerel, outstandingly tender. Noteworthy is the pricing, which stands out as thoughtful amidst a sea of overpriced Korean/Asian lunch offerings.

Evenings at Hortus take a turn towards the refined with the availability of a tasting menu for two as well as a la carte selections. The prix fixe menu, which my fiancé and I enjoyed, strikes a perfect balance in portion and palate. Standout starters such as the king crab, crispy uni, and beef tartare pave the way for a succulent steamed black seabass, elevated by the traditional Chinese black bean sauce.

Ending on a sweet note, the Thai milk tea crème brûlée and mango sticky rice desserts crown the meal without tipping into excess sweetness.

Hortus earns my hearty recommendation for both a laid-back yet intriguing lunch or a casual yet special dinner date.

Recently under new management, the revamped diner presents a bright, clean, and cozy ambiance that's immediately welcoming. While I didn’t sample the tempting baked goods on display, the Banana Smoothie I opted for did not disappoint; thick, full of flavor, and served in a no-frills plastic cup, it hit the spot.

Brunch offerings were extensive, leading me to choose the Pancakes Decker. Despite the presentation and missing honey differing from the menu's depiction, the fluffy pancakes, coupled with fresh berries, were delightful. My husband’s Monte Cristo, though slightly smaller than anticipated, was satisfying with well-seasoned meat and a robust flavor profile.

While the menu photos might not be a reliable guide, the overall experience was positive, leaving me curious to explore more of what the diner has to offer.

Title: A Meat Lover's Vegan Thai Delight

I recently visited a vegan Thai restaurant that genuinely impressed me, a self-proclaimed carnivore. My vegetarian companions and I decided on the $30 4-course menu special, eager to explore a variety of dishes. We shared a Drunken Noodle and a Vegan Sausage platter. To my surprise, the tofu-centric offerings outshone the soy protein alternatives. Standout dishes included a vibrant papaya salad, the flavorful Drunken Noodle, and a heavenly mango sticky rice for dessert. This establishment proves that dietary restrictions need not compromise authentic Thai taste. The staff's welcoming attitude and the restaurant's cozy atmosphere completed our delightful dining experience. Highly recommend for anyone looking to satisfy their Thai cravings, regardless of dietary preferences!

This restaurant is bumpin. It's loud, super busy, and there seems to be a lot of action. We went on a Friday night, and it was a little more than an hour wait for two. No prob, we grabbed a drink and returned an hour later. Seating is a little cramped, but it's New York..The cocktail menu is reasonably priced, and we deccided to start with a frozen beer. It's a super cute drink, and if you like hops you'll love the topping. The menu is awesome because it has pictures of all the dishes. It made it more fun to pick out what We wanted (and also took me twice as long). We ordered the fish cake soup, the doggie, the mew chicken, the kushi yaki, and cream udon. If I were to come back, I'd definitely order the doggie new chicken but I might skip the cream udon. And I missed out on ordering the Mew salmon roll!This was a fun dining experience, and I'd definitely recommend checking it out - maybe on a weekday when it's not as packed.

Title: "Fast-Paced Sushi Experience with Quality Bites"

I recently visited a bustling sushi spot that redefined my concept of fast food sushi. Despite the "cheap" pricing, the quality didn't disappoint. Our late-evening sushi craving led us to this establishment, where the queue stretched out the door, hinting at its popularity.

Even at 7pm on a Saturday, our wait time was a reasonable 20 minutes for a party of three. The restaurant's setup was intriguing; each sushi chef diligently manned a station serving about 10 patrons, with orders and their respective timers displayed on screens. The pressure on the chefs was palpable, almost uncomfortably so.

Our selections included salmon, scallop, crab, and toro rolls. While there were no extraordinary standouts, each roll was quite satisfying. We polished off our meal within the same time frame as our wait, a testament to the swift service. A friend humorously remarked that the warm rice and seaweed alone could have sufficed, but thankfully, our experience was much more flavorful than that.

Title: A Rocky Start for a New Eatery

I ventured into this new restaurant on their opening day, and while I'm a fan of the concept, the execution left much to be desired. My vegetarian friend found the meat-free selections such as the veggie wonton soup painfully bland – likening it to "drinking water with boring dumplings."

As for my experience, the meat dishes were underwhelming. The Lion Balls were doused in a peculiar sauce that overpowered the taste, to the point where I couldn’t finish a single one. Other dishes like the shu mai and Shanghai soup pork buns were visually appealing but fell short on size and flavor, respectively. Even the marinated cucumbers seemed more like simple pickles than a crafted dish.

On a positive note, the service was friendly, despite a slight hiccup with the check. While I appreciate the hustle of a new establishment, I left disappointed. Here's to hoping future visits show improvement.

Oh wow didn't expect this Kebab chitpole style spot on 23rd Street is this gooooood!Protein - steak kebab. Not the tenderest meat but great in texture and flavor!Roasted Carrot - soooo flavorful and natural carrot sweetness came out perfect.Broccoli - healthy option expected flavor like normal broccoliKale Salad - refreshing very goodHummus Dip - so good there's little sweetness in it perfect with seasoned rice.Spicy Hummus Dip - I like the hummus better but still good.Yogurt Spinach - usually I'm not a fan of yogurt dip but somehow I finished it.Seasoned Rice - also little sweetness from the shredded carrots  it was so delicious.It was a huge portion and I just couldn't stop eating it!Lunch line at this place was insane almost at the door, Ritual app ordering prior would be a smarter choice..

I recently visited the restaurant and opted for the Mealpal: The Classic Salmon Hawaiian bowl. While the dish was aesthetically pleasing, my experience took a turn for the worse as I fell ill after consuming it. Despite its appealing presentation, this unfortunate incident has dissuaded me from planning a return visit.

Egg Shop in Nolita delivers a photogenic brunch experience that exceeds expectations. Initially, I wasn't sold on its cutesy menu and trendy aesthetic. But upon visiting on a November morning, my skepticism was quickly turned around. Upon arrival at 9:30, my boyfriend and I were seated immediately without facing the notorious waits.

Coffee service was slow, but my cappuccino was worth the wait. While perusing their extensive brunch cocktail menu, I pondered the dedication of regular Saturday brunchers. I opted for the Spandex quinoa bowl ($13.50), a name that belies the delightful blend of flavors and textures, with the tamari dressing bringing it all together splendidly.

My boyfriend's choice, the Hot Chix ($14), a spicy fried chicken and egg sandwich, was a revelation. The heat was well balanced, and the addition of pickled vegetables and cilantro added a Vietnamese twist that was thoroughly enjoyable.

Despite my initial doubts about New York's brunch scene, Egg Shop has made it clear why it's a crowd favorite.

Such a adorable place for brunch! Especially in the nice weather they have some outdoor seating as well. The food is yummy and so are the drinks! There's always a long wait so either get there early or just put your name down and walk around soho for a bit. Worth the wait. @traveleen_gurl

Title: A Sweet Haven for Late Night Cravings

My recent visit to this particular branch of the chain left me impressed, distinguishing itself as one of the better locations I've experienced. In search of a late-night confectionary remedy, the staff's friendliness added a comforting touch to the overall ambiance.

I indulged in both the adagio and a chocolate eclair. Each was a testament to richness, with sweetness tipping the scales, which led me to retreat with leftovers in tow—just a few bites sufficed. The adagio, a fusion of chocolate and passion fruit, was an especially tantalizing treat that I'd urge chocolate enthusiasts to try.

In summary, for those with a penchant for the sweeter things in life, this spot is a must-visit. Just be ready to pamper your sweet tooth in moderation.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a spot serving up some delicious Korean fusion fare – think creatively crafted tacos, tantalizing bibimbap, and irresistible rice balls. The chicken wings, in particular, were simply some of the best I've ever enjoyed. Be warned, though: this place has a unique policy where you need to place your entire order all at once. We learned the hard way that adding to your initial order can cost you – we're talking an unexpected $17 upcharge.

For a seamless experience, be sure to give your full order to the waiter right from the get-go. They're pretty strict about not accepting app-first, meal-later requests. Another quirk to note is the lively karaoke bar situated just above the restaurant – expect a rhythmic, stomp-filled soundtrack accompanying your meal.

Despite these particularities, the food quality makes it worth the minor inconveniences. Plus, they offer enticing shot deals with four for $20, making it a prime spot for large groups seeking a festive evening. When the weekend rolls around, the place truly transforms into a vibrant party scene. In summary, with food this good, a little bit of stomping overhead and ordering protocol are easily forgiven.

Title: A Delightful Dinner Experience

Last evening's dinner at this restaurant was a standout culinary adventure. We initiated our meal with the tuna tartare, which triumphed in both freshness and flavor, particularly with its accompanying sauce. The risotto croquettes, boasting a rich tomato sauce and oozing cheese core, were delicious, though a touch warmer would have made them perfect.

The star of my meal was the margherita pizza adorned with prosciutto. It was, without exaggeration, one of the most impressive brick oven pizzas I've savored. Meanwhile, my husband's whole branzino was met with equal enthusiasm.

In conclusion, this restaurant certainly earns my recommendation for a dinner visit. Whether you're in the mood for pizza or fish, you're in for a treat.

If you're passing through the area or heading out of Penn Station and in need of a quick bite, this spot might just fit the bill. I tried the Parma pizza piled with mozzarella, prosciutto, arugula, cherry tomatoes, and a sprinkle of parmigiana. While the toppings were delicious, the crust was thick and hard, which may not suit those who favor a thinner base. Nevertheless, for a rapid meal, it's a decent enough choice.

Del Posto is insane. Doesn't really require a lengthy review of any sort. Just a few takeaways: It's literally like a 10-star hotel in there so that pretty much sets the mood for the whole evening. Definitely make sure your pockets aren't empty. The staff is amazing and so many actual Italians which is epic. Damiano was our waiter who was awesome. Tania who was a hostess was also dope, and Joe the sommelier too. We did the 8 course. The Vitello tonato was outrageous.  The pasta w broccoli rabe was great. The tuna was great. The gluten free BREAD - wow.  Actual wow...and the butter too :(. The espresso martini is amazing. The glassware and silverware is priceless. Amazing experience that calls for very, very special occasions. Prego

Tucked away in an unassuming location, this quaint sushi establishment surpassed expectations with its delightful offerings. The Valentine's themed cocktail, a blend of lychee and strawberry, was a delectable start, perfectly complemented by their house wine.

Among the shared plates, the sushi sashimi, whimsically shaped like a heart, stood out both visually and taste-wise, enhanced by a drizzle of savory sauces. The fried squid legs were a revelation, reminiscent of rich, succulent chicken, while the chicken karaage paired with spicy mayo was another crowd-pleaser.

A sampling of kobe beef, which melted like butter upon tasting, alongside the toothsome udon noodles with beef, rounded out a gastronomic adventure that highlighted the freshness of the ingredients and the skill in preparation. 

With a vast menu offering an array of choices at reasonable prices, this gem warrants a return visit. While unsure about happy hour specifics, the mention of lunch specials is promising. In essence, a commendable spot for both sushi aficionados and those looking for Japanese culinary delights.

I popped into this spot for a quick Happy Hour and was thoroughly impressed. The bartender was exceptionally friendly, offering insightful walkthroughs of their new summer beer offerings and the Happy Hour food menu. I couldn't resist the Truffle Rice Balls, a steal at just $5. They were a delightful marriage of crispy exteriors and a wonderfully cheesy, gooey interior—worth a return visit on their own merit.

Making use of the HOOCH app, I snagged a complimentary cocktail that was not only delicious but visually appealing too—perfect for the 'gram. The venue also boasts inviting outdoor seating, which is a draw with the lovely weather. I'm already looking forward to my next visit to enjoy the ambiance al fresco.

Title: An Evening at a Culinary Gem

Stepping into the restaurant for dinner with friends, I was initially cautious, wary of the higher-end prices that I'm not accustomed to. However, any hesitation swiftly evaporated as I immersed myself in the experience. The offerings at this establishment are nothing short of a gastronomic delight, with an originality that is as refreshing as it is rare.

The quality of service and the ambiance are impeccable, matching the exclusivity one would expect from such a sophisticated venue. Faced with a broad menu, the decision of what to pick was a delightful challenge, coupled with a drinks list just as varied.

Each dish we selected had its own story:

- Unagi Kabayaki: A delectable eel laid over rice, accompanied by sauce on the side, allowing for a personalized flavor intensity.
  
- Kaisen Kamameshi: A surprise treasure that demands a 30-minute wait, delivering a symphony of flavors that mingle perfectly with the rice.

- New Zealand Lambchop Ishiyaki: This interactive dish grants the pleasure of grilling tender lamb chops on a stone grill, each dip into the trio of sauces enhancing the meat's natural savor.

- Salmon Saikyo Yaki: A testament to freshness and subtlety, the salmon's delicate preparation paid tribute to its inherent taste.

In essence, all the dishes left an indelible mark on my palate, convincing me that this is a destination well worth revisiting for any special occasion. The restaurant, with its unique flair and impeccable attention to detail, truly justifies its price point.

Title: A Slice of Heaven for Cash Carriers

If you find yourself with a wad of bills and a hankering for pizza, this is your spot. Remember, it's cash only before you try to swipe your card. Make a beeline for the artichoke pizza – trust me on this one. The toppings are masterfully curated, the sauce is decadently creamy, and the crust strikes that elusive balance between satisfyingly crunchy and robustly thick. Be warned, the slices are like edible boomerangs, massive in size but you'll keep wanting them to come back for more.

Devouring a slice on a frigid day as a pre-game to a pub crawl felt almost spiritual, and I'd bet it's the ultimate comfort after the crawl concludes. Service is exactly what you'd expect from a NYC pizza joint: no frills, just good old-fashioned pizza slinging. Bottom line, when you're here, the artichoke slice isn't just recommended, it's essential.

I love hotpot with a passion and this is why I try to drag anyone and everyone I can to go with me. Me and my friend went with the hotpot and bbq which comes to $33.Certain tips:1. It's only one hotpot per table. So if you have dietary restrictions be careful what broth you choose. The staff was really helpful in walking me through which has pork in it.2. It is endless amounts of food. No need to rush. 3. Go for the bbq. There are so many cuts of meat. It's plentiful and really pairs well with the hotpot. 4. Icecream at the end you get when you leave the restaurant. My friend really loved the icecream, saying that it was special. I didn't notice. But icecream after hot spicy food is a delight.5. They are very particular about the 2 hour period. They will nudge you to leave as soon as the time is up. Make reservations. It gets really busy.For me I loved that the staff was very helpful and friendly about helping me pick out things without pork. The lady that was grilling the meats decided to do the pork last, so there wouldn't be any cross contamination. That is stellar customer service. Also for your birthday you get a free meal. I can't wait to be back.

I would give this place 3.5 stars.  I've walked by here many times and finally decided to try this place for lunch.  Since I had just started using the Ritual app for takeout, I decided to order on the app for pickup.  It was pretty fast and easy to pick up.  There's a sign for Ritual so you don't wait on the line, just grab the order.  I ordered the chicken tikka masala with rice.  You can also get it with naan instead of rice.  I also asked for medium spicy.  When I opened it up at work, the portion size was decent.  The chicken tikka masala was not spicy at all, in fact, it was a little bit bland.  However, there were very large pieces of chicken which was surprising.  The prices were pretty inexpensive.  If I do come back, I'll probably try their lamb vindaloo or something spicier.

Excellent authentic Chinese food spot, there's the American classics too like general tsos chicken but why would you ever get that when you've got Szechuan classics like Szechuan fish with tofu, or MalaTang? Flavors were fantastic and portions are generous. Come with a group and enjoy a excellent Chinese meal!

Julio was our server he was so lively and so attentive he made all the suggestions and we have no regrets. The food here very delicious. We definitely will be back. The don julio tequila is very yummy I would recommend it was not sour it was perfect in Taste. For entrees we got  al pastor tacos and carnitas as well as the fish tacos it came with a side of rice and beans everything was good. For appetizers the guacamole was very yummy they have plenty of flavors to choose from we got the mild one the jalapeño touch was very yummy. They were jamming on this Friday evening with live singers a violinist as a dj. We had such a blast but we also had a great dinner thanks to Julio who kept checking in on us very funny server we will be back.

Title: A Gem for a Light Dinner

I recently enjoyed a light dinner at this delightful spot, which is conveniently nestled between 5th and 6th avenues. The Kellari chips were a standout—perfectly crispy without being greasy—and the tzatziki sauce served alongside them was absolutely delicious. The location adds to the charm, and I appreciated the quirky touch of being offered an apple while exiting. I'm already planning a reunion with friends here, testament to the great first impression it made. Highly recommended for a casual yet satisfying dining experience.

Title: A Delightful Lunch with a Few Hiccups

I recently visited this eatery with colleagues for a special lunch outing and was charmed by the culinary experience. The standout for me was the tagine, which was bursting with flavor and cooked to perfection. Our party of six arrived at 2 pm and faced a bit of a challenge securing seating - a testament to the restaurant's popularity, though slightly inconvenient for us.

One note of disappointment was the absence of a liquor license at the time of our visit. We had looked forward to pairing our meal with a glass of wine, so this was a letdown, especially since it had been part of our motivation for choosing this venue.

Regarding value, the prices seem steep, particularly for those like us working in the non-profit sector. It may not become a regular spot for budget-conscious diners. However, for a special occasion or an indulgent lunch with the option of day drinking, I'd certainly consider revisiting.

Title: Quirky Spot with a Chilled Vibe and a Confusing Theme

From the moment you step into this vibrant red, donkey-themed establishment, the fun atmosphere is palpable. The bartenders here aren't just mixing drinks; they're crafting an experience, with the white glassware adding an extra touch of cool sophistication. And speaking of cool, this place boasts what might just be the best air conditioning in New York City—a welcome respite from the sweltering urban jungle.

As a Los Angeleno, the motif had me doing a double-take. It's an interesting choice, to say the least, with its bold and somewhat brash Mexican-inspired decor that might raise a few eyebrows. It's as if you've stepped into an eclectic, cleaner, more upscale version of a Tijuana establishment, without crossing the border.

Despite the décor possibly toeing the line, the environment is perfectly suited for business professionals looking to unwind. The bartenders are exceedingly accommodating, ensuring that your moment of relaxation is as refreshing as the cocktail in your hand. So if you're in NYC and looking to escape the "normos" for a bit of off-the-wall charm, this could be your haunt—just bring an open mind and a taste for the unusual.

I recently dined at this charming spot for the first time and overall had a very good experience, although it couldn't quite surpass the high bar set by Emily. We started with the mixed olives and they were quite enjoyable. The highlight of our meal was the Le Big Matt burger and the colony pizza, both of which were excellent, even though I still hold a soft spot for the original renditions at Emily. The okonomi fries were a delightful surprise and I found myself quite taken with them. 

The vodka pizza was decent but didn't stand out amid the stiff competition from other notable spots like Mama's Too. While the chicken parm sandwich was undoubtedly good, it didn’t break into my top favorites within the city. To round off the meal, the chocolate mousse cake was a satisfying end to a fairly delightful dining experience. I'd be inclined to return to see if subsequent visits might elevate this establishment closer to my admiration for Emily.

Recently came here for an early dinner and so very glad I did!  Started off with the Montenegro Mule and the Basito, both excellent!  For our appetizer we had the whipped ricotta which was light with great flavors and they give you plenty of bread to dig  in with.  The main course was my least favorite course because there were no vegetarian main options and the pastas were super fresh and delicious but it was mostly all pasta.  As a vegetarian I usually feel comfortable going to an Italian restaurant  without checking the menu ahead because there's always pasta but most of the time the pastas are served with a healthy portion of veggies and here it was a lot of pasta... while not my favorite, great for pasta lovers.  We had the campanelle and truffle tagliettele because I could never have enough mushrooms!  Both were very tasty and very shareable portions if you are also having a main entree.  We wrapped up the meal with the nutella tart which was really good and the vanilla yogurt on the side tasted almost like a creme fraiche that perfectly complimented the tart.  The staff was very nice and attentive,  the space is super cute, and they offer both indoor and outdoor seating.  It's right around the corner from work so I could definitely see myself making my way back!

Having committed to a beef-less month, I caved for a visit to the much-talked-about Pepper Lunch, intrigued by its status as a popular Asian chain now gracing NYC. The restaurant’s hot plate concept is inventive, allowing patrons a hand in cooking their meals, akin to interactive dining experiences found in Korean and Cantonese establishments.

I sampled the Sambar Pepper Rice, slightly spicy and agreeably flavorful, though I can't pinpoint if the Sambar sauce is a unique creation or an adaptation of Indian stew. The extra table sauces, while numerous and tempting, proved unnecessary; the dish was sufficiently seasoned.

My partner opted for the Jumbo Classic Beef Pepper Rice, which boasted a generous portion of fresh ingredients. Despite the fun of mixing and 'cooking' the meal, the overall experience didn't live up to the hype. Moreover, considering the upcharges for additional toppings and the restaurant's location, the pricing felt steep, especially when pondering the cost overseas.

While the food was good, it didn't justify breaking my no-beef commitment, nor does it entice me for a return visit. If I do reconsider, it will be to explore the non-beef options.

Title: A Seasonal Delight That Never Fades

I have been a loyal patron of this gem for over four years, and it's a place that consistently exceeds expectations, regardless of the season. The restaurant's charm is partly due to its seasonal decoration shifts, which complement the ever-evolving menu beautifully.

Though every dish is a testament to the chef's prowess, the winter selections, particularly the short ribs, stand out for their hearty and savory flavors. During summer restaurant week, the experience was just as sublime. The welcoming duo of watermelon and cornbread set a playful prelude to the symphony of tastes that followed.

The truffle corn gnocchi was nothing short of divine, and the tuna tartare held its own with finesse. The main courses—grilled chicken and king salmon—were satisfying, with the salmon taking the lead in terms of flavor. A side of Parmesan truffle fries, though tipping us into indulgence, was irresistible.

Dessert was a sweet encore with the strawberry covered chocolate and crème brûlée, with the former capturing my favor.

In summary, this restaurant remains a favorite, and I am eager to return in the fall for another round of their culinary excellence.

After hearing much fanfare about the bustling hotspot, I approached with enthusiasm, eager to be swathed in the charm rumored to be reminiscent of the 1920s. Sadly, the decor, which perhaps once shimmered with vintage allure, now only whispered of its dated elegance in the year 2020.

The staff, while undeniably cordial, seemed to dance around the edges of meticulous service, inadvertently swapping precision for pleasantness. A language barrier with our waiter may have tangled our order—a forgivable, yet inconvenient oversight.

My anticipation waned further as a prematurely cleared glass—housing what remained of a modest $6.95 orange juice—vanished from our table, a silent testament to their overeagerness.

Cuisine-wise, the kitchen dispensed dishes that were palatable, if not particularly memorable. They teetered on the brink of gastronomic finesse, yet never quite made the leap, leaving my taste buds in culinary limbo.

Pricing, however, proved to be the restaurant’s saving grace; a gentle reminder that sometimes, affordability can soften the blow of a lackluster dining escapade.

In essence, amidst the trumpeted glitz and glam, I found myself nestled in the realm of the "very okay"—a destination that, despite its promise, delivered a performance that didn't quite match the marquee.

Title: Team Lunch with a View at the Pier

Our team lunch at this establishment proved to be a pleasant outing. Though the weather slightly marred the opportunity to enjoy their outdoor seating, the stunning pier view almost made up for it. 

The appetizer spread, featuring the classic calamari and wings, was satisfying but unremarkable, earning a solid 7 out of 10. The standout of the meal was my juicy, double cheese-laden burger, deserving a robust 8 out of 10 for its flavor and cook.

Regrettably, the accompaniment of garlic fries fell short of expectations, lacking in both garlic punch and crispness, tending towards the soggy side rather quickly.

All in all, the dining experience came through with a commendable 7.5 out of 10. A few tweaks could elevate it from good to great.

A feast for all the senses. Yes the wait is insane, but by starting the Yelp waitlist, it helps cut down the time. Also, if you can kill time with a drink or snack elsewhere in Ktown it's not so bad. There's also a limited number of beers to purchase while you wait upstairs! Once you finally get seated, everything else follows a perfect, magical flow. We split a Beef Platter between 2 people - it was certainly a lot of food, especially with all the delicious banchan, but in the end we did finish everything!I was surprised at the quickness and attentiveness of service - the meat is cooked and cut quickly and perfectly. The banchan is refilled, which was great because we plowed through the first dishes of macaroni and kimchi quickly.Each beef cut was incredible and it's hard to choose a favorite, but the Prime Ribeye and Beef Brisket were standouts for us.A perfect kbbq experience.

Loring Place never ceases to impress me with its on-season palate and impeccable service. I love coming here and sitting at the spacious, airy bar with a friend. I never order salads unless it's something really special - it says something that I order one at Loring Place every time! The grilled strawberry salad with cherry tomatoes was a refreshing start to our meal - bursting with flavor. I also love the pastas here - and the ricotta with sourdough bread (a very filling appetizer). Pastas are cooked al dente to perfection, with a nice balance of cheese and fresh ingredients. A wonderful place to catch up over a relaxed dinner with a friend or for a special occasion. The menu is constantly changing with the seasons, which keeps things interesting and fresh.

I think about these tacos about once every 12 days and definitely dreamt about them on my flight over to JFK. At this point, the tacos here are my gold standard!The carne asada taco has always been my favorite, but the adobada is a close second. I just love how flavorful and tender the meat is! So simple yet so good. I went in at about 3 pm on a Thursday, and there was a bit of a line but not as bad as the lunch/dinner rush. I was in and out in maybe 15 minutes tops. (The standing dining area makes for really quick turnovers.)I will say that if you're going as a group of 4 or more, it might be easier to order separately so you each get a ticket and can give specific instructions to the cook. I've been in with family before and it was kind of difficult to spew off different instructions (no cilantro, flour/corn tortilla, etc) for individual people.

Visited this cool place on several occasions. My first sight walking in was the makeshift Dylan candy store. Love sweets so I looked away quickly to not be sucked into temptation. As I walk passed the check-in area, you encounter the lounge area & library. Passed the library is the entrance to the restaurant Harold's. Since the hotel had igloo/tents set-up in the outdoor lounge, I decided to reserve one for dinner  and was accompanied by a friend. The tents had their own special menu apart from the restaurants main menu options. The selection was great and made it hard to choose a few small plates & one entree to share. The food was delicious and the holiday specialty drinks were very uniquely blended.  The tents were very cozy, had several heaters to keep you warm, games to play with, and it was totally visible from outside the tent. Look forward to next years outside lounge set-up especially if there's a tent/igloo involved with delicious tasty food.

Even though this is a pretty touristy place, I would say it's worth the experience! I mean a chocolate cafe.... you can't really go wrong! Granted, the prices are a bit high, but they don't skimp on the sizes. We ordered the s'mores sundae and the cookie skillet. Both were amazing and hit the spot! I want to go back to try the dessert pizza, although I think it would get old after a slice or so. Cool place overall!

Title: A Noodle Experience Worth the Mess

I recently indulged in a bowl of udon at a local spot, and let's be clear, it wasn't my most graceful moment. The noodles demanded my full, unapologetic attention, with their irresistible bounce and perfect texture. The broth, a harmonious bath of flavors, was utterly addictive — a true testament to the kitchen's mastery.

The Gyunan, a wagyu beef udon dish, was my choice for the evening. While the noodles and broth reached gastronomic heights, the wagyu itself was a disappointment, lacking the tenderness you'd expect and proving a challenge to chew.

Seated promptly at the bar, the service was seamless, and the surroundings were a visual treat, adding to the overall dining experience. Despite the beef mishap, the meal was a success, and I am eager to return for another round of their delectable offerings.

There have been a few times that my sister-in-law told me about this restaurant but we just didn't have time to check all the steakhouses in the city. Recently after going to see the Christmas tree and Rockefeller, we decided to come here for lunch. They opened on Christmas day. It wasn't crowded at the time. We had a nice table, a booth with comfy seats. We started off with Andy's mixed green salad then I had a filet mignon and Hubby had a rib-eye steak. We didn't care much for the salad. The salad was mediocre, nothing special. However, I liked my filet-mignon. It had crispy in the outside and tender in the inside. The seasoning (if there's any) was done perfectly. In the past, I usually had a medium-rare steak but I changed to medium. This filet mignon rock! Get this if you visit the place. Hubby's rib-eye steak was ok. We had our steaks with asparagus. They prepared the asparagus really well with a lot of roasted garlic. I liked this! Service was ok, the one who greeted us at the front was friendly but the service team was just there to work, nothing more. Not a bad thing.

Ordered lunch from here because wanted to eat some healthy food.Got the two proteins bowl (one chicken leg and one salmon). The taste is okay and the portion size is also good. The added charred avo is the most interesting part as the restaurant put some kind of sauce in the middle and it made it taste really refreshing.It's not bad of a place for lunch orders.

My fiancé and I came here on a rainy and chilly afternoon, so we were relieved to come inside the warm restaurant of Silky Kitchen. This restaurant could probably comfortably seat 15 people here, so it's kind of small here. There is also free wifi which the employees freely promote, and as a millennial, I am all for it. I ended up ordering the pork belly cold noodles. The food came out pretty quick, probably within 10-15 minutes despite there being 5+ people ahead of us. The noodles weren't cold per se but rather more lukewarm and without the broth. The pork belly was heavily fatty but sopping in savory deliciousness. Not a great dish to get if you're on a diet, but great to have if you want to feed your soul. The dish was heavy in meat and vegetables, and I wished there were more noodles. However, I imagine most people would want more meat vs noodles, so Silky Kitchen probably caters to the bulk of their population with more meat. Definitely a great place to go to if around Astor!

I still always drop by everytime I'm nearby, but after my last few visits I'm adjusting my overall rating. Although I still love the novelty and ease of the ordering system and the convenience of the price point, the excitement rooted in discovery may have enhanced my overall rating.The rolls are great and fresh, but nothing far beyond the norm. Additionally, the last two times i've ordered the cheeseburger in the Cheeseburger Hand Roll, the meat has been cold .- which makes it a very different experience. Imagine, a warm cheeseburger wrapped in rice. Now imagine a cold cheeseburger, cheese hardened wrapped in rice. Very different.Overall, still a great spot to grab a quick and reasonably priced lunch!

Title: Cozy Vibes and Tasty Bites at Local Mexican Gem

I dropped into this bustling spot on a Monday evening and was instantly charmed by the soulful R&B soundtrack that set a relaxed tone. Despite being the solo waiter on duty, our server was the epitome of warmth and efficiency, ensuring our experience was nothing short of welcoming.

Happy Hour was a delightful surprise, with specials on Margaritas – both flavored and on the rocks – as well as beer and wine available until 7pm. It was the perfect accompaniment to the impressive fare served. This modestly-sized local Mexican establishment really punches above its weight when it comes to their culinary offerings. Whether it's quesadillas, tacos, or any other dish that tantalizes your taste buds, you simply can't go wrong here.

The ambiance caters to small to medium gatherings and feels ideal for a casual catch-up with friends. They also have bar seating with full service for those who prefer a stool over a table. While it may not be the go-to for large groups without prior arrangements, the staff seem happy to discuss how to best accommodate your party.

In summary, this place is definitely on my list for a return visit – for the friendly service, engaging atmosphere, and delicious eats.

I was attending a conference in the area and this restaurant appeared as a good lunch spot. Well they were right, we walked in around noon and it was relatively empty. The waiter handed us menus and we had fresh water soon after sitting. The menu had several choices for lunch. The chips and salsa given were delicious. Not sure if we were just all hungry or the salsa was really that good. Since we were still on the clock we did not get any cocktails, but I saw some cocktails people around us ordered and they looked good. The food did not take very long to come out, and the portions were perfect for lunch. The food was great, and we all felt very satisfied and we didn't even finish all the food. The waiter has an tablet and was able to swipe the credit card right at the table for an easy transaction. Overall a great lunch, the reason it is 4 stars, is because I didn't get to try their drinks sooo that will be left for future reviews

Really love the concept of Chefs Club Counter... they rotate in different restaurants for a short period of time. For July and August, it is hosted by Amar, a healthy offering by chef George Mendes, who is Michelin-rated. The location is on point and great for people watching if you can snag a table outside. Even if sitting inside, it's a win with the aesthetically pleasing decorations. You order up front at the counter, they give you a card number, you sit wherever you please, and they bring you your food. We had:- Summer glow salad- Lobster roll (available for only a limited time)- Red sangria The red sangria was a nice pour and was during their happy hour (ends at 7pm), so it was $7! Loved the summer glow salad. The salmon was cooked to perfection! And the roasted veggies were delish. The lobster roll was a little eh. It truthfully didn't taste like a lobster roll in my opinion, and I didn't feel like I was eating lobster. The seasoning and taste was good, but didn't taste like lobster at all. And although the roll was really good and the perfect toasted amount, it was a lot of bread. The manager was kind enough to check up on us, and go around to all of the tables at 7pm letting us know it was last call for happy hour, that was really genuine and nice. If I'm ever in the mood to grab a quick drink and bite with a friend, this place will be high on my list to go to.

Title: A Sunny Sunday Brunch to Remember

My experience at this charming brunch spot was nothing short of delightful. With an enticing offer of endless mimosas or sangria for just $25, it was the perfect choice for a warm, sunny September Sunday. The restaurant's outdoor setting—with the sun beaming down—made us grateful for the sombreros they provided for shade.

The breakfast egg bowls were the star of the meal; a harmonious blend of quinoa, Brussels sprouts, and perfectly cooked eggs. Not only was the service outstanding, but the freshness and flavors of the food were also memorable. Traveling from our hotel on the east side was unquestionably worthwhile for this lovely dining experience.

Title: Tantalizing Tacos in a Spacious Setting

I recently visited this restaurant with a group of friends and was pleasantly surprised by both the fare and the ample space afforded by its split-level design. The tacos, in particular, stood out due to their innovative takes on traditional flavors. I was especially fond of the fried oyster and shrimp tacos, each offering a delightful culinary experience. As a table, we shared a serving of guacamole with chips that proved to be a perfect accompaniment for our variety of tacos. Our friends tried a range of other taco options, and all received their share of praise. If you're in the mood for a satisfying and creative twist on Mexican cuisine, this spot is well worth your visit.

Having frequented other Westville locations, we decided to visit the branch closer to our home. Tucked away from the usual hustle, this spacious and welcoming establishment proved to be a hit for a family meal. The food impressed us with its flavorsome qualities and generous portion sizes, a trait consistent even with the mimosa carafe, which regrettably we couldn't polish off. This spot has definitely earned a return visit for a leisurely weekend breakfast.

Great food in a nice environment.  I had the Cobb Salad with the Brown Derby dressing.  Very filling.  My wife had the famous Taco Bowl.  Good place for lunch.  And you get to look over at President Trumps famous escalator.

On has swiftly climbed the ranks to become one of my top dining choices. After two visits, I've been consistently impressed with the cuisine - a sophisticated twist on traditional Korean dishes that are bursting with flavor without the typical heaviness. 

Service can be a tad slow in the beginning, but rest assured, the dishes are served up quickly once ordered. Their cocktail menu is a delight; the standout for me is the Earl Grey, a unique concoction that shouldn't be missed, though the Matcha could benefit from a stronger flavor.

The food selection seems foolproof. Vegetables are transformed here, with their grilled kale being a revelation. The octopus, served in five tender pieces, may leave you wanting more, while the fried jalapeños chicken is a mix of crispy rice balls and succulent meat - a dish best ordered in abundance for larger parties.

For meat lovers, the pork chop and oxtail pot won't disappoint, both tender and perfectly paired with their respective sauces. The Dover sole is worthy of an accolade, and if you aim for something more comforting, the Dock pot satisfies, even when you think you can't take another bite.

Desserts are a must - particularly the Pear shaved ice. Light and refreshing, it's the ideal epilogue to a rich and savory meal. While the Mille-feuille is also commendable, it's the shaved ice that triumphs as the closing act. 

Overall, despite the initial wait, On is a gastronomic gem that promises an enchanting taste experience with every visit.

Title: A Pasta Lover's Paradise in Soho

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a fantastic little spot in Soho that absolutely blew me away with its pasta offerings. The ambiance is welcoming and casual, making it a great destination for any night out without breaking the bank.

What sets this place apart is the ambitious mission I've now set for myself: to devour every single pasta dish on their menu. Each pasta I've tried has its own distinct flavor profile and is prepared to perfection, albeit not al dente, which might be a slight drawback for some traditionalists.

The standout for me has been the Squid Ink Pasta Sorrento – a dish that truly tantalizes the taste buds. A close second is the delicate Angel Hair Carpelini Corallo, which is simply divine.

Do not miss the Antipasto Mozzarella for a fresh salad complemented by scrumptious mozzarella - it's a delectable way to start your meal. The selection of affordable wines is a delightful addition, contributing to an exquisite dining experience. And for dessert? The tiramisu is a must-try, rounding off the meal with a sweet note of perfection.

If you're wandering around Soho and have a craving for Italian, this is the place to be. I can't wait to return and continue working through their pasta paradise. Stay tuned for more updates from a devoted fan!

Title: A Vegetarian Sushi Haven

If you're on the hunt for top-tier vegetarian sushi, look no further than this gem of a spot. As a vegetarian, it's rare to find such inventive and delightful sushi combinations, and I've become an avid ambassador, recommending it to all plant-based pals. Their variety caters to every palate, and the presentation is a feast for the eyes—each roll is a masterpiece with its own perfectly paired sauce.

Though space for a leisurely meal is limited, the quick-bite setup doesn't detract from the experience. Plus, the service shines with friendliness and a willingness to guide you through their standout menu. Decision paralysis? Start with my personal favorites: the Spicy Mango roll or the festive La Fiesta roll. Each bite is an explosion of flavor with innovative ingredients like black rice, toasted cayenne sauce, and tomato guajillo sauce.

Dive into their menu, rich with creative options, but when in doubt, prioritize the sushi. From sweet potato to mushroom-based rolls, you're in for a treat, but the sushi is where they truly excel.

Title: A Reliable Late-Night Bite at Joe's

During my recent city trip, I refused to let a day pass without indulging in a classic New York slice, which naturally led me to Joe's. I stuck with old favorites - one white and one supreme slice. Joe's maintains its reputation for offering solid pizza options that hit the spot for a quick, satisfying meal, though it's not the place for a life-changing pizza experience.

Impressively, even with a crowd queuing out the door close to midnight, Joe's service was exceptional. The line moved with incredible speed, and I had my order within 15 minutes – they truly prioritize efficient service.

For those seeking a speedy and delicious pizza without the frills, Joe's is your go-to. It's not the pinnacle of pizza mastery, but it's dependable for a fulfilling bite.

This is My go-to spot for dumplings  . I always get the Seared Pork dumplings, and always eat them with their house sauce, its super delicious. I tried the chicken dumplings once but didn't really like them (thought i would since I eat more chicken than pork).... the staff is always friendly and its cool to see your food being made right before your eyes. Keep in mind that this place is really small.

We came here on a Friday night. We sat at the counter, ordered the standard omakase, plus scallops and fried chicken, and a carafe of sake (one of the cheaper ones you can find on the menu). Scallop was delicious, but for $24 I'd expected a bit more scallop meat there, I think 2/3 of what's on the plate were actually mushrooms. Fried chicken was well executed, juicy and flavorful, but not mind-blowingly good. For the skewers, it's all chicken - and honestly I've had most of those chicken meat somewhere else, don't think I can call what I had here one of the best. Total bill including tip comes to $270+. Here's the verdict. Yummy food, but not worth the price. Don't get me wrong, they were all delicious, but for a price tag like that, I wouldn't have a meal with main focus on chicken.

Can't wait to come back here! It was a chilly night when we arrived, so it was perfect. I'm surprised it was pretty empty inside. What we ordered was:1. Mini shrimp cakes - These were SO GOOD. We waited the longest for these, because we were told they had to make the dough. Totally fine, cause they came out piping hot, fresh, and so flavorful! 2. Chicken Pho w/ Bone Marrow - Pretty good, and honestly for the price of the bone marrow, it's pretty worth it considering many other places charge a ton. 3. Spicy Lemongrass Soup - I can't wait to get this again. It was so refreshing, and not too spicy which was great since my spice tolerance is garbage. Another thing I loved is that all the food was hot. I love when my dishes are piping hot, and when I was nearing the end of the bowl, it was still at a good temperature! Even though there seemed to be only 1 server, we were served quickly and adequately!

Title: A Gem in the Financial District: 5-Star Irish Pub Experience

I'm stingy with my five-star ratings, but this Irish pub nestled in the hustle of Wall Street earns every single one. Breaking away from a work training session, I ventured in for lunch and found both a culinary and atmospheric delight.

The place boasts a chic yet inviting interior, with a lengthy bar that draws you in and a comfortable dining area that encourages you to stay. Service was top-notch, thanks to our exceedingly pleasant and attentive waitress.

Kickstarting the meal with a lobster bisque, I was treated to a generous bowl brimming with fresh, real lobster chunks—a luxurious start. The main course, a chicken pesto wrap special, did not disappoint. The chicken's flawless cook and the wrap's flavors impressed me, while the accompanying fries were a crispy perfection.

A visit to an Irish pub isn't complete without a Guinness, and their pour did the iconic brew justice, satisfying even the most particular fans of the stout.

In short, this upscale Irish pub is a must-visit when in Manhattan's financial district. A place that pairs great service with delicious food and an excellent bar selection. Cheers to a memorable dining experience!

I passed Bubby's as I was on my way to Hudson yards and I decided to stop in and give them a try for brunch. This by far is now one of my favorite restaurants in the city as the quality of the food and service provided by the staff was outstanding. I ordered the fried chicken biscuit at this restaurant which I was hesitant at first to order given that I am not in the south. The biscuit was one of the best I have had to date and the chicken and mustard greens they top the biscuit with, were outstanding!! The dish comes with a side of fries which were also fresh and very tasty! I ordered their Arnold Palmer as my drink and I thought it was one of the best I've ever had. I highly recommend visiting here if you're in NYC and looking for an excellent meal.

First time here, but I was in town to see the Empire State Building. This place had a strong profile and I definitely was not disappointed.Before arriving, I looked into Yelp and placed my name on the waitlist, therefore, when I arrived my wait would be limited. This was helpful as I was on a strict time schedule, but I was lucky to sit at the bar top and be seated immediately upon arrival.Upon ordering, the waitress was extremely helpful and friendly with offering best dishes as well as recommendations. I typically prefer to lean on the staff for their opinions at restaurants I am unfamiliar with. Therefore, the mocha with oat milk was a drink that was highlighted as really popular as well as the chicken and waffle dish. The mocha was really good and wasn't too strong. I throughly enjoyed the chicken and waffle because of the spicy-ish syrup and combination of the quality chicken as well as waffle. Price wise, it was a little costly, but the exceptional service and taste made it worthwhile. I will most likely return here when I am back in town!

Wooooow, so I asked like 5 people where is the first place I need to go eat when I get to NYC and all of them said black tap, so I absolutely had to go. The vibe was cool when we walked in, immediately were seated and our server came right over. I got a peanut butter stout that was incredible, my mom got strawberry lemonade that was def made fresh, my dad got an IPA that he said was pretty dang good and we later got the churro Choco taco milkshake. Per usual, we each ordered a different burger to share, and honestly all were incredible. You really can't go wrong with anything you choose on this menu. It's all so delicious and over the top that you're for sure going to love it, even the classic cheeseburger which may have even been my favorite. Make sure you get a milkshake though because that was the icing on the cake!

I love this spot! The gelato is very creamy and flavorful. If you get a cone, they make it into this beautiful flower! I love that you can get multiple flavors in a cone or cup. It's right near there theater district so me and my family will go here after seeing a broadway show for dessert. The only reason that I did not give it five stars, is that I don't feel that their seating area is well maintained, especially when it is busy. A lot of the tables needed to be wiped down and no one seemed to be doing that. Other than that, it's a great spot for a yummy scoop of gelato!

This is probably by far the best ramen I've had. The almost 2hr wait was pretty crazy but on a cold night that me and my cousins had ventured for this bowl was well worth it.We were a party of 4 and we stayed in line while watching NY Ranger fans find parking while roaming the streets to MSG for a game. We saw many dogs do their business as well which made us stare in amusement.1hr and 45mins later we get to the door finally, the blasting heat made us warm up real fast but then it was overwhelmingly hot, we finally make it through the first door and we started to watch reruns of how Ichiran has opened around the world and how Taiwans location is at a 240hr wait now. People wake up at 6am to line up for Ichiran!I see the green light signaling booths are available and there were 5 in a row that was perfect for our party. Ichiran is known for what they call "low-interaction dining", in which diners seat themselves in individual ramen booths, fill out ticket orders and receive food from anonymous hands through a curtain-covered window. The ramen was topped with chasau, boiled egg(that you have to to peel yourself), scallions and their infamous spicy red seasoning. First slurp I had was the broth, second slurp I had was with the noodles. It was love at first sight, my mouth was watering for even more. With my tall glass of Asahi on the side with each mouthful of noodles I could not stop smiling and just going "mmmm" the whole time. I opted for the Macha pudding to share with my gf. It was so freaking good and we both agreed it was a great way to end our night.Ichiran is legit, 2 thumbs up from us. Do try if you get a chance and beat the dinner rush as I heard there is not a line during the day time. Oh and no tipping is allowed!

Let ma start by saying, they take the 90 mins of brunch seriously. A time chart is places on your table indicating the start and finish of bottomless. The drink options are superb. More options than your standard brunch. I love a good caipirinha. They didn't disappoint. Although I would have appreciated a sugar cane in my drink. I also had mojitos which were good. I couldn't get fancy with a strawberry mojito as it isn't an option. My friends all enjoyed their dishes. My steak was great. I had the maduros and fried rice with steak. Stephan is an amazing server. Very polite. They didn't have many servers so he had numerous tables to tend to and did his best. We don't like waiting very long for our drink refills when we are being timed. This is the reason for 4 stars.

Last night's takeout experience from this local gem was thoroughly satisfying. The delivery did not disappoint with hot, fresh food arriving in secure packaging. My fried shrimp with garlic noodles was a hit – generous shrimp portions and a hefty serving of noodles for a mere additional dollar. My friends raved about their fried oysters with perfectly crisp fries, and the steam bag bursting with succulent crab legs, mussels, and corn. We all left our meal impressed and eager for more. I'm intrigued to dine in next time, suspecting that the full menu holds further tantalizing options. A return visit is certainly in the cards. Highly recommended!

Title: Quick Bite at KatzuNori with Room for Improvement

My recent dining experience at KatzuNori was a mixed bag. On the positive side, the meal itself was decent, and the restaurant's efficiency meant a relatively short wait time despite the bustling crowd. Budget-conscious diners will appreciate the affordable prices coupled with the fast service.

However, the no-tipping policy seemed to detract from the service quality, which felt impersonal and rushed—a clear strategy to turn tables rapidly. This lack of warmth and hospitality, something I value in a dining experience, left me with no desire to return.

Considering the myriad of culinary gems that New York City has to offer, my search for exceptional dining will lead me elsewhere next time.

Had a WONDERFUL experience at L'Angolo- an Italian restaurant on a corner in TriBeCa- close to the financial district. We were seated outside so we could people watch with the other lively New York diners and watch all the action going on. They have specials going on constantly and I had the pleasure of ordering the PESTO GNOCCHI WITH BURRATA. a real THING! It was scrumptious, from the generous amount of burrata infused in the pesto and the gnocchi. It was fabulous. The service was attentive and non-intrusive, with the bread and caprese fighting for attention with the absolutely scrumptious pesto gnocchi. Can't wait to be back and try more delicious dishes!!!

This place has exceptional ambiance and service. We went 3 nights as it was just a few doors down from where we were staying, but Mexican in NYC is going to be a risk...to be fair...they serve Irish options too. They offer a lovely sangria and good beer. Sit at the bar for fun and drinks. But, the food was just ok and overpriced...yes...yes...this is NYC...but it ought to be amazing.
