The bangers my husband had were good, and my burrito bowl was ok. The veggies needed to be grilled a bit more, and the flavor was not spicy...although a hefty serving of guacamole was appreciated.

My friend and I visited Jajaja on a Monday night after finding the restaurant on Yelp. It wasn't busy at the time so we were seated right away. Let me start off by saying that this restaurant is beautiful!!! I would honestly visit just to appreciate the interior decoration and ambiance. This is the perfect place to go for a fun date, friend gathering, co-worker outing, etc. Plus there's a full bar! However, when we visited (mid-January), they weren't accepting cash as a form of payment so beware of that.My friend and I started off with horchatas, I ordered the matcha horchata and she got the almond horchata. Both were pretty good, but I preferred the taste of the almond one. Also, I forgot to take a picture but I loved how they were presented. We then ordered the gorditas, nachos, and the jackfruit tamale. The jackfruit tamale was interesting in the way that it wasn't a traditional tamale; the texture was off and the flavor was lacking. It wasn't bad but I wouldn't order it again. It just didn't hit the spot for me. On the other hand, the gorditas were delicious; they were full of flavor and cooked perfectly. However, the true winner of the night was the nachos. We devoured the dish like it was our last meal, it was jam-packed with tasty ingredients that complimented each other and was mouth-watering to say the least. Highly recommend!!! Side note: My friend and I ordered a total of three dishes because we wanted to try as much of the menu as possible, but even for the two of us, the nachos alone were very filling.I'm very excited to return!!!

I love a good sushi spot. This place makes me feel like I'm in Japan.The sushi was very good and tasted very fresh. I love the presentation. The service was very good.Definitely on my list of a go-to sushi spot restaurant.

Title: Charming Ambiance and Unique Onion Delight at Local Gem

I recently visited a charming little spot with a warm ambiance perfect for catching up with friends. The restaurant boasts both cozy outdoor seating and a spacious indoor area. Our table opted for the highly recommended crispy sweet onions, priced at $15, and they did not disappoint. These creatively squared onion bites are a twist on traditional rings and are accompanied by a delightful sauce — an absolute must-try.

For my main course, I indulged in the Fusili for $24, served in an unusually large and long shape. The pasta's design ingeniously trapped the sauce, though a dash of acidity could elevate the dish to perfection. Although I didn't try the pizza, it's definitely on my radar for a future visit.

Adding to the positive experience, the staff went above and beyond to accommodate a stroller for our group, which was greatly appreciated. All in all, the excellent service and delectable dishes make this restaurant a place to return to.

During a nice day we were strolling in the near by area , after being done we decided to grab a bite & drinks. Outside seating on a very nice day was a bonus, the place looked good ... U order inside then they bring your food out. Drinks had some Brooklyn lager summer ale beer it  was great nice & cold not bad hard to go wrong. We decide to give the Calamari a try since it smelled so good .. it was good but very disappointing as well the calamari was not just calamari it had peppers deep fried as well now .. not that I mind a bit of it problem is it had way too much of it we asked for an order of calamari FYI the peppers, onions whatever was extra is not listed on the menu had we known .. we would have either asked for it w out the veggies or just simply gotten something else for the price they charge for the calamari .. they should give u "calamari" & nothing else.Service was quick, nice ambiance outside. price wise it's ahh.

Title: Authentic Shanghainese Delights in Chinatown

If you're in Chinatown and craving Shanghainese cuisine, this cozy yet bustling spot is a must-visit. It's a personal favorite of mine, and it continually earns the praise of friends and family I introduce it to. Despite visiting at a typically busy time—1:30 PM on a Saturday—I found it unusually quiet, creating a perfect dining atmosphere.

The restaurant's space is on the smaller side, but they maximize it well with a second-floor seating area that’s ideal for dinner crowds. On my latest visit, I dived into an array of dishes: spicy wontons, beef in scallion pancakes, pork soup dumplings, Shanghai lo mein with beef, and a Thai iced tea. The wontons were a highlight—with a sauce that delivered the right amount of kick, balanced by garlic flakes and scallions. The beef wrapped in crunchy, perfectly fried scallion pancakes, complemented by refreshing cucumber, was a standout.

The Shanghai lo mein didn't disappoint either; it was a hearty mix of tender beef, shanghai bok choy, and mushrooms. The soup dumplings, however, are what make this place unforgettable. They're a flavorful burst of soup and pork, though take caution as the soup can be scalding.

The Thai iced tea fell short, being too strong with not enough milk—a rare misstep in an otherwise exemplary meal. The service was quick, and seating was prompt, which is always a plus. Note that they prefer cash, debit, or AMEX for payments.

Overall, this restaurant is a gem for those looking to explore Shanghainese cuisine in Chinatown with a promise of quality dishes and efficient service.

David's Cafe treated me to a delightful brunch experience, significantly outshining the competition with a mere 15-minute wait, in contrast to Cafe Mogador's 30-45 minutes. Their Steak and Eggs, a steal at $21, brought an unexpected twist to a classic dish with its chimichurri sauce, vibrant peppers, onions, and a symphony of spices that created a flavor explosion reminiscent of Brazilian cuisine. The pairing of robust hanger steak with a lusciously runny egg was made even better by the delightfully seasoned roasted potatoes.

I appreciated their thoughtful approach to the mixed greens, sparing them the ubiquitous balsamic vinaigrette which I find less appealing. Service was quick, with all three dishes served simultaneously within 15 minutes, and attentive waitstaff kept our water glasses brimming — a touch of hospitality despite the presence of a pitcher.

Acknowledging the price increase over the past few years, the quality and taste justify the costs. I'm already considering a return visit for the tempting Orange Blossom Pancakes which looked utterly scrumptious. David's Cafe definitely secures a spot on my brunch favorites list.

Title: A Tasty Taco Pilgrimage to NYC

Last weekend's trek from Boston to NYC, dubbed "Jiaming's Taco Endeavor," led us to a true taco treasure. The mission was simple: satisfy a friend's taco craving, but the experience was anything but ordinary.

The spotlight fell on two tacos: the reliable Carne Asada and the unexpectedly delightful Adobada. The Carne Asada was exactly what you'd hope for from a renowned taco spot -- classic, with perfectly cooked steak wrapped in a soft corn tortilla. It was comfort in every bite.

However, the Adobada was the star of the show. It transformed my meat hierarchy, placing pork on a pedestal I never expected. The marinated pork burst with flavors that danced on the palate, and the pineapple -- a potentially controversial addition -- complemented without overpowering, much like a subtle nod to my fondness for pineapple ham pizza.

My recommendation? Next time you visit, double down on the Adobada. It's not just a meal; it's an experience worth the journey.

One of my favorite ramen spots in the city. Delicious noodles with a rich broth. Super flavorful and a huge portion for an affordable price. There can be a crazy wait too, I've had to wait maybe 45 minutes for a party of 4. It's definitely better to not go with a group. I loved the spicy paitan and highly recommend it, if you're not big on meat, don't get the deluxe. It's cash only which is annoying but it's worth the mild inconvenience. The place is pretty loud and the service is good, they come by often because they want to get you out of the place quick.

Title: A Slightly Better Second Take at Woodpecker

After giving Woodpecker a second chance, I've nudged my rating up to a 3.5 stars. Here's the breakdown:

Happy Hour - Solid choice. The signature cocktail steals the show, and if you're looking for a bite to go with your drink, the Hipster Fries won't disappoint.

Appetizers - The buzz around the bacon is mostly hype, and the Wings & Rings are passable at best. Stick to the fries for your bacon craving.

Mains - The salmon stands out, perfectly seasoned and satisfying, a rare find for me. The Beet Salad is a tasty, albeit small, contender, while the Brussels Sprouts also make a commendable side. As for the Lobster Pot Pie and gnocchi, they missed the mark or were missing entirely.

Dessert - The peanut butter and Cheerios treat is surprisingly good—a must-try.

Interior - The throwback decor is curious for such a new spot but overall, the atmosphere is clean and welcoming.

Final Thoughts - Woodpecker is a viable option for happy hour and a casual dinner if you're nearby, but it's not a destination spot for me. Check out my photos for a glimpse of what to expect.

I recently enjoyed a dining experience with friends at this cozy restaurant after our workday. Though the space is on the smaller side - which could be snug for big groups - they cleverly provide ample hangers for personal belongings, which is a thoughtful touch.

For starters, we indulged in the Grilled Chicken Satay and Chicken Curry Puffs, both served in sets of four, making them perfect for sharing, though larger parties may consider ordering more. Each dish was a hit, especially with the accompanying sauce that elevated the flavors.

My beverage of choice was a Thai Coffee, which was a delightful pick-me-up. As for the main course, I savored the Ratchaburi Crab & Pork Dry Noodles. Contrary to its name, the dish was pleasantly sauced, akin to a Mazeman, and thoroughly satisfying.

We capped off our meal with Sticky Rice for dessert; we tried the Taro variety which was decent, though I suspect the seasonal mango option might be a superior choice.

For visual food enthusiasts, their IG: @phothegram, might whet your appetite even further. Overall, the restaurant is a recommendable spot to unwind with good food after a busy day.

Title: A Delightful Evening at a Dad-Approved Eatery

My recent dinner at this restaurant was a true pleasure, especially since my father, whose tastes align perfectly with the establishment's offerings, accompanied me. Arriving at 6pm allowed us to dodge the typical dinner frenzy, which I'd suggest for a more serene experience.

Our enthusiasm was apparent as we ambitiously ordered an array of dishes: Sichuan cucumber salad, steamed pork soup dumplings, sweet crispy fried duck presented in wraps tableside, Yangzhou fried rice brimming with spam, pork, and shrimp, and succulent shredded pork with sweet miso. Each dish arrived with remarkable speed, a testament to the kitchen's efficiency.

The duck, while delectable, sparked a personal preference for self-assembly to select my preferred cuts of meat for the wraps, which were made with interesting taco-like sheets rather than the usual fluffy bread. The fried rice satisfied with its generous portion, and the shredded pork stood out with its tender, miso-glazed bites. Despite good soup dumplings, they did not top those of competing venues.

The star of the meal was undoubtedly the Sichuan cucumber salad—refreshing, crunchy, with a satisfying heat that had echoes of Korean kimchi but distinguished by its more potent chili flavor.

Commendations to the staff for their exceptional attentiveness. They were proactive and efficient, from swiftly supplying a diner with new chopsticks to maintaining the cleanliness of our dining space and refreshing our drinks without prompt. Their customer service skills indeed accentuated the dining experience.

In summary, the fusion of scrumptious cuisine and stellar service ensures our return. Highly recommended for those in search of a delightful culinary evening.

I've been a patron of this gem in KTown for years, and even as I pen this review solo over lunch, the consistency of quality is undeniable. The spicy seafood noodles coupled with the meat jun, a delectable beef pancake, are nothing short of a culinary crescendo. Each mouthful is an umami-packed delight, perfectly seasoned and satisfying to the core. I pride myself on having sampled 90% of the local eateries, yet this one reigns supreme in flavor. In a word, I love it.

Title: A Delightful Experience at Rubirosa with a Minor Glitch

I highly recommend snagging a reservation at Rubirosa at least two weeks in advance; the anticipation only heightens the experience. Upon arrival, our punctuality was rewarded with a prime center-table seating.

Our culinary journey commenced with the Rubirosa salad—a fresh, promising start. As my sister has a gluten-free diet, we were especially appreciative of the GF pasta and pizza options, both of which were delightful. The tie-dye pizza lived up to its vibrant reputation. A warm flourless chocolate cake provided a decadent finale to our meal.

The ambiance at Rubirosa was faultless, exuding a perfect 10/10 vibe that enhanced the dining experience. However, it wasn’t without a hiccup—the "large" pasta portion seemed ungenerous for its $30 price tag and could have benefited from a touch more seasoning. Nevertheless, Rubirosa's charms outweigh this minor shortfall, making it a must-visit spot for those craving refined Italian cuisine with a thoughtful gluten-free consideration.

On our recent Saturday evening visit to this restaurant, we were immediately struck by the beautiful and elegant decor. The attention to detail, especially the charming floral wallpaper, created a delightful ambiance. 

While the staff maintained a level of professionalism, they lacked warmth, leaving something to be desired in the hospitality department. 

As for the cuisine, the offerings were dependable, though none truly dazzled our palates, aligning with expectations for this genre of dining. However, the Spinach Artichoke Dip did catch our attention as a highlight of the meal. 

In summary, while the setting impresses, the food and service don't venture beyond the conventional.

Stopped by this restaurant after the Global Citizen Festival and I was super satisfied. The restaurant is welcoming and the decor is beautiful. The interior looked like the inside of a temple. The staff was also very pleasant. Although we came in on a Saturday night, there was no wait to be seated. I started off by ordering the Tom Kha soup which was tasty with fresh ingredients. For my entree I ordered the chicken pad Thai. I ordered mine medium spicy, which I will warn you, if you are sensitive to spice probably won't be a good idea. However, I really enjoyed it. The portions were filling and I couldn't finish my pad Thai . Although the restaurant looks fancy, the prices were pretty reasonable. The menu was also quite extensive and had so many options that looked really good. I definitely plan on going back to try something new.

Tucked away in Lower Manhattan, Las' Lap is a tropical oasis amidst the urban jungle. Upon entering, you're immediately embraced by the chill Caribbean vibes, with an expertly curated playlist to match. The crowd is as beautiful as the ambiance, with a touch of subtle elegance that hints at its low-key celebrity clientele.

Expect to pay a premium for drinks here, but rest assured, they are crafted to perfection and worth the splurge. Despite its cozy size, Las' Lap masterfully maintains a comfortable atmosphere where you can enjoy your space without feeling crowded. 

While I didn't delve into their food offerings, there's an allure that leaves you curious about what culinary delights they may serve and until when. One thing is for certain: Las' Lap has etched its spot on my go-to list for whenever I'm back in the area.

Came here for dinner recently with friends, and I always have my reservations regarding Thai since it could be a really great experience or a really bad one depending where you end up going, luckily this place was really superb! This little hole in the wall really did an amazing job from the amazing good food to the quick service.We had a bit of everything you'd have when you come for Thai food, the seating is a bit tight but its not bad once your already seated, and the service was attentive and all came out smoothly.I would recommend making a RSVP since they are small and popular spot, but otherwise highly recommend coming here!

The last 2 times I've been to New York, we have ended up at Madison Pickle for brunch. Both times have been great meals. There's was a short wait when we walked in, but there was an opening at the bar so we decided to sit there rather than wait longer. The bartender was very friendly and took great care of us. I got the hot chicken French toast. It was amazing, but a little spicy so be careful if you aren't a spicy food person. The syrup can help cool it down if it gets too warm. I really like all of their chicken meals. They know how to fry it!The prices are very reasonable especially for New York. You can really split an entree here as they are huge portions. Otherwise plan to get a to go box and enjoy it again later. Their drinks were tasty as well. I honestly don't think they anything bad on their menu. Looking forward to my next trip here

If you find yourself nearby, don't miss the opportunity to dine at this local gem. With its emphasis on freshness, each dish, particularly the fish, is a testament to the art of simplicity, enhanced by perfectly balanced seasoning that elevates the natural flavors. A definitive culinary delight awaits you here.

Omg I am a fan !!! Visited Sala Thai for the first time with my Husband and I am glad we walked in.We ordered Veggie Basil Thai fried rice and Chicken Basil Thai Fried rice ( ofcourse spicy version )The portions were great and filling, and the flavors were on point !! Will definitely recommend this place.

Title: Solid Fare at Tuome, But Don't Expect to Be Wowed

Rating: ★★★☆☆

On a busy Wednesday evening, my friend and I ventured to Tuome after spotting it on the restaurant week roster. Though we were a tad late, the place was lively, contradicting our worries about the time. However, the service was brisk at best, lacking the warmth or guidance we had hoped for when choosing our dishes.

We opted for the chicken liver and persimmon-scallop appetizers, which set a decent stage. The main course, 'Pig Out' – a tantalizing promise of pork belly and noodles – fell short of its potential, leaving me underwhelmed despite my anticipation.

Desserts of banana goat cheese and beignets ended our meal on a fair note. No dish struck a wrong chord, yet none played an unforgettable melody. Given the combination of unremarkable flavors and lackluster service, I lean towards a 3-star experience. I'm inclined to suggest other destinations to friends seeking dining recommendations, as Tuome didn’t quite hit the mark for a return visit.

District social was a madhouse so we hopped one street over. There was plenty of room at the bar in the far back so we sat there. The bar is tiny so the bartender was friendly and service was great. He made plenty of recommendations for us and it was great to have seats to catch up! There is no happy hour at the back bar - don't know why but too bad!We stayed here for a while and I'd definitely come back. We only had drinks so I'll try the food next time! I was eyeing the deviled eggs but apparently my friends hate them soooo I'll have to get them all alone.

Probably one of the best pizzas I've ever had. I tried their pepperoni and margarita and they were both delicious, but their pepperoni was exceptional. I had to go back in line for another slice! The crust is crispy and buttery but also chewy with the perfect texture, the sauce is fresh and savory, and they don't skimp out on the pepperoni. Every bite has a generous amount of pepperoni but it doesn't get too salty. The margarita is a great choice as well, more on the lighter side and clean tasting. I would definitely grab both slices again when I'm back in NYC!

amazing experience!! It was our first time trying ethiopian and we will definitely be back. all the meals are served on the same plate, however we decided to just split everything we got anyway. got the vegetarian combo + fried trout (which then came with two veggie sides) so ultimately we tried all the veggies and what we thought we wouldn't be into as much- we ended up enjoying the most. all the sides are great though, especially the chickpea based one and red lentils. the trout is also a 10/10- so lightly fried it didn't feel heavy or oily, and it's stuffed with an AMAZING salad- super flavorful. they don't take reservations and the place is fairly small, aesthetic isn't amazingly traditional feeling or anything, and they have standard table seating. around 6:30 on a saturday it was full, but tables were available. it's also in a very safe feeling area. lastly, the only negative would be that the combos (which seem to be the best deal) don't have a pick your own or meat + veggies option.  We really wanted to try a chicken dish and then also vegetables, but there was no way to do this in a combo form. there was either only vegetables or only various meats. if you wanted to get, for example, a chicken dish, you had to order a portion for one and then two sides yourself. The price is fair if you're splitting it with someone it ended up being about $30 each but if it was just a meal for one expect to pay around $20-$25 and have less sides (only 2). They gave a great amount of injera to go with the meal, we were a bit worried about running out since we had so much food but we had some to spare at the end. can't wait to return! also do you wish they had some dessert options or maybe more appetizers :)
This was only an average burger, they was too well done for my liking. However the burger had a lot of meat. It was just too dry and very expensive. The fries had a strange after taste

Korean American fusion. Not traditional Korean. But still tasty. The beef steamed buns was a little disappointing because I thought it was going to bulgogi, but more like a burger. Still tasty, but bc of the sauce. The seafood noodles were really yummy, had a lot of flavor and didn't skimp on seafood. My friend's bulgogi luttuce wrap was really good and big portion. A lot of meat with miso soup, rice as well. Would get that next time!

It is a little hidden away and through a door I would never think to walk through. I came here for a lunch outing with coworkers and we found the atmosphere good for conversation. Our lunch was at 12:30 and it wasn't particularly crowded when we arrived but was packed by the time we left at 2:30. The food was good, not exceptional but good. The service however, was awful. We had to flag down our server to order  our entrees after we had been sitting for more then 30 minutes and then we eventually had to track down a different server to get our check after it appeared that our sever had disappeared. I would come again since it is well located but be prepared for the service if you do eat here especially if you have limited time.

Nestled inconspicuously between two Korean establishments in Koreatown, Izakaya Mew is a basement gem that's easy to miss. The unassuming entrance leads you down a narrow hallway into an animated, subterranean haunt devoid of phone signal—adding to its hidden charm.

Expect a wait, as its popularity isn't a secret to locals. The menu is a feast for the eyes, sprawling with an ample array of well-priced Japanese favorites, from sushi to noodles, plus some intriguing novelties.

Kicking off with a refreshing Kirin Frozen Beer, the Sashimi Salad set a high bar for our meal, which was maintained by the Omu Soba—an impressive ensemble of noodles and vegetables tucked into an omelette, drizzled with sauce and crowned with bonito flakes. A must-try.

The Katsudon fell short, its usually crisp pork cutlet arriving disappointingly soft. With such a vast menu, not every dish can shine, and we skipped dessert due to a less-than-exciting selection.

Despite minor letdowns, Izakaya Mew radiates with culinary charm and is a spot I keenly anticipate revisiting. Pro tip: Gather a group of four to optimally sample the diverse offerings.

The restaurant was nicely decorated and had a lovely interior. There are two floors and a private section which is great for company events. The service was amazing, really friendly and welcoming staffs. However, I did wish the food was as good as the service here. I ordered the the lychee & rose martini, yuzu soju, yellow tail sushi, grilled scallops, black cod, mushrooms, tiger prawn, two desserts: one was a sweet potato ice cream and another banana and matcha bread. Highly recommend the martini and black cod (so buttery and paired nicely with the sauce they provided) as they were my favorites throughout the meal. The sushi, grilled scallops were good but the avocado to fish ratio for the sushi was a little off and the grill scallops lacked flavor. Personally, I wasn't a fan of the mushroom and tiger prawn as both were too salty. To my surprise, I did like the sweet potato ice cream with pecan. The banana and matcha bread was a big no from me. It was too sweet and you barely taste any matcha. Hope to see them improve some of the dishes! Definitely will be back for martinis and the black cod!

This place has been on my to do list, for quite some time. Its kind of out of the way, so I had to make it a priority to come here.Minca is located on 5th St, between ave a and ave b in the east village.There really isn't much room in this place. We sat at the window sill. But you don't really come here for the decor. You come here for the ramen.I tried the Minca ramen, with two helpings of noodles. The broth was flavorful, but a bit salty. It wasn't out of this world good, but it was still good. I was definitely expecting more, from the reviews of this place and the rankings, that name this place, as one of the best places in NYC for ramen. I tried my friends Minca Sio ramen, which also was good, but not other worldly good.I'd probably come back here, if I was in the area, but I wouldn't go out of my way to come back here again.

Title: Heavenly Slice at a Converted Sanctuary

I recently had the pleasure of dining at what is, in my opinion, the purveyor of the best NY-style pizza around. The ambiance is instantly captivating; the restaurant is elegantly housed within the walls of what was once a church, delivering a truly unique dining experience. 

The wait to be seated was brief, and soon I was enjoying the mesmerizing view of pizzas being skillfully slid into a coal fire oven, the craftsmanship evident as each pie was prepared from scratch. Opting for a custom size afforded me the opportunity to indulge in my all-time favorite toppings - the classic combination of meatball and ricotta.

Each bite delivered a symphony of flavors, with the perfect balance of cheesy goodness and a crisply baked crust, a testament to their culinary expertise. It's an unparalleled pizza experience that left a lasting impression, one that I can only describe as divine.

This spot is an absolute must-visit, especially if you're seeking a family-friendly venue with an authentic slice of New York right at your table.

Title: Value and Flavor Meet at Local Japanese Steakhouse

I'm a regular at this Japanese steakhouse, drawn in by the unbeatable lunch specials. The lunch steak, priced at around $13, may not be their premium cut, but it's a steal when you factor in the tasty sides and soup that come with it. The steak's flavor holds true to what you'd expect from a hot plate establishment, and the selection of sauces enhances the experience deliciously.

However, caution is advised - the sizzling hot plate can be a hazard to the over-eager diner. It's wise to let the dish cool a tad before indulging. Service here is reliably quick and courteous, another reason I keep coming back. Gone are the days of standing to eat; comfortable seating is provided for a leisurely meal. 

While it's no fine dining steakhouse like Peter Luger, it's a commendable option for a savory, meaty lunch without breaking the bank.

We had the meatballs, Toscano Kale salad, Garganelli pasta and the Gramigna pasta. This place makes their own pasta next to their bar!The food was was beyond exceptional. The meatballs were some of the best I have ever had. They should be an entre!I can highly recommend this restaurant.

A very good rice noodle shop! If you like more of a mild taste, tomato soup based rice noodle would be a great fit. If you like spicy once's, the sour fish is a great choice.Personally I like their portion and all the ingredients they put in. You can choose to cook it yourself or let the staff help you. Either way it's very tasty!The shop is a little small and there's some waiting time during dinner. But the rice noodle soups were yummy enough to worth it!

Love the ambiance! It's a cute brunch spot with indoor and outdoor seating. The staff was super sweet and professional. I had a great time at brunch with my friend. I got the egg white omelette and she got the avocado toast. The prices weren't bad and I think our total came out to $50 between the two of us. The food tasted good, I just wish they had more options on the menu.

Umm in my opinion getting poke right is not a tough task to achieve (I might be wrong but it comes across as simple) hence when a poke bowl doesn't exactly have what you ordered, you are bound to be disappointed.Maybe my mistake was I ordered this bowl through Rituals.. my order was atleast 15 mins late than what was communicated.. I waited there during lunch hours and then no prices for guessing but they got the base wrong.. kale in place of spring mix (kale is mentioned as a separate base in their menu) Well I was tired as it was during lunch time and I had to rush back to work so I just let it be. Also the quantity was bit less for a strandard poke bowlSince there are thousands of poke options in and around the neighborhood.. I will try another place when I feel like a poke

Enjoy the friendly atmosphere and fantastic decor. The staff was very attentive in filling our waters, cleaning our tables and attending to our needs.Food - I got the bone marrow toast. Amazing thick cuts of bone marrows served with perfectly crisp toast. I would recommend sharing this for the table, because it does get overwhelming after one piece. Also the bone marrow hardens after a while, so make sure to eat it right away. I ordered the bucatini all bottarga, and love the al dente noodles. Flavor wise it was very very heavy in garlic and thick in texture even though there was no dairy in the sauce! I did enjoy it very much but 3/4 way through it became too one-dimensional and heavy. I would recommend as to share. The rest of the party ordered different items and they all enjoyed their meal.For dessert I got the passionfruit sorbet, this was bomb! Very intense flavors and huge scoops. I would order this again!Oddly enough, the only major con is that they don't take reservations in person, you can only make yelp reservations which wasn't a big deal cause I have a Yelp account. But my friend couldn't make one when he was in person...

I have only been for brunch and it is very good! I absolutely adore the innovative grilled cheese tomato soup spoon bites and their amazing red velvet waffles. There is great diversity on the menu and my bf really enjoys their steak and eggs. Definitely would suggest making a reservation for brunch because they are quite popular!

Title: A Culinary Journey Worth Every Penny at [Restaurant Name]

I recently indulged in the best sushi experience of my life at [Restaurant Name]. Opting for the 16-course menu was a decision well made, offering an opulent selection of premiums like truffle, caviar, uni, and melt-in-your-mouth fatty tuna, all without a significant price jump from the 15-course offering.

Each dish was a testament to freshness, artfully plated and delivering a unique twist on traditional sushi that had my taste buds in a constant state of euphoria. The harmony of flavors was nothing short of extraordinary, and though the price tag is noteworthy, the experience justifies every dime.

This isn't just a meal; it's a special-occasion-worthy adventure I'm eager to revisit. [Restaurant Name] sets the bar incredibly high for sushi connoisseurs. A resounding 100% recommendation for anyone looking to be wowed in the realm of fine dining.

Title: A Cozy Retreat at KTown

KTown may easily be mistaken for just another spot in its namesake neighborhood, but it's truly a hidden gem tucked away in a basement setting. Upon descending the stairs, the atmosphere shifts from the serene to a vibrant buzz, accentuated by warmly dim lighting and wood-adorned decor that evokes the comfort of a grand bar.

Don't let the promise of happy hour mislead you - while it offers delightful alcohol and tapas-style dishes, there's plenty for the non-drinker to enjoy. The chicken wings were a highlight, striking the perfect balance with a crispy exterior and succulent interior, minus any greasy residue. The tteokbokki brought a satisfying spicy zing to the mix, marrying rice cakes with noodles and vegetables in harmony. But the real star of the show was the kimchi pancake, which achieved a state of crispy, savory perfection.

While the restrooms are situated at the back, with a surprisingly longer queue for the men's single stall than the women's, this detail does little to detract from the overall experience. KTown stands out as an excellent choice for those seeking to unwind and reconnect with friends in a laid-back yet lively setting.

Title: A Spanish Gem in the Heart of the City

Tucked away in a cozy corner, this charming tapas restaurant is a delightful find. With a wine list that boasts authenticity and a keen respect for Spanish vineyards, each pour proved a perfect complement to the savory plates. The croquettes were tasty, but it was the chickpeas that mastered the art of being both crispy and succulent. Yet, it was the artichoke salad that stole the show, a dish so ingeniously crafted with flavors so wickedly paired, it lingered in memory long after the last bite. A true testament to the culinary magic at work in this quaint establishment.

Title: Charming Vibe and Tasty Eats at Tacombi

Stepping into Tacombi, you're immediately embraced by a casual and cool atmosphere that simply radiates fun. The interior charms with its super cute decor, and the VW wagon parked center stage is not just a quirky addition but also an Instagram hotspot.

While the menu prices lean towards the higher end, with items starting at $4, the culinary delights justify the expenditure. The Crispy Fish Taco was a standout, combining a succulent fish chip with a perfectly spiced sauce. It's a crunchy, juicy treat that simply bursts with flavor.

Another notable dish was the Yellowfin Tuna Tostada. It's a harmony of textures and flavors, pairing fresh raw tuna with creamy avocado, crispy fried onion, and a sturdy taco shell. Each bite is a well-crafted blend of the ocean's finesse and street food zest.

Do not miss out on the Corn Esquites. This side dish brings sweet corn and a luxurious creamy sauce together for a side that's as comforting as it is delicious.

Overall, Tacombi's vibe and dishes make for an enjoyable dining experience – it's a spot that's definitely worth a visit, especially if you're looking to treat your taste buds and your social media followers.

Title: A Delightful Surprise on a Busy Weeknight

My boyfriend and I decided to try this charming little gem without a reservation and only waited 20 minutes for a walk-in, quite impressive for a weeknight. The staff demonstrated remarkable efficiency, allowing us to browse the menu and place our order while we waited, minimizing the wait time for our meal once seated.

We indulged in the pad Thai and pineapple fried rice, both of which were absolutely delightful – the flavors transported us straight to the streets of Bangkok. Additionally, the free Thai iced tea with a Yelp check-in was a sweet bonus to our meal. Pricing was fair, considering the quality and quantity of the food served.

Though the space is compact, the establishment has mastered the art of quick table turnover without making you feel rushed. Next visit, I've got my eye on trying their udon or curry. Can't wait to come back!

My friend and I stopped by for an early lunch, and luckily there was no wait.  We chose this restaurant on a whim, but I'm glad we did because I was immediately struck by the great service and distinct atmosphere.  The patterned wallpaper, funky decor, and hanging lights make the ambience eccentric yet cohesive.  The bar in the middle of the restaurant is surrounded by tables, the booths especially are quite the vibe.  Trademark would be a great place to have a work function, a lively night with friends, or a romantic date.  I wish I had caught the name of our friendly server, because she was very helpful during our meal.  I ordered the Friday lunch special fish tacos, which I cannot recommend enough.  The juicy fish is covered in a crispy batter and paired with a uniquely flavored guacamole.  Its taste is one of a kind.  This is a super versatile American restaurant with a fresh atmosphere, friendly service, and delicious food.  It was really lucky that we wandered into Trademark for lunch, and I would love to try dinner with drinks here sometime!

Title: A Disappointing Return to a Once-Favorite Spot

I recently revisited an old haunt I frequented during my time in New York, only to be met with a series of unfortunate changes and a jarring experience. Gone is the spacious interior I remembered, replaced by a cramped dining area bisected by an odd wall, presumably part of a misguided renovation effort.

Upon arrival, the welcome was anything but warm. The hostess bluntly informed us of a 50-minute wait for any order—a startling head's up that set the tone for the rest of the visit. Despite the advance warning, we decided to stay, a decision we soon questioned given the staff's apparent indifference.

The restaurant now seems to prioritize delivery orders, a fact made evident by the constant parade of Uber Eats couriers. After a 35-minute wait, my 'hippie ramen' arrived with undercooked noodles, while my friends' meals lagged even further behind, with no explanation or apology offered. Only after confronting our waitress—whose service was as underwhelming as the food—did we receive complimentary tea and fried rice as a meager attempt at amends.

While the fried rice was admittedly tasty and my friends enjoyed their red ramen, no dish could compensate for the poor service and the overall negative atmosphere. It's with regret that I say this former gem has lost its luster, and I won't be returning.

I recently dined at Porteno and, as always, had a wonderful experience. The salads are consistently delicious, with the shredded chicken salad being a personal favorite. What stands out each visit, however, is the exceptional service. Despite its cozy size, we've never encountered trouble finding a seat, even during the busy lunch rush.

This time, we indulged in the pear tart, which was sublime – an absolute must-try. We also sampled the burrata, which, though not listed on the menu, was graciously prepared for us upon request, and a trio of savory empanadas.

Porteno never fails to impress with its quaint atmosphere and superb offerings. Whether you're a regular or a first-timer, you're in for a treat. Thank you, Porteno, for yet another memorable meal!

Title: Cozy Comforts with a Price - A 3.8-Star Experience

My recent visit to this restaurant left me with a solid impression—it's a 3.8-star venue in my book, where good service and satisfying food reign. The chefs here clearly know their way around the kitchen, ensuring each dish is both tasty and comforting. While the presentation is modest, the flavors more than make up for it.

The menu boasts a diverse range of options, complemented by an appealing selection of drinks. However, be prepared to make a reservation, as the place buzzes with patrons consistently.

The portions strike the right balance, being neither too small nor excessively generous. Noteworthy mentions include the hearty pot pie, succulent burgers, and a crispy cod sandwich that's simply divine.

While I do recommend visiting for its culinary delights, the pricing might make you think twice about becoming a regular. It's the perfect "try at least once" spot or a venue for the occasional indulgence, rather than a weekly haunt.

The Smith is an excellent place to eat and drink at! It's a must try restaurant. The food is amazing, as are the drinks. The atmosphere of the restaurant is really cool with subway tiles throughout the restaurant. Has a mix of tables for multiple party sizes, as well as a nice bar area. Wait could be up to an hour, but if there are bar seats, grab them and eat!The restaurant is located in the city, so there are garages and parking lots around. However, easiest would be to Uber, taxi or subway.

Loved this place!Came here for my birthday, and it was so great! I was here for dinner. I was in the area, and found this place. I ordered a hamburger (Linen Burger), and it was so good!This restaurant is super cute and cozy, too. There were lots of people just hanging out at the bar drinking. There is also outdoor seating as well. The burger I had was amazing and delicious. I'm so glad I came here!I would definitely come back here again. This is in a super convenient area and the service was great, as well.

If it wasn't for the BOGO deal, the ramen here would not be worth it!This is a no tip place as you order by the checkout first before your ramen comes. I did the "Build Your Own Ramen" for $7 (normally $14!) My ramen consisted of original noodle (they have different flavors for an additional price!), miso base, pork chashu, half boiled egg, shitake mushroom, spinach, and bamboo shoots.The ramen had all kinds of weird flavors. The half boiled egg was too salty, the shitaki mushroom was too sweet, and the pork chashu was pretty dry. The gelato, which you can get through check-in, fortunately tasted better. It had a nice creamy texture to it. Overall, the place felt really spacious and the staff was super friendly. But food wise, I would look elsewhere for better ramen.

Came here for new years eve dinner with a reservation for two.Our table was cramped near a bunch others and to get in an out of your seat you basically had to shove your ass in somebody else's face and food. They clearly put out more tables to make more money on this day.Our server was very nice and funny, cracking jokes constantly. Food... a waiter came with some butter and very cold and stale bread that was the size of my little finger. That was it, never came again nor asked if we want some more. Should have been a sign... We started with an appetizer, had the burrata salad, the tomatoes to cheese ratio was off... give me more tomatoes god damnit! But the burrata was good. I got the New York strip medium well (no, I dont want to hear it) that came out more medium rare. My partner had the filet mignon medium rare that came out rare AF. Being a steakhouse, dont even imagine that at $70 a piece, you'll get a side. We ordered some brussel sprouts and spinach. All of the above was mediocre. Besides the fact that the steak did not come out as requested and we had to send it back.. it wasnt anything mind blowing, especially not really worth the price tag. The only reason I am giving this place a two star instead of one, is the dessert. We shared a slice of coconut cake which was indeed delicious. Maybe they should rebrand themselves as a bakery or something, cause they aren't any good with meat!

Upon my recent visit to the buzzed-about taco spot, anticipation was high as the queue suggested culinary delights awaited. Alas, the reality was somewhat lackluster; the tacos served were undoubtedly decent, yet they hardly justified the premium pricing—a trait seemingly shared by any number of taco joints.

On a positive note, the topping bar was a highlight, offering an assortment of salsas, hot sauces, and fresh lime to personalize your plate. It's an engaging touch that brought an added layer of enjoyment to the meal.

The drink selection, mirroring the food, was satisfactory but not extraordinary. In summary, while this place offers a convenient taco fix within the market's vibrant atmosphere, the price point leaves you pondering the value. Next time, my curiosity may lead me to explore alternative culinary options.

The restaurant provides a cozy haven for comfort food lovers, offering a delightful array of affordable, homemade mac & cheese that outshines any grocery store variety. With winter's chill in the air, their warm, cheesy bowls of goodness are a perfect remedy. Patrons have the luxury of crafting their unique mac & cheese creations or selecting from a tempting menu of signature dishes. Moreover, the ordering process, facilitated through tablets, allows for a relaxed, leisurely selection of options and toppings. This place is a must-visit for anyone craving a cheesy pick-me-up.

Title: A Birthday Feast to Remember at a Bustling Eatery

I celebrated my birthday at this gem of a restaurant and, while they don't offer birthday freebies, the experience was delightful. The diverse menu catered perfectly to both my partner's and my palate, providing a satisfactory range of choices that were both reasonably priced and generously portioned.

The Yelp waitlist is a must to circumvent the inevitable crowd — this place is a hotspot for good reason. One dish that truly stands out is the Kimchi Cream Udon. Approaching it with high expectations and a dose of skepticism, I was pleasantly surprised to find the dish surpassing its hype. It packed an unapologetically bold, spicy flavor that kimchi enthusiasts will cherish. Easily my top recommendation and a deciding factor for future visits.

The tender, mouthwatering ribs with their addictive sauce also made a lasting impression. We started off with the tofu and avocado, which was a refreshing albeit less remarkable appetizer. The seasonal roll featuring eel, avocado, and tempura was decent but paled in comparison to the other standout options.

All in all, the food was a hit and the meal was a joy. I'm already looking forward to the next visit.

Wu's is a standout among Asian dining spots in the city, a fact my friends and I can attest to after a delightful dinner experience there. The restaurant buzzed with a welcoming vibe, packed with patrons savoring their meals.

The highlight of the visit had to be the wonton soup and crispy pork, each dish channeling the authentic flavors of Hong Kong. The duck served in pillowy soft buns also deserves a special mention for its remarkable taste. Wu's extensive menu promises a culinary adventure, leaving me eager to explore more of their offerings.

Vegetarians need not feel left out; the stir-fried vegetables are a testament to the kitchen's prowess in delivering scrumptious plant-based options. Although I didn't get to try the seafood, the rave reviews from other diners suggest it's worth a return visit.

As a quirky bonus, Wu's sells branded hats in pink and black, perfect for fans who want to showcase their affinity for what is undoubtedly one of my top 10 New York City restaurants.

Title: Cozy Labor Day Lunch at Ajisen Ramen

Despite the rainy weather on Labor Day, my dining companion and I ventured into Ajisen Ramen during a bustling late lunch hour. The restaurant was lively, yet we found reprieve at the quieter bar area.

As a party of two, we sampled the Spicy Ajisen Ramen alongside the elusive Ajisen Deluxe. Initially, the broth seemed lackluster, failing to impress with its mild flavor. However, the noodles were an unexpected delight, coated with a mysterious, flavor-enhancing ingredient. When these savory noodles were swirled into the broth, they magically transformed it into a rich and satisfying accompaniment.

Though the broth's initial presentation left something to be desired, the condiments and toppings redeemed the dishes. The chashu was expertly salted, melting in the mouth, while the spicy ground pork added an addictive kick to the ramen. The marinated eggs were flavorful, albeit slightly overdone.

For those looking to satisfy a ramen craving, Ajisen Ramen is certainly worth a visit. An added perk was a complimentary mochi, awarded for checking in—a sweet end to a savory meal, with green tea, red bean, and vanilla options.

Overall, Ajisen Ramen earns a solid 4 out of 5 stars, with my recommendation for anyone in search of a bowl filled with salty, spicy goodness.

We had a mixed experience. I called ahead and made a reservation with special instructions but the restaurant did not have these instructions because when you call to make a reservation it's made with corporate customer service not with the restaurant so communication was lost.After the hostess called corporate to get the proper instructions for my visit, the visit got better. The tuna tartare was delicious and yummy with a cranberry vodka.Of course you can't come here without trying the steak. Don't leave without trying the steak. I think the most adorable cut of steak is about $50-$70. The ambiance is fun, loud music, and nyc socialites. We didn't stay long but the waiter told us that they have dance parties later in the night.

Tucked away on Greenwich Ave, this adorable brunch spot offers a warm, homey vibe perfect for a casual meal. I opted for a brunch special featuring eggs, tortillas, and guacamole - all of which were fresh and generously portioned. My boyfriend enjoyed a juicy, flavorful burger. Both dishes were satisfying and well-prepared. If you're in the area and craving homestyle brunch or a hearty burger, this spot is a must-visit.

Cute and quaint Mediterranean restaurant! The tapas were perfect as we were in need of a quick, yet hearty meal. The dishes were appropriately sized and super delicious. The service was quick, noise level manageable and love that this spot isn't trying to do too much. Definitely recommend dropping by if you're in the area and in the mood for Mediterranean (also has outdoor seating!). Would recommend getting reservations in advance as every table was full.

It's not bad but it's not mind blowing. It deserves more than 3 stars but less than 4. So we'll round up. Place is tiny and food is okay. A lot of atypical ramen flavors but that's the great thing about it. Curious mind can try different styles versus your typical tonkatsu or miso. The yuzu wings looked like they were butchered from malnourished chickens. That or they cut the wing in half and fried it. I couldn't tell. The spicy yuzu was good but it sounds better than it tastes. You know when you sip on an akumaru modern at ippudo and you go ahhhh... umami. You don't get the same reaction here. The truffle ramen was very salty and only tasted a tad like truffle. Yeah... use of truffle oil is garbage and restaurants over charge but chemically created truffle is still good damn it. It doesn't give you the same truffle burst like a truffle pasta would so its eh ok. I wouldn't pay $21 for this thing again though.

Tucked away near Penn Station, this diminutive eatery is the epitome of a quick-stop breakfast spot for commuters on the go. With time against me, I opted for The Classic sandwich, a blend of breakfast essentials priced around $6, and paired it with a crispy hashbrown for an additional $2. Swapping bacon for avocado was a hassle-free change that added a creamy texture to the sandwich without any extra cost.

However, the sandwich itself was a letdown - it lacked the warmth and tenderness one hopes for in a freshly made bun. The hashbrown was the saving grace of the meal, delivering a satisfying crunch that complemented the main course. The service was efficient and friendly which partially made up for the average fare. Although it was an adequate pit stop for a hurried morning, this place might not see me return for a second round.

Finally I get to write about our Anniversary dinner last Saturday at Manhatta. In a word, OUTSTANDING. I'd give a standing ovation to the entire team if I could, well actually, there was one guy who was in charge of leading us to the elevator who wasn't particularly thrilled to welcome us, perhaps an outlier, so I'll brush him off to give credit where it's due: Danny Meyer (I'm a fan and have been to many of his restaurants already), General Manager, Head Chef and Kitchen Staff, Beverage Team, and our server that evening David, who was really wonderful and attentive. First off, Lauren helped us and was able to move the original weekend lunch schedule to dinner, understanding that this was for an anniversary celebration. She also noted that she will do her best to relay the message that we wanted to be seated by the window for the spectacular views. Both happened and we couldn't be more grateful.We got there 30 minutes prior to our reservation so we got a glass of Champagne each to enjoy the fantastic views from the bar. Once the table was ready, we were ushered in, greeted Happy Anniversary upon being seated and given time to enjoy the moment, the view and to decide what we wanted from the many delicious choices. We were given fresh bread with butter from Normandy, anchovies from Sicily, etc. Delicious, you'd end up wanting more and they offered, but we we're saving some room for the actual courses. I got Foie Gras Reuben for my first course, hubby got the Lobster Quenelle. Both divine and may I say, generous. I've been to France many times and they executed the Foie Gras in perfection! Second course, husband had the Wagyu Beef while I had the Crescent Duck and both were incredible. Can I just say too, I'm not a duck person but went for it, knowing that it would turn out delicious and they delivered! I would in a heartbeat, go back just for this duck dish. The way they included a thin layer of crispy skin created such difference and mouthwatering goodness! As for the dessert, my husband went for the warm date cake while I had the hazelnut soufflé. Unbelievable. I actually thought my dessert was the best of the night until I tasted my husband's dessert. Honestly, I couldn't even taste the dates in it. It's that good! And that vanilla ice cream on top just made it all the more incredible. We also ordered a bottle of champagne and bottle service was simply fantastic! In summary, nothing was spared. Did we pay more than $300? Yes! Did we think it was a lot of money? Without a doubt. Was it worth it? Absolutely YES. Will we go back? In a heartbeat! It was an extraordinary evening and while the views were out of this world beautiful and certainly one of the reasons to go (hello dining 60 floors above New York City!), the food and the service were all above par! Thank you for making our Anniversary dinner one for the books, Manhatta Team! And thanks for the additional cookies! Still dreaming about all of it! Cannot wait to come back again the soonest!

Title: A Bite of Seafood Heaven at Luke's Lobster

Review:
My recent trip to Luke's Lobster was nothing short of celestial. At first glance, the $18 lobster roll seemed steep, but it's definitely on my list for a special occasion. Instead, I settled for the shrimp roll, which was a more wallet-friendly option at $9.80 (tax included).

Admittedly, I would've preferred my shrimp heated up, but even so, the combination of the cold, succulent shrimp with the warm, buttered, and perfectly toasted roll was divine. The flavors and textures harmonized beautifully in each bite.

The staff at Luke's deserves a shout-out too. One of the employees took the time to guide me through the menu and pricing with extraordinary patience – a big plus for a first-timer like me.

I enjoyed the communal seating arrangement, promptly finding a clean spot to dig into my meal. The relaxed vibe made it a delightful alternative to the usual grab-and-go hot dog when I'm around the neighborhood.

Having tried Luke's by Bryant Park, I'm now curious about the location in the Upper East Side. But no matter which Luke's I end up at, the experience is bound to be a treat. For seafood enthusiasts who appreciate delicious bread too, Luke's Lobster is a must-visit. Yum indeed!

This place is not what it used to be. Stopped in for happy hour with a friend and we were not pleased.From drinks to food---everything was meh. We ordered calamari and sweet potato fries. The calamari was tough. Either it was over cooked or just old. And the fries, I don't understand how fries can be bad. We were not pleased. The staff is friendly though but I think they need to step up the food

I recently had the pleasure of sampling Bareburger's offerings when they catered lunch at our NY office. Stepping away from the usual fast food options, their commitment to organic and environmentally-friendly ingredients caught my attention. I opted for something different and tried the Farmstead, a vegan delight disguised as a burrito. This wasn't your typical fare; it was a medley of sweet potato, kale, wild rice patties, hummus, tomatoes, and drizzled with a basil avocado dressing, all neatly bundled in collard green leaves.

At only 380 calories, this burrito packed a punch of flavor without weighing me down. It was filling, and I was pleasantly surprised by how much I enjoyed it. It definitely overturned my initial skepticism.

After seeing my coworkers tuck into their burgers, I have to say, I'm tempted to return and sink my teeth into one of Bareburger's actual burgers. If they're anything like the Farmstead, I'm in for a treat.

I've always been a big fan of afternoon tea with my girl friends. Came here with a Japanese friend visiting New York. As there are a lot of fancy afternoon tea places in Tokyo(her hometown) and Shanghai (my hometown), we normally don't appreciate the overpriced afternoon tea quality in New York (no offense, but that is the fact). We were intrigued by the decoration of this place, contemporary and artistic. The service was pretty attentive, they have "Pink Tea" for this month to support the breast cancer awareness the waiter explained that there would be a big party coming for the same afternoon tea. Therefore if we would like to order that, we need to let them know soon. My friend's host family mom passed away because of breast cancer earlier this year, so we decided to support that. The set was very cute, of course, in pink. The portion was decent, with finger sandwich, scones, and sweets/pastries on the top. $50 per person, including a selection of tea/coffee. I ordered the white peony tea, what a delightful flavor! With the great weather, you can enjoy the view overlooking Columbus circle and Central Park if you are seated in the dining room area. The section close to the entrance is the gallery where you will find a collection of paintings on the wall.We made the reservation through resy, it seems to be a very popular place during the weekend, with family/friends or solo customer enjoying their coffee/tea and spending some time on reading or working.

I recently visited this restaurant for lunch and was impressed by the delicious tonkatsu, which surpassed my expectations. The gyu don was equally satisfying, prepared expertly. I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

During an aimless stroll, we stumbled upon a true hidden gem. Hailing from the south, our barbeque standards are high, yet this place did not disappoint. The brisket served was commendably moist, pairing surprisingly well with the unconventional yet delicious Brussels sprouts. While the collard greens could have benefited from a touch more bacon fat, and the cornbread erred on the side of dryness, the house-made barbecue sauces provided a flavorful remedy, enhancing both the sides and the meat. Overall, this establishment is a delightful discovery for any barbeque aficionado.

There is a line out the door for a $3 cheese slice when there are $1 pizza joints on every other block because this pizza is worth it. Oh so worth it.  Slightly sweet sauce and piping hot cheese that will take the skin off the roof of your mouth if you have problems delaying your gratification and take a bite before you hit the cash register. (Not that I would know from experience. Ouch.). I wanted a white pizza slice but I couldn't risk garlic overload before a client meeting. Since it opens at 10am and closes at 4am, I may be back before my 24 hour NYC trip ends.

Oh..... my... goodness. Minca has completely done me in for ramen in the city and I'll never be the same.I came here after having this place on my list for a while and finding out they serve Tsukemen ramen (dipping style). Exceptional.This is a small restaurant with semi-limited seating, but my group of 3 didn't have a wait on Sunday around 6pm. Also, cash only.The service was beyond amazing and the woman who greeted us/sat us at our table/waited on us was so sweet and helpful. She made sure to explain the different styles of ramen, their recs for type of noodles/etc., and made sure no one had allergies.The tsukemen ramen was incredible. I had the cold, thick, wavy noodles and the broth was a pork/chicken base with fish powder. A soft boiled egg, green onions, bamboo shoots, corn, and pork came with it (served on the side). The broth truly made the dish for me -- rich but not overpowering, so flavorful, not watery or too garlicky... can't recommend enough.

Shinshi Ramen ranks among one of the top ramen spots in Midtown East, if not all of Manhattan for its price point. Despite the ample competition in the area, Shinshi absolutely stands out in terms of taste, service, and general experience. I came here for a Sunday lunch to find the spacious restaurant mostly deserted. I'm sure this is a popular spot among the weekday lunch crowd, but it's definitely a good option if you want a quick, casual bite to eat on a weekend.Our friendly server recommended the Spicy Miso Ramen and the Shoyu Ramen as the two most popular dishes. My fiancé ordered the spicy miso, medium heat level, while I went a bit off the beaten path and got the Saba Tsukemen, which I haven't seen on most other ramen menus. The spicy miso, which I tried a few bites of, was super flavorful and perfectly seasoned. I normally avoid ordering miso-flavored ramen because it's almost always too salty/overpowering, but this one was creamy and nutty. The Saba dipping ramen was also so tasty! The sauce was extremely rich and thick, and clung onto every strand of noodle. I saw that a different reviewer complained about it being "too fishy" but you are literally ordering a dish with mackerel (debatedly the fishiest fish) in its name?! If you happen to like that sort of "fishy" umami, definitely get this dish!Overall, Shinshi is a must visit for any ramen lover trekking through the area.

BOTTOM LINE: I like Mike!TIP/S: have the ...WHO: Party of 2WHY: NovemberfestWHAT: (Deets) As a beverage, I had the plum soup on ice...interesting flavors. I enjoyed it. We also had bottomless hot green tea.We had the $99 menuAs a Starter, We chose the popcorn shrimp & cauliflower, calamari (perfectly fried: crispy outside, Chewy inside), fried wings (flats for the win, the batter was delish), the Snow Crab legs seafood boil easily shareable with 2-3 people (if I could only convey how delish the seasonings at the bottom of the bag are...I didn't want to fully wash my hands because the fragrant spices would no longer be evident and sniffable under my nails...sheesh...sooooo good).To complete the meal, sweet orange wedges...from beverages to dessert...yum!Special appreciation to my fellow YES members Estralda and Byron!!WHEN: late lunch time 11/16/19WHERE: dine in HOW: bike/ public transportation D trainBATHROOM: 2 separate rooms, gender neutral WIFI: did not use DRESS CODE: as you likeNOISE LEVEL: quiet to moderateSERVICE: EXCELLENT. I can't say enough about Mike's anticipation of our needs, smiling face, quiet dignity and pleasant demeanor. The 2 other support staff members were also accommodating & responsive to our needs. Kudos all around!

I consider this place a small hidden gem since there aren't many hispanic food options in the area. The food was good, it is ACTUAL Dominican food, the chicken was well seasoned and cooked. The restaurant itself is small so going here with a group doesn't work out well. However if you are around for lunch time and just want a quick bite, sitting here and "people watching" was nice. The workers seemed to lack customer service a bit.

Title: Mixed Experience at Local Korean Eatery

My recent visit to this local Korean restaurant delivered a mixed bag of impressions. While the tofu soup was decently flavored and valued at $16, the highlight was the fresh banchan accompanied by fish—though patrons should be mindful of the bones. 

However, some aspects left much to be desired. Firstly, ensure your entire party is present before arriving, as you'll be placed on a waitlist otherwise. The waiting area proved to be cramped, which could use some rethinking space-wise. 

An unexpected inconvenience was the restaurant's internal temperature; it was quite warm inside. I advise wearing layers during the winter months, as you might end up overheating in a sweater.

Unfortunately, the meal's staple—rice—was undercooked, a significant letdown for an establishment celebrating Korean cuisine. Additionally, the noise level was uncomfortably high, making it challenging to engage in conversation without raising one's voice.

In summary, while there are positive aspects like the fresh banchan, the overall experience could be improved upon, especially considering comfort and meal preparation.

Don't walk, run here! Best Chinese food I've had since living in NYC. There's always a wait, but definitely worth it. The noodles, the dumplings and the service ALL amazing. Fair warning, very limited seating and waiting area. Cannot wait to go back.

Mediocre food and horrible service! You would've thought they were going to get our water from the Hudson for as long as it took for them to bring us a cup. The waitress was beyond inattentive and it was incredibly difficult to even catch her to get our order put in. Then she never came back to our table so we couldn't ask for the rice we wanted, a margarita, literally anything after the first order which still took her 30 minutes to come back to our table to get. It wasn't busy or anything so they had zero excuse for why the service was so crappy. The food overall was mediocre at best. Wouldn't recommend.

Nestled amidst the bustling charm of Hudson Yards lies a delightful Spanish culinary gem reminiscent of the famed Eataly, but with a distinctive Iberian twist. Mercado, a sit-down treasure within a larger gastronomic haven, beckons food lovers with its bar-style seating and a mouthwatering array of tapas.

The service is commendable, as attentive staff make it their mission to guide patrons through the eclectic menu, enriching the dining experience with their knowledge and recommendations. An extensive selection of alcohol is available, thoughtfully curated to complement the variety of flavors each dish offers.

Mercado's tapas selection shines with several standouts, including the potato cheese croquettes—irresistibly crispy on the outside with a heavenly soft, molten cheese core. The chicken skewers, prepared a la plancha, steal the show with their succulent tenderness and robust seasoning. Equally impressive is the ox tail, bathing in a rich, reduced wine sauce that enhances its succulence. Seafood enthusiasts will revel in the garlic shrimp, an aromatic delight that promises to tantalize the palate.

Not to be overlooked, the veal pork meatballs offer a hearty satisfaction, and the classic combination of jamón and cheese pressed sandwiches will undoubtedly gratify those in search of comfort fare. To elevate your dining adventure, indulge in the recommended rosé—a choice pairing that effortlessly harmonizes with the array of savory bites.

With a promise of return, this review closes on a high note, affirming that Mercado is a destination that warrants repeated visits for anyone in pursuit of authentic Spanish tapas with a touch of culinary sophistication.

During a quest for a breakfast spot, we stumbled upon this quaint place without a wait, which was a pleasant surprise. The seating arrangement was a bit cramped though—the tables small and the walkways narrow, something to note for guests valuing space.

Opting for the French toast with fresh fruit add-ons seemed promising, despite the rather steep price of around $22 per person, sans beverages. While the toast itself hit the mark, the fresh fruit provided a delightful touch. The disappointment, however, lay in the "maple syrup" served alongside. It was a far cry from even the average fake syrup I've tasted; not sweet, seemingly watered-down. Although real maple syrup is available for an extra charge, one wouldn't expect the default option to be lacking.

In conclusion, the meal was decent but didn't quite justify the cost, especially given the abundance of superior breakfast options in NYC at a similar price point.

Title: Mixed Feelings on Burger Delivery

I recently opted for delivery from this restaurant and received my order promptly, with food arriving hot – a good start. I went with their Custom 1/2lb burger, a basic selection with lettuce, tomato, onion, and a side of fries. My only extra was beer cheese, but at $15 for the meal, the price felt a tad excessive, especially given the modest portion of fries.

The burger, while sizable, didn't quite hit the mark. The beer cheese, unfortunately, didn't travel well, arriving somewhat dislodged from the burger, and taste-wise, it didn't impress. I would give the cheese a miss next time. Additionally, though I requested the burger medium, it showed up rare – a significant discrepancy, though I managed to eat it regardless. The burger itself lacked juiciness, and the bun was disproportionately large for my taste, accompanied by a single large lettuce leaf.

In conclusion, the burger experience was underwhelming and didn't justify the price. While I am not deterred from the restaurant entirely, the burger won't be making a reappearance in my future orders. I might consider trying a different menu item next time.

Manero's might be some of the best pizza I've ever had, at least in nyc. And being from Chicago, I've had some good pizza! So far I've had the plain cheese slice which was incredible. The sauce was garlicy heaven and the tomato in it really pops. The crust was also on point with a perfect crunch but still chewy and soft on the inside. Then I've had the Sicilian slice, which I think they don't make until later in the afternoon but is so worth the wait. It's huge, at least two inches thick, and the crust is so soft on the inside. Seriously, stop what you're doing and come here.

Despite an extremely unpleasant experience last summer and one of the most unprofessional managers, I decided to give Blue Fin another chance last night on a spontaneous date night with the hubby. And it was positively delightful. The food delicious. The service, attentive and professional. Because we were catching a show, we were a little short on time. So we kept things simple. We decided to sit downstairs (given our last visit). Nile is excellent. Good at his job. And the young man at the host stand could not have been more welcoming. THAT'S how guests should be treated. The chef's selection of oysters were wonderful and one of the reasons I first came to Blue Fin. The appetizer special tuna tartare with caviar was so good. I'm glad I decided to rise above and not let one bad moment ruin what otherwise has always been a great place for dinner and top-shelf oysters.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Southeast Asian Flavors with Stellar Service

My friends and I arrived at this highly-anticipated restaurant with excitement, our expectations fueled by its buzz on platforms like Buzzfeed Worth It and Yelp, not to mention it being Michelin recommended. The service did not disappoint; we were seated quickly and attended to by a very helpful waitress who provided us with spot-on recommendations. I also appreciated the spotless state of the bathroom.

The ambiance was reminiscent of a vibrant Asian street food market, complete with hanging signs and walls adorned with newspapers. However, the food experience was a bit of a roller coaster. The Thai Iced Tea and Teh Tarik were delightful, each earning a solid 4/5, while the Sweet Ginger Tea was overwhelmingly sweet and missed the mark at 2/5.

We enjoyed the light and flaky texture of the Curry Puffs, but the Roti Canai didn't live up to its full potential without the traditional chicken or potato in the curry. As for the mains, the Hainanese Chicken, which usually boasts a soft, steamed texture, was unexpectedly roasted/fried, leading to some dryness. The Curry Laksa featured in Buzzfeed proved to be non-spicy and dominated by a coconut milk flavor, possibly catering to those with milder palates.

Having traveled from Queens, I can't say the journey was justified by the food alone, as other local eateries offer better taste at a lower price. If you find yourself in the vicinity with a craving for Malay, Singaporean, or Thai cuisine, this establishment might satisfy with its pleasant environment and commendable service.

I recently ventured into the realm of Filipino dining with a Kamayan feast at a local restaurant, booked by my friend days in advance. Opting for the basic pre-fixe menu, the experience was nothing short of extraordinary.

Laid out before us was a Filipino banquet where the tradition is to eat with your hands, immersing ourselves in the conviviality of shared plates. The Banana Ketchup Ribs, Adobong Hipong, and Adobong Manok highlighted the meat offerings, each dish bursting with flavor, succulent and satisfyingly hands-on.

The only misstep was the rice, which was disappointingly dry, reminiscent of scraping the last crumbs from a chip bag. The meal concluded with Halo-Halo, a generously portioned and delightful dessert easily shared between two.

For anyone looking to dive into a unique culinary adventure with friends, I wholeheartedly recommend this Kamayan feast. It's not just a meal; it's an experience.

I had an early dinner at Kaoru which was lovely. I came to the place to built my own bowl as I am fascinated with this concept of eating.  I had Uni(Sea Urchin) Don with add ons, Tuna and squid.  The fish was very clean tasting it melted in mouth.  It came over a bed of rice with was fine.  My suggestion is to cut down on the rice and add some lettuce the meal will feel even lighter.  Nevertheless my eating experience at this restaurant was awesome, I would go back in the. future.
Steak was excellent.  In our party everyone enjoyed their meal.  Sides were good.   Desserts were fine also.  Did not like policy of seating everyone at tables next to each other.   Service was good.

Title: Pleasant Surprise at Vegetarian Haven

I recently ventured into a local vegetarian spot for lunch, despite not being a vegetarian myself, and was thoroughly surprised. The plant-based twist on General Tso's was a taste revelation—convincingly replacing chicken with a delicious alternative that left me more than satisfied. As I dined later in the lunch hour, the ambiance was calm, complementing the very American-Chinese decor.

The value was exceptional, with lunch specials priced around $10, including a fried veggie spring roll. While the spring roll's filling was a touch too uniform in texture for my taste, craving a bit of crunch amidst the mush, it was still a delightful addition to the meal.

In conclusion, my experience was positive enough to warrant a return visit. This spot has certainly broadened my lunchtime horizons.

I recently visited a local eatery known for its personal-sized pizzas and decided to try their Margherita. To their credit, the pizzas are made to order and feature a pleasingly thin dough, which is ideal for those mindful of their carb intake. However, the crust deviated from the authentic pizza experience I was craving. While the overall flavor was decent, the balance of cheeses missed the mark, with an overabundance of Parmesan overshadowing the traditional mozzarella one would expect on a classic Margherita.

On our final day in New York, we dined at George's. The experience was average, with both the food and service failing to impress. My meal was unremarkable, lacking any distinct qualities that would merit particular praise.

At this restaurant, the culinary experience was commendable, particularly the Berkshire pork, which delighted with its perfect crunch and balanced fattiness. The Katsu don was another highlight, with its excellently cooked egg and flavorful rice combination. However, the dining experience was marred by the evident understaffing, manifesting in an almost non-existent service. With only one floor staff visible, attention to diners was lacking, as patrons seemed abandoned, having to solicit their bills actively. Although the venue wasn't bustling with guests, service remained sluggish. While the food scores high marks, be prepared for a service that might test your patience. If unhurried meals are your tempo and culinary quality trumps service in your book, this could still be a worthy destination.

The soup broths was a bit bland so I had to put in chili oil for more flavor. The handcut noodles' texture was quite varied - some parts of a noodle was firm and others were mushy. I liked it but my girlfriend didn't.The beef is leagues better than the lamb option.The fried dumpling were excellent.

Love the decor, music and their ambiance. This is rare gem in Washongton Heights. They recently renovated and did a great job with their interior. I came for brunch and enjoyed the crab cake benedicts. I'll be back to take advantage of their 1.5 hour bottomless brunch one day.

My quest for a swift vegetarian dinner near Chelsea Market led me to Co Ba, and I wasn't let down. Their menu boasts an impressive array of vegan and vegetarian dishes. I opted for the soup vermicelli with vegetable broth—a rarity—and the Vegi LoMein, both of which had a notably fresh and flavorful taste. The service matched the quality of the food, with our server being exceptionally friendly and accommodating. Co Ba comes highly recommended for a great dining experience!
