This review is as of Feb 2019.It's been a while since I ate here last and I'm sad to say the quality of the food has really deteriorated from really good to quite average.The pine nut fish we ordered didn't taste very fresh.  The fried eel was really fishy.  The carp appetizer didn't taste quite right.  The lotus root sticky rice was too bland.  The only item I really enjoyed was the Yan Du Xian soup.Finally, the service wasn't great.  We sat at a booth and it was very hard to flag down any waiters.  We waited a long time for the entrees, after we had finished all of our starters.  No one cleared our plates after we finished the meal.  The waiter forgot one of our orders.  Desserts were brought without any utensils or plates, and we had to ask someone else to bring them.Overall the experience was pretty disappointing.  I don't know if it's just that the head chef went back to Shanghai for Chinese New Year or something.  But it was a bit of a surprise given our past good experiences.  Hoping it was just a one off.

Title: A Tale of Three Dishes at Popular Ramen Spot

My recent visit to the much-lauded ramen restaurant had me sample the talk-of-the-town pork buns, which, frankly, fell short of the communal adoration they seemed to garner on Yelp. They were decent, but not the show-stopper I was led to believe.

The shin tantan-men, however, lived up to its fiery reputation—deliciously so. Be warned, it's a dish that will test your spice tolerance, as I found myself waving the white flag mid-slurp, overwhelmed by the heat.

Finally, the shiromaru hakata classic was a pleasant surprise. As someone who often finds ramen broths overpowering, Ippudo's version was flavorful yet mild enough to prevent the dreaded broth-induced headache, making it an enjoyable experience.

All in all, if you're up for a spicy challenge or seeking a subtler broth that won't leave you reeling, this ramen spot is worth a visit. Just don't expect to be blown away by the pork buns.

I recently visited Gammeeok, a hidden gem nestled on the 2nd floor, accessible only by stairs, and I must say, it never disappoints when I'm in the mood for authentic Korean comfort food. Open 24/7, its convenience is unmatched.

My latest visit on a Sunday afternoon proved to be as satisfying as always. Despite arriving at the usual lunchtime rush around 1:30 pm, my friend and I were promptly seated without a wait. We both opted for the Sogogi Gukbap, a spicy ox-bone broth with tender beef brisket and a medley of vegetables. At $12, not only is it a steal for the portion size, but the rich, full-flavored broth is a true palate pleaser.

The meal is accompanied by a simple selection of banchan, including some of the freshest kimchi and radish kimchi I've come across. The staff, from the kimchi cutter spreading cheer with each slice to the attentive manager, provided impeccable service, readily topping up our kimchi upon request.

Our bill totaled around $26 after tax, which, considering the quality and quantity of the meal, presents as excellent value. Gammeeok continues to be a top choice for me, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

We came here to celebrate a friends birthday, group of 6.All dishes ordered from menu were really satisfying, including appetizers and dessert - very well executed and delicious ... except my meat - it was a bit chewy and fatty. But over all the dining experience was great! Place is cozy and has very nice family feel to it. Love the decor - exposed brick all around and very well thought design.Service was very attentive and staff was on point.

Yin Ji is overrated. The chang fen skin is great, but the overall final product is mediocre. It is smooth and thin and the filling is generous. This is where things get messy. I like my noodles to stay intact and the filling to noodle ratio is absolutely horrible. There's too much filling inside the noodles that everything just breaks apart. I know some appreciate the generous fillings, but is it really "generous"? A Chang fen is like $7 here! They can easily use more noodles for the excessive amount of filling to balance things out. I do have to admit that I did enjoy the beef and shrimp noodle - the beef was tender and shrimp fresh. However, don't get the cha siu - Cha siu is so dry that I can't even. Their congee options are plentiful and the congee itself is huge with a lot of protein. One thing that is lacking in the congee and the noodles is salt though. Everything here is bland.

Title: A Hearty Feast with a Side of Space Crunch

I recently visited this renowned hotpot restaurant with a group of five friends. We ambitiously ordered two deluxe meat platters, a seafood set, cold dishes, crawfish fried rice, and additional meat and noodles – a feast recommended by our enthusiastic server.

The quality of the meat, particularly the Kobe beef, was impeccable, tender and worth every praise. Although famous for hotpot, the restaurant's cold dishes and crawfish fried rice were surprisingly delightful. We chose the Yin and Yang broth; note the "mild" spicy is not for the faint-hearted, yet its rich flavor is irresistible.

However, the dining experience was slightly marred by the cramped seating. Too little space meant our abundant order was accommodated on rolling carts that inconvenienced both us and our fellow diners. Also, a solitary restroom by the kitchen proved inadequate for the bustling establishment.

Despite the spatial issues, the food alone makes this spot a must-visit for any hotpot aficionado. Just be mindful of how much you order and be prepared for a bit of a wait if nature calls.

Title: A Culinary Dream Where Every Bite is Memorable

From the multitude of dining experiences I've had, it's a rare gem to find a place that is beyond reproach, and yet, this restaurant has nailed it. With a delectable fusion menu that weaves together Chinese, Peruvian, and Spanish cuisines, each dish I've savored here continues to linger in my memory.

Service? Nothing short of top-notch, with waitstaff effortlessly accommodating in both English and Spanish, always adding to the pleasant ambiance. The robust drinks complement the meals perfectly – take the Nutcracker, for instance; it's a must-try that guarantees satisfaction with its potency.

My personal favorite, the Pollo a La Brasa paired with the house special fried rice, is consistently cooked to perfection – succulent to the last bite. The Lomo Saltado, another standout dish, won't disappoint either, as my partner can attest.

This restaurant feels like home, and its impact on my dining experiences is indelible. I'm already eagerly anticipating my next visit and encourage you to discover the same joy in their outstanding offerings.

Great Thai Food, sooo tasty too!I love Thai Food and its exotic flavors.  I ordered the Pra Ram with Tofu and rice and OMG it was so delicious I even finished the entire dish!  Also, their passion fruit mojito is really good and refreshing and enjoyable.  We got there around 6:30pm so there wasn't really a wait line and we got our tables right away, we did not wait.  Given that I'm a little claustrophobic (just a little bit), the place is small and the tables are way too close to each other it feels more of like a family dinner than a private one lol.  No big deal, the food made it all worth it. The place is small but very cozy and it has a warm environment.  It is nicely decorated but again too crowded.  By the time we were done, the entrance was very crowded it could seem like a journey to reach the exit door.  Other than that it is a great place to eat!  Again the food is good and I recommend!

Navigating to Bar Boulud can be a bit tricky; 1900 Broadway encompasses a group of eateries, so don't rely solely on Google Maps. You'll find it nestled between 63rd and 64th on Broadway—just keep an eye out for The Smith as a landmark from either direction.

During a recent Restaurant Week visit with a friend and her baby, the service at Bar Boulud stood out as exceptionally accommodating. Even when we failed to specify our cooking preference for the salmon, the staff handled it with grace and professionalism.

However, the cuisine didn't quite match the high standards set by the service. Anticipating excellence from a French restaurant associated with Daniel Boulud, the bread and butter were disappointingly ordinary, failing to impress as much as those from establishments like Marc Forgione. The chilled corn soup started strong but lost its appeal quickly. My coq au vin sandwich, while accompanied by exceptional fries, was surprisingly lacking in flavor despite the promise of fried and braised dark meat, leaving me to whimsically compare it to a Chick-fil-A offering.

In summary, while Bar Boulud shines in customer service, the food experience falls a notch below what one might expect from a venue of its pedigree.

Title: Cozy Charm with Culinary Ups and Downs at Da Gennaro

Upon entering Da Gennaro, its cute ambiance, warm lighting, and tasteful decor immediately set a welcoming tone for the meal to come. However, the restaurant experience did stumble at the first course; the bread served was an unfortunate miss, being cold and chewy rather than warm and inviting.

The main courses displayed both highs and lows. The Osso Buco stood out as the star of the menu, perfectly cooked so that the veal slipped effortlessly off the bone. Paired with spaghetti, mushrooms, and carrots, it proved to be a hearty and satisfying choice, although a homemade gnocchi option was also available.

In contrast, the Chicken Francese's overpowering citrus flavor dominated the dish, overshadowing the accompanying thin, flat spaghetti and the well-cooked chicken.

Dessert was a mixed bag: the Bomba dessert — a delightful concoction of chocolate and vanilla gelato with a cherry heart — was a surefire hit. On the other hand, the cream puffs failed to impress, with a lackluster cream filling, despite the pleasant chocolate mousse topping.

A special nod goes to the greeter whose warm reception undoubtedly enhanced the experience. However, the dining comfort was dampened by both the subpar condition of the restrooms, which were in dire need of renovation, and the cramped seating arrangement that became particularly challenging when the restaurant was at full capacity.

Overall, while the culinary experience at Da Gennaro had its peaks, it was marred by several inconsistencies that, if addressed, could elevate the dining experience significantly.

I had a delightful dining experience at this eatery last weekend. The outdoor seating was perfect, complementing the classic sports bar ambiance inside. The fried mozzarella balls were a tasty start to the meal, generously sized and delicious. Both the Home Base Burger, with its savory combination of fried pickles, caramelized onions, and barbecue sauce, and the OG, a solid classic cheeseburger, did not disappoint. Generous servings of fries accompanied the burgers, much to my delight. The fried Oreos, each served with a small scoop of ice cream, were a blissful end to the meal. The prices were very reasonable, and the service was impressively swift. I'm certainly planning a return visit.

Title: Cozy Comforts at The Meatball Shop in Hell's Kitchen

My wife and I sought respite from the chilly Saturday evening with a pre-Broadway dinner at The Meatball Shop in Hell's Kitchen, reminiscing about our prior visit to their West Village location. This newer spot offers a distinct atmosphere and an updated menu - gone are the customizable sliders, now replaced with a versatile bowl concept.

With help from our amiable server, I savored a hearty bowl of Spicy Heritage Pork meatballs, atop a creamy polenta base, draped in classic tomato sauce. It proved a perfect blend of flavors and textures, rich and satisfying. My wife's choice of veggie balls with her unique pairing was equally delightful, and the shared Brussel Sprouts were a great complement to our meal. Despite initial doubts, the bowls turned out to be a fulfilling choice that left us content and ready for the night's entertainment.

The Meatball Shop offers a focused yet varied menu, with other entrees if bowls aren't to your taste, including pasta dishes and sandwiches. From our experiences at both locations, the consistent quality stands out—definitely a go-to spot for comfort food that won't disappoint.

I regretfully must advise against patronizing the bar/restaurant my partner and I recently visited. Our intentions were to enjoy the end of a slam dunk contest over some casual drinks and snacks, but the experience fell short of even the most basic expectations. First, the price-to-portion ratio for their Japanese whiskey was laughably disproportionate, served as a minuscule, diluted shot for an exorbitant $23. Further dismay followed with a wait time exceeding an hour for merely three pieces of chicken, all while languishing without any updates from the staff. The apparent manager seemed more invested in his social media presence than managing the establishment. Both my usually undemanding boyfriend and I were left thoroughly unimpressed. Please consider looking up reviews before deciding to spend time and money at this venue. I wholeheartedly do not recommend this place.

EXPERIENCE 4/5Went a Sunday Morning so our wait was ~1 hour which was expected. It's really nice that there's a coffee place right next to it to kill the time. The server was really nice and gave us an assortment of butter (thyme, berry, and lemon).The location itself is really cute and nice as a date setting.FOOD 4/5I shared the egg Benedict with potatoes and chicken and waffles. The eggs benedict was beautifully cooked but I personally didn't really enjoy the rich that much. The shredded chicken was really dry and didn't cut the egg very well (pork/salmon work well because they're a bit more salty.) I recommend asking for the house potatoes to be cooked well done to get them extra crispy. The chicken and waffles were amazing! One of the best I've eaten (and I've tried an assortment in LA) The winner of the dish was definitely the waffles and the syrup. The waffles were the perfect consistency to be eaten with the chicken and the syrup was runny and light.

Stopped in for a jumbo slice of pepperoni after a walk across the park. $7 and a few minutes while pizza was in the oven and I had my slice.  I added some cheese and oregano.Just as good as the first time. A quintessential NY slice.

After two thwarted attempts due to long lines, my persistence to dine at this much-buzzed-about first US location paid off on a Thursday night at 9:30pm with no wait—talk about third time's charm! The culinary star of our meal was undoubtedly the shrimp and pork rice roll with chives, a masterful blend of flavors and textures that transcended the ordinary. While the marinated chicken and chive variant, along with the novel fish with chives, were satisfactory, they paled in comparison to the shrimp and pork's excellence. Despite the temptation for seconds, the kitchen's early closure left us yearning. The experience was delightful, but the potential of a 30-minute line might deter a future visit.

After eagerly anticipating our visit due to the month-long wait for a reservation, our experience at the restaurant fell a touch short of our high expectations. The Tie Dye pizza, with its charming pesto swirl, was enjoyable but didn't quite justify the hype or the wait. The meatballs we ordered alongside were passable, though they landed in the realm of the ordinary. Overall, while the meal was decent, it wasn't the culinary spectacle we had envisioned.

I recently visited this bustling spot for a weekday lunch and was immediately greeted by a crowded scene and a substantial line—a testament to its popularity. The system here is straightforward: order at the counter and find a seat, and the staff will bring the food to your table.

The highlight of my meal was, without a doubt, the lamb pita. It was the best I've ever had, memorable for its moist, well-cooked meat, perfectly balanced spices, and the grilled onions and tomatoes that tied the flavors together beautifully. The falafel sandwich was also tasty, although it seemed to be missing a component—perhaps a dollop of hummus to elevate it further—but it was still above average.

I highly recommend this place to anyone who hasn't had the pleasure of dining here. The food is truly exceptional—awesome, in fact!

Such a cute spot in seaport! Very casual, reasonable prices, and a great place for lunch or brunch! They actually just started their brunch this past weekend! Their fresh lemonade is tart but good! The fried chicken sandwhich was very yummy and the mac n cheese was great! The mac comes in a skillet which traps in the heat and everyone in the restaurant was ordering it! The hummas plate was as to be expected. Service was good and the location was better! Such a cute town to walk around in after you finish eating. I would come back for the views and that mac n cheese!

3.5 stars, I'd say it was a pleasant experience and the atmosphere is nice. We got there at 5:26 and they locked the door until 5:40 because they open at 5:30pm on some days and 5:00 on others. Today they open at 5:30pm and there was only Barr seats available since most people made reservations. Especially if you have a big group or you don't like bar areas, I suggest you make a reservation. Food tastes pretty good and a couple to choose from the menu. The drinks seems cool and they tastes good but the cocktails are pretty sweet and I could barely taste any alcohol and it's like juice for me. Not bad but not worth the money, wish it was much stronger. Walkable from the L train and bus stops. Friendly staffs and a bit noisy but not a place you need to yell on top of your lungs either. Funky place and cute interior, but not a place I'd come back often

Title: A Festive Extravaganza Not to Be Missed in NYC

My recent visit to one of NYC's festive highlights could only be described as a mesmerizing experience. As Christmas approaches, the neighborhood transforms into a winter wonderland, with homes showcasing an array of decorations ranging from the classically elegant to the joyfully flamboyant.

The beauty isn't just in the adornments; the houses themselves are architectural marvels, grand in scale and design. As you walk through the streets or drive by, the warmth of the season is palpable, complemented by the convenience of hot chocolate and snack trucks, thoughtfully placed to enhance the holiday cheer.

Safety and organization courtesy of NYPD add to the comfort, while strategically blocked off streets offer a pedestrian-friendly atmosphere. A tip for future visitors: timing is key – arriving early or late can spare you from the bustling crowds that peak during prime hours.

The standout stars of the neighborhood are undoubtedly the 80s streets, with 82nd, 83rd, and 84th stealing the show. Make sure they are on your itinerary.

In all, this is a quintessential NYC Christmas activity that comes highly recommended. Whether a local or a tourist, be sure to add this to your holiday agenda for an unforgettable experience.

My friend and I were in the area and bumped into this cute as a button pink restaurant! We had heard about it and luckily they were nice enough to accommodate us since we did not have a reservation and it was Saturday evening..The establishment is pretty small, the outside is all pink with a few spots that are great for a quick Instagram photoshoot LOL The host took our coats so we have more room and space to get comfortable, our waiter Alex was very friendly and courteous! I was curious to try the "Rosa" from their cocktail menu and it was pretty good, however the lemon made it a bit bitter.. I was starving so we skipped appetizers and went straight for our meal, I had the Bistecca and it was simply delicious! I highly recommend it, yes it's on the pricey side but worth it! Oh and for dessert I tried their pannacotta and wow I really loved it! I was expecting their food to be ordinary but I was wrong, our only complaint was that the table next to us came a while after but received their food and left before us.. I recommend this place to anyone who is looking for a cute small intimate place that has a nice pink environment for some cute photos, especially if it's a girls day or your teenage daughters birthday!

I really liked XO Kitchen! I thought it would be another chinese restaurant serving the usual chinese dishes that I get, but I found that it was a big fusiony mish mosh in here, which sounds bad, but is actually really tasty food!For example - you can get eel over rice here, you can bulgogi, you can get taiwanese zhong zi with gravy ( which I recommend!!! - YUM ), you can get crispy pineapple shrimp ( also yum!)... you get the idea.So in that way, I find it fun to eat here.

Title: A Thai Delight That Won't Break the Bank

I recently dined at a hidden gem offering excellent Thai cuisine that surpassed my expectations, especially considering the affordable price point. With generous portions that beg to be shared, most dinner dishes peak at a reasonable $12-13. The standout for me was the Khao Soi, rich and savory, while my companions raved about the drunken noodles and classic pad Thai.

The menu caters to all spice lovers, with genuinely respected levels of heat that promise an authentic sweat if you dare to go 'very spicy.' A must-try is the zesty papaya salad, brimming with freshness and complemented by crunchy pork rinds. The crab Rangoon also deserves a mention for its delightful flavors.

Although the Tom Yum soup fell short of the mark for me, appearing rather ordinary, it would not deter me from a repeat visit. In fact, the lunch specials are rumored to be an even greater steal, further elevating this charming spot as an ideal dining destination.

As for their delivery service, it was faultless: timely, well-organized, and with personalized labels—a godsend for group orders. Based on my experience, I wholeheartedly recommend this spot for anyone craving authentic, budget-friendly Thai food. I will definitely be ordering from here again.

My friend and I came here with a reservation for 6:30pm on a Saturday night. The reservation was fairly easy to come by on Resy, though their website states that they are primarily a walk-in restaurant. When I came to the restaurant, I was greeted in a strange manner by one of the hosts, who didn't speak English very well. When I said my name, he gestured strangely in the direction of the table where my friend was, which was a bit confusing. After being seated, a waiter promptly took care of us and we ordered. We shared the tuna ssam bap and the cucumber kimchi to start. Both were good, refreshing and simple dishes, but also something that could be easily created at home. The tuna ssam bap consisted of pieces of tuna atop a bed of rice, with some other garnishes, that we wrapped in the seaweed. The tuna and rice on its own reminded me of poke. The ramyun dishes were presented shortly after. My friend had the gochu ramyun, while I got the miyuk ramyun (vegetarian). Her broth was undoubtedly more flavorsome and tasty than mine. It had the delightful addition of doenjang, which I envied, as I slurped my own bowl of noodles. The broth for the miyuk ramen was light, as stated on the menu. It was still pleasant to eat, but not as good as the gochu. The noodles were soft, but still had good texture, with chewiness. Overall, a good dinner, but I wouldn't say I'm running back to eat here again. Ambience was quite simple, and nothing special.

Title: Disappointing Dining Experience at [Restaurant Name]

My friends and I visited [Restaurant Name] on a Wednesday evening for dinner, eager to try their array of dishes. Upon settling in, we ordered a variety of items including seafood ramen hotpot, tiger roll, wings, a spicy pork rice dish, and roasted vegetables.

Regrettably, my experience fell well below expectations. Starting with the portions, we were taken aback by how diminutive they were, especially given the high price point. The tiger roll, though tasty, consisted of just four pieces for $9 - barely justifying its cost.

The wings, priced a tad more reasonably, suffered a similar fate in quantity—mimicking the size of McDonald's chicken nuggets. Nevertheless, they were flavorful and a highlight of the meal.

The spicy pork dish was a letdown, with heat overpowering any distinct flavors. Moreover, the seafood ramen hotpot presented a bland taste, despite the inclusion of clams and a shrimp.

As for the roasted vegetables, their excessive saltiness only amplified our discontent, particularly given their $9 tag. Ultimately, only the wings and tiger roll managed to elicit any pleasure.

I entered [Restaurant Name] with optimism for a first-time visit but left assured that I would not be returning. The inadequate portion sizes, coupled with lackluster flavors, made for an unsatisfying culinary experience.

Title: A Spirited Gem in Midtown: Taco Dumbo Review

Venturing through the bustling heart of New York, my girlfriend and I, along with a local friend, stumbled upon Taco Dumbo in Midtown, near Times Square. Its reputation as a prime Happy Hour spot was the hook that lured us in, and I must say, the experience was deserving of a solid 4.5 rating.

The moment we entered, the vibe struck a perfect chord, offering an island ambiance that managed to steer clear of feeling overdone. The bar's atmosphere was an instant hit with us, setting the stage for a relaxing unwind after a day of city exploration.

Our bartender welcomed us with exceptional service, both attentive and warm, which only enhanced the laid-back experience. What really stood out at Taco Dumbo was their innovative approach to Happy Hour Margaritas. Instead of the usual offerings, they encouraged us to play mixologist, pairing a variety of tequilas with an assortment of juices and unique rim salts. I'm a traditionalist at heart when it comes to margaritas, but I couldn't help but admire their creative flair.

The highlight, though, came when our bartender, upon learning it was my girlfriend's birthday, treated us to celebratory shots, a gesture that truly capped off the evening.

In short, Taco Dumbo is a refreshing find that marries a cool atmosphere with inventive drinks, all rounded out by terrific service. It's a must-visit for anyone looking for a spirited escape in the heart of Midtown.

We popped in for dinner the other night and had to wait about 10 minutes for a table but it was worth it. We started with pork buns - because they are irresistible, let's face it. These were huge and puffy and served one at time. There was a good amount of filling. You can custom mix your noodle soup with 5 or 6 different noodle options. I got thin rice noodles with chicken broth, triple mushrooms, mixed vegetables and pan friend meat dumplings. The dumplings were the most flavorful part of the soup I got. I added hot sauce and soy sauce and concluded I must have ordered the wrong broth. There just wasn't much flavor. The ingredients were good, but I wasn't wowed. I tried a bit of my friend's Chinese dish that was quite good. I'd try something else, or order from the menu specials next time instead of venturing.

**Vegetarian Review of Glaze: A Mediocre Experience**

Visited Glaze for a vegetarian lunch and left underwhelmed. Their menu boasts veg-friendly items such as tofu and vegetable gyoza, but the execution fell short. The tofu lacked flavor despite the dressing, and the gyoza suffered from a suboptimal texture—hard, not the expected crispy.

I yearn for innovation in their vegetarian offerings, perhaps something along the lines of teriyaki seitan. As for the service, it was unremarkable; not particularly warm but not off-putting either. A point many might agree on, however, is the steep pricing, which hardly seems justified given the overall experience. Consequently, Glaze doesn't make my list for a repeat visit.

Title: A Morning Delight at Spanish Diner

My recent breakfast experience at Spanish Diner was nothing short of exceptional. Despite its name, this is not your average diner food. They open their doors bright and early at 7am, and I must say, their breakfast is absolutely bomb!

On my visit, I indulged in a warming Café con leche and a deliciously flaky chocolate croissant – both were outstanding and set the tone for the meal. The Huevos con pisto, a Spanish take on eggs, was cooked to perfection and bursting with flavor. To add a touch of freshness to the spread, the Aguacate was ripe and creamy - a simple yet delightful accompaniment.

Not only was the food authentic and delicious, but the coffee also deserves a special mention. Made with La Colombe d'Or blend, it was fabuloso – rich, flavorful, and simply irresistible.

The total for such high-quality fare came to just $23, a price that speaks volumes of the value provided by Spanish Diner. If you're in search of one of the best and most genuine breakfasts in town, look no further. Spanish Diner has set the bar high, marrying great price and exquisite taste in an unforgettable morning feast.

If you're looking for soul food, this is where it is at. It is a very humble food stand that serves up some fattening yet comforting selection of southern food like shrimp and grits and po boy sandwiches. We got the shrimp and grits and fish po boy and they were pretty solid. The shrimp and grits was $12 but it was pretty small, and the fish po boy was of slightly better value but I could have gotten the food elsewhere for cheaper. Regardless, they were above average in quality, and the grits is overflowing with flavor. It is a bit greasy though, as I can see a spoonful of oil in the shrimp and grits. Definitely share with someone as it could be very filling. Fish po boy was good, a little bit heavy on the mayo. It is something to try, but I feel like the star is the shrimp and grits for sure. For a cherry on top, they were excited that people go to great lengths to check this place out, so they do appreciate the customers. "I appreciate it" as they say.

This place was packed on a Thursday night. Lots of people waiting for a table. Nice atmosphere. I had ground beef bibimbap and it was good.  I didn't particularly enjoy eating out of a burning hot cast iron bowl, but I understand that's a Korean thing. In the winter that might be wonderful. Some of the sides were unusual and not particularly appealing to me.  I had never had Korean food before so my opinion might be of less value. Service was great.

I have heard so much good things about Quality Eats!! Everything was really good, but the Corn Creme Brûlée really blew my mind!! I originally thought it's just a burnt layer of sugar on top, but it was actually creme Brûlée inside, just with corn in it!! It's just so good I almost licked the plate clean hah

I do not know why I got my hopes up thinking this would be a nice authentic sushi place in Chinatown. Of course it was operated by Chinese people. What was I thinking?To be honest, it wasn't that bad. Ambiance and decor is very nice but I feel like I was paying for that more than for the food itself.Now onto the food reviews. The price was a bit high for the portion provided (for everything). The fish I had was pretty fresh, cannot complain but I've had better. Rice was nothing special. The kani salad was unexpectedly spicy and as I have already mentioned, small. It also had a hint of (I believe) lime. Was not a fan. Fried squid legs, not very crunchy.Given the price AND quality, I would just go to Sugarfish. As for the fried squid legs, I would go to chicken v. Unfortunately the one in Chinatown is still closed though. Would I go back? Sorry but no.

Tried Saluggi's East recently and had a decent experience. The Caesar dressing on my starter needed a bit more zing, but I was impressed by the freshness of the ingredients. My Chicken and Garlic Sandwich missed its mozzarella, which was a letdown, but the staff handled it professionally by issuing a partial refund. While the sandwich was nothing extraordinary, the quality service - especially the kind lady on the phone - would bring me back to try other menu items. A solid choice for a casual meal.

*This is a no-tipping establishment*I came here with two other people. I got the Shake Ikura Don ($16), friend got Yakiniku Don ($14.25), and my other friend got Tan Tan Men ($15.50). We also got Yakisoba ($12) for the table. Shake Ikura Don consists of salmon sashimi, grilled fillet roe over rice. I wish they were more generous with the salmon sashimi. The ratio of sashimi to rice was quite underwhelming. I just had too much leftover rice which also lacked flavor. I tried to fill my stomach with the Yakisoba that we ordered to share, but it was way too salty because it had way too much sauce. Service was good though! We came right when they opened for dinner and were promptly seated. Our waitress checked up on us throughout our meal and refilled our waters whenever it was needed.

Title: Speakeasy Vibes and Eccentric Sips at NR

My latest visit to NR, the successor of the beloved ROKC, did not disappoint. This gem is cleverly tucked away, giving it an exclusive speakeasy feel as you step in. The cocktail menu immediately catches your attention with its extensive and unusual offerings. Each cocktail is an adventure in itself – I was particularly taken by the shiso/daikon and cumin/yogurt drinks; yes, they are as intriguing as they sound!

But NR is not just about the drinks. The Kyoto ramen is a bowl of pure comfort with its rich, meaty broth, perfectly fatty char siu, and thick, wavy noodles that boast the ideal al dente bite. This dish alone is a reason to return.

Happy hour promises oysters, and I'm looking forward to that. Add to the experience the welcoming staff and the lively backdrop of jazzy lindy hop tunes, and NR certainly knows how to create a fun, memorable dining experience. See you there soon – I can’t wait to come back!

Ordered from Kiki's Grill via Postmates and had a great experience. I've been to Kiki's proper several times, and the food from the Grill & Rotisserie is exactly the same as far as I can tell.  My boyfriend and I shared the saganaki, zucchini chips, chicken souvlaki with salad, and pork souvlaki with fries. Everything was amazing, though the standouts were the saganaki and zucchini chips!

Tucked away near the NYPLM is a quaint coffee shop that serves up a mean cup of joe – definitely a highlight for any coffee aficionado. However, when it comes to their baklava, brace yourself for a sugar rush. The pastry practically oozes honey, tipping the scales on sweetness. It's best tackled as a team effort, so consider sharing with a buddy or two unless you're up for a solo challenge that might leave you buzzing more than the caffeine.

This probably my 5th or 6th time here over the last several years, and feeling the AYCE hotpot offerings aren't as great as they used to be. Now I get that certain items are more expensive so they have to charge more for them. But for some of the items that are included, the quantity of what is served looks so different from the pics that it's a bit disappointing. For example, the photos in the menu show 8 pieces of dumplings, while the actual order was 4 tiny dumplings. Same issue for the fish tofu, sausage and stuffed tofu. I think it would've felt better even if they gave 1-2 more pieces. Otherwise the broth options were solid and it's a good size space to enjoy a hearty meal for groups of friends. Also they are one of the few hotpot places that take reservations, so idea for group get-togethers.

My recent visit to Barn Joo was a delight, despite the typical 7 PM Saturday bustle. Seated upstairs, where the lively atmosphere matched the downstairs vibe, my appetite was stoked by a day of walking across the Brooklyn Bridge.

We kicked things off with crunchy tofu, which perfectly balanced a crisp exterior with a tender heart, complemented by the zing of fried kimchi. The veggie japchae brought a welcome peppery punch, and the nutty green salad with its sweet almonds and flavorful dressing was a hit. A ginger limeade provided the much-needed refreshment, its coolness reviving us.

By Monday, my cravings led me back, eager for another round of the stellar limeade, tofu, and salad. We added truffle fries and popcorn chicken to the mix. While the popcorn chicken was a crunchy success, especially when dipped in smoked sriracha BBQ sauce, the truffle fries fell short, lacking in the promised truffle aroma and overdone.

I left with a hopeful suggestion to the owner: consider bringing your unique culinary vibe to Michigan, where it would undoubtedly become my go-to spot. Until next time, Barn Joo, keep the culinary excellence coming, and do think about making a mark in Detroit!

Having approached Bond St Sushi with a hint of skepticism due to mixed reviews, I was swiftly converted to a fan. The service proved exceptional; attentive staff ensured a flawless dining experience.

The meal commenced with the highly recommended tuna pizza – a triumph of fresh tuna atop a crispy crust. The fried rock shrimp, enveloped in a delightful mayo dressing, did not disappoint either.

The sushi selection was impressive, each piece of fish exuding freshness and a melt-in-the-mouth quality. The standout dish, however, was the Chilean Sea Bass – its tender, creamy texture with the perfect fat balance was a palate pleaser. But the showstopper was the steak, a masterpiece of flavor, cooked to succulent perfection and complemented by the crispy fried potato cubes.

To cap off the evening, the chocolate fondue provided a sumptuous finale, with ripe fruits dipped into a silken stream of melted chocolate. Bond St Sushi is a testament to the joy of expertly crafted Japanese cuisine – don't hesitate to indulge.

A very cute and hippie like place. The outside seating area is nicely decorated. My friends reccomended going here Becuase of the good reviews and I'm glad we came. The food was great. No complaints whatsoever. It is pretty quiet and there were plenty of seats available.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at Parm

Despite my initial apprehension towards the diner-style setup of Parm - a personal bias against diners - the experience turned out to be rather delightful. Opting for simplicity, I chose the chicken and was rewarded with a dish that was utterly delectable. While the prices lean towards the higher side, the quality of the meal justified the cost. The menu has intrigued me enough to warrant future visits; the chicken parm is already on my radar for next time. Service was efficient, complemented by a crew of amiable staff. I'm looking forward to exploring other locations and sampling more of what Parm has to offer.

Came here recently for a girl's night. I've been here quite a few times over the years for both brunch and dinner, and they've never disappointed. There were seven of us and I made the reservations. If you have a large party I would definitely suggest making reservations ahead of time because it was pretty packed when we were seated and it looked to be somewhat of a wait for a table as well.It was pretty tight in the dining room as there were a number of large party tables all closer together. Our table was right up against the next table and when I asked for them to slide it away so we could sit, one of the guys said it would be too far out for the servers but they failed to realize that only paper doll cut-outs would have been able to slip themselves into the chairs as they were right up against the already inhabited chairs of the next table. The host that showed us to the table took care of it and we sat.Our server was very nice. She was attentive and patient since there were a bunch of us and she had to wait a bit to collect all of our orders.My girlfriend and I shared two plates of their Sliders and Shrimp Mac & Cheese. Everyone enjoyed their food immensely. I also had one of their very weird Mezcal Negroni which was such an odd pairing but I liked it a very much.We split the bill the bills a few ways and our server had no issue with doing so. We tried to make it as easy as possible for her to follow.I like coming to SOE. They vibe is very NY, with a very energetic and young crowd. This is a trendy restaurant and you'll have a good time with a group or just a few people. The food is good, the staff is super friendly and it's located in a hugely walkable area of NYC. You can't go wrong down here.

Title: A Disappointing Return Visit

I recently returned to a restaurant that I had frequented before, chosen as a fallback option when our original choice wasn't immediately available. Despite the staff being quick and friendly, the experience fell short of expectations. 

Sadly, all of our meals arrived cold, giving the impression that they had been neglected before being served. Even the fries, a staple that should be served hot and crispy, were disappointingly tepid. Having spent the day exploring NYC, our hunger couldn't overshadow the letdown of our dining experience.

The rum and coke slushie provided some solace with its refreshing taste. However, the sides were lackluster: the coleslaw seemed stale and unappealing, and the potato salad was bland and forgettable. The cheese grits, which were supposed to be a comforting side, resembled more of a soup than the hearty dish one would expect.

In hindsight, the wait for our first-choice restaurant would have been the better option. This visit was a reminder that not all returns are triumphant, particularly when left with a lukewarm impression in what should have been a satisfying meal.

Title: Cozy Vibe with a Steep Price Tag at Sankaku

My evening at Sankaku left me with mixed feelings, landing a middling 3.5-star rating. The ambiance of the restaurant was inviting and definitely contributed to an enjoyable experience. However, the cost of sake dampened the mood – paying $20 for what appeared to be less than a 3oz pour of something I’d typically pick up for $35 a bottle felt excessive.

While Sankaku is an offshoot of Azabu, it’s worth noting that it doesn't specialize in sushi. Regardless, the Wagyu (Miyazaki) Tataki was a standout dish, tantalizing the taste buds with its delectable flavor. The homemade tofu was equally impressive, although the decision to add uni and Ikura for an extra $25 might not have been the most economical choice.

On the downside, the Snapper Liver was a letdown, marred by a lack of freshness and an overly heavy hand with the soy sauce. Edamame was just okay, nothing to write home about. The Shrimp Tempura, however, redeemed the situation somewhat, being both fresh and juicy.

After indulging in five small dishes and the pricey sake, the bill amounted to $350 post-tip, which felt hefty considering this wasn't a full dinner service. Hi Tribeca, your cozy spot has charm, but the value for money may not sit well with every patron.

After much anticipation, I finally joined my team for lunch at the reputable Mexican eatery by my office, a spot perennially buzzing with patrons. My expectations, perhaps inflated by its popularity, weren't fully met.

We kicked off with a trio of guacamole that lived up to the hype—distinctive and flavorful, a perfect sharing choice for our group of six. The short rib bone marrow quesadilla that followed, however, fell short—an uninspired dish that didn't deliver on the rich taste one would expect from marrow, not to mention the price felt steep for the portion.

Observing my boss's pared-down Caesar salad, with mere hints of romaine, I couldn’t help but feel that its simplicity was a tad underwhelming, despite her satisfaction.

This visit didn't quite hit the mark, but I'm open to returning, hopeful for a more impactful culinary experience next time.

Upon finishing my shift, I ventured into a local eatery where the staff-to-guest ratio was a promising four-to-one. My modest order included coffee and chips, a small purchase to justify my use of the amenities. Unfortunately, the experience fell short of expectations.

The coffee arrived lukewarm and unceremoniously sloshed over the rim, staining my shirt, and lacking the customary saucer. As for the spinach and artichoke dip, it was disappointingly cold and resembled a solid mass rather than a creamy blend, its flavor as uninspiring as its presentation, but the accompanying chips were acceptable.

The ambiance did little to redeem the shortcomings of the meal. The dim lighting and irritating background music contributed to an atmosphere that smacked of a neglected pub rather than a welcoming eatery. The seating was uncomfortable, and a palpable stickiness coupled with a hint of grime made the overall experience one to forget.

Title: Unexpected Gem in New York

Wandering into this unassuming spot on a whim, I was struck by the swift service that matched my urgency for a quick lunch. This unnamed restaurant was a revelation with its well-prepared dishes, particularly the steamed shrimp dumplings that I must insist you try – they were the highlight of my meal.

Despite its compact size, the place never felt overcrowded, striking a comfortable balance between casual and slightly upscale. As an interesting twist, the soundtrack of our visit was One Direction's hits on shuffle – an oddly fitting backdrop that added to the experience.

Overall, for anyone looking for a quality meal without the fuss, this establishment is certainly worth a visit. I left satisfied and ready to tackle the rest of my New York itinerary.

Title: Fair Vegan Fare at a Premium

I arrived at the restaurant with high expectations for a sumptuous vegan meal. While the menu offered a decent variety of plant-based options, the prices were notably steep. The culinary experience was satisfactory, with innovative flavor pairings, particularly the broccoli salad that stood out with its unique nutty and herby paste complementing the roasted vegetable. The rabe, featured as the special of the day, however, failed to impress; it was rather unremarkable.

The tofu bowl deserved a mention, as the tofu itself was well-prepared, and the peanut sauce was a flavorful touch that brought the dish together. I was intrigued by the tofu burger on the menu, but it's worth noting it's available exclusively after 6 pm.

In summary, while the food was decent, the high cost might not make it a go-to option for those who seek value alongside quality in their vegan dining experiences.

The best cinema theatre EVER!!! Not only are there reclining seats, you can also order food and drinks to enjoy while watching a movie!! The food is very decent and it's just such a luxury to dine in a movie theatre!! Service is amazing as well!!

This is a hole in the wall place- don't be confused if you see pizza in there- they share the same store space with the Italian place. Seating is limited and they accept card.I got the chicken, rice and lamb kabab- yummy! Everything was so flavorful. The chicken curry had pomegranate and some nut flavor- it was delicious! The kabab was so soft and full of flavor.The owner is super sweet and let me try something that tastes like lentils- I can't recall the name but it was delicious too.I will definitely go back.

We came here for brunch at 11:20. Breakfast ends at 11:30 and the waitress who was super nice and gave us a heads up about the time. We wanted to order from the breakfast menu so we quickly put in our order and the food came pretty fast afterwards. We ordered the Omelette A and the Biscuits and Gravy. Both were about $14. The biscuits and gravy were delicious and had a very interesting spice palate. It had more of a Cajun flavor which was very new to me! Not your typical dish! Both BF and I enjoyed the flavor but we also like our dishes to be over seasoned than under. I ordered the Omelette A with gruyere cheese with bacon. They def don't skimp on the bacon! It was very yummy and the egg was cooked PERFECTLY. It was such a beautiful yellow! Our service was very good and our waitress was super nice. Def a good brunch place if you are around midtown area!

I recently visited a modest little kimbap joint that offers a satisfactory if unremarkable dining experience. It's the kind of place you'd rate at around 3.5 stars – it doesn't dazzle, yet it does a decent job of quelling a kimbap craving. The rolls are generously sized and palatable; enough to satisfy you on the first go but not quite tempting enough to have you reaching for seconds. Although I did sample the cheese kimbap from my companion's plate, which swapped out the traditional beef for American cheddar – the beef, in my opinion, was the better choice.

The eatery is pretty bare-bones, with a small team of 2-3 people efficiently managing orders and takeout service – there's no seating available, but given the grab-and-go nature of kimbap, this isn't much of an inconvenience. Service is swift; the lady taking orders keeps the line moving, and you won't be waiting long for your food.

When it comes to value, you might find a more substantial meal for the same price in the vicinity, but as a stand-alone snack or a light meal, it holds its ground fairly well.

Title: Mixed Impressions at Jane's Sunday Brunch

After reserving a table for Sunday brunch at Jane, my party of three anticipated prompt seating but instead faced a 20-minute wait. Despite the delay, we were eager to try the well-recommended dishes: the Jane Benedict with satisfyingly meaty and minimally breaded crab cakes, the sizeable and juicy Jane burger accompanied by exceptional fries, and, less impressively, the steak frites. Our steak, requested medium rare, first arrived well done and then, after a lengthy wait, was a passable medium well – at that point, hunger overruled exactness. Although the steak was tasty, once again, the fries outshined the main.

The service fell short of expectations. The closely packed tables resulted in frequent disturbances from the busy staff, and simple tasks like getting the check and processing payment felt tediously drawn out.

In summary, brace for a wait both for seating and dining at Jane. While the food is reasonably priced and generally acceptable, the overall experience suggests you might find better value and comfort elsewhere.

Pho was excellent!! I have never had oxtail pho and there aren't many Chicago pho places that I've been to that serve this. Broth is so flavorful, lots of basil and bean sprouts, friendly staff! Service is super quick and the bowls of pho are huge! When I'm nyc, I would definitely come back here again.

Came here for a late lunch and felt like I was back in Spain...even though this place is italian lol. I really loved the small, tight, somewhat outdoor layout - very European and gorgeous. I get very warm very fast so sitting by the bar and at a place with no ac (or ac was off cause the doors/windows were open) was a bad idea - or at least eating hot ravioli in that weather in these circumstances was a bad idea. We started with the house wine - my 2 friends didn't eat but I got lunch so they have a lunch special - pasta + house wine for $18. It's actually a decent deal, and it came with bread too. I ordered the lobster ravioli and I think I'd probably skip on food the next time because it was a little bland for my liking. Otherwise the spot is very cute + picturesque, and reasonable for lunch!

Tucked away in an otherwise unremarkable part of town, Los Tacos No. 1 emerges as a culinary oasis for those seeking a flavorsome and affordable lunch retreat. As a new local working in the area, I've found solace in the limited lunchtime landscape at this gem of an eatery. For under $10, one can indulge in the most delectable chicken and steak tacos around, each bursting with authentic zest. When the craving for cheese strikes, their quesadillas offer a divine blend of gooey satisfaction, perfectly complementing the addictive crunch of their chips paired with top-notch guacamole. Los Tacos No. 1 might just top the charts as my favorite taco destination in NYC.

Eating at Gari Columbus is a really lovely experience! I saw comments about excessive noise, but it was really peaceful when I went. (Granted, there were only two other groups there so there probably wasn't a lot of preparation occurring.) The people were very hospitable, and the entire restaurant was aesthetically pleasing--it was a nice getaway from the bustling Upper West Side!My sister and I shared a spicy scallop roll and the Sushi Deluxe, which came with a fatty tuna and scallion roll and 9 pieces of nigiri. (I'm not totally sure about the names but think they were mid. fatty tuna, tuna, baby yellowtail, seared salmon, yellowtail, salmon roe, boiled shrimp, fried scallop, and one seared one which I don't know.) I really enjoyed all of the pieces I tried, although the seared salmon piece was almost completely split in half for some reason. (Also, my sister said that the unidentified one was too gamey for her taste.) I would definitely get the fried scallop and the seared salmon nigiri a la carte in the future, and I really liked the fatty tuna roll and the spicy scallop roll and would order them again as well.We had made the mistake of eating a lot for breakfast, so we were quite content with this amount of food, but I think under different circumstances, we probably would have wanted to order more. However, the pieces are pretty large (especially the spicy scallop cut roll) and we had a number of fattier cuts of fish that left us very full! Thank you to Gari Columbus for a wonderful dining experience!

The first time I came to Qi was when it was located on Eighth Avenue by the Port Authority. So glad I checked the address again because I didn't know they moved to the corner of Ninth Ave.& West 48th St. Anyway, we stopped in for a drink and appetizers before a performance. This new location wasn't all decked out with chandeliers like the one before. However, it was very nicely decorated and furnished in an Asian style.We started out with Yummy Ling Ling Vodka drinks ($14.00). The drinks were served in cute Panda bear containers. Our appetizers consisted of delicious steamed chicken and shrimp dumplings and veggie steamed rolls with tasty side sauces.Our server Jom was absolutely delightful from start to finish. The rest of the staff was very good too!I would definitely return for a full course meal in the very near future.

One of the few places I've been to that delivers on the Thai spice as it should be. The beef skewers were very good. Tender, sweet, salty, and a light spice. The fried chicken, while good, is probably something I wouldn't get the next go round. The spring rolls were crunchy and also packed a mild spice punch. The drunken noodles were very good. I got pork. Good flavors and textures to match. For me the highlight was the fried rice. It was spicy and jam packed with flavor in every bite. This is certainly the one dish that would be ordered again next visit. This place is around some very good bars so I am sure that I'll be back here again soon. You should definitely check them out. ENJOY!!!

I'm here for brunch a few times a month cause I enjoy the vibe and more importantly the food.  Great shakshouka, benedicts and french toast.  Coffee tends to be on the bitter side and they are sometimes inconsistent.  Last time eggs were a bit cold and they were skimpy strawberries on the french toast.

Title: A Satisfying BBQ Fix at Virgil's in Times Square

After our initial dining plans fell through on a bustling Saturday night in Times Square, my fiancé and I were fortunate to snag a last-minute reservation at Virgil's via Open Table. A fan of BBQ, I was enticed by their reputation for tasty ribs.

We arrived slightly ahead of our 7:00 pm slot and were promptly seated on the main level, with an acknowledgment of more space available upstairs. Keen on their Memphis style spare ribs, I opted for the quarter rack paired with two sides and cornbread, all for an impressively reasonable $19.95—particularly for the location.

The hickory-smoked ribs, served with a dry rub, were delectably tender and further enhanced by a variety of BBQ sauces available at our table. The mac and cheese side was a standout, delivering a creamy texture with well-cooked pasta, although the fries were somewhat forgettable amidst a carb-heavy selection.

Although the cornbread didn’t entirely meet my preference for sweetness, it was still enjoyable. On the other side of the table, my fiancé's Black & Bleu Burger was a hit, featuring the zesty combination of bleu cheese, applewood smoked bacon, and blackening seasoning.

Service was friendly and attentive, culminating in a thoughtful touch of hot towels at the end of our meal—a step above the standard wet nap. Our total bill came to just over $50, which we topped off with a New Year-themed $20.20 tip.

Virgil's turned out to be an unexpected triumph, providing us with a satisfying meal amidst the Times Square hustle. I heartily recommend it to BBQ enthusiasts and look forward to a return visit.

Another great mid-town lunch option! They have about 15 lunch options for 10$ (offering discount when paying by cash). The wasabi mayo the use is a nice kick to the sandwiches. Lots of folks love their boils as well. Relatively knew and worth checking out.

This place I is a great "find" on restaurant row (46th & 8th). They don't take reservations but the wait has never been more than 20 min on a sat/Sunday during lunch. Pick off of the picture menu and write in the number of items you want.- Dim Sum starts coming out. 4 ppl can eat until stuffed for ~ $120.

I came here with my boyfriend (who absolutely loves this place). He considers it to be his main staple for lunch (since its near his office). This place definitely lived up to its hype.. I can see why he loves it so much. We both got different "plates" with different sides. The food is extremely tasty, I love all the different meat and "side" options they have! The portions are also really good - definitely worth it for the price.Will definitely be back to try some more!

Authentic Mexican food cooked by authentic grandmas. Family owned and run. The late night workers there are so sweet, made us gringos feel like family. Even brought us fresh queso to cool our mouths when we dared to eat their table chili peppers! You hope places like this never close, cuz they're the grit, heart and soul of New York City.

Solid veggie ramen, but probably not worth going back to when there are so many other options in the city. I got the miso soy milk vegan ramen which was admittedly well priced at only $15, and they even gave me a side of chili oil for free (instead of charging $2 like basically every other place). The soy milk broth was pleasantly creamy. The noodles were good. The braised tofu was not the greatest - sort of funny tasting. The service was excellent. It's worth noting that the place is inside the Wyndham hotel. To enter, you first go into a big sports bar, then climb up a couple stairs to get to Shinka, which detracts from the atmosphere a little.

Last Tuesday evening, my three friends and I visited this gem of a restaurant at 7pm and were delighted to be seated straightaway. I opted for the pork set, priced at a reasonable $19, featuring a comforting pork curry rice and a crispy pork cutlet, all washed down with a diet coke. Thankfully, I chose the Level 1 spice, which offered just the right amount of heat without overwhelming the palate—my companions who ventured into Level 2 and Level 3 territories weren't as fortunate, finding their dishes intensely spicy.

Especially recommendable for those seeking a warm embrace from a curry dish on the chilly streets of NYC, this spot doesn't just hit the spot—it also delights with its ample serving sizes, value for money, highly attentive service, and indisputably scrumptious food.

If you're in the mood for a Mediterranean twist on your brunch, this is the place to be! Anticipate some waiting time — it's best to arrive once the initial crowd has ebbed. I highly recommend the haloumi eggs Benedict, complemented by a tangy side of shug and harissa. While I do find myself yearning for a more generous helping of haloumi, there's an abundance of zaatar pita to leave you satisfyingly full. A delightful spot for an authentic and flavorful start to your day!

Title: High Hopes Partially Met at Popular NY Thai Spot

As a newcomer to New York, I was eager to try a Thai restaurant that boasted a 4.5-star average from over 2,000 reviews on Yelp. With such high praise, I anticipated an exceptional dining experience.

Upon arrival, the 20-minute wait for a table indicated a bustling, beloved locale. The service was commendable—prompt, friendly, and efficient. The staff's recommendation of the clay pot fried rice piqued my interest, but as a Vietnamese diner familiar with similar dishes, I found it satisfactory but not extraordinary. The lychee martini, however, was a delightful standout and came highly recommended.

The appetizers, like the overly peppered calamari, were decent but didn't leave a lasting impression. While the food quality was generally good, it seemed to cater to a more fusion or Americanized palate, which, for me, detracted from the authenticity I expected from a Thai establishment.

In conclusion, although the visit didn't merit a full five stars, the overall experience was positive. Would I return? Certainly. Does it rank as the best Thai food I've ever had? Unfortunately, no. Despite this, the restaurant remains a solid choice for a casual night out in New York.

Discovered this place by random while I was walking towards Times Square. It looked like buffet at first, but when I walked in it was different. It seemed like, they were known for making Dry Hot Pot Bowls. Everything was shown in front like assembly line. Good Chinese food. I would definitely say their food is on the healthier side. Freshly made to custom orders. Would highly recommend the pepper steak with beef fried noodles. Good portion size. Very clean and friendly staff. Would highly recommend if you are in the area. Stop by and grab a bite. Definitely worth the money. Ambiance - Fast Food nothing FancyService - 10/10WiFi - Not Sure

Went here last month to celebrate my company's anniversary. Our server Oliver was very helpful and friendly. We started off with a bottle of Cava and the tilefish lettuce wraps. The fish was super delish and I loved the spicy sauce that came with it. Next we moved on to the chicken thighs which were perfectly fried and so tender. For our mains we had a pasta with a sausage and mushroom sauce. Loved the umami on the sauce and how it melded together so well. I could have scooped the sauce up with bread it was so good, Also had the rotisserie chicken main which was super tender and plated elegantly. For dessert i had the Yuzu and berry cheesecake. This citrusy cheesecake was light and fluffy and the perfect ending to an excellent meal. Also the manager of the restaurant congratulated us on our business and we were surprised that he had heard of the documentary we worked on that was in the Nashville Film Festival.

We took a chance on Yelp being from out of town-awesome choice: We got 4 slices and 2 can sodas which came to $22. The pizza by the slice I loved was gabagool made with capricola and banana peppers AND Grandma! The crust here is so delicious and the ingredients fresh. They do have one bathroom and it's very clean. Upscale but great pizza nonetheless. The gabagool is the only one of its kind in all of NYC the piemaker said. The flavors are I creole with every bite-plus the fresh mozz!

Four of us had a business breakfast at Tribeca's Kitchen recently.  We met at 8 am, so it was not very busy.  Service was prompt and efficient throughout.  Food came out quickly and everything was as requested.Orders in the group included a smoked salmon and cream cheese on a toasted bagel, an egg white veggie omelet, a ham and bacon omelet, and a steak breakfast wrap.   Toast, hash browns, and other typical accompaniments came with the entrees.  Everyone enjoyed their meals, and I had the salmon bagel - but also tried the steak wrap which was really tasty.   I tried an apple turnover to start - it was nice and flaky, but a little light on apples.  I believe they bring the pastries in, not made inhouse.Tribeca Kitchen is a perfectly acceptable place for a good home cooked breakfast.

What a great find! My husband and I love Thai food and so we wanted to check this place out. I don't hand out 5 stars often but this place earned it! I'm so glad we stopped because the food was as amazing as the ambiance. We had Thai coffees to drink, which were a fantastic balance of creamy and delicious. Our waiter was terrific and very patient with us. I had the pad see ew, which I rarely order anywhere other than "our" traditional Thai place. It was so great! Perfect ratio of noodles and chicken and spice! My husband had the green curry which he loved. I thought it was delicious from the few bites I was able to sneak.Out of the gazillions of restaurants we had the choice of, I'm glad we tried this one! I highly recommend this restaurant because of the great service and excellent food!

10 star experience.Amazing if you're solo because you don't need to interact with the waiter. Water stations behind you. Food was incredible and came in a traditional Japanese set up. Just as good as the ramen I've had in japan. You DONT need extra toppings and as the amount it comes with is enough.
Good quality coffee. Staff was super friendly. I didn't get to try the sweets but they looked  appealing. Cute little place.

During my recent visit to this gem with a quintessential LA health vibe, I discovered the "mushreuben" - a dish that took my tastebuds on a delightful journey, outshining any traditional Reuben sandwich I've encountered. A full week later, the flavors linger in my memory, beckoning me to return. Despite the tempting array of options, like the 'Sunrise Kingdom' teasing my curiosity, the allure of that same mushreuben experience presents an irresistible challenge to my culinary diversity.

The adorable interior compliments the wholesome atmosphere, creating a welcoming space that makes the premium prices easier to swallow, especially knowing a portion of the proceeds goes to a good cause. This spot is a must-visit for anyone searching for a fresh take on classic comfort food with a side of conscience.

We walked here from Sleep No More. They're open late and you just can't go wrong with their artichoke pizza! The slices will be enough for two people. I'll need to come back to try the other flavors. We ended up taking ours to go and took it on our flight back to Los Angeles.

Title: A Taste of Greenwich Gem - Worth the Price Tag

Review:

I visited a quaint spot in Greenwich on a quiet Sunday evening and had an experience worthy of 4.5 stars. The slightly elevated prices were justified by the delightful dishes and the ambiance of the restaurant. The interior decor was tastefully done, which complemented the overall dining atmosphere.

The service was efficient, perhaps aided by the fact that there were only a few other occupied tables. My dining companion and I opted for the "little pot" with a spicy kick and the tomato beef soup. Each dish made a flavorful impression. The "little pot" broth was rich and aromatic, though a tad salty for my palette; however, my friend found it to be perfectly seasoned. The accompanying minced pork was reminiscent of succulent, fluffy meatballs, and the pickled vegetables added a pleasant, balanced tang.

The tomato beef soup was notable for its sour yet refreshing broth, teeming with tender slices of beef and punctuated with fiery red chilies for an extra punch.

An added bonus was the attentiveness of the waitstaff and a generous coupon offering $10 off a future visit of $30 or more within a 10-day window—an enticing reason for a prompt return. Despite the slight nudge on the wallet, this restaurant certainly merits a visit for those seeking quality fare in Greenwich.

Title: An Authentic New York Slice at Joe's Pizza

If you're like me, a native New Yorker who measures the worth of a pizzeria by its classic cheese slice, then Joe's Pizza is your kind of place. Recommended by a Macy's staffer amid the Black Friday rush, Joe's popularity was clear from the queue spilling out the door.

But don't let the line intimidate you. The staff at Joe's operate with a speed and efficiency that's nothing short of miraculous, ensuring you’re biting into their heavenly pies without catching a cold.

Their cheese slice? Divine. The spinach variant? Equally impressive. And if you're in the mood for something a bit more robust, my cousin's blissful reaction to the Sicilian slice says it all. Joe's keeps it real with a cozy, no-frills space that embodies the authentic New York pizza shop vibe. It's the kind of place you pop into for a quick, delicious bite - there's no lingering, yet you never feel rushed.

For my mentee's inaugural New York pizza experience, Joe's did not disappoint. We're talking best slice material, certainly making my personal top 2. For that quintessential slice that cuts to the heart of the Big Apple, Joe's is a must. Loved it, will absolutely be back!

Super cozy Thai tapas place in Hell's Kitchen! The vibe is really homey and not super upscale. Very comfortable and relaxed environment. If you are eating with people, I would definitely recommend each person getting the pick and mix 2 and then just share everything so you get a taste of all they have to offer! Their dishes are all veggie, meat, or seafood, and they don't have noodles but the dishes more than make up for it. I would definitely recommend the pork belly, panang beef curry, and braised short ribs. Those dishes are done so well and the curry goes so well with the rice they give you. I would go for the red rice because it's more interesting than the typical white jasmine rice, but that's personal preference. And last thing, definitely get the Thai iced tea (pictured)! You can get it with or without milk. Without milk, the Thai iced tea is still pretty sweetened. This goes well especially if you're ordering any spicy foods!

I like Tappo. Just like I like Gruppo, Posto, Brado, and their other sister spots that specialize in cracker crust pizza. Personally, I prefer a bit more chew to my crust (I want crisp, not crunchy), but I'm not sad about eating this pizza, especially since they rock out with the toppings. Whether you're looking for a simple pepperoni or one of the combo pies like the Shroomtown, the Chickpotle, the Big Pineapple (purists may not like a bacon and pineapple pie, but they are just lying to themselves), this pizza tastes good.They also do an excellent lunch business because they offer all kinds of pastas, salads, sandwiches, and pizza specials in the $12-14 range. There's not many spots where you can sit down with waiter service at that price point, and it does get crowded right around noon (so go early). I recently rolled with the Millionaire's Chicken sandwich. I like to imagine that they have a rich guy in the back ready to eat lunch, and when I order it they go back there and steal his sandwich and give it to me. He's probably pretty upset, since I thoroughly enjoyed the pesto/bacon/bibb thing happening in my mouth. Although, the bread was over toasted...whoever's running these places really likes crunchy carbs. To each their own, I guess.

My recent visit to this local eatery was fueled by a craving for Japanese curry, leading me to try their Berkshire pork katsu curry. The katsu did not disappoint, delivering great taste as anticipated. When it comes to curry establishments, the spotlight shines on the curry itself. If this particular style of curry is what you're after, you'd likely rate it a perfect five stars. Personally, while I found the curry good, it missed the mark of being spectacular. Nevertheless, it managed to satisfy my craving adequately.

Had a team lunch reservation on 1pm on a Friday. After all the hype about this place, was super excited to finally try some of the well-reviewed dishes. We ordered a ton of food and everything we tried was outstanding, not a single doubt about it.Complementary bread and butter were a nice touch. Tasty, naturally tasting butter. Hot potato chips blue cheese fondue ($9) were just plain chips with dip. Skip, get something else that's actually a restaurant cooked dish. Shishito peppers ($9) tasty, well cooked. A bit oily. Big portion for the price. Skillet roasted Mac and cheese ($16) was a major surprise. Disappeared from the table pretty quickly. I'm not a fan of mac and cheese, but even I dug in and consumed an unfathomable amount. Very creamy, cheesy, and balanced taste profile. Not bland at all, which is a common pitfall of mac and cheeses.Calamari ($15) were tender and light. Great golden batter that easily peeled from the calamari. Ricotta gnocchi ($16 for appetize size, $24 for entrée size) with truffle cream were the biggest surprise of the day for me. I'm not a fan of pasta, so I gingerly tried one gnocchi. Then reached for seconds. And thirds. And fourths. One word for this dish--superb. The gnocchi were super tender and light. Definitely didn't taste frozen. Felt like perfect, fluffy balls of goodness. The truffle cream was the bomb. Give me a bowl and I'll eat it with a spoon! The truffle elevated this dish from simple to upscale. Seriously spectacular! The first pasta dish in my entire life that I'll remember and tell others about. Supreme burger ($25) dry-aged short rib blend, raclette cheese, watercress, red onion, green peppercorn sauce, gruyère bun, fries. The best bang for your buck. Huge portion. A mound of fries. Took the leftovers home.The only downside to this amazing dish is the heaviness I felt afterwards. The fries were light and fluffy and I had only a few, but my stomach felt extremely full and bloated afterwards. I didn't have any dinner that day, as the feeling lasted well up until I went to bed. The next day, when I got to those leftovers, I experienced the same prolonged heaviness and lack of appeties that lasted the entire day. Chicken sandwich ($18) burrata, tomato jam, basil aioli, toasted sesame semolina, fries Chicken pot pie ($25) roasted chicken, baby portobello mushrooms, pearl onion, cheddar biscuit top.Caesar salad ($14 for small, $19 for large) was nothing special--very difficult to make such simple staple stand out. Opt out for something more unique that you can't try anywhere else.Honeynut squash ($14 for small, $19 for large) goat cheese salad apples, frisée, spiced pepitas, apple cider vinaigrette. Bright, light salad. Nothing extraordinary to speak of, but tasty. Braised short rib cavatelli ($23) 10 hour short rib ragu, mascarpone were a hearty portion, good proportion of meat to pasta. Salmon ($26) pastrami spiced, apple cider braised cabbage, roasted parsnip, watercress, horseradish crema. Small portion: definitely not to stuff yourself but to savor the ingredients. Pretty presentation. Very well-seasoned, tender fillet. Delicate vegetable medley and crema. Delicate taste profile. Nothing crazy mind-blowing, but a solid option.The service was superb. Our waitress was super patient, warm, and helpful with menu recommendations. She even put up with our awful humor, which was a great testament to her character and training. We took our time ordering and staying for over two hours. Our entire experience was spot-on, impeccable. The atmosphere is casual. Very loud noise levels--prepare to raise your voice and strain to hear the conversation. The place has a toooon of seating, so big groups are welcome. Gets packed around lunchtime and dinner, with slow, calm time falling between 2 and 4pm. Fun fact: there is a peep hole in the bathrooms downstairs ;D Go check it out!Dark chocolate pecan tart ($11) chocolate pecan fudge, brown butter ice cream was a decadent indulgence. Not too sweet, which was a nice surprise. Very balanced taste profile. Thanks to the heavenly chocolate fudge and crunchy caramelized pecans, this was very rich and filling--good to share. Enjoyed the contrast between cold and smooth ice cream and warm, gooey texture of the tart. A perfect conclusion to a scrumptious meal. Get this!! Caramelized apple pie ($11) local honeycrisp apples, toasted almond cookie crust, bourbon ice cream was huuuuge. A great portion to share amid 2-3. Delicious, golden crust. Fragrant apples. Ice cream on top is a nice accompaniment. Overall, now I understand what the Smith hype is all about and totally will return for another great experience again!

I recently dined at this steakhouse during restaurant week and was pleasantly surprised by the high quality of food and service, enough to consider returning at full price. The dining area exuded class with its soft lighting and impeccably dressed servers, offering an upscale atmosphere that made me feel rather fancy.

The service was highly attentive throughout the meal. The appetizer, a braised BLT bite, was a standout with its remarkable texture and flavor; I'd eagerly order it as an entrée if possible. My friends were equally pleased with their soup starter.

I opted for the salmon entree, which was a highlight, perfectly cooked and my favorite dish of the night. The chicken my friend ordered was also commendable, maintaining its juiciness with a generous portion. Another companion's petite filet, while tasty, was slightly overcooked beyond the requested medium. The sides were hit or miss - I did not sample the potato skins, but the haricot vert on my plate was excellent.

Dessert did not disappoint, with the crème brûlée being so irresistible that I savored every last morsel, including the mint garnish, while the sorbet was a refreshing finish for my friend. Overall, this experience was a definite win and has opened my eyes to the allure of fine dining at a steakhouse.

Title: A Brunch of Variety at a Bustling Spot

I visited the restaurant on a busy Saturday afternoon and was fortunate enough to secure a table for two amid the brunch rush. The space accommodated the crowd well, although our table was small and unstable, a minor inconvenience that required some balancing act to prevent drink spillage.

The menu offered an eclectic mix with the shoo shoo breakfast—a delightful assortment that included an Israeli salad, goat cheese dip, feta, smoked salmon, soft-boiled eggs, and more. The dish provided a tasty smorgasbord that catered to a lighter palate, though those craving something heartier might find solace in the shooshooka on a future visit. The bread served was freshly warm, sprinkled with sesame—a perfect canvas for the accompanying flavors, especially when paired with the salmon to offset the salad's strong onion taste.

My dining companion's green frittata, however, fell short. Its vibrant color was misleading, revealing a spongy texture and lack of seasoning that we would not recommend.

Service was impressively swift despite the throngs, and the staff did not rush our dining experience, allowing for a leisurely meal. The takeaway? For a more serene vibe, consider off-peak hours or weekdays for your visit.

This place is absolutely perfect. Not only does it have a clean appearance and an air conditioned interior, its menu is full of reasonably priced, delicious food.I got the two item BBQ rice plate, and opted for roast pork (char siu) and cuttlefish, which is an extra dollar.
