It all came out to 7.25 which is extraordinarily affordable. The plate is packed with food. So much meat, and the rice is perfectly drizzled with the juices from the BBQ. The best part is that they also give you a ton of steamed Napa cabbage. It could honestly be split into two meals since it was so much food. I regretfully ate the whole thing in one sitting but won't do that next time so I can savor the meal twice. They also serve complimentary hot tea with your meal. Everything about this place is perfect. Will be back very soon!

World class Cantonese with global locations. Interior design transports you to a high end restaurant on The Bund. The Hakka cocktail with sake, coconut water, passionfruit and lychee was a decompress from the day and segue into a dinner date noshing on the crispy pork belly and best dim sum. An afterwork go-to in Midtown.Orig Post 3/30/17#dodrinkdine

Title: A Quick Bite at Balthazar with Hits and Misses

After hearing much buzz about Balthazar, my curiosity finally led me to its bustling setting in Soho for a Saturday afternoon meal. The popularity of the place was evident, yet my date and I were promptly seated, which was a pleasant surprise.

In anticipation, I had my heart set on a scone, but alas, they were sold out—a testament to their demand, perhaps. My date's choice, the steak frite, was a winner, arriving perfectly medium rare and topped with a generous dollop of savory herb butter. The accompanying fries were a crunchy delight, and the condiment selection was intriguing, notably an unusual mayo.

I ventured to taste the apple tart tatin for dessert but found it overwhelmingly sweet to my palate, leaving it unfinished. While the flavors overall were appreciable, the steep prices leave me hesitant to return. However, I am pleased to have satisfied my curiosity and found solace in the excellent rosemary ciabatta from the adjacent Boulangerie—a takeaway that capped the visit on a high note.

I would love a return trip to give a full experience, but from the drinks side of things, this was an excellent spot. The food looked delicious but my partner and I were bar hopping and glad we got some cocktails. I was absolutely in love with the bourbon smash here! Very well made with cute garnish and truly tasty. My partner had a seasonal gin drink (can't remember the name) but had honey and it was stellar! Pricewise it's pretty much right down the middle for Manhattan, and a little under for such a tourist friendly spot. Looking forward to coming back when the weather is nicer!

Title: Mixed Feelings at [Restaurant Name]

I recently dined at [Restaurant Name], where the food was truly excellent, showcasing complex flavors and impeccable quality. Unfortunately, the service experience left a lot to be desired. Despite having made a reservation for one, I was greeted with the news that my table wasn't ready upon arrival. Inexplicably, I endured a 20-minute wait, only to be informed that there was no table available and was relegated to the bar.

What puzzled me most was the apparent disregard for the reservation system. The wait staff's absence during my wait compounded the frustration, and their attitude came off as dismissive when addressing the issue. Furthermore, once the order was placed, the wait for the food was painstakingly long, and seemingly out of sync with other patrons who arrived later but were served promptly.

While the culinary offerings at [Restaurant Name] are top-notch, the service shortcomings are too glaring to overlook. A more attentive and efficient service would make this establishment a must-visit. As it stands, one might need patience and low service expectations to fully enjoy the exceptional cuisine.

Holyyyyyy this place is absolute fire !!!! A Portuguese cuisine restaurant that specializes in seafood. Every bite was erupting with flavor- portions are fair but here you are going for quality not quantity. I was still very full after eating.Got the prawns, the clams, the bruschetta, and the fried tilefish. I would recommend all 4, but especially the first 3. Ask for more bread to dip in the sauce.For drinks I'd recommend the chilled red wine- so delicious!Service was great and the ambience was quiet and quaint. Highly recommend as a date spot.

These comments are confusing cuz some are talking about the taco truck experiences and some about the fine dining down stairs!!! llsFine Dining:Came here for a bridal shower and it was everything!  Honestly my only complaint was seating 12 people at a 10 person table.  The atmosphere was an experience that reminds me of old New York very exclusive and trendy.  Its was dark and romantic but still very causal at the same time.  The staff was very friendly and attentive to our party the whole time.  I arrived early so of course I went to the bar, and the Hibiscus cocktail was sooo tastey!!Since we had a large party we were served their prefix menu family style.  It was all delish and a good way for EVERYONE to eat well at the same price.  There isn't one dish they served us that I did not like....I don't eat octopus but people at the table said it was yummy:-)I would say it was worth the money to experience this spot!!  I might be back for date night something sexy:-)!!!!!

Worth slurping in public! Definitely one of the best places I've been for ramen. I lucked out while traveling for work and was able to get a table for a late lunch with some colleagues. The pork belly buns are a must. The meat will melt in your mouth and the buns are worth the carbs for those of you who go bunless. :-)The ramen was simple but complex if that makes sense. The pork broth was perfect in flavor and the noodles were cooked just right. I ordered the traditional ramen and added shigureni (pulled pork). I can't wait to return for more and next time I'll "kae-dama".

Side note: So what's with Murray Hill now having 4 Turkish restaurants? It's too bad the only bad one is right nearby work. Anyway:Not to be confused with Sofra Grill, Sophra just opened recently. It's a bit more on the casual side compared to the other places though the food is similarly good. The staff here (which I believe are all family members) are very nice. The man there gave me some free tea which was good for a cold day. I decided to order two smaller dishes instead of a kebab of some type or some other dish.Içli köfte: "Cracked wheat stuffed with ground meat, walnuts & herbs." Icli kofte is fried stuffed meatballs in short. It came two to a serving (for $12) and they were piping hot and quite flavorful. The meat also had some walnuts as well as some sweetness. Along with the lemon (to curb the richness) you see served with every other dish, they were on top of a spicy tomato paste. I believe it was ezme which was a nice touch and a good thing to mix with the very flavorful meat.Lahmacun "Anatolian version of ancient turkish meat pie with ground lamb topped with parsley, fresh tomatoes, red peppers and onions all on thin dough"Lahmacun is one of my favorite dishes and when I saw it on the menu, I decided to enter this place (seeing that they have this and a lot of pides on the menu.) I wasn't expecting two massive pieces for the price (it reminded me more of NJ more than Murray Hill.) For those who don't know, the purpose of the onions, tomato, parsley, and lemon on the side are to put on top of the rip-able pieces and eat it together. I think the spices could have been a bit stronger but it's hard to complain with the portion size. Very good.I was stuffed so I decided to get dessert to go (and not the Kunefe as that is prepared hot.) I walked up to the dessert case and after going through a few options, I asked whether the Tulumba (the cylindrical pastry) or their semolina cookies were better. The man recommended the latter as it was homemade unlike the other dessert so I went with that one.Şekerpare: Semolina cookie with walnut topped with pistachio.This was quite delicious and a good recommendation. Not super sweet of a syrup and very soft. I believe it was $6.50 though I don't know if you get three for the price in the restaurant or if they gave me one extra.The food here was quite good and I might as well compare to the other local places. I think it was much better than Sahara, a bit better than Turkish Kitchen (especially for the price,) and a bit worse than Galata (which is also a bit more expensive.) I'll be back to try their kebabs but at this point, it's quite a good new place. I'll stick with rounded up score for now as I hope they succeed as well.

Title: Busy Spot with Hits and Misses

Visited with friends on a bustling Sunday evening and the place was vibrant at 8 pm. Remember to bring cash to this extensive-menu eatery. I tried the Ginger Duck ($13.50), which proved a bit disappointing due to excessive fat, but once trimmed, the seasoned meat paired with the mild ginger was quite enjoyable. We shared Clams with Black Bean Sauce at the table, but they were unremarkable and not something I'd recommend. In terms of service, it was efficient; food arrived within 25 minutes of ordering, which is commendable considering the crowd. Worth a visit if you're selective with your choices!

3.5/5 Comfort Hong Kong/Canto food at its best, where the staff will just plop it down in front of you and please don't expect it to look nice. Also, you can cook this, and your mama can cook this for you - it's that simple, but dammit, somehow it tastes even better when eaten outside -.- Condensed Milk Butter Toast ($2): suchhhh a classic! Must order every time, just because I really miss that warm, fluffy, sweetened pieces of bread. Satay Beef Ho Fun ($6): Idk why I ordered this in soup form because the satay beef lost its satay-ness immediately after being dunked in soup. Pass. Pork Ramen Stir Fry ($8.50): dude, who can resist stir fry ramen?? These are the packages of instant noodles just wok-fried with other ingredients. Saucy, salty, and delicious. Ordered it on both occasionsBaked Pork Chop Over Rice ($7.25): these baked rice dishes are just sooo good! I love the cheesy baked rices more, but this was delicious as well. The meat was a little on the fattier side, but meat itself is tender, flavorful, and tender. While I always enjoy this, the ones at XO Kitchen is noticeably tastierCurry Fishballs: when the fishball craving hits and the street carts are gone...Calamari: baby calamari that's not too tasty. SkipppYakult with Jelly: they definitely added enough yakult that the drink wasn't diluted. Only thing was that it was too sweet for me

hmmm. i was torn about the rating for this place. the food was good, not amazing, the service was fine, not amazing... the view WAS amazing however. given all that, i probably wouldn't opt to come back here myself, only if others insist. The pre fixe menu was a fairly good deal, but i thought the amount of food was a bit on the small side. nothing was particularly revolutionary, except the foie gras (i'll come back to that), but everything was solid, just fine. that foie "reuben" though was actually pretty exciting. based on the pictures it seems that the foie dish gets updated periodically, but at least for the dish i got, i was impressed. the foie was creamy, the brioche toasty and rich, and the mustard and sauerkraut really complimented the rich foie. i thoroughly enjoyed it. the steak was well cooked, but whatever glaze they put on it was a bit thick and cloying. i would have preferred that on the side i think. the leak and potato were fine, but again nothing special. piece of steak was a bit on the small side. service was fine. wine pairing was fine. they give a few options for each course, which makes me feel like they aren't REALLY pairing it with the dishes themselves. but i mean, at least it wasn't too pricey.

Title: A Refreshing Oasis with Farm-Fresh Flair

I stumbled into this charming eatery to escape the sweltering heat and was immediately impressed by the strong, free WiFi - a perfect haven for catching up on work. The ambiance is perfectly suited for a working lunch, and the drink menu did not disappoint. I opted for the "Green Monster Juice" blended with mint lemonade - a genius mix that is both refreshing and health-conscious, reducing sugar intake without sacrificing flavor.

What truly sets this place apart is their dedication to freshness; they grow their own herbs and integrate them beautifully into their offerings, exemplifying the farm-to-table philosophy.

Service was personable and attentive. Jessica, the server, was an absolute delight, going the extra mile by offering complimentary cookies (note: not gluten-free) and even topping off my juice for free.

Whether you're seeking a cool workspace or a fresh, garden-inspired beverage, this spot ticks all the boxes.

Title: A Remarkable Culinary Experience Worth Every Praise

From the moment I stepped into the restaurant, the warmth of a family greeting enveloped me, setting a tone of hospitality that only intensified as the evening progressed. Despite my early arrival, my reservation was honored with immediate seating, a gesture I greatly appreciate.

The server was the epitome of service excellence – attentive, knowledgeable, and truly remarkable in every interaction. His expertise shone brightly when he paired one of the reserve wines with our meal flawlessly, enhancing the flavors of both the succulent scallops we started with and the scrumptious pasta dishes that followed.

Having visited their Brooklyn location before, my expectations were high, yet the culinary prowess on display here managed to astonish me again. The dishes were a symphony of flavors, skillfully crafted and beautifully presented, leaving no doubt about the kitchen's talent.

Adding to the experience was our server's generous gesture of opening an additional bottle of wine on the house, which was just as delightful as the first. This act of kindness was mirrored towards the end of our meal when, after ordering coffees to cap off a sumptuous feast, we were surprised with a complimentary tiramisu. This final touch of sweetness was not just delectable; it was a testament to the restaurant's exceptional service.

In conclusion, the phenomenal staff made our dining experience unforgettable, treating us as part of their family. Heartfelt thanks to the entire team for a night characterized by culinary excellence and unmatched hospitality.

Come here for the service, though the food is OK too.I trust Yelp more than I trust three of my four children, but I felt somewhat let down in this case. First, the people here are wonderful; the place is clean; service is outstanding. The food though? We weren't overly impressed.My wife and I reserved a post-theater dinner here, and we were quickly seated next to a French couple enjoying NYC for the first time. Cool experience. As is usually the case, I ordered calamari while we waited on the main -- half plain/half eggplant in this case. The calamari here is par for the course. Not bad. But not memorable. It was served hot and nicely browned ... with a little more chew than average. The marinara was delicious though.Pizza here is Neapolitan and the crust was true to the style: mostly soft. Though the toppings were quality, we just felt like something was missing. It was bland as a whole, and seemed blah in most every way. Not bad ... at all. But not great either. My thought, after seeing some regulars here, is that the pasta dishes are clutch. I would certainly come back here and try them, and hopefully up my rating (I hate mediocre ratings for mom & pop businesses). But I would not come back here for the pizza, when there are so many better places within a short cab ride.

Title: A Taste of Paris with Room for Improvement

As an enthusiast of all things French, I was eagerly looking forward to a Parisian escape at the end of my day. The restaurant, with its promise of authentic French cuisine and architecture, seemed like the perfect substitution for the City of Light itself.

The establishment boasts a well-thought-out layout, featuring a restaurant in the back and a front-facing bakery section for convenient takeout. The availability of business cards was a nice touch for those wishing to recommend or revisit.

Service, however, was a mixed bag. Our server, Brittney, exhibited an average level of customer care, lacking the enthusiasm and engagement one would hope for when indulging in French hospitality.

On to the sweeter note, the Adagio ($6.80) was a standout. Despite the lack of descriptive signage, Brittney did her part to describe this delightful pastry. It was a light and elegant chocolate mousse with a surprising passion fruit center, balanced atop a flourless chocolate biscuit and finished with a glossy chocolate glaze and a miniature almond macaron cookie—a truly enjoyable confection that spoke to the finesse of French patisserie.

The French Macaron duo, on the other hand, didn't quite hit the mark. Absent were labels for flavors and prices, contributing to the establishment's poor reviews for lack of customer information. The vanilla and chocolate passion macarons crumbled upon opening the restrictive plastic packaging—unfortunate, as the cookies themselves were just average and failed to surpass the quality of macarons available elsewhere.

In summary, while the bakery captures a slice of Parisian indulgence with certain standout items, there is a clear need for improvement in service and presentation. A more customer-oriented approach, with attention to detail in signage and packaging, could transform this establishment into a true gem for Francophiles seeking a taste of Paris close to home.

I've heard great things about this place, I know people who literally swear by it. However, for me it's pretty meh...If you're thinking Cajun as in Gulf Coast Cajun, you would be sadly mistaken - just as I was. The first sign that this might not be a good idea is that there are a lot of Asians in this place. Which means Asian seafood not Gulf Coast seafood. If you're from or frequent Louisiana and/or the surrounding areas you will know the difference and I'd advise you not to eat here. Since I was starving, I decided to give a try despite my misgivings. So, I ordered:Shrimp and Crab Combo (Snow Crab)Lobster Roll w/ a Side Salad& A Side of BroccoliFirst, the Garlic Butter Sauce here is Trash. If you're gonna go with something, try the Cajun Seasoning. Second, the Shrimp here do not come from the Gulf Coast. It lacks in color, texture, and flavor. As for the Lobster Roll, it was meh...And, the Broccoli here was blah as well. The bright side is they have a bar! It seems decently stocked and the bartender was knowledgeable. Overall the venue was cleanly, as well as the restroom - and, the servers were nice. Will I be back? To have a drink, maybe. To eat, not likely.

4 stars cuz I ordered  red stewed spicy beef noodles an we got the plains 5 spice beef noodle soup. Beef were very scanty. Soup was very scanty but tons of noodles. Soup was not tasty.  So not coming here again.Fried rice was good. It has small fried fish and Chinese pork sausage.We run into this place walking around NYC. Wouldn't return here..

I made Yelp reservations and you need to have reservations as this place is jumping on a Saturday night.  We came here slightly late but had called about our delay and when we arrived, we were seated right away, right behind the hostess desk, in a cozy booth for 4.  With yelp check-in and purchase of an entree, you get a complimentary empanada so we had separate checks and each got empanadas which were ok.  We ordered the Pollo Asado, Pernil Asado, Ensalada de Salmon con Mango, and Ensalada de Pollo con Limon y cana.  My chicken with lime and avocado was good but as chicken breast goes, it was slightly dry.  The atmosphere was great, alittle noisy but I was hoping to hear some lively Latin music and we did but there was no place to dance.  For dessert, we ordered the tropical cheesecake and flan.  The cheesecake was a small slice for $9 which is a bit high for a small piece.  All in all, it was a nice experience, server was attentive and atmosphere was lively and noisy.

Was such a great experience! Went hear with a friend and the dining was really nice from start to finish. The restaurant looks nice with a lot of people around, but still felt intimate. I had never cooked my ow food before, but ended up loving it! We were able to get a special where we tried different types of meats and sides, all pretty good, in addition to 2 DOLLAR BEERS! Unheard of in NYC, especially on the UES. And that was recommended but the server who was very informative throughout. Would definitely come here again and recommend to others!

Title: Quirky Morning Fare at a New NYC Coffee Joint

On a bustling NYC weekend, I decided to give a new coffee shop a whirl, hoping it would stand out in the crowded café landscape of the city. The menu had an interesting take, branding a variety of pastries as "danishes," though that might be a generous interpretation of the term.

I opted for convenience and ordered a to-go selection through Grubhub. Among the offerings, loaves of bread, enticingly displayed behind the register, caught my eye – certainly something to consider for next time.

The chocolate and hazelnut danish I chose leaned heavily into its chocolate identity, with hazelnut playing a supporting role. Nevertheless, the flavor balance was commendable. The pistachio coffee cake didn't fare as well, coming off a tad dry – though, in fairness, it was an end slice, which may have been the culprit. The accompanying latte was standard fare; nothing that would make it a standout in the city's competitive coffee scene. A wider array of drink sizes available for delivery would have been appreciated.

This café may not have completely wowed me, but it's got potential. I'm intrigued enough to consider a second visit for what I hope will be a redemption arc in the form of their proper breakfast fare.

Had a really solid meal at Rong Chen House.  I read about the Dan Dan Noodles and the MaPo Tofu so I had to try it.Both were very well seasoned.  The Dan Dan Noodles although very tasty lacked the overall fire that I have come to expect with this dish.  I ate it all, don't get me wrong but not especially spicy.The MaPo Tofu made up for it.  The combination of garlic, ground pork and chili and green onion, it was all so good together, it gave you the numbing burn on your lips a good szechuan dish requires.The prices were reasonable for the city, the service was top notch and the atmosphere pretty authentic.All good reasons to come back again!

This NYC eatery lives up to its reputation as a hot spot, evidenced by the hour and 15-minute wait. Fortunately, guests can leave their cell number and stroll the nearby High Line while awaiting a text for their table. The menu delights with offerings like the succulent Chicken Biscuit, savory Steak Sandwich, fresh Avo Toast, and a classic Hamburger. Each dish was met with pleasure from our group, ensuring a satisfying dining experience.

I recently brunched at a spot that masters the art of reinventing the classic with a delightful American Southern twist – their take on the Eggs Benedict, the "Benedict Johnny," is a revelation! With a base of cheddar cornbread and a juicy maple chicken sausage replacing the traditional English muffin and ham, this dish strikes the perfect balance between innovation and comfort. The poached eggs are draped in a sumptuous roasted tomato hollandaise, elevating each bite without overshadowing the simple, grounded flavors. Accompanying the dish, the home fries are nothing short of a crispy, seasoned triumph – little bite-sized treasures that complement the main without competing for attention. It's worth noting, securing a table for brunch requires foresight to book a few days in advance or the patience to endure a lengthy wait, but rest assured, it is entirely worthwhile for such a gratifying meal.

Title: Quick Sushi Fix at Sashimi Express

Looking for a swift sushi solution without breaking the bank? Sashimi Express has got you covered. Their enticing offer of 7 rolls for just $21.75 means you can satisfy your sushi craving on a budget, with a variety of rolls to tantalize your taste buds. 

They operate out of two conveniently placed outlets, one on East 78th and another on East 74th — a gentle reminder to double-check the address when calling in your order. Service is fast, the staff is amiable, and the prices are easy on the wallet. 

While it might not rival the upscale sushi joints, Sashimi Express delivers on freshness and value. And if you're not in a rush, they've got seating, so you can comfortably enjoy your meal on-site. For those in need of a quick sushi bite, this spot is highly recommended.

Title: A Delightful Pink Gem – Pietro Nolita

From its Instagram popularity to its charming pink interior, Pietro Nolita is a millennial’s haven tucked away in the bustling city. This quaint Italian eatery not only entices with its visual appeal but also satisfies the palate with exceptional cuisine.

As a first-timer, the restaurant immediately impressed with a festive and cozy atmosphere, complemented by lush greenery – a perfect backdrop for those social media snapshots. But let’s talk about the star of the show – the food.

The Brussels sprouts appetizer set the bar high, a delightful concoction that even had a self-proclaimed bacon skeptic nodding in approval. The main course, lemon fusilli pasta, was a symphony of flavors, expertly portioned to satiate without overwhelming.

Accompanying the delicious fare was the Sneak Pink cocktail, a refreshing masterpiece that had me at a loss for words. Pietro Nolita is not just about looks; it’s a culinary experience that keeps you coming back for more.

The intimate yet vibrant setting was perfect for a delightful dinner with friends, and the anticipation of exploring their breakfast offerings has me planning my next visit. Pietro Nolita, you've earned a spot on my go-to list for Italian cuisine!

Title: Pricey but Delicious Korean Fare in the Big Apple

Last night, my friends and I dined at a Korean restaurant in New York, and the experience was a mix of delight and surprise. The food, I must say, was commendable. We indulged in both the pork and beef combos, which were cooked to perfection, and paired our meal with an assortment of drinks.

However, what stole the show was the melon bar makgeolli – a recommendation I am eternally grateful for. It was an absolute treat, capturing the essence of the beloved Asian melon bar ice cream in a refreshing alcoholic beverage. It's a must-try for anyone visiting.

On the downside, our wallets felt the weight of the city's reputation for lofty prices. For a group of eight, the bill soared close to $700, which was an unexpectedly steep spend for Korean cuisine. Despite the steep prices, the quality of the food in New York, particularly at this restaurant, lived up to its fantastic reputation.

If you're a Detroit-style pizza aficionado, then this is your haven. Upon visiting, I indulged in the 'Big Ang' and 'The Angel' pies — both exceptional in their own right. The 'Angel Pie' is a symphony of flavors with its creamy ricotta, earthy mushrooms, and decadent Truffleist mushroom cream, confirming my love affair with anything truffle. The 'Big Ang', on the other hand, offers a harmonious balance of house-made vodka sauce, rich ricotta, sharp double pecorino, hearty meatballs, and a kick of banana peppers. Both pizzas boast a fusion of ingredients that create an unforgettable taste experience. This place is a must-try — especially for truffle and ricotta enthusiasts!

Celebrating my birthday at this spot turned out to be a fantastic decision. While the ambiance leans more casual than romantic, the quality of the cuisine truly stood out. As someone with a keen appreciation for good food, the glowing reviews that led me here were spot on. The menu, which I'd describe as upscale bar food, did not disappoint in the slightest—every bite from appetizers to entrees, accompanied by well-crafted drinks, was a delight. It's also worth noting that this would be an excellent choice for unwinding after work. Highly recommend for fellow food enthusiasts looking for a laid-back yet delicious dining experience.

Upon stepping off the ferry at Governors Island, a delightful eatery welcomes you to the left with its swift service and inviting atmosphere. The spot boasts a commendable beer selection perfect for every connoisseur. As you sip on your brew, you're treated to a spectacular view of the Manhattan skyline that truly enhances the dining experience.

The culinary highlight is a burger imbued with a tantalizing grilled essence, paired exquisitely with refreshing homemade guacamole. The side of fries is no mere afterthought; they add a playful twist to the meal.

Special mention must be given to Zen, whose empathetic service ensures that every order is captured with precision. The staff's overall efficiency and friendliness are reasons enough for a return visit. A true gem on Governors Island, this spot is a must-visit for anyone looking for good food with a great view.

Got in right under the buzzer on a Thursday for happy hour.  The server was kind enough to honor happy hour even a few minutes after it ended. The house wine was ok, but the mango margarita was great.  I was surprised we got a table to sit at in the bar area since it was a Thursday night. Also ordered spicy guacamole which was delicious.  Would definitely come back here, at least for happy hour, if not dinner.

Szechuan food is one of my favorite cuisine and this place did not disappoint. Was craving for some spicy and Málà Chinese food while in the area and this place delivered. We ordered a bunch of dishes including sautéed string beans, spicy garlic eggplant, fish fillet in numbing spicy broth and everything was spicy and yummy. And also the portion was beyond generous for the price and also the food came out super hot and fast. The only thing we ordered that we didn't like (not pictured) was the tofu with crab meat. It did not have any crab inside and was lack in flavor. Service was also super friendly. Definitely recommended

Brontosaurus rib was my favorite here. These are the ones you see in Instagram. It was huge. May be I finished it in three sittings. As you can see in the picture there is oil oozing out of the ribs. This is tallow, which is the natural beef fat. After twenty minutes tallow will solidify into a solid white fat. Dirty frites was also nice and flavorful. Brisket and burnt ends were ok. Whatever you eat, pour a ton of barbeque sauce. There sauce is extremely good. Don't hesitate, just pour all over.

Still probably my fave spot in town! Came here for restaurant week brunch with 2 friends - we had a reservation and were seated more or less immediately upon arrival. Love that during the summer months brunch is on the roof, with both indoor and outdoor seating available! We decided to sit indoors since it was a bit hot, but it's nice to have the option.Restaurant week brunch is also a great deal for $26! I got the hellfire roll, salmon a la plancha with kale pesto, and the vanilla Oreo banana pudding. All of the food was delicious - the tuna on the hellfire roll tasted very fresh, and my salmon was perfectly cooked. I also need to figure out a way to get my hands on that kale pesto recipe - definitely one of my favorite sauces! The vanilla Oreo banana pudding is a restaurant week brunch dessert special - it was a larger portion than I was expecting served in a mason jar, more pudding like than Oreo like, with a lot of berry and fruity tones to it! I was a fan, although it was slightly different than what I was expecting! Highly recommend Catch no matter the meal or time of year, but there's no doubt that restaurant week is a prime time to make a visit and try out some new dishes, too!

I'm not a soup fanatic however there are some creamy soups that I love such as Loaded Baked Potato Soup, Lobster Bisque, and New England Clam Chowder.My Hunny picked me up a large Lobster Bisque soup to accommodate my diet. My meal came with an apple, bread, and a Lindt Milk Chocolate ball. I couldn't believe that my soup was considered a large. The container was awfully small. Albeit the soup was good, I've had better. I'd definitely pass on the extra side of sodium included. After each bite I found myself getting thirstier and thirstier. Soup shouldn't taste processed. I would've appreciated if the consistency was less watery and on the thicker side. Also the soup to lobster ratio was off.

After much anticipation, I finally visited a restaurant that came highly recommended by my husband's cousin. My expectations were surpassed as the ramen proved to be quite delightful—rich in flavor and generous in portion, easily shareable between two. The gyoza also left a lasting impression, tempting my taste buds with its savory taste. Our party of eight faced a bit of a challenge finding seating together, which was a minor inconvenience. Additionally, there's a $9 per person minimum to be aware of. Despite the seating hiccup, the food experience alone is enough to warrant a return visit.

Took my dad here the other night for a nice dinner and we were definitely not disappointed. We started with two aperitifs: crispy, slightly sweet beet chips and chickpea fritters with aioli. Both were light and delicious. We got the cauliflower steak, which was resting on the most delicious sauce ( I don't recall exactly what it was, but it was pesto-y and so tasty). My dad ordered the trout. The piece was on the smaller side, but he said that the fish and string beans almondine were delicious. I got the summer corn gnocchi- the gnocchi were large and fluffy, and the corn gave it a sweet flavor that I wasn't expecting, but definitely enjoyed. To close, we tried the lemon tart, and my personal favorite: the warm, housemade Madeleines. (They were phenomenal.) To add to the amazing food, the service was absolutely amazing from the moment we walked in, throughout our meal, until we left.

Title: An Authentic Japanese Culinary Journey at Shuraku

I stumbled upon Shuraku while seeking a unique Japanese dining experience for my boyfriend’s birthday, diverging from our usual omakase routine. Their eight-course tasting menu, priced at $110 per person, seemed like an exciting alternative and was reasonable for a tasting menu.

The meal commenced with a simple yet satisfying homemade tofu in dashi soy with wasabi. The highlight arrived early with seared Miyazaki beef sushi topped with uni, a sumptuous combination complemented by pickled daikon. Not all dishes were hits; the spring vegetable gelée was a miss, but the perfectly seared cherry trout redeemed the course.

Yakitori offerings, including chicken and duck paired with citrusy yuzu kosho and black shichimi, were memorable, although it was hard to distinguish them individually. A palate-cleansing broth featuring spring turnip and baby sardines followed, setting the stage for the standout grilled carabineros prawn, reminiscent of my time in Barcelona, and a succulent Hokkaido scallop.

The washu beef culotte was perfectly cooked, though I was left curious about the option to upgrade to the Miyazaki A5. The Inaniwa udon with ikura and ume tororo was an unexpected cold dish and didn't quite meet the warming, chewy noodle finish I had anticipated.

My boyfriend's night culminated with homemade strawberry ice cream, which he adored, although it struck me as ordinary. As for drinks, my lemon cocktail was passable, while his old-fashioned was reliably good.

A small disappointment was the lack of birthday acknowledgment, despite having noted the occasion when reserving seats at the chef's counter, but it was a minor blemish on an otherwise impressive evening.

The ambiance at Shuraku, with its minimalist design and even a bidet-equipped restroom, transported me back to Japan. While there were a few imperfections, the overall experience was a delightful foray into Japanese cuisine.

Upon visiting this charming restaurant on a bustling Friday night, our experience was delightful despite the brief wait for a table of two around 8 PM. The staff was exceptionally friendly, adding to the warm atmosphere. We savored the enchiladas and pork quesadillas, both of which were scrumptious and well-received. The quality of the meal and the service received made the visit worthwhile. We left with the intention of returning, eager to explore more of the menu. Highly recommend for a satisfying dining experience.

I recently visited this local pizzeria and was pleasantly surprised by their unique selection of gourmet slices. The ravioli and chicken Parmesan with vodka sauce pizzas were standout choices, offering a delicious twist on classic Italian flavors. At $5.25 per specialty slice, the prices reflect the quality and creativity of the offerings. The restaurant boasts ample seating, which made for a comfortable dining experience without a long wait. Service was prompt and friendly, adding to the positive experience. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Mayas grain bowl , green shakshouka eggs, tomato and grilled halloumi poached eggs All rolled out one by one and neither of them was below average. I will say in terms of Technical's cooking, the Sunnyside and poached eggs were cooked to perfection respectively and the seasonings were rather mild. However it was really the flourless chocolate cake with a warm ganache scoop, And a swirl of caramel that stole the show. Very busy and can't get loud but is an iconic spot to hang out for brunch

Title: A Unique Twist on Korean Cuisine That Impresses

From the moment my companions and I stepped into this innovative Korean eatery, we were captivated by the vibrant atmosphere – an ideal setting for both romance and spirited business discussions. The staff was exceptionally helpful, guiding us through a menu replete with creative twists on classic Korean dishes, a true godsend given our limited experience with the cuisine.

The Korean BBQ served here is unlike any I've encountered; it's a must-try for both aficionados and newcomers alike. What really stood out was their conscientious approach to gluten-free options, ensuring that dietary needs didn't compromise the quality or uniqueness of the meal.

The Bi Bim Bap arrived sizzling in a stone bowl, its flavors and textures a delightful surprise. Don't overlook the sticky buns and the Kalbi Jim – both dishes were remarkable and left a lasting impression. Whether you're a Korean food veteran or eager to explore, this restaurant is a standout choice that promises to excite the palate.

Title: A New York Gem Not to Be Missed!

Ever had an experience where a single dish compels you to alter your travel plans? That's the power of "The ROB" sandwich from this unassuming NYC eatery that has now become my must-visit spot in the city. It's not just a sandwich, it's a revelation! The perfect harmony of flavors - from the freshly baked bread, tender kale, savory ham, melting cheese, to the divine touch of balsamic - left me utterly enamored.

Size isn't everything when it comes to restaurants, and this cozy spot is proof. The seating may be limited, but it's more than compensated by the quality of the food and the cordial service. The menu, although modest, is a showcase of well-thought-out delicacies. The gentleman at the counter was notably helpful, offering detailed explanations and ensuring a pleasant ordering experience.

Beyond their phenomenal sandwiches, the establishment also offers a selection of cold beverages. The prices? Surprisingly reasonable, especially considering the high-quality fare served.

In short, this restaurant delivers an exceptional culinary experience that outshines any ambiance reservations. Do yourself a favor - don't miss out on this place next time you're in NYC. I know I won't!

Oh I really wanted to enjoy my meal but something was off with the uní (sea urchin) I had on Monday night. I am a big uni lover and do not have a sensitive tummy but oh boy, I didn't do so well the morning after having my uni don dinner.I think it was a fluke that the uni wasn't super fresh (I also tasted some pieces of rocks in my uni). My friends got other bowls such as the three amigos and they loved it!Aside from my bad experience, the place was very cozy with oversized booth and the staffs were friendly.Also give the plum/orange wine a try, it was delicious. If the yam sticks are on the menu, make sure to try that!

Title: A Taste of Singapore with a Steep Price Tag

Ambiance: Chill and nicely decorated, the restaurant immediately set a positive tone upon our arrival, honoring our reservation with prompt seating.

Starters: The fried lotus root starter was a delightful novelty—crispy and well-seasoned with peppers, salt, and onions. Although the chicken wings were perfectly fried, they lacked any standout qualities.

Mains: The highlight of the meal was the Singaporean laksa, boasting a mix of thick egg and thin rice noodles in a fragrant coconut curry broth, accompanied by tofu and cucumber strands. The redang beef was tender and flavorful, while the Assam laksa's tantalizing aroma hinted at its spiciness, which deterred me from sampling it given its heat. The portions were reasonable, yet the absence of protein in the Assam laksa was noted.

Value: While the restaurant captures a semblance of Singapore's culinary essence, the prices are steep compared to nearby alternatives in Chinatown.

Conclusion: Despite the satisfying flavors, the high prices are a deterrent for frequent visits. Worth a try for those seeking a Singaporean cuisine experience, but be prepared to pay a premium.

eh, i didn't pick this spot and it shows...  lol.the restaurant wasn't too packed when we showed up on a sunday (and it remained so the whole time while we were there).  anyway, we debated between the bottomless brunch and decided to just order the brunch entrees.  -crab cakes benny:  tasty and super filling-southern sweet hash and eggs: my friend got this and she liked it okas stated on the menu, the brunch entrees come with fruit cup, coffeecake, coffee or tea, and a cocktail.  not sure if our server was new or they're trying to skimp on things, we didn't get the fruit cup, had to ask for the coffee, cocktail (peach bellini was WEAK), coffeecake.  when i asked about the coffeecake, the server legit asked, "oh, you want the coffeecake?  how many?"  well how many brunch entrees did we ordered?  by the end, our server had gone missing and we had to ask a different server for our check.  quite frankly, the food was aight but service was very sorely lacking.

Title: A Toast to Memorable Mixology and Charming Surprises

Review: My recent visit to this gem as a self-proclaimed tourist can only be described as an awesome experience. My coworkers and I decided to explore the local drink scene during a work trip, and we made our way here for some happy hour indulgence. The cocktail selection blew us away! Not only was it extensive, catering to every conceivable taste preference with creative traditional, sour, spicy, and sweet concoctions, but the menu's unique organization by glass type added a touch of flair to our selections.

But the highlight? The delightful twist of a complimentary postcard service. Guests can pen a message and have it sent anywhere in the world, courtesy of the restaurant. It's a thoughtful, personal touch that elevated the entire evening. Kudos to this establishment for not only mastering the art of mixology but also for adding a little extra heart to the experience.

Title: A Lukewarm Experience at DokoDemo

My latest jaunt to DokoDemo left me with mixed feelings. As an aficionado of Japanese street food, I came in with expectations shaped by previous experiences, particularly Otafuku's okonomiyaki, which this eatery struggled to match. The chicken okonomiyaki I sampled was unremarkable—underseasoned and lacking depth of flavor, saved only by the welcome crunch of cabbage. The takoyaki fared better, with a balanced dough-to-octopus proportion and a tasty wasabi mayo (worth the extra charge), though be warned—they're served almost too hot to handle.

While the food didn't hit all the marks, the setting didn't disappoint. With a genial staff and a spotless environment, DokoDemo has the makings of a decent pit-stop, especially post-drink cravings hit and you're in the vicinity. If nothing else, the experience was boosted by the presence of friendly service and a clean, communal space.

I completely forgot to take pics of our food because when it arrived it all looked so good I just had to dive right in! Wait was about 10 minutes at 7PM on a Thursday night! I had seen this Tacombi getting ready since I moved to the UWS in November and couldn't wait to try it once it opened. The decor/ atmosphere/ aesthetic of this restaurant is awesome! It was very photographable and I love the big windows letting all the light in. I do wish that the high top stools had a little ledge I could rest my feet on ... but that's a personal issue lol. I like the idea of filling out a sheet of paper for our order but also kind of felt like that was a waste of paper ...The staff was incredibly nice. Every waiter/waitress came up to us and asked if we needed anything, filled our waters as soon as they needed it, and were just so gracious and sweet. We got the queso to share (thought it was going to just be chips and queso and it ended up being so much more!!!!!) it was so so good but we hadn't even gotten thru half of it by the time our food arrived! Everything arrived very fresh and very fast- I do wish they would have maybe spaced out our entrees so we could have had time to digest and enjoy our appetizer. I got a pork taco and chicken taco which were both incredible. I thought I would like the chicken more but the pork was by far my favorite. The chicken was a litttttle too spicy for me but I'm also a big baby so don't listen to me. The pork was a little sweet and essentially melted in your mouth. It was so good. My boyfriend got two kinds of seafood tacos and he loved his too! We also got rice and beans to split but we were so full by the end of it we decided to just wrap it up and take it home. The gave us a postcard to take home with us at the end and the whole meal was super cheap and great for a quick weeknight stop when you don't feel like cooking! Will definitely be coming back. One more shout out to all the employees here- so so so nice, I cannot stress that enough!

Title: A Mix-Up with a Silver Lining at [Restaurant Name]

During my recent visit to [Restaurant Name], I encountered a bit of a mix-up. Intending to dine at the restaurant, I was unwittingly seated in the adjoining cafe, leading to a bit of confusion over the dual menus and their offerings.

The limited options were exacerbated by a series of communication mishaps, culminating in my desired dish being unavailable. However, the responsiveness from the staff was commendable. The manager's repeated apologies and offer of complimentary drinks were thoughtful gestures that didn't go unnoticed.

Ultimately, I settled on the bagel and lox. To my delight, the smoked salmon was exceptional, arguably the best I've savored to date. As for the standard breakfast plate, it was unremarkable but competently prepared.

Despite the initial disorder, the staff's attentive service and the quality of the smoked salmon make [Restaurant Name] worth another visit, albeit with clearer expectations.

Title: A Seafood Convert at My New Favorite Spot

After my delightful second visit to this local gem, I'm convinced it's the ideal destination for all my special outings. My culinary journey began with skepticism towards seafood, but the spicy chicken sandwich from my first visit had me hooked and curious to dive deeper into the menu. This time, I braved the snow crab legs, and they did not disappoint. Served with corn, potatoes, and a heavenly garlic butter sauce, they were nothing short of spectacular.

The culinary adventure didn't stop there; coaxed by my mom, I sampled an oyster. Despite its off-putting appearance, I was pleasantly surprised by its burst of flavor. It's safe to say, I'm now an oyster aficionado.

During our visit, the 1 1/2 pound lobster, although modest in size with its "freaking skinny legs," was delectable and complemented with a choice of shrimp or clams. We capitalized on the happy hour deal, savoring a dozen oysters at merely a dollar each.

Despite my enduring love for the spicy chicken sandwich with its tangy Cajun sauce and the option of fries or salad, what truly capped off this visit was the turnaround in customer service. Unlike the initial visit marred by Anastasia's lackluster service and reluctance to split our check, this time we were greeted with warmth and attentiveness from our server, whose name escapes me. It's reassuring to see that good service can prevail in the same establishment where it once faltered.

I am eagerly looking forward to my next visit for another round of exceptional seafood—and yes, maybe another spicy chicken sandwich too!

This is definitely not the best or most authentic Vietnamese experience you can get in New York, but for the area it's in, it's pretty understandable. The prices here are relatively affordable and the portions are filling. I was surprised they also sold tea by the pot, but they only put one tea bag in the pot so it tastes quite weak. The food is just okay. It definitely tastes like it's missing something like a bit more fish sauce or lemongrass. The restaurant itself is nice and clean and the bathroom is huge.

Title: Reliving Seinfeld’s Magic at the Iconic Diner

During my recent visit to the famed diner from Seinfeld, the experience was more about soaking in the nostalgic vibes than the culinary offerings. As a long-time fan of the show, the opportunity to physically occupy the space where so many hilarious scenes unfolded was nothing short of epic. Though the food served was basic and what you'd expect from a typical diner, it wasn't the main draw. Instead, sitting at the very spot where the iconic quartet of characters bantered and delivered their perfectly timed jokes allowed me to witness the diner's unique charm. It's a must-visit for any Seinfeld enthusiast looking to capture a piece of television history.

Title: A Delightful Seafood Experience at Seamores

My wife and I recently dined at Seamores, where we indulged in the "Reel Deal," and let me tell you, it was an absolute delight! The fresh haddock was seasoned to perfection, accompanied by three scrumptious sides that added to the meal's charm. To top it off, the red curry was a standout—rich and full of flavor. I can't recommend the Reel Deal highly enough for anyone visiting this establishment. As for the ambiance, Seamores boasts an elegant and bright setting, making it an ideal spot for a spring or summer date. Overall, Seamores didn't just make my wife happy—it left us both thrilled with a dining experience to remember.

Their mac and cheese with pepperoni pizza is. The. Bomb. From the crispy thin crust to the cheesy buttery goodness of the mac and cheese to the pepperoni, they were all so good and surprisingly worked really well together. I honestly wasn't expecting it to be that good, but it was well worth my $4. Would most definitely go back again to try their other pizzas or just stick to this one.

The desserts pushed this one to 5 stars for me: the chocolate mousse with meringue "crackers" was heavenly. It's a creative spot, blending French technique and American classics (like their take on cheese sticks). It's all biodynamique, including the wines. (The red wine we had was ok, but I loved my white wine!)My chicken entree was great--juicy and with creamy whipped potatoes. But surprisingly my favorite thing (besides dessert) was the lentil salad!

Nestled in Hell's Kitchen, this gem brings Korean flavors beyond the typical bounds of K-town. A trio of us indulged in a spread including succulent galbi paired with creamy corn cheese, a mix of sweet and spicy chicken wings, and the comforting heft of dukbokki topped with a crispy chicken katsu. Each dish left us satisfyingly stuffed, a testament to the generous portions. Hospitality was top-notch; both the owner and our server exuded warmth, enhancing the dining experience. This spot has earned its place as my go-to Korean eatery when I'm in the neighborhood.

Title: A Memorable Evening at a Superb Italian Gem

After a recommendation from a friend, I experienced a fantastic dinner at a delightful Italian restaurant that truly lived up to the hype. Despite a brief mix-up with our group going to different locations, we were easily accommodated just a few blocks away on 9th Ave. The warm welcome was complemented by a vast array of enticing menu options.

Choosing to bypass the Restaurant Week offerings, we indulged in the normal menu, with an exception for the burrata from the prix fixe menu. This decision did not disappoint. The shared starters of burrata, Brussels sprouts, and crab cakes were nothing short of phenomenal, setting the stage for our main courses.

For our entrees, the pasta dishes reigned supreme. My rigatoni with pink sauce was exquisite, a divine indulgence that validated every carb. Accompanied by top-notch wine selections, the meal was culinary bliss.

Service throughout the evening was impeccable—attentive without being overbearing. Although there was a slight delay in receiving our checks, this minor hiccup did nothing to dampen the spirits of an otherwise perfect dining experience. I can confidently say this Italian place is a must-visit for foodies and casual diners alike.

This place is f***ing incredible. I've never tasted chocolate so rich in my life. The service is pretty good and sometimes you have to wait, but we were able to get a reservation just 20 minutes in advance (check open table before you go there to avoid waiting at least a half hour)!I ordered the peanut butter hot chocolate, which was the most amazing hot chocolate I've ever tasted in my life. It was the perfect balance of peanut butter and chocolate. Everyone at my table also ordered dessert drinks (hot chocolate and milkshakes) and agreed that my drink was the best.We also ordered a "The Works" dessert pizza! It was $19 but worth it to split between four people (and believe me, that's plenty). All of the flavors in this were so great. I would highly recommend!! It's also right next to Union Square - great location and ambiance. They also have a chocolate gift shop in the entrance! And their chocolate covered pecans are the best things I've ever tasted.

Title: Cozy Dinner Before a Show

My husband, best friend, and I stopped by this ramen spot last Sunday before catching The Christmas Spectacular Rockettes. Craving a warm bowl of ramen, we decided to finally try this place. Despite no reservations, a 35-minute wait, eased by drinks at the nearby Center Bar, wasn't too bad.

The atmosphere captured us upon being seated – buzzing and vibrant. Our server, Steven, was proficient. Opting for the Smoked Pork Ramen on recommendation, we passed on the Spicy Beef Ramen. My friend enjoyed the Ginger Scallion Noodles. We sipped sparkling rosé and Tiger beer alongside, both agreeably good.

While the smoked pork in my ramen was a highlight, the overall dish was a bit of a letdown, particularly because the broth served lukewarm didn't hit the spot. Next time, I'm keen to try the Spicy Beef Ramen in hopes of a five-star experience.

Title: A Cozy Swiss Haven in the Heart of the City

My companion and I sought refuge from the biting cold in this charming Swiss enclave, greeted by its warm and inviting atmosphere. As a recently-returned Swiss enthusiast, my friend was keen to indulge in a shared culinary journey back to the Alps.

We settled on a communal fondue experience, enriched by a rare Swiss wine selection that paired exquisitely with the hearty, melted delight. It's a rarity to find such authentic wine outside of Switzerland, and it's a testament to the restaurant's dedication to an authentic experience.

Augmenting our meal, we savored an additional shared entrée. The veal was a standout – its tenderness and savory gravy were a testament to the kitchen's prowess.

Service was commendable; patience personified as we mulled over the enticing options. The presence of numerous regulars hinted at the restaurant's role as a cherished local haunt, perfect for unwinding after a long day.

In summary, this gem offers an unrivaled combination of ambiance, exceptional cuisine, and wine. It's an idyllic spot for reconnecting with friends and savoring the warmth of Swiss hospitality right here in NYC.

My recent visit to a local restaurant renowned for its clay pot rice, or "rice casseroles," was prompted by a desire to compare it with my experiences at Clay Pot NYC. Confirmation that their specialities began at 11am set the tone for an anticipated meal.

On arrival, I opted for the combination pot featuring yellow eel, salted chicken, and beef navel. Patience during the 15-20 minute wait was rewarded with a beautifully crisped rice base, hallmark of a well-executed clay pot dish. While the quantity was generous, easily serving one or stretching to two meals, the toppings lacked the robust flavor I craved. Resorting to soy sauce for enhancement, I noted this as an area where Clay Pot NYC maintains an edge with their specialty sauce.

Despite this, the $10 price point offered incredible value, especially considering the ample inclusion of meat. Sampling my friend's char siu and cuttlefish rice, I was impressed. The char siu, notably succulent and well-seasoned, stood out as one of New York's finest.

The restaurant presented a clean and bright atmosphere, accompanied by good service. Although limited to four-person seating, this minor inconvenience would not dissuade me from future visits.

In summary, this establishment delivers on its promise of tasty, value-driven dining options. It's a spot I'll surely return to, eager to explore more of their culinary offerings.

Really enjoyed my experience at Yunshang. Came here for lunch on a Saturday as a party of 4 and we were seated quickly.I got the Spicy broth with no add ons and felt like it filled me up perfectly. They brought out the ingredients first. The ingredients were fresh and I really enjoyed the noodles (endless noodles!). Next, they brought out the soup bowl (sizzling) for you to dump the ingredients into and "assemble" your soup. They also gave some recommendations on what ingredients to put in first and for how long. I also felt like the spicy broth was quite flavorful. Overall, I highly recommend this place because they give a pretty good amount of food for a decent price!

Title: A Friendly Nook with a Touch of Old World Charm

After a peaceful ferry ride to Wall Street, my search for a stroller-accommodating and proximate dining option led me to this restaurant. The staff welcomed us with open arms, confirming their child and baby-friendly policy. While navigating a stroller required conquering a few steps, the team was helpful, prying open the double doors to assist us.

The ambiance, however, struck a somber note. Amidst the summer's cheer, the restaurant's dim lighting and drawn curtains transported us to a bygone era, reminiscent of clandestine elite gatherings. It added a touch of drama but was unexpectedly dark for an afternoon setting.

Our culinary journey began with a spicy pineapple margarita and white sangria, accompanied by a selection of small yet savory oysters, a fresh baby kale salad, and a satisfying burger. The pricing of the oysters at $3 apiece seemed steep against their size, and a curiously cut lemon became a tiny hurdle in our dining experience.

A brief misstep occurred when our drinks were momentarily forgotten, but the staff's gesture of complimentary mimosas smoothed over the hiccup. Both the libations and the food delivered on quality and taste, confirming that good things do indeed come in small packages—or in this case, small, dark, but decidedly welcoming spaces.

Cute small restaurant specializing in truffle in Greenwich VillageOverall: 4/5Food: 4/5Service: 4/5Value: 4/5We got the two classic pastas topped with black truffle. Both were fantastic, very flavorful and the portion was right such that it wasn't overly filling. Feel like one of the pastas got more truffle on top than the other, but I guess that's the variation in hand grating. The bread was nice and warm as well, and perfect for scooping up every last drop of decadent sauce! It's a small spot so reservations probably recommended. Service was pretty good. The prices definitely aren't that cheap but truffle is expensive which I assume is the bulk of the cost... a nice date spot overall if you're willing to spend a bit!

I recently visited a quaint little eatery that specializes in Japanese street food, and I must say, I was thoroughly impressed. The standout dish was the yakisoba drenched in a savory tonkatsu broth – simply divine with its perfectly seasoned flavors and delightfully chewy noodles. I found myself wishing they offered a soup ramen twist on this dish; I'd be eager to taste it. We also savored some takoyaki, which was tasty, although the octopus inside was slightly on the chewier side. Nevertheless, this spot is a gem for street food aficionados.

First time at Han Dynasty was a 5 star experience! I went with my mom and we were seated promptly. Service was quick and friendly without being overbearing. We shared the dan dan noodles which were very tasty with a peanut tasting sauce that was pretty spicy (warning for wimps). We also had the wontons in chili oil which were INCREDIBLE. One of my favorite dishes I've had in New York to be honest. A unique flavor I haven't had elsewhere. I can't wait to come back and try more!

Title: Perfect Pre-Theater Dining Experience

My go-to spot for a meal before catching a show is this gem of a restaurant. Though the wait can be expected, it's always swift, ensuring you're on time for your event. The generous portions make it ideal for sharing, which suits our group perfectly. Our staples include the antipasta salad and a variety of pizzas and pastas, all delectable without exception. The gluten-free pizza is a noteworthy option – flavorful and satisfying. Highly recommended for a tasty, efficient dining experience.

I recently had the opportunity to try the veggie teriyaki bowl from this restaurant, as it was chosen for my first day of work team lunch. While I missed out on the actual dining experience, I found the food to be solid overall. The bowl was flavorful and fitting for a lunchtime meal. As for whether I would make this a regular lunch spot, the jury is still out, but it's a definite contender based on this initial tasting.

Rubirosa in NYC didn't just meet expectations; it soared beyond them. Their thin-crust pizza, a masterpiece of flavor and texture, has confidently claimed a spot in my top five NYC pizza rankings. My boyfriend and I shared a half-and-half pizza – one side classic, one side vodka. Though we skipped their famed tie-dye pizza due to his aversion to pesto, there were zero regrets. The classic sauce leaned towards the sweeter side, while the vodka sauce was beautifully light without being overbearing. And the crust? Exquisitely crispy, making me yearn for another slice as I write.

We kicked off the meal with mouthwatering appetizers: mozzarella sticks and meatballs, the latter containing veal – not my usual pick, yet these were undeniably the most succulent meatballs I've had the pleasure of tasting.

The main course, a shareable chicken Parmesan, came with homemade spaghetti. It was portioned perfectly, leaving us both satisfied with an equal helping of chicken and pasta.

Alas, our indulgence in the savory left no room for dessert. This isn't goodbye, Rubirosa – it's a definite "see you soon" for yet another round of culinary delight.

A solid Chinese American takeout like you would find in many neighborhoods. I would give Totten an extra star for being able to remain open whole most Chinese takeout restaurants in NYC have closed during this pandemic. The pork fried rice was moist and not dry. The general tso chicken was crispy and moist but could use a little less sauce which was overflowing and more heat.

This place has been on Wall st since 1827. Can you imagine what people have eaten in this dining room over 100 years ago?John Jacob Astor, Frank W Woolworth, James Cash Penney, Gorden Gekko. (Lunch is for wimps!) and now, Me. Billy Salts. It's New York City Restaurant week and I had to bring my wife for dinner. She's never been here and I wanted to show her a nice night.When you first walk into the lobby, to the left is cooler that has the different cuts of beef. From Dry Aged Beef to their signature cut, Delmonico's has history. It's the first restaurant to have table cloths, the first restaurant to serve eggs Benedict and the menu explains how they invented Lobster Newburg as well as Baked Alaska.Over the years I remember ordering their dish called "Shellfish Chateau": Oysters, Lobster, King Crab, Blue Crab, Jumbo Shrimp and Green Tip Mussels.Tonight we're here to experience their Delmonico Cut Signature Steak but I have to write about their dessert. It was soooooo good! I told my wife we have to try the baked Alaska. She said we had the baked Alaska in Alaska? I was going to order the cheesecake but the chocolate souffle sounds really good. The chocolate souffle comes to each of us, there is a texture inside the souffle, it truly was a dessert symphony. The signature steak? From the first bite, it was very decadent. The exterior had a great crust. The steak was cooked perfectly, it was a nice thick cut. Maybe because of restaurant week, my cut was very fatty. I had to trim off at least 10 percent fat off. I know marbling is flavor but this was just too much IMHO.Overall, we had a great restaurant week meal. I can honestly say, this was one of the top five steaks in New York City. Very easy to get to by the subway, take the 2/3 to Wall St. Look for those iconic massive doors!

Title: Celebratory Feast at Golden Unicorn's Lunar New Year Banquet

I recently had the opportunity to attend a Lunar New Year Banquet at Golden Unicorn, a place I'd been eager to try. This experience was not their typical dim sum offering but a special event, which made it all the more exciting.

Upon arrival, we were greeted with a variety of family-style dishes. The appetizer platter was a delightful kickoff, featuring a mix of Seaweed Salad, Sliced Jellyfish, Fried Pork, and Fried Chicken. The seaweed salad, in particular, was refreshing and set the stage for the courses to follow.

Throughout the meal, we enjoyed an array of dishes, with the steamed buns and a savory beef dish standing out as personal highlights. While some offerings were simply good, others lacked a wow factor, leaving a bit more to be desired.

As the banquet drew to a close, we were served Red Bean Soup with mochi balls, a dessert that was surprisingly not sweet. While appreciative of the tradition, I couldn't help but think the Piglet Buns with egg custard would have been a more fitting and festive end, especially given the Year of the Pig.

The service staff at Golden Unicorn was commendably efficient, ensuring everything ran smoothly and even accommodating take-home boxes for leftovers—a nice touch for a large event.

In conclusion, the Golden Unicorn's Lunar New Year Banquet provided a fun and filling experience, though a couple of dish tweaks could enhance future festivities. It's clear a return visit is necessary, if only for those charming piglet buns!

Great tasting authentic Mexican food! Had the chance to enjoy their "Chicken tacos a la lomita" and was not disappointed. Their horchata is also realllllyyy good! Some places make theirs too cinnamony or sugary but here its perfect.

My recent visit to this gem of a diner was a delightful experience, with excellent service that matched the quality of their comfort food offerings. The value for money here is fantastic. The menu doesn't promise culinary acrobatics but delivers heartwarming simplicity perfected on a plate, with an impressive array of hot sauces to embellish your meal. With a voluminous nine-page menu, I'm already planning my next visit to explore more of their mouthwatering selections. Highly recommend for a no-nonsense, tasty meal!

Probably one of my favorite restaurants in the broadway area for pre/post show meals. Although it is very touristy the menu is interesting, food quality is always good, and if you enjoy margaritas they make them well!

Title: A Delightful Dive into Seafood at Grand Central's Oyster Bar

I've always held Grand Central Station close to my heart; its bustling atmosphere and the array of shopping and dining options make it a destination of its own. After years of anticipation, I finally visited the legendary Oyster Bar nestled in its depths and it didn't disappoint.

Post a satisfying lobster roll from Luke's, my friends and I decided to keep the seafood spree alive. We arrived without reservations on a busy Friday afternoon and were met with a somewhat curt hostess. Undeterred, I assured her we'd be swift, and we were seated.

The extensive menu immediately grabbed our attention, complemented by a broad selection of beers and spirits. Opting for the house brew, I indulged in a seafood sampler, to which I boldly added six colossal shrimp. The platter's arrival was a sight to behold, and although I'll admit my memory is a bit hazy from the day's libations, the quality of the seafood left a lasting impression. The portions were generous enough that I gladly shared with my companions, who seemed equally pleased with their choices.

Considering the volume and quality of food, the price hovered reasonably around $50 after tacking on the shrimp. Our server was the highlight—attentive and genial—making our swift dining experience all the more pleasant.

Despite the initial cool reception, the Oyster Bar proved to be a cool oasis on a hot New York summer day. Its accommodating space is perfect for groups, and while walk-ins are welcome, it's wise to secure a reservation. For seafood lovers, this iconic spot is a must-visit in Grand Central Station.

This restaurant impresses with its thoughtful variety of crusts, catering to all preferences with delicious whole wheat, gluten-free, and cauliflower options. The vegan cheese is notably tasty and they don't skimp on the range of toppings available. Their large pizza is generously sized, making it an ideal choice for family gatherings, while the medium is the perfect pick for a couple looking for a delicious meal with the bonus of leftovers. Even their small pizza is sufficiently ample for two people to share. Highly recommended for anyone seeking customizable and satisfying pizza experiences.

Mid week cheat meal for a friend's birthday!! If you love chocolate and have a sweet tooth, I highly recommend this spot. We had their spicy pasta primavera and mozzarella flat bread pizza which were good but the best thing was their dessert. We ordered their Classic European fondue, it comes with strawberries, banana, marshmallows and brownies and we chose dark and milk chocolate fondue. Not a large portion for the price you pay(which is $25) but I love the milk chocolate here and can keep going for that. Since it was a little cold that day, I ordered their hot chocolate with marshmallows and it was delicious. Coming back for this again!

After matinée and before the train ride home. Have heard of Lydia Bastianach's pasta and here it is. Huge place, great service, nice room and reservations needed. We had a drink in the bar as we waited for our table with early reservation for 4:00. Drinks were NYC expensive. Nice table for two by the wall but had to change chair to find a little stability. Bread, spread and olives on table were excellent. We opted for the Sinfonia di Pasta and were really happy with our choice. It comes with a choice of Caesar Salad or Antipasto Misto which was our choice. This was a plate of marinated and grilled vegetables [super] and either a seafood side of octopus salad and a bite of skate with romesco or burrata with honey and fresh peas. We each had a different version with the octopus salad a winner. The three pastas [and you get all three] were spaghetti in red sauce with basil, orrecchiette with pancetta and cabbage and Sicilian style gnocchi made with a touch of semolina and then seared and bathed in a light cheese cream sauce [looked just like scallops]. Gnocchi were our number one choice. Servers walked around the room each with a different pan of pasta so it was all you could eat. Had a nice glass of white wine from the Bastianach line.

Walking into ST&B it is very trendy and the vibe is fresh. We came by at happy hour and sat in the high top tables. Our server, Mannie came over with the menus and told us about the drinks for HH. But since we do not drink I ordered a bottle of sparkling water. (Side note: the water is $8 which I find to be a tad bit high) I asked for orange slices for my water and I kid you not, the bartender cut me fresh slices. WOW. Now that won me over. To take the time to cut me an orange Was a nice touch. Now for the food:We ordered the:Charred Calamari & Celery with green olives, oregano, parsley, chili flakes, red wine vinaigrette. OMG it was delicious. The calamari was tender and not rubbery where as other restaurants we have been to have been cooked way too much!Lemony Teenage GreensRoasted artichoke hearts, shallots & grape tomatoes, haricots verts, feta cheese, red quinoa  Again this was amazing. I asked to not have the red quinoa in it because I'm trying not to eat too many grains. The salad was very Las the even without the quinoa. We will definitely be back because the food was amazing and the service helped make this experience and even better one!!Thank you Mannie so much for wonderful service.

The hang over from Saturday nearly killed me! Bowery road saved me!! I needed food, was so hungry! Came across this place. It is an amazing cute place. The place is clean and the service was fast. The food was great.

Title: Convenient Post-Show Dining Experience

I recently visited this restaurant after catching a Broadway show and was pleased with the experience. Despite the crowd, we were seated promptly, which is always appreciated. The service was efficient and attentive, ensuring a smooth dining experience. Food quality was solid, though no particular dish stood out for me - it was all-around good. The drink selection was a highlight, with a variety of nice options on their alcohol beverage menu. It's a place I'd consider revisiting when I'm in the area again.

Passed this place multiple times and decided to finally give it a try since I was craving thai food. The restaurant is small and there are no bathrooms. There are about 6 stools that is considered bar area, I believe five 2 seater seats. Ordered thai ice tea and that was sweet and delicious. Got the crispy fried tofu and they gave a sweet side sauce and it tasted alright. Bland and nothing special. Our pad thai was not what I expected. It was pretty sour and sweet. I got beef and my friend got chicken. My beef wasnt good. Hard to chew and had no flavor. I gave up on it and left it on the side. I didnt like to waste food but it really wasnt good. I never had pad thai that was that sour and sweet. The portion was good but it was a bit too sour and sweet for my liking, even my friends too. Overall, I might give this place another go if I am craving thai food badly enough in chinatown. We went to this thai place instead of the one in the corner since I heard that it was good thai food. The pad thai wasnt appealing to me so I wouldnt order that again here. There was only one server which makes sense for a small space and less seating.

So my friends took me to this Chicken place. The food was fantastic. I chose the only boneless chicken option (my preference) in sweet chili. It was flavorful. But one of my friends ordered one of their hottest sauces on the side for me to try. I did dip one of my chicken pieces in it thinking I can handle spicy food. Oops. I don't think a gallon ice water would have quenched my heat thirst. The spicy aftertaste lingered for a long while. It was good, but a bit overwhelming.

My recent visit to The Meatball Shop for a Sunday brunch was a delightful surprise as we were the first patrons of the day. The service was exceptional, with a server going above and beyond to detail the menu and ensure our drinks were never empty. While they lack drip coffee, the espresso options were ample, and they obligingly whipped up an americano. We shunned the predetermined brunch menu for customized meatball bowls. Choosing a veggie base with chicken meatballs and pesto proved to be a mouthwatering decision. Highly recommend for a satisfying brunch experience!

Title: Fresh Flavors at a Serene Spot

We kicked off our evening at this sushi haven with some delightful dim sum, opting for both shrimp dumplings and a combination of shrimp and pork shumai – both proved to be yummy starters. The main event included a shared crazy salmon roll and a selection from the sushi omakase, with the salmon roll stealing the show with its surprisingly superior taste compared to the standard sushi fare. The fish across the board was undeniably fresh and palatable.

Dessert was a pleasant ending with green tea mochi, which was well-prepared and enjoyable. While the food left us content, the ambiance was noticeably subdued for a Friday night - at 7:30 PM, only three tables were occupied. Nonetheless, the restaurant delivered a very good dining experience with its high-quality offerings.

Best Mediterranean burger? Best burger variation? Whatever category the sandwiches here fall under, it's going to dominate.A must have is the folded cheese burger, and the minute steak sandwich isn't far behind.The folder cheese burger has everything a traditional burger comes with but with the additional of a sexy cheese skirt. Also the fluffy pita is really an amazing bun alternative. The best part is you don't feel heavy or groggy after. The minute steak, so much tender meat stuffed into a fluffy pita. I ate both and could've went for a third. Both sandwiches were flavorful and light. Also hands together for the kitchen staff, everyone doing their thing and dishing out great food at lightning speeds. I really can't wait to come back. It may be my new favorite sandwich in NY.

Title: A Hidden Gem Despite Service Hiccups

After a lengthy wait for the right moment, I finally experienced the restaurant that had been on my radar forever. Despite the notoriously limited seating and their lack of reservations, a quiet Monday evening worked in my favor, allowing me to secure a spot at this culinary haven.

Greeted by a friendly host, my dining companion and I were originally offered seats at the communal table but were advised to enjoy a short interlude at the bar. Patience paid off as we soon found ourselves in a cozy, private booth. The menu was an adventurous fusion affair, brimming with options that made choosing a single dish nearly impossible.

The scallion pancakes were a revelation, pairing bacon with a lightness that defied expectation. Pan-fried pork buns burst with a satisfying blend of flavors, and the grilled jumbo shrimp bathed in a red curry sauce were aptly named and perfectly balanced, enhanced by a medley of fresh veggies.
