But the star of the evening was the crispy skin smoked chicken, a boneless wonder with a nod to Peruvian zest that lingered in my memory long after the last bite.

Regrettably, the one blemish on an otherwise stellar night was our waiter's aloofness, who, despite the quality of the fare, didn't check in on us once, making it difficult to award a full five stars. Nonetheless, the meal itself was an outstanding success and one I'd eagerly repeat.

Hidden (literally) gem in Midtown East! You have to go into the office building and let the front desk know you're going downstairs to the restaurant. The ambiance does give you a feeling you were warped to a lowkey restaurant in Japan. My party had a reservation and we were seated immediately.The staff were very attentive; they consistently checked in on us, refilled tea, replaced dishware, etc. They also offer hot tea which was much appreciated after coming from the cold! Dishes came at a comfortable pace. Some highlights from our dinner included:- Hiyayakko: The tofu was great and the toppings added texture to the dish. The tofu itself was very enjoyable and the consistency was just right.- Nasu Dengaku: Eggplant lovers must try this! The eggplant is soft (not chewy like some eggplant is) and comes with three different types of miso toppings. My personal favorite was the egg yolk miso. - Miyazakigyu Ishiyaki: You get to cook your own beef on a small hot stone (don't worry, they replace it if it cools off). The beef was tender and cooked very quickly. - Nihachi Soba: This is definitely one of the better sobas I've tried in Manhattan! The texture is great; there's some firmness to it and it holds up well even with the dipping sauce. The portion is fairly large so my party shared one order. - Black Sesame Creme Brulee: This dessert is a bit pricey for the size and unconventional, but it was amazing! I highly recommend wrapping up your meal with an order of the creme brulee. The ice cream itself was tasty and paired very well with the crispy The two dishes that were a bit less impressive included the Chikuzen Ni (assorted root vegetables) and Salmon Onigiri. These seemed relatively standard compared to the other dishes. Overall, definitely recommend trying this restaurant for great ambiance and tasty Japanese food!

The food here is delicious. Great ambience. Not too loud. The waiter was very attentive and patient. The food is so filling. They give you complimentary appetizer of aloo. The sauce is delicious! They do have hard alcohol but not a wide selection. Wine and beers. No happy hour here but sort of romantic and intimate.

I came here for brunch on Monday with a friend, and I wasn't impressed. On their site it says 'Michelin 2019,' which is one of the main reasons I wanted to check this spot out.I ended up getting the Shakshuka with a side of gluten free pita. It was okay, had a nice flavor to it, but the egg was over cooked, the pita was cold. I'm not sure why they didn't serve it warm? My friend decided to get the avocado and egg bowl with salmon. For $17 she ended up getting this tiny bowl of avocado purée with one poached egg and a few slices of salmon. We were both surprised by how small the bowl was and how they presented it. This should literally be a dip or appetizer. She had to ask for a pita because it was a dip essentially.Service was okay, food came out quick. The place itself is very clean and has some cool decor. It's a bit loud, I'm not sure how considering the place wasn't packed.All in all, we were not impressed. My personal opinion is that some of the dishes are overpriced for what we're actually getting.

Title: Lackluster Lunch Experience for a Large Group

My coworkers and I visited this restaurant for a lunch gathering, enticed by their ability to accommodate our large group. I started with the chips and guacamole – a standard fare that unfortunately failed to stand out, particularly when compared to offerings on the west coast. The main course, ropa vieja, promised a comforting bowl of light beef stew. Yet, it delivered a forgettable experience with its bland, shredded beef, paired with equally unimpressive beans and rice that I found myself barely touching. While the convenience of booking for a big party is noted, the insipid flavors mean I won't be returning. The quest for satisfying culinary delights continues elsewhere.

The food here is soooo good. You can adjust the spice level so don't be afraid! We got the lamb dumplings, lamb noodles and beef noodles. Get the mild spice level if you want flavor but don't have a high spice tolerance. There are some chairs to sit on but this is a very low key and simple place. Will definitely have to come back here.

Sorry, Can't do much with this one.Saving grace was the service.  Staff was good and attentive, but infrequently. Didn't come by that often.Decor and atmosphere..Nice. Able to have a conversation.Food, First the Guac...Just a pile of watery mush in a bowl. Don't do it. Next, the Skirt Steak Fajitas....just ok. Not a whole lot of spice and flavor. Like I said, just ok.Lastly, the enchiladas, or what was supposed to be enchiladas.....a plate full of mush.In closing, nope, better Mexican choices around.

Title: Unbeatable Bottomless Brunch at Bryant Park Gem

I recently visited an exceptional bottomless brunch spot in Bryant Park, where the service was unparalleled from the moment we sat down to our last sip of mimosa. Our attentive server kept our glasses brimming without missing a beat, and the flexibility to switch between 12 different drink options each round was a boozy brunch dream come true.

The menu was well-priced with a diverse range of mouthwatering choices. My avocado toast paired with egg whites was a healthy yet delicious pick, and my friends were equally satisfied with their dishes. The unexpected delight of mojito popsicles served with our bottomless drinks added a fun and refreshing twist to our brunch.

This place is a must-visit for an indulgent brunch experience. Whether you’re looking to enjoy a laid-back meal or dive into a bottomless adventure, you won't be disappointed. I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit to explore more of their scrumptious offerings.

Title: The Pinnacle of Vegetarian Dining at Abcv

Review:

Abcv isn't just my favorite vegetarian restaurant, it's a culinary treasure that perfectly embodies the concept of a fine balance in every aspect. The chic, clean, and warm atmosphere immediately embraces you upon entry, setting a mood of relaxed sophistication without a hint of pretension.

Service here mirrors the ambient charm—attentive, knowledgeable staff guide you seamlessly through an inspiring menu, offering insightful recommendations that hit the mark every time. Their approach is unobtrusive yet supportive, ensuring a dining experience that feels both personal and professional.

As for the cuisine, Abcv excels with deceptively simple dishes where the natural flavors are the stars. The turmeric elixir sparkles with vitality, and the lettuce wraps are a must-try that dazzle the palate. With a menu diverse enough to delight any taste, this spot truly caters to all.

What's more, Abcv offers an Instagram-worthy aesthetic that actually lives up to the hype, delivering a feast for both the eyes and the stomach. It's the rare gem where trendy meets quality, and they do it flawlessly.

Don’t just take my word for it—Abcv is a must-visit that promises—and delivers—a dining experience you won't forget.

Title: A Dipping Delight at Local Ramen Spot

I finally indulged my curiosity for dipping ramen and was absolutely thrilled with the experience at this gem. The broth stole the show with its savory depth, enhancing the dish to become much more than your standard ramen—thick and delectable without the overwhelming saltiness often critiqued by others. Admittedly, it did become slightly salty towards the end, but that didn't detract from my enjoyment. The karage was another hit, fried to golden perfection. With the attentive and friendly staff adding to the positive vibes, I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit.

Title: A Seafood Delight at a Bustling New York Gem

My partner and I dropped into this popular seafood joint on a rainy Saturday evening around 5 pm and were pleasantly surprised by the swift seating options. Opting for a cozy table for two, we immersed ourselves in a celebratory feast for my boyfriend Ericks's birthday.

The nostalgia of this place remains unchanged since its opening - a testament to its unwavering popularity is the persistent queues. However, the wait is justified by their exceptional offerings. We indulged in a seafood extravaganza, selecting Combo B with lobster and shrimp ($45), a Dungeness Crab ($35), clams ($15), southern fried wings ($12), and garlic bread ($4). While the "boil" sauce—a garlicky, buttery, Cajun mix—complemented the seafood beautifully, in hindsight, we might have overdone the garlic theme for the evening.

Despite the crowd, the food, remarkably fresh, was worth the wait. The steamy southern wings arrived first, tiding us over until the main spread. The service was five-star quality; attentive staff ensured our experience was smooth, frequently checking in, refilling drinks, clearing shells, and even assisting with wet wipes at the meal's end.

If you're a seafood lover in New York, make this spot your go-to. But remember, it's cash-only. Take it from someone who's tried the rest—this place is the real deal. Five stars all the way!

Title: A Cozy Haven for Pho Enthusiasts

I recently stumbled upon a gem that I'm eager to revisit. On a dreary, rain-soaked day, I found solace in a bowl of pho that featured high-quality beef brisket, rich in flavor and perfectly comforting. The restaurant's ambiance is as impressive as its service, with an interior that invites you to relax and enjoy your meal. Alongside the pho, the spring rolls were a flavorful complement, making for a well-rounded dining experience.

This spot has earned my highest recommendation to friends and has quickly become my go-to for a satisfying meal. Note to future visitors: it's cash-only, but don't let that deter you – it's more than worth the trip to the ATM.

Title: A Tacotastic Experience!

If you've ever been to El Gordo in Vegas and left impressed, prepare to elevate your taco standards even further! This bustling gem offers a streamlined service that is both simple and efficient: join the queue, place your order, pay up, grab your ticket, and watch the taco assembler work his magic.

Priced at around $4 each, the tacos provide bang for your buck. Don't be fooled by their size; two tacos make for a satisfying snack or a light meal. The standout was the Pollo taco – juicy, hearty, and generously filled, all tucked into a sturdy shell that holds together bite after bite (a massive plus in my book!).

Don't come expecting a sit-down meal; it's a grab-and-go situation with a lively vibe. But for those seeking exquisite tacos without the typical sit-down wait, this spot is a true winner. Delicious, efficient, and wallet-friendly – what more could you ask for in a taco joint?

Title: A Hidden Gem in Midtown – Manting’s Magic Dry Pot!

If you find yourself wandering through midtown Manhattan with a rumbling stomach, seek out Manting, a culinary treasure off the beaten path. This eatery may seem unassuming at first glance, but once inside, the aroma of their signature dry pot is unmistakable. The unique pricing model will catch your eye—cost based on the weight of your chosen ingredients pre-cooking ensures you get a bountiful plate without breaking the bank.

Though Manting's menu doesn't boast every traditional item you’d find in Flushing—think fewer innards—the flavor profiles are spot on, rivaling those of more established stands. A particular standout is the braised pork belly, a dish so masterfully executed that it will linger on your palate and in your memories.

Adding to the charm, the staff is as delightful as the food they serve. Their helpful and pleasant demeanor make the dining experience even better. And if you’re lucky enough to meet the owner, you're in for a treat. His warmth and hospitality embody the very essence of welcoming.

In sum, Manting is not just a meal, it's an experience that’s as rich in flavor as it is in kindness. A must-visit for any food-lover in NYC!

My recent visit to this Latin-owned eatery came with high hopes of supporting the community and discovering a new culinary gem. Despite my eagerness, the food unfortunately fell short of expectations. The 'downtown arepa,' which I had anticipated with excitement, presented itself somewhat lackluster in appearance upon arrival.

While generously stuffed with meat, the arepa was notably lacking in the vibrant flavors I had hoped for. The meat was disappointingly flavorless, which detracted from the overall experience. I couldn't help but feel that a guided tour through a spice aisle might benefit the kitchen and, in turn, truly revolutionize the dining experience they offer.

On a positive note, the customer service was quite acceptable, with attentive staff that ensured a comfortable visit. Still, I would be remiss not to mention the unmet potential in their cuisine. With some adjustments and a bolder approach to seasoning, I believe this restaurant could truly shine and fully celebrate its cultural roots.

I recently visited this chic spot for drinks and tapas in the basement, and I highly recommend it for a date night. While it leans towards the dressier and pricier side, it's well worth it for the ambiance and the culinary experience. The tapas were exceptional, and the chatter suggests that the rest of the menu is just as impressive. The decor throughout is stunning, adding to the overall appeal of the venue. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Stumbled upon this Michelin starred restaurant and my mind was blown.  I had no idea tempura could be so delicate and softly crunchy.  It is certainly an experience to be had!  Sitting at the counter, you are given the privilege of watching the chefs at work.   When they dip the batter, they do this elaborate dip and swing to get rid of extra batter and it is simply beautiful.  Any tempura is amazing, sushi is ok, but then again, why would you come to a tempura place for sushi?

Tucked away in downtown Manhattan, this classy Victorian-esque gem offers a delightful fusion of French and Austrian cuisine. The ambience channels the opulence of a rich rail baron's library, especially evident in the connected bar next door.

Upon seating, the ritual begins with a selection of fresh bread served with olive oil and butter - a simple yet satisfying start. The cheese soufflé appetizer impresses with its airy richness, while the pickled beet dish, although somewhat plain, is a modest accompaniment.

The mains are where the kitchen truly shines. A unique take on the pork chop, served medium-rare, reveals a tender and delectable new way to savor this cut. For those favouring beef, the black pepper goulash is a revelation: braised, slow-cooked beef that virtually dissolves on the tongue, perfectly paired with soft, slightly chewy spatzle.

Service is top-notch, with staff exhibiting both attentiveness and an impressive knowledge of the menu. The whiskey-based cocktail selection is noteworthy, adding to the overall refined dining experience.

Treated myself to the price fixed lunch ($32) here with a co-worker and was impressed foremost by the attentive service and then by the flavors. The tomato salad was great although they seem to skimp on the feta. The dorade has a mild taste, but buttery and delicious. I loved the honey lavender ice cream. If you're a fan of subtle floral notes in your food, you'll want to try this. It paired very well with the walnut cake. While not the most generous, portions were satisfying and tasted excellent!The feel of the restaurant is upscale. You can see the vessel from inside. Try to make a reservation if you plan on trying this place and come during lunch to get the most bang for your buck.

Title: A Serendipitous Five-Star Discovery at Totto

Review:

It’s a rarity for me to award a full five stars on a whim, particularly based on a singular dish. However, Totto has earned this exceptional accolade with resounding success. Initially second choice to its bustling rival, Totto welcomed my date and me with a refreshingly brief wait and the inviting intimacy of bar seating—evoking what I imagine to be an authentic Japanese dining enclave.

Our choice, the Mega Paitan, was an exercise in culinary spectatorship as we observed the chefs’ adept handiwork while sipping on beers and nodding along to an infectious Offspring soundtrack—kudos to the DJ! The dish itself was a symphony of flavors: a trio of succulent pork cuts nestled among perfectly al dente noodles, fresh veggies, and a touch of garlic, all swimming in a rich, balanced broth that eschewed the common pitfall of excessive saltiness.

Totto not only surpassed expectations but also surpassed its well-known competitor, ensuring my swift return. A meal at Totto isn't just a meal—it's a definitive experience etched onto my list of favorites.

Title: A Convenient Burger Joint for the Office Crowd

Located in the lower level mall of 1 New York Plaza, Schnippers is a worthwhile pit stop for anyone craving a quick and affordable burger or chicken sandwich. The selection of waffle fries and sides is satisfying, and the inclusion of free iced water is a refreshingly thoughtful gesture.

Vegetarians and vegans will appreciate the veggie burger options, though, as a non-vegetarian, I find them more suitable as a side dish. Unfortunately, the fish sandwich—my preferred choice—has been removed from the menu. Its absence is felt by many patrons who opt for fish over meat or tofu options. Here's hoping Schnippers will reconsider its menu choices and reintroduce the fish sandwich permanently.

Despite this, the service at Schnippers remains commendable for its friendliness. I'm looking forward to returning, especially if the fish makes a comeback.

Came for a special occasion and it was unforgettable. We splurged for the 16-course omakase (menu here is quite simple; there are two types of omakase that you can choose between), and never had anything quite like it. Chef/Owner Pham's omakase is not traditional in the Japanese sense...he uses decadent ingredients from all over the world, foie gras, truffle shavings, sturgeon caviar, gold foil, and of course uni and wagyu beef, to create delightful combinations of flavor and texture. While the meal is rich with all of this, it is not cloying or overdone, and all of his dishes still felt distinctly and fundamentally Japanese.Tables are quite limited so highly recommend reservations. Service was attentive and polite.

hard rock is a staple for us regardless of the city, state or country which we visit because we have a family member who collects their memorabilia. Unfortunately my burger was complete with a dry bun and not correctly made-to-order. Mother's Cobb salad, on the other hand, was an interesting treat for her with the pomegranate and pepita seeds.  Our server (Jessica T), was pleasant and upbeat!  The NY cheesecake tasted store bought and doctored -- NOT at all as described in the menu (see photos).PS - still bought swag sooooo......

Came for happy hour on a Friday and loved the cute vibe and open space. We had a reservation for three and were seated immediately even when our party didn't all arrive yet.We got 4 dozen of the happy hour $1 raw oysters and topped it off with a bottle of white wine ($30). Don't judge!! I believe they have a rotating selection on the oyster so it may vary each night.We also got the shrimp fritters and mussels. Both are to die for!! Shrimp fritter was crunchy/crispy and the aioli sauce didn't make it heavy. Mussels in thai curry sauce were so flavorful I started drinking the sauce!! The mussel meat were on the smaller side but the sauce made up for it.It does add up and can get quite pricey with our order the total came out to be $121 not including tip. Overall the service was attentive and not obtrusive and it's a cute date spot! Will definitely return again!

Great spot in the Flatiron for a wonderful meal. We attended a party here so were in the private room upstairs. It's a great place for a holiday party or a birthday by using the private room. Ample space with a private bar. Friendly and attentive staff.The food was wonderful. Highlights were the lamb chops, tender, grilled perfectly. The fried chicken, crispy and juicy inside. The risotto which was creamy and had great flavor. Also the fish, fresh and wonderfully cooked. Top it off with the dessert donuts and you have a wonderful meal. I'll definitely be back.

I came to this bar for a drink with an old college friend of mine. The bar is conveniently located a block away from Rockefeller Center (where my friend works near), we were were able to walk easily to the place. We met around 5 PM, and the place was relatively empty (even on a Thursday). They were having a happy hour specials on beers, which my friend got, while I got a signature cocktail (I honestly don't remember what the name of this drink was and I can't find it on their menu online. It did come in a cute Tiki cup). Pros:- Quick and kind service - Great tasting cocktail- Aesthetically pleasing restaurant - Great location Cons:- Expensive ~ I paid about $20 for my cocktail, but then again it's Manhattan Overall: - My friend and I enjoyed our time at this bar. My cocktail, while I don't remember it's name, tasted really good and I enjoyed the ambiance of the place.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Wayan, a gem recommended by a friend, and it did not disappoint. Securing a reservation for Saturday night was a bit of a challenge—a testament to its burgeoning popularity—but the effort was well worth it.

Upon arrival, we were promptly seated in a charming half booth that added to the overall romantic ambiance. The Indonesian decor was stunning, plunging us into a sensory escape from the bustling streets of New York.

The service was impeccable from the start, with our waiter explaining the shareable nature of the dishes, prompting us to indulge in a variety of flavors. Standout dishes included the succulent chicken satay, which left us craving more, the flavorful baby back pork ribs, the spicy kick of the eggplant balado, and the sweet pandan custard dessert. 

Although the clams Jimbaran fell short of our expectations with a lackluster topping and absence of the promised coconut infusion, the drinks, particularly the coconut-rich Kelapa, were a high note of the evening.

Wayan has truly captivated us with its excellent service, enchanting atmosphere, and mostly delectable cuisine. It's a place we eagerly anticipate revisiting.

Title: Midnight Delight at The Night Owl

Last night's visit to The Night Owl was a feast for the senses. The ambiance was bustling with good music and infectious energy, perfect for a satisfying late-night bite. Though we may have been overly ambitious with our order, the food did not disappoint—one taste of the meatloaf and grilled cheese, and any regrets about the hour vanished. The warm, buttered bread served upon arrival was divine, but a word of caution: indulge sparingly, or risk overshadowing the main event.

Our drinks, a blackberry Mojito and a classic margarita, were expertly mixed and beautifully complemented the meal. What's more, the leftovers made for an unexpectedly delicious breakfast. The Night Owl truly knows how to satisfy its nocturnal patrons. Highly recommended for those looking to cap off their evening with flair!

Thoroughly enjoyed my meal here today. If you live for that tingly feeling of Szechuan spice, this place is for you. Zest Szechuan boasts authentic Szechuan food yet still has attentive wait staff which can sometimes be lacking with Chinese restaurants. I normally don't eat tripe but the tripe appetizer here is bomb. Would also highly recommend the grilled fish. This dish alone would have been big enough to feed an entire family. Loved the whole fish, which was tender and flavorful. The dish also had an abundance of veggies which are always welcome. Overall had a great experience. Susan, the owner, is a genuinely delightful and very down to earth person. Will definitely be recommending his place to my friends!

Title: A Taste of Szechuan Splendor at Han Dynasty NYC

From the moment I stepped into the spacious Han Dynasty in NYC, reminiscent of a venue grand enough for a wedding, I knew I was in for a treat. Having been a fan since my first experience in Philadelphia, my expectations were high—and I wasn't disappointed.

Seated immediately for a late Friday dinner, the ambiance set a vibrant stage for the culinary adventure ahead. The appetizers set the tone: the Dan dan noodles were a spicy, peanut-tinged delight with perfectly al dente noodles; the crispy cucumbers added a refreshing heat, while the wontons in hot chili oil were decent but eclipsed by the other starters (mental note: try the dumplings next time).

Portions are generous, so sharing is the way to go. The standout entree for me was the seafood tofu soup—overflowing with succulent fish and soft tofu steeped in a flavorful broth. The dry pepper style shrimp also impressed with its crispy skin and robust taste. The dry pot style chicken, while tasty, fell short on the spice scale for my palate.

The drink offerings were adequate. I opted for a merlot Cabernet blend, which didn't quite hit the mark; however, I heard positive murmurs about the cocktails.

In summary, Han Dynasty NYC is a vibrant haven for Szechuan cuisine enthusiasts. With plans to return, I'm eager to explore more of their menu—and perhaps try one of those talked-about cocktails.

We came on a Sunday evening and waited for a hour. If you prefer quiet and spacious area then this is not the place for you. We both ordered the nozawa trust me pre fix and it was decent. Overall experience 7/10

Dining at Per Se was nothing short of spectacular, thanks to the generosity of a friend. From start to finish, the impeccable service complemented the extraordinary culinary journey. Each course, part of a sumptuous seven-course meal, was a testament to the chef's prowess, leaving me satisfyingly full three hours later. 

The visual feast of our dinner is best conveyed through the photos I've shared, as they capture the essence of the intricate dishes we encountered. Despite the ample offerings, we were able to take home the remaining desserts—a sweet reminder of the evening.

Per Se's attention to detail even extended to gifting us with a folder containing the night's menu, a keepsake I'll treasure. The highlight was undoubtedly the visit to the kitchen, where we met the skilled chefs responsible for our culinary delight. The presence of a live feed, showcasing the synchronized dance between Per Se and its sister restaurant French Laundry, was a unique touch that connected both coasts through their shared passion for gastronomy. Truly amazing!

Patsy's was amazing. We booked their upper level for the first night of our conference to feed all our participants. They were very accommodating and we were so thankful for the experience. I highly recommend booking at Patsy's if you have an event!Staff is friendly and made us feel right at home. Their pizza is great! The options are endless. And it is cooked to perfection. Also for over 40 people I was amazed at how quickly the food came out!Decor is modern with a homey feel. They have two floors and are able to accommodate quite a few people in there!I would like to extend a big THANK YOU to Patsy's for feeding so many people. It was delicious!

At the heart of Pera Soho lies a stunningly picturesque outdoor seating area—a true urban oasis accentuated by strategic lighting, chic wooden furnishings, and lush greenery that transports you away from the city bustle. Yet, this enchanting ambience was marred by an unwelcome swarm of bugs at our initial table by the wall, prompting a necessary relocation.

The restaurant shines during happy hour with its wallet-friendly offerings that belie its upscale location. Pera Soho's imaginative cocktail list blossoms with summer vibes, and the two-for-one happy hour deal is a steal—$8 for two delectable small plates. The culinary standouts were the decadent truffle fries and the creamy labne. If it weren't for the pesky bugs, Pera Soho would have been the scene of an impeccable dining experience.

After much anticipation, I finally visited the quaint Italian restaurant that had been calling out to me through appetizing online photos. The macaroni alla Norma, highly praised and a clear favorite, did not disappoint. Its thick, uniquely shaped pasta was dressed in a creamy tomato sauce, enriched with eggplant and a generous sprinkling of cheese. While the sauce's flavor profile was a bit unusual, possibly due to the eggplant, it truly made the dish a standout.

On the other hand, the tagliatelle with ragu and truffle failed to impress. The pervasive truffle flavor overwhelmed my palate, overshadowing the surprisingly tasty ragu. This dish won't see a repeat order from me.

In summary, while the macaroni alla Norma alone was a memorable treat, the overall experience doesn't have me planning a swift return. It was, however, intriguing to understand what all the fuss was about.

Solid spot. Indian food done in a fast food type of way. I got the bowl and was too full to finish it. I really want to try the taco next time. They are so photogenic. The ginger chai was AMAZING. It has a little bit of a kick which is great for harsh winter weather. The establishment is tiny. There are a handful of seating and outdoor seating (but it's way too cold to eat out.)Quick and easy spot to get Indian food. I liked it.

Flor de Mayo is like revisiting an old friend. Sharing fun memories. And reincarnating them at the dinner table. I used to come here fairly often and honestly haven't been here in years. Me and my great friend decided to stop in on a Saturday night. It was crowded and smelled good. We started with a pitcher of sangria at the bar area. It was sweet and juicy. Refreshing, but it didn't have that kick I like. Think, wine and juice and tons of fruit. But it was great and light to pair with our meals. I had shrimp in lobster sauce with sweet plantains and fried rice. The fried rice was sooo darn good. The plantains were carmelized and sweet. The Shrimp were jumbo and covered in the gooey egg mixture and it was delish.It's so far but it was nice revisiting the place of my 'youth' for drinks and food. It's sorta just one how I remember it but different at the same time. I like that. Don't change.

Title: Burger Heaven at Virginia's

Last night's quest for the ultimate burger led me to Virginia's, and it certainly did not disappoint. Greeted warmly, we were quickly relieved of our wet umbrellas and extra baggage for a clutter-free dining experience, despite the cozy table arrangements.

Our universal choice was the burger with a side of fries – and what a choice it was! Without prompting for our preferred doneness, our burgers arrived medium rare, a tad bloodier than my usual, yet exceptionally thick, juicy, and brimming with flavor. Paired with thin, crisp fries, it was a carnivore's delight.

The dessert, a standard flan, failed to impress and will be a pass on my next visit. However, the commendable service deserves a mention. Our waitress was attentive and accommodating, exchanging a drink without fuss, and the collective staff effort added a touch of warmth to our meal.

Count me in for a return visit – that burger is calling my name for an encore.

Title: Underwhelmed at Restaurant Week - A Danji Experience

I visited Danji with high hopes during Restaurant Week, drawn in by the buzz of stellar reviews, only to leave feeling underwhelmed. The promise of authentic Korean cuisine fell short; the lack of traditional banchan was my first clue.

The KFC wings I ordered were flavorful, but I couldn't help but pine for the classic soy garlic variant I adore. A word of caution: save the accompanying radish for after the wings unless you want an unexpectedly sour throat. Nonetheless, it did serve well as a palate cleanser post-wings.

My main course, the hot stone bibimbap with bulgogi, was sufficient—customizable heat levels thanks to the side-serving of spicy sauce were a plus. My friends tried the restaurant's take on "poke," which, while tasty with its blend of yellowfin, salmon, and sprouts in spicy mayo, was disappointingly scant, especially at the $26 price point.

The service struggled to keep up with the bustling crowd, leading to slow service. Make sure to reserve a table to avoid lengthy waits. Despite the decent flavors, the meal did not satisfy my craving for traditional Korean cuisine. At around $31 with tip and tax, I sought an experience that Danji did not deliver. Regrettably, I don't foresee a return visit.

Kanoyama, I finally found what I was looking for!  Fresh, luscious fish.  Affordable.  Not crowded and laidback.  Sometimes you want above average sushi and you don't want to break the piggy bank. Kanoyama is the answer!  Came as a group of 4 on a Thursday night and even though we had a reservation, we could have walked in.  Tables were half full so not overly loud or crowded.  Nice decor, polite service, although not outstanding.  Had to look for our waitress a few times to order another bottle of sake and then ask for the check.  Would've been nice if she checked in on us without us having to look around and flag her down but I'm not complaining, we had a great time.  All the dishes we ordered were great!  My favorite was our sushi & sashimi because the fish was fresh, silky and tasty.  Will definitely be returning one day soon and for the omakase!

Title: A Nod to Italian Tradition with Room for Improvement

Rating: ★★★☆☆

My experience at this storied red-sauce Italian restaurant, positioned as a prelude to a visit to the Tenement Museum, was a journey through time—though not always a palatable one. While the concept of dining in a space that claims a century-old heritage is charming, the execution of the menu left my taste buds yearning for more.

The complimentary bread and butter started us off on a neutral note, solidly average and hence deserving of a precise three-star rating. As for the appetizers, the artichoke with breadcrumbs was less impressive, scraping by with just below three stars. In contrast, the Italian mozzarella in carozza shone brightly with its authentic flavor, earning a well-rounded four stars.

For main courses, the sole francaise's lunch portion was commendably generous, and the flexibility to substitute pasta with broccoli was appreciated, nudging its score to a 3.25. However, the Caesar salad fell flat, with a dismal 1.5-star rating, even from my usually easy-to-please companion. As for the green salad topped with an overwhelming amount of chicken breast, it was a stark reminder of uninspired culinary choices.

The penne vodka maintained the three-star trend of acceptability, but it was the potato gnocchi in pesto cream that provided a glimmer of excellence, with its tender dumplings earning a well-deserved four stars.

A highlight of our visit was the friendly and accommodating staff, ensuring a pleasant environment if one's after Italian comfort food served in hearty portions. The ambiance of the space is inviting, although a less-than-stellar men's room detracts somewhat from the overall experience.

In conclusion, if you're seeking a meal that reflects an era of simpler tastes and expectations, this restaurant fits the bill. However, don't come in search of culinary innovation or brilliance. It's a place that seems to have stood still in time, and while there's a certain appeal in that, it might not be enough to satisfy modern palates.

My visit to Szechuan Mountain House was a delightful foray into spicy Szechuan cuisine. Upon arrival, the efficient number system allowed for immediate seating once my party was complete. The table was already set with pickled cabbage that packed a punch and deliciously spicy, along with a pot of jasmine tea kept warm over a flame.

We indulged in sliced pork belly, presented innovatively on a mini rack with cucumbers, a combination that was elevated with a tasty dipping sauce. However, the ox tongue, tripe, and mala pig intestines were somewhat overshadowed by an excessive saltiness in their sauce. The standout dish for me was the water spinach – a deceptively simple dish that shone with freshness.

To end the meal on a sweet note, the house offered a complimentary red bean dessert, which was a thoughtful touch. Overall, my experience was positive, with notes to potentially explore less salty options in the future, such as their fish stew. I'm keen on a return visit to Szechuan Mountain House.

Title: A Seafood Feast to Remember!

I had the pleasure of visiting this gem of a seafood restaurant last Saturday night, and I simply cannot rave enough about the experience. No reservation? No problem! We cozied up to the bar and dove into the culinary delights awaiting us.

First up, the oysters – each one was the epitome of freshness, practically singing of the sea. But what really caught our attention was the uni, decadently served right in its spiky shell. A true delicacy that's not to be missed!

Then came the main courses: a lobster roll so generous with its chunks of succulent lobster, it was pure indulgence in a bun. And the grilled sea bass? Divine. Grilled to perfection with a hint of sea salt and herbs, its flavors whisked me away on a Thai-inspired journey without leaving my seat. Accompanied by simple white rice, it was the perfect vessel to savor every last note of seasoning.

In short, this spot has secured a place in my seafood-loving heart. If you're drooling now, just wait until you taste it for yourself!

Great brunch spot. They have a nice open space in the back with see through roof and perfect for a Sunday brunch date. One of the best lasagne I've ever had. The eggs Benedict was also pretty good. They have amazing selection of cocktails as well :)

Deliciously flavorful food! First time I've had Somalian food but was blown away by the spices. My friend and I had dinner here on a weekday and there was no wait time; we were immediately seated in the humble 7-8 table restaurant and greeted by the very welcoming and friendly waitress. My friend and I decided to share the Sabayaad (first pic) which comes with a large chapatti bread with sauted veges and a perfect dollop of sour cream to add a tangy taste, nicely sized portion for sharing. I had the Hilib Ari (goat) as it is the most popular dish at the restaurant and it held up its reputation! So perfectly roasted to fall right off the bone and spiced with a light spice and savory flavor that I couldn't stop until I picked off every last strand from the bone itself. Both dishes were complemented by a sour citrus-y green dip that was so delicious and lightens up the meat dishes! Overall an incredible hole in the wall restaurant in Harlem, definitely recommended for those who have not tried Somalian food before !

Title: Burger Monday at Tetsu - A Savory Delight

My experience at Tetsu on their Burger Monday was nothing short of exceptional. After hearing rave reviews from First We Feast's Burger Show and discovering their enticing deal ($25 for a burger, fries, and beer combo usually worth $40), I eagerly made a reservation for a rainy Monday night.

Upon arrival, the hostess's thoughtful gesture to check our umbrellas was much appreciated. My boyfriend and I were seated at the bar, directly in front of where our burgers would be masterfully grilled—a culinary performance amid the restaurant's relaxed yet stylish vibe.

We opted for both the lamb burger with taleggio and the beef burger with white cheddar, accompanied by Bushwick Pilsners. On a whim, prompted by our attentive server, we added shishito peppers to our order. The peppers, grilled to perfection and dipped in miso yogurt, were irresistible and perfectly complemented our meal.

The main event, however, was the burgers. The beef burger's smoky flavor paired with the rich, yet not overpowering, melted cheese was a revelation—no need for additional condiments or toppings. The lamb burger was even more of a standout, its tender, flavorful meat virtually dissolving in our mouths. It was unanimous; the lamb burger would be our choice for future visits.

As for the fries, they were a crunchy, savory masterpiece mixed with bacon, fried garlic, and rosemary. Despite being full, I found them impossible to resist until I reluctantly passed the last few to my boyfriend.

In conclusion, my recommendation for anyone seeking a top-tier burger is unequivocal—head to Tetsu on a Burger Monday. An utterly satisfying dining experience that promises no regrets.
Went here for lunch, service was very fast. But the Mac and cheese was salty and the collard greens wasn't all the way cook (they were crunchy). Yams were very good though.

I recently dined at this local Thai restaurant and was quite impressed with the generous portions they served. The quality of the Thai food was excellent, truly capturing the essence of Thai cuisine. The only slight drawback was the Thai ice tea, which leaned towards the sweeter side for my taste. Overall, a delightful dining experience for anyone craving authentic Thai flavors.

Reliable restaurant with one of the best veggie burgers in town. Other and newer establishments may have a veggie burger on the menu but the version here is a classic and amazing. I was eating veggie burgers here before it became trendy. I change up the side occasionally between the amazing cole slaw and sautéed greens but this time I tried the braised cabbage (topped with goat cheese) and this is probably my new favorite. This place is one of those places easy to overlook simply because it's been around awhile (which should indicate something - the business does well!) but I find myself returning when I'm in the area and want to catch up with friends. Great, spacious bar in the front too for after work drinks.

My coworkers and I decided to bar hop. So we stop at this gem and it was definitely worth the turn up. Excellent prices and the wings are bomb. Very affordable appetizers and drinks. You could NEVER go WRONG with $2 shots. Good spot to pre game or turn up with a few friends or coworkers.

Came across this pizzeria while on our way to catch Megabus out of NYC and, wow, what a find! Absolutely phenomenal! There about a dozen pies from which to choose your slice (or slices.) Prices include tax and are about $5-$6 per slice.  Definitely worth the price in both portion size and taste! I opted for the potato pizza which was basically scalloped potatoes on a crust! Whoa, momma - it was to die for!Located behind Madison Square Garden, and adjacent to Penn Station, and just a few blocks from Megabus stop, you won't want to.miss this pizzeria if you are in the area. Your tastebuds will thank you. Carryout or grab a seat at booths in back.

Very good food and reasonable prices. The portions are also huge. We started with mozzarella sticks which were great. Even though they were delivered, they were still crispy on the outside. I got the eggplant Parmesan and it was a huge portion and thickly cut. The flavor of the sauce was also great and there was a perfect amount of cheese. I asked for vodka sauce instead of tomato sauce on the pasta which was really good. My husband got the chicken parm hero which was big and had great flavor. He also got the fettuccini bolognese and really enjoyed it. I would definitely get delivery from here again.

Looking for Japanese street food? Here's the place to go. The okonomiyaki takes a while to make, but it is well worth it. With all of the dishes here (except the takoyaki), you are allowed to choose your protein so it's also a great spot for vegetarians. Definitely give the takoyaki a try too! The place is casual. You order upfront and pick it up when they call you. Sit anywhere you want. There's also a water station by the window or you can purchase a soft drink. There is a bench (but no table) outside so you can eat outside.

Stumbled upon a gem in Hong Kong that's a must-visit for Korean cuisine enthusiasts. The crispy chicken here is sublime, perfectly paired with exceptional fried rice. Opted for the bundle deal, which included a generous portion of wings, drumsticks, and two refreshing beers. The inclusion of an arugula, mixed greens, beet, and cherry tomato salad was a delightful surprise that complemented the mains. The extra soy garlic sauce and pickled radish were the cherries on top, adding a flavorful punch to every bite. Above all, the ambiance was incredibly welcoming, and the staff exuded friendliness. Highly recommend for a casual yet satisfying dining experience.

My sister recommended this place because shes been here before and was a fan of it. I liked I was able to join their wait list on Yelp so we were seated within 5 minutes. We opted to sit at the bar because we had to wait an additional 20 minutes if we wanted a table. The inside of the restaurant is decorated beautifully!We both ordered the pad thai. My chicken pad thai was absolutely delicious! I loved how it was a little sweet but also tangy especially with lime on the side. For $16, the portion was big and worth it. We also got a shot of butternut squash soup on the house. The soup was an acquired taste and not for me.The service was also good. The bartender was attentive and friendly. I would definitely come back here again.

A very different experience than $1 / slice pizza. Upside pizza is the upscale version of pizza slices to go. The Sicilian pepperoni pizza is outstanding. The peppers on the sausage slices added a delicious layer of flavor. The mushroom slices were also very good. The location is take out - we took the pizza in a box and ate the pizza elsewhere.

Title: A Flavorful Arancini Adventure at [Restaurant Name]

Review: Arancini lovers, take note! [Restaurant Name] offers a delightful variety of these scrumptious rice balls, capable of satisfying an array of palates. As someone who isn’t vegan, I was pleasantly surprised by the Beyond sausage-filled arancini; they boast a savory taste that mirrors real ground meat impeccably. The pizza ball arancini is another crowd-pleaser, perfectly encapsulating the essence of a good slice in a bite-sized delight.

For those with a sweet tooth, the Nutella-stuffed arancini is a heavenly treat that melts in your mouth, rounding off the meal on a high note. However, a minor critique would be the texture of the rice — a tad overcooked for my liking. Thus, while the flavors hit the mark, the execution takes a slight dip, landing [Restaurant Name] a solid 4-star rating. Worth a visit for any arancini enthusiast!

I recently dined at this delightful spot where both the food and service truly impressed. The restaurant boasts a fun and casual atmosphere, ideal for unwinding. Sports lovers will appreciate the TVs on the main floor, always tuned into the latest games. They also offer enticing happy hour specials Monday through Friday. It's definitely a great place to visit whether you're looking to kick back with friends or simply enjoy a tasty meal. Highly recommended!

Oooh man Tacos in NYC! If you crave a late-night taco, welp, here it is at Los Tacos No. 1! My NY girlfriend took me here after spending the evening exploring the city upon my early arrival. This place was packed and busy, but the line just kept going and we didn't wait long. We grabbed the Carne Asada (one with flour and the other corn tortilla). The sauces were amazing, although, be careful as one of them is spicy!The meat was cooked perfectly and seasoned well. Easy to eat and go - could get messy though. Please note there are no chairs, so you will be standing and eating. Definitely, a good place to go for late-night and dinner. It's inexpensive and ordering enough tacos could fill you up! Highly recommend this place to friends and family!

After an unassuming arrival in NYC and a few culinary stops, we stumbled upon a restaurant that truly celebrates the culture of rice. It's a hidden gem that proves the adage: if you can't find something you love, you're not looking hard enough. This place caught us completely off guard with its delightful offerings.

Our taste buds were treated to an exquisite rice bowl crowned with sumptuous braised beef and innovative quinoa bao buns that added a contemporary twist. Even the yucca puffs were a revelation. In retrospect, the only regret is not having the appetite to sample one of everything from their tempting menu – a mistake I intend to rectify on a dedicated return visit.

A special shoutout to the staff member who, with infectious enthusiasm, guided us through the menu, ensuring we experienced each dish as it was intended. The music, too, was spot on, adding to the already vibrant atmosphere.

I found myself thoroughly immersed in the experience – a harmonious blend of location, storytelling, and culinary adventure. Kudos to Chef JJ, whose vision and flawless execution left an indelible impression. That experience wasn't just good; it was Gucci.

I walked in with my boyfriend for a dinner on a Wednesday . We had the dinner special . 6 wine tasting each ( 3 white , 3 red) , and appetizer of cheese and meat ( they only have pork which we don't eat so we had cheese only) , 2 entrees , And a bottle  each to go home .The place is VERY SMALL you're basically sitting on top each other and other guest . The decor reminded me of old school French cafe so that was cool. Our server wasn't very engaging and didn't explain the wine he gave us or their origins well  so I didn't like his service at all ...the food  was VERY BLAND and not well described in the menu . Definitely not worth the money. I wouldn't come here again .

So this is my second time going here. The first time I could not remember the name. I had to wait on a friend to give me the location again. They have happy hour pretty much all night long. The drinks are so good, great price, and well sized. I have not had a chance to try the food but I have had the miso soup. That is one of my favorites!! They have a constant flow of traffic, really busy place. We had such a great time. People that come in are extremely friendly and are looking just to have a good time. Just a FYI...If sitting at the bar, you pay as you order. I really do mind.

Moderate sized Korean restaurant specializing in on-table BBQ. Saturday night, not crowded at all, as I was able to sit down without any wait.Menu is extensive with all sorts of selections for both BBQ and single dish options. Went for the Short Rib Bibimbap ($18), and a bottle of Pomegranate "Good Day" Soju ($15). Drink comes out first - a 375ml bottle of cold flavored soju that tasted a lot like medicine and only became acceptable after the alcohol hit. Bibimbap is served in a hot stone pot with a layering of rice, meat, veggies, and egg. Meat was more burnt than it should been, though the egg was perfectly runny to complement the rice. Yelp check-in offers a free Dumpling appetizer - several fried pieces of beef dumpling that was probably the best part of my meal.Service here took it's sweet time to get my order in as well as for the check, while the dishes were delivered quickly. Wasn't feeling the food all that much, so probably won't try the BBQ options.

Despite my initial reservations about the overly polished decor at this establishment, my visit was a pleasant surprise. The bartender truly impressed us with both charm and mixology skills. While one of our drinks experienced a slight delay, the bartender proactively comped it without any prompt from our side — a gesture of excellent customer service. As for the food, we sampled the beer salad which proved to be exceptionally refreshing and flavorful. All in all, this place exceeded my expectations and I'd recommend a visit, even if just for the delightful drinks and commendable service.

I was working across the street (on 34th street) when this Hooters location opened on 33rd street off of 7th Avenue. Known for their wings, a couple coworkers and I went for lunch and I remember one person, in particular, being thoroughly underwhelmed with the food.Now, years later, I've returned and honestly the food was just "meh." Our waitress Meg was An absolute pleasure, incredibly sweet, and attentive. That being said, the red sangria seemed to lack any alcohol and the food was just ok. Not that one would expect five-star flavors from here, but I probably won't be running back any time soon.

Title: A Bright New Addition to the West Village Dining Scene

Review:

Nestled in the West Village where a vacant spot once stood, a delightful new restaurant has sprung up, boasting a gorgeous interior complete with a charming skylight that promises to enhance the ambiance further when daylight lingers past the early twilight hours.

The menu, while concise, offers a tempting selection of snacks, small plates, and hearty entrees. A must-try starter is the crackling Chicken Skins, modestly priced at $6, which are as crisp as one could hope for. Complementing this is the Roasted Chile Focaccia for $7, a savory delight that leaves you wanting more.

The star of the mains is undoubtedly the Chicken priced at $29. What truly elevates this dish is "Mom's Rice," a side so exquisitely flavored that it deserves its own spotlight on the menu. This dish alone is worth the visit; it's not just a meal, but a comforting culinary embrace.

In summary, this new culinary star in the West Village is a welcome addition, offering an experience that is as satisfying to the palate as it is to the soul.

I recently visited a highly talked about restaurant, keen to make my own assessment despite hearing mixed reviews. Opting for an early afternoon visit on a Thursday, I found it comfortably uncrowded. While the service was pleasant and the decor tastefully done, unfortunately, the food didn't live up to the hype. I tried the sweet & spicy wings accompanied by a side of mashed potatoes. Disappointingly, the wings were overcooked, resulting in a tough and difficult to bite texture that detracted significantly from my dining experience. In my opinion, this place isn't worth the buzz, especially when considering the cost versus the quality of the food.

Once upon a time, many years ago, way before Veselka was a late-night hotspot for those who had a few drinks too many and need some hearty eats, my family used to come here for some authentic Ukrainian food (my mother is from there, so we know what we're talking about).Nowadays, it's a zoo and you're stuck waiting for a table. Thankfully, service is fast and they turn tables quickly. I think during my last visit I waited about 25 minutes, which was totally fine.Get the pirogies (vareniki), they're a classic, and you can order them by the piece and mix and match what they're filled with. I like the meat, potato, and cherry ones (apparently these are seasonal), AND you can get them fried of boiled.They also have NY classics like egg creams because lets face it, this is the East Village, and it is a diner-style restaurant so some things HAVE to be on the menu.

I recently visited this restaurant and opted for the lemongrass pork on rice stick. Unfortunately, the dish fell flat with no discernible lemongrass essence, and the pork was overcooked to the point of being dry. On the upside, the prices are reasonable, and the staff is welcoming. While my dining experience was underwhelming, I might consider giving this place another shot if I find myself craving Vietnamese food with no other options available.

Title: A Surprising Delight at [Restaurant Name]

I stumbled upon [Restaurant Name] by chance and the bustling crowd on a Saturday afternoon convinced me to give it a try. Unfamiliar with malatang, I opted for the seafood variety priced at $13. It turned out to be a remarkable discovery—abundant in protein and vegetables within a broth that boasted an indescribably unique flavor profile.

A word of caution—heed the staff's advice on spice levels. My medium-spicy choice pushed the boundaries of my spice tolerance, bringing me to the brink of tears. Next time, I'll be sure to go for a milder heat.

I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit to further explore the menu. For those unacquainted with malatang, [Restaurant Name] is a must-try for an exciting culinary adventure.

I came here last night with my friend  for dinner. She told me she's friends with the chef. I didn't know what to expect but from the moment we walked in we were welcomed and sat down. The food was delicious ! We had the eggplant chips , calamari , buratta with vegetables, rigatoni with Veal and meat, spaghetti with vongele, doughnuts with caramel and cream dip , & chocolate cake with vanilla ice cream. I really enjoyed the sauce on my dishes and the pasta was cooked aldente perfectly!!! I would defiantly come back here again to try more dishes. It's an upscale crowd with very positive vibes !!!!!

Title: A Slice of Bangkok in Manhattan!

If you're scouring Manhattan for the most authentic Thai noodle experience, look no further. This unassuming gem captures the essence of bustling Bangkok street food with its bowls brimming with joy. Their egg noodles are a revelation, particularly the beef stew, grilled duck, and the zesty Tom yum soups. Each dish transports you to the vibrant streets of Thailand's capital with every spoonful.

Don't miss out on their stir-fry basil with white rice — it's simply outstanding and a must-try for any Thai food aficionado. While their somtum (papaya salad) doesn't quite hit the mark (Somtum Der holds the crown for that), it's a minor misstep in an otherwise remarkable menu.

Be warned: their popularity means you're in for a wait, as the cozy venue does not accept reservations. But patience is a small price to pay for some of the best Thai noodles in the city. So, brave the waitlist and get ready for a memorable dining experience that promises to be super delicious!

There was only one bartender for a very busy weekday night so ordering drinks took a very looooong time. We just got Corona's and a $3 happy hour acid drop shot and didn't even bother waiting around for a second round.There's a lot of seating, so finding a place to put our drinks down wasn't a problem. The only thing this tiki bar is missing is sand. You're able to order drinks from your table by scanning the QR code. I didn't try this myself, so I can't rate speed of service but I will say it was nice to have the option to do so.Would probably have been a 4-5 star review had they had more bartenders.

I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant and must commend the incredibly fresh and delicious fare. We indulged in the seasonal oyster appetizer – a true standout for its remarkable flavor and top-notch ingredients. Although prices run high, the quality more than justifies the cost. Desserts were decent, but paled in comparison to the gastronomic delight of the oysters. Highly recommend for those seeking a meal where taste and freshness are prioritized!

Title: A Cozy Haven for Pizza Lovers in NYC

During a recent day trip to NYC, I was whisked away by a local friend to his top pizza pick, and the experience did not disappoint. Despite the dismal rain, the moment I stepped inside, the welcoming scents of melting cheese and sizzling pepperoni provided instant comfort.

I indulged in a classic slice of pepperoni and cheese, each bite oozing with flavor and perfectly balanced. Venturing outside my comfort zone, I sampled the gorgonzola pear slice from my friend's plate – a combination I would normally shy away from. To my surprise, it was delightful, making me question my past cheese choices.

This place might not be your typical hidden gem, but it triumphs where it counts: delivering mouthwatering pizza that beckons for a return visit. Whether you're a traditionalist or an adventurous eater, this spot is a must-try for any pizza enthusiast in the city.

Amazing Thai food. The tofu and vegetable spicy mee goreng (pictured) was hands down the best dish I have ever ordered from a Thai place, but also something I have never tried before as I have not seen this on other menus. Incredible flavor - spicy with a hint of sweetness. My only complaint is there were only 3 pieces of tofu in my meal, and the portion size is small for the price. We also tried the shrimp pad Thai which was also super flavorful. Will definitely order from here again, happy they are still open when so many places have shut down.

I finally got to visit the restaurant my friends have been buzzing about, but pro-tip: reservations are key for parties of four or more, smaller groups can take their chances. My Wednesday night drop-in for three worked out perfectly with no wait.

The starter, Niku Uni, set a tasty tone, and we dived right into a meat feast with filet mignon, short rib, and ribeye. The short rib and filet were standouts—fatty, tender, and enhanced by a divine garlic butter sauce. The ribeye, while decent, didn't reach the same heights, coming through tougher than its companions.

Quality across the board shone through, from the food to the service. The attentive staff guided us through cooking times and techniques for our DIY grilling experience.

The downside? Portion sizes versus price. The 6 thin slices of short rib and ribeye or a slightly larger filet won't lead to a full belly unless you're willing to splurge. We padded our meal with three bowls of rice which helped.

Takashi delivers on taste and service, but be prepared to pay for the pleasure if you're after a truly satiating meal.

I came here on a Thursday evening with a party of 2 and we were seated right away. We were seated incredibly close to another party of 2 which was slightly uncomfortable. Also, We came here for the dim sum but it ends at 4pm everyday, so we'll have to come back for that later! We were given a pot of jasmine tea (water available upon request). We ordered fried dumplings, laksa noodle soup, and three mushroom noodle soup. The dumplings were filled with cabbage, mushroom, and carrots and were delicious. The three mushroom noodle soup was a little bland but the veggies were lovely (and I love mushrooms so I liked this dish). The highlight was the laksa noodle soup which was spicy, tangy, and delicious!! I would order this again for sure. One strange thing was that both noodle soups had thick udon noodles which I thought was a little out of place. For the price, you are given a lot of food and it is very yummy. I would definitely recommend this place!

Having dined at Wok to Walk on three separate occasions, I can confidently say that each visit has outperformed the last. Admittedly, newcomers might find the menu puzzling, as sauces sport peculiar names that give little away about their flavors. However, once you've navigated the initial confusion, the experience is rewarding. The service is notably swift, and the prices are wallet-friendly. While the staff's warmth could use a little boost, it doesn't detract much from the overall experience. Locals looking for consistent quality and value will appreciate Wok to Walk. Tourists might need a moment to acclimate to the ordering system, but the learning curve is well worth the delicious results.

Title: A Local Gem in Uptown: Tom's

If you're wandering uptown looking for a quick, satisfying bite, Tom's will not disappoint. The restaurant offers a versatile menu that includes everything from classic chicken parmesan to fluffy pancakes and hearty burgers. 

Service at Tom's is commendable; the staff exudes friendliness and efficiency. My recent visit reaffirmed this, as it took scarcely ten minutes from ordering to receive my food, steaming and ready to be enjoyed.

The eatery's walls, adorned with celebrity photos and snaps of local patrons, instill a sense of community and history. It's evident Tom's isn't just a restaurant but a long-standing neighborhood fixture.

Opting for the simplicity of a burger and fries, I found it to be nothing short of satisfying, a testament to Tom's commitment to quality across all its offerings. My experience solidified Tom's as a future staple for my uptown culinary adventures.

Stepping into the classy, buzzing atmosphere of this well-known restaurant, further popularized by Robert De Niro, sets the stage for an upscale dining experience. Our group was comfortably seated in a welcoming back dining room, complete with the warmth of a real fireplace.

The meal commenced with a Beetroot Carpaccio that pleasantly surprised my typically beet-averse palate, although the pistachio vinaigrette could have benefited from a bolder presence. The Duck Egg Crostino, topped with freshly shaved white truffle at our table, was a notable dish, albeit singular in its presentation.

The standout was undoubtedly the Mezze Rigatoni, sporting a flawlessly seasoned white veal bolognese and pasta cooked to al dente perfection. Meanwhile, the Pan-Seared Sea Scallops were executed with an impeccable texture, yet the overall flavor profile was underwhelming.

Culminating the meal was a Limoncello Semifreddo, a refreshing and airy dessert that left a lasting impression, especially due to the zesty lemon basil crema.

Service throughout was attentive and professional, ensuring our evening was without fault. While each dish was executed with skill, the overall culinary journey did not quite take my breath away, prompting a solid four-star rating for this reputable establishment.

I came here with a friend on a Tuesday evening, eager to catch up. It was a bit of a trek from Brooklyn, and it reminded me of my college days haunting around LES's grunginess. It took a while to find the place, as it was truly a hole-in the wall and tiny -- just wide enough to fit one large dining table, comfortable enough for 8 guests at a time, with the kitchen in the back. If you need to use the bathroom, you have to awkwardly pass them by.We arrived at 6:30 PM and took our seats in the middle. The plating was very simple, but beautiful, as most Japanese eateries are. The menu was interesting because it wasn't necessarily a ramen bar, as a lot of their mains were broth-less (but not sauceless or flavourless!). The menu also stood out in that it was had clear indications of food allergies/meat types, which I appreciated.Service was impeccable, naturally, as the sole waiter/maitre-d/cashier was within a 5 foot reach. We decided to have an alcohol-free dinner, so I went with the duck mazemen and my companion the steak mazemen as our mains. To start, we got the uni-toast, which was AMAZING. I'm not sure what I was expecting, but it was not the tiny square cracker-sized buttered crunch goodness with generous dollops of uni. I will think about this starter until I die. The duck mazemen and steak were both strong in umame and delightful as dishes, though a tad small if you're looking to get full off of that alone. The flavours were amazing and I was really impressed that there was no broth to back it up.I'd definitely come back to Niche if in the area, and I might even seek it out. However, I'm only giving 4 stars for a reason that is a double-edged sword -- as aforementioned, the menu is simple, but with that, it didn't offer me enough things that I wanted to try, so after the starter/dishes we had, I was still left hungry.

We arrived as walk in at 1pm on a Thursday afternoon for lunch. This place was full happy guests as the restaurant was filled with happy buzz. We were told by the host it would 20-25 mins wait. We were ok with that and was asked to wait in the wait area near the bar.  We were asked if we wanted a table to kitchen bar; whichever is faster. About 11 mins later we were seated at the kitchen bar. It was fun sitting at the kitchen bar as we were able to observe and watch all the action in the open kitchen. All pasta is made in-house. We ordered:-Acqua de Jamaica drink: non-alcoholic cocktail $7. It was delicious! Hibiscus tea, OJ and orange soda- appetizer local Buratta: with marinated fig, balsamic and 3 toast. The buratta was very smooth and light. So yummy!- Gramigna: curly pasta, house made sausage, broccoli with no chili flakes : this tasted earthy and was really tasty. -Campanelle: was really good with burrata.  The pesto was a bit salty according to my hubby. Otherwise really good.  Dessert - Nutella tart - this is to die for! Must order as your dessert here. Was really nice with espresso. I loved the ambiance here. The customer service with all the staff  looking after guests and each other was nice to see. My hubby and I had a wonderful time dining here for lunch.

This review is for their late night RAMEN! Nobu San has done it again! The ramens are truly amazing- definitely one of the best ramens in the city and comparable to ramens in Tokyo. the north is rich but not too salty. The egg is cooked to perfection and is melty in the yolk. The ramens are around 17 dollars and you can add a mini rice bowl to the ramen (this combo is around 25). The portion is on the smaller size but considering they start serving ramen at 11pm on weekdays and midnight on the weekends, then the portion is pretty big hahaha how much can you really eat at 11pm at night?DEFINITELY WORTH A TRY!!!

Most of the time when you run around Manhattan and see a new Thai restaurant the decor either looks like something out of a music video or a new night club (or both).  However, when I saw the interior of Taladwat, it looked like something else entirely: a nice, rustic, comfortable restaurant with large windows that let the sunlight flood in.  It is completely welcoming and draws you in.Taladwat works in an interesting way.  You sit at long picnic style tables, so there is a nice communal feel.  The tables each have a tray with several items ready to go including napkins, forks, spoons and a delicious (and spicy) hot sauce.Their system of ordering is called "Pick & Mix" where you select two dishes from a wide array of choices.  For lunch it will run you $16 and $18 for dinner.  Here's a rundown of the dishes my girlfriend and I tried:VEGETABLE GREEN CURRY (Cauliflower, Bamboo shoot, Asian broccoli, Thai eggplant, Coconut milk)It may seem simple, but green vegetable curry seems to be a dish that either goes really well or really badly in most restaurants.  It either has great flavor or almost none at all.  Thankfully this was a perfect example of the dish.  The vegetables were tender, but not soggy and the the curry was delicious.  Good flavor and not an overwhelming amount of spice.BRAISED SHORT RIB (Peanut, Ginger, Sweet soy, Tamarind garlic sauce)It is important to remember that the food served here is not made to order.  Many of the dishes are made in batches.  This made me worry that the short ribs would be tough, but nope!  The meat was wonderfully tender and fell right off the bone.  The sauce was sweet and savory at the same time.  I would get this dish again for sure.ROASTED CHILI CALAMARI (Onion, Long hot chili, Sweet basil, Roasted chili sauce)Calamari is a trick dish for any chef.  Cook it wrong one way and it's a mushy mess.  Cook it incorrectly another way and it is rubber.  I am happy to report that this dish was cooked perfectly.  The calamari was tender and delicious.  The sweetness of the basil and the chilis were wonderfully balanced.PANANG CURRY BEEF (Kaffir lime, Long hot chili, Coconut milk)Like the short rib, I was a bit worried that the meat would be tough in this dish but it like the short ribs it was wonderfully tender.  The sauce was not particularly thick but man did it have plenty of flavor!  Despite being a curry beef dish, it was not particularly spicy - just very savory.The service at Taladwat was fantastic.  Everyone was very attentive and I never felt like we were being neglected.  The food was great and the space was comfortable, clean and welcoming.  An absolute must try!

Be clear on what this is before coming with the wrong expectations. It's tiny for a reason. It's intimate, it's laid-back, it's fun. Let go of haughtiness, leave it at the door. You won't need it. You're not coming here for the absolute best or authentic food, you're coming here for the collective experience. It has the quirky speakeasy-like entrance, wonderful to surprise someone with. We got some champagne and were able to take the whole bottle downstairs. When you're seated, you get two slips of paper to write down your song pick for the night (it feels like you're picking your entire fate). While the selection is limited, it's a bit less nerve wracking that choosing from the entire world's history of songs- although if you're on a date, it might be fun to discuss what you WOULD pick if the options were limitless. There's a dedicated vinyl DJ, who danced through the night. I adored the staff, they were so engaging and attentive without hovering. And you can curate how much you want to engage. They are super in tune with personalities and the kind of night you want to have, so it felt like a choose-your-own-adventure kind of atmosphere. You can be intimate, you can be rowdy. it's all good. We were lucky to sit at the chef's counter where we had conversations with the chefs. I consider it a huge part of the experience, to watch the food being made and plated. Honestly, the food doesn't take itself too seriously, and neither should you. The snacks were fun accompaniments to the whole meal. Cucumber, popcorn, and pretzels. They were good enough to graze on and abundant enough to not feel like there wasn't enough. They don't do light salt. Things definitely contain MSG. I received a text message before the meal asking about dietary restrictions, and I love that they customize exactly to your needs like, "Okay I'm lactose intolerant but I'm not so lactose intolerant that I won't eat the pineapple cake." Other people dogged on it, but I loved the torched salmon over potato salad. I LOVE potato salad, and for some reason this combination was just perfect. The mayo was delicious, and the two together melted in my mouth and just felt really interesting. I can't eat pizza, so they made me some delicious french fries. And he gave me a slice of pizza anyway, for fun. I tore off the cheese and gave it to my date. The food was filling enough that I didn't feel like we really needed the pizza at the end. But it was a fun cap to the night. Take someone open-minded. Be prepared to be entertained.

Title: A Gem in the Heart of Greenwich Village: Don Angie

Rating: ★★★★☆

Don Angie is an Italian American treasure with a modern twist that makes it stand out in Manhattan's bustling dining scene. However, landing a table can feel like winning the lottery due to its popularity— persistence and patience are key.

Once you do get in, opt for an outdoor table for a more tranquil experience. The interior can buzz with chatter, so those looking for a quieter ambiance will appreciate the outside seating.

The menu, while on the pricier side, boasts inventive dishes worth shelling out for. The Stuffed Garlic Flatbread is a marvel of culinary engineering—impossibly thin and stuffed with melty cheese, it's a garlicky delight not to be missed. The Tonnato Vitello, a rare find, combines veal tartare and tuna carpaccio with a crisp, acidic lemon twist.

Pasta lovers should dive into the Stracchino Gnocchi and Buffalo Milk Caramelle, both unique in shape and preparation, although the portion sizes can leave you wanting more. Skip the lasagna and save room for the star of the show—the Prime Rib Braciole for Two. Despite its steep price at $116, it’s a masterpiece of flavors worth every penny. This dish is limited, so inquire as soon as you arrive.

For dessert, even skeptics of zeppoles will be converted by Don Angie's light, non-greasy version, complete with pistachios and whipped robiola cheese.

While Don Angie may not claim the title of the ultimate Italian establishment, its distinctive menu offerings certainly carve out a memorable niche. It's a place that surprises and delights, ensuring that every effort to secure a table is well rewarded.

I recently visited a charming pizza joint, where the cozy ambiance was a delightful backdrop to our meal. The three of us started with the fried calamari appetizer, which was surprisingly satisfying and set a promising tone for the main course. We shared one pizza pie and found ourselves comfortably full by the end of the meal. I personally savored the thin crust of the pizza, though my companions mentioned a preference for a thicker crust. Nevertheless, the experience was overall enjoyable and the restaurant nails the brief for a decent pizza place.

Title: A Rustic Noodle Encounter at 88 Lan Zhou

Upon visiting 88 Lan Zhou in Chinatown, I was greeted by a straightforward, no-frills atmosphere. Larger than the quaint hole-in-the-wall, this place offers sit-down service, akin in its brusqueness to that charmingly curt counter-service we've all experienced.

During my visit a few months ago, the hand-pulled noodles were the star. I opted for the beef noodle soup, modestly priced at $7. The broth was a delightful surprise, rich and flavorful, while the noodles themselves were delightfully chewy. However, the beef fell short of expectations; a more premium cut would enhance this dish immensely. Despite this, the portion size was generous, ensuring you won't leave hungry.

Take note, 88 Lan Zhou is a cash-only establishment. Service can range from indifferent to outright unfriendly, though it's undeniably efficient. The seating arrangement leans towards the communal, adding to the authentic experience, but be aware that you won't find complimentary water here.

Overall, for a hearty meal that won't break the bank, this spot has potential, especially if they amp up the beef quality.

I decided to start with four stars, because I made an order to take home. I didn't stay to participate in the whole dining in experience, but I can tell you that there will be another visit from me. I was so satisfied with what I did take home, which was two orders of soup dumplings.  They both were really good and I liked how they package them for home delivery. So when I got home they were still hot and delicious and one order I was able to warm up really nicely for the next day. It was like I just resteamed them myself using my microwave. I also loved the way I was treated when I arrived, I was given a menu, I asked a couple of questions and then made my order. Everything was made fresh and I liked the whole vibe of the restaurant, and I can tell you it was really clean and had alot of character to the place.So from just my first visit, it was good, and I cant wait to return to see how the whole dining experience works out.F.Y.I. they take cash, and cards.

Carnitas ($26): served in a little cast iron skillet thing, this roast suckling pig has some really good grilled/charred exteriors and pretty moist meat. But ahhh very salty (as expected of a carnitas dish though). It's pretty good, but I probably wouldn't get this again as it's a little on the pricey side for the solo portionAvocado Fries ($8): first time trying avocado fries and I've decided while I'm a huge fan of avocados, this isn't really my thing. The color on this wasn't really golden, it's a little dirtier than that lol. Good crunch, but inside was super mushy in a way that guac doesn't make me feel the same.
