Guacamole ($12): hate paying these prices for guac but these were some chunky delicious pieces Carne Asada ($28): didn't try the steak on this but the fried rice is soo good. I love the kind of fried rice that you can taste every grain of (which surprisingly, not a lot of places can master well) and it was super flavorfulAs for desserts, churros were good (but duh, churros) and the banana cake was of the thicker pancake kind (instead of thin crepes) so not too soft, and over the top sweet.

Title: Cozy West Village Experience with Room for Flavor Enhancement

After a year of anticipation fueled by glowing recommendations, my visit to this much-talked-about West Village gem finally came to fruition. A bustling Saturday night scene necessitated a lengthy 1.5-hour wait—perhaps exacerbated by news of its upcoming closure.

We indulged in a trio of offerings: chicken, potatoes, and gnocchi. Both the potatoes and gnocchi edged out the chicken in terms of satisfaction, presenting a well-executed balance of comfort and taste. While the chicken fell short of its hyped reputation, lacking the expected burst of flavor, it was nonetheless a decent dish.

No single plate left a memorable imprint of culinary excellence, but the overall experience was pleasant. This quaint establishment certainly warrants a nod for a reliably good dinner spot, worthy of a repeat visit should the opportunity arise.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at Spot Dessert Bar

After much resistance due to its hype, I finally succumbed to the allure of Spot Dessert Bar in New York—and I'm glad I did. The skeptics were wrong; this place isn't just a show of mediocrity with a steep price tag.

Even on a bustling Saturday evening, the service was impeccable, with attentive waiters ensuring our glasses were never empty and our experience was top-notch. We dove into two of their famed concoctions: The Harvest and the Milky Puff.

The Harvest, a dessert that has flooded social media feeds, was an unforeseen delight. As a cheesecake skeptic, I was taken aback by its exceptional moistness and lightness, harmoniously paired with fresh berries and an unexpected layer of chocolate cake. Despite the raspberry sorbet's overly tangy note, the dessert's layered complexity won me over.

Then came the Milky Puff, which stole the show for me. Featuring a dreamy union of milky ice cream resting atop a flaky pastry, it was drizzled generously with honey and accompanied by a white chocolate bark. Although the honey's sweetness was slightly overpowering, the pastry itself was a standout—worthy of a solo encore.

In summary, Spot Dessert Bar exceeded my expectations with their sophisticated offering of desserts that were as thoughtfully plated as they were flavorful. Contrary to my initial reservations, I can confidently recommend this dessert bar to others and will surely revisit it myself. Spot is a sweet symphony where culinary craftsmanship meets dessert artistry—undoubtedly deserving of its acclaim.

Believe it or not, this was my first time having ramen. My family is in town so we took the trip out to New York for some Christmas activities and stopped at Yama for lunch. It's very small inside and seems to get a bit crowded at lunch time. We waited about 20 minutes to be called for a table. I ordered a hot tea to keep me warm until the ramen arrived. My boyfriend ordered a Sapporo Japanese beer. I saw there was a veggie option so I went with that. I ordered it shoyu style which is the soy sauce based broth. I added a poached egg for an additional $2. I now fully understand why people love ramen. It's such comfort food and it heats you up quickly, especially on a cold winter day like yesterday. My ramen was delicious. I found myself trying to get every last drop of broth in my mouth and eating the noodles before they got cold. There is a unisex bathroom. Walk towards the entrance and behind the sushi counter to find it. It was clean inside and they had a diffuser in there that made it smell nice. When the bill came, my boyfriend's brother picked up the tab. He signed for everything and then our waitress came back with another receipt and said she forgot to add 2 beers. It was odd but we didn't question it. Service was pretty good otherwise.

Located underground in Ktown, you can spot this restaurant by its happy hour sign on the sidewalk. Came for their happy hour to celebrate a friend's birthday on a. Wednesday evening. There were only a few parties and the rest of the tables were empty. Ordered:Watermelon soju - thought it could be a little sweeterGrapefruit soju (bottle)Fried Chicken with ktown sauce - the sauce is amazing and mild at best, highly recommend Buddae Casserole - similar to buddae jiggae it has sausages, spam, noodles, rice cake, cabbage and tofu in soup. This one has a kick to itYou need to order drinks in order to get the happy hour food. They also give the table a small plate of nachos and salad. Service was good and accommodating. They also let us put our friend's birthday cake in the back to keep it cool. TLDR; get the fried chicken with ktown sauce

Title: Lukewarm Experience at Melt Shop

I recently visited the Melt Shop with a gift card in hand, hoping to indulge in a quick, savory snack. The visit, however, was underwhelming from the outset. I received no welcoming gestures upon entry, which was disheartening in the desolate and confined space.

Deciding to dine in, I ordered the cheesy tater tots and hot honey tenders, only for them to be served suspiciously fast. This speed of service raised concerns about the freshness of my meal—a hunch that proved correct as the tenders lacked both heat and crispness. The one redeeming feature was the flavorful hot honey sauce. The tater tots fared slightly better in texture but failed in temperature, with the cheese overpowering in its saltiness.

Regrettably, the experience did not justify the prices, and it seems pre-cooked fare may be the norm here. While I may give another location a chance for the sake of my gift card, my return to this particular Melt Shop is definitely off the table.

Service well, the first time my sweet potato fries  were cold. Had to change them. The second time while enjoying my fries i find what looks like beard hair.Ew I had the guac burger was decent tasted like a taco And the seasonal lemonade which was matcha YUCK it was not good.

Title: Morelos Truck - A Must-Visit for Taco Lovers in Williamsburg

If you’re on the hunt for mouth-watering tacos in Williamsburg, look no further than the Morelos food truck, conveniently parked next to Dunkin' Donuts. This gem is my go-to spot, rivaling even my other favorite, Yummy Taco in Canarsie.

The Morelos truck doesn't disappoint with their fresh, made-to-order fare. My favorites include the succulent pork and zesty fish tacos, but the chicken and steak options are equally tantalizing. Prices are fair, portions are generous, and every bite is packed with flavor—especially the steak-loaded nachos!

For those sensitive to heat, ask them to hold the hot sauce; they're accommodating. Each order comes with a creamy guacamole, crisp radishes, and lime to enhance the taste experience.

Did I mention they accept cards, with a reasonable minimum? So there's no stress if you're not carrying cash. Trust me, you'll want to grab at least a few tacos—with four setting you back just $16, it's an absolute steal.

In short, Morelos is a culinary delight you can't afford to miss. Indulge in their delectable tacos and thank me later!

Maybe I should have just stuck the pizza. Judging by the reviews and all the people at my table who ordered pizza, everyone enjoyed it. I decided to be different and order pasta because the Pappardelle in Carbonara Sauce sounded really good. It was Pappardelle tossed in homemade carbonara sauce made with bacon and pulled chicken white meat, shiitake and portobello mushrooms, white wine and cream. In theory, it sounds good - I love pappardelle and carbonara. Sadly, it did not taste good. The chicken tasted like leftover chicken, and there was no flavor to the dish. I had to keep adding salt and red pepper flakes. At least the pasta was al dente and the garlic bread it was served with was good (albeit a bit oily). The drinks are not any better. The aperol spritz here isn't very good - pretty sure it's just aperol and seltzer, and the wine is pretty terrible. I tried a sip of the pinot noir my friend ordered and we both agreed it tasted like the three buck chuck from Trader Joe's, except it was 4x the price for a glass, and was served in a water cup.It was a pretty disappointing experience in general. Not sure if I'd want to come back to try the pizza.

Felidia is a classic upscale Upper East Side establishment. Think white table cloth but classic Italian feel. My Aunt and I dined here mid-week and the first striking thing noticed is the dark wood tones and the exquisite décor. The service here cannot also go un mentioned. It was of the upscale professional variety which is befitting of the establishment and the neighborhood. The food here really shines, specifically the fish and pasta dishes. It is a little on the pricier side but it is worth every penny if you want to treat yourself to an upgraded and elevated dining experience.

Title: Pleasantly Surprised Despite the Wait

I recently dined at a newly opened restaurant that I felt deserved a solid four-star rating, particularly due to the excellent quality of the food. Despite initial skepticism from lower reviews, my experience was quite the contrary. The staff's manners were impeccable, contributing to a top-notch service rating from me. Friendly and attentive service is crucial, and I am happy to say they delivered.

However, there was a notable hiccup with the timing of our meals. My dining companion received her food promptly, but I was left waiting for my salmon sandwich long after she had finished eating. Despite the delay, the sandwich, when it did arrive, was delicious and met my expectations.

The waitress was apologetic about the situation, which speaks volumes about their customer service. While the wait for food was a drawback, I understand that new establishments have teething problems, and I am optimistic that this issue will be resolved.

Overall, the quality of the food and the service left a positive impression, and I am looking forward to returning in the hope that the timing issues have been ironed out.

Title: A Culinary Gem Worth Your Reservation

I highly recommend this bustling gem of a restaurant, where reservations are a must, even for a party of two. The bar may offer a cozy spot for a drink or a bite, but the full experience demands a table.

The pasta shines here – cooked to perfection with a flawless texture, and accompanied by a savory, well-balanced sauce. Their Scampi, with its delightful crunch, is a testament to the kitchen's attention to detail. Don't miss out on the bread sticks, which come with a subtly spicy tomato dip that complements them beautifully.

Wine selection is solid, though the cocktails, while adequate, may not justify their premium pricing; they're on par with what you'd find at a good lounge.

Desserts are a highlight, with the sorbets receiving mixed reviews based on personal preference. The chocolate pudding, however, is a standout, boasting rich flavor, perfect consistency, and beautifully paired with fresh cream and crunchy hazelnuts. It's a decadent treat best shared, given its richness.

The service is top-notch, unswayed by the occasional mishap – a testament to the staff's professionalism. The atmosphere strikes the right balance, lively yet not overly loud, with a setting that accommodates both casual and dressed-up patrons equally.

In summary, this place is more than just a meal; it's an experience in good taste and impeccable service. Suitable for a variety of occasions, I eagerly anticipate my next visit.

Title: A Burst of Flavors and Vibes at the New Noodle Spot

My anticipation for the opening of this new noodle joint had been building ever since the signs and construction caught my eye. Finally stepping inside, I was greeted by an atmosphere oozing good vibes, with super cute decor, ample seating, and an incredibly welcoming staff.

The menu's versatility impressed me. Whether you go for a pre-made dish, tweak it to your tastes, or go rogue and create something uniquely yours, the choices seem endless. And it's not just noodles—they offer salads too, customizable just the same.

I opted for their kimchi dish, and it was a flavor explosion that did not disappoint. My friend’s dish, while I can’t recall the name, was equally impressive in taste. Each dish was not only delicious but also a feast for the eyes, presented with vibrant colors that commanded attention.

We hit a small snag with my friend's order, but the staff handled it with grace and efficiency, immediately replacing the dish with no fuss—exemplifying top-notch service.

The cherry on top was a chat with the owner, whose presence that evening added a personal touch. Her warmth and passion for her craft were as clear as day, making sure to touch base with customers, reflecting her deep care for the restaurant.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit when I'm back in the area. This spot is a definite must-try for its delectable flavors, beautiful presentation, and heartfelt hospitality.

Title: Hidden Gem Discovered - New York's Finest Pizza

If you're on a quest for the ultimate New York pizza experience, look no further. I've been sampling slices at all the famous joints and top Yelp-reviewed eateries across New York for years, but this time, I stumbled upon an uncharted treasure that's not even listed online, and it's blown me away.

Tucked away from the digital map, this unassuming pizzeria is a revelation for any pizza aficionado. My group and I sampled a delightful array – the classic cheese, a verdant veggie, and a flawless margherita, not to mention the divine garlic knots. The beers on offer complemented our meal perfectly, creating an unbeatable pizza and beer combo.

The margherita won my heart with its impeccable balance and taste, while my husband crowned the cheese pizza as his favorite. The veggie variant also received high praise from our friends. Each pizza boasted the kind of thin, crispy crust that dreams are made of, with just the right harmony of sauce and cheese.

Adding to the charm was the owner's family – a hospitable trio of husband, wife, and son who provided a delightful and engaging experience. They created a family-friendly atmosphere that was particularly welcoming to the children in our group.

In short, this place delivers not just a meal but an experience: mouthwatering pizza perfection paired with warm hospitality. It's a must-visit for anyone seeking the best New York pizza without the hype. I wholeheartedly recommend this pizzeria for an unparalleled slice of the city!

I recently dined at this local eatery and had the pleasure of trying their spinach pie. The dish was delicious and truly satisfied my cravings. The flavors were well-balanced, and the pie was cooked to perfection. However, it's worth noting that the preparation time was somewhat lengthy, so I'd suggest placing an order in advance if you're short on time. Despite the wait, the quality of the meal was undeniable, and I'm definitely looking forward to my next visit.

Came here for brunch today with another couple and it was pretty busy right at the opening. The prices are pretty normal for NYC, drinks around 14-15 dollars, and our brunch bill for two people was 47.00 with tip with only getting tea or coffee. We both got the eggs Benedict which were good but nothing amazing for the price. The home fries could've been crispier, but that could be more so us for not asking for it.

Title: Quaint Charm but Culinary Misses at [Restaurant Name]

Walking into [Restaurant Name], you're immediately enveloped in a pretty and cute atmosphere that's well-decorated, giving off a homey vibe. To avoid disappointment due to its cozy size, I'd recommend securing a reservation, especially during dinner hours.

Opting for the full tasting menu, which promised to showcase the restaurant's best, I found myself underwhelmed. The opener of beet juice-soaked deviled eggs lacked the punch of flavor I anticipated and bordered on blandness, while the accompanying biscuits were unfortunately dry. 

The main course brought a glimmer of redemption with succulent fried chicken and a delightful mac & cheese that hit the right comfort food notes. However, the pickled watermelon side, doused in an unexpected savory sauce, missed the mark for me, clashing with the fruit's natural sweetness and freshness.

Dessert was a mixed bag; the bourbon in the pecan pie overwhelmed my palate, but the slice of Key Lime Pie was spot on—striking the perfect balance between tart and sweet without being overbearing.

In summary, [Restaurant Name]'s efforts at innovation fell flat for some dishes, and the overall experience didn't quite deliver the southern charm I craved. Coupled with the steep prices, the meal felt just "OK." Should I return, I'd stick with the fried chicken and pass on the rest.

Title: A Spicy Delight at Mala Project

If you're a fan of bold flavors and customizable meals, look no further than the Mala Project. This gem offers an inventive twist on the traditional hot pot with its 'dry pot' experience, sans the broth but stacked with a wide range of meats, veggies, and a generous dollop of spice.

The ordering process is simple and interactive; you pay by the ingredient, designing your own pot from a variety of proteins—including beef tenderloin, fish, and even adventurous options like tripe and kidney—priced between $4-$12. Vegetables and other sides such as enoki mushrooms and tofu skin are also available, generally costing $3-$5.

I am a spice aficionado and the 'Spicy' level at Mala Project hits the spot. On my visit, an $18 combo of fish fillet, lotus root, pig intestine, and potato left me more than satisfied. It's hard not to relish the dish presented in a grand wooden bowl, finished with cilantro and sesame seeds—a true feast for both the eyes and the palate.

The ambiance of Mala Project is both cozy and quaint, making it an excellent choice for a romantic date or a casual meet-up with friends. Its ability to blend a convivial atmosphere with scrumptious, customize-able fare makes it a go-to spot for anyone craving an authentic dry pot experience. I'll definitely be returning to savor more combinations from their diverse menu.

Last Friday night at 8 PM, I dined at Blue Smoke, nestled in the bustling heart of the city. We had a reservation, which I highly recommend, as it allowed us to be seated immediately despite the restaurant being quite busy. The atmosphere is laid-back with a casual dress code, and the service is swift and attentive, with a no-tipping policy that is quite refreshing.

My evening kicked off with a Blood Orange Margarita that was nothing short of delectable, especially with the thoughtful touch of salt on just half the rim. For the main event, we indulged in the Rhapsody set, a $45 per person meat feast that included brisket, ribs, chicken, pulled pork, and sausage, coupled with a range of sides from biscuits and cole slaw to mac and cheese, fries, collard greens, creamy spinach, and beans.

As someone with a BBQ background from both North Carolina and Texas, I have quite the high bar for what passes as good BBQ. The standout dishes were the ribs—tender and well-seasoned, the brisket—savory yet moist, the lusciously creamy mac and cheese, crispy fries, and the flavorful beans. The collard greens deserve an honorable mention despite being slightly overcooked.

Regrettably, not all that glitters is gold. The pulled pork and sausage failed to impress, as both were parched and bland—in stark contrast to the other mouthwatering offerings.

Would I return? Absolutely—but I'll be there for the sublime ribs and the delectable sides. And I'm already eyeing the wings for my next visit, curious to see how they stack up against the famous fare at Pig Beach in Brooklyn.

This is a relatively new option at the Korean cafeteria so I was curious to try it.They display a lot of their more popular dishes which makes it easy to choose. I had the Seafood Pepper Bomb (extra spicy) for $12.99 and I absolutely loved it. I like the width and thickness of the udon noodle. There were plenty of big shrimp, mussels, etc. It's quite a large portion so I packed part of it for my next meal. I also got their chili powder and kimchi which are complimentary. If I were to compare it to other places at the Korean cafeteria, I feel like it's similar to the $10 (no meat) spicy noodles at Kobeque. These noodles were spicier and a bigger portion which I definitely liked. (I liked how you can adjust the spicy level here so if you wanted it mild you could choose that instead). The noodles at Kobeque can be paired with bulgogi beef or spicy pork for $5 more so it just depends if you're more into red meat or seafood etc. I would come back to try the Jjam Bbong ($10.99). It looks similar to the Seafood Pepper noodles in terms of the sauce and flavors, but it's a noodle soup.All in all, I was definitely impressed.

Got the chili, loved all the onions!  The garlic fries were good, but nothing I couldn't whip up at home ($7). The sliders were not my fave.  My hub ordered them and enjoyed them, where I felt the meat tasted reheated.  The Jack's something or other dark beer was really good!  Loved the atmosphere.  We chilled for a while, ordered well tequilla shots ($10/per)...listened to great music.

Disappointed of the ramen. I have been hearing good things about shinka ramen. My friend ordered bone marrow. Only half of the bone marrow can actually be put into the soup. Soup is great but extremely oily. My spicy ramen soup is oily as well. It is not bad but nothing special. The waitress actually makes me want to walk out of the door. She is annoyed that i asked about free yelp checkin edamame. I can see her using the app line all the time in the corner. Customer actually need to wait a long time to get her attention and once they do she is very unfrendly. Me and my friend ended up asking the girl from the bar for help.Btw this is not a japanese ramen place. The dishes are bone marrow noodle and spicy pork noodle.

We came on NYE after somehow getting a reservation just 5 days in advance. I'm so glad we had the forethought to do so because the place was packed. In addition to the main dining room, there's also a cozier and more romantic dining room next to the bar, which was where we were seated.For drinks, we had the Pietradolce rosé and the Montepulciano; both of which were Italian and delicious. The wine list was decently long and varied, with wines from both Italy and others.For NYE, it seemed they had a special menu, which also included many of their regular menu staples. To start, we had the burrata caprese and the fried shiitake caps stuffed with shrimp. The caprese was creamy and bright and wonderful. The shiitake mushrooms were good, but not our favorite, as the shrimp had a chewy texture and a flavor similar to a shrimp/fish cake you'd find in a bowl of ramen. This was really surprising because this dish was recommended by Michelin.We then shared the squid ink pasta with seafood entree, which was surprisingly both a hit AND a simultaneous miss. The pasta was cooked to a perfect al dente and the sauce was phenomenal! However, the seafood was over-cooked to death (the mussels looked like raisins, tiny and wrinkled). This didn't detract from the amazing flavors of the dish as a whole, but seafood in a seafood pasta should shine as brightly as the pasta.We ended our meal with the tiramisu, which was, without a doubt, the most delicious tiramisu I'd ever had. I generally find Italian desserts to be overly sweet and heavy, but this tiramisu was light and fluffy and moist and delicious!

I recently visited Chelsea Market and had the pleasure of indulging at a spot renowned for its cauliflower dish. As someone who isn't normally a fan of cauliflower, I was skeptical but ended up pleasantly surprised. The dish was remarkable—skillfully charred, seasoned with just the right amount of salt and oil, yet it still managed to embody a feel of Mediterranean lightness and health. This visit was a culinary highlight amongst other noteworthy stops, including a fabulous Taiwanese dan dan and mock duck experience that I declare the best in the city. Chelsea Market's vibrant atmosphere remains unbeatable, and this establishment is a must-visit for both skeptics and cauliflower connoisseurs alike.

**Title: A Night of Culinary Elegance with a Side of Duck**

Last week, my friend and I decided to treat ourselves to dinner at a local culinary hotspot. Upon arrival, a receptionist courteously directed us to our dining floor, hinting at the establishment's expansive setup.

The ambiance of the dining room? Nothing short of elegant and classy—perfect for a weeknight escape from the everyday.

Our mission was clear: Roast Peking Duck. We opted for the half portion and threw in some appetizers and entrees to round out the meal, one of which was the lobster rice dish. Let me tell you, it was a plate of pure, delightful indulgence.

But now, the main event: the duck. If there's one culinary takeaway, it's that this might very well be the city's premier Peking Duck. Complete with a tantalizingly crunchy skin, the right blend of spices, and a hint of smokiness, it was evident the chefs here take their craft seriously.

Admittedly, the duck was a tad fattier than the traditional fare you'd find in Asia's top Peking Duck establishments. Nonetheless, for a local rendition, it was nearly impeccable.

Would I return? For a duck that's borderline divine, you bet.

Title: A Mixed Experience at a Caribbean Spot in New York

My recent visit to this Caribbean restaurant was truly a roller coaster of highs and lows. Celebrating my birthday, I was enticed by the promise of authentic Caribbean cuisine in New York, which I believe is unmatched in its authenticity outside of the region itself.

We made a reservation through OpenTable and arrived around 8:30 PM, stepping into the lively atmosphere created by a fantastic live band. It was immediately apparent that this wasn't my usual choice of a more low-key establishment, yet the excitement of the evening was undeniable.

The service started on a high note – the host was polite, and our server greeted us with warmth. I decided to try the curry salmon on the server's recommendation, accompanied by collard greens, pumpkin rice, and a side of mac and cheese. Unfortunately, not all that glitters is gold; the standout of the meal was, surprisingly, the mac and cheese. It's a sad verdict when the supposedly supporting dish overshadows the main.

While the live band was a delight, playing all the tunes I adore, their presence proved to be a double-edged sword. Our server seemed overwhelmed by the noise, resulting in a challenge to communicate and a lack of attention towards our table. This detracted from the dining experience, as the vibrant ambiance became a source of distraction.

The most disheartening disappointment came in the form of the flavorless pumpkin rice. Billed with promise, it turned out to be no more than plain steamed rice in disguise – a letdown for a dish I had high hopes for.

Although the evening had its pleasant moments, it ended on a sour note with an erroneous notification from OpenTable indicating that I had never shown up for my reservation. In reflecting on the entire experience, I have concluded that this restaurant might be suitable for a casual outing with small bites and drinks, but I might hesitate before counting on it for a full dinner service again.

Cool place. Love the interior. Great happy hour with the 19 dollar bar steak (the bavette cut). Its 5-7 during the week. And they have a couple drinks on happy hour for 9 dollars too. The Negroni is pretty good. I thought it was heavy on the sweet vermouth but i love sweet vermouth so i liked it. Bar tender was nice, kind of snappy attitude in the beginning but he gave great service. We both got the bar steak with curley fries. Mine was undercooked so had to send it back but the staff adressed it quickly and I didn't need to wait long. The steak was pretty chewy, but it had great flavor, I still really liked it. And curly fries where great too. The steak sauce is okay, on the vinegary side though. I loved the dessert we got, the smores cake. So delicious huge slice of dense cake that was sweet and chocolatey. Def can be split with up to 4 people. It was really rich. The smores flavor didn't jump out at me. Tasted mostly like sweetness and chocolate but it was so good and a good ending to the meal. I felt so satisfied. Will definitely come back during happy hour. And also a great place to bring business clients. Saw this place on the Flay list, Sophie Flay's pick for a steak house. Its a good pick!

Title: Unbeatable Udon at Raku NYC

If you're an udon enthusiast like myself, you can't do better than Raku in New York City. This spot has earned the top position on my list with their impeccable noodles – the chewiest, most perfectly prepared I've come across to date. No matter how full I am, I can't help but devour every last strand.

My go-to selections are the ankake, with its comforting egg in rich soup, and the nameko, a delightful mix of mushrooms and seaweed, both featuring the satisfyingly dense broth I crave. Portions strike that just-right balance between hearty and overwhelming, complemented by a fair price point.

For those wanting to skip the lines, I recommend hitting up their Soho location where reservations are an option. Don't miss out on what I'd boldly call the best udon experience in the city.

Very poor managerial service.  My waitress did her best to accommodate us, but due to a mix up in the kitchen, my order was delayed, delayed, delayed...Manager stereotyped me with another party then was very unapologetic with the service. Repeating "I took it off your bill" but if I couldn't afford to eat here. I would not have made reservations.Nevertheless the truffle mash potatoes I had were very good and thank you for the tequila shots ... UPDATE:  40 minutes later, meal received... but donated to the homeless outside.

Wednesday lunch for 2 at noon. Made reservations. It got busy.Super cozy place and convenient place for a weekday lunch meet around work with my friend, coming in from NJ. Lively but quiet enough to have an intimate conversation. Loved all the details of the menu drawer in the table, the wooden spoon displays and the lighting. One thing I would recommend is to have coat/bag hangers near the back tables so that they would be nearby. The chair backs are rounded so you can't hang a bag on the back of it. And during winter, I would like to hang my long coat on the wall vs the back of my chair.Food - we both ordered bimbimbap in the hot iron skillet (+$3). I wasn't too hungry but I finished the entire entree, which means it was good!I would go back to try the bulgogi sliders and have a drink at the bar for another quick lunch meet.

Title: A Delightful Surprise at an Underrated Gem

My husband and I stumbled upon this cozy eatery before returning home, and what a pleasant discovery it turned out to be! We were so enamored with our first experience that a second visit was non-negotiable. Despite its unassuming ratings, this place shines with its wallet-friendly prices and absolutely delectable pizza. Don't let the modest reviews deter you – it's a must-visit spot for anyone in search of a culinary treat!

Title: New Eatery Offers More Style Than Substance

Rating: 2.75/5 – It’s Okay

Just opened, this restaurant boasts an impeccably clean and modern interior with an eye-catching minimal bar design. It's a great choice for both drinks and dinner. The highlight of our visit was the cocktail menu; both the Don Agrio and the Lime Out the Door were meticulously crafted at $16 apiece and proved to be the best part of the evening.

The food, albeit good, didn't quite match up to our drink experience. We started with Potato Fritters ($12) served with a delectable salt cod aioli. Despite being a tad mushy inside, they were surrounded by a deliciously crisp exterior. The Roasted Delicata Squash ($15) impressed with its perfect blend of softness, bite, and crunch, earning the spot of my favorite appetizer.

For the main course, the Snowdance Farm Half Chicken ($29) was served with 'mom's rice'—a perfectly cooked combination enhanced by the smart addition of olives. The chicken itself was moist and well-seasoned, but slightly on the salty side.

While the staff was polite, the restaurant seemed to lack a unique character, with the team performing their duties without emotion, which, sadly, left the atmosphere feeling flat. It was a dining experience that, while satisfactory, lacked memorable moments. Overall, everything at this new spot was just "good," but nothing stood out as exceptional.

My favorite NYC Deli, the food is absolutely delicious and portions huge! The service is fantastic, shout out to Max!My friend ordered her usual meat platter, half pastrami, half brisket. It would never have occurred to me to order that, but next time I'm there, it's exactly what I will get, except all pastrami. OMG, the flavor! It literally melted in your mouth. Dip it in 2nd Ave Deli's signature mustard and it's perfection on a plate. For my meal I ordered a tuna salad sandwich and then realized, there is no way I could finish an entire sandwich. Max actually heard me saying this and came back to our table to see if I wanted to change my order to a half sandwich and a bowl of matzo ball soup. Why, yes, I would! Much better choice. The soup arrived with carrots, egg noodles and a ginormous matzo ball. Max then poured the delicious golden chicken broth over the contents and I dug in. So satisfying, comfort food at its best! Served with sweet, soft Challah bread, it could be the entire meal. The tuna salad was delicious, white tuna flaked very thin with mayo and celery. Served on rye with lettuce, tomato and red onion, a half sandwich was plenty!We left no room for desert but did enjoy the shots of chocolate egg creme that came with our check. Wish I had bought some Rugelach and Kugel pudding to take home. It is prepackaged and lines the deli counter.  Next time for sure!Prices are high but food is so delicious it's worth it! Btw, the 2nd Ave Deli is located on 1st Ave.

Title: Nautical Nibbles with a View at Pilot

Nestled among New York City's eclectic boat bars, Pilot stands out as a hidden gem offering a reprieve from the crowds—boasting what may be the best skyline view of its competitors. This vessel affords diners the novel experience of dining practically atop the lapping waves of the harbor, with a vista that's as breathtaking as the city itself.

The cocktail menu is a highlight, with the 'Permanent Vacation' being the perfect accompaniment to a sun-kissed day on the water, delivering a tropical infusion that's as refreshing as the sea breeze. Straying from the drinks, however, the culinary voyage at Pilot can feel somewhat adrift. While the oysters pass muster, the remainder of the menu seems to be navigating through overpriced and uninspiring waters. The lobster roll, albeit tasty, is notably small for the steep cost, and the burrata and ceviche offer little more than a fleeting taste, hardly enough to satisfy the appetite of a seafaring guest.

Despite these culinary setbacks, the overall ambiance at Pilot is undeniably charming and laid-back, making it an ideal spot for those looking to simply unwind with a drink in hand and the city's skyline as a backdrop. It's a venue best suited for light snacking and sipping rather than a full-fledged dinner. In short, Pilot is your go-to for a serene, scenic sip—just don't drop anchor looking for a feast.

I stopped by this charming eatery for lunch and was pleased to find a short wait time and ample seating. Opting for the minute rib eye, I was initially skeptical about its size, but it proved to be satisfyingly hearty. The pita bread served alongside was a delightful companion - soft and fluffy, enhancing the robust flavors of the meat and sauces. The staff was welcoming and efficient, ensuring a swift delivery of my meal. All in all, it was a gratifying dining experience.

Came here for Valentine's Day and enjoyed it so much!! Very traditional Japanese restaurant and the meat is very high quality. I came back from Japan recently and can honestly say it's very comparable. We got the foie gra and filet and the wagyu uni sushi pieces to try first. These were delicious but I guess you can never really go wrong with wagyu uni. Of course we had to get the treasure box and on that day it was wagyu sirloin. Thought the concept of this was really cool. We also got the premium 4 types of beef, which was okay. The garlic fried rice was probably my favorite HAHA and the cold noodles were also super refreshing. It was an expensive meal but you pay for what you get!

This is one of my favorite places for afternoon tea and fine dining experience. The atmosphere is just beautiful and comfortable with gorgeous china. The service is exquisite; attentive and yet gives you enough space. We ordered both the regular Whitby afternoon tea and the healthy afternoon tea. A few of us ordered off the lunch menu options. The presentations, flavors, and textures were all spot on. Their afternoon tea was very reasonable at $45 per person with $3 extra for certain tea options when we first started visiting. But the price has since increased to $55 per person.All in all, this is an excellent place to have a chill and pleasant afternoon tea and evening dinner. Definitely make a reservation ahead of time so you don't have to wait for a table.

Title: A Sweet Ending at Mercado Little Spain

My wife and I ventured to Mercado Little Spain for the first time last Friday night and wound up our meal with a visit to their churro stand after dining at Mar. Despite the bustling scene around 8:15 PM, we decided to indulge in some churros for dessert.

The churros themselves were a delightful treat, striking the perfect balance between a crispy exterior and a soft, airy interior. Dipping them into the accompanying hot chocolate, which was rich and flavorous, made for a heavenly combination. It was so irresistible, in fact, that we devoured the dessert in merely a minute and a half!

In a comical admission of my sugar addiction, I couldn't bear to part with the chocolate and ended up taking it to go, sipping on it like a guilty pleasure.

In short, the churros at Mercado Little Spain were an absolute hit with us, and I would heartily recommend them to anyone with a sweet tooth looking to cap off their meal with something special.

Title: A Refreshing Stop for Drinks and Apps

My company and I stumbled upon this spot while in the area and decided to grab some drinks at the bar. The Watermelon Margarita I sipped on was delightfully flavorful, subtly strong, and gave a nice buzz towards the end. The Coconut Margarita also garnered praise. After the hefty margaritas, we shifted to Dos Equis, a good, lighter alternative.

Hunger nudged us towards appetizers; the Fried Shrimp and Flautas didn't disappoint. The shrimp were succulent, paired with a zesty dipping sauce that packed a punch. Meanwhile, the Flautas featured well-seasoned chicken, a satisfying crunch, and were tastefully topped with cheese, sour cream, and lettuce.

The bar area was appropriately spacious, boasting a well-stocked counter and ample seating. Service was attentive and efficient. Prices generally met expectations, though the large margaritas leaned towards the pricier side. Overall, a solid choice for a casual drinks and appetizer outing.

Nestled near the bustling streets of SOHO is a charming little gem called Noodlelove, a trendy noodle shop that's all the rage for those craving a casual yet contemporary dining experience. The counter-service setup encourages a create-your-own adventure in noodle crafting, while also offering an appetizing selection of pre-designed bowls.

On my inaugural visit, the Tingy Tangy Noodle bowl caught my eye—and taste buds. A delectable assembly of stir-fried udon noodles, baby bok choy, and white kimchi, each element was harmoniously tied together with a garlic sesame vinegar sauce that danced on the palate. The addition of ground chicken and a scrambled egg elevated the dish to pure comfort food bliss.

For the more adventurous foodie, Noodlelove presents the opportunity to play culinary matchmaker with a variety of noodles, proteins, and veggies. The freedom to mix and match ensures that even the pickiest eater can craft a bowl to their liking.

The ambiance of the restaurant deserves its own accolades. With a modern flair that doesn't sacrifice warmth, it's the small touches—like the vases of flowers on each table—that make the space inviting. The condiment and utensils kiosk stands out too, with an array of sauces to personalize your bowl even further, not to mention the complimentary sparkling water on tap.

In summary, Noodlelove is a delightful spot for noodle aficionados and novices alike, delivering on flavor and charm with every bowl served.

Title: A Disappointing Follow-Up to Luzzo

I ventured into this establishment with the taste of Luzzo's lunch still lingering, hopeful for an equally delightful experience. The chosen dish was the amatriciana—a spicy pizza adorned with sweet sausage. While the pizza base was satisfactory, the unexpected addition of scallions was a misstep, overpowering the dish with their pungent bite.

Unfortunately, any culinary promise was overshadowed by the service—or lack thereof. A baffling 30-minute void where our order was somehow unregistered left us hungry and expectant of a gesture of goodwill that never came. The eventual arrival of our check, devoid of any acknowledgement of the inconvenience, was the final straw.

Rating the pizza alone, I could extend a grace of three stars. However, the overall experience soured the meal to such an extent that I regretfully cannot endorse this venue. A return visit seems highly unlikely.

I dined at Oceans last night for a early Valentines Day dinner. Beautiful restaurant, friendly staff, & high tech toilets. I took away 1 star because the service was slow at some points and they never brought my leftovers which I requested to be put to go (it was 1/2 a fish & 1/2 of a side). Now to the food! Appetizers- after reading several reviews and hearing the waiters recommend it to nearby tables we were sold on the Rocketman roll! It was pretty good but idk how I feel about warm sushi, was not what I expected. We also tried the ceviche mixto which our waiter recommended which was good and different than your typical ceviche.Entree- we shared the whole branzino 1.9lbs. Was the perfect size for 2, served lightly grilled, it was cooked to perfection. Side- lobster Mac & cheese, a good shareable portion with chunks of lobster meat, I highly recommend. Too bad they didn't give me my left overs to go! Dessert- we went with the chocolate molten cake which was very rich and nothing special, I should have tried the 16 layer lemon cake They are opening an Italian section / separate restaurant next door. Looking forward to trying it. Not sure if I would return to Oceans but I would recommend it as a one off for a special occasion.

My plans got fuct with my original spot closed and other places too busy. Bleecker Street Pizza to the rescue! My little fam was able to secure a table within a few minutes while I ordered pizza at the counter. We tried a fresh and delicious plain pie while I had a slice of White which was one of the best I've ever had! Their dough was so soft and tasty and all the ingredients tasted fresh. Though they got pretty busy, service remained calm and friendly. Very dependable!!! Trust me- I'm from Jersey. :)

Not as good as I remember is the first thing that came to mind here. What was really weird was that it was empty for lunch. I don't know if it is the location or food but not a soul in there when a lot of other places were busy.  I went with the classic meatball with tomato sauce and 2 sides. First off the meatballs were dry and not the best. They tasted like they were overcooked or a day old. The kale side was more like creamed spinach than anything. The roasted carrots were ok at best.I had high hopes from coming here a couple years ago. Not sure why the standards fell but they did. Very disappointing.

Though a tad bit expensive for our tastes me and my coworkers did enjoy happy hour here. It does offer some unique features that you can't find in your typical bar.In terms of happy hour beers they have some Australian branded and imported beers to choose from. Classic Australian brands like Fouster's and Cooper's are here though none of it is draft. Me some of my friends got the "oil cans" which cost a bit more but are huge meaty cans of Fouster's beer.Additionally, they even offer a Moscow Mule menu! This was quite a surprise to me because some bars don't even offer mules and this place was offering 5-6 different types. None of them were in copper mugs but I did enjoy the variety of options. It at least gave me the opportunity to introduce the cocktail to my friends.They have some nice Australian menu items. The Kangaroo burger was quite fun to try out and I guess the closest it tasted like was beef. Me and my coworkers love to order fries with our beer and though we enjoyed the ones here we would of also enjoyed a bigger basket.Service was really great and uniquely they display both cricket and rugby games here. As a group with a lot of Indo-Americans it was enjoyable for us to watch the cricket games in-between other conversations we were having!Overall, Australian NYC is a nice place and I am sure plenty of people would love what this place has to offer. For our typical Friday nights however we will probably stick with our local and cheap Irish pub.

The Thai food here was rather mediocre, and we mostly ate here because we were looking for a good Thai option nearby. I think next time we will make the longer journey to some place else for better food. We went right at opening and the kitchen wasn't quite ready yet so be prepared for that possibility.

This place is quite affordable and offers a variety of Japanese food (from yakisoba to okonomiyaki), but the taste is more or less mediocre. You order at the front, and they make the entire thing for you, and then they call your number and you pick it out from the front.I had the okonomiyaki with pork, and it was just okay. The variety of toppings usually available was limited, and in our case they didn't put it on top, and just on the side. It tastes okay, if you kind of want to hit the spot for it, but it's not anything really all that good or special.

Tiny spot with a menu of a few select dishes. My friend and I shared the Ho foods classic red cooked (beef noodle soup with wide noodles) and Lu rou fan (pork belly). Everything was very tasty. Not sure I'd return again unless I was craving that exact soup, but it was good. 3.5 stars.

This place has a good happy hour deal and many seafood options! I came here for lunch during the weekdays and it was very quiet. I had a great time and I will revisit here sometime. I had Salted cod tater tots and Lump crab mac & cheese. I wasn't a big fan of mac & cheese because it was oily and heavy but I loved the cod tater tots!! Other foods on the menu sound tasty and I would try them for the next visit. The most popular drink is the painkiller but I didn't get it because I didn't feel like having sweet drinks on that day. I just had a sip and it was good. I got some prosecco instead. The owner served us and he seemed nice. He was the only person working at that time but he did his best to accommodate everybody. I recommend this place!

You can never go wrong with Mexican food. The service alone deserves this placs a lot of recognition. I came with my cousin after attending a comedy show at PIT (literally walking distance). We got there just in time for happy hour which I believe is 9-close M-F. Let me just start off by saying I came here starvingggg and left in a food coma. We started with passion fruit and mango frozen margaritas ($1 extra for flavor), which weren't too overly sweet. We ordered the queso fundido as an appetizer and tacos for entrees. I got the carne asada and my cousin got the surf and turf. The cheese was melted to perfection and not too filling making it a great appetizer. The tacos tasted amazing and were bursting with flavor. They didn't skimp on the ingredients either. Just a note - the surf and turf tacos are a little spicy but it's a nice kick. I definitely underestimated the 3 tacos and thought I was still gonna be hungry but I was stuffed after. Perfect meal!

You can't go wrong coming here--delicious, inexpensive food, friendly staff, and ample seating. I always enjoy a place that gives chips and salsa as a standard intro, like bread and butter/oil, and the chips and salsa here were awesome. Also, the crowd for lunch isn't bad at all; we got here around 12:15 and there was plenty of seating in the back. This is a good casual spot for lunch and dinner; I'll definitely be back. Harrison Street - At $14, this meal was perfect. The chicken enchilada was completely smothered in cheese, which definitely made the dish look especially appetizing. Under that cheese was tender chicken and a flavorful enchilada casing. The beans and rice were excellent accompaniments as well. Although I foolishly waited until nearly finishing to eat my guacamole taco, it was a solid item on its own. Ideally, I would have eaten this with the enchilada, taking advantage of the chicken and cheese, but that'll be for another time. Portion-wise, this is a fairly large dish, perfect for someone who likes big portions. Price: 5/5Quality: 5/5Quantity: 5/5Service: 4/5Atmosphere: 5/5

Delicious food and super affordable. Great for NYU-ers noticed some people dining with their laptops and doing some work at the same time without any hostility from the staff for taking up space. It wasn't too crowded around 730pm on a Sunday evening, I imagine it gets busier during the week. Service was super friendly but one of the waitresses had a hard time understanding me so ordering wasn't the easiest. We got the meat lovers spicy stew which was delicious minus the meatballs. They weren't bad just not my cup of tea. Also if you're not adventurous don't order this, there is tripe. Wish there was a bit more veggies in it. Some of the ingredients were a bit random like we got 3 little pieces of rice cake and 3 leaves of baby bok choy. I mean can you throw in a whole one? Also got soup dumplings and the dumpling skin was thick and doughy, not my fave, but the filling was on point! Can't wait to try the dry pot.

My experience at this upscale restaurant was exceptional from start to finish. Upon entering, the ambiance set high expectations for a fine dining experience. We were promptly seated at an ideal corner table, which was a charming touch.

The culinary journey began with the black truffle caviar deviled eggs, which were simply a taste revelation. Not to be outdone, the berry bubble cocktail provided both a visual spectacle and a burst of delightful flavors.

For the main course, the surf and turf did not disappoint, with perfectly cooked seafood and steak. The lobster mashed potatoes were a standout side, alongside the flavorful brisket sprouts. This restaurant has swiftly become my favorite destination for the best of land and sea.

Simple menu, but each item delicious and inexpensive. Grilled cheese and tomato soup, comfort food perfection. The roasted chicken perfectly cooked, excellent sauce, and served with creamy polenta. Large drink menu and full bar. My only wish would be they turn up the lights a bit as it was very dark to eat.

Title: A Refreshing Surprise at the Beer Garden

I recently visited a local beer garden and discovered that their menu holds a delightful surprise: a genuinely delicious and healthy salad option. The Kale salad, generously dotted with honeycrisp apples and toasted walnuts, exceeded expectations. I opted to add "crispy" tofu to my salad; while it wasn't the crunchy bite I anticipated, it was a well-prepared, flavorful addition that elevated the dish beyond the standard garden fare.

Although the tofu wasn't deep-fried or encased in a batter, it was a cut above the typical tofu offerings at similar establishments. I assumed the salad was vegan, as there was no cheese in sight and the dressing, a tangy delight that seemed to be made in-house, was wonderfully light and not the least bit creamy.

The portion size was perfect for an entree, leaving me satisfied but not overstuffed. This beer garden has mastered the art of combining the casual ambiance of a pub with the sophistication of a dish that is both nourishing and appetizing.

I think I had super high expectations when I made the choice of this place for dinner. I've had really really good dim sum before but this fell a little short of what I'm used to. I wish I could have given 3.5 stars but I couldn't. And they deserve more than a 3 star rating. I will say that they are not stingy with their liquor. I ordered a lychee martini and it was strong! That was a plus. Here's a review on a few things:-Seafood Shu Mai: 2/5 A little fishy but overall good-Shrimp & Chive Dumplings: 2/5 Lots of chives-Shrimp Dumplings: 3/5 Ok flavor to the shrimp-Chicken Juicy Bun: 4/5 Very juicy and good flavor-Shrimp Rolls: 5/5 Anything usually deep fried wins-Pan Fried Noodles: 4/5-Pineapple Cheese Wonton: 5/5 MUST TRY!I feel like the food could have used a little more flavor. But overall, it was not a terrible experience. If I had not been comparing it to other dim sum places I've visited in the past I'd probably rate this place higher.

Found this spot on Seamless a couple of weeks ago, when we were craving some Indian food for dinner. Never been to the actual location, but I went ahead and trusted the raving reviews the internet had left for the business -- they were def not wrong and delivered amazingly delicious food. We ordered:(2) Dum Pukht Gosht Biryani / Lamb Biryani ($15.95/each) -- DROOL! So glad we ordered a 2nd one to save for leftovers. Biryani is always a must-order at any Indian restaurant, and this one was one of the best I've had. They didn't skimp on the meat, and it was just as delicious (if not better) the next night.(2) Garlic Naan ($3.95/each) -- Literally same as above, minus the meat part. (1) Kashmiri Chicken Korma ($13.95) -- Pretty good, safe option. Nothing particularly special, but we still saved the leftover curry to cook into other stuff the next day. The beauty of yummy extra sauce!(1) Gobi Palak ($11.95) -- Blown away! I was so pleasantly surprised by this dish and would totally recommend, even for non-vegetarians/vegans. I wanted a veggie dish and this cauliflower/spinach concoction balanced out the rest of the meat/carb-heavy meal so perfectly. Also saved the sauce and added in my own cauliflower the next day, in attempts to recreate the dish with the leftovers. Obviously wasn't as great as theirs, so I'd def order this again.I love that they also included a complimentary papadum with sauces. Overall great quality food with affordable prices.

No stars for the tsukemen, but the regular tonkotsu is alright. These raving reviews are quite alarming, so here goes my two cents.I don't even know what to say about the tsukemen. Is it possible we had a bad batch, because the broth has been simmering for that long? Because the tsukemen ordered was unquestionably sour and vinegary. The sourness was incredibly off-putting and alarming. The fishiness was also insanely strong. (No, this is not my first tsukemen, so I know it's a fish based broth, but there's a difference between mild and severe, and this was off the charts.)Tsukemen ($18): the broth was served first, and a whole two minutes later, the noodles were served. I looked at the table next to us, and it was the same situation. Not sure what the restaurant is thinking - am I supposed to let my broth get even colder as I wait for the noodles? Am I supposed to drink the broth as if this isn't a tsukemen? (Excuse my sarcasm.) I also understand that Tabe Tomo wants to serve the broth NOT piping hot, but honestly, because of this, it tasted like a warm bowl of sour fish soup. Yes, I am also aware of the hot stone thanks to social media, but the fact is, we were here right at opening time, no one came to check in on us, and we definitely weren't able to flag someone down for a stone to reheat the broth. I do have to say though - the noodles for the tsukemen is much better than the noodles for the regular tonkotsu ramen. Additionally, while the egg that came with this was super beautiful, it tasted plastic to me - like it had been sitting under some artificial lights, or been wrapped in plastic film and I was eating that (you get the idea). Tonkotsu ramen ($18): upon being served my ramen, the first thing I noticed was the disgusting oil film on top of my broth, which I had to meticulously pick off. It's definitely a very fatty broth, but there's no depth to the flavor. All I taste is...fat. The noodles are also massive - think gigantic udon type of noodles, which I wasn't a fan of because it was just so hard to slurp and chew. Chashu is pretty decent (definitely one of the more tender chashus in the St Marks area!)Not a fan of the beansprouts that took up 1/3 depth of the bowl. Couldn't finish both the noodles (again, too big) or the broth (too fatty), and considering it was $18 a bowl, I definitely wasted my money, but my stomach was pretty upset with me over this already. Finally, service. It shouldn't make a difference, but we were seated next to the window, so it was actually the hostess who took our order (after seeing that we were frustrated by the lack of service and our waitress was busy taking orders alllllll the way down). I definitely noticed that other tables were getting attention except for the people sitting by the doorway. We were also in line for 5PM opening, so while it was starting to get busy, there was still no reason to not give us any attention! Due to the restaurant wanting to turn tables quickly, the minute I put down my chopsticks after I finished my tonkotsu ramen, the waitress showed up to ask if I was done. Thanks for rushing me . . .

Visited for brunch with friends on a busy Sunday and faced a typical 45-minute wait. The venue is charming and accommodates vegans well. Ordered the avocado toast – it was tasty though somewhat over-salted. Overall, a decent choice for brunch, albeit standard fare.

I had the pleasure of savoring the Chicken Pad Thai at a local restaurant tonight, and it completely exceeded my expectations! The dish was bursting with rich, authentic flavors that set it apart from other Thai eateries. Notably, the chicken was of remarkable quality, tender and flavorful in a way that suggests a higher standard of ingredients. Unlike typical shortcomings in lesser establishments—such as an overpowering fish sauce aroma or soggy noodles—this Pad Thai struck the perfect balance, both in taste and texture.

The portion size was generous enough to provide two satisfying meals, making it an excellent value. I left the restaurant already excited to return and explore more of their menu, especially the Pineapple Fried Rice. This dining experience was truly a five-star delight!

Title: Charming Bistrot Leo Delights, Service Falters

I stumbled upon Bistrot Leo when a craving for Steak Frites struck during NYC Restaurant Week. Alas, a rescheduled reservation meant missing out on that particular dish, but the brunch we experienced instead was exceptionally satisfying.

The ambiance of the bistro is delightfully French, from the authentic music to the selection of wines and the culinary artistry on display. Both my wife and I reveled in the cozy environment, shaking off the brisk outside chill with hot coffees in hand.

Our brunch choices did not disappoint. The Charcuterie plate was the standout - highlighted by a remarkable chicken liver pâté with organic butter that nearly stole the show. The Jamon ham with grain mustard perfectly complemented the freshly baked baguette, making for a delectable experience.

I indulged in a Croque Monsieur that was textbook perfection, served alongside a suitably dressed salad. My wife’s omelet was a revelation, with pillowy egg whites and a cheese blend that resulted in a creamy, luxurious texture. The accompanying potatoes boasted a delightful contrast of a crunchy exterior and a creamy interior.

Unfortunately, the impeccable food was not matched by the service. Towards the meal's end, our previously attentive waiter seemed to forget us, prioritizing other tasks over our needs. This lapse in service was particularly noticeable in an otherwise empty restaurant and slightly marred an otherwise lovely dining experience.

In conclusion, despite the hiccup with service, Bistrot Leo offers a slice of France that is undeniably enticing. I eagerly anticipate my next visit during French Restaurant Week for another attempt at the elusive Steak Frites. For those in search of a bit of French charm and flavorsome comfort food, Bistrot Leo is a solid choice. Au revoir, until next time!

This is my favorite breakfast stop in NYC partly because of its close location to Penn Station but mostly because I love the food and friendly service.  My recent visit was excellent as always.  The decor has a cozy but busy atmosphere.  The serving staff is always friendly and accommodating.  There are no reservations and your entire party must be present before they seat you.  For this visit, I chose the egg white omelet with veggies and wheat toast.  It was yummy and healthy but also filling.  I'm not normally a coffee drinker but decided to try the Dirty Chai as a latte.  This was a Chai latte with a shot of espresso.  WOW!  Definitely give this cafe a try if you are in NYC..

Title: A Breakfast to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

I recently had the pleasure of dining at an amazing breakfast spot where the food isn't just good; it's unbelievable. Each dish we tried was not only incredibly flavorful but also presented immaculately. The standout for me was the shrimp egg white frittata, which was both light and satisfying. On a whim, I inquired about getting just a single blueberry pancake, and the accommodating waitress made it happen without hesitation. That pancake, crowned with fresh cream, was an absolute delight - a must-try that's worth coming back for. The restaurant itself exudes friendliness, with an ambiance that's both great and peaceful, ideal for savoring each bite. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a top-notch breakfast experience.

This charming little restaurant is an ideal spot for a leisurely lunch with a close companion. Having visited numerous times with my boyfriend, we've consistently enjoyed meals that hit the mark every time – a solid 10/10. The ambiance, with its soothing classical music, complements the dining experience perfectly. Meals are well-rounded, always accompanied by a side of vegetables, providing a sense of a complete and balanced dish. The chicken avocado is a personal favorite, and the bulgogi never disappoints with its delicious flavors. For those with a penchant for heat, the jeyuk offers a satisfying spicy kick. Highly recommended for a delightful dining encounter.

Delicious delicious delicious! Everything here is so so good I can't wait to go back! This restaurant menu is created by Michelin star chef George Mendes and model Sanne Vloet which is really cool! It was definitely one of the reasons why I wanted to try this placeWhen you first walk in, you are greeted by the staff at the counter/cash register. You go in and you order your food. Then they give you a number and bring the food to you once it's readyMy friend and I ordered the quinoa paella with chicken, the smoothie bowl with oat milk, and the pastel del nata, plus a latte.The quinoa paella with chicken - it looked and sounded so simple but the taste was amazing and far from simple or basic!! The seasoning on the chicken was so good and really well done. Eat it with the arugula, the quinoa, the goat cheese and it's a party in your mouth! It's so good and the chicken is so tender - again very well cooked/grilled. Never would have though to eat goat cheese and chicken together! The smoothie bowl - absolutely a must if you like açaí bowls. I have never tasted an açaí bowl/smoothie bowl as good as this one. You pour the milk on it and you mix it up and eat it. I was amazed because it's so flavorful! You can taste the freshness of the fruits and the açaí at the bottom, but then there's also a taste of toasted oatmeal and nuts, and basil! Never thought basil in my açaí bowl would taste good but it was such a fresh flavorful addition to it! The pastel de nata - I loved both flavors (egg custard and blueberry). The pastry part was very flaky but also like a croissant and the custard part was so creamy and light! I would eat this every day if I could! Yummy yummy!! All in all, food here is really well done. Staff is friendly and the space is beautifully decorated. You should definitely come and try the food or the pastel de nata!

Title: A Flavorful Foray into Spanish Cuisine at Mercado Little Spain

I recently ventured into Mercado Little Spain, and I must say, I'm perplexed by any negative banter surrounding this gastronomic haven. Likening it to the famed Eataly is fair, though with a notable bent towards on-site dining over take-away groceries. Yes, the prices are on the higher side, and one might argue about the authenticity compared to dining in Spain itself. However, for those new to Spanish flavors, Mercado Little Spain is an excellent primer.

The culinary offerings are diverse and vibrant. From the crisp and savory cocas to the delectable tortillas de patatas and the hearty empanadas, there's a taste for every palate. Sharing the experience with friends is the way to go here—dividing and conquering the array of kiosks makes for an enjoyable and social tasting experience. For those seeking a more traditional restaurant vibe, there are dedicated bars and dining areas for a sit-down meal, although I didn't try these spots.

In summary, Mercado Little Spain serves up a delightful exploration of Spanish cuisine that complements the shopping experience at Hudson Yards. Whether you're a newcomer to Spanish fare or a seasoned tapas enthusiast, there's a slice of Spain waiting for you here.

Title: A Satisfying Lunch with Only a Minor Hiccup

I recently found myself returning to a favorite haunt, lured in by the memory of their exceptional frozen margaritas and crave-worthy vegetable nachos. Despite it being an early lunch at 1 pm, the place was bustling—a testament to its popularity.

As usual, I ordered the go-to veggie nachos, loaded with carrots, zucchini, and some other delightful greens whose names escape me, and on a whim, added chorizo for a twist. There was a mix-up when the dish arrived—it was all chorizo and no veggies. However, I hardly had time to be disappointed as our attentive server (whose name I missed) promptly addressed the oversight, ensuring my plate was corrected without delay.

My friend Christina enjoyed her chicken quesadilla, which she described as crunchy, cheesy, and garnished with a tasty combo of corn and pico de gallo, not to mention the delightful side of guac.

The frozen margaritas once again lived up to their reputation—sweet but not cloying, with just enough kick to feel indulgent without tipping into excess.

Service here remains a highlight; swift, seamless, and just present enough without the annoyance of being checked on incessantly.

Despite the small hiccup with my order, the quick fix and the quality of the food and drink ensured that my experience remained a positive one. I'll certainly be back for another round of those margaritas—always finding myself ordering seconds.

Title: A Hidden Gem in Harlem – Unmatched Thai Flavors

I recently visited a charming Thai eatery nestled in the heart of Harlem after hearing rave reviews from colleagues, and I can't wait to share my delightful experience. This quaint shop welcomes patrons with super cute decor, including gorgeous live plants adorning each table, setting a warm and inviting atmosphere.

Once inside, the tantalizing aroma from the kitchen stimulated my appetite to the point where choosing just one dish was a challenge. Thankfully, their fantastic lunch and happy hour specials offered a variety of options. I opted for the spring rolls, which were nothing short of excellent – crisp, flavorful, and a perfect introduction to their cuisine.

The freshness of the salads caught my eye, promising a return visit to explore more of their delicious offerings. Above all, the wait staff's friendliness enhanced the dining experience, ensuring that my next visit to this delightful spot is just around the corner. A must-visit for anyone craving authentic Thai food in a cozy environment.

We recently came here for restaurant week to try out this steakhouse. The menu had a great amount of options and also gave an option of a side to order with the standard appetizer, main and dessert. For the appetizer I got the Club A Bacon which was really good and served with a steak sauce. It was a thick cut bacon that was just the right amount of saltiness.For entree I had the filet mignon that was cooked to the requested cooked temperature. Not the best steak I've ever had, but good. I think if they had added herbs like rosemary it would enhance the flavor. I enjoyed the creamed spinach side which was plenty as a serving. For dessert I had the tiramisu which was a nice sweet note to end the meal. Service was really good overall. Our waiter made sure we had everything we needed. There was also some entertainment from the musicians on the main floor which was really nice.

I honestly think these are some of the best wings that I've had in NYC, and that's saying a lot. The wings are perfectly fried and there are plenty of flavors to choose from which would satisfy anyone's palate. I tried the inferno, garlic parmesan, lemon pepper, and sweet BBQ. All of them were delicious.It's a small, casual place with most people congregating around the bar area when I went (on a weekday at 6PM). My friend and I chose to sit at a table and we had to order from the bar area, which was not a problem. Everything is made fresh to order so there may be a short wait, but it's definitely worthwhile. I've never seen any specials on the wings, but they do have a few daily drinks specials to choose from.Next time, I definitely have to try the boneless wings!

We went on a Saturday around 4:30 pm.  It is a little store with a few steps to go down.   Very easily missed. There were 5-6 tables with 2-4 seats each.   You have to find your table and gathered the seats.  Share table between strangers is expected.   Old style window air conditioner unit does its job.   Staff yelling orders in Cantonese to kitchen and taking your orders with pen and paper.  It feels like home- the feeling of those HK style eatery Place my mom used to take me when I was a child.   Loves it at the first sight.  We got half a table first and cleaned the surface ourselves.   Customers kept coming but mostly ordering take out. We ordered: 3 orders of Curry fish ball. $1.25 ea order for 6 balls.   My kids went crazy with them.  Breakfast B ( all day breakfast) : spam Macaroni with soup, egg sandwich and drink $4.50.  No complain.  Beef chow fun with sauce $8.   Taste ok.  Lots of beef.  Soy sauce chow mein $2.50.  Yum! Cold HK milk tea $2.50.  Other reviewers raved about it. I found it not smooth enough.  My husband likes it though.  Iced honey with lemon $2.50.  Strongly recommend. Thick slices of lemon with just right the fresh lemon Ho eye taste.  Not too sweet.  Cold hollicks. $2.50   My son never had it.  Loved it.  Rich hollicks flavor.  They ran out of congee and fried rice noodle rollPrice is very reasonable.   Total was around $27 feeding family of 4.  No tips required.  You picked up the tray and clean up yourselves.  Owner said goodbye to us.  Definitely return.  I appreciate the feeling of home and honest business.

After an hour of indecision between a Chinese eatery and a Malaysian spot, we finally settled on Nyonya in Chinatown—and what a delightful choice it was! The rave reviews were spot-on: service was prompt, prices reasonable, and the portions more than satisfactory.

The Hainanese Chicken, although potentially an acquired taste, was a standout, particularly for its flavorful sauce. The Nasi Lemak was a revelation with its savory curry—an absolute must-try. The Ginger Duck, while unusual, left me ambivalent, but it was certainly worth the experience. And I cannot recommend the Curry Mee with Young Tau Foo enough; it was sheer deliciousness in a bowl. If you're in the area, Nyonya is a gem worth discovering.

This might be one of the best Italian restaurants I have ever been to. We came here on a blissfully empty Passover/Easter weekend. It's a compact little basement restaurant bursting with character. A big part of the kitchen is open so you can see a lot of the food prep happening. It's byob and we were well prepared with a bottle of wine. We ordered the bruschette plate which came with toasted bread and a selection of toppings. It was outstanding. It was a collection of things that I would never expect to go together, but were truly perfect. For the special I got the pesto shrimp special, which also was extraordinary. The pasta was perfectly cooked. The pesto sauce was very flavorful.I will 100% be back and would 10/10 recommend.

I absolutely loved the concept of this place and the quality of the food. Upon walking in they ask how many in your group and remind you they do not take cash. They then take you to a both where you order using a piece a paper which your circle your requests and then press a button for them to pick it up. A few mins later your hot delicious made to order ramen arrives and it is delicious. Best of all no words are spoken, no awkward stares from other customers, no awkward looks from servers if you request a refill of noodles. All an amazing experience especially if dinning solo. If you come with someone you can easily open up the middle dividers and enjoy your meal with your partner. Compared to all the other little tourist traps around Times Square this one seemed to be the most reasonable and best quality. The drinks are a little steep but it is Times Square so it makes sense. If I ever come back to NY this place will be a must on my bucket list.

Title: High Hopes Dashed at Bleecker Street Pizza

I ventured into the heart of New York with high expectations for a legendary New York slice at Bleecker Street Pizza, prompted by its rave reviews. Anticipating an extraordinary experience, I was met instead with a mixed bag of letdowns peppered with modest wins.

Upon my midday arrival, the place was eerily quiet, though it didn't take long for a lunch crowd to gather. A friendly staffer at the register warmly welcomed this first-timer from Alabama and recommended their signature pie, the Nonna Maria. This sizable slice, adorned with cheese, spinach, and chunks of tomato, was decent. However, the uneven sauce distribution and a crust a tad too crispy for my preference marred the experience.

Hoping to rebound, I opted for a BBQ chicken pizza next. While the chicken was nicely seasoned, the overall dryness and excessive crispiness again left me wanting. The scant drizzles of BBQ sauce were insufficient to moisten the arid landscape of this slice.

In retrospect, despite Bleecker Street's acclaim, my search for that quintessential New York pizza slice continues. Perhaps I'll steer towards the classics if our paths cross again. But for now, the quest remains unfulfilled.

During a bustling lunch hour, I had the pleasure of dining at a popular spot renowned for its dry pot, which interestingly, offered a dedicated queue at the back. The variety of vegetables was impressive, with unexpected delights like melon, okra, and sweet potato among my favorites. Meat options were reasonably varied, though not as extensive as the veggies.

I opted for the medium spice level in my dry pot, which, to my disappointment, was milder than anticipated. Next time, I'll trust my instincts and go for the highest spice level. Taste-wise, the dry pot was decent, but there's room for improvement: a more complex blend of spices could elevate the flavor profile.

The scallion pancake came with a delightful surprise of egg, although it lacked the green scallion in the egg, which would have perfected it. The spring roll was quite satisfying. With a menu beckoning for a more extensive exploration, I left wishing for a larger party to indulge in the variety this restaurant has to offer.

Elegant, cozy, trendy restaurant inside in a hotel in Koreatown. We had an amazing late dinner, we got reservations, everything was great. From the wine we ordered to the spice roasted carrot salad.Its a must in New York!Restaurante elegante, acogedor, trendy adentro de un hotel en Koreatown. Tuvimos una excelente cena tarde, hicimos reservas, todo fue espectacular. Desde el vino que pedimos hasta la "spice roasted carrot salad."Es un must en New York!

I like this place much better than Mala Project. They have a couple of locations in Flushing, but this is their first in Manhattan. If you choose the dry pot option, you go up and choose your ingredients. It is $11.99 a pound for meat and seafood, and for vegetables it's $10.99 for however much you can cram into the little basket. Because of their pricing, it's fairly easy to spend over $30 on a dry pot. I don't like the pricing of the vegetables since the basket is really small. They're probably making x10 the cost of the vegetables. I feel like I need to find a better way to optimize the vegetables better. Maybe find the vegetable with the best cost per area it takes up. It's still considerably cheaper than Mala Project where an equivalent bowl would be around $60.My favorite things to get are the pig intestines, cow stomach, and tripe. I think they over-bread and over-fry the fish fillet. Otherwise, that would also be one of my favorites. When you choose the ingredients, it may look like a lot, but it cooks down a lot. After choosing the ingredients, you choose a spicy level. They say you can choose level 1-5, but in my opinion they only have three spice levels. I've tried 2-5 to try to find the perfect level, but all of them are off. 2-3 are the same with no spiciness at all. 4 is just a little spicy, and 5 is extremely spicy. On the receipt it also says in Chinese small, medium, or big for the spice levels instead of numbers. I wish they had a spice level between 4 and 5. For me, 4 level isn't spicy enough, but 5 is too spicy for me to enjoy the flavor.This place is also very ideal for takeout since dry pot is so fast to make. If you want rice, you have to pay extra for it. I think it's nice that all the waiters and waitresses speak Chinese, which seems to be the opposite of Mala Project where it looks like the waiters and waitresses mostly speak English.

Title: Charming Eatery with Impressive Flavors
