My affinity for this restaurant has only grown stronger after two delightful visits. It strikes the perfect balance between quaintness and a lively atmosphere, making it ideal for either a relaxed gathering with friends or a charming date night. For those in a rush, the bar offers expedited service for drinks and quick bites.

The courteous wait staff provides prompt service, contributing to the seamless experience. My first visit during brunch introduced me to a scrumptious smoked salmon sandwich, while the Cucumber Cooler champagne pitcher was an absolute hit among us. Returning for dinner, the cheese steak spring rolls stood out with their unforgettable taste – small but mighty in flavor. The perfectly cooked bacon cheeseburger reaffirmed the kitchen's competence.

Notably, the menu caters to a variety of dietary preferences, with commendations from my friend for the veggie burger. This spot is a gem for those seeking a casual yet stylish environment with bold, satisfying dishes.

Lunch in Hell's Kitchen, Midtown West summons Thai.  This business was on my Yelp bookmark list since forever as I am finally making progress.  Living in New York City gives access to various cultures and ethnic cuisines without travelling the world.  As a foodie and a Yelper I am always seeking good food and good experiences at quality businesses despite travel restraints.  I am enamored in the full immersion of culture and ethnic foods.  Food is the international unspoken language that bridge the divide for people from all lands, cultures, languages, religions, economic, educational, and character differences because as humans we live to eat.  I believe food comforts the soul and heals the heart.  Keep writing!For Thai cuisine my default entree choice is Pad Kee Moa (aka Drunken noodles) as it is my ultimate favorite.  This business is immensely popular and received high praise resulting hustling extremely busy and heavily crowded for peak lunch hour at 1:22 pm.  I was able to attain a seat at the counter ledge (not a table).  For the lunch crowd get here early about fifteen minutes after opening.  This business is cafe size as it is small and I do not suggest large groups of four and greater.  The staff is friendly, attentive and accommodating with patrons' requests.  Chopsticks are available in addition to forks.  A female Asian neighbor patron who sat next to me leaned over to my plate two disruptive annoying times spurring inquiries for the illusion of a hard sell food critic / writer.  "What's that? What's this? What's in that drink? What kind of noodles is that?" Thai iced tea contains cold milk which neutralize and ease the pain of spicy food to wash a burning mouth.  Not water.  Thai cuisine is generally spicy but the heat index level varies and Pure Thai Cookhouse offers: mild, medium and spicy.  I have yet to see someone break into a sweat on one's face from spicy foods.  Woman, stop rudely disrupting my meal and ask the waiter as I am not a professional food critic/ writer! Let me enjoy my meal in peace, please woman!! A male wait staff firmly stated "there is only one Thai iced tea and it contains cold milk" to set her straight which is obvious this female Asian neighbor patron have NOT been exposed to various ethnic foods/ cultures.  Background music is boisterously loud and is inaudible with patrons' loud chatter.  This business is not ideal for dates as it is not conducive for conversation.  This business is located on 9th Avenue where rival neighboring Thai businesses are also located and the annual 9th Avenue International Food Festival occurs.  Business cards and takeout menus are available for grabs.  I suggest to dine-in as the food is fresh and immediate for consumption rather than wait twenty minutes travel arrival time to one's destination it becomes less exciting.  Price is very reasonable and will not break one's budget.Pad Kee Moa with shrimp $14Flat dry rice noodles, tomato, baby bok choy, snow pea, chili puree, Thai basil (aka Drunken noodles)Flavorful to the tee and I substituted chicken with shrimp, and the snow pea were fresh.  This entree ate my fill as it was solid and upholds substance.  Portion was good as there were no shortage for vegetables or flat rice noodles.  Substitutions are available with pork, chicken $13; beef, shrimp, calamari, mixed vegetable, tofu $14.  Yum! I always choose mild for the spicy index heat.  This entree is served in a bowl not a plate.  I can understand why / how the origins of high praise from previous Yelpers.  Pure Thai Cookhouse concocts substantial quality food.Thai iced tea $4.50Average but it was refreshing.  Thai iced tea is my only saving grace from spicy food.

3.5* My coworker made fun of me for choosing a happy hour place for meal pal It was Presidio Pesto Sandwich which has shredded chicken in pesto sauce, mozzarella, tomato on toasted bread. It looks like their menu has this under wraps but it's actually a sandwich. It came in a huge paper bag that could probably fit four or five of their boxes vertically. The box could probably stack three sandwiches vertically. It was hilarious showing this to my coworkers and they got excited for me. Based on pictures I think they give chips/fries when you eat this in person. I was hoping they'd give that too but nopeeeeYeah I was slightly disappointed to not get anything more than a sandwich. Sometimes I feel like MP meals are meant to be sad, but it's dingdingding surprising/add points if there's more than the bare minimum.  Or maybe I was too impressed by my MP meals from before that this slightly disappoints me. As for the actual sandwich. I'm glad it was still slightly warm by the time I ate it. The tomato was juicy which was good to give moisture. The pesto chicken wasn't dry as I was afraid it'd be and the pesto sauce wasn't too green. It might have a bit too much garlic because I had a bad breath after eating. The moz was still soft and slightly pully which meant it's still warm. The toasted bread was stiff without being too hard, like I noticed it but it didn't bother me. Overall (pass/fail) slightly higher than "pass" for this, but I can't put myself to say it's GOOD. It's a basic item but each ingredient can be upgraded further. I know I'll be back for happy hours, but will I necessarily come back for lunch/mealpal? Probably not?

First time here for dim sum and it's good. My biggest complaint was the xiao long bao. It was not good because the skin was thick and the top of the XLB was dry and hard. But besides that one dish all the other usual suspects of dim sum dishes are good. From the shaomai to the ha gao and the chicken feet are pretty good.I'm just surprised they didn't have cherng fun or the beef meat balls. I thought that was common dim sum dishes????

The dumplings here are indeed costlier than what you can get at your average Chinatown dumpling shop, but pricing for food is all arbitrary and no one can make a profit selling dumplings for 25 cents a pop in the  East Village, so I think the complaints about their prices are moot points. The rotating monthly specials are always so inventive and are what keep me perpetually keen on return visits. This time it was the French Onion Soup dumplings that caught my  attention and absolutely delighted my taste buds.February is a good month for a special like this because we're all just seeking something warm and comforting to get us through these winter blues. While it might be tempting to share a few options with friends, I think the move here is to get a plate to yourself so you can have the joy of biting into the al dente dumpling skin and letting the cheese and flavorful soup fill your mouth over and over again. Yes the experience is as sensual as it sounds.Douse your dumplings in their house made chili oil for extra oomph.

Title: Quick Service and Hit-or-Miss Dishes at Local Spot

My experience at this eatery was a mixed bag, though it leaned positively thanks to the prompt service. First off, the waiting setup is less than ideal; expect to stand awkwardly in the dining area, dodging diners and staff.

On to the food—do try the fried dumplings. They're sizable and satisfying, delivering on both taste and texture. The duck fried rice was another delightful surprise, a dish I hadn't encountered before but would gladly revisit. 

However, the restaurant stumbled with their tomato beef noodle. Something was amiss with the seasoning, and it simply didn't mesh well with my palate. On the upside, the ribs offered a generous portion that justified the price, and the scallops were bursting with flavor I wished was present in the noodle dish.

I'm willing to return to explore more of their menu, with a hopeful eye on the scallop and potential crab offerings. Despite the tomato beef noodle disappointment, the rest of the fare warrants a second visit.

This is my favorite restaurant and the best thai place in nyc! The workers are extremely friendly and always greet you with a smile. Food is made fresh and arrives quickly. They are halal certified and have a partial halal menu (please ask). Ive been here so many times. My favorites on the menu are - thai fried rice & basil fried rice (with chicken or shrimp for me) - crispy shrimp roll- thai iced tea - veggie dumplings Also check out their spicy udon, thai curries, and pad thai! Im not a fan of pad thai bc of the sweetness but Top Thai makes it perfect, its not too sweet and I really enjoyed it. Its usually packed and you have to wait outside but trust me it's worth it!

Title: A Hidden Gem in FiDi - Cozy and Delicious

I recently dined at this charming spot on a bustling Friday night and was thoroughly impressed with both the food and atmosphere. Kicking off the meal with their spicy beef noodle soup, I was pleased to find it had just the right level of heat. The wide, flat noodles were perfectly chewy, creating an ideal texture. While the beef noodle soup packed a punch, the braised pork belly noodle soup was milder yet still robust in flavor. Both soups boasted generous portions of meat, leaving me satisfyingly full.

The pork panfried dumplings were a standout – their crispy exterior gave way to a juicy filling that made each bite delightful. I learned that you could request any of their dumpling varieties to be panfried, so I'm already planning to try the lamb version on my next visit.

The mouthwatering chicken with its cold, chili oil-infused meat and crunchy peanuts provided a nice contrast to the hot soups. As for drinks, the hibiscus lemon tea was a revelation; its rich, sweet, and zesty notes were refreshing.

Service was nothing short of friendly, adding to the welcoming vibe of the place. With its affordable prices, diverse menu, and cute setting, this Chinese restaurant is definitely a gem in the Financial District. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a cozy dining experience with authentic flavor.

TLDR; worth it. Typical price point of an Italian restaurant in nyc, but actually really good and worth it.Love the calamari starter since it's not deep fried. This version is refreshing and has great citrus flavors with the crispy potato slivers. We also got the salciotta pizza and tagliatelle ragu pasta. The pizza was the winner here! THE SAUCE. The red sauce on it was just perfect. The ratio of cheese wasn't overwhelming and the thinness of the pizza made it seem like a lighter meal. The tagliatelle was good as well, just not the most memorable in my opinion.Overall it's a super cute spot in Greenwich/West Village for an intimate dinner.

My visit to Egg Shop was underwhelming and leaned more toward style than substance. Despite its charming minimalistic décor and quirky egg-themed ambiance, the execution fell short of expectations. The Saturday brunch rush meant a half-hour wait, which seemed reasonable given the restaurant's popularity.

I chose the aesthetically pleasing but ultimately unfulfilling "Fish Out of Water" dish, while my friend enjoyed the more satisfying "Pepper Boy" sandwich. It's advisable to opt for the heartier options to leave content.

The service was mediocre, likely strained by the busy hour, and it was a challenge getting the attention of the limited waitstaff for simple necessities like water refills.

While Egg Shop has the potential for a great dining experience for egg enthusiasts, it's best to manage expectations – go for the heavier meals and be prepared for service that might not keep up with the crowd.

Title: Worth the Wait for Exquisite Pad Thai

I visited this gem of a restaurant during dinner rush and encountered an hour-long wait, as they had stopped taking reservations by the time we called. However, the patience required proved to be a small price to pay for the experience that followed.

Upon entering, I was immediately taken by the stunning interior decor and the warm, inviting ambiance that enveloped the space. Opting for a seat by the bar to avoid a longer wait, I was greeted by incredibly friendly staff whose welcoming attitudes added a pleasant touch to the evening.

My meal of choice was the pad Thai, which not only tantalized my taste buds with its rich flavors but was also presented so beautifully it demanded a photo (attached). The portion was generous, ensuring that my appetite was more than satisfied.

In summary, the initial wait faded into insignificance against the backdrop of delicious food and delightful atmosphere. This establishment has certainly earned my return visit.

During my initial visit to this restaurant, I indulged in the kamayan feast—an engaging, albeit slightly pricey experience at over $60. The allure of their culinary craftsmanship drew me back for both brunch and dinner. The highlight of their menu, the garlic fried rice, is a sublime creation, paired wonderfully with their stellar seafood glass noodles and a notably satisfying chicken adobo. The meal reaches a delightful crescendo with their halo-halo dessert—a perfect conclusion to a memorable dining journey.

Tonkotsu Ramen spicy and non spicy version!! Every time I came to New York, I cannot not stop by Ippudo ramen!! The ramen is always satisfying, and the broth is very rich. Even the spicy sauce is very special!!! I have tried many different places and this by far is the best!!!

Affordable and tasty ramen in the ktown area. They have lunch specials M-F 11:30am to 2:30pm ($10 ramen) and then happy hour from M-F 3pm to 6pm (discounted drinks and appetizers). I've only had their signature ramen with medium spice and it was delicious. It came with a handful of noodles and half an egg that was marinated and nicely soft boiled. The ramen could've came with a little more veggies - there were only a couple pieces of bean sprouts and bok choy. The cha siew was cooked and marinated well, slightly sweet and not too much fat. The broth did not look spicy but it was popping with flavor. When you mix around the contents of the soup, it becomes slightly pink which comes from the spices. Overall, a great option for ramen around the area especially with their lunch special pricing.

The fried chicken legs and fried pork chops are good ($2.50 alone and $5.75 with preserved vegetables and noodle soup), but everyone else is just okay. The oyster pancake ($6.95) was too wet and not crispy enough, and the fried crispy shrimp ($5.50) were very artificial tasting. The salt and pepper chicken ($4.75) was decent.

Title: A Gem for the Conscious Foodie - Westbourne Review

If I had to sum up my recent dining experience at Westbourne in one word, it would simply be "Wowowowow." This all-day menu bursts with both sweet and savory delights catering to every conceivable gastronomic whim. Decision-making here is tough, but it's a struggle of the best kind—with dishes so tantalizing, you'll wish for a bigger appetite to try more.

Be warned, this spot's popularity does mean there's often a wait, as they don't take reservations. But patience is a virtue and your virtue will be rewarded. Westbourne's commitment to vegetarianism, zero/low waste, and community investment shines as brightly as the flavors on the plate. Every bite supports their collaboration with charitable programs like the Robin Hood Foundation and The Door.

Eating at Westbourne is a feel-good journey for both your taste buds and your values. I'm already planning my next visit—and the one after that. Join me, and let's indulge in food that's deliciously responsible!

We heard so much good things about Keen's that we made it a point to make reservations to eat there.  We were hoping to eat on the first floor so we could check out some of the rare collectible items they have there such as vintage grandfather clocks, old guns, the playbill that Abraham Lincoln was supposedly holding when he was shot.  If you look up at the ceiling, it's covered in 45,000 smoking pipes which some belonged to special members of Keen's pipe smoking club, like Babe Ruth, Teddy Roosevelt, Albert Einstein as well as many others.  So we were kind of bummed out that they stuck us up on the third floor (personally we didn't even know there was a third floor).  So when making your reservation try and see if you can request the 1st floor or at least the 2nd floor.  I think dressing nice helps as most of the people on the first floor was in suits and dresses.  Not saying we were dressed casual or anything as we were dressed nice but not that nice.Well anyway on to the food.  We received three rolls of bread and a vegetable dish with carrots, celery, pickle, and olives and ranch dressing came after we sat down.  We were eating some bread and munching like rabbits on the veggies while looking over menu.We got the Caesar salad ($15) and shared it.  It was kind of small, maybe more like for one person.  They didn't make it in front of us like they do at one of our favorite places back home.  I wish they did though as we would of told the person to not put too much anchovies as it had a dominant taste in the salad.  So if you don't care for that taste either, then I would recommend asking them to not put too much.Next came our Pan-Roasted Broccoli and Cauliflower ($14) and let me tell you, it was so tasty and this is coming from a person who doesn't care to eat veggies.  I could have eaten the whole thing myself.  Finally our Prime Porterhouse for two ($114) came out and it was done to perfection.  We ordered it medium rare and it was served just like we asked.  They had some finishing salt where we could dab our tender pieces of steak on.  Well both my wife and I love salt so in no time it was all gone.  We asked our waitress Nancy if we could get some more finishing salt and she came back with a little ramekin of it and we were so happy.  It made the steak taste even better.  We asked Nancy about what she recommended in a bottle of win.  We were leaning on a Malbec and low and behold she asked us a couple of questions and recommended two of them both from Argentina and she said to go with the cheaper one ($32).  I was thinking of the more expensive bottle but we were so happy we went with the bottle she said as it was really tasty that we took home what we couldn't finish to drink later on.Keen's now we know why you are one of the oldest eating establishments and are going strong.  Just next time, please don't seat us on the third floor.  lol

This restaurant is a great choice for group brunch gatherings. While the menu features classic brunch offerings, prices are slightly higher than average. However, the portion sizes are well-balanced; they leave you satisfyingly full without feeling overstuffed.

Title: Disappointing Experience at [Restaurant Name]

Unfortunately, my visit to [Restaurant Name] was underwhelming. My colleagues and I, working late, decided to order food for pickup as delivery wasn't an option. The order was simple, but upon returning to the office, we discovered that two of my three tacos were missing. When I called the restaurant, they were apologetic but refused to deliver the missing items just down the block. Although they issued a refund, it didn't address my hunger.

The one taco received was a salmon "taco" - more akin to a deconstructed sushi roll. While the flavor was satisfactory, the execution fell short with soggy seaweed, causing it to disintegrate after just a couple of bites. At $5 for this small, two-bite dish, it was certainly not worth the price or the hassle. 

In summary, poor service and an unsatisfying meal mean I won't be returning or recommending [Restaurant Name].

Title: A Love Letter to Udon at Raku

Raku has swiftly stolen my heart as the go-to destination for udon aficionados in New York. Their noodles are impeccably prepared, with a divine broth that perfectly complements a diverse array of top-notch toppings. Each dish we sampled, from the tender octopus to the crispy agedashi tofu, was nothing short of delectable. Be warned: the cozy space demands a reservation, lest you be prepared for a short wait – which, given the efficiency of service, is a minor inconvenience. My experience was so memorable that a return visit is guaranteed. Raku is an absolute must for any noodle lover in the city.

Recently revisited the charming Great Jones cafe nestled in the heart of Noho. This gem has bounced back with style, offering a menu that’s as considerate as it is enticing. The atmosphere is perfect for unwinding, featuring plush couches and trendy seating arrangements that invite you to linger.

I started my day with a flat white that lived up to its "killer" reputation, every sip smooth and robust. The exclusive escargot pastry, a delightful twist with chocolate and pistachio, was a testament to their dedication to unique, baked-on-site goods.

Whether you're looking for wholesome choices or something more decadent, this spot has you covered from breakfast through dinner. The owner's passion is evident in every detail. It’s a must-visit for foodies seeking quality in a relaxed setting.

Title: A Unique Culinary Experience at an Elite Black Badge Event

I recently attended an elite Black Badge event at a unique venue – a hotel room repurposed as a private dining space, reminiscent of the fresh concepts like Airbnb and Turo but with the novelty of a restaurant/bar setting. The ease of acquiring permits for such an innovative idea was enlightening, as the host shared.

The transformation within the four-seater space was remarkable; despite the obligatory floor layout posted on the door, the ambiance suggested a departure from the conventional hotel vibe. The decor was immersive, creating an alternate universe that perfectly complemented the dining experience.

Culinary delights were crafted by a remarkably skilled chef, with the tuna, barracuda, and Uni making for an unforgettable trifecta of flavors. The food was extraordinary in both presentation and taste. A sake sampler accompanied the meal, perfectly curated to enhance the flavors of the dishes; it was a worthwhile addition.

The event also served as a delightful reunion with fellow Yelpers, both veterans and newcomers. The warmth of the gathering and the exceptional dining made for a thoroughly enjoyable evening. I eagerly anticipate future events and the continued exploration of such inventive dining experiences.

Title: Stellar Service and Cozy Brunch at [Restaurant Name]

My wife and I recently visited [Restaurant Name] for their sociable brunch, and the experience was undoubtedly elevated by our server, Napoleon. His attentiveness and knowledge of the menu were remarkable, making him an asset to the restaurant and well-deserving of every tip he receives.

We opted for the eggs benedict on focaccia, which was a delight, featuring a lusciously creamy hollandaise sauce atop a perfectly poached egg. However, the French toast didn't quite hit the mark for us with its inclusion of nuts - a preference rather than a flaw. The pizza, while adequate, was nothing beyond the standard fare you'd find elsewhere in the city.

My five-star review is a testament to Napoleon's impeccable service, which truly made our visit worthwhile. The ambiance of the place was fantastic, though it might be beneficial for the management to take a page out of Napoleon's book and offer a smile occasionally.

Overall, [Restaurant Name] provides a decent meal with an excellent vibe, perfect for those in search of a value brunch and top-notch service.

As Chinese takeouts go, this is definitely one of the better ones. Fast, easy ordering and pretty decent food for a very low price point. $5.25 for well-cooked Beef Ho Fun (Chow Fun) is hard to find. The house special fried rice is just okay. It lacks flavor but maybe that's what all those mystery duck and soy sauce packets are for. I wouldn't know because I've never used them.Will come back again for the Ho Fun dishes. An amazing deal.

4.5/5! TDLR: come at 5-5:40pm or you'll be waiting for seats, skip the sashimi don and go for the tataki/carpaccio and the kimchi udon, and drinks are quite strong! All the food we had was REALLY good, and 10/10 would come back againMatcha Sparkling ($9): it's quite strong! Only gripe is that while I tasted all the other components (the vodka, sprite) I couldn't taste the matcha...I know it's only "infused" but stillHamachi tataki ($11): we LOVED this, and would come back for this alone. Lightly seared at the edges, the fish was so freaking buttery and fresh. The garnishes actually worked with the fish and wasn't just there for presentationSashimi don ($13): if I had to do this again, I would just get their salmon. I normally don't like thick pieces of salmon, but this one was soooo smooth and fatty that I wished the other sashimi pieces were salmon as well =( the rice underneath the fish is the reason why this place isn't a 5/5: rice was quite mushy and just not cooked well good that day. Kimchi cream udon ($12): soooo creamy! I tasted the kimchi with this, but I wished I tasted MORE of it. For a dish drenched in sauce, it's actually lighter than you would think, but so so tasty. If only there were more than two pieces of shrimp here!Kalbi ($15): another reason why I can't give full points - there seemed to be two different batches of short ribs! Some pieces were super duper tender, while others were a little rough and we spent some time savagely trying to eat itTempura set ($12): I'm biased because my taste buds tells me that no tempura I've had can compare to the ones I've had in Tokyo. With that said, my partner lovedddd this: he said the shrimp was very very bouncy, and the batter is light too. Both true - and I did enjoy the "soup" that came with this that we dipped the tempura into. That added a lot more flavorService was quite attentive! They cleared tables easily, and we had our first raw orders within minutes of ordering! It does get a bit loud in here, but definitely still a very nice date night spot to have some amazing food

Title: Unforgettable Grab-n-Go Delight

I'll keep this brief given the multitude of praise already heaped upon this gem, but the takeaway is simply this: For those in search of the ultimate hangover cure or a speedy meal that doesn't skimp on flavor, look no further. The roasted pork dish is a revelation – tender meat paired with the perfect balance of rice and steamed cabbage, all brought together with a tantalizing glaze. It offers unbeatable value for its price.

While I can't personally speak for the duck, my husband's enthusiastic, utensil-free devouring of it in a bustling park scene serves as testament enough to its deliciousness, despite some fiddly bones.

Dining al fresco among exercising elders provided a charming backdrop to our hearty feast. In short, a no-frills spot that wholeheartedly deserves its accolades.
Nevada is awesome! The vodka pizza is absolutely amazing!!!!! First time here loved it!

Title: A Culinary Delight Not to be Missed

My recent dining experience at this gem of a restaurant was nothing short of delightful. The menu boasted a variety of dishes that my companions and I eagerly sampled. Our selection included the vibrant Insalata de'Medici, the savory Linguini nere di mare, the tender Polpettine di vitella, and a stand-out fettucine special adorned with mushrooms and black truffle. Each dish was a testament to the kitchen's prowess.

Not to be overshadowed by the mains, the desserts – a heavenly strawberry sauce Panna Cotta and a rich, flourless chocolate cake – concluded our meal on a high note.

The service complemented the meal perfectly. Despite our late companion, the host graciously seated us, and our waiter's patience and attentiveness added warmth to our experience. The cozy and inviting atmosphere, highlighted by charming outdoor lighting, is suitable for any occasion, from a friendly gathering to a romantic rendezvous.

In summary, it would be a mistake not to visit this establishment. The food is impeccable, the service is top-notch, and the ambiance is just right. I wholeheartedly recommend it and eagerly anticipate my next visit.

A great place right by Bryant park, with very high ceiling and modern decor. The entire place is very airy. The service was excellent, the waiter Johan did an excellent job checking on us from time to time and explained the special.We are party of 2, I ordered the grilled octopus, itt was nice two big pieces nicely tender, paired with black rice and pumpkIn purée. Our table also ordered the regular burger, it was not very impressive, the patty could be a bit juicier but I was cooked a bit too well done, the truffle fries is amazing. The rest of the food in the menu is also looks amazing, each appertizer is around $20 and each main is around $30-40 so it's a bit pricy. They also have a good selection of deserts, which didn't get to try.

My recent visit to this charming eatery was a delightful indulgence for the occasional treat. It's not surprising that the prices have slightly increased over the years, but the expanded menu offers more variety. My son and I ambitiously ordered individual waffles, only to find that the generous portion and richness could easily have been shared between us. The sweetness was quite overwhelming, making this meal something to savor now and then. Overall, it's a lovely experience that's worth repeating—albeit sparingly, perhaps every few years.

Title: Hits the Spot with Room for Spice

Rating: ★★★½

Tucked in the bustling heart of the city, this eatery delivers solid Mexican fare that satisfies rather than dazzles. The guacamole served as a pleasant appetizer—adequately portioned with a texture balancing chunky and smooth, though a notch up on the spice scale would enhance its appeal.

Moving on to the main course, the carne asada tacos featured tender steak with harmonious ingredients, yet the size left something to be desired for those with heartier appetites. A common thread seemed to be the need for a bolder touch of heat to elevate the flavors.

Where the restaurant excels is in its prompt service, catering well to diners in a hurry. Be forewarned, the energetic ambiance often escalates to a cacophony, which may not appeal to everyone. Overall, it's a decent option for a quick Mexican meal that fills the void without too much fuss.

Title: Reliable Thai Eats for Dine-In or Takeout

My visits to this local Thai spot—once for dine-in and once for takeout—proved to be solid experiences. During my first dine-in trip, I had the Pad Thai, which was fairly standard but satisfying nonetheless. 

The second trip was for organizing an office event, and the restaurant's suggestion to order through Yelp made the process efficient. The food arrived early and without any mix-ups, a pleasant surprise for a group order. I particularly savored the drunken noodles on this occasion; they were rich in sauce and bursting with flavor. The curry dishes also received thumbs up from the team. However, it's worth noting the Pad Thai was a tad dry when ordered for delivery.

The restaurant itself is on the smaller side, offering limited seating but providing table service for a cozy dining experience. For those opting to carry out, I'd recommend online ordering for its convenience. Happy dining indeed!

The steak was too tough and the food overall was a bit too heavy for me. Not a great ambiance inside. Poor wine selection (only two house wines and they only had the white available that night, which was a cheap sweet wine). Unfortunately will not be returning.

Sweet Chick never disappoints, especially when it comes to their renowned chicken and waffles. During my latest visit, I indulged in the house cocktail, "Sweet Chick," which offered a refreshing kickstart with its blend of vodka, watermelon, lime, and a spicy rim. I ventured into new territory with the bbq lamb ribs accompanied by harissa yogurt, peach slaw, and a sprinkle of za'atar - a choice I didn't regret.

The mac and cheese at Sweet Chick is legendary; its creamy, cheesy richness is a must for regulars. It's simply non-negotiable. On a more experimental note, the "Purple Drank" gin cocktail with grape soda was a miss for me, reminiscent of cough syrup.

The star of the show, the bbq fried chicken paired with sweet corn waffles, lived up to its reputation, with the herb butter being the perfect complement. Dessert was a playful donut ice cream sandwich, elevated with vanilla ice cream and a unique Ritz cracker topping. I cleansed my palate with the "Unicorn Purp," a more enjoyable purple-hued beverage than my previous choice, mixing rum with lavender and blueberries.

All in all, Sweet Chick delivered a meal brimming with flavor and comfort, solidifying its status as a go-to spot for both classics and twists on Southern comfort food.

Title: Hearty Sandwiches with a Quick Service at Lenwich Deli

I've visited Lenwich Deli on a couple of occasions, each time sampling a different sandwich. My first encounter with the Lenwich sandwich left a favorable impression with its robust flavors and generous fillings. On my second visit, I tried the TC sandwich, which appeared to be a healthier option but was somewhat overshadowed by the dominant coleslaw flavor.

Both sandwiches were served on a 7-grain whole wheat bread that was pleasantly soft, although it tended to become soggy rather quickly, especially noticeable when dining in. Despite this, the portion sizes were satisfying.

Aside from the food, I appreciated the quick service at Lenwich Deli, although the ordering process can be a bit confusing for first-timers, with different stations for various food types. However, they simplify this by directing orders to the cashier towards closing time.

The one drawback is their early closing time at 4PM, which has been a small letdown on occasions when I've craved a late sandwich.

In summary, if you're in the mood for a tasty, hefty sandwich and efficient service, Lenwich Deli is pretty decent. Just remember to visit before they close, and perhaps experiment with different types of bread.
Delicious onion soup and escargot.  The lamb was perfectly cooked.  The chateau briand was good as well but on the small side.  Nice tatin to end.  Good wine list.

After numerous passes by the inviting Brooklyn Diner, my curiosity finally culminated in a take-out experience. At the tail end of a bustling weekday, around 8pm, the service was commendably swift—a perk for the hungry patron. A pro tip for fellow diners: orders for take-out are to be placed with the bartender, a quirk I rather enjoyed.

Our dinner for two comprised a heart-warming Chicken Soup at $11.50, the comfort-infusing Matzo Ball Soup priced at $13.50, and the much-talked-about Chicken Pot Pie, which tipped the scales at $25.95. Both soups resonated with rich, homey flavors that beckoned for an encore on future visits.

Regrettably, the Pot Pie didn't rise to its fame, delivering a performance that hardly justified its steep $26 price tag. Taste and value considered, the pie plateaued at mediocrity.

While the flavors mostly delighted, Brooklyn Diner's prices cast a shadow on the experience—$55 for three items seems exorbitant, even by New York standards. In summary, I'd label this a worthwhile diner, though not without its fiscal faults. A solid four stars, with room for financial finesse.

Took a trip to NY in January and we had so many placed bookmarked but once we stopped here we came 3 more times! The food and service was amazing, everything was so delicious, honestly out of this world !! From there Caesar salad , to their tie dye pizza, and pastas everything so delicious....oh and can't forget about there cocktails.!!!!! It was hard to just have one! Such fund memories that for my husband and i anniversary was in feb I painted him a card of there amazing famous tie dye pizza A place you must tryFood was amazing Service was great and on point Reasonable prices for the quality Miss you Rubirosa, much love from LA and stay safe

This review is for the Happy hour only ....Last days of summer & we happen to walk by nice warm day out & the "happy hour" "frozen sangria" sign caught our attention , we came in & sat at the bar asked about the happy hour & the frozen sangria .. not included go figured - strike one.. we still wanted to try it so we got it , it comes in a wine glass barely half full - strike two.. & finally that half glass was $15 dollars ughhhh strike three !! Now listen living in NYC u get used to overpaying for things which I understand but in no way shape or form is a half glass of anything worth $15 dollars the drink was more than some of the food on their menu WTF!! The drink itself was not terrible taste wise why I gave it the 2 stars, it's more of a Rose wine sangria than your typical red or white. Really not cool how they jack up the price on this drink, unacceptable.

Title: A Satisfying Feast at Au Cheval

My long-awaited visit to Au Cheval's New York outpost confirmed that their reputation for crafting legendary burgers is well-deserved, despite a slight hiccup with seating. Despite a reservation mix-up attributed to a bathroom repair and a confused host, the experience rebounded quickly.

To apologize for our wait, the staff presented us with a complimentary plate of bacon—a gesture that set a positive tone. Our lunch selection spotlighted their honey fried chicken, which I'd rank among the top three chicken dishes I've ever savored. It's an absolute must-try, boasting a harmonious blend of flavor and crunch.

The star of the meal was undoubtedly the burger. Topped with bacon and egg at my request, the burger's seasoning and perfect cook made it memorable. While there are other sandwich options, it might take great self-control to deviate from this delightful choice on future visits.

The fries, while overshadowed by the other heavy hitters, were enjoyable, particularly when smothered in a delicious mystery gravy.

The drink menu complemented the food excellently, offering a variety of beers that paired well with our meal.

In summary, Au Cheval lives up to its fame. It's the ideal spot for anyone looking to indulge in a supremely satisfying meal. I'll certainly be returning for another 5/5 burger experience.

Really great American brunch place! We were 10 minutes late and ended up running in, but Almond accommodated us without any problems. The biscuits were warm and the fruit puree/jam paired perfectly with it. The salad itself was very fresh, and I liked that it had mixed greens instead of iceberg lettuce. The artichokes 2 ways was a huge hit at our table, the combo of salty roasted chunks with tender shaved slivers is amazing.

Title: A Fresh, Plant-Based Addition to NYC - Veggie Grill Review

Rating: ★★★★☆

Veggie Grill has made a vibrant debut on 23rd Street, bringing its popular vegan fare to the heart of NYC just in time for a spooky Friday the 13th official opening. Having had the privilege to taste their offerings during their soft opening, I'm convinced that this 100% plant-based menu is a siren call not just for vegans and vegetarians but for anyone seeking a healthier bite—even a self-proclaimed carnivore like myself.

Their bright, clean interior is a feast for the eyes, with a modern touch of painted brick walls and blond wood furnishings. If you're on-the-go, the self-service kiosks and a dedicated pick-up area for online orders amplify convenience.

The menu is a visual and gastronomic delight, filled with an array of colorful salads, vegan buffalo wings, plant-based chicken sandwiches, beyond burgers, tacos, and tempting desserts. The Lux Burger, paired with a refreshing ginger hibiscus tea, did not disappoint. Dressed with a white truffle cheese sauce, roasted mushrooms, arugula, and a zesty sriracha ketchup, the burger was a flavor-packed testament to how delicious vegan options can be, even if the accompanying fries were just passable.

Veggie Grill stands as a fast-casual gem for the health-conscious and the flavor-seekers alike, registering high on taste and innovation. Prepare to be pleasantly surprised.

Title: Noodle Nirvana with a Twist of Disappointment

I am an absolute devotee of this ramen haven! Their customizable firmness and the freedom to tailor your toppings transforms each visit into a personal flavor fiesta. The broth? Divine. Each sip is like a fiery dance of spices that warms the soul.

However, let's talk chashu. It desperately needs a tender touch. The current iteration is a letdown – too tough, too dry. It's a misstep in an otherwise flawless symphony of tastes.

And then there's the jabako bowl debacle. While innovation is appreciated, this one's a miss. The reduced broth ratio hampers the slurp-worthy experience and plays havoc with my chopstick mastery. Despite claims of equal broth volume, my extra noodle request met a brothless end.

In short, ramen lovers, your taste buds will thank you here, but steer clear of the jabako and keep your fingers crossed for improved chashu.

My recent dining experience at CajunSea was a delightful nod to my expectations. My boyfriend and I indulged in a shared feast, starting with their Cajun fries, which were a personal highlight with their perfect blend of spices. The Lobster Mac and Cheese was a creamy, cheesy delight, while the pound of king crab legs was a sumptuous treat that left us more than satisfied, despite our waiter's suggestion to order more. Every dish was flavorful and well-prepared. Additionally, the convenience of booking through Yelp Reservations was a plus. CajunSea definitely nailed the flavors of the South, and I would happily return for another round of their savory dishes.

Sometimes all you need is a good friend and some delicious indian food(mostly the latter). Came here to @gupshupnyc for brunch on Sunday. My friend and I got dal makhani, Chole poori and garlic naan. First of all the dal makhani here never dissapoints, it's so rich and creamy in flavor. My friend tried the dal makhani for the first time and loved it. The chole poori was comfort food and reminded me of home. Garlic naan is also delicious here and we ended up ordering extra. For drinks I got "Hot like Kohli" , first of all I love the innovative name and the cocktail was a spicy tequila mix which I enjoyed. My friend got the "Ayurvedic Jackass" which was a fun twist to a classic Moscow Mule. Overall this spot never disappoints and I can't wait to be back here again :)

Bad service. Decent meats but the meats are better at almost all the Korean bbq places in the city so might as well just go there. Long waits so definitely need a reservation. Book on opentable in advance - the times book up quickly. The only time they had available when I went to book was a 9:45pm. Do not take that time. They close at 10 and that's around when last call is so you have to order right away and then later if you decide you're still hungry and want to order more, too bad, so sad. They didn't even have our table ready until 9:55 so we were told to look at menus and decide what we wanted while we were standing and waiting in the front so we could order as soon as we sat down. When they brought the raw food out, we put it on the grill to start cooking and someone came over to say "how's the food? Great, right? Ok thanks!" And ran off. We obviously hadn't even started eating to be able to answer him.As for the food, the pork belly and the short ribs were probably my favorites. The miso salmon and cow tongue weren't bad either. We spent about $80 for two people (just food, no drinks) and both left feeling hungry. Probably won't be returning.

During a cloudy Wednesday mid-morning, I encountered a refreshingly orderly scene outside a local eatery famed for its rice rolls – a new craze among millennials and tourists alike. Although a queue of 10 awaited entry, the atmosphere was calm, with patrons patiently anticipating their turn.

The staff were a delightful representation of diversity, interacting in various dialects including Mandarin, Cantonese, and English, all while maintaining a cordial demeanor.

The menu's highlight, customizable steamed rice rolls, offered an intriguing option of incorporating egg into the batter, resulting in a unique, eggy texture. While it didn't revolutionize my palate, it proved to be a delightful culinary experience worth sampling.

Do not come here for brunch around 4pm.  Not only were they slow with taking our orders but we literally waited and hour for our food.  We were on the verge of cancelling but they said 5 more minutes then the food finally arrived. Too bad cause the food was actually good but the experience was terrible.
A little bit overpriced in my opinion for what you get, but very well made. The indoor decor is also very beautiful.

I never realized how enormous this restaurant is. Regardless of how many tables they have, definitely make a reservation, because it's nonstop, especially during lunchtime. I came here with someone who's a regular, so we were taken to a table in the back by the wall, where he always sits, so we could talk more easily. There's both small and large parties, and it's a professional setting with mostly suits. I got the monkfish, and it was pretty good! The fish portion size was so small, but it was cooked very well and it was so fresh and tasty. It came with spaghetti squash and polenta, so I was filled up. However, I'm glad I didn't pay for lunch, because I would've felt ripped off if I did! It's expensive here - my dish plus the chicken Caesar salad was $70, so come if you're okay with spending dough. I feel like the dishes are hit-or-miss here, so maybe there are others that are more so worth it. Overall, they are pretty standard dishes but made with quality ingredients, so it's not going to blow your mind, but it'll be reliable. Service was great, from the hostess to our waitress to the busboy. Come here more so for the elite atmosphere and the professional staff.

7% cash back !This place reminds me a lot of szechuan mountain house. The menu is also extensive and the food was equally good.Ordered the fish fillet soup with pickled green collard, mapo tofu with beef, and the beef tendon. Everything was pretty tasty. For 2 people this was more than enough food...have leftovers to take home in the end.The mapo tofu and beef tendon have peppercorn in it but luckily we had 1 dish at least, the fish fillet soup that didnt have peppercorn in it. It seemed that a bunch of tables ordered the grill fish that comes in a large tray. Maybe next time I'll try that here? Nevertheless was satisfied with my meal.

It was a warm Saturday afternoon and my husband and I were looking for a place to have dinner by the water. After some search I found  this gem. I purchased the tix through their site and use the code from Yelp to save $5 per tix which was amazing. Usually you have to pay $10 as a cover which it isn't horrible. You pay the cover to get on the boat which is sort of like a bar/restaurant that sails every hour hand half for 40 mins. Your tix is for the whole day so you can spend as much or little time there are you want. When we got on the boat we decided to check upstairs deck to see if we could find a place to seat. We were lucky enough to find two free seats. A server welcomed us and gave us some menus. I decided to have the original lobster roll and my husband got the bacon lobster roll. Also we ordered the lobster fried Mac n cheese balls to share. I have to say both rolls were delicious and very generous with the amount of lobster in each of them. Totally worth every penny. However I was a bit disappointed with the Mac n cheese balls. They were very tasty but didn't have a lot of lobster so I don't think they are worth $16. I can't remember the name of my drink but it was really good and plenty of alcohol. While we were eating we sailed towards uptown for 40 mins. Then you come back and dock for another 40 mins and then it sails again and so on. This is such a cool concept and I will for sure be coming back very soon.

I love Otto's tacos! They have a new lunch deal from 2-5PM where you can get two tacos and a soft drink for $5 on all weekdays!! That's a great deal, especially in the West Village where the typical lunch is $9-10. Yes, the tacos are small, but they're loaded with meat, salsa verde, cilantro, and onions. The au jus from the meats in the taco makes every bite mouth wateringly delicious. I've had the chicken, carnitas, and the brussel sprout ones and loved them all. An added bonus is that there is both indoor and outdoor seating. Service is friendly and prompt, leaving you more time to enjoy your lunch break.

Title: A Charming Evening at a Quaint Spot

My partner and I chose this establishment for date night, and whilst the food was pleasing, it lacked that wow factor to be truly memorable. Nonetheless, the warmth and attentiveness of the staff more than compensated, creating a delightful dining experience. The ambiance is another reason to swing by; it's inviting and enhances the overall charm of the place. The concept and music selection hit just the right note, adding to the enjoyment of our evening. Considering everything, I'm happy to round up and give this eatery a well-earned 4 stars. It's definitely worth visiting, especially if you're looking to spend a lovely evening with that special someone.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at Kyma

Despite initial reservations due to mixed reviews, my venture into Kyma for a Friday lunch was a revelation in fine dining. Opting for the price-fixe weekday menu was a wise choice: at $29 for an appetizer and main dish (an extra $5 adds dessert), the value was exceptional.

The ambiance struck immediately – a blend of class and comfort, with warm lighting, white-washed walls adorned with pottery, and an impressive display of fresh fish. Service started on a high note with complimentary pita, fragrantly drizzled with olive oil and rosemary, to which we couldn't resist a second serving.

The octopus appetizer was a star – unexpectedly large and impeccably tender, while the grilled calamari shared from my friend's plate offered a delightful smokiness, a perfect preamble to our mains. Although there's an option for fried calamari, the grilled version and its accompanying tangy tomato sauce were spot on.

Then came the Branzino, a triumph in both freshness and taste with perfect crispy skin, and the oven-roasted salmon, which was well-paired with crispy leeks though the accompanying spanakorizo was noted to be a tad salty.

Service was attentive, keeping our water glasses perpetually full, the only hiccup being the wait for our mains which seemed longer than necessary given the less-crowded dining room.

In summary, Kyma exceeded expectations, delivering generous portions, high-quality seafood, and an atmosphere that elevated the entire experience. A gem worth considering, especially with their weekday menu deal.

Calling all Primates, Neanderthal's, and Homo Sapiens. Let's get one thing straight..This ain't the the jungle gym you used to get down in back in grade school. Nor is it the Monkey Bar(s) you used to try and impress all those 4th grade hunnies back in the day...You know who you are. And let me tell you, this is the ONLY bar-restaurant in NYC where Monkeying Around WILL NOT make the bar tender Go Bananas. ----------------------------------------------------Ahhhh The Monkey Bar! What a cool place. I came her for a business meeting some years back and I will always remember my experience. It was my second time being in New York City and I still remember how nervous I was to be meeting with the 'big boss' for dinner. Walking through the doors, I felt like I was stepping back in time to what I would describe as "Old Hollywood". It was elegant yet, relaxed and has a charm to it that only Manhattan can pull off. We shared the Steak Tartare as our appetizer and I will never forget how amazed I was by how much I enjoyed it.  Years later, I found myself in Paris ordering the beef tartare where I used the Monkey Bars tartare as my scale of reference and let me tell you, Monkey Bar is the King of the Jungle. The rest of the meal was top notch; the service, the drinks, the ambiance and the overall experience was everything you would expect in a high end spot that's been serving New York's finest since 1936. So the next time you feel like dressing up in your best monkey suit, make your way to the ol' Monkey Bar where you will fit in like a chimp, I mean a champ!

Percy's Pizza is a hidden gem for anyone craving an excellent slice without breaking the bank. At just $1 per slice, I was blown away by the quality and taste – it's easily some of the best budget-friendly pizza out there. It's worth the extra travel to enjoy not just the pizza, but also the warm and welcoming staff that make the experience even more delightful. Highly recommended!

Title: A Gastronomic Delight Wrapped in a Chic Vibe

From the moment you step into this eatery, you're greeted by a stylish ambiance that sets the tone for an exceptional dining experience. As a first-timer, I embraced the culinary journey, indulging in a vast spread that included appetizers, mains, and desserts. Each dish that graced our table was nothing short of phenomenal, paired perfectly with expertly crafted drinks that hit just the right note.

Despite the challenge of an ever-tempting array of dishes, each flavorful bite made it impossible to stop, a testament to the kitchen’s prowess. The restaurant's design, boasting two levels complete with seating and well-appointed bars, adds to its allure, making it an ideal spot for both casual dining and private events.

Service here deserves a shout-out as well – the servers are attentive, ensuring a seamless experience. This place not only guarantees a return visit but also motivates one to hit the gym to make room for the next indulgent affair. Highly recommended!

My favorite place for soup dumplings!!! The wonton soup was very flavorful and the wontons were delicious. You can tell that the noodles and wrappings are handmade, fresh, and yummy!! My family and friends had other dishes which they say are all good. We will definitely be back again.

Restaurant week is a great time to give places like this a try, my friend & I decided to stop by & check it out. We had our rsvp came in & had no issues being seated, once seated we asked our waiter for a suggestion with some wine, we went with a bottle of white not bad a Chardonnay I believe? it was good. Limited menu for restaurant week appetizers we tried the Burrata & tomato, very good the burrata practically melts in your mouth & the Pasta small dish, good pasta nice taste. Main dishes we had the Filet Mignon , cooked well very good great flavor to the meat & the Chicken w some veggies & pasta, oven baked chicken nice taste. on the Dessert we went with the Baked alaska seems to be a favorite here can see why it was delicious & the Cheesecake good cheesecake. Great looking restaurant u feel like u are stepping back in time, old world type decor, service was good to begin with seems like they forgot about us after not fun to feel rushed through your meal & then have to wait forever to get the check, price wise good for restaurant week definitely on the high side otherwise, we enjoyed our meal it was worth giving it a try.

This small pizza place right around the corner from our hotel had a large selection of pizza flavors sold by the slice and fountain drinks. They serve by the slice, the entire pie, as well as specials with drinks and a few slices or options for the other pizzas inside. When we ordered they placed it back in the pizza oven for a few minutes to heat it and make it crispy. I chose the white pizza which was just cheese but had several ricotta pockets on top. My friend chose the buffalo pizza with cheese. Both were fast and delicious and crispy and warm. Small , no nonsense inside without a ton of seating but great flavor and great pizza quick and in a hurry!  The best we had in NYC!

I came here after going to gym around 8:30pm and this place really hit the spot! I'm a huge Dos Toros and Chipotle fan, but Oxido is now my #1 Mexican bowl place in the city. I absolutely LOVED it! The containers were full of food even at that time, and the employees are super nice and pile your bowl up. I got half garlic steak and half chicken poblano bowl. One criticism is that the garlic steak doesn't really have much flavor, and definitely no garlic flavor, but everything else was amazing so I won't take off any points.I really enjoyed the fact that you could add Mexican squash to your bowls along with different types of sauces like Salsa Verde and the crushed up tortilla chips! My bowl was huge and everything was tasty, not too salty where I need my water all night, and it felt healthy.

Got two slices of pie and a Diet Coke- Sicilian and cheese for $9. The pizza was good the vibe is even better. It's a cross between Louisiana and Italy. I love it here. It's a chill casual vibe. There's a table of tweens playing cards like they are in their living room and nobody is bothered. A true rarity in the city.

We came here for dinner on a Friday night. I made a reservation at the bar.  We loved everything and the waitress was great.  We had the sweet potato sourdough, gem lettuce, and the chicken.  We shared everything which filling for both of us.  We did not get any drinks.  I thought it was all well priced and nice portion sizes. The restaurant is also very beautiful and they have a flower theme.  Every menu item has some sort of flower in it. The restaurant also sells flowers in the front and they occasionally have classes.

Tucked away on the shabby-chic Corlandt Alley lies a bustling culinary gem that's worth navigating through its deceiving exterior. A word to the wise: reservations are a must, and with the lunch menu mirroring dinner, you might have an easier time snagging a mid-day spot. I found myself amidst the Sunday 3pm crowd, where the vibe was electric and the tables were in a state of constant flux.

For those with a penchant for lighter fare, this might not be your haven, as the menu leans towards the indulgent. After indulging in the cuisine here, a bump in my cholesterol meds seemed necessary. That said, their Burger, especially topped with bacon and a fried egg, is the standout wonder — a flavorful foray into why this dish reigns supreme.

Don't wrap up your experience without delving into one of their unique coffee concoctions, a delightful capstone to the meal. While prices are on the steeper side, they parallel the quality and experience, making it a culinary indulgence that's truly justified.

Visited the restaurant one more time and tried the brunch feast. Good as usual, liked the tapas - potatoe, lamb, and salad. The paella is huge, maybe will order the alternatives next time. The churro sundae is great! Always romantic and tasty! Love it!1 star is deducted because the food is a little bit salty and pricey.

a very cute bakery! they have lots of sweet and savory choices. my personal favourite was the strawberry and cream cake. it was light and fluffy but so tasty without being soggy. they also have a variety of self serve coffees which you can refill. the grab and go section was also very fresh and had lots of healthy options including chia seed pudding, quinoa salad, parfaits and fruit cups
We visited in December and this place was great!  Food was hot & very flavorful. Unique experience, a little bit expensive but was worth it.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Delights at Yum in My Tum

Entering Yum in My Tum, I was greeted with the promise of a quintessential pizza experience. The pepperoni pie didn’t disappoint - it was a deliciously greasy, cheesy delight, hitting all the right notes for comfort food enthusiasts. While I wasn’t personally taken with the arugula and prosciutto pizza – the prosciutto came in overly generous, thick slices that I found rather overwhelming – it certainly had its fans among the crowd. 

The crust on every pizza was perfect, striking a delectable balance between thick and thin. Salads are often an afterthought at pizza joints, but here they shine: from the olive-laden Greek salad to the bold Caesar with decadent Parmesan slabs, and not forgetting the house salad with its punchy sun-dried tomatoes.

However, it wasn't all smooth sailing. The restaurant could barely handle our work event, which led to some seating scrambles, and the staff's inability to accommodate us was noticeable. Additionally, their selection of house wines was underwhelming at best.

In summary, if you're seeking a slice of pizza heaven with a side of fresh salad and can navigate a crowded space with sometimes indifferent management, Yum in My Tum is worth the visit – just maybe skip the wine.

Title: Quick Bite at a New Burger Joint

I recently ventured out to a new burger spot through MealPal, arriving just before the lunch rush to find a quiet atmosphere with only a couple of occupied booths. Service was swift; my order, The Standard, was ready for pickup without delay.

This classic beef burger came with American cheese, dill pickles, caramelized onions, and a special sauce, all neatly sandwiched in a brioche bun. While the accompaniments were spot on, the beef patty was unfortunately a tad dry for my liking. However, the environmentally friendly paper wrapping was a thoughtful touch.

Having dined here previously without issue, I'll chalk up the dryness to an off-day. I encourage fellow burger aficionados to give it a try and form their own opinion.

Being the only Laotian restaurant, this place is unique. Prices were generally higher. I went on a Saturday right round 5:30, when they open for dinner. I was the only customer at that time. As more people started coming in, the place got very loud. Complimentary sticky rice was good. The hot sauce, which came with it was really hot. Creekstone farms sesame beef jerky was a flavorful version of jerky. If you like jerky, you should try it. Sweet chili bell and evans chicken tasted more or less like general tso's chicken. Unlike general tso's, this had a lot of sauce, that it can bind the entire plate of rice.

I tried the steamed pot stickers, chicken mango dish. The pot stickers was good. The chicken mango entree didn't come with rice but was good. I checked in on yelp and got a free ice tea which was ok. CASH ONLY so bring cash. Service was good. Will be back to try more dishes.

We were told there would be a 45-minute wait at Katz's, so we left. As we were walking down the street we saw this place and saw what great reviews it had. It deserves all the reviews. The vegetable dumpling was the best I've ever had. It tasted so fresh. We had udon noodle soup, which my husband said was the best he's ever had. And they did a Yelp incentive for checking in, which was a real nice surprise.

Decided to try this place fort bday dinner with some friends. It wasn't crowded which I really like. The restaurant is a few streets from Korea town and maybe that's why it wasn't too crowded. The staff was friendly and we had a fast service. The prices were reasonable as well. We tried the bbq and it was good! I got a coupon  when I checked in through yelp and they honored it so I got a free drink and it was delicious. I recommend this place if you are looking for a less crowded place and reasonable prices.

Xu's Public House is a upscale Chinese restaurant in Union Square, New York. The service is superb, the ambience is elegant and the food is very good.K and I enjoyed a lovely Mid Autumn's Festival dinner here. The restaurant was filled with people but the waiters, waitresses and hostess handled everything with grace and care. The best dish was the King Crab noodles with Uni. Best tea was the Chinese Almond Pearl Barley. We shared the following.Morchella Esculenta Soup Dumpling- this was a gigantic soup dumpling with savory mushroom meaty soup with lots of morels inside. I loved the metal straws that came in a tiny glass jar. It was so fun to share this dish! After the soup was enjoyed, we cut up the soup dumpling to enjoy the morels. The skin was surprisingly thin and delicate for such a large dumpling. I've had much thicker skinned soup dumplings in Shanghai. Shanghai Truffle Wontons- these were nice and crispy on the bottom. They smelled so good and were moist inside. It was slightly better than your usual wontons.The King Crab Cold Noodles with Uni and caviar- this was the best dish of the night! I loved the fresh caviar. We mixed it so the caviar, cold cucumber, and king crab coated each noodle. The noodles were al dente and the uni offered this oceanic taste to the dish. K loved it too! We fought over the last bite. Sautéed Tier Prawn and Lobster Risotto- The lobster tail was cut up already. The tiger prawns were springy and well cooked. This was more of a fried rice than a risotto. It was good.Flaming Ribeye- this was very entertaining. The rib eye was cut up and well done. I loved the stones that were lit on fire. The meat was flavorful and cooked completely. For dessert: egg yolk sesame ball. I liked this. It was the combination of two great dim sums: salted egg yolk bun and fried sesame ball. Tea: Chinese Almond Pearl Barley tea. This was slightly sweet, warm and clear clean taste. I loved it! Reminded me of my mom's barley soups.Lung Ching Green Tea- this was ok. Tastes like the typical green tea. I would definitely return for the Barley tea, King Crab Cold Noodles and Egg Yolk Sesame Ball! I would return for their dim sum and desserts!

Title: A Slice of Naples in NY: Sorbillo Delivers

After an unforgettable experience at Sorbillo's in Naples, I approached their New York location with a mix of excitement and skepticism, wondering if the Atlantic divide would have stolen some of the magic from their pizzas. To my delight, the New York Sorbillo lived up to its Neapolitan roots.

The pizza was a mirror image of its Italian counterpart – the char, the chew, and the tangy freshness of the sauce were all there, creating a mouthwatering symphony of flavors. The crust was exceptionally thin yet robust enough to support the generous, quality toppings without a hint of sogginess.

The highlight of my visit was the margherita di buffala. Its simplicity shone, allowing the high-quality ingredients to take center stage, each bite as sumptuous as the one before.

For anyone in search of authentic thin-crust pizza, Sorbillo in NY is a must-visit. It is a testament to their commitment to tradition and quality that one doesn't need to book a flight to Naples to enjoy a genuine slice of heaven.

I had been looking to coming here for awhile and left with mixed feelings. It's a busy place so having an intimate conversation would be better at somewhere less noisy. The drinks were very good but the food didn't quite match them. The variety of tacos were what pulled me to this restaurant however, they ended up being on the small side and so the value was not met. We ended up going to the Thai restaurant down the street because we were still hungry..If I were to come back, I would consider just getting drinks and eating somewhere else.

I definitely enjoyed this restaurant, it was crowded, but in a good way. I enjoyed the noice and livelihood of this place. The food was delicious, my friends ordered various sushi dishes which all looked so beautiful but I did not try, none the less they seemed to enjoy them! I can, however, vouch for their bang bang shrimp, it was scrumptious! And for my main course I had their chicken which was yummy and of course last but not least the main course: desert. I tried so many different deserts that night with my friends, I forget the names but each one was a major hit with me, it was very much what my taste buds needed that night.

Made a reservation for two on a Tuesday, which was the right call as the place was buzzing with activity by the early evening. Tables are very close together as we nestled into our seats and were eventually given menus.Decided to go the "mezze" route and order a bunch of small items. Between two people: Eggplant Carpaccio ($14), Hummus/Falafel/Spicy Feta Combo ($18), Taboon Bread ($4), and a glass of Israeli wine ($12 each). Loved the spicy feta and falafel combo, and the Taboon bread is super/warm soft which went well with the hummus. Eggplant dish was shallow plus cooked into an odd texture; best eaten with the falafel for texture.Service started off slow then improved as the night went on. Would have enjoyed more elbow room as tables are packed tightly enough to overhear most conversation nearby. Would come back for a less busy night.

What a great experience at this cute French restaurant in the heart of Times Square. Don't be fooled because it's in a tourist area. Finally came here after months of having it bookmarked. Definitely come on a Sunday as street parking is free. The owner and workers at this place were so welcoming and genuine. It's been a long time since we received service that amazing! FYI: Weekend brunch has a mandatory $33 pre fixe but it's such a great deal. I had the escargots which was perfect. Well seasoned with butter and garlic. Not overly salted and chewy. I had the infamous French onion soup burger with a side of mashed potatoes (instead of fries). The French onion soup burger is unlike any other burger. Cooked perfectly with lots of sweet onions. The cheese was amazinggggg! It's served on an English muffin which worked well for this type of burger even though I'm a brioche bun kind of guy. It's almost a fork and knife kind of burger because the onions kept falling off.The mashed potatoes was silky smooth with a slight sweet undertone. Also really enjoyable. My wife had the new Steak Au Poivre burger. At $25 a pop, it's well worth the money. This seemed to be more of a messy-to-eat burger as there were tons of savory mushrooms on top. The au poivre sauce was a great touch to the burger. Pepper tones complimented the burger well as the burger seemed to more tamed on flavor. Really great burger. Came with a side of steak frites they were so perfectly crispy. I don't even like steak fries but these were beyond satisfying. Ended the meal with a creme brûlée. Last time I had one was in Paris and this was almost as equal. Can't wait to come back!

I recently tried delivery from this restaurant and was left underwhelmed. I started with the spicy tuna crispy rice, which was a disappointment; the rice was overwhelmed by a very salty sauce that led to an unpleasantly soggy texture. Moreover, the freshness of the tuna was questionable. I also had the Chili chicken ramen; the broth erred on the side of too salty for my taste, though the noodles themselves were satisfactory. Overall, the experience didn't inspire a return visit—both dishes were just mediocre, and I'm not eager to dine in or order again.

I recently visited this restaurant with a friend before catching a Broadway show, and I was delighted by our experience. It's not always easy to find a place that caters well to both vegan and non-vegan diets, but this spot nailed it. Arriving on a Sunday evening without a reservation, we were pleasantly surprised to be seated within a mere ten minutes. Our server was exceptionally friendly, enhancing the warm atmosphere. Both of us savored our meals and the drinks were equally pleasing. Highly recommend this place for its diverse menu and top-notch service.

I usually anticipate an exceptional dining experience at Ruth's Chris, and this visit was no exception—with one small hiccup. Despite our early 6:45 PM reservation, they had unfortunately run out of lobster, which was a surprising letdown. I settled for an alternative dish that, while decent, wasn't quite what I had my taste buds set on. Nevertheless, the remainder of the evening was delightful as we celebrated our friend's birthday in the restaurant's welcoming ambiance.

You can never go wrong with Los Tacos No. 1. This place is just as good as the location in Chelsea if not better as it is less crowded during non-work hours.  When ordering, they give you the option of doing flour or corn tortilla. My go-to is and will always be corn! They have the usual add-ons including freshly cut limes, various salsas, radishes, hot peppers and tomato salsa. The tacos are plentiful in meats and toppings. Super moist pork and beef, which were the two tacos I had.  SO GOOOOD!!

Title: A Delightful Takeout Experience with Uber Eats

My latest culinary adventure was enjoyed from the comfort of my own home, thanks to Uber Eats. Opting for a tantalizing plate of drunken noodles, I was impressed by the perfect spice level, which enhanced the flavors without overpowering them. The chicken accompanying the noodles was a standout - well done with a hint of smokiness and expertly seasoned. 

The experience was further elevated by the side orders of spring rolls and vegetable dumplings. The spring rolls arrived hot and crispy, indicating they were freshly made. Meanwhile, the vegetable dumplings were evidently homemade, filled with a savory blend of corn and greens that spoke to the restaurant's commitment to freshness.

The delivery service was quick and delivered with a smile, adding a warm touch to the entire experience. It's worth noting that the menu boasts an extensive variety of choices, ranging from rice and pad Thai dishes to wok stir-fries and soups.

All in all, this Uber Eats experience delivered on all fronts - timely service and truly delectable flavors. Highly recommended for anyone looking to indulge in quality takeout!

How can you say no to all you can eat! We made reservations for 7:45 and it took a little long to be seated. Came here for restaurant week $42 dinner is not a bad deal. My best friend and I came here and let me say all the meat we had was really good. Medium rare is the way to go. Definitely need reservations for this spot or you probably will never be seated for dinner time. Salad bar and steak is buffet style. Dont miss out on desert make sure you got some space for that as well. Highly recommended brazilian steakhouse. It was absolutely delicious and super filling. My friend and I was definitely in a steak coma from eat 2 hours of non stop steak haha. The wait was worth it.

The service was wonderful--the lady at the cash register was patient and gave some good suggestions since it was our first time visiting and with two little people in tow who can't tolerate spicy dishes.  We had lamb dumplings (which we didn't enjoy because they were a little too oily), a spicy tofu soup (which was delicious!), and hand cut noodles with oxtail and chicken.  The hand cut noodles were delicious and had a nice spongy texture just difficult to eat since in both cases they were long noodles.  The oxtail didn't have much flavor to me while we really loved the chicken.  So we had a bit of a mixed experience but sensing it is because we had put the no spicy restriction at the beginning.  The noodles were great, just not too sure if it was enough to persuade me to come back to visit.

I recently stumbled upon a gem of a restaurant that I'm elated to share about. The decor immediately piqued my interest with its intriguing design, setting the stage for a delightful dining experience.

Starting off with the spring rolls, while modest in size, they were a suitable appetizer that didn't disappoint. The real star of the show, however, was the vegetable curry. It struck a heavenly balance between the sweetness of coconut and the heat of spices—neither too hot nor too sweet—just a flawless harmony of flavors.

Service throughout the meal was nothing short of pleasant, complementing the impressive ambiance of the place, which was especially cinematic on a rainy night. Another plus is the restaurant's late closing hours—ideal for those evenings when cooking is off the cards.

During my visit, the place wasn't packed but maintained a steady stream of customers, suggesting it's likely more bustling at peak times. Regardless, I would heartily recommend this spot to friends, family, and as a potential date night venue. It's a thumbs-up from me!

I was craving chinese food so I went in and really pigged out! It satisfied my cravings. But objectively, I don't believe this cafe deserves more than 2 stars because the items it serves would normally retail 3$ in flushing, or 5$ in flushing. Instead they are selling these items for 9$ (yes I know it's Manhattan-- I don't mind its price itself-- but if you're having me pay 9$ for noodles, I'd hope they are more than just noodles in simple sauce with (what to Chinese people we'd consider fast food type of) pork bits on top. Seriously? You can get 'toppings' but you'd quickly be building up your bill dollars by dollars.... the amount of laziness in this restaurant in terms of the way they've 'curated' their menu is actually insulting, which is why I'm giving 2 stars. If the price were more fair- say 6$ for what they're serving, or if they just put more toppings othet than just the pork bits stir fry on their carbs, I would have given them 3-4 stars. With all this said, however, this cafe was cozy and all right for a meal- not to say I will ever be back because, although my meal went well there are so many better options actually worth your coin out in NY, don't get scammed out of your $$ here- and I appreciate their playlist. To mitigate the cost, definitely check in for a free drink: the soymilk goes great with the bam bam noodles, which are really not spicy if you are worried about spiciness!

First of all the venue is lovely. It's cozy and nicely decorated and would be great for brunch/dinner/any meal of the day. I came for Sunday lunch and had to try their Carbonara pasta. I loved that they added chili oil and the fresh yolk. It filled my up for the rest of the day. My friend got the Avocado toast which came with two  poached eggs and she seemed to enjoy that too.I'd come back here to try their pizzas and other pastas.

I came here for a special event put on by my firm.  The space is elegant and upscale without feeling stuffy.  We rented out almost the entire space, so we spent time in a big ballroom and another long room that faced south that had a nice bar and was a bit more intimate.  It was nice to have a boisterous space with loud conversations as well as a room where you could have more relaxed conversations by the bar.  The views were fantastic all around.  We were there at night so, the Midtown sky was lit up and it felt that much more special.  The staff was also very good, friendly and helpful in pointing us to bathrooms and elevators, etc.  The food was banquet style, but was delicious.  We had steak, fish and some really great side dishes.  The bartenders were also very good at making cocktails, too.
