I visited this eatery for a colleague's birthday lunch on a Monday, and the experience was a mixed bag. The service shined throughout our stay, with attentive and friendly staff. 

Starting on a high note, the bread served was delectable, albeit a bit messy to handle. The butter, appropriately featuring in the restaurant's name, met expectations. A standout dish was the portobello mushroom carpaccio, which served up a delightful contrast of chewy and firm textures, complemented by a hard cheese that was either Parmesan or Asiago. The balsamic was applied with a restrained hand, which was much appreciated.

The burger, unfortunately, fell into the realm of the mundane. While the sauce and fries accompanying it were satisfying, the patty itself was distractingly salty. On the other hand, my friend's choice of the zucchini lasagna received high praise, declared "bomb" despite its deceivingly healthy appearance - a choice I might regret not making.

To cap off the meal, the blackberry cake aimed to be the grand finale but missed the mark. Its cloying sweetness and lack of nuanced flavors left me disheartened, especially as a dessert enthusiast. 

In summary, while some dishes hit the right notes, others were simply unremarkable, making for an uneven dining experience.

Food 4Value 4.5Service 5Décor 4Good bang for your buck! This place has become a local favorite of mine-- super fresh sashimi. The uni bowl is delicious and the best priced item on the menu. Tres amigos bowl is also fantastic. Customer service is always great- everyone here is very friendly. Good wine list as well.

Title: A Modern Twist on Traditional Fare at [Restaurant Name]

My experience at [Restaurant Name], a new addition to the international chain that spans from China to the US, was nothing short of delightful. Thanks to my partner's mother's excellent recommendation, situated conveniently close to my partner's sister's workplace, we discovered this gem with its strikingly modern and inviting ambiance. The spacious interior boasted a unique transparent roof that bathed the dining area in a warm, natural glow.

The extensive menu presented a challenge with its array of traditional Chinese noodle and soup dishes, each described in mouthwatering detail. While torn between the Hotpot Beef Noodle Soup and the Yellow Croaker Fish Noodle Soup, I opted for the latter to avoid the spiciness of the beef. The Yellow Croaker Fish arrived in a deliciously milky white broth (whose secret remains a mystery), providing a rich, sea-infused flavor that was worth every spoonful.

My companions each found satisfaction in their choices as well – the lion's head meatball noodle soup for both my partner and his dad, the dandan noodle for his mom, and the tomato and egg noodle soup for his sister. Each dish was met with appreciation and contentment.

For those who haven't yet ventured to [Restaurant Name], I heartily suggest you give it a try. It's a place that, without a doubt, could entice me to consider a permanent move to New York just for the regular indulgence in their culinary delights.

Came to Marseille for brunch on a Sunday. I found a 11:30 am reservation through OpenTable the evening before, and when my friend was running late, the restaurant was happy to adjust my reservation when I called to let them know. As soon as I arrived, they seated me while I waited for my friend. By the time we left around 1:30 it was extremely crowded and there was a long wait (but tons of people were eating at the bar).The brunch menu had a lot of awesome food, especially vegetarian options (multiple omelets). I got the Mushrooms Pain Perdue and my friend got the California omelette with egg whites. The mushroom dish was amazing - the parmesan french toast was really soft and the eggs were well done. My friend really liked the California omelette as well. They kept the coffee coming and the service was excellent. The food came out really quickly and they didn't rush us after we finished eating to give up the table.Overall, would definitely recommend for a great, trendy lunch in a comfortable environment with great service with groups or individuals.

I've had the pleasure of experiencing one of the most exceptional brunches at this bustling spot. Despite the hectic atmosphere, it's the ultimate indulgence destination. Sharing is the way to go here – the French toasts, regardless of the variety, and the potato pancakes are personal recommendations. Each bite is a sinful delight. In short, this place is a gastronomic gem for those looking to treat themselves to an unforgettable brunch.

Title: A Warm Haven Amidst Snowy Weather at Ippudo

On a chilly, snow-bound day, my friend and I stumbled into Ippudo at 5 pm, feeling lucky as we snagged a table with no wait – quite a feat considering the queue that had formed by the time we left at 6:30 pm.

We started off with the pork buns, which come two to an order, and they were divine. The pork was lean yet tender, swathed in a perfectly balanced sauce, all nestled within pillow-soft buns.

For my main course, I opted for the Shiomaru Hakata Classic ramen and added a soft-boiled egg. The real star, however, was the broth – an absolutely captivating concoction that I couldn't get enough of.

In conclusion, wait or no wait, Ippudo is a must-visit for anyone craving exceptional ramen in a cozy setting. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

We had breakfast here one morning on our last trip to New York.  I think the main reason was for those Lemon Ricotta Pancakes.  Everything was pretty good, pretty standard for breakfast, but I do remember their breakfast potatoes were nice and crispy and seasoned really good.

Title: Cozy Spot with Strong Coffee and Tasty Eats

I recently visited a quaint little restaurant that, despite its size, provided a surprisingly swift seating experience. For those planning a visit, a word to the wise: expect a wait during peak hours due to the limited space.

The coffee, although on the lighter side in appearance, packed a pleasantly robust punch with attentive servers ensuring my cup never hit empty. As a self-proclaimed truffle enthusiast, I couldn't resist the truffle hashbrown with rosemary pecorino for $7. It delivered on both aroma and flavor, with a satisfying crunch that lived up to its promise.

My main course, the $14 ago egg sandwich, arrived looking like a work of art on a plate – definitely Instagram-worthy. It was a fresh and light avocado sandwich that, while more visually impressive than its flavor profile, still contributed to a solid breakfast experience.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a gem for those seeking great service, a mean cup of joe, and some well-crafted breakfast fare.

Title: A Valentine's Day to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

My date and I celebrated Valentine's Day at [Restaurant Name] and it was absolutely delightful. As soon as we arrived, our reservation was honored promptly, despite the bustling atmosphere - a testament to their excellent crowd management.

The service was outstanding; our waiter was the epitome of attentiveness, ensuring our glasses were never empty of their exceptional Classic Margaritas - a contender for the city's best, in my opinion. For those who favor a kick, the Picante Margarita was perfectly spicy.

The guacamole was a hit with us; a harmonious blend of citrus and salt that paired wonderfully with their spicier salsa and chips. Deciding to indulge in all the taco varieties was a wise choice. Each one had its own charm: the cactus offered a unique, pleasing texture, while the barbacoa and brisket impressed with their robust flavors. The chicken was succulent, and although the cod was a touch fishy, it was redeemed by a stellar sauce and crisp exterior.

Already looking forward to another round of margaritas, chips, and salsa during the summer, I highly recommend [Restaurant Name] for anyone seeking an enjoyable dining experience with a fantastic selection of food and drinks.

Title: A Slice of Authentic New York at Joe's Pizza - 14th St

Joe's Pizza on 14th St is a slice of New York City in every sense. It's my go-to for what I consider "pro-grade pizza" - reliably hot, fresh, and consistently delectable at any hour. The secret might be in the sweet tang of their sauce or the uniform excellence no matter the chef manning the oven.

The 14th St location mirrors its Carmine St counterpart in delivering an authentic NYC experience – brisk, efficient, and zero-tolerance for dawdling. You know what you're getting, and you get it fast.

However, if you're the sort to relish a celebrity photo-laden ambiance or to have an undying allegiance to another neighborhood joint – this may not be your top pick. And if the likes of Domino's tops your pizza list, then Joe's authentic New York flavor might just be lost on you.

In conclusion, Joe's Pizza stands out as a slice of New York culinary tradition that's hard to fault. If I could, I'd make it a staple of my daily diet – it's that good.

From the entrancing seasonal decor to the classy, magical ambiance, this restaurant ensures an immersive dining experience perfect for special occasions. Despite the premium pricing, the $69 unlimited wine dinner offers value with a delightful appetizer, main course, and dessert, all paired with copious wine selections. The savory, crisp peeky toe crab cake appetizer set a high bar, complemented exquisitely by the succulent braised short ribs, which were tender to perfection. The charming gingerbread ornament dessert, both in taste and presentation, wrapped up the meal delightfully. Marking our anniversary, the restaurant's generous gesture of an additional complimentary dessert was a thoughtful touch. The first couple of wine glasses left a notably high-quality impression, enhancing the overall fantastic culinary journey. Highly recommended for marking your next milestone celebration.

KazuNori? More like MayoNori. They love mayo here. If you're getting a non-fish hand roll (like scallop, crab, or lobster), it will probably have mayo mixed in. It makes sense that the same people who own KazuNori also own SUGARFISH. The mayo couldn't overuse itself over at SUGARFISH (they're too busy drowning everything in ponzu), so I guess they had to do it here.I must say that I do appreciate their waiting system. It's bar-style seating so if you get there before the rest of your party, you can tell them how many people there are in a group, and then wait in line. That being said, it's best to come with small groups since most of the seating frees up in pairs. I got there on a Thursday at around 5:30 and ended up waiting about half an hour for a party of three.As for the food, I went with the 6-Hand Roll menu ($29), which includes toro, yellowtail, salmon, bay scallop, crab, and lobster hand rolls. I enjoyed the toro, yellowtail, and salmon. But as I mentioned earlier, the non-fish rolls have entirely too much mayo in them. It covers up the taste of the shellfish, which makes you question its quality. The crab roll tasted exactly like the one over at SUGARFISH - canned tuna. In theory, $29 is a great deal but then when you think about it - is it really though? If half of the rolls aren't good? If you are dying to try this place, I would recommend coming early, bring only one friend or go solo, and stick to the fish.Tip - just as the Japanese do, there is no tipping here so that was pretty nice. Also, each person automatically gets their own bill so it's probably a good first date spot if you want to avoid that whole awkward check dance.

Came here with my wife on a Monday night. It was not busy and it was the perfect spot to have a fun time and great conversation. The server Steven was amazing and very knowledgeable. He made us feel very welcome and was very attentive. We ordered the burrata and the ribeye. Both dishes were amazing and was full by the end of the meal. Definitely would recommend coming here and having a great time!

Title: A Prime Spot for Sports and Spirits in Midtown – Stout NYC

Stout NYC stands out as one of Manhattan's premier bars, boasting a colossal selection of drinks, which includes a vast array of beers on tap and an impressive lineup of imports. Located just a stone's throw from Penn Station, it offers an incredibly convenient spot for pre-game meetups or for those simply looking to unwind while waiting for a train.

The atmosphere is electric, especially during post-work hours and the weekend rush, which only amplifies the venue's vibrant energy – a testament to its popularity. Whether you're looking to catch the big game or celebrate after, Stout NYC delivers an unmatched experience in the heart of midtown. Definitely a go-to sports bar for locals and travellers alike.

My husband and I are super fans for the rabbit house so we were really excited to hear they opened up their second spot. We were here for their 6 courses Omakasa Prix Fixe dinner during soft opening. Overall, the food was amazingly delicious but the service should be improved to operate more smoothly. Firstly, we were served when we waited by sake bread sticks which was sake-smelly with soft texture. We both loved all 6 courses which were delicate with high quality ingredients and surprised us every moment we had. Our favorites were Foie Grass and Risotto with Wagyu beef, the Foie Grass was amazingly soft and melted in your month, the Risotto was flavored with truffle and little bit chewy which we loved the texture. The best thing was the chef introduced every dishes with ingredients, stories and meaning when she served.Only complaint was their service, attentive but reluctant since it was the first day for the waiter. Moreover, we had our reservation at 6:00 pm (There were only 2 time slots: 6:00pm and 8:00 pm) and waited more than 30 minutes to be served. The chef told us she needed to wait another group but, for us, they should take their own responsibilities since they were late.

Title: An Unforgettable Encounter with Arroz Negra Cremoso

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a restaurant renowned for its Arroz Negra Cremoso con Calamares, and the dish did not disappoint. Delivered in an individual-sized cast iron pan, the squid ink rice boasted a mellow, unassuming appearance until it was topped with five expertly grilled calamares. The accompanying aioli, when stirred into the rice, transformed the meal into a culinary climax unmatched by any other this past year.

Upon arrival, I was greeted with a selection of olives that were remarkable in their nutty, butter-like quality, served in aesthetically pleasing hammered bowls. Although no bread was offered to accompany my single dish and soda—perhaps an oversight?—it did not detract from the overall experience.

Seated at the Chef's counter, I gained insights into the orchestrated precision of the kitchen team as they applied finishing touches to dishes bound for other lucky patrons.

My next visit is already planned, with aspirations to indulge in the grilled fish and, without a doubt, a second helping of the stellar squid rice. And this time, I hope to sample their bread as well.

Solid place for ramen. I really enjoyed the chicken and fish broth, which is something I don't think is common in ramen places. You could taste the fish in it (in a good way)- it adds flavor and depth and it's not overly salty like most ramen broths I've had (where they overcompensate for "flavor" by just adding salt). I had the miso ramen. The noodles was good and it came with a nice mix of other ingredients in it. I also tried the spicy salmon hand roll which was also delicious.The staff is nice and attentive, and what I also liked was the amount of different Japanese drinks (coffee, juice, soda, sake) available. I wouldn't exactly venture out of my way to go here but I wouldn't be opposed to stopping here again if I were in the area.

Title: Another Delightful Dinner at My Go-To Spot

I recently dined here on a Monday evening to celebrate my sister's birthday and was pleasantly surprised to find it was restaurant week, offering a three-course meal for just $42. True to form, this eatery delivered yet another fantastic dining experience.

We indulged in the tuna tartare and snow crab appetizers followed by a 10-piece sashimi selection and a beautifully cooked sea bass. Each dish arrived with impeccable presentation. The tuna tartare and sashimi stood out; they were simply the stars of our meal.

For dessert, we tried the red bean panna cotta and the intriguing shiro choko. While enjoyable, I must say I've been more impressed with the tofu cheesecake and black sesame mousse in the past.

The service was outstanding as always, adding to the overall excellent dining atmosphere. And a special nod to the authentic Japanese toilet—always an interesting experience!

All in all, this is a restaurant I firmly recommend and will no doubt visit again soon.

Title: A Caribbean Gem in Manhattan

I recently visited the new black-owned Caribbean restaurant in Manhattan for a Saturday brunch and was blown away by the experience. The highlight of my meal was the shrimp and grits entree, perfectly complemented by the bottomless mimosas, all for a mere $35. The ambiance was vibrant and inviting, reflecting the warmth of Caribbean culture. Additionally, the service was nothing short of exceptional; attentive and efficient wait staff ensured a fantastic dining experience. Although initially advised of a 25-minute wait, it was a pleasant surprise to be texted just 10 minutes later. This place is a must-visit for anyone looking for an authentic Caribbean feast with an upbeat atmosphere.

Title: A Brunch to Remember

From the moment we arrived 10 minutes before our 12:30 pm reservation, our experience at this restaurant was nothing short of wonderful. With a party of six in tow, finding a suitable spot for conversation can be challenging, but the staff had us perfectly accommodated with a ready table conducive to dialogue - a request they fulfilled with the utmost consideration.

Our server, Melissa, was the epitome of service excellence – attentive, cheerful, and incredibly helpful, enhancing our dining pleasure without the slightest hint of rush. Her demeanor allowed us to truly relax and savor the moment.

The appetizers were a hit, featuring an eclectic mix that included tater tots, house-made bacon, Babka, and a grains salad - each one a delightful prelude to the main event. For the main course, I indulged in a crispy oyster omelette, while my companions enjoyed a variety of dishes from fluffy waffles to a savory turkey sausage hash with Brussels sprouts, collectively nodding to the quality of their meals.

Our collective verdict is clear: this establishment lives up to its promises. Fantastic food, exceptional service, and a genuinely great dining experience. A strong recommendation for anyone seeking a top-notch brunch spot.

For creativity this is a 5 star but overall taste wise it was peculiar. I thought the hint of green was food color but it really has that pickle juice brininess. Very interesting and had the pickle chips as garnish. I decided to go all in with chocolate syrup it help with the bitter sourness. I ironically ended up finishing the hold thing lol. Also the restaurant have elevated to the future. You order everything on the tablet on the left wall. I was bit thrown off by the process but for someone that hates interaction I appreciated it.

Pretty expansive and interesting menu of pastas, all the same price ($17). Price is decent considering quality and portion size, especially given the lack of mid-tier pasta places in the neighborhood. I ordered the truffle Mac and cheese which came piping hot (kudos considering the distance from my office) and cheesy/gooey with a strong truffle flavor. There was a large piece of shaved black truffle on the Mac as well. I found the noodles to be just a little too soft, but I like my pasta fairly al dente so this may be a matter of personal preference. I was looking for something decadent and heavy after a night of heavy drinking and Cotenna definitely supplied on that front. Wish the delivery fee were a little lower, but cest la vie. Will order again to try another of their pastas.

Upon discovering a spot reminiscent of the Boiling Crab in New York, my excitement levels hit the roof. I indulged in two pounds of succulent shrimp, expertly coated in a medium-spiced 'everything sauce' that was nothing short of sensational. The sauce's richness and depth of flavor elevated the fresh seafood to a new height of deliciousness. We also paired our meal with garlic bread, which proved to be an unexpectedly delightful companion to the sauce. While garlic noodles would have been the cherry on top, the bread still made for a fantastic addition. A highly recommended feast for any seafood lover in search of a flavorful adventure!

Title: Unearthing a Gem Amongst Rice Roll Aficionados

After stumbling upon Yin Ji Chang Fen amidst a sea of mixed reviews, my expectations were modest at best. However, as a seasoned rice roll enthusiast, I was compelled to put this Guangzhou chain to the test. To my delight, the rice rolls transcended my nostalgic memories of dim sum experiences. The R13 "Marinated Chicken sliced with chives rice noodle roll" stood out with its delicate, silky texture and the perfect balance of fresh ingredients, far surpassing the ordinary offerings elsewhere.

Observing a queue of discerning elderly locals, I knew there was authenticity in the air. The congee complemented the meal beautifully, with a spot-on consistency and a rich depth of flavor. The authentic taste extended to their beverages; the HK milk tea being a robust, creamy delight.

The long lines in the morning speak volumes, yet the extended hours until 10:30pm afford the flexibility for a rice roll fix beyond conventional times. Yin Ji Chang Fen secured my future patronage, proving itself as a bastion of quality in the heart of Chinatown.

I stumbled upon this charming little spot in my quest for an inexpensive lunch option in NYC. The ambiance was quaint and inviting, with a palpable coziness complementing its compact size. Service, though delivered with a generous smile by the friendly waitress, did lag a bit — a surprise given the scant number of patrons.

However, any frustration with the wait dissipated once I took my first bite of the arepa. It was wonderfully flavorful, striking an ideal balance between satiety and portion size for a midday meal. For those working nearby, this restaurant is a gem, offering tasty and wallet-friendly lunch escapes from the hustle of city life.

On a spontaneous evening out, my husband and I found ourselves dining at Ippudo on 5th Avenue, our first foray into the brand's array of locations. We quickly discovered that the menu diverged from its East Village counterpart. The no-phone-number check-in system was a tad unconventional, adding to the anticipation of our evening as the bustling lobby thinned surprisingly fast, our 30-minute wait uneventful.

Service shifted gears upon seating, delivering prompt and efficient attention. The shared Karaage was a hit, its delectable flavors setting the stage for our main course. The Karaka Spicy Kasane was my fiery choice, while my husband enjoyed the rich depths of the Akamaru Kasane. Learning that even the broths diverged from the East Village recipes only piqued our interest.

We left content and curious, eager to compare the Ippudo experience across their other locations on future outings.

Had fried pork belly and spicy miso ramen. Huge portions and very affordable! Ramen noodles was a bit over cooked. I'd have prefer a firmer texture. Chashu pork was tender and huge. Veggies were perfect. You can ask for chili oil if you want it to be extra spicy. fried pork belly stays crispy even after many hours!service was over ok. They shouldn't ask how you're  doing when your mouth is full. It's just awkward.

I recently stumbled upon this gem of a ramen spot after dodging the lengthy queue at Totto Ramen downstairs, and it's quickly become my favorite. The half-boiled eggs here are sublime — a must-add to any bowl. If you have a penchant for heat, the miso ramen with spicy sauce will not disappoint. It's a perfect blend of flavor and kick, with the eggs rounding out a truly satisfying meal. This place has certainly earned its spot as my new go-to for all things ramen.

I visited Los Tacos amidst considerable hype, only to be met with disappointment. The offerings I sampled, namely the cactus tortilla and the quesadilla, lacked flavor and were underwhelming in size. In contrast, the neighboring Mariscos provided a more satisfying experience with a variety of seafood options like shrimp and fish tacos. Given the limited chicken and pork options at Los Tacos, coupled with the daunting queue, I can't recommend it. The food at Los Tacos didn't live up to expectations, and overall, it wasn't worth the wait.

Super casual and chill vibes here, a great spot to stop and enjoy some tacos and other comfort California themed comfort foods. I loved the chorizo breakfast tacos and you can't go wrong with the churros ice cream sandwich at the end!

Review is just for the happy hour menu. First off - holy cow happy hour even on weekends from 5pm to 11pm? That's crazy! Call it New York's first and most consistent "Happy Night", albeit all day everyday! Ambiance wise, its not the most swankey or upscale bar, but it does give off a chill and relaxed, no frills atmosphere. A bit in between a true dive bar and a classy lounge. Came here on a Saturday night at 7pm, and the restaurant/bar was about ~75% full. My friend and I just opted to get drinks at the bar, and we got the lychee martini and the red sangria. Both of these drinks were made incredibly well, you can taste the lychee really distinctly in the drink, while the alcohol was really smooth. Same goes with the red sangria, I don't think I've had such an incredible sangria in the lower east side in awhile. All of this for $7 this is such a steal.

MY FAVORITE PIZZA SPOT IN NEW YORK.My boyfriend and I were craving pizza at midnight during out trip to New York and we saw that Joe's Pizza was open. We stayed at the Double Tree Metropolitan on Lexington and this location was in Times Square. It would take about 15 minutes to walk there which was not that bad but the only downside was that it was FREEZING. We went during January 3-8. We decided to bust out on an adventure and walked over to Times Square. It actually took us about 20-25 minutes while walking which was not too bad since we were able to see the lights of Times Square. It was crowded when we arrived about 12:30am but the line went by so fast. (One thing I love about New York is the quickness of everything. BAM BAM BAM). We ordered by the slice since we were not that hungry and we tried the Caprese Pizza, Supreme, Pepperoni, White Sauce and Cheese. We decided to walk back to the hotel to eat since my sister was waiting for her slice as well. The walk back took longer and sadly, by the time we got back, the pizza was not as hot as before. BUT STILL SO DELICIOUS!We decided to go back the next day for lunch and the pizza just tasted so much better in the store. The Caprese pizza was my favorite one ever and I wish I were eating another slice now. This location gets super crowded, especially with it being in Times Square. The prices are decent and ranges between $2-$4.50. In my opinion, a little pricey but it was one of the better pizza spots we tried. The slices are also very generous, and although it is thin crust, the crunch and juiciness of everything just makes it so worth it.

My recent Happy Hour experience at this spot was a delightful surprise! The creative drink selection was not only competitively priced but also a hit with our group. While my cucumber concoction packed an unexpected spicy punch not indicated on the menu, my companions thoroughly enjoyed their flawless beverages. To top it off, the summer outdoor vibe added a lovely touch to our gathering, and the appetizers, although we didn't indulge, appeared tempting and worth a try next time. Highly recommend a visit during their Happy Hour for a fun and satisfying outing!

I had a chance to come here for lunch with a friend and we shared two lunch sets. Normally people would each  have one meal set, but we wanted to try both. The beef sukiyaki was delicious with a savory broth. The udon with the katsu don were also delicious but the sukiyaki was the star of the meal. The peach oolong was sweet and refreshing and good for if you are craving something similar to fruit teas at bubble tea places, but just water would be fine if you want to savor the flavor of the sukiyaki. I like how they provided complimentary hot green tea at the end of our filling meal to balance out the cold water right before we leave for the cool weather outside. The service was attentive.

Was craving pasta and this joint hit the spot!My party of three swung in at 6pm to a restaurant just emptying out a large party so they had plenty of seating! Woohoo!We ordered their three specials, as our server said that was what they were most known for. Those three included their signature truffle pasta ($49-ish), gnocchi with mozzarella in pesto sauce, and their mushroom risotto.Our favorite was truffle then gnocchi then risotto as least favorite. Everything had great flavor, my only dislikes was that the truffle pasta at almost $50, its noodles were pretty overcooked. It was also a tad salty from the cheese and the truffles. We were sucking down our waters like crazy! As for service, waters were constantly being refilled and servers were very polite. Attentive but not hovering. Just right! The place itself is super clean, right on the corner so they're easy to find. They're also super small with like 15 tables, so they will fill up quickly. Overall, this is a cute spot that's definitely worth a visit!

Title: A Quiche to Remember in NY

My sister and I stumbled upon a gem during our girls' weekend in NYC this past November. In our hunt for the perfect breakfast spot, we trusted the high praises on Google and Yelp — and boy, were they right on the money! Around 9:30 AM, we cozied into this charming restaurant and were tempted by the day's special: a broccoli and Swiss quiche with a side salad. Deciding to indulge in the quiche (sans salad for me — it's breakfast, after all), we were blown away by the flavors. I'm still dreaming of that quiche; it's the good stuff of foodie love stories.

The place wasn't just about fantastic food, though. The service we received was impeccable — attentive, prompt, and with a smile. And the coffee? Strong, but in that perfectly brisk way that wakes you up and warms your soul simultaneously. Before we left, we couldn't resist grabbing some pastries to go. 

For anyone seeking a delightful breakfast experience, you can't go wrong here. I highly recommend giving this place a visit; your taste buds will thank you.

Last night's dinner at Zuma was an exceptional experience from start to finish. Seated promptly at 8pm, our host was the epitome of grace, expertly guiding us through our first foray into the restaurant's culinary delights. Zuma's three distinct kitchens offer an array of raw and cooked options, all presented in a tapas style ideal for sharing.

The evening kicked off with a succulent garlic and sweet chilli glazed edamame and a notably tasty fried softshell crab with a subtly flavored wasabi mayo - delicious without overpowering. Not typically a wasabi fan, I found it pleasantly mild and complemented the crab perfectly.

The chicken skewers were a hit - we enjoyed three orders - each piece grilled to perfection. The skirt steak for our main course was tender and cooked to a delectable medium, and while the prawn and avocado rolls initially presented a slightly fishy taste, they grew on us, despite the rice being a bit drier than expected.

Dessert was a sumptuous molten chocolate cake with caramel sauce and ice cream, a rich treat made for sharing. Our Old Fashioned, made with a Japanese whiskey twist and an artistically branded orange slice, was a testament to Zuma's attention to detail in presentation.

The restaurant's intimate seating fostered a friendly ambiance, leading us to mingle with a delightful couple from the UK. The chic and sophisticated atmosphere makes Zuma an excellent choice for date nights or celebratory group occasions. Although warned about the 'bathroom mission' due to their distant location, this did little to detract from the overall enjoyment.

Admiring Zuma's architectural nuances, I left feeling thoroughly impressed and would recommend the restaurant to anyone looking for a sophisticated and unique dining experience. It's definitely on my list to revisit, and perhaps next time, its London location!

So glad I was able to try Thai diner! I know its new and has been opened a couple months. I believe it's part of Flower Shop or the owner of Flower Shop opened this (not sure but something along those lines). When you walk in, you definitely get that Thai vibe, especially with the decor and the food smell! The only thing I would complain about is that the service is a little slow. Other than that, the food was amazing and pretty spicey (depends on what you order). What I ordered:- Thai Diner Egg Sandwich (MUST GET!!): egg, cheese, sai oua herbal sausage wrapped in roti- Phat Bai Horapha: spicy thai chili, garlic&basil stirfry topped with crispy cried egg- Crab Cakes

Returned for dinner after unsuccessfully trying to get in at Hillstone; my friend friend and I secured a walk-in here instead. Started with the Tequila mockingbird cocktail, which was amazing, then shared:+ Whole crispy mushroom - I'll probably get this every time I come here, it's that good + Fluke crudo - another standout + Estrella (chicken liver pasta) - decent but not sure it's worth the hype+ Duck - good, had a really vinegar-y flavor though which is not my thing + Pear crisp - amazing, I can never resist a fruit-based dessert Next time: I want to finally try the burger, which is only served at lunch. 4.5 stars.

Title: A Scrumptious Scandinavian Delight at Essex Market

Tucked away in the Essex Market, Nordic Preserves Fish and Wildlife offers an escape into the flavors of Scandinavia amidst the hustle of NYC. The shop itself is a pristine jewel, with a gleaming glass display that showcases an impressive array of smoked and cured seafood, from salmon to sturgeon, accompanied by traditional Nordic sides.

I indulged in the "Lax Rulle" sandwich, a delectable creation featuring Norwegian smoked salmon, Lingonberried Red Cabbage, and Horseradish crème ensconced in a baguette. Although its appearance may deceive, the sandwich is generously laden with succulent salmon. The horseradish crème is pleasantly mild, allowing the other flavors to shine through, while the pickled red cabbage adds a subtle, sweet tang. The baguette, rich and hearty, completes the ensemble with a satisfying texture, although a slimmer slice or additional toasting could elevate the experience.

Despite the minor critique on the bread, the sandwich impressed with its freshness and the thoughtful addition of herbs and a zesty lemon garnish. At $10 plus tax, the meal provided both quality and quantity. Service was as friendly as it was efficient, with an emphasis on crafting each sandwich from scratch without haste.

Nordic Preserves may not follow New York's culinary trends, but it undoubtedly sets its own. The care in preparation and the unique selection make it a must-visit for those seeking to step off the beaten path. In short, nothing fishy here—just pure, delightful eats. Consider the mic dropped.

In the heart of a beautiful Latin party avenue, filled with good restaurants, shopping and things to do and see, this large corner restaurant is a gorgeous spot to dine, chill and enjoy the local culture. The seafood is ultra fresh and this chef is a wizard with the sauces to match. Shellfish, mangoes, salmon avocado and all the wonderful citrus to complement it all. I enjoyed a special menu for a graduation party and I am thrilled to have enjoyed delicious sangria to wash it all down. I would love to bring friends here again.

The concept of fresh eel from Japan really caught my attention. I'm a big eel lover which lead me to this restaurant.When you walk in, the whole place looks dark; black walls and very dimly lit. Food: 2.5/5The eels were Japan so no doubt on the quality but the taste and presentation can be better. We ordered an appetizer which was egg and eel omelette, the egg didn't have much flavor and the only thing saving it was the eel. We also ordered 3 entrees to share, 2 dishes were eel with uni and one just eel (forgot the name of the dishes); one dish was steamed eel and uni. Honestly, all of them tasted the same, which was really disappointing. For the price point, you expected something more unique to every individual dish. Our dishes did come with desserts, we ordered the matcha pudding, sesame ice cream and red bean ice cream, all of which were very mediocre. Sadly to say, I won't be coming back to this place and definitely wouldn't recommend it to anyone, as I've had better eel dishes elsewhere for a cheaper price point too.
These milkshakes are amazing! A bit pricey (around $15) but honestly they are so good. The burgers are also tasty. I strongly recommend this place!

Diner connected to the Wellington Hotel therefore great location. We popped in this morning around 8:30 and were seated right away. We were greeted, ordered and served pretty much right away.Prices fair for NYC. We ordered 2 lumberjack orders for 2  adults and 1 child. They were huge servings! Lots of bacon, two large eggs and huge, thick, fluffly, moist and tasty pancakes. 2 adults can totally share this meal therefore totally worth the $17. My 5 stars is for breakfast food and service on a Saturday morning.

Wokuni is a luxurious sushi spot near Grand Central.I came here a while ago and was whelmed. The fish is good quality but nothing outstanding. I will say the that skewers are top-notch. We also had a solid yellowtail collar.Service is great. The room is super sleek and it definitely feels like a hotspot, with nice lighting. Nothing compelled me to return as it's just way too pricey for what it is, but they do have a great happy hour special.

An awesome place to satisfy a quick sudden sushi craving. Definitely meant for a grab n go lunch or you can sit down. They have about 8 bar seats, there's hooks too! You order on a screen when you walk in and they'll call your name when your order is ready, or I think you can pay cash up front as well. Most of their rolls look pre made, but the quality definitely was not bad. They're pretty generous with the fillings as well. I got 3 rolls and it came out to around $13. The rolls aren't huge but maybe the size of your palm, pretty generous with filling, and.Shrimp avocado roll was probably more bland than the other two rolls I had, but it definitely wasn't bad. I loved the spicy tube roll! Lots of tuna, actually spicy and flavorful. I also had the salmon avocado with quinoa, surprisingly I actually enjoyed this. It said recommended on the screen, so why not give it a try. The rice and quinoa could use a bit more  vinegar but that's good probably a personal preference. They also have snacks, regular sushi pieces, and even mochi. Would definitely recommend for a quick lunch.

Hands down this place serves up some really good dishes!  from the tasty appetizers such as the Aromatic Beef, Sichuan Wonton, Scallion Pancakes to the entrees, which we had their Sautéed Lamb w. Cumin, Braised Slice Beef w. Spicy Chili Sauce and shared some their Pork Fried Rice.  Seating was quick due to Yelp's Reservation feature.  The servers were very friendly and knowledgeable and were on top of your every need.  Sorry I didn't take any pics of the food to share but that only means that I will have to go back!! to indulge and take pics... :) . The only pic that I took was of the Birthday Boy which was very delighted that I brought him for some great Asian Food experience.  Great Job!
I love rice rolls, I can eat mad plates by myself. I'll share begrudgingly but not the liver rolls -- those I'll eat a whole plate of myself!!! GET THE LIVER RICE ROLLS.

After attempting to find a place to eat at the Mercado, I ended up at Spanish Diner and glad I did.  I grabbed a seat at the bar and the service there was excellent.  I ordered the eggs, fries and jamon iberico which I completely devoured.  I felt the price of $24 for the dish was on the high side, but the place is very nice and spacious compared to the Mercado and service was great, so I didn't mind paying a little extra for those things.  If you find the Mercado overwhelming, I would definitely stop at Spanish Diner for a bite.  Good food, great service and lovely ambiance.

We were walking around the city looking for a spot to have a drink and found Smith's.  The open air bar area drew us in right away.  It was nice to find a comfortable restaurant bar in the Times Square area adjacent that isn't touristy.  This place is comfortable and like a place down the street from home.
Good food and amazing decor! This place is very close to where I work and I am surprised I did not visit it before.  The service is attentive, quick with yummy food and good atmosphere

Title: A Letdown on the Ramen and Bao Front

I recently found myself at this spot after a day of shopping, eager to satiate my cravings for ramen and bao. Unfortunately, the experience left much to be desired. The bao bun promised a pork-filled delight but fell short with scant amounts of meat and an unwelcome presence of iceberg lettuce—a personal turn-off. Moving on to the ramen, while the broth had a decent flavor profile, the rest of the bowl was a portrait of minimalism. A few slices of average pork, mere shavings of mushrooms, and some scattered scallions could not rescue this dish from its bland fate. Despite the server's commendable friendliness, the food itself proved to be a rather underwhelming affair.

I was in the mood for some ramen when looking around we came across this place glad we decided to give it a try. Appetizers we gave the Sticky ribs a try, wow these were delicious meat falls right off the bone they are fried which I didn't realize initially when we ordered but it worked out great tasting sauce. Ramen I had the Chicken very good nice tasting noodles & broth, my company had the Pork Ramen good as well. Next visit we gave the Dumplings a try they were great, very good comes out sizzling hot good with some soy sauce. I had the Tonkotsu ramen very good, I could do with out the pork? Just because but it was good nicely thin pieces, great tasting broth.  my company had the Tantan this is a spicy coconut broth not bad. Small location , nicely decorated first time around we sat at the bar so service was pretty easy & quick , second time at one of the communal tables personally not a fan of communal tables just because never seems like u have enough room, here is was ok a bit tight the space.  Decent prices good place for ramen & quick service will definitely try to visit from time to time.

Excellent first impression in this Brazilian Restaurant. Elegant ambiance, with high ceilings. We sat at the upper bar to order a la carte. The main salon is for the "eat as much meat you want" + buffet.My husband had for main a huge steak on the bone with riceMe, a vegetarian option , cauliflower steak with quinoa and lentils, served with guacamole and asparagus. It was unbelievably tasty, delicious. We both had caipirinhas with cheese bread (tapioca flour, gluten free) for starters. The bill was very reasonable US$ 70 for both of us. I really recommend this place, well located, just opposite to the doors of Moma on 53

Cheap, causal delicious. It's hard to find a meal for less than 10 in the city. Roast pork over rice for $4.25 or a large (for 2 ppl) for $6.00. VALUE. The roast pork is definitely on the fatty side but it's so flavorful. They also pour sauce on top of it so the rice and cabbage also soaks in the flavor.Even if there is a line, it moves quick. No complaints for this value meal.

During our return visit to the Black Derby, the food was just as good as I remembered, as well as the service for the majority of the night, up until the very end - but more on that later.We ordered a starter to share, the short rib and lamb as our mains, and two desserts to split. The short rib was super tasty and tender, but the dark horse of the dish was definitely the mushroom purée. The lamb was also extremely tender and contrasted nicely with the sliced fennel and orange peel on top.Our main server for the night was also super friendly and attentive, checking in with us at just the right moments throughout the night. When it finally came to paying the bill, we paid in cash and received large bills as our change. When my date requested for smaller bills as change instead (to adequately tip) via a different server who was passing by, the server took out his own wallet (?!) and tossed a dollar bill onto our table. The behavior was so out of left field - I would never expect a restaurant's employee to take out his own wallet from his pocket at a fast food joint, let alone a place where diners are paying a premium for ambience and service. The action had a pretty negative connotation and showed general unprofessionalism that left our dinner ending on a sour note. Normally I would try to justify the behavior in my head, but it wasn't even that busy - we dined at the earlier side of a Saturday night dinner service and there were plenty of empty tables around us.I really hope that the restaurant's management takes more priority in training their front of house. No matter how solid the food is, you can really ruin a diner's experience and memory of a restaurant with little slip-ups in details such as these.

My husband and I went to the Mermaid Inn last year on Amsterdam Avenue on the other side of Manhattan and we loved that one.  This one well not to much . We didn't relaize that we had to make a reservation, I actually looked on open table and there was no times open . We decided to sit at the bar the waitress was alright very attentive though which we liked . The oysters were very good along with the mini tacos . When we received our check we were kinda disappointed cause we were looking for the mini dessert that we received last time which was a small chocolate pudding in the cup along with a lobster fortune.  Unfortunately we did not get either . The service was great and left a tip and the waitress rolled her eyes and was annoyed cause it was a high enough tip like give me a break.  Next time we will go back to the other Mermaid Inn we loved that location.

Title: A Hearty Pre-Theater Dinner at Totto Ramen

My friend and I had the pleasure of dining at Totto Ramen for an early dinner before catching a play. Arriving at 6 pm on a Tuesday, we were seated immediately in the subterranean space that felt a tad dark and slightly stuffy, yet watching the chefs expertly torch the pork and craft the ramen bowls added an authentic flair to our experience.

We couldn't resist the allure of the mega-ramen, priced reasonably at $18. It was a substantial upgrade from the original ramen, boasting generous portions of succulent pork – both belly and other cuts – and an array of vegetables suggesting a nod to pho elements. The inclusion of the soft-boiled egg, a non-negotiable for me, sealed the deal. 

Though termed 'mega', this bowl could easily pass for 'meat lover's ramen', overflowing with over half a pound of meat. Admittedly, it was more than I could finish, but the meal satisfactorily powered me through the evening's activities. In conclusion, Totto Ramen delivered an enjoyable and fulfilling dining experience, adding another ramen to my ever-growing list of favorites.

Title: A Cozy Spot for Shanghainese Delights - A Mixed Experience

My friends and I recently dined at a Shanghainese restaurant, hoping to satisfy a craving for soup dumplings. The atmosphere was welcoming with traditional Chinese décor that exuded effort and culture, from the red placemats to the intricate statues. The menu, rich with historical snippets, promised authenticity.

The service proved commendable with an almost instantaneous seating and attentive waitstaff, yet the experience was bittersweet. While the menu offered an impressive variety, the soup dumplings, the main event, were a letdown – lacking in the wow factor and not the best rendition I've had. The saving grace was the beef noodle soup, with its savory broth and tender beef – a dish I'd recommend.

However, the portion sizes didn't quite match the slightly steeper prices, especially when compared to other local Shanghainese eateries. My friend's spring noodles fell short, needing a generous dose of chili oil to elevate the taste.

The restaurant shines in its ambience and could be a perfect spot for a quiet get-together, but when it comes to the food, it's a mixed bag. My rating: 7.0/10. Would I return? Possibly for the lunch menu on a weekday. Yet, would I bring my Chinese grandparents here? The jury is still out on that one.

Such a cute spot on the upper east side!  A trifecta of scrumptious food, fun decor, and friendly service. What we ate:- Soup dumplings: great way to start off the meal.  Good skin that didn't break when picked up, and delicious juice inside.  Perfect for a cold wintery evening!  Get vinegar with ginger slices to dip it in and you're good to go.- Ribs: sweet and savory, a house fave!  The glaze on these beauties was at a high sheen--just look at the pic!- Tofu and beef tomato hotpot: this was my FAVE!  Just look at the ceramic that it comes in.  Gorgeous.  So flavorful that I think I drank up all the soup before my friend could get a word in edgewise. Everything went great with a bottle of white wine at a good price point.  If you're craving solid Chinese food on the UES, this is the place to go!

I really enjoyed my experience here. It is a cute and cozy place, perfect for a weekend brunch. The service was very good. The servers were knowledgeable, attentive and pleasant. I was also seated right away when I arrived, even though my friend was on his way. I appreciated that. When my friend arrived, we were served a baguette and butter. The baguette was crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. The butter was placed on a warm plate, so it kind of melted a little, but that was fine for me because I like my butter soft and easily spreadable anyway. I ordered the fresh squeezed orange juice and the poached eggs with veggies and balsamic jus. I also tried some of my friend's hot chocolate and home fries. As a hot chocolate snob, I thought the hot chocolate was not bad. The chocolate they used tasted decent, and I particularly liked that there was a thick layer of milk foam on top. The orange juice was, in fact, fresh, and the oranges they used were sweet. The poached eggs were really good. They were runny, just as I liked them. The tarragon seasoning on top was really really really good. I like how well the plate came together with the avocados, the tomatoes and the mushrooms. I only have 1 complaint: when I got my main course, the mushrooms were a little cold while everything else on my plate (except the fresh avocado) was hot. Not sure whether that was intentional, but I would have preferred that the mushrooms were the same temperature as he other cooked ingredients on the plate. Nonetheless, that dish still tasted really good. I'd totally come back here.

I got the single cheeseburger, and I know there's a lot of hype to this restaurant and I believe it lived up to the hype. However, I wouldn't say it is the best burger I've ever had in NYC... nonetheless, I would say it's top 5! Would recommend the bacon as a topping, it was cooked perfectly and had a glaze to it that added a lot of taste. The fries and aioli sauce were delicious, as well. I would come back again for the burger!

Good food, intimate place. Pretty steep prices for the food you get. Their kubaneh and smoked eggplant carpaccio were really awesome. Also loved their branzino it lamb chops weren't that special unfortunately. I would go again but wouldn't get the lamb chops. Their suggested amount of food for two people is one type of bread, two dishes from the left side of menu and two dishes from the right side of menu

My friend and I opted to skip our usual coffee routine and instead snagged a slice at a no-frills, hole-in-the-wall pizzeria. I went with a Hawaiian slice, which was pretty standard fare but hit the spot just right. Service was commendably quick. A heads-up for card payers: there's a minimum charge of $7.00. The atmosphere was mostly quiet, adding to the laid-back experience. Plus, the staff was friendly, contributing to the pleasant visit.

Title: Quick Service and Tasty Bahn Mi with Room for More

My recent visit to this eatery for a pork bahn mi and a special bahn mi left me mostly satisfied. The service was impressively swift, with both sandwiches arriving posthaste. The flavors were quite enjoyable, capturing the essence of a good bahn mi. However, the sandwiches would have been even better with a more generous helping of paté and a bit more meat. Despite this, the overall experience was pleasing. Would recommend for a quick and tasty meal.

My friends and I decided to come here for dinner. I have not been to BCD tofu house in years. When we walked in, the hostess sat us down really quickly. In the past, there's would usually be a 15-30 minute wait. I ordered the mixed seafood tofu soup and beef and bulgogi. The waitress kept asking if I wanted glass noddles with my tofu soup but I kept saying no.  After ordering our food, the waitress starts us off with fried fish. However, there was three of us, she only gave us two. She said she was going to come back with one more but I guess she forgot about it. I feel like the portion of the food is less now compared to previous times I came here. The taste was different too. I asked for a little spice but there was no spicy flavor at all. There flavors were not the same anymore. The bulgogi was the start dish of the table. It was sweet and tangly. Just perfect. The manager came to every table and asked if everyone enjoyed their food. I thought it was really nice of him to do that.

- Small restaurant with cute decorations. They really put a lot of thought into creating a particular atmosphere- The food was REALLY good- The portion sizes are big so even one appetizer per person can fill you up - Service was lacking. We sat down and it took a while for them to give us the menus. We ordered drinks and food at the same time yet it took 30min just for the drinks to come out. - The food took another 10min- Don't come here if you're hungry and looking to get your food right away. - When we were ready to get the check, we couldn't find someone available to help us. It felt like we spent most of our time trying to get someone's attention.- Make sure to sit at the bar so you can be looked after better

Just okay, though the food was tasty.I don't really understand why a takeout shawarma pita is like $8.50 here and a sit-down pita (dine-in) is like $14.50, but okay. I was hungry for shawarma and had just arrived in the city - I found this place on Yelp.Service was abysmal - she didn't even bring me silverware, I had to ask. She started me off with hummus and pita, and then my chicken shawarma sandwich and side salad arrived.The food was excellent which is why this place gets 3 stars instead of 2 from me. The sandwich had a slightly spicy sauce on it and was great. They give you a small complimentary piece of baklava too but it wasn't that good (I recently had some Detroit area baklava which was way better, so that didn't help).On my receipt, they charged me 2 cents for a "rounding" fee, which is super sketchy. I wasn't going to argue over 2c but I'm curious about it.Probably would seek out a better place next time though I wouldn't be opposed to takeout.

**Restaurant Review: Route 66**

Despite initial plans to visit Upstairs at 66 for games, my friends and I ended up at the downstairs section of Route 66 due to a private event. The silver lining was their happy hour from 4-7 pm, where I enjoyed a generously poured house whiskey ginger that didn't disappoint.

The food, however, was a hit or miss. The Cracklin' Pork Clouds paired with green sauce were the highlight, while Sarah's smoked wings were too salty to enjoy fully. The Truffle Brussels were underwhelming, failing to live up to their "special" label, and the fries were sadly soggy and oily.

In summary, Route 66 might not be a foodie's destination, as Stone Street seems more tailored for drinks and socializing. Fingers crossed the game room upstairs is available for your visit!

Great place for a quick bite (and reasonably priced!) near Penn Station. We ordered two chicken gyros (one in a pita, one in a wrap) and the spinach feta rolls. The food came out quickly and tasted very fresh. The meat was nice and tender, not tough at all. The sauces were very good, especially the yogurt-based sauce. The service was exceptional. Even though it is a counter setup and not sit-down, they waited on our table and brought the food out. The workers were extremely friendly and hospitable. They brought us complimentary Turkish tea when we went in on a cold day. I will definitely be returning next time I have to go to Penn.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Carmine's

Our experience at Carmine's was a bit of a rollercoaster ride. Kudos to the staff and management for handling our group of 18 seamlessly, honoring our reservation promptly, and quickly rolling out our appetizers. The fried calamari deserves a special mention – it was the highlight of our meal, and the portions were incredibly generous.

The variety of main courses, from the penne alla vodka to the chicken marsala, chicken parmesan, vegan pasta, and shrimp scampi, were well-received by the group, although they could have benefited from a sprinkle more salt for enhanced seasoning.

Unfortunately, a sizeable cockroach made an unwelcome appearance during our dinner. While it's not uncommon in NYC to have such encounters, it significantly tainted our dining experience. Due to this incident, I am rating Carmine's 3 out of 5 stars - ample room for improvement in ensuring a more pleasant and hygienic environment.

Been to this location several times for dinner...usually with a big party for a birthday or holiday celebration. Easy location to get to as it's close to the train station. Overall service and staff were good... check in downstairs with the hostess (who was a bit rude the last time I came). Not the only ones she was rude to...customer service is important!Note: They don't seat incomplete parties so make sure every one shows up on time! Restaurant is spacious and portions are family style. Complimentary bread for startersAppetizers to share: baked clams, fried calamari, stuffed mushrooms, proscuitto and burrata  - deliciousEntrees: Chicken parm, eggplant parm, rigatoni ala vodka, penne with broccoli and garlic, linguini with white clam sauce, chicken francese, string beans, sausage and meatballs -- all were good... Make sure to leave room for desserts, which are family style too!Dessert: NY Cheesecake and strawberry shortcake to share! Great time had by all...We will be back!

I recently stumbled upon a hidden gem that offers an incredible deal: a 99¢ pizza slice that hit the spot perfectly. The pizza here is not only affordable but also deliciously satisfying, providing a hearty meal without breaking the bank. One of the best parts is the quick turnover rate, ensuring every slice is fresh from the oven. While it deviates from the typical thin crust found in NYC, the thicker base here was a delightful change that I thoroughly enjoyed. The seating is sparse, so it's tailored more for those looking to grab a quick bite on the go. If you're in need of a quick, warm meal that's easy on the wallet, this is the place to be.
Came back to get main courses, got spicy chicken country style, cumin lamb and spicy grilled fish. Really good for eating and sharing.

Title: A Delightful Lunch Experience at the New Neighborhood Eatery

I recently visited the new branch of a favorite restaurant, conveniently situated just around the corner from my workplace, on its soft opening day, 2/22. The experience thoroughly lived up to my expectations. The service during lunch was impeccable, with attentive staff who were both friendly and helpful. Dario, my server, was particularly warm and provided excellent drink recommendations, while Patrick, whose role I can't recall, was equally engaging.

As for the food, I opted for the ebi katsu as an appetizer, which came with a deliciously spicy sauce and perfectly light fried shrimp. The grilled duck ramen was my choice for the main course, featuring a nicely cooked duck leg and noodles that maintained an ideal texture throughout the meal. To accompany my food, I tried a lychee martini and the hightea—both were on the stronger side, but nonetheless enjoyable and a good value. I'm thrilled to have this establishment as a new lunch spot option and look forward to many more meals here.

I recently dined at a restaurant in Brookfield Plaza and was disappointed with my experience. I ordered the chicken wonton soup for $15, expecting a hearty dish, but received a mere five wontons. Considering the price point and the multitude of dining options available in the area, I found it overpriced and underwhelming. Unfortunately, I wouldn't recommend this place and don't see myself returning.

The side dishes concept is pretty gimmicky, but it's definitely worth a try! My cousin came here on a Sunday afternoon. Upon stepping in, I must say, the interior was nice and bright! There was plenty of warm air and yummy smells floating around, making this place perfect on a cold winter day. You order by marking what you want onto one menu. The servers were swift and helpful in explaining how everything works. It's a big plus if you know Mandarin! For appetizers, we got the Cold Glass Noodle ($5) and Salty Crispy Chicken ($6.50). After seeing both tables next to us order it, my cousin had to get the Cold Glass Noodle as well. They remind me of jellyfish but with rice noodle instead- it was just alright. The popcorn chicken was served with mayo. It tasted pretty good, but honestly, you could do without as the main course is already filling enough. My cousin got the Yunshang Rice Noodle Soup with Pork & Pickled Cabbage ($10) while I got the original ($9.50). You get the side dishes, noodles in a separate bowl, and the broth bowl itself so it's A LOT to put down on a small table. I have no idea what some of the side dishes were but I just dumped everything in the broth and it tasted super flavorful! My broth was more mild and creamy while my cousin's definitely had a kick to it, which I enjoyed better. The quality noodles definitely made the dish enjoyable. TIP: Your first soda is free! I thought I would be getting a can soda but they actually put it in a cup with a glass straw too! Overall, I had a great experience here. I would go back on another cold day, as the food here was perfect for that!

Title: A True Taste of India in the Heart of the City

I've found my top pick for Indian cuisine in the city—an authentic gem that mirrors the quality and taste of India's finest eateries. The crispy okra here is a revelation; so sublime in its crunch and flavor that the accompanying avocado becomes an afterthought. I left yearning for these okra chips to be packaged for takeaway—a sentiment sparked by a memorable experience in Jaipur.

The Nizam's Haleem is not to be missed, tender lamb slow-cooked to perfection, melding with a symphony of spices yet pleasantly mild in heat. Served with an assortment of about eight spices and condiments, it was an interactive feast, especially when tucked into buttered naan like a sandwich. The pickled ginger, mistaken for radish, was a standout among the condiments.

My meal concluded with the Frozen Cutting Chai, a perfect portion of handcrafted tea ice cream accompanied by whipped cream and toasted coconut—a delightful end to a culinary journey I can't wait to embark on again.

Title: Disappointment Follows a Once Pleasurable Experience

I ventured back to the restaurant on a chilly Saturday night, accompanied by friends A.L., B.K., and T.H., craving the warmth of a repeat stellar dining experience. Unfortunately, expectations crumbled faster than poorly prepared tofu.

Our order included two servings of tteuk mandoo guk, each bowl presenting adequately cooked rice cakes accompanied by slivers of beef and topped with fresh Asian chives. While the broth leaned towards the salty end of the spectrum, it remained acceptable. A.L.’s yukwe jjang, a normally delectable spicy braised beef soup, this time packed an extra punch, and the usually tender potatoes arrived undercooked.

The true letdown of the evening was my soondubu jiggae. As a previous admirer (and at-home chef) of this dish, the difference in quality was unmistakable. The soft tofu, which should delicately melt away in your mouth, was egregiously overcooked and had disintegrated into the broth, leading to a truly unsatisfying texture. When confronted, our server offered an unconvincing explanation of "expensive specialty tofu," but my prior experience and culinary expertise led me to see through this guise.

To add insult to injury, the service plummeted post-complaint. Staff avoided our table, offering neither water refills nor the courtesy of checking on our satisfaction.

The stark contrast between my previous 4-star praise and today’s experience has left me with no choice but to award 2 stars. Misrepresenting a dish and neglecting customers post-complaint are not practices that I can overlook or forgive.

Regrettably, this establishment has lost a patron; the attached comparison photos of the soondubu from 10/23/19 and 11/9/19 should illustrate why.

Title: A Delightful Lunch Experience at Ippudo

My friends and I recently visited Ippudo for an early lunch and were greeted with a perfectly ambient atmosphere. The lighting was balanced and we could comfortably converse without any intrusive noise, likely due to the restaurant being less crowded at around 11:30 am.

The staff at Ippudo were exceptionally friendly and attentive, readily assisting us with our queries about the menu. A highlight of our visit was discovering the lunch special (available from 11 am to 3 pm), which offered an additional rice bowl with a choice of meat for a mere $3 with any ramen purchase. My friend and I opted to share the Akamaru Shinaji ramen and a spicy fried chicken rice bowl, both of which were delightful and adequately portioned.

The rice bowl impressed us with its harmonious blend of rice, mayo, and chicken, leaving no excess rice behind. As for the ramen, the noodles had just the right texture, and the broth's richer saltiness was suited to my palate.

I wholeheartedly recommend Ippudo and am eager to return for the much-acclaimed pork buns. Whether you're a ramen enthusiast or a casual diner, Ippudo is sure to satisfy.

I recently visited a local spot renowned for its inventive pies and decided to try the much-talked-about crab slice. True to other reviews, the sauce was delightfully creamy, brimming with a generous sprinkling of crab. It's a rarity to come across crab pizzas, so this was a pleasant divergence from the norm.

What truly captivated me was the crust – despite the thickness that usually predicates a doughy bottom, I was met with an impeccable crunch that paid homage to the revered New York slice. It's an unusual offering that won't become my go-to, but its uniqueness ensures I'll be returning for the occasional indulgence.

Title: A Brunch to Remember at Vic's

After a hiatus of over five years, I revisited Vic's for a family brunch during the festive season, and it was as delightful as I remembered. The egg and fontina sandwich I ordered was scrumptious, but it was the carrots with capers that stole the show, transporting my taste buds straight to flavortown. While there was a hiccup with my salad, the staff handled it gracefully by removing the charge from my bill, a gesture of customer service that didn't go unnoticed.

A word of advice for those planning to dine with a larger party: the acoustics in the restaurant could use some improvement, making it a challenge to engage in conversation with everyone at the table.

Despite that, Vic's has rekindled my fondness for their kitchen's creations, especially those phenomenal carrots, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

A proper NY Slice with proper NY fold. Best by the slice place in the City. Most by the slice places in NYC are not very good anymore. Joe's reminds me of the pizza I grew up with in Brooklyn. Good stuff.

Horrible employees. We will not be back. We have a small company that spends a few thousand dollars a week on lunch for our employees and we used to come here 2-3 times a month. The employees here are rude and unhelpful. One of them spilled one of our lunches in the bag and did nothing besides tell us to "be careful."When we asked for extra green sauce they flat out told us "no, only 1 per customer." The portions have gone down significantly and the chicken I had was dry and tasteless. On top of that, the people that work here are a bunch of useless idiots. One of them yelled at us to hurry up and pay while we were still waiting for our last plate to be made. After we paid, they realized they didn't charge us for the last one and ended up wasting even more time.

Title: Birthday Brunch Bash with Room for Improvement

My friends and I decided to celebrate my birthday at this trendy spot on a bustling Saturday afternoon. The setting was ideal for our lively group of 20, complete with energetic music and a youthful vibe. Opting for the bottomless food and drink package seemed like a no-brainer for such an occasion.

Our server, Edwardo, was the star of the show – his attentive service ensured our glasses were never empty, which is a rarity at many bottomless brunches. While the tapas-style offerings were decent, they weren't particularly memorable. The main issue was the pacing; dishes arrived sluggishly, struggling to keep up with the appetites of our large party. Despite this, Edwardo was apologetic and remained diligent throughout our experience.

In summary, while the atmosphere and service were on point, the food could use a speed boost to match the otherwise vibrant energy of a group celebration.

Title: A Delightful Turnaround at The Jin

After an initial visit to The Jin left much to be desired with an excessively breaded katsu, I approached my second foray with caution. To my delight, the experience was a culinary redemption. Their Korean Fried Chicken wings hit the mark with a perfect crispy crunch; the Soy Garlic flavor was a savory treat, and I look forward to sampling the Spicy and Original next time.

Moving on to the Bulgogi Japchae, it was a testament to the notion that simplicity perfected is a craft in itself. The noodles had an appetizing al dente texture, and the addition of spinach gave the dish an enjoyable twist. The pork belly dishes, paired with corn cheese and kimchi, were succulent and satisfying.

A special shoutout to the Pineapple Tok Tok cocktail - a fruity concoction so smooth, the alcohol was almost an afterthought. It's a must-try for those who prefer their spirits sweet and subtle.

In summary, The Jin has demonstrated that it has the chops to be a strong contender in NYC's Korean dining scene. Highly recommend giving it a try for the fried chicken, japchae, and a surprise hit cocktail.

Rating: 4.5/5

Came here on a Tuesday night and it was completely packed! View was great. Cocktail was so so, overly sweeten. But really surprised on the food here. We only ordered Kale and Calamari, which were perfect combo. The Kale was really light on dressing (some people may not like) but we enjoyed a lot and good portion. The Fried Calamari was on the contrary fatty but very delicious. Love the dipping sauce came with it very flavorful. Healthy + Unhealthy together for perfect late night snacks

Title: A Mixed Bag at a Charming NYC Taiwanese Spot

As an avid lover of Taiwanese cuisine, my expectations were high when I stepped into the latest Taiwanese restaurant to grace NYC. With its adorable interior, complete with Drake-inspired lights, the ambiance was immediately welcoming. The service matched the setting, with a staff that was genuinely friendly and attentive.

I was taken aback by the prices, which were significantly steeper than what you'd find in Flushing or Chinatown, but was pleased to discover that at least some of the dishes justified the cost. The pork soup dumplings, for instance, were exceptional. Easily the star of the meal, they surpassed any I've tasted in the city. The shu mai, adorned with fish roe, was another standout, offering a harmonious blend of pork and shrimp that was both fresh and flavorful.

The angry pig feet, while popular among my friends, missed the mark for me. The preparation had the right amount of spice, but the failure to remove the hairs from the skin was off-putting. Disappointment followed with the Taiwanese beef noodle soup, which was lackluster and dominated by an overpowering chili oil taste that resembled hot water more than a rich broth. The beef, though tender, was awkwardly large for the dish.

In summary, while some dishes like the dumplings and shu mai are worth a visit, others are forgettable. This eatery is a hit-or-miss that requires selective ordering. Would I return? Perhaps for the dumplings, but I'll be giving the noodle soup a hard pass.

As someone who loves cheese, this place was absolute heaven. Went with one other person and we split the Croque Monsieur for an appetizer and I got the burger with smoked cheese and the other person got the Mac and cheese. Note that the Mac and cheese doesn't come with table side scraped cheese. I would highly recommend all of these dishes, but honestly didn't need to split the Croque Monsieur to start since we had so much food. The entrees are big portions so we each took home our leftovers. The restaurant is small  with the tables very close together. It can get a little loud and hard to hear during peak dinner time. I would definitely make a reservation ahead of time!

The things I could say about Delizia. I am no big pizza fan. Yes, I'm a native. No, I'm not a vegan. It's just not one of my top food groups. My significant other on the other hand would set his life on the line for this place.After weeks of talking about how amazing this place is, he dragged me over for dinner. I gotta admit it's pretty tasty. Around the corner from his apt, we tend to pop in after bar crawls at all hours in the night. 6pm, 10pm, 2am. The guys are always jolly and serving up fresh slices.It's been over 5 months and there some slices I haven't tried yet. They make new types from time to time. I will say, if you want it hot af -- def tell them "Hot and Crispy" And avoid the chicken slice, they're a bit bry. BBQ chicken tho....heaven in a slice.It's a great joint.

Minca is a cozy, cute little ramen shop that serves delicious food, suitable for the young and old. I say this because I dined in with my family and my little one (LO) loved the dumplings ... LOVED. Actually, I don't mean to call myself old, as I am NOT old, but I am sure an older person would adore this spot as well. My other half and I enjoyed the ramen and the leftover scraps of dumpling that our LO left us. Likewise, our LO loved the leftover ramen we left her, continuously asking for more. The location is sort of out of the way for us, but we'd stop by again if we were in the hood.

Dear carnivores,Please note. This is an excellent place for meaty meat consumption. If you are a veggie fan you will need to stick to the sides. Keep in mind they will be delicious. I thoroughly enjoyed the japchae which is vegetarian based.We had three meats including classic galbi and pork belly and tongue. Don't get the tongue it's not the same. The galbi and pork belly are decent. They don't give you rice automatically but I'm not that into rice. I proficiently ate this meat enough to raise my body temperature at an almost meat sweat level. They do have exhaust fans in place for the Korean BBQ scent but it ends up on your clothes a bit. That's what you accept when your food is cooked right in front of you. And yes you don't have to cook it at all. I mean I tried and they just were like, girl no, and took away the tongs to cook the meat. They cook it and cut it up for you while you enjoy the grill smells.Enjoy the heat,Your beef loving Yelper Mer

I have tried the classic poke and pork buns here.  The poke was decent and comparable to other poke places in the area.  The fish tasted fresh and there are a multitude of toppings you can add to the bowl.  The pork buns were fine.  It's not the best pork buns I've ever had, but it wasn't bad either.  Unlike most other poke places around, Oki also offers hot/cold appetizers, ramen, and donburi's.  Next time I go I will try some of their other menu items.

It's always been a personal opinion of mine that everyone needs to have a good go to "Chinese food" place.  I came to Pig Heaven for dinner on a Friday night, and from the moment I walked in to the minute I left, the staff was spectacular - from the warm hellos that the hostesses greeted me with, to the hands on GM, and the wait staff, my experience here was stellar.  Not only was the entire wait staff knowledgeable with the menu (extra bonus points for their recommendations that were on point), our water glasses were always filled without having to ask for more water, and our plates were changed out without even needed to ask between courses.  Additionally, even the bartender came over during our meal to see make sure the drinks we had ordered were ok.  How often, if ever, does that happen especially at your local eateries?If this service staff doesn't say anything about Pig Heaven, then let me tell you about the food.  Those ribs I mentioned before - OMG they are delicious.  I can't remember the last time I had spare ribs that were not only tasty, but also tender and could be bitten right off the bone with ease.  I can see how these are a must have!  In addition to the ribs, my party also ordered the Chicken Soong (chicken lettuce wraps) as an appetizer as well as the Hotpot Fish w/ Mixed Vegetables.  The Chicken Soong was crisp/cool and delightfully spicy (avoid the red peppers if you can't take the heat) and exactly what you need on a warm summer day.  The Hotpot Fish is a newer addition to the Pig Heaven menu and it has all the right elements of Szechuan flavor - from that distinct taste of the Chinese peppercorn to all those yummy asian veggies, I loved this dish!  The fish was light, tender, and boneless (which was my favorite part) and tasted so yummy with my bowl of rice.  The new Pig Heaven menu is now a lovely hybrid of Canton and Szechuan flavors, and because of this I can honestly say that there will be something for everyone in your party.  Additionally, the portions here are generous, so come hungry!  Whether it's for take out, delivery, or to dine in - Pig Heaven is a great place to call your own if you can.
