This has been one of my bookmarks for about 80 years or so, give or take a few years.No line or crowd whatsoever on a cold December day at lunchtime.  A few of NYPD's finest bought some soup getting ready for New Year's Eve.I went with the jambalaya (small size) and it came with a banana and nice fresh roll.  The small was actually good-sized and perfect for one person.  With the fruit and roll, that's a good deal, especially so in New York where a bagel might cost you $45 in some places.The soup itself was hot, loaded with sausage, had a good amount of heat, and was delicious.No sign of the "Original Soupman," of course, but I believe he's long gone, at least from the stores.  Interesting signage (see the pic).Obviously, the place has novelty value but I thought the soup was excellent and a great value.

Nice little hole in the wall. Nice but loud , typical Irish pub. Large beer selection and reasonable prices. We got the burgers and they came out so fast. They were cooked perfectly and tasted great. Worth walking off the beaten patch to enjoy

With the amount of Chinese restaurants in the area, Jing Fong just doesn't really compare. I was here with a group of 5 for Chinese New Year dinner and just didn't have a great experience.  We ordered seafood soup, sweet and sour pork chops, dou miao (pea shoots), half a peking duck, clams, and a seafood bowl. I enjoyed the seafood soup/dishes for the most part. The pork chops and veggies were okay, but definitely have had better. My biggest issue may have been with the server himself. We asked him for more vinegar for the soup (he gave us a small little dish to begin with to share with 5 people) and gave us a bit of an attitude. We then asked for more sauce for the peking duck as well because same thing, we only received a small little dish, and he flat out told us no... that we already have enough sauce and it's limited to one a table.... Okay. The worst part of it all was when he actually attempted to cut our peking duck. He was clearly struggling and cut off what he could (mostly just skin), and told us that he was going to bring it back into the kitchen and have the chefs cut the rest. Well he never came back with it............ If you look at the photo, you can see just how little it was. Towards the end of the meal, we asked him where the rest of the duck was. He went back to the kitchen to check and finally brought out the rest. For almost $300 on this meal (with some beers and tip/tax), it's definitely a no go for me.

Title: A Delightful Solo Lunch at Sugarfish

I finally had the chance to dine at the much-raved-about Sugarfish for a solo lunch on a bustling Friday afternoon. Although I was initially 13th in line for a seat at the bar around 1:30 pm, the wait was worthwhile.

The ambiance of the restaurant was welcoming with its minimalist wooden decor, complementing the premium sushi dining experience they're known for. I opted for the "Trust Me" menu with an added Anago sushi—after all, what's a sushi meal without eel?

True to its reputation, Sugarfish did not disappoint. The sushi was exquisite, with each piece melting in my mouth, packed with natural flavors that made additional soy sauce unnecessary. The staff's friendliness and efficiency heightened the experience, offering clear explanations and personal engagement.

Though the price is on the higher end, the quality of the sushi justifies every penny. Sugarfish has set a new bar for my sushi standards, ensuring that I'll be returning in the future.

I visited a charming yet cozy restaurant recently. Its appealing aesthetic was complemented by high ceilings and stylish decor, which provided a pleasant dining atmosphere. However, the space felt cramped as tables and chairs were packed tightly, with little room to navigate. The food, while not particularly exceptional, was decent. Overall, the experience was mixed, with the ambiance outshining the culinary offerings.

Definitely worth the wait.For my group of four that Saturday night, it was about 50 minutes.When we entered, the hostess quickly approached us to help us put our names into the system. She took my name and number and gave me a rough estimate of 45 min to an one hour.To kill the time, we decided to hang out at the Thursday Kitchen outpost location right next door. Once we returned to get seated, we had the option to hang our coat or go straight to our booth and settle there. Immediately after being seated we were given menus and water. The table and table setting was clean and organized for us by their staff, who were all efficient and friendly throughout the night.We all reviewed the menu and agreed that the options all looked very appetizing and that there were enough options. Because we were celebrating the fact one of my friends in the group just returned to NYC, we decided to order a few of the appetizers to share. Our food and drink orders all came out relatively quickly. The Chamame and Karaage were my personal favorites amongs the small dishes. Each element of the TONKOTSU CHASHU TSUKEMEN left me wanting more. The egg and pieces of chasu were all perfectly soft and tasty. The dipping ramen had a beautiful garlicky flavor to it that I've never had anywhere else. Overall fun time with great service and food. Certainly would enjoy coming back to this location.

Title: Mixed Impressions at a New York Diner

My dining experience began with anticipation as I ordered the lemon ricotta pancakes, which unfortunately fell short of expectations. They arrived heavy and dry, prompting a return. The waiter indicated that they were gluten-free, a detail that was subtly noted on the menu. This oversight on my part might explain the texture, but I believe the option for gluten should remain a choice rather than a default.

Moving past the pancakes, we opted for two sandwiches: a turkey, avocado, and pepper jack, as well as a grilled chicken with gruyere. Both were delectable and redeemed the meal, boasting excellent flavors and quality ingredients.

However, the dilemma of rating the restaurant loomed, torn between the quality sandwiches and the initial disappointment. Ultimately, the high price point of approximately $20 per dish, despite being in New York City, influenced my decision. I settled on a 3 out of 5, as the sandwiches alone couldn't completely overshadow the earlier misstep and steep prices.

3 stars compared to all diners I have ever been.Food is ok, but prices are just too expensive. Then, wait is the point of going to a diner?Service was just ok.Ordered 2 dishes+small cup of warm milk: ~$50+tip

Title: A Gastronomic Gem with a Side of Repetitive Entertainment

I recently dined at a local restaurant that truly impressed me with its culinary offerings. I arrived just in time to indulge in their Happy Hour specials and decided to try a Chinese beer, which turned out to be delightfully refreshing. The highlight of my meal was undoubtedly the Pork Bao; a dish so perfectly prepared it seemed to dissolve effortlessly on my palate.

However, I must admit that the ambiance was slightly marred by the repetitive video looping on all five TV screens. The 5-minute clip played incessantly throughout my visit, which became a test of my patience.

Despite the modest size of the space and the less-than-entertaining visual aspect, the food experience alone merits a return visit. I'm already looking forward to my next meal here, especially the highly praised Noodles with beef bone marrow. This spot may not be perfect, but for food lovers, it's a must-try. Three stars for now, with hopes for a more varied entertainment selection in the future.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Little Tong, where the concise menu mirrors its sister locations. Drawn to the unique offering of Cifangao, I opted for the variety pack featuring all three fillings: Bacon, egg, cheese; Ragout, meigancai; and butternut squash with soy. At $10 for two small squares of each type, the value was exceptional.

Each Cifangao was deliciously savory with a delightful crunch that defied choosing a favorite. Little Tong's menu still holds unexplored treasures for me, and considering The Deco hosts eight other vendors, future visits promise the joy of culinary mix-and-match. An experience that's undeniably worthy of a return visit.

Located in the Brookfield Place's Hudson Eats food court, this place is super convenient to get to for those working near the World Trade Center. On weekday lunches, their line is one of the shorter ones in the food court, and their service is extremely quick.Ordered a beef noodle soup for lunch. For $15, you get a good amount of beef, a meh-amount of noodles, and maybe a tablespoon of vegetables. the beef was not bad, but the noodles were definitely overcooked and I wished they had included more vegetables. It did come out quickly, and I would come back here if I needed a quick noodle soup fix.

I'm a perennial fan of Spot Dessert Bar, a place where my sweet tooth is never satisfied with just one treat. On my latest visit, I indulged in no less than three desserts, plus a pair of their irresistible cookies. To accompany the confections, I sipped on an iced latte that truly hit the spot, albeit a tad too milky – a note to self to customize my order next time.

The highlight, as always, was their divine matcha lava cake, an absolute must-try for matcha enthusiasts. The matcha cookie was equally delightful, with a perfect balance of sweetness and that distinct green tea flavor. A pleasant surprise was the cookie skillet, a newfound love in my dessert repertoire. It's safe to say, the cookie skillet has earned a permanent spot on my order list for future visits. Spot Dessert Bar remains a top-tier dessert destination that never disappoints.

Title: A Cozy Retreat Despite the Wait

I ventured into this Michelin-starred restaurant at 6:30pm on a bleak Sunday evening. The cold, rainy weather was somewhat checked by a heavy curtain at the entrance, although a persistent draft managed to follow us to our seats. The 45-minute wait predicted by the waitress turned out to be a more bearable 30 minutes, although we still hovered momentarily upon our return before being allocated a snug round high table by the bar.

Our coats found a home on a nearby rack, and soon after, our culinary journey commenced. The cucumber kimchi opened the show, presenting a decently fresh mixture of sweet, spicy, and tangy flavors, though it didn't particularly stand out. The squid with nuts followed, coupling tender seafood with the satisfying crunch of lightly salted, roasted nuts, all enhanced by a side of gochujang sauce. The fried chicken, arriving in a quartet of lightly breaded pieces, was a textural delight, especially when accented with a squeeze of lime and creamy gochujang sauce. 

A 20-minute interlude preceded the arrival of our noodles. The Miyuk Ramyum, a vegetarian option, shone with its perfectly cooked strands crowned with garlic, chives, and mushrooms—an absolute treat. The squid with nuts was tender and flavorful, reaffirming its earlier success. The Gochu Ramyum and So Ramen both arrived with commendations from our palates, and the option for extra noodles at a mere $2 was a boon for my friend's hearty appetite.

Admittedly, my expectations for my first Michelin Star experience were sky-high. Although I couldn't label the offerings as phenomenal, they were undeniably good. This restaurant provided a comforting sanctuary from the inclement weather and left us feeling satisfied, if not completely wowed.

Title: A Rare Gem: L'Artusi Review

L'Artusi stands out as a pinnacle of Italian dining in NYC, tantalizing the taste buds with each visit. Scoring a reservation during peak times may require patience and a bit of luck, but the gastronomic rewards are well worth the effort.

Over several visits, sampling a wide array of their ever-changing menu allowed for a thorough appreciation of their culinary craft. The ambiance exudes warmth and sophistication, matched by impeccable service that enhances the dining experience.

The true stars, however, are the pastas. Their simplicity belies the high-quality ingredients and meticulous preparation, resulting in dishes that are flavorful without being overwhelming—a testament to the kitchen's prowess.

A must-try is their olive oil cake, a consistent showstopper. Its delicate texture and perfect balance of sweetness, paired with cream cheese and grapes, create an unforgettable dessert that tempts one to indulge in seconds.

In conclusion, L'Artusi is an essential visit for Italian cuisine aficionados. Despite the challenging reservations, it unequivocally merits a place on your dining bucket list.

This is the restaurant in The Edition Hotel.  The first morning we ate here it was okay. The pancakes were really good.  Just our food was cold... like the butter wouldn't melt (at all) in the oatmeal.  That's pretty cold.  The next morning it went from cold to worse.  They poured our coffee and didn't come back for TWENTY minutes with the cream.  It was kind of cold at that point. Give me a break.  The waiter had such an attitude.  Like sorry I want SLIGHTLY warm coffee. Dare to dream!

Title: Au Cheval NYC - A Windy City Wonder Arrives in the Big Apple

As a Chicagoan at heart, I approached the newly opened Au Cheval in NYC with high hopes—and I'm thrilled to report that it surpassed all expectations. This establishment has set the bar high in Chicago by serving what many deem the best burger in America, and lucky for New Yorkers, the magic has not been lost in transit.

Stepping into the restaurant on opening day, I was struck by the sense of space—an upgrade from its Chicago counterpart. The simplicity of the décor mirrors the menu's approach to the classic American burger; no unnecessary frills, just exceptionally well-executed favorites.

The signature "single" burger—which is a misnomer, as it comes with two patties—is a must-try. This dish is a tribute to traditional backyard barbecues with its perfect medium-rare cook and mouth-watering flavor. Burger enthusiasts can take it up a notch by adding a fried egg. As for the fries, which I've found hit-or-miss in Chicago, the NYC outlet has outdone itself. They arrived excellently fried, well-seasoned, and accompanied by a flawless aioli.

For a decadent treat, the bone marrow is non-negotiable. Rich, indulgent, and perfect for sharing, it's a side that confidently struts its stuff as an appetizer. Pair your meal with a visit to the on-site Sawada coffee bar, where latte aficionados can indulge in the unique military or black camo lattes; the former a blend of matcha and espresso, the latter a mix of roasted green tea and espresso—both executed with flair and finesse.

Service was nothing short of excellent. Attentive waitstaff ensured a seamless dining experience, even amidst the lunch rush of opening day.

In sum, Au Cheval NYC is a delightful homage to its Chicago roots, with a flavor that resonates with the heart of American cuisine. Here's hoping it remains one of the city's best-kept secrets, allowing us burger and bone marrow aficionados to relish in its offerings without the legendary Windy City wait.

Roll me up in rose petals, chandeliers and bite size tacos, tostadas and guac.  Cause if you seek the sexy side of sexy-Mexy, this hidden gem won't be unknown for long.So do you like me, and make your OpenTable reservation for a weeknight where you can enjoy the ambience before it gets extremely loud, which the space can get due to the tile floors and metal ceilings.  Let them pamper you from the moment you walk in down the small hallway with bouquets of roses along the floor and romantic candlelight getting you in the mood for something sexy special and spicy.With a rez made on Open Table, I came in with my man friend on a recent rainy Tuesday night and were immediately attended to in that perfect blend of maître d' and "we really want you here!" vibe.  Just a few guys on duty but they seamlessly wrangled coats, umbrellas and seating.  It was a fun lead up to the plush seating along the walls.We took a seat at one of the side booths that have chairs facing across them. Both seating size whether the chair or the booth were cozy comfy. The menu is brief, see my attached photo, but every damn thing we tried was stupendous!! First of all yes you must start with the guacamole. I am a bit of a wussy puss when it comes spice, so we had the least spicy flavor. Be careful, it comes with the onion sprinkled on top which you may want to ask on the side.Quite delightful were the three small tuna tostadas. The balance of flavors was unusual yet perfectly acidic creamy and meaty. Three seems so small when I saw it but it was strangely filling due to rich taste. All that umami!  My compatriot preferred the shrimp tacos, but for me they were a little bit average. I think it's a flavor point issue. But definitely at the price of under $17 for each of our plates, no complaining there!My dining companion is a big drinker and had three large Woodfords on the rock, which I think is why, when we let slip by accident that it was my birthday, which truthfully had been a couple days before but this was finally our birthday dinner together, it was a delightful surprise that when we ordered the chocolate mousse (stupendous and not a blob of wet sticky shit but a perfectly molded mousse... cake?... ) it came with a ROMAN CANDLE! Omg.  Yes I was sufficiently embarrassed, but the extremely sweet bartender, Ivan, came over and gave a thorough explanation of the aged mescal shot that he provided for my friend, and a non-alcoholic shot for me. In fact my friend was so enthralled with the complexity of the flavor of the mescal that he and Ivan ended up having a good 15 minute conversation, which then led to some further sampling.  I realize that we were fortunate that it was a slow night but that kind of intimate tableside service, where we had so much explained us, made us enchanted and wanted to come back more not only to drink this delicious new not cheap beverage that we had been introduced to (mescal can get $$$!) but to be around these people who are so passionate about their food and beverage.  That was the kicker!Passion is a rare thing in the Manhattan restaurant scene. Status and social climbing tend to take the place. That's why I felt a real special experience here and want to come back and enjoy it over and over again.  The romantic expression in neon by the shared baths (3) was adorbs, too ;)TL/dr New secret sexy mex joint tears the wrapping pf traditional Mex food and swaddles it in tasty new spice, portion and quality to make a delightful dining and holistic night out, on the right evening!

First thing you notice when you come into this Shanhainese restaurant...it's relatively fancy and not like your traditional chinese restaurant. No surprise...the dishes are consequently a bit more expensive. The prices listed are all if you pay in cash, and if you don't they charge 4% more, but they will also round up in the receipt (a little distasteful if you ask me).The food. We got the pork soup dumplings + pan fried pork buns + crispy eel + a pork soup. The total bill for this was $60 and we weren't full fwiw. So....not great there.My favorite was the soup dumplings. They were amazing. Really enjoyed it, I think there were 6 in the order. Skin not too thin, came out perfect temperature (although some people want to probably burn their tongues as a right of passage), soupy, and very fatty/juicy pork.The crispy eel was something that was surprising good too. It was deep fried with some sweet and sour sauce on it. Great appetizer to just crunch on (although this came out AFTER all our other dishes).The pork soup felt homey, nothing too special about it, not a lot of meat by any means. Relatively expensive for what it was (bowl is enough for two people).The pork buns...looked promising, but the inside just wasn't soupy. Very disappointed there, still on the lookout for some good sheng jian bao's. I'd only come here for soup dumplings, and even that, I'm sure there are better places in NY for them.

Went here on a Saturday night and it was a good time. Even though I showed up earlier than my party and had to wait 45 minutes for them to arrive, I had no problem finding a table and having a few drinks while waiting for everyone else to arrive. Between the staff and the other customers that were there, everyone was so friendly. They did not make me feel like I was by myself. So between the drinks and the food, (and eventually my friends) I had a great time here and look forward to coming back to this place.

We stumbled in here on a Saturday night and were informed they were closing an hour early than they normally do, which meant we had a half hour to order eat. We were famished so we took the opportunity, placed our orders right away and we're happy to have the food come out promptly. We never want to 'those people' who linger after closing time, but we were caught off guard by their choice to close early. Fortunately for all involved, we ate quick and we're paying our bill by the time they were looking to close.I ordered the chicken club without mayo and it was pretty good, I liked the crispness of the bread. It made ordering something carb-heavy worth it. I definitely suggest if you don't do mayo, to get some kind of dipping option or dressing. It's a bit dry without it. The waiter didn't come up to us after bringing our food otherwise I would have asked for a bottle of hot sauce. Never fail with hot sauce.The restaurant is well lit, well designed and spacious. The decor is modern and has some Instagrammable spots. Just sayin if we had more time we probably would have been *those* people

Title: Delightful Takeout Experience at La Shuk Restaurant

I recently had the pleasure of ordering takeout from La Shuk Restaurant on the Upper East Side, and I must say, it was a fantastic decision. The process was a breeze using Yelp and Grubhub, complete with the convenience of adding special instructions for both my order and delivery.

Not only was the menu user-friendly, but the prices were reasonable as well. For instance, the Vegetable Couscous was $12 and customizable with additional meat options for a small fee—$15 with grilled chicken or $16 with kofta kebabs. My sister-in-law savored her Half Grilled Chicken, boasting generous portions and vibrant flavors enhanced by the signature dipping sauce. As for me, the Chicken Shish Kebab Platter hit all the right notes with its seasoned grilled chicken, perfectly cooked basmati rice, and an array of fresh salads including a delightful pickled beet salad.

The Beef Cigars were a highlight—crispy phyllo pastry enveloping savory ground sirloin, elevated by that delicious spicy signature sauce. Every dish showcased the restaurant's commitment to fresh, healthy ingredients.

Our order arrived earlier than anticipated, and the delivery was seamless with a very pleasant delivery person. My takeaway experience from La Shuk was top-notch, and I'd recommend it to anyone craving Moroccan cuisine, whether for takeout or dine-in. Next time, I'm eager to try their lamb dishes!

Title: A Tranquil Omakase Experience at Neta

During a spontaneous pre-move visit to New York, I stumbled upon the gem that is Neta, a sushi bar offering a delightful lunch omakase - a rare find in the city's bustling sushi scene. 

Pros:
- The fish couldn't have been fresher, with each slice boasting top-notch quality.
- Opting for a late lunch on a weekday meant having the cozy ambiance all to myself - a solo diner's dream.
- Service was impeccable; attentive without being intrusive, ensuring my glass was perpetually filled.

The standout was the generously portioned Uni - a true testament to Neta's commitment to excellence.

Cons:
- Truly, none.

Neta is now on my must-return list, especially for those quiet weekday afternoons. Living in New York just got even better with these culinary treasures within reach.

Had a delightful breakfast at this gem of a spot! I opted for the two eggs with bacon, gluten-free toast, and potato hash - a feast that did not disappoint. The place prides itself on its inclusive menu, offering nearly everything gluten-free. Although dairy-free options limited my choices, I was able to indulge in the potato hash made with ghee, which I can tolerate, and it was a savory delight. Adding the house jam to the meal was a stroke of brilliance; it was simply fantastic. The portion sizes were generous, leaving me more than satisfied.

My husband chose the chicken and waffles, a gluten-free staple of the house, and he had nothing but rave reviews for his dish. It's worth noting for those with dairy sensitivities that this option contains buttermilk. Nonetheless, our experience was top-notch – delicious food that catered to our dietary needs without sacrificing flavor or satisfaction. A must-visit for anyone craving a hearty, inclusive breakfast experience!

This place has been on my list for quite some time and I have been wanting to try it because they have vegan nuggets. I ordered the Vegan Buffalo wings and Vegan Tso Swag wings. I ordered 3 pieces of each and it came out to be like $14.. It was good, tender on the inside and crispy on the inside but it's very overpriced. The size of the nuggets are small. The cashier also recommended the blue cheese dip with the Tso Swag which was an interesting mix to me. Another thing I noticed is that they have enough space to add more stools so not as many have to stand. I luckily went at a time where it wasn't too big of a line or crowded but I can see how it would get annoying if it was crowded.

Took my husband here for our annual Christmas dinner and we were both blown away. The restaurant has a beautiful dining room, consisting of tables and some booths. We were seated in the booth section, and were brought drinks menus and water immediately. We settled on the seasonal tasting menu, which lay in the mid-range of prices at $155, between the prix fixe, and the longer tasting menu. The menu contained one meat dish (pork), which I asked them to adjust to a pescatarian dish, which they happily accommodated. The tasting menu then consisted of 5 courses, with additional little things thrown in. Everything was presented beautifully, and we really appreciated the little complimentary things that came out. All dishes were sensational, and I loved the chocolate tray that came at the end, in addition to the dessert. They also gave us little bags of breakfast bread to take home. Utterly delightful, and would love to return. Highly recommend for a splurge dinner, or just because.

Wow. I am not a brunch fan, but I was so glad that my friend picked this place for us to rendezvous after church.  It's a little bit difficult to find as it's behind the lobby of a hotel, but the entrance is that of a little theatre, as a little clue to future clients reading this post.One of the things that I love is the skylit center row of tables.  It creates absolutely the perfect lighting for photos and for food.  Everything is so beautiful, you don't even want to eat it.  Things that we shared included:Eggs Shukshuka:PROS:- served hot in a little warm iron skillet- slices of fresh bread: not stale or cold, super soft and fluffyCONS:- noneOlive Oil PancakesPROS: - super fluffy and warm- olive oil flavor was just light enough to create a slight difference from a normal pancake but it was not overwhelming in flavor- lightly sauteed bananas added a mild sweetness to the savory olive oil flavorCONS: - none (minus the drippy syrup: container was not the best for pouring)Definitely would come here again.  It'd be a great spot for a bridal shower if you could book the center table.

My boyfriend and I came in on a Monday night around 6:30pm and were seated immediately. This place is very unique, since I've never had a mala dry pot before! I ordered a bowl with sliced eye of round, lotus root, wood ear mushroom, and mustard greens and got my dish spicy. My boyfriend ordered pork, frog, fish fillet, and bok choy. We left the restaurant extremelyyy stuffed! I think we made the mistake of ordering individual 4 ingredient bowls, when we really should've ordered one 6-7 ingredient bowl to share. That would've also saved us some money. The portions here are huge! The quality of the food is great, but the dish was a bit too salty for my taste. I had to keep pairing my dry pot with rice which made me even fuller. Overall, this place is worth a visit but be prepared to spend a bit of money.

For today's lunch, I got the slice fish with vegetables.  It is just ok, with a fishy taste not from real fish.  And the wonton soup is sad with nothing but two wontons that don't really taste that good.  I have a friend who goes to Chinatown for wonton soup when she's feeling down.  Well, after this wonton soup, she'll be sadder than ever.  However,  my lunch was saved by a nice container of the chicken corn soup, which is so amazing, just like my grandma used to make, but she definitely used real chicken.  Stick with the corn soup!

Decent bar to watch premier league games at. Downstairs got super crowded for the Chelsea game. There were tons of people standing. In the little alcove area behind the flags they were showing another Italian game, with only one other Tv showing the Chelsea game in that section. I have not tried the food so can't comment on that

Brussel sprouts Brussel sprouts!!! I can give this place 5 stars just for brussel sprouts! I have heard many good things about this place from friends and finally one day I thought I will give it a try and not I was not disappointed. I was bored of eating at sweetgreen everyday and was looking for some healthier alternative and I landed here. This place is a much higher quality of DigInn or little beet. The way it works is you choose a base first which is either quinoa or rice, then choose 3 veggies that is when you choose 3 potions of brussel sprouts..lol (kidding but may be not.. lol) , the dips if you are lucky enough you will find spicy hummus which is delicious, Persian eggplant and cucumber or spinach yogurt so so good, then you proceed towards choosing your skewer which can be any of the meat options or for vegetarians tofu and at the counter ask them to give you hot sauce on the side. That's it!!  It's so so simple and yet very delicious flavorful and tasty. The only reason this place gets a four star from me is because I have to come here again and also I was not a big big fan of the tofu. I will definitely come again and adjust the review about the tofu!

For 1 dollar you get a slice of cheese pizza, any topping costs 50 cents more. The price is totally out of the question. I ordered the pepperoni slice of pizza and it was delicious! It is definitely not the best pizza I have ever had, but for that price of a slice, it is unimaginable. The best bang of your bucks is right here! I would recommend this place to anyone who craves for something cheap and good quality. The reason why I give 5 stars, I wish I could give 4.5 stars is because of its mind-blowing quality for a dollar a slice. Check them out yourself!

Title: Pleasant Atmosphere with Room for Service Improvement

My recent visit to this bustling eatery on a Saturday late afternoon offered a glimpse into its popularity. The outdoor seating added to its charming appeal, and the expansive bar was a focal point for socializing. Our party secured a high top near the bar but were informed of a one-hour time limit due to a subsequent birthday reservation, which was a slight inconvenience.

The service was adequate, though our order was limited to a side of fries. The fries arrived well-prepared with a hint of rosemary—a divisive choice that pleased some in our group more than others, but I personally enjoyed the aromatic touch. This short visit has piqued my interest, and I am keen to explore a wider range of their menu offerings, particularly the brunch, in a future visit.

Title: Szechuan Surprise in the East Village

If you're in the East Village and craving Szechuan cuisine, this place is a must-visit. The extensive menu has something for every level of heat preference, ensuring a satisfying meal for all. Each dish I tried was deliciously flavorful, though rich enough to warrant a post-meal rest.

The only hiccup during my visit was the service; despite the welcoming staff, it was somewhat slow and disorganized, noticeable even with the dining room not being full during Sunday brunch.

Despite this, the quality of the food makes a return visit a no-brainer. I'd recommend stopping by when you're not in a rush and ready for an indulgent feast.

Great service. I like how the outside dining area accommodate the natural trees that were there first. Cool inside and bar or area near entrance. Mushroom ravioli was great as was the Burrata and tomato salad. They were able to accommodate one person's garlic allergy.Nice environment, not as expensive as we expected. It was a quick walk to our hotel. Definitely a good recommendation.

I came here for lunch on a Saturday afternoon with a friend.  We ordered the Koku ramen and the kimchi tantan ramen.  The egg was super cold and slightly overcooked.  The pork broth was spicy and flavorful though.  Service was a bit rushed even though the place wasn't crowded.  My friend didn't finish eating and they kept asking her if they can take her bowl.  I may or may not come back, there's better ramen places in the area.  FYI - there's a minimum $15 to use credit card.

Was at the Whitney and decided to stop here with my teen after the latest exhibit. Disclaimer I am very familiar with Peruvian food as my parents are from Peru. We often make ceviche at home pretty adeptly and are usually prepared for disappointment when we eat ceviche in restaurants. It's located in the center of the market and has a pleasant white beach feel. We ordered the classic ceviche and inka cola. After a brief wait I was presented with a good sized portion of ceviche (I ordered a small) that was perfect for two to share as an app - or one person to eat alone as a light lunch. Presented in the composed style Limenos seem to adore; it was a layer of tender lettuce, topped with a good amount of lime and hot pepper marinated flounder. (Ceviche is technically raw but cooked in the lime juice). The fish was surrounded by piped sweet potato mousse (great idea that totally elevated the dish) fresh choclo corn and its crunchy counterpart canchas. Also in the mix wafer thin sliced red onion and I thought a touch fresh cilantro. SUPERB! Really, really good. **One pro tip** the container it is presented in is deep rather than long please take a spoon from the counter and spoon the juices gathered on the bottom over your ceviche before you dive in - that's what makes it wonderful. A cold inka cola (kind of cream soda flavored but better- deliciousness) makes this perfection for me. I will be back and next time going all in with the ceviche, causa, and an aji de gallina bowl.

I recently stumbled upon a new restaurant that's dangerously convenient for my daily routes. The ramen they serve is so addictively delicious that I foresee many future visits. It appears I'll be indulging in more ramen than ever!

Came here during lunchtime and decided to grab a quick bite at the bar which has their own separate menu from the main seating area.  Ordered the double cheeseburger and a side of fries.  The burger itself was actually pretty tasty and I enjoyed it quite a bit.  Fries were like any other fries so I had a hard time justifying the $10 price tag on something so simple.  Burger costs $14 which I had no problem with since it also came with chips and a pickle.  Overall you can easily rack up a lunch bill over 30 bones just for burger and fries.  Of course this was anticipated since this isn't some Burger King or McDonalds.  Venue is beautiful and spacious.  Very modern chill vibe at this restaurant/bar.  Servers were attentive so no complaints on my end.

Title: Hearty Flavors at a Premium

My latest dining experience bags a solid 4 stars. The highlight was undoubtedly the seafood tofu soup—rich and satisfying, with the complementary rice creating a perfect match. The array of banchan, especially the kimchi and macaroni salad, added a delightful variety of flavors.

While the $17 price tag for tofu soup might raise an eyebrow, considering the location, it's somewhat justifiable. It's worth noting the server's welcoming attitude towards sharing an entrée; the extra utensils and bowls were a thoughtful touch.

All in all, the tasty soup, complete with a side of fried fish and an egg, along with the stellar banchan, ensures I'd drop by again when in the vicinity.

My best friend has been raving about this place for quite some time. Finally got the chance to try it. Prices are reasonable, with the exception of drink prices that seemed on the high side. On a Thursday evening, the restaurant was busy but not too crazy. We did not have reservations, but I would probably make one if I came on the weekend. Menu is good sized, lots of great sounding pizzas and other options. I would like to try all the different pizzas. I am quite the picky eater when it comes to Italian food, as I don't like seafood. We chose 3 different things and shared them - the quattro latte pizza, eggplant parmigiana appetizer & lastly the Radiatori in Cartoccio.  Thought we were going to have too much food and that there was no way we could finish it- I thought wrong. Everything was so amazing, not sure what was my favorite because it was all great. You could just tell the radiatori was fresh pasta, cooked to just the right amount of tenderness. They cook the radiatori in tinfoil, which I originally thought was a gimmick, and maybe it was- but the pasta was so good, so I don't care.Service was good - the server constantly refilled our water and asked how things were. I liked that they split our dishes for us when they brought it out.

I was soooooo ready to get my hands dirty! All the seafood were freshly steamed and boiled, then tossed in one of their signature seasonings and served in a bag. I don't even know where to begin, this was truly a life-changing experience. I finally had my first Cajun/Creole seafood boil and it exceeded my expectations in every way. As a seafood boil virgin, I dove straight in and got their combo bag which contains 1lb. of crawfish, 1lb. of shrimp, corns, and potatoes. You get the option to pick 1 spice level and 1 seasoning. Now, there's nothing better than going to a restaurant where the staff knows their menu inside-out. Here, they do. I was strongly advised by our server to get their medium spicy. Their medium is more like a spicy in other places so if you're sensitive to HEAT, then be careful here. ⁣Next time I want the fiery spice for sure! I also got a side of Cajun fries and the whole meal was like a punch of seasoning, but in the best way possible. I was literally sweating but I love it because the food is so interactive if you know what I mean. It's not just a boring sit-down meal. You literally wrestle with your food to get the best out of it. The seasoning in my bag was so well distributed, hot, garlicky, and spicy. Heaven in a plastic bag. If you're ever stopping by in NYC, you HAVE to come here. Literally put it on your bucket list. They have so many options and you can basically create your perfect meal. ⁣

Title: Freshness and Flavor Wrapped in a Hand Roll

I recently visited this sushi spot for lunch and was pleased to find the same freshness and quality I experienced at their California location. Despite arriving during a busy time at 12:30 pm on a Tuesday and facing a 20-minute wait, my solo status got me seated quicker than anticipated.

Settling in at the bar-like seating arrangement, I tackled the straightforward menu with a pencil in hand – a quick and efficient approach to ordering. The environment is perfect for a swift yet satisfying meal, whether for lunch or dinner.

One standout is their iced green tea – a refreshing complement to the sushi. Opting for the 6 hand roll special at $29, I found it to be a delicious bargain that hit the spot perfectly.

Payment is a breeze, with no tipping involved, as you settle your bill with the cashier on your way out. Given the quality and experience, I wholeheartedly recommend this eatery. Even with a potential wait, your patience will be rewarded with an exceptional sushi experience.

Came here on a Saturday night and it was pretty empty around 9pm. Got seated immediately and ordered the beef noodle soup, sesame tofu, shredded chicken and the prawn with egg yolks. Also got the house made soy milk to try. The beef noodle soup and the shredded chicken were awesome and loved the flavors. The beef and the chicken were super tender and the noodle both was flavorful. The sesame tofu and prawns were pretty disappointing. I love tofu but there was just too many different flavors going on that did not complement each other well. The sesame sauce was too thick and did not have an appetizing texture. The prawns were not worth the price at all, the shrimp was definitely not fresh and tasted like frozen shrimp and the fish lacked egg yolk flavor. I've had much better at other chinese restaurants and their portions are much bigger. Last thing to mention is that the "house made" soy milk did not seem house made at all. I saw them pour it from a store bought bottle into a serving bottle.Overall would come back for the noodle soup and the chicken but would skip the other items I ordered. Wouldn't go out of my way to come here since it's overpriced and can find the same flavors in Chinatown or flushing.

I really wish I could give this place 4 stars, but the service here is awful - mostly the front desk. Came here around 10:30 and had to wait about 20 minutes for a table. The restaurant looks more like a bar but they have appetizers, good amount of ramen choices, and a raw oyster bar. When we had asked the front desk of how long till we could sit and she stated that she has tables that have checks and that they're just waiting for them to pay. We then tried to clarify our question for an actual time estimate and she repeated the same thing she said but with more attitude.When we finally sat down, I ordered the Spicy Shrimp Bun and the Okinawa Ramen. Although the but was tasty with shrimp and spicy mayo, it was upsetting to see that only 1 bun costs $5.50.. I really enjoyed the ramen since it has plenty of vegetables, noodles, and a gingery broth. However, throughout the night we were trying to wave our waiter down to take our order and to pay out our bill. Another encounter was the front desk kept bumping into our chairs without apologizing.. The space may have been small to maneuver around, but it only takes less than 5 seconds to say "I'm sorry for bumping your chair". I don't think I would come back because the bad service trumps the quality of the food.

My dining experience at this restaurant was nothing short of amazing. Each dish was a masterful blend of flavor and heat, with a unique twist that set it apart. The seasoning was impeccable, elevating every bite. I’m already looking forward to my next visit!

We recently enjoyed takeout from this gem of a spot, and their arepas left us thoroughly impressed. The standout was the Pabellón arepa, filled with succulent beef that tantalized our taste buds. The Del Gato arepa also held its own, but the Pabellón simply stole the show. The flavors were so inviting that we're eager to dine in next time to explore the sides on offer. Highly recommended for a taste of authentic arepas.

I recently visited a ramen restaurant and tried the spicy miso ramen, which is my usual choice. It was delicious and the portion size was just right. They also offered a good selection of sake. I appreciated the relaxed atmosphere on a weeknight, and the service was excellent. Highly recommended for a cozy and satisfying meal.

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Artichoke Basille's Pizza

My dining experiences at Artichoke Basille's Pizza can only be described as heavenly indulgences. With a deep affection for pizza that trails just behind French fries and sushi on my list of favorites, this spot has quickly climbed the ranks after a mere two visits.

Each encounter with their pizza, particularly when savored fresh from the oven, has been nothing short of phenomenal. A word to the wise: patience here is a virtue, as the piping hot slices demand a brief cooling period before you dive into the molten cheese and perfectly crisped crust that will have your taste buds in rapture. As I recount my experiences, the memory alone is enough to coax a salivary response.

Artichoke Basille's slices shine as the ideal post-party delight, meeting the late-night hunger pangs with gusto, without breaking the bank. The generous portion size ensures your money is well spent.

In summary, whether you find yourself slightly tipsy after a night of dancing or simply in pursuit of pizza perfection, I wholeheartedly recommend Artichoke Basille's Pizza. It's a promise—I'll be returning for more of those divine slices.

CREDIT AND DEBIT ONLY!But even so, you would think the lines would go faster. We waited over 35 minutes to grab two slices for take-out. Honestly, I would not come here if it wasn't for their artichoke pizza.

I gave it a shot but I'm not sold on Emmy.. I do generally prefer Neapolitan style pizza so perhaps this shouldn't be a surprise. That said, I absolutely love Prince Street Pizza's square pepperoni topped pizza. So I'm not sure.. I think the topping combo at Emmy doesn't quite strike my fancy and I don't particularly love the thick dough either.

Title: Chic Plant-Based Dining at abcV

Review:

I recently dined at abcV, a Jean-Georges vegetarian restaurant, and was left with an impression strong enough to merit 4.5 stars. The venue boasts a trendsetting modernity with a clean, chic design, although it flirts with pretension. The tapas-style menu resonated with my preferences, allowing for a communal and varied tasting experience.

What stands out is the creativity imbued in every dish. The culinary finesse shines as the kitchen foregoes meat mimicry, instead celebrating vegetables in their authentic glory. Each plate arrives as a work of art—flavorful, meticulously crafted, yet admittedly on the pricier side.

Service was impeccable, and the open kitchen added to the experience, although we did experience a slight delay in seating despite our reservation. The restaurant's flexibility with dietary requirements is commendable. They skillfully adjusted their vegetarian offerings to suit a vegan and nut-free diet without any fuss—an accommodation that is far too rare.

Despite the delightful ambiance and cuisine, I must admit that the satiety factor was lacking; a mere hour later, I found myself hungry again. While the menu fares well for a vegetarian palate, I missed having substantial protein options.

Would I return? Perhaps not, as I prefer leaving a table feeling fully satisfied. However, for those seeking a sophisticated, plant-based culinary adventure, abcV stands out as a strong contender worth recommending.

Title: A Chic Blend of Cultures at Jean-Georges' Latest Venture

My husband and I had the pleasure of dining at the new Indonesian French fusion restaurant started by Jean-Georges Vongerichten's son, an intriguing concept that sparked our curiosity. Booking a table through Resy required a bit of foresight, as prime-time slots fill up weeks in advance, but we managed to secure a 6pm reservation on a Thursday.

Upon arrival, we were enveloped in the restaurant's energetic ambiance, devoid of music but alive with the buzz of conversation. The interior was a tapestry of elegance and Asian sophistication, and we were fortunate to be seated at a cozy corner booth, which felt like the venue's pièce de résistance.

Our waiter was prompt and insightful, guiding us through the menu. Heeding his suggestions, we indulged in an array of dishes, such as the pork ribs glazed in soy tamarind sauce—a bit on the dry side, yet the presentation was unmatched—and the delightfully flavored lobster butter noodle with impeccably cooked lobster. The coconut milk-garnished clams and the fried squid were personal favorites, offering a taste of the fusion done right. The nasi goreng, although a simple side, was ample and satisfying, especially with the theatrics of the server breaking the yolk of the sunny side up egg right at our table.

Priced in line with Manhattan's modern Asian eateries, the restaurant justifies its costs with attentive service. Our server's regular check-ins made the experience all the more enjoyable.

I'd recommend this spot to anyone seeking a refined evening out, keen to experience the marriage of French and Indonesian flavors curated under the watchful eye of a legendary lineage.

Loved this cute restaurant. Came in on a Saturday around 620. Hour wait for the dining room so tried the bar waitlist instead. Was seated within 10 minutes. Tried the shrimp avocado slider, oysters, crab and spinach dip. All were awesome! They give you everything crackers and butter- also awesome! Great service- friendly, attentive bartender. Made a great Aperol spritz. They even give you a complementary chocolate pudding dessert at the end of your meal. Oh- and all of those things were on happy hour all day Saturday until 7 pm. Bonus!

I gave this place four stars because they make a pretty damn good margarita that bears their name. I'm not talking about the frozen one. Margarita was not overly sweet and the tequila was good qualityI had the mushroom taco and al pastor, the guacamole with chips. And I tried a fish taco. Everything was pretty good. The guacamole could've used a little more spice, but the avocado was ripe and deliciousNow I live on the Lower East Side where we have good food at affordable prices 24 hours a day, but for the upper West side, this place is great. It's a little cramped, some tables are a little close to the kitchen and hot as a result, but all in all this is the best you're going to find in this area with overpaying.Also the service was very attentive.

Friendly staff, close to the train station, a full bar, and a free skewer with every beer. What else can you ask for?Whether you're here for a meal or just a drink and a snack, Noree Thai is a great choice. I'm a huge fan of spicy food and these guys will make it as spicy as you need it. My favorite entree is the pad kee mao but there are plenty of great appetizers as well. The fries, wings, shrimps, mussels, crispy pork belly, and oyster omelette are all great choices. Of course, the skewers as well. A good go to in Chinatown.

This might be one of most disappointing Japanese restaurants I had tried. This is a Chinese type/style of Japanese restaurant meaning food are different from an authentic Japanese restaurant. Such kind of restaurant tend to serve more varieties of food ranging from hot food(many kind of appetizers, all kind of teriyaki, noodle including soup and stir fried, fried rice) to cold food(sushi, sashimi and specialty roll). Walking in during dinner time and it was pretty empty that was a sign of no no type of restaurant. Sat down, look through the menu thinking since it was pricy maybe it was a good restaurant. For the appetizers, we got the aburi otoro(tuna belly - $25) which was not fresh at all with fishy taste. The tiger claw($10) came in two pieces that was made of shrimp/(maybe) crab meat paste on to a claw then fried. At least, it was decent. Then we got the seafood teriyaki($28), sushi shinagawa($35) and sashimi shinagawa($45) to share. Seafood teriyaki came out cold with bad quality and quantity. One piece of salmon, few pieces of other type of seafood. The worst was cinnamon apple on the same plate that really didn't make sense. For the ridiculous price of $28, it is totally not worth it. Both sushi and sashimi combo came with sample appetizers. Those were actually good compare to the rest of the stuff that we have ordered. Sushi and sashimi were not fresh. All the raw fish were not fresh and had a fishy taste. I would never come back after this experience. Never was expecting such bad food with ridiculous price.
Excellent South Indian vegetarian fare with friendly staff.  It was the perfect post workout high protein lunch.

A pretty decent Chinese restaurant. Not sure if you can consider this place a hole in the wall, but it gives off that vibe as the decor isn't really well maintained and the signage is in desperate need to replacement. The interior is in dire need of a renovation, but it's not as bad as Cheeky Sandwiches if you've ever been there.I came here for a family gathering and we got 12 different items off the menu and all of them were fantastic. Some of the highlights included the Fried Rice, Cantonese style Lobster, Salt & Pepper Fried Squid, and the Whole Fish (Sea Bass I believe). Everyone thoroughly enjoyed every meal with no complaints.Service is pretty good. Just need to grab their attention and they'll do whatever you need from them. Wouldn't mind coming back here from some authentic Chinese food.

Title: A Time-Honored Gem for Steak Lovers

Palm Too, a quintessential New York steakhouse, continues to deliver the indulgent experience that has endeared it to meat aficionados since the '80s. A highlight is the half & half, a generous mountain of crispy chips and onion strings, which despite its size, disappears swiftly when shared. While some updates have touched the menu, favorites like the classic Gigi salad can still be had in its original glory with a simple request. The star of the show, the meats, remain superbly unaltered. Even with a smaller filet, there's plenty to savor especially when capped with a colossal slice of chocolate or carrot cake, both of which are sumptuous enough to satisfy your entire table. Palm Too is a place to indulge in tried-and-true culinary comforts.

I absolutely adore the space - it's beautifully laid out and thoughtfully designed.  First thing to note is that the entrance to the restaurant is actually on 26th Street and not Park Ave S.  We arrived for our brunch reservations a bit early but were seated pretty promptly once our whole party had arrived.  I couldn't stop looking around, admiring everything around me but had to focus on choosing what I wanted to eat because there were so many items on the menu that piqued my interest.  Luckily, I had some overlap with my friend, so we ordered a couple of dishes to share.  We ended up getting the California BEC and the fried chicken sandwich.  The BEC consisted of an egg soufflé and caramelized onion bun that was heavenly.  The egg was soooo fluffy!  My only gripe with it was that it was just the sandwich with no side.  A small salad or even fries to accompany it would have been great.  Additionally, the cheese could have been melted - it was just...there.  I also really enjoyed the fried chicken sandwich (which did come with a side of fries).  Thought the avocado mash and alfalfas were a nice touch, but the chicken itself could have been a bit more flavorful, but juicy nonetheless.  Would come back to try some more dishes soon!

Title: A Sophisticated Haven in the Heart of New York

Review:
During the bustling Christmas season in New York, our group stumbled upon a surprisingly serene gem. The restaurant's peaceful ambiance was a rare find in the city that never sleeps, proving that tranquility can coexist with popularity—as evidenced by the fully occupied seats.

The patrons here seemed to have mastered the art of sophisticated conversation, contributing to the delightful atmosphere. Our culinary experience was exceptional, particularly the gnocchi and tartare, which were so irresistible that we couldn't help but order seconds.

Even without a large appetite, the tantalizing appearance of the dishes promises a reason for a return visit. To add to the charm, our server was incredibly engaging, though his name escapes me. His warm service only highlights my recommendation of this establishment for a beautiful evening in a gorgeous setting.

I recently had lunch at this spot around 1 PM, and it was pleasantly quiet with just a few tables occupied, though it did fill up a bit as we dined. The service was on the slower side, and it felt as though we were occasionally forgotten after our order was placed. Seating for pairs is tight, especially with larger dishes like the Farmer's Meal.

Our meal included crispy chicken buns, which were the highlight with their Korean Katsu-like flavor tucked into a bun. The tuna poke was an unusual twist, reminiscent of a chicken salad sandwich filling rather than traditional poke, leading my boyfriend to dub it "midwestern poke." The Farmer's Meal featured cubed kalbi, which lacked excitement despite the novelty of wrapping it ourselves.

While the atmosphere was cool, it's not likely a place I'd return to for a meal, though it seems promising for a happy hour visit.

We are very disappointed Location: I can't even consider being in a place this tiny for dinner. And as the day goes dark, customers continue to come in. It's nothing but waiting time for customers who consider dining here. For me, basically sitting next to stranger for food this close is unbearable. Food: they serve more food on the weekend than during weekday. That's being said. All I can order is noodles and lu rou fan and soft tofu. Price is way too high. For a noodle that size which costs me 14 dollars?! Nope. And the noodle is nothing special. To be honest, I have experienced and dined in much better noodle place in Manhattan. Don't know where the hype coming from. 3 stars is all I can get. Just disappointed

This Italian restaurant is perfect for large groups. It's classy with dining room that fits large group without feeling crowded. Both their pizza and pasta are solid, and it has nice cocktail bars nearby.

Title: A Satisfying Thai Brunch with Room for Improvement

I recently visited this local spot for their weekend brunch special and left with my Thai cravings well-satisified. We started with a vibrant papaya salad and delightfully crispy coconut shrimp, both of which set a promising stage for the main course.

I opted for the ground pork sautéed in a robust Thai basil sauce, while my friend enjoyed the crispy fish fillet complemented by a similar basil-infused glaze. Each entree came with a perfectly cooked sunny side up egg, adding a classic brunch twist to the meal.

While the flavors were spot-on, both dishes were somewhat overwhelmed by the sauce, detracting slightly from the overall experience. Nonetheless, the generous portions and properly executed proteins—succulent minced meat for me and a satisfying crunch to my friend's fish—kept us content.

For anyone seeking a Thai flavor fix in a cozy neighborhood setting, this restaurant is certainly worth a visit. Just be prepared for a saucy affair!

After hearing rave reviews, I finally tried this local gem for dinner and it did not disappoint. The menu was diverse, but I was particularly excited to see cauliflower rice—a trendy and delicious option I adore. I opted for the cauliflower rice with chicken, and it was exceptional; it surpassed all my expectations with its flavors and textures.

The ambiance of the restaurant only heightened the dining experience. My friend and I were charmed by the quaint decor and the vibe set by a fantastic playlist, contributing to a delightful atmosphere. Additionally, the service was flawless, attentive and friendly, complementing the overall excellence of the evening.

A standout feature that deserves mention is the visibility of pride flags throughout the restaurant—a heartwarming touch that celebrated inclusivity and community. It's a place I'd enthusiastically recommend and will certainly be returning to.

Title: A Mediterranean Gem with a Turkish Twist

If you're yearning for Mediterranean cuisine with an authentic Turkish flair, this restaurant is a must-visit. Our dining experience was exceptional, with an extensive menu that sets it apart from your typical Mediterranean fare.

As a party of four, we delved into an array of dishes including tender octopus, succulent lamb, and a generous meat platter. The zucchini patties were a delightful surprise, and the phyllo rolls melted in our mouths. Every selection, like the flavorful dumplings, was a testament to the chef's culinary prowess.

What stood out was the meticulous preparation of both meats and vegetables. The meats were impeccably cooked, achieving both the ideal texture and depth of flavor. The vegetable dishes were equally impressive, showcasing innovative cooking techniques that highlighted their natural taste.

In summary, we left with our palates thoroughly satisfied, already planning our next visit to explore more of this culinary treasure trove. Whether you're a Mediterranean cuisine aficionado or a newcomer eager to explore Turkish specialties, this restaurant is sure to impress.

I have always heard Ippudo was the ramen spot to go in New York. My friends have raved about how good this place was a few years back. I guess it's a reason why I barely hear anyone mention Ippudo these days. Regardless, I needed to try this place once to see if the hype was real. Upon arrival, I had trouble finding where the entrance was as there's no noticeable sign/door. I came before noon on a Monday, so I was seated right away by the Chef's table. I asked for recommendations and ordered the Akamaru Modern. I was sadly disappointed on how bland the ramen taste and the noodles were a bit on the harder end. The only positive thing was the portion size, although a bowl of ramen was at least $16. Overall, I wouldn't come back to Ippudo as it felt like I was paying for overpriced average ramen.

Title: A Late Night Delight with Minor Hiccups at Joe's Pizza

Last night, my craving for pizza led me to place a late order through GrubHub from Joe's Pizza. Impressively, the delivery arrived right on schedule, complete with a generously provided side of Parmesan, garlic salt, and a sprinkling of herbs—a delightful touch! 

However, there was a slight mix-up; despite our request (and willingness to pay) for a side of marinara, it was missing from our order. While it was a bit of a letdown, the pizza was so exquisite that it hardly mattered. The pizza boasted a quality that left us yearning for Joe's Pizza back in Vegas—the thought of not having it close by brings a tear to my eye.

From the first bite, it was love at first slice. The dough, oh the dough! It was pure perfection, a delicious foundation to the high-quality cheeses that tantalized our taste buds. We devoured the entire pie with an enthusiasm that left us wishing for more.

I am utterly smitten with Joe's Pizza and although the delivery experience was nearly impeccable, I'm eager to visit the shop in person. Perhaps, I'll remedy that by heading there tomorrow for another round of what is sure to be a memorable meal. Joe's, you've got a pizza my heart!

Title: A Satisfying Late-Night Find

My friend and I wandered into this eatery for a late-night meal on a bustling Friday, and we were met with prompt seating and warm smiles from the staff. The straightforward menu boasted an ample variety of dishes ranging from savory dumplings to heartwarming soups and an array of protein-centric entrees.

Our taste buds were treated to crispy fried chicken dumplings, succulent steamed pork dumplings, flavorful Peking duck spring rolls, and delectable green onion pancakes. The bill was a modest $35, leaving us both content with the value.

The food's prompt arrival and mouth-watering taste were highlights of our visit. This no-frills spot delivers where it counts – exceptional food quality and service. For anyone in search of a casual dining spot that caters to lunch, dinner, or those late-night cravings, this place is a gem. Highly recommend.

Who doesn't like the taco trucks scattered throughout LA? And guess who missed them when he moved across the country to pursue his dreams.Indeed, I had my taco cravings one evening. And in my quest to find the good Mexican food places in the five boroughs, I ordered some tacos from this place.The delivery time was less than 30 minutes, and the food came warm and packaged with care.The tacos were huge! They had generous portions of meat, were topped with cilantro and onions, and to my pleasant surprise had packets of Valentina hot sauce! The meal was more than enough to satisfy my hunger. The three tacos hit the spot, and left me ready to chill the rest of the evening. The next time I crave tacos, I'll definitely consider ordering from Otto's again!

Title: A Satisfying Slice of Italy in the Big Apple

My recent dining experience at this Italian eatery left a positive impression, proving that you can find a decent plate of pasta without falling into the "red-sauce" trap that typifies so many Italian-American joints. The menu spans the breadth of Italy's regional cuisines, and the chefs handle the classics commendably.

The arancini caught my attention with their crisp exteriors and flavorful fillings, although they are on the petite side. Conversely, the pasta servings are generous, providing a toothsome al dente texture that any pasta aficionado would appreciate. However, watch out for the oil content in the dishes; they don't shy away from it, which might leave you feeling full longer than usual.

For those who enjoy a glass of vino, the wine list is a highlight, showcasing a selection of whites that are surprisingly affordable for New York City standards.

In conclusion, this restaurant delivers a solid Italian dining experience. It's a place where indulgence in flavor is guaranteed, and your wallet won't suffer too much for it. A recommended spot for when you're in the mood for Italian but want to avoid the clichés and the price tag that often come with the territory in NYC.

Title: Mixed Experiences at a Disappointing Dinner

Service at this establishment started on a high note with Ting, an attentive and accommodating server, and a warm receptionist. Unfortunately, the dining experience took a sharp nosedive when it came to the food, overshadowing the stellar service.

The Shishito peppers, priced at nearly $7, were a letdown, undercooked to the point of rawness. The steak, requested medium-rare, arrived disappointingly overdone, and a second attempt brought a steak that was rare and lackluster in flavor and size, especially considering its $28 price tag.

Xiao Long Bao at $9 for four pieces also fell short with no soup inside, sticking together and not living up to expectations. While the shrimp dumplings were satisfactory, they were not compelling enough to offset the other issues, especially at $7 for four.

Unfortunately, post-meal interactions with the staff exacerbated the poor dining experience, with inappropriate comments that were unprofessional and offensive. This experience leads me to advise future diners to take their appetite and money elsewhere, perhaps to Chinatown, where the value and authenticity of similar dishes seem far superior.

Rating: ★☆☆☆☆ (1/5 stars) – Due to the poor food quality and subsequent unfortunate interactions with the staff.

My recent visit to Don Antonio's was absolutely delightful! The staff was prompt and efficient, seating us quickly without any hassle. Our party of four shared three dinner items, each dish more wonderful than the last, leaving us all thoroughly satisfied. A unique touch was the live kitchen feed displayed on a monitor, adding an engaging glimpse into the culinary action. I can't recommend this place enough!

I recently visited a casual Cantonese eatery boasting a menu of light fare like dumplings, steamed noodle rolls, and dim sum. Eager to sample their offerings, I opted for the beef chow fun and beef fried rice. Unfortunately, both dishes were disappointing, lacking the depth of flavor I had hoped for. The preparation seemed haphazard, as if hastily thrown together without much care. Service also left much to be desired; the chef appeared more interested in socializing than cooking, and the counter staff was notably slow, contributing to a lengthy wait for my food. While steamed dishes might have potential when paired with soy sauce, based on my experience, I wouldn't recommend the individually cooked items. Regrettably, I won't be returning.

I arrived at the restaurant with a ravenous appetite and was thoroughly satisfied by the time I left. I opted for the basic curry at spice level 3, complemented by a pork cutlet. The total came out to a reasonable $14.98. The dish delivered a spicy kick that was flavorful without overwhelming the palate. While the food was a delight, the service lacked a bit of attentiveness. Nonetheless, for anyone craving a well-balanced curry, this spot is worth checking out.

Upon entering the restaurant, we were greeted with a limited seating arrangement and a somewhat disinterested staff. The culinary offerings included customizable salad bowls, enticing noodle dishes, and a variety of banchan. The process for ordering and receiving food was confusing and lacked clarity—especially when it came to the calling of orders.

As for the food, my friend's vegan ramen was disappointingly lukewarm, and my Korean Temple Salad with tofu (which came with an additional cost) was underwhelmingly bland. The kale was tough and the overall flavor profile was lacking, failing to justify the $16 price tag.

Regrettably, the service was the most notable aspect of our visit, but for the wrong reasons. The cashier's selective enthusiasm when greeting customers was quite apparent; she was noticeably more welcoming to certain demographics. Simple inquiries seemed to be a chore for her to answer, and her behavior carried a discriminatory undertone that was particularly discomforting.

Overall, the experience left much to be desired both in terms of culinary execution and customer service. It's uncertain if this treatment was isolated to us or indicative of a broader trend, but it certainly impacted our dining experience negatively.

On a recommendation from my friend, we stopped by this local hotspot for a late lunch and what a delightful experience! We kicked things off with the Mussels Creoles, an adventurous and messy endeavor, but every bit as delectable as we hoped. The mussels were succulent, swimming in a divine tomato-chorizo sauce that beckoned for bread-dipping once the shellfish were devoured.

We couldn't resist trying the steak tartare, which, despite its smaller size, was a triumph of flavor and seasoning—a perfect companion to the bread and salad served alongside it.

Our main course, the rabbit, did have a hint of gaminess, but it only enhanced the overall taste, complemented by an outstanding cream sauce that still haunts my culinary dreams. The vegetable sides, especially the squash puree, were so memorable that I've been attempting to replicate them in my own kitchen. The staff's generous offer of a vegetable refill was a welcome surprise.

The restaurant's payment policy was a slight hiccup, accepting only cash and Amex, yet this did little to dampen the shine of our meal. Overall, a gem well worth visiting, with flavors that linger fondly long after the plates are cleared.

I regret to inform fellow diners that my experience at this restaurant was deeply disappointing. Despite going in with optimism because of a pleasant view of the ice rink in December, the dining experience itself was underwhelming, particularly given the steep set menu price of $55 per person.

The meal commenced with a tepid serving of bread paired with unspreadable butter. Hopes of redemption were dashed by a jumbo shrimp cocktail that was tough to the point of being inedible. The lobster bisque followed, watery and lacking any discernible flavor.

The main course, a grilled chicken salad, was no better, featuring wilted lettuce and chicken that tasted far from fresh. Similarly, the hamburger was a letdown and remained mostly uneaten.

Dessert, sadly, did not improve the situation. An apple pie that seemed to have overstayed its welcome was neither warm nor fresh, giving the impression of a wholesale store purchase. The key lime pie was the sole item that did not invite criticism.

I must advise against dining at this establishment. You would be better served enjoying a New York street pizza or a hot dog, which are sure to provide more satisfaction for your taste buds and wallet.

I stopped by this eatery for a lunchtime bite and came away with mixed feelings. The service gave me pause; attention from staff seemed intermittent, and there was a noticeable delay before my order was taken. As for the cuisine, it was certainly satisfactory, though it lacked a distinctive flair that would beckon me back eagerly. In summary, the experience was pleasant enough but didn't leave a lasting impression.

Last Friday, my friends and I stumbled upon Dons Bogman Black after facing an over an hour wait at Jongro. A knowledgeable friend recommended this Korean BBQ gem, and it did not disappoint. Arriving at 7:45 PM without a reservation, we were immediately swept into the spacious, comfortably private interior, decked out with massive LED screens.

The menu tantalized our taste buds. We indulged in the prime ribeye, pork belly, tofu mushroom dolsot, and kimchi stew—all delectably satisfying and easily shared among the five of us. The quality and portion sizes deserve high praise, making the dishes recommendable without hesitation.

Service was on par with the food—attentive, efficient, and proactive, especially with refills of the smaller side items. 

Dons Bogman Black proved to be a superb alternative to the usual 32nd Street Korean BBQ hustle. It's a spot worthy of both a detour and a primary destination for those in the know.

Another hip Korean restaurant in NY. I didn't know whether to leave a review or not because my experience was just ok, but the Octopus and Calamari Salad with Yuzu Dressing was SIMPLY AMAZING. I could've just ate 2 of these by myself and called it a day. ORDER THIS (I think it's seasonal).On the other hand, I did not enjoy the Seafood and Veggie Hot Pot (C5) one bit. The soup tasted like it came from a package, the rice cakes were super mushy (apparently this is how it's supposed to taste after I asked my waiter why it was so mushy to the point where it just fell apart), and the cocktail I also ordered (Peach Blossoms) was average. Depending on what particular dish you order, places like Her Name Is Han is a hit or miss. Good luck.

Title: Noodle Delight with a Side of Disappointment at Dun Huang

I recently visited Dun Huang’s East Village location, having been enticed back with the offer of a complimentary lamb and rice dish due to my absence from their Yelp event. The experience was a mixed bag. Let's start with the positives: the noodles and soup were a standout, possibly hand-pulled, with a texture that left me longing for more. I also enjoyed the free kelp salad, which was flavorful with a nice balance of sesame oil, chili, and vinegar.

However, the meal wasn't without its letdowns. The presentation of the complimentary lamb and rice was unexpectedly poor, resembling a haphazard pile of leftovers rather than the enticing dish one would anticipate from a restaurant. Not only was it visually off-putting, but the lamb was tough, steering us clear of additional lamb dishes.

I appreciated the gesture of freebies like the kelp salad for checking in on Yelp, but that couldn't entirely make up for the shortcomings. Despite my love for the noodles, the lingering aftertaste was too potent, making me reluctant to return unless I have no social commitments afterward.

In summary, while the signature noodles beckon a revisit, the overall experience was bittersweet. I'm left with the hope that the presentation and taste of other dishes will rise to meet the standard set by the delightful noodles and soup.

Omg best steak in NYC! It is so juicy and delicious! Arigato gozaimasu!! Location: It is located in the heart of 5th avenue, it is near all the food chains, at first we can't find it because it is in a covered walk. The interior is like a typical restaurant but you can see how they cut and cook your steak!Service: Our server is super nice! He explained everything in the menu and how to order. Apparently we have to look at the menu and order at the spot where they cut the meats, then tell them how you will like it. Even the guy who cut the meats is nice! (See my video)Food: I ordered Ribeye in medium well! Damn the steak melts in your mouth, so juicy and buttery! Also you can add all the side dishes for 5 dollars! Best decision I have! There are varieties of sake (I don't drink so I am not sure) The miso soup is kinda salty but otherwise good.Price rating: 9/10, 50/person including tax and tip. Hey it is damn good and worth it! :)I will definitely come back here!! Amazing staff and great, juicy and buttery steak!!! Please do add all the side dishes!!

I recently visited this restaurant twice, drawn in by the tantalizing photos of their kimchi cream udon—and it lived up to the hype. The restaurant fills up quickly after its 5 pm opening, so early arrival is recommended to avoid a 30-40 minute wait later on.

Service was impressively speedy; dishes arrived within ten minutes of ordering. The star of the show, the kimchi cream udon, was a delectable fusion of creamy and tangy flavors with a generous helping of shrimp and kimchi. The beef tataki, served with yuzu sauce, was a hit on both visits despite a slight dip in presentation the second time around.

On the less impressive side, the ramen fell flat with overcooked noodles and a lackluster broth. However, the squid legs and fried chicken did not disappoint and rounded out the meal nicely.

The restaurant also offers a selection of drinks which I'm keen to try on my next visit. Overall, this spot is definitely worth returning to, especially for another bowl of that exceptional kimchi cream udon.

Came here mainly due to curiosity and since I was meeting someone who seem like a food lover himself, I trusted his choice! FYI - A la carte menu is mainly at the bar. This review is for the Seasonal Tasting menu (Late Autumn/ early Winter).We started off with banchan, where each small plates was unique on its own. My favorites were the oyster and the steamed egg in a shell. For the tasting, I went for the urchin ($10 supplement) and lobster. Urchin melts in your mouth and is served with quinoa. The lobster was decorated with floral herbs and spices was also delicious, cooked just right. I believe I had the black cod that was served with red pepper soy. I'd have to say this might by my least favorite of the dishes. Perhaps it was the sauce that didn't go well with my palate. However, the Iberico pork was divine, and cooked perfectly to highlight the seasoning and texture of the dish. To end the evening of the dishes, a pear palate cleanser was introduced as the beginning of desserts, For dessert, I went for the brown rice choux that was served with tiny scoops of ice-cream and it was unbelievable delicious! It was unique and had a lovely warm flavor. At the very end of the meal, three mini pastries were also served.Service overall was phenomenal - table was kept clean and you were informed. If you have a food allergy, the waiter/waitress is very keen on making sure you're provided an alternative. My friend is a vegetarian and he was also provided a wonderful vegetarian course.
