This place is perfect for long dinner talks, special occasions, and/or a foodie's excuse to explore great food.

Title: A Mediterranean Gem with Room for Service Improvement

My recent visit to this well-situated eatery left me with a mix of impressions. Awarding four stars for its charming ambiance and delectable Mediterranean fare, I found the dining experience overall pleasing. The pre fix menu is a highlight, offering an enticing selection that did not disappoint in flavor.

However, the service took a dip in quality. Our table experienced notable delays and an unfortunate sense of neglect, which was particularly disconcerting as I was dining with a media colleague who had recommended the restaurant. This aspect could certainly benefit from enhancement.

Despite this setback, my appreciation for Mediterranean cuisine and the potential I see in this establishment compels me to plan a return visit next month, hoping for a noticeable improvement in service speed and attention.

Title: A Memorable New York Culinary Experience

My first night in New York City was made unforgettable thanks to a visit to this renowned dining spot. The anticipation had been building from all the positive chatter I'd heard, and it did not disappoint. Arriving at 9pm with colleagues, we found it bustling, yet the staff eased our brief wait with a gracious offering of champagne—a welcomed touch following our flight.

The ambiance was electric, reminiscent of a scene one might imagine in a Sopranos episode, with decor to match. Exceptional service was on display from the get-go, with the wait staff eager to guide us through the menu. Our selection started with an impeccable steak tartare and their signature duck fat fries—indulgent and moreish, paired wonderfully with a creamy Burrata.

For the main course, the shared duck confit, delectable tortellini, mussels, and a second round of those irresistible fries rounded out a culinary feast. Each dish was flawlessly executed, leaving us not just satisfied, but genuinely delighted.

Closing thoughts - this establishment is a must-visit for any food lover in NYC. Their combination of ambrosial food, swift service, and vibrant atmosphere is the recipe for a repeat visit. I wholeheartedly recommend it and am eager for my next meal here.

Red Farm is a lovely restaurant. The decor and atmosphere are beautiful and it makes you feel like you've left New York City for a few hours. I loved the warm light and comfy, chic feel of the whole place. (This was the best I could do in terms of describing the inside- I loved it. Hope that makes sense haha) We arrived at 730 on a Sunday night and there was no wait for two people. The host was a very chipper and kind man. He had a smile on his face the entire time he spoke to me and immediately helped me as soon as I walked in the door. I feel like at some places the hosts barely even look at you, he was excellent. When we were seated another kind man walked us over to our table. He pulled out my chair for me which was a lovely touch of courtesy and class. Our waiter came to us relatively quickly asking us if we wanted any beverages other than water.We ordered some Crispy Zucchini and Eggplant Fritters with Okra Lemongrass Dip to start along with an order of the Crispy Oxtail Dumplings. The zucchini and eggplant dish was fine, I personally loved the dip which is why I think I kept eating the zucchini and eggplant pieces. But the fritters themselves were nothing to write home about. The crispy oxtail dumplings were to die for! Not too spicy, and the sauce it came with was very good- but I ended up dipping mine in the okra lemongrass dip- I'm telling you I could've drank the stuff. (Don't judge me till you've had it.) For our meal we split the Diced Lamb with Chinese Broccoli and Pickled Shallots and the Asparagus with XO sauce. Our waiter had told us that the lamb was a bit spicy (because I had told him that I wasn't a big spice person) and he told us he could have them make the dish without the chili to make it not spicy. I really appreciated that he offered that up because it showed he was paying attention to my likes and dislikes and it also showed that this place makes everything fresh- the chef was clearly making the sauce per order and was able to customize ours to meet my (bland) needs. The lamb was amazing. Super tender and really great sauce. We ended up eating the entire plate- like every last bit of it- even the little pancake like thing it came on. It was SO tasty. I dipped everything I could in that sauce. We got a side of asparagus with XO sauce- still not sure what XO sauce is but it was good. Just tasted like regular asparagus so maybe skip this if you're looking for something a little more flavorful. All in all it was a great experience. The atmosphere was great, the waiter was attentive and friendly, and our food came out quick and tasty. My one complaint is that I don't really think the prices reflect the food. Yes, it was good- but do I think I should have paid $36 for the diced lamb? Absolutely not. This was a wonderful place to stop for date night. I may come again if we aren't sure where else to go but, living in NYC, I'll probably tire out my other fancy dining options before I decide to come back here.

Really fun place to stop a taco craving. Ordered the fish taco platter. Very nice. I'm not a fan of slimy fish tacos. Mad dog cooks the fish firm, adds so much more flavor to the taco. Very thin corn tortilla. Only issue was that the platter should have had quattro tacos. Once we dug through the toppings generously applied atop, we discovered only tres tacos! A-yeeeeeee! Brought it to the server's attention, and she was ON IT. Server said she informed the manager and they wanted to offer us a complimentary dessert for the error. This hombre never says no to complimentary dessert. How do they know me so well?!It was national ice cream day, so I thought to make it INTERnational ice cream day I should have the Mexican fried ice cream. WOW! It stole the show. Seriously, this was the best dessert I've had in a long while, and I've done a LOT of dessert, folks. Mad Dog is good. Tacos were very nice, service, as mentioned, did me right, but save room for dessert. Finally, Mad Dog touts 36 tequilas to try. I'm a taco and dessert guy. No tequila for me. Bueno!

I came here for lunch with a friend on a Friday afternoon since it was close to my work.  The place was surprisingly packed for lunch on 2nd Ave.  The place was bigger than I expected with a lot of tables and a large bar area.  We sat at the bar since we didn't feel like waiting for a table.  They have pretty good lunch specials, $12 entrees which come with miso soup or salad.  The entrees included chicken, steak, shrimp, or veggie with no extra charge which was nice.  I ordered the miso soup and the drunken noodle with chicken.  Despite the restaurant being packed, the food came out pretty fast.  The miso soup was packed with ingredients (seaweed, enoki mushrooms, tofu) and quite a large portion.  The drunken noodle had a good spicy kick to it and wasn't too greasy.  It also was a large portion.  Service was okay, quick and attentive.  The place was better than I expected since Murray Hill doesn't have good Asian places.  I would come back to try their other dishes for lunch.

Nice and lounge-y new restaurant without any wait (yet), because it's a bit hard to find (discreet entrance with no sign then go up to second floor) and still under the radar.Food is more modern than the average Korean spot on the block, nicely presented, and less oily.  The menu didn't come with photos so a bit in the dark when we were ordering, but we ended up enjoying all the dishes.Ambiance is nice and conducive to conversation - ever so slightly dimmed lights in a trendy industrial looking high ceiling space with nice stereo speakers.  Not as rowdy and packed like many other Korean places on the street where you lose your voice by the end of the meal from shouting so much.  Definitely above average service.I would avoid sitting in the high chairs area as the tables there seem more closely spaced (it's a personal pet peeve that I really don't enjoy having to hear strangers' dating stories while at dinner) and just plain less comfy.Portions are big and we couldn't finish two entrees plus one appetizer between two people.  Good choice of a regular spot in Ktown - assuming the wait time stays short.Music was dialed up at 8.  So depending on what you're looking for, might want to go before/after 8.

Came here for brunch for the first time with my mom, aunt and grandmother. I was the only one that partook in the unlimited boozy brunch. I had some flavored margaritas that were pretty good. Definitely got a good buzz after 3 of them. For food we shared a guacamole that was delicious, it also came with a few different sauces. I picked a salad to have as my main, not sure which one it was but it had so many good things on it! Very good, though I wished they gave it to me mixed. All the different ingredients were in a line in the salad when I got it. My aunt really enjoyed the enchiladas!

This place is too hit or miss. The biscuit was tasty, crumbly and buttery. The chicken was okay--the salt added to the top added a depth of flavor, but it all felt a little lacking.  I also noticed that when I asked for the coleslaw on the side I lost the sauce that's supposed to be with it so that may have affected the flavor. However. How. Ever. This place has the saddest mac and cheese I've ever had the depressing misfortune to try. It had zero cheese flavor, and was more pasta and bread crumbs than mac and cheese. I'm mad I wasted those calories on trying it. Hard pass. I don't think I'll come back because that mac was an insult.

Tried this place for restaurant week. I've been to different Brazilian Steakhouses but definitely hands down on this one. Fast pace but never rushed if you only flip to the no sign. Their salad bar quality was incredible. So many varieties, very fresh!!! We would love to go back!!

Title: Quick Korean Fix in the Neighborhood

During a recent neighborhood stroll, hunger struck and we found our remedy at a cozy little eatery that takes a page from Chipotle's book, but with a twist—serving up Korean fare instead. The food quality is pedestrian, which, for a connoisseur of Korean cuisine like myself, means it falls short of more authentic experiences. But, in the spirit of fast food expectations, it's unfair to nitpick. The establishment shines as a no-fuss, convenient option, especially for local employees seeking a swift and satisfying lunch. The service is efficient whether you're dining in or grabbing a bite to go. If you're in the area and in need of a quick Korean bite, this spot is worth the swing by.

Bread and butter: 5 starsJambon madeleine: 5 stars. I like crispy cheesy madeleine edges. Brouillade: 4 stars. It's nice to eat once but I probably wouldn't get it again because there are other apps I would love to try. It's very garlic buttery. I do love escargot.Blanquette de Veau: 4 stars. Veal stew in cream sauce. It was exactly as expected and like what I had in France. Can't really complain here. It's a perfect winter dish.Tarte au riz: 5 stars. Nice balance of rice pudding, dulce de leche, and a buttery crust.Baba: 5 stars. I've only had the Italian version of this. This was a really nice delicate version. Must like rum and pineapple. Service was attentive but not obtrusive. Online reservations weren't available - we called and got a table for 6pm. It was starting to fill up around that point.

My second visit to Chef's Table and a reminder of why I consider it my favorite 3 Michelin. Chef Cesar takes quality ingredients and manage to perfectly balance them in his dishes. His uni and truffle toast is second to none. The toro tart was magical. The duck ravioli was a tease that left you wanting a bowl of it. And the frozen souffle was like eating a delicious cloud. I really can't say enough good things about Chef's Table. I will be back yet again.

Title: A Taco Gem Worth the Early Arrival

I swung by this bustling eatery on a weekend, arriving at a strategic 11:15 AM, just ahead of the opening. The anticipation was palpable, with a line already forming. Impressively, the flow was swift, a testament to the restaurant's efficiency. 

A word of caution: seating is a free-for-all, a scant commodity given the crowds drawn here, but it's a small price to pay. The star of my meal had to be the Adobado tacos; the corn tortillas were a perfect vessel for the succulent meat, elevated by the brilliant addition of pineapple. Perfection in a bite!

I also sampled the Carne asada, which, while flavorful, was overshadowed by its Adobado counterpart. A cool, creamy horchata provided the ideal complement to my meal, sealing the deal on a truly satisfying dining experience. Despite the seating scramble, this place is a definite must-visit for taco aficionados.

I was excited to try this place for lunch. It is right by my work and I have heard great things. I created my own rice bowl with shrimp. I love Mexican food and most grab and go places don't have fresh shrimp so this was a plus! The place is very clean and the servers were really nice. The reason why I hide 3 stars is because I really didn't enjoy the food. It was a worse version of chipotle. There is another Mexican place by work called Dos Toros that I much prefer. The prices here are also pretty high. I don't think I will be back.

Title: Quick and Tasty Noodles at Bow Ramen

Bow Ramen impresses with its speedy and savory noodle dishes served in a cozy, easy-to-access storefront. The restaurant is a welcome newcomer, offering hassle-free, sit-down lunches even during the busiest hours. They've also perfected the art of takeout ramen, ensuring the quality doesn't drop when you grab and go.

The evening crowd hasn't caught on yet, so here's hoping their robust takeout service keeps them bustling because these noodles deserve an audience. The menu is concise but thoughtful, featuring six distinctive ramen options, a trio of appetizers, and a range of drinks and customizable toppings.

On my visits, I've twice indulged in the Bow Chili ramen – a hearty, spicy chicken broth with pork belly – and it's a testament to its deliciousness that I haven't yet explored the other bowls. The cucumber salad is a refreshing complement, adding a nice veggie balance to the meal.

Bow Ramen is the ideal spot for an affordable, uncomplicated lunch where you can unwind with a companion. With attentive service, fair prices, and straightforward yet satisfying fare, it's definitely a go-to for a quick, quality noodle fix.

Title: A Step Down from the First Experience

On a return visit to a spot where I'd previously had a splendid experience, I opted for the "Italian Stallion" pizza to share, hoping for a repeat performance. Sadly, the ensemble of toppings—pepperoni, sopressata, broccolini, pickled chili dressing, smoked mozzarella, ricotta, and oregano—proved overwhelming. The pickled chili lent an unexpected fiery jolt, and the broccolini felt like an odd piece in this complex flavor puzzle. To accompany my meal, I chose a beer that was satisfactory. Reflecting on this visit, it seems the particular choice of pizza may have been the misstep. Nevertheless, this latest venture did not live up to the first's high standards.

Seeing as this place was near Boba Guys, my fiancé and I decided to try Peppercorn Kitchen out! On a Friday afternoon around lunch time, Peppercorn Kitchen wasn't too busy; there was only a couple of customers aside from us inside. However, it is a small restaurant with only a couple of tables, so that could have been a contributing factor. We  weren't too hungry, so we split the dumplings and the mala tang. The dumplings were heavenly! They had pork on the inside, although the sweet chili sauce was the definite highlight of the dish! 6 dumplings were large enough when paired with the mala tang. The mala tang was moderately spicy, although it was a bit too hot for us! We didn't have many pieces of fish nor noodles as we would have liked. The mala tang mostly had spicy broth as well as vegetables. Nonetheless, the whole dish was delicious, despite having to wait a while for the mala tang to cool down before we could eat it. Loved Peppercorn Kitchen overall! This place is a bit pricey, but if coming here with someone, the 6 pork dumplings and mala tang will be sufficient to keep you guys full!

I recently have been into dumplings and so was really excited to see what Vanessa's Dumpling was all about! It's a small restaurant and it was very crowded when we went. The food smelt soo good I was super excited to taste it. The home-made dumplings are SO GOOD!Fried Dumplings Cabbage and Pork: These dumplings were filled with a good amount of meat. The dough was crispy, but also a little thicker than the ones I had before. With a little soy sauce and sriracha, the dumpling was perfect!Boiled Dumplings Cabbage and Pork: When i first saw the dumplings, it looked really soft and tasteless so I was not sure if we should have ordered the boiled dumplings. Then on the first bite into the dumplings it was SO JUICY inside!! It was not doughy like I thought. In fact, it was pretty thin layer of dough around the meat. Sesame Pancake with Roasted Beef: The sesame pancake was so fresh and crispy! It was a very neat way of a sandwich. If you love sesame and crispy sandwiches you will not be disappointed with this!Would definitely recommend!

Deciding to indulge myself at this fine dining spot was a decision well made. Initially eyeing the middle-tier omakase, I ultimately surrendered to the allure of the priciest offering – and what a triumphant choice it was! The chefs weren't just masters of their craft but also the epitome of hospitality, readily swapping any offerings to cater to personal tastes.

The omakase itself was a parade of luxury, with each morsel adorned in the likes of uni, truffle, caviar, and the most succulent toro. Every bite sang with complex, harmonious flavors, and it goes without saying that each piece of sushi presented a delight that had me relishing in the moment. No piece was left untouched, no flavor unappreciated.

To top off an already exquisite culinary journey, a complimentary dessert of matcha coconut panna cotta alongside Yuzu sake was served. The panna cotta was so divine, I fancied the thought of seconds – or thirds! This is a restaurant experience I eagerly anticipate to repeat.

One of the best standbys in the city for me -- a place where you know you can get really excellent food that just about everybody in your place will like. Borderline 4/5 stars for me.Latest visit, we came with a group of three and got a lot -- five meats/cheeses (mortadella, prosciutto, squacquerone, parmigiano-reggiano, and the outstanding parmigiano "gelato"), the tortellini in brodo, three pastas (tagliatelle with bolognese, garganelli with cream sauce, and mezzaluna with squash and brown butter sauce), the veal with prosciutto and truffle cream, and three scoops of gelato (ricotta with fig, dark chocolate, and vanilla). The tagliatelle was the last dish we decided to order, and was probably our favorite -- this reminded me of Italy to some extent. Everything else was great as well.

Title: A Delectable Dive into Southeast Asia at Laut Singapura

Having family roots in Singapore and Malaysia, my anticipation was sky-high for Laut Singapura, and I'm thrilled to report it exceeded expectations. The space is massive, revealing an inviting layout, complete with an open kitchen that allows a peek at the culinary action. The decor is a visual treat with its eclectic furniture and vibrant hues.

Laut Singapura kicks off the dining experience with an engaging touch – compressed towels that blossom with a pour of hot water, a neat and hygienic start to the meal.

The Jumbo Prawns in salty egg sauce were the first to impress; their massive size and the succulent, almost lobster-like texture melded beautifully with the salty, savory sauce. As for the entrees, each dish arrived as a visual masterpiece. The Nasi Lemak radiated with vibrant colors, the Indian Mee Goreng made an appearance in an adorable miniature wok, and the Chili Crab beckoned all senses with steamed or fried bun options – I went for the fried, which proved to be an excellent vessel for scooping up that spicy, tangy sauce.

Dessert was no less exceptional with the "Tisu" roti – a gigantic, cone-shaped spectacle served with lychee ice cream. Drizzled in condensed milk and sprinkled with fruity pebbles, it was a playful and deliciously hands-on finale.

I'm already planning my return to Laut Singapura to delve into more of their offerings such as the LaKsa and Satay. If you're seeking an authentic and exuberant Southeast Asian dining adventure, this is the place to be.

Always like to come here for lunch with friends.Reasonable price and great food. Today we order shredded pork with spiced tofu (this is one of my favorite from their lunch special)Chicken with strings beans, pretty good, but taste more on the sweeter side.Long sour beans with minced pork. Very good to eat with rice.We also order spicy boil beef which is not on the lunch special. $16 per person great deal in midtown

During my recent dining experience at the local eatery, the standout refreshment was undoubtedly the Bissap drink—a delightful counterpart to the Jamaican sorrel, minus the ginger kick, which I found quite refreshing. The proprietors were generous enough to offer a sample of their Ginger drink, a potent concoction that was far from sweet and packed a fiery punch reminiscent of pure ginger extract—certainly not for the faint of heart, it left a lasting tingling sensation.

For the main course, I opted for the Lamb gigot. The lamb shank served was impressively sizable, accompanied by a fiery sauce that added a welcome spice to the dish. The lamb was cooked well and the portion generous, easily sufficient for sharing between two diners. As a side, the fried plantains were mediocre but did their job of complementing the meal. Overall, a satisfactory dining experience with a few memorable highlights and generous hospitality.

We were here for lunch on a Sunday. This place was packed but we got seated right away. It was a fun experience being here. We really enjoyed Sylvia going around the table singing and asking everyone where they were from. We ordered a smothered chicken and a salmon bite. The chicken came with 2 side dishes. The food was good and the service was good too. We thought it was a bit pricey. But overall fun experience.

Title: Convenient Breakfast at a Bustling Chinese Bakery

I stumbled upon this delightful Chinese bakery perfect for a swift breakfast on-the-go or a speedy snack during your daily commute. Nestled just outside Chinatown, the bakery occupies two small adjacent storefronts; my visits have primarily been to the right side, where I grab an array of buns.

Despite the compact space, expect it to be packed during rush hours as locals dash to work or drop off their children at school. The pricing won’t break the bank, with most buns ranging from $1 to $2, and they don’t skimp on variety either! I've particularly enjoyed the ham & egg, swiss, and roast pork buns, not to mention the sweet coconut filled ones.

Besides buns, the bakery offers a selection of coffee, tea, and cold beverages, along with cakes. An insider tip: post 7pm, brace yourself for a queue as they discount the fresh daily buns. Remember to hit the ATM first—this gem is cash only!

Title: Disappointment Over Gluten-Free Options at NYC Pizzeria

I recently visited a pizzeria in NYC expecting a variety of gluten-free (GF) options, as advertised online. Unfortunately, upon arrival, we were informed that they had discontinued their GF offerings, leaving my daughters with limited dining options. For an establishment that has promoted GF alternatives heavily, a notice about such a significant menu change should have been communicated online for diners who rely on this information.

Beyond the GF mishap, the restaurant itself fails to impress. As a resident of Sacramento, I can name at least five superior pizza places in my hometown. Although service was adequate, likely due to a notably empty dining area, it was not enough to redeem the overall experience.

The concept of selecting different pizza crusts is intriguing, and I will admit, the crust was the highlight of the meal. However, that alone isn't enough to warrant a return visit, given the plethora of excellent wood-fired pizza options elsewhere in the city. The lack of transparency regarding their GF options casts a shadow on the establishment's reliability. My final word: don't bother with this place, especially if you're in search of GF pizza.

Title: A Surprising Pizza Haven Near Work

I recently stumbled upon a hidden gem near my workplace, a pizza spot I'd been curious about for some time. Opting for the artichoke and crab slices, I was immediately taken by the unique approach to the crust—a thicker base to support a luxuriously heavy sauce reminiscent of a rich Alfredo, teeming with spinach and artichokes.

The crab slice, which initially had me doubting the authenticity of the seafood, turned out to deliver on flavor, with what I believe were true crab chunks. The crispy crust harmonized with unexpected dollops of what seemed like ricotta – a delightful touch, though both slices bordered on too salty for my taste, leaving me quite parched.

At $6 per slice, the price mirrored the size – generous to the point where half a slice was enough for the moment, with the remainder making for a satisfying later meal.

Service was notably efficient, with a brief wait for my slices, despite the budding line at 1:30 pm. All in all, it's a place I'd return to, perhaps with a larger drink to temper the saltiness of their otherwise delectable pizzas.

Bo Ky is nothing fancy in fact it's extremely non-fancy. If you're looking for a quick meal, and a good bang for your buck, this is your place.Also you should like Chinese noodles because that's mostly what they serve. I had the duck noodle soup with mushrooms. It hit the spot. I'm not sure what region this cuisine is from--the menu has a lot of different noodle soups and some appetizers. I didn't find any plates of vegetables and the appetizer selection is not wide. The food comes really fast and the service is fine.I've eaten at a lot of places in Chinatown in New York. I will keep exploring.

Title: A Hidden Brunch Gem near Columbia

Located conveniently next to Columbia University, this charming brunch spot deserves more than its current three-star rating. This was my second visit, and the restaurant continues to impress with its stunning décor, varied seating options, and an outdoor area perfect for pleasant weather.

The menu selections were delightful. The fruit plate ($11) was a customizable treat—kudos to the attentive staff for accommodating my brother's fruit preferences and throwing in a delicious mango surprise. My classic Benedict featured a handmade chicken sausage patty, a testament to their commitment to quality, though the accompanying home fries could have been slightly better cooked. While I didn't taste the waffle my brother ordered, it looked tantalizing.

Service was exceptional, with our server eagerly checking details for us and going above and beyond. My brother’s request to purchase a coffee mug from their collection resulted in a complimentary gift from the manager, which was a lovely touch.

I recommend this spot for anyone looking for an excellent brunch experience with attentive service and quality food. A solid choice that's certainly worth more praise.

During my recent trip from New Jersey, I was compelled to visit this pizzeria twice in a single week — a testament to its allure. While the prices may seem steep, the pizza warrants every penny with its delectable flavor. Perfectly situated for a pre-cinema bite at Village East Cinema, the restaurant provided a convenient and satisfying dining experience.

The staff deserves recognition for their exceptional coolness and kindness, enhancing the overall atmosphere. Despite its popularity, seating was readily available, and service was impressively swift. The standout recommendation? The upside-down slice — a culinary masterpiece that's simply irresistible. Do yourself a favor and savor this gem of a pizza.

Tucked away in a cozy nook that evokes the charm of an old speakeasy, the establishment greets its guests with a warm and comfortable ambiance. The cocktail menu shines with creativity, showcasing mixology that is both delightful and skillful; each concoction is a testament to the bartender's prowess.

Though the menu may not boast an extensive food selection, and prices tend towards the higher end, the quality and taste do not disappoint. A standout dish, the pastrami short ribs, is a culinary triumph that alone warrants a return visit.

Complementing the dining experience, the staff's attentive service ensures a pleasant visit, making it an enjoyable destination for those in pursuit of fine cocktails and delectable meals in a snug setting.

Title: A Delightful Date Night at a Charming Thai Spot

I recently visited a quaint Thai restaurant for date night and the experience was quite remarkable. Admittedly, Thai cuisine tops my list of favorites, so expectations were high. Despite not accepting reservations on Fridays, the staff estimated our wait at 1.5 hours; however, we were pleasantly seated in just 45 minutes.

The two-story establishment boasted stylish decor and a cozy bar area. Upon seating, we were greeted with a complimentary tangy butternut squash soup—a nice touch to whet the appetite. For starters, we indulged in curry puffs and dumplings—both exemplary and generous in portion.

Our main courses consisted of flavorful drunken noodles and a savory ground chicken dish topped with rice and a fried egg. The only hiccup was my egg was served cold, which was a bit disappointing. However, the drinks more than made up for it. The 'Amethyst' and an unnamed tequila cocktail were exceptional, and being served drinks during the wait was a thoughtful gesture.

Despite the place's compact size, which might feel cramped to some, the overall ambiance and service made for a wonderful dining experience. I'm thrilled to have checked this Thai gem off my Yelp list. Highly recommend for a filling and enjoyable meal.

It's quite spacious! I really loved the seating deeper inside, it's booth style with wooden wall dividers type (see pictures) and so clean and comfy looking! Came at 12PM on Saturday with reservations, but the line was already quite long minutes before the restaurant even opened. 12-1PM is definitely fine without reservations for a small party (2-4 people) - you won't experience a wait for a table. Tantan: spicy miso pork udon. Reminiscent of a ramen broth, but also stands out. Very rich and creamy, but not served hot enough that I could really enjoy burning my tongue on a cold morning :D Limited portion of pork, and the runny egg didn't actually add anything to the tastes of the bowl, but overall, this was reallllly delicious. Loved the soup! The noodles were thinner than I thought it would be, and mine was just slightly overcooked (not too much bounce). Also, these noodles looked more like flat noodles than udon, actuallyNiku: short rib with honeycomb tripe. Such generous portions of short rib and honeycomb! Four pieces of each type of meat. Loved the fatty pieces of the short rib, but not as tender/soft as I've had from other braised short rib places. Broth is cleaner and much sweeter - a big difference to the miso version. Served searingly hot (unlike my tantan!) the noodles are also different, thicker and bouncier. We actually ended up dipping the udon from the niku bowl into the tantan broth :D Nonetheless, we polished this super quick! Definitely hype worthy and the portions are filling enough as well.

Just had the escargot and duck at Marseille. 1 st time. Spur of the moment. Absolutely delicious. Duck was medium rare and delicious. Escargot was to die for. Holy cow. I'm in complete heaven. Can't wait to come back. Love French food and this  French Restaurant is the greatest. OMG. The service was unbelievable as Well.  From the manager to my awesome server. Thanks

Heading to this city gem for a combined bachelor/bachelorette brunch turned out to be a fantastic decision. The place offers an all-you-can-drink package that's both affordable and lively. While their brunch menu doesn't stray far from the classics, every dish is executed flawlessly, especially the truffle fries which are a must-try. They nailed the truffle flavor, making it a crowd favorite. Everything served was not only delicious but also visually appealing. I'd definitely recommend this spot to anyone looking for a great brunch experience.

I've heard of this place being a fancy hot pot place, and the claims are true! It's definitely an upscale hot pot place that's great for a nice date. The decor and architecture are both chic and cozy. The high ceiling also makes the restaurant seem exceptionally spacious. The food is no doubt fresh, it's just that sometimes the raw pieces of chicken that came in a small bowl looked a little unappetizing. And there was also a long and old loofah-looking seafood piece that none of my friends knew what it was (I was only told that it was crunchy and had no taste), and it was just weird. Be careful of the spice levels! If you're not sure of how spicy the broth will be, I suggest that you start off easy because the medium spicy level was too spicy for me! But the mushroom broth was delicious! It is rather expensive, considering that it is an upscale place, but I didn't leave with a full stomach, even though we paid $60+ per person. The waiters were very attentive and always filled our glasses up. I would come for the overall experience.

Title: A Square Slice of Satisfaction at Detroit Pizza Frenzy

I recently joined in on Detroit's pizza craze and stopped by a popular spot on a Friday evening. To my delight, there was no wait, which is always a bonus for those quick bite cravings. The display boasts a variety of pizzas, including traditional and square slices, all temptingly placed behind glass.

I opted for the Grandma slice, priced at $4.50. It was generously ladled with tomato sauce and topped with a perfect measure of cheese. The highlight was the crust: crisp without a hint of charring, which really elevates the whole experience.

While the price point doesn't quite match up to the value found at some other local Detroit-style pizza joints, and seating is limited, this place stands out as a solid choice for a speedy and satisfying pizza fix.

Best Dim Sum by Time Square.Me and one other person had their food three times during my six day stay in New York.  Dim Sum Palace was nearby, they offer free delivery, serves dim sum until 1:30am, and is damn good.  We had our food delivered twice and dined in for one night.  We enjoyed their popular Shrimp Dumplings and Shu Mai.  I also loved their flash fried green beans with garlic and creamy egg yolk bun.  Yum!!!!  Everything is always served hot, perfect, and fresh.  When we ordered their food came much faster than it said it would.  When we dined in we had great service.  Their pricing is reasonable and they have a large variety.  I recommend if you want some dim sum in the area.

Title: A Unique Japanese Dining Experience

Last night's dinner at this Japanese-inspired restaurant was a delightful surprise, particularly for a Thursday evening. There was no need for a reservation, and the service was impeccable - attentive without being intrusive.

The highlight of our experience was the interactive element where we got to catch our own striped bass. The preparation of the fish was equally impressive, offered both as tempura and sashimi for shabu shabu. The use of the entire fish was admirable, with a flavorful miso soup crafted from its bones.

To accompany our main adventure, we ordered tako wasabi and tori kara-age, both of which were prepared to perfection, attesting to the kitchen's skill.

The evening concluded with a birthday celebration for my friend, complete with a song and a dessert, which made for a memorable finale.

Intrigued and satisfied by this innovative dining concept, I am already planning my next visit to explore more of their menu. This is a place not to be missed for anyone looking for an engaging and delectable meal.

I love Vietnamese food, but this place was quite the disappointment. My friend and I both LOVEPho do we decided to give this place a go...but none of the dishes were to our liking. The papaya salad was shaved in thick strands that made it hard to chew and the flavor wasn't fully infused. The shrimp vermicelli was really bland and we barely touched it, and the red curry was really nothing special. I thought the best dish of the night was the lemongrass pho, but my friend didn't even like it.Not sure how this place has such high reviews or if it's because it's a neighbourhood gem in that area....but the food really doesn't stand up to all the other competitors in the city

Title: A Gem on the Upper East Side - Flex Mussels

I absolutely loved my first visit to Flex Mussels! The happy hour set the tone for a delightful evening, with appetizing mussels drenched in savory sauces that I thoroughly enjoyed. But the oysters took it to the next level – they were the stars of the show. 

The service here deserves a special mention. The servers were incredibly warm and personable, enhancing the already inviting atmosphere that strikes the perfect balance between sophistication and a relaxed vibe.

As if the seafood wasn't enough to ensure my return, the meal's sweet finale of exquisite donuts sealed the deal. Flex Mussels is without a doubt a standout spot in the Upper East Side, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Title: Irresistible Hot Pot Haven in the East Village

I recently indulged in an all-you-can-eat hot pot experience in the East Village that I can't stop raving about. As a hot pot novice, I was blown away by the delicious variety of broths complemented by an ample selection of meats. While the vegetable options could have been more extensive, it hardly detracted from the overall enjoyment. The service was exceptional—attentive and polite, effortlessly managing our large group. They even offered a whimsical birthday serenade courtesy of the Monkey King, making it a fantastic spot for celebrations. If you haven't yet dived into the hot pot dining scene, this charming spot is the perfect place to start.

While visiting NYC for the weekend, my friend decided to take me to bottomless brunch here. This place was decorated adorably and the ambience was very classy yet still cozy. The waiter was also very attentive, checking in on us regularly, and not trying to rush us out the door since we had to wait a little bit of time for the rest of our party to show up.All of us got the bottomless brunch, which was a pretty good deal. $22 for your choice of bottomless mimosas, aperol spritz, and a couple of other cocktails that you were able to mix and match. Not a bad deal.For the entrees, I ordered the The Ouefs Meurette en Cocotte (pictured in the skillet) and it was incredibly delicious. The entree itself was pretty filling, and the only critique I would have is that it was a little on the bland side. My friend ordered the Boba Burger which came with a side of fries and honestly it was one of the best burgers i've had. If I had to critique one thing, that would be the prices. There was not much for what you did get, and the entrees were all similarly priced although ranged in sizes greatly. Although there was a time limit for the bottomless brunch, we did not feel rushed at all. All in all, with some minor critiques, it was an incredible meal in a cozy yet stylish and sophisticated restaurant.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at what could only be described as the original high-end red sauce establishment. The star of the show without a doubt was the veal parm. Quite simply, it was the best I have ever tasted—a truly phenomenal culinary experience that sets a new standard for this classic dish. Highly recommend a visit for anyone seeking the pinnacle of comfort cuisine with an upscale twist.

So I took my little sister to this location since there's restrictions of age in the other one and i must say I think I liked this one a bit too much . It's close ! My margarita was awesome . My little sister had a great time for her birthday , service was awesome they wasn't pushy "! Cough cough .  Food didn't take 5 hours , cough cough.  Came out with the candle and the little fudge cake and the happy birthday song and my sister was happy , and we called it a day ! They made it happen .  Would go back for another margarita !

The lunch special here is a great deal and is offered on weekends too! The sushi rolls are slightly smaller than normal, but pack a punch in flavor and texture. Salmon skin, salmon avocado, and shrimp roll were freshly made and delicious. There was no need for soy sauce because the rolls already were full of flavor.The picture of the BBQ pork pig buns posted on Yelp was the reason for dining here. Cute pigs faces on dumplings appear to deceive. I learned not to judge a bun by it's cover. Skip it unless the sole purpose of ordering is to take a picture.

Title: A Spirited Brunch with a View at Midtown’s Rooftop Retreat

My recent visit to this 4th-floor rooftop eatery in Midtown was a mixed bag, yet undeniably lively. The panoramic view coupled with a vibrant atmosphere made for an engaging brunch experience. However, conversation competed with a rather booming soundtrack that had diners shouting over tunes.

The unlimited mimosa deal at $25 for 90 minutes presents a good value for those looking to indulge, while other beverages are standard fare. Service seems to fluctuate – we encountered a tepid response from our bartender during the early moments of our visit, but thankfully our server’s patience and amiability somewhat redeemed the day.

Food quality hovers around average, meriting a respectable 3-star rating. It's the fun vibes, including impromptu Conga lines, that elevate the overall mood. Decor is charming, and the clientele is energetically sociable, making it a potential go-to for group gatherings.

One caveat is the establishment's policy on gratuity. An automatic tip was added even for a simple drink at the bar which felt unjustified, especially with the bartender scarcely present. The same applied to our small group dining bill – more understandable, yet still a point to be mindful of. Keep an eye on your receipt, as discrepancies have been noted by others.

In conclusion, if you're seeking a brunch spot with an effervescent crowd and scenic views, this place may warrant a revisit, though it's wise to manage expectations on the culinary front and scrutinize the bill.

Yayoh was our hostess and she was the best. So good at suggesting dishes and was friendly the whole time. So this place is the new addition in the Nordstroms downtown. The store itself is so big and spacious. There are some nice dine in options and cafe options through the store. We tried out Jeannies and so glad we did. I got the shell pasta with meatballs. It's kind of a baked dish with the cheese melted on top. So good! My friend had the shrimp salad and that was pretty good too. But the best dish of them all was the brussell sprouts. Trust me on this one. Just order it. And don't share cause it's that good. Really nice for lunch or if you want a quiet place to catch up with friends and it's not crazy crowded.

I love this place. I've been coming for years and it never disappoints. The best sangria that I've ever had. Their food is consistently delicious. Love the chicken, the paella, and sweet plantains.  I've ordered other items, but these are may favorites. Their Chinese dishes are really good too, but this is what I come for!        I love the staff and the atmosphere at both locations. There's usually a bit of a wait any day that you go. So, just be prepared to stand at the bar and take advantage of your time by drinking some sangria

We had a great time at St. Tropez! Great food and wine list and our server was attentive and informative. He helped us decide on wine options without being pushy. They also didn't rush us even though it was a busy night.We ordered the Burrata appetizer and it was yummy! For my main entreé, I got the scallops and it was also very good. Just the right amount of seasoning. It was also a great price for $22 and my wine was only $12 which is on the lower side for NYC.I would come back there again and maybe try their happy hour.

I recently dined at Thai Son, acting on a tip from my cousin, and discovered a little piece of Vietnam right here in NYC. It's refreshing to find a Vietnamese-owned restaurant, suggesting authenticity and a deeper connection to the cuisine.

My wife and I began with the vegetarian summer rolls, which, while only average, were a decent foray into the starter menu. The real stars of the meal were the entrees: my wife's flank pho was exceptional, rich in flavors, and an absolute delight. My grilled pork rice dish did not lag behind, delivering a punch of well-balanced spices and perfectly cooked pork.

If you have a palate for Vietnamese food, Thai Son definitely stands out in NYC. It's a place worth revisiting, even if just for another bowl of that remarkable pho or a serving of the vibrant grilled pork rice.

For those seeking a quick, wallet-friendly bite, this neighborhood pizzeria certainly delivers. With plain cheese slices at just $1 and the luxury of adding extra toppings for a mere 50 cents each—then briefly baked for that perfect melding of flavors—it's a steal. The convenience factor is unbeatable, especially for locals like myself. The pizza here is a solid go-to for a satisfying, no-fuss meal.

Good music, great vibes. We wanted to finish off our last night in the city bar hopping and did a quick search on Yelp. This place had great reviews and served food until 11pm! We ordered their signature tailored burger and quinoa salad. The burger was so thick and juicy I had to squish it to bite into it. The salad was well dressed and the quinoa paired well with their Mediterranean dressing. The portions were large enough for us to share. My husband enjoyed his moscow mule and I enjoyed my beer on tap. They had great music playing in the background and the atmosphere was pretty upbeat.m. Overall, I was impressed with the staff, especially the bartender who was holding it down by himself. We met great people and got local tips. Give them a try if you're looking to turn up in the city. ;)

The bar is spacious with multiple flat screen TVs in every corner of the room and 2 large screens opposite of the bar. It's a sports bar, but the decor is more chic' and modern with an upscale feel to it.  I've been here twice to watch the GOT episodes. The first time was the Winterfell battle and they were understaffed for the event. They had 1 waiter and 2 bartenders to take the orders and a few bus personnel to serve the food and handle the tables. I give the staff a lot of credit handling the situation and managed to serve us and other patrons.  The second time, there were plenty of staff at the bar, but no wait staff. We ordered our food at the bar, and then the food was served to us via number system. We had to take the initiative to get a bottle of water and condiments because there was no wait staff.  The staff was attentive and served as much as a good to handle the load of patrons.  I had low expectations of the food since it has so so yelp reviews.  The food was actually delicious. The prices are on the higher side, but to be expected of the area.  The hanger steak flatbread to start was outstanding. My friend ordered it during the battle of Winterfell and we opted to order it again for the Bells, and it was as good as the first try.  The apple poppy salad was top notch with all those amazing ingredients: cranberries, apple, frisee, roasted pecans and the yummiest vinagrette. The sandwiches were decent; we had the macaroni burger and it was as greasy as expected, but I still enjoyed picking at the macaroni oozing out of the burger. The short rib grilled cheese I would skip because the bread didn't hold up and it was soggy at the end.  The beers on draft were delicious.

Title: A Convenient Taste of Joju's Banh Mi in Midtown

I've long awaited a visit to the famed Joju from Elmhurst, and thankfully, their new Midtown outpost brought the experience closer to home. Sampling both the Sweet Joju with its trio of pâté, ham, and caramel pork and the savory beef bulgogi banh mi, replete with kimchi, each sandwich was enjoyable yet leaves room for refinement.

The pickled carrots and daikon, critical for that banh mi zing, fell short with an overly mild and sweet profile that cried out for more acidity. Additionally, while the baguette was reliable, it missed the hallmark airiness and crackling bite one hopes for in a top-tier banh mi.

Nevertheless, these are competent sandwiches worth trying. I suggest enhancing your order with a hit of spicy mayo, jalapeños, and their luscious aji verde, best enjoyed on the side to preserve its integrity. Solid, with potential for perfection, Joju is still worth the visit for a savory fix in Midtown.

Title: Convenient Pre-Show Dining at Mamasita's with Room for Improvement

Mamasita's offered a convenient dining spot before our Broadway evening, greeting us with salsa, guac, and chips - a welcoming, if not complimentary, start. While the house margaritas we ordered had an odd, soda-like taste, revealing the use of a pre-made mix was a letdown for fresh cocktail enthusiasts like us.

The enchiladas suizas with chicken were a highlight, accompanied by tasty pinto beans and rice - a recommendable dish despite my preference for black beans. Although the surprise tres leches cake was a kind gesture, it failed to impress, especially since it wasn't suitable for my vegan companion.

Service at Mamasita's shined for its accommodating nature, comfortably bridging our time before the show. Here's hoping Mamasita's improves its margarita game to match the quality of their food and service.

Tasty sandwich from a place I had never heard of.Stopped in and got the William polls special sandwich from meal pal. it came with ham, turkey, Swiss cheese, coleslaw and Russian dressing. It was a rather nice sandwich for mealpal, size wise and tasted very good.I noticed they sold a lot of other snacks and such, but didn't get a chance to really get anything else.

Title: A Southern Brunch Delight

As a connoisseur of Chicken & Waffles, my latest brunch adventure led me and a friend to this charming spot. We were greeted by a wonderfully attentive waitress, brimming with helpful recommendations for our inaugural visit. The cocktail highlight was a French 75 that truly rivaled any I've enjoyed since my move to the city – a perfect start.

The star of the show, Chicken & Waffles, did not disappoint. I come with a critical Southern palate, and my standards were met with exceptionally crispy, Cancún-seasoned chicken. The waffles were airy, though a hint of vanilla and cinnamon would have been a personal touch of perfection. Nonetheless, the heavenly brown butter maple syrup they served came to the rescue, rounding out a rather pleasing flavor experience.

I walked away from this experience already planning my next visit to dive into their happy hour offerings. This place is certainly worth penciling in for a return!
Everything here smells, looks and tastes wonderful. We went on a Saturday afternoon and it was mobbed. Had a few small bites and all were great. I'll try again on a less crowded day.

My group of friends decided to stop in the Plaza Hotel Food Hall after checking out the Christmas decorations during the holiday season.  After browsing several of the different food joints, I settled on Luke's Lobster and it did not disappoint!  I had the lobster roll with chips and a drink (and of course, I requested a pickle once I was at the pick up counter).  The lobster was so fresh and the hearty pieces of meat had a delicious sweet flavor to them.  The roll was perfectly toasted and had a light buttery finish.  The topped off the roll with a light dusting of old bay and it made for a great sandwich.  The drink selection is a diverse group of "craft sodas" in glass bottles like root beer, ginger soda, and other fun flavors.  I had the ginger soda and it was crisp with a nice bite.  Overall a great experience and I would gladly come back.  Next time I want to try the 3-roll sample meal or some of their chowder--both looked excellent!

The 4th Marinara just opened, moving further downtown into Flatiron now, this time just like the OG one in that it's greatly needed with no other good slice joints near it.It's a very solid New York style slice, but some of the squares here I think are more worth the trip and are the standouts, especially the excellent very thin and crispy square MVP slice, and the very thick and also great stuffed crust pepperoni slice.Just came for slices tonight so I didn't check, but I believe they have lots of other hot food too, like some great mozzarella sticks. This is a great new spot for a quick bite in the area, so I'll definitely be back.

Stars : 3.5Our food was great. I like the lobster ravioli. It had caviar in the sauce. Yum!  Mildly seasoned and filling portionMy couscous had too many peppers in it. It's watered the dish downWe enjoyed the atmosphere and decorThe staff was gracious and professional yet super rushed. Made us feel uncomfortable.  It's my birthday and I wanted to feel the ambiance and enjoy ppl watching. It appears they want you outta there at a fast food type of timing rate. After much pressure and not even an hour there, we left. Came, saw, done.

Title: A Relaxing Saturday Feast at Ashoka

My recent visit to Ashoka turned a lazy Saturday into a delightful Indian buffet experience, complete with the required post-meal nap. The restaurant's cleanliness and spaciousness set a positive tone from the start. My friend and I were pleased with the variety, as the buffet offered around nine dishes, including three meat options.

While the food's lukewarm temperature was slightly disappointing, the flavors mostly made up for it. The chicken tikka masala and fish curry were standouts, both incredibly tender and beautifully seasoned. Unfortunately, the tandoori chicken, despite its fine spices, had a questionable taste that suggested it had been marinated too long.

The vegetarian options, like palak paneer and fried peppers with mushrooms, were appetizing and well-prepared. The naan bread was the undeniable star: warm, soft, with just the right touch of crispness.

At $15 per person, Ashoka's value for money is impressive, making any minor flaws easy to overlook. I'm already excited about my next visit!

Title: A Satisfying Lunch Stop at Thy's Noodles

During a bustling day downtown, I stumbled upon Thy's Noodles, a new eatery still boasting its grand opening banner. Its allure drew me in after just a block's hesitation. Opting for the spicy noodles with minced chicken, I found the heat level a tad milder than preferred, but the flavors were still very satisfying.

Thy's Noodles serves as an ideal lunch destination for those looking to enjoy a quick, hearty meal before diving back into the work grind. While I'm curious whether the noodles are freshly made on-site, their quality certainly didn't leave me wondering about their tastiness. Definitely worth a visit for anyone in the area seeking a comforting bowl of goodness.

Title: Disappointing Downturn in Service at a Beloved Korean BBQ

My latest visit to what was once a favorite Korean BBQ haunt left me disillusioned. Despite being a loyal patron since 2016, I was compelled to downgrade my previous 4-star rating after a series of letdowns.

On an evening that should have been filled with the familiar warmth and attentiveness, the service noticeably faltered. Typically bustling atmospheres can challenge any establishment, but it's no excuse for the dip in service quality - a crucial element that complements the dining experience.

The once seamless flow of banchan to our table turned into a cumbersome task, as requests had to be continually made for these essential side dishes. An experience heightened by servers' ability to anticipate needs was replaced by one that felt neglected.

Worse still was the rushed and careless grilling of our meat by the server. Urging them to slow down to avoid charring our meal contradicted the excellence we'd come to expect.

Perhaps it’s an issue of understaffing, but until the restaurant rectifies the slippage in both service and consistency, my friends and I have resolved to explore other options. With a heavy heart, this visit merits a 3-star rating – a testament to the underwhelming service that overshadowed what used to be a gem of a dining experience.

I can get a little picky because I grew up having Korean food. I mainly went for the naengmyun (cold noodles in beef broth), primarily a summer dish. We ordered the spicy rice cake and General Cho's to share too. I really liked the rice cakes here. Don't expect softer rice cakes though. Theirs is a bit fried on the outside, slightly sweet, and has a nice bite to it. I'm normally not used to this, but it was a win in flavor and texture. The General Cho's was okay. It's heavy on the batter, but it's super cripsy and coated in a slightly sweet/tangy sauce. It's basically the Korean version of General Tso's and it's pretty common in Asian fusion restaurants. The naengmyun was so nice and cold on a hot day. I loved the beef broth as well. It's a very salty dish so don't make the mistake of drinking too much broth (was dehydrated the rest of the night). The noodles were nicely cooked. I only wish I could add a bit more vinegar and mustard for spice, but maybe I could have asked for it. If you want a summer dish, definitely go for the naengmyun.Overall, I liked Hanjan. The menu here isn't extensive though, and it's a bit pricy. It seems to be well suited for groups since the dishes are all shareable. It kind of stinks the banchan here is $10 because those small side dishes are traditionally free with Korean meals. Otherwise, Hanjan was pretty okay. I'd go back for the naengmyun and rice cake.

This is the best seafood cajun place I tried. I am a big fan of seafood boiled in spices. I went for the craw fish and king crab combo. Everything was very fresh. The craw fish was a lot bigger than the craw fish I had from other places. King crab legs was the best thing. Never miss it. In 1lb, I got just 2 legs. So it was big, and had a lot of meat in it. Instead of trying other crabs with a lot of shell, I recommend king crab. For sauce, the boil sauce was very good. That is their signature sauce. I went for spicy, and I would say that is the right level of spiciness for me. If you enjoy spicy food, I would recommend you to go for spicy instead of medium. Spicy was not too spicy for me.

Title: Second Visit Solidifies Stellar Experience

Our decision to give this restaurant another shot proved to be excellent. Our initial visit was good, but some aspects didn't quite hit the mark. Returning on a Friday night changed everything—this time, it exceeded expectations.

We kicked off with the Caesar salad and veal meatballs, both of which set a high bar. The meatballs were tender and succulent, while the salad was perfectly dressed. The main courses maintained the high standard; the veal Milanese was exemplary in its breading and fry, accompanied by a fresh and well-seasoned arugula topping. Meanwhile, the pasta with lobster savored by my companion was nothing short of scrumptious.

The well-paired wine and a finely crafted old-fashioned enhanced our dining experience. Although we had no room for dessert, it’s on our list for the next visit.

A heartfelt thanks to Suzanna and the entire staff for their outstanding attention to detail and service which made our meal truly delightful. We're already looking forward to returning.

Title: Perfect Pit Stop for Breakfast Pastries

I am a regular at this gem of a bakery conveniently perched above the W. 4th St. subway station, which has become my go-to for a quick breakfast en route to work. They win me over every time with their delectable, freshly made warm pastries. The star of the show is the steam egg creme bun—utterly divine and a must-try, though you'll want to arrive early as they sell out quickly!

Despite being a haven of carbs, the affordability is a huge draw. The buns are priced below two dollars, and the pastries are under three, making it a wallet-friendly choice for mornings when time slips away. Besides the egg creme bun, I highly recommend their flavorful tuna pastry and the classic egg tart.

On a special note, I once ordered a birthday cake from here, and it was a hit—perfectly balanced, not too sweet, just the way I like it. If you're looking for a satisfying, budget-friendly breakfast spot, this is the place to be.

Always a go to place for hotpot! I've also tried their hotpot + bbq combination and you definitely go with a prepare mentality. Soup bases i've tried are:- spicy mala: beginning is sliiiightly spicy but obviously gets diluted towards the end- chinese herbs: i honestly dont really recommend this bc the soup gets really sweet bc of the dates in it -- so i was getting a little nauseous towards the end of my meal bc it was so sweetTheir sauce selections are great and i really recommend the satay sauce and their hometown sauce!! As for quality of ingredients, i would say its pretty up there; i've never gotten something and been skeptical of it. Altho they do sometimes forget / mistake your ingredient requests so you have to be mindful of that+ you eat free on your birthday!
Great pizza slices and even better staff. The cashier was very nice and very helpful. If you ever get a chance please visit.

I had a delightful dining experience where the chicken al pastor tacos and fish tacos were the stars of my meal, bursting with authentic flavors. The duck enchiladas were another standout, showcasing a perfect balance of rich taste and delicate texture. To elevate the meal, a bottle of Spanish red wine provided a wonderful accompaniment, enhancing the overall enjoyment of the cuisine. Highly recommend for a taste of culinary excellence.

I really wish I could give this place four and a half stars because it really deserves that extra half star. This place has probably the best veggie ramen I have tried in the city. The broth contains an explosion of flavors that you normally miss out on when ordering veggie ramen other places. There are lots of vegetables and other stuff in the ramen that makes it so much better than other places where you get veggie ramen and its like two mushrooms and watery broth.  The place itself is super cute, tucked away around 145th street, it is easy to get there from the train or from Columbia Medical center. It is a great date spot. The space is intimate and small but not overcrowded. The lighting is just dim enough to add to the intimate feeling of the restaurant. The drinks looked amazing, but I didn't get a chance to try them this time. I definitely will be back!

Summary:Came here for lunch and the food was alright. It fits the bill of serving you sushi, but there was nothing interesting or spectacular beyond that.Food:Ordered the sushi and sashimi lunch set, which came with the basic sushi, nigiri and sashimi pieces (tuna, salmon etc.). Nothing particularly standout or special form this. Also had the uni nigiri piece, and it was decent, but the uni quality could have been a little bit better (it wasn't bad, just not particularly standout).Service:A little slow, but not bad. The place was surprisingly not too crowded during Wednesday lunch.

Title: A New Year's Eve Indulgence at the Hilton Garden-Midtown Hotel Restaurant

I recently rang in the new year with a delightful dining experience at the restaurant connected to the Hilton Garden-Midtown Hotel. Convenience is king here; you can glide seamlessly from the hotel's check-out desk to your table without ever braving the elements outside.

After a lengthy drive from Virginia, my initial plan was just to savor a few drinks before evening festivities. However, I stumbled upon their mac and cheese burger, and it was an absolute game-changer. This masterpiece is sinfully delicious–imagine the creamiest mac and cheese cascading from a succulent burger. It's a heart-stopper in the best possible way, and undoubtedly a calorie bomb, but "on Gawd," it's worth every last bit of indulgence.

Admittedly, prices are on the higher end, but considering the quality of what you're getting, my wallet didn't complain. Service was a tad slow, but given it was New Year's Eve and staff was seemingly short-handed, this was a minor hiccup in an otherwise superb experience. 

In sum, if you find yourself at the Hilton Garden-Midtown, treat yourself to a meal at their connected restaurant–your tastebuds will thank you.

We came before the Matinee show for brunch.It was a very hot summer day and teh front Windows were open. Gladly, we were sated inside where it was well air-conditioned, so that was good start when you have both options available for you.Bloody Mary was very tasteful, spicy but it came served I a room temp, in spite of all the ice in it. Don't the bartender know rule #1 of vodka (which he wasn't shy with)? Keep it in freezer (or at least refrigerator) and shake it well with lots of ice before mixing! And so is the bloody mix-refrigerated. Steak and egg was good but medium rare steak came out more  medium and very chewy. Breakfast taco salad was small but tasty. Service was VERY good, pleasant, friendly, attentive. Hence the 4th star.

My partner and I chose Cafe Clover for our date night, seeking a balance between healthy dining and a delightful meal, and we weren't disappointed. The staff impressed us with their exceptional service, and the menu was nothing short of incredible, offering a plethora of exquisite choices. The ambiance added a lovely touch to our evening, enhancing the overall experience. I have nothing but praise for Cafe Clover; it wholeheartedly exceeded our expectations.

I had been craving Singaporean food for quite some time and I'm so glad I was able to stop by Laut Singapura. They offer so many traditional dishes in an upscale environment with great service. The food came out pretty fast since we got there pretty early. We ordered:Salty egg prawns - The salted egg coating on the outside was super-rich from the egg yolk and the prawns were MASSIVE. This was one of our favorite dishes.Singapore Hokkien Mee Noodle - This is definitely my favorite Singaporean food after having studied abroad there, so I was super excited when I saw it on the menu. It has a strong seafood flavor and the broth was not too thin. They give a good amount of shrimp and seafood but the chili paste was too sweet.Kway Teow - I think great kway teow should have more of a smoky flavor from the wok and be a little more salty and rich. The kway teow here was a little too sweet for me but still tasted pretty good. The noodles were a good texture and the chicken was cooked well.Beef Rendang - Rich coconut flavor and the beef was very tender. Hainanese Chicken - Chicken was super tender and flavorful, rice had a nice garlic flavor and you could taste the chicken broth in it tooMango Pudding - very creamy and strong mango flavorI would recommend checking this place out for their variety of Singaporean/ southeast asian food and quality!

The space is clean and the service is quick.  I was very impressed with the broth and the short ribs.  The fact that you get dessert or a bubble tea with your entree is the icing on the cake.  I come here for dinner frequently and it's on Yelp cash back so they are throwing the kitchen sink at you.

sad to give this place a poor review, as i was looking forward to trying this vegan restaurant. i ordered the mapo tofu, and while it tasted great  there wasn't all that much of it. the dumplings were bland and were delivered without any dipping sauce to perk them up. overall the portions here are way too small for the price to justify me ordering again.

Title: Hidden Gem in the Heart of the City

Don't judge a book by its cover—or a restaurant by its facade. BaoHaus might appear unassuming from the outside, but this small, gritty spot packs a flavorful punch that's worth exploring. Propelled by curiosity after seeing owner Eddie Huang on TV, I ventured to taste the much-acclaimed BaoHaus sandwich.

Despite its modest size, slightly larger than a slider, the Chicken BaoHaus delighted my palate, striking a perfect balance with its seasoning. It's a reminder that good things often come in unpretentious packages. Make sure to stop by BaoHaus when you're in the area; it's a testament to the adage that sometimes the best flavors are found where you least expect them.

I gave Omakasa a second chance and was again disappointed. I had the vegan impossible bao / bun again and it was dry again. Still tasty because it's impossible meat, but it should not be dry, per the owner's comment on my previous review. The impossible patty was also so tiny compared to the bun, so there are too many meatless bites. I also had the veggie crunch salad, which was a complete disaster. Is bitter melon supposed to taste like laundry detergent? Even when I removed all of the bitter melon, the flavors of the salad were terrible. And I love salads! I wonder if the chefs here don't eat salads and assume they are supposed to taste bad? If you want a little vegan meat snack, sure come for the impossible bun. But proceed with caution on the salads.

Title: A Slice of Paris in Manhattan: Maison Kayser

Review:
Venturing into Maison Kayser in Manhattan feels like a quick jaunt to a Parisian boulangerie, a charming aspect that's consistent across their numerous NYC locations. The Croque Madame I sampled maintained an authentic French simplicity, with its thin profile and tasty ham, albeit a touch more cheese and Bechamel would have perfected it. The Oeuf Cocotte Champignons was a revelation; the poached egg was a masterpiece, with the yolk providing a rich complement to the divine mushroom and red wine sauce – a delight when mopped up with their sublime French bread.

What sets this location apart is its warm service, which is unusually attentive by Parisian standards. Maison Kayser delivers both on atmosphere and taste, making it a must-visit for those yearning for a French culinary escape in the heart of New York.
Delicious food that feels healthy, but I think the price is too high for what it is. Salmon bowl. My chosen sides were the cucumber salad and the kale salad. After tax, it's about $15.50.

Title: A 5-Star Feast Worthy of a King

My dinner experience at this bustling restaurant was nothing short of exemplary—a well-deserved 5-star experience. Despite arriving on a busy Sunday evening, there was no delay; our table was ready the moment we walked in.

My husband and I opted to indulge in the main attraction straightaway—the steaks. The King's prime rib he ordered was a thing of marvel, a juicy behemoth so generously portioned, it promised leftovers. My choice, the fillet with au poivre sauce, was a triumph of culinary excellence, aged and rested to sheer perfection. Accompanying our mains, the fries and mushrooms were equally commendable.

Despite the presence of a large group that could have overwhelmed the kitchen's pacing, our dinner arrived swiftly, cooked to perfection, and without any compromise in quality. Even the au poivre sauce stood out as the best I've ever savored.

We rounded off our meal with a shared cheesecake, which concluded our dinner on a decadently high note, leaving us delightfully overstuffed. Service throughout the evening was attentive, and the wine list piqued our interest with its intriguing selections.

There's no doubt about it—I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Title: A Gem in the Upper West Side

My latest dining experience at this adorable spot on the upper west side was absolutely delightful! Despite the distance, the journey was completely justified by the charming ambiance, delectable cuisine, sensible pricing, and superb service.

Upon our 6:30 PM reservation on a bustling Friday evening, the importance of booking ahead was clear. Our waiter was prompt and attentive amidst the crowd.

The complimentary bread was a welcomed starter, setting the stage for the main courses. The chicken parmigiana, with its generous portion, was scrumptious and certainly warranted a take-home box for leftovers. The rigatoni gamberi with a luscious pink cream sauce, succulent shrimp, a generous sprinkle of cheese, and earthy mushrooms (a personal substitution for broccoli) was nothing short of pasta perfection.

For anyone seeking authentic Italian fare, this place is a must-visit. Just be sure to save room for the next day – the portions promise a delicious encore!

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience Post-Celebration

I recently visited a delightful restaurant after a birthday party and was lucky to find a spot in the bar area. The service was top-notch, with a notably charismatic waiter who added charm to our evening. Taking advantage of a Yelp check-in offer, we enjoyed a free cocktail alongside our entrees, kicking off the night on a high note.

To start, the complimentary chips were a welcome touch and set the stage for the delicious artichoke appetizer – a must-try. The steak frites I chose for my main course were cooked to perfection, bursting with flavor and tender in every bite. The portion was generous, especially the scrumptious fries, of which I could only finish half.

Dessert was the highlight; the apple pie served in a skillet was so divine that it haunted my dreams with its taste. The restaurant had a relaxed ambiance, the right balance of energy and acoustics that allowed for comfortable conversation.

Returning after several years, I was reminded of what a gem this place is. I highly recommend a visit for those looking for great food and a laid-back vibe, serviced by an exceptional team.

Title: A New Banh Mi Hub on Water Street

If you're a banh mi aficionado weary of the limited options outside Chinatown, take heart; there's a new contender right by the Starbucks and Dunkin' Donuts on Water Street in South Street Seaport. With multiple visits under my belt, I can vouch for its consistency. Although the Special Baguette often sells out, the Grilled Pork Baguette steals the show. It outshines the standard sliced pork option with its savory addition of pate, truly hitting all the right notes.

Not only is the food mouthwatering, but the service is also lightning-fast. Expect to have a warm, delectable sandwich in your hands within 10 minutes—perfect for a swift lunch break. When in the Seaport area, don't miss out on this gem for a quick, satisfying bite.

Title: A Hefty Yet Tender Steak Experience at Ikinari

My craving for steak led me to Ikinari, a spot with a heartening recommendation behind it. The decision to indulge in their 14 oz ribeye proved to be spot-on, as each slice was exceptionally tender, making it a memorable meal for both of us.

I experimented with the steak sauces offered, finding one overly sweet and the other slightly less so. However, my recommendation would be to forgo these and let the quality of the meat shine with just a sprinkle of salt and pepper.

The cost did make us raise our eyebrows, as the meal was not on the friendly side of our wallets. Be prepared for prices that reflect the establishment's confidence in their cuisine.

A word to the wise on the meat's marbling – while the inner marbling contributed to the delightful tenderness, the exterior fat was more than I bargained for considering the price. It is something for the restaurant to tune up, given the premium cuts on offer.

In conclusion, Ikinari serves up a steak that's hard to forget, but make sure your budget is ready for the splurge and you've got an appetite for indulgence, both in flavor and fat.

We have strolled pass this restaurant for the past 3 years and never tried dining there. Today we changed that. It was impromptu for a Friday night  but in spite of having no reservations, they seated us in about 2 min. The place was busy, as it typically is when we have walked by. The waiter was very nice and knew his stuff. He attempted to seduce us with the evenings 3 course Lobster special for $40 but I immediately stopped him since someone (who shall remain unnamed) has a shellfish allergy (kill joy). The meal must go on, therefore we ordered anyway. Bridgette had there Chicken Pot Pie (which was huge) and she washed that down with a regular Mojito which she really enjoyed. I ordered a sausage & cheese individual pizza with  BBQ Chicken slider (2 sliders on the plate). I opted for only an unsweetened Iced Tea since I knew I had to work late tonight. We both enjoyed our meals, our service and the decor. Neither one of us had room for dessert so we didn't get a chance to review the menu. Maybe next time.....and there will be a next time!

Dining at this gem in Little Italy is a guaranteed delightful experience. The starters, from the earthy beet salad to the rich antipasto platter and creamy burrata, set a high bar of tastiness. The main course pastas, particularly the linguine brimming with seafood, hearty lasagna, and the standout gnocchi Sorrentina, were all exemplary. Not to overlook the pizzas; the classic Margherita was simplicity perfected. Coupled with the warm and friendly service, this is an eatery that ticks all the boxes for a fantastic dinner outing.

Decently priced but they give you a GOOD amount of food. Was craving halal food and passed this place, decided to get the chicken gyro platter. The platter comes with a side (I choose rice).Overall the chicken was perfectly cooked, amazing flavor, juicy, and would definitely get that again. The only things that I was lacking was the white sauce and hot sauce- the white sauce was a bit too thick for my liking and they didn't have the classic red spicy sauce, instead it was legit hot sauce you'd get from a bottle.Regardless, it did hit the halal spot I was missing and there was plenty of food for two servings.

The Mermaid Inn has great happy hour deals on food and drinks until 7pm daily. It's a great place for value, particularly given that it is located in Manhattan in a happening location with a nice interior. I ordered two fried oyster dishes at $5 each. Each dish comes with two oysters, so it was four in total. They weren't bad. The sauce maybe could have used more spice, but still a good deal. I also ordered fried calamari at $7.50. It was a decent sized basket, plenty for one person. I like how they don't just serve rings. There are the funny looking bits too, which are good. It came out kind of lukewarm and a bit drier than I expected, but certainly not the worst I've had.On offer during happy hour is also a miniature lobster roll at $9. It's pretty small, but again, a good deal if you're not that hungry but still want to satiate a lobster fix.
