It's not as seasoned or as tender as the lobster at Luke's, but still pretty good.Lastly, I tried one of the oyster specials. This one was a Smith Island Bay, Virginia-based oyster called Chunu. Oyster Rater says these are "The same oysters as Misty Point, tumbled frequently so they stay small and form deep cups. The closest thing you'll find on the East Coast to a Kumamoto (which was the idea)." I am a big fan of Kumamotos and mostly all West Coast oysters, so I gave them a shot. They were actually a bit bigger than Kumamotos, almost like Totten Inlets. They did have deep cups, but they present very much like East Coast oysters on the palate, with salt and brine flavors and none of the creamy texture of West Coasts.I washed all this down with a tequila citrus cocktail for $9. Very refreshing to cut through all the richness.The Mermaid Inn is a pleasant experience if you can get there early enough without having to wait for a table and to be able to take advantage of the happy hour offerings. I can see why people like it.

If you come here to order only their Ramyun, I can see why they got their Michelin star, however everything else missed its mark for me. The dishes are beautifully presented, however the whole point of food is its taste, and it was, honestly, very lacking. We ordered the following: - Toro Ssam Bap- Jeju Chicken Wings- Fish Coop Ramyun- So Ramyun- Oishii berries for dessert- Jeju Gose (beer brewed with Yuzu)- Elderflower LemonadeBased on the highly recommended suggestions on Yelp, we ordered the Toro Ssam Bap. This dish encourages you to make your own hand roll: It comes with fatty tuna, scrambled egg, and rice with a side of seaweed. It seems they intended for the saltiness of the seaweed to bring out the flavors of the rest of the ingredients, however a touch of salt or even a few drops of soy sauce on the fatty tuna would have brought this dish to another level. The wings were perfectly crispy, however I've had better elsewhere, and it is definitely not worth $14. The best part of my meal was when I finally got to try their ramyun. I really enjoyed the Fish Coop. I wanted a lighter option for dinner, which led me to order this particular ramyun. The broth of this dish was amazing, and flavorful. The dill is a nice surprise to the palate, and the pickled cucumber gives this dish a very nice, refreshing note. The pork belly was cooked to perfection, and the noodles were perfectly al dente. There is a hint of spice coming from the jalapeno, but the dish itself is not spicy. Their drinks are good too, I liked the Elderflower Lemonade, and the Gose beer. The beer is only brewed for Jeju Noodle bar, and the yuzu in the beer is apparent, and the beer itself is very light.Overall, I would come back for the ramyun if I was in the neighborhood, but I honestly would skip out on everything else. Service was really good. The waiters were very attentive, and friendly. They currently have one dessert, which is 3 seedless strawberries for $9. It is nice and sweet, but I would recommend saving your money on this one.

Han Dynasty has been a staple of my lunch option ever since I started working around here in Union Sq. I quite enjoy their Spicy Szechuan lunch menus and so far none of them has disappointed me. I've also gotten take outs here after ordering through their own online website, its a bit shame that they're not part of Grubhub but in the 3-4 times I've ordered here they never have gotten my order incorrectly. The food is always ready before the time they quoted and still very warm by the time I walked to my office.This latest time I tried both their Cumin Chicken and Dry Pepper Chicken. Both are really quite a economical meal at around $10 each. The portions were quite decent certainly enough for a single person for a very heavy lunch. I quite like how they allow you to choose the spiciness of the dishes right on line from scale of 1 - 10 definitely very helpful to those like me that can't handle very spicy foods.Since their orders were always ontime I never had to wait when I go pick up my order and the hostess has always greeted me quite nicely making the whole experience very pleasant. The food is very authentic and not overly salty and I look forward to coming here quite regularly in the future.

Guang Zhou famous rice roll that came to NYC? Guess I gotta try it out. Get the beef and shrimp rice roll! My favorite one.  The food comes out pretty quick and when I went there was a small line out the door. The congee was pretty good there as well because it comes with a lot of ingredients in it. The curry fish balls were puffy and good. I got a beef rice roll and added egg but I feel as if I didnt really need to add the egg. The fried cruller roll was good too!

During a lunchtime visit in search of comforting congee, I popped into what appeared to be a quintessential Chinese eatery, offering an array of traditional dishes and barbecued meats. The congee served was pleasingly hot and thick, with toppings provided in ample quantities. However, a peculiar odor emanated from the meat, raising concerns about its freshness—fortunately, this did not affect the taste. Curiosity might bring me back to sample their wonton noodles and beef chow fun noodle.

This is a pretty good slice of pie I had here.  You pick whatever pizza slice you want and wait a few minutes for them to warm it up.  You can see they got their assembly line system to perfection as you see the workers in the back working furiously to bake and pack their pizzas!  The slices range around 3-5 bucks depending on the toppings you want.  The sauce was really good and I love the cheese on top.  Great place for a quick slice of NYC pizza!

Negative first - they do the suggested tip on the after tax amount.  You don't tip on tax.  Pay attention to your bill.  Calculate the tip yourself pretax.I randomly found this spot while looking for a place for a quick dinner.  Reviews seemed good.  The place wasn't too packed when I arrived so that was great.  No need to wait for a table.  Eat, pay and then leave.  Nice and simple.  All ramen spots should be like this.   Oh and this place is also awesome because it is owned by Japanese people and run by Japanese.  I'm a little biased when it comes to my ramen, so when I see it is owned and run by Japanese, that is a positive sign. One thing I do suggest is for the place to install more bag hooks underneath the bar area or put some hooks up for bags/coats, especially now that it is winter time.  It is not fun to eat with a big coat on or with a bag on my lap.Karaage - this was okay.  I would give this a pass because this was pretty bland and tasteless.  The majority of the taste came from the sauce, which is not a good sign.  The chicken was also kinda stringy inside.  Tan tan - this was surprisingly good!  I wasn't too sure what to expect to be honest.  The broth could have used a little more flavor, but everything else was good.  I felt the broth was on the safe side and not as rich or flavorful as it could have been.  The mugifuji pork shoulder was absolutely delicious though!  Looking it, I thought it was going to be tough and dry, but this was melt in your mouth and full of flavor.  I would get extras of this.  The egg also looked a bit dry and overcooked, but the egg was actually pretty good.  It was very soft and tasty.  The ramen noodles itself was okay.  Overall though, I would eat this again.  It was a solid bowl of ramen.Tonkotsu - same comments regarding the noodles, egg and pork shoulder.  The broth for this was much better.  It was more flavorful and rich.  I could have used a little more flavor, but it was good enough.Overall, this is a great spot for the area.  Prices are a bit high so they should adjust accordingly.  I think if they have a loyalty program via a stamp card or something, that would keep me coming back.  Definitely not bad ramen for the area.  Happy I came!

Very pricey for korean bbq but it is authentic korean bbq. The location is nice and very personal for a first date. The staff was very attentive. They would cook and cut the meat for you. The meat was ready in about 10-15min. Had marinated beef and pork belly. The meat was very rich and the beef was my favorite, very chewy with lots of flavor. Gave lots of sides as usual. Enjoyed it despite the high price relative to BBQ. My boyfriend liked it a lot as well!

Title: A Classic Rodizio That Never Disappoints

I revisited a classic Rodizio restaurant that I used to frequent years ago and was reminded of how delightful their buffet is, particularly the salad bar which remains impeccable. Timing my visit before a Broadway show proved to be a perfect choice for dinner. The service was outstanding as always, with the bartenders and waiters providing top-notch attentiveness.

While the meat selection was succulent and drool-worthy, I'd suggest a pinch more seasoning for those who prefer a bolder taste, though the current lighter touch will surely appeal to those who enjoy a fresher flavor. With already high expectations, I look forward to my next visit – especially on an evening when they feature their live band, which is bound to be a fantastic experience. This establishment continues to be on my go-to list.

Title: A Delicious Find That Delivers on Its Promises

I'm delighted to report that the restaurant not only lives up to its well-deserved buzz but also delivers an exceptional dining experience. My visit over the weekend proved that despite its bustling atmosphere, efficiency reigns with a mere 25-minute wait for our group.

The interior, while unassuming, offers a tranquil backdrop to the culinary adventure that awaits. The menu shines with standouts including the savoy shitake and shrimp buns, rice cakes, and notably, the two cold noodle dishes which, although I can’t recall their names, were truly memorable. Each dish was bursting with flavor, asserting the kitchen's commitment to a palate-pleasing experience. 

While the pork ramen was satisfactory, it slightly missed the mark for me due to a broth with an overwhelming bacon essence. Nonetheless, even this small critique doesn't overshadow the overall excellence of the meal.

With great food and service wrapped up in a comfortable setting, this is a spot I'm eager to return to.

I recently dined at a restaurant that truly impressed me with its offerings. The iced crawfish was the highlight of the meal - each one was generously sized and exuded freshness. The menu boasted an array of options including flavorful Cajun seafood, succulent BBQ sticks, and a variety of regular dishes, all of which were exceptionally tasty. The cleanliness of the establishment was noteworthy, maintaining a neat environment. Additionally, the service was commendable, adding to the enjoyable experience. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone with a penchant for well-prepared seafood and great service.

Title: A Delightful Surprise at the "Pulled Bacon and Eggs" Experience

I recently ventured to a local eatery, lured in by a craving for an egg sandwich and intrigued by their menu's "pulled bacon and eggs" offering. Admittedly, when the dish arrived, I had an initial moment of surprise, expecting something a bit different. However, the meal exceeded my expectations. The bacon was unexpectedly sweet and succulent, perfectly complemented by a softly cooked egg, crisp peppers, and the ideal choice of bread, which altogether satisfied my craving and then some. The aioli was the standout, adding a delicate, sweet spice that brought the sandwich to a new level.

Whilst the sandwich itself was a hit, I did find myself wishing for a double helping of eggs to match the hearty size of the bread. The side salad, meanwhile, seemed superfluous to the main event and didn't leave an impression. Additionally, the side of potatoes and garlic was a letdown, lacking in flavor even with the accompanying sauce - a rare misstep in an otherwise enjoyable meal.

Service was prompt and friendly, contributing to the restaurant's inviting aesthetic and vibrant atmosphere. With whispers of live music and happy hours, I'm already planning my next visit. Overall, it's a strong 4 out of 5 stars for me - a return is certainly on the agenda.

Title: Charming Pre-Dinner Cocktail Experience at the Bar

My friends and I stumbled upon a delightful spot for pre-dinner drinks around 7:45 PM and were pleasantly surprised to find that we could comfortably squeeze around a small table at the bar. Our server, Darlene, was the highlight of our visit – her ability to navigate the bustling space with a tray full of beverages was nothing short of impressive. She was incredibly polite, weaving through the crowd with a gentle "excuse my ladies," which made us feel more like welcomed guests than obstacles.

The drink selection was a treat, with the espresso martinis standing out as a group favorite – they were the perfect pick-me-up. The bar boasted an array of specialty drinks, providing plenty of options to suit all our preferences, and the inclusion of mocktails was a thoughtful touch for anyone preferring a non-alcoholic option. Darlene's excellent service and the quality of the drinks ensured that our night started on a high note.

The decor of the place is quite interesting. I'd like to praise the zeal and skill of strategically placing the name of a dish right above the restrooms sign.Even though the interesting decals preceded the sumptuous food, the rest of the evening was quite delightful. We ordered a number of dishes including Hainanese roast chicken fried rice, Spicy night market noodles(the best), curry laksa with steamed bread(SO good!!!) and a Shrimp dish which was on the specials menu. Drinks were also glorious, especially Geylang. Can picture myself downing several of these with my girlfriends next time.Coconut sticky rice dessert is avoidable. Definitely recommend this place for its swift service and delicious food.

Discovering the sibling to the Canal Street Market favorite, this spot offers a delightfully less crowded atmosphere. Here, the dedication to freshness stands out as they steam rice rolls to order. Opting for Joe's combo, I indulged in a savory blend of shrimp, pork, and beef. The flexibility to substitute bean sprouts with corn at no extra cost was a welcome touch. At approximately $9, the plate was both satisfying and generous, making it an excellent choice for a quick and casual meal.

Came here on a pretty chill Easter/Passover weekend for brunch. They were able to seat us at the bar immediately. The service was excellent. They kept our coffees filled and were consistently checking on us, but not in an overbearing way. They were all very pleasant even though the restaurant was quite busy. I ordered the green shakshouka and liked the presentation immediately. The food itself was just okay. I hate to say it was bad because maybe I just ordered the wrong thing for myself? My friends enjoyed their food, but a star was lost over this dish. It wasn't horrible or anything, it just wasn't all that great! Kind of a disappointment. Either way, I would come back to give this place another chance if I'm in the area!

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience with a Few Hiccups

I recently dined at this charming eatery and came away thoroughly impressed. The food was very good, hitting all the right notes from appetizers to dessert. The Razor Clams, chopped and seasoned to perfection, were a delightful start to our meal, while the Brussel Sprout Salad impressed with its incredible flavors. Both come highly recommended.

Our main course, the namesake Mafaldini, was a scampi lover's dream and satisfied with its just-right portion size, contrary to some critiques I've seen. To cap the meal, the olive oil cake accompanied by homemade rum raisin gelato was divine.

Though our waiter occasionally disappeared, the rest of the staff seamlessly ensured we were well cared for, underscoring their team's attentive and service-oriented nature.

The drink offerings, the Allora and the Irish Clover, however, were a touch too sweet for my palate, despite their eye-catching presentation.

In summary, the delicious food, friendly staff, and cohesive teamwork made for a great dining experience that has left me eager to return.

I recently dined at a unique Thai spot in Hell's Kitchen, which offered a refreshing departure from the usual fare in the area. Although on the pricier side, the distinctive menu justified the cost. The venue comfortably accommodated our party of six without a lengthy wait, a pleasant surprise for a bustling Saturday evening.

The culinary experience was impressive, with each dish presenting a robust burst of flavors. Highlights included the succulent short rib and a particularly memorable panang beef. The curries stood out with their aromatic spices and heat that tantalized the palate. Regrettably, the red rice did not meet expectations, proving to be grainy and not the ideal companion for the entrées. Next time, I plan to opt for the white rice. Despite this minor letdown, the dinner was a delightful adventure, and I'm eager to return.

Venturing into the unknown culinary delights at Caravan of Dreams, I approached my meal with a blend of excitement and curiosity. My choice, the Lemon Cashew Pasta, was a tantalizing but somewhat unbalanced affair. Although the freshness of the asparagus and the rich, creamy delight of the cashew cheese hit all the right notes, the intensity of the lemon hijacked the dish, overshadowing the subtler flavors I had hoped to enjoy.

On the brighter side, the accompanying side salad was a tasty, well-executed addition to my meal, offering a refreshing counterpoint. The dessert, a modest brownie, promised a departure from cloying sweetness, which it delivered, but unfortunately at the expense of vibrant flavor.

Despite these mixed experiences, Caravan of Dreams has piqued my interest enough to warrant a return visit. Next time, however, my adventure will lead me to different dishes in hopes of uncovering a more harmoniously flavored meal.

I recently dined at a charming little Thai restaurant that truly impressed me with its incredible $8 lunch special. The spicy basil chicken was perfectly seasoned, bursting with flavor, and the green curry was equally delightful with just the right amount of heat. The accompanying salad was a fresh start to the meal. Cozy ambiance and great value – an absolute must-visit for Thai cuisine lovers!

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Busy Memorial Weekend Dinner

I visited the restaurant on a crowded Memorial Weekend Friday night with a few friends. Despite the bustle, the staff admirably managed to squeeze in an extra person at our table, which was appreciated. However, it was surprising and disappointing to find they had already run out of oysters by 7:30 pm.

Our experience with the food was underwhelming. The Balthazar salad was remarkably bland, offering just a lonely, small piece of ricotta cheese that did little to elevate the dish. The Bouillabaisse, which was highlighted as the dish of the day, fell short of expectations. Priced at $47, and with anticipations of a flavorful and exotic stew, it was decidedly too acidic with an overpowering tomato base. The promised seafood - a few pieces of fish, a single lobster tail, and a couple of clams - failed to justify both the cost and the dish's featured status.

On a positive note, service was a highlight; our servers were both friendly and attentive. The ambiance of the restaurant was inviting with warm lighting and comfortable booth seating, which did enhance the overall dining experience. Despite the comfortable setting and attentive service, the food's lack of flair made for a forgettable meal.

My boyfriend and I walked in at around 6 PM on a Friday and got seated right away. We shared the carrots, crispy onions, cacio e pepe and fusilli. The only thing I didn't love was the onions, which surprised me because they're so popular. Just not my thing. Anyway, the pasta was incredible and the service was impeccable. Adorable flamingo wallpaper in the bathroom, too! 4.5 stars.

I recently visited this restaurant for my sister's birthday celebration, and it was a delightful dining experience. As a carnivore at heart, I was thoroughly impressed with the Meat Lover's option, offering a variety of succulent and flavorful meats. While the specific names escape me, as they weren't labeled, the standouts on the platter were memorable for their taste.

In addition to the meats, the soup and salad were also of high quality and did not disappoint. This place is perfect for special occasions or if you're planning to dine with a large group—there's plenty to go around. It's an ideal choice for birthday gatherings, providing a festive and abundant meal. I'm looking forward to my next visit to enjoy the generous spread once more.
Do Not try the Steak Here!I know I know my fault this is a great Greek Fish restaurant but i am a meat guy... big mistake, the have no idea how to cook one, off even where to buy a good steak either.

My husband and I made our first visit to Bill's and it definitely won't be our last! Fantastic meal and service! We had the wedge salad, beet salad, beef Wellington and bone in filet. All were exceptional. Probably the best Beef Wellington I have ever had! Nice decor and atmosphere too!

It took me awhile to come back but I'm glad I did. I came here because I found out our city council is voting on whether or not to ban foie gras (possibly this month). For those interested, the New York Times and Eater have deep dive articles into the issue, challenging the idea that foie gras is cruel, and giving voice to the argument that these ducks are actually healthier and better treated than the majority of our farmed animals. You can contact city council woman Carlina Rivera who is currently refusing requests by owners to visit the farms that would be closed if the ban passes. They actually have a whole section on their menu addressing the issue of foie gras, with both sides of the issue being represented with viewpoints from Hudson Valley Foie Gras Farm as well as PETA. I started with the seared foie gras with balsamic glaze. I don't particularly care for balsamic, butI don't often see foie gras seared and I had only been eating terrine so I decided to try it. I loved the texture and taste of the foie gras itself, meaty, like a steak or a portobello mushroom. Instead of a pate flavor, it tasted more like the delicious fatty portions of duck breast. The glaze is very thick, and while it was not my favorite flavor profile the quality of the dish made up for that. I also ordered the escargot with butter, garlic, and shallots. My waiter said they made the best in the city and they are some of the best I've ever had, though I admit to not having them in many places. The garlic and shallot flavor is aggressive - in a good way! The bread they endlessly bring to your table is perfect to sop up the leftover butter - make sure to scrape out the best parts from inside the snail shell, all the flavor collects there. For my entree I had their Mussels Creoles. Served French Caribbean style (how could I order anything else?) in a pink rum sauce with heavy cream, herbs, and chorizo. I was worried the chorizo would be too aggressive and overpower the other flavors, but it ended up pairing well. This was such a luxurious and well done dish, with a nice spicy sweetness. I also got the "small" and for $15 this is an absolute steal! It's a huge portion, a full bowl, I can't imagine what the large must look like. Service was very sweet, ambiance romantic and intimate, music lovely. They also have Kwak beer, a delicious 8.4% Belgian beer I don't much see outside of craft beer bars.

Title: A Valentine's Day to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

My partner and I celebrated Valentine's Day at [Restaurant Name] and had an exquisite dining experience. Unlike many establishments offering limited set menus on special occasions, here we were pleasantly surprised to order straight from their regular selection – a freedom we appreciated.

We commenced our culinary journey with a shared spec pizza and squid ink linguini. The pizza, boasting just the right amount of truffle, complemented by the umami from prosciutto and rich cheese, was simply sublime and easily ranked amongst the best truffle pizzas I've savored. The linguini was equally impressive; twirls of perfectly al dente pasta married harmoniously with a garlic and olive oil sauce, generously adorned with a variety of seafood.

For our main course, the branzino was a revelation, grilled to perfection with a hint of rosemary and thoughtfully presented deboned. Accompanied by a vibrant salsa verde and tender white asparagus, these sides were the perfect foil for the delicate fish.

Regarding value, the food was reasonably priced, especially for NYC standards. Our entire meal totaled around $200, but considering the wine accounted for half of that, the quality to price ratio for the food alone was outstanding.

Service at [Restaurant Name] was a mixed bag. While our main waitress was the epitome of sweetness and professionalism, some supporting staff members dampened the experience slightly with their lack of finesse, being somewhat unprofessional when serving dishes and rearranging silverware.

Despite this minor hiccup, I wholeheartedly recommend [Restaurant Name] for anyone seeking an exceptional meal in the city. Whether it's a special occasion or just a night out, this place is certainly not to be missed.

Tucked away on the fringe of bustling Bryant Park, you'll find a culinary retreat that draws quite the midday crowd. My party of 14 ventured into this hotspot for lunch only to be met with a perplexing culinary experience. The mussels were a letdown, embroiled in a consistency battle and swimming in an overly thick coconut broth that left me questioning the rice accompaniment's purpose.

Their chicken wings showcased a spark of creativity with an inventive glaze, though the wings themselves failed to take flight beyond average. Calamari was par for the course, thankfully lifted by a zesty spicy citrus vinaigrette. Aesthetic efforts were not amiss, as every dish presented a visual feast, complemented by serene, zen-like table settings.

Despite my personal grievances with the food, which included a truffle oil dominance on the menu that isn't to my taste, the restaurant earned redemption through impeccable service and a tastefully designed decor that leaves an impression.

Not one to be deterred by a single experience, I commend their four-star service and ambiance and remain open to revisiting, perhaps for a hopeful redemption at brunch.

I'll start by saying the reason for the 4 stars not 5 is due to cost. My salad was $15 which to some might not be a big deal but to me its a little pricey.Now for the food. Omg my salad was delicious!! I got the Edamame salad. I added Baked Pesto Tofu, not usually a pesto fan but it was so good, it gave the tofu so much flavor. I would definitely come back here again if the prices were lower. As for the service, the woman taking the orders was very friendly, however the one lady making them was rude. I'm sure she was just overwhelmed with so many orders and no help but you still have to be nice to customers.

Went with a group for a friend's birthday. We made reservations due to the group size. The staff was very accommodating and friendly. We had the queso dip and guacamole which was really tasty. Ordered the chicken tacos with rice. The chicken was authentic and very flavorful. The rice was okay but needed some sauce to flavor it. Everyone seemed to enjoy their meal and the overall experience there. Overall, good atmosphere and experience especially due to group size. The staff was friendly and worked to accommodate us. I would check this out again when return to the area. Good food, prices, and nice space.

This place is top notch. Waited until my second visit here to write a review. Here are my takeaways:1. This place is incredible and I'm shocked their overall rating is 3.5 (inaccurate)2. If you want cheap food, don't come here (and don't do them the disservice of complaining about it on Yelp). And honestly, it's not THAT expensive.3. If you don't want to wait to be seated, don't come here either (they're popular and worth the wait. Go walk the high line until they're ready for you).4. Always order the biscuits regardless of what your entre is.Anthony served my girlfriend and I on both visits. I was impressed both times that he remembered our orders without writing them down (even special requests). He was polite, attentive and checked up on us multiple times. This time I ordered the Abe Lincoln Breakfast and I give it an A++! Portions sizes are perfect, very filling and I cleaned off the entire plate. Such a great variety of different breakfast foods and very fresh. I love the silver dollar pancakes because I get a nice taste but do not over fill. Sausage and Bacon (I subbed bacon for ham) is stellar and I've never loved grits but these are fluffy, light and tasty.Last time I got fried chicken and pancakes. They were amazing but I enjoyed Abe Lincoln's breakfast more. My girlfriend got the avo toast and pancakes last time and they were also A+. We split the mimosa flight, delish.I was mostly motivated to write this review because their rating is 3.5 which seems insane to me. A lot of people are complaining about the price and wait.... amateur move. If you want a cheap sh*tty breakfast, go a block down to Hectors.

I recently visited a gem of a Mexican restaurant and it instantly ranked at the top of my list for Mexican cuisine! Despite the snowy weather, the place was buzzing with activity, yet the service remained efficient. I indulged in the adobado quesadillas – one with corn and another with flour tortillas. Both variations were outstanding, achieving a harmonious balance of flavors, especially with the addition of pineapple slices on top. Although I'm not typically a fan of flour tortillas, these were exceptional. The horchata I ordered was, without exaggeration, the best I’ve ever tasted. While my companions found their dishes on the spicier side, I felt it was spot-on. This eatery has earned my hearty recommendation, and it's marked as a must-visit for any future trips.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Comfort Food

I recently stumbled upon a quaint, retro gem that harkens back to classic diner days. This diminutive hole-in-the-wall spot has a charm that's absolutely worth experiencing. I savored their soups—a standout being the robust yet simple split pea, though a pinch more salt would have perfected it. The crunchy blintzes, filled with a sweet, ricotta-like cheese, are a must-try, especially when paired with applesauce.

For just $25, my companion and I enjoyed a hearty meal of two soups, a knish, and two blintzes—ample food for two. The good borscht reminded me that this is a kosher-dairy spot, so don't expect meat, but do expect flavor. While the knish was delightful, its accompanying gravy could have benefited from a bit more zest.

Beyond the classics, they offer a variety of sandwiches, omelets, and fresh juices. I even noticed some patrons enjoying a traditional egg cream. Operating since 1938, the diner walls are adorned with vintage photos, and the staff's dedication is evident. Just remember to bring cash when you visit. This little restaurant is a testament to the timeless allure of good, simple, and affordable food.

Hidden in a tiny basement, this sake bar tugs hard at my heart strings for being so reminiscent of Tokyo bars (except a lot bigger!) Impeccable sake menu with plain jane descriptions for everyone to enjoy exactly their type! Generous pours for reasonable pricing. They literally fill your cup til it runneth over. The food menu also looked great, and I'm hoping to try that next time I'm back. Love love love!

Not sure why it took me such a long time to finally come to Cocoron. Perfect place for warm soba, which I've never had before coming to Cocoron. I usually prefer cold soba, but I just couldn't get myself to order cold soba on a 30 degree day.Ordered the mera mera dip soba, which was very delicious (I never had dip soba before Cocoron either.. lots of firsts here). The soup was very flavorful and hit the spot for a cold, winter day. Dip soba was nice since you can put in small portions in the soup and don't have to worry about the noodles getting soggy, but it is a lot more work than getting the regular soba.

This little gem has been hiding in plain sight for quite some time. I usually get a Gyro from the Gyro truck and eat it in the park right in front of this restaurant and I have never noticed this place, it's a good thing my lovely dinner date suggested it for us to try.  Once you get inside the restaurant it is actually quite cozy.  The walls are decorated with With what one can only assume would be the atmosphere and vibes in Cuba with the classic American cars and the festive music the only thing i was missing was my flip flops and some sand. As an appetizer we got the Bolinho de Bacalhau which are tiny codfish cakes with red peppers inside and a dipping sauce that was very flavorful. For dinner imI ordered the Gaucho  Steak which came with Yucca fries and a margarita to drink.  I ordered my steak medium and it arrived at the table just the way I ordered it and seasoned to perfection on too of that.  I don't usually like when my steak is pre-sliced but this pre-sized steak was amazing I could not stop talking about how well it was seasoned and how perfectly cooked it was. I absolutely can see myself sitting down here and having another steak and another few drinks, i thoroughly enjoyed my visit here and I definitely will be coming back

Title: Underwhelmed by the Hyped Chicken and Rice Bowl

I had high hopes for the chicken and rice bowl at this establishment, but unfortunately, my experience was far from satisfactory. The dish arrived lukewarm after a wait that raised expectations for something much hotter, especially considering it was served in a pan. While the presentation was indeed appealing, it couldn't compensate for the lack of heat that I expected from pan service.

Moreover, the overall freshness of the meal was questionable. The hummus was particularly disappointing, bordering on inedible, and the tahini didn't fare much better. As if that weren't enough, the accompanying vegetables were both cold and bland, adding to an already lackluster dining experience.

The saving grace, if any, was the well-seasoned and generous portion of chicken, which warrants the two stars this review begrudgingly awards. However, with a price tag of around $14 per plate, the value for money just isn't there. This meal did not live up to the surrounding hype and stands out as one of the more forgettable dining experiences I've had this year.

Title: A Fresh Take on Banh Mi at JoJu

I recently visited JoJu in the bustling hub of Time Square for a modern twist on traditional banh mi and was delighted by the experience. The establishment boasts an impeccably clean environment, a testament to their dedication to a great dining experience.

Unlike the greasier versions I've encountered at other spots, JoJu's banh mi felt like a refreshing change of pace. The process of ordering via a tablet and the convenience of seating on both floors added to the streamlined experience, although it's worth noting there’s just one bathroom on the main floor.

The lemongrass chicken sandwich with a supposed runny egg was the highlight of our meal. Despite the egg not being as runny as anticipated, the flavors still managed to impress, particularly thanks to the warm toasted bread and the standout pickled carrots and radish. These elements added a crisp, clean bite to the sandwich, making it feel light and enjoyable.

For drinks, the lemon Thai tea, a lactose-free variant of Thai iced tea with a tangy lemon twist, was my preferred choice and provided a refreshing accompaniment to the meal.

Hearing rave reviews about the pork banh mi from a neighboring diner has piqued my interest for a return visit. JoJu is a gem for anyone looking for a quick, tasty bite in the heart of New York City.

My friend recommended this place and raved about how good the food here was, after reading the mixed reviews I didn't know what to expect. My first impression upon arriving was wow this place is really small and super packed. We had reservations for 9pm but we decided to wait a little longer in order to sit outside. From the beginning we were greeted by a really friendly host who continuously check up on us throughout the night. The employees do a great job at making you feel welcomed! We ordered the maccorone eggplant pasta and the lobster linguine. The lobster linguine was good but the lobster was just a tad overcook for my preference. The eggplant pasta was delicious! The portions here are huge but I kept eating more of the  eggplant pasta because it was just too good to stop. They brought us complimentary cannolis at the end of the meal. I don't think I've felt this stuffed in my life but it was really worth it because the food was delicious. Definitely recommend this place if you're looking for great Italian that doesn't break the bank.

My wife and I were exploring the new Essex Market and walked by Nordic Preserves Fish and Wildlife Company. Any place that has a painting of a naked woman on full display earns my business! There's art and smoked fish, man do I love New York.My wife & I were looking at the various smoked fish on display, it all looks deelish. Online in front of us were two of the cutest older woman. They're ordering and tasting different smoked fish. We start talking about different fish and based on their suggestions we ordered some of the most outrageous smoked fish I had in a long time.The Scottish Smoked Salmon was very good. Its my preferred choice over Norwegian Salmon. Scottish Salmon is more buttery and a more smokier salmon. What I also loved was the Pastrami cured Salmon. My wife was apprehensive at first but this was also a tasty treat. Here's the issue. I live far away from the Lower East Side. I would love to come here weekly and buy *everything*. I highly recommend the Nordic Preserves Fish and Wildlife Company. Their selection of smoked fish is one of the best I had in New York City.

Great service and great street tacos. Beer was very cold! Perfect! I got street tacos and a fish taco. My husband got a carnita taco and a shrimp taco. All were excellent! My son got the shrimp tacos and not a bit was leftover. Great food...and happy, good natured staff.

We were staying in a near by hotel & this was the closest place we could find for brunch.We came in & were seated right away the place was pretty empty since it was a bit early still, drinks we had some Mimosas they were not bad.For my main dish I had the Burger, Egg & Cheese - burger this was very good, homemade English muffin with some herb butter & home fries great taste to the meat , good combo with the egg, good home fries. My company had the Avocado toast with a poach egg, good size toast good as well , the "Fed" burger was good too, comes with fries good burger. Nice location, service was good, prices are high for brunch but am guessing they are  typical to the area. brunch should be a bit more enjoyable & less costly this was a pricey one. we enjoyed our food but not sure I would come back for brunch.

Title: A Saucy Affair at Blue Smoke

Walking into Blue Smoke, the tantalizing aroma of barbecue hits you like a warm welcome, setting high expectations for the meal to come. While our initial server seemingly disappeared shortly after we ordered drinks, Ben's timely rescue transformed the experience. His attentive service salvaged the evening, reflecting the friendly atmosphere of this no-tipping restaurant.

The lack of pressure to vacate our table post-meal was refreshing, allowing us to unwind and fully enjoy the ambiance. Blue Smoke's menu is a carnivore's dream with its variety of barbecued meats, but it's the bbq salmon that's the unsung hero. Don't be fooled by its understated menu presence; request it saucy, in the same style as their brisket, and prepare for a revelatory experience thanks to the kitchen's willingness to indulge.

The sides were hit or miss; the macaroni and cheese didn't win us over, and the cornbread received mixed reviews, although I found it irresistible enough to finish every crumb. The deviled eggs passed the table's taste test with flying colors, but it was the biscuit bread pudding draped in butterscotch sauce that stole the show – a dessert that calls for an encore. Pair it with the Narragansett Lager, especially if wheat lagers are your brew of choice.

Blue Smoke's vibe is down-to-earth cool, with a comfortable, spacious setting and decor that complements its cuisine. Though we missed out on the jazz cafe below due to a sell-out, the $30 cover seems a fair price for those seeking a musical ending to their dining experience.

In conclusion, Blue Smoke is a barbecue haven with a twist, offering a laid-back dining experience with standout dishes and a staff ready to step up when it matters most.

We frequent Houston's Bergen county very often and just recently learned that NY locations have sushi, so we tRied it out. They have mostly all the same foods, few differences.     The sushi was alright, I am a big sushi lover so I had to try, we had California roll, spicy tuna & coconut shrimp. The cal roll was prob my least fave. Coconut was pretty damn good. Side note * We were a little late, because, well- NY traffic *eye roll* but they accommodated us with no problem. Drinks came out fast. They had live jazz which was cool. Waitress very attentive. Would return if I'm the area.

Sister restaurant to Ikinari Steak, which is closing 9 out of its 11 locations in NYC and converting 2 of them to Pepper Lunch. The 1st location to open is in Midtown West and we decided to come give it a try for lunch. When you first enter, you place your order with the cashier near the entrance. Then they give you a stand with a number on it and you take it to any available table so they can identify you and deliver your order to your table. Our food came out like milliseconds after we were seated, which was such a pleasant surprise since we were both slightly hangry lol. The food was so good! We shared the Classic beef pepper rice and the Kimchi cheese beef pepper rice and they were both amazing. Just a heads up: the classic has a very peppery taste when you first eat it but you eventually get used to it. It sort of reminds me of Chinese clay pot rice because it's served on a hot iron plate so the rice becomes slightly crispy as it continues to cook. The menu lists the kimchi cheese beef pepper rice as level 1 spicy but I didn't really find it to be spicy at all. I love how the sourness from the kimchi, saltiness from the melted cheese, and sweetness from the corn blended so well with the rice. YUM! Aside from the food, the service and dining environment were also excellent. Honestly the only negative I can think of is the location. A bit out of the way for me and fairly close to the tourist-ridden Times Square but!! their 2nd location is slated to open in Chelsea, a much more accessible location. Will definitely be back to try out that branch when it opens!Tip: There's a flyer outside the restaurant that you can use to redeem a free soft drink! Offer ends May 31, 2019.

During a recent meander through Chinatown, my attention was captivated by the gleam of roast pork (cha siew) from a restaurant I hadn't frequented before. Overcoming the temptation to stick to my usual haunts, I decided to take a plunge and ordered a pound of their cha siew at a somewhat steep $10 per pound. It was, however, a price that proved its worth. A pro tip: request the "half fat cha siew" for that perfect symphony of meat and fat. The flavor was unexpectedly delightful, earning a round of gastronomic applause from my family.

Unfortunately, the establishment seems to be steering clear of in-house dining due to profitability challenges in maintaining a safe, limited customer capacity. Takeout is the operative mode here. On a side note, I'd recommend giving their soy sauce chicken a miss, as it failed to impress the familial taste testers. In summary, for a superior cha siew fix, this spot is a takeout gem in the heart of Chinatown.

Dining at this eatery is a delightful culinary journey best enjoyed with companions. Our group of six indulged in a cheese trio - Swiss, black truffle, and Pyrenees - each variety exuding its unique charm. The main course, a succulent filet, was cooked to perfection in our choice of oil and red wine, leaving a lasting impression. The finale, a dessert of velvety milk and intense dark chocolate, accompanied by fresh fruit, dainty cakes, and fluffy marshmallows, was pure decadence. This restaurant is unequivocally worth the visit for an exceptional food adventure.

My dining experience at this quaint spot on a bustling Saturday evening was notably pleasant. Despite its size, the restaurant handled the crowd well, which was a surprise. Our reservation ensured we were seated promptly.

We chose two dishes from the weekly specials: the branzino and the chicken. The branzino, partnered with sautéed vegetables, was the star of the meal, outshining the chicken in both flavor and preparation. 

The rustic decor added a cozy charm, enhancing the overall ambiance. The meal wrapped up beautifully with a serving of tiramisu, which was delightful and deserves a special mention.

All in all, this small restaurant is a gem worth visiting for anyone looking for a nice dinner in a warmly inviting setting.

I recently revisited a childhood favorite, where my mom used to bring me just for the iced tea. True to memory, it remains the best iced tea I've ever had - a nostalgic blend that never fails to impress. Highly recommended for fellow tea enthusiasts.

Nothing beats dinner with a nice view, and by view, I'm referring to Jake Gyllenhaal and Tom Sturridge sitting cozily at the table across from me. Jake, who was incredibly hot in person, and I made steamy eye contact when he caught me staring at him. Unfortunately for him, my mouth was preoccupied all night with other meat and creamy substances. Every dish I tried was incredible! I didn't think lamb ribs that tasty existed outside of New Zealand, and boy was I wrong. The burrata was the creamiest I've ever had and the beef tartare was exquisitely textured. Sorry, Jake - better luck next time.

Title: A Delightful Thai Surprise!

I recently dined at a lovely spot that genuinely took me by surprise with its charming ambiance, complete with soothing Thai tunes and tastefully appointed decor. The culinary journey commenced with an appetizer of betel leaves that tantalized the taste buds; it was a delectable, lighter nod to the authentic versions I've savored in Thailand. 

Moving on to the main course, the Khao soi did not disappoint. It boasted a creamy coconut base infused with the nuanced depths of a good curry. Pro tip: Swirl in the accompanying sauce for an extra layer of flavor, though don't expect a fiery kick as the dish maintains a milder profile.

Dessert was a simple affair of coconut ice cream— mostly adorned with whipped cream and crushed Thai peanut sweets. While it wasn't the star of the show, it still delivered a pleasant end to the meal. 

Verdict: This restaurant is a must-visit for those looking to indulge in Thai cuisine's complex flavors within an inviting atmosphere.

I recently visited a local eatery with hopes of indulging in some comfort food, starting with their Mac n Cheese accompanied by a side of miso vegetable soup. Unfortunately, both dishes were somewhat underwhelming.

The miso soup was packed with a variety of vegetables and tofu, which is great for those looking for a nutritious option. However, the overall flavor didn't leave a remarkable impression.

Moving on to the Mac n Cheese, I had my expectations set high, hoping for a gooey, cheesy delight similar to what you might find at a place like Potbelly. Instead, I was met with overcooked small-shell pasta lacking in both the rich, creamy texture and the sharp taste of cheese that one craves in a Mac n Cheese. As a pasta lover, I always question the carb indulgence, and regrettably, this dish didn't justify it at all. Perhaps a little more sauce and seasoning could salvage it. 

On another note, while the bacon and mushroom worked wonders in their salad option, they couldn't replicate the magic in the Mac n Cheese.

I also tried the chocolate chip cookie, which was passable but not extraordinary. For those interested, it includes soy, which is a plus if you're aiming to increase your soy consumption.

The visit was a hit and miss, with more room for improvement in flavor and texture to live up to the expectations of comfort food enthusiasts.

Last night's visit to this local pizzeria proved to be a delightful experience. I savored the Sicilian pepperoni slices that were generously topped with a hearty amount of pepperoni and smothered in gooey, melted cheese. The crust struck a perfect balance, contributing to the overall enjoyment. My companion opted for pepperoni, cheese, and mushroom slices. Despite the pepperoni being slightly overcooked, there weren't any complaints as the taste clearly compensated, especially with the cheese slice that was a definite hit. The mushroom slice, notable for its appealing look, didn't disappoint in flavor either. This spot is a notable upgrade from your average dollar slice joints, and given its proximity to numerous rehearsal spaces, it's an ideal pick for a quick and satisfying bite before or after practice sessions. Highly recommended!

Decided to eat mexican today and ordered chicken fajita and kale-aid juice for lunch.The chicken fajita is disappointing as it doesnt taste like anything. It didnt have enough salt and seasoning and the chicken is dry.The juice looks deep green (not really appetizing i have to say). But the taste is much better than it looks and its not bitter and very fresh.The three star mainly points to the food.

Title: A Standout Solo Dining Delight at the Unique Ramen Haven

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a ramen spot that's breaking all the conventions. Upon arrival, I was surprised by their distinctive service model. Here, diners get personal booths, ensuring privacy and swift seating, especially for lone visitors.

The ordering process is interactive; you customize your Tonkatsu Ramen on a clipboard while queuing. I recommend the default set for a generous assortment of scallions, mushrooms, extra pork, and a soft boiled egg. For personalization, I prefer light salt, medium oil, a hint of garlic, with toppings like scallion, chashu, and a triple spike of spice. A bonus laminated card offers a complimentary noodle refill, inviting you to experiment with different noodle textures.

Once seated, you pass your order through a slot to the server and can navigate your dining experience with helpful instructions posted in the booth. However, skip the matcha beer; it's an overpriced gimmick.

Noteworthy points: no tipping required, credit cards accepted, and the experience mirrors a unique Japanese dining adventure without leaving town. A must-try for both ramen enthusiasts and those seeking a new way to dine solo.

Title: A Taiwanese Treat on the Upper East Side - Tri Dim Shanghai

After an enriching afternoon at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, we were delighted to stumble upon Tri Dim Shanghai for a Taiwanese culinary experience. The restaurant entices with a special offer on Yelp: check-in rewards you with four complimentary chicken dumplings, and there's a cashback incentive for registering your credit card.

We savored the hot soup and dumplings. While the soup dumplings were enjoyable, especially when dipped in ginger vinegar, a slightly less sweet filling would have perfected them. The chicken dumplings did not disappoint, and the chicken corn soup was a comforting delight.

A standout dish was the Ants Climb up Tree - a must-try, true to Taiwanese flavors, featuring glass noodles with savory minced beef atop steamed greens.

Service was exemplary; staff were both attentive and hospitable, ensuring a memorable dining experience. For those on the Upper East Side in search of Taiwanese fare, Tri Dim Shanghai is a worthy destination.

I recently ducked into Lucky Pickle, cleverly sidestepping the crowds at Jacob's Pickled, and I was pleased with the ease and efficiency right off the bat. The self-serve kiosks were user-friendly, allowing me to quickly place my order which was ready almost instantly. I opted to dine in, enjoying my meal at one of the casual communal tables.

I kicked things off with their DIY iced tea bar and was not disappointed. The honey ginger tea hit the spot, and I noted other inviting flavors to try next time. The dan dan noodles, while tasty, were a touch greasy and not as hot as I'd prefer, but this was a minor hiccup in an otherwise delightful meal.

The ambiance of Lucky Pickle added to the experience, offering a fun vibe with an excellent soundtrack. Despite the lukewarm noodles, Lucky Pickle has won me over, and I'm eager to return for the dumplings and more of that tea.

Title: Spicy but Not Memorable: A Visit to the Curry Spot in Koreatown

I ventured to this renowned spot in search of the "spiciest Korean curry ever" as per Insider's spotlight, only to find myself tucking into what seemed more like a Japanese curry in the heart of Koreatown.

Opting for the vegetable curry at a daring level 4 spiciness, I expected an inferno but was met with a tame blaze. Surprisingly, I breezed through the dish with minimal water breaks. Sampling the level 2 confirmed my thoughts: palatable, yet unremarkable.

The curry, while satisfactory, left no lingering impression on my palate. Fast service, reasonable prices, and a convenient location do make it a viable option for a casual outing. I wouldn't reject an invitation to return, but a solitary craving to revisit is unlikely to strike.

Set against an enchanting backdrop, this restaurant promises a magical dining experience. The whimsy begins right from the elevator ride, adorned with tree branches twinkling with lights, setting the stage for the evening.

Upon arrival during a weekday dinner, my party of five was seated promptly. Opting for a healthier beverage option, I was somewhat let down by the lack of a freshly prepared juice, instead receiving a bottled variety.

The main course, a pasta dish, piqued my interest on the menu but ultimately fell flat in execution. In retrospect, I regret not choosing one of the meat dishes, as my companions' plates certainly outshone my own in both appearance and, presumably, taste.

Despite the culinary missteps, the restaurant's cozy and elegant atmosphere facilitated enjoyable conversation and an overall pleasant experience. While the food didn’t quite hit the mark, the ambiance did, and it is for this reason I find myself willing to return. Next time, I'll certainly diverge from my initial choices in the hopes of a meal as captivating as the surroundings.

I was walking south from the upper west side and decided to stop and have a little snack. I am always looking for new places to have a little nosh and found the Muffins Cafe. It is very small and there are several tables where one can sit and have coffee, etc. I was waited on immediately and opted for a cup of coffee and a chocolate croissant. It would have been even better had it been heated but it was still delicious. It is reasonably priced and the staff is very accommodating, to everyone who was waiting on line. I would recommend.

Title: Authentic Flavors with Room for Improvement

I recently visited an Indian restaurant that tantalizes with its authenticity, evident by the approval of elderly Indian patrons. The food, flavorful and genuine, offered a glimpse into the rich culinary traditions of India. However, despite the tasty offerings, there are elements that leave me hesitant about a return visit.

My main gripe is the naan, a staple in Indian dining. Disappointingly, it lacked the light, airy texture and the characteristic smoky touch of a traditional tandoor. This was a significant letdown, as a good naan can elevate the entire dining experience.

More concerning was the aftermath of my meals. On both occasions, I experienced a sense of discomfort, which is unusual for my generally resilient stomach. It's hard to pinpoint the cause, but this discomfort is a deterrent for future visits.

I'm open to giving the restaurant another chance, perhaps trying the dosa next time to see if it agrees with me more. For anyone who values naan or has a sensitive stomach, this might not be the first choice. However, for those seeking authentic Indian flavors and can overlook these aspects, it's worth a try.

While exploring the vicinity of our hotel for dining options, we chanced upon this delightful restaurant on Labor Day around 6 PM. To our surprise, the place was comfortably uncrowded. The service was exceptional, complementing the tasteful meal we had. The potstickers I ordered stood out particularly, and I would highly recommend them. It didn't seem to be a tourist hotspot, which might contribute to its relaxed ambiance. The menu was extensive, offering an array of choices. Overall, the restaurant exuded a pleasant vibe, ensuring that we would certainly consider returning on our next trip.

Dined at this spot on a Wednesday evening before the theater due to the unavailability of seats at another restaurant. We started with the age tofu and tuna tataki, followed by a selection of rolls including tuna, yellowtail scallion, and the Manhattan roll for our mains. Disappointingly, the dishes fell short of expectations. The age tofu was the only passable item, while the rest were lackluster, with the tuna tataki standing out for its stale taste and overpowering, artificial sauce that failed to complement the fish. The rolls were mediocre and forgettable. Additionally, the cost of the Manhattan roll at $17 did not reflect its size or quality. Considering the wealth of dining options in the area, we have no intention of returning.

I recently revisited a spot that was once just mediocre and was pleasantly surprised to find they've truly upped their ante. Now, when craving a value Chinese Dry Hot Pot, this place rivals Mala Project. The unique service style caters to various preferences; you can handpick ingredients for your bowl at the counter and then savor it at a table, or opt for traditional menu ordering. It's an ideal mix of self-service and waiter assistance. If you find yourself in the W4 area with a hankering for dry hot pot, I'd definitely recommend dropping by.

During a work trip, my colleague and I popped into a bustling family-style Italian restaurant, just a short walk from our hotel. Despite it being a jam-packed Saturday night, we managed to snag a table, immediately noting the regulars-filled atmosphere.

I sipped on a lemon martini while tackling the overly dressed apple & pear salad, then dug into the classic lasagna that, although decent, was calling out for a punch of salt. Service could've been sharper; our waiter seemed to be elsewhere.

Although the prices were fair for the generous servings, the meal didn't leave the lasting impression I'd hoped for. Still, the place has potential, and I'm willing to return to explore other, potentially more exciting options on the menu.

Title: Festive Brunch with a Minor Guac Glitch

My friends and I visited this establishment for their Cinco de Mayo brunch, enticed by the promise of bottomless drinks, and let me tell you—those margaritas did not disappoint. They were the highlight for many in our group, who couldn't stop singing their praises.

I opted for the pollo sandwich, and it was, in a word, phenomenal. The savory flavors meshed perfectly, and every bite was a delight. As for the starters, the guacamole was a hit among us. Fresh, creamy, and paired well with the lively atmosphere of the celebration.

The huevos rancheros were another crowd-pleaser, with several friends noting just how delicious they found the dish. The flavors and presentation seemed to capture the essence of the festive occasion.

However, the experience wasn’t without a slight hiccup. There was a miscommunication regarding the guacamole—we were under the impression it was part of the brunch deal. It turned out to be quite pricey as an add-on, which was a bit of a downer once we got the bill.

Despite this, the overall experience was positive enough that I'd definitely consider returning. The slight misstep with the guacamole wouldn't deter me from coming back to enjoy the ambiance and mouthwatering food once again.

I recently stopped by this 24-hour diner during a hectic day in town and was pleasantly surprised by its extensive menu, which included brunch specials. It's worth noting they also offer beer and wine, so have your ID handy if you fancy a drink. I opted for a cheeseburger and fries which hit the spot – both the food and service were commendable. Although I didn't indulge in desserts, the tempting display of cakes, pies, and cheesecake suggests that I need to come back with an appetite. Definitely a must-visit for those looking for variety and a satisfying meal.

The first time I heard about Camellia was via a post on IG.  I kind of fell in love with a picture of their rainbow noodle ramen and knew that I needed to try them out.  I got the chance to do so yesterday. I ordered the Build Your Own Ramen ($16).  For this dish you can choose your noodles (original, matcha, butterfly pea flower, rainbow, etc.), soup flavor (tokatsu, miso, shoyu, tsukemen, etc.), protein (pork, chicken, shrimp or tofu) and toppings.  I got mine with Rainbow noodles, Tsukemen dipping broth, pork chasu and toppings of half boiled egg, baby bok choy, and bean sprouts.It's a very colorful dish and I just loved the presentation.  The best part is, their ramen is made with natural flavors and ingredients.  For the colorful rainbow noodles, they use butterfly pea flower, cuttle fish paste, beets, matcha and carrots.The noodles were perfectly cooked, the egg was delicious with a nice soft yolk and the pork chasu was super tender and had a nice smoky flavor. The Tsukemen dipping broth was a little too salty to sip as a broth but perfect for dipping. I also got an order of their pork belly bao ($4).  The baos comes with a piece of lettuce, spicy mayo, pickled mustard, and finely grounded peanuts. The ground peanuts were a nice touch of texture and the pork belly was melt-in-your mouth tender.  Absolutely delish!You get a free scoop of gelato with your meal or with Yelp check-in. Both ramen, teas and gelato are all made in house daily.   I ordered the Ferrero Rocher gelato and it was excellent!  Not overly sweet with a nice creamy texture.  Perfect way to end a ramen meal.Definitely will be coming back again!

Thanks to NYC restaurant week I got to enjoy a Michelin star restaurant for my mom's birthday. I was allowed to call for reservations 2 weeks in advance for lunch on a Thursday & they were absolutely pleasant on the phone. They even asked for my party's allergies & inquired if I was celebrating anything. So very thoughtful, remembering this is service for an excellent restaurant. It's located on the 2nd floor of a luxurious hotel. Beautiful walk up the curved staircase to the entrance. We were offered coat check but we were able to keep our coats. The table setting was lovely. For restaurant week, they offer the 2 course for $26 or the 3 course for $32. We of course got the 3 course! For starters, the zuppa di topinambur (sunchoke soup, pickled celery root & creme fraiche) looked plain & simple with few textured ingredients but it was very soft, light & creamy. My mother loved it. I ordered the terrina di anatra (duck pate, cranberry, pickles, pecan) which I thought was going to be a paste, however it wasn't. The plate looked beautiful, the duck was cooked well, not overcooked & each bite with the cranberry was the best. Entrees: My aunt got the salmon (pan roasted with butternut squash, quinoa & swiss chard) which was also presented lovely. The salmon was cooked well & she said she loved pairing the butternut squash the best. Mother & I ordered the costolette (red wine braised ribs, polenta & glazed root vegetables). The plate is served with one rib. My mother's dish had more polenta than I did, but I wasn't going to be upset about that. I was a tad bit disappointed in my rib piece which was meaty on one side & on the flat side had a tough fatty tissue that was inedible. The meaty part had gelatin- looking lines in it. I wondered if that's what you call "marbling" but it wasn't as tender & juicy as I would imagine it would be.Dessert: the limone curd with meringue & grapefruit granite was amazing. It's a small portion, but I loved it regardless. I feel that it was better than semifreddo (chocolate mousse, cardamom & salted caramel ganache). The most thoughtful thing they did was surprised my mother with an extra birthday ice cream dessert. I was so pleased with their kindess & making her feel special. Ai Fiori is amazing dining experience.

Title: A Lively Brunch Spot with Room for Improvement

I recently had the opportunity to experience the unlimited brunch at a bustling eatery on a busy Saturday afternoon. Despite our tardy arrival, the staff was accommodating after a courteous phone call to update them on our delayed situation.

On arrival, we initially aspired for a spot on the coveted back patio but settled for the bar due to full occupancy. Thankfully, the ambiance didn’t disappoint; the restaurant was lively without being overwhelming, and the patio exuded charm once we got seated.

The culinary journey began with a mediocre guacamole, but the main courses elevated the experience. The chilaquiles dazzled with their perfect combination of sunny side up eggs, crispy tortilla chips, and fresh salsa, while the enfrijoladas catered delightfully to vegetarian palates.

However, a note of caution to fellow diners: extra sour cream comes with a steep $2 charge for a minuscule portion, a detail I find unnecessary.

Service was a mixed bag – attentive at times but lost momentum when it came to replenishing our unlimited drinks, which is essential when you're investing $20 for the experience. The smoky jalapeño and traditional margaritas were hits, though their premade nature meant a race against dilution over time. And do steer clear of the overly thick mimosa.

In verdict, I’d consider a return for the fun atmosphere and tasty entrees, with a hopeful eye on improved drink service.

After a stroll in Central Park, a 20-minute journey led me to an enchanting dining oasis surprisingly close to the zoo. The restaurant, a Middle Eastern-inspired haven, was adorned with lush greenery, radiant lights, and rustic wooden accents. A visually stunning bar area completed the scene, making it one of the most aesthetically pleasing spots I've dined in.

Opting for the lunch special, I was treated to a hearty meal at an unbeatable price of $12, which included an entrée, a choice between soup or salad, and an appetizer. The Iced Thai Tea Lemonade was a refreshing delight, while I found the Iced Thai Tea overly sweet and milky, which I wouldn’t recommend. The Kua Gai with chicken surpassed expectations with its flavorful profile, a dish I'd gladly suggest. Conversely, the red curry, served traditionally in a pot alongside a mound of rice, was lackluster in taste and presentation when compared to others I've savored.

As for the starters, the veggie soup and edamame hit the spot, though the steamed dumplings with shrimp and chicken had an unusual flavor I’d rather not revisit. The salad was average, and the accompanying sauce didn't win me over. Despite a few culinary missteps, the stunning setting and overall value made for a satisfying experience. For Thai cuisine aficionados in NYC, this place could easily become a go-to spot.

Title: A Hit for Company Outings!

My team and I recently visited this lively spot for our company outing and it didn’t disappoint. The service was swift as the food arrived promptly, ensuring our evening flowed without a hitch. An eclectic mix of tunes set the perfect ambiance for an upbeat and enjoyable night out.

The highlight for many of us was the inclusion of ping pong tables, which provided a playful twist to the evening. To our delight, a pro ping pong player mingled with our group, challenging us to matches with the incentive of drink tickets for the victors. Despite our best efforts, the pro remained unbeaten, yet his friendly demeanor and ability to tailor his skill level to match each participant made the experience enjoyable for all.

Whether you're planning a casual company outing or a social mixer, this spot strikes the right balance of fun, food, and entertainment. I highly recommend it for a relaxed yet engaging group experience.

I know I'm not an expert on Dominican food but I thought the food here was amazing. It is definitely very fatty and probably not good for you, but the food was packed with flavor. I came here with my Dominican friend and I let him picked all the dishesAlso get yourself a beer - El Presidente - goes very well with the food hereTres Leche cake at the end is a must

I recently visited a local eatery known for its ramen and decided to try their spicy miso variant. Upon recommendation, I added a soft-boiled egg, which truly exceeded my expectations—it was a highlight with its rich umami flavor. The ramen broth itself was a unique blend of spicy and sweet, an interesting but strange combination that could be appealing to those with adventurous palates.

While the broth was memorable, the dish's balance left something to be desired: a greater portion of beef to complement the generous amount of soup would have been appreciated. Additionally, the bean sprouts included didn't quite hit the mark for me.

Despite the ramen's flavorsome qualities, I am compelled to dock a point for the service. With a 30-minute wait after ordering and a 15-minute wait for just water, the service speed was disappointing. It seemed there might have been a rush, but the wait times felt somewhat excessive.

I would rate the ramen itself a solid 4 out of 5. As for the dining experience, I might recommend this place for a one-time visit to try the ramen for its unique flavors, but the slow service might deter some from becoming regulars.

My favorite hummus in New York! I have been to 12 chairs 4 times now, and I have never been disappointed. The dishes I have tried include lamb burger, hummus, hummus falafel, shashuka and Israeli salad, and all of them are so delicious. The hummus is my favorite dish out of all because of how creamy and how flavorful it is. Moreover, the pita accompanying the hummus is always warm and soft. The service here is very friendly, and the vibe is warm and romantic, so I would say it is good for all occasions - no matter if it is family dinner, date or friends' catchup. The only downside is that this restaurant is indeed sooo tiny and has less than 20 tables, so it does get crowded at times. If you come in party of four or more people, be sure to make reservation beforehand

What's a vegetarian doing in a steakhouse? Well it's the company you keep! Good news is that the nice hostess did improvise on a pasta preparation, which for some reasons had chopped Brussels sprouts but turned out to be pretty good. House bread was actually warm and good (so they do pay attention). Have not been to any other Capital Grille but this one sure seemed a bit dark. Perhaps largely because of being in Manhattan's concrete jungle. Reservations strongly suggested and if you are a vegetarian, don't visit if you are too hungry.

Amazing authentic Italian. I ordered the black truffle  ravioli which was incredibly flavorful with the perfect amount of truffle. The calamari and prosciutto were excellent starters. The tequila cocktail was delicious and I would highly recommend. My only complaint would be the tight seating (we were shoved in the corner by the front door and were constantly bumped. The wait was long but worth it for the food Other than that, The pasta was amazing and this is definitely one of my new favorite Italian spots.

I absolutely adore this Harlem gem! With every visit, I venture into a new dish and it's always a delightful experience. It's a rare find where consistency in excellence is guaranteed. Highly recommend for anyone looking to be impressed time and time again!

I recently visited a local eatery renowned for its cheesesteaks and was thoroughly impressed. I opted for the medium cheesesteak with mayo and onions, adding fries and a drink to my order for an additional dollar—a bargain bringing my grand total to less than $13. Not only was the meal satisfying and delicious, but the service was incredibly fast; I was in and out in less than 10 minutes. While this is an outdoor location requiring takeout, the convenience is great, and they also offer delivery. The menu diversifies with chicken steak options and even includes breakfast. I will definitely be returning for another fantastic and affordable meal.

Title: A Birthday Feast for a Lobster Lover

My family and I chose this establishment for my husband's birthday, drawn in by their renowned 4-pound lobster, a dream come true for any lobster aficionado. True to expectation, the seafood did not disappoint and left my husband thoroughly pleased. Alongside, I indulged in a perfectly cooked 14 oz NY Strip, which was nothing short of excellent. Our daughter opted for the child's Filet Mignon, which, although exquisitely prepared, came as a surprise in its petite, one-bite size. Be aware that sides are separate from the entrees, making the dining experience quite pricey. Despite that, the exceptional service and the warm welcome by the staff rounded off the celebration on a high note.

The food was delicious but the ambiance was only okay. We can here on a Thursday around 11:30am so there wasn't too long of a wait (around 10-15 min) which was nice. The place is pretty (with white walls and nice lights), but felt pretty cramped. We ordered a Hot Chix (fried chicken) and a Steak & Egg. Both were really good, I prefer the chicken though since the steak was a bit more tough in my opinion. They were both around $15, which seems standard/on the cheaper end of a brunch place in the city. However the worst part of this experience is that it took us forever to order and get our bill. The restaurant got gradually less busy as time went on, but it still felt like the service was extremely slow. I'd probably only come back for a weekday brunch, as I feel like it's only worth waiting 15-20 min max at this place and can see this having a long line on the weekends

I recently visited a ramen spot for a weekday lunch and was thrilled to find no wait for a table – a definite perk for those looking to avoid the crowds. The menu boasted an array of options, of which I chose the miso paitan and the spicy mega paitan.

The first thing that caught my attention was the texture of the noodles; they were firmer, more al dente than what I'm accustomed to. While surprising at first, the texture quickly grew on me. As for the soft-boiled egg, a staple in a good bowl of ramen, it fell short of expectation with slightly overcooked edges and a lackluster flavor.

Both ramen broths were rich and hearty, yet they bordered on being overly salty for my taste. The miso ramen featured a robust umami flavor from the fermented paste, a note that might not be everyone's favorite. Meanwhile, the spicy mega paitan boasted a high level of saltiness, making it difficult to enjoy the broth by itself.

While I’m keen to explore other ramen venues, this place is a solid option if you're looking for a quick, line-free experience. However, it’s worth noting the spicy mega paitan comes with a hefty price tag of $18, making it one of the pricier bowls I've encountered.

In summary, this ramen joint offers a convenient and swift dining experience with decent options, although some elements like the eggs and the saltiness of the broths could use improvement. The pricing of certain dishes might give pause, but the lack of a wait might just make up for that.

Spot Dessert Bar truly does desserts right! They're classics are incredible, Golden Toast among my favorite. However, their seasonal desserts are also fantastic. I love going to Spot with friends and trying everything. Although the location is small, the wait is never too long. Desserts are reasonably priced and very photogenic. Overall, a fun spot to stop by after any meal.
Good spot for a game, wings and beer. Not bad for Sunday brunch although the service is sub par. The food was good but nothing special. I'm sure you can find better choices in The City.

Something different from the usual spots in the area, Vietnaam provides a large menu of Vietnamese cuisine in a large setting. Given the amount of space they have outside and the large awning covering the sun, decided to get a table outdoors for two people (and a dog).To start off, shared the Vegetable Summer Rolls ($8) - two tightly wrapped veggie rolls with two sauces to the side. Mostly raw sprouts and herbs that was made way better with the accompanying peanut sauces. For the main entree, decided on the Pork Belly Banh Mi ($13) - a hearty sandwich with layers of pickled veggies, mayo, and tender pork. Looked like it would be dry, but the juice from the meat comes through as well as the mayo. Flavor has a good amount of spice from the jalapeno without being overwhelming.Service is prompt and they filled our water periodically. Like how the full menu is available as soon as they open, so will come back in the morning again.

I recently dined at this local spot renowned for its traditional fare. While I wouldn't recommend the barbecue, the soups here are worth noting, particularly the kalbi tang, which is my personal favorite. What's more, they offer a fantastic deal on weekday mornings with their soup specials for just $10 plus tax. It's a bargain you shouldn't miss if you're in the mood for a heartwarming meal to start your day.

Came for lunch on Thanksgiving and waited about an hour for a table for two. The lobby downstairs was packed with people waiting for their numbers to be called. Although there is an elevator, there isn't really a place to sit in the lobby so you may want to keep this in mind if somebody in your party needs an accommodation. The carts were constantly getting refilled with more items so if anything ran out I didn't have to wait long for it to become available again. There were many servers walking around the tables picking up any empty baskets. Oftentimes as soon as I took the last piece from a plate or basket somebody would immediately clear the plate/basket from the table.Everything I tried was pretty standard with a few highlights:-the fried items were not greasy at all! Sometimes the items I get at dim sum places feel very heavy due to all the oil but the items here were not like that.-there was a small dish with a chili sauce and mustard sauce on the table. Complimented a lot of dishes we got, especially the fried bacon-wrapped shrimp.-the egg yolk custard buns (liu sha bao) had an awesome runny filling, which some dim sum places fail to do.
