I wish I had the chance to try the buns with the cute animal designs but the plain buns were great on their own.They do take credit card and were accommodating about splitting the check. The dishes and tea cups at the table could have been cleaned better.

Title: Quirky Name, Quirky Experience

My evening at 'Taste of Temptation' was a mixed bag. Initiated with fried halloumi, the meal peaked early as the salty cheese hit all the right notes against the sweetness of grape accompaniment. The chicken kebab followed suit with its tender juiciness, though it was let down by the lackluster couscous.

However, the green shakshuka, surrounded by hype, was disappointing. Overcooked eggs and an underwhelming sauce failed to deliver the anticipated culinary delight. As for the ambiance, the space charmed with its cuteness, but the service could use a tune-up. An air of snark and lack of helpfulness from the staff, particularly pre-coffee, detracted from the overall experience. 'Taste of Temptation' nails the name but needs a few tweaks to truly live up to it.

Title: Charming Ambience, Mixed Dining Experience

Our recent group dinner at this cozy establishment offered a welcoming atmosphere, with its downstairs bar and dining area adorned in dark wood and an extensive selection of wines outshining the tap and bottled beer options. The upstairs space, accessed through a winding staircase, catered well to our large party, boasting private areas with the potential for a mini-bar and a generous dining set-up.

The Market Salad was a minimalist affair, likely to appeal to vegetarians with its raw vegetables and subtle shallot champagne vinaigrette. The cast iron chicken presented beautifully at neighboring tables, setting high expectations. However, my choice of the Mediterranean Branzino fell short; despite resting on a delightful yet sparse basil pesto sauce, the fish was slightly dry, paired with mediocre jumbo asparagus and uninspiring fingerling potatoes.

In summary, while the venue charmed and the menu promised, the execution didn't quite hit the mark. Perhaps a smaller gathering with choices from the regular menu would afford a better representation of their culinary potential.

This place was pretty good - good pasta, you get bread. I did like my black fettucine, but it was a little too oily. They have a nice-ish backyard, where we sat, but honestly not super memorable. Definitely good if you want some standard Italian food.

Title: Tantalizing Tacos Worth the Times Square Trek

From the winding queue that spills onto the bustling streets, you might question the hype surrounding this compact culinary gem. But patience, my fellow foodies, is a virtue richly rewarded here. Despite the throngs, the line advances with surprising swiftness, ushering you into a haven where the aromas alone validate the wait.

The menu is a masterclass in focus: a meat-lover's mosaic with a nod to vegetarians, ensuring no palate is overlooked. My taste buds were treated to what I can only describe as a taco triumph - a symphony of flavors that had me mouthing "WOW" with every mouthful.

Interactivity is at the heart of this experience. Upon ordering, you're handed a ticket, which becomes your golden pass to personalized taco bliss. Choose your tortilla, declare your desired toppings, and watch the magic unfold before your eyes, all while engaging with the friendly chefs who are the maestros of this tantalizing show.

The salsa bar is a treasure trove, a colorful lineup of condiments that invites you to crown your creation with the perfect spicy flourish. And while the space forgoes seats for standing room, it's typical of the no-frills NYC food joints that focus squarely on what matters most: the food.

In a city where culinary excellence can be found at every corner, this taco spot near Times Square is a standout not to be missed. Highly recommended for an authentic bite that's fast, flavorful, and fantastically unforgettable.

Tucked away in the bustling city, I discovered a charming Chinese bakery brimming with delightful treats. This cozy spot may lack seating, but their variety of traditional baked goods more than compensates. I indulged in both a warm steamed pork bun and its baked counterpart topped with a sweet glaze; each offered a comforting, authentic taste of Chinese cuisine. Don't miss the chance to try the egg custard tarts or the unique banana tea leaf rice triangles. For a genuine taste of Chinese pastries, this little gem is undeniably worth a visit.

Good food. Great service. My only complaint is that their bakery items are not good at all. We tried the blueberry muffin and it was sub par ...We had the egg white omelette and the avocado toast. Portions are pretty large They only have bottled salsa which is a bummer. I was expecting some homemade pico de Gallo. The menu has something for everyone. There's healthy stuff , sinful stuff and a few Mediterranean options like mezzo and Israeli salad. I would recommend this place if you are in Times Square and want a solid meal in a less hectic environment

I recently visited this restaurant for a dinner with friends, and it was an awesome experience. The highlight was the beef and pork combo for 3, generously portioned enough for the 4 of us to share. What stood out to me were the delectable sides of cheesy corn and egg custard that accompanied the meats along the rim of the grill. The tenderness of all the meats was impressive, and they paired wonderfully with an array of dipping sauces. The only downside was the cramped space, which made the setting feel a bit tight. Nonetheless, I’d recommend this spot for anyone looking to enjoy a hearty meal with good company.

Title: A Perfect Late Night Bite with an Excellent Wine Selection

My recent visit to this restaurant confirmed it's a fantastic choice for anyone looking for a lively late-night dining experience. We arrived at the prime time of 9 pm on a bustling Friday night and were delighted to be seated promptly. The atmosphere was electric, with a loud, sociable buzz that added to the fun.

The wine list impressed us, offering bottles that cater to both the budget-conscious and the lavish spender, ranging from $50 to the upper hundreds. Service was both attentive and swift, a real plus for any late-night cravings.

Culinary-wise, we opted to share two mains: short ribs and mushroom ravioli. Each dish stood out with its flavors and execution, the short ribs being particularly memorable for their succulence. We're already excited to return, with plans to dive into their wine and cheese plates. Highly recommended for anyone in search of great food, vibrant atmosphere, and a diverse wine selection.

Came here last minute with a friend a few weeks ago and was pleasantly surprised we didn't need a reservation on a Thursday night. They have a great happy hour Tues-Sun (5pm-7pm) which includes $5 draft beer, $6 sake, and $7 wines. Score!!They have bar seating in addition to tables that can accommodate large groups. Service was warm and welcoming. The menu is quite extensive and can be a little over whelming so I have listed my favorites down below. FAVORITES:-Grilled Prawns (super juicy)-Grilled Shishito peppers (not too spicy)-NoMad Glabi (flavor was incredible)-Sesame Ice Cream -Hot Pot with Mussels (mussels were fresh and was a generous amount)

Beautiful interiorWonderful serviceDelicious foodTasty cocktailSwordfish was my favorite, firmer in texture yet flavorful, round, and fresh. Love the asparagus grits came with it. Filet Mignon was very good also but my medium rare was a bit too cooked, should have gotten rare. Soft Shell Crab was tasty but nothing special. Shishito Pepper stuffed shrimp was interesting but could use heavier seasoning? Chocolate Souffle was a perfect ending! Would definitely love to come back.

**TL;DR Version:**

- Stellar Korean Fried Chicken!
- Expect a brief wait for fresh orders - worth it!
- Superb value for top-notch cuisine.

**Long Winded Version:**

**Food:** 5/5
The Korean fried chicken is a knockout every time. It's freshly prepared, seasoned to perfection, and thankfully doesn't resemble the overgrown variety. The sauces? Heavenly. Do yourself a favor and ask for extra.

**Location:** 4/5
Situated ideally for transit users with a plethora of other dining and drinking spots around. Plus, if your heart desires, there's karaoke rooms to sing your chicken praises post-meal.

**Atmosphere / Ambiance:** 3.85/5
Unpretentious to the core, it's the spot for a laid-back meal among friends or a relaxed post-date. It's the essence of a Korea town hangout.

**Quality:** 5/5
They cook their chicken fresh per order, which hits the spot in both taste and price. And the cherry on top? The staff is as welcoming as the food is satisfying.

First you must have a reservation. Second it is well worth it. Everything is a wonderland for the tastebuds. I don't remember the names of everything but had a fresh tuna appetizer. Some bahn mi buns, some delicious carrots, spicy beef ramen, lobster noodles and more. Everything was great and the service was friendly and engaging. And the drinks were creative and deceptively strong. Don't miss this spot hidden in the back of the mall.

Title: A Kaleidoscope of Flavor at Camellia

If you ever find yourself yearning for a culinary adventure that's as vibrant as it is flavorful, Camellia is your go-to spot. This eatery brings a brilliant spectrum to your palate with their signature Rainbow Tsukeramen. The playful twist on traditional ramen features noodles in hues derived from natural ingredients like beets and butterfly pea flower, each bowl an edible rainbow amidst the metaphorical clouds of ordinary dining.

Unable to resist the allure of Camellia's dessert menu after devouring the ramen, I treated myself to an array of gelato. The lemon cookie zest sang with zesty notes, while the matcha was a creamy nod to tradition. The rose lychee added a floral freshness, and the coffee caramel was a rich endnote. Each flavor was a testament to Camellia's commitment to quality and creativity.

With more dishes and flavors on the horizon, my taste buds are already anticipating the next visit. Camellia isn't just a restaurant; it’s a delightful escape where every dish promises a return trip.

Title: A Slice of Tokyo in NYC at Tonkatsu Matsunoya

Tonkatsu Matsunoya transports you to the heart of Japan with its wooden decor and communal-style seating, complete with optional partitions. Ideal for solo visitors or small groups, the restaurant specializes in mouth-watering katsu dishes.

On a brisk NYC evening, I indulged in the pork katsu curry with Set A. The starter, a rich pork and vegetable soup, was a savory delight offering warmth and comfort. The accompanying cabbage and potato salads, dressed with a zesty ginger dressing, served as refreshing interludes to the main star—the katsu curry.

The curry itself struck a harmonious balance of umami, sweetness, and a hint of spice, artfully enhancing the crispy yet succulent pork katsu. Every crunch of the katsu combined with the velvety curry and rice was an audible and palatable joy, leaving me thoroughly satisfied and full.

At $19 for a generous, flavor-packed set, and no tipping required, Matsunoya stands out as a top choice for katsu cravings in Midtown. Whether you're seeking a hearty meal or something lighter, this establishment is a must-visit for authentic Japanese cuisine.

3.5. I wish we could leave half stars. Daniel has been on the bucket list for years now. We decided to have a pre Christmas splurge meal and just go for it. I will say that the expectations are very high when you go to a high end, Michelin starred restaurant. Daniel stands in a league with very few NYC institutions so the bar is set that much higher. You can see in every facet of operation and execution where the Michelin stars are earned. The staff is friendly, professional, attentive, and extremely knowledgeable when it comes to both the food and wine program. The space itself is open and inviting. We arrived 15 minutes late due to the traffic caused by the sudden snow that day. They were very accommodating in that regard. We began with a cocktail before dinner. We opted for the 7 course chef's tasting with a wine pairing. I will say that the build up of the meal from start to finish was executed expertly. It feels like you will never get full by the sizes of the dishes, but by the time the beef dish is served you are certainly full and satisfied. As you can tell by my picture, the presentation on every single dish is pristine and elegant. I won't go through each course individually but will say that the scallop I had with the cauliflower puree was quite possibly the best I have ever had. My gf has a shellfish allergy and she was accommodated wonderfully. She loved the black seabass she had in place of her scallop. Aside from the scallop, the strip loin was another of the stand out dishes. The bread selection was actually delicious. I know this is something that may not be mentioned or easily overlooked, but it is absolutely worth mentioning the freshness and execution of the breads. The petit four was a tiny delicious treat packed with great burst of flavors as well. Everything else was also good. But many of the other dishes, while beautiful, left something to be desired on the taste buds. The creativity and the artfulness is certainly there, but the depth and complexity one might expect was lacking in certain dishes. Overall, I am glad I went and had the experience. I don't know if it was the mental build up I created for myself that created unrealistic expectations or the $1,100+ price tag that left a little something to be desired at the table. I have had $600-$700 dinners that have not only rivaled but surpassed this experience in overall flavor. And at the end of the day, the ultimate scale that matters is that of flavor. If you want to have a special meal and a unique once in a lifetime experience, I suggest you save your pennies, get dressed up and go! ENJOY!!!

I recently dined at Quality Bistro and was thoroughly impressed. The superb attention to detail in the decor creates a stunning and inviting ambiance. The service was excellent, with attentive staff ensuring all our needs were met, and the bar area was particularly comfortable with its high-backed stools.

The drinks were a highlight, starting with the French Bird cocktail - a potent and sweet mix of rum and pineapple, served in a charming pineapple-shaped glass. The Lillet Cup was equally enjoyable, offering a lighter and refreshing option with its blend of gin, strawberry, and mint.

As for the food, the French onion soup was outstanding, arguably one of the best I've had. The addition of duck fat croutons and short rib pieces transformed this classic soup into an extraordinary culinary experience, maintaining the essential cheesy and onion flavors.

In conclusion, Quality Bistro is a must-visit. The combination of beautiful ambiance, attentive service, and innovative twists on classic dishes guarantees a memorable dining experience. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Title: A Stellar Experience Worthy of More Than Five Stars!

From the moment I stepped into this exceptional eatery, I knew it was deserving of more than the conventional five-star rating. The food was nothing short of exquisite, leaving me without a single complaint. It wasn't just the flavors that tantalized my palate; the presentation was equally impressive, with each dish crafted to visual perfection.

The service matched the high quality of the cuisine, with staff members proving to be nothing less than phenomenal, adding to the overall exceptional dining experience.

In my excitement, I regret not capturing better photographs as my family delved into the meal with eager haste, but that minor detail pales in comparison to the culinary journey we embarked upon.

Presented with the choice of a 4-course or 9-course prix fixe menu, my only wish was that we had indulged in the more extensive option. The four courses we enjoyed left me yearning for more of the chef's masterful creations.

I am already looking forward to my next visit, and you can bet I'll be reserving a spot for the full 9-course experience. If you have the chance to dine here, don't hesitate. It's an opportunity you won't want to miss.

Title: A Hidden Gem Uncovered!

I stumbled upon an incredible dining spot that exceeded my expectations! The staff was not only helpful but brought a lively and enjoyable energy to the table. Their recommendations didn't disappoint; every dish was a hit.

The spiced cauliflower was delightful, but the truffle-infused mushroom dish was a showstopper for my palate. Additional standouts included the flavorful guacamole and the perfectly seasoned street corn. My husband raved about the vegan chorizo and the impossible taco, which were both delicious and arrived promptly, accommodating our rush to catch a show.

The restaurant's atmosphere was undeniably hip and cool, setting the stage for a memorable experience. The margaritas, which I'm typically not fond of, won me over with fresh fruit and customizable rim flavors, complemented by a happy hour that extends into the night.

Having visited another location with consistent quality, I can confidently say this place is a solid 10/10. It's not just about the food, but the whole package: tasty eats, speedy service, and a fantastic vibe make it a must-visit. I’ll definitely be returning!
Busy place at 3:30, more busy around 4ish since near early dinner... Katsu is crunchy since freshly made but service if kind of slow since lack of staff.

I recently visited a local Indian restaurant for lunch and was thoroughly impressed by their all-you-can-eat buffet, priced at a reasonable $15. The variety and quality of dishes on offer were exceptional, allowing me to refill my plate twice, leaving me satisfyingly stuffed. An added perk was the freshly baked naan brought directly to the table. A great find for any food lover, highly recommended! 🍽️ @traveleen_gurl

Came here for dinner on a Wednesday night, it was fairly busy around 7 so we had about a 15m wait. Their waiting area is fairly small so I'd definitely recommend making a reservation, though they do offer a text service that alerts you as to when your table is ready. They have a pretty expansive menu with a wide variety of soup and rice based dishes. They also have some solid drink specials, but their portion sizes are pretty large here so I wouldn't fill up on the drinks before eating unless you're sharing a few dishes. For my first meal back in the New York cold I knew I had to go for something warm. I had never tried Tan Tan Men ramen and as spice lover I was pretty intrigued given how often it's compared to Dan Dan noodles. The broth had tasty chili oil flavor to it, but the richness certainly overpowered that at times. The pork was tasty but also had the same opposing taste to the broth. I thought the noodles went best with the chili taste and had a nice thick texture to them. While the dish was good, I felt like the spicy take they were going for is better served in a dry dish and the rich flavors suited the ramen better. Overall, I think it's a solid spot if you're in Hell's Kitchen and looking for a place with a lot of filling options it's worth checking out, but I wouldn't go out of my way to pay a visit.

My husband and I were in the area and were craving Thai food and came upon this place. We ordered pad kee mao and basil fried rice with chicken. The food tasted excellent and the restaurant was nice and clean. The service was a bit slow, but overall it was a good experience.

I can't help but rave about my repeated visits to B-Squared! Their accommodating staff is always ready to tweak your meal to your preference, such as altering the sweetness of their pasta. Plus, the affordability of the menu is a delightful bonus. Highly recommend for a personalized and wallet-friendly dining experience!

Tucked away on the corner of Amsterdam and 80th, Two Wheels may be small, but it packs a punch with its Vietnamese cuisine. The no-frills venue seats just a dozen, so expect to cozy up and order at the front in this first-come, first-serve eatery. Their elevated kitchen adds a quirky touch to the compact space.

The concise menu features staples like pho and banh mi, fitting for the family-friendly Upper West Side. During a weekend visit around 6PM, the high turnover meant a short wait for seating despite every table being filled.

The Two Wheels pho, priced at $11.95, offered a generous portion of noodles and broth, though it yearned for a richer umami depth. The brisket, although scant, was tender and enjoyable. The clear standout, however, were the Vietnamese wings ($9.95) - sticky, saucy, and irresistibly hot. The Parmesan truffle fries ($7.95) were a crispy side note, but nothing extraordinary.

My boyfriend's Vietnamese Iced Coffee ($4.50) held a complex profile of chocolate, caramel, and a smoky finish that delighted the palate. At roughly $50 for the meal, Two Wheels is a promising spot worth revisiting, particularly for the iced coffee and the wings. It's a welcome option for a semi-casual meal when in the area, even if the pho might not beckon me back without a specific craving.

Happy hour delicious drinks and oysters! There is a line before the restaurant opens but it goes quickly. The ambiance of this place is amazing! There is a 2 hour limit on the table to keep traffic moving. The drinks are refreshing - the servers are knowledgeable on their wines and drinks. The oysters are my favorite part!! One of my favorite happy hour/oyster combo place!

Came here for happy hour after work with some coworkers. It's a seat yourself kind of place. We got there at 630 on a Tuesday and all of the outside seating was taken already & a few tables close to the doors were reserved. So I suggest maybe making a reservation or getting there early if you want to sit outside. The happy hour specials are pretty lame, my coworker got a burger which was the only food item on the happy hour list. Just a burger, no sides- $5. She did say it was the best burger she's ever had though (she was also tipsy so.... maybe not the best judge.) the service was interesting, little tablets at some of the tables you could use to order and then swipe your card. This made it nice when we wanted to leave because we didn't have to wait for someone to bring us the check. Only issue was we didn't know how much to tip considering no one was taking our order or anything, just bringing out the food. Happy hour drink options were also very limited. Nice atmosphere though and was a good spot for a group of 9 people !

Title: A Chic Twist on Korean Cuisine at Hortus

My quest for contemporary, upscale Korean cuisine led me to Hortus on a Thursday night, and the experience did not disappoint. The reservations process was a breeze with options for seating; we chose the soothing grey elegance of the upstairs dining room, though the chef's table downstairs would be an intriguing choice for a future visit.

The cocktail selection, based on soju, was a delightful surprise. Both the "Garden" and the "Peachy" were exceptional, with the latter providing a refreshing twist with its hint of star anise.

Choosing from the menu, we went a la carte over the pre fixe. The truffle noodle was the star appetizer - creamy, decadent, and with noodles done just right. The calamari tempura, a unique take with fried seafood-stuffed egg and squid tentacles, was enjoyable albeit unexpected.

For our main course, the braised pork belly was sumptuous, practically melting in the mouth, and the grilled onigiri offered a subtle anchovy twist that complemented the dish well. We availed of a Yelp check-in deal for a complimentary side, which was a nice touch.

Service was competent, despite a brief wait initially and a bustling waitress. The meal progressed unhurriedly, a welcome change from the usual rushed atmosphere in Koreatown.

Hortus is a gem, offering an ambiance that's both upscale and inviting and a menu that cleverly reinterprets Asian flavors. It's an excellent choice for a date or a small gathering of friends seeking both quality cuisine and cocktails.

Title: A Refined Culinary Journey at DaDong Near Bryant Park

My experience at DaDong, nestled by Bryant Park, was nothing short of elegant. The restaurant radiates an upscale vibe, perfectly blending a modern Chinese bar and dining experience. Arriving earlier than my reservation, I enjoyed a lychee rose concoction at their inviting second-floor bar, accompanied by the most addictive spicy fried Chinese snacks.

When my party arrived, we were promptly seated in the serene third-floor dining area – a quieter yet sophisticated ambiance that I favored. We indulged in the Restaurant Week menu, supplemented by DaDong's renowned duck, which was delectable and reasonably priced.

The squid ink noodle soup was exceptional, as were the unique avocado noodles, reminiscent of a cold dan dan noodle dish. But the star was the duck, satisfying in every sense. The main courses followed, with the fried pork standing out for its robust flavor and perfectly balanced seasoning.

To finish, the dessert was intriguing, especially the fruit cup with its Asian fruits in a jelly-like juice – a sweet note to end the meal.

DaDong is an impressive establishment that stands out for high-end Chinese fare, ideal for memorable dates or business meetings. Highly recommended for those seeking to impress with a touch of culinary sophistication.

Came by for the joju fries which comes with spicy mayo, spicy green sauce, pickled daikon and carrots with cilantro.  I am hoping it's not too spicy for my tastebuds.Near the right side, there are patrons waiting for their orders either standing or sitting on the benches or the wall.  If you continue straight, you will see a line that goes to 1 manned cash register and 3 kiosks to order you food.  When my turn arrives, I went to the cashier and requested my order, pay the amount and went to wait for my name to be called.The employees getting the order ready are efficient.  I waited about 5-7 minutes then I heard my name called.  The fries came in a green square box.  The fries were still crispy on the outside and soft on the inside especially since it took me a little while before I got a chance to taste it.  The pickled daikon and carrots helped soothe any spiciness.  Next time I have to add meat to make the meal more complete to the bahn mi inspiration.This caters more for takeout place than eat-in.  However, if you are lucky to score a table/seats bear the back of the restaurant or the second floor mezzanine, definitely eat there.Can't wait to try the other fries and items.

Came here recently with a friend before seeing a show on Broadway because I'm vegan and she isn't. We loved how easy it was for us both to have a good selection of food here! We went on a Sunday evening without a reservation and only had to wait for ten minutes before getting a table. Our server was super nice and we both enjoyed our food and drinks!

Title: A Heartfelt Plea to Skip IHOP in NYC

As someone who has paid their dues on the soccer field, resulting in a less-than-perfect leg, I generally prioritize comfort and convenience when it comes to dining out, which explains my recent, regrettable experience at an IHOP in Manhattan. To be blunt, visiting an IHOP in a culinary capital like New York City is a disheartening choice, especially when the city offers an incredible array of exceptional dining options.

During a late-night food excursion, a friend lured me into this establishment, and it's an experience I struggle to understand. If you're a true food enthusiast or respect my culinary perspectives, IHOP should be off your radar—its offerings are simply subpar. It's akin to settling for a frozen meal, warmed up in your microwave, but at a higher cost and with the same level of disappointment.

This particular IHOP is no different from the rest, perhaps even falling below the already low standard. In a city where food can reach dizzying heights of deliciousness, settling for the bottom of the barrel at IHOP is a culinary crime. My advice is straightforward: save your money, spare your taste buds, and explore the true flavors of New York City instead.

The food itself is very good and flavorful! The portions are huge and can be easily enjoyed by two people. However, It is a bit confusing figuring out where to line up for food orders. There is no clear menu with pricing and items for those whom are not familiar with the cuisine.

Raku truly lived up to its reputation during my recent visit. A reservation proved essential on a bustling Saturday at this cozy establishment. My dining experience started with the much-lauded chicken tatsuta – a delightful dish served with a tasty sauce and enhanced by a squeeze of lemon. With options of 6 or 10 pieces that are generously sized, these are perfect for sharing.

Heeding the advice of prior patrons, my friend and I decided to split a bowl of their mammoth udon after the appetizers. A word to the wise: these bowls are enormous, and we were nowhere near finishing them. They’re not ideal for leftovers either, so sharing is the way to go if you want to indulge in a variety of starters.

We sampled the tantan and niku udons. Both impressed, but the tantan stood out to me with its rich, spicy broth, in contrast to the sweeter niku, though both contained a surprising abundance of beef short ribs and tripe.

Raku delivers on its promise of ample portions at fair prices, making it a destination that's well worth the trip for any udon enthusiast.

Title: A Feast to Remember During Restaurant Week

Last week, my group of four ventured out during Restaurant Week and we landed at a gem that mixed contemporary flair with divine flavors. Our adventure took us through a culinary journey that combined Restaurant Week specials with classic menu offerings.

We indulged in an array of shared dishes. The "Quack on Brioche" set a high standard, while the "Cauliflower with Blue Cheese Miso" and "Chicken Liver" from the Restaurant Week menu were notable for their unique taste profiles. However, it was the "Snow Crab Noodles" that stole the show - an absolute must-try that left us dreaming about the next visit.

Other highlights included the creamy "Japanese Sweet Potato" and the hearty "Pig Out for 2," which was a communal delight. While the "Wagyu Beef Steak" and "Rice with Duck Sausage and Kale" were solid contenders, they were overshadowed by the previous stars.

We ended the feast with a sweet note of "Chocolate Torte" and whimsical "Chinese Beignets," both from the Restaurant Week selection, which were delightful but paled in comparison to the savory dishes.

Hands down, I'm marking this restaurant for a return visit - if only to relive the magic spun by those Snow Crab Noodles. A restaurant that not only participated in Restaurant Week but truly celebrated it with standout dishes.

I have had the pleasure of dining at Morimoto both during NYC Restaurant Week and regularly outside of that time frame.  Regardless of when you go, the service is impeccable and the ambiance is classy and special without making you feel like you need to be on your best behaviour.  You can easily relax and enjoy your meal, but still feel special and enjoy your evening out.The prices here are to be expected with a celebrity chef - high, but the quality of the food and the creativity behind the meal is wonderful.  If you have the option to sit at the sushi bar, definitely do it as you will get to see the workings of the sushi and simple cooked foods line chefs.  My only qualm about this place is the quality of the sushi you get when you dine for restaurant week.  Granted, you are paying a significantly lower price, but isn't the whole point of restaurant week to give that special experience to those who normally might not be able to get it?  The tuna roll and sushi pieces I got during restaurant week were on par with supermarket sushi (edible, but nothing to rave about).  However the sushi I've gotten (like their sushi roll take on a lobster roll during the summer) was delicious and something to rave about!  Nonetheless, the service is great whenever you go, and the food overall is yummy.

Title: A Mixed Experience at the Chinatown Ramen Spot

Upon my visit to this Chinatown gem, I found myself at a crossroads, teetering between a 3 and 4-star experience. The ambiance was welcoming, and the location convenient, setting a positive tone from the start. Happy hour was the highlight, with half-off sake and shochus paired with delectable seafood tacos - the lobster and tuna were crisp, chilled, and notably fresh.

Service was commendable, with a single waitress handling the floor with efficiency and a smile, never making us feel rushed. A special nod to the generous and perfectly salted bowl of edamame, alongside an impressive selection of sake and shochu. The yuzu-infused sake, playfully presented in a shot glass overflowing into a wooden box, was a delightful touch.

The bone marrow ramen, unfortunately, failed to live up to the hype. At $18, expectations were not met with the undersized offering of bone marrow, especially in light of the larger portions glamorized on screen. The overpowering garlic also detracted from the dish, though the ramen itself, along with the beef and egg, was quite satisfying.

Overall, this spot is worth the visit for a spirited happy hour and their other menu offerings. However, I'd advise skipping the overrated bone marrow ramen in favor of their other selections. Your palate (and wallet) may thank you.

I recently dined at a local eatery where the Pad Sie Ew truly impressed me, standing out among the many I've sampled over the years. While the Spicy Basil Fried Rice left me wishing for a bit more zest, the swift and courteous service more than made up for it. Overall, a delightful dining experience that I would recommend, especially for fellow Pad Sie Ew connoisseurs.

Title: A Memorable Evening at a High-End Haven

From the moment I stepped into this culinary gem, I was captivated by its high-end ambiance and striking decor, complete with an enchanting infinity pool centerpiece. The warm lighting set the perfect tone for what was to be an unforgettable dining experience.

Our reservation was honored with minimal delay, and the staff courteously attended to our coats upon arrival. The mushroom starter was a revelation – three varieties cooked flawlessly, creating the most delectable mushrooms I've ever savored, further enhanced by a zest of fresh lemon.

While the absence of vegan main courses was noticeable, a special request for a bowl of linguine with tomato sauce was graciously accommodated, although it arrived sans the expected vegetables. Nevertheless, the pasta itself was a flavorful delight.

My family's experience was equally impressive: the salmon entrée married taste and artistry in a generous portion, while the 26 oz steak was devoured with gusto by my brother, a testament to its quality and preparation.

The service was the cherry on top; our waiter was amiable and knowledgeable, offering excellent recommendations to enrich our meal.

In summary, this establishment promises a return visit – it's a rare find that excels in creating both a feast for the senses and an exceedingly pleasant atmosphere.

I was hesitant about this spot based off their reviews and inside Eatery as it's always crazy packed with tourists. But my coworker said they have the best mushroom truffle pizza. Oh man was she ever right! It was light, flavorful, everything was so amazing!We also ordered their ravioli. The presentation was underwhelming and messy and the noodles were just slightly overcooked, but it had good flavor. Staff were very friendly, always refilling our waters. But we're a bit too anxious to turn the table as they tried taking our meals when we were still eating. Not an issue but if you're looking for somewhere where you can sit and talk, this isn't probably the place for your group.

Amazing food! Easily my favorite veggie burger in the city. Always so fresh. The salad and slaw were delicious and flavorful. This was my first time trying the sushi and definitely won't be the last loved it!

Title: A Return to Moroccan Delights

Having previously enjoyed the unique offerings at this local Moroccan gem, we eagerly revisited, and it did not disappoint. Despite the lack of reservations and a brief wait—a testament to its popularity—we were eventually greeted by Andromeda, our warm and hippie-named waitress, who expertly guided our culinary journey.

We commenced with perfectly paired hummus and babaghanush, both accompanied by soft, fresh pita. For the main event, our table was a mosaic of Moroccan classics: the chicken bastilla was a sweet and savory revelation, while the grilled merguez and mixed grill kabobs served over rice were cooked to perfection. My personal triumph was the chicken tagine, a harmonious blend of lemon and olives nestled next to fluffy couscous. Each dish was met with praise and clean plates all around.

Dessert was a shared affair of a zesty lemon custard cake and a divine, warm kunefe. The kunefe, with its melty cheese, delicate rosewater, and just-right syrup, crowned with shredded filo and pistachios, was a dessert to remember.

Such a meal is sure to linger in memory, a reminder of the rich flavors that Moroccan cuisine has to offer. This restaurant remains a must-visit for any aficionado of the genre.

Tucked in the bustling Canal Street Market lies a culinary gem that seamlessly marries Japanese and Filipino flavors — "Somewhere between Manila and Tokyo". The restaurant's inventive fusion is a true standout, particularly their offering of sandwiches and bowls.

During our visit, we indulged in the BEC sandwich, a delightful take on the traditional Silog, featuring a hearty slice of Spam Tocino and a perfectly cooked egg. The decision to add avocado for an additional $2 proved to be a wise choice, enhancing the overall richness of the dish. Each bite was a symphony of savory and sweet, thanks to the exceptional sauce and the subtly sweet Pan De Sal.

While prices tend to be slightly higher due to the prime location, the quality and creativity behind the dishes justify the cost. The chef deserves accolades for elevating the Filipino/Japanese culinary experience. It's a no-brainer — this spot is a must-try. Next time, I'm keen to explore more of their menu offerings.

I planned a 21-person get together for lunch at Havana Central and was very pleased with my experience. The restaurant has quite a few meal and beverage packages. I believe our event breakdown was about 116 bucks per person, which included empanadas appetizer, a main course with 8 or so options, a choice between three desserts, and a two-hour open bar with premium liquor, sangria, fun cocktails, and wine. Although the meal and alcohol package were combined, the restaurant was nice enough to allow the two non-drinkers to be exempt from the alcohol portion of the bill. Our server, Michael, and the manager, Daisy, were  AMAZING!!!! Micheal always made sure that our drinks were full, and Daisy checked in with us a couple of times to ensure that we were well taken care of. Note: if you are splitting the check for a large party, you should tell your guest to bring cash because the restaurant will let you split the charge between two cards.

I'm here for an event on Thursday night. The owner greeted us warmly once we got there. The event was private so they put up several tables together for us at the back of the room. We arrived around 8:30pm, there are some people still at the restaurant. The inside is quite spacious and they have some quite interesting decorations. Since the portion is quite huge, we decided to do family style and share all the dishes. We have tried many and I will only point out the top three I love! Tomato beef soup/stew is one of my favorite, it is really good for sharing at winter time. The tofu in the hot pot is the best! And the the soup has a lot of tomato in it. Note, it's a bit spicy. Pig heaven dish, it's a sweet dish that name after the restaura

Title: A Delicious Discovery

We recently dined at this gem of an eatery, and it was an absolute delight! I ordered the vegan sandwich melt, which was superb and savored each mouthful. My fiancée chose the fried chicken melt and was so impressed she lamented not ordering a double portion. A special shout-out to the cheesy tots – they were exceptional, easily the best we've ever indulged in. This spot is now a must-visit for us whenever we're back in the area. Highly recommended!

Wow! We found this place on Yelp and saw they had a lot of reviews! The food looked amazing and we loved the idea of handmade pasta. When we got there it was pretty crowded and we didn't have a reservation. The host was super friendly told us he would see what he could do and ended up finding us a table. We ordered 2 glasses of montepulciano and the burrata appetizer to start. For entree's we ordered the cavatappi with vodka sauce and the short rib! We loved the burrata and the short rib but unfortunately weren't fans of the pasta. The entire dish was undercooked. While this would usually mean 3 stars, Daniel went above and beyond for us and explained the kitchen had been having some issues with that particular pasta. We appreciated his honesty and he even sent us complimentary tiramisu which was delicious! After the amazing hospitality we received, we will definitely go back!

How I haven't written this yet I don't know.  Cafe Katja is, hands-down, my favorite German restaurant this side of the Atlantic.  And I make it a point to stop here at least once every trip to NYC.Highlights: authentic German cooking, good alcohol selection, relaxed atmoaphere even when booked, and if something goes wrong the great staff make it right!  Cannot emphasize enough: order some sausage at least once!  Bratwurst is over the moon, and the emmentaler suasage is excellent!  Regular menu is complimented by seasonal special and dessert menus.

Great go-to NY diner food. Pricey for diner food but they have massive portions and menus that are the size of short novels. Great free mints and cookies. Can almost always get in, plenty of space. 8/10

I came here to meet people that had already eaten and was just in for dessert, so that is my caveat.  Now that we have that out of the way, I came here for dessert just before the dinner rush the other day.  The host and staff were all very friendly and welcoming.  I had the flourless chocolate cake.  It was decadent and delicious.  The desserts are not huge, but the portions are a bit on the generous side, so they are probably better to share, especially after a meal.The space has a dark wood, dimly lit scene that reminds me of Houston's / Hillstone's, with old school jazz music playing.  Upscale, but not fussy.

This was a very hyped taco place, so of course we had to check it out when we visited Chelsea Market.  The line looked very long but went by pretty quickly.  My friend and I both got the pork tacos. Honestly, I expected SO much more.  The tacos are delicious, but I've had much better.  It doesn't even compare to west coast tacos.  It's worth trying if it's your first time, but I cant see myself standing in that long line again for these tacos.  Frankly, we found the dumplings from the stand next to it (Mokbar) way more delicious.  No complaints about the tacos -- they were tasty.  I just expected a lot more for a place with such outstanding reviews.

This restaurant is located in Brookfield Place and has indoor as well as outdoor seating. The service is great and the staff is really nice. The food takes some time to get to the table but it's really tasty!They're known for their burgers which definitely looked good. I went for the lobster roll which comes with fries (all of their sandwich type items come with fries). The roll was buttered and toasted to perfection. There were good chunks of lobster stuffed in it as well. The fries were thin and seasoned with sea salt. There was actually a lot of fries given! My friends got burgers and the crispy chicken sandwich which they also liked and would recommend. Although the restaurant is on the more expensive end, the meals are definitely filling and the ambience is nice.

I never went to the old location, but the new one has cute decor inside! I ordered the pad Thai and my sister ordered the green curry with chicken. We both also got Thai iced tea. I thought everything tasted pretty good. The restaurant is a bit small, so you might have to wait if it's full, but we didn't have to wait for too long and we were served fairly quickly! I would recommend stopping by if you're in the area :)

Title: My Neighborhood Pizza Gem

I'm absolutely smitten with my local pizza spot - it's become my absolute go-to for any pizza cravings. Serving up heaping slices that are generous both in size and topping goodness, they've nailed the pizza craft. Whether you're swinging by for a late-night bite, grabbing a quick lunch, or need a delicious slice on the go, this place has got you covered. The warm and friendly staff only adds to the welcoming vibe. I consider myself fortunate to have such a fantastic pizzeria right in my own neighborhood.

Delicious brunch spot! My friend and I were in the mood for a hearty brunch at a new spot after our workout on Sunday. We headed down to west village after our class as I perused Yelp along the way. We were actually on the waitlist for another restaurant but my friend didn't want to wait the 20min. I knew the wait would be long no matter where we went as it was peak time and we had no reservations, but we popped in here and the hostess offered us bar seating that was available. We sat down and the bartender was super nice and pleasant throughout, always refilling our waters and giving great options and recommendations. The service was fast, and the food was absolutely delicious. I had the ginger mimosa which was absolutely amazing as I love ginger. We started off with the hummus, and it was perfectly made and incredibly well-seasoned with some of the best pita I've ever had. I ordered the chicken shawarma, and while it was a way heftier dish than I thought it would be, it was absolutely amazing. The chicken was perfectly seasoned and flavorful, and the yellow sauce they used was unreal. My friend loved his cocktail and lamb burger as well, everything was done so well and brought out quickly!I definitely want to come back for their dinner menu as I see the reviews are great. It's definitely a popular place so I highly recommend making a reservation!

Title: Dumpling Delight in a Cozy Nook Off Mulberry St.

If your cravings are steering you towards fried dumplings, let them lead you to this hidden gem just off Mulberry St. With its modest size and a mere four chairs, this little hole in the wall is a go-to for quick takeout rather than a sit-down meal. The dumplings themselves are a standout: scrumptious, crispy, and astoundingly affordable at 5 for $1.50. Efficiency is the name of the game here; I barely spent a minute from ordering to receiving my food. Remember to hit the ATM first, though, as it's cash-only—no credit cards or digital payments here. For a speedy snack that doesn't skimp on flavor or value, this spot is unbeatable.

Great lunch special menu for bargain prices. You get two appetizers and your entree for about $15 per person. We also had the fried banana dessert with coconut ice cream.Service is prompt - they have the lunch special down. I was really hungry when I ordered and appetizers were on the table within five mins.  After we finished these, entrees were served almost immediately.We really enjoyed the chive cake (dense but small), salad and spring roll appetizers. Panang curry was so flavorful; really spicy. Vegetarian Pad thai and chicken pad see yew were both great. The venue is cool and bohemian. A great informal lunch spot or a quick date with someone you might not want to linger with!

Title: A Comforting Culinary Haven - Veselka Shines!

There are few places that consistently hit the mark, but Veselka is one such gem. Their borscht soup is simply the best, rich and hearty - the kind of dish that leaves a lasting impression. And if you're in the mood for comfort food, Veselka's pierogis are a must-try; each bite, paired with their selection of delightful condiments, is a nod to authentic Eastern European flavors.

Amidst the current climate, Veselka stands as a beacon of normalcy, with doors open wide. They've adapted with a limited menu, but the choices remain impressively varied, ensuring there's something for everyone. I recently savored their Reuben sandwich, a flavor-packed choice, alongside their 13th Anniversary bowls—a tempting trio of mushroom, meat, and cheese pierogis—complemented by a tangy side of sauerkraut and cauliflower. Every dish was a reminder of why this spot has earned its stripes.

Service here has always been on point, with waiters who are attentive and quick to meet your dining needs. During these times, Veselka doesn't just meet the standard; it soars above it, inviting patrons to support a local business that's clearly dedicated to its community. Whether you're a regular or a newcomer, Veselka promises a dining experience that's both comforting and delicious. A great spot, indeed!

I am thoroughly impressed by the food, craftsmanship, and the lovability of Chef Don Pham. I've been to quite a few omakase places in NYC - Azabu, Teisui, Nakazawa etc., Sushi Ishikawa has got to be one of my favorite Omakase that I've ever been to. Came here on a Wednesday night with a 830pm reservation at the sushi bar with my best friend, who was visiting from Australia and was his last night in NYC. If you want a memorable meal to impress, I highly recommend Ishikawa. Chef Don Pham served us that night, and boy was he good at his craft. There were three menu options each priced at $85, $120, and $155 (The Matsu). Courses vary with price point, but with the $155 option it came with 16-17 courses. Both my best friend and I went with the matsu to kick off this legendary meal. *Warning - be prepared for a flamboyantly extra and a TON of uni  (four different types) + Truffles that will be served to you! AMBIANCE:Ishikawa is a small sushi restaurant, with typical minimalist Japanese decor that you see in a lot of these sushi restaurants. Definitely doesn't feel as posh compared to Azabu or Nakazawa, but it definitely still is a place to impress. Dress code is on the slightly casual end of things, but you still see patrons coming in dressed up in business casual or formal. Sushi bar only seats about ~12 guests at a time. There are 3-4 four tops behind the counter, hence definitely a small venue.PROS:1. Nodoguro (blackthroat sea perch) - Definitely liked it! the fish tasted was pretty fatty but I did enjoy the citrus and the microchives on it. Definitely gave cut down the fattiness of the fish2. Tairagai (Japanese scallops) - So fresh! Chef Don pham definitely was able to bring out the brininess of the scallops3. Gindara Black Truffle (Black cod) - Fish was very fatty, and it was top with a layer of japanese salt (correct me if im wrong, but it was a white powder that was incredibly fluffy and umami). Definitely super flavorful.4. Dungeness Crab Toro Caviar - This was one of the best pieces of the night! Chef Don Pham definitely knows how to be creative and extra in making his sushi pieces. On top of a layer of dungeness crab, he adds a giant piece of fatty tuna and caps it with black caviar! The flavors complement each other so well, as the brininess of the caviar, the sweetness of the crab, and the fattiness of the otoro tuna tasted incredibly fresh and flavorful!5. Sayori (Japanese Halfbeak) - This fish was sligthly on the leaner side, but Chef Don charred the sushi a little bit with a blow torch which added a little smokiness and charred texture to the fish, which gave new flavors to the omakase experience. 6. Chu Toro 3 Layer Black Truffle (Tuna) - Chef sliced three pieces of tuna to make his nigiri and topped it off with a layer of black truffles. Incredibly decadent!7. Botan Ebi Foie Gras (Japanese shrimp) - The shrimp nigiri was good, and it came with a tab of butter on top. Chef seared it with his blow torch which added a level of creaminess to the shrimp.8. Uni Ikura Caviar Black Truffle (Uni with fish roe on biscuit) - First uni course of the night, the uni was very buttery, creamy, and definitely paired well with the acidity of the fish roe that it came with. Wasn't too sure about the biscuit that it came on top of it - Felt it would have been better if it came like a nigiri or sushi roll. 9. Trout Miso - Fish was a slightly fattier version of salmon, but had a good wallop of caviar on top which added some acidity and brininess to the fish. Very tasty! 10. Uni Zucchini Tempura Black Truffle - Again, a lot of black truffles in this course! The tempura was fried very crispy and airy.11. Wagyu Foie Gras Garlic Soy (Beef nigiri with Foie Gras) - Talk about extraness, this has got to be another one of my favorites of the night. Chef Don pulled out a giant slab of A5 wagyu, sliced it, torched it, and then added a giant piece of duck foie gras with a lightly seasoned salad with the Japanese white powder. The wagyu was SO GOOD, the surprisingly the added foie gras really enhanced the flavors and the butteriness of the wagyu nigiri. HIGHLY recommend this piece!12. Chawan mushi (Steam egg custard) - Really umami egg custard, there were bits of scallops inside which gave it a nice surprise and seafood flavor to it!13. Tako Hotaru Ika Cu Ceviche (Octopus salad) - The octopus was definitely poached really well and cooked to perfection. Not sure if the acidity really complimented the rest of the dish though, felt like it could use a little more fattiness or butter to really bring out the flavors of the octopus. It also came with a cute little cuttlefish and pieces of squid. Cuttlefish was a true delight!Other pieces we got include - Hamachi vinegrette (good), Hotate oyster tempura uni (FANTASTIC), Otoro caviar (good), and the uni caviar handroll (INCREDIBLE).OVERALL:I am in love with the craft that Chef Don is putting out here. Highly recommend for all sushi lovers!

We had this catered into work just now. Amazing pork meatballs. Garlic soy rice was nice too. The drunken chicken was interesting and also good. The chicken curry bao was also really amazing. Even the vegetable bao was flavorful. The braised tofu was decent for tofu.Food wise I highly recommend.

Title: A Seafood Lover's Go-To Spot

I recently revisited an old favorite of mine, a seafood restaurant that has remained a reliable source of excellent seafood and chowder over the years. Their happy hour is a real treat, especially with the dollar oyster special and well-priced drinks that make for a perfect early evening indulgence.

The quality of the oysters here never disappoints—they're consistently plump, fresh, and available in a variety of choices. And for those on the go, a neat little secret is the take-out window just to the right of the main entrance, up a slight incline. It's a hidden gem for grabbing a quick bite, offering a selection of fresh seafood sandwiches, an array of chowders, and raw bar favorites to enjoy wherever you like.

Whether you're sitting down for a meal or taking it to-go, this spot continues to be a standout for seafood aficionados.
Literally one of the best pizza spots in NYC. Quick, easy and always delicious. Love the crispy thin crust.

I'm a noodle fiend. My last meal on earth would be noodles, and if I had to pick one thing to eat everyday for the rest of my days it would be noodles. The satisfaction of good QQ is pure bliss. Look up that NYTimes article on QQ if you don't know what I mean.Thy's offers excellent value for your hard earned dollars. You can get a full meal here replete with noodles, veggies and dumplings for less than you'd spend for lunch at most places in the area. My favorite dishes here include the brothless sesame sauce noodles and the vegan Chengdu dan dan noodles. The noodles are fresh, chewy, and pick up the sauce they're in very well. This is a quick serve grab and go type of place, but there are a few tables here should you need to sit down to enjoy your meal. Howard the owner is always there and truly cares about giving his customers a great experience.

Mani in Pasta, at first I was thinking Mani is a guy, but no , it's a rough Italian translation for arms, or hands in pasta. What does it mean , is it that to make the dough for pizza you got to work it or and give it a beat down, don't know but I think it's Bout yeast ? But the square slice I got tastes good, I normally don't go for thick crust but these are lite and not heavy. Crunchy on the outside but chewy on the inside. They have a readymade selection to pick from, margherita, burrata, carbonara, diavola, and at least 4 more others. So now when I want a pizza I got to think do I want New York, Roman, Sicilian, or Detroit slice and do they use a pan and where I get it the best one, life was so simple when I was a kid but now, WOAH This was the soft open and I was to over whim with all the vendors at the Deco to remember what else Mani in Pasta had besides Roman Pizza.  But Meat Balls, Croquettes, Eggplant Parmigiana and Lasagna could be on the menu also.

Title: A Haven for Hong Kong Classics

Review:

Don't let the unassuming service deter you; this gem of a restaurant is a culinary delight for anyone craving delectable Hong Kong fare. Their pan-fried rice noodle rolls are perfection on a plate – easily a five-star standout. The menu excels with temptingly priced options that never fail to satisfy. Must-tries include the sumptuous sandwiches, flavor-packed Singapore curry noodles, and the decadently buttery French toast. Wash it all down with the classic Hong Kong mix of coffee and milk tea for an authentic experience.

While the service might lack the warmth of a smiley welcome, the staff is nothing if not quick and efficient, ensuring your food arrives promptly. However, my latest visit did suffer a slight hiccup due to a particularly odorous waiter and a seemingly disinterested new waitress, which slightly marred an otherwise stellar experience. In spite of these service glitches, I am here for the fabulous cuisine, and on that front, this establishment delivers with flying colors. Solid four stars.

Title: Surprisingly Delightful Lunch Break at Koi

I recently stopped by Koi for a lunch break and was immediately glad we'd made a reservation – the place was buzzing with the lunchtime rush. We started with a selection of appetizers, and I must say, the shishito peppers were a standout – although they packed more heat than I'm accustomed to, they are not to be missed!

We hit a slight snag when we found an unexpected item in our food, but the staff was exemplary in their response. Both the waiter and the manager were profusely apologetic, swiftly served us a new dish, and removed the charge from our bill. Mistakes happen, and it's the response that counts. Koi's team handled the incident with grace and professionalism.

With that level of service, Koi earns a well-deserved 4 stars from me. I'll definitely be returning – hopefully without the extra surprise next time!

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at Don Antonio

I ventured into an area I don't often dine in to meet a friend and decided to try Don Antonio based on its reputation. The visit was worth it, particularly for a pizza fanatic like me. I opted for the Pistacchio & Salsiccia pizza, and it was a triumph. The combination of pistachio pesto, sausage, mozzarella, pecorino, basil, and EVOO was a masterclass in flavor. Although the crust was a bit doughy for some, it hit the spot for me.

The only hiccup was the service, which mirrored the frenetic pace of Times Square. Our Montanarine Genovesi appetizer arrived post-pizza, which was less than ideal. But if you can look past the hustle of the service, Don Antonio delivers where it counts with its pizza offerings.

Title: A Disappointing Experience at Abiko's Japanese Curry

I'm an enthusiast for Japanese curry, but my recent visit to Abiko's left much to be desired. To start, the curry's spiciness was unexpectedly intense. I ordered a medium spice level, but it proved too hot for comfort, leaving me grateful for my Sprite's cooling effect.

The food itself was subpar. My pork cutlet was dry, and the curry was disappointingly bare, lacking the usual staples like potatoes and carrots—it was just a curry sauce. A side order of pork was necessary to add some substance to the meal, but it was hardly a saving grace.

Service was remarkably poor, a first for me in terms of unfriendly staff at a restaurant. The encounter was so unpleasant it made me rush through the meal and leave as quickly as possible. It's particularly disheartening to pay for an unsatisfactory meal and feel obliged to tip after such treatment.

Though the floors of the restaurant were off-putting, clean tables and seats convinced me to give the place a chance—a decision I now regret. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend Abiko's to those seeking a delightful curry experience or hospitable service.

This was more like a 3.5 stars I feel~ don't get me wrong we had a lovely romantic cocktail hr here, but there just wasn't enough to keep us from leaving. First, my drink called the lady winser was fantastic! Refreshing, light and really showed off some mixology! It was super smooth with the right amount of zest! I would definitely get it again! My bf doesn't drink so we also ordered an app to share- the menu wasn't very enticing. Of the items they had, we just went with the cheddar croquettes served with a goat cheese aioli. The plate tasted fine lol just no connection between the prosciutto, croquette n goat cheese. The prosciutto was just laid on top of everything lol The portion was solid (which made me feel relieved bc it was $13 for some potatoes!) we enjoyed the hearty plate. It did a good job soaking up the booze lol but we were ready to move on after that. The live music really set the mood which was my favorite part at BB! My bf n I were able to get really cozy n enjoyed the music with some snacks! I would return for a chill night out. It's a very nice spot for happy hr!

Title: A Symphony of Italian Flavors at Spaghetti Heaven

My dining experience at this much-raved-about restaurant surpassed expectations, especially with their much-acclaimed spaghetti, which I can boldly declare as the best I've ever had. Securing a dinner reservation on a Sunday, I walked into an aesthetically pleasing bar area adorned with a floral ceiling—utterly adorable.

The dining space boasted cute seating that further accentuated the restaurant's charm, while the service was in line with the most reputable of establishments. Their bread service, an impressive variety far beyond the typical warm rolls, served with an array of spreads including tomato, eggplant, olive oil, and mascarpone, set a high standard for what was to follow.

The meal commenced with the braised short ribs paired with risotto—an exquisite combination, with the ribs so tender they seemed to melt under the fork, and the risotto was no less delightful.

Next came the star of the evening—the spaghetti. Simple yet executed to perfection, it was al dente and served under a fascinating dome presentation, a testament to the culinary artistry housed within.

We also tried the halibut accompanied by roasted fennel and snap peas in a light yet creamy sauce. Although I'm no authority on fish, the halibut was skillfully prepared, albeit slightly underdone at the center for my taste.

Despite skipping dessert due to satiety, the gesture of complimentary biscotti was a charming touch that solidified the restaurant's commitment to excellence. And for those looking for a libation to complement their meal, do try the San Remo cocktail—it’s a must.

Eagerly anticipating my next visit, this restaurant has etched a lasting impression with its exceptional cuisine and generous hospitality.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Tenho Ramen

On a chilly evening, I sought comfort at Tenho Ramen, only to be met by a bustling crowd and an oversight that prevented me from joining the Yelp Waitlist ahead of time. The unwelcome draft by the bar where I settled added a literal chill to the already lackluster dining experience. 

Their vegetarian ramen failed to impress - a bland broth, overcooked wheat noodles, and a sparse scattering of vegetables hardly satisfied my craving. An attempt to remedy the dish’s lack of flavor with a spicy paste led to an unpleasant surprise: undisclosed ground pork, which was a serious concern being a vegetarian. The server's response to this oversight was apologetic but unsatisfactory, brushing off responsibility without addressing the underlying issue.

My partner's traditional tonkotsu ramen was similarly disappointing, lacking the rich flavor and noodle texture we anticipated. The evening concluded with a sense of regret, having spent over $70 for an experience that left us both hungry and disheartened. The discovery of pork in an unexpected place and inadequate service response further soured our visit. 

In conclusion, Tenho Ramen earns a mere two stars from us – a reflection of both the uninspiring food and the need for better transparency and communication.

Title: A Timeless Vietnamese Gem

If you're ever in the neighborhood and craving Vietnamese classics, look no further than this old-school staple. Despite years between visits, I was delighted to find that absolutely nothing had diminished in quality or charm. The dishes arrive astonishingly fast, as if measured in femtoseconds, without any compromise on taste. The portions remain generous to a fault, ensuring you leave with a full belly and probably a takeout box. The staff exudes warmth, adding to the welcoming atmosphere. And here's a tip: don't be deceived by the deceivingly titled "lunch menu" – those same savory options are up for grabs at dinner as well. Highly recommended for a hearty, authentic experience.

The food is decent, some dishes were delicious. The service was atrocious. We were seated and served water. After 15 minutes, no one came to take our order. We asked the person who served us water to let the waiter know we were ready to order...10 minutes later the waitress showed up to take our order. We almost got up and left. The food was good once we got it. The restroom was filthy, water splashed everywhere. The floors had hand towels and toilet paper on the floor. It's 2pm on a Sunday. They were only 1/2 full. No reason for the slow service and shoddy facilities. In a city filled with restaurants, good food itself is not enough, you need decent service and facilities too. I would not come back here.

This place is very hot on Thursday night, so I can only imagine how crowded it is on weekends. If you don't have a reservation, try another time. Don't plan on doing the Yelp waitlist because it may close within minutes. I ended up skipping my fitness class and going there an early to put my name down after seeing that the waitlist is closed at 5pm. The host estimated it to be an hour wait, which turned out to be at least an hour and a half wait if we didn't escalate our frustration. Food: Not bad, very interesting flavor. Please note that I usually do not eat vegan. Pretty big portion- guac: very high in lime acidity- nachos: sizable, better to share in large group- ceviche: interesting flavor - burrito: very basic and full with rice- taco: really good, especially since it's vegan- Enchiladas: taste more like a gumbo?- Pumpkin pie: a bit more acidic than I like - Coconut Dream Cake: THE HIGHLIGHT! It even has real coconut pieces, which make the cake super nice and light. Service makes up for the hefty wait, but not sure I'll be back for food. Maybe for the bar and cake, seems more like a place for drinking.

Love Wokwok for my go-to delivery order. I have a few favorites but I find any of their noodle dishes to be very delicious. They hold well during delivery which is most important to me. I've also tried the beef curry and hainese chicken. All really excellent and fresh.Lastly, in every order, regardless of what I get, I always add Taiwanese popcorn chicken as an app. You can choose your spice level so I always get it extra spicy. It is soooo good and plentiful. Like gigantic in portion size. Easy to share between 2-4 people.

Delicious spot. Peanut sauce wheat noodles were off the charts and the pork and chive dumplings ( fried ) were amazing! Highly recommend this spot to anyone looking for a delicious 5$ combo ( pasta & dumplings ). :)

Title: A Serendipitous Find in the Financial District

During an impromptu visit to Manhattan's bustling financial district, I fortuitously discovered a gem of a restaurant while seeking a dinner spot post-sightseeing. Abandoning my usual Yelp-reliance, this leap into the culinary unknown proved to be a delightful surprise.

Highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the mulligatawny soup, arguably the best rendition I've ever savored. With a rich tapestry of flavors that negated my habitual reach for the salt shaker, it was a testament to perfect seasoning.

While the chicken vindaloo was also impressive, a tad more potato would have been ideal. However, given the dish's potent heat, it's hardly a sticking point, especially when paired with refreshing beers and a cooling side of raita, both of which provided a pleasant counterbalance to the spice.

My experiences in Manhattan are infrequent, but this restaurant has secured a spot on my must-visit list for future trips.

Really enjoyed Trademark!I stumbled in here because a different restaurant on the street had too long of a wait and I was pleasantly surprised. It's HUGE, and the menu is great and reasonably priced. My friend and I shared the tuna poke appetizer and it was fantastic, and a large portion too. I had the kale salad and added salmon and it was excellent. My friend had the chopped salad with steak. Her steak was undercooked (she ordered medium-rare but the steak was basically raw) and the staff had no issue not charging her for it. (I like my steak rare and I had a bite. It was good, but hey, to each their own). We came in at the perfect time when we could still be seated without a reservation. However, by 7:30pm on a Thursday there wasn't a single empty table.

Fantastic spot for drinks and a casual hangout. There's ample indoor seating split into two decently sized rooms, and also space for outdoor seating as well. Came here on a Thursday night at 6:00pm and the place wasn't too packed. We were immediately seated by the hostess. Came here only for drinks, my cousin got the "Watch me matcha" drink and I got the "Houston" drink. Happy hour lasts till 7pm and we managed to make it. $11 for a cocktail during HH so its a small discount from their regular menu during normal business hours. Drinks were fantastically made. My houston drink was really smooth - think of a moscow mule vibes. The watch me Matcha drink was beautifully made too - the egg white really adds more flavor to the matcha-ness of the drink, and neither drinks were too overpowering.Love the ambiance here, music wasn't too loud so great for a good conversation. Definitely a great spot to visit either for a date or just catching up with a friend.

Title: A Touch of Havana for Lunch

If you're in search of an adorable Cuban corner, look no further! Tucked away and unsuspecting, this little gem impersonates a slice of Havana with its spacious interior, boasting a welcoming bar and dual dining areas. Stopping in for an early lunch around 11:45 am, the place had yet to bustle, providing a tranquil dining atmosphere.

The lunch menu is impressively authentic and reasonably priced. I indulged in the mushroom sandwich, accompanied by a generous side salad, all for just $14. The basil dressing drizzled over the sandwich was so tantalizing I requested an encore. Meanwhile, the dressing on my salad was equally delicious. My companion's Tiger Salad also received high praise—it's worth noting my side salad matched up to her main in size!

Their lunch special deserves a shout-out too: choose between soup/salad or sandwich with a soup for about $16. To wash it down, I opted for a non-alcoholic mojito, which was the perfect compliment to the meal.

Service was top-notch; our waiter radiated friendliness and efficiency, ensuring our meals arrived promptly. Both my dining buddy and I left satisfied and relaxed. This charming spot offers a serene lunch experience without the typical midday clamor. 

I'm eager to spread the word about this place. It's ideal for anyone craving a laid-back yet flavorful lunch. Definitely worth a visit!

Meet some friends here before an event in the area we were looking to relax w some food & drinks. This place is a little hard to find I completely past it since it's a bit hidden. Once inside very small location but u don't feel too squished in? A little close but not terrible.Took advantage of the happy hour specials I had the 3 tacos , very good steak nice taste good tasting chicken & not bad on the beef.  Had me a frozen margarita ahh this was ok didn't really taste much liquor for the most part. My company had the Quesadilla this was good & a mango margarita ahh same deal not a lot of liquors. Other friends did better since they got beer can't go wrong. Such a small location, funky decor .. decent food & prices during happy hour.

In a city full of tons of pizzerias and Italian restaurants, it's hard to find good, high-quality, and mouth-watering pizza. Look no further than Rubirosa because once you've had the pizza here, everything else will never taste the same. They have an entire gluten-free menu (in addition to their regular menu), like what, are you serious? I've had plenty of gluten-free Italian food, but none of it compares to the level of quality, taste, and texture that my palate experienced at Rubirosa. I got the gluten-free Tie-Dye pizza and my friend got the regular Tie-Dye. The gluten-free pies are a bit smaller but still enough to fill you up. We also got gluten-free mozzarella sticks (mind-blown). The Tie-Dye pizza is the most famous on Instagram and for good reason - I highly recommend it!Definitely make a reservation if you can, especially for dinner because those time slots fill up 3-4 weeks in advance. Lunch reservations are pretty readily available though. If you don't have a reservation, you'll probably end up waiting 1-2 hours for a table (walk-ins are welcomed), which isn't ideal but it's worth the wait.  The restaurant itself is small and cramped - very New York. The service was above average, nothing exceptional but it's so busy that you can't expect for the servers to check-in with you every so often. The bathroom is very, very hot and not the cleanest, so I wouldn't recommend going number 2 in there (dairy-free folks, remember to take your lactase pills).

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Bustling City Eatery

Upon visiting a popular New York restaurant during a busy weekday evening, my experience left me with a sense of ambivalence. Despite the commendable hustle and bustle at 6 pm, the restaurant's policy requiring complete parties to be present before seating seemed inconvenient, though their consideration of post-dinner show plans was a thoughtful touch.

Unfortunately, the main event – the food – fell short of expectations. The chicken taco I ordered was a letdown with its dryness and lackluster size, failing to justify the steep price point. On the brighter side, the guacamole served alongside provided a fresh reprieve from the otherwise disappointing meal.

The atmosphere, while lively, proved to be a double-edged sword. Its energy bordered on overwhelming, making it a challenging venue for serious conversations as I found myself raising my voice to be heard.

In conclusion, while the location and certain details were favorable, the combination of subpar fare, high prices, and a noisy setting only warrants a two-star rating for this establishment. Perhaps it was an off-night or an unfortunate menu choice, but as it stands, I remain unconvinced of the value this restaurant offers.

Title: Quick and Easy Pizza on the Go

I recently visited a spotlessly clean and sleek pizza joint, notable for its celebrity-endorsed wall and an eye-catching display of pizza varieties, including a unique Mac and cheese option. I opted for the pesto pizza, which, while not overwhelmingly flavorful, hit the spot for a quick and convenient meal. The crust and breading were passable - not exceptional, but certainly adequate for a meal in transit. The prices were reasonable, adding to the convenience factor. For those busy with shopping at the underground market or about to catch a subway, this place offers a decent pizza fix that won’t slow you down.

Pretty good, solid choice for Thai or basic sushi in the area. Small, cozy restaurant, quick and friendly service and portions are pretty generous. I didn't love all of the appetizers we ordered but rock shrimp was great and so was the special sushi rolls we ordered. We also had a bottle of sake which was excellent!
Reliable bar food and friendly staff.  Reasonable selection of beers on tap.  Get the Australian Burger with a fried egg.  Their fries are thick and still crispy.  Excellent!!!!

Title: A Brunch Haven Overlooking Bryant Park

My dining experience at this gem in the heart of Manhattan was, for the most part, delightful. The restaurant's interior struck me immediately with its soaring ceilings and grand windows offering a picturesque view of Bryant Park. The well-spaced tables, a rare luxury in the city, provided a sense of privacy that is often hard to come by.

My friend and I started with raspberry mimosas, though there was a slight hiccup when we were served the wrong drinks. The server promptly fixed the mistake, reflecting good service recovery. I indulged in the truffle burger on the server's recommendation, and it did not disappoint—lush with shaved truffles and justifiably priced at $20. We also shared the borscht soup, which was a pleasant addition to our meal.

Dessert was a strawberry mousse cake titled "love me, love me not," a beautifully executed finale to our brunch. However, the service wavered again when my Americano arrived in an espresso cup, which led to another mix-up. This second instance drew the attention of a manager whose intervention, while appreciated, felt more confrontational than helpful—a slight tarnish on an otherwise lovely visit.

Overall, this establishment offers a relaxed atmosphere for a catch-up with friends and an excellent location to explore Bryant Park afterward. Despite a few service missteps, the quality of food and ambiance shine through.

Take me back to a time where all restaurants had the same charm as Delmonico's. A classic feel - just think of all the influential people who have dined here.. It was a Thursday night during restaurant week, my boyfriend and I had reservations for 8 PM (made 2 days prior). The restaurant was packed and there were a heard of people waiting for their reservations amongst us. It was such a beautiful space. We only waited about 10 minutes for our table to be ready.
