As we were seated, we found the Delmonico signature plates neatly placed on our table. Our server greeted us and ran through the specials, but we already had an idea of what we were going to order. Appetizer; - Crispy local Burrata: My goodness, the most milkiest and soft textured burrata you've ever tasted. - Heritage Pig Bolognese: Perfectly cooked cavatelli with a tasty bolognese sauce. Great portion for an appetizer, too much of this would be too heavy. Entrees; - 18 Hour Braised Short Ribs: A standard short rib, just a tad dry in my opinion. - Prime Delmonico Rib Eye (medium cooked), accompanied with a side of mixed vegetables: A-freaking-mazing, that's all I have to say. So worth the $20 supplement. Dessert; - Baked Alaska: I saw this all over Yelp, I had to taste it for myself, did not disappoint. I've never had a baked Alaska this good.- NY Style Cheesecake: Honestly, a great piece of cheesecake. Really would recommend if you are on the fence. I hate to say it but service was a bit lacking. We tried to flag down our server for something and we couldn't get a hold of him. He was a bit inattentive which was surprising for a restaurant at this standard. Delmonico's can be a little pricey, thank you for participating with restaurant week!!

I don't enjoy ramen, but when I do, it HAS to be in New York. The lines are a drag, especially for a weekend dinner. Ordered the Spicy Chicken Miso Paitan, which comes flavored with rice-malted (koji) miso with a half boiled egg, scallions, onions, chicken (or pork).

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Prince Street Pizza

If you're craving some top-tier pizza, Prince Street Pizza's Spicy Spring Square is an absolute must-try. The pepperoni's flavor is robust, the cheese generous, and the dough thick yet cooked to perfection. Believe the buzz – it lives up to its reputation. 

Don't be intimidated by the queue; it’s deceiving. The staff is a model of speed and efficiency. Payment is a breeze with both cash and credit accepted. Although there's no formal seating, a bit of luck might snag you some coveted counter space.

A side note on their margarita slice: it's a solid choice for variety. But nothing could steal the spotlight from the Spicy Spring pie. Even as someone who's not typically a pepperoni aficionado, I was thoroughly impressed.

Prince Street Pizza is worth the wait, and I’m already looking forward to my next visit. It’s clear – this place is a cut above the rest.

Title: Bottomless Brunch Falls Short on Flavor

I recently visited this establishment with high hopes for a delightful bottomless brunch experience with friends. Unfortunately, the food did not live up to expectations. The Lechon Asado Con Mojo, a dish featuring shredded suckling pig, was disappointingly bland, lacking any real flavor or culinary depth. The Moro, a classic side, was unevenly cooked, leaving me with an inconsistent mix of soft and undercooked, hard grains - far from enjoyable. The saving grace of our brunch was the unlimited drinks, which were indeed plentiful. However, when it comes to the search for authentic and tasty Cuban cuisine, I find myself inclined to look elsewhere in the future.

Amazing vegan food, fun, exciting atmosphere, and good drinks. Their reservation policy is relatively strict in that they hold tables for only 15 minutes and won't seat you until all parties have arrived. However, they seated our party of 4 when only 3 of us had arrived, and we didn't feel rushed even though they have a policy of trying to keep diners there no longer than 90 minutes. The food was yummy and had tons of flavor. I'm not vegan or vegetarian and found the food delicious and the menu wasn't too limited for me. I had the pomegranate jalapeño cocktail which was great. A slight kick, not too sweet, and the lemon slice with dried cranberries on it was a nice touch. Took a little bit to get asked for my drink order which was the only negative, but all was great other than that.

So I've been working in Midtown forever, and this place is like literally two blocks away from my job, but I've never been here before.  Though of course I've passed by countless times.  This is strictly based on the lunch I've just taken out from here.  Salmon burger with fries.  Very well done and tasty.  Although I wish the bun wasn't as multi grain/seeded as it was.  Then again, since this is a 'healthy' place I guess that would make sense it's not just a plain bun.  Also the fries weren't the type I usually go for, they were bit spicy, I left most of them alone, as I was just recovering from last night's awful heartburn and also because the salmon burger was pretty suffice on its own.  I was pleasantly surprised that the salmon w/the fries only cost me 10.83.  Considering this is a 'healthy' place and the fact that this is Midtown, or pretty much anywhere in the city, I expected it to be more expensive.So far so good.  I've yet to try their other foods to fully access the place.  Because I'm not familiar and not understanding why such low rating.

Málà Project is perfect for spicy lovers but if you don't, you have the choice of non-spicy dry pots. Just know that the flavor might not be there since it's all about the spices and seasoning that make their dry pot tasty. Went on 2018 Near Year's Eve for dinner with my family (9 of us). There was no wait and we were fortunate that this place still opened when most of the restaurants were closed around Times Square. We ordered 4 appetizers and three dry pots with 7-8 items in each pot. We ordered purple rice to go with it (extra $) or else it would be too salty. Portion wise, everyone was content and the total bill for the whole table wasn't too bad. It was a bit higher compared to the same type of cuisine in Chinatown and Flushing, however.Notable appetizers: "Mouth-watering chicken" and "Husband and Wife Lung Slices" - by the way, these terms are direct translations from Chinese but are they good!A tip when ordering dry pots: Separate your proteins (beef, chicken, pork) from the seafood. Make one pot with more proteins and 1-3 vegetables, and make your second pot with seafood and a lot more vegetables. This would allow you to experience different taste and flavors.

First and foremast, Ho Foods is a tiny restaurant! It can sit no more than 15ish people, so I would recommend coming in a small party. My friend and I came here on a Saturday night and waited around 40 minutes. The menu is short, to the point, and solid. There are literally only 4 dishes! The dishes are classic and done pretty well, but I expected more given how much focus goes into just 4 items. Come expecting East Village Asian food prices. -Beef noodle soup ($14.50): I got my "rich and spicy" ($2 extra), which means there's more bone marrow, and there's added spice. There are other add-on variations you can get. You have the option of getting thin or wide noodles (I opted for the thin). The dish was overall pretty solid, albeit a little overhyped in my opinion. I liked the broth, but thought it was lacking a little something. There wasn't a ton of depth to the broth itself besides the spice. The standout part of the bowl was the beef. The meat/tendon practically melted in my mouth - so impressed! It's amongst the better beef noodle soup in the city, but you can definitely find comparable ones in Chinatown for cheaper.-Soy cucumbers ($6.50): delicious, standard cucumber Asian side dish. Great to pair with the beef noodle soup, but nothing to rave home about-Homemade soft tofu ($8.00): loved the century egg that came on it but didn't love the tofu itself -Lu ro fan ($8): pork belly on rice. It was tasty and filling. The service was excellent!The food was all around solid, but I can think of better places to get comparable items of each of the dishes, at a cheaper price as well. Having said that, I think it's worth checking out if it's peaked your interest, and you will definitely walk away happy and full, but it's just not super memorable to me. The meat in the beef noodle soup was the star of the show.

Title: A Chance Encounter with Menkui-Tei

I stumbled upon Menkui-Tei in midtown, a promising spot for a ramen aficionado amidst a sea of burgeoning noodle houses. My first visit, though impromptu, warrants a second; not out of sheer delight but rather the quest for a truly satisfying bowl.

Opting for takeout, I tried their Gekikara Ramen, a dish that promised a spicy miso kick. Unfortunately, it missed the mark, delivering neither the anticipated heat nor the depth of miso flavor. It wasn't a letdown, simply forgettable.

However, the Aspara Shimeji was a revelation—stir-fried asparagus with shimeji mushrooms in butter—an exquisite dish that certainly calls for seconds.

The service shone brightly, and with prices that don't break the bank, Menkui-Tei is on my list for a redo. Next time, I'll be dining in.

I recently had the pleasure of brunching at a delightful spot that puts a modern twist on the most important meal of the day. The menu is refreshingly health-conscious, with a focus on seasonal ingredients that bring out the freshness in each dish. Alongside my meal, I sipped on a comforting chai tea, charmingly served in a cute clay mug—just the kind of detail that makes a dining experience memorable. This restaurant is the perfect setting for a brunch date, blending a contemporary culinary approach with a cozy ambiance that invites you to relax and savor the moment. Highly recommend for anyone looking to start their day on a deliciously wholesome note.

I recently visited this charming restaurant and had the pleasure of trying their Penne Alla Gennaro. The dish was a delightful blend of penne pasta, peas, prosciutto, and a rich cream sauce. It was not only delicious but also arrived promptly, which I greatly appreciated. The wait staff struck a perfect balance of attentiveness without being intrusive, ensuring a comfortable dining experience. To complement my meal, I opted for the lemon vodka martini, which proved to be a fantastic pairing. I would highly recommend this dish and drink combination to anyone looking for a satisfying and well-coordinated meal.

Title: A Satisfying Bowl of Ramen in Manhattan

As someone who isn't a ramen expert, I was pleasantly surprised by the flavorsome broth at this cozy Manhattan spot. The rich, umami-packed broth paired with slightly al dente noodles created a delightful culinary experience that's kind to your wallet. The ambiance strikes just the right note – intimate enough for a casual outing yet suitable for an unpretentious business lunch. Whether you're a ramen enthusiast or just in the mood for a tasty lunch, this place is definitely worth checking out.

Title: A Chelsea Gem Serving Authentic Italian Flavors

I recently discovered a fantastic Italian restaurant tucked away in the heart of Chelsea. Despite visiting during the busy lunch rush, the experience was nothing short of delightful. The standout starter was the burrata appetizer — an indulgent creamy dream, perfectly complemented by a pesto drizzle that tied the flavors together on the accompanying toasted bread. 

The main course, a beautifully crafted rigatoni pasta, featured a generous dollop of rich ricotta, with sopressata and onions lending depth to each bite. The handmade pasta is a game-changer, elevating the dish to new heights of culinary excellence. This place left a lasting impression, and I'm already eager to return for another taste of their authentic Italian offerings.

Finally got a chance to try out Tzarevna and so glad I did. Came here with family and we had the most amazing meal, fantastic wine and great service. Every dish we ate I could recommend. Dumplings, khachapuri, rice, borscht, everything. Great job. Can't wait to come back!

Title: A Splurge-Worthy Feast at One of NYC's Top Korean BBQ Spots

If you're searching for an exceptional Korean BBQ experience in NYC, look no further. This gem stands out with its mouthwatering marinated short ribs – an absolute must-try for their juiciness and robust flavor profile. Their bulgogi doesn't fall far behind, with its remarkable tenderness that's sure to please your palate. Beyond the grill, the restaurant offers an enticing array of spicy non-BBQ dishes that are equally impressive. Perfect for a night out with friends who aren't shy about indulging a bit, despite the higher price point, this eatery is a solid choice when you're craving quality Korean cuisine.

Noree Thai was recommended by a friend.  When I asked where it was I was very surprised that it was in Chinatown (it is usually the case where the concentration of great Thai spots are usually in Queens).  I must have passed it many times without realizing. It is conveniently located near the B and D train station near Grand Street. It was a bit chilly when I had decided to go and visit the place and I was looking for some great Thai food. The interior decoration I would describe as very cool because it kind of makes you feel you are eating at a Thai street shop.  One wall has some well placed graffiti and there is a decent amount of seating as well as a very fully stocked bar.  During prime hours I can see how this place might be busier. When I arrived, it actually was not too busy. A gentleman acknowledged me (they were busy) and another person directed me to a nice seat against the wall (opposite the bar).  All the employees whom I dealt with were very polite and courteous.  My beautiful server, Nattaya deserves a lot of praise. She was usually always busy but very thorough - checking on all the tables and helping make drinks behind the bar with another employee.  But she always checked back with me to make sure everything came out all right and if I needed anything else. As busy as she was, she was also genuinely polite and understanding when I could not decide what to order initially. Since it was my first time there, I asked her what she would recommend as the menu has quite a few items that I was not familiar with.  She made some suggestions and I chose what sounded like the tastiest (and I had to take into account that it was only me dining in).  Skewers - a mixture of chicken, beef, lamb, seafood and vegetables with different seasoning (cumin, satay and lemongrass).  They were all very tasty. It was a total of six skewers which was a great appetizer.Rib Eye Steak - it was cooked a bit more than I would have liked but still tasted great.  It came with sticky rice, raw cabbage, cucumbers and dipping sauce.  Chicken Khao Soi (crispy curry noodle) - During my visit I actually did not see it on the menu.  When it comes to noodle dishes for Thai, I usually stick to what I know is good and had never tried this particular dish before.  She explained all the ingredients and spoke very highly of it,  I was warned it had a kick to it.  When it is all mixed together (the egg noodle, scallion, onions, bean sprouts and pickle mustard greens) this is a very hearty meal. I usually just have a soda pop or water with meals but I was a bit curious about the drink menu. She recommended the Tender Storm (Suntory Whiskey, Lime Juice, Simple Syrup with Lavender Extract drops).  I checked the menu and did not see this item either and was informed that it was a new drink at that time.  Needless to say it was very strong and the flavor combination worked. This is a very good after work or happy hour type drink in my opinion (if you partake in alcoholic beverages).  Noree Thai is a spot that I would highly recommend if near and around Chinatown.  It is perfect for big groups, eating with a few friends or if you are just looking for some very good Thai food and very courteous customer service.

Close proximity to Rockefeller Square. We did make a reservation just in case. Your standard looking Italian restaurant. Personally, I do think prices were a bit high for the quality. I do understand that the price will be more because of being in NYC, but I've dined in many upscale cities and restaurants with similar dishes and didn't find anything exceptionally different about this place. Honestly, I've made linguine like this at home and it wasn't far off. So not handmade pasta. Not sure if this place is a chain, but it sure felt like it. The service was a bit lacking, pace wise and check-ins. Reminded me of an upscale Olive Garden.

Tucked away in Kips Bay, this charming Italian eatery offers a warm and inviting atmosphere along with attentive service. The menu, reasonably priced throughout, accommodates with delightful gluten-free options. A true hidden gem for Italian cuisine aficionados.

I really enjoyed our meal here. We got the following:-zucchini and eggplant chips: this was great and I definitely recommend. I did like the zucchini better than the eggplant. The breading was light and crispy, which was perfect and the yogurt dipping sauce was great.-Greek salad: we loved this. The tomatoes were so fresh and the feta was great. The dressing also had great flavor. We ordered another salad after we finished the first because it was so good. -spanakopita: we didn't like this dish. The filling didn't have much flavor. I wish there was more feta mixed in with the spinach.-Branzino: very fresh and a good portion. We also loved the lemon potatoes that came with it.I would recommend going here if you want good Greek food.
Inside a food court, had the bbq chicken with rice, Mac and cheese and cole slaw. Flavor was fine overall though the chicken was a bit dry. Enjoyed the Mac n cheese very much.

Glad I rediscovered this place I forgot how good it is.  First time back we had no rsvp no biggie wait time by the bar area is great since they have the late happy hour, we got the Lychee martini sooo good!! Great tasting & good amount of alcohol, usually my go too here. Kalbi short rib is amazing great tasting sauce grill just a few minutes each side & it's perfect.. definitely a favorite. Great tasting Filet Mignon.  Meats tend to be excellent here.  We also tried the Shrimp very good with the garlic sauce. The Sauté chicken was good as well, do prefer the meats. On the sides The Chicken garlic noodles are great, nice tasting noodles great flavor. Can't stay away from the Garlic rice lorddd so tasty. Sauté Spinach in garlic is delicious such a great taste. Appetizers can be tricky since it can be too much food, the Calamari is really good lightly battered great dipping sauce. Wings are good as well. Rsvp help but are not necessary, service is quick & prices are very reasonable great tasting food & drinks at reasonable prices will for sure keep coming back.

Title: A Cozy Noodle Haven in the Heart of NYC - Ichiran Ramen

If you're craving authentic Japanese ramen without crossing the Pacific, Ichiran in NYC is your go-to spot. Its unique solo dining concept, featuring individual booths, makes for an intriguing experience. You're not totally isolated, though – dividers can be retracted for shared dining. Ordering is a breeze, thanks to the straightforward paper forms, but be warned, their 'medium' spice level packs a punch!

Opting for a vegetable broth requires a quick chat with the server, but it's worth the extra step. Service is incredibly efficient, with steaming bowls of ramen arriving promptly – a perfect remedy for the New York winter chill. Pricing is reasonable, especially considering the no-tipping policy, which is a welcome departure from the usual added cost.

Overall, Ichiran is a must-try in NYC for a taste of Japan. The anticipation for my next visit is already brewing!

I recently dined at a sushi spot that proved to be good, albeit not hitting the 'great' mark for me. Admittedly, I'm more of a roll aficionado than a connoisseur of the traditional sushi experience, which may color my opinion. The establishment didn't cater to my roll preference, focusing more on individual nigiri pieces. However, I must commend the freshness of their offerings; the salmon sashimi appetizer was notably outstanding, and pairing it with their green tea comes highly recommended.

My companion and I opted for a modest meal of six and five pieces, respectively, which proved to be just satisfying enough without leaving us overstuffed. We contemplated ordering more but ultimately declined. A word to the wise on timing: we faced a half-hour wait to be seated, but thereafter, the crowd seemed to dissipate.

All in all, if you're a purest in pursuit of fresh, quality fish, this might be your haven. Roll enthusiasts, however, might want to look elsewhere.

Title: A Mixed Experience at the New Ramen Spot

My friends and I, avid ramen enthusiasts, were abuzz with excitement to visit this new ramen shop in town. Eager to dive into their offerings, we started with an assortment of beef skewers - washugyu skirt, ribeye, short rib, and a spicy washugyu. The skewers did not disappoint, especially the ribeye and short rib, which stood out as table favorites.

Moving on to the main event, each of us selected a different ramen bowl, under the condition that they all were based on a non-vegetarian, pork broth. Sadly, the ramen fell short of our expectations due to an overly oily broth. As someone who usually enjoys the richness of fats and oils, I was surprised to find the broth’s greasiness overwhelming, preventing us from sipping it as we would have liked. Despite this, the toppings deserve commendation for their robust flavors and helped redeem the dish marginally.

In an attempt to mitigate the oiliness, I seasoned my broth with spicy garlic and chili powder, which somewhat counterbalanced the slick texture. Although we had mixed feelings about the ramen experience, I appreciate the variety this place brings to the city's food scene and am glad we gave it a try.

Reservations aren't needed, but if it's more than 10+ people it's better to make a reservation. Usually it's busy but not crazy so it's fine. Decent food and alright prices. Not the best Chinese food I've had and alright ingredients but they still tastes good and had a nice gathering with friends. The rice was okay but a bit on the harder and drier side like it's not really fresh. Braised and stir fry dishes are better and fried dishes are not as good. Soups are fine. Duck was decent but not as satisfying as other places I've been to, just felt like something was missing but I couldn't quite tell what. We had a room of two tables (almost 20 people) but the AC downstairs was broken and they didn't have a fan either. It was really warm and felt a bit suffocating but the staff said there are two empty tables upstairs and luckily we got to move up. They were a little pushy saying the other table ordered 8 main courses but we only had 5 and some are appetizers that it won't be enough. We added two more dishes and she still said it won't be enough for us to eat. Decently clean and one restroom at the back of the restaurant. Not hard to find and walkable to subway stations. It's a okay place but not my go to and not something I'll particularly recommend.

Title: Cozy Dinner at Ocean Prime After Santa Land Festivities

We chose Ocean Prime for our post-Santa Land family dinner based on a friend's glowing anniversary experience there. Arriving at 9:40 PM, we were immediately seated despite a bustling dining room, which, to our relief, maintained a pleasant noise level.

Our server was prompt and courteous, an appreciated professionalism considering our seven-year-old’s fatigue. Although our meal choices were made hastily, they included a tender and well-seasoned Filet Mignon (9/10), and a somewhat dry Teriyaki Salmon (7.5/10) unexpectedly paired with mushrooms, which was less to my liking.

The Creamed Spinach (8/10) was tasty, if a bit overly salted, and the Roasted Garlic Potatoes were enjoyable, even though I again encountered mushrooms. My daughter's Cheeseburger from the kids' menu seemed agreeable, though she didn’t take to it for reasons unknown; the fries, reminiscent of Cajun fries from Five Guys, were a hit with me.

Crowning our meal was a shared slice of cheesecake (10/10) – a large, rich, and flavorful dessert that emerged as the highlight of our dining experience.

While the service and ambiance of Ocean Prime were impeccable, the food was a mixed bag – good in parts, but overall average. Despite this, the merits of the steak and dessert hold enough promise for a potential return visit, with a more careful selection of sides next time.

Last night's dining experience at this gem of a restaurant was a delightful journey for the palate. The establishment radiates a warm and inviting ambience complemented by an exceptional cocktail selection that elevates the entire meal.

As part of a large group, we had the pleasure of indulging in a diverse range of appetizers. The clear standout was the luscious burrata paired with a crispy fried green tomato – a testament to the chef's ability to season and balance flavors exquisitely. Seafood lovers were treated to fresh offerings, including uni, scallops, and raw oysters, which, although not personally sampled, received high praises from my trusted companions.

My main course, a beautifully fresh halibut, could have benefitted from a pinch more salt, but its freshness was unmistakable. A testament to the restaurant's promise of using only fresh, never frozen fish.

Dessert was a shared adventure, with every option on the menu gracing our table. The sour cherry tart won me over with its impeccable crust, while the strawberry meringue dazzled with its innovative blend of matcha and yuzu flavors. The cheesecake, a bit too adventurous on the savory side for my taste, was fortunately saved by an exquisite raspberry mint sorbet.

In summary, this restaurant delivers a fantastic dining experience, with a few minor tweaks that could make it unparalleled. Whether it's for the food, the ambience, or the drinks, I will undoubtedly be returning.

Went on a relatively early Sunday morning so we were seated immediately.  The individual booths made for an interesting experience but overall was expecting a little more for the price. Had the Classic Tonkatsu Ramen with the recommended toppings set. The ramen noodles were good but the chashu topping was a bit dry. Worth a try for the experience but probably won't be returning.

Great place!  Cool location (on top of what used to be One Chase Plaza). You're 60 floors up in a swanky looking pub with floor to ceiling windows that display amazing lower Manhattan views.When you first arrive there is a large bar area that serves a lunch special for just under $20 all inclusive.  There is no menu, you get soup, sandwich and chips.  It's very high quality and definitely worth it.They also have a lunch menu with other choices.  I've tried their lamb burger which was also great.I believe to get inside if you do not work in the building is to go to the north side of the building / Liberty St. and take the elevator to 60.

We made a last minute decision to come to a pretty expensive restaurant. All in all, our experience was about what we expected: good food, good service, good steak - but not spectacular. It was nice that they had a toddler option of pasta, which our little one loved (for like two minutes at least). We ordered the Caesar salad, which was amazingly flavored and nice and crisp. The bone marrow with mushrooms was somewhat of a miss - the mushrooms and the sauce were amazing, but there was just so little of it and the bone marrow was too thick and lumpy, so it was very hard to spread on bread. The porterhouse for 2 is the steak we had and I thought it was nowhere close to the best steak in the city and it's certainly priced as if it was. There were bites that were overseasoned with too much salt and the big thing was the steak really lacked "sizzle". Sure it was hot, but it just didn't come out perfect. I just think there are many other places that are better in the city.

Title: A Must-Visit for Ramen Lovers

My husband and I finally visited the Japanese restaurant that my boss, an avid fan who frequents it thrice a week, had recommended. My husband, whose passion for ramen knows no bounds, was beyond thrilled with their curry ramen. He couldn't stop raving about the rich, multi-layered curry broth and the chashu that was so tender it simply melted in his mouth.

Although ramen isn't my cup of tea, I found solace in the non-ramen items like the cha-mayodo and menkoi set from their limited but appreciated selection of alternatives. The cha-mayodo didn't particularly strike a chord with me, but I must admit, the chashu in the menkoi set was delightful and matched my husband's enthusiasm.

We left with satisfied palates and the resolution to return. This spot is a gem for ramen aficionados and those who accompany them!

I came here for dinner on a Monday night with a friend.  I've been to the Queens location and enjoyed it.  However, the Queens location is in Whitestone so it's a bit far for me to get to.  I ordered the spicy lemongrass pho (small) with beef eye round and brisket.  The small was a good enough size for me and I don't think I could ever finish the large portion.  There was a lot of meat and noodles even in the small size.  There was a lot of fresh herbs and the soup was not too oily.  There was a good kick to it and there was a strong lemongrass flavor.  The service was very fast and attentive.  The only thing was that if you pay with credit card, it will be 4% more.  I would come back and try their other dishes, the curry looked good.  FYI - you get a free Vietnamese iced coffee or Thai iced tea with Yelp check-in.

Title: Mixed Experiences at Mont Blanc 52

My family and I visited Mont Blanc 52 for a birthday brunch and we left with a mixed bag of impressions. The meal kicked off with escargot and Swiss cheese fondue—while the former was overcooked, it still pleased the palate, but the fondue had a slightly overpowering white wine flavor for my taste. The raclette, however, was a standout, delivering a satisfying combination of ham, potatoes, and melted cheese.

Unfortunately, the kitchen had a few mishaps; the poached eggs arrived closer to hard-boiled, service was slow with our entrees arriving staggered, and my bratwurst was disappointingly cold inside. The French onion soup lacked depth and the weiner schnitzel was nondescript. On a brighter note, the chocolate fondue was tasty despite not being served warm.

While the entrees underwhelmed, the fondues and raclette showcased the restaurant's strengths. The ambiance was cozy, but the arrangement of raclette machine wires on our bench seating posed a potential safety risk.

Service was friendly, but the wait times indicated perhaps a struggle to accommodate our group of 12. The genuine kindness of the management team did compensate for some of the dining shortcomings. I advise future diners to stick to the Swiss specialties. I'm giving Mont Blanc 52 three stars for its homey feel and some memorable dishes amid the lapses.

Title: Late Night Delight at Half the Price

I always look forward to my post-9pm visits to this gem of a restaurant, where their 50% off sale is the perfect excuse to indulge in their mouth-watering array of dishes. Whether it's the savory premade bowls, fresh sushi, flavorful dumplings, or the fluffy baos, this place doesn’t skimp on taste or health.

The green tea cakes are a particular highlight for me – light, airy, and with just the right touch of sweetness. It’s worth noting that drinks, cakes, and certain items in the fridge don't fall under the half-price deal, so plan your treats accordingly!

The staff is adequate, though this might be attributed to our late dining habits. Regardless, the food is the star here, and it absolutely shines.

This place is solid. Great food, beautiful space, excellent service, and fair prices are a few reasons I will definitely be back. FAVORITES* Bone-In NY Strip ($31)- This 28 day dry aged steak was served with a side of watercress salad and salsa verde.* Lasagna al Forno ($23)- The tomato sauce used for this dish is amazing. * Calamari ($17)- Extra crispy without it being overly breaded or greasy. Perfectly seasoned as well. Generous portion.FYI* Corkage fee $25* Street parking available around the area.* Private Room in the basement available for large parties.*Outdoor seating available during warmer months.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Cozy Eatery

I recently dined at a restaurant that caught my eye with its reasonably priced menu and generous portions. The interior charmed me with cute wall art, adding to a cozy ambiance. As a vegetarian, I was initially excited by the array of options available.

However, my excitement quickly dwindled after tasting my meal. I chose peanut and teriyaki sauces for my dish, only to find the peanut sauce overwhelmingly strong, overshadowing the other flavors. Additionally, while there were many choices, crafting a satisfying vegetarian plate was challenging, as each vegetable added to the cost. This made it difficult to create a well-rounded meal without the price creeping up.

In the end, the combination I opted for didn't hit the mark. For fellow vegetarians contemplating a visit, I'd recommend inquiring about milder sauce options and accounting for the extra cost of a diverse veggie selection.

Title: A Slice of NYC Delight

My jaunt through NYC led me to a quaint pizzeria just a stone's throw from my hotel. The promise of authentic New York-style pizza was too tempting to resist. This small establishment immediately impressed with its clean interior and a commendable variety of veggie options that caught my eye.

Service was swift and efficient—no sooner had we entered than we were attended to. While the pricing felt premium at nearly $40 for four slices and two drinks, the culinary experience justified the expense; it is New York, after all, where top dollar for top flavor is the norm.

The pizza was nothing short of divine. Each slice boasted a crust that straddled the line between tender and crisp, robust enough to support a generous blanket of toppings yet still providing that satisfying crunch. A slight uptick in tomato sauce would have perfected the balance of tang and creaminess, but this was a minor quibble.

The portions were generous; a single slice was a meal in itself. The backdrop of the city's energetic pulse added to the ambiance, enhancing the dining experience. With an offering that extends beyond pizza to salads, various entrees, and tantalizing desserts, this pizzeria stands out.

I left already planning my next visit. For anyone craving a true taste of New York with a side of urban vibrancy, I heartily recommend this gem.

TabeTomo is a refreshing standout in the ramen scene. Distinct from the tightly bound traditions of other Japanese cuisines, ramen’s relatively recent invention and Chinese-influenced noodles invite chefs to get creative, and TabeTomo seizes this opportunity brilliantly. Shattering any preconceived notions set by instant ramen of our youth, TabeTomo offers a palate awakening experience with its 60-hour pork broth that imparts a richness to the dish that is simply unforgettable. Opting for the "dip-style" ramen, where noodles are served on the side, enhances the experience, allowing for control of the noodle texture as you savor the broth. Don't miss out on the fried chicken with tartar sauce – it’s a triumph in its own right. Coupled with great prices and service, TabeTomo isn't just having a moment—it's setting a new standard.

Title: Mixed Feelings at the Dry Pot Delight

I visited this restaurant on a fairly quiet Saturday noon and was surprised to be asked to wait upon arrival despite many empty tables. The brief delay was made longer by our waiter's diversion to photograph another table, which was frustrating as I was in a rush.

We ordered the recommended dry pot for two, selecting nine ingredients – a perfect amount as it turned out. The chicken feet appetizer, advertised as boneless, unfortunately still contained joints and lacked flavor, making the $9 price tag seem steep.

The rice at $2 each was a disappointment - small portions, served lukewarm, and far too tough, especially the overly cooled top layer. The utensils were visually appealing, though using a chipped spatula and a cracked bowl did little to enhance our experience. The clear chopsticks were aesthetically pleasing but functionally cumbersome, constantly rolling off the plate.

The restaurant's napkins, stamped with their logo, raised a concern regarding the safety of the ink used, which could potentially bleed when wet.

As for the dry pot, it was my first experience with this dish, and the spiciness was manageable and pleasant, unlike the anticipated mala-style numbness. Instead, it delivered a slight lip plumping and mild mucus generation but reminded me more of Malaysian curry than anything.

The ingredients were hit-or-miss. The eye of round beef was lackluster, the tripe inconsistently chopped, and the pork belly forgettable. The chicken thigh, however, was quite satisfying. Other ingredients like fish cake and enoki mushrooms were not cut for easy eating, and the boy choy was disproportionately large. The confusion between tofu skin and bean curd sheet was an unnecessary complication.

The tipping system, starting at 18%, felt pushy for a midtown spot, and a 15% option would have been appreciated.

Our total bill came to $66 – a bit overpriced considering the meal and ambiance. Subtracting the underwhelming chicken feet, it was still $27 per person. While the portions were reasonable, there are certainly better-valued options out there where one could leave feeling full, unlike me.

In summary, while the dry pot was enjoyable, the overall experience was marred by minor nuisances and a sense of overpricing. It's unlikely I'll rush back.

**Restaurant Review: A Symphony of Flavors**

Last evening, I had the pleasure of dining at this gem of a restaurant with a couple of friends. From the moment we were seated, courtesy of a reservation made by one of my companions, the experience was delightful. The waitress proved to be a wellspring of information, guiding us through the menu with patience and expertise.

What truly sets this establishment apart is its ever-changing palette; the daily menu rotation ensures that each visit is a unique culinary adventure, offering an array of dishes that tantalize the taste buds with an exquisite blend of flavors. Overall, the dining experience was comfortably nestled between an 8.5 and 9.0 out of 10.

While we did miss out on the much-anticipated rotisserie duck - note to self and others: reserve this dish in advance - there was no shortage of gastronomic marvels. The standout for me was the sizzling Grilled Flatiron, a dish of such finesse that it rightfully earned a full 10/10 rating in my book. Paired with shaoxing cream sauce and enoki mushrooms, the beef was a tender triumph.

The journey began with Maine Uni over rice, an elegant introduction to the world of fine dining and a dish that dances with a spectrum of flavors. Following that, the Shellfish & Sambal made a spicy statement with its robust coconut-infused sambal, though the shrimp did not quite hit the mark for me when compared to similar curry dishes from more modest establishments.

Capping off the meal was the coconut pie, a dessert that upended any preconceived notions with its dark, decadent appearance and a masterful balance of sweet and savory. It was, without hyperbole, the best coconut pie I've had to date.

In summary, this restaurant is a culinary chameleon, offering a delightful array of dishes that are sure to please the palate. The occasional need for pre-reservation on select items is a small concession for the overall quality and adventure provided by this splendid dining experience.

Top Thai in Greenwich is now my go to Thai restaurant in the West Village. This place is tiny so thank god that there was 50% occupancy policy put in place at that time!We started our dinner with Thai draft beer that went well with fried calamari and Thai fried chicken. We shared Tom Yum shrimp soup and we found it really savory and spicy but the star of the night is the crispy deep fried whole red snapper with spicy basil sauce, it was flavorful and crispy. Note, you can choose from five different sauces for your snapper. From presentation to flavor and its size, we found it more than enough for two people. It came with a top-rated Thai fried rice but in my opinion a jasmine rice is probably just as good as well.The service and the staff are commendable, the entire place is clean which was appreciated, especially with our current situation. We will definitely come back here whenever I crave for that snapper dish!

Title: A Sweet Gem with Room for Improvement - Paris Baguette

I frequently find myself returning to Paris Baguette, a beloved spot from my days living nearby. As a fan familiar with their origins in Korea, I've sampled an array of their breads. My personal favorites are the raspberry croissant, the creamy pudding, the strawberry cake, and the custard bread. However, be warned: the sought-after raspberry croissant is often sold out by evening.

On a recent visit to the area, I popped in for coffee and bread while waiting for a table at Wonjo restaurant. It's imperative to try their strawberry cake - a delight even for those who shy away from sweets. Unlike the typically overly sweet American cake, this one strikes the perfect balance. If you don't see slices available, just ask; they’ve been accommodating in my experience.

Their blackberry jam is another must-try, especially slathered over toast. Sadly, not all aspects shine; service can be hit or miss, including a past altercation with a staff member. Cleanliness also falls short, often necessitating self-service table cleaning.

While the breads are exceptional, the service and cleanliness could certainly be improved to match the high standard set by their bakery offerings. Despite these drawbacks, its convenient location keeps me, and likely many others, coming back for more.

I recently visited a local Mexican eatery and was profoundly disappointed with the experience. The guacamole, served unorthodoxly in a coffee cup, was a watery disappointment devoid of any hearty tomato presence or textural variance from onions or other typical ingredients. It lacked seasoning to such an extent that I left it unfinished.

Moving onto the tacos, they were so overwhelmed by grease that it detracted from any potential flavor. The carnitas within were not only bland but also possessed an unpalatable, rubbery texture. The chorizo was a culinary misstep; it appeared as nothing more than cubed, generic supermarket sausage links, completely missing the mark on authentic spices.

The sole redeeming aspect of the meal was the horchata, which was actually well-prepared and enjoyable. However, that alone is not enough to warrant a return visit or to save this establishment from a poor review based on the dismal main courses.

My visit to this bustling tapas spot on Labor Day weekend proved to be a delightful culinary adventure. Despite it being a busy Sunday, the wait was manageable at 40 minutes, with the convenience of a text alert system. Fortunately, we snagged seats in front of the kitchen, where we enjoyed the live culinary show without the worry of leaving with clothes smelling of food.

Kicking off with a refreshing and well-prepared red sangria that set a perfect summer tone, we delved into an array of scrumptious tapas. The Spanish tortilla genuinely tasted homemade and was a standout, while the croquetas boasted an ideal creamy interior encased in a crispy shell. The cheese and charcuterie plate was a finely balanced array of flavors, especially the paper-thin jamón and luscious goat cheese accompanied by pan con tomate. As sides, the corn stood out, and although I didn't try the shrimp, my husband's swift consumption was testament enough to their quality.

The grand finale was churros filled with a generous amount of dulce de leche, an absolute must-have that avoided being excessively oily. Paired with the hot chocolate laced with just the right hint of brandy, it was the perfect end to a meal that was as much about the experience as it was about the food.

The service was impeccable, with a server who ensured we were never rushed and could savor every moment. For a taste of Spain that truly satisfies, this restaurant is a destination worth marking on your culinary map.

Title: Upscale Noodles with a Side of Wait Time

If you’re on the hunt for freshly made soba and udon in New York, this restaurant is a robust choice, though be prepared for both a wait and a hit to your wallet. The ambiance and service are commendable, hitting a solid 4.5/5 on my scale, providing a pleasing backdrop and attentive care throughout the meal.

The menu, while somewhat high-end in pricing, does feature a delectable highlight in the form of their squid stuffed with sticky rice ($11.50) – a dish that, despite its challenging consumption, dazzles with its rich sauce and flavor. However, while the in-house made wakame hot udon ($15) delivers on quality, it doesn't quite justify its price tag due to its simplicity.

Similarly, the enoki mushroom cold soba ($15.25) is pleasing to the palate but might leave you desiring more for what you pay, especially if you opt for more elaborate toppings – expect to spend upwards of $20-$30 for a more substantial experience.

Even though I lucked out with no wait at 7:30 on a Saturday, others weren’t as fortunate. Considering the plethora of excellent soba/udon offerings in the city, this spot may not be my go-to due to the steep prices. But if you catch it during a lull, it's certainly worth a try.

Overall Rating: 4/5
Value: 4/5
Food: 4/5
Service: 4.5/5
Decor: 4.5/5

Title: A Shanghai Surprise in the Heart of Chinatown

Review:
I was pleasantly surprised by our dining experience at this bustling Chinatown eatery on a busy Saturday evening. Despite the chaos of the packed restaurant, we were seated within a reasonable ten minutes. Our meal was a delightful journey through authentic Shanghainese flavors, a surprise given the Cantonese background of the chefs.

The standout dishes were numerous: The Xiaolongbao was generously portioned, each dumpling a succulent treasure trove of flavor. The Shenjianbao won me over with its crispy bottom and tender meat filling, making it the star bao of the night. The beef with green onions was aromatic and well-seasoned, with portions that left us more than satisfied. The stir-fry bok choy with tofu skins was an unexpected favorite, bursting with umami goodness, while the shrimp stir-fry, accompanied by asparagus and those mysterious yet delightful yellow nuts, was a dish I'd vehemently recommend.

Though the chili wontons were merely okay, with a tad thick skin and a sauce needing a touch more peanut and chili oil, this was a minor note in an otherwise harmonious meal. 

For an exuberant, authentic, and affordable Shanghainese fare, this restaurant is a hit. The ambiance is quintessential Chinatown—loud and lively, which only adds to the genuine experience. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Title: A Cozy Hideaway Amidst Winter's Chill

Tucked away near the bustling rink and the twinkling lights of the Bryant Park Christmas Tree lies the Lodge—a sanctuary for those braving the biting cold. Stepping inside, prepare for the lively din that embodies the spirit of the season, though it might take a moment for your ears to acclimate.

My quest for warmth led me to Ovenly, one of the surrounding stalls, where the promise of hot chocolate beckoned. At $4.75 before tax, it's a small price for a cup of genuine comfort, meticulously crafted with real melted chocolate, not mere powder.

The result is a velvety indulgence, a companion as you lose yourself in the joy of skaters and the charm of holiday stalls. If you find yourself here, let this hot chocolate be the highlight of your wintertide wanderlust.

Returning to NYC meant a beeline for Totto Ramen, and their Spicy Nibo Paitan did not disappoint. Its broth takes the already delectable Chicken Paitan to new heights with a fish-flavored sesame oil twist. The spices are masterfully blended, yielding a rich and creamy soup that's a feast for the taste buds. Topping it off with a seasoned boiled egg only intensified the ramen's flavor profile, making each slurp more satisfying than the last. A must-visit for any ramen enthusiast.

I recently visited a local eatery that offers both take-out and dine-in options, with the added bonus of outdoor seating on pleasant days. My lunch experience kicked off with a white wine sangria that was quite enjoyable. To start, I ordered guacamole served with chips and salsa. However, the service was a bit off; the chips were prematurely cleared, leaving us unable to finish our dips.

The main course featured steak tacos with grilled skirt steak and cherry tomato pico de gallo, topped with salsa taquera. The filling was delicious; however, the corn tortilla didn't meet my expectations, prompting me to forgo the taco shell and savor just the flavorful interior. Despite the odd service hiccup, the savory steak ensured a satisfying meal.

Title: A Soho Gem for Sustainable, Wholesome Dining

I recently had a revelation about the impact of my eating habits when a craving for something wholesome hit me hard last Friday night. My tired, nutrient-starved self found solace in a charming vegetarian spot in Soho that takes sustainability seriously. I indulged in their "Over the Rainbow" bowl—a hearty, yet guilt-free, concoction that was a bit more than I bargained for, but too delectable not to finish. The standout was the jalapeño tahini sauce; it added a kick that perfectly complemented the lentil falafel and tied the whole dish together. While I skipped dessert, the pie selection seemed promising for a future visit.

The self-service format added a casual touch, with attentive staff ensuring the food arrived promptly after ordering. This restaurant's dedication to sustainability resonates with me deeply, particularly in our current climate of environmental awareness. Food that feels good and does good? It's a clear favorite, and I'm eager to return to what's now a top dining destination on my NYC list.

I recently visited this restaurant and decided on a margarita pizza topped with pepperoni, which did not disappoint – it was quite flavorful. Unfortunately, there was a mix-up with my pasta order; I received penne alla vodka instead of the penne arabbaita I had requested. The pasta was mediocre, but the error was irritating. Despite that, the quality of the pizza would bring me back. Service was efficient, allowing me to be in and out in roughly 20 minutes, which is notable for a Friday night when it wasn't overly busy. Overall, I'd recommend the restaurant for their pizza.

Title: Stellar Flavors Dampened by Service Missteps

My recent dining experience at [Restaurant Name] was a culinary rollercoaster of highs and lows. The food undeniably deserves applause, with the popcorn chicken stealing the show—a delectable mix of saucy, spicy, peanutty, and cheesy, all while maintaining the perfect crunch. The "Matcha Made in Heaven" cocktail was powerfully robust in flavor, though a bit too intense for my palate, making the house red wine a pleasantly light and fruity reprieve.

However, the service was where the stars began to fall. As someone with a carrot allergy, my experience was fraught with anxiety and frustration. Despite clear communication about my dietary restriction, my bibimbap arrived not once but multiple times with carrots, even after staff assured me they were serving radishes. My dish was finally presented devoid of all ingredients save for meat and rice, a bland shadow of what it should have been, long after my friends had finished their meals.

The takeaway is as clear as it is urgent: the staff must prioritize allergy awareness and kitchen communication. If accommodations cannot be met with absolute certainty, it would be more prudent to inform guests with allergies upfront rather than risk their health. This disconnect between the kitchen's capabilities and the serving staff's assurances can turn what should be a delightful dining out into a severe inconvenience, or worse, a health hazard.

Came across this place , people have been raving about . Decided to give it a shot on Fathers Day !! My Dad is a fan of Indian food and good drinks . BabuJi menu seemed pretty interesting. We made reservations for 7pm. As we walked in , we were greeted and table was ready. We took a flight of stairs up to the main restaurant. It was quite packed but the noice level was moderate. The ambiance of the place reminds you of India and the old times, they even had a classic movie playing on the Projector. In one shot we reviewed the menu and ordered drinks to dessert. Drinks and Appetizers came out first . Drinks were really good. Appetizers were really good as well , just the portion size was a bit small. Between 3 people we shared 3 apps. On to the main-course, it came perfectly after 15 mins of us finishing the Appetizers. We had orders 3 entree with a Naan Basket . It worked out perfect for us three. Lastly we ended it with the Chai Kulfi on a stick. That' really topped everything, IT WAS REALLY GOOD!!Ambiance- 10/10Service -10/10(Henry was amazing)WIFI- Not Sure Happy Hour - Not Sure Brunch - Weekends Halal- Not Sure Parking - Good Luck

Title: A Miss at the Market: Chicken Tacos and Chips Experience

I recently indulged in a meal of chicken tacos and chips with salsa, expecting the rave reviews to hold true. Unfortunately, it seems I hold an unpopular opinion: it was underwhelming. The tacos were passable but didn't wow me. The chips seemed stale, lacking that crave-worthy fresh crunch, and the salsa was overwhelmingly garlicky, a flavor that overstayed its welcome well into the next day. A lack of heat left my spice-loving palate yearning for hot sauce, which was nowhere to be found.

The practicalities of dining also dampened the experience. The absence of seating forced a less-than-comfortable meal standing in a hallway, while payment options were limited—no American Express meant dipping into personal funds on a work trip. It was a disappointing use of a dinner opportunity at the Market.

I am very very confused as to how Set has 4 stars..... This may be the only time an overall Yelp rating has tricked me into trying out a restaurant..... The only reasons for my 2-star rating was the quick & friendly service, and affordable prices. The food and drinks are subpar, period. I went to Set with a few girlfriends for drinks & dinner after work on a Friday. We ordered the Set Loaded Tots & Tempura Shrimp poppers to share. The tots had wayyyy too many toppings & flavors going on (just didn't work well - sometimes less is more) and the shrimp was definitely straight out of the bag (comparable to the precooked frozen baby shrimps I buy from my local grocery store) topped with some sort of spicy mayo sauce; nothing special. We also each ordered one of their "Sets" as our meals. Each Set comes with one slider, one skewer, and waffle fries. Honestly, this wasn't anything to write home about either. My slider (beef) was extremely chewy, although my pork belly skewer was tasty. All in all, the place is a bit divey and the food is nothing to write home about. I don't think I will give a second try.

Settled in the heart of culinary innovation, this Danny Meyer gem offers a spacious and inviting atmosphere perfect for indulging in exquisitely crafted tapas. Pro tip: it's a hotspot during weekends, so securing a reservation is a wise move.

Fresh from absorbing culture at The Whitney, our 3 pm brunch experience was buzzing with energy. Opting for bar seating proved a delight, allowing us to marvel at chefs masterfully at work in the open kitchen.

The menu was a parade of hits: the roasted cauliflower with toasted almonds and apple was a textural masterpiece, while the salmon poke was impeccably fresh, boasting a delicate sesame charm. The duck with wild rice and shiitake was deceptively satisfying in its portion, and the grand finale—a cloud-light carrot cake, crowned with granola—left us craving more.

Accompanied by stellar service in a non-tipping establishment, this dining experience left an indelible mark. It's an unequivocal must-try for any Whitney visitor.

I recently visited a new dining spot that has taken up residence in what was once a Turkish restaurant. Despite its small size, the cozy ambiance was welcoming. Upon arrival, I was seated without delay and was promptly served a pitcher of refreshingly icy cold water.

While perusing the menu, I opted for the drunken noodle dish with shrimp – a choice I didn't regret. The dish was served swiftly and boasted the perfect amount of spice that I had hoped for. The waitstaff deserves a special mention for their attentiveness and willingness to accommodate.

Although I was informed that the restaurant is temporarily closed, my experience was positive, and I would certainly recommend it for anyone in search of a good meal with a spicy edge once it reopens.

I've really had my fill of Mediterranean food over the past couple of weeks, let alone my entire life. In terms of takeout/casual dine-in options, Omar's kind of blew me away. For such a reasonable price, you get a dope lunch deal, which includes an entree plus two sides. They also throw in a small greens salad, hummus, pita, and baklava on the house. I got the chicken kabob, which was a good six ounces, based on my eyeballing skills. It was so delicious, especially with their amazing garlic sauce. Also got the cucumber yogurt salad and the eggplant sides - killed both in a heartbeat. So good! Even if you don't like eggplant, you're going to love this remix. The place is cute, casual, and clean. Service was great. Waiter was friendly and fast. Host was friendly and attentive. Really impressed with this midtown spot.

I tried delivery from this restaurant for the first time and my experience was very positive. The 3 roll special, which includes a soup or salad, was a steal at under $20 with delivery and tip. Among the salmon avocado, shrimp avocado, and spicy tuna rolls, the latter stood out for its freshness—a rarity in spicy tuna offerings. I'm already planning my next order, whether it's for delivery or takeout. Highly recommended for sushi lovers!

Title: A Delectable Feast for Vegans and Omnivores Alike!

Review:

I would gladly return to this gem of a restaurant! The culinary experience was extraordinary, with my companion and I savoring four perfectly portioned dishes that were a burst of flavors. Despite initial concerns that we may have over-ordered, the quantity was spot-on. Impressively, the vegan offerings won over my typically selective, non-vegan mother, much to my amazement.

The service shone with warmth and attentiveness, enhancing the already charming and cozy atmosphere of the establishment. The standout for me had to be the night's special, a turmeric pasta stuffed with a vegan "ricotta" that was nothing short of divine. We concluded our meal with a sublime strawberry cheesecake that left us both in a state of dessert-induced bliss. Highly recommend!

This great date spot to grab pizza is a favorite.If you are looking for a date spot look no further delicious apps, entrees, and bottles of wine located near a bunch of bars in the east village.I have gone here a few times and the staff has always been very nice and the food has been really good.Rice Balls - were very good and super flavorful but were a little expensive for the quantityGnocchi with Zucchini in a blush sauce - the sauce here is great and the blush sauce with the gnocchi and zucchini is a perfect match Tri-Pie -  Tomato Sauce , Vodka Sauce, Pesto Sauce with fresh mozzz all on one pie! Wow! This combo on Joe and pats thin pizza with a great crunch is the way to goPizza - you gotta get the cheese pie when you go to a new spot and they did not disappoint their sauce is unlike anything I have had and is a great go toIn short:- Great Date Spot- Great Pizza

Not much to eat around this area and I was happy to see this new addition to the neighborhood. It has a nice clean feel to it and although it is a small place there is usually open tables. It wasn't overally busy for lunch which is troubling considering it is new and there is a lot of foot traffic outside. For lunch I ordered the beet trio salad. It is light and delicious but also a small portion so I left a little hungry honestly. If you dont order it with protein it may not be enough for lunch. My partner ordered the quinoa salad with salmon and enjoyed it too. It is a little on the pricier side than other restaurants in the neighborhood but that doesn't take away from the fact you get good quality food here.  Service is pretty good too and they have wifi which is always a positive. They also have a dinner menu that has entrees in the $30 range which seems high. Anyway, come check it out and make your own judgement!  Good luck Terravita!

Title: A Satisfying Post-Jury Duty Bite

I recently visited this restaurant for a post-jury duty lunch with some new acquaintances, and the experience was unexpectedly delightful. Arriving around 1 pm, we found the place quiet but it wasn't long before the lunch crowd filled the seats, creating a lively atmosphere.

The lunch menu seemed to have been updated recently, as it didn't match the one pictured on Yelp. However, it boasted a variety of dishes, including a couple of vegetarian options. Despite not recalling the exact name of my dish, I remember it being scrumptious, especially since the kitchen staff accommodated my request for extra spice.

In terms of payment, the restaurant is pretty flexible, accepting both cash and Venmo. One thing to note, though, is that they prefer a single Venmo payment per table, which might be a slight inconvenience if you're used to paying separately. Nevertheless, the great food outweighed this minor hiccup in an overall pleasant dining experience.

After all the buzz surrounding Xi'an Famous, my curiosity finally led me to their Chinatown spot. My taste buds were treated to three dishes, starting with the much-acclaimed spicy cumin lamb noodles. They lived up to my expectations, delivering a punch of cumin-infused lamb with veggies drenched in a zesty chili sauce, perfectly complementing the thick and chewy noodles.

Moving on, the Mt. Qi pork noodles presented a lively dance of spicy and sour on my palate, though the sour notes slightly overpowered the harmony for my liking. However, the flavors were robust and kept me engaged.

The final act was their stewed oxtail noodles, which showcased a rich and savory meat, albeit with a tad bit of effort required to liberate it from the bones. My only wish was for a more generous helping of sauce to elevate the somewhat subdued noodles.

In brief, the cumin lamb noodles were a hit, the Mt. Qi pork was boldly flavored but overly tangy, and the stewed oxtail was delicious but needed more saucy accompaniment.

Title: Charming Spot Marred by Service Issues

As a frequenter of this neighborhood gem, I'm continually charmed by its vibrant atmosphere and delightful offerings. Both the veggie tempura and fish tacos hit the spot every time, and the totchos are nothing short of a crowd-pleaser. Their happy hour is a go-to for me and my colleagues, thanks to the unbeatable deals on both drinks and eats.

However, the service experience consistently falls short. Despite being a regular, I've encountered persistent issues with waitstaff who seem indifferent at best. The lack of attentiveness when ordering or seeking a second round dampens the overall dining experience. It's frustrating when seemingly unnoticed by the staff, and a task as simple as obtaining the check becomes a challenge.

In all honesty, this place has all the makings of a local favorite. Still, there's a pressing need for management to address the service shortcomings. Here's to hoping for improvements that match the quality of their cuisine and the allure of their establishment.

This is a great date spot for ramen.  I had the Ichiraku which is unique because it is a chicken broth.  The broth was appropriately salted and tasted like it had a slight miso flavor mixed in.  The noodles were straight which I'm not as used to at a ramen spot but that did not stop me from finishing the entire bowl.  The waiters were very prompt and the food was delivered quickly.  We came around 2pm on a Sunday and only waited about 15 minutes for a table.  The bathrooms were really clean and nice.  I would definitely return to try more of their menu.

Unfortunately, my recent visit to this Italian fast-food chain on 9th Ave. was disappointing. The dishes lacked the robust flavors and proper textures one expects from Italian cuisine, which may stem from the absence of Italian hands in the kitchen. Considering the gastronomic letdown and the journey to get there, I'd advise skipping this place. For those craving genuine Italian fare, nearby eateries such as Manganaro's, Tavola, and Sergimmo Salumeria are far superior choices worth your appetite and time.

I was invited to try their restaurant  as a yelp event and at a convenient location since I live an avenue away. I really love this place because the ingredients are fresh and it's a different take on veggie/meat bowls.  I ordered the braised beef with vegetables. The dish came in with a hefty portion of meat and veggies. For the price point, it's a deal. My meal came with a side and I ordered the crab pockets, which the filling came in steaming hot, so let it cool off before getting a bite. I paired my meal with half tea and half dragon lemonade. I'm glad I split the drink as an Arnold Palmer because the drink was too sweet. I spoke to the staff and they are going to have soup bowls for the winter, which I'm excited for. I'm so happy for this new addition of affordable casual dining in this area. I will definitely try the soups once they are included in the menu. Thank you for the opportunity to dine here!

YIKES! Not worth the money at all. We made reservations and yet we were taken to the dumpy side of the joint. Our waitress was friendly but I didn't appreciate her flashing her pink undies while squatting down to take our orders.Food was boring, the best thing were the fries. Nachos were gooey and not even sure it had cheese. The fried macaroni may have been good if it would have been served warm. Drinks were drab and lacked alcohol. Group tried margaritas and mojitos.The music was good and a few folks danced.The view, horrible because you need to stand and your looking out dirty plexi-glass dividers.Ick!

Title: Pricey for What You Get, But Noodles Impress

I recently dined at Ippudo and found myself torn about the experience. On one hand, the thin noodles were exceptional – perfectly cooked and a highlight of the meal. The shin tan-tan men, touted as "extremely spicy," fell short on the heat scale but delivered on flavor with a thick, though somewhat overly dense, broth.

Sharing pork buns and fried chicken as appetizers with friends, our per person cost hit $47, which felt steep for a "quick ramen meal." The pork buns, while flavorful, were overwhelmed by sauce, resulting in a soggy experience. The chicken was unmemorable, fading into the background of our meal.

Though Ippudo has been hyped up, it didn't quite meet my expectations, especially when compared to my favorite, Ichiran. While Ippudo offers a solid bowl of ramen, the value proposition is lacking. Worth a visit for noodle aficionados, but my heart – and wallet – will stick with Ichiran.

Rating: ★★★★☆

Great location and fun to get brunch on the weekends when the weather is nice. We sat outside and had the best time. Getting a table can be a wait, but it goes fast and the service is good. The guacamole was yummy and I got veggie enchiladas which were pretty awesome. @traveleen_gurl

After reading some of the reviews I promptly hopped on Opentable and snagged a last minute reservation. This little strip of 4th ave has some really excellent restaurants. Pylos was my first endeavor in elevated greek food and based on my experience here it definitely won't be my last. I struggled to choose between the Saganaki Tou Merakli  and Haloumi. The description for the saganaki won me over. How can you say no to three greek cheeses melted in a clay pot? So simple, tangy, and rich. Definitely save the fresh pita served on the house to pair with this. Although the complimentary hummus is great as well. We split the moussaka and baby lamb chops as mains which was the go to move because man, moussaka is filling. The star of the show was by far the lamb chops. The chops were so tender and meaty without that gamey after taste. While the moussaka is a comforting, filling dish, it felt like something we could make at home.For dessert, you can't go wrong with the galaktoboureko. It's crunchy, flaky, creamy, and topped with Greek mountain honey. SO good!This review is way overdue since we visited back in February. One main downside is being seated in the front during the winter. The front of the house kept swinging open the curtain which let in bitter NYC air. Aside from that, I highly recommend Pylos if you're looking for a cute new spot in the East Village.

I really liked the decor and feel of this establishment. For lunch it was also not too packed which I alsoI liked. That said, I overall liked everything  about this place but the drinks ; I would just ordered classic drinks bc all their specialty drinks were too sweet .It was special to have experienced , a few first times here;  this was my first time having avocado fries which were so much better than I imagined, waygu meat, and it was first time had sushi with doritos on it!! The best sushi I have ever had; who would  have ever figured that it would taste so mind blowingly delicious ( Rock and Roll Specialty Roll; It's genius )

Lombardi's is a must-visit for anyone seeking the quintessential New York pizza experience. As America's oldest pizzeria, it offers more than just a slice of history; stepping inside transports you to the heart of New York's rich culinary tapestry. The pizza here doesn't just live up to the hype—it sets the standard with its delectable flavors and perfect crust. However, skip the breadsticks; they lack the expected garlic punch, and even our server recommended against them. Be sure to bring cash, as cards aren't accepted, though there is an ATM available, and prepare to savor your entire pizza without the lure of free drink refills. Minor inconveniences aside, Lombardi's earns its place on any top 20 NYC must-visit list.

I recently visited this restaurant for a birthday dinner with a party of four and was thoroughly impressed by the experience. The staff was exceptionally accommodating with our seating preferences, ensuring we were comfortably situated in a cozy room with just a few other tables, which added to the intimate ambiance.

We opted for the prime/marinated package at $110 and a large soy bean stew for $16, which proved to be the perfect amount of food for our group. The cooking was expertly handled by our server, who skillfully managed to meet our diverse cooking preferences, including well-done meat for two of our party.

The meat quality was outstanding and the side dishes were a delightful complement to the main course. I'm already looking forward to returning to try more of their packages. 

Service was a high point; it was both friendly and prompt. The staff's attentiveness made our dining experience smooth and enjoyable. A minor detail to note for those celebrating with dessert: they have a cake policy of $2 per person.

All in all, this restaurant offers great food, excellent service, and a wonderful atmosphere. Highly recommended and definitely worth a return visit!

There's a reason why this spot is always packed! The tacos are as authentic as they get. Tacos come with meat, corn or flour tortilla, cilantro, onion, salsa, and guacamole!The meat is well cooked and the tortillas are freshly made. I had the grilled chicken and the steaks and both were so good but the chicken was better. Their aguas frescas (except for the jamaica) are super good and tasty. The sauce that comes on the tacos is super good and they have more on the sides. It's hard to find a spot to eat but it's still worth it. I would definitely recommend it to anyone :)

This place caught our attention when we found it on open table. Listed as an Irish American restaurant, we have it a try since we had an actual person from Ireland with us. The restaurant itself is visually intriguing. Part of the bar came from an actual castle in England and the place has the feel of an old English pub. Paintings and mirrors hung high to the ceiling and the ceiling itself is done with plaster details. The menu features Shepard's pie but that's about it as far as "Irish" fare. The remaining menu featured salads, sandwiches, chicken and steak options. We tried the Shepard's pie, chicken pot pie, chicken empanadas, and a chicken sandwich. The empanadas were tasty. The Shepard's pie looked promising but made was with ground steak instead of the traditional lamb. It was good but nothing we'd go back to order again. 1/2 of the chicken sandwich was very good but the other 1/2 was missing condiments and the chicken was dry. On the recommendation of one of our tour guides we tried the cheesecake which was supposed to be the best in New York City. We respectfully disagree. We found it to be flavorless and grainy as if the ingredients hadn't been blended well. The crème brûlée on the other hand was outstanding! All in all, our party agreed we would not return which is a pity given the ambience and history of the restaurant.

My friend and I tried to eat here twice and we were successful after the second attempt! Friday nights seem to be a lot busier than Saturday night at this place. The restaurant was small but cozy, decorated with cute ornaments; it looked like the perfect date spot. Indeed, there were a number of couples sharing pasta and other Italian delights. We each got the famous pasta in the cheese wheel and split the meatballs. The food came out promptly after our order. Not a big fan of Italian food, I was pleasantly surprised at how good the meatballs were. They were flavorful and perfectly cooked, pairing well with the tomato sauce. The pasta was well cooked, al dente, and not too cheesy. Its saltiness cut by black pepper kept me going back for more. Overall, I really enjoyed the pasta.One downside would be the price. Although the place is a $$ on Yelp, each pasta was $20, which I found a little too over board.

Title: A Melting Pot of Flavors That Delights

My recent dining experience at this impressive new establishment proved to be a pleasant surprise. At first glance, the eclectic menu, boasting everything from oysters and crudo to pastas, short ribs, and bibimbap, was admittedly intimidating. Yet, the execution of each dish alleviated any concerns.

The standouts for me were the truffle squid ink gnocchi and the slow braised beef short ribs - both dishes were sublime in their flavors and presentation. While the desserts provided a comforting end to the meal, it was clear that savory dishes are the restaurant's forte. This is a spot that fearlessly brings diverse tastes to the table and excels at it.

The decor of Manting is simple, bright and clean. It's a great place for a quick fix meal. Their service was not the best but attentive and friendly. They served a great variety of ingredients for spicy dried pot with affordable price. Their food was cooked decently but looked not fresh at the counter. The portion wasn't bad and came with complimentary rice. If we are eager for spicy dried pot we will visit again.

The obvious hype of Lazzara's comes from El Presidente giving this a 9.3 rating. The main problem with our experience was the service. The pizza took about 25-30 minutes. The waiters are leaning over to hand you the food and drinks. It's very rushed and sort of small on the inside. We ordered one regular and one pepperoni. The pepperoni was very oily, so the regular pie was way better. All in all, good pizza (not the best), just a bad dining experience.

Title: Cozy Ambiance Meets Mixed Dining Experience at Local Eatery

My inaugural visit to this charming restaurant was met with an immediate sense of warmth, thanks to its wooden interiors and enchanting Christmas lights. The spacious setup was perfect for a comfortable dinner in a booth with my boyfriend, providing ample space for diners.

Unfortunately, the service did not match the inviting atmosphere. Despite being attended to by a waiter, the lack of enthusiasm and personal touch was a letdown, with not even a smile to be seen.

The food, however, arrived with impressive speed. My Ribeye ($30), accompanied by mixed veggies and a scrumptious loaded baked potato, started wonderfully with tender, medium-rare bites. As the meal progressed, the steak's uneven cooking led to a disappointing dry and tough finish. My boyfriend's Melbourne Porterhouse ($33), paired with broccoli and fries, outshone my dish with its consistent cook and juiciness.

In spite of the ribeye's shortcomings, the experience was overall enjoyable, leaving us happily sated.

Tucked away on the 3rd floor of the Shops at Columbus Circle, this gem of a restaurant offers both a feast for the palate and the eyes. With its pristine cleanliness and ample space, the establishment provides a serene dining experience, accentuated by the charming view of Columbus Circle and a slice of Central Park seen from the comforting window seats.

My visits allowed me to sample the core of their menu and the delights of their afternoon tea. The Fish and Chips, while satisfactory, left something to be desired in terms of the fish's tenderness. However, the afternoon tea was where the restaurant truly shone. Opting for the Pink Tea option, the beautifully presented tower and individual teapots felt like a personal indulgence.

The tower's arrangement encouraged a journey from savory to sweet, starting with an array of sandwiches, including the standout Smoked Salmon and Truffle Egg & Spinach. The scones, both plain and fruit, were a highlight, perfectly paired with Strawberry Jam and Hudson Valley Clotted Cream. The sweets, with Grapefruit Tarts and Hibiscus Rose Macarons, provided a delightful finish.

With three tea options ranging from $50 to $70, there's something for everyone, whether you're in the mood for a gin cocktail or a splash of champagne. Service was impeccable throughout, attentive without being intrusive, and the monthly menu changes promise a fresh experience on each visit.

Happy to eat once again in Pastis after all these years...Atmosphere of the spot is (kind of) preserved, food is better than it used to be, however both service and price disappointed... maybe the 2019 meatpacking effect.Glad I checked it out, but not sure you'll see me again on Gansevoort street unless I really need my Escargots, Boudin blanc and bread. Or maybe I am just too old?

My friends ate at this chain in Japan and raved about it when she came home.There seems to be a never ending line at the door. Well worth the wait though so just suck it up. The concept is very different but not difficult, especially when the staff up front walls you through what to do. Our party of 4 was fortunate enough to get seats together even tho we were in separate stalls. Thought it would be awkward but no, it works!
