Especially cause I can enjoy slurping in a private setting. Now let's talk about the food! I ordered extra meat and a side is seaweed and mushrooms. There's a soft boiled sated egg that's given to you whole. You have to crack and peel it yourself. Lucky for us, they include a little sheet with instructions on the best method for peeling the egg. Open it up and you'll find a perfectly cooked soft boiled egg with a creamy, slightly runny yolk. It paired so well with the ramen! The noodles in the dish are very thin and cooked to perfection. The broth? Omg its all about the broth! So much flavor in every spoonful. It's a very clean pork flavor and super rich. Usually when I eat noodle soups,  hungry shortly afterwards but after this bowl, I was stuffed the rest of the night.  I absolutely love noodle soups of all kinds but have never been a fan of Japanese ramen. I just realized now it's because I wasn't eating the right one. Thank you thank you thank you Ichiran for opening my eyes to my new love of Japanese ramen!

We went for dim sum and was happy to find this place in NYC and not have to go to Flushing. They still do the dim sum carts which for me brings back a ton of memories of being a little girl. Every thing we had was amazing and the service was fantastic. They had food to us in no time and constantly checked on us.

Michelin star Chinese / fusion places are always scary. It's always a hit or miss for me. I decided to give Tuome a try because their pig out dish looked amazing from pictures.I came for their first seating on a Friday night. It was pretty empty when we arrived ,but the whole restaurant started to fill up after we got seated. I recommend making a resy.Our server recommended that we order two started, two mains, and a side for 2 people. Foodz:Fluke tartar - [tartare, yuzu coconut, cucumber] - we loved this dish, it comes with a viet rice cracker thing that went perfect with the fluke, the yuzu gave it the right about of acidity for this dish. Super refreshingChicken Liver - [mousse, ny maple, milk bread] - of my fav dishes of the night! Perfectly smooth mousse and the milk bread was a unique spin. The honey gave it the right about of sweetnessPig Out (for 2) - [berkshire pork, spicy peanut noodle, condiments] - the portions are extremely big! It comes with a side of spicy peanut noodles too. The two sauces were amazing and I loved the peanut noodlesScallops - [black lentils, onions, and peas] - We were pretty stuffed after the pig out but the scallops were amazing. The sauce with the black lentils was so delish Broccoli - [fermented shallot, garlic, Sichuan chili ] - this was prob the best broccoli I had at a restaurant. The sauce made from homemade ingredients was a homerunBeignets - Must have dessert - the buns were nice and hot and the sauces made it a perfect end to the night.I was extremely satisfied by the end of the meal. Every dish was spot on. Service was good and I think they definitely deserve their one Michelin star.

Venturing to Thai Villa promises an authentic Thai culinary journey worth the visit. With no reservations required, they offer a savvy "waitlist" option that efficiently reduces wait times to a mere 20-30 minutes. The bustling takeout and delivery scene observed during the wait hints at the popularity and high demand of the restaurant's offerings.

Upon arrival, if you discover open seats at the bar, you can seize the opportunity for immediate seating, bypassing the wait altogether. The menu may be a mystery, as we didn't catch the names of our delectable selections, but each dish delighted us with its flavor and generous serving size. An unexpected treat was the sample shot of yellow squash soup—a delightful preview of the meal's quality.

Thai Villa is not just a dining spot but a culinary destination suited for smaller groups—ideal for up to six diners. Mark it as a top contender for a "must-visit" on your restaurant list.

Title: A Thick Crust Convert at Prince Street Pizza

I must confess, I've always steered clear of thick-crust pizzas, fearing a bloating aftermath. Prince Street Pizza, however, has been a game-changer. Each bite of their pizza strikes a perfect balance between satisfaction and lightness, leaving you comfortably full. Their trademark pepperoni cups, brimming with a delightful hot oil, pack a punch of depth without the overbearing saltiness often found elsewhere.

The crust's outer crispness sets the stage for the harmonious melt-in-your-mouth cheese, while the quality ingredients come together to create a culinary symphony that had my boyfriend audibly appreciating every single mouthful.

Yes, the tiny shop's popularity often leads to lines, but picking an off-peak time to visit rewards you with minimal wait. Prince Street Pizza is more than just a meal; it's a must-try experience. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

The kind of spot that makes a NYer feel like a tourist in all the best ways. The bartenders are absolutely lovely and knowledgeable. Special shout out to the bartendress with the beautiful henna on her hand! The setting is gorgeous. The cocktails delicious. What more can you ask for?

Knowing that this is Marc Forgiones place , I had high expectations for American Cut. Was somewhat disappointed at the experience. Came here Friday night in a group of four for restaurant week. I got the yellowtail crudo, tenderloin with hash browns side, and chocolate sundae for my restaurant week dinner. My meal was $42, and total bill for the four of us came to $216 tax and tip included. AMBIANCE:Love the ambiance here. Think classy, old school speakeasy meets trendy steakhouse. PROS:Want to start off with the bar first. I was waiting for my party to arrive so decided to get a drink first. I got the old fashioned, and I must say that was one of my favorite old fashioned that I've gotten in NYC. It's smokey, it's strong, and so smooth. These bartenders surely know their craft here. The drink was $10 since I came during happy hour, which ends at 730pm. Would come back for the bar most defiNitely! 5 stars out of 5just for the drinks and the bar. There are also $4 beer options and $6 wines for happy hour if and old fashioned isn't your scene. Now to the food: I must say the yellowtail crudo was spectacular. It's tangy, zesty, and the fish oh so fresh. The hash brown and cauliflower sides were also fantastic, they killed their sides. Portions were great. Hash browns were crispy on outside and airy and fluffy inside. The addition with sauteed peppers and onions added an extra flair of flavor to the hash browns.CONS:I was somewhat disappointed with the beef main course and dessert. Tenderloin was definitely wayyy too salty. The red wine reduction, although noble, wasn't reduced far enough and thus you can taste strong hints of wine. IMO I don't think that tastes good cause it just tasted like a piece of steak doused in wine.Chocolate Sunday wasn't special at all. The ice cream tasted like it could've came from Ben and Jerrys, it wasn't smooth, and was somewhat chalky. Felt like the sundae didn't require any technique to make as it really was a scoop of ice cream, brownie chunks, whipped cream, and a wallop of chocolate fudge. A four year old can make this, and I expected so much more coming from American Cut.Also the amount of whipped cream on the sundae was absurd. I'm not a whipped cream fan and would have appreciated that there was going to be that on my sundae.OVERALL:The bar is fantastic. The RW deal leaves more to be desired.

Cozy restaurant and relaxed atmosphere with friendly laid back service and super yummy food.  We visited for brunch which is a steal at $16.  You select an entree and get a bunch of small appetizers to go along with it.  In fact, if you add another $7 you get unlimited mimosas or sangria.  We opted for the coffee this time which was a Turkish strong coffee that they give to you in a cool little pot to pour into tiny cups. For my entree I got the salmon Benedict...awesome.  Poached eggs on smoked salmon over toast on top of some delicious crispy potatoes.  My wife ordered the shakshuka which was also delicious.  The other 2 in my party didn't opt for the brunch and ordered the falafel taco platter which was served with tahini, babaganoush, Israeli salad, and tahini.  The other person in our party got the falafel wrap which I believe came with chick peas.  We will definitely be back and if you're going to a show it's super convenient to most theaters.  Also, check in on yelp for a free hummus appetizer.  We saved ours for next visit.

My experience at Naruto was a mixed bag. Despite the chaos of our visit, the food was enjoyable. The restaurant's small size and counter-top-only seating are not conducive to large groups, as we found with our party of eight. We were seated sporadically and were unable to sit together even as seats became available, due to the restaurant's strict seating policy.

The constant movement of deliveries added to the disarray, forcing us to shuffle around frequently. As for the food, I tried the tan tan ramen, which was decent, though not the best I've had in NYC. The elements of a good ramen were present - pleasant flavors and an affordable price - but the broth lacked complexity and the noodles were a bit too firm for my taste.

The service and dining experience didn't quite make up for the cramped space. While Naruto has potential, it falls short in delivering superior ramen and a comfortable atmosphere, leading me to rate it at 3 stars.

When I went to NYU, this location used to be a mediocre, run-down dumpling shop. When I came back today, it had turned into a Thai spot with terrific reviews so I had to try it out - and I agree this place is absolutely fantastic! For $11-12 we got a lunch special that includes an appetizer, entree, and drink (for +$1 on the drink you can upgrade from a soda to a Thai iced coffee/tea). Although the entree portion wasn't as large as some of the other Thai lunch specials we've been to (it's half a case), it was still filling and delicious. I ordered the Pad Kha Pow, and I loved that it came with eggplant and bamboo shoots, instead of just the traditional cheap carrots, peppers, onions, beans, etc. And don't worry about the spice - I ordered the Thai spicy but it wasn't true Thai spicy. The fried tofu was fine and the Thai iced coffee was a bit sweet.After picnicking in WSP, we came back again for some happy hour drinks later in the afternoon (Sunday). They had BOGO beers ($5 for 2) and sangria ($11 for 2) and $8/$10 cocktails (12/16oz). The 4 of us ordered 2 margs, 2 mojitos, 4 sangria's, and 2 beers, and everything was delicious and awesome value. The sangria's were well fortified, and they even put real sugarcane into the mojitos! To top it all off, since we chilled outside their sidewalk, they even gave us some crunchy chips topped with sweet chili sauce to munch on as we drank.Will definitely be back when I'm in the area.

Prepare for spice! This was my first time eating Szechuan and boy was it hot, but in a good way. For lunch, I had the Qong Ping Chicken, which was super delicious. My friend had the Tofu dish and said it was spicy, but good. We ordered the Popcorn shrimp as an appetizer- omg! Their popcorn shrimp had this delicious sweet sauce on it that made it 1000x better than its American equivalent. Overall, a great meal. The staff was very friendly as well. I will definitely go back to Zest sometime!

Title: A Midtown Must-Visit for Sushi and Ribs!

My recent dinner at this Midtown hotspot was yet another reminder of why reservations are a must; the place was bustling with energy. Arriving early, we managed to snag seats at the packed bar, a testament to its popularity. Thanks to the full bar's diverse mixed drink selection and the bartenders' friendly demeanor amidst the rush, the pre-dinner drinks set a pleasant tone for the evening.

Once seated, our server proved to be very attentive, effortlessly guiding us through the specials. However, my decision was already made—I was there for the sushi and the ribs. The sushi selection was nothing short of spectacular, a culinary triumph not to be missed. But the star dish for me, as always, was the ribs. Prepared to perfection and paired with shoestring fries upon request, plus coleslaw, it's a combination I can't resist and always leaves me satisfied.

This restaurant continues to be my top choice in Midtown for a reliably delicious meal. Whether you're a sushi enthusiast or a ribs aficionado, this eatery won't disappoint.
Authentic vibe, love the ambience and decor. The price was a little higher than average but it was totally worth it. Overall 8/10

**Review of Malaysian Dive Bar in FiDi**

Nestled in the heart of the Financial District, this quirky Asian dive bar offers more than meets the eye with its authentic Malaysian flavors and a unique twist of Jameson shots to top off the dining experience. The vibe is fun, laid-back, and perfect for a casual group outing.

We indulged in the "yummy noodles," which lived up to their name with a robust Malaysian curry zest, paired beautifully with "mama's curried chicken" that was rich in flavor and authenticity. The standout, however, was the "crispy fried rice," true to its name with a delightful crunch and a recommendation to opt for the Chinese sausage variant – it did not disappoint.

As for the ambiance, the energetic music set a vibrant mood, and the attentive owner made the rounds, ensuring everyone was enjoying their time. This little gem in FiDi is a solid recommendation for those craving genuine Malaysian cuisine with a convivial atmosphere.
Good atmosphere, excellent service. Food was below average. Ordered spaghetti and some of it was uncooked/dry.

This is probably one of my favorite bars in the city so far. The interior design really gives you a sports bar feel and the food is incredible. We ordered the dukes sliders and honey BBQ wings. I definitely recommend both choices, the slider was filled with a crispy fried chicken and the wings were cooked just perfect.

I had a delightful dining experience at this gem of a restaurant, thanks to its great atmosphere. The macaroni burger I ordered was not only mouthwateringly delicious but also incredibly filling. Be warned, it's so massive, it could easily be shared between two people. I visited on a bustling Friday during happy hour and, despite the crowd, managed to snag a couple of seats in the bar area. This spot is a must-visit, and I'm already looking forward to my next meal here.

I've passed by this place so many times not knowing what it was, until my friend informed me that it was a speakeasy! I absolutely love speakeasies , so I gathered my friends one night and ventured down here! We didn't have to wait, the bouncer informed us there was standing room, but it was very small. We were okay with. We went in and it was packed! The bartenders were super cool, we didn't have to wait long for a menu and our drinks came fairly quick.My friends and I tried a few of the cocktails and for the most part, they were great. This is a really cool spot, and it's worth checking out if you're in the area. And hey, they'll tell you for fortune too for a cool $20

I've ordered delivery from this local gem on two separate occasions and have been thoroughly impressed both times! My first foray was with their Latin omelette, a substantial offering generously topped with creamy avocado and spicy jalapeños. Accompanied by buttery toasts and a fresh side salad, it made for an incredibly satisfying brunch.

On my second go-around, I decided to try the clam pasta, which was delightfully good, capturing that homemade essence despite the pasta reminding me of something you'd pick up at the grocery store. Still, the dish was hearty, complete with dinner rolls and a side salad, crafting a filling meal that hit the spot. Plus, the buffalo sauce I requested on the side added that perfect kick. Would recommend for a comforting and filling meal at home!

Title: A Delight for Herbivores and Carnivores Alike!

Our dining experience at this gem of a restaurant was a unanimous hit. Often navigating dining out can be a challenge with our vegan daughter's strict dietary choices and my husband's meat-loving palate, but this place catered to both flawlessly. The vegan nanban buns were the opening act and set the bar high, tantalizing our taste buds with their deliciousness.

The diverse ramen bowl selection was a crowd-pleaser, satisfying everyone's cravings. Our server, Bo, deserves a special mention for his exceptional service. His patience in answering our multitude of questions regarding flavors, spice levels, and exotic vegetables transformed our meal into an enlightening culinary adventure.

The ambiance is laid-back yet lively, perfect for groups seeking a fun, casual dining atmosphere. Despite the buzz of chatter adding to a slightly noisy background, it didn't detract from the enjoyable experience.

In summary, this restaurant is a fantastic pick no matter what your dietary preferences. It's a place where vegans, carnivores, and the curious can all find something to savor and enjoy, with service that makes you feel both welcome and informed. Two thumbs up!

I recently dined at Gansevoort Market and was impressed with its versatility, making it an excellent spot for groups with its plethora of food options. The ambiance was relaxed and comfortable, with no overcrowding, which was a plus.

My choice for the evening was the "Burger inc." burger accompanied by bacon fries. The burger didn't disappoint – it rested on a soft, buttery brioche bun and was notably juicy. As for the bacon fries, they were nothing short of spectacular – albeit a tad pricey at $6.50, their flavor-packed punch and delectable sauce justified the cost.

For those looking to save, I recommend using the Crave app – it snagged me 50% off the burger, sweetening the experience even further. All in all, Gansevoort Market is worth a visit for anyone looking to indulge in a variety of tasty offerings in a laid-back setting.

I think Barepas just became one of my favorite restaurants! We came in at about 5:30pm for an early dinner. All the reviews were great so I knew we were in for a treat. First thing I noticed was the decor - very nice and industrial. I especially loved all the wine around the walls. The restaurant was pretty empty so we were tended to right away. Ellen was our server and she was very friendly and fast all throughout. They have a pretty extensive wine selection and a couple of beers. I can't recall the name of the one we selected but it was delicious. The menu is mostly composed of tapas and arepas - we went with the following: (1) Pabellon Criollo: my favorite out of all the dishes we tried, the sweet plantain with the beef and the rice fritter with the refried beans was the most perfect combination; (2) Spicy Chorizo Patacones: these mini bites of fried green plantain with cheese and chorizo were heaven sent, very flavorful; (3) Mini Empanadas: an assortment of cheese, beef, chicken and sweet plantain and I loved them all; (4) Mini Cachapas: the cheese and sweet corn tortilla were perfectly balanced; (5) Sour Mango Salad: the citrus highlights in this one were everything, the mango, radish and the sald dressing together were amazing; (6) Tequeños: very crispy and full of gooey cheese on the bite, I could've ate 5 alone; and last but not least (6) the Quesillo: the venezuelan version of the flan (custard) which was good, but I think the caramel had bourbon and it became a little too much at one point. We also had a glass of a Porto dessert wine to finish our meal which was marvelous. Additionally, they had live music for the night; we decided to stay until it started at 7:00pm and it was great. All in all a great dining experience. It's a beautiful chill spot for some good wine and delicious tapas and I'm really glad I found it. Its not cheap per say but the quality and taste of the food makes up for the prices. There's no doubt in my mind I'm going to become a regular and will be coming back veryyyy soon to try their cheese platter!

Very basic hotpot place. It's exactly what it is....hot pot with your normal sauces on the side, very basic broth etc etc. No special sauces from what I saw and everything was just really average.Not that it was a bad thing. My friend and I got the $11.95 lunch special which came with your choice of meat, a roll of noodles, one fish ball, one fish tofu, one crabmeat...some watercress and nappa cabbage. I think for $11.95 the portion wasn't that big (not all you can eat**) but if you're not that hungry it's filling enough and also saves you a good $10-15 compared to eating at other places in the area like Hou Yi Hot Pot ($26/person for lunch) and 99 Favor Taste ($23/person all day) ((I get those are all you can eat compared to this but like I said if you're not that hungry you can get away with this lunch deal)). Also if you need or want more food, you can always order more which my friend and I did (we got another 6 fish tofus for $4).Overall it was an okay hotpot place. I don't think it was amazing. I just found it very average and basic and the food tasted exactly how it should taste but all the flavor I feel came mostly from the side sauces (hoisin, garlic, etc) rather than the broth.

Title: A Delightful Evening at Blue Smoke

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Blue Smoke and must say, it was a fantastic experience. Meeting an old friend in the area after a work training, we decided to give Blue Smoke a try based on its stellar reviews. Upon arrival, we found the bar area bustling with activity, thanks to a popular happy hour offering $2 off drinks - a deal that's worth arriving early for, as seating quickly becomes scarce.

We were greeted warmly by the staff around 5:30 PM and warned of a potential 40-minute wait, though pleasantly, we were seated in just about 15. It's noteworthy to mention that larger parties should consider reservations due to the crowd.

The food and drinks certainly lived up to expectations. My Daiquiri was perfectly robust, complementing the Rhapsody in 'Cue I relished, which was both delicious and generous enough for leftovers. The cornbread added to the meal's homey vibe. For dessert, the Beignets with café au lait sauce were an absolute treat.

Overall, Blue Smoke offered a memorable evening filled with great company, scrumptious food, and a lively atmosphere. I'm already looking forward to my next visit and to exploring more of their menu. Highly recommended!

I confess this is not an equal replacement for my Tex Mex breakfast/general taco loves and desires. But this does remind me enough of the general gist without upsetting me that I'm all about this taco truck which typically I cannot enjoy much due to its location within the northwest corner of Madison Square Park and the hours. It's not really on my way to work but I found it one day on a day off where I actually made it to the portable stand before they closed.People who don't really miss tacos may not understand or appreciate this taco which is made in a kitchen and brought to eat during the early morning hours before 10. I managed to try this again in the taco drop option for the new normal that is 2020. They included several options of which I truly enjoyed the breakfast and the bean tacos the best. Reheating instructions included.The flour taco gives me slight H.E.B. Vibes which makes me just miss those fresh tortillas and fresh tortilla smells. No this is not that Cali taco truck taco either. This is the NYC attempts at classic Texan breakfast taco tradition similar to those egg and cheeses on a roll that I devoured in my assimilation to NYC. And I'm all about it. Next try is Queso!

Title: A Single Visit May Suffice

After hearing buzz around the neighborhood for years, I finally decided to give this well-established spot a try. I dove straight into their pho, which admittedly did have a leg up on the usual Chinatown fare. However, the price was a bit steep, nearly double what I'm accustomed to, and while good, it didn't quite justify the cost. The serving size also gave me pause; although the small bowl was sufficient, it lacked the generous portions you'd typically expect for the price.

Curiosity led me to sample the bone marrow, a dish that's made the rounds on social media. The aroma was inviting and the flavor satisfying, but the portion size was underwhelming. It's a dish to try once for the experience, but it's not one I'd indulge in again.

The ube cheesecake, a crowd favorite, remained untasted, as I couldn't bring myself to splurge $12 on a single dessert. In summary, while the food here shows promise, the value proposition falls short, leading me to conclude that a return visit isn't high on my list.

I went to The Palm for a birthday dinner with my family visiting from out of town. Although it was a bit noisy, due to the layout of the dining room, the food was great and the service was wonderful! Our waiter was funny and informative, as well as attentive and prompt.  Everyone LOVED their meals, from salads and sides (sautéed spinach, Mushrooms and potatoes) to steaks and lobster.  Top notch service and food.  If you're looking for aRestaurant in NYC for a special occasion, this is IT!!

Title: Great Food Marred by Poor Service

I've been a patron of this establishment for over a year, drawn by the delectable cuisine that consistently pleases the palate. Unfortunately, the dining experience is significantly tarnished by the lackluster service. The servers convey a palpable sense of disinterest, bordering on rudeness, which creates an unwelcoming atmosphere for my friends and me. It's a shame that the exceptional food must be overshadowed by the discomfort caused by the staff's demeanor. While the culinary offerings earn a solid four stars, the service leaves much to be desired.

Title: A Solid Choice for Veggie Lovers in Kips Bay – Mike's Pizza

If you find yourself wandering through Kips Bay with a pizza craving, Mike's Pizza is a convenient stop to satiate that desire with a pretty decent slice. Their pizza might not send you into culinary euphoria, but it's reliably good and gets the job done.

I'm particularly impressed with their dedication to providing a variety of veggie toppings – a boon for the vegetarians in the neighborhood. The broccoli mushroom slice I had last night was a pleasant veg-out for just $4.50. Mike's seems to whip up different veggie combinations daily, so there's often something new to try.

While Mike's may not be the spot for a pizza that'll haunt your dreams, it's undoubtedly a fine choice for a quick, tasty bite, especially if you're on the move.

The LRoom cafe presents itself as a dessert lover's dream with an emphasis on presentation, prompting anticipation for an equally stunning taste experience. However, the reality somewhat underwhelms. I opted for the creatively named "Head in the Clouds" and the "Mango," both of which looked visually appealing, almost art-like in their presentation.

Regrettably, the Mango dessert's amalgamation of white chocolate and mango flavors was a misstep. The attempt at a delicate balance between rich and fruity ended up clashing rather than complementing, despite the visual finesse including a striking green shadow detail mimicking a real mango.

The Head in the Clouds, while okay, did not justify its price point—it was essentially an ordinary scoop of ice cream paired with cotton candy, leaning more toward a visual spectacle than a culinary one.

In summary, The LRoom is an "instagrammable" spot that prioritizes aesthetics over palate. If your objective is to capture a photogenic treat, it may be worth the visit. For those seeking a dessert that tastes as good as it looks, it may be best to look elsewhere. The experience is best described as style over substance, with a serving of mediocrity.
Fun local place. You have to be ok with close seating tho.  Food was good, kinda cool place to see all the patches on walls.

After countless recommendations, I finally visited Los Tacos No.1, and it lived up to the hype. The flavors packed into their tacos and quesadillas were outstanding, with each bite leaving me wanting more. Expect a lengthy lunch queue, but rest assured, it's swift-moving and the service is speedy. The ambiance strikes the perfect balance between a food truck vibe and a bustling food court, enhanced by lively music. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit to explore more of their delicious offerings.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise Despite Some Missteps

Despite stumbling upon this Italian eatery amid a sea of middling reviews, my dining experience left me pleasantly surprised. The quiet atmosphere—likely attributed to the sparse Sunday evening crowd—set the stage for a meal that surpasses its reputation.

The menu, while nothing out of the ordinary for an NYC Italian restaurant, offered a satisfactory range of options, albeit in smaller, tapas-style portions. For my boyfriend and I, known for our hearty appetites, an appetizer, two pasta dishes, and a side proved to be ample.

We were greeted with complimentary bread, which, unfortunately, was the low point of the meal. It was stale and unappealing, and not even butter—served cold and unspreadable—could salvage it. I settled for using my pasta sauces as a dip.

The Costicine di Agnello (grilled lamb chops) was a standout, arriving first and delivering on both taste and accompaniments. Following that, the Fettuccine ai Funghi offered a no-frills satisfaction that seemed best suited for someone specifically craving it. However, the Lasagne Bolognese fell short, presenting a perplexing temperature inconsistency between the sauce and the pasta that hinted at a lapse in kitchen timing. The Cavolini (roasted Brussels sprouts), on the other hand, was a simple delight, rounding out the meal nicely.

While not without its faults, this restaurant offered a solid dining experience that warrants a return visit. It may not be Via Carota, but for a quick find, it delivered a gratifying meal that succeeded in defying its underserved low rating.

Title: A Late Night Delight in NY

I recently found a gem right next to my hotel on a late Thursday night. My group was seated immediately at this adorable establishment, with waters served as we settled. The service was exceptional, almost telepathic, with side soup and salad arriving promptly after ordering.

Despite being on a work trip and needing separate checks for expenses, the staff accommodated us without any hassle, a rarity compared to other restaurants we've visited.

The decor was charming and inviting, though my Chicken Cutlet Don-group B was somewhat underwhelming in flavor. But what the cuisine lacked, the service more than made up for, providing a standout experience.

Astonishingly, when it came time to tip for their stellar service, we learned they don't accept tips. In today's world, it's rare to see such dedicated service given without the expectation of a gratuity. And, as a testament to their customer care, they even dashed out to return my forgotten phone.

I left feeling valued and cared for. This restaurant has not only earned my glowing recommendation but my eagerness to return on my next trip to NY.

Tonight's experience at one of my favorite NYC eateries was delightful. The coconut curry was a flavorful triumph, and the triple chocolate brownie was an indulgent masterpiece. Highly recommend for a memorable dining experience.

HOLY COW WHAT A BEAUTIFUL PLACE. Honestly we looked for a restaurant for a really long time at like 9pm and found this and decided to walk over. Didn't need a reservation then, got seated immediately. Corn cheese wow and also the signature cocktails are awesome. Loved the pancake and kimchi rice - basically we ordered more than we could eat because it all looked awesome and it was. Please go here.

Title: A Vibrant Celebration at Amor

We celebrated my girlfriend's mother's birthday at Amor and the experience was delightful. Despite its cozy size, the staff efficiently seated us at a prime spot near the live band with ample room for our stroller. Evening parking was a breeze compared to daytime woes, but make sure to reserve a table, especially on a packed Saturday night like ours.

The culinary offerings were top-notch, from the savory empanadas, tostones rellenos, and calamari starters to the expertly prepared skirt steak and the flavorful ropa vieja my husband savored. The drinks complemented our meals perfectly, and the live music added a festive backdrop throughout the evening.

A special touch was provided when a birthday dessert was served and the band serenaded my girlfriend's mother. While the ambiance is perfect for date nights or group gatherings, it might be too lively for little ones on music nights – thank goodness for baby headphones!

Management's frequent check-ins to ensure our comfort and the baby's well-being reflected their commendable service. Amor has certainly earned a spot on our list for a return visit.

If you want fresh rice rolls, Yi Ji Shi Mo is worth checking out.  The storefront and seating is extremely humble.  Maybe seats about 8 people.  Their menu is limited but that's never a bad thing.  They do a few things and they do it well.  Each item is made to order so there is a bit of a wait.  We waited about 10 minutes for our beef rice roll, sweet corn rice roll, and  curry fishball rice roll.  If it's not jampacked here, you can watch the guy work his magic making your rice roll.  Personally, I was mesmerized.1 star taken off because of service speed but this really can't be helped since everything is made to order.  Primarily it's because they do not accept credit cards.  Even if they do a $10 minimum, that'll be great.   Businesses today, even Chinatown businesses should start taking credit cards if they want more business.  It's just convenient.  I happened to have cash on me but if I didn't, I would've just went elsewhere.

I recently visited this gem during Restaurant Week and was thoroughly impressed. The selection on offer was commendable—a perfect showcase of their culinary strengths. The modern interior provided a stylish yet comfortable ambiance, which further enhanced the dining experience. The dishes were exceptional across the board, equally matched by the attentive and friendly service. To cap off a memorable meal, the dessert was a creative masterpiece, both playful and delicious. A must-visit for any food enthusiast looking for a top-notch dining experience. Highly recommended!

Title: Great for Groups, Watch the Salt

My coworkers and I ended up at this spot after a morning seminar, with no issue getting seated ahead of our reservation despite our group size of 13. The menu was diverse enough to please our varied tastes. We started with a round of Caesar salads, calamari, and chicken wings, which hit the spot. Our mains ranged from penne alla vodka with chicken and seafood pasta to pasta with shrimp – all flavorful, although a tad too salty for my liking. We were stuffed by the end, so desserts will have to wait for another visit. It's a solid choice for large gatherings, but I'd likely pass on a solo return due to the salt level.

Title: A Mixed Bag for a Trendy Brunch Spot

My recent experience at this rooftop restaurant, while celebrating a birthday brunch with a large group, was a rollercoaster of highs and lows. The restaurant impresses with its aesthetic charm and ambiance, boasting a perfect 10/10 in both. With its myriad of photo opportunities, from a cool backlit wall to a champagne bottle tower, this place is a social media enthusiast's dream.

The brunch music was another highlight, with the DJ spinning an impeccable selection of 2000s and current hip-hop, R&B, and reggae, creating an upbeat atmosphere that's hard not to enjoy.

However, the food and drink components of the brunch fell short of expectations. The limited vegetarian options left much to be desired, and the vegan burger I ordered didn't come with the advertised caramelized onions and was served with a mere handful of veggie chips. Non-vegetarian dishes such as the salmon also suffered from inconsistent preparation, with parts served undercooked.

Drinks, an essential part of any brunch, were underwhelming. The unlimited mimosas and sangrias lacked strength, and the 1.5-hour window felt restrictive.

Customer service was where the experience notably waned. Despite a reservation, the management's communication about seating arrangements was confusing, and once seated, it took longer than expected to receive basic attention such as water. Furthermore, inconsistent pricing on hookah services left a sour taste.

Overall, I rate the experience a 7/10. The venue is worth a visit for the vibe and music alone but is not particularly vegetarian-friendly. My recommendation for large groups is to bring cash for an easier payment process—especially for hookah services, which are cash-only at $35.

Title: An Exquisite Thai Delight

I recently dined at a one-star Michelin Thai restaurant that proved to be a true gem. The standout dish for me was the dessert – toasted coconut ice cream that was simply delish. The frog legs were another highlight: sweet, tender, and cooked to perfection. The mango salad didn't disappoint, and the spicy cabbage was exceptional. Even the tea was great, adding to the overall enjoyment of the meal. The rice was passable, but not a standout.

Service was attentive and the staff showed an impressive knowledge of the menu, enhancing our dining experience. An added bonus was the convenience of walking in late without a reservation and not having to wait for a table.

Overall, I would rate this establishment an impressive 4.5 stars. It's definitely a must-visit for any Thai cuisine enthusiast.

This was my first time trying Indian food, so I might not be the most credible source. BUT this food was absolutely amazing in my opinion. We got the butter chicken and saag paneer with a side of rice and garlic naan. I loved it all! I'd have to say the butter chicken was my favorite - so flavorful, rich and creamy. It was amazing to put over the rice and eat with the naan. I do highly suggest making reservations. We sat at the bar because there weren't any tables available. They have an amazing drink selection as well. We didn't get any, but we saw so many cool things being made. Great experience!

During restaurant week, despite the overwhelming crowd and reported wait times of up to an hour and a half, our experience at this dining establishment was surprisingly pleasant. Our frustration with the wait despite our reservation was swiftly addressed after a word with the manager, who kindly accommodated us at the sushi bar—an unexpected yet delightful twist to our evening. The food was nothing short of fabulous, effectively compensating for any initial inconvenience. It turned out to be a lovely dining experience, and we are eager to return.

Pretty good place to get lunch. There are plenty of tables and it's a pretty causal environment. I had a beef taco salad which consists of ground beef, guacamole, pico del gallo, sour cream and some corn chops on top of romaine lettuce all in a fried tortilla bowl. There was a good ratio of toppings to the lettuce. It was very good! The tortilla bowl was oily and very flaky. Not bad, but messy to eat. The portion size was filling. No bathroom though.

Ugh  .....not sure how to give a real review for this place......so if you are going simply for the food DON'T......if you are going for the party it's a green light......my orginal meal had to be sent back...which was shrimp and grits.....because the grits were hard and clumpy......I then got chicken and waffles.....and it was ok.......but like I said.....this is not a place for upscale dining.....nor promt service......you go here solely for the party.....and difiently not a date spot......music is too loud to hear the person you are with........so yeah why my 3 star rating is over generous.........that's solely on the fact I had a fun time and it was lit ......

Title: A Slice of Home at Joe and Pat's

As a Staten Island native, I was thrilled to find that a piece of my childhood, Ciro, had made its way to the city with the expansion of Joe and Pat's, conveniently situated just a block from my new East Village apartment. This neighborhood gem is a testament to true Italian cooking, offering an unbeatable menu from which I highly recommend the "Tri Pie" and the chicken franchese. The mozzarella in corozza is a cheesy indulgence that is simply beyond words.

The authenticity of this establishment shines, especially in its famously thin-crust pies. My frequent visits in the past two weeks are a testament to the irresistibility of their dishes. For those on the go, you can grab the best slice in town Monday through Thursday, between 12-6pm. Joe and Pat's is definitely the place to satisfy your Italian cravings in the heart of the city. Check out my latest culinary escapades with a few snaps I'll be posting soon. If you're ever in the area, treat yourself to a meal that's truly delizioso!
was amazing helping us with excellent service and hospitality! Very good Russian vibes ! Excellent spot so if you in NEW YORK definitely. Good stuff right there :)

Cozy little spot at The Shop at Hudson Yards. The cashiers are always delightful and high spirited. I go here to get my lunch because it's a quick grab. They have Korean specialities like kimbap, chicken katsu, sandwiches, and other Asian snacks.
Good place to grab a drink before going out- the cocktails are on the pricier side, but that's typical for NYC. The hibiscus margarita was delicious.

I recently visited the Mighty Quinn BBQ outlet at Hudson Eats and came away underwhelmed. Opting for the half-pound of Burnt Ends, priced at about $13 and served with pickled veggies and coleslaw, I anticipated the chain's typical quality. Unfortunately, I encountered issues from the start, including a lack of utensils and napkins with my to-go order. 

While the convenience of a moderate line and quick pickup through the Ritual app was a plus, the burnt ends themselves were a letdown—overly fatty, drenched in an excessive amount of BBQ sauce, and the pickled veggies were lackluster. The overall value fell short of expectations, leading me to conclude that I'm unlikely to return to this particular location for my BBQ fix.

Popped in here for a dinner with friends and it took a while to order, but once we were served, we had a few of the dishes:- Signature Yunnan Crossing Bridge: Yunnan noodles that they prep one bowl for you at the table, and any others are brought out already prepared for you. Ingredients include: 4-hour chicken broth, silkie (black) chicken, beef, pork, fish, bean sprouts, tofu skin, scallions and Chinese chives. This was not bad but not as many toppings and flavors as the shop down the street.Tofu pudding looked good from my friend, a tofu pudding, minced pork, carrots, scallions, cilantro, pickled cabbage and Chinese chives. Included the noodles and looked tasty.Pork on a stick was delicious, actually reminded me of the lamb on a stick from Xi'an. Brown chicken (spicy) included braised chicken, potato and konjac tofu, was ok but not as good as the pork on a stick. Overall satisfying but have had better flavors and service at other similar restaurants.

Madangsui is a great spot for Korean BBQ. If I'm looking for a place that's a little quieter where I don't have to battle the 32nd Street crowds, where it's less smoky, where I can leave without smelling like BBQ meat, and where I don't feel like someone is timing my meal from the moment I sit down, they're one of my top choices.We often order appetizers, like seafood pancake or japche, to round out our meal, and while they're fine, we're really there for the BBQ. The marinated beef options are delicious. I'm partial to bulgogi, but all the ones I've had have been good. If you want something other than beef, the spicy chicken is one of my favorite things there. I also like that they give you a lot of banchan. The prices are a little on the expensive side for BBQ, and the portion sizes aren't huge, but over the years we've been going there, the quality of the BBQ has been consistently good, which is why we keep going back.

Title: Happy Hour Haven with Top-Notch Margaritas

I'm a regular at this spot for their unbeatable happy hour offerings (Tues-Fri 4-7pm & 9-11pm, Sun-Mon 4-7pm & 9-close), where the frozen margaritas outshine the ones on the rocks in both flavor and kick. Just remember, to score these deals, you've got to grab a seat inside, as the outdoor seating sticks to regular pricing.

The service is snappy, especially when it comes to their fresh, zesty guacamole and chips—a personal favorite. Tacos here come with a spicy salsa that's nothing short of sensational. Despite the occasional crowd, the ambiance retains a lively and welcoming atmosphere. It's my go-to spot for a relaxed hang with friends and top-tier drinks.

Despite its steep prices, the restaurant delivers on taste. Our $17 lobster roll and $13 crab roll came generously filled with sumptuous seafood. The crunchy toasted bun complemented perfectly with the divine butter. The lobster roll hit all the right notes, although the crab roll erred on the salty side, masking the natural flavors of the seafood. A lighter hand on the salt could help highlight the inherent sweetness and freshness of the ocean's bounty. Still, both offerings were quite scrumptuous.

Title: A Sizzling Experience in NYC That Keeps Me Coming Back

Whenever my coworkers and I visit New York City, dining at this restaurant has become a delightful tradition. The excitement of having our meals cooked right before our eyes contributes to the vibrant atmosphere that never fails to entertain us. This visit, while our waiter may have seemed a tad brusque, the quality of the food remained unimpaired—mouthwatering, to be precise.

Reservations are highly recommended, as this popular hotspot is usually bustling with food enthusiasts. Our feast was plentiful and diverse, featuring a succulent combo of pork, an assortment of beef cuts, and tender chicken. The standout for me was the marinated beef, so flavorful that it lingered in my memory long after the meal. Complementing the meats were a variety of pickled vegetables that added a refreshing crunch to our dining experience.

The glass noodle dish, consistently my favorite, was irresistible. I found myself captivated by its delicious simplicity. Although our waiter wasn't always prompt, this minor hiccup didn't detract from the experience. We embraced the opportunity to pluck tasty morsels straight from the sizzling grill—casual and enjoyable.

An especially memorable spectacle is the staff maneuvering hot coals with finesse, replenishing the grills at each table, a testament to the restaurant's dedication to an authentic and engaging experience.

In conclusion, this dining experience is as fun as it is satisfying. Just be prepared for a bit of a wait if you’re without a reservation, but rest assured, it’s worth it.

Came for the $10 burger at happy hour. Pretty substantial burger size and comes with a side of fries. The pickle was a bit underwhelming and not quite pickle enough, like a rubbery cucumber. Short selection of draft beers with happy hour. Also really interesting that they take reservations at happy hour. The place was empty when we arrived around 6:30 but the waitstaff told us that we should wrap up our meal before the 8pm reservation. Not sure what that was about but we were done by 8pm anyway. Not really a space to hang out with a large group for happy hour but rather a more intimate happy hour meetup.

First time in this place. My sister was visiting from out of town and in the lieu of the Christmas spirit, decided to take her. This place was decorated with so much holiday spirit, it was so beautiful. There was minimal wait for brunch. Food was good and service was good as well. I would say my favorite part was the decor and ambiance of this place. I would love to go back one day.

Title: A True Gem for Farm-to-Table Enthusiasts

My dining experience at this restaurant was nothing short of superb. The philosophy of simplicity shines in their small yet meticulously curated menu. Each dish feels carefully crafted, starting with the special acorn squash soup – a perfect balance of flavor without overwhelming saltiness and just the right texture. The kale salad was a vibrant, flavorful appetizer that set the stage for a memorable meal.

The entrees were a culinary trifecta; the tortellini, steak, and chicken were each cooked to perfection, with the tortellini being the standout for its rich, buttery excellence. Drinks from the bar were a revelation – they were not only reasonably priced but expertly mixed, showcasing the bartender's mixology prowess.

I wholeheartedly recommend this dining spot for anyone seeking an outstanding farm-to-table experience. Their attention to detail and quality across the board ensures that my first visit will certainly not be my last.

This place EXCELS at delivering quality, fresh Poke at an excellent price. The minute you walk in, you notice the pristine upkeep of the shop. I loved how there was ample seating and a clean restroom upstairs. Everything about it  projects comfort, warmth, and cleanliness. For $11.95, you can choose one of the preset bowls or customize your own by choosing a base, toppings, mix-ins, and a sauce. Toppings and mix-ins are unlimited!! I love to load up on onion crunch, garlic crunch, tempura crunch, masago, and crab salad to spruce up my bowl. They certainly do not skimp on fish either. By the time you're through the lineup of ingredients, you'll have yourself a hefty bowl full of fresh, delicious goodness. dI'll definitely come back the next time I have a sushi craving.

Excuse me waitress*waitress comes*Can I have a small bowl and plate please?*waitress leaves**waitress comes back with small bowl and plate*Thank you!*waitress leaves*Talk about minimal interaction, not even a head nod or a smile. Food here is not as good as the decor. The baked pork chop spaghetti is the worst I've ever had - it's basically ketchup + corn syrup + sugar + gelatin mixture + more sugar. If you like ketchup flavored jello, you will dig this. My boyfriend basically eats everything and has a zero waste policy and he couldn't even finish his half. No pasta deserves to be a treated this way - sugared up, abandoned, left in the cold with no respect, and eventually in the dumpster.

Despite the lunchtime crowds, this bustling eatery efficiently accommodates diners with quick service. The affordable lunch special, which includes a hearty portion of edamame, tantalizing octopus balls, and a flavorful bowl of ramen, offers excellent value. Initially skeptical of my appetite, I was pleasantly surprised to find every dish irresistibly delicious, leaving no morsel uneaten. A cool spot indeed, I am eager to return for another satisfying meal. Highly recommended!

I randomly stumbled upon this place while looking for a place to get lunch. Based on the name, I thought it was a fast casual salad place like Sweetgreen. It turns out it was much more. Yes, this is a fast casual place but it is more like the Dig Inn chain.They do offer salads here, but the menu is way more varied. They also have food platters where you choose a protein with sides, and sandwiches and soup too! Like Dig Inn, the food is on the healthier side, but does not skimp on taste. The main proteins offered here are their salt and pepper chicken, chipotle chicken, salmon, steak, falafel, and fried chicken.Speaking of the chicken, the chicken was way juicier and tastier than the dried up and hard chicken at Sweetgreen. This is definitely a solid lunch choice for this neighborhood.

Long time favorite. If you are going to enjoy oysters in NYC there is no better place. Their inventory selections are unmatched. They have the largest variety of seafood options in the city and I never had a bad meal. Of corse, you'll want to try the clam chowder. They still prepare in the same  steam pots used 100 years ago. A must in NYC. Don't dress up. Come as you are. And, all you ladies the saloon has the largest inventory of handsome eligible men lubricating for the train ride home after work.

I recently dined at this spot and had a truly enjoyable experience. The food quality is superb, albeit the prices are on the higher end, the portions justify the cost. I opted for a filling bowl that combined rice, greens, luscious hummus in Greek style, and falafel, accompanied by warm pita - the hummus stood out as one of the finest I've savored in New York City. Although the falafel was good, I'm tempted to try grilled chicken for my next visit. Be mindful that the lunch rush does create lengthy lines, so it's wise to place your order in advance to avoid the wait.

Came by with my friends for happy hour and this place was already so packed. The venue is actually so spacious with long tables for seating!! Pretty sure there was a company holiday happy hour going on when we came. They had some pretty good deals for happy hour but I opted for a tall glass of raspberry cider (hard cider with a splash of raspberry) for $13 total. We also ordered nachos and the large pretzel to share, which were both so good!! Would recommend getting those for the table. It was kind of hard to hear each other with all the noise in the background but it's a great spot to start your evening with lots of bars nearby!
Good atmosphere and great food. The average steakhouse ambiance, dark lit and loud conversations. However, the shrimp cocktail presentation is memorable. Would I return? Yes!

so disappointed with the dim sum here. very limited selection for a weekend brunch and it seemed like they were out of a lot of things. it felt like the only carts circulating were primarily dessert carts.... also we were seated in the worst possible area (the last stop i guess) even though our floor had way better spots available, so by the time something we wanted came by that cart was empty. it also took a long time to get a servers attention. it was like they actually sped up when they wheeled by our table lol. the piggy custard buns and the shrimp rice roll were good but that was about it. the other dim sum was kinda bland and so carb heavy that the other ingredients were an afterthought.

I recently attended the "Ugly Produce is Beautiful Dinner" at Stella Trattoria, and it was yet another remarkable experience. The evening was a journey of culinary excellence from start to finish. From the very first bite of the amuse-bouche to the last morsel of dessert, every dish exceeded expectations. Admittedly, I overindulged, but it was impossible to resist such exceptional fare. Kudos to Stella Trattoria for transforming ingredients often overlooked for their appearance into a feast that was nothing short of a masterpiece.

I stopped in for a quick breakfast on a Wednesday morning and was pleasantly surprised by the prompt seating. The coffee arrived swiftly, accompanied by an adorable mini creamer pitcher – a nice touch. The real stars of the meal were the pierogis; each one was delicious, but the potato and truffle mushroom options stood out as particularly delectable. A delightful morning dining experience!

During my visit to the restaurant, the dumplings were disappointing and seemed to lack quality and care in their preparation. Even when paired with the accompanying sauce, they did not rise above the impression of being cheaply produced. However, the restaurant's prices are notably low, making it a potential option for diners seeking a filling meal without concern for culinary finesse. Please note that the establishment does not offer tap water, necessitating the purchase of bottled water to stay hydrated.

Pretty and nicely decorated fusion Indian restaurant. They have HH from 5-7pm on drinks. Tried could dishes and we liked them all! - soft shell crab - as good as it can be, the sauce was interesting and pairs really well. - grilled prawn - very very tender and fresh prawn, would hope the spinach bed below and get some dressing as well. - scallop - simply tasty, I also really like the yellow smushy thing came with it underneath.Cocktail menu are fun and very artistically presented.

Title: A Pho-nomenal Experience at Sai Gon Dep

Sai Gon Dep has quickly become one of my top pho destinations in the city, charming me with its unique and adorable interior design. During a recent visit with my boyfriend, we indulged in the pork summer rolls and both the beef and chicken pho. Each dish was a revelation; the summer rolls boasted a perfect balance of protein and vegetables, and the pho's broth was refreshingly free of the excessive MSG and salt that often plague other establishments, allowing the true flavor of the chicken to shine through.

While prices are a touch above average, reflecting its urban location, the quality of the meal validates the cost. Sai Gon Dep has secured my future patronage, as I am eager to explore more of their authentic menu. Highly recommended for pho enthusiasts seeking a meal that tastes as if it's been crafted with care.

The pizza is definitely the star here. Twin wood fire ovens working overtime to produce arguably some of the best thin crust pizza in the area. Marta also has an impressive wine list as well as a selection of handcrafted cocktails from the well stocked bar. I enjoyed my bottle aged Negroni. The interior space is impressive and the service is decent considering that Marta does not take tips. The bathroom is a bit of a hike through the hotel bar in the back, but this makes you want to check out this unique space for an after dinner night cap.

Upon my recent visit to this bustling hotspot, it seems the initial long wait times have subsided, yet I would still suggest utilizing the Yelp waitlist for convenience—though an in-person check-in might be superior for accuracy.

As for the main event, the cheese dakgalbi, it's a communal affair requiring at least two servings per order, which generously accommodates two diners. My party of five found three servings to be ample, especially with the delightful extras: udon, rice cakes, fried dumplings, gimmari, and fried sweet potato. The medium spice level delivered a perfect harmony of flavor and heat, while the mild was pleasantly aromatic, albeit not spicy.

Do note that the side dishes, while tasty, will only be replenished upon request—and overall service could do with more attentiveness. The culinary experience concludes with a cheesy fried rice finale, made upon request as you wind down your meal.

In terms of value, the dakgalbi is indeed solid but the pricing can feel steep as it doesn't include the cost of additional toppings which I find essential for the full experience. The rice cakes are a standout but seemed scarce in each serving.

In summary, while you'll find the dakgalbi to be delectable and the experience enjoyable with a group, prepare for a slight hit to your wallet and be proactive with service.

Went for the burrata pizza. Wasn't disappointed. The other posters are correct, the middle part where the burrata sits is kind of mushy crust wise, but honestly how can you possibly support that much cheese? I liked it anyway.

Snagged a reservation for 4 at around 5pm on a Saturday, didn't actually get seated until close to 5:30. That table by the door got pretty drafty so they were more than gracious to let us move when another table opened up. Got the tartiflette, mac and cheese, and the New York for 2 with their house raclette and then the porcini afterwards. Pros: TastyPrompt with serviceAble to split the bill how we requested (one of our group had ordered wine while the rest of us did not etc etc)Affordable at ~$30ppCons:Cheese could've been hotter, seemed like it re-solidified soon after it hit the foodThe mac and cheese was made with tiny pasta? Not really a con but not really the pasta shape I was expectingNot for the lactose intolerant

The ambiance was great. I wasn't a fan of the food. The staff was dead on. Also they were very friendly and right on top of things. But I have to say the food was lacking. The wings were way over breaded to my liking. And my wife had a cob salad that she didn't care for. I'll def go back for drinks because the place is great looking and the drinks looked great.

This review is entirely based on the pesto meatball sub, because, that's the only thing I need to taste to write it! Absolutely must-have. Something I've been craving ever since I had it. The pesto has a nice savory flavor, some sort of mozz drizzle brightens it up, and the meatballs are some of my favorites anywhere.

I love thai food and this is honestly one of the best thai places in the city. Let's start with decor - it is absolutely beautiful. They have chandeliers and decorated walls - a perfect setting if you're looking for a nice place for a date. The food itself was also very good. I loved the pad thai I ordered but it was definitely on the pricier side of thai food especially in the city. If you're coming with a group, you have to all be there or you won't be seated. And it gets very busy here (especially on weekends) so make sure you try and beat the rush.If you love thai like I do, this is a MUST try place!! Ambience: 5/5Price: 2/5Food: 4/5

This is a cute little bakery/cafe to pop by in. I ordered the spanaskopita. Which was a spinach bakery item. The crust on the outside reminded me of the outer layer of a baklava. They heat it up for you as well! We went in the morning, but I can see them selling out of items fairly quickly.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Noodle Lovers

I recently discovered a wonderful little noodle shop that's perfect for a hearty late lunch. Despite its quiet ambiance, probably due to its novelty, I was impressed by the spotless setting and the warm, attentive staff who made me feel right at home.

Their menu offers the delightful duo of noodle soup and bubble tea—a combination I couldn't resist. I opted for a comforting ginger tea, which was a delightful prelude to the star of the meal: beef noodle soup. The soup was a symphony of flavors, with a spicy kick that was perfectly balanced and an ideal mix of noodles and savory beef.

If you find yourself in the neighborhood, I wholeheartedly recommend dropping by this charming noodle haven. It's certainly earned a return visit from me!

I had the fortune of snagging a table for two in less than 30 minutes on a Monday evening around 5pm at a buzzing restaurant that typically has guests waiting for hours. Despite the hype, the pricing of the burger was pleasantly surprising – not overly expensive. The meal itself was exceptional; a juicy, well-seasoned burger patty topped with thick bacon and a perfectly cooked egg, creating a harmony of flavors that was nothing short of delightful. The swift seating and delectable dinner made the experience entirely gratifying.

If you find yourself by Trinity Square Park with a pizza craving, you're in luck. The pizza spot right across provides a swift and satisfying fix. Choose your slice from an array of options, watch it get reheated to perfection, and enjoy a sizeable piece of pie for just $4-5. As a bonus, the joint is connected to a place that offers Philly steak and an assortment of sweets, including cookies and pastries. And if that's not enough, you've got a smorgasbord of food trucks just across the street. While it may not match the iconic New York slice, this place certainly delivers a tasty and budget-friendly bite.

I did a search on Yelp of the best bars in the area, and was delighted to find this wonderful place. . .  It has open late - CHECK,  creative signature cocktails - CHECK, and delicious bites at the bar- CHECK.  After 10:00 pm, only pizza is offered, but the pizza is so good, it didn't matter. The atmosphere was just the vibe I was going for:  more relaxed, classy,  beautiful speakeasy decor...  A lovely place to relax and enjoy a classic cocktail.  We were going at a perfect time it seems, based on reading the other reviews which note how popular / crowded this place gets. This was late on a Sunday night, and while there were a number of customers, there was plenty of room in the downstairs bar area, and it lacked the loud, hussle and bussle of other bars we passed by.  The service was spectacular too.  We totally relied on our waiter for suggestions, and he delivered.  I had the El Guapo, recommended by our waiter - with Tequila/Cucumber/Chili/ lime and Agave.  Simple but wonderful! I had two of these.Nick had the Dr. Zhivago with Mezcal/Tequila/Lime/Ginger/Agave/Chili.We selected the margarita pizza, which was also a favorite of our waiter. We really liked the manager Austin who came by to check on us.  We felt well taken care of of.    Wonderful experience.

Decent quick ramen. I like coming to Ramen Setagaya for a fast, pit-stop meal and drinks. It's fairly small but you can usually get a seat (although a little tight). I got the Spicy Miso Ramen recently and I loved how the pork was so melt-in-your-mouth. I did find my broth to be quite salty and thick though, which is a first for me. Also, I tried the Hot House Sake and enjoyed it as well. Overall, I think Ramen Setagaya is a consistent place for average, quick ramen--which is more often than not, all that I'm looking for!

This place is always packed so I'd recommend making an online reservation prior to coming here. We came here on a Thursday night and waited about 15 minutes before being seated. I got the yuzu eskimo, which consists of frozen Japanese cream bar, slices of fresh strawberry, and chocolate sauce. The cream bars are tart, which pairs nicely with the sweet chocolate on the side. The strawberries add a refreshing finish.

Title: Friendly Service, Overwhelming Salinity

I had the opportunity to dine at this restaurant courtesy of a family member a year ago. The staff was commendable in their friendliness, and Chef Daniel even made a point to visit our table, which added a personal touch. However, my main critique lies with the food's saltiness. My palate, unaccustomed to heavy salt, found the flavor overpowering and it detracted from my overall enjoyment. While the dishes were well-prepared, a lighter hand on the salt might have swayed my opinion positively. The restaurant offers a pleasant one-time experience, but its salt-heavy approach means I am not inclined to return. Had I not been treated, I doubt it would have been on my list of places to visit.

Title: Mixed Impressions at Local Thai Spot

My experience at this restaurant was a flavorful journey with a few hiccups along the way. I opted for the lunch special, beginning with steamed Thai dumplings. The highlight here was the surprising peanut flavor, which intriguingly overshadowed the meat. My companions tried a variety of appetizers. While the spring rolls were satisfactory, the curry puff, a lone piece, left us wanting – it's not the best choice for those enjoying a lunch special.

The main course, pad see ew, was a standout with its authentic "wok hei" – that much-coveted essence of wok-cooking – making it a delight. However, the pad Thai missed the mark. Instead of the traditional tang of tamarind, a tomato-heavy taste prevailed, leading to a disconcerting comparison to tomato-flavored spaghetti.

A word on the service: it seems a 20% gratuity is the norm here, added automatically to our bill. For a party of five at lunch, this felt steep. Diners should take note, especially when budgeting for a group meal.

In summary, while some dishes impressed, others fell short, and the tipping policy could surprise unwary patrons.

I recently visited a restaurant where I had the pleasure of sipping on a fantastic frozen watermelon margarita for just $9. While I didn't delve into the food menu, the drink alone was a highlight – refreshing and perfectly crafted. Paired with the restaurant's killer view, it made for an exquisite late afternoon treat. Highly recommended for a casual, scenic escape with a tantalizing cocktail to unwind.

I recently visited Banter for a lunch outing and sampled their Avocado Toast with an added poached egg. The avocado was spread generously, but the bread's hardness, especially at the edges, detracted from the overall experience. While the avocado toast itself seemed reasonably priced at $13, the additional $3 for the poached egg wasn't quite justifiable.

The cafe boasts a vibrant yet cozy ambiance, enhanced by trendy decor that makes it a delightful setting for a meal. Service was notably efficient, with the staff exhibiting both friendliness and attentiveness throughout the visit.

In conclusion, Banter offers satisfactory food paired with excellent service at prices that won't break the bank. I would definitely recommend it for a casual lunch for two.

Had no idea about this place, until I came here for a private birthday party and was blown away! The food, the atmosphere (rustic décor) and the fact that they can host multiple parties on any given night are huge assets. Don't let the storefront fool you, the space as a whole is ginormous! It is split up into sections. The front houses the bar, table seating and some lounge seating. The back area is the main dining room with multiple private dining spaces off of it. They also have a second floor loft space and a lower floor cellar for larger parties. We sat in the "Cabin" which accommodated 12 people at a long high top table. The room was definitely a bit snug, but I wouldn't say that warrants a star demotion.Our party host was able to create a personalized menu for the party (see photo). We did family style dining. For our first course we had the Bone Marrow (delicious to me, but not for picky eaters), the Wild Mushroom Toast (one of my favorites of the night) and the Grilled Baby Octopus (my favorite and cooked perfectly). The second course consisted of Porcini Confit White Pizza (another favorite), Pork Belly Chicharrones (the shredded apple pieces really complimented the dish) and the Sicillian Eggplant Caponata. The main course was Seared Branzino Filet, Crispy Skinned Amish Chicken (came with ricotta gnocchi, sooo good) and Chipotle Braised Short Ribs. Finally, for dessert, Apple Cider Doughnuts (with caramel dipping sauce), Lemon Cheesecake and Chocolate Caramel Tart (all bite-sized). Everything was delicious!The staff was attentive, our wine glasses were never empty and we were able to enjoy ourselves! I'd definitely come back, specifically to try their Truffle Parmesan Gnocchi which another reviewer raved about.Tips: They have a coat check, can accommodate parties up to 100 seated or 120 reception and are conveniently located near an Icon parking garage (where I prefer to park because they offer coupons).

Title: Pre-Concert Delight Next to Madison Square Garden

Located conveniently beside Madison Square Garden and The Hotel Pennsylvania, this little gem of a restaurant was the perfect pit stop before heading to a Mariah Carey concert. My party and I were seated immediately—no wait, which is always a big plus in the bustling area.

I decided to kick off the night with their specialty mixed drink, "Autumn Never Falls." While it was a touch heavy on the cinnamon for my palate, the craftsmanship was appreciated. At $14, it was a bit steep, but as a treat during my vacation, it felt justifiable.

The fish and chips, which I shared with my mom, comprised two pieces and a moderate serving of fries. Although an extra piece of fish would have made the portion perfect, I was nonetheless satisfied. The crust on the fish was uniquely scrumptious—definitely a highlight.

My friend's choice of tacos with plantains was a revelation, and my brother's grilled panini, which he ordered sans cheese, received a thumbs up. We wrapped up our meal with a couple of $9 tequila shots—a price that felt quite reasonable.

The service was top-notch, with attentive staff ensuring we were well taken care of, though it's worth noting that my brother's lemonade went unrefilled. Nevertheless, the experience was a positive one.

If you find yourself in the area, consider giving this spot a try. Signed off with gratitude, a visitor from Los Angeles.

Cheap and delicious! The wraps are really cool--they come with fries in them which I've never seen before. The halloumi was great, and we also liked the skewers. Was too full or I would've ordered the loukamades for dessert. Highly recommend.

Title: A Hearty Feast for Carnivores at Dallas BBQ

My family and I have become regulars at Dallas BBQ, thanks to its convenient proximity to New York Presbyterian Hospital where my parents work. This spot has become a family favorite, catering to our love of meat with consistently satisfying meals.

Each visit, I find myself drawn to the baby back ribs – they never disappoint, offering a juicy and tender indulgence every time. Paired with perfectly crisp fries and soft, tasty cornbread, the generous portions ensure you leave with a full belly and often, a takeaway box for later pleasures.

While I haven't ventured into their drinks menu as much as I'd like, what I have tasted has left a good impression, suggesting an extensive and quality selection. For those looking to add a spirited finish to their meal, the drinks at Dallas BBQ seem to promise a well-rounded dining experience.

In summary, if you're in the mood for a meat-centric meal that will fill you to the brim and potentially tip you over with a great drink, Dallas BBQ is your go-to place.

Title: A Bustling Gem Near Lincoln Center

Just a stone's throw from Lincoln Center and The Beacon Theater, I discovered a vibrant and lively dining spot that turned out to be the highlight of my evening. Despite its buzzing atmosphere, I was pleasantly surprised to be seated immediately upon arrival.

Our waiter, Mitchell, was prompt and attentive, greeting us with drink inquiries within minutes of sitting down. He also guided us through the Saturday specials, which was a nice touch. The do-it-yourself guacamole was an ingenious highlight. With fresh, perfect avocados and an array of customizing ingredients like pomegranate, pepitas, jalapeños, cilantro, and onions, everyone at our table crafted their dream guac to their own fiery desires.

I indulged in the buffalo cauliflower, which was simply divine. While the wings were just satisfactory, the tortilla soup impressed with its rich flavor and hearty serving size, substantial enough to satisfy as its own meal.

The atmosphere, service, and delectable offerings at this establishment created an overall delightful dining experience. It's a definite must-return for me, and I can warmly recommend it to anyone in the vicinity looking for a lively spot with delicious, customizable fare.

Nope, nope, and NOPE.Please do yourself a favor and avoid this place at all costs if you want to avoid possible food poisoning. I stopped by for a quick bite of garlic knots which I was charged $1 for 3 pieces (great price for the city). HOWEVER, the service is bad and the workers here do not enforce food safety standards. Their menu is expansive and pizzas are in the open case everywhere (three tiers of them). All of the pizzas looked as if they were sitting out since morning (I came mid afternoon). The worker there did not reheat my food properly to kill the germs and it was still room temperature in the center when I received it. The garlic knots itself tasted more like just salted bread because there was barely any garlic, butter, or parsley on it. My experience goes even more downhill when I had to pay with my credit card. I'm not sure why, but the process of paying with my credit card took longer than it did to "reheat" my food. Then, another customer comes in ordering slices of pizza. Instead of quickly finishing my transaction so I can leave, the staff literally walked away from the card reader to help the other guest leaving me there to awkwardly stand at the counter staring at my card stuck inside the reader. What the actual... When he began firing the new customer's order, he carelessly threw the slices in which resulted in it almost falling out of the oven and I saw him use his bare hands he used for to handle the register to push the pizza slices more in. Again, what the... Completely unsanitary, especially when he had tools right by the oven to handle did but chose to use his hands instead.Now back to my credit card which was STILL stuck in the reader at this point. The worker kept ignoring me and it wasn't until another staff member came out and saw I was standing by the counter for a while that he realized something was off. He opened the ovens to check if I was waiting for anything and when he noticed I didn't have an order inside, he asked me what's wrong. I eventually got out of the place, but wow, I'm never returning ever again. Save yourself, your money, and your stomach. Don't come here.

Wanted a nice Roman restaurant to celebrate my moms birthday this past weekend, and thought that Lupa fit the bill. They have an amazing, extensive wine list. You start with fresh rosemary bread, as well as crostini with fava bean spread (my favorite). We ordered the crispy squash blossoms, they were phenomenal. My dad got the crispy cod; the tomato wasn't as spicy as the menu described, but it didn't have to be- the dish was delicious. My mom got the Bolognese special of the night and thought it was yummy. I went for the classic Cacio e Pepe- I thought it was very good, but be warned if you're not great with pepper, there's definitely a good amount of it in this dish. The only thing that wasn't our favorite was the side of corn risotto (I don't recall the exact name). It was pretty good, but just seemed to be lacking some spice of some sort. Overall, a delicious restaurant- we'll be back!

Overall food/experience was a ~3.5/5 but rounding down because I wouldn't return or recommend to others. I've been wanting to go to Casa Mono for years, but never bothered to even pull up OpenTable because of how notoriously difficult it is to get a reservation. However, it turns out there's plenty of openings for weekend lunch. My fiancé and I shared 6 dishes. We were advised on 2-3 per person, but 6 definitely wasn't enough to get full on. Perhaps I just have a gigantic appetite, but if I'm dropping $150 on lunch for two, I'd like to get full. First major bummer, they didn't have their famed razor clams on the menu! I'm not sure if this was a permanent removal, but I'm quite sure there is only one menu for lunch/dinner and when I asked our server about it, she suggested mussels as a replacement (more on that later). Anyway, the dishes ranged from delicious to pretty bad. Our meal started off strong with the creamy eggs and uni, which had such a lovely mouthfeel and was well-accented by the drizzle of anchovy oil. Next were the fried sweetbreads which were drenched in some sweet and sour sauce (nothing to write home about). The foie gras was pretty good (hard to ruin foie), albeit the sauce was a bit too sweet and the portion was bad for sharing. The confit goat was pretty stringy, although maybe that's just goat? The bone marrow was delicious (but that's just the ingredient itself) but the flatbread it came with was downright awful. It had the texture of microwave pizza (or maybe cold Lunchables pizza) and had zero taste. The mussels, which capped off the meal, was probably the worst offender of all.
