The broth tasted like there was a full cup of paprika dumped in--I couldn't taste the mussels themselves at all. It made the whole dish extremely bitter and unappetizing. I ate through my half quickly just to get it over with.Given the hit-or-miss food relative to the price and the accolades, I can only recommend hopeful future dining patrons to keep their expectations lower.

Title: A Love Letter to Edo - Unjustly Rated and Deeply Missed

I must express my bewilderment at Edo's mere 3.5-star rating - it's a hidden gem that's been my sushi haven! Having frequented this spot for its stellar lunch specials in the past, circumstance – from an office relocation to a brief move out of NYC, and even pregnancy – unwarrantedly kept me at bay. But nothing could hold me back any longer; my sushi cravings had to be satisfied.

Diving back into my all-time favorite, the Spicy Roll Combo, confirmed that my affection for Edo hadn't waned a bit. As a self-proclaimed sushi connoisseur with high standards set by places like Kazunori, I assure you that Edo stands tall amid the sushi elite. Their offerings are inexplicably addictive; dare I say there's a secret ingredient that keeps you coming back for more.

The longstanding staff here is a testament to Edo's quality; they're savvy, efficient, and make no fuss about getting you what you need. This place may be unassuming in its ambiance, but it's this simplicity that underscores their mastery of sushi.

Edo, you have my heart. Thanks for remaining my go-to sushi spot in NYC, through and through.

This ramen place was underwhelming to say the least. Despite the hype and the long lines to get a seat at this place, I was disappointed with my experience. I ordered the veggie ramen and it was just your average ramen (and smaller in portion as well). The broth to noodle ratio was off- there was way more broth than noodles. I was very excited to try the matcha beer since I love matcha and have never had matcha beer before, but it was just beer with matcha powder- nothing too special. However, the interior of the place was nice, which included traditional Japanese eating booths and service. I wouldn't particularly recommend this ramen place in New York City since I've had better ramen elsewhere. In addition, in my opinion, the ramen is way overpriced. My veggie ramen and matcha beer cost me $30!

Upon trying a recommended sushi spot through a Seamless promotion, I found the experience to be decent but not exceptional. While I appreciated the quick delivery and neat packaging, the three-roll lunch special – featuring spicy yellowtail, spicy tuna, and a California roll – was merely a notch above average. Both spicy rolls were underwhelming and nearly indistinguishable, lacking the uniqueness I expected from the yellowtail, and the rice was overly sticky.

The California roll was passable, but marred by poorly sliced cucumber. The standout elements turned out to be the miso soup and salad, which were notably tastier than those from other venues. At $15, the price was modestly steeper compared to neighboring eateries, which usually offer similar specials for less. While not a poor choice for sushi delivery, I'm inclined to explore other options in the future that promise a better value.

My friend and I came here for restaurant week. It was very good. The items on the restaurant week menu are pretty solid. For appetizer, my friend got cucumber yogurt soup. It's very refreshing and appetizing. I highly recommend it. I got heart of sucrene with bacon. It's also very good. For main course, I got the flounder. It's excellent. It's very flavorful with corn flavor yet it has a little bit of kick in the sauce. My friend got roasted chicken. The flavor is pretty strong. It has an Asian flavor in it. The chicken is very juicy. For dessert, I got the roasted peach. It's refreshing and feels like summer. The chocolate cake is also great. My friend loved it.Overall this restaurant is very solid. The restaurant week menu is definitely genuine, unlike some other restaurants that give out not so good food. Our waiter was great too. The restaurant is a little bit noisy and crowded though.

Wok 88... seriously some of the best americanized chinese food I've ever had. Delicious lunch specials, appropriate lunch portions with brown rice substitute-- what's not to love? I've dined in once but I think i eat here weekly after finding out about it. I'm a huge fan of the chicken and broccoli. It is so tasty and covered with the right amount of sauce and grease that it coats the rice and adds a depth of flavor. Had the scallion pancakes which are thick and crispy that come with a nice vinegary soy sauce. My gf loves the bean curd with garlic sauce. Wok 88 is a true gem on the upper east.

Worst hot pot experience ever. I've been here a couple of times before but never had any issues before. I came in on a Thursday at around 6:45 hoping to use my Pulsd deal for two. They said we would be seated 8:30 to 9, and that next time, we should try making a reservation (Spoiler - there isn't going to be a next time). I tried explaining to them that I had actually called a few weeks ago, trying to reserve for two, but someone had told me that reservations are for four people and up and that I could just walk in if it's only two people. The hostess proceeded to tell me that they do accept reservations for two people. OK fine, I wasn't going to stand there and argue with her because it was too late at that point anyway. She said our other option was to call and complain to Pulsd and try to get our money back, so I'm guessing that 99 Favors has a lot of angry Pulsd customers. We decided to wait because our deal was expiring the next day and I didn't want to go through the trouble of calling Pulsd (hint - it would have been less trouble to call Pulsd) I I guess everyone else had the same idea and that's why it was so packed. If you are going to add your business to these deal websites, you really need to figure out how to handle the influx of customers because the place was a shit show. So she added us to the Yelp Waitlist, which by the way they closed on the app so you can't add yourself ahead of time. You have to go to the restaurant, and they will manually add you. She asked if we minded sharing a table and said it would probably quicker if we were willing to share. More lies. We came back at 9, but weren't seated until 9:15. We really just waited three hours for some mediocre hot pot. We ended up sharing a table with two other pairs, and we got the bitch seat, all the way on the inside. It was annoying because we couldn't really get up as we pleased without annoying the other diners. I went to make my sauce and there was a huge line at the sauce station too. They ran out of bowls, which took them a while to get, and they also ran out of some of the sauces. I got the tomato broth that I usually get and it wasn't as good as it used to be. It had a weird ketchup-y taste to it. We got the standard items - sliced beef, sliced lamb, marinated pork, crab, shrimp, tofu, beef balls, fish balls (they were also out of some of the menu items too). The food is your typical hot pot fare, so no complaints there (except for the out of stock items). There was also a seafood pancake, so that was nice that you can order it as a part of hot pot. But it was this whole ordeal we had to go through that has made me sure that I will never return to this place. Hot pot is supposed to be fun and relaxing. This was a very stressful experience. In hindsight, I should have just forfeited the Pulsd deal.

Went here with a group of people on a weekday evening. We came before rush hour, so it was completely empty, but then more people starting showing up around 5:30. It was regular Italian food, nothing special. The wine was cheap quality, entrees were good, dessert was okay. Nothing out of the ballpark, but nothing terrible. Service was decent too.

I visited this restaurant for the first time during lunch and was pleased to find it wasn't crowded. I opted for the leg and thigh, accompanied by broccoli and mac n cheese as sides. The chicken impressed me with its juiciness and flavor, holding its own even without the need for additional sauce; however, their hot sauce was a delightful complement. The broccoli, while slightly charred, was a minor letdown due to its small serving size. The mac n cheese, on the other hand, was quite satisfying. The meal was rounded out with crisp pickles and a side of toasted cornbread, making it a solid value overall.

Everything I had from here was of top quality. And the taste was excellent. Gaucamole seems to be a very popular item here. I went with the frutas option. Gaucamole was very fresh. It had fresh pomegranate and mango in it. Combination of gaucamole and fruits is very good. Salsa which came with it was also really fresh. I am pretty sure they made it there. Chips was good too. Breakfast burrito had excellent flavors. If you go for brunch I highly recommend this item. I also went for chapulines which is nothing but grasshopper taco. Grasshoppers were fried crispy. The taste is very different from a regular taco. It has some grass kind of a flavor to it is what I felt. For a first timer you may not like it much. Overall this is an excellent restaurant. The best Mexican food I ever had.

3.5 starExpected to be quite overpriced since that's how the brand is. Llama brand is know for creativity on their flavor and sauce heavily used, meaning the ceviche doesn't have to be the freshest. We tried the Scallop Ceviche $22 and Hamachi Tiradito $24- both are delicious in the sauce/soup-like. Both are enjoyable since the flavor were on point. Just that can tell it's not the freshest raw seafood though. Given the price it was not okay. Aged Duck Nigiri - 4 little piece for $26. Unfortunately it was a very boring dish and since the duck is so mini, barely could tell what I was eating beside the rice. We shared the Short Rib entree $32 which was absolutely delicious! It has strong charcoal smoked flavor and rim surround. Served lukewarm but the flavor and texture was great.  Glad we finished with a great one. Dessert - banana miso semifreddo, where's the miso?? Tried 5 cocktails as well, not bad but little too sweet on most of them. We sat at the bar, two bartenders only it was quite slow but the bartender was super friendly and sweet and professional. The host on the contrary not so friendly.

I liked Yves a lot - it reminds me of a slightly more grown-up (and hometown) version of Maison Kayser. I came here for brunch so I can't speak to the dinner but the food was pretty tremendous. Let's just say if you can't get a table at Locanda Verde, Yves is by no means a consolation prize. Y'all know how much I can never pass up granola on a brunch menu. The version at Yves' was something I'll definitely try to replicate in my own kitchen with the addition of one unique ingredient, rhubarb! It lent a sweetness that went really well with the strawberry and honey. My group's dishes were all delicious too, I tried each one and I couldn't pick a favorite. You can't go wrong. The seasonal quiche with gruyere probably stood out the most: know that for $17, you are getting your money's worth with an enormous slice and a perfect, flaky bottom. Also liked the croque madame and the blueberry pancakes that the waitress offered with vanilla ice cream. We were all still feeling an enormous meal the night before but if I had come back in an hungrier mode, there were more than a few appetizers I had my eye on (the boursin and the Arctic char tartine).

I was in the middle of a great NY trip filled with sightseeing, food, pizza, and desserts.  I was craving something healthier and wanted a big fresh salad.  I found a delicious salad here!!  The Greek Salad was perfect-fresh chopped romaine, cucumbers, tomatoes, olives and two dolmas.  I added chicken, which was perfectly seasoned and cooked.  The vinaigrette was on the side.  It was served with fluffy pita bread.  The service was great and so was the price.  Perfect lunch!!

Title: A Morning Delight at Yin Ji Chang Fen

Having heard the buzz around Yin Ji Chang Fen's rice rolls, I was eager to try them out but deterred by the notorious long lines. My patience paid off when an early Saturday errand run led us to the restaurant at 10:30 AM, with only a short ten-minute wait in line — a rarity at this popular spot.

In our hungry eagerness, we may have over-ordered for two. A word to the wise: the portions here are generous! Starting with the Sticky Rice Wrap, I was pleasantly surprised. As someone who's typically not a fan, Yin Ji Chang Fen's version won me over, outshining many dim sum establishments. The sizable serving meant sharing was a strategic move.

The Marinated Beef with Shrimp and Chives Rice Roll was a standout, combining two proteins you'd normally have to choose between at a dim sum place. The rice roll was expertly crafted — thin, yet sturdy enough to envelop the flavorful filling.

I took a chance on the Sweet Corn Rice Noodle Roll, adding an egg for an extra dollar. Although the egg addition is usually a no-brainer, it somewhat overpowered the dish, and the use of canned corn detracted from the freshness I'd hoped for. It was more than I could finish, especially since my fiancé isn't a corn enthusiast.

The Sliced Pork, Liver, & Kidney Congee was a hearty affair, with a portion size ample enough for two or three people. Laden with quality ingredients, it's a must-try for congee lovers but comes with a generous topping of cilantro, so be sure to request otherwise if that's not your cup of tea.

Intrigued by other menu items like the fish slices with chives rice roll, I'm open to a return visit, but only with minimal wait times. Although I'm not keen on early mornings or long lines in Chinatown, I will consider a revisit when the hype settles. For those less adverse to a bit of a wait, Yin Ji Chang Fen is certainly worth a try for its quality and ample portions.

Definitely worse than the original NYC location, mainly based on service time - the taste and quality are pretty standard. Not very authentic experience (I have been to Ikinari in Japan for comparison as well).The main issue is the service - extremely slow, roughly 30 minutes until my steak was delivered, whereas my past experiences at the East Village and Tokyo locations were basically instantaneous (even with a packed room). What was worse was we were the second set of people to order and the entire restaurant was pretty empty the entire lunch hour, which probably reflects the same issues we experienced ourselves.I am a ribeye or top ribeye kind of girl, so that's always what I order. Sad that the garlic fried rice isn't sold during lunch. Also, the steak sauce was way too soy saucy/salty, so definitely opt for extra garlic / garlic butter when you order (which was also forgotten. Had to ask again later).

Enjoyed my time here. The drinks are made by mixologists which means they're not your typical bartenders their knowledge in craft is extravagant and if they can't make you a drink to make you happy then you probably don't know what a drink is! We were lucky enough to get Ella who was an amazing mixologist and we will be back for her expertise

Title: A Tale of Two Experiences at a Split-Service Eatery

I had the opportunity to dine at a unique restaurant recently, where the establishment is clearly divided into two distinct sections. Upon entering, customers are greeted with a deli-style front area offering a tempting selection of sandwiches, pastries, bread, salads, and a variety of drinks from the cooler. Though convenient for a quick grab-and-go, there's a catch: items purchased here can't be enjoyed in the comfort of the dining area, a policy relayed to me by a friend prior to my visit.

Moving past the register to the dining area, the environment shifted to that of a traditional sit-down experience. The menu item I sampled was a croque monsieur, which sadly didn't live up to expectations. While the concept was there, the execution resulted in a soggy sandwich, save for the crust edges. The accompanying side salad, though fresh, required an additional request for more dressing to enhance its faintly dressed leaves.

Service began on a high note with an attentive waiter; however, mid-meal, a switch to a new waitress led to a noticeable decline in attention. For a lengthy 45 minutes, our table seemed to be out of sight and out of mind, causing us to accidentally forgo our after-lunch coffee and dessert plans. When we were ready to depart, it took effort to flag someone down for the check, which revealed our originally responsive waiter had been replaced by the now absent waitress.

Despite the service hiccup and a less than stellar sandwich, the overall atmosphere and quality of food were enough to pique my interest in a second visit. In summary, the restaurant presents a decent dining experience that, with a bit of fine-tuning, has the potential to shine.

Every time I am in the city, I have to get my Schnippers. So yesterday was no exception. I had been out drinking all night to celebrate St Patricks day and a promotion at work. Sunday morning was one of those mornings when you wake up in your hungover state of mind and you need one of those amazing hangover cures known as a big giant burger. So I came in after waking up somewhere around 4pm on Sunday morning and fumbled down the street. Looking for a burger I fumbled by shake shack and decided it was too darn cold. Then it came to me that I had not made my way into Schnippers in about a month. So now I had to go in and get down to Business. I got in and was greeted by the most friendly staff at the register. She took my order of a bacon cheese burger and fries. I found the perfect seat by the window and waited for the food to come out. There were a lot of people in due to St Patricks day, so I knew there would be a wait. The food came out and the burger was actually missing the bacon which was ok! It was super busy. So I politely walked up, and told them. We all had a good laugh about it and they got us the bacon and put it onto our burger which was a super simple mistake when its busy and an easy fix. When I bit into the burger, it was amazing. Everything I had hoped for. I left feeling recharged, cured of my hangover and amazingly happy after all  of that. I was so glad that they took such good care of me despite being super busy. I will be back for more. of these amazing burgers and fries! Good times!

Title: "City Pizza: A Triumph in Burrata Brilliance"

I recently made the delightful discovery of City Pizza and couldn't resist trying their much-talked-about burrata pizza. Upon arrival, I was greeted by slices that looked lifted straight from a food lover's dream; particularly noteworthy were the bruschetta burrata slice and a classic cheese burrata option. Each generously topped with a whole burrata that was as fresh as it was creamy. 

The square slices boast a focaccia-like crust, providing a perfect, pillowy counterpoint to the indulgent topping. I opted for the bruschetta slice, slightly warmed, to savor the cool creaminess of the burrata - though I'm confident a fully heated slice would yield an equally tantalizing melted cheese experience.

City Pizza's burrata slice transcends the ordinary; this is not a mere one-time indulgence but a culinary highlight that beckons for repeat visits. While I've yet to explore their other offerings, the promise of future tastings is alluring.

The venue itself matches the quality of the food, with ample seating in a clean, contemporary setting. City Pizza is not just a meal; it's a repeat destination for anyone seeking a sublime pizza experience.

Title: A Unique Thai Experience with a Few Misses

My evening at this restaurant was certainly not your run-of-the-mill Thai dining affair. The ambiance was cozy and welcoming, setting the stage for an adventurous culinary journey beyond the usual suspects like pad Thai and drunken noodles.

While I appreciated the originality on offer, the meal didn't quite hit the mark for me to warrant a return visit. That said, I was pleasantly surprised by the value of their mix-and-match deal – two distinctive dishes for $22 is a steal. Sampling a wider palette for just $11 per dish is a commendable option for the curious taste buds.

The standout of my meal was, without a doubt, the Thai tea – it's a must-try and the best I've ever had. Also, the dessert was a delightful surprise; warm longan fruit with sticky rice was both comforting and scrumptious.

As for the mains, they didn't quite live up to the same standard; each entree had something just a bit off. The crab meat Tom was overwhelmingly spicy. The shrimp and calamari in the Tom yum soup tilted too far on the sour side. The whole fish was great, but the fried Japanese pumpkin was inconsistent, with some hard chunks distracting from the texture. The red rice, however, was a solid choice.

In sum, if you're after a different take on Thai cuisine and enjoy pushing your palate's boundaries, you might find this spot worth a try – at least for the tea, dessert, and the experience of something new.

The pepperoni Sicilian is a good slice. When I went to Prince Street Pizza this afternoon the line wasn't that long- about 15 minutes. I ordered the slice that's been all over Instagram and wasn't disappointed. Ordered:Pepperoni Sicilian ($5)- a thick Sicilian slice with fresh mozzarella and curled pepperoni cups. It was greasier than other slices I've had but the flavor was good. Even though there's often a line, they move quickly. I asked for tap water and they said they only sell bottled water. That's a little annoying but oh well. I'm glad I tried Prince Street Pizza. I enjoyed it but I don't think I'll be back.

Located in the heart of Chelsea, this lively restaurant is easily accessible, nestled within walking distance to the convenience of various bus stops, the blue line, and the L train. Upon stepping in, one is immediately greeted by the warm, inviting atmosphere, complemented by friendly staff and a clientele that's equally amiable and spirited. The ambiance is further enhanced by the selection of music, often inspiring patrons to join in with a sing-along or even some impromptu dancing.

The food here is decent, offering the expected fares at prices that are slightly elevated, which is not unusual for the area. Although the portion sizes might not match the cost, the quality is sufficiently satisfying for a post-drinks or late-night craving. While it may not be my top pick for a taco joint, the combination of a delightful interior and the convenience of late-night hours makes it a solid choice for those looking for a lively spot to wind down the evening.

Title: A Falafel to Remember

If you're on the hunt for fresh and tantalizing Mediterranean flavors, look no further than this unassuming gem of a spot. While our food tour only allowed for a taste of their renowned falafel, the experience left a lasting impression. The falafel was a delightful surprise, finely crafted with a perfect balance – flavorful, lightly fried with a crisp exterior, and a moist, smooth interior. The bright green hue hinted at the freshness, and each bite packed a punch that more than satisfied the palate. The tahini sauce complemented it perfectly, enhancing the overall experience. In summary, for falafel aficionados and novices alike, this place sets the standard. Don't let the humble facade fool you, the magic is on the plate.

Highly recommend making a reservation in advance, especially if coming on a weekend, otherwise expect a 1-2 hour wait. The ambiance doesn't disappoint. Extremely instagram-able. Service was good as well. As far as food, it was surprisingly delicious! I guess I made the assumption given the amazing ambiance and the fact it's part of a furniture store, they could get away with mediocre food. However, I will say that the food is pricey. Ordered the artisanal prosciutto. This was mediocre for me, especially for the price. Prosciutto pieces were huge, but the "seasonal fruit" was just a small thing of grapes. I think it should also come with a spread of some sort because it's pretty dry with the bread. Also ordered the kale caesar. Really tasty, but there wasn't any kale which was odd. Perfect sharing size for 3 people. My entree was the burger. It comes with 2 patties and crispy fries. Really delicious! Friends ordered the ribeye sandwich and roasted chicken which they both enjoyed. Overall, I think this place is worth trying for the ambiance alone and would be great for a girls brunch or celebration. I don't think it's worth a 1-2 hour wait so definitely make a reservation. Another side note, they don't have cocktails just wine and champagne which I think is a big miss.

Came here for dinner on a Saturday night. There was a 30-45 min wait for a table for two. Since moving here I've definitely had to adjust to getting less space BUT I really felt like there was no space in this restaurant. It was difficult for people to get into the booth and you're basically sharing a table with people on either side.For the food, we started off with bruschetta which was quite fresh! For dinner we got the beet root ravioli and the gnocchi with truffle flakes. FYI it's an additional fee to get truffles. Both the entrees were fine but with so many other Italian restaurant options I don't know that I'd specifically return to this restaurant.

This is just the same as their store name, very little kitchen, they only have today of 4 tables, that can fit total of 10 guests at once. Their dinner prefix menu includes 1 appetizer, 1 main course, and 1 dessert, cost around $19 plus tip and tax. You can use Crave app from iPhone App Store to receive a 20% off from your bill, good deal. Food overall was acceptable and around average, it's more like Americanized Thai food, but portion and pricing are very friendly. They only have 1 person cook in the back and 1 server, and service wasn't bad. Parking around there during day time is hard, you will have to park few blocks away or pay $4 per hour on meter until 7pm. Unless you use 20% off to try, otherwise, would suggest to try other real Thai restaurants. But overall it's a nice new place to try out.

los tacos no. 1 is located inside chelsea market and can be hidden, we missed it our first time walking through. we came on a monday at around 3 pm and luckily there was no wait and no line. after reading so many reviews and popular spots to eat in chelsea market, we came for the tacos.food - i got the carne asada and pollo asado. i wanted the adobada tacos but i didnt think i could eat three.carne asada - this was DELICIOUS. perfect with a corn tortilla. i wish i knew you could get a cheese shell or else i wouldve loved it even more and the spice level would have gone down. extremely tender and juicy meat. pollo asado - this was a bit spicier to me. for someone who is not able to handle spice at all, i was able to finish it, but it did burn a bit. i got it with onions, cilantro guac and salsa. got to do it all if youre getting a taco!once you get your food, you can get salsa and lime or whatever else you need. after you order, it is hard to find a spot to sit which is why it is only a 4/5 because it is super crowded after you grab your plate and napkins. overall - delicious for a east coast taco, but LA and SD does it best. it's the best as far as it goes for new york, but if you are in the west coast, they do it best.

I recently visited Nish Nush based on glowing recommendations and was pleased to find it conveniently located just a stone's throw from where I spent my evening. Opting for a light meal, I sampled the side of falafel, which featured a trio of flavors with two pieces each – all delectable. Alongside, the crispy cauliflower was a delight. The staff's warmth and friendliness added to the experience. I'm eager to return for the full falafel platter when my appetite allows. Highly recommend for a tasty, casual bite.

Soothing and delicious bowl of pho. $9.75 for extra large bowl of pho with everything (#1). Portion was generous and I was able to make 2 meals out of this bowl. Wait staff were friendly and food came out quick. No wait on a Saturday nigh. Cash only

I recently visited a vegan eatery that truly turned my skepticism about plant-based cuisine on its head. The menu is designed with sharing in mind. The Cheese Crostini, a great opener, was delightfully creamy and indulgent. Though it initially comes with two pieces, we added an extra for our trio, which the kitchen accommodated seamlessly.

The beet hummus followed, accompanied by crisp, fresh root vegetables - a perfect blend of earthy flavors and crunchy textures. The grilled wild mushrooms packed a savory punch, though I found them slightly on the salty side for my taste. The standout, however, was the eggplant dish. It boasted a perfect contrast between the crispy exterior and the tender heart, all topped with a swoon-worthy baba ganoush purée.

Despite the seemingly light fare, we were satisfyingly full at the end, reflecting the richness of the dishes served. This spot is now firmly on my map for its delectable takes on vegan cuisine.

Title: A Slurp-worthy Experience at Kurume-style Ramen Spot

I had the pleasure of indulging in some traditional Kurume style ramen recently, and I must say, it was nothing short of delicious. The tonkotsu broth's rich and creamy consistency was the star of the show – a testament to their unique "yobimodoshi" method. The thin noodles complemented the broth beautifully, while the perfectly cooked soft boiled egg was a delightful addition.

Although the skewers were quite good, they didn't quite distinguish themselves from other yakitori offerings across New York City. The decor of the restaurant was modern and inviting, which was matched by their excellent service.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit, with the spicy tomato ramen at the top of my must-try list.

THEY SEE ME ROLLN; THEY HATINI wasn't expecting much when my roommate dragged me here when I wanted to go to Arby's but I was pleasantly surprised! The guys behind the counter were super friendly and offered us some Tim Tams in honor of Australia Day if we ordered with an accent.I tried the spicy salmon and shrimp rolls which were good but the cheeseburger rolls were my favorite! The Big Mac/sushi fusion was unexpectedly delicious and I ended up eating 3. For the price ($3.50-$4.00 per roll) this place is seriously worth a try!

Title: A Fresh and Satisfying Culinary Experience

I recently dined at a delightful eatery that managed to impress with its culinary creations, starting with the salad—truly one of the best I've had for lunch. It featured a harmonious blend of flavors, a perfect dressing-to-greens ratio, and a texture that made every bite a pleasure.

Although I can't recall the salad's name, the photos I snapped serve as a testament to its appeal. Beyond the greens, we enjoyed a serving of brussel sprouts as an appetizer. While tasty, I found the portion size a touch disappointing.

The ambiance hits the sweet spot between casual and upscale, making it suitable for both a relaxed lunch and a more formal dinner. Our server was the cherry on top; his attentive service and insightful menu recommendations enhanced our experience.

Seating in the front part of the restaurant is a treat, with abundant sunlight and open windows inviting a gentle breeze. Overall, I wholeheartedly recommend this spot for a delightful meal that won't disappoint.

My partner and I visited this restaurant for a belated Valentine's Day celebration and our experience was mixed. We chose the combination D with a Cajun twist, along with fresh scallops in garlic and scallions, cucumber with garlic, and Dan Dan noodles. The dishes were satisfactory, but not exceptional.

Unfortunately, the staff's aggressive sales tactics detracted from our dining experience. When we first arrived, we took turns using the restroom, during which the waiters persistently tried to upsell their fresh seafood to each of us separately. Even after indicating a preference to wait for my boyfriend's return to order collectively, the waiter hovered nearby, pressuring us to order more than we needed.

While the food was decent, the total bill amounted to $162 with tip, which felt steep for the Chinatown area, especially for a seafood boil that didn't quite live up to those at competing venues. Though we would consider returning to try the regular seafood dishes in a larger group setting, this visit left us considering our options elsewhere.

I am giving this restaurant the highest rating I can. I wish I could give it a higher rating. When you first walk into the restaurant you are immediately greeted by the sense of fun and lightheartedness. Do not let that fool you the food at this restaurant is hardcore.  When you are first seated you are greeted with a taste of the house sake. I am not a traditional sake fan and found the house sake to be absolutely delicious.We were encouraged to start our evening with the tuna sushi slightly seared with a mango chutney, it was over the moon delicious. Then a plate of cheesy corn. Just like you read, it's a plate of gooey gooey delicious sweet corn with cheese that you cannot stop eating until the plate is clean.We also enjoyed the Bao Bun with chicken, and chicken wings and Chicken Karrage. We look forward to going back for their curry and their short ribs.One of the interesting things we found to do was to participate in their bottle keep menu. You purchase your own bottle of Shochu, a light Japanese distilled beverage and decorate the bottle with stickers and markers anyway you want, I suggest going all out. They will keep your bottle for you for when you return.We will return.  Our bottle is waiting for us.

I recently tried the bacon avocado sandwich for lunch at this spot and came away feeling underwhelmed. While the food presentation was charming and the mint-infused water was a delightful touch, the sandwich itself lacked that 'wow' factor. It was simply okay—edible, but not particularly memorable. A bit more effort and flavor could have made a big difference.

Been here quite a few times for the lunch special. 90% of the time when I go the place is basically empty and it's amazing to just relax when I'm on my lunch break.Food is really good. Not amazing but good nothing I've had on the lunch menu has been amazing. I came once for lunch with co-workers when the lunch special wasn't going on and we got the chicken Marsala and some pasta with mushrooms and truffle oil and both were amazing!!If your looking for cheap and good lunch is for you but if you want to pay a bit more for better food come for dinner.

Tucked into the quaint streets of the Upper East Side, I found a charming breakfast spot. The plate before me was a classic: eggs, bacon, hash browns, and a biscuit. While the biscuit was on the dryer side, the portion of bacon generously made up for it. The best part? All this breakfast goodness came at a steal for just $8.95. If you're looking for a hearty morning meal without breaking the bank, this cute little place might just be your next go-to spot.

So sad I heard this restaurant is closing as it is one of the most delicious places in the country (maybe world) for vegan food. I was lucky to be in NYC recently to go before it closes. I got the wild mushroom crepe and it was phenomenal. It was stuffed with so much more than mushrooms and also had butternut squash, spinach, tempeh, chick peas and more inside. The garlic truffle aioli on top was the best sauce I have ever had. It had the perfect about of garlic and truffle and completed the crepe perfectly. It came with a beet and fennel salad on the side. I am not the biggest fan of beet or fennel but even the salad was absolutely delicious.  They also serve a bit sized starter which was this delicious cornbread bite. The restaurant is definitely on the pricey side but prices are completely understandable given quality of food. Still I would have loved to have had an appetizer or dessert but just got an entree due to the price. Would definitely recommend going to this restaurant before it closes and hoping it finds a way to stay open.

Title: Fresh Sashimi Oasis Worth the Journey

My recent dinner at this hidden gem proved to be a delightful experience. The sashimi was exceptionally fresh, pairing beautifully with their selection of sake. Although the location may be off the beaten path, it's a culinary excursion worth making—especially for their lunch specials, which are rumored to be both delicious and economical. Don't miss out on the grilled yellowtail appetizer; it's a perfect start. The sashimi combo is a must-try, offering a freshness that is sure to please any seafood aficionado. Highly recommended for a satisfying Japanese dining adventure.

I'm always down to find a new ramen place and Camellia was only open for a few weeks when I stumbled upon it! It certainly is an interesting combo of foods & flavors but I kept it simple: Stewed Pork Spare Ribs Ramen with matcha noodles and some gelato at the end.There are 7 kinds of noodles you can choose from. I really liked the consistency of the matcha noodles. The pork was really good, bested only by the soft boiled eggs. And who'd-a thunk that bok choy would be so good in ramen?Food came out fast and on the way out we got our complimentary (as of this post) gelato. Also be sure to see if there are any additional Yelp check-in perks!

Title: A Gluten-Free Haven with Exceptional Service

My experience at this restaurant was nothing short of spectacular, particularly for those with gluten sensitivities. As we entered the bustling space an hour before our show, the hostess deftly accommodated us at the bar with menus and swiftly took our orders to ensure a leisurely dining experience. Her thoughtfulness shone through as she seated us at a spacious four-seater table.

The culinary highlight was the gluten-free gnocchi smothered in a rich bolognese—the best dish I savored during my entire four-day NYC trip, outshining even the city's top Italian eateries. It was tender and delectable, perfectly complemented by a robust and well-spiced marinara atop the gluten-free ravioli.

My boyfriend's old fashioned cocktail was a hit, too, developing a deeper complexity the longer it sat. Impressively, the service was quick; our glasses were never empty and our needs were silently anticipated.

For those with gluten allergies or anyone who appreciates impeccable service and divine Italian cuisine, this restaurant comes highly recommended.

First attempt to come. It was closed for a private party. 2nd attempt we really trying to eat here due to friends recommendations. Got in, not busy.Interior was nice, nice ambiance. Service was ok, what I remember, we were ordering items we thought were good. You know we Asian so we gotta get the papaya salad and some chicken. I ordered the pad see ew which was $42! Lol I literally ordered that for the gram. It was "ok" not worth $42 though. For the papaya we asked for spicy and the waiter was implying that it was spicy and we were like ok yes, spicy then he would say well I just want you guys to know it's spicy and people have returned it, lol like ok. We want spicy sir. They give a jeow with some sticky rice as a starter which I enjoyed. More then the food itself. The rest of the food was good but not as good as it was hyped up to be. Also the papaya came, and no it wasn't that spicy lolWe finished our food and somehow we talked about our ethnicity and I mentioned I was Laotian. The waiter then mention that the owner like meeting his Laotian customers because a lot of us don't usually come by? He was at a wedding at that time so maybe next time I visit

Okonomiyaki literally translate = how you like + cooked but most importantly is a Japanese savory pancake. Dokodemo is a quaint, casual restaurant. Kind of like a fast casual because they have an assembly line of the sort and offer a lot of classic Japanese food options to eat like ramen, takoyaki, or okonomiyaki.Came here with a friend and was able to enjoy some okonomiyaki. Quite tasty with a lot of toppings and the mix was good. My only comment would probably be to use more egg and make it more pancake-y. There were so many toppings and mix ins that it made it hard for the pancake to not crumble apart. My friend got the takoyaki which was as good as anticipated. Little bits of octopus to munch on but the sauce and flavoring was all there. Great combinations and options for food.I think next time I come, I definitely want to try some of their other dishes like the ramen or the okonomiyaki wrap. Everything was also very affordable and quite filling. Would definitely suggest coming here for something quick and casual.

I recently enjoyed dinner at this revamped eatery on a Tuesday evening with a companion, conveniently situated near my workplace—previously known as LA Tart Flambee. The Thai décor immediately set an inviting and unique ambiance.

Our culinary adventure began with the Thai steamed dumplings, which were an absolute delight, followed by the chicken drunken noodle as our main course. Both offerings were generous in portion, with the drunken noodle delivering a satisfying kick that truly lived up to its "spicy" billing. Freshness and expert seasoning were evident in each bite.

The pricing was reasonable, adding to the overall value of our dining experience. Service was a high point; our server was both efficient and diligent in attending to our needs. The fantastic lunch deal caught my eye—a tempting $9.99 for an appetizer and entree combo—and it's a certainty that I'll be returning to take advantage of it. Highly recommended.

Grabbed a quick bite from Tasty Dumpling while walking around Chinatown. It's similar to many of the hole in the wall dumpling shops in the area, but unlike many others, it has seating.They also serve more than just dumplings. I grabbed an order of dumplings and a sesame pancake with beef. The dumplings were as good as any other in the area, but for $1.50 as opposed to the more common $1 price per order. The pancake was pretty bland, and the beef was dried out. I would stick to the dumplings

Came here tonight to have dinner with my husband. It wasn't planned we randomly went to this spot. Walked in and was seated right away. We ordered everything at once. I ordered a frozen margarita, salmon empanadas and the enchiladas. My husband had the berry mojito, jumbo shrimp, and the angus burger. The drinks took a little long to come which wasn't a big deal at the time. Our appetizers came and they were absolutely delicious. After we ate our appetizers my husband food came and mines didn't. So he waited to eat until I gotten my food. 5 mins, 15 mins 20 mins pass  and no food. I got the attention of waitress just starting her shift and she said it will be out soon. I told my husband to just eat his food at this point. 10 mins pass still no food so I stop the young lady again and she apologized and said it will be out. I explained to her just cancel it she suggested she will have it to go. Another 15 mins pass still no food, at this point I am upset. I told the young lady to just bring the check, the guy who originally took our order came over and said I never ordered enchiladas. I said yes I definitely did, he apologized and said he never put that in and walked away. I was very disappointed in the service we received. No one never checked on us we had to flag ppl down just to put in another drink order. They didn't seem to care that my order was never put in and when it was no one seemed to care to check on it. When we asked for the bill why the enchiladas was on there. Smh... I called the young lady back and she took it off. I don't think it was that busy there for them to treat us like this.

I don't know what Donohue's has such mediocre reviews and a few untruths to boot. After reading some reviews that stated you need reservations, I looked on open table and saw that Donohue's isn't listed there. I googled it, and no where does it say reservations are accepted, although maybe I could have just called and they would have taken them over the phone. We threw caution to the wind and showed up at 8pm on Friday night, and there were a couple of tables available-we were given a booth without asking (of course we wanted the booth). This place is neither a dive or full of old people. It has a diverse crowd, young and old, some people were alone and looked like regulars and some were in groups. The staff was very pleasant, we didn't have to wait long to place our order and our food was out very quickly. (Btw, the reviews in the Wall St Journal are way better).The Food: we ordered simply-We both had the French Onion, which was on par with Balthazar's-it was quite good. I ordered the burger and my companion ordered the turkey club. I would feel comfortable ordering the fish or the steak, but felt like a burger. We loved our food dishes. If your looking for an old school NYC low-key restaurant, this is the place for you. It's been there 50 years or so, so they must be doing something right.

TLDR: we over-ordered for a group of three, so just get the yucca fries, paella to share, a steak dish, and don't forget that mojito, and you'll be good to go!_It's really the little things that matter! I booked this through Opentable, marked it as a birthday celebration, asked for booth seating if available, and they came through with my request! (Which doesn't always happen.) At the end of the meal, when we were too stuffed and rejected the dessert menu, the hostess was confused and asked, "Oh isn't it someone's birthday? We can give you a dessert on the house!" All because they actually took the time to remember guest occasions and to make the experience more memorable for diners. A+ right there! THANK YOU! Service otherwise was also very attentive and friendly, even though the entrees were a little slow to get to us. Yucca fries ($6): the green sauce that came with this was so smooth and good! Love how crispy and delicious the fries are, and was a decent portion for the price.Favela wings ($9): can skip this. It's not spicy wings, it's more like a spaghetti sauce wings, which is nothing to rave about. Red sangria and mojito (happy hour pricing at $8/each): wowwwww the mojito was STRONG! GET IT! Sangria is typical to other restaurants, but still yummy. Seafood paella ($25): favorite of the night! This one, though it doesn't look that big, was actually packed with a very generous amount of seafood. I was expecting a big sizzling plate of paella, but this one is more on the "wet" side, but I really enjoyed the flavors and the overall dish. Since there was quite a bit of rice in here, I would recommend getting this to share; it'll definitely be filling!Ropa vieja ($24): braised pulled skirt steak. The skirt steak itself came in a little honey pot type of plate, so it wasn't a super big portion, and the meat itself was heavy on the salt, but combined with the rice and beans, we polished this easily. Frango ipanema ($19): half rotisserie chicken. This one was a miss for our group. The chicken breast was on the dry side, and it was too heavy on the lemon that it was pretty much all I could taste with each bite.Molten lava cake with vanilla ice cream ($9): the lava cake wasn't super runny when we cut into it, but the sweetness was done right, and made better eating it with the cold ice cream.

Nice, lovely little place. I've been to other Amorino outlets and this one was very nice. Staff were attentive and made a lovely cappuccino. We stopped in for a cappuccino and a macaron while waiting for my daughter. My friend had a pistachio macaron, I had chocolate. The place was delightful except for the ill-behaved little kids whose parents were far too lenient to either get them to behave or remove them.  I have kids, I get it, everyone wants some time out to enjoy themselves, but when your little goblins are ruining it for everyone else, you suck at parenting.I have to give the staff major credit for handling it so well and cleaning up after the hurricane. I wish them an easier new year with lots of pleasant patrons who tip well.So yes, the coffee and the macarons were delightful, the bathroom was clean, and the place was lovely. I'll get gelato next time I'm there.

Tonight my best friend and I were in a hotel room in midtown. He wanted pizza and I didn't feel like walking around in the search for the best pizza in New York so.. My best friend ordered on UberEats. I saw the photos and thought that this company was clearly trying to deceive people. But then the pizzas were herein a quick 20 minutes. I still had very low expectations but in they came. The pizza looks amazing!!! It's hot, fresh, tasty and looks just like the photo on the app. Even better!! I highly recommend getting pizza from This restaurant. I want to order a dozen more!!

An absolute gem--I'm in love with Alta.Sitting unassumingly, but looking gorgeous from the outside, on a tree lined block in Greenwich Village one can easily pass by Alta.Once you step inside, the ambiance will take your breath away. At least it took mine. It was dimly lit and cozy with different seating options across several floors. A true townhouse with a  beautiful vibe that sets the mood for a date (lucky you or me in this case) or dining with friends/family.Service was extremely good as I wouldn't expect it to be otherwise and the waitress was helpful by  answering any/all questions. Alta serves Mediterranean inspired  tapas or small plates and it was recommended at least 2-3 per person.We both got things started with a glass of Rose (mine being the less dry option) which was delicious.As far as food, we stuck to a seafood and chicken theme to accommodate my eating preferences. And once we placed our order, the plates arrived individually (I appreciated that a lot) to savor each and every selection. We ordered:Tuna tartare--5 perfect slices of fresh and delicious tuna garnished with dollops of sauce and greens. Fried goat cheese bites--4 small balls sitting on a coating of honey. Absolutely divine and must try.Scallops--3 pieces nicely grilled and delicious.Paella--one of my favorites. A medley of different seafood that tasted lemony and fresh.Chicken shawarma--pieces of chicken lying on a bed of hummus. Very delicious and nice accompaniment to our mainly seafood selections.Black Cod---a few pieces that was combined with tomato and greens.(Refer to the menu for a more detailed description of each selection).There was not one misstep regarding the meal as everything was excellent and executed very well. The flavors of each plate were amazing but keep in mind, they're not generous portions (nor are they inexpensive). Since they're small plates, the option remains to double up or order more. There was a large variety from the. menu. Your choice. I think it's fun and appreciate making a meal of small plates on occasion. By the way, for $600, Alta will serve the entire menu of plates to your table!Alta is an elegant, well run restaurant that does everything right. You'll leave impressed. I did.

Title: Docks: A Disappointing Experience

We stumbled upon Docks with high hopes drawn by its bustling atmosphere and an intriguing menu. On entry, the vibrant energy suggested we had discovered a hot spot. Unfortunately, this impression was short-lived.

The initial buzz, we soon realized, was the remnants of a happy hour crowd. Once they dispersed, the true nature of Docks emerged—an overpriced establishment living on past glories, offering subpar cuisine. Our dining experience was marred by lackluster service and a noticeable decline in ambiance.

As frequent oyster patrons, we found Docks’ offerings to be a disappointing departure from the quality we've come to expect, especially for a restaurant that purports to have a top-notch raw bar. To our dismay, the raw bar was nothing more than a neglected ice shelf tucked away and a cramped corner at the bar for sushi preparation.

The calamari, a staple in many eateries, was on par with what one might find at a fast-food joint, a surprising find for a restaurant with a three-dollar-sign price point. It was promptly sent back. The deviled eggs managed to be just passable, yet the audacity of a $6 house sparkling water still baffles me.

Our enthusiasm quickly soured to disappointment, prompting an early departure. To salvage the night, we opted for a reliable comfort—fries from Shake Shack—as we reflected on this being the third strike against the sister restaurants group. It may be a while before we consider returning to any of their establishments.

I'm basing my review off of one visit where we ate dessert only.  I have had some pretty bad experiences walking into a restaurant and asking to be seated for dessert only but not here. From the beautiful decor, to the friendly service, to the house made desserts and delicious coffees, I loved everything about L'Adresse. We arrived to a beautiful, modern restaurant. The warm toned wood panels, extra high ceiling and sleek lighting fixtures were modern but cozy at the same time. There is an area at the back just for people that want only coffee, dessert or a drink. You can sit at the bar or the two large communal tables. We chose to sit at the bar (which has bag hooks underneath ladies!). The young women making the coffees and lattes were true artists. It was seriously mesmerizing to watch them make beautiful artwork on each drink. Sitting at the bar was perfect for us because we were able to talk to the girl working there. She recommended the RAF coffee and smetannyk cake (made fresh that morning). Both were amazing! Each and every employee we interacted with was excellent. We will definitely be back to try out their food (and more desserts) very soon.

Title: A Cozy Gem Serving Up Mediterranean Marvels

From the creative minds of the Matthew Kenney Cuisine Team, this NYC establishment is a Mediterranean-inspired haven for food and cocktail enthusiasts. Starting with the hummus - oh, the hummus! It's quite possibly the best I've ever had. The smoked variety is served with a green harissa, a dusting of sumac, and warm, fluffy pita bread. The perfect blend of texture, temperature, and taste, it sets the bar high.

Following this, we delved into the cashew halloumi paired with Za'atar crackers, paprika, black olives, and radish. The cheese stood out, but overall, it was satisfying rather than sensational. However, the green pea and fava falafel definitely deserves a mention. Though I've had better, its uniqueness was notable.

Service here is as impressive as their spread. Prompt and pleasant, our waitress was eager to offer suggestions and insights into the menu, adding a personal touch to our experience.

The atmosphere complements the dining experience beautifully with its rustic chic decor, including a patio and a gentle glow emanating from the fireplace. It's a cozy setup with well-spaced seating and dim lighting, adding to the overall ambiance.

Be prepared to pay a premium, but rest assured, the quality of your meal and experience justifies the price. It's not just a meal; it's an investment in a delightful culinary journey.

Title: Disappointing Experience with the Summer Special at Essex Market

I visited Essex Market with high hopes for their touted Summer special: the Thai Pineapple Chicken. Sadly, my excitement was met with a letdown. The dish's preparation method—frying the chicken beforehand and then refrying upon ordering—resulted in a piece that was misleadingly crunchy on the outside yet disappointingly cold on the inside. While the pineapple served alongside was undeniably fresh, it could not redeem the excessively salty sauce drenching the dish.

Equally underwhelming was their Hainanese Chicken, which was dry to the point of being devoid of flavor. Traditional accompaniment of sweet soy sauce was replaced by an unpalatable thick, fruit-flavored concoction that did no favors to the chicken. Furthermore, the sides of liver and gizzards were overdone and parched.

Regrettably, this stall failed to deliver on its promise, and I’ll be sure to skip it on my next visit to the market.

Food: 3/5Atmosphere: 3/5Service: 3/5Extremely average Japanese restaurant in midtown. I loveee Katsu and was really excited to try this place. The portion was great, but food lacked flavor. I also ordered the beef curry, but the flavor was quite strange. Nothing like the kind of Katsu or curry you find in actual Japan :/Service was also meh. The server was not very friendly and at one point, he was arguing with the customer next to us, causing a scene in the restaurant.

Title: A Blooming Good Time at Amorino Gelato

If delight is in the details, then Amorino Gelato has it nailed with their signature gelato flower cones. Visit this charming spot not just for a dessert but for an experience, as you witness the artful creation of your chosen flavors transformed into a stunning flower right atop a crunchy cone. The menu offers the standard array of gelato and sorbet, with enough chocolate and nut variations to satisfy the traditionalist sweet tooth, though a broader flavor selection would be the cherry on top.

Every bite of their creamy gelato is a testament to quality, although on the day of my visit, I found myself craving a little more adventure in the flavor department. The interior boasts a bright and contemporary décor, effortlessly inviting with its floor-to-ceiling glass doors that beckon you inside.

The staff deserves a round of applause for their patience and friendliness, making sure each customer leaves with a smile as bright as their gelato flower. Amorino Gelato is not just a dessert stop; it's a spot that adds a dash of joy to your day. Two thumbs up for this delightful dessert haven!

Party of two for hot tea, a bowl of fresh fruit and soda which enables a male acquaintance to utilize their facility.  This restaurant is a traditional diner.  The energy does not appear very busy nor positive.  Customer service fends a dissatisfied tone when serving our table possibly because we did not order a full meal with ulterior motives of utilizing their facilities.  Our male server did not disclose what kind of berries were included in the bowl of fruit.  Blackberries, strawberries, blueberries, or raspberries?  "It is mixed berries- just berries!!"  Our server took an eternity to distribute our order and consequently shot us a rude scowl look with cold malice eyes of hostility and extreme strife upon out exit.  Unspeakable atrocity! Egregiously vulgar and menacing.  Insolent! Sinister!  We were full from an earlier meal but we were willing to place food orders at New Amity Restaurant, nevertheless a rude antagonistic and insolent attitude is surely not required nor acceptable in the hospitality field.  Every customer is esteem and important as every order either big or small bill is important.

Just had a very filling delicious lunch here. I've been in the area countless times over the past couple of years trying to get into this place and I've only ever actually gotten in once as there's usually over a 30 min wait. Nice to see they recently joined Yelp waitlist as I'm sure that's definitely helped with the huge amounts of people that frequent this kbbq spot.It is on the 2nd floor and there's a sign when you walk in that a 5th floor location is currently under construction.Ordered the large combination beef platter for 4 people and was happy with the amount of food provided. I would say that compared to some of the other bbq spots adjacent, that Jongro had a few less appetizers and other little table eats to go along with the meat that you order. I really loved the decor on the inside though, it felt like this is probably a super famous restaurant in Korea as even at 12pm when they were opening, it was already packed with plenty of people.

Title: A Mixed Experience During Restaurant Week

I recently dined at this establishment, enticed by the varied pre-fix menu offered for Restaurant Week. The service was competent, facilitating timely ordering. Initially, we were served a modest portion of bread alongside butter and oil, followed by an amuse-bouche of cream truffle soup. Careful though, the soup was served blisteringly hot, overshadowing the subtlety of truffle with its predominantly creamy taste.

The starter, a hearty risotto, sadly fell flat in flavor, though the added walnuts did provide a welcome crunch. Main courses consisted of monkfish and salmon, both adequately sized and served at an appreciable temperature. However, while the fish avoided the trap of dryness, both suffered from under-seasoning, and the accompanying eggplant was notably bland.

Desserts, on the other hand, were the highlight. We indulged in a scrumptious crème brûlée with berries and a delightful pistachio cake with blondo orange compote and honey ice cream – a definitive factor in our restaurant choice.

Despite the lovely ambience, the overall experience didn't warrant a return visit for me. Presently, I'd rate it a fair 3.5 stars, recognizing potential but ultimately left yearning for more culinary excitement.

I recently discovered a hidden gem that has quickly become a must-return spot for me. My boyfriend and I enjoyed a delightful dinner, sharing a range of dishes including a savory Roasted Butternut Squash Bisque, a perfectly roasted Acorn Squash, and an exceptional chicken that the kitchen thoughtfully split for us. Although we indulged in a generous amount of food, we still made room for the Flourless Chocolate Cake, which, while not quite as impressive as the preceding courses, could not dampen the overall positive experience. This culinary win has left me eager to come back for brunch.

I recently dined at a restaurant where the culinary experience was truly memorable. The highlight was indisputably the crab cakes — undoubtedly the best I've had in years, bursting with real crab meat and refreshingly devoid of any fillers. 

Following that, the lamb chops easily matched the high bar set by the appetizer. Despite their reasonable price, they rivaled more expensive cuts I've had elsewhere, both in flavor and succulence. 

The sides did not lag behind in quality. Each — the creamy mac and cheese, crisp asparagus, and the perfectly whipped mashed potatoes — accompanied the main courses without a hitch. 

I'm already looking forward to my next visit to indulge once more in this splendid fare.

Came here on a Thursday night following a show. We had a reservation and got seated right away. It was SO loud in there. I felt like I had to scream across the table to have a conversation. It is a young/lively place. Good cocktails- maybe a little too sweet. Good food- we tried the everything pretzel (must try! It was our favorite), the ahi tuna over seaweed salad (delicious) and the mac and cheese (good but nothing special).  Probably won't be back just due to the noise level.

Excellent food and great service . One of the few that does not offer a buffet but has specials that are a great value and very tasty . We had the goat meat curry on the bone that was delicious and ordered the eggplant special that came with dal as well as vegetables . Definitely recommend .

One gets the feeling that there used to be a lot of cafes like this in the City ... but Veselka is a survivor.  And it's fairly clear why it survived -- the place is crowded & noisy, pretty much all the time (open 24/7, no reservations accepted), yet the service is prompt, the wait staff is courteous, and our coffee mugs & water glasses were refilled regularly.  Oh, and the food ... not the best pierogis I've ever had ... but pretty close!  And if you've never enjoyed a proper blintz, here's your chance!  Reminiscent of a bygone era ... and if you have to wait for a table (and you will, unless it's 3AM), it's totally worth it.

Nothing crazy special about the food, or drinks here. The menu is not extensive at all, which is fine because it means the few things they make are made well here. What is nice about this restaurant is that they offer shaded outdoor seating during the warmer months, and is pet-friendly too so you can bring your pup to brunch with you. It's a solid place to grab a bite to eat and catch up with friends during the warmer months. There was a wait when I arrived at 3pm on a Saturday, and they do not seat incomplete parties.

During our recent NYC trip, my husband and I dined at a local gem we'd been eager to try, making it our inaugural city meal. Despite its cozy size suggesting take-out for larger parties, the restaurant's delectable offerings make the tight squeeze worthwhile. With wallet-friendly prices and a plethora of bubble tea options, the culinary experience far outweighs the one downside: a trendy but unkempt bathroom. Our advice? Visit, but perhaps take a bathroom break beforehand. The flavors are not to be missed.

Title: A New York Dining Gem with Sky-High Views

I recently dined atop one of New York's majestic skyscrapers, and it was nothing short of spectacular. The restaurant's ambiance, with panoramic views of the cityscape, sets the stage for an unforgettable gastronomic journey.

Beginning with the lobster quenelle, I was immediately impressed by the balance of robust flavor and delicate texture – a masterful execution that allowed the lobster to shine. My entrée, the duck, followed suit in excellence, its succulence enhanced by a thoughtful fruit pairing that elevated each bite.

Service throughout the meal was attentive, ensuring a seamless experience from start to finish. Eager to enjoy the daylight views, I look forward to returning for lunch. This restaurant is a must-visit for those seeking a taste of luxury high above the hustle and bustle of the city.

Title: A Scrumptious Delight at an Instagram Favorite

After the social media buzz, my palate finally savored the infamous Mafaldini "Scampi" at this charming spot - and it's a flavor revelation, surpassing even the photogenic hype. Equally impressive was the Tuna Acqua Pazza, a symphony of fresh, balanced flavors with its clever play of cucumber and tomato. Dessert didn't falter; the Budino, crowned with sublime hazelnut gelato, ended the meal on a high note. The ambiance? Cozy and versatile, befitting any dining occasion. And the prices? Surprisingly reasonable for NYC's standards. This restaurant isn't just a feast for the eyes; it's a genuine gastronomic celebration.

Title: A Burger Haven with Service That Shines

Our recent experience at this bustling eatery left us raving about two things: the service and the sweet potato fries. Service was top-notch, thanks to our server Adiana, whose sweet demeanor, menu knowledge, and impeccable politeness elevated our dining experience. Hats off to Adiana – she's a gem who deserves every accolade!

The burgers, while tasty, were deceptively filling. Don't let their appearance fool you; a few bites in, and you'll feel the heft. Both my husband and I, despite skipping meals earlier, couldn't conquer our portions – he tapped out at the halfway mark, and I left my plate with a burger unfinished. The sweet potato fries, however, stole the show; they were spot-on.

We had eyed the shakes for a post-meal treat but were bested by the burger's belly bomb. Next visit, we'll beeline for the desserts instead. The Arnold Palmer was a refreshing companion, striking a perfect balance without being overly sweet.

The estimated wait time of 1.5 hours turned out to be conservative; we were pleasantly surprised to be seated in under an hour. The ambiance hit the right notes – a fun vibe, cool interior, 90's tunes, and exceptionally clean bathrooms.

In sum, fantastic food, impeccable service, and a lively atmosphere make for a crowd-pleaser. We're already planning our next visit – just for dessert!

Title: A Delightful Discovery for #bignightin at Ponche's

In desperate need of a pick-me-up, Ponche's came through with their comforting homemade tortilla chips - a blissful cure for quarantine blues. We indulged in their guacamole and chips to kick off our #bignightin, a choice so satisfying we nearly doubled down on the appetizer alone.

Moving on to the main course, my partner enjoyed a hearty vegetable burrito while I savored the vegetarian enchiladas topped with fresh queso fresco. Both dishes were flavorful and generously portioned, transforming our evening into a filling fiesta.

Stumbling upon Ponche's open for takeout was nothing short of serendipity. Picking up our feast was a breeze and turned an ordinary night in into a delightful dining experience. Don't wait as long as we did to rediscover this gem - Ponche's is ready to make your day with their delicious offerings.

*Smorgasburg review*I'd been to this traditional dim sum / Cantonese seafood restaurant a number of times with my family growing up, so I was VERY surprised to hear that Jing Fong had joined the very hip Smorgasburg in Williamsburg this past spring season. I think I found out through my Instagram Explore tab, where I saw a post of the very classic Ginger & Scallion Lobster Sticky Rice - I just couldn't believe that we'd be able to get this traditional Cantonese dish (that I grew up on!) at this young & hip food market. Last Saturday, 6/29 was the last day Jing Fong would be there, so I wanted to check it out while I still could. Making a trip out to Williamsburg in 100-degree humidity took A LOT more effort than just going to the restaurant in Chinatown, but... I just needed to experience this.On this VERY hot, almost unbreathable day, my boyfriend and I headed straight to their tent once we arrived and ordered the Lobster Sticky Rice for $23.95. THANKFULLY it came with a choice of Jasmine Tea Cold Brew or Chrysanthemum Tea Cold Brew - we sooo needed this, and it totally made the dish (and commute) worth the price. If you didn't want a drink, you had the choice of getting one of the dim sum dishes they offered for free (siu mai, ha gow, etc.) which is a pretty great deal w/ the lobster sticky rice. Not to mention the complimentary stickers too!The lobster sticky rice came in a sizable take-out box and had about 6 pieces of lobster in it. It tasted super authentic and delicious, exactly like how it should be at any local Cantonese seafood restaurant. I was thoroughly impressed that they were able to cook it in a tent and make it taste so good. I just have to reemphasize that it was pretty trippy to be eating this traditional dish on a picnic table in hipsterland. Portion wise, I shared it with my boyfriend so it wasn't enough to make us both full, but that's why you're at Smorgasburg anyway - to try out all the other foods. (We went to Noodle Lane afterwards ugh we're so painfully Chinese if you couldn't already tell: yelp.com/biz/noodle-lane… )All in all, pretty interesting experience and I lowkey hope to see Jing Fong/more traditional Cantonese dishes around at these types of food markets - not just in Chinatown!

After a year-long anticipation, Soho Diner has opened its doors to the delight of food enthusiasts. Situated on the ground floor of the illustrious Soho Grand Hotel, with its entrance greeting guests on West Broadway, this eatery has swiftly captivated a bustling crowd, achieving popularity without the need for advance promotion.

The diner presents a cocktail selection that is nothing short of impressive, indicating that the bartenders are as skilled in mixology as the chefs are in gastronomy. The menu, an inventive take on diner staples, infuses contemporary zest into beloved traditional dishes.

Visually, Soho Diner pays homage to the quintessential American diner experience while elevating it with high-quality materials and meticulous attention to detail, creating a space that is at once familiar and refined.

Functioning around the clock, Soho Diner stands as a welcome addition to the local dining scene, offering patrons a sublime spot to satiate their cravings at any hour. Whether you're a night owl or an early bird, Soho Diner is poised to become a go-to spot for both the nocturnal and the diurnal city dweller.

We walked along Restaurant Row in Midtown looking for a place to have dinner prior to a Broadway show.  The white lights illuminating the outside of Scarlatto caught my eye and we decided to go for it.  We were quickly seated on a Sunday evening around 5:30. I immediately liked the warm, inviting feel of the dining area and service was phenomenal.  Our drinks were filled as needed and we were checked on quite frequently. I ordered the Carne del Giorno (chicken rollatini) from the specials menu.  The chicken was very tender and nicely filled with spinach and roasted peppers and easy on the cheese. The portion size was quite large.  My husband ordered Tagliato Di Manzo (strip steak) for dinner. He felt it was a decent American steak. For dessert, I ordered the chocolate cake, which was on the smaller side, but tasty.  It was my birthday and the waiter had the plate decorated with chocolate along with a candle. As with many of the restaurants around the Theater District, the prices are a bit high for the quality of the food.  You could probably get much better Italian food for a lot less in other parts of the city, but it's the tradeoff you pay for to be near the theaters.  Food: 4Service: 5Price: 3Ambiance: 4

Love this place! Best to go for lunch so you have some elbow room and can hear your group chatting. In the evening its packed inside and outside seating. Outside closes during bad weather it's not covered.Our group had the lunch happy hour goodness and margaritas are delicious peach - nice and light, mango - bit stronger than the peach, watermelon - like a concentrated jolly rancher... hahaha nachos are plenty for a table to share, not enough cheese and the guacamole is out of this world! Chicken wings are good but a little dry and no flavor if you ask for sauce on the side... they do offer ranch or blue cheese on the side that can get you by.The waitresses rock at this place though. Very attentive to our group and kept everything full and functioning on our table the entire time. It was fabulous! Definitely a spot to pop I to if you're in the area.

It was suggested I visit The Champagne Bar at The Plaza Hotel while I was in New York City.  The Champagne Bar is in the lower level lobby. Beautiful setting where we sipped some very expensive glasses of champagne. Larry took care of us providing wonderful service. Upon being seated, se were presented with a trio of dark pistachio chocolate and two different nuts. We decided to have a bite to eat with our champagne and shared a meat platter, cheese platter and tuna tartare.  The tuneup was very fresh served with avocado and micro greens with thin crackers on the side. Both the cheese platter and meat platter had generous portions of four different types of cheeses and four different types of meats.  They were both served with perfectly grilled bread.  The cheese and meat platters were certainly worth the money charged. The champagne was $30+ a glass and was a little too pricey seeing what a bottle of Vueve Cliquot Rose costs. When all was said and done, the cost of two glasses of champagne along with the cheese, meat and tuna dishes was $200. Of course, you're paying for the ambience and experience, and I enjoyed every minute of it!  If I ever get to New York again, I would love to do high tea at The Plaza.

Title: A Delightful Encounter with Authentic Flavors

I recently dined at this charming establishment that immediately impressed me with its well-crafted ambiance. From the moment we walked in on a quiet weeknight, we were greeted with the convenience of being seated promptly by the entrance.

The star of our meal was undoubtedly the Big Plate Chicken. A harmonious blend of hand-pulled noodles, seamlessly mingled with a symphony of sauces, achieved the perfect texture – chewy but not tough. The chicken itself was succulent, absorbing every bit of the flavorful sauce, accompanied by potatoes that complemented the dish with a light spice and saltiness that urged you to savor every bite.

While the fried rice cakes offered a unique twist to traditional Chinese fare, they were slightly more al dente than preferred, yet they didn't skimp on taste. A duo of appetizers, featuring eggplant and potato, was a succulent prelude that stimulated our palates.

I would wholeheartedly recommend this culinary gem but suggest coming in a group. The dishes, rich in both carbs and flavors, beg to be shared. A visit here is a chance to indulge in a spectrum of gastronomic delights that are too good to enjoy alone.

If you find yourself near Chinatown or the Brooklyn Bridge with a pizza craving, this spot is a must-visit. The margherita and mama's vodka pizzas were both fantastic choices, bursting with flavor. I'm already looking forward to my next visit when I'm back in the area. Highly recommended!

Title: A Joyful Dumpling Experience at Mandoo Bar

If there's a name synonymous with exquisite dumplings in Korea Town, it's Mandoo Bar. Having been a patron since 2010, I was thrilled to see this gem bounce back from its 2019 closure due to a fire. Mandoo Bar remains a personal go-to for authentic Korean dumplings, with their Mool Mandoo (boiled dumplings) and Goon Mandoo (lightly fried dumplings) stuffed with pork and vegetables leading the pack. The variety caters to all, offering equally delectable vegetable versions for non-meat eaters.

Prices are reasonable, ranging from $6 to $16, which means indulgence without breaking the bank. My usual order? The crispy Goon Mandoo coupled with the sizzling Bulgogi Dolsot Bibimbap - a harmony of flavors and textures not to be missed.

The staff here adds to the experience: they're not just friendly, but impressively attentive and swift, ensuring a smooth visit. With minimal wait times for small groups, and a dumpling-making spectacle to entertain you if a queue does form, Mandoo Bar is definitely a culinary highlight worth visiting for dumpling enthusiasts and Korean cuisine lovers alike.

Title: Mixed Experiences at Spiegel's Brunch

My anticipation for a savory Mediterranean brunch led me to Spiegel, where the allure of Jewish cuisine options piqued my culinary curiosity. Despite the dreary weather dampening our day, the vibrant atmosphere of the restaurant upon arrival was a welcome change. However, the cramped corner seating and a table barely large enough for our drinks and menus posed an immediate challenge.

The breakfast platter had been the main draw for me, but a curt clarification from the waitress that it was unavailable until after 11 left me scrambling for an alternative. I settled on the breakfast hummus with shakshuka, which turned out to be quite lackluster, except for the satisfyingly warm bread. The cauliflower side dish was disappointingly bland, lacking any notable flavor or texture. On a brighter note, my husband's chicken schnitzel sandwich was a hit, quickly consumed and thoroughly enjoyed.

Patience was tested with slow service, despite a visibly staffed space. The single bathroom situation was less than convenient, further complicated by delivery personnel bypassing the queue. While the prices were reasonable and the location favorable, the overall experience fell short of expectations. Given the combination of service, space, and culinary misses, I'm hesitant to plan a return visit to Spiegel.
