Roasted duck + kale salad for $60. Such a great deal! It is my first time eating beatrice's food and I have to say I am very very impressed.Everything I got from Beatrice tastes amazing. The duck is definitely the highlight. It is so juicy and tender inside and has so crispy skin. The sauce is very flavorful and a bit sweet because of cherry. The portion is also more than enough for two people. Finally, the little handwritten card from Angie makes my heart melt. She is writing a card for every customer during COVID time. It is great to know that the restaurant owner actually cares about her customers!

Totally delicious! I don't think there is a dish here that wouldn't be yummy. I was here with a groupAnd loved everything about it- from the lights to the bottles of wine to the seating! So cozy. But not too intimate. I was at a work dinner with my colleagues and it was very relaxing. I had a great salad with avocado and delicious heirloom tomatoes. My pasta dish (I never have pasta mind u) was out of this world- frutte de mare! So delicious paired with a yummy red wine. I love that it is attached to the Kimpton Hotel somif you want to play chess or take out a bicycle you can! This is such a special night out in my book! Waiters are very knowledgeable as well!

Title: A Tasty Bento Lunch with Upscale Vibes

I recently stopped by for a lunch break and decided to try the bento box special. The meal began with a warming miso soup which set the stage for an array of flavors to come. Accompanying the soup were sides of tangy kimchi, fluffy rice, fresh veggies, and a crisp salad, providing a well-rounded meal. For the protein, I opted for the spicy chicken thighs, which were succulent and well-seasoned, though they required some extra grill-time - monopolizing my side of the grill to cook them all at once.

While the prices were slightly higher than average, the upscale ambiance and food quality justified the cost. The dishes were all delectable and the experience was enhanced by the pleasure of a sit-down meal in congenial company. Unfortunately, service faltered at the meal's end; it became a challenge to get the attention of our server for the check as we were pressed for time to return to work.

On a final note, I recommend a stroll down the hallway to the bathrooms. There, you'll be treated to impressive murals, and find the restrooms themselves to be exceptionally clean and stylish—quite the noteworthy aspect, though not the main allure of this dining establishment.

Dined at this gem with colleagues for dinner and we were collectively impressed by the cuisine, particularly the standout original lobster roll. The service was exceptional – a fantastic experience all around! Highly recommend for an enjoyable meal.

Having not dined here since a happy hour visit a decade ago, my anticipation was high, particularly for the Japanese wagyu touted in a recent article. The experience did not disappoint. The seared chuck flap, lavishly adorned with salmon roe and a decadent uni sauce, started the meal on a high note. The chicken tsukune offered a comforting teriyaki embrace, while the marinated eggplant provided a refreshing counterpoint.

The centerpiece, a wagyu beef tasting featuring skirt, short rib, and chuck flap, was a culinary performance with the cooking done tableside. Each cut was a revelation in its own right, their marbling yielding a delicate tenderness and juicy flavor. It's clear that the beef's quality is uncompromising.

However, be prepared to pay for the privilege – while exquisite, the portions are not designed for the ravenous, and a full belly might require a liberal ordering hand. Price aside, the flavors delivered and my palate left satiated. Delicious indeed.

I recently dined at a restaurant that boasts a comprehensive gluten-free menu, a feat I find rather impressive, especially considering they offer gluten-free fried chicken. The food was decent—nothing extraordinary, but the ability to convert nearly their entire menu to gluten-free options is commendable.

I opted for the standard burger and salad, which came highly recommended by the bartender. While it was satisfactory, it didn't quite live up to the enthusiastic praise. Price-wise, expect to pay a bit more, though it seems to align with the going rates in the area.

The staff deserves a shoutout for their excellent service, contributing to a pleasant dining experience. Also noteworthy is the full bar, an inviting option for those seeking a drink with their meal. In summary, this spot is a solid choice, especially for those on the hunt for gluten-free dining.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Sushi Aficionados

Inspired by Pete Wells' glowing review, I ventured to this understated sushi spot, only to find it surprisingly accessible on a busy Saturday night. Perhaps the influence of New York Times critiques isn't what it used to be, but no matter – this restaurant deserves attention on its own merits.

Opting for the $95 omakase tori, my dining companion and I took our seats at the bar and paired our meal with a bottle of Dassai 50. Our dining experience began with a mixed bag; an appetizer that featured whelk was a touch sandy, though flavorful.

As we progressed to the sushi omakase, my palate was treated to an exceptional sardine – the best I've ever encountered. The toro surpassed expectations, and the uni cup firmly held its place as my personal favorite.

In a delightful twist of generosity, when we inquired about specials, the chef offered us halves of two different types of fish, allowing us both the opportunity to sample without having to make the torturous choice of one over the other.

This establishment prides itself on quality without the pretense, even daring to place soy sauce on the table – a nod to personal preference despite traditional omakase etiquette.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a high-caliber choice for those seeking a top-notch sushi experience without the usual pomp and circumstance.

Title: A Pleasant BBQ Feast with Great Service

I visited this BBQ restaurant on a Saturday afternoon and was pleasantly surprised with only a 10-15 minute wait without a reservation. The host was considerate, offering a cozy long table instead of the prospect of sharing. At $27.99 per person, the all-you-can-eat menu, though not extensive, offered a satisfying variety.

The sauce bar, allowing guests to craft their own flavor concoctions, was a highlight. The cooking, performed tableside, maintained the meal's excitement from start to finish. Both Amber and Edwin, our servers, brought warmth and exceptional service, even taking care to debone our shrimp before cooking.

Their attentive nature continued throughout the meal, always inquiring what we'd like next and keeping our glasses full. An unexpected Chinese New Year treat allowed us to draw a red envelope, gifting us an instant $5 discount—though it did require a cash payment for the bill.

I'm already looking forward to returning to try the hotpot. This place has earned my recommendation for anyone craving a friendly atmosphere and a flavorful BBQ experience!

I've never been a big fan of Chinese food, especially when it's oily. This was exactly the case here. I had the lamb noodles which was nothing to brag about. The hand made noodles was quite good but only if they kept the grease and oil to a minimum I could have finished the plate. The lamb burger was the worse and too dry. The bread they use to make the lamb sandwich was too dry to even eat.This place gets packed but service is quick. If you're looking to dine in and have a large party, forget it. Maybe it's just me but my daughter said it's the best Chinese food she's ever had.

Title: Disappointing Culmination to NY Culinary Adventures at Thai Villa

I regret to report that Thai Villa did not match the high expectations set by its lauded reviews on our final night in New York. The Thai tea held promise with its delightful flavors, but the meal quickly descended into disappointment. Our appetizer, the curry puffs, fell victim to an excess of oil, compromising their enjoyment.

The main courses further accentuated our discontent. The royal pad thai, despite its visual appeal, was cloyingly sweet to the point of being inedible after a few bites. My boyfriend's five spiced duck was marred by a surprising dryness that no sauce could salvage.

Leaving Thai Villa, our spirits were dampened. Our anticipation for an authentic Thai feast was met with an experience that paled in comparison to unassuming "hole in the wall" spots. While the ambiance of the restaurant might attract some, those seeking a culinary delight should cast their eyes elsewhere.

Title: A Taste of Ukraine in the Heart of the East Village – Veselka

Having grown up with Ukrainian heritage, I fancy myself quite the pierogi aficionado, so believe me when I say Veselka in NYC’s East Village is the real deal. There's even a family legend that my great aunt once graced their kitchens, which adds a personal touch to each visit.

The ambiance instantly transports you to a cozy Ukrainian home, and the food? Pure comfort. The borscht here would get my mom's nod of approval—heartwarming and authentic. But let's talk about the star of the show: the pierogis. Veselka elevates these little dumplings to new heights with a variety of fillings that go beyond the traditional potato and cheese. Think mushroom, broccoli, cheddar, and more. My pro tip? Get them fried. It’s a game-changer, especially when slathered with a generous dollop of sour cream.

Being open 24 hours is a godsend for satisfying those late-night cravings for rich, carb-laden Ukrainian classics. Whether you're coming in after a night out or seeking a taste of Eastern European hospitality, Veselka delivers comfort food that speaks to the soul.

Why are good tacos so hard to come by in New York! Taco Dumbo is your white-washed taco joint. With bright pink neon signs and catchy phases, it gets a +1 for the IG. Their food on the other hand is a different story. It's extremely pricey at $5 a taco. It's not filling either. Thrillist apparently named their roasted fish taco "the best summer dish in NYC"  Okay, who is their reviewer because that person needs to be fired. I think I ordered a vegan taco by accident and it was meh. Totally tasted like a taco-bell hard shell. Their chicken taco was a bummer too.For a $15 lunch, I left hungry. Don't be lured by the bright signs.

Heading to Abiko Curry for lunch is a decision your taste buds will thank you for. Imagine indulging in a perfectly fried crispy pork cutlet, resting on a fluffy bed of rice and generously draped in a savory garlic gravy. This isn't just a meal; it's the epitome of comfort food. Priced at an affordable $10, the lunch portion is sizeable and guarantees satisfaction. 

Not in the mood for pork? No problem. Abiko Curry caters to diverse cravings with chicken, beef, and shrimp alternatives. Enhance your bowl with complimentary scallions and garlic or splurge a little on premium toppings to elevate the experience. 

Worried about the spice? Fear not, as Abiko offers a range of spice levels. For those with a milder palate (like myself), the ‘baby spice’ level is a charming touch that ensures you can still enjoy the flavors without the fire.

Though my focus was narrow and I didn't explore beyond the curry offerings, based on the delectable pork curry alone, I'm sold on Abiko Curry. I’d return in a heartbeat for another round of that comforting, crispy pork delight.

I recently paid a visit to a charming spot that evoked fond memories of The Standard Biergarten, complete with an inviting outdoor area perfectly paired with a cozy interior. As one might expect in NYC, the outdoor seating was a hotspot on a sunny Friday evening, though I was pleasantly surprised by the manageable wait time for a table.

The absence of a happy hour was a bit of a letdown and might deter more frequent visits. However, the food was a highlight, with the mac & cheese delivering a delightful cheesy indulgence, and the fried calamari and shrimp hitting the mark as well. The drinks, while not extraordinary, were a solid accompaniment to the meal.

The staff was amicable, contributing to the overall allure of this cute establishment.

With Ladybird temporarily closed, we decided to order delivery on Caviar from their sister restaurant Avant Garden and I'm so glad we did!In the mood for some comfort food, we snagged the national burger day special: 2 loaded impossible burgers, chili cheese fries and bottle of wine for $46. So super tasty and the red wine was a really nice treat (you get to choose red, white or orange- not totally sure what orange means). We also got the Miatake Buns ($6 each). Although it's generally on the pricer end- Avant Garden is truly worth it.

Title: Chic UWS Eatery Needs Fine-Tuning

I recently dined at a contemporary restaurant on the Upper West Side that caught my eye with its stylish ambiance and friendly service. The beautiful tableware added to the visual appeal of the place, setting high expectations for the meal to come.

However, there was a hiccup when it came to the practicality of their utensils. The hearty toasted bread accompanying my avocado spread with salmon was a challenge to tackle without a serrated knife – a minor detail that significantly detracted from the dining experience, as I found myself shaking the table in a battle with my breakfast.

As for the toppings, while a garnish of carrot strips visually enhanced the dish, the sheer quantity was overpowering, overshadowing the delicate flavors of the avocado and salmon.

On the menu front, variety could be improved; the addition of more than one soup option and the introduction of a simple salad plate would be welcome enhancements. These changes might just be enticing enough to encourage a second visit.

In summary, with a few adjustments on the practical and culinary fronts, this restaurant has the potential to excel.

ehh.. I gave them a chance. I really was excited to choose them over all the fast food joints in the area, it was getting late. I guess of all the foot traffic doesn't help with the moral of these employees. Either way my meal was ok.. They did mess up one of the orders 3x and the vibes were off so... I don't know where I stand honestly.

We waited 35 min and got seated a little after 8pm on Saturday (the lady at the front was actually really accurate about the wait time). They serve their house made tofu (soo good) alongside some side dishes in the beginning. We ordered the spicy raspberry pork belly, spicy seafood ddukbokki, and kimchi tofu stew with beef to share amongst 3 ppl, which was a good amount. The seafood ddukbokki came out first and it was WAY spicier than we anticipated. All I can remember is that it was spicy. The other two dishes also were the same color but were much more mild & enjoyable. The beef in the kimchi stew was surprisingly really juicy and chewy.If you're not good with spicy, skip the ddukbokki!

Title: A Taste of Peru Right Here!

After a recent trip to Peru, my cravings for authentic Peruvian cuisine led me to this gem of a restaurant. I ordered the seafood mixto and it did not disappoint! The seafood was incredibly fresh, and the sweet potato mousse topping was a delightful surprise that complemented the flavors perfectly. The portion was so generous that it could stand alone as a satisfying meal.

I want to address the complaints regarding the lime flavor and acidity in the ceviche. It's important to understand that ceviche is inherently acidic—that's a signature characteristic of the dish. Criticizing a ceviche for its lime content is akin to faulting a meatball sub for containing marinara sauce—it misses the point entirely. On a personal note, the ceviche here was even less acidic than many I sampled in Peru, striking a pleasant balance for the palate.

In summary, for anyone missing Peru or wanting to dive into Peruvian flavors, this restaurant is a must-visit. Ignore the misguided negative reviews; the staff is doing a great job keeping the cuisine authentic.

I still come here often. The food is just delish and the lunch specials make it SO worth it. I've gotten the chicken ravioli = my FAV. If your really hungry then this won't be enough food but its SO GOOD. The burger is amazingly good. The very first time I had it - they added pickles onions on my burger- that was the first and last time i got those type of onions. They were amazing but any other time I've gone they added raw onions. Sometimes I add an egg to the burger and it's super good. I've gotten the chicken caesar salad. I wouldn't get it again, not worth it. Overall, I'll keep coming back. This place is goooood goooood.

I visited the restaurant again today, having previously enjoyed their dessert offerings last year. This time, I opted for the matcha dessert, which was decently balanced in sweetness. However, the lava cake didn't quite hit the mark. The texture seemed off, leading me to wonder if it had been reheated in a microwave, which was disappointing. At $13.10, the price felt steep, particularly given that the overall experience wasn't anything to write home about. Unfortunately, this visit did not live up to past experiences and I'm inclined to say it will be my last.

My spouse and I recently decided to try the West Side Palms, and I'm delighted to share our experience. Upon arrival, the cleanliness and warm atmosphere immediately caught our attention, and the hostess welcomed us with a friendly greeting. Although the restaurant was fully booked, we were fortunate to find seating in the bar area, where the space is cozy yet comfortable.

The service was prompt as our waitress came over to take our order. We began with the fried calamari which was simply outstanding — crisp and perfectly seasoned. Following that, we tried the creamed spinach; it was tasty, although not the best we've had. We also indulged in the half fries, chips, and onion strings combo, and I must say, it was a delightful mix of textures and flavors.

Overall, West Side Palms delivered a pleasant experience with delicious starters and an amiable atmosphere. It's certainly a spot worth stopping by, especially if you can grab a seat in the bustling bar area.

Title: A Banh Mi Haven in the Heart of the City

If you find yourself with a banh mi craving, look no further than this gem tucked away between Chinatown and Little Italy. It's a small joint, perfect for quick stops with a couple of bar stools if you fancy a bite on the spot.

The house special sandwich I tried was exceptional. Imagine a sandwich toasted to a delightful crunch on the outside, yet still pillowy within. The marinated meat is a standout, mingling flawlessly with the assorted cold cuts. Since I passed on the veggies, they generously heaped on more meat, making the sandwich substantial enough for two meals.

In a city with no shortage of Vietnamese eateries, this place rises to the top. Its sizable, delectable sandwiches will have you planning your next visit before you've even finished the first half. Highly recommended for any banh mi enthusiast!

Soooo delicious! I'm a big cheese lover! First we got the american grilled cheese to share. It was definitely bigger than we thought it would be and so delicious!! Then we each ordered the suisse with veal which comes with 2 choices of cheeses so i got traditional & black truffle. The plate didn't look amazing..potatoes, meat looked like pastrami slices & some bland greens. But OMG once they melt the cheese on top, it just makes everything in the plate taste amazing!

The long-awaited Peruvian Nikkei style restaurant from the Llama Inn team just opened in a nice space on 6th Ave.There's a lot of fun stuff to try, like the Duck Nigiri ($24), and the octopus & crab fried rice situation ($30), which were probably the two best things. The Chicken Thigh ($26) was also great, so this is one of the few times where the large entrees were much more interesting than the small plates. The Iberico Pork ($36) is also very worth trying, and comes a serving of Udon Verde that pairs very nicely with the crispy pork.For dessert, the Miso Banana ($10) is the definite winner of the 3 options, with the Chocolate ($10) coming in second.There's also a tasting menu option, which might not be a bad idea since the a la carte options can get pricey.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Blue Hill in New York, and it was truly an unforgettable fine dining experience. The restaurant places a strong emphasis on local produce, crafting a menu that's inspired by the week's harvest. This commitment to freshness is palpable in every dish, each one a veritable work of art on the plate.

Moreover, the wine list is as considered as the food, featuring producers dedicated to artisanal techniques that pair perfectly with the seasonal ingredients. The connection to local farms, like Blue Hill Farm in Great Barrington, Massachusetts, and Stone Barns Center for Food and Agriculture, reinforces the restaurant's ethos of sustainability and community support.

If you're looking for an exquisite culinary experience that embodies the essence of farm-to-table dining, I cannot recommend Blue Hill enough. Each bite is a testament to the care and creativity that define this establishment.

We stumbled upon a gem on a bustling Friday night, and the experience was delightful. The restaurant welcomes guests to bring their own wine, which they serve without any uncorking fee – a pleasant surprise. Service was quick, with each dish arriving promptly, tasting delicious, and served in generous portions. To top it all off, the prices were remarkably reasonable. This spot has earned a return visit from us, without a doubt.

I went with the birdhaus Bao and the spiceland Bao. Both were really good. Chicken was crispy. Birdhaus Bao was slightly sweet. Taro fries were really good too. Being slightly more starchy, taro fries were crispier than French fries. The sauce which came with it was very flavorful.There is a restroom in the corner of the shop. That is the smallest I have ever seen. There is no light or wash sink there. Use it only if there is no other go.

We visited the restaurant recently and had a delightful experience. The service was efficient, with staff being both courteous and attentive. Our meal was exceptionally tasty, and we were pleasantly surprised by how promptly our dishes arrived. As a funny aside, we initially mistook Best Sichuan next door for our intended destination, but the mix-up was quickly forgotten once we settled in for our delicious meal. Highly recommended for both the food quality and swift service.

I recently visited this eatery on a Monday to take advantage of their appealing burrito and margarita deal for $17. While the nachos proved tasty, they quickly turned soggy. The burrito was satisfactory, heavily leaning on rice and beans, but lacked complexity. The major letdowns were the drinks and service. The margarita was notably weak on alcohol, and service fell short. We were unexpectedly billed for chips and salsa, assumed to be complimentary, and the inattentive server made any interaction a challenge, despite the sparse crowd. In summary, it's a spot for acceptable food at a fair price, but set your expectations accordingly for drinks and service.

Errrr... Honestly not my favorite hot pot place and no where near being my favorite. The quality of the food is quite nice but there wasn't a lot of variety of food choices for the buffet. There were small things like beef balls and fried tofu skin that you have to pay extra $2.99 or $3.99 for.. and when ordered - it only came with 5 or 6 beef balls or 4 fried tofu skin.. like what? l o lIt's a beautiful space and staffs were pretty nice but I seriously didn't enjoy this place that much due to the lack of variety.

Title: A Delightful Chinese Culinary Experience

I recently dined at a local Chinese restaurant that positively delighted my taste buds. Their hot and sour soup was a standout, rivaling my all-time favorite from Henry Hunan in San Francisco. Each dish my family ordered was a hit, with special nods to the scrumptious chicken lo mein and the perfectly crispy scallion pancakes.

A word of caution to the spice-averse: my brother's noodle soup packed a fiery punch that may not appeal to everyone. Also, while the Mapo Tofu was bursting with flavor, those who prefer their tofu firm or crispy might find its soft texture a bit underwhelming.

Overall, I'm eager to return and explore more of their menu. If you're a fan of authentic Chinese cuisine, this is a spot you won't want to miss!

Title: A Seafood Haven Worthy of More Than 5 Stars

I wish I could visually share the culinary masterpieces from my recent visit to this gem of a restaurant, but capturing images felt a tad too gauche for the sophisticated ambiance. However, rest assured, every dish is superb.

The smoked fish appetizer is a must-try, featuring an impressive variety including trout, salmon, and sea bass. The fish here is a true highlight, with a seemingly endless array of options, all executed to perfection. Accompanied by delightful sauces and fresh veggies like scrumptious Brussels sprouts and asparagus, each bite is a testament to the kitchen's prowess.

The impeccable meal from starter to dessert was matched by faultless service. The cozy warmth of a fire added to the romantic allure of the setting, making it an ideal spot for a date night, or for any seafood aficionado looking to indulge in beautifully prepared cuisine.

In sum, this restaurant is a dazzling culinary star that deserves every accolade. Five stars simply don't do it justice — I absolutely love this place!

Title: Solid Dinner Experience with Room for Improvement

My recent Friday evening dinner at this restaurant offered a delightful array of dishes, particularly the seafood and healthy options which stood out for their variety. The service matched the food in quality, contributing to an overall pleasant experience.

The dessert selection ended the meal on a high note, though it was somewhat overshadowed by the lackluster bread served at the beginning, which lacked freshness and flavor.

However, my visit was marred by the state of the restroom facilities. The absence of toilet paper and the scattered paper towels suggested a lack of attention to cleanliness that needs addressing immediately.

In conclusion, while the food and service were commendable, the experience could be enhanced significantly with improvements in the bread quality and restroom maintenance.

When u are at Macy's all day , this might be a good place to take a load off . Other yelpers not so happy with this venue , they have wood fire ovens & a full bar with a great cocktail menu , views , and attentive service .Spacious and contemporary room .Beautiful windows with lots a light coming thru .We liked it !Check it out , THE BREAD SERVICE  omg

Came across this place while wandering around the Chelsea Market.Absolutely no regrets for doing so.You order at the cashier in the corner of the booth and then find yourself a seat, either at the counter or the surrounding area.Tacos we ordered: japanese curry beefchicken adobocarnitasbraised short ribBraised short rib was the winner.  So soft and juicy and savory.  The curry beef was interesting as it came on a crispy taco shell.  The chicken adobo and carnitas were ok - I've had better in L.A.The meal hit the spot and left us full and satisfied.  It's a cool concept and wish them much success.

Title: A Twist on Tradition at a Former Seafood Haunt

Recently, I visited a restaurant that has taken over the old Live Bait location, a former seafood mainstay. The interior hasn't strayed far from its predecessor, maintaining a familiar ambiance. The menu, however, has charted a new course with its Tex-Mex and fusion offerings rather than sticking to traditional Mexican cuisine. Choices like pastrami tacos and duck tacos hint at a creative, albeit non-authentic, spin on classics, while the smoked brisket burritos deliver a comforting smoky flavor. The torta, though, was reminiscent of a typical deli sandwich, which may disappoint those seeking the robust profiles of Mexican street food.

While the food is passable, it's their drink selection, particularly the margaritas and tequila, that stands out, both for quality and value. To sum up, if you're in search of an affordable spot to enjoy a casual drink and are open to an unconventional take on tacos and burritos, this could be a satisfactory choice.

Title: Cozy Dinner with Robust Flavors at Anand

My visit to Anand on a surprisingly quiet Friday night was a delightful experience. Accompanied by my dad, we were welcomed by ample seating options, which set the stage for a relaxed meal. The Gobi Manchurian appetizer was the first to impress with its perfectly fried cauliflower, doused in a robust tomato sauce that balanced flavor and spice exquisitely.

Our main course included a shared spread of paratha, fluffy basmati rice, creamy chicken makhani, and a mild dal tadka. Each dish was skillfully prepared, with the chicken makhani stealing the show with its rich, flavorful sauce. The lighter dal tadka offered a pleasant contrast, proving that subtlety has its own charm. The generous portions further added to the sense of value.

Anand's atmosphere was quiet but comfortable, fostering an environment ripe for conversation. For a meal that satisfies the taste buds without breaking the bank, I wholeheartedly recommend Anand. It's a gem that promises a tasty meal in a setting that feels just right.

Title: A Dimly Lit Culinary Gem with a Side of Decibels

My recent foray into the New York City location of this Chicago original left me with a mix of shadows and culinary highlights. Tucked away in an alley that could be described as suspiciously dark, the restaurant's interior doesn't stray far from its exterior, embracing a dimly lit bar atmosphere amplified by a soundtrack turned up high. 

The menu shone despite the lack of luminance. The classic burger, crowned with an exquisite layer of bacon, was transformed into an epicurean delight, the smokiness elevating the perfectly cooked patty to new heights. Complemented by a substantial bun that capably mopped up the flavorful juices, it was a dish I'd come back for. 

My dining partner was equally enamored with her house-made bologna sandwich, declaring it a must-have for future outings. And for those with a sweet tooth, the gargantuan mille-feuille is a dessert that's as Instagram-worthy as it is indulgent, especially when adorned with sparklers to celebrate a special occasion. 

However, the auditory overload did mar the overall dining experience. Struggling to converse over the blasting tunes subtracted from the enjoyment, prompting me to remove a star from an otherwise stellar review. A little volume control could go a long way in making this spot as comfortable for the ears as it is pleasing to the palate.

My wife and I had a delightful lunch experience at this restaurant. We savored the Pas See U beef, which was served with a complimentary spring roll and salad, and found it to be delicious. The staff impressed us with their friendliness, and the establishment's decor was aesthetically pleasing. Despite its bustling atmosphere—a clear testament to its popularity—we were well taken care of. Given my wife's fondness for Thai cuisine, we will definitely be returning. Highly recommend!

Title: A Tale of Two Classics at Burger and Lobster

I recently dined at Burger and Lobster, drawn in by the name and the promise of their two namesake dishes. The popularity of the place was evident in the wait times, both for a table and service, but the staff remained amiable throughout.

Their original burger was satisfying, yet it didn't quite match the high expectations set by their claim of having the best burgers around. The house special sauce was a nice touch, though it couldn't elevate the burger to the extraordinary.

Now, the lobster roll was a different story entirely – a delightful surprise. Served chilled, the lobster was impeccably fresh, and the toasted, buttered bun was the perfect vehicle. Together with the shoestring fries, the star of the sides was the truffle mayo, which was simply divine.

While I might forego the wait next time and opt for takeout, it's the lobster roll that would undoubtedly bring me back to Burger and Lobster. It's clear where their strength lies, and it's worth the visit – or the wait, if you're patient.

I visited this eatery for a birthday dinner and had a mixed dining experience. The appetizers impressed, offering a tantalizing start to the meal. Moving on to the soup, it was passable but didn't leave a lasting impression. The steak, ordered well-done, was cooked to the proper level of doneness, yet it seemed to lack the robust seasoning one might anticipate from a premier steakhouse. While the steak's texture was commendable, the flavor profile was underwhelming. For those who favor their steak well-cooked without a strong seasoning presence, this place might suit your tastes. However, seasoned steak enthusiasts might find the offerings a bit bland. The highlight, undoubtedly, was the appetizer, which I would recommend.
Food was mediocre.  Portions were ok.  Service was ok as well.  First time trying but not a fan. Servers were gracious and attentive.

The food here is absolutely divine. Everything we ordered was cooked to perfection. Cocktails were beautifully presented and delicious. There was a DJ when we came by so the ambiance was lively. The portions were rather small for the prices, but I would definitely recommend this place! I will be stopping by again.

Tucked away near the theater district, this gem evades the typical tourist trap vibe with its genuine charm. The value is exceptional, with generous portions at wallet-friendly prices. The shrimp noodle soup, a delightful blend, featured a robust beef broth with spot-on noodles and fresh greens. The five tableside flavorings provided a fun, customizable twist to the meal. The chicken and noodles, another hit, showcased tender poultry amidst more of those perfect noodles and an array of intriguing, though mysterious, additional ingredients. Both dishes left us thoroughly impressed. This unassuming spot has secured its place on our go-to list. Highly recommend!

Came in on a Sunday to have a drink while we waited for our table to be ready at another restaurant. It also happened to be happy hour - $6 beer, $7 house wine, $8 select cocktails, and $9 martinis. I ordered the aperol spritz because I figured an Italian restaurant couldn't screw this up. But I was wrong. They put this extra syrup in there which made it taste off and super sweet. Y fiancé had the Taste of LA (bourbon, grapefruit, honey syrup). The bartender used two different types of bourbon (odd) as used the same shaker as he just used to make someone else a vodka martini (more odd). The drink didn't really taste like grapefruit but more like remnants of a martini. On top of the bad drinks, the restaurant was stuffy from the heat, so people were complaining to crack open the door. Then when the door was cracked, you had another group complaining it was too cold. This went back and forth a few times. I can't imagine this would be a very comfortable dining experience, since it wasn't a great bar experience. Probably would not be making a return trip.

This spot is a must-visit for noodle enthusiasts! Their hand-pulled noodles, particularly the cumin lamb noodles, are a delightful balance of soft and chewy, generously coated in a wonderfully rich and spicy sauce. Not only is the food mouthwateringly good, but it's also wallet-friendly. With multiple locations across the city, it's convenient too. I can't visit without indulging in the cumin lamb noodles and on my latest trip, the spicy lamb dumplings were an excellent addition. Both dishes are highly recommended for an authentic and satisfying meal.

Title: Underwhelmed by Restaurant Week Experience

I attended the restaurant week dinner expecting a great value meal but was left with a feeling of discontent. Despite the food being quite tasty, the price tag of $68 for a "discounted" dinner, inclusive of tax, tip, and a single beer, seemed unjustified given the lingering hunger I felt post-meal.

The pork belly appetizer was disappointingly scant with just two small pieces, and while my companion's clams were a tad more generous in portion, the ginger infusion wasn't to my liking. The prawn entrée was indeed flavorful, with the garlic rice being a highlight, but three medium-sized prawns didn't suffice in sating my appetite. Even garnishing the meal with a few cucumber slices couldn't make up for the overall lack of substance.

Dessert was a reasonably portioned mango sherbet - refreshing, though not particularly satisfying as the final act of a dinner. My sentiment towards the dining experience is tepid: I'm content to have sampled the offerings, but the combination of steep prices and modest servings ensures I won't be planning a repeat visit.

Upon entering the restaurant, I was immediately struck by its charming ambiance, reminiscent of old school Korea, which made for a very pleasant dining atmosphere. My lunch experience was, on the whole, quite enjoyable although the kalbi didn't quite hit the mark. It lacked the tenderness and thin cut I've come to expect from short rib, leaving me questioning its authenticity. 

Fortunately, the rest of the meal did not disappoint. The spicy cold noodles had a kick that was nicely balanced, the bulgogi was flavorful, the tofu bibimbap had a comforting warmth, the japchae was perfectly seasoned, and the spicy tofu stew was delightfully hearty. Service was attentive throughout our meal, ensuring a smooth dining experience, even if the sides were merely average.

The restaurant is conveniently located on the second floor of the building, adding an element of privacy and seclusion from the bustling street below. 

All things considered, this place earns a solid 3.5 stars from me. Despite the kalbi hiccup, the rest of the offerings make it a spot worth visiting for those craving Korean cuisine with an authentic feel.

Title: Generous Portions and Friendly Service Shine at Local Eatery

I recently dined at this restaurant and was impressed by the copious portions of delicious food served. Although the meal began on an underwhelming note with the Pao de queijo – which was dry and seemed hastily reheated – the rest of the experience more than made up for this slight misstep.

The Bobo de Camarao was a standout dish with its succulent, perfectly cooked large shrimps, enveloped in a delectable sauce that truly delighted the palate. My wife's choice of Frango com quiabo was similarly praiseworthy, her enjoyment evident through the savory sauce that accompanied her dish.

The attentive and amiable wait staff elevated the dining experience, ensuring we were content throughout our visit. Despite the initial hiccup with the appetizer, this restaurant delivers on both taste and service, making it a place worth revisiting.

What can I say? A bunch of things that could go wrong, sort of went wrong. I had high expectations for The Mermaid Inn as it is a sister location to the Mermaid Oyster Bar in Greenwich Village. I recommend going there instead.I arrived for my 6 PM reservation late, which was my fault. However, coincidentally, the restaurant's reservation system was crashing so the hostesses could not locate our table anyway. It soon became known that the power was also out in the back and the chefs were continuing to cook in the dark, which I'm sure is a safety hazard.They were willing to keep guests waiting, most of the guests unbeknownst to the problem, even when they themselves had little idea of when the power would come back. Eventually, some of the people with reservations left before the power came back.After willing to stick around for Happy Hour, which was ending as we were being finally seated in the back, we were finally able to put in our order after having to wave down a server. The server to table ratio was pitiful in the back, including the back patio, with what appeared to be two servers only and a handful of bussers.During the dinning, I also overheard what sounded like one of the bussers explaining that he had accidentally charged the wrong person's credit card. I'm not sure what happened there exactly, but I felt like it deserved a mention.The food was actually pretty decent, a bit pricy, and small portioned but I still enjoyed it. However, we were presented with the calamari, which I did not order. The linguine with clams also took forever to arrive, nearly half an hour after all the other items were finished. Wrapping up the check also took some time, and again we had to wave down the server. We were also informed that they were out of the chocolate pudding at the end which was very disappointing.

I had the opportunity to meet the owner on my very first visit here. It's easy to spot on Grand street, but many people could miss it thinking it's a bar and not  a barbecue restaurant. From the warm welcome to the expert advice of the team- I ordered practically everything on the menu!!! The collards were perfect, the clams were delicious and the brisket was so perfect with the spicy bbq sauce provided at the table. I'm a fan of tables with wares and napkins all ready for the guests but including your specialty sauces... HELL YA! Everything was on point and I extremely enjoyed their Happy Hour specials. Try the Kielbasa sandwich! That was my favorite.

Title: A Delightful Lunch at a Charming Spot

I recently visited an Italian restaurant for Friday lunch with a group of five friends, and it was a delightful experience from start to finish. Our party was seated upon arrival, and the friendly waiter ensured our order was promptly taken in the quaint, vintage-styled interior.

The complimentary bread and high-quality olive oil set a promising start, and the dishes that followed, a perfectly creamy and well-seasoned Cacio e Pepe, and an unforgettable vegetable soup with a dollop of ricotta, did not disappoint.

The kitchen's efficiency was impressive, with all our dishes arriving almost simultaneously, mere 20 minutes after ordering. The bill amounted to roughly $25 per person, which is on the higher end, but given the quality of the food and service, it was well worth it.

In summary, for anyone in search of top-notch Italian cuisine and a quick, pleasant dining experience, this place is a gem worth trying out.

Title: A Delightful Find for Mexican Fare in NYC

I recently visited a charming Mexican restaurant in the heart of New York City and was thoroughly impressed by the experience, even though I only sampled one appetizer. The highlight was the frozen margarita, which was nothing short of fabulous - a perfect blend of tangy and sweet, with a kick that kept me sipping.

Although my stop was mainly for post-brunch drinks, the bartender's attentiveness added to the enjoyment. Not only was he swift with refills, but he also ensured we had plenty of water, keeping us hydrated and happy.

The steady stream of people popping in for takeout orders was a testament to the restaurant's popularity. While my taste of the menu was limited, the buzz from satisfied customers was enough for me to wholeheartedly recommend giving this spot a try for anyone craving authentic Mexican cuisine in NYC.

I'd call this a "no frills, focused on quality and taste" ramen shop. Small place, ~12 stool seats, order at the counter, open kitchen so you can see the chef work his magic. Each bowl is neatly prepared with broth, noodles perfectly laid, and toppings. We both got the shoyu - you can def smell and taste the truffle which is a very nice and delish touch!  The broth has a simple depth to it which carries flavor/umami yet is pure. You can see the layer of fat that makes the broth delish!Karaage is dark meat, perfectly fried - not too crispy or soggy, and the meat is well seasoned but goes well with sauce. Edamame is served with Yuzu salt on side - I would of asked for more! Cucumber is a nice cold side dish to go with the ramen.

Tucked away in the East Village, this gem of a sushi restaurant is an absolute must-visit for anyone with a penchant for fresh, delectable Japanese cuisine. From the moment I sat down, each dish was a testament to quality and flavor, with the highlight being the creatively presented and aptly named avocado bomb, which lived up to its moniker in the most explosive way. Small plates are the way to go here, offering a chance to sample the breadth of their culinary expertise. My taste buds are already anticipating a return visit for the omakase, which, if it's anything like the dishes I've tried, is sure to be an unforgettable experience.

Probably one of the best sushi experiences I have ever had in my life. It's a pain to be able to book a spot to eat here because they don't take reservations and you literally have to go to the restaurant and put yourself on the waiting list which will take a minimum of 90 minutes on a weekend. Holidays could take up to 3 hours and even more depending on what kind of holiday it is. But it's definitely worth the hassle.I came here on a Sunday with 5 other friends around 2pm and the wait was about an hour so we just walked around Union Square to kill time until we got a text notification that we were about to be up in the queue. We were seated promptly after checking in with the hostess and the great experience begun.I got the Nozawa Trust Me combo where I got to have a slew of sushi, rolls, and sashimi. They are all prepared as fresh as they can be, each bite with such amazing flavor and taste. You can tell the quality is not to be messed around. You get one sashimi plate, five various sushi rolls, and two hand rolls along with a plate of edamame. Each is served as soon as they are made so you'll get served six different plates before you're fully done with the experience. All of this costed 49$ including tax and tip.The service is exceptional. They break down how they roll, all of the options on the menu, and clarify menu options such as the difference between the select combo options. It is printed on the menu that there is no tipping as it's priced into the menu already which I like. Overall, it's a very wonderful experience and will be back in the future when I find the waiting time not too long or just plan ahead that day.

Tuome is a hip, urban restaurant located in the LES that features American food with an Asian twist. We made a reservation on a Wednesday night - the place was full but I think it would be possible to walk-in and get a table. I'd advise sticking with a small group (or a date) as the space is small. From beginning to end, our servers were remarkably considerate. We even had two separate servers consistently checking on us throughout the meal. Honestly, I could have done with even a little less attention. We tried a number of their cocktails and wines. All of their cocktails are wine based which I thought was an interesting twist. I really enjoyed the blushing dragon sangria but be warned that it's very sweet and fruity. I also tried the east village blossom which was a heavier, spicier drink. For the food, we started with the caviar on shrimp toast. These were small, crispy seafood puffs topped with a spoonful of caviar on a wasabi aioli. It was a nice, light start to the meal. We then tried the octopus which is served with a fingerling potato whipped mousse. I really liked the texture of the potato mousse paired with the octopus which was perfectly cooked. Finally, we split the snow crab noodles. While these are a little pricey for a bowl of noodles ($33) they are hands down the BEST noodles I've had in nyc. The creamy, nutty sauce that coats the noodles is amazing. And the noodles themselves are perfectly cooked with just the right amount of bite. I can't recommend these enough. Overall, I had a delightful experience at Tuome. The trendy but intimate ambience along with the interesting cocktails and delicious food made for a wonderful dinner. I'm looking forward to going back!

Prince Street Pizza is famous for their thick square pepperoni pizza, and it is thickkk. Personally more of a fan of their thin/regular pizza. A few bites of the pepperoni square pizza are good, but it's on the saltier side and it's a little too much dough for me.The margherita pizza on the other hand is amazing. Perfectly slightly sweet sauce with thick, gooey cheese, and fresh basil, and chewy crust.It's chaos in there and you have about two seconds to order so be prepared. Honestly if the line is out the door and crazy long I don't think it's worth it. Come back on an off time.

This place is the real deal. Definitely worth the wait and I never, ever say that. Obviously the quintessential square pepperoni is great stuff but don't sleep on the vodka slice, its equally delicious.

I usually approach new dining spots with enthusiasm, especially when they come with glowing recommendations and the allure of celebrity patronage. However, my recent visit to this hyped pizza joint was dramatically underwhelming. Despite its fame and incredibly low price of $3 per slice, the experience was a letdown from the start.

The staff's treatment of customers left a lot to be desired. I witnessed a server being outright rude to non-English speakers, responding with almost mocking simplicity when asked about a certain pizza variety. It was my first real encounter with the stereotypical 'rude New Yorker,' and it did not sit well with me.

As for the pizza itself, the quality was subpar at best. Both slices I received had charred bottoms, yet the overall temperature of the pizza was merely lukewarm – a perplexing and unappetizing combination. The flavor did not redeem the poor texture; it reminded me of the underwhelming pizza served in elementary school cafeterias.

My companions and I couldn't even bring ourselves to finish our slices, choosing to discard them rather than force down another bite of what can only be described as a culinary disappointment. Greasiness can be excusable in a delicious slice of pizza, but in this case, it only compounded the negative experience.

My advice? Save your time and appetite for a pizza place that delivers on taste as well as service.

Title: A Love Affair with Vapiano

If you're a fan of customizable Italian cuisine, Vapiano should be on your list. The restaurant offers an impressive range of pizza and pasta choices that will satisfy any craving. The concept is brilliant: select your desired pasta type, then pick a sauce like pesto, Alfredo, or carbonara. You can elevate your dish with add-ons such as chicken, shrimp, beef, or salmon. My personal favorite is the pesto pasta topped with shrimp—a dish that has never disappointed. 

My friends have also praised the pizza offerings and the creamy Alfredo pasta. Don't miss out on the bruschetta; order the duo option for a taste of two delightful varieties. And a sweet tip before you leave: grab some gummy bears as a little treat for the road. Vapiano charms with its variety and quality, making it a coveted spot for any Italian food enthusiast.

My friends and I visited this restaurant on a Saturday night and were charmed by the quaint ambiance and the exceptionally friendly staff, which definitely elevated the dining experience. Although the atmosphere was inviting, my curry goat dish fell short of expectations – it was passable but not remarkable. This place might be better suited for a casual evening of drinks and light snacks accompanied by great conversation.

Just the nicest bar. Beautiful design. Like you stepped back in time to the US around the 1890's. Lighting great. Comfortable in a plush way. Best of all you can hear the person you are speaking to!! The service started slow but she ended up being charming. The drinks were excellent and well priced. I really enjoyed it.

Title: A Slice of Szechuan Heaven on the UWS – Pig Heaven Review

I recently stumbled upon Pig Heaven on a casual stroll through the Upper West Side and, propelled by a Chinese food craving, decided to give it a try. The dining experience turned out to be exceptional beyond my expectations.

The menu at Pig Heaven delighted me with its mix of traditional Chinese offerings and exciting new Szechuan dishes. Our culinary adventure began with their soup dumplings, which were a revelation. Each dumpling was abundantly stuffed, and the broth they bathed in was utterly delectable.

But the star of the show had to be the famous BBQ Spare Ribs. Label me impressed, for they were quite possibly the best spare ribs I've ever savored. The meat was succulent and tender, and the sauce? Oh, it was a flavor-packed masterpiece.

Just when I thought I had reached the pinnacle of the meal, out came the pièce de résistance – a stunning hot pot, which we were told was sourced from overseas. This exquisite dish, brimming with fish and vegetables, packed a delightful punch even at a mild spice level. It was, without exaggeration, a phenomenal dish that warrants a repeat visit.

Complementing the food was the exemplary service, spearheaded by manager Lisa. Her helpful, kind, and professional demeanor only enhanced what was already a fantastic dining experience.

In summary, Pig Heaven is a must-visit for anyone in search of authentic and elevated Chinese cuisine. It's a place I'm eager to return to, and I wholeheartedly recommend it to other food lovers.

Title: A Flavorful Return to a Seasonal Delight

After a long hiatus, my curiosity was piqued once again by the seasonal offerings at this quaint eatery, leading me to wonder why I had let so much time pass between visits. The promise of old school shoyu ramen, motsu nabe, and a unique matcha tiramisu proved too enticing to ignore.

On arrival, the advantage of reserving a table became immediately clear as I bypassed the wait and was seated promptly—15 minutes ahead of schedule, in fact.

The shoyu ramen, while lacking a certain depth, was pleasing on the palate, and I relished each bite despite its simplicity. The motsu nabe presented a fiery challenge to my modest spice tolerance, but its quality shone through the heat. The harami skirt steak lived up to expectations, a favorite cut that was tender and perfectly marinated, though left me craving just a bit more.

The meat lovers set was an ideal choice for someone who steers clear of the more adventurous meats, offering a delightful array and leaving only the chicken to fall short of expectation. The corn, however, deserves a special mention for its succulent sweetness.

As for desserts, the matcha tiramisu landed comfortably in the realm of the satisfactory, with potential for a second chance—solely for my enjoyment next time.

Service was a highlight of the evening, with attentive staff seamlessly taking over from one another mid-dinner, ensuring a gracious dining experience. A special nod to Tenzen (if that’s the correct spelling) for his kindness and assistance.

One minor observation was the frequent grill changes, which personally suited my preference for a charred touch to the dishes.

For those considering a visit, take note of the 6pm cut-off for happy hour specials. And while I overlooked the grilling instructions in the menu, future diners might benefit from a quick study to perfect the cooking of their selections.

In summary, this restaurant has renewed its place in my culinary heart and comes highly recommended for those seeking a taste of tradition with a seasonal twist.

we loved Le Coucou for a special date night, it was hard to get a reservation but definitely worth the effort. the restaurant is so beautiful and charming that when you walk in it feels like you stepped off the streets of SoHo and right into Paris. service was perfect; very friendly and attentive. the maître d' was especially kind to honor my request for a window table even when the place was packed (it was the day before valentine's) the food was absolutely delicious, highlights include the Quenelle de brochet "Route de Reims" (eggy soufflé looking thing with caviar), Foie gras grillé aux artichauts, and the prime filet. i'm still dreaming about that filet, with its tasty marrow soaked potatoes... only thing to skip is the seaweed ice oysters, they were kinda boring and we wished we had tried the clams instead. otherwise... une nuit parfaite

Title: "A Brunch to Remember at Twisted Delights"

If you're looking for a dining experience that merges quality with an unexpected twist, look no further. But be warned, you'll need to pace yourself to fully enjoy the spread at Twisted Delights.

Right off the bat, the trio of warm biscuits - corn, jalapeño, chive - will welcome you with their heartwarming and satisfying presence. Moving on to brunch, which truly shines here, the deviled eggs are a revelation, perfectly balancing flavors and textures that tantalize your taste buds.

The standout main courses include the Norwegian pancakes and the Double Cheeseburger. The pancakes are a delightful blend of salty and sweet, topped with Viking cheese, Nordic berries, and a generous scoop of whipped cream. On the other hand, the Double Cheeseburger is a study in simplicity done right - just classic, no-nonsense deliciousness with meat, cheese, onions, and pickles. Occasionally, all it calls for is a dip of ketchup to reach perfection.

While the fries may not steal the show, by the time they arrive, you’re likely to be pleasantly sated. The friendly staff round out the experience, ensuring your meal is as enjoyable as the food.

In short, Twisted Delights offers a brunch that's worth every bite, particularly that burger which I could happily indulge in any day of the week.

During my recent visit to the local Italian eatery, I sampled the Linguine del Pescatore, which unfortunately did not meet expectations. The dish appeared to lack a certain depth, possibly due to an underwhelming sauce that failed to enhance the flavors. Although the pasta was quite average and did not leave a lasting impression, I couldn't help but notice the tantalizing pizza being enjoyed at neighboring tables, which I am keen to try on a future visit.

The service that evening was stretched thin; the limited number of servers was evident as they hustled to attend to diners. Nevertheless, their effort and diligence in managing the busy dining room did not go unnoticed. It's clear they were working hard to provide a pleasant experience regardless of the circumstances.

I'm a huge fan of Mari Vanna in DC so on my most recent business trip I hoped to visit and see if the NYC one was just as good. I came in at 7:30 and promptly went to the bar as I could see it was quite busy in the main area of the restaurant. Unlike the DC location, this spot is smaller and not 3 stories so definitely make reservations at busy times.Things I can highly highly recommend food wise: the borscht, which comes with rye bread and salo. The beef and pork pelmeni with an abundance of sour scream are scrumptious! I also got a side of mashed potatoes and was truly reminded Russians make the best mashed potatoes around. For a drink I got the Klobpnechka martini which was an unfrozen version of a strawberry daiquiri.Service was OK. Even though I'm Russian, the young Russian bartender didn't really try to make conversation. Normally I don't mind this but on business travel, it's nice to sit at the bar and have someone acknowledge you as a person and not just a customer. Maybe that's just me :)Great time, I will be back!

On the UWS, it's easy to find a pizza place, with breakfast, not so much. Went with the Yelp reviews, and Friedman's didn't disappoint. Popular local spot for a Saturday morning breakfast, with both strollers double-parked and older folks filing in, too. Service was friendly and helpful from Bridget, and it really wasn't her fault that the food took awhile to come out. Good news was that we weren't in a hurry, anyway. As we sat down we were offered "complimentary water"- still or bubbles, a nice touch. I'd highly recommend the Chicken Chilaquiles (sunny side eggs, fried tortillas, avocados, tomatillo salsa, cotija cheese, $17), a generous portion with just a little spice. One of those dishes you know you should stop, but you just can't because the flavor is so good! We also had the Eggs With Style (2 eggs, potato hash, toast, and a choice of breakfast meat or toast, $15).  Eggs were prepared just as requested, over medium +. All in all, a good breakfast, but not inexpensive- with $5 orange juice, the total came to  just about $46.

After a weekend of partying, my friends and I decided to try out Mentoku for some ramen, following enthusiastic recommendations. Despite its small size, Mentoku impressed us with its value and extraordinary flavors. We arrived at an off-peak time, around 1:45 PM, and were seated immediately, with the restaurant being almost empty.

I opted for the Hakata Ramen with an added egg, priced at $15. Service was speedy, with our dishes arriving promptly. The ramen itself was a delight, brimming with flavor, and accompanied by a perfectly cooked egg. For anyone in search of top-notch ramen, Mentoku stands out as a must-visit spot.

Title: Cozy Valentines Delight with a Modern Twist

I celebrated an early Valentine's Day at this charming, compact restaurant boasting a modern, minimalist night market ambiance. The diverse menu didn't disappoint, with the highlight being the army stew – a delightful introduction to Spam for me, and a dish brimming with tasty sausage, adorable mini dumplings, and addictive ramen.

Equally impressive were the Korean fried chicken wings, a godsend for us lactose-intolerant diners, thanks to the milk-free batter. The bibimbap, topped with succulent pork, was another hit, served in a generous portion that ensured leftovers for later enjoyment.

The seafood pancake, despite its stunning presentation, sadly fell short on flavor when set against the stellar lineup of other dishes.

I'd recommend this spot for a romantic date or a fun evening with friends, just remember to secure a reservation to avoid missing out on this culinary gem.

Came here to get the fried chicken and the fried porkchop bento box. Both the chicken and porkchop used the same breading and it kind of tasted the same. I enjoyed the chicken and it reminded me of other taiwanese popcorn chicken. The porkchop was just an inferior version of the chicken IMO. It seems like they knew how to do the chicken, and they just applied it to other meats. The bento comes with some rice, one tofu, one egg, and some cabbage. It helps you fill you up. I would just come here for the popcorn chicken tbh.

Title: A Lavish Hotpot Indulgence at Dalongyi

If you're seeking a luxe hotpot extravaganza, Dalongyi undoubtedly sets the bar high. My 7pm reservation for two was honored with prompt seating despite a bustling dining room. Our feast was sumptuous, with a final tally of $180 pre-tax and tip, reflecting the superior quality of the spread we indulged in.

The star of our table was the Dalongyi three-way pot, featuring a rich tomato base, earthy mushroom, and the signature beef oil chili broth – the first two winning my particular favor for their robust flavors and lighter oil content. The chili broth, ordered mild, offered a harmonious dance of spice and tingling sichuan peppercorns that still packed a punch.

The freshness of the fare was unmistakable. Portions were generous, a pleasant surprise compared to other upscale hotpot joints. Standouts included succulently marbled meat, premium angus ribeye, the delightfully chewy kung fu beef tripe, and savory Japanese black pork belly. Each cut showcased an exceptional quality that justified the price point.

Adventurous eaters will appreciate the duck intestines, while the shrimp paste and lobster balls were a testament to the seafood's freshness. A grand mushroom platter rounded out our vegetable selection, impressing with its variety and quality.

In summary, Dalongyi offers a hotpot experience that bears the marks of luxury and satisfaction. I wholeheartedly recommend a visit for anyone looking to explore the upper echelons of hotpot dining.

Amazing place and wonderful food!I came here for a private event on the rooftop and it was such an incredible time!The food was delicious - I had the salmon, pasta and vegetables. It was extremely fresh and delectable. Everything was cooked perfectly. I would most definitely come here for dinner, again.The rooftop views of Times Square were very enjoyable as well! There aren't too many places where you can get such an incredible view.The bartenders and servers were very friendly and comical, as well. I would highly recommend this place and would definitely come back here, again!

Heading to Thursday Kitchen, you'll find a lively tapas spot with a selection of delectable drinks that easily becomes the highlight of your dining experience. Unfortunately, they don't accept reservations over the phone, so eager diners often show up 30 minutes to an hour early to snag a spot for the evening. I aimed to be there 30 minutes before opening, but life had other plans, and I arrived 45 minutes post-opening. The consequence was a 1.5-hour wait – a testament to the restaurant's popularity and the price to pay for a walk-in-only policy.

Thankfully, the company was great, and the wait proved to be a small price for the culinary delight that followed. The anticipation only heightened the enjoyment of the meal, which was so memorable that I'm already looking forward to exploring how the menu changes with the seasons. Thursday Kitchen is a place I'll undoubtedly return to – the earlier the better.

This place is super tiny. There was just two counter seat inside, and a small table outside. I went in a cold winter day. Fortunately I was about to sit on the counter seat. Most of the people were taking out. I went with the famous crepe, which was Nutella banana and strawberry, with a scoop of ice cream. It was amazing.

Title: A Memorable Treat with a Side of Waiting

If unforgettable experiences tickle your fancy, this restaurant promises just that. However, a word to the wise: ensure your party is complete before attempting to be seated. We endured an hour's wait under the relentless December downpour due to a brief absence of one of our group, which turned into a seating saga.

The food, while tasty, teeters on the edge of "is the wait and price justifiable?" It's a question I'll leave you to ponder. But the shakes—oh, the shakes! They arrive not so much as a drink but as a spectacle, crowned with an entire piece of cake atop an imaginative, frosting-laden, sprinkle-embellished glass. It's this grandiose touch that might just turn your "maybe" into a resounding yes. Despite the initial hurdle, the shakes alone are an experience that you'll carry with you long after the last spoonful.

If you come to Balthazar and don't try the Cucumber Gin gimlet have you really been? Not their tag, just me being proud of myself for trying a new cocktail which I loved. Now if you couple your sexy cocktail with an oh so fresh and extremely tasty (seafood) ceviche, you've officially entered the (Freeyah) Knycky zone because that combination took me to a zone.Staff is mature, very mature looking and friendly. Kevin the barman, thanks for you suggestion dude. Their musuem-esque toilet is downstairs. I made  a friend or two on my both trips down and up. On my visit (Saturday evening), there was a nice loud family type vibe to it. Except for old dude in the corner I thought was with his daughter. Nah, that's not his child, you don't do that to your child. My eyes, my eyea. Haha. The End.

Restaurant Review:

I visited a chic speakeasy-type restaurant on 6/24, anticipating a smooth experience after their proactive communication for my 8:45pm reservation. While the alleyway entrance added to the intrigue, the initial service fell short. Despite assurance we'd be seated next, several duos were prioritized over us, which was disappointing after such effective pre-arrival updates.

Seated at 9pm, the ambiance was lively, complemented by a great music selection. The food was a hit—especially the decadent crispy potatoes with duck gravy and the expertly seasoned bacon. The burger impressed even without the usual toppings, although unexpected soggy fries arrived and appeared on our bill, causing some confusion.

Service slip-ups aside, the kale caesar was satisfactory, but the standout was the satisfying root beer float, and the on-site coffee shop seemed promising. While these hiccups marred what could've been a 4.5-star experience, I'm giving this establishment a tentative 3.5 stars. Future visits might prompt an updated review.

Recommendations: crispy potatoes with duck gravy, the burger (add egg and bacon), and a side of bacon.

Would I return? Yes, for the food quality and to see if service can match it next time.

Title: A Dining Disappointment in NYC

My recent dining experience at a local NYC eatery left much to be desired, turning a night out into a frustrating ordeal. Despite a friend's recommendation, the restaurant failed to meet even basic expectations.

The absence of a water station and restrooms in a sit-down establishment is perplexing and inconvenient. Furthermore, the staff's indifference, particularly from the cashier, set a negative tone from the start. To my surprise, the place was practically deserted on a Sunday evening, and the disengaged wait staff made no efforts to maintain a presentable dining area.

The menu was disappointingly limited and disproportionately priced. The dumplings I tried were unremarkable and could easily be outdone by a grocery store's frozen selection, yet they were priced four times higher. Additionally, the organic chicken noodle soup I ordered was so lackluster that I left it unfinished. Even my health-conscious wife struggled to find pleasure in her macro bowl, eating it more out of obligation than enjoyment.

The bottom line is that a restaurant charging such rates should at least offer the courtesy of basic amenities like water service. Dining here feels like a waste of both money and time. We ended up ordering takeout from our hotel in an attempt to salvage the evening—an extra expense, but necessary to erase the memory of this regrettable meal.

Delicious food, best eel I've ever had. Excellent service. I really disliked the decor. Painted black walls. Poor light. I think that would factor into my decision to return. Just not a space I want to spend much time in. But the eel was excellent, and the dishes that accompanied the eel were tasty as well (some type of rare daikon radish). I would recommend trying this place.

Title: Delightful Seafood Curry Noodle with A Dash of Disappointment

I had the pleasure of dining at this casual eatery on a Sunday night, and I must say, the ambiance was as inviting as the lack of a wait time. We were seated immediately, setting the stage for what I hoped would be a perfect dining experience.

The star of the show was undoubtedly the seafood curry noodle. The curry broth was aromatic and robust, complementing the perfectly chewy noodles that seemed eager to sop up the delightful flavors. A minor yet memorable highlight was the discovery of a hidden drawer at our table containing utensils and napkins—a charming touch that added a sprinkle of novelty to our meal.

Regrettably, the journey to culinary bliss was abruptly halted when a short black hair made an unsolicited appearance at the bottom of my bowl, intertwined with what remained of my seafood. This stray hair, most certainly not my own, was an unwelcome guest that marred an otherwise delightful dining experience.

In the end, while the food impressed, the hair incident prevented me from awarding a full five stars, landing this restaurant at a reluctant four-star review.

Title: A Hidden Gem in Ktown

I absolutely adore this restaurant! It's a breath of fresh air with its cleanliness, spaciousness, and tranquility – a rare find in the bustling Ktown scene. I was pleasantly surprised on a Saturday night to walk right in without a wait, likely due to its newness and tucked-away location within a building – just take the stairs or elevator up.

The dining experience was exceptional. My table enjoyed the beef tripe tofu stew and bulgogi vegetable bibimbap; both were delicious. Starting with complimentary appetizers that are refillable upon request was a nice touch. While the prices are in line with Ktown's popular spots (you might find cheaper versions in a food court), the quality here is evident.

I highly recommend visiting before the word gets out – this place is bound to become a hit! I'm certainly planning a few more visits myself.

I don't give out many 1 star reviews but this place nailed every criteria for it.  The place was busy when we came which is always a good sign but I left extremely disappointed. The Yelp reviews weren't flattering so I probably should have listened to the Yelp Nation on this one.Where do we begin. First off the waiter didn't seem to be listening to what I was ordering. I asked for my eggs cooked well without any runny yolk... that is pretty simple right? They come out over easy. He even takes them back because I guess he forgot and they STILL came back runny. I also ordered some avocado and there was an egg shell in them. Not good. Now you would think the eggs come with home fries like any normal diner. Nope. They came with frozen french fries that the waiter said were "the best". no home fries??! They were terrible.  We also got 2 cups of chicken noodle soup ($4 each) which wasn't bad. Also the check came with a whole bunch of numbers on them. I went to the counter and the lady couldn't even figure it out. It ended up being $46 for 2 people for lunch? We didn't get anything out of the ordinary but they probably tagged some more things on. Who knows and who cares... it was not a good experience. Very few 1 star reviews in my history but this is one of them.

First time we when, it was 8 of us. At the time, staff didn't have the iPads for taking orders. One person in our party was annoyed he had to wait for quite some time for his food and also had to order it twice. Second visit: My friend and I abandoned our plans to go to the movies when we agreed to hit up Kikoo again since we enjoyed our first visit. This time they had the iPad which seemed to make taking the order easier. So my friend is VERY specific when she orders certain items... I even told her that I'm not taking a picture of some of here food because people may misunderstand and think that the way they usually serve it. Will definitely return.

Title: Gastronomic Bliss at an Exclusive Spot

I recently revisited one of my absolute favorite restaurants, and it remains a slice of culinary heaven on earth. The dishes here are nothing short of amazing. Their tartare and mini burgers are mouthwatering, while the modified mac & cheese is a creative, comforting delight. But it’s the black cod that is simply divine; it’s so good that we shamelessly ordered seconds – and without regret!

The last time I dined, amidst the feast, there was one minor hiccup; the air conditioning was out of service, leaving us to rely on fans in the sweltering heat of July. Despite the discomfort, the food and drinks were so exceptional that it hardly dampened the experience. I trust the AC issue has since been resolved.

The service is consistently good, adding to the overall positive experience. A fun fact for newcomers: access to this gem is referral-only, adding an air of exclusivity. And for those who appreciate a side of history with their meal, the building was once owned by Andy Warhol, who even had a studio upstairs.

In conclusion, if you have the chance to be referred, don't hesitate. This restaurant is a must-visit for any serious food lover.

I could wax poetic about every dish I had at this restaurant, but others have articulated the experience with greater flair. Instead, I'll focus on a singular, unforgettable highlight: the Japanese Sea Urchin from Hokkaido, topped with truffle. An indulgence, it stands out as one of the most exquisite flavors I've had the pleasure of tasting. A word to the wise: when the time comes to settle the bill, you may want to shield your eyes. The cost is decidedly steep, but for that sea urchin alone, some may find the splurge justifiable.

Great value and super tasty!Dropped in here for a quick grab n go lunch today.  I did a little recon online and settled on the N2 bam bam noodles and the A1 tea eggs.The bam bam noodles were only of medium spice even with the extra spicy oil I asked for eith it. The flavor was still good and there was a lot of meat and noodles in the dish for less than $10.  The tea eggs were interesting. Once you crack the shell, you're left with a darkened egg but has lovely flavor from being boiled in tea, soy sauce, and spices.  For $3, you get two and it was highly worth trying something new.I came before noon but got my order in less than 5 minutes. That's some insane speed. Ample seating inside if you want to eat there.

I enjoyed a delightful lunch al fresco on a gorgeous day at this local dining spot, which proved to be a bastion of relaxation complemented by rapid, attentive service. My fish taco, while tasty, arrived slightly less than warm, a minor hiccup in an otherwise seamless experience. My companion's pesto chicken sandwich was a hit, boasting freshness and flavor that impressed. The expedited service enabled a leisurely yet efficient meal that fit perfectly into our lunch hour. Its proximity, just a block away from my office, is an added convenience that makes this restaurant a top choice for lunchtime.

I thoroughly enjoyed my recent visit to Javelina. The staff won me over with their exceptional friendliness and attentiveness. Despite the bustling atmosphere, our food arrived promptly, with the veggie quesadillas, brimming with fresh zucchini and squash, being an absolute highlight. The drinks didn't disappoint either; they were potently mixed and provided a delightful buzz. Moreover, the staff went above and beyond by assisting with additional lighting for my photographs — a charming touch of service. My only wish was for the option of a margarita pitcher to share with the table. Despite this minor point, my experience was overwhelmingly positive. I highly recommend Javelina, especially for their delicious veggie quesadillas.

I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant where simplicity meets excellence. The menu, featuring classics like pizza, fries, burgers, and sandwiches, is elevated by the evident quality and heartfelt preparation. Their lemonade is a must-try – refreshing and perfectly balanced, it's a standout.

I opted for the spicy chicken sandwich and I couldn't have been more pleased. It packed the right amount of heat, with zest that tickled the palate. The chicken was expertly thin-sliced, making each bite delectable, and the bun was simply heavenly. 

Kudos are also in order for the superb service that added to the delightful dining experience. This place has definitely nailed it with both their food and hospitality.

Title: A Stellar First Experience at the Equinox Hotel’s Restaurant

My inaugural visit to Hudson Yards concluded with a splendid dining affair at the Equinox Hotel's restaurant. Without reservations, my party and I were swiftly ushered into the outdoor lounge, a serene tableau bathed in the warm hues of the sunset.
