Nature's bluster nudged us indoors where the staff gracefully accommodated us in the cozy lounge area by the bar.

Commencing with the crispy polenta fries, each dish became a collective favorite, followed by the delightfully savory potato flatbread. The duck dumplings' understated flavors were the only dish that didn't quite tantalize my palate. While the salads burst with freshness, the side dishes were somewhat lackluster in comparison.

The heartier fare did not disappoint; the chickpea pasta was a standout amongst the mains, its flavors as vibrant as the setting sun. The other proteins, including the Berkshire pork and prime ribeye, were succulent companions to their sides, though some sides could benefit from a flavor boost to better complement the main attractions.

Dessert was a parade of indulgence with no holds barred – we sampled nearly every option. The chocolate moon rock emerged as a table favorite, though the strawberry & cream’s gluten-free decadence was a close second, and the innovative electric lemon curd sparked excitement with its playful pop rocks.

Set within a breathtaking venue suitable for celebrations, the Equinox Hotel restaurant charmed with its outstanding dishes, even if some were more memorable than others. It was a joy to dine amidst such opulent comfort, and I eagerly anticipate my next visit.

Cocktails we tried were amazing. Good crowd on the Friday night we visited. Food was definitely not authentic... and mehThe dumpling was gross... Salt and Pepper shrimp obviously was small low quality shrimp and I feel the shell was still on... Anyways would come back for the weekend night (also a dance spot at the basement) but run away from the food.

I'm truly disheartened to witness the decline of Ikinari Steak with their closures around town. Their "in and out" dining philosophy isn't just innovative, it's genius for the bustling lifestyle of the city-goer. The concept where you get your perfectly cooked steak on a hot cast iron platter quickly without skimping on flavor is unparalleled in New York City. The lunch specials are a steal, the service impeccable, and the prices don't break the bank. For anyone who's ever in a rush but refuses to compromise on quality, Ikinari Steak is your savior. I've never waited more than five minutes to be seated – a testament to their efficiency. And if you're a regular, don't miss out on their rewards program through the app; it's a great way to earn points on your meals. I miss the Park Avenue location dearly, but I'll cherish the innovative dining experience Ikinari Steak consistently delivers.

Title: A Quirky Gourmet Experience at Salt Bae's Burger Haven

I recently visited the much-talked-about Salt Bae Burger joint, a new gastronomic venture by none other than the viral YouTuber #saltbae himself. The restaurant strikes a unique balance between chic and casual, with servers dressed sharply, exuding an exotic flair amidst a clean yet diner-style setting. 

Notably, the establishment offers a complimentary vegetarian burger to women, a generous gesture that doesn't skimp on size or presentation, easily outshining the other menu options like the "easy burger" which I found a tad greasy and cheesy. 

The star of the show, however, is their "wet burger" – a succulent masterpiece tasting of seasoned cumin lamb that simply dissolves on the palate, an indulgence I couldn't recommend enough. On the side, the fries were a crunchy delight, and while we didn't indulge in the tempting milkshakes parading by, they're certainly on my list for next time.

The pricing is fair for the basics – our meal was just $20 – but be warned: indulgences here can add up, with luxury burgers hitting the $100 mark, not to mention the exclusive Voss bottled water on offer. 

Salt Bae's spot is certainly an innovative addition to the food scene, merging opulence with comfort food in a way that tantalizes both the palate and the imagination.

I recently dined at this charming spot and was thoroughly impressed by the authenticity and comfort imbued in each dish. The wonton soup provided a warming start, leading perfectly into the main courses. The braised pork with taro fell apart with just a nudge, and the pork dumplings delighted with their flavorful filling and pleasing texture. The crab tofu was another highlight, tender to the point of challenging chopstick skills. Although the string beans showed signs of age, their flavor profile was well-executed. Overall, a delightful culinary experience.

Cute interior/decor and probably good spot to go for girls drinks esp if you were in area shopping (right now probably easy to get last minute resi for a group) - but the food is relatively mediocre and service could be improved. Food. The good: frog legs and fries. Get the frog legs! It's a little scary but they really do taste like chicken and they are easy to eat as prepared by the restaurant. Basically like very mini drumsticks. The fries that came with the steak frites were also solid. Everything else was mediocre. The jus with the steak was meh and the steak itself was also nothing special (though I will say they did a decent job cooking medium rare as requested). We also had the gnocchi and agnolotti and both were just ok and also relatively small serving sizes. The bone marrow looks super impressive-looking but other spots in the city do this dish way more justice. Escargot was uniquely presented (instead of typical shelled pieces in a plate with divots to hold the snails, snails were still in their shells). Kind of fun but our group generally agreed we'd rather the other style so it was more soaked in flavor/sauce and easier to consume. Finally, the deconstructed peach cheesecake was incredibly bland. Beautifully plated but not enough to make up for the disappointing lack of any real flavor. Would have preferred actual pieces of peaches vs the useless pretty flower petals. Service. Waitress basically forgot about us- we put in an order of apps and then had to struggle to flag her down to place entree orders and then again later to get our check. She also forgot to apply the yelp discount (despite us showing and confirming with her literally when we asked her to give us the check). A manager or another individual helped us with it, and then when she came back to process it on our credit card she took forever - we could see her from our table and it seemed she was confused.

I recently dined at this gem during restaurant week and was thoroughly impressed by the freshness and flavors on offer. The tomatoes in both the salads and the caprese were notably crisp, boasting a perfect balance that enhanced each dish. The standout for me was the Crudo di Salmone, which I highly recommend for its exquisite taste. To top it off, the dessert portions were incredibly generous – one dessert could easily satisfy a party of three. A delightful dining experience that I would urge food lovers to try.

I haven't had the pleasure of eating this pizza in-person. My husband and I have had plans of coming here for as long as I can remember. With all the craziness going on in the world, we finally caved and ordered online (through Goldbelly) instead.One word to describe this pizza: wow. The spicy pepperoni is out of this world. The crust is delightfully crispy yet doughy. The fresh, mild mozzarella is the perfect complement to the spicy pepperoni. Pairs perfectly with a nice, cold beer.We cannot wait to try in person. This is some of the next (and most unique) pizza we have ever had.

A european style bistro, ideal restaurant for any occasion: a Sunday brunch, a night for fancy cocktails, a dinner celebration or lets feel we are in Paris dinner.  The holiday light decorations twinkled and the Christmas tree as the showstopper in the middle of the restaurant. The decorations amplified my Christmas feels despite it's the 28th of December. The staff were top notch and worked well together, bringing the dining experience to the next level. For appetizers, I got the bowl of mussels, perfectly steamed and the sauce, delicious to sip like a bowl of soup. I paired my starter with the Nathalie cocktail, a refreshing, balanced drink, garnished with pomegranate seeds. My dining partner had the Oui Mademoiselle cocktail, liquor mixed with berry puree, topped with a pine leaf as decor. These cocktails were fantastic and worth every sip. The weather called for French onion soup and to overfill the cup with gooey Gruyere cheese, yes please.My main course was the Steak Frites, made medium, the meat soft, not chewy. The steak was topped with peppercorn sauce, a distinctive flavor and a delicious dipping sauce for my crispy french fries. My dining partner had the short rib cavatelli made al dente, not too soft or overcooked. The braised short rib was fork-tender and the ricotta added a bit of sweetness to the dish. We paired our main dish with red wine, suggested by the waiter.  To complete the meal, My dining partner and I shared the lava cake with rich, warm chocolate filling, that came with vanilla ice cream and berries, the perfect palate cleanser.      Thank you to The Consulate management for an amazing dinner experience, tres magnifique!

Tucked within a fancy midtown hotel lies an overpriced dining disappointment. The menu, while alluring on paper, failed to translate into palatable pleasure. My Dutch Orange Soufflé Pancake arrived in a cast iron skillet, deceptively cold and uninviting. The soufflé's intended lightness was absent, replaced by an unwelcome density. The intrigue of embedded oranges turned sour, imparting a bitterness that lingered far beyond the first bite. As a devotee of culinary shows, my anticipation was high, but the reality left me underwhelmed. The bustling crowd and waitlist upon departure befuddled me—perhaps they came with different expectations or simply for the ambiance. The meal's one saving grace was the attentive and pleasant waiter, a beacon of warmth in an otherwise lackluster experience.

Nice little Japanese spot for sushi and cooked dishes. The sushi quality is decent; Marumi is in a tier above the more affordable sushi joints but not quite high end. In this sense, prices are on point. I appreciate the diverse menu, including rice dishes, noodles, and an array of appetizers. The early bird dinner special offers good value and a lot of options. Service is polite and accommodating without any hovering. I'd go again if I'm in the area.

Wow! What a find in adorable Little Italy! No where else can beat this homemade pasta! Our server friendly, honest about the kitchen's "situation" (slow & behind) and on top of our water needs as it felt like it was 90 degrees inside! Seated upstairs in what looked to be a cute room with windows, we couldn't quite enjoy all the atmosphere as the place was STIFLING hot. Besides the uncomfortable room, the burrata appetizer was excellent. I ordered the chicken Parmesan, which was way too spicy for my taste but my friends homemade pasta in a light cream pepper sauce with prosciutto and peas was delicious! I wish the menu had said how spicy the chicken was because I would have ordered something else.  Definitely more homemade pasta.

This has become my go-to place for post-run brunch, and it hits the spot! Most important is that the coffee is great, like really great, and the refills are free. This makes me happy. Food is good and quick, and the counter ordering system is actually really nice because you don't have to try to flag someone for a check when you're ready to go. Nice job guys!

Joe's Pizza epitomizes the classic New York slice with its crispy thin crust, spot-on cheese-to-toppings ratio, and foldability factor for the ultimate NYC experience. Our taste test included the mushroom, supreme, and white pizza, each one a delightful treat after meandering through Times Square. With doors open until 2:30 am, Joe's is your go-to for that late-night pizza craving. Highly recommended for a savory slice of the city that never sleeps.
Not bad but as Peruvian chicken, Pio Pio is much better.Stir Fry Veggies surprisingly delicious though really enjoyed the flavor.

Title: Mixed Feelings at the BBQ Joint

During my recent visit to a local barbecue restaurant, the experience was a rollercoaster of tastes and textures. The standout was the brisket, which impressed with its super tender profile that fell apart effortlessly, hinting at a skillful low-and-slow cooking process.

However, the dirty frites, a dish combining fries with barbecue sauce and burnt ends, fell flat with its stale-tasting fries that lacked the fundamental crispiness and heartiness of real potatoes. The burnt ends accompanying them also missed the mark, not achieving the anticipated crunch.

On the side, the mac and cheese promised comfort but delivered disappointment. Although it contained an abundant amount of cheese, the dish’s texture was a letdown, arriving solidified rather than creamy, making it difficult to differentiate the pasta from the cheese concoction.

The spare ribs, slightly redeemed by an accompanying barbecue sauce, were unfortunately on the dry side. A variety of pickled vegetables were available to complement the meal, providing a much-needed tangy counterpoint to the meats.

In conclusion, while the barbecue meats had their moments, particularly the brisket, the sides were a collection of missed opportunities. The restaurant shines in the meat department but could benefit greatly from an overhaul of its side dish offerings.

Nice little place. Very good service - they had it booked but allowed us to have the table until a certain time, that was awesome of them as we wanted a fast meal.Appetizers were both refreshing. We got:-Lobster tacos-Tuna tartarDinners:-Sea-bass with potatoes- very good-Salmon with truffle potato mash- this was excellent Dessert:-Warm mixed berry cobbler with vanilla bean ice cream- worth a try

Title: A Hidden Gem for Food and Jazz - The Flatiron Room

I recently celebrated a friend's birthday at The Flatiron Room and was blown away by the experience. This spot is known for its live jazz, but the food deserves a headline of its own. The menu, which the manager informed me was recently overhauled, is nothing short of spectacular, ensuring that they will soon be known as much for their culinary delights as their music. Every dish we sampled, from starters to entrees, was a hit - crafted with care and bursting with flavor.

The ambiance strikes a perfect chord between fun and sophisticated, providing an ideal backdrop for the two incredibly talented jazz bands that performed. Add to that the attentive and polished service, and you have a venue that hits all the right notes. The Flatiron Room is a must-visit for anyone looking for an exceptional dining experience complemented by top-notch entertainment.

Title: A Bite of Bliss at Han's: More than Just a Meal

From the moment my dining companion's Bibimbap ($16) graced our table, it was clear that Han's was going to offer an experience sprinkled with delight. The dish, a mosaic of vibrant ingredients, offered comfort that extended beyond its immediate consumption, proving to be just as satisfying as leftovers.

Han, the culinary maestro of the establishment, serves a tofu dish that's nothing short of a flavor festival – black sesame dressing paired with fried onions creating a dish that outshines the traditional agedashi in both appeal and excitement. While I missed the advertised cauliflower in the mix, the unique touch didn't go unnoticed.

The small plates were memorable showcases of skill, particularly the baby octopus. Its light charring paved the way for a symphony of sweet, acidic, and tender notes. The side of Kimchi accompanying the Bossam was exemplary; however, the pork bellies themselves fell short of the same acclaim.

Regrettably, fullness precluded a foray into desserts, but the black sesame Panna Cotta beckons for next time, along with a promised indulgence in black sesame ice cream. Other offerings like dumplings, grilled bulgogi, and the fire-grilled meats were satisfactory but didn't ignite the same excitement.

Han's ambiance is a testament to aesthetic pleasure, from the sturdy wooden tables to the earthy plates and linen-adorned staff. On arrival, the buzz of a busy service was palpable – our pre-reserved table at 5:45pm stood as the last bastion of calm before a bustling evening.

In essence, Han's has etched itself as a culinary haunt I eagerly anticipate revisiting. It’s a place that melds taste with artistry, beckoning at least one more indulgent encounter.

Came here knowing that it's an overpriced place but well still wants to support asian restaurant here just hope it can last longer.Like everyone else said, it's smells great, but quite tasteless... So I think it tasted almost like on the healthy side. Which I guess is fine.Radish and pork feet was the best, both had enough flavor and soft.Skip the Napa cabbage that was not cooked enough and extremely lack in flavor. I know you probably don't want to cook longer since vegetable shrinks, but cmon, you can't cheat on Napa cabbage for Lu Wei.......

Review Time: I work down the street from this joint. The restaurant was huge which would be perfect to throw a birthday or Holiday party. As we sat down, the water gave us water. Something was stuck on the inside of the glass, so he was like "have this water (which there was one next to me waiting for a coworker to drink). To be honest, the service sucked, I couldn't count how many times we flagged down the waiter. The food was good but not the greatest. It's a one in a life time experience to try their food experience.Food: Appetizer, it tasted great. I actually enjoyed the taste and texture of this dish. A lot of flavors were there. Lunch Entree,  first the meatballs were super dry and a little burnt. I couldn't taste the lamb which is one of my favorite tastes. The veggies were burnt which totally threw the dish off and ruined it for me. The squash purée was the only thing that hit the spot. Dessert, the flourless chocolate cake was good but a little too much, so I advise you to share with a friend or family member. Also pair it with red or white wine. For the restaurant, my advice is to eliminate the white crap and replace it with a raspberry sauce (you're welcome). Will I recommend this place to folks? Ehh, I'll think on it. Will I eat her again? No, I will be sitting at the bar during their HH because it close to my work.

My recent dining experience at this establishment offered a clean atmosphere complemented by delectable dishes and enjoyable drinks. However, the price point felt steep; even during restaurant week, the bill for two approached a hefty $200. While the food was seasoned to perfection, the cost, particularly of the beverages, was unexpectedly high. Service-wise, our server was amiable and showed great hospitality, although he appeared somewhat scattered and even made an error on our bill. The quality of the meal was undeniable, but the value proposition may be a consideration for those mindful of their budget.

Title: A Salt Overload at [Restaurant Name]

I recently visited [Restaurant Name], enticed by their much-talked-about tomato toast. Unfortunately, my experience took a turn for the worse due to an extreme amount of salt in the dish. It wasn't just the overpowering taste; the sodium levels were so high that they led to physical discomfort for hours after the meal, including noticeable swelling in my hands and feet.

I observed the chef liberally seasoning dishes, which in hindsight, should have been a red flag. While I don’t typically react to salt, the quantity used here was excessive and most likely not of the higher quality sea salt variety.

This experience was not just disappointing but genuinely concerning as it has prompted me to seek medical advice to ensure there are no serious repercussions to my health. It's a stark reminder that while culinary showmanship can be entertaining, it should never come at the cost of a diner's well-being.

Great quality pizza, pretty long lines bit they've got a friendly staff and even a bouncer in front to keep things under control. While the pizza was flavorful, toasty dough, sweet sauce, great cheese, basil, and all the right criteria, our first slice was cold, and our second slice was forgotten in the oven. So, forgetting about those little inconveniences, it's certainly worth frequenting for a late night pizza fix.

Good food and an interesting experience. I ordered from the 3-course dinner menu: venison, hen of the wood, and arctic bird's nest. Each course was flavorful, was presented well, and fit their wintry forest motif. The arctic bird's nest seems to be one of their most famous dishes, and it was the most elaborately assembled one that I had that night. Three eggs with a very thin white chocolate "shell" and a goat-cheese parfait "yolk" inside. Takes some finesse. There were 5 amuse-bouches that acted as mini-courses: hibiscus tea, bread, gravlax, ice cream, petit fours. Although it didn't detract much from their food, Aquavit doesn't always strike a perfect balance between taste and concept. The fennel marshmallow is unusual, but it doesn't taste any better than an ordinary marshmallow. The nasturtium leaves on top of the venison appetizer ultimately don't add much compared to ordinary garnishes. The biggest criticism I have is that Aquavit's theme is largely an illusion that falls apart easily upon closer inspection. They describe themselves as a seasonal Nordic restaurant. A few menu items are authentic Scandinavian--the gravlax, for example--but most aren't. Mangalica pork? Hungarian breed. 7X beef? From Colorado. Montana trout? Yup. Pacing was maybe slightly slow for a 3-course menu. That's in part because there were several mini-courses, but there was still a bit of a pause. Gives you a chance to talk though. Service was fine. Efficient coat check (didn't need a ticket, probably because I had a reservation). Slight wait at the bar though I had a reservation. No published dress code. I'd say half the men wore jackets and most of the rest wore business casual. The bathrooms are ordinary but fine. The paper hand towels are luxurious.

Title: A Wing Fling at IWF - Where Cravings Meet Satisfaction

Last night's wing craving led me to a delightful discovery: the quaint IWF. Although small, the eatery offers a cozy dine-in experience with a straightforward menu that punches above its weight with an impressive lineup of 18 house-made sauces.

I dove straight into the wing selection, thrilled to find that IWF uses all-natural chicken, a testament to their quality. The standout for me was the bright, zesty cilantro-based sauce that, when coupled with their extra crispy wings, resulted in a flavor fiesta. For those who dare, the spiciest sauce on offer is a daring challenge – it was indeed a tad too fiery for my palate.

Not overlooking the rest of the menu, the buffalo chicken sandwich was scrumptious despite its gloriously messy nature, hitting the spot thoroughly. The dusted fries were a savory treat, loaded with cheese, bacon, and cilantro, and I confess, I couldn't resist the allure of a good ketchup drizzle.

Pricing felt fair, ensuring a guilt-free indulgence. For those preferring the comfort of their own space, delivery is available within the vicinity.

The experience was rounded off with sterling service. The warmth and eagerness of the staff, including the owners who mingled and chatted with guests, added a personal touch to the dining adventure.

IWF is definitely on my radar for future visits. Whether you're a wing enthusiast or simply searching for a satisfying meal, IWF promises a return-worthy experience.

Title: A City Gem Not To Be Missed!

I recently dined at this urban hotspot for the first time, and the experience was nothing short of spectacular! Ana, our server, set the stage with her swift, amiable service, ensuring every detail was perfect throughout our meal. Despite the restaurant's evident popularity, as evidenced by the quick-forming line, my wait was a mere 10 minutes—a testament to their efficiency. And the food? Absolutely amazing! To anyone considering a visit, take my advice: don't hesitate. It's thoroughly worth it!

Title: Unfulfilled Expectations at Ruby's

My anticipation for trying Ruby's in Kip's Bay was met with disappointment. For a place that appears charming from the outside, the dining experience fell short. An initial gut feeling suggested we leave upon seating, and retrospectively, we should have.

The Kale salad I ordered was unremarkable and suffered from a bland Tahini dressing. My dining partner, Jayson, found the sweet potato fries inedible to the point of returning them and was equally dissatisfied with the Brussel sprouts.

The lackluster service exacerbated our experience, which was surprising given the staff-to-guest ratio in such a small setting. Although Ruby's has its advocates as per online reviews, our visit simply didn't align with the positive feedback. Ruby's could be a hit for some, but sadly, it wasn't for us.

I was pleasantly surprised during my recent visit to the restaurant where I ordered the curry chicken quinoa bowl. The flavors were delightful and every bite was packed with taste. However, I was a tad disappointed to find my meal served lukewarm rather than hot off the stove. Despite this, the overall experience was enjoyable enough to merit a return visit in the future.

Title: A Slice of Heaven with a Side of Attitude

I recently had the pleasure of tasting what could arguably be described as some of the best pizza out there. The Margherita was a standout - that cheese was sheer perfection on a slice. Even as someone who isn't usually a pepperoni enthusiast, I was pleasantly surprised by their Pepperoni square slice. Crispy, savory, and just plain delicious.

However, the experience was slightly marred by the customer service. The staff, particularly the gentleman taking orders, could definitely work on their friendliness. Additionally, for some reason, there's a slow-moving line that seems disproportionate to the simplicity of ordering pizza. Patience will be your virtue here. 

But let's not get bogged down by service when the pizza is this good. It's worth the wait, and a must-try for pizza aficionados.

We stopped here for lunch after taking a tour of the catacombs, nearby.  This is the real deal: small, authentic, and family owned.  The staff are friendly and attentive.  The decor is simple but inviting.  Menu is focused but has plenty of options to please everyone.  We opted for Cesar salad, a (very large) bowl of lentil soup, and a margherita pizza.  Service was fast.  The food was hot, fresh, and very tasty.  Loved the slightly thicker yet still crunchy pizza crust, which appears to be more Sicilian style than Neapolitan style.  Prices are very reasonable.  Everyone left full and happy.  Highly recommended.

Title: Sizzling Satisfaction at Samwon

If you're yearning for top-notch Korean BBQ, Samwon is a must-visit that impressively outshines its competitor Jongro with superior quality and flavor. Although on the pricier side, the cost is justified by the restaurant's inviting ambiance and recent sleek renovation, which includes an expansive second floor—perfect for group dining. However, planning ahead with a reservation is wise, particularly on bustling weekends.

While Samwon's menu extends beyond BBQ, most offerings come across as unremarkable, save for the unique and delightful egg soufflé. Its customizable toppings add a special touch that’s not commonly found elsewhere. In conclusion, Samwon is the go-to for an unparalleled Korean BBQ experience amidst a few average dishes, with the egg soufflé as a noteworthy exception.

I had the opportunity to come sample some of what Pig Heaven had to offer this summer, for a special "summer tasting menu" hosted by Lisa, owner of the restaurant. Having tasted Lisa's other venture, Zest Szechuan in Midtown, I was very excited to see what new things the kitchen had cooking up in the UES. From the service, to the variety of foods offered, to the ambiance - it was absolutely delightful. My friend and I got the chicken soong appetizer to start (minced chicken with vegetables, in a savory sauce with lettuce wraps on the side) - delicious, and probably my favorite thing of the meal. For entrees, we got the BBQ spare rib as recommended, and the ginger and scallion soft shell crab. The BBQ spare rib was a little sweet and lacked the smokiness that I crave and have grown accustomed to from Chinese BBQ, but the rib itself was still well cooked and delicious nonetheless. The traditional Chinese soft shell crab is served with salt and pepper, but since they had another sauce (ginger-scallion), we decided to try that instead. The crab itself was delicious, juicy and soft on the inside, but the sauce on the outside unfortunately fell just off the mark for me - it had the same flavor as the appetizer, and as it was a wet sauce it lost the signature crunch that I was looking for in soft shell crab. All that being said, this place is a great place to take your family, have a group gathering (there were two 8+ people parties eating there when we went), for a quick meal before heading off to the many museums on the East side (4 blocks away from the Met, holla), and is definitely one of the better Chinese food options in the upper east side. Thank you to Lisa and the entire staff who graciously hosted us for lunch, we will be back again!

Great sushi!! We sat at the bar and ordered three rolls: salmon avocado, spicy tuna and California. The sushi was so fresh and the rice was very sticky. We didn't even need to add soy or ginger--tasty enough as is! Our bartender was very friendly and personable. We ordered a pollinator cocktail. It tasted like sour patch kid candy-- very good!

Title: A Brunch to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

I recently celebrated a surprise birthday brunch at [Restaurant Name] with a couple of friends and was thoroughly impressed by the experience. The highlight on the menu for me was the Grilled steak and fromage sandwich – a savory delight that tantalized my taste buds. My friends opted for sweeter options, indulging in pancakes and French toast, both met with our unanimous approval for their deliciousness. The food quality was matched by its value – reasonably priced and satisfying.

Service at [Restaurant Name] was top-notch, thanks in no small part to our waiter's enthusiasm and genuine warmth, which added a welcoming touch to our celebration. The birthday festivities were taken up a notch with a sparkling dessert and a lively rendition of Birthday Song by 3 Chainz, much to my joy.

However, the ambiance, while generally charming and fitting for a brunch spot, was marred slightly by the overwhelming volume of the music. Positioned directly under a stereo, we struggled to converse without shouting, which detracted from the overall experience.

Despite the acoustic hiccup, the experience was memorable. The combination of delectable food, inviting service, and a quaint atmosphere makes [Restaurant Name] a recommendable and affordable brunch venue.

Title: A Satisfying Dim Sum Delight at XO Kitchen

After an exhausting day exploring museums, my dining companion and I stumbled upon XO Kitchen in Chinatown, hankering for some authentic Chinese cuisine. To our delight, XO Kitchen serves dim sum all day and night – a rarity that we were all too eager to take advantage of.

The décor is unpretentious and it's cash-only here, but that's no issue for those with a keen focus on the food. We were ushered to the back room, which was a welcome respite from the bustle of the main seating area. 

Our table was soon brimming with a selection of dim sum, including perfectly steamed pork spareribs, succulent beef rice noodles, and the daring choice of chicken feet, each dish bursting with flavor. We also dove into the heartier mabutofu with rice, satisfying pan-fried chicken chow mein, and a sweet and savory barbecue pork lo mein.

Every bite was a delight, and by the end of the meal, our plates were wiped clean – not a single morsel left behind to take back to our hotel. The experience left us wholly satisfied, and it's safe to say we'd return to XO Kitchen in a heartbeat if time allowed.

Title: Refreshing Vegan Treat at by Chloe

I recently stopped by by Chloe for a quick snack and had a pleasant experience. It's worth noting this is a vegan, plant-based eatery with a menu that may seem limited to some, but I appreciated the curated selection as it wasn't overwhelming.

The dining space is spacious, offering a comfortable environment to enjoy a meal. A minor inconvenience is the restriction to credit/debit card payments only; no cash transactions accepted.

Most of the baked items left were chocolate-based, which I wasn't in the mood for, and the banana bread seemed a bit too dense for my liking. However, I settled on a red velvet cupcake, modestly priced at around $5. Though smaller in size when compared to neighboring stores, it was a perfect snack-sized portion. The cupcake was notably less sweet than anticipated, which was a delightful surprise. Plus, it came in an adorable, convenient box, adding to the overall experience.

For fellow patrons with canine companions, there are also puppy biscuits available - a quirky and considerate touch.

I'm hopeful for a wider variety of non-chocolate baked goods in the future, but for now, the red velvet cupcake at by Chloe gets a thumbs up for those seeking a sweet yet not overly indulgent vegan treat.

Came here to celebrate our 12th anniversary and high hopes because of the great reviews. We had reservations which was a good idea because it was pretty packed which was surprising to me on a Monday night. We were seated in the middle area of the restaurant between two tables that were pretty close to us (which meant lack of privacy in our conversation). We started off with the oysters on the special menu, chowder soup and crab guacamole. All of the apps were just ok I've certainly had better. I did enjoy the Cabernet (which i wrote down the name) and my hubs liked the blueberry bourbon drink he had. For the main i got the lobster roll with fries. Lobster roll had a bit too much lime so had a bit of a tart taste but they gave a lot of lobster meat and the fries we good. We ended up spending $200 on our meal which i don't think was really worth it. If we came back It would be for the happy hour.

Title: Fresh Mediterranean Flavors in the Heart of FiDi

I just checked out the new Mediterranean spot that's opened its doors in the Financial District, and it's a build-your-own bowl concept similar to Chipotle. The variety of fresh vegetables immediately caught my eye – a real highlight for someone who appreciates their greens.

On my visit, I opted for a bowl packed with crisp lettuce, wholesome wheat rice, a hearty mix of potatoes and vegetables, and the well-seasoned chicken doner. While the ingredients were fresh, the execution felt a bit haphazard as everything seemed to be hastily tossed into the bowl.

A quick tip for first-timers: snag a menu before you queue up for the made-to-order line. It's the key to a smooth ordering experience since there aren't any signs to guide you through the offerings. Also, be prepared to project your voice a bit to communicate your choices or to inquire about the dishes.

Once you get a hang of their system and figure out your preferred flavor combinations, I'm confident your next visit will be even more satisfying. This place has the potential to be a go-to for a quick, customizable, and healthy meal in FiDi.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Local Dim Sum Spot

Upon visiting this dim sum restaurant, my experience left much to be desired. The quiet atmosphere, with the place being three-quarters empty, contrasted sharply with the number of staff present, who despite their friendliness, lacked attentiveness. It took a while before we were even provided with water, a basic courtesy I would have expected to be prompt.

On to the food—the dim sum was a hit or miss. The Shu Mai stood out, its combination of shrimp and pork striking the right notes of flavor and texture. Similarly, the Buddha Delight Dumplings met expectations, delivering both taste and satisfaction.

However, the meal took a downturn with the shredded duck wonton soup, which arrived lukewarm at best. Even after requesting it to be reheated, the soup failed to impress, leading us to abandon it after a few sips. The taro cilantro and pork dumplings also missed the mark for me, although my companion found them to be acceptable.

The saving grace for this establishment might be its prices, which are quite reasonable for the area, with dim sum items ranging between $6.75 and $11.95.

In conclusion, while the cost is a plus, the service and inconsistent quality of the food are notable drawbacks. A restaurant's size and busyness should not excuse a lack of attention to patrons—this aspect needs significant improvement.

Nothing like ramen when the weather drops by like, 3 whole degrees. It's the first thing I crave when it is even remotely chilly out. Or even just, not hot out. Like, if maybe I should wear a light sweater just in case, I want ramen. Our table of 8 got a table right away around 11:45, always a plus. We started off with a few appetizers: the takoyaki and the shrimp shumai. The takoyaki was like a fried octopus ball, it came 4 to an order and were really tasty. It was more creamy than just fried dough, which I really liked. The shrimp shumai were also soooo good. Basically just shrimp dumplings without the breading. Get all the apps because they are that good and also they are 50% when you order a lunch entree. I got the tonkatsu ramen and it was delicious. The broth was packed with flavor, the pork was so soft, and the noodles were plentiful and perfectly cooked. I could barely finish half of it, the bowl was so big. I definitely recommend this spot. Check in on Yelp for 20% off!

On my return visit to the restaurant, I decided to try the a la carte menu, hoping for a repeat of the excellent experience I had during the omakase at the sushi bar previously. Unfortunately, I have to dock a star this time around. The sashimi bowl, although still on the pricey side, did not live up to expectations. Particularly concerning was the freshness of the fish, especially the uni, which was noticeably below par. It must have been an off night for the kitchen, as my last experience here was outstanding. Despite the mishap, I'll remember the restaurant for its earlier high-quality offering.

It is a fancy Indian restaurant with good food and great ambience. Pros-ambience is really great-food is good. (Vegetable and bread is good)-they have great variety of breads.Cons-quantity is very less-little priceyRecommendations:-Make a reservation. It is a huge two floored restaurant but generally very pack. -Mint parathas, onion kulcha-panner lababdar-Daal makhani-Amritsari sikhThose who love Indian food you need to try this place.

Title: Disappointing Return to Casa Mono

As much as I regret to say it, my recent visit to Casa Mono fell dramatically short of my initial impression. The excitement for a repeat experience was met with a barrage of disappointments.

To begin, the Bacalao Croquettas with Orange Aioli were overwhelmingly salty, to the point of being inedible – a sentiment that was acknowledged by our waiter but not reflected on the bill until I pointed it out. Alongside this lapse, the service was marred by a careless handling of our wine, neglecting it to warm under the sun for an unacceptable duration.

The Pulpo with Fennel and Grapefruit was bland and unappetizing, resembling a pureed dish devoid of the expected culinary finesse. The Red Snapper, while a step in the right direction with a complimenting sauce, was overshadowed by its meager portion size and its steep price.

The Sweetbreads with Fennel al Mono, despite their intriguing texture, were compromised by overly crunchy garnishes, making them a challenge to enjoy. It was only the Confit Goat with Avocado Queso that managed to satisfy, being well-flavored and appropriately portioned – a safe bet that seemed popular among diners.

Regrettably, with just one out of five dishes hitting the mark and service that detracted from the dining experience, I can only justify a one-star rating for Casa Mono. It's a stark contrast to what one could find at superior tapas establishments like Boqueria.

Last Friday evening, my wife and I decided to visit a bustling German restaurant and bar, and it certainly lived up to the cozy ambiance we had heard about. Although faced with a considerable wait of 30-45 minutes, the experience that followed was worth it. We started with Potato Pancakes, which were delightfully crispy and perfectly complemented by apple sauce.

For my main dish, I savored the Bauernwurst, which came with two richly flavored sausages and a potato salad that was nothing short of exceptional. My wife enjoyed her entree (the specifics of which escape me) just as much. I stuck with water, while she paired her meal with a beer, adding to the authentic vibe.

The portions were generous, leaving us extremely satisfied with leftovers in tow. Our visit was marked by a warm atmosphere and scrumptious food. A word to the wise for our next visit – and there will be a next time – is to order conservatively. The potato pancakes alone could suffice for a fulfilling meal!

Happened upon this Sutton Place area cafe that looks more like a bar than the named Beach Cafe. Even the decor doesn't really scream beach or a full on cafe. I'm going to presume the owner likes the beach and just wanted a different name to keep things interesting. LOL  Truth be told, it has a neighborhood charm feel to it even though no one on Yelp seems to get why it is. Just accept it...and between us, I don't think they're hurting from the confusion or lack of stellar Yelp reviews.As I entered shortly after 9am on this brisk 10 degrees January morning, I noticed i was the only customer.  Sign says breakfast served at 8am so I was excited to find a sit down (non-diner/non fast food-esque) place here in the East 70's. I had a choice of table, any seat I liked. I parked myself at a table closest to the bar so I could see the TV screen. Dining alone gives me time to read my newspaper or watch the TV without cartoons on.  ;-)TV's at the bar were set to cable TV news and stock tickers scrolling across the screen. But interestingly, the music playing was rhythm and blues with jazzy songs in between. As I write this, I'm listening to "Unforgettable" (song by Nat King Cole), however it's sung by a woman...snazzy. Looking over the decor while I was settling in, I see Frank Sinatra on the wall. Guess that review I saw about the Friday night vibes and singers has something to do with the other singers on the walls.I couldn't decide what to eat with the yummy breakfast menu before me but I always love a Croque Madam if the opportunity presents itself. While the variety of eggs Benedict options were plenty, I had to take up this opportunity to try the French breakfast.I ordered hot coffee as well...boy it was plenty hot.  Then when my breakfast plate appeared, it was just the right temperature to drink without wincing. My plate was packed with goodies... Side salad with house dressing to accompany my breakfast open faced sandwich. The eggs were perfectly sunny side up, on top of melty gruyere, tomatoes, and ham. The toasted French bread was a bit charred on the sides but soft and warm otherwise. Perfect. The sandwich was so filling and served with lightly seasoned tator tots. Great breakfast indeed. There was even a mini blueberry muffin served warm, on the side. Didn't need it as my plate was plenty full but it was a nice touch.By the time I was halfway through my meal, some locals came in as the waiter, Singh, seemed to know them by name or by their face. He even knew what they liked to order... Asking if they wanted the usual. At this point, he's already refilled my water and coffee without me asking for anything.Not sure what the bad reviews are about but I had no such experience here. I am curious though about the name of the place and unless there's some personal reason to keep the beach theme, this place doesn't need it. It is a cool cafe. I can just picture why it's the cat's meow on a happening Friday evening even though I was here in the daytime. Food was on point and service was great. I'd love to return for the boozy brunch I read about if I'm ever in this hood again.

Been here a few times and it's always been busy.Located on Prince St near Mott St in Soho.I've seen this place a bunch of times on restaurant review guides for the best pizza in NYC. It hasn't been until recently that I had a chance to stop by.Had to wait over 20 minutes the first time I tried this place. I think it was a combination of we caught them in the middle of making new pizzas and the number of people waiting, that led to the long wait. Tried the infamous pepperoni square slice. I was impressed by the taste of the slice. I'm usually not the biggest fan of pepperoni on pizza, but I liked this slice. Nice and crispy and flavorful without being overpowering. The portion sizes were decent. For me two slices was pretty filling.It was a little pricey, but considering the location it wasn't too bad.

Came on a Sunday noon, and there was no line at all. Both setup of the restaurant and the taste of the noodle soup is the same as that in Tokyo. Undoubtedly, the noodle soup tastes amazing, Flavorful creamy soup, great charshu topping, and noodle with texture. However, I find it a bit too pricey. Paying 20+ bucks for ramen is a bit overwhelming.In all, good to try if you want to experience authentic ramen, but maybe no need to become a regular. There are other ramen places as good as ichiran but much cheaper

Last night was our anniversary of 4 years and was looking for a nice soul food spot. We saw this on yelp and came to try it. There are many mixed reviews but mostly good. Here is my take on this restaurant.What I liked:The owner/chef of the restaurant comes out and greets everyone. He is very warm and friendly I certainly appreciate that greatly. The lady who was the server was phenomenal and very helpful when serving and taking the orders. The atmosphere was very quiet which was perfect but a little music does help.What I liked foodwise:The mac and a lotta cheese were on point. That is the way it is supposed to be done. Collard Greens was done the way my mom and dad would have made it with the ham hocks inside, however, adding black-eyed peas to it is different and yet delicious.What I didn't like including the food:The meatloaf was well seasoned and delicious, however it is supposed to be very moist on the inside and outside. The take on frying it was not all that good. It made it harder around the edges. It was supposed to be like a chicken fried steak but meatloaf isn't usually chicken. My friends' grits was ok and it could've used a little more salts and butter. The skirt steak was beautiful. Everything but the steak was seasoned well. The fact they ran out of okra so fast was like Oh my goodness but it wasn't the end of the world.Finally was the drink I created which was so darn expensive it should be cheaper, half lemonade, half iced tea with Whiskey came to $36 in a small glass. No way, smh is that possible, even in a restaurant like The Cheesecake factory that would've been lower.We was here to celebrate our anniversary and the atmosphere was nice, the food was ok, the customer service was on point I was looking for a reason to come back. I made the reservation online and said I was here to celebrate. Even asking about the first dance song or what can we do to help you celebrate would've been fiyah but it sort of wasn't. That's where the soul food part of this restaurant was missing. Soul food isn't just about the food but it is also about the vibe, the love, the passion, the music and family orientation of place. This is more like southern food in hell's kitchen.

During my New York visits, I never miss brunch at this gem of a restaurant. Their Sweet Tea is the highlight, exquisitely delicious and a must-try. The food consistently impresses with its quality and flavors. Highly recommended for a delightful brunch experience.

- Typical midtown cocktail bar clientele - Absolutely gorgeous interior- Check out the photos for reference; it's even more impressive in person- We came for happy hour (4pm-7pm) and got the $1 oysters, which were super fresh, and the truffle fries - All the food that came out to the other tables looked good- Got the Waiting Game and let me tell you the drinks are strong - Definitely coming back!- There was a company event on the second floor so the first floor was extra pack- The only down side is that it gets super loud. We had to shout across the table. - Come when it's emptier

Title: A Sweet Spot for Dessert Lovers

I've probably spent a small fortune at Spot, and I have no regrets. This isn't just an Instagram-worthy dessert bar; it's a taste bud haven. I'm a regular here, often bringing my friends or treating new acquaintances to an array of beautifully crafted desserts that are as delicious as they look.

What sets Spot apart is how their desserts achieve a perfect balance in sweetness, ensuring every bite is a delight without overwhelming your palate. Their serving sizes are just right, providing a satisfying experience for around $10 per dessert, which is a steal compared to the upscale alternatives.

My personal favorite? The matcha lava cake, an irresistible treat that keeps me coming back for more. One heads-up: weekend waits can be long, so plan accordingly. Trust me, the wait is worth it. Spot is a standout dessert destination that consistently satisfies the sweet tooth without breaking the bank.

I recently dined at a restaurant that's definitely a contender for serving one of the best Katsu don dishes in the city. The quality of the food is impressive, with a delicious broth that will have you savoring every spoonful. Although I had to dock a star due to the soba noodles not being quite perfect—the hot soba seemed overcooked while the cold soba was a tad too hard—the portions were generous, ensuring you get great value for your money.

The service was outstanding; the staff were extremely nice, adding to the overall positive experience. Moreover, its proximity to Times Square makes it a convenient option for both locals and tourists alike. Despite the slight hiccup with the soba, this spot is well worth a visit for anyone looking for a satisfying meal in the heart of the city.

Great dinner! This place was recommended by a Greek person, so I had no doubts. First of all, the restaurant is beautiful. The songs are very good too, even though it might be loud for some people (we liked it). We started off with drinks, and I had this watermelon drink recommended by our server Nicole. For appetizers: fried calamari, spreads (tzatziki, eggplant - forgot the name lol, fish) and the best tuna tartare I've had in a while! We moved on to the main course. I had the steak with Greek fries, while the rest of my party had the Red Snapper and scallops. We were all very happy with our choices! Nicole recommended the cheesecake and baklava and, at that point, we trusted her 100%. No regrets - this was one of the best baklava I've ever had!!! The cheesecake was great too, but the baklava was the star of that evening.

Came here for restaurant week with colleagues. The decor was nice but we were also seated in a corner next to a loud large group and the waiter was not very attentive. Food was not bad. I had the calamari and steak and fries. The steak was really perfectly cooked and seasoned but the fries seasoning was overwhelming. Everything just sort of was missing the "wow" factor especially at the price point I was not impressed.

I've been to NYC twice and this is the best meal I've ever had here. Everything about the restaurant was great. The set up, ambience, food, cocktail, and staff made this an amazing experience. The shrimp tasted incredibly fresh and my dish was seasoned perfectly. I recommend making a reservation because they do get busy. We made ours and walked past a large crowd and were immediately seated. This is currently my only five star review.

Restaurant Review: Raku - Udon to Crave!

I'm convinced Raku offers the best udon in town — so irresistible you'd yearn for another bowl the following day. My boyfriend and I dropped in at 6pm on a Wednesday, promptly seated without a reservation, though I'd advise booking in advance as a queue formed shortly after.

I savored the Chicken Curry Udon ($14), a dish that made me a fan of thick soup due to its richly flavored broth and perfectly chewy noodles. My boyfriend's Niku Udon ($17) didn't disappoint either; the beef short-ribs were tender, swimming in a light yet tastefully potent broth.

Raku hits the spot for udon cravings with its generous servings, attentive service, and credit card convenience. Their cuisine is nothing short of DELICIOUS. Highly recommended!

I had an extraordinary dessert experience at this restaurant, with their 'atom bomb' dessert truly living up to its explosive name. The chocolate lava cake was a delicious delight, perfectly complemented by the unique and authentic rose petal ice cream. It was an unexpected but sublime pairing, achieving pure perfection on the palate. I wholeheartedly recommend everyone to indulge in this dessert. You won't regret it!

Came for dinner.  Cute place.  Pros:  food was good.  Pasta tasted fresh.  Loved that the complimentary bread came with delicious, airy ricotta instead of butter.  Had the paccheri with eggplant and enjoyed it.  Also had the artichoke appetizer and enjoyed that as well, though it should've been categorized as a salad.  Con: my pasta was room temperature - not hot enough; restaurant was loud.  I'd come back if I were in the area and looking for Italian.

Title: Cozy Italian Spot in Little Italy

I recently visited a charming, homey restaurant on the cusp of Little Italy with four friends. Arriving at 5:30 on a Saturday evening, we were delighted to be seated immediately in a setting that exuded a quaint atmosphere. The spot was decorated with specials scribbled on the walls, complementing the traditional printed menus.

Service was attentive throughout our dinner, and refreshingly, the venue never became overcrowded. The plethora of pasta options was impressive, but I opted for the evening's special: spaghetti carbonara. As a first-timer to this dish, I had no baseline for comparison, yet found myself somewhat disappointed by the lackluster flavor—save for the occasional savory bites of pancetta. While the dish certainly didn't lack in meat, I found it in need of a stronger punch of cheese or pepper. On a positive note, the pasta was cooked to al dente perfection.

One minor gripe, the portion size felt meager compared to typical Italian servings, which wouldn't have been as noticeable if not for the standard pricing. On the other hand, I thoroughly enjoyed the glass of Montepulciano wine I ordered, which was a delightful accompaniment to the meal.

In essence, this restaurant offers a pleasant ambiance and satisfactory service, but when it comes to their special—while cooked well—there's room for a flavor boost to match its price.

Venturing to the Upper East Side for a dining experience at NR is unquestionably rewarding, no matter which part of the city you're coming from. The ambiance welcomes you with a comfortable warmth, setting the stage for their divine cocktail selection and scrumptious fare that won’t disappoint.

One of the highlights is the inventive way drinks are presented – the Apple cocktail I savored came warm, an ideal companion to the chilly weather, and served in an intriguingly fun vessel. It’s a detail that adds to the overall charm of NR.

Their Happy Hour Oysters, fresh and succulent, paired with Karage and an irresistible matcha salt, offered a tantalizing start to the meal. The Kyoto Ramen I opted for was nothing short of delectable, a regional specialty that allows you to taste the culinary diversity of Japan’s cities.

However, it was the service that truly set NR apart. The staff's thoughtful action of moving us to a quieter spot without a fuss when a louder group arrived, showed a remarkable level of customer care.

NR is more than just a dining spot; it’s a place where every detail is attended to with a thoughtful touch. If you find yourself nearby, don’t miss the chance to visit this true Upper East Side gem.

Came here for reservations, loved how the Glazed St. Louis Ribs were tender and falls off the bone! The ribs were flavorful & a bit smokey, and the BBQ sauce was perfectly spiced! The spice lingers on your tongue to provide that perfect kick. We also tried the Pork Buns, the Pork Buns were tender and not too fatty. Our favorite by far was the Whole Roasted Fish Ssäm, which was a white fish in a ginger-scallion sauce.The menu was a bit small, not many items to choose from, but the ones we tried were a hit!

Delicious and romantic dinner place. The ambiance is perfect for a date. We stopped by for late Sunday dinner around 9.30 and the place was quiet and empty. We chose to sit outside because it was beautiful out. Our waitress was extremely professional and nice. We had the escargots, the lobster pasta, and the spicy cumin lamb. Everything was delicious! The lamb was probably the best because it tasted more like a Chinese fusion dish with cumin. Will definitely come back to try other dishes here!

Title: A Michelin Star Experience in Quarantine Times

I recently had the pleasure of indulging in Michelin Star cuisine during quarantine, and I must say, the affordability of such fine dining was an unexpected delight. Starting off, the French Fries scored a solid 4 out of 5, though a touch more garlic would have made them exceptional. The roasted brussel sprouts, however, were nothing short of delectable. There's a suspicion that the fries might not have been fresh, but the ketchup and the unconventional mustard with soy sauce combo were interesting accompaniments.

Now, let's talk about the Chef Special - Tuna Tartar Sandwich. A show-stopping 5 out of 5! The tuna's melt-in-your-mouth quality paired with the explosive burst of salmon roe created a memorable texture contrast, all encased in a fresh, toasted brioche bun. The addition of diced red onion brought a lovely sharpness, elevating the entire sandwich.

The Hall Salad was a mixed bag but still earned a respectable 4 out of 5. The gem lettuce was remarkably fresh and spicy, while the soft-boiled egg was cooked to perfection. However, the side components of egg salad and potato salad seemed out of place and rather plain.

Meanwhile, the Wagyu Burger, as per my girlfriend's review, was full-flavored with just the right balance of cheese, onion, and a sweet yet subtle sauce, deserving a top rating of 5 out of 5.

As for value, it's a resounding 5 out of 5. It's rare to find Michelin Star quality at such an accessible price point.

In conclusion, I wouldn't hesitate to order from here again. In the midst of the world's current stressors, such a culinary treat is more than welcome.

Overall Rating: 4.5/5

Tabetomo has been on my list of ramen places for more than a year as I am a fan of Jiro style ramen. I was glad to finally make it over here for lunch with my friend and her husband on a cold winter's day. We walked in at prime lunch hour on a Sunday and were easily seated at the bar. I ordered the tonkotsu chashu tsukemen which came out relatively quickly, which was great because I was ravenous after doing a work out class. It was not piping hot as I would have liked so after eating less than half of my noodles, I asked for the hot stone which made it more palatable.The broth was fatty, salty and garlicky and paired well with the chashu topping and noodles. I ended up eating about 3/4 of the noodles before giving up. It is rare for me to not finish my noodles in ramen and given how hungry I was, I was honestly surprised I could not finish it.After I left the restaurant, I felt uncomfortably full for hours and I ended up going to the gym to work it off in order to not feel so sluggish. This ramen was good but I think you definitely need to be in a mood to eat something really fatty to enjoy it. I can't imagine I'll crave this or be back anytime soon but I think this place might be good after a night of drinking or something.

I love that this restaurant opens super late! Perfect for a late night meal in the winter time (or summer b/c perfect for whenever). I usually come during off-peak hours so I don't have to wait because this place can get packed during prime dinner time. I usually get the seafood tofu soup and galbi combo. The soup is savory and will warm your stomach. The galbi is really good here as well, it's tender and pairs perfectly with the soup. I also really like the seafood pancake! It's chewy and has lots of seafood bits in it. My boyfriend got the spicy rice cake and it was honestly ok, wouldn't recommend it here. It's average and not worth wasting stomach space when there are better things to eat. ALSO, you get a whole small fish as a side dish! It's not that much meat but still good.

I won't comment on the bathroom because I didn't use it, but next time I'm here I'm gonna have to check out the two-toilet situation. Service was great and so was the atmosphere in the patio area outside. I was going to order the white sangria but the server suggested I try their festive "Hallo" sangria, and it was pretty good (ppl who like drinks that taste like juice and not alcohol would enjoy this). My friend ordered some other cocktail that ended up tasting strongly of cucumber when there wasn't supposed to be any cucumber in it, so the server allowed her to replace her drink with the same sangria.The server also offered us free shots (had apple cider & vodka I think?) and Halloween-themed chocolate cake on the house. Everything was very Halloween themed, so it made for a fun experience.

I recently decided to try out a new spot for some takeout and ordered a noodle soup with wonton and pork. I must give credit where it's due—the delivery was impressively quick, and the food arrived piping hot. The ramen noodles and wontons were satisfying, but that's where the positives end. The pork was a letdown; it arrived dry and utterly lacking in flavor. Even the broth failed to pack a punch, tasting rather bland and unfortunately, it seemed to be loaded with MSG, leaving me feeling excessively thirsty for the rest of the evening. While I appreciated the thoughtful packaging of the broth, the overall meal was a miss. Considering the myriad of dining options in the area, it's unlikely I'll order from here again. It was quite disappointing.

We had just driven into the city for the weekend to attend a show the next day. I had an idea of where I wanted to eat when we arrived but it wasn't open. So we walked a little further, maybe a block, and stumbled upon Pepper Lunch. It was quiet and looked inviting. We came in and placed our order at the front counter by the door. The staff were all wearing plastic half masks. I'm wondering if this is because of the coronavirus or this is what they wear all the time?I got the wild angus steak with miso soup. It came in a sizzling iron pan like fajitas. I asked for medium temp and it came perfectly done. Meat was soft and not chewy at all. Quite reasonable prices too for a New York lunch. Really enjoyed the atmosphere. As I said, it was quiet. Surprised with the hustle and bustle of the city on a Saturday, there were few customers. Before I left, I used the restroom. Now, I won't write about a restroom unless it's particularly good or bad, but this time, I just want to mention that I used a bidet for the first. And oh-my-gosh, why have I never used one before. They're wonderful. I have to admit that I giggled because the water squirting on me was a bit tickling. Okay, that was too much information. This bidet had heated seats too. So it was nice on a cold March day. I need a bidet. We all need bidets. The Japanese people are so spoiled.

From the moment we stepped into this charming establishment, we were greeted with an ambiance that was both cute and welcoming. The service we received was exceptional, catering to our every need with attentiveness and a smile.

The menu boasted an impressive selection of pastas, all priced under $20, a delightful surprise for such quality. The option to mix and match pastas and sauces added a personalized touch to our dining experience.

We savored a variety of dishes, including the parpadelle alla vodka, gnocchi with pomodoro, and orecchiette with sausage, each dish bringing its own unique and delectable flavors to the table. Unfortunately, the cacio e pepe fell a bit short on taste, requiring an extra sprinkle of parmesan and a pinch of salt to bring it up to par with the rest.

Overall, everything else hit the mark, leaving us impressed and satiated. This spot is a must-visit for pasta lovers who appreciate a cozy setting, superb service, and the freedom to tailor their meal.

Wow! The dining experience at Buddakan is absolutely DIVINE, nothing short of perfection!! Words can't justify how much I enjoyed my time here. The interior was timeless - art pieces of all sizes decorated the walls. The lighting was pretty dim, however it gave off a relaxed yet very fun ambiance paired with the funky music. It was not crowded at all since I came on a Tuesday night, making it very easy to chat amongst our group. The service was amazing! All the servers were super attentive and professional - if you want to know what it feels like to be dined and wined like royalty, COME HERE! FOOD: all the dishes are meant to be served family style so our table ordered a bunch of appetizers and 3 main entrees. We got the cauliflower lollipops, pork dumplings, edamame dumplings, lobster egg rolls, wild mushroom chow fun, lobster fried rice, and black pepper beef. I'm not going to go on about each dish, but all of them blew my mind! Let's just say my taste buds were in heaven! Can we also mention how visually appealing the plating was??!For dessert, we ordered the crying chocolate and the coconut flan. That was the BEST decision of the entire meal!! Granted I have a sweet tooth, it was unanimously agreed upon that both dessert were the BOMB. We were blown away with how rich and flavorful they were, and honestly we were left craving for more. This place is the epitome of fine dining - come here if you want to treat yourself to a nice meal (or for a nice dinner date)!!

Cozy little spot nestled on east 33rd, Spoon is a great place to catch up with friends for a quiet brunch. I made reservations on Yelp so we were seated right away but the place was pretty packed by the time we left. They have a good variety of dishes and cocktails. I got a Bellini to start, which was a very generous pour and tasted delicious. I ordered the sausage biscuits and gravy after having seen it all over Yelp. The dish came with two yummy biscuits in a skillet filled with a sausage cheesy gravy and 2 poached eggs. I will be honest, the dish was good but it was lacking something and I couldn't quite put my finger on it. Maybe more salt or a little bit of spice, or even a sharper cheese. The other people at my table enjoyed their food - the shrimp and grits and bodega sammie. Overall, a solid spot if you're in the neighborhood but nothing out of this world. Service could have also been a bit more aggentk

Title: Surprising Seafood Delights in the Big Apple

I ventured into this establishment during NYC Restaurant Week, a bit hesitant as I'm not typically keen on seafood. To my surprise, I was thoroughly impressed. The fried calamari stood out as the star appetizer – a dish that I would wholeheartedly recommend. Even the lobster appetizer, which I usually wouldn't gravitate towards, was quite remarkable.

The restaurant itself boasts a formal ambiance, lending itself to a more refined dining experience. Although I savored the meals, the remainder of the Restaurant Week menu didn't quite capture my urge for a return visit. If you're a seafood enthusiast, it might be a different case for you, but I'll be waiting to see what other culinary options this spot might offer outside of this event.

We got tips from friends to sign up on the waitlist on yelp beforehand because the wait time can be well over 2 hours. We put ourselves on the list while we were on the train from NJ, about 1 hour before 5pm on a Saturday. Right after we got on the waitlist in spot 18, the time went from 21-30 mins to over 90 minutes. Thank goodness we did it when we did. Our timing was perfect: we got to Thai Villa just as we were #2 on the waitlist. We came with a party of 3 and barely had to wait 10 minutes before being seated. The staff was friendly, patient, and cooperative. Onto the food: I know why this place has such a long wait time. It is AMAZING! I don't think I've had better Thai food, and I've eaten a ton of Thai food in my life. The flavors were incredible, the spice level wasn't overwhelming, and the texture of the noodles/tenderness of the meats was in point! We started off with the calamari and the shrimp cake. It was a good amount of food for appetizers. We decided we like shrimp cake more than crab cake now lol. We ordered a few lychitinees and an old fashioned. The drinks were very aromatic and flavorful! For the main course, two of us got the squid kea mao (drunken noodles), one got the tofu kea mao, and one of us got the royal pad Thai. My mouth is watering just thinking about the food. It was incredible. We really can't wait to go here again in the future. Our best advice is to get your name on the yelp waitlist atleast an hour before you expect to arrive! And make sure you're at the venue within 5 minutes of that time if not earlier!

Title: A Culinary Triumph Worth the Reservation Rigmarole

My dining experience at this establishment was nothing short of exceptional, albeit securing a table was a test of patience. The reservation process demanded nightly attempts a month in advance for a coveted early evening slot, narrowly escaping the less desirable late-night bookings.

Upon arrival, the service was outstanding, marked by a staff exuding warmth and attentiveness. The personal touch added by the servers, who offered thoughtful recommendations, was a highlight that enhanced our meal.

The offered fare lived up to the hype. The signature Charles Cut Prime Rib was a standout—a dish for true prime rib aficionados, served with a preferred rare center. The suggestion to repurpose leftover prime rib with eggs for a subsequent breakfast was a delightful touch that did not disappoint.

Accompaniments were equally impressive. The corn side dish invoked the essence of elote, balancing sweet creaminess with a zesty kick, while the blue cheese-laden creamed spinach was reminiscent of a rich dashi broth, a testament to the kitchen's culinary finesse.

Rounding out the meal, the burger was a triumph in its own right, solidifying the fact that every dish here was worth the indulgence.

In summation, the effort to dine here is a small price to pay for the exceptional quality and service provided. Highly recommended for those who appreciate delectable food paired with a genuinely hospitable atmosphere.

New Wonjo is my go-to KBBQ spot in K-Town.  The food is always fantastic, prices are reasonable, and the wait is never too, too awful (sometimes, if you're lucky, there may be no wait at all).  Also, I love that they use use real charcoal grills, instead of gas or electric ones.  Although my palate is not discerning enough to taste the difference, it def feels extra special when you sit down and they bring out the trays of glowing charcoal to BBQ your meats.  I've been coming here for years, and def see myself continuing to do so for years to come.During my most recent visit, we ordered the jap che, seafood pancake, premium gal bi, and non-marinated pork belly.  Everything was delicious, as always, including the banchan (side dishes).  Note that your first order of steamed egg is included, but additional orders cost $3 for a small and $5 for large.  So in addition to an extra order of $3 steamed egg, a bottle of soju, tax, and tip, our total worked out to $37pp.  How can you beat that?For those who care, you won't find the friendliest service in town here.  But what the servers lack in overt friendliness, they make up for in efficiency.  New Wonjo operates like a well-oiled machine.  The only thing that slows things down a bit is that not all the waitstaff are fluent in English, but hey, you make do.

I love to finish my meals with something sweet so here's a look at not one but three of the dessert options on the Rosa Mexicano menu for Restaurant Week Winter 2019 - Tres Leche, Churros and Pastel de Chocolate Mexicano. The tres leche was precisely sweetened and not over soaked, something really difficult to achieve. The churros were warm and crispy with just the right amount of cinnamon. Last but not least, the chocolate cake was rich and decadent. Thankfully, the spice didn't overpower the chocolate which I've found common at Mexican eateries.

Title: Underwhelming Experience Despite High Hopes

After often walking by and being lured in by tantalizing aromas, my recent visit to this minimalist eatery left me somewhat underwhelmed. Our appetizer, gomatofu with uni, was a disappointment. The tofu's gritty texture strayed from the expected silken smoothness, and the uni's presentation, complete with an uncleaned vein, demonstrated a lack of attention to detail.

The main course, matsu unaju, showcased fresh eel but failed to justify its $35 price point. While the quality of the ingredients was apparent, the dish – eel with rice under a sweet sauce – did not impress or inspire a return visit.

In summary, while the food was acceptable, it fell short in delivering value for the cost. Consequently, I find little reason to return.

Heard about this spot on Barstool Pizza reviews and although we thought Portnoy's 9.3 for their thin Square Pie was a little ambitious, the pizza was delicious nonetheless. Our Fried Calamari starter was also delicious, tender and lightly battered. The atmosphere is great as well. Hidden, up some stairs and set back felt like you were in an old time speakeasy. Great service from our waitress, who got us set up as quickly as she could during a busy time. Highly recommend.

AMAZING STEAKHOUSE! I highly recommend this place and cannot argue enough how great the service was! I came here with a group of friends for restaurant week. Loved the service, ambiance was amazing and loved the vibe. Big shout out to BRUNO!

Had brunch here yesterday and I was not impressed with the food.  My friend and I both had the pre-fix brunch menu, which was a little less than $30.00, which is not bad. Each person gets a drink, either Bellini, mimosa, coffee, or tea. I had the brioche French toast with a mimosa. The French toast was not great. It kind of taste like a whole grain bread. Best part was the fresh fruit that it came with. My friend had the egg Benedict with smoked salmon. It needed a little more sauce to add flavor. Will come back for dinner and see if this changes my perspective.

If you want big portions of noodz for an affordable price please check out this Northwestern Chinese eatery in the East Village. Wheat-based foods are the centre of Northern Chinese cuisine, which means that they are known for noodles and dumplings! With this knowledge, we had to order their noodles. We were a party of 3 and we came on a Monday at around 1 PM. There was only one other table when we arrived and so we were seated immediately. We ordered:A starter: Glass noodles and cabbage with egg crepe in a sizzling pan ($12):This dish had such comforting savory flavors and a satisfying amount of textures: with the crunchy cabbage, slippery glass noodles, and fluffy egg. and One house special: the small XinJiang big plate chicken with bone ($16).The big plate chicken comes with or without bone (without is more expensive) and in a small or large size for both options. Another table ordered the large and it looked mouth-wateringly delicious but too hefty for the three of us to tackle on our own, as we wanted to try another dish as well. This was definitely the star of the show. Fall-off-the-bone chicken meat atop fresh knife-cut noodles. I can assure you it tasted as good as it looked! The chicken was perfectly braised and the noodles were so soft and easy to sink my teeth into. Chili and bell peppers decorated the dish giving it both extra colors and flavors.If you come to Jiang Diner, bring your big appetite and order the big plate chicken!!!

I was meeting some friends for a movie and they told me they had eaten already so I was looking for a quick bite prior to meeting them. I did not want a sit down meal but something quick. I stumbled upon Kut-kebab. I asked them how it worked. You have your choice of a sandwich on oriental bread or flat bread, salad in a bowl or a kuttie [a half sandwich] I opted for the flat bread with chicken [all natural, no hormones, artificial ungredients] with a yogurt sauce-there are other options for sauces] hot and cold vegetables [ I got tomatoes, lettuce and cheese and red cabbage] Hummus is $2 extra-in my case it was all wrapped up similar to a burrito and was delicious. I did not see table seating but there was counter space on the periphery. They do deliver and tax is included in the meal. I would recommend and return.

Solid mussels, but surprisingly even better appetizers.I came here recently as part of a group of 4. We arrived promptly at 5:30pm on a Monday and, as expected, we were wayyyy early as there was not a single customer inside. However, as the evening wore on, more and more tables began filling up.If you're coming to Flex Mussels, then you're here for 1 reason, the mussels! Or at least that's what you would expect. If anyone is interested in their happy hour, I believe it is from 5:30-7, but it can only be at the front bar. For anyone else dining here, they will have to stick with the regular menu.Before getting to the mussels, our table decided to order a few appetizers to start to warm us up:Burnt Fingers (crispy fried calamari, shrimp, oysters, spicy aioli)- Nice hodgepodge of fried seafood. All of it was solid and the spicy aioli definitely was the kicker.Fish Tacos (beer battered haddock, red cabbage jicama slaw, chipotle mayo)- Unfortunately there were only 2 fish tacos in the order because this was freaking delicious. Perfectly fried haddock combined with the slaw and mayo.Parmesan Fries- Exactly what anyone would expect. Great appetizer to just pick at.Watermelon Salad- My fried ordered this even though it wasn't on the menu and it might have actually been the best appetizer. It was so simple, yet so refreshing.Crab Guacamole- Another one where you can't go wrong. The great thing was that not only were the tortillas huge, but they were extremely generous with the amount of guac as well.As for the mussels, everyone at our table ordered a different one, but I went with the Florencio, which included shrimp, pesto, parmigiano cream and basil. I was really looking forward to this flavor mainly because of the pesto and it did not disappoint. The mussels were tiny, but the sauce was so good.
