There was a ton of flavor, but yet it wasn't too salty. Each order was accompanied by bread, which was a welcome site considering how much sauce was leftover in each pot of mussels.Everything here was great. The service was good and quick and the food was fantastic. All of our appetizers were delicious as I enjoyed every single one. Most importantly, the mussels and their sauces were amazingly tasty. This would definitely be an NYC spot that I wouldn't think twice about revisiting again.

My favorite Mexican restaurant close to the Union Square area of NYC. Good solid menu of Mexican staples for lunch and dinner. Portions are hearty and filling. Service is friendly and drinks choices are plenty. Nice decor and setting but only drawback can be seating is limited so leave time to wait if you have a group going. There is though a take out option for locals which helps. Been here a few times and never had a problem with the food.

Title: A Night of Flavor and Dance at Londel's

On a bustling Saturday evening, my party and I ventured into Londel's around 8 PM. As one might expect in the city, parking was a challenge, but the effort was well worth it once we stepped inside. Londel's presents a cozy arrangement of tables suitable for dining, coupled with a modestly sized dance floor and an inviting bar area.

I opted for the whiting fingers, which turned out to be a succulent choice – certainly a dish I'd recommend. Throughout the evening, I indulged in several mixed drinks, all of which were satisfyingly robust.

Our primary reason for visiting was to partake in Steppin', and Londel's did not disappoint. The music was lively and had us on our feet, enjoying every moment of dance. Based on this experience, not only am I eager to return, but I would also encourage others to join in the festivities at Londel's for a truly enjoyable evening out.

Title: A Spicy Delight with Swift Service

I had a delightful experience at this restaurant, where the ambience set the perfect tone for a memorable meal. Service was impressively quick, never leaving a dull moment. As a spicy food aficionado, the Thai red curry was a fiery pleasure that truly hit the mark, packed with flavor and just the right amount of heat. This spot has certainly earned a return visit from me. Highly recommend!

We were in the area and saw the reviews for the Chow House.  We had a quick lunch and really enjoyed the experience.  I wish that we would have tried more but there is always next time.  Again it was a quick lunch so we shared a few things.  Started off with Dumplings and then finished off with Shrimp Lo Mein.  The dumplings were very tasty and had good flavor.  The Shrimp Lo Mein was good.  Again had good flavor and a nice sized portion.  This is a smaller place but was packed.  I would recommend.

some of the best pizza on the upper east! highly recommend their margherita pies. so simple and so good! great wine list, great prices, the friendliest staff. great for date night/out with friends, highly recommend their delivery if you're looking for a night in too!

My recent visit to Sotto 13, intended as a birthday treat for my wife, was a letdown. While the establishment boasts an appealing interior and serves decent pizza, other dishes like the Tuscan Eggs with their bewildering licorice flavor fell short. The most disappointing aspect, however, was the management. Our reservation, made a month in advance, was not honored in a timely manner, resulting in a 40-minute wait, during which time later arrivals were seated before us. The manager's response to our concerns was dismissive and outright rude. The waiting staff did their best under the circumstances, offering prompt and friendly service, but this did little to offset the management's lack of courtesy and poor handling of reservations. Coupling these issues with the questionable food quality and steep prices leaves me no choice but to advise against dining at Sotto 13.

My boyfriend and I walked in here because we didn't want to pay the outrageous prices inside of Javits for the auto show. We decided to eat beforehand. We ended up splitting a poke bowl because it was PACKED. We got eel, tuna and salmon for our protein and the price was under $15!We absolutely loved the spicy aioli sauce and it made every bite extremely enjoyable. All the ingredients were extremely fresh, including the mango, which is extremely rare as far as poke bowls go. I was lucky enough to be there to see the truck full of fresh ingredients delivered right to their door. It was nice to actually see for myself that the ingredients are fresh. I was so shocked at how large the serving was for each topping/add in but I'm definitely not complaining. It was the first time I was able to eat protein in every bite!

During a recent visit to NYC, I discovered a Pepper Lunch, rekindling fond memories of my first experience with the brand in Milpitas, CA. This NYC outpost adopts a casual fast-food vibe - order at the counter and grab a number to claim your table. While the menu seemed less diverse than Milpitas, missing favorites like udon and beef, the classic rice sizzling hotplate did not disappoint. Delicious and swiftly served, Pepper Lunch is an excellent choice for those seeking a tasty meal in a hurry or squeezed into a tight lunch break.

I grabbed some lunch at the food truck and it was amazing! Don't be surprised by the prices; seafood, especially lobster, is always pricier, and this place is sustainably sourced so I'm willing to pay a little more. Even so, I think the prices are fair for what you get. The lobster rolls are $17, which I think is standard for lobster rolls in NYC, and all the dishes come with HUGE chunks of lobster. I had the lobster tots ($14), which had tons of lobster meat, pico, and cilantro sauce. The lobster bisque ($5 a cup) was thick, rich, and creamy, even though it's a small cup. Overall, I was extremely satisfied with my lunch. Plus, the food truck workers were so quick! One person in front of me ordered meals for 5 people so I expected to wait forever, but my food was ready much quicker than expected.

Title: A Quiet Gem with Quality Fare

My recent dining experience at this establishment was nothing short of delightful. For what it's worth, the price reflects the high quality of the fish - a true testament to their commitment to fine cuisine. I was taken aback by the tranquil atmosphere, which made for a perfect dinner date setting, yet the ambiance is versatile enough to cater to a lively gathering of friends or coworkers. The service was impeccable, with waitstaff striking the right balance of attentiveness and courtesy. While the prices lean towards the higher end, the value received in terms of food quality and dining experience is unquestionable. I highly recommend this restaurant for those seeking an upscale culinary adventure.

I've only seen this place on instagram, but I have never been to a branch in the U.S. or in Asia. This is one of those places where you order up front, pay, and they give you a number to place on your table. I went on a Saturday evening, and it was pretty empty at first (around 7pm). I ordered the classic pepper beef rice because I thought it was a safe choice, and I might get that and more again. I came to dinner pretty hungry, and for the price of the meal ($14/$15), I expected it to fill me up. I wish there was more food. The service was pretty good--the waitress gave us our waters as soon as we sat down, and our food was out within 5 minutes.

Great rolls!The spicy mang is terrific! Fresh, doesn't feel "too healthy".  Beyond sushi is a great lunch option for when I'm not looking for anything that'll put me to sleep and I'm not in the mood for a salad. I also think it's great for my friends who are weary about sushi and raw fish. The rolls are tasty and everyone enjoys them. The dumplings...the texture of some of them...really makes you wish you didn't. Texture is a big part of the eating experience for me and quite honestly after one set of dumplings I know enough to stick to the rolls. Maybe try pan frying them.

3.5 Stars but rounding up to 4 Stars.I used to go to Amber alot when they were located across the street, in a much larger and much nicer space. But rent in the UWS is no joke and they moved to its current, smaller (& not as nice) space a couple of years ago.  Service and hospitality is still great, however, their food, albeit still good, is just not as good as it used to be.  I still go to Amber sometimes because they have great Lunch Specials!Today's lunch:My friend had two sushi rolls of his choice, which came with soup and salad.  He said it was "okay, same old, same old" but good value at $11.I had the chicken with green curry, which came with choice of mini appetizer (I picked sui mai), soup AND salad for $13.  Now that is alot of food!  By the time my green curry dish came, I was getting full and only ate about a third of it, and took the rest as a doggy bag...lunch for tomorrow!  The food was good but not great.  Green curry was super mild and not spicy at all.  Still tasty but a little "dummied down" for the UWS.  Would I return?  Sure, as my friend said, it's a good value lunch. Amber is still a pretty good option for this neighborhood!

Title: A Breath of Fresh Brunch Air

I had the pleasure of experiencing a truly unique brunch at this gem. Their artichoke chaat was a standout dish, bursting with flavor and innovation. Portions were generous, ensuring you get great value for your meal. The menu's creativity is worth multiple visits to try everything they have to offer. While service could have been quicker, the warm and attentive staff more than made up for the pace. This establishment is a delightful departure from the typical brunch offerings around town and is definitely on my list for a return visit. Highly recommended!

Working across the street in the hospital it is an honor to have Paris Baguette's support during this pandemic. They have welcomed the community along with the healthcare community with open arms. They have been offering Health care staff free small coffes every day and I could not be more grateful to know that they have our back during this crises. I love and appreciate it....and cant wait to try all the pastries. The place is very clean and spacious, the pastries look delicious and I highly recommend checking this new addition to the community. THANK YOU PARIS BAGUETTE!! Welcome to the midtwon west family!!

It doesn't look like a restaurant upon initially viewing it from the street. I didn't understand having a pawn shop in the storefront, but going through the rear door opens up to a completely different look and feel in the restaurant, it's kind of cool. If you got it, spend it but in my opinion, this is a place you take someone you've been dating for a while, someone you care about and want to spice things up with here. This is one of the places where the ambiance and energy of the place will entice you to want the food here - you will NOT be disappointed. You can split and share everything, our waitress recommended 4-5 items and that is plenty for a dining party of 2. It was my pleasure to share this with you all who read it, you'll enjoy it.-The grilled cheese dumplings tasted great and I'm glad I followed the crowd on this-The Burger is a mix of different meat and is delicious, and the fries seasoning complimented it greatly-The spaghettini was extremely flavorful, don't let the zucchini distract you from choosing it!-The dessert shot was a perfect sweet nightcap to the meal. I was too full to eat another actual serving but was happy to have something sugary. Good:-Grilled cheese, smoked bacon & tomato soup dumplings (MUST HAVE)-House Salad (refreshing and tasty)-Chicken Meatballs (it's chicken but still tastes like something your grandma would cook for you on Sundays)-Spaghettini (the lemon makes the taste pop)-Beauty & Essex Burger with BBQ Fries (I didn't want to share this)-Birthday Cake Milkshake Shot (ice cream with Jack Daniels)-RSVP via OpenTable for points-The ambiance is energetic-The music being played in the background made you bop your head while you were eating (older hip hop and R&B)Bad:-Cranky New Yorker rant: the people/customers, in my opinion, I felt wanted to be seen and photographed here mattered more than taking in and appreciating the full speakeasy experience/vibe and enjoying the meal. By no fault of the restaurant, it can feel pretentious, don't let that deter you from the delicious meal you'll have.

My husband and I visited for a late dinner and were met with quite friendly staff. I chose the EAK ramen and found the broth flavorful and the thick noodles perfectly cooked – not too soggy, just right. However, the dish was surprisingly simple, featuring only some cooked spinach, toasted nori, and a few slices of chashu pork. Considering the $15 price tag, the minimal toppings fell short of expectations. Additional garnishes came with extra costs, even $1 for green onions, which was a bit disappointing.

I have always wanted to try out Hanjan and did so last night! The place was relatively full when my friends and I got there at 7:45pm. By 8:30pm the place was half full which was nice as we were able to spread out and speak normally. We ordered the following:Seafood pancake: nice, crunchy, filling, fresh, straight out the fryer Tofu dumplings: 4 dumplings per serving, again very tasty and served fresh out of the fryer Spicy ricecake: good level of spicyness and nice chewy texture Spicy seafood tofu soup: again good level of heat and pretty nice and spicyness. Served with rice Soy poached Black cod: comes with a lot of sauce but we enjoyed itBanchan set: usually served for free at most Korean restaurants but not here. Was nice regardless. The above list was plenty to feed three ladies and we walked away pretty full. Whole dinner with three drinks, tax and tip ended up being $52 per person. FYI I made the reservation via Seated so was able to get extra perks. Restaurant ambience was nice; good for catch ups however bear in mind we were there on a Monday night.

I recently dined at Bareburger with colleagues and was impressed with its prime location. The option to sit near the open window, weather permitting, adds a delightful patio ambiance. Despite the bustling lunch crowd, the service did not falter.

We started with a round of refreshing strawberry lemonade and shared onion rings and fries – the accompanying special sauce was outstanding and not to be missed. My first encounter with the Impossible Burger was a savory surprise, although it was cooked to rare rather than the requested medium rare.

Regardless of the slight hiccup in doneness, Bareburger offered a pleasant dining experience with memorable flavors that beckon another visit.

Title: A Stellar Sushi Experience

I recently dined at this gem and was floored by the exceptional quality of both the food and service. The attentive staff ensured my cup was never empty, reflecting their dedication to providing seamless service. The standout was undoubtedly the sushi, with the small squid-topped piece leaving a lasting impression on my palate. The handrolls here are unrivaled — they're the best I've ever savored and worth a trip back on their own.

A special mention goes to the A5 Wagyu topped with uni, a sublime offering that truly melts in your mouth, justifying its premium. Although $85 might be on the higher end for an omakase, this experience justifies every penny. The meal paced to perfection, leaving me perfectly satiated without being overstuffed. It's an unequivocal yes from me, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this local spot known for its Mexican cuisine, and I must say, their tacos are truly exceptional. Each bite is a burst of flavor, reflecting the authenticity and care put into their preparation. While the guacamole and chips were decent, they didn't quite reach the same heights. However, the margaritas were a highlight, perfectly mixed and a fantastic complement to the meal. Overall, if you're in the mood for great tacos and a refreshing margarita, this is the place to go.

I recently dined at a local restaurant and found myself with mixed feelings about the experience. On the plus side, I was impressed by the lack of wait time for dinner and the attentiveness of the servers. The establishment also offered ample seating, contributing to a comfortable environment.

However, the dining experience was marred by the food's flavor, or the lack thereof. I opted for the marinated beef platter, which, disappointingly, didn't taste marinated at all. Given its steep price of almost $90, I anticipated a meal that would be both flavorsome and substantial, but it failed to satisfy on both counts – the portion was only sufficient for one.

In contrast, the chicken platter, priced at $24, provided value for money with a generous serving size and more discernible flavor.

Another downside was the volume of the background music, which proved to be excessively loud, impeding conversation at our table.

In light of these aspects, I am inclined to say that I won't be returning to this restaurant. While the service was commendable, the main draw of a dining establishment — the food — was underwhelming, particularly the overpriced and underwhelming beef dish.

After numerous visits to this establishment, courtesy of a friend who inexplicably adores it, my bewilderment persists. Service here consistently hovers at a level of mediocrity; the staff often emit an air of disinterest. The menu rarely entices, posing a challenge when selecting a dish. On my latest foray, I opted for an omelette with salmon, accompanied by a redundant side of fries—thanks to an uninformed decision as the waiter failed to mention the dish included potatoes. An oversight that, in my opinion, is quite unprofessional.

My companion's pasta with salmon seemed to meet his approval, though my own meal was lackluster at best. To compound the lackluster dining experience, we were seated in a less-than-ideal spot despite the restaurant's vacancy, a misstep that has become a predictable pattern here.

Regrettably, despite my loyalty to my friend’s preference, my patience has worn thin, and I will advocate for an alternative dining experience in the future. There's an abundance of more inviting options nearby.

Title: A Surprising Delight at Mel's Burgers on Broadway

During an impromptu dinner hunt in the Broadway area, I stumbled upon Mel's Burgers – a decision that would delightfully shape my dining experiences for the next two weeks. The atmosphere was welcoming, thanks in no small part to the very friendly bartender who promptly set me up with a seat and a Left Hand Milk Stout, a personal favorite, immediately earning my favor.

The “Hot Mess” burger, my inaugural choice, despite appearing modest, proved to be quite the hearty meal. Although the accompanying fries were somewhat lackluster on seasoning during that first visit, they did not disappoint on subsequent trips. Indeed, I found myself returning twice more, tempted by the memory of that satisfying burger. The "California Burger" solidified Mel's as a consistently good choice, paired with significantly improved, well-seasoned fries.

In short, after dining at Mel's Burgers three times in a fortnight, it's clear that they offer delicious food, with a standout staff. Based on my experiences, Mel's has earned my recommendation for anyone in search of a good burger in the Broadway area.

Title: A Steak to Remember in New York

Review: From the first bite, it was clear why this steakhouse comes so highly recommended. The steak I had was, without exaggeration, the best I've ever enjoyed—perfectly cooked and brimming with flavor. Hunger drove us to bypass appetizers, diving straight into the main courses. My filet mignon was a feast for the senses, accompanied by an indulgent lineup of sides: crispy fries, creamy lobster Mac n' cheese, and smooth mashed potatoes, all shared amongst our group. The service matched the culinary excellence, attentive and swift, ensuring our experience was nothing short of exceptional. This place is a must-visit for any steak aficionado in New York. I'm already planning my return visit.
Updated 2 photos on two new things I tried last time we went: the coconut pudding "bunnies" and fried sticky rice "carrots" desserts. Cute shapes. Tasted okay.

Title: A Quaint Disappointment in a Trendy Neighborhood

Upon entering the charming facade of this local eatery, nestled amidst a district renowned for its upscale vibes and dining abundance, I found myself intrigued by its outward promise. The ambiance is, in a word, delightful—inviting enough to dispel any initial reservations I held, spurred by less-than-favorable online visual previews.

The service staff deserves commendation; they were attentive and conscientious, ensuring that my water glass never reached its drought point—a detail I hold in high esteem.

However, the central tenet of any restaurant experience—the cuisine—failed to align with the allure of its environment. The menu's austerity could be forgiven if what was offered transcended or even met the standard of its competitors. Sadly, the burger I opted for was a lackluster affair; modest in size, it was sandwiched between a bun that I could have sourced from a local grocery store for a casual backyard gathering. The fries did not rescue the burger from mediocrity, bearing an all-too-evident resemblance to mass-produced, freezer-aisle fare.

My companion's chili provoked a mere shrug of indifference. Despite the reasonable prices, the food's mundanity left me puzzled, especially given the establishment's bustling nature. Perhaps its success hinges on a vibrant happy hour culture or the loyalty of those seeking a neighborhood haunt's familiarity.

While I appreciate the restaurant's aesthetic and service, the unremarkable culinary offerings render it a spot I'm unlikely to revisit or recommend. For a place that stands amid a sea of abundant dining excellence, it does little to stand out, falling into the category of "fine for a single visit, but forgettable."

This places has the most tender crabs that I've ever eaten. The staff is extremely helpful and kind. Despite the busy atmosphere, they give you all of the time that you need. The crab legs were extremely tender. Melted in my mouth. The Sauce however didn't make top 5 for me. I even asked for lemon to bring more flavor to the sauce and it helped a bit. I think that if they had a better Sauce they would be much better. The portion size was good as it was about 1 and a half clusters as 1lb. Other establishments give only one cluster for the 1 lb. I ordered 1 gin and pineapple and it was well made. I didn't get a chance to get the woman's name but it was delicious. Would come again.

**Title: Bustling Dim Sum Delight with a Side of Sharing**

**Rating: ★★★★☆ 4/5**

I recently dined at a little gem of a dim sum spot that's definitely worth a visit, albeit with a few caveats. Firstly, expect a crowd before 2PM; this place is a local favorite, and for good reason. Don't be surprised if you end up sharing a table with another family – it's all part of the experience here, and it's actually quite fine.

The variety of food on offer is impressive, though I did notice a lack of vegetable options. Despite that, what we tried was delightful. One minor hiccup was that some of the dishes listed on Yelp were no longer available, and there were no physical menus to peruse – you'll choose directly from the carts that weave around the tables, which is an adventure in itself.

Timing your visit is key: post-2PM or right at opening will save you some wait time. And you mustn't leave without trying the durian cake, an absolute standout.

One odd moment was when our temporary tablemates left and the staff immediately cleaned up their half of the table. It didn't quite rush us out, but it did add a hint of pressure to wrap up our meal.

In summary, if you're after authentic dim sum and don't mind a bit of organized chaos, this is the place for you. Just remember to time your visit wisely!

This place is honestly more trouble than it is worth. It is always crowded to the point where you can't even see a view which is the best part of a rooftop. 3 stars because I do actually love the Frose, but everything is over priced as well. Would go to Press Lounge for a chiller vibe and better views.

Nowon features inventive dishes that call home to Korean ingredients, dishes, and styles and draw influence from other cuisines (e.g. xo sauce, mole, duck confit). There's not a single dish on the menu I can say that I've seen somewhere else. Cool vibes and decor here too!WHAT WE ORDEREDHONEY BUTTER TATER TOTS | labneh, seaweed seasoning --- my absolute favorite item here. So crispy with good/light honey butter flavor. SHIN RAMYUN CHICKEN WINGS | gochujang glaze, buttermilk dressingJAE'S JJAJANG CLAMS | bacon, black bean brown butter, lemon, bread crumb --- the clams were cleaned well!NOWON'S DOUBLE CHEESEBURGER | dry aged steak blend, 'murican cheese, kimchi mayo, dill pickle --- I thought this was over-hyped/all right but my friend really enjoyed it! I expected the meat would be rarer/thicker based on photos I saw.

**Restaurant Review: Hudson Yards Dining**

Last week, while attending a conference in New York, I had the pleasure of dining with colleagues at an exquisite venue in the new Hudson Yards towers. The restaurant boasts beautiful decor, with stunning views of The Vessel and the Hudson River. Despite being in a large group that was somewhat cramped at long tables, making conversation and service less than ideal, the dining experience was commendable.

The menu did not disappoint. I indulged in a variety of dishes, including superbly cooked lamb chops, white fish in sea salt, rainbow chard, and a seasonal fruit plate. The lamb chops were a culinary delight – cooked to perfection on the bone and temptingly juicy. They truly stood out, and resisting the urge to have a third serving was a challenge. The white fish, while praised by the staff, was underwhelming and lacked flavor. However, the meal concluded pleasantly with a fresh and tantalizing seasonal fruit plate, a refreshing choice among the many dessert offerings.

Overall, a venue that marries fine dining with a mesmerizing backdrop – ideal for those looking to impress or simply enjoy good food in a prime location.

Title: A Wholesome Start to Your Day

If you're seeking a healthy and nutritious breakfast that doesn't compromise on taste, this eatery is your go-to spot. Boasting a variety of oatmeal options, customizable breakfast sandwiches, and hearty quinoa bowls, there's something for every health-conscious diner. The service shines with its speed and the staff's welcoming demeanor adds to the pleasant dining experience.

I relished a simple yet satisfying breakfast of two fried eggs on a whole wheat bagel thin, peppered to perfection, for just $3.50. The real eggs and freshly-prepared sandwich provided a warm and comforting meal that stood out in a sea of nearby fast-food options like Dunkin' Donuts and Starbucks.

For those seeking value and quality in their morning meal, this restaurant offers an affordable alternative that doesn't skimp on the wholesome goodness.

I stumbled upon a charming little spot for brunch that truly deserves a shout-out. The menu was brimming with tempting choices, but I couldn't resist the shrimp and grits. Trust me, it was a delightful choice – perfectly cooked and seasoned to impress. If you're in the mood for a cozy brunch experience with a dish that will leave you savoring every bite, this is the place to go. Highly recommended for a scrumptious start to your day!

Cute spot with a different take on sushi rolls. Hesitated to try because it is a bit pricey and portions looked small compared to Japanese restaurant sushi rolls (where pieces are cut up). Nevertheless, here I am. Ordering is a BREEZE. Super easy, delightful, carefree and no rush. Love having time to scope out the offerings and even pay at my own convenience. Ordering takes longer that having your name called out for your order being ready. Cheeseburger roll - fun and different. Got cold fast though. I think if I had it on the spot, it would have been amazing. Cheese sauce is delicious. I dipped everything I ordered in that sauce. Spicy salmon with quinoa - pretty spicy but good. Quinoa was different and tasty with the roll. It does cost extra so the total is $4.20.  Spicy shrimp inari - this was a curious combination. Sweet yet spicy yet kinda chilled. Good! The spicy in the shrimp added a lot of flavor to the already sweet and soft inari (tofu skin).These are fairly small rolls. Three big bites and you're pretty much done. Rolls come in a sustainable, recyclable brown bag. So don't count on ordering and walking too far back to the office or commute unless you bring your own bag or tupperware. Price can be a bit steep. Total of less than $13 for these three items including tax.

I was just randomly looking for a chill place to eat by myself and this place exceeded my expectations. It's one of the only chinese places that TAKES CARDS! :) Great portions and loved how they did not hold back on the toppings! Prepared quite fast as well.Lots of meat and veggies. Really chill environment and perfect for a hot meal on a cold night.Picture doesn't do it justice, the food was amazing!!!If you want spicy, they won the back at all!

Title: A Worthy Splurge at Madame Vo

Upon first discovering Madame Vo through a Munchies YouTube tutorial, I was captivated by the unique approach to pho by Jimmy Ly. Having replicated his recipe at home with decent success, the draw to experience the authentic dish on-site was undeniable. During a recent trip to New York City, I seized the opportunity to dine in Madame Vo, an experience that proved to be a delightful foray into high-end Vietnamese cuisine.

It's a familiar refrain among those dining at ethnic restaurants – "I could make this at home" or "it's pricey" – and yet, Madame Vo transcends these clichés. The bowl of pho, steep at $22, justifies its price tag through layers of complex flavors that elevate it above home-cooked attempts. Investing in the $6 short rib addition to the dish further enriches the already exceptional pho, creating a fusion of textures and tastes worth the splurge.

While I also sampled the BBH (Bun Bo Hue), it didn't quite captivate my palate as much; however, that's a personal preference, being someone who's not overly enthusiastic about BBH.

Madame Vo may not be the spot with queues around the block, but that shouldn't deter you. If you're open to spending a bit more for a traditionally inexpensive cuisine and are seeking a culinary experience with finesse, Madame Vo demands a visit. Reservations are recommended but walking in could be just as rewarding for those spontaneous culinary adventurers.

Title: A Second Serving of Wholesome Delight

Once again, this quaint eatery doesn't disappoint. My return was greeted with the familiar comfort of healthy yet flavorful dishes, each bite reaffirming why it's worth coming back for more. The green shakshuka remains my top pick; its fresh, herby taste captivates the palate every time. However, note that the portions are on the lighter side—you might find yourself peckish a couple of hours later.

Despite its popularity, the restaurant does not take reservations, so plan for a short wait. We arrived at 10:20 am on a Sunday and were seated after a bearable 20 minutes. The wait is a small price to pay for the quality of fare that awaits.

In a spur of the moment while in the area, I decided to go to this restaurant to try it.The place looks nice and you are greeted by a friendly hostess to sit you.I picked the Adobo, the Aligue pasta and the Japanese style chicken wings.The wings were delicious!  Freshly fried, crisp enough but juicy inside with a delicious spicy house made dip.  Next time I could order 2 of these as my main course.The aligue pasta was very mild with some crab pieces on top.  It was good.  Aligue is the tamali (orange fat) found in female crabs under the shell as you open up the crab.When my adobo chicken came, I was expecting a light turmeric color instead of brown soy sauce.  The chicken seemed to have been either baked or broiled?  It had the soy sauce based seasoned sauce on top.  It was a big dish - almost like half a chicken with broccoli and some eggplant and a little cup of rice.  This seemed so much like a Westernized version of an Asian dish.  Reminds me of the early years when one cannot find the ingredients and you try to make an Asian dish.This was one dish that I was not to keen about.Fortunately, I did try the kale Laing in place of the chicken dish.  I brought home my left overs and this dish got better when I reheated it at home.  Maybe because the spices in it blended better with the vegetables after a while.Will I go back?  If I do, I will have 2 orders of the fried chicken wings as my main dish.  The pasta too.  Maybe I will try other dishes.

Being able to get hand rolls in a fast casual setting is what dreams are made of. Great variety of menu items, ingredients are pretty fresh, and decent price point. Small space so it's more for a quick bite or grab and go. Love that they have quinoa as a rice substitute as well.
Great sceney brunch spot.  Drinks were nicely made.  Moules frites were fantastic and the benedict also looked good.  Escargot was average and the profiteroles were too sweet.

My recent visit to the restaurant was average, falling short of extraordinary. I ordered noodles, which unfortunately arrived somewhat cold and not fully cut, detracting from the overall experience. I do acknowledge that we arrived close to closing time, which may have influenced the kitchen's performance. However, despite this, I believe the service could have been more attentive. I'm uncertain about giving this place another try in the future.

It was a cold day and I was craving for some soup. I wanted to have the Korean ox tail bone soup because I can't easily find it in the states. If you're looking for a clean tasting bland broth soup, this wouldn't be the soup for you. The good thing is, their homemade fermented kimchi really helps add in the rich flavor. They serve unlimited kimchi too so it's awesome! The waitresses are super observant and very attentive. The meal is simply perfect for a cold day in NYC. I'll definitely come back to try out their other dishes.

Beyond sushi is the ultimate sushi spot for ALL sushi lovers that just so happens to be vegan. It's crazy that there is a place out there that can make vegetables taste like fish. When you put it that way it sounds weird but it totally isn't! This is a chain restaurant that can be found throughout the city the one I particularly went to is in Chelsea Market. There isn't a whole lot of seating right by beyond sushi but there is more if you walk further down from the booth. Pricing is okay not super cheap but won't break the bank either. All in all I will definitely be back to visit this place!

Very busy place, good food, great price, ok service. Some dishes were outstanding like the pork belly (we had 5 orders of this), salt and pepper shrimp, and bo luc lac. The entrees were on the sweeter side, we've tried the pad see ew and pad Thai. I usually prefer the pad see ew but think they do a better job with the pad Thai at this restaurant because pad se ew is not suppose to be a wet dish which is how they make it here. Would recommend doing a bunch of apps instead of the entrees. The cocktails were very creative and delicious. Service was ok, we had a large party, they kept reminding us of the spend minimum over and over again, waters were never refill. Ambience is good for dates and groups, they have seating on the second floor as well.

Awesome Korean cuisine!! I came here multiple times usually after midnight! They are open until really late (Fri and Saturday until 7 am). After you tell them your orders, they start you off with their amazing free side dishes that includes a fried fish, kimchi, seasoned broccoli, pickles and more. Service is fast.

Stepping into this restaurant is like being transported to the heart of old New York City; it's a traditional steakhouse that wholly delivers both in quality and value for money. Their bacon appetizer stands out, striking the perfect savory note compared to the often sweeter renditions found elsewhere. The Tomahawk steak is a majestic offering, generously sized for sharing and exceptionally satisfying. It's not my first visit, and I'm continually impressed by the consistent excellence in both the food and service. This establishment is a must-visit for anyone craving an authentic steakhouse experience.

Pretty no-frills pizza joint, despite actually looking like a nice sit-down place. The pepperoni and mushroom slices were fine, if not a bit forgettable. Thin and crispy enough, and pretty foldable. Not the greatest, but far from the worst.

Adults night out no kids we had reservations and were seated as soon as out entire party was there our server was very nice and explained to us how they operate almost a family style dinner there was 6 of us and he told us that they would prepare enough for all 6 of us no matter what we ordered and just pro rate the price which was fine with us since we like to taste different things.  all there food was delicious the steak was moist the soup dumplings were amazing so much flavor packed into one bite the salmon was soft and tender you didn't need a knife overall we had a wonderful night and enjoyed the food don't be surprised when you get there and see a pawn shop just walk right in and straight to the back door

Delicious Italian restaurant with fresh pasta! They have a lot of vegetarian options and the service is great. I like the cozy feel with the bricks and dim lighting. It seems like there is an outdoor space which would be nice in the summer or when it warms up. The prices are reasonable. I had the Gorgonzola gnocchi and I also tried the spinach ricotta ravioli. I really enjoyed the gnocchi and would definitely come back for it. Something about the ravioli sauce was off to me but my boyfriend liked it. They serve bread with marinara prior to the meal which was good. The ricotta cheesecake was light and sweet. There are a lot of dessert options which are not listed on the menu, the server lists them for you. This is a cute date night spot and I would be happy to go again.

Nice space in a great location. We sat at the bar waiting for happy hour which for NYC looked excellent. We wound up just getting a snack and going out to dinner later. The bartender was a tad grumpy but tolerable. At his suggestion, we got the shrimp tacos which were excellent. They came with fries and a side salad which were hot and the salad was fresh and tasty. I would have preferred the taco to have a crunchy element but it was just the sauce covered shrimp and tortilla. It was still great and I didn't have to take out a loan to pay for it!

Title: Unique Experience with Room for Improvement

My experience reserving a table for my students’ Senior lunch trip at this restaurant was quite the feat, requiring two months of advance planning and a bit of persistence, as the best way to get in touch was via email. However, the restaurant does offer a variety of group rates to suit different needs, which is a plus.

Upon arrival for our large reservation, the staff were notably accommodating, especially to my students with autism, who were thoroughly entertained throughout the visit. Service was attentive, with prompt drink refills and a sufficient number of waitstaff for our group's size.

The food was generally good; my grilled chicken Caesar salad was both tender and generously portioned, leaving me quite satisfied. Unfortunately, the sodas lacked fizz and were a letdown.

While the restaurant's theme contributed to a showy atmosphere filled with effects and props, I found the overall "spooky" theme and performance somewhat dated and corny. Although not particularly appealing to me, the students were enthralled, suggesting it resonates well with a younger audience.

In summary, while the food passed muster and the service was excellent, the ambiance seems more suited to children and teens. As an adult, Jekyll and Hyde doesn't top my list for a return visit, though it has its charms for the right audience.

Title: Lackluster Pizza in a City of Stars

In a metropolis celebrated for its pizza, this venue unfortunately doesn't stack up. Sampling a few of their pizzas left us underwhelmed and craving the robust flavors synonymous with New York's finest. However, it wasn't all a miss; their pappardelle pasta managed to delight.

Prices here are a tad steep, especially when considering its direct competition with the local favorite, Prince St. Pizza. While the moderately priced wines and inviting ambiance are pluses, the overall experience doesn't justify the cost or the potential long waits due to its popularity.

For those in pursuit of that quintessential New York slice, I'd suggest skipping the possibly lengthy queue here and venturing to Prince St. Pizza instead.

I would classify this place as more of a diner than a cafe. The thing is it is always packed!  I'm not sure what the draw is with the place. The food is bland and like I mentioned it reminds me of your typical diner. Listen, I love diners but this "cafe" doesn't hit a home run.  The egg white omelet was bland and although it was a big portion that didn't help. The prices are reasonable so that is a positive. Another positive is that the food comes out quick.  Perfect place to grab a quick bite before getting back to work or in a rush. Don't expect to be blown away though.

Areppas offers  Latin American delicacies. The famous ones are Areppas, Rice Bowls and Empanadas. These are all like make your own Areppas or bowls. You choose all the fresh ingredients that goes into your dish. Areppas- There are three kinds of bases. Our favorite was the green one. The avocado chicken salad mix is a filling you must have! Rice Bowl- The quantity is enough for a meal. Loved the options given. Empanadas- We tried the cheese, vegan and chicken empanadas. Chicken empanadas were our favourite and its a must try.

I've been here a few times for brunch and I have to say I love this place. Ths prices are much better than a lot of establishments and the food is so good. I really want to try it for dinner because the specials look SOOOO GOOOOOD. There drinks are reasonable, delicious, and a wide variety. This is definitely a good place for a date or a group with so many tasty options.

We went right around noon and just walked in and were seated immediately. This seems like a good place to come with a bunch of people. If you sit at a table, there's a 3 slice minimum. Because it was my friend and I, we sat at the bar and could each just get a slice. We tried the artichoke pizza of course, and it was $6 a slice, but these were massive, like Costco-sized, so it was worth it. Each slice is cut in half and they give you paper plates to eat off of. The artichoke pizza was super creamy and rich, next time I'll try a slice with normal red sauce.

Didn't like at all! Sorry I thought it would be great for brunch and lunch... nope. You see I have fries but it was suppose to come with home fries. They ran out said the waitress.... wow, thanks for telling me when my food came out. The corn beef was bland... where the sauerkraut and cheese??? Not here... "If I don't like it, I don't swallow". I guess I'll starve today because the food is nasty!

Title: Delightful First Experience at Maison Pickle

My anticipation for Maison Pickle, conveniently situated opposite the AMC theater, was met with pure satisfaction on my inaugural visit. We arrived to a welcoming, less crowded ambiance, which allowed us to appreciate the restaurant's spaciousness and charmingly old-fashioned décor.

The staff was prompt in seating us and the waiter expertly recommended the 3-course lunch special—a steal at $21. The starter, a sumptuous broccoli and cheese soup, set the bar high with its comforting warmth and flavor. Both entrees were generous in size; my classic dip sandwich was an indulgent assembly of juicy roast beef and melted cheese on a hefty roll, further enhanced when swathed in au jus. The buffalo Mac and cheese was equally commendable, with a richness that rendered it almost too decadent to finish, especially with dessert in mind.

Speaking of dessert, the pie selection concluded the meal beautifully. The Oreo pie was a luscious treat, while the key lime pie offered a zesty counterbalance to the preceding courses.

Service throughout was friendly and unobtrusive, contributing to an overall delightful dining experience. Maison Pickle left me eager to return with friends in tow, to share in the visually appealing and equally scrumptious fare.

I went here the other day with a bunch of my classmates for our friendsgiving lunch. Let me esplain something to you this is the best pizza in new york. I dont care what anyone says. All 16 of us were in love with the food. The margarita pizza was off the chain, it was crispy but saucy and cheesy and the sauce (mama mia) was the best sauce ive ever had. We tried the clam pizza, dios mio, i died and went to heaven. We got drunk off that vodka pizza. The sangria was bananas (no actual bananas used in the making of the sangria). Even the President, Dave Portnoy himself, rated this place a 9.0. We know how conservative the Prez can be with his scores so the fact that he gave this place a 9 really should tell you that its a 10.

Embarking on a culinary voyage along the Hudson River aboard a boat, I recently indulged in an exceptional dining experience featuring lobster, oyster, and an array of seafood delights. The mere cost of entry is $10, which is a small price to pay for the promise of such a scenic journey. 

While the food prices are on the higher side, one must consider the spectacular views that come as part of the package – the New York skyline, easing past as you savor each bite, is worth every penny. The seafood served is impressively fresh; a live display on the boat tantalizes with what's to come on your plate.

Guests are welcomed to linger for as long as they desire, which is a delightful perk. Dining in a party of eight, we discovered the gratuity is included automatically – a practice not uncommon in NYC establishments. Overall, the experience is one to be savored, perhaps not just for the food, but for the unique ambiance that can only be captured aboard this floating feast.

Having seen the attention-grabbing 99 cent pizza video, I was eager to see if the hype was justified. And indeed, for a mere dollar, you can't go wrong with a cheese slice. I sampled pies from two different establishments claiming the 99 cent price tag, discovering a bit of inconsistency between them. The first spot piled on the cheese but was a bit stingy with the sauce, while the second had a sweeter tomato sauce that overpowered the cheese. Regardless of these slight variations, both slices delivered on value. The 99 cent pizza experience is a budget-friendly delight that's certainly worth the buck at either location.

I came back here for a dinner with a friend as I decided to give it another try. We each got a cocktail to start the dinner. I got Capri Sun which was a good mix of passion fruit and tiki spices; it was very refreshing! My friend got View from Positano, a gin based cocktail with black pepper and strawberry. I liked my friend's slightly more because the blend of black paper and sweetness from strawberry masked the taste of alc and felt like I was drinking a delicious strawberry juice. I highly recommend both of these cocktails. For appetizers, we got: - Cecina with Calabrian tuna: we wrapped this Italian chickpea pancake with the tuna tartare and chili sauce made of garlic and shallots. It tasted like a delicious, unique, savory crepe and I'd definitely want to get this if I come here again! - Squash Carpaccio: I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS!! I felt in love with it at first bite. Thin squash layers drenched in sweet honey agrocolce, cheese, and sunflower seeds tasted HEAVENLY! If you're dining at Santina, you should definitely try this. - Lamb meatballs: very juicy and melted nicely in my mouth. The sweetness from agrodolce Italian sauce and pecorino cheese complemented the meat sooo well. For entrees, we got: - Shrimp Zingara with spicy tomato and olive: it was light yet flavorful; it reminded me of shrimp fried rice but with nice tomato sauce! It wasn't really spicy either, which was perfect for me. - Tortellini Sorrentina: tortellini filled with sheep's milk ricotta definitely hit the spot! Especially with familiar pesto and tomato sauce, I don't think you can go wrong with this dish. - Spicy Potatoes, Garlic Broccoli, Grilled Mushrooms: got these as side dishes and they were all delicious. I especially loved the grilled mushrooms and spicy potatoes. These crispy fried potatoes with the chili sauce can get spicy but they were so good I couldn't stop eating! - Santina Sundae: the dessert came in a giant bowl with 3 big scoops of delicious ice cream flavors -- cherry, coconut, and pistachio. The ice cream was so creamy and true to the flavors. It was a huge sundae so I think it's definitely shareable among 2 or 3 people! I learned more about Santina after my second visit and I can definitely recommend here for a date night, nice gathering, or any occasion. Even from my very first visit, I'm still in love with this unique Italian seaside/ coastal themed restaurant with a mix of fancy and vibrant atmosphere. It is a slightly pricier restaurant, but with the unique and excellent atmosphere, diversity of the menu, and quality of the food, it does pay off!

Made a reservation for 2 about 45 minutes before arriving and they sat us with no problem. Great service and the District burger was fantastic. Definitely would recommend and the food came out relatively quickly. They have happy hour 4 to 7 with a couple $5 beers and $8 wines. A few other things on that menu as well but not sure of the prices. Definitely check this place out. Had a lively atmosphere for a Friday at 6.

One of my fave dumpling places in the city. I usually get fried pork and chive since they're the cheapest and fastest and always tasty. Sometimes I take home a bag of frozen ones. Excellent deal for the price and filling. I also love the scallion pancake sandwich with duck. It is busy no matter when you go and often hard to find seating since it's not a large place.

We and I came for dinner on a Wed night with reservations.  This adorable wine bar and restaurant almost has the feel of 3 separate establishments.  When you first walk in, you're in a room that feels much like a standard bar: a long bar that spans the length of the room on the left with many small 2-top tables on the right.  Past the bar and down a short hallway is a more spacious dining room with tables that seat 2 and 4.  Keep walking through a door in the back of the restaurant and you're in a lovely patio space that's covered and heated in the winter.  We went for the patio as it felt less formal and more lively than the dining room.Unsurprisingly for a wine bar, the wine list is substantial.  They also have a decent selection of imported beer.  The food menu is comprised mostly of appetizers and small plates, which makes this place well-suited for groups who want to try a bunch of items.  For appetizers, we shared the 3 dips (cucumber-dill yogurt, Japanese eggplant, and guac, $18), garlic-ginger shrimp ($15), and crab cake ($16).  We also shared two entrees: the wild mushroom ravioli ($26) and the salmon ($28).  The appetizer portions were very small (i.e., 5 shrimps for $15, 3 crab cakes for $16), but very, very tasty.  The entree portions were larger, of course, but much less impressive in terms of flavor.  Both entrees were just a little bland and boring, although the salmon was was perfectly crispy on the outside yet still moist and soft on the inside.All in all, Wine:30 is a great choice for large groups as well as intimate dates.  If they have room, def choose the patio seating outside.

I had a fantastic weekday lunch at this restaurant, particularly impressed by their special lunch menu for burgers. Opting for a burger accompanied by truffle fries was a delightful choice. Cleverly, they served the truffle separately in a ketchup container, ensuring every fry had its fair share of truffle goodness. The experience was a resounding "Nom nom nom!" in my book, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Highly recommended for burger aficionados!

I really liked this place... Clean, organized and non pretentious. We ordered a nice bottle of soju accompanied with watercress pancake to start with.Then came the assorted complimentary small plates... My favorite part of any Korean meal.Their speciality is they make their tofu in-house. Needless to say it was super fresh and melt in the mouth texture.For main course I ordered specialty seafood pot (without shrimps as I'm allergic to it) with tofu stew.It was one of the best seafood pots I have ever had. I think it's the in-house made tofu stew that did the trick and worked so well. Their chef deserves an applause for sure.It's definitely worth a second visit coz I am already craving a nice hot pot made with silky fresh tofu..

I went with a friend for brunch on a Sunday afternoon. We made a reservation; the place wasn't too packed, you can definitely do a walk-in. The restaurant is very spacious - from the open windows in the front to the back area to the downstairs seating. We were seated in the back corner where it was decorated as if we were eating outside in a forest. I loved the vibe, it really complemented the warm weather and our mood. This place would be great for a big party!To start, of course, we had to order the guac and chips and a frozen margarita. Even if the main course is bad, I'll be content with that. The guac was nicely seasoned, although the portion is tiny, the flavors made up for it. They also serve the chips with this tomato sauce which I loved. Not sure what it was, but I couldn't stop dipping my chips in it. I even dipped my steak in it.For my main course, I ordered the carne asada y huevos, aka steak and eggs. The steak was a little too dry and bland but the tomato sauce made it a little better. The service was great. I think there was a manager actually walking around refilling our margarita glasses, which I appreciated. I would definitely come back here, however, I'll be trying another entree.

During a bustling Friday afternoon, my best friend and I ventured into the culinary hotspot of Los Tacos, a popular joint known for its savory Mexican offerings. Despite it being a weekday at 1 pm, we were greeted by a daunting queue—a testament to the spot's acclaim, which I've noticed swells even further on weekends.

We dove into a feast of tacos, sampling the carne asada, pollo, and adobada, all nestled in soft corn tortillas. Each taco was a symphony of tenderness, with meats that melted in the mouth and a well-balanced flurry of flavors. The addition of crispy onions lent a satisfying crunch and zesty kick, while the silky guacamole and vibrant pico de gallo crowned the tacos with layers of complexity. At just $3.95 apiece, or $3.75 for chicken and pork, these tacos offered remarkable value; a duo of them proved to be a hearty meal.

The pollo reigned supreme in my ranking, but frankly, each variety showcased impeccable taste and quality. Amid the energetic thrum of Chelsea Market, Los Tacos stands as a culinary beacon, dishing out affordable, exquisite bites that are wholly worth the wait.

HALLE-FREAKING-LUJAH. There's finally a dim sum place close enough to my apartment so I no longer have to trek all the way to Chinatown (I'm lazy, sue me) or Flushing whenever I have a craving. Not only is the location v ideal, but the actual dim sum is v v v delish too. Having grown up eating dim sum once a month with my family, I can attest that Dim Sum Palace's Har Gow (shrimp dumplings), Shumai, Chicken Feet, Lo Bak Go (radish cake), etc. are just as good as the ones I always loved eating as a kid and now as an adult. The Mango Smoothies my boyfriend and I got were also so fresh and yummy too. The only dish that fell a little flat for me was the Xiao Long Bao, which was unfortunately just not flavored very well. Both the meat and the soup were pretty bland and just left so much to be desired. Aside from that, however, everything else was extremely tasty and will definitely be ordered again the next time I get that dim sum itch.

Arrived at 7:15p for our reservation and was seated within 5 minutes.  Ended up ordering the RW fixed price menu within 10 min after flagging down our waiter. 30 min pass and still nothing - not even bread.  We asked one of the servers for bread and he brought it finally to the table.  Another 15 min pass before they finally bring out the appetizers (they had to ask if we had already gotten them!).  The ravioli with truffle was delicious- the pate was not.  After about 20 minutes our entrees came out - except they we're the wrong ones.  Ended up having to wait another 10 minutes but at ke I st our waiter let us keep the erroneous entrees.  The hangar steak was not bad - the fish however was very bland.  The cornish hen was also just okay.  For desserts, they ended up bringing out the wrong ones again - again our waiter let us keep the erroneous desserts.  The banana brulee was okay and ditto for the profiteroles.  The croquant was tasty however.At the end of our meal our waiter told us there was an error in the system with the kitchen basically replicating the order of the people who sat at out table before us.  That's excusable I suppose, but what isn't is the fact that our meal, all told, took nearly 3 hours!In summary:Service: 2/5Food: 3.5/5Ambiance: 3/5 (super loud)Value: 3.5/5Had the food quality been better, we would give it another shot.  Unfortunately it was not and we will not be back.

Title: A Hidden Jerky Gem in NYC

If I were a local New Yorker, I might be tempted to keep this place a well-guarded secret – the Malaysian-style jerky here is that good. Nestled in the heart of NYC, this spot is a carnivore's delight, crafting fresh, melt-in-your-mouth jerky on the daily, and let me tell you, the hype is real. Their popularity is evident as they occasionally run low; I witnessed a customer purchasing a whopping 20 pounds!

This isn't your typical tough and chewy jerky. Forget about gnawing endlessly or encountering unyielding fat – this jerky is tender, succulent, and bursting with flavor. With a variety that includes pork, beef, chicken, curry beef, and even shrimp, there's something for every palate. Both the pork and beef options come in regular or spicy, but even the spicy is pleasantly mild.

Travelers take note: they offer vacuum-sealing for easy transport, exemplified by our own 8-pound haul back to Hawaii. Price-wise, this jerky may not be the cheapest on the market, but it's a prime example of getting what you pay for – sheer quality. One crucial tip: this is a cash-only establishment, so come prepared. Trust me, it's worth every penny.

Pricey choice for lunch. The food is ok, nothing special, not super tasty nor super awful. However, with the food pricing I could spend it somewhere else for more bang for a buck. I'd come here only if I can afford it. I came here to try it out and I will try to avoid this place at much as possible The ambiance, however, is great and enjoyable

YUM! We were looking for a close breakfast spot while staying at the Marriott on Times Square and we found this gem. Absolutely delicious! We tried the daily special which was an apple and caramel crepe, and we also tried the crepe with strawberries and nutella. Both were amazing and we would return should we find ourselves in the area again! The staff was friendly but the upstairs seating area was pretty dirty during our visit, so that was disappointing. The cleanliness affects the 3/5 stars for this review.

Title: A Cozy Return to Antalia for Turkish Delights

My recent visit to Antalia only reaffirmed my love for this gem. The staff's kindness is unparalleled, setting a standard that others should strive for. Having dined here before, my friend and I had high expectations for the Turkish fare and were not disappointed.

On arrival, despite my friend's tardiness and my own discomfort from a muscle injury, I was gratefully seated without delay. While we intended to sip on Turkish white wine and were initially informed it was unavailable, the Pinot Grigio proved a refreshing alternative. The warm bread with olive tapenade, further complemented by olive oil upon request, was irresistible.

For our mains, the Meatballs (lamb) with a vibrant medley of veggies for my friend, and my choice of Chicken Adana, were spice-laden and satisfying, especially having substituted rice for more vegetables. Both dishes were hearty and left us content.

To top off our meal, a Yelp check-in earned us a free dessert, but the waiter's generosity extended to an additional sweet treat. We indulged in a luscious Turkish flan and a dessert akin to Baklava, whose name I can't recall.

The ambiance at Antalia was welcoming and pristine, though the lighting could be softened. Nevertheless, we relished several hours of delectable food and delightful company. Nestled on 45th Street, Antalia is a haven of Turkish comfort food. Do try it - and don't miss out on the Chicken Adana!

Title: A True Italian Gem

I'm thrilled to have discovered an Italian restaurant that truly stands out from the crowd. Their spaghetti tangled perfectly with a dollop of exquisite burrata—a dish that simply melts in your mouth. The margherita pizza, a blissful blend of flavors, showcases a sauce distinct from the spaghetti's, highlighting their dedication to authenticity and variety.

Curiosity led me back for their gnocchi, and I was not disappointed. The creamy dish, enhanced by the freshness of the burrata, was a testament to their culinary prowess. My husband's clam spaghetti was a marvel of balance, delivering the essence of the sea without being overwhelmed by sauce.

This establishment has swiftly ascended to my list of favorite Italian spots, sparing me the trip to Chelsea for exceptional pasta and pizza. The harmonious relationship between quality, price, and service confirms that this is not just another Italian restaurant—it's a culinary experience to cherish.

Best place for a valued takeout lunch of Chinese BBQ meats over rice. Place is small, only a counter for ordering. There is always a line out the door but it moves fast. Longer line during lunch and evening hours. The roast pork or chicken over rice with vegetables is only $4.25. Very tasty and satisfying.

Fried chickens were delicious. But I want to share my experience about a hostess there. She was rude and unfriendly. So I went back to check in after I received the "table is ready" text, then she told me to line up at the back while helping other people who just walked in and gave them a table. I felt discriminated and was disappointed.

What a great find! Spanish food at a reasonable price. Came here to celebrate my partner's birthday and they made it very special. We had a bunch of stuff and very happy about all of them.Sparkling sangria- took the large pitcher and thought the amount for that price was completely reasonable. Lots of fruits and nice wine :)The empanadas with beef was excellent. Crispy shells and well done tender pieces of beef inside. Spices were nicely balanced and the shell had a lovely flavor too. The sauce was great too!The baby lamb shanks were so well done with mint something something. This comes with roasted veggies which were absolutely tender and melts in your mouth. Patatas bravas- what can I say! I love potatoes and spicy ones at that. They were cooked fully with the right amount of texture left. This dish is beautifully spicy. The paella takes 30-40 minutes so I ordered it the minute I sat down. Ordered the valencia and it was very homely. Very comforting. And full of meat. Everything was cooked to perfection. Their flan with fresh fruit was It's perfect for a date night when you don't want to visit a $$$$ restaurant but still have a nice time and have good food. I also got the vibe It would be great for groups.

5 Stars, because it's a great spot to grab lunch and super healthy. This place is reasonable in quality, quantity, and pricing. The staff is by far the sweetest people and they're always willing to help and answer any questions you have. I preferably love the MANILA (crispy pork belly or grilled chicken, Chinese broccoli, bean sprouts, scallions, crispy garlic, crispy shallots, poached egg, adobo sauce), rather than getting the crispy pork belly or grilled chicken I ended up replacing it with the crispy tofu. The dish is savory, so if you like something not too sweet, this is a good dish. I have tried many of their dishes, they are GREAT but Manila is my favorite. I highly recommend this place to Friends + Coworkers, especially those that are visiting NYC.

There's been a lot of buzz around Barn Joo and I was excited about finally having the chance to give them a try. Since they're very popular, they won't seat you until the entire party has arrived. This can be an amusing sight to see, as folks anxiously wait for their companions to arrive before the tables are snagged. We didn't have a problem for a party of 2 at 5:30 on a Tuesday. We had the seafood pancake and bulgogi hot pot (and a side of rice, not included with the bowl). They're definitely pricey for the portion size, but the food is so so good - high quality ingredients packed with flavor.

If in search of soup dumplings, I would recommend this spot for their black truffle one. It's a unique burst of flavor. Otherwise, the standard pork soup dumplings and Kung Pao chicken we tried were tasty, but obviously not unique to this restaurant.I definitely plan on returning for the black truffle soup dumplings. Everything if very fair priced as well.After I second visit, I should add that even the entreés here are delicious. The tangerine beef, in particular, is perfectly crisp with just enough hint of citrus. I highly recommend this restaurant. To clarify, this is Shanghai 21 on Mott St. There is another restaurant with a similar name in the area.This was an excellent spot for a group outing- super affordable with a generous portions and no lack of options.

I enjoy dining at Burger & Barrel. It's a great place to get a burger. The restaurant is helmed by chef Josh Capon of Lure Fishbar and it does a good job. Mr. Capon's burger is a multiple award-winning masterpiece, having won at the New York City Wine & Food Festival and the South Beach Wine & Food Festival. The Bash Burger is available here in a six oz Patty version, but there is also a dual 4 oz (eight oz total, i.e. a half-pound) version. It's delicious. It's what a Big Mac aspires to be, if one were sentient and could fortify itself with better quality ingredients. They also have many wines on offer and have a good selection of cocktails, such as a Hemingway daiquiri. It's a kind of an upscale-feeling dining space, especially for a burger restaurant, but it's still comfortable. Service was very attentive. They even give little amuse bouches, which is an unexpected nice touch. I'm glad this place exists.

I love this soup kiosk! I tried the beef chili with rice and cheese. It was fantastic! The beans, beef and chili soup was well seasoned and super savory. If you're looking for something a bit spicy, this definitely isn't a spicy chili. However, they have tobacco sauce right on the counter if you'd like to add a little extra. For $10 I got a large soup with rice cheese and bread cost $8.50. I gave the remaining $1.50 for tip. Again super tasty and a bargain lunch that really fills you.

First time here to try their pie...it was delicious. Service was great and friendly. Did not like the cash only part, nor their no refill on the drinks. Would definitely order their pizza again....takeout.

We orders the curry nan, and chicken satay for appetizers. Got a free Thai iced tea once I checked in! For entrees we got chicken pad Thai and some other Thai spicy noodle which I forgot the name. Everything was  really good, and they were playing Reggaeton music which is  for me! Lol couldn't believe they been open for 3 years and this was the first time we ate there. Food wasn't overpriced like the Thai restaurant on ST. Mark st. "Cough cough" anyway it's in the basement which is why I never noticed it. The only complaint I had was towards the end I wanted to pay with my credit card and their machine was offline so I had to drive to my bank to get money. Wish they could of told us before but it happens. The food made up for that

Came before a show at Joe's Pub. Happy hour seemed good but I wasn't expecting much for $3 margarita. It is what it is. The food was very tasty and nicely presented. Service was attentive and polite. Atmosphere was nice chill and cool. Some dishes seemed a bit higher than Hell's Kitchen Thai places.  My shrimp fish did have a good amount a shrimp in it. Might come again before a show.

I recently visited this bustling restaurant using the Ritual app, which ensured my order was promptly ready despite the crowd. I opted for the chicken bun, which was delicious and perfectly portioned for a satisfying meal. I'm already looking forward to my next visit to try out their bowls. Highly recommended for a quick, tasty bite!

Title: A Stylish Spot with Room for Culinary Improvement

My anticipation for visiting the new Chinatown branch of this restaurant, having eyed its Greenwich Village location, was met with a mix of impressions. The interior exudes a modern charm, complete with palm tree wallpaper, and offers ample space with a mix of tables and booths. The aesthetic appeal made a strong first impression.

Service was prompt; we were seated immediately upon arrival. The menu offered an enticing variety of appetizers and main courses, with enough options to pique anyone's curiosity. We decided on the Fresh Summer Rolls and Fried Spring Rolls, both priced at $8. While these starters were decent, they didn't stray far from what one might expect—standard fare without much to distinguish them from any other restaurant's offerings.

A slight hiccup occurred when our main dishes arrived—there was a mix-up with my order. However, the staff managed the situation with swift apologies and a speedy resolution, which was commendable.

The main event was the Bun Bo Hue, attractively presented and reasonably priced at $12.95. This dish, featuring brisket, beef slices, and Vietnamese ham in a pork broth, promised a rich experience but fell short of delivering a memorable taste. The absence of a "WOW factor" left me contemplating the value and flavor profile compared with local pho spots, which seem to offer more bang for the buck.

In summary, while the restaurant scores high on style and service, the culinary experience itself doesn't quite match up. It's worth a visit for those in the area seeking a visually pleasing dining environment, but for those chasing extraordinary flavors, the local pho joints might still be the better call.

Title: A Piadina Paradise You Won't Want to Miss

I've long anticipated my visit to this charming eatery, famous for its Piadina – an Italian street food delicacy that's a must-add to any foodie's bucket list. The airy stroll from mid-town to Soho did wonders to whet my appetite for the scrumptious Romagnola piadina, a delightful flatbread meal that shuns the bloat for a light yet satisfying experience, perfect any time of the day.

This gem offers a haven for those seeking an authentic taste of Italy with their variety of piadinas, cassoni, and piadizzas. The cassoni, a cheesy, sealed pocket, and the piadizza, mirroring a thin, crunchy pizza, further tantalize the taste buds. The option to customize your piadina ensures that each visit can be a new flavor adventure.

Eating on the go is a breeze with their convenient set-up of stools and a standing counter. The service matches the quality of the food – friendly and efficient, they make sure your gastronomic journey is a smooth one.

Don't let the limited seating deter you; these treats are best enjoyed fresh and warm. I'm already planning my next visit and eagerly eyeing my next piadina creation. The doors are open Monday to Friday from 7am to 8pm, and on weekends from 8am to 4pm – mark your calendars and indulge in this Italian street food rarity.

Fast service and good bar food. I usually order a side of fries & wings. If you want something more filling they have the best burgers in the area. I would recommend this place for lunch and dinner.     Sandro, was friendly and checked up on us. They have happy hour drinks/food. I had drinks here, they have a very good list of beer and cocktails . If you want a great atmosphere or a place to watch sports with a  good menu & reasonable prices come here. I'll definitely be coming back. Great friendly service every time I go.

AWESOME ATMOSPHERE! It was like checking into a five star hotel. Free coat and bag check, fancy interior design and a really minimalist hip modern vibe. The food was delicious but not the best I've ever had. I felt like quality and portions did not match the price point. The truffles were flavorless and expensive. It might have just been shredded paper dusted with soil. The sushi was good but I've had fresher sushi from other places. The dessert was lacking. It was meant to be modern gastronomy-esque but they basically served egg whites in the form of styrofoam. There's a good way to serve meringue and there's whatever we were served. I would only come back for the fancy 9k robo toilets. The bathroom and hospitality were the redeeming qualities for this overrated restaurant

Damn. First off I was fortunate enough to meet the owner, Chris tonight, he was extremely personable, loving, and hilarious. Then, the manager Chris was even funnier and amazing! The bartenders Justyn and Sherley were hilarious, ambitious, and extremely loving. Them tenders were so damn tender !!! The sauces were delicious and the music. Yo. I felt like I was at a black BBQ in the 90s living my best life. They made us margaritas with tequila from 1942- Don 1942... my drawls feel off at first taste. If you want to have a great personable experience ... come here!

Super easy to make a reservation using the yelp app, and the food is delicious. The restaurant is quite small so we were seated right next to the door with cold wind blasting in when opened. Otherwise service was on point and presentation of dishes was beautiful.Food wise, I'd highly recommend the lamb chops! We ordered two of these; they just melt in your mouth. Also get the ghost chili chicken and peri peri prawn appetizers, methi chicken entree (which pretty much tastes like chicken curry) and coconut kheer dessert. I took off one star as the butter chicken didn't blow me away and the daulat ki chaat was grainy.

A visit is must during the holidays and without it I'd say the holidays are not complete!! Everyone participating in this beautiful tradition of decorating their houses surely do an awesome job. Each house literally reminds me of how wonderful Christmas time is and the joy it brings to my heart. There's no fee but can get a guided tour but not necessary though. Definitely plan your trip accordingly as it gets really busy therefore finding parking can be a hassle but should be fine if you park 15-20 mins away. It's a residential area so be mindful of not disturbing the residents and littering on the streets!! Weekends are very busy as I went on a Saturday around 9pm barely had a spot to stand. It was cold so dress warm and be prepared for walking around a lot.

Looking for a light lunch to share on a sunny Saturday and I remembered I wanted to try this place.  I'm so glad we did.First the service at the bar with our friendly bartender was outstanding.He said yes to everything we asked for... light ice in our drinks.  No problem.  Medium well on the steak.  No problem.  Baguette instead of Ciabatta bread.  No problem.   In other words, they are VERY accommodating and didn't make us feel weird about it.   We sat at the bar and shared that hanger steak sandwich along with a couple of fruity Rose Sangria's.  It was a really nice day and meal.  Felt like family.   Stop in but late in the week for dinner, try to make reservations as it's a bit small interior.   Wonderful and will be back.

Can't speak to the food because I've only ever been here for drinks, but their prices are very reasonable for this area. A large frozen margarita is $8 ($5 on certain days!) and good prices for other drinks too. Had to knock a star because the bar area is too cramped, but I'll always come back when I'm craving a marg.

We stopped here briefly while we were in New York City. We had been walking around and were starving. We had passed this place a few times and noticed that it was never ever not busy. Based just on that we assumed the food had to be great and fresh and we were not disappointed. The food was quick affordable and very tasty. I would suggest a stop at this restaurant if for nothing else than just for the experience

Lounge UES with a cool ambiance.This was a favorite spot for the first number of visits, but was very disappointed the recent visit. The lounge has lost its magic for me with major declines in service, drinks and food. Ambiance.  Comfortable seating with booths, tables, a sofa great for groups of friends and dates.  Dark and really like the brightly lit yellow wall, creating visual silhouettes as patrons walk by.  Two Big TV screens in the back show horror greats, but I much preferred the old black and white horror classics I've seen in the past- which added a magical flare to the lounge --  to the  Batman scene on my recent visit - showing the half mauled face of the joker as I was about to eat my tuna tar tar of a similar  "consistency".  Disturbing, and I needed to switch seats so my back was to the screen.  Service.  The servers we've had in the past were attentive and friendly, including one who let me take a couple photos of her against the backdrop a previous time.  But the recent visit the server was MIA, and after waiting a substantial amount of time to get a first, then a second drink and appetizer, I had to find her myself both times to place the orders. When I asked if they could make any of the drinks that used to be on the menu, she said no, they don't even have the ingredients.  When I told her I wasn't happy with the coconut drink, as it was too sweet, she said it was made exactly how it was described on the menu.  Note:  besides being poor service with such a response, the menu did not describe the coconut drink as syrupy and sticky sweet, which would have been an accurate description. When I was about to give her our food order saying I would check on my friends drink, she turned and walked away from me as I was talking, without even saying excuse me.  Very rude.  The one plus is after deciding we wanted to go elsewhere to have food and drinks, telling her we needed to catch a train, she did rush the appetizer order. Food and drinks.
