Another big disappointment.  They used to have so many creative quality tasty appetizers and specialty drinks that are not on the menu now.  The smoke drink I liked and a couple others were gone, and the cool looking drink served in a coconut with burning cinnamon which I enjoyed when I had it previous visits, tasted like syrup and was awful. I like sweet rum drinks but this was all sugar and minimal flavor. I opted for an old fashioned which was well made.The tuna tar tar we ordered, while pretty, if your eyes were closed you would not even be able to tell you were having tuna tar tar.Great lounge for its ambiance, but I would not go out of my way as I would have before, and would skip the food and specialty drinks.

Title: A Hidden Gem That's Well Worth the Splurge

My boyfriend and I were eagerly anticipating our dining experience at this tucked-away New York eatery, having reserved our table nearly three weeks in advance. This decision was a highlight of our trip. The restaurant's inconspicuous entrance, nestled beside a hotel, could be easily overlooked, but what awaited us inside was a meal to remember.

Opting for the $120 set meal each, we indulged ourselves further with an additional whole lobster for a $68 surplus. Our culinary journey began with an arugula, calamari, and shiitake mushroom dish in a delightful ponzu sauce that awakened our palates with its refreshing zest. A procession of crispy yet light tempura—including shrimp heads, shrimp, okra, Japanese onion, red snapper, eggplant, and cauliflower—followed, masterfully fried to avoid that unwelcome greasy feeling.

The whole lobster was the pièce de résistance, justifying its cost and elevating the meal to new heights. It's a decadent choice that I wholeheartedly recommend.

The service was impeccable. The staff, with their meticulous attention to detail, promptly wiped any spills and constantly refreshed our water, all while providing insightful guidance on how best to savor each dish, whether it be with tempura sauce, seasoning, or a simple squeeze of lime.

While the price point is steep, the quality of food and service renders this dining experience a worthwhile investment. This restaurant is a culinary treasure I look forward to returning to in the future.

Title: A True New York Deli Gem: Angela's

If you're on the hunt for that quintessential New York deli breakfast sandwich experience without breaking the bank, Angela's is your go-to spot. My first encounter was back in early 2018 when I was on a mission to satisfy a friend’s craving for an authentic deli experience. Just a stone's throw away from St. Patrick’s Cathedral and Central Park, Angela's not only delivered with its prime location but also nailed the classic deli vibes.

My friend's Reuben was a hit, and my own pastrami & egg sandwich was nothing short of spectacular – even more so considering the steal of a price at $3.50. And don't get me started on the hazelnut coffee; it's a must-try!

Repeated orders via Grubhub have solidified Angela's as my breakfast haven, especially with its proximity to my office. My go-to pastrami or ham and egg sandwiches, with an occasional side of their delightful hazelnut coffee, always come in under $6. A pro-tip: don't forget to request ketchup packets.

My most recent indulgence, the Hobo Special, left me both satisfied and stuffed, all for about $6. It's places like Angela's that remind you of the simple joy of a superb, affordable meal in the heart of the city.

Title: Convenient Vegan Sushi in a Bustling Market Setting

I stumbled upon Beyond Sushi while seeking a spot to pass the time, and what I found was a decent vegan sushi experience tucked away in a crowded NYC supermarket. The space, though challenging to locate initially, offers an intriguing range of products and food stands.

In the heart of the market, Beyond Sushi serves up its plant-based delights with efficiency. I tried the spicy mang roll, which was promptly prepared and packed for takeaway, alongside a refreshing yuzu lemonade. Despite the seating crunch, I managed to carve out a nook for myself to savor my meal.

Be warned, the seating area could benefit from some attention, as I noted an unattended spill during my visit. However, the staff at Beyond Sushi were amiable and the food enjoyable. This isn’t your traditional lunch retreat, but rather a grab-and-go gem for those looking to enjoy good sushi and perhaps some unique grocery finds.

During a leisurely stroll through Hudson Yards mall, my friend and I discovered a charming little gem of a convenience store known for its Asian fare. To our delight, right as we prepared to pay, the cashier announced a timely 'Buy One Get One' deal on kimbaps starting at 4pm, which allowed us to snag both a spicy chicken and a tuna kimbap for merely $11. The deal was as savory as the food itself: each kimbap was a delicious fusion of flavors, fresh, and satisfying. While the store is strictly takeout, the mall provides ample seating to enjoy your quick snack. A delightful find for a quick, affordable, and tasty bite in Hudson Yards.

Title: A Galactic Refuge in Hell's Kitchen

Tucked away in the heart of Hell's Kitchen, Galaxy Diner shines as a beacon for the inebriated seeking solace in greasy delights. Stumbling in post-cocktail revelries, I discovered that this place truly understands the assignment when it comes to comfort food.

The service staff deserves a shout-out – they're downright accommodating. Case in point, they resurrected my favorite cheeseburger that had vanished from the menu, all with a can-do attitude and a smile. My customized order arrived steaming and swift, a testament to the kitchen's efficiency.

I'm a creature of habit, indulging in their burgers on repeat visits, so I can't vouch for the entirety of the menu. But, the potato skins? They're a scrumptious bet.

Be warned – late hours transform Galaxy Diner into a boisterous extension of nightlife. It's not your quiet corner booth experience, but if you're looking for a lively atmosphere with tasty eats post-midnight, this diner is your spot.

Title: Service Woes Overshadow Tasty Fare at Local BBQ Joint

My husband and I eagerly looked forward to our dining experience after purchasing a voucher from Gilt, exclusive to this establishment. Regrettably, our excitement dwindled as the staff appeared untrained in voucher redemption, resulting in a prolonged and disorganized ordering process.

The service disappointments extended to our table, where a 20-minute wait ensued despite a near-empty restaurant and the availability of ready-made items like mac & cheese. The visible disregard from the staff, including the manager, when reminded of our order, fell short of basic hospitality standards. Such indifference is unacceptable.

On a positive note, the cuisine, when it eventually arrived, was commendable. Generous portions satisfied, and the spicy chicken wings, boasting a perfect blend of flavor and tenderness, are a must-try. Yet, unless the service undergoes significant improvement, one might consider exploring other venues for a more reliable American BBQ experience.

Title: Disappointing Experience at a Supposedly Upscale Eatery

Our Saturday night dinner at this establishment was unfortunately underwhelming. Service was significantly lacking; our server failed to offer dessert menus post-entrées and prematurely presented the check. After requesting a dessert menu, we then had to ask for spoons to eat our dessert, only to have them strangely cleared away mid-bite.

The food itself was disappointing and did not live up to expectations. I barely touched my meal due to its lackluster taste. Although I didn't consume much, the server did not inquire about my satisfaction but instead left a takeout box for us to pack ourselves—a first in my dining experiences.

For the prices charged, I anticipated a level of service that simply wasn't provided. The appetizer was passable, but nothing distinguished itself from the average fare. Considering the quality of service and cuisine we received, there are far superior dining options available in the city.

Additionally, the state of the restrooms was off-putting; they were not only outdated but also in need of more frequent cleaning. Overall, the restaurant gives the impression of neglect and deterioration. Based on this visit, I cannot recommend dining here.

My boyfriend and I arrived around 1:30 in hopes of having a nice brunch and were seated right away. Our food came out fast and so did our drinks - BOY was everything delicious!!! We had the Ceviche for our appetizer (very great proportion), and I ordered the seafood gumbo which came with a delicious biscuit and some rice. My family is from the south and I must say, that was a bomb meal. Brought me back to my roots. My boyfriend ordered the Cod Po Boy and like every typical female, I took a bite- YASSSSSS !!! Well seasoned and it wasn't dry at all !! The French fries were a lil on the salty side but it was good to sop up all the Hennessy I had drank from the night before. We didn't kill our pockets either. The meal was very reasonably priced and so were the drinks! We had a very tasty inexpensive bottle of Rose- $40! In total we spent $95 for a great brunch experience. Also- the live jazz was a nice touch... wish there were more black people but you know ... lol. We will be back!

Title: Eco-Friendly Efforts Boost Experience at Local Eatery

I recently dined at a spot that’s big on environmental consciousness, and while I’d typically rate it a 3, their promotion of reusable bowls is a standout feature that nudges them to a 4. As a newcomer, I was left to navigate their menu without guidance, leading to an unexpectedly steep $13 for a modestly-sized meal, thanks to unadvertised extra charges. However, after a few visits, savvy ordering skills got my meal cost below $10 - albeit sans cheese and chicken/protein.

If you value sustainability, this place might resonate with you. Just be wary of the chaotic lines and figure out the system before you dive in, to avoid any surprise costs. Comparatively, their process could benefit from a page out of Chipotle or The Little Beet's playbook, ensuring a smoother and more streamlined service.

We arrived early around 6:30 and figured we barely made the cut for the happy hour that ran from 4-7pm. When we arrived, there was no host nor bartender that greeted us for at least 10 minutes. Finally a server acknowledged us and told us he'd get the host. About 10 minutes later, the host said he'd seat us soon. It was already 6:55 so we asked the bartender (who seemed disinterested in anybody) for their happy hour specials. She finally mentions the happy hour was only for the rooftop. Our reservation was at 7 so we decided to just wait. We asked the host and they said all parties had to be present.When we were finally seated, we had to ask the host for the menus and more forks/napkins as they were missing utensils on the table setting. We each only also received once piece of bread; why they didn't provide us with a basket is beyond me. Also it was a humid day and I was thirsty, but the water wasn't refilled until 8pm (at least 20 min later).The pasta arrived pretty quickly however, albeit the wrong order. On top of that, they charged us a fee ($40) for the cake we brought. We were pleased with the food but overall unsatisfied with everything else.Overall, ultra slow service, unpreparedness of the staff, the inaccurate order, and the hidden fee makes it one star. The quality of food makes up for it a bit so I'll round it up to 2 stars. Would not return or recommend.

4.5/5Sai Gon Dep is my new favorite pho restaurant in NYC. I first visited for a Saturday lunch (the $15 lunch combo of pho + spring/summer roll of your choice is a pretty good deal, relative to the other slightly "upscale" pho places) and visited again the following Tuesday for dinner to try out other dishes. The menu is pretty concise, which I can appreciate!The dishes I've tried across my two visits:- Pork summer roll: extremely passable/forgettable but not badly priced as a $2 add-on during lunch.- Shaking beef cubes: tender cubes of beef, glazed with a savory sweet sauce, served with bone marrow, watercress/red onion salad, and a fried egg. Tasty but a bit overpriced at $28. Also not sure on what cut of beef this was, but I've only ever had this dish in Vietnamese restaurants back in CA and it's always been made with filet mignon (but this felt like a tougher cut). If you do end up ordering this because ~money ain't no thang~ then definitely stuff the rice into the bone marrow to soak up the juices and you can thank me later.- Chicken pho: this was touted as their specialty by food blogs, and while this was tasty, the beef pho was subjectively much better. It came with their chicken fat dipping sauce which was super addicting and a perfectly runny egg yolk which I used to dip my noodles in. My only complaint was that the chicken meat was pretty dry after being boiled for so long. - Beef pho: tastiest beef pho that I've tried so far in Manhattan. This had a lot of depth in flavor and the meatiness of the broth managed to not be overshadowed by all the other herbs and spices. It was definitely a bit on the salty side but that didn't stop me from downing the entire thing. I only wish there was more meat included (without having to add more for a premium). My serving only had a couple bites of the shredded oxtail which seemed a bit stingy since it is a BEEF pho. I also think the crueller add-on is a waste of money, because it's basically a you-tiao which you can get from Chinatown for under 25c but you do you.In terms of ambience, the space is pretty small and cozy, and you sit very, very close to your neighbors. I didn't mind it as much because it's definitely quieter and less rowdy than Hanoi House (the chef's old haunt), but it can be a little too loud to hear yourself think if you have the poor luck of sitting next to a particularly rant-y fellow diner...Anyhow, definitely a place I will return to and recommend to friends!

Title: A Hip but Lackluster Experience at the Freehold Hotel's 18th Floor

I recently attended a school happy hour at a restaurant perched on the 18th floor of the Freehold Hotel, known for its tropical and sophisticated ambiance. While some might find this theme current and stylish, personally, it felt somewhat pretentious, perhaps indicating that I'm not quite the target demographic.

The venue is well-suited for group gatherings, offering a variety of seating arrangements and dual bar areas. Beware, though, as visibility can be quite poor, making it challenging to spot your companions. Those seeking breathtaking city views may be disappointed; the rooftop vista is modest and not conducive to the skyline photography aficionados.

The hosting service was relaxed; however, the general staff attitude carried a sense of apathy that was off-putting. I sampled an average naan-type appetizer, which was unremarkable in both flavor and presentation.

In sum, the restaurant has the makings of a fantastic social spot but falls short on delivery. It should not be written off entirely, but for now, it's not living up to its full potential.

Title: "Fancy Facade, Mediocre Fare"

Upon first glance, the restaurant exudes an air of elegance, with a roof design that lures you in to peruse the menu. Expectations of grandeur, nurtured by the exterior, are somewhat deflated upon entering—a standard Chinese restaurant ambiance prevails.

The staff, comprising middle-aged male waiters donned in attire reminiscent of my boyfriend's casual wardrobe, presented a menu promising high-end Chinese cuisine. Yet, the reality was disappointingly ordinary, not living up to the creative descriptions.

We indulged in the Wagyu Beef with Papaya—a novel combination that offered a balanced taste without overpowering the meat. Regrettably, the dish fell short on quantity and the beef itself was on the dry side. The Stir Fried Vegetables in Black Truffle Oil were the highlight with their robust flavor, though the dish became excessively salty by meal's end, especially when paired with the insufficient rice serving.

Priced between $20-$30 per dish, the cost was steep given the diminutive portions and the unremarkable taste experience. While it was interesting to try something new, the price-quality ratio makes a return visit unlikely.
Good slice of pizza when tipsy and need a slice. They were quite busy for the average Tuesday night. No complaints here!

I have been here 3 times in the last 2 years.  We love coming here to meet up with our friends from NJ and Long Island and this is the 2nd year in a row we came for St. Patrick's Day. We started at a table and as our group grew to 11 we moved to the bar and high tops area so we could chat easier.  Service was great.  Food is good pub food.  My friends had burgers,  nachos,  quesadillas,  pretzels,  and wings and all were good.  Ice cold beers served with a smile is what it's all about. There are lots of TVs to watch sports and it's a good sized bar for Manhattan. The ventilation by the bathrooms could be better because as the day goes on the smell becomes a bit intense.

Not what I remember. Maybe it has to do with the fact that it was 3 am after a night in the club but always remember it being better. Food was good but not worth the wait in this tourist trap. It's very small inside. Best part was the pork fried rice.

Title: A Hidden Gem in Ktown: The Maze

If you're prowling through Ktown for a late-night haunt, The Maze is a must-try spot for drinks and bites. Nestled away from the bustling streets, this cool, dimly-lit venue comes with an element of surprise – an elevator entry that sets the tone for an exclusive experience. Greeted warmly by the host upon arrival, we felt quite special — just remember to carry your ID to avoid any hiccups.

Perched at the bar, my boyfriend and I delved into the cocktail menu, each sip better than the last. We paired our drinks with their calamari, and it didn't disappoint. Lightly battered, impeccably fried, and served with a tantalizing dipping sauce, it was the highlight of our night. A fresh squeeze of lemon added that extra zing, elevating the flavors even further. The Maze is your go-to for a relaxed yet sophisticated late-night outing.

Title: A Pizza Haven in the Heart of Soho

If you're hunting for a trustworthy pizza spot in Soho, this restaurant should be at the top of your list. Thanks to my friend's foresight, we dodged the queues with a 6:30pm reservation on a recent Monday evening.

Our meal kicked off with the Italian wedding soup, which was rather underseasoned for my taste—a little more salt and pepper would go a long way. The half Funghi pizza was a surprise, generously blanketed in arugula, which gave a peppery contrast to the earthy mushrooms. The half Supreme pizza did not disappoint and lived up to its reputation as a crowd-pleaser.

The black and white tagliatelle, a seafood lover's dream, was a true standout with its mix of mussels, clams, shrimp, and calamari, all enrobed in a delicate sauce. Definitely a dish I'd come back for. Then came the Lasagna for 2, a hearty and classic choice that delivered on the comforting promise of meat and pasta.

Dessert was a playful bread pudding paired with a bourbon gelato that was simply "fire." Though, a slightly more indulgent, soggier bread would have been the cherry on top.

Service was prompt and attentive throughout our meal, complementing the restaurant's cozy, dimly lit ambiance. Whether you're a pizza aficionado or just in for a diverse Italian feast, this spot is worth the reservation.

Title: A Cozy Delight at ON

My dining experience at ON exceeded all expectations on a chilly Sunday evening. Not only was the food exceptional but the service was equally commendable. My companion and I began with the octopus appetizer, which left us wanting more. The real star of the night, however, was the mushroom bulgogi pot – a comforting blend of flavors that was the perfect portion for the two of us. It was served with complimentary mushroom rice that complemented the dish flawlessly.

The ambiance of ON added to the meal's enjoyment, with attentive service that truly enhanced our dining experience. Our server took the time to prepare the rice and hot pot at our table, providing a detailed walkthrough of the process, which was as informative as it was engaging. Her proactive advice to steer us away from the raw lobster appetizer, perceiving it was not to our taste, exemplified the thoughtful service ON is clearly known for.

In summary, ON is a restaurant that doesn't just feed the stomach but also warms the heart with its excellent food and service. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a meal that is both satisfying and served with care.

Title: A Day of Culinary Delight at an NYC Gem

Review:

My fiancé and I had the serendipitous pleasure of dining at this hidden jewel in NYC—twice in one day, no less! The first visit was a breeze, with no wait at 11:30 am on a Saturday, but for dinner, we braced ourselves for a 50-minute anticipation that was more than rewarded.

As a dry pot aficionado, having savored its delights in Beijing, I can attest that this establishment rivals, if not surpasses, those experiences. The beauty lies in the customization; our lunch and dinner pots were entirely unique concoctions.

We boldly chose the 'spicy' level, a delightful third tier of heat that struck a balance between sinus-clearing and flavorful. Our chosen ingredients, like the moist chicken breast and a variety of vegetables including the crunchy lotus root and succulent shiitake mushrooms, melded harmoniously. The thinly sliced pork belly was the only mild disappointment, offering less flavor than expected. However, the addition of purple rice was a revelation—chewy, subtly sweet with a surprising hint of fruit, complete with a solitary date.

Each meal was a reasonable ~$30, leaving us satisfyingly full. This place is a definitive must-return for us. Whether you're a dry pot veteran or eager to try something new, do yourself a favor and visit—you won't regret it.

Title: A Feast for the Eyes at Brunch

I recently visited this restaurant for brunch, and I must commend their stunning presentations and the variety of side dishes, certainly deserving of 4 stars. The aesthetics of the meals, particularly the tuna tataki, were impressive, though I found the dish itself lacked the punch of flavor I anticipated. Perhaps the high expectations, borne from eagerness to dine here, played a part in that.

On the service front, it was a mixed experience. Initially, the staff was pleasant and accommodating. However, as closing time approached, their frequent check-ins made it clear they were ready for us to leave, which was a little uncomfortable, especially while catching up with a friend for the first time.

While I understand the staff's perspective and the importance of respecting operating hours, I would recommend to future patrons to plan for an earlier visit to avoid feeling rushed.

Despite the slight letdown in taste and the urging towards the end, the sheer beauty of the dishes beckons me to return. I'm intrigued to see if the hake fish can live up to the level of flavor I'm seeking. So, I look forward to giving this place another chance to wow my palate as much as it has my eyes.

Title: A Celebration with Hits and Misses

My recent experience at this establishment offered a mix of delight and disappointment. On a positive note, the service was nothing short of excellent. Attentive and detail-oriented, the staff ensured our special occasion was marked with a complimentary slice of sumptuous chocolate lava cake, complete with Haagen-Dazs-style ice cream and fresh raspberries—a truly memorable touch.

The Bone-in Ribeye, ordered medium, was executed with precision, tender yet could have benefitted from a tad more seasoning. A standout side dish was the Garlic Mashed Potatoes, which was simply divine. Paired with the Whipped House Butter, it was a reminder that sometimes, side dishes can steal the show.

Unfortunately, not all dishes rose to the occasion. The Broiled Shrimp appetizer lacked any real flavor, presenting as tough and chewy, while the Shrimp Scampi was a letdown—devoid of seasoning and wine sauce, it barely passed as palatable. The Lamb Chops, too, were under-seasoned but somewhat redeemed by a vibrant Mint Jelly.

The Lobster Mac and Cheese boasted a generous portion of lobster yet suffered from the same seasoning issue, and a lackluster breadcrumb topping only compounded the dish's mediocrity. Similarly, the Creamed Spinach was a miss, tasting of unseasoned raw onions and bearing the unfortunate texture of frozen produce.

A highlight of the meal was the Pineapple Hennessy cocktail, which was exceptionally crafted and beautifully served with a dried pineapple. The wine selection, including a Lisa Vanderpump Rosé and a New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc, offered a pleasurable diversion, with the latter taking precedence in quality.

In summary, while the location is ideal and the service impeccable, the inconsistency in the cuisine makes it difficult to recommend this steakhouse. New York City is brimming with competitors that promise both exceptional service and delectable fare, leaving this venue in need of a culinary reassessment.

Smack in the middle of Greenwich village is an Italian joint that will really impress you.  For the food?  Of course.The eclectic location, very cool.  The ambiance, well that probably cinches it.  We walked in the other day after having walked over half a mile in the neighborhood just checking things out.   We finally ran into our lunch destination, Olio.  I had heard of it and was looking forward to the carbonara.The place was a little busy so we cheated, we sat at the bar.   It paid off immediately as the bartender got our drinks, and helped with our food order right away.  The complimentary appetizer came out fast.  tasty olives and some of the best hearty bread I have had in a while.  The tomato soup came out next, and I think I could have just ate that and been happy.But then came out the meals.  My Pasta Carbonara was even better than I could have imagined.  I broke the egg yoke sitting on top and ran it throughout the pasta.  It was a joy to say the least.   In New York I rarely repeat, But I WILL hit Olio again.  So may tasty option on that menu.

Years ago, Num Pang Kitchen's sandwiches didn't quite capture my culinary heart, despite their creativity. However, their fame for the elusive pork belly sandwich remained a whisper in the food circles, one I hadn't managed to experience until recently. Rediscovering Num Pang in the bustling Hudson Eats at Brookfield Place, I seized my chance and indulged in the much-acclaimed "Five-spice glazed pork belly" sandwich.

To say that the sandwich was a revelation would be an understatement. It harmonized a cacophony of flavors: the sweet and savory glaze of the pork belly, perfectly complemented by the aromatic five-spice, the acidity and satisfying crunch of pickled carrots, and the unique sweetness of Asian pear slices, all tied together with fresh cilantro. The bread was a textural marvel, crispy on the outside and pillowy soft within.

This sandwich has not only reignited my interest in Num Pang but also left me craving more. I'm torn between returning for another pork belly delight or venturing into new territory with the tempting peppercorn catfish sandwich. Either way, Num Pang has finally won me over.

Title: A Gastronomic Delight Worth Every Penny

My visit to this restaurant was nothing short of amazing, both in terms of food quality and service. We opted for the set pre fixe Menu #2, which, though on the pricier side, proved to be an excellent value considering the abundance and variety of dishes provided.

The flexibility of the menu was particularly appreciated, as we were able to accommodate the dietary preference of a pescatarian in our group without any additional cost. The staff, especially our waitress, were commendable for their attentiveness and helpfulness in navigating the menu options.

Standout dishes from our feast included the succulent edamame dumplings, the flavorful pork loin noodles, a delightful peking duck salad, and the crispy spring rolls. To conclude the meal, the dessert was a highlight and solidified the dining experience as exceptional.

In all, the restaurant delivers a top-notch dining experience, ideal for those willing to indulge in a culinary adventure that is sure to satisfy.

Title: Quaint Vegetarian Fare with Room for Improvement

I stumbled upon this vegetarian nook during a post-lunchtime lull on a Saturday afternoon. Despite the misleading 'Chicken' in the menu, all items are plant-based. The ambiance has an untouched, vintage charm, though it may benefit from some sprucing up.

Seated immediately, we were greeted with hot tea— a delightful start. The pan-fried dumplings, although on the oilier side, were sizeable and savory, especially when dunked in the accompanying sauce. However, the notion of 'healthy' took a back seat. Dumpling enthusiasts would appreciate the chewy texture and taste.

The Szechuan 'Chicken', a mock meat creation with mushrooms, was less impressive. Absence of the expected side of rice aside, the dish was subpar in both the promised Szechuan zest and healthfulness, leaning heavily on oil and soy. At nearly $18, it was a letdown. For those considering a visit, my advice is to focus on the dumplings, which seem to be the highlight of this spot—a boon for vegetarians craving a twist on the classic.

An okay hotpot place on saint marks. We came in on a thursday night - a party of 2. Hostess asked is if we minded sharing a table and we asked how long the wait would be. She said 45 mins so we agreed to share a table. Went down to the basement where there were many empty tables- I guess they were saving for larger groups? Due to the layout of the restaurant, it was a bit awkward sharing a table. We were sat in a booth and it was hard to order and eating w strangers so closely can be a tad bit awkward.I got the pork bone broth which was kinda flavorless and the texture of the fatty beef was very stringy, and cut into very small pieces.The drinks were good! I loved the watermelon Juice. It was so refreshing. Sauce bar had a great variety of sauces but some of them were empty and no one refilled.

Talk about the perfect date night restaurant from start to finish! Tarallucci in the East Village was perfection to the max. It would be really stretching to find fault with anything from our dinner.As per usual, we set out to go to one place, after a two hour search on Yelp, only to make the fast switch as we exited the subway. (After 15 years of marriage, it works.) We got to Tarallucci, on the early side, as we had a movie to catch around the corner. What a beautiful and quaint space. With the windows surrounding the front and dining room, it makes the small space seem specious and inviting. It's beautifully decorated, kind of cozy meets modern with an upscale twist, without being overstated or overdone.The host, who was also one of the owners, greeted us with enormous friendliness and made us feel very welcome. Of course, I started with a dozen oysters, which were just perfect. Well shucked. Great brine. Not too big or small. They hit the spot. I should also mention that they had me with the disco music playing, which clearly put the bartender in a good mood, as well as those seated who found it hard not to sway a bit from time to time. Everything on the menu looked amazing. But, given that we were on a time crunch to catch a movie, I ordered the Polipo: Charred Spanish  octopus, potatoes, kale, cherry tomatoes, and paprika aioli. Note to Upstate: THIS is how you cook and serve the perfect charred octopus. Jayson had the pan-seared scallops butternut squash purée , green apple, soppressata, pepitas.He also had the broccoli soufflé, pecorino fondue, with crispy bread, while I had the butter roasted cauliflower, bagna càuda sauce.This was a flawless meal. Seriously. It was off the charts good.Jayson, who loves scallops, but can sometimes be disappointed, sawt he eyes roll back in his head as he savored each bite. I loved the buttery sauce on the broccoli. I wish they'd served that with the cauliflower. I'm not much into cold sauces with warm vegetables. But given the excellence of the entire meal, it didn't even register. (I just used the buttery sauce from Jayson's broccoli. LOL.)This is definitely on our must repeat list. It was just amazing. You can't go wrong here.

Tucked away in the bustling Chelsea Market, this gem serves up the best tacos I've had the pleasure of tasting. Ordering is streamlined: simply pay at the cashier, present your ticket to the culinary team, and in no time, you’re handed a plate of perfection. With a variety of salsas to customize your tacos, you're spoilt for choice.

I indulged in both Carne Asada and Adobada tacos, with the latter stealing the show with its rich, savory flavors. Topped generously with onion, cilantro, and guacamole, every bite is a fiesta in your mouth. Be warned—patience is a virtue here as the queue can be daunting, but the reward is worth every minute.

Seating is communal, capturing the vibrant market atmosphere (grab a spot if you can!), and there's a $5 card minimum to note. As for me, I'm already planning my next visit to Happy Fiesta—those tacos are calling my name.

My favorite restaurant in NYC! This place serves some seriously good Korean food, and some of the best banchan (side dishes) I've ever had. Very friendly staff, high quality dishes, great banchan and the perfect ambiance makes this place a must-try in K-Town. I always look forward to the banchan that is served when dining at a Korean restaurant, and this place has some great banchan. You're not just getting your typical low quality dishes, but you're getting a lot of  banchan that is typically not served in restaurants. Some of my favorites were the braised pork + egg and the sweet shrimp. I couldn't tell what the rest were but they were good! I really could have a whole meal with nothing but rice and their banchan. Don't forget to ask for your free refills!On to the entrees, they're superb. We ordered the fire-grilled pork, Korean style pancakes, and the seafood japchae. If I were to recommend one I'd say the pancake - it's tasty and will fill you up for a good price. Each dish here is of such high quality and there are so many choices to choose from here. Prices were pretty fair considering the fact that you also get unlimited banchan.Also huge shoutout to the staff. The staff here is very warm and welcoming, and were always refilling waters or bringing more banchan. That, along with the restaurant's presentation and the overall vibe made it a perfect choice for a dinner out.Overall, Her Name is Han gets my vote for best restaurant in K-Town. If you're craving Korean food, I'd recommend this place over any others in Koreatown.

Thursday mid morning before Easter, this place was packed !Three of us were in serious need of some brunch, and this spot was nearby. Around 11am, it was amazing how tight it was in this restaurant. Even staff had a time squeezing between the tables. I went with eggs benny - $22. It was ok. Instead of an English muffin, it was on top of a brioche type hamburger bun. I missed the muffin taste and texture. Egg had playoff porn. Hollandaise sauce was light on flavor, and I could have used just a little more. Served with a side of potatoes. Service was good. Return ? Probably not.

Title: Slurp-tastic Noodle Heaven!

If you're a noodle aficionado, look no further than this gem! With an impressive selection of over 25 hand-shaved noodle dishes, choosing just one might be your toughest decision. My husband and I devoured the Spicy and Tingly beef noodles – a generously sized dish that's perfect for sharing as a hearty snack. Every bite of the noodles, perfectly balanced between chewy and soft, presented a flavor dance complemented by the sublime, melt-in-your-mouth beef. We opted for the regular spicy level, which offered a delightful slow burn, sneaking up on us enjoyably towards the end of our meal. 

No need to splurge on drinks – there's complimentary water on hand. The seating policy is first-order-first-sit, so timing is everything for the best spots. But with noodles this good, you'll forget all about the wait. Do your taste buds a favor and give this place a try!

I visited this charming little restaurant on Valentine's Day with a Groupon in hand, expecting it to be a quiet evening. To my surprise, it was bustling with a 20-25 minute wait. The cozy ambiance made the wait more comfortable, and the complimentary glass of champagne offered while in line was a delightful touch.

Once seated, I found the dinner to be delicious without being overpowered by noise—a perfect balance. The chicken doused in a succulent wine sauce was memorable, although the steak was just average. The experience was enhanced by the attentive and swift service by the friendly staff.

Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed my visit and am keen to return, perhaps with a small group of friends to indulge in their wine tasting event, reasonably priced at $25 per person. This spot is a definite gem worth revisiting.

An instant neighborhood favorite. Staff is very friendly and food is great. So far I've only gone twice, but everything has been wonderful both times. The pierogi is so soft and flavorful. I also tried the daily dessert today (cherry turnover) and that was yummy. And the price cannot be beat. It's basically a cheap and delicious homemade meal.

Joe's Pizza is an iconic stop for anyone craving authentic NY-style pizza in Manhattan. The experience is unparalleled, especially when you savor a slice fresh out of the oven. The harmonious blend of oozy cheese and rich tomato sauce will convince you that Joe's truly serves the best pizza in town. A must-visit for both locals and tourists alike.

Title: A Late-Night Culinary Gem in Times Square

Last night, my experience at this buzzing spot near Times Square was nothing short of spectacular, making it a must-visit for both date nights and family outings. Our late 10:30 pm reservation turned into a delightful evening that cruised past midnight to the lively rhythm of a Cuban live band adding an authentic vibe to the already electric ambience.

The star of the menu has to be the chicharrón de pollo - a generous bucket of succulent, fall-off-the-bone fried chicken served with an array of dipping sauces that elevate the flavors to new heights. Do not miss out on this mouthwatering delight!

We also indulged in the queso with shredded beef which pairs perfectly with the provided bread, though it's best enjoyed quickly before the cheese cools. To round out our meal, we savored the generously sized empanadas, each stuffed with either chicken, ground beef, or a tasty veggie mixture - the trio making for a satisfyingly complete meal.

And the mojitos? Simply divine. Robust and skillfully crafted, the guava and passion fruit variations are particularly exquisite. Strong and flavorful, they're the perfect cap to a joyous dining adventure.

In summary, for fantastic food that keeps up with the city that never sleeps and an atmosphere that beckons you to stay a little longer, this place is truly a winner.

Let's call this a positive two star review. I mean I'd probably go 2.5 if Yelp allowed it (get on that already!). You see, nothing horrible happened at Crompton Ale House to warrant the low score, but then again, nothing happened to warrant anything higher. An unfortunate feeling to have after my friend's B-Day dinner. Let's get into it.Well, I suppose there are a few small positives that took place. Though, the only true thumbs up I can safely muster would be the ambiance (and maybe the sweet potato fries). Besides Crompton being a run of the mill restaurant/bar of Manhattan, I did enjoy the wall of old books, cogs, and vintage steering wheels making it feel like we were dining in some fantastical library. But from my writings, the aesthetics usually mean the least in respect to the review.What matters most should be food and service, though these were both significantly forgettable. When I first got there, my attempts to grab a drink from the bar were rather difficult, especially when the total count of bartenders was basically one (or none). It at least gave me an opportunity to peruse the beer menu which (I don't want to sound beer snobbish, but probably will) wasn't anything special. They did have their own Crompton Ale and a Crompton Special Brew so I put that in my back pocket as a choice, but before deciding, I noticed a spot on the menu that said "Ask your server about our rotating beers." I figured this might result in a unique selection or something more locally craft. Instead, once finally grabbing the bartender, it led to a confused glance/statement when I asked. I reworded my question not using "rotating" (which seemed to be what threw him for a loop) and was then told that Crompton Special Brew (a lager) was what they had...okay. So a misleading menu statement and a less than stellar staff member started things off on the wrong foot.What did I drink? That Crompton Ale which was honestly meh (a great word to describe it). Stated as a red ale it had no malty flavor and didn't rouse my palette in any way. Even if he accidentally had given me the lager, it was still a boring brew that could easily have been mistaken for a Budweiser. My second round was a safer bet via Breckenridge Vanilla Porter, an actual solid beer available on tap.Beyond the suds, the food didn't do much for my liking. The menu seemed promising from app and sandwich choices, though I chose their 26th St. Burger (which consisted of a Pat La Frieda blend patty topped with swiss cheese, mushrooms, onion confit and barbeque sauce) for my dinner. It sounded better than it tasted. I mean, you can throw around the La Frieda name, but when the meat has a few hard, possibly bony, pieces in it, I question the quality. The shrooms, onions, and Swiss assisted in creating some resemblance of enjoyment, but halfway through the burger I was basically eating it more out of hunger than for flavor. The only taste I had was a bad one left in my mouth by the end of this whole dining session. Overall, I guess this Crompton Ale House review isn't so positively-based (whoops). Starting things off on a negative note at the bar led to more of the same once we sat (might I add our waitress seemed like her working here was a punishment). Maybe their actual cocktails and appetizers and other food factors are better, but from this experience, I just don't see a need to return to figure that out. I'll take my money elsewhere in the city with better results from start to finish. I'm positive about that.

Absolutely delicious spin on the classic Mac and cheese recipe! S'MAC is definitely a place to check out if you are in the East Village area. After contemplating for 20 minutes on what to get I finally settled for the buffalo mac and cheese. It came with pieces of chicken, buffalo sauce, blue cheese, and bread crumbs. It was a perfect size to share or have on your own! I will definitely be coming back if I'm in the NYC area :)

Title: A New Gem with Flawless Flavors and Service

My experience at this newly opened restaurant was absolutely amazing, striking a rare balance between impeccable service and culinary excellence even within the first few days of opening. From the outset, the host and waitress set the tone with their friendly and attentive demeanor.

Although faced with a two-hour wait, a detour to the bar downstairs proved to be serendipitous. The drinks were crafted to delight, and the carne con queso fries were nothing short of addictive, convincing us to stay put for our reservation. The fries were a tantalizing prelude to the impressive meal that awaited us upstairs.

Surprisingly, the bone marrow, which I'm typically hesitant to try, was a revelation - perfectly cooked, paired with light and fluffy toast, and a sauce that complemented it beautifully. The duck hash was another standout, crisped to perfection, brimming with flavor, and elevated by a gravy that was rich and savory, with a fried egg that tied it all together masterfully.

The double cheeseburger, a classic choice, was executed flawlessly. It wasn't overly salty, as I often fear with burgers; instead, it was juicy and flavorful. I opted for added bacon and egg, and while the bacon was satisfactory, it was the burger itself that held my affections.

In summary, this restaurant is an absolute must-visit for any food enthusiast looking for a flawless dining experience. Whether you're a regular patron of high-end eateries or merely seeking a satisfying meal, this establishment promises and delivers an unforgettable gastronomic journey.

I recently dined at a well-rated Italian restaurant, but the experience fell short of expectations. Upon arrival, the staff failed to greet us, and there was confusion about being seated, with the bartender expressing indifference. The service was inattentive, as our waitress left in the middle of taking our order to converse with another staff member.

Concerns for a guest with food allergies were mishandled. Despite assurances that certain dishes were safe, butter—a stated allergen—was included in the sauce, leading to unnecessary back-and-forth to secure an appropriate meal. The restaurant’s rigidity in modifying dishes aggravated the situation.

The food quality did not salvage the visit; the raviolis with salmon were mediocre and overpriced, while the lasagna was unremarkable, comparable to less expensive establishments. Although they offer gluten-free pasta, their inability to accommodate simple modifications for allergy requirements was disappointing.

I would not recommend this restaurant, particularly for those with dietary restrictions, due to the lackluster service and food quality that does not justify the pricing.

Title: Decent Spot with Some Quirks - A Mixed Bag Rooftop Experience

I recently visited a rooftop restaurant that was fairly average in many respects. The space is on the smaller side and quickly becomes packed even in the early evening hours around 6 to 7 PM. One of the highlights includes a complimentary coat check, which is a thoughtful and mandatory service that's much appreciated.

The staff members were amiable, contributing positively to the experience. As for the view, it's okay, but it doesn't stand out when compared to other rooftop venues. I tried the Perfect Pear cocktail; while it was enjoyable, I found it to be overly sweet. Moreover, the alcohol content didn't quite match the $16 price tag—I expected a more generous pour, especially based on what I've received at similar establishments.

The restaurant's eagerness to maximize space utilization was notable, to the point of feeling cramped. It was slightly off-putting to be asked to move to accommodate a private party setup, particularly given that several other events were occurring simultaneously. It felt disorganized and left me with the impression that the experience could be more guest-focused. Overall, this rooftop has the potential but needs to balance atmosphere and service to truly shine.

My dining experience was exceptional. The pork, kidney, and liver congee was a massive bowl of satisfying flavors, while my boyfriend's BBQ pork rice crepe had a generous portion size. The side of mantou with condensed milk was a delightful contrast of hot, crispy exterior and sweet, gooey dip. The curry fish balls were a highlight, offering a perfect balance of spice and fish - far from the filler-heavy versions. The HK milk tea impressed with its smoothness and authenticity, which brought back memories of my time studying in Hong Kong. At an affordable $22.75 for the entire meal, I would wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to anyone seeking a taste of true Hong Kong cuisine.

Title: A Delicious Surprise for the Taste Buds

I recently visited a new gem of a restaurant on a leisurely Sunday afternoon with a friend and was pleasantly surprised by the high-quality fare offered at such reasonable prices. This spot operates on a credit card-only basis, which was a minor detail to note before diving into their delightful menu.

The ordering process was straightforward – make your selections at the counter, and your food is brought to your table, a convenience I appreciated. The interior boasts a sizable bar area complete with a bartender, an excellent spot for enjoying their Happy Hour from Monday to Friday between 3-7pm.

As a vegetarian, I was thrilled by the variety of options available. We began with their nachos – a generous appetizer that set the stage for the main event. We both indulged in the #2 combo, which featured three generously filled tacos plus a side. My choice included the truffle mushroom, vegan chorizo, and short rib tacos, all of which were bursting with flavor, but the truffle mushroom was a standout, offering a rich and savory experience. Accompanying my tacos was a side of Mexican street corn, served off the cob—a thoughtful touch for ease of eating.

My friend raved about the fish taco, which seemed to be just as impressive as the rest of the offerings. The guacamole, a staple for any Mexican-inspired meal, did not disappoint either. It was apparent the portions served were above average, leaving us satisfied and content.

In all, this restaurant's prime location makes it an ideal spot for a quick, delicious lunch with coworkers, and I am confident in its success. I wholeheartedly recommend this place and eagerly anticipate my next visit.

Cute cozy-ish (ish because its actually quite spacious inside) greek spot in east villageWe tried:- poikilia 6/10: aka the three dips. I really liked the fish one but i prefer a thinner/lighter tzatziki and the eggplant one was very bland- afrata keftedakia 7/10: meatballs were decent but were they really worth it..i dont know. It lacked a bit of flavor so i found myself combining forces with the dips above- moussaka 9/10: now this i really enjoyed. It was a solid portion and i could really taste the different ingredients- lamb chops 7/10: its not that they didn't taste good, it just wasn't great -- which is really what you should be aiming for if youre eating lamb chops outside. I had read somewhere that the lamb here was really delicious so we were disappointed with the lack of flavor (and also had asked for rare but got more of a medium rare) All in all everything was slightly pricier than i wouldve liked and food was a little bland all around.

Title: A Brunch to Remember at Sarabeth's

Sarabeth's, with locations on the Upper East Side and near Central Park, consistently delivers an exemplary brunch experience, true to its esteemed reputation in the New York dining scene. The fare, atmosphere, and service are mirror images in both locations, ensuring that the Sarabeth's experience is uniform, no matter where you dine.

The Four Flower Juice is a refreshing preamble to the main course, and the green onion and cream cheese omelette is a testament to the kitchen's ability to elevate simple dishes to heavenly heights. Their eggs are famously fluffy — indulging in them feels like biting into a cloud.

The beauty of Sarabeth's lies in its simplicity. It shuns complexity for quality, and that's evident in every bite. Despite its popularity, which can draw a mix of patrons — including the stereotypical Upper East Side clientele — the restaurant remains inviting to all.

Service is attentive and impeccable, contributing to an overall delightful dining experience. Be warned, though: securing a weekend reservation can be a challenge. But take it from a regular — plan ahead. The effort to enjoy a lazy Sunday brunch at Sarabeth's is more than worth it.

I went on a weekend for dinner. The place was very slow, so that made me nervous. However, the servers come immediately when you ring a doorbell at your table, they had a good variety of foods, and it was decently priced. I was very satisfied with the vegetarian options, since often there aren't many options at a Korean bbq. But the hot stone tofu bibimbap was excellent! I wish I had some leftovers.

So excited to have this in the neighborhood as there aren't any other spots like this right around here. The fish is really fresh, which is obviously a deal breaker. The are one of the only places that have their fish options pre-marinated/ already mixed with the sauces, rather than you choosing which sauce you want. All of their mix combos are really good, so no complaint on not picking my soy sauce and what not (note they have soy sauce packets to go)!There are a few tables and a window bar. A good amount of seating for the small space they have. Very clean, too. A friend and I split the big kahuna and the blazing tuna. They are noted on the menu that they have a little spice to them, and it's the perfect kick of spice! The rice was so fluffy and perfect. I love when there are a lot of toppings and they don't disappoint. Also love that marinated kale is an option for a base... haven't seen that anywhere else!Big Kahuna: Tuna & Salmon Classic Poke, Yuzu Salmon Poke, Firecracker Tuna, Crab Salad, Pickled Ginger, Seaweed Salad, Wonton Crisps..... such a variety of different fish,, def for the fish lover!! Seaweed salad was really good add on. Blazing Tuna: Firecracker Poke, Avocado, Jalapeño, Cucumber, Bean Sprouts, Tempura Flakes, Onion Crisps.... Really good, next time would do without the jalapeno because too much spice for me!Will definitely be back, especially given that it's so close to work.

Title: A Bittersweet Dining Experience

My anticipation for the celebrated Fried Mushrooms was met with disappointment upon learning that they were unavailable on my Sunday evening visit. The Mushroom Pizza and Upland Cippino, while intriguing, leaned towards the saltier side, detracting from their potential.

However, not all was lost. The Fried Duck Wings were exceptional, and the complimentary Brioche Bread was a delightful touch. The Bucatini Cacio E Pepe impressed with its creamy, peppery sauce, perfectly capturing the essence of the dish. Accompanying the meal were the Roasted Beets and Carrots, served in a generous portion that did not disappoint.

The dessert selection, though limited, was quite pleasing. The Mixed Berry Sorbet was a refreshing palate cleanser, while the warm Anjou Pear Crisp, topped with deliciously crunchy cinnamon oats, provided a comforting end to the meal.

The restaurant's ambiance exuded romance and intimacy, which complemented the overall experience. Service flowed seamlessly throughout the evening, and the well-curated wine list was a notable highlight.

In conclusion, despite the initial setback with the Fried Mushrooms and a couple of overly salty dishes, the meal was redeemed by other delectable offerings, and the atmosphere and service were noteworthy.

Really an excellent breakfast. Starting with a tasty cup of coffee is great, and the espresso drink she had was also delicious.We asked the server for some help regarding the chorizo and biscuit on the menu, or the special omlette. The biscuit was the winner... And it was a winner. To be healthy, we also got the kale hash. (it's not really super healthy). It was lacking for a bit, then we found the buried goat cheese that really changed the plate.Although a hike, this is definitely a spot we will head back to soon.

I'd give this restaurant a solid 5-star rating. The steak sandwich was utterly delicious, and the French fries maintained their excellence even after delivery. I also sampled the kale salad and a dish with farro, feta, avocado, and onions. While both were prepared with quality ingredients and a tasty dressing, they fell just a tad short on excitement. Nonetheless, the overall experience has left me eager to explore more of their menu, with the steak sandwich already on my reorder list.

Last night's dining experience at this cozy spot was a delight, particularly for our party of eight. While space is snug, the necessity of reservations and pre-ordering the Kamayan feast ensures a personalized and efficient service. The meat lovers package chosen by my group, featuring succulent Filipino sausage, flavorful chicken adobo, and tender ribs, alongside perfectly garlicky rice, was a highlight. Generous portions meant we happily left with leftovers. The simple yet smart use of banana leaves for serving made cleanup a breeze. Capping the meal with the superb halo-halo, complete with delectable ube ice cream, was the perfect touch. This place is a must-visit for groups craving a hearty and authentic feast.

This place is a little hole in the wall. They have a couple tables inside but it really is for pick-up. We ordered shrimp with vegetables and chicken with vegetables.Glad we were able to find it. The food was amazing and fresh. Highly recommend it. Wish we were able to go to it again but didn't have time. Go check them out.

The pizza here is SO GOOD!!!!! I wasn't sure what to expect, because it's thick dough which is very not New York style. But let me tell you - it's different, and it's good!!! Not better lol. It's different and it's very very good!The dough is thick: it's soft and still crispy around the edges. The edges even extra crispy because of the cheese crust. Very salty and delicious. We got the classic, and the sauce was perfect in flavor and amount.They sell only one size. It's a rectangle shape which they cut into 4 pieces. It could feed 2 as a snack lol. But if you're hungry, def order your own tin. Prices vary 10-14 based on topping.Classic is 5

One of the best places to order fresh pork dumplings.  $4 for 8 dumplings is not a bad deal.  And I love getting them steamed.  I like the texture of them as you chew them and slide down your mouth. They are also stuffed generously.  When ever I am in the area or craving dumplings I will always think of this place and take a ride over here.  I never tried the noodle soups. But they look very good too.  The dumplings come out quickly.  Inside it's pretty clean and plenty of seats to dine in.  They r open till 11 pm. Some night I wish they were open later.  But it's ok because they are good the next day as well. Throw them in a pot with a little beef stock and a little soy sauce and let them steam up until they r ready to eat again.  The lady that took my order was really nice as well.   If ur in the area this is my go to dumpling spot.

Restaurant Review: Morimoto

Ambiance: Modern chic venue with a touch of elegance perfect for fancy dining experiences.

Cuisine: Iron Chef Morimoto showcases Japanese small plates that are as delightful on the palate as they are to the eye. The menu presents an array of sophisticated dishes such as broiled Spicy King Crab and a visually impressive toro tartare adorned with caviar and micro garnishes.

Dishes: The small plates are a gastronomic adventure. The Pork Gyoza, with its unconventional tomato, creme fraiche, and bacon filling, is a unique twist on a classic, though not a highlight for repeat orders. The Hot Stone Wagyu offers an interactive experience, though be ready to wrestle a bit with the meat sticking to the stone. A stand-out dish is the Yakitori Sasso Chicken, which is not just the most affordable entree but also an enjoyable and engaging dish that comes with crispy rice for a mix-and-match delight.

Desserts: The Shoga Choko brings a fiery presentation that captivates, while the Beri Kasu presents a delicate concoction that fears the touch of a fork, though both round off the meal pleasantly.

Value: Contrary to initial impressions, Morimoto offers a dining experience that won't necessarily break the bank. Opting for à la carte selections allows for a more controlled expenditure.

Overall: A gratifying escapade into Japanese cuisine with an innovative twist by a renowned chef. The experience exceeded expectations with promises of a return visit. Recommended for those seeking quality Japanese small plates in a stylish setting, with the advice to select dishes judiciously for a well-priced meal.

During a recent NYC hustle - from a busy day in the LES to a late-night Sheepshead Bay crab feast - my search for a vegan bakery treat at 1am was thwarted by closed doors citywide. The munchies led me to Max Brenner, an establishment I had lauded since its early 2000s glory days. Greeted by a chocolate shop flush with packaged goods and a confectioner's display to my right, my nostalgia was quickly replaced with disappointment: no chocolate mousse on a dessert menu at a temple of chocolate?

Reluctantly, I opted for an overly indulgent crêpe loaded with Nutella, caramel, churros, and butter popcorn. Post-dessert, guilt plagued me - not just for the dairy lapse after two vegan months but for the lackluster chocolate quality that paled in comparison to Brenner's storied past. My husband's lava cake fared no better in our late-night critique. 

Max Brenner seems to have lost touch with both its roots and the evolving tastes of its clientele. If I'm going to succumb to a treat next time, it'll be for chocolate that wows, and sadly, I'll likely be seeking it elsewhere.

Greek cuisine enthusiasts rejoice at the arrival of Uncle Gussy's food truck, and I am certainly no exception. My partner recently treated me to a meal from this culinary haven, and it was an experience worth relishing.

We indulged in the Hercules Combo and the Chicken Gyro Combo. The Hercules was a feast fit for the gods, generously portioned and paired with a fresh Greek salad, golden fries, aromatic yellow rice, succulent lamb, and perfectly seasoned chicken. 

Though I didn't sample the Chicken Gyro my partner ordered, our shared fries were a highlight. The balance of fresh oregano, salt, and cracked black pepper on the fries created an addictive crunch that still lingers in my memory. While the fries serving was modest, it did not detract from the overall satisfaction.

In summary, Uncle Gussy's delivers on both quantity and quality, and for Greek food aficionados, it's an unmissable delight on wheels.

Title: Unique Ambiance and Stellar Service at a Bank Vault Bistro

I recently visited a truly unique dining establishment, located within the confines of an actual bank vault, giving it a cool factor that's hard to match. While I only sampled the sliders from the happy hour menu, which were tasty albeit difficult to get wrong, the overall service and ambiance elevated the experience.

My companions had a lukewarm response to their meals, so I can't fully vouch for the food based on their "meh" impressions. But if you're not solely there for a culinary adventure, the restaurant has a lot to offer.

During happy hour, the bar area can get quite noisy, but if you're seeking a quieter atmosphere, there's a solution: simply request a table in the more tranquil dining room located towards the back.

As a spot for enjoying happy hour or hosting a work dinner, it's impressive. With this in mind, I'm giving this cool and service-oriented venue a solid four-star rating.

If paradise were made of chocolate, it would be named after this place! I arrived with only one intent – to indulge in an experience tailored for the cocoa bean enthusiast. Boasting an impressive 4,500+ Yelp reviews, my expectations were sky-high, and I was not disappointed.

Nestled into the bustling energy of a Saturday night, the wait was short considering the crowd, and the expansive interior meant I was soon seated comfortably upstairs. Prepare to be dazzled by their dessert menu; it's extensive and nothing short of spectacular. Everything a chocolate lover could dream of is beautifully presented and just waiting to be savored.

My selections for the evening were the '80s Milkshake and the Crystal Churros Fondue. The milkshake was a masterpiece – a visual and taste sensation that would make a chocoholic swoon. Served in a cup so adorable it nearly left with me, it was a concoction of milk chocolate ganache and vanilla, crowned with a scoop of vanilla ice cream encased in a crunchy chocolate shell. It boasted a purity of flavor that converted me from a childhood skeptic to a full-fledged chocolate shake devotee.

Accompanying the shake were the churros, fried to perfection and paired with a seductively smooth milk chocolate fondue alongside toffee and raspberry sauces. Each dip was a delight, with the toffee and milk chocolate being my personal favorites. This dessert could easily be shared, but on this occasion, my selfish side won.

Despite the bustling atmosphere, service remained attentive and efficient. The laid-back vibe is an alluring contrast to the serious business of chocolate indulgence happening at every table. By meal's end, I was as satiated as if I'd had a multi-course dinner.

Before leaving, the chocolate bar captivated my attention, where you can watch the magic happen, and the store offers treats to extend the euphoria at home. I wholeheartedly recommend a visit for those seeking an extraordinary chocolate experience. This spot is not just recommended; it's a must-visit! The praise is well-deserved – the chocolate here is nothing short of amazing.

Title: Cozy Spot with Warm Service but Over-Salted Fare

I recently visited a quaint eatery that pleasantly accommodates larger parties with ease. The service shone from the get-go with an inviting offering of warm bread and butter - a delightful prelude to our main courses.

I opted for the Oven Baked Mac and Cheese with Salmon, a dish that fell into the realm of mediocrity. It had an overly enthusiastic salt presence that overpowered the potential nuances of a "fairly fancy" mac and cheese. While the price point was reasonable, the dish's heavy-handedness in both salt and sauce weight proved too much, leaving room for improvement with a sharper cheese blend and a lighter touch.

The salmon accompanying the mac and cheese was of good quality, though it too suffered from the kitchen's heavy hand with salt. Presentation-wise, the dish was a feast for the eyes - so much so, I documented it with a photo.

However, the sizzle of the dish outlasted its welcome, remaining distractingly hot throughout our dining experience. The dilemma between waiting for a meal to cool and tediously blowing on each bite detracted from an otherwise enjoyable meal.

My ratings would be as follows:
- Price: 4/5
- Quality: 3/5
- Quantity: 4/5
- Service: 4/5
- Atmosphere: 4/5

In summary, a charming spot with a few tweaks needed in the kitchen to transform good to great.

Title: A Spicy Delight with Service to Match

I recently dined at a gem where not only the food but also the service truly shone. The staff was remarkable, brimming with politeness and attentiveness that enhanced the entire experience.

The culinary highlight was their soup dumplings, which struck the perfect balance between delicate and durable, enveloping a delicious broth. The spicy peanut butter wontons were a unique twist, marrying the creaminess of peanut butter with just the right amount of heat. As for the mapo tofu with fish, it was a clever combination that allowed me to savor two favorites in one dish.

However, the star of the show was undoubtedly the spicy chicken—its perfect crispy exterior and mouthwatering spiciness had an addictive quality that will keep me coming back for more.

Every bite was matched in quality by the attentive service; the wait staff ensured our glasses were never empty and our needs promptly met. As someone who works nearby, this spot has easily earned a place in my regular dining rotation.

I came here to celebrate my birthday with a group of friends after hearing buzz of a trendy Indian restaurant with a creative menu. The restaurant is two floors and has a cool modern vibe with interesting wall art. We were really impressed by the waitstaff; our waiter explained every item of the menu and was very attentive throughout the meal. We tried the chef's tasting menu ($62) with the wine pairing ($34). We were incredibly impressed with the spread. Standouts included the colonel tso's cauliflower (an Indian play on the Chinese general tso's chicken), and the thali spread which included butter chicken and a coconut chicken curry. We were surprised that we each got our own individual thali spread - there was SO much food, we left feeling very full and satisfied. The wines were lovely too, we had a white, two roses, and a red. Overall, we had a truly memorable experience. The environment was hip and fun for a big group, the service was excellent, and the food was a delicious unique taste on Indian cuisine.

I decided to go with the business lunch. The business lunch let's you pick two appetizers, one entree and one dessert. For my two starters I decided to go to the chef daily sushi set and the seared tuna. For the entree, I decided to get sashimi chirasi donburi and for the dessert I decided to go for their special chocolate which is not in the menuLet me start that the food was spectacular. The taste of every dish was outstanding. But their special chocolate is exquisite. I applaud the chef for making such a delicious masterpiece. My only complaint is that the server was more interesting in gossiping/flirting than actually working. While I was there, the server didn't give the exact change to another costumer and the server had to be call out. For me, the server forgot to serve me my drink. I understand that some days we might be a little off but if you are going to be flirting/ slacking off with the coworkers make sure to get the order. I made sure to let the server know so for him/her to step up for the rest of the day.

We walked our legs out to try and make it here before closing. Sorry to the workers! I use to work in retail so I understand "those customers" that walk in right before closing. Well we became those customers. Xian was highly recommended and after three hours of researching where to eat between a nice sit down dinner or casual dining, we had our hearts on the noodles here. They were nice enough to take our orders as long as we did take out. Majority of the items from the menu were no longer available, such as the lamb and beef, basically all of the menu but was able to walk away with at least one lamb item and the rest were pork. All the food were devoured within minutes. I don't know if we were really hungry or if the food was outstanding, but either way we enjoyed it. I preferred the dry noodles over the soup. Some say the spice level isn't there. The spiciness in the spicy cumin lamb was there. It's enough for me to want to reach for a glass of milk. I applaud those who think that's not even spicy at all. Very good chewy noodles and tender meat. Wanted to come back before we left the city. When it leaves a lingering impression, you know its good.

Title: A Carnivore's Delight Exceeds Expectations

Our group of four was eager for a meaty feast, and this restaurant did not disappoint. We indulged in a range of dishes including the legendary Lamb Chop, Prime Porterhouse for two, and a well-done Prime Rib King cut, complemented by oysters with baked crab, asparagus and Hollandaise sauce, hash brown, roasted market vegetables, and a delightful carrot cake to finish.

The complementary fresh vegetables and house-made bread set a welcoming tone for the meal. Both the lamb chop, with its subtly sweet sauce, and the simply seasoned porterhouse, were juicy and tender – a testament to the chefs' skill.

The Prime Rib, suggested by an accommodating waiter for a well-done preference, surprisingly retained its juiciness and tender texture, debunking the myth that well-done equals dry and tough. It was perfectly cooked, albeit not very steak-like, and generous enough in size to satisfy more than one diner.

Paired with a cocktail and a glass of red wine, the meal was an epicurean's delight. At around $100 per person, we left with satisfied palates and some leftovers. This experience not only filled our stomachs but also surpassed the renowned Peter Luger in quality, setting a new benchmark for steakhouse excellence.

Title: High Hopes Dashed at Balaboosta

Having harbored high expectations from my love for Taim, I ventured into Balaboosta, eager to experience the culinary prowess of its renowned chef. Unfortunately, my anticipation was met with disappointment. While the cafe exudes a charming ambience, perfect for a relaxing brunch with its light and airy feel, the experience was somewhat marred by our tucked-away seating which made attentive service a challenge.

The meal commenced with a green salad, a simple dish that was satisfactory yet unremarkable, even with the addition of pan-seared dorade— a decision that inflated the price by $9. The shakshuka, a brunch classic, also graced our table but failed to leave a lasting impression. It was akin to something I might easily prepare at home, lacking the culinary flair one might expect from such an establishment.

In light of the underwhelming food, I find myself unable to recommend Balaboosta. Despite its aesthetically pleasing setting, the overall experience was not compelling enough to warrant a return visit.

Title: Brunch Bliss with a Side of Patience

Walking out of the restaurant, I was filled with a sense of "no regrets." Recommended by a friend and buoyed by favorable Yelp reviews, my fiancée and I joined her for what turned out to be a fantastic brunch experience, despite a few hiccups.

Located in a picturesque spot, the restaurant exuded charm. We arrived during the Sunday brunch rush at 1 pm, but the welcoming hostess seated us without delay. Although friendly, our server's attentiveness didn't quite match the pace of our hunger. It took about 10 minutes before our drink orders were taken, and the overall service was leisurely, to put it kindly.

A minor oversight in service was the timing of the food. Rather than staggering the small plates and entrees, everything landed on our table simultaneously, which felt a tad overwhelming. Moreover, a simple lemonade order took its sweet time arriving.

As for the food, it was nothing short of exceptional. The chocolate pancake was a confectionery dream, its sweetness perfectly counterbalanced by savory bacon and buttered hash. It's the sort of dish that makes any service shortcomings fade into the background.

In sum, if efficiency were on the menu, this spot would be a solid five-star establishment. As things stand, it's a beautiful place with exceptional food that requires a touch more patience.

Title: A Delightful Experience with a Pricey Touch at Macchina

I recently joined a friend for their birthday celebration at Macchina, where the vibe was as effervescent as the drinks we enjoyed. The spotlight might be on their Instagram-famous burrata pizza, but I'll say upfront, the $24 tag felt steep for its size. Despite that, kudos to Macchina for turning it into a sensation.

The real culinary star, though, was the Cherry tomato pizza. I'm no tomato fan, but this pie won me over with its rich flavors. As for the snacks, the Mac n' Cheese balls were an absolute triumph — perfect munchies to accompany our lively drinks.

Speaking of libations, the Carburetor from the happy hour menu was a highlight. With its refreshing blend of rum, mint, lime, watermelon, and prosecco, it brought a Mojito to mind and was flawless on a warm July evening.

Service was impeccable, adding to the overall meal satisfaction. I'm already planning a return visit to dive deeper into Macchina's offerings. Despite the burrata pizza's price tag, the experience is a draw in itself and certainly warrants another round.

Title: A Dim Sum Delight Near Grand Central

After arriving in New York on an early lunch hunt for dim sum, we skipped the trek to Chinatown and found a gem not far from Grand Central. Despite the unavoidable wait in the cramped quarters typical of NYC, we spent a reasonable 30 minutes anticipating our feast.

The ordering process was a breeze - a checklist menu kept things moving in this bustling spot. We dove into an array of dim sum: succulent shrimp rolls, savory seafood shu mai, daring chicken feet, the comforting bite of steamed spare ribs, a mix of shrimp & pork shu mai, plump shrimp dumplings, hearty pork soup dumplings, and a side of fragrant fried rice to round out the meal.

Each dish was a hit except the pork soup dumplings which were let down by overly thick skins. However, every other item was spot-on, delivering the rich flavors we craved.

If you're near Times Square and yearn for quality dim sum without the lengthy commute, this restaurant is a must-visit. Just be ready for a short wait; it's well worth it for the delicious offerings that await.

Title: A Mac n' Cheese Haven Worth Every Visit

If indulging in Mac n' Cheese is your idea of culinary heaven, look no further. This place is a goldmine for variety, ensuring there's a dish for every palate. As a long-time fan, I can't recommend the Garden Lite enough. Elevating it with breadcrumbs and roasted veggies has become my go-to move.

Taking advantage of their online ordering for pick-up was a breeze, and the charming little poem that accompanied my meal added a delightful personal touch. It's these thoughtful details that transform a simple takeout experience into something quite special. If you haven't already, give them a try. You'll find yourself making excuses to go back!

So I came to this place many years ago (opened in 1999). I remember back then it was one of the vanguard of Korean restaurants starting to break out of their insular immigrant shell to join the ranks of other ethnic foods that had become actual dining destinations. The only problem was that despite all the accolades, when I went, it didn't taste good. I don't remember what I ate then but I remember leaving sorely disappointed and distrustful of all those who hyped these ethnic finds despite what I thought was a culinary failure. Fast forward to today and we were in the neighborhood and desperate for a light meal to tide us over until a dinner later that night. It was a completely different story and now the lines that went out the door seemed to all make sense to me. Although they serve food other than the eponymous mandoo - but why bother eating anything else? We tried 3: the steamed kimchee mandoo, the pan fried mandoo, and the mool mandoo. The kimchee one had the nice brightness of the kimchee to contrast the taste of the filling. The mandoo wrapper was thick enough to withstand the steaming giving it a nice chewy bite. But I found the taste of the filling to be a bit bland. The pan fried mandoo filling was very flavorful and the crispy fried wrapper gave the mandoo a nice crunchy texture. Usually the fried mandoo is my hands-down favorite, but I have to say that the mool mandoo was even better. First, the filling was very similar to the tasty filling in the fried mandoo but second, the wrapper was a thicker variety. This let it survive the boiling in water and retain a nice chewy texture. We were all very happy with our choices and in some way, this place was redeemed in my mind. Service was efficient and quick. Definitely a great place for a light meal.

Hands down one of the best poke spots I have tried in NYC. Not only are the ingredients fresh, they have a wide array of selections to choose from and toppings are unlimited!
