I usually build my own bowl with salmon, scallops (yes, they have scallops!), spicy salmon and/or shrimp, over a bed of kale noodles (say what!) and greens. I have never even heard of kale noodles, but they exist and complement the poke bowl pretty well. More importantly, it tastes pretty darn good. There's plenty of unlimited toppings and delicious sauces to top off your bowl, so make sure you add some weight to it!

Gotham Bar and Grill has long been on my list, and I picked it as the restaurant to take my husband to for Christmas dinner this year. Reservations were fairly easy to come by online, I had no difficulty in securing one for prime dinner hour on a Friday night. We came in half an hour late on this particular evening, I had called a little earlier to let them know and the staff were very accommodating. When we arrived, they seated us immediately at a corner table, and we enjoyed scanning the view of the room. The ambience here is elegant and beautiful in a classic old New York way. The dining tables have white table cloths on them, with a single candle and a vase. We decided to go with the three course menu, and started with oysters and stracciatella. These were good, but they were also uncooked and therefore hard to mess up. For main dishes, my husband had the porcelet (pork chop), while I had the lamb shoulder. We waited about 20 minutes after finishing our appetizers to get our mains. We fine dine a fair amount, but were a bit taken aback when our mains arrived and we saw how small they were. I immediately knew I wasn't going to be full, and flagged down our waitress to ask if there were any sides available (we hadn't seen any on the menu). Once she came over, I said I had seen another table that received a side of fries, and asked if they had any other sides. She said they didn't have any "official" sides, but that we could order the fries, which she said were cooked in beef fat, and amazing. The fries were served within 10 minutes of ordering. They were definitely good, and a nice addition to the small main dishes. Overall, our mains of pork and lamb were not bad. We had nothing to complain about, but they were unexceptional. After we'd finished our mains, we decided to further fill up on dessert. They had a dessert special that evening, an apple tarte tatin for two. The waitress recommended that we get in quickly to order this one, as they had a limited quantity of the dessert. Order it quickly we did. The server presented us first with the whole pie, just to look at it, and then whisked it away again to cut it in half, and put it on two plates, with a dollop of vanilla ice cream. The dessert was the highlight of the meal. The tarte tatin was perfectly crisp on the outside, with caramelized apple slices that were delicious with the vanilla ice cream. The service was very good. Overall, the two of us were glad to tick a classic New York restaurant off our list, but would not recommend dining here if you are looking for a mind-blowing dining experience.

Title: A Classic Gem Revisited

Sometimes the charm of an old school establishment outshines the rest, and this lovely little spot is a testament to that! With a lunch special that truly speaks for itself, I was treated to a delectable salmon paired with a Core de Rhône that complemented the dish flawlessly. The bread served alongside was fresh and set the stage for the meal.

Opting to dine alfresco, I was immersed in the tranquility of their stunning garden—a perfect backdrop for a serene meal. The water arrived perfectly chilled, paralleling the cool demeanor of our waiter, whose service was nothing short of excellent.

A simple request to substitute green salad for potato salad was accommodated without fuss, and the result was a meal that was not only delicious but also beautifully presented and generous in portion. The experience was thoroughly enjoyable, leaving my palate and soul satisfied.

It had been ages since my last visit when it was an Italian restaurant, but the evolution has been remarkable. This revisit has reignited my excitement, and I'm eager for my next visit to this charming spot.

I'm saying it - one of the best burgers in the city! We ordered from Nowon during quarantine and it was better than expected. The food arrived early, perfectly intact and still hot. We had the Nowon Double Cheeseburger and the Chopped Cheese Rice Cakes and wow. Not only were they both delicious but the burger was cooked perfectly. Do yourself a favor and order both of these. Thanks Nowon for such great food and service during lockdown!

Title: A Fair Deal at DiwaneKhaas, But Don't Set Your Hopes Too High

I recently decided to try DiwaneKhaas for lunch while exploring the Financial District and was drawn in by their budget-friendly combo menu prominently displayed on the window. The concept is simple: choose from 2, 3, or 4 dishes, paired with basmati rice or naan, for a price that seems almost too good to be true, especially for FiDi.

Opting for the 2 dish combo, I paired Chicken Tikka Masala with Palak Paneer, and tossed in a mango lassi for good measure. The portion seemed modest at first but ended up being adequately filling. However, the lack of partitions in the container meant that the dishes almost blended together, although they fortunately remained separate.

Sadly, the quality of the food didn't quite live up to the tempting offer. The rice was inconsistently cooked, with some grains harder than others. The Palak Paneer was watery with a lackluster taste, and while the Chicken Tikka Masala had generous chicken portions, it was only moderately flavored and didn't impress. As for the mango lassi, priced unusually at $3.28, it was disappointingly room temperature, though fairly acceptable taste-wise.

In retrospect, the meal didn't meet my moderate expectations, based on prior reviews. Although the prices are a major plus in the expensive neighborhood, the food was a letdown. I'm open to giving DiwaneKhaas another shot to try different dishes, but I'm not holding out for a drastically different experience.

Title: A Midwestern Oasis for Korean Cuisine at Barn Joo 35

In my quest for authentic Korean flavors in the Midwest, Yelp directed me to Barn Joo 35, and it did not disappoint. The dinner experience on a Tuesday evening surpassed expectations. 

The bibimbap, with its fresh seafood, offered a complex flavor profile that was both satisfying and a testament to authenticity. Their seafood hotpot was a fiery delight, perfect for those who appreciate a good spice kick. Complementing the meal, the Japanese whisky, served neat, was a refined addition.

We rounded off the meal with their nap buns stuffed with beef — a delectable finale. Service was commendably attentive, and while the hostess was visibly under pressure, her warmth never waned. The ambience struck the right note, enhancing the overall dining experience.

Barn Joo 35 has secured a spot on my list for repeat visits. It's a gem for anyone in the Midwest yearning for quality Korean cuisine.

I am glad I chose Basso56 for a very special birthday occasion. As I have moved to NYC recently, I was looking for a good Italian restaurant and I was very pleased.Made reservations in advance and was seated immediately. It is a pretty small space, but enough so no one is spilling over into your seat.To start, we ordered the special appetizer Burrata cheese wrapped in prosciutto. OH MY GOD. I do not think I can do it justice in text, but here goes. The Burrata was a melt in your mouth cheese while I believe they had used the oils from the cooked prosciutto to warm the cheese making it a wonderfully savory treat.For mains, we ordered the lobster crepes and Orecchiette. Both were amazing, lobster crepes came in a delectable sauce and the orecchiette came with garlicky sauce and sweet sausage.Love love love this place, and I look forward to another excuse to dine here.

Seasoned Vegan is a very famous spot in the vegan scene of New York City. Their location in Harlem, their story was widely spread on social media, and they attract many people - vegans and non-vegans. Today we were in the area and it was perfect opportunity to try it out! We arrived at brunch time on Saturday, and the place was full. After a short 10 minutes wait, we were seated.The place has a simple design, maybe too simple (and even unkempt). Our server was super kind but it took the food too long to come out. Now enough with the critics, it's time to talk about the food - YUM YUM YUM!Very interesting options on the menu, some that I've never seen in vegan places, and all tasted really good! We started with the quesadilla pizza with mushrooms (it's wasn't good looking for a pic, sorry), and for entrees we had the tuna melt sandwich and the chicken drumsticks on pancakes. Perfect brunch, we really enjoyed it!! And we were so full, we weren't able to have a dessert unfortunately...

Title: A Buzzing Gem with Tasty Eats and Live Jazz

I stumbled upon a local hotspot at 6pm on a Wednesday, assuming I'd nab a bar seat without a hitch. I was wrong. It took a good 20-minute orbit before I finally perched solo at the bar, but the silver lining was the live jazz from a talented trio that set a perfectly balanced auditory backdrop.

Word to the wise: this place is packed nightly, so reservations are a must. The ambiance strikes a fine balance between dark and chic – suitable for both business dinners and personal outings. The menu – an array of elevated American cuisine at reasonable prices – had my mouth watering.

I chose a sushi roll encased in fresh fish that was nothing short of excellent and a kale salad with chicken that was zestier than anticipated. Spice-lovers would rejoice over this dish. Despite the bar's constant whirl, the bartender doubled efficiently as my server, always keeping tabs on me without missing a beat.

All in all, the staff demonstrated a commendable symphony of service amidst the dining room's lively hustle. If you're in NYC looking for quality fare with a side of vibrant atmosphere, this is your spot – just don't forget to book ahead!

Perfect meal of savory, spicy comfort on an unseasonably chilly Late May afternoon in NYC. Opted for. Spicy chicken stir fry with wet noodles. It was as flavorful as it was colorful! The steamComing up from the noodles coupled with the  fragrance wafting from the kitchen was nostalgic. Classic NYC.  Some of the best food on some of the most unsuspecting Streets ...To be clear didn't go looking for this place. I went looking for soups & salads on Yelp and learned I was literally around the corner - love a good YELP SCORE! To say that I'm hella full is an understatement. Thankfully I can continue to warm up and make room for dessert by walking it off.Stop in - you won't regret it !

Title: A Modern Twist on Authentic Chinese Cuisine at The Tang

If you crave authentic Chinese food with a creative flair, The Tang, nestled near Columbia University, should be your next stop. With its modern decor that tastefully blends traditional touches, The Tang offers a vibrant and engaging atmosphere where you can witness the chefs at work in their open kitchen, all without being overwhelmed by noise or kitchen aromas.

Despite the limited seating, the service here is a standout – friendly, attentive, and accommodating even for customers with service animals. Just be sure to book ahead during peak hours, as the place fills up fast.

Onto the food – The Tang is nothing short of impressive. The Braised Beef Noodle Soup brings comfort in a bowl, featuring tender beef and a rich broth. For those with a palate for herbal notes, the Herbal Chicken Noodle dish with its robust, herb-infused broth is a must-try, offering boneless, succulent chicken alongside.

But the showstopper for me was the Fried Tiger Prawns with Salted Egg Yolk – an indulgent and beautifully balanced dish with the sweetness of mango cutting through the richness of the salted egg yolk. The Seared Beef Short Ribs and Roasted Eggplant, both displaying simplicity in seasoning yet excellence in taste, are also high on my recommendation list.

Don't miss out on the Fried Peppercorn Pork Belly; its traditional zest makes for a perfect appetizer best enjoyed fresh.

The Tang truly provides a memorable dining experience that respects traditional Chinese cuisine while delivering it with an innovative edge. Ideal for foodies and Columbia students alike, this place is a testament to how Chinese food can be both authentic and ingeniously modern.

On the rare occasion I want to sit down for lunch during a work day, this place is one of the reasons.I usually get the special Udon Noodles in curry with Fried Shrimp and then a side order of Chicken Katsu. The fact that all that food and tip comes to approx. $21 for a lunch in the popular Empire State Building Area is really a great deal. There lunch special is $10.99 and filling but I usually come here super hungry because once you have it, that curry craving will creep up on you from time to time.Word to wise - regular spicy is spicy. I'm Indian and eat spicy food and am so glad I didn't try to downplay this. They know what they're doing.It does get busy during peak hours but they give you a menu and even take your order while you wait.Pictures and all other positive reviews match up - definitely a must try especially if you work in the area!

Title: A Tasty Discovery: Fusion and Flavors Galore

Stumbled upon this gem on Yelp and it didn't disappoint. The open concept layout of the restaurant offered a relaxed atmosphere, perfect for a midday meal. It's a spot that echoes the spirit of tapas dining, emphasizing shared plates and a variety of tastes.

We kicked things off with soup and veggie dumplings; both exuded that coveted homemade vibe. Moving on to the main courses—the chicken pad thai was decent, though it didn't stand out from the usual fare. However, the drunken noodles were the star of the show with their delightful chewiness and perfectly seasoned, succulent chicken.

Intrigued by the pork buns, a novel take with the meat ensconced in dough, they were interesting but didn't quite win me over like the more familiar bao. Despite that, the culinary experience was top-notch.

Would I return? Absolutely. The meal was a hit, and it's one for the books when craving a fun, shared dining experience with flavorful dishes.

Title: Disappointing Experience at a Kosher Restaurant

I recently dined at a kosher restaurant on a Saturday night and was underwhelmed by the experience. Patrons should note that despite the 7 PM opening time listed on Yelp, the establishment did not open its doors until around 7:45 PM, resulting in a wasted hour for our large group dinner.

Food quality here does not compare favorably with surrounding eateries and the kosher designation seems to elevate the prices unjustifiably. I opted for the tomato soup priced at $11, which was decent but not outstanding. My friends chose salads and eggplant pasta, both of which were generously portioned but seemed overpriced considering the low cost of ingredients. Meatier dishes like fish come at an even steeper cost.

The restaurant imposes rigid rules, such as a mandatory $20 minimum spend per person and a $6 sharing fee, which can be off-putting. Despite a slight leniency on my below-minimum order, the vibe from the staff was less than welcoming. Furthermore, the staff missed an opportunity to enhance our experience by not acknowledging my friend’s birthday, even with reservations indicating the celebration.

Overall, unless you're dining with someone who strictly adheres to a kosher diet, I find it hard to recommend this restaurant given its high prices, restrictive policies, and lackluster atmosphere.

Title: A Cozy Hidden Gem for Ukrainian Comfort Food

Thanks to Yelp, I discovered the unassuming Streecha, a casual spot reminiscent of a cafeteria, yet it serves up some seriously authentic Ukrainian comfort food that hits the spot. The menu features classics, and I decided on the stuffed cabbage and pierogies. While the stuffed cabbage was satisfying, the pierogies stole the show – they are the epitome of tender, melt-in-your-mouth goodness and are hands down the best I've ever had. In comparison to the popular Veselka, I might give Veselka a slight edge for their stuffed cabbage, but when it comes to pierogies, Streecha is the clear champion. A must-visit for anyone craving a taste of Ukraine.

Title: A Cheesy Delight Worth Returning To

My recent visit to this mac 'n' cheese haven was an absolute treat! Lucky for me, I dropped in at lunchtime, avoiding the much-talked-about crowds. The kiosk ordering system was slick, though I could see it potentially struggling during peak hours, where additional staff might be needed.

Now, let's talk about the star of the show – the food. Their menu takes the comforting classic, mac and cheese, and elevates it to mouthwatering heights. I indulged in the Neapoletana Mac n' Cheese, and it was simply divine – imagine your favorite pizza but in creamy, cheesy pasta form.

Given the brisk weather and my intense hunger, devouring this dish was nothing short of incredible. Portion sizes range from the modest 'Nosh' to the party-worthy 'Partay,' catering to all appetites.

There's a tempting selection of vegetarian options I'm eager to explore on my next visit. And a tip for future patrons: bring friends and dive into their sampler skillet for a communal feast of mac 'n' cheese varieties. I can't wait to come back!

LOVE LOVE LOVE!! That's all I can really say about this place. Their weekend lunch buffet has a ton of offerings at a reasonable price. In a neighborhood full of Indian restaurants, Dhaba stands out. The tandoori chicken legs (part of the buffet but delivered to your table) and the saag paneer are delicious! The bread basket has a great variety as well. They have ample seating, but I could imagine it gets crowded in the early lunch hours. I hope to be back soon for this delicious, filling and reasonably priced buffet!

This spot is a must-visit for drink aficionados; the concoctions here are irresistibly smooth and delectable. It's wise not to run a tab, as these tantalizing beverages make it hard to say when. The buzzing crowd is testament to the allure. Kudos to the mixologists for maintaining exceptional standards. Cheers to a fantastic night ahead!

Title: Cozy Japanese Gem in the East Village

During our recent holiday visit to New York's East Village, my wife and I, along with her cousin, decided to dine at a quaint Japanese restaurant renowned for its culinary finesse.

The food was an absolute delight. Following our server's recommendation, we started with the seared Tuna Tataki, served with a miso-based sauce. Although typically not a fan of creamy miso, I was pleasantly surprised by the dish's flavors, despite blotting some sauce away. The tuna was expertly seared with precision, leaving a sliver of cooked edge that maintained the fish's integrity.

I chose the Unagi Don for my main course. The unagi's portion was generous, a comforting choice for the chilly weather. The dish was tasty, yet it fell short of exceptional, partly due to the presentation which made it somewhat challenging to navigate.

The restaurant’s atmosphere exudes cleanliness and careful maintenance, although the dim lighting was less to our preference. It's a snug spot, so coming early or preparing for a wait might be wise.

Service was a high point - attentive, knowledgeable, and commendable for great recommendations from the appetizers to the sake.

Price-wise, it's on par with similar establishments in the area, making it a reasonable choice for those seeking quality Japanese cuisine.

Overall, despite the dim ambiance and a few personal quirks with the food, the restaurant delivered a memorable dining experience with standout service.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Thursday Kitchen

My recent visit to Thursday Kitchen was overshadowed by an unwelcoming experience and a series of culinary missteps. We were initially drawn in by the novelty of their LED light cube drinks, but the service quickly dampened our enthusiasm. Despite not ordering alcohol myself, I was asked for ID, which felt unnecessary and intrusive.

Although my party chose three dishes to share, the waitress aggressively pushed for more, incorrectly assuming it was our first visit and lecturing us on the tapas-style servings. This insistence was both condescending and unwarranted as there was no minimum spend required.

Regrettably, the food did not redeem the service. The steak lacked tenderness, the soft shell crab was overdone, and the kimchi paella suffered from dryness. The lone highlight was the popcorn ice cream, but it was not enough to save the overall experience. In summary, Thursday Kitchen fell short of expectations, both in hospitality and culinary execution.

I've been to some of their other locations before and enjoyed it but wasn't too inclined to come back for the price. The other day, however, they were doing a special promotion where you could get a drink, a dessert, and a cookie for only $10 which is essentially half off. This definitely was a good opportunity to try everything, as I probably would never otherwise get a cookie or drink here since I mainly think of The Spot for its decadent, Instagrammable desserts. Honestly the cookie may have been my favorite out of everything. It was so warm and gooey and absolutely delicious. My hot taro tea was quite nice as well, but by the time the desserts arrived, I was almost to the point where I couldn't really take much more sugar without feeling awful. Since the deal required each person at the table to order their own set, we had way more food than we were able to eat, which feels a bit disappointing, but at least we were able to try so many different things.

Title: A Delightful Evening at a Hidden Gem

My dining experience at this restaurant was nothing short of delightful. Arriving at 5:15 PM on a Wednesday, the place initially greeted us with tranquility, but it swiftly buzzed to life within the half hour, creating a lively atmosphere.

The starters set the stage with the spicy tuna tacos being a standout - four small discs that packed a crispy punch of flavor. The shrimp & pork gyoza were tasty, although a slight hiccup was their tendency to cling together.

The entrées impressed us further. The classic ramen, accentuated with black garlic oil, featured succulent slices of pork, a rich broth, and noodles that hit the mark of doneness. The spicy ramen, on the other hand, brought heat without overwhelming the palate, achieving a balanced and enjoyable dish.

Complementing the food was the service - attentive and cordial, enhancing the pleasant ambiance of the restaurant.

This establishment left a lasting impression, compelling me to consider not just a return visit but also to go out of my way for a repeat experience.

The short: really, really delicious, clean food in a contemporary setting with great staff. The longer: we made a reservation on OpenTable and came here on a Monday evening. The space was super quiet, and our waitress was very nice. We shared a large beer. The menu is a mix of tapas and regular size plates. We started with the tandoori shrimp in a tapas size. Amazing. 3 jumbo shrimps in the order. Then, we shared the okra masala, chicken tikka, dal & some naan. Rice is complimentary -- which I appreciate -- and they give you refills if you need them. The food was all super fresh, wasn't overly oily or creamy, and was generally just very good. It's nice to have such a high-quality, trendy Indian tapas spot in the neighborhood. I highly recommend!

I love Takashi!!! Recently they started a Sunday brunch menu with Beef Ssam and two types of Beef Ramen!! Of course I had to get a reservation!!There are only two time slots - one at 12pm and one at 1:30pm. You have to email them and they will make the reservation for you. It feels up really quickly and if you have a party of less than 4, you will most likely have to share a table because every seat in the house is filled up!Today, we tried the regular beef ramen and the grandma's spicy ramen. Both of the bowls come with beef belly, crunchy intestines, half a poached egg, seaweed, green onions, sesame and noodles. The grandma's one also had spicy paste.Personally, I really loved the beef broth. I felt that it was so hearty and sastisfying and felt a lot less fatty than the usual pork broth that ramen is in. I really enjoyed it! It was like a big fat warm cozy full bodied hug on a brutally cold winter day. I'd definitely come back!

Excellent food, ambiance, and service! We stumbled into Terraversa on a Thursday early evening. The restaurant was empty at a time but it looked so welcoming that we had a good feeling and ventured in.First of all, the price to portion size was fantastic. When I saw 16 dollars for plates of pasta like lobster ravioli, I assumed they would be small portions. But they were sizable portions and very delicious. The penne with shrimp pesto is a highlight. The shrimp was perfectly cooked and the sauce was creamy and flavorful.My bf and I shared the plate of meat and veggies. He doesn't eat beef or like salmon, so they made it with only chicken and lamb chops. It's like our waitress knew exactly what we wanted. This was also a very large portion, with all types of veggies like squash, mushroom's, potatoes, and bell peppers.We closed out our meal with the cheese cake which was also fantastic. The bruleed suger on top was a great touch and something I've never had on cheesecake.While the food was fantastic, what really made this a 5 star experience was the service. Our waitress was attentive and sweet. We had free bread with olives/oil flowing all evening long.

Delicious food. Phenomenal drinks. I enjoyed the calamari and steam dumpling. The sauce that accompany the calamari is delicious. The happy hour drink menu was reasonable. Overall the environment was welcoming and food was fresh and hot and wait wasn't long. I would definitely be back.

This place is an amazing little find! You can snag some vegan eats loaded with superfoods! I decided on the platter to try 5 items over brown rice and the helping was perfect! The food was perfectly seasoned! I had the turmeric tofu, Chana masala, kale salad, quinoa salad, cucumber and tomato salad, along with mango lemonade. This isn't ideal for groups, but is a perfect small place to grab a quick and healthy bite!

Title: Cozy Spot for a Speedy Ramen Fix

I recently dined at a quaint little ramen shop that was a study in efficiency and warmth. The seating was promptly handled, with a choice between a few cozy tables and a welcoming bar area. Service was swift, as was the arrival of our hearty bowls.

My sister, a repeat patron, recommended the curry ramen but decided to indulge in the Tan Tan this visit. She was not disappointed by the creamy delight of her choice. I took a spicy turn with the seafood ramen, a dish that garnered my affection with its perfectly cooked egg and well-seasoned meat. Though I found the meat portion slightly modest, the ramen itself boasted an ideal al dente bite.

However, there was room for improvement with regard to the flavor impact of the toppings, which I felt could have elevated the dish significantly. On a side note, service was passable, though it took some effort to catch the staff's attention.

In conclusion, this ramen shop offers a good meal with a few areas that could use some fine-tuning. Perfect for a quick, satisfying noodle fix.

My brunch experience at this spot was a delightful surprise! The ingredients were top-notch - fresh and of great quality, with flavors that truly satisfied. The service was commendable, efficient without being rushed. An added bonus was the lack of wait time on a Sunday morning, which is a rarity. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone in search of a pleasurable brunch outing.

Overall this place lives up to the hype! Expect a decent wait, but I'd say it's totally worth the wait.- burger is smaller than the Instagram picture you saw. That said, solid flavors and absolutely delicious. On the pricey side of $26. Comes with fries- Pizza looks kind of small but can feed 2 and you'll be very full. Got the meatball with vodka sauceOne-time items:- they took 45 minutes (aka forever) to bring our pizza out- they acknowledged this bad service and gave the pizza to us on the house- Our Emmy burger was kind of soft and could have been executed a little better- might have just been a bad one- The dough in our pizza was pretty undercooked- not inedible but definitely not up to par to what I've had before- Probably just a bad day but today they lacked on execution a bit. I'll give them the benefit of the doubt and keep this rating at 4 stars.

Title: Cozy Corner Spot with Trendy Eats

After much anticipation, my visit to the bustling restaurant by Bryant Park, just around the corner from the B/D train station, did not disappoint. Despite a rainy Monday evening, the place filled up quickly, a testament to its popularity.

Seated without delay, we found the two-person tables near the entrance a tad too close for comfort, allowing us to inadvertently eavesdrop on our neighbors. Despite this, the evening was enjoyable.

The Mushroom Flatbread, though unexpectedly shaped and slightly on the greasy side, offered a generous portion for sharing, yet the crust's lack of crunch was a letdown. The highly praised Truffle Burger, complete with a spicy sauce that delivered a punch, was a hit with my boyfriend. The accompanying truffle fries, irresistibly delectable, nearly vanished before we delved into the rest of our meal.

The Brussels sprouts with Chinese sausage made for a savory, albeit greasy, side that fascinated our taste buds with its unique pairing.

For dessert, the Affogato catered to coffee aficionados with its intriguing mix of warm espresso and vanilla ice cream, perfectly complemented by a biscotti for dipping. The RAF coffee, a creamy Russian concoction resembling warm, molten ice cream, provided a lush finale that could easily double as dessert.

The modern decor and spacious atmosphere, paired with swift and attentive service, rounded out our dining experience on a high note.

My friends and I went because we bought a travel zoo deal. We loved it, but also got bottomless brunch which is not actually on their menu. The servers were all really friendly and the food was delicious. I decided to try every drink on the menu since I had bottomless, and no one batted an eyelash. The location was really nice. I'd recommend it even without bottomless.

I've been coming to Rue 57 for well over 20 years.The owner Mark Packer runs amazing eateries throughout New York City.I've always been a regular here but unfortunately my last 3 visits in seven weeks have been subpar at best and only made better by the waiter once I complained.The hostesses do their job but don't seem to really care.the acknowledgments are lukewarm and the last time she didn't pay attention to me at all even though I was standing there.My last visit I came with a friend and we were seated corner booth I requested. as the hostess put the menus down as she was walking away she said enjoy...umm ok.I waited over 15 minutes before finally getting up to look for a manager and ask if a waiter could please take our drink order.What I found repulsive is that there were 4 servers and at least two bus boys in our section and all of them just looked at us among themselves and we were ignored. Literally!Once again after complaining and asking for help and service did the service turn out to be impeccable but unfortunately by then the experience is already quite Dampored.The menu doesn't change over the years so when you go there you always know what to expect truffle fries, burgers, fish and steaks, several omelette egg dishes. Unfortunately they do not have many vegetarian and non-existent vegan options.They also have a variety of Japanese and sushi items.I ordered a champagne by the glass. they have 2 different kinds.Moet which is better and another kind which I didn't care for.The decor is cozy with woods and red booths.They also have a beautiful party room downstairs for private events.In the spring and summer they have outdoor seating in for its location on 57th and sixth Avenue it's a great place to people watch.I wish Mark came to this restaurant more to observe on what's going on it's really disappointing to find out how much it's changed and how bad the service lax  unless you complain.So many years if I was going to be eating in the city or wanting to meet a friend this was the first place I thought of. The food is good the location is great the ambience is good but unfortunately I don't want to have the same experience that I've had the last three times so it will probably be the last place I think of.They are not consistent anymore.

I still really like Balthazar, but I think the prices can be high for what you're getting. Over the past couple of years I feel like the quality hasn't always been top notch, and the service not always as friendly as it could have been.I won't go into much detail on the waitstaff, French waiter jokes and all. But the food is really what I care most about. There have been a few misses, but on my most recent visit the puff pastry with creamy scrambled eggs, mushrooms, and fork-tender asparagus had stale pastry. In some places rock hard, completely inedible. There's no excuse for that in a $22 brunch entree. Everything else was spot on, and that's usually how things go sideways here, everything is almost perfect except for one big component that you can't help but be disappointed in.My bacon was crazy good, their green juice was impossibly smooth and refreshing (if not criminally small for the price). I'm not swearing them off, but I can't still come here and guarantee the people I'm bringing a perfect meal.  Also, if you're going to put oysters on your brunch menu don't scold me when I try to order them at brunch! Humpf.

Stopped in for brunch before a broadway show on Sunday and got sat right away in the dining room. Service was good, our table was by the kitchen so I got a front row seat to that chaos everyone was moving to get those orders out! The menu has plenty of options, I got the grilled cheese with tomato soup which was pretty good but had a tad too much broccoli in the sandwich. I tried the pancakes as well which were very fluffy and full of flavor, yum! My friend had the eggs and she said they are cooked perfectly so all around the food was very tasty.

I sorely miss the Queens Bodega scene and this is a quite good fix for all sorts of things! I have come in here a few times for MealPal, and their service is fast and the sandwiches are really good. I've had their smoothies and sandwiches on the regular and they do a great job. I'd be curious to try the hot bar and the pizza as it always does look good. They're 24 hours, convenient, and they have a wide selection of drinks and small grocery items. I'm a fan and it's been there in a pinch!!

If you find yourself in Chinatown with a hankering for pho, I've discovered a gem that serves up a steaming, generous bowl that's sure to satisfy. This spot hits the mark with a deliciously robust broth that, while enhanced with a hint of MSG, doesn't overwhelm the fresh flavors. A bountiful serving of meat meets okay quality standards, and it pairs perfectly with the fresh noodles and crisp bean sprouts. They offer limes, which add a welcome zest to the meal, and I personally recommend throwing in some red peppers for an extra kick. The staff are decent and efficient, contributing to the positive experience. At $9 a bowl, the value is undeniable for the quality and portion size.

Title: A Flavor Fiesta in Hell's Kitchen

After exploring several Mexican eateries in Hell's Kitchen, I've finally discovered my top pick. The steak quesadilla was a revelation, generously stuffed with succulent, flavorful steak that promised – and delivered – a delectable experience from the very first bite. Each of the four hearty quesadilla triangles ensured I left completely satiated and eager to return.

My boyfriend's short rib tacos garnered high praise as well, adding another must-try dish to our list. While the culinary journey was impressive, the service left something to be desired. The attentiveness of the staff did not match the quality of the food; more frequent check-ins would have enhanced the overall dining experience. Nonetheless, the food alone is a reason to come back for another round of Mexican bliss.

Title: A Disappointing Brunch Experience at Sall’s

My enthusiasm for supporting new eateries was severely dampened after a frustrating visit to Sall's for brunch. With a Puls'd voucher in hand promising a $39 deal for two, inclusive of 90 minutes of unlimited mimosas, my companion and I were disheartened by the lukewarm beverages that necessitated a request for ice.

The food experience was no less disappointing. We faced an unjustifiable 20-minute wait to be informed of the absence of burger buns. A proposed switch to steak and eggs carried an unwaived additional charge of $10, despite the previous burger order. Meanwhile, a fellow diner's unsettling discovery of a foreign hair in her meal was met with an accusatory response from the staff, rather than concern.

Our order of chicken and waffles resulted in a meager offering of chicken with a waffle shaped like a cone, accompanied by an unappealing cold slice of butter. To add to the letdown, the much-anticipated side of lobster Mac and cheese, costing $18, was portioned for a child and served post-meal.

The final bill presented was astonishingly more than the voucher, including double sales tax and automatic gratuity, with an insinuating space for an extra tip. An attempt to discuss the disappointing chicken and waffles with the manager resulted in a dismissive retort and a reluctant removal of the sales tax, leaving the steak and egg surcharge unaddressed.

Regrettably, I cannot endorse Sall's, for the brunch experience fell far short of expectations. The unwillingness to honor the advertised deal and the poor service overshadowed the venue's aesthetic appeal. In the realm of brunch options, there are undoubtedly better choices where the value and customer experience align more closely with the promise.

So, the food isn't anything to go out of your way for, but it's good, and the restaurant is a nice, homey, neighborhood spot.  There are always lines out the door on weekends for brunch.  It was open for Christmas today.  I had a burger and fries, which again, weren't amazing, but were both solid.  They have coloring books and crayons for kids and welcomed my toddler.  I'd definitely come back.

Raku is one of my Japanese boss's favorite restaurants and we visited there a couple of times with a larger group. The decor of Raku is elegant, classy and bright. We highly recommend to have their signature udon and side dish karaage for the first try. The food was delicious and delicate with reasonable price even though the portion was small. I had Oyako Don which was chicken and egg over the rice last time and it was pretty decent. The chicken was tender and the onion was sweet-flavored.

I love Panzerotti too now. I didn't know what Panzerotti was until today. It's like a calzone as we know it, but fried instead of baked. And the dough is rolled out thinner. It was yummy. They offer savory and sweet panzerotti. I would give the food five stars because it was very fresh and the bread part was delicious. I got smoked salmon, fresh mozzarella, arugula and it was served on/in an empty calzone/panzerotti "shell". It really really scrumptious. Unfortunately I had to send my first Panzerotti back because it had truffle oil on it. I detest truffle oil. So they really need to indicate that on the menu. Fortunately another person behind me also ordered the salmon too and overheard me me mention the truffle oil. She also did not want truffle oil. Fortunately, they made another Panzerotti for me. Sadly, I waited 15 minutes for my Panzerotti to be remade. It does not take 15 minutes to put smoked salmon, mozzarella and arugula on a calzone. I got there about 11:50 AM. So it wasn't that crowded. I'll attribute it to the staff getting ramped up. I have to say that the homemade spicy potato chips were a highlight. They had just the right amount of heat. and they weren't barbecue flavored, which I liked. I would've liked to have eaten the with my sandwich but because I was waiting so long, I ate all my chips before I got my panzerotti. Oh well. The food was excellent and I think my instance was probably a one off. I also sampled their "Classic" which was already made. I preferred my panzerotti with the smoked salmon. I would come back and order the one I got sans truffle oil (and avocado) and I recommend you confirm what is on your made to order panzerotti.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Dumplings

I recently visited a dumpling restaurant where the experience didn't quite justify the price tag. For $28, I expected the 16 dumplings we ordered to be exceptional. We tried the Mimi Cheng dumplings and the pan-fried reinvented classic, both of which tasted fresh and homemade. The first plate arrived swiftly, but due to a mix-up, we endured a 10+ minute wait for the second, leading us to inquire about the delay.

The forgotten order was promptly rectified, though some dumplings seemed slightly undercooked. The highlight was the intriguing secret sauce, adding a unique twist to the meal. While the dumplings were decent and the venue might be worth a try for first-timers, the lapse in service and value for money left room for improvement.

Had just wrapped up a meeting when I strolled past Oceana. It was the lunch hour and there was seating by the bar area, so I stepped inside and grabbed a seat next to a window to watch the street traffic.Staff was friendly and immediately brought menus and water. Ordered a glass of the Milton Park Chardonnay.Fresh bread and oil were brought.Inquired about the fresh oysters. Decided on a half dozen of the Fisher Island oysters. These were lighter in flavor and perfect over the lunch hour.Next up, Shrimp Winter Greek Salad. Pricey and delicious. Cabbage based with feta cheese, beets, and grilled shrimp. Enjoyed my lunch and would definitely return.

Looking for a quick bite, we walked by Zorba Grill and decided to give it a try. The staff greeted us with warm smiles and were extremely welcoming, mind you it's New York City, so the vibe was different than what we've encountered so far. We ordered their lunch special; chicken doner wrap along with cheese wispers and ginger ale drink.I love how you make your own wrap and choose your toppings. The process is simple, you choose between a wrap or bowl, then your meat and 3 toppings. The hummus and yogurt dressing were my favorite. At the end, they heat your wrap and it comes out warm and delicious.The place was clean and well organized. The fridge had so many delicious options!!:D If you're around the neighborhood, make sure to give them a try. Portions are relatively filling and reasonably priced. Thank you New York for this delicious food and amazing staff.

Worth every penny!! Everything from the food to the cocktails, ambiance and service was exceptional! We ordered the tasting menu which was very generous and absolutely delicious. Loved every single dish from its thorough description, artistic presentation to its unique Indian flavors. Busy place, even on a weeknight so reservations are encouraged! Upscale spot for date night or client lunch/dinner.

Title: A Bowl of Heaven at Jin Ramen

Last night's experience at Jin Ramen was nothing short of exceptional. With a group of five, each of us dived into different ramen dishes and emerged with resounding praise. The consistency and quality of the food were evident in our collective contentment.

The ability to reserve a table through Yelp added to the convenience, and our wait was minimal. I savored a "Special" Ramen, which may have slipped my mind name-wise, but not flavor-wise. It featured succulent pork belly, tender baby bok choy, and a custom medium boiled egg nestled atop. At $18, the portion was generous enough to provide a second delicious meal at home.

The magic lay in the balance of the broth - a harmonious and sumptuous embrace to the perfectly cooked noodles. It's fortunate for my self-control that Jin Ramen isn't a local temptation for me. But for those nearby or visiting, it’s an absolute must-visit for an unforgettable ramen indulgence.

Title: Satisfying Soul Food Sunday at Amy Ruth's

My recent Sunday brunch at Amy Ruth's with seven friends was a delightful surprise. Despite the party size, we were comfortably seated in a mere 20 minutes. The menu pays homage to notable African Americans; I indulged in the "Gabrielle Union"—two large, smothered pork chops with sides of mac & cheese and candied yams. The meal was exceptional: the pork chops delectable with perfectly seasoned gravy, the yams offering a sweet symphony without being too sugary, and the mac & cheese was simply divine, setting the bar for soul food excellence. The only hiccup was an inconsistency in the tenderness of the pork chops, an oddity that didn't detract from the overall deliciousness. Be warned: the portions are generous, leaving no room for dinner! Service and ambiance are straightforward, no-frills, but effectively supportive of an overall very satisfying dining experience. Amy Ruth's is a must-visit for soul food aficionados.

So I popped into this bar while looking for a fast place to eat. And it caught my eye with the fire wood pizza on the window... unfortunately the pizza was a bust. The lady that served me was sweet but i should've ordered a salad the topping were cold and the crust tasted worse than a frozen pizza from the store. Will not be returning.

Title: Surf, Turf, and Satisfaction at Burger and Lobster NYC

At Burger and Lobster, a London-based sensation that's taking New York by storm, the name says it all. This eatery has pared down the menu to perfect two decadent choices: burgers and lobsters. Their approach to the classic "surf and turf" is simple yet sublime - you can indulge in a juicy burger, savor a whole lobster, or revel in the glory of both.

Each combo is thoughtfully served with crispy fries and a fresh salad, striking a satisfying balance on your plate. The lobster shines whether you opt for it whole or nestled in a brioche roll, while the burger stands out—a must-try for meat lovers.

Be warned: the appeal is no secret among the locals. To snag a spot at this popular joint during the bustling lunch or dinner hours, it's wise to book a table online in advance. Long lines are a testament to the quality and popularity of Burger and Lobster, but with a reservation, you'll bypass the wait and dive straight into a mouthwatering meal that's well worth the hype.

I came here for dinner during restaurant week. I would ultimately rate this restaurant a 4.5 out of 5. There were some hiccups during the evening but ultimately it was a great experience and would definitely recommend. We made a reservation for a party of 2 at 5:30. When we got there on time, there was a huge crowd at the front waiting to be seated. We waited for a bit for our table. It seemed as if the restaurant just opened for dinner or something as seating was pretty open. Once we got seated, service was great. I love the decor of the restaurant. I got the burrata, skirt steak, and creme brûlée. Also taster the crab toast and halibut. The burrata was creamy and the peach complimented it very well for a summer-y dish. The crab avocado toast was so good. A good amount of crab on top. However, the hot sauce that it came with wasn't really spicy which would have been a nice kick, but more a fruity sauce. The skirt steak was cooked perfectly and nicely flavored. Portion-wise overall was a lot.  I was pretty full by dessert. The creme brulee was the only thing I didn't prefer. It was a lot denser and sweeter than I typically like it. But overall, great meal with reasonable prices. The drinks though really added to the bill for 18$ cocktails were a bit pricey.
I think this is a must try while in new York! It's actually 99 cent pizza for a big side of pizza. Pizza was really good, line went by super fast!! I highly recommend it!

During a recent weekend brunch at this new and trendy spot, I was treated to an amazing dining experience. The clean, simplistic ambiance set a welcoming tone, complemented by attentive service with frequent water refills.

The $25 Pork Katsu Sando, despite being slightly tough, was delicious and well worth the price for its spot-on flavors. The $23 Duck Leg was another highlight, served with an egg and a corn mash - its mature flavor profile provided a delightful contrast to the Pork Katsu Sando. Both dishes were memorable, and I left with no regrets, just a satisfied palate. Highly recommend for a brunch with a touch of sophistication.

I don't know what to make of this place, nor could I figure it out reading other reviews. One of my dining companions said he vacations in Mexico every year, and he thought his dinner was authentic. Then I saw others that said it was authentic Mexican, others saying it wasn't, and others saying it was authentic Dominican. I'm not really sure the Mexican pizza I ordered was that authentic either. It was cubes of grilled chicken with some sauce and cheese on a warm, soft pita, with a large side of sour cream, cut into 4 pieces. I didn't think it was anything special, but you know what? The chicken was tasty and it did hit the spot. Warm salsa? I'd never had it, and again some friends who have traveled there say it is warm in some regions. Now those frozen margaritas...  it was pretty much a layer of fruit syrup of choice on the bottom topped with frozen margarita mix, and you had to channel your inner "Washing machine agitator" with your straw, stirring and spinning, and moving it up and down if you wanted any chance of distributing the flavor. It was hardly the tastiest frozen margarita I've ever had, maybe not even a semi-finalist, but it got the job done (the job being to infuse my body with tequila).I think our timing was right for visiting here, i.e., later at night. It's not necessarily a place I'd go for dinner, but definitely a place for a nighttime fix.

The atmosphere was very old-timey and classic. It felt very vintage, and the servers were extremely approachable and nice. I also appreciated the bathroom's cleanliness and the interior decor in general. The food was unfortunately not worth the price. It was delicious, yes, but I did not think brunch would end up being $73 for two. We ordered the eggs meurette and the eggs florentine, and were somehow convinced that there would not be bread, so we ordered a pastry as well. When the food came, there was indeed complimentary bread, so the croissant was not necessary. The food portion was decent, and did not fill me up excessively. The eggs meurette were a little bit too salty while the eggs florentine were a little bit too light. To be honest, not the most memorable place for brunch.

I recently indulged my Vegan Mexican cravings at this gem of a place, and it did not disappoint—vegan or otherwise, the flavors here are irresistibly delicious. My order arrived promptly via Caviar delivery, with hearty portions that were perfect for two. We savored the "chorizo" burritos, which were packed with taste and texture, alongside a generous serving of nachos—an instant hit and the highlight of our feast. The corn on the cob was a sweet complement, and we finished off with a delectable caramel flan. The nachos were a standout; make sure to give them a try!

Tucked away in the heart of the city, Indochine stands out as a trendy hotspot, inviting diners into its exotic 80's themed ambiance, replete with palm-adorned walls and sultry red lighting. The pre-theater menu, available between 5:30 and 7 PM, is an exceptional deal, offering mouthwatering selections even without traditional Vietnamese staples like pho.

We dove into starters of spicy squid and spring rolls, each dish a visual feast scoring high on presentation. Entrées did not disappoint; the spicy chicken and sizzling beef arrived sputtering on hot plates, perfectly complemented by the autumn festival reminiscent sticky rice – a must-try that enhanced our meal's savory depth.

Dessert, while not groundbreaking, was scrumptiously satisfying with a rich chocolate mousse cake and a tangy lemon tart. Indochine impresses with its spacious comfort and an explosion of flavors that ensures a repeat visit is in order.

What an AMAZING dining experience!We decided on La Pecora because it was in walking distance of our hotel, and the weather was sweltering, even in the evening.  We didn't have a reservation, and the friendly hostess said the "Chef's Counter" was available.  Why not???  At first we were the only two, but more came and it sits five a little cozily.They have a great wine list that is reasonable, and we opted for a Super Tuscan....soooo good!  We shared the kale salad, and watched how it was prepared.  The dressing alone I could just drink!  I ordered the pork chop which was seasoned with a little rosemary....delicious, and the grilled plums were sooooo good!  Daveed had the skirt steak, which was grilled perfectly.  We shared the tagliatelle with beef and pork bolognese, which paired very well.  Again, we were able to see your meals being prepared and it was fun to watch the Chef call out the orders and to make sure the presentations were perfect.We also had to have dessert.  We shared the olive oil cake, which with the whipped cream and strawberries, was like a shortcake but oh sooooo good!  And we also had the dense chocolate mousse that had the perfect balance of chocolate to sugar and was not overly sweet like some.  A shot of limoncello and two cappuccinos and we were stuffed!Our server, Eric K. was great!  Kept an eye on us, but I think knew we weren't those demanding diners that need attention.  He thought we were from Hawaii.  I hope he has a great time when he goes.  The restaurant was full when we walked in, and people were still coming in. I do suggest making a reservation, but I also highly recommend the Chef's Counter.  It was very entertaining, and it was much more fun watching the kitchen than watching the other diners.  If you don't have a great experience here, there's something seriously wrong with YOU!Thank you La Percora!  You are my new favorite NYC restaurant!

During a recent dinner at NYC19, I had the pleasure of indulging in their Tsukemen, a dish that stood out for its exceptional quality and flavor. The Karaage (Japanese fried chicken) served alongside scored a respectable 3 out of 5 – it was tasty, though not extraordinary. However, the broth of the Tsukemen earned a perfect 5, striking an impressive balance of depth and richness that enhanced the entire dish.

The noodles also received top marks; they were cooked to perfection, maintaining the ideal chewiness that is so integral to a satisfying Tsukemen experience. The Chashu (braised pork belly) was enjoyable with a score of 3, but I found it slightly lacking in comparison to the other components. The Tamago (seasoned soft-boiled egg), on the other hand, was fantastic – a true delight that complemented the rest meticulously.

The meal concluded with the restaurant’s signature 焼石 (heated stone) feature, which was a remarkable experience, elevating the dining occasion even further. In summary, the experience at NYC19 was "as good as it gets." This restaurant is a must-visit for any Tsukemen enthusiast or someone looking to discover the heights this dish can reach.

I frequent my visits in the Dyckman strips for years now, but for whatever reason never stepped foot into Il Sole. Went on a Friday night after work to catch the happy hour which consisted of $6 Sangria, Margaritas, and I believe some beers. Me and my friend had the sangria to kick off then later on the passion fruit margarita. We sat at the bar and was serviced by the AMAZING bartender Gabby! We were soo impressed with her service as it's rate to find within the surrounding establishments. She was very attentive to us and made us feel comfortable throughout our whole stay. We did order some appetizers which hit the spot too. Overall, great customer service, good ambiance although small, but cute. Good for small groups and music not too loud that allows for conversation. I would definitely go back and recommend to others. I look forward trying some of the entrees.

Yes,  this a place to have your NY strip steak! We had a big party of 10 ppl and the service totally made our dinner perfect. While everybody were gathering, we were waiting on the bar area, bartenders were really good, very fast and tasty cocktail! Once we were sat, the waiter worked very fast and efficient. He was at the table when we were in need of him without us asking. The service is top notch. All appetizers came out fast and tasty: foie gras was cooked to perfection and seafood was fresh! For the main course I got NY strip steak medium rare - 1000% recommend, such a tender piece! For the side we shared a lot of staff, my favorite was mac&cheese.... and creme brulee is so goodAmazing place, definitely come back

I was excited to try this place. It wasn't particularly good or bad. My friends were underwhelmed. Bread came out with a weird dipping concoction that had beans in it. I got a drink with fig. Wasn't overly sweet and was a weird consistency - like consistency of pulp. We got the mozz and tomatoes. Nothing special. Exactly what you would expect. My friend got the octopus. There were 2 huge octopus in a weird purée. My friend said the octopus was not seasoned well and didn't really have much flavor. She didn't think the purée added anything and took the octopus out. I got the special pasta dish. Was like a ravioli with eggplant and truffle in a butter and cheese. It was pretty good. But nothing I would travel back here for. The pot de creme was pretty good.My friends didn't really care for this place. It got super crowded later in the evening.We all decided we would not come back.

My boyfriend took us there to try because he always pass by it. I was skeptical at first because he didn't know the name of the place so I could do my research on it before we got there lol. I wasn't in the mood for ramen but decided to share and give it a chance. Surprisingly it was amazing. We ordered the Soul Ramen to share with chicken. The set up was ok. You order at the iPad then sit wherever you want. They bring you the food. The staff was friendly. But I wonder what happens when they get super busy. How do they remember who order what and where they are sitting. Anyway check out the pictures. We will come back to try something else next time.

Belated birthday dinner 2019 for party of three was delightful.Reservations are recommended via OpenTable.com as mine were made and my party was promptly seated.  A modern American steakhouse of cozy atmosphere with bright lighting of high ceiling, large space, comfortable seating and abundant table space easily accessible by 6 train at 28th Street station in north of Madison Square Park walking distance on East 28th Street intersecting 5th Avenue and Madison Avenue.  Customer service is impeccable for efficiency, attentive, respect and professionalism.  Quality Eats alleged claim their meat embedded on their plates: "verified, super high quality, satisfaction guaranteed."  Their signature cuts are served with a choice of curly fries or salad.  Boisterously loud background noise from patrons' constant chatter and it is certainly not conducive for conversation.  The background music was not loud.The Hanger $28This is my favorite choice of steak and traditionally considered more flavorful as it is known for the tenderness and juiciness.  Unfortunately, the meat was not juicy as expected but burnt edge and dry interior from being overcooked amid my request to be cooked medium.  The meat is fresh of a good portion size, but disappointingly dry.  Only condiments available are chipotle sauce and traditional steak sauce which I believe taints the cook's preparation and cooking.  Since my entrée was excessively dry I had no choice but to add traditional steak sauce, but I prefer black pepper peppercorn or sea salt as condiments.  I find Quality Eats meat average quality.  The meat was not tender ergo it was not easy to cut using a steak knife that I had to apply excessive force and pressure.  I opt for the salad.  It is a tri-color salad of red radicchio lettuce and balsamic vinegar embedded.  I prefer Cesar salad with romaine lettuce topped with Parmesan cheese.Sirloin Strip $46This entrée was abundant in portion served with abundant curly fries.  My party member also had to use traditional steak sauce as it appeared this meat was also overcooked dry and burnt edge.  The curly fries were a delight and thankfully not burnt.Afterwards, we browsed the dessert menu but decided to opt out when suddenly a plate of Birthday Cake Sundae filled with vanilla malt ice cream and frosted confetti cake with a lit birthday candle was provided on the house.  The restaurant is very accommodating to patron's request for special occasions as to celebrate my belated birthday.  The vanilla ice cream and pieces of cake embedded were a delight, but it was certainly too much cake pieces and insufficient ice cream.

During my recent visit to the NYC branch of Ichiran, the anticipation was high given my past extraordinary ramen experience in Japan. The wait was brief, a tolerable 10 minutes, leading to paired seating. The hallmark of this spot is indeed the flavorful broth—enhanced by a dash of vinegar, a personal tip for future patrons. The customization of noodle firmness was an unexpected delight; a complimentary coupon allowed me to savor the ‘firmer’ option, and the taste distinction was evident.

Each diner is treated to a unique solitary booth experience, limiting interactions with staff and fellow diners, though the expected quietude is not always observed by all guests. While the ramen was enjoyable and the dining experience distinctive, the $22 price tag places Ichiran in an occasional visit category, especially given the plethora of other ramen offerings abound in the city.

We came on Labor Day weekend and the wait time was average. It's definitely a lot cleaner than a lot of place in Chinatown. The complimentary dessert option is delicious.  The portion size for each order was very generous. Highly recommended 7/10

Title: Mixed Feelings at Fishmarket - Not Quite Hooked

Despite the buzz on Yelp about Fishmarket, my family's Saturday dinner experience left us swimming in a sea of mediocrity. Greeted by the dive bar ambiance and a cacophony of noise, the setting was more pub than chic eatery, and the worn exterior did little to welcome us with open arms.

The highlight reel includes the aromatic fish soup and the well-seasoned cod with its silky mashed potatoes, as well as a zesty chicken curry that transported us momentarily to Southeast Asia. These dishes proved that Fishmarket can indeed serve up flavorful fare worthy of its name.

However, the meal wasn't without its pitfalls. Portion sizes at Fishmarket play a game of hide and seek, with key items like the fish and chips and calamari playing hard to get amidst breading and soggy chips. The "Yummy Noodles" were a misnomer, delivering a lackluster performance with an overpowering artificiality, while the bok choy was an understated boiled affair one could easily replicate at home.

At around $100 for the entire meal, the value proposition sunk like a stone with the underwhelming dishes. If you do find yourself at Fishmarket, steer your taste buds towards their Asian-inspired selections with caution.

In all, Fishmarket cast a net that was too wide and caught too little. It's a place with potential, but one that might require a more selective approach to navigate its menu successfully.

Title: A Consistent Pleasure at Shalel

Despite my fondness for its former name, which I felt captured the essence of its sultry ambiance, Shalel continues to be a go-to spot for an enchanting evening out. The revamp of the menu has not deterred this gem from delivering an outstanding gastronomic experience.

The restaurant excels at crafting a memorable date night or serving as the perfect retreat for a sophisticated post-dinner drink. The allure of Shalel is evident in the compliments it receives from friends we've introduced to the establishment. They, too, are captivated by its distinctive character and stunning decor.

Above all, the culinary delights are what truly set Shalel apart. Each dish, be it an appetizer, entrée, or dessert, arrives piping hot and bursting with flavor. If you seek a venue that consistently impresses with great food and a mesmerizing atmosphere, Shalel should undoubtedly be on your list.

I've passed by this place so many times thinking "man this place looks great I gotta come here soon" and I haven't for so long but I regret not having gone sooner. They have a great menu and a very nice interior design and setting. I had the spicy night market fried rice which was soooo goooood! I couldn't believe that I've taken this long to come and tastes their food. I wanted pad thai but the fried rice sounded good and it did not let down. Rice was great and it was spicy and I really want to come back to try some more food. Service was fast and there's a lot of tables inside so I wouldn't be too worried about coming and the place being full.
Just stopped in for a drink before dinner and the bartender was not very pleasant. Other than that the place is pretty cute but it was pretty empty.

I was visiting my friend in NYC from SF and wanted to get some good Korean food since SF doesn't have too many good Korean food options. I was going to just go to NY's famous Korea-town for Korean food but our friend highly recommended Oiji. You might at first think Oiji is a fusion Korean restaurant. It is not. It is so authentically Korean in all its flavors yet so contemporary and elevated in the presentation. It's like eating traditional Korean food in new and fun ways, without taking away any of the true Korean food taste. We got the oysters (one of the best oysters I've ever had hands down), fried chicken, jan-jo-rim (this is mind-blowing, a must have), and the spicy pork wraps for two. The pork wrap comes with sticky rice wrapped in lotus leaves which I thoughts was such a modern twist on this Korean dish, executed extremely well. We also tried their cocktails, which were very delicious as well.The only thing that threw us off, hence the 4 stars, was that when we were eating the spicy port wrap dish, the minute the lettuce wraps were gone, one of the waitress came to us immediately and asked if we wanted more. She said it in such a smooth way. We obviously said yes because in Korea, or in any other Korean restaurants, lettuce wraps are something you can always ask for more of. We saw in our bill later that they charged us extra for the lettuce wraps. I found this to be really sly and unfair. She should've at least told us it was extra cost when she so naturally just asked us if we wanted some more. I would've said something but we were in a rush to leave towards the end and she was no where to be found.

Came here with friends for lunch. Quick service l, amazing Thai food. I had the pad see eiw, one friend had red curry and the other had massaman curry. We all had lychee martinis. I had spring rolls and they had fried chicken dumplings. Food was delicious and our bill came out to $60. Not bad at all! Highly recommend this place!

TongKatsu specializes in, unsurprisingly, outstanding katsu dishes that are not to be missed. I had the pleasure of tasting a variety of items, including the Chicken Karage, Chicken Breast Katsu, and Pork Tenderloin Katsu, each accompanied by rice, slaw, TongKatsu sauce, and Japanese pickles—a delightful contrast to the fried fare. The fries with curry sauce, though initially missed, became a highlight once the oversight was corrected.

The kitchen pays attention to detail, ensuring each item is well-drained, preserving the crunch and texture. While the menu heavily leans towards fried options, this is expected of a katsu-centric spot. Among the mains, the Chicken Karage stood out for its succulent dark meat.

Do take note, space is limited in this cozy establishment with about ten seats, so plan ahead. The host's excellent service left a lasting impression, making TongKatsu a go-to destination for those katsu cravings.

Title: A Nostalgic Visit to Burger and Lobster Turns Bittersweet

Having been a frequent visitor of Burger and Lobster years ago, I was eager to indulge once more, this time at their new midtown location. It pains me to say that the experience fell short of my treasured memories. While the lobster's flavor was as remarkable as I remembered, the quantity left much to be desired. At $30, one expects more than just a fleeting encounter with eight modest bites of lobster, despite my prowess in crustacean cracking.

The days of a complete meal being a mere $20 are gone, and unfortunately, so seems the value. Although the lobster roll presents itself as a more reasonable option, the whole lobster no longer justifies its price tag. It's with a heavy heart that I foresee this being my last visit for what was once a beloved dining experience.

I visited this restaurant for lunch and was immediately impressed by the pleasant ambiance. The service was commendable, attentive without being intrusive. As for the food, it was quite satisfying – particularly the pork chop bowl, which boasted a traditional fish marinade and a delightful grilled flavor that felt authentic and well-executed.

The only caveat to my experience was the pricing. It was a bit steep, especially for a lunch setting and when considered against the yardstick of typical Vietnamese fare. Nonetheless, if you find yourself here, I'd recommend trying the pork chop bowl despite the prices. It's a well-crafted dish that stands out.

I really like the atmosphere here. It is dimly lit and very small inside with cozy booths. The drinks are very good and I enjoyed the astoria martini.  We had the king crab and oysters for appetizers and both were good. The prime rib was cooked rare which I did not care for, it was quite underwhelming overall. The sundae dessert was disappointing, the "hot fudge" was just chocolate sauce. The service was poor and our dinner took almost 3 hours.

Went to 5 Napkin Burger for brunch with friends. The location was great, we were able to make a reservation online before coming so we were seated right away. I'm vegetarian so I had the impossible burger which was really good. I liked that they offer $16 bottomless mimosas during brunch, that's such a great deal in NYC! Rating 3 stars because the service was so very slow. It was never clear who our waiter was because we had 3 different people who came to wait on our table. We also felt rushed out of the restaurant towards the end, my water glass had been empty for a while and rather than filling it, one of the three waiters came and took it away. Service aside, I would be back because I'm a sucker for burgers and fries!

Title: Second Visit Solidified My Love for This Gem!

I recently revisited a local restaurant for the second time, and my experience was fantastic. I highly recommend starting off with their breadsticks—delicious, but be warned, the portion may leave you wanting more.

My first visit involved a minor hiccup with the beignets which, to my brother's surprise, were undercooked rather than filled. However, the second visit was a stellar redemption. Dining in for dinner, the staff was exceptionally friendly, and the meal portions generous.

Opt for the individual-sized plates over the family-sized, as they offer plenty of food, especially when shared with a selection of appetizers. Their pasta dishes are hearty and satisfying, perfect for any Italian cuisine enthusiast.

The sundae was an ambitious and delightful attempt to conclude the meal, even though we couldn't quite finish it. Lastly, a heartfelt thank you to the team who accommodated my special request to congratulate my boyfriend on his academic success with a personalized note on the dessert plate. Such thoughtful gestures make a dining experience truly memorable.

I was pleasantly surprised with my lunch at Peak Thai today, so I'm going to award them 4 stars, and maybe that'll encourage some folks to give it a shot. The lunch specials start at $10.95. I ordered the drunken noodles with chicken, extra spicy. A few minutes later, the waitress brought out my starters, an egg roll and a small salad. Nothing fancy; modest and enjoyable. Next, the noodle dish. The serving size is hefty, though not outrageous. The noodles were soft without being mushy. There weren't a ton of vegetables: I could have done with more tomatoes, some bell peppers. The flavors were great and the textures worked harmoniously. Nicely done. For a randomly chosen lunch spot, Peak Thai treated me well.

KBQQ is good. Actually, it's great. But have you ever had it as take out? Me neither. While searching for some Korean food on Seamless, Samwon came up as an option that was pretty well rated. However, most people get the stews. Understandable. Who wants to eat grilled meats that's been sitting in a box for an hour. After all, KBBQ is best eaten there.I ordered the spicy short rib stew. Do not make the mistake that I did! This already comes with rice and a box of banchan! I probably missed it when ordering but I didn't think it came with anything and ordered it just to be safe. The stew itself had several chunks of short ribs that maybe made up one whole beef rib. As with any Korean stew, this had that pleasurable spice factor and good for the soul type taste. If you're in the mood for some Korean soups/stews, this is your spot.

Title: A Pho-nomenal Find in NYC!

As a fresh New York City transplant on a mission to satisfy my pho cravings, I've finally hit the jackpot close to my new abode. This gem stands out as the premier pho spot among the contenders I've sampled thus far, offering an experience that beckons for repeat visits.

The warmth of the staff complements the consistently delectable food, ensuring a pleasant dining atmosphere each time. My go-to order, the vegetarian pho paired with vegetarian summer rolls, is a testament to the kitchen's prowess. They've mastered the art of a robust, flavorful broth—a feat often unachieved with vegetable bases.

Anticipation bubbles at the thought of introducing this culinary delight to my like-minded, pho-enthusiast friends on their upcoming city sojourns. This establishment is without a doubt my newfound pho-tastic haven in NYC!

The bread roll was probably my favorite part! Put me into a food coma right after. I got the shrimp roll jumbo, which means there's more shrimp than just the regular one. It was really good especially because there was also some sauce on it that went great with the roll. Next time I'd want to try the trio!

Fun and buzzy. An electric take on Taiwanese food, which makes it fun for friends or a date. We ordered the following: Oyster Omelette: I was probably most excited for this childhood classic. It was okay and there was a lot going on. Tapioca flour made for a nice, sticky texture, but it didn't feel or taste like an omelette. Would love to see more egg. I wasn't hugely a fan of all the bean sprouts and ketchup. Sausage Patty: The sausage was objectively good, but the sticky rice didn't land for me. The delivery was cute and they shaped the sticky rice like a hot dog bun, but the flavor wasn't there. Too bland. Lo Ba Beng: Surprisingly my favorite dish. It was a flavorful pork dish topped with bamboo shoots and an egg. Simple, but tasty. I would come again and try other items. Reasonably priced and nice service.

Title: Stellar BBQ and Exceptional Service at Hill Country Amidst Pandemic

As a long-standing admirer of Hill Country, I’ve consistently enjoyed their delectable BBQ, robust drinks, and the exuberant vibe. Recently, I snagged a fantastic Pulsd deal promising a feast of Pitmaster dinners and drinks at a steal. Despite the COVID-19 restrictions impacting dining experiences, Hill Country impressed me by honoring their Pulsd deals for pickup orders.

Taking advantage of the offer, I picked up our meals with a touch of disappointment turned to delight. Their commitment to customer service shone, extending the validity of vouchers for future dine-in opportunities. The pick-up process was seamless, and the Hill Country team greeted us warmly, even accommodating our drinks for the road.

Sampling the food at home, the brisket remained the standout, retaining its mouthwatering juiciness and rich flavor. Every bite reminded me why Hill Country holds a special place in my culinary heart.

A heartfelt thank you to Hill Country for not only providing a comforting and satisfying meal during trying times but also for showing resilience and adaptability. Their gesture serves as a reminder to support local businesses as we navigate the challenges presented by the pandemic.

Rating: 5/5 - For the impeccable food and the exceptional service that goes above and beyond.

Barn Joo is a very cute restaurant with some great food. The soju drinks are tasty. I had the Omurice: the beef was cooked and eggs were delicious. My friend and I also shared the churros for dessert. They were served with graham cracker crumbs and ice cream. Delicious! A definite must visit.

I came across this cafe while walking On Amsterdam Avenue. As I approached the waiter, he told me that all the tables inside were full, however he had a table available outside. Considering that it was a nice afternoon, I thought it would be wonderful to sit outside. Little did I know, I was in for a huge disappointment. In fact-being disappointed is an understatement. I was sat at a table that had an obtrusive waste pipe in the middle. It was so obnoxious. I requested another table and Sadly, The waiter was unable to accommodate me anywhere else although there was availability outside. After placing my order, I didn't see the waiter again until it was time to pay for my meal. My entree was great but the service was poor which takes away from the entire experience.

Last night, post-fireworks and a crowded subway journey, my dining companion and I were fortunate to find this 24-hour gem. After a reasonable 20-minute wait via their kiosk system, we were seated in what turned out to be a delightful dining spot. The concept is simple yet satisfying: choose your broth and enjoy an assortment of add-ins along with a bowl of noodles – with the bonus of free noodle refills and a complimentary first soda.

We savored the coconut curry broth, which offered a touch of spice and paired wonderfully with both the add-ins and noodles. The pork comes standard, but alternatives including vegetarian options are available for a small extra charge. The meal proved not only delicious but also an excellent value – hearty and wallet-friendly.

The only hiccup was an outdated Yelp check-in offer promising 20% off, which had expired back in 2019. So, a word to the wise: double-check those offers' fine print before planning to use them. Nonetheless, the overall experience was a hit – definitely a spot worth visiting for a late-night meal.
