Tucked away in northern East Village, The Athenian is a charming Greek wine bar by the same folks behind The Immigrant. It’s a snug space, with about 10 bar seats, that sees a continuous flow of patrons. My boyfriend and I chose this spot for a weekday date and were met with amiable service, particularly when navigating their selection of natural Greek wines. We sampled a couple, each unique and pleasing without boasting top-shelf status.

The fare, surprisingly robust for a wine bar, ranged from dips to meatballs to seafood. We shared a few plates – the cuisine was consistently good, though not extraordinary, with the exception of the succulent shrimp and octopus dishes. Both left a memorable impression with their ample, flavorful portions.

The final bill was steep for the laid-back ambiance, averaging around $50 per person. Despite the price point, The Athenian is a warm, family-run establishment that’s definitely worth a visit.

We came here for brunch this past weekend and we were a little underwhelmed. Especially the amount you pay for what you get. We both got the American breakfast with a side of sausage gravy. The slab bacon was quite tasty. The breakfast potatoes and eggs were very ordinary. The biscuit was decent for one in NYC. Very buttery. When I asked for jam, the guy came back and said sorry for taking so long because they just made it fresh In the back. I was pretty impressed with that. The gravy was very meh. It tasted more like gravy you have at thanksgiving than anything. And then we ended up paying about $60 for everything (not drinks, just coffee) which is just too much for all that in my opinion.

Title: A Casual Bite at Andrew's Coffee Shop

After trekking from Philly with heavy luggage in tow, the welcoming exterior of Andrew's Coffee Shop was a sight for sore eyes. Contrary to its name, the interior screamed diner — simple but sparkling clean, with a promise for a quick sit-down.

The menu seemed standard, so we played it safe. We split a pepperoni pizza that, despite its size, was surprisingly fresh. The "disco fries" were a letdown, crying out for seasoning and cheese distribution. My very berry smoothie was an acquired taste, thick and slushy, but ultimately thirst-quenching.

In summary, Andrew's is your go-to for no-frills, decent eats in Manhattan. It's a solid 3/5 — not exceptional but convenient for a basic meal. Would I return? If I'm in the area with a craving for simplicity, sure. Just don't expect culinary fireworks.

Title: A Japanese Delight Post-Anime at West 4th

After soaking in the whimsical wonders of "Penguin Highway" at the IFC Theater, my family and I ventured to satisfy our Japanese cravings at a nearby spot I stumbled upon on Yelp.

The moment we stepped inside, the spacious and brightly lit ambiance warmly welcomed us. Even without reservations, we were swiftly seated in a comfortable four-seater, eager to dive into the menu.

I opted for the pork cutlet with egg over rice, accompanied by miso soup and pickled cucumber—a seemingly large presentation in the box that was deceptively portioned. Despite this, the $16 price tag felt justifiable for the enjoyable experience.

My son's search for ramen ended in compromise with the nabeyaki udon with shrimp tempura, which proved to be a savory delight "to the last drop". Adding a mini chirashi for a mere $7 extra rendered our meal a steal, with an assortment of fresh sushi that tickled our taste buds.

My wife went for the gluten-free soba with chicken curry, encountering an additional but reasonable $3.50 for her dietary needs. The portion appeared modest, yet the dish won her over, the chicken notably bursting with flavor, both filling and satisfying.

The friendly waitstaff added to our overall delightful dining experience. If you find yourself in a Japanese state of mind around West 4th Street, this place comes highly recommended for its inviting atmosphere and tasty fare.
Hand over a dollar and they'll make you a hot slice of cheese pizza! Simple and cheap, and was pleasantly surprised by the quality.

I am rating this for the bar scene only.  It is a cool trendy modern feel to it in the heart of Koreatown.  I love that they have kegs of Hite to order at the table.  They do run so show up early if you want HITE.  The service is great, the ambiance is a chill relaxing place.  A perfect place to take a date before a basketball game or before or after dinner.

This is a new diner that opened in the Soho Grand Hotel, but one of those serving "elevated diner fare", and it's all really good.It's a fun retro diner atmosphere that will surprisingly be open 24 hours. The fries are great, and accompany the also excellent Beef on Weck that you should definitely try. The Rigatoni is also a solid choice, as is the Ham Steak & Eggs.

I wish I liked this place better but the prices just threw me off completely. 2 mini tacos for $11 is too over priced. Why? My fish taco had 1 tiny piece of fish the size of an Oreo (see picture). It didn't fill me up at all and I'm a pretty small person. This isn't your average mexican restaurant where they offer you free chips and salsa either. Nope. Had to pay extra $8 for chips and salsa . It'd be $12 if we included guacamole which is so crazy to me. I will say the food was very flavorful, the salsa verde on the fish tacos topped it pretty well. However, their servings can't justify their prices. This isn't a high end fancy restaurant where the servings are supposed to be small. You're better off finding a Mexican restaurant around the city that offers free chips and salsa. You'll get a better run for your money with better stomach filling tacos.

I had a wonderful experience ordering from this restaurant through DoorDash. The packaging was impressive, sealed thoughtfully with a sticker indicating it was handled with care, which was reassuring. I ordered the bulgogi stew and the CDG japchae, and both dishes were absolutely delicious. A delightful surprise was the inclusion of traditional side dishes with the bulgogi stew, just like you'd get when dining in at the restaurant. I highly recommend this place for a taste of authenticity and quality!

We came here around noon on a Sunday and it was packed but we just had to wait 10mins to be seated.  This is a very dog-friendly restaurant and they give all the dogs water bowls. The menu was extensive and the portions were good. I got the Greek Omelette which came with salad and a bread basket. The Blueberry Pancakes were also delicious, much thicker than normal pancakes, but very filling and good. I would definitely come back to try more of their lunch dishes, the small plates and hummus looked amazing.

I visited a bustling eatery on a Saturday night at 8:30pm, greeted by a crowd due to the front-ordering system before seating. Once settled in the spacious downstairs area, it took about 20-30 minutes for our food to arrive, during which free Wi-Fi was a welcome amenity given the poor cell reception.

Our meal consisted of squid and pork sisig with garlic rice, accompanied by crispy pata. While generous in portion, suitable for our party of three, it proved to be a rather heavy selection. The sisig, in particular, was excessively crunchy to the point where the meat's texture was lost—suggesting perhaps an overzealous approach to frying. I'd recommend against pairing these three fried dishes in one sitting, as it made for an overwhelmingly greasy experience.

I mean let's be real. The pizza is $1. No tax. Cash only. $1. To me this is the nyc experience. Go get a slice, put so many toppings on it that you can no longer see the cheese, and prepare for an amazing experience.

Title: A Hidden Gem Just Off Union Square - LAUT

Whenever I face the daunting wait times at other local eateries, I find solace at LAUT, a vibrant haven that never disappoints. Tucked away near Union Square, this restaurant boasts the hippest decor around, replete with eye-catching wall adornments that add to its allure. There's a buzz that even the legendary Anthony Bourdain has stopped by, giving it a subtle nod on their menu.

The Nasi Lemak I ordered, Malaysia’s national dish, is a masterclass in flavor, offering a satisfying variety that tantalizes the taste buds. My companions, who've indulged in the pad thai, can vouch for its authenticity and tastiness. It’s a testament to LAUT’s consistency that everyone in my group leaves content every single time.

What sets LAUT apart is the manageable wait time, a rare luxury in this part of town. For a delectable feast that's sure to impress without the long lines, I couldn't recommend LAUT more!

Whenever I find myself back in New York, a visit to this Italian chain with German roots is a must. The unique service starts the moment you enter; a scan card is handed to you, keeping track of your orders—a clever touch.

Craving pizza and salad, I beelined to the pizza station and chose the Diavlo—a decision I didn't regret. Topped with the right amount of pepperoni, onions, and friggitellos, it provided a delightful heat that wasn't overpowering. The standout, however, was the pizza dough: thin and crispy, just as I prefer.

The salad that accompanied my pizza was equally satisfying—the portion was perfect, the dressing was light, and the cherry tomatoes added a burst of freshness. A simple, efficient dining experience capped by a swift checkout with the card. This place is a testament to how simplicity often leads to perfection when it comes to good food.

Title: Exceptional Pizza at Roberta's, Seating a Dicey Game

My experience at this Roberta's outpost could easily warrant a 10-star rating based solely on their sublime pizza. However, I've settled on a solid 4-star review because of the food hall's limited seating options, which can be quite challenging for groups. My party and I found securing a table to be unpredictable. That said, the service did not disappoint; it was both swift and personable. 

Although you might notice prices are a tad above average, the pizza quality more than justifies the cost. And don't leave without trying the garlic knots—they're an irresistible treat at $2 apiece and worth every penny. In short, Roberta's delivers an outstanding pizza experience if you can navigate the seating situation.

Title: A Slice of Perfection at a Cozy Pizza Haven

From the moment you join the eager queue that often spills onto the sidewalk, you know you're in for a treat at this charming pizza joint, which easily ranks among my top three favorites. Despite its compact interior and the scramble for the limited seating, the anticipation only heightens the eventual delight.

I went classic with a plain cheese pizza, while my companions opted for the square pepperoni slices—each choice turned out to be a masterpiece of flavor. The house sodas provided a refreshing complement to the savory bites, marking another win for the establishment.

Our table was abuzz with praise; we simply couldn't stop raving about our delicious experience throughout our trip. For anyone in search of pizza perfection, this spot is a must-visit. A flawless 10/10, I wholeheartedly recommend a visit to this little gem.

Title: Lukewarm Experience at Budget Slice Joint

Unfortunately, I found the latest dollar slice contender in NYC to fall short of expectations. Unlike the reigning champion, Percy's, the pizza here disappoints with a soggy crust and an overwhelming saltiness that distracts from any authentic flavor. While I acknowledge the allure of a one-dollar slice, there are other spots offering more bang for your buck in both taste and quality.

On the service front, it was passable - not exceptional, but not deserving of any particular criticism. Beverages follow the economical theme, with cans of soda also priced at a dollar, maintaining the budget-friendly vibe.

However, the cleanliness of the place leaves much to be desired. The lack of tidiness fails to create a welcoming atmosphere, further detracting from the overall dining experience. If you're searching for a quick, cheap pizza fix and cleanliness is not a priority, this might fit the bill. But if you're hoping for that perfect blend of frugality and flavor, you'll want to keep looking.

First time having Ethiopian food.  I didn't know what to expect.  This place is awesome! I had the beef Samosas for the appetizer and the combination platter for the entree.  The samosas are delicious and not too spicy.  The combination platter for 2 comes with 4 vegetarian and 4 meat options.  The platter comes with wraps to use to scoop up the food.  I preferred eating with the a fork because I didn't like the taste of the wrap.  The wrap has a sour taste and it was changing the taste of the food.  The food tasted delicious when I ate with the fork!! I also had the honey wine .  Absolutely delicious! The service is great.  Very friendly and attentive.  This place is very small so I would say make a reservation before hand or come on a week day.  Highly recommend checking this place out!

Title: A Delightful Upscale Twist on Traditional Asian Cuisine at Hunan Slurp

Hunan Slurp offers a refined departure from the bustling Chinatown eateries, presenting traditional Asian dishes in an elegant setting perfect for a date night. The serene and well-appointed dining room enhances the experience without compromising the authenticity and robust flavors one would expect from Asian cuisine.

The fish mifen was a standout, boasting a savory broth that I couldn't resist finishing – a testament to its deliciousness despite the potential sodium overload. Diners should note, however, that care is necessary as the fish may contain small bones. 

The appetizer, playfully mislabeled as a "salad," comprised photogenic eggplant rolls with a pleasantly spicy stuffing – a dish I would happily recommend. Accompanying our meal with a shared pot of tea, the dinner was satisfying, with the final bill amounting to a reasonable $35 per person before tip.

While the experience was largely positive, I did encounter an all-too-common policy that can detract from the welcome: the insistence on not seating partial parties, even in a visibly quiet restaurant with ample seating and a reservation in hand. This minor annoyance aside, Hunan Slurp is certainly worth a visit for those looking to elevate their Asian dining experience without forgoing flavor.

I recently made a spontaneous visit to a local Chinese restaurant, and it turned out to be a delightful experience. We arrived just as the staff were finishing their own meals, indicating that we were early birds. After pondering over the concise menu, my companion and I decided to share a dish of sautéed rice cakes with chicken in a traditional sauce. Initially concerned about the portion size, we were pleasantly surprised by the ample serving, perfect for a light meal for two but also sufficient for a hearty eater alone.

The dish had a kick of spice, particularly toward the bottom where the sauce pooled, yet it remained palatable for those with milder taste preferences. The rice cakes themselves were a highlight, their bouncy texture complemented by robust flavor. Even the chicken breast, often at risk of dryness, was succulent and tasty.

This place is definitely on my radar for future visits—especially to try the big plate chicken that caught my eye. Anyone looking for good Chinese cuisine should give this spot a try when they're in the neighborhood.
The food here is not bad. It's pretty good. I would like to come back and try other things on the menu.

Awesome vegan place in Chelsea! Our group ordered two mushroom appetizers and pasta dishes for the dinner. The flavors were on point. I specifically loved the mushroom scallop-imitation appetizer and the main truffle pasta dish. The tiramisu dessert also didn't disappoint- the coconut flavor was very refreshing.I also loved the feel of this place. We sat upstairs and it felt like we're in someone's cozy home. The wait staff was nice and welcoming too. It felt good to sit around, eat delicious food, talk with your friends, and enjoy a cup of tea. I'll be back!

Title: A Slice Above the Rest!

If pizza perfection is what you crave, then look no further! This gem offers both by-the-slice indulgence and whole pie satisfaction, all dished out by the friendliest staff around. With a diverse menu that guarantees a swift grab-and-go experience, this place rivals—even surpasses—the big-name pizzerias. Each bite bursts with the delectable taste of expertly crafted dough and savory sauce. Trust me; you won't leave disappointed. A must-visit for all pizza connoisseurs!

Nami Nori aims for innovation in their hand roll selection but doesn't quite hit the mark. The chef's set of 5 temaki featured salmon, yellowtail, a vegan option, a California roll, and sea bass. While the fish offered decent quality, it failed to leave a lasting impression. The hand rolls were unfortunately dominated by the sauce, which overshadowed the natural flavors of the seafood. The inclusion of wasabi, and in generous amounts, was less than pleasing. For a more balanced and enjoyable hand roll experience, my recommendation would be to try KazuNori instead.

Title: A Tale of Two Experiences at Ted's

Upon visiting Ted's, drawn by the polarizing reviews, I found myself pleasantly surprised by their unique take on oysters, which were a delightful meld of traditional and bold with the addition of sliced jalapeños and citrus segments. They were a fresh and scrumptious start to the meal.

However, the spicy cauliflower failed to live up to its name, lacking the promised heat, and the truffle flatbread was underwhelming. Despite the promise of truffles, the flatbread seemed lackluster and reminiscent of something pre-made. The mushrooms added little excitement to the dish, and the sparing use of truffle oil couldn't elevate the experience.

On a positive note, the service shone brightly, with excellent attention from the bartender who made our visit more enjoyable. However, there was a slight dip in attentiveness once our entrees were served, as no one checked back to gather our thoughts on the meal.

In conclusion, Ted's is the spot for innovative oyster enthusiasts, but those in search of a more fulfilling dining experience might consider looking elsewhere.

Title: A Comforting Udon Heaven in SoHo - Raku

Raku stands out as a cozy SoHo gem, perfect for savoring a hot bowl of udon on chilly days. I indulged in the curry beef udon—truly comforting with its profoundly flavorful broth and delightfully chewy noodles. This Japanese eatery is a haven for udon enthusiasts, offering both steamy and chilled versions, alongside rice bowls and an array of starters.

The serving sizes are generous, sure to satisfy the hungriest of souls and perhaps even usher you into a blissful food coma. The agedashi tofu we sampled was equally impressive, a must-try. Price-wise, Raku hits the sweet spot with reasonable rates for its location.

A tip for potential visitors: use Resy to snag a reservation. We faced a 30-minute wait at 6:30 pm on a weekday, but the text notification for walk-ins is quite convenient. Service didn't disappoint; we enjoyed prompt and amiable attention throughout our meal. In summary, Raku is a delightful spot for beautifully crafted Japanese comfort food.

Upon escaping a sudden downpour, my senses were immediately embraced by the vibrant atmosphere of this charming Cuban hub, where the rhythm of a live band set the tone for an unforgettable dining experience. Renowned for their Mojitos, the energy was as intoxicating as their signature drinks. Opting for a twist, I savored a Watermelon Margarita—an expertly crafted concoction starting with a bold statement and softening into a sweet finale.

The culinary journey continued with a salad drizzled in a tangy vinaigrette, striking a perfect balance with the succulence of my shrimp entree. The star, however, was the appetizer, served with a garlic sauce that was nothing short of heavenly—a unanimous sensation among my dining companions.

Regrettably, the presence of an uninvited fly was the sole blemish on an otherwise perfect evening. Nevertheless, this minor disturbance hardly dampened the allure of this vibrant eatery. A strong 4 out of 5 stars, without question.

Title: Mixed Impressions at a Trendy Spot

I recently visited a well-talked-about restaurant with a 6:15pm reservation on a quiet Wednesday. Seated upstairs, we missed the charming balloon lights of the first floor but were greeted by an alternative ceiling décor. The intimacy of the space was quite pronounced, with tables closely packed, almost inviting neighboring diners into our conversation.

Regrettably, the service lagged, likely burdened on the solo server attending to the upper level. However, the kitchen was prompt, and our starters arrived swiftly. The pork belly, lacking the anticipated crispness, was nonetheless enjoyable alongside its pickled companions.

My roasted duck noodles necessitated a liberal application of sriracha to combat its inherent blandness, and even then, the dish teetered towards too salty. Conversely, my boyfriend's Khao Soi was a delight with its rich curry broth; although, the late-coming heat might deter the spice-averse.

In sum, our experience was unremarkable, and it's my feeling that there are more compelling venues for Asian cuisine. While the ambiance may beckon the social media savvy, the culinary journey here is less likely to inspire return visits.

The pizza is actually really good. Definitely tastey fresh and has flavor I would give them 5 stars easy.However I ordered a pie to go half cheese half roni and Italian sausage and to me the sausage needed to be better cooked and smaller pieces. The pepperoni was great and there was a lot of it too. The second big pit may have been my fault but it was soggy when I got home. The cheese had slid all the way off which was probably my fault but the pie it's self needs to be cooked longer. I like a stiff pie what can I say ;-). Next time I'll just ask for it to be crispy and I'm hoping that will do the trickBut I cashed out a nice size pie for $23Awesome addition the the neighborhoodThere's two stools to sit on but there really isn't any space at all. As soon as there's 5 people ordering it's feeling a little pack ratty. It's literally in and out

Title: A Satisfactory Visit to Haile: Missing the Charm of West Village

My search for a replacement for my beloved, now-closed Ethiopian spot in West Village led me and friends to Haile on a bustling Saturday evening. The foresight to reserve a table paid off as we bypassed a waiting line and were seated promptly at 6:30 pm.

Each of us dove into Haile's varied combination platters – a thoughtful offering catering to vegetarians, the meat-inclined, and carnivores alike. While the dining experience was competent, the dishes failed to reach the flavorful heights of my old West Village haunt.

In conclusion, Haile served as a decent Ethiopian eatery for a group dinner downtown, but it didn't leave a strong enough impression to warrant a return visit, unless my cravings for Ethiopian cuisine grow urgent.

My friend has been wanting to check Sanpoutei out for a while now since it seems to be getting good attention in Chinese media. A group of four of us were finally able to go recently, and I couldn't help but be a little disappointed.Sanpoutei is known for their niboshi shoyu ramen, which is a fish-based broth that is lighter than the normal pork-based broth many other ramen places use. The flavors were simple and clean, but I honestly missed the fattiness and creaminess of a good tonkotsu broth. This is probably just pure personal preference. I did enjoy their noodles which are made in-house and had a great texture. However, it was a bit odd that we couldn't add-on extra noodles at a small cost like at other ramen shops.We of course also had to try their gyoza considering that it is in their name after all. We got both the pork gyoza and beef gyoza. The pork gyoza was great --- crunchy thin skin on the outside, moist and flavorful filling on the inside. The beef gyoza was just OK and not worth the added expense ($3 more expensive than the pork gyoza).The restaurant itself is surprisingly big and has very classy decor -- simple, modern, and clean. Definitely worth checking out if you enjoy niboshi fish-based broth, but fans of tonkotsu pork-based ramen might be a bit disappointed.

Quick, Cheap, and Tasty. What more do you need? For just $5-$8 depending on what size food you want, you can get a whole meal's worth of delicious food. Don't be scared away by the line, the workers are incredibly efficient and you'll be there before you know it. If you are in the area, you MUST stop by here. They've received lots of publicity and are really famous for their roast pork which I highly recommend. Get the sauce on top too! Would definitely come here if I was in the area :) (Also it is not a sit down and eat place, it is a grab and go hence, fast food).Food: 5/5 Price: 5/5

I recently ordered a spicy noodle lunch special with tofu through the Ritual app from this restaurant and the dish exceeded my expectations in flavor and quality. However, there was a downside to my experience as my order was incomplete; both the spring roll and salad that were supposed to accompany my noodles were omitted. While the food itself is commendable, the service fell short on attention to detail. If the service improves to match the standard of their cuisine, I'd be more inclined to return.

Had really good breakfast sandwich! Great customer service, but thought the items were a bit on the pricy side. I had the classic sandwich and loved the combination of the spicy aioli and the fried shallots. If you're okay with the price, def budget around $10 per person and you should be good.
Great spot to have ippudo without the long wait. Delicious and satisfying. Although not as plentiful as the large location still as delicious and fast!

The only thing modern about this place is the decor and not the food. I don't understand the high rating at all. Some reviewers said this was the best Chinese food they have ever eaten. Please, hop on a taxi and go to Chinatown instead. Wanting a quick dinner before we head back to New Jersey, we decided to try this place because the menu looked promising.Here is what we ordered: - Braised Duck Dumplings (sounds good, right)?- Asparagus with garlic sauce- Fish Fillet w/ginger & scallionThe only thing good about the duck dumplings is how pretty they wrapped it. Tastewise, I didn't like the texture of the wrap and I could not tell that I was eating duck. The flavor was weird and we all didn't like the brown sauce that it came with. What was even worse were the two entrees that followed. Both dishes were heavily laden with brown sauce. So much so that it tastes like sugar. Huge disappointment when there are many other choices we could have gone to.Service-wise, the host and waiters/waitress could barely crack a smile. Let me rephrase that, they didn't smile at all.

Upon entering the restaurant, one can't help but notice the peculiar ambiance set by the pervasive pink lighting, which gives the space a surreal quality (refer to my photos for a glimpse). The menu offerings were acceptable but unremarkable. The Dragon Roll, a standard fare in Japanese dining, was competently prepared but didn't distinguish itself from countless other establishments. The Gyoza had a decent taste, though the filling could have been more tightly packed. As for the Fried Octopus, it fell into the common trap of relying on frozen seafood, resulting in a dish that was rather typical of basic fried offerings. In summary, the dining experience here was average: not disappointing, but not particularly exciting either.

I recently visited a Mediterranean quick-service restaurant for a friend's birthday lunch, and the experience was pleasantly efficient. The birthday girl chose the spot, and the expansive menu offered a satisfying variety of options to assemble our meals.

The chicken soup, sampled by my husband and friend's mother, was a hit, praised for its deliciousness. My husband and friend opted for the lamb bowl entrees that came with a choice of two sides – a feature that allows for some customization. While I found the lamb just satisfactory, with its diced pieces not quite hitting the mark for me, my own plate of shrimp with brown rice, beets, and vegetables was quite enjoyable.

The seating area accommodated us comfortably, reflecting the establishment's capability to host a fair number of guests. Overall, the restaurant offered a straightforward and quick take on Mediterranean dishes. While not every item was a standout, the place is undoubtedly a solid choice for a casual lunch with a diverse menu to please different palates.

Stepping into this charming breakfast-lunch eatery was like a nostalgic journey to a cozy small-town diner, with walls adorned with antiques and an inviting display of cakes. The food truly captured the essence of home cooking—simple, hearty fare that's satisfying without unnecessary frills. My choice of corned beef hash was generous in portion and deliciously reminiscent of a homemade meal. The whipped butter served alongside was notably exceptional. My companion's French toast had an eye-catching allure that promises to be the highlight of my next visit. Service was smooth, save for a slight delay awaiting the check. Overall, a delightful dining experience that beckons a return.
Got the chicken shawarma for lunch on MealPal and it was really good! Chicken was juicy and the pita was warm and soft. Pretty filling and well seasoned!

Came here on a Friday night and this place was packed. The wait was the main issue I had as they had a waitlist where we put our names on a clipboard, but the staff didn't really follow it and just pulled whatever groups were waiting. That means some of the groups that just walked in were seated immediately while other's who were there for 30 minutes were still standing around still waiting to be seated.We started out with appetizers and got Sweet Potato Fries and Shrimp Tempura. The Sweet Potato Fries came with a spicy sambai mayo dipping sauce which I enjoyed. The Shrimp Tempura was served on top of a cabbage salad which tasted great because of all the creamy mentaiko mayo they put on top of the appetizer. For ramen, I got the Spicy Miso Ramen. They gave you a warning on the menu that it's super spicy, but it's not too overwhelming for those spicy enthusiast. It will make you sweat, I'll give it that. My gf got the Koku Ramen which is their signature ramen. This is slightly spicy which balances out well with the rich creamy broth it comes with.The food is pretty good overall. What this place needs to work on is the service and crowd management as they do not do a very good job in this category. Otherwise, this place has the potential to be a great ramen shop.

Title: "Uninspiring Eats at an Average Spot"

If you're on the hunt for an exceptional dining experience in NYC, you might want to skip this establishment. The service was passable and the interior acceptable, but the food left much to be desired. My panini's mozzarella was strangely unmelted and unnaturally white, raising suspicions of a microwave mishap. And the chicken was tough to the point of being impenetrable by a serrated knife. In a city bursting with culinary delights, this place doesn't quite make the cut for a dinner stop.

Walked in with a couple friends on a Friday evening (around 8:45pm) and had to wait about 5-10 min for a table of 3. They were preparing a table inside, but we saw an open one outside, next to the front doors and asked if we could sit there instead. Thankfully they let us, as it was the perfect night to be dining alfresco. We got chips and guac ($16.50) for the table to start, salsa on the side. My friend told me that they usually prepare the guac right in front of us (cut the avocados, etc.) if we were sitting inside... unfortunately I didn't get to experience that since there was limited space outside. Defff pricey for what it was but I guess average compared to similar moderately upscale Mexican chains in NYC.One friend got the Flautas de Pollo ($10.75) but he wasn't a fan of it, and the other got the Carnitas entree ($25.50), which came with a small side of rice and beans - her usual. Big portions and I wanted to try some especially since it's her favorite dish, but I was too stuffed from my order, the Pescado Baja / fish tacos ($19.50). I didn't know what to expect since the menu said it'd just be 3 tacos, but they were HUGE and came with a side of creamy corn salad. Disappointingly, the pieces of fish were grossly battered / deep fried yet bland and unseasoned, so the corn was desperately needed for flavor + texture. I also felt my heart + body get heavier and heavier as I finished the second taco, and absolutely couldn't finish the third. It just made me feel awful and it wasn't worth it at all. Would recommend the restaurant to grill the fish instead or lightly fry please... ugh. Maybe I could've requested the modification?Service was ok but a little on the slower side. We weren't in a rush so we didn't mind.

Came here for brunch and I got their golden folded eggs ($15) and it was yummy! I love their sourdough toast and the eggs were cooked very deliciously. This place is great if you are looking for very healthy brunch/lunch options. It's very cute inside although it's pretty small so you may have to wait a bit on the weekends.

Back in Harlem again,& had to stop at my favorite fish joint. Had the All-Fish, which comes with 2 slices of whole wheat bread. The 2 slices don't stand a chance against all that fish. You literally can get 2 maybe 2 1/2 fish sandwiches out of The All Fish.my wife decided to have the Fish and Chips she could only finish half of her order, kept asking me to eat some of these fries...I couldn't help her ,I'm trying to finish mine. As usual it was all so delicious and well seasoned. We also had a cup of SWEET TEA & LEMONADE. When I say SWEET,I mean SWEET. If you're a diabetic,I advise you to govern yourself accordingly. You can't go wrong with any of the food here. Now, one more thing there is no parking area just Street parking,however  cars were double and even triple parking,and Today I saw New York's Finest rolling up in their MARKED CARS & were writing tickets to occupied  vehicles and putting them on the windshield of said vehicle,I saw one lady coming out with her order and the officer handed her a ticket. So if you're going to order leave an adult in the vehicle (preferably a license driver). I was told by the officer he was just looking for unoccupied vehicles double parked today. So heed the warning.

Title: A Satisfying Bite for Every Palette at Bareburger

I recently revisited Bareburger for the first time since 2016, and it's safe to say their culinary prowess with burgers is still spot on. Nestled in a busy spot, they managed to accommodate us promptly on a bustling Saturday afternoon.

The menu is a haven for variety, catering to both vegan and non-vegan preferences with an impressive array of customizable options. My choice, a beyond burger adorned with faux bacon and crisp lettuce, hit the mark, capturing the essence of a hearty, plant-based patty. Sharing a side of French fries and onion rings, it was the latter that took the spotlight—striking a delectable balance between crunch and tenderness.

While the fries were tasty in their own right, the onion rings undoubtedly stole the show. Bareburger's dedication to pleasing diverse tastes is commendable, and the attentive service only enhanced the dining experience. The chain's expansion to places like Buffalo would be a welcome treat.

Recommendation: For a universally appealing eatery with a knack for crafting both vegan and traditional fares, Bareburger is a top contender.

Title: A Thai Gem with Authentic Flavors

Review:

My recent visit to this Thai restaurant was an exceptional 4.5 out of 5 experience, marred only slightly by an unwelcoming host who mistakenly insisted we couldn't have a pre-dinner drink at the bar. However, this misstep was quickly overshadowed by the extraordinary Monday night that followed.

The moment we stepped in for a birthday celebration, the ambiance transported us straight to Thailand, with classy, gorgeous decor and a private cabana-style table that added to the exotic charm. Our server, possibly named Jay, struck the perfect balance of attentiveness.

Starting with drinks, we moved on to a selection of starters and entrees that were nothing short of wonderful. As someone with a background in Thai culinary arts, I can vouch for the authenticity of their delectable Thai Iced Tea and the Red Curry, while the freshness of the Branzino stood out. A special nod goes to the Chicken in Pandan leaves, a rare find that did not disappoint.

We concluded with desserts, including a taro-based treat, which was nicely adorned for the birthday occasion, although it didn't wow me personally. That said, the blue tea offered a distinct and enjoyable end to our meal.

While the prices reflect the high quality of food and experience, it's justified, making for a worthwhile indulgence. This restaurant undoubtedly deserves a return visit.

Ever since seeing the DB Bistro Burger on a few lists if "The Top 100 Burgers in America", I knew I had to stop b y the next time I was in The City for a Broadway show. We did not want dessert so we skipped the $$ saving Prix Fixe,, so it was a little pricey.But hey, that's NYC.2 apps + 2 entrees + 3 glasses of wine = $170 + tip(fairly priced) Parking directly across the street.Great staff. Very attentive and knowledgeable.One drawback is that there bar is very small....maybe 10 seats max?So don't depend on the bar to wait for your table on busy nights.THE FOOD....This is a Daniel Boulud restaurant ( bistro). He is one of the world's most well-known and successful  (Michelin-rated, James Beard winning) chefs.Menu had the perfect amount of items, not too much, not to small, and every dish sounded better than the last....A very good wine & cocktail list too.APPS tried:ROASTED BRUSSELS SPROUTS SALAD--Radicchio, Croutons, Pickled Red Onions, Caesar Dressing, shaved (Grana?) cheese..this was amazing. I think there was also bacon in it...I could eat a huge bowl of this for dinner.ESCARGOT PERSILLADE--Half-Dozen Burgundy Snails, Garlic, Almond-Herb Butter ...this was a A++ version of the French standard. Viva Le France!(The Bread Service was ample and well thought out)ENTREES:POULET ROTI--Roasted Sasso Chicken, Chanterelles, Corn, Grits, Sauce Estragon was Fantastic!!. I so want this dish right now...and the fact is I only had a small piece of my wife's! Just such a warm, cozy French dish.....but as you know I had the infamous:THE ORIGINAL db BURGER--Sirloin Burger filled with wine Braised Short Ribs,Foie Gras and Black Truffle, Parmesan Bun,with crispy Pommes Frites .....this was a truly amazing burger. I feel that it is one fo Must Do foods to seek out.But for me I think I went in with exaggerated expectations... I mean IT IS a hamburger after all and after having this one I realized I'm more of a purist with my burgers. I may like all the ingredients, but maybe more by themselves. But it is a great burger with amazing creativity that deserves to the on the 100 list.Very happy we went and will be back.

If I could , this review would be 4 and a half stars. Nice people working here. The burger is generously sized, nicely grilled, juicy and reasonably priced, especially considering you are in Manhattan. I sat at the counter and was served promptly. I did not order one, but the steak fries are huge. My first time here, but it wont be my last.

Steakhouse in Midtown, I was only able to stay for appetizers so will have to come for steak and dessert next time.  Staff was gracious as I seated myself at the bar to wait for my friends and bantered a bit with the bartender. The whiskey sour mixed drink has house made sour and is nicely done. Appetizers included some reasonably priced oysters from BC on the West Coast that were cool and delicious. The bacon was thick and rich.. salty, though,  I recommend 2 to 3 ppl share a serving otherwise probably too heavy. The waiter's accent was strong and was a touch difficult to understand the menu.Look forward to the steaks next time, and the multilayer chocolate cake that I know the downtown one serves so well!

Title: Cozy Cantonese Comfort at [Restaurant Name]

If you’re in search of an authentic Cantonese breakfast, brunch, or dinner, [Restaurant Name] might just be your new go-to spot. My brunch visit kicked off with an immediate warm welcome from a friendly lady at the counter, marking the beginning of a homey dining experience.

The highlight was undoubtedly the wonton noodle soup, recommended enthusiastically by the staff. It didn't disappoint – the wontons boasted a smooth, delicate wrapper with a filling that struck the perfect balance between meat and shrimp, enhanced by the subtle taste of yellow chives. The noodles, al dente, complemented the clear, unobtrusive broth.

I also tried the shrimp rice noodle roll (ha cherng). The texture was spot-on gelatinous, enveloping fresh, juicy shrimp. While the restaurant may be modest in appearance, the peaceful ambiance adds to its charm. The conversation with the lady, who shared my hometown, added a personal touch to the meal.

It’s not about flashy culinary fireworks here, but rather well-executed, comforting Cantonese classics. I rate this homey establishment a solid 4 out of 5 on Phil’s 5-scale for its unpretentious vibe, top-tier service, and delicious food. [Restaurant Name] will definitely see me again for the great hospitality and hearty, familiar flavors.

Came for brunch on a Sunday and easily snagged a spot outside. None of our group was vegan or vegetarian, but this came up as a healthy brunch option. I ordered their kale caesar salad, with hemp/cashew dressing, tempeh bacon, avocado, and capers. I assume their substitute for the typical parmesean cheese was nutritional yeast? Caesar salad isn't the hardest test of vegan substitutions, but as a regular omnivore who doesn't normally think about dietary restrictions it was a tasty salad overall.It seems they rely on natural lighting in the morning, but considering their outside space faces an alley it felt a little dark inside. Otherwise a cute, quiet place with delicious vegan options.

Nestled into a cozy corner of town lies a quaint gem that instantly charms with its light and airy atmosphere, thanks to an abundance of windows creating a welcoming openness. The gentle hum of well-maintained air conditioning promises comfort, matched by the warm smiles of the friendly wait staff.

Although the appetizers presented themselves as fairly standard fare, the complimentary sharing platter—featuring focaccia, cheese, eggplant, and salami—was a delightful surprise that set a tone of generosity and flair.

The true star of the meal was the steak, boasting perfectly charred edges encasing a succulent medium-cooked interior that would please any carnivore's palate. Ending on a high note, the dessert did not disappoint, with a rich chocolate cake and an authentic tiramisu that both sung with flavor.

Our experience was nothing short of delightful, a testament to this establishment's ability to elevate the simple to the sublime. This small wonder is not just worth a visit—it beckons a return.

This is a cute spot in Lower East Side across the street from Russ and Daughter's Cafe. You sit at high tops that are reminiscent of school desks. They have an open kitchen as well. We ordered the potato darphin with Maine uni, beef tartare, black maitake, confit bacon toast, and pork milanese. Overall the dishes were all very good. The only item that was only okay was the pork. Service could be better however. They forgot my drink and didn't remember until I reminded them 20 minutes later. They also had to ask me for my order again. I'm always rather annoyed when waitstaff try to impress by remembering orders. I'm more impressed when you write it down and get my order right the first time around. But all that said, the food was good and the service wasn't horrible. I'd come back to give it another chance.

Here is the 3911th review of Buddakan, an old favorite that still delivers the sexy sleek factor along with a delightfully good delicious assortment of Asian Fusian cuisine! Here's is what we enjoyed and recommend:- General Tso's dim sum- Tuna Tartare Spring Rolls - Tea Smoked Spare Ribs- Lobster Fried Rice- Wild Mushroom Chow Fun - Mongolian Rack of Lamb- Stir fried Asian Green VegetablesEvery menu item was well executed and delicious!  Our hostess was an exceptional veteran of nine years who memorized our entire order.  Service was smooth from start to finish. Reservations are highly recommended Wishing you all a splendid holiday season!

It's the morning after taking our engagement pictures in Central Park and we're still on such a beautiful high. Out of the large list of New York brunch spots we landed on this one so we invited 2 of our friends. Here's how it went...Atmosphere/Appearance: Naturally like almost any other restaurant or business in Manhattan, good luck with street parking. Lol. Once inside you're engulfed with Dock's elegance. There was a small live band right at the entrance which was a nice little touch. The black and white tile on the actual oyster bar really added a... maybe... vintage feel? I think that's the word I'm looking for. Anyway, the place is huge and has multiple floors for seating. We were sat in the window facing 40th Street so there was plenty of people watching to do.Service: Quite excellent. I wish I could remember his name, but he did a fantastic job making sure we had everything that we needed.Food: Portions were a bit small in my opinion, but the real draw here was the bottomless mimosas right? They were quite fantastic and made to my high expectations! The complimentary muffins and bread are delicious and worth trying with the different spreads that come along with it. For my entree I went with the Short Rib Hash which comes with potatoes, a poblano pepper and poached eggs. It was fantastic. The flavors were so simple, but still packed quite a mouth-punch. The portion was just small... like... "I do crossfit, eat 8 small meals a day, grow my own food and drive an electrical car small". I wanted some FFOOOOOODD man! Lol. It was good for what it was and I appreciated the quality of the meal and that's what matters.Value: SO... (rubs hands together). $30.00 will get you a brunch entree and bottomless mimosas, bloody marys, coffee or juice. That's a GOOD DEAL, especially in freaking Manhattan.In conclusion I am a big fan of Dock's Oyster Bar. It fires on all cylinders and delivers a very quality experience. I just know that I won't get full and that only leaves room for some Magnolia Bakery banana pudding or some street food! Lol. Or... I could just be a fatty. Either way, I loved this place and I definitely recommend it.

Food is awesome, service is awesome, price gave me my bank account a heart attack :') When I read this is the go-to place for Warren Buffett, I had to pay it a visit. On my trip to NY, I went there at dinner service and wanted to order their prime rib but it was out of stock. Understandable since it was a Friday night. Instead, I ordered their filet mignon, waiter's recommendation. If I remember correctly (I was there in early June and I'm trying this in August), the price was around 55.00 USD, but it was a huge piece of meat. I wanted it medium-rare like usual, but my waiter recommender rare and I'm soo glad I listened to him. The order came clean on a plate with nothing else but the filet mignon, love it, no bullshits haha. Although the meat looked like it's still bleeding, it was deliiiiiicious and tender. Almost forgot, my friend and I also ordered a fried calamari entre. It was crispy the way I like it. The main dish also came with a tomato soup, a bit salty but still very delicious. Our waiter is the asian guy and was super funny, and high five to him for his recommendations! Price aside, I definitely want to come back and try their prime ribs!

I recently visited a local restaurant eager to try their much-touted special drink, Hot Sii, alongside their specialty dish, Mofongo. Unfortunately, both items fell short of expectations. The Hot Sii lacked any discernible flavor, coming across as a bland disappointment. As for the Mofongo, it left much to be desired; the pork belly was excessively dry, and the plantains seemed undercooked and devoid of taste. The pork itself was scant, forcing me to search through the dish for the meager portions provided. Overall, the dish was a poorly executed amalgam, and I was left underwhelmed by the experience.

This review is mostly for the brunch. The dinner is always great. The brunch is jumpin and lively in a good way. We had a reservation and thank God we did because it was PACKED! They asked for a credit card to hold the table but it was no problem.The AYCD sangrias were fun - I had a rosè and a white. My friends liked the red. It was strong but still tasted refined. Service was friendly and professional. My only issue and it's kind of significant is that there was not nearly enough food for our group. We were charged per person and it is served family style but after everyone took a tablespoon - that was it. We all left hungry and disappointed. We all got pizza immediately after leaving.I would definitely be back for dinner.

Rag Trader & Bo Peep is definitely an experience I'll repeat. A girlfriend from out of town and I went for lunch. We both had the kale salad (I added salmon) and several glasses of wine. The service was fairly quick - not perfect - but we looked like we were in deep conversation, so I can understand that. We finished up with the donuts for 2, and those were amazing! The dining room is great for a more intimate meeting, but the bar looks amazing. I'll definitely sit there on my next visit.

I have been experimenting with Ramen spots for the past three weeks and I must say shinshi is the best one I have been to by far. They serve an appropriate amount of noodles compared to the broth. The price is right and the flavor is bountiful. Not much else to say!!

Title: Disappointment at Arlo Bloom's Courtyard

I had high expectations for Arlo Bloom's Courtyard given its reputation, but my recent visit left me feeling let down. Despite the steep $300 minimum for our party of three, the experience did not match the price tag.

The service was notably poor from the onset, with a 15-minute delay before we were even acknowledged with water. Our waitress, Grace S., seemed unfamiliar with both the specials and the menu, often replying that she needed to find out more information. Moreover, we were provided with dirty utensils, a basic oversight that should not occur at any establishment.

The waitstaff's attention to our table was minimal; Grace checked on us just once and then vanished without introducing her replacement, leaving us without service for extended periods. It was quiet enough to expect better service, with only three other parties present and another section entirely unused.

On a slightly positive note, the prosciutto flatbread and asparagus were commendable. However, this was not enough to salvage the overall experience. Regrettably, I cannot recommend Arlo Bloom's Courtyard and have no intention of returning, despite leaving a tip out of courtesy.

I came here for brunch and was extremely impressed! We came at approximately 12 pm on a Saturday. It was pretty crowded, but we only waited approximately 10 minutes for a table for two.The whole atmosphere was lovely. Lots of laid back conversations and great music. The food was also delicious and very reasonably priced. We got the Shakshuka which came with Israeli salad and DELICIOUS bread and homemade veggie cream cheese. We also got the blueberry pancakes (a set of three) that came with really fresh blueberries and maple syrup. The pancakes (similar to Clofoutis) had a little bit of a lemony / yogurt-y taste and were extremely moist. In total (with tax / tip), our bill was less than $40 with two entrees and coffees (the serving size was solid and we had so much food that we had to pack it).If I lived in the area, I would want to make this my go-to spot for brunch every weekend. Alas, I'll have to settle to come every time I am in the neighborhood or craving Israeli brunch. Would highly recommend for groups or in pairs - you won't regret it!

Dallas BBQ is an infallibly good time. It has been this way for as long as I've been going to restaurants of my own choosing.DecorThis isn't what you go for.ServiceThe staff are polite and the food harbingers (they're not wait staff, but they're also certainly not just bus boys) are wonderfully skilled at bringing a whole village's feast in one go.FoodSticky wings. They're sized for a real meal, delightfully tender and always delicious. I have never, ever, ever been disappointed with them! Texas sized drinks. With wine. And a shot.All other menu items, while enjoyable, are tertiary.I've probably been to Dallas BBQ more times than just about any other restaurant I frequent, and I don't expect to stop soon.

Title: Mixed Feelings on Italian Takeout

Last week, I decided to try home delivery from a local Italian restaurant. The service started on a high note with punctual delivery, and their proactive communication about the lack of cappuccino was appreciated—I settled on an extra tiramisu instead.

Sadly, the fritto di calamari left much to be desired. At $15.95, you'd expect crispy, perfectly cooked calamari, but it was mostly soggy and undercooked. The accompanying marinara sauce was the dish's only saving grace. The included bread bites were bland and uninspired; they were only consumed out of hunger rather than enjoyment.

The tiramisu, priced at $10.95, was pleasing but unfortunately came in a disappointingly small container. The cake layer's lack of traditional espresso or liqueur infusion resulted in a less authentic experience, though the creaminess was a plus.

Customer service was commendable throughout the process, but the restaurant falls short in value for money. Every item, including a $6 cappuccino, seems overpriced. Based on this experience, particularly the calamari and the cost, I'm hesitant to reorder from here.

Been meaning to try this bar/restaurant forever - a long standing hangout in the seaport for drinks/seafood/Chinese food. From the outside the place looks completely abandoned (especially when they're first opening for the day), but inside there's a dive-bar feel with a welcoming bartender to boot.After starting off with a draft beer ($6), went to town on the Fish Tacos ($14) and Popcorn Shrimp ($12). Shrimp comes out within 15 minutes - a giant basket of browned fish served alongside tartar sauce. Surprisingly not oily and easy to eat as the name suggests, especially with a little bit of lemon. Tacos come out next, a couple of double wrapped two-handers with fried fish inside each. Not as good flavor as the shrimp, though I quickly ate them as well. The fries that it comes with was overkill, yet they were fresh made and not overly salty.Out of all the restaurants at the seaport, you probably will get your best value here. Try to come around 2pm as they take some time to get started.

Title: A Spice of Manhattan: A Review of Lower Manhattan's Thai Treat

In the bustling streets of lower Manhattan, nestled near the serene Trinity Church, one of the area's two Thai food trucks stands out as a beacon for those craving authentic flavors at a fair price. Despite the inevitable lunchtime crowds, arriving just before noon still meant a short wait behind a handful of eager patrons, revealing the truck's unwavering popularity among the downtown crowd.

At a glance, the menu parallels its local competitor, with a few unique offerings to pique the interest. The pricing is gentle on the wallet, with chicken-based dishes at $8 and beef or shrimp options nudging up to $9—a reasonable ask in the Financial District.

I opted for the Drunken Noodle with chicken, an $8 investment in culinary satisfaction. Service operates at the hands of a solo chef-cashier dynamo, whose warm demeanor shines despite the pressures of managing a one-woman show. Ten minutes ticked by, a fair exchange for the freshly prepared meal that awaited.

The serving size didn't overwhelm but certainly sufficed in quelling hunger. As requested, the noodles arrived with a fiery spirit, delivering a robust, spicy zing that lived up to its name without overpowering the palate. Those with milder tastes should advise accordingly when ordering.

While a closer Thai truck lies within my regular orbit, the quality and value of this mobile kitchen warrant the occasional extra steps. In the realms of FiDi's lunchtime offerings, an $8 to $9 flavorful, spice-infused escape feels nothing short of a steal. For the downtown workforce in proximity to Trinity Church, this truck is a culinary gem worth the visit.

I rank tonight's dinner closer to 3.5 than the full 4 but the gnocchi and the service from who refills the water pulled me closer to the 4. We came in much earlier than our reservation and we got to be seated immediately otherwise which was great. We were greeted shortly after with drink menus and given tap water. Upon first glance I noticed some menu items I was looking forward to wasn't on tonight's menu (boo!) but to be expected since I believe some items are seasonal. We went with the famous rolls, gnocchi Mac and cheese and the BBQ short rib. The rolls - I mean it's bread can't go wrong with that but nothing crazy. The butter spreads were amazing though. Gnocchi - to DIE for. My favorite part of the meal. Short rib - tasty, but not sure it's worth the price considering it didn't come with anything else. Service however was not great. Our waiter never came by to check in until the end, nor offer to refill my husbands tea. BUT. Whoever refills water was very attentive all night and didn't let our water go below half.

Came to the Gothan West Market for ice cream, and could not resist trying the mazemen and pastrami buns from Ivan Orkin. I'm a sucker for garlic, so I had to get the Triple Garlic Mazemen, which was composed of wheat noodles in chicken broth topped with minced sesame chicken, bean sprouts, scallions and garlic - absolutely delicious, I just wouldn't advise on a heavy makeout session immediately after partaking in this.The Pastrami Buns were the true all stars though, the spiced creamy mustard contrasts with the juicy fattiness of the pastrami, and were I not full from the ramen, I probably could have polished off half a dozen of these.Honorable mention goes to that yuzu lemonade, which was tart, sweet and a perfect companion to the fatty meal.

I've frequented this gem often for lunch due to its convenience to my workplace and its superb accommodation of my dietary needs. The fare, from the aromatic Tajine and fluffy couscous to the hearty Chii Sans Carne, creamy hummus, and comforting butternut squash soup, has been consistently delightful. Service is efficient, ensuring minimal wait time—a boon for those on a tight work schedule. Seating is ample, with tables at the front and high tops at the rear, and complimentary bottled water is a thoughtful touch. The staff's pleasant demeanor and readiness to assist only enhance the dining experience. Highly recommended for a satisfying and hastle-free meal.

Title: A Hearty and Spicy Meal to Remember

My friend and I dined at this establishment on a Saturday afternoon as soon as it opened its doors at 1 pm. Our culinary adventure began with a spicy baked bun and beef shumai for appetizers. The bun was a delightful start - soft, fresh, and topped with tantalizing spices that perfectly complemented the sautéed rice noodle dish, which came bursting with traditional flavors and tender lamb.

Speaking of portions, they were generous to say the least. The star of the day was the Big Plate Chicken (Boneless, small for $18) — a magnificent medley of potatoes, succulent chicken pieces, and wide ribbon noodles, all steeped in an enchanting spicy sauce.

While every dish had its own fiery charm, the beef shumai, despite its cumin kick, was the only item we felt was non-essential to the experience. We even took home a substantial amount of leftovers for another meal!

Service was initially attentive, but as the restaurant filled, our lone waitress was stretched thin. Despite the busyness, she maintained her kindness, and we didn't mind the slight wait for our check.

In conclusion, if you're a spice enthusiast, this restaurant is a must-visit. Just be prepared for a substantial feast and some patience required with the service.

This was a adorable Georgian restaurant! Came here w/ a few friends on a weekday for lunch. Thanks Yelp for the free glass of wine w/ check-in! I was very excited to try the famous AJARULI KHACHAPURI - the egg/cheese bread boat. It was super delicious and fun to eat - sizeable portion better for sharing.  As a vegetarian there weren't too many options but I ended having the Lobio Kotanshi which was a type of lentil soup served w/ cornbread and pickled cabbage. The lentil soup was very flavorful and served steaming hot in a clay bowl. It was fun to try a new dish, slightly similar to the spices used in Indian cooking but yet different. The cornbreaded appeared fried and tough so didn't eat that, but enjoyed the softer fresh bread from apps. My friends had the chicken shish kebab and Chakhokhibili which they both thoroughly enjoyed!Overall service was great, ambiance was cozy and food different/delicious. I'm glad we were able to come here for lunch, will visit again if in the area.

The food was pretty good. We got 2 burgers and a burrata pizza with sausage and mushrooms. The burger was good nothing out of this world. I wish there was less cheese but now I know for next time. The pizza was really good but I would go with plain burrata or the classic next time. We got too excited and added too many toppings. The pizza tasted even better the next day. The dough was soft and crunchy and the burrata was creamy. They are kind of pricey. Our three items came to 100 dollars including tip.Mera's Tip: try the pizza

Title: A Taste of Southern BBQ Up North!

Finding authentic barbecue worth its salt in the north can sometimes feel like a fool's errand, but this joint is a pleasant surprise! As a Southerner with a penchant for perfectly smoked meats, I didn't set my hopes high, but I was promptly proven wrong.

The cuts were flavorsome, though a notch higher on the thermometer would've made them spot-on. Customizing the portion by weight is a clever touch, allowing diners the flexibility to indulge as they please.

The side dishes, however, did pinch the wallet more than expected. While the lack of a classic meat-plus-sides combo deal was disappointing, the mac and cheese did enough to soften that blow with its creamy, comforting goodness. The sauce selection was limited, yet the quality did not falter, adding a tangy kick to each bite.

In essence, this BBQ spot gets the meat right and the vibe even better. Would I recommend it? Absolutely, to anyone in search of northern BBQ that almost rivals its southern kin. Just be ready to spend a little extra for the full experience!

Tucked away in an inconspicuous streetfront lies Ise Restaurant, a gem for those who cherish high-quality Japanese cuisine. The ambiance strikes a perfect balance of minimalism and professionalism, with a soothing atmosphere that elevates the dining experience.

Upon entering, the transformation from the unremarkable exterior to the delightful interior is instantaneous. While the outside may not scream 'romantic date', it's an ideal spot for a casual weeknight dinner.

The attention to detail at Ise Restaurant is evident. Each dish is presented with care, making their offerings not just a meal but a visual feast. The Hexagon stands out—a chef's choice bento that acts like a budget omakase, offering a little bit of all the best they have to offer, perfect for those overwhelmed by the extensive menu.

Their soba noodles are a must-try, a signature dish that keeps regulars coming back for more. But let's not overlook the sushi selections; the chirashi bowl, for example, is a treat for any sushi enthusiast. While the prices are moderate, they reflect the quality and beauty of the food served.

Ise does offer lunch specials, though they tend to sell out quickly—a testament to their popularity. If proximity permitted, I'd be a frequent visitor. I can confidently recommend Ise Restaurant for anyone in search of an understated yet exceptional Japanese dining experience.

Had a nice lunch here last weekend. Great ambience- nicely decorated without being stuffy or contrived. Loved the flowers on the larger tables that give a little privacy if you're sharing the table with another small group. Even the restroom has nice flowers! Had the salad, small calamari and orecchiette. All were perfectly prepared and very flavorful. Desserts looked good but we wanted to leave room for a walk around the neighborhood. It's a very small restaurant so you'll definitely need reservations. Book ahead bc they book up quickly.

Title: Hidden Gem in the Village: Denino's

During a summer stroll, we serendipitously discovered Denino's and were enticed by the lively outdoor scene of patrons enjoying pasta and sangria. The Tuesday special—$10 pastas and half-price happy hour beverages—sealed the deal for a spontaneous dining experience.

We indulged in penne vodka and pesto pasta, both of which were delightful and accompanied by a notably delicious sangria. The portions were generous enough to warrant leftovers, ensuring the meal's value.

Service at Denino's was commendable; the staff was warm and proficient, promptly seating us and serving our meal. The prime location adds to its charm, making it an ideal spot for social gatherings or a relaxed date.

With a plethora of daily specials and a bustling happy hour, Denino's is a local establishment well worth frequenting. Don't miss the chance to support this neighborhood cornerstone that might otherwise be overlooked in the daily hustle.

Came here for my birthday dinner. Out of the thousands of steakhouses in NYC we chose this one because it was nice inside and it was affordable. Other steakhouses were either too expensive, or affordable and had a casual rustic interior. Which I didn't want for my birthday. It's smaller and darker than it looks inside, when we got there it was practically empty. We were sat right away. Our server was not giving off good vibes. He made us feel like he was judging us. Kept pushing us to order although we needed some more time to look at the menu. I didn't appreciate that. As an appetizer we started off with clams. They were so tiny but delicious and fresh, you could practically taste the ocean lol! And they gave us complimentary bread and crackers with butter and some kind of sauerkraut? No idea, but we weren't really a fan. As entrees my boyfriend and I both got bone-in ribeye medium rare for myself and medium well for the gentleman. First off...the steak was AMAZING. Knife cut through like it was butter and the sear was delicious. Didn't even need steak sauce or anything (which was provided on the table). The sides we got to go with it were mash and sautéed spinach. Also delicious. For food, we really can't complain. However, we felt like we were being blindsided being charged for sparkling water without being told that it was going to be an extra charge. Also, my boyfriend was under the impression that my birthday dessert was going to be complimentary but it wasn't. It was included in our bill. Which was kind of misleading and upsetting being as though the guy on the phone told him it was gonna be free. We spent more than we were planning too which was annoying, due to things we didn't know we'd get charged for. Maybe we're inexperienced with fancy steakhouses? LOL! But all in all, we enjoyed the food a lot. Don't know if we'd come back.

Title: Finally Tried Los Tacos No.1 - A SoCal Taco Aficionado's Verdict

After years of skepticism, assuming Los Tacos No.1 was just another tourist trap, I caved in – and what a pleasant surprise it was. Hailing from Southern California, I take my tacos seriously, but this place managed to impress.

The highlight is undoubtedly their fresh, made-to-order tortillas. The corn tortillas are superior here: thick, chewy, and utterly satisfying. The flour tortillas, while fresh, didn't quite hit the mark for me – too thin for my California burrito standards.

With a simple selection of meats and cactus for vegetarians, the menu may seem limited, but it's all about quality over quantity. Each taco – adobata, carne asada, and pollo asada – was a flavor-packed delight, with the adobata stealing the show. Though they don't top it with the traditional pineapple slice from the spit, the side offering still complements it well.

Salsas and limes are abundant, and the medium smoky green salsa earned my personal stamp of approval. The experience echoed good memories of dining at Tacos el Gordo back home, but the pricing is a bit steep in comparison – you're looking at $3.50-$3.75 per taco.

The only letdown was the horchata. At $3.75, I expected more than a watered-down rendition in an ice-pre-filled cup that diluted the flavor even further.

Overall, when the craving hits in the theater district, Los Tacos No.1 is now my go-to for a taco fix, albeit with a sigh at the price and a pass on the horchata.

On a dreary Wednesday evening, I chanced upon a brightly lit pizza parlor that was surprisingly empty. In true slice shop fashion, an array of pizzas waited behind the glass, ready for a quick reheat. I opted for their Bruschetta Burrata Slice, retailing at approximately $6. It was an ample square of doughy goodness generously smothered in tomato sauce and crowned with a fresh ball of burrata. A brief wait for reheating, plus an additional minute for temperature management, and I was faced with the challenge of navigating the delicious mess to take a bite. The flavors were robust, with the burrata surprisingly milder than anticipated. Although on the pricier side, the filling slice justified itself, adequately satisfying for the evening. Kudos for the cordial service, especially for accommodating a card payment for a single slice. All in all, a worthy stop for a quick, hearty meal.

My recent Friday night dinner at this spot was a delightful surprise. Seated immediately upon arrival, the service was prompt and welcoming. The star of the show was the Grilled Haloumi, a Cyprian cheese that curiously echoes the taste of chicken, which was deliciously paired with grapes, creating a harmonious blend. Additionally, the lamb lasagna proved to be a savory treat, rich and satisfying. A whimsical touch for diners of all ages, they offer crayons to draw on the paper menus, adding a bit of fun to the dining experience. Highly recommend for a tasty meal and a relaxed atmosphere.

Came here to try the infamous Emmy burger, and it was pretty good! I know this place is primarily a pizza restaurant for the Detroit style slices, but we'd heard so much about the burger that we had to each get our own! The burger is pretty sizable with 2 patties, and the pretzel bun is awesome with great flavor. It also holds up to what really is the star of the dish, that sauce! It's sweet with a little spicy kick. The caramelized onions are the perfect compliment as well. We each were sure we wouldn't have stomach space for the fries that normally come with the burger, so our waiter was nice enough to shave a couple bucks off the price so that we would get the burgers without fries. That being said, the burger is still pretty pricey, coming at $21 without fries. Is it the best burger I've ever had? No- but it is tasty and I can see why people love it.

Stepping into the Mercado Little Spain transported us back to Barcelona and especially el Mercado San Miguel in Madrid. Here we found everything we craved. The prices are slightly higher than Spain  but the quality and flavor is spot on. We had our favorite Churros and chocolate Vermouth, & patas bravas. We will have the paella next time. You will find everything gastronomic her that you will find abroad the only thing that was missing was our favorite calamari sandwich. I hope they that sandwich to market. Price point: average for Manhattan. Food: quality, fresh, & delicious Beautiful market transports you back to Spain.Very clean Staff friendly and efficient Fun & lively atmosphere Plenty of scattered around seating Clean restrooms Enter under highline on 30th street, or via the entrance at the Hudson Yards mall.

Not bad of a place. Its a food truck like no other, and they have all sorts of mexican foods available. Burrito, quesadilla, rice and beans, tacos... i ordered the steak burrito, came with rice and beans, cheese, steak, pico and hot sauce. I did request to add guac, and paid for it, however it was no where to be found once i ate it. Over all food was good. I did like what seemed to be a freshly done tortilla, aka wrap. Didn't care for the beans, as they were a bit hard for me, almost as if they were under cooked. But the chips are made there as well, and they are awesome.

Title: A Culinary Gem for Asian Cuisine Lovers

If you're on the hunt for some of the best Asian food around, look no further! The limited seating is a non-issue as most patrons happily grab their food to go or eat with gusto before heading on their way. 

The spicy and sour lamb dumplings are a standout, boasting a pleasantly thick skin that adds a desirable chewiness. The juiciness of the filling gives a nod to the beloved xiao long bao, while the tender meat bathed in an exquisite spicy sour sauce is a flavor revelation. We found ourselves irresistibly dipping all our other dishes into this sauce - it's that good.

Adventurous eaters will revel in the spicy cumin lamb noodles, a dish not for the timid. Cumin takes center stage here, creating a bold and memorable taste experience. The noodles themselves are cooked to chewy perfection, though be warned, the dish is slightly on the oily side. But what it does have is flavor in spades, making it well worth a try.

The stewed pork burger is the culinary glue of the meal; crispy on the outside, succulent on the inside. It's the perfect vessel for all those leftover sauces - dunk it in the dumpling or cumin sauce, and elevate a simple burger to divine heights. Simple, yet so effective - the sauces from other dishes truly enhance it.

In short, don't walk – run to this spot for an Asian food affair that you won't forget!

Clean store, order at the register and then pick up. Sauce was spilled in the bag so had to clean that up when I went home. The lamb isn't as fragrant or tasty as Mahmoun's lamb gyro sadly, just greasy and heavy sadly. The salad looked better, will try that another time.

Title: Energizing Sunday Brunch at a Popular Spot

I stopped by this bustling eatery for Sunday brunch and immediately sensed its popularity with a 30-minute wait for our group of four. In need of a caffeine fix, I ordered a lathe that arrived swiftly despite the crowd, serving as a perfect pick-me-up.

Opting for something on the healthier side, I tried the shakshuka. It was a delightful choice, with egg whites neatly blanketing the plate and a tangy tomatillo sauce that hit just the right note. The toast struck a pleasing balance between soft and crispy, making for an excellent companion to the dish.

Leaving the restaurant, I wasn't overly full, but pleasantly satiated and ready to tackle the day. It's a spot I'd recommend for anyone looking for a satisfying brunch that energizes without overdoing it.

Came in with skepticism about the glowing reviews, but definitely surpassed my expectations in every way. The food was delicious, the atmosphere is cozy, the staff is friendly. I would definitely recommend. We started off our meal with a summer roll. It was surprisingly refreshing and yummy. The wonton crunch with the other fresh greens made it even better. I've been allergic to shrimp for a decade so I'm really glad I can have something that tastes a lot like a summer roll. For our entrees we got the pho ga and beef pho with bone marrow. The chicken pho broth was amazing -- intense flavors without being too heavy. The noodles were bouncy and chewy and just the perfect amount of noodles. A lot of pieces of white meat and they provide a house sauce for the chicken... so good but very spicy! The beef pho on the other hand was fragrant and earthy. Everything was flavor bombs. The bone marrow was a nice addition but I can do without. The pho was already really good without it.

Title: A Delightful Lunch Experience

I stumbled upon a lunch special at this charming restaurant and was thoroughly impressed. The kui Chai appetizer, a delightful fusion of crispy scallions in batter, was addictive with its perfect contrast of crunch on the outside and softness inside, savored with a sweet soy dip. The star of the meal, the crispy whole fish, was expertly fried to achieve a sublime crunch, its flavor enhanced by a sweet and sour sauce that was nothing short of complimentary. Though the Thai iced tea didn't quite hit the mark, tasting somewhat diluted, it was a steal for only $1. With generous portions at such reasonable prices, I am eager to return and explore more of their menu.

This place is cute inside but the $5.00 slice I got wasn't over the top. It did the job bit lacked flavor and overpriced. It is located on the corner of 33rd and 3rd ave which is convenient to where I am living for the weekend. I am sure the pizza competition is stiff around here!

We stopped by for Sunday brunch at 11 am and were pleased to find plenty of seating available. The service stood out, being both efficient and friendly. My avocado toast and my husband's quesadilla eggs were quite satisfying, matched by generous portion sizes. The yogurt we had was a nice addition. While the food was enjoyable, it would've been great to see a wider range of healthy options on the menu. The brunch came with a beverage choice, and the constantly refilled coffee was a thoughtful touch. Overall, this spot offers a good, pleasant experience, though it's not particularly unique.

Title: A Classy and Whimsical Culinary Gem

I recently dined at a restaurant that can only be described as the epitome of class with a delightful thematic twist. The atmosphere was instantly engaging, with whimsical pigs adorning the walls, complete with quirky writing— a playful touch that set this Chinese eatery apart.

The service was impeccable, guided by a knowledgeable waitress ready to steer the dining experience with her seasoned recommendations. She was a culinary compass, candidly advising us against the frozen bass in favor of more tantalizing options.

Culinary delights included a lamb and peppers dish bursting with flavor, perfectly cooked scallops, and a generously sized soup designed for sharing. The standout, however, had to be the much-hyped ribs—a popular item on Yelp for good reason. They were succulent and tender, truly 'fall-off-the-bone' fantastic.

While the restaurant is not shy with spices, the dishes I sampled were balanced, ensuring the heat enhanced rather than overwhelmed.
