The menu's breadth guarantees a return visit is in order, as one meal was simply not enough to explore its vast offerings. With hearty portions ideal for groups and a service that makes you feel like a regular, this spot is a must-visit for anyone looking for a memorable dining experience.

Title: Service Shines Bright at Local Vegan Eatery

From the moment we walked in, the service at this vegan restaurant impressed us immensely. The staff was nothing short of attentive, offering excellent recommendations and ensuring that our dining experience was comfortable and enjoyable.

As for the food, it was decent, although when stacked against other vegan dining options, the flavors seemed to fall a bit flat. The notable exception was the dessert, which was outstanding—perfectly balancing tartness with sweetness and delighting the palate with an array of textures.

The nachos and spaghetti were fairly standard, not leaving a strong impression. However, I did appreciate the pleasing crunch of the crispy eggplant, which was a highlight of our meal.

In summary, while the main courses were unremarkable, the dessert alone is enough to draw me back. I’m not certain I'd opt for a full dinner here again, but I'd definitely return for a sweet treat.

Speechless.PROS:atmosphere menu designpositive vibeschill staff cool tunesdelicious foodCONS:none Can you deliver those chicken tacos to Boston? Drool worthy.Margs were also delish.Dumbo you know what ya doin.

Came in on a Friday night for a friend's birthday dinner with a reservation for 6:30 for a party of 7. We skipped the apps and went straight for the entrees. Prior to coming in, we all thought we wanted the box of dreams ($48). This is literally a box with 9 little bowls of at least 9 different varieties of sashimi, served over sushi rice. But then our waitress threw us for a loop and recommended the Sushi Deluxe ($45) - ten pieces of nigiri and a roll. I went with this one because I figured it would be less rice than the box. I really enjoyed it (except the ikura one, but I'm also not a fan of ikura). I'm also glad I ended up getting this one because the box of dreams had the cooked cold shrimp and the sweet egg thing, which I do not care for. My fiancé got the box (he liked it) and I still got my IG-worthy shot of it.At the end of the meal, they brought the birthday girl some mochi ice cream, so that was a nice touch. Next time, I may splurge and get their omakase (which at $100 for 15 pieces/$120 for 18 pieces is very reasonably priced, compared to a lot of other higher end sushi spots).

3.5 stars.First time dining at the Midtown East Patsy's and overall, it was above average.Walked right in and chose to sit near the entrance as it was cooler in terms of temperature. We were originally going to be seated near the ovens,  but with summer weather in full swing, it felt very hot. Keep that mind. Note, there was also an upstairs level.Service was prompt and attentive and we got things started with a house Pinot Noir ($9.50). Very good.The menu had traditional Italian options--lots of pizza and pasta varieties---we decided to share a 13" pie and a pasta dish.For pizza, we went with the Old School round cheese. Our pasta dish was Shrimp Scampignola which was linguine with 6 jumbo shrimp, garlic, herbs in a white wine sauce (red sauce, also an option).Both came out very shortly after we placed the order. We immediately devoured half of the pizza which was delicious with a perfect balance of sauce and cheese. The crust was chewy---not paper thin. The flavors were very good and the pie itself was an adequate size.The misstep of the evening was the pasta dish. While the flavors were delicious and garlicky, the linguine was way too overcooked. Anyone knows that overcooking pasta is a cardinal sin. For that reason alone, I had to shave off the 1/2 star. Some would subtract more. I just cannot approve of soft pasta. And it was such a let down.Again, food was good overall. We really liked the pizza. Atmosphere was cute and spacious. The overcooked pasta couldn't be dismissed as far as my rating however, I would definitely visit Patsy's again.

We visited this spot for their bottomless appetizer deal, which, at $60 per person, seemed promising. The restaurant accommodates BYOW, with a corkage fee of $20 per bottle, which we took advantage of. Although the endless apps offer value, the food didn't quite hit the mark for me. Overall, while it's a reasonable choice for those seeking quantity, it fell short of compelling me to return.

Mixed feelings about this spot. Actually was here a year ago, and then again recently. Our server actually was able to do a sampler of the three dips (smoked hummus, beet dish, muhamarra) which was actually really great. I liked the cashew cheese truffle halloumi, but didn't love it. I personally thought the falafel's presentation was better than how it actually tasted, and I wasn't really a fan of the cauliflower (I don't think the tahini it comes with actually complements it well). Our meal came out to near $60/pp for three people including wine. A couple extras - our server was actually kind of rude towards the end of our meal, and we went for a birthday that we had made clear and were surprised they didn't offer dessert. Wish I loved it more!

As a Michigander at heart, I found Lions, Tigers, and Squares to be a delightful slice of home. The clever name initially drew me in, but it was the sumptuous fare that truly captivated me. They've mastered the art of pizza with a crust that's the epitome of perfection - crisp at the edges, yet tender and substantial enough to support a bounty of fresh toppings. The mushroom pie, adorned with a well-seasoned marinara, was exceptional. Adding to the experience, the staff was the embodiment of friendliness, noteworthy was the charming order-taker who made our visit all the more pleasant. Affordable prices seal the deal. This spot is a firm 10/10 in my book, and I wholeheartedly recommend it!

What a stunning restaurant and facility! Definitely catering to the moneyed & well-heeled crowd, but for what's offered I think it's more than worth it for the rest of us, too. It's very peaceful & posh here, from the glistening ground lobby to the shimmering 25th floor lobby, Electric Lemon feels like an instant classic, almost an "I've been here before" or an "I've always wanted to come here" vibe. Although brand new it's fine-tuning makes it feel well-established. Everything about my very leisurely & indulgent meal here felt very relaxed and gratifying, which is very much appreciated considering the gridlocked walk through Herald Square & Penn Station & Hudson Yards; but once finally inside it's an entirely different world altogether. Magnificent ceilings & walls & floors, majestic windows & overviews, all very generously allowing for the very comfortable & spacious & beautiful tables & seats & banquettes -- but of course the exciting & refined food deserves zealous-mentioning, as do the innovative cocktails. The entire experience was excellent & memorable.

Title: Hidden Neighborhood Delight - A Must-Visit!

After years in the neighborhood, I finally discovered this unassuming spot, and it’s nothing short of a culinary treasure. It strikes a rare balance, offering dishes that feel both home-cooked and indulgently restaurant-quality.

The gyoza dumplings are a revelation, with a delicate shell that’s brimming with savory filling, elevated by a sprinkle of garlic crisps. Both varieties of the katsu curry – chicken and pork – impressed with their crispy exterior and tender meat, all swimming in a heartwarming curry sauce accented with sweet carrots.

The ramen deserves a special mention. It’s a bowl of pure comfort: perfectly al dente thin noodles, a flavorful broth with a gentle heat, complemented by a soft egg, seaweed, and succulent meat.

I’m already planning my next visit to this culinary gem. It’s a full-hearted recommendation for anyone looking for comforting food with a gourmet touch.

This seemed to be a random spot. But we definitely didn't mind. We had the spring rolls as an appetizer, then pad Thai and the drunken noodle for dinner. Everything was delicious and I would recommend if you're in that area and are craving thai. They didn't ask the spicy level of the pad Thai that they usually do, so it wasn't spicy at ALL. But I still really liked it. My fiancé loved the drunken noodles and would highly recommend.

Finally visiting a long-awaited dining spot, my boyfriend and I snagged the last reservation at this local gem before a show at Arlene's Grocery. The food exceeded expectations, particularly the buffalo mozzarella appetizer, which rivaled the freshness of its Italian counterparts. The daily pasta special, Orecchiette with tuna, impressed with its flavors, and the meat lasagna held its own as well. We ended our meal with a comforting dessert of cookies and hot chocolate, rounding out a delectable experience. This place absolutely deserves its 4.5 stars – a must-visit for anyone in the area.

First, ambiance. This place has it by the bucket load. There's so much to take in about this place from the ceilings to the antiqued mirrors to the art work and bar, it's a visual symphony that will keep you entertained throughout your stay.The food is outstanding. This was my second visit and I was with two friends. The nacho appetizer was incredible. Our sandwiches were utterly amazing and the drinks were on point.As for service, the wait staff checked in frequently enough that we didn't lack for anything without being annoying. They were friendly and helpful.Oh, and the music. Awesome. It was mostly 80s, but my friends and I loved it. This is a great place to unwind after work. It's also a cool and relaxing lunch spot mid-day as well.We love this place and plan to make it our regular spot on every trip to New York.

This place has my favorite vegetable dumplings! The dim sum is very authentic and there is a great variety of options to choose from. The pricing is slightly high but there are usually some offers going around for the restaurant. The taste is great and I would recommend if you want solid dim sum.

When I pull my pants down, everyone gets to see Mamoun's.Yet another location of Mamoun's and they're turning out good food which is a little bit better standard than MacDougal Street's packed-all-the-time location, and way better than the ones in New Haven and the like. But not as good as the gold standard over in Hoboken as far as I can tell.Get the shawarma falafel combo pita with all the extras inside it.Now would you like all my extras inside it?

My past review as well as my past experiences at Upland was based upon dinner. This day we had lunch at Upland. We ordered to share a Winter Salad, the Tomato Soup, a pasta dish Estrella and finished with the Anjou Pear Crisp.  Without going into the intracacies of each dish it sufficies to say that they were all perfectly prepared and composed offering a complexity of balanced flavors within each, and beautifully presented. Each disH alone is worthy of 5 stars +. Our two cocktail starters, a Cider Car and Roger Rabbit were equally delightful. Our server was charmingly friendly and suitably knowledgeable about the  entire menu including the newly added offerings and provided exceptional perfectly timed service. Service rating  5 stars +. A member of our party left their glasses at the table completely unaware, I received a call from Upland within 20 minutes of our departure at the height of the lunch rush. Upland pleasantly remains on my list of top places to dine in Manhattan!

I visited the restaurant during the off-peak hours on a Saturday afternoon and was pleased to find there was no wait time. Service was notably quick and efficient. We indulged in an array of dishes including uni bibimbap, an eel hot stone bowl, and bulgogi tacos. Each dish was packed with flavor, but the uni bibimbap was the standout - a complex mix of savory, sour, crunchy, and creamy elements that came together in a delightful explosion of taste. It was an absolute highlight and made the meal exceptionally memorable.

My sister, mom, and I stopped by this charming little restaurant for an early dinner last Friday. Despite its small size, the decor is stunning and creates a welcoming atmosphere. We kicked things off with the Ahi Tower and the Set D Edamame, both of which were recommended by our friendly and attentive waiter. We were particularly impressed with the freshness of the ingredients. Although the prices seem a bit steep for the portions provided, the quality of the food was undeniable. We are already looking forward to coming back to experience their 30-minute omakase.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Margherita in Little Italy

I recently visited Margherita in Little Italy after looking for some delightful small eats to enjoy on the go. Unfortunately, my experience was far from what I had hoped. Upon entering, be cautious as there's a bit of an unexpected uphill step.

The service left much to be desired; it was as if the staff was perturbed by our presence rather than welcoming. The indifference was epitomized by our waiter, who disappeared after taking our order, leaving us without any update or explanation. When my friend's calzone finally arrived after a tiresome wait — long after we had finished our meals — it failed to impress and was ultimately discarded along with much of our uneaten food. My eggplant parmesan was similarly underwhelming, bland and forgettable.

Although the calamari was satisfactory (it's hard to go wrong with fried food), one decent dish couldn't salvage the overall experience. What truly capped off the disappointment was the realization that the glowing reviews on Yelp didn't match the reality, leaving me to question the reliability of such platforms.

In retrospect, this visit to Little Italy and Margherita was a letdown, and I can't recommend this restaurant to fellow Italian cuisine enthusiasts.

Cha Chan Tang is one of many restaurants on Mott and Bayard with the comfort food concept of Hong Kong style restaurants. The Pineapple Bun with the slice of butter is pretty phenomenal but the rest of the food is average and nothing special. The service is pretty horrible and unfriendly. I sat in a empty restaurant with only two occupied tables and no one greeted or approached to take my order until I flagged a server over.

If you find yourself hankering for noodles at any hour, look no further than this remarkable spot that's open round-the-clock. My late Sunday visit was a pleasure with no crowds to speak of. A dive into their cold dish offerings, like the crisp shredded potatoes and the intriguingly flavorful pig ear with celery, was a refreshing start. The star of the show was the original soup – a DIY diner's delight with a selection of sides ready to be plunged into the steaming, boiling broth. The process is part of the fun: add the meat first to cook in the heat, followed by the rest of the accompaniments. It's a customizable feast that leaves you wanting to explore more of what they have to offer. Count on me being a repeat customer, eager to sample the other broths on my next visit.

I went to this bar with a few people on a Friday evening since they're known to have a happy hour that lasts until 8. Most people must know about this spot because it was pretty packed when we walked in around 7. Regardless, it's a huge space that can definitely fit a lot of people. We walked in and our group of five was able to find space at their bar in the back.They've got a few drinks included in their happy hour selection. Some cocktails, a wine, and a lager. I stuck with their lager the entire time we were here which was around $8. There were also many bartenders here so we were able to get multiple drinks without having to wait long.The place is nice because it seems like there'll always be a lot of people here. However, if you're looking for a spot where you're able to either have more intimate conversations or a spot that has a more enjoyable ambiance I'd go elsewhere. Midtown isn't my go to spot for bars but this place is worth visiting if you're limited to the area and are looking for a happy hour deal.

Title: Satisfying Lunch Special at a Great Value!

I recently visited this restaurant for a quick lunch date and was impressed by their lunch special offerings. I opted for the stir-fried chicken with black bean sauce, paired with vegetables, and found it delicious—the sauce hit the spot as a personal favorite of mine. For $9.55, the portion was generous, with a good amount of chicken and veggies, and included the choice of rice and an appetizer, which is a pretty solid deal for the area. The ambiance of the restaurant is quite nice, reflecting the essence of sit-down dining at a quality Chinese establishment. Despite its appeal, getting a table was a breeze, with plenty of seating available. Overall, a great place for a satisfying and budget-friendly meal.

Had a nice birthday brunch. Food was plentiful and drinks were strong. Lovely view. Since it was my birthday I asked a staff member in a maroon shirt if he mind taking our picture before we left of the skyline. Asked us to wait a few minutes and walked away. We took a selfie and called it a day. I said to him "thanks for not taking our picture and walking away" as I walked out. I would come early again it seemed the later it got the more packed it was. DJ was great. Staff member who was rude just turned me off. Our waiter was great and attentive.

I recently enjoyed both lunch and breakfast at a delightful diner conveniently located within walking distance of the Marriott Courtyard and Hudson Yards. The food was quite satisfying, offering good value with reasonably priced and generously portioned dishes. Overall, a great dining experience for anyone in the area.

Title: A Culinary Adventure at Blue Ribbon Brasserie

My experience at the Blue Ribbon Brasserie, part of the illustrious Blue Ribbon restaurant group, was nothing short of a delightful adventure for the palate. On a Monday evening, our group of five gathered for a business dinner in the establishment's unique setting, which sets itself apart from its siblings with an eclectic menu catering to a diverse crowd, including the city's own culinary maestros until the wee hours of 4 am.

The range of our selections spanned the menu's broad offerings. We commenced with a fresh shellfish assortment that featured both east and west coast oysters, king crab, shrimp cocktail, and whole shrimp served New Orleans style. The rich terrine of foie gras was a luxurious follow-up, succeeded by a creative presentation of chicken wings that came with a personal grill to enhance their flavor.

Although the wings differed from Blue Ribbon's famed fried version, they proved to be a satisfying deviation. Next, the bone marrow and a "pu pu platter" with a mix of ribs, chicken skewers, more wings, and pierogies graced our table. Our main courses scored unanimous approval, including a succulent duck breast, a crispy half-fried chicken complemented by honey, steak tartare (which, personally, was not my top pick), and a cheeseburger that I didn’t sample.

The lavish side of paella, loaded with traditional ingredients, was a fitting tribute to our indulgence. Despite the enticing menu, dessert was a challenge we could not surmount after our bountiful feast. Service throughout the dinner was impeccable – our server was attentive, punctual, and cordial, enhancing the overall dining experience.

While I have a pronounced bias for Blue Ribbon's sushi and their irresistible wings with wasabi honey, the Brasserie is a wonderful variation from their usual fare. For those who crave a taste of what keeps NYC's restaurant scene vibrant, give Blue Ribbon Brasserie a visit. You’ll dine like the very chefs who set the bar for this great city.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this gem of a restaurant with my business partners and it was an unforgettable experience. The ambiance was elevated by the amazing music that set a lively tone for the evening. Each dish we sampled was delicious, but the fish tacos stood out as my personal favorite. The drinks, particularly the margaritas, were expertly crafted and complemented our meals perfectly. And the dessert was memorable, ensuring that the meal ended on a high note. Highly recommend for a blast of good food, great drinks, and fantastic atmosphere!

Thoroughly unenjoyable and probably a generous 2. Got there with a buddy around 12:30. Place had a good crowd but was not full by any means. We sat promptly and were tended to quickly. From there, it was downhill. We ordered diet sodas and pizzas which were legitimately the worst sodas we've ever had. Pure syrup and no carbonation. It was flat gross syrup. We nicely asked for unsweetened iced teas instead. After about 20 minutes, we saw the waiter again and asked again for the ice teas. About 5-10 minutes later, the drinks and pizza came. The pizza was not great, had no structure and was barely cooked; not sure what happened during the previous half hour. In my picture, you'll note what it looked like when I picked up the slice; it just completely collapsed and tore apart. It's also worth mentioning that the setup is poor. Presumably due to the thin hallway, every smell and sound lingers. At one point, a woman walked through who appeared to walk to the kitchen, and the lingering super potent smell of pot remained for a long time. The only reason it subsided was that later, someone walked by and cigarette smoke overpowered our table for several minutes. I couldn't wait to leave. Overall, the service, food, smells and experience was sub-par. No chance I'd go back.

Title: A Birthday Feast to Remember at Bustling Local Gem

My family and I visited this bustling hotspot for my mom's birthday on a Saturday evening, and it was clear right away why reservations are a must—by 8:30 PM, the place was packed. Despite the crowd, we received outstanding service throughout the night.

We began with grilled octopus, burrata cheese, and a dozen oysters for appetizers. For a group of nine, it seemed modest, but the complimentary bread helped tide us over. Each dish from the appetizer to the main courses was nothing short of phenomenal.

The pan-seared Chilean sea bass with coconut curry sauce I ordered was sublime, cooked to perfection with just the right portion size. Other highlights at our table included squid ink pasta and a perfectly cooked sirloin steak. While I can't delve into every dish's detail, I can assure you, they were all fantastic.

The service truly set this restaurant apart. Our waiter was not just polite, but engaging, fielding our questions with ease. The manager and the bartender mirrored this attentiveness, with the latter offering me several bourbon samples to find the ideal cocktail mix—a thoughtful touch that did not go unnoticed.

Be prepared for New York prices—entrees range from $26 to $45, and cocktails sit at about $15. While not for those seeking a bargain meal, you certainly get what you pay for here. We left satisfied and eager to return. Highly recommended for those looking to indulge in a memorable dining experience.

Title: A Flavorful Introduction to Ramen - Quick and Budget-Friendly

I recently ventured into the world of ramen noodles at a local eatery, and the experience was nothing short of delightful. For a first-timer, the assembly of the ramen bowl was captivating, watching each component come together to create a harmonious dish. The buns deserve a special mention - stuffed with succulent pork, crisp lettuce, ripe tomato, and a kick of spicy sauce, they were truly wonderful.

Although I can't show you a snapshot of my satisfaction, the empty plates and bowls stand as a testament to the deliciousness of the meal. The establishment left a positive impression on me with its offerings.

One quirk is the location of the bathroom; navigating through the kitchen was unusual and the restroom itself could benefit from a remodel. Seating is snug at the counter, but the efficient use of space is impressive. In an unexpectedly swift visit—just 45 minutes from start to finish—I was served, dined satisfactorily, and had settled the bill.

On the whole, this restaurant provides a tasty and cost-effective dining experience, despite a couple of peculiarities. Highly recommended for those looking to dive into the world of ramen without breaking the bank.

Stepping into the restaurant, you're instantly transported to an Old Western scene, complete with wooden tables and a relaxed vibe - an unexpected find on a bustling Manhattan street. Even at the dinner hour on a Wednesday, the place was comfortably quiet, offering both cozy indoor seating and an inviting outdoor area for those who prefer dining al fresco.

In a nod to sustainability, the restaurant has ditched plastic straws, a small but admirable effort towards going green. Be prepared for Manhattan prices – with mixed drinks at $14, although the 'East Side,' a refreshing blend of cucumber, mint, and gin, was worth every penny.

The double Bubby burger, priced at $22, was a highlight of the meal. It was a delicious, juicy indulgence, albeit a bit messy with grease. Opting for the salad over fries may not have been the best choice, as it turned out to be a rather uninspired mix of lettuce and onions. On the sweeter side, the pie caught my eye—priced at $8, it was not only visually appealing but seemed generously portioned.

Overall, while the place carries the typical cost of dining out in Manhattan, it offers a delectable escape into a Western-themed experience. Just be sure to bring your appetite—and maybe a few extra napkins.

Living in LES, it's weird for me to travel so far for Chinese food. Came here as a group of five and got the wintermelon soup, la zhi ji (small cubes of fried chicken), eel in chili oil, black fungus, and garlic shrimp. Coming here, you can tell it's a bit more upscale than your traditional chinese restaurant, atmosphere is more classy, food presentation is nicer, and service is nicer.The ingredients seem to be of higher quality, but I'm not sure I fully enjoyed everything more than your other chinese spots. The black fungus was good, tasted fresh. The wintermelon soup was good (same as your other place though). The la zhi ji had a lot more breading than I was used to, and the chili to chicken ratio was surprising (too much chicken!). It seemed healthier, but it just didn't have the classic crunch to it. The eel was a very interesting dish as I've never had eel like this and I enjoyed this one. Normally my eel is very soft (think unagi in sushi) and this one was a bit more tough. The garlic shrimp had probably a bit too much butter and garlic for me, very overwhelming taste.Don't think I'd come back here, not upset that I tried it though.

Title: Refreshing Ambiance, Mediocre Poke

Upon entering the restaurant, I was immediately struck by the welcoming and refreshing atmosphere, which was complemented by the kindness and helpfulness of the staff. Leveraging a free meal voucher from their rewards program, I was assisted in choosing from an extensive variety of food options.

I settled on a poke bowl, which turned out to be relatively uninspired. The ingredients, largely raw vegetables, were fresh but lacked the pizzazz I was hoping for. The sauce provided was sparse, and even with an added splash of soy sauce for a flavor boost, the dish remained underwhelming.

For a dish that typically costs between $11-13, I expected a bit more excitement on my palate. Although the meal was filling, it did not deliver the savory satisfaction I crave. While I would encourage others to give the restaurant a try—perhaps their taste buds will differ from mine—I personally don't see myself returning. My quest for a tasteful and fulfilling meal continues elsewhere.

I recently visited Tipsy Shanghai, the New York offshoot of an esteemed Shanghai establishment dating back to 1905. Given its storied lineage, I anticipated a rich tapestry of flavors and authentic Shanghai culinary offerings. Regrettably, the fare fell short of expectations, veering towards the bland and undistinguished, leaning more towards American Chinese standards such as shrimp with lobster sauce and sweet & sour chicken, rather than delivering genuine Chinese cuisine.

While the ambiance of the restaurant was quite inviting and the service commendable, these aspects could not compensate for the lackluster dining experience. Our quest for something extraordinary was met with a feeling of letdown as the promise of historic Shanghai flavors remained unfulfilled at Tipsy Shanghai.

I recently dined at this bustling spot for a lunchtime feast and was promptly seated upon arrival. The culinary adventure began with the Celery Pig's Ear in Garlic Sauce, a refreshing deviation from the traditional Sichuan style I'm accustomed to – the celery provided a delightful contrast. However, the chicken dish fell short of expectations; misled by its Chinese name on the menu, I anticipated a baked delight rather than a fried one. While tasty, it wasn't the experience I hoped for.

The Noodles in Original Pork Bone Broth were a highlight, with a hearty base and generous portion perfect for sharing. The added bonus of a tray with various accompaniments, including lamb, made for a satisfying bowl of noodles. Service throughout the meal was commendably quick and friendly. Overall, a solid choice for an authentic and enjoyable lunch.

Cafeteria offers a trendy and inviting atmosphere complete with a modern vibe and a musical backdrop that adds to the dining experience. On warm days, the restaurant enhances its charm by opening its windows, creating a pleasant and open environment for patrons. However, it's worth noting that access to the restaurant requires navigating a rather steep staircase, which may pose challenges for some guests, particularly the elderly.

The menu at Cafeteria consistently impresses, especially for fans of mac and cheese like myself. The trio of mac and cheese is a personal favorite, offering a delightful variety to choose from. The cheddar and fontina mac and cheese I recently enjoyed, shown in my attached image, was both tasty and generously portioned, ensuring a satisfying meal.

In summary, Cafeteria guarantees a delightful visit with its good food and vibrant atmosphere. It's a spot I always look forward to returning to.

Based on a glowing recommendation, my visit to this restaurant on a bustling Saturday night did not disappoint. The wisdom of securing a reservation became clear as we were seated without delay in a setting that struck a perfect balance between cozy and elegant. The meal commenced with an appetizing serving of bread complemented by a creamily delectable pesto sauce.

A berry and basil-infused drink was a delightful prelude to the culinary excellence that followed. The star of the show was undoubtedly the homemade pasta; my Gnocchi Sorrentina was a triumph of texture and taste, while my husband's Linguine in clam sauce was equally impressive. Service was exemplary, with our waitress exuding attentiveness and efficiency.

The experience has left me eager for a return visit, with the burrata appetizer and potential dessert already on my future indulgence list.

Came here for restaurant week and the food is terrible. Not one thing taste good even cheaper places taste a lot better. Dessert was bad as well. Presentation looks good but taste is very off. Lobster with saffron rice - no taste mehAppetizers sweet and sour ribs- meat taste weirdDumplings- meat not totally cooked through Pawns- too much mayo too sweet and too hardEntree ribs tips - meant too rubbery not enough taste Duck - bad bad bad - go somewhere else to eat pecking duck it's so unauthentic here.Dessert - no good.Service was the only thing that was good. Food was not.

Title: A Tasty Visit to The Bao with Mixed Feelings

After a tantalizing article from a Shanghainese native in Quartz declared The Bao as the premier spot for xiaolongbao (XLB) in New York, my girlfriend and I ventured there with high hopes on a quiet Sunday afternoon. The place welcomed us with open tables and immediate seating. Our choice? The traditional Nanxiang XLB and an inventive chocolate XLB, setting us back a reasonable $20 with tax and tip.

The pros were undeniable: the XLB burst with freshness and the meat filling was noticeably leaner than its Shanghai counterparts. Each dumpling's broth was a fragrant and flavorful delight, hitting the seasoning sweet spot. The chocolate XLB surprised us pleasantly, marrying banana and rich chocolate in a combo that's hard to fault.

However, not everything lived up to the hype. The dough skins were on the thicker side, bordering on chewy, hinting that a longer steaming might be the key to perfection.

In conclusion, while The Bao offered a delectable experience, it fell short of dethroning my personal favorite, the Shanghai Yu Garden in Flushing, for the ultimate XLB crown.

AMAZING DESSERT EXPERIENCE. Came by on a Saturday afternoon and there was a 2 hour wait!! So we opted to sit at the bar with no wait and still the same full service menu. Definitely the way to go to avoid the wait if you don't have a reservation! Still received great service. DESSERTS- soooo many options of incredible things. We shared the dessert pizza with everything on it (so worth it to pay less than a dollar more but get so many toppings) and the fondue. Both were INCREDIBLE. The fondue came with all the right things to dip in and the set up was so cute. It was a good amount (not too much or too little) and everything was delicious. A must try for anyone with a sweet tooth! Will be returning

Title: A Delightful Discovery at Tang

I recently dined at Tang with two friends, and our experience was nothing short of spectacular. Upon arrival, our reservation ensured we were seated without delay. It being our maiden visit, the server was immensely helpful in guiding us through the menu.

The standout dish of the night was the Sesame Tofu—an absolute masterpiece! Its blend of soft tofu with sesame paste, chili oil, and garlic created an explosion of flavors that left us in awe. Without a doubt, it's a dish not to be missed.

For vegetarians or those simply seeking a delightful noodle dish, the Hot and Sour Noodles are an exceptional choice. Expertly spiced, they deliver a satisfying kick to your taste buds. Equally impressive were the Ma Jiang Mian noodles; their cold, peanut-sesame infused strands were elevated by a touch of extra chili sauce, catering to those with a penchant for peanut flavors.

The beverage selection complemented the meal perfectly, with a variety of Soju and Asian beers to choose from.

In conclusion, Tang has secured itself a spot on our go-to list—especially for the tofu and noodles. We're certainly planning to return.

Title: Disappointing Delivery Experience with Seamless

I recently ordered from a restaurant via Seamless and left underwhelmed. While the mashed potatoes were satisfactory and the cheese-filled khinkali (dumpling) was enjoyable, the rest of the meal fell short of expectations.

My major gripe was with the lula kebab. Forced to choose two meats, beef and chicken, for a steep $26, I received only a modest beef wrap. Not only was the portion size questionable for the price, but the beef itself was off-putting, either due to the seasoning or lack of freshness. Regrettably, I discarded it after only a few bites.

Additionally, the dumpling assortment was misleading. Anticipating a mix of cheese, potatoes, and mushrooms in each dumpling, it turned out each dumpling contained only one filling. Only the cheese dumpling passed muster for me.

To sum it up, the whole experience felt like a rip-off, and I suspect I was overcharged. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this restaurant based on my recent order and would caution potential diners to temper their expectations or choose elsewhere.

Embarking on a culinary journey at this trendy spot, I was immediately struck by the restaurant's hip ambiance, which was effortlessly echoed in the artistic presentation of each dish. The pricing edged on the higher side, reflecting the quality and experience. Perfect for a romantic evening, the soba here is a standout, and for those seeking a chef-curated adventure, the omakase option is a culinary delight not to be missed.

Cozy and nice market/restaurant around the East Village, Manhattan. It was a little crowded when we went for lunch, didn't have to wait to be seated. They have outdoor and indoor seatings, with AC inside. They have a great option of food to choose and have special menu for lunch. I ordered the Moroccan Rice Bowl from the special lunch menu with a watermelon lemonade. The watermelon lemonade was amazing, it had the right flavor balance. Food was great, big portion, tasty and healthy. Overall, this restaurant was amazing and it was a good place to start my visit in NYC.

Title: A Night of Golden Ambiance and Flavorful Bites

My long-awaited visit to this local hotspot finally came to fruition last night, and despite the bustling 6 pm crowd leading to a 45-minute wait, bar seating offered an immediate reprieve. Next time, we'll utilize the Yelp waitlist for a smoother experience.

The stunning interior, adorned with intricate decorations and a wealth of gold hues, sets a dim yet inviting atmosphere. Although charming, the low light made menu navigation a tad challenging.

Our culinary adventure kicked off with the standout Pla Muk Tod ($12) – a fried calamari dish whose crispy texture perfectly complemented the peanut vinaigrette. Without hesitation, it's a must-try appetizer. The Mango Sunrise ($9), a creamy concoction of mango, pineapple, and coconut, followed suit as a luscious beverage choice.

While the main dishes took their time to grace our presence, they proved worth the wait. The Pad Se-Ew ($15) with chicken was an explosion of flavor wrapped in broad noodles, firmly establishing itself as a personal favorite.

The attentive staff ensured a pleasant dining experience throughout our meal. My boyfriend and I are already planning our return to this gem.

I recently attended a comedy show at this venue and decided to try their spicy watermelon margarita. The drink was average, mirroring my overall experience of the evening. The comedy show, akin to the beverage, was moderately entertaining. The venue presents itself as unremarkable, with no particular attributes that stand out. In summary, the experience was satisfactory, but not noteworthy.

this place is unlike any restaurant i've ever been to in the entire united states. it is an experience like no other. they have fresh fish flown in DAILY from spain, portugal, and greece. so not only is it a gorgeous restaurant, but it is also an incredible fish market. you can literally take a walk through the market to select your fish if you'd like. everything is prepared so simply yet elegantly- so the flavors of every ingredient are showcased perfectly. this is the best place to go for a special occasion or celebration because everyone at the table will feel special. i suggest you try everything you can.... we got the fried zucchini appetizer and it was amazing. we also got the assortment of dips and the greek salad. i ordered soft shell crab and scallops and my mouth waters every time i think about that meal.... you seriously have to try this place if you haven't already- just make sure your pockets are full

Title: A Fiery Delight at Hunan Slurp

My experience at Hunan Slurp was nothing short of exceptional. This eatery is transforming traditional Chinese dining with contemporary flair, and it doesn't disappoint. The Lotus meatball was a particular highlight for me – a filling delight that combines scrumptious flavors with sticky rice to tantalizing effect.

Be warned, though, the authenticity of their Hunan cuisine means that some dishes pack a spicy punch. The shredded beef had me reaching for my water glass more than once, but the heat was a part of the fun.

Service was impeccable. Our waiter was the perfect balance of attentive and non-intrusive, ensuring a seamless dining experience. The only caveat is the restaurant's seating arrangement; some tables are squeezed a bit too closely, which can make navigating to your seat a dance of diplomacy.

Hunan Slurp is a must-visit for anyone seeking a genuine taste of Hunan in an inviting atmosphere. Just be prepared for a close encounter of the culinary kind!

Very cute spot inside the Jane Hotel! Not busy on a Monday around 4 pm. We ordered the burrata and marghareita pizza, both were great but the burrata was amazing. Good service and nice bathroom. Nothing crazy but nice aesthetic and good food.

Get their Sangria pitcher! They have amazing sangria here and they serve it in frozen sangria ice cubes so it won't dilute out when it melts. The tapas here are one of the best in the city. We loveeeee everything here! The steak was extremely well cooked and the squid pasta was on point!!

Title: A Step into Another Era at a Cozy Nook

On a spontaneous decision to explore the local dining scene, my companion and I found ourselves at a bar that whisked us away to what felt like a medieval sanctuary. The entrance had a certain charm that set high expectations for the atmosphere inside. True to form, the bar area greeted us with subdued lighting and a tranquil ambiance that beckoned us to relax.

The beer selection was commendable. I gravitated towards an IPA—its name escaping me now, but with 'bullet' in the title—that boasted a robust flavor and just the right kick of alcohol for a pleasant buzz. Though we didn't partake in food this time around, the menu seemed to offer a modest array of bites fitting for a bar setting.

Service was a highlight with our waitress proving affable and delightful company. Prices were reasonable, particularly for the quality of the beers served. In short, a laid-back evening with good drinks and better conversation. Would recommend for a casual drink if you're in the area.

I recently dined at this charming restaurant with three friends and we had a delightful meal. We indulged in a selection of dishes including the Steamed Dumpling Platter, Stir Fried Choy Sum, Shredded Vegetable Chicken Lo Mein, Pan Fried Turnip Cake, and Sweet Sticky Rice Sesame Ball. Each dish was flavorful and well-prepared, though personally, I found the dumplings were a tad too heavy on the vegetables for my taste. The menu bears a resemblance to that of Original Buddha Bodai but the ambiance here is notably more serene. Overall, it was a satisfying experience and I look forward to returning.

I ventured into this restaurant with high hopes, nudged on by friends' recommendations. My choice, a chorizo chicken sandwich, unfortunately led to disappointment. What was served turned out to be a damp squib – literally – as I was met with a soggy excuse for a sandwich that was a challenge to eat. The accompanying sauce was overpowering to my taste buds, heavy on smokiness and spice that didn't sit well with me. To top it off, the price was a sting to the wallet - almost $20 for a combo that failed to deliver on quality. Though the experience was underwhelming, I'm open to the idea of returning with hopes that a different menu item might redeem my initial impression. But for now, this particular dish gets a thumbs down.

Sadly I could not get in here on day one but I grabbed some coworkers and made it happen today. We took a Fieldtrip literally around the corner and we not disappointed! The ambiance clean, chic, and modern. There is ample seating and the decor is super cute. The themes Fieldtrip and Rice is Culture are tastfully expressed throughout the reastaurant even in their gender neutral bathroom. The food was amazing! We are all foodies so in one lunch we expored half of the menu. It was like a fieldtrip around the world.The braised beef with Texas brown rice and wok vegetables was seasoned just right. Vegetables tender crisp perfect and the brown rice flavored and cooked just right. The carrot sauce with the Nana bread delicous. We enjoyed the crab pockets. Crisp on the outside delicous on the inside! The salmon and China black rice with curry sauce was absolutely amazing! The veggie bowl was tasty and the beans were well seasoned. We were all very satisfied but had no room for ice cream. I guess that means we'll be back soon! Great job on food presentation and customer service. Next time I need a field trip, you know where to find me.

Title: A Letdown After the Hype

After reading a multitude of ecstatic reviews, my expectations for this restaurant were sky-high. Unfortunately, reality fell notably short of the hype. The $98 duck dish, praised by so many, was merely adequate. While the meat was tender and properly cooked, the flavor profile was underwhelming, with accompanying salsas lacking any real zest. Considering the quality, the dish was egregiously overpriced and not worth more than $40.

The disappointment continued with the corn husk merengue dessert. Although the unique casing was as expected, the merengue filling was unexpectedly salty and reminiscent of biting into pure butter—a jarring and unpalatable experience.

On the upside, the service was prompt, even if it bordered on rushing us. However, the efficiency of the service does not compensate for the inflated prices and mediocre fare. As a local New Yorker, I have a trove of preferred dining spots that offer far better value. It's unlikely I'll return to this establishment.

I recently ventured into Xi'an Western Chinese Cuisine, still on a flavor high from my experience at the Michelin-starred Cafe China. I was pleasantly surprised to find that Xi'an's offerings held their own. The hand-pulled noodles, pan-fried in hot chili oil, were a revelation, and the spinach dumplings followed suit, echoing the bold flavors and expert preparation.

The owner's upfront warning caught my attention: dialing down the spice may compromise the dish's integrity. I embraced the heat, and indeed, it paid off. The space was unpretensive with its simple stool seating and bright lighting, emphasizing that the focus here is all on the fare.

For those willing to heed the owner's advice and embrace the authentic level of spice, Xi'an is a standout. The ability to add extra hot chili oil ensures that heat-seekers can tailor their experience. Xi'an Western Chinese Cuisine proves that explosive flavors often come from the most unassuming places.

Sarabeth's has been around for at least 35 years, and I recall it had quickly developed a reputation for hearty breakfasts and quality baked goods that I had bookmarked in my brain to try...someday. Not being a New Yorker, I had never given myself a chance to try it, and in those intervening years, it multiplied to various prime locations throughout Manhattan. My guess is something got lost in their expansion because Jamie W. and I were not overly impressed with what we had as we walked by on Park Avenue South.When I saw the name through the scaffolding, I told Jamie we needed to try it since we were feeling peckish on our last day in NYC. We got seated right away despite the throngs pouring through the front door and the aisles of the dining room. I zeroed in on the $13 Deviled Eggs (photo: bit.ly/300W8a2). Who doesn't love a good deviled egg? Surprisingly they were rather bland even with the purported presence of Dijon, parsley, and paprika. And why only five halves? Who ate the last half? Dammit, I wanted my last egg half. Jamie took the wiser route with his main by ordering the $20 Garden Omelette.To their credit, it was mostly foolproof with mushrooms, green peas, zucchini, and melted cheddar. He ordered the banana muffin to go with it (photo: bit.ly/2NZNQYF). Now that was good, the omelette itself was more by-the-numbers. For some self-delusional reason, I thought the $20 Lemon-Zested Tuna Salad would actually feature fresh ahi. But no, it was tuna salad like your Aunt Fern makes with mayo and by the scoopful even though it was surrounded by grilled sourdough, frisée salad, basil, and marinated diced tomatoes (photo: bit.ly/2O2czLT). Was it good? Like I said. Aunt Fern.FOOD - 3 stars...some predictably good items, some that made me go hmmm...AMBIANCE - 4 stars...quite an efficient operation in a well-appointed spaceSERVICE - 3.5 stars...sporadic, initially attentive, then a disappearance actTOTAL - 3 stars...Sarabeth, I hardly knew yaRELATED - Hungry in NYC? Here's a collection of places I've tried and reviewed: bit.ly/2YS9ELs

I had the pleasure of trying out this burger joint a few months back and was thoroughly impressed with their lamb burger. It's the kind of specialty place I find myself craving occasionally – they offer a wide variety of choices and clearly prioritize the quality of meat. The lamb burger was exceptionally good, making me eager to return and explore more of their menu.

Tucked away in the heart of my neighborhood, this humble Vietnamese eatery has become my reliable spot for fresh and flavorful cuisine. Don't expect lavish decor; the small, unassuming interior exudes a cozy, homelike charm that's inviting in its simplicity. The standout has to be the lunch special – it's a steal for under $10 in NYC, offering great value without compromising on taste.

Whether I'm craving the comfort of Chicken Pho or indulging in the familiar flavors of their Chicken Pad Thai (a playful deviation from tradition), the to-go experience never disappoints. The food is consistently good, making this place a true gem for anyone seeking a quick, satisfying Vietnamese meal. It's a local treasure that's worth visiting for a taste of authenticity that won't break the bank.

Steps from time square.So right before or after the beat down to get time square stop in order a slice and sit , stand or whatever and watch all the craziness of time square. I preferred grabbing a slice then walking over to the square and watching while I ate my slice.Great New York service (attitude) behind the counter. I actually had the pleasure of seeing an employee handle a problem customer the way I would have loved to handle one when I was in the service industry.Inside was typical it seems for most of the places we visited in NY, narrow, not much seating, better for to go orders.Pizza seemed doughy and kick less, what I would call safe pizza, meaning pizza you could give it to someone that was 4 years old or someone 90 . One time stop for me .

Title: A Spice-Filled Seafood Adventure at Sup Crab

Last night, my taste buds were taken on a journey at Sup Crab in Chinatown, a choice inspired by a seafood boil craving during an evening stroll. The restaurant’s expansive and well-lit interior was welcoming, though the eclectic mix of greenery, seafood motifs, and unrelated art left us a bit puzzled about the decor's direction.

Service at Sup Crab was exceptional; attentive waitstaff provided excellent dish recommendations. We dove into a sumptuous $99 group combo, a cornucopia of seafood drenched in a delightful 13-herb sauce. Standouts included the tingling Szechuan-inspired popcorn chicken and perfectly fried, crispy chicken wings. Each seafood element, especially the crab legs, was pristinely fresh and enhanced by the aromatic sauce.

The heat enthusiasts among us savored the ghost pepper sauce seafood boil from combo A, a fiery delight that packed a punch with a slow-building intensity. Our meal rounded out with a satisfying dish combining crawfish meat, broccoli, noodles, and a fried egg—ideal for those new to crawfish.

The restaurant's scallion pancakes deserve a special mention, flawlessly executed and utterly irresistible. Even if seafood boils aren't your preference, Sup Crab's menu extends to a variety of Szechuan and Hunan dishes to cater to all palates. Plus, their all-day happy hour featuring affordable beer and wine under $10 is a steal.

As a sweet finale, we were treated to a complimentary plate of juicy fruit, a refreshing end to a delightful dining experience. Whether you're a seafood aficionado or just looking to indulge in some spicy culinary excellence, Sup Crab in Chinatown won't disappoint.

Title: A Chic Spot for Indonesian Flavors: Wayan Review

Nestled in a bustling part of the city, Wayan has rapidly become one of my regular destinations. Its elegant ambiance pairs perfectly with an attentive service, promising a delightful experience every time. While authenticity may not have been my initial draw, the Indonesian-inspired dishes tantalize the taste buds with a bold spicy kick that's hard to forget.

The setting is ideal for post-work gatherings, offering a fine selection of cocktails and small bites that perfectly complement the relaxed yet chic atmosphere of the bar area. Despite the occasional challenge of securing a table, the bar is a welcoming spot to unwind.

My palate was particularly impressed by the lobster noodles and the eggplant balado, both of which showcased a masterful blend of flavors. However, it was the pandan custard that truly captured my heart. This dessert, with its perfect balance of sweetness and a tart passion fruit twist, is a crave-worthy finale to any meal here.

Brunch at Wayan is another delightful experience. The coconut pancakes are a personal favorite, providing a comforting yet exotic start to the day. Every visit is enhanced by the exemplary service; the staff’s professionalism and eagerness to offer personalized recommendations never go unnoticed.

Wayan stands out as a fashionable spot that eschews the cliché and is an exceptional choice for hosting out-of-town guests or simply enjoying a trendy night out in downtown. Whether you're in for the food, the drinks, or the atmosphere, Wayan delivers an enchanting experience that beckons you back for more.
Delicious falafel platter that was filling, healthy, and delicious. All vegan and I especially loved the harissa falafel!

Title: A Hidden Gem with Irresistible Happy Hour Deals

I can't get enough of this charming little spot that I discovered just last month; it's already seen me return thrice! The size is modest, but the warmth is abundant, and I've never had to wait for a seat—what a delight!

The eternal happy hour steals the show with half-priced bottles of wine and unbeatable pitcher deals that beckon for a toast at any hour. While the food menu is extensive, it hits some high notes and misses a few; the truffle fries fell flat, and the Greek salad was average. However, the pasta was satisfying and my boyfriend can't stop raving about the grilled chicken panini.

It's the perfect low-key hangout for gatherings, especially since you're welcomed to linger over drinks without the pressure to dine. Despite the culinary hiccups, it's the sort of place that has earned my loyalty, and I'll undoubtedly keep coming back.

Overall always a solid Spanish tapas place, but last time I came it was definitely better. It's a bit overpriced for the size, but fairly authentic Spanish food and good ambiance. Seafood is the star here, definitely recommend the razor clams, squid, and scallops. Their sauces and flavorings are perfect and bring out the best of each seafood. If you're not used to Spanish food it's going to be a bit salty, so just pair it with a good wine and you'll be all set. One complaint I have though is their squid could have been hotter... the food was served a bit more on the colder side. Overall? Would come here if I feel like splurging a bit more on small quantity but high quality Spanish tapas.

Slightly overhyped imo. When we stopped by back in January, we got the signature artichoke slice as well as a vodka one... the artichoke slice was too thick for my liking and the flavor was just okay, but I'd be open to giving it another chance. The VODKA one though was waaaaay too saucy omg never again! Partially my own fault for underestimating how runny the sauce was and stupidly dropping a huge slab of it on my down jacket, leaving a nasty stain. Had to bring it to the cleaners and it was this whole unnecessary and expensive ordeal. Wasn't worth the mess. If you get it, please be careful, but I also remember it being overly salty. (Or maybe that was just me - overly salty about the stain, heh)Came back last Saturday and tried the crab, margherita and pepperoni slices. (Shared between a few people! I could barely finish one of their huge ass slices on my own) Nothing special or amazing about the margherita or pepperoni, but the crab slice was such a pleasant surprise! As others before me have mentioned, it really tasted like a clam chowder on pizza - super creamy and comfort foody. If you must come here for pizza, I'd recommend the crab slice.

Amazing food and ambiance. Definitely one of the best taco places I've been to in the city so far. They also have happy hour from 3-7 pm Mondays - Fridays! My friend and I tried the rotisserie chicken tinga, beef short rib, spiced cauliflower, roasted fish tacos, and they were all equally amazing. However, the most unexpected surprise, and now my favorite Taco Dumbo dish, was the coconut sticky rice with black bean mash. I would come back here just to order that side dish. The rice was seasoned perfectly with salt and lime juice, and the black bean mash added a creamy consistency to the order. The margarita was refreshing, and we could barely taste the alcohol in it! The ambiance made it feel as if we were on an island getaway-- palm trees, beach chairs, and neon art of surfboards and the sun. We even sat under a gigantic wicker dome. It was almost tragic when we had to venture back into the cold weather and walk past grey Midtown buildings.

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Prince Street Pizza

As a self-proclaimed pizza connoisseur, I've found my slice of paradise at Prince Street Pizza in NYC's chic SoHo district. Nestled amongst the trendiest of fashion boutiques, this pizzeria is a beacon for both locals and tourists, so expect a queue that's as popular as the pies themselves. TIP: Beat the crowds by ordering takeout early or visiting in the morning.

My latest pilgrimage to Prince Street did not disappoint – the legendary pepperoni pizza lived up to every memory. With each bite, the perfect blend of spices, melty cheese, and those iconic, crisp-edged pepperonis reaffirmed why this place has captured my pizza-loving heart. Be warned though, the portions are generous, so arrive hungry and ready to indulge in what is, hands down, one of the best pizza experiences New York City has to offer.

I had a delightful dining experience at Yoyoka, conveniently located right outside the 2nd Avenue subway stop. Perfect for satisfying a Sunday night ramen craving, I arrived at 6pm and found it pleasantly quieter before the 7pm rush. The shoyu ramen, priced at $14, although slightly on the saltier side as other reviewers mentioned, was unquestionably tasty and gratifying. The restaurant had a serene ambiance, and the staff allowed for a relaxed meal without the pressure of hurrying out. Service was impressively swift. The shoyu came with a savory homemade soy sauce broth, tender chasu pork, fresh spinach, ajitama, kikurage, crisp nori, scallion, and perfectly cooked straight noodles—a solid choice for those new to the menu. I'm thrilled to know that Yoyoka is an option whenever I'm in the area again.

Tonight I visited HALL for a second time. What a special place! Very classy, intimate, and just amazing overall.I've only ever visited the quaint speakeasy-ish cocktail joint in front, but I hear the dining room is just as enjoyable! I also hear they have a killer lunch!Try any of the drinks! They are high end, classy, and a bit pricey... but well worth it! Especially enjoyable is the Hall Old Fashioned and the Dama D'oro (a Mezcal drink).I'm so happy this place is located a few doors down from my office! This is my second visit, and I definitely plan to become a regular!

Title: A Delight for the Discerning Diner at Motel Morris

If ever there was a gem for those days when your taste buds are feeling particularly discerning, Motel Morris would be it. Despite any skepticism kindled by less-than-justice-doing food photos on Yelp, this restaurant needs to be experienced firsthand.

During a recent visit with my world-traveling best friend, who initially doubted my choice, Motel Morris not only met but exceeded expectations. Throughout our meal, my friend couldn't stop expressing her delight, and her daughter's nods of approval were the cherry on top.

The takeaway is clear: don't judge this book by its cover—or this restaurant by its online images. Dive into the menu, pick anything that catches your eye, and I'm willing to bet you'll leave as contented as we did. Trust me; Motel Morris is the answer to your picky palate's prayers.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Mr Chow

My recent visit to Mr Chow presented a dichotomy of impeccable service and underwhelming culinary experiences. Right from the entry, the service was attentive—ensuring privacy by thoughtfully spacing out diners and providing well-lit tables to easily read the menu. However, the seating was a letdown, with chairs that were not only uncomfortable but also outdated, much like the 80s décor that desperately calls for a refresh.

On a positive note, the chicken satay did not disappoint, and the pot stickers were the true stars of the evening. Had I surrendered to the temptation of indulging in several orders of these, perhaps my review would lean more towards the raves I'd previously heard.

Unfortunately, the main courses did not live up to their introductions. Portion sizes were typical of Manhattan but failed to impress. The drunken fish, rather than being infused with wine, was overwhelmed by a too-sweet honey syrup, and the four-color cauliflower, despite its vibrant presentation, offered little beyond aesthetics. The crispy beef was a miss—lacking substance and dripping with oil.

In sum, my hopes of discovering the lauded flavors of Mr Chow were met with the stark reality that the glowing reviews did not align with my experience. It's a shame when the service outshines the food at a dining establishment.

Curry leaf improves eyesight, aids digestion, relieves nausea, fights infection. Himalayan pink salt balances electrolytes, mineral rich, aids metabolism, detoxifying. Lentils increases energy, high in protein, fiber rich, benefits heart health. Chili pepper enhances memory, relieves pain, anti-inflammatory. Cilantro aids digestion, removes heavy metal, antibacterial. These are some of the elements to Mulberry & Vine's food alchemy and eat clean concept. Located in the heart of TriBeCa, this place offers well-prepared clean wholesome food with a laidback, almost cafe-like ambience. Their line is almost always long, especially during peak hours like lunch time... and then there are times where it would go all the way out the door and onto the street. Fortunately it does move fast. They have plate and bowl options. The plate option allows two veggie items and one protein item. The bowl is basically a salad with two veggie items and one protein item. They frequently offer deals, which includes customer appreciation day at least twice a year where every dish is $5. Also you can sign up on the "Thans" app to get the first order on the house. And with every 3 referrals, you get a complimentary entree.

It was amazing as usual. I had the steak Oscar which included a 16 oz New York strip steak, a crab cake and asparagus. With a side of garlic mashed potatoes. I had no complaints. The service was impeccable, the waiter was amazing. The food was amazing! It was a tad bit cold in the dining room, but it was freezing outside so it was to be expected. All in all, it was amazing. The steak was so big, i took half of it home. Will return, and highly recommend.

My dining experience kicked off with a 500ml serving of Kimoto sake, striking a pleasant balance with its dryness and crisp notes, thanks to the polished rice. The highlight of the evening was the 10-course omakase, a delightful journey through expertly prepared sushi and sashimi offerings. While both were enjoyable, the sashimi boasted a slightly larger amount of fish per piece.

While the sushi morsels felt petit, they did not skimp on flavor, melting like butter with their freshness. To further satiate our cravings, we opted for extra bites, including ikura, a creamy uni, a salmon roll, and a succulent yellowtail roll—each bite confirming the kitchen's prowess.

Dessert was a chocolate trio that indulged my sweet tooth with its richness, complemented by two lovely macarons courtesy of the house. The restaurant's cozy ambiance and meticulous service underscored an exquisite dining experience.

Title: A Gem in the UWS: Yu Kitchen

If you're looking to satiate your Chinese cuisine cravings in the Upper West Side, look no further than Yu Kitchen. This establishment has quickly become a personal favorite, thanks to its consistently delicious offerings. Their scallion pancakes and beef stir-fried noodles will have you returning for more, and their Chongqing beef with soft tofu dish is a revelation.

Yu Kitchen triumphs not just with its food but with exceptional service that stands out in the Chinese restaurant scene. On one memorable occasion, when my 10-month-old child flung a chopstick to the floor, a waiter was at our side with a replacement in a blink. This attentiveness is the norm here, not the exception. The staff is incredibly accommodating, always ready to adjust seating to suit any party's needs, especially those with children.

The cozy size of the restaurant adds to its charm, but it's wise to remember that it isn't meant for very large groups; it comfortably seats around 30 patrons. Yu Kitchen has become a staple for my Sunday lunches due to its tasty, generously portioned meals at great prices and its unmatched service. It's a must-visit spot that never disappoints.

During my initial visit to the restaurant, the Shrimp Empanada made a memorable impression with its superb flavor and pleasing texture. However, on a subsequent visit, I noticed a dip in flavor quality, evidenced by my photographs, though at $2.50, it remains a fair deal. The Beef Empanada also deserves mention for its favorable taste; priced at $2, it's quite the bargain. I do hope the establishment strives to maintain their food quality consistently.

I have been to this restaurant multiple times for lunch and once for dinner.Personally this is the best Thai restaurant in the Financial District area, it's hard to find. It's a hole in the wall.  When I came here for lunch they definitely had the buffet, which was really good. I would get the Siamese pork over rice. It's only served during lunch in their buffet section and now their lunch special. However, recently I had a craving for duck noodle soup. I ordered the duck noodle soup with thin noodles for $9.95 and it lasted me two days. The noodles and vegetables were packaged separately so it became a DIY dish which was nice.  I have been here for dinner and had small bites which was ok, nothing special. I would skip the appetizer and stick with the entrees. This restaurant is also opened for takeout and delivery so if you're in the area order lunch and support local businesses.

I love Westville. There's something for everyone here - healthy or indulgent, vegan or meat/cheese. And I love the casual atmosphere - you can look nice or dress in athleisure and feel welcome. I recommend the market plate, which contains your choice of four sides. The sides are always changing with new seasonal additions, and everything can be prepared vegan. The mashed potatoes, tofu, broccoli, artichokes and mushrooms are all delish. The quinoa artichoke burger on the other hand... I would expect something with the word artichoke in it to taste like artichoke or just generally be flavorful, but other than the spicy ranch this did not have much flavor. Skip this and go with the market plate.

Had to come home from dinner and write this review. Starting off by: yes, it is worth the hype. You will need a reservation. This dinner was full of pleasant surprises. The menu is pretty simple, you get three courses and you get to choose from many interesting options. We started our dinner with drinks. They use soju, a Korean liquor made from rice. I had the drink that resembles a gin & tonic, which was very well done. My husband had the drink with soju infused with jalapeño, that also had grapefruit and resembled a margarita. It was interesting to try something new with soju. Our choices were:First course: beef tartare + crab. Second course: sunchoke + pork and shrimp. Third course: pork belly + duck. You also can choose some of the a la carte choices, charged extra. I really wanted to try the fried chicken and my husband really wanted the ribs. We ordered it all. The first course came REALLY quick. Seriously. We had some crispy nori before that (devoured). The beef tartare was so fresh.. it also had pineapple in it, unexpected but so good. This one was on the spicier side. The crab, on the other hand, was very citric and refreshing. It had a lot of endives that gave it an interesting texture. Second course came with the sides of rice (white and special - $2 more - which had spinach. We love rice, so later on we needed a refill... Kimchi was 1) mustard greens and 2) radish. I usually think kimchi is too spicy, but the mustard greens were perfect! Husband loved the radish mixed in the white rice. The sunchoke was delicious! It had mushrooms, truffles and oranges - another great surprise! - in it. The presentation was so pretty. I love mushrooms so this was a win. Pork and shrimp was very unexpected.. it was a sausage! Flavorful combination. Third course was the pork belly, covered by mushrooms. The pork belly was perfectly cooked and there was actually a considerable amount of it! The duck was served as a broth.. I didn't try it, but apparently it was just good - nothing out of this world. The star of the night were the ribs. They come with two sauces (chimichurri and a Korean one that I forgot the name), leaves and pickled radish. It was a half rack, therefore a pretty large portion. The ribs fell off the bone... they do bring an extra side of rib sauce but it was not needed. It was just perfect. Surprisingly we still had room to share a dessert. We chose the semifreddo with honey. It was a great way to finish this experience. This dessert was very light and satisfying. Extra points for the service. Everyone was super nice and attentive. We'll definitely be back soon!

Recently, I dined at a fantastic new Mediterranean restaurant that also serves up some delightful Israeli specialties. We kicked off our meal with the creamy hummus and a fresh Israeli salad, which were both fantastic. For the main course, we indulged in their savory shawarma, crispy falafel latkes, and perfectly grilled calamari. Each dish was outstanding and the portion sizes were generous, perfect for sharing. This place has quickly become a strong contender, rivaling my other local favorite, Shuka. If you're in the neighborhood and craving Mediterranean cuisine, I highly recommend giving this spot a try.

Walked by this place and stopped. What a great choice. Can't believe that a small neighborhood place could be so good. ENTRANCE- an intriguing red awning is the entrance way to a small local restaurant on Lexington Avenue. It was an early evening Wednesday but the staff greeted us rather quickly. We had our choice of any table as it was only 5:30 in manhattan. SERVICE- extremely nice and attentive to every whim. The owner and son were actually waiting on us and super friendly. We even had a third party meet us (after a call to say how good the place was) and they accommodated a last minute order timed to perfection when they arrived. BREAD & DIP - fabulous the bread was classic Arthur Avenue Madonna quality. They had a dip that was to die for. Super flavorful. APPETIZERS - had the artichoke with crab in a tremendously great broth. A must try. ENTREES- wife and I went with fish specials halibut and Bronzino that were perfectly prepared. By that I mean crispy on the outside and soft and moist on the inside. A must try when available. Which could be every day lol. What do I know. VINO - very good Italian selection and not exorbitantly priced for Manhattan. DESERT - so full only cappuccino. Let me know what u think if you try a dessert here. PRICE - for a last minute group of 3 with bottled water drinks and specials, and crazy almost 9% sales tax the bill without tip was $230 so realistically $$$ but more like $$$$ depending on what you order

Decent pizza, bad experience overall. First of all, this is primarily one of the by-the-slice joints that tend to be a rarity in the artisan pizza world, so that I appreciate. Slices go from $3 (plain cheese) to $5.50 (special squares) so it's definitely pricey if you're ordering a lot. They do full pies too but I didn't check out pricing. It exists in limbo between a no-frills slice joint and an instagrammable/trendy spot much like Russ and daughters - is the food good? It's solid. Is it worth the wait and hassle? I say no.I ordered the upside down cheese square and the al pastor slice. The first was unexceptional and was more like a cheesy focaccia. The latter was unusual, but had some interesting flavors unlike what I've had before. The real downside is that it took me 15 minutes to get through a line of, i don't know, 6 people - so there are clearly some inefficiencies there. And worse, after I had ordered it was another 15 mins before the slices were ready. Again, they're premade, so all they have to do is pop them in the oven to reheat. I've had entire pizzas made in a shorter time frame. Also, one woman ahead of me ordered a pepperoni slice and after she ordered, they seemingly sold all of them, so she had to wait an extra 10 minutes to get her food.Seating is limited. Much like the parent restaurant Sauce, it has a weirdly positive reputation despite how unfortunately average the food is. With prince street, rubirosa, Pasquale Jones, and more in close proximity, this is probably the last place I'd recommend. All in all, decent pizza but will not return due to higher-than-usual prices, slow service, etc.

I came here to enjoy happy hour with my coworkers, and it was decent. The service was average, the food was good, the drinks are good for a happy hour drink but overall It'll get the job done.  Since I was mainly there for the happy hour, I decide to have the shrimp tacos so I could avoid getting too drunk. The taco was good, they were three average size taco which were pretty flavorful. I paired my tacos with a classic margarita, which was pretty tasty as well. For $6, you can't go wrong. My coworker had the chicken burrito, which according to her was decent. She ate it all, so I'm personally assuming it was good. She had the passion fruit margarita, which she also said was good. I know that the works "good" isn't convincing enough to try it, but I believe you can't go wrong with a $6 margarita. Icely I will give them a 3.5 stars them a three star the food and margarita are decent in price. The service was a little delayed.

I entered the restaurant with high hopes, having heard it might even surpass Soba-ya. Unfortunately, it fell a bit short. The soba was satisfactory; however, the flavors failed to fully permeate the noodles. I tried the Tsuke Cold Soba, which was decent, although lacking the desired chewiness. My companions went for the Chirashi Lunch Set, a steal at just $10, and thankfully, it did not disappoint taste-wise. The ambience was average, not quite capturing the immaculate essence of a Japanese eatery. The hot tea provided a cozy touch, yet the visit as a whole was neither memorable nor lackluster.

We came here Monday for afternoon tea.I made a reservation in advance to get the window seats. The restaurant is quit big, and busy for Monday afternoon.  They got 3 choose for afternoon tea.1. Pink tea $50/ person2. Pink G tea $60 / person (with gin-based cocktail)3. Pink bubble tea $70/ person (with champagne)We decide to go with Pink G tea, which included traditional high tea with a cocktails.From the bottom, they have 4 different flavor sandwich. -coronation chicken, apricot and raisins-smoked salmon and copper crepe fraiche-truffle egg and spinach-cucumber, cream cheese, dill and chivesFor the sconesOne fruit, and one plainServe with strawberry jam, Hudson valley clotted creamAnd cakes on the top-strawberry Victoria sponge-grapefruit tart- hibiscus rose macaron-raspberry rose jelly We got extra fries on the side.Everything taste amazing, plus the view.We couldn't finish the top sweet section, we we had that to go. The serves was great, the waiter keep adding hot water to our tea pot. And we were too happy to chill and stay there pretty late, but they didn't ask us to leave. I saw other people's lunch looks tasty as well, will come back to try it!

I recently had a fabulous brunch experience at Pongal that I just have to share. I highly recommend kicking things off with their fried idli appetizer – it's a unique twist that sets the tone for what's to come. The onion rava dosa was a standout dish, boasting an amazing crispy texture that you won't forget anytime soon. For dessert, don't miss out on the rice pudding; it's the perfect sweet note to end on. The service here deserves a shout-out too – attentive and quick without missing a beat. Everything was served fresh, hot, and packed with authentic flavors. If you're in the mood for an unforgettable brunch, Pongal should definitely be on your list.

Title: Decent Pho with Room for Improvement

I visited the restaurant for a lunchtime Pho and found the experience to be just average. Priced at $15, the Beef Pho was served with a clear broth, but the meat was disappointingly tough. While the portion size left something to be desired, with a somewhat smaller bowl than expected, the service was notably quick. However, there seemed to be some inconsistency with the dish presentations among diners. Overall, the Pho was decent but certainly has ample room for refinement.

I visited this well-hyped spot right at its 5:00 PM opening on a Sunday, and I'm pleased to report we were seated immediately. The contemporary vibe paired with welcoming staff sets a pleasant scene. As for an affordable Michelin Star experience, it delivers. While the food ranged from okay to good, it didn't hit superb this time. However, I'm keen to give their prix fixe menu a go on my next visit, holding out hope that it'll elevate my opinion of the place.

I ordered delivery from here for the first time and it was so good. My order arrived hot and in less than 15 minutes.I ordered the Hummus Bowl with pita and a side of pulled pork (with no bbq sauce). Honestly it was some of the best hummus and pulled pork I've ever had. The hummus is creamy and amazing and the pulled pork is juicy and cooked perfectly. The pita was also delicious. You should definitely order Taboonette if you're in the mood for hummus or surprisingly, pulled pork haha.

Title: A Cozy Spot for Tsukemen Enthusiasts

I recently dined at a local restaurant renowned for its tsukemen, a Japanese dipping ramen, eager to relive memories of Los Angeles’ Tsujita. Arriving at 7:30 PM on a Sunday, I was seated promptly, although the place filled up quickly thereafter. This was my second visit, driven by curiosity and nostalgia.
