I ordered the Tonkotsu Tsukemen, anticipating the exceptional experience I had in LA. However, while it didn't quite live up to Tsujita's standards — the broth lacked the same richness and adhesion to the noodles — it was still enjoyable. The pros certainly outweighed my modest disappointment.

Pros:
- The service was stellar, complete with a thoughtful sake pairing and a hot stone provided to keep the broth warm.
- For tsukemen options in New York, this restaurant did not disappoint, especially given the perfectly cooked soft-boiled egg and the substantial portion size, despite the broth's unexpected tanginess.
- Ambiance is on-point: tasteful decor for a convivial dining experience or a night out with friends.

Cons:
- Exclusivity to walk-ins may deter some, but both my visits only required a maximum 20-minute wait for a party of two, so it shouldn't be a dealbreaker.

In summary, while it might not surpass Tsujita's tsukemen, this restaurant is definitely worth a visit for its great service, ample servings, and inviting atmosphere.

Best tacos ever. Reminds me of Mexican food in Queens. They're fresh and authentic. I always come here for lunch. It comes with guacamole sauce, onions, cilantro and the little red radishes. They even have a phone number and you can order ahead of time. There is usually a line and a wait. Def better than the fake Mexican places in the area such as Playa Betty's and El Mitote etc. although they are sit down restaurants and this is just a truck, if you want authentic tacos this is your place!

I was lucky that this place is next door to a bar. Sorry, I could not help myself. Lucky's is the perfect place to grab post-drinking burgers and fries and soak up some booze after barhopping in Hell's Kitchen. Overall, the place has decently priced burgers and friends. Are the burgers out of the world amazing? No. But, they definitely get the job done. In addition to the standard burgers, Lucky's have a wide array of chicken sandwiches, salads, and hot dogs. So, there's a little bit for everyone. The night of our visit (a Wednesday), our cashier/server was very cool and fun.

Great drinks, reasonably priced, and great food, albeit a bit limited for late lunch menu.   For appys, get the Brussel sprouts and onion slices - delicious!  For lunch, the Artic Char was a good portion with some nice spice.   My brick oven Soppresata pizza was terrific - it's hot soppesata so be ready for a little hot spice with a tangy sauce.   Really good!   I finished with an Affogato - ice cream and biscotti with espresso poured over - wow!

I love this place, great for date night or night out with friends. Their drinks are great and the food is awesome! They have plenty of vegetarian options which taste great for me. The service is awesome as well! @traveleen_gurl

Upon visiting the yakitori omakase that has raised some eyebrows considering its price point, I was pleasantly surprised. Despite initial skepticism, the experience proved to be more than just a meal; it was a full-on event. The ambience, the interactive show of the chefs at work, and the exquisitely prepared food justify the cost. Meat lovers might find this a welcome change from the usual sushi omakase.

The fare was deceptively simple but executed perfectly. Notably, the vegetable skewers were exceptional, and the commitment to a no-waste philosophy was evident with each skewer showcasing different parts of the chicken. The standout for me had to be the chicken oysters—absolutely divine.

Side dishes are available and recommended; they are an excellent complement to the skewers. Although I missed out on the ramen—temporarily unavailable—I'm told it's a returning favorite.

The service was impeccable, with staff ensuring our comfort and satisfaction throughout the extended sitting. That said, the one critique I have is the duration—a lengthy 2.5 hours—which might have been better if trimmed down to a more concise 1.5 hours.

Whether you're famished or just peckish, this yakitori omakase warrants at least one visit. It's a unique culinary retreat from the norm. My companion left quite full, while I wouldn't have minded a bit more—then again, I'm always up for more food.

Second time here and this time we came in a larger group on a weekday! I've always thought Lido is a little expensive thus the four stars, but their service is always top notch. Interior - they still got outside seating during the winter and its perfectly heated! Make sure to make a reservation during the weekend, they get busy.Service - though there were barely any customer cuz it's a random Tuesday during lunch, our server was delightful and helped us with separating the check, getting all different orders very efficiently.Taste - their winter menu is a bit small for brunch, and since i didn't want their signature French toast (which is delicious btw!), I went with the sausage omelette. It's great portion, comes with greens and the perfect ratio of toppings to eggs. Overall, I will always come back to lido for its amazing service. Thanks for making my day!

Bao by Kaya is one of my favorite Broadway Bites popups. The duck bao is my favorite, 2nd fave pork belly. The popcorn chicken with spicy mayo (basically karaage) is the perfect accompaniment. My husband just wants the duck bao so I buy 6 individual baos for him. What really makes the duck bao is the hoisin sauce.Broadway Bites tends to run out of duck by the end of the day, so I usually pick it up at lunchtime to take home for dinner. The bao hold up really well and don't get soggy.Never been to the actual location, but Bao regularly appears at Broadway Bites, conveniently located near work.

Title: Scenic Brunch with Room for Improvement

I recently visited this restaurant for a birthday brunch and my experience was a mixed bag. The service was a definite high point, with our server making us feel welcomed and ensuring our needs were met promptly.

The avocado toast presented a challenge with bread that was too tough, which detracted from the enjoyment of the dish. I also tried the pasta, but unfortunately, it was overcooked, and the excessive amount of romano cheese overpowered the delicate taste of truffles, which was a letdown.

However, not all was lost. The RH scramble was a standout, prepared flawlessly and a testament to the kitchen's potential. The drinks menu, on the other hand, was underwhelming and failed to impress.

The true star of the visit was the scenery. The restaurant offers an escape from the hustle and bustle of the city, making for a serene dining atmosphere that almost makes up for the culinary missteps. All in all, the setting made the experience better, but I hope the kitchen tweaks some dishes to match the lovely environment.

If you're in search of a great place for a business lunch, look no further. My coworkers and I have dined here multiple times, always experiencing prompt and professional service. The food consistently hits the mark, especially their sushi lunch special — a steal at $12 for any 2 rolls or $16 for any 3. And when the weather turns chilly, their ramen becomes a go-to. Highly recommend for a quick, satisfying midday meal.

My family and I recently dined at this restaurant and were left rather disappointed by our experience. The food quality was subpar; both the fried squid and fried soft-shell crab seemed to have been frozen rather than fresh. Additionally, the e-noodles with mushroom were improperly proportioned, consisting predominantly of mushrooms and falling short on noodles, which was insufficient for our group.

Vegetable dishes were a personal focal point due to my garlic intolerance; however, despite explicit instructions, our vegetables came with garlic, which was quite problematic for me. Customer service also detracted from our experience, as the staff displayed unprofessional and defensive behavior when we attempted to rectify a mistaken drink order.

Ultimately, the situation escalated to the extent that my aunt chose to leave the establishment in search of a correct smoothie elsewhere, underscoring the evening's frustrations. Sadly, we cannot recommend this restaurant based on our latest visit.

Title: A Swift and Satisfying Gem Near the Opera

Following an enchanting performance of The Phantom of the Opera, my companion and I seized the opportunity to dine at this nearby establishment. To our delight, we were promptly seated at the bar, captivated immediately by the expansive dining area and the warmth of the staff.

Service was attentive and personable, and our culinary journey commenced without delay. The sangria, rich and fruity, was a lovely prelude to the meal. The salad, abundant with fresh tangerine, was a burst of citrus delight, while the garlic bread provided the perfect garlicky crunch.

Every dish arrived swiftly, yet it was evident that speed did not compromise quality. The experience was a harmonious blend of timely service and delectable flavors.

For those in search of a quick bite without foregoing a flavorful experience, I highly recommend this restaurant. It’s a sure bet for a tasty and efficient dining encounter.

Peking Duck House presents itself as a typical Chinese restaurant bustling with activity. Service levels were satisfactory, neither exceptional nor disappointing. The highlight dish, Peking Duck, priced at $60, featured a smaller-sized bird. While the skin achieved a pleasant crispiness, the meat beneath was somewhat lacking in volume. Overall, the dining experience left no particularly memorable impression, casting doubt on the likelihood of a return visit.

Stopped by for a few happy hour drinks. Service at the bar was quick and efficient, but I was shocked to get the bill and see that one mixed drink was almost $14! For that price, I would have preferred for the drinks to be much stronger as well. The receipts aren't itemized, they just show you a grand total, so there's no way to see what you're paying for. The place was nice and spacious, but I definitely did not expect that price for a simple whiskey ginger.

Own by Stephen Starr, this place is grand and beautiful with a lavish 16th century Parisian decor. It has a club-like atmosphere with loud music playing in the background. So far I have came here for two occasions: my birthday dinner and a friend's bachelorette dinner. And on both occasions, the service, the food, and the drinks were spot on. Edamame Dumplings - I really like this appetizer. It's served with shallot-sauternes broth. The dumplings are silky soft, juicy, clean, and light with a rich edamame filing. Chilled Udon Noodles - It's served with a lime sorbet and peanut sauce. This dish is wonderful and it's perfect for the hot summer weather.Pork Buns - It's served with charred pork belly, spicy shallots, and Napa cabbage. The pork belly is tender with a perfect amount of fat and lean meat. It's really good. Spicy Yellowtail Sashimi - It's very fresh with a good amount of spiciness. I really like this one too.Glazed Alaskan Black Cod - Very flavorful. It's served with chili eggplant and black bean relish. For dessert, we have tried all of the desserts on their menu and they were all very good but my all time favorite is still the Crying Chocolate (special thanks to Anna H. & Richard E. for the hook up). P.S.: The hostess won't seat you unless everyone from your party has arrived. But regardless there's ample amounts of space for you to sit down and wait or to do photoshoots around the restaurant.

Tortaria presents a decidedly average dining experience. The offerings, such as the guacamole and chips, are passable yet hindered by pre-packaged portions that fall short when sharing. My entrée, a crispy eggplant bowl with added spicy chicken, left no lasting impression, echoing the sentiments of my companions' unremarkable selections. The portions across the board were underwhelming. While the margarita menu shows promise for those seeking a drink, those in pursuit of a fulfilling meal might consider exploring other local establishments.

I recently visited this spot with high expectations for their much-touted margaritas, and let me tell you, they did not disappoint! The margaritas were absolutely fantabulous—perfectly crafted with a balance of flavors that was both invigorating and refreshing.

As for the food, while it leans towards a super Americanized version of Mexican cuisine, it was quite decent indeed. It may not be the most authentic experience for a Mexican food purist, but it definitely hits the spot for those looking for familiar flavors. The highlight, however, was the salsa served with the chips—this Smokey concoction was super yummy and added a delightful kick to the starter.

All in all, a great place for a drink and some satisfying, albeit Americanized, Mexican fare.

Title: A Disappointing Delivery Experience

Unfortunately, my experience with this restaurant fell well below expectations. While many have praised their food and service, my delivery order was marred by mistakes and overpricing, leading me to caution potential future customers.

The latte, priced at $5.50, was a letdown. It arrived in a small cup, not filled to the top, and contained coffee grounds instead of the promised espresso – nothing but an expensive cup of coffee with almond milk.

The broccolini, while flavorful with fresh garlic, was not worth its $9 price tag considering the meager portion size. And the Smith Burger, coming in at $17, was equally disappointing. The burger featured a minimal amount of bacon and pickles, and despite my request for mixed greens, I received a side of subpar fries – thin, soggy, and both dry and oily at the same time.

Spending $47.88 on this meal felt like money down the drain, especially after kindly leaving a tip. I regret to say that I cannot recommend this establishment, and I will certainly not be a repeat customer.

Hidden away in ABC city, Yoli's is a modest jewel that shines with the warmth of Dominican hospitality and the rich flavors of homestyle cooking. This quaint eatery specializes in breakfast and lunch, offering a takeout option with a few in-house stools for those who prefer to savor their meal in its snug interior. Despite the limited seating, the vibrant community gardens and public spaces nearby provide ample opportunity for al fresco dining.

Don't be put off by the space's unpolished charm; Yoli's prides itself on delivering authentic Dominican comfort food that's big on taste and low on frills. The menu, scrawled above the counter, may not reflect the day's actual offerings, but the rotating selection of proteins—chicken, beef, pork, and sometimes fish—promises something for everyone. They're served with perfectly cooked rice and beans or starchy sides like tostones, all doled out in generous portions across small ($5), medium ($7), and large ($9) sizes.

Standouts include the succulent pollo guisado (braised chicken) and flavorful braised pork, both of which are steeped in layers of island spice. While I've yet to try the pernil (roast pork), anticipation runs high based on the consistent quality of Yoli's dishes.

The experience may confuse first-timers with limited Spanish or unfamiliarity with Dominican cuisine, but it's part of the charm and adventure Yoli's brings to the table. Aim for lunch when the kitchen is bustling with the day’s fullest selection—just be mindful that once a dish is gone, it's gone for the day.

Service at Yoli's is unhurried and friendly, insisting that you slow down and enjoy the moment. The eatery's regular clientele, an integral part of the ambiance, welcome you into the fold. With a chilled beverage in hand from the fridge, embrace the leisurely pace and let the flavors of the Dominican Republic transport you, if only for a meal. Yoli's is a true testament to the love of feeding people, encapsulating the essence of the DR in every bite. Mic dropped, experience savored.

I've been eating Vietnamese food for a long time and I've gotta say I am impressed with Madame Vo!! The food is impeccable and I can see what all the hype is about. There are many dishes available that reminded me of the food I had in Vietnam and it did not disappoint! I made a reservation for 8pm on a Wednesday, thinking that I'd be able to walk in and grab a table if I arrived early. The yelp reviews were not kidding, it is was super packed even on a weeknight, making walk ins difficult. I eventually got seated 10 minutes after my reservation since the previous party did not leave yet. This place was really poppin' with liveliness and made for a fun experience. The prices are a little higher than your average Vietnamese restaurant, but it excelled in terms of the whole dining experience. FOOD - we ordered some appetizers to share on top of our entrees. We got the chicken wings, the banh xeo, the bun bo hue, the vermicelli dish with pork + spring rolls, the grilled pork chops over rice, and the madame vo pho with short rib. We also ordered a bunch of drinks - 2 coconuts, a coconut smoothie, and the lychee refresher. I gotta say the actual coconut drink was my favorite. All of the dishes turned out amazing, especially the chicken wings!! Definitely try that out if you're a fan of spice. My main suggestion would be to make your reservation in advance to secure your table!

It's located in a hotel. It will blow you away. Awesome Italian. It's fast you can slow it down if you ask but we were in drinks apps and dinner in about an hour. Delicious. Probably the best Caesar   salad I ever had. And the black ravioli stuffed with lobster !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!For I must say I have it to my wife. But I told her that is what you want. When she got it it was insanely good. I had a chicken dish which was nice but not like the ravioli.

Title: Zesty Thai Delights with a Kick!

Last night, I visited a local Thai spot and decided to try the Lemongrass Chicken with Panang Curry over jasmine rice - a decision I didn't regret. The chicken was perfectly juicy, tender, and the curry packed a serious punch of spice that was exhilarating for those who dare. As for sides, I opted for the Larb Mushroom and Cucumber Salad. Both were sweet, a bit too much for my palette after several bites, overshadowing the main dish's flavors.

I had hoped for green beans or cauliflower, but it seemed they were out, perhaps due to my late arrival. The staff, however, were the epitome of friendly and service was fast, adding to the experience of savoury Thai cuisine.

An added bonus for eco-conscious diners, their ongoing promotion (valid through December 2019) offers a free side when you bring your own bowl. It’s initiatives like these that make me eager to return—not just for the delicious food, but also to support environmentally friendly practices.

In summary, I'd definitely return for another round of that delectable curry, although next time I'll be sure to diversify my side choices for a more balanced meal.

Nestled amidst the bustling Upper West Side, The Viand catches the eye with its charming shades and inviting outdoor seating area. On a recent visit, my companion and I were lucky to nab one of the last tables in this evidently popular spot.

The coffee service was unremarkable, yet satisfyingly hot; a standard fare that served its purpose without fanfare. Meanwhile, the menu presented an intriguing blend of diner classics and upscale offerings. I was particularly taken by the Mediterranean flatbread appetizer – a medley of olives, onions, tomatoes, and feta, skillfully combined into what I consider one of the best flatbreads around. My entrée, blueberry pancakes topped with a dollop of whipped cream, didn't disappoint either. Fluffy and light, they were a delightful testament to the kitchen's prowess.

Service at The Viand was commendable. Our waiter was prompt and efficient, contributing to an overall superior dining experience.

Would I return? Absolutely. The Viand delivered on both food and service, making it a must-stop whenever I find myself in the neighborhood once more.

Title: A Charming Venue with Authentic Flavors

I recently dined at a delightful restaurant that offers a refreshing approach to portion sizes – serving dishes that are perfectly adequate without being overwhelming. While the menu prices may not reflect the smaller portions, the quality of the food certainly justifies the cost. The highlight of my visit was the pasta, notably fresh and served so promptly it could have still been dreaming of the pot. The carbonara I chose was a solid rendition, with a luxuriously rich sauce and pasta hot enough to gently cook the egg yolk as it was stirred in. Although I found myself yearning for a touch of sweet onion or perhaps a sprinkle of peas for added texture and flavor, the dish was nonetheless satisfying. All in all, the restaurant's ambiance is as inviting as its fare, and based on the quality of the pasta alone, I am eager to return and sample their pizza. If the pasta is anything to go by, I'm sure my next visit will be just as memorable.

I returned once again to my go-to taco spot in NYC, a testament to its irresistible allure. The cashier's inquiry about my prior visits was met with a fervent affirmation – I'm a repeat customer for a reason! As usual, I indulged in two Carne Asada tacos which were nothing short of heavenly. This place consistently confirms why it's my favorite.

My recent visit to Maya left me underwhelmed. The service was notably slow and lacked attentiveness, detracting from the dining experience. The food itself failed to impress—my fish tacos, unfortunately, featured a soggy fried fish that reminded me of lackluster frozen fish sticks. Additionally, their margaritas didn't hit the mark and were forgettable. Considering the abundance of Mexican cuisine options in the city, I'd suggest exploring other establishments for a more satisfying meal.
Cute and cozy date spot.  The food was very good.  The atmosphere was ok the best part is that cooking at the table can be cozy. The staff was friendly the drinks were delicious.

Title: A Delightful Taste of Russia at Mari Vanna

My dining experience at Mari Vanna, post its summer renovation, was nothing short of delightful. Accompanied by a Russian friend, whose expertise guided our ordering, the evening kicked off on a positive note. Despite being opening night and the restaurant filling up quickly, our reservation ensured a seamless start to a flavorsome adventure.

The set-up of our meal included a variety of appetizers and shared entrees, allowing us to sample a wider range of dishes. The Herring Under a Fur Coat was a commendable rendition of the classic, although a tad small for the price; thankfully, my indifference towards carrots ameliorated my inability to discern them in the dish. We dabbled in a culinary dilemma over the Siberian versus veal Pilmeni, settling on the former for its dual-meat offering. While I found the dough somewhat on the thicker side, it might very well adhere to tradition.

An unexpected highlight was the Georgian Pizza, not definitively listed on the menu but graciously crafted upon request. It stood out with its absence of tomato sauce and use of atypical cheese for pizza, culminating in what became my favorite dish of the evening.

Our time was constrained to an hour and a half due to policy, yet it proved ample for our pre-theater dinner. I left Mari Vanna with a satisfied palate and an eagerness to return, particularly with the famed medovik in my culinary crosshairs. For a genuine and delicious Russian dining experience, this place certainly earns my recommendation.

I remember when this place opened over a year ago the line was for hours long and that they even ran out during their soft opening. I'm not sure if things changed throughout the past year, but the Tonkatsu Chasu Jiro Ramen was subpar compared to the vast variety of choices around Manhattan. The ramen was almost like a thinner and chewier udon noodle, which I did not expect. Furthermore the broth was way too heavy, leaving me slightly nauseous after my meal. Two stars because they were generous with that chasu and the place was relatively clean. Also, the stone reheating method was really cool, especially if you get the tsukumen. Despite this, I would not come back.

I recently dined at a restaurant that maintains the reputable quality consistent with its other locations. The food was top-notch, and a standout dish is the Chinese hamburger - a reliable choice that has yet to disappoint. However, the ambiance was slightly marred by a chilly draft common in the winter months. Overall, a nice place for a satisfying meal if you can overlook the need for an extra layer of warmth.

Title: A Warm Cuban Escape in Chilly NYC

On a frosty night with the mercury dipping to -20C, my companions from Portland and Mumbai sought a lively dining experience in the bustling heart of New York City. We navigated the typical Saturday evening crowds and the daunting task of last-minute reservations until we stumbled upon Havana Central at Times Square – a vibrant Cuban oasis that welcomed us without the anticipated wait.

Despite the full house, service was prompt, and we quickly nestled into our seats, surrounded by grand paintings that pay homage to Cuba. The restaurant's authenticity extended to the live Cuban band, filling the space with an infectious energy that tempted us to dance. However, our focus remained on the culinary offerings of the night.

We sipped on Draft Modelo and Sangria, curiously served in Brooklyn Brewery glasses, yet no less delicious. The Caribbean Wings, while not the anticipated flavor, were a pleasant honey-sauced deviation. The Chicharrones, however, fell short, failing to deliver as a standout dish and resembling something you might find at a fast-food chain.

On a positive note, the Salmon & Shrimp with yellow rice and black beans was a hit among us, and although the Paella de vegetables was stickier than preferred, it was tasty. The Fiesta Avocado Salad rounded out the meal nicely.

Throughout the evening, the ebb and flow of live music paired well with our lively conversations and the overall dining experience. While not all dishes impressed, the company, coupled with the vibrant ambiance and good food, crafted a memorable night at Havana Central. A suitable retreat for those looking to thaw in the heart of a chilly New York City night.

Title: A Hidden Gem with Soulful Jazz in NYC

My recent discovery in NYC's bustling scene is nothing short of awesome—a true hidden gem that jazz enthusiasts and whiskey lovers alike should not miss. Despite having made my home in the Big Apple for half a decade, it was only while seeking out live jazz that I stumbled upon this fantastic spot.

From the moment you're greeted at the entrance till the very end of your visit, the staff's warmth enhances the experience. Their attentive service is just the icing on the cake in an ambiance that's perfectly suited for a romantic evening out. We had a reservation, which landed us prime seating right in front of the stage, but there's ample space for all party sizes and even an open bar area for those looking to mingle.

The venue's reputation for an impressive whiskey selection is well-deserved. The menu boasts an array of choices, and the server's recommendations were spot-on, guiding us through a delightful tasting journey, though, admittedly, the names of our drinks escape me now.

While we didn't indulge in the food offerings—none seemed particularly intriguing—the music more than made up for it. The venue hosts two bands each night. While the early set was decent, I highly recommend the later performance which truly resonated and showcased exceptional talent.

In summary, if you have a penchant for smooth jazz tunes and a fine glass of whiskey, this place is an absolute must-visit.

I am not a big fan of this place or especially the stuff we ordered. This is only for the Lunch menu, please note not for the dinner menu. The service was average as the waiter made a face when we asked to be seated in the corner place(the restaurant was almost empty and we had reservations through yelp). It seemed like the waiter had some issues with our table while he was happily serving other tables sitting adjacent to us(in the same area). I am not too thrilled with this place as their food is a little bland and is not spicy at all. If you want your food to be spicy then please don't visit this place even their harissa is not spicy. I would have still voted for this place if the food was flavorful but it wasn't and it was a big disappointment. It took me a long time to finish my burger and the potato fries on the side were too much to take and it also took forever to finish. The food is very healthy and well represented but not for me. They didn't have great selection of entrees too. We ordered the burger (same order for 3 ppl) and ordered grilled tofu sandwich which was so so dry we could hardly chew on it. Definitely not coming back.

Title: A Manhattan Gem for Korean Noodle Lovers

If you're hankering for authentic and affordable Korean bites, make sure to visit this remarkable noodle stand nestled inside Food Gallery 32 on 32nd Street, but be sure to plan accordingly as they shut their doors in the afternoon.

Amidst the bustling Korean stalls offering an array of delicacies, this newly opened spot has quickly earned a devoted following, and it's no wonder why. The dishes here are not only delicious and hearty but also easy on the wallet—a rare find in Manhattan.

Its location in a Korean food court may be unexpected in this part of the city, but it stands out, potentially outshining even the offerings at Canal Street Market. The food served here feels more wholesome, more filling, and with a touch of authenticity that is often sought but seldom found.

In summary, for a food experience that's as fulfilling as it is affordable, this Korean food stand is a must-visit. Just remember to get there before the afternoon hours to indulge in a truly satisfying meal.

BCD is one of my favorite places in the K-town area!  For this review, my friend and I came around 5pm on a Thursday.  We were seated immediately and the restaurant was about half full.  By the time we left around 6pm, it was packed and there was a line.  I've eaten at BCD during both peak lunch and dinner times and they have an efficient system and quick turnaround.  Of course, if you can, try to avoid the rush!  I haven't tried anything here besides the soondubu since that's what they are known for.  I've had the soondubu with curry ($13.99), beef ($14.99), dumplings ($14.99), seafood ($14.99), and pork ($14.99).  The dumpling soondubu is my favorite.  You can customize the spiciness of your dish.  If you can eat kimchi, you can handle the regular level.  I have always drained by bowl and left happy.  There's nothing particularly outstanding about BCD's soondubu but it gets the job done if you have a craving.  I also think BCD is overpriced across the board.  Service here is a mixed bag depending on the time you come and the person you get.  Expect service to be worse during peak times.  I've never had an issue with the time it took for my food to come out though. One thing that sets BCD apart from other restaurants in the area is their variety of banchan.  Overall, BCD is a safe choice to satisfy a soondubu craving!

Banter is a small, cute and artsy place for brunch. The vibe the restaurant gives off is very nice and is probably great for some insta posts. However, regarding the food, it wasn't my favorite. The food wasn't bad, but it didn't leave me amazed or wanting to return again after my meal. The price for the food just wasn't worth it for me. I ordered the sweet potato fries with some spicy mayo sauce and 2 poached eggs on toast. I was honestly kind of disappointed, the eggs barely covered the toast and the sweet potato fries were just normal fries. My favorite part about my meal was probably the spicy mayo sauce, that was good! Overall, an okay place that I personally would not recommend, but if you're looking for a brunch place with a good atmosphere and don't mind paying a few extra bucks for an ordinary brunch then this is the place for you!

Nestled in the vibrant East Village, Jiang Diner offers a delectable escape into Northwestern Chinese cuisine, featuring bold cumin and Szechuan pepper flavors that invigorate the palate. During a pleasantly quiet lunchtime visit, the attentiveness of our server enhanced the dining experience.

The highlight was the XinJiang big plate chicken with bone, a harmonious mingling of savory chicken, onions, and peppers atop a bed of hand-cut noodles that masterfully captured the robust sauce. The dish's texture and taste left a lasting impression.

Additionally, we savored the steamed lamb shumai. These lamb dumplings, swimming in hot soup with delicate, translucent skins, were packed with umami. They're best enjoyed fresh and piping hot. There's also a beef variant for those who prefer different meat options – while H favored the lamb, I found the beef version superior in savor.

We couldn't resist the crispy fried lamb short ribs, boasting a perfectly seasoned cumin crust. The meat was succulent and fell off the bone, the fried exterior executed impeccably.

Jiang Diner is a gem to be revisited, offering rich flavors that promise a delightful return to those eager for more.

Probably some of the best tacos I've ever had. The only reason it doesn't get 5 stars is because they were out of the pork tacos. From reading other reviews, this seems like a common problem. I got the steak, chicken, and cactus tacos. The steak was so tender. The chicken was okay, nothing special. The cactus was unique - not my type of taco, but good vegetarian option. We had to wait in line, but it actually went by super fast. It's not your typical sit down. They have standing tables where you can quickly grab a bite for a fair price! Highly recommend!

Title: A Disheartening Return to a Once-Favored Pho Spot

As a former New York local and a Vietnamese cuisine enthusiast, I frequented this restaurant for their reliably excellent pho. After a two-year hiatus, I returned with high expectations but was met with a disheartening culinary experience. The pho Dac Biet deluxe, which I anticipated eagerly, was disappointingly bland—a far cry from the rich, flavorful broth that is the hallmark of good pho.

Attempting to salvage the dish with hoisin sauce and Sriracha did little to infuse it with the necessary zest, leaving me with a bowl that hardly justified its $16 price tag. The dearth of meat in the so-called deluxe bowl only added to my dissatisfaction.

Despite this culinary letdown, I must commend the staff for their service and the restaurant's ambient setting, which earns the establishment a generous two-star rating. However, I lament the downturn in the quality of a dish that once brought me much joy.

I'm in NYC for the weekend and really wanted Italian food.  Baker & Co had really good reviews (plus) and they take reservations on Open Table (double plus). The service was excellent. I had the gnudi which was vegetarian friendly & so delicious. Would definitely go back when I'm in town again!

Title: A Slice Above the Rest: Unforgettable Artichoke Pizza

If you're torn between pizza joints in the NY area, let me make your decision easier. Among the top contenders - Artichoke, Joe's, and Prince's - one reigns supreme in my book: Artichoke.

Their signature artichoke pizza is an absolute revelation, boasting a creamy, rich topping that'll remind you of the most decadent pasta sauce, cradled by a perfectly cooked dough. This isn't just another slice; it's a slice that gets better with every bite, leaving you eagerly anticipating the next. The flavor is sumptuous, bordering on addictive, making it the highlight of any New York trip and a must-visit for any pizza aficionado in Berkeley, CA.

Artichoke's pizza isn't just good; it redefines the pizza experience. It stands out not only for its unique taste but also for how it successfully makes each mouthful more delightful than the last. I personally can't wait to indulge again. Whether you're a local or just passing through, make sure Artichoke is on your culinary itinerary. Trust me, you won't regret it.

Title: A Gem in the Meatpacking District

Review:

Pastis truly lives up to its reputation, offering an exceptional dining experience in the heart of NYC's meatpacking district. The decor is both beautiful and buzzing with energy, perfectly complementing the vibrancy of the area.

The menu didn't disappoint; the food was fresh and every dish we tried was a hit. The filet mignon was tender, the burger juicy, and the fries with garlic aioli were a flavorful twist on a classic. Standouts included the delectable steak tartare and a crab salad that was the epitome of light and refreshing.

Although we had no room left for dessert, it simply means a return visit is in order. Scoring a reservation might be tough, but it's worth the effort for a taste of Pastis' offerings. Don't hesitate—if you have the chance to dine here, even late at night, take it.

Although I was wary of eating here at first because of all the recent hype, I was pleasantly surprised! This modern, hip Vietnamese restaurant serves up different types of pho, as well as a variety of rice dishes and vermicelli bowls if you're not feeling like having soup. I was intrigued by the fusion dish "Viet X Cajun Pho" (crawfish, shrimp, corn, and rice noodle in Cajun seafood broth) off their summer menu, and decided to try it with soft shell crab. The bowl came out HUGE compare to my friend's pho, and I loved the crispiness of the crab, bites of sweet corn, and the bold, fragrant seafood broth in it. I still think that I'd like the regular pho with beef broth more, but really enjoyed the Cajun twist to this one.Note that this spot is cash only!

I was invited to brunch by one of my favorite people we have been planning on having brunch for the longest time but the weather has been awful. In the matters of rescheduling we finally decided on this weekend and no matter what we will make it to Cafe Clung. I actually met my friend there because she lives close by I arrived to this place which is on a quiet street in the city's West Village. When I arrived the hostess ushered me to where my friend was seated it was early so the place was still quiet, this French place had a cozy atmosphere about it , the wait staff were all wearing stripped shirts which gives it  a Paris sense of style. After sitting down and a little chit chat I ordered coffee with half and half while we browsed through the menu. We finally decided on the Breakfast sandwich for me and my friend had the Egg Benedict with a side a fries for both of us. The coffee was absolutely delicious and the food I must say was the best I think my sandwich was on a brioche bun which I loved. I must come back to try the French toast I heard it is delicious.

Title: Unforgettable Artisanal Pizza Experience

I recently visited an extraordinary pizza haven that has easily climbed to the top of my favorites. The magic starts with their bread – an unforgettable foundation that's soft, flavorful, and flawlessly harmonizes with a generous array of topping choices. While prices are slightly above average, the culinary experience is worth every penny, and I'd happily pay more for another round.

The staff's attentive service complements the open-kitchen ambiance, where guests can admire their meals being crafted in traditional, old-style ovens. Their commitment to authenticity is indeed a reason to indulge in their slightly pricier offerings.

Forewarning to potential visitors: parking is a rare commodity in the vicinity. Opting for a taxi or the subway might save you some pre-dining frustration. Also, consider throttling back on the in-house spirits – they're notably pricey. A pre-meal visit to the adjacent bar could be both strategic for your wallet and the perfect prelude to pizza bliss.

Final verdict? A resounding A+ for those ready to invest in top-tier pizza artisanship.

Title: A Charming Lunch Spot in the Heart of Manhattan

I can confidently say that dining at this Manhattan establishment offers a remarkable experience, particularly for a sunny day lunch. The restaurant exudes a charming ambience, complemented by a soothing, vintage soundtrack, perfect for a touch of romance.

The staff's amiability and professionalism enhance the experience; the waiter impressed me with enthusiastic meal suggestions, indicative of their genuine appreciation for the menu. The French Onion soup, a highly praised dish, did not disappoint. It was a delightful dance of gooey cheese and steaming broth, presented with an eye for elegance.

For a lighter touch, the mussels were tantalizing to the nose and tender to the taste, though they could benefit from a spike in flavor. Nevertheless, the accompanying sauce was splendid for bread dipping, which arrives at no extra cost.

Considering the quality of food, its French culinary roots, and its coveted Soho location, the prices struck me as quite reasonable. For a satiating meal or a light bite in an enchanting setting, this restaurant is a commendable choice.

Title: A Charming Brunch at The Mermaid Inn, UWS

After much anticipation, I finally dined at The Mermaid Inn on the Upper West Side, a place I had long admired from afar. My companion and I snagged a reservation for an 11 AM Saturday brunch and were promptly seated upon arrival in their inviting main room, bathed in natural light—perfect for people-watching.

The ambiance of the restaurant is effortlessly cozy, with white walls and delightful nautical accents that make for a relaxed dining experience. Opting for the baked egg shakshuka, priced at $15, I was thrilled. The dish, familiar from a past encounter in Boston, did not disappoint. A well-balanced blend of roasted peppers, spinach, and feta paired with bread made for a satisfying, flavorful meal that left me eager to recommend it to other brunch enthusiasts.

The service at The Mermaid Inn matched the quality of the food—attentive and efficient, ensuring our coffee cups were never empty. Given the popularity of the spot, I suggest booking in advance, as it quickly fills up.

In conclusion, The Mermaid Inn proved to be an ideal locale for a laid-back brunch. The lunch offerings also caught my eye, so a return visit appears to be on the horizon.

I went in a little after the opening hours over the weekend and within the hour, the entire place was packed. They had a really bad start as they weren't ready when I went in, they told us that they were also short staffed, and ultimately, they messed up on just about all the orders in the restaurant. I saw most people grow increasingly upset, shaking their heads (as was I, tbh!) when most of us kept receiving the wrong order. I didn't get my food until about 45 minutes after ordering, and I was the first to order. The One & Only Spring roll was half slightly burnt and it was presented to me with the burnt parts face down, see the pictures! It didn't taste burnt, but the texture, it basically fell apart after dipping into the fish sauce - that they forgot to add fish sauce to. They mentioned that the person who usually handles the sauce was not in that day. This excuse is mind boggling to me, how do you serve your customers the fish sauce for dipping without the main ingredient? When I finally received my correct medium pho tai, they still got my order wrong as I had requested no greens and I spent the next few minutes picking them out. As for the food and broth itself? This is probably the only Northern style that I've encountered and like. The broth is on the lighter and sweeter side with a bit of depth. You won't get your bean sprouts, basil or lime with your pho, so don't expect those. They need to get their priorities in order in order to thrive here. They did apologize for the service and we did received their 25% discount for August even after we mentioned that they didn't put any fish sauce in their dipping sauce. I understand that the restaurant is new but there isn't an excuse for burnt food, forgotten main ingredient for a sauce, and messing up just about most of the orders in a span of one hour. Extremely disappointed in the service that was experienced that day.

Title: A Disappointing Dining Experience at a 5-Star Hotel's Restaurant

I had high hopes for brunch in the restaurant of a luxury hotel where the rooms and service are exceptional. Unfortunately, the restaurant did not live up to the hotel's 5-star reputation. The ambiance was the only aspect that matched the grandeur of the hotel; everything else fell short.

For roughly $100, the breakfast offerings were underwhelming. It seemed telling that the restaurant was nearly empty. It's a shame the service was not more attentive — our waiter mixed up our order with another table and even charged us incorrectly after our departure. Moreover, items from our order were forgotten and required a reminder.

The food quality was comparable to that of a complimentary hotel breakfast buffet, but with a much higher price tag. The pastry basket was a letdown, with only the croissant passing muster. The so-called cheese danish lacked any real cheese, and the muffin was mediocre at best. One might find better value at a local deli.

The crab cake benedict was merely average and did not justify its price tag. Although the poached egg was well-executed, the accompanied few potato wedges felt almost stingy. The saving grace was the bacon, which was forgotten initially but delivered perfectly crisp upon reminder.

In sum, this establishment is in dire need of reevaluation, especially when the surrounding competition likely offers better value. It's my hope that hotel management will take note of these reviews to improve the restaurant experience.

Came for dinner with a friend. The place is decorated beautifully, but the chairs are not comfortable and look like crap. The staff is awesome. The menu was interesting and the food was solid for the most part. We ordered an appetizer sized portion of risotto to start. It had a really good flavor, but it was undercooked. The rice was way too hard and not pleasant. The peas in the dish sort of overpowered it too. For our entrée we shared a 16 Oz ribeye. It was served with a hassle back potato and a fennel, red onion salad. This was delicious. We also ordered 2 sides. Asparagus and sautéed broccoli rabe. The asparagus was perfectly seasoned and cooked well. The broccoli rabe was okay. The waitress surprised us with a delicious dessert to make up for the risotto. I would definitely come back to try the pasta.

On a late Saturday afternoon, I stumbled upon a rather unassuming sandwich shop. The aesthetic was no frills with supplies visible, non-operational TVs, and dated furniture. Despite its appearance and the lone staff member working the counter, the experience was pleasantly surprising.

I ordered the Classic Sandwich, priced at a reasonable $7.50, featuring shredded pork and ham topped with a generous heap of pickled veggies on a toasted bun. While simplicity led my expectations, the sandwich impressed with its flavorful filling and non-greasy nature, albeit after discarding some of the excess carrots to achieve the perfect meat-to-bread balance.

The woman behind the counter was amiable, efficiently serving our food within minutes. While the shop's ambiance and food presentation won't cause a stir, the taste and swift service make it a worthwhile stop for anyone seeking a quick and satisfying bite.

I visited this location for my last meal and Manhattan. I finally found a winners. The waiters and waitresses are super courteous and provide top notch service. The Pesto Fettuccine was amazing. The cheese cake and Tiramasu were to die for.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Kenka in East Village

I recently visited Kenka on Saint Mark Street, drawn in by the buzz that usually surrounds this East Village haunt. Expectations were high thanks to its reputation for eclectic installation art and a promise of authentic Japanese fare.

Regrettably, the experience didn't live up to the hype. The menu, while ambitiously priced, delivered disappointment. I found the chicken skin inedible—tough to the point of frustration—and the rest of the dishes lacked the depth of flavor one would anticipate from genuine Japanese cuisine. This was not the culinary adventure I had been excited for; it was, frankly, a disaster.

Service was middling at best; a perplexing wait outside despite visibly unoccupied tables within added a needless chill to the evening.

In an attempt to be fair, considering the establishment's popularity and unique atmosphere, I'm offering a generous 3-star rating. However, this is a gentle reminder that not all that glitters on Saint Mark Street is gold.

Title: A Salty Experience at a Hibachi Grill

As someone who has outgrown the dazzle of Western hibachi restaurants, my recent visit to a popular grill came with a heavy dose of skepticism. I accompanied a friend with the hope that my past disappointments would not be mirrored, yet my experience hovered around the expected.

The exuberant performance typically associated with hibachi dining wasn't enough to distract from the main issue: an overzealous use of soy sauce. The inundation of salt was regrettable, as it smothered the potential nuances of flavor in the vegetables, fried rice, sirloin steak, and particularly the scallops — a dish that pained me to see oversalted.

Moreover, my request for a medium-cooked steak went unheeded, as it arrived well-done, a disappointing slip in quality. On a brighter note, the matcha pork buns provided a palatable reprieve from the salt-laden affair.

The waiter's performance, albeit corny, is part of the packaged entertainment, complemented by the playful tradition of catching zucchini with your mouth and the complimentary sake streams.

In conclusion, a hibachi outing is best approached with expectations angled towards the showmanship rather than a culinary delight. It's a venue for those looking for a lively night out, not a gourmet experience. 

A final word to the dieter at my table: deception is no substitute for willpower. Your antics did not go unnoticed.

Honestly one of the best restaurants I have been to in NYC is a long time. I tried to come here a month ago but the wait was more then an hour and now I know why. The menu is promoted to be ordered in a tapas style so they suggest for two people to order 3-4 plates. Not a problem for me, I am a huge foodie. The menu is extensive with every item having a photo corresponding with the description. I actually loved that because then I knew what the item would actually be like (plates came out looking just like the pics). We ended up ordering the spare ribs, one of the fried chicken dishes and two sushi rolls; Dynamite and Volcano I think. The sushi was incredibly good! We would have ordered more but we had to leave to make a comedy show. The two apps were good but the sushi outshined them by far. Mew also has a fun drink menu. I order the Moscow Mewle and my dinner parter ordered one of the other cocktails. Great price for the drink, they were each $9. Such a great price for a good drink in NY. We finished with a Zen Sake bottle. The decor is warm and inviting. Kind of modern industrial with some quirky pieces like the sewing machine by the bathroom. I have already been back once and I definitely see this place being a every two weeks stop kind of place.

Title: Hidden Gem in the Food Court

I popped into this unassuming spot for a lunch break on a Monday and found it tucked away on the first floor's right corner, just past the stairs. Opting for the beef pho to-go, I was impressed by the impeccable packaging – the steaming broth survived the journey back to my desk without incident.

The meal was deconstructed for optimal freshness, with crisp bean sprouts, vibrant cilantro, zesty lime, and the essential sriracha and hoisin sauce on the side, allowing customization to taste. The rice noodles hit that sweet spot of being flawlessly al dente, though the beef serving left me yearning for just a few more savory slices. However, the star was undoubtedly the broth, rich in flavor, aromatic, and thankfully not weighed down by excess oil.

Service here was a highlight – staff were not only friendly but efficient, ensuring a swift return to my work without a long wait.

In spite of longing for a bit more meat in my meal, the overall experience has left me curious about their noodle variety. This place has earned a return visit on my calendar.

Title: A Dim Sum Delight in Chinatown

If you're craving authentic dim sum, look no further than this bustling hotspot in Chinatown, which may just serve the best dim sum in the neighborhood. Be forewarned: weekends are peak times, and despite a promised 15-minute wait, be prepared to linger for closer to 30 minutes before being seated. But the wait is well worth it.

Our party of four came ravenous and left both sated and $99 lighter – a testament to the quality and addictive nature of the fare on offer. The user-friendly carts feature signs with pictures of the dishes, aiding diners in their quest to sample a variety of delights. A pro tip: engage with the cart attendants—our limited Chinese was enough to successfully navigate the menu.

Among the standout treats are the adorable pig-shaped custard buns, which are easy to miss concealed within their steamy vessel, so keep your eyes peeled for their cart. Equally memorable are the rich baked bbq pork buns, the sweet pineapple buns, and the savory bbq pork pastries. Veggie lovers, be advised: green options are sparse here.

In short, this restaurant not only rivals but surpasses the experience at Jing Fong, offering a dim sum feast that's not to be missed. Indulge in the variety and be enchanted by the flavors—just don't count on fulfilling your daily vegetable quota.

This review is based soley on the tea and ambience as we didn't order any food. First of all, the waitresses were amazing and very attentive. Never coming over to often or not enough. P.S, there's free hot water refills for your tea. I think we tried 5 or 6 teas all in all. Each with complex flavor notes. A lot people I saw had ordered the duck, so maybe next time I'll pair the food and the tea. For a quiet intimate date this was a great place to sip on some tea!

Tucked into the heart of the city, this gem of a lunch spot has quickly become my go-to destination. One of its greatest luxuries is never having to wait for a seat, coupled with the efficiency of service that ensures your food arrives promptly.

Remarkably, the establishment does not entertain tipping, which is a refreshing departure from the norm. For those who enjoy a sweet treat after their meal, the presence of a bubble tea shop next door is a delightful bonus.

The star of the menu for me has always been the katsu – a dish that manages to be tender, bursting with flavor, yet remains crisp without weighing you down after your meal. My companions have vouched for the quality of the bowls as well, though my loyalty to the katsu hasn’t wavered just yet, it’s tempting to explore more of what they have to offer.

In sum, this restaurant is a fantastic choice for anyone looking for quick, delicious food in a comfortable setting.

This is a very fun atmosphere! It is definitely a dance spot. I had come during Sunday brunch. We had stayed upstairs in the booth area which was nice. Staff, dancers, bartenders were all great. The menu is pre-fix and we were able to try it all. Some dishes were good, desserts were great!. The DJ played all the latest hits and it had everyone dancing. Make sure to wear a matte foundation because you will be dancing. Lol Fyi, parking is always better on Sundays in the City.

BG is located at the 7th floor of Bergdorf Goodman building and overlooks Central Park looking towards the NorthWe went for Sunday afternoon tea and had a 3pm seating for 4 people We arrived a minute or two early and they promptly greeted us and took us to our table. We were fortunate to have a window table on a fall weekend when the nyc marathon was going on Wonderful service from white jacketed professionals for the entire event. They served the tea and champagne very quickly followed by the towers of sandwiches and sweets I highly recommend!

During a weekend lunch escapade at Galata in NYC, my friend and I stumbled upon an unbeatable deal - an appetizer, soup, and main dish for just $18. We kicked off with warm Turkish bread dipped in fresh olive oil, which was simply delightful. For starters, my friend's shepherd's salad was a fresh combo of tomato and cucumber, while the creamy hummus I chose paired excellently with the bread.

Moving on to the soups, we savored the lentil and chicken soups. The addition of a lemon wedge was a zesty touch that enhanced the flavors. Our main courses, a veggie casserole for my friend and a Mediterranean salad topped with chicken for me, were both refreshingly light yet satisfying.

The staff at Galata were notably accommodating and the atmosphere was cozy and versatile, suitable for families, groups, or a romantic date. This spot has certainly earned a return visit from me. Highly recommended for anyone craving authentic Turkish cuisine without breaking the bank!

A fun, atypical spot for brunch. I'd never think to get tapas for breakfast, but my friends and I loved it. You have a couple options, either you order individual meals a la carte, or you can get their $42 brunch deal. That seems like a lot per person for brunch, but you definitely get your money's worth. The brunch deal gets you your choice of 4 tapas, a main dish of benedict or paella, dessert of churros con chocolate or a churro sundae, and unlimited sangria and/or mimosa. They cap you at 2 hours, but we were there nearly 2.5 hours and not once did they rush us or remind us of our time cap.For the tapas, we chose patatas bravas, tortilla espanola, albondigas, and pan con tomate. You also get a few slices of serrano ham and manchego cheese. All was delicious, particularly the tortilla and patatas! This alone had us pretty full and satisfied. We chose paella for the main, which is a brunch paella with eggs on top. I'm not a big fan of egg on paella, but it was still very tasty. Wonderfully flavored rice and extremely tender chicken. Despite being full, we managed a few bites and boxed the rest up for later. The churros came last, and well, there's always room for dessert...we annihilated those. All the while, they kept our sangria glasses full the entire time. They'll keep refilling your glass, but you're welcome to switch to a different type of sangria or mimosa--just ask! Oh and you can make brunch reservations which I highly recommend. We had an 11am reservation and by noon it was absolutely packed, so imagine walk-ins are tough on the weekend. I've been here for dinner too, along with another location, and it's just as delicious. Always great service too.

Dined for brunch on Saturday at 10AM. There was no wait at that time but there were some tables already filled. The place filled up quick. It was a nice sunny day so they had the front of the restaurant opened so I was able to have my dog sit right outside. The seats in the front are high tabletops. They have bar seating and seats in the back which I think were the normal tables. Looked like they had a full bar. The staff was friendly and didn't rush us out. Food was hearty and delicious. The California Benedicts was delightful. The hash brown was a nice touch instead of an English muffin. I added salmon to the benedict and it was perfect! The Shakshouka had excellent flavor. My only critic would be having the poached egg to slightly show so you can see it before digging into the bowl. It would make the dish visually nicer. I recommend this place for a nice casual catch up dining spot with friends or family, before or after a workout, and if you're looking for a healthy and hearty meal with excellent flavors and good options to choose from. I'd go back for brunch/lunch again!

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience at a Charming Venue

I'm thrilled to award this charming restaurant a full five stars! From the moment we stepped in for an early dinner, the ambiance swept us off our feet with its soft, romantic glow, and impeccable cleanliness. Seating was prompt, and our server was the epitome of experienced hospitality, offering recommendations with finesse.

With time against us, we sampled an array of dishes, relying on the kitchen's efficiency—and they delivered with gusto. Every dish made a swift entrance without compromising on presentation. The simplicity of the Caprese salad belied its exquisite taste; it was a testament to the fresh, high-quality ingredients, the mozzarella being a standout.

The veal, perfectly seasoned and cooked, was another highlight of our culinary adventure. Pricing was more than fair for the value, and the attentive service was matched by pristine bathrooms. This cute little gem of a restaurant has earned my hearty recommendation!

This is one of my favorite restaurants in Ktown. They have a bit of everything, both Korean and Japanese, from sushi rolls, rice bowls, udon noodles, deep fried dishes, to ramen. You will definitely find something that you want to try and depending on your appetite, you can go for a full meal or just opt for small bites to go along with a drink. Everything on their menu is around $10 - $18 which is decent. They also have a decent happy hour deal for beer, wine, and sake, but their regular cocktails are also delicious. Two of my favorite dishes to get from this place are definitely their creamy kimchi udon and oden soup. You MUST try the kimchi udon -- I don't usually like fusion dishes but I think this one is very well done and it's soooo delicious you will not regret getting it. The oden soup is also my favorite because I love fishcakes and it's great for sharing. Inside the restaurant is very cute and cozy, even though it could get a bit loud since it's supposed to be a 'bar'. One downside is that they don't take reservations, so you have to wait in line. However, I keep coming back to this place because of their food so I highly recommend coming here if you have never been!

Stopped in to get some breakfast/brunch this morning. This place is pretty close to my apartment and I've been meaning to try it for a while. Being a weekday, it wasn't super crowded. I sat at one of the high top tables. The waiter was really patient as I decided what I wanted. I ordered a flat white with soy milk and the banana bread. The flat white was absolutely amazing (not to mention pretty lol). They were really quick to bring out my food as well. The banana bread was so delicious! It's plated very nicely and has a great taste. It comes on top of Greek yogurt (which was perfectly sweet and not at all bitter which was my feat when I ordered it), red grapes (I wish it had more), a sprinkles of granola (also wish it had more, it was barely any) and a drizzle of caramel (added an amazing flavor). Although it was super tasty, you don't get a lot for what you pay for honestly. My total bill was $15 without tip and I left a little hungry still. There are other amazing things on the menu as well that I would like to try, but don't come with a big appetite.

Title: Heavenly Pizza Haven in Little Italy

If you're in search of the ultimate pizza experience, look no further! Nestled in the heart of Little Italy, this spot may very well serve the best pizza on the planet. Skip the salad and dive straight into their pizza offerings; you won't regret it. The standout for me is the hot pepper topping, adding just the right amount of fiery zest that complements each bite perfectly.

Both the red and white sauces are equally divine, but what really sets their pizza apart is the sublime texture of the crust – it's pure perfection. Beyond the food, the ambiance of the restaurant captures the essence of Little Italy wonderfully, making each visit an experience to savor. Whether you're a pizza aficionado or just in the mood for a slice of heaven, this is the place to be.

It ended up being one of the cheaper dinners I had in NYC during my last trip early this month (yay ethnic food). My cousin, sister and I popped in without a rezzo and we were lucky they weren't too busy so they sat us right away.It's definitely a no frills atmosphere, florescent lighting and basic tables and chairs.We ordered a few dishes to share family style and they were all delicious.Here's what we ordered:1. Bo Tai Chanh Carpaccio- thinly sliced raw beef with lots of great flavors and herbs, it was like my dream of a meat salad.2.Vietnamese Steak- so tender and juicy, very flavorful as well!3.  Oxtail fried rice- it was their special that night and man was it good, I love Oxtail!We didn't want to go too crazy because we were going to Chikalicious after for dessert and this was the perfect amount of food to be shared by the party of 3.I also ordered a cocktail- it was called something with the word sunrise in it and it had guava in it. Sorry guys, should have taken a photo of the menu but didn't in the moment- but it was pretty tasty!All in all, I would recommend this place, especially when you can come with several people so you can share and try different dishes. I'm glad it ended up being cheaper too compared to some of the expensive dinners we had in NYC!

Title: A Culinary Triumph Overshadowed by Service Lapses

My recent dining experience was a tale of two stories: the superb gastronomic offerings and the front-of-house performance, which unfortunately, fell flat. Had the maître d' service risen to the occasion, this review might have boasted a full five stars. But, regrettably, the culinary delights had to rescue the evening from a dismal beginning – elevating an otherwise two-star encounter to a modest three.

Upon arrival, the service saga began with an inexcusable 60-minute delay despite a reservation firmly in place. The lack of a compensatory gesture, such as a complimentary glass of wine, only added to our growing frustration. Further indignation was felt when discovering unoccupied tables upon finally being seated – a glaring oversight that could have averted our unnecessary wait.

The subsequent service did little to smooth over the initial mishap. As we observed other diners receiving bread and prompt attention, we found ourselves having to flag down a server for a semblance of acknowledgement – a disappointing lapse that the hostess seemed aware of but did little to amend, aside from a token order of arancini.

Moving beyond these service grievances, the meal's narrative thankfully took a turn for the better. The sommelier, reminiscent of David Guetta, shined with his congenial nature and expertise, perfectly planning our wine journey across two bottles. The culinary creations were nothing short of sensational: from the innovative Parmesan gelato and duck liver mousse to the sublime amalgamation of burrata with strawberries and pistachios.

The pasta dishes were the evening's crowning glory, with each of the four varieties we sampled offering a unique testament to the prowess of the kitchen. My personal highlight was the garganelli with truffle cream, prosciutto, and peas – an indulgent delight. The corn ravioli epitomized delicate perfection, and the olive cake provided a sweet conclusion to the meal and my birthday celebration.

In closing, while the food and sommelier were deserving of stars, the lack of customer service acumen by the front-of-house team significantly tainted what should have been an entirely joyous birthday dining experience. Lesson learned: a restaurant's success hinges not only on its culinary achievements but also on the equal importance of gracious hospitality.

Alfred Portale is a talented chef who brings real bold flavor to his newest spot in the Flatiron. Large double room and subtle lighting, but don't be fooled as this is real chef driven food not some sandwich maker opening a restaurant- no shade.Ate:Salmon with artichokes $32Escarole $9This is a no bread Italian and the house made bread is $6. I passed on this visit. The food was pretty darn palate pleasing. The salmon with spicy artichoke and lemony garlicky escarole was perfect. I imagine pastas are a knockout too. I can forgive the bread being extra when the food is this amazing!

Have been meaning to try by Chloe, and I was going to see a show at Radio City so this was a great choice for something nearby and quick! We arrived around 6pm and there was plenty seating available for our group of 4. The place is decorated very hip and chic, and was cleanly! Only 1 bathroom so I had to wait on line for a little. For everything on the menu being vegan, this was quite delicious. I had the quinoa taco salad and the chorizo tasted so good. I recommend asking for extra dressing as you can barely taste it. My friend got the thai salad which she also enjoyed. One friend got the burger which was mediocre and just a burger no fries. It's fell apart as she was trying to eat it. My last friend had the Mac n cheese which she said needed a lot more salt. All in all we decided that if you were to come, definitely go for a salad if you're hungry, it's a lot more food and more filling. We all shared a kale artichoke dip and I really enjoyed that! The staff was so kind and brought us our food, cleaned up for us and even snapped a picture for us! So sweet.

Title: A Delectable Vegan Delight at Bareburger

I recently dined at Bareburger for the first time and was thoroughly impressed by their revamped menu which now boasts a comprehensive vegetarian/vegan selection. Eager to taste their plant-based offerings, I started with a refreshing strawberry shake followed by their vegan take on the classic Big Mac. The customization options for the burger were diverse, with a variety of bases like lentil, beets, impossible, and chickpeas – a dream for any veggie-lover.

Opting for a side, we chose to split a medium order of sweet potato and regular fries – a savvy and delicious choice. Although we missed out on the mimosa special due to a lack of sparkling wine, the sangria we settled on did not disappoint.

Service was timely, with our food arriving in about 15-20 minutes, and it was nothing short of scrumptious. The veggie burgers were perfectly cooked – a rarity in many restaurants – and even sported a charming heart sign on the bun. Our waitress was attentive without being intrusive, and the personal jar of water for our table was a thoughtful touch.

Bareburger proved to be an exceptional find for vegan cuisine, and has certainly earned my anticipation for a future visit.

Title: A Carnivore's Dream at American Cut Steak

For anyone who truly appreciates a superb steak, American Cut Steak is a must-visit. I can confidently say, after my third dining experience, that they serve the best steak I've ever had. Their signature medium porterhouse topped with chili lobster—oh, what a surf & turf delight!—is simply divine, bursting with juiciness and rich flavors.

Pairing the steak with the classic sides of mashed potatoes and creamed spinach never disappoints, complementing the main course perfectly. The service only enhances the overall experience; it's exceptional. On two occasions, Jon was our server, and his friendly, funny demeanor added a special touch to our evening. His expertise also impressed us.

American Cut Steak delivers on all fronts—flavorful dishes and top-notch service. We are already looking forward to our next visit. Thank you for consistently making our dining experiences memorable!

They have an okay happy hour. I hate though when a craft beer bar advertises a decent sounding happy hour that does not cater to your dreams. Till 7pm its $5 select beer, $6 wine, and $7 cocktails but I guess the bar picks one drink for each category. On the particular night we went in it was the Tavern 29 pilsner (which let's not kid ourselves this is re-branded bud or miller), Rose, and a bourbon strawberry smash that was way too sweet. I tried all 3 obviously at some point and then took a look at their beer menu and was like 'this is stupid'. . . . there are so many great beers on tap and I'm here drinking miller lite and a strawberry caprisun with a shot of bourbon. Caved and did a flight for $12 - which isn't too terrible. It's really the way to go if you want to try a couple of beers on tap. I went with: Blue Point Heavier Things, Breckenridge Holidale, Dupont Avec les Bons Voeux, and the Cigar City Humidor. Favorite surprisingly was the Holidale - it had a nice barrel aged creaminess and was super smooth. The others were great as well but this just wowed me. We split their truffle fries which was almost a meal in itself to me. Large portion, ranch sauce. Puts on fat happy pants. My friend got their burger and I got their mac and cheese. Really solid mac. One of the best I've had in awhile. It wasn't cheap either - $16 but a large portion that became two meals. It's made with rigatoni noodles and holds that perfect consistency of being creamy and cheesy. I will say that re-heated it is not the same because it's also a truffle mac so the oil starts to separate from the sauce the next day. But that's my fault. I will be fantasizing about this macaroni and cheese for awhile. Overall, I really want to love this bar. The seating is kind of neat with having private booths off to the side. So its like you're sitting in your own little room. The bar was already super crowded by 6pm. Wish the happy hour included more select drinks than just 1 singular beer, 1 single wine, 1 cocktail of the week or day I guess I might understand. It could be fabulous but for now it's decent.

Although the decor and ambiance was elegant and classy, food didn't make up for it. I've never been so disappointed with food that was so uninspiring at a Michelin star restaurant. My boyfriend and I came for lunch and opted for their Prix Fixe ($69/person) which gives you a choice of antipasto, secondo and dolce. You can also order an additional pasta for $15/person which we did. Here is what I ordered: ANTIPASTI -Trio di SALMERINO con Radice di Prezzemolo Artic char crudo, confit and tartare with parsley root and parsley PRIMI (must order same pasta dish for the table) -LASAGNE all'Amatriciana Baked pasta layers with guanciale, tomato, and peperoncino SECONDI -Peposo dell'IMPRUNETA~$20 suppRed wine wagyu beef short rib with anson mills polenta and spinachDOLCI-PANNA COTTA di Riso Nero Forbidden rice and vanilla bean custard with black sesame and concord sorbetto I usually eat food that are on the saltier side but EVERYTHING was too salty. The shared lasagne was salty and my wagyu beef short rib dish was way too salty. My boyfriend got the chicken entree and this was way too underwhelming; it lacked flavor and was slightly undercooked. It also had an unusual smell so he couldn't finish it. We also saw the table next to us return their chicken entree--probably for the same reasons. Our waitress recommended Lavender Spritz drink and this was simply a waste of $11. I only drank a sip and left it alone throughout the meal. Spent close to $300 for overpriced food that lacked flavor, overly salty, and was overall disappointing. The only 'ok' thing was the bread and cheese butter that they serve in the beginning. It pains me to write such review since I've only had good experiences at Michelin star restaurant, but I won't be returning to Del Posto.

Craved for lomo saltado and man I was so happy that I found this place. Ordered the squash salad, lomo saltado which came with chinese pancakes and gauc. Also ordered the lucuma shake. Food -5/5 Loved everything we ate. The lomo saltado was my favorite thing. The fries were atypically wedge-cut, and I loved that I could grab a hunk of potato and dip it into the sauce from the meat. Every component of the meal was smart. The Chinese pancakes were crispy. Not sure if it was intentional but a couple were pretty burnt. The avocado that accompanied them was great, in my opinion a little too tart. Roasted squash salad I would order again. Loved the mint and yogurt dressing which lifted an otherwise heavy vegetable. The lucuma smoothie was also great. Couldn't tell there was coffee in there.. The cashier was extremely friendly and welcoming. Can't wait to come back soon and try the chicken/rest of the menu. Highly recommend!

We made an rsvp & arrived a little early no problem being seated as the place was not crowded. Once seated we started with some drinks gave the spiked lemonade a try, it was good nice taste. on the food we ended up sticking with the appetizers, we had Black pepper beef taco, wow this was great nice taste to it nice combo with the meat, avocado & cilantro. next the Duck wings another wow here these were delicious really great tasting with sugar glaze, duck wings? who knew!! Next up the Pooty fries very good as well these fries are asian poutine with cheese curds & short rib gravy, very tasty. & Finally the Lettuce wraps u have pork sausage with some cilantro, basil & onion great taste all together. Small location, nicely decorated .. service was good we happen to come in during happy hour so that was nice since they offer some specials on drinks & appetizers. everything we had was very tasty , decent drink & prices we enjoyed our time here.

Title: A Dumpling Delight Not To Be Missed

If you're on the quest for dumplings that rival the comforting taste of home, look no further! This gem serves up the best dumplings I've had outside of my own kitchen. Transporting me straight back to childhood with every bite, their selection spans various scrumptious flavors, with the spicy beef and chicken basil standing out as personal favorites. Customers can choose to have their dumplings steamed, fried, or cozily tucked into a soup.

Although the menu also features sesame sandwiches and noodle bowls with dumplings, I find myself consistently drawn to the standalone dumpling orders – they're just that satisfying. Typically, I opt for a double helping to satiate my appetite. On the rare occasions when I'm visiting the city, I leap at the chance to take their frozen dumplings home. Not only are these delectable pockets affordable, but they're also easy to transport and prepare. Do yourself a favor and give them a try – your taste buds will thank you!

a friend and i came to thalassa during restaurant week over the summer and we had such a lovely time! the staff is so friendly and attentive and the food was delicious and so elegantly presented. the restaurant is also very cute as well. everything from the appetizers, entrees, and desserts were absolutely gorgeous and tasty. i would come here again.

During my recent visit to this establishment, I had the pleasure of tasting the "El Chapo" burger, and it certainly lived up to the hype. Tucked between the buns were delectable layers of pepper jack cheese, rich and creamy guacamole, tender short rib, a kick of jalapeño, and a slathering of chipotle mayo that added a smoky depth. It's hard to pinpoint any shortcomings, though if pressed, I'd mention the short rib was a tad dry. However, the overall mastery displayed by the chef deserves commendation.

Complementing my meal were the side fries, which were nothing short of perfection. Despite my aspirations for a sculpted physique, these fries proved irresistible, and not a single one was left behind.
