The service was top-notch, attentive and prompt without being intrusive. The varied drink selection only added to the experience, ensuring that there's something for everyone's taste. It's a versatile spot, ideal for both a quick meal or a leisurely dining experience.

I'm already planning my next visit, eyeing a perhaps less adventurous but equally promising burger option. Without a doubt, this restaurant has earned itself a repeat customer.

I ordered takeout from this restaurant I had placed an order for a medium white pizza with artichokes on it, which was extra as well as some garlic knots. The pizza was sooooo delicious!!!! I don't know why this place doesn't have more stars. The pizza slices were generous and huge! The pizza wasn't  too salty and the crust was absolutely perfect! The perfect blend of crunchy/crispy and doughy. The garlic knots weren't a hit but after I heated them they tasted pretty decent. But overall I'd definitely order from this place again and I think they deserve more stars. Not to mention the pricing is worth it. I believe that the $33 for the medium pie and the garlic knots was definitely worth it. They're also opened pretty late 7 days a week so totally worth it on my humble opinion. I wish they had this pizza place in Atlanta  I guess I better eat as much of this pizza before I leave NYC!

I absolutely fell in love with this place. I came here for dinner with my boyfriend and I was here earlier than the time on my reservation. The staffs were all very nice and accommodating. The hostess showed me to my seat and I found the decor of this place to be very fancy yet casual.While I was seated to wait for my boyfriend to arrive, I ordered a cocktail that had some chili in it - they understood I have a very low spice tolerance and accommodated to me by lowering the level of chili. Personally, I still found it to be very spicy and later passed the drink off to my boyfriend. However, they did check in with me on the taste and noticed that I still found the drink to be too spicy. Our waiter became super insightful and lessened, eliminated and separated all the dishes that we ordered that can be potentially spicy for me. He was super nice about it and so attentive!We ordered the Fluke as an appetizer and it was sooooo good - highly recommend this. This is one of the best Fluke I've ever had. And of course, I had to order the Mafaldini "Scampi" and I have to say.... it was really freaking good. I 100% saw this all over instagram (hence the reason I found Scampi and decided to come here) and I was not disappointed with its presentation and the way it tastes.I would love to come back here just to get the Mafaldini if anything. Ugh. Everything was spectacular and honestly, I think the price point is very fair. I would love to eventually come back here with a bigger group for a birthday dinner or something. I love this place so much and it's only been the first time! Hoping to have many more times here :)

Ok so let me start off by saying there is basically a copy cat downstairs, this place is upstairs. When I called for a reservation the guy was insistent that we come to the one upstairs. So don't be fooled, this review is for the one upstairs. The decor is off the hook, there are so many lights on the ceiling its unreal what the electrical bill must be. Its so much fun! The restaurant is very long and skinny, but this seems pretty typical in NYC, if this place was full it would be pretty stuffy I could imagine. So we will start off with my next favorite thing and that was the owner, he was there, he hugged us and welcomed us like family, he waited on us and was very friend to us the entire time. Now my least favorite part, yes unfortunately was the food. Just not tasty enough. Indian food usually has a really good and unique flavor that I crave, and this was mediocre at best, so I was sadly disappointed. Thank you for your hospitality and really cool ambiance!

Gi-normous slices of pizza here!  They kindly cut mine in half because i knew i wouldn't be able to finish it.  I'm a purist, so I stuck with the plain cheese slice.  It was very  good and filling.  Prices not bad too!Clean place, with ample seating.

Title: High Hopes Meet High Prices at Trendy Eatery

My sister and I stepped into this much-hyped restaurant, tantalized by the myriad of glowing reviews. The ambiance hit the mark with its charmingly dim lighting and an Asian beach bar aesthetic. Electing to sit at the chef's counter, we were excited to watch our dinner unfold before our eyes.

The star of our table was undoubtedly the lobster noodle dish. Despite the initial letdown of scant-looking lobster portions that seemed mismatched with the price, the dish redeemed itself upon further exploration. Rich in flavor, with perfectly cooked noodles, the sauce sang with each bite. It was, without question, the highlight of our meal and is highly recommended for future diners.

However, not everything met our expectations. The crispy baby back ribs fell victim to an overzealous char, which rendered the edges too bitter for my liking. Although aiming for that fall-off-the-bone tenderness, it sadly missed the mark, presenting us with an interior that tasted underseasoned.

On a side note, the Nasi Goreng was a decent rendition of fried rice with a well-cooked egg on top, but it failed to leave a memorable impression—pleasant but not extraordinary.

Ultimately, while some dishes like the lobster noodle shone brightly, the overall dining experience was shadowed by steep pricing that didn't always align with the value on the plate. Good food? Yes. But when the check suggests excellence, "good" just isn't enough.

Really like their summer rolls here, very freshly made! Their prices are also a great bargain for sure. I enjoy getting anything on the menu but really love their phos. The broth is really tasty and I definitely recommend giving it a try! Best in all of Chinatown in my opinion. The Vietnamese coffee (iced/hot) is also a great accompaniment with your meal!

Tucked away upstairs in what feels like a converted apartment, this speakeasy-style sushi spot offers a quirky but cozy dining experience. The space is tight, so it's not ideal for those with claustrophobia or in need of privacy. Dinner featured an unconventional but delightful peanut avocado roll amongst other sushi staples like the salmon crunch and spicy tuna - all fresh and well-made. The rock shrimp tempura leaned more towards a fried shrimp dish than tempura, and service timing was peculiar, with sushi arriving ahead of appetizers, a phenomenon not uncommon in sushi establishments. With a lunch special boasting three rolls for $13.50 and two for $9.95, the value is exceptional for New York City. Despite its charm and solid offerings, fierce competition within the city holds this spot at a steady 3-star rating.

Title: A Valentine's Dinner to Remember at Capital Grille

My long-anticipated return to Capital Grille since my last visit in Boston back in 2016 was one for the books. Celebrating Valentine's Day might have added a rosy tint to the evening, but the culinary prowess on display needed no such embellishments. The Filet Mignon, which I ordered medium-rare, was a masterpiece of tenderness and taste, outshining my already high expectations.

Complementing my main course, the Lobster Mac 'N' Cheese was stellar, an indulgent side that's absolutely essential. Meanwhile, the Grilled Asparagus, enhanced with a fresh squeeze of lemon, held its own with understated elegance. Together, they formed an impeccable trio with the steak.

Service was top-notch, enhancing the dining experience with attentiveness that made our night special. Reflecting on the meal, the balance of price and value is commendable. Capital Grille not only met but exceeded the cherished memories of past meals. This is a restaurant that truly knows how to make an occasion memorable, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Between a 4 and a 5. The food was great. Was it two Michelin Star great? Probably not, but for the price we paid and the fact that it was takeout it definitely delivered. For $125 (incl tax) you get an obscene amount of food for two. We feasted on three different types of herring, potatoes, cheese and bread, eggs, shrimp, gravlax, meatballs, sausage, more potatoes, and a variety of accoutrements like lingonberries and pickles. Everything was packaged perfectly, and some of the food stood out as incredible. My favorites were the cheese, gravlax, meatballs, and the shredded potatoes. The gravlax was an unreal portion - there was easily a quarter to half pound of the best I've ever had served with lemon and sauce. I could have been happy with that alone. Reheating directions were easy and simple for the hot dishes, everything was packaged perfectly, pickup was easy, and all in all it was a fun, unique, and filling takeout experience. Thanks Aquavit!

There were 3 of us who visited this place Troquet, a French bistro, in Soho - one of us who is frequents due to its simple delicious menu.It was a weekday lunch, and we all ordered Fixed Price lunch ($21) - with appetizer and entree.I ordered the carrot ginger soup and the daily special which was way beyond my expectations. Baked eggs with tomato, bacon, & cheese. Much better than the description!!!HOWEVER.......The reason I am giving 2 stars then ....The server : No smile. No greetings. Machine automated voice explanation when asked a question.And the next reason may be personal, but I do feel underserved when restaurants are serving the customers "chipped" plates. One little but a huge detail that I cannot overlook. Just does not feel right. Restaurants should throw away "chipped" plates !!!!!!

Got the spicy beef noodle soup and the pork soup dumplings.  The soup dumplings have a fair amount of soup in them but it is a little lacking in flavor.  The beef noodle soup was a nice level of spicy but was a little bit on the salty side.  It's a nice portion size with a ton of noodles and the beef shank is tender.

BBQ wings were incredibly good. I got the 6 pc with fries on the side. The BBQ sauce wasn't overly sweet and each wings were nice and crispy. There was a small chunk of salt that wasn't melted, but it was still amazing.

Honestly, if you don't even know if your foods are cooked thoroughly, you shouldn't be a chef. We ordered the steamed beef shumai - 6 in one order and one of them wasn't even cooked! My cousin bit into one and it was completely raw. But what's confusing was that the wrap was cooked, so I'm confused why the filling wasn't. So how many times have they served that dish thinking it was cooked? How many people ate the whole dumpling trusting that the chef knew what he was doing? We asked the server and he agreed that the filling was not cooked. We received a new order but not one apology. Along with the shumai, we also ordered the stir fried noodle, sauteed lamb with cumin, and the Xinjiang Big Plate Chicken (with the bone). The stir fried noodles dish was soggy and way too salty. The lamb was too rough and just wasn't worth the calories. However, the Xinjiang big plate chicken was very good. The flavored chicken (with the bone) was served over a plate of thick noodles. Loved that - great spices and the noodles were the perfect texture. Because we started out with the uncooked dumplings, I was very wary of the things I ate that night, which is not a good feeling.

Food 4.5/5Service 5/5Atmosphere 4/5Very enjoyable experience for dinner on a Tuesday night. We were seated quickly and offered sake. We chose the house sake which was hot. Very delicious and would recommend.We ordered about half a dozen rolls to share. All of them were delicious and the portions were generous. The presentation of the sushi rolls was also very nice. Very much appreciated as I think appearances are important too.Overall very nice experience and very good service. Would recommend if you're looking for some decent, reasonably-priced sushi.

Title: A Trendy Spot with a Mix of Hits and Misses

Upon stepping into this trendy restaurant, the ambiance immediately set a positive tone for our dining experience. Our culinary adventure began on a high note with the unique and delightful edamame pancake - its sweetness and satisfying crunch, complemented by a fluffy cream cheese spread, was a surprising hit.

We followed up with the grilled eggplant atop mushroom rice, a harmonious combination that was perfect as a precursor to the main event. Do note, this dish is a mushroom lover's dream due to its potent aroma.

The beef tataki, however, was a miss for us - lacking in seasoning, it left an underwhelming impression of just raw meat with chives.

Our main course, a large bulgogi hot pot with burdock, though tasty, felt insufficient for our group of four. Curiosity lingers for the tomato seafood pot, an option we bypassed due to a dining companion's allergy.

On the plus side, the prices were reasonable, and the service, impeccable. The experience left us eager to return and explore more of their hot pot varieties.

So glad I lucked upon this place when looking for lunch! Ordered the basil fried rice with crispy duck, and the green curry with chicken and...... WOW!! Everything was delicious. Loved the overall ambience and coziness of the restaurant. Would highly recommend it!

Title: A New Thai Gem in Hell's Kitchen

As a devotee of Pure, I was intrigued to try its sibling establishment, which is vying to top my list of Thai eateries amidst the culinary abundance of Hell's Kitchen. With its astute bench seating arrangement, you're guaranteed a seat without the dreaded wait—a rarity in this bustling neighborhood.

The fare here is a refreshing departure from the monotonous offerings that plague many Thai menus. The two-item combo is a must-try, allowing you to indulge in inventive delicacies like their succulent squid, buttery butterfish, and an unexpectedly scrumptious stir-fry squash with egg. The omelette is another standout, perfectly fluffy and partnered with a 'not spicy' but utterly flavorful dipping sauce.

Don't miss out on their free pickled veggies, a tangy delight served in charming little jars to kickstart your meal. Seasonal specials consistently impress, reflecting the kitchen's commitment to innovation.

In short, while Pure might hold the crown, the absence of an interminable wait at its sister restaurant elevates it to the pinnacle of accessible Thai cuisine in Hell's Kitchen. If you're craving Thai without the hours-long queue, look no further.

Title: A Hidden Russian Gem with a Spirited Vibe

I stumbled upon an incredible Russian bar through Seated, and it turned out to be the best discovery. Despite initially encountering a packed venue and a policy that discouraged loitering, the staff's thoughtfulness shone through. A waiter promisingly informed us of upcoming table availability, and true to his word, we were swiftly accommodated, initially sharing with departing patrons before being relocated to our own space.

The bar exuded a remarkable sense of camaraderie, and we felt immediately woven into the venue's vibrant tapestry. Our cocktail experience was elevated when we were pleasantly surprised with complimentary shots alongside our bill—a charming touch that truly made our visit memorable.

While we indulged in a delectable cheese plate, the only thing missing was a slice of bread to perfect the pairing. This minor detail, however, isn't enough to deter my planned return. For anyone craving an authentic slice of Russian hospitality, this small establishment is a must-visit.

Came here for Restaurant Week lunch on a weekday with a reservation. The restaurant was decently busy with people dressed relatively nicely. The interior was nice and spacious. The $26 Restaurant Week menu comes with an appetizer and an entree. I chose the Lobster Bisque and the USDA Prime Junior New York Sirloin. I think the the Restaurant Week menu is a pretty solid deal given that the normal Lunch Prix-Fixe menu is $15 more expensive and includes a dessert a select few more options for the other courses. Unfortunately, the waiter informed me that free creme brulee with Yelp check-in does not combine with the Restaurant Week deal.The waiter brought out bread for the table which was nice and warm and pretty soft. The Lobster Bisque came out pretty quickly. It was rich and creamy and a tad over salted for my liking. The oyster crackers went really well with the dish but I was a little disappointed in the amount of lobster present and the minimal lobster flavor in the bisque.The entree came out shortly after I finished my entree. The sirloin came with the bone in, which I appreciate, paired with a small potatoes and mixed veggies. I ordered my steak medium and I thought it was cooked just perfectly. There was a good ratio of fat and lean meat and the steak was extremely tender. The seasoning was on point, complimenting the flavor of the meat. They have a bottle of steak sauce at each table which I don't think is needed at all. The steak sauce tastes like cocktail sauce and goes well with the potatoes.Overall, I had a great experience dining at Benjamin Prime. The steak really is top notch. I didn't enjoy the Lobster Bisque as much as I'd hope but still was an enjoyable meal. The service was great without being too overbearing.

Title: Fresh, but Familiar Fare at a Premium

I recently dined at this establishment, indulging in the $75 omakase which offered a standard selection including soup or salad, 10 sushi pieces, and a hand roll. The soup failed to impress with its peculiar taste, though my husband's salad was redeemed by its notably unsweetened dressing—a welcome departure from the typical fare at Japanese restaurants.

The array of sushi, boasting fresh fish such as tuna, salmon, sweet shrimp, scallop, and yellowtail (twice, with toro as well), was fresh yet undistinguished. Without inventive sauces or unique offerings, the value of the omakase at its price point was questionable in my eyes. However, the spicy toro hand roll stood out and would be my go-to should I return, perhaps alongside their sushi rolls.

My husband's chicken teriyaki, served unconventionally with dark meat, was satisfactory to his palate. In sum, while our experience was decent, the restaurant hasn't secured a spot on our list of must-return dining venues.

Wow , Urbanspace has now opened their new food hall with over a dozen vendors some of which are not found at there other locations.The layout is similar to Urbanspace Lex which also has a mezzanine level. It's is in the back side of the AXA Building and has entrances on 52th Street and on Avenue 6 1/2, yes 6 1/2 look it up it a pedestrian walkway running across several blocks and had outside seating during the summer months. Their is also an interesting mural that spreads out the name 'named 'Urbanspace W52' across the width of the food hall.The vendor list is as followings;Black Iron Burger               Classic American Burgers Cafe Patoor                        Brazilian Brigadeiro cake, breadsCall Me Pasta                     Customizable pasta barCity Tamale                        Mexican food gluten-free!Coney Shack                     Hot Dogs, Tacos with an Asian twistDorado                              Mexican street foodEisenberg's                        Deli sandwiches Egg CreamGo Fish Sushibox              Sushi rolls ShasimiLoLo's Chichen Shack       Customizable Chicken bowlsPartner's Coffee                CafePita Yeero                          Greek street foodPlant Junkie                       VeganRobertas                            Wood fired PizzaSustainable Seafood         SeafoodTomo Tomo                       RamenDon't wait for reviews, just go and try them out for yourself their has to be a least 3 or 4 that you will like.

Title: A Hearty Feast with Room for Improvement

I recently visited an all-you-can-eat establishment that offered a reasonable deal at $24.99, including the option for BBQ. My advice to future diners is to make a reservation, as it seems to be a popular choice, especially for large groups. The service was good; attentive without being overbearing.

However, the dining experience wasn't without its faults. The variety of sauces and condiments was disappointingly limited; they even ran out of several choices during our dinner time, which detracted from the overall enjoyment of the meal. Moreover, the soy jelly drink on offer was disappointingly watered down and lacked flavor.

The restaurant spans two levels, but I'd suggest securing a table on the first floor if possible. The basement seating suffers from poor air circulation, making the dining experience less than pleasant if you end up seated there. Compared to its Chinatown branch, this location seems to have fewer menu options.

On a positive note, I discovered afterward that the restaurant is BYOB, which is a definite plus and not always a given at all-you-can-eat venues. This could certainly enhance future visits.

In summary, while the restaurant checks the boxes for price and service, it falls short in ambiance and culinary variety. It gets the job done if you're hungry and in the mood for quantity, but there's room for improvement in quality.

We loved the atmosphere. Very happy staff, good music, light vibe. I had the Madame Freda.  Although a little dry in spots, it was quite delicious. The salad was a bit flavorless, but the Bloody Mary more than made up for it. My niece had a breakfast bowl and she loved it. All in all, a good spot to have a good breakfast!

Title: Hits and Misses at The Local Bar

My latest visit to the bar area of this restaurant offered a mixed experience. The service stumbled a bit with a new waiter providing some comically unhelpful dish descriptions – telling us a hamburger "has beef" isn't quite the insight one hopes for. Nevertheless, the bar's unique offerings remain a draw, and the flexibility to order à la carte from the main menu is appreciated.

We skipped oysters and ventured to sample the amuse-bouche, a curious composition of a wafer with olive crème and grape slices – more intriguing than satisfying. The fluke crudo, however, paired with American caviar and a rich olive oil, was a standout, especially when sopped up with the delightful selection from the bread basket.

The blue crab spaghetti was another triumph, its al dente strands laced with just the right amount of spice, and the kitchen graciously accommodated our request to split the dish. The white label burger held its own with a succulent patty and a bold combination of Calabrian aioli, fontina cheese, and pickles, though the accompanying pommes dauphines fell flat, lacking the anticipated crispy contrast.

Dessert was met with lukewarm enthusiasm; the cioccolato featured a chocolate mousse and honey bourbon crema that were forgettable at best, although the honey gelato did shine through.

In summary, while service left room for improvement, the culinary high points – notably the fluke, burger, and spaghetti – ensure I'll return for the food, if nothing else.

Title: Cozy Night with Fresh Bites

On a brisk Sunday evening, my party and I ventured into the warmth of a bustling restaurant, where we were promptly ushered to seats at the bar. The ambiance was immediately inviting, enhanced by the sight of a dedicated oyster shucker meticulously at work.

Service was commendable; the waitstaff proved both amiable and knowledgeable, which enriched our dining experience. We indulged in a selection of oysters that were not only fresh but also complemented by an array of delicious sauces. Moving on to the Korean fried chicken, however, we found our expectations slightly dimmed as it failed to arrive at our table with that just-fried, piping hot sizzle we anticipated; it felt as though it may have been fried earlier and then reheated.

Our culinary journey continued with an assortment of handrolls – unagi, tuna, snow crab, and yellowtail. The eel and tuna were standout favorites, the former delivering a wisp of smokiness and the latter showcasing the handrolls' impeccably crunchy seaweed, alongside rice that was nothing short of perfect in texture and temperature. The tobiko pasta, while flavorful, fell short on temperature, arriving at a lukewarm state when a dish served hot would have enhanced its appeal.

In brief, the handrolls and oysters were the heroes of the night, with an emphasis on "fresh" being the takeaway. The hot dishes, though, left a bit to be desired in terms of serving temperature. With a little attention to ensuring dishes arrive hot to the table, this restaurant could easily elevate its already enjoyable dining experience.

My friends and I came for restaurant week and were not disappointed. First, they serve you bread with whipped butter... and we all know this is very important--it came out piping hot. The waiter was very nice, and the restaurant was very large for a Manhattan location. Anyway... the first course I had tomato basil soup, which was very good. There was a little oil on in, but that's the be expected in a soup. My entree was an 8oz filet with a side of mashed potatoes. The steak cut like butter, and was cooked exactly how I ordered it. We all ordered the same steak, with different preferences, and they didn't mess it up... which is RARE (get it?) for a restaurant these days. Perfectly charred and cooked, and the portions were great. For dessert, I had pumpkin cheesecake. I was a little disappointed with the selection, as I was only given one option, but nonetheless... it was good. They treated us very nicely and the hospitality was A+. I'd probably come back when it's not restaurant week because it was that good.

After three attempts to dine at Thursday Kitchen due to its notorious wait times, my friends and I finally managed to experience what all the buzz is about. This place lives up to the hype, offering a refreshing take on Asian fusion through an assortment of tapas-style dishes.

The ambiance is as distinctive as the food, creating a chic yet inviting atmosphere. Despite the constant bustle, the wait staff impresses with their warm and attentive service.

The highlight of the drink menu is the alcoholic caprisuns, a sweet and vibrant concoction that's a shout-out to anyone with a penchant for sugary drinks. As for the food, the truffle mac and cheese is a symphony of sound and flavor, oozing with rich truffle essence. The tenderness of the steak is unparalleled, practically disintegrating on the tongue. Meanwhile, the honey sriracha popcorn chicken delivers a perfect balance of sweetness and heat, all wrapped up in an irresistibly crunchy exterior.

In essence, Thursday Kitchen offers an innovative menu that superbly intertwines traditional Korean tastes with a diverse range of global influences. It's an unparalleled dining mosaic and a solid 10/10 on my list of New York City eateries.

Could not complain about the food . It is genuinely good and a very unique experience . Specially when you are with a group of friends .The watermelon and musk melon sojus are amazing and refreshing and is something i have never had before. The hot pot was flavored and well cooked along with the chicken skewers and vegetable rice . They have a  delicious spread and variety of options in the menu as well.

Title: A Touch of Nostalgia with a Side of Pop at New York's Timeless Eatery

Walking into this venerable New York establishment, one immediately senses the inspired homage to a famed British actress, with every corner of the restaurant meticulously curated to echo the grandeur of her mansion. Despite its storied walls and historic air, the restaurant presents an unpretentious selection of satisfying bar fare, ensuring the food remains accessible, if not adventurous.

The service shines; both the host and the waitress added a personal touch that made the experience more inviting. Unfortunately, the ambience is marred by an incongruent soundtrack of relentless cheesy pop rock, which, while perhaps aimed at energizing the crowd, detracted from the otherwise charming setting.

Admirably, the restaurant welcomes the festive season with open arms, transforming into a yuletide haven – a gesture that does not go unnoticed. In response to a request for a quieter dining environment, the staff kindly obliged, demonstrating a considerate approach to guest comfort.

In sum, this restaurant's blend of history, heartfelt service, and a cozy holiday spirit warrants a solid 4-star rating. It's worth recommending for those seeking a taste of New York's classic scene, with a note to bring friends who'll appreciate the nostalgia – and can tolerate a pop-infused playlist.

I stopped by this no-frills NYC pizza joint with a client for what turned out to be some fantastic thin crust pizza - and truly, I could just stop the review there because that's how good it was. Seating is limited, so be prepared to stand or grab and go. The service comes with the quintessential cranky New York attitude, but hey, it's all part of the experience at no additional cost. We each had two slices, and both of us walked away loving every bite.

Title: A Mixed Bag with Generous Portions at [Restaurant Name]

My visit to [Restaurant Name] for lunch had its ups and downs. The temptation of a free shot with my food, courtesy of a Yelp check-in offer, was a nice touch. I settled on the fish and chips, accompanied by a whiskey.

My initial impression was positive—four hefty pieces of fish over fries promised a fulfilling meal. However, after a few bites, my excitement faded. The breading on the fish was overly thick and disappointingly undercooked on the inside. While the cod itself was passable in flavor, the texture was too mushy for my liking. As for the fries, they were noticeably greasy and sparse.

In conclusion, [Restaurant Name] seems more suited for drinks and socializing rather than a quick lunch stop. The generous fish servings couldn't outweigh the shortcomings in food quality. Next time, I'll probably stick to happy hour.

Disappointment loomed during our visit to Superiority Burger, a highly-hyped spot known for its Beyond Meat offering. The restaurant is minute, squeezing in dining space for barely four. Though we shelled out $6 for palm-sized burgers, expecting a taste revelation, it turned out to be a letdown. The patties, lacking inherent flavor, relied heavily on seasoning, evoking an unappealing bean-and-grass concoction. We left unsatisfied, seeking solace at a nearby Shake Shack. Regrettably, I can't endorse Superiority Burger – it simply didn't live up to the acclaim.

For all the hype I expected so much more. The space was gorgeous, the staff was attentive and gave good service but I found the food beyond subpar. Had the steak and eggs and did not enjoy any part of it. Meat wasn't good quality and wasn't cooked medium like I asked. It was like chewing gum. The potatoes were terribly overdone. Everything was cooked till black and greasy. See photo for reference.My friend enjoyed her pasta dish so there was that.

Title: A Gem for Steak and Seafood Lovers

Rating: 9/10

Would I eat here again? Definitely.

Review:
I recently dined at this restaurant and was immediately struck by its simple elegance. The ambiance is relaxed yet classy, creating a comfortable atmosphere for a delightful meal.

Service was top-notch, attentive without being intrusive – a balance that many establishments struggle to find.

The highlight of my meal was the dry-aged New York strip paired with fresh oysters. The steak was sumptuous and expertly cooked, albeit slightly under-seasoned. However, the oysters were some of the best I've ever tasted, brimming with freshness.

The tagliatelle with mushrooms was another win, both hearty and satisfying, with flavors that melded beautifully together.

Overall, this restaurant delivers on all fronts – ambiance, service, and most importantly, food. A must-visit for anyone with a love for well-prepared steak and seafood.

Request to sit at or wait for table # 205 to open. You're welcome in advance!! The portions are large and the prices are very NYC- a bit pricy (but what can I say). This restaurant is popular across America and is for the pasta lovers. I'm recommending the spinach artichoke dip to share and anything chocolate dessert for yourself!! Considering how we were tucked away in the best corner, our waiter was very attentive. He forgot our requests a couple of times but it's no big. What a fun night- made good memories here!
NY 19. Dinner review. Tacos.Ordered:3 - Corn taco (Carne asada)4 - Corn taco (Pork adobada)5 - Fried quesadilla (Pork adobada)Overall, "I'm a fan."

Upon my recent visit to this gem in Chinatown, I was greeted by the usual line—a testament to its popularity. The affordability of the menu immediately caught my attention, followed by the expedited service that didn't compromise the quality of food. 

I indulged in the duck and roasted BBQ pork, both of which were a cut above the rest. I've savored some of the best BBQ pork in Vancouver BC, and I must say, this establishment nearly rivals that high standard. The pork was not only bursting with flavor but also maintained a succulent juiciness that is hard to come by.

The accompanying rice and cabbage rounded out the meal to perfection, leaving me thoroughly content after a day of exploring NYC. If you're in the area and craving authentic, delicious, and quick Chinese fare at a great price, this is the place to go.

Pretty space.  The spreads were delicious and the artichoke was amazing.  The fish tagine was a bit too soupy but nicely seasoned as was the couscous.  Unfortunately they rushed us out and didn't even ask if we wanted to look at the dessert menu.  Guess there were people waiting it was odd.

I recently had the pleasure of visiting a phenomenal taco truck that absolutely deserves a shout-out. Not only were the ingredients incredibly fresh, but the staff also radiated friendliness. As a vegetarian, it's often a struggle to find accommodating eateries, but the team here went above and beyond to assist me with meat-free options. I highly recommend giving the veggie tacos a try, especially with their spicy sauce and salsa verde – it's a flavor-packed delight. To top it off, the prices are wallet-friendly, making this place a standout. If you're looking for quality eats without breaking the bank, this taco truck is the perfect combo.

It's been about a year since this place opened and I feel I need to drop a star. I find the quality of the pizza to be really inconsistent, which is disappointing to say the least, especially since I know how much potential L&T&S has on a good day. When they're good, it's lit-- their pepperoni squares give PSP a run for its money with its deliciously caramelized edges and surprisingly light dough. But when they're bad, it's awful. The pizza gets barely reheated and the cheese is left a bland and concealed mass atop the bread.I hold a lot of love for L&T&S, even through all the times they changed their pricing, but I think they really need to work on their consistency.

I popped into this spot for a beer and pretzel—both of which I thoroughly enjoyed. However, the bustling Saturday crowd and booming music detracted from the experience. Loud to the point of shouting over the table, the atmosphere left a bit to be desired for a casual evening out.

**Char Sue: A Lower East Side Gem**

Tucked away on the trendy Lower East Side, Char Sue offers an eclectic and relaxed dining experience that's perfect for both low-key date nights and lively group gatherings. The layout boasts widely spaced tables at the front and a cozy bar at the back, reinforcing its vibe as a chill spot for dinner and drinks – think beer, wine, and sake, as the cocktail list is not the focus here.

Happy hour is a can't-miss event, running until 7 or 7:30 p.m., and features an array of food and drink specials. While the reduced-price appetizers are modest in size, they are massive in flavor. The black pepper beef taco stands out at $4, delivering a punchy, crunchy bite with ample meat. For a dollar more, the pork taco offers a delightful variety of tastes. The "pooty fries" are a playful take on poutine, loaded with Asian spices and short ribs for $7 – they're perfect for sharing. The yakitori bacon and enoki is passable, but there's better to be had on the menu.

The entrée worth mentioning is the 5-Spice Short Ribs Rice Bowl at $20. With perfectly cooked short ribs and tangy pickled veggies, it's a flavor-packed dish that's even better with an added egg for $2. Beverage-wise, happy hour beers and wines are friendly on the wallet at around $4 and $6, respectively.

Service is notably swift and attentive, ensuring you can focus on the "fantasTACOS" and the feast before you. Char Sue is a definite must-visit for anyone craving innovative Asian-influenced eats at a venue that boasts both character and comfort.

Title: A Theatrical Prelude to 'Hadestown' at a Marvelous Eatery

My husband and I decided to dine at this establishment before our evening at 'Hadestown,' and what an exquisite pre-theatre experience it was! Upon our early arrival, the hostesses greeted us with exceptional warmth. 

The highlight of our meal was undoubtedly the truffle filet tartar; as a steak tartar aficionado, I found it divinely unique and a step above the rest. Paired with the lobster bisque, boasting generous chunks of lobster in a sumptuous creamy base, our appetizers set a high bar. Despite feeling sated, we couldn’t resist sharing the 12oz filet – a generous size for the two of us – accompanied by a luscious side of creamed spinach.

Friendly, efficient service complemented the culinary delights, making the experience seamless. While the price tag was steep at approximately $200 for the meal with drinks, the exceptional quality and the standout truffle tartar made it a worthwhile indulgence. A perfect pre-theatre treat, this restaurant undoubtedly deserves a standing ovation.

This is a bit of an modern dim sum/Chinese place with some South East Asian and other things mixed in along with a hibachi menu. The menu is in short a bit all over the place but there's some good dishes mixed within. I think they're trying to be a fancier place but they have a few general issues.In terms of the dim sum, it's generally overpriced but you'll get better food as well there aren't many good Chinese places in the area. The matcha bun is alright with the outside being more like a melon bun with the sticky sweet filling being the star (as also with the a bit overly sweet baked pork bun.) The sticky rice rolls with pork are fine as are the dumplings. I think the sago pudding from the dessert section was honestly the best thing from there. Not super sweet and very refreshing.The main dishes are served with surprisingly miso soup or salad which brings even more Pan-Asian mix to the food. I agree with someone else's assessment of the the Singaporean Laksa. It's well portioned for lunch and while it lacks the complex broth or better noodles of very good places, it's not like there is anywhere in the local area where you can get Singaporean/Malaysian food. It's in short alright.My personal favorite dish is the oink oink fried rice by a long shot. The forbidden/black rice used adds a good nuttiness and there's a good amount of meat. It's slightly sweet but not overpoweringly and there's a few vegetables around also. This is a very good variation and for the price, there aren't many better options in the area. I wish it was a tad less sweet but I guess I could ask for some chili sauce next time.If this place was in a better food area, I wouldn't see it survive for too long. Outside of the very good fried rice, the dishes are alright, It's in general a bit too expensive for the quality, but for the area, the place is fine. The service is a bit too much hit or miss also. I've waited for the check a bit too long a bit too many times so I am wary to go unless I have a lot of time. Mid 3 rounded down for inconsistency/service.

I came here for Italian Restaurant Week for a solo dinner. The restaurant appears deceptively small but it has 3 floors, the first floor is the bar and section for regular and high end clientele. The second floor is where all the new people/tourists sat. The third floor I believe was where private events would take place. When I entered the restaurant the hostess and staff were polite but I sensed there's a type of prejudice. The hostess sat me in the corner with my back turned to the crowd. After a few minutes, the server saw me and repositioned me to let me enjoy the ambiance of the place. The server and staff was really nice and accommodating but service was quite slow. I feel that the staff was selective and prioritizing who to serve first. The food in this place is amazing. I had no complaints about any of the dishes ordered. The scallops on the capesante were cooked perfectly and the amount of vegetables and sauce balanced the dish perfectly. The vitello was awesome and it was the best veal dish I have had in a long time. The tiramisu was  beautifully presented and tasted like no other tiramisu I had. The dessert was to die for. The overall experience would have had five stars if the service was on point as the food. Hopefully I will return for the upcoming NY Summer Restaurant Week to try other dishes.

I came into this restaurant to eat in rather than order delivery. The space is rather small, but it seems like everyone get orders food here is mainly getting delivery. Regardless, this may be one of the best Thai restaurants you can order from the UWS.My girlfriend and I got a few items:Chicken Curry Puff - Delicious and the size of the puffs are very generous.Tom Kha Soup - Very interesting flavoring. It's not really spicy as advertised, but would recommend if you like that sweet coconut taste.Pad Thai - My girlfriend got this dish and I ended up liking her dish over what I ordered. Love the noodles and the peanuts when you mix it all together. She got her's with Tofu.Drunken Noodles with Flat Noodles - This is what I ordered. It's not very spicy, but the hint of spice is there. The sauce goes very well with the noodles. I got mine with Chicken.

We stopped by here for lunch, given they seemed relatively quiet and most of the other lunch spots in the area were packed. We used our check in deal for a free suppli, which is a fried risotto ball. It was hot and delicious! We also got two trapizzinis. They were just rolling out their brunch menu so we tried one of their egg and tomato sauce ones. It came with a poached egg inside which was pretty delicious but a little too gooey. Like they described, it tasted like a shakshuka in a pocket! The dough itself is a sourdough-like bread which was the best part. I think the meatball one was much better and went well with the bread and sauce.

**Title: A Delightful Feast for the Senses at the Cozy Hot Pot Haven**

From the moment I stepped into this charming hot pot haven, the decor commanded my attention. It was as if I had walked into a whimsical wonderland filled with oohs and aahs at every turn. Celebrating my mother-in-law's 78th birthday, we were treated to a private room that was nothing short of a visual feast. The walls came alive with moving images, and the table settings were a masterpiece of elegance and perfection.

The menu, illustrated with vivid pictures, made ordering an effortless experience. With eight rich and flavorful broths to choose from, each one was a testament to the restaurant's commitment to quality—certainly the finest broths our palates have ever savored.

A particular standout was the hand-sliced beef, so tender it nearly dissolved on the tongue. We found ourselves ordering two more platters, captivated by its delectable taste. Furthermore, the freshness of every dish was palpable, especially the fish slices, which were succulently plump and had the most luxurious buttery flavor.

A round of applause is due to Leo, our server, whose attentiveness was the icing on the cake. Whether offering a genuine smile or intuitively assisting with my mother-in-law's light jacket, his dedication to service excellence was unmistakable. He ensured our experience was seamless, always appearing at just the right moment.

Granted, this enchanting spot may be a tad pricier, but it delivers a dining experience that's worth every penny. Prepare to linger a while, as the joy of hot pot is in its leisurely pace, allowing for the savoring of each bite.

As an additional note, the music and acoustics provided the perfect auditory backdrop, complimenting the visual and gustatory marvels. Keep your eyes peeled for the delightful details, like the ceramic bowls on the ceiling or the playful images dancing across your table from above. This is a place where dining is not just about eating, but an immersive journey for all the senses. Enjoy the swish and savor of a truly memorable meal.

Title: A Delicious Reason to Exercise Patience - Smith & Wollensky

My boyfriend and I finally visited the renowned Smith & Wollensky during NYC Winter Restaurant Week, and it's safe to say it's become one of our top dining destinations. The Restaurant Week deal was an absolute bargain: a three-course feast for just $42 per person.

However, patience was a requisite for the evening. Despite having a reservation, we waited an additional 25 minutes to be seated, and service throughout the night was slower than expected. A friendly server did little to expedite our bread basket, drink orders, or meal request. At a high-end establishment like this, the service lag was a disappointment.

The silver lining? The food was utterly divine. The everything-seasoned bread crisps were irresistible, especially when slathered with the homemade butter. My Caesar salad was a crisp start, but the main event, the 10 oz. filet mignon, was the star of the table. I finished with their famed coconut layer cake and vanilla ice cream, which lived up to its reputation of being light, sweet, and moist - the perfect finale.

My boyfriend's selections were equally impressive, particularly the split pea soup, which was the best he's ever tasted. The roast beef hash, a usual feature at the attached grill rather than the steakhouse, was a revelation. Served house-style with a plethora of sauces mixed in, it's a dish that surprises in the best way possible. His meal concluded with a creamy and satisfying cheesecake.

We also indulged in a bottle of wine and shared a side of creamed spinach, which complemented our entrees well. While the prolonged service was a noteworthy downside, the sumptuous flavors of each dish made the waiting a small price to pay. Smith & Wollensky's culinary excellence shines through – it's a place where the dishes are worth the wait.
Two words: food poisoning. Looks like a dump, food equally as bad.I shared three rolls, none of them tested rotten but within two hours I knew I was doomed. Avoid.

I'm always a bit nervous about hole in the wall places in Chinatown just because they don't always look the most sanitary. The 3.5 stars on the review didn't exactly win me over either, but my friend assured me that this place was good. When I actually arrived, I had to say that I was pleasantly surprised. The restaurant is old, but it looks clean (and it was well air-conditioned too!). We went a little crazy with ordering because everything looked so good and it was also just so cheap. For the three of us, we ordered the following:1) H.K. Style Steamed Rice Noodle: 3.5/5 - This dish is a rice noodle roll that is covered in a sweet soy sauce and peanut sauce. It's not as soft as your typical steamed rice noodle roll, but it's still good. However, since one of our party is allergic to peanuts, the sheer quantity to split between two made it easy to lose its appeal amongst all the other good food that we had too. 2) Shrimp Steamed Rice Noodle: 5/5 - I have a soft spot for this dish, and this was so good. For only $3.50, the portion almost seems bigger than what you'd get at your traditional dim sum restaurant. The sauce was very good and the shrimp very tender.3) Fried Dough: 2.5/5 - This dish was just okay. We had originally intended to eat this with our congee, but the congee came first and we sort of forgot about it. It was a bit more oily than I would have liked but not too bad. It's only $1.50, so what more can you expect?4) Preserved Egg & Lean Pork Congee: 4.5/5 - It's been a while since I've had a good bowl of this congee (the last place I ordered it from was so gross so I was worried I was going to get something similar). However, it was actually really flavorful. Highly recommend!5) Pork Chop with Instant Noodle: 5/5 - I never thought I would come to a restaurant to eat instant noodles but this was so good. There was actually a good number of pork chops in the noodles and the noodles themselves were cooked to just the right consistency. It does make me think though that I can probably learn to make this myself at home, but nonetheless, it was nice to learn that it isn't always a bad idea to order instant noodles at a restaurant.6) H.K. Style Milk Tea: 5/5 - Perfect for the very hot day that we were eating on. The sweetness was not overwhelming and it was overall very refreshing.7) Pan-Fried Dumplings: 3/5 - It wasn't bad, but compared to all the other dishes, it failed to shine. I think it was also just so heavy and with how much food we already consumed, it wasn't super appealing anymore to have to finish a plate of dumplings. There are definitely better dumplings in the Chinatown area.Service is on the slower side, but they were very nice and got us everything that we needed. Overall, I'm definitely down to go back and try some of the other things on their menu!

We were wandering around the city and wanted a quick lunch.  The reviews for My Pie were great, so we checked it out.This is counter service, and you can choose from MANY slices of premade pizzas. They were fantastic. They have a process where they use two different temperatures in the oven--one for the bottom and one for the top.  This makes for a perfect crust.The place was casual (take out kind of casual), but it had seating.  It was clean and service was fast and friendly.  A great place for a quick slice!(And only order one slice--you will be fuller than you think!)

This Korean gastropub is located in midtown Manhattan (Koreatown), on 35th Street near 6th Avenue.  They serve some great fresh oysters and other pub fare and some nice drinks.  The place is a bit dark, but in all, a nice atmosphere.  I liked it very much!

A lot of college kids, but great food and drinks with plenty of TVs to watch sports!Tips: Make a reservation before you go especially if you have more than two or three peopleAtmosphere: Casual/cozy sports bar - be aware that it's also very loud Food: Something for everyone! I had the taproom burger (get the tater tots they're to die for) and my friends had the 307 Chicken sandwich - everything was delicious. Reasonable prices for NYC and you'll leave with a full stomach.Drinks: We went on a Saturday so we missed happy hour, but during the week there looks to be one. However, we had some awesome winter drinks (a little on the pricey side but totally worth it). I had the mulled wine and my friend had the spiked hot apple cider.

Mouthwatering marinated Galbi is to die for! Would literally just eat a meat salad of just their galbi. Excellent service and great atmosphere. I love how with all the noise of the grilling you can still hear one another speak. Also the wings are excellent and absolutely loved the egg soufflé. The potato salad bonchon was a nice surprise as well!

The charm of this venue remains intact, boasting not only good food but also exceptional service, notably from Feng, our personable server who truly enhanced our dining experience. A standout feature was the attentive refilling of our hot pot with broth, ensuring the spicy side remained robust throughout our meal. Additionally, the Rose tea comes highly recommended for a delightful finish.

Delicious fast casual Asian "fusion" which is just really bringing Asian flavors closer to home while putting it in a bowl like many of the places that have popped up in the city catering to the quick bite client.The space is definitely in need of a cleanse on a Saturday night but other than that I really enjoyed my flavorful bowl of food which also felt super healthy and clean. Best things I ate were the chimichurri sauce, the beets with the sweet potato noodle which changed color also in a beautiful way. The steak and the salmon are delicious. If you're looking for meat packed dishes you'll have to pay extra. Otherwise it was a great mix of tasty veggies and flavors.

I freakin love Taiwanese food!!! Last time I was in NYC, I had a horrific experience at another Taiwanese restaurant. However, 886 is a completely different story. Came in on a rainy afternoon and we were seated immediately. The service was extremely fast. Our waiter was a tall asian guy. I'm not sure what his name was, but he was extremely hospitable! He was always well mannered and served us promptly, always had a smile on. Great customer service doesn't always come around often these days, so I appreciated that a lot. In terms of the food, we ordered the lo ba beng, sausage party, savory soy milk, honey popcorn chicken, and a bottle of Taiwan beer. I really have nothing bad to say about anything that we ate. Everything was fantastic! I think the restaurant does a great job of putting their own American twist to traditional Taiwanese dishes without losing its authenticity. Also love that they have Taiwan beer. It's a classic in Taiwan and always paired with anything savory. Since it's light, it goes really well with heavier flavors. If I had to highlight my favorite dish, I have to give it to the lo ba beng. That pork was sooo soft and fatty. The juices from the meat paired with the rice was absolutely delicious. Great job 886! Will come again for my Taiwanese fix when I'm back in the city.

Title: A Cozy Spot for Unique Pie Flavors

My recent visit to this charming eatery left my palate delighted, especially with their mushroom pie—a must-try that melds the buttery goodness of garlic knots with the rich topping of juicy, chunky mushrooms and melted cheese. It's a slice of heaven for fungi lovers!

The mustard pie was an intriguing twist, catering well to those with a penchant for mustard. Although it may not be for everyone, as the taste could overwhelm, they cleverly serve it with a vodka sauce dip that provides a tasty respite for the taste buds. While the ham embedded within adds a nice touch, it could benefit from additional toppings.

The service was the cherry on top, with the exceptionally friendly guy at the counter elevating the overall experience. His warm interactions created an inviting atmosphere that would make anyone consider becoming a regular.

In summary, this spot is a solid choice for a casual bite, particularly if you're in the mood for a twist on classic pizza offerings. I'll certainly be back to sample more of their innovative slices.

Title: Satisfying Team Lunch with Room for Improvement

Our team ventured to this restaurant for a lunch outing and delved into the lunch special menu. I chose the Sichuan chef special chicken, which was a delightful treat, while my colleagues also expressed satisfaction with their meals. The service was commendable, attentive without being intrusive, and contributed positively to our experience.

Breaking it down:
- Food: 3.5/5 - The flavors were good, but I've experienced more impressive Chinese cuisine elsewhere in the city.
- Service: 4.5/5 - Efficient and friendly, the staff did well to ensure a pleasing dining experience.
- Price: 4/5 - The lunch specials were affordable, although there are competitively priced options in the area with superior fare.
- Portion: 5/5 - Generous servings that guaranteed nobody left hungry.

In summary, while the restaurant doesn't top the charts for its cuisine, it scores high on portion sizes and service, making it a solid choice for a team meal without stretching the budget.

Tried this location following my positive experience in the Midtown location before.Pretty much the same positive vibe.  Nice ambiance, professional service, good cut of steak that's cooked perfectly.  Nothing here from an overall perspective was bad in any way.  The food came promptly - from the salad to the NY strip to the (always) monstrous chocolate cake.  This is your standard gut-busting indulgent NY steakhouse meal.  Definitely a place that I recommend as a solid choice for huge cuts of meat.  Prices are what you'd expect for a steakhouse of this caliber.  Overall the experience was the same as my visit to the other location.  It's a great choice if you're looking for a consistent and reliable option for a meat haven.  And yes - the cake is gigantic.  I ate like 1/10th of it and took the rest home.  Still tasted divine a day or two later as I tried to slowly chip away at it ...

Pretty solid vegetable fajitas served with a ton of different vegetables. I went here with friends and it's a pretty good place for groups. Location is central around the Murray hill / gramercy area. I have had better fajitas in the city, but these stand out for being very filling.

I recently had the pleasure of visiting a delightful restaurant with an ambiance that strikes the perfect balance between warmth and invitation. The bar is notably spacious, yet it retains a cozy feel, catering to a variety of preferences with its extensive and playful drink menu. Although my visit was limited to sampling the appetizers, each option was delectable, leaving little doubt in my mind that their dinner offerings would be equally impressive. I highly recommend the Kiss Kiss Bang Bang cocktail for a refreshing and well-balanced treat.

Title: A Decent Thai Fix at At Nine

I recently visited At Nine for a weekend lunch and came away with mixed feelings. While the absence of special lunch deals was a slight disappointment, the prices remained fairly reasonable, with noodle dishes ranging from $13-$15 depending on your choice of protein.

The pad thai, although robust in taste—likely owing to the tamarind—fell short on moisture, yearning for a more liberal application of sauce. Alternatively, the spicy pad udon told a different tale; it was well-sauced and flavorful, though it bordered on too salty for my palate.

The compact dining area of the restaurant provided more than enough space, likely due to a slower weekend crowd. Service was prompt and satisfactory, adding a positive note to the experience.

In summary, while At Nine might not top the list of Thai eateries, it stands as a solid option for those in the vicinity with a hankering for Thai cuisine.

I was interested to try Maialino because Danny Meyer rarely fails me, but the food was just not... great. The restaurant is located inside the Gramercy Park Hotel and definitely has the vibe of a hotel restaurant (e.g. small children running loose). My group of four met up for a weekend lunch and ordered four pasta dishes to share among the two couples. I got to taste both the Fettuccine alla Bolognese (suckling pig ragu) and the Cacio e Peppe. The bolognese was yummy (albeit, small portioned) but the cacio e peppe was SO salty. It gave me such a bad mouth feel. I am all for pecorino and going all-in on cheese but the dish just wasn't pleasant. The latte I ordered was good though (the juice was SO overpriced), so I'd say stick to popping in for a quick caffeine fix if you're in the area/staying at the hotel, but avoid it for an actual meal if you're someone who actually likes bang for your buck (there are plenty of Michelin-starred Italian restaurants that are even cheaper).

We were here for dinner on a Friday. We ordered the assortment of spreads and the chicken yeero on pita bread. The assortment of spreads comes with 3 spreads and 2 pita breads. The spreads were delicious and the bread was really soft. The chicken yeero was good too. The service was ok. The pita bread was a little too greasy. This was more than enough for 2 people and worth the price. The one thing that bothered me was that they used plastic utensils when we were eating there. I would understand if it was a takeout. People need to start thinking about the environment.Overall I would give it 3.5,Food: 4/5Service: 3/5Price: 5/5Environment friendly: 2/5

Last evening, we chose this restaurant for a birthday celebration and it didn't disappoint. Their accommodation for dietary restrictions was outstanding, as I have celiac disease and the staff ensured I had a delightful meal tailored for me. The Greek salad was fresh, and both the grilled chicken and veggies were cooked to perfection. They delivered excellent catering service that truly enhanced our party experience. Highly commendable!

This spot is strange. The location is kind of killer, and the prices are low but the restaurant itself has a terribly offputting front window and almost zero atmosphere inside.During our weeknight visit, the only person working seemed to be cooking in back as well as begrudgingly taking orders and serving food.I think we enjoyed our food ok, but for me, it was mostly about the weirdly intense broth. It made me realize when I make things at home, maybe I'm in fact NOT overseasoning as my wife would like to tell me. The broth here is funky and heavy on flavor, even if the things floating inside it are marginal at best.I'm sure I'll never be back, but I'm glad I had the experience.

Oh man this place was recommended to us by multiple friends back in Texas and it lived up to its hyped! We had the beef seven ways and it was amazing! Definitely a must try for sure, recommended to everyone if you enjoy beef. Staff was friendly and even cooked our meat for us. We didn't get to try the whole menu but will come back for sure.
Ah I was hoping to really like this place! Been searching for good breakfast tacos in the city. These weren't bad but just nothing compared to real tex-mex! I'd stop in for some margs and queso!

I recently dined at a restaurant that thrives on customizable stir-fry dishes, allowing patrons to choose from an array of fresh ingredients including various types of rice, noodles, proteins, vegetables, and sauces. The beauty of this place is in watching your selection skillfully stir-fried on the spot, guaranteeing a hot and personalized meal. The choices are plentiful enough to promise a unique experience with every visit. I'm already looking forward to returning and experimenting with different combinations.

Title: A Rocking Experience with Flavorful Vibes

I recently dined at a spot that genuinely deserves the term "rocks," and not just for the lively beats echoing through the air. The West Indian Curried Shrimp was a standout, bursting with flavor that transported me straight to the islands, while the soju mule added a refreshing kick to the meal. The exclusive soju-based cocktail menu makes for a unique twist, and frankly, the quality of food and vibe made it easy to overlook the lack of other hard liquors.

However, be prepared for a bit of a wait as there's just a single bathroom catering to the crowd, which inevitably leads to a queue. Also, the prices are a slight stretch for the wallet, but considering the overall experience, it could be justified.

And if it's your birthday, brace yourself for a memorable celebration complete with sparklers, pulsating music, and a decadent funfetti cake that rounds off the night on a high note. This place isn't just a meal out, it's a vibrant celebration of food and fun.

I went to 'Cesca for brunch and I loved it. There was supposed to be a group of 10 but only 3 of us showed up--a lot of restaurants don't seat people if the entire party is not there but 'Cesca let us sit. Also, one of the ladies in the group knew about a deal (a two for one bottomless brunch), so I went in on the deal. You can change beverages so if you want a mimosa but then decide that you want a bellini, no problem, you can change up. Also, they didn't restrict me to one hour, in fact, as I paid the bill, the server gave me a mimosa for the road...lol. I got the "eggs your way" (eggs over medium, potatoes with toast and bacon) and duck fat fries. The food was great especially the duck fat fries with the aioli. Our server was very attentive and I liked the ambiance. I highly recommend 'Cesca for brunch--I would like to try this place for dinner.

Title: A Pho-nomenal Experience at The PhoBar!

I've been skeptical about Pho until my latest visit to The PhoBar, which honestly turned me into a believer. The cool, trendy vibe set the perfect scene for a delectable lunch. Note to future diners: it's a cash-only establishment, but every dollar is well worth it.

The star of my meal was the Classic Beef Pho, steeped in what they call the "Crazy Rich Broth." It lived up to its name—rich, aromatic, and simply divine. Accompanied by a variety of traditional fixings and a zesty chili paste, it's a dish I'm still savoring long after the meal.

While the wings didn't quite hit the mark for me, I wouldn't let that deter you. They were passable, but with Pho this good, who needs wings?

I'm already planning my next visit and would urge anyone with even a passing interest in Pho to give The PhoBar a try. Their Pho is not just good; it's remarkable. A definite must-visit for anyone looking to be wowed by a bowl of noodle soup.

Maison Pickle serves as the sophisticated sibling to the well-loved Jacob’s Pickles and the more recent Lucky Pickle Dumpling Co, offering a hip, less congested dining experience with striking decor. My visits, once for brunch and another for late-night drinks, were both delightful. The brunch menu presents a classic French/American selection; the French toast paired with chicken was a notable choice. The cocktail offerings are impressive and contribute to a perfect backdrop for a catch-up session with a friend. On a busy Friday night, the space was surprisingly uncrowded, a welcome contrast to its relatives. I’d recommend Maison Pickle for a stylish brunch or a relaxed drink. It’s an ideal spot for those looking to dine with a dash of trendiness or simply unwind with good company.

I recently dined at a new spot that took over a previous restaurant's location. As a vegan, I found the menu choices somewhat limited; for example, the vegetable dumplings unexpectedly contained meat. With limited options, I opted for the Mapo Tofu as my main dish and a side of Mustard Greens with Tofu. While both dishes were palatable, they lacked a distinctive flair that I was hoping for. The Mapo Tofu, in particular, departed from the traditional preparation I am accustomed to, leaning more towards a basic stir-fried tofu than the piquant, Sichuan classic it's named after.

On the upside, the availability of brown rice was a welcome addition to the meal. The service staff was amiable, though it felt as though the team was still in the process of ironing out their service flow. Overall, the experience was decent, but there's room for refinement both in the culinary offerings and the service execution.

This restaurant is an excellent choice for a quick bite, especially if you're craving a perfectly fried piece of chicken, a flavorful tea egg, or a hearty fried pork chop over rice. Service is swift, and you can expect generous portions that promise to satisfy your hunger.

Came by for lunch the other day and there was no line and the restaurant was empty at 11:45 am!The staff seems to be Thai and there were Thai patrons dining at the venue. The restaurant reminded me of Thailand!Lunch service started off with a complimentary salad which was quite tasty and fresh! The complimentary lunch dumplings were also filing and tasty!Ordered fish cakes as an appetizer and they were delightful! Fresh, fragrant, and flavorful!Spoke with the staff and customized the drunken noodles to be topped with soft shell crab and the dish was heavenly! The noodles were fragrant and flavorful! The soft shell crab was lightly fried and complemented this entree nicely!Staff was friendly too! $31/head after tax and gratuity for lunch! :D

Title: A Little Slice of Cuba

From the moment you step through the door, it feels like you're transported to another place entirely. The full immersion experience is undeniable, setting the stage for an exceptional dining adventure.

The cocktail menu shines with its simplicity and robust flavors. The Tropicana is a sweet, smooth siren that lingers on the palate, while the Havana Mule stands out as a memorable concoction with its refreshing zing.

Appetizer-wise, the plantain cups are a delight, especially with the trio of meat variations that tantalize the taste buds and leave you craving more. Each meat is tender and layered with flavors that are both comforting and exotic.

Moving onto the entrees, the pork shank is an absolute standout, especially when available as a special—it's tender, juicy, and enhanced by a savory brandy sauce. The ropa vieja, a constant presence on the menu, is on par in terms of deliciousness. Paired with impeccably cooked saffron rice and beans, it's a dish that truly celebrates Cuban cuisine.

The restaurant is easily accessible, and a weekday visit after 5 PM meant walking right in without a wait. The happy hour specials offered at the bar add an extra touch of joy to the early evening.

Sitting downstairs, the music enveloped us in an ambiance that felt authentically Cuban. The atmosphere throughout was cozy and inviting, contributing to an overall dining experience that was not only delicious but also remarkably comfortable.

I decided to order a minestrone soup today for lunch . It was odd, usually minestrone is a tomato based broth. It was tasty though, a little too oily for my taste though. The bowl was $14, with a diet coke it came out to be $20. Also, the service was super slow. So if you're in a rush for lunch, this may not be your place

We came here because we were starving and needed some shelter from the rain. My friend and I split the chicken parm platter which was good but definitely not the best I've ever had.  However the portion when we split was perfect to satisfy our hunger but not make us stuffed. Staff was attentive and nice and the chicken was what we needed at the time.

I recently visited a local pizza spot that served up fresh and tasty pizza with impressive speed. The staff was quick on their feet, which made the experience all the more enjoyable. However, there was a hiccup with my order, as I received different slices than what I had paid for. While the pizza I received was fine, it wasn't exactly what I had been looking forward to. Had the attention to detail been sharper, this review could have easily been a full 5 stars.

Extremely spacious, pretty attentive kbbq-grillers/servers, and I surprisingly left without smelling like I'd been cooking in a meat sauna. Phew! However, my kbbq craving was not satisfied after this, mostly because I was expecting extremely well marinated and succulent pieces of meat, and this didn't exactly deliver. Chef Special Roll ($17): super plump rolls, but quite pricey for the amount. Fish was decent, but the rolls overall were quite salty (that's before soy sauce was even added, and also, their soy sauce was loaded with sodium that I had to dip v e r y carefully and sparingly). Gogi on 37 Rolls ($14): you can see from the pictures, but presentation was severely lacking for this one. No angling of my phone or the plate could've salvaged what looked like some one just hurriedly tried to send this to our tables. Bulgogi was pretty dry, so not the biggest fan of this as wellCombo Option A ($95): comes with kobe beef brisket, prime beef ribeye, and prime beef shortrib. Quality wise, it's decent, but I was just really surprised that it came un-marinated. Or if it was marinated before-hand, I definitely couldn't taste it. They do come with some dipping sauces, but it also wasn't that great. However, the juicy rib eye really stole the show here - soooo good and a good amount of fat that had me licking my lips as I tried to reach for another piece before it was all gone (it was gone within seconds, seriously)Beef Tongue ($31): ok it's good but you REALLY need the sauces for this oneUnfortunately, for the prices and tastes, I would be heading elsewhere next time for my meats!

I'm not sure if I get the hype about this place although I admit my experience here started off on a negative note: My friend and I had a reservation for brunch and were made to wait 20 minutes from our reserved time. No apologies or anything for making us wait.My dosa was fine but I was still hungry after eating it. My friend's dish was pretty flavorless. I didn't really feel there was anything special about this place to warrant a second trip.

Title: Mixed Feelings on Cinco De Mayo Feast

I opted to celebrate Cinco De Mayo at home this year by ordering from a local spot, and my experience was a rollercoaster of flavors. While the portion of chips left me wanting more for the price paid, the salmon tacos were a delightful surprise. First time trying them and they did not disappoint.

On the downside, the shrimp fajitas fell short. The seasoning didn’t win me over, despite being authentic, but I must commend the freshness of the ingredients and the packaging. It was all top-notch.

The star of the show, however, was the margarita. It was the ultimate frozen concoction, achieving a perfect balance of flavor where so many others tend to be overly sweet. Kudos to the establishment for mastering this mix.

In the end, the sublime margarita has convinced me to give this place another try. Despite the hits and misses, I'm willing to come back. If it was just for the margarita, my rating would soar to a full 5 stars, but taking everything into account, I'll be back for a second round to see if the food can match up to that excellent beverage.

So food is pretty good and the Galbi was well seasoned and cooked. However, for $17 I received literally a few thin small pieces of meat, a lot of rice, and the tiniest amount of vegetables! We came to the restaurant Friday night slightly before 8:30. By 8:47 the chef came over and pretty much told us we need to leave bc he closes at 9. Wow! Ty for rushing us out! Not impressed by food quantity or service

My Friday night dinner at this restaurant with family and friends was a delightful experience! Reserving a table for our group of seven proved wise, as the wait times can be quite extensive. Opting for the pot hot and BBQ combo, my sister was thoroughly pleased, while the rest of us indulged in the two-hour all-you-can-eat BBQ. The service was commendable, with the staff setting up and preparing everything at our table. Each meat selection, from savory beef to succulent pork belly, was bursting with flavor, and the addition of vegetables rounded out the meal nicely. I’m already looking forward to my next visit!

Title: Hit or Miss at the New Location

I had a soft spot for the establishment's original site on 6th Street, which had fine-tuned its offerings right before moving. Their relocation, sadly, places them further from my daily hustle, making my recent visit long overdue. Upon finally dining at the new venue, I encountered a mixed bag. The half chicken meal, priced at $17, offers generous portions of poultry and rice, securing an excellent value and thus a three-star rating from me. However, the quality was inconsistent; the white meat was unexpectedly rubbery, and the once vibrant green sauce now tasted disappointingly diluted. On a positive note, the rice maintained its delectable reputation. Despite the issues, which could be early teething problems or a downturn in standards, I was neither impressed nor deterred by the customer flow at noon. Here's hoping the kitchen finds its rhythm soon and restores the chicken to its former glory.

Drinks: 2/5Stopped by for a drink. I asked for a gibson and the bartender looked at me confused. I asked for a gimlet and she still looked confused. Vodka soda, please. She understood that one.Service: 3/5The bartender was nice and accommodating. Wish they knew more about cocktails though.Ambiance: 4/5Nice bar. Pretty spacious and clean. I like the vibe in here. It's elegant and has a barn like feel.

We landed past midnight and were thrilled to find this hot pot restaurant still open. The menu prices were quite fair. We enjoyed a combination of savory hot pot and barbecue dishes. Although we suspect the staff had a light-hearted jest at our expense, as my friend caught on in Mandarin, the experience was still recommendable. A great late-night dining spot!

Came back less than a month later and really solidified my love for this place. My husband and I got into line ~35 minutes before opening and were the third ones in once the doors opened up. This time, we were dining with another friend so we got to try out even more things on the menu. For a group of three, we felt 3 small dishes and 2 large dishes was the perfect amount to share:The sweetbread salad was great - very refreshing and not at all spicy. It was on the milder dishes but had wonderful texture.The fish collar was very moist and flaky. This was also super mild compared to other dishes, so not a must-order but it was very tasty and pretty good value.The bone marrow was my least favorite of the night. You couldn't really taste the marrow, because of all the sauces and the charred bread.The pineapple curry duck was definitely delicious although a bit on the pricy side. For ~$30 you get 5 slices of perfectly cooked duck breast and large cup of rice (tasted like it was flavored with liver, in a good way) on the side.My favorite of the night was the crab fried rice. It was so flavorful and had very generous chunks of crab. This was so comforting yet luxurious to eat.Overall, another fantastic meal at Uncle Boons! Now that I've toured more of the menu, I'd say best meal would be: khao soi noodles, crab fried rice, and short rib curry.

Cheap, delicious Chinese food for a quick bite to eat or on the go! We ordered the beef stir fried hand pulled noodles, boiled dumplings, and fried dumplings. Everything came out within 10-15 minutes and was fantastic. The hand pulled noodles were perfectly chewy and flavorful. The dumplings were hot and had a nice crispy outer skin. Don't come here expecting outstanding service, but you will definitely get inexpensive and yummy food.

I visited with high expectations but faced disappointment when many menu items, including the black and white sando and spicy chicken kimbap, were sold out by 3 pm. We settled for the crunchy krab kimbap and chicken katsu, which, despite the steep prices typical of the area around The Vessels, seemed worth a try. Unfortunately, the limited selection dampened the dining experience.

Title: Delightful Dinner Experience

My husband and I enjoyed a wonderful dinner at this restaurant, which truly exceeded our expectations despite some mixed reviews online. To our pleasant surprise, the service was impeccable—attentive and swift. Our glasses were never left empty without a waiter inquiring if we needed a refill.

I indulged in the burrata to start, a generous and delicious portion, while my husband savored the tender calamari. For the main course, the artichoke and avocado salad I chose was refreshing with a zesty lemon dressing, and the thin pasta in my husband's lasagna was a highlight, elevating the entire dish.
