We capped off our meal with a delightful tiramisu, a perfect sweet note to end on. Based on this experience, I wholeheartedly recommend a visit to this restaurant for anyone looking for a gratifying meal with great service.

Title: Disappointing Packaging Overshadows Tasty Eats

I recently joined a friend for what I hoped would be an excellent Mexican meal at a local spot I'd often admired from afar. While the pork carnitas taquitos were flavorful and freshly prepared, with the kitchen accommodating my aversion to white onions, the experience was marred by the presentation. Drinks arrived in disposable plastic cups, the food in takeout containers, and we were equipped with plastic utensils – a disconnect from the otherwise charming ambiance.

In a confusing nod to sustainability, paper straws were provided, yet the excessive use of single-use plastic seemed incongruent with an eco-friendly message. Service was another sticking point; despite the takeout vibe, we felt obliged to leave a 20% tip, as per my friend's habit.

The quality of the wrap on the taquitos unfortunately aligned with other reviews – tough and unappetizing, at times indistinguishable from the paper it was wrapped in. To top it off, the blaring music made conversation nearly impossible. Overall, the visit left much to be desired, highlighting a need for a reevaluation of both environmental impact and dining experience.

Reasonable prices and tastes good. Different options to choose from the menu. Not sure why Jap Chae is on the appetizer menu because it's a large plate and unless you have bigger appetite you might need two people for that as main course. It does taste good and family style like the ones my friend's mom would make. I really enjoyed Jap Chae and the side dishes weren't bad. The steamed dumplings taste good, I really liked that dish. It's simple and light on my stomach. The tofu soup my friend had was okay, didn't taste as fresh or more like the soup taste like it's cooked with tap water rather then filtered water. It's not bad my friend had no complain and she liked it a lot I'm just personally very sensitive to the taste of liquids. It's not a place I'd frequent or a place I'd come all the way out for but if I'm craving some korean food and I'm around the area, I'd come back again. In fact, I would like to come back again to try other dishes since I see some mixed reviews and I'm very curious. The korean lady who was our waitress was really nice and so adorable. The other waiter that cleaned our table is pretty quiet but nice. Overall, it's not a very memorable experience but I did enjoy the service and the food.

I find most locations of The Smith to have a pretty comparable experience to each other. This one's dining room was loud, on par with most locations and maybe even a little louder. I'm not sure if it's the acoustics or what, but every location seems to have a low ceiling that creates a run. Anyway, I was happy to snag a last-minute reservation after being at a conference. I enjoyed the short rib cavatelli, which was rich and flavorful but not mind-blowing. The chicken pot pie was...interesting. Not in a bad way, it was just an unusual preparation that looked almost like French onion soup from the top due to the cheese. Service was speedy and reasonably friendly. I also had a nice virgin cocktail whose name I can't remember. Solid. Just don't come here wanting to have a deep conversation because you probably won't be able to hear your table mates!

Came here around 4 pm on a Tuesday and was able to get a table right away. It is a cute restaurant that is hidden away because of the construction happening around it. I split the bulgogi banh mi ($12) with my friend as an appetizer. It was very flavorful, highly recommend. Then the waitress recommended the Famous Beef Pho ($14) when I asked which was her favorite spicy Pho. The broth was amazing if you like spice. Not too spicy, just right.

If you haven't been to Carmine's with a group of friends yet, you're truly missing out on an essential Italian dining experience. The buzz around town is absolutely justified—Carmine's is the epitome of family-style Italian fare in the city.

A recent visit with two friends left us overwhelmed—in the best way—with their generous portions. We ordered a Caesar salad, zucchini fries, ravioli, and a meatball each. The pasta was perfect for sharing, but we barely scraped the surface of the salad and zucchini. It's clear that Carmine's is meant for larger groups; the value is unbeatable when you're splitting the cost among many.

Their bread basket deserves a mention too—delicious and quickly emptied. I'm eager to return to Carmine's with a bigger crew for another round of their hearty, traditional Italian dishes. If you're planning a visit, my advice is simple: gather your friends, go hungry, and get ready to be wowed by the size and the flavor. Trust me, your wallet (and your taste buds) will thank you.

I absolutely love this spot . My husband and I went here one summer afternoon and we were always dying to come to this spot so we decided to finally go . We were also trying to make it to there famous happy hour , we were glad we were able to make it to there . I can't wait to come back to this spot.

Stopped in here during Ana in the Big Apple fabric shopping day. On that rarest of events for me, an enjoyable shopping day, I foolishly got so caught up dashing from store to store that I forgot to eat (also exceedingly rare for me). I zipped into this place in a somewhat desperate blood sugar state. Fortunately, this is Napolitano style pizza, so it took mere minutes from the time that I ordered to the time that my piping hot pizza was ready. So delicious, and not only because I was famished. Comparable to the best wood-oven pizza that I've had at Pizzeria Libretto in Toronto. All ingredients are non-GMO, no additives, no preservatives. A substantially sized Margherita is only $9. In downtown NYC. I had enough left over for two more meals. The resto is clean with white subway tiles. The large restroom easily accommodates those in walkers or wheelchairs. I know this because there was some kind of outing for seniors going on. I had the impression that they come here on the regular. Polite service. No troubles with my allergies.Would happily stop in again the next time I'm in the garment district.

You order and pay with an iPad on which you can choose different preferences for your ramen, which is very convenient and don't have to wait for the check after eating. The waiter suggested the bold ramen as everyone's favorite as well as cheeky ramen and soul ramen, so I got the bold ramen with extra garlic and green onion. I highly recommend choosing extra on those ingredients as they made my ramen very flavorful. The broth was SO GOOD. I'm a big fan of Tonkotsu broth and it was so flavorful, probably one of the best ramen broth I've had in the city. But I was very disappointed with their marinated egg, which was supposed to be a soft-boiled egg but it came out as a complete hard-boiled egg. The pork belly chashu was also thin and gave a dry and hard texture instead of being a soft and juicy pork belly meat. The noodle was slightly undercooked but it was chewy. There's free seaweed on the table so you can also add it to your ramen. Overall, this is a solid ramen spot and I would give it a 5 star, but I'm settling with 4 because of the hard-boiled egg.

Just left here and man-- what a disappointment. We got seated pretty quickly (about 10 minutes after arriving). We were brought some bread, which was not warm, unfortunately. It would have been a nice touch. We got three bread rolls- one white bread and two multigrain. I asked for another piece of white bread and let's just say, I am still waiting for it... I asked three different people throughout dinner for bread and never received it.We decided to have drinks. My boyfriend's was good. I was brought the wrong drink. They replaced the drink with the correct one, but unfortunately it came in a glass that had someone else's lipstick on the rim. Fortunately, the manager came over and apologized for that and comped our drinks, which we were appreciative of.For the appetizers, we ordered the the French Onion Soup, a slice of Bacon and the Lobster Bisque. The french onion soup, although really cheesy, lacked flavor and basic seasoning. The bacon was okay. But my bf loved the lobster bisque!Next came the Porterhouse for 2, which was great, cooked perfectly and is the sole reason for the 3 star rating. Otherwise this would have been a 2 star rating. We ordered the corn side, which was lackluster in flavor. It tasted like wet cornmeal. Disappointing.Service was poor. We were always looking for someone to flag down. We also didn't have time for dessert since everything took so long and we had to be somewhere at 10pm.All in all, we will not be back.

Fast, delicious and cheap. This place hits all of these three requirements of a great greasy spoon. I got the "signature" wonton noodle soup and it was perfect on a cold wintry day. The broth was nicely seasoned but if you wanted a little more heat or salt, there was chili and soy on the table. The noodles were perfectly cooked and the number of wontons was appropriate. I hate when you go to other places and they chintz on the number of wontons. The filling of shrimp and pork was good. Some might not like the rough chop on the filling but it didn't bother me. I should have taken 1/2 of my dinner home because I could have definitely enjoyed it the next day but it was so yummy, I ate the whole bowl. The service was fast and our waiter was attentive. This place will not win you over by its ambiance but that's why it's a greasy spoon and they can make the food affordable. I recommend and I suggest you order the A3. I can't speak for the other dishes.

Title: Accommodating Service and Delightful Flavors for Groups

I recently had the pleasure of dining with a large group of eight at this restaurant, and the experience was nothing short of exceptional. Despite the last-minute nature of our reservation, the staff was incredibly accommodating, even when we needed to add additional guests to our table.

The restaurant offers a delightful array of dishes that cater to various dietary preferences, including vegan options, which is a thoughtful touch. Our table indulged in the Aloo Gobi, Chicken Tikka, and Dhingri Makai Palak, accompanied by the obligatory Garlic Naan. At roughly $17 for the vegetarian entrees and a little more for the meat options, the value was impressive. We shared two vegetarian dishes and one chicken dish among three people, alongside three orders of garlic naan, and we still had leftovers – though I suspect the portions might be just right for a heartier appetite.

The service was commendable; our waiter was attentive without being intrusive, striking the perfect balance. An unexpected delight was the complimentary appetizer from the chef, a thoughtful gesture that added a special touch to our dining experience.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a gem for large groups seeking quality food, variety, and excellent service. Whether it's for a family gathering or a friendly meetup, you're in for a treat.

Crepe was ok and the lady making it was nice but the other lady at the cashier was not good.I want a drink and picked the OJ, I've asked if was freshly squeezed and without even looking at me she said no.So I got the red ice tea, I've asked what it was and she said - Ice tea.I could clearly see that it was ice tea  but wanted to know the flavor however, she was so entertained chatting and avoiding eye contact that I couldn't be bothered.

Title: Hit & Miss at Trendy Spot for Thursday Dining

My recent dinner at this chic eatery started promisingly with a friend but ended on a less positive note. The lack of crowds meant we could walk in without reservations, a plus for spontaneous diners. The décor was a visual treat, perfectly curated for the social media savvy.

We kicked off with avocado fries – a novel and delicious choice I'd eagerly reorder. However, the main course, blue crab carbonara, was a disappointment. Despite its appetizing presentation, the crab managed to taste suspiciously similar to imitation crab, falling short of its tantalizing promise on Yelp.

Service started acceptable but quickly spiraled downward. After being virtually abandoned by our initial waiter, who seemed to vanish after his shift, a second attempt at ordering a drink from another server proved futile. Despite a detailed consultation on the beverages, my drink never materialized.

Though I'm tempted by the thought of more avocado fries, the lackluster main dish and inattentive service mean I won't be returning. In a city like New York, with an abundance of dining options, it's not hard to find establishments that deliver on both food and service.

Nami Nori is hands down one of the best new 'sushi' restaurants to come to the city. I say 'sushi' because it's more like sushi tacos, or open style temaki handrolls. Each piece is incredible. The only negatives are there is always a wait here unless you can arrive 30 minutes before they open, whether lunch or dinner. Otherwise the wait will get more unbearable. I highly recommend lunch because of the $20 lunch special which comes with chef's choice 4 temaki handrolls and appetizers. It's a good deal, and you can order more a la carte of course.My first visit involved a 30 minute wait with a group of 3 on a Saturday for lunch, just before opening. There was no line at all at first, but 15 min later, there were at least 10 people waiting. When they try to seat you, definitely ask for the counter (especially if with a small group, or else they'll try to seat you at a table). We all ordered the lunch special, which consisted of miso soup, edamame, spicy sea bass, yellowtail scallion, california, and cucumber black sesame with miso plum (vegan). Additional orders included furikake fries, x.o. scallop, uni, toro scallion, and spicy crab dynamite. You can witness the incredible presentation of each temaki in attached photos. The chefs are furiously preparing each roll but still with care and diligence. I loved every roll, and I was really surprised by the vegan roll too, in which the black sesame sauce was fantastic. The uni, toro, and scallop were totally worth ordering on top of the lunch special. While still good, I could have done fine without the spicy crab dynamite. It's very creamy and rich, so I would avoid if you've had one too many rolls already, or I would order this last as a finisher. The best part of this temaki though is the crispy seaweed, which I think should be an option for every roll (please). Everything from the seaweed to the rice to the fish at Nami Nori was just near damn perfect.Definitely recommend Nami Nori to sushi lovers or just any food lover in general. If you've been reading up on alot of hype about this place right now, there's good reason. I was skeptical at first, but all expectations were exceeded. The lunch special is a reason to return for sure, but make sure to order some primo rolls a la carte because it will be worth it.

This is part 2 of my so-called stakeout quick eats.  I was in an unfortunate situation where I was tasked to man the car in New York City, whilst  busing my MIL from one appointment to the next.  What better thing to do during these moments of boredom than to scope out some good quick eats on the Yelp app?I did just that and was delighted to learn that just mere 10 yards ahead of my perched car was the Yiwanmen or yee won mien, which literally means one bowl of noodle.  Since this was to be consumed in front of the steering wheel, I had to forgo their staple noodle entrees and go for their snacks -- specifically their savory crepes (jian bing) which were actually prominently featured in their menu.  I was going for their Pork Belly Crepe for $6 based on the takeout menu.  To my dismay, the new price was now $8. I thus changed my order to the Pork Belly Bao and the Beef Bao instead.It took a mere 5 minutes for my order to be ready.  While welcomed in light of the fact that my car was illegally parked, it wasn't a good sign for the food.  The buns weren't very fluffy; I had to wonder if their were microwaved. The visuals were enticing; unfortunately that was dampened by their miniature sizes.  I'd liken them to the size of my credit card.  A bit of a bummer.  The pickled radish gave each bite a nice crunch, along with a sweet and acidic kick; however, the pork belly wasn't moist like I had expected.  Between the two, I preferred the beef Bao, partly because I had no expectation.Despite the modern glass exterior, this is a hole-in-the-wall joint with charming interior and fun menu items.  While not impressed on this outing, I wouldn't mind trying their other offerings in the future -- but not their baos.

My dining experience last night was a far cry from the high expectations set by my usual go-to, Dynasty Soul Food. Reluctantly, I visited this establishment upon finding Dynasty unavailable. To my dismay, the evening took a shocking turn when my companion J.R. was unexpectedly shot amidst our meal, casting a further shadow on the night.

A word to the wise—Dallas might pride itself on barbecue, but this place, unfortunately, reinforces the subpar reputation I associate with BBQ in both Dallas and New York City. The offerings here simply can't hold a candle to the authentic flavors and quality I've come to appreciate elsewhere.

I would hesitate to recommend this restaurant but, for the sake of fairness, suggest that the adventurous give it a try to form their own opinion. However, if you find yourself craving BBQ in New York, I'd steer you towards Mighty Quinn's at Summerlake for a more satisfying experience. This spot barely scrapes by with a single star, and that's solely because it isn't part of a chain.

The service here is quick and friendly and the Sichuan salmon bow was delicious and filling. The space is extremely clean and welcoming even if it is small. I will be coming back to this spot for the delicious poke bowls!

My friends and I decided to come here for dinner. We made reservations in advance for a Wednesday night and the place itself was decently packed when we got there around 7 pm. The place itself is pretty cozy and cute, the place was more long rather than wide and they do have a pretty big seating area in the back. There were four of us and we got seated in a booth. The menu had a mixture of Viet and Thai styled foods and they did have a variety of items and for some of the dishes, you could definitely swap out one meat for another and we were also able to adjust the spice level for some of them which I thought was pretty nice! All my friends decided to get the Khao Soi but they swapped out the chicken for tofu/shrimp (shrimp was an additional $1) and they all loved their dishes. I went with the Laska which was extremely well flavored and delicious. It was the perfect cold day comfort food, on the menu it did mention that it was spicy but I did not find it to be spicy at all. The Laska had both pork and shrimp and the portion size was pretty big for the price. They were also extremely generous with the pork and the shrimp in the dish as well. The only one downside is that I found the noodles to be slight soggy for my liking (I tend to noodles a little harder) but other than that it was delicious.Overall, I definitely see myself coming back here in the future!

Title: Unmatched Lunch Experience at Jean Georges

Rating: ★★★★★

Once again, Jean Georges delivers an impeccable dining experience, solidifying its five-star status. The lunch deal is unbeatable - at $44, you indulge in a three-course meal that commences with a delightful serving of complimentary sourdough bread.

Today's surprise was none other than Jean Georges himself gracing the establishment with his presence. A testament to the restaurant's commitment to excellence, the food was flawlessly prepared. The tuna tartare was a refreshing starter, and the hake entrée was a savory delight – though a word to the wise, its spiciness is not for the faint of heart. The meal concluded on a high note with a chocolate cake that can only be described as perfection.

For anyone seeking an exquisite lunch in town, look no further. Jean Georges remains the culinary gem that continually shines bright.

I recently dined at Ruby's and I have to say, the culinary experience was nothing short of delightful. The shrimp pasta and creamy chicken pasta tantalized my taste buds, while the fries and mushroom omelet only added to the medley of flavors. The ambiance of the restaurant, bathed in various shades of pink, provided a charming and quirky vibe that was quite enjoyable.

However, the dining experience was marred by the excessive wait times. The fact that they don't accept reservations is a major downside, particularly for a restaurant of its size. The policy of not seating incomplete parties is also a point of contention. For instance, last night, despite having arrived early to enjoy some drinks, my friend and I were denied a table until our entire party was present, which felt rather inflexible. Furthermore, the restaurant's layout can best be described as cramped, creating an uncomfortable dynamic where navigating between tables feels like an intrusive dance with fellow diners.

In summary, while the food at Ruby's is exceptional and the decor delightful, the logistical aspects of managing wait times and seating need significant improvement. I like dining at Ruby's, but would be more enthusiastic if they implemented a reservation system for better customer experience.

Really good pizza but didn't exactly blow me out of the water. As Lombardi's claim to fame is that it is the first pizzeria in the U.S., expect it to be busy any time of the day. My friend and I went here on a Wednesday night and waited around 15-20 minutes so nothing crazy but I would expect a much longer wait during peak times. We stuck with one of their signature dishes- the clam pie.  Pros- a more than adequate number of clams, a solid crust, and enough to share among two people (not sure about three people, or maybe I just eat too much). Cons- a solid crispy crust shouldn't necessarily mean that the pizza itself should be ridiculously crispy as well. No, it was not as hard as a rock, but it definitely could have been better than what it was. Rather than that, I don't have any complaints. Definitely squeeze the lemon they give you over the pizza. Or, rather, squeeze it over each individual slice before you eat it so it doesn't get soggy quickly. Enjoy!

Pretty solid but a little basic option. Glaze is an affordable midtown spot that is relatively healthy and hearty. Choices are essentially a rice bowl with a main like protein/veggies with teriyaki sauce and a little salad with dressing or a salad composed of mixed greens, edamame, tomato, and cucumber with your choice of dressing (not sure I got sprouts in mine as listed).
Had the truffle shuffle from their stiletto pizza line to go.... LOVED IT.  The pepperoni and salami? Is good on it's own but the truffle ranch is really really really good.

York Avenue, I pretty much never end of eating around there. My wife and I had just left an event nearby, and we wanted to end the night with a good meal. Yelp helped us find this relatively new spot, and the menu and reviews looked interesting enough to warrant further investigation.It's a super rainy Monday evening, and when we got we ended up being the only customers there. The emptiness didn't throw us off, and we were quickly seated by our server for the night Grace. She let us take a seat wherever we felt comfortable.After getting settled in we perused both the drink and food menus. The drink menu is underwhelming, with no cocktails and just a few beers and wines. The food menu is what you go there for, and it didn't have that many options as well. Placing our orders was easy, and the drinks and food came out quickly. My wife ordered a glass of red (you have three options), and it was quite the generous pour. As we waited for the main dishes, Grace brought out a complimentary small plate of glass noodles. The noodles were beautifully soft and had great flavor.The main courses had plenty of flavor as well. My wife ordered a pho, and asked Grace for hot sauce. Grace encouraged us to try a spicy spice they usually add to the pho as they cook it upon request if you want it to be spicier, and my wife liked it. My pancakes had a great savory flavor, and the sautéed mushrooms had great flavor as well.I recommend you check this place out when in York Avenue.

Title: A Tasty Affair at Laut

Review:

My experience at Laut was nothing short of delightful. Despite the Friday night crowd, we were seated promptly—a stroke of luck for our party of six. Future diners take note: reservations are a wise move during peak hours.

The restaurant exudes a vibrant yet cozy vibe, striking a perfect balance between fun and intimacy. The culinary journey we embarked on was impressive, with shared dishes like Roti Telur, Nasi Lemak, Massaman Curry, and the standout Mee Hoon Goreng Noodles, each bursting with authentic flavors.

The service deserves applause; our meal arrived swiftly, and the staff was attentive throughout. With a menu rich in variety, I'm already anticipating my next visit to explore more of Laut's offerings.

This place is very trendy, but to me it's your typical hotel type of restaurant. Normally, I don't find these restaurants wowing from a taste factor, but aesthetics-wise this place is modern and trendy. I came here in the winter with my friend, but we did sit in the outdoor enclosed and heated portion. I bet in the summertime this place is more packed. I got a simple burger which was juicy and cooked well, but again I can't say the burger was so memorable to the point where I'm thinking about it again. I would totally come back here to grab a drink since the bar area looks trendy and upscale. It's a good hotel addition.

Yes, found a good quick service spot for some Korean street food!The dukbokki is good and the fried stuff is of course good. The kimbap is pretty good for the area and if you can't be in Flushing. The combos are fun and is something that really helps me want to order from here. I would like to see a few more K-Street food make an appearance here, but this is all you would reasonably want in a hole-in-the-wall K-town QSR, so that's two thumbs up from me.

Haymaker is located conveniently by Penn Station. My high school gfs and are scattered in North Jersey, Long Island City, and Central Jersey (moi). We decided meeting in the City would be the perfect compromise and voila, Haymaker. The bar also takes reservations online and we were able to find a reservation easily last minute on a Friday night.Haymaker has an upscale pub vibe, and a wonderful draft menu. I got an amazing peanut butter stout. The cheeseburger was juicy and delicious, a double patty of greatness. I wish they asked how you want your burger cooked, as I like mine medium and not well done. My friends said their veggie burger and mac n cheese were good. We shared the brussell sprouts as an appetizer. I don't like sprouts at all, but these were actually pretty good.

Title: Superb Dining Experience with Stellar Service!

My dining experiences at this restaurant were nothing short of fantastic, on not just one, but two separate occasions. The first visit was prompted by family from the UK, and despite our lack of reservations, we were warmly accommodated with a prime table boasting an impressive view. Their kindness truly made us feel special.

The second visit celebrated my cousin's engagement, where the establishment generously offered complimentary champagne and appetizers, a delightful surprise that added to our festivities.

Culinary-wise, the restaurant hits high notes with standout dishes like the exquisitely grilled octopus, Banana Leaf Sticky Rice, succulent black angus bavette steak, and the savory lamb dim sum. In contrast, the only miss was the upside-down pineapple cake, which fell short of our expectations.

Service throughout was exceptional—attentive and personal. The ambiance complemented the dining experience perfectly, enhanced by the picturesque views of the Vessel and the water.

In summary, this restaurant offers not only mouth-watering cuisine but also exceptional service and an inviting atmosphere, easily making it a go-to destination for any special occasion or casual outing.

I recently visited a fabulous spot that's perfect for a late-night drink. With both indoor and outdoor seating, it's an ideal choice for those balmy summer evenings. The ambiance is laid-back, matched by the cool and friendly staff, along with an inviting local crowd. To top it off, the drinks are not only delicious but also reasonably priced. It's a gem for anyone looking to unwind without breaking the bank.

Came here with my coworkers and have mixed feelings about this place. First off my initial impression was the atmosphere is undeniably unique. I felt like it was so thoughtfully decorated. It was loud and hard to hear at moments. In addition, this was on a week night and it was very crowded. I'm mixed with how I feel about the food. I ordered a chicken quesadilla; it was bland and tasteless. As for the chips and guacamole, generally acceptable and in a cool bowl. Margarita was a standard, nothing special and pretty expensive. Side note: After I already paid for the margarita I checked into yelp to learn you get 50% off a margarita. I was pretty mad at myself for not checking in before I brought it. I would probably come back for just the guacamole.

Interior - very cozy yet a bit dressy vibes here, especially since they got Christmas decorations up!! They have a lot of tables also a bar.Service - great service! They happily answered all the questions I had regarding the choices of food.Taste - they make great seafood here! Most of us got seafood plates and they all tasted very consistent. The tiramisu was delicious and decent portion for $8.A three course meal took us about two hours to finish, great time duration to gather with friends during the holidays. This place did get a bit out-of-expectation pricy so thus the four stars. Overall a pleasant experience here

I recently visited a surprisingly spacious ramen shop on the Upper East Side and was impressed by the generous portions they served. I opted for the tonkotsu chashu ramen and found the serving size larger than the usual ramen offerings. While the broth initially seemed a tad bland, a touch of chili oil was all it took to enhance the flavor profile. The chashu itself was tender and satisfying, truly hitting the spot. Additionally, the fried chicken dumplings were a delightful complement to the meal. I'd certainly recommend this place to anyone looking for a hearty ramen experience in the area.

"Stepping into this quaint eatery, the alluring aromas of simmering broths immediately tantalize your senses, promising a feast for the soul. My experience here was highlighted by a generous serving of niku udon, a steaming bowl of comfort topped with a perfectly cooked egg. The beef and tripe were the epitome of tenderness, melding flawlessly with the savory broth for a harmonious symphony of flavors.

Do yourself a favor and don't overlook the appetizers – the chicken is an absolute delight. Boneless, succulent, and with just the right amount of chew, it could very well stand as a hearty dish on its own. If you arrive with an ample appetite, this place is a gold mine. Just be warned: the portions are hearty, so come hungry!"

Title: A Perfect Pregame Bite at a Charming Spot

I recently visited this charming little restaurant conveniently located near MSG, and it was exactly what I needed before heading to a game. The ambiance strikes a comfortable balance between casual and refined, with its inviting new interior, versatile seating options from cozy booths to bar stools by the front window, and a tranquil area with tables at the back for a more relaxing experience.

The beer selection impressed me with its range of seasonal options, showcasing the care put into curating their offerings. I opted for a refreshing beer to accompany my meal, setting the tone for a great lunch.

The food was straightforward yet delightful. The tuna salad was exactly as described, a straightforward heap of tuna atop lettuce - unpretentious but fresh. The highlight was the veggie burger, which packed a delightful kick and came with a side of unique, tasty coleslaw that had a healthful twist.

I would heartily recommend this spot for anyone looking for a great meal in a lovely setting before or after an event at MSG. It's a place I'm certainly marking for a return visit.

Title: Cozy Ambiance, Good Eats, and a Few Service Hiccups

I visited a local restaurant this past Saturday with a group of seven friends for a dinner celebration. We were promptly seated upon our arrival, thanks to our reservation. The winter-themed decor provided a cheerful, though somewhat spartan, atmosphere for our evening.

Service started off on an unusual note, with our waiter appearing somewhat distracted, especially during our drink order. While half of the group opted for a bottle of Sancerre, the other half was left unqueried. Additionally, one of our party had to wait noticeably longer than the rest to receive their drink, which was puzzling.

Our diverse order included indulgences like Yellowfin tuna crudo, crab cake, and pumpkin ravioli, alongside healthful options from the vegan menu such as Caesar salad and Kabocha squash. The butternut squash soup and Brussel sprout leaves were delightful starters, while the main dishes like Branzino, salmon, and halibut were all cooked to perfection.

Unfortunately, the short rib didn't quite hit the mark, arriving too dry. However, the chicken dish stood out for its moistness and flavor, and the vegan options were appreciated by those with dietary restrictions. As an accompaniment, the broccoli and Cheetos, and the truffle waffle fries were unique and tasty sides.

Though we skipped dessert, the restaurant gracefully surprised us with two complimentary desserts to celebrate a birthday in our group - a thoughtful touch that enhanced our overall experience.

In summary, despite a couple of service missteps, the night was enjoyable, marked by very good food and a warm, inviting atmosphere.

Good, but average. I don't know, to me most Korean BBQ places are overpriced and taste the same. We got their marinated beef and a plate of pork belly. It was good, but I don't know, I wouldn't say it was anything special. They cook the food for you, so that was nice because everyone can eat at the same time instead of one person cooking.The interior is pretty cool. There are like little shacks within the place.Definitely use Yelp's active waitlist! It was so busy when we came.

Let me tell you, this place is pretty amazing! For one, it's super pretty inside! Very well lit, cozy, and quite spacious. Very relaxed atmosphere overall. Perfect for a regular lunch/dinner stop or even for a birthday celebration.The staff members are as friendly as they get. Very attentive and willing to help! Now let's talk food. The menu is huge!My friend and I spent at least 20 minutes looking through it, trying to figure out what to get because the options are endless. We decided to start with the oysters and fried calamari appetizers. SO GOOD. The fried calamari specially, I did not want to stop eating.For our main dishes, I decided to go with Combo A which consisted of 1 pound of live crawfish, 1 pound of big head fish, potatoes and corn. Let's just say it was A LOT and I ended up leaving with a leftover bag.My friend got the fried diced chicken with spicy chilly and it tasted amazing! Next time that's definitely what I will be ordering. All in all, I liked this spot and I would most definitely recommend!

Visited this restaurant drawn by its inviting ambiance and found it to be favored by an older clientele. However, the food didn't quite match up to the prices charged. Both the carbonara and the fried fish we ordered were passable but forgettable. Service was adequate, though our waiter's insistence on pricier options felt somewhat overbearing. The drinks offered some consolation, being decent, but failed to reach a level of 'amazing'. While not a total letdown, the overall experience wasn't compelling enough for a dedicated return visit—might reconsider if convenience brings us close by.

Despite initial skepticism owing to its unremarkable star rating, my experience at the restaurant for a quick lunch with my visiting parents was surprisingly good. The lunch specials were not only wallet-friendly but also truly delectable. Seating by the expansive windows offered an excellent perch for people-watching, adding to the dining experience.

While the ginger salad dressing deviated from the norm, it was a pleasant departure from the usual fare. The Beef Negimaki, in particular, stood out as a highlight — it was utterly scrumptious and I would certainly recommend it. The spicy tuna roll, on the other hand, was a letdown with an off-putting flavor that didn't hit the mark.

We also had the opportunity to try the fried king crab triangle appetizer, which was a delight and rounded out our meal on a high note. Overall, the eats were impressive and I would return for another savory venture, perhaps steering clear of the spicy tuna next time. Yum indeed!

I had higher hopes for Telio.  I had heard that the food was quite good, so we gave it a try.My biggest gripe is the way it is laid out.  It isn't huge, so they have found a way to fit as many tables in the place as they can (think Tetris!).  Unfortunately, we were literally on top of other diners.  I could barely squeeze in between the two tables, and once seated, there was not room for my purse and that of the lady sitting next to me (whom I didn't even know).  I ate with my purse on my lap.  My nephew had to sit with his chest to the table so that the waiters could get past our table.Service was slow---not horrible, but slow.  It took quite a bit of time to get someone to take our order. Once our food arrived, only three of us were served.  Apparently the fish my son ordered took longer---about ten minutes longer.  The scampi was so oversalted, it was inedible.  The moussaka was quite good.I think this place has potential.  I would be willing to try another dish or two, but the layout of the place really makes me not want to go back.

Title: Twice as Nice - A Slice of NYC Heaven

During a weeklong escapade in New York City, one pizzeria commanded our attention not once, but twice. This gem, nestled amidst the vibrant chaos of Times Square, serves up a triumvirate of pizza perfection – cheese, pepperoni, and the more elaborate supreme, along with a no-frills white pizza for those inclined.

What makes this eatery stand out? It's the winning combination of wallet-friendly prices and mouthwatering quality. The classic cheese and pepperoni pizzas took top honors in my book, boasting an irresistible thin crust and generous proportions that can only be described as New York-style grandeur.

However, a word to the wise: these slices are best devoured fresh. Leftovers lose their luster by the next day. Also, prepare for the inevitable queue, a testament to the food's allure and its prime location. 

A pro tip for fellow diners: Know your order before reaching the counter. This little prep work helps the line move swiftly, getting you to pizza paradise that much faster.

In summary, for an authentic slice of the Big Apple that satisfies your taste buds and your budget, look no further. Just remember to enjoy it hot and on-the-spot!

This place has the best lunch deals. Around 10 dollars for an appetizer and a main. Absolutely mindblowing deals in my opinion. The service was great and I liked the ambience too. I ordered the Thai dumplings, and they sure are a unique treat. The skin is layered, with chicken and peanuts inside. It was both soft and crunchy, and a genuine flavor explosion in my mouth. I also had their pad thai, and you can never go wrong with pad thai. The peanut and lemon blended well together with a slight sourness. Honestly great portion size-too big for me to finish-for the price you are paying. The green salad also had a lovely spice and crunch to it, and the fried rice had an aromatic soy smell. Overall, great lunch and would definitely return to try other dishes!

Havana Central serves overpriced Cuban food, but it's expected being a block away from Times Square. Their number one selling point is their ambiance- it's dim, there's latin music in the background, and their interior decor is retro-tropical themed. They also have decent alcohol menu with visually attractive drinks.For 1 drink and 2 entrees, the bill came to $98 including tips. Holy cow. Recs:(+) Tour of Havana $28- it's a small 3 plate dish stacked on a 3 tiered stand. Comes with a plate of rice and beans which is not explicitly stated in their menu. Meats include: pernil (roast pork), ropa vieja (braised beef), and chicarrones de pollo (cuban fried chicken). The chicken was dry and rather tough. The pernil and ropa vieja were the highlight of the night-tender and flavorful. This is a must try for those not wanting to commit to entree sized portions of these meats. To skip: Seafood paella $32. Had I known the Tour of Havana would include rice, I would not have ordered this. It was far too much for my sister and I. Ideal for a party of 4 who have ordered a lot of appetizers looking for something starchy to complement their meal. Lesson learnt, if you're a party of 2- aim for their apps only.

So I've been to their other location and I wasn't too impressed- but this location right here, changed my opinion of black tap! For starters, the servers, and people you meet when you enter are a lot friendlier! There was a bit of a wait- and in the winter it isn't fun since there is no standing space and you have to wait outside. We ended up waiting just a little under 30 minutes but it was worth it. As mentioned, staff were all great! That's always a a huge point for me. We started with their onion rings- they were massive and delicious! I went with their vegan bowl with quinoa. I loved the bowl, it was hearty, filling and didn't feel too heavy. We saved room for dessert, because just look at those shakes! We went with their cake shake. The waiter told us to cut the cake and add it to the shake- great tip and highly suggest it! The shake was delicious and the cake on its own was delicious as well! I would definitely come back here again!

There is a French renaissance in NYC starting wIth Frenchette, Pastis, Le Crocodile & now Quality Bistro & the soon you be reopened Le Veau De Or.  Quality Bistro is a sprawling sumptuous room , crowded on a Monday. Banquettess, & booths abound. I sat at the bar- some revamped olD school stools which were comfy and awkward at the same time. The decor is impressive.Ate:Escargot $16- small portion Now, I'm a fiend for these delicacies &  I love Pastis version in buttery cups of cast iron. These uniquely come shell on laying in an addictive garlicky green sauce. The snail can be tricky to remove and one refused completely. Very delicious. I will be back for much more. The wait staff is super accommodating.. PS water should be chilled - no ice unless requested as befitting a dining experience at this high price point.

I recently visited this restaurant for their Friday happy hour, which I must say is quite the steal, especially for a downtown spot. The mango margarita I ordered was delightful and, at $8, felt like a bargain. 

The happy hour food menu didn't disappoint either. The chips and guacamole were bursting with flavor and made for a perfect shareable appetizer. However, the highlight of my visit was unquestionably the octopus tacos. At just $8, not only were they surprisingly affordable, but they were also delicious. The octopus was expertly cut and seasoned, transforming what could have been a mere snack into a memorable culinary delight. I left satisfied with the flavors and the value I got. Highly recommend checking out their happy hour for some tantalizing treats!

Madame Vo has been on my "must go list" for a while now. It's been recommended to me by several people who appreciate good Vietnamese food. I definitely suggest making a reservation as the restaurant is on the small side. We had a 6:30 pm reservation and they seated us promptly. The service was very good-- our water glasses were filled often, when we asked for Items they were brought quickly, etc. Now onto the food!Ordered:Cha gio ($13)- they serve four fried spring rolls per order. The shell was crunchy and inside was a full shrimp with the tail sticking out. I found this presentation to be clever. To be honest, I didn't taste much crab or pork (also inside the spring rolls) but the flavor was good anyway. The sweet sauce on the side was tasty. The best thing on the plate in my opinion was the pickled jicama and carrots. So so good! I'd order this dish again. Vermicelli Bowl ($15)- this bowl had a generous portion of tender grilled chicken on top with cucumbers, pickled jicama and carrots, mint, chopped peanuts and crispy fried garlic, all on top of vermicelli. I'd also order this again. Suon Kho ($16)- this was the real winner of the dinner. Little meaty pieces of spare rib, cooked in a sweet and tangy sauce made of coconut and pineapple juices, this dish was awesome. I should point out, this dish is hard to eat "prettily"- since there are little bones in the spare ribs. As long as you don't mind working at it, I say get it!Madame Vo ($16)- although I enjoyed this soup, I don't think I would order it again. This visit showed me that there are other great dishes to order at Madame Vo. Madame Vo is a nice addition to my list of Vietnamese restaurants I visit. I'd recommend it.

We were in NYC for a quick vacay and stayed at the Madison Hotel, which was right across from Moonstruck. Our hotel window was facing Moonstruck and I often wonder how this place would be like. My husband and I decided to give it a try on our last day for brunch. When you enter, you're greeted by all the cakes and pastries in the front behind the glass case. The restaurant looked like it transported me into some sci-fi alien like place but I felt a little confused about what the theme was supposed to be. Our waitress took us to be seated at the back. The restaurant was packed with people already and it was a Monday morning. People were rushing in and out before work for quick to-gos or dine in. I ordered a cup of coffee to start out and my husband ordered a fresh squeezed orange juice. After a few minutes of looking at the menu, I decided to get the smoked salmon with hollandaise sauce. Our order came 20 minutes later and it looked awesome! The salmon was nicely salted and perfectly smoked. Most smokes salmon I've had in the past we're super salty, but this one was perfect and the sauce complimented it well. The potatoes were nothing special, but it was nice to have it as a side. I wouldn't say this place was the best, I've had better brunch elsewhere but it was a nice little restaurant I was curious about and decided to satisfy that curiosity.

What's someone from the Lower East Side doing up here? Going to the Museum of the History of New York.And stopping by El Aguila for a taco lunch. I had the al pastor and fish tacos, and some ice cold horchata. Yum! Al pastor was moist with obvious pineapple pieces. Fish was fried tilapia I think. They had a nice selection of sauces. For NYC Mexican, this place is better than most. It's super casual. Kind of like a Mexican diner with a menu that includes breakfast options. It's a step above a dive--a small step. People were coming and going. The service was nice and fast. The place is clean. The decor makes you feel you're in Mexico.It's not fancy, but good tacos.

So I really really really enjoy the esthetic of this place and the vibe here. Only mistake was bringing kids, well I should say brining MY kids lol we had to dance battle another family for a table because my kids couldn't reach the bar height tables. I got the pulpo, which was amazing, and the chicken paella (pass). My kids got pizza opps I'm sorry I mean cocas and that was really really good too. We were still hungry so we also got a steak sandwich which was just ok.to wash everything down we got a dozen churros which were just ehhh. Overall this place looks cool af but for me missed the mark on some of the food. Granted I didn't get everything but out of all the food I ordered the pulpo and the cocas were the only notable dishes. I would love to see more places like this pop up. Salud!

I had the pleasure of dining at this charming restaurant for brunch with a party of six during restaurant week. The ambiance was cute and cozy, perfect for our Sunday gathering. The standout dish was undoubtedly the biscuits, which were simply amazing. We also couldn't get enough of the mac n cheese – it was cheesy perfection! As for the fried chicken, it was executed flawlessly, boasting an irresistible crispy exterior. Highly recommend for a delightful brunch experience!

From the very moment I stepped into Ichiran, I was enveloped in a culinary sonnet. The broth was nothing short of divine, carrying depth and warmth in each slurp. Noodles were a triumph, springy and delectable, a perfect dance partner to the broth's rich embrace. Service was exemplary, attentive yet unobtrusive, a fine balance rarely achieved.

Though nestled in the bustling heart of Times Square, Ichiran's atmosphere was a surprising haven. The serene music paired with a soft symphony of low-volume chatter created an oasis of calm in the city's chaos.

Granted, dining here may be a touch pricier than other spots, but the experience justifies every cent. I indulged in the recommended set and found myself savoring every last drop. Ichiran is not merely a meal; it's a poetic experience, a love letter to ramen that's worth every penny.

A gem in the city. Perfect for a date night, special occasion, or just a night out in the city. Came here at about 9:30pm, was seated within 10 minutes but it does seem like it can get super packed so please be advised. Not sure if they take prior reservations but I think they do as it's a popular establishment. The food here is great, especially the Mac & cheese!! Add in some chicken or bacon for protein.. the service here is pretty quick. We were stuffed from dinner so we didn't get dessert but the people around looked like they really enjoyed the fondue. Definitely returning! 10/10 would recommend.

Title: Scrumptious Pizza but Service Could Improve

I recently had the pleasure of tasting what could very well be the best pizza I've ever had! We tried the pepperoni square and the margherita at this local spot, and both were absolutely yummy. Fortunately, we arrived at an opportune time and only faced a 20-minute wait, which was surprisingly short considering the quality of the pizza.

However, there were a couple of hitches to our experience. The menu didn’t list prices, leaving us in the dark about the cost until payment. Though it felt worth it, we were caught off guard by a surcharge for credit card payments, a detail that was poorly communicated via a messy note at the counter. A heads-up would have been appreciated so we could have opted to pay in cash.

Additionally, while the pizza left nothing to be desired, the staff's demeanor could have been better. As first-timers with questions, we weren't met with the friendliness we expected.

Despite these issues, the pizza alone makes this place a must-visit if you're in the area. Just remember to bring cash and prepare for a no-frills service experience.

I'm going to start this review and say that the Omakase here is completely worth it. Even though I do have to say it was more rice as far as the servings, but it was still well presented and served. I mean, look at the photos. I'm not kidding and for what? $80 you get all of this?! Omakase is a different experience than what you have if you go to just a sushi restaurant. It's hard to find good omakase in an affordable amount. There are omakase out there for a whole set for $400/person. It can get ridiculous crazy, but if you never had this type of experience I would highly recommend it to those who want to try it out but at the same time not break the bank over one meal.Anyways, the menu was quite extensive. I've broken it down of what I had:Oyster TartareSquid LegsGolden eye snapperMedium fatty tunaMarinated groupie OtoroStripe jackHorse MackarelSpot PrawnUni over ikura over riceScallops with truffle butter soy sauceSeabassA5Otoro with pickled radish hand roll Egg CakeYes. I believe that's all of it. For the price of this place along with the amount food you get for it and the experience, it's definitely worth it. But I feel like you can't get this anywhere else as far as for the price. Omakase is a very intimate relationship that you have with your chef and that is why you shouldn't expect it to go by quickly. The chef makes it right in front of you and there's an automatic feedback to the chef of his creation. So, TLDR; Affordable omakase for starters and you should definitely try it before dropping more money on more expensive omakase if you decide that you want the next level.

Restaurant Daniel in NYC has effortlessly secured a spot in my top three French dining experiences in the city. With its Michelin star rating and abundant accolades, my expectations were high, and I'm thrilled to report they were surpassed.

A pre-Holiday Saturday evening visit saw the place abuzz with energy, yet it retained an air of sophisticated calm. Beginning with a visually stunning white cosmopolitan at the bar, the transition to our dining experience was seamless, with attentive staff ensuring our drinks were refreshed and even offering a tantalizing scent of white truffles, a luxe addition for the night.

We indulged in the four-course prix-fixe menu ($158) known for generous portions, and couldn't resist adding two extra courses because why not? The Golden Ossetra caviar, a revelatory favorite, was an opulent start. My menu selections – from the buttery Escargot to the delicately seared Maine Sea Scallops, and succulent Elysian Fields Roasted Lamb Chop – were each a harmony of flavors and textures. Even when the lamb was slightly over, the chef's swift rectification and the bonus Canard Liberty Farm Duck Duo dish exemplified their commitment to culinary excellence.

Complementing the exquisite food, the Head Sommelier provided stellar wine recommendations, elevating our meal further. The dinner concluded on a high note with the vibrant Orange Sanguine dessert and an artful complimentary "Mont Blanc" - a sweet nod to the Franco-Italian Alps.

In short, Daniel is a quintessential New York French dining destination that truly delivers. With impeccable service, extraordinary food, and an ambiance to match, I eagerly anticipate my return and the opportunity to partake in their renowned events.

This restaurant has been around for 100 years! So when you sit down and you want serious Ukrainian food this is where you go they are open 24 seven! So brunch on Saturdays and Sundays is from 9 AM to 4 PM that's reasonable brunch! We ordered the stuffed cabbage of course get the mushroom gravy you won't be disappointed. You must have pirogi filled with sauerkraut with some fresh horseradish and beet juice with sour cream on the side of course. Don't be deterred by the fact that there is a line waiting on the side of the building services fast the restaurant is big you can sit outside or inside outside of course is always fun because it's people watching and it is the East Village in New York City. Someone who has never been to this area of New York must visit! I worked in Manhattan a lot so 2nd Ave. and E. 9th St. is a very comfortable neighborhood for me. You will find Polish donuts you will find smoked sausages along with CBD shops .I know you'll be full lift you eat plates and plates of pierogies but do take home one of the black-and-white cookies that's in the front showcase. Of course you might need a coffee mug with the name of the restaurant as well as shirt it's all in good fun.

Wow went in here while shopping and was pleasantly surprised!! This food is GOOD. I'm a pad see ew lover and have tried all of the places in Austin where I'm from. This blows them all out of the water! Noodles taste soooo good and the pork is cooked perfectly. Quick + nice no frills service. Wish I lived in New York now lol, I'll definitely come back to try more items on the menu next time.

From the moment the sight of scrumptious pizzas lured us in from the street, our experience at this gem of a restaurant only soared higher. The staff welcomed us with open arms and a sense of humor that immediately put us at ease. The dizzying array of pizza options made choosing a challenge, but we settled on the vodka sauce pizza, the buffalo chicken, and one with marinara sauce — each one a flavor-packed masterpiece. The buffalo chicken stood out with its perfectly crispy yet succulent bite. This spot truly satisfied our cravings and left us eager to return for another slice of pizza paradise.

Title: A Quick Trip to Ramen Bliss at [Restaurant Name]

Review:

My latest venture to [Restaurant Name] left me thoroughly impressed with its modern touch and efficiency. Straight from the onset, the iPad ordering system is a delightful nod to Japan, streamlining the process and slashing the long wait times notorious at places like Ippudo. The atmosphere of the restaurant is all about quick service without compromising on the dining experience, epitomized by their "Order, get seated, eat and go" philosophy.

The star of the show, the soul ramen, came tantalizingly close to perfection. I was tempted to slurp down every drop of the flavorful broth, though the cha shu was a miss due to its toughness – an area ripe for improvement. On the other hand, the perfectly cooked egg, albeit at a steep $3, and the quality noodles rounded out the dish handsomely.

I'm keeping my fingers crossed for [Restaurant Name] to expand to midtown, where its swift service model would cater brilliantly to the bustling lunch crowd. A small suggestion to boost the experience: a self-service water stand would be a welcome addition, especially during peak times when the place is buzzing and service tends to be scant.

In conclusion, for ramen aficionados hunting for a quick and delectable meal, [Restaurant Name] is a must-try. Worth a visit, without a doubt.

Title: Joe's Pizzeria - Not Living Up to the Hype

Sadly, Joe's Pizzeria didn't quite hit the mark for me. As a first-timer intrigued by the buzz around its New York-style pizza, my anticipation was met with disappointment. The touted mozzarella slice left me underwhelmed; the crust was excessively crispy, detracting from the overall experience, while the flavor profile of the cheese was merely passable - not the robust, mouth-watering delight I had envisioned.

My companion's pepperoni option did fare slightly better in terms of taste, but it wasn't enough to salvage the overall lackluster impression. At $4 a pop ($3 for a plain cheese slice), one might expect a slice to sing a little more in terms of taste and texture.

On the practical side, Joe's does have a few positives - the line, although present, is a quick hurdle, and the staff seem to have the assembly line down to an art. Just bear in mind that it's a cash-only establishment and seating is virtually non-existent, making it a grab-and-go situation.

For those seeking the quintessential NY slice experience Joe's frequently promises, temper your expectations, or at least opt for the pepperoni over the plain mozzarella.

Are the people who rave about ROKC the same ones who live uptown and therefore don't have access to the plethora of much more awesome ramen downtown? Because I took an especial trip to come here and I don't get what the fuss is about. I had the Okinawa ramen, and the broth was bland, the lone piece of chicken flabby and meager and the toppings sparse (half an egg, a piece of chicken, and scallions chopped so coarsely that every bite was a big peppery hit). Worst of all, the noodles were so disappointing - I understand that very few ramen restaurants make their own noodles, but what I got was thick, and not in a chewy/springy way, but in a soggy and overcooked way.The cocktails are slightly better. I went out on a limb and tried the Hijiki, which has seaweed in it. It was served in a soup bowl, which was unique. but honestly I just couldn't have very much of it since it was so strongly seaweedy and savory. It's like a novelty drink that's such a novel and intellectual concept but I had no interest in taking more than a few sips. The grapefruit drink was a little better, or perhaps simply more mainstream, and I enjoyed the accompanying smoking incense stick for atmosphere.The oysters were in my opinion, fresh but nondescript, but for $1.50 during happy hour, sure.This place runs a tight ship. I arrived a little before 7 pm on a Thursday evening, and we very luckily obtained the last pair of seats. Anyway. Don't waste your time commuting here for the ramen (it's not that great) or the atmosphere (it's way too busy and they're just shoveling people in and out). BUT if you're in the neighborhood, sure, why not drop by because there's no other Japanese/cocktail/oyster place in the vicinity?

Title: A Mexican Gem in the Theater District

Review:

I've always been partial to this gem of a Mexican restaurant nestled in the theater district, and my recent visit reaffirmed my love for it. The experience kicked off with a tantalizing fruit guacamole, perfectly paired with warm tortilla chips and a rich, smoky tomato dip that set the bar high.

For the main course, we indulged in two delectable taco options: the shrimp tacos burst with freshness while the el lechón tacos offered a succulent, savory bite. A classic side of rice and beans complemented the tacos perfectly. The El Tropical Margaritas added a sweet, refreshing twist to the meal, striking just the right note of indulgence.

Dessert was an adventure on its own, with the crepes coming highly recommended by our waitress – and rightly so. They were a delightful finish to our feast. Accompanying our dessert with a cappuccino and a coffee was the cherry on top.

Throughout the meal, what stood out was not just the delicious food but the attentive service. Despite the growing crowd, our waitress was exceptionally observant, ensuring our experience remained top-notch from start to finish. This restaurant continues to be a favorite for good reason – fantastic food paired with impeccable service.

Tucked away along East Broadway, this gem of a dim sum restaurant is the kind of place you could easily miss if you weren't looking for it. Yet, to the delight of discerning foodies, this spot maintains a low profile without the frantic wait times typical of popular establishments. On a bustling Saturday, we were ushered to our table with no delay.

The experience was authentically traditional, with carts laden with steaming baskets of dim sum weaving through the tables. You simply choose the dishes that catch your eye as they pass. The variety is impressive and the flavors are spot-on, capturing the essence of Cantonese culinary artistry.

A word of advice: bring along someone who speaks Cantonese to navigate the menu like a local. This place is a must-visit for anyone craving an authentic dim sum experience without the usual crowds.

Title: A Tasty, Yet Pricey Bowl of Ramen

I recently dined at a local spot touted for its top-notch ramen, which indeed lived up to its reputation flavor-wise. However, the price point is a tad steep at $24 for a bowl with the usual extras like char siu pork, seaweed, an egg, among other ingredients – add-ons that typically come standard at a lower cost elsewhere in NYC.

Nonetheless, the customization options at this restaurant are impressive. Diners can personalize their dish down to the noodle firmness, broth richness, and spice level, which is a rare find. Additionally, the cost includes an extra serving of noodles and a no-tip policy, somewhat lessening the sticker shock.

While the noodles and rich broth were delightful and the premium pork worth the splurge, the egg was a letdown. Instead of the expected soft marinated ramen egg, I was served a medium-boiled egg that I had to peel myself, not adding any value to the meal or justifying the cost.

The atmosphere does offer a unique experience with its 'quiet' booth setting, which provides a respite from the typical NYC hustle and noise – a boon for those seeking a more tranquil dining experience, even if we don't always adhere to the silence rule.

In conclusion, if you don't mind the higher price and can bypass the ordinary egg, this restaurant definitely serves up a delicious and customizable ramen experience.

Really enjoyed ourselves here. It's tapas style, Mexican themed and owned by Bobby Flay, so you know the menu is going go be super creative. I got the Shelby drink to start which was whisky based and nicely strong.We got the seared yellowtail, eggplant and the eleven layer potato (which I wouldn't recommend). The waiter suggested the rice mushroom paella, which we did like a lot - the crispy rice really added an element of surprise and texture to it.The scrambled eggs were good but the bread that came with them was really the best part. The apple strudel dessert was probably the best I've ever had. We spent about $125 before tip on everything here. Portions are small, but it's a good amount and great if you like tapas style. We definitely did not leave hungry.Only complaints is that it was extremely cold in the restaurant, to the point where we had to keep our jackets on.

We enjoyed outdoor dining at this charming spot, taking advantage of the beautiful weather. The Margherita pizza and little neck clam pie were divine, showcasing a delectable thin crust that I particularly favor. However, the portions did not quite match the steep prices. Despite this, the quality of the pizzas would beckon me back for another slice on a sunny day.

Ordered delivery from here the other night. Ordered the calamari and nanas salad.Delivery arrived on time and everything was correct and packed neatly. It arrived with free bread.The bread was soft with a crunchy crust. I dipped it in the marinara for the calamari. The marinara was good and not too acidic. Excellent.The calamari was delicious and cooked perfect. Crunchy batter fried to perfection. Great flavor and love the fresh herbs. Squid not chewy or rubbery. I'd order this again. Great portion size too! I was full and couldn't eat my salad!Nana's salad was a disappointment with cost vs portion size. It was an expensive small salad. Great flavor with the fennel but not worth it. I wouldn't order this again.

Title: A Savory Slice of Venezuela

As a culinary explorer, my quest for the world's tastiest foods led me to an intriguing discovery on CNN's list— the arepa. This treasure has two famed variations: Colombian and Venezuelan. My recent visit to a local gem offered an authentic taste of the latter.

Unlike its Colombian counterpart, which is sweeter with toppings piled high, the Venezuelan arepa cradles its stuffing within a warm, cornmeal embrace. For those new to this delight, I recommend sampling both types for a full arepa appreciation.

The eatery of the day, while not named in my notes, stands out for its dedication to Venezuelan arepas. In contrast, Arepa Lady is a go-to for Colombian-style. At this Venezuelan spot, it's essential to select an arepa that suits your palate. My choice, the Hot Queen, unfortunately lacked the fiery punch I crave. Conversely, the De Pabellón packed a flavorful punch, reminiscent of my first visit, where the arepas left a more memorable impression.

Additionally, I indulged in yoyos—ripe banana and cheese encased in a cinnamon-infused batter and fried to perfection. A word of caution, though: steer clear of the Cocada drink. Despite its promise of coconut bliss, it fell short of expectations.

Be prepared for a cozy experience. The restaurant's size is quaint, to say the least. Seating comes in the form of small crates and the tables are tiny, mirroring the compact kitchen and restroom. Patience might be required for entry, but for those devoted to arepa exploration, the wait is a small price for the indulgence awaiting inside.

Cute little spot with great lunch specials! It's quite small but they seem to accommodate the lunch crowd really well. I suggest the banh mi (sandwich) or vermicelli bowls.  Being from the west coast, I simply don't trust pho in nyc, and given the other reviews, I'd say if you stay clear from that you're good to go! My friends and I are definitely making this one a regular spot.

Title: A Toast to Flavors and Creativity

My recent dining experience at this establishment was nothing short of delightful, thanks to their great food and service. The Sangria selection is commendable; both the pineapple and red wine options stood out with their refreshing taste. The patatas bravas arrived in a generous portion size, making it easy to fill up quickly on this savory staple.

The tenderness of the octopus was much appreciated, and the mushroom flatbread added a flavorful diversity to our meal. I found myself wishing for a more substantial serving of the lamb skewers, yet this minor qualm was overshadowed by the brilliance of the dessert menu. The standout dish, the churro s'more, is a marvel of culinary creativity. Disguised as a "cookie" due to its shape, it surprises you with its perfect marshmallow center, lightly charred to enhance its flavor.

However, the restaurant's cozy arrangement comes with the trade-off of closely set tables, and a restroom located a tad too far from the dining area. These are the small details that, if improved, could elevate the overall dining experience. Nevertheless, this spot is a must-visit for anyone looking to indulge in creative dishes and delightful flavors.

Rating: 4/5 Stars
Great pizza with amazing crust and fresh ingredients! We were looking for something near the Vessel and affordable for this high priced area of NYC.  This place delivers!

Wine geek, orange wine lover, please come to this place. The wine selection trully massive. Steve was really helpful and I love all the wine that they got here.  Place quite tight so please come as soon as they are open.

I had the pleasure of dining at this gem on the Upper West Side, which serves excellent Szechuan cuisine. The authenticity of the dishes shines through with their masterful seasoning, striking a delectable balance between spice and heat. The service was both friendly and attentive.

A standout dish was the cold beef and tripe, a dish of remarkable tenderness and just the right touch of heat from the Szechuan peppercorns to enliven the palate without overwhelming it. The stir-fried cauliflower with Chinese bacon was another highlight, boasting that elusive wok hay, leaving each bite perfectly cooked with a satisfying crispy crunch. The fish was impeccably prepared as well, flaky and moist.

This spot is a fantastic addition to the neighborhood and a must-visit for anyone craving authentic Szechuan fare.

Located at a prime spot on Broome Street, this spacious and new restaurant offers a pleasant dining experience ideal for a date night or a casual drink with friends. The menu, while clear-cut featuring a selection of pastas, substantial protein-centric dishes, starters, and salads, doesn't venture into the realm of the culinary adventurous, providing satisfactory but unremarkable fare.

A notable highlight is the tuna crostini, priced at $18 for three pieces with an optional $3 Uni supplement, a worthy appetizer to kick off the meal. Of the pasta offerings, the Lumaconi Gigante stands out as the best among the trio sampled, coming in at $24. While the atmosphere is commendably inviting, the food doesn't quite hit the mark as a standout necessity for those seeking a unique gastronomic encounter.

Visited this gem in January 2020 and was pleasantly surprised. The true stars of the menu are the skewers – particularly the innovative pork kidney and lamb combo that sets a new standard for skewered delights. Their treatment of grilled eggplant and enoki mushrooms, thinly sliced for maximum flavor, is another game-changer. Don't miss the baked scallops and oysters, served in charming little foil containers. While the shrimp boil was competent, it pales in comparison to the skewers. Skip the seafood fried rice, though; it's disappointingly bland. To cap it off, the warm pear juice served in a tin teapot is a cozy touch for winter evenings. Overall, a strong recommend for skewer enthusiasts.

After eating the pasta with mushrooms, I decided on the five star rating regardless of anything else.  All I can say is wow!  And I don't even like mushrooms!  This food is solid.  I also had the onion soup, burata  with tomatoes and strawberries, and French fries, all of which were delicious.  French fries were somehow perfect even though I got delivery.  The only dish I would not get again is the sirloin steak with potatoes and broccolini.  Something was a bit off with the texture of the steak, and the sides suffered from delivery.  Maybe the dish is better if you dine in the restaurant.  I will definitely order again - especially the pasta - which I dream about!

Tucked beside the more ostentatious Veselka, this unassuming spot serves up a satisfying Ukrainian feast without breaking the bank. Their pierogies and kielbasa hit the mark – real comfort food that transports me back to the homey basement gatherings of my youth. Service hiccup aside (our large group's order got a little jumbled), the experience is always one of nostalgic warmth and generous hospitality.

Today's lunch at this spot was outstanding. The service was speedy and finding a place to sit was a breeze. I opted for the classic tuna sandwich, which was sublime – seriously, it's crave-worthy to the point of wanting it daily. Despite its generous size, I polished it off with gusto. I'm already planning my next visit. Highly recommended!

Title: A Tim Burton Fan's Haven at Beetle House

Last night's dinner at Beetle House was a memorable immersion into Tim Burton's quirky world. Don't let the size of the venue fool you; its decor envelopes you in a fantastical ambiance that's larger than life. The characters, including a spot-on Beetlejuice whose in-your-face antics added to the authentic vibe, brought the experience to another level. His bar stool performances were nothing short of spectacular. 

The dedication of the performers was evident, as Jack and Sally not only looked the part but engaged us in delightful banter, making the night even more personal. For those hoping to meet specific characters like Sweeney Todd or Edward Scissorhands, a tip: call ahead, as the roster changes nightly.

Service was swift and unobtrusive despite the lively goings-on, and the bartenders impressed with perfectly balanced concoctions. My Bio-Exorcism was just right, though a word of caution: dry ice can be a tongue-tripper; handle with care.

As for the cuisine, the Mac & Cheese was unexpectedly delightful, and the Sweeney Beef was a savory culinary triumph. This place is a must-visit for Tim Burton fans who'll revel in the vibe. However, it's not for everyone, especially children, as the adult themes are as vivid as the characters that roam the restaurant.

Instagram worthy food at the price you'd expect to pay for such aesthetic looking drinks. Don't be surprised if every single customer here pulls out a phone and takes hundreds of pictures of their food, drinks, and themselves with the food and drinks.Honestly though, their drinks were pretty tasty.

I absolutely adore Abiko in K-Town – it's a gem for curry lovers. The wait time is minimal, both to be seated and for your food to arrive, which is a big plus. The menu is user-friendly, guiding you through the ordering process with ease. The variety of choices is impressive, allowing for full customization of dishes to suit any palate. Be cautious with the spice levels – their curry packs a punch! I can handle quite a bit of heat, and Level 1 is plenty spicy for me. All in all, Abiko is my go-to spot for a curry fix. Highly recommended!

Title: A Dumpling Duel: King vs. Vanessa's

I recently tried King as a potential contender to my go-to dumpling spot, Vanessa's. Price and quality-wise, they're neck and neck. Although King offers a slight edge with $1.50 for four dumplings, compared to Vanessa's, this small saving didn't tip the scales for me. The dumpling dough at King was a tad too thick for my taste, but they didn't skimp on the delicious filling.

I was tempted to add pork buns to my order, priced reasonably at $2, but a 20-30 minute wait time was a deal-breaker. Here's where Vanessa's bustling kitchen, driven by its notoriety, ensures a continuous flow of fresh offerings, albeit sometimes with a queue.

In conclusion, those nearby to both establishments might find choosing between King and Vanessa's a matter of flip-of-the-coin. Personally, the slight proximity of Vanessa's might sway me on a lazy day, but King is absolutely a strong contender. I'm already planning a second visit for the scallion pancake with duck – fingers crossed it tips the scales!

Tucked away atop the flagship RH store in Chelsea, the restaurant offers a beautiful rooftop dining experience. Despite the Saturday afternoon bustle, we were promptly seated within 5 minutes, sans reservation. The menu boasts fresh, healthy options; my boyfriend's arugula salad, a crunchy meld of fennel, grapes, and sunflower seeds, tossed in a zesty citrus vinaigrette, was a delightful choice. I opted for the citrus green juice, and while it took some time to arrive, the quality justified the wait. Similarly, the arrival of my daughter's chai latte was delayed, but she found it worth the wait. Throughout our visit, the service remained cordial, and the ambiance, both indoors and out, was undeniably stunning.

Title: A Nostalgic Favorite Loses Its Consistency

I've been a regular at this eatery for many years, appreciating its once unwavering quality. Recently, after a brief hiatus, I returned three times, only to be met with an experience that could best be described as mediocre.

The burger, a staple that kept me coming back, still holds a solid place on the menu, though its preparation has become unpredictable—the patties often arrive more well-done than preferred. The fries are average, yet the availability of yellow mustard is a small touch that I continue to admire.

Service has taken a confusing turn with the new system of taking orders at select tables, leaving behind the straightforward counter service that epitomized efficiency.

While the restaurant remains decent, its consistency has faded, and its once-hidden charm is now a matter of public knowledge. For those willing to endure the long lines and aren't particular about the doneness of their burger, it remains a trendy spot for a casual meal and a snapshot.

In summary, the place still has remnants of its former glory, but don't expect the reliability or the insider's gem it once was.
