Went there for a birthday dinner. Overall experience was good. Decor was very elegant. Atmosphere was very quiet in the beginning and then turned louder when more ppl coming in. Food was good, especially their signature beef courses, except for the beef sushi I am not a huge fan. Dessert the green tea tiramisu was yummy. Only downside for the whole experience was service being very slow, because they obviously were short in staff. The whole dining room with around 10 tables there were only 2 servers and 1 bartender. The waiter that was serving us also responsible for at least 4 more tables with greeting ppl, serving food, getting the pot for sukiyaki ready, explaining food, preparing checks, etc. He was very committed but super busy - he almost ran back and forth. He did a great job though the management should consider adding more staff. Our whole dinner took almost 2.5 hours vs the expected 1.5 hours.

Title: A Taste of Motor City - Detroit Style Pizza Delights!

I recently had the pleasure of trying out a spot that specializes in Detroit style pizza, and it did not disappoint. For those new to the concept, imagine a pizza that marries the shape of a Sicilian slice with an Instagram-worthy aesthetic. Served up in rectangular pieces, I opted for the pepperoni, which was adorned with perfectly curled and charred roni cups that are nothing short of drool-inducing.

While the crust could have benefited from a bit more crispiness to truly honor the Detroit tradition of a thick and crunchy base, the overall experience was satisfying. The sauce stole the show, teeming with a rich umami essence that had me savoring every bite, though I did note some inconsistency in distribution across the slices. The pepperoni itself was on point—striking a fine balance between flavor and fat content.

Service was swift, and the price point makes it an accessible option for a hearty lunch that could easily serve one or be portioned out for a later treat. If you're in the mood to deviate from the classic New York slice and embark on a pizza adventure, this establishment is a commendable choice.

Title: A Seafood Delight at Mermaid Inn

I recently dined at Mermaid Inn with my fiancé, and I have to say, it's a spectacular spot for anyone craving East Coast seafood vibes. We had the good fortune of using a 50% off coupon from our Time Out Table for Two box, so we indulged in the finer dishes on the menu.

Our server was the epitome of friendly and attentive, and on her suggestion, we began with an assortment of East and West Coast oysters. Each was a fresh, delightful taste of the sea, and although we passed on the Happy Hour specials, the $1.25 oysters sounded like a steal.

The mermaid fish tacos were a revelation – hands down, the best I've tasted outside California. The "nearly famous" lobster roll lived up to its reputation, overflowing with succulent lobster paired with crispy fries. As for the smoked gouda mac & cheese with lobster, which was a mere $5 add-on, it was rich and comforting, leaving us with leftovers to savor later.

Capping the meal with complimentary chocolate pudding and a whimsical fish fortune telling game was the perfect quirky touch. If you're after a lively spot with excellent seafood, Mermaid Inn should be on your go-to list.

If you love seafood, then you gota check this spot out! .All combos come with potatoes & 1 corn.Pick a sauce: - dry (no sauce), garlic butter sauce, o' bay sauce, ragin lemon pepper sauce, the boil special sauce (all sauces).Pick a level:- mild, medium, spicy, fire.I got the 1 lb shrimp & lobster Combo in the boil sauce with medium spice & it was absolutely delicious!! The lobster was hard to get thru but it was worth it when you dip it in the sauce! It takes time to go thru the whole bag so definitely best to go when you have time while hungry & ready to feast!

been trying to visit this place for the past few months and i finally made it! When i say I have coveting the pull apart bread I MEAN IT!Tried three of their most popular cocktails including the razzle & penicillin.Yum, a little pricey but well worth it since most craft cocktails usually are a little expensive. Get literally any of the  pull apart bread is amazing. but the honey butter is my personal fav!Also get the porterhouse for two, i ate it so fast i regret not taking a picture TWO THUMBS UP

I recently dined at Hummus Be Joking and was left vastly underwhelmed. The restaurant operates with a confusing pricing strategy that leaves a lot to be desired. Unlike Mamoun's, where generous portions are the norm, here you're nickel-and-dimed for every addition to an already pricey sandwich—it's not hard to rack up a $20 tab for a single item.

The quality of the food compounds the disappointment. The gyro meat was notably dry and seemed stale, and the chicken didn't appear much more appetizing—though I didn't venture to try it. It's a far cry from the fresh and flavorful offerings one would expect from Middle Eastern cuisine.

In essence, the restaurant presents a Chipotle-esque model for Middle Eastern food, but with a steeper price and without the anticipated authenticity or quality. Personally, I find both establishments unappealing, but at least at Chipotle, you don't leave feeling overcharged.

In short, Hummus Be Joking was a letdown with its steep pricing, lackluster food quality, and overall experience. It won't be on my list for a return visit.

Title: A Memorable Anniversary Meal Before Broadway

My spouse and I celebrated our 33rd wedding anniversary at this high-end tapas gem before catching a Broadway show. The ambiance was perfect from the moment we walked in. We indulged in the brunch special which included an array of tapas, a couple of entrees, and a dessert to share.

The standout dish was their signature patatas bravas – a delectable mix of crispy potatoes and savory spices. The creamy croquettes evoked pure joy, melting in our mouths. Though the lamb meatballs fell a bit short of our expectations and the tomato toast points didn't quite make the mark, the meal was largely impressive.

The egg entrees were a delight, particularly the Benedict with its flavorful roasted pepper touch. It all culminated in a dessert of hot churros dipped in a rich Mexican chocolate that was nothing short of extraordinary.

In summary, the restaurant provided a mostly exquisite dining experience that set the stage for a wonderful evening.
Not sure why a lot of ppl had bad experiences. I've been here three times so far. Always had good service and the ramen was always tasty. Good spot to just grab food while you're around the area!

Title: Two Visits to Friedman's - A Tale of Consistent Culinary Delight

I've had the pleasure of dining at Friedman's on two separate occasions, and I'm already looking forward to my third. A bustling spot at brunch, I learned quickly on my first visit that the Yelp waitlist is the secret to securing a seat at the coveted bar area. Despite the 45-minute wait, the experience was worth every minute. My server, Will, was not only personable but also insightful, guiding me to a refreshing red sangria and introducing me to their heavenly blueberry butter. His service, coupled with a hearty egg white omelette and chicken sausage, left me thoroughly impressed and, frankly, a bit tipsy.

On my second visit, the Yelp waitlist worked wonders, and I was perched at the bar in no time. Ashlee, my server for the day, was a gem—attentive and knowledgeable, she helped me navigate the menu, and I settled on a satisfying plate of steak & eggs, with yet another glass of their irresistible red sangria. The hospitality didn't end there; a surprise "mistake mimosa" from the bartender was the cherry on top of an already fantastic experience.

Kudos to Friedman's for exceptional staff and standout service; it's rare to find a place that consistently offers not just a meal, but an experience that fills you up in more ways than one.

Solid burger. 4 stars.We had a group of 8 for lunch. Ordered a round of drinks and shared the nachos. The nachos platter was huge and was enough for all of us to partake while we were waiting for a couple people to arrive. Bonus, the nachos come with cheese sauce (yes, the fake stuff) rather than melted real cheese, which is how I like it (don't judge). I ordered their signature 5 napkin burger, which came with melted gruyere, carmelized onions and rosemary aioli. Delicious. Cooked medium and very juicy. More than I could finish, so I ended up taking part of it home with me. Would definitely come back to try other burgers.Bonus - This place has gluten-free options for the celiacs in your group.

I recently visited a charming, unstuffy French bistro that truly hit the mark. The highlight was their lamb burger, which was nothing short of delightful. As I savored each bite, I indulged in some people watching, thanks to the bistro's bustling atmosphere. Despite the cozy space, which was a bit tight on elbow room, the experience was comfortable. The service struck a perfect balance - friendly and attentive without being overwhelming. It's the kind of place that would become a regular haunt if I were a local. Highly recommended for a casual, delicious meal with a side of lively ambiance.

This restaurant is a hit that promises not to disappoint! The customer service shines, and the diverse menu, offering everything from sandwiches to salads, caters to all tastes. I've enjoyed several slices of their standard pizza, but the highlight was indulging in a chicken parmigiana hero. Delectably satisfying, it's a choice I pat myself on the back for making. While most patrons might save half for later, I couldn't resist finishing the whole thing in one sitting. Eagerly anticipating my next visit, the penne pasta is already calling my name. Highly recommended!
Mmm... nice bulgogi. Very tasty. I liked everything except for the Mandoo Ramen. It was literally instant ramen for $10. Avoid the ramen. Get anything else here and you'll be satisfied.

On the residential block of West 74th street, a new restaurant has found a home.  Leyla is one of the newest Mediterranean restaurants located on the Upper West Side.  During the day, the space has a bright and airy feel because of the exposed white brick and sunlight that peeks through tall windows.  In the evening, this restaurant transforms the ambiance with the perfect dim lighting and tealights on each table.Leyla offers Mediterranean food with a Turkish influence.  The menu is sectioned into Pide (flatbread), Salad/Mezze (which is similar to appetizers), Hot Starters, and Main Dishes.  Their Pides are made in the oven brick oven, which can be seen from the front of the house.  I ordered the 3 Cheese Pide, and this was the first time I had truffled honey, which was so appetizing.  Between the cheese, truffled honey, and freshly baked bread, I saw Jesus in the first bite.     The majority of their menu is designed to be shared, which is excellent because it will allow the sharing of multiple items.The service at Leyla was stellar.  I noticed how attentive and knowledgeable each server was with other tables.   This is a restaurant I plan on visiting in the future, and I highly recommend it.  The environment for Leyla is perfect for a quiet dinner to catch up with a friend, solo dolo dining, or even excellent date spot.

During a bustling lunch hour, we decided to try the set menu at this gem of a restaurant - a decision that did not disappoint. For an exceptional value, the meal included four sides, rice, soup, and a main course. We opted for the spicy pork belly with kimchi soup and beef belly with soft tofu soup. The standout was undoubtedly the spicy pork belly which delivered a fiery punch that was both satisfying and addictive. The soft tofu soup, brimming with seafood, was a revelation with its impeccable flavor profile.

While the kimchi soup veered towards being overly salty and could not quite reach the heights of the tofu soup, it was still enjoyable. The beef belly, tender and flavorful, also lived up to the high standards of our meal.

The service was the cherry on top - prompt, attentive, and courteous, ensuring our dining experience was smooth from start to finish. This place has certainly earned my recommendation for anyone seeking a worthwhile dining experience.

My friend and I were in the area and wanted some pasta from Little Italy before we had to go back by a certain time and this place delivered on taste, speed and service. We were going to get food to go but honestly, pasta just doesn't taste the same if you were to reheat it so we decided to eat in and they were able to accommodate our time crunch. I ordered the tagliatelle pasta with a carbonara base and the beet salad. The beet salad comes with an overwhelming amount of ricotta cheese (almost too much) but the beets were good. I loved the pasta as it had a great al dente bite to it and the sauce was good. My friend got the squid ink pasta with clams and while i'm not the biggest fan of squid ink (too iron-y for me) she practically finished her entire dish so she liked it.

Title: Patience Pays Off at Kenka!

If you're venturing to Kenka for a Saturday night feast, brace yourself for a wait—but trust me, it's worth it. The pre-opening line hinted at the popularity of this spot, and the anticipation builds as you're queued up, name on the list, stomach grumbling. It's wise to nibble on something beforehand unless you're prepared for a test of patience.

Once ushered into the dimly lit interior, you're greeted by an eclectic mix of funky Japanese decor that sets a vibrant stage. The menu is a visual treat in itself, resembling a colorful comic book that's as extensive as it is enticing. For first-timers, it's a boon to have a Japan-savvy friend navigate the offerings. Authentic and varied, the dishes we tried were exceptional—a testament to Kenka's dedication to replicating a true Japanese dining experience.

Perfect for an evening of fun with a side of gastronomic adventure, Kenka is a must-try. Just remember to arrive with your hunger at bay to fully enjoy the culinary journey! Highly recommended.

Amazing pizza at such an affordable price! I literally got Two slices of pizza and a drink for just a couple bucks. This place is open late night and is really central so you can pop in whenever for a slice.Friendly staff and fast service. There's room to eat standing or take a slice to go. The crust is very crispy and they add a lot of toppings. The slices are pretty big too, you really get your moneys worth at this place! The quality of the pizza is really good too, I would say it's better than Little Caesars or dominoes. They have a lot of hot sauce, red chili flakes, and garlic you can add to your pizza which is so cool! I've never seen garlic toppings for pizza where I'm from. My favorite toppings are sausage and pepperoni, and I came here on two separate nights while I was in town.

We decided to try our luck on a busy Friday night at this rooftop spot without a reservation and were pleasantly surprised to get seated promptly. The terrace offers a comfortable space that's cleverly divided between indoor and outdoor seating. Our gaze was immediately captured by the impressive view of the World Trade Center—certainly a highlight of the evening.

One can't help but appreciate the slightly cooler air up here, a welcome reprieve from the city's summer heat. Sipping on a $20 frose by the pool was a delightful experience. Although it lacked a discernible alcohol kick, the frozen blend's texture was spot-on.

Title: A Little Italy Gem for Soup Dumpling Aficionados

If you find yourself in Little Italy with a hankering for some authentic soup dumplings, Tiny Shanghai should be at the top of your list. This humble establishment has earned its stripes as a reliable and affordable go-to alongside rivals like Noodle Village and 3 Times, particularly for its soup dumplings (XLBs) and beef scallion pancakes.

My visits to Tiny Shanghai have been nothing short of satisfying, quickly quelling any craving for those succulent pockets of broth and meat. Though the space is small, it exudes coziness and has never been overcrowded, offering immediate seating even during busy weekends—an appreciated convenience.

The menu has standout offerings, such as the classic pork dumplings at only $6.25, and the luxurious black truffle & pork dumplings, which are a steal at $13.95. While I've yet to dive into their truffle fried rice and spicy beef noodle soup, their Shanghai Lo Mein with Mixed Meat & Shrimp was passable, though not noteworthy.

However, the dish that truly deserves a shout-out is the Sliced Beef Wrap in Scallion Pancakes. Priced at $7.25, it's a flavorful concoction with fresh scallion and cucumber, well worth the inevitable scallion-laden breath.

In summary, Tiny Shanghai is a serious contender for the best XLBs in the area, with prices that are easy on the wallet and flavors that please the palate. It's worth popping in, whether you're a local or just traversing through Little Italy.

I had a plan to get some Xiao Long Bao for lunch at the Bao in the East Village.  Of course when I got there, they told me that they don't serve XLB for lunch, so I was forced to find an alternative - Uluh.  This place is nicer inside, has better service (initially), and serves XLB for lunch.  Perfect!We had a nice lunch at Uluh. The XLB (Shanghai Pork Soup Dumplings)  had good flavor, we're consistently juicy and the dough was nice and soft.  Also tasty was the Kung Pao Chicken.  The Dragon Well green tea was a bit more expensive than what I'm used to paying for tea ($7.00) but the presentation was nice so I wasn't too bothered.  Overall, I thought that Uluh is a very good spot to stop for lunch.  The food, service and decor are all inviting (cleanest/nicest restaurant restrooms in the city, hands down).  There's so much more on the menu which we didn't try, but the experience on record was very good.  I'm a fan of Uluh.

Last Friday night turned out to be a delightful culinary adventure at a local restaurant, wherein my friends and I, a party of four, walked in without a reservation yet were promptly seated—a testament to the establishment's welcoming vibe. The interior boasted ample space, pristinely maintained, with decor that caught the eye and walls adorned with engaging artwork, adding character to our dining experience. The comfortable, spacious seating was a plus.

We indulged in the $99 special, adequately portioned for 2-3 people, starting with a delectable combination of fried chicken and calamari. The chicken was particularly memorable, earning the accolade of "sooooo good!" Next, we dove into a seafood feast, opting for shrimp and crawfish bathed in a slightly spicy sauce, a choice that did not disappoint. Accompanying our main course were the classic sides of corn, potato, and sausage, each element contributing to the overall satisfaction of the meal.

Service was the cherry on top, with our server exemplifying kindness and attentiveness throughout the evening. While everything was top-notch, I’m already craving a return visit for the fried Dungeness crab. This restaurant certainly secured a spot on my go-back-to list.

Cute, uncrowded restaurant that can accommodate large parties. Our server was super friendly and attentive. They have a great happy hour that ends at 7. The menu changes seasonally. I had the brisket which was good but a bit salty. I would like to see a bit more variety on the menu- especially wanted to try the squid ink pasta I saw in a photo. However, I would definitely come back for the hh or to try new offerings on the menu.

This place was great. Me and my friends came here to celebrate a birthday. The drinks were awesome. I do wish they had shrimp on the menu. I had the salmon was super tasteful. Maybe consider adding more options to the menu I felt like I wasn't given much choices. However all the food we ordered was great so I can't complain about that. The place has a romantic elegant feel to it. All staff were friendly. Super attentive to us.

I had a delightful experience at TabeTomo on a bustling Saturday night. Leveraging the Yelp waitlist was a stroke of genius as it ensured I bypassed the crowd and had my table ready upon arrival. The place was packed, but thankfully, the 30-minute digital queue meant I avoided the wait.

I indulged in the Tonkosu Charsu Jiro ramen, a soothing concoction for a chilly NYC evening. The dish featured a soft-boiled egg, five generous slices of charsu, seasoned bamboo shoots, all swimming in a rich pork broth that had been perfected over 60 hours. Not only was the ramen scrumptious, but the portions were also hearty and offered great value for the price. TabeTomo is definitely a smart pick for ramen lovers seeking warmth and satiation.

Title: A Culinary Afternoon at The Arlo

I recently visited The Arlo, not as a guest in their rooms, but purely for a taste of their culinary offerings—and oh, what a taste it was. Immediately upon entering, I was greeted by an interior straight out of an Instagrammer's dream, all trendy decor and perfect lighting.

I had come with a friend, armed with the expectation of needing a second meal elsewhere after a few drinks. However, the Arlo's fare swiftly changed our plans. From 2 pm until the evening fell at 7 pm, we remained, happily ensconced in our seats. The star of the show was undoubtedly the Impossible Burger—so delectable that we couldn't resist ordering thrice.

While the vegan pizza didn't quite hit the mark, the skillful bartenders dazzled us enough to compensate—so much so that our tab boasted around eight drinks each by the time we bid the establishment adieu.

Although my visit didn't grant me the pleasure of the rooftop in its prime during warmer weather, it was easy to see the potential for a delightful outdoor experience.

With food and service that invite you to linger longer than intended, The Arlo is undoubtedly on my list for a repeat visit.

I got the bacon egg and cheese on a roll. I personally thought it wasn't the best quality bread, tasted a bit stale, and it tasted like any other breakfast sandwich around this area. I would only come back out of the convenience factor in that it's right on 9th Ave in a very good location on the corner. There's ample seating area, but I've only gotten food on the go here. My second or third time to come here. Tip: If you ever order after 11 am on a weekend, they add $1 to your item! Something to be aware of that isn't made very obvious until you pay at checkout.

This place is still amazing. Choose this location for a date Sunday night and we ordered pasta. I ordered the Shrimp Linguine, and I honestly forgot what he ordered (apologies) but we both cleared our plates; so you know that's a good sign. The last and first time I was here, I ordered a pizza with my sister and we loved it. Everything here at this restaurant is good, staff are very nice and accommodating to customers as well. Honestly no complaints, If you're strolling by in this area and would like a quick bite stop in here, they do have space for groups; however, I would definitely look into getting a reservation if they do that.

Title: A Bustling Midtown Watering Hole - The Liberty

After countless days of passing by The Liberty on my way to work, curiosity finally won over, and I ventured in for a post-company holiday party session. The bar's spacious interior was a pleasant surprise, stretching back further than one might expect from the outside and featuring an oval-shaped bar that serves as the centerpiece of the establishment.

As anticipated, the venue was brimming with white-collared workers unwinding after office hours, making the most of The Liberty's attractive happy hour offerings. Tables lined the sides, catering to patrons with a hunger for more than just liquid refreshment.

However, the popularity of the place was a double-edged sword; as my coworkers and I found ourselves packed in, vying for the attention of the bartenders. Service though, was attentive, with servers navigating the crowds to take orders.

The prices were fair for a midtown haunt, but the high energy of the place—complete with booming music and the hum of sports fans cheering on their teams—made conversation a shouting match. Ultimately, a few of us sought out a quieter venue to continue our evening.

In summary, The Liberty is a hit for its happy hour specials and vibrant atmosphere, though perhaps not the spot if you're looking to chat. It's a popular choice among the after-work crowd, and for a good reason, but be prepared to speak up if you want to be heard.

Visited this historic restaurant with high hopes, but was let down by the lackluster fare. The Cobb wrap was a disappointment, prompting me to switch to pancakes that proved to be mediocre. The saving grace was a refreshing tall glass of fresh orange juice, coupled with attentive service. Despite its past charm, I'm unlikely to return of my own volition, though my friends' preferences might sway me for a second round.

I'm writing this as my second time coming to Maison Pickle. The first time I came here, I came for brunch and it was PACKED. I think I waited for at least an hour. The portions were ridiculously huge and the food was really good. I wasn't super impressed by the food for brunch, but it wasn't terrible. I came back for dinner and I was incredibly impressed with my food. I came on a Friday night at around 6pm without a reservation. I didn't have to wait for a seat for 2, but we were placed on a bar-like table overlooking the first floor. The only issue I had with this table was the fact that the bar table is really slim, so for the size of the plates they serve it's actually quite small and uncomfortable to eat at. We requested to have our seats changed for a table, but they were unable to do so since they were apparently booked. Bummer. I would suggest everyone to make a reservation when coming here and under the special request you should request a table (and not bar seating). Anyways for the food:My sister and I ordered the lamb sausage dish and the chicken and eggplant Parmesan. The lamb sausage dish was really good. The lamb was seasoned really well. My only complaint was that there were too many golden raisins that made the dish taste a little too sweet and it didn't taste that great with the seasoning already on the lamb. The chicken and eggplant Parmesan was delicious. I honestly have no complaints on that dish because it was so good. My sister and I finished every last bit of it. To finish off we got the 24 layer chocolate cake. If you're a sweet tooth it's a must. The only issue with this is that the plate sizes are so huge that if you were planning to get this dessert maybe you and someone else should split an app and a dinner dish so that way you'll have room for it. Anyways we ordered it and man it was so decadent. LIKE AMAZING! It felt like you were eating a cloud of chocolate. The greatest thing about it was that it wasn't that sweet, which I was pleasantly surprised by. Since my sister and I couldn't finish it, we took it home and it was still good a day later! The service this time was amazing. We had a great female waiter (unfortunately I don't remember her name) but she was very prompt, even thought she had to service a table of 11 10-year olds who were dining as a birthday party behind us. Just wanted to acknowledge her great service!

Airy, crunchy, delicious pizza goodness. This was my first time having Biga style dough pizza and the difference is incredible. So simple ingredients done well created some of the best pizza you're ever gonna taste in the lower east side. Cute interior and the owner Giovann is a great host. Bring a date or come here with friends!

During a casual stroll through SOHO, I discovered a quintessential pizza parlor bustling with variety. The pizza hit the mark of satisfaction, though it fell just shy of remarkable. Nonetheless, the ambiance compensated, offering a genuine neighborhood vibe, underscored by an inviting stream of locals, a lively soundtrack, and a notably amiable team behind the counter. A solid choice for anyone in the area craving a slice.

Title: Pleasant Surprise at Bareburger on 14th Street

I recently visited Bareburger on 14th Street, curious to compare their offerings to other locations. While some Bareburgers vary in menu options, this visit was about the Impossible Burger since the Beyond Burger wasn’t available.

Service was commendable from the get-go; the bar attendant was friendly, and my order arrived promptly. The burger, however, came without the usual trimmings—lettuce, tomatoes, onions—which made me second-guess my order. Yet, I was unfazed as the burger itself—nestled between a vegan bun with vegan cheese and organic ketchup—was the star.

Juiciness was the standout quality of the Impossible Burger. It reminded me of a classic flame-broiled Burger King patty, well-seasoned and satisfying. For a moment of fun with unsuspecting friends, this would be my go-to choice to introduce them to plant-based patties, masking as the real beef deal.

Comparatively, the Beyond Burger has its merits, notably a more authentic meat taste, but risks a veggie aftertaste if overcooked. The Impossible Burger wins for me, especially when seasoned just right – simple salt and pepper when dining out.

In conclusion, if faced with a choice, I'd lean towards the Beyond Burger for personal preference, but wouldn't hesitate to enjoy or recommend the Impossible Burger for a juicy, flavorful experience at Bareburger.

Wanted to try Azuma for a very long time, but never had the chance to go. Azuma was good but did not really live up to it's hype. Azuma follows the standard of allowing up to 3 portions of noodles like most soba places, which was a great surprise (since it's the city). I had gotten the cold soba katsu curry set. The soba noodles were firm and not too soggy for me. The wasabi was a little light though I had felt, the sauce was pretty fine though. While the dipping sauce is meant to be light and clean, I still felt the sauce was a little too kight. The katsu is katsu, it's pretty hard to mess katsu. The curry itself was good, but nothing special.The place wasn't hard to get seated and the restaurant is very calm and relaxing. Waiters are nice but did take a bit of time for my order/check; probably because they were understaffed.

I approached this restaurant with an open mind despite some negative reviews, but I must agree with the skeptics. Lunch proved to be a disappointingly average affair; the decor's charm was not matched by food or service quality.

During my visit, I tried the Drunken Noodles with shrimp, a dish that traditionally packs a spicy punch. Unfortunately, mine lacked both spice and flavor. The shrimp were overcooked, noodles clumped together, and the typical vibrant ingredients like garlic, basil, and pepper pods were nowhere to be found. The absence of an authentic Thai kick meant I didn't even need the Thai iced tea I typically rely on to temper the heat.

Customer service was just as lackluster - impersonal, inattentive, and with a distinct lack of warmth. I was left waiting for the basics: a greeting, water, even chopsticks - essentials I'd expect as a given, especially in an Asian establishment during a hot and sticky post-Labor Day afternoon.

In summary, this restaurant failed to respect the nuances of Thai cuisine and culture. The handwritten bill, indecipherable as it was, and the business cards, promptly discarded, were my final impressions of a place I left feeling both disheartened and resolved not to return. A firm "Goodbye" from me.

This place in my opinion is a fantastic place if you are looking to go to a traditional Szechuan restaurant. If you don't intend being able to feel your tongue due to the mala tang spiciness, check this place out! I was in the mood for some ma po tofu and Mountain House does a phenomenal job with this dish. Instead of just being inundated with chili oil to make it spicy, it also uses the fermented bean paste as a good base for the dish, in the traditional fashion. The thinly sliced pork as an appetizer is also very good and I would definitely get it upon return. I also got a pale-ish pork soup that was spicy and sour. I can't remember the name of the dish for the love of me but it was also quite good. Haven't had anything quite like it since and it explores different parts of the palette that is rarely tickled in western cuisine. Definitely worth the time and wait.

Title: A Cozy Brunch at B&Co – Familiar Comfort with a Side of Attitude

As I settled in at B&Co for an early weekday brunch, the initial quiet ambiance gave way to a more inviting atmosphere as the morning progressed. The charm of the quaint patio drew us to a table outside, though the interior beckoned with even cuter decor.

The menu at B&Co doesn't stray far from the beaten path of American brunch classics, but where it lacks in novelty, it more than compensates with execution. The tuna crudo appetizer was a hit, featuring chewy, well-garnished tuna that set a high bar. My main course, the salmon eggs Benedict, was a showcase of balance and culinary competence – perfectly poached eggs atop smoked salmon, coupled with a side of fresh greens and a savory potato accompaniment. Each element was cooked and seasoned to satisfaction, resulting in a fulfilling meal that hit the spot.

Service, though, was a mixed bag. Our waiter's lack of enthusiasm and absent smiles were noticeable, yet his service remained swift and efficient. The absence of dairy-alternative milks like almond or soy was a letdown, as was the policy on coffee refills – a misstep for any brunch spot.

In conclusion, B&Co offers a solid, dependable brunch experience that won't disappoint, though it might not dazzle with innovation or service warmth. It's a safe choice for anyone craving a well-crafted, traditional brunch.

Title: A Fresh Culinary Chapter at Portale

After 34 years of culinary leadership at Gotham Bar and Grill, Alfred Portale has embarked on an exciting new venture with his eponymous Chelsea hotspot, Portale. This chic new eatery dazzles with a beautifully curated menu that captures the essence of innovation, off to a splendid start.

Despite its novelty and bustling crowds each evening, the service at Portale doesn’t miss a beat - attentive and well-coordinated. Beverage-wise, the cocktail offerings are exceptional, boasting creativity and flair, and the wine selection complements the experience with a thoughtful range of choices.

Portale is already shaping up to be a tantalizing addition to Chelsea's dining scene, ensuring that diners will be coming back for more.

Let's be honest- you come to Wah Fung not for healthy, wholesome dishes. Instead, you're craving greasy, freshly roasted meat-filled platters. The line streams out the door and there's usually at least a 10 minute wait time to get to the counter. But you still eagerly stand there and look at the window lined with hanging meats because the food is so worthwhile. It's cash only and takeout only. You can get a combination of roasted pork, duck, chicken with rice and cabbage for a filling meal. Sometimes, I buy half a roast duck and put it in my lunchbox for the next 2-3 days (it's only $11!)One of the most famous Chinese butcher establishments you can find, and also one of the best cheap eats in the city.

tl;dr Great breakfast place! Highlights were the soy milk, lu rou fan (which is usually not available for breakfast but was a special this day), and the radish cakes. I went in a group of 5 for breakfast and had everything on the menu, with some repeats. It was a more than sufficient amount of food. Service was fast and pleasant, food was solid, I would go again when I'm craving a Taiwanese breakfast in New York!It's a small place with not too many seats so be prepared to wait a little. There's a nice cafe across the street we killed time at.

Very tasty tacos; the line appears to be very long but it moves quickly. You pay for your taco in advance at the register and then customize when you bring your ticket to the person who assembles your taco/quesadilla. I got two adobada tacos without cilantro which were just under $4 a piece. They were a little pricy but worth getting. It's a place to get your food and eat elsewhere; they have foil so you can wrap your plate and eat it to go. I would recommend ordering at least two tacos. The quesadilla is very small so you will need at least two of those if you are getting that instead. However, the quesadillas were open-faced which is a bit different from what I was expecting.

Title: Authentic Flavors with Room for Improvement at Rice Noodle Crepe Spot

Walking into the East Coast location of this Guangzhou-born chain, founded in 1958, we were enlivened by the promise of authentic rice noodle (cherng fun) crepes, an item my family had relished at the original location. With the excitement of this familial endorsement, we went in, ready to indulge.

Seating three people proved a bit of a wait given the restaurant's layout favoring pairs with only a few tables accommodating larger groups. We spent about 15-20 minutes before being seated at 9:15 AM on a bustling Saturday morning, witnessing the ebb and flow of the customer tide.

Our table enjoyed three variations of cherng fun:
- Beef & Shrimp with Chives ($6.95)
- Beef & Pork with Chives ($6.95)
- Fried Dough ($4.50)

The generous filling in the meaty crepes justified the price, though the presentation differed from the original venue, with a single thickly stuffed crepe replacing the dual crepe offering. This led to a slight imbalance in the filling-to-crepe ratio. Meanwhile, the fried dough stood out for its crispy exterior and tender heart, served alongside sweet and peanut butter dipping sauces. However, the delicacy of the wrapping was evident as the crepes struggled to maintain their integrity.

A bowl of Lai Wan (Seafood) Congee ($5.95), though ample and shareable, presented a novel inclusion of fish fillets - an adjustment for those unacquainted but nonetheless a flavorful venture into the porridge-like dish.

The HK Style tea ($2.75) fell short of expectations, leaning bitter with a lackluster tea infusion, leaving much to be desired even after sugar's attempt at redemption.

Facilities met cleanliness standards on my initial visit, but caution is advised as floors tended to get slippery later on.

In summation, while the cherng fun and congee are must-try items reflective of their experience in this culinary art, there is room for improvement in the beverage department and crepe consistency. It's an establishment well-suited for small group dining, offering a taste of Guangzhou with an authentic twist.

I don't make it down to Chinatown too often, but my brother does and always sends me pics of the different places he goes. While my interest is piqued, I've just never made the effort to sample them myself. That being said, I've kept a mental note to try some of these places if circumstance found me in the area. Flash forward to the other day when one of my colleagues bought in buns from Hop Shing for breakfast. It was Friday and a change from the usual bagel and schmear, so of course I had to try.The buns were warm and substantial, a simple presentation yet so inviting with their perfect, shiny coatings. There were two varieties - sugar and pork. Since I didn't feel like eating warm pork at 8:45am, I decided to go with the sugar. Wow - there was a decent amount of sugar inside without being overpowering, and that being combined with the warmth of the bun itself made it melt in my mouth.Overall, I really enjoyed my bun from Hop Shing. While I'm not sure when I'll be visiting, they're definitely on my radar if I'm ever in the area.

I found the Vietspot from passing by many times while going to Blink FiDi. The smell of their Pho soups is pretty obvious when you walk by this hole-in-wall restaurant. I only tried their beef pho twice afterwork. The portions are big and filling for their price. BTW, I noticed an $1 increase recently for all their menu items. Overall, I really enjoyed their pho and I don't have to commute to Chinatown when a random Viet food craving strikes. NOTE: This place is pretty small. There are about 10-12 stool seating.

I've found my ultimate Banh Mi spot in NYC at Saigon Deli on 369 Broome St, and dare I say, it might top any other in North America. This place deserves a shoutout for its curry chicken Banh Mi – a massive and flawlessly crafted sandwich that's a feast for the taste buds, crafted by one of the friendliest proprietors around.

Despite the sandwich's greatness, this gem remains underrated, much like the talents of Summer Brielle, but it's high time that changed. I introduced Barbie to their Banh Mi, and her approval sealed the deal – it's a hit.

The curry chicken filling is a divine concoction that elevates the Banh Mi experience to new heights. It takes a couple of minutes to prepare, but patience is rewarded with every delectable bite.

To sum it up: Saigon Deli's Banh Mi is a culinary masterpiece that's both an essential NYC eating experience and a testament to the art of sandwich-making. Whether you're a die-hard foodie or just seeking a superb meal, this place is a must-visit. Barbie and I agree – this Vietnamese delight is not to be missed.

I recently enjoyed my first brunch at this Taj property, and it certainly won't be my last. Opting for the 3-course experience, each dish from the appetizer to the dessert was delightful. Service was impeccable, living up to the Taj reputation. I'm already looking forward to my next visit. - @traveleen_gurl

Amazing. Just... amazing. No other word sums up my experience here better than that. I am addicted to sugar and desserts so I was very excited to try this place with two other friends. We came on a Monday night and there was plenty of seating available. The ambiance was nice and cozy inside. Everything on their menu looked so good and I wanted to try it all so badly... after a few difficult minutes, we decided to order the Milky Puff and the Matcha Lava.These desserts were so delicious that eating them improved my quality of life. I'm not exaggerating. I was thoroughly blown away by the decadence and taste of both. The Milky Puff had an impeccable blend of richness from the warm puff pastry that paired so well with the sweet toppings. I couldn't stop eating it. The Matcha Lava was also delightful. I was very impressed by the flavor of the matcha ganache and the chocolate cake was incredibly moist and warm. I still remember the sheer bliss I felt eating these. A beautiful experience. I love this place and I already can't wait to come back and try their other desserts / inhale their entire menu.

Title: Chic New York Elegance with a Side of Expense

Upon entering the restaurant, one is immediately struck by its quintessential New York vibe – an ambience meticulously crafted through a well-chosen array of bottles lining the bar, set against a backdrop of dark wood and perfectly tuned acoustics that foster a sense of intimacy without dampening the lively hum of conversation.

The culinary offerings parallel the decor in their artful presentation, with dishes that are familiar yet slightly askew in preparation, creating an illusion of innovation. The food, while not transcending the ordinary, is unquestionably delightful and satisfying to the palate.

Service is where the establishment truly shines, providing an exemplary model of hospitality. Staff are warm, knowledgeable, and exude an authentic niceness that elevates the dining experience.

However, the pricing does reflect the upscale atmosphere and quality, leaning towards the steep side. One could argue that the cost is a shade higher than one might prefer, with a modest reduction making the experience more palatable for the budget-conscious diner.

Passed by this place so many times within the last year, decided to finally check it out for brunch!Service was great, the food was good.I ended up getting the cowgirl omelette and the pancakes.I wish they had the option to get pancakes as a side instead of an entrée only.

Went for brunch on Saturday at 12.  Party of 6. Great location on the UES across the street from Bloomingdales    love good food and good service.  We don't mind spending $$$$ when we have a great meal but I have to ask:If I order a Greek salad ($19) for brunch and choose to add salmon should a restaurant add another $20 for the salmon?I don't think so but they did.   So not worth it.     Oh well.   We've eaten here several times but not sure we'll come back.  We hate feeling ripped off.

2nd time here. Was very good. Had a ceviche while cousin had a couple fish and shrimp tacos. Hits the spot. The challenge Remains the seating. Be patient and don't linger way past your eating. Let someone else sit once you're done.

I recently dined at a local restaurant where I had a delightful experience. The service was top-notch, attentive without being intrusive. I ordered a burger which, to my delight, was cooked to perfection and absolutely amazing in taste. For dessert, I was served a colossal portion that was as delicious as it was large. The cleanliness and brightness of the establishment added to the pleasant atmosphere. While the price was steep—$50 for both the burger and dessert—it was well worth it for the quality and taste. Highly recommend for those willing to indulge in a pricier, yet delicious meal.

Lovely restaurant situated close to the Central Park. Jean-George is really the quality assurance. Love the ambience and the contemporary decor of Nougatine. We had a party of 7 coming here on a Sunday for a brunch. The service was very attentive. We picked a few appetizers and entrees to share, finished with a couple lovely dessert. The presentation of the food was great, and the ingredients tasted fresh, beautifully seasoned, very flavorful. We were very impressed by the pasta, the Sea bass and beef tenderloin, very savory and tasty, highly recommended! For the dessert, the passion fruit pavlova and the Green apple flavored sorbet tasted so refreshing, great finish!The restaurant had ample exposure to the sun, we totally enjoyed the beautiful weather and the wonderful dining experience. Forgot to mention - we bumped into the fashion designer Alexander Wang in the restaurant that day.  How lucky we were

Tucked away in the bustling heart of the Lower East Side, this pizza joint serves as a convenient refuge for those in search of a quick fix for their late-night cravings. Amidst a backdrop of lively bars, it offers a no-frills experience with a New York twist.

During my visit, the BBQ chicken pizza slice, ringing up at $3.50, felt steep for the standard it delivered. While the pizza itself was satisfactory, with a classic crispy, thin crust that pays homage to traditional NY style, it didn't leave a lasting impression or have a distinctive flair to differentiate it from the myriad of other options lining the streets of New York.

This is a cash-only spot without the amenity of seating, making it clear that it's tailored for those on the go. In summary, it's an average pit stop for a quick slice, but don't expect culinary fireworks.

Four stars for the tasty soup dumplings (some of the best I've ever eaten), the helpful waitress (graciously accommodated substitutions in one dish), and the clean dining room.While the chicken with garlic and the shredded beef were fairly good dishes (could've been spicier), not on par with the fantastic dumplings.

Great value dim sum. Nice ambiance. Definitely liked the things I chose from the House Special section on the menu more, as those selections ended up having more unique flavors that I haven't had at other dim sum places in the city.1) Lemon BBQ pork buns: standout, very interesting taste, subtle lemon flavor made it something I've never had before2) Pork soup dumplings: not the best in regards to soup dumplings in nyc but served in individual spoons which was nice. The dumplings were stuck to the spoons which caused the soup dumpling eating process (of drinking the soup first) pretty difficult.3) Fried lobster dumplings: smaller than I expected, but was my second favorite. The shrimp taste and texture overpowered the lobster, but was very good nonetheless4) Baked pork buns: good, in regards to buns I recommend getting the lemon ones over the baked ones. 5) hello Kitty buns: good! Got this for free from the yelp check-in promo.

Glad I stumbled upon and tried OTT. Hiccup in my delivery order due to an issue with the third-party notification system. But the second they knew they handled it perfectly, offered a tasty something as apology for the wait, and expedited the order. Everything was well packed, freshly made, and the delivery guy was friendly. Calamari stayed decently crispy and wasn't too rubbery. Their wonton soup is awesome. Top three I've ever had. Their wontons are handmade and super delicate. Presentation doesn't translate in delivery due to how delicate the wontons are. But that's the only issue; you tell it hits all the marks when dining in.Pad Thai flavor and noodle moisture also on point. Protein overcooked. But that was just the pork. They have an awesome variety of proteins, including salmon. So looking forward to repeat orders and working my way through those options.Very solid delivery option, and I'm already interested to pop in if ever in their area.

I visited Per Se on my own during a trip to New York City in March 2018. I didn't make reservation ahead of time so I had to go during the lunch time when there were a lot more available tables.I chose to have a 5-course lunch instead of doing the full tasting menu. Can't recall the exact price but it was not too bad.Experience was pretty much what one would anticipate at a fine dining restaurant: Food was beautifully presented in the matching dining ware which were like a piece of artwork by themselves. Service was friendly and staff were knowledgeable...everything seems alright, but why only 4 star not 5?The reason was I found the highlight points of the entire meal were not well paced. My liking for each dish...unfortunately, would probably draw a downhill curve (though even the lowest point was not below par still!). The salmon tartare amuse-bouche and the famous oyster and pearl appetizer were indeed amazing, foie gras was beautiful, but the rest were more like the ordinary way of deliciousness without the "wow" factor. One could argue that it was because I chose a shortened course, but since it was presented as an option on a Michelin 3-star restaurant's menu, I'd rather expect it to be as much well designed as the full course.Overall still a restaurant worth to try.

The UES is not the neighborhood that comes to mind when I want some killer tacos. I think part of the problem is the sheer volume of mediocre spots between the 70's and 90's. Cascabel has a lot going for it in terms of sticking out among the overload of options on 2nd ave, particularly their emphasis on fresh ingredients and quirky decor. How can you not love a spot with the slogan, "Eat ~ Drink ~ Love Tacos"? Unfortunately, after ordering a bunch of their menu I can't say I'd ever recommend anyone to come here for anything except the booze. And even that's a questionable "eh".   The good:Nachos libres - The nachos were great. Although I wish they were transparent about the size of the "fiesta time" (aka happy hour) serving. This was not enough to split between 4 people and I would have happily sprung for the normal menu version if our waiter had given us a heads up. Their cheese sauce is bomb and I bet these would've been great topped with chorizo. The not so good:Yuca fries - Yuca is such an underrated veggie so I was ecstatic to see it on their menu. I was hoping to convert my fry enthusiast friends who had never tried it before. This does not do yuca justice. I'm not sure how they prepared these, but they were chalky, undercooked, and hard as a rock. Wish I would've scanned some reviews before ordering these because it seems to be consistent feedback. Mexi Wings - I'm not a big wings person, but I love me some cheese, so I was drawn in by the idea of cotija dressing. While that aspect of the dish was great, the wings themselves were sickeningly sweet. These actually left me craving for real wings. Drinks - All together, we tried the pomegranate, watermelon/basil, house marg, and sangria. We actually passed our drinks around trying to find a decent one out of the bunch. They all tasted watered down, particularly the watermelon/basil. Granted, these were from the "Fiesta time" menu and a lot of bars don't go all out on discounted drinks. Not a big deal, but maybe stick with their expansive tequila menu. It might seem like we ordered a lot, and we did, but between the portion sizes and overall questionable edibleness we left Cascabel in search for real food. Come here for the bar and cozy space, skip the food.

VERY vegan friendly, but they have meat too if you're into that. But no dairy! Feels like a hybrid between fast casual and a hip place you'd want to have a margarita. Impossible Taco is great, like the crunchy beef tacos from your childhood but upgraded and cruelty free. Prefer this over the vegan chorizo taco and veggie taco but both of those are good too. Taco salad is good. You can add chickpeas or probably bean mash if you're trying to keep it light and don't want to load up on chorizo. Caesar salad was surprisingly tasty and hearty, though didn't taste like traditional Caesar. I subbed romaine for kale and added chickpeas. Solid guac. Side of coconut rice with black bean mash... don't get me wrong, I liked it, but it had an unexpected tang to it. Neutral about that but beware. Elote corn is fine but not a must. The little hot sauces are great - love the orange one. Margaritas taste like tequila if you're into that (I'm not).

Title: A Festive BYOB Birthday Dining Experience

We chose this bustling establishment for a joint birthday celebration, drawn by the BYOB policy that caters perfectly to my friends' discerning tastes in wine and beer. With foresight, we'd made a reservation, which was essential on such a busy Friday evening. A Turkish member of our party took the lead in organizing our table's selections, which allowed us a delightful sampling of dishes—ranging from fresh salads to a rich calf's liver.

While I played it safe with the Chicken shish kebab, which unfortunately proved underwhelming in flavor, the culinary adventure was not lost on me. I found myself enjoying bites of the robust kofte and the layered complexity of the musakka my friends had ordered. The branzino, albeit too bony for our liking, was the single downside, contrasted by the unexpectedly savory chicken chops.

The evening concluded on a sweet note with two dessert offerings—one an enigmatic yet delicious treat, and the other, an assortment of flavor-infused baklava that perfectly capped our meal.

Through it all, the service was impeccable—every dish was presented with a warm smile. Despite my less thrilling choice, the experience has left me eager to return and explore more of the menu. The BYOB aspect not only added a personalized touch but also made our festive gathering more affordable. All in all, a place worth revisiting for both the atmosphere and the culinary exploration it promises.

hillcountrybbq is honestly a neighborhood gem! I'm so glad to have come across! Once you step in, you get warped into a whole new world of meat lovers galore & you forgot that you're in NYC let alone manhattan! The ambiance is super lively with cafeteria style ordering & spacious communal seating. It's just an amazing experience, especially if you love bbq meat like me!  Briskets are my favorite but you can choose from a variety of meats & sides to try & order more as you pleases. If you're craving some good old fashioned smoked bbq from the Wild West then you should definitely check this spot out! I can't wait to go back!It does get super packed so make sure to make a reservation before you go!!

Must try: Eats Regular with Thai Tea! (Free soup)Why: Thai-styled Hainanese chicken was tender and tasty. It was plentiful over the ginger jasmine rice and comes with the three sauces: sweet soy, green chili, and ginger dressing. I used all the sweet soy and ginger dressing on the chicken and rice. I also liked the cilantro and cucumber garnishes, which added flavor and crunch. The meal also came with hot chicken melon soup that complements the chicken and rice. Actually, I enjoyed taking a sip of soup after each chicken and rice bite! At first, I didn't like the idea of no ice in my Thai Tea but then realized it was cold enough, refreshing, and more liquid to wash down the food! Notes: What a great lunch deal ($12.50 before tax and tip)! Very quick meal prep since it's a simple dish, which is helpful for lunch on the go. I will definitely come back for lunch!

Title: A Harlem Gem That's Here to Stay

I've visited Cecil's three times over the last couple of years and it's crystal clear why it has become a staple in Harlem. The recipe for their success is no secret: outstanding customer service, skilled chefs and bartenders, along with astute management – they all come together to earn a top-notch rating.

Each visit has been marked by consistency in all the right areas – delicious food, tantalizing drinks, warm customer service, and a lively music backdrop that ties the whole dining experience together. It's a refreshing sight to witness an establishment that not only survives but thrives in Harlem, where others have come and gone.

My last Friday night at Cecil's matched the upbeat vibes of my previous visits, solidifying it as a reliably good time. The word is spreading too – I've introduced several co-workers to Cecil's, and their glowing reviews mirror my own. They've even considered booking the party room for future events.

I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit to Cecil's and have no doubt that they will keep up the excellent work. Harlem has a true gem in its midst, and I'm confident Cecil's will remain a favorite for locals and visitors alike.

I came to try the beloved Artichoke pizza and wasn't impressed. The $6 slice was big enough for a meal but I felt it was just having Alfredo sauce on top of pizza. The crust was a bit tough and the pizza cheese wasn't warm. I wished they had heated up the pizza slice in the oven before serving it to me. If you're looking to try, I recommend going to the take out line in the back. There's a small bar/table near the cashier where you can stand and eat.

I stumbled upon this place with my girlfriend and her family while seeking far and wide for a great Mexican restaurant. Skeptical to eat at this location given the nature of crowds and excess people, I was pleasantly surprised. Our waiter showed a ton of sass when ordering but the food tasted delicious.Their menu is pretty expensive. They have your staple dishes like quesadillas, burritos and to Quito's. Their drinks are well-crafted in the frozen margaritas were a hit at our table.You will certainly feel rushed to order and complete your dining experience given that you're in the middle of Times Square but that shouldn't stop you from at least frequenting this spot. There are no surprises here! Then again, sometimes all you want is a dependable Mexican restaurant in retired from the streets of New York.

One of the BEST pizza I have ever had. It took a PIZZA MY HEART (my attempt at puns)..:: FOOD ::. Spicy Spring pepperoni pie (square) $5: It's in a square form covered in the pepperoni with a cup shape. TBH, I gave it no hope and thought "ITS ALL HYPE" because they have a wall full of celebrities that have  ate there before and I'm not exactly a pizza fanatic or anything. BUT it met every hype that my friends have told me about. They do NOT have a non-spicy version of the pizza but the cashier PROMISED that it's not that spicy. SO I trusted her and it was definitely not TOO spicy. Just a bit of a kick which I could totally handle (coming from a girl that cries eating Hot Cheetos). The cheese was SOOOO good, it was melt in your mouth. The crust was crunchy and well made. Not too thick, not too thin. The pepperoni was the star as it was very flavorful and satisfying with every bite. YES, a bit of a hefty slice. So come hungry. .:: Service/Ambiance ::.I feel like the cashier was a bit brush off-ish and snobby. You order with the pizza cutting guy then proceed to pay at the cashier right next door. The place is SMALL. Definitely not good for big groups. Little to no room. They have wall tables along both sides of the restaurant. Honestly fits only 5 people on each table. No seats. Just standing. They have two walls full of celebrities that have stopped by for pizza. A lot of people just stand outside the restaurant to eat.

Title: A Midtown East Gem for Delicious, Healthy Eats!

If you find yourself in Midtown East craving a meal that strikes the perfect balance between mouthwatering flavors and health-conscious choices, look no further! This restaurant is a must-visit for anyone seeking a quick lunch or dinner without compromising on taste or nutritional value.

Catering to a diverse palette, including those following a vegan lifestyle, the menu boasts various options, ensuring there's something for everyone. I tried the Penang Bowl, a beautifully composed dish featuring tender chicken atop a bed of brown rice, complemented by a flawlessly poached egg, crisp cucumber, and a sprinkle of zesty spices, all brought together with a tantalizing peanut curry sauce. It was an unforgettable meal that left me completely satisfied without any feelings of dining remorse.

The portion sizes are generous, ensuring you get great value for your money. Service is quick, making it an ideal spot for a grab-and-go meal that doesn't skimp on quality or flavor. This restaurant has quickly become a non-negotiable staple in my dining routine, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

What a hidden gem! Came here for a bite before a Knicks game a few weeks ago and was very pleased. Originally walked in because the location is right next to MSG and heard it was the go-to spot to booze before a game :-)Must order:-Parma flatbread (super thin prosciutto yummm)-Blue crab Mac & cheese-Tartufo flatbread -Charred Spanish octopus (so freaking tender!)-Pomegranate duckAlso love sitting at the bar with a dirty martini. Have come back several times since because the food, drinks, bartenders & service are all PHENOMENAL.

I recently indulged in what has swiftly become one of my favorite old-school-style burgers at this charming establishment. Opting for the Bistro Burger, complete with succulent bacon, rich cheese, and perfectly caramelized onions, I requested it be cooked medium rare — a choice I would highly recommend. While I did notice the service was on the leisurely side, the wait was a small price to pay for such an exceptional burger. I'm already planning my next visit, and with the whispers of a new portobello mushroom burger, it seems there will be something to intrigue both carnivores and vegetarians alike. A definite must-try for any burger aficionado!

I recently visited an amazing little gem perfect for a date night, boasting a cozy atmosphere coupled with great service that exuded a charming, humble vibe. The shrimp pasta and lasagna were truly enjoyable, satisfying my cravings for well-crafted Italian fare. While the wine was decent, it didn't quite steal the spotlight. Nonetheless, the overall experience was delightful, and I would definitely return for another round of their delectable dishes.

I had really high expectations of ABCV after hearing so many great things about this place but I left disappointed and hungry for more. I ordered the wild mushroom, poached farm eggs, shallots and herbs and the avocado lettuce cups to share and each plate was more disappointing than the next. The wild mushroom dish was ok but expected more for the price tag (same went for the avocado cups). Overall, if you're on a diet and in need of some healthy, guilt free food, I would recommend this place but otherwise eh, I'd probably pick somewhere else.

My friend and I came in here for Sunday afternoon tea. We did the full classic tea for two set.The wait was a little longer than we were expecting- was told we would be seated in 20 but ended up taking around 40 minutes.Once we got seated, we selected our tea choices, sandwich choices and scone choices. As for the tea, the pots were huge and so cute! We were able to get unlimited selectionn of tea but because the pot was so large we only really got 3 types of tea each. For the food, the scones were really good- they also had a vegan scone whIch tasted a little more dry than the other scones. For the sandwiches, I really liked the curry chicken sandwich- it was very flavorful. The bottom layer (of the three layer tea set) was cookies and cake. The cookies and cake were a good variety and the slice of cake was huge. My personal oPinion was that the cake ran on the sweeter side but it could be nice paired with a more bitter tea like black tea. I had a more floral one so maybe that was why it tasted sweet to me.Overall, I liked this spot as a nice hangout place to just sit and have casual tea. It's definitely a good way to spend a lazy afternoon. I noticed they also have a good selection of brunch menu- including sandwiches, so there's also possibility to order those instead of the full tea and to get tea separately.

Hmm, I am not sure if it was an off day for them, but the steamed rolls I got were over-cooked to a mush, which made them very hard to pick up with chopsticks. They were also a bit flavorless, even with the addition of sauce (I think the pork inside was under-seasoned). I've had steamed rolls in the past with more of a bite to them and with more flavorful filling. Maybe they are still working through the kinks of a soft opening. I was really excited to come here, as I heard so many great things, but as things are now, I probably won't be hurrying back, especially at this price point. At least the interior is clean.

Yum! Loved the Zha Zhang Mian and Shanghai Pork Soup Dumplings in particular. FOODThe Zha Ziang Mian's noodle texture was fantastically bouncy while the sauce had the perfect balance of salty/sweet with tender bits of meat. Loved the amount of carrots and cucumbers they topped it with. The sweet and creamy egg worked really well with the dish too.The soup dumplings were large, FULL of soup, and filled with tasty gingery pork. This is now my go-to spot for soup dumplings outside of Chinatown.The boneless pork trotters had a good amount of heat but the one-dimensional gooey texture left something to be desired. I recommend getting rice with this dish to get a hold of all the flavors.I had one of their hot loose leaf green teas - can't recall the name now but it was the third one starting with T. Very clean/earthy and paired well with the food. Moreover, it was beautifully presented in a functional double layered insulated cup over a wooden coaster. It stayed warm throughout the meal!SERVICEOverall, really great. They saved a table for us even though my friend was late. Good timing of taking orders and giving us the check after we requested it. My water cup was never close to empty (I drink a lot of water). They forgot our order of jasmine rice (ordered it later) but the staff was kind and the rest of the food came pretty quickly!

This place has been open since the new semester started. I don't know why I haven't written a review yet... I actually haven't been here to try the Chinese food yet, so I can't comment on that. I mainly come for the bagels, so I usually try to get here in the morning. I like getting the egg salad, as it's not too bad here. However, more recently I've been getting the nussbaum classic but without capers and light cream cheese. They're usually pretty good at keeping it on the light side of cream cheese, so they do care about getting your order right. Hence, I'm willing to give a 4 star, even though this place is a little bit more expensive than absolute bagels.Pro tip: you can shorten the time your bagel order takes DRAMATICALLY if you choose not to have your bagel toasted.

This is good Mexican fare. I had recently been to a Mexican restaurant that everyone raved about and I was disappointed. But a friend brought me here and it was excellent. I really liked it. The drinks are great and reasonable. I usually stick with a Negro Modello as my drink of choice, but they do have the usual drinks you find in a Mexican Restaurant. The chips on the table come with both salsa (spicy) and guacamole. You can get free refrills on this. My friend had a quesadilla which looked better than most I had ever seen.  This one was fresh and filled with chicken and cheese. They did not skimp. I had the chicken fajita which was truly fresh. The onions and peppers were cooked just right. In fact they had a good crunch and not over cooked. The tortillas were a bit skimpy. I could have used 4 instead of 3 small ones. But the rice and beans were good as well. So I made a meal without them anyway. I really liked it.Hell's Kitchen is a good experience. Definitely a "Keeper" on my go-to places.

The kind of place you have to go at least once. First impression: CRAMPED is definitely the first thing. My part of 4 was crammed into a VERY tiny, upright booth where we were practically knee-to-knee. It feel more like sitting on the edge of a stool than a seat where you could relax. We're all pretty small, and it was TIGHT. 4 normal sized people probably couldn't fit there. Space aside, if you're looking for that Facebook-famous cheese scrape, you have to order one of the items from the "raclette" section. I split the Mediterranee with another person. Prices are premium, but I was not disappointed at all by the quality of cheese and food that arrived on the plate. The cheese (and rind!) were AMAZING and went perfectly with the tomatoes, bread, and greens. The traditional cheese was wonderful!

It's been years since my last visit this area unfortunately isn't always the easiest to visit. I happen to be in the area & we wanted to grab some food this place had no wait time. To start we went with a bottle of white wine, a Pinot Grigio not bad, can't go wrong. They start u off with some bread & olive oil very good, olive oil + nice soft bread .. dangerous combo Lolll. Appetizers tried the Burrata mozzarella wow ... amazing fresh tasting Burrata practically melts in your mouth. Main dishes the Farfalle alla Campagnola pasta dish is very good light tasting sauce , good pasta w some Italian sausage & dried tomato. Pizza we gave the Bufalina a try also very good, the crust could be toasted a bit more but over all nice taste with the buffalo mozzarella, basil & olive oil. Very small restaurant it can feel a bit jammed packed, rustic simple decor. Service was good prices are typical to the area, we enjoyed our meal.

I recently visited this restaurant for a work dinner and was thoroughly impressed with the quality of the cuisine. The highlight for me was the tuna belly pasta, which was exquisitely prepared, though the specific type of pasta eludes me. The mozzarella featured in the caprese appetizer was of outstanding quality, adding a rich, creamy texture to the dish. An accompanying eggplant side was also noteworthy for its flavorful preparation. On the beverage front, the gin gimlet I ordered was mixed to perfection, striking the right balance between zest and spirit. To cap off the meal, the tiramisu proved to be the star dessert, truly the best I've had, leaving a lasting impression of sweet satisfaction. Overall, a remarkable dining experience I'd recommend without hesitation.

This was a small cozy dimsum place where you order from the menu. My friend and I ordered one order of pork soup dumplings, an order of crab soup dumplings, chicken feet, Shumai and steamed spare ribs. Their dishes were all pretty tasty - the typical dim sum taste and flavor. What I was most impressed with was the crab soup dumplings. Being someone that doesn't really enjoy the fishy taste, I never really ordered crab soup dumplings but my friend wanted to try them so we got them here. They were super tasty and juicy but it didn't have much of a fishy smell. They were probably one of the best crab soup dumplings I've had.The prices were pretty standard. The service was also very good, the waiter was nice and attentive and overall I had a good experience here. I would definitely come back!

Title: A Cozy Spot for Flavorful Comfort Food

Last Friday evening, I had the pleasure of dining early with a friend at this charming new restaurant. Right off the bat, we were struck by the tantalizing array of dishes on the menu, making it a delightful challenge to choose.

We started with the Roti Tellur, a fluffy egg-infused roti complemented by a curry sauce that, while delicious, would benefit from a tad more heat. The Chicken Satay followed; tender skewered chicken topped with peanuts was decent, yet not extraordinary.

However, the standout of the night was the Kway Teow. The wide rice noodles were a symphony of flavors, hitting the perfect note of spiciness. Coupled with the unique addition of squash and carrots, this dish was a revelation in both taste and texture.

As the restaurant filled up, the good service remained unwavering. I wholeheartedly recommend this place, especially for the Kway Teow. It seems we weren't the only ones impressed — our neighboring diners ended up mirroring our order, clearly enticed by the visual and aromatic appeal of our meals.

Walked in with $25Walked out drunk, full, and happyPros:Cheap and affordable pricesGood foodBetter drinksSpacious outdoor seating Cons:Small indoor dining areaLong wait times Tip:Pace yourself especially with the frozen drinks...a frostbit drunk is never cute

It was my first time in Hudson Yards, stopped by Wild Ink after watching a show, the kitchen had just closed but the cocktails were in full effect!  I was tempted to go for the Hudson old fashioned and made a last minute switch to the Kohlipe Kohlada.  It was a great choice.  Given my Puerto Rican roots, I was nostalgic with the flavors of cinnamon and coconut.  It was like indulging in a coquito slush.

During a casual walk down 3rd Avenue in Midtown East, I had the delightful chance to encounter a charming food cart offering a concise selection of momos. Their straightforward menu is a breath of fresh air where one can opt for beef, chicken, or vegetable fillings, and decide between steamed or fried, with the bonus option of a savory gravy.

The pricing is incredibly fair for Midtown, where just $6 scores you 8 succulent steamed momos – a true bargain! For the more indulgent palate, a small additional charge grants you the fried/gravy variants.

I indulged in a beef momo drowned in rich gravy and a classic steamed chicken momo. Both were exceptionally tasty, but the chicken momo stole the show with its perfect blend of flavor and tenderness. 

Make a mental note: whenever you're near 46th & Third Avenue, this food cart is a must-visit. It offers an unbeatable combination of delicious eats and value that promises not to disappoint.

Title: A Noodle Shop's Rise and Fall

My initial visit to this quaint Japanese noodle shop was a delightful experience. The staff made an excellent impression with their attentive eye contact and clear communication. Service was swift, and both the curry pork and the curry noodle soup did not disappoint with their flavors. Table service was competent, prompting plans for future visits.

Sadly, my most recent visit on February 27, 2019, marked a drastic decline. The beloved counter chef has hung up his apron, a new management team has stepped in, and the once Japanese staff has been replaced. The quality of the sashimi and eel over rice plummeted, with improper cuts and telltale signs of being previously frozen. It's with a heavy heart that I say farewell to what was once a favorite spot.

As a seafood lover, I'd be happy to give this place a 5 star rating, but on the other hand my vegetarian friends didn't love it as much, as the options were limited. However, if you eat seafood and meat, I HIGHLY recommend you try them out! I started off with the truffled scallops which were incredible, and my main was a squid ink noodle with crab meat, which is basically all of my favorite things in one. Although it is on the pricier side, I definitely recommend giving it a try! -Navya J @nyconthetable

I was walking and suddenly saw Bice in the middle of Manhattan. I knew Bice in Buenos Aires during my honeymoon. Find it in New York on the day of my birthday was really a present. The waiter, another surprise! A very nice Brazilian guy that really made my day. The service was amazing, and the dessert came with a Happy Birthday sang by all staff. The food as expected: amazing! Thanks Bice for having delicious food and incredible staff.

**Restaurant Review: Sushi Ishikawa**

**TLDR:** An unforgettable omakase journey by former O Ya executive chef Don Pham awaits at the Upper East Side's Sushi Ishikawa.

From the onset, it's clear that Sushi Ishikawa takes an uncustomary route with its omakase. The establishment, steered by the adept hands of Chef Don Pham, is not one for sushi purists seeking traditional edomae. Instead, the chef inaugurates the experience with an atypical, though exceptionally succulent, nodoguro that's akin to tasting pure fat.

The procession of the 'Market Price' menu can only be described as a lavish assault of the senses. Each piece of nigiri is a testament to extravagance, crowned with ingredients like uni, ikura, caviar, truffles, and gold flakes. The toast adorned with these sumptuous toppings, and the botan ebi with a touch of butter and bottarga, are particularly striking. Chef Pham's dishes are a cinematographer's dream, undoubtedly created with visual appeal in mind.

Though the latter part of the meal, featuring small plates, fades from my memory, the climactic hand roll—or more aptly, 'hand bouquet'—returns to form with its generous embellishments of uni, ikura, toro, and a hint of rice crackers.

For those with a palate inclined toward rich flavors like truffle, foie gras, and caviar, Sushi Ishikawa is a treasure trove offering significant value. Although my personal preferences veer away from such opulence, for the connoisseur of indulgent tastes, Chef Pham's creations at Sushi Ishikawa will be nothing short of a culinary revel.

Another meh experience this past week with a not so great restaurant (should we call it that?). I've been to my fair share of Turkish restaurants and I wasn't so impressed with this place. I didn't realize that this was better for a takeout and get out experience than a sit in experience. Maybe the pictures I saw on Yelp beforehand were a bit misleading. I also didn't realize how cramped it was in the back and the limited seating available. In fact, they didn't even have a legit dining in menu (like a booklet or laminated paper), I was given their 3-folded takeout menu. Let's start with pros:* Aesthetically pleasing setting: while the place is cramped, I liked the surrounding design and the traditional serving ware used (makes instaworthy photos) * Turkish tea and sigara borek (Philo rolls) were good. But hey, you can't really go wrong with these items at a Turkish restaurant, imo*  Convenient location- 5 minutes from the subwayCons-* Not good for sitting in and dining.
