You're not going to get that dining in experience here. Waiters are super busy handling the grub hub orders coming in (oh yeah, you'll hear the grub hub announcement going off every now and then too). It was hard to get their attention. * Their menu wasn't the most clear. Even though it says all the dishes under the Meat section are served with rice, salad, and bread, it's only in fact the first 3 or 4 dishes on the menu. There was no perforated line or anything separating the last couple of dishes on that section to indicate those were treated differently! I ordered lamb iskender and it was a lot of meat with soaked in bread. Ugh. It's a gravy filled dish, so some rice would have been nice. * Ok, so I'm not really one who comments on restaurant bathrooms but this one really got to me. It was basically a closet in my opinion. It was hard to get in since there is soo little space between the toilet and the door. Horrible. The bathroom mirror was put waaaay above the bathroom sink, making it futile. Either the contractor who made this bathroom was not the brightest or this bathroom was not built for the vertically challenged or anyone beyond a size 2, which is sad since the waiters were not that much taller than me (just saying...) Overall, for the price I paid, it really didn't live up to my expectations and I prefer many of the other Turkish places I frequented. Probably good for grub hub orders though

For starters, ignore the bad reviews because they couldn't be more inaccurate. Mr. Chow is wonderful! The service is impeccable, food is outstanding, and ambiance is comfortable and inviting.We had reservations and couldn't get our table right away so the Maitre D' provided us with two glasses of champagne on the house. We finally found our table and ordered a bottle, which was poured for us immediately. A server approached us within minutes of sitting and recommended the Mr. Chow Prix Fixé based on our desired order. Food:- Lobster Shumai: FINALLY a restaurant in NYC that knows how to make shumai correctly. If it's made right it doesn't need a sauce. The dish speaks for itself and it's lovely. There are two tiers with 3 shumai on each.- Chicken Satay: MUST ORDER. The butter sauce that tops the tender chicken is delicious. I'm used to eating a dry piece of chicken and usually avoid this dish but I heard we had to try. I'm so happy we did because we left and couldn't stop talking about that sauce. - Mr. Chow Noodles (Vegetable): Absolutely perfect. I don't know how anyone could say something bad about this dish, unless they're used to American style greasy noodles. I will order this again without hesitation. The table next to us said they wished they had ordered it after seeing it. So good!- Shrimp Fried Rice: Perfectly cooked fried rice with limited shrimp. I wish there had been more shrimp but again, the rice on its own was so delicious that I didn't realize the lack of shrimp until later.- Bok Choy: Al dente and flavorful! I'm happy we went with this vegetable dish because it perfectly complimented our entrees.- Green Shrimp: OMG!!! You have to order this dish! I can't express how much we loved this dish. Plenty for two people, delicious, addicting.- Chilean Sea Bass: Tasted like candy with a tasty sauce. Four thick slices of sea bass, tender, and hearty. I wish there were more of it. Still, very impressed and happy we ordered.- Lychee: How can you beat this dessert? Fresh and the perfect dish to cap the night.There are many reviews stating Mr. Chow is too expensive for what you get... I didn't have that experience and I'm a foodie. If you don't want to pay the rate then go to a lower end Chinese restaurant. The service is fantastic... our table was cleaned instantly and champagne topped off without ever asking.We'll be back! Thank you!

Title: Brunch Delight at Olio e Più

My previous experiences at Olio e Più for dinner and lunch had set a high bar, so I was excited to try their brunch offerings. Despite dealing with a large party, the service was impeccable - attentive and undisturbed by our numbers, which is no small feat in New York City.

Upon arrival, the host's warmth stood out, graciously allowing us to gather at our table while we waited for the rest of our group to arrive. The ambiance of Olio e Più is particularly charming, boasting a rustic decor that truly comes to life when the weather allows for an open atrium feel.

The true highlight, however, was the food. I indulged in the squid ink pasta with octopus and shrimp, a dish that, despite its $32 price tag for brunch, was utterly remarkable and justified the expense. To complement the meal, we were treated to a half-off bottle of wine special which showcased an impressive selection.

Olio e Più has yet again proven its consistency across all meals. Whether it's for brunch, lunch, or dinner, I wholeheartedly recommend this gem for a delicious and satisfying dining experience.

I visited this restaurant for a weekday lunch and was pleased to find that making a reservation through Resy was a breeze. Opting for the Sansai kinoko soba, I was delighted by its flavorful broth which truly stood out. The sashimi, fresh and tasty, did not disappoint either. Service was attentive and added to the positive experience. I would certainly recommend this spot for anyone seeking a slightly upscale yet unpretentious midtown lunch.

Nestled on 10th Avenue, this quaint Italian restaurant is a gem perfect for both group dining and romantic date nights. Reservations were a breeze to set up, which is always a plus.

Our party of three indulged in the mushroom bruschetta, chicken parmigiana, and pappardelle sausage pasta. The mushroom bruschetta stole the show with its warm, savory mushrooms bathed in a delightful sauce and smartly complemented by pecorino cheese.

The chicken parmigiana was tasty and met expectations without much fanfare. The pappardelle with sausage was enjoyable, although the pasta didn’t quite hit the mark on texture - it came across a bit tough. 

All in all, if you find yourself craving Italian and happen to be around 10th Ave, this spot is worth a visit, especially for that bruschetta.

Title: A Brunch Delight with Fantastic Happy Hour Deals

If you're in the neighborhood and craving a solid brunch with the bonus of affordable drinks, this spot is worth checking out. The brunch menu shines with offerings like the flavorful omelet packed with chorizo and peppers. Though the steak tacos might come across as petite, they're nicely paired with the traditional rice and beans side, making for a fulfilling meal.

What sets this place apart is their happy hour—margaritas and a selection of drinks are just $5 each during brunch hours, which is quite a steal. Service here is efficient and friendly, and if you arrive post-lunch rush around 3pm on a Sunday, you'll likely score a seat easily as the restaurant is only half full.

Do note, the ambiance seems to pick up in the evening, so if you're looking for a quieter dining experience, earlier might be better. Overall, it's a solid choice for brunch that won't disappoint—definitely give it a try if you're in the area.

I've never been to a dim sum place that rolls around the food in carts and stops by each table with fresh food. I personally like this a lot because you're not really sitting around waiting for your food after you order. However, this is dangerous if you eat with your eyes, and don't realize how much you've been eating until you're really full! The food not only looked delicious but tasted really good as well. I think my favorite out of all of them was the salted egg bun. I wouldn't say this is the cheapest dim sum place I've eaten at but prices are decent for good quality food. Between 4 people we got 9 different dishes and without tip and tax paid ~$15. The only downside about these carts is not knowing which cart has the kind of food you're looking for. Luckily, the staff is pretty good, if you ask multiple times, about directing the carts with the item you're looking for towards you.

It really doesn't look like much, and the entrance is downstairs, but the food seriously tasted great. When I checked in on yelp, I also got a free thai iced tea by ordering an appetizer! The iced tea was super creamy and sweet, which was great. I absolutely loved the original roti we got for the appetizer. It was probably my favorite dish of the meal. The roti was light, fluffy, and chewy at the same time. The curry we dipped it in was super flavorful too. For the mains, we ordered fried Hainanese chicken over rice and an egg noodle dish that started with Penang but I do not remember the entire name. The portions were very large so it was a great value deal. The chicken was very flavorful and tender, and the rice had oil dripped over it, but it didn't taste overly oily. The noodles were pretty good: I mean I always love eating noodles, but they weren't the star of the meal.

I stopped in here with a coworker for lunch. We were in the area for a meeting and it started pouring, so we decided to stop in to grab food but also to seek reprieve from the rain. I've always wanted to try Rosa Mexicano, so it was a win- win for me. For our appetizer we ordered the empanadas! They were so delicious that we ended up placing a second order. The meat and cheese combo is perfect the dough of the empanada was light and crispy. For my entree, I ordered the fish tacos. I love a good fish taco so I definitely wanted to try these. The fish tacos were really good! , I only ate one because I was full from the empanadas but I was definitely pleased with my dish. I ended up taking the rest home and they were still good on the second round. Oh...I can't forget my street corn! I also ordered the street corn which I didn't realize was off the cob. At first, I was a bit annoyed because I actually like eating on the cob, but I was pleasantly surprised. They street corn was very good and still had the flavors that I was expecting. It was certainly a good choice for a quick lunch. Four stars only because it took a while for a server to take our order once we were seated.

Title: A Slice of Suprema's Best

As a frequent diner at Suprema, located conveniently near Penn Station, I can attest to their exemplary New York-style pizza. Particularly the Meat Lovers and Suprema pizzas are my go-tos, boasting fresh ingredients and a remarkably tasty red sauce. Despite the lunchtime rush, service remains swift, ensuring a quick turnover for seating. The staff is amiable, and cleanliness is clearly a priority. For anyone seeking to indulge in some of the finest pizza New York City has to offer, Suprema should be at the top of your list.

Good place to get ramen, but I wish they have a vegetarian option. All the broth for the ramen is meat based. For this reason I was only able to have the rice, which was pretty good. I went with two carnivores and they liked everything they ordered. The place is always busy and usually there is a 10-15 min wait. @traveleen_gurl

I recently dined at a restaurant where, unfortunately, I had a concerning experience with the bill. After leaving what I thought was a generous 19% tip, I noticed that the server, Viet, had increased the tip amount on my card without my authorization. While I can't confirm if this was intentional or a mistake, it's a serious issue that needs addressing. Patrons should always double-check their statements for discrepancies.

Oh my god. It's been 12 hours and I still can't stop thinking about the Whole Fish Red Snapper with Spicy Basil Sauce. My god. It was so good. Honestly life changing. For $29 it is the most expensive item on the menu and still a bargain for this quality and presentation in this city. The place is small but efficient at getting people in and out. Service was quick and friendly. Just look at the other reviews. Don't think twice. If you want the best Thai in a city chock full of Thai joints. Just come here!

Navigating the late-night hunger pangs, I ventured to Bread and Butter despite reservations stoked by not-so-rave reviews from coworkers. Opting for safety, I ordered the chicken Parmesan panini, which set me back almost $10. Regrettably, the price didn't correspond with quality, as the panini was disappointingly not made fresh.

Finding a restroom in NYC can be a challenge, leading us to discover a new dining spot purely by necessity. In an attempt to be courteous patrons, we ordered takeout and tea before using the facilities. Regrettably, the service we experienced lacked warmth and efficiency, with an unexpectedly lengthy wait. When we finally settled in to enjoy our meal, disappointment ensued. The takeout, particularly the egg rolls, was disappointingly greasy and overall unsatisfactory. While our primary need was met, the culinary side of the experience left much to be desired.

Title: A Fair Bloom at Park Avenue

My recent visit to Park Avenue was met with high expectations, intrigued by their promising Spring menu. Although the concept was enthralling, the culinary execution fell short of remarkable.

Service & Atmosphere (★★★★★): It's hard to fault Park Avenue here. With its soaring ceilings and sophisticated decor, the ambiance is a diners' delight, and the swift, professional service only amplifies the experience.

Value (★★★★☆): While not a budget-friendly spot, Park Avenue keeps its prices from soaring into the stratosphere, which is a feat in this upscale corner of New York City.

Food (★★★☆☆): My companion and I shared two appetizers and main courses, with the standout being the creatively wrapped coconut shrimp. However, the excitement tapered off with the less impressive crispy mussels and an overly buttery sweet corn agnolotti.

Return Potential (★★☆☆☆): New York City is a culinary playground with a plethora of options. Considering the plethora of extraordinary dining experiences available, a return to Park Avenue doesn't quite make it to the top of my list.

Overall, while Park Avenue wins points for service and ambiance, the cuisine fails to leave a lasting impression, leaving little excitement for future visits.

Title: A Flavorful Farewell to NYC at Distilled

As my culinary journey in NYC came to a close, Distilled was the delightful final stop. The restaurant's ambiance enchanted me, and although parking presented the typical urban challenge, it was a small price to pay for the experience that awaited inside.

The service was commendable; staff were attentive, and our food arrived swiftly. The standout dish was the bananas foster waffle, a harmonious blend of taste and texture, enhanced by a sauce that was nothing short of perfection. It was a reminder of why I love exploring food.

However, an adventurous detour to the bar led to a less pleasing discovery—a cocktail with a peculiar taste that prompted a puzzled online search. It turned out to include Cholula hot sauce, an ingredient I believe is better suited to food than a drink. The cocktail was underwhelming enough to send back, but it's a reminder to inquire about ingredients before diving in.

Despite the cocktail hiccup, Distilled left a positive mark, and I wouldn't hesitate to return. The lesson was learned, but the food was unforgettable.

Wow, where do I begin? The concept of this establishment is very creative; Pawn shop that sells beautiful vintage jewelry when you walk in, take a few steps going through another set of doors and you walk into a gorgeous restaurant. Chandeliers large plants dim lights the esthetic is on point. My friend and I came for restaurant week for an 11PM reservation. Did I say 11PM? This restaurant's latest reservation is 1AM which is a rare occurrence in the city. To continue restaurant week comes with a pre-fixe 3 course dinner menu for $42. We tried the tuna poke wonton tacos and Chile relleno empanadas for starts both were incredibly tasty. We also ordered off menu BBQ fries which were so damn good.  For the entrees we both had the grilled Atlantic salmon. One of us was going to order the sweet potato ravoli but the waitress did say it was small portioned. Nonetheless the salmon was BOMB and the pearl couscous was yummy. I'm not the biggest couscous fan but I did enjoy theirs. By then we were really full and forgot we had dessert on its way but we pushed through. The LES NYC Doughnuts were really good dipping sauces were very sweet though, and the apple pie milkshake shot was tasty but it was really sweet. Those who have a sweet tooth these items are for you. We spent $60 pp after taxes and gratuity. Normally it would've been more. We had an amazing time at Beauty& Essex and I can't wait to come back with a bigger group of friends for dinner and maybe even for their Beauty Parlor Sunday Brunch.

I love Ivan Ramen. And I've eaten a lot of ramen in my life. The chicken paitan with an added garlic bomb will make you rethink what a bowl of soup should taste like. I love the texture of the rye noodles Ivan invented. The Slurp shop was great because there was absolutely no line, which is exactly how I prefer my lunch. But I did really miss the appetizers that are only available at the other location. If you haven't already, Make sure you watch the Netflix Episode of Chef's Table on Ivan Ramen before you go. It really adds to the experience.

Title: Quick Noodle Fix in Hell's Kitchen

Tucked away within the bustling streets of NYC's Hell's Kitchen, I stumbled upon this small, yet quintessentially New York, noodle spot. The seating is cozy, ensuring you're elbow-to-elbow with fellow diners—a necessary compromise for a taste of their offerings.

The ambiance provides a slice of entertainment: choose to face the kitchen and be mesmerized by the hand-pulling noodle artistry, or face the front to indulge in a visual feast of food videos and Japanese cartoons.

Service is brisk, teetering on the edge of curt, but understandably so—there's a perpetual queue of hungry souls eager for a seat.

The fare, however, is where this eatery shines. My party of four dove into a smorgasbord of dim sum, sampling delectable steamed pork soup buns, succulent pan-fried shrimp and pork dumplings, and the standout scallion pancakes with sliced beef, among others. The highlight was undoubtedly the ramen—the vegetable, spicy beef, and shrimp with dao xiao noodles provided a comforting warmth, with the latter offering a much-needed respite from the heat.

We capped off the meal with the comforting Sweet Babao Rice dessert, a symphony of rehydrated fruits mingling with sticky rice.

A word to the wise: keep an eye out for the subtly included 15% gratuity on the bill—a small-print footnote on the menu easy to miss amidst the culinary excitement.

In all, if you're seeking a rapid reprieve from the city's chaos with a side of savory satisfaction, this Hell's Kitchen haunt is a sure bet. Just remember to check your bill with care!

Title: Great Drinks, Lackluster Fare at [Restaurant Name]

Review:
My dining experience at [Restaurant Name] was a mixed bag. Considering the price point, my expectations were higher for their fish and chips. Unfortunately, both our dishes fell flat - the fries arrived cold and the fish lacked any noteworthy flavor. On the positive side, our beverages were a delight, particularly a pina colada-like concoction whose name escapes me, but it was undeniably delicious. Service was another high note, with our server Bowers providing exceptional attention. I'd recommend stopping by for their refreshing drinks, but you might want to consider dining elsewhere. Solid three stars for the service and drinks alone.

Came here for their restaurant week promotion! Overall the meat was seasoned very well, and the ambiance of the restaurant was nice. We had a reservation at 6:15pm on a Monday, and the place didn't get really crowded until later that evening.I got the fried chicken appetizer, bulgogi main, and the banana cream dessert. There was a slight mixup in the orders, where I was brought out a different appetizer at first, but the waiter quickly addressed this and it was corrected within no time. The fried chicken was fantastic! There were 4 pieces, which I thought was quite a lot for only an appetizer which was great. The bulgogi had a good flavor, and my only downside is that the grill was quite small, so my two friends and I could only really put down one piece of meat when we were cooking.

I really enjoy sauces, and was told that by CHLOE has the best ketchup. I was not disappointed! I wasn't too hungry so only tried the sweet potato fries and sauces and the pesto pasta. The fries were standard, but definitely worth it to get them to try the aioli and beet ketchup! The latter's got the tart-sweetness of typical ketchup but the flavor's dominantly beet; truly a genius creation. The pesto was actually kind of heavy. There's a good amount of texture, specifically crunch, to it, and I especially appreciated the choice in pasta. It was quite crowded when I went pre-quarantine, but the staff's great and efficient. Overall think it's a great spot to grab a pretty healthy and filling bite in a casual setting.

Upon visiting the restaurant with the expectation of a broader menu, the selection was disappointingly confined primarily to desserts. Opting for the Matcha Egg Waffle and my companions selecting the Beauty Salad, we found the flavors to be quite standard, failing to justify the premium charges. The eatery's design is undeniably photogenic, boasting neon signs and charming decor that suggests a potential variance in satisfaction based on menu choices. Unfortunately, our experience was marred by a lack of warmth in service; interactions with the waitstaff were awkward and lacked the friendliness that can turn a meal into a memorable occasion.

Title: A Genuine Taste of Taiwan at The Braised Shop

My quest for authentic Taiwanese noodles led me to The Braised Shop, a gem for anyone looking to indulge in customizable Taiwanese culinary delights. The promise of a free noodle base via Yelp check-in was a delightful bonus, making the experience that much more enticing.

I chose a satisfying mix of broccoli, seaweed, tofu skin, and dried tofu, while my husband's bowl brimmed with an assortment of toppings like braised egg, tofu skin, and okra - each accentuated by the aromatic touch of scallions and garlic. The noodles themselves were flawlessly al dente, or "cui" as we say, striking the perfect balance of chewiness.

We appreciated the fresh, high-quality ingredients that filled our bowls, perfectly portioned for a mid-day meal. The Braised Shop’s limited seating and simple decor contributed to an unpretentious, cozy dining atmosphere, suitable for a low-key lunch or a casual dinner.

While The Braised Shop’s offerings may not eclipse all competitors in the East Village, their noodles are undoubtedly heartening and fairly priced. Will this be a repeat destination for us? Unlikely. But do we regret our visit? Not in the slightest. It was a welcome taste of Taiwan that we were pleased to savor.
Such An amazing Thai place went here for takeaway and got the green curry with shrimp it was delicious everyone very courteous thankful for these lovely restaurants during these difficult time!

Title: A Cozy Italian Gem Worth Every Bite

Upon my visit to this quaint Italian oasis in the heart of the city, I was charmed by its snug yet welcoming ambiance. The culinary journey was exceptional, with the pasta special, a sublime lobster spaghetti, stealing the show. Do yourself a favor—order it.

The grilled octopus deserves applause, boasting a perfect char that gives way to tender succulence, embodying a fusion of smokiness and oceanic zest. Complementing the meal, the creamy burrata left no doubt why it reigns as a crowd favorite.

Attention to detail is evident in the handcrafted pasta's impeccable texture, revealing the authenticity of their craft. Staff service mirrored the quality of the meal—attentive and warm. This establishment has etched a spot on my list of must-visit eateries, and I'm eager to explore the rest of their menu offerings on a future visit.
Definitely a hidden gem. The ramen was cooked to perfection. The avocado added an interesting texture. The egg was phenomenal. This place met my expectation.

Title: A Playful Omakase Experience at Ishikawa

Last Monday, my dining adventure at Ishikawa proved to be quite the delightful experience. What sets this place apart is the chefs' interactive and jovial manner, which adds a layer of fun to the dining experience. They're not just skilled at their craft, but also possess a knack for keeping diners entertained.

The omakase menu itself is a visual treat, with each course presenting itself as a tiny work of art that's bound to grace many Instagram feeds. It's playful and unconventional, a real treat for those who appreciate a modern twist on sushi. The service is attentive; our waiter was consistent in checking on us and took the time to explain each course.

Despite it being a Monday, the restaurant buzzed with energy, a testament to its popularity. For the best experience in the winter, I recommend securing the first counter seating to avoid delays, as adding on extra pieces can slow service down. 

Be aware that if you're a purist seeking a traditional omakase, Ishikawa might not meet your expectations. This is a place for those who relish contemporary flair, like a bit of truffle or enjoy their fish with a touch of sear. While the fish was satisfactory, the frequent use of Maine uni wasn't quite to my taste.

The presentation across the board was impeccable, although the chawanmushi did fall a bit flat on flavor and could benefit from some enhancement.

In summary, Ishikawa offers a vibrant, modern take on omakase which my friends, and now I, truly enjoyed. It's a spot for those looking to depart from the conventional and dive into a more playful gastronomic experience.

Cute new place in the Nomad area. Walked on the later side of lunch (1pm) and yet there was a little line going. Lost of people picking up via MealPal or Ritual. One thing I noted here is the protein comes pre-marinated 'Hawaiian style'. You have the option of pre-made bowls or BYOB. The byob list featured 6 proteins (main ones being tuna, salmon, surprisingly sesame chicken, some 'catch of the day' and of course tofu). No octupus on the list, which I really wanted. I went for a premade bowl, the Big Kahuna. It had a mixed of tuna and salmon poke, additionally the yuzu salmon poke and firecracker tuna, a bit of crab salad on top. I found both fishes to be fresh and delicious. I chose brown rice and marinated kale as bases. Liked the kale much better, the rice was a tad on the hard side. Their most expensive (14.50)  and filling poke bowl. I wish it came in the shortie (smaller) size since I didn't come in super hungry. Staff was very friendly. Overall a good experience.

Title: A Stellar Meal with Room for Improvement

My recent dining experience at a renowned three Michelin Star restaurant was thoroughly enjoyable, though it fell slightly short of extraordinary. The culinary journey was highlighted by the best duck I've ever savored, and the wagyu beef was an absolute delight. However, the fish dishes and desserts left me underwhelmed and longing for more.

Due to dietary restrictions, I was unable to partake in their shellfish offerings, which could very well be the stars of their menu. I couldn't help but compare the service unfavorably to that of other elite establishments such as Le Bernardin and Per Se. The staff's hurried explanations diminished my understanding and appreciation of the fare, and not receiving a menu until the meal's conclusion was an unwelcome surprise.

In sum, while the restaurant serves up some exceptional dishes, particularly the duck, the overall experience did not quite live up to the high standards set by its peers in the same echelon.

Title: A Winning Combo of Sports, Views, and Fine Eats!

Review:

We recently visited a delightful bar/restaurant that was an absolute hit with our group. As sports enthusiasts, we were thrilled with the atmosphere, complete with TVs showcasing the latest games, which set an upbeat tone for the evening.

Our culinary journey kicked off with intriguing starters: frog legs and a beautifully prepared tartare. Moving on to the main course, we sampled the steak, salmon, and chicken, each dish resonating with flavor and expertly cooked to our satisfaction.

An unexpected surprise was the stunning view of the Empire State Building, best appreciated from the restaurant's restroom corridor, adding a touch of New York charm to the experience.

Overall, the place struck a perfect balance between a casual sports bar vibe and a commitment to quality dining. We're already looking forward to our next visit. Definitely a spot worth returning to!

Yes. Worth the wait & worth the hype.Korean-style tapas.Quiet, yet trendy. You'll feel cozy but able to enjoy each other's conversation.All dishes we tried were excellent. Even desserts, which sometimes can disappoint in Asian restaurant.

Eh. 2.75 stars. Why? Ever have one of those moments where you have 2 beers with a friend while you are waiting for orchestra practice to start near union square and then realize you're drunk and haven't eaten anything and you don't want to spend money but you have 3 hours of violin practice ahead of you? No? It's just me. Awkward pause. Well I yelp searched 'dollar pizza' near union square and went here assuming it was dollar pizza. It was not. It was like $2.95 a slice pizza. 2 plain cheeses/soda (I don't drink soda unless there is alcohol in it so this is irrelevant to me) for $5.95 deal. I decided to go with a pepperoni slice and it cost me almost $4. And this was when I intended on spending only a dollar for dinner. The slice in itself - was okaaaaay. It was greasier than most and just tasted and felt still like a dollar slice. Next time I'm screwed over as far as food goes before practice I probably would be seeking out other options.

minigrow is a great concept - unique because the vegetable spaghetti isn't a huge thing yet and people are too lazy to do it on their own, and very healthy toppings to go along with it. I generally get the zucchini noodles with salmon, and all the included toppings, like the chickpeas, carrots, kimchi, cherry tomatoes, broccoli, corn, and lemon squeeze. The price is very high for what you're getting, but it makes sense, as it's midtown and it takes physical labor to make these noodles. Still, they should keep in mind that you can get so much more right down the street at other healthy fast casual places for the same price, and be much more full. I do like how their menu by the line includes calories, but I doubt it's accurate as what the server gives you varies enormously each time. Some improvements I'd suggest are to stop hiding the extra toppings towards the end, like the cashews, by the cashier, and to hire actually friendly people for your store. I've gone time and time again, and they get worse and worse as time goes on. The big manager dude is so rude, and I've also encountered a few other guys who work here who are just nasty. One last point is to stop being so frugal when it comes to protein. People are paying extra for it, so give us an actual piece bigger than two ounces! Yes, I've literally weighed the protein portion, so I know what I'm talking about! FYI, no bathroom, outlets, or WiFi here.

This was a so-so tapas experience. The strawberry sangria was very tasty but the food was just okay. The flavors were not that intense and everything was very buttered up. I liked the cozy feel of the restaurant and fast service. Our food came out pretty quickly.I tried:-Sparkling Strawberry -Chipirones Fritos (calamari)-Banderillas Con Chorizo De Pato (duck sausage skewers)-Langistinos (prawns)-SpinachAll the dishes came out at the same time and they were nothing to write home about. I was still hungry at the end of our meal.When I came in to ask for a table the staff seemed flustered and gave me a 25 minute wait time. Shortly after, a couple came in after me and was also given the same time but then seated before me.

Title: A Satisfactory First Visit to Xi'an

My initial visit to Xi'an left a very favorable impression, primarily due to its convenient take-out setup and the flavorsome offerings. Opting for N9, the spicy noodle with pork, I found myself savoring every bite of the succulent, chewy noodles entangled with nicely spiced ground pork. The balance of spices and seasonings was spot-on, enhancing the overall experience without overwhelming the palate. Priced around $10, the dish felt like a value for money indulgence. Based on this positive experience, I am eager to return and explore more of their noodle dishes and burgers. Xi'an has certainly earned a repeat customer in me.

It is difficult to make a reservation here so prepare yourself for a rather lengthy wait. Stopped by another local bar for drinks to pass the time. We waited over 2 hours.When I saw the name of the place, I was super skeptical. However, my friend told me it was Michelin guide recommended and she'd been dying to try it for some time now but never had the patience to wait.We got the rotisserie chicken. And it was this night that I realized every other rotisserie chicken I've ever eaten was dry. How did they get it that moist? I literally did not even think this level of juicy was even a feasible characteristic of rotisserie chicken? Mind. Blown.We also ordered the Khao Soi - vegetarian. I was super skeptical but holy shit this really blew it out of the water. I was convinced I would be okay with it but really, its worth it. Vegetarian or not.Kind of wish I had saved room for dessert because I have no doubt it would be anything short of phenomenal. Will have to come back for sure.

I am such a fan of this place and I wish I can have more as I am writing this review. They make rice rolls which are rolls filled with different toppings. We got the curry and pork. They were so chewy and perfectly cooked. You can see them making it fresh to order, which was so fun and cool. I love how they taste with the soy sauce. I liked the pork better than the curry. The curry came with fishballs which was interesting and tasted delicious. The place is tiny, so it was hard to claim a seat, but we ended up getting one last minute. All in all, a great place to go for a snack or a meal.

We visited on a Saturday evening.  It was very busy and we were lucky to get seats for 7.  The waitress was very helpful and quickly got us a table setup.  The place is your typical bar atmosphere, loud, busy, music and friendly.  Our meals were good. I would say nothing above average however no complaints. As busy as they were their staff was friendly and eager to help.  They were in constant contact with drink refills and making sure our food was good. Pretty cool atmosphere and a neat local hangout.  I'm glad we made this a stop.

Really 3.5. It is on the backside of port authority so going there in the dark might be a little sketch. The service was solid, but it might be because we were sitting at 5:00 before the small place filled up. The pizzas were all fresh and tasty. They used a real wood burning brick oven which creates a great char taste. I recommend the burrata and focaccia for apps. The wine list is limited so don't expect much for a $40 bottle. It worked for a pre theatre dinner but was pricey relative to location and servings.

Title: A Novel Noodle Nook with a Side of Silence

If you've ever fantasized about a ramen rendezvous designed for introverts, this restaurant with its private booths aims to transform that dream into a reality. The concept is intriguing, promising an immersive culinary journey free from the usual hubbub. However, in practice, the not-so-high partitions mean you might still catch snippets of your neighbor's conversations.

The restaurant champions simplicity with a sole focus on a classic tonkotsu ramen – a boon for the indecisive. Yet, the execution, while tasty, isn't groundbreaking. The ramen is decent with chashu, scallions, garlic, and a spicy red sauce contributing to a familiar flavor profile. At $18.90 a bowl sans tax, the portions are modest and might leave your wallet feeling lighter than expected—unless you splurge on a toppings bundle for an additional $5.

Where the establishment truly shines is in its premium yakibuta offering. The pork is exceptionally tender and flawlessly seasoned, and despite an initial sticker-shock for $10 extra, it’s a standout item that justifies its price tag.

Although the restaurant presents a novelty and the yakibuta is a must-try, the overall experience and value proposition don't inspire a repeat visit. It's worth a one-time adventure for those curious about the setup, but when it comes to ramen, there are other venues that offer more bang for your buck.

I wasn't completely blown away by the food here, but it was certainly very satisfactory and very affordable for midtown. I work a block away, but only visited for the first time on Saturday... Seems like I've been missing out on the awesome lunch specials! I feel like I don't eat Indian enough to judge the authenticity of the food, but I'd consider it that.Around 5pm, our party of 3 was seated immediately. Cozy vibes. Definitely got busier (and darker) by the time we left, with a few people waiting for tables. We got the free basket of naan (courtesy of yelp check-in) which paired well with the Chicken Korma ($16). The chicken korma tasted like standard curry to me ... whatever that means lol. Maybe we should've gotten it a tad spicier, but it was a good, typical comfort dish.You bet we ordered the garlic naan ($3.50) as well -- it is of course the go-to, must-order. Did not disappoint! And I might have burned my tongue a bit from the vegetable samosa ($3) but it was worth it. Would like to try the lamb/pea one next time! No complaints about the mango lassi ($4) - refreshing and delicious, as it should be. Lastly, the Lamb Biryani ($17) was just *chef's kiss* -- this was plenty of food to share between 3 people, and I'd return for lunch to satisfy any future Indian cravings!

I love how this place feels so family style and that the staff here are so kind! My friend and I probably occupied a table for 15-20 minutes before our friend came but they never tried to hurry us or ask about our friend.The food was also very good and tasted more home cooked like, which is great if you're concerned about health. A great spot for Korean food if you're near Chinatown and don't want to travel up to Ktown!IG: @phothegram

Have been to 10 Corso Como twice and we love it. Awesome pasta dishes, a great vibe with wonderful service in a beautiful space. Desserts are great, as are the cocktails and the wine selections are excellent at all price points. Go to 10 Corso Como, relax and have a wonderful meal. Mangia! Enjoy!!

Title: A South Indian Delight That Hits Close to Home

During a recent bout of craving for some authentic home-cooked South Indian flavors, I found myself at a charming little restaurant that promised just that and delivered wonderfully. To kick things off, I indulged in the samosa chaat, which was a delightful precursor to the main event. Both the paper dosa and coconut rava masala dosa were not only delectable but also surprisingly affordable, making this eatery a must-visit for those who appreciate value as much as taste.

My only quibble was that despite requesting an extra kick of spice, the dishes fell a tad short on the heat scale for my palette. However, this minor setback couldn't overshadow the clean environs and the commendable service provided by the staff. It's safe to say that my search for authentic South Indian cuisine has a new checkpoint. I am already looking forward to my next visit.

Pat'e Palo Bar & Grill truly elevates the brunch experience, ensuring that "adulting" feels like a treat rather than a chore. The ambiance of this pristine spot sets the stage for a fantastic brunch, where the mimosas and sangrias are as delightful as the food is delectable. Their appetizer soup impressed, and the service was nothing short of excellent. Plus, the transformation at night is not to be missed – the place becomes absolutely lit. A definite must-visit for brunch enthusiasts and night owls alike.

Title: A Bustling Spot for Burrito Lovers

My sister and I hit up this popular eatery post-work and despite the crowd, we snagged a seat thanks to her early arrival. We dove into their jerk and BBQ chicken burritos alongside chips with salsa, and topped it off with a frozen margarita—though I suspect it was guava instead of mango due to its pink hue.

Service was swift; the food arrived promptly. The burritos, generous in size, conquered our appetites to the point of surrender, with half destined for a to-go box. The BBQ chicken packed a heat punch I found intense (fair warning for fellow spice-averse diners), but my sister disagreed, finding it just right. As for the jerk chicken burrito, it was a flavorful delight that we sadly couldn't finish in one sitting.

The salsa and chips were a crunchy, satisfying pair, and the margarita, mistaken flavor and all, was a refreshing companion.

Verdict: Heartily recommended for their hefty, tasty burritos and a chilled frozen margarita that's ideal for unwinding after a long day.

Warm, fun, professional, kind- this place has it all. I really enjoyed my dinner (try the black spaghetti, yummmmmmmyy). The bartenders, waiter & waitresses and hosts- all very lovely people who make you feel like you are at home. The olive oil cake was delicious. I'll definitely be coming back.

Title: A Mixed Experience at a Cozy Bar

My friends and I made a spontaneous decision to grab drinks at this little spot after dinner nearby. We cozied up to the bar area, which had a welcoming vibe with great music in the background. I took a sip of the Spicy Margarita my friends recommended, but quickly found it overpowering for my taste buds – it's definitely meant for those who can handle the heat. Switching to the regular Margarita, I found solace in its classic, well-executed flavor.

The service here deserves a shout-out; attentive and friendly, making sure our experience at the bar was smooth. However, there's one pressing issue that the establishment needs to address – the temperature. It felt like a sauna inside, and without adequate cooling like fans or a stronger AC, it was uncomfortably warm which detracted from the overall experience. It's a shame; with better climate control, this quaint location would be quite the gem for a casual drink.

Title: A Whopper of a Burrito at Zaragoza - A Worthwhile Gamble for Your Appetite

If ever there was a call to culinary arms for the hungry and daring, it's the three-meat burrito at Zaragoza. This isn't a place for the faint of heart or small of stomach. Tucked into a tiny space that somehow manages to accommodate "big" tables, Zaragoza offers a laid-back atmosphere with nominal table service and a selection of beers to wash down your feast.

For $13, the three-meat burrito is an investment that pays off in flavor and Instagram glory. Topped with a trio of sauces that mimic the Mexican flag, it's as photogenic as it is hefty. On our visit, the burrito was loaded with steak, chicken, and carnitas – a delightful surprise that offers a different taste with each visit. Just steer clear of the chips; they don't match the burrito's high bar.

After losing a bet, which led to a hefty order of six burritos, chips, and beers, the total came out to a very reasonable $85 – tipping generously, you're still looking at around $100. And while they offer a four-meat burrito for $15, only the bravest souls dare to go beyond the already overflowing three-meat option.

The staff at Zaragoza are the cherry on top – friendly and welcoming, they make the dining experience all the more pleasant. So if you're ready to challenge your appetite and don't mind leaving with the feeling of near explosion, Zaragoza's burrito is calling your name. Just remember, during these times, to stay safe, avoid dangerous health advice, and perhaps consider takeout to help flatten the curve!

Ok. Adding this to my growing list of nyc ramen baes. I did not expect how good this place was, but I am so happy I gave it a try. This review is actually for my second time there, same reaction both times. The restaurant is pretty small, and none of their chairs have backs so it's good for posture (?) but the ramen is WORTH. You can lineup before you get there on the yelp waitlist. Super handy and my friend and I got there almost right as we got seated (8 pm on Wednesday). I'm going to include reviews for the foods I got both times below-- Apps: Chicken wings - really good. great texture & juicyness, cant go wrongPork bun - we were sitting at the bar so I got to watch them make my pork buns. They blow torch them. Trust me this shit is so good. I saw them make a bbq pork bun also and wanted that too but it's okay my OG pork bun was really goodShitake bun - SO unami. such a good balance of flavours. I really like Shitake though so might be biasedEntrees: Pork bone - Really great broth, slightly on the rich side (personal preference) but it tasted fresh as well. Noodles have great consistency and the black oil on top is one of my fave ramen additions (real great smokey taste). Can't go wrong.Spicy Pork Bone - I can't handle spice so this was actually a bit too spicy for me, but it's not THAT bad. If you can't handle spice you can challenge yourself with this and not be disappointed. It's hot though. All of the good of the pork bone plus that spicy oil kick. Uni mushroom mazemen - I love broth so much, but this dry ramen blew me away. It is SO good. Uni is amazing, first of all but the strong truffle-y creaminess of the ramen mix killed me. Again, biased bc mushroom. My friend that I went with got this both times so testament to how great this place is. The place does a lot of take out so I'm jealous if you live nearby. Nowhere to put your bags / coat though so don't bring too much.

Such a relief that the food and experience was SO much better than last remembered- came here for late night HH of lychee martinis, beer, NY strip, garlic ribeye, garlic noodles, crispy tuna, and pork dumplings. Meats were tasty and well-seasoned; dumplings crispy (almost too crispy). Would be happy to be back! Tuna rectangles tasty but a bit too much rice for tuna ratio, rice lover that I am. Garlic noodles perfect texture of chewiness, served on hot plate. Loved!

Title: A Genuine Irish Vibe at The Dubliner

Nestled in the bustling environment of Stone Street, The Dubliner stands out as a quintessential Irish pub, promising an experience that holds true to its roots. Boasting an impressive selection of Jameson and other Irish whiskeys, this pub knows how to cater to those with a penchant for the spirited nuances of Ireland.

Come evening, the place buzzes with energy, particularly in summer when patrons spill out onto the cobblestone street under a tented area, beer in hand, adding to the vibrant streetscape. It's the perfect spot to soak in the lively atmosphere with a cool drink.

Speaking of drinks, the menu doesn't stray far from the traditional, featuring staples like Guinness on tap alongside some intriguing local brews. The whiskey selection is noteworthy, though be forewarned, some labels carry a hefty price tag. Nevertheless, a Jameson and ginger ale is a safe and affordable bet at $8.

On the culinary front, The Dubliner serves up the beloved, hearty fare expected of a pub, with a leaning towards the greasy and meaty – comfort food at its most authentic.

The interior presents a spacious and spotless setting, echoing the clean, classic feel of a well-kept pub. Service is quick and cordial, even when the bartender is caught up serving a crowd of regulars.

Be mindful that weekends here attract a throng, hinting at the potential pandemonium of their St. Patrick's Day celebrations. If you're seeking a truly Irish experience without crossing the Atlantic, The Dubliner is a bet worth making.

Title: A Flavorful Vegan Feast in the Heart of New York

I recently stumbled upon a delightful vegan restaurant during a stroll through New York. The extensive menu immediately caught my attention, prompting an impromptu dinner with my mother. We indulged in a variety of dishes including crispy spring rolls, a mango soy cutlet dinner special complete with fried rice, salad, and a particularly memorable steamed bun, as well as savory sautéed spinach noodles topped with crispy seitan.

The food was not only a treat to the taste buds but also remarkably inexpensive considering the generous portions. The mango-infused dinner special stood out with its rich flavor, while the steamed bun easily became the highlight of our meal. The seitan, with its crispy exterior, was a novel touch, although it received mixed reviews from us.

Regrettably, the service did not match the culinary experience. We faced delays in ordering and an asynchronous arrival of dishes, leading to a slightly cold main course. The wait for the check further prolonged our visit. Despite the bustling atmosphere of the restaurant providing some context for the service issues, there's room for improvement.

Nonetheless, the quality and value of the food make it a place I'd happily revisit when next in the neighborhood.

Title: The Go-To Happy Hour Haven Near Times Square

If you’re on the hunt for a post-work sanctuary offering solid happy hour specials, look no further. Our office favorite, nestled on the fringe of Times Square, hosts happy hour deals that are hard to resist: $8 frozen margaritas that pack a punch, $6 well drinks, and $4 house drafts.

The frozen margaritas are not just potent but also generously sized, ensuring you get more than your money's worth. It's one of the compelling reasons my colleagues and I are regulars!

Aside from the drinks, the food is noteworthy—indulge in the delightfully crispy fried pickles, the sinfully gooey mac and cheese balls, and the hearty nachos that offer more than enough to share. The vibe is incredibly laid-back, and with a spacious bottom floor, overcrowding is never an issue, making it ideal for group gatherings.

Service is consistently reliable, though it’s worth mentioning there's an odd credit card fee. Despite this minor quirk, the combination of great deals, tasty bites, and a chilled atmosphere makes this spot a winner for anyone looking to unwind after a long day at the office.

Not sure about the hype. The fried chicken was good, not great. It was crispy, but we had expectations for the flavors and were let down. We did a half and half medium combo. The flavors were okay, spicy wasn't very spicy, and there wasn't a crazy amount of meat on the pieces. We also got a Korean pancake with seafood. It as super greasy and undercooked. We probably won't head back.

Had a delightful lunch at Peach Mart recently. The Chicken Katsu sandwich and a stuffing special were satisfactory, but it was the Chicken Curry Sliders that stole the show—truly scrumptious. And don't get me started on the Peanut Butter Cookies; they were exceptional. The food court has ample seating, making for a comfortable dining experience right there. Highly recommend for a casual meal with some standout dishes!

Take a break. And why not take a fancy (fine dining) break?We have jump from one food place in the Hudson Yards to another checking what's on their menu. And we ended up in this grill. We went to a family style late lunch that includes a house salad, kid's grilled flatbread cheese pizza, buttermilk fried chicken, pasta with shrimp & basil and the vanilla ice cream that comes with the kid's.All of the food seems to be good. My daughter, I and my wife liked the texture and taste of the grilled flatbread pizza. The salad taste good as well but more of your typical salad you get in other "authentic" italian restaurant. The fried chicken seems to be salty for my taste and good thing it comes with a coleslaw and some veggies on the side to tone down its saltiness. The pasta is good as well and the shrimp was perfectly cooked. I did asked the waiter to bring some cheese to compliment the pasta. Ambiance is really nice. The low lighting, big beautiful wall arts, comfortable seats and tables, and kudos to the well-dressed, well-mannered ushers/usherettes, very attentive and courteous waiters and waitresses and the chefs, cooks abd staffs behind the scene. Keep up the good work.Looking forward to visit this place again.

Today in my visit  in New York I wanted to try out Da Gennaro Italian Restaurant   Maybe some where down the line we have family history within the name but the restaurant deserves the 5 stars hands down. Walked in off the street for two and was given this cute little table inside the restaurant with doors open to the patio. A great setting for dinner. The style of the establishment is well decorated old style charm.  Started off with some drinks. Gennaro fresh. Made with vodka cucumber and mint. Refreshing. Smoked manhatten was the next drink. Made with smoke bullit bourbon and bitters. Very good. We had a Freese salad with Gorgonzola and walnuts  dressed with a garlic vinaigrette. Amazing. Also had the mussels in a garlic wine sauce that came to the table in its own pot still steaming.  Absolutely incredible. The mrs. Had spaghetti con polpette   Very tasteful   Noodles perfectly light and cooked to perfection. The meatballs were charred just perfectly on the outside while the inner meatball was tender and flavorful mixed with fresh basil. I had the Lasagna Della. Baked in its own tray straight from the oven. Made with an amazing meat sauce and fresh mozzarella cheese. I gotta say. I was highly impressed with the meal.  I have tried many Italian places and compared to grandmothers dishes and this comes way close to home. We ended with a affogato and a pistachio coppa The espresso served with a scoop of vanilla cream was so delicious. The pistachio coppa  is an absolute must. I would have licked out the glass if I could. Lol. Excellent. Our wait staff was amazing. Valeria and Victor took such good care of us. Attentive. Great customer service. Great recommendations. A pleasure with conversation. Just made the whole dinner experience delightful. I will definitely make this a place to visit again when back in New York. Bon Appetit'
Banana walnut muffin was only ok, but the sausage and egg on croissant was amazing. You really can't go wrong with any of the hot food options here.

As someone who grew up in a household that made homemade dumplings every week, I have a bit of a hate love relationship with Mimi Cheng's. Their dumplings are delicious, but incredibly overpriced. I'd recommend going to check out their monthly collabs, which are usually done with chefs of other notable NYC establishments. These are often dumplings that have super interesting flavors and sometimes venture into the fusion realm. This location itself is a pretty small space that has seating for about 10-12 people on top of a communal table!

This is our go to prebroadway fuel up spot.  We like to arrive about two hours before our show.  We eat and drink than walk down broadway to kill time until the show starts.  Certainly the best Mexican food I have ever had and reasonable prices.Really like ordering the fajitas, cerviche, and octopus but you can't go wrong with any of the dishes (free chips are really tasty)We usually buy our parking with the best parking app and have it between the restaurant and our show between 8 and 9th to make it easy.Great pre-broadway spot for dinner

After opting to switch things up with MealPal, I visited this burger joint just ahead of the lunchtime rush. The ambiance was pleasantly laid-back, with only a couple of pairs nestled in the booths enjoying their meals. Service was prompt—the "The Standard" burger I ordered was ready for pick-up in no time.

This classic beef burger comes with American cheese, dill pickles, caramelized onions, and a special sauce, all sandwiched in a brioche bun. The eco-conscious will appreciate the paper wrapping—a nice, sustainable touch. On this visit, however, the beef patty fell short, proving a tad dry for my palate, though it didn't spoil the overall tasty experience. I've been here previously without this issue, so I'm chalking it up to an off day.

If you're curious about a decent burger, I'd still suggest giving this spot a shot—hopefully, your beef will be juicier!

Title: A Vibrant Brunch Spot with a Minor Glitch

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this lively and well-decorated restaurant for brunch on a whim, and I was not disappointed. Without a reservation, my companion and I snagged a pub-style table along the perimeter, which, although lacking a significant view, provided a pleasant atmosphere thanks to the bright decor and open air.

The highlight of our visit was undoubtedly the food and drinks. The Tres Leche French Toast was a stroke of genius, offering a delightful twist on a classic. The Eggs Benedict with shredded pork was equally impressive, as were the savory steak tacos. Each dish was a testament to the kitchen's culinary prowess.

To add to the ambiance, a DJ was on-site, delivering entertaining banter and setting the mood with a great selection of music. It was a delightful accompaniment to an already splendid meal.

However, it's worth mentioning a minor hiccup: the paint on the pub tables seemed to be chipping off, or perhaps melting, resulting in a stain on my companion's pants. Future patrons might want to exercise caution when seated at these tables.

Despite this small issue, the restaurant delivers a fantastic dining experience that I would recommend to anyone looking for a great brunch spot.

Can you imagine eating glazed bacon on Indonesian restaurant?! only in Wayan, this Indo-French restaurant tucked in the lovely neighborhood of NoHo has truly elevated Indonesian cuisine.We came here for brunch to entertain a visiting friend. The restaurant looks small but it was actually not as the layout is "train car" like long and narrow but if you prefer to be seated in front of restaurant, an advance reservation is recommended. Our group of 5 were seated at the front near the window that we enjoyed both the restaurant interior and the street view on a nice sunny day.The family style dining prompted us to order everything at onceThe dishes that we ordered are:1. Nasi Goreng with glazed bacon2. Avocado toast "Gado Gado"3. Corn fritters4. Salad Nicoise "Indonisiene"5. Lobster Noodles6. Mango and Cucumber salad7. Sate Chicken Bowl8. Extra glazed baconWe ordered extra salad as they ran out of chicken wings, a minus star for that (my mantra is; it better be available when it's on the menu). Special mentions to the Nasi Goreng with bacon and the Lobster noodles we felt that it stood out among the rest of the dishes. Over all it was a lovely experience and our server was super attentive and we are definitely considering coming to try out their dinner menu in the near future!

Visiting this eatery gave off a quintessential college dive bar vibe, yet it delivered a pleasant surprise with impressive fare and genial service. Despite the music being a mismatch for my taste, likely tailored for a private birthday bash upfront, it didn't overshadow the culinary experience. The fries arrived in a generous heap, the red wine was adequately satisfying, and the BBQ mushroom burger stood out with its mouthwatering flavors. A definite return is on the cards for me, albeit with a polite request for a quieter soundtrack.

During a recent visit to Food Gallery for a late lunch, I decided to try the kimchi fried rice with chicken from Hanok. Priced reasonably at about $12 after tax, the meal was served with a perfectly cooked egg on top, complemented by miso soup and kimchi on the side. The portion size was generous and certainly hit the spot for my fried rice craving. While I have preferred kimchi fried rice from other local sit-down restaurants, Hanok offers a convenient and delicious quick-service alternative that doesn't disappoint.

Small, clean and modern. Not a typical poke bar you would think since the ingredients are not layed out in front of you. Their menu is fixed although they have add-ons and substitutes. I ordered salmon with avacado, plantain chips and substituted rice with kale, yellow sauce on the side. Honestly,  the ingredients didn't go well together and tasted bland. I wish they have more vegetables substitutes or maybe just more veggies options... I'm not a sauce person but some alternative options would be nice. My friend didn't enjoy her tuna combo either said having pictures of items would be good references. The service was quick. Also, checking in on yelp gets you a free cup of house made tea.

Title: A Flight of Hits and Misses at a Local Ramen Spot

Heading into the restaurant with high hopes based on tantalizing menu descriptions, my experience proved to be a mixed bag. I visited with two friends, our appetites set for a promising feast.

The complimentary wings were the unexpected star of our meal - crispy and bathed in a light, sweet onion soy sauce, a dish I'd return for in a heartbeat. The edamame was standard fare, nothing to write home about. My anticipation for the katsu sandwich was met with disappointment; the tangy vinegary sauce failed to impress my palate.

My main course, the mentaiko cream ramen, was a letdown. The idea of garlic and mushrooms sounded perfect, yet the excess of cream smothered the potential complexity of flavors, leaving a bland impression punctuated only by jarring bites of large garlic pieces. This dish I'd willingly skip on future visits.

On the other hand, my friends had varying experiences - the Koku Ramen received a nod of approval, while the chicken shoyu was deemed forgettable due to its lack of flavor.

Service was passable, but the ambiance truly shone - providing a relaxed environment perfect for casual dining with friends. Despite some culinary missteps, the allure of those exceptional wings and the promise of Koku Ramen ensures that this spot will see me again.

TLDR: An underdog for great happy hour on a budget. Half off drinks. And a delicious chicken avocado bowl that hits the spot!Came here with friends after a short brunch. We were mainly looking for happy hour places in the area. This was by far open the earliest and most affordable happy hour in the area. In the end every single one of us found something we enjoyed. We each got 3 dollar Sapporo beers. They didn't taste as nice as fresh from the bottle so maybe we'd try a different beer next time. Another thing we got were sake drinks. One was mixed with lychee the other was mixed with peach. It was basically sake, a flavored syrup, and seltzer? (I forgot). Those drinks were 4 dollars.In addition we saw these really tempting chicken teriyaki avocado bowls. A picture of it is shown. The bottom is mostly rice but it's filled with lots of chicken teriyaki and avocado. Since we all ate earlier, a friend and I split it and felt super full after. The chicken is crispy and very savory because it was fried. The avocado added a good amount of creaminess and the teriyaki complimented everything. In terms of ambience it is decorated like a village on the inside. On tv there was some interesting  stuff to say the least: on one tv was a man eating hundreds of dumplings and on the other was a street food show. It definitely entertained us for some time. We had a lot of good laughs and had a great time.  We even had a few friends stop by too, and the servers did not mind the extra people in our party.Overall, I would come here again and try the different drinks. For half off, you can't go wrong. I'd get the chicken avocado bowl again (in fact I'm salivating just thinking about it). It's a great place to hang out with friends after work. And with the winter season upon us, I want to go back and try some of their ramen

Le Sia is amazing, and I'm so excited they've opened a location in Midtown! They're known for their seafood boils, but I thought the highlight was actually their excellent skewers. They have online ordering for take-out and delivery on their website (free delivery on orders $50+).I tried a bunch of skewers and a few other dishes here, and my favorites were:-Dough drop and assorted vegetable soup ($13.95) - thick soup with tomato, eggs, vegetables, and cooked dough (think the dumplings in chicken dumpling soup, but smaller and slightly scrambled). Delicious and comforting, perfect to hunker down at home with amidst the current chaos :/-Pork trotters ($3.50) - extremely delicious pig feet, chewy and cartilaginous and amazing. I would honestly order extras of these to eat the next day.-King oyster mushroom skewer ($2 each)-Pork intestine skewers ($2 each) - crispy and fatty :)-Baked Chinese bread skewers ($2 each) - crispy seasoned mantou slices-Lamb skewers ($1.50 each)The crawfish ($16.99/lb) was also good but not as great as the skewers, but I think their seafood would also travel well.Some comments about dining in (maybe not so relevant now :/ ): service is exceptionally attentive and nice. As an additional plus, the bathrooms are really clean and have Listerine in case you want to get rid of your seafood breath after eating.

Title: A Perfect Spot for a Bachelorette Bash!

My sister's bachelorette party at this gem of a restaurant was an absolute delight, thanks to the meticulous planning by Zach, the event coordinator. The private space we were allocated was both cozy and chic, with a fire pit, plush couches, and a beautifully set long table just for us.

Service was impeccable – quick to clear and eager to please, keeping our wine glasses full and our appetizer plates refreshed. Every bite was sumptuous, a testament to the kitchen's prowess.

Although our booking was slated to end at 10:30 PM, the staff graciously allowed us to bask in the revelry until midnight, securing our privacy by cordoning off the area. It's rare to find such accommodating service!

In summary, gorgeous ambiance, top-notch service, and delectable cuisine made for an unforgettable evening. Highly recommended for anyone looking to host a special event!

My dining experience the other evening was delightful, kicked off with dollar blue point oysters that offered both excellent value and flavor. The grilled eggplant starter impressed with its perfectly executed taste. We continued to be pleased with the cheese ravioli, a harmonious blend of ricotta and spinach complemented by a light, flavorful sauce. The lobster ravioli didn't disappoint either, packed with plenty of taste. Eager to explore more of the menu, I'll certainly be returning. The service was another high point—friendly and efficient.

Title: Perfect Valentine's Date Night at a Steal

My partner and I decided to celebrate Valentine's Day at this gem of a restaurant and it did not disappoint. We made our reservation through OpenTable well before the date, anticipating a crowd. Opting for the Meat Lovers Special for two, we were struck by the exceptional value - just $65 for a veritable feast. The special included two soups, two salads, a generous helping of white rice, and an unexpected bonus of fried chicken. But the highlight was the five different meats for the grill, perfect for those who love to cook together. Our meal concluded sweetly with s'mores for dessert.

The service took our experience to the next level. The attentive staff seamlessly changed out our grill grate without us having to ask, ensuring our meats cooked perfectly throughout the evening. It's rare to find such proactive and thoughtful service. The staff's dedication truly made our date night special. Highly recommended for a fun, affordable, and impressively served dining experience.

Title: Quick and Casual Korean Eats in Midtown

If you're darting through midtown in search of a speedy, wallet-friendly bite, this Fast Casual Korean spot might just hit the spot. My key piece of advice: specify how you want your egg in the bibimbap.

Service (5/5): A return visit here revealed a refreshing improvement in service. Communication was seamless, especially with an English-speaking staff member at the register around noon. They were attentive to my order preferences, quickly rectifying a minor egg mix-up in my bibimbap with no fuss.

Ambiance (3/5): This isn't the place for large gatherings; seating caters more to solo diners or small groups. It's compact and functional - clean up after yourself and don't linger for a crowd-free experience.

Food (3/5): The Spicy Pork Hot Stone Bibimbap ($13) serves up a decent meal. It's sizzling hot, offering that sought-after crispy rice, but the pork could use a punchier marinade. Note that without a generous dollop of gochujang, the dish might lack zest. Portions are generous, ensuring a full stomach for under $20.

Final Thoughts: While it's not gourmet, and the flavors might not rival your favorite Ktown haunt, it's a solid choice for a quick lunch. They also offer enticing incentives like free sodas for a Yelp review and potential Groupon deals. 

Verdict: Worth a drop-in when time and budget are of the essence, just remember to clear your table and clarify your egg preferences!

The newly resurrected Pastis is already so much better than the old Pastis (different location & menu & management) ever was. It's the same concept, extensively authentic & obsessively detailed, but it's so much more spacious & comfortable, while also being much more relevant when it comes to seasonal ingredients and beautiful preparations. Don't get me wrong, I "grew up" in Pastis (as well as Spice Market & Florent, Lotus & APT) in the early 2000s. Some of my most fond(led) memories were created down the street at The Lure & Hell, or around the corner at J's Hangout, and nothing ever ended a wild evening quite as lovingly as their legendary peppery 'burger; but, honestly, every single aspect of the new Pastis blows the old Pastis out of the water, and this is the only restaurant in this tourist-congested neighborhood (oh how it has changed! no more grit or grime; now there's an Hermes & Loro Piana right next door!) that I can see myself enthusiastically wanting to frequent.

The first thing you have to do before going to Daniel is to remind yourself that you DESERVE it! You work hard, you take care of those you love, you probably pay your taxes, and darn it, you vote!Then, be sure and make an early reservation. Take your time, relax, enjoy. The Staff is at their best when you're comfortable and un-rushed.We deliberately did NOT dine at Daniel before the theater. Daniel IS the evening's event; anything after that might just be anticlimactic. We so enjoyed getting to the bar early enough to have a cocktail (have a Manhattan in the heart of Manhattan!) That atmosphere took us back to a more elegant time when we could luxuriate in the leather comfort and warm lighting.Once we gave a discreet nod, we were seated at a generous table with a wide view of the room. Arriving for early supper allowed us to enjoy a hushed conversation along with a glass of Champagne to toast our special day together. You have to remember that Daniel is a dining experience, to be shared and remembered, each time.Arriving early to the dining room allowed the background volume to rise gently, almost imperceptibly, as the room filled slowly, and we enjoyed our meal. The staff was suave and professional, yet still warm and welcoming. Our waiter knew the menu flawlessly and guided us through the courses deftly. We chose the 4-Course Tasting Menu, and opted for a couple of "supplements" for Caviar, and Foie Gras. We selected our own wines, as opposed to the accompanying wine pairing selections. The wine list truly made me as excited as a kid in the proverbial candy store. Though when the first course arrives and you may convince yourself that you will be hungry at the end of the meal, but you must disabuse yourself of any such notion. We thought that we were more than satiated by the time we saw the first dessert offering. But we dutifully pressed on!We were there to celebrate our anniversary, and doing it in style. We knew that this was going to be hard to surpass for our next milestone. Daniel staff had printed up a personalized menu ahead of time and presented it with compliments. The dessert plate was also a delightful surprise, and encouraged us to imbibe in some special port to compliment the chocolate.As we were set to retire for the evening we felt compelled to express our compliments to the dining room manager. He was, in turn, excited to take us to the orchestra pit, if you will. We were so very impressed, when we stepped into the kitchen, how quietly, efficiently, and professionally the staff moved about, communicated, and delivered. It was like opening up the back of a fine Swiss watch. You can truly see the value, and not just the time.Remember, you DESERVE your evening(s) at Daniel, the time with your friends, and the memory that will never fade.

Title: Miznon: A Pita Paradise in the Heart of NYC

If you're on the hunt for sensational pita sandwiches in New York City, look no further than Miznon. This culinary gem doesn't just serve up the standard fare; their pitas are a masterclass in texture and taste. Each pita is a cloud of warmth and fluffiness, creating the perfect vessel for their extraordinary fillings.

The magic lies in the variety and quality of their offerings. Whether you opt for grilled meats, the beautifully seasoned chickpea, or the iconic cauliflower, you're in for a flavor experience that simply can't be matched by other pita shops in the city. 

The cauliflower pita sandwich, a personal favorite, exemplifies their triumph of taste with its harmonious blend of creamy tahini sauce, tender cauliflower, all wrapped in that irresistible pita bread. This combination doesn't just satisfy the hunger, it soothes the soul.

A pro tip for potential visitors: take full advantage of Miznon's online ordering system. It's a lifesaver for bypassing the weekend rush. Trust me, your taste buds will thank you for the pre-planning.

In conclusion, Miznon is a must-visit for anyone seeking the ultimate pita sandwich experience in NYC. It's not just a meal; it's an unforgettable encounter with flavors that will leave you craving more.

COME HERE FOR BRUNCH! Make sure Jose is your waiter!!! If you do, you are sure to have a great time. My friends and I were looking for a bottomless brunch on a Thursday. We found Mezetto who offers brunch and bottomless mimosas daily! Jose greeted us warmly and from the time we sat down to when we left our champagne glasses were NEVER empty. We were there for a bachelorette party and even got some tequila shots. I got the Mezetto breakfast which had eggs, hummus, pita, quinoa and some other yummy trimmings. Food was very good. Do yourself a favor and do not drive to this brunch (not that many people do in the city?) bc drinks are flowwwinngg. Also, the lighting here is bomb for pics.

I had a delightful experience at this noodle spot, where the hand-pulled noodles truly showcased their fresh, artisanal quality. Following recommendations from Yelp and the friendly cashier, I opted for the cumin lamb noodles. This dish packed a punch with its bold, fiery flavors and tender lamb that was generously seasoned with cumin. Though I'm not typically a lamb person, it's worth a try for fans of the meat. Be warned, the spiciness level might not be for the faint-hearted, and the portion size was quite substantial – definitely suitable for sharing among 2 to 3 people. The thick, chewy noodles had a comforting similarity to Thai pad see ew. Although this was the only item I tried, the cleanliness of the establishment and the helpfulness of the staff left me with a positive impression.

I came on Valentine's Day and was able to quickly make a reservation ten minutes before. It was a very fancy atmosphere, with dim lights, and cute table decor. The food was absolutely amazing. Period. I wanted to cry because the food was THAT good. I got the Zia- Maria chicken, which was possibly the best decision I ever made, but the penne vodka also tasted good. I'm sure everything on the menu is fantastic. Warning: If you want to buy an alcoholic drink, but look young for your age, be aware that you should have more than 1 form of a state/federal issued ID (ex. a digital copy of your passport). My friend looks young, but is 22. Until she showed them her passport in addition to her state ID, they weren't going to let her buy a drink because they thought that her real ID was fake.

Title: A Delightful Evening with a Touch of Fusion at Kenny's

My recent dining experience at Kenny's was an absolute pleasure, thanks to the warm hospitality extended by the owner, Kenny himself. Though we encountered a slight delay with our reservation, he personally ensured our party of eight was well taken care of.

A word of caution for future visitors: the restaurant's entrance is on 15th street, not Union Square West as the address may imply—we almost missed it!

Stepping inside, I was greeted by a charming ambiance with comfortable seating and appropriately soft lighting, setting the perfect stage for an enjoyable dinner. The service was impeccable, matching the serene noise level that allowed for easy conversation without competing with background music.

Of the many dishes we savored, three stood out distinctively: the Blue Crab with Rice Cakes combined the unique flavor of salted egg yolk with scallions to perfection, the King Crab Squid Ink with Shanxi Flat Noodles impressed with its truffle-crab fusion and flawless texture, and the Live Crab Meat Scallion Noodles showcased exquisite Japanese-inspired cooking with daily-made fresh noodles.

While we appreciated the freshness of the Sauté Tiger Prawn and the unconventional take on Lobster Risotto, the fusion approach was more pronounced than preferred. The Crab Meat Soup Dumplings and Shanghai Truffle Wontons offered traditional thicker skins and a bold truffle essence, respectively. The Miyazaki Wagyu Beef, albeit well-flavored, was slightly overdone for such a premium cut. The Truffle Sea Scallops were rich, though the mystery blue sauce left us curious and a tad confused.

Desserts ended the meal on a high note. Tao Jiao Egg Tarts, despite their oily nature, were irresistibly flaky and fresh, and the Egg Yolk Sesame Ball was a delectable treat with its crunchy exterior and molten center.

The only hiccup was a missed dish in our order, the uni pastry, which was replaced without notice by a uni chanwamushi. Nevertheless, the overall experience was a flavorful journey well worth repeating. Thank you, Kenny and team, for a memorable evening!

Title: A Refreshed Menu at The Whitney's Restaurant Delights

My latest visit to the restaurant at the Whitney was an utter delight, as their revamped menu has done away with the puzzling duckless duck ramen, presenting a selection that is both sensible and innovative. The standout for me was the burger paired with a beets salad. While I found the burger slightly on the salty side, this minor quibble was overshadowed by the enjoyment of a special pickle accompaniment that added a welcome tangy crunch.

The beets salad was the true revelation of the meal. The addition of coconut crumbles was a stroke of culinary genius, transforming a simple dish into a symphony of flavors and texture that tantalized my palate. It's clear that the chef has a talent for thinking outside the box, adding unexpected twists that elevate the dining experience.
