Overall, the restaurant at the Whitney now offers a menu that is both grounded and inspired, and I am eager to return.

Got the dumplings, dry hot pot, and coconut and tapioca soup. The dumplings were less than mediocre, but it was all made up for by the hot pot. They tell you to choose about 8-10 ingredients for 2 people, but my friend and I only got through half of it. Also, the spice levels are higher than most other places. Spicy is pretty spicy. The coconut and tapioca soup was a good finish to the meal. Soothing after all the spicy was.

Disclaimer: No one apart of this review is a Vegan. Saturday night reservation for three people. The restaurant is small and causal but we've heard great things from our Vegan friends so we wanted to give it a go. We tried  different appetizers/salads and shared entrees among the three of us. Drink menu was innovated and the drinks were yummy. We always appreciate restaurants who are socially responsible, which Candle 79 is, so bring on the tequila that supports others! Apps/salad: wild mushroom ravioli, grilled flatbread, seaweed salad Entrees: eggplant Parmesan, wild mushroom crepe, roasted cauliflower Another disclaimer, I am a health nut so I am used to eating different substitutes. I knew going into this not to expect the eggplant parm to taste the same as my Italian grandfather would make it. Out of everything the consensus was that the seaweed salad was the best. Everything else we wouldn't order again.

Title: A Hotpot Haven with a Personal Touch

I recently visited an incredible à la carte hotpot restaurant that truly stood out from the crowd. Unlike typical all-you-can-eat spots, this gem offers a stunning variety of meats, seafood, and veggies. The rib eye and Jeju pork were particular highlights among the diverse options we sampled.

The ambiance of the place struck a chord with its clean, inviting atmosphere, which is enhanced by private VR areas perfect for larger parties. The unique offering of personalized hotpot bowls allows for individualized flavors and a dining experience tailored to personal tastes.

With a choice of delicious base broths and an array of items to add to your pot, the culinary possibilities seem endless. And to top it all off, the six different condiments provided meant we could craft our own sauces, adding another layer of customization to the meal.

I'm already planning my next visit to delve deeper into their extensive menu. This restaurant is definitely a must-try for hotpot enthusiasts and those looking for a flavorful adventure.

Visited a local ramen spot recently and it was a decent experience. While the ramen didn't top my list, the staff was commendable for their friendliness and attentiveness. The small dining area provided a cozy atmosphere, and I appreciated that it wasn't overly crowded - perfect for a swift meal. It's a solid choice for anyone looking for a quick, no-fuss dining option.

Title: A Weekly Delight at This Hidden Gem

I've found myself irresistibly drawn to this local Thai spot on a weekly basis, and I challenge anyone to resist its allure. The true star of the menu is the Yum Woon Senn – a symphony of glass noodles, succulent shrimp, tender squid, and fresh vegetables, all tossed in a sweet and tangy sauce that's light yet bursting with flavor, a refreshing alternative to the heavier Pad Thai.

Portion sizes are generous, especially considering the wallet-friendly prices. For those who like it hot, requesting "extra spicy" is no idle boast here – they deliver on the heat, outshining any other Thai place I've been to.

Don't miss out on the Pad Krapow Gai, reminiscent of a lettuce wrap but reinvented with finely minced chicken and ultra-crunchy veggies, offering a punch of flavor and texture that'll leave you craving more.

From the moment you step in, the energy is infectious. A chorus of warm welcomes rings out from no less than seven vibrant staff members, ensuring you feel valued, no matter how busy it gets. It's clear that excellent service is part of this restaurant's soul.

In summary, if you're after authentic Thai flavors, ample portions, and a place where service shines bright, look no further. This spot is a must-visit for any Thai cuisine enthusiast.

I recently visited a charming brunch spot that boasted a cozy neighborhood bar feel with homey decor. Despite a smaller menu selection, the quality and presentation of the food were both impressive. Service was attentive and quite satisfactory. I opted for the avocado toast, accompanied by a side salad, and was pleasantly surprised by the generous portion size that left me feeling full and content. This place is a delightful find for a fulfilling brunch experience.

I recently ordered takeout from the local restaurant and was very pleased with the experience. The Chicken and Shiitake Soup was exceptional, especially the rich, flavorful broth that was just perfect for warming up on a chilly winter day. The Dan Dan noodles were also delicious, with just the right amount of spice and seasoning. Both dishes exceeded my expectations, and I recommend them to anyone looking for comforting, well-prepared meals.

Visited this charming spot last evening and indulged in their chocolate martinis, each concoction more delightful than the last. The shared slice of chocolate cake was the perfect end to our gathering, leaving everyone in high spirits. Would recommend for a sweet night out!

Came here for dinner on a Saturday night. Was seated pretty quickly and it was packed. Lots of families and tight seating.  Food was decent, average service. Uttapam was delicious and tasted fresh , however the items in the thali seemed like they had been sitting around all day and were just re-heated at best. Some dishes were room temperature and they didn't even bother warming them up.  Overall, I would recommend this place for good South Indian food , but would stay away from any dish which looks like it could be recycled or re-purposed.

Tried the beef pho spicy rib meat. Good amount of meat and very tender. Soup was pretty good and flavorful, but being that I like my broth less oil as possible, it was slightly oily for my liking. Still, very good broth. Interior is very new, clean and posh. Almost like the tropical theme, not your traditional pho place decor. Their prices are slightly more expensive than typical Vietnamese place in Chinatown but you are also getting high quality and fancier veitnamI would definitely come back to try other items, and see myself coming back again.

Title: A Culinary Odyssey with Chef Don Pham

At the helm of an unforgettable culinary adventure, Chef Don Pham presents a sushi journey that is both ambitious and exquisitely executed. From the outset, Pham's thoughtful approach is evident: each piece of sushi is meticulously balanced, with just the right amount of rice complementing the fresh fish, ensuring diners remain eager for the next bite, all the way to the 16th morsel.

A delightful interlude awaits mid-course with the comforting chawanmushi - a silken steamed egg custard adorned with earthy mushrooms, giving diners a gentle reprieve before diving into the sashimi chapter of the meal. Here, Pham’s artistry truly shines, with masterfully cut slices of fish, uni, and fried oysters, each enhanced by a symphony of vinaigrettes and a standout uni miso paste.

The crescendo of the meal arrives with a visually striking Eiffel Tower-shaped stack of decadence: layers of toro interlaced with caviar, all crowned with gold leaf flakes. The handroll follows suit, a gargantuan creation of toro, tangy pickled vegetables, and a lavish spread of uni.

Throughout the omakase, Pham doesn't shy away from luxury; truffle graces five of the sixteen plates, uni another five, and on three occasions, both prized ingredients unite, creating an opulent dance of flavors. Caviar also makes three appearances, underscoring the indulgence that defines this dining experience.

Finishing with a soothing coconut pudding draped in matcha sauce, the meal leaves you sated yet yearning for more. When deciding on your omakase, opt for the 16-piece indulgence. Chef Don Pham’s culinary finesse is an experience not to be moderated. Embrace the extravagance for a truly remarkable dining encounter.

I've returned for the third time to what has become a favorite spot, now charmingly rebranded as Julia's Tea and Dim Sum House. Visiting at 7pm on a Monday proved to be a delightful experience, made all the more special by meeting Julia herself. The consistency remains, with the dim sum continuing to impress with its fantastic flavors. A must-visit for anyone who appreciates the art of well-crafted dim sum.

Title: A True and Affordable Ramen Experience at NYC's Hidden Gem

As an avid ramen enthusiast, I'm genuinely puzzled by the modest 3.5-star average rating of this cash-only gem. It seems that some patrons may not fully appreciate the traditional, no-frills ramen experience offered here, which stands in stark contrast to the overpriced options in the more upscale parts of New York City.

Price (5/5): The value here is unbeatable in NYC. The ramen is affordably priced without compromising on quality—a rarity in a city known for its exorbitant costs.

Atmosphere (4/5): True to its authentic roots, the restaurant buzzes with energy, mirroring the vibrancy of Japan's ramen shops. The thoughtful addition of coat and bag hooks under the counter is a small but welcome detail that enhances the experience.

Food (4.5/5): The Naruto Ramen is a steal at $9, generously accompanied by several slices of succulent pork, albeit the half-egg was not runny as one might find at higher-end establishments like Momofuku. A minor critique would be the overabundance of scallions, which slightly overpowered the other flavors. A tad less would perfect the balance.

Service: It's a no-frills spot, and the service reflects this with efficiency. Though minimal, it's completely adequate with attentive water refills and prompt order taking.

Extras: For the Pokemon Go players, this spot uniquely doubles as a gym, adding an extra layer of fun to your dining experience.

In conclusion, if you're looking for a genuine, delicious, and wallet-friendly ramen experience in NYC, look no further. Just remember: bring cash, and read up on the soy sauce-based broths before you visit to avoid any surprises!

Title: A Taste of Variety at the New 42nd Street Food Hall

I recently visited the newly inaugurated food hall on the east end of 42nd Street and was greeted by an eclectic array of dining options spread across two floors. Although it's still in its soft opening phase, with some establishments like Bee Pattern and Yaso Noodle Bar yet to open their doors, the ones in operation show promise.

The star of the show is undoubtedly Yaso Noodle Bar, tantalizing with its Shanghainese creations – the lionhead meatballs and ribs being particular highlights. For curry aficionados, Curry42 serves up a delightful selection of Thai curries that are richly flavored and satisfying when paired with their aromatic rice.

Those in the mood for Japanese can head over to Rice-On, where sushi rolls and bowls satisfy with fresh ingredients like mango and crunchy spicy tuna. While I couldn't indulge in desserts at Bee Pattern, their menu boasting egg and ostrich egg bubble waffles served with gelato and fresh honeycomb has me excited for future visits.

The bubble tea selection at Debutea Mini is quite extensive, featuring classics like brown sugar milk tea and refreshing fruit teas that are perfect palate cleansers after a hearty meal.

A slight inconvenience at this food hall is the central cashier system, which requires guests to pay before collecting their food from individual vendors, resulting in additional queuing. But, for those willing to navigate this minor hiccup, the variety and quality of food on offer make this new spot worth checking out.

I recently visited this restaurant with my coworkers and was thoroughly impressed by the variety of drinks on offer. The sausage platter was particularly superb and the giant pretzel proved to be a delightful treat. With ample seating, the ambiance allowed us to enjoy each other's company comfortably. This spot is a definite go-to for anyone looking to have an amazing time with friends or colleagues.

During a recent visit to the upscale version of a beloved Los Angeles-based Korean restaurant, my craving for tofu soup was splendidly satisfied. Having frequented its LA Koreatown counterpart, typically as a late-night comfort food destination, I was pleasantly surprised by the elevated ambiance that set it apart from the diner-like vibe I was accustomed to.

The meal was as comforting and delicious as always, complete with the standard array of banchan, amongst which the fried fish stood out. A special mention must go to the fish cakes – they were exceptional, and the kitchen was prompt in refilling them without hesitation. Service was on point: attentive enough to ensure a seamless dining experience without crossing into intrusiveness.

In summary, the restaurant maintains the quality and taste of its LA roots while providing a more refined dining environment, making it a fantastic option for both familiar and new patrons.

Title: A Sizzling First Korean BBQ Experience!

I had the pleasure of venturing into the world of Korean BBQ for the first time, and the experience was nothing short of fantastic at this hidden gem of a restaurant. With a reservation in hand, my two friends and I were promptly welcomed and seated without a hitch.

Though we were initially daunted by the unfamiliar menu, our Korean cuisine-savvy companion helped us navigate the options. We ended up feasting on an array of mouthwatering selections. Pairing the meal with soju turned out to be a delightful choice, especially since it was my inaugural encounter with this Korean spirit.

The highlight was undoubtedly the sheer quality of the food, which had us all basking in a contented hush, fully immersed in the culinary magic on our plates. The dining atmosphere added to the charm, enhancing an already superb meal.

In short, the restaurant delivered an impeccable introduction to Korean BBQ. Given the chance, I would eagerly come back for another round of this authentic, flavorful adventure.

Douzo was my first experience in a restaurant specializing in sushi handrolls. I'm very traditional and like my nigiri omakases. There are a few other famous restaurants in new york which are similar - Sugarfish and KazuNori - which I haven't been to. The restaurant is bar seating only. It wasn't too clear on the website if they needed reservations, but I recommend calling them to make one. I walked in and was lucky there were 2 seats available. The menu is straightforward. You can order a set of Temaki (handrolls) or a set of Gunkan sushi, which are little "boats" made of nori, pressed seaweed, a small amount of sushi rice on the bottom.I opted for their Douzo ($40) set menu which consists of 6 handrolls.PiecesYellow TailCrab MeatSnapperNori ToroHokkaido ScallopShrimp TempuraMy favorites were the scallop and crab meat rolls. All the seafood was super fresh. The sushi chef hands you one piece at a time like a sushi omakase.Although I thought the handrolls were good, I do prefer nigiri over handrolls. I wasn't too full after the set and would recommend ordering more rolls. I haven't been to the OG handroll spots. so I don't have much to compare this too. The DIY handroll set also looked really pretty, but i'm lazy and did not want to roll my own haha. Douzo was a good break from the normal nigiri omakases I usually get and I would recommend this place if you don't want to wait in the long lines of the other handroll joints.

Title: A Comfortable Christmas Dining Experience at [Restaurant Name]

This Christmas, upon a friend's recommendation, my company and I chose [Restaurant Name] for our festive dinner. Despite the restaurant's promise of seasonal themes, the holiday decor was understated to the point of being unnoticeable. Our seating was less than ideal, with a wobbly table tucked away in the back.

However, the culinary experience offered by the prix fixe Christmas menu - at $89 per head for an appetizer, entrée, dessert, and sides - was surprisingly delightful. The crabcake starter, accompanied by a flavorful avocado crema, set a high bar. My halibut entrée followed, perfectly flaky and seasoned. A shared platter of assorted sides was provided, with the stuffing standing out, although it didn't capture much of my attention.

Dessert was a sticky toffee pudding, which, despite its pleasing taste, was my least favorite; nonetheless, the accompanying ice cream provided a necessary sweetness and balance.

Service was attentive, and the restaurant atmosphere was cozy, ensuring our Christmas meal was a pleasant one. Despite minor setbacks, [Restaurant Name] delivered a very enjoyable dining experience. I'd happily return and give it a solid 4 stars.

Our next choice for winter restaurant week, we now officially dined at all three branches of Boucherie. This one is at the corner of Gay street. From its name the place is really very tiny (we asked couple of times to switch tables for a little bit of privacy)The service and attentiveness of the staff was really commendable, we started with a good glass of Cotes du Rhône then ordered the following dishes:To Start:1. Mousse de foie gras2. Escargot, these two appetizers we found are good for sharing served with a warm toasty bread.Main Course:3. Boeuf Bourguignon 4. Chateaubriand, we found both dishes very delicious and it was cook to perfection.To finish:5. Creme Brûlée 6. Chocolate mousse, we shared both dishes and we felt the creme brûlée really stood out.It was a lovely dinner that left you satisfied yet not overly full.This is an excellent restaurant week choice so be sure you don't miss the opportunity to dine here.

Wow food was good and the pickle ice cream was the best finishing touch. Super cheap too. You must try this place.It's just to the left of e's bar and Jacobs pickles.When you go in, you can check out the menu to the right. Then order from the electronic board on the left. They have some seating to eat there on premise if you so desire. I don't know if it happens every time but we were able to get our ice cream after we finished our meal.If you need extra chili oil or soy sauce they have them in little containers up by the kitchen.The pickle ice cream twisted with pumpkin ice cream is so good. Don't let the thought of it being pickle persuade you from trying this. It really is the perfect level of tangy and sweet and sour.Highly recommend.

Title: A Mediterranean Gem on the UWS!

Last Monday, my friends, freshly settled in from Tribeca, decided to explore their new locale's culinary scene. We stumbled upon a bustling spot, known for its half-off wine deal to beat the Monday blues. Despite our tardy arrival, the staff graciously accommodated us with an outdoor table that complemented the crisp evening air with glasses of warming red.

Complimentary bread and olives set a welcoming tone, promptly followed by an array of Mediterranean delights. We indulged in tender grape leaves, savory lamb dumplings, creamy baba ganoush, a robust eggplant moussaka, and the star attraction, the Bodrum pizza, adorned with succulent lamb meatballs. 

Ours being a table of Mediterranean aficionados, including a pal with Lebanese roots, we found unanimity in our praise for the Turkish spice flair that dazzled our palates. The lamb dumplings in particular left us enamored with their unique charm. 

It's worth noting that the service was nothing short of fabulous, complete with that quintessential NYC edge. A hearty recommendation for anyone craving a taste of the Mediterranean on the Upper West Side!

Title: Family-Friendly Eatery with Generous Portions

My family and I had a delightful experience at this restaurant, where comfort meets convenience. The seating arrangement caters to all group sizes, with large tables at the front equipped with handy hooks for personal belongings, and smaller tables at the back perfect for couples.

The food exceeded our expectations in both preparation speed and quality. Everything served was fresh, hot, and tantalizingly flavorful. We indulged in grilled vegetable bowls - one with udon and the other with rice - as well as rich ramen noodle soup and udon noodle soup. The portions were impressively generous, so much so that we took half our bowls home for later.

The udon noodle vegetable bowl was a standout, drenched in a savory sauce that paired perfectly with some borrowed rice from my sister's dish. This restaurant is a gem for anyone looking for delicious meals that won't break the bank. Their commitment to serving hearty food in a clean and inviting atmosphere certainly won us over!

Prince St Pizza lives up to the hype.A lot of flavor in the spicy pepperoni and the thick crust is executed perfectly. Good sauce to cheese ratio as well.It's worth the wait, a half block line of people takes like 20 minutes. They take credit cards. No seating inside, take it to go and eat it outside! Would go back!

I recently tried out the much-talked-about mushroom ravioli, a popular starter among Yelpers, priced at $18. Unfortunately, the dish didn't live up to the hype, as the ravioli skin was disproportionately thick and overshadowed the scant mushroom filling, leading to a rather flour-heavy experience. Although truffle oil was present, it did little to save the dish from being overly greasy and lacking in depth of flavor.

Additionally, I sampled the ancient grains salad, also $18, which turned out to be quite underwhelming. It consisted merely of a sparse scattering of quinoa, a few meager slices of avocado, and a small garnish of greens. It was a disappointingly minimal offering for the price.

Service at the restaurant left much to be desired, with a notable lack of attentiveness from the staff. Considering the high prices and the less-than-impressive food quality, it wasn't surprising to find the restaurant relatively empty, especially in stark contrast to the bustling Italian eatery, Cotta, which had diners lined up for tables right next door.

Title: A Spicy Surprise at Rong Cheng House

My fiancé and I recently had a dining experience at Rong Cheng House that left a strong impression. Upon our Sunday evening arrival, the modest space was quiet, hosting few patrons, which allowed the staff to be especially attentive. Once our adventurous order of eel and a whole bass was placed, they thoughtfully relocated us to a larger table for comfort.

The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the whole bass, which arrived in a mere 15 minutes despite its significant size. Drenched in a fiery red sauce that my fiancé adored, the bass itself was tender, though the overwhelming spice overshadowed its natural flavors. Personally, the fried eel won my favor with its more balanced seasoning, enhancing the eel's taste beyond mere heat. Both dishes were well-complemented by the side of white rice, a savior for tempering the intensity.

Regrettably, a subsequent engagement at Carnegie Hall meant no leftovers for us, which is a shame, as I would relish the chance to savor the flavors once more. With food that hits slightly above average and service that shines, I've given Rong Cheng House a solid 4-star review. If your path takes you nearby, it's worth stopping in for a boldly spicy meal.

Initially called in advance on a Thursday night to see if they had space for two, which they did at the bar. Seemed worth it, so headed over and was pleasantly surprised when they sat us at a table instead. Spacious interior and not overwhelming with it's decor, making for a perfect date night scenario.Menu is definitely on the expensive end, with appetizers priced from $14-18 and entrees at $28-40. To start off, decided to split the Dahi Chili Paneer ($17) - three large squares of marinated paneer served alongside tangy chutney and pickled onions. Amazingly fresh and just the right amount of spice. For the main course, settled on the Banana Leaf Chicken ($27) - a combo of rice and thick chicken leg curry encased in a banana leaf. Tender meat that falls off the bone, and plenty of curry left to finish off the rice. Only downside was that my cocktail ($15) wasn't very memorable.Service is top notch as we are taken care efficiently without being disturbed. One of the better options for upscale Indian food.

Decent for Restaurant Week, but wouldn't necessarily come back for dinner.I've had Jue Lan on my must-try list for a while for the cool ambiance and those coveted Chicken Satay skewers, but this meal wasn't necessarily my favorite. Not terrible, but not a meal I'd want to drop another $200 on.I made reservations on OpenTable so we were promptly seated when we arrived. We opted to sit inside since we visited during NYC's recent heatwave (plus, I think those pink umbrellas outside are a bit *too* much lol). The inside is gorgeous and we were seated at a cool corner booth. Definitely good for a date so I'll give myself a pat on the back for that.We each decided to go with the 3 courses for RW2019. Here's what we tried:- the Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce (1/2 the reason I even suggested this place)- Crispy Rock Shrimp Tempura with Spicy Mayo- Wok Charred Beef, Broccoli, Cauliflower, with Mongolian Sauce- Filet Mignon, Fingerling Potatoes in a Black Pepper Sauce (an extra $10 for this one)- Choice of 1 rice for the table: Chicken Fried Rice- Molten Chocolate Cake with a Cherry Compote- Vanilla Creme Brulee with Chocolate Chip CookiesDishes that were 5 star: the Rock Shrimp, Charred Beef, and Filet Mignon.Dishes that I wish we didn't order: everything else.The Chicken Satay was definitely not comparable to those at Philippe's. It was just pink-colored chicken smothered in condensed milk. Not the worst but definitely not something worth top $$$. The Molten Choc Cake wasn't "molten" at all, and the Creme Brulee was cold. Def all passes from me.Our bill was so $$$$ because we each got 2 drinks during the meal. Normally I'd roll my eyes at this, but the frosé was the actual best I've ever had so I'd happily come back and pay $16 per glass.Our waitress was super sweet and helpful but throughout our meal, other servers kept bringing us the incorrect plates and leaving them on our table before we could even correct them. So weird.I'd come back for the frosé alone, but I'd eat somewhere else.

Title: Decent Ambiance, Underwhelming Portions

I recently dined at an okay eatery that boasted a pleasant outdoor space, perfect for those rare good-weather days in the city. Staff members were courteous, though there was a hint of displeasure when my party opted for water over pricier drinks.

We sampled the octopus appetizer, a sausage and onion pizza, and fettuccine with veal. While each dish was tasty, the portions were disappointingly small given their price points – the $16 octopus consisted of merely three tentacles, the $18 pizza was more suited for one, and the $19 veal ragu didn't justify its tag. New York City has a plethora of Italian restaurants that offer similar or superior flavors at a better value. In summary, this place is alright, but there are better options out there for Italian cuisine lovers looking for both quality and quantity.

Title: A New York Gem That's Worth the Wait

If you find yourself in NYC with an appetite, there's one spot where the wait feels worth every minute. This place isn't just about good food; it's about superb food that doesn't break the bank. Their breakfast-to-go specials epitomize convenience and affordability—a rare find in the city.

Open 24/7, this eatery stands out with offerings that cater to the most nocturnal of us. For me, the rotating selection of seasonal pierogies is a standout feature, showcasing a commitment to both variety and tradition.

I opted for the blue plate lunch special, a comfort food delight featuring a heartwarming matzo ball soup paired with a half chicken salad sandwich, all for just $12. The portions were perfect, leaving me satisfied but not overstuffed. The quality of the food is undeniable, and it's clear this restaurant understands the balance between quantity, quality, and price.

This spot isn't just a restaurant; it's a culinary haven in the bustling streets of New York City. Whether you're a local or just passing through, make sure to give it a try. Trust me, it's worth the wait.

I've been to Luke's Lobster before and after a long travel day and a late flight in, we ventured to Luke's a block from our hotel for a quick light dinner just before they closed.I had tried the obligatory lobster roll before so on this visit I ordered Luke's trio ($19.50), which came with a half shrimp roll, a half crab roll, and a half lobster roll. The lobster was generous and meaty and the crab had a nice little sweetness to it. The roll that was somewhat disappointing was the shrimp. It had no flavor.  My dining partner ordered a lobster roll ($17) and the lobster corn chowder.Luke's was empty on the snowy night that we visited and the employees were preparing to close. Yet, they provided good customer service and we had an enjoyable fast bite. Next time, I'll stick with the lobster as that is what they do best.

Tucked away on the fringe of Times Square lies a hidden gem of a noodle shop that's well worth your attention. Despite its modest size, this eatery proves to be a perfect spot for slurping down a hefty bowl of hand-pulled noodles, either swimming in a rich broth or stir-fried to perfection.

My visit post-lunch rush meant snagging a seat was a breeze. I indulged in the roast duck noodle soup—a harmonious blend of tender duck pieces, baby bok choy, and greens, all in a savory, well-balanced broth. The noodles struck that ideal texture: satisfyingly chewy without being tough.

While the ambiance is simple and unpretentious, the cleanliness and convenience of credit card acceptance are big pluses. The cordial staff adds to the welcoming vibe. It's noteworthy to see that locals, rather than tourists, fill the tables—a testament to the authenticity and quality of the food.

Stumbling upon this spot was a true delight. For anyone craving an authentic, comforting bowl of noodles amidst the buzz of the city, this place is a must-visit.

I stumbled upon this place with a line out the door, a promising sign. My experience calls for a solid 3-star rating. The supreme pizza I ordered unfortunately gave the impression of being previously cooked and then inelegantly reheated, resulting in a burnt bottom. Despite this mishap, the establishment did offer generous slice portions at reasonable prices. Next time, I'll opt for the fresh pepperoni slice, which looked far more appetizing as it came out of the oven. Worth a second visit for the potential redemption of that first impression.

Loved this hidden gem. I am from out of town and my cousin brought our family here to celebrate my mother's birthday. The food was delicious and fresh! They brought us this delicious chips and salsa that were so yummy and addicting! I asked for more chips and salsa! The salsa tasted home made, spicy and all ingredients on point! I ordered their shrimp creole with veggies and a side of tostones (fried plantains). I ordered Morir Soñando mojitos all night because they were AMAZINGLY DELICIOUS! At the end of our meal, the staff came to sing my mom Happy Birthday...our family had a great time.They also had a a live musician all night and he was great. Great music, ambience and great attentive staff. The restaurant seemed real busy being the middle of a weeknight, with some wait when we got there. Make sure you call ahead and make reservations if offered. I will definitely come back every time I am in town!

Title: A Birthday Bash to Remember at a Vibrant Tapas Joint

I recently celebrated a friend's birthday at this gem of a tapas restaurant, and it was an absolute delight. The ambiance strikes a perfect balance between cozy and energetic, creating a festive backdrop for our lively gathering. The staff were the epitome of warmth, contributing to a memorable dining experience with their friendliness.

The menu was a culinary excursion through Spain, with a stand-out tortilla española that rivaled those I've savored on Spanish soil. The dátiles con beicon were a sweet-meets-savory revelation, and the croquetas cremosas offered a delectable divide between vegetarian and meat options. The cojonudo and pintxos morunos were also hits at our table.

Despite the high marks, the mushrooms did fall a bit short, coming across as overly simple and tipping the salt scale. As for dessert, the Nutella churros were indulgent, but it was the caramel nuances in the caramel Nutella that stole my sweet tooth's heart.

Be warned, as with any tapas place, the bill can climb, but for a festive night out, this spot is worth the splurge. Whether it's a birthday or just a craving for spirited Spanish fare, this restaurant comes highly recommended.

Alex Stupak just officially opened his second location of Empellon Al Pastor in place of Salvation Taco inside the Pod 39 Hotel, and even though it might not feel as cool as the original East Village one given it's in Murray Hill, it's a really really good restaurant.All of the food is top notch, as can be expected from the Empellon family. I definitely wanted the new stuff, such as the really good Fried Chicken Sandwich ($7) and the best Sweet Potato Tacos you'll ever try ($10 for 2).As always, chef Stupak always has the most interesting desserts that you should always leave room for. The Crunchy Corn Masa Ice Cream ($6) is solid, but you should definitely get the very fun "Pineapple With Five Other Flavors" ($12). You get to light some pineapple on fire and coat it with 5 different toppings that make for an unexpectedly delicious dessert.This is easily the best restaurant in this neighborhood now.

I absolutely adore this restaurant! The food is exceptional, with highlights including scrumptious corn, succulent short ribs, flavorful al pastor tacos, and a surprisingly delightful fried shrimp taco. To top it off, the homemade churros were incredibly fresh. The service is top-notch; both the manager, Kevin, and the owner took the time to personally greet us and ensure our dining experience was outstanding. Plus, the BYOB option is a fantastic touch. This establishment is a fantastic new addition to the local dining scene.

Went with a friend around 3:00pm on a Sunday. It was fairly empty, granted they close early. Ordered a matcha latte with almond milk which was truly phenomenal. The food...not so much. Ordered a mushroom toast and it was extremely difficult to cut through the bread. Good thing the toppings made up for it. Overall, it is worth a try!

Visited this restaurant once more for lunch and the culinary experience continues to shine, earning a well-deserved five stars for the food. The cavatelli was exceptional; despite the generous portion, it was so delicious that I had no problem cleaning the plate. Their beets salad remained consistent in freshness and taste. I was delighted to find my favorite cake and ice cream combination on the dessert menu, with the cream cheese ice cream being particularly delectable. However, I have to deduct a star due to the noticeably slow service, which has room for improvement.

Title: A Sunday Morning Delight in Chinatown

If you find yourself in Chinatown on a Sunday morning with a craving for authentic dim sum, prepare yourself for a mandatory wait, which I assure you is a small price to pay for the culinary experience ahead. This bustling establishment serves up what is arguably the best dim sum this side of town, and while service might leave something to be desired, the food will sweep any misgivings right under the table.

As traditional carts laden with an assortment of delights weave through the tables, your senses are treated to a tantalizing parade. Do not miss their signature pork shumai or the impeccably steamed shrimp dumplings – each bite a testament to their craft. For the more adventurous, the short ribs, tripe, and chicken feet are exceptional choices that will reward your palate.

And just when you think the meal could not get any better, their lava buns enter the scene, oozing with rich, sweet flavor, providing a blissful close to a sumptuous feast. In summary, for an authentic dim sum experience that is well worth the wait, look no further than this local gem.

Title: A Serene Visit to Chloe — A Delightful Surprise

I recently revisited Chloe after avoiding the chaotic scene from years past in Soho, and to my delight, the experience was peaceful perfection. Opting for a lighter fare, my companion and I shared their renowned quinoa salad and a glass of their not-so-ordinary lemonade. The salad remained a refreshing and addictive masterpiece, while the lemonade surprised us with its minty cucumber twist — so good we contemplated seconds.

The ambiance was vastly improved with more open space and fewer crowds, which may have been due to our early dinner timing. It's a spot that caters to all — from children entertained by coloring books and crayons to health-conscious families and the social media savvy crowd seeking picturesque plates.

Room for improvement? Certainly, a little more attention to table cleanliness and swifter food service would elevate the experience further. Despite these minor critiques, Chloe is back on my radar for a satisfying, tranquil meal.

I've been to this restaurant twice - once for dinner and once for lunch. The lunch options are plentiful, with a full spread tray for one person, complete with stew, bulgogi, etc. and a wide array of side dishes. It's easiest to get a table for lunch, especially if you go when it opens.For dinner, get the octopus salad. It's citrusy, light, and unique. The seafood stew was also great, though a little sweet for my liking. We also got the tiramisu for dessert - highly recommended! It has a smoky flavor and an airy, creamy texture. If you can brave the wait, the meal is well worth it.

Title: A Midtown Gem for Group Celebrations

My experience at this midtown restaurant for a graduation dinner was exceptional, notably for its affordability. With a party of eight, we paid roughly $38 per person, inclusive of food and drinks, which is a bargain for the location. Those looking to stretch their dollars should take advantage of the Yelp check-in offer—a free drink with a $30 food purchase. I recommend the Joe Collins from the drink menu; it's a refreshing take on spiked lemonade.

For dinner, the skewer selection was satisfying, particularly the chicken meatball and shimeji mushroom wrapped in pork belly. The sesiri and bonjiri stood out with their rich flavors and complementary sauces. Along with a comforting side of white rice, the portion sizes were generous. We concluded the meal with a serene round of green tea, which was a delight for everyone.

The cleanliness, professionalism, and tantalizing flavors make this restaurant an easy recommendation. It's a spot that shouldn't be missed for enjoyable and delicious dining experiences in the heart of the city.

I don't often eat szechuan but it's always an exciting meal. Come with a group of friends so you can help each other out when it gets too spicy. They also have non spicy options. The restaurant was clean and inviting, with paper table cloths. The servers were friendly and refilled our water several times. Lisa recommended the popular dishes to us and we went with the fried fish (big enough for a few people, great presentation, comes with lots of spicy vegetables), mapo tofu, and chicken in chili oil. The menu is extensive and comes with lots of photos to reference. Everything tasted good and fresh. It was very lively on a weekday after work. Looks like a great place for those weekday lunches too.

Okay so I was super excited to come here because I had the wildest craving for dim sum. So I ordered my food and I did pretty early 11:03 it was sent in and said in the works 11:04. I get there 11:25-11:30 I figure that's enough time since they open at 11Anyways I end up sitting there waiting for at least 20 minutes. I wish they would have just said hey we didn't smart making it yet.. something anything so then I could just come back at a later time..When I get my food it's okay but there were chopsticks and I don't enjoy eating soup dumplings with a fork.. also none of the dim sum dishes had the sweet soy sauce that usually comes with.. disappointing considering how long I waited

I recently dined at a charmingly decorated restaurant with a unique color palette of black, white, aqua blue, pink, and red accents that created an inviting atmosphere. The layout was spacious, though this contributed to a somewhat noisy environment. Despite the ambiance, service lagged, with noticeable delays in food delivery to not just our table but others as well, leaving me curious about the cause of the holdup. When our pizzas finally arrived, they were delightful, well worth the wait. Additionally, the shishito peppers were a flavorful treat. Overall, a pleasant experience once the food graced our table.

I recently dined at a remarkably classy establishment that impressed right from the entrance with its elegant decor and attentively dressed wait staff. Despite lacking a reservation, my party was accommodated immediately—a testament to their excellent service.

The menu boasted a beautiful array of choices, from sumptuous steaks to fresh seafood and more. The steaks, ordered by three of our group, arrived perfectly cooked to our individual preferences, while the shrimp dish was equally delectable. Sides of green beans and creamed spinach complemented the main courses marvelously.

We were also treated to a pre-meal offering of crisp celery, carrots with a smooth hummus, and warm Italian rolls, setting a delightful tone for the meal. It’s worth noting that the menu is a la carte and on the pricier side, so plan accordingly.

For those in search of an outstanding steak in a sophisticated setting, this restaurant will certainly meet—and perhaps even exceed—your expectations.

Title: Authentic Tapas and Exceptional Service

We stumbled upon this gem while Beecher's Cellar was closed for Labor Day, and what a delightful surprise it was! The Spanish tapas served were truly authentic, offering a delectable cheese and meat selection that more than satisfied our cravings. Accompanied by quality sangria and cava, our dining experience was elevated to new heights. The service was nothing short of fantastic, making us feel welcomed and well-cared-for throughout our meal. We've already marked our calendars to return!

I've only ordered delivery so I can't vouch for the in person experience. Delivery is always on time and smartly packaged. You can't go wrong with the pho cari lunch special. It's particularly a good deal since upgrading to shrimp is only a buck extra. It's creamy, comforting, and filling. I wish they'd beef up the noodle portion since there's always leftover broth but can't really complain. All in all a great spot to satisfy your pho craving on the UES.
Super juicy and high quality Peruvian chicken & sides. Great value with combo plates under $15 with two sides.Ate:Quarter chicken whiteSquash MadurosTake out during the pandemic for your chicken fix!

Title: A Feast for the Senses at a Local Gem

I recently dined at this bustling spot and I'm still reminiscing about the meal. A friend, already savvy to the menu, guided our culinary journey. We were greeted by the delightful burst of flavors found in their soup dumplings—an auspicious start.

The Don Don noodles, a recommendation, didn't disappoint. Warning: they pack a spicy punch, but dare I say, it's worth the thrill. The sesame chicken was the star of the night, crisped and glazed to perfection—a dish I'm still savoring a week later.

We rounded off the meal with grilled cauliflower, spicy yet unbelievably addictive. It alone could satisfy as a main dish.

Service was swift and congenial, enhancing the experience. A tip for future diners: arrive early. We settled in at six, and by the time we departed, the crowd had swelled. This place is clearly a hit, so expect a wait if you're a latecomer.

**Review Title: Pricey but Quality Ingredients – A Mixed Bag Experience**

**Rating:*** ★★★★☆ (If you're willing to spend) or ★★★☆☆ (On a budget)

If you're ready to splurge a bit, this restaurant could be a solid four-star experience. Expect premium prices, possibly due to the high-quality ingredients, a notch above typical Chinatown fares.

The pork soup dumplings scored an 8/10. They're in the "Pretty Good" category but not exceptional when considering value – six dumplings here cost $10, unlike Chinatown's eight for $6. Despite the price, their happy hour might lure me back.

The zhajiangmian was a letdown at 6/10, lacking the robust flavors you'd expect from such a staple dish. The unnamed chicken dish earned a 7/10. While the portion was generous, my forgetfulness about its specifics and a $25 price tag make it a questionable choice. The string beans also garnered a 7/10, decent enough to consider reordering but not a must-have.

In summary, decent food but weigh the value before diving in. The restaurant fares well if your wallet is as ready for an indulgence as your palate.

I was really quite excited to try Upland on my latest work trip to New York and while the food was mostly really good, the service was definitely off. We had a table of 7 and we ordered a lot of dishes as we were told it was best to share. Having never been to the restaurant we were looking for guidance from our server who said we ordered enough for the table but nothing crazy so we figured we did a good job. We actually ordered way too much and the service was slow. By the time we received our last plates, we all just wanted to go to bed. During our service one of the expeditors by accidentally knocked a full wine glass over the table  which I can understand happens and he apologized but what was off for a restaurant like this was no one refilled the wine or offered a glass on the house. Also, the guy who acted as if he knew wines, didn't have recommendations for us when we asked. He didn't seem to know too much about wine at all which again was just weird. Favourite dishes were the mushroom as well as the clam pizzas. The pastas were yummy and the crispy duck wings were awesome. The decor is beautiful and the restaurant has a good vibe to it. Overall the food was good, it's the experience that left me feeling underwhelmed unfortunately.

Title: Crispy Crust Heaven at My New Favorite Pizza Joint

I've finally found my pizza paradise in the city! This spot boasts an outstanding thin crust that defies logic; it's impossibly crispy, even under the weight of a generous meat lovers' topping. Every crunch is a symphony of flavors, with a sauce that makes the experience even more joyous. I'm almost relieved I don't live nearby; otherwise, I'd be in serious trouble with an addiction to these mouthwatering, crispy delights. Simply put: my taste buds are ecstatic, my stomach is content, and this pizza place is unrivaled. An absolute must-visit for thin crust enthusiasts!

Did some takeout here for dan dan noodles, eggplant, and cumin lamb.Honestly, given those items not sure what the hype is for this place. The dan dan noodles were good, nothing to really rave about. Noodles weren't homemade, not a lot of meat, no "numbing" (ma) to the dish. Definitely have had better.The eggplant was good, spicy, thick sauce (great to drench some rice in).The cumin lamb was a bit hard, good flavor, but just surprised the lamb was so stiff. And per usual, don't get much meat in this dish.Did get free rice in the takeout tho, so that was nice.

I got the spicy cumin lamb and it was the perfect amount of spicyness! The cabbage, celery, green onion, red onions and lamb were all well marinated and tasted great. Flavor was great and everything tasted great.I took my order to go and after arriving home in 10 minutes, I opened my to go to a very sticky set of noodles. They were hard to pull apart and had dried up a bit. Next time I'll eat it straight there and would recommend others to eat it right away when it's fresh or else it starts to stick together. Overall great taste though!

My boyfriend & I went to Joseph's during NYC Winter Restaurant Week and had a lovely experience. We went on a Friday night, and the restaurant was surprisingly not very busy, and it worked to our advantage because we had such excellent wait-service. It seemed that all waiters were honed in on us having a lovely evening.We ordered a bottle of wine off of the recommendation of our waiter and ordered the following:His: Eggplant Rollatini, Veal Picatta, and CheesecakeHers: Gulf shrimp, Rigatoni alla vodka, and tiramisu Everything was fantastic, and for $42 each, such a steal! We both agreed that the eggplant appetizer and rigatoni alla vodka stole the show.I would recommend coming here for a romantic Italian meal anytime, even outside of Restaurant Week.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Local Taco Spot

My recent visit to this taco restaurant was underwhelming. We ordered a mix of chicken and steak tacos, complemented by a couple of margaritas. Unfortunately, the food was mediocre at best. The side of rice and beans arrived without any silverware, and the steak in particular was overdone to the point of being burnt, while the chicken lacked proper seasoning. The margaritas were passable, though far from impressive.

When the bill came to $65, we were surprised to learn of a mandatory tip for debit card payments over $20. Service was lackluster; we were greeted with an empty front and a 10-minute wait. While there was no offer of water, the staff did provide agave and brown sugar upon request, which was a small, accommodating gesture.

The lack of outdoor seating and strictly to-go service may deter some. At a total of $66, I expected a more enjoyable dining experience. Unfortunately, I left feeling that both the service and the food did not justify the cost.

When it comes to dim sum I don't have super high standards, but the food needs to at least be edible with a comparable price. My experience at Pings was mixed. Some of the menu items are not as advertised and they will not adjust the prices for anything. Don't order the shrimp on the sugar cane, because they are not real shrimp, they are an awful fish tasting mess! The only thing edible were the different types of dumplings along with the calamari. The steamed rice rolls were not the best, I noticed most people left them on the tables around us. The fried foods were very oily, and the servers were super pushy if they were trying to unload undesirable dishes. Other items were either out, or offered to selected tables. Prices? Four people, 10 selections, almost a $100. Outrageous.

Takeout orders during lunch times seems to be always incorrect (missing guac, different empanada than ordered) but the food itself is worth that five stars. Smaller than anticipated for the price of each empanada, but taste wise, it is DELISH. My favorite are the cheese ones: the cheesesteak, the desayuno, and the ground beef corn empanada is also super tasty. These make up my must orders! I know everyone raves about the seafood viagra empanada, but I think that one is pretty standard. Overall, I just love that the filling is sooo moist and juicy, while the deep fried shell is just the perfect amount of softness and crispiness. Plantains and guac: always order this, and never fails to be less than satisfyingSangria: always order this as well, and some days it's strong, and other days, it's very watered downMy favorite is the omelette dish that I can't remember the name of, but it filled me up insanely quick, and was so full of flavor. A bit on the salty side, but everything about it had me licking my plate clean and I'm still thinking about comfortingly delicious that was.Meat platter: I loved this, but the greasiness got to me after a few bites. Definitely can't eat this by yourself - meant for sharing!

I ordered the Honey BBQ Club from their Signature Creations with Poppers, which includes sassy bbq, honey, chopped bacon, shredded cheddar and crispy shallots. I also added french fries as the base of my basket, it was so delicious! I ordered a side of purple slaw on the side as well. As for my extra sauces on the side, I got Sunny Mustard and Cray sauce. I was pleasantly surprised as to how food you get in the medium size basket, wasn't ready for it. All of this came up to $17, I also wasn't ready for the price, didn't think chicken poppers, fries and slaw would cost that much. Food was however delicious as like their other locations. This location has a very cool, young, hip vibe.

Title: A Timeless Culinary Treasure

My first visit to this restaurant was an absolute delight, and I'm keen on it not being the last. The prime rib and their renowned mutton chop were culinary behemoths, yet they didn't compromise on tenderness or flavor - both were cooked to succulent perfection. The delicious fare was complemented by the historic ambiance of the place, making the dining experience unique and memorable. Friendly staff rounded out the experience, ensuring that every aspect of the meal was enjoyable. A must-visit for anyone appreciating classic dishes done right.

Fun brunch spot! Great views and the DJ was spinning good (loud) music! Came on a Sunday afternoon and it was packed. Looked like a popular place to celebrate a special occasion. Tip- make sure your full party's present otherwise they won't seat you. Everyone at our table of 8 got the prix fixe deal that comes with an appetizer and main dish. We didn't all have to participate, but we went for it anyway! Great deal - the appetizers were full size dishes. In hindsight we realized half of us should've gotten the deal to share the appetizers since we were all pretty full before our main dishes even came, but it was worth it!Our table started with two orders of chips and Guac. Good portion of guac for all to share. Tried the spicy chicken sandwich and burger for main dishes and the mac n cheese and donuts for appetizers. The spicy chicken sandwich was disappointing and not that tasty. I'd recommend the burger, which came with an over-easy fried egg and super crispy tater tots!

There's a lot of Mexican restaurants that are similar to this hole in the wall in Hell's kitchen. I used to work on 11th Ave and 46 so I've tried many of them. This place is OK if you're in a hurry, but the food is nothing special. The menu is pretty limited. Seems like they recently changed it to offer more gringo friendly items such as burritos, burritos, burritos.If you're not in a rush and want to find someplace great you'll come back to, keep looking. But if you want a taco and then hit the road, it will do.

Title: Serene Brunch Escape at Harlem Ale House

My experience at Harlem Ale House in Central Harlem was the epitome of a perfect, low-key brunch. The bar was comfortably quiet on a Sunday, with just a handful of other patrons, offering the calm reprieve we were seeking from the often crowded and boisterous brunch scene.

The service was a highlight, with an amiable woman – possibly the manager or owner – ensuring our orders were taken with warmth and friendliness. Although the selection of draft beers was unfortunately limited and several menu items were not available due to delivery issues, her amiable nature and helpful recommendations softened the disappointment.

Despite not being able to try the anticipated crabmeat hash, the alternative dishes arrived promptly and were thoroughly enjoyable, leaving us without complaints. With the hope that the full menu will be restored by my next visit, Harlem Ale House remains a charming spot for a comfortable and satisfying brunch.

The Mughlai special is a great deal. For $16, you get an appetizer, entree, naan, and condiments. I chose to get the aloo papri chaat and saag paneer. I was pleasantly surprised by the appetizer; it was larger than I expected and delicious! The aloo papri chaat is a cold appetizer of chickpeas and potatoes with a tangy tamarind sauce. The saag paneer wasn't bad but could use a little more flavor. It was a little on the weak side. It comes with rice. The naan seemed fresh. It was nice and soft! The Mughlai special comes with a lot of food, enough for two meals. The food isn't spicy at all, which is exactly how I like it. I also had a mango lassi which was thick and sweet.Everything was nicely packaged to prevent spillage and they even added paper plates and not the flimsy kind either! I would definitely order from this restaurant again! Thank you, Mughlai, for being open during the pandemic and feeding my lazy ass!

Such an incredibly beautiful restaurant on the fifth floor of Hudson Yards.  The service is good, with the exception that they do cater heavily to the alcohol drinkers and not so much to the non-drinkers. Possibly because the tab will be less?  Idk.  Some of us felt invisible. That being said, the food is incredible.  The presentation is beautiful.  It's on the pricey side but it's worth every cent.

I recently visited the much-hyped spot famous for its viral milkshakes and it lived up to the buzz! The milkshake was expertly crafted, boasting playful toppings, including a whole ice cream sandwich that added a delightful twist. Despite arriving mid-afternoon on a Tuesday, there was a significant wait of about 40 minutes, but the experience was worth it if you're not in a hurry. The staff was quick and cordial, enhancing the overall positive experience. Definitely a place I'd revisit!

Cortile was super amazing from the excellent customer service to the delicious food. I would like to start off with giving props to our excellent server Angelo; we were a big party of 12 he had a lot to work with but he was a pro. Angelo went above and beyond, I wanted a sweet wine and typically The Muscato that I wanted you had to buy it by the bottle but I didn't want a bottle I just wanted a glass so instead of me having to purchase a bottle Angelo open up a bottle for me to have 1 glass. The bread that was provided was warm and tasty. My sausage pasta was the perfect portion and it was very good. Typically when there is a big party the restaurant do not like to split the  check but Angelo went above and beyond and split our tab into four receipts making everyone happy. Cortile is a must go to when in Little Italy you will not be disappointed.

Title: A Hip and Tasty Experience at The Tang

The Tang, located on the Upper West Side, offers a refreshing blend of modern aesthetic and culinary delight that caters well to both adventurous foodies and Chinese cuisine enthusiasts. As someone who isn't fluent in Chinese but knows a good dish when I taste one, I was thoroughly impressed with the array of offerings at this vibrant spot. Despite some debates among my native Chinese companions regarding the authenticity of certain dishes, I found the quality and flavor to be top-notch, reflecting the diverse interpretations of Chinese cooking, much like the regional variations found in Italian cuisine in Italy.

With its affordable prices and lively atmosphere, The Tang hits the mark on creating a comfortable yet energizing dining environment. The youthful staff adds to the charm, and the open kitchen provides a glimpse of the culinary action, contributing to the overall experience.

Watching the cooks casually sample their creations while expertly preparing meals was not only entertaining but to me, a sign of confidence in their food. If you're looking for a place with good vibes and delicious eats on the UWS, The Tang is certainly worth a visit.

It's yummy. You come here for the hand pulled noodles and it delivers. I got the regular hand pulled noodles with roasted duck. Decent portion of vegetables mixed with it and the sauce is good but not overwhelming. Don't expect great service. It's a typical Chinese restaurant so you're in and out. You will get crammed into a table and be sitting next to a complete stranger. But they give you your order and they will give you tea and water. Basic service and no frills. I'm giving four and not five stars because of the meat portion. The duck pieces were few and most of them were fatty and I couldn't even eat most of it. I also tried the pan fried chicken and vegetable dumplings- they weren't terrible but they weren't great. You can get better dumplings elsewhere in Chinatown. The noodles were good. And that's what you come here for.

The lunch special is a great value!  For $13 you get an appetizer, soup or salad, and an entree.  The food is good, not great, but good.  The service is friendly but not the most attentive.  The restaurant is clean and has nice decor and ambiance.  We had the chive pancakes, spring rolls, pad thai, tom kha soup, cashew chicken, and massaman curry.  Also something to note, they do not give refills on sodas.

Tiny place with interesting seats. The view from the window is nice but good place to have brunch for only two people. I cannot believe that it can fit more. I have to say the service is pretty bad. I ordered the smoothie and turned out that the waiter didn't order for me. The food is good, normal brunch. Not very special.

Having been a longtime patron of this establishment, it's with disappointment that I report a notable decline in the quality of their spanakopita. Once a delightful dish, the spinach pie has been transformed into something resembling a Hot Pocket, disappointingly scant on filling. The balance has shifted to an overwhelming amount of filo pastry, leaving a trace amount of the spinach and feta that once made it special. Regrettably, this change signifies a severe cutback that has influenced my decision not to return.

Title: Generous Portions, but Misses the Mark on Texture

If you're a fan of hearty portions and aren't too particular about noodle thickness, Yin Ji's rice rolls are a commendable option after Joe's Steam Rice Rolls. They serve up their dishes with remarkable generosity, offering up to two pieces of meat with each bite, which is quite the leap from the norm at Joe's. Expect to pay $7-8 here, which is a step up from the usual price, but the quantity of meat provided justifies the cost.

The shrimp and beef rice rolls stand out, thanks to the cubed meat that's tastefully marinated—this dish was a highlight for me. However, I'd suggest you pass on the pork rice rolls. Although the intention to be generous with the soy sauce is appreciated, it's a tad too sweet for my palate. Furthermore, the pork comes in chunkier pieces, which isn't my preference.

Note that the rice noodles at Yin Ji aren’t quite as delicate as those at Joe's; the first layer may be translucent, but the subsequent layers lose that finesse. If the noodle's texture is a deal-breaker for you, this might not be your top pick.

In essence, Yin Ji secures second place with its abundant meat fillings and well-seasoned beef, despite the noodles lacking the thin, refined quality of their top competitor, Joe's.

(See attached pictures for noodle comparison.)

I was excited to support a local Thai restaurant during these difficult times and ordered takeout on May 2, 2020. However, my experience was underwhelming. The Pad See Ew, typically a favorite of mine, was disappointingly overcooked. The noodles were reduced to mush, which detracted significantly from my enjoyment of the meal despite the flavors being satisfactory. I'm hesitant to return after this experience. #NoMoreThai.
Very good food. Would recommend sharing everything, as it is great to try a little bite of all the wonderful food. Highly recommend the khachipuri adjaruli and the phkali trio.

They don't accept reservations, and the place is pretty small so it's best to come with a small group. Our party of four came in on a Thursday at around 6. There were no tables available so we sat at the counter by the window. Slightly uncomfortable, but not the worst. I had the spicy ginger stamina ramen (comes with a half boiled egg, pork belly, ground pork, cabbage, bean sprouts, chives, scallions, cilantro, shredded ginger, shredded and chopped red pepper and spicy oil) that everyone is talking about, and it did not disappoint. The noodles were perfect, and the broth wasn't too salty or spicy. Plus, I think it's slightly less expensive than those other popular ramen spots (which I don't even think are that good). Definitely recommend this place if you are in the mood for some noods!

One of the best meals I had in NY. We started with the Calamari which was perfectly flash fried. I had the Bone-in Filet with the Asparagus with Hollandaise Sauce and Chophouse Corn. Everything was cooked stupendously. The Butter Cake is a definite must get, you can pass on the Chocolate Cake.

Stopped in before a movie and was able to sit at the bar and grab coffee and food in less than an hour. Opted for the BBQ Turkey Burger with fried onions and sweet potato fries on the side and it was so tasty. The small size of fries felt more like a large and would work for sharing. They have all milk types for the coffee since they have a coffee window. Service was attentive without being overbearing. Would go back when in the area!
The place is small but packs a big punch. The music along with the delicious crepes are sure to keep you coming back. Try the Sugar and Lemon cake with Ice Cream!

I had a wonderful dinner here and would recommend it for a nice date night. There's a cozy, intimate atmosphere and the staff are all so friendly and attentive. They recommended a sake for us based on our taste preferences, and we did love it! For food, we had the avocado fries (a must-try for the amazing dipping sauce), which came out piping hot and freshly fried. We got three rolls to share between two people: rainbow, sake hana, and spider. I personally loved the sake hana because of the eel; it was surprisingly crispy! My man loved the spider because of the soft shell crab tempura. They even gave a few pieces of the tempura on the side. I made reservations through Yelp.

I had the pleasure of dining at a gem of a restaurant where the authentic Spanish food truly transports you. The ambiance felt genuinely warm and inviting, reminiscent of a cozy eatery in Spain. Their sangria was an absolute delight, a perfect balance of fruity and refreshing, enhancing the dining experience.

For dinner, I indulged in a fresh, well-composed salad, and the sides served with it were deliciously complementing the main course. Although there was a wait for the table, it was well worth the patience. The highlight, apart from the cuisine, was the exceptional service; attentive, friendly, and efficient.

In conclusion, the restaurant provides an authentic Spanish culinary experience accompanied by superb service that I would eagerly recommend to anyone in search of a slice of Spain.

I have saw this place all over social media and was super excited to come here with my friends. We arrived around 1 pm on a Saturday and the place itself was not super crowded there were plenty of empty seats around, but they were throwing a huge birthday party in the back. The place itself was super cozy and our waiter was super nice and friendly. They have a lot of different options but we knew that we wanted to try out their pizzas! -Burrata Pizza: this was what we were most excited for, as this is probs their most popular or most hyped item since it is the item that is featured most on social media. This was pretty good! Super cheese-y but it went well with the pizza. -Egg's Benedict Pizza: This one was a unique take on your usual brunch food: egg's benedict. I was a little skeptical of this combination, but it really worked. The flavors went extremely well together. -Avocado Pizza: This was VERRYY refreshing compared to the other two pizza. It was very light and tasted pretty "healthy" but in a good way. It was a good balance between the two "heavier" pizzas. -Italian Stuffed French Toast: This was a nice end to our brunch because it felt like dessert. It was on the sweet side so if you are not into sweet brunch foods, I would pass on this, but it was pretty good. Our food came out fairly quickly and it was absolutely delicious. I can totally see myself coming back in the future!

Read the good reviews and decided we had to give Coco a try. The restaurant has a nice, distinctly French ambience and is located in a quaint square of the Meatpacking District near the Gansevoort. I ordered the Salmon which was frankly a superb dish; the fish had a nice crisp skin while being cooked perfectly. It was paired with a tasty side of Israeli cous cous and some of the best broccoli rabe I've had. Paired with a light rosé, the meal capped off a very nice summer day. We shared the chocolate soufflé for desert which was just the right balance of richness and lightness. If you're in NY and want an authentic French meal at a price that won't break your wallet and great service to match the quality of the food, give Coco a try before positive press/reviews makes it tough to get into!

Awesome pizza joint diagonally across from Madison Square Garden. There's tons of pizza by the slice options. You can also order a whole pie. There's plenty of seating and a public restroom. Cash only but there is an ATM inside. I ordered a slice of the Suprema (thin) and a slice of the pepperoni Fra Diavolo (Sicilian style With no mozzarella). The crust on both was awesomely tasty. The sauce is also delicious.

The perfect middle ground between New York style and deep dish at the best price I've found for Detroit style. You get the delicious thick crust without feeling like you have a tire in your stomach afterwards, and the caramelized cheese on the crust might be the best part. If you're in the area and want a cheap quick bite I can't imagine finding a better deal than the plain person pie for a little more than 5$. Adding the pepperoni is well worth the extra cost, it completely covers the pie (and is double stacked on some parts) and has a nice flavorful kick to it. I've had mixed experiences with some of the other toppings, but the sausage and mustard seems to be the classic Detroit style option and I enjoyed it. Wasn't as big of a fan of the vodka sauce, but that also seems to be pretty popular.

I really like this place. The staff is so friendly and helpful. They answered any questions I had. And when they called out my order and I didn't hear them, they brought it to me. They were kind and polite. The food tasted really good. And the price was reasonable. I missed the lunch special. But I was able to get beef with vegetables with brown rice and a bottle of soda for $20.91.I got the small size. But that portion was plenty. They have plenty of seating. They said I could sit as long as I liked. I had some time to pass before the event I was going to. There are restrooms. And they accept credit cards. And their air conditioning is great. I left a Kosher restaurant a few blocks down cause it was like an oven inside. But here it is nice and cool.

Title: A Mixed Experience at a Buzzed-About NYC Eatery

During a weekend trip to NYC, my friends and I decided to check out a small restaurant we had seen in a Facebook video—possibly a Buzzfeed feature. The place itself was quite compact, and a minor inconvenience was the lack of a restroom, which meant we had to seek one elsewhere.

On the plus side, the service was commendable; the staff were genuinely friendly and accommodating. As for the food, our feelings were mixed. While we weren't blown away as anticipated—perhaps the hype had set our expectations a tad too high—it wasn't a letdown either. A standout was their Mango Chile, a unique flavor that delighted us and is definitely recommended.

In summary, while the restaurant may not have fully lived up to the viral hype, it offered a decent meal with great service and one particularly memorable dish.

The Kati Roll Company presents a refreshing take on Indian cuisine with its out-of-the-box offerings. However, the establishment's size leaves much to be desired; it's a tiny space that quickly feels overcrowded. Service speed suffered during my visit, with a 25-minute wait for food in a stuffy room dampening the experience. While the flavors hit the mark, the small portions, particularly the scant amount of protein in the rolls, were a letdown. I left the venue still feeling hungry, reluctant to endure another lengthy wait for a second helping. I'm open to giving it another chance during a quieter time, hoping for a more comfortable dining experience.

Title: A Gem in the East Village: The Copper Still

If you find yourself in the East Village with a hankering for a cozy spot that almost invites you to belt out "Galway Girl," The Copper Still might just be your place. On a personal note, it's become a staple for my brother and me—it's conveniently a block from his place, and we drop by every chance we get.

Don't let the size of the menu fool you; this establishment proves that less is more. With a focused selection of dishes, they've perfected what they serve. Take the Brussels sprouts, for instance; they're a side that eats like a feast. Meanwhile, my brother swears by their sliders and fries—frequent indulgences that are small in size but pack a flavorful punch.

Amidst the cornucopia of eateries on 2nd Ave, The Copper Still stands out with its laid-back yet lively atmosphere and attentive staff. It's the kind of place you shouldn't overlook when the area offers you an abundance of choices. Whether for a pint of Guinness or a comforting meal, The Copper Still is a choice you'll be glad to make.

This review is my wife's opinion...the best thing about this place was the toasted bread. She was under the impression the crab and/or lobster would be hot. It was served cold with melted butter(that was cold too). Just overall not impressed.

Title: A Slice of Thailand in NYC at Top Thai

If you're in search of a spot that suits virtually any dining occasion – whether it's a romantic evening, a girls' night out, a gathering with the boys, a formal business dinner, or even a reflective solo meal – look no further than Top Thai's new location. With seating for over 100 guests, it's clear from the moment you step in why this establishment has quickly become the go-to for authentic Thai cuisine in New York City.

My recent visit, prompted by a friend's suggestion for a girls' night, proved that Top Thai is indeed "the bomb dot com." Their success in crafting an immersive atmosphere is undeniable. The decor transported me straight back to my travels in Chang Mai, with servers decked out in traditional Thai garb enhancing the authentic vibe. The layout is a thoughtful nod to Thailand itself, complete with a display tuk tuk and intricately placed light fixtures and trinkets reminiscent of the country's bustling floating markets.

Our server, Eric, was exceptional, enriching our experience by sharing the restaurant's history and guiding us through the menu with expertise. Now, let's get to the heart of the matter: the food and drinks. The Thai ice tea took me right back to the streets of Chang Mai, while Singha beer was on deck for a perfect pairing. The kitchen's magic ensured that each dish arrived promptly and brimming with rich, well-balanced flavors. And as someone who doesn't eat pork, I was thrilled to find a Halal menu, eliminating any dietary concerns.

The culinary journey featured an array of tantalizing appetizers including various types of dumplings, calamari, and curry puffs. The entrees were truly a standout, especially the three spice red snapper and the crispy duck with basil atop udon noodles – both bursting with zest and beautifully presented. With generous portions that are as pleasing to the eye as they are to the palate, Top Thai secures its position at the pinnacle of New York's Thai dining scene. Whether you're a local or just passing through, this gem is a must-visit for a genuine taste of Thailand.

I recently visited this restaurant with friends and had a wonderful experience. If you're in the mood for curry, this is the perfect place to go. We arrived at a non-peak time, 3pm on a weekday, and were seated immediately without any wait. Service was swift, and before we knew it, our meals were served, piping hot and full of flavor.

The curry here is truly exceptional – rich, aromatic, and satisfying. Portions were generous, leaving us feeling contently full for hours. The price was reasonable too; we paid about $20 each after tax and tip, which felt quite fair given the quality and quantity of the food served.

All things considered, this restaurant is a fantastic choice for anyone craving a curry delight.

One of the best pizza! I ordered a square pepperoni pizza and one slice was so fulfilling and flavorful. It was served hot and the sauce and pepperoni were a great combination. The crust is not too thick and still has great chewy texture. The place definitely draws a crowd so be prepare to wait in line.

This was my first time at Bareburger but it was a great time. They recently revamped their menu and now include a full vegetarian/vegan side. I promptly ordered a strawberry shake and one of the preset vegan burgers, their take on the Big Mac. You also have the option to make a burger and with many options (lentil base, beets, impossible, chickpeas) for the burger itself you can't go wrong. Fries come separate but if there's two of you it's a better deal to get a medium or large fry than each get a small order. We got the sweet potato and regular fries split half and half. Yes, you can do such a thing and it's great!! They also have mimosa specials but the sparkling wine was out so we went with sangria. The food came maybe 15-20 minutes later and it was sooooooo good. You always worry about a place overcooking their veggie burgers because they don't know what they're doing, but Bareburger gets it right. The burgers have a heart sign on the bun when it arrives and it's adorable. Our waitress was lovely and checked in on us at all the right moments. I also loved that we had a jar of water just for our table. Bareburger is a fantastic spot for your vegan fare and I'm already looking forward to a return.

What a great experience. It's a little loud overall but the service was wonderful and the food was excellent. They have a variety of speciality food while having a few of the normal. The veggies that came with the goat stew were phenomenal and crunchy, perfectly seasoned. The staff was  really nice and when the table we wanted was reserved later in the meal the host came over and apologized for not being able to seat us there. Super SUPER sweet staff that worked well together to get people in and out. Make a reservation, Friday nights are busy. ENJOY!

Stepping into Bessou provides a welcomed respite from the relentless energy of New York City, its quaint and cozy ambience offering a delightful escape. Arriving on a Friday evening to a moderately busy scene, the atmosphere hinted at the necessity of reservations for future visits, particularly for larger parties.

The space at Bessou strikes a pleasant balance, suitable for both romantic dates and laid-back gatherings. The practice of sharing an array of dishes comes highly recommended. Our party of six opted for five selections: chicken karaage, soy ginger branzino, smashed potatoes, prawns in chili oil, and a seafood hotpot.
