A tip for the chicken karaage: request it to be halved due to its generous size. While standard in flavor, the shiso tzatziki accompanying it was notably refreshing without overpowering the palate. The steamed soy ginger branzino, tender in its foil wrap, relied more on its garnish for zest. The smashed potatoes were a standout, their harmony with the mentaiko aioli meriting particular praise.

The prawns, more akin to shrimp, were pleasantly seasoned with a chili oil that provided heat without diminishing other flavors. The seafood hotpot's abundant offerings made it perfect for sharing, and came paired with rice and nori, rounding out the meal. Service proved attentive, with staff eager to recommend their favorites.

Overall, Bessou made for an enjoyable dining experience, serving up refreshing dishes sure to entice a return visit for anyone in the neighborhood.

Title: Swift Service and Tasty Eats at Local Gem

I recently decided to grab takeout via Yelp from this spot, and the experience was notably efficient—my order was ready in a mere 10 minutes. The menu selection was tempting, and I indulged in a cheesesteak hoagie and buffalo chicken cheesesteak salad, accompanied by a side of plain fries.

The hoagie was a standout, generously sized and bursting with flavor, easily providing enough for two servings. It's a must-try, and despite a slightly premium price, it's something I'd consider splurging on again. The buffalo chicken cheesesteak salad was enjoyable, though its cost-to-delight ratio makes a repeat order less compelling for me.

While the fries were decent, they didn't maintain their crispness on the journey home, arriving with a bit of sogginess after a 15-minute wait.

Prices across the board seem influenced by the location, and while I find them on the higher end, the hoagie could tempt me back. Post-pandemic, I'm eager to return and experience the atmosphere of their bar firsthand.

My best friend recommended a hidden gem of a restaurant and, even with them unable to join, we ventured forward. The food exceeded expectations; the sake flight variety was commendable. Our server, Karma, paired impeccable service with deep menu knowledge. Highlights included the melt-in-your-mouth Hokkaido umami carpaccio and the must-try unagi kabayaki - pricey at $45 but worth every cent. The staff's 'break the wood' ceremony added a hilarious touch to my boyfriend's belated birthday celebration, complete with a complimentary dessert. Overall, an unforgettable dining experience.

The steakhouse presented itself as a purveyor of aged meats, a claim that unfortunately did not translate onto the plate; the steak lacked the distinctive taste of aging. Surprisingly, the side dishes of baked potatoes and creamed spinach stole the show, overshadowing the main event. Service was efficient and professional, yet it lacked the warmth one might appreciate, possibly a byproduct of the bustling NYC atmosphere. All in all, the experience was decidedly average, not quite living up to the expectations set by its promises.

After a couple of years since my last visit to the bustling original Chloe in Soho, my recent dining experience at the Chloe outpost was a tranquil delight. The famous quinoa salad remains as refreshingly addictive as ever, and the unique lemonade—infused with a minty cucumber twist—was so delightful that we couldn't resist ordering more. The serenity of the place, perhaps due to our early dinner timing, was a stark contrast to the frenetic energy of its Soho counterpart, offering a more spacious and peaceful environment that was much appreciated.

Chloe caters to all, from children amused by coloring books and crayons to health-conscious families and the Instagram-savvy crowd seeking photogenic meals. That said, the establishment could benefit from more attentive table cleaning and swifter service. Overall, a pleasant and tasty experience, reflective of Chloe's reputation but with the added comfort of space and quiet.

I think this burger joint deserves much more love than it gets here on yelp...we tried it cuz it was literally across the street from our hotel & we wanted something fast/easy before a Broadway show we needed to be off to asap. Timing was great, lines not long, plenty of seating. Pleasant surprise of live music. Family friendly for sure, lots of tourists with shopping bags. We had a great & knowledgeable waitress who successfully unsold us on a fun cocktail & one of their local beers. Burger was great & obscenely huge. I would revisit, get another cucumber mojito & order a smaller burger! Recommend fries over the onion rings, FYI.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Sweetness at Spot Dessert Bar

My friends and I stumbled upon Spot Dessert Bar in East Village on a bustling Saturday night. With hopes high, we opted to share the milky puff 3 way. The dessert hit the right notes on taste, but unfortunately, it fell short on presentation; it was messy and didn't mirror the advertised image. Despite the flavors being on point, the overall value didn't justify the double-digit price tag. The portion did not stand out compared to other New York dessert haunts. However, the unique offerings of Spot have piqued my interest enough to warrant another visit, albeit sparingly, more for the novelty than anything else.

Title: A Stellar Evening of French Cuisine and Wine

From the moment we were seated with a view of the kitchen's bustling action, our experience at this Michelin-starred gem was nothing short of exceptional. The wine selection is outstanding, capturing the essence of a perfect pairing with each dish.

The four-course dinner, priced at 155, is a culinary delight, particularly when accompanied by the recommended wines. The standout dish, langostino tartare, was a symphony of flavors, melting delightfully in the mouth. Meanwhile, the himachi black truffle was another winner, starting our meal on a high note.

The presentation of the sturgeon tart, enveloped in aromatic smoke, was both a visual and gastronomic pleasure. The lamb for two, our main course, was cooked to perfection, and the chocolate and grape sorbet dessert was an exquisite finale to a magnificent meal.

Service throughout the evening was flawless; attentive without being intrusive. For anyone fond of refined French cuisine without the commitment of an extensive meal, this restaurant strikes a perfect balance.

Highly recommended for its excellent food and service, this establishment has rightfully earned its Michelin star.

Title: Tasty Pizza with a Side of New York Charm

I recently dined at a local pizzeria that served up some seriously good slices. Several friends in my group opted for the special, a budget-friendly deal at $5.95 for two slices of cheese pizza and a drink. I went for a mix, snagging a slice of the classic cheese and the buffalo chicken. The buffalo chicken pizza was the standout for me; it had just the right kick, especially when I added a drizzle of what I believe was Red Hot sauce, along with some ranch from the convenient condiment bottles.

While I personally think Tony's takes the top spot, this place still delivers a slice worth savoring. It might not fold as effortlessly due to the crispier crust, but the flavor didn't disappoint. I'd definitely come back for more.

Service? Swift and no-nonsense. And as for the ambiance, there was no trouble finding a seat to enjoy that New York pizzeria experience. In short, this pizzeria is a solid choice for anyone craving a good pizza in the city.

Title: A Gem with a Slight Rough Edge – Otto's Dining Experience

My evening at Otto's was an impressive affair from the moment I stepped through the door. Despite a rough start with one of the bald bartenders, who had been rather brusque with my friends, I addressed the issue, and we moved past it to enjoy his expertly crafted old fashioned.

The wine selection was tempting, and we indulged in an organic Cabernet priced at $65. Unfortunately, it packed more of a punch than anticipated, leaving a reminder the next day that organic doesn't equate to hangover-free.

The cuisine was the standout feature of the night. The Squid Ink Pasta with shrimp was a bold choice that paid off with its rich flavors, and the classic pie – simplicity perfected – showcased the kitchen's prowess with Italian classics. A ball of mozzarella paired with prosciutto was a delightful dance of textures and tastes.

Service was another highlight, thanks to our waiter, Mike. Attentive and earnest, he ensured our evening was as comfortable as it was delicious. 

While the encounter with the bartender was a hiccup in an otherwise flawless evening, the sumptuous food and exceptional service at Otto's have secured my return for future celebrations.

My best friend suggested this place.  I've never tried Peruvian food before but she raved about it and I decided to give it a try. The food here is incredible! I ordered the 1/4 chicken with maduros and white rice as well as a tres leche cake.I surely was not disappinted at all! The food was fresh, hot and delicious. The chicken is very tender and so is the rice. If you eat here do not forget to get the  green sauce to add some extra flavor to your meal.No complaints about Chirp, it's a winner in my eyes!! One of the best new discoveries for me!

After a long day at work, I stumbled upon a gem in the heart of the city. Their pizza slice, priced at a typical New York $3, exceeded expectations – it was simply phenomenal. Alongside, I indulged in garlic knots that struck the perfect balance between moistness and a generous hit of garlic, exactly to my taste.

Surprisingly spacious, the restaurant offered plenty of seating, dismissing the usual hustle of a grab-and-go joint. The walls, adorned with photographs, narrated a story of fame and acclaim, featuring an array of celebrities from the silver screen to the music stage.

In a city that never sleeps and is crowded with culinary options, this place stands out for its top-notch pizza and an ambiance that celebrates its well-deserved reputation. A must-visit for both pizza aficionados and those who appreciate a slice of New York's vibrant food scene.

I recently visited this charming restaurant and had a delightful experience. I started with a twist on the traditional mojito, opting for Sprite instead of club soda, which added a pleasant sweetness to the drink. The server was commendable for their attentiveness throughout the meal.

The highlight, however, was the Rockaway pizza - a beautiful creation featuring a rich vodka sauce paired with creamy burrata mozzarella, all topped with fresh basil. Not only was the pizza delicious, but it was also satisfyingly filling. Overall, it was a simple yet remarkable culinary experience that I would recommend to anyone seeking a cozy meal with a touch of elegance.

Title: A Hidden Gem That’s Worth the Wait

From the moment you descend the steps into this captivating establishment, the allure of a well-kept culinary secret enfolds you. The bustling atmosphere is a testament to the restaurant's popularity, with eager patrons waiting for a chance to savor the widely talked-about dishes.

I navigated the crowds with ease using the Yelp Waitlist—a lifesaver during the busy dinner rush—and I highly suggest you do the same. The cozy bar near the waiting area is a pleasant surprise, offering tempting happy hour deals to kick-start the experience.

The menu is a food lover's dream, stretching from perfectly crafted dumplings to tantalizing sushi and rice dishes. I indulged in the Salmon Sashimi tacos, which were a revelation with their fresh ingredients encased in a flawlessly crispy shell. The sushi selection did not disappoint, with each roll surpassing the last in taste and presentation, particularly the house specialty roll that seemed to be a favorite among diners.

This establishment not only lives up to the hype but also exceeds expectations with its exceptional service and delectable cuisine. Be prepared for a bit of a wait, but rest assured, it's utterly worth it.

A true New York staple, this eatery's artichoke pizza is a revelation – super dense, brimming with rich flavor, and a delightfully creamy texture. Be warned, the heartiness means one slice usually suffices. The fresh artichokes are a standout, masterfully cooked. A must-visit for any NYC trip; it's a culinary experience that surely won't disappoint.

What a great location. Beautiful al fresco dining and great decor inside. This is a must try. The warm bread is served with olive oil, olives and a vert tender artichoke. Yum! Next up we had the calamari/shrimp appetizer who was lightly breaded and delish. The course timing was perfect. Everything we ordered was freshly made and the perfect temperature. The entrees were the right size as we planned to do some bar hopping and catch a comedy show. You will definitely be satisfied with the portion size. It's enough that you'll be satiated, but won't need a "doggy bag" to carry around the city all night.

Title: A Slurp-Worthy Experience at the Local Ramen Joint

My recent visit to this noodle haven was nothing short of delightful. The craving for Tonkotsu ramen was strong, and this place did not disappoint. Getting seated was a breeze; the lack of a waiting line was a pleasant surprise.

I opted for a customized bowl, dialing up the dashi to a robust intensity with a full clove of garlic, scallions, and extra-rich flavors. The chashu adorned my dish with a slightly salty edge, but it was just to my liking. I played it safe with the heat - half spicy red sauce, but there's room to crank it up on a future visit. The firmer noodles were an impeccable choice for texture.

Each spoonful of the soup burst with savory goodness, and the soft boiled egg added a creamy decadence. Yes, at $24, it's not an everyday eat, but the exceptional quality and service justify the splurge. This experience has me looking forward to a culinary adventure at their sister restaurant in Osaka.

In summary, if you're in for an authentic and customizable ramen experience, this spot is a must-try. Highly recommended for those willing to pay a bit extra for a premium dining encounter.

This falafal in a lafah ($13) must have been one of the most filling, healthiest, delicious and freshest wraps I've had. Its filled with vegetables, that add flavor and texture, the lafah is so good, tastes like food you would have at home. The owner, is a pleasure to speak with, makes everyone who comes in feel welcome. You will leave with a smile. Yesssss this is my falafal spot!

I visited the restaurant on a Tuesday evening at 8pm and was delighted to be seated immediately. Our orders for the evening were the smith bar steak and the skirt steak, both topped with a savory garlic herb butter. There was a slight mix-up as I didn't get to choose between fries or salad for the side, and fries were served by default. Nonetheless, the portion was impressively generous.

The side of jalapeño cheese grits we tried was outstanding and comes highly recommended. Our main courses arrived promptly; however, there was a slight issue with the doneness of our steaks - the bar steak, requested medium, was actually more rare than the skirt steak we'd asked to be rare. Despite this, the flavors were enjoyable, particularly the garlic herb butter.

Overall, the experience was positive with room for some improvements in service.

Title: Nautical Nibbles and Sips at Pilot – Brooklyn's Secluded Summer Gem

Pilot sits like a hidden treasure at the serene end of Brooklyn Bridge Park, offering a delightful escape from the urban sprawl without truly leaving the city. The setting aboard this vessel grants diners extraordinary views of the Manhattan skyline shimmering across the East River—a vista that truly captures the essence of summer in New York.

The cocktail menu, albeit steep at $15-16 each, shines with creative concoctions. A standout is the Spirit Animal—a whimsical mix of rum, Aperol, coconut, lemon, and strawberry, served in a playful pink that unexpectedly educates patrons on the hue of hippo milk. This refreshing blend earns its stripes as the quintessential summer libation.

Be prepared for a charge on water, which initially raises eyebrows until the rationale is revealed: maintaining potable water on a boat has its costs. The added bonus is that your hydration supports a charitable cause, softening the blow to your wallet.

In summary, Pilot provides an idyllic waterfront dining experience that's worth the navigation through Brooklyn's quieter pathways. Just be mindful of your beverage budget to keep your seafaring adventure afloat.

Title: A Delightful Blend of Speed and Flavor for Family Celebrations

My family and I chose this restaurant to celebrate a belated wedding anniversary alongside Mother's Day, and it didn't disappoint. Booking nearly a month in advance secured us an early dinner slot at 5:30pm, and the restaurant was punctual in both opening its doors and seating us.

The decor immediately set a welcoming scene for our special meal. With two young boys in tow, we were grateful for the swift service, allowing us to order and receive our dishes posthaste.

We sampled a broad range of offerings: the corn fritters were a foolproof start, satisfyingly deep-fried. Our children devoured the yellow rice, prompting a second order. The crispy baby squid and chicken satay, though different from the versions I cherished in my childhood, were commendable renditions. The clams and steamed cod with asparagus were flavorful, and the generous portion of lobster in the lobster noodles was a highlight, although a little more noodle to accompany it would have been preferred.

Despite the appealing menu, our children's restlessness meant we missed out on dessert. A notable mention is the sambal sauce that came with the squid—it was a standout and paired wonderfully with the dish. The spice levels seemed to skew higher for the kids' palates, so families take note.

In summary, the restaurant offered a pleasant experience with its efficient service and tasty Indo-inspired cuisine. It's certainly on the list for a future visit—next time, hopefully, including dessert.

Title: Solid Choice for a Casual Dinner

My dining experience at this spot was generally positive, particularly for those looking for a swift and satisfying meal. I opted for the lobster mac n' cheese which, while enjoyable, was a touch too milky and could have benefited from a stronger cheese flavor to meet my tastes. Nevertheless, it was a pleasant dish. My companion's choice, the fish n' chips, was exemplary; the fish was cooked to perfection, avoiding any hint of dryness, paired with fries that struck an excellent balance between crispiness and a fluffy interior.

On the value front, the prices didn't disappoint, aligning well with the quality of the meal. Service timing could use improvement—I noted a longer-than-expected wait of 30 minutes for our food despite a nearly empty venue. Yet, this was a minor hiccup in an otherwise complaint-free visit.

Small hole in the wall from the outside but it is actually a lot bigger in the inside. Came here on a whim with a friend on a Saturday night.Got seated immediately, there were a lot of empty tables. Ordered an order of pork soup dumplings, three flavor soup dumpling combo (truffle, crab&pork, and pork) and General Tso's chicken over rice. Prices are super reasonable. All dishes are under or around $10. Between the two of us, we were full/content after eating it all. Bill was around ~$40. The soup dumplings here compared to other places are definitely on the milder side. The soup is not that strong, not as salty. Definitely tastes a lot more clear and somewhat blander--which isn't a bad thing. I feel like the truffle dumplings was a one time thing. Maybe it's worth it to try out once but we agreed it wasn't something to order every time we come here. The general tsos was very good. Service was pretty good, they always kept our water full, food came pretty quickly. 4 stars instead of 5 because it's pretty standard...nothing TOO special. Just a place to eat.

Title: A Satisfying Sunday at Spicy Pot Haven

I visited a local restaurant last Sunday evening with three friends, and we were immediately struck by the calm atmosphere, perhaps due to our early arrival at 5:30 pm. The extensive menu offered a tantalizing array of dry hotpot, stews, and more, but we zeroed in on the dry hotpot—ordering was a counter affair with a customizable ingredient list.

Our group chose both beef and seafood hotpots, ensuring we got a taste of the variety of proteins, which were notably fresh and generously portioned, likely thanks to the pay-by-pound system. However, the selection of green vegetables left more to be desired, both in variety and quantity—our vegetable basket was not as full as we hoped.

Admittedly, as first-timers, the ordering process was a touch confusing, and the staff member assisting us could have been more patient. That said, the delightful flavors and swift service more than made up for the initial hiccup. The food arrived quickly, each bite bursting with flavor, and left us full and our palates tingling from the peppercorns—a testament to the hotpot's authenticity.

In summary, despite a few areas for improvement, the dining experience was one to remember for its delicious food and swift service. I'd recommend this spot to any hotpot enthusiasts looking for a hearty meal and a taste bud adventure.

Title: Quirky Experience on Pancake Day at [Restaurant Name]

I ventured into [Restaurant Name] on March 12th to indulge in their free pancake promotion. Anticipating a massive turnout, I arrived at the early hour of 7 am, hoping to beat the crowds. To my dismay, the service was surprisingly sluggish. Despite the lack of a large crowd, what I expected to be a quick pancake pit-stop turned into an hour-long endeavour.

A light-hearted moment did occur while we were ushered to the waiting area. A curious incident unfolded as a mother and her young daughter entered the restaurant. The child, puzzled by the pancake giveaway, asked her mother if they were commemorating the passing of her grandmother, which couldn't help but elicit chuckles from those around.

Despite the slow service, the whimsical conversation overhead provided a delightful twist to the morning. [Restaurant Name], while not the most efficient, certainly offered a memorable start to the day.

Title: Ichiran's Vegetarian Ramen – A Spicy Delight!

I recently had the pleasure of trying the new vegetarian ramen at Ichiran, and I must say, it's a game-changer for plant-based noodle enthusiasts! You'll need to request the special vegetarian menu, which offers a decent array of customization options, from the spice level to the addition of scallions, garlic, or mushrooms. However, unlike their classic tonkotsu ramen, you can't tweak the oil and salt content.

Diving into my bowl with a level 2 spice, I found it packed quite the punch – adventurous palates might want to venture into level 3 territory! For those keeping it strictly vegetarian, note that the spicy red sauce contains honey, but the rest of the ramen is vegan-friendly. Served up in Ichiran's iconic rectangular bowl, the straight noodles were impressively good, holding their own even for someone who typically prefers the curly variety.

The broth was tasty but might lean towards the bland side if not for the spicy sauce's kick. Despite the slightly steep price tag, pushing just over $20, this ramen offering is a solid choice for vegetarians seeking an authentic noodle experience, though it might leave Ippudo devotees weighing their loyalties.

Location: east village bound.  Place seems to be larger than before but still you need to squeeze into space with strangers. Food: had fig , tomato, and complete   Hmmm.fig and tomato tartines are delicious but complete raclette is not what I expected. I guess i would never be a fan of cheese after all these years. Wine selections are good too and cheap. Service: prompt and nice clean. Overall: 3.5 stars. I am no cheese fan so my review could be bias.

Great decor as a somewhat upscale Irish-style pub. Just walking by, this place caught my eye - a bit more of a flair than your average Irish pub in Manhattan. Decided to come for a drink and was greeted with an attentive bar staff. Drink menu is definitely simple, but well made. The Irish food offers a unique touch (including a truffle burger which was great)! Perfect location for not-too-loud happy hour with nice decor and great bar food. Definitely recommend!

Title: Quirky Thai Spot with Room for Taste Improvement

I recently dined at a charming, petite Thai restaurant nestled in Chelsea. While I had high hopes for a stellar culinary experience, I unfortunately encountered a hiccup with the Pad Kee Moa, which struck my palate as oddly flavored and regrettably inedible. On a brighter note, my boyfriend had no such qualms, suggesting a potentially divisive dish.

Thankfully, the meal was partially redeemed by the savory pork chop platter and the Tom Kha soup, both of which were flavorful and enjoyable. On the service front, the staff was nothing short of prompt and congenial, enhancing the dining atmosphere.

A highlight worth mentioning is their adventurous menu, which includes contemporary selections like the impossible meat option - a nod to modern dietary inclinations.

In summary, while there's a slight discrepancy in food quality, the restaurant offers quick service, friendly faces, and a few standout dishes that might just tickle your taste buds.

Title: Satisfying Filipino Fare with a Side of Patience

I recently dined at this cozy Filipino spot on a Thursday evening with two friends, and my experience was a solid 3.5 out of 5 stars. Arriving early is wise, as seating is limited. We indulged in a variety of dishes including the lumpia shanghai, pancit bihon, mouth-watering grilled pork belly, tantalizing tinapang bangus, and fragrant garlic rice. All came in generous portions and were quite palatable, with the pork belly and garlic rice stealing the show.

Despite the delicious food, service lagged due to the presence of only one waitress, and this was with the restaurant not being fully seated. While the prices were slightly above what I'd normally expect for this cuisine, having frequented more budget-friendly Filipino joints in Jersey City and Woodside, they seemed to align with the area's average. If my travels bring me back this way, a return visit could be on the table.

The ramen itself is definitely great. Not the same quality as ICHIRAN Tokyo, but definitely better than most places in nyc. It fell short in two areas though, and I don't think that I'll return for this reason:The wait times were way too long. We spent 45 min in line which I can live with, as the better ramen places do have waits. However once we were seated and ordered, it took another half hour to serve our ramen. That is way too long. Also it's much too expensive for what you get. $25 is a lot for ramen noodles. I'm guessing ICHIRAN's Manhattan location is much more profitable than its Tokyo location... actually given the really slow turnover, maybe not.

Food 3/5.Service 5/5. Overall the food was not that authentic. First course: The pork dumplings and spicy wontons were on point 5/5. Very authentic and best out of the courses. I would compare it to the same quality at the ding tai fung in taiwan. Second course: fried rice with steak. Steak was great and the rice was decent 4/5. Little bit on the pricy side for what you get.Third course: 3 cup chicken. This course was a dud for me. The chicken had the right consistency but the flavor was extremely bland. Three cup chicken should be sweet (coming from a Taiwanese) but this dish was overly salty and lacked the basil punch. I had to ask for it to be returned and swapped it out for the veggie and mao po tofu (both which were much better). 1.5/5 very disappointed. Overall, I would give it another try, but would like to see the three cup chicken improved.

Tucked away in a cozy corner of the neighborhood, this unassuming pizza shop serves up slices that are all about the basics done right. Though seating is limited to a bit of counter space—consider yourself fortunate if you snag a spot—patrons are here for the pizza, not the ambiance. The pepperoni pizza reigns supreme among regulars, generously topped with an ample amount of cheese and a bounty of pepperoni on a hearty dough. My personal favorite, however, was the Margherita pizza. Its thinner crust provided a delightful contrast, with just the right amount of cheese to complement the simple, fresh flavors. Whether you're a pepperoni aficionado or a lover of classic Italian simplicity, this no-frills establishment is well worth a visit.

During an impromptu weekday lunch, I found myself at a steakhouse nestled amidst the corporate landscape of midtown. The establishment exudes a rustic charm, with its brick walls and a delightful bouquet of flowers adorning the bar, where I dined.

In a place celebrated for its meats, I opted for the unconventional choice of a salad, only to be met with disappointment. At $45, the salad failed to impress, coming off as bland and dry, and certainly not outshining something one might pick up at a standard salad bar.

The restaurant presents a unique atmosphere – a curious blend of earnestness with a hint of a laid-back undertone. Although my encounter with their fare didn't inspire a return visit, I appreciate the experience for what it was.

During my visits to the city, I've dined at this charming restaurant twice while meeting up with friends. The ambiance exudes warmth and friendliness, matched by the attentive and pleasant service staff. A standout dish that captures my palate each time is their delightful regular gnocchi pasta – it's a dish I find myself craving long after I've left the table. Highly recommended for a satisfying dining experience.

After a night out with cravings for pizza, we stumbled upon this bustling spot. Despite a lengthy line signaling popularity, it moved swiftly. We opted for two "slice of pep" – a term endearingly used here – and weren't disappointed. Fresh from the oven, our pizzas were almost too hot to handle, necessitating a brief cooling period. Once manageable, we indulged in the perfectly melted, stringy cheese and generously topped pepperoni. For anyone seeking a post-show or late-night bite in New York, this place merits a visit. I'll make sure to return on my next city adventure.

Great ramen spot in Chinatown! I love coming here when I am in the city and craving some ramen. Food is awesome, pricing is reasonable. I got seafood ramen and it was only $11. I felt like I had twice as much noodles as other spots like Zundoya for the same price. Definitely worth the price in my opinion. They also offer some sushi rolls and I thought the Big Boy Roll tasted amazing. If you're ever feeling some classic ramen, this is the place to go.

Title: Bustling Tuesday at Trendy Spot with Hits and Misses

I recently visited this local hotspot on a crowded Tuesday evening and enjoyed an array of dishes with varying degrees of success. The Fried Tiger Prawn with Salted Egg Yolk Plate was a standout, delighting my egg yolk-loving palate with its succulent shrimp. The Mouth Watering Boneless Chicken Thigh Plate, while unexpectedly mild, was nonetheless a tasty and tender treat. The Stir-fried Shredded Cabbage Plate was well-executed with good flavor, although slightly heavy-handed with the sauce.

The Dan Dan Noodle dish fell into the realm of just okay for me, with perfect noodle texture but a dryness that had me reaching for extra sauce. The Minced Pork over Rice was hearty and well-topped but would benefit from a less watery sauce to enhance its flavors.

Unfortunately, the Fried Peppercorn Pork Belly Plate missed the mark completely, with an overly fried preparation that masked the taste of the pork.

Service was warm and attentive amidst the chaos, although there were noticeable glitches with the ordering system, leading to repeated dishes and mix-ups.

Overall, this place is a promising addition to the neighborhood, showing potential amidst its inconsistencies.

Title: A Mushroom Lover's Mixed Experience

My dining experience was a journey through an exciting mushroom-focused menu, with hopes that soared high. The "Fun Guy" dumplings shattered my skepticism, offering a delightful burst of flavor that defied any fear of texture issues. However, the Chili Mushroom Soup left me underwhelmed, its mushroom presence less than I craved.

The "Nutty Buddy" stood out with its tangle of soba noodles and a ponzu sauce that added a fresh zest to the dish. Contrasting this was the "Spicy Mang," which, despite its promising name, lacked the advertised heat and mango infusion, ending up as the biggest disappointment of the meal.

"The Mighty Mushroom" delivered a satisfying chew with its mushroom and baked tofu duo, though it whispered rather than shouted with its subtle flavors. Redemption came in the form of the Lemon Almond Cake – a warm, dense delight with a perfect sweet note, slightly marred by an icy accompaniment.

In summary, while not every dish reached the anticipated heights, the starters and desserts shined, leaving me with an impression of a restaurant that has both areas of brilliance and room for flavor enhancements, particularly in their sushi offerings.

My coworkers and I stopped in here on a Friday mostly for their long ass bar. We tried several other places in the area, but most places were too crowded. Farmhouse (before dinner) was a good compromise. They have lot of classic cocktails (the bartender told us her specialty was the Old Fashioned, and she wasn't lying!). I also had a ginger martini, which was nice and spicy.While we were here, we also ordered a bunch of small plates. The meatballs were great, but the burrata stole the show!The place really started filling up around 7:30-8, so plan accordingly!

Pig heaven is a great experience if you're looking for authentic Taiwanese food with homey dishes!My friend and I ordered the soup dumplings, BBQ ribs, and Pig Heaven chicken. All are great choices! The soup dumplings were delicious and the soup portion was rich. The Pig Heaven chicken is a diced chicken dish that reminded me of home. Super good and not spicy. The BBQ ribs were the big kicker -grab a side of rice and dive in! Each bite has a punch of their great savory marinate and the meat was juicy. A must!I definitely recommend this restaurant. The waiters were nice and informative. They have your standard dishes like fried rice and scallion pancakes but branch out and go for the meats!

Breakfast here was amazing.  We made reservations so we got right in. I got the crunchy French toast with caramel sauce and maple syrup. It was really good. Perfect amount of sweetness.  The hubs got the cheesecake French toast and WOW!!!  Sweetest French toast we've ever tried. Maybe too sweet. First few bites were incredible, then it kind of got to be too much!!  But I'm so glad we got to try it. I didn't like the orange cream on the inside but the hubs did. I'm glad we have this place a try. Pretty pricy compared to most breakfast spots though.
Love the Chicken Patacon! Juicy and flavorful. Very happy on this new addition cart in East Village

Title: A Flavorful Adventure at Fig & Olive During Restaurant Week

I ventured into Fig & Olive for the first time during New York's Restaurant Week and the place was buzzing with activity. The restaurant week menu tantalized us right from the start with a selection of bread and olive oil, including an exceptional orange-flavored variety and an exquisite 18-year-old balsamic vinegar.

The roasted cauliflower appetizer was a winner, perfectly prepared without being too crunchy. The cocktail menu didn't disappoint either; the Moroccan Old Fashion was a refreshing twist on the classic, with unexpected lemony notes.

For the main course, the organic lemon chicken was succulent and satisfying, although the generous portion of the cauliflower made it challenging to finish.

Dessert, while scrumptious, left me wanting more - it was rather small for a dessert aficionado like myself. Service on the night felt a bit scattered and slower than preferred, suggesting room for improvement in organization.

Despite that, my experience was overwhelmingly positive. Fig & Olive certainly knows how to deliver a memorable meal.

Title: A Delectable Escape from Jury Duty at Lan Zhou

Lan Zhou truly lives up to its esteemed reputation. Tucked away within a stone's throw of the courthouse, my jury duty lunch break turned into a culinary adventure at this gem of a noodle house. Following both a trusted friend's recommendation and stellar online reviews, my expectations were high, yet Lan Zhou did not disappoint.

The appetizer set the stage: boiled pork dumplings, impeccably cooked, bursting with succulent juices - a perfect pairing with the tableside hot chili oil and soy sauce for that extra kick.

Opting for something less conventional, I tried the ox tail hand pulled noodle soup. While it was flavorful, the ox tail presented a bit of a challenge compared to the ease of their traditional beef offerings. It's a tasteful nod to the authentic, though next time the beef will likely win my vote.

With a hearty bowl and the tender dumplings, Lan Zhou provided a much-needed respite from civic duties. It's a spot I'll surely return to - jury duty or not.

I recently visited a spot that prides itself on being a "whimsical cocktail bar and full service restaurant," though my experience left me feeling like I had stepped into an upscale dive bar instead. Their claim to fame is an award-winning burger, however, as a non-burger eater, I can't comment on that. I opted for the broccoli, which turned out to be a rather ordinary dish, lacking any noteworthy flavor that might have elevated my visit. Overall, I wasn't particularly impressed.

Emmy Squared serves up delicious Detroit style pizzas, and is a restaurant that you can consistently go to for reliably great food, whether at their West Village location, or newer East Village spot. We'd been to the West Village location previously, and were big fans, so one Saturday night, we decided to drop in spontaneously into the new Emmy Squared. It was about 6ish, and we didn't have a reservation, but we managed to be seated immediately at a table. The staff brought us copies of the menu and waters immediately, and gave us a few moments to order. We decided to share two pizzas between us: the Colony, and the margarita. We'd previously had the colony at their west village restaurant location, and I would have to recommend this as a must-get. With slices of pepperoni, and a drizzle of honey, it's not hard to see why this is one of their most popular pizzas. The margarita pizza was something we could have done without. As Emmy squared serves thicker, Detroit-style pizzas, I feel like the thicker base of these pizzas are more suited to heavier toppings, rather than the lighter Neapolitan style pizzas which are suited to having just a few. It was not bad, but we both thought we would have enjoyed another pizza with more toppings even more. Service was friendly and efficient. The ambience here would suit diners looking for a casual meal, and prices are likewise reflected. This is a solid spot downtown for anyone looking for Detroit style pizzas and hearty food.

Title: A Toast to Tantalizing Tipples and Delectable Dishes

My recent visit to this charming eatery left me with a newfound cocktail favorite – the spicy limoncello drink. It was a zesty revelation. For the main course, the scallops paired with cauliflower were a culinary triumph, delighting my taste buds. While the rigatoni was perfectly satisfactory, I suspect their lighter, white wine sauce pastas might better tickle my fancy on a future visit.

Dessert was a decadent Nutella tart, a must-try for chocolate aficionados. The restaurant's interior exudes a cozy allure, and the attentive staff ensured a delightful dining experience. Whether you're there for the exceptional drinks or the scrumptious fare, contentment is likely to be on the menu.

Title: A Cozy Trivia Night Haunt in the Heart of St. Mark's

I recently discovered a gem in the bustling streets of St. Mark's that's become not only my trivia team's go-to spot but a cozy retreat that feels worlds away from Manhattan's frenetic pace. The decor is both inviting and romantically inclined, a perfect setting for the #over30crowd looking for a peaceful dining experience.

The restaurant's participation in the NYC Trivia League initially drew us in, but it's the reasonably priced menu, varied and tasty offerings, and the friendly service that keep us coming back. During our first visit, the bartender doubling as our server made a great impression with a cool demeanor and attentive service.

While the ambiance is consistently appealing, there are a couple of wrinkles to iron out. Trivia nights would greatly benefit from an additional staff member on the floor to handle the increased patronage, ensuring timely orders and refills. On a separate note, I encountered an appetizer that wasn't quite up to par, but luckily, it didn't result in any adverse aftereffects.

Despite these issues, the restaurant's inherently chill, "no frills boro vibes" are a rare find in modern Manhattan. In these challenging times, I'm inclined to extend grace to the hospitality industry. Nonetheless, I'm hopeful for enhancements in menu and service soon, which would make it easier to wholeheartedly recommend this spot.

I'm looking forward to my next visit, rooting for the establishment's success post-quarantine life. Good luck—can't wait to enjoy another trivia night with you all!

Fun atmosphere. Service was mediocre if that. I don't think anyone taught the staff to wait on firing the entre until the apps are close to being done. We ended up at a tiny table with a 3 dishes and drinks. Another thing was that we ordered beef chili queso- but what we got had zucchini and other veggies def not any beef. Lastly, our waters were empty for 5-10 mins while eating the main course and the server never realized all the while he was serving people next to us. When I could finally flag him down to ask for water it was brought promptly. The Cali club  was okay pretty basic, but the chicken and churros was really tasty  Also the side "salad" that comes with the Cali club is literally spring mix straight from the bag with a light dressing. I wouldn't call it salad, more like side of leaves.

Title: A Hidden Gem Near the Theatre District

On a spontaneous quest for lunch, I stumbled upon a little restaurant tucked away just around the corner from La Mama theater, sharing the neighborhood with the NeoFuturists and Kraine Theater. To my delight, I discovered a $15 lunch special that could easily pass for a hearty dinner.

The meal started with a delicate kale and beet appetizer salad, remarkably balanced and void of the typical 'overpowering purple giants.' Each bite offered a delightful shift in subtle flavors that kept the palate engaged without overwhelming it.

The main course featured a robust puttanesca spaghetti, brimming with olives, capers, and small tomatoes. The dish was a celebration of simple, well-executed flavors that confidently stood without the need for aggressive spicing or heat. It captured the essence of 'street' pasta without the unnecessary bravado often associated with its 'putta' origins.

A neighboring diner's pappardelle bolognese looked equally tempting, boasting simple ingredients and subtly crafted sauces that echoed the overarching theme of flavor-rich yet unpretentious dishes.

Despite the restaurant being only 3 weeks old, it is run with a sophistication and grace suggestive of long-standing experience. The $15 lunch special is not just a meal but a pleasant culinary encounter. For those in the area, this charming establishment is well worth a visit.

Very clean upscale sports bar. Very cozy. We called beforehand to see if they'd be willing to play a soccer game and they put it on especially for us. It was very calm on a Saturday afternoon and the music was played at a very acceptable volume. Definitely keep this place in mind if you're looking for a beautiful sports bar with a relaxed atmosphere!

Title: A Royal Feast at a New Neighborhood Gem

From the moment we stepped into the recently opened establishment, we were greeted with a stunning royal-themed ambience that promised a dining experience like no other. During our visit in the establishment's initial partial opening phase, every aspect of the venue impressed us, starting with the exceptional service. Our server, Mohan, was the epitome of professionalism, adeptly guiding us through the menu when we felt overwhelmed by the tantalizing options.

On Mohan's recommendation, we started with the vegetable samosas, which set the stage for the culinary delight that followed. The butter chicken masala was the star of the evening, rich and flavorful, and it paired divinely with both types of naan and rice. The chicken curry was equally noteworthy, maintaining the high standard of quality throughout our meal.

As we savored the last bites of our entrees, we were pleasantly surprised with a complimentary serving of Rasmalai for dessert. The delicate cottage cheese patties soaked in sweet condensed milk were a perfect endnote to our dining experience.

In summation, this establishment is a welcome addition to the neighborhood, raising the bar for Northern Indian cuisine. The unforgettable flavors and impeccable service ensure a swift return for another taste of their exquisite offerings.

Title: A Tale of Two Ramens - Hits and Misses

I recently ventured into this local ramen spot, eager to slurp my way through their menu. The star of the show here is undoubtedly the Steak Mazemen. It's a dry ramen that exceeds expectations with its succulent, well-seasoned steak, generously coated in a sumptuous sauce that clings to every noodle. The addition of an egg enhanced the dish's creaminess, elevating it to pure comfort food status. It's a must-try and easily climbed to the top of my dry ramen favorites.

On the flip side, the Bone Marrow Ramen fell short, delivering a rather bland experience that didn't live up to its indulgent name. While it's a novel concept, the flavor didn't pack the punch I anticipated, and I found myself yearning for more depth.

In conclusion, stick with the crowd-pleaser: the Steak Mazemen is where this place shines. While they might miss the mark with some options, when they hit, they hit big.

I was disappointed with my recent dining experience at this restaurant. My order of steamed tofu and vegetables was unsatisfactory due to a hair I found on my tofu, which was off-putting. Additionally, the serving included only six pieces of tofu, which is less generous than what I've typically received at other Chinese establishments for similar dishes. Sadly, I cannot recommend this place based on my experience.

Awesome spot for ramen! I wanted to try their dip ramen and it was delicious - Miso tsukemen. You can also just get miso ramen if you don't want to dip your ramen. I have also gotten the karaage and fried oysters, both were very tasty and crispy. I give four stars because I wish they had more variety for their ramen. It's also pretty pricy for the fried oysters for the amount they give you but they are fresh every time. The best part of the meal is the EGG. It is cooked to absolute perfection every single time, especially the yolk part. If you love eggs in your ramen, you'd be happy to pay this place a visit. Overall, their food quality is always on point and is a great ramen fix. I've been eyeing their matcha beer for some time so I will be back to try that!

I came here with a group of 5 friends after moving in nearby last month. The interior is large, lengthwise and boasts booth seating. There are also colorful patterns and artwork on the walls. For example, there is a painting of half Frida Kahlo's face and half a black and white skull with roses on top. Another painting is of the American flag, juxtaposed with the Mexican flag. These lovely touches brightened the place up. We were served multiple servings of complimentary chips and salsa, which were quite tasty and helped to somewhat quench our hunger. I had the horchata drink (as long as it's the menu, I'm sure to get that), which was pretty good, but not as sweet or full of cinnamon flavor as usual. For my entree, I ordered the Picadera Colombiana, which consisted of mixed grilled chicken, sausage, beef, french fries, tostones, along with slices of cured onions and tomatoes to top everything off. This was massive and I love how it encompassed everything I was curious about trying. There was a generous amount of each food item. The grilled chicken was packed with flavor, slightly seared with perfect char marks. The sausage was juicy and well seasoned. The beef was probably my least favorite meat because it tasted a little dry and on the bland side. The french fries were wonderfully crispy and had an irresistible potato goodness taste. Tostones were pretty good, complete with a satisfying crunch. The onions and tomatoes were a nice compliment to the dish. Since the platter was so large, I saved the rest for the next day and it still tasted fresh and delicious! Our waitress was friendly and attentive. My friends and I had a great experience here and I would definitely return.

I've been meaning to try this spot for hot pot. Usually I go outside of Manhattan but I have to say this is one of the top spots for hot pot in Manhattan. The menu is typical- fixed price to load up with plates of meat, seafood, and vegetables. (Warning: some special items are available for an additional cost) It's fun getting a bunch of sauces. The broth options here are very nice which is probably what gives it the lead here. You can order a pot for one kind of broth, or two, or three. you've two hours to finish your meal. Also like the sweet rice dessert too. Reservations are accepted for larger parties. Only wish they offer bags to store belongings (like your coat) so you don't leave smelling like the restaurant.

If you're in search of a swift and satisfying meal, look no further. Imagine a delightful hybrid of a calzone and an empanada – that's what you'll find here. I opted for a hearty filling of ham, cheese, and mushrooms, and it didn't disappoint. Each one is crafted fresh upon order, striking the perfect balance between filling and crust without an overload of dough.

Do note, these are fried rather than baked, for those who have a preference. For smaller appetites, or perhaps for a sweet finish, the half-sized versions are just right – reminiscent of the dessert options.

To complement your meal, try the Italian-style sodas; they're a refreshing accompaniment. And don't miss out on the freshly made potato chips. Seating is limited to counter space, so I recommend grabbing your meal to go and enjoying it at a nearby park for an impromptu picnic.

A favorite! This place is packed but while you wait in line you probably can get served some sake! We came on Valentines and of course it was packed but we loved the energy. They always over pour and I love that. We had the sesame okra, sweet potato crisps, and the edamame goyza; those goyza were hands down the best part of the meal. All the sakes are great and the waiterS gave great recommendations.

Title: A Delight to the Senses at BondST

My visit to BondST was nothing short of remarkable, living up to every bit of the praise I'd previously encountered. The culinary creations here were a feast for both the eyes and palate, striking in their freshness and inventiveness. Each dish was a masterpiece, with stunning presentation that elevated the dining experience. The sauces deserve a special mention for their ingenious flavor pairings that complemented each roll and dish impeccably.

The service was top-notch, our server attending to our needs with both warmth and professionalism. However, it's worth noting a minor misstep in an otherwise flawless evening—the reuse of our utensils for consecutive courses felt out of place in the context of BondST's high standards. It slightly marred the perfect culinary canvas they laid out, especially when anticipating how the remnants of a Tuna Pizza might intermingle with a sweet dessert.

Despite this hiccup, the overall experience was extraordinary, and I am already looking forward to my next visit to this amazing establishment. BondST truly stands out as a gem in the dining scene.

Title: A Gem for Vegans and Foodies Alike: Seasoned Vegan

Nestled in East Harlem, Seasoned Vegan beckons with its quaint, cozy cafe charm, offering a little slice of foodie paradise that lives up to its name. Despite a modest wait, the atmosphere in this full-service spot is buoyed by the warmth of its staff—a special mention goes to the radiant expectant mother who served us with a beaming smile, reflecting the cohesive team spirit here.

The dining space, snug but airy with a few tables overlooking St. Nicholas Avenue, and a small, welcoming bar, sets the stage for an unexpected journey from brunch to dinner—as the versatile menu enticed me to opt for a sampling feast.

The Lemon Crusted Chicken Nuggets are a textured delight, with a flawless batter, while the Grits with Cheese, despite being slightly overdone, hit the comfort food spot. The Hoe Cake is indeed a flawless flapjack, but it was the Mac & Cheese that stole the show, ranking high in my list of vegan renditions—a delicious bonus that came with a side of leftovers.

Prices are fair, portions generous, and the vibe is all "Ma'am & Love," making Seasoned Vegan not just a haven for plant-based eaters but a must-visit for anyone in Harlem. Come for the food, stay for the experience—Seasoned Vegan is a heartwarming nod to Love & Light in the culinary scene.

During a recent visit to a bustling restaurant for a light snack, I found myself in a snug bar area, which operates on a first-come, first-serve basis. The close quarters were especially noticeable during the holiday rush. While the lounge menu differs from the main, more space would have certainly enhanced the dining experience. To note, patrons will find restrooms located upstairs.

As for the fare, the oysters were a highlight, served impeccably cold with a clean taste and just the right hint of brine, complemented by zesty horseradish and cocktail sauce. The jumbo lump crab cake also impressed, even earning praise from a Maryland native, though it would benefit from a more generous portion of crab meat.

The Hamachi sashimi, on the other hand, fell short of expectations. The sour yuzu was overpowering, creating an imbalance that did not do justice to the fish. Equally underwhelming were the lamb chops; their heavy and oily preparation cried out for a refreshing citrus salad accompaniment. As for the sushi, it was pedestrian at best, on par with what one might find at a local grocery store such as Wegman's.

To sum up, this dining experience was a mixed bag, with standouts like the crab cake and oysters and other offerings that were less than memorable.

Title: Ideal for a Leisurely Afternoon Bite

I've noticed that this spot doesn't strictly adhere to its noon opening time, especially on Mondays when I've frequently seen it still closed at 12:30 PM. That said, once you do get a chance to dine in, the food doesn't disappoint and fits perfectly as a late lunch or an afternoon treat. Just make sure not to bank on it for an on-the-dot midday meal.

I recently visited Chumley's in the West Village for my wife's birthday and it did not disappoint. This historic speakeasy has been transformed into a cocktail bar that pays homage to its past, complete with literary memorabilia that transports you back to the roaring twenties.

Though Chumley's may have shed its dive bar skin, the atmosphere remains its winning attribute. The intimate dining space is tightly arranged, so reservations are wise. Expect to be close enough to join neighboring tables in conversation, contributing to a convivial vibe.

The menu is curated but sophisticated, with standout dishes like Hemingway's Chili—an inventive mix of shrimp, cuttlefish, and cannellini beans, topped with crème fraîche. It's the sort of place that invites you to linger over every bite and savor the flavors.

The cocktails deserve a special mention; they are expertly crafted and elevate the dining experience. While the prices suggest moderation, the quality warrants indulgence. Whether for a date night or a casual evening with friends, Chumley's is a West Village gem that invites curiosity and delivers on its promise of a memorable night out.

I came here for an early dinner with my girlfriend. We got the pork belly bun, nabe yaki udon, and tonkatsu curry. The waitress was very friendly and quick with service. The pork belly buns were SOOO good. I cant not get a pork bun if i see it on the menu. The udon came with two pieces of shrimp tempura, and then the rest was traditional udon. The noodles were thinner than im used to but it was good. Especially on a cold day like any other day of new york winter. The pork tonkatsu curry was filling and savory. I dont know if its the best ive ever had, its not, but it was very good.I enjoyed everything, maybe i was too hungry, but very good!

Title: Pricey Sips with a View

I recently visited a well-positioned restaurant overlooking the bustling holiday ice skating rink. Expecting upscale pricing, the establishment did not disappoint—or rather, it did, depending on how you look at it. At nearly $20 a pop, both the frose and the frozen spiked lemonade packed a punch to the wallet, if not entirely to the palate. The lemonade erred on the side of saccharine sweet, while the frose was acceptable but unremarkable.

Service was a high note with our server promptly catering to our needs. The atmosphere definitely capitalized on the seasonal charm, adding a festive touch to the dining experience. In essence, while the ambiance was a delight, the overpriced and underwhelming drink portions mark this venue as a classic tourist trap. Proceed with caution and a well-padded wallet.

DokoDemo is one of my favorite places to get authentic Japanese street food in the city. When you walk in, watch your step, as you enter a place that might look a bit like Japan. On your left, you see the staff working hard at the grills, making delectable Japanese dishes, ranging from familiar ones like yakisoba (stir-fried ramen dish) and fried rice to more obscure ones like okonomiyaki (Japanese pancake) and takoyaki (octopus balls). On your right, there are tables and stools where you can enjoy your meal. There is definitely plenty of seating, but be warned that if you come in a big party, you'll most likely be huddling around a table together, so get nice and cozy!As for the food, I have had the yakisoba, okonomiyaki, and the takoyaki. As for the yakisoba, I found the noodles quite chewy, just the way I like it, and filled with flavor from the seasonings used. To put it simply, it is Japanese comfort food for me. The big hitters though are definitely the okonomiyaki and the takoyaki. I'm sure both dishes are what captivates people when they see them in photos. First, I'll talk about the okonomiyaki. I believe that the restaurant makes Osaka-style okonomiyaki, which is done by mixing all of the ingredients together, as opposed to Hiroshima-style, where the ingredients are layered on top of each other. In this case, the pancake usually consists of a batter mixed with vegetables and whatever you want in it, including meats like pork, chicken, or beef. The top is then glazed with Japanese mayo. You can even get cheese in it! As for the taste, the pancake is savory and filled with umami. The combination of flavors complement each other greatly and it's not really heavy, so one can easily finish the whole thing.The takoyaki was really good as well and packed with flavor. Takoyaki are these batter-filled balls with pieces of octopus inside and then glazed with some Japanese mayo and Takoyaki sauce (which I believe is similar to Worchestershire sauce) while being topped with bonito (fish) flakes. P.S. that's the stuff that's moving on top of the takoyaki. The different flavors work together in harmony, making the takoyaki rich and savory.Overall, DokoDemo does its best in showcasing the many wonders of Japanese street food, as its okonomiyaki and takoyaki are as appetizing as they look. It's definitely worth a try for those who may have never had these Japanese delicacies.

Title: A Night to Remember at [Bar Name]

I recently visited what has quickly become my favorite watering hole, largely thanks to an outstanding experience facilitated by the inimitable Roz, who may just be the best bartender in town. Not only was she the epitome of friendliness and fun, but she also managed our libations and appetizers with impeccable timing.

A word to the wise: if you're perched at the bar with a drink and some light bites, be prepared for a cash-only policy—though an ATM is conveniently stationed nearby for those caught off-guard. For those settling in for a full meal, rest assured that cards are readily accepted.

Do yourself a favor and order the "Beetle's Juice," a blackberry-lime concoction that reinvents the margarita with a mojito twist. After just one sip, my friend abandoned her original drink in favor of this irresistible mix.

On the food front, the "Frankenfries" - buffalo-seasoned fries with subtle hints of blue cheese - are a revelation, especially for those like me who subscribe to the #FlexitarianLyfe. The buffalo aioli dip is the cherry on top; it's simply divine. While the Risotto appetizer was praised for its flavor, note that it's on the petite side for those with heartier appetites.

This place sidesteps the typical tourist trap atmosphere for a genuinely cool, laid-back vibe, where a bartender like Roz, who truly shines in her role, elevates the experience. A Tuesday night visit proved an ideal time with a comfortably full bar and availability for seating. Weekends, however, hint at a bustling scene where space becomes a premium.

In summary, if you're looking for a fantastic bar experience with stellar drinks, tasty bites, and a charismatic bartender who's found her true calling, look no further. Just be sure to bring cash if you're grazing at the bar!

Title: A Slice of NYC's Iconic Pizza Experience

During my latest NYC escapade, a visit to an iconic pizza joint was non-negotiable. Scoring a dinner reservation was akin to finding a rare gem, but lunch proved a more promising endeavor. Even walk-ins navigated the wait with ease.

The deceptive storefront belies its spacious interior, where service shines and dishes arrive with admirable speed. My dining companion and I, restrained by numbers, sampled a modest selection.

The Rubirosa Salad ($16) was a medley of greens, tomatoes, mozzarella, cucumbers, celery, croutons, and regretfully, an unrequested guest – pickled red onions. Despite this oversight, each forkful affirmed its fresh and robust persona.

Our pizza adventure was a tale of two halves – Sausage & Broccoli Rabe and Tie-Dye ($24). The former melded the bitter bite of broccoli rabe with the sweet tenderness of sausage atop a triumphantly thin, crisp crust. The latter, a novel concoction, balanced sweetness with a verdant pesto flourish, both sections portioned into three generous slices.

In summary, the experience was a testament to culinary prowess and charm. This establishment has undoubtedly earned my future patronage – a 100% guarantee.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this local BBQ gem and it was nothing short of delightful. While it doesn't boast traditional wood pit smoking methods, this spot has solidified itself as a reliable go-to in the neighborhood. The service won me over with its warmth and friendliness, not to mention the generous portions that promise you won't leave hungry.

Their Oklahoma-style ribs are a must-try, conveniently available by the platter or individually for those who prefer to sample. However, the real stars of the show are their sliders, which are deceptively named – they're as big as regular burgers and packed with flavor. The Oklahoma hot slider, with its savory combination of sausage, cheese, onions, and pork rinds, is a mouthwatering masterpiece. The beef brisket and Ruben sliders follow closely behind in excellence, ensuring there's something for every palate.

Don't pass up on the burrata salad; it's a refreshing complement to the hearty meats. All in all, this BBQ spot is a must-visit for anyone in the area craving quality comfort food.

Title: A Hearty Meal at Xi'an Famous Foods

If you're roaming the streets of New York in search of a quick yet satisfying meal, Xi'an Famous Foods is a culinary gem you're likely to stumble upon, given its 15 convenient locations throughout the city. This modest, hole-in-the-wall establishment – which seems to be on the cusp of expanding – offers a delightful array of hand-drawn noodles, perfect for customizing with your preferred meat and opting for broth-based or dry versions.

During my visit, I indulged in the stewed oxtail, a hearty choice I'd certainly recommend to those who prefer alternatives to lamb. The noodles, thick and delectable, are a testament to Xi'an's reputation for serving up deliciously comforting fare.

With reasonable prices and the promise of a swift dining experience, Xi'an Famous Foods stands out as a solid choice for anyone in search of a flavorsome, filling meal on the go.

I love the cocktails here! I came here with a group of four and we each got a different cocktail to try and they were all delicious! The lunch deals are great as well! I believe my wrap with fries was around 9 dollars and it was pretty good!! Not the best food I have had but I gave it four stars because for the price I do feel the food was worth it. If I was taking out of town guest somewhere I probably would not take them here but if you are in the area and want a quick lunch this is definitely a good option. The service was very fast and water pitchers were being refilled without being asked which is also what bumped it up to 4 stars from 3. Overall would probably give it 3.5 if possible. Not sure how often I would come for lunch but will definitely be back for drinks!

Poached Eggs with Avocado on top wild rice, seeds and sprouts was a healthy and tasty start to my Sunday morning! We went at 10am before the Sunday brunch crowd and were seated immediately. The restaurant has neat modern decor with a warm woody feel. Staff were attentive and food came out quickly. The portion of the California Bowl was a bit lighter than expected but it was delicious!

Tucked away in midtown, this charming restaurant offers delightful Thai cuisine. The lunch specials are notably affordable, and I recommend arriving before noon to beat the rush. Service is impressively swift, ensuring a pleasant dining experience without delay.

I recently had the pleasure of celebrating a birthday dinner at this gem of a restaurant, and I must say, the experience was outstanding. The evening kicked off with classic old fashioneds that set the tone for the delicious dinner to follow. The menu boasted a range of appetizing options, but the crispy octopus and the ever-reliable burrata and tomato starter were the perfect precursors to the main event.

The star of the show, however, were the baby back ribs glazed with pomegranate molasses – an absolute must-try. Tender, juicy, and flawlessly complemented by the molasses' sweetness, they truly stole the spotlight. For the pasta enthusiasts, the mushroom bolognese with its combination of cut fettuccine, kale and cashew pesto, and grana padano, topped with herb breadcrumbs, was a delight, providing a solid foundation for an evening of drinks. Speaking of drinks, discovering the bar's stock of Nikka Coffee Whiskey was a pleasant surprise that kept our spirits high.

Our night didn't end with dinner. We descended downstairs to enjoy the lively piano and singing, which flawlessly rounded out our celebration. Though we missed the burlesque performances upstairs, the atmosphere throughout the venue was vibrant and accommodating, allowing both casual and fancy dress without missing a beat.

As the 'rowdy corner group', we felt right at home and left with nothing but good times and laughter. My only gripe was the unfortunate mix-up that led to my leftover pasta finding its way home with someone else. But that's all the more reason to return – and I certainly intend to, be it for the drinks, the entertainment, or another round of that memorable dinner.

Title: A Gastronomic Gem During Restaurant Week

I cannot recommend this spot enough after experiencing their Restaurant Week offerings. The roast duck breast was both generous in portion and delightful in taste, a true appetizer hit. The grilled octopus, according to my boyfriend, was equally tender and flavorful.

Our entrees, however, were the real showstoppers. The snow crab, uni mazemen, elevated with a bone marrow supplement for a mere $3, was a luxurious twist on noodles that I'd return for alone. My keisen bowl was as visually impressive as it was satisfying.

Though they were out of mochi, the substitute water cake was a palate-cleansing surprise, and the matcha cheesecake was intensely satisfying for true matcha aficionados. A special nod must go to the yellowtail platter, a triad of preparations that is an absolute must for yellowtail enthusiasts.

We're already planning our next visit to delve into their regular menu, lured by the promise of consistent quality and fair pricing. The attentive staff, ever-present to refill our tea, solidified our stellar dining experience. A return visit isn't just an option—it's a must.

Title: Unbeatable Lunch Specials in K-Town!

If you’re wandering around NYC looking for an unbeatable lunch deal, this spot is a solid gold find! With five-star quality food at incredible prices, it's a lunchtime game-changer. The agony of choosing from the plethora of tasty options is real, but trust me, it's worth it.

Opting for the combo lunch menu, I devoured beef short ribs accompanied by a soothing soup, all rounded off with an array of delightful banchan (side dishes) - and for the grand total of $10! It's a steal that'll have you planning your next visit before you've even left.

My friend's beef stew (the name escapes me) was a flavor-packed pot of goodness, brimming with noodles, veggies, and mushrooms. Satisfying to the last spoonful!

Perched upstairs, the restaurant's cozy charm is enhanced if you snag a window seat overlooking the vibrant streets of K-town. With waiters who are the epitome of attentiveness and friendliness, your dining experience is sure to be as pleasant as mine was.

Mark my words, this spot is a must-try. I'm already recommending it to everyone I know!

- Came for brunch- Cute little spot in the village- Got the cheddar waffles & eggs ($19): It tasted so good and I wish there was more. The portion was kind of small. For me.- Bright and beautiful lighting at the tables near the front of the restaurant- The back area is kind of dark- Found out after that they have a lunch prix fixe menu for $32. I might go back and give that a try.

I recently visited a local Italian restaurant and decided to give a few dishes a try. The Bagna Cauda stood out as genuinely authentic, with an interesting depth of flavor; thankfully, the anchovy broth was pleasantly subtle, not too overpowering. Moving on to the salads, the Insalata Verde was a simple, refreshing dish, although it was pretty basic with just leaves. The Radicchio Treviso, unfortunately, fell short of expectations due to its greasiness. In stark contrast, the Verzo salad—a blend of cabbage, farro, and speck—proved to be a delightful combination, refreshing and full of flavor. To finish, the Olive Oil Cake was a bit of a letdown as it turned out somewhat dry. Overall, the experience merited a 3.5 out of 5.

Title: A Gem in Tribeca: L'Angolo's Delightful Italian Fare

As a local exploring dining options near One World Trade Center, I was surprised by the average reviews of surrounding eateries. Venturing into Tribeca, I found salvation at L'Angolo Tribeca. Greeted by a swift seating and excellent service, the experience started on a high note.

The bread set a promising tone, followed by the standout meatball appetizer—juicy, well-seasoned, and complemented by a sauce that enhanced without overshadowing. The Cavatelli pasta maintained the momentum, with perfectly cooked Italian sausage and broccoli rabe mingling in an olive oil and Parmesan embrace. Each bite was savored until not a morsel remained, leaving no space to indulge in dessert.

In summary, L'Angolo Tribeca is a culinary beacon worth visiting for those seeking satisfying Italian cuisine amidst the sea of average dining options downtown.

These Australian brunch places are great!! The layout of this tiny place is split into two wings - the left and right - when you first walk in. I was seated in the left wing. There are many tables, but space between tables are super compact. The atmosphere was warm and cozy under the heater. It has a natural and modern style because of the soft wood color and lack of decoration.I ordered the Big Breakfast for a full, hearty, and nutritious meal. It came with two poached eggs, two pieces of sourdough bread, cherry tomatoes, mushroom, one slice of avocado, and 3 pieces of bacon. There are some arugula pieces underneath. ((Speaking of poached eggs, it is SO SATISFYING to break a perfect poached egg and watching the yolk spread out.)) It fulfills anyone's daily requirement of getting protein, veggies, and carbs. And! It was healthy and filling. At other brunches, this breakfast costs maybe $25-$30. Here, it was only $18! I think I know a steal when I see one. I would definitely recommend to others. I'd recommend coming here on a weekday since spaces don't fill up too fast, and to order their brunch menu. Feel free to ask for hot sauce!

Title: A Misstep in Ordering Can't Overshadow Potential Delights

While my choice of lemongrass chicken didn't hit the mark — lacking both in sauce and the titular herb, whilst erring on the oily side — my disappointment was tempered by the enticing dishes surrounding me. A glance to my right revealed steaming bowls of noodle soup, their aroma reaching me and hinting at what could have been. Adjacent to my left, an assortment of bento boxes paraded vibrant colors and variety, teasing a range of flavors I missed out on. This experience has left me eager to return and explore the menu more wisely. The potential for a more satisfying meal clearly exists—I just have to seize it next time. Stay tuned for an updated review upon my second voyage to this establishment with much promise.

Only ordered takeout from here during the 2020 quarantine. Overall, pretty impressed with the food. They have a variety of dips and meat selection. For the dips, the roasted eggplant sauce, hummus, and baba Ganoush were all delicious. My favorite surpringsly was the roasted eggplant sauce. For meats we ended up getting the lamb shish kabob and lamb kofta kebab platter. The meat was a little dry (I think maybe because it was takeout) but if you dipped it in the tzatziki sauce and hot Sauce it tasted great.

Fun spot where the servers all yell welcome and thank you's to you as a gesture of making you feel like you're wanted here. Very tourist and non Korean patron friendly but the food is good enough where a native Korean like myself wouldn't complain. They have an endless variety of combos of bbq meat to choose from as well as a decently priced a la care menu as well.Banchan, side dishes, they have it down to a simple science with signature dips and such that they lay out beforehand and I like how they serve the cheesy cream corn and the egg custard as half rings cooking around the grill that you'll be grilling on. Ventilation is good here so I don't come out of here strongly smelling like Korean bbq either.We usually stick to one of their combos since it's usually a group of 4 plus I'm here with and all of their meats are really fresh and deeply marinated. The staff is really attentive and will bring over more Banchan without prompting if they see that you're running low on stuff, but if you want more of the egg custard and cheesey corn, that's extra.

If you are looking for a place to celebrate a special occasion, impress a date, or just to live your best life, Lincoln R. Is your place! This is one of my favorite places to eat. It's located in Lincoln Center. The impeccable service starts from the moment you step foot through the door. I came with my family to celebrate my birthday. We were seated at a table with cosy leather chairs with a view of the service prep in the kitchen--LOVE! Our waiter and and sommelier both greeted us and explained specials/ offered us the drink menu. You could tell everyone knew the menu cold in terms of offerings and taste. We settled on a prix-fixe menu which started off with an amuse bouche-- always a nice touch. Then came out their specialty focaccia bread- warm crispy in the outside, soft on the inside--So yummy-- I could eat it all day. Our meal was spectacular. At the end they bless you with some homemade biscotti. The menu changes seasonally ( but there is always that focaccia ), which is what I also love about this place. The staff is very attentive and makes you feel special. Can't wait until my next visit!

A hit in the heart of Chinatown! Peking duck, wonton soup (the before wontons are my favorite), and BBQ pork are standouts among a table of delicious food. It's big enough to accommodate our party of 10, and service was fast. The environment can get loud from talking, but at least there's no overwhelming music blasting from the speakers. Your can get takeout or cold cuts from the front counter or come inside for a dine in experience.

Title: Quaint Takeout Spot by Mount Sinai

I recently stopped by a modest Chinese takeout place not far from Mount Sinai, which offers a decent lunch special complete with a soda. While the ordering experience might catch you off guard with the attendant's booming voice, it's just her way; no rudeness intended.

The place is small, accommodating diners with just three tables, which works if you're up for a quick dine-in. I tried their Chicken Lo Mein - it was passable, though lacking the silky texture typical of chicken at other takeout joints.

A bit of a menu puzzle is their Chicken Chow Mein. It's listed, but when you try to order it, you're informed that 'chow mein' here means only vegetables, a quirk I've run into at another nearby spot as well.

In a nutshell, it's your run-of-the-mill Chinese takeout, with a few quirks to keep things interesting.

One of the best after party place to have some comfort food! They have pretty much everything. Good big portion, Greasy and tasty. We had philly cheesesteak sandwich, onion rings, and burger with fries. Best thing you could get at 2 am in the morningYes, it's a little expensive but they are pretty much the only places that's open so...

Title: Disappointing Lunch at a Premium Location

I recently visited a restaurant that seemed to promise a delightful lunch special, but left me disillusioned and lighter by $19. While the location may justify the price for some, the food certainly did not meet expectations.
