The concept was simple: choose three sides and a protein. My selection included mixed greens, tostones, avocado, and rotisserie chicken. Unfortunately, the chicken was alarmingly undercooked, presenting an unappetizing pinkish-red hue. The sides didn't fare much better, with the avocado being notably bland and minuscule in size.

I did cave to peer pressure and tried the much-hyped empanada, which was tasty but not exceptional enough to justify its $3.19 price tag. Considering the quantity and quality of food, even the empanada didn't redeem the overall experience.

Those looking for value and a health-conscious meal might find this place disappointing. Perhaps the rice and beans could be a safer bet here, but I remain skeptical. It's unlikely I'll return, except maybe for the empanada, though I suspect there are better and more reasonably priced options elsewhere. My advice: Save your money and appetite for a place where the food matches the price and hype.

Title: Fresh, Flavorful Brunch at Westville

I finally got to experience the much-talked-about Westville, conveniently located near our post-workout spot at Switch Playground. This particular Westville boasted spaciousness, avoiding the cramped feel of smaller venues. The market plate caught my eye, an excellent choice for any veggie enthusiast. My group and I shared it, opting for asparagus, Brussels sprouts, green beans, and eggplant — each was fresh, bursting with flavor, and perfectly cooked.

I chose the avocado toast topped with egg whites for my main, which proved to be a delectable choice, pairing seamlessly with our vegetable medley. The entire menu was tempting and after such a satisfying visit, it's clear I'll be returning to Westville to indulge in more of their flavorful offerings.

Tucked away in the heart of the city lies a gem perfect for an evening of relaxation and romance. With an exquisite selection of wine and rosé, this rooftop sanctuary invites you to unwind and indulge in idle chatter as the sun dips below the horizon. The ambiance is undeniably romantic and classy, making it an ideal date spot for a pre-dinner drink. Although I didn't sample the cuisine, the presentation alone was tempting. And for those seeking a picturesque Instagram moment, this venue won't disappoint. In finding a cozy corner with ease, my evening here was a serene retreat in the urban skyline.

Came here on a Thursday night around 9:45PM after a broadway show nearby (very fitting and probably only available dinner after a 7PM show). My friend really liked their tacos and I've never been.I ordered 1 grilled cactus and 1 chicken. She ordered 1 steak and 3 chicken. Next time, we shall try pork.  The line wasn't too long and they placed our order and served us within 10 mins. When we were there, it was about to close at 10PM but I think they take last orders at 10PM and let you finish before closing.The tacos were very flavorful and you get your fair share of like to pick from. You pick either corn or flour tortilla - I chose corn and the order comes "con todo" with all onions, cilantro, guacamole and salsa. Once you give them the ticket, they ask you what you prefer. The service is really quick and cool to watch over the counter line. After you grab your order, you can stand at any of the table tops. I would imagine this gets busy during peak lunch and dinner hours. It's not exactly a place I'd recommend for a sit down (since there are no chairs to sit) and not the best for groups unless you don't mind huddling....but for a quick easy bite to grab and go, definitely worth a try! One down side  is that I wish they had seafood options like fish or shrimp.

Over the past year, my favorite dessert has become churros! After going to Mexico last year, I developed a love for the sweet and saw a stand while in Dekalb Market Mall.I saw there were a variety of stuffed churro flavors and I know, based on my past experiences with sauces, what to choose. I ended up with a Creme Brûlée, Dulce De Leche, and Peanut Butter. The best one was the Dulce De Leche (a classic) and the Creme Brûlée was very good. Not a fan of the Peanut Butter Flavor. They had Nutella as another flavor too.

We were here on a Saturday at midnight and the place was packed. We tried their original milk hot chocolate and the chocolate surprise tiramisu. They were both great!!!! Will definitely be back to try their other desserts. And our server was great too.

Title: A Lively Experience at Panna II

Walking into Panna II is an experience unlike any other. The restaurant is famously decked out in what can only be described as an 'obnoxious' collection of Christmas lights, which, surprisingly, contribute to its unique charm rather than detract from it. The BYOB policy, coupled with the energetic vibe and the background music, creates a festive atmosphere that's hard to find elsewhere.

As someone with Indian heritage who knows their way around authentic Indian cuisine, I found the offerings at Panna II to comfortably sit in the 'middle of the road' category. While the food is sufficient, and you're likely to find similar quality in many other local Indian eateries, it doesn't ascend to culinary heights. 

That being said, Panna II earns its stripes with the sheer joy and fun of the dining experience. It's the place's ambiance that would tempt me to add an extra star to its rating. If you're looking for a night out that's as much about the atmosphere as it is about the food, then Panna II won't disappoint.

This establishment used to be named "Flaming kitchen" but it has recently changed to "Sup crab." The restaurant still has the same owner but they decided to change the concept  a bit - now it's more of a seafood boil with a Szechuan twist. The decor was revamped to a nautical theme and it's super cute. The menu is extensive- they have bar snacks, stir fry ,and vegetarian dishes so even if you don't like seafood you have lots of options to choose from. I tried the popcorn chicken which was crispy and fried to perfection and had a little spicy kick. For the entrees I had the salted yolk crab. Oh my goodness this was soo delicious. If you are a huge fan of salted yolk chips (which I am), this will be right up your alley. The crab is super crunchy and some of it even cracked off and you could eat it like chips.I tried the seafood boil with original  Cajun sauce. First off the portions are huge and you can definitely  share one combo with two people. Usually when I get the seafood boil at other places , one bag portion is only for one person but not enough to share.  We got the seafood boil combo with shrimp, crawfish, and snow crab legs. They were very generous with the crab legs and the Crawfish were huge. Not sure if it's crawfish season but I've never seen crawfish  that huge - look at the picture for reference. Lastly had to balance it off with some veggies and I got the cauliflower with Chinese bacon . As all with all the other  dishes , this dish  also had a nice spicy kick to itThey restaurant also gave us watermelon at the end which was perfect and refreshing after eating lots of spicy food. Overall the food was delicious and I would come back again and next time with a big group to try everything!
Had a fried chicken sandwich with pickle and some sauce on it also came with a side of fries. Good flavor and decent size portion. Would get it again

I recently tried out an Ethiopian restaurant, despite the cuisine not being my usual preference. To my pleasant surprise, the veggie platter for two was filled with fresh and flavorful vegetables, exceeding my expectations. The portion sizes were quite generous, ensuring we had plenty to enjoy. Additionally, the service was commendable, with the waitress being notably attentive throughout our meal.

Nestled just a few blocks from the Canal Street train station, Thai Son offers a straightforward Vietnamese dining experience that's as reliable as it is affordable. The no-frills ambiance is a perfect backdrop for devouring their standout dishes, like the beef cube fried rice which is a must-try if you're veering away from their soul-warming pho. Prices won't break the bank, making it a go-to for a casual meal. Just remember to stay hydrated, as their delicious pho seems to pack a bit of MSG – but it's a small caveat for a broth that's packed with flavor.

Solid brunch spot on the weekends with it ending late. Usually go to Jacobs Pickles as my go-to brunch spot but wanted to try something new. This was a good choice. Service was not rushed although it does get packed around noon on a Sunday. 1. Pancakes - 3 in a stack, loads of carbs. Delicious with the syrup and comes with fruit. Overall, I'd come back for more brunch and is a solid option in the UWS.

I don't know why this place doesn't have many customers every time I went but this place is truly a hidden gem!! Really hope more people could know about them! The combos we had were absolutely delicious. Side dishes were on point! Every single one of them was so yum! Great quality food and experience! Also alcohol is 50% off throughout June.

On Sundays, we brunch! I was looking for a brunch spot in the city that takes reservations and can accommodate for a group of 10. Jane was one of those spots. I made a reservation a couple weeks in advance, and we were all set when we arrived at 12:30pm.Their brunch menu has enough variety depending on if you're in the mood for something savory or sweet, big or small.I went with the Steak Frites (~$26) which includes flat iron steak, house-made steak sauce, and rosemary fries. I also got a Passion Screwdriver (~$12) to go with that. It's basically a regular screwdriver but with passionfruit juice!The steak was cooked medium, like I asked. It was a little on the dry/chewy side. I wish they had cut the steak into slices. It also definitely needed some butter or another element of flavor here. The rosemary fries were crispy and super addicting! The Passion Screwdriver was not as enjoyable as I thought. It was a bit too sour for my liking. I think the ratio of orange juice to passionfruit juice was a bit off.Despite being such a large group, our waitress, Alexis, did a great job at taking our orders and getting our food out efficiently and quickly. She was super friendly throughout!Jane is a great brunch spot for large groups. The ambiance is very casual. I would recommend it if you like American-style brunch.

Came here for dinner with a group of friends. Service was great, but I thought that the food was pretty average given the price and lacked flavor/spice. The palak paneer was a little bland, the jaipur kofta had a flavor that we didn't quite like, and the butter chicken was pretty standard. Of everything we ordered, the chana masala was probably my favorite.

Title: A Gem with a Slight Reservation Hiccup

My recent outings to this restaurant left a lasting impression, with the food and drinks fully living up to the hype. The palatable dishes, sumptuous desserts, and an array of amazing drinks were complemented beautifully by the trendy decor and inviting atmosphere. 

However, the experience was slightly marred by the twice-canceled reservations on the day of our planned visits. While I could empathize with the first cancellation due to bad weather affecting their chic rooftop setup known as "The Lodge," the second instance felt more inconvenient. The late notice of a private event taking over the rooftop could have been communicated more promptly, as it disrupted well-laid plans.

Despite this hiccup, the quality of the meals and service did shine through. I've dined here twice and recommend giving it a try—just brace yourself for potential last-minute adjustments. Caution advised, but certainly worth the visit.

Title: A Solid Choice for Ramen Enthusiasts

I've visited this ramen spot on two different occasions, sampling both the shio and spicy miso ramen. The latter stands out with a pleasant zest that adds a satisfying kick to the meal. Despite being consistently busy, my timing seems to have been impeccable, allowing me to avoid long waits.

The ramen bowls are fairly priced around $15-$16 USD, but keep in mind that dinner service includes an expected tip, pushing the total to about $29 CAD after taxes—somewhat steep, partially due to the unfavorable Canadian exchange rate. Although it's not the pinnacle of ramen experiences, the quality is commendable. If you're craving a decent bowl of noodles and broth, this eatery is worth your time.

Title: Authentic Touches at a Bustling City Gem

Navigating the city's parking can be a headache, and this spot is no exception. If you can, skip the drive to save on parking fees. Upon arrival, a delightful cultural nuance greeted us--staff welcomed us with a Japanese greeting, which they consistently maintained throughout, providing an immersive experience.

The restaurant prides itself on fair wages, reportedly eliminating the need for tipping—though I'd appreciate insight on this policy. With only three locations globally, reservations are recommended to secure a spot, especially since this restaurant draws a crowd.

The ambiance strikes a balance between austere and thoughtful, with dark, simple decor; it's not particularly romantic but has an intentional design. The menu offerings were generally good, though not groundbreaking. The pot stickers were standard fare, while the Eho-maki roll was unfortunately missed by our server. For mains, I'd advise going for a regular-sized bowl over the mini Katsu Don unless you're grazing or unfamiliar with the dish—the mini size is carb-heavy with minimal protein.

As for the sides, the cold Soba is a refreshing choice, albeit not extraordinary in flavor. Dessert was an interesting exploration with the Anmitsu, featuring green tea ice cream, mochi, red beans, and a pourable sauce—pleasant but not a standout.

Overall, the food quality is competent, and with judicious meal selection, the portion sizes can be quite satisfying. It's certainly worth a return visit to dive deeper into their menu. Do remember to book ahead—this city favorite fills up fast!

Love this/their baking headquarter. Wheneve I walk in, their pastries look super duper fresh and exquisitely delcicious. They have a coffee selection to go with and a couple seating arrangements. Its small, cute and absolutely as delcicious as it looks. Absolutely great for low key, super cute dates/desserts. Their buscuits and scones looked scrumptious although it's not my go to. Ended up getting a heart butter cookie whose tip dipped in chocolate and a palmier -- yum! So many pasties I wanted to try...

You hear that Yin Ji is a classic for Hong Kong style rice rolls and it lives up to the hype. Yin Ji specializes in rice rolls, but you can also get congee with fried dough sticks or Hong Kong style brunch menu items like toast with condensed milk here.I got the marinated beef and shrimp with chives rice roll and cleaned my plate instantly. The rice noodles are translucent and light while the soft beef and large pieces of shrimp give it substance. The chives are a great addition that cuts the greasiness of the flavors. The portion is not so large that you can't have a small dish next to it. If you are hungry, you can get the curry style fish balls. The 10 large fish balls had an on-point curry flavor. These were some of the best HK style fish balls I have had. The HK style cold milk tea is very strong! They put no ice in the milk tea, so you know they aren't  joking around. It goes well during or after the meal. Prices are high in comparison to other rice roll spots in the area ($7 for a rice roll!), but Yin Ji delivers in quality what it demands in price. Do not go during rush hour as there may be a line. There's ample seating but also lots of customers to take up those seats at any given time.

Title: A New Giant in Town – Big Slice Pizza NYC

Amid the bustling pizza scene of NYC, a new spot has emerged with a tantalizing offer: the "giant" slice. True to its claim, the slice is a behemoth, easily two to three times the size of a regular slice – a formidable challenge that left my kids delightfully overwhelmed.

The newly renovated space is inviting, boasting shiny new tiles and ovens that instill confidence in its cleanliness. The layout is accommodating; with double tables for larger parties and chic bar-style seats for solo or duo diners.

Staff members at Big Slice Pizza are commendable for their patience and warmth, providing excellent service during our visits.

As for the pizza itself, expect a no-frills, traditional approach. The Pepperoni slice we tried was generously oily upon folding – a guilty pleasure for those who relish an authentic drip. Although the selection was somewhat limited, this is likely an early-days issue, with the promise of an expanded range in the future.

Price-wise, it's a clear winner, offering a wallet-friendly alternative to its pricier neighbor Farinella, without sacrificing the essence of what makes a good, traditional pizza.

All in all, if size matters to you in the world of pizza, and you're after a simple yet satisfying bite, Big Slice Pizza is worth a visit.

This was excellent. I was somewhat torn on 4 or 5 stars, because I'm not sure it's in my absolute top tier in NYC, but it's not far off. The slices had perfect structural integrity and really great ingredients, especially their burrata (which you can add to any slice). It's a really fluffy crust, even more so than Mama's Too on the rim and significantly thicker in the middle. Some will love that, some won't (eg my wife) -- I was somewhere in the middle, in that it's not my perfectly preferred style, but I really enjoyed it for what it was. We got a lot in our first visit: two plain (one with burrata), a margherita with burrata, two pepperoni, a square, and garlic knots. We weren't crazy about the knots, but we really loved all the slices. The only one I probably wouldn't make sure to get again is the square, which is a more traditional Sicilian slice, rather than the new NYC-style square which is a bit thinner. I wouldn't mind trying the soppressata as well next time around.

Title: A Sizzling Success at the Heart of the City

My recent visit to this restaurant, nestled near the Rockefeller Christmas tree, was nothing short of stellar. A party of 15, we were greeted with impressive efficiency, swiftly seated at a combined arrangement of a large table and booths at around 5:30 PM, before the dinner rush.

Initially, the ordering process seemed unconventional, with servers present yet orders placed directly with the butchers. That said, once we navigated this unique system, we opted for the ribeye—our favorite. Taking heed of the wall's advice, I daringly ordered my steak raw, a decision that paid off due to the sizzling hot plates continuing the cooking process right at the table.

When the steaks arrived, perfectly heated and inviting, we doused them with the recommended sauce, enhancing the ribeye's innate flavors. The additional sauce available on the table also proved to be a hit. Our sides of rice and the accompanying corn rounded out a satisfying meal.

The ambiance does come with a caveat; expect to carry the restaurant's aroma on your attire. However, a thoughtful touch awaits in the back—a supply of Febreze spray to combat any lingering scents before you step out.

In a nutshell, the restaurant delivers a memorable experience with perfectly cooked steak and thoughtful touches. I'm already plotting my next visit. A must-try for any steak enthusiast visiting the area!

Tucked away in the city's bustling streets lies Cocotte, a charming French wine bar and restaurant that's as quaint as it is delightful. Though small in size, this gem makes up for it with an infectious vibe that will draw you in for an evening of indulgence. The happy hour at Cocotte is a true highlight, boasting an array of delectable appetizers paired with exceptionally curated house wines, all at pleasing prices.

As the perfect backdrop to your culinary experience, the music hums at just the right volume, striking a balance that encourages conversation without the need to raise your voice. The ambiance is convivial, inviting diners to engage in pleasant table talk as they savor their meals.

Service at Cocotte is nothing short of stellar. The staff are attentive, genuinely pleasant, and go above and beyond to ensure your dining experience is seamless. A visit to Cocotte isn't just a meal; it's a warm embrace by a team that cares. Kudos to Cocotte for crafting an experience that feels both personal and luxurious. Whether it's for happy hour or a full meal, this French haven is an absolute must-visit.

Title: A Hearty Feast at Au Cheval

I finally ventured into the much-touted Au Cheval in Chicago, a place I'd bypassed despite my numerous visits to the city. My friend's invitation was the perfect excuse to indulge in their famed burger, specifically the one topped with foie gras—an extravagant choice that admittedly put my wallet to the test.

The single cheeseburger, laughably, comes with a double helping of patties, which certainly fills the plate—and the stomach of any light to moderate eater—with succulent, perfectly cooked beef. The toasted bun was a crispy delight; however, I would recommend foie gras enthusiasts to order it on the side, as the robust beefy flavor does overshadow the delicate foie. Traditionalists beware, you won't find ketchup or other condiments here.

Their hashbrowns are a generous, shareable side, crispy and light on grease. However, take note, they are best enjoyed fresh and don't fare well as leftovers.

Serendipity brought us a complimentary fried chicken—misordered but gratefully received. Though it was a considerable portion that added to our already bountiful meal, it could have benefited from a bit more crunch. It's a flavorful dish but doesn't quite hit the mark for fans of the Korean fried chicken crisp.

Service at Au Cheval was commendable, even at the bustling bar seating. While nabbing a table might enhance the experience, the bar was a worthy compromise for walk-ins. I would return, though perhaps infrequently, as the menu doesn't quite align with my everyday eating habits.

Title: A Festive Filipino Feast at Ugly Kitchen

I recently celebrated my birthday at Ugly Kitchen with friends, and it turned out to be an exceptional dining adventure. The highlight was the Kamayan Feast, priced at $35 per person, which offers an authentic and interactive Filipino dining experience where the food is spread out on banana leaves and eaten with your hands.

The array of dishes included in the feast, such as bone marrow, fried fish, pork ribs, chicken skewers, head-on shrimp, rice, and a creamy vegetable stew, was nothing short of a culinary delight. The fried fish and pork ribs stood out as my personal favorites, although the bone marrow's richness wasn't to everyone's taste.

The experience was heightened by the novelty and fun of eating communally without utensils (gloves provided), though it did take some getting used to. A nice little bonus was a free house shot offered for checking in on Yelp.

However, I must note that service suffered on the busy Friday night we visited. The staff was stretched thin, which meant we sometimes struggled to get their attention. Additionally, the waitstaff's uniform blended in with the attire of many patrons, causing occasional confusion. The energized atmosphere was somewhat compromised by live music that overwhelmed conversation at times.

Despite these drawbacks, Ugly Kitchen provided an upbeat and delicious birthday celebration, earning a solid four-star rating for its flavorful offerings and unique dining experience in the heart of East Village.

I just want to start off by saying that the service here is outstanding. Literally have not seen anything like it. It was a really hot and humid day so anything could really trigger me, so I can't imagine how the servers are with handling an entirely full restaurant that's outside patio/open windows. Our server always checked up on us and made sure we were comfortable. One of the workers also gave us an order that wasn't even ours but told us we could keep it for our table (even though it wasn't even touched yet). It's the little things and professionalism that makes all the difference! That was 5/5AS FOR THE FOOD, a solid 4/5. My favorite was the carbonara that almost everyone orders. So delicious and tasty without it being too salty or creamy. Loved the egg touch. This dish is what you see on almost every popular social media outlet. Definitely a signature dish you can't miss out on. So tasty!! Everything else was good but nothing that stood out. Although then view was worth it. I love how nice open patio and even inside is. It's the perfect place for a date. Super romantic and rustic. Almost as if you're in Italy or something! I'd love to visit again and try some other dishes!

Time for an update--only less than a week after my first visit and review.And here's why--I'm anxious to share the variety of food and its copious amount I ordered for a recent family occasion. However, it was a takeaway and just as good as my first time experience dining in.We carefully looked at the lengthy menu (all vegan--Chinese and Sushi selections) and while doing so were served some delicious Chinese hot tea (even though it was sizzling outside). At the time of our arrival, it was the start of dinner and the restaurant was filling up.Our order took about 30 minutes to prepare once submitted (and was carefully packaged to our delight with all utensils and hot/side sauce included).Here is what we ordered:From the main section: *Vegan Curry Chicken with Vegetables--warning--VERY spicy but so delicious. Loaded with carrots, cabbage and other veggies. The vegan chicken was moist and flavorful with the ability to fool the most diehard carnivore. Recommend.*Chow Fun Noodles. A bit oil slicked but these were broad noodles with strips of vegan pork that was absolutely delicious and filling. Recommend.*Stir Fried Eggplant with Garlic. The eggplant---which is known as the sponge of vegetables---was somewhat oily but delicious when accompanied by the steamed white rice (which BTW was not included. Rice was $1.50 per carton). Very nicely prepared.I would recommend the eggplant or another vegetable main to switch things up to accompany the vegan entrees.From the Dim Sum section:*Two orders of the Sticky Rice in Lotus Leaf . Having already tried it, this was one of my favorites since the rice was moist and flavorful including plenty of mock roast pork. Definitely recommend.*Two orders of the Steamed Shrimp Shu Mai. The dumpling skin was translucent, the filling plentiful and the side sauce, delicious. Recommend.*Curry Dumplings. Same translucent dough as the Shrimp Dumpling. A nice curry palate pleaser & winner.*Buddha fried spring roll. A divine cheat. Three rolls to a portion. Delicious/recommend.*Crispy fried taro ball. I loved this dim sum since the fried, but not oily, crispy coat coupled up nicely with the starchiness of the taro. Recommend.*Ribs in Black Bean Sauce. Only dim sum selection I wouldn't order again. These were vegan ribs with green  peppers and onions sitting in a very salty brown black bean sauce. Pass. Not a favorite.Overall, we had a feast (total for all of the above--$88.08) and I'm obsessed with this restaurant. As mentioned, the food was packed well, piping hot and plentiful. Portions were very much shareable. Only nitpick was the charge for the white rice but a small inconvenience. I am aiming to try their sushi next.One of my favorite and new go to places.Make your way there soon.
This is a self serve place, but very sinple and clean. Not much choices on the menu but just enough. Very good sauce making the rice, salad and meat delicious. Average manhattan lunch pricing

Title: A Worthy Wait for Satisfying Ramen

I'd give this bustling ramen joint a solid 3.5 stars. It was the final ramen stop on my trip, and although there was a bit of a wait, it was manageable, especially with the option to grab drinks upfront. Despite the crowd, the service remained attentive; water refills came without a hitch, and the server was helpful in addressing my menu queries.

I dove into the Akamaru with an added soft egg and bakudan, experimenting with the taste through customizable additions. While the broth delighted with its rich flavor, I found myself wishing it was served hotter. The noodles, while firm, lacked the perfect springiness I crave.

We also shared kabocha croquettes which, although a bit pricey for the portion, hit the mark with their consistent taste and texture. Overall, this place nails the flavor but could fine-tune some details for the ultimate ramen experience.

Loeb Boathouse in Central Park offers a delightful dichotomy for those looking to enjoy both the simple and the upscale in one location. My husband and I discovered this gem at 4:35pm after a tiring walk, and it was an ideal place to relax. The bar served us well; my husband's Mimosas were expertly mixed with the perfect bubbly-to-juice ratio, while my Mojito Mocktail was refreshing.

We initially considered eating at the bar but quickly realized that most patrons opt for the bustling main lakefront dining area or the outdoor café. Unfortunately, we missed the lunch service which ends at 4pm, and dinner wasn't until 6pm, so we settled for the outdoor café.

The café offers a straightforward menu that matches its indoor counterpart, featuring soups, breakfast items, sandwiches, and more. My husband enjoyed his Sausage & Peppers, and my Garden Burger, along with the shared fries, was quite satisfying. The drinks at the bar came to $38, which was reasonable for the quality.

While we couldn't stay for dinner due to a nearby concert, the Loeb Boathouse left a lasting impression. I eagerly anticipate returning for an enchanting lakefront dining experience, fully immersing in the quaint charm that Central Park dining has to offer.

What a stoke of luck to have found this wonderful place while in route to another. We Yelped it and decided to change our original plan accordingly. And are we glad we did! Not only is it delicious but it had different menu options which were a breathe of fresh air in our culinary existence. I ordered the "Gyro" salad. And yes, those quotation marks have a significance. There is no gyro. So it is everything that would be in a gyro salad, minus the meat. Fear not, it was scrumptious and helped me save points on Weight Watchers. Game on! My Mom choose an item under the starters menu, Eggplant Bruschetta. She thoroughly enjoyed it. I could tell by her clean plate entry. This little place turned out to be an unexpected oasis.

I recently dined at a conveniently located restaurant near the entrance to the cruises and had a pleasant experience. The menu is classic American fare; I opted for a cheeseburger with onion rings and found the rings to outshine even those at Juniors by Marriott Marquise on 45th Street Times Square - they were that good. My companion enjoyed a spicy chicken sandwich accompanied by quite satisfactory fries.

Although the food was standard, the sandwiches were tasty and served promptly. What set this place apart was the exceptional service. The staff were the epitome of hospitality - welcoming, courteous, and truly focused on customer satisfaction. An added bonus was the variety of condiments on offer, including mayonnaise, which is not always a given.

Overall, while the food was decent, it’s the service and the prime location that would draw me back.

Title: Decent Ramen Experience with Room for Improvement

I recently tried the Chicken Chashu Ramen through Mealpal and thought I'd share my thoughts. The portion size definitely provides good value for the money; it's quite generous. However, the chicken chashu itself was a letdown, as it was overly sweet and the flavor was too intense for my liking. After one piece, I couldn't bring myself to eat any more of it.

On a positive note, the egg included in the ramen was the highlight, prepared just right and quite enjoyable. The noodles were on the thicker side, which might appeal to some, but I personally have a preference for thinner noodles.

Overall, the ramen was decent, but the chicken chashu isn't something I'd recommend or order again. Despite the setback, the experience hasn't deterred me from the restaurant. I see potential in their other offerings and I'll likely return to try a different ramen dish next time.

Title: Late-Night Craving Satisfied at the Bao Shoppe

I popped into the Bao Shoppe last minute to quench a sudden craving for pork belly bao, and it didn't disappoint. Open until 10 pm, it was the perfect spot for a post-dinner treat. The place was quiet and somewhat empty, which added a serene touch to the late-night snack experience. 

Service was slower than expected, considering the lack of crowds, but the wait was worth it once I bit into the bao. Although the portion of pork belly was on the smaller side, the meat's tenderness and flavor packed a punch. The accompanying pickled veggies weren't to my liking, as they leaned heavily into Vietnamese-style pickling which isn't my preference. 

In terms of value, the price was reasonable and it definitely hit the spot for my cravings. If you're in need of a savory late-night bite, the Bao Shoppe might just do the trick.

I recently dined at Cousin Maine and was thoroughly impressed by both the service and the food. The staff were welcoming and attentive, adding to the warm atmosphere of the restaurant. I indulged in the Connecticut roll, which was generously filled with hot, buttery lobster - a pleasant departure from the typical mayo-laden lobster rolls. Alongside, I savored the rich lobster bisque and couldn't resist the tater tots topped with pico de gallo, accompanied by an irresistible dip.

Despite the roll's deceptive size, it was packed with substantial chunks of lobster, proving to be quite satisfying. The venue boasts plenty of seating, perfect for enjoying a meal with friends, and a selection of beer and wine to complement the dining experience. Eagerly anticipating my next visit, I'm looking forward to trying the lobster quesadilla. Cousin Maine is a must-visit for any seafood aficionado.

This restaurant nails the perfect bowl of ramen – absolutely delicious and at such a reasonable price! To top it off, a complimentary gelato with our meal was the cherry on top. The service? Friendly and speedy. I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

Really good sushi spot on the UES. Has become my "go-to" for take out and delivery. Prices are in the mid-range and they offer some decent deals for the various combos / dinners.I like their spicy tuna roll a lot. Obviously they have these everywhere , but they're especially good here. Also I will normally just do some pieces of sushi / sashimi which are always pretty fresh and tasty. Also their ginger salad dressing is too notch- makes for a great avocado salad.Overall great spot,I expect to keep coming back.

We were here on a Sunday. The place was busy and they said there is a 5-10 mins wait time. We waited for 35 minutes and got seated after some other tables that came after us not sure why. Anyways we ordered the samosa chat and chicken biryani. We often come to this place for their chat. The samosa chat was delicious. But the biryani had no flavor. It was like white rice and plain chicken mixed. The two female server there are really nice. Service: 4/5Food: samosa chat 5/5, chicken biryani 1.5/5Price: 3/5

I'm usually very skeptical about modern Indian cuisine being Indian as it lacks flavor and spice most of the time. I was happily surprised as everything we ordered was delicious. We got the pinwheel samosas and lassan Gobi pops which were on point. For our main, we had the paneer Bhurji and Kadai paneer which wasn't too dry, and everything with a perfect level of spice. The goat cheese naan and garlic naan were both crispy and perfectly heated. Rice is an add on. Service was a bit slow but the food came out in a timely matter. They don't have their liquor license yet but it's apparently BYOB (there's a wine/liquor store across the street). I was a little disappointed because I wanted to try the rhubarb falooda but it's not on the menu anymore. I would definitely come back and excited to try more dishes.

I visited Peppercorn midday during the weekend and was surprised to find it empty. Opting for the vegetable Mala Tang with sliced beef, I found the dish to be quite flavorful, boasting a delicious soup base and a generous helping of vegetables. However, the portion size was underwhelming, especially considering the $14-$15 price point. Served in a small paper bowl, the meal featured scant noodles, and unfortunately, it fell short of filling me up. The overall experience left me feeling that the value did not match the cost.

Cute little wine bar-esque spot in the East Village. Stopped by for happy hour with some friends on a rainy Tuesday night around 7:00PM and the restaurant was almost completely empty with just a few people at the bar.  Full disclosure- the food here is more of a 3.5 then a 4, but rounding up because it's a cute little restaurant and perfect for happy hour / dinner in a convenient location. SETTING: nice and spacious place, perfect for happy hour, dinner, dates, etc. The bartender said they are usually more packed during the week which I can believe because their happy hour runs till 9pm! FOOD: we ordered the gnocchi, meat and cheese plate, braised short ribs and eggplant lasagna. The standout by far was the gnocchi - I don't usually like gnocchi as I find it too doughy but this gnocchi was delicious and perfectly soaked in a really creamy sauce. It was so good.Everything else was solid but nothing to write home about. The meat and cheese plate was OK but pretty small portions of meat and only hard cheeses. They said the chef changes the selection every day so might have just gotten one that consisted of all hard cheeses. SERVICE: we sat at the bar and the bartenders were very attentive, consistently filling up our waters and always asking if we wanted another drink once our glasses were running low.VERDICT: I probably won't be back but if I'm in the area and need a casual but trendy spot to drink wine and eat gnocchi, this place will be an option.

This is a pretty cute place nestled away in the heart of the financial district. I came here with a friend, who had an offer to have up to $40 of her meal comped. The food here is relatively inexpensive, so my friend invited me to share food with her. This place makes home-cooked style chinese food. I was pleasantly surprised to see several vegetarian options on the menu. I ordered the cucumber salad, the scallion pancake and mapo tofu. My friend ordered a chicken appetizer and a beef noodle soup. We both enjoyed the food. While the food is not top-tier michelin-level cuisine, it's cheap, it's pretty good, and it's comfort food. The cucumber salad was cool and refreshing with a bit of heat. It was cucumbers abd wood ear mushrooms in a chili oil. The scallion pancakes were soft and fresh. The mapo tofu was pretty spicy (just at the edge of my tolerance level). It was seasoned tofu cubes and was not made in the corn starch-based sauce. Nonetheless, it was pretty good. It was served with a side of rice (which tasted slightly of scallions) and a side of "tofu greens." My (Taiwanese-American) friend said that the pork dumplings tasted exactly like her mom's. The decor was cute - small tables for two in an intimate setting. I particularly appreciated the level of service. Our server was friendly and enthusiastic. She gave a good explanation of the menu, especially of what my options were as a vegetarian, and was very patient with my and my friend's questions. At the end of the meal, I also appreciated that the server gave us warm haw tea for digestion. If you're looking for a quick, decent meal, this place is good for that.

My second NY Restaurant Week reservation included this amazing Big Eye Tuna Tartare appetizer from STK Meatpacking. The tuna was incredibly fresh, sitting atop beautifully ripe avocados and the Miso sauce was perfectly balanced as it tied the entire dish together giving it the necessary umami goodness.  The only downside to STK, the noise level, at times its hard to hear even the person directly across from you.

I enjoyed a delightful meal at this cozy establishment on Sunday evening. Despite its small footprint, the restaurant's minimalistic decor creates an inviting atmosphere. The gyoza, fried to perfection, surprised me with a generous helping of vegetables alongside the pork filling. Their fried eggplant topped with a quail egg offered a pleasant kick, reaffirming the belief that eggplant and spice is a match made in heaven. The fried chicken was another triumph, boasting a perfectly crisp exterior while retaining a succulently moist interior that was piping hot. Rounding off the meal was the donburi, a hearty serving of fried pork cutlet over rice that satisfied with both flavor and portion size. Overall, a fabulous dining experience with memorable dishes.

Title: A Taste of Senegal at Pikine – Almost Perfect

Upon recommendation from a Senegalese Uber driver, I finally visited Pikine with high expectations, which the restaurant met and exceeded. The menu offerings transported me right into the heart of West Africa, starting with the Dibi Lamb — a succulent, grilled lamb chop dish accompanied by spicy rice, onions, and a perfectly fried egg on the side, adding a comforting touch to the meal.

My companion opted for the Thiebou Yapp, a hearty serving of tender, possibly braised, lamb on the bone. The lamb was nestled beside a heap of the same aromatic rice that came with my dish, making for a poignant reminder of the rich culinary traditions of Senegal.

The bustling atmosphere spoke volumes of Pikine's popularity, evident in the number of patrons waiting for tables and the steady stream of takeout orders. Despite the crowd, we were fortunate enough to snag a table just in time.

While the food and atmosphere were without fault, Pikine could improve by including high chairs to accommodate young families. Juggling a baby on my lap with the sizable lamb chops proved to be a bit of a challenge.

In summary, my dining experience was a delightful one, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Pikine offers an authentic taste of Senegal that’s hard to find elsewhere, just be mindful if you're bringing along a little one.

Visited ROLLN for the first time around 7:00pm on Friday. It wasn't busy. When you enter, order your food using their self ordering system to your left. Once you submit your order, it should be ready very quickly.When I submitted my order of three hand rolls, I am pretty sure the employee called my name within 3 minutes.When my wife and I saw the rolls, we were so excited because the fish and avocado looked amazing. When we took our bites everything made sense. The employee was able to "prepare" our items within 3 minutes because everything was already made. We looked at the glass counter and saw pre-made hand rolls sitting and waiting to be ordered.Although the fish and avocado were decent, the rice and seaweed had been sitting and you can tell. The combination of the two were a chewy mess. I think ROLLN is trying to streamline food ordering, but it doesn't work for sushi or hand rolls and it probably never will.

This place is amazing. The food was very flavorful and the prices were amazing. My wait staff is so very attentive and they were very funny. Upon entry she took us right to our table. Our food came out together on a cart and the portion sizes are literally perfect. I couldn't even finish my food. It was a lot of food. I highly recommend this location for any meal.

NOTE: I hate writing a review based on service and not on food but I forced to based on this experience. This is my third time coming to Olma and I will NOT  be coming back. This would have been a 4-star review but this place is complete bs. We ordered the royal caviar trio which was a 4/5 experience (and in the past we ordered other caviar). In the past we had a waiter who took our order and when it comes to service we are not that picky. Today, we (3 of us) were told that they were self-serve today. Again no biggie, but at the end we were charged for an 18% tip automatically. Excuse me, what did you do that required an 18% tip? We went up and ordered and picked up the food. I had to ask 3 times for the check and you charge us for the tip.

Title: "Mixed Drinks Miss the Mark, But Snacks Satisfy at Upbeat Eatery"

I recently visited a local restaurant's upstairs bar, enticed by their happy hour specials available until 7pm. Despite the promise of deals, their Vodka & Cranberry was disappointingly juice-heavy, and my companions found little to celebrate in their lackluster Jack & Coke and Jameson & Ginger Ale. Fortunately, the Delirium beer I ordered stood out as a worthy choice with its robust flavor and punchy alcohol content.

As hunger set in, we indulged in Garlic Honey Wings, which were a savory hit thanks to a delightful sauce. The Truffle Parmesan Fries were enjoyable, though they could have benefitted from a stronger truffle presence. The Beer Battered Shrimp were a highlight, with their generous size and tasty dipping sauce.

The venue itself boasted a classic bar atmosphere across two spacious floors. Service was commendable, and prices reasonable. While our drink experience was a mixed bag, stick to the beer and the satisfying eats for a good time out.

Stop, drop, and roll on over to Burger & Lobster because I'm telling you, you're missing out if you haven't been.  The food is high quality and the prices are surprisingly good for what you get.  I ordered the skirt steak and lobster brunch.  It came with breakfast potatoes and two eggs.  To be honest I didn't need the potatoes or the eggs because the surf and turf was plenty of food.  My parents ordered the burger and lobster.  I feel like this food experience was elevated by the beautify garlic sauce that is served with the lobster. Steak and lobster is fantastic on its own, but the garlic sauce really takes it to another level.  The decor of this Burger & Lobster is very hip.  Great vibe!  Also, the location is perfect for tourists.  Right next to Times Square.

Title: A Mixed Affair at Hanjan

I recently ventured into Hanjan in Flatiron, lured by rumors of their upscale Korean Chinese offerings. The ambiance is trendy, with a vibe that's reminiscent of Oiji, but be prepared for a hit to your wallet; their prices are steep.

The standout dish of the evening was the Spicy Rice Cakes - a delightful twist on traditional ddeokbokki. They nailed the texture: the cakes were enjoyably doughy with a crisp outer layer, all bathed in a sauce that delivered the perfect punch of heat and savoriness.

The main courses, however, didn't quite live up to the appetizer's promise. The jjampong (spicy seafood noodles) lacked complexity in flavor, and the texture left much to be desired with noodles that clumped together and undersized seafood portions. At $26, the value just wasn't there.

Similarly, the jajangmyun (black bean sauce noodles) fell short. The normally hearty and indulgent sauce was too subdued for my taste, and the tidiness of the presentation stripped away the dish's usual rustic charm. I missed the messy, slurp-worthy experience that typically comes with this dish.

While I didn't leave completely dissatisfied - those rice cakes really were something - I wasn't wholly impressed either. I might circle back to Hanjan if I'm nearby, but I'd be hesitant to make a special trip just for another round of noodles.

It tasted good but definitely not worth the price. The service was good though. I wouldn't mind paying $12 for dessert if flavors were unique or there was some special baking technique. However, I feel like you are literally just paying for a picture here and not for food. The harvest seems like an easy dessert to make, just layers of cake crumbs and cheese frosting in a potted plant. There was also nothing special about the flavors. I couldn't even taste the earl grey I poured over this. I mean it was good but I've had better desserts for ~$10-15. This is something I wouldn't mind skipping if I did my NY trip again. P.S. my friends and I did not enjoy the matcha IPA

Tucked away in the bustling food market of the subway, this gem offers foodies a delightful experience with their good-quality gourmet burgers. Pair your meal with their irresistible aioli fries, and wash it down with a refreshing Pilsner beer straight from the tap. It's the perfect spot to fuel up before spending the rest of the day exploring the beauty of Central Park just across the street. Highly recommended for a tasty and satisfying meal!

My favorite restaurant in Chinatown.  Table clothes, silverware & waiter service.  The duck is prepared to table side & it's quite a show, like in Beijing they take real pride in the presentation, ambiance & quality.  We share a $60 duck & it's more than enough for 2 of us.The duck is so sweet & juicy, This skin is crisp to  perfection.  We've never tried anything else, the duck is the signature dish & it's never disappointed!

Tried the buffalo chicken sandwich and it was good. I wasn't expecting it to be made of chicken fingers so the chicken kept falling out of the sandwich.  The bread is a bit thick and doughy too which makes the bread to filling ratio off. They do give you a ton of fries but unfortunately they are soggy and limp. They should definitely work on their fries recipe.

Place was small with cute decor. There was a bar and stools to eat in (probably only 6-7 could sit up there). Menu is simple and the prices are perfect. I got the classic and the chicken pot stickers pan fried and they were delicious. Cooked through, flavorful and a good size. I got 6 and they filled me up decently, though if I went back, I think I'd try the Bao bun because it looks great too.

BEST pad thai I've ever had! There's a poached egg on top that you can mix in with the noodles to make the dish nice and creamy. Good portion, a little bit sweet, comes with chicken and shrimp. Delicious! I get takeout every time I come to NYC.

I've been going to this restaurant for many years. I think it's 20+ at this point, pretty much whenever they opened. As far as food goes  I pretty much only get the steak tartare because I know that I will never be disappointed. The steak tartare, frites  and some mayonnaise for them, that's what I like though I have tried many other things on the menu, ALL awesome. In addition I have taken no less than probably 20 girls on dates to this restaurant, I probably shouldn't be putting this out there but I called it the "pre-formulated date" I would do exactly the same thing on dates from the age of 22-43. Granted I'm 43 now and there are some Long term (5 to 6 years) relationships in their but when single this would usually assist in sealing the deal often that night. The "pre-formulated date" is something that just kind of evolved for me over time where I am in my absolute comfort zone that's giving me a phenomenal vantage point I suppose you could say. If any gentlemen have any questions about this please message me, I think you can do that on this.Anyway, The great thing is that it's a really fancy French restaurant crossed with like a TGI Fridays or something lol, I mean that in the least insulting way possible. What I'm saying is that it's just a very chill place but not quiet like you would take someone for Valentine's Day that you've been with for a while, that makes for a strange date. What I mean by that is that it loud, fun and with great drinks (though I don't drink on a first/second date...ever it's a very bad idea especially nowadays days, trust me you don't need to). No matter what the occasion this is a wonderful place to go that's probably why it's still so incredibly popular,Baltazar just has a certain charisma about it.

Must try: Grandma square pizza slices - Apple Bacon, Calabrese, and Grandma. Why: Love the crust as it's thin and airy with a nice crunch. Apple Bacon is my favorite because of all the amazing flavors coming together that complement each other: bacon, sliced apples, and crushed walnuts. I also enjoyed Calabrese and Grandmas (oily pepperoni cups - yum!)Notes: The Tartufo was overwhelmingly topped with rosemary that overtook the cheese, mushroom, and truffle oil. Good addition to UES pizza scene as they replaced Two Boots.

I recently visited this cozy spot known for its breakfast offerings, and I must say, their waffles are a true delight. The banana and pecan waffle, in particular, stood out with its perfect blend of sweetness and crunch. As a pleasant surprise, the biscuit was also scrumptious and worth a try. However, the hot chocolate didn't live up to the rest of the meal as it seemed to be a simple mix of powder and hot water. Despite that, I'd still recommend the place for their spectacular waffles and biscuits.

When we first arrived there was a sign knocked down in front of the entrance so we weren't sure if it was open. We then went in and it was quite empty, but we decided to stay and the food was honestly quite good! I would definitely go back for brunch again.

I recently dined at a restaurant where, despite the slightly outdated decor and lackluster ambiance, the food pleasantly surprised me. The ravioli I ordered was well-cooked, al dente as it should be, with flavorful ground beef filling. However, the pesto sauce's overpowering basil was more intense than I prefer. The shrimp Fra Diavlo, while tasty, packed an excessive spicy punch reminiscent of a fierce jalapeño, which overshadowed the dish's flavors.

Overall, it was a decent experience, but given the culinary competition on the Upper West Side, I wouldn't prioritize a return visit.

Title: A Pleasant Outdoor Surprise on Spring Street

I finally gave in to the lure of the quaint outdoor seating at this Spring Street gem on a rare balmy January day in NYC. The warm weather had New Yorkers flocking to enjoy meals under the sun, and I was no exception.

The dining experience kicked off with a simple yet welcoming crusty bread with butter. For the main course, my steak frites were decent – they hit the spot for a no-fuss meat and potatoes kind of meal but didn't quite venture into extraordinary territory. In comparison, my friend's blackened salmon on greens was a flavor-packed winner and definitely the star of our table.

Service was remarkably attentive, considering we were seated at a quieter side spot, which is always a plus. The generous portion sizes mean you get good value for your money, and I'm already planning a return visit to delve into their pasta offerings. Overall, a satisfying experience worthy of a repeat.

Title: A Delightful Thai Gem in the Heights

I recently dined at a new Thai spot in the Heights and was thoroughly impressed with their awesome lunch deal. For just $8.00, I savored a flavorful Green Curry with Tofu accompanied by a small side salad, white rice, and two delightful spring rolls, with water included, available until 4pm.

The green curry itself was a standout, boasting a perfect blend of spices that tantalized my taste buds. Alongside the excellent food, the staff was incredibly kind and helpful, taking time to walk me through the menu and ensure I had a great experience.

Not only is their lunch offer a steal, but the dinner prices are reasonable too. This Thai haven has definitely won me over with its combination of fantastic flavors, affordability, and friendly service. Highly recommended for anyone in the Heights looking for a satisfying meal!

**Title: Taco Triumph at a Bustling Eatery**

From the moment I stepped into the restaurant, the vibrant atmosphere made it clear that this was a place of serious taco craft. With a straightforward menu signaling a confident specialization, my anticipation grew despite the initial confusion in navigating the order-to-table process amidst the lively crowd of apparent regulars.

Patience is a virtue here, as the hand-off of your order receipt to one of the busy chefs might take a moment—but it’s a small price to pay. Watching my tacos being skillfully assembled in mere moments was part of the charm.

Opting for both beef and chicken, each taco was a revelation: succulent meat harmoniously paired with fresh, flavor-packed toppings. The medium spicy salsa verde added a delightful kick, while a generous availability of limes was a thoughtful touch. The lack of seating, replaced by standing high tables, contributes to the bustling ambiance and quick turnover—grab a spot when you can!

Finishing my meal left me with a mix of satisfaction and longing—the kind that only the best meals can inspire. A cold bottle of real-sugar Mexican Coke was the perfect accompaniment.

In summary, make no mistake: this is a must-visit for taco aficionados. My advice? Don’t walk—run to this place. Your taste buds will thank you.

**Maison Pickle Review**

I recently dined at Maison Pickle, a bustling neighborhood spot not particularly worth venturing across boroughs for, but a decent choice if you're nearby. After an initial hiccup with a late companion, the hostess proved to be charmingly accommodating.

Despite the cramped seating, the bar service was efficient and the staff friendly, with a nod to an apparent connection with the bartender. The buffalo mac and cheese was the highlight, striking a delightful balance between creamy comfort and the kick of buffalo sauce. Paired with their namesake kosher dill and hot sour pickles, the portion was generous enough to satisfy a small group.

The gin martini with house pickle juice, however, left me wanting more of that signature briny punch. Priced at $45 with tax and tip, I left quite full, and although initially ambivalent, there’s a draw to return—next time, for the french dip.

Quirky tiny Taiwan noodle place Atmosphere- tiny! Only 2 tables and 4 bar seats. The bathroom literally only fits one person.  I am also confused why they are playing Mexican music the whole time. However, I am impressed how clean the place it. It is perfectly clean everywhere I looked.Food - good but a bit overpricedThe beef noodle soup here tastes so good! The broth has very deep taste and the flat noodles pair well with it. The chunks of beef are so soft and flavorful. I was full after finishing the whole bowl. Cucumber salad is also nice, but it doesn't justify its $8 price tag.All in all, don't come if you are in a big group, if you don't like overpriced food, but do come if you want authentic Taiwanese food.

On a sizzling evening out, a rendezvous with an old friend led us to a charming spot near Grand Central, craving the cool comfort of frozen margaritas. While the establishment boasted a cute ambiance complemented by an attractive and courteous staff, the drinks, unfortunately, fell flat. Both the frozen and straight-up margaritas were disappointingly lacking in spirit, leaving us entirely buzz-free after two rounds.

The nachos, though served with impressive speed, were nothing out of the ordinary, merely meeting the expectations for standard pub fare. Ultimately, while the service was stellar, warranting a solid four-star rating, the culinary and cocktail experience hovered between a mediocre two to three stars, suggesting that future visits might be better tailored to those seeking aesthetics and service over a potent tipple and gastronomical delight.

As long as I can remember Bar Six has been around in an otherwise changing West Village.Looks wise, Bar Six has a French Bistro atmosphere and the food with both French/Moroccan influences. The food is standard, a little higher priced but that's likely in part due to the neighborhood. An old faithful pick for both brunch, lunch and dinner. There are a couple small tables outside that are coveted in the nice weather.

Came here for a quick bite and some hookah. We sat outside because we had our fur baby. We got a chicken wrap, white sangria and mango hookah. When you check in you also get a free glass of wine. Nice spot to relax and chill and last night was nice and warm to chill outdoors. The waitress was attentive..

Had a delightful brunch at this charming neighborhood gem with friends. They offer a prix fixe menu that includes coffee at a steal of a price. The ham and gruyere omelette was a highlight—fluffy, buttery perfection paired with crisp fries. Plus, the coffee hit the spot! Fast service, cozy vibes, and a fantastic alternative to those overhyped brunch spots with the endless wait times. Highly recommend for a fuss-free, delicious start to your day.

They have the best quarantine bento box! Not exaggerating.I had the Double Skewer and Tonkatsu Bento in a week ( yes I couldn't want to come back already ).The presentation was perfect.The variety of the vegetable was more than 10 types and just purely delicious. Each bite was made with their care and love (I think... Ha)And it comes with purple rice topped with plums instead of just white rice.My favorite of the favorite quarantine bento box in LES. Please support them too~

I visited a charming restaurant on Friday night with my cousin and was immediately taken with the place. The food across the board was delightful and fairly priced, although the specials were slightly on the higher side. The standout was the octopus appetizer, a steal at $20, especially with the side of burrata. Accompanying my meal with a $9 glass of wine felt just right. I decided on the green fettuccine special with wild boar ragu; it was delectable albeit a tad salty for my taste. I’m already planning my next visit but will likely explore the regular menu, which promises savings of $3-4 per dish. It’s worth noting that space is cozy—bordering on snug—so reservations come highly recommended to avoid the inevitable wait, which started around 8PM.

Was in the area and decided to come here for dinner. I wasn't really in the mood for Chinese Szechuan cuisine tonight but was still able to find some food I wanted to eat. Ordered the spicy pepper chicken, tomato fish stew, spicy garlic shrimp on hotplate and a cabbage stir-fry. They brought out the order pretty quick, didn't have to wait to long, the pepper chicken was ok, I feel like it can be a bit crispier. The garlic shrimp was superb and I recommend this dish if you come here. Not over cooked, enough flavor and the good size shrimps. Tomato soup with the fish was good, fish was fresh. I would probably eat it again but traditionally it would be served Hotpot style which would keep the soup hot and have more flavor to the broth. The cabbage was good, came out on the mini flames wok and served hot. Pricing is also very fair for a pretty authentic Szechuan cuisine in the city.  If your looking for some spicy Mala food in Manhattan, definitely keep this place in mind. Clean restaurant with nice decor.

A korean bakery They got wide range of option.Fresh made everyday, their quality is very goodWe love to order their cake for birthday.Not too sweet, very soft cake with good flavor. I like strawberry , chocolate and blueberry flavor.Never disappointed!

Title: A Cozy Dining Experience at Your Doorstep

I recently discovered a gem that truly elevates the takeout game. This restaurant sends your meal not in the typical plastic containers, but in an actual clay pot, complete with metal utensils—it’s like receiving a treasure trove of comfort food. 

The presentation is so impressive it feels as if you've been transported to the restaurant itself, all the while enjoying the comfort of your pajamas on a rainy day. The clay pot is robust and retains the perfect temperature for the meal within.

The shrimp and salmon clay pot was my choice, and it was a triumph. Adding the ginger-scallion and teriyaki sauce they provide turned the dish into a symphony of flavors. The crispy rice at the bottom of the pot was a crunchy delight, although a bit more would have been appreciated.

Despite these tiny desires for more, the meal was hearty and satisfying without breaking the bank. This place truly knows how to bring a restaurant-quality experience to your dining table.

Title: A Modern Twist on Traditional Korean Flavors at Her Name Is Han

Her Name Is Han offers a unique take on Korean cuisine in a setting that melds a Brooklyn loft with a hipster French bistro – it's charmingly eclectic, if a bit incongruous. The standout service is predominantly English-speaking, accommodating those less familiar with Korean language – although the staff's expertise wavers slightly under in-depth culinary inquiries.

The food itself champions quality over quantity. The banchans are served modestly, allowing for a more selective and less wasteful dining experience, echoing the homey essence they aim to capture. Standout dishes from our Year-End feast included the Country Fried Chicken and Spicy Marinated Blue Crab – both impeccable in flavor and execution. The Seafood Japchae was, unfortunately, the evening's underperformer, lacking the memorable taste that graced the rest of the meal.

The Spicy Rice Cake Hot Pot provided a comforting and satisfying centerpiece, well-suited for the winter's chill. Desserts were both a visual and sensory delight, with the Homemade Green Tea Biscuit Crumbs with Black Sesame Ice Cream dazzling in its variety of textures and the Soy Flour & Black Raspberry Tiramisu offering a more intricate, savory end to our meal.

In summary, Her Name Is Han stands as a culinary beacon in K-town, promising to draw a diverse crowd with its innovative approach to Korean classics. I eagerly anticipate future visits to uncover all that this establishment has to offer. Highly recommended.

Mealpal Cheeseburger with friesI was surprised how big the burger is. The patty is like a whole inch thick. It's quite tender and juicy. The burnt marks on the outside gave it good smokey flavor The bun was buttered! That made the bun slightly soggy but that's ok.The fries were soggy, my fault for not eating it right away. I put it in the oven and it got better but still nothing crunchy. Don't think the fries were salted, at least not obviously. I didn't need to dip ketchup for any of the fries (there was a lot) because it had slight flavoring to it....Reminds me of seafood. My conclusion is that the oil used to fry the fries also fried seafood beforehand. Like the fries had that taste of the batter outside fried fish/shrimp, quite yummy

My recent visit to Deja Vu steakhouse in NYC was an experience that indeed lived up to its name, making it a memorable spot among the city's plethora of steakhouses. Our waiter, George Ramirez, was the epitome of friendly and attentive service, prompting us to recommend him to our parents for their upcoming visit.

During restaurant week, we indulged in a three-course feast that left us more than satisfied without breaking the bank. At $42 per person, the value was undeniable, especially for a steakhouse in New York. I savored the fresh field greens salad and a perfectly cooked filet mignon, followed by a delectable cheesecake. My husband enjoyed the hearty chowder, a flavorful NY strip, and a decadent coffee chocolate cake.

For those with a penchant for wine, there's an optional pairing menu that adds to the experience for an additional $28. The ambiance of Deja Vu is distinctively masculine with a man cave vibe, showcased by its preserved animal decor and angular architecture. If you're scouting for a steakhouse that offers a hearty meal, excellent service, and a unique setting without an extravagant price tag, Deja Vu is a place you'll want to visit.

Came here with Pulsd deal with one appetizer and two main ($20 each) and two drinks. Saturday lunch was empty. Apart from us there was another table at noon on a weekend. So service was fast. Most of the famous Sichuan dishes are 29.90 which is very expensive compare to the Sichuan restaurants nearby. So we ended up couldn't order the ones we wanted; I guess that what the deal I got so I have no complain. But for the price in this place I would not come back without any sort of discount. I saw they have $35 for $50 on yelp deal. Instead of giving discount why not just try to lower the price. The fish fillet in chili sauce is good spicy but nothing really special. Lamb with cumin also taste very decent.  The steam chicken with chili oil (口水鸡）doesn't taste like anywhere I had before, not spicy at all the with funky taste. Tan tan noodle was very disappointing, the noodles were cooked too long and was broken apart, despite not having enough sauce to mix it.

I recently tried Great Sichuan, a Chinese restaurant specializing in Sichuan cuisine. It's worth noting this is not your average Chinese takeout joint. I opted for the beef lo mein, which is Cantonese, so keep in mind this may not be their forte. The dish fell short on flavor, with insufficient sauce to properly season the noodles, particularly at the top. However, the sauce itself had a decent taste. Based on this experience, it might be wiser to choose a Sichuan dish to truly appreciate what Great Sichuan has to offer.

Title: Unique Solo Dining Experience at Ichiran NYC

Ichiran in NYC checked off my restaurant bucket list with its specialized Tonkotsu ramen and unique solo-dining booths. Although the restaurant is better suited for individual diners, their staff were accommodating to our group, efficiently seating us with minimal wait time.

Upon arrival, we were handed menus and pens to start ordering. The menu could use more clarity, particularly in explaining what's included in the $18 and $24 ramen bowls. Opting for the customizable $18 bowl, I inadvertently added marinated pork loin, not realizing the bowl already included meat. A perk with this option is the complimentary noodle refill, which isn't available with the premade $24 bowl.

Despite the confusion and the less-than-impressive pork loin and chashu texture, the ramen's flavor and broth were outstanding—arguably the best we've ever tasted. While this was the priciest ramen experience yet, the delicious flavors ensure a return visit is in the cards.

Overall, Ichiran provides a great dining experience. I would recommend this spot to both NYC visitors and locals alike, especially for those looking for a solitary but memorable meal.

Delicious! Great Staff! Clean! I loved it! Honestly I don't give such a high recommendation to many restaurants. #Scarpetta has gone above and beyond in service, entertainment and brunch.The waiters are highly trained, they come and can take the dirty silverware without you even knowing. The food was savory. We were a group of 6 and had a few warm up dishes of salads, and the  cauliflower which was okay, it needed a bit more flavor. Than came my pancakes which were soft, with a delicate touch of white sugar powder and warm maple syrup. I also tasted the french toast that could have been a bit less soggy. Nothing is perfect but this sure was close. My drink was a foamy expresso coffee with an orange peel.It was my friend's birthday and they served her a surprise cake with ice cream. What a fun morning. P.S. the bread they serve in the beginning is the sweetest flat scone with Jelly and soft fresh butter. I could eat that with a cup of coffee. I tried to eat and savor it... it was that delicious.(ending it where I started)Handicap-- the bathroom is downstairs in Hotel James- where we waited till our reservation was ready. Stand by for pics!

Title: Authentic Chinese BBQ on a Budget at Wah Fung

If you find yourself on the Lower East Side with a craving for Chinese comfort food, Wah Fung should top your list. This no-frills Chinese barbecue joint offers unbeatable prices for a variety of savory roasted meats served over rice.

Don't expect to lounge around – Wah Fung is all about the hustle of grab-and-go dining. The space is compact and authentically worn, providing a slice of old-school New York charm. There's typically a queue, a testament to its popularity, but it moves swiftly thanks to the efficient staff.

Among the must-tries are the deliciously sweet char siu (barbecue pork) and the perfectly crispy-yet-juicy pork belly. Served over a bed of rice and cabbage, they create a harmony of flavors that's both filling and immensely satisfying. Portion sizes range from small (ideal for solo diners) to large (enough to share), all priced from a budget-friendly $4 to $8.

Be warned, fan favorites like duck may run out early, so swing by sooner rather than later. And since there's no seating, plan to enjoy your meal amidst the urban outdoors in nearby parks and gardens. Just be sure to know what you want before you reach the counter – it's a place that values decisiveness and swift transactions.

In short, Wah Fung is a culinary gem for those in search of quality Chinese BBQ without breaking the bank. It's the kind of place you'll want to frequent once you've had a taste. So go ahead, dive into the flavors of Wah Fung – just be ready to "Wah Fung and go"!

Rating: 4.5/5 – For its mouthwatering eats, quick service, and exceptional value.

This has been bookmarked for a bit and I finally got a chance to visit it. My friend has been raving about it so it gave me a push to go even more. I mean who doesn't love tacos ?? Upon arrival i noticed the place was packed, good sign right.. anyway we hear a 45 min wait.. uggh really.. the bar was packed so we had to find a littlr nook to stand and chat. I went to the bathroom and i dont understand why they only have two stalls.. it's a fairly big place , no one wants to wait 10 mins on line to use the toilet..  We ended up waiting less than 45 more like 30. However, i noticed several empty tables in the restaurant. For more than 20 mins. Think that makes no sense if theres ppl waiting to be seated. Anyway when we finally get seated its right by the door.. well just great .. i guess ill eat with my coat on why not. The draft from the door opening constantly was annoying. Food- i enjoyed my pollo recado quesadilla. It was tasty because i added guac and their jalapeno green sauce. It was the best thing i had. The el pastor and baja fish taco were just ok. Nothing exciting but not the worst. Needed more flavor. Service was good. Waiter was attentive and friendly. Manager did come over and apologize about sitting us next to the door stating that the heat was on 83 degrees. That was nice of him. What would've been nicer is another table. All in all i wont be in any rush to come back. Nothing really new that I cant get from another closer taco spot.
Fantastic space for delightful deserts, small cakes or sandwiches.  I enjoyed the eclair, unmistakably French, rich and creamy.

I recently tried takeout from a local restaurant via the Ritual app for a weekday lunch and was left underwhelmed. Despite ordering ahead, the meal wasn't ready as promised, leading to a frustrating wait that cut into my lunch break. I opted for the Chirashi, but it was unlike any I've had before - and not in a positive sense. The dish featured a single, flat slice of each type of fish rather than the standard, more generous portions I expected. For $15, I anticipated a satisfying meal, but this Chirashi was a letdown. The disproportionate amount of sushi rice to fish left me with an unbalanced and unsatisfying meal, forcing me to look elsewhere to satiate my hunger. I won't be returning for seconds.

Title: A Satisfying First Visit to Field Good

I recently made my inaugural visit to Field Good, unsure of what to order. Fortunately, a helpful staff member at the counter came to my rescue, offering a generous tray brimming with an array of selections for under $18. The highlight was undoubtedly the boneless chicken breast - perfectly charred skin and expertly seasoned. Accompanying the chicken were sides of quinoa, refreshing cucumber, a delightful sweet potato mash, and more hidden treasures beneath.

While I expected cornbread and found a brown sugar blondie instead, it was a pleasant surprise. The mac & cheese, however, was begging for a cheese with more punch. The sweet potatoes surpassed mediocrity, but as a die-hard fried chicken enthusiast, my heart remains elsewhere.

Despite not finishing everything, Field Good impressed me with both its food and service. It's a promising spot that I'm convinced will become a cherished addition to our local dining scene.

Following the praise from David Portnoy, we decided to try out this local eatery, intrigued by its reputed charm. Contrary to the puzzling low Yelp score, our experience echoed Portnoy's commendations. The choice to sample two half pizzas—Margarita and Mexicana—proved wise. While the Margarita was satisfactory, the Mexicana truly delighted our palates. The captivating flavors have ensured our return, confirming that this place is deserving of its acclaim.

Title: A Taco Haven Worth the Wait

I recently visited a local gem renowned for its tacos, and I must say, the hype is well-deserved. The chicken tacos, snugly wrapped in corn tortillas with a generous helping of toppings, are my absolute favorite. Reasonably priced, you'll find that three tacos hit the spot, but if you've got an appetite, go for four and you'll be more than satisfied.

The ordering system is straightforward: queue up, grab a ticket, and exchange it for some delicious fare. Fair warning—arrive late and you might find yourself at the tail end of a winding line, especially around peak lunch hours. I made it just before noon on a Friday, and the crowd was already spilling out the door.

Despite the rush, the service is commendable; the staff efficiently keeps things moving without compromising on friendliness. My advice? Beat the lunchtime bustle and head in early. It's worth planning your schedule around.

Title: Mixed Feelings on a Long-Anticipated Visit

After frequently passing by and feeling the pull to try out this local spot, I finally gave in and ordered their galbi. The meat itself delivered on flavor, credit to a commendable marinade that brought out a rich taste in every bite. The accompanying soup impressed, complementing the meal with its own savory notes.

However, the portions presented a letdown. The rave reviews didn't mention the meager serving sizes, and I was relieved to have ordered extra banchan to fill the gap. The presentation was admittedly misleading; a hidden bone padded beneath the four pieces of meat gave the illusion of abundance that simply wasn't there.

While the food quality sparks interest in a potential dine-in experience—observing a more content crowd on those occasions—I can't ignore the lackluster service during my pickup. An inattentive gesture left me with a sharpie stain, a small but needless annoyance in an otherwise quiet setting. It's these details that can make or break a customer's experience, and I hope for improvement on my next visit, should I decide to return.

Title: Satisfying Dumpling Craving with Room for Improvement

After a refreshing facial session in the vicinity, I found myself at a cozy little dumpling spot to address my cravings. The menu was refreshingly uncomplicated, focused squarely on their dumplings, without the distraction of an alcohol list. However, the absence of customer restrooms and a seating capacity of a mere 10 people might deter some.

I opted for a mix of the classic and vegan dumplings. The classic dumplings won my preference, although the vegan option was decent as well. Both were elevated by the tantalizing sauces and the zing of hot pepper oil provided.
