On impulse, I decided to try the red bean mochi cake as I left. Despite an unusually long wait and slightly burnt edges, the mochi cake was quite delightful – a treat I would indulge in again.

A slight letdown occurred at the end of my visit; overhearing a subsequent customer being offered a rewards card – a perk I missed out on. This would have been a great incentive to return. Despite this oversight, the overall experience was enjoyable, leaving me with a likelihood of coming back for those dumplings.

These are the best rice noodles I have ever had! The soup is SO flavorful and the noodles are smooth yet bouncy, and clings onto the soup perfectly. The staff is friendly and attentive, and ready to answer any questions. I got the extra spicy rice noodle and my significant other got the tomato rice noodle. Both were super flavorful and well balanced. Their chili oil is also super flavorful and you can add in black vinegar and numbing oil. There's the option for you to add in your own toppings or for the staff to add it for you. It's either great for the experience or if you're lazy you can still enjoy it too! Definitely one of the things I'll miss the most from NY!

Came in within the last hour and was greeted by a server that immediately told us that the kitchen was closing soon and we'd have to order in a few minutes. Okay, no problem. I've worked in service before and understand the workers want to go home on time. My friend and I scanned the menu real quick and decided on the dduk boki since it said it was enough to serve 2 people. We were seated at a 4-top and after we ordered, one of the servers basically threw some cutlery on our table, not even in front of us, but in the empty seats next to us. Okay... Then came the salad with some cabbage, carrots, and dressing. No kimchi at a Korean restaurant? Really? Even the stalls at the Food Gallery across offer kimchi and pickled radish. The dduk boki itself was alright, nothing special but not bad. I paid the check as soon as the food came but didn't stay long cause I didn't feel very welcomed. In the end my friend and I packed the food to go.

Xian Famous Foods was OK. I think it is overhyped. I had the spicy cumin lamb noodles and the spicy cumin lamb burger. The noodles were thicker and harder to chew than I expected. The flavor and sauce was good and had the right amount of spice. The lamb burger bun was also harder than expected. I got both items to-go and ate it later but I did try the noodles at the restaurant (as recommended) to know the "intended" texture and flavors of the noodles. Sadly, it was not as good as I expected. The lamb, in general, was tasty but there could have been bigger pieces; it felt like lamb scraps in both the noodles and bun. Service was quick and the price is pretty cheap for NY standards.

Title: A Culinary Jewel in the East Village – My Thursday Kitchen Experience

Review:

There's a reason Thursday Kitchen has been the talk of the town, and suffice it to say, a mere 5-star rating doesn't do it justice. My friends and I descended on this gem nestled in the East Village, a space alive with energy albeit a tad cozy and buzzing with conversation. It's a vibrant date spot if you don't mind the wait and a lively backdrop for catching up.

Our evening kicked off with potent drinks, the guys sipping on the pure strawberry soju, while the girls opted for non-alcoholic options. A word to the wise, these concoctions are deceptively strong!

Each dish that graced our table was a revelation. The edamame dumplings struck a delightful chord with their unique twist, and the gnocchi with its hint of heat and seaweed crunch was a flavor fusion done right. Even as someone who's not an avocado enthusiast, I was taken aback by the pomegranate-accented avocado dish—simply incredible.

The showstopper, though, was the Kimchi Paella— a dish that echoed the authenticity of Spain yet imbued with a distinct Korean flair, cooked to sheer perfection. The popcorn chicken that followed was succulent and well-seasoned, the steak a divine interplay of caramelized sauce and tender meat, and the mac n cheese? Well, it's their signature for a reason, and it completely won over this picky eater.

Yes, Thursday Kitchen may be a bit of a splurge, but the culinary experience is worth every penny; it's a symphony of Korean-Spanish flavors that leaves you craving for more. This restaurant just comfortably settled onto my shortlist of NYC must-visits, and as I recount my experience, I'm already yearning for the next visit.

My family came here on a Sunday afternoon. When we entered, we waited maybe a good 3-5 min before someone came to help us, which is fine except I made eye contact with the host who was near the bar. When the host came over he let us know we were sitting in upstairs and to follow the server up. The server placed two menus down nicely on the table and then chucked the other two onto the table which led to the little drinks menu being knocked over and hitting the salt over.We ordered a dozen oysters ($1 each!), the 5 Mile Stone burger and replaced the regular fries with truffle fries, the fish and chips and the crab cakes benedict. Each entree came with a complimentary drink because it was brunch. We got the mimosa, peach Bellini and the raspberry Bellini. I'm not a fan of the drinks because I could taste the alcohol, but my sister like the peach Bellini and the Mimosa. The oysters were thin and not sweet, but it will satisfy any cravings. I would say Barnjoo has better oysters for happy hour. The batter that the fish was fried in was too heavy and thick for my taste, but other than that it was good. Be careful not to burn your mouth like I did! The regular fries and truffle fries looked the same except the truffle fries had cheese sprinkled on it. The truffle fries were good, but I wish it had a stronger truffle taste. Both fries were quickly devoured. The crab cakes were really thin and it was hard to taste the crab because of the egg over it, but that's not an issue if since I ate it separately. The little salad that came with it was refreshing and light and the home fries were good. The burger was a normal burger, nothing special.

I'm traveling with Comfort Tours Canada on a 4-day 3-nights (Hyatt Regency Newbrunswick NJ) trip from Toronto, ON to New York City, NY.  Our Tour Director is Natasha and Driver is Miriam on a Kunkel coach bus.It's really humid (...and the temp is 90 degrees Fahrenheit) walking around NYC Midtown so hydration is the key, hence it is off to T.G.I. Friday's!Two 20oz Budweiser draft for $7.50 during happy hour to start plus an order of Loaded Chicken Nachos $15.99.Bartender Tian provided good service but the food was average.  The positive thing was that we were well hydrated before the ride back to our hotel!

The broth was too salty for me. For being one of the best ramen places in NY I thought it was quite average. A tasty bowl indeed-- perfect soft boiled egg, noodle texture on point, a cute naruto on top, a hefty pile of seaweed, and tender thin sliced pork belly. However I thought it was lacking a special something. Maybe it was the ambiance with the sleek modern dim lit and hip vibe that threw me off. The customer service was fast and attentive which was nice. I do like that they shout at you in japanese when you enter

Title: A Cozy Spot with Quick Turns and Tasty Eats

Upon arriving at this bustling eatery, the cozy atmosphere was immediately noticeable, with a packed dining space suggesting a local favorite. The recommendation to arrive early is a solid one, especially over the weekend. Anticipating a 30-minute wait, it was a pleasant surprise to be seated in a mere 5 minutes—quite the prompt start to an evening already made cheerful thanks to a hastily-enjoyed mai tai nearby.

The soju sampler was a highlight of the visit, the little lights adding a playful touch that showcased the drinks' vibrant hues and complemented their delightful flavors. The extensive menu held much promise with an array of tantalizing choices, making it difficult to decide.

The fried tiger rolls were a decent appetizer, but the bulgogi stole the show. It was as flavorful as any top-tier Korean BBQ joint, hitting that perfect smoky note that aficionados seek out.

In all, the experience exceeded expectations, and I'm already planning a return visit to explore more of the menu. If you're in the mood for authentic flavors and a lively atmosphere, this spot is definitely worth checking out.

Tucked away in a charming 1767 carriage house in the heart of NYC, this restaurant, established in 1973, truly lives up to its title as the fifth most romantic restaurant globally. The moment you step inside, elegance envelops you—quality and service of the highest order, with food that matches in excellence. Yet, it's the ambiance that weaves the magic spell.

As you enter, a beautifully crafted bar greets you, complete with a cozy fireplace, setting the stage for a dream-like experience. The dishes are delicious, and the wait staff navigates the space with a hushed grace, ensuring an uninterrupted romantic soiree. Outside, the courtyard dazzles under white lights, creating a fairy-tale setting.

Though not seated by the window, the view was still enchanting, leaving me yearning for that spot on my next visit. For anyone seeking to elevate a romantic engagement, a birthday, or an anniversary, this gem is the place to be—it promises to make your special occasion unforgettable.

If you're like me and didn't know what northwestern Chinese food was, do yourself a favor and make your way to Jiang Diner.  This new restaurant specializes in northwestern Chinese food and it is BOMB!I got several dishes to share and while all were good, some were especially great!My favorite was the big plate chicken dish. The chicken was so incredibly tender and the perfect level of spice. The noodles at the bottom were also chewy and had soaked up the delicious sauce. Huge fan. One person could definitely eat a small portion by themselves and it would be a great meal.The fried lamb was also delicious. Somehow soft yet crispy with great dipping sauces (a chili one and a cumin rub) the northerners do lamb right. We also ordered the lamb shumai and sauteed crispy baked buns with cumin flavor. The shumai were like little savory pockets of meat and juice, nom! I would recommend eating them right away as they come out so that the skin on top of the shumai doesn't dry out.  The sauteed crispy baked buns was also good--we got ours with beef (how they make all their meat so unbelievably tender is a secret I need to learn). The crispy buns were like fried bread/croutons. Pro tip: dip the bread into the sauce from the big plate chicken for some mouthgasms. You're welcome!Overall, great food and super attentive service. I'm so sad I left the east village right as all these great Chinese restaurants started popping up!  Will definitely have to make my way up again soon for some big plate chicken.

Title: A Gelato Gem in London

My visit to Bring in the Gelato transformed my evenings in London into a delightful quest for the perfect scoop of gelato. This spot is a must-visit, especially considering the vast array of flavors that tantalize the taste buds with their authenticity - think mango, raspberry, lemon, to the richer, cream-based delights like vanilla, chocolate, caramel, and an irresistible blueberry cheesecake that swiftly became my personal favorite.

With the option of mixing up to five different flavors in one cup, or having your cone crafted into an exquisite rose, the experience is as visually appealing as it is palate-pleasing. Although prices are on the higher side, the exceptional quality of the gelato justifies every penny. Without a doubt, Bring in the Gelato serves up the finest, most authentic gelato I've ever had – a nightly tradition that my daughter insisted on, and one I'd happily uphold.

looking  to spice up your life? dine at at Mughlai Grill on Clinton Street.Mughlai Grill is a casual Indian restaurant doling out flavorful dishes on the Lower East Side. i get takeout and delivery from Mughlai. however you can dine in at Mughali as well...as it has medium-sized charming dining room perfect for casual relaxed lunches and dinners.recommendations: baghari jhingha--a must if you like spicy shrimp; both the gobhi palak and aloo gobhi are great cauliflower dishes options for vegans + vegetarians; and the chicken tikka is good option for those who want a flavorful dish that is not too spicy.the naan is freshly-made, puffy, crispy bread add-on that is so good.on every takeout and delivery order, Mughali included a complimentary order of papadum. nice touch.as the weather turns cooler, enjoy comfort eats via Mughlai's south asian offerings.drops mic cuz the spice is righti outzzz

Overall: 3/5Mediocre place. People mostly come for the location as it's one of the few "Asian food" places in the area. It caters to a more well off crowd in the surrounding area and propositions more on its decor/vibe than food/value. Go to Chinatown for some real Asian food!Service: 3/5Below average. Staff actually understood Korean, which is a +1 for that.Food: 3/5Average. The chicken wings with soy garlic sauce were good, but that was more on the garlic sauce than the chicken.Value: 2/5Poor. Portion sizes were very small. Prices were on the high end. Drink prices weren't bad for Manhattan.

During my weekend trip to New York, me and some friends decided to get brunch Saturday afternoon.We decided on Friedman's because we had never gone before and they had many options on the menu to choose from. It was also nice that 99% of the items on the menu are gluten free.I got pancakes. a side of hash browns, and the lemonade special(matcha mango). I will say that the lemonade was really good, however the pancakes and hash browns were underwhelming. The servers were really nice and friendly though which made the experience betterThere are many things on the menu so I do see myself coming back because to try their other items. I do find Friedman's slightly overrated compared to other brunch experiences that I have had elsewhere.

Always looking for authentic Japanese restaurants, we wanted to love Hirohisa. While Hirohisa's food was very good and service was excellent, we were not "transported" to Tokyo for a couple of hours. The shrimp tempura was very greasy, rather than the light coating that you normally find in Japan (and the best tempura spots here). The beef was good and the rice dishes were excellent. So net, net it was good but just not the ethereal experience you have in the truly best Japanese restaurants. We will be back, but not be regulars.

On a bustling Saturday evening, my visit to this conveniently located restaurant, attached to a hotel, was met with prompt service as my coat was checked and I was swiftly seated. The menu's flexible structure of 1st and 2nd course selections allowed for a tailored dining experience, where I opted for two appetizers followed by a main dish in appetizer size—a wise choice given the generous portions I observed around me.

My culinary journey commenced with the hamachi tartar, which initially raised my eyebrows with a slightly fishy first bite, only to be redeemed by a symphony of flavors and textures, notably the unexpected crunch of celery and capers. The pea soup, while abundant in serving size, struck me as somewhat monotonous despite the textural variance from whole peas.

The star of the evening was the asparagus risotto, a harmonious blend of flavors accentuated by earthy maitake mushrooms and the dual textures of asparagus. My meal concluded on a sweeter note with a strawberry tart, which, while pleasant, didn't quite dazzle, though the accompanying vanilla ice cream was a hit. A complimentary batch of Madelines provided a delightful final touch.

Overall, the experience was solid, and the restaurant's offerings have piqued my interest enough to warrant a return visit.

I use to love this place came by because I was in the neighborhood. Got a seat quick. I remember it being exclusive, dim lit, sexy,and always booked. Now, Interior is run down. I dont remember Max Brenner being this messy. Upsides food was still good and Staff were friendly and accommodating. But bring back the old vibes!

My friend works night shifts so our group has been meeting up really late in the day, lately. I'm usually not able to go out with them at that time, but this time I did and lucky for us, Boka is one of those places that stays open past midnight, plus they're not crowded at that hour, so there's no wait for a table and it's a chill place.I had the bulgogi bibimbap in the hot stone bowl, but they have the option to have it serves cold, as well. I'd strongly recommend getting it hot though, because any Korean food connoisseur (not that I would consider myself one) knows that the best part of bibimbap is the crunchy layer of rice at the bottom, and that's exactly what I got at Boku. Plus, it comes with a poached egg, which is my favorite way of having eggs, although this one wasn't as runny as I would've liked but hey, a poached egg is a poached egg.

Went to Spot Dessert Bar tonight for the first time. It's a very small space with few seats so there was a wait to be seated. A very nice employee approached me and offered her assistance. She pointed out that certain items on the menu are seasonal and will be removed soon. I decided to go with a seasonal item. Everything on the menu looks delicious. The presentation is top notch too. The place looks clean & organized. They also offer beverages. I ordered a bubble tea. The tea was excellent but the tapioca bubbles were tough and chewy. I probably wouldn't return here for bubble tea, but I definitely would for the  desserts. Very nice selection! Great presentation.

While nothing will ever replace The Great Jones Cafe, Gabriel Stulman is giving it a try with The Jones. Stulman, the successful West Village restaurateur behind Joseph Leonard and Fedora, among many other hot spots. The vibe at The Jones is casual and local and food is great too. The cocktails are really good. The starters are better than the main courses, but all are good.

As a regular patron of Sticky's, I recently visited a new branch with high expectations, only to be let down. The chicken, usually a highlight, was uncharacteristically bland, and not even the sauce could rescue the dish. The saving grace, if any, were the fries that retained their familiar, satisfying taste. I'm left uncertain about revisiting this specific location.

Title: A Seaport Gem for a Satisfying Meal

In the hustle of South Street Seaport, finding a tranquil spot for a meal that's gentle on the wallet and the stomach can be a tough order, but this little diner checks all those boxes. Amidst limited options, it's a haven.

My choice was a classic salmon with rice pilaf, accompanied by broccoli and a simple side salad—though calling it a "salad" might be a bit generous. The greens were sparse and uninspired, but with a drizzle of olive oil, they did the job.

Thankfully, the main dish was well-executed. The salmon was cooked properly, flaky and moist, the rice was flavorful, and the broccoli was crisp-tender, all defying the often-met fate of these foundational dishes being botched in less careful kitchens.

Service was attentive and pleasant, which could be due to the sparse crowd at the time of my visit—so take that as it may. As a side note, brace yourself for an adventure en route to the bathrooms, which come with a dose of New York character and a slightly eerie descent.

Overall, this diner is a solid choice when you're in the area. Despite its quirks, it delivers where it counts: satisfying food in a cozy setting. I'll be back for another peaceful meal the next time I'm in the neighborhood.

Title: Savory Savings at Fumo During Unprecedented Times

In a world adapting to the pandemic, Fumo cleverly responds with enticing pick-up specials that cater to both our wallets and our palates. With a generous 15% discount on food and an irresistible 50% off on bottled wines, Fumo ensures you don't miss out on the dine-out experience from the comfort of your home.

Opting for mixed drinks over wine, I found both the margarita and Paloma for just $6 each to be delightful. The margarita, in particular, struck the perfect balance between tart and sweet, and when served in a salt-rimmed glass, it truly hit the mark.

The artichoke dish, a flavorful treat, would have reached perfection with a lighter accompaniment; the rich mayo dip was overwhelming. I concur with previous critiques that a subtler vinaigrette would enhance rather than overshadow the artichoke's natural taste.

As for the penne vodka, it met all expectations—comforting, satisfying, and definitely worth a repeat order.

Fumo's pick-up option isn't just a deal—it's a meaningful way to sustain local businesses during these tough times. Don't miss out on this opportunity to indulge and support your community at once.

Title: A Slice of Authenticity at Cafe Rustico II

During our New York City escapades, my wife and I found ourselves ravenous, eager to satisfy our cravings for the famed NY pizza. That's how we stumbled upon Cafe Rustico II. Despite our initial reservations, prompted by the sparse customer attendance at 3 pm, the tantalizing scents wafting from the kitchen could not be ignored. The minimalist English of the staff only solidified our hunch—this was the real deal.

The restaurant's cleanliness tipped the scales, and soon enough, we were sinking our teeth into an array of pizza slices—classic original, loaded supreme, hearty Sicilian, and fresh margarita. Each bite confirmed our hopes: the crust was simply unparalleled, a texture and taste beyond my prior experience at a Minnesota imitation. The homemade sauce, fresh sausage, and vibrant veggies adorned my supreme slice, making it evident that these were ingredients of quality.

Now, Cafe Rustico II isn't perfect; my supreme slice could have used a bit more warmth. Yet, that minor hiccup doesn't overshadow the fact that, on this four-day New York tour, Cafe Rustico II has set a high bar for any subsequent pizza places. Should we discover a superior slice, we promise an update. But for now, Cafe Rustico II stands as a proud representation of authentic New York-style pizza, and we're thoroughly enjoying the taste of the city. Four stars.

Craving guac! The chips are too thick but I love the creaminess was of the guacamole and the tacos were good too. I liked the cabbage slaw on the shrimp tacos, but what I enjoyed most was the amazing guacamole. Would go back for just that.

I came here at the recommendation of a friend, and had high expectations after hearing that it was run by the same people as Los Tacos no. 1, which I had previously really enjoyed. I didn't have the same positive feelings about this place though. At Los Mariscos, they specialise in fish tacos, and Mexican seafood dishes. The location is near Chelsea Market, and it is a bustling place, in which you order and pay before eating. There are a couple of benches at which you can sit, and it's not the kind of place you linger at after finishing your food. We shared the oysters, while my husband had the fish tacos as his main. The oysters and the tacos were presented in a timely fashion, but the red aguachiles that I ordered took a much longer than expected time to come out. I'd never had this dish before, and also have never seen it any menus in Mexican restaurants. It consisted of a raw prawns in a slightly spicy red sauce, with cucumbers and red onions. I liked the flavors in the dish, but overall, wouldn't rate it as amazing or a must-order. My husband enjoyed his tacos, but also said they weren't the best. The oysters are not something I would recommend. Would not come back based on this experience.

Title: A Spirited Brunch at Pig and Khao

If you're on the hunt for an affordable bottomless brunch, Pig and Khao has you covered. At $16 for two hours of endless refills, your glass will never run dry. My friend and I popped in on a Sunday afternoon and were swiftly seated, a pleasant surprise given the usual brunch rush.

However, the atmosphere struck a discordant note. The vibrant music, more suited to a Saturday night escapade, clashed with our hopes of a relaxing meal, making conversation a challenge.

The food was satisfactory, yet not exceptional considering the price point. The Sizzling Sisig and steak paired with eggs were decent but failed to justify their costs, especially at $18 for a dish that only hit the "mediocre" mark. The rareness of the steak was notable, and while the Vietnamese iced coffee ($5) leaned towards the less sweet side, the excessive ice was a drawback.

On the brighter side, service was impeccable; our servers were nothing short of welcoming and accommodating, elevating the overall experience.

Ratings:
Ambience: 3.5/5
Food: 3/5
Price: 2/5
Service: 5/5

In summary, Pig and Khao might be a buzzing locale for those craving unlimited mimosas and lively tunes, but those seeking culinary value and quiet conversation might find it lacking.

Came here to try some Malaysian cuisine! They are cash only! The internal design of the place is very nice and they have these buttons on their table where you can call for service. I like their Thai iced tea a lot and it helped cleansed the palate from the spiciness of the dishes we ordered. Most of their dishes are spicy and you can ask for less or more. I plan to come back and try their curry/noodle dishes next time ! The halo halo was good!

My friend and I recently visited this restaurant for brunch and were left underwhelmed. Despite a promising menu, the service was sluggish, which was surprising given the sparse number of patrons. Additionally, there was an unexpected charge for a mango juice refill, which the waitress failed to mention when I requested it. While the experience wasn't terrible, it's not a place I would recommend unless you're in dire need of a bite and options are scarce.

Um...not sure what happened this past weekend, but service was bad! It's a shame bc the food and sake were decent. Came here with several friends and had a corner table, ordered a few appetizers and a couple bottles of sake. We put our app orders in at two different times, and being a busy night, it took about 30 minutes for the first round to come out. The fried squid "fries" were really good, a little like jerky, really tasty and interesting. The kura-age was basically popcorn chicken, bite-sized morsels freshly fried and crispy. When it came to the pulled pork bao I ordered, after 30 minutes there was no sign of them. Understanding it was busy we asked the server and he said they were being made and kitchen was a bit behind. 10 minutes later no word. My friend goes to ask the server again and he says that the order isn't ready but then also adds that it wasn't the pork bao on order but the vegetable one. Huh?? When I placed the order, I especially repeated my order and had him repeat it back to me bc the table next to us was very loud...we ended up cancelling the order bc they couldn't provide an actual time when the food would be ready. Beyond annoyed bc I hadn't had dinner and was super hangry waiting for those bao to come.

I recently dined at a lovely spot where I had an amazing bowl of hot pot that was perfectly seasoned and utterly satisfying. Additionally, the veggie ramen was a standout—deliciously rich and packed with flavor. The cute decor added to the overall charm of the restaurant, making it a delightful dining experience. The value for money was spot on, making it a place I would highly recommend for a fantastic meal.

Good food, fine service, very popular happy hour location. Food comes out really fast during happy hour when you sit down and eat because everyone is drinking :)I would not go out of my way to return but it's a gem in the rough area that is Harold square.

I recently visited this bustling spot for a lunch outing to celebrate my coworker's birthday, and we lucked out snagging one of the last available tables at the noon rush. Service was lightning fast: within five minutes of sitting down, we had browsed the menu and placed our orders via their efficient iPad system.

I went with the lunch rolls and tacked on a few a la carte hand rolls, while my coworker chose various a la carte selections. The rolls arrived promptly, and we gleefully devoured them in record time – our entire meal wrapped up in under an hour.

The standout was undoubtedly the scallop roll; its flavor and freshness were so impressive that we both ordered seconds. On the flip side, the vegetarian roll was underwhelming, akin to a simple salad encased in rice and seaweed - it might be worth skipping unless it’s part of a lunch special deal.

Wrapping up, we both left satisfied with the quality and speed of our meal, which came to a reasonable $120 after tip and tax. My advice: arrive early to beat the queues, as this place doesn't take reservations but is definitely worth the visit.

We stumbled upon this gem of a restaurant right after our delightful visit to Rose Mansion. The place boasted an impressive size, and we were warmly greeted by the host who ushered our group inside. Craving some classic bar food, we indulged in a variety of dishes including wings, mozzarella sticks, burgers, chicken sandwiches, and fries. Each item was satisfying, though if I were to nitpick, I would have preferred the fries and mozzarella sticks to arrive a tad hotter; they were just a notch above warm. Nonetheless, the overall quality of the food was undeniably good, making our post Rose Mansion adventure a deliciously memorable one.

Title: A NYC Gem That Delights the Senses

I recently dined at a stunning addition to Stephen Starr's restaurant empire, and this Manhattan hotspot lived up to the buzz. With an interior that pays homage to the vibrant essence of New York City, the space is adorned with jars of preserved lemons and an impressive display of wine and glassware, all framed by tall, inviting windows.

Our culinary journey began with the BBQ Point Judith Squid—each bite of this seemingly charred yet tender dish revealed a smoky flavor elevated by the crunch of pickled cauliflower. The Spaghettini followed, a masterclass in subtlety charged with the briny whisper of oceanic bottarga di muggine. It was a pasta dish impossible to put down.

The showstopper, Shrimp + Rice, featured succulent pacific prawns atop a bed of perfectly crisped cast iron rice, rounded out with a creamy garlic aioli. The meal was not just a dinner, but a celebration of flavor that felt as though it was in honor of all of us there.

In this 900th review, I'm delighted to say this place steals the show—every New Yorker and visitor should take a seat at this table.

An unforgettable place. I've been here twice--today being my second time, and every time I can say it does not disappoint! I normally don't like fusion food, but this Korean mixed with lots of other eccentricities in tapas plates is simply delicious. We ordered the Truffle Mac & Cheese, Soft Shell Crab, Cauliflower, Lucky Noodles, Eel Taco, Duck Confit, and a Capri Sun alcoholic drink (note: just as delicious and shapely as a Capri Sun, but not sponsored nor affiliated.) The truffle is A MUST! It's a huge portion and it'll fill you up. The cauliflower was a similarly huge portion and plated beautifully on only one side of a blue-tinted ceramic plate. All the plates/bowls are different for each dish. The Eel Taco, Duck Confit, and Soft Shell Crab were tinier in portion which I was really sad about because they were so good! I would've ordered more but these dishes were more than enough to fill a party of 3. Any of their alcoholic drinks are tangy and does the job! Overall, love the tapas, plating, food fusions. I've never been to a restaurant that does all 3 successfully while being fairly priced and filling.I always come early, around opening at 6pm so I can be seated within 30 minutes. I came today around 6:30pm on a Saturday so the wait was an hour. Be sure to come early or prepare to wait about 2-3 hours. This place doesn't take reservation.

Title: A Quaint Escape into Old World Mexico

I finally decided to step inside a restaurant I'd often passed, lured in by an old-world Mexican ambiance that speaks right to my Dia de los Muertos-loving heart. Settling at the bar, the attentive bartender impressed me with her knowledge and service.

The drink of the day? A delightful Red Sangria – two glasses worth the mention – with a promise to myself to sample the white on my next visit.

My appetizer, Roasted Mexican Corn, arrived post-entree, which was a bit disjointed for me. While enjoyable, I found myself wishing for a heavier sprinkle of Queso – a cheese-lover's dream slightly deferred.

The main course featured Shrimp Tacos with a side of rice & beans. The tacos, a quartet of flavor-packed miniatures, were satisfying, but I'll be ready to amp up the heat with some hot sauce and perhaps a pinch of salt and pepper for the sides on my next round.

Dessert was a parade of Churros, but the mystery of the dipping sauce remains unsolved. As a chocolatier, I couldn't quite identify the thin, possibly strawberry-laced chocolate sauce, though unique and tasty in its own right.

Despite the minor hiccups, it was a delightful meal with an assurance of a return. There's more to try, more drinks to toast, and perhaps, the secret of the churro sauce to unveil.

Came here once before on a night out and got their spicy tan tan ramen. Which to me was ok.. then I tried a bit of my friend's cold ramen. That's when I thought to myself I HAVE to come back for this. Many months later, I came back with the same crowd and we all got their cold ramen. It's very different and refreshing for a hot day. Also to share we got their karaage (fried chicken) and when is fried chicken ever a wrong decision??

I was here last night with my friends and coworkers for a goodbye hangout. Bar just opened at 4pm and I got there 8min after. I was the first to arrive, got my drink and grab 2 tables in the back. Vibe is nice. Would definitely cone back- this was my first time here but it's a regular spot for my coworkers.Ordered my usual drink; margarita with espolon tequila. Yum.

Title: A New Favorite on the Culinary Scene

I recently visited my now-new favorite restaurant, branching out from their grain bowls to their highly praised pasta menu. Opting for the shrimp spaghetti, my expectations were met and exceeded. The pasta struck a perfect balance - creamy, packed with flavor, yet not overly heavy, a true testament to the kitchen's finesse.

Accompanying the pasta, the truffle fries were exceptional. Golden and crispy, served with a delectable sauce, they're an essential addition to any order. While the OJ mimosa was rather standard, it didn't detract from the overall excellence of the meal.

Word has it, the Bronte burger is next on the must-try list, and I'm keen to return to explore more of their offerings. At this restaurant, disappointment seems off the menu.

Tried this place for dinner the other night with friends in town. Guacamole Not seasoned at all. This tasted like someone just cut up some avocado and threw it into a mortar. We  can make better guacamole at home. Fundido Queso This was super skimpy and wasn't that impressive. Mixed Grill Fajita Decent sized and served on a skillet. Came with chicken steak and shrimp. On the bland side but with the green sauce and hot sauce was OK. ChurroThese were done well and crunchy. Drinks Sangria was super water down. Margarita was super water down as well. Nothing to write home about. Nothing really stood out about this meal other than the fact that things were bland and undersalted. Staff was friendly and accommodating though.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Xi'an – Not Quite Living Up to the Hype

After reading numerous raves about Xi'an on travel blogs and recommendation sites, my curiosity finally won over, and I grabbed a friend for a quick lunch break venture. Echoing its fame, I went in with high expectations.

First impressions: the restaurant is spacious, with an efficient setup for those seeking a speedy solo meal. Orders are placed at the counter, and you're left to wait for your number amidst a sea of bar-style seating.

The star of the show was the spicy cumin lamb hand-pulled noodle, touted as a signature dish. True to form, the noodles were homemade, flat, wide, and perfectly al dente, while the aromatic symphony of lamb and cumin hit all the right notes with a spice level that tantalized without overwhelming.

However, the dish was swimming in oil. I understand this is traditional, but it may not cater to all palates – certainly, it's an acquired taste that I'm not sure suits frequent cravings.

The food, undoubtedly good, was marred slightly by service that, while quick, lacked the warmth which can elevate a dining experience. Prices, at least, were fair, tipping the scales back toward a positive note.

In sum, while Xi'an delivers on certain fronts, it falls short of its legendary status in my book. I'd return, but perhaps not with the urgency the hype would suggest.

High class omakase meets warm hospitality. While the omakase experience here is not as "refined" as restaurants that feature celebrated chefs, Suite 1001 makes up for it with style and grace. $125 for 17 courses served at an intimate 4-seat counter in a redesigned hotel room with an incredibly friendly host is quite the steal.My favorites of the night included(1) the rice + uni + toro + ikura dish, a.k.a. the richest and tastiest rice I've ever had,(2) the ikura, with the perfect tension, size and saltiness, this dish made for a beautifully composed sushi,(3) the uni (of course), the generous helping of uni was amazing,(4) the scallop, incredibly fresh, soft and slightly sweet,(5) the ebi, with the perfect texture(6) the golden eye snapper with hand torched crispy skin(7) the zuke akame,(8) and the tamago which had a wonderful light brown crust.I had to stop there because I was about to name all the courses. My least favorite were the more typical dishes, such as salmon or toro. Hamachi is usually one of my favorites. It was good here, but not that memorable.What truly stood out was host Joshua's friendliness. You can tell he loves good food and really cares about the whole experience. He now has gotten me into Dassai 50 sake and into this one of a kind omakase experience. He's a rare find and a great person to spend and evening chatting about sushi.

Title: A Mixed Surf n' Turf Experience at Steak n Lobster

I recently visited Steak n Lobster, a restaurant with an undeniable charm, especially during the holidays with its lovely decorations. The venue is large, spacious, and boasts an exquisite bar that truly stands out. Despite the beautiful setting, I was surprised to find the restaurant quite empty on a Monday evening, which doesn't do justice to its warm hospitality and fantastic Happy Hour offerings.

Service was top-notch throughout the evening, with attentive and welcoming staff ensuring a pleasant dining experience. But let's talk about the main event - the food. My group of eight opted for the surf n' turf special at $30 a head.

The meal kicked off with a delightful garden salad, fresh, crisp, and paired with a flavorful citrus dressing. As for the star attractions, the lobster, though small, was a hit. It was cooked perfectly, and the lemony butter it came with was a zesty complement, available both grilled and steamed.

The steaks, however, were where Steak n Lobster sadly fell short. With limited preparation options (Kogi medium or well-done, Cajun only well-done, and NY Strip to personal preference), they missed the mark. My medium-rare NY Strip lacked that coveted grilled sear taste and, according to the group consensus, the other steaks suffered from being overly well-done and underwhelming in flavor.

Despite the steak letdown, the potential of this establishment is clear. The ambiance and service alone are reasons to return, and I'm inclined to give their seafood another try, perhaps steering clear of the steaks next time. A final note - their bar and Happy Hour are hidden gems that shouldn't be overlooked. Steak n Lobster is well worth a visit, but for now, the search for the perfect steak continues.

Title: A Slice Above: A Gem on the Upper West Side

After many years, the Upper West Side has finally been graced with a much-needed pizzeria that ticks all the right boxes. This quick-slice spot stands out with its delightful pizza, excellent service, and inviting ambiance.

The pizza itself is top-notch, boasting robust flavors and impeccable preparation. Whether you crave a single slice or a whole pie, the variety here won't disappoint. And if your slice needs a quick warm-up, rest assured the wait is brief. Don't let the "quick-slice" tag fool you, though; the establishment feels more like a traditional pizza joint, albeit with slightly higher prices.

The clean, spacious interior invites patrons to sit and savor their meal in comfort, with restrooms available for convenience. Adding to the allure is the availability of alcohol, with a selection of beer and wine to complement your pizza—albeit at a premium and served in a soda glass, which may dim the experience for some.

In summary, this pizzeria proves itself as an excellent dining choice, whether you're in for a leisurely meal or just grabbing a bite on the go. Despite the minor quirks with beer presentation, it's a noteworthy addition to the neighborhood's culinary scene.

What a disappointment! Wow. They asked my sister and I if we weren't their 'bottomless brunch' when we said no, they sat us in the front of the restaurant on high top tables.. rather in the back with everyone else. Cool. To start we ordered their bacon guacamole, which was not so bad. Probably the best thing we ordered. What we ordered: Short rib empanadas- OK. The outside of the empanada was soggy but the short rib was flavorful. Carnitas tacos- SADDEST TACOS I HAVE EVER SEEN. I wanted to cry. It was so blain, no color, they didn't add a lime to the side! It was the saddest tacos I have ever seen. For being a Mexican restaurant, you really destroyed these tacos. The carnitas wasn't even flavorful. The taco truck has better ones. Maya Benedict- let's talk about how ALL THREE eggs were NOT RUNNY, what an egg Benedict is suppose to be. My sister couldn't even eat it all because at that point it is so unsatisfying. Their bottomless brunch is worth the price, I get it. But that's if you are looking to just get drunk and not really care about that food. Thankfully, I care about the food.The service was alright, our waiter not once came to our table asking if everything was ok. The guy picking up our table was the only one who came over. It is hard to impress me with Mexican food, and Maya destroys everything about Mexican.

This is of the best fancy, sit down places that you can go to in NYC hands down! While I have been to this restaurant before, my second visit left me equally impressed. Located right next to Bryant Park, Gabriel Kreuther is very easy to find. If you look for the Grace building, a white marble building with a sloping design, it should be easy to spot as Gabriel is on the first floor. After entering the restaurant, I was immediately greeted by a modern, open sitting area for dinner guests. Separate but not too far from this seating area was a well stocked bar. With respect to service, the maitre d had us quickly seated and I was honestly impressed with the skill of all the staff. Our water glasses were filled almost constantly.Finally, and most importantly, the food was fantsatic. On the night I visited, I was offered two different set menus, each of which unlike other restaurants did not list the dishes that would come out. As such, each dish was a surprise. Each dish was extremely impressive and I would venture to say that all of the dishes had artistic qualities. A bravura performance.

Title: A Dreamy Afternoon at RH's Chic Eatery

I finally had the chance to experience the much-raved-about RH restaurant, and it certainly lived up to the hype. Nestled atop a five-floor visual feast of stylish furnishings, the RH store itself is a design lover's paradise. But the pièce de résistance is the elegant restaurant on the fifth floor.

Though we visited on a bustling Saturday afternoon without a reservation, a 35-minute wait was a breeze with delicious Bellinis in hand, lounging amidst luxe decor. The ambiance of the restaurant is sheer opulence, with lush plants, gleaming marble, and golden chandeliers casting a warm glow over the dining experience—it's as if you've stepped into the pages of a RH catalog.

Despite the chilly weather, I glimpsed the terrace which promised al fresco dining perfection come summer. As for the food, it was nothing short of superb. Yes, it's a splurge, but it's also NYC, and quality comes at a price. The roast beef sandwich, burger, salmon, and chicken were each a delectable testament to refined American cuisine.

In short, RH delivers an exceptional dining experience where the beautiful presentation is matched by equally impressive flavors. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Title: Classic Ambiance with a Taste of Elegance

Making a reservation at this esteemed steakhouse, widely recognized as the oldest in NYC, is a must – I managed to snag one for three people at 8:45 PM, just a day ahead. Upon entering, the dimly lit space exudes a timeless charm, bustling with energy that heightens the dining experience.

The service was competent, though the process of selecting wine via an iPad detracts from the traditional, tactile pleasure of perusing a physical menu – a minor, yet noticeable tech intrusion.

I opted for the New York sirloin, a solid choice with an impeccably charred crust and a perfectly cooked medium-rare interior. While the steak was tasty, it didn't quite reach extraordinary heights. My friend's Gotham, on the other hand, with its succulent meat and crispy onion accents, edged ahead in flavor.

The star of the evening, however, was the Wagyu steak. A friend's order turned into a table envy, delivering an unforgettable experience. The Wagyu's buttery texture, complex flavors, and tender bites were unmatched – simply the best I've had.

Overall, despite some minor hitches, the quality of the Wagyu alone earns this classic steakhouse a well-deserved 5-star rating.

Title: A Delightful Surprise with Stellar Service

Stumbled upon this gem around dinner time and was immediately impressed by the warm welcome from a super friendly host. Despite some underwhelming reviews I'd seen, my experience was top-notch, with five-star service that left a lasting impression.

The menu offered a variety of Mexican and other Latin favorites, like Ropa Vieja and Pernil. Our group sampled these along with tacos and empanadas, accompanied by delicious maduros. Each dish was satisfying, particularly the Ropa Vieja, which was bursting with flavor. While the Pernil was tasty, it was slightly on the fattier side for my preference.

The food was good and came at a reasonable price, but it was the exceptional service that truly elevated our dining experience. Every staff member we interacted with was excellent, showing a level of hospitality that you don't encounter every day.

Overall, it was a great experience – one that I would recommend to anyone in search of tasty Latin cuisine paired with unparalleled service.

Title: Quaint Find with Hearty Fare

My dining experience at this unassuming establishment on a lazy Sunday afternoon was pleasantly surprising. While we initially set our sights on the "Torta for a Two" special, which, to our slight disappointment, begins at 3pm, the detour was fortuitous. 

Opting instead for a simple cheese quesadilla, chips with queso, a sandwich whose name escapes me, and an intriguing hot tequila beverage that mimicked a spiked tea, we embarked on a culinary adventure. The meal was unexpectedly satisfying given the cost-effective pricing. The quesadilla was exactly what one would expect—basic, yet strangely comforting. The chips and queso duo provided a delightful crunch and creamy contrast.

Although I didn't personally try the sandwich, it was reportedly scrumptious. The warm tequila was an unusual but enjoyable concoction, akin to a hot lemonade with a boozy kick. 

For those looking for a quick, inexpensive meal that satisfies without any frills, this spot definitely checks the boxes. It’s a testament to the idea that sometimes, simplicity paired with a touch of novelty is all you need for a worthwhile dining experience.

I went here yesterday after the movies and I have to say the spacing is quite small but overall the inside is nice. The staff was very kind and helpful which is always a great thing. This is a family size restaurant so if you are going with 2 or more people you should share the meals and appetizers because it really does feed how many people it says on the menu. Since we were celebrating two birthdays really we gotten a free sundae ice cream which was huge!! the three of us couldn't even finish it!! the food was soo good. we ordered the small chicken parmesan which comes with 3 pieces of the chicken , a small salad and garlic bread which was very delicious as well. A small feeds 2-3 and a large feed i believe up to 6 people. I have to say you get what you pay for. I will definitely be coming back to try out other dishes. Make sure you make reservations as well , as that's what i did. I make reservations anywhere I go that I know you can make reservations at because I do not like waiting for long.

3.5/5 stars but not 4.Had dinner here for five people on Saturday at 6:45pm. Making a reservation was easy and the place had quite a few empty tables when we arrived but became more full as the night went on. FOOD: for dinner we had the oysters (West and east coast), shrimp and trout. Everything was ok. Dinner we had cheeseburgers and the fried chicken. Though the fried chicken came highly recommended from our server, it really wasn't anything special and pretty mediocre. Nice crispy skin but kind of dry and no flavor. Same with the cheeseburger - very mediocre.VERDICT: Overall this place is fine/ok... worth coming only for ease of making a bigger group reservation same night but otherwise there are plenty of better places/food in NYC.

Title: A Delightful Omakase Experience at Sushi by Boū Suite 1001

Last Sunday evening, my party of four enjoyed an impeccable omakase experience at Sushi by Boū Suite 1001, a quaint hotel suite turned sushi enclave that accommodates just as many guests. Promptly seated upon arrival, we embarked on a 17-course sushi journey that was nothing short of spectacular.

The chef was a true artisan, swiftly delivering high-quality sushi that tantalized our palates. Although initially unfamiliar with about 40% of the menu, the presentation and taste were nothing but exquisite. Each bite was a revelation of the classical Japanese sushi craft, highlighted by the perfect blend of taste, texture, and temperature.

Among the many delights, the tamago stood out with its unique cake-like texture, an unexpected twist on the traditional recipe. The 'flight' of tuna—featuring akami, chutoro, and otoro—was a masterful demonstration of the fish's range, showcasing its elegance in various forms.

The intimate setting allowed for personalized interactions, as the chef narrated the omakase offerings while keeping pace with our New York minute rhythm. With the option to pair the sushi with sake, cocktails, or non-alcoholic beverages, the entire dining experience felt tailored and exclusive.

For those seeking a high-end sushi experience without spending an entire evening at the table, Sushi by Boū delivers exceptional value. I wholeheartedly recommend it for an indulgent taste of Japan right in the heart of the city.

Tryna find those staple spots to frequent when I move to NYC, and my friend had told me about it.... def made the list! The hand pulled noodles were perfectly cooked. And the cumin lamb was spiced to absolute lusciousness. Def coming back to try the other items on the menu! Tips: restroom is for customers only as the access code is on your receipt.There's some condiments available like chili oil if you want to add more by the drinks.

Best service ever!!! Loved everything about this place. the food, the ambiance, the people, the music. Yes it's a bit cramped but everyone we met around us were super nice.The lobster pasta was amazing - get this if it's available. Also loved the grilled octopus.Best Panacotta I've had in a long time.But the best part is the waiter as we were leaving pulls me and we start dancing to volare! So much fun!!!Highly recommended!

This review is based on my order placed on Taim App:One of my employees ordered from Taim recently and I was impressed with her falafel sandwich.Thus, on this rainy afternoon I decided to order the same sandwich.I already had downloaded the app and received 25% off my order.There are a lot of options to choose from when ordering the falafel:Green falafel or harissa or regular red falafel.Pita, of course, whole wheat or white or salad platter.You can add additional toppings for additional charge like spicy peppers or kalamata olives.I ordered the falafel with a combo of red and greenand  a side of fries that came with saffron aioli.I mistakenly pressed pick up instead of delivery, no big deal, since Taim is located three blocks from my job. I also was curious to see the establishment: very small, barstool and counter seating but my order was ready before the estimated time.Thus 5 stars are for:Delicious fresh falafel, the pita was stuffed with a ton of falafel, Israeli salad, hummus and tahini worth the $8.95.The fresh cut fries were a tad greasy but really good. The saffron aioli was meh.The 25% discount was a nice introduction to Taim.My order was ready earlier than estimated time.Love the food and this will probably turn into a beautiful friendship!

The Sicilian Pepperoni Slice is absolutely delectable. It features an airy, but crispy dough and crust and delectable cheese with perfectly crisp pepperoni. This is the only slice I tried, but based on taste and convenience of take alone, would highly recommend.

Title: A Serendipitous Midtown Discovery

I recently visited a midtown restaurant on a quiet Sunday early afternoon with a group of eight friends. Despite initial concerns due to the lack of patrons, we were promptly seated, and the establishment clearly had ample space to accommodate our large party. The interior boasted charming wooden high top tables and drink menus, although some of the menus were slightly worn.

To our delight, the venue featured an impressive selection of whiskeys and spirits, and their specialty cocktails did not disappoint. I indulged in the "Nobbly Cobbler," which struck a perfect balance between sweetness and refreshment, though there was a bit of a wait for our drinks, which was surprising given the sparse crowd.

Opting to skip traditional entrees, I tried the trio of sliders, with the venison and cream sauce pairing proving to be an unexpected favorite, surprisingly devoid of any overly gamey taste. While the BBQ pulled pork slider was delightful, the fried chicken thigh slider fell short of my expectations and did not resonate with my palate. The buns, however, were a universal hit—fluffy and buttery heaven.

Our server was the highlight of the experience; despite a hiccup with finding the sliders on the menu, his attentive service and the use of an iPad for ordering signaled to me a commendable blend of personal care and technological savvy.

Overall, I'm eager to return to this hidden gem, conveniently located near Penn Station and MSG, and I would confidently recommend it to anyone in search of a great drink and a hearty meal in a welcoming atmosphere.

Title: Mixed Experience at Hama Sushi

My dining partner and I, eager for sushi before a show, followed the siren call of glowing Yelp reviews to Hama. Upon arrival, with the restaurant at half capacity, we were seated promptly—though initially at the bar, we had to request a table amidst many vacant ones.

Service soon proved to be the Achilles' heel of our experience. We were subjected to a lengthy wait, feeling invisible as the waitress attended to adjacent diners multiple times before acknowledging us for a drink order. The waiting theme continued, even as the restaurant filled to two-thirds its capacity.

Opting for both bento boxes and a shared sushi entree (number 8 on the menu, a standout selection), we anticipated a feast. The quality of the food, when it finally graced our table, was undeniably excellent—a testament to the kitchen's prowess.

Yet, the memory of our meal is tarnished by a parched plea for water, as attempts to flag down service had us fresh out of patience.

In a nutshell: Hama's culinary delights earn a resounding 5 stars, but the lackluster service leaves much to be desired, eking out a single star. Would I return? Perhaps, but only if I'm not pressed for time and armed with a well of patience.

I recently ordered the grilled chicken platter from Mealpal and was thoroughly impressed. The chicken was grilled to perfection, and the flavors were outstanding. Not only was the taste top-notch, but the portion size was generous, providing great value for the meal. The green sauce served alongside added an extra layer of deliciousness that complemented the dish wonderfully. Without a doubt, I'm planning to return to Mealpal soon to explore more of their offerings.

Title: A Delectable Italian Retreat at Eataly

As a New Yorker, it's not often I stumble upon a place that stops me in my tracks, especially after a long day of walking. But my first experience at Eataly did just that. Tucked away at the bar, Kishan's warm welcome quickly dissipated any trace of city fatigue.

The cheese and cold cut platter was an exquisite kickoff, each bite better than the last. And let's talk about the fried calamari - it was the epitome of perfection. Crisp, flavorful, and cooked to a golden delight.

But the showstopper was the grand Pear cocktail. To say it was DELICIOUS is an understatement; it was like sipping on a sumptuously crafted dessert. Kishan's attentive service was the cherry on top, softening the blow of the high bill with his charm and attentiveness.

While Eataly sits on the pricier side, the quality and experience justify the splurge. I'm already planning my next visit - after I save up a bit, of course.

Title: A Hearty Feast in a Bun – No Sides Necessary!

I recently tried the delivery-only option for the 5 Napkin Burger, which turned out to be a colossal and mouthwatering experience. The burger was a culinary delight, arriving perfectly medium rare as requested. The gruyere cheese was divinely gooey, beautifully complementing the sweet caramelized onions, although the avocado could have used a tad more freshness.

The star of the show was the rosemary garlic aioli, which was utterly delectable; my only gripe is that I craved even more of it! The bun did succumb slightly to sogginess during transit, but that was a minor setback in an otherwise excellent meal. Indeed, this burger lives up to its name – be prepared with plenty of napkins for this deliciously messy endeavor.

True to their promise, no sides were needed; the burger alone was satisfyingly filling. Service was prompt, with my order arriving quickly and without error. I'd happily recommend this to any burger enthusiast and will definitely be ordering again.

Finally visited this casual Michelin one star restaurant!More jammed seating like typical East Village restaurant, waiters are mostly friendly but some seems clueless.Food -Quail - amazing, the flavor was perfect and the quail was very very tender.Crab Noodle - everyone raved about this but honestly I feel it's something you can get in other restaurants as well. It's good but not that amazing to us. Pig Out - love the crispy skin and the sauces came with it, pork itself is pretty good but also it's personal preference as one likes pull pork or chunk of pork. More for experiencing their creativity I think. Sausage Sticky Rice - yummm our second favorite other than the quail. Perfectly even in flavor, (sort of like the dim sum lotus leaf wrapped sticky rice.) Cocktails are on the light and boring side for me. Ordered sake after our first drink.. Definitely a spot worth trying though

Title: A Toast to Gluten-Free Options at a Cozy NYC Spot

During the bustling San Gennaro Feast of 2019, my family sought refuge in a quaint eatery, lured by its reputation for accommodating gluten allergies. True to NYC form, the space was snug, yet the efficiency of the staff had us seated in under two minutes—sans reservation.

The wine list was a pleasant surprise, sporting reasonably priced bottles that promised a budget-friendly toast. While their moscato was a delightful highlight, the sangria sadly missed the mark.

As for the fare, "generous" doesn't quite capture the size of the portions we were served—massive might be more apt. Ingredients radiated freshness, and the gluten-free menu was a playground of creativity. Though some dishes could have benefited from an extra pinch of flavor, the overall experience was fulfilling.

A visit to the associated bakery down the street sweetened our day, although a word to the wise: the gluten-free, preservative-free treats are best enjoyed posthaste, as they tend to succumb to the green tinge of spoilage rather quickly.

Despite this minor setback, the wealth of gluten-free options guarantees our return. This spot is a testament to hospitality and inclusivity in the heart of NYC.

Restaurant Review: GupShup - A Slice of Bombay in Gramercy Park

My culinary journey at GupShup, an Indian gem nestled near Gramercy Park, was a delight, offering a tantalizing array of Bombay-inspired dishes alongside classic Indian staples.

From the moment I stepped through its doors, GupShup impressed with a thoughtfully crafted interior that evoked the charm of a boutique hotel, and the exterior was equally captivating.

The menu left me spoilt for choice, beckoning with an array of must-try items. Highlights included the Ghost Chili + Garlic Chutney, which delivered on flavor without the fiery aftermath I'd braced for, and the Lamb Keema, a standout dish that cleverly fused Indian spices with the comfort of a Sloppy Joe, all encased in a crispy bread shell.

The Chicken Tikka was another star, a simple dish executed to perfection, tender and bursting with flavor in every bite. While the Delhi Butter Chicken proved a tad too creamy for my palate, the Naan was a non-negotiable marvel of hot, crispy perfection.

The Braised Lamb Rack with Biryani, despite its spectacle, was overshadowed by its $46 price tag – a good dish, but not quite exceptional enough to warrant the cost.

GupShup has undoubtedly left its mark, prompting a desire to return and explore their brunch and lunch offerings. For those frequenting the area, GupShup could swiftly become a new favored haunt for Indian cuisine aficionados.

One Monday I had a craving for a pizza from this place.  It was my first time in at over 7 years eating here. I don't eat here because they don't sell individual slices so I have to get friends to join me. It's one of the best thin slices of pizza I have had. But in this case I was alone so I ordered a cheese calzone for $13 and it was huge. Just by looking at it, I was like I can't finish this but the cheese and the bread was divine that I ended up eating the whole thing. I definitely want to come back for happy hour which ends at 6pm on weekdays, I believe. If any of my Yelp friends are in the downtown Fidi area hit me up so we can enjoy some awesome pizza.

Title: In Search of Heat: An Abiko Curry Review

Star Rating: ★★☆☆☆

Having developed a serious penchant for Japanese curry in Tokyo, I had high hopes for Abiko in NYC's Koreatown, famed for its fiery Japanese curry options. Sadly, my experience left me underwhelmed.

The restaurant accommodated me quickly on a cold afternoon, offering a variety of Japanese comfort dishes with a choice of five spice levels. Ignoring the waiter's caution, I boldly chose the 'extra spicy' pork curry over rice and a side of natto.

The service was swift, yet the curry itself was a letdown. In stark contrast to the robustness of CoCo Curry in Japan, Abiko's rendition was unexpectedly watery and, surprisingly, lacked the fiery kick expected of its 'extra spicy' label, though it was otherwise suitably flavored. Moreover, at $13, the curry felt slightly overpriced, particularly as my side of natto was forgotten.

While I'm curious about the 'spice guru' level, my quest for that authentic Japanese curry thrill continues. Abiko didn't quite hit the mark for me, leaving my spicy cravings unmet.

Visited for a late-night dinner and decided to try the 'Willy Wonka' cocktail. While the presentation was inviting with a foamy top and marshmallow, the drink itself fell short of expectations. For a safer bet, I'd suggest sticking to their other cocktail offerings. The guacamole and chips didn't disappoint and come recommended. However, steer clear of the Mac and cheese and the eggplant chips, which unfortunately were on the soggier side despite the creative touch of honey. The service, though, was impressive; both the waitress and bar staff were on their A-game, showcasing dedication and efficiency. I'm open to giving their cocktails another chance based on the service alone.

Ordered the spicy lemongrass pho with bone marrow and it was great.  Nice spice but not over powering.  Also had the sweet and spicy wings which were delicious also.  It might be over spicy for some but overall tasted great.  Spring rolls are what you would expect so no surprises there.  The chili oil they give with the pho was very good as well.  Ambiance is casual but as it is a little dim but can be a welcome depending on scenario.  Service was good and food came quickly.  Overall a great experience and would recommend/come back.

Title: A Busy Saturday at Joe’s Shanghai - Worth the Wait?

I found myself caught in the bustling queue of Joe’s Shanghai on a Saturday afternoon, indicative of its appeal to tourists and food enthusiasts alike. Despite the hour-long wait, the company of a friend made time pass reasonably.

Once seated at a communal table, the hunger pangs had us ordering promptly. The menu was reminiscent of your typical Chinese eatery, yet we gravitated towards their signature Pork and Crab Xiao Long Bao (XLB), accompanied by a serving of string beans and a tempting half braised duck.

The XLBs, arriving in sets of eight, were a culinary spectacle with their translucent skins hinting at the rich broth within. Each bite into these delicate parcels revealed a harmonious blend of pork and crab, delighting our taste buds with their succulent complexity.

The string beans, albeit standard fare, were slightly undercooked with modest garlic adornment - satisfactory but unremarkable. In contrast, the braised duck was the star of the show – its savory, fall-off-the-bone tenderness epitomized the craft of braising.

In summary, Joe’s Shanghai offered a solid dining experience with a few standout dishes. The hype may overshadow the overall simplicity of the place, but the flavors on the plate held their ground.

Title: A New York Noodle Staple Continues to Impress

Whenever I find myself landing in NYC, my tradition mandates a pit stop for hand-pulled noodles, a streak I'm compelled to maintain. This visit led me to indulge in pork and oxtail noodles with a mild seasoning. Between the two, the pork noodles triumphed owing to their superior flavor and a generous pork-to-noodle ratio.

The eatery is reminiscent of a narrow bowling alley, cozy and straightforward, with counter service at its heart. Towards the rear, a smattering of counter seats beckons, though many opt for takeout. Whichever you prefer, stay alert; the dishes are known to arrive with surprising speed, ensuring a swift and satisfying noodle fix.

Wow... wow...wow. Where do I even begin. Great website- can make reservations online and no need to worry about calling in and they are closed. Got there and service was AMAZING! My friend recommended the place and so worth it! Go with an empty stomach and an appetite! Your meal will not break the bank either. Anything on the menu is amazing but the French Toast options are AMAZING!! I couldn't even finish my plate, it was too good to leave behind. I am definitely going again! My recommendation... make a reservation!!! Worth the effort because you get seated right away! Great staff and service! The location was also clean and well maintained.

Title: Unbeatable Happy Hour at Flex Mussels – A NYC Gem

My love affair with Flex Mussels spans both their Upper East Side and West Village locations, and it's a relationship that's only grown stronger over countless visits. When it comes to Happy Hour, this place is unmatched—exceptional quality meets extraordinary value.

A visit typically involves my best friend or husband, where a chilled glass of Vinho Verde sets the stage for a feast. The fresh oysters, sourced from Prince Edward Island, are a steal at $1.50 each during Happy Hour. Yes, they've nudged up from a dollar, but they're worth every penny.

But the real star is the Mussels with Fries deal. While the accompanying beer has been dropped, the essence of the offer remains irresistible. An upgrade to Truffle Fries? Yes, please! The San Marzano mussel pot is my personal favorite, boasting a tomato sauce with just the right kick.

And let's not forget the donuts – a little sweet indulgence in the form of cinnamon and sugar, chocolate, and salted caramel, all tied together with a divine vanilla bean sauce.

The staff's attention to detail ensures every visit is as delightful as the last. Flex Mussels isn't just a restaurant I frequent; it's a cherished dining experience in NYC. Highly recommended!
Dolls oysters?! Yes please! All day they gave this special and they have $6 drafts and wine from 11 am to 7 pm. The oysters were big and definitely worth it.

The food is four stars, but the experience here is five stars. We got a coupon in the mail for this spot and had to try it. It was so incredible getting to sit with our dog Gerbert at a delicious steakhouse right on 14th street and 9th on a gorgeous summer night. Where else can you do that? My favorite dish of the night was the Napoleon dessert - what an all-star! Layers of crispy, creamy, light, refreshing. So great. The corn side dish is also a must, tastes so different from the usual corn I've had. Almost grilled tasting and sweet. We ordered the executive steak which is a plate of massive, thick slices of sirloin with these divine crispy edges that you can dip in melted butter that pools at the edge of the plate. Also had the lobster meatballs which were tasty, though fried, would try another appetizer next time, perhaps the lobster mac and cheese. I also want to try another steak next time that's even fattier. The servers and the manager are also so sweet. They really care about you having a great time here and enjoying your night. Five stars!!!!!!!

Title: A Delightful Impromptu Crawfish Adventure

My fiancé and I stumbled upon this gem on a whim, eager to indulge in some savory seafood. The first thing that caught us off guard was the restaurant's cash-only policy, so a heads-up to future diners: come prepared with bills!

Despite not being overly hungry, we couldn't resist the intoxicating aroma of garlic and butter wafting through the air. We settled on a shared lobster roll and 2 pounds of succulent crawfish seasoned with their signature Boil Special Cajun Blend. The lobster roll, at $20, was a bit of a splurge for its size, but the flavors were divine—with cold, fresh lobster housed in warm, buttery bread.

The crawfish truly stole the show. They were a mouthwatering delight, perfectly complemented by the spicy, garlic-butter richness of the Cajun Blend. The staff was attentive and helpful, offering tips on the art of eating crawfish, complete with bibs, gloves, and a handy bucket for discards. We did have a minor hiccup with the bill initially being incorrect, but the issue was swiftly corrected.

Having reserved our table in advance, we avoided any wait time, which was a plus. Although prices were on the higher side, the quality and taste of the food made it worth every penny. Overall, the experience left us satisfied and eager to return.

Just when you had a clean day and saw a surge on seated. Booked this joint right away and went a little ham. I ordered the hot mess with sweet potato fries and the mel's double burger with salad. The sweet potato fries cannot be half portioned. The fries were unfortunately soggy and I wasn't feeling the BBQ sauce with the fries but the taste itself was spot on. No frozen starchy taste present. The side salad was a huge surprise since they salad options suck. The side salad had onions, tomatoes and leaves that I was craving for. The portion size was also very satisfying. As for the burgers, we ordered medium well and there was not a hint of dryness or red noted. They were both well flavored. The hot mess was a thick meat patty vs the double burger was two thin patty which I think are both a total of 8oz. The bread was warm and soft - perfect for individuals that care more about the inside of a burger than the bread since it wasn't thick. As for the interior, it was great for hanging out. They have a ton of happy hour deals but OMG is the service slow. It took 1 hour for our order to be served. ONE HOUR is a long time for hungry folks like us.

I had a wonderful experience at this spot for a late-night snack! The homemade dumplings offered an interesting contrast with a crunchy exterior, although they were slightly mushy inside. The tiger rolls were a highlight, and I absolutely enjoyed the kimchi which was bursting with flavor. Don't miss out on the veg pancake—it was a delightful treat. Service was top-notch, attentive and friendly. Plus, I was pleasantly surprised that I didn't need a reservation to get seated immediately. Highly recommend a visit if you're in the mood for some tasty bites!

Title: A Gastronomic Delight with Excellent Service

My recent dining experience at this charming restaurant was nothing short of delightful. The service was top-notch, making the meal all the more enjoyable. Each dish presented to us was a work of art—both visually stunning and packed with flavor, truly a testament to the skill in the kitchen.

While I did find the sticky rice a tad too dry for my taste, it's understandable that occasionally a single element may not be perfect. Despite that, the chance to savor other cultural delicacies more than made up for it. This restaurant is an excellent spot for those looking to broaden their culinary horizons and enjoy a meal that's as pleasing to the eye as it is to the palate.

Walking to my car after working 12 hours as a fluid station volunteer at the Marathon, I needed a good meal and a chance to rest my feet (stood / walked all day). The Grazie welcoming location drew me in. So glad it did. It looks like a popular, reliable local favorite. I waited at the door as an elderly, elegantly dressed woman with her aide entered first. I asked if this was a good spot. The look I got - "are you kidding" - told me to grab a seat. The room, narrow but deep, was crowded. I sat at the window - an extension of the bar keep's responsibility - and was greeted and offered a menu after a few minutes wait. I had a wonderful shrimp appetizer that came with a basket of toasted dipping bread wedges. Yum! Then, I had the chicken with capers, artichoke hearts and tomatoes in a rich olive oil sauce. Simple but rich with flavor. It had a generous portion of lump-free mashed potatoes that needed a pinch of salt. Dessert was their chocolate cake with a side of vary good vanilla ice cream and drizzled with chocolate sauce topped the meal. It's a reason alone to come back! Good vibe. Welcoming staff. Professionally prepared Italian fare. A new favorite!

I've never been to Naples but now I really want to go! The pizza is a good size but maybe ordering one per person might be a better idea than sharing one between two people. I was genuinely surprised at how good this pizza was. It is really thin but so flavorful. The truffle oil really brings together the prosciutto, mushroom and mozzarella. Glad I stumbled into this place, highly recommend and will be coming back. Would love to try to fried pizza next time!

Excellent food. I ordered the chicharron mofongo. And oh boy, I really enjoyed the food Local:Is set up as a bar and it only has two tables that fit 2 people per. I believe in the bar it fits about 12 people. The food:Mofongo is a traditional Caribbean food from the puerile Rico or Dominican Republic. The mofongo came with a patato/meat stew which flavor was beyond this world. Definitely will come back when I am back in New York.

I've been here 3 times now and I'm never sick of it. It's delicious and it's such a cool concept. Aesthetics and vibes? Super uhhhmazing. Presentation is beautiful and the food is just superb. Everyone is friendly and they are very knowledgeable of the food.Highly recommend you to come here and if you have a big group - no worries, the more the merrier. No one will be disappointed :)

Title: A Slight Miss at My Favorite NYC Burger Joint

As a long-time patron and burger enthusiast, I eagerly returned to my beloved NYC spot for my birthday, enticed by the allure of their classic, no-frills burgers. The old school charm is usually part of the appeal, but on this visit with a group of five, the execution didn't quite live up to my fond memories.

I ordered my usual cheeseburger, medium rare with extra cheese, anticipating that familiar, perfectly melted embrace of cheese. Unfortunately, my burger leaned more toward medium-well and the cheese hadn't reached its usual gooey glory. My companions didn't fare much better, receiving well-done burgers instead of the medium-well they requested.

Despite this experience falling short of the high standards set by previous visits, the fundamental flavors were still present, reassuring me that the kitchen hasn't lost its touch entirely. It's possible the post-renovation rush on a Sunday afternoon contributed to these missteps.

I'm confident this was a one-off disappointment, so I still recommend burger aficionados to try this spot for themselves. I'm hopeful that my next visit will restore my faith in this establishment, and I plan to update on that experience.

Rating: Still hopeful, but room for improvement.

I recently dined at a charming restaurant that truly captured the essence of Mediterranean cuisine with a delightful Greek atmosphere. The food was absolutely delicious, with every dish speaking volumes of freshness, which is a testament to their high-quality ingredients. The presence of olive oil on each table added an authentic touch, allowing me to tailor the flavor to my preference. Moreover, the service was commendable; the staff was warm, friendly, and incredibly attentive, ensuring a welcoming dining experience. For anyone who appreciates the comforting taste of the Mediterranean, this place is a must-visit!
