Came here for a expo tasting and fell in love with all the food and the space. Was lucky enough to have a work happy hour here, and my favorite dish ever is that butternut squash ravioli. I HAVE DREAMS ABOUT THIS DISH. Don't sleep on it! Other great mentions were the fries, the pizzas, and gnocchi. I wasn't too crazy about the pork buns (they look like baos - too soggy) and the flourless chocolate cake was just okay, not a fan of the candy fruit on top). The bread pudding with ice cream is yummy though . Overall love this spot!

The ricotta gnocchi!! For sure my favorite gnocchi I've ever had. We had a great dinner experience here this weekend. The weather was beautiful so they opened the windows. We made reservations for Friday dinner and would suggest them especially on the weekends. Our service was great. The atmosphere was nice. Awesome place overall!

Title: A Delightful Duo of Visits to Bareburger

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Bareburger, a gem that caters to a range of tastes including a thoughtful vegan menu. On my visit, I opted for a large salad teeming with crisp greens and fresh veggies, elevated with the juiciest bison patty I've ever savored - a truly harmonious blend of healthful and hearty.

The shared sides of onion rings and waffle fries were indulgent perfection - crisp, flavorful, and downright irresistible. The experience was so enjoyable that my sister and I were compelled to return for a second feast within the same week. Bareburger is a must-visit for anyone craving a satisfying meal with a side of comfort. Yum, indeed!
Carbolicious! I had the noodle with chicken. It was flavourful and filling! I have a big appetite and I couldn't finish it.

Take it or leave it lucky cat ramen was a Grubhub late night fix but all I did was taste the broth before falling asleep.   My broth had a kick and was absolutely delicious; my girls was bland and the ramen dish fell short too.There isn't enough in the ramen to justify the purchase.   Mine was a minced pork ramen which tasted good but I wanted an egg, some scallion, anything and everything more but it was all so basic.Not basic in a bad way but certainly not in a way that would bring me back.The only thing that will definitely bring me back in fact, is the pork gyoza!  Man it may have been the best I've had (they seemed burnt but didn't taste it and they were large and juicy) granted I just had a treat earlier which started the ramen craving to begin with...

Title: A Crispy Delight and Noodle Perfection

My recent visit to this gem with friends left us raving about the appetizers and main courses alike. We started with the Karaage and Tori Kawa - both were exceptional, with the fried chicken being notably crispy yet juicy, and the chicken skin so light and crispy it nearly melted in the mouth.

For the main course, I indulged in the Tonkotsu Chashu Tsukemen, which was served with a generous portion of both broth and noodles. The chashu was tender to the point of perfection, and the broth was flavorful and rich. Adding a personal touch, I spiced up the dish with a heap of Japanese chili powder, and it certainly did not disappoint - the heat level was just right and elevated the already delicious meal.

In summary, the visit was a culinary delight. With its deliciously light and crispy offerings and a standout noodle dish, I'm already planning my next visit. Highly recommended for anyone seeking great food and a satisfying dining experience.

Title: A Milkshake Haven for Late Night Cravings

If your sweet tooth is calling, heed its call and head straight to this dessert paradise. The variety of milkshakes is impressive and, trust me, the hype is justified. A late-night visit an hour before closing gifted us with a nearly empty eatery and lightning-fast service—a rare treat.

Our picks, the brownie and chocolate chip cookie milkshakes, were indulgent to a fault. Bring your appetite or an army of friends because the portions are generous, to say the least. While we didn't venture into their savory fare, rumors of their burgers' excellence have piqued my interest for a future visit. For a delectable experience that's best shared, this spot is a must-visit.

Ordered from here twice in one week! Love this spot and the friendly people who work here. I've only ordered for pickup, not eat-in. I loved their beef satay, fried fish fillet banh mi sandwiches, papaya salad and noodles. Ordering for pickup is 15% off all day every day! What a deal. Their hot sauce is actually very hot (I usually have a pretty high tolerance) so use sparingly if you've never tried it before. I appreciated the cashier going over the menu to avoid items I might possibly be allergic to. Also thought it was sweet how the hostess always knew who the patron's partner was as people went to meet their already-seated significant other. She did it three times in a row - it's obvious this is a favorite for locals and they remember their loyal patrons.

I think the 3-star average review rating is just about right for this joint. I mean, I like the cheap prices, but the food just isn't that good. Also, the staff seems kinda mean and shady. I guess these old Chinese folk just get tired of slaving over the same stove day in and day out while the owner doesn't really hook them up. Who knows. Either way, I think the food might be worth trying once, but it's really not that unique or amazing to go out of your way for.I had the Sesame Pancake Sandwich (P1) with peking duck and it was decent. The flavor was sort of bland and tasted a bit burnt. I had some pan fried dumplings as well which I couldn't really tell the difference from the frozen ones at Costco. I clearly didn't have the best meal experience.I'd pass up on Vanessa's--there are so many other great spots for dumplings.

Came a bit after 12 on a Sunday and was lucky to be seated right away. The menu is pretty traditional for a dinner. Service was a bit slow and the waitress constantly kept checking in, not in a bad way but maybe a pressuring way to rush us out. Overall though the food was decent and portion size for price was well worth the value compared to some other places in Manhattan. Got the bacon egg and Swiss on a croissant substituted with ham and appreciated the flexibility

Came here for a pre-show dinner; when I first arrived the restaraunt was not very busy but after an hour later it was packed and by time I left it was vacant again. Service was prompt and courteous as they asked me what time the show would be. I thought I would be underwhelmed by the menu options, but I was more than happy with everything I ordered. Started with the escargot in garlic butter and then for dinner I had the shrimp and grits with spicy sausage. A little more sausage than shrimp, but that was fine by me. For dessert I had a cherry pecan pie a la mode. It was perfect and not too sweet. Staff was concerned with getting everyone to their show on time which was considerate. I had a great experience here and would definitely recommend.

Expensive for no reason. I wasn't too hungry, so I just ordered one roll - the Snow Special Roll (spicy tuna topped with white fish, honey wasabi mayo and wasabi tobiko - $15). This was probably the best-sounding roll, because the rest of the special rolls are pretty uninventive - just a bunch of spicy fish with random sauces; so I guess same with my roll but honey wasabi sounded very intriguing for some reason. I still can't decide if I liked the honey wasabi or not. It was interesting with the sushi, but I'm pretty sure it was just honey mustard. The roll was bad, but I just don't think the quality was worth the price tag. It tastes like your typical take out sushi. BF had the Volcano Roll (spicy tuna topped with tobiko, tempura flakes and chef's sauce. - $12), salmon avocado, and spicy salmon roll and pretty much agreed. I tried the volcano, and it was just drenched in eel sauce and tempura flakes - couldn't even taste any fish.Tip - if you check in on Yelp, you can get 15%. I would have been pretty mad if we had to pay full price for the quality of sushi we had. Also, you can reserve via Open Table, but you won't earn any OT points for it.

Went on a brunch date with some friends and I must say that this is one of the nicest brunch restaurants I have ever been to. The restaurant is not too small, but it is pretty comfortable. The aesthetics are so cute and there would definitely be cute picture opportunities here; the only thing is that the lighting is a little dark. We were seated immediately since there were not that many people on a Wednesday afternoon. The server was extremely nice and helpful as well. Food overall was pretty delicious. I ordered the maple sausage sandwich and it tasted like a fancier version of the McDonald's breakfast sandwich. I loved every part of the sandwich! They give jalapenos and sriracha on the side, so if you like your food spicy, you have the option to add those in. Like I said, this is one of the nicer brunch spots and I would definitely return again.

Title: Style Over Substance at the Pink-Hued Eatery

I was initially drawn to this restaurant by its striking pink façade, a siren calling for the Instagram crowd. Yet, beyond the photogenic exterior, the dining experience proved to be somewhat underwhelming. I indulged in the risotto, which was satisfactory in taste but came with a price tag that outweighed the portion size, leaving me less than satiated. The menu selection was scant, offering few choices to entice a return visit. Overall, my visit was a pedestrian affair, with the ambiance outshining the cuisine. The restaurant rides on its aesthetic appeal, but for those seeking a meal that matches the external charm, you may want to just capture the moment with a photo from the sidewalk. The experience inside doesn't quite live up to the picturesque promise of its exterior.

TLDR: Solid Italian eatery by that stretch of Cleveland Place and Lafayette. This is more on the authentic side, smaller portions, not too much red sauce. Pricier but good stuff. Service could be better.I've been here a couple of times. I've always thought the food was solid but found the service to be lacking. The tables are packed a bit tight and it gets busy here frequently. It was annoying that all the tables around us had gotten their bread before we did, they sat after us too. I felt I was constantly trying to get my server's attention to just even place an order or whatever.On to the food. This is closer to the kind of food you'll find in Italy. I do like the boards you can order with different kinds of meats or spreads. On our most recent visit, we did the duck liver mousse, smoked trout and felino (type of salami) to start. They serve these with these grilled pressed medallions of bread. Awesome.The duck liver is excellent. If you've been to Tuscany and you're craving for that liver crostino - this is pretty dam close. The smoked trout was good too. However, my favorite on this board is the lardo they give you. It spread on the bread like butter but.. it's pork fat and herbs. So good.All the pastas here are $25, except on Mondays after 9. Mondays after 9PM, it's Industry Night where some pastas are $12. What a steal! They do have an extensive pasta list with some rare shapes. So if you're a pasta connoisseur.. when's the last time you saw gramigna on a menu in New York. Not too often.So we've done the Cappelletti which is similar to a ravioli. It's tossed in this truffley butter sauce with strips of prosciutto. The first time we had this, it was really good - the second time something was lacking. The pasta a bit too al dente and the sauce was kind of bland. Most recently I got the Mafalde which shrimp, scallops and crab. Imagine thin ribbons of lasagna, tossed in seafood. It wasn't bad but nothing really stood out to me on this.I haven't tried their entrees yet, so I'll have to report back. So far, I think the meat/spread boards are their strongest offering. So while I wasn't blown away by Morini, I'm still down to give it another try.

The food was great here. Came in for lunch after reading the posts about the lunch specials. Forgot to read the fine print that the offer was only good Monday-Friday. So I ended up paying full price :( . The food in itself was good. The gratuity was thrown on my bill automatically which I wasn't overly thrilled about - especially when it it was just myself. All that said, if I had to do it over again, I may have chosen to get an item that was a bit less expensive.

Title: A Mac 'n' Cheese Heaven in the Heart of New York

If you and your best friend are on the quest for the ultimate mac 'n' cheese experience in New York, look no further! This gem of a spot serves up mac 'n' cheese that hits all the right notes, with a perfectly crispy cheese crust that gives way to an ooey-gooey, piping hot interior. The variety of flavor combos on offer ensures there's something to satisfy every palate.

My visit during the Halloween season added to the charm, with the delightful sight of children trick-or-treating within the restaurant. Despite the bustling crowd, the service remained impressively swift, and the presentation of the dish in a sizzling hot cast iron skillet added a touch of elegance to the meal.

In short, for mac 'n' cheese aficionados seeking a fast, friendly, and delicious experience, this spot is a must-visit. It's the kind of place that turns a simple comfort food into a special occasion, every time.

Tucked away near the Vessel, Spanish Diner at Mercado Little Spain is a charming spot well worth the search. The highlight of my visit was the surprisingly delightful combination of avocado, olive oil with salt, eggs, and mushrooms - simplicity perfected. However, the experience was marred by the somewhat comical but ineffective heaters reminiscent of a 1960's hair salon that failed to ward off the chilly drafts seeping through the windows.

Service, or the lack thereof, was a notable misstep. After being seated, a 15-minute wait and a signaling maneuver were required before an apologetic staff member attended to us. Requesting the basics of salt and pepper resulted in a mysterious offering of spicy ketchup, which makes one wonder about the kitchen's stance on seasoning.

The potential for a pleasant dining experience exists, but improvements in ambiance and service are imperative. Perhaps a bigger party would prompt better service and a warmer welcome. Despite the drawbacks, the diner has a certain allure that might just coax me back for another try.

Small poke spot gem in Chinatown. The salmon ikura chikarashi is the best thing here. Good proportion of salmon and the rice is good as well. The bowl isn't that big so its for one person only. I also like to get the ponzu salmon when I wanna switch up from the salmon ikura. It's also one of the only few places that I know that serves dole whip!! A place where I can get my Disney world pineapple ice cream craving. Small spot where it has stool seatings and fits about 10 people.

I recently visited Toloache for a work meeting and had a mixed experience. Upon arrival, which coincided with the restaurant's opening time, the staff seemed a tad disorganized – they offered water options that turned out to be unavailable and it took some time for our waiter to inform us of this minor hiccup.

The food was satisfactory, though I found the prices to be on the higher side. For example, tacos ranged from $14 to $20 for a pair, accompanied by a modest serving of rice and beans. I opted for the Torta Ahogada, a pork carnitas sandwich with vegetables and avocado, which was nicely presented but came with slightly burnt bread. Despite this, it was still enjoyable.

We also tried the Trio de Guacamole. While it offered better value than the single serving, I found both to be overpriced given the quality which was good but unremarkable. My colleagues had various tacos and observed that the accompanying rice packed some heat.

In conclusion, Toloache offers decent food with room for improvement in value for money and organization during the early hours of service.

Title: A Delightful Indulgence at [Restaurant Name]

My recent visit to [Restaurant Name] was nothing short of amazing, albeit with a menu that leans towards the indulgent side. The experience started on a delicious note with a shared plate of crispy hash browns smothered in a savory duck heart gravy — a must-try dish that had us savoring every bite. We also tried the fries topped with gravy and a perfectly cooked egg, another testament to the kitchen's flair for comfort food.

While both were exceptional, the hash browns stood out the most. My only quibble is a desire for a more generous portion of the hash browns, considering how delectable they were on their own. 

Moving on to the main course, I opted for the cheeseburger, to which I added bacon and an egg — a decision that elevated an already substantial meal to new heights. The burger was so sizable and stuffed with rich flavors that it could be easily split between two.

To wash it all down, the house root beer was a refreshing choice, further enhancing the meal without overwhelming the palate.

Overall, [Restaurant Name] is a gem worth exploring for those with a hearty appetite and a penchant for classic comfort fare with a gourmet twist.

Title: Healthy Cravings Satisfied

I recently visited this neighborhood gem on a Saturday evening and was delighted by the experience. Despite arriving during dinner hours at 6:30 pm, my brother and I were promptly seated as the place was comfortably bustling but not overcrowded.

Our cravings for something healthy were superbly met by the chopped salad and sirloin hummus we ordered. Not only was the salad bursting with fresh vegetables and perfectly balanced acidity, but it also managed to be delicious while maintaining its healthful qualities.

The standout dish, however, was the sirloin hummus. The generous chunks of well-seasoned sirloin mingled with the creamy, aromatic hummus created an indulgent yet satisfying dish. Paired with a plentiful supply of whole wheat pita, this dish provided an enjoyable textural contrast and depth of flavor that kept us dipping in for more.

As an added bonus, checking in on Yelp earned us a free mezze hummus, further enhancing our experience with its freshness and taste.

With the entire meal coming in at around $30 before tax and tip, the value was undeniable. This dining experience certainly left a positive impression and I'm already planning my next visit for another dose of great food at a great price.

Don't get me wrong, I still love this place dearly. I had an incredible experience at the Kang Ho Dong in LA and was excited to take my boyfriend to this location in Manhattan. Food-wise: The meat and banchan were high quality and so yummy (get the lunchbox with rice, egg, kimchi, and deliciousness--you won't regret it!). One of the best parts of this place is that they cook all the meat for you so it's cooked evenly and the perfect amount. However, there were a bunch of problems with our grill lighting in the beginning, and while the meat cooked fine, the sides (cheese/corn and eggs) barely finished cooking by the very end of our meal, and the veggies were just slightly warmed. I was so disappointed because that was one of my favorite parts about my experience in LA.This restaurant has Yelp waitlist which helped our wait tremendously. Their estimate was definitely on the high end for us, though; they originally told us the table would be ready in 28-45 minutes and then texted us 15 minutes in saying our table was ready and we had 10 minutes to check in.The service was excellent and the staff was somewhat apologetic about the grill experience, but I'll definitely try out other KBBQ locations around the area before coming back again.

Really enjoyed my experience here! Not only was the food delicious but the service and atmosphere are also great! We shared the kale pest arancini and it was very good! The people I was with got the burrata pizza which they said was amazing! I would get that the next time I come because if looked really good!I got one of their specials that night which was a grilled cheese sandwich and tomato soup! The grilled cheese was perfect, could not imagine it being better! Will be coming back here for sure!

Like hockey? Manhattan? No? Well the correct answer is Yes! Yes! Yes! That subtle hockey joke will get picked up by any Islanders fan, and it should! I mean if you're in the city, what better place to watch the Isles then at Offside Tavern?Seriously, there isn't a superior spot, especially within the confines of the city that never sleeps. I mean, it's probably more of a Rangers town anyway which makes Offside that much more enjoyable. You really get to see some die hard fans come out to cheer on their blue and orange team, which is great to be a part of, and ever since I saw the commercial for this cozy spot during an Islanders game I knew I needed to check it out. Finally, several weekends ago, I made it happen, with next to perfect results.For starters, I gotta say the pictures on Yelp don't do OT justice. It's slightly more spacious than what it looks like with plenty of tables in the back and a nicely-sized viewing room (complete with projection screen) to fill out the area. It all plays well for hockey action as most of their handful of TVs will be turned to the game (Isles, if you haven't figured that out by now) with sound piping through the place. Oh and you better hope the Islanders score big that night because they'll also blast the goal song which just puts a cherry on top for the ambiance and feel.Beyond aesthetics, I can't say Offside is a beer-lover's paradise. Most of their choices are pedestrian, but they did have a few Coney Island taps as well as (you know where this is going, hopefully) an Oyster Bay Brewing Company handle. Let's just say I downed a few Barn Rockers before the end of the Islanders 2-0 victory. My buddy and I also chowed down on some solid barbecue wings, creamy Mac and cheese bites, and Tater Trotz. What's that you ask? Well hopefully it's something Barry himself would enjoy as it's a layer of tater tots smothered in cheese, bacon, and pulled pork. Hungry yet?Okay, so what if you're not an Islanders fan. What makes this place so good? Well, beyond the welcoming atmosphere, the owner and employees are all friendly and were ready to take my orders right away. Our food was delivered right to the random set of bar stools we sat at which was pretty impressive as well. Might I add that Offside hosts some video game nights? That evening, before the Isles, half the TVs in the back were donning video game systems with that aforementioned projection screen showing some larger than life gaming action. Oh, and the handful of Alabama fans seemed more than comfortable amidst the Islanders blue and orange as they watched The Tide get beaten by Auburn. Hey, as long as you're enjoying your time at Offside, who cares who wins? (Actually I do. Let's go Islanders!).Overall, Offside Tavern is an Islanders fan's paradise. It's unfortunate I don't live closer (like my sister who is literally a 6 minute walk from the place, #jealousy) because I'd be here for every game. It's just that much fun. The space is perfect, the food Is rockin', the staff is welcoming, and the beer is totally fine (just down those Barn Rockers!). Okay, maybe I wouldn't always be there. Every once and awhile ya gotta experience the Isles live, but if I had a second choice, it would be Offside Tavern, for every game. You can say Yes! to that more than just three times.
I like the ambiance here. I'm ok sipping on their house wines and having a quick bite.

Visited BKK about an hour prior to closing with a little fear of being able to order ( or potential attitude). 100% opposite: stellar service, courtesy and all smiles. The food speaks for itself and I have visited Thailand multiple times . Curry Duck, Pad Thai , chicken satay and some cheese spring roll of sorts . Everything was exceptional including the hot sauce. Probably the best Thai I have had in NY - willBe back !!

Title: Fresh Obsession at KazuNori

My culinary affections have been wholly captured by my latest discovery, KazuNori. Initially unassuming, this eatery might have you questioning the allure of hand rolls - until you try them here. To say they're amazing would be an understatement.

The ambiance within is effortlessly cool, centered around a bar-like seating arrangement that enhances the dining experience. It's intimate and engaging, allowing you to witness the creation of each hand roll up close and personal. I went for the 5 hand-roll selection featuring succulent crab, rich yellowtail, decadent lobster, and two other types of fish that have slipped my mind but left a lasting impression on my taste buds.

The ritual here is unique: you're only served your next roll once you've relished the one before you, ensuring each bite is as fresh as possible. Yes, the pricing leans towards the premium side for hand rolls, but when the quality of the fish is this superb, it's an indulgence that feels justified.

KazuNori is a must-try for anyone who cherishes the finer points of sushi. I'm already planning my next visit and I can't recommend it enough!

Came here for a double date on Valentine's day, they sat just pretty much when our restoration was and our seats were pretty spacious. The place itself is pretty big, they have a top and bottom floor and all the tables are pretty far from each other so you dont feel like you are eating on top of another party. They have a pretty wide selection of things to choose from and although it is on the pricier side I think that its worth it once in a while. We got a bunch of different items ranging from meats to regular foods.-Modeum So Gui : this was their beef combo and in my  opinion this was just okay, nothing special.-Samwon Galbi: AMAZING, the beef was soo flavorful and it just melted in your mouth-Egg Souffle: Another hit! It was super fluffy and yummy-Kimichi Fried Rice: This was also super tasty and I highly recommend this, it is on the spicy side so if you cant handle spicy, maybe pass on this.They also have a very affordable deal for a pitch of beef and a bottle of soju for $20 with check in which is pretty cheap for this area! The service is also really good! Our server was really friendly and nice. At one point, a portion of the grill fan fell onto our meat and they immediately apologized and replaced our meat right away. Overall, this is a pretty solid KBBQ place!

This place is fine. It's pretty expensive. The burger will not be the best burger you've ever had. Not top 5 or 10, but maybe 20, at least because it's unique with the thick cut bacon. But I came with two friends and it was nice to catch up with them :) the ambiance is: dimly lit, leather couch-benches, upscale bar-y, with low frequency bass musak thumping on repeat the entire time. I think a coffee was like 8 bucks (didn't get one). I would come back if someone else was paying for it.

From the moment we walked in, the restaurant's impressive space set it apart, exuding the ambience of an upscale dining establishment rather than a mere café. As newcomers to the vegetarian/vegan lifestyle, we were pleasantly surprised by the delightful flavors and inventive dishes that left us completely satisfied without any longing for meat. Each bite was a testament to the thoughtful and skilled preparation behind the menu items we chose. We're eagerly looking forward to our next visit to explore more of what this remarkable restaurant has to offer.

Title: Cozy Home-Cooking Meets Trendy Dining at [Restaurant Name]

My Thursday night experience at [Restaurant Name] struck the perfect balance between home-cooked comfort and a modern dining atmosphere. We were pleasantly surprised to be seated within a brief 20-minute wait, despite not having a reservation.

The complimentary banchan set the tone for the meal, delighting us with steamed eggs, sweet anchovies, exceptional kimchi, and a verdant side dish. For our main course, my husband and I opted for shared plates, indulging in a Crispy Pancake with Shrimp & Chili Peppers, Bulgogi, and a soul-warming Steamed Homemade Kimchi and Pork ribs in an Anchovy Broth.

While every dish was a delight, the Steamed Kimchi and Pork Ribs stole the show with their spicy broth, tender ribs, and silky tofu. The Crispy Pancake was a textural triumph paired with a zesty dipping sauce. The Bulgogi, although recommended, was on the sweeter side, which may not suit everyone's palate.

A word of advice: book a table ahead of time, bring friends to share the culinary journey, and on chilly evenings, don't overlook the comforting "Share a Pot" dishes — as they're generous and perfect for a group.

In summary, [Restaurant Name] is a gem for those seeking generous portions of lovingly prepared food in a chic yet relaxed environment. The leftovers were a bonus, guaranteeing the enjoyment of their delicious fare beyond one seating.

Title: Second Round of Satisfying Indulgence at My Go-To Hotpot Spot

I made my second pilgrimage to this haven for food lovers where the All-You-Can-Eat (AYCE) hotpot and BBQ reign supreme when hunger strikes hard. It's an affordable affair with a generous menu that keeps me coming back. The spread of proteins is remarkable – from endless slices of lamb, beef, chicken, to adventurous picks like pig intestines, beef tripe, and stomachs. There's no skimping on portions here.

Seafood lovers aren't left behind, with crab, shrimp, fish, and squid on the list, though the fancier catches like lobster come at an additional cost. True, there are a few items not included in the AYCE deal, but what's on offer is more than sufficient for a hearty, casual meal without burning a hole in your wallet.

The service doesn't miss a beat – swift and efficient, bringing dishes out within minutes. The venue itself impresses with its sheer size and cleanliness, not to mention a ventilation system so effective that you walk out smelling as fresh as when you entered, even after a 90-minute feast.

The sauce bar adds a personal touch to your meal, complete with two complimentary dessert options. However, a suggestion for the owner – consider swapping out desserts for fresh fruits. It seems the sweet endnotes weren't as appealing to the diners, and a citrusy or melon-infused palate cleanser might just be the perfect finale.

Overall, this place is a gem for those who love to eat to their heart's content without compromising on quality or their budget.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience at [Restaurant Name]

I've become a regular patron of [Restaurant Name], drawn in by the consistently enjoyable atmosphere, prompt service, and wallet-friendly prices. The presence of numerous Japanese diners suggests a stamp of authenticity, which is always reassuring.

While the yakitori hasn't quite hit the mark for me, I find myself gravitating towards the dishes listed on the white page at the start of the menu, adorned with Japanese characters – every selection there has been exceptional.

Standouts worth a special mention include the fried squid appetizer, which is a crunchy and succulent revelation, and the cod roe pasta, offering a unique blend of flavors that has me coming back for more. The omusoba is another must-try; it's a delightful fusion of omelette and soba, executed to perfection.

For anyone seeking a genuine taste of Japan without the frills, [Restaurant Name] is, without doubt, a top recommendation.

Title: A Tale of Two Meals at a Friendly Local Eatery

I recently visited this restaurant twice, experiencing both their dinner and brunch offerings, with a preference for the latter. The establishment boasts a spacious interior, with a quirky bar adorned with green and copper dog heads leading to ample booth and table seating, all set in a welcoming atmosphere.

During my initial visit for dinner, I opted for the grilled salmon sandwich accompanied by sweet potato mash. The menu's flexible side options were appealing, although a touch disappointing when my desired upgrade to Parmesan truffle fries was declined despite my willingness to pay extra. The sandwich, priced at $8.50, was decent—though the focaccia bread choice proved problematic, resulting in a crumbly texture that overshadowed the tender but underseasoned salmon. However, I did manage to enjoy the Parmesan truffle fries a la carte, which were a standout with their perfect crispiness and robust truffle flavor.

Brunch, however, elevated my dining experience. I indulged in a pancake tasting trio, featuring chocolate cherry, granola, and apple varieties. The chocolate cherry pancake was a clear winner, with its gooey chocolate and tangy cherry pieces creating a delightful balance. The granola pancake also impressed with its unique flavor, while the apple pancake, unfortunately, missed the mark entirely. Though the pancakes were denser than my ideal, the accompanying hash browns and pork sausage were exemplary in their crunchiness and savory juiciness, respectively.

Service throughout was competent, marked by knowledgeable waitresses, attentive water refills, and prompt meal service. Despite some hiccups in the dinner menu, the enjoyable brunch has left me open to another visit in the future.

100% vegan French restaurant with incredible vegan savory and sweet crepes and a plethora of authentic French dishes!Food****I enjoyed nearly all the food on the table minus my plate ( Vegan Steak Tartare). I used to eat steak tartare when I was younger and really enjoyed the taste but since this was not similar to what I used to eat when I was non-vegan it had a peculiar taste. I definitely recommend trying the Vegan Tournedos Rossini (incredible and so delicious), Plateau de Fromage Vegetale, La Lolotte, and Ratatouille--these dishes definitely made up for mine and I would certainly go back and order any of these! Portion sizes are definitely adequate as well!Service***Service was quick but I felt personality was lacking in both waiters that served us and one waiter spilled all my fries on the table and just said "oh well". The other waiter was very nice and accommodating to our table. I'm not giving this less stars because that waiter could have just had a bad day! Atmosphere****Small but cute and comfortable, which is typically difficult for restaurants to pull off but Delice and Sarassin does with effective lighting and seat spacing!Price$$$Over $15 per Dish and sometimes in the 20s and even 30s for certain Dishes but worth it!

Title: Chic Fusion and Imbibe at Windmill LES

Nestled within the Lower East Side, Windmill emerges as a fashionable destination, the brainchild of celebrated bartender Sother Teague and the team from Le French Diner. It crafts an inviting atmosphere for those seeking French and Japanese culinary harmonies.

My experience was delightful, beginning with the savory chawanmushi and skillfully prepared skewers of heart and breast – each bite a testament to the kitchen's prowess. Complementing the food, a brandy-based cocktail impressed with its balance and price, a reasonable $13, notably modest for the locale.

Though the dishes lean toward the pricier side, making the venue more suitable for a light bite than a full meal, the total cost is justified by the quality. The service didn't miss a beat, attentive without being overbearing.

As for the ambiance, Windmill strikes the perfect note. On an early Friday night, it was buzzing yet comfortably uncrowded, presenting the ideal backdrop for a casual outing. A minor inconvenience, they were cash or Venmo only during my visit, but it hardly detracted from the overall charm.

In sum, Windmill is a chic spot ideal for those looking to indulge in small plates with big flavor, all wrapped in a cozy, lively setting.

Title: A Taste of LA Glam in the Heart of NYC

I recently celebrated a birthday at a restaurant that felt like a slice of Los Angeles had been transported to New York City. With its young and on-trend crowd, this place could easily have been at home on the Sunset Strip rather than the streets of the Big Apple.

Our group, which was sizable at 11, faced a strict adherence to the reservation policy: no seating until the full party arrived. Although this rule was clear from the start, the hostesses' manner of enforcing it left much to be desired. Their tone was unnecessarily brusque, which put a damper on the start of our evening.

The restaurant's interior, a mix of modern and rustic with its brick walls, spread comfortably over multiple floors, including a rooftop lounge that promised al fresco allure in warmer weather.

Opting to share our meal family-style, we dove into a diverse menu and found the fare to be unexpectedly excellent, contrary to some lukewarm reviews we'd come across. Standouts included the Oven-Roasted Whole Branzino, Crispy Whole Snapper, and a show-stopping dessert named "The Carnival"—a confectionery delight of warm ricotta donuts that were downright addictive.

The hit of the night, though, had to be the "Hit Me" Chocolate Cake, a decadent affair that, despite its steep price, could very well be worth the splurge for those willing to indulge.

Cocktails, pricey at $18 each, did not disappoint, with the Pineapple Trainwreck and Lush Lemonade being particularly memorable. The bartending was a high point in an otherwise inconsistent service experience that ranged from professional (kudos to the rooftop bartender) to less than stellar.

In the end, the vibrant scene and impressive cuisine nearly balanced out the initial service hiccups. While one might overlook the frosty reception for the culinary delights, it was enough to nudge my overall rating to a 3.5 out of 5 stars. A worthwhile visit for the food and atmosphere, if you can navigate the potential service snags with grace.

I recently ordered from Krua Thai and was thoroughly impressed with the quality and speed of service. The spicy eggplant dish was a fiery delight, and the cashew chicken was a flavorful journey that I greatly enjoyed. While the pad see ew fell short of expectations, it was the only minor letdown in an otherwise fantastic meal. Both the egg rolls and veggie dumplings were crispy and satisfying additions to the feast. The ingredients tasted fresh, indicative of high-quality food. Overall, Krua Thai has secured a repeat customer in me, though I'll be passing on the pad see ew next time.

Title: A Must-Visit for Vegan Comfort Food!

If there's one thing you do at this gem of a restaurant, let it be sampling the vegan onion rings. Thick, crispy, and utterly addictive—these are hands down the best I've had, vegan or otherwise. Don't pass up on the breakfast burger either; it's a deliciously messy affair that hits all the right spots. The unchickn avocado sandwich is another crowd-pleaser that shouldn't be overlooked.

On a day when the trains tested our patience, the kindness of the staff at this place was a welcome surprise. They graciously allowed us to stay inside during an unexpected delayed opening due to the transportation hiccup, which was a warm gesture on a cold day. Exceptional service is matched by the delectable food here.

Oh, and did I mention the vegan desserts? Don't leave without trying them; they're the cherry on top of an already splendid dining experience.

Absolutely outstanding! The onion rings were cooked perfectly and the Sweet Heat sandwich was delicious. The sandwich has a bbq sweet sauce that has a bit of heat to it. The sandwich also has a variety of sweet peppers & jalapeños which makes for a delicious sandwich. I am so excited this place exists. The sandwich & onion rings were ard 9 bucks and the sandwich alone is ard 6 bucks. I'll tell you this, this sandwich is in the lead for one of the best fried chicken sandwiches out there. I actually prefer this sandwich over the popeyes fried chicken sandwich. Sweet heat is cooked to perfection & is a great size too. I definitely recommend this place & you have gained a repeat customer for sure.

We recently visited this charming restaurant after receiving a gift certificate and were absolutely won over by the experience. It's advisable to book a table in advance to sidestep any delay in indulging in the culinary delights. The setting was both warm and inviting, contributing to an overall cozy atmosphere. I savored the carbonara, which was perfectly creamy and satisfyingly hearty, a true comfort dish done right. Tasting a bit from others' plates, I can vouch that every entrée was top-notch, leaving no room for disappointment. This place has certainly earned a spot on my list for a return visit the next time I find myself in the city.

Came here for some tacos our first night exploring NY. The line was out the door, but surprisingly it went by pretty fast. I ordered two cactus tacos and my husband got carne asada. He absolutely loved them and mine were great as well, I just wish they had cheese in them haha!

Title: Time-Honored Middle Eastern Delights in the West Village

Despite showing signs of wear from its longstanding presence, this West Village gem continues to deliver reliable and fresh Middle Eastern cuisine. Its enduring charm and unfaltering quality make it a beloved spot for those seeking traditional flavors and a cozy dining experience.

Yummy and unique spot for dessert! Definitely a great place to gather with a few friends and indulge in unique and photo-worthy desserts!We had the Matcha Waterfall and the Big Orange. The Matcha Waterfall was a delicious powdered matcha cake filled with a matcha creme. The Big Orange was alright, it was basically a monkey pull apart bread with a scoop of icecream and drizzle. It was a bit on the pricey side. Two small desserts was about $21. Nonetheless, it was a fun experience and tasty!

If you're on the hunt for a fast casual spot to satisfy your pho cravings, look no further! This place has it all: delicious pho, generous servings, speedy service, and wallet-friendly prices. While you might find more authentic options with tastier broth elsewhere in the city, this joint is a solid choice, particularly if you're nearby. I would definitely recommend giving it a try!

Title: Exceptional Value at Impeccably Clean Hot Pot Restaurant

As someone who typically doesn't gravitate towards hot pot cuisine, I was pleasantly surprised by my experience at this well-maintained establishment. The cleanliness of the restaurant was impressive, a detail that never goes unnoticed. Opting for the lunch special, I found the variety of both vegetables and meats to be generous and diverse. To sweeten the deal, the inclusion of unlimited drinks provides an added bonus that truly makes this offering a steal. For the amount of food and the quality of service, the value here can't be beaten. Whether you're a hot pot aficionado or a newbie to the scene, this spot is definitely worth a visit.

Our go to French bistro! Since becoming vegetarians, we have gotten salmon on many occasions and it never disappoints! Our favorite dish is with salmon over large butter beans. Sunday brunch yesterday with the jazz band was exceptional.  Thank you for always bringing your food A game!

My friends wanted to go here for their birthday. Wouldn't recommend. The people acting are very cool and all, and it's fun watching them. For people who bring their friends here without telling them everything, there are performers that get touchy with the customers. It can be uncomfortable for sure. But the worst part of this experience is the menu, $30/$40 prix fixe or a two drink minimum... oof. The food is small portions and not that good either. I think if Tim Burton is really your thing, you should go. If you don't like paying absurd amounts for not much food, stay at home.

Title: A Slice Above the Rest!

During our visit to town, we couldn't resist trying the local pizza joint that everyone's been raving about. Let me tell you, it did not disappoint. The pie we ordered was piping hot, with a sublime crust that struck the perfect balance between thin and crispy. Each bite was a harmonious symphony of flawlessly proportioned sauce, gooey cheese, and savory pepperoni - creating a taste that was nothing short of divine.

The slices were generously sized, ensuring you're getting a bang for your buck. Even my boyfriend, who isn't typically a pizza enthusiast, proclaimed it to be the best he's ever savored. That's high praise coming from him!

If time permits, I'd jump at the chance to slide into this pizza haven for one more indulgent slice before our departure. It's an absolute must-visit for any pizza aficionado or anyone looking to experience pizza perfection.

This is a solid choice for a filling breakfast/brunch. It's a pretty big space and plenty of room. The brunch for $18.95 including drink isn't a bad deal considering it could be your only meal till dinner. Not too loud; a pretty relaxed atmosphere for a lazy Saturday morning. My eggs Benedict was OK, but could have had a toastier English muffin and more hollandaise. And the hashbrowns could have been crispier. Tasted pretty good though and plenty of food. My husband didn't like his eggs rancheros at all; it seemed to be full of veggies and no meat. That's a personal preference though. Service was friendly but not especially attentive. I'd probably return if in the area.

We came by on a random Saturday evening, craving Thai food. There is a lot of competition in the neighborhood, but Pa Pa Thai definitely gives its run of the money. Upon entering, there weren't a lot of people in the restaurant but the take out game was strong. We ordered their recommended mango curry, massaman curry, pad see ew, and a bunch of other dishes I can't exactly recalled, and found it all to be very delicious!  Dishes were not too sweet and packed with a much needed punch. I definitely think  Pa Pa is a strong contender for solid Thai food in the neighborhood and would recommend. Our hostess was also incredibly honest in guiding us on what to order and informing us what was seasonal/fresh. We also ordered the fried banana (not quite like the banana pancake in Thailand) which was more akin to a lightly fried and flattened banana egg roll, and the coconut pudding which was actually a delightfully warm dessert (much welcomed on a cold rainy night). Unfortunately they didn't have the mango sticky rice as mango was out of the season (the host/manager even explained to us that their shipment was sour - quite admirable as many restaurants could've still capitalized on poor produce).Overall: would definitely recommend this place as a solid choice for Thai food, and would return! Kop Kuhn ka!

I recently visited a truly enjoyable spot with superb service that certainly deserves applause. As a vegetarian, it's not often that I come across a faux meat dish that not only mimics the real deal but also tastes delightful. Their fried vegetarian chicken had me doing a double-take—it's that convincing! Paired with their scrumptious waffles, the meal was a hit. Definitely a must-visit for anyone who appreciates a good plant-based twist on classic favorites. Kudos to this fun place! - @traveleen_gurl

Title: Mixed Bag at Eclectic Eatery During Restaurant Week

I recently visited an interestingly decorated restaurant for lunch during restaurant week, greeted warmly by the maitrê d' who ensured a smooth check-in process. The establishment intrigued with its unconventional decor featuring trucks and figurines adorning the walls, adding a quirky charm that I personally enjoyed.

However, the dining experience hit some snags, particularly when it came to wine knowledge. Our waiter, while pleasant, provided incorrect information about the wine selections, which was a disappointing oversight.

For starters, my friend's Caesar salad was deemed just "okay" and unremarkable, while my goat cheese ravioli was nothing short of divine, bathed in a delicate Parmesan cream that truly enhanced the flavors. The main courses were a study in contrasts; my friend's salmon over heirloom rice was simply "good," with no further commentary, whereas my pork loin left much to be desired. The meat was under-seasoned, and even the maple jus failed to inject much-needed taste, resulting in a dish that was surprisingly bland following such a promising beginning.

Despite the culinary inconsistencies, the service was attentive and friendly, with special thanks to our server, Reneda, for her diligence.

In summary, while the ambiance and decor were highlights (A for effort), the food was hit-or-miss and has definite room for improvement, ultimately earning a C for taste. Here's hoping future visits showcase a more consistent and flavorful menu.

Service: B+
Decor: A
Ambiance: B+
Food: C

I've come here a few times for drinks before/after Zest, the sushi spot across the street.  It's super nice inside but I get a bit of a pretentious vibe.  Drinks are kinda pricey for what you get, $15 cocktails, $10+ beers and what not.  It just seems to be a weird spot for that kinda bar, considering you can go to Zest across the street and get $24 bottles of wine, enjoy $4 sushi, a $13 pitcher of beer, etc.  Or get some bomb margs next door that definitely give you a buzz.  In any case, it served its purpose as a one drink hangout for us to kill some time, but it's not somewhere I would go out of my way to go to or become a regular at.

Title: A Hidden Gem in Midtown West - Nippori Ramen

Nippori Ramen may not top the "best of" lists in NYC, but it's a spot that ramen aficionados should take note of. My visit on an early Friday evening revealed a quiet start that quickly transformed into a bustling scene, thanks to its prime location near the theater district.

The menu offered the familiar ramen selections with some appealing extras. Our appetizer game started strong with shishito peppers—simple yet addictive—and the steamed pork buns, which were a standout thanks to their generous filling and delectable sauce.

The Samurai Ramen at $16 was our choice for the main course. Served in a huge bowl, it didn't disappoint. Topped with a variety of ingredients, including charrshuu pork, black fungus, and a perfectly cooked soy braised boiled egg, the flavors were rich and well-balanced. The star, however, was the Tonkotsu broth, irresistibly tasty and worth savoring to the last drop.

We walked in looking for a quick meal and left as total converts, convinced that Nippori's delightful offerings merit a spot on New York City's culinary map.

I been to this location several times. I tried the heritage sausage, veggie, and the pepperoni. It always comes with the sauce. I really like the concept. The sauce is good but the square slices are too hard. The pizza also never comes out hot. I like this place and it's by my home. Hopefully they improve.

Title: A Taste of Modern Mexico at La Loteria – A NYC Restaurant Week Gem

During my inaugural NYC Restaurant Week excursion, I ventured into the heart of the West Village to experience the much-talked-about La Loteria. Named after a popular Mexican game, this eatery carves out a niche in the New York food landscape with its modern twist on Mexican cuisine. La Loteria is the brainchild of Chef Julieta Ballesteros and Jamie Herrera, who have masterfully infused traditional dishes with French elegance—reflective of Ballesteros’ training at the French Culinary Institute.

The restaurant itself boasts a modern and vibrant décor, celebrating Mexican culture in a chic setting that includes delightful outdoor seating perfect for the city's warmer months. But, let’s cut to the chase—the food.

Commencing with the Restaurant Week Menu, the Ceviche de Pescado was a zesty introduction, while the Tostaditas de Atun, featuring chile-rubbed tuna with a harmonious blend of sweetness and heat, was as visually stunning as it was delicious. The entrées followed suit, with both the Tacos de Carnitas and Tacos de Pescado leaving a flavorful imprint, especially the latter's Valentine Aioli that truly sung.

An impromptu side dish, Yuca Frita, proved to be an excellent decision, adding a nice counterbalance to the other flavors on the table. Dessert was the grand finale with Flan and Churros—each dessert standing out in its own right, but the Flan, in particular, was remarkable with its just-right sweetness and impeccable texture.

In summary, La Loteria is a must-visit spot in the West Village, especially for those wanting to indulge in a modern take on Mexican cuisine. The ambiance, food, and hospitality are all reasons I am eager to return.

My friend and I were in the area and was a bit hungry and decided to try our luck with Nami Nori. We were pretty lucky since they had a table for 2 right at 530 PM which was when we walked in. We were seated right away and browsed the menu and decided to go with the Chef's menu and ordered the fried pickles as an app. The chef described each "taco" roll to us and was very flavorful. I've been to a couple of hand roll places and preferred this concept a lot better. The chef was also very funny and charismatic. Overall, the ambiance, the food and the decor was amazing. The service was just as spectacular and the price point was unbeatable. I can't wait for this establishment to open up again so I can come back!

Just popped into this restaurant to soothe a pre-St. Patrick's Day hangover, and the "Bueno Bowl" paired with organic peach tea did not disappoint. A minor hiccup at checkout—I missed the chance to grab a brownie—but the helpful cashier offered a bean-for-broccoli switch, which suited my greener diet aspirations. The repurposed bottle vases showcased eco-friendly ingenuity. The meal was satisfying for the price, and the peach tea was a delightful surprise, despite not being my usual pick. The place radiated positivity, thanks to its bright decor and outstanding service. I left content, planning a return visit for another feel-good meal.

Little spot dedicated to the French dip and more with serious chef cred. Comfort classics like Grilled cheese,fried chicken on brioche, French onion soup and the star the French Dip plus a really good tomato soup and a Caesar salad Green salad. Seating is minimal, but it's cute spot with great value on St Marks.Great addition to already great spots nearby like Foxface and Superiority Burger. Will come back and try more.

I was so excited to get into this place for a very long time! it totally worth the wait and the money! our experience did not start great though, we made a reservation a few days ahead, we called them a few times one hour before our reservation to change the time and every time we called them they picked up the phone, the moment I tell them I need to modify my reservation they hung up the phone ! I was a bit disappointed about that however I managed to get there with my friends on time for our reservations. it was 5 pm and they were so busy but 10 minutes after we got there and were seated the line started getting longer and longer.  it was very beautiful inside, we ordered combo 1 and crab/lobster which were beyond my expectation. OMG, the Lobster and the garlic sauce were delicious. Combo one comes with salad, fries, burger and lobster for only $37 , it is a very decent portion for one person and I would not recommend sharing that if you are hungry. All of my friends loved that place! Can't wait to go back! Also they had gender neutral restrooms, keep it up Burger and Lobster !

I came here with excited expectations after hearing about how it is a franchise in a bunch of Asian countries and Australia. Coming here on a weekday, the place was empty! There was a cashier by the door who explained that we would order and pay up front first, before being seated. Interesting concept, but I don't know if the indecisive me could approve as I would probably be standing there for hours. Fortunately, the decision process was easy, as I just ordered their Classic Beef Rice ($11.50) and my partner got the Salmon Pepper Rice ($12). Both the dishes came in sizzling metal plates that would eventually cook the raw meat. But I must admit, upon my first glance, I was lowkey worried and disappointed by the portion size. There was barely any meat, with the salmon only having around 6 teeny pieces. The TV and posters plastered on the walls demonstrate how to fully enjoy your meal. Definitely mix in the soy sauces they have (garlic and sweet) as it really adds a punch to the rice! I actually did not expect to be full by the small looking meal but I was! Delicious, but it was nothing special. I'm excited to come back and try their Kimchi Cheese rice and hope it would taste better!

Title: A 24/7 Haven for Noodle Lovers in Chinatown

I recently dined at a new noodle shop in Chinatown, and it’s a noteworthy addition to the neighborhood's dining scene. The establishment gleams with cleanliness and offers comfortable seating, including a spacious back area for additional diners.

Visiting on a weeknight, the lack of a wait was a delight, and the seating was prompt. The menu, while straightforward, focuses on customizable noodle soup bases and a variety of meats. Additionally, their appetizer selection impresses, especially the cucumbers in garlic sauce – a must-try that stands out for its flavor.

The rice noodle soup with shredded pork and the pickled cabbage sauce with beef both offered a rich, warming taste that's perfect for chilly evenings. Presentation scores a full five stars, with boiling soup and noodles served on the side, allowing for a fun, interactive dining experience where you mix in the fresh ingredients at your table.

A highlight worth mentioning is the complimentary extra noodles, ensuring a satisfying meal. This place is a keeper in Chinatown's competitive food scene, and it has saved me future trips to Brooklyn or Flushing for my rice noodle soup fix. I’m already looking forward to my next visit.

This was great. First visit, we started with the maguro avocado, and then both did the seki special. The app was very good, and the pieces that come with the special were excellent and pretty unique. Can't say I'd do it very differently next time, although I'd probably try to sit at the bar, since everything inevitably comes out fresher that way. That said, there are also other places I'd love to try that are priced similarly, and I didn't think this was was anywhere near as good a value us somewhere like Sushi Yasuda, which is less creative, but in my opinion higher quality.

I had an excellent lunch here. Minimalist, warm decor, lots of muted earth tones with music to match. The lunch menu included both lunch and brunch items, so if you want eggs benny on a weekday afternoon, this is your place. Service was attentive and sweet.I ordered the seafood cobb salad: Maine lobster, crab, shrimp, avocado, bacon, hard-boiled egg, tomatoes, red onions, blue cheese dressing (I subbed Caesar). I love big salads and for whatever reason they're not so common in NY (Elaine Benes I feel your pain), and this one is admittedly very luxurious. For $25 they really give you a very generous portion of everything - there's tons of bacon, seafood, and half an avocado. The seafood was fresh and delicious. The Caesar dressing is pretty mild, but my server also mentioned an oregano vinaigrette that goes nicely with this that I'd like to try. I also ordered a side of rosemary fries, not realizing how big the salad was. The fries are also a large serving and were delicious. Thin, some crispy some soft, but they could have used a little salt.Cocktails were delicious. The pumpkin spice martini is made with Pisco instead of vodka, so you can tell yourself this is not a basic bitch order and enjoy it guilt free (me and the lovely bartender both agreed this to be the case). Their Engine 24 made with chipotle syrup is also great. I'll definitely be back!

Delicious place and very good Cuban food. Service is quick and food is comforting. This is one of my boyfriend's favorite restaurant/ hole in the wall in NYC and I'm always happy to go with him. This place gets really busy during lunch time.

Title: Second Chance Disappointment at Local Ramen Spot

I recently revisited this restaurant, hoping for redemption after an underwhelming first experience. Seating was prompt likely due to current social distancing measures, but the visit quickly unraveled from there.

Excited by a special dish featured on their Yelp story, the spicy sesame tan tan with pork, I encountered my first letdown when I was mistakenly served a beef variation, to my dismay. The dish was reminiscent of a hamburger thrown into ramen, failing to align with my expectations. The broth, advertised as spicy, was disappointingly dominated by yuzu flavor without the promised heat. Even an additional side of chili oil couldn't salvage the zest I craved.

While the noodles were commendable in their consistency, they were overshadowed by the overall dissatisfaction with the main components of the dish. Also, I was disheartened by the portion size leaving me unfilled.

Trying to find a silver lining, my boyfriend did enjoy his tontoro pork bowl, but personally, my quest for a gratifying meal at this establishment remains unfulfilled.

Came here for their amazing Artichoke pizza but ended up receiving a burnt slice of dough with spots of cheese. No signs of artichoke ... anywhere.Disappointed! Don't expect ANY gooey melted cheese stringing from the pizza when you take a bite.You can order a sampler with 3 pieces of different pizza slices for $20 or you can get 3 pieces of the same pizza for $20. If you order the sampler, just know that you're potentially getting the leftover slices that have been sitting there for a bit.Artichoke pizza -- horrible. The bottom crust was burnt, the middle layer of dough did not rise, no artichoke whatsoever, half the cheese was missing on the top layer and was just dough.Crab pizza -- not as bad with the imitation crab meat mixed with cheese. Worth the try. The taste kind of reminds me of Mac and cheese. Meatball and parm -- nothing special tbh. The sauce was pretty dry, as if it has been sitting there for a while under the heat lamp. The huge slice was cut in half for us and we both got a small piece of meatball.

Tucked into the heart of Seattle's bustling food scene lies a Thai gem that refuses to play by the conventional culinary rules. With a daring twist on traditional flavors, this establishment elevates Thai cuisine to an avant-garde level. The freshness of the ingredients is palpable in each bite, leaving a memorable imprint on the palate. This isn't your run-of-the-mill Thai spot; it's a delectable dance of funky innovation and taste. A return visit is already on the cards for my next trip to Seattle. Highly recommended for anyone craving a Thai experience that's anything but ordinary.

Looking for a great boozy brunch? This is one of the best spots I've been to in a long while $32 all you can drink mimosas, bloody mary's, screwdrivers, and regular beers with an entree. WOW! And they really stay on top of filling you up and making sure you're boozed up. The food is honestly pretty good! Split and order of buffalo wings, which were tasty and fresh, my partner and I both got the breakfast burrito, which was really delicious, and splurged on the dessert sampler, which was decadent. The breakfast burrito was the star of the meal! It was loaded up with eggs, meat, and cheese and the beans and pico on the side were great to mix in. Definitely a knife and fork burrito. The dessert sampler was so yummy. Deep fried oreos and cookies with ice cream to boot. That deep fried chocolate chip cookie was outrageous. Would recommend and would certainly come back here.

This place USED to be better.. I was very disappointed.. ordered cheese kimbab, lack of vegetables (they could have put more vegetables in it. please do not say order vegetable kimbab. you know what I meant). this ajumma (seemed like an owner. there was older ajumma there though) kept talking while preparing for kimbab.. please do not put saliva in my kimbab lol.not sure if i would be back. food galley kimbab is way better

Speedy service, solid food and super cute decor! This was a fun and vibrant spot to enjoy some tasty eats. I think they did a really great job with the island vibes decor. It's very Havana nights / hipster with lots of fresh greenery, patterned wallpaper and illuminated signage. The menu is Cuban and Asian fusion and is large with lots of entrees and small and shareable plates. We shared three small plates which was satisfying without leaving us overly stuffed. The Cuban sandwich spring rolls were filled with deliciousness and came with a tangy mustard sauce. Shrimp empanadas were a little plain but the habanero dipping sauce was nice and flavorful. The highlight of the meal was the duck bao which came with three plump baos and a side salad. The meat was shredded and tender goodness. They have a bottomless brunch special offering if you order an entree. It's something like $25-$30 for 90 minutes of drinks, which seemed like a solid deal considering one drink is around $15. We only ordered small plates and were in and out in something like 40 minutes. But if you are looking to enjoy a leisurely brunch and a few drinks it's a solid deal. I'm glad I stopped in and would do so again if I was looking for a bite in the area!

Was here this past Saturday for another friends birthday. We had a celebration at an residence rented out by an Air BnB that didn't turn out so well so this was the best alternative considering I knew the promoter and it was FREE entry all night! We got there a little after 12 but there were at least 8 of us and we met a few more ppl there. Drinks were good and music was even better than expected ( there were 3 Djs there spinning that night!!! ) After a few drinks we got settled in and had fun. Kinda reminded me of another place called C lounge that I also attend last weekend. Small, limited seating space but good bar area. Good mix of people but everyone seemed to be into themselves and the people they were with and t a lot of room to mingle.  However this place is a " go to " if your in the Avenue A area and you want some  hookah and a nice drink. Best to come with a friend..

Upon entering the restaurant, the unconventional layout is immediately apparent, with seating on one side and the kitchen on the other. The ambiance is very casual, characterized by simple wooden benches and tables. Greeted by friendly and accommodating servers, my family and I perused a concise menu featuring classic Chinese dishes, including the intriguing option of a dry hot pot.

Our experience was not without hiccups; they were out of spare ribs and, surprisingly, hot tea. Nevertheless, we enjoyed the alternative choices: shredded pork in garlic sauce and spring rolls, which did not disappoint. My husband praised the egg drop soup with corn, although I did not partake.

For the main course, the shrimp with garlic sauce, beef with broccoli, and sweet and sour chicken were all standout dishes. The food struck a balance between mouthwatering spiciness and freshness, offering a modern twist on traditional Chinese takeout.

Despite being in the heart of Times Square, the restaurant transported us to a semblance of China Town with its authentic flavors. My family's consensus warrants a resounding four thumbs up—I foresee a return visit in our future.

I really love Beyond Sushi! This is the second location I've been to and as opposed to their full sit down on 37th this once is just a small quick service place good for takeout or dine in (but limited seating). This location is nice because it's easy to come solo vs doing a while sit down deal. I got the Spicy Mang but I really wanted the bean topping from the La Fiesta so they were nice enough to make me a roll with with Spicy Mang for the filling but the bean topping from La Fiesta. It was great!Also has the watermelon mint lemonade. Loved it.

Title: Hearty Eats and Treats at Blockheads

Blockheads certainly packs a punch with its delightful array of flavorful foods, refreshing drinks, and reasonable prices. The recent addition of a vegan section is commendable; the seitan and tofu burritos, in particular, are delectable treats that cater to a variety of palates. When it comes to beverages, the margaritas are notably enticing, adding a splash of fun to the dining experience with an extensive range of drink options to choose from.

Service-wise, the staff here lean towards the pragmatic side, focusing strictly on efficiency rather than a warm, welcoming interaction. While this approach is not inherently negative, a friendlier touch would have enhanced the overall dining atmosphere.

Ambiance-wise, the indoor music volume can be overwhelming, making it challenging to engage in comfortable conversation. For those who appreciate a more serene dining experience, I'd recommend considering their outdoor venue on 50th Street when the weather is pleasant.

In summary, Blockheads stands out for its food and drinks; just be mindful of the service style and noise level indoors.

Decided to come here as it was one of the few places open late on a Sunday night and I am so glad with that decision. The ambience was nice with the music playing loudly, the candles lit, and the heat nice and warm on a cold night. The food was absolutely delicious. I devoured my Pollo en Mole which had great flavor and amazing tenderness and really just exceeded my expectations overall. The enchiladas were also delicious and I definitely plan to come back and try more things.

I usually love hooters wings and do crave them from time to time.  The crispy crunch and delicious buffalo sauce.  I have to pass on this hooters I feel bad Bc the Waitress was nice and it is a nice location and it's two floors with a nice bar set up with a lot of tvs.   But if you can't make the wings the right way then it's just some bad bar with cute girls.  And on top of that being that the Hooters are in a prime location the prices were a little higher.  So I was expecting you these to be the better of the hooter wings.  Boy was I disappointed.  I ordered 10 wings and a Buffalo trace neat. The first batch of wings came out really fast and they looked like a greasy soggy mess.  Like the wings have been sitting in a tray and waiting to be ordered already cooked.  It wasn't a busy day when I went. And I don't mind waiting for food if it's cooked right.  But when they brought the wings to me they weren't even hot and the breading was soggy.  I don't like to send things back but I couldn't eat them. So I told the waitress and she returned them.  She waited for the next batch to be ready and they came out just as fast. They were a tad bit hotter and a little more crispier then the first batch. I didn't want them either but I'm not sending food bacon twice.  I seen the movie "waiting". Lol   I ate the 10 wings watch a little of the game and left.  Hope they get the wing thing right.  Even though I probably won't be going back to that hooters again any way.  My bill was $36 for 10 wings a buffalo trace and some celery and they also charge for ranch sauce. Lol.  Little pricey for some crappy wings. And a couple oz of bourbon.  I gave it two stars for the waitress she was really nice.  If not for her. Just one star.

Well, i'll start with the wonderful atmosphere in here.  I love the set up and got a sense of comfort as soon as you walk in.  The bartender was really attentive and so welcoming. This was our first real stop in the city, as soon as they opened we were there and ready to get one of their dessert cannoli's for my friends birthday (dessert for a birthday breakfast--i think so!!!) I was immediately taken back by the menu, there were so many options and everything sounded amazing so of course I had to order more than a cannoli, I couldn't let a menu like that pass me by, even if it was only one thing.  We got the bone marrow bruschetta because it sounded amazing.  It came out and was even more beautiful than expected, HOWEVER it's taste was extremely disappointing.  It was like a fatty grease ball on burnt bread. The only thing that shined through was the burnt edges of the bread and the overbearing amount of grease on  the top and throughout it.  The cannoli came out after and it made up for the bruschetta to an extend.  It was absolutely huge with two sides (hot chocolate and espresso) I didn't really like the hot chocolate side but the espresso cream was delightful.  We made it about half way through before we couldn't stuff anymore down.  My personal favorite part of the whole meal was my coffee with a shot of baileys, it was delicious, i'll probably think about it for awhile LOL. While the cannoli was cool, I don't know if I will actually come back to try more on the menu, because it's not cheap and i rather not be disappointed by the dishes.

Title: A Delightful NYC Restaurant Week Experience

I had the pleasure of dining here during the 2019 Winter NYC Restaurant Week and was thoroughly impressed by the value and charm this place offered. Unlike many other participants offering just two courses for 26 dollars, this gem stood out with a three-course lunch deal that caught my attention.

The ambiance was immediately inviting, with tasteful decor that piqued my curiosity. I'm already looking forward to returning in the warmer months to enjoy their outdoor seating area. This restaurant also regularly provides a tempting $19.99 lunch special, which I'm keen to try out next time.

The culinary experience was delightful. My friend and I shared the appetizing tempura shrimp to start, followed by well-portioned, flavorful mains: the classic beef and broccoli, and a succulent miso-glazed salmon paired with a side of hearty vegetable fried rice. Despite feeling full, we couldn't resist the creme brulee complemented by pecan cookies—every bite was heavenly.

Service was noteworthy, with all hands on deck ensuring a smooth experience, even with just one waiter. The teamwork of the staff contributed greatly to our enjoyment. I eagerly await my next visit for another round of great food in a lovely setting. Highly recommended!

I have been going to Ippudo for years and was so excited to find their takeout restaurant Kuro-Obi at a couple Urbanspace locations.  With so many ramen options in Manhattan, I tend to be particular about where I go.  Ippudo is one of the top ramen restaurants on my list and I have been very happy with the food at the Kuro-Obi locations. My most recent meal was when I ordered ramen for dinner via Seamless when I worked late and ate at my desk. ***I accidentally posted this review before I was done***I ordered the "Kuro-Obi" Layered Chicken Broth Ramen. The order arrived quickly and was still hot.  Other than how great it tasted and how quick it arrived, what was impressive about the order:- not only are the noodles separated from the soup so as not to get soggy, etc., but - all the other components arrive in separate containers, including the garlic oil, umami paste, pork chasu and vegetable toppings- in the case that the order is not still hot, a little card with instructions comes with the order on how to best reheat it and then combine it. Such a great idea to leave the broth separate for reheating before adding the oils, toppings etc to it! Impressive!

So how many people can say that they've dined in a bank vault?  This restaurant certainly has history and uniqueness.  The decor is top notch from the entryway vault door to the old elevator shaft near the bar.  I recently dined here for Sunday brunch.  The food was fair and service just okay.  I would however highly recommend the bread pudding for dessert.  It was phenomenal!!  I would return just for the dessert alone.  It might have been bettered to visit for dinner instead of brunch.  The menu would be a better representation of the food options.  I think a return visit might be required to truly experience all this restaurant has to offer.

A toast to the New Year!An impromptu meet up with a friend for drinks on 1/3 turnt out to be a launching pad for some 2019 goals and resulted in my first review of the year.In the Chelsea area earlier for lunch at one of my low key favorite Thai spots, I hit up a friend (shout out to Tameeka B.) to say hey I'm in the neighborhood. With some quick text'n back and fourth. We made plans to grab drinks after work. We arrived @ about 6:30 to a light crowd at the bar (to your right) and only a couple of tables occupied (to your left) on a Thursday evening. We were promptly seated and quickly realized HH ended @ 7pm. Our waiter Evan did not hesitate to put in our orders for both round 1 and 2 quickly before the clock ran out. Lol. Drinks (HH $10):-Still Fashionable-HoneybeeFood (Appetizers):-Bourbon Wings ($14) -Hot Chicken Sliders ($12)Service was great as Evan was a delight and the drinks were on point. I'm one who enjoys a good old fashion and their version was good but the Honeybee shined bright. The appetizers were also great, my preference would be the Wings (w/ ranch only plz) over the Hot Chicken Sliders. They were tasty but too much bread, the ratio of chicken to carbs was off. My friend agreed, since she has frequented TCS and had them previously noting larger pieces of protein to handle the buns.TCS is new to the Chelsea area, only a few months old but solid. With a dim welcoming feel of lighting and decor of some classic brands of alcohol tastefully adorning the walls it's perfect for drinks and something to nosh on while in the area. Just A Note:They feature a different HH special each day along with the drinks and they honor HH table side. (it's not just bar only)

Visiting NYC for the first time and saw this taco place pop up on Yelp. Walked a few blocks hoping not to be disappointed, and boy was I not!!The place was a little small, and no chairs were provided (clearly they wanted you to eat and get out of there) but for good reason. This place was super popular and constantly you could find a line. I got 3 tacos and I have to say, these were by far the best taco's that I have had. The meat was so flavorful, the sauces were amazing, and the spice level was just right. I 10000% suggest coming to this place for some tasty tacos, you will not be disappointed.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Chinese Cuisine

I recently dined at a local restaurant that far exceeded my expectations. On a quiet Monday evening, my sister and I were treated to a relaxed and enjoyable meal, with attentive service that struck the perfect balance between friendly and unobtrusive.

The interior design was a stunning blend of modern and classic, weaving together Western and Chinese elements that created a beautiful and inviting atmosphere. It was the kind of space that immediately sets a delightful tone for the dining experience.

As for the food, it was nothing short of exceptional. As someone who is quite selective about Chinese cuisine, I was thoroughly impressed. The radish puffs were a flaky, buttery delight, and the scallion pancakes—paired with an irresistible sauce—were a revelation, even for someone who usually isn't a fan. The bok choy with garlic was a simple yet perfectly executed dish, and the fish fillet with rice wine was light, fresh, and flavorful.

Despite its somewhat hidden location and slightly higher price point, the restaurant delivers authentic Chinese food that is absolutely worth it. I wholeheartedly recommend this establishment and give it a rare 5-star rating. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit. 10/10.
