I'm extremely inspired by our night at Bazár.  So much so that I felt the urge to review them on the way home, completely dumbstruck by the overwhelming mediocre and highly disappointing dining experience we just had.I was so annoyed and bothered that we pretty much ate and paid to get out of there. I was getting very upset. From the service to the Amateurishly shucked, low quality oysters, it's not what I'd expect of a place like this. I had high hopes for this date night pick. It's been bookmarked for awhile. Got the life of me, after now going there, I can't imagine why. It started out great. It's a lovely space. Spacious with a quaint feel. It went downhill from there.  I was craving oysters. My usual obsession. And I figured since we weren't paying for happy hour oysters, the quality would be decent. Boy did I misjudge. The ones Bazár offered at regular price tasted like bought really cheap $1 once from some other places left over $1 cheapies and tried to pass them off as edible. To top it off they were poorly shucked. That's INEXCUSABLE. There's never ever, ever an excuse or justification for poorly shucked oysters, especially when they're being touted at market price. I was spitting out shells with each. They were just vile. Not to mention, they weren't released. That's beyond low class and just bad restauranting. If you don't know how to serve something, don't serve it. But, to give a guest shell filled oysters that aren't even released, is wrong on so many, many levels. I only ordered a half dozen, and I couldn't even finish them, which is almost unheard of with me. I never not finish my oysters, especially such a small number of them. As for the cocktail sauce, it was blander than bland. It was some kind of flavorless red gunk. I had to ask for tobacco sauce for some taste.  I basically had to run to the bathroom four oysters in and rinse out my mouth from the nasty taste and residual shell still stuck in my throat. (Note: After writing my review, I ended up throwing up from the rancid oysters.)The hubby ordered the Filet Mignon special with a side salad. To their credit. This was quite good. Perfectly cooked with a delicious sauce. My charred octopus was not the worst. A bit on the bland side. Maybe they should take time out and stop by ABC Cocina near by, which can show them both how to make a great charred octopus. But it was hard to appreciate either after the start of the meal, along with the nearly non-existent service.  The two servers on the floor seemed much more interested in attending to the others around us.  Seriously, the blonde server who originally took our drink order seemed to do everything she could to avoid stopping by, including three specific times where she was walking towards us, saw me wanting something, turned and went to a table that seemed to be drinking (and potentially better tips, which is funny to us, because we typically over tip when we get good service). The male server kinda did a a wave by, without actually stopping once. But beyond that, we only got to see them as they went to other tables. Thank heavens for the runner. At least someone knew we were there.Maybe it was because we don't drink. Or maybe it's because it's part of the corporate culture, where they celebrate bad service and promote poor training, where their team is taught to look away and around customers rather than offer attentive service that should accompany a restaurant like this ... or actually any restaurant with paying customers.And, they weren't particularly busy. The back half of the place was nearly empty.My husband is in the service industry, so we tend to be very aware and sensitive when servers were having a bad or difficult night. They guys were just not all that interest in serving or waiting.I was so upset by this restaurant and this meal that I literally asked for the check as we were taking our last bite and got up and left Jayson to handle the bill. It was that infuriating. This is definitely one place we will not be adding to our repeat list, ever. So disappointing!

Tucked away in the heart of Chinatown, a stone's throw from FiDi and downtown, lies a humble Korean eatery, its interior unpretentious yet welcoming. As part of the banchan lineup, a pleasant surprise of steamed egg accompanied the standard side dishes, though this could have been a special perk of ordering a combo.

The spicy pork was competent, pairing nicely with the reasonably authentic kimchee and tofu soup — a comforting combination for those familiar with Korean cuisine. Price-wise, the establishment offers a slight reprieve from the steeper tabs found in K-town, making it an appealing option for locals seeking a quick, satisfying Korean fix without breaking the bank.

Came here with a Pulsd coupon for 2 which the choice of 2 appetizer, 2 main and 4 drinks. This place is located very close to the subway, so it's easy to get to at the corner of ludlow and delancey. It's a multi floor venue with bar/restaurant on the first floor and above for party.First floor is classic setting, high ceiling with a lot of chandeliers. Service was very fast, the waitress is super nice. Ordered steak tartare and mussels for starter, pretty good taste and good portion. Main I had steak which is $6 extra for the coupon. Steak was very juicy and cooked perfectly pink inside. My partner ordered the burger, the size of the burger is so small, it's bigger than a slider but smaller than regular burger. If you are hungry don't order this. Truffle fries are amazing. Crispy and thin. I'm surprised to find out this place offers very good food. And good cocktail as well. Just the price is a bit high.

*Claypot Rice Bowl*.I got chicken & shrimp as my protein topping in the clay pot rice bowl that comes with aromatic Jasmine rice, topped with fresh ginger, scallion, corn & splash of soy sauce  Absolutely enjoyed every single bite of this dish! I am so thankful to have had the opportunity to try this because I never came across a dish like this before so my taste buds were thanking me  This was my first food tasing invitation & it was such a great experience from beginning to end with such great service! Thank you for everything Eric!.That crispy rice & special sauce tho  What ever is on that sauce they put on top was crack with the awesome crispy rice I definitely recommend this to try!.They have another location in St. Marks so I'll def check that out as well!

Came for the burger last night, have been meaning to try it for years! Really wanted to have the burger in the original OG location so I'm happy we did. Got lucky with only a 15 minute wait and was seated at a nice table in the back. Started off with a cup of chilli (+ onion and cheese how they suggest) which was ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS! I'm very picky with my chilli and don't usually order it out but I'm so glad I did here. Not too many beans, not too much meat and the cheese is cubed up Velveeta and the red onions provide a nice bite! Strongly recommend. The burger.... was AWESOME! I understand the hype. The patty is fat and it's seasoned generously. The cheese was melted perfectly and the pickles and onions gave a great crunch. Super super juicy meat was medium rare how I ordered it, simply succulent! I'm really impressed with the burger and it definitely ranks Top 5 classic burgers on my list in Manhattan!*oh and it's cash only*

It was truly a pleasure dining here! I was extremely pleased with the quality of food, decor, cleanliness, and especially the customer service! My favorites are Iskender (grilled lamb and tomato w/ yogurt sauce) and octopus salad. Enjoy!

Title: A Feast for the Senses at [Restaurant Name]

My dining experience at [Restaurant Name] was exceptional, beginning with a wise decision by my friend to reserve a table at 5 pm, saving us from the wait. We indulged in the six-course prix-fixe menu, and it did not disappoint. Generously served to cater to four people, the meal left three of us wonderfully satiated.

The culinary journey commenced with the Toro ssam bap—an exquisite mix of seaweed, rice, toro, and egg—that simply danced on the taste buds. The Jeju chicken wings followed, presenting a fresh take on crispy Korean fried chicken, perfectly accompanied by fresh vegetables and dip. 

A highlight was the Truffle roasted mushrooms; as a box of truffles was opened tableside and liberally shaved over the dish, the aroma set the tone for the rich flavors that followed. 

The Prime Ribeye Ssam was beautifully tender and juicy, making for a delightful wrap with the accompanying pickled cabbage and fresh lettuce. The Gochu ramyun added a pleasant spicy zest to our taste adventure, rivalling the famed Ippudo with its robust flavor.

The So ramyun proved to be a creamy, thicker take on seollongtang and an instant favorite for its comforting qualities.

We culminated our meal with a trio of desserts—decadent chocolate that struck the perfect balance of richness without being overly sweet, a vanilla that was more akin to sweet milk with a subtle flavor, and a lemon sorbet that was the epitome of fresh, with just the right touch of zest.

While service was commendable throughout, it slightly waned as the evening bustled on, though the diligent plate changing was a nice touch. A minor detail observed was that the dessert spoons and bowls appeared frosted, as though fresh from the freezer. The ambience was enhanced by a well-curated playlist that added to the overall enjoyment.

In short, [Restaurant Name] delivered an elaborate and thoroughly gratifying dining experience that I would eagerly recommend.

Rating: 4.5/5

Title: A Mixed Affair with Flavors at Local Eatery

I visited a nearby restaurant in hopes of finding a spot with homemade tortillas, only to discover they serve standard, bag-warmed tortillas. The real stars proved to be the quesadillas and sopes, which stood out with their rich texture and taste. While the al pastor was somewhat dry and the lengua passable, they didn't quite wow my palate. The accompanying radishes and garnishes could have been fresher. However, it's worth noting that the kids devoured the quesadillas and sopes enthusiastically. Ultimately, this place is decent, but my quest for the ultimate taco shop in New York marches on.

Title: A Homey Dining Experience with Exquisite Flavors

We recently visited this gem of a restaurant and were met with an experience nothing short of fantastic. Sayed, our host, extended a warm welcome that made us feel like guests in his home, rather than customers. Although our first visit was premature as the restaurant hadn't opened, he kindly showed us the menu and encouraged us to return. True to his hospitable nature, Sayed remembered us upon our return and promptly invited us to settle at a table of our choosing.

The service was nothing but outstanding throughout our meal. As for the food, the filet mignon was a highlight—it was incredibly tender and bursting with flavor. Accompanying sides of steamed spinach and mashed potatoes complemented the filet perfectly, each mouthful as delightful as the last. And the chocolate cake? Simply put, it was a 'wow' moment on its own. We're already planning our next visit and highly recommend this restaurant to those seeking a cozy atmosphere coupled with delectable cuisine.

Came here on a Sunday night and it was nice and quiet which we liked.  Ordered a few sides and entrees to share which all came out hot and fresh.  I tried the branzino for the first time and LOVED it. So well-prepared!  It was well-cooked and like it had just come out of the pan.  The sautéed spinach side was also delicious along with chick pea fries and deviled eggs.  I got a dessert to go (red velvet cake) because I was so full, but devoured that too :) Looking forward to trying out some of their daily specials and all-day breakfast items.

Title: A Culinary Gem Birthed from Iron Chef Mastery

Having been an ardent fan of the Iron Chef during its peak in Japan, I was thrilled to dine at the restaurant of one of its most celebrated contenders. The establishment did not disappoint, providing a memorable experience where culinary prowess and creative flair were on full display.

The highlight of our visit was the indulgence in the chef's signature Hazelnut beer. It was, unequivocally, one of the finest I've ever savored – a bold statement that speaks volumes of its quality.

Appetizers took the spotlight for me. A particular delight was the rock shrimp accompanied by an array of phenomenal sauces, elevating the dish to new heights. Equally stunning was the tuna pâté, garnished with caviar; it was a masterpiece of both taste and presentation that truly blurred the lines between cuisine and art.

Our main courses were a testament to the chef's Iron Chef roots – delicious, satisfying, and well-crafted. It's worth noting that portions were generous, and despite my best efforts, I regretfully had no space to explore the dessert menu, an omission that assures my prompt return.

In summary, this restaurant is a must-visit for those seeking to witness Iron Chef caliber cooking in a setting where every dish is a testament to culinary excellence.

I stopped by a bustling spot for a quick bite and decided to try the pepperoni square, priced at $4.40. The standout was undoubtedly the pepperoni—exceptionally crispy and flavorful, I could easily indulge in a plate of those alone. The in-house made cheese lived up to its promise, adding a touch of authenticity to each bite. Unfortunately, service slipped as the distracted staff neglected to heat my pizza properly, which was a letdown as a warm slice would have elevated the entire experience. Also, they charge extra for card payments, so carrying cash is advisable. Despite the oversight, the quality of the toppings has me eager to give them another shot.

im going to start off my review by saying that i loveee 5 napkin burger in midtown and ive been there several times and never had a problem. I came here with one of my friends for brunch a few weeks ago and we both got the bottomless mimosas, the guac ranch burgers, and fries to share. This is a pretty standard order. Nothing seemed awry until much later; we were both sick all night with stomach aches!! This was the only thing we both ate all day too. And this was not the fault of the bottomless mimosas either since we were not over-indulging and ive done many of these and not a one got me sick like this! To be fair the service was good and the food seemed fine until later. I still love their food but im never coming back to this location again.

Before catching a Ranger game, my companion and I decided to try a new spot. On arrival, the hostess stand was unmanned, but shortly a lady from the bar seated us. The restaurant boasts a tasteful ambiance with comfortable seating, table cloths, and an unexpectedly spacious second floor.

Our waitress was efficient, if not particularly warm, on what appeared to be a slow night. While the service team was friendly—assisting with additional drink orders—the limited wine and beer list did not detract from my enjoyable Chinese beer selection.

The food menu covered all the typical dishes one expects. Highlights included the steamed dumplings, which were delightful, and a savory beef with scallion dish. Less impressive were the egg rolls, which I found small and flavorless, and the pork lo mein, which was unremarkable. A beef and vegetable dish erred on the salty side but was passable.

Portion sizes didn't live up to Chinatown generosity and felt meager considering the premium pricing—nearly $120 for two without matching the value we expected for Manhattan.

Despite price concerns, it's worth noting the restaurant did offer excellent happy hour deals on drinks. Overall, it wasn't a culinary home run, but for a pre-game meal with a few standout items, it might be worth a visit—especially for the dumplings and drinks.

Title: A Birthday Brunch to Remember

I recently celebrated a friend's birthday with a brunch at this gem of a place, and what an excellent experience it was! The brunch deal, priced at $37, offers incredible value and variety – an absolute steal in my opinion. The deal allowed us to pick one pizza, two brunch dishes, and a side, all shared amongst our group, ensuring a communal and plentiful dining experience.

The quantity was generous, leaving us all satisfied without the need for extra orders. The drink policy was sensible and appreciated – one carafe per two people, striking the perfect balance for a convivial atmosphere without the rowdiness often found at bottomless brunches.

Our waiter’s attentive and sweet demeanor added to the overall delightful experience. I wholeheartedly recommend this spot for anyone looking for a shared brunch that's both high-quality and comfortable. It is sure to impress without breaking the bank.

Title: A Gem That Feels Like Home

During a recent visit from Detroit, I stumbled upon a delightful spot that instantly felt like a favorite bar back home. This place might best be described as a high-end dive bar, boasting a selection of satisfying bar fare and a commendable array of alcoholic beverages. The ambiance is cozy and welcoming; it's a pub that exudes warmth and friendly vibes. The service only enhances the experience, characterized by its friendliness and prompt attention. I was so charmed by the place that I found myself returning for a second visit within just four days. If you're looking for a homey retreat with the comforts of good food and drink, this is the place to be.

Been coming here for years before all MSG games or events. Always my go to place. Such a cool atmosphere and always good dependable food. Started with a cheese  pizza which wasn't good with a horrible fake sauce   Also ordered a Parma flat bread which was prosciutto fig jam with arugula salad. That was divine. I ordered the pork chop I say chop cause only one tiny chop with some baby food Potatoes under it. For 32 dollars was a Tiny dish. 2 friends ordered lobster rolls which they said were good .  My buddy ordered a New York strip steak which he said said it was ok nothing to write home about. Waitress was a Sweetheart and they got us in and out quickly so we can watch the Knicks get destroyed. Maybe this dinner was best part of night. Def best place to come to before an event. Really nice bar. Not cheap but it's better then most places around here.

Stepping into the restaurant, one is immediately taken by the lush interior, complete with fiddle leaf fig trees and a vast skylight that instills a sense of openness. The ambiance set the stage for a meal that was generally nothing short of exceptional.

The highlight among the dishes was the braised kaofu, a symphony of woodear mushrooms, shiitake, and dried lily flowers enveloped in a subtly sweet sauce that was a triumph of umami. The bean curd shreds with chili sauce and the simple yet delicious steamed pea shoots in garlic sauce also left a deep impression.

Conversely, some selections like the noodle with scallion oil and mushrooms lacked complexity, while the stewed fresh shrimp with vermicelli needed a punch of acidity to reach its full potential—something easily remedied at home with a squeeze of lime and a touch of hot sauce.

While the eight spices crispy tofu was agreeable, it didn’t stand out in the way the superior dishes did. Nonetheless, the culinary hits were compelling enough to warrant future visits with an eagerness to explore more of the menu.

The service deserves a special mention for being attentive, helpful, and kind, allowing us to savor our meal at a leisurely pace without any pressure. To top it off, the reasonable pricing was the cherry on top of a delightful dining experience that earned a well-deserved 5-star rating.

I recently revisited this restaurant with a bit of amnesia regarding my last meal here, and I must say, it was a blessing in disguise. The Singapore mei fun was nothing short of fabulous! If you're a fan of bold flavors and delightful noodles, this dish is a must-try. It seems they've really upped their game, and this particular item has won me over completely. Highly recommended for a tantalizing taste of Singapore!

Title: Unpretentious Spot with Satisfying Eats

I've visited this no-frills eatery on three occasions, always greeted by the sight of eager young patrons and swift service. The highlight of my visits are undoubtedly the pork dumplings – initially small but packed with flavor, prompting an inevitable second order. On my latest visit, however, the increased size meant I couldn't tackle more than one serving.

Accompanying my dumplings was a sesame pancake, notable for its impressive thickness. Curiosity already has me eyeing their steak or pork sandwich for my next visit, mere minutes after placing my order – the wait time here never exceeds five.

Although it's far from a lavish setting and the strong aroma necessitates dining in the cafeteria, the food is a pleasure for those sporadic cravings.

Tucked away on Elizabeth Street, this cozy little spot may be small, with only two tables, but it's bustling with takeout orders, a testament to its popularity. Quick service is a standout - my friend and I were swiftly served our steamed rice rolls, with my companion giving a thumbs up to their soy drink.

Opt for a small serving unless hunger strikes hard, then a large will satisfy. A minor hiccup occurred when they had run out of chicken, leaving me to settle for pork - delicious, but a letdown when you're set on something else.

A pro tip: ask for your preferred sauce, like peanut sauce, when ordering; it's added directly to your dish rather than found on the table. For a wallet-friendly, swift bite in Chinatown, this joint is worth a shot.

Really aesthetic Chinese restaurant with plenty of food options. Came here with a group of friends and shared a couple of dishes family style. Some parts of the interior are more secluded, but we sat right in the center of the main area where it was really well lit and open. What we ordered: Garlic Fried Pork Chops with Spicy Soy Sauce - exquisite tasteHand-Pulled Noodles Mixed with Braised Fresh Lamb Szechuan Roasted Baby Cabbage and Vermicelli NoodlesCold Noodles with Shredded ChickenSteamed Pork Soup DumplingsSticky Rice Siu Mai (only 3 piece but very delicious!!)All the ordered menu items were above average on taste, but not sure if I would come again because of the price. Definitely more high-end than your local family-run Chinese restaurant, but nonetheless still worth a try!

I had an absolutely delightful experience with this restaurant's Korean cuisine - their fried chicken was perfectly crispy and their Tteokbokki was wonderfully tender, melting right in my mouth. A huge bonus is their efficient delivery service, bringing these delicious dishes right to my doorstep. Highly recommended!

So I was worried when I first arrived herebecause there was an uncanny smell that I didn't recognize to be ramen or Asian food. The space was so warm and comfortable though compared to the brutal cold outside so I decided to stay and I am so happy about that!The food here was absolutely delicious and the servers were friendly! I ordered the pork dumplings, fried chicken legs, and the spicy-miso ramen. The dumplings were nothing to brag about-- your typical frozen then reheated dish; still tasty though. The fried chicken legs were fried to perfection. The right amount of time in oil and the seasoning was just finger licking worthy. I wish there was a sweet sauce to help compliment the saltiness of the dish. I will say if salty food isn't your thing, then I would not order this dish. Or possible ask the servers not to add any additional salt as it was also garnished with salt and pepper. Finally, the ramen was just ahhhhh sooooo yummy. The spice was not too overpowering and allowed me to really enjoy the flavors of the vegetables, ramen noodles and the ground pork. And speaking of ground pork-- it was marinated in some sort of sweet peppers sauce that really popped the dish even more. So as if you couldn't tell already, I would easily get order this dish from here again lol P.S. I'm going to give it a 4-star because of the smell and part of my ramen being clumped together when I was eating. It was so frustrating because it was like a mini ramen ball in the soup and I couldn't quite grab it with the chopsticks.

Meh. Skip. I've ordered from Sant Ambroeus on Postmates before so I figured I'd finally check it out in person. The highlight is the outdoor seating - perfect for mutual people-watching; Sant Ambroeus is a place to see and be seen. Seating inside, conversely, was dark and dingy. It adopts the decor of an upscale Italian café but abandons the vitality and charm. Prices for brunch are around $18-$21 which is fairly commensurate with other spots in the area. Portion sizes are small and the food is mediocre at best. My friend had the smoked salmon platter (with bread and creme fraiche) and I had the Norwegian eggs Benedict, which came alongside a few bitter greens with a sort of mustard-based dressing. Both dishes left us hungry and we half-jokingly suggested going for a second brunch afterwards.The real clincher for the 2 star review was the service, or lack thereof. The waiter looked at my friend and me as if we were gutter rats the whole time, and his demeanor ranged from mild pretension to outward contempt. Note that my friend and I were nothing but lovely from the moment we arrived and made no requests that would be deemed unreasonable. Basically, the treatment was entirely unwarranted.All in all, hard pass. Sant Ambroeus offers a great opportunity to see a D-list celebrity or Instagram model, but not much else.

Heading to Soho with a craving for mouthwatering fried chicken and sublime udons, we hit the jackpot. Arriving at 5:30pm on Thursday, our party of two was seated immediately, though it wasn't long before the place buzzed with incoming diners.

The service shone bright - staff were courteous, attentive with water, and the food arrived swiftly. The menu boasted a variety of options, but I zeroed in on the shrimp tempura udon to truly appreciate the noodle texture and the nuanced broth. True to form, the meal, including the karage, was scrumptious without tipping into heaviness, embodying comfort on a cold winter's evening.

It's decided - this spot deserves a repeat visit.

There's nothing like coming back from a year of living abroad to a good ol' New York slice, especially from a place like Joe's Pizza. It's got the crunch, the thin crust, and perfect balance of cheese and sauce. The pepperoni slice was everything I'd been craving. This East 14th St location is just blocks away from the nearby AMC Village 7 and Village East Cinema. Perfect place to grab lunch after a matinee movie or before an afternoon flick. Make a date of it!

I'm not used to people standing outside of restaurants and trying to gesture me in outside of beach towns like Miami or in Vegas, but for once I am glad that he did.  Turns out the place had great deals such as $1 oysters, $6 cocktails and a $19 2-course dinner (with options for dessert and certain proteins for some extra bucks).  My friends and I were down for this, so we went in.  We were seated right away, and no time was wasted taking our food and drink orders.  I had a vodka sangria that was delicious, and I wish the ice wasn't in there to water it down.  It was just so refreshing!  While waiting for food, complimentary bread came out with a delicious olive oil and pesto.  The appetizer (organic mixed greens in my case) came out expeditiously and it was a nice size!  It was just the type of refreshing salad I needed, honestly nothing to complain about.  The main dish was Penne Alla Vodka, which I thought was perfect.  The pasta itself was the perfect texture, and the flavors were so good that I was sad when I finished.  There was just the right amount of sauce too!  When I took the last noodle there wasn't much sauce left, but every noodle was saturated.I also couldn't help but notice that they had an eclectic playlist and the staff were all incredibly nice, approachable, friendly people.  I don't live in the city, but I will definitely keep this place in mind for when I am ever hanging out in Times Square.

Title: A Flavorful Fusion at Pig and Khao

Review:

Pig and Khao? More like holy cow – what an impressive dining experience! This Southeast Asian fusion gem is a must-visit for anyone who appreciates vibrant and thoughtfully-prepared cuisine. The standout for me was undoubtedly the Pork Jowl and Brussels Sprouts (5/5) – a dish that demands you order it. The jowl is succulent, with just the right chew, melting enchantingly in the mouth, while the sprouts add a satisfying contrast and harmony in flavors, complete with a perfect touch of acidity.

The Sizzling Sisig (4/5) brought the heat in both temperature and taste, its crunchy texture playing well with the freshly cracked egg on top, making for an exciting dish. The Khao Soi (4/5), a robust curry noodle offering, was deeply satisfying, and the Half Hainanese Duck (4/5) showcased a tender, flavorful twist on a classic, though it's best enjoyed with a generous dunk into its accompanying sauce.

Bottom line – Pig and Khao is an establishment I'll be returning to, eager for another round of their delectable dishes. A high recommendation for any fan of Southeast Asian flavors looking for a meal to remember!

Title: A Cozy Korean Comfort Food Haven

If you're seeking solace in the form of delectable Korean cuisine, this gem in the city might just be your culinary retreat. As a regular patron, I have a deep-seated affection for their unique Kabocha and Potato Pancake - a dish that's hard to find elsewhere. The kabocha infuses a subtly sweet charm, complementing the potato's savory notes. Masterfully crafted, each pancake boasts a delightful crunch that yields to a satisfying chewiness.

The Spicy Chicken (dakgalbi) here is another favorite of mine, brilliantly blending perilla leaves, rice cakes, and sweet potatoes, creating a symphony of flavors that I simply can't get enough of. While the restaurant's jjigaes are popular, I personally find them to be just fine, with the highlight being the exquisitely fresh tofu made in-house.

Timing is everything; visiting during off-peak hours like mid-afternoon grants you attentive service without the wait. However, brace yourself for a more hurried experience during the bustling dinner rush or weekend lunches, where the eagerness to turn tables is palpable.

For those in need of comfort wrapped in the warmth of Korean culinary tradition, do yourself a favor and drop by this local favorite. The Kabocha Pancake and Dakgalbi are must-tries that will likely have you returning on your own quest for solace.

Title: A Late-Night Sushi Delight at Stanford East Sake Bar

Last night, faced with a sushi craving and a late arrival into Penn Station, my friends and I stumbled upon Stanford East Sake Bar in K-Town. Despite our unplanned visit around 11pm, we were greeted with prompt seating and extremely courteous service.

Kicking off with their cold house sake, we found it to be an excellent start to our meal – light and invigorating. Our shared dishes included the uni tororo, tako yaki, chirashi don, salmon avocado roll, and the uni hotate roll. Each dish was a hit in terms of flavor and freshness, except for the uni tororo, which was an adventurous letdown with its unexpected texture reminiscent of cold grits; a choice I won't be repeating.

However, the misstep was easily forgiven thanks to the standout uni hotate roll, which was truly exceptional, and the chirashi don which lived up to its 'bomb' reputation. With the bill rounded up to $42 per person after tax and tip, Stanford East Sake Bar proved to be a reasonably priced haven for delicious late-night sushi and quality service.

In summary, I'd recommend the Stanford East Sake Bar for anyone in search of a sushi spot near Penn Station that offers great value for money – just steer clear of the uni tororo unless you're feeling daring!

Title: Dumpling Delight at a Cozy Spot

I recently visited a bustling dumpling haven that immediately made the top of my comfort food go-tos. Despite the crowd on a busy Saturday, we were promptly seated away from the drafty door – a small, but appreciated, detail.

The service was swift and attentive, with water on our table and menus in hand in no time. The star of our meal was, without a doubt, the dumplings. We indulged in both the pork soup dumplings and the pan-fried pork dumplings. To our delight, the soup dumplings arrived almost instantly, piping hot and brimming with a savory, salty broth that complemented the tender, juicy filling. The pan-fried version boasted a perfect textural balance, sporting a crispy exterior and succulent, steamy interior – so irresistible that we couldn't help but order a second serving.

For mains, my lo mein with vegetables was a hit, featuring perfectly cooked noodles and a generous portion of veggies, albeit slightly greasy. The spicy beef soup, praised by my dining companions, struck an exquisite balance between spice and flavor, delivering warmth without overwhelming the palate.

The ambiance matched the casual, welcoming nature of the food, with a diverse clientele indicating the restaurant's broad appeal. The space may be snug, but it's comfortably suitable for groups.

If dumplings are what you crave, this spot is a must-try. You just might catch me there, working my way through yet another plate of those delightful bites.

I used to love coming here more often. Spacious restaurant with lots of seatings. Staff was friendly. Roti: it was okay. Pretty big portion and the curry was pretty good.Indian Mee Goreng: a bit greasy and small portion.Prices are reasonable. Food wasn't as memorable as it was to me though.

Title: Disappointing Bao Experience

I regret to say that my recent visit to this eatery was underwhelming. At $9.19 per bao, the value simply wasn't there. Opting for a combo with two baos and a drink totaling $19, I expected much more.

Despite its generous size, the bao bun was a letdown. It lacked flavor and disintegrated on the first bite, a problem seemingly known to staff as I was promptly offered a fork upon seeking assistance. While the meat inside was passable, it didn't redeem the meal.

Struggling through one bao and discarding the other, I left unsatisfied. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this place based on my experience, as both the food and the price left much to be desired.

Walked by this place one Saturday night with some friends and decided to come in the next day to try it for lunch. Really tasty and authentic Yunnan noodles. I got the Little Pot Rice Noodles for $15.The broth was very flavorful and the noodles were nice and soft. The texture of noodles is different than a lot of other Asian noodle dishes, it is quite soft and bouncy and the noodles pick up the broth very well. The ground pork was tasty and complimented the rest of the dish. The pickled veggies were also done very well.Some other guests got the Signature Yunnan Crossing Bridge which seemed like a very delicious option as well. May have to go back here and try that.Overall, a delicious and filling meal for an average Manhattan price. Would definitely recommend visiting here on a cold, rainy day for a warm noodle soup dish.

Title: A Delightful Foray into Northwestern Chinese Cuisine at Jiang Diner

I recently had the opportunity to experience Northwestern Chinese cuisine for the first time at Jiang Diner, and it was a revelation. The meal commenced with an unexpectedly delightful steamed eggplant and potato dish, bursting with garlic and chili flavors—both light and refreshing, a perfect choice for summer dining.

The beef shumai then took center stage with its aesthetically pleasing presentation, and its surprise burst of soup upon the first bite created a harmonious fusion between a traditional shumai and a soup dumpling.

For heartier appetites, the spicy baked buns were an excellent accompaniment to the big plate chicken with noodles. Don't let the name fool you; even the small serving of this dish was generous and satisfying, with the noodles lusciously absorbing all the robust chicken flavors.

For those less inclined towards spicy fare, the stirred noodle with shrimp offered a milder yet equally tasty option, featuring a tomato-based sauce that perfectly complemented the chewy noodles.

Service at Jiang Diner was impeccable, with the owner not only providing excellent hospitality but also giving us a taste of an upcoming seasonal treat—a fried chicken dish reminiscent of the Taiwanese style, characterized by its crispiness and savory seasoning.

A final note for future diners: Jiang Diner is a BYOB establishment, so feel free to bring your favorite beverage to round out this wonderful dining experience. Keep an eye out for new dishes and don't miss out on this culinary gem!

I was surprised to see how low the ratings for DaDong were. I went for an early dinner with my parents, so it was like we had the whole upper dining hall to ourselves. The food was great, and the service was even better. Maybe it gets hectic later in the night, but our host was checking up on us throughout our whole meal.We came solely for the Peking Duck because there are so few Peking Duck restaurants in Manhattan, but we were pleasantly surprised by the other dishes as well such as the black bean noodles and the kung pao chicken. These comfort fast food dishes looked extra as heck but they were presented in such a pretty way that I didn't think it would be possible.The Peking Duck wasn't out of this world, but it was still really good. It's pricey but that's what you should expect if you do your research.

During a work stay at the Marriott Marquis, I popped into the Broadway Lounge for a speedy meal. The bar menu, though standard, offered enough variety for a satisfying meal. Opting to dine at the bar, I was met with exceptional service; the bartender was notably attentive and personable, enhancing our experience.

We indulged in the grandma flatbread and wings to start. The flatbread was pleasantly light, complemented by delectable meatball toppings - nothing revolutionary, but certainly satisfying. The wings, however, packed a punch with their spiciness, which my companion appreciated. The burger followed, boasting a perfectly cooked patty and a harmonious blend of flavors.

A word to the wise: the lounge quickly fills up, mimicking the buzz of Grand Central. For those who revel in a lively atmosphere, this is your spot. Those seeking tranquility might consider dining elsewhere.

Title: A Festive Feast at Bill's

Celebrating Christmas in New York City, I found myself craving the simplicity of a great burger and Bill's Bar & Burger was bookmarked as the go-to spot. After soaking in the holiday spirit at Bryant Park, Rockefeller Center, and St. Patrick's Cathedral, Bill's enticing location beckoned from just across the street.

Despite a 45-minute wait, our anticipation was met with a delightful meal. The chocolate shake was rich and decadent, a perfect holiday treat. The burger itself was excellent, cooked to perfection, and paired with amazing onion rings that added a satisfying crunch to each bite. The mac and cheese, while adequate, didn't quite match the high bar set by the rest of the meal.

The cherry on top? The two of us dined for under $50 - a budget-friendly win on an NYC Christmas day. Bill's Bar & Burger was definitely a festive culinary highlight! #winning

Title: A Satisfying Slice at Pizza Rollio

During Labor Day weekend, my family and I found sanctuary at Pizza Rollio after a long drive from Boston. Strategically nestled within a charming boutique food court in the Plaza Hotel, it's a popular spot bustling with patrons, but fortune smiled on us with an open table.

Our culinary mission was clear—pizza for our selective eater—and Pizza Rollio didn't disappoint. Yes, there's a bit of a wait, and the prices reflect its upscale location, but the experience justifies both.

We settled on the cheese pizza, a minimalist choice that showcased the quality of their offerings. What's remarkable is how they strike a balance with their pizza—it's delightfully thin yet surprisingly satiating. As someone six months post-op with no stomach, quantity is a concern, but their pizza found the sweet spot between light and fulfilling, a culinary feat that's rare for me.

If you're ravenous or in a larger group, consider doubling or tripling your order—these delectable pies will leave you craving more.

In summary, Pizza Rollio is an absolute must-visit. The memory of that perfectly cheesy slice lingers, tempting my taste buds long after the last bite. I enthusiastically recommend it for anyone in the area looking for a sublime pizza experience.

When this place wins a James Beard award as Best New Restaurant in NYC, expectations are high. But like a visit to Disney, this place exceeded all of them. Has to be one of my favorite meals in a long time. Why?  For one, service. I feel like I could be besties with our server. Helpful, friendly, and efficient, she was about everything you could ask for. But she had a team behind her. Water glasses filled every few minutes seemingly. Food brought out at the right pacing, allowing you to linger and savor every bite. Because you will. The wine too is not inexpensive. But we got a Beaujolais that I didn't know could be so good. As for food: the trout beignets were not fishy at all. A light start. Don't miss the boquerons (anchovies). They have a salty oily deliciousness that were the perfect start to the meal. Then the apps: white asparagus was the vegetable I didn't know I needed. Poached, it had a ton of flavor. And the broulliade: soft slow cooked scrambled eggs with the consistency of polenta with escargot. You've never had anything like it. Get it. Then on to Duck Frites with bernaisse sauce! The duck was so tender! But my favorite dish with halibut eith mushrooms and spring peas.  Literally Spring on a plate. So good. Great coffee too. Yes, it was expensive. But it was fantastic. Make the reservations 30 days out. You won't regret it.

Title: A Hip Tsukemen Twist with a Dash of Caution

I recently dined at a trendy tsukemen spot that truly hit the mark on hip ambiance and friendly service. My meal was a delightful exploration of flavors, and despite the seemingly modest portion, the rich broth packed a full, satisfying punch. Clever touches like a complimentary hot stone to reheat the broth mid-meal set this restaurant apart and showcased their innovative approach to traditional tsukemen.

However, not all experiences at the table were equal. My friend's Tonkotsu Chashu Tsukemen was overwhelmingly salty and differed substantially from the standard Tonkotsu Tsukemen, contrary to the staff's explanation. While I relished my dish and am keen to return for the ramen, my friend's dissatisfaction was a note of caution in an otherwise enjoyable visit.

After much anticipation heightened by friends' recommendations and positive online critiques, my dining experience at this establishment fell short of expectations. The centerpiece of our meal, the broth, failed to impress and left us feeling underwhelmed. Personally, I found that my home-cooked ramen holds its own against what was offered. In short, our group departed with a sense of disappointment in the culinary quality of our dishes.

Title: A Rockin' Bite in the Lower East Side

Tucked away in the vibrant streets of LES, we discovered a gem of a spot that marries the love of rock and roll with delicious Japanese fare. The eatery, still fresh on the scene, boasts an inviting atmosphere where music enthusiasts and foodies alike can rejoice.

The charm of the place was evident before we even walked in, as a cheerful couple at the window beckoned us with an enthusiastic thumbs up. Inside, the space may be modest, with a cozy dining area at the fore and an open kitchen where all the culinary action happens, but it's the private room at the back that truly captivates. It's a treasure trove for music lovers, decked out with an impressive collection of posters, vinyl records, CDs, and even vintage cassettes.

As for the food, we indulged in a selection of Japanese-style skewers that were both visually appealing and flavorful, clearly made from fresh ingredients. Though we didn't venture into the rice bowls this time, the skewers alone have us planning our next visit.

The heart of this review lies in the overall experience – the creative theme, the welcoming staff, and the unforgettable 'Man Cave' ambiance. It's a complete package that sings to the soul. This place hits all the right notes and is deserving of an encore.

Absolutely stellar dining experience at this establishment where every dollar is justified. The pink vodka sauce enchanted my palate, undoubtedly a must-try. The duck ragu was equally impressive, cooked to perfection. Both the ambiance and service were top-notch, ensuring a memorable evening. Highly recommended for anyone looking to indulge in culinary excellence.

There's tons of pizza places in the city, from grab & go dollar slices to 45min deep dishes... but there is a reason why Artichoke has become a name in itself amongst the crowd.This particular location is cohabited with a bar, so its nice to be able to sit while munching down one of their gigantic slices (length and width of two paper plates). $6 for the one, or $39 for the whole pie.There's a rotating 7ish to choose from, but their LITERAL bread & butter (because how else could their sauce be so creamy) is the artichoke pizza. That's a must. A little thicker on the crust, but good for absorbing all the cheesy goodness oozing in. I was lucky to be dining with my partner in consumption so I got my second favorite - another white sauce one - the crab. It  reminds me of a flavorful seafood sip. So much deliciousness.Quick & easy, as most pizzas are premade and just need a short toasting in the oven. Definitely recommended.

Title: A Gastronomic Gem for Asian Cuisine Aficionados

Upon my recent visit to this local Asian culinary outpost, my taste buds were treated to arguably the best Pad See Ew I've encountered in my extensive Thai dining experiences. Opting for the lunch portion with shrimp, the dish's delectable flavors left me craving more, although I must note the serving size was a tad less generous than I would have preferred.

The menu's pricing warrants attention—$8 for spring rolls seemed steep, though it bears mentioning that the extraordinary quality of the food justifies a splurge. Additionally, the establishment offers a worthwhile happy hour, signaling potential for both palatable and penny-wise enjoyment.

My enthusiasm is piqued to explore the remainder of their offerings. Next time, I shall come with a readiness to invest a bit more, assured by the knowledge that the culinary delights that await are well worth the expense.

Title: Worth the Wait for Delectable Meats

My dining experience was initially overshadowed by the dauntingly long line at this local gem, but the wait proved worthwhile as soon as we savored the first bite of their succulent, flavorful meat. The popularity is no surprise given the quality of the meal we enjoyed. A word to the wise, plan your visit either before the rush or after the peak hours, or call ahead to inquire about reservations. If you're a meat lover, this spot is a must-try, but timing is everything to avoid the dinner crowd.

Title: Brunch with Charm and a Dash of Disappointment

Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3.5/5)

Walking into the restaurant set a positive tone, with live music welcoming us and a bustling brunch atmosphere. The complimentary corn bread, drenched in maple syrup, was a delectable start that promised good things to come.

However, despite the restaurant's charming upscale farm-themed decor and spacious rooms, the dining experience was a mixed bag. The price point is on the higher side, as highlighted by a $38 bottle of champagne for mimosas without a bottomless option.

My choice, the corn flake French toast, was a letdown; it looked appetizing but proved too dense, and the unique corn flake element did not live up to its potential. Thankfully, the caramelized bananas did provide a delightful sweetness.

My companions, on the other hand, thoroughly enjoyed their meals, hinting at the restaurant’s potential. Although the service was standard and the ambiance delightful, my personal gastronomic experience fell short of expectations. Would I revisit? Perhaps, to explore the menu further and give the restaurant a chance to redeem itself.

The dumplings themselves are good enough to warrant 5 stars for the price.  So why 1?  This place is a comedy of errors.  They charge 50 cents for takeout, which isn't something any other similar place does ... Seriously, I challenge you to find another Asian food spot that does this.  Okay, fine, they charge extra ... So clearly they are going to do something better with packaging?  No ... They'll give you no dumpling sauce or chopsticks with your takeout order - your expected to do that yourself.  Okay, so fine, are the dumplings cooked well?  Actually, no.  The women who make the dumplings pre-cook them if you order them seared (it's why steamed dumplings take a lot longer to prepare than the seared ones), and then simply reheat them on the flat top.  And that's actually not that bad.  The bad part is that these women couldn't care less about cooking and leave the finishing to the guy taking orders, who is clearly not a cook ... So things end up burnt (see picture).  Oh, and as for the guy taking the order, he is more interested in practicing his chinese than anything else ... No matter who it is.  So don't expect a goodbye or a thank you after you fill your own sauce, get your own napkins, or get your own chopsticks.  All around this place is horrendous.  But the dumplings can be quite good if made fresh and none of the shenanigans are happening.  In case owners are interested I went there on April 1st at around 10:50pm, during the time there was about 100 pre-cook dumplings sitting on the griddle. (PS ... This is my 50th time here, so the review is well earned)

The tali lunch at this place is pretty decent with good variety of food and portion, though it might not be the most exciting one in the center of the Curry Hill... I waited for around 10 - 15 minutes for my food when there were not so many guests. However, when the place came, everything is very hot especially the Indian bread, making the waiting time so worthy. The bread tasted so good when it's hot and probably the best piece of the whole meal. For the vege pieces on my plate, they were bit lack of flavors.

Calle Dao, a bustling spot my friend and I found ourselves in, didn't disappoint with its vibrant atmosphere. As reservations filled the place promptly, we were greeted by an exceptionally friendly and attentive server. Although we missed out on the Oxtail Croquettes, our taste buds weren't left hanging. The Beef Sliders were a savory teaser, and the Cuban Sandwich Spring Rolls presented a delightful twist. The real stars, however, were the Black Rice Seafood Paella and Lechon Asado with Fried Rice, both generous in portion and novel in their Cuban-Chinese flavor fusion — a delicious divergence from the Chino Latino food I know. Sadly, the feast left no room for dessert, giving a perfect excuse for a future visit.

Very very aesthetic cafe to visit in New York! Super instagram worthy drinks and snacks! Basically, this cafe is an eye-pleasing cafe. However, the drinks are mediocre, I found a piece of hair in my drink and when I tried to tell the server, she looked at me straight in the eye and walked away from me. They seat you at a table and bring you the drinks so you have to tip them as well. But I was not happy with the service at all. The food and drinks are pretty overpriced not to mention the merchandise they sell there are extremely overpriced! If you are in New York and is a big instagrammer, I would recommend visiting once. A good first time experience but won't be going back again!

I am so blessed to be working in SoHo. Chinatown is super close and I can eat all the cheap Chinese foodz. Yi Ji's specialty is their azn rice rolls. There is man constantly cranking them out fresh! I ordered their small beef rice roll with added corn and their small shrimp rice roll. It did take awhile for my order to be ready, so if you want a quick grab and go meal, this is not the place for you. They will give you a number and call it out when your order is ready. Everyone there is super azn so they will call out the number in Chinese. The lady knew I was an ABC and she called my number out in English lolll. The rice rolls were perfect. They were nice and silky with a fair amount of meat in it. Don't forget to add the soy sauce or the dish will be bland! You can request them to add peanut sauce or spicy sauce to the noods when you order. There's a few seats in the store, but it's super small. You'll be sharing the table with azn grandmas and grandpas haha. I was pretty full off the two small orders which was $6 total. So worth!

Sign outside says $10.95 luncheon special, including entrée and wine drink, almost unheard of in midtown Manhattan.  We couldn't used our Hilton Elevated Rewards vouchers for the prix fix items, but the regular priced entrees. Colorful interior with brightly painted murals on the walls.  Band stage, but not for a weekday lunch.  Wife orders the $22 corvina, and I order the $24 paella marinera.   We also order a coke and coffee to push the order over $50, as our vouchers come in $25 denominations, and exclude tip and gratuity.Decent service, as we don't have long to wait.The Corvina al estilo Hemingway comes with 4 ounces of white sea bass, lima beans, peppers and clams in a light red sauce.   A bit on the bland side.  Comes with white rice and an overly salty black beans in sauce on the side.  The Marinera comes with Spanish rice, mussels, clams, calamari, tiny scallops and a single shrimp.  The calamari are the big bracelet size rings, dominating the plate, not too rubbery, but cools fast.  Not much flavor, but it goes well when mixed with the Spanish rice and the 10+ potent flavored mussels and clams.    $3.50 for one serving of coke in an 8 ounce glass with ice.  Hey, they have to make money somehow, in this high rent area of mid Manhattan.Service prompt and attentative.We will come back to Guantanamo, I mean Guantanamera.  Don't want to go to Guantanamo, even with it's better tropical weather in Cuba, even with free transportation courtesy of Uncle Sam prisons!

Title: A Culinary Haven for Every Palate

My recent visit to this charming eatery was a delight, offering a varied menu that caters to all tastes. Each dish we tried was a testament to their commitment to flavor and presentation. The creamy shrimp pasta was a decadent treat, while the chicken and avocado salad impressed with its freshness and the delightful addition of caramelized nuts and apple slices.

The crispy rice bowl lived up to its name, perhaps a bit too much on the 'crispy' side, making it a workout for the jaw—but the flavors were impeccably balanced. A side of sweet potato fries stole the show, ranking as some of the finest I've indulged in.

Despite being nestled in a cozy space, the restaurant operates like a well-oiled machine—especially noticeable during the bustle of a Tuesday lunch rush. Quick service and high turnover didn't detract from the dining experience. This place truly stands out as a versatile gem in the culinary landscape.

I recently visited Gari's Sushi for an omakase experience on a Saturday afternoon and left thoroughly impressed. While this spot may not cater to sushi purists due to its creative flair, the imaginative and well-considered combinations are both thoughtful and exciting. Each serving, including 12 delectable pieces for $120, was perfectly portioned. The sushi rice struck the right balance of flavor and stickiness, enhancing the overall taste. Additionally, the seaweed salads were a delight, with a slight preference for the one adorned with mushrooms. Gari's Sushi is undoubtedly a place to indulge in an unconventional yet exceptionally tasty sushi adventure.

Title: A Hidden Gem with Comfort Classics

I recently found myself at a delightful little spot that turned out to be a gastronomic revelation. The ease of making reservations set a positive initial tone. The welcoming staff orchestrated a lovely evening for me and my companions.

Our table indulged in a range of savory treats such as the rich and hearty buffalo mac and cheese, the sweetly spiced hot honey chicken and toast, and the indulgent deluxe french dip—one of the best I've had, requiring a fork and knife for proper enjoyment. The portion sizes were generous, justifying the fair prices. Additionally, the french onion soup, priced at $11, could easily satisfy two, and it was truly one of the finest renditions of the dish I've ever tasted.

The server's thoughtfulness shone through when they split the french dip for my friend and I without a fuss. However, the fondue fries fell short—a bit gritty and overwhelming in quantity, they ended up soggy beneath the cheese sauce.

While the restaurant has a slightly dim ambiance, it boasts a unique layout with varying dining spaces, which could easily cater to private parties.

One small gripe was that the restaurant week menu didn't feature any of the establishment's famous dishes, leading us to order à la carte. Nevertheless, this was a minor point in what was otherwise a fantastic dining experience. Highly recommended for anyone craving comfort food done right.

A great place for happy hour food and drinks! All the items from the happy hour menu were easily shareable and delicious. We ordered the Tteok & Cheese off of the HH menu and it was another great shareable plate. The dish reminded me of gnocchi and an Italian dish rather than something Korean. I personally really enjoyed the soy glazed wings! Overall great happy hour option.

Title: A Heavenly Hybrid of Steak and Sushi at Tender

If culinary excellence had a name, it would be Tender. As a seasoned patron of both premier steakhouses and sushi joints, I can testify that Tender stands out with its exemplary culinary craft. With a dozen visits under my belt, I've been consistently impressed by the meticulous attention to both the sublime flavors and the exceptional service.

The essence of Tender's triumph lies in its exceptional food quality. This place sets a gold standard for flavor; there's not a single item on the menu that falls short of delicious. As a self-proclaimed connoisseur, I attest that Tender is an outstanding steakhouse with a very commendable sushi offering. It may be a challenge to excel in both arenas, but Tender does so with grace, serving up succulent steaks alongside commendable sushi.

For a perfect meal, begin with the sushi appetizers. While the rock shrimp tantalizes with its sweet, heavy breading, those preferring a less sweet kick might substitute it for a taste of "The Blessing" sushi roll, an unforgettably divine choice. For the main event, the Tomahawk steak is an absolute must-try, best shared and paired with your choice of bearnaise or chimichurri sauce for an extra flavor dimension.

Take it from me or ask the waitstaff if you're searching for guidance—you're in for a treat. Tender isn't just a restaurant; it's a culinary destination that promises and delivers a sensational dining experience.

Don't let the street/road construction deter you from restaurant.  If coming from Walker St, stay on the left side of the street (you will see a sign) and walk 1/2 way down the block to find the restaurant.  Walk in the door, there is a short hallway then you walk into a semi-dark dining room.After reading all the reviews I had no expectations about the burgers since it ranged from either it's ok to it's absolutely amazing, in the end you will have to decide for yourself unless you have similar tastebuds to me.If you had a big group like we did, make sure to make reservations.  With a big group, we got to sample quite a few items.  Here's what we ordered:Beverage:Sanarac Root Beer - always on draught -- if you like/love root beer, got to order this or as a float for dessert (great for sharing!).Appetizer:General Jane's Honey Fried Chicken with chili, sesame seeds and cilantro.  Must get though don't fill up on this dish.  The sauce is great for dipping fries as suggested by our server and it's true.Caesar SaladChopped SaladSide dishes:French Fries which comes with a mayonnaise thick dipping sauce and garlic aioli.  Note: some dishes comes with fries so don't order too much.Hash Browns didn't have much flavoring.Entrees:Shaved Prime Rib Sandwich (French Dip) - this is pretty good and cut into 4 so it's easy to share.Single Cheeseburger - double patty and pretty good though I only had 1/4 so I can try other dishes.Double Cheeseburger- triple patty which is more meat if you can finish it.  It's a big meal!Note: for cheeseburger add egg (+$1) and add bacon (+$1)Dessert:Mille Feuille - vanilla cream is not too sweet and layers are flakey.Napoleon - malt, salted caramel and dark chocolate.Root Beer Float - great for sharing!The restrooms are located downstairs next to another bar saloon.  There are 2 stalls in the restrooms though it's not brightly lite though you are able to see.Come hungry and an open-mind so you can decide for yourself.

Jeepney restaurant pays homage to its cultural roots not just in name—after the vibrant Filipino public transport vehicles—but in the flair it brings to classic Filipino cuisine. We began with banana ketchup ribs, which, while slightly on the dry side, were redeemed by a delightful smoky-sweet glaze complemented by a punchy vinegar sauce. The sisig tacos, packed with various cuts of pork, were toned down in spice, but the addition of kalamansi and cilantro brought freshness to the dish.

Our mains included pancit malabon with perfectly al dente noodles in a savory-spicy seafood sauce, and the pork bicol express—succulent, slow-roasted pork shoulder in an irresistibly sweet and spicy sauce, though a tad salty. The side of roasted bok choy provided a nice contrast.

We concluded with halo-halo, which fell short of expectations due to the ice's coarse texture; a finer shave would have made a world of difference. Despite minor setbacks, Jeepney stands out for its colorful approach to traditional Filipino dishes.

Title: Cozy Brunch at Sveta

Decided to give Sveta a try for a Saturday brunch as it was newly opened and could accommodate our group of five without a hitch, unlike other West Village spots that were fully booked. The reservation process was smooth, and our party was seated promptly upon arrival despite staggered arrivals.

At 1pm, the restaurant was comfortably uncrowded and we received efficient service. Our meals arrived swiftly. I sampled the lobster pelmeni with its unique black dough, which was enjoyable though it didn't quite dazzle my palate. It was accompanied by a side of sour cream for a traditional touch. The veal pelmeni was met with approval from my husband, and my brother savored his crepes topped with caviar.

The ambiance of the restaurant is appealing, with a quiet atmosphere that's a welcome respite from the city's hustle. Pricing is what you’d expect for New York, and the service is warm and welcoming.

In summary, while Sveta is a nice spot for those looking to try out a new Russian eatery, it doesn't necessarily stand out as an essential experience. However, it's worth a visit for its calming vibe and friendly service.

It was a Friday evening in the city. Rain coming down. We were all famished from walkIng to all the sights around Time's Square. One place booked, another had a long wait, yet another closed for a private party. Via Brasil welcomed us like an old friend. The 5 of us were promptly greeted and seated. Several Brazilian gentlemen circulated through filling glasses, taking orders, bringing bread and ensuring every detail was attended to! The presentation and professionalism was impressive. For an app we munched on the fresh, lightly battered calamari that was accompanied with some poppin side sauce that had just the right amount of kick! We ordered our various menu items. For me, the showstopper was my Brazilian braised beef with mashed potatoes. The absolute tenderness was unbelievable!!! Cut through it with a fork kind of tender. Another dish was served in a pineapple. Yet another was served in an acorn squash. Layers and layers of flavors! Oh how I want to go back! Near the square, but want an off the beaten path...head down 46th to this little gem! Bon appetite!

Title: A Stunning Culinary Gem at Electric Lemon

My dining experience at Electric Lemon, nestled in the Equinox Hotel, was nothing short of exceptional. With breathtaking views of New York City, this restaurant easily topped the list of places we dined during our trip.

From the moment we were greeted by the exceptionally lovely host, the stage was set for a remarkable meal. The cuisine, to put it simply, was incredible. The Apple Endive salad was particularly memorable—it was as delicious as it was beautifully presented, satisfying both the palate and the eyes.

The attention to detail at Electric Lemon was noteworthy, with clean plates and flatware promptly provided between courses—a small but appreciated touch that reflects their commitment to a flawless dining experience.

Electric Lemon has indeed checked all the boxes for an amazing meal and exceeded expectations. Thank you for an unforgettable experience. We will definitely return!

Great location across the street from Bryant Park, there will likely be a line when you go to this hopping brunch spot. Was disappointed to learn their Matcha French Toast is unavailable on the weekend. That was one gripe. Another gripe was the prices! My mom and I got the Burrata and Fig Toast and the Avocado and Salmon Toast. Both were good, beautifully-plated, and were rich and flavorful. We'd recommend both. However, the portion sizes could've been larger especially given the high prices.My latte was very cute and yummy, but again, not worth the price.

Decent soba noodles in NYC, but I think I've had better around here. Came here on a Sunday night at 530pm with a friend of mine. Restaurant wasn't too packed so we were immediately seated. I ordered the tempura soba cold ($17.50) and my friend got a shrimp tempura soba hot ($15.00). Total bill came about ~$32.50, tax and tip not included. AMBIANCE:I really like the minimalist decor in Soba Azuma. Its not too pretentious, and definitely more so on the casual side. I like the Japanese aesthetics that they are striving here at Azuma.OKAY:My soba noodles were okay. I think portion wise you have three options, small medium and large. They are all the same price, so I opted for the large portion size. The noodles were very fresh and tasted nice. I liked the soba dipping sauce that the noodles came with, and the scallions and wasabi pairs nicely with the noodles. The tempura leaves more to desire for. They're good, but nothing spectacular and at times I thought it tasted slightly bland. The tempura dipping sauce did make up for the blandness. You're given 3 shrimp tempura, a onion tempura, green pepper tempura, and a potato-ish/radish like tempura. Not the best selection of tempuras, but if you're paying $17.50 I guess its costs justified. My friend had similar thoughts with his hot tempura soba. The soba broth was nice and the noodles were tasty and fresh, however at times it felt the noodles tasted a little bland. OVERALL:I had an okay-ish experience at Azuma. Its decent, but nothing too spectacular that will blow your mind away.

Title: Cozy Comforts and Generous Portions in the West Village

Tucked away in the vibrant heart of the West Village, my friend and I discovered a charming restaurant that offered much more than just a meal—it provided a cozy retreat reminiscent of a comfortable living room. The interior was spacious, with several rooms including one that housed a large, welcoming couch, a TV set, and a fireplace, all contributing to the warm ambiance that greeted us.

Choosing to lounge on the plush couch with a low table, we were immediately enchanted by the homely decor featuring wooden furniture, tasteful stone tile flooring, and a bookshelf that completed the domestic vibe. The complimentary chips and salsa served were a crunchy, well-seasoned delight with the salsa adding a pleasant kick to start the experience.

I indulged in the Chimichangas—a generous dish of two hefty fried burritos with a choice of varied and tempting fillings. With the helpful guidance of our wonderful waitress, who kindly accommodated my preference for two different fillings, I settled on a combination of chorizo and chicken. The former was a standout, bursting with juicy, flavorful sausage and oozing cheese, while the chicken was tender, well-seasoned, and no less satisfying.

Though the accompanying Mexican rice failed to make a lasting impression due to its mild flavor, the sheer size of the portions ensured I left feeling more than satisfied. Not only was the food hearty, but the service was attentive and genuine, adding to the positive experience.

Considering the reasonable pricing, especially for the West Village, I would say this spot is worth a visit. While the plethora of nearby dining options means it may be some time before I return, the unique ambiance and the delightful Chimichangas have definitely left a lasting impression.

I'm totally in love with Air's! It's the perfect combination of cute + sexy + cozy + sultry. I had a quick day trip up to NYC for work and prior to catching my train back to DC I dropped by here for a celebratory glass of bubs. It was raining outside, so I rushed in to be welcomed by a space that was dim lit, filled with plants and most importantly, the coolest most warm, welcoming and service oriented staff I could have ever dreamed of. Seriously, they are all gems. Chill, natural, conversational, nurturing, attentive (but not smothering.) I'm running out of adjectives here with this gush session, but they are just awesome. I ordered a glass of vintage which was delicious, but really I could have had that anywhere and it wouldn't have made for an actual experience beyond a nice taste. It truly was the environment and the wonderful staff that left me feeling happy, satisfied and like I experienced a little bit of magic away from the rain.Thanks so much to all of the staff at Air for being the absolute best!

This is definitely one of the nicer restaurants in the area and the decor makes it feels like you're in a "Thai Market" per se. I came here with one other friend and was able to be seated immediately for lunch on a Sunday. There was a party who wanted to grab a table before us, but they wouldn't budge until the entire party is present to be seated.We got the lunch deal that they offered where you get to choose an appetizer and an entree for $10. If you wanted shrimp or beef as your protein instead of the chicken, it would cost you an extra $2. I got the Yen Ta Fo for my entree which they have the description as: Pink noodle soup, fish tofu, fish ball, morning glory, fermented bean curd sauce. For appetizer, I got the Curry Puff which is Curried chicken, potato in puff pastry. My friend ordered the Pad Se-Ew with Steamed Thai dumpling.The appetizers came out first and I was surprised that I only got one Curry Puff while my friend got two Steamed Thai Dumplings. It may be because it's the lunch special, but I've been to other Thai restaurants where they serve more than just one even as a lunch deal. The entree I have no complaints about food wise.The service on the other hand needs some work. When the food came out, it was just thrown on the table rather than placed in front of the person who ordered what. It just seemed rather unprofessional and came off somewhat rude as that is essentially the job as a waiter. Other than that, everything seemed just fine.It would be interesting to see what the portions would be like if I didn't get the lunch special (if I'd only get one Curry Puff again). Will keep you posted the next time I visit.

Came here on a Friday at 10:30am for breakfast with a friend. There was no wait and the place was semi-empty! The interior of Jack's has a clean diner aesthetic. This place is very cute and definitely instagrammable if thats what you're into! (Like their menus have cute little doodles on them)I ordered the Green Shakshuka - theres 2 eggs baked in green tomatillo and served with two slices of toasted brioche. I ordered this because it was unique! When it came, the bright green shakshuka really caught my eye. Flavor was good and I especially loved how soft the bioche was. However, because the brioche was so soft, I had a hard time eating it with the shakshuka as it couldn't really hold much of the sauce/egg on it without falling. Service was great and food came in a good time - my water cup was always filled and waiters checked in periodically to make sure everything was going good. I would recommend if you wanted to try something unique such as a green shakshuka!

Stopped here on a whim because we were hungry.  What a cool place.  Love the French theme.  The food was outstanding.  We had a bacon and egg open-faced sandwich on sourdough bread.  Really great.  The eggs were so well seasoned and the bread had a really nice crispiness to it that contrasted well with the fluffy eggs.  I ordered the Salad nicoise.  Really flavorful.  Really unique taste of France.  They were generous with the Tuna too.  I also got the chocolate almond croissant and the white chocolate and pecan viennoise.  Both were outstanding.  The croissant was unlike any croissant I've ever have before.  It was very light and airy like a croissant on the outside but gooey and doughy on the inside.  It had this sort of chocolate filling that was incredible.  It was also my first time having a viennoise.  It ended up just being a muffin.  But a really good muffin.  A bit on the dry and crumbly side, but really flavorful.  Highly recommend it.We ended the meal with something called the cardinal.  A raspberry mousse dome filled with a creme brûlée center.  One of the best things we had on the entire trip.  Looked too good eat at first, but temptation got the best of us.  We actually left and did some sight seeing before stopping in here again and checking out the pastries.  We had the Mangdor, the Agadio, the eclair, and a couple different types of the tarts.  All were phenomenal.  My favorite was the apple tart.  Very similar to the one I had in Paris when I was a kid.  Fresh apples layered nicely on top, glazed with a cinnamon sugar that was amazing.  Great flaky pastry on the bottom.  The most interesting was the Mangador (A rectangular mango flavored mousse layered dessert). Really stunning looking.  I had originally thought this place was a one-of-a-kind type deal, with maybe a sister restaurant in Paris or something.  Turns out this restaurant\bakery is all over New York.  I found about 10 or so just in the immediate area.  Still, you would never guess this place was a chain.  So cute and quaint on the inside, and the food is all high quality.  Very happy to have stopped by here.

From outside appearance, I thought this place was an outdated small place. But surprisingly the place was quiet modern, with a good number of seating. Goon mandoo, which is the fried version of mandoo was my favorite. I liked the pork/chive version the most followed by vege version. Mool mandoo was good as well. For that also pork version was better than vege version. I also liked the complimentary veggies they gave.

Title: A Gastronomic Delight Worth the Wait!

From the moment I arrived at this bustling eatery, the buzz and popularity were palpable. Pro tip: leverage Yelp's waitlist feature to manage the inevitable wait time, which can stretch over an hour – a testament to this place's allure.

A friend's high praise led me here, and the experience didn't disappoint. Each dish we ordered was a revelation, but the standout was the Kimchi Creamy Udon - a perfect balance of flavor without overwhelming spice.

The anticipation to explore more of their menu is already building. This restaurant has earned a spot on my go-to list, and I can't wait to indulge in another culinary adventure here.

I was craving for sweets on a Friday afternoon and remembered there's by CHLOE behind my building. I stopped by and got the gluten-free chocolate chip cookies. It was sweet but kind of missed the chewiness of the regular chocolate chip cookies.

Went here for dinner by myself the other night.  The restaurant has a very authentic, albeit upscale, feel.  Sat at the counter, which was oddly empty.   I ordered the Niboshi Shoyu Ramen and thought it was spectacular.  Probably the best ramen I've had in NYC, dethroning my next favorite at E.A.K.  Broth was very "clean", not oily at all like a tonkatsu style, and had a wonderful dashi-like flavor.  Noodles and toppings were also way better than is typical of ramen in NYC.  It was so good in fact that I finished the entire bowl, soup and all, something I don't think i've done in many years.  Next time I plan on bringing a friend or two, so that I can share some of the non-ramen dishes.

Title: A Fresh, Satisfying Lunch at the New Spot in Town

Having heard about the recent opening, I decided to give this new restaurant a try through Mealpal. My selection, the Mediterranean Supergreens, was a delight. The dish featured a fresh salad accompanied by three warm falafel pieces and pita bread – a portion that was satisfying without leaving you stuffed. Impressively, the falafel arrived piping hot, a testament to the kitchen's quick turnaround, as there were no warming lamps in sight. The bustling atmosphere added to the experience, with a crowd of diners creating an energetic vibe. This restaurant is a hit in my book, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.
Cool spot to hit when you need a venue for a pre Madison Square Garden meet up.   Bourbon selection lives up to this place's name

Came here after a drunken revelry with a few friends on a Saturday/early hours of Sunday to indulge our drunken appetites before going home. We came as a party of 4, and were seated outside immediately. The servers seemed harried, as if they wanted to rush us out and be done for the evening, though there were a number of people also still eating. The four of us decided to get 4 dishes to share, including two pizzas, a burrata salad, and fried calamari. All the food was served quickly, but the way it was cooked seemed like it had been thrown together haphazardly and carelessly. The pizzas, while kind of tasty, were thin to the point of being near soggy. The calamari was nothing to write home about. My favorite dish by far, was the burrata salad, which contained surprising slithers of grapefruit, which pleasantly offset the creaminess of the cheese.Overall, I had a higher expectation for this place based on the reviews and would maybe come back at proper dinner hours to see if the cooking fares better.

This place is every Instagrammer's delight. Everything is so pretty, pink and perfect looking.They score 10/10 on presentation. They have a unique gourmet type menu filled with sumptuous looking desserts and drink options.
