Only problem is most of their stuff is a bit overpriced for eg: flower milk shouldn't be $7 or a raspberry mousse can be lower than $14.However they kill it with their presentation, every item ordered was pleasing to the senses; eyes, nose and mouth... The rose shaped raspberry mousse was a treat for sore eyes; pretty to look at and equally delicious in taste. We loved every bite of it. Their chocolate hazelnut cake with passion fruit jelly was my favorite; mix of sweet chocolate with tangy jelly was the winner of the evening.They serve very good coffee as well, we enjoyed our caffe mocha and cappuccino. My friend's affagato was good as well.We could see such pretty looking desserts and drinks being served around us.. I can't get over the aesthetic beauty of everything in that place. I wish I had taken better pictures to substantiate it.Though u land up spending quite a bit for just coffee and dessert, you come out feeling happy and visually satisfied.

Well Brooklyn Fare the grocery store might not make a proper deli sandwich, but Brooklyn Fare Chef's Table is one of the best fine dining experiences I've had. The dishes are based on Japanese cuisine, which I love, with some delightful French and New American influences. Importantly for me, and unlike my experience at some other fine dining establishments in the city, the dishes are savory but not heavy, and you end the night feeling satisfied but not weighed down.In terms of particular items, where to start. I loved all the seafood dishes, particularly the fish dishes. The Saba was delightful, tender, cooked perfectly, as was the Chiba (Japanese Sea Perch). The uni was surprisingly light, almost as if it was whipped, and not cloying like I sometimes find at other restaurants. And the wagyu was like butter, it reminded me of my favorite Saga Beef restaurant in Tokyo (Kira Ginza). As for the desserts, all were delightful, but my favorite was the cream with soy caramel. It's hard to describe the flavor, but it was something well worth savoring. And I can't say enough good things about the wine pairing. I especially loved the Clemens Busch Trocken Riesling from the Mosel region, and the Sauternes dessert wine. Service was professional, attentive and friendly. No one missed a beat. In short, we felt that this experience hit the mark in every way and cannot recommend it enough.

There are only few seat in Minca so you might need to wait sometimes but not too bad. There are 5-6 different noodles style you can choose from which is great. Their broth was rich and chashu was well cooked. We also love their gyoza with spicy sauce.

Title: An Enchanting Evening at Il Cortile

Last night's dinner at Il Cortile on Mulberry Street was nothing short of spectacular. A friend's recommendation led us to this gem, and it did not disappoint. The ambiance in the Garden Room was elevated by the delightful live music, creating the perfect backdrop for our meal.

The service was impeccable; the staff went above and beyond to ensure a memorable experience. Starting with a variety of appetizers, each was a tantalizing prelude to the main courses. The Veal Piccata was exceptionally tender, easily yielding to a fork's touch. Meanwhile, the Bronzino stood out with its flawlessly prepared rice accompaniment, and the Rib Eye Steak was impressively large and packed full of flavor.

Dessert was a glorious finale, with creamy ice cream and an indulgent Lava Cake that blissfully melted in the mouth. Without hesitation, I wholeheartedly recommend Il Cortile for those seeking a delightful dinner experience that is sure to please.

Title: A Noodle Experience with Authentic Ambiance

As a newcomer to the world of hand pulled noodles, my anticipation was high upon visiting this establishment. The noodles themselves possessed a delightful similarity to dumpling dough: think chewy, dumpling skin transformed into lengthy strands, perfect for slurping. My choice of the day was the vegetable hand pulled noodle swimming in soup, a dish that promised comfort.

Unfortunately, the broth didn’t live up to my expectations - it lacked the depth of flavor I had hoped for, and the accompanying vegetables didn't make a lasting impression. However, the generous portion size provided great value for the $12 price tag, ensuring this meal was definitely one to fill you up.

The restaurant's decor transported me straight to a traditional Chinese setting, complete with oriental furniture, intricate artwork adorning the walls, and charming miniature (though artificial) bonsai trees gracing each table, adding a touch of tranquility.

My visit, amid the pitter-patter of a rainy weekday noon, found the place quiet and serene, perfect for reflecting on this new culinary adventure.

A humorous and thoughtful touch was the provision of Tide bleach pens, a quirky and practical solution for any enthusiastic eater prone to spills.

In summary, while the meal had its shortcomings, the ambiance and cultural immersion offered a pleasurable experience.

Had lunch here the other day. We were seated promptly and the restaurant got packed within ten minutes. We had the following :Lamb Club I was expecting the lamb to be warm and tastier but it was a bit on the bland side and somewhat cold. Hanger SteakThis was part of the lunch prix fix for $28. It was very small. The steak quality was good as we requested for medium rare and taste was good but the serving was definitely on the skimpy side. Fries that came with were crispy and good though. Almond Cake Cake was light which I enjoyed. Some almond cakes are too dense. This was just right. Not too sweet. Cocktails. We had a few cocktails with lunch and they were good. If I remember correctly we had the punch and the old fashioned. Both were well made cocktails. Staff were alert and pretty attentive. Didn't need to flag them down at all. And they did a very good job anticipating when you needed something without being overbearing.

Ok, so it's quarantine so places that are still open automatically get a +1 stars. This meal had raw food  which is an automatic 1 star, so this is a 2 star experience. Let's dive in ...Scallion Pancake (3/5): Beginning positive, the pancakes actually have good flavor which was nice. The center of the pancake was undercooked but not raw. The sauce is rather sweet which I thought was fine. Vegetable Roll (4/5): Cooked through, crispy, and sweet. For a couple of bucks this checks the box. Hot and Sour Soup (4/5): Standard hot and sour with a decent balance of flavor and ingredients.Chicken Seaweed Broth Soup (4/5): It's some seaweed and chicken broth. Take it as what it is. Vegetable Lo Mein (2/5): This veggie lo mein is not only lacking flavor but also vegetables. Basically consists of lo mein noodle, a bit of vegetable oil, and a sprinkle of shred carrot and onion. General Tso's Chicken (3/5): This is your mall-quality General Tso. The chicken is sweet, fried, but not saucy enough -- and a few florets of steamed broccoli accompany this too. It could have achieved a plus one if there was any sauce to dress over this two-ingredient dish. Pork Soup Dumplings (1/5): So as eluded to, this was raw. Each dumpling has a tiny piece of raw pork surrounded by gelatinous broth. The picture does a better job of describing this than words can. TL;DR: If the soup dumplings were cooked through we would have ordered from here again (at least during quarantine).

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Arenstein

My boyfriend deserves all the accolades for recommending Arenstein, where I was fortunate enough to discover the pizza that has ruined all other pizzas for me: the Arenstein pizza. This masterpiece came with a vodka sauce base, layered with pepperoni, and graced with a perfect balance of pickled chili and a sweet honey drizzle. Forewarned by our attentive waitress about the heat of the chili, we opted for half the pizza with it and half without – a wise decision for someone with spice sensitivities like myself.

The symphony of flavors in this pizza was nothing short of divine. The sweet, tangy, and spicy elements complemented each other flawlessly, making every bite memorable. Even my attempts to recreate it at home failed to capture its essence, solidifying its status as a must-have. Initially, the price made me hesitate, but one bite in, and there's no question about the value for money – the crisply baked crust and top-notch ingredients speak for themselves.

We also dived into the Emmy Burger on the recommendation of fellow diners. It was a hit, especially with my boyfriend. While it wasn't my favorite, it was still a decent meal.

Since my visit on November 9, 2019, the unique combination of vodka sauce, pepperoni, and honey has left a lasting impression on my taste buds. Arenstein didn't just serve up a meal; they provided an experience that I'll be trying to relive for a long time to come.

Was a decent place to get a meal. I'll go back and try more options. Looks busy and the food seems to move quickly. So I'll review again once I've tried a couple more options. But nice staff decent amount of food for a good price and place was very clean.

Apparently this place was started by the same people who started artichoke pizza. While I've long been a fan of artichoke, after trying this place, my loyalty has shifted to Lions & Tigers.Their deep dish pizzas are loaded with toppings. You can't even find a crust (I admit I skip the crust on most pizzas) bc there's just meat and cheese all over the whole thing. We suffered through intense choice paralysis. If only they sold them by the slice so we could try everything!! Ultimately we got the pepperoni pizza. Even though it was $6 more than the classic pizza, the amount of pepperoni on it and the amazing flavor made it worth it. There are only two small round tables to eat at so we took ours to the high line to eat. The hardest part is smelling your pizza the whole walk there but I promise it's worth it!

While the culinary wizardry at [Restaurant Name] left an indelible impression, the service marred what should have been a stellar celebration. From the onset, our server's condescending tone when ensuring our dishes would arrive sequentially was both unwelcome and unwarranted. This promise quickly dissolved, as the flow of dishes became a logistical tangle, with subsequent courses arriving prematurely and empty plates lingering like unwanted guests at our cramped table.

The chaos was exacerbated by the food runner, whose contempt for patrons was on full display, from mocking slow-moving guests to rudely instructing neighboring diners on how to eat their food. His behavior oscillated from aggressive plate-shoving to premature attempts to clear our table, disrupting an otherwise enchanting parade of dishes like the stunning foie gras with grape leaves and the knockout pork with anchovies and chicories.

Crammed seating compounded the disarray, with other diners jostling our table on entry and exit. The lack of space was incompatible with the premium dining experience one would expect at such price points.

Despite the kitchen's undeniable talent, capable of earning the restaurant its Michelin Star—and hinting at the potential for more—the front-of-house team's contemptuous, almost hostile demeanor toward customers left us opting to forgo dessert and seeking solace in a nearby ice cream parlor. A pity, as with a service overhaul, I could envision a second star on [Restaurant Name]'s horizon.

Au Cheval has graced New York City with its presence, delivering the same world-renowned burgers that took Chicago by storm. Their menu takes classic diner fare to new heights, with the standout being their indulgent burgers. Don't let the menu names fool you— the "single" boasts two patties, while the "double" packs three, each one a delightful contradiction of a crispy exterior and succulent interior. Toppings are perfectly proportioned, with just the right amount of cheese, mayo, and pickles, all nestled in a soft brioche bun. While the egg is optional, the thick, peppered bacon is non-negotiable and adds an irresistible smokiness. In a city where dining excellence is the norm, Au Cheval's burger is a sinful pleasure that stands out in the bustling culinary landscape.

So it's important not to judge the food by the outside of a place and good thing. This place was pleasantly a great hot pot place. All you can eat. Check off what you want on menu and it is brought to you. Got pork broth base and mild spicy which was just right for me. Ate everything. Free drinks or cans of soda and good array of ice cream flavors for dessert.

CASH ONLY!! CASH ONLY!! CASH ONLY!! CASH ONLY!! CASH ONLY!!Located downtown Manhattan this place will be a parking nightmare if you are driving this way, specially during the day times. So do yourself a favor and catch a shared ride, do not spoil your day and meal on a insatiable quest for parking, and even if you find it, it will not be free, trust me. Went here with a friend so he already knew what I was going to eat, I was glad to be honest since it is a difficult menu if you are not used to this cosine.ROTI CANAI-  thin pancake with chicken curry dip. Amazing!!! the pancakes are super crispy and at the same time they are fluffy and fun to dip in the chicken curry. there's plenty of curry for all pancake. HAINESE CHICKEN-  This chicken comes at room temperature and it looks like it is a boiled chicken that is cooled imediately after cooking. to be honest it was not for me this dish, it is very popular though so I guess it is just a mater of personal taste. it is by no means a bad meal, it was just not for me. BEEF CHOW FUN- this is a like a stir fry, very nice, I was super glad we got this guy, it was salty yet not too much, it went perfect with rice and the noodles we got, this was just perfect protein choice.MALAYSAN COFFEE- it was ok, but not comparable to the Thai tea. I think I was ok trying it but again it was not something I will be having again. overall this is a very popular and busy restaurant, they have many featured dishes that are very popular. This is definitely a good place to try and visit if you are around the area.

Food purists need not apply, the trend of using Mexican food as a vehicle for wrapping other cuisines (think sushi burittos, Filipino quesadillas and now Indian tacos) is reaching peak saturation in New York City, and people are rightfully eating it up.Places like Goa Taco and Tac N' Roll have already been in the asian-food-in-taco game for a while now, so I was curious to see what Taco Mahal would bring to the table. You have the option of a roti taco shell or a naan one, with roti being the obvious choice for its fried pillowy texture versus naan, which would be more akin to the sort of dough you get with a wrap. The roti is satisfyingly buttery but had less of the fried flavor I crave from the paratha you can get at Goa and Tac N' Roll. Of the handful of veggie options (which simply appear as one "Veggies of the day" line item on the menu, so you need to ask) I went with Saag Paneer and Chana Masala. The Chana Masala was pretty standard but the Saag Paneer was standout delicious. The spinach in it tasted so fresh and creamy, I would have gladly ordered several more.The side of rice and lentils was lackluster. Definitely better off ordering another roti or naan instead.

I recently tried the popular dry stir-fry trend at a local spot, reminiscent of Málà Project's offerings, where the concept is to pick your ingredients and spice levels for a custom meal. In my takeout experience, I selected seven ingredients, which cost between $3 to $6 each, totaling $28. I expected a hearty portion for that price, but was disappointed to find it comparable to a single entree at other Asian restaurants. While $28 could net me two main dishes elsewhere, here it barely made for one. Though I can't speak for the dine-in experience, as a takeout option, it didn't deliver value for money. Next time, I'd opt for a traditional menu item over the customizable pot, especially at this price point.

This place used to be my "Go - To" lunch spot but once ETC opened up they've been replaced. They get 4 stars in terms of appearance since everything is so clean and well laid out. Even when it's busy, it doesn't feel overcrowded and you can get by. Staff is very friendly. I'd say the best part to is their stir-fry station and their sandwiches. I'm totally bummed out that they got rid of the Mediterranean Station and replaced it with Melts. They're buffet looks enticing but they really get you on the price per weight. I'll end up walking away paying $14 for just a couple of items just because things like broccoli happen to weigh a lot. Their sushi rolls look enticing, but for what you'll end up paying, you're better off just going to a sushi place. This place definitely got overshadowed by ETC (see my review), which definitely beats them on price, variety, and the quality of their Asian Station. Also, the juice bar will bend you over for a few nutritious ingredients and vitamins that will leave you hungry one hour later.

Title: A Pho-tastic Experience at Cha Pa

As a connoisseur of Vietnamese cuisine, I've become a frequent patron of Cha Pa, nestled in the heart of midtown. This gem outshines its pricier neighbors, offering a wallet-friendly menu that doesn't skimp on flavor. Their lunch specials are a highlight, especially the banh mi, which I've savored in every variety – the traditional one stealing the top spot on my list, particularly when coupled with a creamy Thai iced tea or the robust Vietnamese iced coffee.

Appetizers here? Simply divine. The pork belly steamed bun and the summer and beef rolls are mouthwatering preludes to any meal.

The half banh mi, half beef pho special is a gastronomic adventure, although it’s been marred by a mishap with packaging—a sad sight as delicious pho broth arrived only half full.

While I relish their food, there's room for improvement on the service side. Customization seems to be their Achilles' heel – my banh mi often plays a game of mayo roulette, and my plea for a less sugary beverage is routinely overlooked.

Despite these hiccups, Cha Pa's flavors keep me coming back. It’s a 'pho'sure' bet for a delightful Vietnamese meal. Pho'reals.

I had a disappointing experience at this restaurant. Despite the freshness of the ingredients, both pita dishes I sampled lacked flavor. The seasoning on the steak missed the mark and the meat was tough, while the chicken was overcooked and dry. The pita bread itself was overly hard at the bottom, leading me to leave it uneaten. Additionally, my pick-up order was delayed by over 20 minutes. Unfortunately, I won't be giving this restaurant another try.

This place is a cheap and cheerful joint offering great Chinese roast meats amongst many others. Added bonus with it being an "A" rated restaurant by the health dept. Came here and picked up 1lb of char sieu (bbq pork), 1lb of siew yoke (roast pork) and 1lb of chicken. All to go and ended up being $24. There are no seats in the restaurant but you could always eat it at the park across the street if the weather is nice. Slight queue when I got there but it moved pretty quickly.

We were hungry after seeing a play ("To Kill a Mockingbird") so we looked on Yelp for nearby pizza places. Joe's was highly recommended so we walked a few blocks to this location. The long line was daunting, but we were assured by others ahead of us that it would move quickly--which it did. There were many interesting celebrity photos and testimonials to keep us entertained as we waited for our turn to try the famous pie. We got three slices--combo, fresh mozzarella, and pepperoni. THEY WERE DELICIOUS! The slices were quickly heated in s brick oven to be piping hot. The pizza slices and a bottle of water cost $17. Not bad. Next time I want to try their white cheese, regular cheese, and caprese pizza. There are several high tables and bars to eat in the restaurant. Or it's close enough to Times Square to eat while people watching. Many people said they were getting pizza to take back to their hotel. Great new favorite in NYC!Oh, and they're open until 3:30 a.m.  Wahoo!

Newly opened outpost of this restaurant had barely anyone inside on a Tuesday afternoon. Lots of tables to choose from, but decided on one of the bar stools instead.The first time I tried Whitman's was for one of their burgers (only okay). This time, opted for the Local Beer Sausage ($9) to go along with a craft beer ($8). Surprised by their beer selection, draft list is nominal though several interesting cans to choose from. As for the food, sausage is giant - served with a side of onion, mustard, and greens. Meat was a solid compliment to the beer, and the mustard had just the right kick. The greens that it came with were dry and were only in the way.Service started off slow but picked up as I was finishing. Good spot for lunch, could see it getting busier.

Finally, I've been waiting to try this place for months! Perfect time to catchup with my old colleague. Reserved our table for two, the restaurant has a chic ocean vibe (hence Mar lol) which I found to be really relaxing. You have the option of sitting at the bar which has a view of the gifted chefs while they're at work or dining at a table. The experience was wonderful from start to finish, I had to change our reservation since we ran a little late, the hostess was so sweet, made our changes without a hitch. When I arrived first she smiled when I gave her my name and was so cordial as she walked me to our table. Since I arrived first I ordered a glass of Cava which was perfectly poured. We started with the Tun rojo balfego, made with Bluefin tuna, served with mini toast.... all I can say is wow!! Both of us did not want to stop and when it was gone, we could have ordered another!  For our mains, my friend ordered the squid with black ink, beautifully prepared. When our waiter delivered it, he says gently may I serve you! I just love great customer service, both my friend and I giggled well of course and thanks so much! I enjoy eating out a lot, and waitressed throughout undergrad. It's takes great skill to make to someone feel at home and our waiter did just that throughout our entire experience. I decided on the pescado a la plancha con patatas panadera, incredible! Beautifully prepared, buttery with a light crisp beneath it sits delicate, thinly sliced potatoes!! This was crazy, taking a bite of the fish with the potatoes was like a piece of heaven! We of course had to try dessert so we decided to share the mini lionesas. Perfect to share, served with a molten chocolate sauce.... whew obviously I will need to be come back soon! Mar was lovely from start to finish. Enjoy your experience!

I recently dined at this gem serving scrumptious Thai cuisine at very reasonable prices. Despite being situated in a somewhat dark and cramped basement setting, the authentic flavors and skillful use of spices completely overshadowed the ambiance. The staff were both friendly and efficient, ensuring a pleasant dining experience. With drinks included, our party of five paid a total of $200, which felt quite fair for the quality of food we enjoyed. A delightful spot for those prioritizing taste and value.

Was in town visiting some friends and they mentioned how much they missed this Thai place when they used to live in Manhattan. Since we were near by we decided to go even though my husband is not a big fan of Thai food. From the start I was very pleased, the interior is very nicely decorated and they have used their space very efficiently. We ordered a lunch special that came with soup and a choose of a small appetizer on the side and then an entree. Everything was amazing!! Also ordered the Thai tea and it was perfect. My husband ended up loving everything he ordered. Highly recommend!! I don't think you can go wrong with any dish.

After dining at Balthazar on two consecutive days thanks to generous clients, I can confidently say their sandwiches are a delight, particularly due to the freshness of their bread—though it does have a short shelf life. The cinnamon donut was a stand-out treat, incredibly yummy. The brownie bites fell into the realm of mediocrity, while the cookies, despite a satisfying taste, were too crunchy for my preference as I lean towards softer varieties. I'm intrigued to explore more of their menu options in the future.

Went on a Wednesday after work with friends, got sat right away. Food came out super fast! Big portions, I had enough to take home. And only paid $10! Update: came again and got the chicken pho, which is still severed in beef broth. It comes in a medium size bowl and I don't know how I even finished it, its huge!

This is a full blown LIVE yelp documenting my Pondicheri experience. Pondicheri came highly recommended to me from my homegirl Yuli. Shoutout. I just left the store and the girl working (wish I had gotten her name) was epic and helped me select the Lamb Keeba with Quinoa as well as the Besan Ladoo chocolate ball (both gluten free). First off, the service was impeccable and very friendly. Food came out in about 5min and was packaged beautifully as you will see in the photos. Place is clean with a pretty preparation display window of the food and a welcoming environment for sitting and eating in house. I also had Ladoo ball in house while I waited for my food and it was incredible. Didn't know "chickpea fudge" existed. One of the first things I can say is wow, unbelievable portion size. I envisioned this being a 5 star review with a portion size disclaimer but this container of lamb is outstanding. Not only that, but I have 4 side sauces, 2 of each (yogurt and cilantro chuntey sauce). Bear in mind I didn't ask for either ! Virtually unheard of. In my head right now I'm primarily pondering if I'm gonna finish this or not - which is a truly crazy thought. Normally I'm pondering what my next food intake will be because the meal I'm having isn't enough. Now this is different than being at a concert and filming the whole thing on your phone, just an FYI. Yes I might be slightly distracted from my food by my review but I'm also enhancing my food experience but carefully analyzing each bite and the full experience. Just wanted to note this. Anyway, I'd say I'm about halfway thru now. Going great. Using the 2nd sauce containers now. Yogurt is perfect here and the indian quinoa is amazing. Looks like I won't be using the full 2nd sauces but I think that's okay. You also gotta love food that takes time to eat, a rarity in nyc. Thankfully I'm at my desk so not feeling the pressure of rushing back to the office but this review started like 15min ago so I'm really taking my time out here. One thing I haven't made note of yet is the egg in the dish. Nice little touch and quality egg. Also the white stuff between the egg, salad, and the quinoa - not sure what it was but very dank. So I'm wrapping up now. One downfall of a live review is not aftermath review. Aka if I got food poisoning that would blow.  I like this place a lot so I'm putting faith in them to release this review prior to evaluating that. Overall, 10/10 meal. Little stuffed and could use a nap but need to keep striving for greatness out here. Happy Friday fam

Title: Pleasant Early Dinner Experience with Room for Improvement

My dining experience at this restaurant started on a positive note, with an early dinner seating that was efficient and satisfactory. The front-end team made a great first impression with their pleasant and professional demeanor.

We kicked off our meal with an appetizer of crostini featuring crab and sheep ricotta, which were truly outstanding, setting high expectations for the courses to follow. 

Unfortunately, the lamb sliders that came next fell short, being too soft and lacking in flavor, a disappointment for our palates. 

The wine list also proved to be a letdown, with a scant selection of quality choices under $100, which was surprising given the expectation of finding a nice bottle at this price point. 

The pasta course, featuring both Malfide and Parcheri, was competent, though they didn't stand out in the competitive Manhattan food scene. 

Despite being full, we noted that the chicken and steak come highly recommended, so we might opt for one of those on a return visit. 

In summary, while the meal had its highlights, notably the crostini, there are areas that could use enhancement to truly make this restaurant a standout.

I really wanted to enjoy this meal but everything was just ok. We had the following:-prawn and cod dumplings: these were interesting, but a little mushy on the inside probably because of the cod. The dipping sauce was very good but I probably wouldn't get this again.-salmon and tuna tartar: this was ok. I like this dish better at morimoto because it comes with a bunch of garnishes. This was pretty plain. -yellowtail sashimi with ponzu sauce: this was pretty good and the sauce made the dish.-corn: I really enjoyed this side dish. It was very interesting.-spicy beef tenderloin: this dish was just ok. The beef was cooked perfectly but the sauce was a little too sweet. -sea bass: this dish was very good and I would recommended getting this. The sauce was really good.-toro sushi: this was very expensive and not that good. My husband said he prefers the toro at our local sushi restaurant better and it's about 1/3 of the price.-spicy tuna roll: this was mostly filled with tempura crunchies rather than fish (you can even tell in the pictures). It also didn't taste that fresh. I wouldn't recommend. -mango and raspberry sorbet: the raspberry sorbet was my favorite but the mango was also really good.-the cocktails are also great!I did enjoy trying this restaurant, but I'm not rushing to come back

Great place for a steak dinner. Dined there several times on a Friday nite which I've found to be a less busy nite. Ordered the sirloin and ribeye... perfectly cooked as usual. Friendly and attentive staff. And as always, they gladly accepted my Living Social coupon. Will definitely come back again.

I don't really think there is much to say about Kati Shop other than THIS PLACE IS AMAZING. Sometimes words can not properly articulate the way we feel about a certain thing. Thus is true for me about Kati Shop. It's amazing. It's delicious. It's a hit!

This review is for a private party here!It was in a room with A/V set up (but it was quite loud from the adjoining party) and was very private. They had a prix fixe menu with house red or white wine. I have no idea about the price as someone picked the tab thankfully (it is a pricey place I know)The food was excellent and the service was great. I think the manager (assumption though) checked in on us a couple of times too.I started with the multigrain toast with avocado on top and then some crabmeat with pickled something something. Every bite of that appetizer was delicious. And not because avocados are my favorite thing. Because the crabmeat complemented the avocado texture along with the crunch from the toast. Yummy! (I am going to try and re-create this in my kitchen shh)Disclaimer before entree: I'm a picky duck confit eater. I don't like my dick rubbery as is very easy to do with a confit gone wrong. This confit was so beautifully done with the crispy skin outside and the tender perfectly cooked meat inside. It came on a pesto-y base with veggies and beans. Again, kudos to the chef for pairing the confit with that base. Absolutely delicious!The dessert was interesting. Almond something something- what I tasted was almond flour based hybrid between pudding, custard and cake. Yes, it is scrumptious. It came with these liquor infused cherries (was that kirsch btw?) that were probably too alcoholic for everyone else (just a heads up). I made sure i took a bite of my dessert along with that cherry (hoping that's how it was designed to be eaten). Beautiful place, fancy with a casual vibe, definitely will be back :)

Title: A Pleasant Surprise: Discovering a Culinary Gem

Last night, our original dining plans fell through when our intended restaurant unexpectedly closed early. As we wandered the neighborhood in search of an alternative, we came across a quiet yet inviting eatery that beckoned us inside.

Our meal began with a delightful complimentary hummus and pita bread plate, which set a high standard with its unmistakable freshness and rich flavor. While the chicken Adana did tip the scales towards being overly salty, the accompaniments of babaghanoush and Turkish eggplant sauce were savory highlights, complementing the main course nicely.

One of the most satisfying aspects of this impromptu dining experience was the portion sizes – generous by city standards, especially given the reasonable pricing. It's a welcome change to enjoy a hearty meal without the nagging feeling of overpaying.

In conclusion, what started as a change in plans led us to uncover a restaurant that serves up satisfying dishes with a side of good value. This spot may have been plan B, but it delivered an experience that could easily become a regular go-to for those in the area.

Whenever hunger pangs hit me during the wee hours in Koreatown, BCD Tofu House is my sanctuary. Their array of side dishes never disappoints, offering a perfect prelude to the main act - a sizzling bowl of flavorful tofu soup that's simply divine. The impeccable taste and comfortable atmosphere make BCD an essential stop for any late-night foodie.

Title: A Pasta Lover's Paradise

I recently dined at a fantastic restaurant that is perfect for pasta aficionados seeking a touch of elegance. Imagine an upscale version of the well-known Italian chain (you know the one), boasting endless pasta and breadsticks. The comparison is merited, yet this establishment stands a notch above.

The dining experience was delightful, especially as a prelude or finale to a Broadway show, enveloping you in the vibrancy of the city. The popularity of the restaurant is evident, with every seat often filled, so reservations are a must to avoid disappointment.

Despite the bustling atmosphere, the service remained impeccable, with staff members ensuring a memorable and efficient experience. It's worth the visit for the seamless blend of fine dining and the comforting indulgence of a hearty Italian meal.

There were rumors flying around that the Mac and cheese burger was a must-try and BOY it didn't disappoint! I went here with my family a while back. It was a very welcoming casual atmosphere with dim lighting and cool wallpaper. The Mac and cheese burger was amazing and I suggest you try it!

As the summer season comes to a close, I'd be remiss not to recommend the hidden gem that is the seasonal special at this restaurant: the green tea watermelon noodle. A delightful and refreshing dish, it's a must-try for those warm days, yet it's not listed on the menu, so be sure to ask for it explicitly.

Additionally, even as someone who typically steers clear of beer, I found their matcha beer slushie surprisingly delightful. It's the perfect balance with a slushie layer on top that complements the drink wonderfully. Don't miss the chance to savor these summer specialties before they're gone!

Entwine proved to be a delightful find on Yelp when I was in a pinch to locate an affordable, yet charming, venue for a bridal shower. Nestled in the heart of the Village, this gem offers a quaint, mismatched decor that exudes a homey vibe, especially in the sparsely decorated backyard which is perfect for a low-key gathering.

Happy hour visits sold me on the atmosphere; it's like cozying up in a friend's living room rather than a bustling city bar. While we faced minor bumps during the reservation process, the accommodating staff smoothed things over by generously extending our reservation time at no extra cost.

On the day of the event, the welcoming team at Entwine allowed us to personalize the space with our decorations, adding a special touch to the celebration. The vibe was complemented by their excellent music selection, enhancing the relaxed ambiance the bride-to-be cherishes.

In essence, Entwine is an ideal spot for those seeking a comfortable venue in the city that feels like a well-kept secret. Its delicious food, warm staff, and distinctive atmosphere make it a venue worth visiting for any casual occasion.

Title: A Cozy Spot for Ramen Lovers

After a visit to the Vessel, I stumbled upon a quaint ramen gem. Its small and welcoming interior is paired with a rather limited seating arrangement which, I must say, may require a bit of a wait, as I noticed several eager patrons lined up outside.

The menu boasted a good variety of choices, though it's worth noting that the prices lean towards the higher side. I chose the spicy pork bone ramen and it didn’t disappoint; the broth was rich in flavor, perfectly balanced in saltiness, yet I found myself craving more heat.

This isn't a venue for lingering conversations; the bustling atmosphere and tight seating clearly cater to a quick turnover. Despite the pricing, the quality could beckon me back to try another bowl, but perhaps on a less crowded day.

Title: A Spicy Delight at a Cozy Hotpot Hideaway

Upon entering the compact yet well-designed hotpot establishment, I was greeted immediately by a quaint bar with limited seating. Past the bar, a narrow walkway lined with round tables led us to our seats, with additional space available at the back catering to both small and large parties.

The service was impeccable. Our waiter exhibited a thorough understanding of the menu and adeptly guided me, a hotpot novice, towards the classic offering: a spicy pot flanked by a milder, non-spicy broth for seafood, fish, and vegetables. The spicy broth tantalized the taste buds with the perfect balance of heat and numbing sensation, while the herbal non-spicy version complemented the ingredients without overpowering them.

Opting for the Tang deluxe combo at $80, the selection presented exceptional value—featuring Kobe beef, abalone, and more. The meal was interactive, encouraging us to summon our attentive waiter to add to our feast as desired.

A lychee with rose cocktail, whose name eludes me, served as a sweet interlude to the savory fare, although the lychee purée leaned towards the sweeter side. The meal concluded with a complimentary dessert, leaving no room for guilt, only satisfaction.

In sum, this hotpot spot offers a great meal with exceptional service—a place I eagerly anticipate revisiting.

Came on a Friday evening for dinner with no reservations. I was pleasantly surprised the wait wasn't too long for a party of 5. While waiting for our table, I decided to grab a Tom Collins at the bar. Very refreshing and the gin to club soda ratio was just right. Once seated, it took f o r e v e r for our waitress to come by our table. By the time she came over, we were more than ready to place our order. Throughout our meal she was nonexistent...you basically had to glare at her in order for her to come to our table.I had the Po' boy lobster roll which came with a side salad and French fries. Decided on this roll as the lobster was prepared differently than your typical lobster rolls. Hey...anything fried is good, right?! Wrong. The lobster was rubbery and the cornmeal crust lacked flavor. The remoulade sauce wasn't spicy as advertised and boy was there a lot of it at the bottom of my brioche roll, making it somewhat soggy. I appreciated the extra crunch from the homemade pickles, but felt the lettuce, tomatoes, and onions didn't add to the roll. Both the salad and fries were okay...nothing special. Maybe I picked the wrong entrée here, but man, fried lobster never again. For those who are parents, note there is no kids' menu here. You'll have to order a regular entrée or settle just with a side of fries. C ended up with the original burger, which again came with a side salad and fries. For $20, this burger was huge at 10oz, but definitely not for a toddler. Not sure why they can't offer the 6oz burger (included in the Combo for 1) as a kid's meal option for a more reason price.My first experience at Burger & Lobster was a bust, so unfortunately won't be returning when I'm back in NYC.

Title: Cozy Sushi Spot in Manhattan with Room for Service Improvement

I recently dined at a charming, compact sushi restaurant recommended by a sushi-loving friend. As a sushi novice, I was eager to dive into the experience. The ambiance of the place is unmistakably 'Manhattanesque' with its small size, comfortably accommodating about a dozen diners.

The cleanliness of the venue was apparent, and the menu prices aligned with typical Manhattan establishments. I opted for a simple meal of steamed broccoli, salmon sushi, and a delightful mochi ice cream to finish. The food was served promptly and met my expectations in taste and presentation.

However, the service left something to be desired. The staff, while not overtly rude, didn't exude warmth or attentiveness. My waiter, in particular, seemed indifferent to our presence, failing to check in on our table or respond to attempts to catch his attention for the check.

Nonetheless, the quality of the meal would entice me to return when in the neighborhood, though I'll temper my expectations for service. It's worth noting that while this eatery has its merits, it isn't the only sushi game in town—a consideration for those who value customer service as part of their dining experience. Solid 4 stars.

My recent visit to the local bar was decidedly average. The self-service set-up was hassle-free, requiring patrons to fetch their orders from the bar. I opted for a beer while my companion selected wine, which was curiously served in a standard cup instead of a wine glass. Although not a deal-breaker, it was a slight letdown.

We chose to snack on fries, but found that not only were they limp rather than the expected crispy texture, but the establishment also charges extra for dipping sauces - an unwelcome surprise. As for the ambiance, it was unexpectedly quiet for a 6pm visit with sparse patronage.

The bar did boast a laid-back feel with entertainment options like a large Jenga set and arcade games to engage guests. However, a major low point was the restroom facilities, which were in a deplorable state, suggesting a lack of regular cleaning.

In summary, while the experience wasn't dreadful, it was far from impressive, with several areas in need of improvement.

Parlour stands out as a quintessential dining experience on the international culinary scene. Nestled in the vibrant IWS of NYC, this eatery exudes a classic charm that transcends trends. The absence of White Claws on the menu is a minor oversight, eclipsed by the stellar quality that consistently earns Parlour a resounding five stars.

Title: A Slightly Bumpy Start to a Flavorful Evening

Last Friday night's visit to the restaurant began on an odd note, as we encountered a peculiar seating hiccup despite numerous vacant tables. We were initially denied immediate seating for two and had to wait for a text from the hostess informing us of a shared table available minutes later—a confusing scenario, to say the least. 

Once seated, the experience took an upward turn with excellent service from our attentive server. The beverage menu was satisfying, though the drinks could have benefited from a more generous hand with the spirits. 

Culinary highlights included the crispy fish tacos, which lived up to their reputation, and the Chile relleno taco was a delightful surprise that truly impressed. Although the tacos were slightly on the pricey side at $4-5 each, they were well-executed and flavorsome. 

My companion enjoyed the chicken taco; however, the pork version failed to impress due to its dryness. The side dishes we selected—chips with salsa, beans and rice, and corn esquites—were a mixed bag. The corn and chips were definitely worth a reorder, while the beans and rice were average, leaving me wishing I had opted for another taco instead.

In conclusion, after navigating an initial snag, we were treated to a tantalizing meal that would warrant a future visit, armed with the knowledge of which dishes truly shine.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience at Club A Steakhouse

My boyfriend and I stumbled upon Club A Steakhouse during our New York trip, prompted by its stellar Yelp reviews. We were lucky to visit during restaurant week, which added to our excitement. I indulged in a caesar salad that was flavorful, a surprisingly generous petite filet mignon cooked to perfection, and a cheesecake that won over even my usual disinterest in the dessert. My boyfriend ventured into steak tartare, finding it the ideal introduction at a steakhouse, followed by a satisfactory hangar steak. However, he too was swayed by the exceptional cheesecake, preferring it to his profiteroles.

Our waiter was the epitome of hospitality, contributing to the venue's enchanting ambiance. It was a flawless dining experience, one that thoroughly impressed us both. Club A Steakhouse, with its commendable cuisine and atmosphere, earned our genuine appreciation. We left with nothing but praise and full stomachs, glad to have picked it for our dinner.

Title: A Homely Gem with Hearty Flavors

I stumbled upon this gem last night and was immediately taken with its "down home" vibe. The interior is adorned with stunning murals of notable African American figures, adding a meaningful and artistic backdrop to the dining experience. 

The jerk chicken I tried did veer towards the dry side but was redeemed by its exceptional seasoning - a true flavor explosion. The mac & cheese, on the other hand, was nothing short of phenomenal, a testament to a recipe perfected with love. The mashed potatoes were another highlight, deliciously thick and buttery.

Adding to the charm, the drink options like Uptowns and the Kool-Aid of the Day with its classic sweet kick reminded me of home. This place is unapologetically simple, embracing its no-frills atmosphere to deliver good, soulful food.

During our New York City tour, we made a stop at a bustling barbecue restaurant that left a fantastic impression on everyone. The chicken and ribs were a hit, with the shrimp and French fries being equally delectable. The portions were generous, ensuring no one left hungry. If you're a barbecue enthusiast, this spot is definitely worth a visit.

This place is small and honestly you can easily pass it but the food is actually really good and the staff is nice and attentive. Came hear looking for food and I got it. I got chicken fajitas which were reasonably priced and equally delicious. For drinks I got water and decided to partake in a pina colada. The pina colada was great too. I would definitely be back if I am ever in the area.

Title: A Hello Kitty Surprise with Delectable Delights

My friend and I initially ventured into this Hello Kitty-themed eatery with eyes for the infamous Hello Kitty buns, which charmed our taste buds with their yolky custard filling. But, oh, were we in for a delightful surprise! The ambiance was the first hint that we had stumbled upon something special - modern and refreshing, a departure from your typical Chinatown vibe.

While the Hello Kitty buns were a hit, it was the culinary tapestry that truly won us over. The Roast Duck Matcha Buns were a unique treat, marrying the subtle notes of matcha with savory duck - a must-try for the adventurous palate. The Dim Sum Sampler arrived in a traditional bamboo steamer, presenting an adorable and scrumptious variety.

The Shrimp Pad Thai, though, was the dark horse of the meal. Surprisingly phenomenal, it featured well-balanced flavors and generous, perfectly cooked shrimp. It's a dish that warrants a repeat order. And let's not forget the Roast Pork Buns - these beauties could rival any found in Chinatown!

In summary, this spot is a gem that's redefining where to find exceptional dim sum and Asian flavors. It's about time we got such a treasure uptown. I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Cheers indeed!

Title: A Gossipy Good Time at Tsismis NYC

Walking into Tsismis is like being enveloped in a warm embrace, with a staff that greets you like an old friend and only gets friendlier as the meal progresses. The hospitable environment was only the beginning, as the wonderful hostess who seated us quickly transformed from a stranger to a companion by the time we said our goodbyes.

I had the unique pleasure of being introduced to Chef Jappy, thanks to my dining partner, which led to an extraordinary culinary journey through nearly the full spectrum of their offerings. If your eyes happen upon anything fried on the menu, consider it a must-have. The Tinapa Croquettes are a sublime example—crispy on the outside, savory and comforting on the inside. Vegetarian dishes shine just as brightly here, especially the vibrant Kale Liang, which delivers both on taste and texture.

Pork enthusiasts, rejoice and indulge in any of the pork selections—each dish is a testament to Tsismis's deftness with this succulent meat.

Admittedly, the vegan options are few, which leaves room for the menu to grow and accommodate diverse dietary preferences. That said, with the delightful dining experience I had, I'm eager to return and witness the menu's evolution. Tsismis isn't just a place for food; it's where every meal feels like a hearty conversation with good company.

We had little time after we got home from work to freshen up then scram to Chelsea for a bite to eat, then pound to Ephrat Asherie's performance over at The Joyce Theater on a Wednesday. I really had my sights on Jungle Bird's gorgeous design, menu and cocktails (for hubs)- but it was packed- both at the Bar and regular seating. Next.Located a couple of doors down though from The Joyce Theatre, Cooper's was seriously a great hit coming through on ALL levels. Cooper's style has lots of natural raw wood, and beams at the bar. Ladies & gents restroom are downstairs with utility sinks outside of them. Ladies room is small but makes up with a chic and rustic style to it. Interestingly enough- Cooper's menu is VERY diverse and accommodates every palate. Because the performance started within 30 minutes from the time we sat, there was no time to shoot the breeze. Hubs explained to our server- who was sooo understanding- we had a show to attend and asked which menu items had less prep time and she suggested Pretzel Rods and Truffles Fries. Let's just say- Pretzel Rods had the right amount of coarse salt- plus they had a slight crunch with chewy goodness and Truffle Fries were delicious- wished I had another bowl.Cocktails and Mocktails? Check! I asked and our server quickly mentions a Moscow Mule. Even regular Moscow Mules weren't my thing- but awesome Cooper's had a Moscow Mule Mocktail choice and not the mundane Mojito Mocktail. By the way- my Mule was tight and was taken to a new dimension even down to the Candied Ginger on top! Place had the right amount of good vibes and music was cool with some Indie Rock going on! Everything- and I mean everything worked out fine. Thanks to our server who was so point with timing!

Title: Quirky Pig-Themed Spot with Killer Margaritas

We swung by this vibrant spot for pre-dinner drinks and were immediately taken with its expansive space adorned in pig and bacon-themed decor. Despite the moderate bustle, the atmosphere was inviting.

Our thirst was quenched by the audaciously named "Shut the f$#% up" margarita, which proved to be as potent as its name suggests, even with premium liquor. The habanero margarita followed, delivering a satisfying spicy zing.

Bartender Niko ensured our experience was top-notch, and the entire staff was on-point with their attentiveness. While we passed on food this time, the chicharron nachos at a neighboring table caught our eye (and came highly recommended).

With an amusing and lively ambience, plus the intrigue of bacon-infused concoctions, this place is certainly on my radar for a return visit. Highly recommend for a fun outing and a mean margarita.

Can I just say the service was quite wonderful. Genuine Southern Indian earnest politeness. Missed the thali window by a good 40 minutes. When I enquired about it, the waiting staff asked me to call before coming next time so that they can save the food for me. Very sweet! We ordered Gongura chicken and Spicy fish curry with rosemary naan and onion kulcha. I liked them all. My bf wished the Gongura wasn't blended to a purée, had to agree with him. Technically, the leafy part of the dish - Gongura is only coarsely mashed which gives a different texture to the dish. Nevertheless, it was a good experience. Will return and try thali next time

Title: Crispy Delight in a Cozy Corner

We decided to brave the Friday night crowds and arrived at 7 pm, pleasantly surprised to be seated within 15 minutes despite the bustle. A heads-up for future diners: the seating arrangement is quite snug. But any concerns about comfort are quickly forgotten when the food arrives.

We kicked off with the burrata appetizer, which was a creamy dream, elevated by a tangy balsamic glaze and the sweet freshness of heirloom tomatoes. For our main course, the pizza did not disappoint. We chose a half-and-half pie: half original, half "tri pie." The crust was phenomenally thin and crispy, a feat of culinary magic that maintained its shape with no droop.

For those familiar with Rubirosa's thin crust, this spot offers a similar, yet distinctly worthwhile experience. All in all, it's a must-visit for pizza connoisseurs, and every minute of the wait is rewarded with flavor-packed bites.

Cosy little gem with a wide variety of sake. Don't know much about sake? No worries - the menu include a brief description of the drink, flavors and if the drink is bubbly. Other than sake, they serve shochu, cocktails and whiskey too. I went with a big group on a holiday eve - it was crowded but they managed to give us a seat within 10 minutes. I would go back to try out other types of Japanese liquor!

During my recent solo lunch at Speedy Romeo, I gave their menu another go and was pleasantly surprised by the improvement since my initial visit. Opting for the pizza topped with mushrooms and egg proved to be a delectable choice. However, I couldn't help but desire a lunch special similar to what Motorino offers, particularly as the prices here lean towards the higher side. Despite that, the quality of the meal was undeniable.

Here's the thing. You don't go to the Tick Tock because you're looking for a gourmet meal or to impress a date. You're not going there because they make the best this or the best that. Frankly, except for their mac and cheese balls (which breaks every carb rule and diet on this planet), you probably are not going to remember exactly what you had there when you went. You go to the Tick Tock because it's 40 minutes before the movie starts at AMC across the street and you want to grab a quick burger. Or you go there because you got out of the movie at 11 p.m. and you're craving something and don't want to go running around town looking for a place to eat.The Tick Tock is simply a long-standing NYC diner that happens to be better than most, and extremely conveniently located.When I went a few weeks ago it was because it was 10 degree weather and I was catching the opening of a play three blocks away and I didn't want to be walking around so I picked it because I literally came up out of the train station and walked three feet into the diner.Now, the other night after we had been out helping the homeless for four hours our crew balked at going there fore to chill because after being out in 10 degree weather, no one wanted to eating overpriced food that was mediocre at best.It is, what it is, and that's what makes it great.Plus, the staff is always friendly and happy to serve.

If you're looking for a fast, reasonably priced, delicious lunch, this place is it!  You can choose your base of white rice, brown rice, and salad and add toppings. The toppings are beautiful, varying from purple hued pickled onions, lemongrass, bright shredded carrots, mellow cucumbers, and more. They make a pretty bowl for your camera to eat before you dig in :)  the veggies are pretty much all pickled, so the bowl has a lot of sour/pickle to it. Keep that in mind when choosing your toppings. The grilled chicken was super flavorful, and the sauces added even more of a punch!  Deeeelicious :DThey have a communal table, a high table by the wall with seating, and a few window seats.  Lots of people were coming in and out for takeout. It can get busy during the lunch rush, but there was always a few seats available. On a side note, skip the kimchi and avocado unless you'll die without them; the kimchi is $1 extra and the avocado (a mere 2 slices!) is an extra $1.50.  Enjoy!

Title: Perfect Spot for Happy Hour and Sports Enthusiasts

If you're looking for a place with tasty bar food and an excellent selection of happy hour drinks, this is the spot for you. Arriving at 6 pm, the place was bustling with a lively and friendly crowd, creating a great atmosphere. With plenty of TVs strategically positioned, sports fans can catch all the action from any seat in the house. Definitely a go-to venue for a casual evening out with friends or to unwind after work.

Title: Airy Summer Spot for Groups, But Just Satisfactory Overall

Review:

"Eh" seems to sum up my experience at this Manhattan eatery. While the space shines in the summer—airy and able to accommodate larger parties, a real perk in the city—the restaurant doesn't quite hit the mark in other areas. Service was unremarkable, neither disappointing nor impressive. The prices, on the steeper side, likely reflect the premium of New York real estate rather than an exceptional dining experience. It's not a place I'd seek out on my own, but I wouldn't turn down an invitation if it came up. A solid 3/5 for being just okay.

Title: A Gastronomic Joy at Brontë's in New York

I recently dined at Brontë's, and it was an unforgettable experience that easily soared to the top of my New York dining list. The staff exuded warmth and the atmosphere buzzed with a vivacious energy that made the meal even more enjoyable.

My dining companion and I indulged in the Brontë burger and the creamy shrimp pasta. While both dishes were faultless, the Brontë burger stole the show with its juicy patty, a subtle hint of caramelized onions adding a touch of sweetness, and a bun that was toasted to perfection. The accompanying sweet potato fries and the harmonious aïoli were the cherry on top.

I can't recommend this place enough and the Brontë burger is a must-try. I'm already looking forward to bringing more friends to enjoy the remarkable flavors and delightful atmosphere at Brontë's. This isn't just a meal – it's a joyful celebration of good food and good company.

TLDR: Solid Italian restaurant in Midtown East. If you're in the area and are looking for just a good bowl of pasta or a savory meat entree - Toscana is a great choice.I worked in Midtown East for years and I just avoided this place for a long time. It just screamed tourist trap at me but somehow, I ended up here one day with coworkers. Boy, was I wrong.The restaurant has some outside seats for when it's warm but the inside tables are nice. I ended up eating here many times after the first because it was a place I could count on to satisfy my Italian cravings. There's a bunch of Italian restaurants in this area but most of them are just okay.The linguini alla vongole is very good. It's garlicky, not too much oil and very flavorful - most times I try this at other restaurants it's bland.For entrees, my goto has always been the Veal Saltimbocca alla Romana or the Chicken Scarpariello. Saltimbocca is a staple of Roman cuisine and this is the most authentic version I've tried in the States. The veal is pounded very thinly with the taste of the crispy prosciutto, the sage and that sauce reduction beneath. The Scarpariello here is just a bountiful plate of chicken and sausage, all mixed in with that roasted garlic, the white wine sauce.Toscana may look like just another New York Italian restaurant but it's actually a good one.

Title: A New York Sushi Gem that Exceeds Every Expectation

Upon entering the restaurant, I braced myself for the all-too-familiar letdown of New York eateries that don't live up to their hype. However, this sushi spot was a sublime exception. The sushi I savored here was not just delicious, but some of the best and freshest I've ever encountered—a true culinary revelation.

The crispy rice, in particular, was a standout dish. It found the elusive balance between moist and crunchy, paired with a sauce that can only be described as perfection on a plate. Each bite was an indulgent delight that left me craving more.

Accompanying my meal was the peachy lychee drink—an intoxicating blend of bold flavors and freshness, with a pleasant surprise of actual lychee nuts awaiting at the bottom. It was robust and refreshing, the perfect complement to an exceptional meal.

In a city teeming with dining spots, this restaurant sets the bar high with its unparalleled sushi and innovative drinks. It's a must-visit for any sushi aficionado in New York.

Title: A Long-Standing Favorite with Consistent Quality

I've been a loyal patron of this restaurant since 2009, and it has consistently remained one of my favorite places to dine. Despite transitions in the kitchen staff, the quality of the food has impressively maintained its high standards over the years. Among the menu's standout offerings, the pan-fried rice noodle drenched in a savory soy and luscious peanut butter sauce holds a special place in my heart; its flavors never cease to delight me, no matter how often I return. For anyone seeking a reliable and tasty dining experience, I heartily recommend giving this spot a visit. My enduring satisfaction earns it a solid 8/10.

Title: Authentic Japanese Breakfast with a Minor Letdown

I recently visited this restaurant for their famous Japanese breakfast set and walked away mostly satisfied. The highlights were unmistakably the mackerel fish (saba) and the perfectly cooked onsen egg, both of which were a delight to find outside of Japan and prepared with such finesse.

Unfortunately, the experience was slightly marred by the arugula salad, which lacked the fresh, peppery bite one would expect. The salad seemed like an afterthought, reminiscent of pre-packaged greens rather than market-fresh produce. Additionally, the presentation strayed from the traditional Japanese style - the mix of items on a single plate rather than in individual containers detracted from the authenticity of a 'set' meal.

On a more positive note, the iced barley tea provided a refreshing accompaniment, and the overall healthiness of the meal, coupled with attentive service and stunning decor, made for a very pleasant dining experience. Despite the minor setbacks, I would recommend giving this breakfast set a try, especially for those in search of a taste of Japan.

Beauty & Essex is nondescript from the outside, taking the guise of a jewelry shop. However, once you enter a door from inside the shop you are transported to a chic supper club. You really feel like you are entering somewhere exclusive.Attendants take your coat and you're directed to your table. This place so distinguished, you will feel like you're in a James Bond movie...especially looking up at that gorgeous skylight. The food was simple and sophisticated all at once:Roasted bone marrow: incredible. The shallot marmalade gave the marrow a savory sweetness. The Texas toast on the side was a welcome crunchy touch. Lobster mac & cheese: light with a kick. The lobster was tasty and they aren't shy with the portion.Double cut lamb chops: Jesus Christ, this lamb was cooked to PERFECTION. Nice crust on the outside, and inside was soft and juicy. Once you get the bone the flavors literally slap you in the face. The polenta underneath was creamy and seasoned.Grilled cheese, smoked bacon & tomato soup dumplings: these are popular and were highly recommended...for good reason. I'd wager to say this was the best thing on the table. This is an example of what I meant by simplicity and sophistication. Something as simple as grilled cheese and tomato soup was presented and tasted worthy of a dish from a Michelin starred restaurant.Beauty & Essex was really something special. Do take your loved one there for that special occasion. They won't dare forget it.

I just finish devouring my spring rice roll and got on to write this review, that's how good it is. It's been a while since I've been so inspired by the taste of something and felt the need to share it. All it was was one spring roll with scallion garnish, cold, no sauce.  At first I was thinking, this is going to be underwhelming but one bite in and I change my mind. It's beauty is that it's so simple but it packs a punch, unlike all the food out there that looks good but has no substance. Hak box did not come to play. The spring roll was so flavorful and delicious. I didn't expect it to be cold. At first I had my doubts that the rice roll texture would be too hard but it was perfect, fresh, elastic and chewy. It was filled to the max with scallions and baby shrimp and sesame on top, and with each bite all you can taste was flavor. There was no sauce, they knew how good it was and felt no need to add on a sauce to cover or enhance the taste. My only regret is that I only got one roll, but I'll def be back!!!

My family and I decided on this place for dinner, arrived just in time for happy hours so we sampled the Hell's Kitchen barbecue jumbo wings - they tasted a bit like Korean bulgogi bbq seasoning and had sesame seed toppings on it! The wings were good but the coleslaw provided with it was a bit too vinegar-y according to my family.Then our orders of burgers arrived and while the size portion was more than enough, the fries are not served with it so you must order the ones of your choosing (we chose a large fries and onion rings to share). I did think they were pricy just for the fact that you only were served the burger and nothing else (almost all of them cost ea. 15$The cancan burger was delicious albeit the peppercorn provided an interesting texture as the meat and mushroom were well seasoned with the Brie yet when bit into it, sometimes one would find the grittiness of the peppercorn which I was not particularly a fan of. The 5 napkin burger was great as well. I was told that the bacon cheddar burger was decent but that the only complaint my dad and sister had were that the choice of buns provided with it were not the best as they absorbed the moisture too much and became soggy and unappetizing afterwards. The atmosphere was very classy in a casual kind of way with outdoor and indoor seating - it did seem to me that they do not have tables for large parties as they had to place us at their only round "large" table when we were only a family of 5. The waitstaff was friendly though it seems that we arrived when they were preparing for a rotation change (they were having a meeting halfway through our dinner order) or something as we had to grab their attention multiple times to refill our water, ask for plates, etc. I noticed the bathrooms were kept clean and gender neutral as well as family friendly.

My evening at the new neighborhood gem was a serene delight, perfect for a cozy night out. The ambiance is charming with its simple decor and soft lighting. While the menu may be concise, what they do, they do well.

We started with the yuzu edamame and Japanese karaage, both appetizing in their own right. The edamame had a pleasant hint of yuzu, enhancing the experience without overwhelming. The fried chicken was a standout, perfectly juicy and wonderfully complemented by the unique matcha salt.

Their ramen selection caters to various preferences with fish, chicken, and mushroom bases, along with a curry noodle option. The Kyoto ramen, with its savory fish base, succulent pork belly, and perfectly cooked egg, was a bowl full of comfort, especially with the house spicy sauce adding a delightful zing. The Yokosuka curry mazemen offered a richer, non-soupy alternative with its coconut milk and green curry base, tagging along a unique flavor profile that's heartening in every bite.

Though they don't serve desserts, the culinary excellence presented suggests that any future additions to their succinct menu would be equally satisfying. This place is a must-visit for anyone in search of a tranquil dining experience with a side of seriously tasty food.

Title: A Mix of Elegance and Missteps at Posh Sushi Spot

Upon entering the restaurant, one is immediately struck by the posh ambiance, accentuated by large chandeliers and a striking bamboo-like ceiling covering. The restaurant wasn't overly crowded, yet our initial seating was disappointingly cramped; thankfully, the hostess reseated us at a more spacious round table upon request.

We started with a bottle of Wakatake sake, which regrettably arrived at an improper temperature but was promptly remedied with an ice bucket. The menu boasted a variety of appetizers and sushi meant for sharing—the standout being the koi sticky rice with tuna, though consistency varied between orders. The tuna tartare was a buttery delight, and the lobster mini tacos were quite satisfying.

While most signature sushi rolls were a hit, the rainbow roll and the yellowtail with scallions, the spider roll was a letdown—overly breaded and lacking in advertised fillings, eel, and shrimp. The staff handled our complaint professionally, removing the item without issue.

A management apology for the earlier oversights in the form of a complimentary bread pudding was a gracious touch. However, the steep final bill of $398 left a lingering sense of expectation for a more uniformly exceptional dining experience.

Had an impromptu  lunch date with my bestie who only eats Italian food so I knew I had to bring her to a gorgeous restaurant to try a new cuisine! I've read about their lunch special on Yelp before and never made it into the area at the right time to do it til now!The lunch special menu is awesome. You pay based on protein ($13-17) for a soup or salad, an appetizer & an entree! We both got the house salad with the yummiest peanut dressing. She opted for edamame and I got the dumplings that were soooo yummy. For entrees she got the sauteed beef in peanut sauce in the first section of entrees (maybe Pakaran... sorry lol) and I got the Massaman Curry with shrimps. Absolutely delicious! We had such a nice time  and I got a pot of beautiful blooming tea that they didn't charge me for ! They even let us sit after warning us the kitchen was closing for the staffs lunch break. We'll totally be back!

I feel there's a new Mexican spot popping up like in every NYC corner. Mexico Lindo in the Kips Bay area though, has been long-running...for 47 years! Lindo is more about comfort food. And by the way- it's far, far away from the whole farm-to-table flow, diet fads or the latest trends we all know. And if Tacos are what you're looking for- this isn't it. Instead, it's more entrees than anything else: stewed Fish, Shrimp dishes, meats, etc. Lindo's style is cozy, almost villa-style with brick walls showing through. Decent-sized dining space, small bar area at the far end and a cozier seating area with 26th St's side view. Aside from a few folks dining in the main area, we practically had the area to ourselves by the window side. Service was friendly from the guys on the floor and our server Ely. And let me not forget... Old school Salsa with Frankie Ruiz, Jerry Rivera and so many others- played throughout the night. Since I'm detoxing majorly, Tamarindo Juice was it- and boy....that sh*t was amazing! While hubs had the Sangria which he said was, "good". I really wanted to start with a Nopales salad- but none is available. Guacamole was freaking fresh though- but agree with someone else mentioning lots of chopped onions in it. My Camarones al Ajillo's were good. The hero-type bread was a bit unusual but hey...I dunked that sucker right in the garlic sauce (the hell with Keto!) and hubs liked his Chicken Fajitas with fresh veggies- down to the mushrooms. I don't mind coming back here. Seems like Mexico Lindo has a knack for serving it up real good...for this long in these parts.........despite their 3 & 1/2!

Came here for Sunday brunch at 11am and was told there's a 30minute wait, which turned into a 1hour 15 minutes wait for our group of 6. The wait sucks, but the food made up for it. The guy who comes out with donut holes for waiting customers made the wait a little better.- chicken and waffles: yum! 1 wing and 1 breast. Both chicken pieces were super crispy and not greasy. Came with 4 crispy waffles, syrup and 3 kinds of butter. Was a little worried about the small portion from reviews below but it turned out alrightz Portion was not huge but wasn't tiny either. Between this and the extra biscuits I got below, I wasn't able to finish my meal.- biscuits and gravy: another delicious dish. I got the chicken sausage gravy. Creamy gravy smothering warm, buttery, crumbly biscuits.- Bloody Mary: served with a piece of bacon, pepper and celery and rimmed with chili powder. Not bad.

my friend and I went here for dinner on a Sunday night. the place was pretty full but not completely packed - I'd say it was comfortably crowded. we were seated down pretty quickly, and they serve us Pao de Quejo right away (Brazillian cheese bread) an it tasted super good! service was good, friendly staffs, and very attentive. food were circulated very regularly there will be a small round paper next to you. put green side up when you want to be served and red side up when you've had enough. there is also a salad bar in the middle that serves various side dishes too and even sushi. i can't even remember what did I took but I tried so many and everything was good. even the sushi was good so i was surprised. we also ordered some side dishes - the fried banana is really good, the fried yucon flour is interesting to try, the polenta wasn't very good though (I'd rather fill up with something else)for the meat, the only one I don't really like is the flank steak. the others were good! I always ask for rare cut and they can deliver that. the notable ones are probably the ribs, ribeye, garlic steak, and platiformaby the way, dessert is not included in the AYCE package. i mean i'm already too full to get dessert anyway. plus the fried banana already tasted like dessert (and I'm not usually huge on dessert) but if you do want to try I think they have quite a variety of Brazillian dessert like Quindim, Brigadeiro, and various cakes. I wonder if I they have grilled pineapplehowever, honestly I think the price is a bit too expensive for the experience. for the meat only I wanted to give this place a 3.5, but with the service, side dishes, cleanliness etc I think it's worth rounding up to 4

When your friend, who knows Thai food says this place is Mommy approved, who am I to argue with experts.  To give some perspective, my friend's mom's palate is harder to please than my friend.Arrive here on a Monday afternoon for a late lunch, we sit in the last 2-seat tables.  Note: There are 5 2-seat tables and 2 4-seat tables.  There is a special lunch menu which consist of the traditional items.  My friend said no lunch menu, we are going for the regular menu.  We order: Crispy Spring Rolls (2): this is crispy on the outside and the vegetarian ingredients are hot.Chiang Mai Noodles: curry noodle soup with egg noodles, onions, thai pickles, cilantro. (Didn't taste this - have to try next time.)Yen Ta Fo Noodles: flat noodles with shrimp, squid, crispy tofu, shrimp ball, fried wonton and Chinese watercress in pink broth.  This soup was savory and so fragrant.  It made our neighbor table re-think their order.  I thought I couldn't finish this bowl but I couldn't stop eating it.  It was so good.Thai ice tea is on point.Have to come back and try more items!  You should try the noodle soups!

Recently visited this spot I found on Yelp for a team happy hour and it didn't disappoint! The shareable appetizers were a hit, especially the pizza and the 'home base platter'—a delicious combo of house-brined chicken nuggets, fried mozzarella balls, and beef sliders. An added bonus for our group was the free shot offered when we checked in on Yelp. While I haven't experienced their brunch, it's apparently quite the crowd-pleaser. I'll definitely be back to try that and would recommend this place for a fun, casual gathering!

So I'm not the biggest taco fan as nearly all of the tastes similar to me and most of the time they are great whether the authentic food truck kind or Taco Bell. With that said this place was the bomb.com There's a few key details. One is that the tortillas are hand made whether corn or flour. AMAZING. On top of the the meat is freshly greilled and you can taste it. SO SO good when you put those two elements together. Plus free guacamole.JEANS: OK by farORDER: at the counter then take your ticket to the taco assembly window where someone will take your ticket and make your tacos. Then viola.

Wow, this place sucks and does not come close to matching the hype. I'm giving it two stars only because they're not just serving up Impossible or Beyond burgers.I got the namesake superiority burger ($6), made vegan with different cheese and bun. This thing is small, more akin to a slider. The biggest problem, though, was the burger patty, which is mushy, starchy and bland. Frozen bean patties from the grocery store are better than this. The vegan cheese also tasted terrible and had the look and feel of plastic.The burnt broccoli salad ($4) was a bit better, with a nice interplay of cashews and vegetables. That said, they didn't integrate the sauce well---it was an ashen, lumpy thing at the bottom of the container.The space is tiny and has seating for maybe 5 or 6 people at most. If there's a line, do not bother coming here, because it's not worth it. If you still have morbid curiosity to try it, come off-hours.I applaud Superiority for trying to do something from scratch and not just serving up frozen food-tech from Silicon Valley. That said, Superiority has a lot of room for improvement. And it's not even vegan, which is also weird. It's 2019---vegetarian is dead.

Tucked away in the bustling streets of New York, we stumbled upon a culinary treasure that defies its modest exterior. This unassuming Korean eatery proved that appearances can be deceiving, delivering an unforgettable dining experience that outshone every expectation.

The bulgogi tacos were an infusion of traditional flavors packed into an innovative twist, making each bite a revelation. The fried pork dumplings were succulent, encased in a perfectly crisp shell that crunched satisfyingly with each mouthful. But the true star of the show was the crispy chicken buns – an impeccable blend of texture and taste that will linger in your memory long after the meal is done.

Even the spicy mayo was a standout, adding a punch of flavor that elevated the entire meal. This restaurant has set a new standard for what I consider to be the peak of New York's culinary scene.

Without a doubt, this place has earned itself a permanent spot on my itinerary for every future visit to the city. And with a menu still brimming with untried dishes, my taste buds are already tingling in anticipation. If you're in search of the best, look no further.
