Service is quick and food is mostly on point. Ramen is still best. Had the spicy classic and that's all I needed. Broth was rich and satisfying on a cold day. Chasu was tasty and a good bite. Next time I'll add egg and kaedama. Today was just what the doctor ordered

Nestled in the heart of the Lower East Side, open 24/7, is a gem of a spot for empanada enthusiasts. On a leisurely Saturday morning at 11am, my dining companion and I walked into a surprisingly empty and spacious eatery—serendipity for those who enjoy a quiet meal.

Eager to sample their array, we dove into an empanada tasting, each priced at an affordable $3.99. The shredded beef was a savory delight, the jerk and cheese a fusion of flavors, and the ham and cheese a classic done right. However, I'd steer clear of the spicy chicken— it didn't quite hit the mark.

Our indulgence continued with a hearty Cubana arepa at $9.50 and a generous portion of chicharrones for $13. The latter, served atop golden fried plantains, was a standout, offering a perfect blend of crispy and chewy textures. The arepa, while satisfactory, didn't dazzle as much as the chicharrones did.

In sum, this spot delivers on taste and value. It's a solid choice for anyone craving Latin American fare at any hour.

I've been hearing about this place for a while and finally was able to stop by. The restaurant is quite tiny, so be prepare to wait a bit, especially if you have a party larger than 2 on a Friday/Saturday night. I ordered the Killer Bee Pizza and it was amazing. It doesn't look like much, but the flavors are so unexpected and work so well together. The crust was light and fluffy and just how I like it! Service was quick once we were seated. It was about $20-25 for a personal pie, but it was worth the hype!

Title: Average Brunch in a Bustling SoHo Spot

I recently visited a SoHo eatery for brunch and had a pretty average experience. The restaurant's atmosphere was notably energetic, albeit very loud, making conversation a bit of a struggle - not ideal when trying to catch up with friends.

As for the meal, my burger was standard - cooked to a medium doneness as requested, yet it lacked any wow factor. The accompanying sauce seemed to be a lackluster mix of mayo and BBQ, which was a bit of a letdown. However, the fries were a high point; they reminded me of Popeyes' fries - crispy and nicely seasoned.

All in all, the place was just A-ok. Given the plethora of brunch options in SoHo, I might branch out to see what else is out there next time.

I was on town for a few days and Aunt Jakes was recommended to me by a friend. I took my mom and sister with me. We made early reservations (530pm) and the place was pretty empty and quiet. I usually eat an earlier dinner so this was perfect for us. We loved our experience here. Our server was fantastic. I wish I remembered his name. We all had a drink, wine or sangria. Followed by the burrata starter. We ordered the family size because the server said it was good for 3+ people. It was HUGE! BUt delicious. Light and airy burrata on top of toast with tomatoes. Delicious! Even though it was a lot we finished every last bit. Next was the pasta. I loved the concept of pick your pasta pick your sauce. It's as simple as that. I had the cavatappi alla vodka. Delicious. But next time I will chose a less dense noodle. The other pastas ordered were ravioli and cavatelli. Both great as well. They each got the roasted garlic pecorino white sauce (I can't remember the official name of the sauce on the menu). That was phenomenal. So good. I can't wait until I'm in town again and will definitely be back!

Disclaimer: I was invited to attend an event here with fellow yelp elite's. All items we had were complimentary and there was a space reserved for us within the restaurant beforehand.I, along with several other Yelpers were invited to Camellia for a complimentary dinner to try several of the items on their menu and allow an opportunity to give constructive criticism about the dishes. The restaurant recently opened about two months prior and they're still looking to refine a few things on their menu if necessary. We were told to order anything we'd like and that we sure did.When my friend and I first arrived we were able to start with a beverage. I decided to go with the mango passion tea with lychee jelly, apparently one of the owners favorites and I can definitely see why. It was AMAZING. Light and fruity without too many overpowering factors. It's the perfect summer drink.When it came time to order our food I went with the salt and pepper fried chicken for the appetizer and the stewed pork spare ribs ramen for my main. Both dishes were, in my opinion, excellent. The chicken wasn't too overcooked which gave it an easy to bite into texture and the sauce that accompanied it was equally great. The ramen was  my favorite thing from the evening. Beautiful broth, well cooked noodles, and meat that pulled from the bone effortlessly made for one of the best bowls of ramen I've ever had. The portion sizes for both were also generous.We all ended the night with a choice of their gelato. I went with the matcha which was sweet, but not so much so that it overpowers your taste buds. All in all a great spot on third avenue to visit if you're looking for guaranteed excellent ramen as well as a variety of tasty apps that'll definitely have you coming back sooner rather than later.

For someone who enjoys dining out a lot I've never had Cambodian food. We were looking to try something a little different and a quick search on the Michelin bib gourmand list led us to Angkor. We didn't have a reservation so we tried our luck by arriving around 6p on a Friday and we were pleasantly surprised that we were able to be seated immediately (albeit to a shared table with another couple). We ordered a few items off the menu, my favorites from top to bottom:- Green Curry: I've never had a curry where I've literally taken a spoon to the sauce and drank it like like a soup. The curry sauce was so incredibly delicious with the perfect level of heat. I've never had pumpkin in a curry before and it was so sweet which was the perfect offset to the heat of the curry. - Amok: Alright I'm never one to order fish at a restaurant because it will either be really good or really bad. Our server recommended this dish and I figured we should at least try one adventurous dish. The presentation was beautiful, a clay pot which was waiting like a gift to be opened. The fish was surprisingly tender and the added heat from the red curry sauce added an additional dimension of flavor to the dish.- Summer Rolls: I'm a sucker for these and order them 100% of the time if they are on the menu. - Old Fashioned Pudding: I'm not going to lie the corn in this dish was a little odd for me personally. I haven't traditionally eaten corn in desserts (so this was a first), but the corn was sweet and added overall texture to the sticky rice. I'd definitely try this out once but I probably wouldn't order it again if I came back. The condensed milk made the dish a little too sweet for me personally. Service was excellent here and we received a good amount of food for the price we paid for the entrees. Thank you for our server who took the time to explain the menu and what we should expect with our entrees. I will definitely be back!

Title: Fresh Poke Bowl in a Casual Setting

I decided to shake things up by using the MealPal app to discover a new dining spot and landed on a poke bowl place, feeding my current sushi and poke cravings. Upon entering, I didn't find the staff particularly welcoming, except for a friendly cashier who promptly processed my MealPal QR code and handed me my meal.

Today's choice was the poke bowl special, boasting fresh ingredients that were immediately noticeable. It differed from other venues in that it was more rice-heavy with fewer toppings, but for the area, it was satisfactory and offered a decent dining alternative. For those looking to stay, the place had plenty of seating to enjoy your meal on site.

Really enjoyed the appetizers (fennel salad and creme brulee). They were fresh and unusual dishes with amazing flavor. We both got the pasta in the wheel and that was cool - I like going to places with a unique element / gimmick. The pepper was a little overpowering and the pasta wasnt amazing but it was ok. They give you a large serving so you get your money's worth. We were too full to even consider dessert but looked at the menu anyway - nothing stood out enough to tempt us, which was just as well.

Had a reservation at 7PM which I made through Yelp on a saturday for one of my friend's birthday. I was running a little late about 15 minutes, but they still seated us once I got there. When I had made the reservation, it says they only hold the seats for about ten minutes after our reservation so I'm very glad they were still able to seat us. My friend and I both got the Douzo Set for 6 handrolls, priced at $35. I thought all the rolls tasted fresh and unique. My only critique would be that the seaweed wasn't that cripsy and soft for the beginning pieces. I usually love scallop but there is a bit of a crunch which I didn't particularly enjoy but my friend did. I think it just depends on the person. My favorite was the red snapper, as it had a yuzu flavor and it tasted very different, something I never tasted before. Service was great, as I did not feel rushed and our waitress checked up on us to see if everything was okay. Overall, I enjoyed the ambiance of this place and had a pleasant time with my friend. It's a bit more quiet, as compared to Kazunori, one of my favorites in nyc, as they specialize in hand rolls. They're both different in their own way. This place however, you do need to tip.

Tucked away in a cozy corner of Bryant Park, this dessert haven is a satisfactory spot for those with a sweet tooth. It might not blow your mind, but the convenience of grabbing a snack and lounging in the park is a definite plus. A tad on the expensive side, their sizable waffles are made for sharing and come with an array of toppings to choose from. Service is swift – a boon for anyone in a rush. Texture-wise, expect a pleasant contrast between the crunchy exterior and soft interior. Be warned, portions are generous, and finishing solo could be a challenge. In short, a good place for a quick and indulgent bite if you're in the vicinity.

Really loved the ambiance of this place - only complaint is that they advertise their happy hour A LOT and when we sat and asked for the deals, we were told they were only available if you were sitting at the bar (sad). We just got drinks and some appetizers, definitely a little expensive. The staff was really nice and gave us little pretzels in olive oil to snack on while sipping our drinks. Would be a nice place to go for a *little* fancy dinner.

Came to Don Antonio as it was my friend's recommendation for our lunch rather than it being on my list of pizza places to try during my trip to NY. I wasn't about to ignore his opinion, as he is a native New Yorker and a pretty decent foodie himself. Just had to prepare myself for the idea that this would not be a place for traditional pizza.Decided to be basic as hell and opted for the popular Montanara, which is the pie with lightly fried pizza dough. I found the pizza dough to be very soft and fluffy with a little crispiness due to it being lightly fried. The tomato sauce and smoked buffalo mozzarella were top-notch quality. Overall package was excellent, I was definitely a fan.Service was great, no complaints here. Don Antonio is definitely a bit more upscale then your typical pizza joint, and it shows in the service.Admittedly, Don Antonio wasn't exactly what I was looking for in a NY pizza joint. But quality comes in all shapes and sizes! Would love to try some of the other pizzas here in the future.

The horny ram caught my attention with its unique outrageous name & their menu had me wanting the Fried chicken sandwich at first sight! It has jalapeño Cilantro Slaw, Spicy Mayo on Ciabatta. I loved each & every bite of it so no regrets there. I'm not a big fan of slaw but this Jalapaneo cilantro slaw was a game changer & added so much flavor along with the spicy mayo to the sandwich! I mean anything with spicy mayo is bound to taste great to me..The interior is super cute with wall decor & you guess it! Rams paintings everywhere! It's a cool place to check out..The only thing I was concerned about was how long they took to make and bring out the food. I came during my lunch break & the food took longer than expected to come out. Other than that, it was a great experience!

The moment it even gets a little chilly I start to crave big bowls of warm soup. So happy to have found Tatsu Ramen where you can customize everything and you can order Gluten Free noodles! The broth was rich and flavorful. Vegan broth also available. Soo goood!!

I had the pleasure of dining at this Harlem gem on a busy Saturday afternoon. To my surprise, I was seated immediately in the otherwise minimalistic setting. Heeding the waitresses' advice, I went for their famous chicken on a waffle, accompanied by an unconventional iced coffee—a delightful twist to my weekend indulgence.

True to its popularity, the dish arrived promptly, and the hype was justified— the fried chicken was nothing short of spectacular, sealing its place as my go-to comfort meal. I couldn't resist but return twice for the very same reason. 

The peach cobbler was another star of the show. Laden with juicy peaches and served at the perfect temperature, it was a pleasant end to a hearty meal without being overly sweet.

For those in or around Harlem, do yourself a favor and check out this spot. Its simplicity and authenticity might even give the famed Red Rooster a run for its money.

I recently visited a Korean restaurant that truly impressed me with its authentic flavors. The wait staff was pleasant and helpful, providing us with everything we needed despite not frequently checking on our table. The standout dish was the soondubu stew, which featured deliciously soft tofu. The pajeon was slightly on the greasy side, but its flavor made up for it, although the $14 price tag felt a bit steep. My companion thoroughly enjoyed the hot bibimbap, which was evidently a hit. We were treated to an assortment of fresh and tasty little side dishes, reminiscent of genuine Korean dining. Overall, this place is a gem that I would gladly return to for another taste of Korea.

During my November 2019 visit to the restaurant, I tried their drink of the month - a vodka cranberry lemonade. The initial sip was strikingly sour, courtesy of the lemonade, but as the drink settled, the vodka's presence became unmistakably clear. It was a refreshing yet potent concoction.
The pizza was pretty good. I got cheese pizza and found bacon bits so that was really gross but otherwise it was good old nyc pizza.

Title: My Go-To Spot for Delicious Eats

I've dined at this gem of a restaurant more than 15 times, whether in person or via delivery—it's my default choice when indecision strikes. The menu is reasonably priced, and every dish packs a punch of flavor. Service is commendable, adding to the overall positive experience.

Their cocktail selection is fairly standard but hits the sweet spot with the pricing. A must-try is the flaming jalapeño drink—it's a fiery twist on a night out.

I regret having few pictures to share; the food is so enticing that I dive right in before the thought of snapping a photo crosses my mind. Yes, it's irresistible.

For a tantalizing treat, venture into their dry pot options. My personal picks are perfectly fried potatoes, enoki mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms, and their unparalleled cauliflower. Also worth savoring are the eye of round, fish fillets, pork belly, and bok choy. Although I tend to stick with these favorites, I was pleasantly satisfied with their dan dan noodles, which offer an authentic taste.

In essence, it's a fantastic spot that keeps me coming back for more. Highly recommended!

Title: Cozy Italian Eats with a Relaxed Ambience

Last Thursday night's quest for a casual dinner led me to a quaint Italian spot that delivered just that. The ambiance was immediately welcoming with a chill vibe and tasteful decor setting the stage for a relaxed meal.

We started with the garlic knots, which, despite being on the pricier side at $6 for four, hit the spot with their Parmesan-laden crust and a side of marinara. My main course, the Sausage, Peppers, and Onions Hero, was satisfying. It was a well-rounded dish, but I wouldn't have minded an extra dollop of marinara for that perfect saucy bite. The accompanying side salad was a refreshing addition.

When it comes to value, the pricing could be more competitive. However, the portions were generous, and the quality was solid, making it mostly worth it. The staff was attentive and friendly, contributing positively to the overall experience. 

In summary, the restaurant's atmosphere stands out with a perfect score, and the service, quality, and quantity closely follow. It's a spot I'd recommend for anyone looking for an Italian fix in a cozy environment, with just a minor tweak needed in the sauce department.

Ratings:
Price: 3/5
Quality: 4/5
Quantity: 4/5
Service: 4/5
Atmosphere: 5/5

Leyla is a very cute restaurant on the upper west side on a pretty residential block. In front of the entrance was a sign for daily happy hour deals that end at 7pm. I was excited to participate, but the happy hour only applies to people who sit at the bar. I'm not going to lie... I hate paying full price when literally sitting somewhere else gives you a deal. Most of the cocktails were 15 dollars. The three we had were all very good! The botanist was so beautiful with shaved cucumbers layering the inner surface of the glass. It was also very light and refreshing. The na ne li and the frappe mezcal sour were really good. I liked that they were not overly sweet.We shared the vegetarian pide, which was delicious though a little pricey for the size of the pide. The fava bean bruschetta is a must. I couldn't believe how good it was. I didn't try the beet salad or the zucchini rolls, but my friends liked them. I got the branzino, which had the perfect amount of crisp to the skin. I wish that it came more with just a tiny tiny portion of salad for 26 dollars. I definitely see myself coming again. I can't seem to find the happy hour menu online, but the next time I come, I'll be sure to sit by the bar!

Came here for a birthday and we had a wonderful meal!!! Service was amazing and the restaurant has an old-timey house vibe whichi really liked. The walls are decked with museum-like paintings and artifacts and the menu comes with a story about the restaurant and its origins on the back.As for food, we had:- they give you veggies (carrots, celery, olives, pickle) to dip in sauce + bread- thick bacon 9/10: it was a little fatty which might be offputting for some people but i really enjoyed it!! Also comes with a small (smalllll) side of salad & tomatoes which were a nice touch. They give you three slabs of bacon- shishito peppers 7/10: wasnt anything spectacular but i do think it was a nice contrast to the otherwise very meat heavy meal- prime rib 9/10: i think the presentation could use a little work bc we got rare so it came out looking a lot like just slabs of pink meat lol but the quality was amazinnnnnnng- mutton 10/10: definitely the highlight of the meal!!! We got it rare and it was cooked so perfectly and the veggies in the middle were also a reallly nice touch and the salted flakes on everything was just simply amazingOn my reservation i had marked that it was for a birthday so they presented us with a slice of key lime at the end!! Which i thought was really nice and the cherry on top to the alread excellent serviceAnd sidenote: all of the above was more than enough food for the (quite) hungry two of us so we got to take it to go, which they generously included the horseradish sauce & mint jelly with

My recent visit to Wallse was a delightful experience, though it stopped just shy of being truly extraordinary. The atmosphere set a fantastic vibe, complimented by the warmth and attentiveness of the staff. Opting for the tasting menu, my friend and I savored an array of dishes, including Kumamoto oysters, foie gras torchon, spätzle, mushroom goulash, schnitzel, and glazed duck, with each dish allowing for sharing.

The mushroom goulash and the glazed duck stood out with their exceptional flavors, while the foie gras, surprisingly, fell below expectations. Generous portion sizes added value to our meal. The dessert, a Linzertorte, was delicious, yet it was the unique chef-designed spork that captured our attention as much as the food (picture attached).

While Wallse impressed, I still find the offerings at Schilling to be superior, particularly when considering the cost. A minor oversight occurred when I left without my leftovers and had to return to retrieve them. Despite this, Wallse earns a solid 4.5 stars for a commendable dining experience.

Visited this spot on a Friday just in time for happy hour. The "loaded" truffle fries, although not quite as "loaded" as anticipated, were paired with a John Doe Ale for $12—a fair deal. Service felt rushed as the waitress seemed impatient, but both the beer and fries were satisfying. Be prepared for a boisterous atmosphere, typical of a lively bar scene. Despite the noise, it was a positive experience overall.

Federoff's is my favorite cheesesteak in NYC. I mean, nothing compares to the real deal down in Philly, but Federoff's puts on a good showing. This location is just a pickup window. Tell them what size you want and if you want wiz whit. Never seen a place offer a "small" cheesesteak, but I'm a fat ass and went with the regular/large. Came out quick and then I had to go find somewhere to eat it because it was gooey and greasy, and I was wearing nice clothes. But goddamn, this thing was delicious. The bottom of my bun was a little too burnt, but otherwise, it was pretty damn near perfect!

I told my boyfriend I liked the lobster roll more than him. I told him I was joking, but hmmm was I? We were in the Financial District and this was the #1 recommended spot in the area so we decided to give it a try. Upon entering, we were welcomed by a nice, friendly worker who would later on, personally deliver our orders. We both had the Lobster Roll ($17) although I actually wish I had Luke's Trio instead just so I am able to sample all 3 lobster, crab, and shrimp. Either way, the lobster roll was absolutely delicious! The roll was unfortunately tiny but I could definitely see the craftsmanship in it with the fresh lobster, buttered bread, seasoning, and dash of that lemon. Even though the roll was expensive, it's fresh seafood and it was filling! They also offer free water inside the drinks fridge. I definitely recommend this place if you have the money to splurge or just want to try some quick quality seafood!

Title: A Birthday Feast to Remember at Kamayan

I recently celebrated my birthday with a long-anticipated dinner at Kamayan, a Filipino culinary gem that had caught my eye after a Yelp event. The surprise was courtesy of my husband, and I was joined by my sister and son for the feast.

Parking was a breeze, located conveniently across the street, and although we had to navigate a snug front house with our sizable stroller, the staff was accommodating, providing us a comfortable spot at the back. 

We kicked off our meal with delectable lumpiang and a bone marrow dish that was simply divine—a sentiment shared by my family who are no strangers to the allure of marrow. For the main course, we indulged in a medley of flavors from the chori burger to the fiery bicol express, succulent head-on prawns, and a tender beef rib special. Each dish was a testament to the authentic and rich taste of Filipino cuisine.

The meal concluded with a halo-halo dessert, a blissful mix of ube ice cream, candied fruit, flan, and crispy elements—an exemplary end to my birthday meal.

Kamayan didn't just deliver great food but a promise of an authentic feast that I can't wait to experience again. The kamayan feast still awaits, and I’m eager for my next visit.

Always make a reservation...My friend had come from the west coast and she was really excited about this max Brenner. This is not widely spread throughout the country and in the USA, only NYC-Boston and Phili have this outlet.I live in NJ and come to NYC so often but never heard of this restaurant ( I am not chocolate lover) so plz spare me :PIt was the 31st night. We came here for desserts and we realized we should have made our reservation. It was 1.5 hrs. waiting. We were 6 folks and could not get a table.  We got the mini table Near to take away counter, but that was not enough. Anyway, we managed somehow to grab seats together. We ordered three types of their famous hot chocolates ( $6 each)HazelnutMarshmallowAnd Classic one.And we also ordered Waffle celebration (your choice of 3 waffles from the menu).My friends - they really liked it. Superb... ( me- don't ask. Why I found the taste same like Dunkin hot chocolate... Hyped?? Sorry folks, plz don't come after me).  I liked Godiva chocolate shakes tastier which is on 5th avenue.They also have merchandise section. I bought their famous hug mug for my wife which was really cute.  You can buy coffee power and various other things. They do have lunch and dinner menu but make sure you make a reservation. Its always crowded and there is always waiting

Great value for what you get! Came with the brother for lunch on a Sunday at 1230pm. We had reservations so when we got here we were immediately seated at the sushi bar. We both opted for the $26 dollar pp restaurant week special. I got the Neta sushi with Salmon Ikura don. He got the Neta sashimi with the Szechuan Salmon Don. AMBIANCE:Definitely check out the sushi bar here if you get the chance! It's definitely very refreshing to be able to see all the line cooks and chefs make your food in front of you. It's quite an experience!PROS:Both our szechuan salmon don and the salmon ikura don were incredible! Fish we had was incredibly tasty and fresh, the roe was very tasty, and the garnishes on top of the szechuan salmon bowl gave a unique crunchy/seaweed like taste to it. Highly recommend the szechuan salmon bowl as it is quite unique and the flavor profile and textures are more complicated compared to the salmon ikura don!Sushi fish was great and very fresh. I got scallops, hamachi, salmon, and I believe fatty tuna. Tuna hands down was the favorite cut as I do tend to favor fattier fishes, and salmon comes at a close second. Delicious fish indeed! Sashimi was just as fresh. Crab legs were definitely the highlight for that appetizer. CONS:Biggest complaint would be the size of the sushi we got was rather small, and the ratio between fish and rice seemed rather off. The rice was tiny in comparison to the size of the fish we got. *Note - portion size does tend to be on the smaller side, so we were still slightly hungry after the meal. OVERALL:Definitely would come back to Neta! I would try their omakase option as I heard great things about it. But overall had a pleasant experience and highly recommend their restaurant week menu as you get an incredible value for incredible food and great flavors!

After reading the glowing reviews, I was excited to try the BBQ rice platter at this establishment. Unfortunately, the experience did not live up to the hype. Priced at $15, the platter consisted of plain white rice, a simple beansprout soup, corn, beansprouts, and shredded carrots, which felt rather basic for the cost. The highlight, bulgogi, was not only a disappointingly scant portion but also lacked any standout flavor that would justify the price. In hindsight, I regret not venturing further into the restaurant to try the bulgogi over rice, which might have been a more satisfying choice.

Title: Mixed Feelings at By Chloe's NY Location

I'm a fan of By Chloe, so I had to check out their New York spot on a recent trip. This time, my experience nets them 3 stars. My partner and I were seeking a respite from our dining indulgences, hoping for a light but satisfying meal.

We ordered two taco salads, seasonal mandarin lemonades, and a cookie, which set us back about $40. Unfortunately, the salads failed to impress, dominated by lettuce with little of the variety we've enjoyed at other By Chloe locations. The lemonades were a disappointment, reminiscent of canned mandarin juice rather than the fresh zesty flavor we anticipated. The cookie was dry, lacking the moist, chewy texture you'd expect from a fresh-baked treat.

Thankfully, the lemon vinaigrette dressing on the taco salads was delicious, which somewhat redeemed the dish. Also, a quick note on amenities – there's only one unisex bathroom, so plan accordingly.

In summary, while I love the brand, the New York location didn't quite live up to expectations, especially considering the price. Here's hoping for a more consistent experience across all By Chloe eateries in the future.

Title: Burger Perfection at NYC Hotspot

I had the pleasure of sinking my teeth into what can only be described as the best burger I've ever had. This NYC gem has earned its stripes with a Top 5 burger accolade from the New York Times, and it's no wonder. Opting for anything but their steak—or, more specifically, the burger—would be a missed culinary experience.

The burger I chose was a mouth-watering masterpiece of tenderness and robust flavor, expertly cooked to a perfect medium rare. It was an unforgettable combination of succulence and taste. I went for the bacon and blue cheese burger, customized to my liking, and it was sublime, paired with a side of crispy fries. This dish was nothing short of culinary dynamite.

For fellow burger aficionados, this eatery is a must-visit. The hype is real; prepare for a burger that will ignite your taste buds and leave you craving more.

Paris Baguette stands out in the hustle of Times Square, offering a welcome respite for those seeking a swift and satisfying breakfast or a lunch on-the-go. This particular location caters well to busy professionals with its convenient range of sumptuous pastries and a selection of sandwiches. Their mini croissants are a bite-sized delight and ideal for snacking, while the adorable Mr. Bear chocolate cake and the indulgent chocolate croissants are personal favorites that shouldn’t be missed. For the regulars, the Paris Baguette app is a boon, allowing you to accumulate points towards rewards. However, be prepared to pay a premium for these treats, like the Mr. Bear cake at $2.75, which may be steep compared to other venues. Nonetheless, for those craving quality and convenience in the city, Paris Baguette is a tempting choice.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a unique spot that offers an impeccable fusion of Chinese-style Cajun boils. Opting for their shrimp boil, I was intrigued to experience how this blend would unfold.

The star of the meal, undoubtedly, was the sauce—a brilliant concoction reminiscent of both Szechuan and Cajun culinary artistry. Laden with minced garlic, the sauce started mildly but gradually intensified, a thrilling journey for the palate. A word to the wise: keep water handy to tame the gradual spice crescendo.

While the potatoes included in the boil were somewhat understated in flavor, acting predominantly as a cooling agent, the konjac noodles were a revelation. I cannot recommend them enough; they were not only fun to eat with their delightful texture but also excelled at absorbing and showcasing the complexity of the sauce.

In summary, for an adventurous taste exploration that marries the fiery spirit of Cajun cuisine with the boldness of Chinese flavors, this place is a must-visit. Don't skip the konjac noodles—they are integral to the experience!

The place is small but super lovely and decorated with subtle elegance. We were greeted almost immediately when we entered and our table was ready. The staff was super nice, smiling and helpful, and although it took some time for the food to arrive--naturally, as the restaurant was almost full!--it was totally worth the wait. The pickle plate was delicious and both of our Khachapuris (one with bacon the other one with crabmeat) were heavenly, especially the one with bacon!! Not to mention that they're HUGE and stuffed with so much cheese that it's impossible to eat it in one sit. I've seen other people around us ordering different dishes and all looked appetizing so I'll go back to try other goodies as well.

Tucked away on the edge of Koreatown, this charming shoebox-sized addition to the Hand Hospitality collection is a gem waiting to be discovered. Its service is warm and welcoming, with a menu that offers both quality and quantity at pleasing prices—don't miss out on their house-infused grapefruit sowuju for a mere $36 a carafe.

The food here is a testament to indulgence. From the crispy corn croquettes and savory mandu to the succulent pork belly, delectable fried and grilled chicken, and the standout kalbi, our table may have overindulged, but the flavors warranted every bite. While banchan takes a back seat, the braised daikon with short rib deserves a solo performance.

Regrettably, dessert was a course we couldn't entertain after such a feast. This spot is unquestionably on my list for a return visit.

Title: A Flavourful Brunch Experience at L'Adresse near Bryant Park

While in search of a lunch spot by Bryant Park, we stumbled upon L'Adresse, which impressed with its spacious interior and ample seating. Our culinary journey began on a high note with what could easily be described as some of the best blueberry pancakes I've ever savored. Accompanied by a side of Turkey Kielbasa that was exceptionally meaty and bursting with flavor, the meal started promisingly.

The L'Adresse Skillet was a symphony of flavors, hearty and quite filling, though the eggs were slightly overdone. A minor hiccup occurred when two Truffle Burgers, topped with a lavish amount of shaved truffle, were mixed up. A medium rare and a medium well were confused, and due to a premature bite, we had to request further cooking for one. The wait for the corrected burger was lengthy, presumably due to a complete remake.

Acknowledging the error, the manager personally apologized and offered a small discount for our inconvenience. Despite the setback, the overall brunch experience was enjoyable. It was clear that customer satisfaction was a priority for L'Adresse, and their efforts to remedy the situation were appreciated.

The experience left me eager to return and indulge in more of their offerings, confident that any future visits would be met with the same level of attention and service.

Tucked away in an unexpectedly grand area, Au Cheval Diner presents a curious contrast to its upscale neighborhood. Once inside, the diner ambiance dims the prestige of its location but doesn't quite elevate the dining experience. The much-hyped Single Patty burger, adorned with bacon, a fried egg, and an assortment of toppings, is a visual treat but lacks the anticipated flavor punch, with the meat needing a bit more seasoning. However, the bacon's standalone excellence is undeniable.

The Shaved Prime Rib sandwich delivers on texture and spice, thanks to the red pepper, though it skews towards the saltier side. Accompanying this was a side of crispy fries with a delightful garlic aioli, but one can’t help but eye other tempting fry options available.

Service inconsistencies were noticeable, as a neighboring party received their meal before mine despite ordering later. This slip-up was professionally acknowledged by the staff, resulting in my burger being comped—a redeeming gesture.

In conclusion, while Au Cheval didn't completely live up to the hype this time around, the quality ingredients and the customer service response show promise. I am intrigued enough to return and explore the menu further, and the allure of the basement bar is an added draw for a future visit.

Went expecting the best thin crust pizza of my life, and felt like it was good but fairly on par with a Sbarro slice of pizza I could order at my local mall food court. It was delicious as most pizza is, yet it didn't stand out to be as being exceptional.I ordered a slice of cheese pizza. I loved the cheese, and the crust was truly the thinnest crust I have seen on a pizza. I have seen some reviews saying they take card for a certain minimum, I ordered 3 slices which came out to $9 and was asked for cash only still. They have an ATM right outside the door if you don't have any cash. Overall, the location is small and doesn't have much seating which I think is fairly standard for a NY food place.

Title: Unexpected Gem of Gastronomic Delight

If I had to describe my experience at this restaurant in one word, it would be 'unexpected!' The food is absolutely delicious and left me wanting more. The ambiance strikes the perfect balance of laid-back and trendy, making it a cool spot to unwind.

The service? Outstanding! Make sure to ask for Kira – she knows how to make your dining experience special. Plus, the prices won’t break the bank, which is always a plus in my book.

I just can’t contain my excitement, hence all the exclamation points! It’s simply that good and worth every bit of the hype. My top recommendations include the brisket bowl, the succulent salmon bowl, and the innovative quinoa bao buns.

Do yourself a favor and check this place out. It comes with my highest praises!

Title: A Shucking Good Time at Barn Joo, Union Square!

I recently ventured into Barn Joo on a friend's recommendation, seeking out NYC’s best raw oysters, and let me tell you, it did not disappoint. The Union Square location buzzed with energy, and the immediate seating with a friendly staff set the tone for a fantastic evening.

Specializing in Korean fares along with an impressive cocktail and wine list, Barn Joo's highlight was the $1 oyster deal during happy hour. The freshness of the ocean was evident in each succulent blue point oyster we had, and paired with a crisp Rose at $7, it was the perfect kickoff. With a policy of 6 to 24 oysters per table, our duo managed a dozen each and could have easily indulged in more.

But the culinary journey didn't stop at the oysters. The truffle fries were a hit: generous and flavorful. Additionally, their chicken wings – we opted for the hot and spicy – were a crispy delight with an unexpected sweet twist at a reasonable $8 a serving.

While I skipped dessert, my companion indulged in a dulce de leche ice cream that was a sweet end to a satisfying meal. Though stuffed, I'm already planning a return to delve into their full menu.

The charming and quaint atmosphere, with options to dine alfresco, only added to Barn Joo's allure. An added perk for Yelpers is the post-6 p.m. "wheel of fortune" spin with dinner for a chance to win a free treat.

Barn Joo is a must-try: fantastic food, warm service, and a lively atmosphere. It's a gem that I'm almost hesitant to share. But good finds like this are meant to be praised. Don't miss out!

I usually love RH and this was no exception! I didn't love however, the table we received. It was pretty close to the front of the restaurant but it was private enough because we sat on the couch. I ordered kale caesar with shrimp and iced cold brew and my friend ordered the eggs with the toast and decaf cold coffee. Our waiter was a bit slow (actually I wasn't sure who the waiter was because one person took the order; another brought the coffee and I had to ask the busboy for a glass of ice at least twice. I was able to refill my water bottle at ease since it was over 90 outside. It is a beautiful setting here and I absolutely love it! Again, it is too hot outside to sit so we opted to sit inside. The bathrooms are unisex . I like that we were able to have lunch here and dine at our leisure.

Title: A Bite of Deluxe Indulgence at Au Cheval

I recently visited the highly-acclaimed Au Cheval, and the experience did not disappoint. Reservations, via Resy, are highly recommended and we secured our spot a week in advance. A pre-meal drink at the cozy bar set the evening off to a good start.

Seating was prompt; our anticipation for their renowned burgers had us ready to order upon arrival. We indulged in both the single and double cheeseburgers, with the single boasting two patties and the double surprisingly featuring three. Each burger was topped with succulent egg and crisp bacon, enhancing the flavors to new heights. The burgers lived up to their reputation – they were exceptional and stand out as some of the finest in New York City.

A side of fries accompanied by a rich, garlicky aioli completed the meal, complementing the main attraction well. Despite the price tag being on the higher side, the quality justified every penny. Au Cheval is a must-visit for burger aficionados seeking a lavish twist on a classic favorite.

PURCHASE: Draft beer (cheapest)TOTAL: $9  PROS:+ Incredible view: 26th floors up. There are two viewing decks and an interior that is certainly a date spot. The larger viewing deck has the view of everything between financial district towards uptown. IT IS SICK. The second viewing deck faces the Financial District. It was used a private party space on the evening I went. It faces towards the south west. CONS: - Seasonally crowded: Between mid May to late October, it will become more crowded during the hot times (week nights). IMPRESSION: Definitely a top rooftop bar. Of many rooftop bars, I consider this a top-ten spot. If you are interested, please see my bookmarked locations listed under, "NYC Top Rooftops."

Every time I passed by I noticed a huge line, but not for tonight, due to an incident around the block. So I decided to get inside for an adventure. After settling down and staring at a small window stays shut infront.1. We may customize and build a noodle soup on our own.2. A private box for every one.3. No tipping!4.if you follow every step right by the ordering, you may not need to be spoken in the whole process.Presentation: unique, unlike the usual round noodle soup bow, it is a shape in rectangular.Taste: the broth is such an ecstasy, deep and rich.As Part of same Asian, while others joyfully in creative their soup, I wasn't that excited, even I was hopping that they should have fixed a set so it saves my time to tick the boxes on the ordering sheet.By the way, my bill was $26, not that I ordered too much extra, it wkind of expensive for having a bow of noodles, even for a Japanese standards.

Title: A Heartfelt Thanks to Tony's for Nourishing Frontline Heroes

As an ardent supporter of Tony's delightful cuisine, I felt a surge of pride upon learning of their initiative to donate meals to frontline workers. My interactions with Bruce to arrange a delivery for my unit were seamless, which came as no surprise given Tony di Napoli's reputation for impeccable service.

When the food arrived, the generosity was immediately evident—the portions were enormous, staying true to Tony's style. The choice of chicken or eggplant parmigiana with the side of rigatoni a la vodka promised a hearty meal for both lunch and dinner from a single serving.

Besides the main course, we were pleasantly surprised to find dessert included, an unexpected touch of sweetness to end our meal. This act of kindness from the staff at Tony's not only satiated our hunger but also uplifted our spirits, giving us an added boost to continue our vital work.

Heartfelt thanks to Tony's for the delicious food and for the thoughtful gesture that resonates deeply with all of us on the frontline.

I need to update my review from my last one. I decided to try this place again upon the owners request to give them a second chance, and since I love tacos I did. And I'm so glad I did. My friend and I came in and we were promptly seated. When you come in you're given a slip of paper with their tacos and drinks and you can mark down what you want. It's like ordering dim sum from a restaurant. We started with Guac and chips, which was really good. The Guac wasn't too spicy and it was a really hefty portion of it. The tortilla chips seemed twice fried, which is awesome because it gave it an extra crunch. For the tacos we tried the shrimp, the seared fish, the fried crispy fish, and the chicken taco. The shrimp tacos were really good and juicy. It has a lot of shrimp filling for the taco. It's one of my favorite seafood tacos that they have. The fried crispy fish was really good as well. The batter wasn't too thick so it was a pleasant surprise. The seared fish was good, but I actually preferred eating it outside of the taco shell. One of my favorites was the chicken taco. It's a really huge portion of chicken for the tortilla shell. It was absolutely delicious. I decided against getting the horchata since I didn't have a good experience last time and instead got the agua de pina and agua de hibiscus. My friend loved the agua de pina since it was like a very refreshing drink. I actually really enjoyed my agua de hibiscus because it wasn't too tart like I've known other hibiscus drinks to be. All in all, I'm really glad I gave this place another chance and tried more of their menu. It's possible my friend and I came on an off day last time but this time it was fantastic.

I recently visited this spot for a post-night-out snack and was pleasantly surprised. Service was quick—I got my slice without delay. Opting for the $3 cheese slice, I was treated to a delightful thin crust, topped with perfectly melty, low moisture cheese that packed a flavorful punch. It's a great value for a late-night cheesy treat! Highly recommend for those on-the-go pizza cravings.

Whenever I clock out late and crave ramen, Yama never disappoints. The Yama big bowl is my go-to, an indulgent Tonkotsu Ramen packed with braised pork jowl and pork belly, complete with bamboo shoots, corn, wood ears, and scallions. What stands out is the sublime balance of fat to meat in the pork belly that just melts in your mouth. The portion is generous, leaving me satisfyingly full, and the broth? Simply divine. A must-visit for any ramen enthusiast.

A new Asian food hall in Midtown East located in the former Yaso Tangbao space.  The concept is basically like an Asian night market where there are multiple food vendors packed in a small space.  Today I checked out Curry 42 and Debutea.  I wasn't overly impressed with the green curry chicken I got from Curry 42.  The curry did not have enough flavor or spices.  The chicken was cut in big chunks and some pieces were super dry.  It was also not spicy at all.  Green curry is supposed to bring the heat, but it was barely mild.  I had to add a bunch of siracha sauce just to add some heat to the dish.  Debutea was quite good.  I got the Red Ruby w/ cheese layer and really liked it.

Went there for one of the anniversary dinners. My entree was delayed so they gave us complementary lobster dumping apps as apology. This is what I mean great customer service. Food though, being critical here, was fair with no surprises.  Grilled lobster was good. A little upset they took the head off cause I am one of those odd eaters who loves lobster head. The grilled fish and fried oysters were okay.

I thought the ambiance was okay. It was in the hotel where we were staying and we had a bunch of hotel credit so we thought we would try it out. Also, I've never really had Spanish food.We got the sandwich with side dish of pan con tomato and paella.The sandwich was a bit dry. The cooked chicken skin was tasty. However, the sandwich was a bit pricey for the quality.The pan con tomato reminded be of bruschetta which I love. However there wasn't enough sauce for the bread in my opinion.The paella portion was HUGE, which is a good thing. However, we couldn't finish it. It was an interesting experience with paella and my first time so I enjoyed it.Overall, I think the price is too high for this restaurant. We ended up paying around $60-$80 for this food and it was just okay.

I came here as a recommendation for a friend and I was HIGHLY DISAPPOINTED. The environment is good and so is the food, but the customer service is HORRENDOUS. I cannot be anymore disappointed with the customer service. I came here with the friend who highly recommended it. The food was spectacular, but we could not feel anymore uncomfortable. The server we got took our menus away and then gave them back, it did not make sense- she did not explain what she was doing, she just took them away from us. When we asked to switch seats because our friend was joining us, she rolled her eyes and said "sure". We sat down and ordered and she was very repetitive when asking questions, as if she didn't want to be there...her attitude was horrible. I came here with my friend who is a local for my boyfriend's birthday and it was the WORST EXPERIENCE. I DO NOT RECOMMEND it if you get this waitress. Once we were done eating she dragged our plates and said "are you done?!" I am leaving highly upset. I can't believe it. As most people would feel in this situation, I was upset but mostly confused. Why would someone who works in customer service treat clients with such poor attitude? When she came over and gave me attitude for asking for butter and a beverage refill, I simply asked her "What is wrong? Did we do something to upset you?" She scoffed and said "No, nothing is wrong."yet again with attitude!!!! Then I proceeded to tell her "The entire time for the moment we asked to sit in a different table when first coming in you had a problem with that, until now. You work in customer service, you cannot treat clients with such disrespect, especially because you're not having a good day. I work with my clients and I never give such horrible customer service, you cannot when working with the public, they will be inclined to go elsewhere." She then proceeded to go to the register and shout that our hour for bottomless was over. When we received our check it was not split between our party, and the other waitress did not want to split it saying it was already done like this- yet, we asked for it to be split amongst our party from the beginning, only two checks. The original waitress came over since speaking to her said we did, and fixed the issue. It was not until I spoke to her telling her that her attitude was wrong that she didn't stop. The kicker? The local that sat near our table looked at my boyfriend once and then kept covering her mouth and eyes so she would not see him, she proceeded to ask to switch tables and still kept giving us the same glare, avoiding my boyfriend because she is a racist. Check your cameras and tell me what we were doing that was so obnoxious. I took two calls from clients outside, my boyfriend spoke to family on the phone and filmed our party since it was his birthday, our other friend was figuring out trip details. No one was loud, nor obnoxious, we even partook in conversation with the clients next to us. If I get bad service I am going to be upset and ask the waitress why, anyone would.Worst experience of my life.

I was excited to have a steak for lunch and Tads looked like just the place to hit the spot. It's cafeteria style walk up and order. Now, for the price and location right off of Times Square, it's worth it. You get a complete meal with salad and bread. But if you are looking for fine dining and a great steak you might be disappointed.

I came here with a party of 2 on a Wednesday around 7pm and were seated right away. It was great timing for us since the place is very small and there were only 2 tables free. We ordered the Teppan gyoza and shiso truffle fries for appetizers. They were both fine but nothing amazing. The real winners are the ramen though. We got the Torigara and the Tontoro Pork ramens. The Torigara has thin noodles with a light broth but it still has lots of umami and felt filling. The Tontoro Pork has thicker noodles with a creamy broth that was hefty in an amazing way. We also ordered a green tea but it never arrived :( the other food though comes out relatively quickly!Would definitely recommend coming here and trying their ramen, if you can find a seat!

i would skip this place, despite the hype and reputation i left disappointed.we ordered pork buns, spicy beef ramen, and the smoked pork ramen. the beef ramen was flat and one dimensional, and seriously lacked any heat whatsoever. the pork ramen just tasted.. off. i don't know how to describe it, but no other flavors came through except the heavy handed smoke. the pork buns were excellent, especially with the ssam sauce. also the yuzu lemonade was tasty and tangy. i recommend getting those items as an app, and then promptly heading down to ipuddo westside for some better ramen.

What a great invention! The chicken was crispy, flavorful, not dry and the different sauce options were perfect. I tried the yellow bbq, maple syrup, peri peri and bbq. The peri peri has a dry heat which will really give you a kick by the time you finish your bite. The maple syrup and bbq are safe choices. The yellow bbq is a nice twist to the regular bbq for the mustard bbq lovers. As for the cone, I loved the crispy and warm texture. It is similar to the freshly baked cones at an ice cream shop but not 100% crispy that it breaks apart after one bite.

Over the course of multiple visits to Yin Ji, I have had the opportunity to try most of their menu offerings (barring the ham chin peng, which according to the staff is because they can't procure a skilled enough chef?). I would definitely recommend the Lai Wan Congee ($5.95) which comes with a hodgepodge of ingredients and their hot HK-style milk tea ($2.75). As for their cheong fun, I've said it before and I'll say it again-- the fillings are too chunky and rolling the batter once makes the filling spill out too easily. I generally prefer their cilantro rolls ($4.95) or corn rolls ($3.95) as they are simple enough to showcase the batter.

Hmmmm so what can I say about the Perrine?  I had a great (3) course meal for a great price during restaurant week.  I have to admit it would not have been a place I would have dared to go to but it was something different and new for me.  The wait staff were very friendly and inviting which I know is a plus. You can not put a price on great customer service and hands down this place has mastered it.  The location of the restaurant is in a very nice posh neighborhood in the upper east side of new York city right next to Central Park so after the meal you can take a stroll and walk off the delish desserts they have to offer.I had the grilled shrimp salad, spring Chicken and the delectable chocolate cake did I say yummy already :-).  Everything was great very clean and the bathrooms were beautiful.  They also had an area where it appears you can have social events like weddings and parties etc...I would definitely say give this place a try even if it seems over you pay grade this deal fit into my budget and was worth it :-).

Title: A Pasta Lover's Paradise in NYC

If you're craving authentic Italian pasta that delivers on taste and portion, look no further. This gem requires reservations, and rightfully so—it stands out as one of New York City's premier pasta destinations.

The menu, fairly priced, especially when considering the generous servings, features standout dishes like the squid ink pasta, flawlessly cooked, and a carbonara that strikes the ideal balance of al dente texture and creamy richness. It's evident that they don't play into the overhyped scene of Italian cuisine; they simply deliver excellence.

Service here is as remarkable as the food. The knowledgeable staff glides through recommendations, pairing your meal with the perfect drink, all within an ambience that is nothing short of perfection.

This high-demand eatery operates like a well-oiled machine, thanks to its efficient and great team. Any genuine pasta aficionado in New York City would be remiss to skip this elite establishment. It's unquestionably among the best of the best for pasta in the city.

If you didn't know about this mini mini mart before visiting, then you wouldn't even know it's in the Shops at Hudson Yards. Honestly, if I visited the Shops more frequently, I wouldn't mind it's hidden location actually because it's truly a hidden gem inside.The mart (one of David Chang's creations) is a great option though for those looking for a quick bite and want to grab and go. There's pre-made sandwiches (potato salad, black + white, chicken katsu) to choose from, as well as pre-made kimbaps and tons of snacks lying around. We ended up getting a chicken katsu sandwich and spicy chicken kimbap. Rarely do we say we love eating pre-made food sitting around, but DAMN it was good. The chicken katsu sandwich was really big and we both split it. The katsu was flavorful and had a tasty sauce spread on it. The kimbap also hit the spot. We really loved the kick it had, but it wasn't too spicy. If people want to enjoy their food on the spot, there's seating right outside of the mini mart. Great stop to make if you're just looking for a small snack and want to continue on.

Tokyo Record Bar is a hidden gem that truly deserves a five-star rating! Despite some lower ratings online, my experience was nothing short of fantastic. For $50, diners are treated to a delightful fixed menu that does not include drinks. The food was nothing less than amazing, leaving a lasting impression on my palate.

What sets this place apart is the personalized touch of allowing each guest to pick a song to play during their meal, adding to the ambiance and creating a unique dining experience. The service was impeccable, attentive without being overbearing. Tokyo Record Bar also has the perfect vibe for a fun date night, and I am already looking forward to my next visit. If you're in the mood for great food and a unique twist on dining out, Tokyo Record Bar should definitely be on your list.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Hong Kong Comfort Food

Don't let the unassuming exterior of this café fool you – it's a treasure trove of delectable Hong Kong snacks at unbeatable prices. While it's not the place for a gourmet feast, it's perfect for those craving authentic, comforting flavors from a classic Hong Kong-style menu.

The offerings of rice noodles, macaroni soup, spam sandwiches, and toast are simple but satisfying. Each dish I've sampled, including their delightful milk teas, has hit the spot. Admittedly, the cafe's space is limited—a bit of a gamble for seating—but the take-out option is just as convenient, with a serene park nearby for an impromptu picnic.

Having visited three times, I'm already planning my next visit to work my way through the menu. For anyone in search of straightforward, tasty fare at wallet-friendly prices, this café is a must-try.

There really was nothing "wrong" per se but there was just nothing exceptional either.  We were greeted warmly and immediately upon arrival.  They were a little full so we were seated in the basement area.  Nothing wrong there just not as nice as upstairs.  The girl hostess walked halfway to the table and pointed before the entire party was even down the stairs.  She seemed as she had better things to do.As this is a big city the restaurant has typical challenges and despite the best pest control its possible to still see an insect crawl across the floor.The waiter was pleasant yet efficient and the bus boys filled the water religiously.The food was OK.  Nothing wrong with it but nothing remarkable either.  most of the dishes were Olive Garden Level - EXCEPTION being the Lasagna was really good.This was priced like a 5 star restaurant so while the location is convenient the value is not so much.

The boyfriend and I headed here for a few drinks and a bite to eat after attending a nearby concert. It's a sexy little bar and restaurant, with unique historical and monkey-themed décor reminiscent of 18th century British imperialism in India. Unsure about whether you should order their PAANCH of the day? Don't ask questions, just trust the process and order one! Think delicious spiced fruity tea-like cocktail, you'll love it.The food was excellent, albeit pricey for leaning towards the smaller side of portion sizes. Their Paneer Tikkas makes a great appetizer, because who doesn't love giant hunks of fried cheese?? I can vouch for the ultra-savory Masala Bombay Lamb Chops and Malabar Coastal Shrimp Curry, as well. Would definitely come back and recommend to friends!

I ADORE this place! Came here for lunch and thanks to Yelp reviews/photos, I knew I had to really look for this hidden place. It's tucked between two places so you have to look carefully otherwise you can easily walk by it. The restaurant is downstairs and we got a seat quickly. Ordered a miso ramen and it was so good! I wasn't expecting it to be so yummy. Plenty of ramen, love that it comes with an egg (and not paying extra for it like other places), vegetables. My favorite is the minced meat (pork?) that comes sprinkled across the noodles. Adds a burst of flavor and is a great combo in the meal. The broth was just a tad spicy and enough to add flavor. Not overwhelmingly spicy so someone like me (who can't handle heat) can actually enjoy it. It's also reasonably priced for ramen compared to many other places. Good size and makes you plenty full. Definitely enjoyed my meal here and can't wait to try more of their lunch dishes.

Came for restaurant week with some friends. Pretty curious since the site described it as Laotian, but some of the popular dishes include pho and Banh mi? Probably more of a fusion place but down to try it out.Appetizer I got scallops, which were cold marinated in some sort of vinegar/picking based marinade, were a decent start. Opted for the hanger steak which is basically a noodle dish, steak was cooked great to order but the dish overall felt like something I could get at a generic stir fry place. The tangerine sorbet which I assume in house was pretty good, and cleansed the palate.I recognize Restaurant Week can be pretty off compared to their standard fare, but for $42 I'm unimpressed and wouldn't come back. They had much more breadth in their regular menu, but when you can hit $30s with just entree, not sure I would take that chance alone.

Awesome meal in a super cozy space. If you manage to get a reservation, whether it's 5pm or 11pm, you must go! The service was great from the moment you walk in - you feel like you're at a friend of a friend's. Our waiter was extremely enthusiastic and a great salesman for the menu items (a bit performative too, sort of Carbone-like).As for the food, all the dishes we tried were extremely solid. Between the four of us, we shared:- American Cheeseburger with bacon and egg. SO delicious! It tasted like a highly elevated McDonalds McDouble and I mean that in the best way, like how the ultimate cheeseburger is supposed to taste. I think the egg added a bit of umami from the runny yolk and the bacon on its own was delicious, but probably unnecessary because it distracts from the burger.- French dip sandwich (off-menu and runs out by later seatings, but a must try!)- Chicago cut prime rib (delicious prime rib, but prime rib isn't one of my absolute favorite food items in general, so I probably wouldn't order this again, just so I have more room for the burger and trying new things)For sides, we got the truffle mac and cheese (yum!), loaded baked potato, and charred broccolini. We also got the chocolate cake for dessert which was pretty pricey, so probably a pass (but still a good option if you're a dessert person).Next time, I'm definitely getting the burger again, as well as the french dip, and trying more sides such as the creamed spinach. Can't wait!

Title: High Hopes Dashed at Thai Villa

I visited Thai Villa with a sense of anticipation due to its stellar reviews, inviting three friends to join me. While we were initially taken in by the restaurant's ambiance and the food's visual appeal, the overall experience fell short of expectations.

Despite intriguing appetizers like the Ray Rai Nah Phi and the standout Tod Mun Koong shrimp cakes, which were bursting with flavor and lightness, the meal took a nosedive from there. After a lengthy 30-minute wait post-appetizers, we were met with a series of unremarkable entrees. The Moo Obb Nam Puaung had tender pork but lackluster coconut sticky rice. The Ped Ron offered ample, well-crisped duck that was shy on flavor, and the Kha Nom Boung Youen was a letdown with its overly sweet cucumber relish. The Royal Pad Thai, while beautifully presented, was merely average and undistinguished from any basic version of the dish.

The meal's pacing was disrupted by an inefficient waiting system that led to frustration and a total of 2 hours of waiting for a meal that was far from exceptional. While the ambiance and initial bites showed promise, the end verdict was of an overpriced and overrated dining experience that didn't justify the wait or cost, totaling $160 after tax and tip.

In summary, despite the lure of beautiful presentation and a couple of tasty appetizers, Thai Villa did not live up to the hype. The inefficiency and underwhelming main courses lead me to award just 2 stars— one for the appetizers and another for the decor. There are other Thai venues that offer more satisfying fare without the hefty price tag or the wait.

Rating: ★★☆☆☆

I recently visited the takeout spot for a quick bite and decided to try the tomato and mozzarella sandwich. Opting to have it warmed up, I was pleased with the improved taste this gave to the already delicious sandwich. While the place offered plenty of seating, it was a bit of a challenge to find a free table, suggesting its popularity among diners. The customer service was average, aligning with the typical fast food experience. Overall, the meal was satisfying, but the service could use a little boost.

**Review of [Restaurant Name]:**

Upon my latest visit, I'm pleased to report that [Restaurant Name] still delivers an exceptional dining experience. I was thrilled to see the introduction of the Nibo ramen from their 51st Street location to the menu—a welcome addition for fans of the chain. While I do have a nostalgic pang for the long-gone Avo Tina appetizer, the restaurant's primary allure remains its stellar ramen.

A notable improvement is the clarity in noodle preference options, ranging from soft to al dente to firm. As a patron who favors firmer noodles, this customization is much appreciated. My choice of the extra spicy miso ramen, complemented with garlic paste, proved to be an outstanding selection. This dish was a veritable umami explosion, satisfying my craving for depth of flavor.

In short, [Restaurant Name] continues to uphold its reputation for crafting a superior ramen experience that caters to individual tastes.

The people at Sojourn were attentive and accommodating. The were always available if we needed anything and made sure everything was perfection when it arrived at our table. I had a 3 course meal that included duck spring rolls, salmon and chocolate cake. I loved every portion of my meal but I will break it down. The duck spring rolls were bomb. They had a crispy outside and the plum sauce that came with them was both sweet and spicy, which was perfect. The salmon had crispy skin but was tender . The star of the entree, however, was really the mushrooms. The salmon is on a bed of mushrooms and they are delicious. The flourless chocolate cake was full of flavor! Between the Nutella, the caramel sauce, bourbon, and ice cream... it was delicious.The cake it self was chocolatey and delicious! It was a wonderfully done meal

Chef JJ does it again!  And with rice this time.  Great flavors being turned out of an open kitchen with an array of options to choose from.  The braised beef bowl doesn't disappoint, perfect balance of savory heat.  Enjoy the playlist curated by JJ while washing everything down with a Sugar Hill Ale on tap.

Honestly I'm not sure what all the negative ratings are about? First off Moses the manager is a gem to this place and him introducing himself made this meal 10x better. It's always great to have a manger come and make sure the meal went ok! A simple gesture goes a long way. The VEGETARIAN MENU IS BOMB! Someone initially came and asked if we had any food allergies etc which I really appreciated. The guacamole was good but the sangria pitcher was amazing! I highly recommend ordering the pitcher it's ample sangria for 2. I had the avocado vegetarian thing it was DELICIOUS!

3.5 stars. - Loved the rice noodle dishes. Recommend the rice noodle with dried shrimp and regular shrimp. - I didn't love the Fatty Pork with Broccoli in Clay Pot. The pork pieces were 60%+ fat, just so fatty that it was borderline nauseating. My hubby and I picked at the meat and skin but didn't touch the fat. Several hours after eating, just thinking about fat made us slightly sick.

Churrasceria had long been on my radar before I delved into my first rodizio dining experience. The visit kicked off on a rocky note with the host failing to locate my reservation in her ledger and a lack of apology despite my email confirmation -- a hurdle that was overcome with a brief five-minute wait, thanks to a buzzer system.

The salad bar was commendable, though the accompaniments proved unremarkable, save for some notably creamy mashed potatoes. The parade of meats, however, was the star of the show; particularly the succulent lamb chops and delectable chicken, served in a continuous, delightful flow that lived up to the rodizio hype.

Desserts were satisfactory, without standing out. Table service was top-notch throughout the meal. When it comes to value, I remain on the fence -- while the meats wowed, the overall experience has me leaning towards the more tailored offerings of a la carte steakhouses, given the hit-or-miss nature of the non-meat options at this establishment.

Mamoun's is an NYC institution. It was opened in 1971 by Syrian immigrants, and is still a family run business, and now small chain. It is the quintessential ethnic hole-in-the-wall and I say that in the most loving way.I came to the original MacDougal St location. The storefront is very small, probably only about 12 feet wide. There is always a line but it moves fast. Being the first time, I had to get the classic falafel sandwhich. It's freshly fried falafel (fried fresh in store, but the batter is made in Mamoun's commisary kitchen in NJ), lettuce, tomato, hummus and tahini. It cost about $5. It is a little messy but easy enough to walk or stand and eat. Their falalfel recipe is unique because its is very heavy on the parsely and herbs, making it very green. This is a winner!

Title: A Delightful Evening at an Unnamed Restaurant

My friends and I decided to visit this gem on a bustling Friday night, and what an experience it was! Greeted with an inviting ambiance, we were seated promptly, a testament to their excellent service.

Opting against waiting for non-existent happy hour deals, I indulged in a $14 Paloma cocktail that was just the right kind of refreshing—a welcome splurge that matched typical NYC prices. But let me tell you, the real star of the show was the food. The tacos, with their freshly made tortillas, were a revelation, each bite better than the last. Accompanied by a communal bowl of rich guacamole and crisp chips, along with individual servings of rice and black beans, our table was a landscape of culinary delight.

Portions were generous, to say the least. If your stomach's grumbling, a duo of tacos with a side will hit the spot. My friends and I left satisfied and already planning our next visit. A must-try for anyone craving a great meal in a great atmosphere.

I felt like a Queen dining over her subjects thanks to their rustic, almost medieval decor. Perched at a corner table on the upstairs level, I had the full view of the main dining room and what was on everyone's plates. If the atmosphere doesn't make you feel like royalty, the level of service will. I was privileged to have a date who knew his wine and aperitifs, but our server was expert in giving suggestions and feedback. The pork empanadas were stellar as was their take on Patatas bravas - fried fingerling potatoes with puréed feta, pomegranate molasses, and fresh herbs. To keep with the queen-feels, my ass got decadent with two desserts (shared, of course) pictured below. The "brest" was like eating a doughnut stuffed with halva. The olive oil gelato was like eating custard with a subtle taste of extra virgin. I completely understand why people choose Alta for celebrations. Go be king and queen for a night!

Title: A Fusion Feast with Just a Pinch of Letdown

From the moment I stepped into this cozy Korean fusion eatery, I knew I was in for a treat. The truffle Mac n' Cheese was the star of the show, with the perfect hint of truffle to complement its creamy goodness – nothing short of perfection. Equally impressive was the Avocado dish, a medley of flavors that delighted with each bite.

The concept of small plates boasting bold and innovative tastes was mostly a hit, with the exception of a couple of dishes that fell flat. The flan, for one, was overwhelmingly sweet and missed the mark for me. The bigger letdown, however, was the Korean chicken. As a staple in Korean cuisine, especially in a fusion restaurant, expectations run high. Unfortunately, this dish lacked the crispy, succulent punch I had hoped for.

Despite these hiccups, the culinary journey here is largely a successful one. Just be prepared to experience a couple of bumps on the road to flavor town.

I had a delightful dining experience at this restaurant. The food impressed me with its flavors, particularly the beef platter, which was generous enough to be shared. The sides were a great complement to the meal, and the customer service was notably excellent. Additionally, the convenience of reserving a table through Yelp was much appreciated, considering the restaurant's popularity and the ever-present long lines. Highly recommended for a satisfying meal with efficient service.

Needed a place to get some cheap food for lunch. I asked my co worker about a good pizza place  and she suggested Champion. My break was only 30 minutes but I took the short walk anyway. Usually I would order my food then walk back to the office to eat but not today. This hidden treasure was filled with decor of pictures of famous celebrities and great vibes. The employees smiled and were accommodating. I felt the need to slow down because the pace was a bit laid back. Ended up sitting down to eat two cheese slices with a soda to wash it down.  Then my "stinkin thinkin " kicked in and I bought another slice to eat as I walked back to the office. Ppl were lusting over my pizza as I hustled through the street. It was hilarious .. The pizza itself was great. Thin crust with some good cheese. Wasn't very oily. I'll be back for sure.

Title: New Year's Noodle Feast at Meet Noodles

I recently celebrated the New Year with a delightful lunch at Meet Noodles, a gem my friend and I discovered on Yelp. We arrived at 2 PM to find the place comfortably bustling, which allowed for immediate seating. The restaurant's decor was particularly captivating – clean lines and an organized setup created a welcoming environment.

Service was a highlight of our experience. The staff greeted us with warmth, and our server, although seemingly new and occasionally needing assistance, was extremely courteous and attentive, frequently checking in and ensuring our glasses were never empty.

We were pleasantly surprised by the complimentary edamame, perfectly cooked without being overly salty – a great start to our meal. My friend and I shared a few dishes, including the Tomato Beef Tendon and Brisket Noodles, which featured al-dente noodles in a fragrant broth. My critique is minor: the tomatoes could have been stewed longer for better integration into the soup, and some pickled vegetable on the side might have tied the dish together beautifully.

The Fried Pork Chop with Rice was a tasty bento offering, with complementary veggies and egg, though the meat was a touch on the dry side. Nonetheless, the flavors were spot-on. A surprise hit was Ken's Pancake – the combination of meat, lettuce, egg, and honey mustard was unexpectedly delightful.

In summary, Meet Noodles delivered a fantastic dining experience, and I'm eager to return on my next visit to the area.

I recently dined at the downtown branch after finding the midtown location closed, and I was pleased to discover no wait for a table at 5 pm on a Saturday. The customizable menu at Ichiran is a highlight, allowing patrons to select the broth's richness and noodle firmness to suit personal tastes. The waitstaff was helpful, providing guidance for newcomers to navigate the variety of options.

The tonkotsu broth did not disappoint; it was rich, flavorful, and served steaming hot—a comforting embrace for the taste buds. However, I was less enthusiastic about preparing the hard-boiled egg that comes with the meal, as peeling it myself left room for bits of shell to linger.

While the experience didn't quite match the memories of my time in Hong Kong, the ramen here still holds its own as a solid choice for anyone craving a bowl of hearty, personalized noodles.

Title: A Quiet Evening with Great Service and Good Food

I visited this restaurant for a pre-fashion show dinner on a Wednesday night and found the place surprisingly quiet with only one other couple dining. The tranquility meant our waitress lavished us with attention and engaging conversation, a pleasant perk to the evening.

Taking advantage of a Pulsd deal, we indulged in two entrees, a bottle of wine, and gelato to finish. The house Chardonnay was a delightful choice, crisp and paired well with the meals. I savored the sea bass, which was cooked to perfection, while my friend's short ribs were flavorful, though the sauce was reminiscent of a simple A1 and ketchup blend, not entirely hitting the mark.

Dessert was a highlight with fresh-tasting strawberry gelato for her and a superb maple walnut for me, rounding out the dining experience.

We left satisfied and would certainly return, if not for the calming ambiance, then for the good food and excellent service that made our evening.

Get ready to be blown away by the food and ambiance at BKK! What sets BKK away from the many other Thai restaurants in NYC are its lavishly floral accents, creating the illusion of dining in a garden of fresh blooms and greenery. The menu doesn't have too many surprises so I decided to order Shrimp Pad Kee Mao with mild spice. My first bite was surprising, A. Because it definitely DID NOT taste like mild spice and B. Because the noodles were so flavorful and perfectly chewy. I loved every bite (except when the spice became too overwhelming) and was very satisfied by the time I cleaned my plate. They have a lunch special deal where you can order a main for only $11.95! I'd love to come back for another lovely dinner and have no doubt I'd be just as amazed with the charming ambiance and delicious food.
