Last evening, I arranged for dinner delivery to my Wall Street location from a local restaurant, and I was thoroughly impressed with the punctuality of the service - the food arrived at the precise time requested. I decided on an order of 6 Shrimp and Vegetable Pan-Fried Dumplings and Roast Duck Hand Pulled Noodles to share, and both did not disappoint. The portions initially seemed modest, but once plated, it was clear that the containers were generously packed, providing a perfect meal amount for two. The quality and quantity of food were exceptionally satisfying for the price of just $20, inclusive of tax, with the added bonus of free delivery courtesy of Delivery.com. This restaurant nailed it on both the flavors and service, making it a remarkable dining experience.

Good variety of a modern take on Filipino food.Came here with a group to be able to try as much of the menu as possible. There are very few Filipino restaurants in nyc so we always have to try the new ones. We started with the happy hour (5-7pm only at the bar) and then moved to a table. Kale laing - We had heard good things about this so we had to try. Some of of our group loved it, but I personally didn't love it (I also don't love kale), but I did love the coconut milk. Kinilaw - this was great and everyone in our party loved it. It is the Filipino version of ceviche.Lumpia - I've had great lumpia in my lifetime, and this was far from it. This tasted like a veg spring roll from a takeout Chinese restaurant.Liempo kawali - I really liked this very crispy pork with the fish sauce dipping sauce, but not everyone in our group loved this compared to other Filipino crispy pork dishes.Kare kare - I don't know anyone who doesn't love kare kare whenever it's served, and this was no exception. This was definitely the star of the meal and I'd definitely recommend it if you don't have someone at home who can make this (however my bf's mom's is light years better)Reggie's pasta aligue - I really liked this - the different flavors and the crab. It was a little small to share among 5 people, but not everyone in the group loved it. It could've used a little more sauceSinigang - the vegetables were good but I didn't love the salmon in this - it was slightly undercooked.Garlic fried rice - this was a great bite to have with each of the dishes.

Decided to check this spot out while in Brooklyn Heights. It was a Friday night , we were seated right away. Got a good view to the city from this restaurant. The waiter was super nice and went over the whole menu and suggested a few items. We went with the Cheese Plate , which had variety of cheeses with jam. Also had the Grilled Calamari as the appetizer. For the main course we had the roasted Crystal Valley chicken and the painted Hills ribeye , they were both delicious. Presentation was top notch. Ambiance - 10/10Service - 10/10Views - Excellent WiFi- Not Sure Large Groups- YesParking - Paid Garage around the corner Definitely booking a table for July 4th . Best spot to have dinner watching the  fireworks.

I recently visited this spot and would give it a 3.5-star rating. The restaurant prides itself on serving quality, fresh food. The highlight for me was the Little Necks from the raw bar, which were truly delicious. I also tried the Lobster roll; it was decent, though your standard fare. The Fish and Chips boasted a nice batter and tasted good, but didn't particularly stand out. The accompanying fries were pretty satisfying as well. Impressive was the service—attentive and swift—even in the midst of a bustling crowd. Overall, a solid dining experience with room for some culinary excitement.

Dominican Cravings serves up a selection of comfort foods within the new Essex Market. ((Note: the address is wrong currently on Yelp. The address should be 88 Essex Street, the new Essex Market address. For some reason, Yelp and the owner haven't updated the old address [120 Essex St], despite Yelpers including myself sending in corrections))Dominican Cravings is stall #49, close to the Broome St side of the new Essex Market, 88 Essex Street. it's a brand new looking space. very clean. empanadas and soft drinks viewable in front. small kitchen/grill behind the counter. there is small order counter which accepts cash + debit & credit cards. the food? good to very good. the empanadas are priced around $2.50 + tax. the cheeseburger empanada is the way to go: cheesy, meaty in a crispy shell. and the shrimp empanada is also a nice option. the chicken Chimi is a sauce-dripping long roll sandwich filled with chunks on seasoned grilled chicken and topped with shredded cabbage. the soft long roll is perfect to cradle this savory sandwich. $7 + taxi've been here 5 times trying to order the beef Chimi (a Dominican style sandwich) and each time they haven't had it, despite it being on the menu. maybe it's time to take it off the menu. Thank God there are other great eats to order! also Dominican Cravings serves a traditional Dominican breakfast. a platter of mangu, salami, quesofrito, etc. the problem? they open at 11 am and serve it for less than an hour. lol. why not serve it all day? a variety of patacons are also served here. the service is pretty good and fast. it's inconsistent though. sometimes you get the dipping sauce with empanadas. other times you don't. sometimes they charge tax. sometimes they don't. AND the last time I was here the staff seemed to be arguing with one another and a bunch of customers including myself were kept waiting while they sussed that all out. not super professional imo, but the food is so good so whatevz. drops mic cuz i'm toasting' with these tostonesi outzzz

Just as amazing as my last visit. Such friendly service, Greg is so welcoming. The place has expanded since my last visit. We love the Nonna Maria pizza. Can't beat the flavors and the sauce. All the slices have the perfect crust to them. The white slice with the ricotta is amazing as well. Perfect cream with the crust. And you can't go wrong with pepperoni and jalapeños. We always recommend this place to friends visiting NYC. We go out of our way to come and eat here. Best pizza

Can never go wrong with BCD! We came here exactly noon on a Saturday and were seated immediately for a table for two. I was very surprised since it's always packed. Once we sat down, though, it filled up quickly. All in all, always expect a line. There are two levels of seating and we sat up top. We both ordered the pork soondubu at varying spice levels. I would say that the spice levels here are spicier than the "typical" spice level you would expect. Mild was good for me, but usually I would expect mild to actually be more mild. The soondubu never disappoints and is always perfect for a sore throat and a cold day. All the banchan was great as well! Not many places give you a fried fish as part of the banchan but I enjoyed it. They also gave us brown rice tea which came in a soup bowl and had rice at the bottom which was yummy!

Title: A Slice of New York Perfection

I've found my top pizza spot in NY! Conveniently a quick subway ride from Madison Square Garden, nestled in a charming neighborhood, this gem awaits. The cozy space is complemented by an extra side room for dining in.

The pizza here is truly exceptional – it strikes the perfect balance with cheese, a crisp crust that's never burnt, and mouth-watering toppings. We popped in for a snack, but I was left craving an entire pie. Pro tip: Check in for a complimentary fountain soda. Don't miss out on this pizza haven!

During a recent visit to a local restaurant, I opted for a to-go lunch, selecting the vermicelli rolled beef which seemed like a healthier choice compared to my usual preference for vermicelli with spring rolls. The service was quick, minimizing my wait time—a plus when on a tight office schedule.

The dish, priced at $11, was packed with care; the fish and chili sauce and peanuts were segregated to preserve the integrity of flavors. Once back at the office, everything combined into a delightful, fresh-tasting meal that didn't disappoint. However, it's worth mentioning that while the food was commendable, the choice of a styrofoam container was a letdown. I appreciate sustainability and would have preferred a reusable plastic or biodegradable packaging option.

Despite the packaging misstep, the quality and taste of the meal assure that I'll be ordering from this establishment again.

Upon entering the unassuming eatery, you might be surprised to find that it boasts a Michelin Star. The ambiance strikes a perfect balance between laid-back and welcoming, without a hint of stuffiness often associated with fine dining. The cuisine, however, leaves no doubt about its prestigious accolades.

The culinary journey commenced with the shrimp toast, a delightful nod to dim sum, delivering a lighter and more refined crunch. Next, the chicken liver mousse proved to be a symphony of flavors – savory, sweet, salty, and crunchy – generously spread on petite slices of bread.

Then came the snow crab pasta, a luxurious dish that married the richness of fresh seafood with the clever addition of crumbs for a satisfying textural contrast. The chicken, a dish I had modest expectations for, was a revelation with its moist flesh and paper-thin crispy skin, all resting on a bed of porridge that was reminiscent of a subtle risotto.

Dessert was a tale of highs and lows, with the mascarpone falling short of memorable. However, the petite beignets more than made up for it with their crunchy exterior and warm, soft interior, made all the more delightful with a variety of dips including honey, ice cream, and jam.

This restaurant is now a personal favorite and a recommended dining destination for anyone looking to impress with an understated yet exceptional gastronomic experience.

From the moment we entered, the tantalizing aromas of meats, fried vegetal protein, and sumptuous broth greeted us. Despite the hour-long wait, which we pleasantly passed at a cozy Thai bar across the street, the expansive and well-decorated interior of the restaurant quickly won us over. Nestled comfortably on the long wood benches amid the modern yet slightly gimmicky decor—complete with the occasional birthday mascot—we prepared for a feast.

This place offers an impressive combination of hotpot and BBQ for an all-you-can-eat experience at $25 per person. The sauce station was bustling, and while the restrooms struggled slightly under the crowd, it was a small price to pay for the otherwise great atmosphere.

Service was efficient, if not overly friendly, and the sheer variety of food was staggering. Favorites included the fried tofu skin, winter melon, caviar fish cake pockets, Achoy, and squid. The selection ran the gamut from traditional meats like lamb and beef to the adventurous pig brain and tripe. We indulged in an assortment of balls, fish cake, mushrooms, vermicelli, and more. Our chosen broths, half kimchi and half pork bone, started light but evolved into a richly flavored base for our ingredients.

In conclusion, this restaurant delivered an exquisite budget hotpot experience that felt anything but. It's a gastronomic haven for those seeking value without sacrificing quality.

This was literally one of my favorite to go spots while working in Soho, the cheap lunch special with the 20$ all day special bottle of red or white wine was a good deal...until ICame in with my colleagues to celebrate my last days of work transitioning into my new career. What a disappointment and complete turn off when my colleague found a bolt/screw in his pasta. We all nearly flipped out, not only because of the possibility of him swallowing it...it made us question what was in our food and how could this happen. When we called the server over a woman came over who I believe to be the manager and handled the situation very poorly. She took the plate and said what else would he like...NO APOLOGY, NO SINCERITY. Like imagine finding a bolt in your food and this is your first experience at a restaurant. This was so unacceptable. Even the gentleman sitting across from us lost his appetite...when they noticed no one was touching their food anymore the woman came over and said the entire check will be comp'ed. We felt as if the gentleman who saw the entire incident should have been apologized too as well he could not finish his food. My colleague went to management and communicated this with them before we left and they said they would handle it. Through this poor experience that same gentleman and my colleague exchanged business cards and the gentleman went out of his way to let us know he was not apologized too at all. After this experience I would never come back and it left a bad taste in my mouth as well as my colleagues.

On our recent visit to this bustling restaurant, the staff displayed commendable patience and grace as they accommodated our large group of 180 people – no small feat! Service was swift and courteous, with a touch of personal care that was much appreciated.

We had a pre-selected menu with options including burgers, chicken sandwiches, and Caesar salads. Despite my gluten-free needs, they seamlessly adapted the Caesar salad to suit my dietary restrictions. The highlight, however, was the kind gesture from our waitress who brought out a warmed, gluten-free brownie in sealed packaging – an unexpected and delightful treat.

As I was overseeing a group of students on a school trip, it was crucial that the dining experience ran smoothly. The restaurant exceeded our expectations, and the students left content and pleased with their meals. Kudos to the team for their exceptional service and for making our group outing both stress-free and enjoyable!

Needed to find a new Szechuan place since Szechuan Mountain House in St. Marks is always so packed, and came across Zest, which was a pleasant surprise!My Szechuan favorite soup is the fatty beef picked mustard so I had to have it here and I was not let down! It was deliciously flavorful and not too spicy. The pot is big enough for a few to share if you get other dishes. I came with only one other friend so we got the fatty beef soup and a stir fried pork cabbage dish which was also very tasty!The service was also very efficient and friendly. After out meal, we stayed to chat a bit and even though the restaurant was full, they kept coming over to refill our tea. I will be back to try more of the dishes!

Best pizza hands down in NY!! My bf wanted to come here because it was shown on Spider-Man. I don't really care for pizza but THIS. CHANGED. EVERYTHING. The pizza is on a whole other level. The crust is so thin, but the cheese was balanced perfectly. The supreme has sausage, pepperoni, onion, and mushroom, the right toppings!! Love that they are served per slice. We walked it home to our hotel and it still tasted bombdiggityyy!! We had it 2 times and I wish we had it more! I would go back to NY just for this pizza. I am drooling just thinking about it, ugh!! Don't be deceived by the line because it goes by fast.I'd bring back a whole pizza if I could. Sac, step up your game ????

This place is great. Stopped by cause I wanted a good salad for a quick bite. I got the Greek salad with chicken which was pretty classic but had a really fresh dill vinaigrette that made it really special. It also came with a toasted baguette topped with goat cheese that also elevated the dish. It was a very large salad - probably enough for 2 people with normal appetites but I of course polished off the entire thing. I sat by the bar and I was served very quickly and efficiently. Overall, really fresh, clean, healthy eating options, great service, and great location in Hell's Kitchen on 9th ave. Will surely be back soon.

Title: A Brunch Delight in NYC

Review:
I have an unwavering adoration for this brunch gem in New York City, which has become my go-to spot. No visit is complete without indulging in the Madame Freda, a culinary masterpiece of a sandwich featuring a perfectly cooked egg, generously drizzled with hot sauce, and elevated with succulent duck. Although I've noticed a price increase and the patience-testing 30-45 minute wait lines, the exceptional flavors and the satisfaction that follows are undeniable, making the experience utterly worth it. A must-visit for brunch enthusiasts!

Title: A Gastronomic Delight Worth Every Bite!

I recently dined at a culinary gem where the fusion of flavors left me utterly satisfied yet craving more. The naan pizza was an innovative twist that paired perfectly with the General Tso's cauliflower – both dishes being an absolute yes for any visitor. The butter chicken melted in the mouth, a testament to the chef's mastery of spice and succulence.

Not to be overlooked, the short rib korma was a standout, rich in taste and tender to the fork. While the jumbo grilled prawns were indeed tasty, I found myself longing for another appetizer or perhaps an additional curry to explore the menu further. The mango lassi proved to be the perfect palate cleanser – refreshing and sweet.

Next visit, I'm tempted to indulge in the tasting menu. If you're in search of flavors that sing in harmony, this is the place to be.

Title: Slice of Heaven at Artistic Pizza

In the competitive pizza landscape of New York, Artistic Pizza emerges as a delectable haven of New York-style slices. This small, unassuming spot in a vibrant neighborhood outshines its fancier counterparts with an authentic charm that rivals the best in Manhattan.

The quality of the pizza here is undeniable. The crust is perfectly crisp, the sauce is seasoned just right, and the cheese is delightfully stretchy. It's the kind of flavor that makes even the renowned Artichoke Pizza pale in comparison, which is no small feat.

Service at Artistic Pizza is as warm and inviting as the aroma that greets you at the door. It's a place run by people who clearly love what they do, evident in every slice served. Open late, it's the perfect spot for a post-night-out bite that won't disappoint your taste buds or your wallet.

While the pizza may not be "life-changing" compared to the legendary Joe's or Bleecker St Pizza, Artistic still holds its own with undeniable appeal. It remains a five-star experience for those who appreciate a truly great slice served with a genuine smile.

A visit to Artistic Pizza is recommended without reservation. Just don't look for restrooms—this place is about the art of pizza, not the art of restroom decor. And in the end, that's exactly how it should be.

Title: A Delightful Girls' Brunch Experience

I recently visited this gem on a Saturday afternoon for a girls' brunch and was thoroughly pleased with the culinary experience. The menu variety immediately caught my eye, catering to diverse palates with ease. I indulged in the Irish Brekkie, which was a comforting and hearty choice, while my friends enjoyed the Croque and Smoked Salmon Eggs Benny. Each dish was prepared to perfection, boasting a symphony of flavors that left us all satisfied.

Although I didn't partake in the All You Can Drink (AYCD) brunch special, my friends who did were delighted by the value and quality of the mimosas, berry mimosas, and bellinis offered. As someone who prefers non-alcoholic options, I greatly appreciated the flexibility of ordering food without the pressure of a drink package—something not all establishments offer.

The experience was truly delightful, with every element from food to service hitting the mark. I'm looking forward to my next visit and would wholeheartedly recommend this spot for anyone in search of a stellar brunch destination.

I recently ordered lunch through Yelp from this restaurant and was thoroughly impressed. Not only did the food arrive earlier than expected, which is always a bonus, but it was also fresh and absolutely delightful. I'm eagerly anticipating my next meal from this spot. Highly recommend for a tasty and prompt dining experience!

Tucked away in a modest, no-frills space, this small diner operates on two levels, though my experience was limited to the ground floor. The seating is a tight squeeze, with a handful of cramped booths and counter space, which proved to be a cozy spot for my meal. I went for the "Palace Wrap" and found it to be a straightforward, unfussy option that skipped the frills of sides. Service here was amiable enough, with servers who brought a touch of warmth to the place. Notably, the kitchen was quick to deliver, making it a decent stop for a speedy bite.

Came here for restaurant week and had an incredible meal. The restaurant is so beautiful and elegant, and service was impeccable. We added the wine pairing for $20 extra and it was so worth it. Compared to other restaurants I have tried for restaurant week, the serving size was generous. Every course was full size. We tried a couple of different things but the main stars of the dinner were the truffle waffle fries buried in truffle and the branzino. One of the best I've had! I will definitely return for their fall menu.  They also have their own wine pairing menu for $70 or $80. But you have to make a reservation for it.

Fabulous authentic Taiwanese food! This place is a gem located in the original vintage manhattan Chinatown! The pork chops and salt and pepper popcorn chicken was soooo tasty they are a must get! But not only that the prices are to die for! Very inexpensive for local and tasty asian cuisine! Only downfall is the vintage interior but it brings a good taste of the original Chinatown perspective!

What is this deliciousness that is the **Krabi Seafood Noodles Soup? I had a hunch and I was right that their most interesting dishes are under the "Pure Thai Noodles" section of their menu. The broth was a mixture of tangy, spicy and sweet that reminded me so strongly of my time in Thailand. It came with some red pepper flakes and clear spicy pepper liquid. A drooly four stars.The other two dishes we got were fine but more run of the mill. The Pad See Ew was fine but it had a smoky burnt aftertaste and the chicken was dry. The Pad Thai Noodles lacked flavor in some places showing it was just not mixed or seasoned well. Three stars.Next time I will stick to the Pure Thai Noodles section. Especially since all of the dishes there sound so interesting.

This is one of my new fave ramen places! The staff greeted every person who came in and was very friendly, creating a good atmosphere. The ramen was a good serving of rich buoyant noodles in a rich broth, with plenty of meat and vegetables. There's no way you'll leave unsatisfied.

Title: A Satisfying Korean Feast with Excellent Service

I recently dined at this charming Korean restaurant and left thoroughly impressed. From the outset, the complimentary small dishes and a delightful fried fish set a welcoming tone. The bbq beef entree was succulent, not a hint of dryness, while the spicy seafood tofu soup brimmed with fresh clams and a medley of seafood, each spoonful bursting with flavor.

Portions were generous, ensuring a satisfying meal. Despite the temptation to explore more of the menu, be warned: the dinner rush can lead to lengthy waits. For a more relaxed experience, I recommend visiting during lunch hours. The attentive and pleasant service only enhanced the dining experience. Without a doubt, this is a place I'll be returning to soon.

I recently lunched at Friedmans, sampling their Nova Benny—a delightful dish of poached eggs atop potato pancakes with smoked salmon, all smothered in hollandaise sauce. The eggs and pancakes were impeccably prepared, though the salmon, while tasty, didn't elevate the dish beyond its $19 price tag, which seemed steep for the serving size.

However, the attentive and speedy service, coupled with the classic, detailed interior full of seating, added significant charm to the experience. The super friendly waitress deserves special mention. All in all, I'm pleased to rate Friedmans with a well-earned 4 stars, making it an excellent choice for a cozy lunch or brunch.

Title: Lackluster Experience at Local Hotpot Joint

My recent visit to a hotpot restaurant in the city left much to be desired. On a Tuesday evening at prime dinner time, my cousins and I were surprised to find the establishment nearly deserted. Even with a reservation, we noticed the redundant precaution as the staff barely concealed their disinterest amidst the lackluster ambiance.

Opting for the spicy hotpot, we were directed to a self-service skewer station featuring a sparse selection of meats, vegetables, and other hotpot staples, all priced around sixty cents each. The portions on the skewers were disappointingly scant. At the sauce station, we were taken aback by the additional charge of three dollars per sauce dish.

While the primary flavor of our hotpot was indeed spicy, it lacked the depth and variety one would expect from a richer culinary experience. Regrettably, this visit has prompted me to continue my quest for a more worthy hotpot destination within the city.

This place is great! They had yummy fish and chips and a great fresh Greek salad. I also liked that they had a DJ later on in the day. It's close to the courtyard Marriott if you stay in that hotel so makes it super convenient. It was also modern looking inside. You could choose to sit in the bar part or go in the more restaurant looking part so you get the best of both worlds.

I don't have a wide experience in Taiwanese food but this place was super tasty tapas place. The fried chicken sandwich was no lie spicy but a little fatty for my taste and don't be fooled, it's a large sandwich enough for 3 people to share if you're doing shared plates. I actually really like the Taiwanese sausage (pork) with crispy rice, a good appetizer to share. The Lo Ba Beng did not look THAT amazing but IT WAS. Super savory with mushrooms and soft boiled egg perfectly flavored the rice. My friend and I agreed it was our favorite. I will say the servers weren't super attentive but the food came out super fast (almost questionable) but still tasted great.

I had high hopes for the novel vodka sauce chicken parm slice, but unfortunately, it fell short of expectations. The slice was disappointingly dry, highlighting the need for a generous helping of cheese and sauce to balance out the flavors and textures. While the concept was enticing, the execution left much to be desired.

Finally got to try this pizza shop near Port Authority. Limited choices and no frills pizza shop. Got a slice of the mushroom pizza for $4. Loved the crunchy thin crust and pizza had a hint of lemon which was tasty. No seatings but there area few high table outside on the sidewalk. Great place to grab a quick bite. Would love to try other flavors next time.

When we arrived I was in the mood for a special evening. Instead, I felt like I was eating on an airplane.First off, they put twelve of us on a table that should have held eight. So I'm sitting there cramped between two other folks and this is supposed to be a relaxing end to a day of business dealing? Not happening.I had an Old Fashioned and it was a GREAT drink. Then the little kid in the seat behind me started kicking me. Well, it was actually every waiter in the restaurant. As they walked by our table they would use their off hand to judge where they were. Like a blind person with a cane, they would tap my seat EVERY time going back or forth (with food or not). I don't know if they were irritated that the boss put a chair in their aisle or if it was a habit. Either way, a restaurant with this level of expectations should hip you like an irate stewardess driving the drink cart. We had a few of the appetizers that were off menu. The prawns/large grilled shrimp were very good. I liked the seafood combo thing a LOT.The salad was a standard house salad. I didn't get to order as I had a couple lined up. What came out was about as pedestrian as you could get in this city. Did nothing but fill me up.At a certain point, I wonder if I ordered poorly or they had poor choices to be ordered. I'll share partial blame for the rest of the meal. I skipped the pasta course. I thought it would be too much food. It wasn't. Everyone had some awesome pasta and I just hung out looking at what was the salad.I totally blew the entree. Or, they should never serve that. I didn't want a huge steak as I'd been traveling for much of two weeks and the fish items didn't do it. I was in a chicken mood and this was it. Sad mistake. The chicken with an almond crust was just mealy. The asparagus seemed under cooked. And I was left with enjoying a plain potato. Between the under par entre and the non-stop hammering (even after I said "excuse me" twice to waiters playing paddy cake on my chair) did it in for me. Maybe you will be seated better and definitely avoid the chicken.

After hearing several glowing recommendations, my anticipation was high as we finally decided to dine at this much-lauded establishment. Thanks to the convenience of OpenTable, our reservation ensured we were seated promptly upon arrival.

The service was exceptional from the start, with a helpful waiter who made our menu navigation seamless. We began with oysters that boasted extraordinary freshness, followed by the Cuban spring rolls—an exquisite choice.

The main event, a 5 spice skirt steak, was a culinary triumph. Cooked to perfection, the steak's flavors were complex and satisfying. The accompanying rice and beans, along with a flawlessly balanced hot sauce, rounded out a delightful meal.

In conclusion, this charming restaurant lived up to its reputation, delivering an outstanding dining experience. I'm unequivocally pleased with our decision to venture out and indulge in what this establishment had to offer.

Title: Lackluster Afternoon Tea at a Quaint Spot

I recently visited this establishment for afternoon tea and left with mixed feelings. The charming atmosphere provided a promising start, but the lack of a menu was my first hint of an unexceptional experience. Pricing for additional items and an outline of the fare would have been appreciated.

On a positive note, my request for vegetarian sandwiches was accommodated, yielding delicious egg salad sandwiches, goat cheese tomato tarts, and cucumber chive butter sandwiches. The scones, however, fell short - warm but disappointingly doughy rather than the anticipated crumbly texture. The assortment of sweets failed to leave a lasting impression.

The standard tea offerings from Harney & Sons, like English Breakfast and chamomile, were uninspiring. Thankfully, the 'Paris' flavored black tea did stand out as a highlight in an otherwise mundane selection.

In summary, while the sandwiches were a treat, the overall experience didn't quite meet the expectations set by the charming setting.

Use Yelp's waitlist. It will get you a spot in line and seated, quick and efficient. It's the original location. Small little shop that is hard to spot unless keen to the exterior. (See my picture below)Service was without complaints.Ok, food. First I thought, it's udon, just how good can it be? Blew my mind. Raku almost makes me prefer udon over ramen! Super large portions, so despite the priciness, you are getting your money's worth.  It's about $17 a bowl, a rather large bowl. The noodles are perfectly cooked, bouncy and chewy.  The broth differs depending on what udon you order, but for the two I tried (Gyunan and Niku), both were fantastic. Rich, flavorful, high-quality udon. Highly recommended to all!

Harry's is delicious pizza! Its located underneath Rockefeller Center. There is no seating there, only standing room, but you can just take you pizza outside and sit in the open fresh air and people watch while you eat. The pizza is super delicious and they have so many toppings to choose from. Also its great if you are on a time crunch and just want to eat something fast. Everyone who works there is super friendly and nice. Definitely check this place out!@traveleen_gurl

Mocktails alone make it a trip worth coming. A well deserved ONE Michelin Star- no more no less for sure . That combined with the excellent service, ambience and Decour it makes for a stellar dining experience.Now the food:The complimentary amuse bouche poached eggs with caviar being too solid in the yolk - not perfectly poached -  is the reason I docked a star . But with that awkwardness out-of-the-way I can go on to say that it was truly one of the best dinners I've had in New York City. The strawberry elderflower mock tail left me with an aftertaste that was gently and pleasantly as surprising as a cool breeze in dead of a humid summer day. All the mocktails were fresh And we had the mango lime, strawberry elderflower, raspberry and honey. They were all amazing in their own right. In apps: The oysters really stole the show-they actually came with their own seasoning and no additional sauces. They also had a salad on the menu with beets ricotta and strawberries - the summer triad straight to my heart. The tuna appetizer was still solid but nothing to write home about. Gazpacho look interesting on the menu but I avoided it since I have become a snob since moving to New York City in this regard and living next to Jose Andres mercato - little Spain  for a few days where they have an actual authentic gazpacho stall. We had two main entrées which both wowed and a chef special spaghettini with crab. One Andre was to sea beam in what appeared to be a lemony refreshing garlic sauce. Chef Michael Antony really outdid himself with that. The vegetarian entrée of mushrooms and asparagus also retained a lot of flavor and was very hearty while still keeping it light and healthy. Also going into the docking of the one star the spaghetti ratio of crab was a little low, And while the pasta was perfectly hand cut I have had better in New York. You can imagine that I had to request an extra bowl of flakes of Parmesan in order to truly bring out the flavor in this dish. The dessert was solidly good-a blueberry tart with rosemary butter composing the crust and a necessary dolop of creme Anglais. They call it a blueberry pie but that is a misnomer. It was clearly American Thanksgiving inspired dessert and perhaps I am a little bit biased there with my leaning towards French desserts so take it with a grain of salt but the rosemary did not complement the rest of the tart as well as I would've liked. Still props for the creative thinking.I've heard the cheeseboard is amazing. Would definitely go back just for that next since it is right here in the neighborhood!

I was looking for a burger for a MealPal lunch and was surprised to find this restaurant on my MealPal app. The offering sounded interesting: NOIR burger, which is a black bean burger served with avocado, lettuce, tomatoes, and cumin aioli on a brioche bun. And it was accompanied by a side salad. I had to check this out. I walked into the restaurant to pick up my order and the place was spacious and bustling. The food on everyone's tables looked so appetizing. I got back to my office to chow down on the burger and was very impressed with the construction of the burger and the taste! I checked out the menu online and now am determined to try out the restaurant in person dining in. What a great find!

Came here on a cold winter night, and was pleasantly surprised by the ramen options and portion of the whole grilled squid. Comfort food for sure!We ordered the curry base ramen, the Tonkotsu ramen, and grilled squid. This lighting in this place was quite dim, and I remember the tables were quite close to one another. Still a good place to go for good ramen!

Quaint restaurant in Little Italy with cute decor that makes for an intimate setting. However, the food wasn't memorable to me. I ordered the chicken parm and wasn't blown away at all. I didn't find the sauce to be very flavorful. The chicken wasn't pounded out well enough either and also lacked flavor. My friends really liked their food, but me coming from an Italian family and being raised by a parent with good food taste, I unfortunately wasn't impressed. I wanted to because the restaurant was so cute and the staff was really friendly and hardworking. They earn the stars for a nice setting and nice people.

A great ramen place in Chinatown, but after hearing it was called "the best and most authentic ramen in NYC" I was a bit unimpressed. My boyfriend and I came here for lunch on a weekend - The place was empty!There is a wide variety of ramen, ranging from vegetarian, to chicken, to fish, to beef. They have rice noodles but the restaurant is NOT gluten-free friendly. The waitress was very helpful in making selections from the menu, but I was only able to order rice noodles and vegetables in a basic chicken broth because I can't have gluten.This is a good stop if you're in the mood for ramen in Chinatown, but I wouldn't necessarily call it "the best ramen in NYC."

When we were in Chinatown-NYC, we were looking for a restaurant that takes credit cards. YunShang Rice Noodle House is one of the restaurants that take credit cards. Also, it is one of the restaurants that is clean.YunShang Rice Noodle soup reminds me of pho and ramen. They serve their soup in a hot pot so it is kind of like shabu-shabu. You need to add your meat, ingredients, and the noodles to the boiling broth. They will give you a tray of ingredients that you can add to your soup to make it more delicious. My sister ordered the one with the coconut curry sauce while my SO ordered the plain rice noodle soup. The broth are very delicious. They also gave us a free noodle refill, which is great. As for me, I ordered salted crispy chicken. It was good as well, but I wasn't a fan of their dipping sauce. I think it was mostly spicy mayo.The restaurant was really clean, especially if you compare it to the other restaurants in Chinatown. The servers were also nice as well. We will mostly comeback when we are in the area.

Extra tiny burger spot - they have 4-6 stools to sorta sit but no tables. We found this spot on Ritual App. We ordered ahead and it was ready to go within 10minutes! We tried the Thursday chipotle special- burger, with sautéed onions and bacon.  The combo included a small curly fry and fountain drink (self serve) pricing was reasonable and food was good! I didn't like the bun - but otherwise it was good! I wouldn't necessarily recommend to friends or tourists visiting otherwise since it's a grab and go place and there's no where to really sit and eat. It is near Port Authority for those traveling! People also were ordering the milkshakes- we didn't try but they looked good!

Best Vietnamese Restaurant! If you want cheap and authentic Vietnamese restaurant go here!!Location: It is located in Chinatown! The restaurant is big with a lot of seatings! The interior is okay, you go here for food so it is okay if its like a normal restaurant.Service: They are okay, they just take your order and that's it. :)Food: Everything is good here! PHO: all the phos are good!! The noodles are perfectly cook but the main thing is here the soup, it is soo delicious! PORKCHOP: omg they are soo good, thinly sliced and marinated well! Dip it on their sauce that taste like vinegar with fish sauce! PAPAYA SALAD: so refreshing! Sliced fresh with shrimp and bits of cashew!!Price rating: 4/10 very cheap with the kind of goodness they offer!Get the porkchop they are the bomb!! The Pho is good as well! Perfect for any kind of weather!

Title: Upscale Dining Experience at Gramercy Park Tavern

I recently visited Gramercy Park Tavern with my work colleagues, thanks to our national sales director celebrating our annual success. The tavern boasts a rich history and a stellar reputation, accompanied by a price tag to match. At $200 a head, we indulged in a three-course meal that started with a zesty lemon and chicken soup, followed by a delicately cooked tilefish, and culminated in a refined cheese platter.

While the cuisine was undeniably exquisite, I found the portions slightly lacking for someone with a hearty appetite. Although the tasting menu caught our eye, we opted not to explore it further. Nevertheless, the staff's exceptional service shone brightly, contributing significantly to the four-star rating I've awarded the establishment. The attention to detail was apparent down to the spotless, albeit cozy, bathrooms and the thoughtful parting gifts of chocolate truffles and banana bread.

Gramercy Park Tavern is a fantastic dining choice if budget isn't a concern. Just be sure to book in advance, as their popularity keeps them bustling. On my scale, where a 3 represents a satisfactory experience, a 4 denotes something special, and a 5 is absolutely outstanding, Gramercy Park Tavern stands proudly at a solid 4. It was the serving sizes that held back that extra star.

This was my first time at Hooters in NY as I have been to Hooters in other cities. I heard that this location had the worst service but my experience was completely far from it! Our waitress, Trinity, knows what she is doing! She made everything for our friend's birthday special and was so attentive to our whole group even if it was a busy night with other birthdays! I love a good buffalo wing so I was a happy woman when I had my buffalo wings, although, for those that love a spicy wing (a spice that makes them want to cry), they don't have that many choices. The fried pickles and totes were okay, I have had better in other locations, but obviously the wings were the center of attention. The Thai chili sauce chicken wing was also good as well! At the end of the night, we got some complimentary beer since it was our friend's birthday and they even did the whole cake and song which made his night even special. Trinity did a fantastic job making this location and changing our friends' previous experience and for us to even come back! The facility was clean and the place was spacious.

Came here on a Wednesday after work with some friends. The employees were really great, and a member of our party used to work here so they gave us a HEFTY discount which was really nice of them. We sat in a pretty secluded corner which would have been easy to forget about or miss as a server but our waitress was always coming back to check on us and was very attentive. The food was SO good. I got the shepherds pie and a side of fries (I love potatoes, okay?) to split with my boyfriend. So so good, I could've eaten an entire other one and then some. I also liked that the happy hour deals go until 8PM. So many places only go till about 7/730 and by the time I get out of work and get to the bar it's pretty much over so this was nice. I got the rose vodka soda ..... honestly .... skip this .... it was new on the menu so when I asked our waitress if she liked it she hadn't tried it yet so I got it on a whim .... it tasted like college .... Cool spot though and will definitely come back whenever I'm looking for a good shepherds pie or happy hour in the area!

Lured in by the flood of Instagram raves, I ventured out to sample the much-hyped XL-XLB. The wait, a bearable twenty minutes, ended with the arrival of a steaming bamboo plate. Although the novelty of puncturing the dumpling with a provided paper straw piqued my interest, the experience unravelled quickly.

The soup within the oversized bao, which lost its grace upon escaping its doughy shell, didn't pack the punch I expected. Sure, the meat filling was decent, but it lacked the intimacy with the skin that gives smaller dumplings their characteristic charm, turning into more of a chaotic puddle than a culinary marvel. As the bao cooled, the soup thickened into an unappetizing meaty sludge.

In hindsight, the XL-XLB felt more experimental than exquisite, failing to justify its $14 price tag. A one-time trial, not a repeat indulgence.

My friend and I found this place on Yelp when we were in the area. We were a little surprised as we walked in because it's not a proper sit down restaurant but more like a to-go restaurant with limited seatings. We decided to get food to go coz we didn't see any available seats considering it's lunch time. We got Baja Bowl with chicken and Zucchini & Red Peppers with guacamole. The portion is a bit small compared to the price and the taste is ok. They gave way too much beans and I couldn't finish it. I like that they accept credit cards and that they use paper containers. I wish they had more seating space tho. Overall, I give 3.5 stars for this place.

Had a great meal here. I started with the hook line and sinker cocktail - excellent - and had the crispy fish tacos for an entree. I also had a bite of my boyfriend's fried fish sandwich and sweet potato fries. The food was delicious and those fries are up there with some of the best I've had. Awesome spot!Edit 6/2019: the churro ice cream sandwich is incredible, don't miss it.

Bubo is one of my go-to places for a good drink in Murray Hill. It helps that the food is delicious too!I've been here for brunch, happy hour, dinner, and late night drinks. Everything has always been great.Brunch: It's never crowded during brunch and the brunch options are all light, fresh, and delicious. The avocado toast is deceivingly simple, but perfectly seasoned and prepared. Also tried the eggs benedict. The poached eggs were perfectly cooked with a gorgeous runny yolk.Happy Hour: Weekdays from 4-6:30 PM. Fresh $1 oysters. Not much more to say!Dinner: Most of what is served is Mediterranean inspired. So far, I have only had the opportunity to try the mussels, charred shishito peppers, and truffle fries with feta. All three were spot on, and prices are extremely reasonable given the quality.Late night drinks: The bartenders that have served me have always been friendly, but more importantly also made great cocktails. Most of the cocktails are around $12-$14, which is actually quite cheap compared to most of Manhattan. The Boulevardier is honestly one of the best I've had in the city!They have a bar area up front and a larger dining area in the back, which also has its own separate bar.Bottom line: Highly recommended for both food and drinks.

Fieldtrip definitely deserves all of the hype it's been receiving (see New York Times review). JJ Johnson created this fast-casual restaurant in the hopes that it'll be a community spot for to get nutritious food, and it's been executed perfectly. Fieldtrip specializes in rice bowl dishes. All of his rice is non-enriched, non-bleached, and directly sourced from farmers. However, this isn't a build-your-own bowl type of restaurant. JJ crafted each bowl with unique flavors, and you can't go wrong with any order.I came in on a Sunday afternoon, and they unfortunately already ran out of the braised beef and salmon. I opted for the shrimp bowl, which consisted of sticky rice, toasted coconut, and green curry sauce. It was absolutely delicious, with very unique flavor arrangements. The quinoa bao buns are also a must-try! I'm not used to any bao buns without any meat, but these buns were pretty extraordinary. They came with mushroom, corn, avocado, cilantro, mozzarella, and yucca chips. The crunchiness of the yucca chips perfectly complemented the soft bun and quinoa patty. The dragonfruit lemonade was not only pretty to look at but also balanced between sweet and tart. Everything is relatively affordable, and the service here was very hospitable. I'd definitely be willing to make the trek uptown to try the braised beef or crispy chicken rice bowls!

You can never go wrong with walking into a restaurant on 9th Ave but boy were we glad we came here. I was really surprised at the setting of this place, reminded me of a bbq place with the long tables and long chairs.We were seated right. Our waitress June was simply amazing. We did the pick and mix. This is $16 per person. This deal comes with two entrees and rice. Between four people we had 8 entrees.  Although the portion size were small they filled us up. We ordered the spicy calamari,  crabs and turmeric, shrimp and mushrooms,  green vegetables curry, fish tom tom, steamed fish, fried fish and squash. Every dish was simply amazing. Crabs and turmeric was my favorite.  Spicy enough and creamy enough. The squash was also good. Everything was good. Try them all lolIt was a friends birthday and they gave us dessert for free.Definitely will be coming back!

The restaurant was very hot! Omg walked in a sweater through the meal. Totally get it was a warm day, but please make the dining experience enjoyable. Everything came out in odd orders, with starters mixing with mains. The steak tartare was really chunky, wanted it a bit more minced. The food was good but nothing was wow. Don't know that I'll rush back...

El Camion lured me and three friends with the promise of a festive National Margarita Day brunch, but unfortunately, the experience didn't quite hit the mark, landing a 3-star rating.

The highlight was the complimentary frozen margarita that came with my brunch entrée—opting for mango, I was pleased to find it brimming with real fruit, a refreshing and delicious touch.

However, when it came to our food, the kitchen seemed to juggle our orders like a series of hot potatoes. My huevos diablos should have come with pork carnitas and avocado; the avocado made it, but the pork was amiss. My friend's request for steak and eggs sans beans was noted but unheeded; beans appeared anyways. Another’s huevos diablos were marred by hard-boiled eggs instead of the expected poached ones, and a similar egg-based mishap befell the fourth in our party. The staff made efforts to correct these blunders, but it was disconcerting to see each order miss its mark.

Our waitress navigated the chaos with grace, but even her pleasant demeanor couldn't quite salvage a seamless meal. Here's to hoping my next visit finds El Camion in smoother waters.

My friends and I shared calamari, fried chicken, oxtail, and ssam platter to share. Everything was good, but I especially loved the fried chicken because its skin was very thin yet crispy and the meat was very tender. It went really well with their soy sauce. I also highly recommend the ssam platter as it's very filling and so delicious. Instead of just white rice, they served glutinous rice rapped in bamboo leaves that reminded me of Chinese zongzi. In terms of the portion size, I think 2 appetizers and 2 entrees is just right for 3 people. We could've gone for another appetizer but we saved our stomach for the dessert: honey butter chips with vanilla ice cream. IT WAS SO GOOD! They literally drizzle warm honey over crispy potato chips and it tastes amazing with the ice cream.I also got their watermelon gin and it was so delicious! The only downside is that the food came very slow, but I would definitely come back here to try more food.

This place is a classic Italian chain with quality eats. I wouldn't say this place has the best Italian food you could find, especially in NYC. I ordered the Cacio e Pepe and two Empress Gin based drinks. It's a solid place for a quick bite, but I think the dishes are a bit too greasy. My stomach was killing me after I had my dish and I didn't have an appetite for the rest of the day. The Tribeca location is especially nice in the spring/summer because it's opens to the outdoor. I don't know if I'd go again by choice if I had other options in mind, but I would go again if I wanted a cozy Italian lunch/dinner when I'm in the area.

I had a delightful weekend brunch experience at this well-situated restaurant. Arriving at 10:35 on a Sunday morning, the place buzzed with patrons, a testament to its popularity. I'd advise getting there early to avoid waiting in line. My Americano was decent - nothing to write home about, but the pulled pork sandwich was a standout, with its well-seasoned meat encased in a perfectly crispy sweet bun. The scrambled eggs deserve a special mention; they were exceptionally creamy, soft, and smooth. If you're looking for a brunch spot, this one comes highly recommended!

Title: A Lovely Evening at Love Korean BBQ

My party of five descended upon K-town's Love Korean BBQ last Saturday evening, finding a gem amidst the plethora of all-you-can-eat joints. Due to its popularity among a diverse crowd that spans enthusiastic students to cultured elders, securing a reservation online is a smart move to dodge the bustling peak dinner wait times.

The fare was impressive, with a variety of sides including hearty soups and tangy pickled vegetables complementing the high-quality beef and pork options. Service was handled by a friendly and attentive team, justifying the slight premium on the bill. Expect to invest around $30-40 per person, which is reasonable considering the overall experience and without including drinks, tax, or tip.

I’m already looking forward to a return visit for either lunch or dinner the next time I'm in the vicinity.

Have an oyster craving after work?  If you are are around Grand Central Station, stop by Grand Central Oyster Bar... If planning to have dinner, best to make reservations. This place is huge but also a bit noisy when having conversations. Overall food and service were good. At times hard to remember who is your server and we had a minor thing with one of our dishes, but was quickly remedied. There are several bars as well and restroom in the saloon section in the back. Complimentary bread for starters was good.Appetizers: Clam chowder soup was ok - a bit watery for me, but had lots of clams.Fried calamari to share was ok.Oysters rockefeller - was ok, prefer it with bacon and less parmesan cheese, spinach was more of a creamed spinach than expectedMedley of shellfish platter - each of us had our own. Quite filling after appetizers... 8 oysters - 2 each from New Brunswick, NJ, Massachusetts, British Columbia, Washington State  (had to be careful as shells were broken and inside the oysters)2 clams - 1 small and 1 large (a bit to fishy for me)3 mussels covered with mayo - interesting2 coctail shrimp - yumDessert: keylime pie to share...crust was a bit hard to cut through but keylime was good, not tart at all.

I always drooled at their pics on yelp and now I finally got to taste! Two of my friends and I came on a Saturday afternoon. Points for not being crowded. You have to order in front BEFORE you get seated. I wonder if that is a traditional way of ordering. We ended up ordering lumpia ($8 for 5 pieces) and two orders of sisig (pusit [squid, as was recommended] and pork ~$18 each). With two order of garlic fried rice and one order of white rice. We thought it would not be enough but it was way way too much food for the three of us. So make sure you estimate less. The food was really good, very rich in flavor, greasy and crunchy! Lumpia was a solid as well. I wasn't a big fan of the garlic fried rice as had a lot of -burnt- garlic flavor. As the sisigs had a TON of flavor and are really salty, they definitely went better with the white rice to balance out the flavors. Overall great place, tasty food. Service was great, attentive, refilled our water VERY often. The prices were pretty steep though so I don't think this is a place I will frequent often but maybe for special occasions.

We came here with 9 friends and colleagues on a busy Thursday night. We were attracted by the tasting menu and the fun and rustic decor. The tasting menu was served family style. I will say that it was awkward to have a family style dinner with 9 people. The first course was an impressive seafood platter that was full of yummy goodness. However, it was hard for everyone to judge what was a "fair" portion as it made its way around the table. When there is a limited number of something (e.g., shellfish), sharing can leave some people (either at the front or end of the line) with only a morsel. The other courses were very good. The beef was a highlight. It was served with a bone marrow sauce that was amazing. Everyone tore up the candied brussel sprouts but the shishito peppers left nearly untouched. The cocktails were clever and delicious, but expensive. In all, we enjoyed ourselves and thought the food was very good. If I were to come back, I would have happy hour someplace else and order off the regular menu.

3.8 stars... solid tapas and sangria but definitely not the best I've had. The paella was also above average but definitely not something to write home about. The flan was unique as it is mocha flavored. The value and the service were below par thus it's sub four stars in my opinion. The ambience is cozy and intimate but nothing special. 50-50 I will return.

I decided to stop in here for dinner after seeing the Yelp and Groupon+ offers. I was seated immediately and my server was friendly, quick and efficient. I went with the popular and classic Ajisen Ramen which was good ramen, the broth and noodles were on point. I really enjoyed it.  The menu overall was pretty diverse but they are known for their ramen. I also took advantage of their Yelp offer of a free mochi and it was choice of three flavors so I went with the green tea flavor.  The mochi was a perfect end of my meal. I can't wait to return to taste dishes other than the ramen.

During a February 2019 NYC trip, we sought authentic Korean cuisine, a rarity in South Florida. Missing out on Cote, we dined at Hanjan on a Thursday night. The cozy bar and seating set a welcoming scene for two ravenous travelers. We opted for the $60 Korean homestyle dinner, a decision that did not disappoint. Standout dishes included a memorable fish (likely branzino or sea bass) and a succulent pork dish. A surprising highlight was the introduction to "rice beer," an elusive delight we've yet to rediscover back home. The Hanjan experience was truly a feast for the senses.

Docks had a great atmosphere, relaxed yet classy. Docks offers a large variety of seafood, appetizers and salads. The happy hour at Docks is very good with quite a few choices including $1 oysters and various sushi rolls. We had a few oysters each (they come with lemon, ketchup and horseradish). We ate them before a picture could be taken. We also tasted the wings (excellent and slightly sweet and spicy) and the chips with a "fondue" of bleu cheese and bacon. It is not what I'd call a fondue, but it was a very tasty combo of bleu cheese crumbles, bacon and small bits of chive. Docks also has good drink specials at happy hour, which was 4-7 on the day we were there.

Pretty cute spot, pretty formal vibes and a solid menu. Prices are not cheap and the place kind of feels like a mini version of one of the larger Felices. We've come here a lot and you can't go wrong with the pasta, or anything on their menu for that matter. I'm taking off a star simply because of pricing but otherwise it's a great spot!

I enjoyed lunch from this restaurant today, starting with the spicy chicken coconut soup. While it was delicious and brimming with fresh flavors, it was slightly too oily and not as spicy as expected—still very enjoyable. The papaya salad was crisp and satisfying, though the dressing leaned a bit too sweet for my taste. Despite these minor points, the meal was good, and I'll definitely order from here again.

Tonkotsu ramen was delicious! I slurped up all the rich broth, the noodles were a great consistency, and the meat tasted perfect. The textures of the whole dish went together, and the saltiness and umami all balanced each other. A+ service and ambience; Momosan proves that the key to having really great restaurant vibes is a really great music playlist!Sake/drink list was extensive. I like cocktails so we went with the mango matchashu, which was smooth and light and not too sweet--perfect! Will definitely come back!

Title: A Hidden Gem on the Edge of Koreatown

Tucked away from the bustling streets of Koreatown, this restaurant has become one of my top dinner destinations in NYC. Ideal for both romantic dates and family outings, it offers a unique culinary experience that transcends the typical neighborhood Chinese eatery of my childhood.

Welcoming my traditionally hesitant parents to this spot, their doubts quickly dissipated as our feast unfolded. The table BBQ ribeye was notably fresh, despite a slight hiccup with the uneven heat of our personal grill. However, this did little to diminish the delight of cooking our own succulent meat.

The tapas selection was a showstopper. From crispy chicken buns to fried dumplings and roasted veggies, each dish was met with resounding praise, especially the soy garlic wings which we snagged at a happy hour discount.

While the menu could tempt one to splurge, the experience merits every penny. Whether you're a returning patron or a first-timer seeking diversity in your dining adventures, I wholeheartedly endorse this establishment for an unforgettable meal.

Title: "809 - The Go-To Spot for All Occasions!"

If you’re searching for a dining experience that impresses time and time again, look no further than 809. I’ve had the pleasure of visiting this gem for dinner, happy hour, and brunch, and each visit has been nothing short of awesome. The happy hour deals are simply unbeatable – your wallet will thank you!

But it’s not just about the prices. The quality of both drinks and food consistently exceeds expectations, delivering satisfaction with every bite and sip. Adding to the allure is the warm ambience; it’s the kind of place that instantly makes you feel welcomed, as if you've just stepped into the home of a dear friend.

The real highlight, though, is the 809 team. Their exceptional service and genuine warmth make you feel part of the family. This sense of belonging is why I am wholeheartedly committed to supporting 809 FOREVER. Whether you're a first-timer or a regular, 809 is the spot that keeps on giving!

Went here for restaurant week, and thoroughly enjoyed it! The service was very good and the food was awesome! They gave us the wrong dish and quickly gave us the correct dish and told us we could keep the initial dish (free entree woohoo!) Food was super flavorful, loved every bite of it!
Storefront name says it all!Why you line up +'s:+ $1+ Fresh+ Fast+ Thin crust with chewy levels just rightwhy you keep walking -'s:- No seating find a space to stand- Cash only

Title: Cozy Spot with Hits and Misses – Le Sia

Review:

Our impromptu dinner at Le Sia, on a bustling Saturday night, turned out to be a pleasant surprise with no wait for our group of six – a rarity worth acknowledging. The shared plates started strong, with the standout cauliflower dish receiving unanimous acclaim. Pork belly bao and edamame also made a positive impression, though we quickly learned that appetizer portions necessitate a generous order.

Transitioning to the main courses, the short rib ramen was a personal favorite of mine, showcasing a depth of flavor that was sorely missed in the chicken chili ramen, which, regrettably, fell flat for a friend, marred by an oddly sour and spicy broth. Other options like duck salad and fried udon had their moments but didn't outshine the starters.

Service was amiable, yet the comfort of seating could improve – stools without back support and a lack of hooks for personal belongings were minor inconveniences.

All in all, while Le Sia may not boast remarkable culinary feats, it stands as a dependable choice for a group outing, offering a relaxed atmosphere without the weekend crowd. Giving it the benefit of doubt with a 4-star rating, mainly for the ease of seating and the few dish highlights.

my friends wanted indian and the other indian restaurant nearby has such a long wait we found out about this place instead. we called and they said they can have us right away. the place is small and does not look fancy, but in a way it feels authentic. service was quick, no fuss, and friendly. and they deliver the food fastwe got chaat for appetizer, then chicken tikka masala and malai kofta for entree with roti, garlic naan, and pratha on the side. chaat was really good! it's refreshing and light. i like how everything just blends together. by the way, the dish was not spicy at all if you're afraid of spice. the curry was very creamy but taste-wise it was pretty good. although it feels a little bit heavy eventually. the chicken and the kofta was a bit dry for me. all the breads are good though! i mean you really can't mess up naan and stuffs, right?very reasonably priced. i felt incredibly stuffed somehow after dinner. definitely not bad

Came here for lunch today and was seated immediately. There weren't many people here at 1pm on a weekday. Got the sashimi lunch set which was $30 and it came with a variety of small dishes including seaweed salad, tempura (eggplant and pumpkin), miso soup, rice, etc. the sashimi itself was pretty disappointing and not fresh. The cuts of sashimi were very veiny and some pieces were stuck together and very slimy. As you can tell by the picture the color of the sashimi is pretty off and out of all the pieces only the uni and the scallop tasted good. The other pieces were not fresh and I did not even attempt to eat the white tuna in fear of getting sick (cheapest cut of sashimi out there and is known to be difficult to digest). Service was fine although a bit slow as there was only one server.Given it's a korean restaurant it probably would have been better if I had gotten the cooked items but the sashimi set looked appetizing from the pics. Would still give this place a shot the next time I'm in the area but would avoid the sashimi at all costs.

I recently dined at this local Vietnamese spot and was thoroughly impressed with the grilled pork with vermicelli and cha gio (spring rolls) I ordered. Both dishes were fresh, flavorful, and truly authentic – a rare find outside of the typical Chinatown scene. The prices are slightly elevated compared to those downtown, ranging from $15 to $20 per entrée, but this is justified by the generous portion sizes and the upscale neighborhood. Given the longstanding presence of this establishment and its delicious offerings, I have no doubt it will continue to thrive for years to come.

My recent dining experience at Le Jardinier on a tranquil Friday evening was remarkably pleasant. Arriving at 6 PM to an initially quiet space, the restaurant gradually filled with patrons, all the while maintaining an airy and upscale yet comfortably unpretentious atmosphere, complemented by seasonally apt greenery reminiscent of its sister venue, Shun, upstairs.

Service was attentive; our glasses were seldom empty, and the cocktail offerings here edged out those at Shun, albeit the beer selection was adequate yet unremarkable. The menu, skewing towards French with a contemporary American touch, dazzled with its finesse in preparation and delivery. The strategy to share starters proved wise, the baby lettuce salad with avocado epitomizing summer freshness, and the zucchinis with chanterelle mushrooms provided a delightful interplay of textures.

My poached salmon entree was exceptional, avoiding the common pitfalls in salmon cookery, and the mushroom broth was an exquisite pairing. On the other hand, my wife found her chicken portion generous, but the taste was on point with a satisfyingly crisp exterior.

While the menu currently errs on the concise side, which could be limiting for larger groups, the quality of the offerings inspires a return visit. I’m keen to see how the menu evolves with the changing seasons at Le Jardinier – a venue that certainly warrants repeat exploration.
I had the small oxtail lunch. Ladies were nice and the spot was tight and busy. Oxtail was meaty, robust but only a couple pieces. It was a small I believe $8-9.

Venturing into Bond St, I encountered the minor confusion of a multi-level establishment—initially misguided downstairs, then redirected upstairs via elevator. This quirky entry added a touch of intrigue to the dining experience.

Once seated, service was prompt. I indulged in the rose cocktail, an exquisite concoction that easily topped my list of favorite drinks. We started with the scallops and a shareable sushi platter—my memory fails on the exact selection, but not on the freshness and flavor, notably the shrimp which impressively won over my usual indifference to the crustacean.

For the final course, my choice was Bread Pudding and my friend opted for what I recall as Panna Cotta. The bread pudding was nothing short of divine, sealing the meal with satisfaction.

Despite the steep prices, typical of New York, Bond St earns my recommendation for its remarkable cuisine and unique setting.

We had such a wonderful dinner here on our last trip to New York City. Indian food has always been a favorite of mine, so I was excited the second I read the Yelp reviews of Rahi. We were looking for something a bit upscale since we'd be coming from an event, and this place worked perfectly. While it's slightly upscale, there were still lots of people in jeans; so no need to get dressed up if you don't want to. We were sat right away, even though I made the reservation for an hour later than I meant to (I am the queen of messing up the res time.) Our service was wonderful the whole evening, and I was so excited when I saw a drink on the cocktail list that was made with mezcal (always my favorite.) It was a really great drink, and the wine list looked interesting as well.Warning: when they say the 6 chili 5 spice Cauliflower is hot, they mean it. This flavorful dish is made with a house chili blend, 5-spice, spaghetti squash, and lemon, and while it is incredible, it is hot as hell. I struggled through it because it was just that good.For our entrees, we had the banana leaf chicken (bone-in chicken leg, basmati rice, and Kerala coconut curry) and the spaghetti squash kofta (paneer, patty pan squash, and butternut squash korma.) Both dishes were great, but the banana leaf chicken was the star.Don't hesitate to plan a dinner here. We'll be back!

A delightful dining experience and my first 3 Michelin star resto! My friend and I came for the 30 under 30 experience and I must say, it was worth every penny.We were sat right away upon entering and offered the drink menu. Then slowly the scrumptious courses started to flow from the kitchen to our table. My friend didn't like cheese so a couple of her dishes were different from mine. Each dish was plated meticulously and explained well by the server. My fave plates were the signature oysters and pearls, trout and steak. *salivating* The espresso semifreddo was also the perfect creamy and smooth way to end the meal.As a plus, my friend and I were cold and since a server overheard us he offered pashmina scarves to wrap ourselves in. They let my friend keep hers upon leaving. The fact that they heard us mention we were cold and brought out scarves speaks to the service of this restaurant. **Jackets are required for men. My friend's husband had to run back to his apt to get his so be aware! They have jackets you can borrow at the resto if you forget and don't want to purchase one from a store in the mall that Per Se sits atop.

Title: A Feast with a Side of Patience at Morton's Steakhouse

I finally decided to dine at Morton's Steakhouse, a name I've seen across the US but never indulged in until their doors opened this Thanksgiving. The culinary journey was a majestic parade of flavors, starting with a succulent Prime Ribeye steak paired with a trio of delectable dipping sauces. The Burrata salad was a fresh interlude, while the Bacon steak (indeed, a hefty slice of pork belly) was a meal in itself. Gorgonzola gnocchi and Chicken Bianco added a comforting touch of Italian flair, with Truffle fries and Baked onion bread on the side to enhance the experience. Dessert was a dream - the Hot Chocolate Cake and Double Chocolate Mousse were divine closures.

However, the Chopped salad failed to impress, falling flat among the stars of the menu. The greater letdown was the service. Our server seemed to be playing hide-and-seek, resulting in a stretched-out meal that spanned over 2 hours. Constantly flagging down for service is no diner's delight, and having to remind staff repeatedly doesn't sit well when indulging in a fine meal. 

Morton's delivers an incredibly tasty steakhouse experience. The meal would have been nearly perfect with a more attentive server. Here's hoping the service catches up with the kitchen's prowess.

Title: A Lackluster Experience at Nostro

My anticipation for the newly opened Nostro, buzzing with patrons and boasting high Yelp ratings, fizzled after a recent Monday evening visit. Seeking a new go-to Italian spot in the neighborhood, my friends and I found ample seating contrasting the usual crowds.

We started with the Arancini di zucca, which didn't impress due to my aversion to deep-fried fare. The Fiocchi Porcini, although rich and cheese-laden, failed to deliver a flavorful punch, hinting at a missed opportunity for culinary finesse. The Fettuccine Amore was an underwhelming endeavor with an initial fishy blandness mildly redeemed by occasional saucy bites. As for the Fusilli pesto, it was a standard affair, unworthy of a restaurant's menu.

The Tiramisu was our only consolation, pleasing yet overwhelmingly creamy, best shared with a larger group.

In summary, Nostro's offerings fell into the realm of mediocrity. With an array of unexplored, highly touted venues nearby, I see no reason for a return visit.

Title: A Quick Slice Before the Show at Joe's Pizza

As a frequent patron and a Marvel enthusiast, it surprised me that I hadn't reviewed Joe's Pizza until now. Situated conveniently close to the IFC Center, it's the perfect spot to grab a bite before catching a film—particularly appealing to Spider-Man fans who might recall its cameo in the first movie.

Despite its compact size, Joe's can accommodate a small crowd with standing tables and a few side counters, though space is at a premium. I stopped by just before the dinner rush and went with my standard order—a single slice of regular pizza and a Sprite. The slice was satisfying, although in hindsight, a second wouldn't have gone amiss.

Eating at the side counter was less than ideal as the proximity to the evening's growing queue meant frequent jostling, a minor inconvenience in an otherwise enjoyable visit. At around $5, the meal was a steal, and I left just in time to avoid the line that snaked out the door.

For anyone in the area with a hankering for authentic NYC pizza, I'd say Joe's Pizza is a must. Just be mindful of the crowds and consider timing your visit to dodge the rush.

NYC Summer 2019 Restaurant Week Lunch ReviewMy colleagues and i took advantage of Morton's restaurant week lunch menu recently. For $26, you can pick soup or salad for appetizer and an entree. For starters, they gave us a big round bread (with soft whipped butter on the side) for us to share. Both colleagues ordered the Morton's Salad (appetizer) and Grilled 9 oz. Ribeye Steak with Garlic Butter and Mashed Potatoes (entree). They told me that they enjoyed their steak a lot. Meanwhile, I got the Caesar Salad (appetizer) and Broiled Salmon with Beurre Blanc and Mashed Potatoes (entree). I really enjoyed my meal a lot and I left feeling stuffed. The salmon was cooked perfectly and it was still moist. I just wished their mashed potatoes had some brown gravy on top, but other than that it was a delicious meal.The place wasn't super busy when we came at around 12:30pm for lunch. I think there's a lower level that can accommodate larger groups. BTW, you can make your lunch / dinner reservations here on OpenTable.Our waiter was Sebastian. He was awesome. He provided friendly and great service to us. Overall, it was a good experience here for RW lunch.

I recently enjoyed a dinner at this local spot in February and was immediately taken by the cozy ambiance and the excellent service. The menu did not disappoint – the Thai Salad was refreshing, and the Pad Thai was exceptional. The Pad Sew You and Chicken Basil were also standout dishes, brimming with an array of harmonious flavors. I was particularly impressed by the chicken with eggplant dish, which was a delight. This restaurant certainly knows how to blend tastes into memorable meals. I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit.

I came here after checking into the hotel. Was sorta taken aback seeing Los Angeles styled stuff in a taqueria in Manhattan. Like, we're talking L.A. Dodger stuff in the place. I went downstairs and ordered Verdes chicken enchiladas and a house margarita on the rocks. Both were amazing! We were the only people there initially, then the place started to get packed. Great taqueria!

Really yummy izakaya, although I wish they had more variety in foods like skewers. The drinks were good and the service was good. It is a small location located downstairs so be sure to use the yelp waitlist feature to avoid a long wait!

I recently enjoyed an outstanding omakase experience at a very fair price of $150 for 20 pieces. Each selection, starting with the appetizers, was a delightful journey through exquisite flavors, with my personal favorites being the uni, torched salmon, sumptuous toro, mackerel, and the surprisingly tasty giant clam.

Chef Ishizuka's mastery shone through each dish, complemented by his personable approach that added to the overall enjoyment. His deft touch with the torch and soy sauce elevated the simplicity of the pieces, allowing the natural taste of the seafood to take center stage.

The meal concluded wonderfully with a savory miso soup and a delectable sesame mochi macaron. The atmosphere struck a perfect balance between casual and welcoming, devoid of any stiffness sometimes associated with high-end omakase restaurants.

I wholeheartedly recommend this experience and suggest requesting Chef Ishizuka for his delightful company and culinary skill. I'm definitely looking forward to my next visit.

Title: A Hipster Brunch Haven Worth the Wait

I braved the long lines at this hipster brunch paradise, and it didn't disappoint. The vibe is as satisfying as their reasonably priced, delectable dishes—a rare find that's both beautiful and relatively healthy. Their background tunes create a cool ambiance perfect for enjoying their top-notch brunch beverages.

While the place attracts a young adult crowd, families are welcome, and the location is perfect—easily accessible via subway from midtown, with plenty of tourist sights to enjoy along the way. Post-brunch, it's a breeze to hop back on the subway and head to Museum Mile by Central Park. It's a memorable spot that's undoubtedly worth a revisit.

Title: A Must-Try Cheesy Delight at Raclette!

I've indulged at Raclette on two separate occasions and I'm convinced it's a culinary adventure that's not to be missed. The concept is delectably simple yet profoundly satisfying: a blanket of warm, gooey cheese cascading over your plate of meats or veggies. It's a yes in every language!

A tip for fellow diners: aim for the complete version. It trumps the regular with a more generous portion that truly gratifies—the menu could do a better job at highlighting this size difference.

Admittedly, the initial visit spoiled me with multiple cheese scrapings which I found to be reduced to just one on my second visit. The loss of that extra cheese layer was felt, but didn't completely overshadow the experience.

The restaurant's new space complements the overall vibe, making it an even more enjoyable place to dine. So, when you visit Raclette, my advice is simple: go big. You'll leave with a belly full of cheese and a smile just as wide.

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Una Pizza - NYC

After much anticipation, my return to Una Pizza did not disappoint.
