Merely three hours post-landing in NYC, I found myself in the cozy embrace of their bustling dining room, brimming with the tantalizing aroma of authentic pies. A tip for fellow enthusiasts: they offer exclusive pizzas on Friday and Saturday—don't miss out as I did!

Securing a table required some foresight, with a reservation made four weeks ahead for a Wednesday evening. Our group of four was primed for a gastronomic adventure at 8pm sharp.

Service was a standout. Our server exuded an effortless charm, his booming voice a beacon throughout the evening. Initially introducing a trainee who'd be taking charge, it quickly became evident that our main server would be our primary guide. In spite of a surprise fourth guest throwing our ordering into disarray, the staff showcased nothing but grace and patience.

As for the food, the Marinated White Anchovy was an unforgettable starter, each pizza was a masterclass in dough and flavor, and the ice cream a perfect denouement. For a visual feast, peruse my accompanying photos.

In essence, Una Pizza is a must-visit for any pizza aficionado in the Big Apple. One bite, and you're instantly reminded why this place has garnered its cult following.

I went to The Smith for a work event and really enjoyed the experience! We had a private room and were served a number of courses family style, which was really nice because we got to try lots of things! I don't think that all of these are on the normal menu, but I'm guessing that the quality/general flavor palette is the same.Hors d'oeuvres- shishito peppers: well-seasoned and (thankfully) very mild- charred corn & tomato flatbread: well-balanced flavorsStarters- burrata: had a ton of this because it was super great flavor-wise! the only negative thing was that the thicker outside : soft inside ratio was a little high- spicy salmon tartare over crispy rice: I've had similar dishes elsewhere that I also loved--these were delicate and so delicious!- caesar salad: kind of heavy on the dressing but still tastyMain Courses- salmon: really well cooked and not dry at all- brick pressed chicken: didn't really have enough of this dish to judge but it seemed popular- rigatoni with vegetables and parmesan: delicious al dente pasta with a generous amount of cheeseSides- fairy tale eggplant: this dish tasted vaguely Asian and was super addictive- smashed garlic potatoes: these mashed potatoes were very popularThere were also assorted desserts that were standard and less memorable than the rest of the meal. The chocolate chip cookies were chewy and had a sort of molten chocolate interior, but I wished that they had been made with dark chocolate.Overall, it was a great meal, and I'd like to come back here with friends to share lots of dishes! (Warning: be sure to nail down which "The Smith" you're going to; my friend almost went to the other one that is nearby in the Flatiron District.)

Title: A Pleasant Seafood Adventure at a Cozy Spot

I recently had the chance to dine at my friend's favorite seafood restaurant after a movie night, and it was my first visit. The excitement was justified as the food largely impressed me with a solid 4 out of 5 rating.

Our selection included Jonah crab claws, which were decent though not exceptional, but the accompanying salad was a delight with its fresh, fruit-infused Korean style. The Kumamoto oysters, however, stole the show with their outstanding freshness, easily making it to the top of my oyster experiences. The praised sea bass, dressed in a wasabi miso sauce, didn't quite match my palate, feeling a tad salty and heavy, leaving me craving the zestiness of jalapeño.

Desserts were a mixed bag. The coconut pudding was enjoyable, but the mocha caramel brûlée deviated too much into the realm of dark chocolate for my liking. However, the grapefruit sorbet was a revelation, perfectly balanced in sweetness and undoubtedly the best in the area.

Service was impeccable, deserving a full 5 out of 5. Despite arriving just 15 minutes before closing time, we were greeted with warmth and attentiveness without any rush, though I would have appreciated more frequent plate changes.

The restaurant's ambiance scored a comfortable 4 out of 5. The shell-themed decor was captivating, lending a modern yet cozy atmosphere ideal for a date night, though a slightly larger table would enhance the experience next time.

In summary, this is a restaurant I'd happily revisit for the oysters, sorbet, and friendly service, and I recommend it to other seafood lovers looking for a charming dining spot.

Absolutely love the food and their soju. I came here with a group of friends on a Wednesday night around 7pm. The staff was super friendly and we ordered corn and cheese, budae-jigae, stuffed squid, seafood pancake and also melon soju. I loved the melon  honeydew soju. The seafood pancake was crisp and doughy. I loved the budae-jigae. I didn't really like the squid because there was a lot of vegetables inside.

I finally made it to this amazing restaurant.  This amazing Thai restaurant gets really crowded and they do not take reservations on Fridays and Saturdays.  Plus, reservation are taken only for more than 6 people.  Therefore, I highly recommend that if there is a group make sure that everyone shows up on time or else you will have to wait a long time.  Wait time can go over two hours.  It's a great place to have dinner with a group of friends.  Food was amazing and service was on point for a very busy restaurant.  While I waiting for my friends, I had the mango sunrise mocktail, which was very refreshing and held me over until everyone showed up.  Once all my friends showed up, we were finally seated.  Once we were seated, we decided to go family style after observing other diners' main order entrees.  To start we ordered the:Pak Mor Puk ($9): Vegetable crepe dumplings made up of chives, cabbage, jicama, black mushrooms and bamboo shoots and served with roasted bell pepper-peanut vinaigrette dipping sauce. These dumplings are served in few Thai restaurants and is dish that is served to Thai royal families.  The dumplings are to die for.  I wish there would be more than four dumplings per order, but watching how these dumplings are assembled and made, it's no easy task, hence the price of the appetizer.  Por Pia Tod ($9): Crispy vegetable spring rolls made up of glass noodles, taro root, shiitake mushrooms and served with plum sauce. These spring rolls were standard and solid.  They come 6 rolls per order.  Sa Koo Sai Moo ($11): Tapioca dumplings stuffed with minced pork, peanuts and sweet turnips and served with green leaf lettuce.  Another dish that takes a lot of time to make let alone master.  There are five dumplings per order.  These dumplings are the best finger food/bite I have had and there are only a few restaurants that do it correctly, this is one of them.  Definitely worth the $11.  Spicy Chicken Wings ($14): Deep fried marinated tom yum flavor wings with Thai herbs garnished. These wings are a bit messy but tasty. Unsure if it's worth $14 for 5 wings.  Chicken Satay ($11): Grilled marinated chicken on skewers, served with peanut sauce, cucumber relish, and grilled brioche. The dish was standard, glad that the dish included the grilled brioche to make is more complete.  The peanut sauce is really good made the overall dish well balanced.  For the entrees we shared the following:Chicken with Cashew Nut ($17): Spicy chicken with pineapple, jicama, cashew nut, roasted bell pepper, scallions and chili jam. Served with jasmine rice.  The dish was very good and authentically spicy enough for the Thai American crowd that could handle spice.  Kaeng Neur Lamyai Bai Chapoo ($27): Braised jarret beef, betel leaves, curry paste, coconut milk and longan meat, served with Jasmine rice.  This dish is not served in many Thai restaurants, but it was definitely worth the price.  The dish had well balanced flavors and the right amount of spice kick which complemented well with the rice.  We also ordered a side of Steamed Assorted Vegetables ($5), which was a good amount for the price and it complemented the spicy entrees.  Finally, the dish I have been wanting to try and waited over 10 years is Royal Pad Thai ($24) which is pad thai encapsulated in a crepe.  In this case, this dish is made of prawns, shallots, bean sprouts, chive leaves, peanut bean curd and dried shrimp wrapped in net. The dish is beautifully presented and definitely worth the price because it could feed more than one person.  A one of a kind. Can't wait to go back.

The appetizer portions are too small for the price. If you like soba, there is no better place. The soba portions and prices were reasonable. We went on a Saturday evening but made the mistake of not making a reservation and ended up waiting for 2.5 hours for a table. I ordered the jar-jar soba but I liked my friend's goma soba more bc it had more flavor especially if you dip it in their sesame dressing that comes on the side. I would definitely go back to try the other soba dishes. Service here was okay.

This new place is located in Little Italy which seems a bit odd since it's surrounded by all the Italian restaurants. We were excited to try it based on the many positive reviews by the fellow yelpers. Indeed, the place did not disappoint.We went there on a cold and raining day for a late dinner so the place was pretty empty. We were greeted immediately, and service was quick and attentive. There are tables on the main level as well as upstairs. There is one restroom in the basement.Crabmeat soup dumplings: wow, the skin was super thin. I actually broke the first one but handled the rest properly without the soup leaking. They were also very flavorful.Scallion pancake with beef: tasted like the Peking duck as there was hoisin sauce and some cucumber slices inside along with the beef. The skin was crunchy as well. Braised beef noodle soup: not spicy. So much beef which was very tender. Noodles had a great texture and very chewy. Perfect portion.Shanghai noodles with chicken: a bit greasy but tasty.While the neighborhood has become more trendy and many new restaurants have opened that have a pretty high price tag, we were happy to see a new addition in the hood that serves delicious and reasonable food and provides excellent service. Would definitely come back again.

This place is so good for takeout. The sushi is amazing and the rice paper wraps are really good too.I've also been for sit down. Its a LOT more expensive for sit down, but makes sense as i'm sure rent isn't cheap. The sushi is just as good as always. The bread in the clay pot was really good -- and definitely would recommend. It was really oily (they might want to use a little less), but still really good. The hummus didn't stand out, and neither did the guac and chips. TO THE OWNERS: PLEASE OPEN THIS LOCATION AT 11 ON SUNDAYS! There's always 12pm buses/trains from Penn Station and I always want to come here beforehand but can't!

Fantastic tapas restaurant with a cozy vibe, great service and wonderful food.Service.  Bar and table service were very attentive and friendly.Ambiance.  Cozy, comfortable and festive vibe, great for a date or dinner with friends.  Food and drinks.Mezcal old fashioned and sangria were wonderful.  All the tapas plates were well presented and delicious:  - fresh bread - with oil, so good. - fresh, hand cut (at the bar) prosciutto - amazing: - grilled octopus - perfectly presented and cooked. - potatoes in a delicious spicy sauce - asparagus, fabulously flavored- Spanish sausage- amazing, a favorite- Potato omelette - reminiscent of a Spanish omelette in Barcelona. Generous portion, very  good. Everything was wonderful.  Definitely recommend for a tapas restaurant with a date or friends.

Title: A Taste of Georgia with Room for Improvement

During my inaugural venture into Georgian cuisine, I found myself at a charming restaurant with a cozy ambiance marked by warm lighting and dark cherry wood furniture, accented by lovely paintings. Although we missed the opportunity to dine in the picturesque garden-like back area, the front seating was pleasant nonetheless.

The pear-flavored Natakhtari lemonade was a highlight, both aesthetically in its clear green bottle and for its light, refreshing taste. As for the main course, the Fish Kebab, priced at $24, was tender and flavorful but unfortunately, the accompanying vegetables were somewhat lacking in both quantity and texture.

We added an order of Georgian Pork Dumplings ($11 for three), an interesting take reminiscent of soup dumplings but with a thicker skin that detracted slightly from the experience. The pork filling, however, was succulent and well-seasoned.

The dessert, Ideali, was the star of the show – a generously sized honey walnut cake served with a delectable chocolate sauce that left a lasting impression of indulgence.

Service at this establishment was friendly, but the overall experience did not justify the prices, which are typical for the West Village. While not compelled for an immediate return, I am curious about the garden seating and the cheesy bread for a future visit.

Reasonably priced food and reasonably priced drinks. Happy hour was great got there in time. The bar has games you can play with your table. This place is great for watching sports and you can tell it's a frequented bar by the regulars. Quick to get seated, quick to get drinks and quick to get our food. Hands down the best part oF my burger was the fries. The burger was phenomenal too because it was a mix of three meats and cooked perfectly. The bacon on top of my burger was just crisp enough to compliment the meat itself. My only complaint is that the menu on the Yelp page is not the correct menu as the burgers are seasonal. Great customer service though. Will be back when I'm in the area. I also recommend their spicy Moscow mule.

Ummmmm yeah, this place rocks !! There seems to always be a line but it goes quickly! We went on a (our own) pizza / food tour (1 mile radius) and Thai was the best thick pizza !!!! They have both thick and thin but we wanted to try this. We didn't want to stay in line so we ordered a wholePizza that last eat us three days for lunch  lol! Try this place very special !

After eyeing this spot for ages, my friend and I finally dined here for a girls' night out on a Friday at 6:30pm. We dove into the "Pick 10" menu for $38, which didn't disappoint. The sake carafe we chose for $25, a blend of semi-sweet and dry, complemented our selection splendidly.

My plate was a seafood mosaic featuring 2 unis, 2 botan ebi, scallop, fluke, kampachi, fresh salmon, squid, and yellowtail, along with a delightful yellowtail and scallion handroll. The freshness of the fish was impeccable.

Kudos to our waitress for her exceptional attentiveness, ensuring our glasses remained cheerfully filled with sake. The service was as remarkable as the cuisine, cementing our decision to return soon for the tantalizing "Box of Dreams."

Where to begin with this place... Came here for lunch with a party of 10 around noon and was promptly seated. First of all, they already gave off a bad impression when they charge $28(!!!) for a "large" guacamole app, which the waiter admitted only is made from 2 avocados. Highway robbery. My colleagues insisted on getting this and as expected, didn't meet expectations. Two people also ordered Cokes, which were soooo flat that you would think it came from a 2 liter bottle opened 2 years ago. 1 hour later, our food eventually came out. There weren't even that many people in the restaurant so who knows why it took so long. Food was average to below average. My fish tacos were decent, but not fried enough and luke warm. The accompanying rice and beans were astonishingly flavorless. Overpriced Tex Mex food is one of my least favorite things on the planet (the ingredients could not be cheaper), but bad tasting overpriced Tex Mex is even worse. After taking about 1.5hrs for a below average lunch that cost ~$30pp, I HIGHLY suggest spending your time and money elsewhere

Decor is great, but food is lacking. Great spot for a group brunch as it's decorated with a cool edgy nautical vibe. Food was pretty cheap as compared to other nyc brunch spots, but was a bit of a disappointment.I got the crab cake Benedict. The bread/English muffin used was super thin and dry. Almost tasted like it was some generic store brand. For being a seafood restaurant, they skimped on the amount of  crab.

Pizza was delicious but my only complain was they were kind of cheap with the basil as you can see in my pictures. I had a ricotta and margherita both that are supposed to have basil but only two slices made the cut. Sauce is good and I want to say the crust is probably crispy (I ordered take out and took it home) so it's probably best eaten in the restaurant. As for availability, I went around 645 on a Tuesday and people were able to get seats without too long of a wait. I'm sure the weekends are busier. All in all, I'd go back but probably dine in rather than take out. I also appreciate that they specify all their vegetarian pies which are easy to find on the menu. Also if you have a gluten intolerance, looks like they have a fair share of gluten free pies and they have a vegan pie too.

The food here was great. I ordered homemade spaghetti with vodka sauce and both the pasta itself and the sauce were delicious! I'd definitely recommend ordering whatever homemade pasta option they have that day. My friend had the gnocchi which was also good, but a bit on the mushier side. I liked it but I know some people don't like a mushier gnocchi, so it would depend on your preference. The only reason I take away a star is because of the rude manager/owner (not sure what his position was). We stuck around for about 5 minutes after paying our bill, and he came over and basically asked us to leave by interrupting our conversation and saying "Okay, thank you" and stood there staring until we got up to leave. It was super awkward and rude. I understand you might have some tables to seat (even though it wasn't packed), but it could have been handled in a better way. Not cool

I had a wonderful brunch experience at this restaurant, a visit prompted by a friend's suggestion. The menu offerings, though slightly pricey for the portion sizes, were of such high quality that the value was clear. I chose the 'clasico,' a satisfying traditional breakfast with flawlessly cooked eggs, crisp bacon, and perfectly seasoned potatoes – so good that additional salt or pepper was unnecessary.

My companions were equally pleased with their choices, and we shared a delicious chorizo side accented with red pepper. The highlight, however, was the bottomless brunch option. For $18, we savored an array of drinks, with the standout being a refreshing spritz, bursting with elderflower and strawberries.

While the sangria was fairly standard, the service was anything but: attentive yet discreet. Overall, the restaurant delivered an impressive dining experience. Highly recommended for those seeking a delightful brunch with an emphasis on quality over quantity.

This is my first time dining here I heard about it from my brother. Heard raves about how the Mac n cheese is the best thing ever. Well let me tell you this is the creamiest fattiest Mac n cheese I've ever had in my entire life. This is definitely worth the price. The portion is great too, not too small not too large. The presentation is cute too with the lobster tail inside it. I definitely will come back again in the near future to try something else! I'm so glad this place exists and I highly recommend people to come out here and try. I don't give it 5 stars I give it 5000 stars!!!

Title: Discovering the Hidden Gem on Cornelia Street - Palma

My recent visit to Palma was an enchanting experience that I can't help but rave about. Nestled on Cornelia Street, this little gem offers an ambiance that takes your breath away, especially if you get the chance to dine in the incredible back room. It's like being transported away from the hustle and bustle of the city.

The food is nothing short of spectacular, leaving nothing to be desired. Each dish was a delightful surprise, with flavors that tantalize the palate and presentation that pleases the eye. It's clear that Palma doesn't just serve meals; they craft culinary experiences.

I wholeheartedly recommend Palma to anyone looking for exceptional dining in a magical setting. Without a single complaint, I'm already planning my next visit. Trust me, you'll want to share this experience with your friends and return time and time again.

Based on a colleague's recommendation, I ventured to 'by CHLOE.' for a vegan experience due to my dairy sensitivity. The ambiance was quiet and welcoming, without a crowd to contend with. While the menu offered many choices, I settled on the avocado pesto pasta with almond 'parm' - a flavorsome, albeit small, dish for $6. I rounded off my meal with a decent, dairy-free chocolate chip cookie at $2.50. Despite not being entirely satisfied in terms of portion size, the overall taste has piqued my interest to return and sample their burgers.

Title: A Mac and Cheese Haven with a Touch of Home

If mac and cheese is your holy grail, then consider this spot your pilgrimage destination. The menu boasts a diverse selection of around a dozen mac and cheese variations, each served piping hot in a cast-iron skillet that perfectly crisps the edges. Ordering is a breeze with their iPad kiosk system, although patience is a virtue here due to the sometimes lengthy wait. But trust me, it's a small price to pay for cheesy bliss.

As a Philly native, I couldn't resist the Philly cheesesteak mac and cheese. It hit close to home, with the zesty cheese blend and tender steak pieces, though the onions could have been dialed back a touch. Meanwhile, the Alpine mac, a concoction of melt-in-your-mouth gruyere and hearty slab bacon, stole the show. My daughter's verdict? Utterly delicious.

Portions like the Major Munch are generous enough to consider sharing—unless your appetite says otherwise. And for those who tend to overestimate their hunger, convenient self-serve to-go boxes are a thoughtful touch. Whether you're a mac and cheese aficionado or just in search of comfort food that feels like a warm hug, this little gem won't disappoint.

Title: A West Village Gem That Delivers Consistently

Review:

Nestled in the heart of West Village, this restaurant is a rare find that pairs house-made pastas with a selection of great wines. The staff's friendliness complements the warm, cozy ambience that miraculously also feels open and airy – a true rarity in the area. What stands out most is the consistency; I've been a regular since its opening and the quality has never wavered. Their brunch is as commendable as their special Thanksgiving dinner. With every visit, the experience is reliably delightful, free from any disappointment in meal or service. It's no surprise there's always a wait – it's worth it every time.

My friends and I stumbled upon a hidden gem on a weekday post-work dinner in an unassuming part of town. This restaurant might not be on everyone's radar, but it truly is a diamond in the rough. Our group of ten shared an assortment of plates – from noodle concoctions to baked buns and fiery chicken courses.

Standout dishes included the succulent Fried Lamb Ribs, the savory Steamed Beef Shumai (available in lamb as well), and the hearty Xinjiang Big Plate Chicken. The Sautéed Spicy Chicken with Bones, proclaimed as their spiciest offering, failed to live up to its fiery claim but still delivered on flavor, albeit with the authentic inconvenience of bones.

The authenticity of the cuisine is undeniable, reflected both in the food and the predominantly Chinese clientele. While it's a shame this spot hasn't hit everyone's food radar yet, I highly recommend giving it a try when you're exploring the Lower East Side. This place serves up genuine Chinese fare that is not to be missed.

I came here with high expectations. Our food was slightly above average . The service was not.First, we were seated at a table that had a booth on one side and chair on other side , which was fine. But as soon as I sat down, I was really uncomfortable.... my seat (the booth) was SO high in the air, my knees were about 1 inch from the table. I don't know how a bigger person would ever fit. I am petite and I could barely fit. When I asked the "helper" server, I told her my knees were hitting the table - She actually put her hand under the table to see as if I was making it up? You cannot tell me that this particular table has not had this complaint before.  Anyhow , they moved us. There is no dress policy here. People were wearing jeans, sweatshirts, hats, etc. It was very casual. I thought it would be more high end when I looked at prices online- so wear whatever you want!Our server seemed attentive at first, then it died off fast. There was another table of 3 people seated in the middle of the dining room  that got all the attention , and I don't know why. Even the manager came upstairs to talk with them multiple times. Our server was talking with them alot and joking around, it became annoying. Manager never said anything to us. Our helper server delivered our food, not our actual server - And he NEVER came by to ask if our pricey steaks were cooked right or anything. We sat for quite a while for refills on water. I couldn't believe how long it took .He wouldn't even glance in our direction so i could grab his attention. Our steaks were very good. We got the strip steak ($55)  and the tomahawk($75) . Garlic mashed were awesome .  The person I was with said the tomahawk could use seasoning . They do not season their steaks... but I just like salt. They also charge  $5 for bread . Most steakhouses you get complimentary bread.  Our bill for 2 was $190 including  $29 tip. I didn't feel be deserved it, but felt cheap not leaving it.  Overall, it was nice. Food good but pricey- don't give you bread. Service was lacking, no one ever asked if the  $55 And $75 steak was cooked property or if it was good at all. At least give me that - ask how it is ! NOT after we were all done!

Title: A Delightful Dining Surprise

After an unplanned visit, my best friend and I were treated to a wonderful dining experience. The restaurant's ambience was cozy, buzzing with a good crowd even on a Wednesday evening, confirming its popularity. Being seated around 6:45 pm, we noticed the place was packed, yet the service remained attentive and friendly throughout our stay.

For our meal, I enjoyed mussels served in a flavorful green curry, accompanied by a generous basket of bread perfect for soaking up the sauce. Although the mussels were a bit firmer than expected, suggesting they weren't the freshest, the curry itself was a hit. On the other side of the table, my friend indulged in a comforting bowl of pho paired with a side of decadent bone marrow, which she described as 'fatty and delicious.'

We were tempted by the cheesecake for dessert, but our satisfying mains left no room for more. The food presentation was pleasing, and every dish we ordered was a testament to the kitchen's culinary skills.

In summary, the restaurant impressed us with its overall quality. Despite the minor hiccup with the mussels, we walked out content, already thinking about our next visit. A solid 4 out of 5 for taste, atmosphere, presentation, and service. A place worth trying, especially if you find yourself looking for a dining spot when other plans fall through.

Title: A Delightful Lunch at Nougatine at Jean-Georges

Our choice for Restaurant Week 2019, Nougatine at Jean-Georges, stood up to its James Beard recognition with flying colors. The swift seating at a cozy table offered a splendid view of Central Park, setting the scene for a memorable dining experience.

Although there were slight variations from the online preview, the Restaurant Week lunch menu didn't fall short of expectations. I indulged in a uniquely complex gazpacho, bursting with fresh berries and a hearty tomato base, followed by a sautéed flounder in a heavenly red curry sauce that was so delightful, it warranted extra bread for savoring every last drop. My mother enjoyed the fresh heart of sucrene salad and a perfectly cooked chicken breast, both of which were met with nods of approval.

Accompanying our meal with a glass of Sangiovese seemed like a choice well made, complementing the flavors beautifully. The service struck a fine balance – attentive yet unobtrusive, adding to the overall excellent dining experience.

The ambience at Nougatine was sophisticated yet welcoming, hosting a diverse crowd from business professionals to leisurely retired couples. It managed to be chic without a hint of snobbery.

In all, my maiden voyage into the world of Jean-Georges was stellar, leaving my palate eager to explore more of what this culinary master has to offer.

Title: Eggxactly What You Need - A Pleasant Surprise at Tom's

I recently dropped by Tom's Diner, a spot some might recognize from Seinfeld, and I was pleasantly surprised, contrary to some less enthusiastic reviews I'd stumbled across online. My visit was devoid of any preconceived notions from the show, allowing me to enjoy the experience for what it was.

The service was the highlight of the visit. A friendly gentleman welcomed us and added us to the waitlist, and our waitress couldn't have been sweeter, humorously addressing my hunger as she promptly took my order with a considerate "ladies first."

As for the food, it's classic diner fare done right. While it may not claim the title of "best breakfast ever," it definitely hits the spot, especially the perfectly cooked sunny-side-up eggs with a gloriously runny yolk. The side of bacon and sausage was equally tasty and well worth sharing.

The diner is decked out with memorabilia from Seinfeld, local sports, and the police department, giving it a charming and homey atmosphere that I found very endearing.

I'd recommend giving Tom's a chance, particularly if you're in the neighborhood. It's a delightful spot that serves up solid food with a side of excellent service.

I had a burger and fries, it wasn't anything to really write home about. Our waitress was very accommodating it being a large of of 14 of us. We got seated on the upper level which we had it to ourselves. She didn't make any mistakes with our order. It's an Irish bar in the city not much to write about.

I've been here twice. Once many years ago for a office christmas dinner and once this year (2019). I came with about a party of 8. We came to the last show of the night. We arrived early and had to wait outside because the prior seating was still leaving. I was a little annoyed by that. It was cold outside when I went. The line starts to form and it's a little messy with everyone fighting to get in. Security along with another person confirms the parties reservation and tickets.Everything was RUSHED RUSHED RUSHED. The servers were no longer being nice and sweet. You can tell everyone was tired and not really wanting to perform anymore. The food tasted like basic bar food. We stuck with the apps.  We had two of the sampler platters. The drinks werent that good. The Drag-o-Rita wasnt not good. It's a blue mess. Dont order it. Same with the apple martini, it's not good.  We ended up sticking to Tequilas and cocacola. Overall I won't be back. It's not worth it.

Dined here wit a couple of friends on a Thursday night. The place was empty when we arrived and there's one person to greet you when you come in. Our waitress was really nice and went over the menu with my friend and I. Each day there's a special plus a selection of specific foods that they've cooked for the day. So when I went there was legume (vegetables), turkey stew, and beef (which they ran out of). In addition to the daily special there are some other specials on the back of the menu you can order. The downside with their menu is that you cannot order all of the other things listed on the other days. We wanted a side of Akra and patat but they ran out or didn't cook that for the day. We really wanted their Mac but they also were out of that; pretty disappointing. They offer a kids menu but I was told they actually don't provide the food that's actually listed on the kids menu yet which was confusing. Like, why have it listed of you can't serve it? Anywho! The food itself was great! The prices were average for a typical haitian restaurant; between $14 and $25. I would definitely call in advance if I were to visit again to make sure they have the foods I would want.

Title: A Taste of Authentic Italy in the Heart of New York

I recently dined at one of the finest Italian eateries New York has to offer and was thoroughly impressed. The menu brimmed with intriguing options alongside beloved classics, each accompanied by a helpful glossary for culinary navigation. While the by-the-glass wine selection was modest, bottle enthusiasts would revel in a more robust offering.

The cuisine was nothing short of spectacular, with portion sizes hitting the sweet spot between ample and indulgent. The staff embodied hospitality, ensuring a delightful dining experience with their attentive service. Prices were fair, with pasta dishes averaging $20 and entrees at about $30, representing good value for the quality received.

The ambiance, albeit occasionally boisterous, contributed to an authentically vibrant Italian dining atmosphere. This restaurant is a must-visit for anyone seeking an exceptional Italian meal in New York.
I know this is nyc's thing but I wish Chicago had pizza shops like this - quick, cheap pizza by the big slice. It screams convenience but not sacrificing quality.

I'm torn how many stars to give this place.  I'll get the negative out of the way first, this place recommends tip on top of the tax so be careful when you are paying, especially if you are splitting the bill with someone.  This place is expensive as it is, so having the recommend tip on top of tax is a big no no.Food - 4, Service - 3, Prices - 2.5I recommend coming during off peak time or you will be in for a really long wait.  The place isn't very big and they are trying to turn the tables around fast.  I think this is also why people say the service isn't as good. I will give workers the benefit of doubt that they are just trying to work as efficiently as possible by cleaning your table as you finish so they can seat as many people as possible.  I do appreciate that and I personally don't mind my table be cleared because it empties the clutter.  The only bad service I do have to note that I did mind was the person at the front when you go to checkin.  They could be friendlier and more welcoming.  They were very robotic and not friendly.  The servers here can also refill the water more often.  Our cups were left empty for a while.  Not related to their service, but they should figure out a way to redesign the door to the bathroom.  There is no where for you to stand when the door opens so you can easily hit someone as you open the door.Shaky fries - if you like fries, get this.  I thought it was so so and I wouldn't order this again.  This was $7 so I would use my money and order something else.Chili Oil Dumplings - this is super spicy so make sure you like spicy.  I can normally take chili oil dumplings/wontons, but this is on another level.  I was barely able to finish one.  So because it was so spicy, I wasn't really able to taste it.  It's also expensive at $10 so I wouldn't get this again either.Crispy Silken Tofu - this was also just okay.  I've had better tofu.  If anything, this could have used more taste.  I've had better and tastier versions of this, and for much cheaper.  This was $9.  Definitely way too expensive.Oyster Omelette - Out of all the small bites, this was the best.  I would definitely order this again.  I am normally not a fan of oyster or oyster omelettes, but I really liked this.  This is also expensive at $12 so you decide whether or not this is worth it.  This should be a few dollars less.The Notorious TFC - this was basically a fried chicken sandwich.  It was very good and absolutely delicious.  My favorite item of the night, but again, also very expensive at $15.  Lo Ba Beng - this was also absolutely delicious.  I loved the flavors and the pork belly was delicious.  The portion isn't that big though, and definitely not worth the $15.  It's a shame because I would eat this all the time, but not at $15 and not for the small portion.Taiwanese Sausage Fried Rice - this is a very inexpensive dish comprised of very inexpensive ingredients.  This should not cost $13.  While this was very good, I don't recommend this at $13. It is a very small portion for the price.Cold Sesame Noodles - this was also very good and out of all the entrees we got this, $13 was acceptable.  It should probably cost $9 or at most $10 because again, this dish is made of very cheap ingredients.  Brooklyn Kura Craft Sake - this was okay.  Definitely not worth the $65.  Save your money for something else that is better quality.  Overall, the food here is great.  The entrees are much better than the small bites.  The small bites were not that great and also super expensive.  If you must come here, get the entrees and skip the small bites no matter how tempting.  I probably won't return since the prices are just too much.  You can get most of this stuff in Queens for a fraction of the price.  I get it's in a high rent area and why the high prices, but this probably won't last at these prices.  Maybe that's why the restaurants on this side of St. Marks don't last long.

There's a reason there's a looping line at this restaurant even before they open. The prices are absolutely reasonable and well below the value of the amazing dishes we got. The drinks definitely come in instagram friendly containers (it's a bit kitschy for my taste, but fun nonetheless). The eel tacos were just unreal, but the edamame dumplings were so unexpectedly delicious that I can't decide which one was better. The steak lived up to expectations. The only dish I was disappointed with was the Mac & Cheese. It wasn't truffle filled enough, but I think the cheese itself was just a bit too burnt and overpowered the actual flavors. Lastly, I'm biased since salted caramel and popcorn are some of my favorite things, but whoever thought to combine these into an ice cream was simply a genius!!!

I finally snagged a table at this in-demand eatery, renowned for its summer crowds, and I wasn't disappointed. Their falafel sandwich was a masterpiece: a beautiful patty enveloped in pita, brimming with fresh veggies and laced with a divine creamy sesame sauce. Complementing the meal was a delightful tea, and the ambiance buzzed with festive Lebanese music that I absolutely adored. The staff radiated friendliness, and service was impressively swift. Despite the drizzle confining me indoors, the cozy cafe with its handful of stools provided a charming dining experience. Every bite of the ample serving tasted fresh. Eagerly anticipating my next visit!

3.5 to 4. Pretty good for being vegetarian I'd say. Service was attentive and checked in often. Water refills were pretty frequent for how busy it was. So my friend decided to join me here as the one wholely vegetarian restaurant during the trip as consolation for all the other places we went to by her choosing. I wanted to try a few different things out of curiosity. We had gotten an order of the Fun Guy dumplings, shishito peppers,the Chic Pea and Sunny Side roll, black garlic ravioli, and an order of the cauliflower. My favorite things were the black garlic ravioli and the fun guy dumplings. The rolls tasted kind of the same to me eating them. They were still tasty though despite that. The cauliflower was tasty, but I wanted more of the sauce along with it honestly. I think the shishito peppers were the only thing that kinda fell through the cracks. The amount of peppers was very little, and the flavor was lacking with mostly char coming through. Everything else worked pretty well though. It was a bit pricey overall, I'd probably check out other vegetarian places first before popping in again.

Small plates of delectable artisanal Italian food. Romantic yet lively atmosphere. It's a tight squeeze and loud yet still quite enjoyable. Our only complaint is the servings are more to the small bite side. We loved it all, cleaned our plates, and wanted more.We ordered 2 drinks. I had the margherita which was more sour and smokey than expected but incredibly well done and strong in just the right way. For appetizer, we ordered the garlic stuffed flatbread. Don't miss this one.For dinner, we ordered stracchino gnocchi, a perfectly prepared poppy seed gnocchi in a chive sauce. Sopressini & Smoked Mussels was an absolute show stealer. The Smokey mussel paired with a slight kick to the sauce was difficult to stop eating. We also had buffalo milk caramelle which added just that perfect touch of sweetness to the meal. Totally addicting.Our waiter was Brandon and he was wonderful. Made us feel relaxed. Showed up exactly when we wanted him. Made great suggestions. And didn't rush us.A truly special place for a special treat or because you can, because it's delicious.Don't miss this place.

The Maze is a GORGEOUS bar/restaurant in Ktown, perfect as a place to chat/drink. Their menu consists of the staple Korean bar food (wings, dukbokki/rice cakes, fries) and much more. My friend recommended this place for their late HH specials (ends at 8!) and I'm glad I got to check this place out because it was aMAZEing~ The Maze is located on the third floor of a small building so you definitely will need to search for the entrance. After going through the elevator of my nightmares (small, cramped and very old), I was relieved and delighted to see the beautiful interior of this place. String lights, low lighting, good music all added to the fun and inviting bar atmosphere. I arrived at 7:30pm on a Friday with a party of 3 and was seated promptly.I really recommend coming here for their HH specials because you can save so much money. Each drink/food was cheaper by 3-5 dollars so just get your butt here early to take advantage of it! We ordered the kimchi cream pasta (delicious), Mexican nachos (oh yes delicious) and the soy garlic wings (too salty, did not like!). As for drinks, we ordered the yogurt soju and a couple of cocktails. I was originally hoping for the yogurt soju to be something light to sip on but NO- that drink is NOT meant for the weak haha. My friend ordered the "Mint to be" cocktail, which we all agreed tasted like sugar so that drink is a no from us. In general, the prices here are not cheap, but decent for HH (considering we are also in Manhattan). The service at the Maze was great in that all of the staff were very patient and sweet. Our waiter took the time out to recommend popular items on the menu after seeing us struggle with deciding what to order. Overall, I can see myself coming back to try new drinks/food items for HH :)

Would be a 3.5 star review (Yelp...we don't live in a integar world - can't be giving out amateur scores (one bite...everyone knows the rules)). My brother and fam (2 nieces) were coming into the Rockefeller area from Philly, and met them at Limani for a Saturday lunch. Fairly upscale atmosphere, but not pretentious and pretty accommodating for our somewhat fidgety 5 and 1 year olds in tow.  We pretty much stuck to the lunch prix fix menu ($37 for app, entree, dessert).  We pretty much ordered to share everything (3 orders, the kiddies were sharing). And we got:Apps:Mediterranean Mezze - Taramosalata, Tzatziki, Hummus, Ktipiti, Tiropita, Dolmades - with ample table bread and pita, this was quite the crowd pleaser! I particularly enjoyed the ktipiti and taramosalata (Grilled Octopus - Tunisian, sashimi quality octopus ($8 supplement) - the other reviews are correct, this is absolute wellllllll worth the supplement. Lightly charred but not chewy, this was delightful. And they didn't skimp on the amount of octopus either - plenty to go around (and thankfully so, wouldn't to throw some 'bows at the table for the last pieces).Avocado Salad - Served with baby shrimp and drizzled with olive oil - a bit underwhelming, honestly - a half scooped avocado, filled with guac (otherwise all normal avocado) with 3 shrimp on top. At the end of the days, it's still [delicious] avocado...but I could eat one at home.Mains:With the kiddies with us, we played it somewhere safe with two orders of the lamb chops - Grilled and served with Greek fries and seasonal vegetables ($8 supplement), as well as an order of the Loup de Mer, Moist and mild Mediterranean Sea Bass served with steamed vegetables.Lamb chops - we ordered these both medium, but one came out a bit on the rarer side (not that I particularly cared all that much...but there was a notable difference between the two orders, and consistency/order accuracy should matter).  Two chops for per - and the chop that I pulled was more than half fat. The two bites of meat I had were tasty, though. Steamed veggies (broccoli and cauliflower) and the fries were fine.Sea Bass - I wish we ordered two of these. Perfectly tender, no frills, whole fish, with a little bit of olive oil. Delicious.Dessert: We ordered:Karidopita - walnut cake with ice cream - loved the walnut infusion, but a bit on the sweet side, ice cream ironically helped to cut it; thankfully we got some fresh fruit as well. I mentioned it was my (and my brother's) bday, so they graciously gave us another order on the house. Yiaourti - greek yogurt with thyme honey (and pecans atop) - I think this was the winner. Firm, quasi-tart yogurt, with some sweet, savory honey and pecans for added texture...very nice. Fresh fruit - standard assortment, refreshing.A very nice outing overall, very accommodating staff, though with a couple of miscues, but would still like to come back for a dinner...and especially for that octopus.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Authentic Chinese Delights

If you have a craving for authentic Chinese cuisine, this cozy spot nestled on the third floor is one restaurant you shouldn't miss. It's a personal favorite of mine for good reason! Every dish, from the dim sum to the full-fledged Chinese dishes, is nothing short of spectacular.

The steamed shrimp dumplings will delight your palate, while the Chinese broccoli maintains a perfect crunch. Their fried rice, lavishly dotted with flavorful meat, will transport you to culinary heaven. Both the veggie and pork dumplings don't lag behind in taste either; they're exceptionally good.

One quirky charm of this place is the Lazy Susan on the tables, making it incredibly easy to share dishes with your dinner companions. And while the ambiance is simple and unpretentious, highlighted by playful pops of purple, it's the company and the fabulous food that truly make the dining experience memorable here.

The exterior of the restaurant looks very ordinary but once you step inside and turn the corner around the bar, you will be transformed into an intimate and cozy atmosphere. This location makes a great date spot or nice catching-up place. Perfect on a regular weekday night! For the starters we got the escargot and lamb sliders. The escargot was tender and buttery and sat on a fluffy crisp pastry. It's kind of like a savory tart overfilled with tasty goodness. The lamb sliders were small but perfect for two people. Juicy lamb sandwiched between sweet apple chutney and tangy goat cheese and balanced with creamy aioli. For entree I got the filet de boeuf in medium rare. I definitely recommend this! The filet mignon was sooooo tender and juicy and almost melted in my mouth. It was complemented with a bed of buttery soft potatoes and morels. The portion was very generous. I was too full to finish the potatoes. Probably because we ordered two starters already. We didn't get dessert because we were way too full, but will come back again for another date night or girls night! We had a good time!

I had a chance to dine at this restaurant and tried their Scallion Pancake with beef, which turned out to be a delightful choice. The pancake itself struck a perfect balance between crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, while the beef within was seasoned to a tasty perfection. On the other hand, the kimchi fried rice ball was a bit of a letdown; it came across as somewhat dry and lacked the impactful flavor I was anticipating.

Title: A Taste of Spain at Mercado Little Spain

My culinary journey at Mercado Little Spain, which began with a Yelp event showcasing an array of Spanish delights such as patatas bravas, assorted cheeses with olives, savory sandwiches, and canned mussels with chips, left an impression so savory that it lured me back for more. On my return visit, I indulged in the Pepita Ternera – a substantial and flavorful sandwich – and the exquisite Zucchini, bacon, goat cheese, and hazelnut Coca, a flatbread that did not disappoint with its rich taste and satisfying texture.

Priced at $19, the full sandwich might cause one to hesitate, but rest assured, these portions are generous enough to encourage sharing, enhancing the communal dining experience. To truly embrace the vibrant essence of the Mercado, I recommend sampling a variety of their offerings; their carefully curated selection is a gastronomic portal to the streets of Spain.

An aspect worth highlighting is the remarkable staff, whose versatility and helpful nature across various counters add to the market's authentic and welcoming ambiance. A visit to Mercado Little Spain is not just a meal, it's a cultural immersion worth every penny.

Title: Authentic German Vibe at Reichenbach Hall

I recently celebrated a friend's birthday at Reichenbach Hall, and though I've never set foot in Germany, the atmosphere here was strikingly reminiscent of what I imagine a true German establishment to be. The size of the pretzels alone was a sight to see – enormous and enticing, though I didn't indulge in the food myself.

What particularly impressed me was Reichenbach Hall's considerate menu, offering gluten-free options that catered to one of my friends with dietary restrictions. It's not often easy to find such accommodations, especially in a beer hall.

The beers I sampled were thoroughly enjoyable, each one adding to the authentic experience. Beyond the food and drinks, it was the staff that truly enhanced our evening – their friendliness and top-notch service left a lasting impression.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit to Reichenbach Hall – a little slice of Germany right here at home.

Title: Cozy Spot with Comfort Food Favorites

Nestled above Sweetwater Social, this restaurant offered a welcoming atmosphere for an early dinner. The menu, though concise with a somewhat limited beer selection of four drafts and no bottled options, displayed a diverse range of dishes. I opted for the Cooper Pale draft with its refreshingly crisp flavor.

Appetizers did not disappoint; the buffalo cauliflower paired with a sumptuously creamy blue cheese and the delectably seasoned avocado toast adorned with fresh slices of avocado, tomatoes, and a drizzle of balsamic vinegar were both hits.

Their take on fries resembled those from Checkers but were seasoned with a subtler hint of what tasted like Old Bay, which was quite palatable.

The house fried chicken, albeit not traditionally Australian, was cooked to perfection—a dish I would gladly reorder or potentially swap for the meatloaf on a future visit. The chicken was accompanied by a dollop of ultra-creamy coleslaw and a side of smashed potatoes. The potatoes, though missing a gravy companion, were enhanced with a dash of Cholula hot sauce.

Service was commendable, with attentive primary and secondary servers ensuring a pleasant experience. The happy hour was a bonus, with drafts priced at $5 until 7pm, although a draft size of 12oz was noted.

Overall, the restaurant dishes up comfort food with a finesse that's worth a return visit.

During a recent visit to New York City, my husband stumbled upon a fantastic dining spot that I can't help but rave about. From the moment we stepped in, the service was notably swift and cordial, aligning perfectly with my preferences. Each dish we ordered arrived flawlessly prepared, pleasing to both the eye and palate. We were pleasantly surprised by the reasonable prices and the satisfying portion sizes – a rare and delightful combo in the city. This is definitely a gem I'll be returning to, and I highly recommend you add it to your NYC culinary adventures.

Ivan Ramen was featured on Netflix, and well I guess this was on the list of one of my friends. They just got back from a wedding, and they were hung over. I mean, I probably would be as well if I had to wake up at 5 after a night long of binge drinking. Not to say that I had a long night the night before as well. Anyways, onto the food.We shared a couple of appetizers, the Japanese fried chicken and the tongue-katsu and for the entrée I got the Triple Pork Ramen which was a wet noodle type of ramen. There was no broth in it, however it was really flavorful. You would think that it would be dry, but there is sauce towards the bottom of the ramen. I thought Ivan's was tasty. It was different, and I do believe I've had better. I know, but it's my opinion. There are better ramen spots around NY, but this place wasn't bad at all. I do think it's catered to a certain group of people, so it's not somewhere you would find me going back to. However, if you're new to ramen and you want to keep it safe, this is the place you should go first. TLDR; Ivan's not bad, but safe. The Triple Pork Ramen is a wet noodle and flavorful.

Did not meet expectations. I'm came in there wanting to sit and have a nice meal with my coworkers. Ordered a quesadilla and got a pizza... if they wanted me to fold it myself they why not I make it at home where I can do so.

Title: A Tale of Two Experiences: Rib Joint Redemption

Upon trying this rib joint through a delivery service, I encountered a disappointing experience with a pound of spare ribs that seemed more bone than meat—a costly disappointment considering the by-weight pricing. However, giving the place a second chance in person flipped the script entirely.

The ambiance immediately transported me to what felt like a Nashville eatery, bursting with authentic vibes. Opting to dine in allowed me to pick my own ribs, ensuring I got a meaty, succulent selection that lived up to the establishment's reputation. The ribs were simply delicious—a carnivore's dream come true.

Aside from the main event, the side dishes warranted their own applause. The Mac and cheese, alongside the sweet potatoes, were available for a taste test, both leaving a remarkable impression with their comforting and hearty flavors.

Service at the bar was the cherry on top—attentive and friendly bartenders who made sure my glass was never empty and my needs were promptly met. I left already anticipating my next visit.

In summary, while the delivery fell short, the in-person experience at this rib haven was nothing short of spectacular. I can't wait to come again soon!

If you find yourself in K town and in need of a speedy lunch, this spot won't disappoint. The food quality is solid, and the inclusion of rice and soup with your meal makes it a pretty good value for the money.

I visited this restaurant for a family lunch and was thoroughly impressed with both the service and the cuisine. We started with drinks and appetizers, and the spring rolls caught everyone's attention – all five pieces were served piping hot with a delightful crunch, perfectly complemented by a sweet and spicy sauce. The momentum continued with our main courses: the crispy chicken sandwich and falafel sandwich were spot-on, and the mac and cheese was a creamy delight. Every dish was a hit, making our dining experience truly enjoyable. Highly recommend for a satisfying meal!

Cute little Italian restaurant in Chelsea ... meh ... was there as a party of five and we all enjoyed our dinner. Caesar salad however was not worth $32 .... ceasar salad $18 but I added the shrimp so he charged me for the jumbo shrimp dinner.

Title: A Top-Tier Ethiopian Gastronomic Experience

From the warm greeting upon entry to the vibrant decor, my latest visit to this Ethiopian gem has solidified its position among my top two NYC Ethiopian dining spots. The host's recommendation of Meta beer was a revelation; it's now my favorite Ethiopian brew.

As a connoisseur of Ethiopian cuisine, I can confidently say their veggie platter is a standout. The red lentils packed the perfect spicy punch, while the mushroom tibs were a showcase of seasoning mastery, lush with berbere, onions, and carrots. Yet, the true hero of the meal was the injera – fresh, soft, spongy, and with just the right tang.

Despite my current vegan and low-carb regimen, I couldn't resist indulging in the injera, even taking some home to pair with a homemade spinach omelette – a harmonious combination.

I am eagerly looking forward to my next visit, this time with an Ethiopian American friend in tow, to share the love and flavors of this culinary haven.

Delicious and super flavorful!! Extensive menu was a bit overwhelming at first but you can't really go wrong so long as you like spices and lots of flavor. Had the jambalaya, scallops with noodles in garlic, a few skewers (the wagyu ones were the best), and crab legs. The crab legs were so delicious, but as expected a huge pain to extract. They give bibs for your clothes and gloves, but you should still expect to get a little sticky. Worth it!

Paella paella paella! Yes! Anything you get will be good! We ordered 3 different paellas, 2 servings each and some appetizers, it ended up being enough food for the table depsite what the waiters suggested. We were especially happy we didn't get more because it pretty pricy. However order appetizers because the paellas take time to repare, unless you don't mind the wait. Also keep in mind, this will be an expensive meal despite all the sharing!

My family is Cuban and I grew in a predominately Cuban neighborhood with access to fresh and authentic Cuban food.   I was not surprised that this overly priced, midtown location would miss the mark for me!First of all since when is black beans eaten with yellow rice?  That's a gringo thing for sure!  Surely this place was packed with the corporate suits packing on the yellow rice with black beans.   The authentic way is white rice with black beans and pigeon peas with yellow rice.  What's with this green sauce everyone was drowning their food in? The green sauce is Peruvian if I am not mistaken.  I have had green sauce at Peruvian restaurants and it is very tasty indeed but people should know it is NOT authentic to Cuban cuisine!I took one look at the cafeteria style food, it already looked dry by 1pm so I opted for a Cuban sandwich instead.  I chose the potato sticks in the sandwich but we all know a real Cuban does not have the potato sticks, the steak sandwiches do!  But that was my choice.The taste of the pork and ham was decent enough but the bread was as stale as the soles of my shoes! I sure as heck know what delicious fresh Cuban bread taste like and this bread was horrible! To add to the insult it was $11 and change for a sandwich when I can have a significantly better authentic Cuban in West New York or Union City, NJ for $8.50.  It would have been a nice treat to have a Cuban spot near work but after today's experience I rather wait for weekends and stick to my regular authentic spots.

Title: Mixed Feelings on Brunch at [Restaurant Name]

I ventured into [Restaurant Name] for a Sunday brunch with a 2:30pm reservation. The entrance was a tad confusing, leading me through a bar before finally locating the dining area. Staff were attentive upon seating, with menus promptly provided and our waiter swiftly taking our drink orders. The service was a standout, with the manager's frequent check-ins and even stepping in to place an order for us—a definite plus.

Our foray into the menu began with chicken empanadas, which were just passable in taste and disappointingly small, especially considering they arrived as a duo. I chose the classic breakfast—toast, eggs, home fries, and Colombian sausage—which unfortunately failed to meet expectations. The portions were surprisingly scant, leaving me questioning where the rest of my meal was.

However, the bottomless Mimosa option for an additional $25 was the redeeming feature, offering a generous 90-minute window and a well-balanced blend of juice and champagne. Yet, despite the excellent drinks, the shortfall in food quantity had me walking away with an appetite still very much intact.

Title: A Carnivore's Delight at This Hidden Gem

My quest for exceptional Indian cuisine ended at this charming spot, where the menu promises a twist on the traditional. The rosemary naan was an unexpected delight, challenging my usual aversion to bread with its aromatic flair. The lamb dishes, immersed in a secret house sauce, were the stars—tender, flavorful, and abundant, leaving little room for greens or dessert. While I missed the balance of vegetables on my plate, the generous meat portions justify the cost for hearty eaters. The service was the cherry on top; our waiter was the epitome of hospitality, accommodating our photo requests and ensuring our glasses were never empty. A visit here guarantees a meal where the meat takes center stage, with service that genuinely cares about your experience. A must-try for meat lovers, indeed! #MeatyGoodness #ServiceWithASmile

Nestled in the vibrant East Village on Avenue A, Village Square Pizza delights with its signature square slices that pay homage to the much-acclaimed Prince Street Pizza. The pepperoni square slice is a must-try, boasting a remarkable crust that's simultaneously crispy and fluffy, topped with a harmonious blend of tangy sauce, ample cheese, and those delectably cupped pepperoni pieces.

However, the unexpected hero of our dining experience was the transcendent white square slice. Defying the typical need for tomato sauce, this slice wowed even the fiercest critics with its garlic-infused base and harmonious mix of melted mozzarella and rich ricotta. The subtle sweetness of the crust leaves you savoring each bite.

The regular and eggplant squares also impressed, though a thicker eggplant slice could better balance the robust sauce. On a less positive note, the thin metropolitan slices fell short with a crust that could be crisper and a sauce needing that extra zing. The sausage topping begged for a more pronounced spice kick.

In conclusion, Village Square Pizza is a standout in the East Village's culinary mosaic, particularly with its square slices. If you stick to those, you're in for an exceptional pizza experience.

Another great location for a quick lunch at by Chloe. Their salads are really good, reasonably priced ($10.50) and delicious! My favourite is their Kale Caesar Salad with mushroom "bacon". My only complaint is that their mushroom "bacon" is extremely salty and their sweet potato fries (even though they say are air baked, could be less oily. However, these sweet potato fries are delicious- even though they taste deep fried. Another great dish is their Spicy Thai Salad. Would definitely come back.

As a consistent patron of Zuma restaurants, I anticipated a delightful experience at this new location, and it did not disappoint. The standout gripe is the inconvenient restroom situation; with just a single facility on the main floor and the primary restrooms tucked away on the second floor, guests in heels might find this a bit of a trek. However, this minor hiccup doesn't overshadow the delectable cuisine that Zuma is renowned for. The staff was impressive, showcasing their efficiency and swift service. In short, despite the bathroom logistics, this Zuma maintains the high standards of culinary excellence and service that fans have come to expect.

Title: Happy Hour Haven; Food Falls Flat

Visited a quaint spot bustling with local workers seeking after-work solace during happy hour with $8 drinks that hit the mark. While the ambiance hits a charming note, the dining experience doesn't quite match up.

The empanadas left much to be desired; tiny portions disguised in an overpowering spicy cloak failed to impress. A staggering $27 for a bowl of salty, mediocre fried rice further dimmed my meal. Yucca fries were passable, though oddly paired with a ketchup that hinted at alcohol, and an unremarkable secondary dip.

Kudos to a personable server who provided a silver lining to the visit. Utilized a Yelp coupon for free yucca fries, which requires an entree purchase – plan accordingly.

Happy hour might draw me back in for a sip, but I'll likely skip the eats and warn others of the tight quarters during peak times.

Passed along this location while exploring! The chicken pieces in the cone were so moist and juicy! Love the concept and it was so delicious! Was not expecting it to be that good!! The cone was crunchy and it was the perfect combination with the chicken. Eat it fast or else the cone will get soft! Perfect for walking around and grabbing a bite!

Arrived 9:30am Wednesday, December 25 [Christmas Day w/ Dad] It's 9am in NYC and many restaurants don't open until 11am. I'm celebrating time spent with my Father. He wanted to spend 4hrs in NYC [9:30 - 1:00] to be exact eating breakfast, stop by Statue of Liberty and walk around slowly lol - as he is 61yrs old and is taking his time:) Ambiance : Retro rustic "open-kitchen" tapas restaurant. Parking : good'ol NYC street parking, suggested transportation Subway, Uber , Lyft Atmosphere : cute Spanish tapas , good music , cool seating , cool low key vibes. This location is inside of the AC hotel. Seating : window street-level , bar , couples and large group seating (14+) Great place to bring friends , family or hangouts with Dad!

Traditional Taiwanese taro ball dessert! Great quality, portion, and price! If you are a taro ball fan, you would know this place is definitely cheaper and comes with bigger portion compare to Meet Fresh lol the taro ball fruit ice had assorted fruits including dragon fruit and mango. Great quality!

Love their thin pizza-like bread with meat on it!  The lamb spring roll-like appetizer is also absolutely delicious!!  The falafel platter was mediocre at best, and wish they had more vegetarian options.  Their tzaziki (spelling) is quite refreshing especially with their warm house bread.  Ordered delivery next day (yes it's that good) through yelp app and not sure what happened but two hours later nothing was delivered and no one seemed to know what happened.  Definitely a dine-in must to try out! Cannot wait to return soon!

Title: Mixed Feelings at 21 Club During Restaurant Week

Having finally dined at the 21 Club during Restaurant Week, I had high hopes based on its convenient proximity to my workplace. The special prix fixe menu offered a decent selection: three appetizers, entrees, and an option to add a dessert for an additional $8. My experience began positively with prompt seating.

For starters, my friend and I both had the Caesar salad, which was fresh but not particularly remarkable. As for the main course, I enjoyed the moist half roasted chicken, while my friend's banquette de beau was perfectly cooked and pleasantly satisfying without feeling heavy.

Regrettably, the service dampened the experience. Our waiter's brusque demeanor lacked the warmth one hopes to encounter when dining out. This was further highlighted by an interaction with the table next to us, where the waiter sharply addressed guests' confusion over the dessert charge, citing a four-year-old policy rather than providing a gentle clarification.

While the food met expectations, the unwelcoming service and the restaurant's typically higher prices lead me to question a return visit. The 21 Club's food may be a treat, but a restaurant experience is more than just what's on the plate.

Title: High Expectations, Underwhelming Experience

I visited the highly-rated pizza spot on a Friday night at 7pm and was surprised to be seated immediately, despite its popularity online. The expansive interior was mostly vacant – a concerning sign for a place boasting over 5,000 reviews.

We opted for the clam pie and a half white/margarita pie, both of which presented well but failed to deliver on taste. The pizzas were disappointingly dry, with the margarita lacking in sauce and the clam pie requiring a frequent spritz of lemon just to add moisture. I found myself abandoning the crust altogether.

The pricing was steep, not reflected in the food quality. Given its rave reviews, this was a letdown. There's no shortage of excellent pizza in NYC, but sadly, this isn't one of them. In short, it was an overrated experience.

Jongro is located on the 2nd floor. There's a sign if you look up outside. I think they are also expanding to the 5th floor but that's not open yet. We came 15 mins before opening, expecting a line, but I guess New Yorkers don't like standing in line. We were the first there and the restaurant still wasn't at full capacity when we left about an hour after. We wanted to try so many things so we opted for the large beef platter. It's definitely too much for 2 people, but we got to try both the marinated and unmarinated meats. The waitresses cook the meat for you which was nice. All the meats were pretty good, but the ribeye steak was a bit chewy. The side dishes were also really good. The macaroni salad is my favorite. They also refill the side dishes without you asking! The only downside was it's pretty pricey for a korean bbq. I guess because the meats are higher quality and they have excelent service. We might try to go back when we have more people in our party so we can try the pork dishes as well!

Yara is by far one of the best Lebanese restaurants around.  Service to ambiance to food quality,  all 5 stars worthy.  Came for Christmas dinner, and in no way did the skimp on service or food!  Falafel are a must, babaganoush is a must, hummus is a must, chicken shawarma is a must, their fresh hot sauce is amazing!  The hit though were the spicy potatoes!  Cannot wait to go back, all the flavors were unique yet complimentary of one another.

After a substantial menu revamp, we recently revisited a restaurant we hadn't been to in years. Opting to sit at the bar, we indulged in bar-exclusive items, each exceptional in their own right.

Their burger has potentially taken the top spot in our hearts, offering a perfectly seared medium-rare patty accompanied by crispy shallots, American cheese, and a unique twist of mango chutney. The fries matched the burger's excellence, shoestring in style yet creamy internally.

The crab pie was a revelation, encased in a flaky puff pastry and filled with a rich umami crab mixture that left a lasting impression on our palates.

A standout dessert was the kalamansi lime tart, paired with Thai curry ice cream; it was a vibrant play on traditional lemon meringue, so refreshing that it alone warrants a return visit.

Our cocktail experience was just as splendid, notably the negroni noir and lime tree arbor. As an added bonus, the house-made seed bread was complimentary, although not served warm.

The service was proficient, striking a balance between professionalism and comfort. We effortlessly secured bar seating around 6:15 pm on a Wednesday and are eagerly looking forward to our next visit.

I had the pleasure of returning to Nur with friends, and it reaffirmed its status as one of my top restaurant picks in the city. The consistency in the quality of food and service truly stands out. The sesame bagel was a delight, and the souvlaki has become a personal favorite. Both dishes are standout choices that I highly recommend to anyone dining here.

Title: A Flavorful Journey with Room for Improvement

My inaugural visit to this bustling hotspot highlighted the importance of reservations—it was teeming with diners upon arrival. The ambiance was visually appealing, yet the proximity of tables left something to be desired, evidenced by a neighboring diner's mishap involving spilled drinks.

Our server, Dang, was a beacon of hospitality, meticulously guiding us through the tripartite menu. A complimentary shot of creamy soup served as a delectable prelude to an impressive assortment of appetizers. The papaya salad was a standout, easily the best in NYC, while the vermicelli cups with curry paste and crab were picture-worthy and a definite must-try. The veggie crepe dumplings (Pak mor puk) were somewhat of a letdown, as the filling tended to escape its delicate wrapping.

The main course presented an interesting twist on the classic pad Thai—billed as 'royal' for its more authentic sauce and presentation—though taste-wise, it aligned with familiar expectations. The Braised Jarret beef (Kaeng neur Lamyai bai chapoo), however, truly impressed with its fall-off-the-bone tenderness.

Regrettably, our appetites waned before we could explore the dessert menu, a misstep we plan to rectify on our next visit. Despite the spatial challenges, the restaurant delivers on flavor and service, ensuring my return.

Title: A Homely Spot for Health-Conscious Pizza Lovers

On a brisk Australia Day evening, my friends and I found ourselves at Biga Pizza, stunned to find a calm oasis amid the holiday bustle. With no reservation on a busy Saturday, we were pleasantly surprised to be seated immediately in the almost empty establishment.

The service shone brightly, with staff eager to inform us of their BYO policy, even pointing out a conveniently located wine shop across the street. Taking their advice, we ventured across for a bottle to accompany our meal.

Our party of four settled on sharing both a panini pizza and a regular pizza. Biga prides itself on a health-focused approach to their pizza dough, and true to their word, the base of our pizzas was noticeably lighter, crustier, and lacked the usual greasiness found elsewhere.

While the pizzas we sampled were decent, they didn't dazzle the palate in a city that boasts an array of exceptional pizza joints. The concept of a healthier pizza is commendable, and paired with the delightful service and atmosphere, it does make for an amiable dining experience. However, unless you're nearby or particularly keen on a less oily slice, Biga may not be worth a significant detour.

In all, Biga Pizza presents a fair option for those looking for a quick, health-conscious bite, but may not be the top pick for those seeking a pizza to remember.

Was torn on three or 4 stars in this one. Hate to say it but the food is very average and some of the dishes were just not good at all. Granted for that many set courses the price is really fair even though most of them are a shared plate. Vibe is definitely cool and boosted it up to 4 given the "experience". Although to be honest there really isn't much of an experience here other than getting ushered into a basement and then picking one song each that the restaurant plays for you. Sake list is phenomenal and both of the drinks we had were delicious (rose was great and refreshing)Fun time but wouldn't run ba

Food was really good. I took off one star since I had made reservations and still had to wait 45 mins to get a table. Once I got to my table, everything from the service to food was amazing! I started off with the Chilli rock sushi and the oxtail dumplings. I usually don't like dumplings but the waitress recommended this specific one and I'm so glad I tried it. The dumpling had a thin outer layer which made the meat so flavorful. I had the beef filet and lobster rice as my entree which was also very delicious. Ended my meal with the double chocolate monkey bread and crying chocolate which was good but not the best dessert I've had. I'd definitely come back for the ambiance and food.

Came here for Restaurant week. It was crowded. Sat down and we ordered. The pasta was very very good. It is made in house and came with a decadent cheese sauce. They topped it off with truffles. Very tasty, a nice tartness with saltiness. I'm glad I shared with my friend because it was rich. The mezze was okay, nothing special. I didn't like the falafel but the baba ganoush was creamy and flavorful. Hummus was normal. Our mains: my friend loved her chicken. You could taste the cinnamon and other unique flavors it was marinated in. The lamb was gamy and rich in flavor. I really enjoyed the sauce it came with.We also ordered flatbreads and they were very good: crispy bread with different toppings but the flavors blended well together.Dessert was very comforting. The gelato creamy and sweet with a strong unique flavor. The atmosphere if the restaurant is busy. It seems it is a popular spot with older patrons. The wait staff is polite and friendly.Mera's Tip: enjoy the gelato

Had a wonderful girls night here! The food was amazingly priced and delicious. Got a watermelon soda (amazing) which was somehow less than 3 dollars. Then the cup of corn with cojita cheese, the perfect amount of spice. We also both ordered the avocado tostado, which tasted very fresh and was also very affordable. Can't wait to come here again. The place is decently loud, but that was perfect for us

Title: Disappointing Pad See Ew Lunch Special at NYC Eatery

I recently ordered the pad see ew lunch special from a local NYC restaurant, and unfortunately, I was let down by the portion size. It was so small that it seemed more suitable for a child’s meal than for an adult — certainly not what I expected for a lunch offering. Understanding the high costs of running a business in the city, I still believe customers deserve a proper meal size that doesn’t leave them hungry. While the pickup service was timely, the sight of a takeout container not even half full was disheartening. As it stands, if you’re in search of a satisfying lunch portion, this place might not be for you. Despite the punctuality, the disappointing serving size means I won’t be returning for a second helping.

Pizza is Fair; It truly is was it is. If you are looking for Quality Pizza - Exit Penn Station and find one of the many great places out there "on the surface". - Nonetheless, this place serves many people who "just need a slice" - They have been around as long as I can remember. I remember eating there when I used to sneak into the City as a kid.

I recently visited a charming little restaurant with a delightful concept – the pasta is cut right before your eyes, swiftly cooked, and tossed in your sauce of choice. Guests can further personalize their dish with a variety of proteins. My visit on a busy Saturday afternoon was surprisingly smooth, with no waiting time.

The staff deserves praise for their cheerful and accommodating service. I opted for Alfredo pasta with chicken; while the portions were generous, I found the overall dish could benefit from a boost in flavor, and the chicken was a tad too oily for my taste. Despite this, I am intrigued enough by the unique dining experience to plan a return visit, aiming to explore a different sauce and protein combination.

How can you pass up whipped cream ramen?!?!We were in the mood for something different and warm on a cold windy new york night and what better food than steaming hot ramen?
