This was a little hole in the wall so it can def get packed. We were sat near the back and served immediately. My eyes were fixed on the potato based ramen with yuzu kasho noodles and topped with whipped cream. I was in love. I opt for slight spice. The only thing was a little confusing was that nowhere on the menu did it say that it was served with meat and when they dropped off my bowl of ramen it had big pieces of pork in it? Not being a meat eater, I was bummed out. However the base it self was good, the mind is very confused with seeing whipped cream on ramen, but it was a nice balance between spicy, sweet and savory. It was def something different to break up your mundane ramen bowl. Even though it was good, I think this was a once in a lifetime order. The whipped cream was a little too sweet to my liking. Overall the staff was friendly and attentive. I would recommend this little spot for a nice date night.

I recently enjoyed another late-night delivery from IchibanTeik-Out, a spot I love for its extended hours. The chicken arrived still crispy, and the food was piping hot – impressive for a delivery order. The tangy tartar sauce was the perfect accompaniment, complementing the flavors and cutting through the greasy saltiness. The squid tails were equally satisfying, though the overall seasoning was very salty. While I haven't dined in recently, I remember the interior's dark, jazzy vibe, with walls adorned with albums and records, providing a unique atmosphere. Just a heads-up: it's cash-only, and dining in can get quite warm in the summer months.

Solid tacos. The carne asadas were delicious. The meat is what made it super. Meat was quite flavorful and tender.  Highly enjoyable. Although the lines can get long, you can get through rather quickly. The area gets rather congested in foot traffic however. Makes it difficult to find somewhere to sit down and eat.At $4 a taco, I could see myself coming back for more. Would recommend.

I recently visited a local eatery with a craving for some good bibimbap. The staff were welcoming and prompt, a real plus during the busy lunch rush. Pricing was reasonable at $11 for a beef bibimbap. While the beef was tender and well-seasoned, sadly, the rest of the dish didn't live up to expectations - the vegetables were overwhelmingly salty, overshadowing the dish's usual harmony of flavors. Despite the high ratings I'd seen, the meal itself was a letdown. Nevertheless, the service was commendable for its speed and friendliness.

Really great sukiyaki! Their beef was of high quality and dipping it in the egg tasted fantastic! It went well with the udon.Also the the beef croquettes was good, but the grilled fish was a little salty.Would come back again for their sukiyaki :)

Beyond Sushi is quickly proving why it's on the path to world domination – their cuisine transcends the "good for vegan" label and earns its place as simply good food, no qualifiers needed. Dining here offers a refreshing diversity of choices, perfect for my semi-vegan best friend who's often relegated to salads and veggie burgers.

Despite the restaurant's recent opening – signage still in its banner phase and the liquor license pending as of our visit on 2/22/20 – the dining experience wasn't marred by typical new-establishment hiccups. We opted for the Fun Guy Dumplings, Spicy Mang and Sweet Tree sushi rolls, complemented by hummus paired with must-order rosemary bread. Save for the inconvenience of having to order the bread or chips separately to enjoy the hummus, the meal was a hit, especially the aromatic rosemary bread served in a whimsical flower pot.

The Sweet Tree rolls were the standout for me, leaving a lasting craving. Our server was top-notch, the atmosphere ideal for a cozy date, and interestingly, the Israeli-style hummus was a surprise hit in this Japanese-inspired venue.

Despite the slight misstep with the hummus serving method, Beyond Sushi has etched a definite return visit in my books. Highly recommend for anyone seeking exceptional vegan (and non-vegan) fare.

Title: Tasty But Pricey - A Girl on a Budget's Take

My dining experience at this restaurant was a mixed bag: good food but at a steep price. On the upside, there was no wait for a cozy table for two on a bustling Friday night. The hostess offered the comfort of self-seating which set a relaxed tone from the start.

We kicked off our meal with the salami and cheese board, which was fairly standard fare. Though the giant meatball came highly recommended, its $29 price tag for an appetizer sized portion seemed excessive to us.

For the main course, my boyfriend and I shared a "large" serving of the pappardelle. The flavors were spot-on, rich, and satisfying, albeit the portion was quite small. Good thing we weren't that hungry; otherwise, we might have left feeling less than satiated.

In summary, if you're willing to spend, you'll enjoy what you eat, but if you're watching your wallet, you might find the experience a tad underwhelming. Three stars - on a richer day, perhaps it would be four.

Delicious square pizza. Spicy pepperoni. Greasy, sinful, addictive. Walls of photos with celebs who feel the same about the pizza. If you're claustrophobic, like I am, then fuhgeddaboudit. Stay outside. Order to go.

I work often at the Mount Sinai hospital, and this is ideally located between several of the main buildings. Unfortunately I've only had the opportunity to try lunch, because I don't often get to this area in the evening, but I wish I did! They have a fantastic selection of fresh delicious seafood and Italian favorites. I have enjoyed their kale salad with grilled shrimp, woodfired pizzas, and grilled octopus. All of which were fantastic!! Can't wait to get back and try more!! Highly recommend!!

I had oysters recently, and I'd been craving them. I live really close to Brazen Fox, so when I walked by one day, I happened to see that they had a sign for $1 oysters all day, every day. Service was absolutely terrible. I waited right by the door, and the waitress who was tapping away at her phone didn't even acknowledge me. Finally, someone came by and told me to sit at a high top table. Then, I waited nearly 10 minutes for someone to pass by so I could stop them and ask to order. There wasn't a designed person to wait for me. I ordered 10 oysters and sweet potato fries (someone here said they were really good). Both were incredibly mediocre. The oysters weren't shucked well, and I ended up getting a mouthful of sand. Moreover, their cocktail sauce is disgusting. I asked for honey mustard sauce, and they gave me a tiny cup that was 1/4 filled. Their fries are also incredibly mediocre. I'm not really sure how you can mess up sweet potato fries, but they were bland and quite limp. When I asked for my check, I also asked the waitress for a to-go cup so I could take the sauce to go (I had a lot of fries left over). She proceeded to get my check...and didn't get me my sauce container. I stopped another waiter and asked for a sauce container, and he literally just walked away. So I left without a sauce container. Needless to say, I won't be coming back here again. For their prices and underwhelming food and terrible service, this place needs new management. Or better food. And waiters.

Title: A Delightful Thai Gem on the Upper East Side

I recently had the pleasure of visiting a charming Thai restaurant on the Upper East Side, a fantastic find that I stumbled upon quite by accident. So impressed, I dined there two consecutive days. The service stood out with its rapid pace, dishes arriving mere minutes after ordering.

The highlight of my visit was undoubtedly the Panang Curry with chicken—a dish I can't recommend enough. Its robust flavors, particularly the creamy coconut milk, made for a truly memorable meal. The chicken dumplings, while tasty, did come with a steep price tag of $9 for five pieces, which felt a tad expensive even by New York City standards.

In summary, this little spot is a great destination for Thai cuisine enthusiasts looking for quick service and intensely flavorful dishes.

Ordered the cowboy breakfast. It was good if unspectacular in that I was hungry and wiped my plate clean.The sticking out point with this restaurant however is the poor service (or lack thereof). We were one of two parties in the entire resataurant celebrating a birthday and the staff took 20 mins to bring coffee to our table after ordering, and at least 45 minutes to bring our food. That's unacceptable with little to no traffic in the entire restaurant. Just a bad experience overall, would not go back

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this local gem where the fried pork chop over rice with pickled vegetables truly lived up to its reputation – absolutely delicious. Additionally, the stir fry rice cakes with shredded pork were a delightful surprise, offering a unique twist on typical noodle or starch dishes. For a sweet finish, the herbal shaved ice topped with an assortment of sweet beans and jellies was not only refreshing but decidedly underrated. It's a must-try on any warm day.

You will see here that for Nicola's the reviewers are all over the place. This is a place like old New York which elicits strong emotions. This is an old old school New York eatery and is was (and to some degree still is) likes and frequented by New York politicians (Pattaki, Patterson etc) and if dress accordingly and you're a regular or become a regular, they take you into the family. But If you are going to come here in shorts and a T shirt then you'd probably be a bit disappointed by the service.Just keep that in mind.Many many years ago this used to be a German restaurant (the whole surrounding Yorksville area was a group of German restaurants and delis and bakeries) and if you are busy enough, under the white table cloths on the table you might still find the original table covers from back then. The food is a proper (mostly Northern) Italian meal! I tried the spaghetti bolognaise and the rigatoni with veal Ragu. Rich, hot, delicious and filling.You will not be disappointed by the food or the ambience (dimly lit) but remember that like old New York this places welcomes you on its terms and once you understand that you are family.

Disappointing experience overall. First of all, they need more opening hours! Closed entirely on Monday and Tuesday AND only open until 4pm on Sunday and never open for dinner?? It was really a challenge to catch this place when they were actually open. When I finally managed to get there on a Saturday at 1pm, the cashier told us apologetically that the chef had gone out to get some ingredients, so she was unable to serve us anything except drinks. She said he would "be right back" but it took more than an hour! When the chef finally returned, we learned that they no longer offer the half-sandwich-in-a-cone option so you have to get a $9+ whole sandwich. The sandwiches themselves are very good, with fresh ethereal bread and tasty fillings. I got the tomato mozzarella one. If I came back, I'd probably ask them to make it with pesto instead of the balsamic glaze, but honestly, it was so much trouble to get a damn sandwich that I doubt I'll bother to come back.

Title: A Delightful Lunch Experience in NYC

We recently visited this gem of a restaurant for a late Saturday lunch and were thoroughly impressed. The staff greeted us with welcoming smiles and service throughout our meal was top-notch. It was evident that the restaurant prides itself on using fresh ingredients, which was reflected in the quality of our dishes. The Rosé wine and beer selections complemented our meal wonderfully and were a highlight.

In terms of value, the prices were very reasonable considering the quality of food and the dining experience provided. The ambiance struck the perfect balance between inviting and comfortable, maintaining a relaxed, casual vibe that was just what we needed for our weekend repast.

Though we only had lunch, the excellence of the meal has us convinced that dinner would be equally exceptional, if not more so. We're eager to return to this restaurant on our next trip to NYC. This is definitely a spot not to be missed!

What a nice bar! I heard about how crowded it can get, but at 6:30PM on a Saturday night, the place wasn't too packed! The place was pretty tiny, with a bar area and a couple seats and tables on the other side. The waiter, who was dressed pretty surfer like, was friendly and checked up on us from time to time the whole night. We took advantage of the Happy Hour and got $6 drinks of Screwdriver and Paloma, which was a frozen drink of tequila, lime, and grapefruit soda. The Paloma did indeed taste like grapefruit, and it tasted amazing frozen! It's crazy how the drink didn't even taste that strong but it certainly hit pretty strong! The food here was pretty delicious as well! We got the highly raved Dodo Dog ($6), Reunion Tacos (2 for $12) and Totchos ($13). The tacos were my favorite! They were bigger than average and their shell is a bit different, as it looked and tasted like the texture of a scallion pancake. The toppings were amazing and the meat was a good oily juiciness! The Dodo Dog was nothing special, and just tasted like I was eating a burger. I now know I prefer hot dogs without lettuce and warm cucumbers, thank you very much. The Totchos plate was huge! The tater tots came topped with nacho toppings, such as guac, minced beef, and sour cream. It was an interesting fusion, and I recommend trying if you like tater tots! Great place overall! I would definitely go back for their food and Happy Hour drinks!

This German restaurant was in a Bavarian pub like setting. This would be a good place for a big group since their tables are really long. This is my first time trying German food. The sausage was flavorful and it went well with the veggies served along with it. Their brussels sprouts was a little too burnt. I think most of their food is a little bland for my liking. Service was pretty slow. We were seated but we waited awhile before someone came over to take our order. Food took long to come out as well.

Finally, out of all the times I've been in NYC, I get to try one of the places that sell NY Pizza. I wanted to see what all the hype is about. During my stay, I went here twice. First time was near closing time, which wasn't busy as much as during lunch time. FYI, if you go during busy hours, the line can go all the way outside. So, make sure you're not super hungry!I tried the cheese, and caprese. Something so simple makes it so good. Thin crust, nice sauce, not too much cheese. It just seemed well-balanced.I would highly recommend and for tourists to try to get a New York feel. Having this restaurant located in Time Square, parking it very difficult!

Title: A Mixed Experience at Cosme

Cosme's inclusion in the top 50 best restaurants may raise eyebrows, yet its thoughtful design with spacious seating brings an unexpected breath of luxury to the NYC dining scene. A steep $19 cocktail price tag suggests premium spirits, though the value proposition may not hold for a simple margarita.

Service is attentive, guiding diners to order twice per head for sharing, though the lack of complimentary starters is a noticeable departure from the norm. The brunch fare impresses, with the mushroom quesadillas ($9 each) tempting the taste buds without an oily aftermath. A standout is the lobster, chorizo, and bean concoction at $27, a pricey but palatable choice I'd revisit.

Chilaquiles, in both green and red sauces, introduce authenticity, although they may not dethrone West Coast offerings in comparison. The much-anticipated duck mole elicited a polarizing review; while memorable, its intense earthiness fell short of my mole experiences in Mexico.

The $70 lamb dish was the meal's crescendo, complete with tortillas, vegetables, and a trio of sauces—a definite reorder. Cosme straddles a fine line with a 3.5-star hovering, its culinary finesse somewhat overshadowed by the hefty bill.

During a recent trip to NYC, I had the pleasure of dining at a restaurant that left a lasting impression. Our server was remarkably attentive, expertly guiding us through the menu as we pondered our choices. The meal was an exquisite journey, starting with the prime steak and dairy-free chicken umbka puff pies, perfectly complemented by a robust red sauce.

The baby lamb skewer was a standout, with meat that was as succulent as it was tender, paired with an unexpectedly delightful salad. The spiralized and pickled carrots, along with diced cucumbers and tomatoes, provided a crisp counterpoint to the richness of the meat.

But the crowning jewel of our meal was undeniably the oxtail stew. The stew, rich with juicy meat falling effortlessly off the bone, featured chickpeas that had absorbed the stew’s savory essence, enveloping the taste buds in layers of flavor. The inclusion of bone marrow added to the dish's depth, ensuring each spoonful was savored.

From the tasteful decor to the exceptional service and culinary excellence, my experience was truly memorable. This restaurant is a must-visit for any food lover in the city, and I will not only recommend it to friends but also look forward to returning on my next NYC adventure.

During a recent visit to a friend in Hong Kong, we were hankering for some Chinese cuisine and he directed us to a local gem. Opting for delivery, we were impressed with the lightning-fast service. The unanimous verdict after devouring our meal? Absolutely delicious! A spot-on recommendation for anyone craving Chinese delights.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this gem in the midtown area, and the experience was nothing short of fantastic. From the moment my friends and I walked in around 5 PM on a Sunday, we were greeted by the absence of a wait line and the promise of great service. The staff did not disappoint; our waitress was the epitome of attentiveness and friendliness.

We dove into the menu, opting for a burger and a chicken sandwich. Both dishes were served quickly, boasting large portions that justified the reasonable prices. The onion rings were a particular delight – super yummy and the perfect side to our mains.

But the crowning glory of the meal was the crazy milkshake – a cookie ice cream sandwich shake that was as decadently delicious as it sounds. It's huge, so I definitely recommend sharing one between two people. Trust me, you'll want to save room for the main meal.

In summary, if you're looking for stellar service, mouthwatering food, and over-the-top milkshakes, this is the spot to hit. I'll surely be bringing more friends here when they're in town.

Title: A Flavorful Feast at the Cajun Boil

I recently visited a local spot renowned for its Cajun boil, and it didn't disappoint. The process is simple: start by selecting your seafood – from lobster to clams – or get creative with a custom boil. Each order comes with the staples of sausage, corn, and potatoes, and you can toss in extras like broccoli or noodles for a nominal fee.

For the seasoning, I opted for the garlic butter, which was rich and aromatic, though the Cajun classic was equally tempting. The spice level is tailored to your preference, ensuring a personalized kick to your meal. The boil was not only delectable but also a playful, hands-on dining experience, perfect for sharing.

The happy hour specials are an added bonus, with $1 oysters on offer. They may be petite, but they pack a flavor punch without the brine overload – a bargain by any measure.

The staff's hospitality rounded out the experience, with my server exuding warm politeness, and even assisting with my plastic bib, a necessity for this delightfully messy meal. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit.

Title: A Slice of Cuba in the Heart of Times Square

If you're seeking an authentic Cuban sandwich in Manhattan without breaking the bank, look no further than Margon. This gem, nestled amidst the bustling streets of Times Square, isn't about flash; it's about flavor.

From the moment you enter, you're greeted with the tantalizing scent of Cuban sandwiches freshly assembled at the door. The secret to their mouthwatering taste lies in their homemade spread—a zesty concoction of garlic, oregano, lime, mustard, pepper, cumin, olive oil, and a blend of spices that sets their sandwich apart from the rest.

For under $10, you can indulge in a masterpiece of roasted pork shoulder, honey roasted ham, melty Swiss cheese, and tangy pickles, all pressed to perfection within a crusty sandwich roll. While the Cuban sandwich is the star, Margon also offers a variety of hearty Latin dishes that promise to satisfy.

The ambience is reminiscent of a no-frills, neighborhood joint with seating tucked at the back of a narrow space. The staff's welcoming nature will make you feel like a local, offering a sense of community seldom found in the area.

My only gripe? Their doors close at 5PM, leaving evening cravings unmet. Yet, for an afternoon delight, Margon hits the spot every time.

Title: Disappointing Visit to The Irish Punt

My recent visit to The Irish Punt in Manhattan was far from the cozy Irish pub experience I was hoping for. Nestled on a side road near the Stock Exchange, this pub sadly doesn't keep up with the stiff competition in the area.

Quality-wise, The Irish Punt was a letdown. The Mozzarella Sticks and the Soft Pretzel with Cheese seemed to be straight out of a supermarket freezer aisle, improperly cooked to a point where sogginess met an unwelcome chill. The pretzel alone was a testament to the kitchen's disregard for serving passable pub grub. Beer aficionados beware: the selection here is underwhelming, and my draft beer was served lukewarm.

Even considering the smaller portion sizes, the food was overpriced, with $9 Mozzarella Sticks, an $8 Pretzel with Cheese, and an $8 draft beer adding insult to culinary injury.

The pub's ambiance does little to redeem it. While the ties hanging from the wall present a quirky touch in an otherwise standard Irish bar setting, the blaring teen pop soundtrack is an ear sore that detracts from any potential charm the place might possess.

The crowd was inexplicably dense for a venue surrounded by superior alternatives. However, one bright spot was the friendly bar staff, who provided welcoming service amidst the underwhelming experience.

Lastly, be prepared for a parking struggle if you're driving—finding a spot in this area is notoriously difficult.

In conclusion, with a plethora of better options at your disposal, I can't recommend The Irish Punt for either food or atmosphere.

Last week's celebration dinner with coworkers at this gem of a restaurant exceeded expectations. From the get-go, the bread basket delighted us, especially the meat and cheese roll-up which was a standout. A myriad of shared appetizers and entrees graced our table, but let’s talk favorites.

The Roasted Mushrooms were a revelation, appealing even to those less fond of fungi. The Spaghetti’s simplicity belied its depth of flavor, leaving us craving more. The Roasted Muscovy Duck was a universal hit, winning over even the duck skeptics among us.

Other notables included the charred yet tender Octopus, the delicate Kampachi Crudo with its light lemony touch, and the Yellowtail Crudo – the best of our crudo selections with a zesty preparation. While the Diver Scallop Crudo was overshadowed by others, the richness of the Duck & Foie Gras Ravioli was indulgent. The Roasted Beet Salad was a generously portioned, vibrant dish, and the Scialatelli, jam-packed with seafood, was a crowd-pleaser.

The meal's crowning glory was the Vahlrona Chocolate Cake – a gooey-centered treat paired with caramel gelato that you simply can't skip.

Would I return? In a heartbeat. The food, atmosphere, and company turned dinner into a celebration to remember.

My friend and myself love good food, we came here as per his decision. And we were not disappointed at all. My gosh!!! The flavors in all 3 dishes were on point. The dim sum we had with the scallion sauce that goes with it was sooo good. The waiter recommended our whole menu, he told us exactly what most people come for and I can see why. I also had the fried pork belly which appeared to be a coleslaw, the whole thing was good. To drink, the waiter recommended a special drink they were making, it was a combo of a few things, rum, absinthe, pineapple among other things. Overall the combination of the food, waiter and vibe, this night was awesome. I would certainly revisit.

Tucked away in the Lower East Side, this cozy ramen shop is a gem with its friendly staff and expert chefs. They offer an array of mouthwatering ramen options at prices that won't break the bank. I indulged in their Minca Shio ramen, reasonably priced at $13, and a side of scrumptious gyoza for $6.50. The ramen bowl was a treasure trove of toppings: bamboo shoots, mushrooms, Cha Siew, a perfectly cooked half egg, and fresh scallions. Not only was the soup rich and savory, but the noodles had the ideal texture. The gyoza had a delightful crispness, elevated further when dipped in the tangy vinegar soy sauce. Although space is limited, the turnover is swift, making it a smooth stop for individuals or duos. A satisfying experience for any ramen aficionado.

Fantastic pizza. The crust is perfectly crispy and the sauce is magic. I got a slice of pepperoni and loved every bite. This place is usually packed, so prepare to wait. The line moves quickly and Is definitely worth the wait. Joe's is perfect for a quick bite that is sure to satisfy your pizza craving. We stumbled in around midnight on a Sunday and there were 7-10 people in line. Joe's is for sure a must stop when in the city.

Title: Outstanding Experience at CajunSea

CajunSea delivered an exceptional dining experience from beginning to end. Despite my high-maintenance requests, such as changing tables without fuss, the staff remained gracious, with a special shout-out to our amazing waiter, Wolfy Jordan, for his exceptional service and warm demeanor. Management, take note: Jordan sets the bar high. His insight on the menu was impressive, guiding me to try the Cajun blend over garlic butter – a choice that did not disappoint. While I tend to be verbose, I'll cut it short: thrilled with my experience, and I will definitely be returning to CajunSea.

It was hard to get a reservation so I just walked in with a couple of friends. Our wait time was about an hour, so it's hard to get a table without a reservation. Our server made up for it and was very helpful with describing the menu and prompt with letting us know when our food would be ready and how long each dish may take.The burger with the thick cut bacon was fantastic. It's hard to pass up bacon when it's that meaty. The sunnyside up egg along with the bacon really but a classic cheeseburger over the top. I'd definitely go back just for the burger.The fried chicken was also better than expected with big pieces of chicken with a generous amount of sauce. It was an amped up level of general tsao's for sure.Potato hash and Mille-Feuille were just ok. I enjoyed the vanilla cream, but the puff pastry just fell apart which I wasn't expecting. My 5 star review is mainly for the service, the burger and the fried chicken. Everything else was 4 stars. The place was also a bit loud, bordering on levels of a night club in terms of type of music and volume. Not a great spot for a date, but fun with a group of friends even if you have to talk quite a bit louder than normal.

~$200 after taxes and tips for sake and 11 itemsOverall, there were some really good dishes, but most of the others were just average. Nowhere near the quality as Nonono or Izakaya Mew =/ Listed from favorite to least favorite:Zeru Teba Chicken Wings $11: these wings stole the show! I don't know what they did to them, but these were the most melt in my mouth, slip off the bone wings I've ever had. The tenderness level is almost un-heard of! My first bite was of the wing tip and it was just this salty, crispy, and smooth bite all rolled into one. MUST get. Caramel Custard Pudding $5: they drizzled wayyyy too much caramel for this but DAMN the pudding is silky and delicious!Seared Fatty Salmon ($10): good but not that fatty, buttery goodness of salmon I would've gotten from NononoSeared Beef Tenderloin ($15): the sear is great! Seasoning is good, but could've been much strongerYellowtail Carpaccio with Scallion ($10): not the best yellowtail, not the best sauce (very sour), and the grilled scallion doesn't go with the fishDeep Fried Octopus & Squid $7: tiny pieces but good crunchChicken Nanban With Tartar Sauce $11: loved the egg salad tartar sauce on top of the chicken, but the chicken meat inside the batter was really fatty (I bit into a lot of just blubber pieces)Salmon & Salmon Roe Claypot Rice $19: should've gotten the shellfish one instead, but this was too basic and didn't have much of a tasteRaw Squid ($5): wasabi is so overpowering! Cold and slimy, but also has a crunch. I wouldn't try againAvocado Tofu ($9): silly me was expecting a avocado pudding/jello type of texture and taste. Really though, just look at the name and picture it as a mix of smashed avocado and silken tofu that's been molded into a rectangle. Skip. I had to add soy sauce to make it taste betterSpicy Tuna and Avocado Roll ($13): loved the tuna, but hated the roll itself - too much rice and it was wrapped around a really strong vegetable/herb that has this minty taste. Can't recall what it is

Playa Betty's was a great  move for a post work Happy Hour following a realllllly long day. Especially in the winter, Playa Betty's is a welcome, tropical escape from the dreary cold complete with decor, music, and service designed to transport you from the city streets to a beach side taco stand.The tacos and queso were delicious and we were glad our vegetarian friend was able to find a dish that  satisfied her Mexican food craving without violating any dietary restrictions.The only disappointment was the lack of frozen drink options. Call me basic, but I'm always down for a frozen  strawberry marg which was sadly not on the menu.  However, not enough to keep me from coming back (especially for those good Happy Hour deals!)

My evening at the latest trendy Korean restaurant in town left me with mixed feelings. Ideal for a date night with its cute and bustling atmosphere, be prepared for a wait – our appetizers bizarrely arrived after the entrees.

The banchan took a staggering 20 minutes to appear, and the kimchi was disappointingly bland; a watered-down version of the vibrant side dish I anticipated. Their Kimchi Pancake, topped with a trendy runny egg, fell short in spice, despite its crispy texture.

While the Bossam Pork Belly was tender and flavorful, it was curiously served without lettuce wraps, perhaps a nod to the upscale setting. The Bulgogi Pot was oversalted and lacked substance, making the price tag feel unjustified. The Assorted Seafood Pot, a pricy variation of army stew, disappointed with soggy noodles and minimal seafood.

The Fire Grilled Beef, albeit tasty with a deep char, was overpriced for the meager portion served. On a sweeter note, the Soy Flour and Black Raspberry Tiramisu shined, prompting an immediate second order after an initial taste. The Black Sesame Panna Cotta, however, missed the mark on delivering its namesake flavor.

In summary, while some dishes like the tiramisu were hits, the overall experience was underwhelming given the steep prices and average flavors.

Went in on Thursday for the seafood stew (mariscado) special and they had ran out! The nice man in the back suggested the shrimp with garlic sauce instead. Did not let me down! Also I found out that the oxtail (Rambo encendio) I love is on Mon/Weds/Fri...but if you have a special in mind make sure you get there early!

Last night, my friend and I revisited our go-to pizza spot to see how it stacks up against nearby Jet's Pizza. With high hopes, I opted for the Sausage and Onion pizza, enticingly drizzled with honey. Unfortunately, the flavor fell short of expectations, and I wouldn't recommend it over their celebrated Detroiter. The mustard pizza caught my eye, but I remain unconvinced it can be classified as true pizza. A pleasant discovery was the option to purchase pizza by the slice—a great approach for those wanting variety or a smaller portion. While this visit was a mixed bag, my affinity for this eatery remains unshaken. I'm eager to try their East Village location and say hello to Khalifa next time.

Various Hard Rock cafes around the world are a bit of a tradition for our family. NYC was a good one! The music wasn't too loud, which it really can be at Hard Rock. Our waitress was fantastic! Hubby ordered ribs, they fell off the bone. Kids enjoyed mocktails and milkshakes. We were a little disappointed in the flatbread. Burgers were good. If you're in Times Square, stop in!

I love good thai food, always a comfort meal to me. Glur is cute and cozy... there are about 6 low tables and a two seater at the "bar" facing the cash register and a two seater facing the window. It was packed for a Tuesday night!We got:- PARK MOR (HOMEMADE THAI CRÊPE).... Sweet crushed peanut dumplings... big fan... they were fluffy and yummy, although I wish there was some sort of dipping sauce. - PEEK GAI TOD (FRIED CHICKEN WINGS) ... very good wings I wish I had more! The pineapple sweet chili sauce was a perfect combo.- TOM KHA GAI (Lemongrass, galangal, mushrooms, creamy coconut broth, scallion, cilantro)... such a light soup and really flavorful. I got it with tofu. Would def get again. - CRAB MEAT FRIED RICE ... came with a nice light sauce on the side that had the slightest kick to it to flavor it up. Overall was a little dry but still good. - SHRIMP PAD THAI... they make a really good pad thai and don't skimp you on the shrimp/ the shrimps are really big. For drinks, they have thai ice tea/coffee, beers, and wines!I liked that any item on the menu could be made vegan friendly (besides items like wings, obviously). Our waitress, Bella, was really sweet and made sure everything was okay and we were enjoying our meal. Would def do takeout from here in the near future.

Went at 10am on a Saturday and it was so peaceful and quiet. You feel like you're in a quaint Parisian cafe in the morning. So transportive. We ordered the breakfast of champions: their legendary burger and their fruit-and-whipped-cream waffle. The burger is outstanding - deserves all the acclaim. Perfect! Juicy, crunchy, cheesy. All the flavors of a great burger. Coming back here just for that. The waffle was good, but not burger-sized good. I would try something else next time, like their baked eggs with butternut squash creme or ham and cheese crepe. 5 stars!!!!!!

Really just love this place and feel like it's so underrated. Probably my favorite restaurant in k-town. Make sure you season your seollong tang (oxtail bone soup) well with salt, pepper, and scallions! Love getting this with the bindaeddeok because it provides a crispy carb to go with the soup. small portion which is perfect, and not super expensive

Title: A Cozy Brunch Experience with Exquisite Flavors

My Sunday brunch experience at this gem of a restaurant was one to remember. Upon arriving, our reservation ensured we were seated immediately, kicking off a seamless dining adventure. The oeuf au plat, a baked egg delight with mortadella and comte cheese, paired with a crispy baguette, was the epitome of comfort in every unctuous bite. My husband's roast chicken received equal praise for its mouth-watering taste.

Diving into the wine selection, the emphasis on natural wines intrigued me, though the first two white selections weren't to my liking. However, the patience and dedication of our server shone through as they guided me to a lovely rose that captured my palate.

The grand finale, a shared pancake inspired by our fellow diners, did not disappoint. It was a sweet, buttery treat that proved perfect for sharing and rounded out our meal beautifully.

Despite any preconceived notions from the restaurant's hype, we were embraced by an atmosphere that was as warm and friendly as a lazy Sunday morning should be. This place is a must-visit for anyone craving a cozy atmosphere paired with delectable food.

Gone down hill. I came here for lunch and sat at the counter. The service was the best thing about this establishment. I had the Manhattan Clam Chowder and it was very heavy on the salty broth but super lean on clams and vegetables. I had a crab salad sandwich and salad and the bun was  good on the sandwich but the crab salad lack any type of flavor and it was so finely minced I'm not too sure if there was crab in it.  The salad was disgusting, there was black slimy leaves no many places and should never have been served. Safe to say I will never come back again.

Tucked away in one of the city's most charming neighborhoods, this gem of a restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving Italian delicacies. Whether you're in the mood for sumptuous pastas or mouth-watering pizzas, each dish is consistently well-prepared and sure to satisfy. On a warm day, the experience is elevated by dining at their outdoor tables, perfect for people-watching and soaking in the ambiance.

But it's the bar area that truly shines, offering a convivial atmosphere where you can drink and unwind at any hour. The staff deserve applause for their seamless teamwork, contributing to the warm and welcoming vibe that defines this dynamite establishment. Five stars, without a doubt, for both the impeccable food and service.

Truly authentic Thai restaurants are hard to find in my native state of Connecticut so its always a pleasant surprise when we stumble upon a spot that offers so much more than just the standard Americanized Thai fare most people are used to (think pad thai and drunken noodles).Upon entering, visitors are instantly transported to a Thai royal palace with some truly elegant interior set pieces and an aesthetic that is ritzy without being tacky. Food offering wise, we started off with the Pla Muk Yang ( a grilled octopus app) and the beautiful looking Thai Crepe Dumplings. The grilled octopus were perfectly cooked and not rubbery at all, as an added bonus, they also had a nice charred flavor which went well with the fish sauce based marinade. The Thai Crepe Dumplings were not only pleasing to look at, with its bright purple exterior, but also incredibly addicting as each plump dumpling was bursting at its seam with a nutty, sweet and savory filling. Make sure you get a picture of this!For entrees, we ordered the Pad Ped Hoy Darb (a sauteed razor clam dish), and the Khao Soi (a curry noodle soup). While I wasn't too big a fan of the Khao Soi, a bit too sour for my taste, the razor clams absolutely blew me away. SalaThai did NOT skimp on the razor clams with a literal pile of these delightful critters. They were also coated in this addictive basil based curry that begs to be eaten with rice. Its important to note that the flavors are very strong here but that's what makes it perfect with rice.After such an intense meal, we decided to get some of their homemade ice cream to restore some order to the Force. I highly recommend the Thai Medley which is as fun to look at as it is to eat. Here, homemade pandan and coconut ice cream are joined in a holy matrimony inside a coconut shell. This pairing was also topped with sweet red beans, jackfruit, and tender coconut strips - a figurative cherry on top!I can wholeheartedly recommend SalaThai as both an authentic Thai spot and just a good restaurant in general!

Stopped by penn station after seeing Aint Too Proud To Beg. My buddy said this was delicious authentic pizza. They had 20+ options and beer which made the decision an easy one. I opted for the pepperoni and the deep dish. This food didn't disappoint and lagunitas ipa always makes a meal all that more merry.

Title: A Slight Misstep in an Otherwise Charming Cafe

I returned to a favored cafe of mine, drawn in by past experiences of pleasant aromas and tastes. My companion found satisfaction in his baked egg sandwich, a reliable choice in the breakfast fare here. Unfortunately, my selection, a once mild and aromatic couscous, skewed near the edge of sourness this visit. Its beautiful plating caused me to ponder if the tartness was a deliberate twist beyond my palate's appreciation. Regardless, this didn't dampen the cafe's inherent charm. While this dish didn't hit the mark for me, the cafe's ambiance and my previous good experiences will bring me back to sample their veggie burger next.

What a wonderful birthday dinner I had here! First off, we had the best seats in the house...the chefs table! (Trust me, it took a lot of work to get the reservation, never mind one of the best table in the place). Anyway, it was really exciting to watch all of the chefs prepping the food, cooking the dishes, answering to the head chef and watching them make the desserts. The restaurant itself has a very eclectic menu, but everything was delicious. I was a little bummed out they didn't have a bar here, but they do have the ability to make any cocktail you desire. We started off with a round of cocktails and sat deliberating over the menu for quite some time. I sort of thought they would have brought over a little tasting from the chef as many high end restaurants do, but they didn't. In any case...For first courses we went with: morilles, sabayon au vin jaune (peas, ham and confit egg yolk), Navets en guise d'escargots* (turnip, mussel and sea urchin disguised as snails) & Ris de veau a l'estragon  (sweetbreads, cream, tarragon, maitake mushrooms). My favorite was the sweetbread dish. The waiter did say the sauce was excellent, so he sold me on that.  Sauce was incredible and everything was cooked just right. The 'fake' escargot dish was interesting. It was made with turnips and mussels in an escargot sauce. Very unique. The morilles dish was very unique too...interesting flavor combination of creamy sauce, peas and egg yolk. For mains we split the dover sole and the roasted duck with olives. The dover sole was made with a creamy sauce with mushrooms on top. It was delightful and just the right amount of food for me. My parents split the duck which came 2-3 pieces of each of them lightly seared with spinach on the side. Then in a pan in the middle of the table they left them the remainder of the dish which included: a piece of duck breast, green olives, sweet onions, and a delicious broth. We were all pleased with our menu selections.For dessert we ordered the chocolate mousse with white coffee ice cream, which was excellent. Overall service was great. All the waiters were impeccably dressed in fitted suits, which I adore. Everyone was super friendly and hospitable. We had a bit of trouble getting amazing service when the place got pretty crowded come 7:30pm, but before that, it was excellent. I didn't think it was terribly expensive either!

Okay, I thought I wouldn't come here again, but decided to give this place another try. I visited for lunch and was pleasantly surprised by the service and food. I wish I remembered the name of the gentleman who waited our table, because he was a delight (5/17/19 around 2pm). We were seated almost instantly and our food was excellent. I had the turkey burger and holy moly! It was SO GOOD. The caramelized onions were phenomenal and the brioche was perfect. The patty was charred to perfection and the fries were amazing. My boyfriends omelette was great, no complaints from him. So happy that we gave this place another try and we'definitely be back.

Williamsburg Pizza is a sure-bet.  You WILL find delicious pizza and garlic knots here.  I suggest the Sofia Loren slice, however, you may need a little salt on top (because fresh mozzarella doesn't have salt).

Title: A Rooftop Oasis with Flair

From the moment we stepped onto the rooftop, we were greeted with an ambiance that promised a night of relaxation and entertainment. With a pristine pool as its centerpiece, a well-stocked bar, and the vibrant energy from live DJs on select nights, this place has mastered the art of combining dining with leisure.

The cocktail menu was a breath of fresh air – innovative and diverse, catering to a wide array of palates. It's a dream for those who appreciate a well-crafted drink with a twist. And when it came to the food, the appetizers didn't disappoint. The chicken tenders, in particular, were a standout; crisp, flavorful, and paired with a dipping sauce that truly elevated the dish.

In short, this spot is a must-visit for anyone looking to indulge in good food, great drinks, and an unforgettable rooftop experience.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a fantastic restaurant where the culinary experience was nothing short of outstanding. For starters, the steamed dumplings were perfectly prepared, and the Kimchi Fries offered a delightful fusion of flavors. The entrees continued to impress, with the Basil Fried Rice and Pad Thai, both with beef, showcasing the kitchen's prowess and leaving me eager for a return visit. The drinks complemented the meal beautifully, a testament to the bartender's skill. The attentive staff ensured a seamless dining experience, with every dish hitting the mark. Highly recommended for a memorable meal!

Tucked away in the bustling heart of Manhattan lies a true culinary treasure that has become my weekend go-to. In a city where dining prices can soar as high as the skyscrapers, this gem offers an unbeatable lunch special for a mere $14. The deal includes a generous entree, a warming soup, fresh fruits, a crisp salad, and—remarkably—even sushi, all rounded off with soothing green tea. Each visit is graced with exceptional hospitality, making you feel truly taken care of. Each time I indulge in this feast, I find myself baffled at the value—it's almost like they've not noticed Manhattan's sky-high dining standards. This hidden gem is a secret I've been tempted to keep to myself!
Woah. So I've never had crawfish. This place has flavorful food. The sauce was on point. Everything was tasty. Fries were tasty as well. I would pass on the garlic bread though, not work it.

Make reservations or try your luck to be squeezed in for some delish Chinese food. We were immediately greeted by a friendly hostess. He asked if we had reservations (which we didn't) and was able seat us within a minute of us walking in. ORDERCrispy Pan Fried Noodles with Beef - This is usually my go to when eating Chinese (along with Honey Walnut Shrimp which I find it hard to find! Message me if you know where to get some legit  honey walnut shrimp and not the kind at Panda Express.) I couldn't have been more satisfied with the crispy noodles and flavor of the broth, beef and broccoli - Yum! Growing up eating rice; I ordered a side of rice to add to my noodles. Lo Mein - I'm not a huge fan of Lo Mein but this spot impressed me with theirs. It was very good. The noodles were perfectly cooked - not too hard which I find some seem to be. Sichuan flavour Beef - This was one of the top items on the menu and it made the cut. The waitress said it was spicy but it wasn't too spicy for me (and I can't handle too much spice - even as an island girl). By the time we left, a rush of people were waiting in the waiting area to be seated. I recommend making reservations if you don't mind waiting in the event it's busy. Check them out. My visit was around the Chinese New Year but didn't see anything that stood out other than the delicious food.

Title: A Korean Gem in Hell's Kitchen

I ventured into a Korean restaurant at 7PM on a bustling Friday with a couple of friends, expecting the usual crowd but was welcomed by a surprisingly peaceful dining space. Seated immediately, we dove straight into the menu, opting to share the spicy rice cake with an extra cheese topping and a mix of fried chicken wings in soy garlic and spicy hell's sauce.

The cheese-clad spicy rice cakes arrived promptly, oozing with a cheese pull so gratifying it could charm any spice-weary soul, perfectly toning down the fiery Korean sauce. Shortly after, a succulent procession of fried chicken wings landed on our table, accompanied by crisp pickled radish and thoughtful bone buckets, although the "spicy" hell's sauce fell short of our heat expectations, and the soy garlic leaned towards the sweeter side.

Our trio managed to polish off almost everything, leaving just three lonesome wings for a to-go box. We noted the food quality had elevated, a change attributed to a recent shift in the kitchen's head chef as per the neighboring table's chatter.

While the service hit a slight snag with my friend's seamless order, efficiency wasn't notably compromised. It was an agreeable surprise finding such decent Korean chicken wings without the need to venture to Koreatown or Flushing. While I might not go out of my way for a revisit, this spot is a solid choice for those craving Korean bites in Hell's Kitchen.

Really enjoyed a catch up dinner here on a rainy day. We managed to snag a table before it started to fill up just shy of 7 PM. Not gonna lie, didn't even look at the drink menu, knew they had my yuzu sake. We ordered a bunch of skewers, and a couple plates. Food came out quickly, and was quickly enjoyed.takoyaki - we had an order of three, and they were larger than expected, but had the standard taste and toppings, definitely not a bad starter.Absolutely order these skewers:king oyster mushroom mochi wrapped in pork bellysweet potatochicken meatballscallopsEverything else we had was decent, but I'd probably opt to try something new the next time I visited. I was a little sad that the chicken skin skewer wasn't a bit crisper, and the lotus root was a little bit on the light side.Will definitely be back to try some of the other options I've got my eyes on.

I've visited Gammeeok twice, and my latest experience has turned me into a true fan. My friend and I were promised a 15-minute wait, and to my surprise, we were seated exactly on time—a rarity in the city! I always go for the selleongtang, which not only arrives swiftly but also offers incredible value at $12 a bowl. It's a hearty dish, complete with rice and noodles that never fail to satisfy. While the banchan selection is limited to kimchi, the thick-cut kimchi radish served is absolutely delectable. Gammeeok has proven to be a reliable spot for a quick, fulfilling, and delicious meal.

During my recent visit to a local eatery, I sampled several dishes with varying degrees of satisfaction. The Chicken Feet Soup was disappointingly sour, to the point of overshadowing the intended flavors. Hoping for a reprieve, I tried the Pork Bone Soup, but found it only marginally less sour and nearly identical in taste to the Chicken Feet Soup, which was not what I had expected from two distinct offerings.

On a brighter note, the Kale Salad was a delightful beginning to the meal. The light dressing on the salad was genuinely refreshing and set a promising stage as an appetizer. However, the Corn Fritter fell short of expectations, offering scant kernels of corn that left me searching for the promised flavor and texture.

Overall, while the restaurant had some refreshing elements, the lack of variety and balance in the soups and a disappointing corn fritter detracted from the dining experience.

Title: Aromatic Indulgence at The Truffleist Booth

I recently found myself at The Truffleist's booth nestled in the bustling Bryant Park Winter Village. Being a truffle aficionado, my excitement was palpable as I approached their shop to sample their truffle-laden offerings.

I indulged in the Truffle Cheesesteak Burger and the Truffle Cheesesteak Fries, both commanding a price tag of $14-15. Admittedly steep for lunch, the generous portions softened the blow, making them ideal for sharing.

The burger, while promising with its decadent cheesesteak topping, fell short as the patty itself lacked the flavor and quality I had expected. However, the fries stole the show, perfectly golden and imbued with the heady aroma of truffle.

An unexpected delight was their truffle hot sauce, which had me smitten to the point of purchase. It's a flavor I'm eager to revisit.

While my burger experience didn’t quite hit the mark, the fries and the prospect of truffle mozzarella sticks on a future visit have me eager to return to The Truffleist. Truffle lovers, take note: this is a pit stop worth making.

There's always a crowd of people whenever I walk by this place. Finally ventured in to grab a slice of that OG cheese pizza. This is your classic New York City slice, nothing fancy. But it hits the right spots when you're craving for a good slice of pizza. If I have to talk about the positive nuances in flavor I'd say it's got a good char at the bottom and not so greasy feel. The negatives would be the sauce is slightly on the sweeter side with a little skimpy in quantity of cheese. With $3 for a slice ,  I expected some more.  Pretty average.

Finally had a chance to try the XLB dumpling, it was made to order and extremely delicious. The dumpling itself takes 10-15 minutes to prepare and the store makes a limited quantity a day so make sure to call ahead to have them start the order prior to your arrival. The staff  here were extremely attentive, our server gave really good recommendations for us to order and how to properly tackle the XLB without severely burning yourself.

So far so good, I'm pretty satisfied with the taste of the food and still pretty reasonable prices. Healthier alternatives and clear to how more calories they are and what ingredients is in it. You order and they help you like how subway works, and you can add or substitute something. First substitution is always free but after it's extra. You have pay $1 for a recyclable blue bowl and use it twice than return it and it's eco friendly. The utensils and containers' lid is still plastic but the bowl or packaging or bag itself are all recyclable. Friendly staffs and pretty fast. People in and out, usually people take it to go but you can definitely eat there too. It's never packed so the line isn't bad. Walkable to the red subway line and across the street from the L train and blue subway line. Not my favourite spot but definitely a place I'd come back to. I do recommend it too

Joe's Pizza, a staple across NYC, consistently serves up delicious slices of traditional New York-style pizza. It may not top my pizza list, but the quality is undeniable. My personal favorites are their pepperoni, cheese, and Sicilian - all equally fabulous. Despite the bustling crowd at the Times Square location, the line moves swiftly thanks to efficient staff. For a reliable pizza experience that steers clear of the city's many mediocre options, you can't go wrong with Joe's.

Let's say this first, if money is no objective, this place would be 5 stars. Let's also say this, if money is a concern, do not get the Kobe beef (it's 65 bucks for 5 large skinny pieces).We started off with the premium combo and what you notice is the quality of the meats. They were all amazing. This is probably enough for two people, but not quite enough for three.The broth was also amazing. We got the seafood, mushroom, and spicy ones. Spicy was my favorite with the seafood one as my least favorite. You come in here and it just smells like a hot pot shop in China. I would consider this place to be on par with haidilao, if not better

Title: Mixed Experiences at a Trendy Burger Spot

I recently visited a popular burger joint with friends - a haven for those with food intolerances and the picky eaters alike. Our Saturday evening began with a lengthy one-hour wait, which is perhaps expected for the weekend dinner rush.

The menu catered well to our diverse group - one friend opted for the Impossible Burger, another for a standard cheeseburger, and I decided on the Truffle Burger with an egg on top, specifically requesting it to be very runny. As a bonus, my Yelp check-in awarded me a complimentary order of fries.

Unfortunately, when my burger arrived, the egg was overcooked, far from the runny yolk I anticipated. The waitress, though noticeably overwhelmed, was gracious and promptly had my order redone, which returned perfect in just a few minutes. As for the burger itself, I found the truffle flavor underwhelming and the meat rather unremarkable. On the flip side, the Impossible Burger received high praise from my friend.

Upon receiving the bill, I noticed my free fries had not been deducted. The oversight could be attributed to the waitress being quite busy, yet she maintained her politeness throughout the evening.

In conclusion, the restaurant managed to please with its variety and service but faltered slightly with execution and flavor. It's a decent option for a diverse group, but don't set your expectations too high for an extraordinary taste experience.

Title: A Bumpy Start Followed by a Flavorful Recovery

I recently dined at this local gem after attending a seminar nearby, necessitating a last-minute reservation on OpenTable for which I accidentally selected 9pm instead of 8pm. Despite the rainy evening and a slow customer flow, the hostess's unwelcoming demeanor in light of my mistake was a disappointing start. Although I was eventually accommodated, the hostess's attitude was off-putting, to say the least.

Thankfully, the experience improved significantly once seated. The servers were friendly and promptly provided complimentary chips and salsa, a delicious opener for what was to come. I indulged in a pomegranate margarita – a tad on the strong side, but a good value considering the generous pour of tequila.

For the main course, the Chile Poblano Rellano captured my appetite. Served with rice and beans, it was both scrumptious and hearty, warranting its $21 price tag and leaving me with leftovers for the following day.

The night's redemption was further cemented when the GM stopped by my table. After relaying my initial displeasure about the hostess, he displayed genuine concern and ensured my comfort for the remainder of the evening.

Despite the rocky start, this spot remains my favorite haunt in the area. I can't help but also recommend their white sangria, shrimp quesadilla, and queso fundido—each a good reason to return.

Title: A Beer Lover's Haven with Ample Space and Comfort Food

If you're passionate about beer and love exploring brews from around the world, this restaurant is your must-visit destination. The beer selection is impressive, especially the Belgian ales, which are a personal highlight. No matter your preference, you're likely to find a beer that suits your palate.

The restaurant itself boasts a spacious and welcoming interior, with enough room to prevent feeling crowded even when it's bustling. The bar is expansive and well-equipped to serve the multitude of patrons that come through.

As for the food, it's decent. The menu features familiar favorites and comforting staples. While the macaroni and cheese is just average, the burgers stand out and pair well with the beers on offer.

In summary, come for the exceptional beer variety, enjoy the comfort found in both space and food, and you're sure to have a good time.

This was a pop up location. I got the Joe's signature with beef & shrimp. It was made fresh and fast. The quality on the ingredients was really good. You can taste it in every bite. Definitely, miss it already. Probably, the best rice roll that I have had.

I visited this restaurant over Labor Day Weekend and had a delightful experience. The pizza was excellent, and enjoying it in their lovely outdoor seating area on a beautiful evening only enhanced the dining experience. Highly recommended for a casual yet satisfying meal.

I recently ventured to a friend-recommended eatery for the first time and left thoroughly impressed. The highlight of my meal was the delectable dip trio and freshly baked bread; it was absolutely "bomb," easily outshining the tasty falafel and the pancakes we shared. Opting for bottomless booze, we were delighted by the waiter's generosity with champagne and mimosas.

The ambiance was equally impressive, adorned with fun, festive, and unique winter decor that truly captivated us. The experience was so remarkable that I am seriously considering this venue for my upcoming birthday brunch. A must-visit for anyone seeking a delightful dining experience with an extra touch of cheer!

Title: A Charming Spot for Food and Friends - LRoom Cafe

I can't help but express my adoration for LRoom's delightful ambiance – it's simply enchanting. It's become my go-to spot for unwinding with friends. Despite the presence of some less-than-stellar reviews online, my experiences beg to differ.

Admittedly, the prices are a bit steep, but the summer menu, which offers a food item and beverage for approximately $20, provides good value. Sure, some options may cost a bit more, but their happy hour is not to be missed for those looking to save a few dollars.

The savory selections at LRoom steal the show for me, particularly the garlic rice, which is phenomenal. The smoked salmon croissants are another favorite, perfectly balancing delicacy with flavor.

As for desserts, they're a dream. The Rose Waffle is an absolute delight, and the Strawberry ice cream, with its rich cake accompaniment, is a match made in heaven – far from the blandness some have suggested.

In summary, LRoom doesn't just serve food; they craft experiences. And to me, they're utterly delicious. YUM!

Tucked away inside the Arlo hotel, Harold's greets diners with a swanky entrance that leads to a lunchtime delight. Opting for the Market Bowl, I savored a well-prepared selection of salmon, grilled broccolini, and spiced cauliflower—each cooked and seasoned to perfection, save for the lackluster cold quinoa that lacked flavor. Be warned, portions lean towards the modest side; the salmon is presented as a small cube, and a solitary piece of cauliflower might leave the hungrier patrons wanting more. 

Despite this, Harold's earns a return visit from me. The side offerings are not to be missed, with cheddar and chive biscuits that melt sumptuously in the mouth and a Mac and cheese that arrives bubbling and utterly amazing. Harold's knows how to make a few key dishes shine.

Title: A Disappointing Turn at Takashi

I recently revisited Takashi with high expectations, eager to share what I remembered as an exceptional dining experience with friends. Unfortunately, the restaurant appears to have lost its edge. On this occasion, the service was lacking—with difficulty getting the server's attention in the small space—and the server's clarity left a lot to be desired. Additionally, unrequested add-ons appeared on our bill, although they did remove one item after we pointed this out.

The quality of the meals didn't redeem the evening. We ordered premium cuts like the tongue experience and filet mignon, along with assorted chef's horumon, but none of the dishes lived up to my previous visits. My friends, visiting on my enthusiastic recommendation, were equally underwhelmed.

What was meant to be a special dinner left us all let down, and it's with regret that I say Takashi is no longer the culinary highlight it once was.

Came here once with the fam. We got a cold appetizer to start (triple salad) with seaweed, tofu curd, and brined cucumber, which was alright to me. My mom enjoyed it. We also got the Spicy chicken tray that was SO GOOD. I would highly recommend. It had a strong cumin flavor, the chicken was very tender, and I could just drink up the sauce! It's a pretty large tray so def get it to share! You also add orders of noodles to it, which is great to soak up the sauce. We just got one order of noodles since we were getting other things, but you can get multiple orders of noodles.We also got the soup dumplings, which was TERRIBLE. DO NOT GET THE SOUP DUMPLINGS HERE. It had absolutely NO SOUP. -.- We also 2 noodle soups: lamb hui mei and beef brisket. For the beef noodle soup, you could get beef broth or lamb broth with it. We tried the beef broth (you know, like beef noodle soup), which was kind of just like a soy sauce broth that didn't really stew with any beef or bones or anything, so it was more just like a soy sauce soup (but not too salty), without much depth or meaty soup flavor. However, the beef was in nice large cubes and tender and not the thick cut brisket like you eat in hotpot or kbbq. The lamb broth we got with the lamb noodle soup was really good. It had a strong lamb flavor and felt pretty clean (it was a clear broth). Overall I really liked the noodles they had at this place. It had that good chew. They used the thicker/flatter dao xiao (knife cut?) noodle shape.I'd def come here to eat noodles and soup and the chicken tray, but def don't get soup dumplings here. Go to Joe's or some other place in Chinatown.Service left more to be desired. One waitress in particular seemed to have a very sour and snotty attitude toward us like she really didn't want to be there and hated serving us. Gave us a lot of attitude. But if you're a white person coming in there, they seem much more attentive and nice to you like the white family that came in after us. But hey, I'm not surprised a lot of Chinese people treat white people like royalty and give crap service to Chinese people because I dunno, we're used to it?

Nice place to catch a games. Service was friendly and attentive even with a large crowd. My friend got an order of the Hot Chips to start and I wound up eating a lot of them and nearly drank the Bleu cheese and Sriracha dip. When my Pub Burger came I killed the rest of that dip by using it for the crispy fries. Burger was great and cooked perfectly.

Title: Authentic Tacos with a Big Apple Twist

As a culinary connoisseur hailing from East Los Angeles, I've savored my fair share of mouth-watering tacos. Yet, the tacos at this Chelsea Market gem manage to hold their own at the top of my list. The tortillas are authentically homemade, and the guacamole - an essential topping - does not disappoint.

The trio of tacos I indulged in - al pastor, asada, and chicken - were nothing short of spectacular. Each was brimming with an explosion of flavors that satisfied my street taco cravings. However, the absence of a seating area forced me to weather the inconvenience of standing while eating, which admittedly detracted from the overall experience.

Be prepared for bustling foot traffic and a probable queue, customary for a spot within the market's vibrant confines. Price-wise, anticipate shelling out a bit more than the familiar rates of East LA, but for taco aficionados, it's a worthy splurge.

Despite the minor drawbacks, my palate is already eager for a return visit the next time New York beckons, and my hankering for authentic street tacos peaks.

I found out about Parish via Pulsd, when my friends and I were looking for a spot to brunch one Saturday. There was a deal for $29 - one entree + one carafe of mimosas, so we decided to give it a try. We came in with a 12:45 reservation for four, and the place was empty except for one couple dining. It looks more like a cocktail/dinner spot, so maybe not a lot of people know that they serve brunch.I went with the Shrimp and Grits (with andouilles sausage, roasted garlic, charred scallion, Creole BBQ). I really enjoyed this. The shrimp was cooked perfectly and was flavorul. The BBQ with the grits was a different and welcome update to a classic. The mimosas just taste like your typical brunch mimosa - nothing to write home about.For brunch, it can be a little pricey if you don't have a Pulsd deal. However, they do seem to have a unique menu, and the ingredients taste really fresh. Plus, I haven't found a lot of good Cajun places in NYC. I wouldn't mind coming back to try out their dinner menu.

Title: A Sublime Sashimi Experience at Sashimi Saturday

If you find yourself perplexed on what to dine on, let Sashimi Saturday guide your palate with their exceptional sashimi platter. The chirashi dinner I had was nothing short of divine – the sashimi was as fresh as the morning catch, each piece melting like butter in my mouth, a testament to its quality and the deftness of the chef's knife skills. For $25, this meal is not only a palate pleaser but also a steal. My experience deserves a 4.5 out of 5-star rating. If sashimi is your craving, this establishment should top your list.

This place was pretty well run. You pick your Steak then they weight it and cook it for you. I got the Wagyu beef it was $42 for A 7oz cut. It was cooked perfectly.  It came with corn and onions. The cut was very juicy and tender. There was no need for extra seasoning. Definitely z would come back

Nice! Customer service was great. They have plenty of tables to sit. The bathroom was clean. They have good items on the menu. Prices are decent, I mean come on its lobster. I like that they don't cheat you on the lobster either. I wanted the lobster tail and tots on the side but for some reason at 2:00p.m. in the afternoon they didn't have anymore tails. Its o.k. then maybe next time, so I went with the lobster tots instead. I thought that my meal was tasty and had decent size lobster bites, but as for the lobster bisque, although it was tasty, I felt like I was having a small bowl of soup. It was watery. I would have been upset to buy a large bowl as a meal. It has absolutely no lobster pieces in it, and wasn't thick enough like a bisque should be. I was disappointed by that. It makes a great side dish still, just not buy as a full entree. I think, overall that you can add this place to your list of places to get some good lobster. I wouldn't mind visiting again.F.Y.I. They do sell beer and wine. Along with some sweets, such as the Red Velvet Whoopie Pie.

Title: A Satisfying Dim Sum Delight in Chinatown

After trekking through the bustling streets of Chinatown in search of authentic dim sum, my dining companions and I stumbled upon a hidden gem. Despite the buzz of the neighborhood and the lines snaking outside nearby eateries, we were fortunate to snag a table without delay.

Upon settling in, we were promptly served steaming cups of hot green tea, setting a comforting tone for the meal ahead. While it took a moment for the waiter to take our order, the kitchen's efficiency more than compensated for the wait, as our dishes began arriving swiftly.

The standout of the meal was undeniably the scallion pancakes. The perfect balance of flavor and texture, these pancakes were wonderfully crisp, avoiding the dreaded sogginess that can often plague lesser versions. They stood their ground when dipped in sauce, truly a testament to their craftsmanship.

While the fried tofu was unremarkable in taste, a common trait for the dish, it was the duck spring roll that puzzled us slightly. It was enjoyable, no doubt, but the meat within could have been mistaken for any other filling. However, the turnip buns were a revelation. Their softness coupled with their rich flavor profile was an absolute delight.

It was the soup dumplings, though, that crowned the meal. Packed with umami and arriving at our table in a cloud of steam, they were the epitome of what one seeks in dim sum—a burst of flavor encapsulated in delicate wrappings.

This establishment may not conform to the American archetype of dining, where attentive service is paramount, but here, it is the food that commands center stage. Despite the minimal interaction, the delectable offerings more than made up for it.

In short, this culinary adventure was a reminder that sometimes, the best experiences come with patience and an openness to simplicity. Without a doubt, I am eager to return and delve deeper into the menu.

I may have already been tipsy when I walked in late one Friday night and pretentiously asked the waitress for a not so basic cocktail. She hit it out of the park when she brought me the Monkey Business. I also recently had the lamb burger and it was spot on - flavorful and cooked perfectly with the juice running down my arm. If you go after work for happy hour or on a weekend night, you should have a reservation because this place fills up fast and you may have to wait for a table.

Came here with the fiance around noon on a Saturday. Quiet. Lunch specials were going on so we shared a 3 roll special for $11. Good deal! Spicy tuna was good, but a tad salty in my opinion. My fiance didn't think that though. The eel cucumber was good but I've had better. My favorite was the salmon avocado. Very fresh fish. Good service. Nice environment. Worth the visit, especially during lunch hours. Hot sake was a nice addition . The large was 9 bucks.

Made last minute reservations on Valentine's Day. We had a show to catch, so we had to schedule dinner earlier than usual. But loved that I was able to combine history and dinner (lunch spot of the Vicious Circle of Dorothy Parker, et al.).Round Table exceeded my expectations. They sat us quickly near the back for a quieter atmosphere. Great for a date night. They provided a rose for the holiday and had a live jazz singer & pianist. Nice. Cocktail? The Dorothy Parker, of course. NY Distilling Co Dorothy Parker Gin, St. Germain, lemon honey & basil. But it's $18. Prix fixe menu for Valentine's day.Frisee & Baby Greens Beets Salad-fried goat cheese & raspberry vinaigrette. Good.Grilled Jumbo Prawns & Roasted Petit Filet Mignon w/mashed potatoes w/Boursin cheese. Good. Chef's Raspberry & Dark Chocolate Mousse and a couple chocolate covered strawberries. Strawberries were fresh.Servers were friendly and got us through our meal on time to make our show. Perfect.

Title: Unexpected Delight at Wildair – A Respite from NYC's Unpredictability

On a classic New York evening marked by sudden change, after a friend's cancellation, I stumbled upon Wildair, a gem birthed by the culinary minds behind the Michelin-starred Contra – Jeremiah Stone and Fabian von Hauske. Wildair offers a laid-back vibe, with high top tables reminiscent of middle school desks, complete with silverware tucked away under the table.

The meal commenced with an unremarkable bread and olive oil – perfectly fine but lacking a wow factor. Things swiftly ascended with top neck clams bathed in XO sauce and almond milk, delivering fresh flavors with an innovative twist. The "Sicilian sashimi," boasting sorrento lemon and four types of fish, was a masterclass in simplicity yet bursting with taste. Beef tartare came with an unexpected kick, courtesy of smoked cheddar and horseradish, and was studded with Brazil nuts. The group heralded the spicy tuna on toast and the fried soft-shelled crab, the latter commandeering the spotlight with its impeccable crust and divine sauce.

Desserts were a mixed bag. The almond mille feuille, akin to an adult's s'mores, won my coworkers' adoration. The standout for me was the chocolate hazelnut tart, its lightness in chocolate a perfect match for the tart base. The "LES mess" panna cotta was refreshing but didn't quite hit the mark when compared to its predecessors.

Our watchful waiter doubled as a sommelier, guiding us to a delightful bottle of rosé. Despite the service's attentiveness, take note – Wildair is not the locale for whispers of sweet nothings; its boisterous atmosphere and intimate table spacing lean more towards lively camaraderie.

In the whimsical world of New York dining, Wildair stands as a beacon of delectable continuity amidst the city's all-too-common flakiness.

Ehhhhh.. over hyped.I was kind of curious about this concept of classic American fare with an Asian twist that was being promoted as a more Asian American genre of cuisine. How exactly is that different from "Asian fusion" (which usually sucks)? I have actually been to a few burgeoning restaurants in NYC that embody this novel concept of Asian American food very well. Unfortunately, I did not feel Tuome was one of them.First up: the much hyped chicken liver mousse. It was good but not really any different from the many other chicken liver mousses I have consumed in my lifetime (I happen to love this).Second: the much hyped pig out. The peanut sesame noodles were a bit too al dente and the sauce was salty. The Berkshire pork confit was dry which seems like an oxymoron. I did enjoy the lychee salad on the side, if only to cut how extremely heavy the dish was. As far as pork belly dishes go.. meh.We also got a side of broccoli which tasted like normal broccoli. The broth was nice, but ok, it just tasted like broccoli.Pricing was high but typical for Manhattan. Service was decent. Ambiance was nice. I wonder that this may be geared more towards those who aren't Asian food connoisseurs. Overall I did not feel the food was particularly special or tasty.Thank u, next!

Title: Worth the Wait for Fresh Sushi Delights

My visit to this sushi spot was defined by an exceedingly long wait, a testament to its popularity. Yet, the experience compelled me to urge others to brave the queue and discover the culinary treasures within. The sushi was astonishingly fresh, elevating each bite to a delightful experience. Opting for the "Trust Me" combinations proved to be an adventurous choice, coaxing me to sample and savor selections beyond my usual preferences – each one deliciously surprising.

Despite the bustling atmosphere, the service shone bright. The staff tackled the crowds with a blend of patience and attentiveness, ensuring that every table felt looked after. It's a restaurant that justifies an occasional wait, perfectly suited for a "treat yourself" meal. My recommendation? Dive into the "Trust Me" combo and let your taste buds revel in the exquisite offerings of this sushi haven.

Title: A Shanghainese Delight in the City

My fiancé and I recently visited a new restaurant boasting a modern vibe and an impressive layout, making our dining experience not just comfortable but aesthetically pleasing. The service was commendable - attentive and swift from the moment we walked in until our departure.

The menu offered a selection of authentic Shanghainese dishes, each more delicious than the last. The truffle wontons were a standout, enveloping the palate in rich flavors, while the blue crab paired with rice cakes was a symphony of taste and texture. A special mention to the refreshing tea that accompanied our meal, enhancing the flavors and cleansing our palates.

The star of the evening was undoubtedly the ribeye entree, served with a theatrical flare (as captured in the photo) and living up to every expectation in taste. 

Overall, the restaurant offered an exceptional dining experience, one that we would highly recommend.

During my visit to this bustling eatery for lunch, the restaurant was notably crowded. However, the staff impressively orchestrated the flow of diners, ensuring quick seating and an efficient dining experience. The value offered by their lunch special caught my eye—a modest uptick in price from a standard bowl of ramen to a more indulgent spread including edamame and octopus balls. Initially skeptical of my appetite, I was surprised to find myself savoring every last bite of the generous portions. A cool spot indeed, it has earned my return visits for more delightful meals.

During a weekend jaunt to the city, my friend and I, hankering for Thai cuisine, popped into the nearest Thai spot for a quick lunch. Surprisingly, the place was a ghost town on a Saturday afternoon, but we didn't mind the promised swiftness in service.
