I dove into shrimp pad Thai, specifically requested spicy, and a 'lady in red drink.' The pad Thai, while arriving swiftly, missed the heat mark but was passable. The drink, however, was reminiscent of cherry cough syrup - a hard pass for future visits. My dining companion seemed content with her Thai iced tea, though.

Portion sizes didn't quite align with the price, skewing towards the smaller side, but they did the job in sating our appetites. While it wouldn't top my list, this place could see a repeat visit if I found myself nearby with a Thai craving.

Apparently this place is a popular chain in Korea; never been to Korea so can't really compare. You'd have to expect at least an hour wait, so here's the deal: send the boyfriend over first to put his name/number on the list while you get ready at your home. Then, meet your bf at Caffe Bene and study with him until you get a call from the restaurant (Thanks David).   Bf and I ordered Cheese Dakgalbi ($19.95/person) and added Dumplings and Gimmari for $3.95 each. We got it in mild because I'm a fake Korean with low tolerance to spicy food. We also paired it with Grape Soju ($13.95) because we're Korean. Finally, finish your meal and get that full HCC experience with Fried Rice ($4.95). Overall, food itself was really good. It's authentic and price is reasonable for the quality of food you're getting. Portions may look quite huge from the pictures but if you're an eating champion like us, portions aren't that big and you can easily devour everything and still have room for Matcha Lava Cake and Bubble Tea. I'll definitely be back to try their other famous item: HCC Dakgalbi yasss.

My go to lunch ramen spot. Can't beat the $9.99 lunch ramen special. If you haven't eaten all day, the Mega Ramen won't disappoint.Quick and friendly service.Pictures and other positive reviews match up.Only reason this place doesn't get a full 5 stars is because it's not my top 5 ramen in NYC which is a difficult task to meet. But still a must try if you're in the area.

While on our way to another destination, we were lured into this cozy spot by the alluring sounds of live music—and it did not disappoint. The performance was simply amazing, creating a vibrant atmosphere that's hard to leave. The martinis are another highlight, offering a great but dangerous variety that could tempt you to indulge more than you might plan. Though the food menu doesn't boast the same depth and could use a few more options, what we sampled was acceptable. Overall, this place is worth a visit for the music and drinks alone.

My friend and I had just gotten drinks at a rooftop bar in the area and we were craving some quality noodles. I've walked by Chong Qing a number of times and was always intrigued by the pictures of the steamy noodle dishes they have on windows. It instantly popped up in my mind as a place we should try and quite honestly, it was probably the best decision I had made that entire day.We arrived around 8:15 in the evening on a Tuesday. When we walked into the space we noticed that about half of the restaurant was filled at this time (It's a tiny space with about six or seven tables). We were seated immediately and given menu's to look over.When it came time to order I ended up going with the restaurant's most popular dish, the mala noodles ($11.75). The dish was served in a pretty large bowl and was definitely more on the heftier side in terms of portion. The dish itself though was amazing, quality meat, perfectly cooked noodles, and just the right amount of spice in the broth. I was in noodle HEAVEN.The service here was pretty efficient as well. The staff gave us time to look over the menu and brought our dishes out to us pretty fast after ordering. Overall a great spot for some top-notch noodles in Hell's Kitchen.
Such a cute and cozy place! Was able to be seated immediately at the bar on a Sunday around 7pm. The Madame Pho was delicious and the service was friendly and attentive.

Cozy spot near Union square in Manhattan with great food!!The Eggs Benedict with kale sofrito and tomato hollandaise sauce was delicious. I didn't have any room for dessert but the French toast with baked caramel custard in the middle looked delicious.

Updated Review: After giving this local spot a second chance with a brunch visit, I'm regretfully reporting an equally disappointing experience. The oysters lacked any semblance of freshness and were unexpectedly small. As for the smoked salmon omelette, it was a letdown, with what seemed to be just an egg omelette containing a smattering of old, dry salmon. It appears no real effort is being put into their dishes, a sentiment echoed by recent reviews. I see no reason to return in the future.

Title: Slice of Heaven at Artichoke Haven

Review:
Stepping into this quaint, cash-only pizzeria, I experienced what I can only describe as my favorite pizza encounter to date. While there's an on-site ATM for convenience, it's the $6 Artichoke slice that commands attention. With a selection ranging from crabmeat to Sicilian and vodka slices, the options are enticing. However, the Artichoke slice is a must-try; its thickness and heaviness are a testament to its indulgence.

Don't let its heft deter you. The key to its magic lies in the flavorful, rich artichoke sauce, which, after being expertly heated, melds into a creamy dream. If you prefer something lighter, the thinner crust options will not disappoint. For lovers of texture, the Sicilian's double-baked, crunchy crust provides an equally satisfying experience. In summary, this spot is a true gem for pizza aficionados seeking flavor and quality in every bite.

I should have listened to other review to go for the fish cutlet app only! Still ordered the appetizer sampler and well yea. I should have skipped it. If anything, yes the fish cutlet would be the one. Others were either too dry or not sure what I was eating. Chicken Kohtu Roti - I loved the Kottu from Kottu House in LES and I still loved it more after I tried here.It was a go to order and both are okay, just that I expected a bit more :/

Stumbled upon Uncle Mario's Brick Oven Pizza while walking around Hell's Kitchen. My husband and I were hungry and not sure what we wanted to eat. As former residents of NYC who now live in California, we will never turn down a good looking New York slice. We walked by Uncle Mario's and decided to give them a try. It did not disappoint! Upon entering, you have the option to either sit down and eat (with waiter/waitress service) or just go up to the counter and order to go. We decided to take our orders to go. There were plenty of choices to select from but we ordered two plain slices. Although simple, it was heaven in our mouth. A solid brick oven New York slice, not over cooked with the perfect cheese melt. Fast and friendly service from beginning to end! Highly recommend.

Cuisine: 9Service: 9Decor: 7Value: 8Overall: 9Been a regular patron for the last two decades, so this review is well overdue. For the best selection of oysters in NYC, look no further. Roughly 25 different types of oysters available nightly from both coasts, you can always find something for your palate. Last night, I had a hankering for these delectable bivalves, therefore a visit to Aquagrill was necessary.Two of us ordered three dozen oysters from both coasts to start, which were absolutely amazing. They do a great job selecting and cleaning these plump juicy little suckers, I just can't get enough. My favorites were Hama Hama (WA) and Pemaquid (ME). However, Stretch Island (WA), Lucky Lime (PEI), North Bay Cove (WA), and Skookum (WA) were all delicious.A must have for me every time at Aquagrill is the fantastic Billi Bi French Mussel Soup. The saffron and cream blends beautifully with the flavors of the mussels to form one of my favorite soups ever. We finished the meal sharing some Fresh Maine Periwinkles, Roasted Peekytoe Crab Cake Napoleon, and Miso Glazed Chilean Sea Bass, which were all very good.Throughout the meal, the service was friendly and attentive as always. Bartender Ted mixed some great drinks for us as well. Restaurant itself is spacious and comfortable. Aquagrill will forever be on the top of my list whenever I'm in the mood for seafood.

Visited recently and tried the Chicken Kabob Pita which arrived piping hot and satisfyingly soft. The savory filling boasted well-seasoned meat, though it might verge on too salty for some palates. Despite the sizable line, service was swift. A commendable experience overall.

During a lively speakeasy-hopping evening, we discovered a charming tapas gem in the West Village. The true standout was the Gambas San Martin; each shrimp was succulent and bathed in a sauce bursting with flavor. Complementing the meal, the duck sausage skewers added a rich, savory note, while the cheese plate's fresh honey provided a delightful sweetness. Unfortunately, the red pear sangria fell flat, lacking the robustness one would expect, seeming rather watered down. It was surprisingly quiet for a Friday night, adding a touch of tranquility to our experience.

I visited the restaurant at 6pm on a bustling Saturday evening, eager to dive into a Dim Sum feast, which, to my surprise, was available via menu rather than the traditional cart service, alongside the dinner offerings. Greeted promptly upon arrival, I settled in and ordered the shrimp rice noodles and BBQ pork buns.

While sipping on the hot tea provided, I eagerly anticipated my meal. The BBQ pork buns did not disappoint – they were served fresh, with a delightfully fluffy exterior encasing a generous, tasty filling that struck a perfect balance of sweet and savory.

Unfortunately, the shrimp rice noodles fell short of my expectations. They arrived notably less than hot, bordering on cool, with shrimp that had an unpalatable rubbery texture. The accompanying sauce failed to enhance the dish, as it lacked seasoning, and my attempt to rectify it with soy sauce proved too overpowering.

Service was efficient, allowing for a swift payment process and exit. Despite the pork buns being a highlight, the overall experience with the dinner menu dim sum left me underwhelmed. While I might consider giving their cart service a try in the future, I'm not inclined to return for dinner anytime soon.

I ventured into this spot for the first time yesterday and was treated to an exceptionally solid pizza. With an impressive one bite score of 8.3, it's clear this pizza stands out. The cheese slice, generously sized at $3, offers a touch of elegance not found in your typical old-school pizza parlor. Although the prices trend higher, the quality and size of the slice justify the cost, aligning with what you might shell out at Joe's.

The cheese quality is top-notch and became an instant favorite of mine. A standout feature is the perfectly crispy crust and base, which I highly recommend getting reheated for that extra crunch around the edges. If you find yourself in the neighborhood and have a hankering for a premium slice dripping with cheesy goodness, this place is a must-visit.

What a wonderful birthday treat this was!! Absolutely loved the food, service and the view of NYC. When it comes to restaurant week I've always been skeptical as the experience can be miss or hit. Luckily for me it was a hit for sure as I loved every moment I was there. Great dining experience. Food-5/5We ordered from the restaurant week 3 course fixed price menu at $42 per person. For appetizer we ordered New England clam chowder (2 orders) and mushroom and spinach bruschetta. Entree: flat iron steak (2 orders) and potato gnocchi. Dessert: 2 orders of NY cheesecake and special chocolate surprise for my friend. Food was great everything was portioned adequately considering it's restaurant week. I loved the mushroom and spinach bruschetta (the bread was really soft and crunchy on the edges). Steak was served with mashed potatoes and broccoli. Hmm approximately it must have been 4-5 ounces of steak which is a good portion especially at a restaurant like The View. Service-5/5Samir was our amazingly sweet host who went above and beyond to provide exceptional customer service. The moment we were seated he was full of energy and made us laugh throughout the night. Restaurant week menu cannot be substituted but Samir was kind to offer another dessert instead of the NY cheesecake for my best friend. Location & View- 5/5 The only revolving restaurant in NYC located inside Marriott in Times Square. Easily accessible via MTA and taxi service. Driving is your personal preference if you are willing to pay for the outrageous parking fees. The view of the city lights and high skyscrapers was phenomenal. There's room for improvement but nevertheless it was amazing overall.

I was walking past this place which is right across from MOMA and I could not resist trying this place out. This place hits the spicy cumin lamb fresh pulled noodle, spot on even for a fast food joint. The oxtail noodles however was not as good. The meat was not tender and it needs more stewing. The cumin lamb burger was not my thing. Generally do not like burgers, so it was just ok. There were 2 bone chips in it for that added authenticity. Looks like a tale of diminishing returns. Stick with the cumin lamb noodles. It was order at the counter and pick up at the window. The were no square or round tables, just two long counters to sit at. I guess in New York a lot of people do take out.There are also numerous other branches in Manhattan and Queens, since this is a chain. I hope they open up in other major cities.

Title: Mixed Experiences on a Birthday Visit to Manhatta

I celebrated my birthday at Manhatta, partly due to my admiration for Danny Meyer and the restaurant's reputation. The venue boasts an impressive view and efficient service; my friend and I were seated immediately, and the complimentary fresh bread, especially the loaf with chicken fat and everything bagel seasoning, set a promising start. The salted French butter also comes highly recommended.

Regrettably, not all menu items lived up to expectations. The anchovies were overwhelmingly salty with a potent fishy odor, and the Dilja Cocktail was overly dominated by vodka and grapefruit— a concoction I wouldn't order again.

The first course was hit-or-miss. The Scotch Snails, drenched in butter and garlic, were indulgent to a fault; two pieces sufficed. The Foie Gras Reuben was a disappointment, with a mysteriously bitter layer beneath the foie gras and an excessively pungent mustard dijon.

For the main courses, the Butter Poached Lobster offered a pleasing, though slightly oversalted, experience, while the Crescent Duck, served with Napa cabbage and intriguing white berries, was a delightful combination of flavors, although the currants were notably tart.

Dessert partly redeemed the meal. The Olive Oil Sabayon with its strawberry sorbet was a refreshing delight, although its subtle nuances were overshadowed if followed by the Hazelnut Chocolate Tart. The tart itself was lusciously hazelnut-infused, though quite rich. The complimentary Black and White Cookie Cake, despite the kind gesture, was unfortunately too sweet and unremarkable.

The service shone throughout the evening with attentive waitstaff and consistent water refills. While my excitement for Manhatta brought high hopes, they were partially met with dishes ranging from exceptional to subpar.

Title: A Burst of Life and Flavor at a Vibrant Dining Spot

From the moment you step into this buzzing establishment, you're embraced by an aura of energy and life, accompanied by a soundtrack that revives the spirit. It's a place that transcends age, where twenty-somethings and those well into their golden years mingle seamlessly, creating a welcoming atmosphere for all.

Upon arrival, the bar beckons with its crowd and artisanal cocktails. The Beauty Elixir, a popular choice among patrons, offers a refreshing blend of strawberry and light cucumber—perfectly balanced between sweet and tart. Alternatively, the Merchant and Foolish Pleasure showcase the bar's mixology prowess with their outstanding flavors, justifying their premium price point.

As for the cuisine, the tuna sashimi is an absolute must—its taste a delightful revelation that steals the show. Pair it with the innovative grilled cheese tomato soup dumplings; despite what any dissenters may say, these treasures are worth savoring to the last spoonful. The Brussels sprouts toast also makes a satisfactory accompaniment.

Main courses vary, with the beef Wellington earning high marks for its execution, while the Atlantic salmon, despite being cooked to perfection, may not appeal to all palates due to its unique blend of spices. The side of BBQ fries could be a hit or miss, depending on your taste for the seasoning.

Service may experience delays, yet the staff more than compensates with their friendliness and attentive care—exemplary customer service that softens any wait. A complimentary black bottomed butterscotch pot de creme serves as a testament to their commitment to guest satisfaction.

The venue itself is sprawling, with an upstairs bar and dance area that's just as lively as the main space. Even a wait for the restroom comes with its own charm—a mini bar with champagne, adding a touch of luxury to the most mundane of experiences.

In summary, this restaurant is a vibrant, unforgettable destination, ideal for those seeking both excitement and culinary delight. It's certainly a place worth returning to for its atmosphere, drinks, and standout dishes.

I'm definitely a fan! Why? I'll tell you why. First, I've always thought ramen broth was a bit TOO HEAVY and thick and salty. Personally, I prefer pho broth over ramen broth. And don't get me wrong. I LOVE RAMEN! You know, that creamy and rich Tonkastu ramen broth that is oh so good? Ugh! Yummy! But I can only eat it every once in a while and establishments like Ippudo happen to be one of the favorites. However, I really appreciated the lighter chicken broth in the Tokyo Shio Ramen and I was sooooo excited to see how much GREEN was in my bowl. I don't know about you but as I get older I need to get more greens into my diet! The rye noodles were also cooked to perfection meaning they were fresh and soft, not al-dente, like the way I get them when I order at Ippudo. And the portion was just perfect for me. I left feeling just satisfied but didn't feel like I overdid it. I could see how some people would not be open to this type of broth because it's simple! And sometimes simple is better. Less is more! It tasted like homemade. Like I went to someone's house and their mom made it for me and that made me feel good. I could eat this again tomorrow and not feel guilty. I think that's a winner if you get me as a repeat customer! ありがとうございましたArigatōgozaimashita

Title: A Homely Delight with Standout Service

We recently dined at a local spot recommended by a friend, and it didn't disappoint. The standout service began with Lizeth, our attentive server, who provided swift drink service and allowed us ample time for menu perusing and conversation.

My friend and I opted for the vegetarian chili, which was a cheesy delight filled with carrots, beans, and onions. Although delicious, the generous portion topped with an abundance of cheese proved too much, leaving us to take leftovers home. The accompanying corn muffins were exceptional—large, toasted for an appetizing crunch.

My husband tried the warm corned beef sandwich complemented by slaw. While he found the corned beef satisfactory, it wasn't a standout. The side slaw received a thumbs-up for its taste.

Despite enticing dessert options, our appetites were fully sated. Pricing felt fair, though it's worth noting a 4% surcharge for credit card payments. Cash is your best bet here.

For those wondering about amenities, the bathrooms are located downstairs. The ladies' room was clean, spacious, with no wait time—a pleasant surprise to end the dining experience.

Title: A Delightful Ramen Surpise in NYC

My recent lunch at this spot turned out to be an exceptional experience, especially with their ramen selection. I opted for the beef bone marrow ramen, while my girlfriend chose the spicy tonkotsu. The bone marrow enhanced the already rich broth, infusing it with an incredible depth of flavor that truly set it above other ramen offerings. It's clear why this place boasts an award for what might just be the best beef broth ramen in the city.

The spicy tonkotsu was no less impressive, thanks to an intricate mix of heat from kimchi and chili sauce, alongside the savory notes from black garlic oil and a green chili pepper. While the pork was slightly on the fattier side, it was within the bounds of what you'd expect for this dish.

Both bowls left us satisfied and eager to return. Whether it's to relive these flavors or to explore more of their menu, a revisit is certainly in the cards.

Title: Worth the Wait at Rubirosa

After a spontaneous decision to dine at Rubirosa without a reservation, we were faced with a daunting 2+ hour wait on a bustling Saturday afternoon. Despite the initial disappointment underscored by the hostess's emphasis on the long wait, we decided to take a chance and were pleasantly surprised to receive our table in just under two hours.

Upon being seated, we opted for the seasonal white wine recommendation, which proved to be an excellent accompaniment to our meal. The star of the show was the large tie-dye pizza - a masterpiece of thin-crust perfection that wasn't overly filling. The 8 slices were ideal for sharing among the three of us, though hearty appetites might call for additional orders. The flexibility to choose half-and-half toppings allowed for a diverse tasting experience.

Our waitress enhanced our dining experience with her exceptional service, striking the perfect balance between friendliness and humor. Despite the initial wait, our time at Rubirosa was a testament to the fact that good things do indeed come to those who wait. We left with full bellies and fond memories, eagerly anticipating our next visit. Highly recommend for anyone willing to plan ahead or patient enough to endure the wait.

I only had a milkshake so I can't recommend any food. The milkshakes are awesome. The oreo milkshake had a great ratio of cookie and ice cream. The space was clean and quiet. The staff was friendly and worked quickly. This is a cute little spot. There isn't much seating though so just an FYI.

Title: A Flavorful Find in Chinatown with a Splash of Patience Required

Tucked away in the bustling streets of Chinatown, the new rice roll joint is a gem that shines despite its long queues - a testament to its popularity even on a weekday lunch. Pro tip: dine in pairs to navigate the seating dynamic efficiently, as larger groups might find themselves in a waiting game.

Upon finally diving into the culinary offerings, the fried fish skin was a surprising delight; skepticism was replaced by the satisfying crunch and the revival dip that brought zest to the fish. The BBQ pork with chives rice roll was quite standard, yet the lettuce inclusion was a welcome touch of freshness. Meanwhile, the marinated chicken slices roll, complete with unadvertised mushrooms, was the star dish that sang with flavor.

The Lai wan style assorted congee presented an authentic twist to the usual fare. It was a harmonious medley of squid, peanuts, and more, creating a delectable comfort food symphony. The shredded pork and preserved egg congee was reliable and didn't disappoint.

While the meal almost clinched a perfect score, the pricing of rice rolls seemed a bit lofty compared to local Cantonese alternatives. Nonetheless, the congee prices were reasonable. With commendable service and a great dining atmosphere, this place is definitely worth a visit, though perhaps with a more prepared wallet. Overall, it's a solid 4 out of 5 stars for this Chinatown discovery.

Title: A Haven for Burger Aficionados at Bareburger

My family's latest dining adventure brought us to Bareburger, an establishment that radiates artistry and contemporary flair, expertly bridging the divide between meat lovers and plant-based patrons. Their cleverly designed menu—meat-centric fare on one side, vegan delights on the other—offered something tantalizing for each of us.

I indulged in the So Cal turkey burger which was a revelation in both taste and texture; the turkey patty was unexpectedly tender, melting in the mouth with ease, and complemented by the robust flavors of guacamole, alfalfa sprouts, pickled onions, and gooey cheese atop a nourishing sprouted bun.

My son eagerly tackled the Sante Fe chicken sandwich, taking particular delight in its crispy exterior and succulent interior, signifying a well-executed poultry dish.

Meanwhile, my wife sampled the vegan Farmstead, an innovative lettuce wrap featuring a hearty sweet potato, kale, and wild rice patty. Although she savored the flavors, she noted her preference for a more traditional bun in future orders.

A shared portion of Sweet Fries with the house sauce, akin to the renowned Chick-fil-A dip, proved to be a crowd-pleaser, striking a delectable balance between crispy and tender.

Our thirst was quenched by the strawberry lemonade, a refreshing concoction that captured the essence of both fruit and zing without veering into overly sweet territory.

Exceptional customer service was the cherry on top of a satisfying experience, ensuring our planned return later in the week. Bareburger has impressed us with its inclusive and flavorful approach to the classic burger joint.

We stopped in here after going on the St. Patrick's Cathedral Catacomb tour (GO. DO. THIS!), so we could say we ate in Little Italy.  And we did.  We ordered the Bruschetta appetizer, a House Salad, and a small White Pizza, to share amongst 3 of us.  While waiting for our food, the Sangria and cider (Magner's!) were both very good.  The waitress was worried that we might be disappointed in the amount of food, for 3 of us.  But once we let her know we weren't there to really fill up, she was good to go.  We enjoyed every bit of that food, and didn't leave stuffed, but with VERY happy moufs!

My recent brunch visit to the 3rd ave location was a mixed affair. We had a reservation for 11:30 and were pleased to be seated immediately upon arrival, joining around 20 other patrons. A hiccup occurred when we were informed that the French toast, my sister's preferred choice, was unavailable. She settled for the pancakes, which thankfully, she found satisfactory.

I was looking forward to the unlimited brunch, but my anticipation was dampened when told that the frozen margarita machine wasn't operational. Another disappointment was the delayed arrival of the guacamole and chips, served to us 20-25 minutes later than expected, indicating a lack of preparedness for the restaurant's opening.

Our food followed just 10 minutes after the appetizer, but by then, the initial enthusiasm had waned. The overall experience fell short of expectations, leaving room for improvement in both service and readiness.

Utterly disappointed with my experience here. Food was disgusting which is unacceptable at this price. The hamachi ceviche tasted as if the fish had gone bad, and they never brought the tuna we ordered. The banana on the duck was way too overpowering and ruined the dish. The eggplant had no flavor and the pork was so average it's insane how much it costs. My water was only refilled when I asked and every time the server poured he spilled it all over the table (happened like 4 times). Can't believe I paid $300 for bad food and to leave hungry. All the dishes did look very pretty and the pickled cucumbers were insanely good.

I recently had the pleasure of trying the Margherita Pie from a local pizza spot, and it exceeded my expectations. The beauty of a Margherita pizza lies in its simplicity, and this restaurant nailed it. The crust struck that ideal balance of thickness and flavor—a foundation that held up to the scrutiny of a pizza aficionado. The tomato sauce was a standout, rich and robust, complementing the well-seasoned toppings to a tee. The speed of delivery impressed me as well; my pizza arrived quickly and was still piping hot. Taking cues from the rave Yelp reviews, I am delighted with my choice and commend the restaurant for their excellent execution. Big thumbs up for a truly satisfying pizza experience!

We saw the line while out walking around Times Square on Saturday afternoon and evening. The line was probably a block long. Our hotel was just across the street and I had planned to go there for breakfast the next day. When we finally got back to our hotel, I looked out the window around 10:00 p.m. and there was still a line. When we woke the next day, I looked out the window again and there was no line at 7:00 a.m. so we quickly got out there and we were one of the first few people to be seated. It was nice and quiet -- at first.I ordered the bacon, spinach, mushroom omelette which came with tater tots. I love tater tots! Hubby ordered the breakfast burrito. You won't find any complaints here. Food was great and filling. Then, as we were eating, someone walks over to our table and starts singing. I had no idea this was a singing diner where the servers take turns belting out show tunes. I guess, why not, this is New York -- home to all the broadway shows. Towards the end of our meal, a woman comes out, not to sing, but to encourage the diners to fill a bucket for the wait staff who would use the funds to pay for voice and dance lessons. I don't mind so much the asking but they literally walked around the tables with the bucket. I think it would have been more appropriate to leave it by the exit door. We are already paying for overpriced orange juice at $4.95 per glass and $12 slice of cheesecake. And--- they add a 20% tip to your check (only 2 people) with a line for including additional tip. NOTE:  Noise level extremely high. There is a decibel meter that went over 100. Anything over 80 is considered high. If you're sensitive to noise, you would be uncomfortable.

Title: A Valentine's Delight with Minor Hiccups

My partner and I chose to celebrate Valentine's Day at this charming establishment, and it was quite the experience. Walking in, we were immediately enveloped by the warm and inviting atmosphere, a perfect score of 5/5, transporting us to what felt like the South of France.

The special Valentine's Day course menu, at $185 per person, offered an array of tantalizing appetizers. The lobster with caviar and cauliflower cream was superb, as were the rabbit liver ravioli and foie gras. However, the uni and oyster fell short, coming across as excessively fishy and failing to meet our expectations based on previous experiences. My cocktail, the Bell Reve, unfortunately did not excite my palate, lacking the punch I anticipated.

Our second course brought us a flavorful scallop dish paired with chestnut, but the scallop itself was slightly overcooked and sandy, which was a letdown. We communicated our concerns to the staff, and while we declined the manager's courteous offer for a replacement dish, their attentiveness in this matter was appreciated.

The main courses redeemed our evening. The filet de boeuf with its accompaniments was a standout, earning a well-deserved 5 stars. The fish paired with bone marrow and turnip was also quite enjoyable. We rounded off our meal with a selection of desserts, with the chocolate cake stealing the show for its delightful balance and texture.

A lovely gesture came during dessert when we were treated to a complimentary dessert wine as an apology for the earlier mishap, which we enjoyed immensely.

While the food overall scored a solid 4/5, the service was a bit of a mixed bag at 3/5. Despite the attentive moments, there were times where we felt neglected, particularly when we had to pour the last of our $300 wine ourselves—a rarity for a Michelin-starred venue.

In conclusion, despite some service issues and a couple of culinary missteps, the meal was delightful and the ambiance alone could tempt us to return, possibly for another special occasion.

I really love Artichoke. I really do.And I was so excited that through grubhub they deliver at home! Ordered few slices and guess what.- Order was placed around 9.15PM. - Order was confirmed and said that it will take 1h to be delivered (fine. It is just slices and we all know that Artichoke has them ready at the counter but be it)- 1h and 15 min later no news about the delivery. It is still not delivered.- Called grubhub support, they say that order is ready to be sent. Apologies.- 15min later, order still not sent. And estimated delivery is updated to 10.59PM-11.09PM!!!!! This is more than 1.5h from my order.- Got a call for the delivery man, that he is leaving and sorry for the delay.- it took more than 30 min to get here. And I really felt sorry for the delivery man who came all the way here with his bike- Pizza delivered 2h later and slices were of course, COLD.Yes, it is my fault because I've should stayed local and I would have gotten my pizza in no time and fresh from the oven.I took the risk because I really like Artichoke. They crab pizza is just simply amazing.Here is my complaint: either Artichoke or Grubhub. You should not commit to this service if you know that you are not going to meet the min standards. You are not able to deliver in the UES. Don't take this business because it will just affect negatively to your business. It is DECEIVING.What is the point of delivering a cold pizza 2h later?

Was here Friday night after work for dinner before a movie. I've here here numerous times and always have a great experience.Our waiter Anthony was very friendly and helpful especially with drink suggestions. Drinks:Triple Berry Sangria, I always order this. Its so yummy and gives me a nice buzz.Long Island, its a spin on the orginal long island iced tea. My friend loved it.Dinner:Create your own Ultimate FeastMe: lobster tail, shrimp scampi, coconut shrimp and crab legs. Garden salad with ranch dressing.Friend: lobster alfredo, steak, coconut shrimp, jumbo shrimp skewers.We both really enjoyed our meals and were too stuffed to order dessert. Everything was on point. Service was fast and friendly, food was cooked perfectly.

TLDR: From Iron Chef Morimoto comes Momosan Ramen & Sake. It's a solid addition to the Grand Central work area. If you work around here and are craving ramen for lunch or for a post-work dinner, not a bad option. I think there are better destinations if you're making a trip for ramen solely.I had read about Momosan in Eater right before they launched. So when I got a chance to try it, I thought it was really good the first time. The other times I've come back (maybe 3 or 4) it didn't wow me as much.I worked in Midtown East (mid 40s) for many years. So we never really quite had many dedicated ramen spots. Now you have Ippudo a bit West, Kuro-Obi by Vanderbilt and Nishida closer to the UN.I've never had a bad meal here but not really anything that blew me away either. It's decent and will give you your ramen fix though. They do well with presentation though.I've had a good amount of the menu. The gyoza is a bit unique, it comes on a cast iron dish with ginger/scallion. The Tokyo Chicken is my preferred choice if I end up here. The Tsukemen is nice to have as an option but it always feels like it's missing something. The ramen tastes a bit cleaner so if you're averse to a richer ramen - you might not like this one as much.The crispy mimiga (pig ears) are a great companion to a drink if you're here for that.Like I said, decent if you're in the area but not a place I'd go out of my way for or wait awhile.

These are good. Every time we go to NYC my husband has to go to Los taco. Though we prefer the one in Midtown this one is comparable but the prices are higher at this one. Fast and friendly service, fresh food and great flavors. They are streat tacos so they are on a 4" tortilla but they really fill it up. The problem I have is spending $4.00 for one. Other than that, a fun experience and a good lunch

I recently enjoyed a fantastic dining experience at this local gem. Opting for a balanced meal, I chose the 1/2 rice and 1/2 power green bowl, topped with savory chicken shawarma, creamy hummus, and a fresh Mediterranean salad. Every bite was a delight, particularly when I spiced it up with their zesty red sauce – it complemented the rice perfectly and served as a mouthwatering dip for the fluffy pita bread.

Convenience was also on the menu, as I ordered through Ritual and my food was ready in a rapid 5 minutes, despite it being 1:00 PM on a Thursday. To my surprise, the restaurant wasn't overly busy, adding to the relaxed atmosphere.

All in all, this spot is my new go-to for a quick, delectable lunch that doesn't skimp on flavor or satisfaction. Highly recommended!

I recently visited a local gem that served up some of the most delicious Mexican fare I've had in a while. The carne asada tacos were the highlight of my meal – packed with flavor, perfectly seasoned, and truly satisfying. To accompany my meal, I had the Jamaica, which was refreshingly delicious. Everything tasted fresh and had that authentic touch that is often hard to find. The thought alone makes my mouth water; I could easily eat here every day. Highly recommended for anyone craving a taste of authenticity!

This weekend, my sister and I decided to try out Friedman's for brunch while exploring the area. The ability to join the waitlist beforehand was a game-changer; we were seated instantly upon arrival. We cozied up on the cafe side, which had a super chill vibe.

To kick things off, I sipped on a delightful Bellini and we shared a refreshing fruit plate. I indulged in the breakfast burger, which was a satisfying choice, while my sister enjoyed the savory potato pancakes paired with bacon. The food certainly lived up to its reputation—delicious through and through.

I now understand why Friedman's comes so highly recommended. It's a definite must-visit for future brunch outings.

Title: A Toast to Good Spirits and Great Company

My visit to this gem in the heart of Manhattan was nothing short of delightful. The highlight? Sipping on expertly crafted Manhattans while the bartenders dazzled us with their mixology and radiant charm. With each cocktail, the ambiance only grew more vibrant, sparking an infectious mirth among my companions and me. By the end of the fourth round, I was thoroughly imbued with joy—the hallmark of a truly memorable evening. Cheers to the jolliest of experiences! Amen to that!

I had my heart set on lots of Italian food while in NY, and I wanted a casual place that served lunch in Lower Manhattan.  With it being NY and me staying in Soho, Coco Pazzo was one of many choices, and I'm happy I chose it.  I walked in around 2 on a Friday afternoon to see the spacious restaurant full but not packed to the gills.  I was seated at the bar and provided immediate service.  I started with a cesar, which had full leaves of romaine and the perfect amount of dressing--enough to enjoy the flavor in every bite but not too much where the leaves were weighed down.  I loved my cacio e pepe dish.  The bucatini was deliciously al dente, and the sauce was silky, smooth, and had that perfect sheen that a simple, well-made cacio e pepe dish has.  By the time I left the place was packed.  The ambiance here is bright but warm, spacious but not cavernous.  And cheers to the friendly Italian staff!

Definitely some room for improvement here. My friends and I shared a half Tie-Dye, half Rubirosa Supreme pizza. The good stuff: the deliciously crispy crust and the sweeter-than-normal tomato sauce. On a overall level, the pizzas needed work. The vodka sauce on the Tie-Dye was subpar, more tomato than cream. I couldn't really taste the pesto, and the crust was too delicate to hold all the sauces so the toppings were constantly sliding down. The Rubirosa Supreme was slightly better, accentuated by the Prince Street-esque slices of pepperoni.

Title: Cozy Spot with Big Flavors

Last night, four of us dined at this charming, albeit snug, eatery that packed a flavorful punch in every dish. Despite the limited space and the exclusive acceptance of American Express (though an ATM on-site helps), the culinary experience was superb.

A standout was their unique take on Caesar Salad, zesty with a mustard-infused dressing—truly a delightful twist on the classic. While the service was generally good, there was a mix-up with my salad; I requested no croutons, and yet it came with flatbread artistically placed, and unfortunately crumbled in, which I'd hoped to avoid. Normally, a service slip-up might dim my opinion, but the quality of the food won me over.

The signature pasta dishes received high praise, the oxtail was sumptuously satisfying, and the salmon was met with rave reviews. My wife's pasta seafood dish was enjoyable, though she was less vocal than the rest of our smitten party.

In conclusion, despite a few hiccups in service and space, the delectable dishes make this restaurant a must-visit for those seeking mouthwatering meals.

I decided to try their stuffed grape leaves today, it was kind of frustrating tbh. The stuffed grape leaves you could definitely taste were not the canned ones. They tasted pretty fresh, however they were INSANELY cheap with the stuffing to the point it was mostly just grape leaves. The ones that did have stuffing were pretty good, but the lack or consistency amongst them was very frustrating.

Came here for drinks at the ground floor lounge bar. Beautiful space. Cocktail menu some are interesting but the proportion of the ingredients could be more balanced in my opinion. For example I think Nightcap is too sweet ; White Kimchi Gibson is overpowering with Daikon ; Crowned King on the sweeter side ; Heaven's Son was pretty good but more standard. Would come back to try the snacks.

From the quality and taste of the food to the ambience to the people that work there, this place ROCKS.I don't what took us so long to check out Tender Greens, but better late than never. Make no mistake this is not anything like Sweet Greens or any of those make your own salad joints by any means. And, it's everything that Dig Inn should be, but isn't. That was the mistaken assumption that kept us from checking it out before now.  For a bite before catching a movie, or just looking for a casual spot for healthy, tasty and delicious food, TG is the place.The last two times were were there we had the Holiday Steak, their November chef special. It's grilled top sirloin with red wine shallot reduction, crispy brussels sprouts, and whipped sweet potatoes. It's served with a kale Caesar salad, house-made sourdough croutons, and Parmesan. At $14, it's a pretty sweet deal.And if you don't kale, you can substitute it for other greens, which I did this last time. Either way it's yum-meee!We also had the other November chef special which is a pumpkin humus toast with cranberries. It was delish. Reasonably priced. Good food. Great location. Couldn't ask for anything else.

WATCH OUT FOR THIS PLACE!!!! The worker will sign for you and tip himself!!!! Especially if he thinks you're drunk. Came here at 10:30pm on a Friday night. Their POS system is Square. My friend ordered and paid first, I thought it was weird how the worker (Marco) didn't swivel the screen to my friend for her to sign and tip. He didn't even give a receipt either. I, as well as I'm sure many of us, are familiar with the Square POS system and know the flow of checkout. You insert your card, the cashier turns the screen for you to sign and tip, choose your receipt option, and then swivels it back. Right?I ordered next and wanted to give him the benefit of the doubt. Again, he just quickly said thank you and returned my card. No signature or receipt. Thought this was fishy and asked him for a receipt. He immediately got nervous and was fiddling around the screen. He finally printed my receipt and there it was!!!! He had tipped himself and signed for me. Asked him to print my friends receipt as well.. and there it was. I think he thought we were drunk or something? And thought he could get away with this. It doesn't seem like it was his first time doing this either. I confronted him and told him it was wrong of him and that he shouldn't do that. He was deflecting and pretending he didn't "know" how to use the POS. He didn't even own up to it or apologize. Bullsh*t. I told this to the manager as well and all she could do was freakishly smile and say a lukewarm "sorry". I feel like they have been doing this for a while, definitely was not their first go. I immediately asked them for a refund on the tip and they obliged. While I was eating, I noticed Marco ringing up customers. Of course he was finally following protocol and going through the checkout system correctly because he swiveled the screen to the customer to sign! But just 2 minutes ago you signed for me and my friend and when confronted said you "didn't know how to use the system". I would avoid this place at all costs. It's overpriced crepes and they're not even that great! I personally prefer TSwirl Crepe. Never coming here again, they've completely lost my trust and respect.

Came here on a thursday night. There was a line outside already but since we were a party of two, we got inside 2 minutes after lining up.  They scan IDs as soon as you walk in. We were then led to our table.They have an assortment of cheap cocktails and shots. Food is pretty cheap as well. Ordered some shots and cocktails. The drinks came out super quickly and were decently strong. Also ordered lemon chicken, fries, karaage, and calamari.Service is spotty. Have to flag down waiters. One of the waiters placed our order on the wrong table (next to us) and after about 5 minutes, just moved it back to our table. I had no problem w it cause i saw that the other table did not touch it but the waiter did not seem to care about that... Food came out about 20 minutes later. Waiter forgot my salad and rice that came w the lemon chicken and had to ask another waiter for it.Lemon chicken was very sour- the sauce seemed to be just butter + lemon juice but it tasted alright with the rice! Calamari was a little soft, not crispy enough. Fries and karaage were very good!Would come again for cheap drinks and bar food

Came here for a private holiday party in the loft. The space was wonderful for dinner, dancing and a good bar with wonderful views of lower Manhattan and the Statue of Liberty. The passed apps were flavorful and the dinner itself was well prepared, prompt and didn't feel Mechanically produced. The drinks were poured well and not watered down. Private coat check and ambiance made it a perfect spot for us.

If your ever visiting the Mercado little spain market and love seafood this is the area you need to visit you need to visit. The staff that we encountered were all very friendly and helpful. To get a seat was a bit of wait because we had no reservation but I thought it was worth it. There was also plenty of other areas within the market so the wait gave our group some time to explore. I dined with a group of friends and we all agreed that the food was delicious. The only dish that we disagreed about was their endive salad. Personally I thought it was bitter tasting. But everything else we tried I heard no complaints about.For my main entree I ordered a dish called - pescado a la plancha con patatas pandera - which was basically red snapper fish filleted over a bed of potatoes. I also had a dish called  ajo blanco malagueno con gambitas which tasted like a delicious gazpacho soup filled with shrimp. Both dishes were excellent and I would definitely visit again.

I absolutely adore this restaurant! The drinks and food here never disappoint - they're both satisfyingly filling. The only snag is the inevitable wait due to its popularity. Service can be slow on occasion, with some delays in the waitress reaching our table. Despite this, my experiences here keep me coming back for more.

While on a trip to NYC, we had a craving for matzah ball soup, which we can't get at home. So we went to the deli, and the soup was good. They bring you delicious sauerkraut and pickles, which were really good. Potato pancakes were sort of cake-like; not the best. The corned beef, according to others in our party, was lean and tender. The kasha knish was gigantic, and it was pretty good. When we were done they brought us samples of the chocolate soda they make there, which in and of itself was worth the trip.

I had been wanted to come here, but it's ALWAYS packed. So I decided to make a reservation and got the first one I could find on a Saturday about 3 weeks out. When I showed up it was crowded as usual. I had to wait about 5 min to get to the host stand. The vibe here is casual. Both in the tavern and the dining room. Despite the white table cloths, many of the patrons around me were in jeans. I am not sure what I was expecting, but I thought it was going to be slightly more fancy than this. The service was great. Always someone around and people checked in with me frequently to see if I liked my food. I ordered the vegetarian tasting menu. First bite from the kitchen - these are always good no matter what they are. I enjoyed mine, though I couldn't tell you what was in it other than I think it contained kohlrabi.Hakurei TurnipTrumpet Mushrooms, Ponzu. The mushroom was meaty, in a good way. It was bright and tangy from the ponzu. CauliflowerBurrata, Almonds, croutons. Oh my goodness was this good. It was creamy, crunchy. I liked the different textures from the different cauliflower (cooked vs shaved raw). The burrata and the green sauce on the bottom! Oh my! So good. Winter citrus with quinoa. I wasn't a huge fan of this dish. I think it was missing something, but I'm not sure what. The quinoa was cooked well and flavorful. I think perhaps it was missing something with a bit more of a crunchy texture. Ricotta CavatelliButternut Squash, Kale, Pumpkin Seeds - I really enjoyed this dish. It was small, but heavy. The pasta was thick but had a nice almost gummy texture, which went nicely with the sauce. The sauces in there were creamy and rich, and the pumpkin seeds added a nice crunch.  I really enjoyed this! Next was the roasted mushrooms. Following the earlier mushroom dish which I enjoyed, I didn't care for this one as much.  A variety of mushrooms, but I didn't finish. Next was the apple sorbet pallet cleanser. Light and fresh. Finally was the caramelized cheesecake. This was like a cross between creme brûlée and a cheesecake. I enjoyed the flavors and texture. I appreciate that Danny Meyer restaurants are no tipping facilities. I like knowing when I go in how much I'm going to spend, and appreciate even more that the service is still impeccable.Overall, a few standout dishes and a few that were just okay. Great service. Casual ambiance. I'll try the raven next time (if I can ever get a table) to try out that burger!

The dining room is still beautiful, the service is still professional, the bar area is hopping and classy.  Yet it is a new era here.  The menu is completely revamped.  New blood has taken over, suppose the ~30 year Portale legacy has moved aside to allow for change.  Yet, they kept the name and all the advertising of being 3 Stars in New York Times, 1 Michelin Star, and 27 Food Ranking in Zagat.  I don't know of many restaurants in Manhattan that have run for so long under the same name. Most would close for "renovations" and never re-open. So I guess longevity earns a star as well?Stopped in for a simple lunch, the bone marrow burger and steak (cut not mentioned on menu, but it was a strip). Those two items were done very well. It was a quick weekday lunch and not a full meal. Will be back for sure to sit through a proper dinner. Despite trying to "relax" the vibe, most of the lunch dining room were suits, seemingly from out of town. I think (and I'm just a simple guy on Yelp) the right thing to do would be renaming this restaurant so Blamey could earn her own reputation versus trashing the previous regime while benefitting from the history this establishment previously deserved. She's talented for sure and front house, ambiance are still A+, just don't go here for the reputation Gotham earned from the past.

Fabulous and Flawless experience each and every time! The staff, the food and the ambiance are all shining stars and compliment each other perfectly. Last night was just one of the many occasions where I have enjoyed a great evening of food, love, friends and family in this beautiful restaurant. My partner and I arrived around 9pm for an after-work dinner and took advantage of their half-off wine selections, sharing a bottle. We originally ordered the Barbera, but at the suggestion of Marcello, one of their managers we have become familiar with in our many visits, got his highly recommended Barolo instead. The wine was perfect and now a personal favorite. For food, we decided to share two pasta dishes (HANGRY) and we ordered the Black Linguine Special. It was prepared with shrimp and mussels, in a white wine sauce, garnished with jalapenos (cool touch) and tomatoes. We special requested the Parpadelle (on their specials menu) with their house bolognese instead. Everything was well presented, delicious and fresh. Before the food arrived, a warm bread basket and the wine were served. The food is always phenomenal, but the staff may have it beat! Everyone who works here really looks like they love what they do and the food and people they serve. It is the kind of neighborhood place where its easy to become a regular. You are treated like family and the small space adds to a feeling of community. It is very easy to strike up a conversation with the patrons beside you and every outing there feels like a get together with familiar friends. A very special recognition goes out to Marcello, who always makes sure we are attended to and enjoying our meal. Thank you all and we will be back very soon :)

This place was inside of the busy market at eataly. It was noisy and felt like they were trying to serve people in the middle of a grocery store. The food was ...... below average. This is my second time back here and I will not be returning. The calimari was decent. The clam pasta lacked any flavor or sauce and was just pasta with clams still in their shells. The service was good but unfortunately the main dishes, that we barely touched, and paid $150 for left us feeling gyped.

Title: A Hearty Feast at TabeTomo – NYC's Haven for Jiro Ramen and Tsukemen

As a connoisseur of ramen eager to explore beyond the usual offerings, I was drawn to TabeTomo for its promise of rare-to-find Jiro ramen and tsukemen in the heart of New York City's ramen-saturated landscape. TabeTomo delivers on its promise with gusto, serving up generous portions that set it apart from the fray.

Jiro ramen, hefty with its udon-thick noodles, a mountain of bean sprouts, and sizable cha shu slices, is an indulgent delight for those with voracious appetites. Alternatively, the tsukemen presents a playful twist on the traditional ramen – you'll find yourself dunking noodles and cha shu into a separate, rich tonkotsu broth accompanied by vegetables and a perfectly soft-boiled egg.

While the dishes are generously portioned and fairly priced at $18, the robust tonkotsu base – although flavorful – leans towards the saltier end of the spectrum. Keep a glass of water handy to balance out the experience. The true standout, however, is the cha shu – tender, well-marbled, and flavor-packed, it harmonizes with the chewy, broth-clinging noodles. Not to forget the egg, which is an embodiment of perfection with its oozy yolk.

In conclusion, TabeTomo excels in offering an authentic and fulfilling ramen experience, with unique dishes that are a must-try for any ramen aficionado in NYC. Whether you're in for a substantial meal or feeling bold enough to dip your toes into something new, TabeTomo won't disappoint.

I have visited a number of times now and can honestly say that I very much savor their wonton soup which includes bok choy, bean sprouts, onions, chicken/shrimp wontons and a light veggie broth. Aside from the soups, I have sampled almost all of their lunch specials and it's pretty solid fare.Here's the caveat, I'm not usually a fan of thai food.  I do believe that I like the food because it's not your traditional thai food.  Although a number of dishes lean more towards the sweeter end, when an item is labeled as spicy please believe them.It's a small location that is still in the stages of building a steady clientele. The prices are affordable and they're pretty consistent when I stick to the standard basics.

I ended up here last minute on Valentine's Day we had rsvp for 7 arrived a little early & had no problem being seated. I must say I was glad to see that they didn't have any price fix menu for the occasion am generally not a fan of this simply because most of the time it tends to be highly overpriced. Once seated we started with a bottle of wine, a Pinot Grigio not bad good wine.  Next came the bread & olive oil to start very good great tasting olive oil.  Appetizers we gave the Calamari a try this was very good so glad we decided to share since it was a pretty big dish.. lightly battered nice dipping sauce.  Main dish I had the Pesto Gnocchi good gnocchi nice pesto taste. My company had the Spaghetti & meatballs not bad but the sauce lacked flavor. Nice restaurant, seating is a bit too tight not that the place is that big but it would b nice if u had a bit more room in between u & the next table. Nice date atmosphere service was good & prices are not bad & normal to the area, we enjoyed our meal.

It's a very cute restaurant because they have really interesting decor. They have a bar that looks like a van, and a takeout counter that looks like a food stall. I personally feel like the menu is quite small, but everything I had was quite decent! I would say it's a place for a quick dinner as there's always a line, and they would hope that you leave after you finish your food so other people could have the table.

Despite initial hesitation due to a surprisingly low rating, my visit to the cafe endorsed by Queer Eye's Antoni proved to be a delightful experience. The complaints about the pricing seem somewhat justified, although not out of line with similar establishments. The ambiance of the cafe won me over - it was incredibly charming, spacious, and offered comfortable seating, complete with the conveniences of plentiful outlets and WiFi.

The staff added to the charm with their sweetness and helpfulness, making the experience all the more pleasant. As for the menu, the Den Mother bowl was a revelation; the combination of beet hummus, pomegranate seeds, and squash was unexpectedly delightful, while the lentils at the bottom were so perfect that they have inspired my own culinary endeavors.

Although the Thai Chicken didn't quite match up to the high standard set by the Den Mother, it was a decent option that I would still recommend. Overall, a visit to this cafe is a must, especially if you're a fan of Antoni's work or simply in search of a cozy spot with soul-satisfying food.

I hadn't been here in a while but it was getting close to dinnertime and I remembered the last time I was there I had the most delicious steak frites. I decided to have it once again. I walked in, was seated and given a menu. Cold water arrived and shortly after french bread and butter. I knew what I wanted and ordered the steak medium well. It is a large space, square shaped on the corner of 8th Avenue and 46th Street. My food arrived and the steak came with French fries. Usually they are shoestring potatoes but this time the fries were larger and tastier. It was an excellent meal. The staff was attentive and accommodating, someone taking the order and someone would bring it to you when it was ready to eat. I would recommend for either lunch or dinner and/ pre or post theater.

Upon arrival during happy hour, the bustling atmosphere of the restaurant was immediately noticeable. Despite the crowd, securing a table was surprisingly hassle-free, a testament to the establishment's efficient accommodations, which also include reservations. The menu offered an appealing selection of snacks, perfectly complemented by an impressive array of drinks. The piña colada, in particular, was a standout for me, though the diverse drink options meant all tastes were catered to. Price points were slightly elevated, but not unexpected for the locale. Overall, I left as a big fan of the experience.

Luke's Lobster never fails to hit the spot with their classic lobster rolls, a must-have for any seafood lover. No matter which location I visit, the quality is unwaveringly high, ensuring a satisfying and consistent experience with every bite. The craving for one of these delightful rolls just keeps bringing me back. Highly recommended for a reliable and delicious treat.

Vic's never disappoints. Whether for lunch or dinner or brunch, Vic's is always a terrific spot. A sister restaurant to Cookshop, Shuka and Rosie's, Vic's delivers awesome Italian-American fare all the time. Their pizzas and pastas are great, but so is the rest of the menu. Beyond the creative food, the cocktails and the service are terrific too. Great choice any time.

I recently enjoyed an early lunch at this trendy spot after booking easily through Resy. The service was exceptional, with attentive staff across the board. We indulged in the double cheeseburger, which surprisingly arrived with three hearty patties – a step above the already ample single cheeseburger that boasts two. Alongside, the potatoes with chicken heart gravy and eggs were a savory delight. Each dish was packed with flavor, ensuring this restaurant is firmly on my must-return list.

This seems like a decent place to grab food and adult beverages. Alfie's totally has a neighborhood bar/local watering hole vibe to it. I have walked past the place a million times, but this was my first time at the restaurant/bar.  Probably many of the patrons are folks who either work or live nearby. I was a little disappointed with a couple of my cocktails, so I would recommend that you stick to the basics - beer, spirits on the rocks (which I eventually started to drink), or wine. Unfortunately, my martini was not up to par - way too much vermouth and olive juice. Also, the martini was served with an even number of olives. Aren't martinis supposed to be served with an odd number of olives (no biggie for me)? At least, Alfie's has a pretty good selection of beer . . . I cannot speak about the selection of wine. Although I did not order any food, the plates that passed me did smell delicious.

I really enjoyed the happy hour my group had at the Mermaid Inn.  There were 6 of us and we ordered an assortment of foods and drinks from their menu.  I had the Pink Flamingo drink which was gin, strawberry, lemon, and basil syrup.  It was a well-balanced and refreshing drink--not too sweet at all.  I had the mini clam chowder, fried calamari, and an order of the hushpuppies for my meal.  The mini clam chowder is definitely "mini", but very tasty.  The calamari was great.  Very crispy, good flavor, and a generous portion size.  The hushpuppies were delicious and served with a nice remoulade.  There were at least 6 hush puppies served which I thought was a really great portion size. It made for a nice shareable dish. Others in the group shared oysters which they all enjoyed.  Overall a great spot to check out. Very nice decor and great happy hour specials. Good for groups or an intimate date.

Tucked away behind the curtains past the front desk of The Frederick Hotel lies an unassuming gem perfect for those in search of a chill evening. The dimly lit ambiance is enriched with cool, old-school vibes, making it a refreshing escape in the heart of TriBeCa. Enjoying a glass of Gamay, I found the red wine to be quite palatable.

The seating is comfortable and intimate, especially the corner circle booth that allows for effortless conversation without the usual backdrop of blaring music. My companions sampled a variety of cocktails and gave them their seal of approval.

Overall, this spot is a delightful find for anyone looking to unwind in a relaxed setting with good drinks and great company. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

I recently dined at a local spot with friends visiting from out of town. Despite it being a warm summer evening, the restaurant's choice to keep the doors open made it uncomfortably hot, although the AC did offer some relief.

We kicked off with drinks – my cocktail was a highlight. For food, we shared fried chicken sliders and a fig jam & prosciutto pizza. The sliders hit the mark with their crispness and flavor, but the pizza fell short due to a stingy spread of fig jam, which failed to live up to its potential.

Service was amiable, if a bit uneven; understandable given the busy setting, but quicker attention would've been preferred.

The major drawback, however, was the noise level. With no soft surfaces to dampen the sound and music blasting, conversation was a struggle. The ambiance ranged from 'loud' to 'very loud,' making it a challenge for our group spanning a wide age range to engage with each other.

While the place has potential, and I might consider returning on a quieter evening for a drink, the cacophony on a busy night would deter me from a repeat visit if I wanted to enjoy a chat with my meal.

Where do I even begin. The first time I ate at this restaurant was for a friends birthday dinner, I've been hooked ever since! I've ordered several different items from their menu in the past and I've thoroughly enjoyed each one. You receive large portions for a low price. The food is authentic and very flavorful. The best part is that it's spicy AND they throw in a pepper. All you spice lover out their can understand and appreciate my excitement. Especially when you've been to places that claim their food is "spicy", only to be disappointed one you realize it's not. I've eaten at several African restaurants in Harlem and this is my favorite  thus far. Give it a try, your tastebuds will thank me.

What a phenomenal experience. This was my first time at a Michelin Star restaurant and Daniel did not disappoint. It was an entire production- about 3.5 hours from start to finish. I did the four course with wine pairing. For my first course I had the marinated yellow tuna, second course tarbot fish, third course lamb chop and fourth course a Java chocolate dessert. I loved all of my wines except the last, which I asked them to switch out and they did. Service was executed very well. We didn't feel rushed and instead all of the servers explained things well, answered our questions and were very friendly. I loved every dish I had. It was like edible art. Definitely expensive, but worth it!

Title: A Chic Fusion of Flavors at Cosme

I recently dined at Cosme for lunch, scouting it out as a venue for a future dinner event, and it left quite an impression. The restaurant sports a modern look, with a trendy vibe apparent in both the bar area at the front and the dining room at the back.

On a return visit for dinner, the atmosphere morphed into something akin to a chic club scene – a touch too loud for my taste, yet undeniably vibrant.

The culinary experience, however, was nothing short of excellent. I indulged in the Arctic char tostada and the sole entrée – both were an explosion of flavor in modestly sized portions that proved to be quite satisfying, especially when each bite was savored. The meal concluded on a high note with their signature meringue, which was truly exceptional.

Additionally, the agua fresca avocado lemonade was a refreshing accompaniment, complementing the meal perfectly. The service mirrored the quality of the dining – impeccable.

Be warned, the prices are steep, but for those in search of a unique take on modern Mexican cuisine, Cosme is well worth it. Don't expect the casual fare of a traditional taqueria; this place elevates Mexican dining to a new level of sophistication.

Title: Disappointing Return to [Restaurant Name]

My latest dining experience at [Restaurant Name] was underwhelming, a noticeable decline from previous visits. Service was notably absent; flagging down a server to place an order proved to be a challenge.

The carob acai bowl I eagerly anticipated turned out to be a letdown, filled with unappetizing chunks of frozen ice and lacking in flavor. The cappuccino, unfortunately, fared no better—it was burnt to the extent that not even sugar could salvage its taste.

An unexpected 2.5% surcharge on credit card payments added insult to injury. This fee was applied without prior notice—only spotted on the bill after my card was processed. Transparency regarding payment preferences or additional fees should be clearly stated on the menu, as credit cards are a standard form of payment.

Overall, the quality of both food and service has regrettably deteriorated, and the payment surcharge was a displeasing surprise.

I've only gotten take out / delivery from this place since they changed their name. The mapo tofu was really authentic and tasty and that is a good test to see if a Sichuan restaurant is good. I got the pan fried dumplings too but they were about the same quality as store bought frozen ones so that was a little disappointing. I think this place has potential!

After my weekend workout at Equinox, the promise of healthy zucchini pancakes drew me into the restaurant. Unfortunately, the meal didn't quite meet my expectations. The culinary identity of the establishment seemed a bit confused, straddling between French and Mediterranean without a clear direction. However, a delightful surprise awaited in the form of the bathroom – a whimsical space disguised as a bookcase that opened into a 'secret room,' providing a touch of delightful charm to an otherwise underwhelming experience.

The Pho 6 serves pho, banh mi, vermicelli and rice dishes with super fast service and a cozy dining room. All the lunch items were under $15 and they have dine in and take out. Welcome to the neighborhood!Dining room is small, with seats for 24. It's clean and cozy, but not good for big groups unless you're willing to come off peak. Broth is clean, not too salty. Table comes with hoisin and Sriracha. Noodles were perfect. Came with plenty of thinly sliced beef, side of bean sprouts and basil and lime. For the neighborhood, I think the bowls are a steal. I'll have to try the banh mi next. Park across the street if you want to take out and eat al fresco.

Recently, I dined at a restaurant boasting an extensive selection of dishes. The sides garnered praise, particularly the potato croquettes which stood out with their crispy exterior and pillowy soft interior, free from any unpleasant old oil taste. The pork belly was a highlight as well, featuring a perfectly formed crust while maintaining a tender and juicy core.

Unfortunately, not all dishes met these highs. The okonomiyaki fell short, being notably soggy rather than the expected crisp texture. The eel don was a disappointment; it was underwhelming in flavor and the eel itself was scant, overshadowed by tofu and rice. Additionally, although the karaage had a satisfactory crunch, it was let down by a lack of seasoning, leaving me to taste nothing beyond the breading and the oil it was fried in.

Title: Enchanting Rooftop Dining Experience at Edition Hotel

Review:

I recently dined at the rooftop garden inside Edition Hotel, a particularly stunning spot on a bustling Halloween Thursday night. Reservations are a must if you fancy sitting in the garden; thankfully, the inside seating was more than adequate.

The appetizers included Pommes frites at $10, which were decent. The Grilled octopus, priced at $20, fell short with very few pieces offered. However, the Deep dish focaccia, costing $16, stood out as the best starter. Sadly, the Baby romaine salad was underwhelming, with just six leaves for $16.

Moving on to mains, the King crab pasta at $39 was flavorful with fresh crab meat. The Comte cheese tortellini was just okay in taste, and at $34, it came with very few pieces. The Scallops, also priced at $34, included three well-cooked, tasty scallops. The Long Island Duck was comparatively a sizeable dish and delicious for $38.

On the downside, I found the prices to be inflated, likely a premium for the hotel setting. However, the ambiance was delightful, and the cocktails were a hit. Despite the prices, we're already considering a daytime return to experience the garden in daylight. Overall, I'd rate it a solid 4 out of 5 for the combination of ambiance, food quality, and service.

I recently dined at a local restaurant and came away underwhelmed with my meal. I ordered a chicken and cranberry dish that promised a medley of broccoli and cilantro, but these were noticeably absent, leaving me with a bowl dominated by romaine lettuce. The chicken and cranberries were sparse, which was disappointing. Additionally, the bread served alongside the meal was not warm, detracting from what could have been a comforting touch. I was also put off by the lemon peel garnish that didn't seem as clean as one would expect. Finally, the presentation was marred by a sticky cover on the bowl, which was unpleasant to handle. Overall, the experience was lackluster and left much to be desired.

Title: A Bustling New JoJu Branch Worth the Buzz in Midtown

As an ardent admirer of Elmhurst's JoJu and their legendary "Lin-Sanity" sandwich, I was thrilled by the Midtown expansion, nestled a stone's throw from 5th Ave. Despite the inevitable lunchtime crowds, the efficient dual ordering system (in-person and digital) and ample seating spread over two floors make the experience quite manageable. Prices are fair, with sandwiches at $10 and bowls at $11.

I sampled the lemongrass chicken bowl on a recent visit—brown rice heaped with tender chicken, classic banh mi garnishes, and a zesty green sauce. Although I tossed in spring roll bites for an extra $2, they were overshadowed by the bowl's other components. While the bowl was satisfying, my allegiance to their sandwiches remains unwavering, and I'll revert to those on my next visit.

A word to the wise: never overlook the fries. Be it the JoJu or kimchi varieties, these $7 double-fried wonders are culinary alchemy. The kimchi fries, in particular, were an indulgence that paid off in spades. This JoJu outpost certainly carries the torch of its predecessor with aplomb.

Came in on a Sunday afternoon, not too crowded at all. We had the large chicken noodle bowl, lamb soup dumplings, and the fried lamb ribs. Oh my goodness, so much good food. First of all the soup dumplings were incredible - make sure to bite from the top first and then work your way down. A little dry with the first bite of the dumpling wrapper - but that just sets you up for the rest of the dumpling. The juices is overflowing and more than makes up for the first bite. And the lamb - lamb for days and days - juicy, tender, ,mixed right in with the wrapper, the spoon is just to make sure you don't lose anything. Moving onto the short ribs - fried to perfection, crispy, fat trapped in, moist/juicy, tender, a little kick of spice - and with a side of spicy sauce to add if you like it hotter. Then the chicken noodle bowl, oh dear, my eyes were much bigger than my stomach. It's a giant bowl that would have been more than enough for 2 of us, for only $26-28.  Yes it's the noodles that make the dish - larger Asian noodles, flat - but oh so smooth, blends right in with the sauce. The chicken was very tender dark meat (the only acceptable meat) and there were peppers and potatoes, but let's be honest the noodles were the star of the show.

4p reservation. We were seated immediately, however our server did not come over until we waved one of them down. It was 4:20 by that time. The food was ok. Not really hot when it was served and didn't taste fresh. It took a long time (45m) to come out. Not even half the tables were full. The appetizer was scallops with an Asian slaw. The slaw had definitely been pre made and sitting for a while. It did not taste fresh and the cabbage was limp with a watery dressing- it was room temperature, and the scallops were chewy. We both ordered various grilled shrimp dishes...I had some shrimp and pasta and the shrimp was a little over cooked and was chewy. He ordered shrimp as well but it said it came with a side of rice, however it looked like less than a quarter of a cup. I was surprised with the quality (or there lack of) and quantity of the dishes. Especially as they were over $30 a plate. I'm afraid this place has gone too touristy and no longer stands up to the hype

I attended the boozy brunch at this restaurant, drawn in by the promise of good food and flowing drinks. Service-wise, I can't complain; the staff was attentive, ensuring our glasses were never empty. However, the food failed to match the quality of the service. Both the avocado toast and eggs Benedict were disappointments – the former was sparsely topped with avocado, while the latter was lacking in flavorful hollandaise sauce. If your priority is a good meal, I'd suggest dining elsewhere.

Title: A Slice Above the Rest – Bleeker Street Pizza

In the heart of the Big Apple, where pizzerias abound, Bleeker Street Pizza distinguishes itself as a beacon of culinary delight. Crowned "Best Slice in New York" by Food Network for three consecutive years, this bustling pizza haven truly lives up to its accolades. The star of the show, the Nonna Maria Slice, demands your attention. A masterful combination of a thin, crispy Tuscan crust expertly baked, adorned with a hearty, rustic tomato sauce, melted mozzarella, and a touch of fresh basil makes for an unforgettable pizza experience.

Despite the inevitable lunchtime flurry, Bleeker Street Pizza manages to offer a seamless experience with the choice of indoor or outdoor seating. Priced at a reasonable $3.50 per slice, it's a steal for pizza enthusiasts navigating the pricey cityscape. This isn't just another New York pizzeria; it's a culinary landmark that you simply cannot miss.

Great, affordable spot for excellent veggie ramen! I got the vegan tantanmen ramen, which wasn't listed on the menu for some reason, but was featured on a poster on the wall. It has delicious creamy cashew-based broth, and is topped with savory tofu crumbles and chili oil. A delicious bowl of ramen for $13 ($11 for lunch). A side of extra chili paste was $1. My only complaint is that the atmosphere is a little Chipotle-like: not nearly as cute of a spot as the location in Williamsburg, which is worthy of date night. But I'll definitely be coming back for more delicious noodles.

Title: A Mixed Bag at Tetsu - Burgers Triumph, Chicken Falters

Having been enticed by a Buzzfeed "Worth It" feature, my boyfriend and I visited Tetsu with high hopes for an indulgent meal. We decided to dive into both ends of the menu, sampling their renowned burgers alongside the sushi offerings.

The lamb burger was a revelation – my first foray into lamb patties didn't disappoint with its juicy richness far surpassing the beef burger, which, while satisfactory, lacked the same depth of flavor.
