However, priced at $23 each, the burgers seemed overpriced considering their lack of any truly extravagant toppings.

The masa toro roll, our sushi selection, was generously portioned, with a favorable balance of rice to fish, although slightly rice-heavy for my taste. Nevertheless, the high-quality toro made up for any excess starch.

Our shared appetizer, the spicy kari kari chicken, unfortunately, fell flat. While juicy, it lacked a distinctive flavor that would have made it memorable. In hindsight, we would have been better off sticking to the burgers and sushi.

In conclusion, Tetsu delivered a decent dining experience that matched some of our expectations, but with the steep prices and a hit-or-miss menu, a repeat visit doesn't appear imminent.

Wow. This tiny Chinatown restaurant is SO delicious. I ordered the roasted duck noodles with the fat hand pulled noodles (you have a choice between 5 types of noodles) and it was so so good. My friend ordered the roasted pork noodles, with the small wide noodles. The noodle dishes are very large - finish-able if you are hungry but for me served as two meals (one there and one later, from the leftovers I brought home)We also ordered the steamed shrimp dumplings to share, which were standard but good. We were also allowed to bring our own beer (I called ahead to make sure) and the server was happy to open them for us. You can tell that the noodles at this place truly are Hand-Pulled by the fresh taste and variation in size. We will definitely be back. I always like to say that I will come back and order something different but I know that realistically, I will come back and order the same thing.

My favorite tonkatsu place in midtown!! I would recommend the A-set or Gozen with anything! The pork and vegetable soup they give you is so delicious and feels like a warm hug on a cold day. The salad and potato salad are also great and refreshing to eat between bites of the tonkatsu. The skin on the tonkatsu is super crispy and fresh. And the price is so reasonable for a large amount of food!

I got Garlic Knots w/ Cheese for an on the go snack. To my disappointment was a pinch of cheese and that sticking more to the foil than breadI love cheese Read my Yelp bio and you'll see why my disdainNever again

I was looking at yelp and came across this and highly recommend. As soon as we walked in, we were greeted with today's pop and soft music which was a great touch. We ordered steamed dumplings and chicken fried rice. They were both delicious and the prices were fair for the amount of food. We went on a Sunday night at 7 and while the establishment is small, they had a table ready!

Title: A Flavorful Feast at an Unbeatable Price!

My recent lunch at this inviting restaurant turned out to be a delightfully delicious experience, offering an unlimited spread of tantalizing Indian dishes at an amazingly reasonable price. Joined by a party of seven, which included my boyfriend and his relatives, we found the ambiance cozy and the place welcoming, with ample space quickly arranged by the attentive staff.

The lunch menu impressed us with an all-you-can-eat offer on select dishes. Our group mainly chose between chicken curry and chicken tikka masala, though there were also beef, seafood, and vegetarian options available. A word to those with dietary restrictions: the menu doesn't explicitly list allergens, but the staff was vigilant once informed, carefully considering my tree nut allergy throughout the meal, including dessert modifications.

As for the food, be prepared for some heat! The spicy chicken curry and accompanying sides like chickpeas, lentils, and spinach with cheese definitely packed a punch, but the soothing presence of yogurt, rice, and naan, along with a shared mango lassi, was much appreciated and helped temper the spice levels.

The refill policy is generous, allowing for endless tastes of your chosen main dish and sides. While there was a minor commotion with another customer over dietary concerns, the staff managed the situation with composure and continued to provide exemplary service.

Our waiter's genuine concern for our dining experience was evident, as he sought feedback before we departed. My suggestion to the restaurant would be a clearer indication of dietary accommodations on the menu since Indian cuisine is known for its complex and sometimes unexpected ingredients.

All in all, the restaurant delivers a fantastic dining experience with friendly service and a focus on guest satisfaction, making it a superb choice for anyone craving an Indian food escapade.

Title: A Promising Brunch Spot in the West Village - Llamita

I recently visited the new Llamita in the West Village for brunch and had a positive experience. The hanger steak I ordered was quite delicious, served with a generous portion of greens that kept the meal from feeling too heavy. Although the steak was overcooked to well-done when I had requested medium rare, the overall quality of the food made up for this minor hiccup.

Regrettably, Llamita has yet to acquire their alcohol license, so for now, brunch is a dry affair. However, that should change soon based on what they've indicated. Despite these small issues, Llamita is a welcomed addition to the neighborhood. I'm looking forward to my next visit, possibly with a glass in hand.

Was visiting New York and decided to stop in for a healthy meal. It's like a Spanish infused Mediterranean cuisine. I order a make it myself bowl you get a wheat or white pita. With the bowl you get to choose from chicken, steak or gyro, I decided to get just veggie. You choose from there selection of hummus and 4 veggies, I got spinach hummus and for the 4 veggies I got rice, Spanish eggplant,  Mediterranean carrots and corn. For the toppings tomatoes, olives,  cabbage,  garlic sauce, cucumber, onion and fete cheese. And for a drink I got a pinot griego. I went upstairs to a gorgeous view of the city streets, a rustic look with brick walls and wooden table with iron chairs and wooden floors. They have booths or bar stools.  The employee were polite and friendly. They even come around and picked up your tray. As for the food it was good, health but not authentic. The pita was tough could of been toasty and softer. When I tried to take pictures and I was told I couldn't take pictures of the food line. I dont know maybe it's a New York thing.

Great ramen, although a little pricey for what you get. I had the classic miso, which came with a delicious rich and creamy broth, two pieces of cha siu, wood ear mushrooms, and half an egg. It was $15 so I would have liked to have more (only one thin slice of fish cake and half an egg, and charging $1 for chili oil seems stingy) but it was tasty! The good thing is that if you dine in, the lunch special includes a free beer (select drafts only).

We love going to Izakaya, and we found this spot with a really good happy hour menu. Since it was still early evening on Friday, it was still rather empty. I liked the cozy and homey atmosphere. We started off with some Yuzu Sake from Jokigen. Our server poured the sake into the glass, and continued to pour until it started to over flow into a wooden masu square. Sake was fruity, just the way I like it! My hubby was interested in their craft beer. Even more so after the general manager, Kiyo, walked over and started to have interesting conversation with us. He told us that they have the largest Japanese Craft Beer offering in NYC, and continue to add more. I ordered Hokkaido Melon Ale, with a really great cantaloupe flavor, love it! My hubby went with something that was really unique, Kyoto Beer Matcha IPA. It had deep, dark matcha green color, with an interesting flavor. Hint of matcha aroma, with that distinct bitter flavor of matcha. We got to try a few more beers, and they were really good!For food, we tried Smoking Anbai Miso Bacon, that gets torched right in front of you. So meaty and packed with amazing flavor! Totally loved it! Truffle Lotus Root Chips had a great truffle flavor with each bite. Crisp chips, lightly fried, a perfect accompaniment to any drinks! Tebasaki, Nagoya style Japanese chicken wings, came with a really nice portion. When I took my first bite, I must say I had no words...it was soooo delicious, totally out of control! My hubby said I had the "eyes of pleasure" like nothing he has ever seen. LOL.We had such fun time here, and it was really great talking with the general manager Kiyo. He was super friendly, and super knowledgeable when it came to food and drinks. What an amazing spot! We would definitely go back for more amazing food and drinks!

During a swift initial visit to this spot, I had the pleasure of tasting both the margherita and the square pepperoni pizzas. Both varieties left a strong impression, signaling the need for a swift return. While I'm still on the fence about labeling it a go-to destination, it certainly stands out as an exceptional local haunt. It's worth noting that when stacked against the slices from the much-touted F&F, this place had the upper hand. Highly recommend a visit for anyone in search of quality pizza.

As a self-proclaimed spice aficionado, I approached Spicy Village with a touch of skepticism. Initial concerns arose upon noticing my friend and I were the outliers in ethnic background, but the authenticity of the staff put us at ease when communication flowed in fluent Chinese.

Our culinary adventure was twofold. The Spicy Big Tray Chicken arrived in an ample bowl, partnered with tantalizing hand-pulled noodles reminiscent of those from Xi'an's. While the sauce's heat didn't fully satisfy my fiery cravings, it packed enough punch to entertain my palate. I wasn't thrilled by the presence of bones in the chicken but couldn’t deny its succulence and rich flavor.

On a milder note, the Noodz with Beef #16 featured the same delightful noodles sans the spice. The beef was lush and tender, offering a comforting balance to the meal.

In the grand pantheon of New York's spicy offerings, Spicy Village doesn't quite take the crown but is certainly a credible contender. It's worth a visit for anyone with a hankering for heat and hearty, hand-pulled noodles.

I had the pleasure of visiting an upscale restaurant that specializes in breakfast and brunch, providing an exquisite setting perfect for either a luxurious start to your day or an early business rendezvous. The main dining area is adorned with neoclassical decor reminiscent of the nineteenth century, adding a touch of elegance to the meal experience. Both the menu and the presentation of the dishes reflect the high-end nature of the establishment, complemented by impeccable service. This venue is truly a gem for anyone looking to indulge in a sophisticated morning dining affair.

Really unique spot for desserts and drinks! Hands down one of the trendiest cafes I've ever been to. A friend and I stopped by here just for drinks, but we witnessed some pretty creative desserts at neighboring tables. The creations were an experience in itself.I ordered a latte, which was good, but nothing extraordinary. My friend's Nutella Hot Chocolate was really good - rich, creamy, and perfect for the winter. Overall, great place for aesthetics, but everything on the menu is extremely overpriced. I'd recommend, but keep in mind you're most likely paying for the ambiance and overall experience rather than the drinks/food.

Normally when I order ramen, I always pass the pork to my bf because I'm not the biggest fan of the fatty parts of porks. But holy porkorino their ramen is good. I got the tonkotsu chashu tsukemen ($18), which is dipping ramen style. The broth is sooo rich and the pork was HANDS DOWN the best I've ever had. The pork is so tender that I kinda struggle picking it up with my poor chopstick skills and whatever I manage to pick up literally just melts in my mouth. Their portion size is huge and they know it. They offer to put in a hot stone in your bowl of broth to reheat the broth halfway through your meal if you're a slow eater like me. We got Karaage ($8) for an appetizer which was also a winner. Super crispy and meat very tender. We also got a bottle of Mio sparkling sake ($18) which was splendidly fruity and bubbly (aka my kinda drink). We sat at the bar and service was super attentive. Definitely will be back!!

Title: Quick Refuel at Rosario's – Reliably Satisfying as Always

I recently found myself famished on the Lower East Side post-toy event, craving a bite before my next engagement. Familiar with Rosario's for its late-night offerings, I knew it was the perfect spot for a swift and satisfying meal. As expected, the quick stop was efficient: I opted for two cheese slices and a Sprite, skipping the salt for health reasons, but piling on garlic, hot pepper, regular pepper, and oregano for that extra flavor kick.

In the span of 15 minutes, I was refueled and ready to go, with the added bonus of charging my phone and catching up on emails thanks to an open WiFi signal – a small but appreciated convenience. While the temptation for a third slice was there, moderation won the day. Rosario's once again proved it's a dependable choice for good, quick food in the city. No doubt, I'll be back soon.

My friends and I came after seeing the lion king musical the other day. We originally came for sushi however there was a restaurant week offering going on so we swapped a little bit. I would have gone with sushi as planned but the prices of the sushi were ridiculous. I couldn't justify it. I understand we're in Times Square but I still don't care to spend 2x the price of sushi as I would anywhere else. But I did have sushi on the mind so I got salmon nigiri that I think was $11 for two pieces, normally that would be about $5-6 anywhere else. I've had better sushi so I don't think the price was justified. I also got one of the meals on the restaurant week menu. The peach and fig salad was awesome, I loved it. My meal was very tasty but needed pepper, it was gnocchi with veggies. I was too full to eat the dessert so I got it to go. It was chocolate cheesecake with some toppings. The cheesecake was a bit too dense for my liking. My one friend had a spicy tuna roll and miso soup. She loved her roll but didn't love the soup. My other friend got miso soup and I cannot recall what else. But he loved his meal I recall. Service was really slow but it was nice inside.

The Artichoke slice is pretty damn good when it's has time to set up properly and not be a soupy mess on top of a crisp, solid, crust. I never had an issue with the crust from here - I think they par bake them first so all the creamy sauce of the artichoke slice has a solid base.Because this place can get busy the slice I had was pretty liquidy, especially compared to the ones I tried from the Greenwich Village location that was setup pretty nice and can be eaten without dripping everywhere.Overall this place is a bit of a PITA.. long lines that usually stretch outside and limited seating when you do finally order. A good strategy, if you are more than 1 person, is have someone scout for a table or seats while the other waits on line (Flip a coin haha). I managed to find seats at the bar so I got off to a head start with their solid full bar.One thing I noticed was that there was a moldy smell by the bar. I happened to look up to check out the ceiling and it looked like it had dark spots indicating perhaps a water leak above it. The whole experience turned me off a bit, but it is a popular location near the High Line. If dealing with crowds for soupy pizza is your thing this Artichoke Basile location will fit the bill - who knows you might even get a properly baked slice!

Title: Salad Days Are Over at Just Salad

Let's be clear—just because Just Salad is around the corner doesn't mean it's worth the trip. Admittedly, my second visit was more out of MealPal necessity than desire, having already lost the memory of my first bland encounter. The restaurant itself is a typical NYC slice: long, narrow, and utterly devoid of charm. It's a place that takes its name too seriously, stripping away any semblance of enthusiasm along with its personality.

The staff, clearly uninspired, mirror the ambiance perfectly. But I was hopeful, enticed by an attractive MealPal profile for something called Spring Crunch. Alas, expectations were dashed. The reality of Spring Crunch was a far cry from its alluring digital facade. What I received was a dish as lackluster as the restaurant itself—dull, spiritless, and with an unexpected bitterness that lingered unpleasantly.

Not even the break in dreary weather could lift the gloom that settled after this disappointing rendezvous. Just Salad, it seems, is a misnomer. It's not "just" salad; it's just sad.

Title: A New York Gem – Mamma Mia!

I recently stumbled upon what has quickly become my go-to restaurant in New York City – Mamma Mia! The experience was nothing short of exceptional, making my dining visit an unforgettable one.

Upon entering, the classy aura is undeniable; from white-clothed tables to the elegant adornment of paintings, mirrors, and shimmering chandeliers, the ambiance sets a luxurious stage for the culinary delights that await.

The menu doesn't disappoint, with the highlight being the steak – hands down, the best I've ever savored. What you get is perfection on a plate: a delectably crispy exterior with a succulent and juicy interior. Alongside, the hashbrowns were a generous feast in themselves, amply serving up to four people.

To top off the meal, the Baked Alaska was not only a visual spectacle but a triumph in taste – a true masterpiece. The attentiveness and professionalism of the servers did not go unnoticed; they elevated the experience, ensuring every detail was catered to with utmost precision.

This dining experience was a solid five-star journey from start to finish. Mamma Mia! has won me over, and I'm already planning my next indulgence – even if it means spending every last dime. It's simply that irresistible.

Title: Convenient and Tasty Pizza with a Crisp Twist

I recently ventured into the world of mobile ordering with the Ritual app and decided to give the local pizzeria a try for lunch. True to its promised efficiency, my pizza was ready exactly on time. The quality of the pizza itself was more than satisfactory. The crust was exceptionally thin, reminiscent of a crispy cracker, which made for a unique texture that I enjoyed.

Opting for added meatballs and arugula proved to be a delicious choice. The small size turned out to be just right for a solo meal, hitting the spot without leaving leftovers. While I appreciated the broad selection of additional toppings, I did take note of the extra charge exceeding $1 for each, which could add up quickly for those desiring more variety on their pie.

The pizzeria was buzzing with the lunchtime crowd, indicating its popularity among local patrons. While the pizza was good and the quality high, I'm not inclined to make a special trip back. It's a solid option if you're in the area and in need of a quick, tasty bite.

3.5 stars overall.My girlfriend and I got together for an early bird dinner, around 5:30PM.  It was not busy as expected.  Both of us are fans of seafood - especially looking at the menu ahead of time, we spotted the scallops, calamari and steamers.  This is why we came.The dining area was well lit and gave off a fun seaside vibe.  Just missing the salt water smell. LOL The bright and sunny tablecovers (paper) and the sea themed decor - even decorative throw pillows; complete the look.  The staff was welcoming and friendly.  Our server Kevin G., was great.  Super friendly and informative as we had questions about some pricing (market price on the lobster).  Upon asking for our drink order, he mentioned to us that it was National Tequila Day...cool...so it did prompt us to take a second look at the cocktail menu.  I originally wanted to try the Lavender lemonade but they were out of lavender!  Sad.  We both ended up ordering the Mermaid Punch - light rum/coconut rum/Blue Curacao and Pineapple, it's as described.  Lovely color and tasted great.Onto the food:- started with the Fried Whole Clams (one dozen) to share...these were only ok.  Some pieces were definitely larger than others, likely the batter surrounding the meat.  Paired with a cocktail dipping sauce.  Served in a cool looking metal basket.  It got soggy quickly or perhaps not crispy enough to start with.- we also tried the soft shelled steamers which arrived hot and steamy - in a fun bucket presentation.  There were a few pieces that had sand but nothing the wash couldn't take care of.  Drawn better was good - not as rich as I'd hoped.  I did find it a little hard to serve the steamers with the spoon provided, perhaps tongs would be easier.  I didn't want to scoop any of the water.- Grilled scallops for my entree were good.  The grilling was just right as I like to taste my food not that char.  However, the side accompaniments and plating killed it for me. The Beluga lentils in the entree were too watery - too liquid.  It made my scallops wet and topped with the spinach which looked more steamed than sauteed.  What happened?  The colors were less than appetizing.  But the moisture ruined the whole plating.  As I picked up the lentils w/ my fork - it was a watery mess.  It should've been served in a bowl...separate from the scallops.  Sadly disappointing.- Fisherman's basket was my friends' entree.  Plating is everything!!  All of her seafood was mixed together, you couldn't tell the onion rings from the calamari and the fries were just dumped in as well.  Nothing pretty or organized.  This was way too casually plated - but if you wanted to go that route, then use the paper containers to match the table covers.  Not these metal plates/bowls.The whole evening was less than appetizing based on the plating but worst yet...the fruit flies.  There were a few flying around us as we were eating.  Very uncomfortable and not what we should see while eating.  So sorry Kevin, even your attentive serving skills could not save this review.  Had high hopes for this place but fell flat for me.  I do not plan on making a return visit.  Management has got to fix the plating and the fruit flies.

Love this place!! We went in party of two and was able to get seats by the bar immediately. We ordered the combo (1 lb grilled lobster + burger) and an original lobster dinner (1 1/2 lb steamed lobster). Both come with lemon and garlic butter, fries and salad. It was a great meal. Everything was so yummy. Love the brioche bun for the burger. They also cut the lobster in half and claws for you so it's easy to eat.  Service was quick and satisfying. Great location too - right next to time sq close to the theaters. Reasonable price. Will def come back again!

Food was remarkably good.  Pork sliders very tasty,  pork tacos good and calamari was tasty.  Service was attentive.  Good neighborhood pub.  Our margarita drinks were excellent.  Good location.  Was clean.

Title: A Culinary Gem That Lives Up to the Hype

My recent visit to this much-praised eatery not only lived up to its lofty reputation, but exceeded it. The restaurant itself marries a charming ambiance with a flair for innovatively reimagined classics. For starters, do not miss the soft scrambled eggs with escargot—an unmissable combination of earthy tones and rich flavors. Complementing the beginning of our meal, the oysters were fresh, and the gnocchi was a delightful lead into the main course.

Choosing the Bavette au poivre was a decision well made, as it was executed to perfection. With each bite, the anticipation of returning to explore more of the menu grows. This restaurant is a standout that promises and delivers an exceptional dining experience.

Good vibes . We got the colorful shots  and fried Oreos . It came with free games which was a plus . It wasn't too crowded which was another plus. The "shots" were weak and premixed but fun . Can become pricey FAST so be mindful lol . would come back again.

Truly an amazing and inventive restaurant. Loved the pre-theater menu where you get to pick any 2 courses and 1 accompaniment. I chose the tandoori lamb chops, the beef tenderloin, and the butter chicken kulcha. Everything had so much flavor and was really delicious. The service was excellent too. Be aware it is pretty pricey. Probably more of a place for a special occasion.

Title: A Delightful Culinary Experience at Ai Fiori

I recently visited Ai Fiori for a lunch date, and while the company may have been less than impressive, the culinary experience was quite the opposite. With a 2-course lunch priced at $49, it offers a somewhat indulgent experience without causing too much of a dent in your wallet.

Starting with the Vellutata, or lobster bisque, the dish was a creamy delight when paired with the provided bread. We also enjoyed a well-crafted pasta dish, perfectly al dente, in a luscious buttery mushroom sauce. Each starter was a testament to the kitchen's proficiency.

The main course presented a mixed bag. I had the Trofie Nero, an excellent choice with succulent pieces of scallop and a delightful crustacean ragu that elevated the dish. However, the Capesante, chosen by my date, suffered from an overload of salt in the scallops, enough to warrant feedback to our attentive server who graciously compensated with an extra dessert.

Speaking of which, the desserts were standout. The Paris-Brest was a revelation with its luscious hazelnut cream—a dessert I'd happily indulge in regularly. The complimentary tartaletta, provided due to the earlier mishap, was a refreshing fruity contrast and equally enjoyable.

Overall, despite the slight hiccup with the main course, Ai Fiori impressed with its culinary finesse. It's a place I'd recommend, but with a tip: consult with the server about their personal favorites to help guide your choices.

My husband and I stumbled upon this quaint little gem while in the area and decided to stop for dinner. We indulged in the fried chicken, which was perfectly crispy and juicy. The tan tan ramen, with its spicy sesame oil, packed a delightful punch, while the hakata ramen's rich pork bone broth was comfort in a bowl. Everything we ordered was superb, making our impromptu visit a memorable dining experience.
Patsy's is a decent Italian spot. If you are looking for New York pizza however I don't really recommend this place, the Pizza is more restaurant style. The chicken carbonara is excellent.

Title: A Mixed Experience at a Trendy SoHo Eatery

My excursion to this SoHo spot was driven by the allure of their Happy Hour promises, particularly the talked-about $5 soup dumplings. However, upon arrival, I discovered prices had seen a slight increase, dashing my hopes for the famed deal. I decided on the pork soup dumplings and a $6 pale ale from their rotating beer menu.

Let's start with the positives: the venue itself is a feast for the eyes, exuding upscale charm in every corner, evidenced by delightful details like chopstick rests made from LEGOs. The bartender was a beacon of friendliness and made the bar seating experience pleasant.

Now for the food: Those craving authentic soup dumplings might prefer a visit to Chinatown over this establishment. While the dumplings arrived in a cloud of steam, they cooled to a mere warmth within a minute, presenting an underwhelming soup-to-dumpling ratio that was more dough than broth. Although not unpalatable, they were unremarkably greasy and could have benefited from more flavorful soup.

A small hiccup occurred when requesting a spoon for vinegar; confusion ensued, suggesting a potential gap in the bartending staff's familiarity with traditional dumpling accompaniments.

In summary, if you're after small-batch brews and aesthetically pleasing surroundings, this place might hit the mark. But if it's soup dumplings you're craving, set your sights on Chinatown for a more satisfying experience.

I'm extremely grateful that SUGARFISH has remained open throughout the pandemic. The fish is consistently fresh and the packaging is impeccable, enhancing the overall dining experience even when it's takeout.

Tucked away in a prime spot, this charming restaurant offers an unexpectedly roomy interior perfect for post-dinner indulgences. The staff welcomes you with open arms, and the dessert menu is a dream come true for those with a sweet tooth. The standout choices, like the luscious Golden Toast, decadent Chestnut Butterscotch, and playful Cookie Camp, make it hard to pick just one. Given that each dessert is a sweet, rich delight, sharing is the best strategy, especially since the portions are generous. While prices lean towards the higher end, the quality and size justify the cost. It's a definite recommendation for anyone looking to treat themselves.

I recently dined at a local ramen spot hoping for a savory treat but found the experience rather underwhelming. The main attraction, the ramen, priced reasonably at $14, didn't deliver the bold flavors I craved and tipped the scales towards being overly salty. Accompanying the lackluster ramen, the chicken karage—three pieces for $3—was disappointingly flavorless. Additionally, the absence of complimentary water was a letdown. If you're in a bind for a quick noodle slurp, this place might do, but it certainly wouldn't top my list of go-to ramen joints.
Delicious dessert spot! Famous! Lots of matcha options. All are super creative elegantly decorated and presented dessert items. I loved the flavors and the lava cake in particular.

I showed up with a large group -- we all had a wonderful time!  Soon after we were seated, I ordered a bottle of Bruno Giacosa Roero Arneis, which was listed at $45 on the menu and seems to retail for around $25 in stores.  The wine is excellent; we went through two bottles of this white and also drank an Italian red that someone else ordered.  (I think it was a Dolcetto d'Alba.)  My dinner consisted of the tuna tartare special and a pasta special made with rock shrimp and ramps.  I was very happy with both dishes and ordered an affogato for dessert.My one reservation about our experience is that the personnel were not maximally attentive.  For example, it took quite a while before anyone came to our table to ask for drink orders.I definitely recommend Novita if you're in the neighborhood.

I really like this place. Such chill ambience and the indoor seems so modern and contemporary! The place is connected to a hotel and apparently there's a rooftop there as well!! One star off for MIA server towards the end of our meal and overly salty salad. The food was good overall. I particularly liked the chips with the guac and green salsa, the smokey pina colada and the ribs (green salsa with ribs= the best!!!). However, the sauce for the shrimp salad was really salty for me, but the shrimps were cooked so nicely that overall the dish was still tolerable; although I had to eat them with chips to cut the salt flavor. The tacos were decent with good flavors. The ribs though, were ridiculous. Just the right amount of fat, seasoning and tenderness. They also served them with the delicious green salsa... yummm...Probably one of the better ribs I've had in awhile; and I'm picky with ribs and red meat in general since I was so spoiled in the Midwest and the south. My pina colada was creamy, not too sweet, semi strong, Smokey and yummy! Overall, would come back again when I'm craving Mexican food!

Title: A Must-Try Ramen Haven in NYC

If you find yourself hankering for top-notch ramen in NYC, look no further. This bustling spot not only serves some of the best ramen in the city but also promises an experience worth the wait. With a lively front bar, you can easily pass the time with a drink in hand before diving into your bowl of noodle goodness.

As you step through the door, a chorus of "welcome" in Japanese sets the stage for an authentic dining journey. The staff are exceptional—friendly, attentive, and always ready to demystify the menu for curious food-lovers. While the prices are a tad steep, the top-quality ramen and vibrant atmosphere make it a splurge that's absolutely justified. Don't miss out on this culinary staple when you're in NYC.

I came here after seeing instagram posts of their rainbow ramen. However, I wasn't planning on getting the rainbow ramen because I just wanted to get a hearty bowl of warm ramen to fill my belly on a cold winter day.Upon walking in, there were not that many people and we seated ourselves. I decided to get the mayu-ramen. While waiting, they have a jug of tea at the counter for you to self-serve.The wait was a bit long for a restaurant so empty but it's okay since I wasn't in a rush. The ramen itself was al dente and cooked nicely but the soup was too salty for my taste. After eating 3/4th of the bowl, I didn't care to finish because of how salty it was. The egg and chasu were pretty good. Would I order it again though? Nope.When we were leaving, we checked-in on yelp for free gelato and it was probably the highlight of the meal. I got the peach gelato and it was really good. The lady, I'm guessing the owner, was really sweet and allowed us to try different flavors before choosing. She also filled up the cups to the top even though it's free!Maybe I'll be back to try other ramens and to get their gelato, but I can definitely find better ramens at the same price point around NYC.

Title: A Spirited Evening at the Local Beer Hall

Last night at 9 PM, I joined friends for a birthday celebration at a sprawling indoor beer hall, complete with colossal screens broadcasting sports and a live DJ spinning tracks. The beer offerings, available in small to large sizes, kicked off with a Lavender Wheat for me. Although an intriguing take on the classic Belgian Wit, it unfortunately fell flat, tasting somewhat diluted. I swiftly pivoted to the Golden Lager, which proved to be a far superior choice with its full-bodied flavor, and it remained my companion for the night.

On to the fare, which came with a steeper price tag. The beef sliders, contrary to expectations, were delectably juicy and cooked just right—a standout dish. The grilled shrimp skewers delivered on taste despite an unusual seasoning blend, while the grilled cheese stack hit the spot perfectly during late-night cravings.

As the evening wore on, the venue became increasingly crowded, typical for weekend nights post-10 PM. A significant drawback was the bathroom situation: only two facilities to accommodate the masses, which can be quite the predicament after a few rounds of beer. Despite the restroom snag, the lively atmosphere and tasty bites made for an enjoyable outing.

**Review of [Restaurant Name]: A Missed Opportunity with a Side of Glorious Fries**

Entering [Restaurant Name], the expectation was set high – a beautiful spot reputed for one of New York's best burgers, thanks to Chef Masa's "iron maiden" technique. Despite a promising start with a ready table and enjoyable bar snacks, the establishment fell just shy of wowing us.

The space is a treat, roomy and airy – a rare find in the city. We dove straight into a Monday special, pairing burgers with beer and tetsu fries for a tempting $25. The Pollinator cocktail, although a pretty hue-shifter, was underwhelming, tasting more like tart lemonade with the chrysanthemum essence lost in the background.

The Duck Tacos left our discerning palates unsatisfied - the duck was unexpectedly dry and the pineapple hoisin sauce lacked its promised punch. Foie gras became the savior of the dish but at a premium price, we expected better. The Octopus special, although a decent toast topper, couldn't live up to the "sizzling" expectations synonymous with Asian cuisine.

Burger-wise, the Lamb with Taleggio was a standout, juicy and perfectly paired with the cheese. The Beef with White Cheddar was satisfying yet forgettable, and the VIP Burger, though an interesting mix of caviar and truffle, couldn't justify its luxuriousness against its cost.

However, the Tetsu Fries were the undeniable star – a crispy, rosemary-scented delight studded with succulent bacon that merits a return visit.

In the end, while [Restaurant Name] is a lovely spot for drinks and perhaps fries, it might not make the cut for a serious foodie's bucket list, especially considering the price point. It’s an agreeable venue to unwind with friends, but it doesn't quite achieve culinary greatness.

Title: A NYC Gem Offering Exceptional Service and Cuisine

From the moment we entered, it was clear this was no ordinary dining experience. The bustling, fun location of this spacious NYC restaurant set the stage for an exceptional evening. Promptly seated, we were enveloped by the inviting atmosphere.

The service was nothing short of amazing, attentive without being intrusive, ensuring a smooth and pleasant dining experience. Turning to the menu, we were impressed by the extensive variety, offering something to tantalize every palate. Although prices skewed higher, the quality of the food justified every penny. Each dish was executed with a level of excellence that matched the exemplary service.

In summary, this restaurant is a vibrant spot for food enthusiasts seeking top-notch service and delectable cuisine. It's an investment in a culinary delight that's absolutely worth it.

At this no-frills spot, the modest offering consisting of rice, cabbage, your choice of meat, topped with a ladle of delectable meat marinade, provides a surprisingly satisfying meal for just $4.75—a price that had me in disbelief. An upgrade to a large portion costs a mere $6-$6.50, and indulging in a second type of meat barely breaks the bank at $7. While occasionally, the meat can be a bit fatty or chewy, it's a minor quibble given the unbeatable value. The service is efficient, too; even with a line, you can expect to be tucking into your meal within 5-10 minutes. For a quick, delicious, and incredibly affordable meal, this is the place to go.

Title: A Flavorful Foray at Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken

Last visit to New York, I finally satisfied my curiosity about Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken, a spot buzzing with the chicken sandwich craze. I aimed to divert from the commonplace and ordered the Tenders Supreme - a 3 piece meal with a side of fries, accompanied by a nostalgically sweet Boylan soda.

The menu was an inviting spread from classic chicken cuts to eclectic options like hush puppies and loaded fries. While the tenders were satisfyingly crisp, they lacked an adventurous zest - a void filled once I plunged them into the zingy Wasabi Honey sauce. The range of sauces, especially the untried Habanero Hot Sauce, hinted at a missed opportunity for heat.

In conclusion, Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken stands out in New York's culinary landscape. Don't miss out on dousing your meal with their array of distinctive sauces for an extra kick. Worth a visit!

I'll admit I was hesitant to try this place out due to the reviews but I'm glad we ended up going. All of the staff was very nice the host, bartender, server and character impersonator were so friendly so props for good service all around. I saw a lot of reviews about people being disappointed that it's so small and it is a small space but 70 percent of the bars/restaurants are like that in NY so it's not out of the ordinary. If you're coming for dinner I'd definitely make a reservation, the dinner is prefixed but there's several options to choose from which is nice. I opted for the Mac and cheese for my app and a steak for my entree. The Mac and cheese was good, very rich and creamy I wouldn't recommend it as a entree as the appetizer portion is just enough. The steak was good but not great, it lacked a bit of flavor.. The risotto was very tasty as were the cocktails. Overall it was a good experience!

Title: A Ramen Gem Amidst Tourist Traps – Totto Ramen Review

Navigating the culinary minefield of this tourist-heavy area often leads to disappointment. However, Totto Ramen emerges as a delightful outlier. Despite its diminutive size and potential for long queues, my Saturday evening experience was marked by swift service, managing to secure a table without a lengthy wait.

Initiating the meal with the can't-fail pork bun set a high bar, followed by a specialty Ramen whose name escapes me but whose flavors linger on. The Ramen struck a fine balance - savory without the all-too-common over-salting. Generous meat portions added substance to the dish, and I'd argue that adding an egg is essential for the full Ramen experience.

Totto Ramen hasn't quite dethroned Ippudo from my top spot, but it's a close contender, making it a must-visit for any Ramen aficionado in the area.

Had to try this place after seeing a video about it online, and it was pretty good! We got the ash rehshteh noodle soup, and it was super tasty and unique. It was warm and herbacious, perfect for a cold January day. We got the medium which was perfect for sharing, and a great value for the price. Staff was also super friendly and helpful as well. Overall, definitely worth a try!
Amazing, fun bar in Morningside. Doors completely open to the street with a dynamite Happy Hour.Games, Juke Box and great staff. A gorgeous day makes this a win win... Who doesn't love Jumbo Jenga ‼

A friend took me here for drinks after work... happy hour. Didn't know what yo expect so I went in with an unassuming slate.So these frozen magaritas were da bomb! There were different flavors, but the original is always best.We sat by the windows since we were only there for drinks. Needless to say on a Friday the place was packed. The music was great and the ambiance, mood, atmosphere had my feet tapping. I will be back to try the food though. Saw some of well presented plates coming out. Definitely returning to try out a few.

Title: A Thai Gem Worthy of the Stars

Last week, I visited Sabai Thai and was immediately struck by its inviting atmosphere. Perfectly balanced lighting and tasteful decor create an environment suitable for various occasions, from a casual catch-up to a formal work dinner.

The service at Sabai Thai is remarkable, with attentive staff that anticipate needs without being intrusive. As a vegetarian, I appreciated the diverse veggie and tofu options. My veggie spring rolls were delightful, and the staff ensured I had enough sauce without me having to ask – a small but thoughtful gesture.

For anyone on a budget, their happy hour specials are a steal. And let’s talk about the food – simply yummy! The pad prik king, in particular, left a lasting impression. I've been craving it ever since.

Without a doubt, Sabai Thai earns a solid 5-star rating from me. I’m already planning my next visit!

Not sure I can say anything about this place that hasn't already been said! It's the original Mamoun's, so most likely the best of them. That being said, I haven't tried any of the others because this place is so good! The falafel has none of the dryness of what you might experience in an average falafel, and the hummus is incredible. And it is just unbelievably cheap. The only average thing I've tried from this place is the dolmas, which were good but not standout.
I ordered a few dishes from UBS.. but I found 1.5inch long insect leg in my phat see ew... definitely not a pleasant experience. do not order from this place!!!!!

I don't get why the three star rating, I honestly can say that I had a pretty darn good time here earlier today. Either that or I was still coming off the high from the anesthesia from the procedure I had beforehand. I was surprised myself of how good of a time I ended up having here and everything just seemed right. The rainy weather, the awesome tunes that played in the background, the great timing that it wasn't overloaded with people, the chill/vintage vibe of this place, and perhaps most important the location. As it's right on the corner and it was windy and raining outside and we did not want to waste time looking for a place to eat. We tried two other places in the area recently (Jacob's Pickles and the BBQ/burger place I forgot the name) and it seems both are overrated and overpriced. So the UNO turned out to be not only the best deal moneywise but just overall on point regarding pretty much everything. I would definitely come back here for sure. And I can't say enough good things about our waitress. She was the true definition of what a waiter should be. Upbeat, friendly, with a smile, energetic, you name it. I rarely get excited about waiters so take my word for it when I tell you she's great. If there were Waiter Awards she would win hands down.

Upon entering the establishment, I was greeted by beautifully bright décor that immediately signaled a photogenic experience. The attention to aesthetic detail was exemplified in the matcha taro latte, which not only tasted delightful but looked divine in its presentation. Accompanying this was a waffle, adorned with delicate flowers, bringing a level of whimsy to the plate. The waffle itself was light and fluffy, a testament to the kitchen's prowess.

However, it's worth noting that the pricing seemed a tad steep. While the food was enjoyable, it became evident that part of the cost is attributed to the ambiance, which, while moderately lush with roses and appealing touches, may not fully justify the premium. For those looking to splurge a little for a picturesque dining scene, this spot hits the mark, but value-seekers might find the cost hard to reconcile with their culinary experience.

I really thought I was gonna see burly men in beards drinking from kegs and clinking beer mugs in this UWS beer hall. TOTAL opposite! Gerbhard's has an edgy, eclectic and cool crowd. A few steps heading down from street level, entrance on left, then the place comes off three ways: you're in a basement, I just walked into 1981's 'American Werewolf In London' pub and you just stepped back in time to the Middle Ages- all into one. Low ceilings, lots of high tops- plus the Bar area has these funky red lightbulbs bouncing back at their drinking glass rack- I don't know if this is a nostalgia kick for me but I was digging it. Never the beer drinker, hubs though wanted to get his on. I don't know what reigns supreme here in terms of food, but I did a once over at the menu and noticed a few bites I could eat. Menu seems well-rounded with something for carnivores, Pescatarians, Vegans and Vegetarians. Music was an 80s American and British pop mashup with Soft Cell's 'Tainted Love', Blondie, Duran Duran, etc on the playlist. You place food and beer orders at the Bar and then it's brought to you. Bartenders were knowledgeable and well-versed in the beer list when hubs was unsure of a few- plus they also have a beer rundown on the chalkboard.My Vegan Mushroom Tacos with Tofu 'aioli' were delicious plus their ginormous pretzel was warm chewy good. This spot has a nice crowd going- I mean...it was practically filled to capacity. Service was good and honestly I don't mind coming back for the nice menu...while hubs enjoys his beer.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise with Seafood Delights in NYC

During our weekend escapade to NYC, we discovered a gem of a restaurant that swayed my usual aversion to raw oysters. The 5 blue point oysters we ordered were a revelation, exhibiting unparalleled freshness that tantalized our taste buds. To complement the seafood starters, we indulged in the Manhattan clam chowder, which was an absolute delight, hitting the spot with its light yet satisfying character—a perfect choice given that it left us ample room for pizza later in the evening. This restaurant is a must-visit spot for anyone looking to unwind with some exquisite bites before continuing with their city adventures.

Really wanted to like this place but was disappointed in the end.  Waited an hour after arriving at 6pm on a Sunday.  Other people had the same idea, to show up early.  Come here later at like 7 or so and there would be no wait. Did not get to hear the specials that later tables got. Ordered the spring rolls and 2 beef phos, one with added tendon terrine and oxtail.  The spring rolls were oddly greasy but the flavor was okay.  Pho broth was light and mild, lacking the intensity and richness available in other versions around the city.   This is not necessarily bad, as evidenced by NY's desires for different ramen broth. The obvious failing was the temperature of the broth, as it proved insufficient to cook through the few slices of raw beef.  This was a complaint I heard from a neighboring table as well so this was not an isolated incident, occurring (perhaps more understandably) in the bowl loaded with terrine and oxtail as well as the basic bowl.  The oxtail was half fat but the edible meat was fine.  The terrine was a good concept, but it disintegrated in the lukewarm broth, further lowering the temperature and leaving me to fish for the tendon and meat chunks.  I'm a degenerate carnivore but I had to leave a few slices of undercooked beef in the bowl. The ingredients are good but there were a few miscues.  I'd come back to give them another chance, but only if I could avoid the wait.

I recently visited Calle Dao for a boozy brunch and had a delightful experience. While the service was on the slower side, our server Roxy truly made up for it. She was exceptionally accommodating, ensuring our group was well taken care of, especially with our drink needs. Her efforts guaranteed we all had a great time. Thanks to Roxy's outstanding service, I'm giving Calle Dao a well-deserved 4-star rating.

Came here for the second time today.  It's a pretty big space so we were seated immediately around prime brunch time (1pm Saturday). I ordered a bloody mary which was just ok and my boyfriend got a mimosa.  For entrees, the hangover sandwich & a burger. My sandwich was BEC meets BLT + avocado, onion and a creamy chipotle sauce and it was amazing. My boyfriend also swears (for the second time) that this is the best burger he's ever eaten. He customized it with mushrooms, jalapeños and cheese and he was super happy with it.  I was happy to see that they had a sour beer option so I got the du claw strawberry sour which I enjoyed as well.  Overall another good experience and we will continue to return.
We came here as a stop on our food tour and sampled the meatballs. The were very tasty and huge. Cute little place and we will be back to sample the pasta too.

We came early (4 PM) on a Saturday night. This was a good idea because by 5 it we jammed packed and  the noise level increased 10 fold. We ordered the mixed grill for two which was delicious.  As side orders, we ordered the horiatiki salad, kolokithiakeftedes (zucchini meat balls) and a pork souvlaki. Our bill totaled $72 which I thought was on the high side but worth it if you consider the location and atmosphere.  The Greek music played in the background and it reminded me of Greece. It wasn't so loud that you couldn't hold a conversation.Our granddaughter was with us and they had good accommodations for infants. That was something that we appreciated. The service was good. I would definitely come back the next time we are in Manhattan.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a Korean restaurant that left a lasting impression on my palate. We ordered the stir-fried pork and vegetables, which was a delightful mix of savory flavors, and the comforting chicken bone soup. A sprinkle of salt, as recommended, enhanced the soup beautifully. The highlight was undoubtedly the variety of banchan - each dish, from the macaroni salad to the dried seaweed and fish cakes, complemented the main courses exquisitely. The kimchi, in particular, was a standout with its perfect balance of spice and tang. I am already looking forward to my next visit!

Places like this is why I love the west village- Came here on the weekend and it wasn't too packed- Quiet, romantic, rustic feel- Wooden ceilings, wooden chairs, tiled counters, hanging lights- Love the fairy lights outside- We sat by the windows facing outwards and it was so relaxing- Be careful of the candle in front of you. Ours caught on fire and a waiter had to come take care of it lol- The food was great! The lamb was super tender and tasty- I suggest ordering a couple of dishes to share. That way you get a taste of everything- The gimlet was a little bitter but the bartender added more syrup and then it got better- We decided on the tiramisu for dessert and it was heavenly- Don't quite understand the poor ratings since we had a great time- They have long tables in the center so it's good for large groups too- Definitely coming back
Great rich Japanese curry and pork or chicken katsu. Brought me back to when I was in Japan

Title: Island Vibes in the City at [Tiki Bar Name]

If you're a fan of the Jacob's Pickles crew, their tiki bar is a treasure chest waiting to be unlocked. My excitement was palpable, and yet they did not disappoint. By 6:30 PM on a bustling Friday evening, the place was already alive with energy. It seemed luck was on our side as my group of five nestled into a cozy arrangement of table, couch, and chairs tucked away in the back.

The cocktail menu was an invitation for adventure. Among the libations I embarked on were the Bookworm, Frozen Piña Colada, Saturn, Shark Snacks, Zombie, and a mysterious frozen pickle concoction whose name escaped me. The Piña Colada was a tropical dream and took the lead, with the Saturn coming in as a close celestial second. For those craving a potent potion, the Zombie won’t disappoint; it was a boozy journey to the afterlife.

The culinary delights came in the form of "mini" sandwiches that defied their stature with bold flavors and generous portions. The Hot Honey Chicken, Stiki Tiki, and the standout Pink Wave were all worth savoring, and at $5 a pop, these wonders are a steal I'm sure won't last forever.

The ambiance was topped off with a welcoming lei at the door, and wallet-friendly prices, notably the $14 frozen drinks. My only gripe would be the volume of the music; a tad lower would complement the intimate atmosphere better.

In all, this tiki haven garners a well-deserved 4.5 stars. Hoping they'll expand the menu with sides like fries, I recommend you drop anchor here before the secret's out and the prices sail away.

Oysters plus cocktails on a boat? Say less! I love this gem of a restaurant- rain or shine! (I've been here twice, once during a thunderstorm scare!) But I didn't leave I had to wait for the r. The staff is amazing, esp. my friend Kev. Starting from the drinks to the food, I was pleased with all of it. The fries, the ceviche, the caviar service, the fresh oysters... my fav is the Navy Point. Don't forget the Lobster Mac n Cheese! I couldn't stop eating it. Super delicious and clean. You'll even feel the waves at times, esp if you're watching the sunset ;)

Title: An Unexpected Gem in the East Village

I stumbled upon a hidden treasure in the East Village, a Russian café that's somehow eluded my radar despite my affinity for the neighborhood's nightlife and my love for Russian cuisine and libations. It was a serendipitous discovery after seeking a place for a nightcap with friends.

We hadn't planned to eat, so I can't speak to the culinary offerings, but the menu boasted an enticing mix of classics like crepes, pelmeni, stroganoff, and caviar, all at reasonable mid-range prices. Initially, there was an insistence on ordering at the bar unless dining, but thanks to my friend's persuasive Russian skills, we secured a cozy booth.

It seems we weren't the only ones there for the drinks; surrounding booths were filled with patrons sipping on well-crafted martinis. The drink prices matched the food: fair for the East Village. No sign of a happy hour, but the place doesn't strike you as one that would need it. Instead, they offer a selection of intriguing vodka infusions. While they couldn't top the Russian Vodka Room's offerings, the Honey Ginger and, surprisingly, the Horseradish infusions were memorable—though the latter carried a less pleasant reminder the following day.

The true highlight was the live music, an unanticipated delight that transformed the space. When a band broke into "Gonna Have Some Fun Tonight on the Bayou," the café erupted in genuine, joyful dancing.

In a nutshell, this Russian café is more than just a spot for a stiff drink; it's a venue for unexpected joy. I'm already planning my next visit for when the mood strikes for offbeat charm and a good dance.

We went on a Saturday night as a group of 10, and we didn't have any issue getting a spot. We started with the mixed platter that came with a variety of different sauces, grape lives, braised artichoke hearts, and bread. This was good to share among our group. We also got calamari, which they didn't give us very much of. We split a bottle of Turkish red wine, which was very good. For the main meal we split two of the meat platters, which allowed us to try all of everything. The meat was a little overcooked, but my favorite was definitely the lamb. Food was okay, but I probably wouldn't come here again.

Tucked away in the bustling food court, this eatery offers a no-frills dining experience that's easy on the wallet. Speed is the name of the game here; they serve up meals with impressive hastiness, ensuring you're not left waiting when hunger strikes. The culinary fare won't be topping any best-of lists, but it delivers a satisfying punch of flavor to silence midday cravings. The lamb noodle soup stands out as a commendable choice, hitting the mark of being decently delicious. Beverage-wise, expect to find a slightly more interesting range than your typical food court fare. Overall, it's a spot to appreciate for its straightforward, quick, and tasty-enough offerings.

Prince Street Pizza has become a SoHo waystation for tourists and locals seeking pizza. Prince Street Pizza is a small SoHo neighborhood spot that attracts crowds. pretty narrow space. Celebrities' pics adorn the wall. old-school gritty feel. the menu is over the order counter. there are ledge tables on each side of the pizzeria that you can stand at and eat -- no seating. About 8-10 people can stand and eat. during warmer weather, eat outside of PSP or at the various nearby public parks in SoHo. the pizza? good and satisfying. I am a fan of the square slice topped with the crispy cupped ppepperoni. crunchy pepperoni, layer of mozzarella, spicy tomato sauce, and a thick crust make for a satisfying mix of cheese, meat, sauce, and carbs. the slice can be messy, so grab napkins from the counter before you start. i'll be honest  one slice is pretty filling. would I wait 30-45 minutes for a slice? nah, that's strictly for dopey tourists and local dopes. if there's a huge line, come back when it's thinned down. also, during terrible weather and middle of the afternoon and early evenings weekdays have less people on line than weekends or lunchtime on any day.staff is fast and keeps the line moving. i wish they would go back to strictly cash. the debit/credit swiping slows the line down. seriously, who doesn't carry enough cash to buy one or two slices?!! lol also PEOPLE know what you're ordering before you get to the counter! lolPrince Street Pizza is definitely worth a stop if you're in the area and the line is not that deep. drops mic cuz pizza is lifei outzzz

Came here to grab some slices for the SO back in Cali.  Tried out some fresh slices while at the location.It's definitely got the old-school pizzeria feel.  Not a fancy place but the food is on-point.I had a cheese pizza there (which was very good) and fresh from the oven.  Got 3 slices of pepperoni to go and my friend got the mushroom pizza (which was loaded with mushrooms).You can fold it perfectly, which is how you test out the NY Pizza.  It was not over greasy at all.Would definitely be back for more next time I'm in town!

I didn't expect something so good in Harlem!! If you look around standing in front of Fieldtrip, many of the restaurants on the same street are fast food, so this got me really excited to try out Fieldtrip! As an Asian, rice is always a staple in our meals, and for a restaurant that basically developed their menu around different kinds of rice, that pretty much means that they really care about what they serve, and they also know a good deal about it.To be honest, everything I tried surprised me!! The crispy chicken bowl was good, and there's also a good amount of veggies in it!! The crab pockets were so crispy and generously filled with crab mixture, and most importantly it wasn't greasy at all!! I didn't expect to be so full after eating my meal - it's a really good portion!! The drinks are also good. The dragonfruit lemonade was really special, and it's not too sweet!I decided that I also want to try the vegan ice cream although I was so full, and it was interesting!! It tasted very refreshing and you don't feel guilty at all!!If I'm in the area next time, I would definitely come back to try out other bowls!!

Drinks were great, food was decent, they only have one flavor for hookah (mint), the music is great, the bathroom is cute and clean. Having said all of that, it's definitely a hookah spot so be ready for that. I'm not exactly hooked on hookah (**smirk**) so I was not a fan of the poor air circulation--especially at the VIP area. However, this place is so nice that a wedding party came in to continue their celebration with some hookah here. It's very close to the subway and in a very central location for the area.Service was pretty fast, efficient and friendly.  Y es mejor si hablas español.  No complaints here. If you're in the area, check it out. Good for a large group or an intimate date!

During my recent dining experience at the restaurant, I found the food to be delicious albeit on the pricier side. The staff made commendable recommendations, with the Salmon Osaka standing out as a particular favorite. The Orchard Roll also proved to be an enjoyable choice, offering a fun twist to the meal.

However, a notable downside was the uniformity of the sauce across all three dishes, which created a redundant taste profile and detracted from the individual flavors I had hoped to enjoy.

Service-wise, the staff was amicable and welcoming, yet the speed of service did not match the low occupancy, as there were hardly any crowds. Despite just 3-4 groups present, the preparation of our meals was unexpectedly slow. Overall, while the food quality was high, the pacing of the meal and lack of variety in sauces left room for improvement.

Awesome Korean place. Only had one 1/2 small dishes from here, so I can't give a complete review of this place, but from what I experienced, it tasted good. A8 is not bad. A12 is super good. Highly recommend. My friend had a Jeju Island cocktail and he said it wasn't bad, more of a sweet taste. Service was exceptional. Very kind staff, constantly refilling waters and stepping aside for customers. Politeness was through the roof.

Came here with coworkers for happy hour deals (frozen margaritas, cold pressed juice margaritas, tacos, chips and guacamole, etc.) Not too busy around 5PM but definitely picks up around 6PM. Happy hour menu is surprisingly extensive and reasonably priced, especially for midtown. Restaurant is very casual, food I'd say is fast casual. There is a little bit of seating and a small bar area. Tacos were yummy and a good size for happy hour prices. Guac you can add toppings to it or get it plain. We added pepitas and pomegranate seeds that was a surprisingly good combo (there are other topping options). The ambiance is less like an actual bar and more like a casual lunch/dinner spot with a happy hour menu. Still good happy hour option, nice decor, and nice wait staff.

Having stumbled upon this pizza gem, I must say, I've become a regular. With a menu bursting with variety, this place surpassed all expectations. The pepperoni pizza I ordered was not only a generous portion but also deliciously satisfying, easily catapulting this eatery to the top of my favorites list.

The prices are remarkably reasonable for the quality and size of the meal provided. Coupled with swift service akin to fast food joints, this establishment excels in delivering a fantastic dining experience.

Don't be fooled by any snapshots you see; the food is far more amazing in person. Without a doubt, I'll be returning for another round of exceptional pizza.

I've frequented this place many of times. Great date spot, great for a cold day, great for pretty much everything. This is my favorite ramen spot to date! Kinda wish I included a pic of my ramen but devoured it. Always expect a wait; in fact, I've never been there when there wasn't a wait (a telling sign). The line moves fast, eat at the bar if you can!

Smith & Wollensky has been a favorite of mine for years; I've tried most of their menu, including some off the menu secret dishes, and I'm yet to be disappointed. Pictured is their Cajun Style Rib Eye which is jam packed with flavor and cooked to perfection.

Title: A Saturday Afternoon Delight at an Outstanding Restaurant

My recent visit to this restaurant was nothing short of exceptional. Its prime location is complemented by a delightful ambience that sets the stage for a remarkable dining experience. Our decision to reserve online proved wise, avoiding any wait time and being greeted by a very cordial hostess.

Service was swift and impeccable, perfect for our afternoon dedicated to indulging in their renowned drink selection. The drinks passport is impressively extensive, especially the array of tequilas and margarita flavors. Although we missed out on the famous Margarita Tower due to our party size, the pitcher we shared was fantastic. The Coconut Margarita, rated at 4 out of 5, was enjoyable, though a pinch more coconut flavor would enhance it. However, the tequila shot was a solid 5 out of 5, with the wide selection including favorites like Casa Amigos and Patron.

Don't even get me started on the appetizers—the Guacamole is a perfect 10, a must-try. The Mexican Style Nachos did not disappoint either, full of amazing flavor. I was also impressed by the stunning decor and appreciated the cleanliness of the bathrooms.

In conclusion, I can't recommend this restaurant enough. Whether it's for the drinks, food, or atmosphere, it's a place you'll want to visit time and time again.

This is it. This is the place with the most amazing ramen ever. We were trudging around NYC and checking out Yelp reviews to find some lunch. The reviews are right! Top to bottom excellence. We had the ribs, some buns, and ramen. With so much competition around, it's hard to say something is the best, but trust me, you won't be disappointed!

There's a reason why it's so hard to get a reservation for this place. It's tiny, pasta sauce was amazing. But I can only give this place three stars. I ordered Linguine all' Astice. Noodles were mixed very well with tomato sauce, but the lobster was not the best I've ever had. My bf got Ravioli, ragu sauce was delish but the ricotta tasted just as ordinary, imo. Because it's so small, the experience is almost not pleasant.

I wish I could give this place 3.5 stars because it was in between 3 and 4 stars. I ordered the pizza with tomato sauce, buffalo mozzarella and prosciutto and it tasted great, but without the prosciutto it lacked flavor. The tomato sauce just didn't have much taste to it and although the texture of the crust was great, it didn't have a ton of flavor either. However, the crust wasn't soggy like most thin brick oven pizzas, which made up for it.

I recently visited a charming pizza spot known for its thick and flavorful slices. I opted for the veggie slice, which, though priced at $6, justified its cost with quality. The restaurant offers a comfortable sit-down section, making for a pleasant dine-in experience despite the establishment holding a B health rating. While the pizza is undeniably good, the price point might make me consider other options before returning.

A friend of mine invited me to eat and check out the restaurant Camellia. I've heard of this place for it's ramen and gelato in one store concept. Naturally I was curious and decided to try it myself. Camellia is conveniently located by NYU and close to Union Sq. It's a casual sit down with plenty of seats. They had a variety of options you can choose from ranging from beef noodle soup and you're choice of ramen and broth. I ultimately went for the Rainbow Ramen. I wanted to see if it was as good as it looked so I ordered the shio broth and the spinach and fried chicken appetizer.The appetizers came out together with the ramen. Chicken was so crispy and tender whole the spinach was a nice cool and refreshing that checks off the needed vegetable serving for the day. As for the ramen, the texture was made just right without being too soft. The color was pretty cool and not just a hype. To preserve the display of the ramen, it's served outside of the broth. Even though I was pretty full, I had to try the gelato and it did not disappoint. I must've tried like 10 flavors before settling for sesame seaweed. The seaweed salt really brought out the flavor of sesame. I'm told they're made on the spot so it's always fresh and that they also alternate their flavors every so often so it's a must to try new items! Definitely also want to try their beef noodle soup next time!

Cute brunch place! We went on a weekday lunch, so thankfully there wasn't a wait. Weekends are a different story though. The place is pretty small but has a lot of tables, which does make it seem a bit cramped. I still loved the atmosphere. The host and waiters were all really nice as well.I ordered the matcha latte after reading all of the great reviews about it, but unfortunately I was not a fan. You can barely taste the matcha but was still overly sweet. I also ordered the avocado toast, which I never do at restaurants since I never saw the point in paying so much for something you can make at home, but it was worth it, including the extra for the eggs. The egg is a must add-on to the toast.I will visit again, especially to try the sweet potato fries (they didn't have it when I went).

Title: Mixed Feelings on Cozy Spot with Decent Eats

My visit to this restaurant started off on a positive note, with its pleasant interior and ample seating allowing my companion and I to comfortably choose a table by the window. The food received mixed reviews on my end; the highlight was certainly the fried spring rolls, which struck a good balance with a generous serving of protein. Unfortunately, the accompanying sauce was overly thick and excessively sweet.

The lemongrass coconut soup had a flavorful broth and the noodles were a commendable match, yet the meat, which was presented as pork but had the suspicious taste of chicken, was a letdown. In terms of dessert, the ube cheesecake stood out with its unique texture, being hearty and starch-forward rather than creamy.

Service was the low point of the experience. Despite the restaurant not being busy, I found the service to be slow and unattentive. It was a task to get the server's attention for assistance, even with clear gestures. Additionally, a simple request to exclude scallions from my dish was ignored, leading to an unnecessary hassle of removing them myself – an inconvenience that was notable given our table was the only one occupied at the time.

In summary, while certain dishes were enjoyable, the overall experience was marred by service shortfalls and a few kitchen mishaps.

3.5 stars.  Shared a large pizza with my husband.  Husband really enjoyed it and he is very picky about food quality. I could tell that the ingredients were good quality, but I thought the pizza could use a bit more flavor.  I'd definitely come back for more pizza, but I'm not running back.  Service was very good and friendly. Updating review -- tried the Sicilian pizza tonight, and meatballs.  Meatballs were tasty and I definitely preferred the Sicilian to the regular margarita.  The crust was pretty delicious - fresh and doughy.

Ehhhhh. Didn't really live up to the hype for me. I was skeptical even trying it reading the reviews but I wanted to go with an open mind. The cheese was good and I'm not a HUGE cheese advocate but the rice cake was a bit pudgy in texture and not in the good way. The food got dry pretty quickly because of the heat but I figured they would have come up with a way to combat that. The rice at the end tho was great but it's really hard to mess up fried rice. Wouldn't really recommend or come back :/

Title: A Delightful Experience Despite Reservation Hiccups

I learned the hard way that reservations at this popular spot need to be made well in advance, as they were fully booked when I called a day ahead. Chaos ensued at the front with a mix-up concerning another party's reservation, leading to an awkward wait. However, once past the initial hiccup, things improved swiftly.

The promised 10-15 minute wait time held true, and we were promptly seated. We decided to try the Box of Dreams and the Salmon Lovers combo. Our green tea and miso soup set a comforting prelude to the star dishes. The Box of Dreams lived up to its name—aesthetically pleasing and equally satisfying in taste, though on the pricier side. The Salmon Lovers combo, a more budget-friendly option, was a hit for my palate.

Service was efficient, our server attending to all our needs without a hitch. Despite a rocky start, the culinary offerings made the visit well worth it—just be sure to book your table well in advance!

Absolutely  have to check this place out if you're at the Chelsea Market.  The food is delish reminded me of the yummy Mexican seafood I eat back home in L.A.   I love that you can order it all in small plates at reasonable  prices so that you can try as much or as little of the menu that you want.  It's all very fresh including the tortillas which you can see them making right In front of you.   I wish there was more seating, it's very popular so you might find yourself standing  for a bit till a seat opens up. I went on a Friday  night and it was packed so we stood at the tortilla bar and ate our tacos  and aguachiles standing up then later moved over to the bar when a couple of seats opened up.  (But limited seating is common here at the Chelsea Market, don't let that stop you from visiting, eventually  a seat will open up)

Title: Mixed Feelings at 8Hill on the Upper West Side

On a quest for a delightful end-of-season lunch, my colleagues and I ventured into 8Hill. Stepping into its location instantly flooded me with nostalgia, the corner that once housed Isabella's and my old haunts like Blue Nile and Museum Cafe. The interior of 8Hill didn't disappoint with its ornate gold holiday decor, setting a festive mood.

Despite our anticipation, the meal was overall underwhelming, though it did nothing to dampen our spirits. In a nearly empty restaurant, we were initially ushered to less-than-desirable seating near the cold entrance, but after a short wait, we settled into the main dining area.

The lunch menu seemed promising, and the Mediterranean salads we started with were tasty but awkwardly served in bowls that didn't accommodate their contents well. For mains, the Branzino was satisfactory, and the falafel wrap substantial enough for leftovers. However, the free-range chicken shish lacked the advertised eggplant accompaniment, served instead with a rice-orzo substitute without explanation. When inquired about a missing white sauce, the server's response was lackluster, indicating the chicken's marinade should suffice.

Regrettably, the chicken's peculiar, rubbery texture was off-putting, although not inedible. Dessert was an afterthought, as no menu was presented, and we left without sampling the baklava we had eyed on social media.

In conclusion, while the ambiance was a highlight, the dining experience at 8Hill was a letdown. With West End Avenue's rich array of eateries, I had hoped for more from 8Hill to make it a standout destination on the Upper West Side.

I came here with a friend a while back and Im definitely a fan of this place. The ambiance is dim lit and with average volume. You can dress up or go casually but it's up to you. Their food taste fresh and and their cocktails are goods. I don't remember the name of my meal but it was pretty good. I'd come back.

What is the obsession of Asian bakeries with French/European style breads, pastries and cakes?  Not that I'm complaining, mind you, as their riffs on Western boulangerie are often well-executed and pretty darn tasty (and when they miss, at least they were "interesting").  At any rate, I had a pair of excellent eclairs from this Koreatown Paris Baguette, a nice tender choux pastry, and a smooth custard filling that wasn't overly sweet.  Unfortunately, we were there at the end of the day and the shelves were getting pretty emptied out so we couldn't get the milk bread or caneles we were looking for.  But we will be back for more caloric consumption!

Title: A Delightful Italian Feast at Paesano on Mulberry

My recent visit to Paesano on Mulberry was an absolute joy, both in dining and service. The evening started with a delightful treat of warm, complimentary bread, paired with a trio of olive oil, balsamic, and a unique garlic pepper oil that was so addictive, we couldn't resist asking for a second basket.

The fried calamari appetizer set a high bar for what was to come with its light breading and perfect golden-brown fry. For the main course, the Fra Diavlo was a seafood lover's dream, brimming with mussels, clams, and shrimp, each bite infused with flavor.

Even after such a sumptuous meal, we managed to save room for dessert, and the cannoli did not disappoint. A staple when in NYC, this cannoli was truly exceptional with its flaky shell and lusciously creamy filling—a treat I now long for back in LA.

Paesano on Mulberry has won my heart and my hearty recommendation for anyone in search of an authentic Italian dining experience.

STUNNING, ABSOLUTELY STUNNING!!!! Is how I would describe my experience here. This has been on my bucket list for YEARS! dubbed the most romantic restaurant in the United States it  definitely held true to that title. The restaurant itself is beautiful so breathtaking each table adorned with fresh white roses and a white candle. The service was outstanding each staff made sure we were taken care of from the moment we walked in. For starters we  ordered the scallops and pork belly, the pork belly literally melted in your mouth and the scallops were ok small  in serving but delicious. For our entree's we both had the Beef Wellington, both cooked to perfection and were scrumptious. And for dessert we ended our meal with the chocolate soufflé and creme brûlée' both were very tasty. As we enjoyed the meal, I couldn't help but notice just how quite the restaurant was, even with the pianist playing the latest hits  you literally could here a pin drop  it was magical.

Upon my visit to Upland, the standout dish was, without a doubt, the mushroom appetizer. This dish isn't just visually stunning; it's an absolute must-have. Trust me—order it and you'll be sending thanks my way. Everything on the menu impressed, reinforcing the notion that you can't make a misstep here. Just a tip: secure a reservation. This gem is no secret, evidenced by the bustling tables even on a Monday. Don't miss out!
