went here on a Sunday night with some friends. it has a pretty nice atmosphere and quite comfortable to hangout. in fact, it kind of remind me of casual kopitiam places I had back home. the menu was similar too and I actually had a difficult time deciding what to get because at the time everything looks so goodended up with chicken mee siam, and also shared satay and roti telur (telur translates to egg by the way) for appetizer. the roti telur was good! it was served with curry and it was gone before I know it. the satay was tender and the peanut sauce was good too. not authentic but good.i ordered extremely spicy mee siam but it was barely spicy, but that's okay and I'm not complaining. the texture of the noodle was good but I think the taste was bland. i expected it to have a tangy sour and savory taste. so i was not really impressed :( portion size was okay. if you don't have a big appetite you might even can share it. price was decent. however the pad mee hoon is really good maybe i should go with that one next time. overall i gave it a 3 star because it was just okay. definitely not bad, but not special either. just somewhere in the middle

I was meeting my BF for lunch one weekday near his office, and he recommended Uncle Gussy's for Greek. I could always use some Greek food, and this place was also on my bookmarks list, so it was perfect. We arrived a little after 1 pm and waiting about 15 minutes (according to BF, there's always a line). We decided to go halfsies on the Hercules (yellow rice, Greek salad, pita bread, and fries) with chicken, and added a side of lamb. This was more than enough for two people, especially since they don't skimp on the meat. We were still full at dinnertime. I prefered the lamb over the chicken because the chicken has this charred flavor I don't really care for, which my BF loves, so if you like barbecued stuff, this one's for you. The more you eat the platter, the heavier it feels, and the saltier it tastes, but the Greek salad definitely helps cut that. It's worth feeling like a beached whale afterwards, but just make sure you have plenty of water available - you'll need it.Tip - cash only!

One of my favorite restaurants in the world!  Seriously.  Not kidding.  Approachable. Amazing food. Beautiful ambiance.  Outstanding service.  And, it's in a great area.Completely wonderful cuisine that is affordable (even the wine!!!) in NYC's theater district.  Caesar salad or antipasti with three different special pastas are toted around the dining room by an accomplished wait staff, constantly refilling guests' plates.  Oh, and the cost is under $22 at lunch and under $26 at dinner.  And the wine?  Many choices for $33 a bottle!  Yes, real wine - not stuff with a screw too, and many choices.  Now, if you don't want the chef's specials, don't worry, because the menu is outstanding!We went once for lunch and once for dinner while we were visiting NYC (yes, it's that good).  Lunch choices were rigatoni with a tomato sauce, fettuccine with fresh crab, and mushroom ravioli.  Oh my goodness!!!  Heaven!!!  We saved room for dessert (I don't know how), and it was the zabaglione with berries.  That dessert choice was over-the-top sweet, but I survived.When we returned for dinner (make a reservation, and the restaurant has a coat check), we were seated in a gorgeous room with an atrium ceiling.  Service was impeccable, of course.  The choices that evening was spaghetti arrabiata with fried spicy shrimp, asparagus ravioli, and fusilli primavera.  Not a huge fan of the fusilli, but the other two dishes made up for it.  Dessert?  Oh yes, as it was our last night in the city.  I went with the zabaglione again (thankfully not as sweet) and my husband had the gelati trio.  Simply amazing!!!!So, please try to go if you can.  A delightful hidden gem that is worth a trip to NYC!

This is an outpost for their brick-and-mortar Bushwick location.I had their pepperoni pie and I enjoyed every last bite of it. The crust was extremely thin, everything tasted fresh and overall, it was a solid pie. The char from being baked in their brick oven added a nice slightly bitter aftertaste. Sprinkle on some dried chilis for additional flavor. Being that this location is in a food court, seating is pretty limited during peak hours. Will definitely recommend Roberta's if you're seeking a quality thin-crust pizza in the area.

4.5 Star. Overall. 12 tables capacity overall, small restaurant but fast service. Decent prices. Flavorful dishes. On the salty side like most Japanese places, but the flavor is authentic and overall appetizing. We sampled/ordered over half a dozen different items just to try it out. The dumplings ranked #1 with the kids and had to order a second serving. Ramens, appetizers, salad are all pretty decent. Cucumber is on the salty side, the limited 20-bowls-per-day Maji Teppen Ramen was on the salty side for me but the flavor is good and I love the large serving of bean sprouts portion in the bowl. Next time, I'd request for easy on the salt. Was concerned initially due to not many ratings, but pleasantly impressed with the food. Don't regret dining here. Nice and quiet.

I recently had the pleasure of discovering a charming spot while awaiting a show at the New York Theater Workshop. This quick and casual eatery offers an affordable and mouthwatering take on Japanese street food. While it may not win any awards for healthiest meal, the freshness is undeniable as they prepare your order right before your eyes. The customization is a plus – you can select your preferred spice level, choose from a variety of proteins, and more. While I wouldn't necessarily go out of my way to return, I definitely recommend it if you're nearby and craving a taste of Japan.

Tucked away in its new location, this sushi gem continues to surpass expectations. A recent visit to savor the $95 omakase offering confirmed why it holds a special place in my heart as one of my favorite sushi spots. The sushi rice, in particular, was outstanding—flavorful and perfectly seasoned. I was also pleasantly surprised by the generous size of each sushi piece, adding value to the overall experience. Although part of me wishes to keep this place a secret to ensure a table for future visits, it's a culinary experience too exquisite not to share. Highly recommended for sushi aficionados.

Despite my hopes for a satisfying experience, the restaurant's pork and shrimp pan-fried dumplings sadly missed the mark. At $8.15 for a serving of six, the price set my expectations for a burst of umami that one would anticipate from the inclusion of shrimp. Unfortunately, the dumplings fell flat in flavor. Although the texture hinted at the presence of shrimp, there was no taste to match, leaving much to be desired in the overall culinary experience.

This place is pretty cool and great for solo diners. You go in and they assign you a table at one of the singular booths. You fill out the data and they take your order, all with the most minimal people interaction. Great for introverts or people who don't want to talk to others. If you're more social and are bringing someone, you can also take down some of the booth walls and extend the space to talk to each other.The ramen itself was average, with good quality broth and ramen, but otherwise kind of boring. The toppings are a lot less great though, especially the egg which they make you peel yourself (and is kind of flavorless outside of being a soft-boiled egg).

This bar has bras hanging, is not the cleanest, and is out of the way, but Jeremy's Ale House is a south street seaport staple. The owners are friendly, staff behind the bar are on point, their freshly made chips with bacon, sour cream, green onions are delicious, and they serve huge beers (no more styrofoam cups due to NYC ban for establishments - however beers are still huge). I've had their calamari here as well after the Lupus Walk in the summer and it was surprisingly good and no one got sick!If you're in the area, definitely stop by and say hi to the owners and order their homemade chips and fixins!

Emeril just quietly opened a new Greek restaurant in the Hotel Henri in Chelsea, his first restaurant ever in NYC, and the food is great.He provides Greek staples, but some with his own creole twist. One of the best examples of this was the Octopus Beignets ($19 for 3), nice and crispy filled with chopped up pieces of octopus. Definitely get some of the dips to start too, which come with excellent warm pita bread.For the mains, the branzino is great ($32) as is the burger ($25). This is a very good spot, especially for a hotel restaurant in this area.

Tucked away inside a deli on 23rd St., this gem serves up authentic Korean dishes that shouldn’t be missed. At the back of the deli, a small counter with appetizers like kimbob rolls and dumplings beckons food adventurers. I opted for the kimchi ju gae (S-3, $10.50), a hearty and generous serving of spicy kimchi pork stew brimming with sweet potato noodles, tofu, rice cakes, and veggies. The dish came quickly, though I did wish for more pork and a spicier kick over the prevailing sour notes. Despite this, the value is undeniable, and the promise of kimbob rolls and other hot entrees warrants a return visit. Eating in is an option, but the ambiance suggests takeout or delivery might be preferable. A great spot for groups with differing taste buds, as the deli’s extensive menu has something for everyone.

Title: Cozy Hotpot Haven in the Heart of Chinatown

My latest visit to Hometown Hotpot reaffirmed why it stands out in the bustling Chinatown culinary scene. The establishment prides itself on cleanliness and ample space, making it a comfortable dining adventure even on busy evenings.

Location-wise, Hometown is a gem, strategically nestled in the epicenter of Chinatown, offering easy access for a delightful hotpot experience. The extensive menu, featuring a plethora of meats and vegetables, pairs perfectly with the five distinct soup bases. Priced reasonably at $27.99 per person for a 2-hour unlimited feast, it promises value for every diner.

However, my satisfaction took a small hit due to their restrictive serving of premium items, like the fatty beef, which was limited to one plate at a time for our group of six. This policy, while understandable for cost control, led to a minor inconvenience and slight delays in our meal.

Despite this hiccup, the overall experience at Hometown Hotpot remains positive. It is a favored spot for our group gatherings, and we're keen to return for more heartwarming hotpot sessions in Chinatown. 4/5 stars.

During a late weekend visit to a newly opened Japanese restaurant, I was greeted by an exceptionally friendly bartender who provided great company throughout my stay. Opting for a Shochu highball, I was pleased with its strong, lemony zest – a reliable choice when a specialized shochu menu is absent.

The star of the night was the Tenho Kurume Ramen, featuring a robust tonkotsu broth with a well-balanced ensemble of chashu pork, wood ear mushrooms, scallions, toasted seaweed, and a soft-boiled egg. While the noodles were of superior texture, the dish was slightly marred by its saltiness, and the egg didn't quite hit the mark.

Complementing the ramen, I sampled the mitarashi dango – a decadent pairing of glutinous rice cakes and pork belly enrobed in a sweet sauce. Although delectably flavored, the portion did not justify the price, making it a less valuable option if you're looking to share.

Despite the appealing skewer, similar offerings at a more reasonable price and portion size can be found elsewhere in NYC. While the experience was pleasant, especially due to the amicable staff, the menu didn't impress enough to warrant a special trip back. This establishment has potential in its locale, but overall, I'd land on a modest 3.2-star rating.

Went with my friend on a monday night to celebrate her birthday. We chose the restaurant week menu, though regular menu is priced reasonably. The main course is amazing. The duck is superb and the fish dish is great. We both really like the dessert with raspberry. Service is attentive and relaxed. The best way to end a monday night. Will be back and try their regular menu.

Got the Donut BEC but asked them to add a beef patty ($6) on it to make it into a burger. OMG somehow this comes together to equal perfections. Had to eat it with a fork but it was amazing and ive been craving it ever since. Small venue so expect a wait but they text you when a tables being made ready for you.

I've dined at this quaint spot for work lunches on a couple of occasions and intend to return. The establishment offers a good selection of dishes at fair prices. Remarkably, it maintains a serene atmosphere amidst the midday rush in midtown. Highly recommended for a peaceful meal in a bustling area.

That beef pho tho!! I was not expecting to be so impressed by what I thought would be just another bowl of pho. This was no ordinary pho. Between the meat, the broth, and even the noodles, this is the best pho in midtown. There is something in the dish that is a little sweet, and it's a game changer. I felt compelled to debrief with my partner along the way, as I found new flavors in each bite. I was all like, "OMG did you taste the brisket!" "Wow, that broth!" "These noodles!" And so on. I feel like I'm fangirling over here, but you must try this beef pho if you get the chance. On a side note, the beet& mango summer rolls were also a lovely treat and the peanut sauce went a long way. Service was friendly and fast, and they can accommodate a group if youve got one.

I ordered the lamb shank tagine for brunch and super enjoyed it! It was super tender and beautifully seasoned. Everyone at my table enjoyed their food as well, I liked the tomato sauce in the Moroccan eggs as well. The hummus was popular too. The restaurant itself is really nice and cutely decorated. The music was a fun mix of the Beatles and Arab music. We saw a few famous people (VS model and a famous Insta illustrator). Was a very pleasant brunch, would recommend! And they have a covered area to wait if the wait is long, which was nice on a very cold NYC day.

It was my second trip to NYC in two weeks and even colder this time around with the temperature hovering around four degrees Fahrenheit. Once again, I arrived well past 10PM, and even in the Upper West Side, late evening dining options were slim. This fast food spot happened to be a block away from my hotel and open until 2PM. There are six of them in Manhattan, so I assumed they must have quite a following for their chicken.Even walking the one block was tortuous to this Left Coaster, but I made it to find a full staff but just one other customer. They serve ribs, burgers, burrito bowls, and gyros wraps, but they're best known for their charcoal broiled chicken.i decided to order the 1/2 Chicken individual meal for $14.25 as it afforded me a salad and a side (photo: bit.ly/2tjdOL2). What I didn't know was that they were out of several sides like the mixed vegetables and corn on the cob.That left me with the Rice & Beans which were pretty heavy going (photo: bit.ly/2Byu7Z4). The leg and thigh were tender, but the breast was a bit on the dry side. I liberally squeezed the bottle of the honey mustard sauce in order to moisten it. Most of their business at that hour consisted of deliveries and pick-ups, so it was a bit lonely in there. Once I finished gnawing on the chicken and splooged the sauce onto the pita wedges, it was back into the cold for me.FOOD - 3 stars...the dark meat was better than the whiteAMBIANCE - 2.5 stars...kinda messy and a bit chillySERVICE - 2 stars...minimum service required hereTOTAL - 3 stars...if you need a poultry fix late into the nightRELATED - Looking for dining options in New York City? Here's a collection of places I've tried and reviewed: bit.ly/2sGleaS

I was trying to take my mom out for a nice last night in New York but the experience of coming to the restaurant was disappointing. We arrived around 8 PM on a Friday night. The restaurant was fairly packed but the hostess said the wait would only be 15 minutes so we decided to wait. We waited around 35 minutes before we were actually seated. There was no actual waiting area in the restaurant since it was so small so we had to awkwardly stand around the door until we were called in. When we were seated I was very disappointed to see that we were not seated in one of the cute areas that surround the opening. Instead we were shoved into a dark corner on tiny table next to the bar. There was a giant crowd of bar patrons sitting behind us and just made the smaller space even more crowded. Worst yet was this awful guy who decided to stand next to our table halfway through our meal and just kept bumping me with his butt because he talked like a woodpecker - constantly bending over at the waist with no respect for those around him in such a small area. Service was slow as well - it was difficult to grab the attention of our server during the meal. When we finally did, we ordered the eggplant Parmesan appetizer and linguine di mare. The eggplant parmigiana was pretty average - a bit salty but the sauce was good and I was able to bring it home and make it into a good pasta dish the next day. The linguine di mare had a good flavor and amount of seafood. Our main complaint was that the noodles were not cooked enough and had way too much of a bite to them. However, once we told the server about it she brought out a replacement for us which was very nice and did turn out better. All in all, a disappointing night that was just hit and miss throughout the whole experience.

Title: A Disappointing Foray at Pinch Chinese

If you're venturing into Pinch Chinese, tempted by the allure of an association with Din Tai Fung's former executive chef, you might want to temper your expectations. Despite the buzz, the restaurant falls short of its promise of delivering an extraordinary culinary experience.

The heart of the matter is the famed soup dumplings. While the flavor hits the mark, they're disappointingly small, leaving one yearning for more of that succulent soupiness that makes a soup dumpling truly special.

Beyond the dumplings, the menu offers little in the way of surprises. The dishes, though adequate, do not justify the higher price points, especially when compared to the generous portions and lower costs of the Chinatown counterparts merely a stone's throw away.

Yes, you do get a nicer ambiance at Pinch, which may be a deciding factor for some. But when the conversation turns to value for money and culinary delight, particularly in a city brimming with exceptional Asian fare, I find myself puzzled by the average ratings Pinch receives.

In summary, if it's premium soup dumplings you're after, your quest might have to continue elsewhere in the city. Pinch Chinese, despite its pedigree, hasn't quite hit the mark.

While this dumpling house may be on the pricier side compared to others, the cost reflects its offerings. Note that the tip is conveniently included in the check. Although the veggie steamed dumplings fell short of expectations, the pork soup dumplings and fried pork dumplings were a delightful experience, packed with flavor and expertly prepared. The scallion pancake with beef was another standout dish, satisfying with its perfect pairing of ingredients. The house hand-pulled noodles were a testament to the restaurant's mastery of texture, providing a pleasurable chewiness that even my 4-year-old appreciated. Overall, the hits far outweigh the misses at this establishment.

I visited the restaurant for a weekday breakfast with friends and we were promptly seated. I ordered an iced coffee, a scone, and yogurt. While the food was satisfactory, it wasn't particularly notable. Service faltered somewhat as our waiter was absent for an extended period, causing a delay in receiving our drinks. For a quick coffee and pastry, I might recommend opting for the Stumptown in the lobby instead. Overall, I'd give the experience a solid 3.5 stars.

Upon visiting the esteemed Keens Steakhouse, I found the ambiance to be initially stuffy, but this quickly faded as the evening went on. Service was warm if not entirely knowledgeable on the nuances of their red wine selections, which was remedied by a proactive offer to sample.

I settled on a glass of Syrah, although in hindsight, the samples were more intriguing. Nevertheless, a generous pour made up for any missteps. The waiter’s recommendation of a tequila Cointreau cocktail was a highlight and paired nicely with the rustic bread and fresh crudités that greeted us.

For our main course, the oysters Rockefeller were a pleasant prelude to the impressive mutton chop, which arrived with an unexpectedly delightful side of sautéed greens. While the mutton was a spectacle, and certain bites were delectable (particularly the flavorful rind), the main meat could have benefited from more fat distribution for tenderness.

In contrast, the prime T-bone steak was nothing short of exceptional—juicy, savory, and perfectly charred with aged depth. This dish alone reinforced the restaurant’s reputation for premium cuts.

Our meal concluded with the key lime pie, an exquisite dessert that far exceeded its photographic depictions. Its perfection paralleled that of the T-bone steak, ensuring our final impression of Keens was a lasting one.

In reflection, the occasional air of superiority among the staff is understandable, as they operate within what could be considered the pantheon of New York steakhouses.

Title: A Gluten-Free Midnight Delight on the Upper East Side

Living on the Upper East Side and finding gluten-free options after dark can be a culinary challenge, but my recent experience with Centro has left me thoroughly impressed. Craving a slice of pizza well past midnight, I decided to take a chance on their delivery service. To my delight, the pizza arrived within 30 minutes, a delectable cheesy masterpiece that could easily rival any traditional pizza in looks and, surprisingly, in taste.

The gluten-free crust was notably good, a commendable feat for alternative doughs, which often fall flat—literally and figuratively. I appreciate their attention to detail with the packaging; the pizza not only arrived in a box but also on a disposable tin. This thoughtful gesture presumably ensures minimal risk of cross-contamination, an aspect of utmost importance for those with gluten sensitivities.

Initially, it struck me as odd that the pizza hadn’t been sliced, but the reason became clear the next day. While reheating the leftover pizza on the very tin it was delivered on, I discovered a gluten-free pizza cutter, individually wrapped to maintain its gluten-free integrity. Such a simple, considerate touch goes a long way.

Thank you, Centro, for your exceptional service and for those thoughtful nuances that truly enhance the dining experience. You’ve proven that it's the little things that count, and for that, you definitely rock!

This place had a no wait at 6:15 pm on a Friday, so we ran right over from our hotel. The atmosphere was quiet but still casual. The waiter/kitchen accidentally had goat cheese on my friend's salad after she specified she was allergic to dairy, so they made her a fresh one at no cost, however she had taken a few bites before we realized. Luckily it didn't cause a serious reaction. The food was so good!! We'd highly recommend giving it a try.

Matador combo is such an amazing quality meal, enough for 3 people with leftovers. The matador combo includes generous portions of  6 delicious items mentioned in my previous reviews, and over the years I've been ordering this, friends, relatives and my very picky son have all loved the meal. The online ordering option has been great on our recent pick up and delivery orders. I stopped ordering from here due to issues with not being able to order takeout by phone during busy times (getting a busy signal) but the online ordering option solved this problem and has been smooth. Order ahead and allow time during busy times.  Also, their health grade is an A. A previous review indicated otherwise but if there was a lower grade that is not the case now.

The food here is good and the service is even better. We came on a Tuesday for lunch and there were not many people here. After we ordered, the food was served quickly which was nice. I ordered the homemade caramel cinnamon apple crepe and it was delicious. I also tried some of my friend's Le Croque Madame sandwich and it was also very good. If you are really hungry I would recommend going for something savory, but for brunch the sweet crepe was enough for me.

I recently visited a local Mexican restaurant, and I was genuinely impressed with the quality of the fare on offer. The housemade nachos were a standout; they paired perfectly with the wide variety of entrées available. The margarita list was extensive, giving diners ample options to complement their meal. In addition to the food, the vibrant and fun atmosphere really made the dining experience enjoyable. Altogether, a great spot for anyone craving authentic Mexican flavors in a lively setting.

Locanda Verde, helmed by the acclaimed Andrew Carmellini, stands as his premier establishment, and it's easy to see why. Withstanding the test of time, the restaurant continues to exude trendiness and remains a bustling hotspot. The culinary offerings are exceptional, with a vibrant crowd to match. Whether you indulge in their expertly crafted drinks or savor the top-notch service, you're in for an authentic downtown experience. A special nod to the pasta dishes — each one is a testament to the kitchen's consistent excellence. It's clear that at Locanda Verde, you really can't make a wrong turn on the menu.

This is a nice little Korean lunch spot serving healthier versions of what you find in other Korean places. There's a bit less of a grease/oil flavor though depending on your preference for some of the dishes, this might not be a good thing. They also notably selll omiberry tea, a tea made from Schisandra. The tea has a light fruity flavor similar to osmanthum (I guess a red berry tea if you don't know that one either.)I personally prefer the bulgogi in terms of the dishes here. It's not super sweet and generally tender. I've only gotten the galbi once as there wasn't much for the price though the few pieces were good. The japchae has a good mix of vegetables and it is alright. The side dishes are a hit or miss. I don't generally like the one with the spinach/beet as it lacks flavor. A bit of sesame oil would do wonders. The purple rice is a nice touch and quite flavorful.They used to have this mini bulgogi  snack (which I guess it would be tteok-galbi) which was a very good side snack but sadly they don't have it anymore. Their mandoo are fine but I wouldn't go out of my way. The wings are fine also. As per their other dishes, most of their stuff is light.I wouldn't go out of my way to go to this place but what it is, the food is good. Though in terms of modern Korean food, I prefer Her Name is Han (though the lines are terrible) and in terms of bulgogi/other dishes there's certain other places that give more bang for your buck. If you want a healthier Korean lunch/dinner to go, this place is good and the staff is nice.3.5. Rounded up because of the area/nice service/tea.
Oh so good.  Not a lover of the Brucetta made with mushrooms but the pasta is very good and the was excellent

Titled "A Quick Bite for Naruto Fans," this ramen bar delivers exactly what you'd expect: a decent bowl of noodles with a side of anime nostalgia. While the ramen won't transport you to culinary nirvana, it's tasty and served up with efficiency. The counter seating adds an interactive element as you watch your meal prepared right before your eyes. In essence, Naruto Ramen is more of a novelty visit for those drawn in by its name. It's a suitable stop for fans in the vicinity to indulge in a bit of themed dining and cross it off their fandom bucket list. However, for those in pursuit of a ramen revelation, this joint isn't the destination.

I recently had lunch at this local eatery, lured in by their affordable lunch specials. While the pricing was wallet-friendly, I found the dishes on the greasy side, which detracted from my overall enjoyment of the meal. However, the accommodating nature of the staff deserves praise; they were quite flexible in allowing us to modify our reservation without any hassle. Service-wise, the team was warm and welcoming – a redeeming quality that would make me consider a return visit, perhaps to try their dumplings that caught my eye. Though the restaurant's exterior is unassuming, don't be fooled; the interior is rather pleasant.

Special thanks to Ben L. and Elizabeth L. for this birthday surprise!!! Upon entry, I was pretty impressed with the beauty of the old-school décor of huge mirrors and ceiling fans. A trio of us came for my birthday celebration, total surprise for me and I was super excited to try it. We got a basket of bread and butter and carafe of Cote du Rhone - gosh, best wine ever! It was sweet and fruity, super easy to drink! Get it! Chicken Liver and Foie Gras Mousse - HOLY MOLY! THIS IS A MUST GET! I love the combination flavor of everything - chicken liver, sweet red onions, and lightly dressed lettuce on a warm bread. Gosh, this was so good that it melts in my mouth and keep on wanting more! GET THIS OR REGRET!!! We also got Beef Tartare - the flavor was really good and I liked the onion taste. Solid choice but definitely overshadowed by the Chicken Liver appetizer. For entrees, we got the Duck Confit, Branzino, and Steak Frites. Duck Confit, I loved the crispy skin and tender meat. Branzino had the perfect skin and the flavor was so fresh and good. Steak Frites, the fries were really good but I did wish the steak was a bit more charred. Creme Brulee is another MUST GET!!! Probably the best version I ever, ever had! I loved how it has a bit of cinnamon flavor. Sugar crust was perfectly hard and the custard was the perfect consistency - not overly creamy. Still dreaming of this!!! The second dessert we got was the Mango Cheesecake, it was a nice and sweet mango flavor and texture was creamy. Runner-up! Service was phenomenal!!! We were super lucky to have Maria as our waitress - she was bubbly, honest, and had the best recommendations. Love her! Ben L. asked for her recommendations between three wines and she told us to get the Cote du Rhone, which happened to be the most inexpensive one! It was the best wine ever!!! Another noteworthy is that she brought us more fresh bread for the pate because she knew we would need it, love that she took care of us!!! Cheers to 30 Club!!! :)

This place is definitely a hole-in-the-wall. I didn't expect it to be such a small restaurant, and it's extremely dimly lit too. The decor and music are Jamaican, so it's an interesting combination with the Japanese food and liquor. I ordered what seems like their most popular food option--the chicken karate combo. $15 was honestly a steal. The chicken, rice, miso soup, and salad were all delicious. The chicken was tender, juicy, and went very well with the lightly seasoned rice. The sauce that went over the chicken and rice was also delicious--it reminds me a little bit of tartar sauce but a much better version of it. Their miso soup is also not bad, and I enjoyed the refreshing salad. Overall, I enjoyed my experience. The service isn't great and I was the only person there, but honestly, I didn't really need anything. It's a great place for intimate conversations, but I wouldn't recommend coming here with large parties.

Title: A Fusion Feast to Remember

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this Asian fusion gem, and I must say, it was nothing short of amazing. The meal dazzled with unique flavor pairings, artfully plated dishes, and top-tier service. The menu boasted a variety of mouth-watering options, but we settled on the business lunch and the visually stunning dim sum platter, which was a delight with its vibrant colors and delectable tastes. The shu mai stood out with its perfect umami balance and an irresistible tender chew.

The Thai chicken wings were also a hit, thanks to their enticing char and flavorful sauce. On top of that, the Japanese risotto was a mushroom lover's dream come true, rich and satisfying across every forkful. The service was impeccable, prompt, and warm, reflecting the restaurant's commitment to an excellent dining experience.

As for the ambiance, it's rare to find a spot that exceeds expectations the way this place does. The interior struck a fine balance between elegance and minimalism, with quirky touches that extend even to the bathroom. Comfortable seating and a well-designed space made it a solid 6/5 for the environment.

In summary, this restaurant delivered on all fronts, securing a well-deserved 5/5 for both food and service. A visit here is highly recommended for anyone looking to indulge in a symphony of flavors in a beautifully curated setting.

Title: Mixed DoorDash Experience with Quick Delivery but Missing Items

We decided to give DoorDash a go for a convenient meal at home and opted for a local restaurant offering wings and sides. While the delivery service was impressively quick, it wasn't without its faults.

We ordered a small wings with a choice of three sauces, but only received two, which was somewhat disappointing. Furthermore, the expected carrots, celery, and blue cheese dipping sauce that should accompany the wings were nowhere to be found upon delivery, adding to our list of letdowns.

On a slightly brighter note, the chips and queso were a hit with the queso being flavorful, although the accompanying chips were overwhelmingly salty. Thankfully, I had a soda to counterbalance that saline assault. Speaking of the soda, the size for the price I paid—over $4—was underwhelming, as showcased by the pic I've attached for reference.

In summary, while the speed of delivery was a plus, the incomplete order and some quality issues detracted from the overall experience.

Came here on a Friday night around 7pm and only waited for about 5-10 minutes for a table for 2, not bad. We ordered kimchee fries (appetizer) and it's exactly what you'd expect. Yummy crispy fries doused with kimchi and sriracha mayo. We also ordered the banh mi and pho because my friend and I were just craving it. I will say obao's pho and banh mi are pretty good if that's what you're craving. Not the best I've ever had, but hits the spot. The banh mi is smaller than what you'd expect though. Maybe about half or 3/4 the size of a regular banh mi you'd order anywhere else. My biggest qualm with obao though is the price. A meal here is pretty pricy, even for menu items that typically don't cost as much elsewhere. The extra cost of the food is probably made up by the extravagant and luxurious interior environment of the restaurant. They put a lot into decor and vibe. When you go here, it's very intimate and dark with candlelit tables. A great spot for a date!

Not a typical New York slice. Not terrible but not as good as a typical slice.Had some pepperoni pizza from here today.Pretty meh for me. It's ultra thin crust, to the point where it's too easy to get overcooked. Light on sauce, with decent cheese and larger slices of spicy pepperoni.  The schtick here is they give you sauce on the side to dip your pizza into. I wish it was ranch instead like at Gumby's pizza. I only used the sauce for the crust.When slices return, I will try the heritage sausage and al pastor by the slice and will be back to review those interesting slices.

Very cute and clean looking space for omakase. They seat about 12 people at the counter. For about $65 per person you get 12 courses which includes two appetizers and 10 pieces of sushi. The fish did taste fresh, but the rice tasted undercooked or maybe they didn't use enough water? But it wasn't the softer sushi rice I'm used to. I did appreciate the chef asking how everything is pretty often. The more memorable pieces to me were probably the Hokkaido uni, and the foie gras wagyu. I would have enjoyed the experience a lot more if the rice was better.  It might've been just an off night for their rice, but I don't really plan on coming back to see. I was pretty disappointed when I realized our omakase experience here didn't consist of any toro. They did have it as a part of their a la carte menu, which I probably would've tried if it weren't for their bad batch of rice. I think all the omakase experiences I've had so far in the city did consist of a toro piece. I've had good omakase around the city for around the same price that I rather go back to.

Title: Bustling Brunch Spot with Attentive Service and Delicious Drinks

I popped in for brunch right at opening time (12pm) on a Sunday, and by the time I was seated after a mere 5-10 minute wait, the place was already bustling—clearly, this is a popular spot, so come early or risk a wait! Without a reservation, I felt quite lucky to snag a table that quickly.

The service didn't miss a beat; the staff was on their game, incredibly attentive throughout the meal. As for the food, I opted for the mussels, which were fairly average, although the accompanying thin fries were a delightful crunch. I did find myself eyeing the escargot on other tables—next time, I'll be sure to dive into more traditional French fare.

The real star of the show was the Champagne "pick me up" drink—exceptionally tasty and so smooth that the cognac was almost undetectable. Four drinks in, and I could have easily sipped on them all day!

This charming spot is conveniently located right off the Spring Street subway station, making it an easy choice for future visits. I'm already looking forward to returning, perhaps for dinner next time to explore more of their menu. Definitely worth a repeat visit!

I recently visited a charming little spot that's perfect for a girls' night out. The concept of cooking your own food at the table adds a fun twist to the dining experience, although be warned - it can get a bit warm! The portions are generous; we couldn't even finish everything. The garlic rice was a standout, and the chicken I prepared was simply delectable. However, I struggled with the salmon, which didn't quite cook through to my preference, so I decided to pass on it. The drinks were delightful, prices fair, and the overall experience left me eager to return and explore more of the menu.

Title: A Coastal Delight at The Goma Shoyu Spot

I recently indulged in a coastal culinary delight at a local gem known for its poke bowls. The star of my lunch was the Goma Shoyu Tuna bowl – a dish crafted with precision and showcasing high-quality ingredients. The Bluefin Tuna was exceptionally fresh, melded with exotic flavors of Goma Shoyu, a hint of heat from the Chili Oil, and a symphony of textures from Nori, Hijiki, creamy Avocado, and crunchy Garlic Chips. Though some ingredients were unfamiliar, this adventurous combination proved to be a fantastic choice.

To accompany my poke, I selected a miso soup which, to my dismay, was overly salted. This minor hiccup, however, couldn't overshadow the quality of the tuna bowl. While the entire meal cost $25, a bit steep for a daily lunch, the superior taste and quality of the fish justified the expense. It's a place I'd recommend for those looking to treat themselves. I look forward to my next splurge at this establishment.

I was craving banh xeo (Vietnamese pancake) and frantically searched for a restaurant that makes it. For some reason this dish is not available at every Vietnamese restaurant when it should be. Well luckily I found it here, in the appetizer section. When it came out, I was shocked by how big the whole thing was. It is definitely an entire meal by itself and can be an appetizer if shared with at least 4 people. It came with a hefty serving of vegetables and fish sauce. The outside is very crunchy, as it should be, and the inside is softer and contained shrimps, ground pork, bean sprouts and green beans. There is a fair amount of stuffings, and slightly more green beans than I would like , but that's mainly a personal preference. I would have preferred sliced pork belly instead of ground pork, but I believe that's a regional difference.Overall satisfied with my food. And the decoration of this place is quite interesting and eye catching as well.

Small hole in the wall pizza place. Nice greasy pizza made fresh with quick turnaround due to high volume spot. Ordering was easy and quick though was hot and fresh I felt the sauce was a bit bland but overall it was enjoyable

Restaurant Review: A Mixed Bag at Local Eatery

I recently dined at a restaurant with a party of nine and found the experience to be a roller coaster of highs and lows. The venue’s ambience stood out with its lovely fireplace seating and modern touch of digital menus on tablets. The staff's ability to accommodate our large group on a high table was commendable. Yet, this positive start soon gave way to a series of disappointments.

The cuisine offered a mixed bag of flavors. Unfortunately, the service faltered with an order mix-up: my Chicken Shish turned into an unrequested medium-cooked fillet steak. Given the restaurant wasn’t busy, it was a surprising oversight. Eventually, I sampled the Chicken Shish from a friend's plate and found it dry and lacking in the promised truffle flavor, a mundane dish that I could outdo at home.

The Fillet Mignon presented a tale of wasted potential – a fine cut of meat let down by insufficient seasoning, leaving us with the impression of boiled steak, salvaged only by some post-cook seasoning. On the positive side, the Chorizo flatbread was the highlight, delivering a homemade taste combined with well-paired hummus. The burrata salad and a cocktail received lukewarm reception, ranking average at best.

Dessert brought solace in the form of a basic but enjoyable lava cake and vanilla ice cream, which, despite its unusual color, tasted pleasantly rich.

However, the service was the true Achilles’ heel of the night. The waiter’s constant interruptions and intrusive dish-clearing detracted significantly from the dining experience, causing discomfort rather than attentiveness. Although water glasses were never empty and the splitting of the bill was handled with patience, the overzealous service significantly impinged upon our enjoyment.

In conclusion, despite a beautiful setting and some accommodating aspects, the restaurant struggled with inconsistent food quality and overbearing service. The Chorizo flatbread alone can't redeem the shortcomings that cast a shadow over the meal. Unless significant improvements are made, I find little reason to return.

I recently visited a local eatery for a party of 10, indulging in an array of roasted delights. The roast pig was the night's shining star, winning over the crowd with its succulent meat and flavorful presence. My personal favorite, however, was the roast pork, which stood out with its crunchy skin and tender flesh, all beautifully complemented by a Chinese-style BBQ sauce.

The roast duck, while delectable to some, ranked least among my companions, primarily due to the effort required to debone and its distinctive taste, which isn't everyone's cup of tea. This spot is truly for the more adventurous palate.

Our visit at 3pm on a Saturday was surprisingly smooth with a shorter than expected queue. The affordable pricing and the cash-only policy add a no-frills charm to this dining adventure.

Title: A Culinary Marvel in the Heart of NYC

From the moment I stepped into this gem of a restaurant, I knew I was in for a five-star experience. The menu selection was impeccable—the burrata and knots appetizer, and the fried chicken sandwich were highlights, but the hanger steak truly stole the show. Its smoky char and the heavenly butter topping lingered in my memory long after the meal.

Sides like the roasted Brussels sprouts complemented the main courses beautifully, but nothing prepared me for the grand finale: their hot fudge sundae, crowned with marshmallow gelato, was a masterpiece deserving of high praise.

The service was unparalleled, with an attentive team ensuring a seamless experience, and the restaurant's iconic decor provided a cozy ambiance suitable for any event.

In short, this is not just a meal, it's an event you don't want to miss. Skip the plethora of dining options in the city and head straight for this unforgettable culinary destination.

This place has so many good reviews but there are so many better places in Manhattan. We had the rib ramen, tonkatsu ramen, pork and chicken dumplings. The dumplings were great! But my ramen was just eh. Portion was really big. We got the fresh noodles and that was good but the broth was eh. And not hot enough either. Maybe I should have gotten something else. But for Ramen next time I'll pass. Service was good but it wasn't busy so.

My girlfriend and I recently dined at this charming Mediterranean spot and were thoroughly impressed. The service was swift, ensuring our meal arrived without delay. She ordered a steak, requesting it extra rare, and it was perfection on a plate – just glance at the accompanying photo for proof. I indulged in the chicken kebabs, which were equally delightful. The portions provided great value for the price. We're already planning our next visit!

Ambiance: 10/10Service: 9/10Food: 5/10Gitano was super super cute. It's like a hidden garden in the middle of the city. That being said, I felt as though the food was just okay. I think I had high expectations with how cutesy the restaurant was. There weren't too many choices for food. I got the yogurt and it was decent. I was glad that it came dairy free (coconut yogurt) and the fruit options were nice. However, it was a very small bowl and was overpriced. One thing they did really well was drinks. My friends got strawberry mojitos (not on the menu) and loved them!

I recently grabbed a Cobb Salad for pickup dinner from a local restaurant, and I was pleased with the experience. The food was ready at the promised time, which was a bit later than usual but worked perfectly with my schedule. The salad featured a hearty portion of chicken, crispy bacon, creamy avocado, and tangy bleu cheese, drizzled with a delightful vinaigrette – extra on the side as per my request, which the restaurant kindly provided.

For $14, I found the salad to be a terrific value, offering a more substantial meal compared to similar-priced offerings from places like Sweetgreen. While the chicken was somewhat bland, the vinaigrette added the necessary zest to the dish. I did miss the presence of egg and tomato, which would have made it a more authentic Cobb Salad, but overall, it was satisfying and felt like a lighter yet fulfilling meal option.

The interior of the place is charming, though seating is limited; it was bustling at 6:30 PM on a Friday. The outdoor area adds extra space and contributes to the restaurant's open atmosphere. I would certainly consider ordering from here again for a tasty and relatively healthy meal.

Title: A Tale of Two Services at [Restaurant Name]

Review:

My recent dining experience at [Restaurant Name] left me with decidedly mixed feelings. Our initial encounter with the first waiter was disappointing; his rudeness and refusal to accommodate a simple billing request were off-putting. His claim of not understanding English and subsequent dismissal of our group's need for separate checks—"No, I'm not dealing with this. This is too complicated."—felt unprofessional.

Thankfully, the head waitress, a friend of one of our group members, stepped in to save the day. Her efficiency and pleasant demeanor contrasted sharply with her colleague's and allowed us to enjoy our meals without further issues. The chicken parm, renamed creatively on the menu, was generous in portion and delicious, much like the boneless chicken chunks and pork with yuca enjoyed by my companions.

That said, a couple of hiccups did occur. Firstly, our table received unordered sides of avocado, platanos maduros, and flan. While tasty, the surprise addition to our bill was unwelcome, as we had wrongly assumed these were complimentary gestures. Secondly, our small group of three was mistakenly charged an automatic gratuity intended for parties of six or more. Luckily, this was resolved without fuss upon request.

In conclusion, while the food was thoroughly enjoyed and most of our group left with leftovers, the service experience was checkered. The likelihood of a return visit is uncertain, and if I were to consider it, I'd ensure a smaller party and steer clear of the less accommodating staff.

Oh, I don't know what other places do with regard to fried rice. But they are doing it wrong. This place uses spam. And the flavors are so distinctly Filipino that you feel like you are in Manila eating in Intramuros in the food alleys. Both high brow and low key, the service is impeccable and leaves you grasping across the table for the next bite, even when you are full to the gills. Also, whoever was the person that first picked up a ube yam and said why not...bless you. Stellar ice cream. They even have cheese ice cream... what.... lol yes please.

Great location and easy to get to in the Times Square area - less crowded that some of the other locations. Staff is friendly and service is good...Have pre-ordered cakes online or through the app and able to pick up. They have sandwiches and salads now too...have to try that next time.Cakes have the lightest cream! 6" mini-cakes are good for small group and 10" full size for bigger parties...though value wise, purchase the larger cake...Sign up for PB rewards and earn points for every purchase. 60 points earns you a free pastry!

Came here on Sunday night for dinner after work.Searching up nearby restaurant and saw this seafood boil looks pretty good. Looks like cajun Sichuan fusion.There are lots of option on their menus, besides seafood boil, there are also Chinese dishes as well.We decided to go easy so choose the group combo, it includes lots of stuff. Starter: chongqing spicy popcorn chicken- chicken was  juicy crispy. It was medium spicyFried calamari / chicken wings- very crispy too, not oily. I like the flavor of chicken wings, more like Chinese style seasoning.Seafood boil- including crawfish, shrimp, lobster , potatoes, corns, sausage slices. We got the supcrab house sauce. It's cajun style mixed with Sichuan peppercorn, and with lots of garlic . I love the sauce, it was so good to dip the seafood with it. There still some sauce left after we done, i wish there was pasta or bread I can put it in haha.......Anyway, I think overall their quality was really good. And it mixed some Sichuan flavor into their dishes was very unique and tasteful. They also have great deal on their lunch menu, wilL be back and check it out!

I recently dined at a bustling restaurant renowned for its variety in seating arrangements and ambience, only to find the cozy space a tad cramped. The staff was friendly, though the popularity of the place meant a bit of a wait for their signature tie-dye pizza. The seating process was efficient – a brief 20-30 minute wait with a call system to free you from door-side loitering.

The tie-dye pizza, while good, sadly fell short of my lofty expectations. However, it redeemed itself with a delightfully thin, crispy crust and a flavor boost from the pesto. The Rubirosa supreme was the highlight, boasting savory toppings that enriched each bite. Customizable seasonings were a nice touch, although the pizza's tendency to cool quickly did detract from the experience, as the congealing cheese and sauce lost their allure.

Title: A Taste of Spain in NYC's Hudson Yards: My Evening at José Andrés' Latest Venture

Having a penchant for Spanish cuisine and an admiration for José Andrés' culinary exploits in D.C., I found myself eagerly exploring his new gastronomic playground at Hudson Yards. Upon arrival, I was relieved to find it bustling yet comfortably uncrowded. My culinary journey commenced at the patatas bravas station, where the dish delighted with its crispy potatoes and tastefully seasoned aioli.

Venturing further, I sampled the Paella Valencia from Leña. At $17 a scoop, the lackluster flavors failed to justify the price, leaving me yearning for more zest in every bite. However, redemption came at "Bar Celona," a tapas bar where the Olive bite dazzled the palate, although the croquettes and calamari slightly missed the mark. The shrimp tapas, with its enticing garlic sauce, did not disappoint.

Complementing the evening was a refreshing Parrón of Spanish beer and lime soda, one of the many authentic drinks on offer. While the experience didn't entirely transport me back to the streets of Barcelona, it was an enjoyable endeavor into Spanish fare, with the caveat of NYC's premium pricing. I'm reserving my full judgment for a later date, after the entire venue is operational. Until then, whether it's for a sip, a bite, or a dose of culinary curiosity, I'd say it's an experience worth dipping into.

Title: A Fusion Feast at an Unforgettable Happy Hour

I recently dined at an exquisite Cuban-Chinese restaurant on the suggestion of a local friend, who's an enthusiast of their happy hour offerings. Unlike typical establishments offering separate menus for each cuisine, this gem intriguingly melds Cuban and Chinese fare to create an innovative dining experience that's a delight for seafood and rice lovers.

The standout dish for me was a remarkable take on paella, teeming with mussels, clams, calamari, shrimp, and tantalizing black rice. Beyond the food, the service shone brightly; the attentive staff ensured our glasses were never empty and our needs promptly met.

Be prepared for a bustling vibe as happy hour winds down, but embracing the spirited atmosphere is part of the charm. It's clearly a hotspot for good reason—superb food, great deals, and an ambiance that beckons you to linger long after your plate is clean.

I recently visited a quaint little gem of a restaurant that truly requires a reservation due to its size - a tip I thankfully came upon after reading reviews. My foresight paid off when a large group arrived right after us and couldn't be accommodated. My party of four cozied up in the tight but charming space.

We started with the mussels in a garlic and wine sauce, accompanied by the obligatory fries. While tasty, I will say I've experienced more flavorful renditions elsewhere. However, the star of the night was the rainbow trout served over a butternut squash risotto. It was a dish to remember; perfectly cooked and seasoned, it captured my taste buds and has my highest recommendation.

This spot offers an authentic Parisian vibe that's hard to come by. I'd definitely suggest giving it a try for those in search of a little piece of Paris in the city.

If you write a whole essay about how sexy you are, it's a Vain-essay.But this is not that. Although I've written some of those.One of many amazing dumpling houses in Chinatown, as I can now count 5 which I really like, and will get around to reviewing all of them eventually - but I'll be coming back here regularly and Honda was absolutely right with his amazing review.

Have you been looking for a good happy hour? Look no further because this place is the spot for all your HH needs! Located in Flatiron and a very short distanced walk from the train is this neat dine in restaurant. HH is from 4 PM - 7 PM which is pretty long compared to what we have in Chicago. They had $1 oysters & neck clams, $6 drafts, $9 cocktails and a bunch of other HH hour deals to choose from. Never have I ever experienced neck clams shucked as how they shuck oysters so we had to really give it a try. Got a dozen oysters & a dozen neck clams. Was so good that we went for a second round of 1/2 dozen oysters & 1/2 dozen neck clams. The service was good and he was quite attentive. My boyfriend ordered a draft which was flat and he was generous to get him a  new one.

I had to try their Abura soba as I'm a big fan of it ever since I used to live in Japan (3 star, 8/10/2019). I must say theirs is okay, very different from what I'd expect from "abura soba" in general. It is popular in Tokyo and Yokohama. Each noodle shop has their own source/style like zhajiang noodle. My understanding is that you add chili oil and vinegar, and mix with their original sauce at the bottom of the bowl as soon as it is served. In Ramen-Ya, it is not like that. Well, it was disappointing.... I must mention though their dumplings are all good. I've never really come across tomato dumplings outside of Beijing, China. They do good job here. We also tried Cold Beef Noodle which used the similar sauce to Hiyashi Chuka... wish it were as creative as their dumplings. I'd like to try Ramen Lab sometime for abura soba, which happened to be closed today.

A great place to hang with friends for brunch or to drop in at night simply for a pint or two.  Dark and inviting is their bar; while bright and loud is their restaurant.  Impeccable is the service at the bar; while friendly yet slow is the service for meals.  On this particular seating, light was their "Bloody Mary";  beautifully prepared was my medium rare "JWF Burger with Stilton Cheese"; okay fries; disappointing over-baked "Pop-over"; and, as always, stellar was their "Sticky Toffee Pudding".CHEERS!

Came here for brunch and it was honestly just okay. Upon entering the restaurant, nobody greeted us and we just waited awkwardly for few minutes until someone finally took us in. I believe he was the owner--very friendly! For appetizers, I got Lump Crab Cakes ($16) and my friend got Shrimp Cocktail ($15). Both were delicious and needless to say, this saved our whole meal. For entrees, we both got the seafood salad ($22) and it was honestly so disappointing. It was bland and definitely needed some improvement. We both couldn't finish it. Overall, service was friendly, appetizers were amazing, ambiance is cozy. Even though the salad was a miss, I do want to give this place another chance and order something different. Will update soon.

I recently visited a pizza spot in Manhattan and was thoroughly impressed by the flavorful pizza offered at a reasonable price – a rare find in the area. The service was commendable; attentive and efficient without being overbearing. The location of the restaurant is also convenient, making it a must-visit for any pizza aficionado in the city. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a delightful pizza experience without breaking the bank.

Title: A Mixed Bag Brunch Spot with Perks in LES

My initial visit to this popular brunch destination was a mixed bag. The promise of reservations is a draw in this bustling spot, yet our reservation at 12:30 led to actual seating at 1 PM and meals served at 1:30 PM, prompting the question of the reservation's effectiveness. Despite the delayed service, the staff's gracious gesture of comping our pancakes and apologetic demeanor earned points, smoothing over the extended wait.

The restaurant itself is a tad cramped, which could be an issue for some, but it was a minor inconvenience for us. The lamb neck hash I ordered was flavorful and well-seasoned, though I would have preferred a more generous meat portion compared to the bread. The shared banana buttermilk pancakes were a highlight and lived up to my expectations.

While not without its flaws, the locale is unbeatable for a leisurely Sunday in Lower East Side, offering plenty to do post-brunch. Their openness to reservations will likely bring me back for a second chance, hoping for a more timely dining experience. For now, I'm leaving it at a solid 3 stars.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise on a Monday Evening

I stopped by for dinner at this charming eatery on a Monday night and was greeted by a warm ambiance accentuated by pristine white tablecloths – a nice touch that elevated the experience. Despite my casual attire, I felt perfectly at ease in the welcoming environment.

Service here is attentive; it's almost as if you have a personal team of waiters ensuring your meal goes smoothly. There was a small hiccup with my beer order as I received the wrong brew, but the staff was quick to offer a replacement. However, my glass was noticeably dirty, which was promptly addressed upon request.

The main course, chicken piccata, was a delight, although I was surprised by the addition of red sauce on my spaghetti side – I would have preferred a heads-up on that. On the other hand, my mom's filet Marsala was a hit, thoroughly enjoyed and complimented.

Despite the minor issues, the overall experience has sealed my decision – I'm definitely revisiting this spot in the future.

Upon entering the restaurant, the immediate seating due to the lack of crowds should have been a warning sign, but I optimistically attributed it to the holiday season. Unfortunately, my go-to dish, the har gow, fell short of expectations, lacking the garlic punch I so enjoy. The lotus leaf-wrapped sticky rice was disappointing, with an unusual hardness not typically encountered at other establishments known for their perfectly cooked, soft texture. The chicken feet did not escape critique either, needing more cooking time to reach the desired tenderness and a lighter hand with the food coloring. The meal's saving grace, however, was the char siu steamed bun, which was the only item that met my standards.

I went there during restaurant week and I was impressed with the service and the food. Food:For starters, I had an oven-roasted beetroot salad. It is a cold salad and a sweet one. It had a nice balance from the vegetables to the vinaigrette. Sweet in flavors since the beets were roasted. For the main entree, I order the flat iron steak as medium rare and it was cooked to perfection. It was served with bacon cheddar mash potatoes and Kentucky bourbon veal demi-glace. The demi-glace was delicious and went well with the steak. The mash potatoes were on a little salty end for my tasting but overall the meal was delicious. The steak was roughly 8 oz which was plenty. For the dessert, I had a panna cotta that was nice and light. It had a blueberry compote to it that was just the right amount to the panna cotta and a ginger snap cookie. It was like a light cheesecake in my view, sweet and airy. ServiceOur server and everyone there was amazing. Very attentive to detail and we never had our water run dry. My friend and I were coming from another restaurant that couldn't serve our needs and come to a place that viewed us as a valuable customer it was a delight. We did come on a slow day and time.OverallEverything was just to perfection. I would come back, especially for their steaks. Some of the sides were salty for my liking but I usually don't like a lot of salt in my food in general, so this is a personal preference. The steak was cook to perfection and amazing service especially for a busy area in NYC.

When the weather turns warm and you want to eat outside, Pers Soho is the spot. Lots of great Turkish Mezze and other shareable dishes makes it a wonderful choice for groups large and small. Since they have an enclosed corner location, you are eating outside but not right on the sidewalk. The cocktails and wine selection are great too. Service is always good as well. Only complaint, the hummus is too dry.

Last night's dinner at Gato was a delightful experience. My boyfriend, daughter, and I were seated promptly at a cozy table and attended by a superb waitress who expertly navigated us through the menu. The octopus stood out, tender and flavorful—a definite must-try. The Brussels sprouts, enhanced with pomegranate seeds, were perfectly cooked and packed with flavor. The mussels were served in an irresistibly savory sauce, while the grilled shrimp, although slightly spicy for my taste, were satisfying. The veggie paella did not disappoint either. Dessert was the only course that didn't quite hit the mark, being good but not exceptional. Gato earns a well-deserved 4.5 stars from us.

Title: Quaint Contradictions at a Rustic Hideaway

My recent dining experience at this charming, rustic establishment came with a side of mixed feelings. The restaurant's outdoor patio promised summer bliss, a detail that didn't go unnoticed during our quiet visit. The serendipity of an empty venue was a welcome backdrop for my casual Nirvana tee attire.

The cuisine, while light and easy on the stomach, seemed to lack a certain culinary finesse, leaving me contemplating the potential of a more refined menu. Service paralleled with the food—unremarkable and forgettable. Even the ambiance that evening felt diluted, reminiscent of our less-than-robust lentil soup.

In all honesty, the visit was acceptable without hitting any high notes. A return might be up for debate, but thanks to my girlfriend's generosity in picking up the tab, the experience was spared from a scathing critique. A quaint spot, yes, but it might not see us at its tables again.

Title: Thai Spicy Satisfaction at Charm Thai

I recently decided to satisfy my Thai food cravings with Charm Thai via UberEats. Opting for the Pad Thai, I eagerly awaited its arrival, and Charm Thai didn't disappoint. Within 30 minutes, I was unveiling a dish with notably generous chicken portions – a welcome departure from the all-too-common scrimping on quality meat.

But the true test? The spiciness. Charm Thai nailed the 'Thai spicy' level I requested – a fiery delight that left my taste buds dancing. Impressively, the serving size was ample enough to provide two satisfying meals out of one order- a boon to both appetite and wallet.

Efficiency in delivery paired with exceptional flavor execution means Charm Thai has earned my repeat business. When the next Thai spice craving hits, I know who I'll be calling. Kudos, Charm Thai!

This NYC gem is a testament to the city's culinary prowess, nestled down a charming small staircase. It's a place where dreams are served steamed or fried in the form of the most delectable dumplings you can imagine. But let's talk about the Pad Thai – a dish so flawlessly executed, it sets a new standard. This may very well be your first encounter with what Pad Thai is meant to be. A visit here is a palate-awakening experience not to be missed.

Loved the branzino (cooked absolutely perfectly), the steak and the French fries. Be sure to ask for hot sauce on the side. As for ambiance, it was a little loud for my taste but the food was otherwise good and the service amazing. Loved our waiter, who was super friendly, helpful and attentive.

Title: A Quick Bite at Wah Fung No 1 Fast Food

Wah Fung No 1 Fast Food lives up to its reputation for drawing a crowd with its wallet-friendly menu. Prompted by a recommendation from my husband's boss, we braved the heat and joined the line of eager patrons. Be prepared for a cash-only experience and an alfresco dining setting across the street in the park, as there's no seating inside.

We dove into the highly acclaimed duck rice. Served in generous portions, the meal was piping hot, though the rice proved to be an overwhelming ratio to the protein. The duck itself was quite fatty, which might not suit everyone's taste; I personally favor a leaner cut. Despite this, it was a worthwhile visit to this NYC fast-food staple. A little tip: know what you want before stepping up to order—it’ll make the experience smoother for you and the busy staff.

Came with a group of 9 people around 1pm on a Wednesday, the main dining area was full but they were able to get us all seated quickly in the hallway in 2 tables. They were very accommodating in letting us put a 5th chair on a 4 person table but unfortunately the 5th chair stuck out into the hall and kept getting run into by servers and customers walking in and out. The real winner dishes were our appetizers - an amazing pesto cauliflower dish served with pine nuts olive oil and hummus and the grilled eggplant and garlic aioli. We all agreed they were much better than any of the mains. The few mains we did have - $12 avocado toast, Lox and Creme Fraiche sandwich were good but not spectacular, although my cousin did enjoy his banana french toast! Kirsh is a pleasant place to eat a meal, and if you can stomach upper west side prices, you will find the food and the experiance to be high quality!

Barn Joo Union Square effortlessly tops my list for laid-back gatherings, whether it's for happy hour delights or a full meal. The space is amply sized, making it a prime spot for hosting groups with a penchant for diverse finger foods—from savory truffle fries and economical $1 oysters to crispy croquettes and zesty chicken wings. Their tiger roll is not to be missed either.

The happy hour deals extend to a variety of beers, wines, and cocktails, ensuring everyone in your party finds their perfect sip. Additionally, for Korean BBQ aficionados, the option to grill at your table is a fun twist that saves you a trip to K-town.

Brunch here with friends has been a refreshing change from the usual dinner routine, and I've yet to be disappointed. The service remains commendable even when the place is buzzing, although you might need to grab their attention once in a while. No matter the occasion, Barn Joo promises a good time with good food.

If you're in a hurry to penn station, I guess you could stop here? Actually, I think there's better pizza inside penn station from what I remember. $3.21 for an oversized mess of a slice. The moment I picked the cheese slice up, the whole thing caved. The middle of the slice had a soggy crust that couldn't hold any weight and the back of the slice had a sawpaper type crust that hurts the roof of your mouth. The slide is large and has a lot of cheese on it but the sauce was overly sweet. Decor isn't great either but at least the table tops were clean. What adds to the miserable experience was the fact the there is a huge heat fan blowing into the middle of the room and will blow your napkins and plates off the table. I really see no reason to come back here.

Wonderful place right in the middle of the theaters district right next to Frozen in a very busy area. It doesn't have a big store front so you might miss it just walking by. But surprisingly this little time square Chinese restraint is amazingly authentic Chinese food. Got here at 6:30pm was not too busy. Good place for pre-theater fix.Old fashion fish: unlike the fish fillet you have in all the other places, this is their signature. Whole fish with head on really fresh, if you don't mind the big bones, they chop the fishes to pieces instead of thin sliced without bone, the sauce is really amazing, not super spicy but with a lot of wine flavor soaked in the fish. Really unique taste for my liking, will come back just for this. Cumin lamb: very tender and great flavor, it might be a bit salty for my taste but the lamb is very fresh.Peking duck: it's very crispy skin, only thing needs improvement is that the meat kinda fell apart the way they cut it. But I guess I ordered the wrong dish in a sichuan restaurant. There are so many more dishes are really appealing that I didn't get to try, will definitely come back for more. They also have a second floor to accommodate bigger group. Full bar as well even just stop for a drink, very decent price for draft beer $7 and other wine and liquor

I had high expectations for this restaurant, especially with my boyfriend singing its praises. Unfortunately, my experience was underwhelming. The big chicken plate, usually a favorite of mine, was disappointingly salty and quickly became monotonous. While the texture of the noodles in the signature Lanzhou beef noodle dish was spot on, the sauce lacked the familiar flavor I was hoping for. The lamb skewers were passable, yet forgettable.

I was particularly let down by the beef noodle. The noodles themselves were too chewy, as if undercooked, and the beef had a gamey aftertaste that put me off. For dessert, the yogurt was mediocre and the rice porridge lacked depth, reminiscent of an uninspired egg drop soup with a hint of rice wine.

Despite my lackluster experience, my boyfriend maintains his fondness for the restaurant. It seems that taste really is a matter of personal preference.

Update: I was contacted by Jayson Portman in guest services and offered an apology due to a bad experience at this location. I was assured that the lack of training at this location would be corrected and I was given a gift card and asked to give them another chance after the staff was retrained.We did and I must say Jayson, You hit a home run like the other locations I have been to. Thank you again for being a great company and actually caring and taking the time to respond to your loyal customers and hearing their issues and resolving them with the utmost care and love that never goes unappreciated and that all restaurants should strive to be like.I look forward to coming back again and again.Thank you!

After checking the options on mealapp, I was craving a burger and where else do you go for a burger but Blue Smoke.  On the menu is Blue Smoke Burger with BBQ Chips.I picked an early pick up time.  Walked in the restaurant.  The QR code placard was visible and didn't need to go looking for it.  The food was packaged and ready to go  I scanned the information, showed the confirmation and was out the in less than 2 minutes.The restaurant employees were thoughtful to include a wet nap.  How can eating a burger be messy -- I can give you all the examples but let's not go there.  Let's talk burger -- it was juicy and perfect with lettuce and -- it totally satisfied my craving!  My only small complaint was with the chips.  Since some chips were under the burger it became soft and not crispy. Other than that, everything was perfect - Thank you so much.Definitely come here if you want some good burger and pit meat.

Title: Warm Delights at Koku – A Noodle Lover’s Haven

It’s official – I’m head over heels for Koku. There’s a unique pleasure in savoring a steaming bowl of broth and perfectly cooked noodles during the frosty season, and Koku knows this art well. My experiences, both dine-in with comrades and takeout, have been consistently top-notch.

The ramen here is a showstopper; the broths are sumptuously rich, brimming with flavor. I've slurped up their Koku and shoyu ramens and both left a memorable impression. A side mention goes to the crispy pig ears – an adventurous and delicious choice. I’m eager to dive deeper into their appetizers on my next visits.

A word to the wise: the space is cozy and gets busy, yet the turnover is swift, so worries of lengthy waits can be dispelled.

In summary, Koku offers a delectable escape, perfect for noodle enthusiasts looking to indulge in a warm culinary embrace.

1/2 price bottles of wine on Mondays - 4pm to closethey have a happy hour menu, but I couldn't find it when I wentbottomless brunch option: $25 for 2 hours Takes reservations: +70% of the party needs to be present in order to be seated I came here for a birthday party dinner and was impressed by the food, portion size, and service. The table ordered a bunch of appetizers to share, my favorite being the roasted brussel sprouts. For the main entree I had the mussels and was happy with my selection. If you have 4-6 people you can request to have your party seated in the "street taco" van that is located on the second floor. It provides semi-closed off dining experience. Overall, I'm a fan, and will be back.

Have you ever heard of "middleterranean" cuisine? Well neither have I, but that's apparently what Taboonette serves, and the food is simply delightful! This casual, counter-service restaurant features Israeli-inspired cuisine, but it is by no means traditional (after all, where else would you find pulled pork at an Israeli restaurant?). I started with the sweet potato falafel in pita, and these orange-colored chickpea fritters were paired with an arugula-herb salad and tzatziki sauce spread on the insides of the bread. Overall, this pita sandwich fell a bit short for me, as the thin, supermarket pita was served cold, and none of the components were particularly outstanding either. The sandwich was served with za'atar-seasoned homemade potato chips on the side, which were crispy, but didn't really have much za'atar flavor at all.Next, however, I had the lamb kebab pan, which was a homerun through and through! On a stainless steel skillet came a serving of chewy, nutty brown rice topped with crushed tomatoes, some of the most creamy, smokey crushed grilled eggplant, refreshing Israeli salad (chopped cucumber and tomato), and some of the best lamb kebabs I've ever had! These perfectly round meatballs made of gamey ground lamb were crusty on the outside, tender and pink on the inside, and were full of spices and fresh herbs! And one of the best parts of the dish that really brought the whole thing together was a huge dollop of light, creamy tahina sauce that added an unctuousness to the meat, vegetables, and rice! On the side came a spicy green sauce (zhoug), which added a nice kick that went especially well with the meat! Finally, I couldn't help but order a side of the hummus, which was made with lots of tehina and was super creamy as a result!Taboonette might be one of the best casual "middleterranean" restaurants I've tried, and their beautifully-plated, amazingly flavorful pans are the thing to get! This is the type of place I could imagine myself coming to over and over again to sample their variety of healthy, globally-inspired flavors, which are all brought back and fused together with the distinguishing features of Israeli food!

Upon my recent visit to this much-talked-about eatery, the experience fell flat compared to the buzz that surrounds it. My mother and I decided to share the smashed avocado toast and the triple berry French toast. Disappointingly, the avocado toast was far from remarkable; the generous smear of avocado lacked the necessary zest, crying out for a splash of lemon, a pinch of salt, or a dusting of spice to bring it to life. The accompanying bread, while fresh, was unremarkable.

Moving on to the triple berry French toast, it seemed that the syrup was the sole savior of this otherwise uninspiring dish. The rich, mapley goodness could not mask the fact that the French toast itself was forgettable in flavor.

A surprising delight, however, was the espresso, which proved to be the highlight of our morning—rich and perfectly brewed, leaving us wanting more.

The service was perfunctory, and while we were seated promptly, there was nothing particularly noteworthy about the experience. Considering the steep prices—$17 for avocado toast with an added egg and $14 for the French toast—one expects a meal that dazzles, which this, unfortunately, did not. While the menu may boast health-conscious fare, the lack of flavor makes it difficult to justify the cost, particularly when other establishments offer healthier, tastier options at similar or better value.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this local pizzeria and must say, I was blown away by the quality of their pizza. In my experience, it stands as the best I've ever had. One notable highlight is the sauce – it strikes the perfect balance, steering clear of the all-too-common sweetness found elsewhere.
