The crust deserves special mention too; it was the epitome of perfection — fluffy and soft, contributing to an overall amazing taste. If you're a pizza aficionado, this place is a must-visit.

Absolutely a great experience. Friendly staff and delicious food. The weird thing is that I wanted to have some of the little pizzas they gave out during happy hour, and they said "no, that just for happy hour." But if a customer is asking for something, you should just give it to them. Break your rules! My pasta dish with eggplant and tomorrow's and pesto was delicious! The Branzino was awesome. It came in a parchment pouch and was filled with delicious vegetables olives, almost a puttanesca. The vibe was friendly and summery and the window in the front overlooks the hustle and bustle of Bleecker street. A totally great dining experience! I would have given it four stars but the "no pizza for you" thing killed it. :o

I had breakfast with my daughter because we were staying across the street. Eh, nothing spectacular. We saw our server one time, when he took our order. It was difficult to get a refill or ask for the bill. The food was good. Avocado toast was yum, pancakes with blueberry/ricotta were delicious. French toast was good, sirloin/eggs was a good portion. I just wouldn't return, ever. Service was less than mediocre.

Great ramen shop in downtown NYC. Great selection of appetizers you don't usually find at a standard ramen place. The beef tongue is seared nicely and the Japanese fried chicken is scrumptiously tender and crispy. The octopus sashimi has a great texture and a citrusy kick to it.Ordered the spicy miso ramen. Great balance of chilli and umami flavours. The noodles were a little over cooked but not soggy. Also had the plum wine to drink, which was sweet and refreshing! Very prompt service! The vibe from the staff can feel a little rushed as they move people in and out as quickly as possible. Solid spot overall!

Title: A Flavorful Fiesta That's Worth the Wait

If you're searching for a lively spot with exceptional food and service, look no further. This restaurant is a Friday night gem, perfect for groups seeking vibrant energy and delectable bites. The wait is a small price to pay for the culinary experience that awaits.

Upon visiting with three friends, we indulged in the mouthwatering pitchers of guava margaritas – a unanimous table favorite. To kickstart our feast, we savored the guacamole and chips paired with tantalizing salsa. Both delivered a punch of classic flavor enhanced by an extra kick that left us wanting more.

For the main course, we dived into an assortment of tacos – al pastor, pescado, brisket, and Piccadillo. Each one was a testament to the kitchen's prowess, but the al pastor tacos stole the spotlight. Alongside were the shrimp tamale and shrimp tostado, both exquisitely prepared. Every dish was a hit, cementing this restaurant as a must-visit for any food lover.

Title: A Mixed Experience at Mad Dog on a Serene Wednesday Evening

I ventured to Mad Dog on a beautiful Wednesday night, enticed by the allure of outdoor seating. It holds the unique position of being the sole Mexican cuisine option in the region. Snagging a table was a breeze, but I was slightly disappointed by the lack of happy hour specials or complimentary chips and salsa – a common Downtown Manhattan gripe.

Opting for a Blackberry Margarita ($14) and a Pineapple Avocado Salad ($13), the prices felt steep, yet not out of the ordinary for the area. The margarita, however, left something to be desired with its overpowering artificial taste that didn't quite mesh with the tequila. The salad was more of a hit, with the grilled pineapple adding a delightful sweetness that lifted the otherwise average greens, especially when drizzled with the accompanying sauce.

Service was a high point, impressively efficient given the dual demand of indoor and outdoor diners. While the experience was adequate for the occasional evening drink, the premium prices would deter me from becoming a regular at Mad Dog.

This place always seems to have a crowd. It was crowded when I came in as well, but because I came alone, they were able to find a seat for me quickly.I ordered a few things but was not particularly wow'ed by anything. I've had pierogi before, but nothing about Veselka's seemed any different. One thing they had were fried pierogi, which was good overall but some parts were a little tough. I like the generous portion of sour cream and onions.The servers were nice but rushed probably because it was so busy.Perhaps some other things on the menu are good, but my meal and experience was average so I'm not in a rush to come back.

I recently visited a charming restaurant that truly impressed with its excellent service and pristine ambience. The space was open and bright, creating a welcoming atmosphere. During my brief visit, I indulged in their lattes and Irish coffee, both of which were expertly prepared and delicious. Although I didn't have the opportunity to try their food, the experience left me eager to return for brunch. Highly recommended for a coffee stop, and I'm looking forward to sampling their full menu soon.

My sister and I were near the hospital and needed to grab some lunch.  We happened upon Tung Thong. My sister introduced me to the green papaya salad which was really good.  I had the Yellow Curry and my Sister had the Red Curry.  It was some of the best Thai food that I have had.  The service was great and the price was reasonable.  I would definitely go back in a heartbeat.

Title: A Delectable Lunch with Stellar Service

My lunch experience at this restaurant was nothing short of exceptional. The restaurant week menu offered an enticing range of options, and the complimentary appetizers—a delightful surprise—set the tone for the meal. The freshly cut cheese and homemade bruschetta were particularly impressive.

For my meal, I indulged in the meatballs appetizer and the lamb ragu as the main course. Each dish arrived perfectly paired with a wine that complemented the flavors wonderfully, demonstrating the thoughtfulness behind the menu. The portions were generous, ensuring a satisfying experience.

The service shone brightly too; it was fast, friendly, and attentive, ensuring a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience from start to finish. The restaurant's commitment to exceptional hospitality was clear.

This restaurant has earned my high recommendation and I eagerly anticipate my next visit.

I absolutely adore this ramen hotspot! From the energetic greeting to the rapid service, the vibe is infectious from the moment you step in. Their menu boasts an array of delectable starters—truffle fries, pork buns, and wings are all a hit in my book. But the star of the show is undoubtedly the ramen; I'm a huge fan of their spicy pork option which never disappoints with its expertly cooked noodles and flavorful broth. The quick turnaround is a bonus, ideal for a delicious meal under an hour. I've been here five times and counting, and I highly recommend giving their seasonal specials a try. Trust me, you won't regret it!

This is a review of the brunch menu, which I didn't realize at the time is completely different from their normal dinner menu. Honestly, I was disappointed that I didn't have the chance to try their famous cheeseburger or wings. I was nevertheless overall pleased with what I ate for brunch with my friends early on a Saturday afternoon.We first tried the honey butter tater tots while waiting for some friends who were running late. They were really addictive and unlike anything I've ever had before. The creamy tanginess of the labneh paired surprisingly well with the sweetness of the honey. We ended up getting another order when my friends finally came! For my main, I had the fried chicken sandwich which I thoroughly enjoyed. It featured a huge piece of chicken which was perfectly fried -- crispy on the outside, moist on the inside, and nicely seasoned. Definitely filling.A few of my friends ordered the beef & eggs over rice. It's an elevated "chef-y" version of the NYC favorite street food classic chicken over rice. It's beautifully plated. However, the beef and eggs were essentially scrambled eggs with small pieces of beef mixed in. We would have enjoyed the dish more with larger chunks of beef, especially given the $18 price point. All of the staff members were friendly and attentive. Ambiance wise, this is a very hip and trendy restaurant. Make sure to check out the bathroom for an awesome surprise!Overall, I enjoyed the Korean fusion play on American favorites although it's a little expensive for what you get. I definitely plan on coming back to try the burger and wings.

Cafe Clover seems to be a bustling brunch spot on a Sunday early afternoon. I definitely recommend making a reservation (on Opentable!). We had a large group reservation for birthday brunch and it was a doozy. The restaurant is pretty loud and noisy but we were able to still make conversation if we yelled (just kidding but we did have to enunciate and talk with purpose).We ordered a couple of the lavender waffles, which is topped with honeyed ricotta. It was pretty tasty, but nothing as great as I had hoped it would be. Went well with a cup of coffee. I ordered the poached farm eggs, which was not super insta-worthy but pretty tasty. It was simple. Perfectly poached eggs topped with some hollandaise sauce atop two small spaghetti squash latkes and smoked salmon and avocado with a side of lightly dressed kale and and a grilled tomato. It seemed very healthy, which I appreciated. It was super simple that paying $17 for it seemed a little odd. I would have liked a little more hollandaise and a little more finesse but it was fine! I wasn't full afterward, but content. Definitely a lighter breakfast option!Overall, service was great. We were celebrating a birthday and they were helpful in bringing out plates and the dessert we brought. Food-wise, everything was just ok.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Local "Ramen Mecca"

I've visited this much-talked-about dining spot multiple times, trying to grasp the fervor surrounding its offerings. On my recent visit, we sampled the okonomiyaki, karaage, and an assortment of ramens, including the ichiraku (my pick due to a preference against pork broth). The okonomiyaki was mediocre—noodle-laden and drenched in a dominating dark sauce. However, the karaage was a standout, possibly the best I've encountered, boasting a perfect fry and a burst of flavor.

Sadly, the ramens didn't impress. Overly salty, even the dashi-based ichiraku didn't pass muster, tasting like a salty concoction of water, soy, and disappointment. While my companions didn't seem to mind, my sensitivity to salt left me unsatisfied, especially given the restaurant's lofty status in the ramen world.

Financially, the meal wasn't light—two appetizers, three ramens, drinks including whiskey, chardonnay, and sake totaled $165 before tip. On a side note, the chardonnay was particularly lackluster, too sweet and of noticeably low quality.

Service-wise, it was almost impeccable. Attentive and responsive, especially with my need for copious amounts of water to counteract the salt. Even as the evening rush picked up and we felt a nudge towards the exit, the service remained top-notch.

The ambiance matched the quality of service—cool, modern, with a hip open-concept and communal seating. The sole inconvenience was the long trek to the restroom.

Rating: 
Food: 2/5
Service: 4/5
Ambiance: 4/5

Title: A Glimpse of Culinary Excellence at a Bustling Eatery

Upon visiting this establishment with a 4.5-star reputation, I instantly grasped why it's so beloved. Despite the throng, the vibe remained upbeat and the open kitchen added a genuine touch, showcasing the culinary team in action.

Service was on point—attentive without being intrusive, exactly what you need in a vibrant dining environment.

The array of dishes Peter and I sampled did not disappoint. Every morsel was a delight, but the standout had to be the salted egg yolk prawn—generous in both portion and flavor, reminiscent of the fare at Singapore's famed hawker markets. The popcorn chicken was a definitive winner, outshining its local rivals.

Other noteworthy plates included the savory tofu with thousand year egg, the comforting chicken noodle soup, and the substantial pork knuckle noodles.

While the location may require a bit of a trek, it's one I'm eager to undertake again. As for authenticity, it strikes a balance, offering genuine tastes with slight adjustments—take the Panama cotta, for instance, an unexpected hit.

In summary, this dining spot not only lives up to its high ratings but surpasses expectations with its excellent food and ambiance.

I recently visited a delightful brunch spot that truly impressed me. The food was as beautiful as it was delicious—every dish we tried was outstanding. The service only added to the experience, being attentive and efficient. The value set offered great bang for the buck, making our brunch not only enjoyable but also affordable. Conveniently located, the restaurant was easy to find, which was a plus. All in all, it was a wonderful time, and I'd wholeheartedly recommend this place for anyone looking for a lovely brunch experience. We absolutely loved it!

Ordered the lunch special. $10 for spicy string bean with minced pork, fried rice and hot&sour soup. Food was ready in less than 10 minutes and was so good! I asked for spicy and they did not disappoint. Food was really good, great price and made quickly. What more could you ask for?!

Of the pizza places I tried (Bleeker Street and Artichoke Basille), this was definitely my FAVE!!! They have both square and normal pizza slices. Known best for their pepperoni squares and I would definitely recommend the same. This is a must visit if you go to New York! *They accept credit cards*PEPPERONI SQUARE: This was SO GOOD! Definitely on the oily side, but we didn't come here for healthy eats right?! haha Their pepperoni is so unique-smaller, thicker, and flavorful than an average pepperoni. Would definitely come back just for this again!!!LAYOUT: There is no seating. This is definitely a grab and go place as they sell pizza by the slices and wholes (call ahead preferably). They do offer a bar-top along one of their walls, but not a single chair there haha. If taking your order to go, let them know and they will pack it in a box. If not, they can place your pizzas on paper plates. Some people just stand outside or sit on the sidewalk benches even to eat the pizza.*NOTE: Bummer they don't have to-go pepper and cheese packets, so load up using the shakers that are on the bar top.

Came here tonight for a friend's birthday with a party of 13. Service and decor/lighting was great! Happy hour prices were really affordable. Food was good, oysters were fresh and tasty. Fried shrimp appetizer was super delicious and onion rings were big and crispy. Our waiter made sure our glasses were filled and informed us whenn the kitchen was backed up. I got the pappardelle and it was really tasty, the Korean short rib beef on the pasta was very tender and moist. I thought there would be more than one egg as the menu suggested. My friend said the paella was good but another didn't like the bucatini as much. Overall, left pretty satisfied and full.

Title: Another Fabulous Girls' Night at B&L

Once again, B&L did not fail to impress us during our regular girls' night gathering. The entire staff, from the floor manager to the hostess, shone with their usual blend of friendliness and professionalism, swiftly accommodating our seating needs. This visit, Kevin, our waiter, was exceptional — his service was impeccable, and his recommendation to try the White Sangria was spot-on. Delightfully refreshing, the sangria has quickly become our new signature drink for future outings. It's a shame we didn't capture a photo of our beverages, but that's all the more reason to come back. B&L, please ensure the White Sangria remains a staple on your drink menu!

Title: A Carnivore's Delight at Our Favorite Brazilian Steakhouse

My partner and I, in pursuit of a post-Valentine's celebration, revisited our beloved Brazilian steakhouse for Saturday brunch, which proved to be a sublime choice. As regulars, the familiarity of being ushered promptly to a cozy corner table by Italo, our cordial server, was comforting.

Opting to browse the salad bar, a prelude to our meat feast, I found myself indulging in an array of cured meats, cheeses, and notably, the irresistible brown sugar and black pepper bacon – a new favorite that tested my self-restraint.

However, it's the array of succulent Brazilian steaks that stars in this culinary show. The Picanha continues to reign supreme in my heart, with the filet mignon, bottom sirloin, and pork sausage following closely in merit.

Accompaniments arrived – Brazilian cheese bread, mashed potatoes, and fried bananas – although I bypassed the carbs in anticipation of the main event. A diet version of a Brazilian soda was a surprisingly pleasant companion to our meal, sans alcohol.

Concluding the affair, this gastronomic haven delivered once more, providing not just an extraordinary dining experience but also aligning with our wellness goals – I even shed a pound the next day! Tucked beside MOMA, it's an ideal spot for museum-goers to wrap up a day of cultural immersion with a stellar meal. Without a doubt, we'll return.

Good dim sum place in Murray Hill - nothing too special but there's also not a lot of options for dim sum in the area. The prices are higher than what I'd typically expect for dim sum. I'd say the prices are close to Tim Ho Wan, but without the Michelin star or the acclaim. $8 for 4 pork soup dumplings, $7 for the 3 Hello Kitty Buns (2 inches wide ea), $3 per pork bun, and $7 for the BBQ pork rice roll. Everything was good but not exceptional. The soup dumplings didn't have much soup inside, and the buns had a mediocre (slightly soggy) texture. Then again, I also don't expect dim sum to travel particularly well for take out. I originally had 2 Matcha Buns in my order, and since they didn't have those available they replaced it with 2 pork buns without asking me. When I called back about the incorrect order, they were very nice and offered to credit me back the cost for the Matcha Buns.

Title: Cozy Spot with Hearty Portions and Attentive Service

I recently visited a charming little restaurant tucked away on Pell Street for lunch, enticed by a friend's recommendation. The place exudes warmth and has a pricing scheme that's easy on the wallet, offering decently sized portions.

My meal was the Combo A, which included a quarter baked chicken, satisfyingly paired with yellow rice, black beans, and a side salad—a filling combo that hit the spot. My friend and I indulged in shared sides of fried Brussels sprouts and mac n cheese, both of which were served promptly and piping hot—a testament to the kitchen's efficiency.

The service was exemplary; the staff was on the ball, ensuring our experience was without fault. The food, I'd rate a solid 4 out of 5, with everything well-prepared, though the mac and cheese could do with a bit more zest—it was somewhat bland and needed a dash of salt and pepper to enhance it. A side of maduros came with an unexpected sprinkle of cinnamon and sugar, a twist I personally could have passed on.

The restaurant space is apt for small groups, offering a cozy vibe without feeling crowded. To add, they have a pleasing selection of craft beers which complement the meal nicely, and the interior decor contributes to the overall nice atmosphere.

In summary, while there's a bit of room for improvement in the flavor department, the overall experience was delightful. I'm eager to return and explore more of the menu.

Title: A Little Gem for Russian Cuisine

I recently discovered a delightful little spot for Russian food that truly deserves a shout-out. Despite its small size, this restaurant impressed me with its exceptional service and positive atmosphere. As someone craving a hearty Russian meal after a long day, their offerings hit the spot—tasty and satisfying. It's an excellent find for anyone looking to grab some top-notch food to go. Major respect to this establishment for revitalizing my spirits with their culinary magic!

Title: A Feast for the Eyes, But Not the Palate

Walking into the restaurant, one can't help but notice that the staff could double as a lineup of KPOP or TVB stars – stunning and easy on the eyes. However, as the adage goes, looks aren't everything, particularly when it comes to dining experiences.

The food, unfortunately, did not mirror the staff's aesthetic appeal. The poke salad emerged as the night's darling; with the dressing on the side and an adventurous addition of wasabi, it truly tantalized the taste buds. However, the ahi tuna fell flat – its lack of freshness was evident, resulting in an unpleasant, fishy aftertaste.

The salmon and hamachi tataki both left me searching for something elusive – perhaps a hint of freshness or a dash of flavor that just wasn't there. The hamachi was notably chewy, striking the wrong chord for what should have been a delicate dish.

On the brighter side, the gomae delivered a delightful balance of sweet and savory notes, proving satisfying to the palate. The seaweed salad, contrarily, was unremarkable and reminiscent of something one might absentmindedly toss into a cart at Costco.

While the restaurant offered a visual feast and the chance to experiment with a few standouts like the poke salad and gomae, the overall culinary experience was underwhelming. Regrettably, it's not a spot I'd venture to again after going out of my way to try it.

Title: Middle-of-the-Road Fare at a Unique Food Stall

I recently tried an Egg Jian Bing from a standout food stall in a bustling food court. The three-tiered dining setup of the court was impressive, with the stall sharing space with three other vendors.

For $6.50, I landed the menu's most budget-friendly option—a crepe-like dish that promised an intriguing culinary experience. However, the flavor didn't quite live up to my expectations. Despite enjoying the variety of ingredients tucked within the crepe's folds, the overall taste fell flat, hinting at the need for a zesty sauce or stronger seasoning to truly make it pop.

The presentation was pleasing, and the portion served up three of these crepes. Yet, given the taste that barely skimmed an average rating, the price felt steep; $4 would have been more appropriate for the quality of the meal.

In summary, while the Egg Jian Bing had potential with its satisfactory composition, it was ultimately an underwhelming experience that didn't justify its price point.

Calexico offers a tranquil ambiance that exudes a cozy, relaxed vibe, with service to match its friendly atmosphere. Our dining experience began with a creamy and satisfying Esquites, though the Crispy Brussels Sprouts fell short due to an imbalance with the balsamic vinegar – I'd suggest skipping this one. The entrees provided a mix of hits and misses; the Chipotle Pork Taco wrapped in a corn tortilla was a standout, with spices perfectly complementing the pork. However, the Grilled Shrimp Taco was disappointingly chewy and over-salted. As for the Carne Asada wet Burrito, the sheer size impresses, but the dryness of the beef detracted from the overall flavor. In sum, Calexico shines in some areas while falling short in others, offering a mixed dining experience.

Title: A Bustling Bargain for Mediterranean Delights

I stumbled upon a gem on Yelp that promised affordable dining and it didn't disappoint. Reservations are a must, as evidenced by the full house and the queue outside on a Thursday evening. The much-acclaimed falafel and hummus plate was a hit — the hummus was exceptionally creamy and paired wonderfully with two flawless pieces of pita. While the falafel didn't top my all-time list, it was still satisfying. The brie sandwich, nestled in crusty ciabatta-like bread, also made a favorable impression.

The ambiance is where opinions may diverge; it's a vibrant, energetic space which borders on noisy, possibly challenging for those seeking tranquility. However, for an after-work spot with character and budget-friendly prices (under $20 for most menu items), this place ticks all the right boxes. I'll definitely be returning for that sublime hummus.

My husband found this restaurant for us to enjoy our Christmas dinner on our recent vacation in NYC. The location is perfect. Right in midtown Manhattan and close to other areas you will most likely be spending time in if you're a tourist like we were. The decor is unique but also welcoming if that is possibly a thing. Very artsy but still has a touch of Italian family style. Upon arriving, we were quickly seated with our reservation. My mother in law enjoyed a glass of Cabernet while I enjoyed my latte. We all ordered varied dishes. I threw all my healthy mumbo jumbo to the side to order the chicken parmigiana that comes with mini pepperonis on the top. It is a huge portion so I was only able to eat half, but I thoroughly enjoyed it. They were out of their garlic bread so that was the only complaint. But they more than made up for it with their cannolis. We all couldn't stop talking about them after eating them. If you order them, don't try to share like we did. Get your own pair and devour them and maybe order more. They are the best cannolis any of us have ever eaten. Great service. We had a great holiday dinner here.

Pretty impressed but for sure not my favorite brunch in the city. You can feel that it's pretty manufactured because it's such a touristy place. We both got the pancake breakfast (mine with Nutella and berries and his with chocolate chips) with sausage and eggs. You can tell that they just mass produce the pancakes and have them sitting around for a while before they are served, but they are quite tasty. It was absolutely packed by 10:30. We had to wait about 20 minutes. Pretty good food but you might have to expect a wait.

Title: An Unforgettable Italian Feast at Allora Ristorante

From the moment I walked into Allora Ristorante, the warm greeting by staff members Fadil and Merlind made an excellent first impression, only enhanced by the cozy ambiance created by subdued lighting and elegant white tablecloths. The Yelp check-in discount of 10% was an unexpected bonus.

The service was impeccable, with the staff donned in classic black tuxedos. Surprisingly affordable, Allora did not skimp on the quality or the quantity, serving three delightful complimentary appetizers, which included smoked sliced meat, Parmesan cheese, and fried zucchini—though I opted out of the green pepper due to my aversion to spicy food.

A freshly baked bread accompanied the starters, and upon Franko's recommendation, I delighted in a bottle of Brunello, which was both excellent and budget-friendly. Sharing the bottle with the staff added to the familial vibe of the place, reminiscent of a quaint Italian-owned eatery.

My meal comprised a flavorful minestrone, a freshly prepared tableside Caesar salad, and an outstandingly generous portion of chicken Parmesan that rivaled the size of a pizza. The local and Italian chatter around me contributed to the restaurant’s authentic and welcoming atmosphere.

To cap off the meal, they served fresh grappa from a cart showcasing an array of fruit infusions—a complimentary and novel touch. A peach sorbet made a perfect pair with the lemonchello grappa, rounding out an evening of culinary delights.

Allora Ristorante truly delivered a dining experience that felt like a slice of Italy, leaving a lasting impression that I will cherish for years to come.

Adorable. We went to ft a to-go order for lunch and I just wanted to stay. The decor is just so cute, and the layout of the place makes you want to just chill and have some mezcal. The bar area is stunning. On a sunny day, the light streams throughout the restaurant. It felt very peaceful. My friend ordered the quesadillas, and they were so good. Loved the pesto. The coconut cheese was actually really good, and I usually feel really picky about vegan cheeses. I enjoyed my enchiladas mole, but I felt like they were almost too hearty in the end. I preferred the quesadilla. They cook their rice perfectly, though!I really can't wait to come back for dinner!

Came here for a couple of shared plates with a fellow yelper. I was told that this place has the best burger in NY, this was definitely a false statement. I found the burger to be pretty salty and mediocre overall. The rest of our food was pretty tasty. Our waiter was cool though. He made thoughtful recommendations for us. Although my friend and I had a reservation I found that they ran a tight ship. We could only dine at the countertop (which I found to be uncomfortable since there wasn't much leg room and I had to sit sideways) and after about an hour we were told we'd have to wrap it up since they needed the countertop seating for another reservation. This is never something you want to hear after investing in a restaurant. The bathroom had a mural of 90's Hip Hop artists and a disco ball which was really cool. Overall aesthetic of this place was great. I would return for the ambiance if anything. Also, this spot doesn't have it's liquor license so no alcohol served here yet!

Super duper crowded place for lunch. Min 30 mins wait on weekends. You leave your phone number and they will text you when your table is ready. The place is not very spacious in between each table. Tables are small. Food is ok. I had the Jane burger and it was very juicy and tasty. Had green salad instead of rosemary fries. I wasn't crazy about the salad. It was lacking dressing and the greens weren't very fresh. They have a space downstairs that was under utilized. Service was ok.

Title: A Brooklyn Dim Sum Staple That Keeps Me Coming Back

If you've been led to believe that authentic dim sum requires the clatter of carts, let Wu's be your delicious reeducation. Tucked away from the well-trodden tourist paths, this gem in Brooklyn's Chinatown has become my go-to spot, consistently outshining any new contenders in the NY dim sum scene.

What sets Wu's apart is their made-to-order approach. Each dish arrives at your table as a fresh batch, enhancing the flavors and textures that regulars have come to love. From the classic har gow to siu mai, the menu staples are executed perfectly, with larger entrée options available for those seeking something more substantial.

Cleanliness is clearly a priority here, contributing to the welcoming atmosphere. But, in the interest of honesty, I can't overlook their less-than-stellar congee and the absence of tofu hua, which prevents me from granting a full five stars.

Advice for newcomers: arrive before 11 am on weekends to avoid the rush. For larger gatherings, reservations are recommended, and don't miss out on the chance to order special dishes tailor-made for your group.

In short, Wu's is a testament to the fact that great dim sum doesn't need to roll around on a cart to be worth your while.

Title: An Adequate Experience with Room for Improvement

My recent visit to this Vietnamese spot was, in a word, okay. The immediate seating for our party of four was a plus, but the culinary journey began on a disappointing note with the spring rolls. They missed the mark with their bland taste and unimpressive portion size, and the dipping sauce failed to make up for it. We moved on to vermicelli dishes; the lemongrass pork at $14 was decent, but required a heavy hand of sriracha and hoisin to elevate it. The catfish, a dollar more, was on par. The drink selection was average, with tiger beers at $7 overshadowing a potentially more exciting cocktail menu.

The ambiance did have its charms with a grungy feel and enjoyable music, providing a somewhat nostalgic appeal that might resonate with a younger crowd or college students. Service was unremarkable, blending into the background of the experience.

In a city brimming with Vietnamese cuisine, this spot doesn't quite stand out. It's the kind of place that might have boasted novelty in less competitive locales but struggles to make a mark where choices abound.

I'm a drinker and if a drinker goes some place and gets more frustrated  the more drinks they have it's one of two things. They a bad drunk or the drinks weak.  I'm not a bad drunk . I'm a West Indian with ah high tolerance. I ordered Jameson the first drink was about a 7 the second one was water  don't ask about the third cause I wasn't going order that after the second. I ordered and impossible burger  I had my sis my bro my moms and my nephew ass try a piece and the could not tell it wasn't meat.  This is my second time having the impossible and first time having it at the bee. Def the highlight of my dinning experience.  My order of fries was  too salty for me but I'm not a big salt fan. For me my biggest issue was as follows. you have nine people sitting at a table. Two of whom order the unlimited plates so they could order as much as they want.  You bring orders but don't take any plates. What a struggle finding  a space to put food on a crowded table. Thankfully eventually our waitress realized  maybe I should take some dirty dishes. Honestly I have to say my dining experience wasn't dreadful, but the only thing memorable about it was that I was with family.

Sup Crab is a spacious seafood boil restaurant with very friendly staff. My friend and I ordered snow crab legs with quail eggs and shrimp with corn respectively. We also ordered water spinach to share. The sauce I chose was their house special sauce, which in my opinion was not very spicy despite the description. I liked it and did not find it overly salty either. They gave a lot of shrimp and a bunch of corn and they were wonderful doused in the sauce. The water spinach was a simple but good dish. While eating, we were offered rice that I initially turned down, but decided it was a good idea after all. Throughout the meal, the servers was attentive and we were even given complimentary honeydew at the end.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at the Unassuming Poke Spot

I recently discovered a hidden gem when I decided to give the local poke place a try through a lunch app. I'll admit, my expectations weren't high, given that I've passed by its often quiet storefront numerous times without a second thought. But this experience completely changed my mind.

The poke bowl I received was a delightful surprise. Not only was the fish notably fresh, but the sides were harmoniously balanced, which elevated the entire meal. Freshness is a promise many poke establishments make, but don't always deliver; however, this spot holds true to that standard.

The portions were unexpectedly generous, offering a substantial amount of food that was both light and satiating. Despite the volume, the quality and flavors were so good, I found myself happily indulging until I had finished every last bite, resulting in an unavoidable yet satisfying food coma.

After an informal office poll regarding our favorite local poke, this unassuming eatery won hands down, reaffirming my opinion. For those who appreciate a good poke bowl and find themselves in the area, this spot is a must-try. And a tip for fellow workers seeking a quick lunch grab: order ahead to save time.

Overall, this poke place has earned my vote and I'll definitely be returning for more.

I came here on the recommendation of a friend who lived in Manhattan a few years back. I was in town for a work trip and decided to stop by here for a late solo lunch one day and found the environment perfect for some personal peace and a zenful bowl of noodles. There were plenty of written materials and instructions available that you don't really have to talk to staff or patrons, and I needed that after a day of walking through throngs of loud people and traffic. I was seated very soon upon arriving, ordered using their written instructions, and got my order through the window in front of my seat shortly thereafter. I sat there for quite a while savoring this little pocket of space and the substantial bowl of ramen that left me feeling warm and satisfied. I wouldn't say the ramen tasted spectacularly different than what I expected - but the quality was great and ingredients plenty.

This pizza joint truly lives up to the hype with its super thin crust that manages to shy away from being greasy, serving as a perfect late night staple. Add to that their quick service, and you've got a winning combination for any pizza enthusiast. Highly recommended.

Title: A Zesty Vegetarian-Friendly Experience at Mad Dog & Beans

Last evening, my companions and I sought out a vibrant dining spot that accommodated vegetarians and could satiate our craving for Mexican cuisine. We stumbled upon Mad Dog & Beans via the Yelp app and were immediately enticed by the mouthwatering photos and the promise of close proximity.

Upon arrival, we were greeted by an explosion of color and lively decor—think sugar skulls, papel picado, and eclectic wall art—which kept our eyes dancing as we were shown to our table near the buzzing kitchen and the bar. The ambiance was instantly inviting, with each visual detail adding to the festive atmosphere.

An unexpected perk of checking in on Yelp was a complimentary margarita—a delightful and refreshing start. The menu was a treasure trove of Mexican favorites such as tacos, burritos, and enchiladas, each dish more tempting than the last. We began with made-to-order guacamole, which was fresh and easily customizable with the addition of salt and a generous serving of jalapeños on the side—the perfect touch for those who appreciate a fiery kick. The accompanying homemade chips were a satisfying contrast with their warm crunch.

The entrees were a culinary delight. I savored the shrimp tacos that came generously topped with guacamole and were ideal for sharing. My friends were equally pleased; one enjoyed a savory burrito bowl, while the other raved about the Quesadilla de Rajas, which was a pleasantly mild, yet rich and flavorful choice.

While the setting was noisy, making conversation a shout-worthy affair, the background mix of 90s Hip Hop provided a nostalgic and humorous soundtrack to our meal. Admittedly, the prices leaned towards the higher end, but the delectable flavors and the overall experience justified the cost.

Mad Dog & Beans earns a solid 4-star rating in my book, striking a fine balance between a feisty feast for the eyes and a sumptuous spread for the stomach, especially for those on the lookout for vegetarian options.

The egg sandwiches are certifiably decent and are worth it if you can snag a seat quickly, especially at the bar. Otherwise, after a long wait, you might find that you'll need to order some sides to satisfying your hangriness, and you might be a tad surprised with sticker shock when the bill comes out. I ordered the sausage, egg, and cheese sandwich partly because it didn't have a runny egg by default, and also because of the protein it offered. At $14, it was a tad pricey, but the eggs were scrambled in a nicely thick and fluffy way, and the overall sandwich was a tad bigger than what you'd expect of a solid neighborhood deli here in New York. The brunchkins were also satisfying, but rather petite for the price. I lucked out by scoring a seat quickly at the bar, but otherwise I wouldn't necessarily seek out the Egg Shop from afar if there was a long wait, and especially if I could get a comparable egg sandwich from a quality neighborhood deli for half as much.

Title: A Delightful Discovery Through Meal Pal

I had the pleasure of trying this eatery via Meal Pal today, spurred on by glowing reviews, and my high expectations were met with gusto. Arriving sharply at 11:45 am, I was greeted with a near-instantaneous readiness of my order—less than a two-minute wait for food is always a win in my book.

The main event, the pizza, stood up to the acclaim; it was nothing short of delicious. Adding to the charm was the convivial bartender sporting an enchanting French accent, enhancing an already pleasant experience.

This gastronomic gem has certainly earned its spot on my list of go-to places in the neighborhood. I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Highly recommended!

I recently visited Nur with friends, keen to try their renowned Jerusalem Sesame Bagel. The restaurant exudes a 'fancy casual' vibe with a clean and stylish interior, softened by distressed elements. A pleasant touch was the complimentary still and sparkling water, and the menu encouraged family-style sharing - perfect for our group.

Our culinary journey began with the delightful Jerusalem bagel. It was a textural triumph - warm and toasty on the outside while remaining pillowy within. It paired exquisitely with hummus and other dips. Next, the pan-roasted octopus, though tender, could have benefited from a bit more char for added flavor. The accompaniment of vibrant sauces, whose names escape me, did enhance the octopus nicely.

Moving onto the beef scallopini, it was somewhat dry, but the side vegetables brought moisture and balance to the plate. Service shone at Nur; the staff were not only friendly but attentively mitigated the discomfort of summer heat by addressing condensation issues from overhead ducts.

In summary, the dining experience at Nur was largely enjoyable, with standout dishes and commendable service.

Title: A Gem for Asian Fusion Enthusiasts

I must admit, I'm not usually one to judge a book by its cover, but this restaurant had me smitten from the moment I stepped through the door—a solid five stars waiting to happen. The ambience struck the perfect chord for a casual lunch: comfortably average noise levels and a cozy interior that felt both welcoming and chic.

Service was impeccable—swift, polite, and genuinely friendly without a hint of awkwardness. It's a delight when the staff makes you feel at home.

The menu presented a tempting array of Asian fusion dishes that promised variety and delivered on taste. To start, we chose the Korean Taco, accompanied by addictive Truffle Fries, a vibrant Tri-Color Sashimi Salad, and the star of the show, Crunchy Tofu. The presentation of each dish was a feast for the eyes—thoughtful and artful without skimping on portion size. After experiencing my fair share of style-over-substance dining, it was refreshing to leave feeling satisfied.

The sashimi salad burst with freshness, the bulgogi tacos were a tender, flavorful dream, and the truffle fries—you could smell the enticing aroma as they approached the table. As for the Crunchy Tofu, it was a revelation, encased in what I suspect was a perfectly seasoned, sweet gochujang-infused batter.

Peeking at the other tables only confirmed my initial impressions; every dish looked just as appealing. Already looking forward to my next visit, I can't recommend this place enough for those craving an exemplary Asian fusion experience.

This is one of my favorite places for authentic Henan food in New York. The "Big Tray of Chicken" is the signature dish and a must for any visit. Its served in a spicy broth with boiled potatoes and noodles. Be sure to order the thick noodles, and you'll probably want extra depending on how hungry you are. The other must have dish is the Pancake with Pork or Beef. This was one of my favorite street food snacks when living in Beijing. The pancake was cooked perfectly with just a little bit of crisp on the outside.

Title: Authentic Delights at a Bustling Eatery

From the moment we entered the restaurant, we knew we were in for a treat. Despite it being a busy Friday afternoon and having a short 20-minute wait for a table, the experience was well worth it. Our server was nothing short of amazing, embodying the spirit of the entire team whose seamless cooperation and efficiency were a spectacle in itself.

Guided by our server's sincere recommendations, we started with the pork buns appetizer, a decision that did not disappoint. The flavors were outstanding, the perfect prelude to our main courses. Both the Karaka Spicy and the Akamaru Shinaji entrées lived up to the high expectations set by the appetizer, delivering mouth-watering tastes that satisfied our palates completely.

The overall experience at this restaurant was undeniably great, marked by exceptional service and delectable cuisine. It's a must-visit for anyone seeking authentically delicious fare served by a team that truly knows the art of hospitality.

Arrived on a weekday night and promptly seated. This is a place for smaller group. The vibe is good, ideal for a date spot. Was greeted by the owners. They are really sweet. Decided to try the Doro wot with 2 sides. Chose red lentil as one and cabbage as the other. Paired the meal with Ethiopian Honey Wine which went really well with the meal. The meal itself is served in an Injera( for those of you who don't know, it's somewhat like an Ethiopian savory crepe) along with some more on the side. The chicken was flavorful and well marinated. The quantity was just right for 2 people. Don't shy away from getting your hands dirty since that's how you can enjoy every bit of the meal. Definitely one of my favorite spots in the area. Price may seem on the higher side but giving that it feeds 2 people, it's decent.

I have to admit this place is beautiful.  The music was pretty cool. Drinks are really expensive.   If you re staying at the hotel you can go straight up and in just show your room key.   You don't have to go through the front door downstairs.  They kind of give you the once over.   Do I qualify?   Had to tell em we were part of a group that was staying the hotel. Minus one for the run around.  Still beautiful.  The music was pretty good.

Title: A Delightful Scoop of Flavor at The Noodle Nook: A Review

I recently visited a charming little establishment where the promise of "light in spice and warm in the gut" lured me in. The promise came from their cold rice noodles description - an irresistible choice on a sweltering day. The Noodle Nook may be small, seating about 15 patrons, but it compensates with a cozy atmosphere and self-service water to beat the heat.

The staff's friendliness was as palpable as the heat outside, making ordering a pleasure. While I opted for the subtly-flavored cold rice noodles, my companion dived into the popular tofu rice noodles, a dish for those who fancy a bolder taste. The option to pick your spice level is a welcome touch, though I caution fellow mild spice enthusiasts that even their lowest level packs a punch.

The chili oil sauce served on the side is a flavorful addition - use it wisely to avoid overpowering the delicate balance of the dish. While the noodles didn't wholly match their description, they hit all the right notes of satisfaction and refreshment.

Lingering long after our meal was done, we never felt rushed - a testament to the warm hospitality. My recommendation: drop by The Noodle Nook for a 5-star service and a meal that soothes and spices up your day in equal measure.

I recently visited this remarkable restaurant for the third time in as many months, and it continues to impress. The service is exceptional, attentive without being intrusive, ensuring a delightful dining experience. As for the food, it's nothing short of amazing. On this visit, we indulged in a 3.5-pound grilled lobster that was cooked to perfection - succulent and flavorful. This establishment has consistently demonstrated why it's an awesome place to dine, and I eagerly anticipate my next visit.

Title: A Delightful Delivery Experience

I recently decided to try delivery from this restaurant and was thoroughly impressed. The Shanghai lo mein with chicken was a flavor-packed dish, generously mixed with a perfect balance of veggies and tender chicken. Accompanying my order, the shrimp dumplings were notably juicy and utterly delicious, while the scallion pancakes added a delightful and tasty touch to the meal. Portions were more than satisfactory, leaving plenty for a second helping. This experience has definitely piqued my interest in visiting for the full dine-in experience soon! Highly recommended for a tasty and satisfying meal at home.

The location my friends + I went to the one in Hells Kitchen. Obao was eh, that's it, nothing special. I noticed the grade was 'B', so I am not sure what happened there. I usually avoid 'B' restaurants since I'm a picky foodie. I just wish they had more Paleo + Low Carb friendly meals. I was stuck with Tom Yum Soup. When I asked for no rice and more vegetables on an entree, the waitress said that I cannot do that? The rice came as a complementary.  The dessert (WINTER YUZU) was actually different + good. The interior was actually beautiful, so this place would be great for a date.

Tried this place for the first time and was pleased. Ordered as a $1 special through RITUAL app - so the price was right!!!  Tasty and filling. Was ready super fast. I placed the order on the app and it was ready within minutes. Decided to eat in at this location since the pizza was hot, and ate at the counter. Limited seating, just the counter. Good to eat solo, not a good place to eat in as a group.

Title: Decent Bites, But Prices Miss the Mark

I recently visited a local ramen spot that offered a satisfactory dining experience, though it struggled to deliver value for the cost. The meals were certainly palatable—standard tonkotsu ramen shined with a flavorful broth and high-quality ingredients like tender pork and a perfectly cooked egg. But as delicious as these dishes were, they didn't surpass the taste of more budget-friendly eateries.

The sticker shock began with appetizers. At $5 for each bun, I anticipated something exceptional, yet they were on par with less expensive alternatives I've enjoyed elsewhere. It's possible these prices align with the neighborhood's average, but for me, the cost did not correlate with a notable increase in quality or presentation.

Also mildly disconcerting was our server's relentless promotion of an expensive drink special, which became a bit wearying after expressing our disinterest. Although we appreciated the timely service and meal delivery, the upselling tainted the overall ambiance.

In sum, while the ramen itself is a safe bet, the restaurant's steep prices and aggressive sales tactics make it difficult to fully recommend. If you're in the area and willing to pay a premium for good—though not extraordinary—ramen, it may be worth a visit. Otherwise, better value can be found elsewhere.

Came here for brunch and was really impressed with the menu, it had a good variety and everything sounded really good. I ended up getting a Bloody Mary and a pizza. The Bloody Mary was good , nothing special just average. What really gave it the four stars though was the food! The pizza I got was delicious and the sauce had great flavor! The only thing was the bottom was very thin and got soggy fairly quickly but overall the flavors were there. Another person I was with got the fried chicken which I tried as well and it so good! I would definitely get that again if I came back.

Title: A Slice of French Elegance

My recent dining experience at this charming establishment was a delightful immersion into French culture. The aged sliced meat was a standout, bursting with flavors that left a lasting impression on our palates. Accompanied by my wife and her friend, our evening out was anything but disappointing. The ambiance struck a harmonious balance between elegance and comfort, creating an atmosphere that was both beautiful and light. Having visited the renowned Amelie downtown previously, I was pleasantly surprised to find that this venue upheld the same high standards. A recommended destination for anyone seeking a taste of France's culinary finesse.

3.5 stars. Came for Sunday dinner with two friends and were seated upstairs. It's pretty up there, but it's so dim that it was bothering all of us. It's a great place for large group dinners; while we were there, there were two other parties of ten people or so having a great time. The downstairs was filled with tweens when we were there.  Burrata - my table shared this and really enjoyed it. It is loaded, and was big enough to share among three. Lamb - I thought this was okay. The lamb was very good and braised so well, but there was so little of it. It comes with a huge portion of cavatelli, and it was really creamy, but tasteless. I don't know, it's a big bowl, but tastewise, it felt lacking. Affogato- vanilla ice cream with a shot of espresso to pour on it. It comes with two sticks of chocolate biscotti to dip into it. Joe, our waiter, was kind enough to put candles in it, because we were celebrating all of our birthdays. We all really enjoyed this!In terms of service, Joe was on top of everything and helpful with us choosing. The host, however, was pretty snooty and unfriendly; he left a bad taste in my mouth. It was a good experience overall, but my meal was just forgettable. If you want to create your own pasta, Aunt Jake's is a worthwhile option.

Restaurant Review: Zest Szechuan

My recent dining experience at Zest Szechuan was a journey of bold flavors and genuine hospitality. Props to Lisa, one of the owners, for her outstanding customer service that made my friend and I feel right at home from the moment we stepped in.

We arrived for our 6 pm reservation to a relatively calm atmosphere, but by the time we left at 8 pm, the place was bustling. I appreciated the well-spaced tables and the unexpected treat of complimentary boiled peanuts—a nostalgic touch for me.

The tasting menu was our guide for the evening. First up, the Dan Dan Noodles ($7.95) were delicately silky with an intriguing sauce that was intense and unique, though perhaps too overpowering due to a lack of balancing ingredients.

Next, the Thinly Sliced Beef Soup with Tomatoes & Tofu ($23.95) was served in a pot rich with history. The soup's flavor profile was a twist, leaning more towards an Italian tomato vibe with Szechuan nuances. While I adore tofu, its combination with the tomato base didn't hit the mark for me.

However, the Grilled Whole Fish ($38.95) was the star of the night—perfectly cooked with delicious accompaniments of noodles and veggies. It was a well-executed dish that I'd highly recommend.

Despite the hiccup of forgetting our rice, the service was attentive with frequent check-ins and refills, although it's wise to avoid wearing white due to the unavoidable sauce splashes.

While some dishes were outside my comfort zone, the standout flavors left a lasting impression. I'm eager to come back for more familiar choices. Thanks to Lisa and Zest Szechuan for an evening of culinary exploration!

Rating: 4/5 - A return visit is on the horizon for a tailored flavor adventure.

Title: A Gem Unveiled on an Unexpected Evening

My friends and I stumbled upon Kanoyama on a Sunday evening, a night when their acclaimed omakase is off the table. Nevertheless, we were in for a delightful surprise. The Sunday specials seemed endless, but we opted for the classics: Shumai, hamachi kama, black cod, and the sushi & sashimi platter for two. Each dish was a revelation of freshness and flavor, refining what we thought "basic" could ever taste like.

The black cod was the star, melting like butter with each bite. Even without diving into the omakase, Kanoyama impressed us to the core. It's a must-try, and we're already planning our next visit for a Tuesday to Saturday slot to experience what we missed. Pro tip: Don't overlook the black cod—it's transformative.

Rating: 5/5 - A must-visit for any sushi lover.

Title: Quaint Eatery with Room for Improvement – 3 Stars

I recently dined at a small and unassuming restaurant that doesn't seem too concerned with first impressions. Despite its shabby appearance, it was clean, including the restrooms. Securing a table for two on a busy Saturday afternoon, I noticed the cramped seating and lack of warmth from the staff. 

The dining experience is further compromised by the use of inadequate plastic utensils, notably the narrow soup spoons ill-suited for enjoying soup dumplings. The xiao long bao (XLB) dumplings were merely passable, with the spoon issue detracting from the enjoyment.

On a positive note, the Spicy Big Tray of Chicken, while bony and requiring some effort to devour, was flavorful and ample in portion, perfect for sharing among four. The medium spice level was enjoyable, rich in cumin, and the noodles in the sauce emerged as the highlight for me. 

In the end, I might consider revisiting to try the dry noodle brisket dish, but I'm not in any hurry. This spot is worth a shot if you're in the area, but it might not make it to the top of your go-to list.

If you're hunting for a late-night gem with affordably satisfying bites, look no further. This eatery impresses with its monthly specials — always a delectable surprise. I've indulged in the everything bagel, the outstanding bacon, and the savory chicken parm, all of which hit the mark. The current month promises a tantalizing chicken sandwich that's already creating buzz on social media.

Let's talk staples: the buffalo and captain crunch nuggets are the stars, and rightly so. Accompanied by an array of 'fire' dipping sauces, they are a flavor fest. Don't miss out on the seasoned fries either — they're the crispy perfection you crave.

As for the ambiance, the place is cozy, managing to provide comfortable seating for small groups. Night owls and budget-friendly foodies will celebrate this spot. Definitely worth a visit — who knows, it could become your new favorite haunt for those late-night cravings.

I tried this spot out based on a review I found on Pinterest. I loved the location (SoHo) - it was very cute and suburban, which was a nice break from the hustle and bustle of the middle of Manhattan. The service was excellent, and we were able to get a late reservation as this place doesn't close until 4 a.m., which was cool, too. I ordered the fried chicken and things, which was raved about in the reviews. Unfortunately, the food didn't live up to the hype. As a girl with a somewhat country background living in ATL, I expected wayyyyy more from the fried chicken, mash, and collard greens. At the very minimum, good seasoning. The food lacked flavor more than anything. The fried chicken was nicely fried, light and crispy, but if you mess up frying chicken you really shouldn't be frying chicken in the first place (just my opinion). The entire plate lacked seasoning, the greens weren't really "greens" but more like a warm and crunchy salad, and the potatoes were just gross. So again, I loved the service and atmosphere (the margaritas were bangin'!), so that's why I'm giving this place 3 stars. But the food was "ehhhhhhhhhhh I'll pass. Hard pass".

Title: A Seafood Delight with a Side of Slight Delays

Last Saturday, my companion and I visited a bustling restaurant and were pleasantly seated at a high-top as soon as we walked in at 6 PM—quite the smooth start. The initial service hiccup of waiting 15 minutes for our waitress and water was mildly frustrating, considering our tight schedule for a Broadway show. Thankfully, once attended to, the service shifted up a gear, and things progressed smoothly.

Happy hour blessings came in the form of $1 oysters and $8 wine glasses. The New England oysters, albeit mild and ideal for novices, were underwhelming in taste, and the accompanying sauces lacked pizzazz. The wine didn’t leave a lasting impression, but it was a fair deal for happy hour.

Now, let me dive into the pièce de résistance: the lobster and shrimp boil. The choice to go 'hot' with the Cajun sauce was a triumph of flavor. The added corn, potato, and andouille sausage gloriously completed the feast. We opted for a shared portion due to an earlier lunch, but hearty eaters might prefer their own. Though the price was steep, the exquisite cooking of the seafood justified the splurge. Kudos to the thoughtful service touch with bibs, buckets, gloves, and tools, making the experience as seamless as it was savory.

In summary, while the restaurant's appetizers might not rush me back, the seafood boil alone is a contender for a visit. It’s a place where the joy of indulgence in expertly cooked seafood can make one forget the little delays and the bland beginnings.

Simple and fresh - Ootoya is more of a traditional Japanese spot.  We came here on a Sunday evening for dinner.  Service was absolutely exceptional.  Sake selection was impressive but deliberate.  We went for the warm Kira which was lovely.  Subtle and delicate, yet with a stronger finish - a carafe was plenty to share for 2.  For dinner, I ordered the regular chirashi bowl.  There is also a smaller half size, if you are feeling less hungry.  I also chose to combo it up - for $2 you can add a miso soup and a small side of picked veggies.  There is also a clear fish broth soup available with seaweed and mushrooms.  Meal ends with a complimentary green tea that is the perfect digestive.  Leave some room for dessert - we went for green tea and black sesame ice cream and it was wonderful.Again - the service is attentive and very kind.  Ootoya is also a non-tipping restaurant.  The space is lofty and beautiful.  Reservations recommended but easy to arrange via yelp!

Title: An Unforgettable Omakase Experience in the East Village

My evening at the East Village's premier sushi spot was nothing short of extraordinary. The Omakase Tasting, under the expert hands of Chef Isoda, provided a culinary journey that tantalized the senses and set a high bar for sushi excellence. The ambiance and service complemented the gastronomic adventure, creating a harmonious experience from start to finish.

Choosing the Tasting over the Omakase Prestige is a must. With additions like the delightful charcoal miso cod and the diverse sashimi platter, it allows diners to explore an array of flavors. The matcha crème brûlée is a divine finale – an essential indulgence despite the somewhat lackluster ice cream accompanying it.

Although our experience lasted around 2.5 hours, time seemed to stand still with Chef Isoda's engaging presentation and lively interaction, especially as he celebrated his birthday, which added a festive touch to the evening. His guidance through the meal, particularly his advice on not relying on the ginger, enhanced the integrity of each bite. Observing the behind-the-scenes action, including a live training session and an Osaka-style box sushi demonstration, was as educational as it was entertaining.

Highlighting just a few standout dishes, the Charcoal Grilled Miso Cod was a smokey delight, the Crabmeat Chawanmushi was a symphony of savory notes, and the assortment in the sashimi course – with the crispy fried prawn head – was remarkable. The sequence from lean akami to the sumptuous kamatoro captured the essence of tuna's depth. The Striped Bass and Marinated Bluefin were flavorful masterpieces, while the Nodoguro was a rare, delicate treasure not to be missed. The Anago provided a memorable finish to the sushi lineup, being both tender and richly glazed.

Earning its Michelin star, this omakase experience is one for the books. I wholeheartedly recommend this establishment for any sushi enthusiast looking to be immersed in culinary finesse.

Title: Cozy Gem in the Heart of Manhattan

If you're on the hunt for scrumptious pies served in a delightful setting, Vezzo is your go-to spot in Manhattan. The ambiance strikes the perfect balance between cute and casual, making it an ideal place to unwind with friends.

The staff at Vezzo exude warmth and friendliness, which adds to the overall welcoming experience. When it comes to the menu, don't miss out on the Formaggio Bianco and Classica pies—trust me, drizzle them with white truffle oil and thank me later. 

Pair your meal with a bottle of wine for a convivial night out that's surprisingly easy on the wallet. Vezzo stands out as the ultimate gathering place for those who relish great food and great company without the hefty price tag.

So this place is supposedly famous in China and I've been wanting to try it since it has opened in New York. We finally did it today and I can honestly say, I won't be coming back. I took my parents out for lunch for CNY and the place was dead. There was no hostess at the hostess stand and probably a total of 5 parties. The can at your table looks like a soda but don't drink it, it's actually sesame oil. We ordered our food by ticking off the paper menu. Note, they do not serve or have hot tea. Weird for a Chinese restaurant. Also note that your clothes will smell like hot pot afterwards so don't come in your finest outfit or plan to go out after. Once the food arrived, it tasted pretty good. We got mild on one of the broth and it was too spicy for everyone at my table except me. They also somehow did not provide us with ladles which I had to go get myself. They forgot to turn on the music in the restaurant so it was also very quiet. Overall the food is good but the service sucked. Everything seemed disorganized and the menu is set in a way that felt like they nickel and dimed everything. Disappointed overall.

Classic New York establishment perfect for pre theater or any other time.  The plate of 3 vegetables was delicious, the margherita and prosciutto pizza were ok.  Carb friendly which was good but a bit on the dry side.  The lemon dessert was amazing.

I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant, and I continue to be impressed with their culinary offerings. From the succulent lobster and the rich flavors of the crab cakes to the consistently impeccable steak, particularly their rib eye which I order on every visit, this place knows how to satisfy a meat lover's palate. 

Our server, Anthony, was the epitome of professionalism blended with kindness – a true asset to the dining experience. The highlight of the dessert menu, the flourless chocolate cake, was divine, and I must note that they excel at celebrating special occasions, making anyone feel extra special.

Even though I am a regular, I can't help but compare it favorably over their Garden City location, solidifying its spot at the top of my list. I have full confidence in the chef's specials, even though my preference often leans towards the familiar perfection of their steaks. 

I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant - it's a full score from me, 100%.

If you are on a kept diet and not sure where to go, this is the spot. I ordered the custom salad with zucchini noodles, peanuts, cucumber, mushrooms with their ginger miso dressing. I wasn't sure what dressing to get so I asked for the managers ( I believe she was the manager ) recommendation with what I ordered. When she told me ginger miso I was kind of ehh for a bit because I really don't like ginger but I'm glad I went with it because that dressing made my salad amazingggg !!! The taste of the ginger isn't that strong and overpowering. I will be back to try more salad.

It was hyped up and did not meet my expectations. I ordered the fish with black bean sauce and the unrefined palate may have thought it the best thing smoking. I, however, was unimpressed with the size of the entree and detested the taste. A lot of food that I did not like...I returned it immediately to the sender. The egg rolls were GINORMOUS! Bigger does not mean better...yuck! Bright spot: My friends ordered shrimp fried rice and lo mein. They were both consumable, but don't expect the veggies in either at this establishment. I gave it two stars for the experience. Underground eatery was new for my friends and I.

Title: "Satisfying Veggie Burger Experience in NYC"

After leaving Happy Hour with appetites in full swing, my quest for comfort food led me to a delightful food court in NYC, a melting pot of flavors and culinary experimentation. Amidst the diverse offerings, the homemade veggie burger caught my eye and did not disappoint.

The burger was colossal, oozing with rich, savory taste in every bite—a testament to the care put into its creation. Each mouthful was a harmonious blend of wholesome ingredients that left me both satisfied and eager for the next. Accompanying the burger were roasted rosemary potatoes, their aromatic herbs enhancing the golden, crispy edges to perfection.

In summary, this was a darn tasty burger that checked all the boxes for quality comfort food, making my "hungry hour" a memorable delight. Whether you're a local or a visitor, this spot is a must-try for any burger aficionado in the heart of New York City.

My friend and I are always on the look out for a good burger, and this was on her list of places to check out.We came here on a Thursday night, just as they opened. The servers are so polite and helpful! They checked in our umbrellas and my friends gym bag for us.We started off with the fries and we each got the burger. They didn't ask how we wanted it cooked, so I'm assuming they only made it one way. This burger was rare,  but it was delicious! It was well flavored and juicy. The bun was pretty good too, perfectly toasted; however they added too many onions, had to scrap some of it off.And the fries, holy shit they were perfectly crisp! My friend ended up getting a beer, and the cocktail I ended up getting was too strong. The servers were extremely nice and let me switch my drink. I will definitely stop by here again for the the burger.

While walking in the area we just dropped by there for a coffee. It is a small cute coffee place with some really good coffees. Pros:-Good cute place -amazing flavors for coffee-great seasonal flavors. Cons: -I don't think there were any cons. Recommendations(have just tried 2 flavors)-rose citrus -ice lavender latter

Title: A Cajun Twist with Chinese Flair!

I recently stumbled upon a culinary gem that melds Cajun zest with Chinese infusion, offering a dining experience like no other in the city. A lively dinner with friends turned into a feast at this unique spot where we delved into an array of shared dishes, highlighted by their signature combos. These bountiful platters featured succulent crawfish, corn, sausage, potatoes, and an option of lobster, Dungeness crab, or snow crab legs drenched in customizable sauces of varying heat levels.

Kicking off with a popcorn chicken appetizer, we further indulged in choices of calamari, wings, or fries. Each combo brought its own flavor profile to the table, ensuring a delightful sampling session. The crawfish rice dish, in particular, captivated my taste buds with its standout flavor - a must-try on my next visit.

Complementing the delectable food was the exemplary service, making the entire dining experience seamless and enjoyable. Without a doubt, this is the best Cajun spot in the city, and it's one I'll be recommending for a long time.

I recently dined at this charming restaurant and was immediately welcomed by the friendly staff. Seating was prompt, setting the stage for a great evening. I opted for the pork belly with pickled vegetables, a Szechuan classic known for its lengthy prep time, but to my delight, it arrived quickly.

The pork itself was a delectable affair—tender, with the fat and lean parts harmoniously intertwined, creating a light, not overly greasy flavor, although a tad salty for my palate. The accompanying pickled vegetables were a sharp contrast to the richness of the meat, a bit overwhelming on their own but a perfect match for the provided rice. Be prepared for generous portions; we had plenty of veggies left over.

This initial experience has left me eager to return and explore more of their offerings. This lovely restaurant has certainly set high expectations for future visits.

Title: A Tasty Find Post-Museum Adventure

I recently discovered a gem of a restaurant following an enjoyable visit to the natural history museum. It had garnered impressive reviews and boasted enticing images of both the food and the venue itself, prompting me to give it a try.

Upon entering, I was immediately struck by the cleanliness of the establishment and the tasteful decor that set a pleasing ambiance. However, I experienced a notable challenge: the level of communication left much to be desired. Despite my keen interest and willingness to engage with the menu, the language barrier proved to be an unexpected obstacle, which was quite surprising considering the potential for additional sales.

Undeterred, my culinary journey began with a pair of delectable pork buns that were an absolute delight to the palate. The pad Thai, a crowd-pleaser, lived up to its reputation as a favorite and did not disappoint. However, I'd suggest others give the crispy duck a miss – it didn't quite hit the mark for me.

On my next visit, I plan to explore more of their chicken dishes, anticipating another round of savory treats. Despite the communication hiccup, the restaurant presents a promising spot for a delicious meal.

Title: A Brunch Affair to Remember at Flat Top

If you're looking for a brunch experience that will leave your taste buds in awe, Flat Top has to be on your list. Last weekend's visit confirmed why there's such a buzz about their hollandaise sauce—it's genuinely the best I've ever tasted.

Upon arrival for brunch (which, by the way, is exclusively on Sundays, so plan accordingly), my friend had already secured outdoor seating, a definite plus for those who enjoy dining al fresco. Although they were out of Aperol Spritz, their Mezcal margarita with Agave syrup was an outstanding alternative, prompting me to indulge in more than one.

Decisions were tough between the Irish ham eggs Benedict and smoked salmon eggs Benedict, but our waitress expertly steered me toward the former. It was a decision I didn't regret. The dish, served on homemade focaccia with steamed spinach and perfectly poached eggs, was plated beautifully and tasted even better, making it impossible not to savor every single bite.

Despite being stuffed, we couldn't skip dessert. We shared a lemon posset tart with a delightful raspberry coulis, chocolate mousse, and the show-stopping bread pudding. The latter, with its warm apples, pecans, and indulgent caramel sauce, paired with a latte, was the perfect end to our meal.

A word to the wise: Flat Top gets busy, so if you're planning a dinner visit, make sure to reserve your spot. Trust me, this is a dining experience you don't want to miss.

I recently visited a local bar that didn't particularly stand out from the crowd except for its enthusiastic support of Texas Christian College football. My friends and I stumbled upon it after spotting a hard-to-resist happy hour special featuring $5 drafts, wines, and wells, which lasted until 7pm.

The beer selection was respectable, though I was slightly disappointed to find Guinness as the sole dark beer option. I started with a Lager from Yonkers before shifting to the wine, which was enjoyable. We shared BBQ and buffalo wings, alongside truffle fries. While the wings were satisfyingly meaty, the fries seemed a tad overpriced at $12 for a small bowl billed as a side dish.

Overall, the place did its job as an average, somewhat affordable pub. While the food was decent and the happy hour prices appealing, I wouldn't make a special trip back. It's a solid choice if you're already in the neighborhood and looking for a simple, no-frills spot to grab a drink and some bar snacks.

The box of dreams is just WOW. Definitely lives up to the hype and is excellent in both quality and presentation! It's Hatsuhana's version of a deluxe Chirashi 9 miniature bowls in a lacquer Box. Beautifully arranged and each bowl contains sushi rice with raw or cooked delicacies for $45. The range of flavors was remarkable, and the fish was very fresh!If there's just two of you I would recommend a box of dreams, and a reservation is almost certainly required. The ambiance was elegant, simple, yet unpretentious. Our wait staff was friendly and attentive but not hovering. The sushi was phenomenal. I didn't expect it to be some of the best sushi I ever had. Thoughtful presentation leads to a more enjoyable meal.  Each bite had my mouth aroused, left me waiting more. It looks as good as it tastes!

This 2 star Michelin restaurant exceeded my expectation (and my husband's). I highly recommend a visit here! Food was phenomenal, service was exceptional, décor was beautiful, presentation of the food + utensils used were well thought out and aesthetically beautiful like art. Jungsik really deserved the 2 star Michelin.My husband took me here yesterday as an early birthday surprise. Since everyone in the party has to select the same menu option (either seasonal or the signature tasting), we chose the signature tasting one (which consisted of 5 piece of amuse bouche appetizers displayed in this beautiful white squarish/round tower, 9 items in the signature tasting menu & 1 additional extra dessert). We wanted to know why they deserved the 2 star Michelin. They started us on drinks, and we chose cocktails. I chose the "to live a thousand years" which was symbolic. This cocktail was a ginseng w/ soju drink -  it tasted quite good, and was not strong. My husband chose the old fashioned cocktail & his drink was strong but he liked it very much that he ordered another one.Then the amuse bouche (5 appetizers) came and it was beautifully presented on top of the white squarish towers. The 5 items served were: 1) tuna tartare on a crispy cracker, 2) fried oyster, 3) a bun that had basil and something else in it, 4) persimmon, 5) uni w/ caviar on toasted seaweed. The last item was originally something w/ foie gras which I ethically chose not to ever eat. The staff was very catering, and substituted my food items that had foie gras. The amuse bouche were all delicious! Every single bite was decadent, orgasmic & of such high quality. I loved the persimmon as it was the palate cleanser and the taste was truly enjoyable. After the amuse bouche, the 9 items on the signature tasting came one by one. First item was the "Osetra Caviar" which had tuna tartare, caviar, crunchy quinoa. The taste was out of this world (crunchy, savory, salty), and what amazed me (besides how delicious it was) was the presentation of the food. The bowl they used was so beautiful + the pearl spoon you use to scoop the food. WOW! Second item was the "Foie Gras Mandoo" which they helped me substitute (w/ noodles). I ended up getting a large piece of wagyu meat on top of high quality noodles w/ broth that was made for 3 days. This was one of my favorites as I felt the person making this broth was making it with love. The broth was so savory and delicious. It was one of the best broths I have consumed since visiting Korea. My husband loved this as well, and liked the foie gras mandoo very much (he stated it tasted like buttered dumplings). Third item was the "octopus" - also one of my favorites. The octopus was so crunchy and tender. The crust was crunchy & savory while the octopus meat was so soft and chewy like it was mozzarella cheese. It was super delicious! The sauce was excellent as well and complimented the octopus. Fourth item was the "branzino" which was delicious. The fish skin was so crispy and the meat was tender. The white kimchi w/ wild perilla oil exemplified the flavor of the fish more. Fifth item was the "tuna kimbap". This one was also one of my favorites and most memorable.
