It was the best kimbap I have ever eaten, and I have visited Korea 3x so far (have eaten kimbaps in Seoul, Jeju, Busan). The extreme crispiness of the seaweed and the delicious truffle oil rice, tuna & avocado mixture made this morsel a one of a kind. Sixth item was the "galbi". This one was delicious as well. It was a large piece of galbi wagyu on top of rice w/ a piece of shiso leaf. Seventh item was the "pear". This was a palate cleanser. It was very delicious, and I tasted pear w/ pear sorbet and cinnamon. WOW! Eighth item was dessert (my fav) - the infamous "baby banana". This item was exceptional, and one of my favorites. Because it was my birthday, I was not able to pick the banana out of the fruit basket (but got to see my husband do it). I had the banana dessert on my plate w/ a scoop of expresso ice cream, a lighted candle w/ "happy birthday" written on plate. The baby banana was crunchy on the outside, and inside was pureed banana w/ white chocolate. The staff was also very sweet they gave me a small bowl of rice like porridge concoction (forgot what was in it). The staff said in Korea you eat this porridge when it is your birthday. Last ninth item was the "Matang" - pureed sweet potato w/ melted black sugar. It tasted like sweet potato crème brulee. Super delicious!We thought we were finished, and the staff came out with one last dessert. It was 3 petite desserts (white macaroon, some flowery thing, and black chocolate that had grapefruit filling in it). Beautifully decorated & delicious (esp the chocolate w/ grapefruit filling).P.S - even though the portions are small, there was a lot of food. We were stuffed by the end of the meal.

Title: A Lively Neighborhood Gem for Tacos and Margaritas

I stumbled upon a delightful outdoor lunch spot that perfectly captures the essence of a vivacious neighborhood. This restaurant buzzes with energy, making it an ideal place to enjoy the bustle of the street while you dine. The taco selection is robust, but the Baja fish taco stands out as a star with its flavorful and crisp bite—it's my personal favorite. The carne asada is a close second, tender and seasoned to perfection.

The margaritas here deserve a special mention; they are the perfect blend of sweetness and tang, and they complement the tacos wonderfully. Service is attentive and swift, ensuring that your lively lunch experience is as smooth as it is enjoyable.

The decor adds to the festive atmosphere with its bright colors and playful designs, contributing to the overall feeling of fun that defines this establishment. In short, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone looking for a great time accompanied by good food and drinks.

Title: Unmet Expectations in Little Italy's Chinese Eatery

I recently dined at a Chinese restaurant nestled in the heart of Little Italy, lured in by its glowing reviews. Unfortunately, the experience was underwhelming. The decision to serve Chinese cuisine in Little Italy should have been a red flag about its authenticity.

We started with the soup dumplings, which were passable but unremarkable, akin to what you'd find in the frozen section of an Asian supermarket. The main course, a noodle dish, was a letdown with its lackluster flavor profile.

Service was another sore point. There was a prolonged wait despite the restaurant not being overly crowded, and basics like soy sauce had to be requested separately after being initially forgotten.

In summary, this restaurant didn’t live up to the hype, and its offerings could not compensate for the lack of authentic flavors and attentive service.

I was not as enamored with La Contenta as many on Yelp seem to be. My friend and I got there on a Friday night at 5:45 and were seated in one of the two tables in the covered area on the sidewalk - the only table left in this really small restaurant. (That's not a dig just an observation.) The guacamole was ok (although its presentation as a tortilla chip flower was quite pretty). To tell the truth, I make tastier guacamole. We both ordered the fish tacos and mine came (with a side of Brussels sprouts). My friend's did not. He told me to eat - which I did because it was cold outside and the food was already getting cold. Halfway through my tacos my friend had still not received his. We called the waiter and he didn't know my friend had ordered them. (I guess there are people who would sit with a friend and watch them eat but it seemed odd that he didn't hear my friend's order and I did.) Anyway, the fish in the soft taco shell was way too big for the shell. I'd have rather had smaller fish pieces and three tacos than two humongous pieces sticking out of each end and the top of the shell. Like I said, nothing special or nothing better than any other Mexican place that I've been to in the city. (Nothing beats those in CA.) By the time I finished eating the last few bites everything was cold from eating on the street (albeit covered). My suggestion is, if you want to check it out in winter (or at least this freezing fall we're having) do not sit in those two tables. I walked into the restaurant to wash my hands from messy tacos and it was nice and toasty inside. Maybe the waiter didn't want to work outside either?

Yay for happy hour specials that's currently available every night from open to close! $1.50 oyster of the day with all others ranging from $2.25 to $2.75 each and $6/$7 tapas, wine and sake.Oysters were fresh and moderate sized (not big but not tiny). We loved the wasabi lime sorbet and mignonette sauces.Handrolls are $6 each or 4 for $22. Definitely try the unagi - it was warm, had a nice smokey flavor from being torched, and the chocolate sauce was the cherry on top even though you could barely taste any chocolate. The spicy yellowtail was okay but negi toro and spicy tuna were both very lackluster. I'd probably skip out on them.Korean fried chicken was tasty and had a good crunch from the tempura like coating but I do wish the chicken was hotter. It took a while for this small dish to come out so we thought the kitchen may have needed more time to make it but it was lukewarm so that makes me wonder if it had just been sitting around in the kitchen?Overall, a lovely date night spot with dim candle lit lighting but not overly dark that you can't see your partner or the food. There's soft jazz music playing in the background which really sets the mood. Seating is a little tight along the bar but chairs were super comfortable. Service was wonderful but got a little slow once the place was filled. You probably won't get too full here but it's a good place to go for a pre-dinner snack.
I placed a fairly large order: vegetable pad Thai, seaweed salad, spring roll, and mango sticky rice. It was all delicious. And they when threw in 2 masks! How nice!

I had made reservations for the Mermaid Oyster Bar without any prior knowledge of the place, except for their happy hour from 5-7.We arrived right before 5 and there was already a line forming outside. A good sign. The interior had a very cozy and charming vibe to it accentuated by the candlelit tables. It looks pretty tight when you see the restaurant from the outside, but has a pretty spacious area in the back.We ordered strictly from menu. Quite honestly, it was one of the best happy hour menus I've seen for seafood. Here's what we ordered:1 dozen oysters and 1 1/2 dozen clams for $1 each - they have a rule where you can only order 2 dozen raw bar items at a time. The oysters and clams came with cocktail sauce with horseradish and mignonette. We asked for some tobasco. The shellfish were absolutely tasty and fresh. We enjoyed the clams more (had a delightful texture and sweetness) which is why we ordered a 1/2 dozen more after the first round.Calamari - a very decent portion considering it's happy hour and well cooked. Definitely get this.Clam chowder - literally a taster in a very tiny cup. Good for one person or if you want to share magbe 3 ppl can have 1 spoonful each. It was very tasty tho.Mini lobster roll - it was literally overflowing with chunks of juicy lobster pieces. You must order this!!!They also had drinks on happy hour so I had a aperol spritz, and a bloody mary and paloma for the rest of my group.Service was also amazing here. I cannot forget to mention the complimentary chocolate pudding and fish fortune teller that they will sadly be discontinuing due to environmental reasons (plastic waste).It was the perfect meal for a light but VERY satisfying dinner.

Title: A Taste of Authentic Italian at a Cozy Spot

I recently stopped by an Italian restaurant for an early dinner with friends and was pleasantly surprised by the authentic offerings. At 5 pm, the place was quiet with a predominantly Italian crowd, which seemed promising.

For those with a penchant for Italian risotto, this is a must-try spot. The risotto here is cooked al dente, just as you'd find in Italy, and while the rice was firmer than usual, it still surpassed my expectations. We indulged in a variety of dishes, including the capesante, which was exceptionally flavorful if you're a fan of basil. The day's special crab meat and lobster risotto with bell pepper was a savory delight, even though I found it a tad salty for my taste.

Pairing the food with a bottle of Amarone wine was a good choice, especially with an extra sprinkle of cheese upon request. For dessert, the strawberry sorbet was refreshing and well-balanced, with a pleasant iciness that outshone other establishments. While I can't recall the name of the special dessert we tried, it was memorably delightful – sweet, but not overly so.

Our waitress was a beacon of positivity, and the attentive manager ensured our dining experience was seamless. While the open kitchen added charm, the seating could have been more comfortable. The clean and quaintly designed bathroom added to the restaurant's cozy feel.

Overall, this restaurant scored high on food (4/5) and service (5/5), with room for improvement in ambience (3/5). A true gem for those seeking genuine Italian cuisine.

Margarita-only review! My friend has been pressuring me to try the Margarita's here for a long time and I finally gave in this past weekend. The large size (Mama size) is huge and will run you $20-23 depending on the flavor you choose. I had the Mango, which was delicious and not too sweet. Could have had a little more alcohol, but for the size it was not a bad price honestly. I'd come back if I was in the area, but wouldnt make it a priority because the bar area is pretty small.

I recently tried out the Grilled Chicken Melt sandwich at a local eatery through Mealpal. While the sandwich itself was slightly on the dry side and the cheese wasn't particularly prominent in flavor, the overall taste was quite good. Additionally, I opted for an extra side of tots which were average - just okay.

Title: A Slice of NYC Heaven

Review:
My family and I awarded a well-deserved 5-star rating to this gem of a pizza spot in the heart of New York City. Venturing in on a bustling Monday at 7 pm, the line outside didn't deter us, and rightfully so – the wait was a brisk 15 minutes. The options were plentiful, but we went big with a whole pie for just $25, a steal for feeding a family in the city. After a short 20-minute interlude, we were greeted with the quintessential NY-style pizza – flawlessly thin, the right amount of bend, and simply divine in taste. This joint provided an unforgettable experience and a meal that left us planning our next visit. A must-go for that authentic NYC pizza indulgence!

A NYC historic steak institution located in FiDi. I came here for a team lunch and upon walking in it wasn't too busy, very clean and modern interior design. We ordered the Dry Aged porterhouse and sides to share. Everything was fantastic. Great service, good food. No more than you can ask for!

Title: A Birthday Bash Amidst Authentic Italian Flair

If you're craving a trip to an old-school Italian trattoria without leaving town, look no further. This tiny gem not only serves up some amazing pasta but knows how to turn a birthday into an unforgettable celebration. Imagine being at the center of a whirlwind of birthday music, blinking lights, and the charming clang of pots and pans, with a room full of strangers clapping and laughing in your honor. The atmosphere is simply electric.

The pasta here is a standout, each dish arriving at your table in a unique presentation—served directly in the pan. It's a novelty that adds an authentic touch, although be prepared for the metal to cool quickly, which may hasten your twirling fork. But even as the temperature dips, the flavors remain rich and satisfying. 

This little place is a must-visit. Whether it's your special day or you just fancy a quality pasta dish, you're in for a treat. Take my advice and experience it yourself. You won't regret it!

Title: A Gem for Quick Eats and Tasty Veggie Balls

I am a regular visitor to this delightful spot whenever I'm in the area and in need of a scrumptious quick bite or some convenient takeout. The service has consistently impressed me with its speed, whether I'm dining in or grabbing food to go.

As someone who typically steers clear of meat, I've not been much of a meatball aficionado. However, the veggie balls at this restaurant have truly won me over - they're nothing short of amazing. The mushroom sauce is my go-to accompaniment, but it's worth noting that they cater to all tastes with options like chicken and even lobster balls.

The Chelsea location boasts a spacious interior with plenty of seating, adding to the relaxed dining experience. It's the kind of place I find myself wishing was in my hometown. This eatery is my top pick for anyone looking for a casual and reliably satisfying meal.

**The Sweet Spot Dessert Bar Review**

The Sweet Spot certainly stands out on Saint Mark's Place, but not necessarily for all the right reasons. Unlike its sister location in Flushing, which boasts ample space and a modern vibe, this spot is seriously lacking elbow room—it's a tight squeeze, especially given its popularity.

When it comes to the menu, the desserts are a hit or miss. While some offerings are delectably sweet and merit a try, others fall flat and aren't justified by the steep prices. Service is decent, though Flushing might edge it out on attentiveness and efficiency due to less cramped conditions.

Overall, despite its trendy ambiance, The Sweet Spot feels overrated and could benefit from a more generous venue to accommodate its fan base. Dessert lovers should brace for potential standing-room-only scenarios. I’m tentatively awarding it 4 stars for the quality of select treats, but be forewarned: your wallet and patience may be tested.

For those pondering a visit, consider the Flushing establishment if you're after a more relaxed experience with room to savor your sweets.

I recently dined at a pho restaurant that genuinely impressed me. The staff were not only fluent in Vietnamese but Cantonese as well, providing a welcoming atmosphere for a diverse clientele. The service was commendably quick and efficient.

For my meal, I chose the pho bo vien which was absolutely delicious, its rich flavors and perfectly cooked ingredients left me savoring every spoonful. Additionally, I had a banh mi that truly hit the spot with its freshness and authentic taste.

The restrooms were well-maintained, adding to the overall positive experience. This spot has earned my recommendation, and I am already looking forward to my next visit.

Barbie turns on everyone that MEETS HERShe bats lashes and flirts with everyone that GREETS HERBut she's more expensive than Dr. Dre's BEATS ARESo instead get something you can afford: WILLIAMSBURG PIZZAWHATNot to be confused with Williamsbug Pizza (it has bugs all over it), Williamsbrugge Pizza (it's in Belgium), and Williamsbooger Pizza (don't ask), this is a pretty damn good LES Pizza place that you'll probably really enjoy unless you have insane standards for pizza slices like, for example, er, me.I'm going to give you a pizza my mind about how good pizza is in New York City because, well, it's really good and stuff.My notes on this place said - sophia loren or whatever, not my fave slice, dry, but it's not bad and the service is some of the best and sexiest in all mhtnNow what that means is that they were both friendly and really attractive/flirtatious, which I very much appreciated. But that's not really about the pizza, so let's talk pizza, and then maybe one day we can achieve pizza on earth and goodwill towards all the people we come acrust.I'm definitely a fan of this pizza, but in a city like New York City it's tough, because there are just so many amazing slices on this island, and this one - or rather the two that I got from here - isn't anywhere near my list of favourites, so I have to stick to four stars for this pizza even though it is really good.In most cities it would be one of the best in town, but Manhattan standards are at another level, and if you've had a lot of the better NYC pizza slices, you know what I mean.The service here is excellent and I mean really spectacular. The guys were amazingly friendly and the girl here is for realz like my dream girl, Barbie notwithstanding, although Barbie can legit withstand a lot.

This spot tends to have a long wait time. The line is pretty long sometimes. If you crave for one of the best ramen broths. This is the spot for you. It is worth waiting outside in the cold for atleast 30minutes. The seating is different from other restaurants. If you come in a group. They will try to sit the group in a whole roll. Its like sitting in a booth. This place is the perfect spot for single people. You just check box what you want and give it to the window. The food comes out pretty fast.The broth was 5stars for me. It was fatty and flavorful with a touch of spice.The ramen was 4stars. It was fresh. It had bite to it.The pork was 3stars. The one I got was tough and chewy with no fat on. It just had flavor from the broth.Price is kinda on the expensive side for ramen. But everything is freshly made as you order it. So thats a plus.Overall good experience. Would come back again.

Title: A Heavenly Fusion at Burger & Lobster Times Square

Review:

During our first restaurant outing of the decade, my husband, a friend, and I returned to Burger & Lobster in the heart of Times Square. Despite initial reservations about the unusual pairing and its bustling location, this establishment has disproven all doubts, establishing itself as our top recommendation for NYC dining.

On our recent visit on January 2nd, 2020, we kicked off an evening planned around a Broadway show with a pre-theater meal. We commenced with Lobster Bites - a delightful morsel of lobster and shrimp encased in a light, crispy wonton wrapper served with a tantalizing sweet and spicy chili sauce.

For our main course, all three of us indulged in the ideal Burger & Lobster experience by ordering the Combo for 1, comprising a succulent steamed lobster, a perfectly cooked original burger, fries, salad, and the exquisite Lemon Garlic Butter, which was a game-changer for the entire platter.

Our newcomer was thoroughly impressed, continuously expressing her amazement and newfound understanding of the restaurant's concept. The meal struck a perfect balance between upscale seafood fare and comforting burger delight, making it a memorable and unique dining adventure.

Burger & Lobster remains an undisputed favorite of ours, particularly when in the Times Square and Midtown area. We eagerly anticipate our next visit to this culinary gem.

Title: Cozy Evening at Thursday Kitchen

I recently dined at the eclectic Thursday Kitchen and I'm still raving about it! Heads up, they don't offer reservations – but a little tip, arriving at 6:30pm seems to be the sweet spot to avoid the crowds.

The highlight of the evening, aside from the vibrant tapas, was their Capri Sun-inspired alcoholic beverages – a nostalgic twist that was both inventive and delightful. Every dish was a hit, starting with the edamame dumplings; a delicate blend of citrus truffle and green pepper, graciously dusted with parmigiano. The tuna tataki followed, with its dance of hummus coulis, sesame vinaigrette, and a crunch of quinoa, all accentuated by serrano pepper and sumac – sublime!

The truffle mac & cheese with its infusion of manilla clam and aromatic truffle oil was comfort food elevated to an art, while the micro basil offered a fresh counterpoint. The kimchi paella was a revelation, a cheesy wonder with the creaminess of risotto, elevated by white tiger shrimp, mussels, and the brilliant addition of caramelized kimchi. Lastly, the Korean popcorn chicken was impossible to resist, its sweet and spicy sauce perfectly complementing the black sesame crumble.

Thursday Kitchen is a gem that serves up incredible flavors with a side of fun, and I can't wait to go back.
This gelato was delicious. Almost as good as in Italy. I love how they make every cone into a flower. It was an unexpected treat.

Title: "Comforting Vegan Delights Delivered by CHLOE"

Amid the quarantine blues, by CHLOE has emerged as my go-to for top-notch vegan delivery. With two orders under my belt, I'm thoroughly impressed by the variety and quality of their plant-based offerings. Each dish strikes a balance between health-conscious and indulgent.

The standout for me is their innovative mac n'cheese, featuring a creamy sweet potato-cashew cheese sauce, shiitake bacon, and a sprinkle of almonds – a dairy-free wonder that will leave you questioning its vegan authenticity. Equally impressive is the market veggie special; the sweet and spicy brussel sprouts with scallions are tossed in a sauce that tantalizes the taste buds.

The kale artichoke dip deserves applause, arriving warm and serving as a luscious counterpart to their crisp chips. And then there's the tempeh 'chicky' – my first foray into this chickpea-based creation did not disappoint, especially in the 'chicky chicky parm parm', where it's a convincing stand-in for meat.

My only quibble lies with the crispy chicky salad – it's a promising concept that fell short on dressing, a tip I hope to remember for future orders.

A special nod to by CHLOE's staff, whose commitment during tough times is truly commendable. Their efforts have not gone unnoticed, and I eagerly anticipate my next vegan feast from them.

PURCHASED: Philly cheese burger TOTAL: ~$8.50PROS:+ veggies: the mushroom and bell peppers were nicely cooked. CONS:- par to sub-par ingredients: The bun was very dry (see photo). The next to be tasted is the cheese. I don't know... you be the judge (also see photo). - bland: It tasted quite bland. Perhaps the burger would be better designed with a sauce. - inability to read directions: The staff did not cook my "patty" to be medium rare. In hindsight, that might have been a good idea that they cooked it well done. - greasy: As I just finished the last bite approximately 2 minutes ago, I can still taste that taste of oil in your mouth on your tongue. I can taste the quality of the oil too, it doesn't taste like olive oil. IMPRESSION:I saw the other reviews and the average of this spot to be a 3-star. In my opinion, I tried a burger at a place called "Pastafina Pizza" suggestive of a place that probably is not good for what I ordered (philly cheese steak burger). i.e., I actually would come back, but maybe not try the Philly Cheese Steak BURGER. SMH

Holy smokes this places deserves all the stars it can get! The experience was great and the food was delicious. The tikka masala was the best  I've  ever had. We ordered several apps that were just as great and even a tikka masala to go. The service was fantastic. They were busy but took pride in making sure you were attended. I wish I could remember the servers name but it seemed consistent all around. I plan to visit whenever I am in the area.

Title: A Delightful Family Dining Experience at Green Kitchen

My family and I recently dined at Green Kitchen, a bustling diner with an extensive menu that caters to all tastes. The staff outshone themselves with their kindness and accommodation, especially towards the children in our group, making our dining experience seamless and enjoyable.

I savored an avocado stuffed with a refreshing tuna salad, while the rest of my party enjoyed hearty wraps and perfectly cooked eggs. We were all impressed by the generous portion sizes and the undeniable freshness of the ingredients.

Moreover, Green Kitchen's willingness to make substitutions for side dishes without a fuss is worth noting. Such flexibility is a testament to their customer-oriented service.

I'm pleased to say we're all excited about our next visit to Green Kitchen; it's a gem that has undoubtedly won its place as a family favorite.

Pastis has made a triumphant return, taking over the once-dreary Gansevoort Market space and turning it into a marvelous recreation of its previous dining room. The buzz was palpable from the get-go, with crowds flocking in from the opening bell at 4pm. The menu impresses across the board, but the standout is the new Herring appetizer—a must-try for any diner. This place is a shining example of a comeback done right.

Title: A Taste of Tokyo in Times Square at Ichiran

If you're craving authentic Japanese ramen amid the bustle of Times Square, Ichiran serves up a quintessential experience complete with the same delectable flavors you’d find in Japan. Renowned for their pork-based broth, Ichiran ensures that each bowl of noodles is both rich and savory. What makes dining here unique is the individual booths, providing a distinctive solitary dining experience reminiscent of Japan's ramen culture.

Don't worry about carrying cash; Ichiran is a credit card-only establishment and tipping isn't necessary. Customizing your ramen is a breeze - simply check off any add-ons you desire on the provided sheet. Ideal for a speedy yet fulfilling meal, your order swiftly arrives after a few minutes, ensuring you won’t miss your next engagement in the city.

For those inclined to pair their meal with a beverage, Ichiran’s menu includes unique alcoholic selections, such as matcha beer and sake. Embrace the full experience, drink in hand, and enjoy a slice of Japan in the heart of New York City.

I'll keep this short. Portuguese egg tart is soo good and not a surprise since they are known for that here. Coconut tart was not for me, a bit dry and a bit cold. Char sui bun was a hard pass. This was kinda embarrassing you see, if you take a look at the photo you will understand why. Final verdict - come for the egg tarts, skip the rest.

What an amazing place- The food was good. The drinks were fire. The ambiance was fantastic. - We stumbled across this place walking around the west village and I'm so glad we did- It's not on a busy street so the area is very quiet (no need to yell across the table)- The drinks are strong but the food takes a while to come - Halfway through our meal we realized there was a whole section at the back for larger groups and normal tables- They have two high top tables outside and some seating right by the bar- Perfect for warmer weather- Come to catch up with a friend, come for a date, or come with some friends to chill

Dallas BBQ was an ok experience. The most memorable part of my trip was the mimosa cocktail I had. It was pretty big and got the job done, if you catch my drift. The food left much to be desired. The ribs were tender, yes, but the sauce tasted like something they order in bulk somewhere. There's nothing distinct or special about the flavor. The ribs don't seem to be smoked or roasted in any particular way. Same goes for the shrimp - plainly fried and no special house dipping sauce. My side salad was presented without the dressing I requested, and our server didn't come back so that I could ask. My cornbread was from a burnt batch, hard and dry. I'd come back for the drinks, which seem to be a specialty, but you can surely pass on the food here.

I recently dined at this restaurant where the offerings were fairly decent considering the price. I was taken aback when I discovered the mango chicken did not include rice—it seems like a given to pair the two, yet here, rice was an additional cost. The chicken skewed too sour, lacking the expected sweetness. Their beef chow fun featured excellent noodles, though they were mildly under-seasoned and disappointingly scant on meat content. On a positive note, the juices served were delightful, and the roti was indeed a highlight of the meal.

Everything my friends and I tried here were amazing. My absolute favorite was the appetizer. We tried the polpo (fried octopus) I believe and oh my, every piece melted in my mouth. It came out hot and fresh, and I don't think I enjoyed an appetizer this much in a while. As for main dishes, we tried a special w/ anchovies, black squid ink pasta, and crab pasta. The crab pasta was the best out of the three. I'm particularly not a fan of anchovies so although it was an interesting combination with goat cheese, it didn't fit my taste buds. In other thoughts, the ambience was really nice and the service was great. This restaurant is also very accommodating to large groups. Highly recommend!

I came with a group of three to the Mari Vanna Sunday buffet. For $39 you will get all you can eat and all you can drink bottomless mimosas or bloody Marys.  For being in New York, I thought this was a heck of a deal!  Two of us in the group were not Russian, but the third was and they enjoyed conversing with the staff in their native language.  For the rest of us, we were still able to navigate just fine.  It was nice having someone with a russian background with us who could help explain all the dishes, when they are traditionally served, etc.  It  really added to the experience. So if you have a russian friend, bring them with you! If you don't, you really need to get out more :)The buffet offered a ton of different options and I did my best to try at least a spoonful of each. Veal pelmini (yum!), potato pelmini, chicken, beef stroganoff, soups, and a bout a dozen different sales featuring beets, cucumbers, lots of dill and sour cream, and of course, herring.  I was too stuffed for dessert but they had several options for that as well including a crepe-like pastry that you add sweet condensed milk to. I had the mimosa which was very good--a nice balance of champagne and orange juice.  They make these in large pitchers which means refills come quicker than they do with the blood marys which they dont make until you order.  The blood mary that I tried had a great taste and a nice spicy kick, but not so spicy that it would be unenjoyable for those who aren't big on heat.The ambiance is amazing.  I feel like I had stepped into a russian grandmother's home.  The ambiance carried over into the uni-sex bathrooms which were kept nice and clean.  Overall a really great time that everyone should experience at least once!

Title: A Trustworthy Experience at Sugarfish

After much anticipation, I finally visited Sugarfish and it did not disappoint. Despite its hype, the experience warranted a solid 5-star rating. Opting for the Omakase style, we chose both the "Trust Me" and "Nozawa Trust Me" sets. The Nozawa is the pricier of the two by about $20, offering additional Nigiri and two exceptional scallop pieces - a true standout. 

Sauces here complement rather than overshadow the fresh fish, allowing the sublime flavors to take center stage. Each dish from the edamame to the tuna ponzu was delightful, but the toro and blue crab hand rolls were celestial delights I'd return for without hesitation. The Nigiri, albeit excellent, didn't strike me as extraordinary compared to other quality sushi spots.

Be aware, the sushi comes with tender, warm rice that may fall apart easily, but it's a minor inconvenience for such flavor. Service advice is to avoid dipping sauced fish into soy sauce, and they mean it - the flavors are balanced perfectly without it.

Arriving around 4:40pm, we encountered a significant queue, underscoring the restaurant's popularity. Once called from the upstairs waiting area, service was swift, with the entire meal concluding in under an hour. A brief pause between each plate allowed for appreciation of the offerings.

Conclusively, Sugarfish is a must-try for omakase-style sushi in NYC, offering great value. Not every piece may astound, but as a whole, the meal is a culinary triumph. A thoughtful note on the receipt reminded us that tipping is unnecessary as it's included, which is appreciated.

In summary, while not every bite will revolutionize your palate, the collective experience at Sugarfish is nothing short of amazing.
The beef noodle soup was pretty good (as long as you can handle a little spice), but would not recommend getting the bubble tea (overpriced and not great) or the sushi (not fresh at all).

If I had to describe this meal in two words they would be 'sensory overload'. Don't get me wrong, the flavors were very tasty. The calamari was nicely battered and fried, and somehow the food was simultaneously too sweet, too salty and too spicy for me. I remember accidentally biting into some of the many peppercorns in the pepper fish and needing to rinse my mouth with my glass of water. By the end of the meal, my mouth was almost numb from all the flavors.

I recently dined with a friend at this restaurant and was thoroughly impressed by both the food and service. We started off by splitting a poutine, which was delightful. For our main course, we each indulged in the burger with bacon and egg, and it was nothing short of perfect. While I haven't experienced their Chicago location to compare, I can confidently say that this burger stands out on its own merit. Highly recommend for a satisfying meal!

One of my favorite places for Korean food in the city. FWIW I try to avoid eating beef, which rules most of the menu for me, yet I'm still looking forward to the next time I can visit. I really enjoyed and would recommend everything that I tried. The lunch sets that come with a stew are a great deal in my opinion.Standouts:-Busan neighborhood pancake ($21 dinner) - so so good. Really enjoyed the texture (and love the gochujaru in the batter).-Silken tofu stew - really flavorful, and the texture of the silken tofu is perfect. I didn't eat any of the short rib in this but my friend said it was great.-Asian pear sorbet ($7) - delicious and refreshing dessert! It's not too sweet, with a hint of bitterness and a slight tang from the yuzu honey.Recommended:-Grilled mackerel over rice ($18 dinner) - lovely tender texture and crisp skin. The bottom was too salty for me but I enjoyed the rest.-Stone-bowl octopus over rice ($16 lunch) - might be a bit spicy for some but I really liked this.

Tucked away in NYC's bustling Chinatown, this quaint eatery offers all-day dim sum worthy of a patient wait for its freshly steamed delights. Standouts included the Blanched Seasonal Vegetable, offering a sweet and authentic taste of baby Yau Choi, a refreshing deviation from the usual. The Beef Balls impressed with their purity, free from the common aftertaste of tenderizers. Pork Spare Ribs with Rice triumphed with tenderness, edging out the competition from my previous dining experience at THW. The Siu Mai, primarily lean meat, shone with natural flavors, suggesting minimal to no MSG usage. While the Har Gow's craftsmanship was evident in the delicate skin, a fishy undertone from the seasoning made it my least favorite. This local gem is certainly on my list for a return visit.

Title: Great Vegetarian Sushi, But Packaging Needs Improvement

I recently dined at this restaurant for lunch and was thoroughly impressed with the vegetarian offerings of seaweed salad, a sweet tree roll, and a spicy mang roll. The freshness and flavor of the food undoubtedly deserve a five-star rating.

However, my experience was dampened by the excessive packaging. I attempted to request more sustainable options, such as combining the two rolls into a single container and reducing the individual packaging of sauces, but the kitchen setup with the chef's back to customers made communication difficult. The result was a disappointing amount of waste.

In conclusion, the culinary aspect of my visit was exceptional, but I hope the restaurant will consider more eco-friendly packaging solutions. A solid 3-star experience with room for environmental improvement.

"Listen, it's Sunday and it's past my bedtime," I said, my voice wavering and becoming less resolute as Joshua (the bowtie-clad host who gracefully also bartends, spouts sake facts, and jokes -- the good kind) dangled an appetizing cocktail menu under our gazing eyes. Yes, I stayed up past my bedtime to write about this place, because it was that good. Everything about Sushi by Boū says: "Come in, relax, don't worry about a thing."Upon arriving, we had waited in the hotel lobby with sexy bachata music wafting from the speakers. We received plastic key cards to the hotel suite. The menu was tucked into the hotel card sleeve. The key card opens the suite room door, and Joshua kindly took our coats as our evening began. Interestingly, I had just attended an immersive theatre experience the night before, and I feel like Sushi By Boū nailed it. I love the way the hotel room creates a "cleansing" moment - the moment you hear the whirring of the lock opening- the moment that notifies you that you are about to be taken into another world. It's not the run-of-the-mill jazz background music. The music is hip and alive. And the second you sit down at the four seat sushi bar, you know it's going to be a show. Our chef for the night, Ashi, was serious and got down to business; as the night went on we got to coax his winning smile out more than once. He is mesmerizing to watch, his hands flying yet so precise. We knew we had one hour for the $125 omakase menu: 17 pieces. It was one of those experiences that simultaneously flew by because of how orgasmic every bite was, but also seemed to stretch out for a pleasing amount of time because of the atmosphere. The lighting and decor are careful to keep you "in" the experience. I sort of love the timed omakase experience because you're never left wondering for 15 minutes when your next piece is coming. It's right there, in front of you. My favorite pieces of night included the sea scallop (uuuuh), the uni (uuuuuuuuuh), and the toro (uuuuuuuuuuuuh). Ashi's eyes lit up when I moaned at the sea scallop because, I mean, it was his favorite too. Unbelievably fresh. This is about making sushi your new boo (bou). This is about bringing the knowledge and experience of authentic, fresh Japanese style sushi (not your caterpillar or California rolls, okay) to the world. I'm amazed at the intimacy they achieve while being open to banter and lightheartedness. It's so refreshing, and, hot tip, the summertime's gonna be fresh with their new patio bar. So line your Resy up for that date. I'll see you there, room service and all. I'll even stay up past my bedtime for it. After all, you uni live once.

I recently had the pleasure of attending a bachelorette party brunch at Coco J'adore, and it was a delightful experience. Our party of ten was seamlessly accommodated, and we were greeted by an incredibly friendly and attentive wait staff.

Opting for the brunch menu, we were treated to bottomless brunch beverages, including Mimosas and Bloody Marys, which were constantly topped up without a hitch. The food truly shone – my chicken sandwich entrée was nothing short of perfection. Around the table, the egg dishes and French toast also garnered high praise for both presentation and taste.

We kicked things off with a shared Burrata cheese appetizer, complemented by crustini in a rich, tomato-soup-like dip, and the truffle fries were an indulgent and delicious addition to our meal.

I'm already looking forward to returning to Coco J'adore with friends. The charming atmosphere not only enhanced our dining experience but also served as the perfect backdrop for our celebratory photos.

Very good food here! The atmosphere is great and the food options are well-rounded. The menu ordering is a bit weird, because you are writing what you want on a paper and you have to do it all on one paper so it can be a bit confusing with a larger group, especially when the food comes. That being said the tacos are good and everything has a lot of love put into it. Why they didn't get 5-stars: The pricing. Everything is pretty small so we had to order a lot and it's pretty overpriced, even for mid-town. $8 knock-off Modelo beers are decent, but also add up to a LOT.

I've been to the Chelsea market location previously and thought it was good. We came to this location around 6pm on a wednesday evening. The line was short, and moved quickly. The food is cheap, and was served to us right after ordering. There are no seats, just high tops for you to place your food and stand and eat. Not amazing Mexican food, but good for a quick, decent bite.

Despite the restaurant being only half-full, the service was regrettably slow, and there was an unexpected wait to be seated. However, the redeeming quality of this dining experience lies in the food itself, which was both enjoyable and a refreshing departure from typical sit-down fare. It's for this reason alone that I award a 3-star rating.

small food cart parked in front of Target, former of Grand St & Clinton St. The cart operates from the morning til the early night hours. Breakfast sandwiches and coffee served in the morning hours. Middle Eastern styles platters (eg., chicken over rice, lamb over rice, falafel) and a variety of grill sandwiches (hamburgers, hot dogs) from lunchtime to dinner time. Solid option for grab n go meals.Clean-looking new food truck to the Lower East Side area, positioned to take advantage of the increased foot traffic from places like Trader Joe's, Target, and the soon-to-be completes Essex Crossing Market.Prices are decent for a food cart.

Title: A Slurp Above the Rest – Top-Notch Ramen in NYC

I stopped by this gem on a Monday evening and it firmly established itself as a standout ramen destination in New York City. Kicking off with the Kakuni Bao, at $4 apiece, these pork buns are irresistible - do yourself a favor and grab a pair. My main course, the Tan Tan, tantalized with its subtle spice from the coconut curry and the umami depth of red miso ground pork, rounded out by pork chashu, aji-tama, and a fresh hint of cilantro. On the waiter's advice, I added menma for an extra $3, elevating an already delicious dish. Hearty and packed with flavor, this meal left me fully satisfied and eager for a return visit.

Title: "Klong: A Hidden Gem for Thai Cuisine"

I recently lunched at Klong and am happy to declare it a true gem! The value is incredible: an entree with two appetizers for just $10. My choices – sesame tofu and green salad followed by a generous and flavorful chicken red curry – did not disappoint. The curry balanced bell peppers with tender chicken, without being overly creamy or spicy. The sesame tofu was a standout, as was its accompanying sauce, and the salad with breaded tofu and peanut sauce provided a light, palate-cleansing start.

Even the additional crab rangoon and fried rice, brimming with onions and serrano peppers, were delightful, despite the rangoon's surprising combo of crab and egg. Though service was brisk to the point of feeling impersonal, its efficiency was impressive amid the lunchtime bustle, with seating and dish delivery happening almost instantly.

The decor deserves a mention too; it's chic, funky, and sets the perfect scene for a rendezvous. My experience at Klong has firmly established it as my new top pick for Thai cuisine in the city. Highly recommended!

Title: Mixed Experiences at Momosan – Excellence in Ramen Overshadowed by Hit-or-Miss Appetizers

Momosan, a dining spot that's been in the neighborhood for a couple of years, presents a curious case of culinary hits and misses. On my first visit, I was treated to their duck ramen – a dish that's available only selectively and one that set a high bar by being absolutely delicious.

However, a subsequent visit that focused solely on appetizers left me underwhelmed. The Momosan "Salisbury" Steak was overly sweet, more dessert than entrée, earning a mediocre 2.5/5 from me. The Peking Duck Taco suffered from a stale shell and an overly sweet apricot chili sauce, not doing justice to the well-cooked duck – another 2.5/5.

The Zuke Don and Tetsunabe Pork Gyoza were acceptable, both scoring a 3/5, but not without their faults in texture and potential for drying out, respectively. However, Momosan showed promise with the Crispy Mimiga – a delightful surprise at 4/5, and the Sticky Ribs topped my list with the same score, albeit with a wish for a more generous serving.

In short, while Momosan might be the go-to for some exceptional ramen – do consider dipping your toes into the appetizer menu with caution; it's a gamble where you might find a gem or two.

Came here around 6pm for a light dinner with friends. The place was pretty empty when we got there, so we were able to sit down immediately. There was only one waiter, but service was still good. However, I felt that the food was pretty mediocre, especially for the price. The octopus was really chewy and gummy - not a pleasant texture imo. The croquettes were definitely a highlight. The paella was tiny and there wasn't any soccarat at the bottom!!! Soccarat is the best part!

The decor is simple and calming. It's so hot outside and I'm grateful that this place has quality AC. I ordered the Tingy Tangy and substituted the white kimchi for the spicy kimchi which I was charged .50 for. The Sauce was a bit too tangy for me but it does taste like something people would enjoy. The dine-in water situation is pretty interesting. They have cool looking bottles but a refillable pitcher would've been easier for customers to refill their cups. So I only had one cup of water. Im going to give this place more tries and create my own noodle bowl, I don't want to give up on it yet. Staff was nice. Customers bus their own tables which is responsible but a bit confusing if it's your first time to put items in their designated areas.

Resturant week goodness!! Stepped in for lunch and left like I ate dinner. Resturant week is always my favorite because you get to try more expensive resturants at a good price, lunch was $26 per person. You recieved an appetizer and entree. Dessert was a extra $5. So that was a hard pass! I had the crab cake with a seafood sauce, it was a bit too fishy for me (also additional $5) my entree was the grilled salmon with fingerling potatoes and sauteed broccoli. It was cooked perfectly! Others at my table ordered the petit filet mignon...it was well flavored, cooked well and very tender. You did not need steak sauce, but we tried the signature sauce anyway. The sauce was really good.  Overall it was a good steak house experience.

I saw this place on a food Instagram page and I just had to try it for myself. Unlike most restaurants, you order your food at the counter when you first walk in, you're given a number, and you take any open seat you'd like. The food comes out very quickly and it is sizzling! The plate is heated to 500°F in order to cook the meat. My mom and I both ordered the Jumbo Classic Beef Pepper Rice. The idea is very simple; it comes with rice, corn, beef, and green onions, but it's actually really good. When you get your food, you mix it up until your meat is cooked to your liking. I added some sweet garlic sauce, which really elevated the flavors. Order:- Jumbo Classic Beef Pepper Rice (4/5) Pros:- Food is tasty ~ nothing better than the sound of meet sizzling!- A good number of options between Pepper Rice and Steaks- Servers are very nice - Restaurant is clean and wasn't busy when we came by - All the utensils and condiments you need are at the table - No tip ~ although we left a tip because we thought the food and service was good Cons:- Obviously the dish is called "Pepper Rice", but I wish I could have controlled the level of pepper myself. I felt as though my dish had a little bit too much betterOverall:- I enjoyed my meal and thought for the food and idea it was decently priced. I highly recommend if you find yourself in the area!

Came here on a night out at Chelsea Market. There was no line at about an hour before their closed, which was nice. I got a honey fried chicken sandwich that was delicious -- very sticky and the pickles on it were the perfect sour / acid complement to the sweet honey chicken. I do wish the chicken filet was a little bit more plump, which I think could help with the overall mouth feel as well. The sweet potato fries were standard, along with the chocolate malt milkshake -- nothing too awe inspiring. However, the sauce the sweet pots are served with, really good, and they use these big paper straws for the shakes which are fun.

Big fan of Havana Central. Great for lunch, dinner or just appetizers with cocktails. My favorite is the ultimate mojito.As for appetizers, 2 of their bests are the queso fundido and the tostones rellenos (as a personal preference, i avoid the chorizo).

Title: A Flavorful Experience with a Side of Caution

I recently visited a local eatery well-known for its Asian cuisine, and the experience was a mix of hits and misses. We started off with a small portion of fried chicken, which, while tender and crispy, was unfortunately underwhelming in the flavor department. It was passable, but I'm not rushing to order it again.

The main event, however, was a pleasant surprise. The Niku and Kani Ankake udon noodles were the stars of the evening. Despite my usual indifference towards udon, these chewy, perfectly al dente noodles won me over. The Niku udon, laden with beef and tripe, bathed in a slightly sweet broth, was reminiscent of a comforting Chinese beef stew wonton soup – absolutely delightful. Its counterpart, the Kani Ankake, with its robust seafood flavors and aroma, could be overbearing for those less inclined towards maritime fare. Between the two, the Niku was our unanimous favorite.

A word to the wise for future patrons: prepare to pay with greenbacks as this spot is strictly cash only. Despite the minor hiccup with the starter, the aromatic and tantalizing udon dishes make for a worthy visit.

In the heart of Little Italy!The reason I dropped a star was because the hosts were outside smoking and trying to get people to come into the restaurant. We had reservations so we were headed in when one of them came to open the door. While it's such a lovely gesture to open the door for us, it wasn't so lovely to walk through a cloud of smoke and smell his smoke filled breath. Having people greet you with cigarette smoke all around is a turn off. The only reason we went in was because of our reservations. A just a moment in my soap box, smoking causes cancer. It's a nice little restaurant! I found it by searching on Yelp. It was beautifully decorated for Christmas and a small band came in playing Christmas music. My daughter got the pesto pasta and I got the salmon. The bread with dipping oil was delicious! Everything was very nice. The servers were very attentive. Overall, I'd say check it out. Hopefully they'll not have the hosts blowing smoke in front of the restaurant!

My coworkers and I came here for lunch. For the most part it was a typical burger and beer kind of place serving New American cuisine. I had the squid ink pasta and it was just okay. The pasta was rather soft (overcooked) and the flavors were kind of boring. I'll probably stick to a burger next time.

I recently opted for takeout from a local spot and was impressed with the speed and quality of service. My order consisted of Princess Tofu and Braised Pork with Preserved Vegetables, and it was ready in a mere 5 minutes. I appreciated the thoughtful packaging, with each box securely wrapped in a plastic bag to prevent any sauce leakage – a messy issue I've encountered before. Once home, a quick 3-minute zap in the microwave for each dish, and they were as delectable as dining in the restaurant itself. Excellent for a no-fuss, tasty meal at home.

We recently dined at a fantastic restaurant that truly impressed us with its culinary offerings. Despite not being a beet enthusiast, I found their burrata with beets and figs delightful, with the fresh figs and balsamic adding a refreshing touch. The tuna and hamachi tartare stood out with its impeccably fresh fish and a remarkable sauce that elevated the dish.

Their truffle squid ink gnocchi was a star – rich, indulgent, and satisfying enough to serve as a standalone entree. My husband's ivy burger earned high praise, perfectly complemented by the delicious sweet potato fries. Even the Brussels sprouts were a hit, with pancetta infusing them with a savory depth.

In summary, this eatery is a must-visit destination for anyone in the area looking for an exceptional meal. The quality of the food and the enjoyment it brings should not be missed.

I noted that with this order, their prices went up by $1-$2 a dish online compared to the flier I have. (hey its midtown)Overall, this order, the mala (麻辣) was not strong enough and was only slightly existent in the ChongQing Noodles. Very Disappointing compared to my previous visits. A star as been lost on my rating.The first dish I got was the SS3 Chongqing Hot Pepper Noodles.  This was a decent dish with soft long noodles, but without any protein and strong Chongqing mala flavor, probably too expensive at $8.95.  I also got the L5 Kung Pao chicken because I felt like seeing how this places does an Americanized-Chinese dish.  If only it had 麻辣, like I requested, it might have been really good rather than just good.  It had decent sweetness, which I kind of liked, but definitely was not spicy enough.I did state in the special instructions I wanted 麻辣, but didn't get it. Any dish should be able to made mala. Maybe they should think about adding a checkbox to make any dish mala. If its the cost, just charge an extra $0.50 for it.  I'd gladly pay it as that unique flavor is the main reason I go eat Szechuan.After much disappointment with mala at several of the midtown restaurants, including Savour Sichuan, I have bought some of my own Szechuan Peppercorns and will try to make my own seasoning this week with a skillet and a coffee grinder.  I also bought some chili paste from Hong Kong Supermarket that has the intensity of mala I'm looking for.  I will probably come back to try a few more things, but may not need to if I can make my own mala seasoning/paste and cook at home.The lady behind the counter is forever nice.I still recommend Zest.  Just stick with L6 or L14 lunch specials if you seek the mala like I do.  With the price increase, Mala Project and Cafe China are also good alternatives if you live/work closer to those.To date:(Most Favorite) L6 - L14 - SS3 - L5 - L28  (Least Favorite)

Saturday afternoon, plenty of space available in this large casual fried chicken stop. Standard menu of various chicken pieces, meals, and comfort sides.Didn't really want fries (which are included in the combo), instead getting things "a la carte". Decided on a Fried Chicken Breast ($5.85), a Buttermilk Biscuit ($1.75), and a beer ($6.50). Beer is given immediately while you wait for the buzzer to go off for the food. Chicken is heavily breaded, lots of grease inside as well as juicy white meat. Could have used more heat/spices, though you get several dip options at the condiment stations. Buttermilk biscuit was a disappointment - seemed reheated and barely had any flavor (some butter helped).For a quick, greasy fix then it does fine - not worth making a trip over for.

I recently visited a local pizza spot and decided to indulge in a classic pepperoni pie, opting for toppings on just half. While the pizza itself was quite delicious, the price did raise my eyebrows. The final bill came to $33, which felt steep, even by New York City standards. Though I savored every bite, in the future, I might explore other pizzerias in the area to see if I can find a better balance of quality and cost, particularly for delivery orders.

I been thinking grilled cheese for a while now, but I was not going to settle for just 2 slices of white bread and a slice of American kraft cheese in between.And then I saw a review of the Melt Shop and I knew I had to check it out myself. They have a few locations so I went to the one closest to the PABT so I can take it home.The menu is pretty good size and they show what it looks like.  They, of course, have a range of melts for you to choose from with ad-ons so you can customized it even with extra chicken or hamburger, they also got salads, shakes, etc. and some seating in a clean shop.I picked the fried chicken melt with slaw inside, pepper jack. And I added bacon and slice tomato as extra topping mostly on I never had a purple grill cheese before.They give you a buzzer and order came out within a few minutes and it was exactly what I asked for.  It's was a thick sandwich and was a little messy to hold but overall it was very good. The chicken was juicy and fresh. The veggies were all fresh to but the pepper jack was a little spicy for me. I'm not sure if you can mix and match the cheese here.But I will still recommend this place because I got stuffed on the sandwich alone. Next time I get a craving I am coming here again.

This place has a special place in my heart with me and my partner. We lived right around the corner from here for years and this is always the cheap, fast, and delicious comfort food we craved. While there are definitely better places in the city for pho, it's so fast and cheap and the apps are always good. The different types of curry was always my go to because a friend says Vietnamese people often dont eat pho at restaurants because you can have better at home. After eating and drinking the thai tea here for years, I'd recommend it to anyone in the area and people that dont want to wait.

Popped in here for dinner with some friends on a Saturday night while waiting to get in at Attaboy and had a great meal (we were also able to sit at the bar right away). I had the Ume combo (yellow tail, salmon, crunchy tuna) as well as a crab meat and eel hand roll - eel was my favorite. Great bathroom, too - shout-out to that heated toilet seat.Kazunori is still my fave but this is up there. Way chiller vibe, too. 4.5 stars.

I'm really glad I came here for lunch. The food was delicious and the service was great! Since it was Good Friday I couldn't try the meat dishes (I will definitely next time) but what we ordered was still really good. The garlic bread was crunchy and exactly what I want when I think garlic bread. The baked clam was my favorite! The sauce underneath tied the dish together and was flavorful. For the entree we ordered the Lobster Ravioli alla Vodka and Puglia's Famous Rigatoni Vodka. Both dishes were very filling and savory. Since I couldn't resist the Italian atmosphere I got the cannoli for dessert. The presentation was cute and the filling was fresh. The service was very attentive and the food came out at a timely rate. There was a big party dining next to us and the servers put on a live singing performance which was very entertaining. I left the restaurant humming It's Amore!~

So I went here and barn up 35 and Frankly prefer the ambiance here ; slightly less gadtropubby but definitely keeping up the authentic vibe. Got the sashimi bibimbap here and the seafood japchae ; same things I got at at barn joo 35; the back rook,is slightly quieter and better if you wanna talk with your date. Took my brother visiting from California before hitting equinox as a " light snack" ( heavy eating runs in the family) and it's the perfect blend of classy and comfortable casual ; definitely recommend

When I heard Pinch Chinese had a chef from Din Tai Fung (my literal favorite dumpling place), I had to come. I think it is overall a good way to tide me over until I go back to the west coast again / abroad for the original.We came here for happy hour on a Saturday. They have happy hour 7 days a week in the lounge and at the bar. Through Resy, you can also reserve lounge spots, which is really nice and convenient. This place is really kitschy (?) but still trendy - the decor/menu is really funny and charming, but you still get a cool vibe from the restaurant.We ordered the chicken soup dumplings, pork soup dumplings and the spicy wontons. I liked the chicken and pork dumplings - the dough was perfect and the filling was really flavorful and moist (a la DTF), but found the spicy wontons to be more of a "smokey" / oily taste. I probably wouldn't order them again. The chicken wings looked really, really good but the waiter forgot to put in our order for our second round of food / drinks, so perhaps next time.I also got the "Bartender's Choice" mocktail - a delicious blend of rose water / green tea / lychee that was great (and not too sweet). My sister got the red cider and thought it was good (though perhaps nothing to write home about).Overall, I think this place is a solid 4 stars. Come for a date or a good time - the dumplings are top notch and the atmosphere is fun. I would knock of a point or two for the service (they didn't leave the top of the dumpling basket so our dumplings dried out in a few minutes, the waiter forgot to put in our order for more food, etc.)

Title: Authentic Italian Gem Despite the Wait

From the moment you step inside, you're warmly embraced by an atmosphere reminiscent of an Italian family home, setting the stage for an outstanding dining experience. The star of the show is undoubtedly the pizza – simply the best! Each bite transports you to culinary heaven, making you exclaim "OMG!" with every slice.

Be prepared for a considerable wait time; this place is no secret among pizza aficionados. The parking situation is less than ideal, so consider ride-sharing or getting dropped off to avoid the hassle. Once you're seated, the service is attentive and prompt, ensuring your wait is well rewarded. 

In summary, if you're craving authentic pizza with a side of cozy ambiance and can overlook the parking woes, this restaurant is a must-visit!

I recently dined at this spot known for its authentic noodle dishes and was thoroughly impressed. The service was incredibly swift, leaving little wait time before diving into their signature Lanzhou noodles. I opted for the thick noodles, while my friend enjoyed the spicy kick of the Mala Noodles. Both dishes were devoured promptly, a testament to their deliciousness, though a splash of vinegar might have elevated mine even further, reminiscent of my time in Beijing.

We also tried the eggplant salad, which was a hit with its intense garlic flavor. I'm already planning a return visit to tackle the dapanji, a generous chicken plate, and to relish more of their scrumptious noodles. Definitely worth a repeat visit!

After much anticipation, I finally made it to this local brunch spot on a Sunday with a reservation in hand. The uncrowded dining room was a plus, offering a more relaxed atmosphere. However, service seemed stretched thin as one waitress managed the entire space. While friendly and pleasant in demeanor, she was a bit absent-minded. Our main issue came with the bottomless mimosas that we eagerly ordered but frustratingly did not receive alongside our meal. It took an intervention at the bar and a conversation with the harried waitress – who apologized for the oversight – to get our drinks. By the time they arrived, our brunch was nearly finished. Given the delay and the fact that the "bottomless" aspect was moot, a complimentary gesture would have been appropriate.

Despite the high praises I've heard about this place, my experience was shadowed by this lapse in service. While everyone can have an off day, it's left me with reservations about giving it another chance.

Tucked away in the city's bustling streets lies a culinary gem for Georgian cuisine aficionados. While the décor is unassuming, the flavors crafted in this kitchen are nothing short of enchanting. The Khachapuri served here is an extraordinary experience; imagine a tender, warm embrace of cheese nestled within dough, offering comfort with every bite and whispering reassurances of worldly delights. However, the Khinkali, while tender and flavorful with a zesty zing, leaves a yearning for the juiciness one might expect from these traditional dumplings. Wine lovers will appreciate the thoughtful, albeit modest, selection of Georgian wines. A glass of Kisi comes highly recommended to perfectly complement the meal. This restaurant undoubtedly brings Tbilisi's heart to your table with every dish.

This place is Busy! Obviously a lot of people love it and I agree. I ordered the smothered chicken with a side of Mac and cheese and garlic mashed potatoes. The chicken was good the only problem is that they fry the chicken put the gravy on and then put it in the oven, making the crispy skin then become soggy. The chicken It's self was dark me and very juicy. I just wish they didn't reheat the chicken rather leave it crispy out of the fryer and then pour the gravy on it or put the gravy on the side. The mac and cheese was very tasty, make sure to eat it while it's hot, and the garlic mashed potatoes were good but could have used a bit more salt and been creamier. The portions are somewhat small but can be filling. Make sure you ask for the cornbread, which is very moist and cake-like. Over all the restaurant is very cozy, The food is delicious, and the staff is friendly.

Last night's visit to the Brazilian-style steakhouse offered a unique dining experience worthy of 4 stars. The restaurant week menu was a tempting deal at $42, providing an ample selection of meats served tableside on skewers, alongside a diverse salad bar and numerous side options. Newcomers should heed advice: save space for the main event by not overindulging at the salad bar.

The variety of meats, including beef, pork, lamb, and chicken, is the true highlight. My personal favorites were the succulent prime rib and the flavor-packed garlic steak, which stood out among the offerings. However, some cuts like the leg of lamb and the chicken were slightly over-salted for my taste. Still, the pork sausage did not disappoint.

Service was exceptional, with attentive and friendly servers ensuring a continuous offering of meats, dictated by the simple flip of a card provided at the table.

Despite the food deserving a 3 out of 5 due to the seasoning on a couple of the meats, the overall experience was positive. It's a place I'd certainly revisit to sample more of their delicious prime rib and garlic steak.

I came in with high expectations seeing all the yelp reviews, but unfortunately this place was a little mediocre in my opinion and not all that great.Interior -- pretty modern looking, they have a bar area right by the entrance where you can also dine at. Two floors so pretty big, the bottom area wasn't open for brunch and seemed like it was for dinner dining.Service -- mediocre, not much to comment there. They won't sit you unless your full party is here (which makes sense considering how busy they typically are). Food -- but the food was pretty good! definitely didn't make the wrong choice going with their top 1 plate, the French toast. Soft yet a bit chewy. It was sweet yet not too greasy with fresh strawberries and bananas. The size was fairly decent. With the order of a coffee on the side, it came out to be $30 per person with tax and tips. I will be honest tho... didn't think it was worth the price since service typically makes up for a big portion of my dining experience. We came out here from the upper west because of its reputation, but the service was kinda disappointing. Could have just stayed nearby, pay about the same price for similar food, and get much better service :/

Title: A Hidden Gem with a Homely Touch

My recent visit to this quaint eatery was a delightful surprise. The restaurant's unique decor creates a bustling yet serene ambiance that immediately puts you at ease. The staff greeted us with unwavering warmth, adding to the welcoming vibe of the place.

We savored the mixed grill platter alongside the agora salad; both were impeccably portioned, delivering a harmonious blend of flavors that catered perfectly to our appetite. The standout of the dining experience, however, was their old family recipe rice pudding. It offered a refreshing twist on the classic dessert, pleasing our palates with its distinctive taste.

To complement the meal, we indulged in their recommended Turkish wine, which proved to be a refined choice that shouldn't be missed. This charming spot left a memorable imprint, boasting a perfect trio of ambiance, service, and culinary delight.

When I think of classic New York dining, I think of the Grill.  It's elevated classic American fare in an ambiance that feels straight out of Mad Men.  The service is a bit stuffy but friendly and efficient.  The food is decent (stuff my grandpa would like) but totally overpriced for what it is.  The crabcake is delicious, but priced at $40, not for the average person.  The pasta is very delicious.  The sandwiches are okay but pricey and not served with a side.This is the perfect spot for a business meeting.  The dining area is quiet and spacious.  Definitely a spot for an older crowd.

I recently ordered a burger from this spot, and I must say, the burger was exceptionally thick and satisfying, accompanied by a side of deliciously crispy fries. However, a word of caution for fellow diners: steer clear of the tomato sauce. It's laced with an overwhelming amount of cinnamon, which, for me, was quite off-putting. Delivery was impressively quick, although it did result in a slightly soggy meal by the time it arrived.

While in the City I met up with family to enjoy a steak dinner. We got there early so we waited at the bar and had a few drinks. The bartender was quick to get our drinks so our evening started out well. The bar area was large, plenty of bar stools and tables if you choose to dine in the bar area. Giovanni (sp?) took care of us and was the consummate professional. He was knowledgeable and helpful when it came to the menu. We started with an order of calamari and it was perfect. I ordered the petite ribeye which was 12oz., the perfect size being that I was not super hungry and the sides were plentiful. The temperature was perfect-medium rare; wouldn't have it any other way. In addition I ordered the sweet potato casserole. The sweet potato had a pecan crust and were absolutely delicious. My girlfriend had the lamb chops and they were cooked perfectly. The decor was classic steakhouse; the lighting was perfect but more importantly the service was spectacular from start to finish.

Title: Hand-Pulled Noodle Heaven

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this local gem renowned for its hand-pulled noodles and decided to try their Number 2, featuring roasted duck. The noodles were fantastic, offering a chance to customize with extra cilantro and chili sauce, though I passed on the latter. The roasted duck itself was the star, with generous portions of succulent meat that truly enhanced the meal. The broth struck a delectable balance, rich and meaty, and was packed with flavor that did not disappoint. Conveniently located, I chose this spot on a whim while in the area, but I’ve heard their Chinatown branch on Pell Street is just as exceptional. Highly recommended for noodle lovers!

I visited with some friends and made a reservation through Yelp for Saturday at 12:30 pm. It wasn't full, so I'm sure people who didn't have reservations would've been seated quickly, so don't worry if you stop by and forgot the reservations on a Saturday around noon. It's about a 5-minute walk from the D train and very easy to find. We got the 2 starter combos that allow you to choose from a variety of seafood boils and comes with a spicy popcorn chicken starter and a pick two option of fried calamari, chicken wings, or cajun fries. The food was good, but nothing different from places like other seafood boil spots. I wouldn't visit again for the $99 starter combo, it was definitely not worth the price, but I would return to try their seafood boil lunch combo during the weekday. (M-F 11:30am-3:30pm, no holidays for seafood under $22)As for the service, it was spectacular. The women with the single braided ponytail hooked us up with a free soda for checking in with Yelp and had an amazing, happy attitude. Individuals also often checked up on us to ask how we're doing, refill our water, and clean our plates of shells. They even helped us put the bibs on!tl;dr - $99 Starter Combo not worth the price, try the M-F Seafood Boil Lunch Combo, Service was spectacular.

Title: A Mixed Bag Brunch Experience on Father's Day

My boyfriend and I accidentally joined the Father's Day brunch crowd at this local spot. Expecting a long wait, we were pleasantly surprised to be seated within 10 minutes, thanks to the sweet hostess and our attentive server. I indulged in a farmers omelette with asparagus substitution - a truly excellent choice complemented by irresistible sourdough bread. My partner's lemon ricotta pancakes were a miss for him but a hit for me.

However, the experience was dampened by the restaurant's outdated ambiance, a less-than-pristine setting marked by a dirty mug and crumb-laden table upon arrival. Additionally, the premium pricing didn't align with the overall vibe and cleanliness. Though the food hit the mark, the atmosphere and value for money left room for improvement.
Pretty good deal. The fish was very fresh. They also sell fish, including uni (a box for around $75 I think).

I recently had the pleasure of dining in the private room of Capital Grille and the experience was nothing short of lovely. The multi-course meal began with appetizers and moved on to a spectacular entrée, which in my case was the crab and lobster sandwich. The tartar sauce was a perfectly balanced accompaniment. Alongside this, the salad offered a fresh, delicious contrast.

My companions had the steak and fish, both of which received high praise. Dessert was a trio of classics: New York style cheesecake, flourless chocolate espresso cake, and crème brûlée, each one hitting the sweet spot perfectly.

A special shout-out to our waiter, an attentive and friendly gentleman from Albania, whose service was top-notch and greatly enhanced the overall ambience of the dining experience. While I acknowledge the prices might be steep, based on this experience where the cost was covered, Capital Grille delivered a flawless meal.

I look forward to returning to Capital Grille, and for those willing to indulge in a great steak, it is definitely a strong recommendation.

This excellent craft beer bar has become something of a regular hangout for me while in New York, especially while staying at the nearby Marcel Hotel (around the corner). The people are friendly, the service is prompt and the craft beer selection excellent. I've found the food to be good and the portions large.The interior is long and wider than most pubs of this size with plenty of seating at the bar on the right, tall tables along the middle and booths to the left. The ceilings are tin and gives the place more of a local feel - there are plenty of flat panel TVs for watching your favorite sporting event.I try to get in as much local craft as possible - here's a list of what I've tried here over a few nights:Collective Arts Brewing Pineapple Tepache Berliner - Crisp little Berliner, more tart than sour. Super dry and a bit lemony with a yeasty nose. Saranac Brewing (F.X. Matt Brewing Co.) Polar Haze IPA - unfiltered, hazy, good with lots of citrus, mostly grapefruit and orange. Dry finish.Collective Arts Brewing Life in the Clouds NEIPA - Fairly juicy NEIPA, hoppy filled with great citrus notes. Orange and grapefruit dominate. Quite good, with a dry finish. DuClaw Brewing Co Purple Passion Gose - Tasty, passion fruit and berry throughout. More tart and sweet than sour. Nice body with great lacing and a dry finish. Big aLICe Brewing Co Big Bones Belgian Brown Ale - Interesting malty slightly tart dark Belgian with coffee/toffee notes. Effervescent with lacing for miles. Full body and slightly dry finish Brewery Ommegang Gnomegang Belgian Strong Golden Ale - Delicious colab epitomizing the best in Belgian higher ABV Blondes. Golden Ale color with heady fruity flavor profile and warm finish. DC Brau Brewing Turbo Boost Multi Ball IPA - Citrus forward and hazy. Lots of fruit but with a dryer body and dry finish. For food I've had the cheezy Tots and the Beef Fajitas - the tots are worth it. The Fajitas were filling but the meat portion seemed a bit smaller than I'm used to, otherwise very tasty. Service everytime has been fantastic - I especially like sitting at the bar.

Title: Disappointing Birthday Dinner at [Restaurant Name]

I recently visited [Restaurant Name] for a birthday celebration, eager to enjoy their four-course prix fixe menu. Unfortunately, the experience fell short of expectations. While the restaurant wasn't bustling, service was unexpectedly sluggish, and observing later arrivals receive and complete their meals before us added to the disappointment.

The majority of the dishes we tried ranged from forgettable to mediocre. However, there were a few standouts worth mentioning: the Vellutata, a decadent lobster soup enhanced with black truffle, the intriguing pairing of octopus with pork belly in the polipo dish, and the spaghetti, which was elevated by the inclusion of blue crab. These dishes provided a glimpse of what could have been a far more satisfying culinary experience.

In summary, despite the allure of a few select items, the overall pace and quality of the meal did not live up to expectations for a celebratory dinner.

Title: A Quick Bite at Tonii's Rice Rolls

Discovering rice rolls in the bustling streets of Chinatown is a food adventure in itself, and Tonii's is one of the latest spots to join the trend. The ambiance is typical of the area: don't come expecting stellar service. I was greeted with indifference by a young gentleman more engrossed in his phone than the arriving customers, prompting an awkward exchange just to place my order.

Opting for the beef roll with an added egg, I was pleasantly surprised by the generous portion size, especially considering the reasonable price point. Service was brisk, a welcome change from the slower pace of other eateries around.

While condiments like soy sauce and sriracha were readily available to customize my meal, the rice rolls themselves fell short on texture—bordering on soggy rather than the silky firmness that makes for an exceptional roll.

In summary, Tonii's offers a satisfactory, wallet-friendly option for those seeking a quick and hearty meal. Despite this, with the myriad of choices in Chinatown, it wouldn't be my top pick for rice rolls.

Nice spot for happy hour or dinner.  Nice selection of mixed drinks, beer and wine. We sat at the bar in the cocktail lounge.  Nice lighting with great ambiance.I recommend their Kale Salad includes black quinoa, orange, pecans, blood orange with honey lemon vinaigrette. You will think it's tasty! Also.... they offer oysters from west and east coast, thanks we appreciate that:)Closed on Mondays.
