Title: A Hand Roll Haven in the Heart of New York - KazuNori

Before moving to New York, I had not experienced the delight of hand rolls. Thankfully, KazuNori changed that, rapidly ascending to the pinnacle of my sushi favorites list in the city. Whenever I visit, I opt for the largest set (the precise number of rolls escapes me) - but take my advice, as inspired by Shia LaBeouf, just go for it.

The star of the show, without a doubt, is the toro roll - a must-try for any sushi enthusiast. Yet, regardless of which roll you choose, you're guaranteed a mouthful of freshness and high-quality fish that's bursting with flavor.

An additional perk is the no-tipping policy. Prices might seem slightly steep at first glance, but rest assured, they incorporate the service charge, which eases the calculation at the end of a delightful dining experience.

KazuNori is not just a place for local sushi aficionados but also a fantastic spot to impress those visiting from out of town. It's a culinary gem that deserves a spot on anyone's New York dining itinerary.

Title: A Satisfying Vietnamese Feast Delivered to My Doorstep

I recently indulged in a Vietnamese feast from the comfort of my home by ordering through UberEats. Opting for a vermicelli combo bowl along with two types of pho – chicken and beef – I was impressed with the packaging upon arrival. Everything was neatly arranged, with the pho garnishing thoughtfully separated to maintain freshness.

Taste was paramount, and the meal did not disappoint. My family found ourselves savoring the rich, authentic flavors, even circling back to fill our bowls a second time. While one can assume that the experience might be elevated by dining in, the quality of our delivery order was notably impressive.

Given the enjoyable experience and delectable food, this restaurant has earned my repeat business, and I eagerly anticipate our next order.

I finally made it to the highly-acclaimed Los Tacos No. 1 at Chelsea Market, ready to see if it lived up to the hype. Despite the daunting line, it actually gave me time to ponder the menu, settling on a carne asada taco for $3.95. The staff was helpful, guiding me through the ordering process since it was my first time there. After choosing all the toppings and a corn tortilla, I watched my taco being expertly assembled.

The carne asada was the star of the show with its fine chop and robust marination, seasoned to salty perfection. However, the corn tortilla didn't quite match up; it was limply structured and struggled to support the generous fillings, detracting from the overall experience.

In the end, Los Tacos No. 1 served a decent taco, especially if you're in New York with a taco craving, but it wasn't the transcendent experience I was anticipating. For the price and with such rave reviews, I expected more and was left wanting.

Title: Wild Rides but Wilder Prices at the Mechanical Bull Bar

Upon entering the Mechanical Bull Bar, the raucous atmosphere and centerpiece attraction—a mechanical bull—immediately set the tone for a night geared towards the partying college crowd. The coat check fee felt steep at $3, and I hoped that the rest of the experience would justify the cost.

The evening kicked off on a discordant note when I witnessed the blonde bartender lose composure during a heated exchange with a patron. The altercation escalated quickly, ending with drinks being discarded and security intervening. While the details of the conflict were unclear, the lack of professionalism was startling and soured the initial impression.

Attempting to move past the drama, my friends and I settled in for some grub. We ordered the bar's premium-priced burger, topped with bacon and sautéed onions, which thankfully did not disappoint in flavor, although the $20 price tag gave us pause. The Mac n' Cheese balls, however, were a letdown, lacking both moisture and the promised cheesy goodness.

The drink offerings were average, with a noticeable abundance of mixers in relatively small, deceptively thick plastic cups. This detail, alongside the inflated burger cost, suggested an unwelcome penny-pinching approach to service.

The mechanical bull provided some entertainment. My friends enthusiastically took turns, while I personally opted out, noting the duct-taped padding that hinted at potential safety issues despite the fun spectacle.

In summary, the Mechanical Bull Bar offers a certain kind of charm with its lively environment and unique bull-riding experience. However, the price points and a couple of service missteps indicate there's room for improvement. Fun for a night out? Potentially. Worth the premium prices and chaos? That's up for debate.

We got the braised beef dry noodle bowl with pickled bean toppings on the side. The noodles were the right amount of tenderness and not too mushy. It was very flavorful with a combo of spicy, sour, and savory. I did feel the price was pricier than I was used to for the quantity given but besides that, it was a yummy experience.

Title: A Masterpiece Burger at Black Iron, Urbanspace W52

I recently discovered a glorious addition to my burger palate: a sunny side up egg topping – an epiphany that occurred during a trip to the Philippines last year. Imagine my delight when I found this option at Black Iron in Urbanspace W52, aptly named the "Masterpiece."

This burger truly lives up to its name, boasting two perfectly cooked patties, a richly flavored sunny side up egg, crisp applewood smoked bacon, and melted cheddar cheese. The moment you slice into the burger, the yolk runs, melding with the other components to create a burst of savory goodness. If I were to nitpick, a thin slice of pickle would have made it even more perfect.

Make sure to add your favorite condiments for that personal touch. While they offer a variety of burgers, including a build-your-own option, the Masterpiece stands tall in its own right. At $19 with fries before tax, it's not an everyday indulgence for me, but for that special craving of runny yolk and hearty burger, Black Iron is my go-to spot.

Title: A Delightful Lunch Experience

My family and I visited this charming restaurant on a warm January weekend. Despite arriving at the peak of lunch hours at 2:45 pm on a Saturday, we were seated immediately in the moderately bustling atmosphere.

The cocktail menu was a highlight, featuring a variety of tempting options. We indulged in some, which were served promptly and did not disappoint. The lunch specials, priced at just $11, offered great value with well-sized portions of appetizers and entrees. I particularly enjoyed the green curry with tofu, which was flavorful and satisfying without being overly filling.

The service was a standout — attentive and friendly. The staff made sure our dining experience was smooth and pleasant. This restaurant's location makes it a perfect stop after a visit to Central Park, and based on our delightful experience, it's a spot we will surely revisit.

On a busy street with lots of other places to stop. This place has a black awning and you walk up a couple of stairs but easy to get into. It's a small spot but they have lots of seating that's pretty close together and a quick turn around. All the dishes were coming out of the kitchen pretty fast. We got there at just about noon and there were plenty of seats but it filled up soon. We ordered the King Fu XLB, string beans, Shanghai noodles, and chili chicken. We also tried the plum sake and a tsing Tao. Everything was freaking fantastic. Amazing flavor and beautiful presentation. The Kung Fu xlb was one of the best I have had. Great flavor and the broth was amazing. These are pork btw.  The string beans were delicious with a wonderful flavor, salty crispy, goodness. Order then. Eat them. My husband can barely stand heat but for this chili chicken he did it. He loved it. It was so good. There are a lot of chili's that come out on the plate but it's not as intimidating as it looks. It is spicy, don't get me wrong. I love heat and this was just a pleasant heat. They are breaded little chunks of chicken tossed with onions garlic and chili peppers and have a crunch and juicy texture all in one. Again, salty yummy goodness. The Shanghai noodles were a good add on to kill the heat. They had a wonderful grilled taste and had all the comfort food feelings that a good noodle gives you. There is one restroom in the back by the kitchen. The place is a tight squeeze but really I never saw a line. You may be seated by strangers but it's okay. The food is sooo worth it. Get there. Eat there. Die happy.

I came here the other day for lunch with a friend. We really wanted to try the burger, since we heard it was amazing. The service was amazing, the women assisting us was friendly and attentive. The even have gluten free options! My friend and I ordered the burger and mock tails. The mock tails were delicious! Hands down we were quite surprised by how they came out.The burger was really disappointing, it was huge but it lacked something. It wasn't that flavorful and just tasted like any regular burger. And the egg was over cooked, Also, I noticed a few small flies buzzing around us. It was annoying and we had no idea where they were coming from and it was bothersome while we were eating.

There are lots of casual breakfast cafe options in the city and while this one is cheap and in a convenient location, it's not worth your time whether you're a visitor or local. Key miss factors: food was average at best, even for simple breakfast foods. Service was lacking and the place felt like an oven - toasty but in a humid and uncomfortable way. Honestly, look for other local gems for similar prices and casual atmosphere, but don't waste a meal here.

I stopped by this chic new Thai spot late on a Sunday afternoon, sliding in just before their midday break. The restaurant's multi-level opulence is a growing trend among Thai eateries and quite inviting. Despite the looming siesta, I was promptly seated and handed a hefty menu.

Skipping appetizers, I dove straight into the main fare with the Mieng Pla Pao—a hefty $30 tag—but it was a worthwhile splurge. The dish featured a delicately flavored branzino filet accompanied by coconut sticky rice, nuts, and a sweet chili sauce. The fish paired wonderfully with the sauce, its subtle taste amplified by the sweetness, although the coconut rice didn't quite mesh as well with the flavors. Service was swift, with no compromise on the taste.

For those on a budget or looking to experiment, there's plenty more on the menu that doesn't hit the wallet as hard. Overall, a delightful culinary experience with the promise of more to explore.

I was extremely underwhelmed. I had high expectations from the reviews but the food was okay, def did not match the price. I wouldn't go back or recommend because it was overall mediocre flavor, especially when there are so many other places that serve chicken better. The peach cobbler I didnt like at all.

Title: A Gem of a Restaurant with Stellar Cuisine

I had the pleasure of dining at this amazing restaurant recently and it completely won me over. The menu boasts a vast array of choices, especially the appetizers, which come in both hot and cold varieties, and the drink selection doesn't disappoint either. The highlight of my meal was the linguini with seafood, which was both generous in portion and delicious in flavor.

For starters, the tuna with plantains offered a unique and delightful taste combination, while the octopus special was delectable in every bite. Dessert was a triumph too; the Tres leches cake's richness and size made it perfect for sharing.

Service here deserves a special mention; our waiter was the embodiment of friendliness and charm, contributing significantly to the dining experience. Despite its small size, the restaurant's ambiance is cozy and welcoming, making you feel right at home.

Without a doubt, I wholeheartedly recommend this place for an outstanding dining experience. It's a solid choice for anyone looking to enjoy a fantastic meal in a pleasant setting.

Tucked away on the Upper East Side, this Chinese restaurant is quite the hidden gem. Recently under new ownership, the revamped menu shines with its trendy, spicy offerings. While their famed pork ribs are a solid choice, the shredded beef with green chilies truly steals the show. Service is top-notch, with attentive servers ensuring a pleasant dining experience. Don't miss out on the wallet-friendly happy hour, featuring $4 beers, and the soup dumplings that rank among the best in the neighborhood. The decor is admittedly dated, but it's a small compromise for the quality of food and the convivial atmosphere suited for sharing plates. While it hasn't topped my list just yet, it's definitely in the running, and I'm keen to return or opt for takeout in the future.

Returning to Midtown, I stumbled upon a newly opened Vietnamese sandwich spot, right around where I work. Craving a sandwich, the timing couldn't have been better. Upon arrival, I faced a slight wait, buzzing with a modest queue at the kiosk machine. 

My order? A serving of double plain fries and 'The Sweet (JOJU),' a scrumptious combination of classic Vietnamese ham, pate, and caramel pork nestled within a sandwich. I spruced it up with a side of spicy mayo and a tantalizing spicy green sauce. 

The fries were a standout, sporting an irresistible crunch I absolutely savored. The sandwich, meanwhile, was a flavor bomb - the harmonious melding of ham, caramel pork, and pickled veggies was addictive. It's difficult to say which sauce won my heart, but the spicy green sauce certainly left a lasting impression.

Price-wise, it's typical Midtown fare, but for such quality, I'd happily indulge once a week. My next visit will be to explore their rice bowls and perhaps their Vietnamese coffee. In a nutshell, I'm enamored with this eatery and eagerly anticipate my next visit.

Went here for brunch with someone and was amazed at the quality of the food. I was told that it was difficult to find good Mexican food in NYC and after having gone to CDMX last year, I can attest to that. This place hits the spot with their strong, delicious drinks and great torta de milanesa. I liked their selection of drinks that has not only téquila but also mezcal. The sandwich was toasted well and the it was spectacular. I also had a barbacoa taco but it was not as good as the sandwich. However, I plan on coming back to try their blue corn tortilla options.

I had a delightful experience trying the lobster roll at this establishment. The lobster was seasoned to perfection, providing a burst of flavor with each bite. The roll struck an excellent balance between its slightly crunchy exterior and the softness within, making for a truly enjoyable texture contrast. However, be warned that the regular size might leave you wanting more; I suggest opting for the jumbo size if you're looking for a more satisfying meal.

Pretty good pho, esp for midtown. The short rib was on point, but didn't love the broth it came in as much as the regular beef broth. I'd recommend getting the regular beef pho and just adding the short rib for $7.

Title: A Fresh Mediterranean Breeze on University Place

Last night, the newest Mediterranean fast-casual gem graced University Place, sweeping away memories of the lackluster Panorama with its vibrant and expansive setting. The ordering process is as modern as they come, mirroring an Apple Store experience—just spot a staff member with an orange hat, tablet in hand, to place your order, then relax until your phone buzzes with the promise of a freshly prepared meal.

Their Green Baked Falafel, priced at $12, is a delight, rivaling the quality found at the city's top Mediterranean haunts. The Pinenut Matzo Ball Soup, a steal at $8, was a comforting ally against today's bone-chilling 10-degree chill. This place is a surefire hit for those seeking the allure of the Mediterranean with the convenience of a quick, hearty bite.

I went here for dinner with my friends last Saturday night. We had an a amazing time. This restaurant is a chain and is all over the United States. It is a Japanese BBQ, which is similar to Korean BBQ, but has its own twist.We ordered the Samurai platter. It came with everything pictured below. It was fun to cook the meats and the asparagus ourselves. The food was delicious and were definitely pretty stuffed afterwards. If you have four people I kn your group, I highly recommend the Samurai platter. We didn't feel like we were being rolled out of the restaurant, but we all felt a satisfied fullness.

Pricey for a tartinery. I got the roast beef tartinery which ended up being about 18 bucks after tax. The ingredients are not bad and it comes with a good amount of arugula and roast beef over sour dough but for the price and what you are exactly getting, overpriced.

The takeout from here is so good I can only imagine how good it is dining in! Definitely will be going here again!The beef pancake was a huge serving! Beef was flavorful and tender and the veggies had a great crunch! The wonton soup had a great broth, the wontons were packed full, and the noodles were a great consistency. I also asked for it to be spicy and they delivered a little jar of chili oil for me to add that packed a perfect punch!

Title: A Satisfying Ramen Experience at Ajisen

Ajisen may not be the most extravagant noodle hotspot, but it's a destination worth visiting for anyone craving a hearty and wallet-friendly bowl of ramen. With a special perk for Yelp users — a complimentary ice cream mochi upon check-in available in flavors like green tea, red bean, and vanilla — it sweetens the deal, quite literally.

I tried the Spicy Ajisen Ramen and was greeted with a generous serving that struck a balance between meat and noodles. The chashu pork was pleasantly lean, cutting down on the guilt without skimping on flavor. A modest amount of ground pork added another layer of taste. The broth won me over for not being a pool of grease or a salt bomb, making each slurp enjoyable. Alongside were the classic ramen accompaniments: a perfectly cooked egg, crunchy beansprouts, and fresh scallions.

Efficiency was the name of the game during my Sunday dinner visit. The service was swift, defying the bustling crowd, and I had a steaming bowl in front of me in under ten minutes post-order. Be warned that space is at a premium — seating is tight, with tables nestled close together, requiring some agile moves by the wait staff. But for a quick, satisfying noodle fix, Ajisen hits the spot.

Title: Hidden Gem Alert: Rin Thai Cuisine

If you haven't yet discovered Rin Thai, you're missing out on a neighborhood treasure. Despite its unassuming appearance, this spot never fails to deliver an exceptional dining experience. What's even more surprising is that you'll often find yourself among just a few diners, with no need for a reservation.

Service at Rin Thai is impressively swift, ensuring your delectable dish arrives hot and fresh without delay. On the wallet-friendly side, the prices are just as enticing as the food itself. As for the menu, everything I've savored has left me eager for the next bite. Top recommendations include the savory Pad See-Ew with Chicken, crispy Spring Rolls, the perfectly sweet Coconut Shrimp, the ever-popular Pad Thai with Chicken, and a flavorful Original Thai Fried Rice with Chicken.

For those in the vicinity, it's simple: Rin Thai is a must-try. It may not catch your eye at first glance, but trust me, the culinary experience inside is truly memorable.

Title: Buzzing New Spot with Room to Grow

I ventured into this newly opened hotspot, enticed by its limited reviews and hoping to discover an undiscovered gem. The reality was a bustling crowd with every inch occupied – clearly, the secret was out!

Faced with the chaos, I placed an order for sweet potato air fries at the kiosk, thinking a small order might mean a swift service. Alas, even a lap around the block didn't suffice; I clocked a 40-minute wait.

The eatery is a snug 'order-and-go' type with no seating options at present, possibly something they'll address with time. Pro tip: consider ordering via their app or online to potentially cut down on the wait.

When I finally got my hands on them, the sweet potato air fries fell short on seasoning – a pinch of salt away from perfection. And, as a heads up for the purists, air frying doesn't quite reach the indulgent heights of oil cooking.

I recently visited a bustling restaurant where the popularity seemed to surpass the space and comfort level. I found myself at a high table by the window, cramped and waiting longer than preferred for service. The meal, while flavorful, didn’t quite justify the price; although tasty, the portions didn’t measure up to expectations. An order of the "7 Minutes of Heaven" smoothie fell short of divine with its nearly flavorless profile that oddly conjured almond milk with hints of nachos. The struggle with an inadequate paper straw only added to the underwhelming experience.

Friday night for dinner. Ordered the nachos (must try!!) for an appetizer. Comes out piping hot, extra cheesy, and loaded with toppings. Ordered a burger and mac and cheese for our main. The burger was solid and sweet potato fries were good. Mac and cheese was okay- nothing special and the cheese was kind of runny. Bacon was a nice touch. Service was solid. Atmosphere is louder, a few families and great for groups. Highlight was the nachos; I'd go back just to order again.

First, great pizza and My Pie is more than just a NYC closet pizza shop. With a unique dough recipe and toppings that are upscale from the basic American options, My Pie produces some great pizza. Several people were timing their visit by which pizzas were coming out of the oven so that they could get the freshest slices.Many shops in NYC do nothing with their interiors but My Pie is a nice place to eat after you get your meal. Very pleasant place to visit and eat.Since their pizza reflects the pizza in Rome, you are not going to get a traditional slice of "NYC pie."

Title: A Charming Brunch Spot to Satisfy Any Craving

I recently visited a delightful little restaurant for a Sunday brunch, and it was an experience worth sharing. Making a reservation proved to be a wise decision, as the place quickly filled up by noon. The menu was refreshingly concise yet offered ample variety to cater to different tastes.

I indulged in a savory crepe filled with tomato, goat cheese, arugula, and topped with an egg – each bite was a delight, with the crepe itself being particularly noteworthy for its scrumptious taste. I found myself savoring every last piece. To complement my meal, I enjoyed a good cup of coffee, which was refilled continuously without having to ask.

The service was exceptional; attentive and prompt without being intrusive. The atmosphere of the restaurant was cozy and inviting, making it a perfect spot for a laid-back and satisfying meal. I would wholeheartedly recommend this local gem to anyone looking for a delicious brunch in a comfortable setting.

This place has the cutest vibes! You go downstairs to a lobby area that is so well decorated and the restaurant in further in the back. We tried the olive oil pancakes and the eggs Benedict. Both were really filling. The pancakes were fluffy and not too sweet. The eggs Benedict was well made and came with potatoes and a light salad. Both were around $15. The great atmosphere and good food make this place really enjoyable

Vaucluse is another restaurant (newish I believe?) from chef Michael White of Marea. I'd been to Marea before and wanted to try this place for awhile, especially because of its chic dining room. So my friends and I picked this place for a girls' Christmas lunch on a Sunday. We came in at around 1pm, with a party of four. We were seated immediately, and brought copies of the menu and waters. I noted that the dining room was certainly every bit as impressive as it looked in pictures, with an all-white, carpeted interior, large windows that let the natural light in, and white cushioned booths. Within a few moments, we ordered, with just one thing to share as an appetizer, and separate main dishes for each of us. The wait time for our appetizer (leeks) was average for a New York restaurant. We had been brought slices of complimentary bread and butter while waiting also. The leeks were garnished with crushed nuts, and contained the flavor of a strong olive oil. It was not terrible, but not remarkable either. Our main dishes were presented shortly. Myself and a friend both had the Niçoise salad- for a salad, this was quite good, with generous pieces of lightly seared, fresh tuna, amidst hard boiled egg slices and greens. Our two other friends had the epaulettes and chicken paillard - both remarked that their dishes were delicious. Vaucluse has a classically French dessert menu, and some of the girls opted to share an eclair, which they were both pleased with. Service was impeccable and prices were standard with New York restaurants. I suspect their dinner menu might contain more elaborate dishes than the brunch menu, and would come back to try a meal at a different time. Would recommend for a long lunch/dinner.

Title: A Delightful Discovery on the East Side

My recent visit to this understated gem on the east side was a thoroughly enjoyable experience. From the moment I walked in, the warm greeting set the tone for a comfortable and friendly atmosphere. Opting for a seat at the bar, I perused the neatly organized menu and decided on a margarita, a lobster taco, and grilled cornbread.

Each dish impressed me with its freshness and flavor. The lobster taco was particularly noteworthy – meaty and satisfying. The margarita was expertly mixed, striking the right balance between tart and sweet. But the star of the show may have been the grilled cornbread, served with delectably rich butter – a simple pleasure that hinted at the potential of a promising brunch menu.

The ambiance was further elevated by good music and engaging company, including the congenial bartenders. The staff's enthusiasm was infectious, enhancing the overall dining experience.

With plans to return for happy hour and more engaging conversation, this establishment has certainly earned a spot on my list of favorites. Whether the east side will continue to charm me as much as it did on this first visit remains to be seen, but I'm optimistic. Stay tuned for an update post-brunch!
Best tacos in the NYC! Definitely have to try them they are absolutely delicious! They are a little pricy for $3.75 each but was sooo worth it. (:

Delicious food, delicious wine, cool ambiance. We went here for dinner. For appetizers, we got escargot which was really delicious and pate (which we didn't like much but that's on us). For entree, we ordered trout amandine and entrecôte. They were both really really really delicious. Our water suggested us to drink Trousseau (type of red wine) that worked perfectly. For dessert, we got creme brûlée that came with a warm Madeleine. Overall, everything was great and we are excited to go back again!

Artichoke is a great place to go for a quick slice of pizza. Note it is cash only, kind of pricey, and barely any room to eat inside. I recommend getting your food to go. We ordered a slice of their famous artichoke pizza and a slice of the crab pizza. Both were delicious and huge! They were fresh and cheesy and full of flavor. It was even delicious to eat a bite of each together. Reminded me of the crab artichoke dip I love at the Cheesecake Factory.

I decided to give this place a second shot and though it was better than the first time, I don't see myself going back. My friend and I ordered the Beef Tendon with Chili, Cold Sesame Noodles (which were complimentary with a Yelp Check-in), and the Braised Pork Belly with Preserved Vegetables. The Beef Tendon with Chili was a complete miss and tasted as if hot chili oil was just dumped in them and then the chefs called it a day. The Cold Sesame Noodles were good but, let's be honest, it's hard to mess them up. The Braised Pork Belly dish, on the other hand, had meat that was well cooked and very flavorful but there was no need for the preserved vegetables. All in all, I wouldn't go back not because Zest Szechuan is bad but because there's so many better options in the area.

We were walking around and came across this place, we weren't sure at first, but decided to try it and glad we did. It has the wine cellar-type feel. The service was very attentive and quick. I got the margherita pizza and it was extremely good, quite tasty and full of flavor. We also had a salad and pasta, both were good and had nice presentation.

I stopped by and got a to go order of their 10. Royal 2nd Ave triple decker sandwich for $35.  It was relatively busy with quite a few people waiting for a table.  I wasn't sure where to order, but eventually a butcher asked if I was being helped and I gave him my order. In return, he gave me several scraps of Pastrami to try while I waited, which were very good.  I didn't wait too terribly long to get my food.It came with a bunch of their meats on it, but did not come with chopped liver or any other salads.I was surprised it came with pickles, after seeing everyone on here complain they they nickle and dime you for them.  It also came with nice deli mustard and thousand island dressing for those who need those.The sandwich itself was very good. It's basically the meat mountain that Arby's offers, but with deli meats.  I think there was flavors being drowned out by the most power meats.  I would go with something simpler next time.  The meat and bread overall was good, but perhaps I agree with the others that it was a lot of money for the amount provided.  I'd still come back to try maybe the #3.

Title: A Bacon Lover's Haven with Quick Service

If you're seeking a bacon-infused dining experience, this restaurant lives up to its name. Visiting on a Sunday noon, the place was surprisingly peaceful—perfect for immediate seating. Initial hiccups with a wobbly table were quickly remedied by a considerate waitress, who offered us a better spot and promptly handed us brunch menus.

Service was notably swift—our chicharron nachos arrived in under 10 minutes, bursting with flavor and generously topped, though the chicharron might not be to everyone's taste. My friend, however, savored this crispy delight.

Our main courses followed suit in speed. The biscuits and gravy were standard fare, complemented by exceptionally smooth eggs. Shani's BLT, while quick to the table, was average, marred slightly by clumsily sliced avocado and a lack of zest.

Despite the culinary ups and downs, the overall ambiance and stellar service left a positive impression. Bacon enthusiasts should certainly give this spot a try.

Title: Satisfying Slice of Tradition at a Kosher Deli

If you're hankering for an authentic kosher deli experience, this traditional spot delivers all the classics you could wish for—even if it's not strictly a glatt kosher establishment (they're open on Saturday). Be prepared to pay a bit more, but rest assured that the comfort, excellent service, and delectable food justify the costs.

I indulged in the twin sandwiches of thin-sliced, lean corned beef and pastrami, accompanied by a side of potato salad. The meats dazzled with their flavor, evidencing skilled preparation. The potato salad came close to my nostalgic ideal, albeit with a tad more mayonnaise than I prefer.

As a delightful bonus before departure, we were treated to a sample of chocolate soda, a pleasant surprise that rounded off the meal nicely.

This deli might not be a daily destination due to its prices, but for anyone in the vicinity with a yen for quality kosher fare, it's a recommendable choice. Just be ready for the expense—it's a treat worth splurging on occasionally.

Returning to a cherished spot after years can be a gamble, but my recent visit to this French bistro was a delightful reaffirmation of its charm. Despite the bustling atmosphere that greeted me, the service remained prompt with immediate seating and a quick offering of tap water, complemented by fresh French bread and butter.

Perusing the extensive wine list, I settled on a classic chicken club sandwich, which proved to be a scrumptious choice. Served on grilled French bread, the layers of chicken, avocado, lettuce, tomato, and bacon melded into a satisfying ensemble, paired excellently with a side of French fries.

The attentive waiter was the cherry on top, ensuring my experience was seamless, from a consistently full water glass to prompt service. This bistro's ambiance effortlessly whisked me away from the city's hustle, providing a culinary escape that left me satiated, skipping the need for dessert or coffee.

Before departing, I found the restroom downstairs to be well-kept, reflecting the overall excellent care in the establishment. This lunch-dinner experience was a complete delight, echoing the bistro's consistent quality and appeal.
So much food reserved for the kamayan the day before we left town, quick and easy. Food, service and music was good. Would come back if in NYC!

The first time I entered the doors, I found the line was forming close to the door. Thinking Hummus would be like Chipotle with the expectation the line would move quickly, I decided to wait. and wait.. and wait... The food was moving quickly, but the line was stagnant. Then I discovered the staff was preparing a catering order. In the middle of lunch hour? Seems like poor planning.Nevertheless, I ordered "The Greek". Ohh my goodness! Definitely worth the wait! This wrap is gigantic and oversized. I unraveled it and ate it like a bowl since it was so huge. I came back a couple days after and ordered the same and yes the same monster sized wrap was served. The Greek does not disappoint! Note, ask for light sauce or sauce on the side or your wrap will be filled with white soup.

I recently visited a delightful restaurant that offers a set menu at a reasonable price, which includes an appetizer, main course, and dessert. While the beet salad I initially chose was satisfactory, I must urge future diners to opt for the escargot – tasting it made me question my decision, as it was superior. The main course, a renowned mushroom burger, did not disappoint. The unique pairing of the burger with a delectable, juicy mushroom soup atop an English muffin was a highlight; the muffin's absorption of the soup's flavors brought the dish to perfection. To end the meal, the chocolate lava cake was a satisfying choice. Overall, this restaurant is a fantastic choice for a family dinner.

Title: Back to Bareburger - A Tasty Return

After a year away from Bareburger, my recent visit was a delightful surprise, despite noticing that some of my old favorites like the Buckaroo were no longer on the menu. The experience started off well with prompt seating on a busy Saturday afternoon, followed by service that was nothing short of phenomenal.

I opted for the Paul Bunyan burger, accompanied by a side of fries. This substantial burger, packed with bison, blue cheese, Black Forest bacon, and caramelized onions, all nestled in a sprout bun, was topped with a unique bourbon pear jam. While I'm someone who rarely finishes a burger, the Paul Bunyan was an exception. It was scrumptious, though I must note the pear jam slightly overshadowed the taste of the bison. Nonetheless, the burger was a hit and one I'd happily recommend.

Overall, it’s a must-try for any burger enthusiast looking for an exceptional dining experience with a twist.

On a bustling Friday afternoon at 1:00 pm, I visited this local gem of a restaurant during peak lunch hours. The place was buzzing with diners, and I was thankful for my foresight to reserve a table, although we still experienced a short wait.

The octopus starter set a high standard, tender and tasty, though a more generous serving would have been appreciated. It was well-paired with radicchio, hearty corona beans, and olives. The meatballs were a comforting follow-up, the beef and pork duo bathed in a robust tomato sauce that beckoned to be mopped up with the accompanying olive oil-drizzled toast – an invitation we happily accepted.

The skirt steak was a standout, expertly grilled to a succulent medium-rare, and the accompanying garlic potatoes, charred onions, and broccolini made for a delectable ensemble. I savored every bite.

However, the truffle tagliatelle experience was a mixed affair due to the absence of burrata and truffle from the supplier. Despite this, the manager's sincere apology and the adjustment in price were commendable, and the dish still impressed with its rich truffle butter flavor.

I'm inclined to revisit, especially to taste their classic tagliatelle with beef and pork bolognese but would aim to avoid the lunchtime rush. A memorable dining experience overall.

Recommended by a friend but didn't wanna go outside on a rainy day. So we ordered delivery at home. The two pizzas we had were both amazing. Especially the RK truffle one. The special scent of truffle make the pizza more flavorful and you cannot resist to have another piece. Unfortunately, the crusts were not as crispy and fresh as the out of oven fresh pizzas since it's delivery. Hope we  will go in person and try the other pizzas in the near future.

As a longtime admirer of instant ramen, I was eager to experience authentic bowls and decided to visit this local spot. My friend and I arrived at 6pm and were quickly ushered to a communal table, where the close quarters were immediately noticeable.

We decided on the Tonkotsu and the New Tokyo chicken ramen. The Tonkotsu's al dente noodles were a highlight, though the pork belly lacked the expected char. On the other hand, my companion found the New Tokyo chicken to be underwhelming, citing a lack of robust flavor.

While the service was amiable, it was overshadowed by the staff's persistent rushing. Being asked thrice if we were done with our meals disrupted the dining experience and left us feeling hurried.

In conclusion, despite the friendly service, the pressure to vacate our table and the mixed reviews on the ramen quality made for a disappointing outing.

Title: A Hidden Gem Serving Delectable Delights

My taste buds are still singing praises for the little-known culinary treasure that a friend introduced me to. This enigmatic spot proved to be a delightful surprise with its array of irresistible dishes. The standout for me was the Kimchi Cream Udon – a dish so authentic and irresistibly tasty that I couldn't help but indulge even after reaching my limit. 

The Uni Beef Nigiri was another show-stealer, disappearing within moments of hitting our table, testament to its exquisite flavor. The Maki Maki Roll, while not groundbreaking, was reliably delicious. The Mixed Sashimi with Ramen, however, fell short of our expectations – the sashimi was satisfactory, but the ramen was sadly left neglected.

Service here was exceptional – the staff was friendly and attentive, ensuring our dining experience was nothing short of perfect. The restaurant offered immediate seating at 6 pm on a Sunday, but quickly filled up, so timing is key.

Despite its cozy size and the boisterous ambiance, this spot has won my patronage. I eagerly anticipate my next visit to explore more of their menu. A definite must-try for anyone looking to discover a new favorite!

Came in and sat at the bar today.  The place was extremely busy.The bartender was extremely friendly and knowledgeable and the best part of the experience. His accent added to the ambience of the place.  However the food was another story. The "Coq au Vin Sandwich" looked neat, but ended up with the Steak Frites.  It came with Arugula salad and shoestring fries.  The steak itself was prepared properly, but didn't have much flavor by itself.  The fries came cold. McDonald's fries are effectively better.They do have an extremely extensive wine list for those who desire it.The bathrooms downstairs are rather nice and shared with Baloud Sud and there is even a private waiting area down there.  Not sure what that's all about.

During my recent visit to this restaurant, the service left much to be desired; the server came across as quite rude and exhibited a lack of attentiveness. Though I'm open to giving it another chance, I'm inclined to explore other eateries first. On a brighter note, the burger I ordered was tasty and generously portioned. My friend was particularly fond of their sweet-tasting Japanese curry. As for the tomato soup, it was unremarkable and not to my taste, though it did have a fresh, natural flavor.

For $10 lunch, it certainly was a bargain.  However my eggplant stuffed with spaghetti  was a bit mushy and lacked the typically notes you find in a great italian tomato sauce.  Maybe because you cant make 4/6 hour grandma's famous pasta sauce for $10!!! It is packed during lunch so definitely make reservations. I really wanted to like this place but it is just mass produced pasta dishes served in pots ...

I went to Aunt Jake's for brunch and ordered the Tagliatelle pasta with roasted garlic sauce (from the create your own pasta menu). Honestly, I was expecting better from this highly rated Italian restaurant. The pasta was pretty ordinary and the sauce was a typical creamy sauce (little to no garlic flavor). It definitely wasn't bad but it wasn't much better than average. The main reason why I wanted to come to Aunt Jake's in the first place was for the squid ink pasta, but it turned out that they were out of it when I was there! That was a big disappointment.The exterior of the restaurant is easy to miss as it is small and you have to take some stairs down from the street level. The inside is decorated nicely though. The service speed was good and our waiter was helpful and attentive.Overall, Aunt Jake's has slightly above average pasta. My review might've been better if they had the squid ink pasta, but for now, I have to give it 3 stars.

During a recent trip to NYC, my friend's recommendation led us to try Burger & Lobster Restaurant, which we easily booked via the YELP app. The restaurant welcomes diners with an enchanting tunnel of lobster traps, setting the stage for a unique experience. Arriving ahead of schedule, my husband and I savored their Bryant Park Punch, a delightful specialty drink with a refreshing fruity kick. For dinner, I indulged in the creamy lobster Mac n Cheese paired with a crisp side salad, while my husband opted for the succulent lobster dinner. Both dishes impressed us with their flavor and reaffirmed the establishment's reputation for serving delicious food at an attractive price point.

I recently dined at a local eatery that left a lasting impression with its exceptional food and service. The tacos, a standout item on the menu, are a must-try alongside the delectable queso appetizer that comes with a generous serving of chips. Despite the portions appearing modest, they pack a satisfying punch that fills you up with delicious flavors. The quality of the food is unwaveringly high, ensuring that every visit is as enjoyable as the last. However, be mindful that seating is somewhat limited; if you're planning on bringing a larger party, securing a reservation ahead of time is advisable. I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant for anyone in search of a gratifying meal.

We stumbled upon Bazar Tapas Bar and Restaurant in the Fall of 2017 for after dinner drinks.  Our mediocre meal at nearby Korean restaurant, Hanjan, left us more or less unsatisfied.  So we pulled up a chair (or two) at the bar and let our friendly bartender get to work.  We left impressed by both the cocktails and service!  We finally got around to dining in this past weekend for brunch.Admittedly, the service fell short of our initial visit.  The hostess was unfriendly and indifferent and our table service was pretty standard.  The drinks were solid, although arguably their Bloody Mary could use a bit more kick!  The food was tasty and well prepared with exception of the brussels sprouts (over-spiced and over-salted).Their Salmon Eggs Benedict was exceptional and reasonably priced (only $1 more than the traditional eggs Benedict, score!).  The Char Grilled Octopus was also a hit - perfectly cooked and well seasoned, served with tomatoes, olives, capers, and celery.  That flavor combination really worked well!I'd definitely return and can see this place doing great happy hour business.  The space is beautiful!

Title: Sublime Culinary Experience Ups the Ante to Five Stars

My recent lunch at Bouley was nothing short of spectacular, convincingly meriting an upgrade to five stars. The $75 tasting menu proved its value with each sumptuous course.

The sea urchin appetizer set a high bar, its flavor and freshness leaving an indelible impression. A porcini flan, rich and earthy, firmly anchored the middle of the meal, and an unexpected bonus dish of white asparagus draped in cheese sauce was a delightful interlude.

Choosing the lobster as my main was a wise decision; it was impeccably prepared. Dessert unfolded in two acts: a creamy amaretto ice cream followed by the ultimate decision between meringue and chocolate cake. I can assure you that both options conclude your meal with a standing ovation.

The chef's generous gesture of a complimentary walnut cake in recognition of our wedding anniversary added a personal touch that went above and beyond.

Although Bouley does not offer the cheapest lunch, you're paying for an unparalleled gastronomic experience backed by flawless cooking and service. A visit here is a must for anyone who appreciates the art of fine dining.

I recently visited a new spot at 9:45 PM on a Tuesday and had a delightful experience indulging in what might be the best pho in town. While my initial request for mushroom pho with the "crazy rich broth" couldn't be accommodated, the regular mushroom pho I settled for did not disappoint. Laden with an assortment of vegetables – including a variety of mushrooms, bok choy, and onions – the dish was elevated by the option to add bean sprouts from the table. The broth itself was a flavorful journey, complex and rich, which I enhanced with a moderately spicy hot oil from their selection of condiments.

My companion's choice of the house pho with the "crazy rich broth" was enviable, tantalizing in both appearance and aroma, undoubtedly a must-try for next time. The interior ambiance added to the experience, boasting a super fun, modern aesthetic with an open kitchen that invited curiosity and engagement. Additionally, the owner's personal touch in checking on our table was a nice gesture that spoke volumes about their dedication; learning that the restaurant was a mere three months old was quite impressive.

This place has easily secured a return visit from me. Whether you're a pho aficionado or a first-timer, it's a spot that promises not just a meal, but a memorable dining experience.

During the bustling San Gennaro festival, I had the opportunity to savor a Regina pizza at Song E Napule, and to say it impressed would be an understatement. This oven-baked masterpiece was the epitome of pizza perfection – crispy with just the right amount of char to accentuate the flavors. The fusion of the creamy mozzarella, robust Parmesan reggiano, fresh olive oil, and the rich tomatoes created an experience of divine indulgence at every bite. So captivated by the first, I found myself ordering a second to enjoy at home. For any true pizza aficionado, a visit to Song E Napule in Little Italy is a must – it's an experience that will surely not disappoint.

Despite the buzz surrounding Hanoi House, my experience was underwhelming. The food, while reasonably flavorful, didn't live up to expectations as the pho fell short of being the best I've tasted and the portions were disappointingly meager, particularly the crispy spring rolls that disappeared too quickly. I found the bone marrow add-on disappointing due to the scant amount served. However, it was the noisy atmosphere during Saturday dinner that truly detracted from the dining experience — conversation was challenging at best. Weighing the average food against the din, I'd rate it between 3.5 and 4 out of 5, and I'm inclined not to revisit or recommend Hanoi House.

Title: A Delectable Evening of Dim Sum in Times Square

On a bustling Friday evening at 6:30 pm, I found myself wandering through Times Square with an appetite for adventure. Fate led me to a dim sum eatery that, to my astonishment, seated me immediately - a rarity in such a lively locale, but perhaps less surprising given that dim sum traditionally caters to early risers.

The culinary highlight was undoubtedly the chicken juicy bun, a unique take on the classic soup dumpling. While other hotspots like Joe's Shanghai corner the market on pork varieties, this chicken version stood out for its rarity and flavor. Although it housed less soup than some might expect, a dab of chili oil amplified its excellence.

Another star of the show was the egg yolk creamy bun. Its exterior was pillow-soft, breaking away to reveal a luscious cream center that stole the show. This decadent treat easily topped my list of favorites for the night.

Venturing further into uncharted territory, I sampled chicken feet for the first time, encountering the anticipated unusual taste and texture. It's a dish that veers from traditional chicken fare, requiring a certain palate adaptation.

The chicken dumplings, while tasty, couldn't eclipse the splendor of their juicy counterparts. Yet, they were a solid addition to the meal.

Value-wise, the prices were quite reasonable, especially for an establishment in the heart of Times Square. This dim sum dinner was a delightful surprise, offering an array of flavors for both the uninitiated and the seasoned food explorer.

I recently visited a local ramen spot and decided to give their spicy ramen a try. Priced at $16, my expectations were high. The dish included two thin slices of pork, half an egg, bamboo shoots, scallions, and a spicy pork sauce. On a positive note, the tonkotsu broth was impressively creamy, possibly one of the richest I've had to date. However, the bowl felt lacking in the topping department. I found myself yearning for a greater variety and quantity of toppings to enhance the texture and overall experience. While the ramen was undoubtedly tasty, I'm not convinced it reached the value of its price tag. A bit more crunch or additional toppings might have justified the cost.

Title: A Bittersweet Farewell to Ceased Dumpling

In the heart of East Chinatown, nestled amongst the bustling streets, once stood a hidden gem renowned for its culinary marvels - Ceased Dumpling. This quaint little spot could easily have been the go-to place for anyone in search of the perfect dumpling in New York City.

The dumplings served at Ceased Dumpling were not just food; they were a nostalgic journey back to the old days of Toronto's Dumpling House, where love at first bite was an understatement. Each piece was crafted with perfection, echoing the authenticity and charm that is so often sought but rarely found.

But what truly set Ceased Dumpling apart was not just the exquisite food, but the hearts behind it - an adorable couple who poured their love into every dumpling. They ran the place with an expertise that was as warm as it was professional. Their generosity knew no bounds, often gifting free dumplings to those who made the innocent mistake of ordering the wrong item.

The real magic, however, lay in the fried dumplings. Those golden, crispy morsels were a testament to the simple truth that sometimes the best things in life are the simplest, especially when fried to perfection.

Sure, Manhattan and its numerous eateries will always have something to offer, but for those who have had the pleasure of savoring Ceased Dumpling's offerings, the closure of this establishment is a loss that's deeply felt. It seems unfair that what could easily be dubbed the best dumplings in the city, if not the whole city, are no longer within reach.

Ceased Dumpling may have become 'ceased', but it will forever be known as the 'Beast Dumpling' in the hearts of its patrons. So here's to the little dumpling shop that could, and did, but sadly is no more.

After much anticipation, my visit to Madame Vo was a delightful fulfillment of high expectations. The Lychee Refresher initiated the meal with a sweet and invigorating kick. For starters, the Cha Gio Chay, fried spring rolls with a uniquely web-like crust, were a marvel in both texture and taste. We then indulged in the Madame Pho, rich in beefy essence, and the Suon Kho, pork ribs caramelized to perfection, which were a personal highlight. My experience at Madame Vo left me eager to return and sample more of their exquisite Vietnamese fare.

Located in the bustling heart of Midtown, this gem of a café stands out among the many I've visited across New York City for its cleanliness and ample space. Opting for a simple delight, I chose a croissant paired with a small hot chocolate, and both exceeded my expectations in freshness and flavor. Service was swift, with staff demonstrating exceptional friendliness, helpfulness, and courtesy that made the experience all the more pleasant. Highly recommend for a delightful snack in a welcoming atmosphere.

There are two cuisines that make it so damn easy to be vegan: Ethiopian and Indian. I'm constantly amazed too hear people bemoan the lack of vegan options. Do you even injera, bro? Ethiopian food is an utter delight and no matter how much of it I eat, it is never boring or repetitive. This Awash location seems small from the outside and also since it's down a short staircase. But it is popping and around dinner time, gets positively packed (which is when you realize it isn't so small). The staff is attentive and alert and the kitchen cranks food out quickly.We loved the "salad" (timatim fitfit), which was actually chopped up injera mixed with diced tomatoes, onions, jalapeños, oil, and spices. Pro tip: get the salata to go and let it marinate overnight. It's even more delicious. We also recommend the gursha, gomen, missir, and shiro. They are all served on top of injera, which sucks up the sauces like a delicious sponge.

Printers Alley was a quick turn off of from Times Square for a drink and place to hang out. They had specials available every day including weekends. My friend grabbed a frosè and I went with a well drink with their liquor special Honey Jack.  The drink was OK and the frosè, light and fruity.  One issue, several of the menu items were available including ones containing coffee. It seemed some of the staff was unaware of the various drinks on a special menu distributed by the server. They were genuinely confused and so nice so we shrugged it off.  Not a bad place to go, so I'm in the neighborhood in a need to night stop by again.

So good!!! I love a Good omakase and this place did not disappoint. They offer 3 different sets depending on how hungry you are. 8 pieces for $4812 pieces for $6016 pieces for $85Also their cocktails are delicious.

Title: A Culinary Gem for Authentic Eats and People-Watching

If you're on the hunt for authentic flavors and zippy service, look no further – this restaurant is a true find. The spacious interior welcomes you in, while the glass storefront invites you to indulge in a bit of people-watching as you dine.

From the get-go, the employees make you feel at home with their warmth and efficiency. Service here is quick without compromising on attention to detail – a balance that is hard to come by.

Now, let's talk food. The chicken soup is a must-try; it's an explosion of flavor that sets the bar high. It's hard to find chicken soup that matches the richness and depth of what's served here. Likewise, their guacamole and chips are a testament to freshness, offering a perfect starter to whet your appetite.

I'm getting hungry just reminiscing about my experiences here. In a nutshell, it's a spot that's hard to beat for those who crave authentic food served up with genuine hospitality.

Best hand pulled noodles i have ever had in my life!! No seriously. Noodles, especially Lo MEIN/chow MEIN is my favorite Chinese dish ever. They just crazy blew it . I can't explain it much by saying how great this place is. It's in the heart of China town coming from a true Chinese family ready to serve and feed you a true FEAST. If I ever come back in NY, it's a must try ! For anyone who wants to get the best noodles ever, COME HERE ! Highly recommend:Special House pulled noodles Fried pork dumplings Tip: cash only!! & one meal is PERFECT TO SHARE! Don't think it's enough for one person trust us!

Tucked away in the bustling Union Square, I discovered a charming little cafe that immediately drew me in. The ground level where orders are placed exudes a cozy ambiance, and although I didn't venture upstairs, it's easy to imagine it would share the same delightful decor.

My choice for lunch was the "Oh Henry" sandwich, paired with a side of potato salad. The sandwich was nothing short of delicious, managing to make up for the slight disappointment of a stale chocolate donut. The potato salad, on the other hand, was a hit – fresh, flavorful, and generously portioned.

Service at the register was provided by a soft-spoken yet amiable woman, rounding out the overall pleasant experience. I also tried an iced nonfat chai tea latte, which was quite satisfying on a warm day. 

When it comes to value, this cafe hits the sweet spot with its reasonable pricing. Despite the minor misstep with the donut, I'm already looking forward to my next visit to try another of their tempting sandwich options.

Really good new york pizza. There was a long line at this little hole in the wall. They were working so fast back there. We had ordered 4 pizzas for 10 prople. Turned out to be way too much pizza but it was so good. They sell by the slice as well. If you're in the area you've got to pick up a slice.

Title: A Perfect NY Pizza Pit Stop Before Flying

During a brief layover in NYC, my quest for an authentic pizza experience led me to a local gem just in time before our flight from LaGuardia. Trusting the wisdom of Yelp, we arrived right at opening and were immediately immersed in the lunchtime pizza-only policy, which was exactly what our appetites demanded.

Indecision struck us when faced with the choice between a savory Napolitano topped with anchovies and a hearty sausage and pepper pie. Our server, a beacon of genius, suggested a half-and-half pizza, satisfying both cravings in one go. The pizza itself? Utterly delicious, with each slice boasting the perfect balance of flavors and crust that could only be described as a New York masterpiece.

As we wrapped up our meal, the restaurant began to buzz with the lunch crowd—a testament to its popularity and a sign that we had made the right choice. This place captured the essence of NY pizza with both flair and efficiency. Should our travels have us jetting out of LaGuardia in the future, a return visit will undoubtedly be on our itinerary.

Came by just before lunch closing on a Friday afternoon and had the place to ourselves with Jake, the bartender, and longtime employee who used to be at Ma Peche, one of David Chang's other restaurants.We had already had a huge breakfast and had plans for a huge dinner so we sat at the bar, had a few drinks and picked a few dishes.  We shared the pork belly buns of course, the summer corn, and the duck.That was enough.  The pork belly was amazing, but the corn took it to another level with the sauce.  Oh man were our mouths tingling!!  Then came the duck! Oh man!  I love duck but have to say it was not just the duck!  It was the white rice.......the duck fat soaked rice!  I'm telling you it was like crack! (Mind you I've never done drugs in my life).  There is no way I will pass on this dish when I return.

3.5/5Beef Koobideh Kabob: ground beef, tender and soft, less moist than I thought it would be, and also needs a lot more seasoning. But you know what, despite it, this was super delicious. Definitely get the beef as your protein! Chicken Koobideh: not as good as the beef, but still quite juicy. Bland as well but the blandness doesn't work for the chickenBase: yellow rice is fluffy and good, but not seasoned. Seasonal rice is sweet and mixed with carrots (?) and raisins. WeirdVegetables: brussel fries. Ok these brussel sprouts were reallllly salty and ridiculously charred. Like blackened beyond recognition. Yikes. Kale salad: this was strangely sweet? Not a fanSauce: spicy hummus is the only thing you need! I mixed the rice with it and it was awesome

Title: A Feast to Remember at La Mela

My visit to La Mela during the San Gennaro Feast was a delightful culinary adventure. Our party of five indulged in the four-course meal, and it was a feast that left us more than satisfied. The courses, including caprese salad, hot antipasti, an array of pasta in the famiglia style, and a final dish of veal, chicken, and shrimp, offered a variety that catered to different dietary preferences, all for a reasonable $38 per person. 

The quantity of food was generous, ensuring everyone at the table was well fed. To complement our meal, we chose a bottle of Malbec, which was a pleasant surprise in both quality and flavor. Despite the hectic atmosphere of the festival which understandably slowed down the service, the experience was exceptional. It's a venue I'd highly recommend, especially for groups looking to share a diverse and ample meal.

Title: A Breakfast Gem in the Financial District

I recently stumbled upon this delightful New York City diner while seeking out a hearty breakfast to cap off my night out. A quick Yelp search turned up this spot, complete with promising pictures and an ideal location within walking distance of my hotel.

Admittedly, the diner's popularity was evident by the queue outside, but as a solo diner, my wait time was brief. The service mirrored the efficiency of the city itself; my order was simple yet attended to swiftly, and my meal arrived in record time. The classic breakfast--crispy bacon, perfectly cooked eggs, golden toast, and savory home fries--did not disappoint. Each bite was a testament to the diner's commitment to quality without the hefty price tag often associated with downtown dining.

Be warned, space is at a premium here; the cozy confines are a clear trade-off for the bustling atmosphere and great food. But if you're looking to satisfy your breakfast cravings with speed and deliciousness, this is the place to be. Highly recommended for a no-fuss, satisfying start to your day.

From the moment my party and I entered the restaurant, we were met with welcoming smiles and promptly seated, a positive start to our dining experience. The ongoing happy hour offered delightful beverage choices; the strawberry margarita and passion fruit mojito were particularly impressive.

Our appetizer, a portion of wings, arrived crisp and packed with flavor. The main courses followed suit in quality: the salmon was cooked to tender perfection, and the shrimp mofongo was a mouthwatering standout — kudos to the chef's expertise.

Added to the culinary delights was a lively atmosphere, courtesy of the in-house DJ. The staff's attentiveness and friendliness didn't go unnoticed, contributing to the overall excellent ambiance. The option for hookah, wisely limited to when children aren't present, is another thoughtful touch.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit to this establishment that skillfully balances great food, ambiance, and service.

Title: A Gem Worth the Buzz

After hearing so much about this place, I finally had the chance to dine here and it didn't disappoint. The lunchtime crowd was testament to its popularity, but the service remained swift. What delighted me was their inclusive menu, which featured vegan options readily available without needing to rely on additional apps— a convenience that stood out.

The edamame was my first pleasant surprise; they were steamed to perfection, maintaining a firm texture without any hint of sogginess. As for the main dish, the shrimp eggplant paired with brown rice was a revelation. Unlike the all-too-common, overly-thick Thai sauces, this dish was refreshingly light and tasted clean, allowing the quality of the ingredients to shine through.

This restaurant has made an impression on me, and I'm already planning to return during less hectic hours to explore more of their offerings. Highly recommended for anyone seeking a special culinary experience!

Title: Authentic Pho Experience with Generous Portions

I recently enjoyed the mushroom pho at this hidden gem of a restaurant, and it instantly took me back to the streets of Vietnam. The authenticity of the flavors is unmatched, and the generous portions make it an excellent spot for a satisfying lunch. This place is perfect for a quick meet-up with friends, offering both a great atmosphere and the option of a solid meal in under an hour. Do remember it's cash only, but there's no need to worry as there are plenty of ATMs nearby, with one conveniently located on-site. A must-try for any pho enthusiast!

5 stars for the service and the food.Came here for a dinner meeting. I wanted to reserve but they don't take reservations. Was a bit concern that it might get too packed but on a Tuesday evening, it worked out. I started out with a chamomile tea and some apps. We had the dumplings and sweet potato puffs which were delicious. We ordered the chicken kaffir, Thai omelet, pork belly, butterfish, and a plate of snowpeas. Everything came out well cooked and super tasty. We ended our night with a sesame sticky rice. It's made with real coconut shavings! Also never had it with sesame before so that was unique to me.  Water was refilled often, which is a plus! The prices are equal to the neighborhood prices but if you want some authentic thai, this is it.

I recently revisited SenYa during Restaurant Week and was pleasantly surprised by how much it exceeded my previous experience. The grilled octopus appetizer was a delight with its crispy texture, while the beef tartare paired with bone marrow was simply melt-in-your-mouth fantastic. While the chirashi didn't quite hit the high mark set by Hatsuhana's Box of Dreams on fish freshness, it still offered good value. Ending the meal with the matcha cheesecake was a delicious decision, rounding out a satisfying dining experience. What's more, the service was notably impressive this time around. If you're a sushi enthusiast looking for a worthwhile spot during Restaurant Week, SenYa is a strong contender.

My experience at Kusharista was both tantalizing and all too brief. This gem, offering Egyptian street food that captured my heart, has sadly shuttered its doors after just one visit. My encounter with their cuisine was cut short when I dozed off amidst a lazy summer warmth, only to find the leftovers lacking the next day – a testament to their dishes' meant-to-be-enjoyed-fresh quality.

The flavors were exceptional, and as an enthusiast of Egyptian fare, I can confidently say Kusharista served up some of the most delectable eats I've had since my time at Cairo Cafe in Chicago. The loss of Kusharista has left a void in my culinary adventures, and I find myself yearning for their return or the rise of a worthy successor in New York.

For those who missed the opportunity to dine at Kusharista, let's hold onto hope that they, or a rival of equal calibre, will grace our palates once again.

Title: A Szechuan Delight with a Spicy Kick

If you're in the mood for some authentic, fiery Szechuan cuisine, this bustling spot is a must-visit, especially on weekend nights. Here's a pro tip: sidestep the long lines by joining their online waitlist beforehand.

Diving into the menu, the dan dan noodles are a star dish, deserving a perfect score (5/5). Expect a spicy and savory treat with a pleasant hint of sesame. Be prepared for some heat, though, as these noodles pack a punch.

Equally impressive is the pickled chili style fish, which scores a solid 4/5. The fish fillet is succulent and perfectly complemented by an array of pickled veggies, beans, and bamboo shoots, all swimming in a deliciously spicy sauce. While flavorsome, it does tend to be on the oily side.

In summary, this is a spot that does Szechuan classics justice. Just brace yourself for some serious spice and possibly a bit of greasiness, but otherwise, enjoy the culinary ride!

Title: A Memorable Experience Worth Sharing

I visited this gem last July and can't help but sing its praises ever since. The lively ambiance makes it a perfect spot for a romantic date or a casual evening with friends. The highlight was the generous platter that comfortably served two - its flavors still dance in my memory, easily earning a 10/10. Coupled with the stellar service from our knowledgeable server, the experience was nothing short of delightful. The only slight inconvenience was the restroom location, requiring a brief trip to the adjacent hotel. Nonetheless, this place is on my must-visit list, and I eagerly look forward to my next visit. Highly recommended!

Title: High Hopes Dashed by Gimmick Over Gusto

Despite the buzz I'd heard while in California, my anticipated visit to this restaurant fell flat. Anticipating a rich selection, it was disheartening to find the menu picked over by 2 PM, with only ravioli available. My partner and I had no choice but to try an assortment of their ravioli offerings.

In a further bit of misfortune, my order was short a piece, which I tried to overlook, hoping the flavors would compensate. They didn't. The ravioli fillings were poorly contained, escaping with each attempt to savor them, and the pasta seemed far from fresh, hinting at staleness with a disappointing texture.

The service lagged as well, with a longer-than-anticipated wait for our meal. While the experience left much to be desired, I might give it another chance to try their full range—but only to validate if my first impression was just an off day. As of now, my expectations remain unmet.

Spice Symphony delivers on its reputation as a go-to spot for Indo-Chinese cuisine in NYC. Dining here, the spinach chaat appetizer offered a decent start, though it wasn’t particularly mind-blowing in terms of flavor. The real standout was the veg manchurian; its texture and savory gravy harmonized beautifully with garlic naan. Beware the paneer szechuan’s fiery kick - it's not for the faint-hearted. We had to set it aside for a gobhi manchurian, which was tasty but could benefit from crispier cauliflower. Overall, a robust dining experience with a few dishes I would pass on next visit.

This is a bar and you know that by the smell you get right when you walk in. Its that soapy detergent smell that is engrained in my head from working in a bar for a long time. With that being said it is not a dive.  It has a bunch of tables in there and doesn't feel like your typical bar. The menu has a lot of the bar classics but the one that popped out at us was the cauliflower bites. It said it came with aoili but they forgot it.  My glass for water had lipstick on it which is not a huge deal but they just need to tighten up that stuff. For lunch I had the fried goat cheese salad that was pretty good. The goat cheese was pretty good and gave a tangy-ness that worked well with the greens and walnuts. The food was decent enough here. Didn't blow us away but didn't hate it. Did the job and left full and satisfied. Solid 3 star place.

In the passage of my travels summons a British pub for lunch in Midtown West, Manhattan.  Since I am unable to travel to the UK, the UK comes to NYC.  Yelp mobile has the ability to make reservations even within then next twelve minutes.  I am lured by previous reviews of Cock & Bull's renowned Cod and Chips.  Four stars due to the very minimal customer service experienced as it was not very busy nor crowded on a Monday afternoon of 1 pm.  Cock & Bull is the standard sports bar of a British flair of Victorian decorum and British cuisine.  Where are the British pomp and pageantry? TV's are available affixed to the walls by the bar for eyes to be engrossed.  They do carry an extensive craft beer selection - ergo, mate do not request for Coors Light or Heineken.  Upon being promptly seated I immediately placed my food order, but took my time to decide on a drink and the waiter would return to take my drink order.  Forward.  I waited for the waiter to return to take my drink order.  I waited, I waited, I waited and I waited for any waiter or wait staff available for customer service.  Waiting for resolution.  Waiting for absolution. Waiting for salvation.  I scanned the entire business for a staff to seek assistance and finally flagged from a distanced my designated waiter.  In visible antagonistic acquiescence he obliged to heed my drink order of one glass of white wine.  One measly glass of wine does not require concoction of mixing ingredients nor the time required, but only obtaining the wine bottle and pouring.  During my meal I saw a party of three walked in without a reservation for lunch as they were dressed in business casual attire and the wait staff immediately serve them without hesitating or waiting.  I believe it is discrimination for social injustice and deliberate maleficence for a party of one inattentively serviced vs. a large party of three and larger to be immediately served.  Full of malarkey.  An atmosphere of malaise.  Bad customer service is my cock and bull story mate.  No mindful consideration for a party of one.  This business is conveniently located within the vicinity of Grand Central Terminal.  Business cards are available for grabs.  The computerized bill is served affixed to their postcard.  I do not see cheese seftons, custard pudding, Bakewell tart, or trifle on the dessert menu as these are all traditional British Victorian desserts or sweets.Cod & Chips $23.95Fresh Ale battered cod fish & minted mushy peas with bacon served with tartar sauce, lemon and hand cut thick chips.  This entree is a huge meal extensive for lunch.  Fresh Ale battered is not usually my cup of tea as I prefer breaded or fish fry.  The mushy peas is my first exposure to authentic traditional British cuisine as a traditional accompaniment to fish and chips.  I like peas alone and find this format was okay.  It was too green for me like Elphaba Thropp, a fictional character in "Wicked: The Life and Times of the Wicked Witch of the West" by Gregory Maguire. Nevertheless, the actual fish and French Fries were solid upholding substance and enable me to eat my fill.Pinot Grigio, Barone Fini (Trentino, Italy) $11.50Good nose, fruity and nicely chilled white wine.  What year is this wine?  Not specified on the menu.

I love pizza and was open to trying a cauliflower-based pizza and a pasta dish using zucchini noodles. After looking at the menu, also decided to try chicken wings , mozzarella sticks, penne a la vodka, and chicken francese and a few other types of pizza and Sicilian slices. I didn't care too much for the pasta and chicken dishes. My favorite eats here are the pizzas - doesn't matter if dough is regular or cauliflower.. my heart goes to any slice that has meat.. although here I was happy with both meat and non-meat versions. I wish they had dessert!Seating is limited and it's super casual.. not really good for groups like mine unless you luck out which we did

Title: Stellar Service and Delightful Dining at [Restaurant Name]

I recently had the pleasure of dining for the first time at [Restaurant Name], and it was an experience that exceeded all expectations! The star of the show was Mireille, whose ability to multi-task was nothing short of miraculous. Despite the bustling crowd, she managed to take, prepare, and serve orders with an ever-present smile.

As a fellow customer service professional, I was incredibly impressed by Mireille's dedication and efficiency. Her service was the epitome of stellar, making a lasting impression that will surely bring me back. While the food was delicious in its own right, it was Mireille's exceptional service that truly made the meal unforgettable.

Thank you, Mireille, for elevating our dining experience to extraordinary heights!
Upping my rating to 4 stars because on my most recent visit, the beef noodles with bok choy were amazing. Steamed and fried dumplings were also great. Cash only.

I CAN'T BELIEVE IT WAS VEGAN!Yes, y'all! I tried my first ever vegan restaurant in New York, and I must admit, it was "HELLA" good! One of the BEST vegan restaurants in the city, baybee! Blossom is one of those date night restaurants that you take a lovely lover! The food here is delicious. My friend and I took a recent trip to NY and she recommended this place as she is vegan and it was rated very high on Yelp. I didn't mind trying out a Vegan restaurant as long as it had either wine or alcohol, and Blossom answered my prayers! Now,--they didn't offer any alcohol, but they did offer some vegan wine, which I didn't know anything about until I came here! Blossom did EVERYTHING right and DID NOT disappoint me!After walking in an hour before they closed, Blossom didn't have many customers as it was getting late. Inside is nice, cozy, and very inviting. We were able to snuggle in the back near the window as we sipped our wine and clicked glasses to our restful weekend in NY and people watched.The menu offers creative and tasty food choices that will have your mouth watering! I was blown away with how delicious the food was! We started with the Scallops appetizer. For my main meal, I ordered the truffle cashew cream ravioli, which was incredible and flavorful that will fool any vegan thinking it couldn't be vegan, but it is, baybee! My friend ordered the lasagna and enjoyed it!We opted for dessert, and don't ask me how they make a yummy ol' vegan tiramisu but that thang was DELICIOUS! O0H BABY! But WAIT, what about that scrumptious Chocolate Ganache? OH, MA GOSH! Life is GUD'!Blossom is a great place to come for a date night or to celebrate a special event. They also have a large upstairs that holds larger seating groups. Upstairs is also where the bathrooms are! We honestly went to several different restaurants in NY during our quick weekend trip, and must give credit to Blossom as they did a wonderful job in making us feel so welcomed and left happy! This is a costly restaurant and not one to eat out every day, but it's a special little treat in my book!

**Title: Cozy Corner Gem with Delightful Drinks and Comforting Cuisine**

**Rating: 4/5**

I recently dined at this charming eatery, conveniently situated on a bustling corner. The adorable drink menu, encased in a little leather book with a neat button, was an instant highlight. The restaurant's spacious design includes a downstairs area perfect for large groups and a comfortably accessible bathroom.

As for the ambiance, the open kitchen adds a touch of culinary theatre, while the front bar is ideal for casual drinks. My dining experience, shared with two former colleagues on a quiet weekday, was quite delightful. The bucatini stood out for me, overshadowing the much-hyped pistachio pesto, which, despite its reputation, failed to leave a lasting impression.
