An undeniable hit were the truffle mashed potatoes, which struck a delicate balance between aromatic allure and subtle flavor - a true sensory delight. Portion-wise, the generous pastas proved to be hearty and just the right amount for three.

Compliments to our attentive waiter, who ensured our glasses were perpetually filled. A pleasant surprise came with a check-in on Yelp, rewarding us with a 10% discount. A visit to this spot is sure to be a treat for both drink connoisseurs and food lovers alike.

It's like waiting in line for a really good piece of Ellio's pizza, you know the kind that come in the frozen section of the supermarket? Yeah. Don't get me wrong the pizza is tasty lol but the wait isn't necessary. I love coming here to grab a slice of the pepperoni and every time I come I love looking at the walls at how many celebs have been.

Very friendly and helpful staff! Casual burger spot hidden in Chinatown. Breakroom Burger - very good, lots of layers and tasty sauce. It's way too big that I ate it the deconstructed way... Tomato - pork belly - patty - lettuce - onion ring - egg - bun..... Not sure how people can the whole thing together... Pork Belly Taco - very tasty and enjoyed the pork belly a lot as it's not your typical taco option. Fish Tempura Taco - pretty good too but same to me in all other good taco place. Thai Chili - not sure why it's called Thai, just like regular Chili for me, my least favorite among what we ordered. Defiantly a great burger and taco joint!

My recent visit to this Michelin-starred gem left me thoroughly impressed. The excitement was palpable as our party of three opted for the Prix fixe option at lunch, a choice that allowed us to savor nearly the entire menu. Standout dishes included the richly flavored toro ssam bap, the perfectly prepared got stone rice, succulent Jeju chicken wings, and the comforting Miyuk ramyun. Portions were generous; we left feeling wholly satisfied without being overwhelmed.

The service was exceptional – attentive and timely, with our dishes arriving promptly. Considering the quality and the prestigious accolade of the restaurant, the prices were quite reasonable, especially by New York City standards. I wholeheartedly recommend a visit for an unforgettable culinary experience.

**Title: A Charming Encounter at "The Maze"**

Venturing into "The Maze" with friends, one cannot help but be enchanted by its intricate layout as suggested by the intriguing exhibit photos A and B. This place is a delightful hideaway, ideal for a romantic date or a laid-back gathering.

Perched at the bar, we were greeted by an exceptionally courteous bartender whose name escapes me post-second Old Fashioned. His bow-tie and the smooth delivery of our drinks only added to his polished demeanor.

The calamari appetizer was the highlight of our shared plates — it's my absolute favorite. Coupled with prime people-watching opportunities, "The Maze" ensured a lovely, albeit brief, evening.

Given its convenient location just a stone's throw from my workplace, a swift 15-minute stroll, I'm eagerly anticipating my return to this cozy retreat.

Title: A Weekend Brunch Haven for Vegans and More

I recently visited this restaurant for a weekend brunch and was thoroughly pleased with the array of vegan options available. The menu is thoughtfully labeled, clearly indicating vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free choices—ideal for dining with friends who have specific dietary preferences.

I opted for the Arugula Veggie Bowl, a vibrant and satisfying salad that didn't disappoint in flavor or portion size. However, a word to the wise regarding reservations made through Yelp: there seems to be a disconnect with the restaurant's timing. Despite booking for 10:45 AM, upon arrival, we were informed the kitchen would open at 11:30 AM. While we could whet our appetite with drinks, our stomachs had to hold out for food a bit longer.

In summary, despite a minor hiccup with the reservation timing, the restaurant shines for its variety and quality of food tailored to diverse dietary needs.

I had a delightful dining experience at this restaurant, especially impressed by the extremely friendly service upon arrival at 4pm with no wait time. The daily happy hour from 11:30am-6pm is a fantastic deal, offering some great options for cheaper drinks.

The culinary aspect didn't disappoint either. Despite a "B" health rating, the food was both delicious and aesthetically pleasing. The pad Thai packed a punch in terms of flavor, although I found the noodles a tad too chewy for my liking. On the other hand, the beef parang curry struck a perfect balance with its coconut richness.

Overall, I left the restaurant very satisfied with my meal and would recommend it to anyone looking for tasty food paired with excellent service.

Nestled in the heart of Soho, this plant-based eatery is a true hidden gem. The freshness and flavor of the food are remarkable, truly challenging the preconceptions of what plant-based cuisine can be. The menu boasts a variety of delectable bowls, with the Spicy Chili Sin Carne Bowl being a particular highlight, especially when paired with a glass of exquisite La Luna wine. The staff’s friendly and welcoming demeanor only enhances the dining experience. It's amazing to find such organic and delicious options, all crafted without a single animal product. For both the health-conscious and the flavor-seekers, this restaurant is a must-visit.
Korean Bar with American Dessert ‍ Nice mix of Asian American bar food under one roof. Dessert is totally instagram worthy. Just make sure you have someone to share it with cause it's pretty big!

What hasn't been already said about this place...thanks to food network and travel channel. Xian is famous for its foods. Once a hole in the wall establishment that delivered solid and fiery plates is now a household name for good reason. The family owned chain is thriving in the nyc area. Their dishes have Chinese roots but changed for the American market. You know a place is good and noteworthy when craving a certain flavor. This is how I feel about Xian's. The cumin lamb and spinach dumplings keeps calling me back.

I recently dined at Ichiran in New York, renowned for its authentic ramen. The flavors were as delightful as the ones I experienced in Okinawa and Tokyo – consistently delicious. Though the soft-boiled egg was slightly overcooked, it was a minor hiccup in an otherwise enjoyable meal. The pleasant surprise of complimentary extra noodles was a warm gesture, albeit the steep price of $24 for a set meal with modest additions of pork, nori, and green onions came as a shock, especially when compared to the more reasonable $12-13 for a basic order back in Okinawa. Despite the quality, the price makes it an exclusive treat rather than a regular indulgence for me while visiting New York.

Title: Convenient KFC Spot with a Friendly Touch

I've visited this KFC on multiple occasions, drawn by convenience rather than culinary wow-factor. A casual eatery, it now boasts an added treat: beer on the menu. During a recent lunch with a friend and his baby, I discovered they have a single high chair, which the staff thoughtfully reserved for us after a quick phone call – a testament to their attentive nature.

While the food sticks to the classic KFC formula, I found the Theo okkk chicken a touch too sweet and lacking the spicy kick I prefer. It's not a destination I'd seek out specifically, but if you're already in the area with a hankering for a crispy drumstick, this spot will serve you well, complete with a side of warm hospitality.

I recently visited a delightful French bistro that's perfect for a late lunch, as it remains open throughout the day. Opting for the "menu du jour" at a reasonable price of $29, I was treated to generous portions of succulent salmon tartare followed by flavorsome fish balls accompanied by perfectly steamed zucchinis. The meal concluded with a lovely raspberry sorbet—a refreshing endnote. The ambiance exuded a classic French charm, and the staff were nothing but courteous. A recommendable spot for an authentic French dining experience.

Incredibly cheap for the amount of food you get in Midtown! Wish I had known about this place sooner since I work close by.My friend and I each ordered our own dry pots. Would highly recommend getting beef, fish fillet, wood ear mushroom and bok choy. The medium spicy was accurately medium, and I prefer just a tad bit spicier so next time I'd get spicy. For $13 drypot I think this place is amazing. They also have lunch specials for $10. We tried the Kung Pao Chicken, Sweet and Sour Chicken, and eggplant dish. My favorite by far was their eggplant dish and while Manting is known for their dry pot their lunch specials were absolutely delicious.  They have seating along the wall that accommodates small groups, but come early because this place gets packed during lunch!

Title: Quirky Taco Hideout Between Chinatown and Little Italy

Tucked away near Chinatown and Little Italy, this funky hipster taco joint is a true find. The hole-in-the-wall ambiance adds character and promises a flavorful lunch break. During my visit with a coworker, the sweet potato taco stood out—deceptively meat-like in texture and taste. Equally satisfying, though not the pinnacle of its kind, was the fish taco. Be warned, the accompanying red slaw is tasty but perilously runny; a potential hazard to your attire. Nonetheless, the spot resonates with charm, and while it won't top my taco destination list, it's certainly worth a revisit when I'm local.

Title: An Unforgettable Birthday Dinner at a Hidden Gem

My recent dining experience at this tucked-away restaurant, nestled atop a bustling mall, was nothing short of fantastic. Initial confusion about the location quickly gave way to a pleasant pre-dinner drink at a nearby bar, setting the tone for the evening ahead.

Upon entering the restaurant, the warm welcome from the amiable hostesses immediately dispelled any notion of a stuffy atmosphere that one might expect from a higher-end dining establishment. Though not seated by the window, our table offered a charming view of the mall's central circle, complemented by the cozy ambiance of a roaring fireplace.

The staff impressed with their relaxed yet attentive service, quickly setting us at ease. The novelty of a digital drink menu on an iPad was a bit challenging, but our server's helpful walkthrough smoothed that over. My wife opted for the vegetarian offerings while I indulged in the upgraded selections from the regular menu, which proved to be a delightful decision.

Every course was a revelation, not only in taste but also in the attentive detail with which each dish was explained. The servers maintained engaging conversation, ensuring a personal touch that enhanced the entire dining experience. The foie gras and the assortment of desserts were the crowning glories of a meal where every plate was a work of art.

In conclusion, the extraordinary care from the staff, combined with the exquisite food and inviting atmosphere, made for an unforgettable birthday dinner. I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to anyone who not only appreciates culinary excellence but also values a truly special dining experience. Hats off to the entire team for nailing it and for a memorable celebration.

4 stars is strictly for the food because every single thing was surprisingly flavorful and delicious. Came in with one of my best friends to catch up over some food and drinks on a Wednesday evening around 6. The place was super packed - even the bar. So the hostess suggested that we go downstairs to their Cellar Bar - not nearly as much ambiance as the upstairs but still ok. The bartender/waiter (tall Asian dude who didn't bother to tell us his name) was not very pleasant, which is why I removed a star. The cellar bar was empty aside from one other table when we arrived, yet and still we felt extremely rushed and unattended to. About 20mins later it got packed and it went even more downhill from there. Every time I tried to flag him down he made us feel like we were a bother, and then when he actually came over, I wouldn't even be finished with my sentence before he hurried off to another table. The couple seated next to us even left before they got a chance to order. I leaned over and jokingly said, "Why are you guys leaving, because our waiter sucks?" And the woman responded, "Yea it's starting to get crowded so we're gonna go somewhere where the waiter doesn't mind actually waiting on us!" I'll be back because the food was awesome, but only if there's availability upstairs.

I loved the sake sashimi, it was definitely the creamiest and richest salmon I've had in such a long time. Even the wasabi was better than the standard. Quite pleased with that appetizer. Unfortunately, the waiter forgot to bring us the sesame tofu we ordered, so that was a little disappointing. Nonetheless, the cold soba was amazing. The noodles were chewy, and the tempura was crispy too. Don't get the warm soba, they were pretty bad, the noodles were way too soft and had no texture. The dessert was lovely-red bean ball and green tea ice cream. The space was really cute and the wait wasn't too bad for a Saturday night. Overall a really nice place that I would come back to.

It looks as if when I finally decided to write a review for this place, it was the last time I would have my favorite carbonara. I've been twice since writing the review, the first time I thought it was fluke but it was just as bad last night. I don't know if they changed the recipe or the ingredients (or both) but the carbonara is no longer the same. It feels watered down, not as flavorful. Like they use a different Parmesan or much less of it. Before updating the review I also checked with a buddy that loved the carbonara, coincidently he had been just the week before, and also said it wasn't as good.  A lot of the service staff is different and I've noticed the quality of the service had been going down for last couple of months. They take a while to check on you, no longer offer freshly grated cheese with the pastas, etc. Oh well - it was great while it lasted. Funny enough, looking at something of the recent reviews and folks are also complaining about food and service quality. I hope they notice the new reviews and bring the old Olio back!

I recently ordered a '3 veg plate' from this restaurant via Uber Eats and was thoroughly disappointed. The kale and apple caesar was underwhelming with only a single, lackluster piece of apple. The thai chili noodles were a letdown, arriving cold and having a slimy texture that reminded me of subpar airplane food. The only saving grace was the quinoa with squash and mushrooms, which was decent but could not redeem the overall experience. Additionally, the portion sizes were skimpy, not providing good value for money. My advice would be to opt for establishments like Dig Inn or sweetgreen for a satisfying meal with seasonal and healthy options.

Upon visiting Fournos, the initial sticker shock of my $14 lamb lunch plate was soon mitigated by its generous portion size, effectively providing two meals. My plate was an ample assortment of roast lamb with chickpeas, complemented by sides of broccoli, a "Greek and cheese" (presumably a spin on mac and cheese), and rice with lentils. A standout was the spicy feta sauce which, due to its robust flavor and necessity, I lavishly applied to both the somewhat dry lamb and lackluster rice.

The broccoli side was well-prepared and enjoyable, while the "Greek and cheese" was merely passable. Regrettably, the overall experience of the hot food was underwhelming, leaving me with a sense of obligation to finish my meal rather than waste food.

Although I was left unsatisfied with the hot offerings, the pastry display caught my eye and would entice me for a future visit. However, I'd be hesitant to delve into their hot dishes again.

Perched 60 floors high, Manhatta offers expansive views of the city. I had wanted to come here with my family for our girls' weekend but we, unfortunately, booked too late for dinner. Instead, I dined solo for lunch while waiting for planes and a train to arrive. Lunch on a gloriously sunny day meant clear views from almost every angle. Simple and well-designed mid-century modern furnishings, chunky banquette seating, and gold accents provide a comfortable setting for French fare. There is a large, long bar behind the hostess stand, an open kitchen at the center of the space, and a vast dining room.The menu is curated, with the option of a lunch-time tasting menu or a few appetizers and entrées available à la carte. I have always been partial to snails - there is even photographic evidence of me eating snails at 3 or 4 years old - so I had to try the scotch snails. They were fantastic - chewy snails on spicy sausage, drowning in garlic butter. The crusty, warm baguette was perfect for sopping up the garlic butter. And I would have had the entire hunk of bread if I weren't saving my carb allowance for dessert.I hear that the lamb burger is great but I love seafood so I went with the delicious loup de mer instead. Delicate and sweet, the pan-fried fish complemented the pillowy gnocchi, clams, and velvety sauce. I could not resist the light and fluffy pasta, so different than the lumps of hard-to-swallow flour that typically masquerade as gnocchi.For dessert, I debated having either the chocolate chip cookies or the hazelnut torte. Truth time. I actually was thinking of having both. After much consideration - since we are talking about dessert - I went with the latter. The torte was rich and chocolatey so the small portion size made perfect sense. Served with toasted hazelnuts, the dessert was memorable.Equally memorable was the service. Several managers stopped by to ensure that I was enjoying my meal, going as far as to ask for areas of improvement. Before I left, I toured the restaurant and noticed that opposite the bar, there is a spacious and comfortable lounge area. But what caught my eye were the fixed binoculars for sightseeing. I loved that these retro mainstays of road trips found a way into a retro-styled restaurant. Nice! From this area, I saw the best view of Ellis Island and the Statue of Liberty. Another wonderful memory.

This Han Dynasty is located in the lower floor of Dekalb Market Hall, apart from all of the stands. There are many seats inside and my friend and I were able to snag seats at around 7PM on a weeknight with no problem. We ordered their dry pot with fish ($20.95), string beans with minced pork ($15.95), and beef and tripe ($13.95). The food came out in perhaps less than five minutes after ordering. However, the dry pot is rather small for the price and felt more like portion for one person rather than family style. I enjoyed the dry pot, but I did find the dry pot increasingly salty as the meal went on. Even with the saltiness though, it's still pretty darn good. As for the string beans, there was hardly any pork inside, but it was probably my favorite part of this meal. I'm not a fan of their beef and tripe as I found it too hard and salty. This place isn't exactly where you go to find value meals, but the taste is mostly there and I might return for other items on their menu.

KiKi is just too cute not to visit, problem I they are always too popular and sorta have to wait.Beet Salad - expected to get beer salad but it's actually 50% beets 50% apple. I was def not in the mood to eat that much appleSalty Fish Roe Dip - expected to be more fish roe flavor but also mostly is potato with a hint of fish roe only (not too liking)Zucchini Fries - yummy and addicting but heavy Spinach Pie - very good and fresh, pie wasl still crispy Grandma's Lemon Chicken - love the lemon sauce and it makes the potato extra taatyBronzino - Dorado and Snapper were both out so we had no choice, it is how bronzino normally could be, good but expected.Make sure you come early! Seats by the window are cute.

My love of Mercado increases exponentially with Spanish Diner where breakfast is authentic and delicious.Ate: Eggs and pistou Cafe con lecheChocolate croissant Pistou is Spanish ratatouille and the perfect compliment to the eggs and the coffee and croissants were perfection! Amor!

My first experience at noodle bar was mediocre but I returned a second time and had a much better experience. The first time around, I ordered the garlic chicken ramen. The noodles were delicious, but the broth was salty which made it hard to finish once my noodles were gone. It was served in a bowl with a metal spoon rather than the wider, deep spoons I'm accustomed to when eating ramen. In addition to the saltiness, this immediately distinguished Noodle Bar as a place for Americanized Asian Fusion food rather than somewhere to go for an authentic ramen dish. Frankly, I've had better, authentic ramen for a much better price. But if Americanized fusions are your thing, check this place out. I wanted to give the appetizers a try, so I returned for lunch. The pork bun and big eye tuna crudo were delicious and my entree, the ginger scallion noodles, was impressive. Perhaps most memorable was the chickpea ice cream -- unique flavors, sweet with a hint of savory and lightly topped with cereal. Service was very attentive. But as someone who likes exploring NYC's rich cultural foodscape, it's not somewhere I see myself frequenting knowing there's much better places for this kind of food out there.

Title: A Mixed Experience with a Standout Ribeye

My recent visit to this restaurant left me with some mixed feelings, although there were definite highlights. The Wagyu ribeye was the star of the show – impeccably tender and cooked to perfection; it's a dish I'd wholeheartedly recommend. The ambiance, too, was memorable, with the cool décor and private booths creating a perfect dining setting.

The service was attentive and prompt, adding to the overall positive experience. However, the restaurant seems to have a light hand when it comes to seasoning. Both the rolled beef brisket and the rice were disappointingly bland and could have used a more generous touch of flavor – perhaps a savory sauce or a sprinkle of soy.

Despite trying three different meats, the ribeye was unparalleled. While the tenderloin and chuck flap were satisfactory, they paled in comparison to the ribeye's succulence. In summary, when you visit, zero in on the ribeye for a truly satisfying meal, but be prepared for some dishes to fall short on flavor.

Had a great time at this lively bar, especially on their trivia night (Tuesday). It was packed, so a reservation is a must. The service was commendably earnest amidst the chaos. Their extensive and affordable drink menu impressed, along with some sweet deals. I didn't sample the food, but it sure looked tempting. Pro tip: Check in on Yelp for a complimentary 5oz. lager!

Title: A Flavorful Melting Pot at Pure Thai Cookhouse

Pure Thai Cookhouse may toe the line of Thai authenticity with its eclectic mix of Malaysian and Burmese-inspired dishes, but that's the beauty of Thai cuisine – it's a delicious mosaic of its neighbors' flavors. The restaurant buzzes with life around noon, so arrive early to snag a seat when doors open at 11:30AM. A word of caution: the three-chili dishes, like the fiery Jungle Curry Fried Rice, are not for the faint of heart or those with afternoon meetings – they pack a punch! Service is efficient, keeping the bustling lunch crowd moving, and the prices won't break the bank. If you're in Midtown West and craving a culinary adventure, Pure Thai Cookhouse delivers a spirited and affordable experience.

I'm so glad this was one of my meals on a recent trip to New York! It definitely scratched my itch for good Italian food. RESERVATIONS: Made just a couple hours in advance for a Saturday at 6:45, for four people.SERVICE: Professional, no complaints.MUST-HAVES: Of course, their namesake the Mafaldini Scampi (5 stars)! I usually don't like seafood pasta, or more al dente pasta, and despite this fitting both descriptions, I (and everyone at the table) loved this! Mezzaluna (4.5 stars), Chocolate Budino (5 stars) were also amazing.Beets (4 stars), Cauliflower (3.5 stars), Spaghetti/clams (3.5 stars), and Panna cotta (4 stars) were decent, but all the other dishes made the meal well worth it!See my photos for additional details.

Title: A Charming Culinary Getaway at The Loeb Boathouse Central Park

Nestled in the heart of Central Park, The Loeb Boathouse Restaurant offers a picturesque dining experience that is both elegant and romantic. With panoramic views of the adjacent lake, this establishment is a haven for those looking to dine alfresco on the patio during the warm months or enjoy a cocktail by the outdoor bar. The indoor seating maintains the venue's elegance for those who prefer the indoors.

Reservations are strongly recommended at this sought-after location that does more than just serve food; it plays an integral role in the community by hosting fundraisers, corporate events, weddings, and special celebrations.

The Boathouse also provides opportunities for lake excursions with rowboat and gondola rentals at reasonable rates, adding an adventurous twist to your visit. For a quicker dining option, the Express Café serves an array of breakfast items, burgers, soups, salads, sandwiches, and delectable baked treats at prices that are significantly more wallet-friendly than the Lakeside Restaurant.

While there’s no parking within Central Park, the Boathouse alleviates this with a complimentary shuttle service providing informative tours en route—a tip for the driver is a nice touch. Avoid overpriced rickshaw rides; they're not the best value for your time or money.

Service is top-notch, with courteous staff ensuring a smooth and pleasant dining experience. The restaurant doesn't skimp on quality, offering an array of fresh breads with real butter and a surprisingly affordable wine list for New York City standards.

Although on the pricier side, the menu justifies the expense. My own lunch, the Branzino a la Plancha, was a delightful dish with beautifully cooked fish and vegetables. Accommodating staff readily adapted meals for dietary restrictions, as evidenced by my sister-in-law's enjoyable Twin Boathouse Burgers.

While the bread basket proved too tempting to leave room for dessert, The Loeb Boathouse promises a satisfying culinary journey. Combined with stunning views and the charm of Central Park, this restaurant is a must-visit for an elegant and memorable meal.

Title: A St. Paddy's Day to Remember at Scallywags Irish Pub

My visit to Scallywags Irish Pub on St. Patrick's Day proved to be the quintessential Irish experience I was seeking to cap off a festive afternoon. Upon arrival, we were greeted not only by the lively strums of a talented live musician but also by the prompt and welcoming staff.

Our appetizer choice, the seafood stuffed mushrooms, were satisfactory, albeit slightly overshadowed by an unconventional horseradish gravy that seemed out of place. Despite this, the seafood filling was quite enjoyable.

My mushroom Swiss burger was the highlight of my meal - flawlessly cooked, undeniably juicy, and accompanied by the perfect side of crispy matchstick fries. It paired wonderfully with my last beer of the day. Meanwhile, my companion relished in the traditional corned beef and cabbage, deeming it spot-on for the occasion and generous in portion.

Scallywags demonstrated remarkable efficiency and quality, especially notable during the hustle of a busy holiday. The endearing service and the vibrant live music solidified our experience as one worth repeating. I'm already looking forward to my next visit to Scallywags.

I've now come to Danji twice, once for dinner and once for brunch. This is a review for the brunch (dinner was very nice too!). We came in having made reservations on a Saturday, but there was room for walk-ins as well. The restaurant is small and intimate with a bar in the front, a section of communal high top tables, and then a few standard tables in the dining room. I like the subtle asian flair in the decor that extended to the wooden spoon decorations and the sliding table drawers with hidden menus. The service was prompt and our waitress was attentive throughout the meal.They have a few brunch drinks available for those who wish! We focused on the food, starting by splitting the spicy kfc korean fire chicken wings. I liked that they chose meatier wings to serve, and they were certainly spicy although perhaps somewhat lacking in flavor. We then each got our own bibimbap - one kimchi pork and one spicy pork belly - dolsot style. Would definitely recommend paying the extra $3 for dolsot style which means it's cooked in a stone pot and creates the BEST crunchy rice. The bibimbap was also really excellent, with a great combination of marinated vegetables, flavorful meat, and optional gochujang spicy sauce. This was more than enough food for one person; in fact, you could consider splitting one and getting something else in addition if you're not that hungry. Overall, I had a very pleasant experience at Danji. It's a small place so best for a date or a small group - I liked that the restaurant was quiet, making it easy to talk. If you're in the neighborhood looking for a tasty Korean meal this is definitely a good option.

Title: A Soba and Cocktail Haven Worth Every Visit

Visited this gastronomic gem twice, once lured by the promise of exceptional handmade soba and again to satisfy my burger craving, and both visits were nothing short of stellar.

Nestled just opposite the distinguished Odo, this bar exudes a Japanese izakaya-like charm, offering an inspired menu peppered with beef specialties and an inventive cocktail list. The Monday soba special is a must-try, showcasing the chef's prowess honed at Kaijutsu, while the friendly staff ensure your glass and plate are expertly curated.

On Soba Mondays, the place fills up quickly, a testament to its popularity. Their Old Fashioned, a symphony of rye, kuro sato, and black walnut bitters, hits the right notes of sweet and strong. The Jidori Kara-age makes a good starter, but sampling the bartender-recommended tofu or grilled eggplant next time wouldn't be amiss. However, the star was the Cold Kinoko Soba—each slurp was a delight of perfectly textured noodles in harmony with a medley of mushrooms and a rich, yet refreshing broth.

The regular menu doesn't disappoint either. The Sherry Blossom cocktail was a refreshing twist, and the Washyu Short Rib Deluxe Burger—an umami-packed masterpiece—paired with parmesan (and maybe truffle) fries was indulgently good. Rounding off the meal, the Sake Lees Ice Cream Monaka was a fine balance of sweet and refreshing.

With an impressive 4.7 rating, the place stands out in a street of culinary heavyweights. Whether it's for the soba that's a cut above the rest or the finely crafted meals and drinks, this spot earns a fervent recommendation. I'll surely be back for more.

If wings are your thing, then this gem is a must-visit in NYC. After years of consistent quality, it remains a favorite for good reason. The lunch specials offer great value, but let's talk about the standout dishes - the beet salad is simply AMAZING, a refreshing twist that leaves you craving more. Don't skip the Truffle Mac n cheese - it's a creamy, indulgent masterpiece. Pair your meal with a selection from their impressive lineup of beers and ales for the perfect dining experience. Highly recommended for a casual lunch that delivers on flavor and satisfaction!

I don't really understand why people like this place so much, it seems like it's just another pizza joint in the city. After trying it, this is one of those spots where you see a line out the door because their storefront is too small to fit more than 20 people inside.Compared to other pizza spots in New York, it's not something I'd go out of my way for or crave for. It's unfortunate because I think they have 1 or 2 items I haven't seen at other places before but they just didn't deliver that well on flavor or texture. The one everyone seems to get was their square piece of pepperoni that isn't thin crust but also not deep dish style either. It reminded me of a flatbread but on foccasia bread without the rosemary flavor. There were a lot of pieces of pepperoni on top. They have garlic powder here along with chili flakes and parmesan cheese to add on top. But they could use an extra counter for people to solely use the condiments or get napkins etc. The current set up forces people to interrupt the people using the counter to eat to use the toppings because they have to reach in between them etc.The service is also subpar, these guys really seem like they don't care. They seem like snobs who don't care who their customers are or the questions they have about the food. It seems like they want you to choose your food and then get out of the way for the next customer. Not very friendly or giving off good vibes at all.

I recently discovered Takumi Taco during the Ritual App's midtown $1 Food Festival and it's safe to say it's now on my must-visit list. Takumi Taco, tucked away in Urbanspace @ 570 Lex, offers a delightful fusion of Japanese-inspired Mexican cuisine.

Their menu boasts the traditional lineup of tacos, burritos, bowls, and salads, with a variety of proteins topped with unique ingredients like edamame, miso vinaigrette, and Japanese curry. I opted for the chicken adobo burrito, which even at its promotional price of $2.59, felt like a steal compared to its usual $11.02.

The burrito itself was a flavorful, hefty portion that could easily satisfy two or three appetites. The inclusion of edamame added an unexpected but enjoyable crunch that complemented the well-seasoned chicken adobo. Fresh and substantial, the burrito certainly warrants its full price.

Takumi Taco stands out amongst its peers at Urbanspace and has now become a place I'll frequent when in the area. It's notable to mention that they also have locations at 230 Park Ave and Chelsea Market for those closer to those spots.

Title: Cozy and Authentic Hot Pot Delight at 99 Favor Taste

If you're in the mood for an authentic hot pot experience, 99 Favor Taste should be at the top of your list. Making a reservation is a breeze with their phone service, and upon arrival, you'll be greeted by tasteful interior decor and comfortable booth seating.

The highlight of my visit was definitely the hot pot. With individual pots and adjustable heat settings, the personal touch in cooking your meal is exceptional. The menu offers an array of soup bases like the spicy mala and a rich bone broth, catering to various palates.

For those who love to share, the meat and vegetable options are perfect for a family-style feast. The authenticity doesn't stop there; you'll be impressed with their selection of Chinese sauces, especially the sha-cha and house special sauce, which are perfect accompaniments to the fresh ingredients.

The prices are reasonable considering the extensive menu that even includes BBQ choices. A neat tip – paying in cash gets you an 8% discount.

The service matched the quality of the food, with staff always on hand to top up the soup base and water, ensuring that the dining experience flowed smoothly. My personal favorites were the beef tripe and the vegetable platter with enoki mushrooms, which were standout choices for their freshness.

In summary, 99 Favor Taste delivers a warm, hearty meal perfect for cold days, with a combination of great food, fair pricing, and attentive service. This place comes highly recommended for hot pot enthusiasts craving that authentic touch.

Title: Satisfying Brunch at Cortlandt Alley Diner

My Saturday brunch at Cortlandt Alley Diner was a delightful experience. Arriving at 11 am, the diner was bustling with energy and nearly full, but we managed to secure a comfortable round table for our party of five near the bar and kitchen area. 

Service was impeccable from the get-go, with a notable mention for the bottomless coffee that kept coming as we dove into our brunch. The menu, though I wished it offered a few more options, had an undeniable high-quality comfort food charm. 

Standouts included the foie gras scrambled eggs, which were a decadent treat with a generous portion of seared foie gras - a must-try for future patrons. THE burger lived up to its name, a towering example of American-style cooking with large portions and plenty of sauce. Even the granola for the kids was well-received, making for a universally enjoyable meal.

Despite the hearty portions, the service staff made the experience feel welcoming and un-rushed. By the end of the meal, we were unanimously satisfied, with no room left to indulge in dessert. Cortlandt Alley Diner dishes out a solid brunch with the comforting heft of diner classics. Definitely worth a visit, especially for those looking for a taste of indulgence to start their weekend.

Title: A Super Saiyan Evolution in Ramen - Goku's Delight

I recently ventured into Goku, a ramen shop that seems to be a reincarnation of its predecessor, Kame — both names hailing from the 'Dragon Ball Z' anime. My inner sleuth can't help but wonder about the licensing magic behind the scenes. But onto the food: the new vegetarian ramen bowl is a revelation, bursting with umami-rich broth that rivals its meaty counterparts, and a generous mix of veggies, kimchi, and corn that left me thoroughly content.

However, there was a slight misstep — the hard-boiled egg was disappointingly bland, lacking the depth of a traditional soy sauce-marinated egg. It's a fixable flaw, one I hope they'll address.

On the upside, the takoyaki appetizer was a delectable preamble to the main course. And here's a tip: snag a lunchtime bargain with half-priced appetizers with an entree or a nifty 20% off through a Yelp check-in. Just remember, no double dipping on the deals. Overall, Goku brings a strong game to the ramen scene, especially for those favoring a plant-based twist.

Title: Fresh and Filling – Just Salad Impresses!

I recently dined at Just Salad and was thrilled by their extensive selection of fresh and affordable salad options. The ability to customize my salad was a highlight, with an array of bases, toppings, and succulent meats to choose from. I opted for the chicken barbacoa and chicken shawarma, both of which were perfectly seasoned and delightfully moist—a rarity in salad spots!

Their spicy avocado mash is a game-changer, adding a vibrant kick to the salad that I highly recommend. Portion sizes didn't disappoint either; the bowls are generously packed, ensuring a satisfying meal. To top it all off, their smoothies complement the greens beautifully and won't break the bank. If you're in search of a salad that ticks all the boxes, Just Salad is your go-to!

One of the exciting things about going to big cities like New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, etcetera Is the diversity and selection of fine dining that you can't get elsewhere. When we were planning our trip to New York, we decided to have two big fancy dinners out, along with our other food adventures, and one dinner out was here.I made my reservation through open table, and read the reviews which sounded promising. The photos on Yelp looked gorgeous, and I thought that this would be a decent risk for French cuisine, given the reviews.When we arrived, it was clear that there were two dining rooms, and I don't understand how they decided who qualified for what dining room. It seemed like the locals, or the regulars, were in the superior room, and the visitors or out of towners where elsewhere.We were brought the menu, and immediately were excited about their drink list. Coming from the North Bay, I love Fernet, and not only did they have some but they also had one specifically distilled in San Francisco which we ordered and was delicious. What a treat.We decided on drinks, hubby had a gin and tonic, and I had a barrel strength old fashioned, at the encouragement and recommendation of the server. The drinks were fine but nothing to be overly excited about. Menu also looked good, but overall not as interesting as I was hoping it would be.For dinner, I ordered the lobster salad, and hubby ordered the rabbit and cheese ravioli. We intentionally did not order a starter, because we knew how beautiful their desserts were, and wanted to save room. Unfortunately, the way I like my lobster is fully cooked, and this one was lightly poached, and tasted very metallic and far too soft for my taste. Hubby's ravioli was something he raved about, and vacuumed up just as soon as it arrived at the table.For dessert, he ordered the apple tart with ginger ice cream, which was a weird flavor combination due to the ginger being extremely overpowering to the delicate apple taste. I ordered the chocolate souffle which was very light, and our server brought us a complimentary third dessert which was the rhubarb creme brulee, which was by far my favorite.Service was too fast, informative but not overly friendly, and was not very personable or very elegant. The hostess at the front was extremely standoffish and cool to us, especially after I informed her after visiting the lady's room that there was no toilet paper in the entire bathroom. Instead of taking that information as something that needed to be fixed, she gave me quite the glare. Ambiance was fair, however in the dining room that we were sat in, there was a gaudy disco ball at the ceiling, which seemed very out-of-place in an establishment like this. The menu, however it might seem for this area, looked to be playing it safe for the caliber of restaurant that this place occupies within the New York food scene.Overall, this was quite unexpectedly one of the lower quality experiences for food that we have had in New York. We had high hopes, but we thought that they were substantiated. Pricing was high given the overall quality of the food, along with the so-so ambiance, and completely lacking the excitement that we were expecting. This may have been on some top list at some point, but I doubt that day is now, given what we experienced yesterday.

I recently visited this restaurant for brunch and it was truly delightful. The ambiance was lively yet conducive to conversation, allowing us to catch up comfortably. The menu offered an array of choices, satisfying various tastes. Additionally, the coffee was exceptional. It's a spot I'd recommend for anyone looking for a pleasant brunch experience.

This restaurant is one of a kind because it specializes in fusion Asian salad.It's fresh, delicious, and vibrant to look at. Though the ingredients are on the simple side, the resulting product is amazing!I would recommend putting sauce on the side because with greens on the bottom, pouring all the sauce will make the whole salad rather soggy!Would order again!

This is my second time at this establishment. The first time I went was about 2 and Half years ago. I wanted to make sure the fried chicken was actually good and was able to compare it to other places. Well I am here to say this place lives up to its hype. During this visit, my S.O and I had the Soy Garlic Chicken as a starter. The chicken was hot, fresh, and so tasty. For our entrees we had the Bulgogi Bibimbap and the Korean Steak and Eggs over kimichi rice. Both were equally delicious the steak was tender, had good flavor, and was a little sweet. We also tried the Watermelon Soju. We both had about three drinks each.I would definitely return here

A lady on the train suggested we stop here for some delicious pizza and weren't disappointed! We walked through Chinatown and eventually happened upon the restaurant. The wait was only about 20 minutes for a busy Saturday night. Our table was perfect for our party of 6. We got the spicy salad, an order of raviolis, and three pizzas. It was plenty to feed us. The pizzas were all really good... especially the dough. The raviolis were equally good! The service was on point. All in all, we had a great experience here.

Friendly old-timey Chelsea diner with great service and lots of reasonably priced healthy options. Spacious first floor with tables, booths and a bar. They have a second floor as well but I've never been up there. Dinners come with soup or a generous salad with choice of dressing. Last night we both chose chicken entrees which The Dish excels in preparing. My Chicken Castelli included two substantial lean white breasts nicely jazzed up with fresh mushrooms, artichoke hearts and a lemony tomato sauce. You can get side veggies steamed with garlic (I chose spinach). Hubbie got chicken shish kebob resting on saffron rice, a generous and tasty dish with plenty of fresh veggies.The Dish isn't pretentious or trendy in the least, and that's a good thing in my book. We hope they stay in business a long time because there aren't many places left like this in NYC.

At DPJ, the Da Pan Ji is all the rage – priced at a modest $12.50, it delivers a luxury taste experience that rivals the Lamborghini of dishes. Much like the esteemed vehicle, it stands out with no need for fanfare; its flavors speak for themselves. A must-try for any culinary enthusiast.

I had the pleasure of dining at a spot that left me torn between indulgence and practicality, a true testament to its culinary prowess. Reliving the experience through my photos, I can't help but laud some of the standout dishes that set this establishment apart.

First, the uni was a revelation, devoid of the brininess one might expect, boasting a texture so sublime it nearly defied description. Then came the wagyu, a dish so spectacular I found myself daydreaming of a meal composed solely of its buttery, mouthwatering slices. Finally, the lobster - a crustacean so perfectly prepared, its succulent, bouncy texture set a new benchmark for what I consider the epitome of seafood excellence.

In sum, the level of culinary craftsmanship on display was nothing short of extraordinary, leaving me to savor the memory of those dishes, even if I may not find myself returning to the restaurant anytime soon.

TLDR: New omakase addition to the West Village area. Good value at 17 for $125, expect more condiments and accents on your nigiri here.I was looking forward to trying maaser when I heard about them. The first thing I noticed was the noise, it's definitely a louder omakase. The customers talk more and the chefs will encourage the Insta-moments, holding a large crab out for the camera or an uni shell for you to see. I enjoy a slightly quieter omakase but there's nothing wrong with hyping up the crowd.Food was served a bit on the faster side. Our entire omakase was done in little over an hour. Almost every piece had some sort of sauce, condiment, etc. I'm okay with modern nigiri but on certain pieces the add-ons felt unnecessary. The medium fatty tuna with a dab of wasabi sauce, the marinated tuna with onions, the sweet shrimp with a spoonful of caviar. Sometimes these extras take away the taste of the actual fish itself and what makes that piece special gets lost. If you're going to give a piece of nigiri a lot of dressing, it should make me smile sheepishly when I eat it and want to order seconds.One piece that stood out to me was the golden eye snapper, not in a good way. For a historically tasty piece, this one was awful. It was dressed with some thin-sliced onions and there was this strong taste of just.. not good. Perhaps it was just this one time but it definitely put a damper on the meal.Aside from the one piece mentioned, everything else tasted fine. There was nothing that really stood out to me much, no single piece that wowed me or showed me something new.I think if you're in the mood for omakase and don't want to feel too guilty about the price, maaser is a solid place. Also good if you want to go with a group of friends and drink a bit more, the BYOB policy certainly helps.

Really good food and coming from someone who grew up in India. Did the 3 course pre fix dinner and got the tiger prawns, pickled ribs, and Assamese dumplings. Absolutely loved the shrimp and ribs, but the dumplings were pretty amazing too. For the main course we got the chicken malai tikka, sea bass, and ghee roast lamb. I personally thought the malai chicken was too creamy, but the rest of my party loved it. And for the dessert, I would get the treacle tart. It was the best end to the entire meal. And the kheer wasn't too bad either. Overall, great experience. I would love to try their tasting menu the next time.

Title: A Burger Experience Not to Miss at Au Cheval

My quest for the ultimate burger fix led me to Au Cheval, a spot I adored back in Chicago. If you're here, do yourself a favor and indulge in the burger—it's non-negotiable. The patty, a harmonious blend of juiciness and tenderness, did not disappoint. Their signature move of topping everything with an egg is quite the experience, and while I'm not entirely sure of the egg's role on the burger, it's a specialty you shouldn't skip.

We couldn't resist trying the special fries and scrambled eggs with foie gras on the side. If simplicity is your mantra, stick with the standard fries; they shine without the extra sauces. The foie gras, decadently rich and served with toast, creates an indulgent spread reminiscent of bone marrow. Be warned, the prices reflect the quality—with burgers starting at $20, it's a splurge.

Pro tip: portion sizes here are generous. A 'double' burger means three patties, while a 'single' serves up two. Despite the price tag, Au Cheval has earned its place as my top burger destination in NYC.

Came here with my boyfriend for restaurant week! We got an assortment of dishes so get ready for a long review! For drinks we got the Hemingway Wishes and From The Fields. The Hemingway wishes came with these pretty little edible butterflies on it! (And I hate butterflies!) they were tasty though, bf didn't love them. The drink was fantastic. Very refreshing. From the Fields was ok, bf loved it. It was exactly what he expected. For our appetizer I got the Andalusian Gazpacho which had watermelon, tomato, & feta cheese with baguette croutons. It was sooooo delicious. At first I was skeptical but WOW. The serving size was very big and I didn't even finish it but the balance between the watermelon and tomato flavor was really nice and the croutons added a nice crunch to it- and never seemed to get soggy! Our other appetizer was the Crudo Salmon. It was raw salmon over bulgar with a cilantro aioli. It was pretty good! I'm not one for raw fish so I only took a bite but it was pretty tasty! My boyfriend devoured it so I think it's safe to say he enjoyed. Four out meals I got the ricotta homemade pasta thing. I thought it was going to be more of a cacio e Pepe pasta dish but it ended up also having some pesto along with it. It was very tasty, and you could tell the pasta was homemade. Very fresh and filling! My bf got the Harissa Lamb. It was served with tzatziki sauce and a squash purée. The server asked us how we wanted it cooked and we said medium, but it came out very pink! We ate it either way and it was delicious! Meat was very tender and melted in your mouth ... in a good way lol. For dessert we both got the same - I don't remember what it was called but it was almost like the shape of a Twinkie but was a delicate chocolatey caramel truffle almost? It was very soft and VERY rich. So so so good. It also came with a little crunchy chocolate square over some vanilla ice cream. I'm drooling just thinking about it. The service here was excellent as well. Our waiters were kind, funny, able to make good recommendations, and very accommodating. They asked us for any food allergies right when we sat down which I always appreciate. I was definitely worried about trying this spot as I have eaten from the little front bar takeaway area a few times and been severely disappointed. But I guess you just have to go to the restaurant in the back, because this meal and experience was to die for!

The owners of this bar went to extraordinary lengths to bring their DC/Maryland/Virginia background to this NYC bar and restaurant, and it shows: It shows in the menu, the decor, and friendly and welcoming ambience that contrasts with busy and bustling Bleecker street right outside.JoJo's Philosophy also serves as the home of the NYC Caps Crew- and becomes the go to spot for DC natives to watch Washington Capitals hockey in manhattan. During the NHL playoffs (April to June) it can get quite packed, but it's still worth it for the sports bar experience.The menu is very imaginative- offering unique takes on common bar food (like the most interesting item on the menu, sliders with waffle fries serving as the buns) and adds some dishes more native to Maryland, like crab cakes.The bar also runs great promotions, but my favorite by far: Taco Tuesday. $2 tacos, and pretty well priced bar promotions.Great food, maybe the friendliest staff of all time, and great value for a bar situated right in Manhattan.

I'm a regular for lunch at this spot, where the diverse menu keeps everything wallet-friendly at around $10. However, this was my first foray into their dinner offerings, and it didn't disappoint, with plates designed for sharing, featuring 4-5 pieces each.

The BFF roll, a combination of salmon tempura, avocado, and cream cheese, was decent, though I must admit that cream cheese in sushi isn't to my liking. The MEW MUD, reminiscent of a deconstructed poke bowl, was a highlight. It paired spicy tuna, salmon, seaweed salad, crab salad, and avocado with spicy mayo, creating a perfect harmony of flavors.

Sashimi lovers would appreciate the Yellowtail carpaccio and the Hatate Carpaccio. The former was exceptionally fresh, enhanced by a delightful ponzu sauce. The latter featured succulent scallops with a unique and delicious mayo mustard sauce, something I hadn't encountered before but would certainly seek out again.

The standout dish for me was the Kimchi udon; its creaminess perfectly balanced the zesty kimchi, making it a dish I would highly recommend.

In summary, the dinner experience here lives up to the promise of their lunches, with fresh ingredients, innovative flavors, and great options for sharing.

Title: A Festive Feast with Friends at a Vibrant Eatery

My latest dining adventure with a large group took us to a lively restaurant that hit all the right notes for a casual yet memorable meal. Right off the bat, the appetizers set a high bar – the nachos were a crowd favorite, the empanadas and calamari received a collective thumbs-up, and the sweet plantains were a delightful treat.

Burgers were on the menu for a couple of my companions, and they were served up juicy with all the classic trimmings to their satisfaction. My choice, the lobster ravioli, was sumptuous and well-executed – a real winner in my book. The skirt steak, enjoyed by two others, was devoured in its entirety, speaking volumes about its flavor and quality.

A friend's pan-seared catfish caught my eye and apparently tasted as good as it looked, while another's pesto rice offered a unique twist that pleasantly surprised. The lemon chicken served was a generous portion that didn't skimp on taste, and the wings paired with fried plantain chips rounded out our spread with satisfaction.

To wash it all down, two types of pitchers – classic margaritas and the intriguing 'What Happens in Harlem' – provided a refreshing and delicious complement to our meal. The atmosphere was electric thanks to a DJ spinning great tunes, making it a perfect spot for a Saturday afternoon hangout.

While the seating, comprised of high stools and tables, wasn't the most comfortable, it was a small hiccup in an otherwise fantastic experience. A special shoutout to our waitress, whose enthusiasm and attentiveness added to our positive experience.

Overall, the vibrant setting combined with tasty food and top-notch service guaranteed one thing – I'll definitely be returning.

Order the duck spring roll off the Lunar New Year menu for starters. The restaurant week menu was good but not great. The Thai chicken wings were my favorite but the steak was a little chewy for medium rare. The XO sauce under the Arctic Char was too much and too salty.  I don't think it belonged in the dish and took away for the delicate fish which could have used an extra 30 seconds of crispening time on the skin. There was enough intensity and sodium to coat an entire bowl of noodles with the excessively salty savory sauce left at the bottom of my bowl.  The fingerling potatoes were a little oily too and came on both our entrees.  Seemed to be the starch of choice.  Where's the rice? I think one of us should have gotten rice or noodles with our entree. The fingerlings were incongruous and a bit of a cop out in my opinion especially with my fish. The calamansi tart was nice and I enjoyed the coconut sorbet that was served with it. There's a chocolate dessert with ice cream  (I forget what it was) for those who have more of a sweet tooth. The view of the Vessel unfortunately would be the only reason why I would come again.

I've just discovered what I can only describe as THE BEST SEAFOOD PLACE EVER! Their boil sauce is an absolute game-changer – bursting with flavor, it's the perfect complement to the fresh seafood. My go-to order here is a mix of shrimps and clams, with around 1-1.5 pounds per person being the sweet spot. The beauty of this spot is the ability to share dishes, allowing everyone to sample a bit of everything.

We kicked things off with cajun fries and fried calamari, both tasty appetizers that set the stage for the main event. And let me tell you, the shrimps and clams here are on another level – massive in size and perfectly cooked. If you're feeling particularly hungry, an order over 2 pounds gets you the bonus of corn and potatoes mixed in.

While our last visit did include a batch of clams that were more shell than meat, this isn't the norm for this place. Despite clams being heavier and this place pricing by the pound, I can't help but order them – they're just too good. However, the shrimps are the star of the show – they're more than worth it and are incredibly scrumptious.

Make no mistake, this is a must-visit for any seafood lover. Don't miss out!

Title: A Cozy Culinary Haven in the West Village – Jane

On a bustling evening in the West Village, my friend Daveed and I were in search of a dining spot that could offer respite from the crowded streets. That's when we stumbled upon Jane. An inviting atmosphere welcomed us, along with the freedom to select our own seating – we opted for a spot right in the middle.

Jane's air conditioning was a pleasant relief, and their impressive wine list did not disappoint. A Malbec was our companion for the meal, which was just the start of a comforting culinary experience. The menu, abundant in homey delights, immediately resonated with us as tourists.

The seafood chowder I sampled was flavorful, though it left me wishing for a touch more from the sea. My main course, the Jane Street burger, however, was a triumph of taste and preparation. The accompanying fries may have lacked crispness, but hunger made short work of that minor flaw.

Daveed went for the classic spaghetti and meatballs. It was a hit flavor-wise, though he noted that the addition of bread and more Parmesan cheese would have elevated the dish.

Service at Jane was both friendly and sharp, maintaining the right balance of attentiveness without intrusion. As we wrapped up our meals, the restaurant started to buzz with more patrons, yet it never felt cramped.

In short, Jane is a find in the West Village where comfort food and a relaxed vibe take center stage. For locals or regulars, it's easy to see how Jane could become a twice-weekly dining destination.

Upon entering the dimly lit enclave of this Michelin-acclaimed restaurant, one is instantly captivated by the seamless blend of traditional Japanese aesthetics with contemporary flair. The modest menu is paired with an impressive selection of wine and sake, tempting one to indulge in the latter.

Opting for the sushi/sashimi omakase, we found the quality in line with expectations—a testament to the essence of freshness. Yet, amidst the culinary journey, there were moments of discordance with a couple of selections that fell short of our palate's preferences. However, these were minor detours in an otherwise enjoyable gastronomic experience.

The chefs were the embodiment of focused craftsmanship, with interactions scarce as they dedicated themselves to the art of each dish's preparation. Meanwhile, the service staff excelled, attentively ensuring our glasses remained full.

Yielding to temptation, we added an order of uni and toro, both of which were nothing short of sublime. The finale of this indulgent symphony came with a bill of $777, a testament to the exclusivity of the experience for two, inclusive of additional delicacies and sake.

While Kosaka may not top my list of omakase destinations in a city brimming with culinary titans, it stands as a worthy contender, meriting a personal assessment by anyone drawn to the finesse of Japanese cuisine.

Tucked away between Madison Avenue and 6th Avenue on West 32nd, Koreatown's latest gem, Sam Won Artisanal Korean BBQ, serves up a luxurious slice of Seoul's culinary scene. With a legacy stretching back 42 years, Sam Won, although a newcomer to K-Town NYC, comes with a reputation as one of the oldest Korean BBQ restaurants in South Korea.

The ambiance is impressive — a sprawling 10,000 square feet across three levels, with the capacity to seat 180 guests, Sam Won spares no expense to deliver an authentic experience, reportedly investing over 5 million dollars. True to Korean BBQ tradition, it's a place best enjoyed with a group; the communal dining style is part of the charm.

On my visit, I indulged in the Samwon Galbi, the classic marinated beef short ribs, and the Pork Belly, both requiring double orders as per the restaurant's policy. Expect to invest at least $70 for this portion of the meal. The banchan, an assortment of sides, complement the meats perfectly, but a word of advice: hold off on ordering extras until you've nearly conquered the BBQ.

Sam Won's menu also features a mix of traditional fares like stir-fry glass noodles and contemporary twists such as kimchi cheese fries. The service is attentive without being intrusive, with a well-coordinated staff ensuring a seamless dining experience.

Open for almost 8 months, Sam Won is already a strong contender for the best Korean BBQ in NYC. Reservations are recommended but walk-ins are also greeted with a warm welcome. If you're in for an indulgent Korean feast, Sam Won Artisanal Korean BBQ won't disappoint.

Title: A Memorable Evening at Joseph's

My board colleagues and I, in New York for meetings, chose Joseph's for a group dinner and it did not disappoint. From the moment we stepped in, the service was impeccable—warm greetings, efficient seating, and accommodating our request for separate checks with grace.

The culinary journey began with a split mixed green salad followed by perfectly grilled Bronzino. A tablemate savored the halibut, praising every morsel. The wine selection complemented our meal wonderfully, and we indulged in a shared dessert course featuring an unforgettably authentic cannoli and a luscious tiramisu.

Joseph's truly masters the art of Italian cuisine, paired with service that makes you feel right at home. Highly recommended for a leisurely and exquisite dining experience.

Title: A Satisfying Slurp of Hunan Flavors

I recently visited Hunan Slurp with a friend, right as they opened on a Saturday at noon. Despite our reservation, the half-empty venue was a surprise given the quality inside. The decor’s subtle elegance lent an upscale atmosphere, reflected in the price but pleasantly echoed even in the details of the restroom.

The Hunan Salad, priced at $12, was a delightful blend of grilled pepper, eggplant, and the intrigue of preserved duck egg, beautifully presented like a stuffed eggplant. My companion savored it while I took joy in the delectable Hometown Lu Fen ($22)—a noodle dish of remarkable texture, just-right spice, and generous portions tipped in favor of the noodles. The char siu outshone the spare ribs, leaving me wanting more.

While I was enamored with my meal, my friend's Vegetarian Mifen ($18) garnered a less enthusiastic response. It held its own aesthetically but was deemed unremarkable, possibly an issue for vegetarians given the limited choices and the dominance of red cabbage in the dish.

Service was generally commendable, with polite and attentive staff. A minor hiccup occurred when a glass with lipstick was served, but it was promptly replaced upon notification.

I'd return for another round of the Lu Fen without hesitation and recommend it wholeheartedly. My friend agrees on the return, albeit with a hope for a broader vegetarian selection. All in all, Hunan Slurp provided a quality dining experience.

I follow Kung Fu Kitchen @ Instagram. I wanted to eat here when I visit New York. I'm in NYC!  I was excited to eat here. The restaurant is easy to find. It's located near the E and C train line on 8th Avenue. I got off on 42th St Time Street and walked across the street. First of all, the food was good and fresh. I ordered three dishes. I ordered Shanghai pan fried pork buns, pork and shrimp won ton, and hand cut pork noodles. The portions of each dish were big and plentiful. All dishes were not greasy. I especially like the Shanghai fried pork buns. Yum!  The won tons were humongous. It took three bites to eat one. DeliI would have given more stars, however, the restaurant attached a 15% service charge. The service charge was calculated after the sale tax. The bill also had a portion where you can include additional service charge. I don't think this is right at all.
Love their Sushi! So filling and flavorful! The spicy mango is delicious. The bowls are very heavy so good to share!

Title: Cozy Vibes, but Pricing Outweighs Portion Sizes

My recent visit to the local eatery was a surprising mix of highs and lows. The ambiance struck a delightful chord, with a welcoming atmosphere that quickly put us at ease. Anticipating a 30-minute wait as a party of two, we were pleasantly ushered to our seats in a mere five minutes—a commendable efficiency that was much appreciated.

On to the cuisine, the taste did not disappoint; however, I found the pricing somewhat ambitious for the portion sizes offered. The quiche I ordered was rather dwarfed by the accompanying salad—it would have been more satisfying if these proportions were reversed. A note on the Eggs Benedict Florentine: lacking traditional sides such as toast, potatoes, or even a simple salad, the cost was hard to justify for what was on the plate.

The endless drip coffee from Brooklyn coffee roasters held promise, yet the allure faded when no refills materialized, turning the "endless" into a solitary $5 cup.

While there's a buzz surrounding the place that certainly speaks to its popularity, it wouldn't be my top choice for a dedicated food outing.

Bowery road has a nice, upscale vibe, and good food, but the service was definitely lacking. I got the pre fixe menu for dinner, which is $39 for a small plate, entree, and dessert. All the food was delicious and I feel like it was a really great deal for the quantity of food and quality of food. Highly recommend the crispy rice small plate. My main issue was the server was so slow. The people sitting next to us sat down 10 minutes after us, had a different waiter, and had their appetizers before we had even been asked to order. I felt like there were 30-45 minutes of sitting around waiting for him to take desserts, being refills, or getting his attention for the bill. I had the wrong menu (lunch is different than dinner) and couldn't get his attention for a new one in the first 10 minutes. Luckily my friends let me borrow theirs after selecting what they wanted. The food was good enough, I'll definitely give it another shot and hope my service was a one off.

Title: An Unforgettable Italian Feast

One word to describe our first meal of the trip: wow. The pasta at this cozy New York gem is nothing short of divine—one of the best I've ever savored. Insist on adding ricotta to your rigatoni; it transforms the dish into a creamy delight, perfectly tempering the heat from the oven's embrace.

Don't miss out on their champagne-infused concoctions, which add a sparkling touch to the meal. Despite the expected compactness of a New York eatery, the place exudes warmth and the aroma of Italian heaven.

For an authentic Italian experience that will beckon you back, this restaurant earns a resounding 10/10 recommendation. Trust me; you'll be planning your next visit before you've even left.

Title: An Unforgettable Culinary Experience

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a restaurant that offered one of the most memorable meals in recent memory. The setting was decidedly minimalist, providing a serene backdrop for the culinary delights that awaited.

To drink, I sipped on a light, uniquely flavored beverage that set the tone for the extraordinary meal to come. Standout dishes that are an absolute must-try include the beef tartare, which was both incredibly tender and bursting with flavor.

Another highlight was the perfectly prepared galbi. The steak-cut slices of beef were done to medium-rare perfection and topped with crispy chips, creating a symphony of textures.

But it was the fried chicken that truly stole the show. The breading was thin, airy, and surprisingly light — a masterful take on a classic. I highly recommend combining the peanut and gochujang sauces for dipping. The fusion of flavors is simply ingenious.

Dessert was no less impressive. The budino, accompanied by pine honey and delightful crumbles, was the epitome of indulgence — light, airy, and irresistibly creamy.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a gem that beckons with its sublime offerings and thoughtful presentation. A visit here promises a dining experience that you won't soon forget.

I recently had a fantastic dining experience at this superb ramen spot. The standout for me was the tonkotsu pork ramen from their traditional menu, especially appreciated for its low sodium option. It was hearty and the noodles were spot-on in terms of texture. I started with the fried chicken karrage and was pleasantly surprised by the generous portion and exceptional taste. The fried green beans were another hit, coated in a delicious fire sesame-based sauce. A cold beer was the perfect accompaniment to the meal. Quick, friendly service ensured I’d definitely be returning to this gem of a restaurant. Highly recommended for a great experience!

Probably the best hotpot in Manhattan Chinatown. Great interior design, lots of seating, great service. The quality of the produce is excellent too, free dessert station where the sauces are. The spicy Mala hotpot is my favorite, and load up on the fish balls and veggies. Will come back here at least once a year.

I recently tried the sushi burrito at this place and it was nothing short of INCREDIBLE – it's fair to say I'm now obsessed. The tuna filling edged out the salmon for me, although that might just be a matter of personal taste. The only hiccup was the almond bubble tea, which didn't quite hit the mark. Despite that, I'll definitely be back for more of those sushi burritos!

Have been here a few times.  The couscous dish is amazing - I get it with salmon and the salmon is always well prepared.  Couscous comes with a variety of vegetables and a small portion of a sweet raisin stew type thing that I love.  The other dishes don't amaze me.  I'm not a big fan of the hummus or labne.  The pita is decent but also not amazing.  The chicken bastilla was a bit too sweet and not special.  I know the dish is supposed to be sweet, but My husband prepares this dish much much better.  Fast service.  Great option for the neighborhood, but stick with the couscous.

Title: A Mixed Bag at NYC's BBQ Joint

Upon visiting this NYC BBQ spot, my expectations were not sky-high, given the city's limited BBQ scene. While the experience wasn't a total letdown, the meal left much to be desired. On the upside, the service was commendable; our server was the epitome of friendly and attentive, deserving a solid four-star rating despite a dessert delay he courteously communicated.

The culinary journey began promisingly enough with tangy, tender pork baby back ribs, and concluded with a delectable chocolate sheet cake that struck the perfect balance of moisture and sweetness. The Sweetwater IPA was a surprisingly pleasant refreshment for a non-IPA enthusiast like myself, while the sweet tea creatively infused with fresh mint and berries was a delightful concoction.

However, the meal hit a plateau with passable deviled eggs and a standard banana pudding, while the collard greens, although flavorful, seemed scant for their price—a slight sting mitigated by the inclusive gratuity policy.

The downhill slide commenced with the other meats; beef brisket, ribs, and a wing sampler suffered from an inexplicable dryness that made sawing off the meat a chore, overshadowing otherwise acceptable flavors. The pulled pork was mediocre and no match for homemade varieties. As for the sides, the skillet mac & cheese and biscuits were underwhelming, with the former being mushy and the latter too dense, both accompanied by unspectacular condiments. And the beignets? A total letdown—neither the taste nor the texture lived up to my recent delightful experience elsewhere.

In summary, while the service and a few dishes were highlights, the majority of the menu items, particularly the meats and sides, were unimpressive. Adjustments are needed to elevate this establishment to better reflect the potential of a true BBQ haven.

I recently dined at this restaurant and came away underwhelmed. The food quality was mediocre at best—the ribs were disappointingly small, reminiscent of an appetizer portion rather than an entrée. The shrimp lacked distinction, and the rice was notably bland. The service significantly detracted from the experience; our server appeared indifferent and disengaged from both his role and the patrons. Even the Long Island iced teas failed to impress, tasting more like a diluted mix of water and alcohol, although they did contain alcohol, which was the only silver lining. Overall, the experience was lackluster, and nothing stood out as particularly enjoyable.

We had a fun night at this cool Lower East Side restaurant.  I have to say up front that our waiter made the evening. Seth was bright, interesting and funny.  If you ever have the chance to meet him, get to know him.   He's also the sommelier and is very knowledgeable. The only real negative was the table and chairs.  The table was rustic and uneven. Someone was always on the verge of knocking over their glass.   The chairs didn't invite lingering.  Cocktails were pretty good.  The Martini sidecar was fun. We had a solid bottle of Sicilian red wine. The appetizers were excellent- the he. Of the woods mushroom was meaty with really interesting seasoning. It was very different from the equally delicious one served at Upland.  The crab gratin was really good.  I really liked my bacon cheeseburger.  The quality of the meat came through.  The duck fat fries were awesome.  The chicken Kiev was a hit.  The banana toffee pie was good.   We finished the meal with some excellent French press coffee.  Worth the schlep.

Brunch brunch brunch. Did I mention they have an amazing brunch? Came here with my gal pal to catch up. We had mimosas and both got the burger topped with egg. Aka the breakfast burger. That was very tasty. But oh my goodness the home fries were so well executed. Soft on the inside. Crispy on the outside. Flavored with that deep savory goodness. Really great! Cool decor inside with light up beer signs. The service was great as well. Will def be back for that great burger and home fries again!

A casual dinning Indian joint  - Got a chance to give this a try  . The food was good, we asked for spicy and they did not disappoint. The naan was so fluffy and fresh! We ordered Lahore kadai paneer, Mushroom kathi roll.  This was my 2nd time and the food has been pretty consistent! The quantity of the food is solid and the prices are reasonable as well. The staff were friendly and they offered quick service. The place is clean and right in the heart by Herald square .. Great place to grab a quick bite while around this area...  I would definitely visit the restaurant again next time.

As you can imagine, Jean-George can get expensive, but it's one of the finest restaurants and we really wanted to try it.  Thankfully our friend gave us a tip...  got at lunch, the menu is significantly cheaper than during dinner but quality and service is the same.  So that's what we did.  On our last visit to NY, celebrating both our birthdays, we decided to splurge a bit and finally make a reservation.  They take reservations online, a month in advance, and you have to move quick as they are very popular and get full quickly, especially for dinner.We got spot, on a Friday at noon, right when they opened.  We were greeted at the lobby, they checked our coats, and were shown to our table.  The restaurant itself is beautiful, classic, with lots of windows to let in natural light.  The service is superb.  Different staff members to bring bread service, water, food, and a sommelier for the wine pours.We went with the omnivorous menu.  It is a four course menu, with 2 options per course, and dessert.  We decided each get the different menu to be able to try everything and this was the best decision ever!  Each course is beautifully presented and explained as they come out.  They allow you plenty of time for you to take in every aspect of the dish (presentations, aroma, and flavors).The Yellowfin Tuna Ribbons was outstanding and a favorite for both of us.  We were left wanting more.  But the next course came and it was a creamy and flavorful crab risotto that equally took our breath away.  The roasted beef tenderloins was so tender and juicy, perfectly cooked.We opted to add the wine pairing and even thought they have some wines selected for each course, they did ask us what our preferences were so they could customize it for us.   They did such a great job, we ended ordering an extra glass of one they served us during the meal.To end, they have a piece of art for dessert.  A chocolate, passion fruit and peanut dessert.  Very colorful, full of flavors and fun presentation.  They also bring out a tray of mini desserts, with homemade marshmallows, and as they knew we were celebrating our birthdays, they also brought each of us a chocolate cake with a birthday white chocolate ribbon and a candle.  We could not have asked for a better experience.  They made our visit exceptionally special, and deserve more than 5 starts!

Title: A Delightful Thai Experience

I've always been a fan of Thai cuisine, and my recent visit to this charming restaurant only deepened my affection. The establishment offers a wonderful array of dishes that are sure to please both the palate and the pocketbook, making it a perfect choice for either lunch or dinner.
