For my entrée, I chose the drunken noodles with chicken – a personal favorite – and it didn't disappoint. The flavors were balanced and the noodles had just the right amount of spice. My wife enjoyed her pineapple fried rice with veggies and chicken, which was both flavorful and satisfying. The spring rolls we started with were the perfect appetizer, setting the stage for the delicious meal that followed.

With such excellent dishes and an inviting atmosphere, I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Title: A Gem for Ramen Lovers on the UES

Mei Jin Ramen on the Upper East Side is a delightful surprise, especially for those hunting for delicious ramen at wallet-friendly prices. The standout was their tuna tartare appetizer, packed with generous chunks of tuna and cleverly presented in a layered tower reminiscent of a compact NYC apartment, separated by crisp wafers. The level of spice was spot-on. For the main course, the spicy miso ramen did not disappoint - it came with a rich, tasty broth brimming with fresh ingredients, and the shredded pork was tender and flavorful. The final bill, even after tossing in beers, maintained its agreeability. Mei Jin is truly a great find for anyone craving a satisfying bowl of ramen without breaking the bank.

Lower East Side's newest Thai location and the second of its kind. I came here on a Friday afternoon to split some entrees with a friend. There was a good amount of people there. The ambiance was cute and modern--definitely a good date spot. Every dish I had here was amazing and very flavorful. The ribs were so tender that they came right off the bone. The pad see eiw was my personal favorite. The noodles were flavorful and the perfect texture, and the chicken was great. The sticky rice side was good and so was the rice entree. Solid Thai iced tea. The roti and curry were great as well. I don't think I had this good of Thai food in a long time. You can tell that they really care about their customers here, and the service was excellent. Everything came out quick and hot. I also found out that they have a great lunch special too. I left feeling full and happy. Oh, and dessert was great too.

After a long, red-eye flight from Phoenix, we were starving and anxious for a good meal.  Sacco Pizza had 4 stars on Yelp and was within walking distance so we thought we would give it a try.The restaurant is tiny, seating only 14 people at a time.  The three of us were fortunate to score one of the two 4-person tables.  We ordered a 16" pizza, half chicken/spinach and half sausage/pepperoni.  We had several menu questions which were answered abruptly and with a slight sense of annoyance.  After about a 20 minutes, we were delivered our pizza. We were famished and the savory flavors satisfied our hunger. The crust was thin, the cheese was gooey, and the marinara sauce was perfect. The three of us easily finished off the pizza.  We rate the pizza 4 out of 5 and the customer service 3 out of 5.  The cost for the pizza and three bottles of water was $23.75.

Brought my colleagues here-all are from out of town and never eat Japanese food. I just got back from a few weeks in Japan and I'm still craving it. Almost everyone had soba and enjoyed their meal. I had the duck udon...but I couldn't really find the duck. It seemed like there were a few pieces of pork, but not duck. If that was duck, there were like 3 little pieces. The sake however was delicious. Chosen by my Japanese friend. Overall, everyone enjoyed their meal. Had to flag the waitress over a few times for water and the bill.

I have been to this fine establishment a couple of times and I wanted to share it with my friends. We booked a table for Sunday to do Restaurant Week brunch but when I mentioned I may go off the regular menu I saw all of us participate to do RW but everyone agreed with me that it was fine. We ordered a few different items for all share;  longonissa side, 2 garlic rices, 2 sisigs, 2 bahn xeos and a chili pan mee. As usual, everything was beyond delicious. All the contrasts in the dishes really turn it into something special. One of my friends is not an adventurous eater so I was nervous what she would think and she loved it! We passed on dessert because we were very full. Always a great meal here! Hats off to you, Leah.

Title: "A Flavorful Find in Chelsea Market Despite the Chaos"

Review:

Navigating the bustling Chelsea Market, we stumbled upon a vibrant spot serving up tacos that are both kind to your palate and your wallet. Be prepared for long lines and a noisy backdrop, which, along with a somewhat perplexing ordering system, might initially dampen the spirits. Thankfully, local friends clued us in: order at the register, snag your drinks and any starters, like the zesty chips and salsa we opted for, and then clutch your ticket tightly as you brave the counter for the main event.

Although the flurry of activity can be overwhelming, don't hesitate to weave through the crowd to submit your ticket. Our feast included an array of tacos and a hearty steak quesadilla. The differentiation between each taco filled bite was subtle, but they were uniformly scrumptious. Next time, I'd consider skipping the guacamole to let the robust meat flavors take center stage, sprinkled merely with onion and cilantro for that classic touch.

It's a place where you learn to swiftly savor your taco to capture the symphony of flavors and textures in every mouthful. Despite any initial confusion, this experience is one that warrants a repeat visit. I'm definitely coming back for another round of those delectable bites.

Title: Overhyped and Underwhelming

My recent dining experience at this much-talked-about restaurant left me largely disappointed. Contrary to the glowing reviews, I found the food to be quite bland and the portions child-sized. The much-acclaimed MEW special roll was the sole highlight, living up to the hype with its tasteful combination of flavors. The takoyaki was passable, but not memorable.

On the upside, service efficiency was notable; our food arrived remarkably fast. However, this rapidity detracted from the meal, as it felt too hurried. The tacos were minuscule, laughably so when compared to a chopstick, and the miso ramen suffered from overcooked noodles, a lackluster broth, and an overdone egg.

While the frozen beer made for a great photo, it was disappointingly watered down and lacked taste. The kimchee creamy pasta tipped the scales towards indulgence but missed the authentic kimchi zest I was craving. It was a heavy dish that didn't justify its price or the hype surrounding the restaurant.

In summary, this spot may be good for a quick bite or a photo op, but it doesn’t deliver on flavor or value.

Came here with a few friends to grab a quick bite.  I really like how they focus just on Japanese curry too.  One of the things that drew me to this place was how you can customize your curry.  I ordered the shrimp and pork katsu curry but with the baked curry topped with corn and cheese.  PROS:- came out piping hot in a little small porcelain dutch oven: this was super cute by the way.- added cheese: created a nice extra savoriness and richness to the curry- meat and tempura shrimp was hot and crisp: no sogginess, freshly fried.CONS:- none.  Definitely great service, relatively cheap if you don't count all the extra add-ons.  I was super hungry so went for a big order.  Flavor was on point for Japanese curry.   One of the things that wasn't the greatest is that it's a very small seating area and not advisable for large parties - doesn't quite bode for good conversation if everyone is sitting in a row.  The food though is still quite delicious!

My girlfriends and I were looking for a place to have brunch after our 5K race at Bronx Community College a couple of weekends ago. Personally, I love this area of uptown. The food scene here is ever-changing and the variety has grown so much over the years.We were able to reserve a table and did so, just in case it got crowded. Luckily, since the race was over for us orettu early, reservations weren't really necessary and we beat the crowds.Thor was our server. He was very attentive and pleasant. He sat us at a cocktail table, gave us menus and waters. One gf ordered the Breakfast Quesadilla and my other gf and I both ordered Short Rib Benedicts. The food was great. We all enjoyed our meals. They have hot sauce which took everything to the next level. I took it upon myself to also order hubby their Tryon Red Eye Burger with Tryon Fries, which are covered in melty American cheese, bacon, scallion and ranch dressing (they put the dressing on the side). Hubby was overwhelmed. My son would have loved that order but for hubbs, he would have probably enjoyed something a little more understated. He had to eat it in two sittings. I have but one gripe with our experience and I'll explain that now. All of their brunch entrées come with a complimentary drink, either a mimos, bloody mary, coffee or tea or with the option of a 90-minute AYCD add-on. One girlfriend ordered a mimosa and my other girlfriend and I asked if we could get the Man-mosa instead, to which Thor said was fine. He never told us that we would have to pay full for the change in drinks. It wasn't until we were getting ready to leave and pay the bill that we noticed we were charged for our drinks which, I'm fine with but I would have liked to have known ahead of time, especially considering that we were also entitled to our complimentary drinks that we never got a chance to get. It's always best to be completely upfront with diners and ensure no miscommunication.

Terrific little place with delectable beyond burgers and many other vegetarian friendly creations, as well as very friendly staff. I really enjoyed the fried okra with dill sauce, it was unlike anything I've tasted before. The pickle lemonade was definitely weird but oddly refreshing too.

Title: A Gem with a Twist: Delightful Eats and Retro Ambiance

I recently visited a new gem that might just top my list of favorite dining spots. This place sets itself apart with an unmatched, enthusiastic greeting—I was warmly welcomed half a dozen times from the moment I stepped in!

Unlike its sister locations, the decor here throws you back to the 50s and 60s with its unique setup. The pièce de résistance was definitely the candy bar, an unexpected yet charming addition, though I didn't get to sample its sweet offerings.

Opting for something different, I veered away from the usual burgers and shakes and was pleasantly surprised by the Korean Spicy Chicken Wings. They were flavorful without setting my mouth ablaze, but I'll be honest, the accompanying sauce (reminiscent of mayo) wasn't to my taste.

The Black Tape Mule cocktail was a revelation—a must-try for dark liquor aficionados like myself, even with its hint of mint, which I usually shy away from. The chicken tenders also deserve a shout-out for their perfect crisp and flavor.

Service was top-notch, with servers offering great suggestions and interactions that made the experience all the more enjoyable.

In summary, this spot isn't just about the food—it's about the whole experience, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a restaurant with character, good food, and a friendly vibe.

Upon visiting the restaurant, I was immediately drawn to the vibrant ambiance crafted by Ashley Longshore. The space exudes a bright and energetic atmosphere that instantly puts a smile on your face. Although slightly hidden, prompting us to ask for directions, the entrance with stairs descending to the main area added a sense of discovery to the experience.

We started our meal with the triple dip spreads appetizer, which, unfortunately, didn't live up to our expectations and lacked the wow factor we had hoped for. Despite this, the restaurant's lively setting makes it an excellent choice for enjoying a drink or a quick snack.

In summary, while the appetizer may not have impressed us, the overall experience was elevated by the delightful and stimulating environment. It's certainly worth visiting for those looking to enjoy a convivial atmosphere and a casual meal.

I recently visited this local pizzeria and was impressed by their thin, crunchy crust pizza loaded with the perfect amount of cheese and a balanced touch of tomato sauce. Each slice was generous in size, providing good value despite a slightly higher price point, which seems to be the trend across NYC these days. Overall, the pizza was delicious, and I'm already planning my next visit. Highly recommended for a satisfying slice!

Title: A Delightful Surprise at a Hidden Gem

I recently dined at this charming restaurant and it surpassed all expectations! Initially overwhelmed by the innovative menu, the server was exceptional, guiding me to mouthwatering selections. My culinary journey began with a refreshing lychee colada, followed by an exquisite fish ceviche and succulent veggie dumplings. The main courses stole the show; the salmon was perfection, and the lobster pasta, a symphony of flavors. Presentation was impeccable, each dish was a feast for the eyes and the palate. And the cherry on top? The service was top-notch, making the entire experience memorable. I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

Vegan Szechuan isn't a concept you see often, and I was delighted when I saw this place in East Village. While some of the food arguably is not "Szechuan," most of it tastes good, albeit a bit too oily. We ordered the Zha Jiang Noodles ($11), Dry Pepper Style Vegetables ($16), Honey Walnut Edamame Nugget ($10), and Mala Beyond Meatballs ($12). Although the dishes look small, they are incredibly filling, and I would've probably ordered 1 or 2 fewer had I known how full I would be at the end. Everything comes out super quickly and all at once, so be ready to feast!Dry Pepper Style Vegetables (5/5) - This was my favorite dish and probably the closest that this restaurant gets to the Szechuan flavor. I could taste the peppercorns and liked the heat in this dish. Plus, the variety of vegetables made every bite a surprise. Mala Beyond Meatballs (4/5) - These were good! They were loaded with sauce and had good texture. Zha Jiang Noodles (3/5) - Noodles are always good, but I think the sauce could've used more oomph, either through salt or spice. Honey Walnut Nugget (2/5) - This is probably the dish I would've have ordered. The best thing about honey walnut shrimp is the crispy exterior and flavorful interior, of which this had neither. The edamame inside was a bit too mushy, and the outside wet.

Title: A Hop Haven with Room for Improvement

I recently visited a renowned spot in the NY Craft Beer scene, and despite the bustling 2pm Friday crowd, the on-tap selection did not disappoint, boasting rare finds not seen on the West Coast. However, service was noticeably sluggish, attributed to being understaffed, which limited our tasting to just two beers. While the tantalizing food menu was tempting, witnessing the prolonged wait for a neighboring couple's appetizers prompted us to pass. Nonetheless, the visit was a delight for a beer aficionado, and I'm eager to return for a culinary experience to pair with the exceptional brews on my next New York trip.

Well worth the 2 hour wait. The food blew me away, especially the vegetarian dishes! Note that they cannot serve their meat noodle/pasta dishes vegetarian. They weren't able to give us the macaroni without clams so our vegetarian friends missed out. I only tried one drink and thought it was just ok even if it was served in a cool light up pouch.  All 5 stars:Edamame dumplings - get these even if you don't like edamame! They're little pockets of cheesy truffle goodness.Angry Sweet Potato - such a simple dish but done very well. We ordered seconds and thought of ordering more! Crispy sweet potato fries with a very spicy dipping sauce - not for the faint of heart.Truffle mac and cheese - one of the best macaronis I've had! You get a lot of truffle and it's very cheesy. You don't really taste the clams though. Popcorn chicken - crispy, sticky finger licking goodPlantain - cooked perfectly so it wasn't mushy or too hard. Very beautiful and tasty dish.4 stars:Steak - I loved the feta grits but the steak was a little under for me.Broccoli rabe - disclaimer: I'm not a fan of broccoli rabe so most people would probably go with 5 stars. The candied cashews and sauce were awesome thoughCauliflower - a bit underwhelming compared to the other dishes. The flavors were subtle and the cauliflower wasn't crisp the way I prefer.

What's there to say about this place! My first time to have tried their pizza while in NY and it was f-ing amazing! My gf and I went to one of their locations and there was a wait just right outside the door then minutes later it was wrapped around the building! The next night when we were in Time Square to meet some friends up we took them to try it and this time we bought a whole thing of pizza. There's a wait but DEFINITELY worth it! Recommend it to those who are traveling through NY, this is a must try if you enjoy pizza.

Title: A Culinary Gem that Keeps on Giving - Douska (Formerly Douzo)

Having been long overdue for a visit, I was delighted to discover that Douzo had evolved into Hi Douzo, and currently identifies as Douska. This establishment has consistently lived up to its 5-star reputation, and my experience solidifies why.

My partner and I arrived on a quiet Tuesday evening at 6:30 pm, just before the dinner rush. The service was immediate and nothing short of spectacular. Opting for a DIY approach, my boyfriend enjoyed the Temaki Platter, priced at $40. With a humorous misjudgment, he overfilled his hand rolls with rice, leading to an unexpected side order of rice. The platter shined with the inclusion of a delectable side of ceviche. Although the platter seemed shareable, he indulged solo, a stark contrast to the typically unsatisfying portions at omakase restaurants.

I chose the classic Douzo set for $35 and was blown away by the freshness of each roll. The negi toro and Hokkaido scallop were standouts. The chef's warmth and attentiveness enhanced the omakase experience, with a pleasant surprise of a complimentary salmon roll, an unanticipated addition to my set.

Our total bill, with tax and tip included, was just shy of $100 for an unforgettable evening for two. Douska strikes a perfect balance between the upscale allure of omakase and a relaxed, casual ambiance. It's a charming venue for a date, exuding both intimacy and a laid-back vibe.

Douska is a delightful dining experience I eagerly anticipate revisiting.

Title: Style Over Substance at an Overpriced Eatery

Rating: ★★½

My recent dining experience at this locale left me with a less-than-satisfied appetite and a lighter wallet. If you're in search of premium Instagram content rather than exceptional Chinese cuisine, this might be your spot. However, those looking for authentic flavors should steer clear.

The boneless pig trotter, a dish traditionally rich with peppercorn and spices, landed on our table as a rather typical stew. The zha Jiang noodles sorely missed the mark—lacking the robustness expected from such a classic, and the substitution of ramen for the traditional hand-pulled noodles was a major culinary misstep.

As for the stir-fried vegetables curry, it was reminiscent of the all-too-familiar Chinese takeout fare, without any distinguishing features. The attempt at innovation was clear in the black truffle xiao long bao, which were passable, yet the truffle felt like a contrived effort to differentiate rather than a true enhancement of flavor.

While the establishment nails presentation, with aesthetically pleasing plating set against a chic ambiance, it falls short where it truly counts—the food. Overpriced and underwhelming, my advice is to give the stir-fried veggies a miss and perhaps opt for your local takeout instead.

If you live in Manhattan you've likely ether passed by or been to one of The Smiths. The large menu is the same along with the decor and like the other locations volume is always loud, busy and especially at the east village location crowd is 35 years old or younger for the most part. To me a 4/5 means I'll come back and I would here.

This place is quite an experience. We did the 18 course omakase for 185 dollars. Every bite was pretty amazing. The sushi's are more fusion like and very fancy looking. They are more decorated like French cuisine with carviar, foie gras, and squid ink foam etc. The vibe was very good and romantic by the sushi bar. Great sake selection as well. Although I like more traditional sushi's without too much decorations, this place is very tasty and different than other sushi places in the city.

In the area & our previous plans didn't work out we looked to see what was available & came across this place. we were seated but were limited with the time because the tables were initially reserved, we took the seats since we were hungry. Once seated we started we some white wine, Pinot Gregio hard to go wrong. they start u off with some bread, decent bread good with the olive oil, the bread sticks were great.  we ended up choosing options from the specials we had the Burrata & Zucchini flowers. since we were sharing they split the dish for us, the Burrata was very good nice tasting & very fresh. the Zucchini flowers were delicious aside from it being a small dish they only give you 2, it was very tasty. Main dishes we tried the Truffle pasta also off the night specials , very good pasta nice truffle taste. Small location, simple decor service was good .. even though we had limited timing it didn't feel like they were rushing us which is always a plus no one likes to be rushed.  Good service, pricey but not bad overall.

My friend suggested this place for a brunch meet up and I am so happy. It was an amazing ambiance and vibe. It's super cute and small, but doesn't feel small. Their brunch menu is amazing we each ordered two meals. The French toast was so good. My order was so amazing my friend sent his food back to get my order. Everything left me feeling happy. I would suggest walking in Central Park after, especially if you go during the summer.

Title: A Gnocchi Haven in the City

If gnocchi is your go-to comfort food, this quaint city gem is not to be missed. Contrary to what I initially thought, their menu might be exclusively pasta-focused, but it's a pasta lover's dream. The ambiance diverges from the typical Italian eatery; it's a cozier setting with brighter lighting, fostering a casual yet inviting vibe.

Their gnocchi selection is a delightful surprise, offering classics along with spinach and intriguing purple potato options, with the choice to add savory mushroom or cheese fillings. I indulged in the spinach gnocchi topped with a classic pomodoro sauce and was met with a dish where the zest of basil perfectly complimented the expertly prepared gnocchi.

For the indecisive, the gnocchi trio is a steal at $32, providing a generous sampling of sauces that's perfect for sharing. Amongst our table, the pesto genovese emerged as the star, boasting a richness that had us all enamored. I'm already eyeing their truffle sauce for my next visit.

Overall, the restaurant delivers on its reputation, skillfully balancing quantity with quality. Whether you're planning to devour your dish on the spot or take a portion home, you'll leave satisfied. Do yourself a favor and don't pass up on this spot.

Title: "A Seafood Lover's Haven with a Twist"

I stumbled upon a pretty cool restaurant that's a seafood enthusiast's dream, perfect for anyone with a penchant for shellfish. The charm of this eatery is its unique, hands-on dining experience - a rarity in the city, where you can indulge in the fun of cracking snow crab legs alongside friends. Although I'm not a seafood aficionado myself, the atmosphere made it enjoyable to partake in the messy delight with my companions.

As for my non-seafood choices, the sliders were decent, and the Mac and cheese had potential, though it was slightly marred by sticking to its foil container. A heads-up for prospective visitors: the establishment is cash-only, a detail we initially overlooked. Thankfully, we had enough cash to cover our meal. Despite the minor hiccups, this spot is definitely a must-visit for the seafood lovers out there.

Finding an affordable BBQ spot in Manhattan is a tall order, but Brother Jimmy's BBQ stands out as a wallet-friendly option with satisfying portions. Their platter is a particular highlight, offering a choice of protein and two sides, accompanied by cornbread and pickles. I went for the Northern Style Ribs, paired with Grilled Mac & Cheese and Hand Cut French Fries – a combination that hits the spot every time. The flavors are spot-on, and the value is undeniable. A must-visit for BBQ lovers on a budget.

Title: A Delightful Japanese Culinary Experience at an Upscale Eatery

My visit to this upscale Japanese restaurant was a feast for both the eyes and the palate. The high ceilings and spacious interior, complemented by large glass windows that flooded the space with natural light, set a serene ambiance perfect for a refined dining experience. Their tasteful wooden decor and the long grill counter where chefs prepare dishes in real time added a unique charm and interactive element for diners.

The restaurant week offered an exceptional value with a 3-course Prix Fixe dinner menu at $42 per person. I started with the seared tuna salad, which was a delightful beginning. The entrée included a delectable array of grilled salmon, duck and tsukune skewers, a roasted rice ball, and asparagus. Each meat skewer was juicy and tender, showcasing the chef's skill in preparation. The yuzu sorbet was a refreshing finale to the meal.

Additionally, I indulged in the Nigiri sushi assortment at $30, featuring an array of sushi including tuna, yellowtail, salmon, and more. The sushi's freshness shone through, with the vinegared rice providing a perfect tangy complement without overpowering the delicate flavors of the fish.

While the prices are above average for Japanese cuisine, the quality of the ingredients and the preparation justifies the cost. This restaurant is an excellent choice for anyone looking to treat themselves to a high-quality Japanese meal in a beautiful setting.

This place was really good. I was in the area and i looked up good food places to ate plus my friend likes tacos.  So to start i ordered a breaker burger medium and it came out perfect. The food was perfectly cooked. The breaker fries was amazing as well. The place was small but clean nice and need and the people was really cool. Definitely would go back again if I'm in the area.

Tucked in the heart of the East Village, this vibrant quick bite spot has mastered the art of fusion with its delectable paratha tacos. The flavor profiles are diverse and daring, offering something for every palate. Opt for tacos, a hearty burrito, or a satisfying rice bowl to enjoy their offerings. The tikka masala is a standout, rich and aromatic, while the shrimp is perfectly seasoned and cooked. This eatery is a must-visit for an inventive twist on classic flavors.

This was my first time at the 13th St location (I usually go to the UES) - Same great quality of food and service. I think this location may have been a bit more spacious. Anyways, I ordered a few dishes to share with my mom. We ordered the special appetizer of the day, lobster mac & cheese, the little neck mussels ($28) and famous Parmesan truffle fries ($12). We were so stuffed, and unfortunately left no room for the donuts dessert (a bit disappointing, but I saved a few couple hundred calories lol).I really liked the little neck mussels because it came with clams too - Both the clams and mussels were so fresh. The broth was light & a bit spicy, and the breadcrumbs give it a nice texture. I definitely recommend. I really love Flex - Definitely one of my go-to restaurants in NYC.

Came here with a friend because it was recommended on TastyThey have somehat of a good selection, but it's more geared towards people who like to eat vegan imitations of seafood and meat dishes. We ordered the Portobello Strips and the Stuffed Avocadoes to try out. The portobello strips came with 2 sides, and I ordered potatoes and broccoli.The flavor was okay - the Portobello strips had a flavorful sauce and the sides were pretty typical. The portion sizes were decent, but not enough if you're hungry.The interior was nice and dark, but there was no air conditioning. For a hot summer day, this was a bit of a letdown. Overall, the experience was okay. I wouldn't purposely come out here to have a meal, but if nearby, I would give it another chance in the future.

This restaurant is by no means cheap, but my friend was able to have a birthday party here for 20 people. Honestly, the food was really good. I had the fried calamari ($15). It was heckin delicious; I loved the chipotle aioli. My friend actually did eat all the peppers, so I guess it was somewhat worth the price for us? What strikes me as weird is when the snacks are pretty much as expensive as the entrees. I got the Mahi Mahi tacos ($18), which I didn't feel like was as worth as getting the Chicken Parm, Chicken Pot Pie, or the Burger ($16), which all simply looked more filling. I also tried my friends' House Made Burrata and the aforementioned Pot Pie. I never had squash as a burrata topping before, but it really works with the ricotta cheese and balsamic! The pot pie my friend found only okay, but I liked it. It was warm with a good balance of chicken, crust, and veggies.It's funny how the bathroom here does not reflect the price point and quality of the food; the sink was extremely rusty, and the restroom is so small that if you use the sink, you are almost preventing someone from coming out of the bathroom stall. Additionally, there was a singular hot water faucet and a singular cold water faucet, which depicts an oddly old fashioned setup. The 2 bathroom stalls are also kind of grimy looking, i.e. lots of space above and below the bathroom doors. Service-wise, I took no issue.

Good sandwiches, a little pricy for the size, but very good ingredients and a big selection of options. My favorite is The Godfather, with three meats, mozzarella, peppers, and greens (and balsamic...ugh the balsamic is to die for). It runs you $16.25, and it's not the most filling sandwich. As I said, a little pricy. But god it's good.They also have a wide selection of cheaper sandwiches in the $12-13 range as well as some pastas and sides. Their rainbow cookies are good and the garlic bread plate is *chef's kiss*, although also a little pricy at $5.50. They do meats and cheeses by the pound as well. The fresh Mozz is great and would be a nice treat if you wanted to make a caprese or something. The place itself is very small but they're friendly when I've gone to pick up food.The range of sandwiches (around 25 or so) reminds me of Pisillo's, which are bigger and cheaper but not as good. Classic trade off. All in all, it's a great spot and I'll definitely order again.

Amazing sushi. Will 100% be back. We got the sushi platter for 2. Every bite was eaten with delight. I normally don't like California rolls but this was the best one I've ever had. Was sooo fresh and delicious, all of the rolls were like pure sushi butter. Nice service, good sake as well. :)

Really good dim sum in the heart of Times Square! If dining solo just ask to bring them one at a time so the little dumplings stay piping hot! The staff is most accommodating. The jasmine tea is wonderful and made in a pot (not bagged) and the condiments are just divine.  A great pre-theatre spot!

Title: A Quick Bite with a Kick at Uncle Boon's Sister Eatery

As a frequent visitor to Uncle Boon's sister establishment, I ventured inside for the first time to experience their dine-in service. The space is small and clearly oriented towards takeout, yet cozy. Remember to bring plastic; it's a credit-only spot.

Ordering was a breeze; we were given a number and found a seat in the no-frills dining area where water is self-serve and diners are expected to clear their tables, adding to the casual vibe.

The Thai basil with beef short ribs was flavorful, but the surprise came with the papaya salad, which delivered a fiery punch despite the forewarning. While I relished the spice, it proved overwhelming for my companion, and might not cater to all palates.

Comparing this to the legendary Uncle Boon's, the food is commendable but doesn't quite hit the same culinary heights. Still, its swift service and avoidance of long waits make it a worthwhile alternative for a quicker, fiery dining experience.

If you find yourself in the area and in need of a quick, satisfying lunch option, look no further than this spot. The vodka slice is a must-try – a delectable choice that never disappoints. The service is fast, the prices are budget-friendly, and the clean environment makes for a pleasant dining experience. It's become my go-to lunch destination every Tuesday when I'm working nearby. Highly recommended!

Delicious fresh bread with pesto dipping sauce. I really enjoyed my Blue Point Winter Ale. My wife had the rośe and it was wonderful. The prosciutto di Parma pizza was excellente!! The crushed red pepper is muy caliente, so use sparingly at first.

Stopped by for a quick lunch on a cold Saturday- we got in pretty quick with 6 of us. Servers were ok and food came out quickly. Everyone liked there meals, we got soups, salads, eggs/bacon and grilled cheeses. No complaints- food was ok! Was pretty packed when we left as well.

Friendly and quick service! The place is very small so get there early or you will have to wait for a seat. Food was solid and very authentic. I absolutely love their Thai iced tea which had nice tea flavor and was not overly sweet. It was so good we ordered one to go. Ordered the calamari and shrimp herb salad, beef buns, pork and crab dry egg noodle and the beef noodle soup. The beef buns were solid and had really flavorful beef. The salad was a bit too spicy for me but the flavors were awesome and the seafood was cooked to perfection and very fresh. The beef noodle soup was pretty good with a really flavorful beef broth. Although the pork and crab egg noodle is their signature item I did not like it as much. The sauce was too sour for my taste and I really wanted something more savory. However, the egg noodles were excellent and loved the chewy texture. Overall this was a great meal and loved the different flavors that I usually cannot get at the typical Thai place. Will come back again!

My friend was looking for a ramen spot and this popped up so we decided to give it a shot. Small spot but has seating. The staff were SO helpful! They explained the different dishes for us, the different options we have for ordering, adding/substituting ingredients, spice levels etc... I had their little pot rice noodle but the vegetarian option. I loved that their menu had vegetarian sub in options. I went with medium spice and this bowl was packed with a tin of flavors! The serving is a good size, not too much and not too little. I'm not a big ramen person but I was so impressed with this bowl! We also tried their hometown street fries, spicy would be an understatement but it was so delicious! I'd suggest sharing this with someone because even between the two of us it was too much to handle. For drinks we tried their Mu-Ghai Shui. It's different but it paired well with the hot soup and spicy fries! It was a nice sweet, cool refreshing drink. I would definitely come back here, especially now that the weather is getting cooler!

Nestled in the bustling Chelsea Market, this gem of a spot offers a delightful culinary experience with great quality food at incredibly reasonable prices. Admittedly, the ambiance is vibrant to the point of being crowded and loud, and finding a seat can be a bit of a challenge, but that's part of the charm you'd expect in this popular hotspot.

A big draw is the complimentary tortilla chips accompanied by an abundant selection of sauces – a perfect appetizer to kick off your meal. The fish ceviche scores high with a 4.3 out of 5, boasting robust flavors and a satisfying portion that is sure to please. While the shrimp ceviche trails slightly at a 3.8 out of 5, it's still a tasty option, though the fish variant has the edge in my book. Whatever you choose, don't pass up the opportunity to enhance your dish with the zesty sauces provided – they're the secret to an extra flavorful experience.

During Restaurant Week, I decided to try out this fine dining spot located inside a hotel. The ambiance reflected its hotel setting with close-set tables and upholstered booths, attracting an older clientele. Despite the crowded layout, the staff excelled in service, providing an impressively efficient experience without making me feel rushed.

The meal kicked off with crispy fried ricotta balls followed by a satisfying pate de campagne with delightful pickled vegetables. The braised beef paleron main course was competent, yet unremarkable, though it partnered well with the creamy polenta. The real standout was the pistachio entremet dessert, a wonderful complement to the tangy raspberry sorbet.

Paired with my meal was a red wine from Château de la Colombière that was truly enjoyable. While I appreciated the experience and the impeccable service, the restaurant didn't entirely win me over as a favorite dining destination.

This was $6.50, cheap by NYC standards. My go to place when I feel skinny and am craving for pork. Since they are takeaway only, I usually end up at the park opposite, watching kids play basketball - best in spring and fall.

Once a favorite dining spot of mine, I'm disheartened to report that this establishment has lost its luster. The once-tantalizing chicken sandwich now arrives dry and uninvitingly cold. Their signature "manly fries" suffer a similar fate, being served limp, drenched in an excess of sauce, and accompanied by unappealing cold bacon. Preparation times are inexplicably lengthy considering the absence of a visible queue or pending orders. The sole redemption comes in the form of their truffle burger, which they manage to serve with consistent quality. My advice: Visit solely for the truffle burger experience, but for a satisfying chicken sandwich, you're better off at Fuku right next door.

Title: A Spicy Delight with Excellent Lunch Deals!

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this Indian restaurant and I must say, it was a delightful experience. Despite the bustling lunch rush, my family and I were efficiently greeted and seated within a mere ten minutes. The menu immediately caught our eye, offering a variety of tempting dishes, with a particular focus on those wonderful spicy flavors—a bold YES from us!

Lucky for us, we dropped by during lunch happy hour when the prices were astonishingly half off. We eagerly ordered a fish curry, chicken masala, among other savory items and topped it all off with a refreshing mango lassi. The service was swift as our meals arrived promptly, allowing us to relish our lunch for an extended and satisfying hour and a half.

Throughout our visit, the staff was nothing but friendly and attentive, making sure our dining experience was enjoyable. The food itself was not only tasty but also was served and cleaned up with impressive speed. If you're in the mood for an Indian feast that won't disappoint, especially during lunch hours, this is the spot for you. Highly recommended!

I had such a great experience here with my friend for girls night!! Our server/bartender Jay was so amazing and made sure that we were taken care of all night. He is as good as they come!We decided to get a few things to share. We ordered the Parmesan fries, spicy guacamole, and cheese plate. The fries were perfection and came with ketchup and two other dipping sauces. The green sauce was my favorite! It was the perfect amount of spice and I could have eaten that sauce on top of everything. The guac was equally as awesome, but the warm freshly made chips made it outstanding! The cheese plate was also great and had interesting cheeses and meats. My favorite was the brie with raspberry jam.The cocktails here are so interesting cause they are all tea infused! I had the Jasmine of Agrabah. I liked it, but it was a little sweet for me. I wish I had ordered it after my meal and had it as an after dinner drink. This has a really cute vibe and is great for date night, girls night, and everything in between! Try to get one of the window seats. It was fun to people watch and feel as if you are outside!

Came here with a few coworkers on a Friday night and had a great time. Reservations were made for the 7:30 show. You file in, get checked in then are seated. The is a $15 cover on Friday nights which is added on to your tab. There is also a minimum $15 food/drink minimum. You order your food and drinks from your waitress before the show starts. The shows is lively and lots of fun but doesn't last long as there is another show at 9:30 so you don't have the option to hang around at the table. Feel free to bring singles so that you can tip the ladies as the strut around the room. 20% gratuity is added to the check. It's a fun night out and would recommend it, I'll just say have a plan to do something after in case you after looking to hang out for a little longer than a hour and 45 minutes. This is a good way to start the night.

one of the few korean bbq places in NYC where you can make a reservation so that's a HUGE pluscame here with my co worker and ordered the galbi, spicy pork and the uni bibimbap. the unibibimbap is a good portion for 1 person but a little on the smaller side for 2 people. could have used a little bit more rice since it was a on the salty side but plenty of uni flavors to make me happythe galbi and spicy pork portions are smaller than i'm used to in philly but it was tasty! the banchans were also pretty average.customer service was great though, our service was very attentive and nice!all in all, i give this place a 3.5/5

Came here to Coopers a.k.a Coopers-Chelsea as it is one of two locations ahead of going to party where only drinks would be available and no food and this place had no problem satisfying in with food offerings as well as a selection of craft beers. I started with some of the $3 sliders which really hit the spot. Definitely recommend particularly Saturday as this is the daily special for them. I also got the Spicy pork tacos which also get a thumbs up from me, but have had better tacos from more dedicated Mexi restaurants, but I've also had worse so Cooper's still wins there. The Crispy Brussel sprouts were also great which after 3 types of food here tells me they've got that on lock.I had a craft beer that was pretty good, can't remember the name but it was #22 on the list for those curious enough and if isn't switched out. The beer selection sounded good so I'd be willing to try more and would totally recommend coming here for food and drinks. Chill atmosphere and good service.

We came here around 6pm just before the dinner rush hour.  They have a variety of sashimi donburi (rice bowls) to choose from and they were mostly from $20-30 which is reasonable. You can choose from sets or customize your own for additional prices depending on what you choose.  The food came fast, less than 5 minutes after placing our order so that was nice since we were in a rush. Fish was fresh and portions were generous and came with miso soup.I saw a lot of people come in and eat by themselves but they sat at the bar so it's great for groups or solo diners.  I'll be back!

I had never heard of this place until last night but my friend booked it for a birthday dinner for a dear friend. It was located in a part of town I don't frequent as much and tucked away in what I think was a hotel. Very nixe decor inside with lots of cool art.Service was great. We ordered many different oysters, scallops, Mac and cheese and salad.Tried the Lancaster chicken and Burger which I had and they were both amazing. So many food desserts we went with the pear pie and it was super tasty.Great place to go for a special occasion, date and a great meal.

Title: Satisfying Sushi at Amber

Amber restaurants have become a reliable spot for my sushi cravings. The quality of their sushi remains consistently high, coupled with prices that won't break the bank. On my recent visit, I sampled the spicy tuna pancake which proved to be a delightful appetizer. For my main course, the salmon tuna rollover and the tuna gaga rolls did not disappoint, both packing a flavorful punch.

The service was prompt, likely aided by the fact that the restaurant wasn't crowded at the time. While Amber might not be the place for a unique dining experience, it's definitely a solid choice for tasty sushi in a comfortable setting.

Entering the restaurant, one is immediately struck by the breathtaking interior that exudes an almost palatial elegance. The dining experience is consistently delightful, with each dish bursting with freshness and flavor. The standout appetizer wrapped in beetle leaves is particularly noteworthy – a real treat for the palate. Service rounds out the high-quality experience, being nothing short of impeccable. This establishment is a must-visit for those seeking culinary excellence in a regal setting.

Title: Happy Hour Delight at a Cozy Spot

I recently visited a charming little restaurant that excels during its happy hour, offering both delightful food options and enticing drinks. With a selection of Japanese beer and sake, the happy hour sets the stage for a tasting journey through their menu.

The oysters caught my eye, and at $1.50 each, the blue point oysters were a steal – large, succulent, and flavorsome, not far off from the previous $1 price tag, a fair adjustment for the locality. The array of appetizers was a tasty prelude to the main course: crispy fried chicken wings, flavor-packed karage, and the standout fried shrimp, all a perfect match for the drinks on offer. The shrimp shumai was pleasant enough for those with a fondness for these dumplings.

Our shared steak entree was generously sized and came with a sashimi appetizer, which was decent, though it couldn't quite eclipse the joy of the starters. Overall, it's an inviting venue for an unhurried dinner where conversation can flow as easily as the drinks. Highly recommended for those seeking a relaxed dining experience with quality happy hour offerings.

Title: A Disappointing Experience with Bombay Delivery

My quest for a good Indian meal led me to try Bombay Delivery's special, and unfortunately, it ended in disappointment. For $23.41, inclusive of tax and tip, I received a meal that didn't live up to its price tag.

The highlight was the garlic naan, which was flavorful with fresh garlic and herbs. However, the quantity and quality of the entrees fell short. The chicken tikka had just two small pieces with mediocre taste. The chicken curry was a letdown, with rubbery chicken and a lackluster sauce.

Additionally, the delivery was tardy, and the packaging mishap left a saucy mess upon arrival. Any attempt to discuss these issues was met with unprofessionalism from the owner, which only added salt to the wound. 

Regrettably, I won't be ordering from here again. I advise others to seek their Indian cuisine fix elsewhere, where the food and service might measure up to the expectations.

Title: A Satisfying, Yet Unremarkable, Culinary Adventure

If there were an option to award half stars, this establishment would find itself sitting comfortably at 3.5 for its commendable pricing structure and quality fish offerings, despite the absence of a stand-out dish. The restaurant presents an appealing three-tier pricing system, with the teisui tier being particularly filling at 16 pieces for $85, while the regular tier, priced at $60, is noted for its value.

The ambiance is inviting, enhanced by a delectable happy hour lasting until 7 pm, and a noticeably pleasant aroma gracing the bathroom—an odd but appreciated detail. The staff's friendliness is an undeniable plus, contributing to the overall positive experience.

However, not all that glitters is gold. Interaction with the chefs is limited, and they appear rather engrossed in their craft, somewhat diminishing the unique sushi counter experience. The soy marinade brushed atop the sushi was mildly seasoned and lacked depth. Though the assortment of fish—including needlefish, scallop, and ootoro—was impressive, no piece left a lasting impression. The rice suffered from overcooking and was served in larger-than-preferred portions. Additionally, the wagyu slice fell short, being excessively thin.

A creative attempt at diversifying the menu with an uni risotto did catch the eye but failed to impress upon tasting, serving more as a filler than a flavorful component.

In conclusion, while the restaurant exudes a great atmosphere conducive to a pleasurable outing, the culinary experience was underwhelming. The dishes were satisfactory but plain, and despite the value, it may not be enough to warrant a return visit.

Title: Satisfactory Thai Cuisine with Stellar Dessert

My recent visit to a local Thai eatery was enjoyable, albeit not exceptional. The service started off on a slower note, with a noticeable wait before our orders were taken. The menu offerings didn't stray far from the classic Thai selections one might expect.

A standout from the appetizers was the salad with octopus, which I found quite delightful. As for the main course, I chose a noodle dish that proved satisfactorily tasty, accompanied by a standard serving size that didn't disappoint.

However, the highlight of the meal was unequivocally the dessert. It was a remarkable note to end on and left a lasting impression. Coupled with the reasonable pricing across the board, this restaurant presents a decent choice for those in the mood for Thai cuisine, especially if you stick around for the sweet finale.

Title: A Heavenly Slurp at an Unusual Location

Last Thursday night, my sister and I decided to explore a much-talked-about ramen joint nestled in the Wyndham hotel - an unexpected spot for a culinary ramen retreat. Our anticipation was met with sheer delight as the dishes graced our table. 

While my sister savored the famous bone marrow gyukotsu ramen, replete with tender brisket and an impressively sized marrow bone, I indulged in the smoked duck ramen, a dish that not only tantalized my palate but also captivated my senses with its theatrical smoke-enshrouded presentation under a glass dome.

The smoked duck delivered on its promise with every smoky bite, and the inclusion of crisp lotus root, fresh bok choy, and hearty carrots provided a nutritious balance to the indulgence. 

Efficient and cordial service added to the restaurant’s charm, ensuring our dining experience was as seamless as it was enjoyable. With an enticing happy hour offering until 7 PM and the bonus of complimentary edamame through a Yelp check-in, I’m already planning my next visit to sample more from their inventive ramen lineup. A slurp-worthy experience indeed!

I recently stopped by Boqueria during happy hour and it turned out to be a delightful experience. The sangria was the perfect kickoff to a delicious meal, wonderfully concocted and refreshing. For my main course, I chose the cojunudo and montado de bistec. Both dishes were savory and satisfying, but the hanger steak stood out exceptionally. It was tender and cooked to perfection - a noteworthy feat considering this cut of meat can be tough. The combination of aioli and shishito peppers added an excellent flair to the dish. Regrettably, I didn't have the space to sample the patatas bravas, but that just gives me a perfect reason to return.

I've been a regular at this local hotpot spot, which has become quite the destination for my friends and me. One of the biggest draws is their birthday offer—dine for free if your birthday is on or near your visit. Moreover, if you prefer to pay with cash, you're in for a treat with a nice discount.

On our last visit, we had a party of 10, and while the ambiance is cozy, the seating arrangement was a bit of a squeeze as we were allocated a table for 8. It's a good idea to work out your seating plan beforehand, especially since the hotpot stations are a bit cramped, with six individual pots and a larger communal one.

The highlight, undoubtedly, is the all-you-can-eat option, capping at two hours. It's a feast that's not only generous but also a challenge to see how much you can indulge in the given time. Despite the tight seating, the experience remains a favorite, especially for those celebratory birthday gatherings.

Tip: Request a table by the far right windows as that offers the best views of Central Park (see photo, stunning especially during fall colors). They never guarantee such seating upon reservation but they will make an effort if you note you would prefer such seating. Their weekend brunch is a $64 pre fixe menu. Wish they had a couple more options but I chose the tuna tartar and the kimchi chicken and waffle dishes (photos included). I will say for a restaurant within the Mandarin Oriental, I was expecting more "fluff" than substantial content but both dishes were quite good. The kimchi chicken and waffle portion was surprisingly large.While we were eating our desserts, staff began taking down tables and chairs all around us which was a bit jarring. Apparently they had a private party to prepare for. They appropriately offered to seat us in the Aviary (their cocktail lounge) and gave us some coconut chocolate truffles to apologize for the inconvenience. Appreciated their proactive attitude. The food is worth it but I wouldn't pay the cocktail prices. It is definitely a lovely atmosphere and unique view of Central Park.

Yummmm! As a vegetarian, I love that GLUR offers  vegetarian/vegan options easily in their menu. I'm so grateful I don't have to stress out about too much fish sauce upsetting my stomach or feeling like I've betrayed my morals (oh the guilt...). I came with a meat-lover and we both  thoroughly enjoyed our meals. Prices are reasonable, service is quick, and the staff is kind. Will be back!!

Recently, I dined with friends at a charming restaurant where we sampled the Torcia and Cappelletti, both priced at $25. The squid ink pasta in the Torcia was cooked to perfection, complemented by a tasty shrimp ragu. Still, I found myself longing for a bolder seafood flavor that I felt was masked by the strength of the ragu. The Cappelletti, on the other hand, was an explosion of truffle and ricotta - a truly delectable experience, though slightly marred by the smaller-than-expected portion size for its cost.

The ambiance struck an inviting balance of homeliness and elegance, making it ideal for both romantic dates and celebratory family dinners. An added bonus was the hospitable service; despite arriving 20 minutes late for our reservation, we were graciously accommodated, a gesture that did not go unnoticed.

Had my review been based solely on the food, I might have leaned towards a 3.5 rating. However, the exceptional service has earned them a well-deserved 4 out of 5.

The flame to my Red Flame. Great selection of meals to choose from.  Very fast and friendly service and the food was DELICIOUS!!Portions are perfect size and everyone's meal looked delicious.  I kept looking around saying I should have ordered that .... LOL

College clubs ruined most cheap pizza for me. I got so tired of it. I rarely eat pizza and when I do, it has to be interesting or meaty. There's just something about a slice of Joe's cheese pizza that's exceptional to my personal rule. I will envy this pizza culture - fast, cheap, tasty, and by the slice, from my home in Chicago.

Food(2/5)-stopped by dinner with a friend. I've been this place since 2012 and this place wasn't my favorite but my friend wanted go this place. We ordered marinated chicken, spicy pork, prime rib eye, bibim naengmyeon. I am a Korean and I really am picky about food also I am a foodie. I've eaten korean bbq a lot and this place bbq was nothing special to me, not the best in the area too. Prime rib eye was ok, if you're this place with kids, order marinated chicken for them. It's perfect dish for kids, not for me. It was sweet and sauce tasted like bulgogi. I prefer spicy marinated chicken but they didn't have it on their menu. Spicy pork was ok but also it's sweet to me. My friend enjoyed spicy pork and marinated chicken. When I ordered Bibim naengmyeon, I requested them to after bbq. But they gave me bibim naengmyeon when I eat prime rib eye(it was first our bbq). I had to returned that and they gave me when I finished eat our bbq. Noodle wasn't fully cooked and I had no idea how bad sauce tasted. It just like only eating red pepper paste. I couldn't eat because noodle wasn't cooked, too hard for chew. We didn't finished our bibim naengmyeon and my friend told me instant bibim naengmyeon was better than this place. Service(5/5)- our waitress was accommodating and she was super duper sweet. Only problem was she was busy and slow served. I didn't mind cooked our bbq myself if they let me did that. My friend also kept telling me about she really nice person and I never seen like sweetest waitress in NY. Ambience(3/5)- This place just one of normal korean restaurant in Korean town. Nothing special and you have to share your table with other people specially at dinner time. Floors were slippery from bbq. Please be careful when you walk.

This place has been on my bookmarked list for awhile now so when an opportunity came for me to choose the place for a Christmas get-together a friends, I decided to go for it on the 27th. Turned out to be the best decision.For starters, I love the overall interior design and the ambiance of the place. The soft lighting gave off that really cozy vibe for Christmas. We were immediately led to our table by the second floor and staff immediately attended to us but didn't rush us too which was really appreciated.The drinks were good. I'm normally a wine person but made an exception that night to try out their cocktails. El Guapo caught my attention, a spicy margarita which was delicious and had the right balance. Ended up having 2 drinks. For my entree, we all decided to splurge a bit and ordered the 12oz  boneless New York Strip steak and it was the perfect medium rare, loved their au poivre sauce too. It came with onion rings, not a big fan so my friends happily enjoyed it. We ended up hanging out longer and enjoyed all the friendship talk so we decided to order coffee (really really bland though, low point of the night) and shared some mini donuts for dessert (chocolate and vanilla), which was just okay.We really liked the place and could see myself coming back for date night and more meals with friends. We also decided to take a look at the piano bar below but to be required another $25 for entry when we've already spent too much upstairs wasn't really appealing to us. Maybe we'll have the opportunity to check it again one day. :)

During Restaurant Week, I visited an above-average steakhouse in NYC where I embarked on their $42 special for an appetizer, entrée, and dessert. The split pea soup was the highlight, creamy and robust in flavor. For my main dish, the surf and turf was decent, with the lobster outshining the rest. The chocolate cake concluded the meal on a sweet note, yet none of the dishes left a lasting impression.

While the food was certainly good value for the price, the experience was tarnished by lackluster service. The inattentiveness of the staff was notable; I found myself repeatedly requesting water refills and even had to resort to serving myself on one occasion. Additionally, the need to ask for clean cutlery due to dirty utensils was a disappointing oversight. While the meal itself was satisfactory, the service fell short of expectations.

Title: A Tampopo Transformation: A Ramen Revelation!

My culinary adventure at Tampopo has converted me into a Japanese cuisine enthusiast! This was my first indulgence in gourmet ramen, and Tampopo's offerings have ensured it won't be my last.

Upon arrival, I decided to place my dining experience in the hands of our knowledgeable server. Starting with a refreshingly different Nigori sake, served in a shot glass cradled by a traditional wooden box, it packed a delightful punch that hinted at the quality of the meal to come.

The appetizers were a tastebud symphony: the steamed bao buns were pillowy perfection, and the kaarage fried chicken was a crispy, flavorful delight. Moving on to the main course, the recommended spicy miso ramen was a bowl of soul-warming comfort that wasn’t as spicy as its name might suggest, allowing me to savor every spoonful without hesitation.

The attentive, friendly, and informative service only elevated the dining experience. In short, Tampopo is a hidden treasure in the realm of Japanese gastronomy. Miss out on this gem, and you're truly missing out on a culinary delight. I can't wait for my next visit!

Came here with a group for some sushi on a Saturday night. We were able to get a reservation a couple days in advance. We sat at the sushi bar and ordered the pado tasting. The sushi comes out one piece at a time, omakase style. Everything was fresh and delicious! The pado tasting comes with 10 pieces of nigiri and one hand roll. All that for $45 - such a great value. We also added a supplement that included 3 additional pieces for $30. There were multiple supplements to choose from. Overall this was a great experience and we would definitely return!

This is a good option when you're on the go on the UES or would like a quick bite. I think it's fast casual and there's a few tables for seating. I ordered the Gorgon with carnitas and it was $11.43. I enjoyed the ingredients which I felt were very fresh! The pork meat was very juicy and tender. The fried dough texture of the Gorgon was quite unique. However, as I ate it further, I felt like it was too salty and somehow too oily slightly. Mainly though, I think the portion size was much too small to be $11.43. It should have been $6-$7 at most. It's clearly not as large and with fewer ingredients than the average burrito (which they do not sell). They have a $9 taco bowl option which may be more filling as it comes with beans and rice (unlike the Gorgon which I ordered). Other items seem overpriced as well. For example, a horchata is $6.

New level of hot pot. All food ordered was fresh and tasty. It felt like I became a chinese emperor. So niceThey provide a basket that you can store your coat in so that you don't walk around smell like hot pot after the meal. A bit on the pricier side but it's all worth it. Just try it!!

Great place to relax and have a meal or just a drink. The food was excellent, I ate here upon my arrival and the buffet was surprisingly very good. The salads, of all things, were stellar. Cocktails tasted delicious. Views were stunning.

Um.. what?  I ordered a Sandwich De Puerco Asado via mealpal on a Tuesday afternoon and I seriously did not get what was advertised/ pictured.  It's described as a "Latin Hero with Roasted Pork Mixed with Tropical Guava and Tropical Cheese served with Fries and Greens".  What I received was a hero roll with pulled roasted pork in the amount of a slice of deli ham with no cheese in it nor was it press-grilled, a few pieces of frisee, steak fries, and a container of sauce on the side.  No ketchup, and bar napkins.

Title: A Slice of NYC Heaven at NY Pizza Suprema

Nestled conveniently across from MSG and Penn Station, NY Pizza Suprema is a gem for anyone craving an authentic New York slice. With a selection of around 15 varieties, there's a flavor for every palate. My family and I opted for an assortment, including their signature Suprema, zesty buffalo, and a classic plain slice. The generous size of each slice means you get your money's worth at $5.50 apiece.

The consensus? Excellent. The Suprema slice was particularly outstanding, while the buffalo had a kick that didn't disappoint. Even the plain slice had a certain je ne sais quoi that left us all impressed. NY Pizza Suprema clearly earns its title as the best mid-town pizza spot. It was the perfect capstone to our NYC visit.

So happy my friend organized a dinner here for the holidays! I've always wanted to try Han Dynasty. He reserved a lazy susan table in the back of the restaurant for the 9 of us to try the family style tasting, which came with 12+ courses ($40+ per person excluding drinks, but the tasting came with a bottle of champagne). Every dish that came out was flavorful, spicy, and perfectly cooked. Some dishes that we had were dan dan noodles, cumin style lamb, spicy chicken wings, fried shrimp, an octopus dish, fried green beans, chicken in black bean sauce, and a spicy fish fillet dish. There's more, but I lost track in between wiping my tears/sweat and devouring everything. The table was never empty and our server was friendly and attentive. Our group had dietary restrictions and staff had no problem adjusting dishes to accommodate us. I would definitely go back again with a big group of friends again. Check this spot out if you love good food and amazing service!

I recently had the pleasure of sampling a chocolate croissant from this charming spot, and it was nothing short of the best I've ever experienced. The chocolate-filled pastry didn't disappoint either; it was delightful. The coffee impressed as well, boasting a smooth and creamy taste that perfectly complemented the sweet treats. Without a doubt, this place is on my list for a return visit whenever I'm back in the area.

The food here was good and service was ehhh. My boyfriend and I came here to get the lunch special. We got a salad and a pasta dish for less than $19.00 which was a pretty good deal. We got the pear and blue cheese salad. It was a tad bitter, but tasted good with the creamy blue cheese and sweet pears. We didn't eat all of it because it wasn't the greatest salad. We also got the pasta. The pasta was really tasty, but way too salty. As we got to the bottom of the dish, the more salty the pasta became. Although, the pasta was cooked perfectly and seasoned really well. The decor of the place is nice and they have a nice bar to enjoy drinks at. However, the service is just okay. Not the most friendly vibe. All in all, I'm glad I tried it but would not go back again.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Cozy Spot

I revisited this charming restaurant with high hopes, but my culinary experience mirrored my initial visit. The ambiance remains delightful – it truly is a pleasure to sit and soak in the comfortable atmosphere. However, the food continues to be a letdown. This time, I opted for almond flour pancakes, which, to my disappointment, were exceptionally dry, nearly to the point of being inedible. I was tempted to send them back. On a brighter note, the truffle chicken nuggets had a promising flavor, but the appearance of the chicken inside was off-putting, which dampened the overall enjoyment. Despite my critiques of the menu offerings, the allure of the dining environment is enough to entice me for another visit, though I'll be steering clear of the pancakes in the future.

Title: Quaint Diner Fare with a Side of Patience

Tucked away on the Upper East Side, this classic diner offers a satisfactory retreat for those seeking a straightforward breakfast without the frills of an extravagant brunch. Their take on the Lox Benedict is decent, though it doesn't quite hit the mark of culinary excellence. Patrons should be warned: prepare for a wait if you venture in during the weekend rush. Overall, a fair spot for easing into your day after a late night.

Some of the best ramen I have had and in one of the coolest, most authentic feeling environments.  The whole idea of sitting alone at an individual booth, eating ramen, made me feel like I had been transported half way across the world to the streets of Japan.  It was a very cool experience where you ordered your meal off of a sheet of paper and it was brought to you through a small window at your booth, limiting the entirety of your human interaction to the attendant at the front of the restaurant who seats you.  In America and especially the crowded NYC, this is a rare, but welcomed experience.The ramen and pork based broth were also great and they had options to add varying levels of spice, as well as additional things to the ramen.  I also had the matcha beer which was interesting, but flavorful, and is something i would recommend to those who haven't  tried it before.

Ehh I feel like this place could be better. But maybe my expectations were too high. I was walking past this location while visiting the city and we decided to stop in. It's all day happy hour on the weekends which is nice! We ordered the chicken mini tacos, they were out of the beef. The flavoring was good but mini they are. The Guac was good. They also have fish tacos but I didn't get to try them. I ordered a pineapple mojito that also had turmeric. It was very sweet, I thought the turmeric balance it out but it didn't. I want to try this place again before I write it off.

Went for brunch when playing soccer nearby.Honestly can't understand why this place has 4 stars overall.Pros - it's light and airy when you walk in, and the server was nice and friendly.The food was really pretty average. All brunch items were $16,  and we tried 4 different things.I had pancakes and was expecting an impressive plate- I was very underwhelmed for the price.The other dishes came with turkey sausage / eggs etc but the sides all appeared to have been made a day or 2 earlier and partially reheated.2 dishes had a few bits of side salad which also seemed to have been prepped the day before and refrigerated by the look of them.Overall I guess if you are in the area it's nicer than many other spots. But don't go out of your way...

So good and definitely worth the price. I got the spicy tuna roll, which is a large roll and comes with 8 pieces. It also has spicy tuna on top of the roll. It also tastes very fresh. The pieces are a little big to eat in one bite, but that's my only complaint. The tempura sweet potato fries are AMAZING. I've also gotten the tuna tataki salad, which is great but a little small for the price. I would recommend this place.

After a tiring day, my quest for a culinary adventure led me to Little Ochie for some Jamaican zest. The jerk chicken I ordered arrived promptly, boasting a harmonious mix of spices that lived up to its spicy reputation, and the side of plantains was the perfect sweet counterpart to the heat. The cabbage and rice were equally well-seasoned, rounding out a satisfying meal. Seamless service complemented the delicious fare. Little Ochie has secured its spot on my NYC food map for future cravings of authentic Jamaican cuisine.

Title: Upscale Midtown Gem Perfect for Business Lunches

I recently dined at this Midtown restaurant for a business lunch and was thoroughly impressed by the culinary experience. I chose the salmon lentil dish, which was expertly prepared with tender collard greens, a perfectly poached egg, crispy shallots, a dollop of creme fraiche, and a flavorful shallot vinaigrette. The presentation and taste were impeccable. 

I also noticed the lobster roll and steak frites on other tables, which appeared equally appetizing and were noted by my colleagues as delicious. The portions were generous, leaving most of us with leftovers to take home—an added bonus for the quality provided.

Service was exceptional, with attentive staff ensuring a smooth dining experience. The restaurant's setting was the epitome of an upscale Midtown ambience, making it an ideal spot for professional occasions.

While the prices are on the higher end, making it less suitable for casual outings with friends, the quality and service justify the cost for a business meal. Overall, my lunch here was a delight, and I would recommend it for anyone seeking a sophisticated dining option in Midtown.

I recently sampled the lunch special at a local eatery, and at $18, it's a steal for the neighborhood. This deal gives you an entree, appetizer, drink, plus a generous portion of bread—seriously, it's massive.

I chose the iskender kebab with eggplant salad. The amount served was enough for two servings, a real bang for your buck. The kebab, featuring succulent slices of grilled lamb atop sauce-soaked bread cubes, was outstanding and gets my top recommendation. As for the eggplant salad, it was a fresh experience, though not exactly to my taste, particularly as it was my first time trying it.

Despite the bread being a touch soggy from the sauce, I didn't mind; the flavors were that good. Plus, during the quarantine, they offer pick-up and delivery, which is super convenient. If you're in the mood for tasty and ample portions, this spot is worth checking out.

Title: Vibrant Brunch Spot with a Price to Match

My friends and I recently visited a bustling and popular breakfast spot that caught our attention with its lively atmosphere and unique pink accents. However, upon arriving, we were perplexed to find that despite being informed of no seating availability, several empty tables remained unoccupied near the bar where we were offered spots instead.

Once settled at the bar, the ambiance was immediately noticeable, with the buzz of conversation competing against a somewhat overpowering music volume. While this energetic vibe might appeal to some, those looking for a quieter dining experience might find it a tad overwhelming.

The service was commendable; our bartender was not only friendly but also eager to guide us through the menu, which lacked descriptions for several items. A helping hand in deciphering the offerings was much appreciated.

Culinary-wise, I indulged in the tator tot chilaquiles which proved to be a delightful choice—bursting with flavor and well-seasoned, although the base was unfortunately a little on the mushy side. Despite this minor hiccup, the dish was enjoyable enough to warrant a repeat order in the future.

Price-wise, the food was good, albeit slightly on the expensive side, which is something to bear in mind for those dining on a budget.

For those occasional restroom visits, prepare to compete with the loud music, which can make discerning whether the facilities are occupied a bit challenging.

Overall, if you don't mind the lively atmosphere and are willing to splurge a bit, this place is certainly worth a try for its flavorful offerings and friendly service.

crazy popular dimsum place.you get a number downstairs, wait for it to be called, and get told what floor to go to.there are multiple floors and the wait can be hours long. it gets so crowded downstairs, its almost unbearable at times.the service is extremely crazy and its hard to flag anyone down because of how busy it is. make sure to check all the carts, as there is an incredible variety of food. be weary, as the prices add up FAST. they accept all credit cards unlike other asian places, so big plus.

Title: Decent Wings but No Lunch Deals at Times Square Eatery

My visit to this Times Square restaurant for a quick lunch was a mixed bag. Surprisingly, there were no lunch specials on offer, which seemed a missed opportunity in such a bustling area. My order consisted of buffalo and bourbon wings alongside a side of fries. The wings delivered on heat and crispiness, pleasing the palate. However, the fries were a letdown, served on a salad plate with a portion size that didn't justify the price – we felt compelled to send them back.

The flavored lemonades added a sweet note to the meal, enhanced by the perk of free refills. Overall, the experience was just ok. While the wings hit the mark, the lack of value left me without any urgency to return.

La Pecora Bianca has completely stolen my heart. This restaurant exudes a bright and welcoming atmosphere that strikes the perfect balance between casual and sophisticated. It's a rare gem that serves up equally irresistible meals for brunch, lunch, and dinner. Out of all the delightful dishes, the Gramigna is a standout: curly pasta perfectly paired with flavorful house-made sausage, fresh broccolini, and a hint of heat from chili flakes. It's a dish that beckons you back for more. La Pecora Bianca is an absolute must-visit.

After being in New York City, both living in and visiting, for umpteen years I finally dined at Delmonico's.  It wasn't like I never heard of it,  but the inclination didn't exist. Until now.I have to admit that the experience was wonderful and I wonder why I hadn't come sooner. (Well,  one good reason is the number of great places to eat in NYC, and another is I rarely hang out downtown).We had a reservation and courteously were greeting and promptly seating at a nice cozy table at the edge of the main dining room..I liked that they use a line of narrow mirrors on the wall so the person facing the wall still can look back into the dining room. Nice design touch.The noise level in a full dining room is rather deafening, so even with all the soft surfaces you need to talk loudly.  That's the primary downside.I wouldn't characterize the menu as super creative and it's essentially a steak house, as they well note.Our waiter, most professional, told us about the specials and the halibut he mentioned hit a chord with both of us.  It came with lobster on the top, which frankly they could have done without, and also accompanied with green beans.  The halibut was fantastic, well prepared and moist.We started with a salad that was very well made.One thing we had that was totally new as an accompaniment was roasted radishes. What a surprise as they were super wonderful.  Never would I have thought of roasting a radish, but the flavor exuded from the slices.This was all washed down with a bottle of Cakebread Chardonnay Reserve, a perfect pairing for the meal.We left very satisfied and it was worth the time to visit, and the cost too.Very old world New York, but ever so nice.

Title: A Ramen Revelation at Ajisen!

My taste buds are still dancing from the incredible ramen experience at Ajisen! Honestly, I'm already plotting my return visit. This place is a true gem, discovered thanks to a friend's quick decision during a bout of hunger. Although the space could do with a bit of a refresh, don't let that deter you. The continuous flow of patrons is a testament to the exceptional quality of the ramen.

Quick, attentive service ensures your bowl arrives steaming and brimming with flavor. I dared to try one of the spicier options and was met with pure culinary delight. For those in midtown yearning for a swift, savory, and sizzling ramen fix, Ajisen is the spot. Prepare to be wowed; this place is a knockout!

This Korean gastropub has long been a favorite of mine, especially their now gone Broadway & 19th st location that had the coolest whiskey speakeasy-- why haven't they brought it to their Union Square and 35th st locations? RIP The Grain. Barn Joo will appeal to most palates and most occasions. High school reunion? Date? Happy Hour? Girls night? Serious conversation over delicious food?
