Barn Joo is a great spot for all of the above. I know from experience.The entress are pretty intriguing, particularly the uni paella with perfectly crispy rice that forms on the skillet. But the real stars of the show are the small plates and apps. My favorite are the Tteok & cheese, which is essentially mac n cheese but with rice cakes, the truffle fries, fried dumplings, and steamed buns. Getting a group together and sharing a few apps is the move here.

On a cold day after leaving the MET, we were in search of some good 'ol New York style pizza. We found a couple of places and decided on Saba's. Located in Lexington ave between 81st and 82nd. It is a tiny place with barely any seating. They carry pizza with a lot of toppings. Mostly veggies which I love, however I was with my peeps and they wanted pepperoni. They were out, so we just got a plain cheese. It was a little expensive, and not all that tasty, but it was good. Service was OK, because the place is so small, we were privy to some drama going on, which while entertaining it's not ideal. All in all an OK place for a pit stop. Not of you are looking for amazing pizza.

I got a cheesesteak delivered for lunch yesterday, and it hit the spot. Fresh bread roll, tasted just like it should, stuffed with shredded beef, cheese, peppers, and onions. Honestly, could have used more in the middle, but the flavors and textures were just right. If you're used to the cheese steak style popular in Philly and Delaware, I reckon this will do the trick.

Just like the original in Chicago except minus the crazy long waits. My table ordered way more than I particularly ate. I only ate the burger, but the nachos and the eggs were reportedly amazing. My friends also got a lot of tasty drinks. The burger was delectable. It was cooked to perfection, the eggs and patty, the bacon and the buns. It's such an incredible burger. You have to go here.

Despite my high hopes for this establishment, I was met with disappointment. A cardinal sin for a restaurant that includes rice in most of its dishes, the rice I was served tasted old and dry. The proportions were off as well, with an overwhelming amount of rice compared to the fish, which itself was merely passable in freshness and left much to be desired. On a positive note, the avocado served was a highlight, a generous, perfectly ripe half that truly pleased the palate. Service was commendable, attentive and efficient, but unfortunately, it couldn't compensate for the lackluster food quality.

Stumbled on this place as we were looking for an Italian restaurant in UES.   Seating was easy,  service was fast and prompt, and large menu of delicious Italian dishes.   Dinner for two for under $100, can't beat that.   Really enjoyed our appetizers as well.

Title: An Enchanting Evening at [Restaurant Name]

My recent dinner at [Restaurant Name] was exceptional, making it an ideal choice for a romantic outing or a small gathering. The ambiance is truly captivating, with a design that adapts with the seasons, adding an extra touch of magic to the dining experience.

Service was exemplary from the moment we sat near the bar. The staff were exceedingly thoughtful, treating us like royalty, and their menu recommendations were spot-on. The chef's complimentary amuse-bouche, a delightful blend of mushroom, risotto, and lemon zest, set the tone for an evening of culinary delights.

The highlight among our chosen dishes had to be the city's smallest cheeseburgers – so irresistible, we devoured several before I could snap a picture. Paired with perfectly blistered shishito peppers, the meal was full of flavor highlights.

The grand finale, however, was the chocolate cube dessert. It’s an indulgence that alone merits a return visit. In short, [Restaurant Name] excels in both its menu and atmosphere, promising an unforgettable dining experience. I eagerly anticipate my next visit.

Title: A Mediterranean Gem That's Worth Every Penny

If you're on the hunt for top-notch Mediterranean cuisine, this is the place to be. Although they're famed for their brunches, don't overlook the dinner offerings—they're equally impressive. The ambience strikes a chord with its stunning interior, perfectly complemented by the warm and friendly service.

The food here is exceptional. The hummus sets a high bar, rich and creamy, it's among the best you'll savor. Grilled octopus comes perfectly charred, hitting all the right notes on the palate. While the falafel's crunch is spot-on, be warned—it's a cilantro punch that may not suit everyone. The branzino is cooked to perfection, and the duck shawarma paired with wild rice is nothing short of awesome. For dessert, the Nutella rolls are a rich, decadent indulgence, albeit with a $20 price tag that reflects their luxuriousness.

In all, there's little to fault here except the hefty bill at the end of a delightful feast. But for the quality and satisfaction you get, it feels well justified.

Aunt Jake's is ok. The meatball appetizer was good. None of the pastas or sauces really stood out for me, except for the vodka sauce, which was pretty flavorful. The squid ink alle vongole was decent, but I wish it had a more briny taste. I do like that this place allows you to "build your own" pasta into any combination.The server was also meh. We asked for bread sticks 4x and each time he said it would be coming out with our food. Nope, they never came and he never bothered asking if we got them. But the couple who came and sat next to us an hour in got some after they asked for it twice.I most likely won't be back as there are other Italian places I'd rather try.

Good option for brunch..eggs were cooked to perfection and the coffee was flavorful. The grilled cheese was oozing with cheese but I would have preferred it without so much broccoli in it. The tomato basil soup is very good, perfect for a cold day like when I visited. The service was good but not great, it took a while for our server to come back each time she left but understandably it was a Sunday morning so maybe it was busier than normal.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at Union Square

My dining experience at this restaurant, nestled near the W New York in Union Square, was refreshingly pleasant. Despite missing our initial 11:30 am reservation due to a late start to the day, the ease of walking in around noon with no wait was a delightful surprise. The host welcomed us with a smile, leading us to the inviting high chair bar area. The cleanliness of the place and the thoughtful gesture of hot towels set a comforting tone.

Though it took us some time to decide on our order, the mini salmon sashimi, the beef sukiyaki nabe set, and the katsu don with cold soba set eventually graced our table. The beef in the sukiyaki, albeit a bit salty for my taste, was of indisputable quality. My boyfriend, on the other hand, was thoroughly impressed with both the katsu don and the salmon sashimi, relishing in their freshness and flavor.

We ended on a high note with the matcha ice cream with matcha jelly and the almond milk tofu dessert. Both were the perfect palate-cleansers, rounding off our meal with their refreshing taste. This restaurant truly provided comfort, good service, and delectable dishes, making it a gem worth recommending.

Tucked away in the heart of midtown lies a slice haven that's truly in a league of its own. The spot dazzles with its inventive array of flavors, such as the decadent Creamy Potato, the sweet and spicy Hot Honey, and the rich and savory Fig. But it doesn't end there — the Burrata slice is a creamy dream, while the Pepperoni Fra Diavolo offers just the right kick for spice enthusiasts. Complementing the exceptional fare, the service is consistently top-notch, ensuring every visit is as pleasant as the last. If you're in midtown and in the mood for a slice, this place is a must-visit.

Tucked away from the Chelsea Market's frenzy, Los Mariscos offers a serene escape for sea-food lovers. My Thursday night visit revealed a cozy spot with limited space, not quite cut out for large groups but radiating a vibrant atmosphere with its side bar and open-kitchen view.

The menu, while broad in seafood variety, had a tight selection for each category. I indulged in the Fish and Spicy Shrimp Tacos, priced at nearly $10 for a pair. While this might seem steep, the generous fillings provided value for money. The Spicy Shrimp Taco, in particular, won my favor – an explosion of flavor that guarantees a return visit. Overall, Los Mariscos earns a hearty double thumbs up for its culinary delights.

Several months ago I was watching The Best Thing I Ever Ate on the Cooking Channel. Duff Goldman said that B&H Dairy has the best blintzes he's ever eaten. Then on the final episode of Anthony Bourdain Parts Unknown B&H Dairy made a quick appearance because the episode was about the Lower East Side. Technically it's in the East Village but close enough, right? So I bookmarked it and hoped to get there on my next trip to New York. I ate an early lunch there on a Wednesday. It's a tiny place but I was lucky enough to score a table on the wall instead of a seat at the lunch counter. I got the combo with matzo ball soup and 2 cheese blintzes. I ordered a Diet Dr. Brown's Black Cherry to wash it down because that's the best soda in the whole world and I don't drink soda anymore. The soup was very good and the matzo ball was huge but the really delicious part was the thick cut fresh baked challah that came with the soup. No wonder they wear t-shirts that say "Challah por favor!" I'll holla for that challah. After a few minutes the blintzes came out with a side of sour cream. They were gigantic and blisteringly hot. Um, yes, Duff is right! These are the best blintzes I've ever eaten. Better than my grandmothers' (shhh don't tell.) Better than anything. The cheese was smooth and creamy. The skin was tender but brown from being pan fried in butter. I wanted to finish them but I couldn't. I wanted to camp out until it was time to eat again so I could eat here but I had other things to do and see. I'm so glad I made it to B&H Dairy this trip. I'll be back!

Upon hearing high praise for a local soul food gem, my friends and I ventured to Sylvia's for a weekday afternoon treat. We hoped to circumvent the crowds, yet found ourselves waiting for indoor seating. Choosing the immediate availably of the outdoor area, we were met with lackluster service from an inattentive server whose mumbling left us perplexed.

A saving grace, Darnell, stepped in with a level of efficiency sorely needed, yet the experience continued to sour as we noticed our utensils marred by unappetizing dishwater stains—a clear oversight in cleanliness.

The restaurant's celebrated chicken and waffles fell flat; the waffles were inexcusably hard and devoid of flavor, saved only by the syrup accompaniment. The chicken, though slightly more palatable, was dry and underseasoned. In short, my inaugural visit to Sylvia's was a disappointment, and it's unlikely I'll return, possibly turning to Amy Ruth's for my next soul food fix.

Title: A Slice Worth Every Penny

I recently visited a local pizzeria where the slices were exceptionally large, each costing $6. To my delight, they were not only massive but also incredibly satisfying. The crust stood out for its perfect crispiness, reminiscent of freshly baked bread, which was a real treat. The pizza itself was delectable, with every bite bursting with the savory goodness of the flavorful sauce. While it's true the pizza felt rather indulgent and perhaps a tad fattening, it was absolutely worth it for the amazing taste and the sheer satisfaction it provided. If you're in the mood to treat yourself, this is definitely the place to go!

Title: A Delectable Dive into Flavors with a Rooftop Twist

My recent visit to this restaurant was a delightful experience for my taste buds, particularly due to their exquisite stuffed peppers and chicken wings. Our server informed us that the wings were from Amish-raised chickens, promising a smaller but tastier experience. They did not disappoint – the wings had a remarkably pure and delicious flavor, enhanced by a unique brown sugar butter sauce that left me craving more.

Equally impressive were the stuffed jalapeño peppers – spicy yet incredibly tasty. The accompanying sauce perfectly complemented their fiery kick. It's a pity that such culinary gems aren't available back home in Seattle!

We topped off our meal with a visit to the rooftop bar. However, the atmosphere there wasn't quite to our liking. The vibe, possibly influenced by the dated top 40's tunes and an eclectic mix of patrons, didn't resonate with us. We found it difficult to describe precisely why, but it simply wasn't our scene.

In summary, if you're in for a wonderful meal and can handle a bit of heat, the restaurant offers some standout dishes. However, for a more relaxed ambiance, the main dining area might be the preferable choice over the rooftop scene.

Title: A Weekend Lunch to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

I recently had the pleasure of dining at [Restaurant Name] for a Saturday afternoon lunch and it was nothing short of delightful. Despite initial worries about the potential wait time, my party was seated instantly, which was a wonderful surprise.

The menu was uncomplicated and to the point. I noticed the absence of combo deals, likely due to it being a weekend, but that didn't dampen the experience. We settled on the dumpling soup, which I strongly suggest enhancing with the chapchae for an extra layer of flavor. The spiciness level was perfect; present but not overpowering.

However, the highlight of our meal was undoubtedly the spicy pork belly. As someone who's tasted this dish countless times, I can confidently say their version ranks among the top—a generous portion that was truly savory and memorable.

In summary, [Restaurant Name] has secured itself as a fantastic dining spot in my book, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Met a friend her after work one evening because she had always meant to stop in and try this place. Prices aren't unreasonable and the space is huge with a lot of long tables so even though it was pretty crowded it didn't feel overwhelming. Because there are so many tables it can take a while for a server to physically get over to you  but given how many people were there service wasn't terrible. We both drank the Tropic Thunder and it was very good - almost dangerously good and we could have consumed way more of them.

I came here on a saturday afternoon. A busy day, line was long service was quick. The cashier was friendly and the food was very good and fresh!  The chicken was tender and moist and the waffle was fluffy with a perfectly lightly crisp edge.  Their fountain drinks are very refreshing.. i got the cream soda and def got a refill before I left. The seating is interesting so you gotta sort of just catch a seat. People do come here for a brunch kind of thing so people do sit down and take their time.

Yum Yum Yum!! I've been dying to try this place as it is an UES staple.  Came here with a friend and truly enjoyed a lovely meal here. The restaurant itself is nice and eclectic with all their unique pig décor! Service was super friendly and I could see there were def regulars here, the way they interacted with the wait staff, which is always a great sign from a restaurant!As for the food, wonderfully flavored and plentiful. Poached Chicken with chili dressing - chicken was super tender. There were plenty of nuts and cucumbers covered in this mild chili dressing that was wonderfully seasoned from chilies, salt, sesame seeds and scallions. So good and a great dish to share.BBQ Spare ribs - this is a fan favorite of the restaurant. The ribs were fall off the bone, wonderfully dressed in that sticky Chinese BBQ sauce. A must get here. Hotpot fish with mixed vegetables - A great hot dish. The soup was super flavorful, great when paired with rice. It wasn't too spicy which I appreciated. There were plenty of fish pieces with bamboo, celery and cabbage. This dish could easily feed a family of four. Great as leftovers as well! So GOOOOODDDD!Overall, a wonderful meal at Pig Heaven. Love that they really embrace the name. You can taste the care and thought they put behind their dishes, executing it to ensure flavor and quality but not have it be oily.

Title: A Funky Feast at B & L

Walking into B & L is like stepping into an Instagram dream – from the photo-worthy entrance to the funky wallpaper, it's a visual delight, enhanced by the warm welcome from their easy-on-the-eyes staff.

Celebrating my cousin’s 38th birthday here was a blast! We kicked off with a spread of starters: plump, juicy shrimp cocktail, icy briny oysters, and sumptuous lobster and burger bites that had us all reaching for more – the accompanying sauces were a perfect match for the delicious rolls.

We couldn't resist the allure of the top three entrees and decided to dive into all of them. The burger crowned with a generous portion of lobster was a standout, while the lobster rolls, slathered in either chipotle or truffle mayo, were a delightful twist on a classic.

A fair warning: NYC drink prices can inflate your bill, as they did for our party of five, but considering the fabulous time we had and the exceptional service, the experience was worth every penny. We're already planning our next visit to B & L!

I was not expecting to love Taim so much!!!  OMG!  I got the green pita and it was amazing.  So much flavor.  Definitely worth the money, but not something I can afford every week.  I am normally not a fan of this type of food, but I decided to try something new and go outside my comfort zone. I am so glad I did!The sandwich itself is a bit messy so eat sitting down or bring it somewhere where you can eat it in peace.  Get a fork too.  The sandwich is filling so you need anything else. I recommend giving this spot a try if you like falafels or want to try something new.  Order ahead for pick up!
Usually my go to after a night of libiations. But the pizza was awful. The buffalo chicken slice was literally mush. It's fine, I won't hold it against I will be back for redemption.

I'm an ardent supporter of this café, despite it being part of a chain. The coffee is consistently satisfying, pairing perfectly with the stunning array of cakes that are as visually appealing as they are palatable. Not to mention, the baked goods never fail to delight the taste buds. My only gripe is the somewhat cramped seating area. Nonetheless, its convenience makes it an ideal choice for either kickstarting a busy day or winding down in the evening.

My recent visit to this spot yielded one of the best dining experiences I've had to date. Opting for the top-tier omakase was a decision I'll never regret – it's worth every penny. The sushi was so exceptional that we couldn't resist ordering extra pieces even after we thought we were done. Highly recommend for an unforgettable meal where the quality speaks for itself.

Visited TabeTomo on a bustling Tuesday evening to partake in their one-year anniversary BOGO Ramen deal. Despite a full house, we were quickly seated at the bar. Timing seemed key as the place was packed by 6:30pm, likely spurred by the promotion.

I ventured to try the Yasai Vegetable Ramen which initially struck me as overwhelmingly salty. Mitigating the broth intake improved the experience, though the dish would benefit substantially from more vegetables, particularly bean sprouts, to justify its veggie ramen title. Nevertheless, the perfectly soft-boiled egg and the standout fried lotus root added enjoyable textures and flavors.

My companion opted for the Tonkotsu Chashu dipping ramen and was thoroughly impressed. While the vegetarian options at TabeTomo might not shine as brightly, meat lovers, especially dipping ramen aficionados, are likely to find a satisfying bowl here.

I'm confused why this place has 4 stars on Yelp. I don't know if the quality is just lower for restaurant week, but based on my experience on Friday, I would not want to come back. The drinks and bacon appetizer were okay, but everything really went downhill from here. I came here with a group of 4 and 2 of steaks that we ordered were uncooked to the point where it was inedible. Luckily my filet was cooked medium rare like I ordered, but the quality was not there. The filet was much tougher than I'd expect from a supposedly nice restaurant. The fries we ordered to share were also barely edible and looked like it was soaked in oil as if they were refried after sitting out for a while. Guests all around us also seemed to have the same issues and were generally disappointed with their meals. The servers were really nice and definitely apologetic but there wasn't much they could do. Even when they tried to send our food back to the kitchen, we didn't see any improvements. Overall, it seemed like the kitchen / management just didn't care about the quality of the food they were serving.

Title: A Delightful Mistake at Raku

Last night's unplanned visit to Raku, which I mistook for a ramen shop, turned out to be serendipitous. Opting for the fried chicken, I found it delicious though somewhat standard fare. The standout of my meal was the ankake udon - a bowl of thick, flavorful soup that caught my attention with subtle hints of lemongrass in the broth. The noodles were a textural triumph, masterfully cooked to achieve the ideal chewiness. It was a dish I savored every spoonful of and would recommend to any udon enthusiast.

Title: Swift Service and Tasty Ramen

I had the pleasure of dining at this establishment on a bustling Saturday night, and I must commend their efficient service. Despite the crowd, we were comfortably seated in a mere 10 minutes. I opted for the chili chicken ramen and was pleasantly surprised when it arrived at our table in under 5 minutes.

The ramen itself was a delightful experience. The broth was flavorful, with a delicious complexity that satisfied my taste buds. As for the noodles, they were the perfect texture—chewy and smooth, just how good ramen noodles should be. The heat level was mild, serving to enhance the overall flavor without overwhelming it.

My only gripe was with the bamboo shoots, which had an off-putting preserved taste that didn't quite mesh with the rest of the dish. However, that was a minor issue in an otherwise excellent meal. Kudos to the kitchen for their solid performance and to the staff for their impeccable service.

Everything here is delicious. Cash only place. The pork or crab and pork soup dumplings are a must try along with the scallion pancakes. The service here is super fast. This location is somewhat small which can result to a little wait to be seated. I have tried other dishes and they have yet to disappoint.

Title: A Spicy Delight with a Side of Confusion

I recently visited a local restaurant with my sister, and our experience was a savory adventure, albeit with a few hiccups. We decided to share a couple of dishes: the string beans & eggplant and a mala dry pot. The eggplant dish was the star of the show - the eggplant was exceptionally savory and juicy, leaving us craving more. The mala dry pot was a flavorful affair, packed with an array of ingredients including fatty beef, sliced beef, bok choy, lotus root, and enoki mushrooms. However, the beancurd was disappointingly tough to chew.

We ordered our spice level mild, but the dish still packed a serious punch, with stealthy peppercorns giving us a fiery surprise. Portion sizes felt small, particularly for the mala dry pot, but they were sufficient for a light meal.

The restaurant's format was a bit puzzling, combining counter ordering with table service delivery, which led to a rather bare-bones service experience. The lack of interaction and table service, including water refills, left us wondering about the etiquette of tipping in such an establishment.

In summary, for those in the vicinity with a hankering for eggplant, I'd recommend dropping by. The mala dry pot is also a solid choice if you can handle the heat and overlook the chewy beancurd. Just be prepared for a less traditional service setup that might have you second-guessing how to navigate your dining experience.

I recently dined in a midtown gem that left me thoroughly impressed. The value for the money was outstanding, particularly for the location. The portion sizes were generous, especially notable was the set dish that came with a heaping serving of delicious soba noodles. Moreover, the freshness of the fish stood out as a highlight of the meal. Overall, a delightful dining experience with reasonable prices and ample food.

I came here to celbreate a special occasion. It took me FOREVER TO GET A RESERVATION, but it was worth it. What makes this place so special is staff is so friendly and they made me feel SO SPECIAL. This "boss lady" who runs the kitchen came right over poured us champagne to celebrate our special day and honestly they made my day. Some of the food is excellent others options are okay but the level of service and attentiveness they gave us gives this place 5 stars. They even brought us a candle out with a complimentary desert! Not to mention the chocolate contraption desert we ordered off the menu was SO GOOD!  This place is too kind. They will definitely see me again. Make a reservation and don't come earlier than your time because there packed Friday and Saturday. The PASTAS ARE SOOO GOOD!

3 years after I wrote my original review, I gave this place another try in hopes of not finding tortillas as their "house made wraps" for the duck. Without surprise, they are still serving thick tortillas! Authentic Chinese Peking duck wraps are very thin, which is a compliment to the ducks. But when you're biting into the tortillas wrap, it just feels like you're eating a burrito or taco since the wrap is very thick. Overall, I will definitely not return because there is nothing authentic about this place when they are serving out tortillas.

New place before Ranger game opening night. ENTRANCE- there are 2 stations that look like the host. A little confusing but we were promptly helped and seated. DECOR - kind of different with lots of red chairs and booth covering. Also extremely dark. Good I guess for many a forbidden rendezvous. MENU - small but eclectic from the standpoint of varied choices. Including a raw bar. VINO - a nice selection of options. Decent California choices by glass and bottle. APPETIZERS - tried the steak egg rolls that were really good with a bit of spice. Only draw back was the oily product. Maybe drain a bit longer or cook at a higher temp for a bit shorter to lessen absorbing oil. Tried the lump crab Mac and cheese that was really exceptional. Worth a try. ENTREES - for the price portions were ok but felt stingy. The monk fish osso bucco was quite good with hen of woods mushrooms, asparagus and a nice almost Marsala type sauce. The sauce was a bit too saltyPRICE - even with a $95 dollar bottle of wine. The total tab for 2 was about $250. Keeping vino aside it's still $75 per person so definitely $$$$

Awesome place great vibe it looks ancient but is only 7 years old!!!!!Can't wait to go back and grab a bite. It's def a place you'll want to have at least a drink to see. It will take a while to look at all the decor. So go and take it in you'll be pleasantly surprised.

Normally if I want a burger and also save a few bucks, I'll go to a McDonald's. However after running the NYC Half Marathon earlier in the day, I decided to mix things up and check out Black Burger since it was located really close to where I was staying. It was a really small place. A little more than half of the restaurant was the kitchen. On the customer side of the counter there were some counter spots for you to eat your burger, but not enough for more than a few people. I wasn't feeling particularly hungry, so when it was my turn, I ordered just their Black Burger with cheese, cooked medium without any sides. I got the burger with their standard ingredients... lettuce, tomato, pickles, onion, and house sauce. Keep in mind that they'll give you a discount if pay with cash. I hardly ever carry cash these days, so plastic it is!Once my order was up, I took it back to my room to eat. The single patty burger didn't look very impressive, but it did taste good. Also the bun didn't disintegrate while I was eating it. If I do come back here, I'll probably get a double cheeseburger or one of their specialty burgers.

I'm so glad I found this place! I was craving really good Korean style chicken wings, and let me tell you, this place hits the spot. The chicken wings were a decent size; nothing was too small. The flavoring for both the soy garlic and spicy were very delicious  as well. I would have to say the key factor to how good these wings are were due to the perfect crunchiness. The wings had the right amount of sauce where it didn't make the crunch soggy. It was crispy with every bite.They also have happy hour M-F from 5-8! $2 of draft beer and soju.

Title: Disappointing Happy Hour at [Restaurant Name]

My recent visit to [Restaurant Name] for happy hour snacks left much to be desired, especially when considering their premium pricing. I understand that good food and service command a higher cost, and I'm generally willing to pay for quality. However, my experience didn't justify the expense.

The happy hour policy requires patrons to sit at the bar, which proved to be a challenge given the crowded space. After a lengthy wait, we secured a couple of stools. Service was slow, likely due to the busy hour, but what was more surprising was the $6 charge for a bottle of sparkling water, a detail that was not shared upfront.

Food-wise, the fish tacos were average and the deviled eggs satisfactory. The calamari, however, was disappointingly smothered in what tasted like store-bought sweet chili sauce. This oversight required intervention from a manager, who kindly removed the item from our bill.

In summary, the highlight of our visit may have been the drinks, as the experience was overshadowed by sluggish service and lackluster dishes. I'd hope for improvements in both quality and transparency considering the prices they command.

Title: A Clucking Fantastic Feast!

If there's one thing this buzzing culinary hot spot proves, it's that they serve the absolute best chicken and waffles, PERIODT - and that's not an overstatement! Embrace yourself for a scrumptious sensation, but be warned: this place's popularity means walk-ins might face a wait upwards of an hour.

Our order included the classic and a gluten-free version of their star dish, both drizzled with a heavenly habanero honey sauce that we daringly mixed with maple syrup – an irresistible combo that had us swooning. As I reminisce, I can't help but drool!

To complement the meal, while they offer tempting sangrias, we opted for the robust coffee, which proved to be a perfect pairing. The effervescent staff added to the charm, making us feel right at home despite the bustling atmosphere.

In a nutshell, this joint is a love letter to anyone who fancies the soul-soothing power of crispy, tender chicken matched with fluffy waffles. Just be prepared to wait, because good things – and evidently great chicken and waffles – come to those who do.

Morton's continues to be one of my top steakhouse picks in the city, a sentiment echoed by my family as we make it a point to dine here semi-annually. The staff's attention to detail contributes significantly to the personalized experience, notably recognizing and celebrating any special occasions we're there for. On our most recent visit, we indulged in the porterhouse and tomahawk steaks, both masterfully prepared to a perfect medium. Consistency in quality and service is what keeps us coming back to Morton's.

I came in at 5:15p on a Sunday. They had seats available as long as I was out by 7, and also had seats at the bar available.  The bartenders were super busy the whole time making drinks for the table. Even on a Sunday night they were very busy. Of note: the food came out super fast!I started out with the Broccoli & Artichoke dumplings. The sauce it was prepared in had a really nice flavor and the additional veggies in the bowl added great flavor and texture. Next I had the cauliflower tempura steamed buns. It was tossed in a tomato based Chile sauce. I was not a huge fan of the sauce it was tossed in. I likely would try something different next time. Next I went with the Shiitake "cacio e Pepe."  This had great flavors and the polenta was a nice touch to add to the creaminess.  Also of note, the pepper didn't overwhelm which can tend to happen.  I finished up with the chocolate cake. It was moist the way a chocolate cake should be. I'll give it to the avocados (though you couldn't taste them). There were a few things on the menu that I really wanted to try but didn't have space for. That doesn't happen often. Based on the quality of the food I will likely come back to try them out at some point!

Title: A Brunch to Remember at Jane

I recently visited Jane in SoHo on a recommendation purely inspired by tales of their extraordinary bacon. Seizing the opportunity on a leisurely weekday afternoon, my friend and I were pleased to find the place comfortably uncrowded, promising a relaxed brunch experience.

True to the word-of-mouth praise, the bacon did not disappoint. Each slice was a savory delight, perfectly crispy and as remarkable as my coworker had assured. But, the showstopper was the vanilla bean French toast - a heavenly combination of sweet and savory that was both indulgent and satisfying.

Jane proved to be a gem for brunch enthusiasts. Whether you're lured in by the promise of their famed bacon or simply in search of a satisfying meal, this spot is a must-visit when you find yourself wandering through SoHo.

I recently visited a bustling pizzeria for a classic cheese slice. Despite an initial surprise when the pizza arrived slightly over-reheated with a bit of char, I was pleased to find the flavor uncompromised. The crust boasted a pleasing consistency that held up well under the ample cheese. The constant crowd is a testament to the quality. Overall, a solid choice for a satisfying pizza experience.

Title: A Pho-nomenal Experience

My recent visit to this restaurant was a delightful journey into Vietnamese cuisine, particularly their exceptional pho. Although accommodating our large group felt slightly cramped in the back, the overall experience was not diminished, thanks to the super nice service.

We kicked things off with the pork summer rolls, which were nothing short of amazing. Imagine the savory taste of grilled spam, but within the delicate confines of a tightly wrapped summer roll. It had a surprise crunch, likely from a Chinese cracker tucked inside, that elevated the texture and made it a memorable start to our meal.

The main event was the beef pho, and it truly stole the show. The broth was rich and aromatic, hitting all the right notes of traditional pho spices. The noodles were plenty and cooked to al dente perfection, while the beef was the epitome of tenderness. Each bite was a testament to the care and authenticity put into their food.

In short, this place is a must-visit for pho enthusiasts. It's not just a meal; it's an experience well worth savoring.

Japanese food that hits the spot! I got the katsu curry and was not too impressed with it. The katsu could've been fried more and the curry sauce did not wow me. The unagi don though... that on  the other hand gave me a slap in the face of wowness. It was so good! I'm usually not even a eel fan but when I tried a bite of it I fell in love. I also got the beef tataki as appetizer and that was good too! Next time I come back ill be getting the unagi don!

Solid ramen, with unique soda choices.While Churutto's ramen will never rank among the city's bucket list joints, the Tokyo-style ramen is nevertheless worth a return trip.  With the exception of the vegetarian ramen (inexplicably more expensive than the meaty broths), most ramens were chicken-based a la Ivan or Totto.Tokyo bowl was thickened with sesame paste and dressed with pork chashu, while not the most umami of slabs, were nevertheless meaty and generously portioned.  Certainly beat the standard chicken bowl, which was dressed with black garlic oil (a la Nishida Sho-Ten) and a reasonable grilled chicken.A revelation was actually the Mango Creamy Soda.  Imagine Hansen's, made ten times smoother and more interesting.  Try it, then buy a case of it at a Japanese market.Did not order the poke, and would not do so in the future.  Examination of other people's orders appeared to feature a heavy helping of rice under a salad bar's worth of vegetables.  A small scoop of fish served as the poke garnish.  It's sad that poke has been interpreted here to represent a bowl meal, a far cry from its origins as a fish-forward, rice-optional staple served in Hawaiian supermarkets.

If the pasta portions are too big, you can ask them to split it in half and they'll put it into smaller pans when serving. The staffs are super friendly and accommodating. I had the lobster linguine - my honest opinion was that it was a tad too salty and way too oily. Fresh lobster was used and flavors were super bold though. Even so, I loved the atmosphere, the staff, and the location. The truffle wild boar pasta was really good and creamy. For dessert, I had the panna cotta, it was a nutty take on regular panna cotta so quite different but loved it. Will be back for sure.

I recently revisited a favorite spot with friends visiting from LA, and once again, it did not disappoint. We had a diverse selection including egg benedict, various omelettes, grilled octopus, crispy calamari, Margherita pizza, and refreshing four flower juice.

The egg benedict remains a flawless 5/5 – my go-to dish that consistently delights. Similarly, the garden omelette was a vegetable-packed dream, earning its 5/5 with a delightful cotton candy-like cheddar cheese infusion. The spinach goat cheese omelette also impressed with its soft texture and equally sweet cotta cheese notes.

However, the cheese omelette fell short at a 2/5. As a cheese lover, I found it underwhelming and suggest other options. The calamari, overly crispy to the point of distraction, also earned a 2/5, paling in comparison to versions I've enjoyed elsewhere.

The day special, grilled octopus, was tender and flavorful earning a solid 4/5, though it wasn't my favorite rendition. The Margherita pizza surprised with a 3.5/5, being better than expected and a hit with my friends, yet it didn't top my pizza experiences.

Service was impeccable with a 5/5 score. Attentive and accommodating staff made the meal all the more enjoyable, with our waiter particularly diligent in ensuring a pleasant dining experience.

In summary, the restaurant continues to shine with its standout dishes and exceptional service – a reliable choice for both locals and visitors alike.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience

I recently visited a local restaurant with my roommates, and we had an absolute blast. The food exceeded our expectations; not only was it delicious, but the portions were generous, offering great value for the price. The service truly set this place apart. Our waiter was incredibly patient, taking the time to guide us through the dining experience and ensuring we enjoyed the meal to the fullest. The seasoning and sauces were spot-on – a perfect complement to each dish. We also tried some of the server's recommendations, which did not disappoint. By the end of the meal, we left satiated and in high spirits. This establishment deserves a high rating of 4.8 out of 5, and we are eagerly looking forward to our next visit.

What a cute great affordable place! We just had to try the burgers after we saw Bobby Flay has been eating them for years and recommended on the Flay List show. Atmosphere was cozy and warm feeling. Small place at this location. No wait at 6pm on a friday, we sat right now. The place was filled though. The burger was crunchy on the outside and very flavorful but not too meaty tasting. Sometimes thick burgers taste too meaty but this was delicious. Definitely make it a cheeseburger! And they give you lots of pickles and onions to put on top which I love. Super affordable at 12.50The cottage fries were really good too. They are thick chips that are crunchy on the outside but have fluffy potato on the inside. Very good,  I would take these over fries any day. And I like how they are served plain so you can put the amount of salt you want on them. We had the chocolate chip cake for dessert since I have a sweet tooth. Which was a rich chocolate cake. The iceing was very sugary. Tasted like an entenmanns cake but in a good way. And they have whipped cream on the side. Nice to have something sweet after a burger. Can't wait to come back again. I kind of want to try the turkey sandwhich but I don't want to not get the burger again b.c it was the best burger I had at a restaraunt!

Title: Humble Bronx Diner: Generous Portions, No Frills

I've frequently passed this Bronx diner without giving it much thought, its modest exterior mirroring the unassuming interior. Indeed, a touch-up could breathe new life into its worn ambiance. However, necessity led me to venture inside, and I was pleasantly surprised by the dining experience.

The Mykonos salad was a formidable contender, sprawling across the plate – a challenge to finish but a satisfying one. It's always a win when the portion sizes justify the spending. My main dish, a classic combo of two eggs with avocado and home fries, was simple but flawlessly executed.

This place operates with the heart of a diner rather than the pretense of a restaurant, and that's not a negative. It's where you go for an uncomplicated, hearty meal that guarantees you won't leave hungry, and your wallet won't feel much lighter for it.

Love everything about Raku!From the lovely exterior to the small and intimate space. This place is a hidden gem and can be easily missed. There's no sign on the door but lookout for their simplistic curtains. My boyfriend and I come during the weekdays and there's usually no wait and we are always seated immediately.Can't go wrong with anything on the menu, everything is delicious! I am a huge fan of their udon and love the bouncy and chewy texture of the noodles. I always go for their Niku Udon ($17. CASH ONLY) which comes with beef short-ribs & honeycomb tripe. $17 may seem like a lot of money for a bowl of udon but the portion size leaves me feeling full and I appreciate the amount of beef short-ribs and honeycomb tripe they give. The tripe is easy to bite through and the beef is flavorful. The broth that it comes with is light and really hits the spot. The staff are welcoming and super attentive which contributes to the overall pleasant dining experience.Raku is one of my favorite restaurants and one that I will be coming back to time and time again!

I was craving for sweets on a Friday afternoon and remembered there's by CHLOE behind my building. I stopped by and got the gluten-free chocolate chip cookies. It was sweet but kind of missed the chewiness of the regular chocolate chip cookies.

Lunch with a client was pretty great- location is excellent and the ambience is super relaxed but cozy. I thought the service was good and food was as well! We tried the Cesar salad, just ok.. the roasted veggies ( with pine nuts/raisins) really good and split the margarita pizza. Pizza was delicious, great for 2 people as long as you ordered a few sides. It was thin and crispy and the mozzarella was fresh. I liked it! I'd prob try a different salad next time but all in all- totally recommend if you're in the area! Also cute Godiva store is around the corner on the same floor- perfect for a sweet treat on the way out!

Tucked away in the bustling streets of Soho, this gem of a cafe proved to be the perfect pit-stop after an intense shopping spree. Offering all-day breakfast and an array of simple lunch options, the cool and quiet atmosphere serves as an ideal retreat from the sizzling summer hustle outside. I indulged in a pressed sandwich paired with a refreshing salad that hit just the right spot. The service was top-notch with a notably friendly staff, and attention to detail extended even to the cleanliness and quirky decor of the bathroom. For anyone navigating the high streets and in need of a satisfying meal, this adorable spot should not be missed—an oasis of delightful fare that's a must-visit for out-of-towners.

Title: A Gem Near Madison Square Garden

My experience at this restaurant, nestled conveniently close to Madison Square Garden and Penn Station, was a delight. Arriving on a Friday around 6 p.m., the venue wasn't too crowded, allowing for a comfortable start to our evening. Though we were late due to traffic, the staff welcomed us with open arms and promptly seated us at a table per our reservation.

The interior boasted a trendy decor which caught my eye and added to the ambiance. Service was outstanding; the staff was amicable and attentive throughout our visit. Our feast included a savory mushroom/truffle flatbread, perfectly fried calamari, addictive nachos, and flavorful Korean lettuce wraps. The standout was the pretzel, a last-minute addition when our chicken quesadilla order was seemingly forgotten. I wasn't bothered by this misstep, especially after learning that the quesadillas were pre-made, hinting they might not have been as fresh as the other dishes.

Overall, I found the restaurant to be very accommodating with a convenient location and delicious food. I certainly plan to return and would recommend it to anyone looking for a great dining spot before attending an event nearby.

Had a delightful experience at this local pizzeria with friends. We indulged in two large custom-made pizzas, featuring imported pepperoni and an intriguing half cheese, half breaded fried eggplant combination. The pies, which were generously topped and bursting with flavor, boasted a perfectly balanced thin, crispy yet chewy crust. Despite the bustling atmosphere, our meal was enjoyable and unrushed. Eager to return for another round of their delicious offerings.

I'm really impressed with these delicious, flavorful, *giant* (see dumpling prep area prior to ordering!), perfectly steamed/seared pork dumplings. (Shrimp ones were odd, possibly due to old frozen bland chewy corn, so I'd avoid those...)I'm curious about the sauces- looking forward to trying them!

I visited a restaurant after a long day at work to indulge in their General Tso's nuggets, also known as 'Tso Swag,' and I was pleasantly surprised. Each nugget was perfectly coated with a savory sauce and boasted a fulfilling size. These are undoubtedly some of the best chicken nuggets I've ever tasted. If you're hankering for Chinese takeout, these nuggets will hit the spot.

Another new Omakase, this one on Bowery and for $160 and from the former chef of Gaijin, the popular spot in Astoria.Chef Mark Garcia of Gaijin handles the sushi here while chef Evan Zagha handles the introductory kaiseki courses. Though each course is written out nice and clearly on the menu, there are still some surprises in the preparations and the flavors they bring with each course.One of the best courses occurs right at the beginning with the Chawanmushi, here served with a generous helping of Uni. I ate and drank every last bit of this warm satisfying bowl in preparation for the 11 courses of amazing sushi that followed.The highlight, and the one everybody will he putting on Insta for sure, is the Otoro topped with Uni and Caviar. It's gorgeous and delicious and definitely one of the best bites of the night.Even the dessert here is worth mentioning as a must try, which can sometimes be an afterthought in an Omakase. Smooth scoops of black sesame and ginger ice cream sit atop a buttery slice of caramelized brioche, making for a few perfect bites to end the night.Service throughout is also excellent, as chef Mark Garcia is open to engaging in some friendly banter throughout. In a sea of new high price Omakases all over NYC, this one definitely sticks out with several very memorable courses.

Title: A Culinary Triumph in the Heart of NYC

From the moment we stepped into the restaurant, the buzz of excitement was palpable, and I'm thrilled to report that the hype surrounding this culinary gem is well-deserved. My year-long quest for exceptional dining in New York City culminated in a remarkable experience here.

Ignoring previous advice, our party of three ventured in on a Thursday evening. To our delight, at 6:20 PM, we were seated immediately without a wait—a rarity in this city's vibrant food scene.

Our taste buds were tantalized by an array of exquisite dishes. The menu's standout was the duck pineapple curry, a masterpiece paired ingeniously with a jasmine rice duck confit. Not far behind in the flavor parade was the innovative sweet bread salad. Both are essential must-tries.

We also savored the pig ears, which were surprisingly reminiscent of crispy fries, and the pork jowl fruit curry. While the latter presented a tangy twist with its sour notes, the pork's tenderness was nothing short of spectacular.

Despite the overall success, a word to the wise: the Thai tea could use a stronger brew as it erred on the side of watery. Instead, opt for the roti, and definitely don't pass up on pairing the sticky rice with the Pork Jowl curry for an indulgent treat.

Conclusively, this dining adventure was nothing short of magnificent, ensuring my imminent return. If you find yourself in New York City with a hunger for an epicurean delight, look no further.

Delicious, minimalist korean place, border-line/leaning towards fusion. It's also a different style of korean dining than you'd experience in ktown. It is quite pricey so you need to adjust your expectations before entering. Reservations seem highly recommended.We tried:- vegetable rice 10/10: (the base-rice) it was so delicious!! was probably a combination of both the ingredients and the cooking - truffle spaghetti 9/10: (it was a special the day we went, so might not be always available). this was quite delicious and the truffle flavors were strong. only woe would be that it needed a slight more flavor (besides the mushrooms)- octopus terrine 6/10: the octopus was really soft and tender but i didn't think it was worth the cost at all- ori tang (duck stew) 10/10: this was hands-down the highlight of the meal. was surprisingly slightly spicy but not super-noticeably so. the duck was incredibly soft and the texture was perfect. all the vegetables complemented the entire dish really well too. i would definitely return for this dish again.

Title: Decent Eats at a Cozy Spot with a Hefty Tag

My recent lunch outing with a friend offered a mixed bag of delights and letdowns. The prompt seating and comfort of the restaurant set a nice stage for our catch-up session. The staff were amiable, keeping the ambiance inviting and the place spotless, right down to the quaint restrooms.

The food hit some high notes, particularly the Moussakas, which avoided the common pitfall of heaviness, leaving no trace of eater's remorse. The halloumi, with its pleasing texture, did tip the scales toward too salty. The Psita Tis Oras Poikilia was enjoyable but demands a green side to cut through its rich profile.

Desserts offered a seesaw of experiences. The Baklava was a textural triumph—crispy yet succumbing to a near-soggy downfall—thankfully redeemed by its firm bottom layer. The Loukoumades, while initially satisfying, quickly became monotonous, although a second encounter as leftovers saw a resurgence of my affection for them.

A kind gesture from our waiter was the offering of a pine-scented liquor for digestion, an acquired taste that didn't quite hit the mark for me.

While the overall experience wasn't negative, the pricing felt steep for the value received. It's a nice spot to try, and I wouldn't rebuff another visit—especially if companions suggest it—but it's unlikely to become a regular haunt for me. I've heard of varying experiences at other locations, so my palate may yet take another tour before drawing a final conclusion.

Late night place to get a good meal. Service was ok, not super but hey it was pretty late and I think they were down to about 2 peeps. We ordered the guac, comes with bacon....yes please! BFF had a few tacos, they were good and we had the nachos to share, holy moly you get a lot of Nachos and they were delish. No complaints from this muchacha, I would go back!

Great atmosphere, amazing hand rolls, cheap prices, and quick service!  Reservations are another allowed and a lie just forms along the bar as people wait.  There's only one long bar and it's basically seat yourself as people get up.  The rolls and delicious, fresh, and very reasonably priced ($25 for 5).  Would highly recommend and will definitely be returning.

The bacon is heavenly! Tried the cheeseburger with bacon and egg and it was AMAZING! Would definitely come back here again another time. This place has a lot of space for seating and big comfy couch chairs. Despite the space, this place can get really crowded. We ended up waiting 45 minutes for three people. They have a bar downstairs for the

I had the pleasure of ordering delivery from this restaurant tonight, and I must say, I was thoroughly impressed! Opting for the "To the Max Poke Bowl," the option to choose three proteins allowed me to savor salmon, tuna, and omega-3-rich salmon skin. The base of zucchini noodles was a fresh touch and, despite the up-charge, adding guacamole was a decision well made.

The bowl also included cucumber, red onions, scallions, jalapeños, mushrooms, kimchi, and shredded nori, all contributing to a burst of flavors and textures. With a price of $17.70 plus tax, the portions were generous, providing great value for money.

In terms of freshness and taste, this meal hit the mark. I can't recommend it enough for anyone looking for a delicious, health-conscious option. Two thumbs up for this delightful culinary experience!

Title: A Breakfast to Remember at Bubby's

After much anticipation, I finally visited Bubby's for their touted breakfast and it did not disappoint. The sourdough pancakes, which have dominated my social feeds, were a culinary revelation—thin, expertly blended with the right touch of salty and sweet, and sublime with just butter and maple syrup.

My husband opted for a custom Eggs, Tomato, and Avocado Benedict served over their famous biscuits instead of the usual muffins. The biscuits were divinely soft and buttery, and they're clearly a must-have; even plain with a side of jam and clotted cream, they'd be a treat.

Accompanying our meals, the drip coffee was strong and on point, while the cold brew had an intriguing hint of banana—a delightful surprise.

In summary, Bubby's delivered an impeccable breakfast experience. The hype is real—do yourself a favor and indulge in these breakfast delights. Highly recommended!

The food is so amazing!!! This is my first time having Korean food and I am so damn impressed!!! I'm black, like black black from down south. And my momma and grandmother fry some mean chicken but the Koreans KILLEDDDD THIS DISH!! The garlic tofu wings wings were wangssss! We also had the shrimp tempura and that was very tasty. Then we embarked on the Bulgogi with white rice... AMAZING!! The service was also unforgettable. We will be back!

I had never been to Charlie Palmer steak before and thought for Restaurant Week we would give it a try! What a nice evening. The restaurant week menu was a pretty fair price compared to the regular menu. But now having tried the food, I have no problem going back and paying regular prices. You can see the full menu for Restaurant week which had a pretty decent selection. I had the Hanger steak which was delicious and cooked to perfection.  My friend , the birthday girl had the salmon which looked like a painting ! Check out my photo below. So pretty. Dessert we went off the RW menu and I got a special brownie Sundae for the bday girl. Mario was a great server and when we go back I'll make sure I ask for him. He was very attentive and made sure we had everything we needed. I loved that it wasn't too crowded. It's in the Archer Hotel right on 38th Street between 5th and 6th. I'll definitely be back.

The ramen is absolutely delicious, I'd say it's some of the best I've ever had. After writing so many of these reviews it's hard to come up with something unique to say, but all of the components were spot on. Quality nori, perfectly cooked egg, noodles firm but not too, etc.  The spicy gyoza are regular gyoza with a dry spice mix sprinkled on top and are great. But I found the space to be way too cramped. This is one of the smallest restaurants I think I've ever eaten in and the wait can be long. There is no where to wait, they ask you to wait in the vestibule they share with the apartment building above them, which fits two people snugly when no one else is trying to get through. You put your name on a clipboard and they call you, but when there are 4 names and no where to stand but in the freezing cold outside, I'm not sure how this system works. Thankfully we were seated almost right away at a table that didn't have two other tables right on top of either side of it. It's still claustrophobic.  I'd come back, but not if there was a wait. Cash only.

We came here for restaurant week lunch and it was very disappointing overall.I think the service is wonderful and I would give it five stars. For a starter, I had the curried soup and tasted just like an Indian dhaal. It was a little weird to me though as it did not taste like a soup somehow, it was too thick and seemed like a plain curry that would have paired better with rice and I found the flavor to be overly bitter. I tried the ceviche which my friend ordered and the flavor palette was superior to mine except the portion size was tiny. For the entree, I had the pan roasted chicken. I felt it was better than the soup but still left much to the imagination. I mean I imagine chicken to be paired with sides usually. It was a decent chicken and had some sauce but it didn't wow me and I finished all the glaze that came with it in the first few bites and then the second half of the experience, the chicken was dry/unseasoned.My friend had the vegetable risotto, and again, I felt the flavor was stronger for that than the chicken. However, she was not full.Overall, I felt the food was sub par. For example, even the free bread was hard like a rock. I'm a bit perplexed and wonder if they let their quality or menu options slide because it was restaurant week or because it was lunch? Overall it makes me wary to try out Michelin starred restaurants as I fear they may be overhyped as this one was.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience at a Classic NYC Establishment

Last night, our team of 10 had the pleasure of dining at this gem of a restaurant, where the service was nothing short of impressive. With food quality and presentation that were excellent, the establishment beautifully embraced the concept of family-style meals, catering perfectly to larger groups like ours.

The standout dish was the perfectly cooked rib-eye steak, enhanced with a unique bone marrow cream, which can only be described as perfection on a plate. Complementing the steak was a succulent broiled salmon and a rich, flavorful cheese ravioli in a heavenly cream sauce. All dishes were met with unanimous praise from our table.

The ambiance exuded a classic NYC old-school charm that added to the overall experience, making us feel as if we'd stepped back into a more elegant era. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for superb food in an enchanting setting.

Title: Spacious Sophistication at Raku's New Location

My affinity for Raku was reaffirmed at their latest establishment, which not only mirrors the exceptional quality of its sister site but elevates the dining experience with its spacious, modern decor and the added convenience of a bar dining option.

Despite not having a reservation, our wait was a mere ten minutes, thanks to the efficient seating system accessible through Resy. Settling at the bar, we indulged in the chicken tatsuta-age, which delivered a perfect contrast of crispy skin and succulent interior. The udon soup's fresh, chewy noodles were complemented by a well-balanced broth, far from the over-salted pitfalls of many eateries.

The yasai kakiage, however, fell short of expectations. Promised a medley of vegetables, the dish was predominantly tempura onion with scant green bell pepper and eggplant pieces—a minor letdown in an otherwise delightful meal.

Overall, the new Raku location edges out its predecessor with its ample space and reservation system, ensuring a seamless and enjoyable dining experience.

I usually stop by the Smith when in the area but figured to try something new. I had seen Daniel Boulud on tv many times and wanted to check out one of his places. If I was rich I would head to Daniel but I went with the lower end brother of Daniel... Bar Boulud. It is a cool chic restaurant that is bigger than it looks from the outside. They have both booths and table seating. We sat at the table seating in the front. It was pretty slow for lunch which I was surprised about. Maybe the prices scare  people away but it is the upper west side so should be expected. For lunch I went with the yankee burger with fries. It is a 5oz burger and I ordered it medium. When it came out it was a little undercooked but that is better than overcooked. The burger was pretty good overall with all the heavy hitters on it (cheese, pickle, some sort of burger sauce). I could have eaten another one. The fries were also addicting. They are the thin cut ones (my fav) and perfectly fried to have that crunchy yet soft texture. Just the right amount of salt too. My coworker said the salmon club was solid as well. The one negative was that it had 3 slices of bread. I know club sandwiches normally do but it was a little bit of carb overload. They also have a downstairs area for bigger parties with a hallway that is lined with all of their wines. The bathrooms are also downstairs and they are very clean which is always a good sign. I really enjoyed this place and although it is an pricier lunch it definitely had quality to it. Would definitely come back.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Highly Recommended Pasta Spot

Last evening, a friend brought me to a much-praised pasta place with an array of intriguing options. Unfortunately, the bustling, noisy atmosphere and overcrowded seating arrangement started off the experience on the wrong foot, with a tight squeeze just to reach our table.

The real test of patience was the inexplicably long wait for our food—nearly 50 minutes for a simple soup and pasta combo, until a complimentary bread came to our rescue, a much-needed reassurance that we hadn't been forgotten. Thankfully, the tomato soup with croutons and the pasta redeemed the kitchen's timing missteps with their warm, comforting flavors.

A thoughtful touch in their wine service offered three sizes, but the pricing structure gave no incentive to indulge in a larger pour. On the service front, our waiter was the highlight—his friendliness and attention provided a silver lining to the dining experience.

Despite the delicious meal, the drawbacks leave me uncertain about a return visit.

I recently had the chance to enjoy brunch at this local gem for the first time, having been a few times for dinner. Arriving at a surprising busy 2 pm on a Saturday, we were pleased to be seated immediately in a cozy booth. Service throughout our visit was impressively quick.

The highlight for me was discovering their lunch special is a daily offering. As non-drinkers, substituting coffee for alcohol was a delightful option. The Cuban coffee may come in a tiny cup, but it packs a punch—definitely a must-try for caffeine lovers.

Food-wise, the Cubano sandwich was solid, paired nicely with plantain chips. The yellow rice with shredded chicken may have been a modest serving, but it was bursting with flavor.

The restaurant's atmosphere was lively yet comfortable, accentuated by background music that adds to the fun vibe. For those seeking a more vibrant scene, I recommend coming during dinner for the live music experience. Overall, a satisfying visit that continues to cement this spot as a favorite.

Bone-In Pork Belly - soooo good!  Super crispy skin add the crunchiness to the dish. Grilled Prawn - very good and fresh, flavor was great. Manhattan Wings - probably can skip. Sliders - meat was good in flavor Beef Rib - very tender and smoky. Must try! Kings Cut Prime Rib - 30 lbs of meat! A little too much fat parts for me. Smoky cabbage - not as unique as expected. Roasted Brussel Sprout - so yummy and there's blueberry inside, interesting combination. Cocktails are great too

We were here for restaurant week dinner menu, my husband and I both felt satisfied. Overall, amazing food and service. We ordered lobster bisque and wedge salad as appetizers. The beacon in wedge salad was great and matching with blue cheese but we are little disappointed with lobster bisque with light creamy and flavored taste. For entrees, we ordered dry-aged sirloin steak and filet mignon. We loved their steak so much and they were unbelievably tasty and even greater with creamed spinach (extra $7)! In the end, we had cheese cake and chocolate mousse for dessert and it was a good ending. We will definitely come back again for their steak!

TLDR: Tasting menu restaurant from the husband/wife team behind Atoboy. Yes, it is expensive. This is a great restaurant to celebrate a special occasion. Yes, it is worth it. Every damn cent.Booking Atomix was a bit of a challenge, it took me a bit to figure out when the reservations are released, etc. We ultimately booked it 60 days out. Your entire meal/tax/tip must be paid upfront. So, be ready to commit when you book your reservation. This is non-refundable and it is not cheap. Fast forward two months later, we have Atomix for dinner.When we first entered, they weren't ready to seat everyone so we had a couple of drinks at the bar/lounge upstairs. The staff was incredibly knowledgeable and receptive to what our tastes were. When we were finally escorted downstairs to our seats, it felt like we were entering another world. Few restaurants made me feel like I've transcended into a different place, it didn't feel like a restaurant anymore in the traditional sense. It felt not like a meal, more like an experience.We were offered the supplemental white truffles but declined. We eventually did end up getting it on one of our desserts at the end. The server was kind enough to ask chef if this was possible and they accommodated for us.What I love is we were able to pick out our own set of chopsticks which was cool. It felt like a Harry Potter moment.. or just picking your own sake glass if you're not into HP. What I thoroughly enjoyed is the card that came with each course. The theme here is a style of preparation and doing a deep dive into a lot of different aspects of Korean cuisine. The cards are painstakingly detailed. They tell you ever ingredient of the dish, down to the oil base of the sauce, the micro herbs that are there, literally everything. On the opposite side of the card, chef will describe the course and also explain the inspiration for it.As the progression of courses began, there was not a single dish I did not like. Chef's wife was also explaining some of the dishes and she was wonderful to speak with. I'll go into the courses that stood out for me.Course 2 - Hwe: A langoustine tartare with a bit of rice cream around it. So fabulously succulent. If you like langoustine or shellfish for that matter, this is phenomenal. I was literally picking every single morsel off my plate, it was so good.Course 5 - Guk: Confit mushrooms in this delicate mussel broth, mussels on rice.. I love these sets within a set. Course 7 - Gui: Grilled tilefish. The skin was insanely crispy and just bathing in this emulsion of burnt kale oil and sea urchin. Every flake of that fish was just a party you never wanted to end.Course 10 - Husik: The second of the dessert courses. It's hard to really describe what this tasted like. It reminded me of an ice cream crumble if I'm going to oversimplify it. Just imagine the grown up version that's so irresistibly good. Both with and without the truffles, amazing.Undoubtedly one of the best meals I had this year and I'll even say.. one of the best fine dining meals I've ever had. Everything from the ambiance, the service, the attention to detail at every level and of course, the food.Atomix has two Michelin stars and rightfully so. For as expensive as this meal was, not once did I feel like I was gypped. If you're going to venture into this price point, this is what dining at this level should be. Very few restaurants have moved me in the way that Atomix did. I'm literally just thinking of another excuse to come here again.

During my recent visit to the restaurant, I opted for the cold noodles and the potato dish. The cold noodles were quite delicious, although the serving size did not quite match the price point. On the other hand, the potato slices were a letdown – not only were they lacking in flavor, but the $6 price was steep for such a small portion. Despite this, the noodle menu seems promising, and I'm willing to return to sample other noodle varieties.

Was looking for a kosher restaurant on the upper east side, and hummus kitchen fit the bill.  The prices are really good considering that the food is kosher and the food quality is good.  Came with my husband, parents, and in-law's, and everyone really enjoyed the food.  The restaurant accommodated our large stroller.  Service was fast and friendly.  Particularly liked the mezze that we had (beets, cauliflower, and hummus with pita.  Pita was warm and fresh.  Also has the chicken and couscous.  Thought the couscous could have used more flavor, but the chicken was moist and delicious.  Much preferred the chicken in the couscous than the chicken kebab.  I would definitely come back!

Title: Brunch Experience at Rustic Spot Leaves More to Be Desired

My companion and I decided to experience brunch on a late Saturday afternoon at this downstairs, rustic-styled eatery. We were promptly seated in a quaint outdoor area, a casual and welcoming atmosphere setting the scene for our meal.

I chose the steak and eggs, accompanied by sweet potato mash. While the presentation showed care—strips of steak crowned with a sunnyside up egg and a drizzle of chimichurri—the dish faltered in execution. The steak, only four slices, was pinker than my preference and the portion underwhelming. Though not usually a fan of sunnyside up, the egg was a surprising delight, enhancing the steak with its rich yolk.

Unfortunately, the sweet potato mash was a letdown, delivering a bland and soggy texture far from the expected sweetness and firmness. Equally disappointing was the chimichurri sauce, which failed to impart any notable flavor.

Service was adequate, doing little to elevate the overall experience. With a meal that didn't meet expectations and a sense of dissatisfaction lingering, I have no intention of returning.

Have wanted to try the steakhouse for years now. Called for reservations but with a big party scheduled couldn't get 2 in at 5 pm but they were kind enough to put us at Prime right around the corner on 40th Street. ENTRANCE - greeted by 2 people right away. Fairly empty but placed at a nice table nonetheless. The host and hostess were very congenial and propelled a great experience at the start. SERVICE- wow a second to none attentiveness without a doubt. The bus and in particular our waiter RONNIE offered the experience of a lifetime. Only short coming was when the bus began to pour our bottled water he accidentally spilled most of it on the table. The good news is we quickly changed tables. So no harm no foul I guess. MENU - not large and a typical high end steakhouse in NYC. We ordered a few interesting items worth noting.APPETIZERS - I ordered the seared scallops (a Ronnie recommendation) and they were superb. Wife tried the cauliflower side as an appetizer and was pleasantly surprised as to the flavor and taste. ENTREES - no surprise here porterhouse for 2 and couldn't resist. Let me say for an aged steak at least a month. This was tender and easy to cut with a simple non-serrated knife. SIDES - for those new to NY Steakhouses everything is a la cartel but for the things we tried. Really good. The mixed mushrooms are a must. Different types and all flavorful as mushrooms can be lol. We tried the Brussel sprouts and they were really good. Some places try to deep fry whole and that doesn't work. I could tell these were steamed or blanched first so that the deep fry offered a perfect dish. There was an intriguing sauce that kicked it up a notch to quote a culinary legend lol. DESSERT- normally don't get but thanks to YELP had a FREE crepe brûlée. So why not coffee and an after dinner VSOP. Very good ending.VINO - had the Cabernet by the glass. Should have asked but didn't. My bad again. For bar stock it was better than average. BREAD - I'm kind of a snob but I have to mention that the initial table bread was so so and not really  a high end itemPRICE - ok lets get real. A New York steakhouse and 2 people with drinks and a good tip for excellent service the bill was $336. This is a $$$$$ if there was one but worth it if your wallet can handle the pressure. Try and ask for Ronnie. You will be in for a treat he is engaging, interesting stories , professional, and sincere. Who could ask for anything more. Consider it a bucket list check offd

Title: A Singular Hot Pot Experience – Fun for Special Occasions

Review:
I recently had the pleasure of dining at this modern, upscale hot pot restaurant for a birthday celebration and walked away with some mixed feelings, but overall it was a positive experience. Don't come here expecting the best meal of your life, but do expect a solid dining adventure.

The menu offered a wide variety of items, though I missed out on the skewers which were snapped up before I could order. The fresh meats, served in neat rolls, provided generous portions that matched the upscale vibe.

What sets this place apart is the entertainment – karaoke at your table as you dine, which can either be a hilarious addition to your night or a challenging distraction, depending on your multitasking skills.

Be prepared to pay a premium here; our group found it to be on the expensive side, especially with the a la carte menu and the requirement to drop at least $800 for party reservations, reflecting the high-end decor and presumably the New York rent prices.

While I wouldn't classify this as my go-to spot for casual meals, it's an excellent pick for special occasions or when you're in the mood for a fun, interactive hot pot experience without the all-you-can-eat gluttony.

This place was a pleasant surprise as it was within walking distance to our hotel on 8th and 28th. We came for lunch on a Sunday and there was no one inside. I loved it! Food was very good: *Pasta: pappardelle fresche con brasato di coda alla vaccinara ($22, 4 stars) - BRAISED OXTAIL RAGU!! Can you tell I'm excited?! I'm a huge fan of hearty and meaty pasta, and this is it! The pasta is al dente, and the meat sauce very flavorful. This will be even more perfect for a cold or rainy day. *Antipasti: + Highly recommend: Polipetto alla purea di nduja e fave fresche ($20, 5 stars) - DA BEST fried baby octopus I've ever had! I'm pretty sure the octopus was cooked first cuz it was very tender inside but crispy outside. +salsiccia e fagioli all'uccelletto $16 - 3.5 stars - fatty sausage on top of braised cannellini beans.Service was decent, the waiters were both Italians.

The food was good. The steak tacos were a bit chewy but fresh tastingsnd had a different flavor than the fish tacos. Both tasted fresh and were tasty. They were full with filling which is always a good thing.  The guacamole was on point. Full of flavor and chunks of avocado. Mera's Tip:  go for the trio platter

Stopped by on a Thursday night around 7:30 pm and there was a 15 minute wait for a table of 2, so not bad. The ambiance is nice with all the lights.Ordered the roasted duck noodles and the flavor was good, I also tried it with the spicy sauce but preferred it without. I love the wide flat noodles and flavor so I just wish the duck was not dry. So maybe it was a good thing there wasn't a lot of duck? Normally there is more protein in other noodle dishes I've had. I don't eat a lot so I was surprised to finish my dish and still feel a little hungry. So portions are small here! Would recommend ordering appetizers. The Thai tea was not very sweet which I liked but it tasted water downed. I've had better Thai iced teas.Service is great here and the food came out quickly!

Title: A Delightful Indian Culinary Adventure

I recently dined at what is now one of my top Indian restaurant picks in the city, and it was a feast for the senses. The butter chicken here is a masterpiece, boasting a magnificent charred flavor with a medium spice level that's rich in buttery goodness. Even my friend, typically not a chicken fan, was won over by the moist and savory Murg Kesar.

The Palak Aur Tamatar Chaat provided a delicious start to our meal, while the Kosho Mangsho, a standout dish, was absolutely delectable – a must-try for any meat lover. Compliments to our server, Ayesha, whose friendly and welcoming demeanor, paired with her spot-on dish recommendations, added a cheerful touch to our experience.

An added delight was the amuse bouche, which kicked off our meal on a high note. With top-notch service and an inviting atmosphere, this restaurant is one I'll definitely revisit, especially to explore their lunch offerings. A resounding two thumbs up for this gem!

Visited this gem on a chilly Sunday afternoon at 3 pm and was pleased to be seated within minutes. The pork buns are a must-try – absolutely delicious! Also indulged in the Akamaru Modern ramen, which was exceptional. I'm already looking forward to my next visit – this place is a definite favorite!

Great spot to dine but gets crowded really fast. I love coming to a Thai restaurant and they surprise me with authentic tastes and decorations! The service was great and I truly enjoyed everything that we got. Definitely get a curry dish and any of their appetizer Thai crepe dumplings. I also really enjoyed their Thai iced tea!

Thai food is one of my favorite types of food so I was super excited to try out a new place. However, my expectations were quickly met with disappointment. The ambiance was pretty good. It has a dark, intimate vibe to it, which I appreciated for a dinner with friends. We came on a Friday for dinner and were seated immediately. The staff was friendly and attentive, so we never felt neglected. They gave us peanut sauce and some kind of air pop chips (not sure what it was) when we first sat down and our meals didn't take too long to come out. But even with all these good qualities, I was disappointed by the food. I ordered the Bangkok fried rice and asked for it to be very very spicy (I normally order some form of spicy fried rice).
