The rice was not as spicy as I would have liked and everything tasted undercooked. The rice was harder than it should have been, as was the carrots, and the flavor wasn't fully savory. I tried my friend's pad Thai and felt the same way, but she seemed to enjoy it anyway. The prices weren't too bad, but I've had better Thai food for less money.Overall, the restaurant itself was nice because of the vibe and the staff, but the food was subpar in comparison to other places I've tried.

Best lunch money I ever spent! The options here endless! I decided to give the salmon with broccoli and mashed potatoes with gravy a try. The meal was delicious and was the perfect portion. It even came along with a free beverage. Your best bet is to call ahead or order online to avoid the long in-store wait for your meal. It's great that this establishment is located not to far from my workplace. I definitely see myself giving this place another try sometime soon.

I recently dined at a unique communal-style eatery for the first time, using Mealpal to place my order. I opted for the BBQ chicken platter, which boasted an array of sides including dirty rice, creamy mac n cheese, and a spicy coleslaw. The chicken itself was a standout, tender and well-seasoned, while the coleslaw added a nice kick that complemented the meal. The mac n cheese was flavorful, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Despite the slightly bland rice, the meal was satisfying, and the portions were generous. Overall, it was a worthwhile Mealpal experience, and I'm curious enough to return and sample more of their offerings.

Locals and tourists flock to Vanessa's for the extremely cheap and mouth watering dumplings!I found Vanessa's on Yelp on Thanksgiving Day (one of the few places open). Boy, did they come through! This is a must try! The dumplings are so fresh. The outer wrapper is savory and soft and inner meat is served hot and juicy. There will be a long wait and potentially no table to sit at, but if so grab your food to go. This is your next go-to drunk/hangover/comfort food spot.If you haven't tried Vanessa's, you're missing out.

Title: Uneven Experience at a Hospitable Haven

Review:
I would give this restaurant a resounding five stars for service with extra commendations for Lucas and Mina, whose efforts to go the extra mile did not go unnoticed. The staff's attentiveness and warmth were standout features of our dining experience. However, the cuisine didn't quite match the high bar set by the service; the apple fritter with ice cream was merely passable, lacking that wow factor. This spot was a last resort due to its availability, which somewhat tempers my disappointment in the culinary offerings. Overall, exceptional service outshines the average fare.

As a fan of all Stephen Starr restaurants, I had been meaning to stop by for a while, and finally made it here with my boyfriend for Valentine's Day. We had the Valentine's Day tasting menu, and while I'm usually pretty picky with prix fix menus, this one pretty much had everything I would've ordered for myself anyway! I was impressed right away upon entering the restaurant, which is in the new Equinox hotel. The view is great, the music isn't overpowering, and the restaurant was busy yet not overly packed. Definitely would be back in the summer to check out the outdoor terrace!The first course was the marinated diver scallops - I love pretty much all scallops, and these were super light and fresh! I probably finished this in just a few bites - yum!The next course was the squid ink pasta. I'm a carb lover, so I'd be sold on any pasta, but the squid ink sauce and the al dente pasta was a delicious mix. I'd definitely order this again, too.For my main course, I had the Atlantic Cod. I like all fish, more or less, but a lot of them often blend together without much differentiation. This cod, however, easily could have been the best cod I've ever tasted!!Finally for dessert, I had the raspberry white chocolate. I love raspberries and I love white chocolate, and this dessert was a great way to end the meal. I also liked how this dessert wasn't too heavy.Overall, I was very impressed with both the ambiance and the high quality of the food. This spot has earned a spot in our go-to dinner rotation!

Title: Hoppy Times at the Bunny Bistro!

Review:

I recently visited this delightful restaurant with friends and had an amazing experience. The service was impeccable with a team of friendly staff, and the bunnies, ever so charming, readily posed for photos with us, adding a unique and memorable twist to our visit. Standout dishes included a flavorful salmon/avocado roll, a succulent shrimp appetizer, and a perfectly cooked Salmon entree that left us savoring each bite.

The Bunny Bistro is the perfect spot for groups or couples looking for a lively and entertaining dining experience. On our second visit, which was on a Friday night, the venue had an energetic vibe that only added to the fun. Bunny Lauren, with her delightful charm, gave us a tour and her helpful, friendly demeanor made her our favorite bunny of the evening.

Our friends, who were first-timers, were thoroughly impressed. The Bunny Bistro has certainly earned a spot on our list of frequent go-to places. Can't wait for our next hop in!

PURCHASED: Chicken BurgerTOTAL: $11.50PROS:+delicious: The bun was glazed. That's pretty nice and tasty. CONS:-little pricey: Little pricey for the portion size. I am an overweight American and prefer my sandwich to be a little bigger. IMPRESSION:Located within a food court. The portion size seemed small for $11.50. So, after I ate this delicious creation, I went 2 blocks away to another restaurant where I continued to eat like an overweight (BMI greater than 30) American male.

Let me start off by saying my review for this place is a bit biased, as a celiac, because their gluten-free menu and separate preparation makes me very grateful.That said, my brunch burgers was a bit charred and my shoestring fries a bit too burnt. (Partly my fault as I asked for medium well after recently reading about parasites in beef, but I should've specified to cook through, not to burn the outside lol)The cappuccino is great, the service is fantastic, and the ambiance and location hard to beat. So I absolutely will be back, to try a different menu item, since my burger was so charred I ate only 1/3... but next time.

Title: Cozy Spot with Service Hiccups

My experience at the quaint eatery last Sunday evening was a mixed bag. Although my friend and I held a 6:30 PM reservation and were promptly seated upon arrival, we found ourselves at a rather cramped table, a testament to the restaurant’s aim to maximize dining space.

The service kicked off on the right foot with our attentive waitress bringing us water, but her lack of specific menu recommendations left us to our own devices. Our choice, the hummus with fluffy pita bread, was a culinary delight despite the puzzlingly long wait for it to arrive.

Equally perplexing was the wait time for our main courses, especially when noticing that diners who arrived after us were served before us. I indulged in the shakshuka, which was satisfying once it arrived with its accompanying Israeli salad. However, the side bread, an essential component of the dish, only made an appearance post-reminder.

My companion enjoyed her arayes and noted they were "pretty good." A highlight worth mentioning is their all-day breakfast service, which is always a welcome feature.

In summary, while the meal itself was decent, the lengthy waits and service oversights marred an otherwise enjoyable dining experience.

Absolutely amazing!! The service, the food and the ambiance were all great! The coconut rice was phenomenal - almost like it was glazed with sweetness and fragrance but not too sweet or overwhelming. My favorites were the khao soi which was great with the crispy noodles with friend noodles and the green papaya salad which was so fresh. I think the sigsig and pork adobo were also so great and would highly recommend!

Title: A Szechuan Delight Not to Miss

If you're a connoisseur of authentic Szechuan cuisine and don't shy away from some spice, this culinary gem is a must-visit on your next trip to NYC. Every dish we tried was a burst of flavor that delighted the senses — a true testament to the authenticity and quality that this place prides itself on.

Be warned, though: its popularity is apparent with the inevitable long lines. But take it from a fellow spicy food lover – the wait is a small price to pay for the exceptional dining experience that awaits you. I'm already planning my next visit!

I visited this restaurant during restaurant week and had a satisfactory experience. The service left a bit to be desired; our waitress lacked warmth and enthusiasm. The menu offerings were decent; I started with the dumplings, which I was unable to have steamed to my preference due to the chef's restrictions. For my main, I chose the hot stone bibimbap with bulgogi beef. The dish was nicely prepared, with the beef being flavorful and the stone hot enough to crisp the rice – a delightful touch. However, the beef portion could have been more generous. Although the ambiance was pleasant and the decor tastefully understated, I found the pricing on the steep side, particularly for the portion sizes. Overall, it was a fair experience, but there's room for improvement in both service and value.

This place has great food & Beautiful rooftop! Such a great escape from a work day! Or any time of the day!.They have a lunch prefix durning lunch Where you get a choice of an appetizer & a main for $18. Then you can add on a Classic margarita for only $1, exclusive to lunch prix fixe. This deal is def worry the price & taste..I got the sweet corn salad which had Sweet corn off the Cobb with Toasted Corn Nuts, Chile Powder & Lime& the CHEESEBURGER TACOS also for with a margarita for $1..Words cannot describe how mouth wateringly delicious the sweet corn salad was. I've had sweet corn salads before which is a staple to have when having tacos but this is a whole new ball game!!! It's pretty much a deconstructed ELOTE on a plate! The toasted nuts give the corn a nice crunch while the chili powder & lime zest up the corn, bringing out the best flavor in town! I can eat this all day! My mouth is watering just thinking about it

Title: A Budget-Friendly Bite in the City

Whenever I visit the city, I make it a point to stop by this particular Thai spot. The food is generally good, though at times it may lack a punch of flavor. What stands out is the portion size; it's perfect for a hearty appetite, and those with lighter cravings could easily share a dish.

The restaurant offers two pre-fixe menus that are ideal for tourists looking for value—both include an appetizer, entree, and dessert, with one offering a broader selection of main courses. This option is not only economical but also gives a well-rounded taste of what the kitchen has to offer.

Service here is brisk and attentive, ensuring a pleasant dining experience. However, the drink menu might disappoint if you're after a flavorsome cocktail. I've found them to be rather bland in both taste and alcohol content—the Mango Fizz, notably, missed the expected mango punch and leaned towards the sour side. On a positive note, their non-alcoholic offerings, like the Thai iced tea, are consistently delightful.

In summary, this spot is a gem for those seeking a quick, wallet-friendly Thai meal without sacrificing service.

Title: A Must-Visit Mac & Cheese Haven in NY

Every trip to New York isn't complete without a stop (or two) at this Mac & Cheese paradise. The ordering process is a breeze with their quick kiosk system, where you can customize your dish to your heart's content. I opted for the traditional Mac & Cheese, jazzed up with seasoned ground beef, jalapeños, and Everett's bread crumbs - a combination that was absolutely scrumptious. Portions are spot-on for a satisfying lunch. For any Mac & Cheese aficionado, this place is a dream; don't be afraid to be bold with your choices, the possibilities are endless, and there's no going wrong here. Highly recommended!

Top Thai Greenwich wias an excellent surprise.  I travel frequently to Thailand so I am always hesitant to try new Thai restaurants in the US.  I am typically disappointed by the US style of preparation.  This was not the case with this restaurant.   The restaurant is quite small with only 10-12 tables.  The staff is all Thai and the service was excellent.  We tried a few starters including the chicken satay.  They were all perfect.  The main courses which included a noodle dish and a fried rice dish were all prepared to the same taste as you would find in a Bangkok restaurant.  We also enjoyed that they offer their Happy Hour drink prices throughout dinner.  I am looking forward to my next visit to Top Thai.

When you walk in you're immediately hit with this amazing aroma coming from the kitchen. Whewwww! Okay okay, lol. We had mojitos which were great but then we were asked if we wanted quac and salsa as a starter...sure we said. Okay guys, I can stamp this place as having the BEST guac I've EVER had. Yes, I said it. I've never had guacamole that was so well seasoned. By the time we were done we ordered another one, that good lol. I will certainly be back. Everything else was delicious as well but the guac was the shining star

I've been to Upland twice now, both for work dinners. The service is always exceptional, and the food is delicious. The restaurant atmosphere is like an upscale brasserie, with warm, low lights and shelf-lined walls full of bottles of wine and pickled lemons. Both of my meals featured a tasting menu, so I got to sample multiple different appetizers, mains, and desserts. Every single one of the plates has been delicious. Notable favorites: Roasted Senat Chicken (super juicy chicken, roasted swiss chard, beets, onion, labneh)Angus Skirt Steak (nicely grilled steak with garlic and onions)Salmon (tender salmon, hard-boiled egg, spinach, and artichoke)Smoked Jimmy Nardello PeppersChocolate Cake Service was very attentive to our private event, and they kept our wine glasses regularly filled without prompting. Would be happy to come here again any day.

Gimmicky but I liked the concept. Good ramen, and a place for solo diners to feel a little less awkward. Pricey for what is is, but an interesting experience! I could have gone with a little more spice, but the recommend ramen was a good start.

This place is okay. Hookah is super strong, I was very dizzy and light headed. Food was good, but I mean look at my portion, it looks like someone ate some of my fries! We all checked in and it said we would get a free glass of wine.... which was never given to us Wish my wrap had more sauce also

Atmosphere: It was a bit odd getting to the restaurant. We had to go through some type of store and then downstairs to get to the seating area. We went at around 3:30 pm, so it was pretty empty. Service: Service was good. We had a very friendly waiter!Food: We ordered the bulgogi ddukbokki. It was our first time trying bulgogi ddukbokki, so we weren't sure what to expect. The portion was on the smaller side for a $15 dish. The beef and tteok quality was okay; the highlight was the sauce.Overall: Based on one dish, this seems to be a decent Korean restaurant. Because of the prices and food quality, this wouldn't be our first choice for Korean food, but we can't complain too much about our experience.

Title: A Cozy Spot with Great Food and Vibes

My experience at this eatery was a delightful surprise. With drink prices that didn't break the bank, I enjoyed a refreshingly cold beer alongside a scrumptious meal. The ambiance whisked me away to an old Irish pub, buzzing with a blend of locals and tourists, all unwinding after a long day—perfect for a Monday evening, especially before catching the ferry.

The pastrami Reuben sandwich was a standout; expertly prepared, every bite was a delight. Meanwhile, my companions raved about the whiskey chicken sandwich. It looked so appetizing that I regretted not being able to snag a taste myself. If you're in search of a place with a warm atmosphere, delicious food, and well-priced drinks, look no further.

Came here on Friday night after work (5:15pm) for dinner by myself. Got seated at the bar quickly. Place looks beautiful like all the pictures. There are stairs leading upstair (to another floor of more seatings?). Looks very lovely. Menu has 2 sections- traditional classic americanize thai dishes and their local specialty named "royal" thai dishes which looks amazing but so much seafood that I'm allergic to. I stuck with the classic thai dishes; curry chicken puff for appetizers and beef panang curry for my main entree. This panang curry is different as it have sweet potatoes in it (looks like sliced potatoes like fry form). The sweet potatoes help mellow the spiciness for those that can't handle it. I love spicy and could still taste it even with the sweet potatoes. Everything was yummy. I wish I could have order something from the Royal thai section; perhaps if they make it with beef/chicken/pork then I would be fine.

Probably a good spot if you need more space for a larger group and don't have a ton of lead time before the event, (particularly if a corporate event and you're mostly ordering finger foods, apps or desserts). The Wilson is spacious, with an "outdoor" area (currently walled in with heat lamps above guests - that's what gives all the photos I shared a red tint) and a downstairs space. Design aesthetic is a little misc/eccentric (there's a framed picture of "Wilson" from the movie castaway with Tom Hanks), but overall imparts a simultaneously warm/rustic but clean feel (I like the wood floors in the main area and the white tiling). Modern rustic? Who knows- but I'm generally a fan. Music is also not too loud so you can actually hear your friends talk without shouting - underrated pro (unlike most other spots I've visited recently in the city). Service was great but not sure if it's just because the restaurant was pretty empty Sunday evening (we were the only group there for awhile but it was Oscars night so many people may have been home or at a friend's). We were able to make a same day reservation online for 7 and we obviously didn't need the resi. From a food perspective - the fried apps we got were all solid. Fries, avocado fries, burrata. The cauliflower was not crispy though despite the name and was a little salty. Desserts were, in my opinion, the main highlight of the night. Not all made equal though (some better than others). My favorite was the carrot cake in a jar for two- but try one of the others if you're not a fan of dense/sweeter desserts.The entrees were all disappointing and is the primary driver of the 3 star rating. If there were some solid options in our orders I would have upped it to a four but sadly all of it was mediocre to way too salty. Our group tried the salmon, seared tuna (more like well done tuna steak - sesame vinaigrette was tasty though), brick chicken (looked good but too salty), crab carbonara, hanger steak (probably the best of the bunch but by no means great)... The worst was definitely the carbonara- didn't remind us of carbonara at all - was super salty and soggy/way too wet.

Let's start with the good staff. Service: from the door of this cute, modern restaurant design is very welcoming and warm. The Bar tender smiled from behind the bar, the host, who greeted us was a jolly kind of guy. We had reservation but we happened to be there about  1/2 hr earlier. He gladly accommodated. He than brought in the drinks menu. NICE! Very interesting cocktails. Can't remember the name of the cocktail I had, but it was with grapefruit liquor and Prosecco.. it was lightly sweet,  citrusy and of course bubbly due to the Prosecco. Delicious.We then ordered the appetizer as a main dish (the offered to make it larger) - Risotto Langostino and the Tomahawk. The risotto was presented in a very large plate which made it look unattractive, almost like a porridge over a flat dish, with few pieces of langostino on it and the rest of it on the side. It missed the creamy, rich flavor I know and love and no one offered to shave some Parmigiana over it. The Tomahawk - we asked it to be medium-rare it was made medium, but otherwise was tasty and tender! We ordered two glasses of Barolo to accompany the meal. The wine was great, really good and again, the host was wonderful in assisting us choosing the wine. For dessert we ordered tiramisu which was delicious, creamy, but not heavy or too sweet. An absolute winner. The host treated us for a dessert wine which was unexpected but wonderfully appreciated. Overall, we enjoyed the ambiance, the service, but we felt it was a bit overpriced ($250 before tip) for the food we had. Culinary wise, it wasn't the experience I wished for. So... if we come back, it is bc of the service! Maybe I'll give the chef another chance, maybe he had an "off day", we all do, sometimes.

Title: A Taco Haven That Hits the Spot - Every Time!

I recently stumbled upon this gem while scouting for a venue, and it's safe to say it's now top of my list for happy hours, quick bites, and irresistible tacos. Just this week, I found myself here twice, lured by their reasonably priced, mouth-watering offerings.

This spacious eatery knows how to dish out rapid, fresh fare, and believe me, their in-house chips and tortillas are the real deal. Kick things off with their corn esquites, a tantalizing mix of sweet corn, cotija, and smoky morita mayo with a kick of chili pequin. It's a spicy sensation so good I couldn't resist slathering it on my tacos.

The guacamole con totopos keeps it simple and sublime, while the al pastor taco is a slice of Mexico with its perfectly marinated pork and a touch of roasted pineapple. The acapulco shrimp taco is yet another hit, though you might want the chile salsa on the side if your spice tolerance is like mine. Do not pass up on the baja crispy fish taco; this is a bite of California sunshine that's sure to transport you to the west coast with every bite.

Vegetarians, rejoice with the black bean and sweet potato taco—a surprising favorite even for a carnivore like me. On the lighter side, the tuna tostada offers a flavorful zest, while the avocado tostada perfectly replaces the shared guac experience with its flavorful combo over a black bean spread.

For those in favor of cheesy goodness, both the gallo and el gobernador quesadillas will not disappoint, especially with the shrimp variant for seafood lovers. Wash it all down with an agua sandia, a refreshing watermelon and lime blend that's the perfect foil to the flavorful food.

In conclusion, this place is a no-brainer for fantastic eats at great prices, with a speediness that makes any visit a pleasure. It's rapidly become our go-to spot for those indecisive nights without reservations. A must-try for any taco enthusiast!

Went to Beetle House on a rainy Friday night. I don't have the needed obsession to love this place like many of the guests, but they really did an excellent job in bringing this Burton-esque experience to life.Quality: I knew very little about Beetle House before arriving. I assumed it was a bar, but it actually is a full sit down experience restaurant, with just a small bar at the front. Reservations are needed for a table, so we just hung out at the bar. The drinks are full of movie references and almost all of them arriving bubbling and smoking. They are all extremely sweet with odd liquor choices. Fireball, sour apple, and schnapps are all over the the menu. I had Edward's Lemonade, an old fashioned style drink, but from the first sip I felt my teeth aching. Luckily they had some beers too, and since they were finishing the keg, one was on special for $5. As a snack we shared the Buffalo Fries, which were fine to go with drinks. The menu is really set up as prix fixe, so I would recommend committing to a full meal or eating elsewhereQuantity: The cocktails were a fair size and the Buffalo Fries was perfect to share.Value: $12-$14 for Cocktails. $10 for Buffalo Fries. Cash only at the bar.Ambiance: Beetle House is a theme bar built around the works of Tim Burton. It sits in the East Village of Manhattan, and from the outside seems like many other bars in the area. Inside however, you are transported into some combination of Beetlejuice, Nightmare Before Christmas, and Edward Scissorhands. Halloween decorations everywhere, paintings and art of Burton creations, and the gravestone from Beetlejuice as a centerpiece of the bar. The music fits the mood with goth and alternative rock, with the occasional mix of a Burton movie sing-a-long. During our visit there were also Lock and Shock characters running around a quick Beetlejuice appearance.Crowd: This is a place was created for fanatics of Tim Burton and all things halloween. And that was the majority of the guests. Many dressed up and eagerly waited for a chance to sing along to movie songs. Service: Everyone working at the bar really buys into the theme. The bartenders were excellent and love talking about films and music. And the characters that run around seemed to be having as much fun as the customers interacting with them.Parking: Extremely limited street parking in the area.

Shabu shabu is a common cooking form in Japan, but not very typical here in New York. Shabushabu Macoron is the world's only shabu shabu omakase restaurant. The chef visited many shabu shabu restaurants in Japan studying different styles and techniques. She has perfected a style all her own using on the best ingredients, she not typical to shabu shabu. Shabushabu Macoron is a wonderful experience and while completely Japanese, it is one that you can only find on the Lower East Side. If you can set a reservation be sure to go.

I'm a huge Indian food fan, and like most other Indian restaurants this place has a lunch buffet for $10.95 which is a pretty sweet deal. Especially if you are looking to try different plates of Indian food and not willing to buy whole entrees. I went into this restaurant because I was craving masala dosa and I knew Channai Gargen had a variety of masala dosa options. I ordered the traditional masala dosa with regular potato filling. The Dosa came out quick so I was happy, but there wasn't much potato filling whichI was disappointed about. The Dosa to potato filling portion was very unequal which is the reason why I docked a star from my rating. If a restaurant is serving a huge dosa, they should make the potato filling about the same. Ask for extra for filling if you're ordering a masala dosa!

Title: A Sustainable Italian Feast at Mille Nonne

I’ve found a rare gem that marries sustainability with mouthwatering Italian cuisine – Mille Nonne. This delightful spot transforms classic Italian fare by infusing it with a unique twist, offering a variety of organic vegan/vegetarian choices alongside locally sourced ingredients. Their commitment to quality and fast service is akin to fine dining in the guise of a food stand’s convenience.

The owner, a sweetheart, passionately shared their vision of upscale, accessible dining. His enthusiasm is well-founded, as the turkey lasagna was nothing short of fantastic – a definite must-try. The turkey quinoa meatballs stood out too, perfectly balanced with a tangy dressing and fresh arugula. For those with a sweet tooth, their panna cotta with caramelized oranges is a blissful end to the meal.

Vegetarians aren’t left out, with the veggie lasagna and pesto gnocchi both vying for top spot. And don't miss out on their lemonade – an unexpectedly delightful fusion of fresh apple and orange flavors. Mille Nonne is setting a new standard for conscientious yet indulgent dining.

Title: A Hit-or-Miss Bottomless Brunch Experience

My friends and I opted for a birthday brunch at this establishment, enticed by the promise of bottomless food and drinks. The $49 for a two-hour window seemed reasonable, though beware the clock starts ticking from your reservation time. Arriving at 11:30 AM on a Saturday, we were greeted by an expansive yet quiet space.

The variety on the menu was impressive, but the execution was inconsistent. Notably, we received several items we hadn't ordered. The Shrimp Ceviche was underwhelming, heavy on the fruit and light on the shrimp. The Angry Zengo and Citrus Cured Salmon Rolls were decent, but reminiscent of buffet fare.

Unexpected hits included the Salted Edamame and Thai Chicken Empanadas—both were delicious surprises. The Peking Duck and Egg Buns didn't quite hit the mark, nor did the Japanese Angus Beef Meatball. In contrast, the Achiote Hoisin Pork Arepas, Crispy Tofu, Crispy Potato, and Fish Chicharron were delightful finds. The Mexican Chocolate Waffles ended on a strong, flavorful note.

The drink selection was a high point, with the Lychee and Mango Mimosas, along with the Sake Sangria, delivering on strength and taste.

In summary, while not a complete letdown, the brunch experience was a mix of hits and misses, especially considering the price point. The drinks were a win, but the inconsistency in food quality makes it unlikely for me to return, given the better-valued brunch spots I know.

I came here for the cap'n crunch nuggets, but unfortunately they didn't offer them vegan but that's okay because they had other vegan options.I love how they're tech savvy. You can order on an IPad as long as you're paying with card and the checkout process is pretty easy. If you're paying with cash you'd have to talk to a human. I got the regs vegan paired with honey mustard which tasted really good and their cajun fries were awesome. They offer water in plastic cups right next to the counter. My friend said the buffalo nuggets tasted cold and old like they were cooked a while ago and just reheated.We had to stand and eat. There's not too much seating and the place is usually pretty full.

I accidentally found this 3-month-new establishment when I was searching for a different kind of rice rolls. Thanks to the photos on Yelp, I realized this place serves a totally different kind of rice rolls, the Taiwanese kind.  "Rice roll" is really a misnomer and confuses with the Cantonese dim sum rice rolls and the Japanese maki rice rolls. Per its Chinese name and menu, it's really rice balls (Onigiri) which I grew up eating in Taiwan. Instead of sticky gluttonous rice, they raise it up a notch and used the healthful purple rice and wrapped with a sheet of seaweed. And they offered 15 different varieties of fillings instead of the traditional pork floss and pickled veggie, effectively elevating a supposedly humble food into something of a delicacy.It was really hard to pick among the 15 different varieties and it's not shareable. So we all (safely) picked the Special, which is the closest to the traditional onigiri with pork floss in it. There was no one else at the time, yet it took a good 10-15 minutes to get our order. Not sure if it was because it was too early in the morning and they hadn't got all of their ducks lined up, but be prepared to wait. I would call ahead next time.Now the the rice ball looks small but it's filling and satisfying. For me it also brought back a little nostalgia from my childhood, and per the establishment's Chinese name, Nuan Xin (暖心), heart-warming.  If you start in the city early and nothing but bakeries are open, or if you are headed to Central Park or hiking somewhere, I would definitely recommend that you give this place a try.  These rice balls are tasty and  super convenient as a food on the go.

Had a delightful lunch at this spacious eatery – an ideal spot for a quick yet relaxing meal. A special nod to their eco-friendly touch with non-plastic salad bowls. Would recommend for a satisfying midday dine.

Its truly tragic how poor service and disgruntled and unhealthy employees can truly take a wonderful experience with amazing food and toss things out the window. This was our situation last week (Late February 2020) - Around 7:30/8PM. I didn't appreciate the sarcasm from the host; we arrived 15 minutes early - to find an empty restaurant - only to be mocked by the host; Sorry - didn't appreciate your joke. From there, things went just down hill. Waitress was terribly disgruntled and could not make it more obvious that working that evening was the last thing she wanted to do. Thanks for making me feel stupid and repeating my drink over again - "Pina Colada - Extra Frosty".More importantly - the food was excellent; very well crafted and delicious; - ingredients were very fresh. Kudos to the Bar Tender who made me a tasty and frosty Pina Colada. Sad that the delivery and service was so poor; truly left a bad taste in our mouths - we won't be back. Killed my appetite and saddened me.I can confirm, previous comments - portions are rather skimpy. That's disappointing. Pleaded many times for more tortilla chips - they never came. Nobody cared!In short - I don't suggest this place. It tends to attract a rather irritating crowd. I got a kick out of the countless French tourists crowding the bar, speaking French in such a tone as to be obnoxious. It was a lovely touch. Hence - this is likely why staff are conditioned to act in such a away - Looks like I found my answer. A little too European for my liking. Dear Management - Feel free to reach out to me. Don't bother offering me any free meals or such the like. I don't think its appropriate to mention the waitress's name - but, I was sure glad that it said it on the receipt. In summary; - Yelpers deserve better; - Food can be great - poor service and poor attitude from staff truly took things down a notch. Stand up for yourself and avoid!

Vanessa's Dumpling House Review:

Despite some negative chatter, Vanessa's Dumpling House in NYC defies the usual trade-off between hype, quality, and price. The deal of getting four hearty dumplings for a mere $2 seems almost too good to be true in the city. While you might have to navigate a bit of a wait during peak times due to its simple counter-order system, the efficiency of receiving a numbered slip keeps things organized even when it's bustling.

Payment is convenient enough, with cards accepted for orders over $10. Though limited, the indoor seating is a plus, and free sauces add a nice touch to the savory offerings. For takeout, the food is smartly packed in plastic clamshells, ensuring your meal arrives home intact.

The menu diversity tempts exploration, but sticking to the dumplings is my recommendation. The pork buns, at 3 for $2, are somewhat of a letdown—too doughy and overly salty for my taste.

A minor setback is the availability of items; visiting later in the evening might mean they've run out of some options.

In summary, with its unbeatable prices and solid dumplings, Vanessa's has earned its spot as a must-visit eatery in NYC, netting a solid four stars from me. Just maybe skip the pork buns and plan your visit timing accordingly.

Title: Cozy Spot for Happy Hour with Room for Improvement

I recently visited this restaurant for Happy Hour and I'd rate it a solid 3.5. I chose it as a convenient spot for a friend visiting from out of town, anticipating a good time. We arrived to a bit of confusion - my friend was turned away prior to Happy Hour and had to wait outside before we could secure our spot.

Luckily, we were first in line when the time came, directed to comfy seating near the bar where the Happy Hour magic happens. A friendly waiter caught our attention immediately, and we dove into the menu, starting off with an $8 margarita that was quite enjoyable.

For food, we decided on the Guacamole with chips and the street corn nachos. The guacamole won us over, fresh and flavorful, but the nachos fell short. Labeled as 'street corn,' I was expecting a bold char of corn with a generous sprinkle of cheese but, sadly, this was not the case.

However, the ambiance and staff were the highlights. With attentive and polite service, and a nice atmosphere, these aspects did not disappoint.

I'm open to giving this place another try, perhaps to sample something new from their menu.

I have been waiting to try this place for years now. The history this restaurant holds is gold and the food reviews has just been nothing but great. Finally had a chance to visit while attending the US Open. Sitting outside enjoying the great weather and some old guy singing down the street was just what I expected. I ordered the pasta with clam sauce and clams. So so good and fresh. As an appetizer order a few meatballs with marinara sauce. Can't go wrong with that It was truly delicious and you need to try it if you're considering

If you're looking for a nice and fancy place to take your date on a Friday night, you're at the wrong place. This place is where you come with your group of friends on a random Wednesday night to get wasted for someone's birthday. This place has cheap (like $4 cheap) drinks and shots. It's dark, it's loud and it's kind of sticky (from all the spilled drinks).Regardless of all those things, I LOVE coming here. It's a great place to be loud with your friends. If you want to try an assortment of drinks for cheap, you can choose from a lengthy list. They do not make you any custom drinks, so don't even bother asking. Their drinks are strong and if the mixed drinks don't mess you up, just take a $3 shot.I generally stick with the mojito or the Long Island iced tea but I have tried many of the other ones. They're all pretty good. My guy friends tend to like the Adios M (previously known as Adios Motherf*cker). Most likely because of the name and the bright blue coloring of it. Don't expect a drink with lots of layers of flavoring, they are only $6.For the food, I don't suggest getting anything that is not fried. I tried one of their dinner combos a few years ago and I was super disappointed. I can barely remember it because it lacked so much in flavor that I tried to throw the memory out. My favorites are the cajun fries and the mushroom quesadilla. Usually we order a basket of the fries and keep ordering as we go on into the night. They are thin and coated in the cajun powder. So good! The mushroom quesadilla is a good option for your vegetarian friends. You can share the slices or eat the whole thing if you want. The fried calamari is okay, not my favorite but I'll eat it if it's in front of me.Overall, a great place to come with friends if you want to get drunk. I come here probably like once a month or so with friends to catch up and drink. It's only a few blocks away from the 8th Street train station so it's really easy to get to.

This is another huge brunch place. Kinda like the smiths. This is beautiful and spacious. They are clean and busy on the weekend. They have waiting for Weeknd. They have varieties of options. Food was okay, something was off with the flavor and funny taste. We didn't try drinks. Anyways would love to go again.

If you love chocolate, this place is for you. But be prepared, everything is super rich! They overload the items with chocolate sauce and it gets to be filling super fast. We got the waffles and crepes and loved it but couldn't finish it all. Definitely share if you can!

honestly, not my style of pizza.do note that prince street is not known for the typical NY thin slice pizza.they are known for their square slice which is thick, extremely heavy and greasy. its incredibly hard to eat more than 2 slices even for someone who loves pizza like me.so be careful ordering more than than a few slices, regardless of how hungry you are. trust me. you won't be able to finish it.

Title: Pricy Yet Welcoming - A Mixed Dining Experience

I recently dined at a bustling restaurant where the service shined as brightly as the extensive wine list. The staff's impeccable attention made us feel incredibly welcome from the moment we stepped in. While the experience was overall pleasant, the steep prices cast a shadow on the meal, particularly considering the typically modest cost of the dishes served.

The culinary highlight of the evening was undoubtedly the Jerusalem Bagel, the Eggplant Carpaccio, and the Peanut Butter Tart - each dish crafted to a standard that justifies the establishment's popularity. Unfortunately, the rest of the menu failed to leave a lasting impression, fading into the background of an otherwise memorable evening.

Despite the hit to the wallet, the restaurant's atmosphere and select exceptional dishes make it worth a visit, but perhaps only for those special occasions when you're feeling a bit more indulgent. 3/5 stars.

I remember going to this restaurant many years ago when I 1st moved to New York and it was pretty solid. When I saw them on Mealpal I decided to take advantage of a bit of nostalgia. The meal was not ready when I got there but it's OK because the people are nice. But when I open my meal I noticed it was a completely entree ordered than what was supposed to get. Shrimp and broccoli turned into shrimp fried rice. When I asked could regular egg roll be a spring roll, she stated no substitutions.  You changed my who dish! Go figure. When I opened it I notice it had little black pieces of something on top maybe about 5 or 6 pieces. I don't know what it was but I flicked them out. A quality is still the same pretty decent.

Delicious, satisfying food with great attention to detail! I tried this place for the first time via Caviar. I got the vegetarian bibimbap, which was outstanding. A rainbow of delicious vegetables, each more savory and flavorful than the last. The takeout box was so jam-packed with delightful veggies that I wasn't sure if there was any rice at the bottom, but trust me, there is. I also got the black sesame tofu plate, which comes as a block of cold tofu seasoned with black sesame dressing, and topped with slivers of fried parsnip and beet that were crunchy and tasty. An interesting dish, but probably not good enough to get again. I loved that they also included a little box of four sides with my order. Mine were Korean potato salad (slightly sweet mashed potatoes with crunchy onion), kimchi, savory dried seaweed (excellent sprinkled on top of the bibimbap), and dried slices of a root vegetable.

Title: A Culinary Delight Before Flight

As my go-to spot before heading back to the airport, this restaurant never fails to elevate my mood. Today, the tuna tartar was an impeccable start, a fresh and flavorful precursor to the main attraction – the mussels. These succulent delights, swimming in their savory broth, were a highlight indeed. Kudos to the dedicated staff who consistently deliver such culinary excellence. A heartfelt thank you for making every visit memorable. Highly recommended for any traveler seeking a final taste of bliss before departure.

A late lunch/early dinner before the Blue Man Group show...we had the 3 cheese platter (chef's choice) along with an order of Coppa to start.  They were served with a truffle honey, spicy apricots and sweet cherries as dipping sauces.  The cheeses (2 hard, 1 soft) were all tasty, not overpowering and the Coppa was sliced very thin and went well with all of the above.For my main I had the Pescatore (steamed clams, baby octopus, mussels, n'duja brodo for $18)  - each item was cooked properly, nothing overcooked, nothing under...and overall tasty plate.My wife had the Bucatini alla Pastora (tomato, guanciale, smoked ricotta for $15).  The flavors were wonderful, the smokey ricotta and the guanciale paired perfectly together.  Her only compliant (and since I finished her portion, I'd agree) the pasta was slightly under cooked.I even had a bite of the "kids pizza" and it was tasty too...my kids shared a 12" pie and ate it all (minus the bite I stole!)

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience with Top-Notch Service

I visited this charming little gem of a restaurant recently and was met with exceptional service. The staff here not only serve with a smile but are eager to assist, thoroughly addressing all inquiries with expertise and bonus tips.

I indulged in the rice and peas paired with pumpkin stew - a decision I don't regret despite the menu being slightly pricier than average. The meal stood out for its freshness and well-balanced flavors, a welcome change from the over-salted fare typically encountered elsewhere.

This hole-in-the-wall spot left a lasting impression, and I'm eager to return and sample more from their kitchen. For those considering a visit, my advice: Enjoy, stay healthy, and happy Yelping!

Title: A Slurp-Worthy Experience at Ivan's Slurp Shop

I recently ventured into Ivan's Slurp Shop, a gem tucked inside an upscale food court, without much expertise in the realm of ramen but left quite impressed. The service truly shone, with our server being not only knowledgeable about the menu but also incredibly friendly. His recommendations, including the triple garlic ramen—a savory option with less broth—were spot-on.

Despite chatter about skimpy portions, my experience was contrary: the servings were generous, leaving me unable to polish off my bowl. My boyfriend enjoyed the daily special, complete with a pastrami bun that was simply delicious (a bite was enough to make me jealous I didn't order my own).

Our meal, including a custom ramen bowl with additional toppings, was reasonably priced at about $20. The beverage selections, which ranged from lemonades to teas, complemented the flavorsome food and the server's willingness to offer samples was a thoughtful touch.

All in all, Ivan's Slurp Shop proved to be a delightful spot for a ramen novice like me, and I'm thankful to Ivan for a satisfying and scrumptious dining experience.

PURCHASED: All-you-can-eat and drink College Football Championship Special TOTAL: ~$30PROS:+ All-you-can-eat: Mouth-watering sliders and wings (BBQ, Teriyaki or original). Off menu items are extra. You are limited to certain beer (e.g., Coor's Light, Budweiser--the light beers). + Not overly crowded: It wasn't too crowded in late-Fall 2019. We were there for the 2019 College Football Championship Game. Geaux Tigers, as they say. I was not squeezing in between people's personal space at all. + Reservations accepted: We got a massive table of 18 people in the back of the bar which has a massive MEL'S sign (please see photo) illuminating everything and scores of TVs in every direction. + One cool bartender: The female bartender working the main bar apparently was a veteran. She took care of everyone. One of our acquaintance planned to return home to New Haven via the North Metro (2-hour train ride). She adequately gave and re-filled his water to make sure he was going to get back. (Huge + to this bartender. Hope her and all the others are doing well during this COVID-19 situation). CONS: - I can not think of any at the present time. IMPRESSION:This Upper-East-Side spot is owned by a young man in his 30s. The front is a bar runs down the length to the back of the block on one side. There are stool-height couches running along the opposite wall. These couches face the TV to allow for great sports-watching. We watched the LSU tigers push Alabama down a hill in the 2019 College Football Championship Game. It was not crowded. The food was excellent. Quite frankly, the food was excessive to say the least. It was a feast in the middle of Manhattan.

I recently visited Hao Noodle and was immediately impressed by the ambiance. The bright section of the restaurant was lively and plant-filled, reminiscent of a greenhouse, while the inner area offered a cozier experience with high seating and dimmer lighting.

Being early, I appreciated the convenience of free WiFi as I waited at a comfortable window-side circular table. Once my companions arrived, we settled in the dimly lit section as the brighter area had already filled up.

Our meal consisted of shared appetizers and individual noodle dishes. My choice, the chicken and shiitake mushroom noodles, stood out with its wholesome and savory taste. While the hotpot beef noodle soup, marked with three peppers, was less spicy than anticipated and the braised meatball soup didn't leave much of an impression.

The octopus chili and sour appetizer was well-balanced in flavor, though I would have preferred a more generous serving of octopus compared to the accompanying vegetable. Despite this minor gripe, the experience was delightful overall.

Hao Noodle promises a comfortable setting with a menu that largely delivers on taste and quality, even if some dishes might not hit the mark for everyone. It's a solid choice for anyone craving an array of noodle options and a pleasant dining atmosphere.

Title: A Spirited Dive Bar Surprise on a Mundane Monday

Looking for a lively spot on a sleepy Monday night, my friends and I stumbled upon an unexpectedly vibrant dive bar, which, despite its name, was no Irish pub. The night's MVP was Diamond, the bartender, whose exuberant presence and flair on the swings transformed our evening into an animated escapade.

Her knack for doling out shots like a Vegas high-roller created a theme of indulgence. For those on a budget, the spin-the-wheel deal offers a chance to snag some $5 liquid courage. Amid the revelry, a pool table awaits in the back for those with a few coins and a competitive streak.

Kudos to the amusing bouncer who courteously assisted in our swing escapades – a novelty in itself. While I relished the bartender's energetic vibe and the unique experience, this isn't a haunt I'd regularly frequent. However, for anyone seeking a cheap thrill and a night filled with playful abandon, it's worth a shot — quite literally.

I recently dined at a local Italian gem where the promise of authentic flavors was thoroughly fulfilled. The service was impeccable, adding to the warmth and charm of the experience. As a delightful starter, the complimentary bread set the tone for the meal to come.

Not to be outshined, the main course was a standout. I indulged in the pumpkin ravioli from their seasonal menu, and it was an absolute triumph of taste - rich, savory, and perfectly seasoned.

The grand finale, however, was the restaurant's impressive dessert cart. An array of tempting sweets was paraded before us, and despite being satiated, the desserts were too enticing to pass up. This place is a must-visit for anyone craving exceptional Italian cuisine and a sweet ending to their meal.

Title: Sweet Indulgence at a Cozy Local Bakery

I'm a regular at this charming local bakery, which has become a staple for my sweet tooth cravings. Their delightful selection, from cakes and mini cakes to bars and cookies, never fails to impress. My personal favorites are the Amy cake and the linzer tart cookie—both are consistently fresh, perfectly sweetened, and seemingly melt in your mouth.

One of the highlights of this bakery is their commitment to dietary inclusivity: all their treats are dairy-free, gluten-free, and kosher, catering to a wide range of dietary needs without compromising on taste.

The only drawback is the pricing; it's a tad on the expensive side—the Amy cake at $5.50 and the linzer tart cookie at $3.00 each. While the cost is somewhat justified by the specialty offerings, it's something to be mindful of.

Overall, this bakery is a fantastic pit-stop for anyone seeking a quality, sweet snack. 4/5 stars.

Title: Upscale Ambiance, Impeccable Service, but Value Falls Short

Upon entering the aesthetically pleasing interior of the restaurant, which was as impressive as others have mentioned, I was immediately struck by the warmth of the highly professional staff. The thoughtfulness of the hostess, who attentively kept track of our theater schedule, ensured a stress-free dining experience.

The bar, one of my favorite places in any restaurant, didn't disappoint with its stunning setup and extensive offerings. I enjoyed a finely crafted Midtown take on the old-fashioned, while the berry mocktail was a delightful non-alcoholic accompaniment.

Our meal commenced with a platter of dumplings, followed by savory lamb chops and a hearty seafood clay pot, alongside pak choi and fluffy rice. We concluded with a refreshing sorbet. Presentation and flavors were satisfactory; however, the highlight of the meal was more about the setting and less about the culinary experience.

At a total of $226 including tip, the value for the dining experience did not entirely match the expectation. While the polished atmosphere carries its own merit, the overall culinary offerings did not leave us desiring a return visit, especially considering the multitude of other venues that offer more bang for the buck. If you're seeking sophisticated environs with friendly service, Hakkasan may be your spot. Nonetheless, for dedicated food enthusiasts, the cuisine may fall short of justifying the price point.

Its like a hole in a wall kind place located on 1st ave and 22nd street. Their staple is making quartered chicken on the grill with sides. This time, i got their cheeseburger meal. They make you burger fresh on their grill. Even i asked for medium, it was left longer, charcoaled too much. Make sure to ask them to get your fries well done, they were kind a undercooked. But for the price of $10, it was a good meal. The staff is nice and welcoming. Will definitely come back again.

Title: A Flavorful Thai Feast in the Heart of NYC

During a recent family trip to New York City, craving the comforting spices of Thai cuisine, we stumbled upon a gem that tickled our taste buds with delightful flavors. The restaurant's environment was exceptionally cool, offering us a relaxing, unrushed experience which can be rare in the city's day time hustle.

We indulged in an array of dishes which undoubtedly exceeded average expectations. The flavors were robust and well-balanced, with a spicy tray provided that allowed us to adjust the heat to our preference. While I have tasted superior Thai food elsewhere, this establishment has earned a rightful place in my personal top 5.

A standout was the soothing soup, a perfect antidote to the chilly weather and a showcase of the kitchen's ability to comfort and excite simultaneously. Our selection spanned various meats, each dish distinct and satisfying.

While my curiosity about NYC's diverse food scene will lead me to explore further, this Thai spot has certainly made the list for a repeat visit in the future.

Title: A Mixed Experience at a Pricey Mexican Spot

Our Saturday night dinner at this Mexican restaurant left us with mixed feelings. While the establishment boasted cleanliness and comfortable seating, these perks came with a heftier price tag than warranted. Expect to pay a premium, but brace yourself for food that, despite its appealing presentation, falls short in delivering the robust flavors one anticipates from Mexican cuisine. The portion sizes didn't quite justify the expense either.

Adding to the underwhelming experience was the service. On a night that wasn't particularly crowded, our server conveyed an undue sense of haste, detracting from our dining experience. His lack of friendliness set a rather unwelcoming tone for the evening.

On a positive note, the tableside guacamole preparation was a delightful touch, offering a glimpse of authenticity and entertainment. Nonetheless, when summing up the cost, flavor, and service, this restaurant struggles to make the cut for a recommended dining destination.

This is grunge at its best- right on the corner of Essex & E. Houston. We'd finished with an errand in the LES and decided to stay put, grab a quick bite then continue with our night. Online menu was a nice trade off with Salads, Burgers, Flatbreads, etc. Plus hubs liked the idea of their Craft beer selection. When we first walked by Benson's, I just looked at the surface and wasn't sure if I wanted to stay or leave. But I'm guilty and I'm human. I'll leave it at hubs wanted in. Benson's small with enough seating up at the bar, couple of high table-benches and another couple of regular table seating with tile art and paintings. Service was nice immediately and our guy worked his socks off between bartending and serving. Although Benson's menu is filled with a lot of good bites, I really wanted to sink my teeth in their Black Bean Veggie Burger and hubs enjoyed the Bleu Cheese burger with Sautéed onions and Arugula. When everything was said and done, hubs and I had a chill time here and I had a change of heart. Plus their Spotify Indie/Funk play list was real cool. There's nothing fancy about Benson's. In fact, it's the hole-in-the-wall atmosphere (plus food) that'll make me gravitate to this local spot again. Our burgers had major flavor- and I'm sure the rest of their menu is just as tasty. Plus I can tell they put their food right in the forefront.

I ordered take out and enjoyed it! I got the chicken enchiladas. The green sauce was yummy! The rice and beans were absolutely delicious. Loved the rice! Next time I want to try dessert I just wasn't as hungry but the meal was completely filling.

Let me just say that this restaurant had the tastiest California roll I have ever tasted. Who knew such a "basic" roll could be done so well?!I've walked by this restaurant so many times and didn't realize it had been around for so long. Finally got the chance to come here for lunch on a weekday. The lunch specials might be a little pricey (about $17-$20), but the portion is so worth it. I ordered a bento box that came with edamame, salad, pineapple slices, a California roll, and udon noodles in hot broth. I was left feeling super full by the end and didn't even end up finishing the salad/pineapple. The restaurant itself is smallish but cozy and service was good! I would definitely come back for lunch or dinner.

Popped into Bierhaus which was recommended to me by a friend. Tried their flight of five different beers for $11! We also had the fried pickles. I normally prefer my fried pickles in the "chip" style; Bierhaus serves "spears". The spears were pretty good! Battered really well and the sauce they serve it with is good.

A good friend recommended we meet up for dinner between our two places so she suggested Street Taco!Most tacos range from $4-$6 and they come out lightning fast!Tacos Ordered: Fried Shrimp, Carnitas, and Shredded Chicken. Ranking from best would be the fried shrimp which is delightfully crunchy, zesty and sweet to Carnitas (yummy) and then Shredded Chicken which was just okay. Ordered the Passionfruit Jalapeño margarita on the rocks which didn't taste a thing like passionfruit but it's okay because it was still really tasty. Seating is bar stools, booths, bar and standard tables. Will be back! Such a cute spot for a quick bite and/or boozy night.

My mom and I happened to be walking by this pop up just as they opened their doors on opening day. We decided to try it out and I'm so glad we did. The greenery and beautiful decor made for a lovely environment and the staff was very kind and welcoming. The plant based menu offered a unique variety of delicious plates and drinks. We began with the mac and cheese which was made with oat milk and actually tasted better than real mac and cheese. I had a delicious iced matcha latte and we shared a market salad that was so colorful and refreshing. The food was so good that we decided to end with a scoop of turmeric ice cream (non-dairy) and berries with mascarpone at 11AM. I can't even begin to describe how flavorful the turmeric scoop was and the berries with mascarpone were fantastic. Everything was unbelievable from the food presentation to the overall vibe of the restaurant. Looking forward to coming back!

Title: Authentic Japanese Cuisine in the Heart of Manhattan

My family and I visited this bustling Japanese restaurant for a lunchtime treat and were met with a bit of a wait—10-15 minutes for a table, which suggests reservations are a wise move. Once seated, I indulged in the butterfish lunch set, a dish that whisked me back to Japan with its authentic flavors and fresh, clean presentation. The rest of my family's selections, ranging from mackerel and salmon to pork katsu and a warming tofu hotpot, all received enthusiastic thumbs up, marking a unanimous stamp of approval on our dining experience.

Price-wise, expect typical Manhattan rates for Japanese fare, but the no-tipping policy is a welcome touch. If what you’re after is a slice of traditional Japanese cuisine amidst the city bustle, this restaurant is definitely a solid choice.

Amazing location. Arrived around 5pm for happy hour on a Friday night to celebrate a friends birthday. Immediately seated. Drink orders were placed as well as food. All drinks were great and strong and were $5 (beer $3) and food was $10 each item. Both were brought out promptly. The food ordered was calamari (hot, well seasoned, and NOT chewy), empanadas (tasted fresh and sauce on the side...a ketchup/mayo with seasoning), buffalo wings (what's expected), and chicken fingers and fries (very good chicken fingers and nicely fried fries). Occasionally we had to find someone to order more drinks but it wasn't too bad. The music was good from the moment we were seated. Around 8pm they turned the lights on outside and a live DJ started playing. DJ Leslie was the absolute best!!! I definitely recommend. Just note. Gratuity was automatically added to our bill and we were only a group of 4 for an hour then 3 the rest of the time.

Ordered from here for lunch for the first time and I was a decent experience.The shrimp with tofu is seasoned enough and not too greasy or salty. The tofu is silky and soft and the shrimp is cooked well (good number too!). But I would not say it has surprised me or impressed me in any way, just a good healthy dish.I also ordered mango tango smoothies, for $5, what you got is of good value but it is still a little bit too sweet for my likings.Overall, decent restaurant for a lunch spot. I would also with they have some lunch specials prices which will make it much kore worth it.

Title: A Mixed Experience at Olive Garden's NYC Location

On a recent trip to NYC with my daughter, we decided to dine at her all-time favorite, the Olive Garden, famed for its breadsticks. Expectations were high as we approached the towering three-story establishment; however, the dining experience turned out to be a mixed bag.

The climb to the third-floor dining room hinted at our first issue; a malfunctioning air conditioning system made for a stifling atmosphere, and the restaurant's cleanliness left something to be desired, with the air feeling heavy and unsettling.

Service initially lagged, but improved once our waitress approached. The highlight of our visit was undeniably the view, overlooking the bright lights of Times Square. As for the food, the Chicken Alfredo remained a reliable choice, living up to its reputation. My bolognese, on the other hand, fell flat and failed to impress, ensuring I wouldn't be revisiting that particular dish.

A major letdown came with Olive Garden's signature breadsticks which, to our disappointment, were undercooked. The salad also missed the mark, seeming old and overladen with dressing.

In summary, while the service had its moments and the views were a treat, the compromised indoor climate, questions of cleanliness, and inconsistent food quality made our dining experience less enjoyable than hoped. Happy eating, but perhaps temper expectations if you choose to visit this Olive Garden location.

I recently dined at a high-end restaurant, where the cost of a platter for two exceeded $100. Service was a bit too attentive; the staff frequently interrupted my long-awaited catch-up with a friend to tend to our grilling meats. This excess of service, though well-intentioned, imparted a sense of haste to our meal that detracted from the experience. The quality of the meat was undeniable, but its high price cannot be overlooked. A single group beef platter, advertised at $79.99, surprisingly pushed our bill over the $100 mark. While the food was satisfying, the overall experience was marred by feeling rushed and the weighty check.

Title: A True Treasure for Chinese Cuisine Aficionados

If authenticity and flavor are what you seek in Chinese cuisine, look no further. This restaurant is a gem offering affordable prices without compromising on quality. Their cumin lamb noodles boast a robust flavor that cumin enthusiasts will adore. Equally impressive are the spicy sour lamb dumplings—each bite is a testament to their handmade quality, with a filling that bursts with taste. Overall, a remarkable dining experience that will leave you eager for your next visit. Highly recommended for anyone with a love for genuine Chinese fare.

Tucked away in a cozy, unpretentious spot, this sushi joint may be compact with its long, narrow confines and a smattering of window stools, but don't let the size deceive you. It operates on a simple make-and-takeaway basis – no tables, just straight-up good food.

Taking the plunge with the mealapp offer, I opted for the combo of a roll and a handroll. Initially skeptical of the portions, I was quickly proven wrong – the seemingly modest servings of tuna and salmon rolls, both conventional and with a spicy kick, along with the filling yellowfin rolls, left me more than satisfied.

The handrolls intrigue with a playful unwrapping ritual involving a two-step process that keeps the seaweed crisp. While it requires a touch of finesse, the delicious, fresh bites waiting inside are well worth the minimal effort.

In short, don't pass up on this spot – it's a hidden gem that promises to delight sushi lovers with quality in every bite.

Title: A Slice Above the Rest

If I were to sum up my dining experience at this vibrant eatery, I'd confidently give it a four-star seal of approval. The highlight without a doubt was their exceptional pizzas – our group indulged in the fennel sausage, mushroom, and the classic basil with mozzarella, each more divine than the last. It's a must to sample their pizza offerings when you visit.

The meatball appetizer deserves a special mention for its fantastic flavor and pleasing chewiness. The octopus and fried artichokes didn't disappoint either. As for mains, the branzino fish was cooked to perfection, and their pasta, particularly the one with the lemon sauce, was delightful.

As someone who gravitates towards wood-fired pizzas, I could happily return here just for that. However, the other dishes served were equally tempting. The energy of the place was palpable, complemented by great service, although be warned, the noise level can rise. Still, the positive energy is infectious and contributes to the fun atmosphere.

The restaurant offers various seating options – sidewalk, front room near the bar and kitchen, and a quieter back room. With a reservation, our party of six was comfortably seated in the back. A glance at their cocktail list and the selection of wines by the glass impressed us, and it's worth noting their Happy Hour (which we narrowly missed) is very popular, boasting great prices from 5-7.

In summary, this is a fun place for an excellent pizza pie and more, with a side of conviviality. Just remember to book ahead, especially if you want to catch those Happy Hour deals. Cheers to good food and good times!

During my recent experience at the restaurant in question, I anticipated a standout Philly cheesesteak but found it to be merely satisfactory. Although the classic combination of cheese whiz and onions held promise, the portion size was underwhelming compared to expectations, particularly given the $16 price tag. While it's possible the in-restaurant experience might elevate the dish, the delivered version didn't justify the cost. It seems there are better options out there for Philly cheesesteak aficionados.

Title: A Forgettable Brunch Experience in NYC

I headed out for brunch in NYC, optimistic for a good start to the day, but found myself underwhelmed once again. The restaurant, which boasts famous buns, left me disappointed when I learned their key baker wasn't in, resulting in a no-show for the buns. It's a brunch sin to not deliver on your star offerings.

When it came to the basics, the restroom facilities were in dire need of attention, being both unclean and cramped. A minor detail, but it adds to the overall impression.

Food-wise, the egg burrito and mac n' cheese were remarkably unremarkable. Both dishes cried out for seasoning, leaving my taste buds searching for the flavors that should have been front and center.

The wait time after arriving was a hefty 40 minutes, which might have been forgiven if the meal had been worth the wait. Unfortunately, it was not. This spot has the potential with the right tweaks, but for now, it's a pass for me.

I'm embarrassed to say that I would probably come back to ABC Cocina just to bask in the glory of the decor - it is insanely gorgeous. It's a Jean Georges restaurant so be prepared to pay up. I came in with high expectations, and I felt like ABC Cocina met them, but just barely.The drinks were all good, but more expensive than the average cocktail in New York. I found the drinks all lacking inspiration for such a nice restaurant.Food:-Complimentary focaccia and sourdough bread: good/nothing memorable, but I'm annoyed that we had to flag our waitress down to get the complimentary bread-Oysters: very good-Short rib tacos: These were to die for. It was so flavorful and the pork was perfectly cooked. These are a must order!-Mezcal cured salmon: I didn't love the cucumber yogurt relish, but I imagine most would really like this dish-Shrimp with sizzling garlic oil: a complete pass. It was literally 5 small shrimp on a skillet, soaked in chili oil. The dish was heavy without a good flavor to make it worth it. It was pretty bland, and the shrimp was a little bit overcooked-Arroz con pollo: a big dish of crispy fried chicken and rice. The rice dishes on the menu are more expensive than the rest of the menu, but it really fills you up-Winter vegetable posole: a plate of mixed veggies. Overpriced for what it is, but the sauce used was delicious. -Churros: deliciousThe ambience of the restaurant is really sceney, but nice. The restaurant was blasting EDM at one point so that was definitely a turnoff, but it seemed to mellow out afterwards. I felt like the service overall was really, really lacking though. It took forever to place our drink and food orders, and it was hard to flag down our waiter throughout the night. A sign of good service is that your water glass is never empty, and my glass was perpetually empty throughout the meal. The bad service is a huge turnoff and quite surprising for such a high calibre restaurant that's been open for over 5 years. I'll probably be back again nonetheless.

Stopped by for a quick dinner about a week ago and had a pleasant experience here. My friend and I ordered the chicken tikka masala and lamb vindaloo with garlic naan as a side. Both dishes were cooked well and were very flavorful. Only cons are that the lamb vindaloo didn't have that much lamb and both dishes came with a small portion of rice. The portions are usually a little bigger at other Indian restaurants I've been too. However, the garlic naan was delicious and service was great. I'll be back for their lunch specials soon.

Came here for happy hour and it was great! Me and my cousin sat at the bar and has a couple of drinks. The happy hour list was great and tried the following Waiting Game, Spanish Gin and Tonic, and the sazerac. I also had oysters, which were great! Service is fast and friendly. The atmosphere is fun and inviting!

Title: A Delightful Ramen Retreat

I recently enjoyed yet another fantastic visit to a local ramen hotspot. For starters, my companion and I shared the pork Gyoza and Takoyaki. The Gyoza impressed us with their non-greasy texture, perfectly complemented by a flavorful dipping sauce. As for the Takoyaki, they were superb, boasting perfect proportions of sauce to bonito flakes while maintaining a pleasing temperature for immediate enjoyment.

Moving on to the main event, the ramen did not disappoint. Though I opted for a milder version, the dish was still exemplary, leaving me with a slight yearning for the spicy kick I'll be sure to try next time. The service added to the dining experience; being the sole patrons initially, the staff ensured swift and attentive service.

In short, if you're looking for a place that nails their appetizers and serves up satisfying ramen with service to match, this is the go-to joint. Highly recommended!

I truly enjoyed this authentic Moroccan restaurant that I had accidentally stumbled into and good thing it was early because it had filled up shortly afterwards.They place is very cozy, and in the background they play light  French music and the occasional Moroccan jams. It wasn't gaudy or expensive feeling it was the perfect middle ground of what I love in restaurants.The service was alright nothing extraordinary and things came out quickly which was great.   My party and I truly enjoyed the mint tea and babaganoush which came with naan but we also order roti with it as well. Then we had the lamb tagine with Casablanca sauce another one with chermoula sauce, chicken with chermoula sauce, and mixed grill with assorted meats. Everything just hit the spot perfectly!For dessert we got the baklava and knafeh to top the perfect starters and dinner.High recommend this place for everyone!

Title: Hidden Gem in the Heart of the City

After overcoming a bit of confusion upon arrival - the entrance disguised as a corporate building with a doorman, I ventured to the second floor where a delightful restaurant awaited. Despite not having a reservation and the bustle of a Saturday afternoon, my dining companion and I were promptly greeted and seated.

The menu offered tantalizing combo options, showcasing an array of meats that tempted the palate. Opting for the marinated beef selection, we were not disappointed. The service shone with friendliness and efficiency. When the meat arrived slightly undercooked to my taste, the staff was more than accommodating, allowing for a bit extra grill time to achieve the perfect char.

The accoutrements complemented the main course wonderfully, with the pickled onions and jalapeños being a standout. Additionally, the soft tofu stew managed to strike a balance between being notably spicy without overwhelming the senses.

In summary, this restaurant delivered a delightful dining experience. Solid food, good service, and a touch of mystery at the entrance make for an establishment well worth a visit.

Nish Nush remains a delight with each delivery. My boyfriend and I opted for the Falafel trio platter, a harmonious blend of flavors perfectly accompanied by whole wheat pita. I refreshed myself with a homemade lemonade, enhanced by the zesty kick of fresh ginger and turmeric. We also sampled the baba ganoush; while it didn't win my heart, it certainly earned his approval. Eager for my next order, the soup is high on my list!

Hot Bread Kitchen just took over the rotating space in Chelsea Market that once housed Pineapple Express (RIP). They themselves will have rotating vendors in this space, starting with a new location of Gorsha, the DC-based Ethiopian fast casual restaurant.They are serving up just bowls, and they are incredibly satisfying and full of flavor. I tried the Berbere Chicken ($13) loaded up with all of the toppings and sauces. Highly recommended. Definitely visit before they rotate out at the end of October.

I had an okay experience at Oyster Bar, certainly not overwhelmingly good. The service was decent but not incredible for my larger group, though I will say our server was busy that night. I tried my first oysters which was a fun experience, and they were surprisingly good (the splash of squeezed lemon helped minimize the strong fishy flavor). What I was particularly excited for though was the lobster roll I ordered - another first for me in this meal. I had never had a lobster roll before, and to be honest, I wasn't super impressed with what I was served. Knowing that this was my first try of the dish, take this review with a grain of salt, but there were a few things lacking. There was a decent amount of lobster meat on the roll, but it lacked much flavor, and the roll itself seemed to be a day or two old. It was a little dried out and not particularly soft. This was disappointing for a me, not being a local but still wanting to try my first lobster roll while traveling out east. Given all of the other dining options in New York City, I probably will not be back.

Title: A Slice of Cheese Heaven in Little Italy

From the moment I laid eyes on the charming outdoor seating, I knew I had to dine at this gem in the heart of Little Italy. My expectations were not only met but exceeded, thanks to their Quattro Formaggi pizza adorned with fig, white truffle, and Aleppo honey. The harmonious blend of sweet figs and honey with the creamy whipped goat cheese, fontina, mozzarella, and Parmesan sent my taste buds into a joyous dance. It's a cheese lover's paradise on a plate. To wash down this slice of delight, their Rosé Sangria is a must-try. It's the epitome of refreshing, with a crispness that perfectly complements any meal. This spot is an absolute go-to for anyone in search of tantalizing flavors and a sublime dining experience.

Came with my Thai husband who is very picky about his Thai food. Seems very authentic. Cute quiet spot in a basement with open patio area outside. Not too busy around 7-7:30pm on Friday night.Thai iced tea was solid. Wings and curry puffs were really good! Would get again. Wings perfectly crispy and seasoned and come with thai sweet chili sauce. Curry puffs were huge and come with that sweet cucumber sauce that you sometimes get with chicken satay. Husband got the roast chicken which he has had off the lunch special before - he was loving it. That also comes with sweet chili sauce.I wanted to replicate a peanut noodle dish I used to have at a restaurant that closed down so I tried shrimp rama with noodles. The sauce was thicker than I am used to, so it was a little on the heavy side but it tasted good regardless and hit the craving. The plain steamed veggies could use seasoning, but were ok when dipped into sauce. They sort of balanced out the strong flavors of everything else. My faves were def the apps.Service was very fast and friendly. Hardly had to wait between courses...we ate in near silence - a good sign! We were pretty ravenous.

Alright so rating this with the standard of "cafeteria food" - pretty good late night eats. I was pleasantly surprised.The employees were so nice. First, they overheard my sister asking me for hot sauce (which I don't know why she thought I'd have some), so they gave her a bunch of packets. They also cut a hole in the to-go box for the fries, and gave us more ranch than we expected.Looking at the old/stale pies laying out on hot plates at 12 am, I didn't have the highest standards. BUT the hawaiian pizza was decent. The crust was softer than "real NY pizza" but I've found that softer/chewier is my preference. A slice was just as big as anywhere else in NY.French fries were thick, very crispy, tender and fluffy/potatoey on the inside. I had already eaten dinner, dessert, an evening cocktail (basically still sober), and I still shoveled down my half of the box; sister got the other half.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at a Trendy Fusion Spot
