My expectations were exceeded upon entering this spacious, artfully designed eatery, where industrial chic meets cozy traditional vibes. Reservations are a wise choice for large parties; my group of seven, however, was accommodated without delay.

Service was impeccable, showcasing a team of patient and professional individuals who navigated our extensive menu exploration with ease. We indulged in an array of dishes that tantalized the palate with their uniqueness; highlights included Fluke Crudo, Whole Crispy Mushroom, and Crispy Duck Wings, all of which were a departure from the ordinary yet thoroughly enjoyable.

The complimentary potato bread was a delightful touch, and while the Spaghettini for my main course was satisfactory, it wasn't a standout. Dessert, however, was a dual affair of perfection: a tangy Labneh Cheesecake and a sumptuous Valrhona Dark Chocolate Cake.

In the realm of food and wine, this restaurant is a gem worth the visit. Whether for a casual dinner or a special occasion, your taste buds are in for a treat.

Very disappointed by this place. I LOVE omakase, but felt as though this place put no consideration into their omakase - and even calling their restaurant omakase left me feeling very confused.My friend and I were looking for a sushi spot, but everything was booked up. We decided to try this place, with little information about the menu, atmosphere, and price. We came at 8 and they seated us at a table, we were unable to do the chef omakase because the bar was full. The appetizer tasted as though it came straight from the fridge. I'm not even sure why seaweed salad was on the menu. I mean I do enjoy seaweed salad but it left me feeling confused. Beyond that, the salad was just SO cold, I thought my teeth would freeze.I can't remember the other fish very well, but most of it didn't taste fresh to me. I tried my best to enjoy it, but I have a sensitive stomach and some of the pieces just didn't sit well in terms of taste and freshness. For the price of this place (it isn't that expensive), I wouldn't recommend it. It tastes like a place I would order California rolls. I even think sugarfish is better than this place. I thought their Chardonnay was pretty good, but that was about it. Service was okay, nothing special. I liked the hot towels that they give in the beginning though.

I absolutely adore this little gem of a restaurant. Despite its limited seating, the selection of onigiri is impressive, boasting 14 distinct varieties to choose from. My top choices have to be the purple rice with seaweed, shrimp tempura, and fried eel onigiri — each one is fresh and flavorful, making them perfect for a quick bite or a light dinner when you pair two together.

Another convenience is how they're crafted for easy handheld eating, which is a subtle but appreciated touch, especially when you find yourself without utensils. And while you're here, don't skip on the Portuguese egg tarts and other pastries; they're a delightful way to end your meal on a sweet note.

This is a really cute, rustic restaurant in Murray Hill that offers brunch, lunch, and dinner. We were a party of five that went for brunch and we really had a great time! This isn't your typical boozy, bottomless brunch. It's a little more sophisticated than that. They have $25 dollar pitchers to choose from, then small plates, salads, breakfast and lunch entrees. Complimentary mini muffins are on the table for when you sit down, so that's a cute touch. For appetizer, we split the fried pickles which was a nice portion. However, the truffle Mac and cheese could probably be split for only two people, it's a tiny portion (We knew that before ordering because other reviews said that). For entrees, many of us got the fried chicken and waffles. I must say, it was very filling and had great taste. Chicken and waffles seemed fresh- chicken wasn't over fried. It was topped with scallions and their special sauce. Syrup was on the side with the sunny side up eggs. One person made their own omelette and enjoyed it. Overall, the food is pretty good and the $25 pitchers is a good deal. We would go back!

Title: A Birthday Feast to Remember at El Mono

Last night's belated birthday dinner at El Mono was a gastronomic odyssey that my stomach will not soon forget. The six tapas selected were a masterclass in flavor harmony: the strip steak with caramelized onion mermelada melted in my mouth, while the tangy sofrito on the patatas bravas added a zesty kick. The fideos were perfectly paired with chorizo and clams, creating a symphony of sea and spice.

The ensalada mono was a delightful juxtaposition of bitter greens and sweet manchego, all dressed in an alluring sweet and sour vinaigrette. And the pan con tomate – oh, the crispy, garlic-laden toast was a crunchy bite of heaven.

Joining the clean plate club wasn't an option; it was an unspoken requirement, such was the allure of the feast before us. Even with our pleasantly aching bellies, we couldn't resist dessert – a spectacle so divine I'll let the photos do the talking.

El Mono, you are indeed "the monkey," charmingly stealing our hearts and stomachs with your culinary capers.

I had the Lox French toast - YUM! Such a fluffy and delicious piece of French toast. The salmon was pretty good too. Some other people at the table got the steak - skip that, it was only okay. Great service. Good brunch place with cute interior. It is quite packed so make sure you sign up on the Yelp Waitlist to queue up! Overall, a great brunch place especially if you're craving some fluffy, delicious French toast.

This place is pretty cool. The bar area in the front is cool and there's a large dining area in the back. They have lots of beer options, a good food menu and great late night specials. The ambiance is quite chill. Can get a little loud but I don't mind that. I love the house burger. It comes with white cheddar, grilled onions, tomato, etc. The fish tacos are also good. Overall I always have a good experience here. The staff provides fantastic service. This is a great place for drinks and a quick bite in Chelsea.

**Review for [Restaurant Name]: A Mixed Bag, But Dog-Friendly**

Rating: ★★★☆☆

I ventured to [Restaurant Name] after reading a Thrillist article about dog-friendly dining spots, eager to celebrate my pup's birthday with a brunch date. The reservation was a breeze, and the promise of canine treats from their Yelp page added to the excitement.

The experience, however, was bittersweet. We were seated on a so-called "patio" which was more an enclosed, stifling entryway. The space was cramped, sharing too-close-for-comfort quarters with neighboring patrons while a nearby movie shoot's generators rumbled.

On a high note, the drinks shone through – the Pisco Punch was delightful, and my partner's Mojito even more so. As for the food, the chilaquiles were a bit too fiery for my taste, though the staff's willingness to tone down the spice was appreciated. The texture, sogginess inherent to the dish, didn't win me over.

What truly disappointed was the confusion surrounding the advertised dog menu, which, despite being present on Yelp, was unfamiliar to the staff. In a gracious save, they conjured up a chicken and potato dish for my canine companion, a gesture that didn't go unnoticed.

Kudos where it's due – the service was impeccable. Each employee, from the hostess to the wait staff, was friendly, attentive, and genuinely engaged with my dog. They truly understand customer interaction.

Would I return? Possibly, for the drinks and stellar service alone, and definitely in a post-patio-enclosure era. Without my four-legged friend, that is, unless the pet menu becomes a reality.

Title: A Cozy Spot with a Standout Dish

I recently dined at a restaurant that caught my attention for its great vibe and live music. The ambiance is inviting with a spacious layout and a bustling bar at its heart. It's the sort of place where the atmosphere adds to the dining experience, making it more vibrant without being overwhelmingly loud.

The highlight of the menu was unquestionably the baked feta – a dish so tantalizing that it's a must-try for anyone visiting. Unfortunately, while the rest of the offerings were decent, they didn't leave a lasting impression. The flavors, although good, lacked the punch and boldness that I was hoping for in my meal.

Despite the food not fully hitting the mark, the overall enjoyment of my visit was enough to elevate my rating to 4 stars. However, when considering value for money, it's hard to overlook that there are nearby establishments serving up more flavor-intense dishes at similar prices. 

In summary, if you're looking for a place with a wonderful atmosphere and a standout baked feta, this spot is worth checking out. Just manage your expectations when it comes to the rest of the menu and be prepared for a good – but not exceptional – culinary encounter.

Same great taste as the Chicago location, in my opinion. Being New York, it is a fancier version of the original as well as a little more expensive. The hype is still strong as the waits are still long. However, I've been for lunch on a Friday where I had the day off work and waited for 15 minutes. They also have a bar downstairs and coffee shop inside.

What a delight! Was in NYC for work and  needed a place to grab a quick coffee and breakfast bIte.  This was completely unexpected ! Self  serve bakery iteMs and delicious made to order coffees... I will definitely be back!
I love it!!! A 24/7 food place in Chinatown is a great place for those who wants to grab a late night snack. We came here around 11pm on a Sunday night and it was pretty full.

Last night, my husband and I attended an event at Daniel, marking our first visit to this exquisite establishment, which will certainly not be our last. We commenced our evening with beautifully crafted drinks in the lobby, including a delightful vodka and cranberry concoction adorned with a cute flower, and an exceptional gin mixture. My husband enjoyed these as well as a sophisticated take on a Manhattan. The hors d'oeuvres served were a delightful prelude to what was to come.

The dining room’s elegance set the stage for a culinary journey beginning with a hamachi duo that captivated my steak-loving palate as the standout dish. The freshness was unparalleled, with the tartare featuring a symphonic blend of hearts of palm, shiitake mushrooms, and caviar. Following this, the scallops with cauliflower puree and pomegranate were a study in perfection, melting tenderly with each bite.

Our third course, the wagyu steak accompanied by brussels sprouts, rye, cabbage, and a comforting beer sauce, was as satisfying as a warm embrace. Although the rich coffee and chocolate dessert proved to be beyond my capacity after such indulgence, the accompanying madeleines were a revelation.

Each dish was thoughtfully paired with its ideal wine counterpart, greatly enhancing our dining experience. The service was impeccable throughout, from the warm welcome to the attentive care in the dining room, reflecting the high standards of Daniel. This was a dining experience worth repeating and remembering.

Title: A Burger Haven in the Heart of the East Village - Paul's Review

If you’re scouring NYC for a top-notch burger experience, look no further than Paul's in the East Village. As a regular patron for over six years, I can confidently attest that Paul's stands tall among the city’s best burger spots.

Established in 1989, Paul's has become more than just a restaurant for many; it's a second home. Despite the ever-changing neighborhood, this joint retains its original charm with a no-frills, classic New York vibe – think counter seating, checked tablecloths, and a bar-like ambiance that truly captures the local essence.

But the real stars here are, without a doubt, the burgers. The menu boasts a plethora of topping options, catering to a wide range of tastes. From an assortment of cheeses to bacon, mushrooms, and even pizza sauce, Paul's ensures your burger is exactly to your liking. Opt for a deluxe, and you’ll get your burger served with a generous side of delicious steak fries.

On my latest visit, I indulged in the Monterey Jack Cheeseburger with grilled onions, while my companion enjoyed the mushroom and fried onion-topped Saint Mark's. Every burger here promises a satisfying bite into a perfectly cooked, juicy half-pound patty.

For the ambitious eater, top your meal with their not-to-be-missed disco fries, and if you've saved room, a classic root beer float is the cherry on top of this indulgent experience.

Paul’s rarely sees a crowd, ensuring a stress-free dining experience with minimal waiting times. So, whether for lunch or dinner, Paul's dedication to quality and consistency firmly establishes it as a quintessential NYC burger destination.

Let me start by saying the ambiance and service deserves five stars. I came here on a Friday evening and it was pretty full, so I would recommend making a reservation.I had the Thai iced tea and it was great- creamy, sweet, and flavorful. As an entree, I tried the seafood curry laksa and I felt it felt short. I felt like the majority of the dish consisted of lots and lots of noodles. However, the quality of the noodle did not feel fresh and I expected it to be a thicker noodle. Overall, I found the dish a little bit disappointing.

Title: A Fair Experience with Room for Improvement

I recently popped into this spot early to grab a beer and some quick eats. The bartender set a welcoming tone with friendly, attentive service. The beer selection, however, left a bit to be desired for an IPA enthusiast like myself, finding the offerings just okay.

On to the food: the cheese curds were tasty but could stand to lose some of their greasiness. While the spicy pork tacos fell short of expectations and I wouldn't order them again, the wings were a highlight—succulent and smothered in a delightful sauce. Unfortunately, they were let down by not being served hot enough. With proper temperature, they could've been a hit.

Ultimately, nothing at the establishment truly stood out. It's a solid 3-star experience—decent for a casual drop-in. Enjoy!

Title: A Cozy Gem with Flavors to Savor

My experience at this restaurant left me eager to plan my next visit! Despite it being a Monday night, the lack of crowd only enhanced the serene dining experience. The staff impressed me with their respectful and accommodating nature, providing swift service without sacrificing quality. They intuitively moved us to a more spacious table to comfortably accommodate our generous order—a thoughtful gesture that didn't go unnoticed.

The menu was a treasure trove of tantalizing dishes, but the squid soondae was the star of the show with its explosion of flavors, closely followed by the pork and kimchi tofu. The seafood pancake, crispy and satisfying, certainly lived up to the hype as well. With its clean street food ambiance, the restaurant offers a casual yet inviting atmosphere.

For anyone in the area, consider this a must-visit spot; it's a place that marries convenience with culinary delight. A resounding two thumbs up for this culinary gem!

My girlfriend and I decided to come here mainly because it was near our workplace and its ramen!  I was still pretty full from lunch, but the smell of ramen was just too good to pass up.  So I caved in and ordered their ramen and a mocktail (yes I'm not a big drinker cause Asian Flush haha)Food:  I came here with no appetite to eat, but when I saw the Tonkotsu with two options for either a small ($12) or their large size ($15).  I went with the small and it was still pretty big in my opinion.  The chaisu (pork) was really soft and melted in my mouth as the broth was also very flavorful.  Drink: For the first time I decided to try the mocktail at a restaurant, in this case, I got the yamamomo-san (calpico, yamamomo juice, sprite) for $8.  It was a sweet and asian yogurt tasting that made it really good in my opinion.  Service:  The service was really good and fast.  They even tell us how their chairs have storage space for our bags and water kept coming when my cup is half empty so everything was good.Overall: I will come back again to try their different varieties of ramen!

This nyc restaurant chain has been around for a long time and it used to be one of my fav stops in the city (for the table side guacamole - which was novel at the time).  It still has good food years and years later.  We stopped in for an appetizer and drink on my friends birthday.  They were so nice to her for her special day and the nachos we devoured were amazing!  (Lots of cheese - that's key!)

Title: A New York Gem: Gastronomy and Ambiance at Its Finest

Last night's annual foodie field trip led us to an extraordinary dining experience in the midst of the bustling holiday season near Bryant Park. Despite the parking woes and crowded streets, our arrival at the restaurant painted a different picture: a warm greeting from the staff instantly set the tone for the evening.

The restaurant's interior combines rustic charm with contemporary flair, featuring exposed beams and modern artwork that, alongside high ceilings and a mix of lounge and main dining seating, created a warm and romantic setting. It's a space that invites both comfort and elegance, ensuring the night was as much a feast for the eyes as it was for the palate.

Over three delightful hours, we indulged in the Heritage Menu, a testament to the kitchen's prowess in accommodating dietary restrictions, as they skillfully navigated a friend's allergies to shellfish, gluten, and soy. Each dish that graced our table was a masterpiece of flavor and presentation, with highlights including the Aged Long Island Duck Breast, the Grilled Black Angus Beef Tenderloin, and an inventive Green Market Course.

While the corkage fee is steep at $105, it encourages patrons to bring exceptional wine to match the culinary excellence—though be advised, they may reject your bottle if it’s on their extensive list. The evening culminated with exquisite desserts, where the pastry chef truly shone, elevating the finale with White Chocolate Shiso Leaves and an assortment of Petit Fours.

One slight tinge of disappointment was the absence of the celebrity chef sighting we've enjoyed in the past; however, the restaurant's own stars—the dishes, service, and ambiance—more than made up for it. This place is a must-visit for any serious food enthusiast, promising an immersive and delectable experience.

Very charming quaint tea house. I loved the old school decor I felt like I was at cottage in the English countryside. Teas were very good. Great service. Fresh tea sandwiches and scones. Classy place that has been around for 26 years . I hope you are around for 26 more.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Flavors at a Bustling Bistro

Upon entering Three restaurant bar, the lively scene upfront suggested a bustling night ahead. Indeed, the bar area, mingling with some dining tables, was abuzz with activity, a prelude to the fully reserved seating area. Patrons should take heed of the step separating the bar from the dining area—a potential trip hazard.

Service proved to be a redeeming feature, with friendly staff guiding us through the menu. Our culinary journey began with an array of amuses. The rollmops were a standout—a briny, delightful combination of sardines, egg, and pickle. Scallops served in their shells were satisfactory, though not remarkable. The omelette souffle and smoked trout beignets, however, missed the mark for me, lacking in balance and flavor.

The hors d'oeuvres were a mixed palette, with the spaghetti carbonara being marred by undercooked pasta. In contrast, the brouillade, with its soft scrambled eggs and escargot doused in garlic butter, was a winning choice. The Angry fish, although creatively presented, was unfortunately forgettable due to its lack of flavor.

Our entree selections met with varying degrees of success. The duck frites featured tasty duck and fries, but it wasn't the best rendition I've had. A decadently rich and wine-heavy oxtail dish might cater to specific palates. The gnocchi felt slightly dry and underwhelming, while the lamb was well-prepared but paired with an overly heavy gratin Dauphinois.

Desserts didn't quite hit the sweet spot for me—both the black swan and the Paris-Brest a la pistache were excessively rich, with the latter failing to entice beyond the initial taste.

While Three is a restaurant with moments of culinary creativity, there's certainly room for refinement. It’s easy to see why it's become harder to nab a reservation following high-profile acclaim, but whether it will become one of my favorites remains to be seen. A revisit might be on the cards to explore more of what the kitchen has to offer.

Average burger, not a lot of flavor to where you will probably just want to have the meat on a bun, maybe some mayonnaise. Once you add lettuce tomato etc. it kind of overpowers the burger all together. Basically just has average beef flavor, a little bit of flavor that seems to be maybe some A1 sauce mixed in...We were there on a Friday night and the line was out into the hotel which is where the burger joint is, deep inside the lobby, and it was totally not worth the wait. Went back today got two burgers at about 10 bucks apiece and they were just OK. Don't go out of your way or just go to five guys.

Title: A Taste of Italy Just Steps from the 6 Train

During a coveted trip to Little Italy after disembarking from the 6 train at Spring Street, my appetite for authentic Italian fare was satiated by a gem of a restaurant I found through Yelp. This eatery struck gold with its convenient location and wallet-friendly prices.

As I entered, the warmth of the staff's welcome complemented the genuine Italian ambiance, accentuated by the melodious tunes filling the air. The culinary experience was nothing short of stellar with their house-made pasta elevating the authenticity of each dish.

For anyone seeking an outstanding Italian meal that won't break the bank, this spot is a must-visit. I left with a full belly and a touch of envy for New Yorkers who have this treasure within their reach.

Popped in for a quick dinner to go. I was planning on going for a salad but saw the Barbacoa bowl which intrigued me as it was chicken barbacoa! It was absolutely delicious and included all my favorite ingredients. In addition, the staff was super fast in making my bowl. Will definitely be back for lunch or dinner!

During my recent visit to New York, I had the pleasure of dining at a restaurant that truly understands the art of ramen. As a self-proclaimed chicken enthusiast, my expectations were sky-high, and I'm thrilled to report they were exceeded.

The highlight was an impressively large and delicious bowl of chicken-based ramen. The broth struck a perfect balance—richly infused with chicken essence yet delightfully light. The star of the show was the generous servings of tender chicken that seemed never-ending, beautifully complemented by an abundance of fresh vegetables.

Service was as exemplary as the food—efficient and attentive, with water glasses consistently replenished. This restaurant is a must-visit for any ramen lover in New York, and I'm already looking forward to my next meal here.

Title: A Cozy Dinner Experience Worth Repeating

My friend and I stumbled upon this charming little restaurant while in the area and decided to give it a try for dinner. The atmosphere immediately welcomed us with its cozy and homey vibe, despite the place being quite empty upon our arrival.

The menu was straightforward and inviting. I chose a wholesome meal consisting of brown rice, a perfectly roasted chicken leg/thigh, and a double helping of brussel sprouts, all drizzled with a zesty poblano lime sauce. The dish didn't just look healthy; it was a delight for the taste buds as well. The only hiccup was the chicken, which, while succulent, proved a bit cumbersome to tackle as a single piece and would've been more manageable had it been cut into smaller portions.

Service was where this restaurant really shined. The staff's friendliness and helpfulness was the highlight of our visit, ensuring our dining experience was pleasant through and through.

I would heartily recommend this establishment and I'm already looking forward to my next visit when I'm back in the area.

Title: A Taste of Cuba in the Heart of NYC

As a first-timer in NYC, dining at this Cuban gem was an unexpected highlight. We arrived at a bustling 7:30pm to a lively scene set against a backdrop of vibrant Cuban art, pulsating music, and an infectious celebratory vibe, with birthday songs adding to the electric atmosphere.

The menu was an adventure in itself. We indulged in a feast of shared plates including zesty ceviche, sweet plantains, savory empanadas, comforting chicken soup, crispy yucca fries, and the show-stopping Vaca Frita. Each dish was a testament to authenticity and freshness, with the plantains and empanadas winning my personal favor.

The service was impeccable, attentive without being intrusive, ensuring our experience was seamless. The evening crescendoed with live music, reinforcing the enchanting Cuban spirit that permeates the establishment.

This place is a must-visit for anyone craving a slice of Cuban culture in NYC. It's safe to say, this restaurant is on my list for a return visit.

Title: A Shanghainese Gem - China Blue

China Blue stands out as a top-notch Shanghainese eatery in NYC, satisfying even the pickiest of palates. My boyfriend and I were captivated by the sophisticated ambiance and tasteful decor, though the discreet entrance signage could use a touch more prominence.

Our culinary journey included the delicately braised tofu with king crab, the mandatory steamed pork soup dumplings, a fragrant steamed whole bass with ginger, and the ever-so-crisp sautéed bok choy with garlic. The tofu was the showstopper, its flavor enriching every spoonful of rice, while the bass was cooked to perfection, its flaky meat melting away with each bite.

Eager to explore beyond what we've tasted, we're already planning our next visit, with an eye on the acclaimed menu and the enticing happy hour. China Blue is no doubt a must-try for Shanghainese cuisine aficionados.

We came here on Christmas Day because there weren't many places opened and this one looked promising. The place was fairly crowded and the service was pretty slow. Overall, I think the food is good, but not the best. It was also a bit too salty for my liking. I wish the portion for paella was bigger, but it was delicious. The mussels ajillo were probably my favorite because the sauce was really flavorful and went really well with the bread.

Title: A Flavorful Birthday Celebration

I visited a bustling eatery on a Saturday night for a birthday dinner with a party of nine. Impressively, we were seated immediately upon early arrival despite not being a full contingent. Though uncertain if they offer a prix fixe option for large groups, the menu presented a decent selection of traditional favorites.

The culinary highlights included an appetizing fried yuca, a savory rabo, and a fresh guacamole. However, the presentation of the vegetarian bowl on a flat plate was somewhat unconventional. Dessert, featuring delectable flan and tres leches cake, did not disappoint, while the churros fell short of expectations.

Our waiter exuded friendliness but seemed stretched thin, as drink refills and sugar requests were frequent. Nevertheless, the ambiance was lively with a well-curated mix of top 40 hits, reggaeton, and classic salsa at a volume conducive to conversation.

This establishment is worth a visit, but don't mistake it for Havana Central—it boasts a distinct menu and ownership. A minor drawback is the absence of a children's menu, something for families to note.

Overall, I would certainly recommend this spot for anyone seeking to enjoy a memorable meal in a vibrant setting.

Oh gosh. My boyfriend and I wanted a quick treat before we left Chelsea Market, so we decided to grab a milkshake at Creamline. First off - milkshakes are $7 each. That means they better be amazing. We decided to get the two cookies and cream milkshake, and ordered. For some reason, it took over ten minutes to make our milkshake, even though there were no customers in front of us. Not really sure what was going on. After receiving our milkshake, we were intrigued to see that they had paper straws for their plastic lids. My boyfriend tried to force the straw into the lid's hole. No luck, except the milkshake started to pool on top of the lid. I tried. The straw... broke the lid. I didn't use superhuman strength or anything, I just put it in like you would with a normal drink!After trashing the lid and just deciding to use spoons to eat our milkshake, I realized that I was extremely disappointed with the quality of the milkshake. It was very normal, nothing special. And for the best part - I found a piece of plastic while drinking the milkshake! First off - do not put a plastic lid on the milkshake when it is easier to use the spoon anyways due to the big cookie pieces. Second - do not sell your milkshake at an absurdly high price when there is nothing special about it and the size is the exact same at every other store.

Found this by searching "New York's Best Brunch". You definitely get that Saturday/Sunday vibe when you walk in. Most people are sipping coffee or mimosas with friends. They have Egg selections or "Not Eggs". Definitely recommend one of the egg skillets since there are a few to choice from. Didn't order but the biscuits and gravy looked delicious. Good location too!

The food was good and the presentation was nice. Every dish looked beautiful and creative. We had a party of 13 or 14 people. The bill came out to be $559, and $650 after tips. I don't remember the names of the dishes as they were all in Chinese and honestly I didn't order them, but take a look at my pictures. I recommend getting the crab over rice, scallops (it was very meaty), and clam soup. The service was fast and great. Perfect for family parties.

They're motto is "no other square can compare" and they're completely right. This meaty, thick pepperoni slice is perfection. The pepperoni is thick and crispy, the mutz is perfectly creamy and chewy and the crust has a wonderful bake on it. But my favorite part was the fresh tomato sauce bursting with flavor. A must stop for a square slice whenever in the neighborhood!

Title: A Pizza Oasis in K Town

I couldn't believe my luck when a new pizza joint opened right across the street! My first visit on a Sunday was serendipitously during a promotion – buy a slice, get a cheese slice for free. What a treat!

I indulged in a vodka slice, a heritage sausage slice, and the bonus cheese slices. Each variety was a testament to how pizza should be. The crust? Quintessentially perfect NYC-style. The toppings? Generous amounts of cheese, flavorful, and seasoned to perfection. The sauce tied it all together with its savory goodness.

Despite being pricier than your average dollar slice spot, the quality justifies every penny. This place has rescued K Town from its pizza drought, and you can bet I'll be a regular. Totally worth it for pizza this delicious!

Title: Trendy Take on Traditional Cantonese Delights

Nestled in the heart of the city is a vibrant spot that breathes new life into classic Chinese cuisine and caters to the contemporary palate. As a Cantonese, I'm no stranger to the comfort of rice rolls, a staple that this establishment deftly elevates to suit modern tastes.

Upon entry, the cleanliness is striking, and the service, almost too zealous, ensures you'll never find your water glass empty. The staff's eagerness to take orders can be overwhelming, so be prepared to make swift decisions from their menu.

The culinary experience is swift and satisfying. The rice rolls, notably delicate, epitomize freshness, albeit a challenge for chopsticks due to their fragile structure. The selection runs the gamut, with the shrimp and chives being somewhat unremarkable, while the frozen fish variety surprisingly holds its own in flavor. Pork liver aficionados will revel in their rendition. 

The Lai Wan Congee stands out, its robust texture and crisp peanuts offering a delectable symphony of flavors. However, other congee options may not justify their price tags given their simplicity.

For a party of three indulging in four plates of rice noodles, a congee bowl, and two beverages, a bill of $53 including tip reflects a premium experience.

In essence, while the place may not be a haven for leisurely catch-ups due to its bustling nature, it remains a worthy destination for those seeking quality updates on Cantonese classics.

Came here for dinner with two girlfriends. We put our name down at 6:10pm and waited an hour & half. We checked in twice with the waitress before our table was finally ready. After reading some reviews about how the time was cut short I was optimistic but unfortunately we had to wait the entire hour & half. We ended up walking to Milk Bar by the Christopher Street train station to kill about 30 minutes. But also b/c I hadn't eaten in nearly 23 hours at this point and needed food. When we were finally seated we got water right away. Then our waiter came and took our order. We shared the chicken wings, which were lightly breaded and crunchy (we loved the veggies that came with it), the toro ssam bap (this was the highlight of the meal), and the edamame (seasoned with chili oil and yummy, but a little saucy for me). My friend got the so ramyun and gave us her the short rib b/c she didn't want it. I got the gochu ramyun w/ soft boiled egg. It was tasty but the broth wasn't as piping hot as I like (I put the raw short rib at the bottom of the bowl to cook it and it took awhile). The broth was rich, not too salty, the white kimchi had a nice tang, and noodles were good. Overall bill wasn't crazy either (we didn't order drinks). Was the meal good? Yes.Was it worth an hour and half wait? No.Would I come back? Yes, if the wait was under 30 minutes.TBH the appetizers outshone the ramyun for me. And I've had better Michelin star food in LA. But my friend had suggested this place for dinner before they got their Michelin star so we finally went. I may have had a different opinion back then, who knows!

Came here for a work lunch. The hostess was quick to get us settled in with our reservation. There was a coat rack to hang up our winter coats and leave our bags, they'll give you a card number to retrieve your items on the way out.The ambiance was great, perfect for casual lunches, a nice dinner, or business meetings. Thought it would be really prime and proper for a high end steakhouse, but the experience was enjoyable and had a great atmosphere. It wasn't too loud inside either, which is always a plus.They started us off with a bread and crackers basket with butter and olive oil dip. The basket had plain dinner rolls, mini herb bread loaves, breadsticks, and sesame crusted crackers.The service was a bit slow, took a while for our waiter to notice our table, but it's great that they don't rush you at all, which is great if you come here for meetings and need that extra time for privacy. I ordered the French Onion Soup and the Prime Rib Eye Sandwich. Once we ordered, the food was quick to come out. The soup was a perfect balance of sweet and savory with the caramelized onions and the melty cheese. (4.5/5 rating)The Prime Rib Eye Sandwich is big! It came with a handful of thick cut steak fries and pickle slices on the side. The sandwich is layered with lettuce, tomato red onions and the rib eye. The steak cut is relatively thin, but cooked to a perfect temperature of your choice. Only issue I had was there were certain bites that had a bit of a chew since the fat wasn't rendered out enough. Despite the thickness, the bread was surprisingly soft. Overall, really filling and worth trying. (4/5 rating)

I recently dined at a local hot pot restaurant for a friend's birthday celebration. Opting for the split pot, we sampled both the spicy and herbal broths. Unfortunately, the meat offerings were somewhat lackluster, and sauce varieties were limited to the basics.

The restaurant's setup, with a single pot per table, isn't ideal for larger parties; our group of six felt quite squeezed. Additionally, the ordering process—penciling in choices on a paper—led to an oversight where our lamb selection was missed, which was disappointing.

While the experience had its convivial moments, I believe there are superior hot pot establishments in the vicinity that might provide a more satisfying dining experience.

If you're in the city and want dessert go to Max Brenner. Any of the fondue desserts or waffle creations will make it worth the trip. The food is ahhhh.....save yourself and go next door to Maison Kayser and have lunch or dinner then go to Max Brenners. For my first time I expected a grandiose explanation from the waitress. Instead, we got lackluster, confusing, and a somewhat cryptic description of the hot chocolate that I must say comes very very close to Jacques Torres' world famous hot chocolate. Bathrooms were foul, service stinks, and yet they manage to have an overwhelming following. Go early, get dessert, sit downstairs, and don't a warm and inviting atmosphere.
Closest to New York style pizza you can get. Get the caprese pizza and the plain cheese and you cannot go wrong. You'll be drowning in the flavors

Spot Dessert Bar truly lives up to its name, delivering an array of desserts that are sure to satisfy any sweet tooth. During a recent outing with friends, we indulged in the matcha lava cake and the coffee mountain. The matcha lava cake was exceptional, with a well-balanced ratio of filling to cake, allowing the sprinkled matcha on top to shine through without overwhelming the rich dark chocolate center. The matcha ice cream served alongside was boldly flavored and complemented the cake perfectly.

As for the coffee mountain, it leaned towards the sweeter side, but that didn't detract from our enjoyment. It was a textural delight with its crisp cookie and varying levels of creaminess. Though both desserts were on the larger side, they provided a wonderful contrasting experience when shared. Spot Dessert Bar is definitely a place I'd recommend for anyone looking to sample a variety of decadent treats with friends.

This is such a great restaurant for a birthday outing or celebration. The music is lively and the ambiance is amazing. The east and west coast oysters were delectable. The soup dumplings were presented wonderfully and the flavor was astounding. The soup dumplings are topped off with bacon and grilled cheese. The Bulgogi ribeye tacos were quite good in the crispy wonton shell. The grilled Atlantic Salmon was glazed with sherry vinegar. I wasn't too crazy about the pearl couscous but the celery root purée made up for it. Our waiter, Khol (think i spelled that incorrectly) was incredibly attentive and hospitable. This place is great for a party! I will definitely be back !

In an era where old-school NYC gems are increasingly rare, it's heartening to find one that not only survives but thrives. A round of applause for Clyde, who clearly knows the recipe for lasting appeal. The decor is refreshingly unpretentious, eschewing the flash and sizzle of trendier city spots. Yet when it comes to the cuisine, this place competes head-to-head with the city's most celebrated eateries. The seafood salad, when available, is an absolute must-try special. Not to be overlooked, the N.Y. Strip Steak offers a flavor so intense and satisfying, it stands as a testament that excessive aging isn't the sole path to a top-tier steak experience.

Title: A Refreshing Starter with a Side of Delay at NYC Rooftop Gem

My dining experience at this NYC rooftop restaurant began with an early arrival for my 5:30 PM reservation for two. Surprisingly ahead of schedule, we opted for a pre-dinner drink at the bar, where the "Savannah Sipper" proved to be an exceptionally refreshing choice amidst the summer heat.

Promptly at 5:25 PM, we ascended to the rooftop in anticipation of our seating. The hostess was amiable, informing us of a brief wait. However, despite her assurances and the unexpected offer to grab another drink, our eagerness to dine outgrew our thirst; we were craving the meal ahead.

It was a slight hiccup in timing, with our actual seating occurring around 5:45 PM, nudged along by a helpful gentleman noticing our unattended status. Although the delay was mild, for New York standards, the eagerness to sit down to dinner was palpable.

Seated at last, service was swift, with truffle fries promptly gracing our table as an appetizer. My venture into the vegan menu with cauliflower and "crab cakes" was met with delight, while my friend's mahi-mahi tacos rounded out our palatable journey. The taste was commendable; however, the modest portion sizes juxtaposed with the lofty prices left us mindful of our wallets and appetites.

In the spirit of transparency, I'm inclined to offer a 4-star review. The delay and the lighter fare, when held against the cost, were notable. However, the quality flavors suggest a return visit is not off the table. A mixed bag, indeed, but one with potential for a truly satisfying future meal.

I returned to this restaurant after a fantastic experience a year ago, eager to share the joy with a friend on her first day in NYC. Regrettably, the visit proved to be a letdown. Service was notably absent as our waiter barely made an appearance throughout the meal. The chicken meatballs, once a highlight, arrived cold and lacked any semblance of their previous taste. Sadly, this disappointing experience has dissuaded me from planning a return visit.

Had an incredible brunch experience at a quaint spot on Central Park West. The scrambled eggs and Eggs Benedict were cooked to perfection, accompanied by rich, flavorful coffee and freshly squeezed orange juice. Every bite was a testament to freshness and culinary skill. Highly recommend for a delightful morning feast!

Title: A Delightful Culinary Experience at NYC Pizzeria

My experience at this NYC pizzeria exceeded expectations, starting with a smooth reservation process via Open Table, ensuring we were seated promptly. The open kitchen concept added to the ambiance as we watched pizzas artfully crafted before our eyes.

Opting for a Caesar salad to start, we were impressed by its generous size - perfect for sharing. The lettuce was exceptionally crisp, and the dressing struck a delightful balance, enhancing the freshness of the greens.

The star of the meal, a double pepperoni pizza, arrived within a mere 10 minutes. Each bite of the light, airy crust was a taste of heaven. The sauce, with a hint of sweetness, complemented the high-quality ingredients without overshadowing them.

This pizzeria was a culinary highlight and the perfect spot for our final meal in NYC. No doubts here - my sister and I wholeheartedly recommend this gem for anyone in search of exceptional pizza!

Title: Disappointing Detroit Style at a Hyped Spot

I recently visited a local pizzeria with high expectations, drawn by positive buzz. Regrettably, my experience fell flat. As the final stop on a pizza tour with friends, this restaurant emerged as the group's least favorite.

We ordered "The Detroiter," anticipating a savory blend of sausage, pepperoni, onions, cherry peppers, and tomato sauce. Although I've enjoyed Detroit style pizza before in NYC, this iteration missed the mark. The dough was disappointingly thick, reminiscent of cardboard, which seriously detracted from the overall experience.

My biggest grievance, however, was the overpowering presence of cherry peppers. Their pungency was so dominant that they eclipsed all other flavors, turning what should have been a well-balanced slice into a one-note disappointment. It felt as if I was eating nothing but cherry peppers.

In the vast pizza landscape of NYC, this place, unfortunately, does not stand out. Check my detailed photo evidence and further thoughts at yelp.com/user_local_phot….

My husband and I chose this restaurant for date night, and it was a delightful experience. Right from the entrance, the welcoming staff made us feel at home. Given it was a calm Tuesday, we had the luxury of picking our preferred table. We started with the hummus, which set a high bar with its rich flavor. For the main course, my husband enjoyed a hearty combo kebab, while I savored a perfectly cooked salmon served with creamy mashed potatoes and fresh spinach. The portions were generous, and every bite was a treat. We're already planning our next visit!

The pizza was pretty good. 5 adults shared one old fashioned style pizza that comes square, as opposed to their standard 12+ inch personal pizza, which are probably good for one person, if you're hungry.They didn't have any soup left on this Sunday afternoon, the place is a bit difficult to find, and the bathrooms in the basement need a good scrubbing and the door fixed.  The seating on high stools isn't the most comfortable as some seats have backs and others are just stools.The staff was very friendly, prompt and courteous.  The pizza is definitely very good, but overall the experience is really just average.

Burned my tongue. But for my first meal/standing in the rain pizza experience it was great. The boy working was really nice and just so friendly despite the hustle and bustle of 1130pm pizza connoisseurs. Grabbed the cheese (ooooey, gooey, oily, cheesy), the lemon mushroom (just the right kick of lemon, mushrooms perfect) and the square one- the name escapes me (think pizza on thick bread but not like French bread, not bad). The pizza was good, though I wasn't a fan of the crust, little too chewy for me and I don't think I would go for the square one again, just wasn't a fan. But it's fast, friendly and pretty good!

Title: Culinary Excellence at Del Frisco's

My dining experience at Del Frisco Steak House was nothing short of spectacular. The USDA boneless ribeye I ordered, both the 24oz and 16oz medium rare cuts, reached a level of perfection that can only be described as a carnivore's dream. Each bite offered a symphony of juicy, robust flavors that solidified Del Frisco's reputation for me.

Complementing the stellar main course, the watercress and avocado salad was a refreshing palate cleanser, bursting with freshness. The bread, served warm and soft, was the perfect accompaniment to the meal, setting the standard for table breads.

Del Frisco's unquestionably sets the bar, rivaling even the renowned Buenos Aires steakhouses. This place leaves a lasting impression, ensuring that I will eagerly return for another round of their exceptional offerings.

Title: A Slice of Vietnam Uptown

Nestled conveniently close to Central Park, this gem offers a delectable Vietnamese culinary experience, perfect for a quick and satisfying bite. The flavors are robust and genuine, reflecting a true homage to Vietnamese cuisine without compromise. However, the use of plastic for serving dishes does take away from the charm, due to environmental concerns. Nonetheless, for those seeking an unadulterated taste of Vietnam in the heart of the city, this spot is hard to beat.

Upon a friend's recommendation, my party and I ventured into an authentic Northeastern Thai restaurant known for its fiery cuisine. We booked our dinner in advance and were promptly seated upon the arrival of half our group.

The Thai shrimp salad, a fiery contender, was so spicy it left me literally light-headed, packed with an intense blend of herbs and spices. While the papaya salad was pretty standard, it's a solid choice for those who prefer milder tastes. The marinated beef skewers were a highlight, tantalizingly delicious and providing a glimpse into a Thai breakfast experience.

We also enjoyed the grilled marinated pork, succulent though it required some cautious eating due to the bones. In the soup category, the spicy pork cartilage soup packed a punch with its hot and sour profile. Larb, another stellar dish, captivated us with its rich blend of spices and herbs.

The Thai prawn shrimp was a unique experience reminiscent of Korean raw blue crab, offering a softer and chewier texture that's quite different from its cooked counterpart. The Thai iced tea was the ultimate cooler, striking a perfect balance of sweetness to counteract the heat without a hint of artificial flavor.

The service was commendable, and the menu boasted several unique Northern Thai specialties not commonly found elsewhere. Be warned, though: most dishes come with a spicy kick, so a high spice tolerance is a must. Overall, a must-try spot for the spice-savvy and adventurous eaters.

I stopped in for some pizza and a beer while staying at the Redbury. I was a little disappointed at first because I was a guest at the hotel and they couldn't seat me without a reservation even though there were dozens of open tables. So we looked past that and sat at the pizza bar. The waitress immediately greeted us and got our drink orders. She was fantastic! Very friendly and helpful. (Thank you Jenna) I ordered the Margarita pizza as it was happy hour and the pizzas were half price. My pizza was excellent! Fresh ingredients, perfect thin and crispy crust and the flavor was outstanding. If it weren't for the fact that they couldn't seat a hotel guest, I would have given 5 stars. That really didn't sit well with me.

The service and hospitality was 5/5Warm and cordial Food was 5/5 alsoMy fav seafood bibimbap in the cityLoved the mackerel appetizer touchBarley tea was on point Service was impeccable Loved the hands on portion of adding the eggs on the soup ! The best part - open madd lateDefi going back on another weekend whim

I had the pleasure of dining at this restaurant during Restaurant Week in both 2018 and 2019, and it did not disappoint. Reservations were a wise choice, as the place buzzed with patrons each time. The service was consistently welcoming and efficient. Culinary highlights included the teriyaki salmon paired with sticky rice and a remarkable lobster bisque – a treat for any seafood aficionado and a dish I'd find hard to pass up elsewhere. The bisque, in particular, stood out as a rare find. This restaurant has earned a spot on my go-to list, and I eagerly anticipate my next visit.

Insanely packed on the weekends for dimsum (to be expected) but the "waiting area" feels like the crowded Grand Street subway platform with lots of shoving. If you're unfortunate enough to get a table where the waiting area is, it's really a struggle. So switch seats if you can! The dimsum carts, to avoid plowing into customers waiting to be seated, don't have room to navigate in this area, so they will not be coming to you. Odds are, you'll have to get up and approach the ladies to take a dish (which is what we did). Two hours, and I didn't see any of the meat rice rolls, or the salted egg custard buns, or my favorite siu mai. What we did ended up getting, is pretty okay to quite good.  I just wouldn't like to battle the crowds again here. Favorites include: the short ribs (it is on the greasy side) but marinated really well, and was super tender to eat. The fried taro puffs with the meat inside was super crispy, but the taro to meat stuffing inside was disastrously disproportionate. Still, my second favorite. Coconut dessert was extremely fragrant and coconutty. Stuffed peppers was really spicy but not that plump. Not so good: chestnut dessert - bland, tiny chestnut pieces, don't even waste your money. Didn't taste like anything. Durian puff was only strong in terms of smell, and very mediocre. Vegetarian rice rolls was not soft, and also wasn't hot when we received it.

Stumbling upon this gem instead of the intended noodle bar turned into a delightful surprise for me and my boyfriend. Our dining experience was both satisfying and scrumptious. The service at this establishment was a notable standout, with staff exhibiting exceptional friendliness and attentiveness.

For our meal, we shared roasted potatoes, cauliflower, and superb rice cakes (opting out of pork). While the sides were decent, they were overshadowed by the rice cakes, which were the star of the show. Next time, I plan to indulge in a full portion of those rice cakes all to myself. Eager for a repeat visit, I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone in search of a heartily fulfilling meal with top-notch service.

Tucked away in the bustling neighborhood of Kips Bay, this dimsum eatery offers a contemporary spin on classic favorites. Their Instagram fame is well-deserved, with the adorable Hello Kitty bun stealing the spotlight - a perfect symmetry of cute and delicious, thanks to its velvety egg custard filling. While their seasonal menu keeps things fresh and exciting - the just-launched piggy bun with its sweet red bean heart is a testament to that - they also serve up staples for the dimsum purists.

Among their innovative dishes, the house special matcha bbq duck bun deserves a mention. It echoes the familiar flavors of the famed Tim Ho Wan pork buns and is a delightful twist for matcha enthusiasts. The lobster fried dumplings also impress, offering a succulent bite, while their soup dumplings stand out as pretty solid contenders in the dimsum arena. If you're looking to satisfy your cravings with a side of novelty, this is the spot to duck into.

What I tried of the food, I liked - this would have easily been 5 stars in my book had it not been for the rather small (tiny to be precise) portions relative to price. My steak at $44 (most expensive thing on the menu) contained about an appetizer portion of meat. A very thin sliver of meat was slightly undercooked (I had asked for medium well, it came out medium to medium rare - definitely pink and bloody) but I ate it anyway because I was hungry and because it was deliciously seasoned and flavorful. Came on a lovely bed of corn. I would recommend ordering an app or two if you're hungry as all the dishes are rather small.The watermelon amuse bouche was delightful albeit a tad too spicy with the topping. The complimentary cornbread was amazing!! My friend liked her scallops served with blood sausage. Didn't try any of the dessert this time, but definitely plan to be back during the following seasons - the menu and decor changes with each season. Friendly service. Whimsical decor.

Lunch in the passage of my professional travels takes me to Chinatown, Manhattan.  To heed my hope for a quality bowl of Vietnamese pho I take refuge in Pho Bang for lunch.  Customer service is extremely inattentive and inefficient for waiting to be approached by a waiter to place my order.  Waiting for water to be provided.  Waiting for my bill to arrive.  The waiter appeared very visible nonchalant doing the work with disgruntled acquiescence.  I witness the male manager yelling at the staff "no, not that one it goes to her!" and poor communication skills, poor directions to his team.  The tyranny of a warlord manager.  The staff are fluent in Cantonese as well as their target customers.Tai Gau, regular bowl $8.75Combination rice noodles beef soup with fresh eye of round and brisketBroth is average.  Rice noodles are minimal in portion.  Asian bean sprouts are provided at no charge.  My bowl was filled to the rim and served piping hot which nearly scaled the poor bus boy/food runner's fingers.At meal's end I stood up paid my bill at the cashier rather than distributing it to the waiter to wait an eternity for change.  Business cards and takeout menu are available for grabs.  The business card is printed in thermography.   Note:  cash only as the signage is visibly blatantly written and affixed by the hostess stand.

I recently savored a bowl of pure joy at Naya, a Mediterranean oasis akin to Chipotle that captures your taste buds and leaves you yearning for more. The mixed bowl I opted for fused the tender juiciness of chicken and lamb shawarma with a medley of toppings ranging from creamy hummus and smoky baba ganoush to the zesty punch of jalapeños and the tangy crunch of pickled radish. Drizzled with their delectable assortment of sauces, every bite was a symphony of flavors. Naya has certainly etched itself in my culinary memories, compelling a swift return. Trust me, your palate will thank you!

I've been waiting to go to this place for awhile now. I was vegan for a year, and now I just try to be plant based for majority of the meals I consume. ANYWAY, I finally came here for a belated birthday celebration with friends who are very much meat eaters. They were definitely more skeptical about vegan food but were pleasantly surprised to find how delicious vegan food can be. The nachos were a big hit and they all said that they'd come back here. Definitely changed their mind about vegan food which made me happy. I ordered the guacamole burger and I thought it was good but a tad messy. I'm weird about my food.. I can't really enjoy something when it's too messy to eat. The nachos and fish tacos were really delicious though and so were the drinks. Overall this place has good food... but as a seasoned vegan.. it wasn't my absolute favorite... I think I've had better vegan Mexican dishes at tacombi or orale... but it could've also been my choice on entree. I kinda want to go back to try the chorizo burrito!

Atmosphere: Pepe Rosso Social had such a warm and comfortable vibe that was perfect for a date. They had a good balance of a traditional Italian restaurant with modern elements such as a TV with cool visuals such as jellyfish and fireplace. Service: The waiter was super welcoming and explained menu items to us. He had a great sense of humor that kept our date fun and romantic. Food came out relatively quickly as well!Food: We ordered the Pappardelle Oxtail Ragu and Penne Tre Porcellini. The meal was absolutely amazing! The oxtail was so tender and sauce was to die for. The Penne was like a carbonara that had been elevated to another level. Everything was perfectly season and hot. We also got the free dessert via Yelp and chose the Wild Berries Panna Cotta. This was truly the perfect end to our meal and gave a sweet, creamy, and tart finish to an impromptu date night.Overall: While the price might seem a bit high, it was definitely worth the money. The combination of the cozy ambience, cheery staff, and heartwarming food made for one of the most memorable meals in NYC. We would highly recommend any couple, group of friends, or even just yourself to treat yourself to a night at Pepe Rosso Social in quaint Little Italy.

Title: A Slice of Disco Fever at Grandinetti's Latest Gem

If you're on the hunt for the next go-to spot for an impeccable slice of pizza, look no further than the newest brainchild of Roman Grandinetti, co-owner of the beloved Regina's Grocery. The vibe of this slice joint harkens back to the disco era, complete with a sparkling disco ball and John Travolta snapshots adorning the walls—a nod to his iconic character who the place is named after.

The ambiance might be retro, but the slices are timeless. Space is limited—mostly standing room with a sole bench—creating a bustling atmosphere that matches the lively theme. The menu, while concise, is a teaser of classics with promising additions like garlic knots on the horizon.

Our first visit was a taste test through the unadorned pizza options. The Margherita marries the soul of New York with a touch of Neapolitan charm, and the plain slice—an absolute steal at $3—is a strong contender for the city's finest newcomers. The square slice, though slightly overdone, still left a remarkable impression, reminiscent of the famed L&B.

Grandinetti's spot is set to be a downtown staple for anyone craving a premium slice in a flash. It's safe to say that I, along with many other pizza aficionados, will be frequenting this establishment for our fix of doughy delights.

During our recent discovery of a cozy little pub in England, we were welcomed into a setting that was as comfortable as it was friendly. The selection of drinks, including excellent beer, cider, and ale, was matched only by the truly exceptional food. The standout for us was the evening's special, the chicken pot pie, which was nothing short of sensational – so much so that we nearly ordered a second helping. We're already planning a return visit before we leave town, as the fish and chips we spotted on another table looked just as terrific. This pub is a gem not to be missed.

Title: A Brunch Worth The Wait, But Bring Your Own Coffee!

My weekend brunch at this popular spot was nothing short of spectacular, despite a burgeoning line by 10:30 AM. It's a no-reservation venue, so early birds do indeed catch the worm—or in this case, a seat at the bar.

Starting with a black coffee, be warned—they only serve americanos here costing over $4 without the comfort of free refills, a let-down for those of us who cherish a bottomless cup.

A complimentary serving of cornbread with apple chutney arrived promptly. Delightfully tasty, though serving it warm would have elevated the experience.

The Boomer Special, with its hefty $18 tag, proved its worth. The apple pancakes were the showstopper, absolutely divine, and the generous portion of scrumptious potatoes and savory sausage rounded out the meal nicely. However, the eggs were forgettable; lacking the necessary seasoning, they faded into the background.

In sum, a fabulous meal with slightly erratic service—understandable given the packed house. The food is the real draw here, so if you can overlook the coffee situation and the hit-or-miss eggs, you're in for a treat.

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Denino's Pizzeria

If there's a pizzeria that epitomizes the essence of New York's iconic pizza scene, it's Denino's. Whether you find yourself in the charming corners of the village or out in the authentic vibes of Staten Island, you're guaranteed a pizza experience that sets the bar impossibly high.

Their menu flaunts specialty pies that showcase both creativity and authenticity, ensuring each visit is as tantalizing as the last. For those moments when simplicity sings, their classic cheese pie is the epitome of comfort—pure, cheesy bliss with every bite.

On my last visit, I indulged in some mozzarella sticks and calamari as well. Denino's managed to present the humble mozzarella stick in such an artful arrangement, they demanded a snapshot—no small feat for a typically unassuming appetizer. The calamari followed suit in quality, perfectly cooked and seasoned.

In all honesty, Denino's can do no wrong. Everything they serve up is delectable. Challenge anyone to point out a flaw, and you'll likely be met with silence—there's just nothing to criticize at Denino's. It's a must-visit for anyone in pursuit of pizza perfection.

It's literally a hole in the wall and takeout only (no place to sit and the space can only fit about 8 people at a time). However, it's some of the best fish I've ever had in Harlem. When it's warm out expect the line to be out the door and stretched down the street. Even on a cold day you might have to wait outside the door until someone inside has their food and exited. Be patient as the food is truly worth it. I've never had a bad experience with any of the employees there unlike some of the reviewers have stated here. I was greeted everytime I ordered and also was greeted after I left. Always have cash on you because sometimes their card machine isn't working. Black owned so definitely support!

Title: A Slice of Japan at Hudson Yards – Affordable and Satisfying

I recently discovered a gem at Hudson Yards for anyone craving a swift and wallet-friendly bite. David Chang's outpost is a nod to Japanese marts, transporting foodies straight to the Land of the Rising Sun.

The star of the show is the katsu sandwich – a fluffy Japanese bread enveloping a succulent tonkatsu for a mere $9. It's an absolute must-try there. For an unconventional twist, the yuzu and black sesame pbj sandwich is a delightful surprise at just $4; it's refreshingly different and punches far above its weight in terms of flavor.

I also ventured to try the bread pudding, priced generously at $2 for a substantial serving. It's a carb-laden treat that's intriguing to sample but not something I'd revisit.

In summary, this spot is a fantastic find for fast, effortless, and delicious meals that won't break the bank.

I recently visited a local pizzeria and was thoroughly impressed by my experience. The pizza was absolutely delicious, with mouth-watering flavors that clearly justified the restaurant's popularity. Much to my delight, there wasn't a long wait before I could dive into my meal. The slice served was generously sized, ensuring a satisfying meal. I also appreciated the nice selection of their famous picks already made and ready to enjoy. This place is a must-visit for any pizza aficionado.

I recently revisited a bustling local restaurant and am pleased to report that it maintains a robust 4.25-star experience. The meal was impressive once more, with my consistent favorites: the succulent pork jowl, the lively sizzling pork, and the richly spiced curry noodles—all as delightful as remembered. Venturing to try the bbq ribs this time, I found them generous in size but less impressive in flavor; the sauce was a touch too sweet for my palate, though taste can be quite personal. A must-try is the coconut rice, a flawless complement to any entree. While the ambiance is energetic to the point of being noisy, it's a small price to pay for the overall quality and inventiveness of the menu. This spot remains a top pick for delicious and imaginative cuisine.

A nice spot in the theater district, especially given the lack of reliable options around. Absolutely loved the butter chicken and garlic naan. The naan was light and fluffy, the butter sauce rich and savory, and the chicken tender white meat. The sauce is seriously lick-your-plate-clean good. But $5 for a personal bowl of rice seems absurd, especially since one is likely not enough for two people who are sharing. Also, the no refills on soft drinks is always disappointing to me. The appetizers were good but unmemorable. Samosas are small and a little bland without the sauces. I appreciated the diversity of the three offerings, but wouldn't get them again.

My friend and I had a fantastic experience here for brunch. We made a reservation which was good because this place filled up quickly all throughout lunch. Service was superb with the staff being helpful, attentive, and friendly. We ordered a bunch of stuff to share and it's nice that you can choose between a small or large portion. That was we got to try more foods on the menu. We got the biscuits which were our favorite dish with the honey butter and jam. The blue mac & cheese was also good. It had a good  taste of blue cheese while still maintaining its true  mac and cheese texture and taste. We got the burrata which was a tad too salty for me but it went well with the tomatoes. The deviled eggs were a perfect texture and flavor. We also shared the French toast which was okay but we were so full. The top of thE French toast was great but we didn't like that the bottom toast was soggy from the wet toppings. We loved that everything was sourced locally and tasted delicious.

Title: A Redeeming Experience at Tacombi - Flatiron

During my recent visit to Tacombi, I was pleasantly surprised by how much the food and service have improved. We kicked off our meal with the guacamole, which was a pure delight with its fresh taste and perfect seasoning. 

Moving on to the tacos, the Al Pastor was the star of the evening, erasing any past disappointments with its explosive flavor and just the right amount of kick. The Shrimp taco offered a pleasant contrast with a different but equally enjoyable taste. The Huevos Con Pastor was another hit, particularly impressive to my mom with its unique heritage pork.

The drinks were on point with a well-balanced, refreshing Verde juice and a strong, satisfying margarita. A special mention goes to manager Daniel and hostess Ada for their exceptional service, which greatly contributed to the experience.

Kudos to Tacombi for not only providing delicious dine-in options but also thinking of the takeaway experience with their burritos and tortas, which are perfect for enjoying their high-quality food at home.

Highly recommended for those looking for authentic flavors and top-notch service.

I approached the renowned chef's pop-up experience with high expectations, only to find myself underwhelmed by the food's quality. The highlight turned out to be the complimentary dessert tart, a treat for completing their survey.

So the crust is cardboard? So the sauce is more water than tomato? So the cheese is more related to petroleum than dairy? It's just a Susan B. Anthony or Sacajawea dollar, 100 Lincoln pennies, 20 Jefferson nickels, 10 Roosevelt dimes or 4 Washington quarters to get you a hot slice. I'll bet you can scare up enough change from the crevices of your couch for a 2 slice and soda combo meal ($2.50), cheaper than the 2 hot dogs down the street at Gray's Papaya. After late night clubbing, after a movie or show or freezing your butt off NYE in Times Square, you can grab a fresh slice at 2 Bros. Just time it so that the pie just comes out of the oven. If you really cared about the taste, you can drown your slice in garlic powder, oregano leaves or red pepper flake.

Delicious fast casual mazemen which is not traditional brothy ramen but rather coated noodles which reminds me of all the fast casual bowl crazes popping up in the city.This one does not disappoint at all. The tonkatsu sauce is rich and almost peanut-y (comes with chili oil for those who aren't fans omit it). The beef is good with mushrooms and curry egg. I rounded It out with chili nuts for a spicy but not too spicy (medium in my book but there is a tingle) delicious lunch. They play pop music so Justin Bieber is singing yummy as I chow down these noodles. Yes there are vegetarian options here that you could totally make no problem. I'd prob try that next.

Title: A Jewel on Museum Mile: El Museo del Barrio

El Museo del Barrio, situated on Museum Mile, recently reopened after renovations, and it was well worth the wait. As a showcase of the Puerto Rican, Latin, and Caribbean influences on New York, the museum offers a rich educational experience through its art and artifacts. Visiting on Mother's Day was a treat, with the bonus of free entry for mothers adding to the experience.

Navigating the museum is a comfortable endeavor, requiring roughly an hour to fully appreciate the thoughtful curation of photographs, art, and artifacts that speak volumes about the last centuries' migration into New York. The museum serves as a poignant reminder of the importance of understanding the diverse narratives that shape our city through the personal expression of art.

In conclusion, El Museo del Barrio is a cultural treasure that provides invaluable insights into an integral part of New York's history and present-day society. It's a must-visit for anyone looking to deepen their appreciation of the city's rich tapestry of cultures.

I am so glad that we live near up thai. I LOVE this place. Right from its ambiance to its food to service everything is just so perfect. we ordered druken noodles, crispy spring rolls and green salad. I loved the plum saute which is served with the spring rolls and the salad dressing with a taste of ginger. A must go place.

Old Tbilisi Garden is a charming Georgian restaurant in the Village.The food was very good, and the ambience was classy and charming. I loved the tiny waterfall and plants in the backyard patio.K and I had a dinner with a friend one weekday night. The backyard patio was warm and had plants blowing swaying. There was a bubbling waterfall that was so delightful!We shared the following:Georgian wine- it was so amazing and delightful! The semi dry red wine was slightly sweet with complex earthy tones. I loved it! Definitely order this over the Georgian cocktail.Georgian soup dumplings- this was the best bite! I loved the juicy gigantic soup dumplings. You have to eat the dumpling upside down by holding its thick stem. The beef was so tender and flavorful! Yes, you do get some soup on your hands but try to drink it as you nibble the top. Old Tbilsisi- Georgian vodka with lime juice and simple syrup. This was a good drink.Imeruli- this was an excellent stuffed cheese bread. It tasted like a cheesy crusted pizza.Imeruli salad- cucumber, tomato, fresh herbs with walnuts. This was an interesting salad. I liked the fresh vegetables tossed in the walnut paste. Very different than what I expected. Borscht soup- this was a good borscht. It was warming and very clean. Fish kebabs- tender chunks of fish on a plate. It was good.Chashushuli- veal in tomato and red wine sauce with bread. This was a good veal dish. Tender chunks of veal in a tomato sauce. Ideali- honey walnut cake. This was sweet and delightful. The cake was made of walnut paste and honey. It was so nutty. Apparently Georgian cuisine involves a lot of walnuts.I would definitely return to sit in the back and enjoy the soup dumplings and the honey walnut cake with a glass of red!

In the sometimes shady area between Chinatown and Little Italy, there exists a magical place. Hard to spot froM the street due to its subtle entrance, Tora is an amazing secret little yakitori shop.Stepping inside felt like stepping into a typical local restaurant in a suburb of Tokyo. I immediately forgot that I was in the heart of NYC! The service was incredible. The waitstaff were exceedingly friendly and put up with me speaking Japanese to them. I even learned that the hostess is a phenom in kendo! How cool! I enjoyed their Japanese beer selection as well. They have one of my favorite microbrews, Yeast Meets West (pun intended), which is so difficult to find in the USA.And then there was the food. Everything was amaze! They have a good deal for 10 sticks for $45, which was pretty reasonable. I highly recommend their beef dishes, Negima, and their take on a grilled onigiri, wrapped in a piece of marinated steak!The meal was excellent, the food and service so friendly! Here's the score:Food: 5/5Service: 5/5Ambience: 5/5Price: 4.5/5Overall: 4.75/5, rounding to 5. Awesome job!!!

Title: Bustling AYCE Hot Pot Experience at Hometown

I recently visited the popular Hometown AYCE hot pot restaurant on a packed Saturday night. Expect a lengthy wait, as ours stretched to over an hour and a half without the promised callback, but we were promptly seated upon checking back in person.

Hometown competes closely with 99 Favor Taste, offering both hot pot and KBBQ with a more modern and energized atmosphere, complete with multiple floors of seating. The noise level can get quite high, contributing to its vibrant scene.

Diners have the choice between individual pots or communal hot pot dining. The sauce bar is extensive, featuring usual favorites with additional broth varieties like kimchi and tomato. Despite the $27.99 price for AYCE, be aware that certain items like mussels and crabmeat sticks require an additional fee, which is not the norm elsewhere.

The service, however, was a standout; staff were both friendly and attentive. To top it off, affordable drink and beer specials are available, making them perfect companions to the hot pot experience.

Title: A Unique Slice at B Side

My post-Rockettes search for a quintessential NY slice led me to B Side, and although it wasn't your average pizza, it certainly delivered beyond my expectations. Settling in at the bar, I appreciated the already placed menus and prompt service as I excitedly traded my usual wine preference for a thrilling selection from their craft beer list. The passion fruit sour was a brilliant start, matching well with the Oscar the Grouch pizza I chose.

The beer and wine list boasted an impressive variety, tempting enough to divert anyone from their standard drink choices. As for the pizza, it's clear they offer a diverse range that caters to customization, as I noted from the waiter's flexible suggestions to a neighboring diner.

The atmosphere in B Side was welcoming, with attentive servers that added to the cozy experience. While the pizza was pleasing, I did crave a bit more in terms of flavor – a gap I could've bridged myself with the provided cheese and red pepper flakes, had I remembered to use them. The dim lighting was slightly less than ideal for me but it's a small quibble and doesn't detract from the overall charm of this little gem tucked away from the bustle of Times Square and Rockefeller Center.

Title: A Spicy Gem on the East Side

I recently dined at an excellent, budget-friendly Chinese restaurant on the East Side that certainly deserves a shout-out. Not only does it boast a full bar, which is a definite plus for those who enjoy a drink with their meal, but they also have a unique spicy rating system ranging from 0 to 10. I can attest to its accuracy—those dishes pack a punch without compromising on taste.

Their lunch specials are a steal, offering great value for the quality and quantity of food served. Be prepared for a bit of a crowd during dinner hours, but let me assure you, the wait is worthwhile. For those who enjoy authentic flavors, the Mapo Tofu is a standout dish—truly legit and a must-try for aficionados of traditional Chinese cuisine.

This place was quite the disappointment. Me and my boyfriend decided to go to a nice dinner and we found this place. The place is very nice and very cute and the food is pretty good but the service was horrible. We were at this restaurant for TWO AND A HALF HOURS and all we got was one appetizer and two pastas. The waiter was super spacey and ignored us most of the time and then literally forgot our order and came back and asked us it again after 20 minutes. On top of that we ordered a bottle of wine that was like $50 and he also forgot which one we ordered so he said he would take care of it and picked us one that was $80 and charged us for it. Don't get me wrong the food is good but I'm sure there's plenty of other places just as good that won't ruin your whole night.

Title: A Culinary Jewel in Staten Island - Dosa Garden Review

Dosa Garden might just be the contender for the title of the best restaurant in Staten Island, and that’s no small feat. Nestled among a variety of delightful ethnic eateries, this place is a compelling reason to explore beyond the immediate vicinity of the ferry terminal.

Admittedly, getting to Dosa Garden can be a bit of an ordeal if you’re not from Staten Island. With limited options, the ferry followed by a public bus ride into the Tompkinsville neighborhood is your best bet. Despite the travel challenges, my partner and I braved the journey for their lunch special, and it didn’t disappoint.

At approximately $9, the generous lunch special includes a dosa, along with idli and vada - a feast in its own right. I savored the masala dosa while my partner opted for the mysore version. They were substantial enough that sharing one would have sufficed. The idli and vada complement the dosa perfectly, especially when soaked in the rich, flavorful sambar.
