The amount of food is considerable, but after the lengthy trip, our appetites were more than ready. This meal didn't just satisfy our hunger; it significantly enhanced our perception of Staten Island. Against common misconceptions, the island is far from a culinary wasteland.

In closing, Dosa Garden stands out as a must-visit for Indian cuisine enthusiasts. Though the journey there might be a deterrent for some, the culinary rewards are definitely worth the effort.

I'm back here so often, they should know me by name lmao! I came here to try the nugchos (nugget nachos). Before they disappeared. They were this months nugget of the month, and man! Delicious!! First, it's coated in tortilla chips, fried, served drenched in queso, and pico de galo.. omg!!!!! Who thinks of these flavors?! Nevertheless, if you haven't tried them i suggest you hurry because i believe a new flavor comes out in June. See pics below

What can you say about a Michelin *** star restaurant that others have not said before?Pros-food really is amazing, excellent tasting menu, focus is on the food and menu.Cons-the sommelier was a bit rough and the single unisex bathroom outside the restaurant in the grocery store.This is certainly one of the best meals I have eaten.  The food is meticulously prepared with an incredible taste.  The presentation is excellent and the service is professional. Though excellent, a lot of dining has to be in the moment.  The minor cons, which are permissible when there are lower expectations, become a sticking point at a 3 star Michelin.  For this reason it received only a 4/5.Food is really amazing but dining is an individual experience and though wow'ed by many details wasn't blown away by the whole experience.

I recently dined at a local spot that turned out to be a delightful discovery for dumpling and noodle aficionados. The quality of the food is truly unbeatable for the price they offer - each bite filled with flavor and skillfully prepared. However, patrons should be aware that the restaurant does not provide complimentary tap water, only bottled water for a dollar. Also, a word of caution: the bathroom facilities could do with some attention, as they're a bit on the intimidating side. Despite this, the culinary experience was outstanding and well worth it for the tasty fare.

This place was amazing!! One of the best quality cheap- eats in NYC Chinatown. We got the pork house buns, Szechuan dumplings, and the hand pulled noodles with soy bean paste. The pork buns were out of this world! The pork belly was super tender and the fat just melted in your mouth. We also loved the crushed toasted peanuts on top, which gave the buns a nice crunch. The bun itself was very soft and moist, and the ratio of bun to meat was perfect, being more meat than carb heavy (who doesn't like more meat, right?). The Szechuan dumplings were excellent. The sauce it came in wasn't too spicy or oily and the meat inside tasted very fresh and was also leeaaan (no added filler fat!!). I have to say though, the vinegar/garlic soy sauce that's on the table blew me away the most. It was so addicting that I wanted to order 10 more dumplings just to eat more of the sauce! The noodles were quite good and had a nice bounce to them. They were pretty standard as hand-pulled noodles go. We added some chili oil to it, which was delicious but be careful, a little goes a long way! That stuff was SPICY. In addition to ordering two soft drinks, our total for two people was only $20.50! We were both pleasantly full. Can't wait to come back!!

Saggio is a well-renowned Italian restaurant, and with good reason. First, their service is fantastic; everyone, from the busboy to the server to the host, was so professional and welcoming. Second, the ambiance is extremely cozy and romantic. I went with a friend and I thought it had the most intimate interior I've experienced in quite some time. Third, their food is seriously great! My friend got a butternut squash rosemary gnocchi and I tried it - it may have been the best pasta I've ever had. I got a chicken salad and it was so well-crafted, plated, and seasoned. It had goat cheese and pistachios, and the bed of greens was so fresh and high-quality. And fourth, it's all so reasonably priced! I couldn't believe how good everything was for how much we were paying - and what's great is that the place feels like it's so much more expensive than it is. Saggio is doing everything so right. FYI, they do pasta lunch specials! You definitely should come here for that, because their pasta is homemade is just overall perfect and authentic. Ideal dining experience! Come for romantic dates, friend dates, solo dates, and all your one-on-one dining needs.

Amazing ramen in this small restaurant. They have delicious food as well, with the sweet potato fries, pork and mushroom buns being stand outs. My friends got the uni ramen, and I got the spicy miso ramen. I loved the spicy miso broth and liked the noodles a lot, even though I'm a fan of thicker noodles. I tried a taste of the Uni ramen and it was fantastic, and I suggest getting that if you are a fan of umami flavors. My friends and I constantly talk about this place and we want to come back to get our favorites - definitely worth trying! There can be a wait though so going earlier is probably a better bet.

Title: A Toast to the Drinks, But the Fare Falls Flat

If you're venturing into the bustling Times Square area and find yourself considering this spot for a meal, you might want to realign your expectations. The true highlight here is the beverage selection—it outshines the cuisine by a long shot.

For those celebrating a birthday, the restaurant does offer a complimentary dinner (dine-in only), complete with a festive birthday song, a sign, and a delightful flan dessert which, incidentally, was the most impressive item we sampled all evening.

Happy hour enthusiasts will find an array of appetizers to choose from, but the options diminish near the bar. As for the main courses, the pork chops draped in an overly sweet mango sauce were disappointingly petite. Both the rice and beans and various meat dishes suffered from a lack of flavor, with some meats served excessively dry. The paella, a classic dish that should burst with flavor, was also in dire need of seasoning.

Despite the misses on the food front, the expansive bar area and eye-catching drinks might redeem the experience for some. Just bear in mind that you're paying a premium for the Times Square location. In summary, visit for the drinks and the birthday perks, but temper your culinary expectations.

I came to San Matteo on Friday night around 9PM. I was with some friends and we got taken to the upstairs seating. We were seated next to a table of really loud, rowdy, drunk "frat" boys and I could barely hear myself think. We asked our waitress to be moved but she assured us they had paid and were getting ready to leave. (She was right and they left shortly after.) would be nice if they could have told them to keep it down as all of the other patrons eating upstairs were bothered by it as well. We got an appetizer of the crocche di patate - my friends liked it but I was impartial. A little too heavy for me. We then all got three pizzas to split. The dough was really nice and thick which I liked, but the pizza toppings all fell off as soon as you tried to pick it up. The pizza was tasty but nothing to write home about- we also all felt really sick afterwards. I even woke up the next morning feeling absolutely terrible (and we didn't even finish our pizza!) probably won't be coming back here - but our waitress was really sweet !

**Review of Thai Villa in Union Square**

**Rating: 5/5**

Thai Villa is not your run-of-the-mill Thai restaurant; it's a culinary treasure for both classic and exotic Thai cuisine aficionados. Their lunch offerings are irresistible, and though the dinner menu is just as entrancing, be wary of peak hours; the wait can be long.

On my initial visit, the Royal Thai dishes, like the pandan-wrapped Gai Hor Bai Touy, were a revelation. The menu can seem daunting, but the staff's expertise splendidly guides you through it, ensuring you know what you're about to savor.

Crave the classics? Their Thai Basil Fried Rice brings the heat, while the Royal Pad Thai is an artwork in its own right. For the adventurous, the lettuce wraps with pork and crab and the curry soft shell crab are memorable, as is the blue sticky rice dessert paired with exceptional ice cream.

Lunch portions are filling, balancing well with an appetizer, soup, or salad. Pricing climbs as you delve into the Signature or Privileged dishes, but for the unparalleled flavors, it's absolutely worth it.

In essence, Thai Villa is a godsend for those nearby, offering a taste of Thai royalty and culinary innovation that will leave you saying, "I need more of that in my life."

I went with friends for the Sunday Brunch Restaurant Week. The place is big and has lots of space. They have comfy chairs in the entrance, so you can be comfortable waiting for your table. I wish all restaurants had that. Brunch menu had decent options. And dessert was amazing. Service was friendly and attentive. I had salmon and chicken salad. Both were pretty good. Size wise, on a smaller side. But we still left pretty full.Place was not very busy, and it was pretty quiet. It was a very good Sunday afternoon.

Title: A Brunch to Remember at Spiegel

My brunch experience at Spiegel was one for the books. Arriving at 1pm on a bustling Saturday, my companion and I were conveniently seated at the bar—spacious and cozy. With the restaurant nearly full, anticipation for their famed brunch platter, a reason for my initial intrigue, was high. And it did not disappoint.

Spiegel's brunch platter is a weekly rotating marvel, offering new taste adventures with each visit. The variety was exceptional, and the staff was accommodating when we opted for a substitution of perfect-looking fries instead of the sweet potato, with no fuss.

Priced at $40, the platter was a generous feast for two, potentially suitable for three. The culinary finesse was evident, with thoughtful garnishes like pomegranate seeds in the babaganoush and top-notch tahini elevating the spread. Every bite was a delight, with several dishes being delightful firsts for me.

In summary, Spiegel is a must for brunch enthusiasts eager for quality, variety, and value. I eagerly anticipate my next platter adventure there.

I recently had the pleasure of attending a big engagement party at this venue and my experience was nothing short of fantastic, earning a solid 4-star rating from me. The starters, which included a generous spread of bread and salads, were awesome in variety and taste. The standout for the evening was the meat, with the lamb being absolutely breathtaking in flavor and preparation. Both the service and ambiance added to the lovely experience, creating an inviting atmosphere. This is definitely a place I would love to come back to in the future.

To call it a hole in the wall would be an overstatement lol.  The entire establishment is literally the size of a Manhattan bedroom.  My wife and I have been coming here since we were in HS.  Prices have gone up in the last 30 years, but the food is still just as awesome and is still decently prIced.  We rarely come to Manhattan without stopping by and picking up a few sandwiches.  Even if we're catching a show further uptown, we'd come here earlier for a late lunch.  I don't what it is about the place.  Maybe it's partly nostalgia.  But, their chicken and falafel are always perfectly seasoned and prepared.  Their veggies are always fresh and crisp.  And their sauce is just icing on the cake.  It's never too heavy or overly salty.  There is almost always a line out the door.  The "dining area" is a shelf on the right side of the room where 4-5 people can squeeze in and face the wall.  You will be rubbing shoulders and butt cheeks with other  patrons.  In recent years they've added an "outdoor dining" area.  It's 2 benches in a plastic enclosure, good enough to squeeze another 4 small customers into, plus a bistro/bar table without any seats.  We typically eat standing up on the sidewalk.  Or,  if we manage to get a parking spot in front, then we'll eat in the car.  But beware that it's a no standing zone, so don't leave your car unattended.  Or we'll  park on 6th Ave, around the corner,  and walk here.  There are usually spots available there.We've taken our kids and parents there a few times as well, and they too are hooked.  It's become a part of the Manhattan experience every time we're in the city.  Hopefully, our kids  can one day bring their kids to this unpolished gem.

Great Mexican place in the area! The owners are nice and friendly and so is the staff. They made vegetarian tacos and burritos based on our request. The food was delicious. They also decorated the place for Christmas, which was pretty as well! Overall, great variety of food options.

I've become a regular at this spot, and for good reason. Their delivery service is as reliable as it gets, nailing order accuracy and speed time after time. The salads, especially the arugula and artichoke, and the caprese, are always vibrant and fresh, with dressings that perfectly complement the greens. However, the true star of the show is the rosemary bread—simply put, it's addictive. Soft, aromatic, and full of flavor, I find myself wishing I could order it by the pound. Pairing it with their delectable pesto? A match made in culinary heaven. Rest assured, I'll be back for more of these delights.

A restaurant gets 5 stars when I) the food is mind-blowing ii) cocktails are great III) beautiful ambience Iv) excellent staff; courteous and warm v) last but not the least; restrooms are well maintainedMission ceviche is five on five. What a gem on Upper east side.. So glad it opened in this neighborhood. Absolutely enjoyed every minute of my three hours spent here.Fell deeply in love with Tuna Tiradito , have never had a better Tuna before, it was literally melt in mouth texture.Our classic Ceviche (catch of the day) and Nikkei ceviche (Tuna with water melon) were great too. Fresh catches with right balance of flavors. Tangy, sweet and refreshing all at once. Coudnt even nit pick.Last I remember eating such delicious ceviches were in Cartagena.The servers were very attentive and engaged. They spent time giving us the background of the chef, type of food they served and recommendations on what we should try.I'm so coming back for more. Highly recommend to all ceviche lovers

My husband has been wanting to come here for the longest time, and he finally surprised me for lunch one weekend and made a reservation for a date :) Unfortunately, I'm not sure we were blown away by anything we had that day. Since we've never been, we chose to go with the more expensive lunch specials. For $65, you get the chef's special selection teishoku which includes shrimp, seasonal seafood and vegetable tempura (the main reason why we're here haha), bowl of rice, udon salad, miso soup, sashimi, seafood chawanmushi, and dessert.I'm not sure what kind of fish the sashimi was, but there were maybe 3 pieces of it and it didn't have much flavor. I was fine with that though since it wasn't the star of the show! The chawanmushi was outstanding, loved how silky the egg was and how much seafood flavor they got in there. The rice was cooked to the perfect consistency (I'm pretty sure it was good, but I'm pretty sure it tasted extra great to me because I had been going carb-free for a while haha!). The udon was also nice and QQ.Now onto the tempura. There are only maybe around 10 counter seats that get first row seats to the tempura being freshly fried. One of my biggest issues was that there was no seasoning on any of these pieces, so they all kind of tasted one note. And I guess what we got served that day didn't really have much natural flavors in them :( I know you're supposed to dip it in the sauce with the daikon but it all started to taste the same. Here are the pieces we got:Shiitake Mushroom - Not bad, but a teeny sprinkling of salt would have been perfect.Shrimp - seemed slightly overcooked but it was good. I ate the shells too, totally edible :)Crab in Shiso leaf - this is a personal preference, but I don't love crab. I gave this one to my husband to eat hahaLotus Root - I thought this was pretty good, but nothing special.Eel - Not bad, but I think I really expected something way more tender and more flavorful.Okra - probably my favorite piece of the day, I needed something that would cut through the heaviness of tasting something deep fried for the entire meal. This was refreshing.Squid - meh. Hated this, texture was so rubbery.After you finish your meal, you get to order additional pieces if you're still hungry. We wanted to try the eggplant and the japanese pumpkin, which both turned out to be kind of subpar. The eggplant skin was so tough we had to pick them out, and the pumpkin texture just wasn't as fluffy as we expected...and it's not cheap! I think they were $8 for two small pieces. If you want any of the seafood, I believe it's around $25 for the two pieces.The dessert I actually really enjoyed, it was a really creamy panna cotta tasting yogurt dessert with a tart jam.Not sure how different the dinner is considering the price jump, but not sure I'd want to pay that for the tempura I tasted during lunch. I would much prefer Secchu Yokota!

I was really excited to try this vegan dim sum place and I was a little underwhelmed.  The service was friendly but they brought out the wrong dish. It was very busy when we went which is nice to see.  Maybe dim sum just isn't my thing but I felt like everything had a weird taste.We ordered a lot and out of it all I think the chicken fried rice tasted the best.I would return but would avoid the dim sum and maybe go with a noodle or rice dish or the chicken kung pao.

Title: A Refreshed Neighborhood Gem with Attentive Service

I recently visited a revamped local favorite that has transitioned wonderfully from a classic breakfast spot to a delightful dinner option for the neighborhood. A rare find in NYC, the atmosphere here allows for actual conversation—a welcomed escape from the typically noisy dining scene.

The food is satisfying and hits the spot for a hearty dinner at a reasonable price. My fajitas arrived sizzling and continued to command attention throughout the meal, a testament to their freshness and flavor. The manager's proactive service, offering extra tortillas before I even needed to ask, was a standout moment that encapsulates the attentive care provided here.

While it's not claiming to be a gourmet destination, the quality of the food speaks for itself. Case in point: my neighbor's generous portion of Belgian Waffle and fried chicken could easily have satisfied three appetites.

With great food, reasonable prices, and exceptional service, this place has secured a spot on my list of must-return dining experiences.

More like 3/3.5 stars for the ramen but the staff were friendly and the ice cream was pretty good. It's a self service establishment which means you head in to find seating and go place your order at the cashier. A number is given to you on the receipt and you pick up your food and utensils from the counter when it's ready. When you're finished, bring back the trays to the garbage counter area. I got to try a few of their ramen since they had a bogo promotion going on for the month of October. I tried the spicy miso, ma-yu, and volcano and thought the ramen was just okay. They give large portions of noodles and toppings and the half boiled egg was nicely soft boiled but the broths were really lacking. If I had to pick my favorite out of the three, it would be the spicy miso. The ma-yu had a nice garlic flavor but was on the saltier side and the broth turned bitter after mixing in all the paste. The volcano was mainly spice and the white mushrooms were off putting.The ice cream, on the other hand, was great. They have lots of rotating flavors which was perfect after the ramen. I sampled a few and my favorites were the strawberry shortcake, pistachio, and white rabbit. Pro tip: you can even get a free small gelato with the yelp check in!

What to do?  If I give them a great review like everyone else has so far, I'll have to make reservations weeks ahead of time next time?!   Ugh...alas, greatness needs to be shared!This awesome hidden gem is less than a year young but checks off ALL the boxes you'd ever need if you're in the midtown area looking for a GREAT omakase. Still BYOB when I was there in November. Menu that night consisted of the following with the bluefin tuna, toro hand roll and chutoro as our favorites:Kumumoto oysterChutoroYellowtail (Japan)King salmon Red snapper - spicy yuzu pasteScallopEbi (Alaska)Bluefin tuna Shimaji (stripejack)Kimmedai Kohoda Australian ocean troutHokkaido uniYaki-toro Kisu (Japanese whiting) with uni UnigoToro hand roll Overall, hubby and I thought it scored points for being casual and without pretentiousness. If you love fresh fish that comes daily from Japan and you're dining with someone who thinks the same, then this place is for you :)

Came here with co workers to have some drinks and things went pretty smoothly considering it was a last second ask for a party of about 10 or so people.  The staff was very accommodating and attentive.All we ordered were drinks, a bunch of cocktails, which were all great!  Some of the drinks were very creative and tasted great as well!Although it was loud in there, not so loud where we have to be yelling over each other to listen to each other (though whispering might not work either).  Overall, it had a great ambient vibe where people seem to come and relax after work.  If you want to grab some drinks and have a good time, check this out.

Having lived in NYC for more than a decade, this place never changes. It's funny that I recognize the waiters and it seems like they don't age at all. AT ALL! and so does the decor. It's super dated, but always clean. Now having moved away from the city, I make sure I come by at least once during my visit.Dishes I recommend here:Salt & Pepper Pork - my absolute favorite hereKangKong (not sure the actual dish name, but the waiters know this filipino name for it) - asian spinach sauteed in garlic and brothCrab Sauce - yes the sauce they put on the steam crabs, but with no crabs......add bowl of rice, trust me, it's delicious togetherWalnut Shrimp - light mayo sauce is so goodPanfried Noodles - yum! how do they get the noodles so crispy but not burned. I burn them all the time.Susu - (another filipino name I do not know the actual name for) it's snails in oyster sauce.If you come to NYC and want some good chinese food. Come here, you cannot go wrong with any dish.

Title: A Mediterranean Gem for All

If you're seeking a fast, casual Mediterranean dining spot that caters to all dietary preferences, look no further. This restaurant ticks all the boxes for meat lovers, vegetarians, vegans, and those on a gluten-free diet. The space boasts large, high ceilings, creating a casual yet inviting atmosphere with an open kitchen that adds to the allure.

The menu is not only attractive but also reasonably priced, making it a great spot for a casual lunch or a take-out dinner. Service is efficient, with an order and pick-up counter system that surprisingly delivers your meal quite swiftly.

I started with their hot hummus paired with a generous slice of homemade bread. For the main course, the Green Baked Falafel, a vegan delight, was truly scrumptious and not to be missed.

Highly recommended for a swift, satisfying Mediterranean meal that won't disappoint any palate.

On paper, Friedman's seemed amazing -- from the raving reviews to the countless gluten free options. But in reality, I just really didn't get the hype. First off, this place is small. With so many bright, modern-looking restaurants close-by, I was bummed when my phone led me to Friedman's front door, with the dark small interior. But I was so excited about the idea of having gluten free French toast! We sat down, our server was friendly, and he asked how severe my gluten allergy was. When I said I have celiac, he told me something that broke my heart: "Then the French toast is one of the only menu items you can't have." Just my luck. He suggested the lemon ricotta pancakes (one of the day's specials), and don't get me wrong -- they were good! But you can get gluten free pancakes just about anywhere these days. Also, the prices! Are you for REAL? With tax, the pancakes were $22. Also on the menu: $20 avocado toast. Yes, you can pay $20 for something you can make at home for about $3. I get that it's New York, and I get that things are expensive here. But this place is no a frills, diner-style breakfast spot and the prices were over-the-top. Fellow celiacs, I wouldn't go out of your way to come here. It's just average breakfast food at well above average prices.

This spot is open 24/7 and has some pretty worth it options. You order one of the flavored broths and then it comes with 10 small side dishes that you add into the broth along with a bowl of noodles. The bowl of soup is boiling hot so beware before taking your first slurp. I like the original broth flavor and the coconut curry a lot! They also have options where you can add additional meat if you wanted but usually it comes with like 3 slices of fatty beef. So when the bowl of soup comes you just add all the little side dishes in and add the noodles and you let it cook for a little bit. The best part that I think makes this place worth it is that it comes with free additional noodles if you dine in. So save some broth if you have the appetite and get an additional serving of noodle! They also have an area in the back where they have party sized seating. The food comes fast and it's simple.

I recently visited a pizzeria with a unique offering of artichoke and crab pizza slices. The artichoke pizza was a creamy delight; however, its richness meant I could only indulge in half a slice. Despite that, it's still a fantastic choice for those with a hearty appetite. On the other hand, the crab slice was exceptional and clearly stole the show for me – I could easily devour the entire piece without a second thought. A handy tip for fellow diners: the establishment is cash only, so come prepared.

Food: 3.5/5I've been coming here for years. There are days where I think Strip House is the best and other days where I think Lugers is better. Call me weird but.. I think they might have a different chef on Tuesdays. We ordered a caesar salad and two dry aged strips. The strips (on Tuesday) were not good. It was over cooked, dry and tough. There's other times I ate here and it was heaven in my mouth so I'd give this place 3.5 due to their inconsistency.Btw, their 24 layer cake is PHENOMENAL.Service: 5/5The staff here are great. My water and wine glass never goes empty! Very friendly and attentive staff. Ambiance: 5/5This might be one of the nicer steak houses in NY. If we're comparing just the ambiance/interior, Strip House is a lot nicer than Lugers and Wollenskys.

I was nervous about finding a table here on a Saturday at 11am (since you can't make reservations) but surprisingly, there were still tables available.  My friend didn't come until 30 minutes later (I was annoyed) but I was able to find a seat at the bar and have a cold brew while I wait.  At 11:30am when my friend finally arrived, we were seated immediately.Having 30 minutes of wait time means I had plenty of time to go through Yelp reviews and see what I should eat.  I had the Moroccan Eggs with a side of Merguez (sausage).  My friend had another entree with hard boiled eggs (I can't seem to find it in the menu).  The food was amazing and reasonably priced!  I will come again!

Celebrating my birthday at this steakhouse with my boyfriend was a delight. Despite arriving early for our 8:30 reservation, we were promptly seated, and the welcoming waitstaff enhanced our experience from the start. We skipped the $8 bread and indulged in the porterhouse for two, which arrived slightly rarer than our medium-rare request but was nonetheless exquisite. The grand finale was a decadent chocolate cake, accompanied by a cheerful birthday serenade and vanilla ice cream. Although the price tag is steep, the meal justified the cost. For steak aficionados, this establishment is a gem. My boyfriend's endorsement? "10 stars!" A strong recommendation for those seeking premium steak.

Title: A Warm Culinary Haven Beneath the Bustle

Descending into Iron Chef Alex Guarnaschelli's subterranean gem, you're greeted with the casual elegance of a lounge adorned with sofa chairs and a charming bar—a cozy prelude to the dining experience ahead. The staff is attentive, offering a complimentary coat check before showing diners to their tables in a surprisingly spacious and homely setting.

Dispelling any preconceptions of stuffiness often associated with celebrity chef restaurants, the interior blends the comfort of a diner with an upscale vibe. Restaurant Week presented the perfect opportunity to sample the prix fixe menu alongside the regular offerings. A standout a la carte choice on recommendation was the crispy Brussels sprouts and baby spinach salad, a harmonious blend of textures without the nuts overpowering the dish.

The main event, a tobacco-smoked pork chop, defied fancy-restaurant portions, arriving tender, juicy, and amply sized, infused with a subtle BBQ smokiness that delighted the palate. Amidst a selection of well-crafted cocktails, the "Fall" themed quince-infused concoction stood out, adding a sweet note to the symphony of flavors.

Service remained impeccable throughout, with the only conceivable improvement being a personal greeting from Chef Guarnaschelli herself—but perhaps that's a treat for next time. Overall, an experience that proves why the Chef's reputation is so deserved.

Title: A Parisian Dream at Balthazar

I had long anticipated dining at Balthazar, and last evening's experience lived up to every expectation. Celebrating a special 31st birthday, the ambiance transported us straight to Paris.

We toasted the occasion with a bottle of Pinot Gris, an ideal companion to our varied dishes. My Seafood Ceviche was a citrus-kissed delight, teeming with tender squid, octopus, shrimp, and lobster. The birthday girl savored the Onion Soup, while my partner tackled the Escargot with gusto; even my accidental bread-dunk in the garlic sauce was a delicious mishap.

My Moules Frites was a testament to Balthazar's mastery of seafood; plump mussels bathed in classic brasserie broth alongside impeccable fries. Duck Confit for my companions, and the unanimous verdict? Scrumptious.

Let's not forget the bread – crusty on the outside, soft within, utterly divine. Dessert was a shared venture into Profiteroles, with their impeccable balance of light pastry and rich chocolate sauce. The Crème Brulee, too, was a hit, crowned with a flawlessly crisped sugar layer.

Inhaling the heady scent of their Cappuccinos, I knew Balthazar had secured a return visit. Perhaps the Seafood Tower will be the star of our next feast.

Rating: Enchanté!

I recently had the chance to dine at the Grand Central Oyster Bar (GCOB), nestled in the historic Grand Central Station in New York City. Meeting a friend for a long overdue catch-up, we were delighted to be seated immediately, opting for a taste of the sea with an assortment of oysters and a pair of po'boys.

The oysters, freshly shucked and served alongside warm, soft bread, were the highlight of our meal – very good indeed. While the fried shrimp and fried oyster po'boys didn't quite hit the mark, coming off rather bland, they didn’t significantly detract from the overall experience. The bustling ambiance of the landmark location added its own charm to the meal.

While I may not rush back for the sandwiches, I wouldn't hesitate to return for the raw bar offerings and a cold beer, especially when looking to enjoy a bite in a place steeped with as much New York history as the Grand Central itself.

Title: A Regular’s Ode to Becco’s Unbeatable Pasta Experience

Review:

Becco is a gem that I've had the pleasure of visiting multiple times, often surrounding a night at the theater. Their wine selection is a delight, each bottle reasonably priced at $33—a rarity in New York. The meal begins with a generous complementary spread of bread, breadsticks, hummus, and olives, setting the stage for a delicious feast.

Although the menu is varied and appealing, I’m consistently drawn to their tableside unlimited pasta for $20.95. The offer includes a choice of an antipasto or Caesar salad, followed by endless servings of three homemade pastas of the day. One of the pastas is always in a classic tomato sauce, never failing to comfort and satisfy.

On occasion, I've deviated from the pasta to request Chicken Milanese, and despite it not being a listed item, the kitchen has accommodated me with delectable results. The wait staff deserves applause for their attentive and friendly service, ensuring each visit is as enjoyable as the last.

Becco is a must-visit spot in New York—its commitment to quality and value is unmatched. You'll leave already planning your next visit.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at an exceptional breakfast spot that left a lasting impression. The highlight of my meal was undoubtedly the blueberry pancakes; they were the best I've tried in ages, with a delightful melt-in-your-mouth quality and a hint of maple wood that elevated the taste to new heights. Alongside these, the smashed potatoes were perfection, especially when paired with the genuine ketchup - it was as pure and authentic as ketchup can be.

The coffee, sourced from Colombia, was remarkably fresh, and my lathe truly hit the spot, providing that much-needed morning boost. As for the service, it was fantastic. The staff was attentive and ensured a pleasurable dining experience that supplemented my hearty and satisfying lunch.

While the establishment has only one bathroom, this minor detail didn't detract from an otherwise flawless visit. Even the water served in glass bottles was a cut above, infused with fresh lemon for that extra touch of refreshment. This place is a gem, and I can't recommend it enough for anyone in search of a top-tier breakfast or lunch experience.

After frequently passing by, we finally decided to give this restaurant a try and settled on the combo option. While I had high hopes for the lobster rolls, especially in comparison to those from Lunch, The Smith, and Citifield's Catch of the Day, they unfortunately did not live up to my expectations. Despite this, I must commend the staff for their friendliness and the overall cleanliness of the space. However, the underwhelming experience with the rolls means I likely won't be returning. At least my curiosity has been satisfied.

I came here with friends during restaurant week. I went to dinner all you can eat for $42. The menu was very simple, eat all you can eat from salad bar which had lots of options available and freshly madeThe main course consists of selection of limited meat for restaurant week: chicken (did not try); pork loin, juicy and not dry; pork sausage (did not try); prime rib, also juicy and not dry; top round steak, delicious; top sirloin, super delicious; and leg of lamb, delicious and well made From the sides I tried: french fries, great and crunchy; fried bananas, fresh and well made; and veggies, they were okFor dessert I ordered both. I felt the passion fruite mousse was way better than the chocolate one As I previously stated, since I came on restaurant week I got the toned down menu from the regular menu. I heard from my friend that the regular menu is more delicious and worth it. Thus, my experience from this place on restaurant week was A-OK. Comparing this experience with other brazilian places, I feel other places that I have been to are more worth it than this and cheaper than $42 for all you can eat... I would have to try out the normal experience during non-restaurant week to write its experience. But the normal experience is approx. $20 bucks more, approx. 60ish
Surprisingly this little secret spot in a basement at the beginning of Mott street was quite good. Fusion Malaysian and thai cuisines. Food and service was good.

I love the vegan options here.  They have 4 different vegan slices. My favorite is the mushroom by far and second is the potato. The other 2 are still good, but those taste like you would expect. The mushroom and potato ones are so savory and satisfying. The portions are large and you can be full on one slice, but I usually get extra to bring home for later. The crust is crispy but not too thin. Good combo of crispy yet fluffy. Good soda/seltzer options too. My only complaint is that the counter girl questioned me when I ordered multiple slices. She shouldn't judge how many slices I'm getting. I wanted to share some with family later!

This is my second time at a Scarpetta.  My first was at Gurney's in Newport.  This time in NY on Madison Avenue.We arrived almost thirty min early for our reservation and were pleasantly surprised to have been seated. We had multiple cocktails and a medium bodied red wine all suggested by the staff and all were exceptional.We started with the raw scallops and the fried cauliflower.  We had the spaghetti (arguably their most famous dish) and the Wagyu Beef for dinner.  Everything was perfectly prepared as ordered and exceptional.  I can whole heartily recommend this restaurant with the understanding that it is at a high price point.The food and service were great.

Tucked away in Alphabet City, I recently discovered a gem of Serbian cuisine. The restaurant boasts charming decor and offers al fresco dining for those sunny days. My Saturday afternoon visit was hassle-free, securing a table immediately.

The menu presented a variety of tempting dishes, but be warned, it's a cash-only establishment, which slightly limited my choices. I started with the 'Lepinja sa Kajmakom' priced at $6 – a delightful bread with a creamy filling, though unexpected free bread made it rather superfluous.

My main course was the 'Karadjordjeva' for $19, which proved to be a hearty portion. The main attraction, a sizeable fried pork roll, was succulent and perfectly cooked. However, the accompanying fries were a tad too salty for my taste, and the cabbage was unremarkable.

The service was commendable, with our server being attentive and timely. While the 'cash only' policy was a bit of a letdown, and its distance from the train makes me hesitant for a repeat visit, the experience was authentically Serbian and generally enjoyable.

Title: A Gastronomic Delight at Indian Accent

Review:

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Indian Accent and it was nothing short of a culinary revelation. The ambiance strikes the perfect balance between comfort and contemporary chic, creating an inviting atmosphere that complements the dining experience.

The food, oh the food, is simply indescribable. I indulged in the non-vegetarian tasting menu, which was a masterpiece of culinary precision. From the first bite to the last, each course was a testament to the chef's artistry, with appetizers that were so delectably flavored they left me yearning for more.

Service at Indian Accent was impeccable - efficient, attentive, and warm. The staff excels in the art of hospitality, making each guest feel uniquely catered to.

For anyone seeking to explore the heights of Indian cuisine, Indian Accent is a must-visit. This restaurant doesn’t just serve meals; it offers a memorable and exquisite gastronomic journey. Prepare to be wowed and to leave with an insatiable desire to return.

My recent visit to this restaurant left me with mixed feelings. There's a lot to appreciate here, yet a sense of unmet potential lingers. The food lands in the category of good with prospects of being elevated to very good with some tweaks. The tempura stood out in terms of flavor and texture, but the absence of dashi in the dipping sauce was a missed opportunity for an authentic touch. The sushi rolls were commendable, yet they were let down slightly by the mediocrity of the rice, which lacked that special something.

On the beverage front, though the establishment holds a beer and wine license, the selection disappoints, especially for wine and sake enthusiasts. The options are not only limited but also fail to impress, which detracts from the overall dining experience. A thoughtful expansion of their beverage list would undoubtedly complement their dishes and enhance the guest experience.

Love love love this food! Asian comfort food at it's best! The basic lunch set with curry, rice, and pork cutlet is an affordable, filling option for midtown Manhattan at around $10. This is the most popular choice.My main go-to is the cream curry pasta with chicken cutlet and potato croquettes. Karaage is good too. Sometimes the pasta is a little over cooked but I literally can drink this sauce. Always burn my mouth because I am overly excited to dig in - be careful! Don't wear anything nice here...I am constantly slurping and getting droplets on my shirt! It's so good I don't even care. The cutlets and croquettes are perfectly cooked and crispy and awesome to dip in the curry. You choose the level of spiciness from mild to very hot. Utensils and napkins are located in a side drawer in the table. If you are having a bad day, come here and it will melt your sorrows (and the roof of your mouth) away!

First time trying French cuisine and apparently first time trying a $$$ yelp symbol restaurant. I did not do a Yelp search on this restaurant and had I seen the reviews, I would have totally dodged this place. I came here with a friend and decided to give it a try. We were seated outside, which was very nice because you get a beautiful view of New Jersey (?) and the waterfront. It should be noted that this review is solely coming from the perspective of someone who is new to the whole French cuisine concept and therefore expect some culture shock from my end.Food:We were handed two sets of menus, one VERY large and one fairly small. I was shocked to learn the VERY large one was just their drink menu. DAMN! The smaller one was their food menu, which I think still had some alcohol drinks (as if the large menu didn't cover enough options. smh). Everything is of course overpriced in my opinion but I figured, hey if we are going to eat here, might as well get a full French experience out of it. I went for escargot, which is as French as it gets for me. I had a total of 6 pieces. They had a tool that helped you grip the shell, so you can easily pull out the snail. Later, I realized with all the slippery butter, the snail just easily slipped out of the shell, making that tool futile.   It was ok. I mean I mainly taste the flavor of garlic and butter. The snail itself didn't taste like anything. I also had some of their shrimp cocktail. I don't think this was worth it. Tastes like something I can make at home.Dessert:Crème Brule: was good. I had some from my friend. Reminds me of flan.Profiteroles: This dessert was interesting. It's like a crème puff ice cream sandwich. A little bit hard to eat. The bread (puff) part is kind of hard but the ice cream part was good. Service:Was slooooow as the snails when they were alive. While I was properly informed by my friend that the French like to take their time perfecting their masterpiece, I found that the service in general was slow in all respects. It wasn't that busy and yet it was so difficult to get the waiter's attention. Unbelievable. I felt like a lot of time was wasted just trying to hound down a waiter who could take our order. We had one jug (?) of water which was less than the size of a 1 liter coke bottle, that finished quickly and no one bothered to refill. Some nerve this restaurant has to even suggest a minimum 18% gratuity. For the service we had, I would've left them a measly 10% ! We split the bill amongst me and my friend and my share including tip came out to be about $60. Mind you I wasn't even that full. Ugh. Despite my meh experience with French cuisine, I do want to give French breakfast a try, but of course it would definitely have to be someplace else.

This is a place is in Bryant Park, which appears only during holidays. The place is super packed. There is a line to get inside. I had to wait in line for 30 minutes to get inside. It is very tough to get a seat inside. I came for a chimney cake from stackery. Chimney cake as such was very expensive, and didn't found it special.

Love this place. Pizza is freakin awesome!  Ambiance is pure NYC. Stand up tables. Service with an attitude. Sirens wailing on the street.  Grape sodas in the fridge.I had the Sausage and caramelized onions.  One slice set me back $6.50.Whole pies are two slices and you save 50 cents.Pizza is deep dish like. Nice toasted crust and gobs of cheese.It's NYC.

Second time here and the food was just as I remembered; too good! I've gotten the Dibi Lamb both times with jollof rice "red rice" and a side of plantains. It's the perfect combination and the onions they add are such a yummy addition. I've also had the grilled whole fish and it was delicious! Flavor packed and filling of course. I will say that the frozen veggies they put on top of the rice is a huge after thought. They were cold and not fully cooked. As for the customer service here, it's much better than their peers by miles. So while my standard doesn't change for what good customer service is, I felt welcomed and was greeted with a smile as soon as I sat down. Unfortunately I had to get up to finally have my card run, but it's not a huge deal. Lastly, prices are a bit high so beware of any additions to your food. Will be back soon. Probably for both the grilled fish and dibi lamb.
This place is good. Nice place, modern, like the music. The service was good, they take a little extra time to bring us the food but also give us some extra plates from house and that was nice.

I honestly don't know what happened to this place--very dysfunctional. I rarely give 1 star to any establishment, but my recent experience with this place was extremely unpleasant. For appetizers, my boyfriend and I got their 3 kinds sashimi ($18) which consists of tuna, salmon, and yellowtail. It smelled very, very fishy. To avoid food poisoning, we had to send this back. Needless to say, we never tried to return food at a restaurant but this was our first time. Upon telling our waitress this, she got offended and started becoming aggressive saying, "you don't want it? you don't want it? Ok." Upon getting the bill, they still charged us for the sashimi appetizer that we did not eat. No apologies, no accommodations--nothing. Our water was served in the middle of our meal and we had to keep flagging our server for the bill. Waste of $63. Never coming back.

An OK brunch spot. I thought the food was average quality, the drinks were comparable to any other typical bottomless experience ($22), and service was a little slow (although I think that was more due to it being busy, didn't seem personal). I ordered the breakfast waffle sandwich ($17) and didn't really think much of it. It's made with fresh seeming ingredients, but I remember it being a little cold.Overall I didn't think it was bad per se, but just nothing to write home about. Glad to have tried but not gonna make an effort to repeat unless friends want to go.

I absolutely adore this gem of a restaurant! Every aspect, from its prime location to the delectable food and reasonable prices, shines. Recently, I visited for a tasting event and it was sensational. My friend and I indulged in 'The Godfather' crepe – a must-try for carnivores, packed with juicy, flavorful goodness. We also savored the classic combination of Nutella with banana and strawberry, a foolproof choice for anyone with a sweet tooth. Count me in as a regular!

- Navya J@nyconthetable

I came here twice and got a totally different experience in term of food. It is a decent size restaurant with many sakes option. The service was good during both times. From the way they communicate with each other, it doesn't seem like this is open by a Japanese person. Still the food was way better than other restaurants around the neighborhood. Below are the food you have to get. Ahi tower - it was full of flavors. With the size of the tower, it was definitely enough to fill you up. Salmon Osaka - it is a half cook with torch, very tender like melt in your mouth with fresh salmon taste. Hamachi Kama - grilled collar of yellowtail fish. Eat it when it is hot or it might be fishy. All the combo sushi were alright. Quality was better than most of the restaurants but you are paying a higher price for them. Sashimi and sushi set of 8 piece can fill up a person. Then you can add up for your party size of which combo to get.

Title: A Korean Delight Direct to Your Desk - Bap's Delivery Shines!

I stumbled upon Bap via Yelp while in a dire hunt for Korean stew and oh, did it hit the spot! Not only did they deliver straight to my workplace, but the punctuality of service was impeccable. My first foray was the Galbi lunch combo; a sumptuous spread of marinated galbi, a variety of ban chan, and a comforting small kimchi stew, all accompanied by a soda for just over $18. Yes, it was a bit of a splurge for lunch, but the flavors justified every penny.

On a second occasion, I went all-in with the full-size kimchi stew. The balance of seasonings and the heat level were nothing short of perfect. Paired with rice and roasted seaweed, it's the kind of meal that doesn't just fill you up, it warms the soul.

If takeaway from Bap is this satisfying, I'm brimming with excitement at the thought of dining in. For now, their delivery has undoubtedly won me over—highly recommended for those looking to satisfy their Korean cuisine cravings without leaving the office!

A little pricey for my taste however you get a decent amount of food with your order. I ordered the Chicken karaage with curry and found that it had a slightly off taste. Other than that the fries were amazing! The Chicken/pork set was $13.50, curry $4.00 and the Okonomiyaki fries were $9.50.

Man I'm glad I found this place on Yelp! We were complete newbies in NYC this weekend, so I was flying blind when making reservations for dinner. This was one of the best meals I've had this year. It's a neat take on "surf & turf" with 5-star lobster & steak but in a more casual setting. We tried the oysters, the bisque, the lobster bites, and the combo which includes both a 1-pound lobster and 6oz burger. All delicious and fantastically priced! Worth making a reservation!

Came here on a cold and rainy night. Made sure to look for "Mama's Eatery" and found it right away. I was very pleasantly surprised when I walked in and saw how clean, modern, and spacious it was! I recall seeing some reviews calling it a hole-in-wall... Seriously bro you haven't even seen the real hole-in-walls -.-I ordered the curry chicken with pancakes. The chicken was thigh meat, tender and well-marinated. There were also potatoes in the curry, which was just how I liked it. The curry itself wasn't really spicy, which was fine by me, but it also was less flavorful and more watery than what I was used to, and hence the 4-stars rating instead of 5. Thai and Indian curries are more vibrant and flavorful, and Japanese curry is thicker and more peppery; this fell short of all of the above. The pancake/roti though... was where the dish redeemed itself - worth getting as a side. Good portions; would have been a bit too much for me had I chosen noodles or rice.Unlike most places in Chinatown, Mama's Eatery/Asian Spicy Curry takes credit cards and has friendly service.

Title: A Night to Forget at the BBQ Spot

I'm generally a fan of this BBQ joint, but my latest visit after a movie premiere at the Regal was a letdown. It was a quiet Tuesday evening, and yet the staff seemed overwhelmed. The highlight initially was the mango margarita, which was a refreshing start until it ended up all over me, courtesy of a speedy busser. His immediate reaction was to blame me, which was both shocking and disheartening. It’s quite distressing to find oneself the center of attention for all the wrong reasons.

Trying to shake off the incident, I hoped my go-to order of chicken and waffles with henny sauce would turn the night around. Unfortunately, the meal was served lukewarm, further adding to the surreal disappointment of the evening. Even the manager's indifferent response when I voiced my concerns left much to be desired.

In conclusion, this experience has soured my view of a previously enjoyed spot. It's a reminder that service and quality can make or break a dining experience, and on this occasion, both were notably absent.

Title: Cozy Ambiance and Savory Delights at Loring Place

My experience at Loring Place last Saturday night was a mix of initial frustration and eventual culinary satisfaction. Despite having a reservation, our party of six faced a 45-minute wait, which was quite disappointing. Yet, the management impressively smoothed things over - a testament to their customer service.

The atmosphere of Loring Place was unexpectedly romantic and dimly lit, providing a stark contrast to its lively reputation. As for the food, we dove into a shared feast of 8 dishes, complemented by two bottles of choice wine. The baked ricotta and short ribs were the stars of the night for me, encapsulating the kitchen's prowess. However, the grandma-style pan pizza fell short for our table, as it lacked the pizzazz we found in the other dishes.

Ending our meal on a sweet note, we indulged in a single, shared dessert which rounded out the dining experience nicely. All told, Loring Place earns a solid 4 out of 5 stars - a place I would revisit, hoping for a more prompt seating next time.

The restaurant boasts an elegant interior that exudes sophistication, but the absence of windows creates a somewhat claustrophobic atmosphere, reminiscent of a casino. While the ambience is fancy, the food falls short of exceptional, especially considering the price point. Diners seeking out the Hudson Yards experience might find other venues in the area that offer both culinary delights and scenic views.

BCD Tofu House in the pulsing heart of Manhattan stands out as a sanctuary of comfort food, particularly with their signature beef soondooboo. My numerous visits here have consistently been graced with swift service, notable amid the urban rush. Even with the bustling queues, the staff efficiently manages wait times with buzzers and seamless communication via walkie-talkies.

Once seated, often on the second floor, I'm greeted with a delightful arrangement of classic Korean side dishes, paving the way for the highlight: a plate of crisp fried fish to tide over the appetite. The soft tofu soup here, particularly the beef soondooboo I invariably order at a mild spice level, is soul-warming. Served traditionally with rice and a raw egg to crack into the bubbling stone pot, it never fails to satisfy.

A thoughtful touch is the offering of warm rice tea, on the house, capping off the meal perfectly. Departing the restaurant, you're sent off with genuine gratitude from the staff, reinforcing the warm, hospitable atmosphere.

In sum, BCD Tofu House impresses with its efficient, friendly service and those little extras that elevate the dining experience. It's a place I continually return to for that spoonful of comfort amidst the city chaos. Highest praise earned indeed.

Title: A Satisfactory Veggie Burger Experience

I visited this establishment on a Sunday afternoon for a quick veggie burger and was pleased with the ample seating and the promise of free WiFi, ideal for work or streaming, although I didn't personally test the internet connection.

The interior boasted a clean and comfortable atmosphere, featuring both large communal and smaller tables. Be aware there's only one bathroom, which can lead to a bit of a wait.

I ordered the VG Beyond Burger, and it hit the mark with its meat-like yet healthier patty. The menu mentioned a house-made sauce, which I didn't detect, but the burger was flavorful enough to stand on its own without the need for extra condiments.

The meal included a choice of side, and while the server only mentioned fries, soup, or broccoli, I noticed an upcharge could get you alternatives like cauliflower mash, sweet potato fries, or a salad. I opted for the regular fries, and they were exceptionally crispy and plentiful — so much so that I couldn't finish them.

At $14, the price is slightly steep for a veggie burger, but the quality and quantity provided reasonable value for the meal.

I recently visited a charming pop-up stand in Urbanspace, NYC, and it turned out to be a delightful spot for a quick bite. I sampled the Peking duck baos, which were a tasty seasonal offering, along with a trio of dumplings. At $13, the price was quite reasonable for the area, especially considering the premium quality. I'm eager to return to try the other bao varieties, as well as their popcorn chicken, noodles, and perhaps a refreshing bubble tea. Definitely a spot worth checking out for a savory snack on the go.

Title: A Delightful Surprise at a Classy Spot

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a local gem where my gastronomic expectations were wonderfully surpassed. The culinary journey through six dishes left me particularly enamored with the Spaghetti, Short Rib & Bone Marrow Agnolotti, Roasted Beet Salad, and Oxtail Cavatelli – each dish bursting with flavor, though I did crave a touch more warmth in their serving temperature. Complementing the meal was an exceptional Old Fashioned, ranking high among those I've sampled. The atmosphere exuded elegance, perfect for a special evening out. Adding to the experience was Craig, our server, whose sincere and affable service truly stood out as a rarity in NY dining. Thanks to Craig, the night was not just a meal, but a memorable event.

Amazing atmosphere and food in Hell's Kitchen! Great place to go for Asian fusion. The lighting and the music definitely set the mood. Great for a date spot as well as for a big group dinner. Right when you walk in, you are greeted by a friendly hostess, and introduced to the nice ambience of this restaurant. They have 2 floors that have attractive decor and have a very homey feel. They have a good amount of table space and can house large parties. They also have a bar on the first floor. My favorite dish was the crispy pork belly with Chinese broccoli. The texture and the taste were amazing. I also really liked the pork chop and shrimp over vermicelli. Another must-have item is the spare rib appetizer because the tamarind sauce is just to die for. The kimchi fried rice was pretty good as well. They have great Thai iced tea, and their dessert menu features items from one of my favorite dessert places, Spot dessert bar.The service was amazing from everyone who worked here. We had a great time talking with the manager Win, who checked in on us throughout the meal and was very open and personable. I think the concept of this restaurant is very interesting because they do not mix the food from the two countries. Instead they have both Thai and Vietnamese food and make both exceedingly well. Highly recommended!

Title: A Bowl of Perfection That Stays With You

If you're craving authentic, unforgettable ramen, look no further. My last visit here still lingers on my taste buds—the rich, divine broth paired with thick, chewy noodles created a symphony of flavors that I've been longing to experience again. Each bowl is a hearty meld of fresh veggies, succulent meat, and just the right amount of spice, perfect for a winter's evening indulgence.

The pork tonkatsu appetizer was a crispy, juicy delight, evoking fond memories of my time in Taiwan. It's no wonder this cozy little spot fills up fast; it's a treasure trove of culinary authenticity. Counting down the days until I can return post-lockdown to relive the magic of this ramen haven.

Ugh I'm sorry I'm sure the food is good here but the delivery order was just bad.If you are selling noodle please have the common sense you have the separate the noodle and soup. The pho we received just a blob of noodle way soaked in the soup merge into something not edible. Waste of food.Then the rice became just okay because we were mad.

Ordered from here tonight. I ordered a latte and gluten free penne fettuccine Alfredo. Order arrived early and was hot. Only reason they get stars. The latte was only 3/4 full and was bitter. I like my latte a little more creamy and a sweet roasted bean (light roast). Not for me. And it was $5! Waste of my money. It came with rock candy. Very bizarre. I gave that away. It was wrapped and packed neat at least! No spills. The alfredo...I've had so much better at Romano Pizza in Weehawken NJ just recently that this was a 2 at best. It's great that they offer gluten free penne. I wish it were gluten free fettuccine. The alfredo sauce needed pepper and was pretty bland. It was not worth $19.35!! It was a smaller portion size than I thought too. I'm disappointed. I will not be ordering from here again.

We came in after a show, not planned for a dinner but we were hungry. It was off hours, so very few patrons. Service was very nice. We were two ladies ordering salad but still will "modifications". Margarita was perfectly made, cold, refreshing, with my choice of Tequila.Cobb salad, Pear and Goat cheese salad. Both were very fresh and tasty!! I forgot to  ask for my dressing in the side, bc most places will stanch the salad. This one has just the right amount  of dressing! Long story short: Great place! Arrived, food, drink. Music is cool too, ambiance and great place to watch your game! See ya next time!!

Our group of 4 decided to drop in on a Tuesday night and there was still a 15 min wait. This place is fairly small and located in a seemingly random location without any other restaurants around. I decided to deviate from the normal curry and noodle options and ordered the gra prow kai dow which is minced chicken, string beans, basil sauce, chili garlic puree, and fried egg. This was a chef's special on the menu that I thought was absolutely delicious. A nice bonus was that the special includes jasmine rice. The fried egg is actually runny on the inside and the minced chicken has tons of flavor especially with the basil. The portion size was larger than expected and I thought this dish was a huge success.

Delicious food at a good price with fast service. Would recommend! If you come in a smaller group be prepared to sit facing a wall or sharing a table with some other people.The fried chicken is delicious, not too fatty and not too much dough. The beef was a tad too fatty but very flavorful. The curry is very authentic to what Japanese curry typically is. My only complaint is the rice... I've been spoiled by the delicious rice in Japan and this just doesn't measure up.

Visited Kenka for the first time around 9:45pm yesterday and it was lively.My wife, friends, and I wanted Japanese food and we visited Kenka. When we arrived, there was a lot of people standing around waiting for their names to be called. We were excited because that usually means the food is good? We put our names down, 30-40 mins passed and we were ushered to our table. When we entered and sat down, I immediately knew this wasn't a 'restaurant' lol. It was an izakaya or casual Japanese pub. We stayed, ordered our pitcher of Sapporo, and a bunch of dishes to share amongst the table. My favorite was the okonomi yaki (Japanese pancake). The $8 dollar pitcher was a good deal too.My two cents, although the food wasn't bad, don't come here expecting the best Japanese food in all of Manhattan. Come here for the experience, the ambience, and a good time with cool people.

My experience here wasn't 100% because I was getting over a cold. I literally got my food and had to have them box t to leave I felt sick. BUT I was in love with the interior of this place. Super clean, very bright. Fun little touches. When I finally got to eat my egg sandwich a few hours later it still tasted really good, and the fries!!! Because they were so crispy when hot they didn't get sad and mushy by the time I ate them. I can only imagine how much better everything was when it was hot but I can't wait to come back here!

I had a delightful visit to this charming restaurant where the staff shone with their attentive and pleasant demeanor. The flavors across the board were impressive, making for a pleasing dining experience. My only quibble was with the Beijing style dalumen, which could have benefited from a more generous portion of beef. However, the establishment's cleanliness, especially the bathrooms, added to the overall positive impression. Certainly an above-average culinary outing.

Review for dinner service:Next level goodness! Came with a large group who ordered an array of appetizers. Everything I tasted was very good and the devil eggs were some of the largest I've ever seen. For my main I was torn between the French dip (which was a huge portion and a big feature of the restaurant) or the potato crusted salmon- I opted for the salmon and I was not disappointed. The whole dish had flavors that were very balanced and the salmon was cooked perfectly. It was also a decent size portion.The only potential downside was that it was very loud inside and was a bit difficult to hear. They had several birthdays with an extravagant sparkler which was fun to watch but left a bit of smell after it burned out. I would definitely return and try the French dip next time!

"$7 lychee martini, sangrias 5pm to 10pm everyday". That's all you need to know to come here. And they are delicious too. The lychee martini is amazing and a bit strong which is good because you can tell that they add more alcohol than just sugar. I've also had the rose sangria which was good but not as good as the lychee martini. And you can have as many as you want for $7 till 10pm. I've come here 3 times, twice to celebrate birthdays of my friends. We've had a blast thanks to the supply of cheap cocktails. Food wise it's not bad. I really liked the spicy chips, it is actually spicy and has a kick to it. The dumplings were good too. Lo mein the noodles are thin and the coconut rice in Verlaine stir fry is delicious and seems healthy. So the two times I've celebrated birthdays here, the waiter remembered to bring the dessert in the end only once. And they charged us for it too which is fine. The last time I went, I came in super early to tell the waitress to being the dessert I'm the end and say happy birthday. She said sure we can do that. BUT SHE NEVER DID IT! She forgot. So when my friend went to the bathroom, I asked her wheres the birthday cake and she says, "Oh sweety you have to tell me that in the beginning because it takes a while for the cake to come." I did tell her, I came early from work before my friend to tell her that and she said she'll bring it. She wasnt apologetic that it was her mishap, she put the blame on me. She asked me if I wanted the cake but it would take 10 minutes for it come and I have to pay for it. Sadly this was when we were done with the food and ready to go and since it was Wednesday we had work so we had to leave. My friend did ask me about the cake surprise when we left and I felt disappointed.Never in my life has any restaurant staff ever forgotten to bring a candle lit dessert in the end, and if they forget it they make up for it and bring something quickly. And most restaurants dont charge for a birthday dessert either.In short, come here for the drinks. Dont celebrate any birthdays here.

Title: A Quintessential New York Gem

Review:

This gem is undoubtedly one of my all-time favorites in NYC - a true embodiment of the vibrant New York dining scene. Tip: arrive at opening time to dodge the inevitable queues. Trust me, the wait is justified. I've indulged in virtually every dish on offer, with the edamame dumplings occupying my daydreams regularly. The succulent steak and the indulgent truffle mac and cheese stand out as personal highlights. Not once have I encountered disappointment, and it's my go-to spot for impressing visitors. An emphatic recommendation for anyone seeking a taste of the city's finest.

The special for this month was a US wagyu ramen and a spirit lifter which is a curry vegetable broth. I got the US wagyu ramen and it was great. They use noodles from sun noodle so it has a slightly chewy texture and so good. The broth was good and it came with 3 slices of US wagyu along with corn. It fits about 8-10 people and you stand while you eat. You have to write your name on the board that they have outside and a server will call out your name. Each month they have something new so check them out!

Title: A Gem for Croissant Connoisseurs

If you're a fan of expertly crafted pastries, this charming eatery is a must-visit. I've adored their chocolate almond croissants since day one, though a pro-tip is to arrive early as they're often claimed before lunchtime. Coffee aficionados won't be disappointed either; their mochaccino soothes the soul, and the cold brew is a refreshing summer staple.

The baristas here are truly accommodating, ensuring your drink hits all the right notes. Beyond pastries and coffee, they offer a satisfying selection of salads, sandwiches, and juices, all customizable with toasting or warming. For a sweet finale, their assortment of small cakes and mini desserts never fails to delight.

The establishment prides itself on cleanliness and efficiency. My one humble request - an increase in their chocolate almond croissant production to keep up with their well-deserved demand. Keep up the excellent work!

Reliable and affordable in the theater district . Menu has something for everyone whether you want something heavy, greasy, light, healthy- you name it. Spacious, good for groups, and easy on the ears. I generally like the burgers and sweet potato fries

What a cool place for happy hour or to watch sporting events. They have a ton of tv's and no matter where you are sitting you could probably see 2-3 tv's.  The layout is also pretty spacious with the front section being the bar area and the back having long high top tables for groups. We had a big group so we made a reservation for the tables in the back. The service is prompt and they do a good job of making you feel comfortable. I was expecting your normal average bar fare but the food was a step up from that.  It looks like they have put a lot of effort in making good food and it shows. The Nachos were some of the best I have had. Every ingredient popped with flavor and the chips were perfectly crispy.  The same thing happened with the cheese quesadilla which were crunchy and extra cheesy. They had a little chipotle mayo on top. The sliders also were pretty cooked and juicy. The wings also spot on. There was a theme here. Everything tasted like the person who cooked it had passion for what they did. That is the best way to explain it. I would definitely come back not only for the drinks/food or to catch a game but also for the service. Great place.

I recently dined at a Mexican restaurant in Hell's Kitchen and was thoroughly impressed. The service was top-notch, efficient and attentive. The menu offered an array of great, flavorful dishes that were a delight to the palate. The highlight, however, were the AMAZING drinks - expertly mixed and the perfect complement to the meal.

Despite the fierce competition in the area, this spot has won me over, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit. The one drawback, and the reason for a 4 out of 5 star rating, is the additional charge for chips and salsa. Nevertheless, this restaurant stands out as a favorite in Hell's Kitchen for a fantastic dining experience.

I've been here a couple times but my review is for the time I had takeout. I got the chicken kebab and the lamb chops. The lamb chops were amazing. Cooked perfectly and seasoned well. The lemon potatoes are also to die for. The chicken kebabs, on the other hand, were super dry. The tzatziki helped a bit to offset the dryness, but the chicken was way too overcooked for my tastes. I know this place serves good food though so giving it a 4!

Title: A Culinary Gem for Vegetarians and Omnivores Alike at NYC's Michelin-Starred Delight

I recently dined at an exquisite vegetarian Michelin-starred restaurant in New York City, which also offers a vegan menu. This establishment provided a truly remarkable dining experience that even a carnivore like me could appreciate. The culinary adventure started with their recommended dining structure - we opted for a "first order," and instead of a pair of "lighter" dishes, we indulged in three "bolder" choices, finishing with a dessert.

Although the portions were on the smaller side - a common trait in fine dining - they were a gustatory delight. The Tandoor bread paired with spiced eggplant dip tantalized the taste buds despite its modest size. The Cauliflower tempura with steamed buns, however, lacked the anticipated crunch and was marginally underwhelming; it's worth a try but I wouldn't reorder it.

The Pan-seared potato gnocchi with its divine sauce left us wanting more of the scant 8-10 pieces served, and the Tofu-skin pockets with sweet potato were unexpectedly scrumptious. For dessert, the Tandoor roasted pineapple with vegan whipped cream was an unconventional yet must-try treat, highly approved by none other than the New York Times.

The cocktail menu was a show-stopper. The Carnaval - a concoction of cachaca, pineapple, coconut, and espresso powder - was an irresistible beverage that beckoned me to order seconds. The In Pink cocktail, while well-crafted, didn't quite leave the same lasting impression.

Regarding service, we encountered a slight delay despite our reservation, but a 15-minute wait on a bustling Friday night in NYC is hardly a quibble. The service was commendable overall.

In summary, the dining experience was outstanding notably for the cocktails and most of the food offerings. The prices may reflect the smaller portions, but the quality of the flavors justifies the expense. I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit, not just for the innovative drinks but also to explore more of their culinary creations. The Michelin star is well-deserved, although the Cauliflower tempura could use a tweak.

Title: Sichuan Delights in a Cozy Setting

I recently savored the flavors of a local Sichuan restaurant, which boasted a rich menu at wallet-friendly prices within a wonderfully inviting atmosphere. My companion and I opted to share the sliced pork belly doused in a light yet piquant chili garlic sauce, alongside a serving of hearty braised chicken with chili. The pork belly enthralled us with its delicate texture, perfectly accentuated by the garlicky zest. Although the chicken packed a fiery punch that tested my spice threshold, the depth of flavor still managed to shine through, making it an enjoyable dish for those who dare.

The portions were ideally sized for sharing, leaving us comfortably satiated. I highly recommend a side of white rice, not only as a staple starch but as a respite from the heat of the dishes. The restaurant itself offers a great ambience with its tasteful decor, making it an excellent choice for those looking to experience Sichuan cuisine for the first time or simply enjoy a relaxing meal. A visit here is sure to tantalize the taste buds and provide a memorable dining experience.

I recently visited this ramen spot during their happy hour and was thoroughly impressed. The food exceeded my expectations for both its taste and happy hour value. The drinks were equally delightful and well-priced. Service did not disappoint, ensuring a pleasant experience. I'm already planning my next visit to take advantage of their fantastic happy hour deals again! Highly recommended for both food and drink enthusiasts.

I stopped by this restaurant for brunch this past weekend and had a pleasant experience. The frittata I ordered was satisfactory, though it didn't particularly stand out – I likely wouldn't order it again. On the other hand, the mushroom egg scramble received compliments from my companions. While this eatery offers a decent brunch, visitors with limited time in NYC might want to explore other top-tier brunch venues the city is renowned for. This spot could be a convenient choice if you're already in the neighborhood, but it may not be worth a special trip.

I think this will be my new favorite Thai spot! They have yellow curry, my favorite Thai dish, which is kind of hard to find. I ordered it with chicken this afternoon and wow. So flavorful, so wonderfully spicy, and not too sweet! It comes with either brown or white rice. Standard takeout size. Yum.

I appreciate the option of simple, healthy lunch salads in this area, thanks to Pax. I generally get a kale salad with chicken, olives, cherry tomatoes, mushrooms, carrots, cauliflower, and pumpkin seeds, and with a coffee and a banana, it comes out to a pretty reasonable price for midtown, especially if you don't want something deep-fried or cheesy. It's pretty boring food, as it definitely won't be a party for your tastebuds, but sometimes, boring is awesome, satisfying, and healthy, as is Pax. Hey, taste is a luxury, people. There's also rarely a line, because of the aforementioned blandness. Also, they usually have almond and soy milk! Their coffee is extremely watered down, but it's dirt cheap and it's at least half a notch better than Dunkin'. The woman working the cashier is super sweet and will remember you if you frequent for lunch. There's a standard amount of seating, with about five small tables up front. It's simplified, fresh, standard deli food. If you're looking for quick, light and cheap, eat at Pax.

Title: A Delightful Culinary Experience Marred by a Wait

I had the pleasure of dining at Retroactive in February 2018, where the culinary brilliance undoubtedly earned a 5-star rating.  Opting for the chef's platter—a bespoke delight with a no seafood request—each dish that graced our table was a testament to freshness and flavor. The highlight, however, was the Churros. A simple dessert transformed into an unforgettable treat; they are a must-try.

While the food soared high, the service faltered slightly. Despite a reservation, a 40-minute wait to be seated is a notable misstep. Although the complimentary bottle of champagne offered as an apology was appreciated, it could not completely mitigate the inconvenience of the delay. Overall, Retroactive impressed on the culinary front, with a side note of patience required for the service.

Title: Banchan Shines, Main Courses Fall Flat

My latest visit to this once-favored Korean restaurant left much to be desired. The banchan, an assortment of small side dishes, was the sole redeeming feature in an otherwise underwhelming meal. They were fresh and flavorful, with the steamed egg offering a much-needed protein boost.

The restaurant's ambiance is spacious and generally pleasant, but the inconsistent music was a distraction throughout our dinner. Service was prompt, yet the inability to accommodate separate checks was an inconvenience.
