Both main dishes failed to impress. My tteok mandu soup lacked depth of flavor, with the broth and meat both falling flat. My friend's kimchi jjigae was deemed mediocre, and certainly not memorable.

Given the disappointing experience, it's unlikely I'll return, despite the quality banchan and ambience. Two stars for effort, but improvement is needed where it matters most – in the heartiness of their main courses.

You get what you pay for which ain't much on the plate, but it's a super nice place. Even with a reservation the wait was about 45 minutes, but eventually we got seated. The lighting was dark for my liking, but the decor is beautiful. Not much of a fan of Asian cuisine, but I wasn't the birthday girl. I was looking through the menu for something familiar, and there it was. Jumbo shrimp, and not much of else. How do I finish all my meals? With something sweet, of course! Banana cheesecake, maple ice cream, spice cookie, bourbon. Now that my fellow Yelpers hit all the right sweet spots and then some.

I was in Chinatown after an appointment and my mom suggested we try out Jisu for some vegetarian food. Every once in a while, we like having Chinese style vegetarian food, even if we're not vegetarians. The service was very friendly and everyone was very helpful when we had questions about the menu. I had their knife-cut noodles with spare ribs and chicken. The chicken was really, really good. The noodles were also really good. I thoroughly enjoyed my meal. My dish was $9 and you can definitely get pretty full from it. By the time we left, the place was pretty full, so come early!

Bad picture but really good place. I certainly have enjoyed the many times I've been here - it's really a great communal spot for big groups or a fun night out. The food here is very good. I've had everything from the pretzels to the schnitzel and everything in between. My most recent time was the Turkey sandwich which was surprisingly extremely good and had lots of turkey. The soup on the side was also tasty - just a correct amount of food at high quality. I did do their special of mulled wine, which was too sweet and was too much money for a small glass, but it was warming and all of my friends loved the beer. I dont drink beer anymore but I've had their boots and many of the their beers in the past, and it's really a cool spot that's fairly traditional. Would suggest it and would love to come back soon!

I absolutely adore this restaurant! It offers plenty of seating and remarkably swift service. While it's not the fanciest place around, the generous portion sizes ensure you leave satisfied. The extensive menu caters to various tastes, including vegetarian-friendly dishes. I highly recommend starting with the fresh and crispy spring rolls as appetizers. Don't miss out on their #1 item, the large pho – it's warm, flavorful, and simply delightful.

Title: Sophisticated Flavors at an Unbeatable Value - Atoboy Review

My recent visit to Atoboy was nothing short of exceptional, providing a delightful night out for a mere $48 per person. Nestled behind an unassuming exterior, this gem surprises with its stunning interior, welcoming diners into a space that's both modern and chic.

From the moment I stepped in, the service was impeccable with attentive staff eager to address any inquiries or needs. The highlight of the drinks menu for me was the Ginger Rossi, a creative soju blend that’s as refreshing as it is unique, though their selection of wines and beers are equally appealing.

As for the fare, Atoboy's kitchen dishes out Korean cuisine that transcends the ordinary, presenting familiar flavors with an elegant twist. Each dish, from the sunchoke and endive starter to the yellowtail, beef tartare, and tender octopus, was a testament to the kitchen's prowess, save for the slightly greasy fried chicken. The portions are as generous as they are artfully plated, proving that Korean culinary artistry extends well beyond the realm of BBQ and wings.

Don't miss the ginger panna cotta—a fitting end to a remarkable meal. At Atoboy, you'll find culinary finesse at a price that's both accessible and thoroughly justified, solidifying its status as a shining beacon of Korean cuisine. Highly recommended for anyone seeking a taste of Korea's refined side.

This review is for delivery/takeout only. Overall a good option for Sashimi in midtown East Overall: 4/5Portion: 4.5/5 Value: 4/5Quality: 4/5 We got the Hokkaido Uni with choice of 2 proteins (Squid and Fluke) for $38, Uni with choice of 2 proteins (Hamachi and Fluke) for $30, and Bara Charashi ($25). The Hokkaido Uni was more buttery than the other Uni (probably local from Maine judging by the lower price point), although both were quite good. The portions were generous - lots of sashimi and rice. The quality of the fish was fairly fresh but the sushi rice left a bit to be desired in texture and quality. Although the prices were fairly high, I thought it was pretty fair for the portion size, particular for the Uni. Worth a try!

On a trip to the city a few years ago I went to Qi and loved it -- I had to return on my most recent trip and try their new location. The food seemed similar to the first time I had it and I really enjoyed my Pad Thai. I also had the cocktail of the day - not completely sure what it was but it was blue and delicious. We did have a bit of an unnecessary wait as our waitress may have forgotten to put in our orders. We waited about 25 minutes to get our drinks while watching those at tables next to us who'd come after be served quickly. There weren't a lot of chances to ask our waitress about it considering she was serving basically the whole restaurant. Nevertheless, we waited, and promptly after realizing her mistake the waitress apologized and our drinks and food came out promptly. Not the worst thing but it did kind of ruin dinner for me. I might return to Qi if I was looking for a nice Thai dinner and somewhere better had too long of a wait.

Title: A Refreshing New Find: Delectable Flavors without the Wait

If you're skeptical about trying a new dining spot, let your doubts rest and head over to this pleasant newcomer. On a busy Saturday night, we were pleasantly surprised by the absence of a wait and welcomed by a clean, spacious setting – a rarity where smoke-free air is appreciated.

Starting off with the cheese spicy rice cake appetizer, we noted the boiled egg and fish cake were amiss, which the menu had promised. Nonetheless, the generous cheese topping made it a delightful beginning. The main attraction, a pork set, did not disappoint, especially the pork belly, which showcased its high-quality even when savoured without additional condiments. The waiter deserves applause for cooking the meat to perfection.

The kimchi stew, brimming with rice cakes and pork, was comforting and packed with flavor, though it didn't stand out as exceptional. But the star of the evening was the truffle steamed egg. A dish I'm typically indifferent to was transformed into a must-have, brilliantly balancing the rich meats.

On the downside, a minor inconvenience was our wobbly table – a precarious spot for phones and drinks. Service, on the other hand, was attentive without being intrusive, with waitstaff striking the right balance of care and respect for our dining experience.

In summary, this restaurant goes beyond expectations by offering great food in a welcoming environment where you can savor the meal and leave without the lingering scent of barbecue. A return visit is definitely in the cards.

It's been years since my initial visit, I happen to come here to celebrate my company holiday dinner, we are a small firm & had one of private rooms in the back. Dinner was set up buffet style , waiter took the drink orders to begin... I ended up having some Sauvignon blanc it was good. Also tried the Passion fruit mojito not bad good taste. Food to start we had some Hummus they had a few different one's the regular  & pink color hummus were good & so was the tahini sauce good with the pita bread. On the Food, the Meatballs were very good & the Zucchini chips were great, they had a really nice taste. Chicken skewers were ok kinda dry, decent lamb chops but it had an after taste, good shrimp. there was another meat ball which I believe were crab cakes? not too bad.Brussel sprouts were ah lacked flavor, the Greek salad was not bad. For dessert we had two cakes one was like a bread pudding this was not bad & the other had flaky layers that one was better nice taste with a hint of sweetness. Service wise could improved only because when we arrived the room was not properly set up, drinks took a bit of time to come. Restaurant itself is nicely decorated specially during the holidays, the fish smell is very strong in the restaurant, decent atmosphere outside by the bar area, over all we had a nice time.

Cute restaurant in downtown Brooklyn in Dekalb market - right across from Trader Joe's. Lunch time can get busy so it can be a little wait but been able to get a table fairly quickly every time I've been here with friends. Service is good and food is good - prices are bit higher than other places. A lot of the dishes are spicy so make sure you tell them what level of spicy you want. Appetizers: Scallion pancakes, fried dumplings, dumplings in chili oil (spicy), chicken wingsEntrees:  String beans with minced pork is good, though don't really see the minced pork. Usually the salt and pepper shrimp which I enjoy. Also tried the kung pao chicken and scallion beef. All the dishes are good - they usually give rice to share with the table..different that other places when you order from the lunch menu. Overall good, but a bit pricey.Drinks: Hot tea, bubble tea, non-alcoholic drinks and a bar for drinks...good place to try for happy hour and dinner...will need to come back.

Dined  at Fig and Olive  for a work lunch today with two colleagues. We arrived around 1pm and were seated immediately without a reservation. The restaurant was buzzing with the lunch rush. We were seated upstairs. The staff was friendly and attentive. We were served bread and oil after we sat down. I wanted something light for lunch therefore I ordered the Fig and Olive Salad as it. It was perfect for what I was looking for since I didn't want to get too full. It came out quickly and all together. Also I don't think they had many vegetarian options as I thought they would.It was a great place for lunch and even though it was busy they weren't too loud.

My friends and I recently visited this local taco spot and were blown away by the flavors. We sampled a variety of tacos, each one as delish as the last. Alongside our tasty trio of tacos, we enjoyed a side of chips and guac, which did not disappoint. The drinks rounded out our meal nicely. While initially, the prices seemed reasonable, the total bill was a tad higher than anticipated. Despite that, the quick-moving line and popularity of the place are testaments to its quality. The food definitely made a lasting impression, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Highly recommended!

Title: A Mediterranean Gem in the Upper East Side

Review:

As a skeptic when it comes to ethnic cuisine outside of its native enclave, I approached Hummus Kitchen with caution. However, I was pleasantly surprised; this restaurant delivers solid Mediterranean fare that is surely a delight for the neighborhood.

The falafel was a standout, boasting a perfect texture contrast with its moist interior and exceptionally crunchy exterior. Wrapped up, it made for a fulfilling meal that tantalized the taste buds.

A special mention must go to their hot sauce – it's a revelation. Far from the run-of-the-mill Tabasco I was half-expecting, this herbaceous green concoction brought a delightful, and yes, genuine kick to the meal.

I'm eager to return to Hummus Kitchen to explore more of their menu. They've certainly earned my repeat business.

Chipotle style fast casual Thai place.  One of my favorite restaurants in the area.The food is surprisingly good for a casual place.  The curry sauces are extremely flavorful.  I typically get salmon over shredded cabbage with Penang curry, cucumber and mushroom sides, and extra fish sauce.  Beware the spicy curries really pack a punch, not watered down to American level of spicy.Portions are perfectly sized.  The choices are healthy, tasty, and low carb/paleo/vegetarian/pescatarian friendly.It's a little pricey for a walk in restaurant but honestly tastes better than any number of sit down Thai places in the neighborhood.  Lines can be very long but also move fast.  The resto is clean and usually has enough places to sit down.  Cards only no cash (thank God).

The weekend Happy Hour at this venue is a welcome surprise, diverging from the usual weekday offerings. Their Happy Hour oyster option, while not the finest, was satisfactorily fresh. The Lobster Knuckle proved to be an intriguing dish with a pleasant taste but tended to feel overly greasy after several bites. The Shrimp Ceviche, on the other hand, was a hit with its vibrant summer flavors that made for a refreshing treat.

Title: A Gem in Upper Manhattan - Fantastic for Food and Vibes

My boyfriend and I recently stumbled upon a delightful spot near Upper Manhattan and Hamilton Heights that quickly won us over with its cool and friendly staff. They were eager to offer suggestions from their menu of upscale bar food, which did not disappoint.

The atmosphere was buzzing with a younger crowd, yet it was the kind of place where anyone would feel at ease. For our appetizer, we indulged in the Kale and Artichoke Dip. It's a zesty twist on the classic spinach dip, packed with flavor and accompanied by bread that's toasted to perfection for scooping up every last bit of that hearty dip.

We paired our snack with some enjoyable drinks, which made for an excellent break in our New York adventure. Whether you're from the area or just passing through, I highly recommend dropping by this inviting establishment. It's a surefire spot to satisfy cravings and soak up some good vibes.

After going to the gym I decided to eat a burger on the way back to the hotel room because why not? I had already worked off the calories.I saw black burger and went in and was very surprised by the quality of the burger. The room itself is very small and only seats about 8 to 10 people total. it was a smaller Burger as far as burgers go so to be safe I ordered the double cheeseburger with bacon. It was just the right amount but a single Patty definitely would have been too small. The ingredients were fresh and although I'm not a big bread fan the bun was quality.they do have their own brand of root beer which I regret not trying since I am a root beer loving person. They do not offer a restroom to the public so I was not able to review that. all in all I would say it was a good experience and would encourage you to stop by however if you're hungry order two burgers or the double cheeseburger. They were very generous with the fries but I thought the fries were a little overcooked and too crunchy. I'm more of a soggy french fry person.Would I go back? Yes. What I order the fries again probably not.My rating system consists of a 3-star being exactly what you expected and neither good nor bad. A 4 means something was extra special and a 5 means you were blown away.  A 2 star rating was disappointing and a 1-star rating is terrible

Definitely need reservations and do not listen to the yelp reviews. Do yourself a favor, if you are a foodie of any sort, check out this place as it's home to the WORLD'S BEST FEMALE CHEF--HELLOOOOO?!?!  Second time here and I was a fan the first time but super impressed the second time. Definitely a place for 4 (ish) people, so you can sample more of the menu. Came here visiting from LA on a girls trip and the food was on point. We ordered several small plates and some share plates and everything was delicious and the flavors carried throughout each dish from the garnish to the salsas/sauces. It was memorable from the first to last bite. Everyone left HAPPY! We ordered: Herb guacUni tostada (small, order one pp)Crab infladito (small, order one pp or per two ppl)Black trumpet volcan--personal favorite (order one pp or per two ppl) Broccoli tamal (least fave)Black bass--best fish I've had (served 4 ladies)Duck carnitas (served 4 ladies)Dessert:Corn husk meringue Mexican chocolate Order the coffee, it's absolutely delicious and so full or cinnamon flavor; I wish they were open for breakfast so I could have my morning coffee here!

Second time I have been here and the food is excellent.  There are little things that keep it a 4 and not bumped up to a 5.  Happy hour drinks are only available at the bar, our waitress did not know the specials, and the temperature is always a a little cool.All those things can be looked past since the food is outstanding.  This place is a 5/5 for food.  The appetizers, pasta, fish, and desserts are all excellent.  The quality of food and preparation are amazing.  Will definitely be back soon (with a sweater).

My dining experience at this restaurant was nothing short of exquisite. The moment we entered, we were struck by the large, beautifully decorated space. High ceilings and an open kitchen layout graced us with a front-row view of the culinary magic, while Babu, our attentive server, made us feel right at home.

The awe didn't stop at the decor; even the restrooms boasted Japanese heated toilets, adding a touch of luxury to the overall ambiance.

As for the food - where do I even begin? On Babu's recommendation, we started with the live scallops, which were the epitome of freshness. The A5 Wagyu beef skewers melted in our mouths, and the sea bass, lobsters, and crispy tuna rice were outstanding. The sashimi & sushi platter, paired with freshly grated radish, elevated the flavors to new heights.

The restaurant's appreciation ceremony, where the chef and staff express gratitude to the customers, added a personal and warm touch to our dining experience. And the Mochi show is not to be missed – the fresh mochi in matcha and soybean flavors was chewy and irresistible, prompting us to indulge in Mochi ice cream as well.

This restaurant is the perfect destination for a date night, and I eagerly anticipate our next visit. A big shout-out to Babu for making our evening with his fantastic recommendations.

I recently visited a large, new restaurant in the West Village that captivated my taste buds with its short yet fascinating menu. The stand-out dish for me was the Swordfish Milanese, modestly priced at $24. It's a must-try main course that showcases the kitchen's talent.

Interestingly, while not delivering on its 'hot' promise, the Hot Chicken Sandwich was another culinary triumph. Priced at $15 and tucked away on the bar snacks menu, this sandwich, accompanied by some truly delightful fries, should not be overlooked.

The restaurant occupies the space of a forgettable predecessor, whose name escapes me after a single visit. My hope is that this establishment will outlast its forerunner by delivering consistently exceptional dining experiences. Based on my visit, they're on the right track.

Had a fun night here celebrating a friend birthday. Half of us got the hot pot and half got the BBQ. I personally loved the BBQ. Being able to order as mush as you like is amamzing because you can reorder whatever you love. I really liked the chicken breast and the lean beef. The other beef was way too fatty, almost like bacon. It is a little awkward having a host there trying to cook the meal over you while you have conversation. So that was not the greatest. It's not like hibachi where they come and perform and leave. We had a waiter there very frequently just roasting whatever meal was next. I did love all of the options. Being able to get some seafood in their like shrimp was tasty! The meal lasted a long time because we only had some much food made at a time. The stove is not that big. So we couldn't stuff our faces which ended up being great!The place definitely smells so you will be throwing all of your clothes in the wash after a visit.Also, when we celebrated the birthday, someone came out in the dirtiest animal costume I have ever seen. I thought my friend would get sick just touching it!All in all, it's a fun place to go to. The food was good. I was go with BBQ again ovetthe hot pot. It was busy. Definitely good for big groups.

Title: A Mixed Experience with Hits and Misses

My recent visit to this local eatery was a mixed bag when I stopped by for a dinner with friends. Despite not being very hungry, as I had just eaten before arriving, I was intrigued by their menu offerings.

**Food (3/5):** I didn't partake in it myself, but the aroma of the braised frog in hot chili oil was alluring and my friends savored it. Unfortunately, the hot and sour soup missed the mark, lacking in sourness and overly diluted—it ended up in the trash. However, the beef slices with enoki mushroom were the stars of the evening. Deceptively spicy and bursting with flavor, they left a lasting impression and a promise to myself to return just for them.

**Service (4/5):** Despite the long wait for a table and a decision to opt for takeout, the staff was accommodating. The gentleman who took our order was particularly kind and helpful, making the service a notable aspect of our experience.

**Ambience (4/5):** From what I could observe near the waiting area, the modern interior was appealing. The space was clean and well-kept, contributing to a positive overall vibe.

**Overall (3/5):** If half stars were an option, I'd lean towards a 3.5. While this place doesn’t top my list of New York Chinese restaurants, it's worth a revisit. Particularly, I'm interested in trying out more dishes when I'm not just passing through. A heads-up for future visitors: seating may be an issue during peak hours, so be prepared for a potential wait outside. 

In summary, while not a standout, this restaurant has potential, and the beef with enoki mushroom in sour soup alone is worth another visit. Stay tuned for an updated review post my next trip to New York.

Title: Perfect Spot for a Late Night Noodle Feast

I recently discovered an exceptional restaurant just a 10-minute stroll from our hotel, ideal for anyone craving a very late dinner. The standout feature here is undoubtedly the noodles – a culinary delight with a variety of options to satisfy your palate. For the best dining experience, I recommend picking your preferred noodle type first, then pairing it with a protein of your choice. For those who enjoy a bit of heat, the available Sriracha sauce pairs wonderfully with the wonton for that spicy kick. Delicious, convenient, and open late – this place is a must-visit for noodle aficionados.

These desserts! Amazing! If you are looking to try something different, this is the place to go. They have a wide selection of creative Indian desserts. I wanted to try them all, but I decided to try the cookie ladoo, chai pie ball and the besan ladoo. The cookie ladoo was for sure my favorite, but they were all delicious! The girl working was so kind and friendly! She was really enthusiastic and helpful. She said her favorite was the crack ball, so I will be back soon to try it!

Second time coming to Pecora Bianca, this time at the Midtown location. This was much more spacious compared to its NoMad counterpart.AppetizersRoasted Cauliflower Presentation was beautiful. The stacked cauliflower heads were roasted golden brown, with a clean circle of mascarpone and raisins along the plate. The cauliflower wasn't overly-mushy, and it paired well with the creamy marscapone. Grilled OctopusThe octopus came in two tentacles, and it came along with pickled purple cabbage, salty olives, and salami bits. The octopus meat wasn't overly chewy but firm. The pickled vegetables added a nice sour/salty variety. MainsSwordfishMy personal favorite dish in this dining experience. The swordfish was presented like a white steak with fennel salad, lemon/orange slices, pomegrante seeds, and a creamy lemon sauce. The center of the fish was slightly pink, so it helped me appreciate the freshness of the meat.Tagliatelle The tagliatelle  was smothered in tomato sauce and beef ragu. The pasta itself was al dente with a bit of chewiness, and the tomato sauce had all the hallmarks of a traditional bolognese.Service was great, as usual. One thing I like about this location over the NoMad one is that the interior is much larger and more spacious. Though it got a bit busy around 1:00 pm, we didn't have to raise our voices in order to make conversation. The restaurant has a relaxing, clean ambiance that's great to catch up with friends or co-workers.

Title: A Must-Visit for Mazeman Enthusiasts

If you're a ramen aficionado itching for a new twist on your favorite dish, look no further. This gem of a spot takes the crown for specializing in mazeman, the broth-less sibling of traditional ramen, and it's an experience you won't want to miss.

Don't be thrown off by the unusual setup featuring one large communal table—this quirky detail adds to the charm and the focus here is all on the food. The Mapo Tofu mazeman is a revelation with perfectly balanced flavors and an unexpected crunch that elevates the dish. For a lighter touch, the Uni Toast impresses with its subtlety, offering a truffle flavor that enhances rather than dominates.

But the true star is the Steak Mazemen. Opt to top it with an egg—trust me, it's a game-changer. The noodles boast an ideal texture, the sauce is rich and aromatic, and the steak is so tender it virtually dissolves on your palate. This dish is a symphony in which every element sings harmoniously.

I'm already planning my next visit. This restaurant is a 100% must-return spot for anyone who wants to take their taste buds on an unforgettable journey.

Title: A Lively Brunch Experience at Lips!

My latest visit to Lips marks my third time indulging in their vibrant atmosphere, and it has yet to disappoint! The performances are the undeniable highlight, providing an entertainment value that goes unrivaled in the area. Service is impressively prompt; the waitstaff excel at keeping the mimosas flowing, ensuring glasses are never empty—a much-appreciated touch!

When it comes to the food, it's fair to consider it average—though that's hardly the focus at Lips. My choice of steak and eggs was decent, with the steak cooked nicely. However, the standout was the potatoes, bursting with flavor and stealing the spotlight on my plate.

Our waitress deserves a special mention for her efficiency and welcoming demeanor. Deftly handling our large party of 11, she showed great flexibility by taking orders before our latecomers arrived, which was much appreciated. Her attractiveness was a charming bonus to her excellent service.

Ginger Snaps, the host, brought the house down with humor, keeping us all in high spirits. Each visit has offered a consistently fantastic show, making Lips a top recommendation for anyone looking to have an unforgettable time with friends. Whether it's for the spectacle or the bubbly, this is where you want to be for a memorable brunch outing!

It's really one of my favorite Chinese restaurants in NYC. It's more like a mix of Shanghainess food and Cantonese food. My bf and I ordered crab meat soup dumplings (pretty authentic), and BBQ pork buns, one of their branding dishes. I like the creativity in the BBQ buns although it meets more the taste of Americans. Tao Jiao egg tarts were full of milky flavors (but almost too much). Fish filet tasted fresh and tender. Ginseng soup was not great. But overall I'd like to recommend this place.

Title: A Cozy Christmas Day Lunch with a Crispy Twist

My family and I were delighted to find this restaurant open on Christmas Day, escaping the impending rush by arriving just before noon. The post-12:30 pm waitlist bore testament to its popularity.

Service was mostly smooth, marred slightly by an initial oversight - we were neglected a water service while neighboring tables weren't. This minor hiccup was soon forgotten as we settled at the bar, a vantage point I personally enjoy for watching the chefs at work.

Having visited their 55th location, I found this branch more spacious. My go-to dish, a special menu pork cutlet with fried oysters, lived up to my expectations. The combo sets, complemented with miso soup and salad choices, though pricier than average, delivered on the promise of delicious, crispy satisfaction.

For anyone with a fried Japanese food craving, I'd recommend this spot without hesitation.

I recently visited a local diner that definitely brought the cool factor. Their burger lineup was satisfying, with the Bison Burger paired with sweet potato fries being a particularly good choice. Though I ordered mine medium-well, it came out more on the well-done side, so I suggest sticking with medium for a juicier patty. While I missed out on trying their reputed shakes, I found the staff to be the real highlight—welcoming, attentive, and friendly. It’s a spot I'd be willing to give another shot.

Title: A Night of Ups and Downs at [Restaurant Name]

My dining experience at [Restaurant Name] was a roller coaster of emotions due to a mix-up with our Pulsd deal, but the culinary delights partially redeemed the evening.

Upon arrival, I had confirmed our reservation with the host, who was also the manager, ensuring that we could use our Pulsd ticket in the main dining area. However, a miscommunication led to an awkward moment when we were asked to move to the bar/lounge after being seated, a situation that was both embarrassing and handled poorly by management.

Despite the uncomfortable start, the food was the saving grace. The tapas were exceptional—a variety of flavors that tantalized our palates, complemented by a smooth bottle of wine. Standouts included the fresh sushi and perfectly crispy appetizers. The fried cheesecake, in particular, was a showstopper—simply sublime.

The service provided by our waitress was warm and commendable, marked by her friendly attitude and spot-on recommendations.

In summary, management's handling of the Pulsd deal was disappointing, but the exquisite food and attentive service from our waitress made up for the initial misstep.

If you're gujarati, and your mom/grandmother can cook well, then dont bother coming here.  Food is mediocre at best, however the ambiance is an experience.  Worth $34+? Naaaa homie.   No amount of standard veggies (mainly potatoes) are worth that much for a gujarati meal.  We told them in advance we were there for my dad's 70th birthday, but nothing special about our experience here.  My sister who lives across the country tried calling and paying for the meal to surprise him, the guy with the manbun up front wouldn't even hear her out.

Wo Hop is a gem that our family consistently relies on, especially when Chinatown is bustling with banquets. They never fail to accommodate us with a table, adding to the many reasons why it remains our top dining choice. A personal favorite of mine is their two lobsters with ginger scallion—always a delight. Their fried fish, sautéed fish fried rice, and salt and pepper jumbo shrimp are exemplary, consistently prepared to perfection. It's a place that caters to your cravings, even willing to whip up off-menu items. In short, Wo Hop delivers quality, service, and satisfaction every single visit. Highly recommended!

Fantastic spot to have a meal and enjoy a well crafted cocktail near Madison Square Garden. Lots of great bites to pick from but make sure the wings with Fresno chili sauce, sriracha deviled eggs and fries & dips are on your list.  And save room for the cheeseburger which has nice patty flavor only enhanced by its special sauce.

Title: Authentic Ramen Bliss in the Heart of NYC - ICHIRAN Times Square

Review:
Stepping into ICHIRAN Times Square doesn't just transport you to the bustling streets of Tokyo with its Showa-era themed decor; it serves up the same beloved ramen we've all come to cherish, maintaining consistent quality in an iconic New York locale.

Yes, at around $19 a bowl, it's not the cheapest option out there, but considering ICHIRAN's no-tip policy, the overall cost aligns with the city's ramen shop standards. What's exciting about this particular branch is not only its prime location but also its size, being the largest in North America, with a main floor that seats 65 patrons and a promised additional seating area for 38 more to be unveiled in April.

The new ICHIRAN app is a welcome addition for regulars, offering a loyalty program where points equal perks like a free noodle refill or even pork loin. As for the food, the ramen didn't disappoint – served hot, fresh, and customizable to personal preferences, like my noodle refill softer than the default.

The highlight on the menu, aside from their signature ramen, is the delectable matcha pudding, a must-try for dessert enthusiasts. So, next time you're in Times Square, keep an eye out for the nostalgic touches like the wooden "ticket" at the register, and dive into a bowl of ICHIRAN's finest – it’s an experience that keeps pace with the excitement of the city itself.

Came here on a Sunday night to order for takeout; probably the worst time to come since their menu is so limited on Sundays. On Sundays you can't order 5 piece, it has to be 10 pieces or more. For the 10 pieces wings, you can't get half of this and half of that, it has to be 10 of the exact same wings. And they ran out of sweet chili sauce. I order 10 pieces of inferno flavored boneless wings, with an extra inferno sauce on the side. The wings were alright. Didn't taste like wings. Probably won't get boneless again and stick with traditional. The inferno sauce wasn't that hot. Should definitely ask for a sample before ordering.
Loved the catfish rolls (rice paper)! Nothing bad to say as they havr good prices for a generous portion of pho, plus authentic Vietnamese iced coffee.

During my latest visit to the restaurant, I noticed a slight shift in the food's taste and presentation, which could have been just a personal impression. I opted for the two cold dish combo at $15, a better value than purchasing separately. However, there was a mishap: both dishes were served on one plate, causing the vegetarian mock duck to be tainted by the wine chicken sauce. It was quite off-putting, and I couldn’t enjoy the bottom layer of the food; I recommend future diners request separate plates. Additionally, the pan-fried noodles seemed to lack the generous amount of sauce they've had before. As someone who prefers them saucier, I'll need to specify this preference on my next order.

Title: A True Taste of Roman Splendor at Lupa

Rating: ★★★★★

Walking into Lupa, I was immediately enveloped by an ambiance that evokes the historic charm of Rome, accompanied by a perfectly balanced background music and noise level that made conversation a delight. The influence of Remus and Romulus is palpable, and it feels as if you've been transported to ancient times, yet with all the modern comforts.

The service at Lupa is truly unparalleled, deserving of a full five stars. Our server, Ben, was a gem behind the bar, demonstrating a remarkable command of the menu, and an impressive dedication to accommodate our Halal pescatarian needs. It is worth mentioning the incredible attention Lupa pays to dietary restrictions, thoughtfully noting them on their tickets to ensure the kitchen crafts dishes tailored to one's preferences.

From the outset, the complimentary crostini set a festive mood, followed by a stunningly presented rosemary-encrusted bread appetizer. The summer burrata, paired with heirloom tomatoes and watermelon, was a revelation—easily the top two in the city. The ricotta gnocchi, sans meat yet bursting with hand-cut pasta delight, and the pappardelle with exquisite morel mushrooms, offered a gastronomic ascent to the heavens.

The only misstep, if it could be called that, was the tagliette nero. The squid ink shrimp pasta overwhelmed my palate, tasting too intensely of the ocean for my liking. Meanwhile, the cacio de pepe bavette stood out with its classic simplicity, the aged parmigiana and black peppercorn creating a flawless Roman dish.

In conclusion, Lupa is a sanctuary for those seeking a Michelin-level service infused with an authentically Italian passion for food and a sense of familial warmth. While one dish didn't suit my taste, the overall experience was nothing short of exceptional.

Came here on a Tuesday night around 10:45 and was so impressed with my entire experience! From the service to the atmosphere, Bocca di Bacco really made a positive impression on me. This will definitely become one of my go to spots in my neighborhood.Our party of three came pretty late on a Tuesday and I was actually worried that their kitchen would be closed when we got there (I didn't believe the restaurant was really open until 1 AM). However, when we arrived they still were serving dishes and had no problem seating us for dinner. Happy to know there's a decent restaurant that's open that late in the area!When it came time to order I went with the spaghetti amatriciana sbagliata ($18). An EXTREMELY well prepared pasta dish that included smoked bacon, onion, and olives by request. This dish was so hearty I was practically rolling out of the restaurant. I'd 100% recommend this dish if you're looking for a pasta dish that's guaranteed to blow you away.Service here was also friendly and efficient. They didn't have any issues seating and serving us given the time. They made an effort to explain dishes on their menu and also gave us recommendations. A great spot for a twist on classic Italian fare. I'd recommend it wholeheartedly if you're in the neighborhood!

Title: Great Food, Service Could Improve at Hard Rock Cafe

Our recent visit to the Hard Rock Cafe proved once again that they serve great meals, though the wait times can be a bit of a bummer. Taking advantage of the wait, we browsed their store, a nice distraction that kept us occupied. 

Once seated, I indulged in the classic club sandwich paired with onion rings - both were prepared to perfection. My husband opted for the ribs, which deserve a shout-out for their fall-off-the-bone tenderness and rich smokey barbecue flavor. 

However, service didn't quite hit the high note. Our waiter started off friendly but seemingly vanished after taking our order. It was a letdown not to be checked on and quite frustrating to flag down another staff member for assistance and to package our leftovers. A simple heads-up about the shift change and a proper handoff to another server would have made a world of difference.

While the food quality is top-notch, the service hiccup has led to a lower star rating for this visit. We're hoping for a more consistent experience next time.
Kids eats free! They get a small bowl of noodle and soup with I hunk one piece of meat. Consistent taste as other locations but it's always weird paying $25 for a bowl of ramen for me.

Title: A Delightful Discovery for Coffee and More

My recent visit to this charming establishment was nothing short of delightful. Initially drawn in for a casual coffee meet-up with a friend, I was quickly impressed by its traditional, clean aesthetics paired with upscale, inviting lighting. The seating by the window adds a touch of tranquility, perfect for enjoying their interesting food selections.

Although I've yet to delve into their brunch or dinner menus, the offerings looked tempting enough to ensure my return. Nestled in a bustling area surrounded by offices, this gem also caters to the lunch crowd, making it a versatile choice for any meal.

The service was a highlight, with staff exuding friendliness and a willingness to accommodate special dietary needs without a fuss. They even demonstrated flexibility with seating arrangements, allowing my party to start our gathering before everyone had arrived.

Given the positive buzz from other reviews and my own exceptional coffee experience — do yourself a favor and try the Raf coffee; it's divine — I am eager to return. This place has secured its spot on my go-to list for both a caffeine fix and a satisfying meal.

The restaurant offers a decent selection of Chinese cuisine, although it doesn't particularly distinguish itself from others in the area. If given the choice, I find myself leaning towards other local spots for my Asian food cravings.

I recently celebrated my birthday with a delightful dinner at a charming pasta spot nestled in the West Village. The restaurant exudes warmth, particularly on the second floor which projects a cozy, homely vibe, though I'd love to return to experience its daytime ambiance.

We managed to get seated half an hour early, which was a pleasant start. The menu accommodated both family-style and individual preferences, so we indulged in a shared Burrata and a generous family portion of four cheese ravioli in Arrabiata sauce. Individual orders included Farfalle in alla vodka sauce and spaghetti with roasted garlic pecorino sauce. The attentive service enhanced our Sunday evening experience, with our waiter attending to us promptly and with great hospitality.

One standout was the fresh, made-to-order pasta, which we could watch being crafted by skilled cooks using special pasta-making equipment. The breadsticks served were notably soft and delicious. All main courses arrived tasting superb, with portions so ample we left with leftovers. To cap off the meal, the tiramisu was exceptional.

I heartily recommend this restaurant to anyone seeking authentic, freshly made pasta dishes.

I regret to report that my dining experience at this establishment was extremely disappointing. The service was lackluster, failing to create a welcoming atmosphere or attend to basic dining needs. The food, however, was the primary letdown. The happy hour chicken wings had an unpleasant, inexplicable taste, while the tangsuyuk was a far cry from its menu depiction. It appeared stale, save for a few pieces of added fried beef, and the presentation suggested a dish already half-consumed. 

Furthermore, the broccoli accompanying my meal was unacceptably soggy, contributing to an overall subpar culinary experience. To add insult to injury, I was afflicted with food poisoning the following day, enduring a relentless bout of vomiting accompanied by fever and chills. Needless to say, I have no intention of revisiting this restaurant.

TL; DR: Support Chef Malison in his brick & mortar...by getting your delivery game on...by ordering catering your office and/or event (they delivery anywhere in Manhattan!  How many other caterers do that without enormous delivery fees?!)...or do all three.  He and his team are offering the single best thai catering I've yet to source for any office/event, with a WONDERFUL main hostess to boot.  They are about personalized service and quality.  And man, oh MAN!  Do they deliver (heh).The full spread:If you follow my reviews, you know 5-stars don't happen often.  This one is WELL deserved.  I received a confirmation call within 30-mins of placing my online catering order, double checking allergies and number of people I was feeding.  Day of, the driver unfortunately got into an accident.  So the main hostess called to inform me, and she personally brought the order.  My building was a bit rude in allowing her access to my floor.  But she was patient while I resolved it, and kept her friendly smile and understanding nature the entire time.  While setting up the spread, it was remarkable how thorough yet quick/efficient she was, taking great care in presentation.  She walked me through which sauce was meant for which dish, they put the peanuts for the pad thai and papaya salad on the side just in case there was an allergy, and put the dressing on the side so the salad remained perfectly fresh and crisp.And let me tell you...every single last item was stellar (and huge! Those are all small trays, folks!).Veggie gyoza: I'm a big ole carnivore and never order these.  Yet I'd ordered again when paying out of my own pocket.  And I clocked that they package the fried items with the proper venting to allow them to remain as crisp as possible.Shrimp Shumai: Among the best I've ever had.  I was mad I only took two.  I could have devoured that entire tray.Crispy Chicken Spring Rolls: Another item I never order.  Two sufficed, since they are SO generous with how large they are.  And they were so crispy, even with delivery and being in a container!  Another item I'd gladly order again.Thai Papaya Salad: Just look at that pic!  Gorgeous.  Fresh.  Crisp.  Perfect.Pad Thai: Another item I rarely order unless I know a place.  Most places don't season it enough for the proper flavor, and/or it's dry.  This was perfectly moist, though not overdressed, with the noodles remaining al dente, the shrimp were cooked well and given tail on, providing a very nice presentation.  I'd order out of my own pocket in a heart beat (and let me tell you.  My office is primarily healthy folk who practice portion control.  Everyone's plates were piled HIGH with the stuff!).Khao Man Kai: perfect chicken with the most tender skin, and lovely ginger rice (I'm drooling while typing from the memory).  Gentle, subtle, though present flavor profiles in each bite, with a really nice side sauce.Basically, at least 2/3 of this spread are items I ordered for general palates rather than ordering my favorites.  Chef Malison has me rethinking what I order next time I get Thai delivery.Can.  Not.  Wait until the next time I need to cater.  Suross Thai Bistro is firmly at the top of my rotation.  If they continue to be as competitive in pricing and availability as they are and keep up this level of quality in food and customer service?  I'll keep recommending them time and time again!

The pizza here is pretty good (but for NY standards, wouldn't say it was amazing). I got half margherita and half ricotta with red sauce. It was good but the crust was a little too hard for me (and not in the thin crust way). The portion size was pretty big (for a 10", there were 8 pretty big slices), and decently priced. Overall it was good and one of the few places open on Christmas Eve. The food came out pretty fast and the service was good.

I won a $15 gift certificate for this place, so I made a reservation for Friday night and went with a friend. When we walked in, there was no one around to greet us, so we had to flag down a bus boy who finally found someone to seat us.This place is quite busy, loud and dark - Your standard sports bar with an upstairs level toward the back. It seems to me the thing that elevates this bar is the menu, which I found to be unique with a lot of variety. They have changed the menu since my visit and it looks even more appetizing. Also, they donate a portion of their profits to charity, which I found very cool and I do appreciate that part of their operation. My friend and I shared 2 appetizers: Italian egg rolls and risotto balls. The Italian egg rolls, with a drizzle of dark brown vinegar sauce on top, was delicious! The skin was perfectly crispy and the filling of hearty ground sausage, onion and plenty of cheese was incredibly flavorful. The meat was juicy, tender, and the addition of the other ingredients added to the tastiness. The egg rolls didn't even need the pizza sauce served on the side. The risotto balls were just okay. There were some herb seasoning but it was kind of bland and not that cheesy. For my main course I ordered the lamb sliders, which did not come with tater tots. The waitress suggested I order the tater tots as a side, which would have been $8. A little expensive for just tater tots. The lamb sliders were cute at least. The lamb was in between pita bread with tzatziki sauce, with an olive and cucumber slices. When I took a bite of the lamb slider, the interior of the meat was pink. I don't like my meat rare and I realized I was not asked how I preferred my meat cooked. I let the other waitress know and she took it back. I decided to order something different and went for one of the flat breads, consisting of pulled pork, Jack cheese and pickles. The server brought me the Buffalo Chicken flat bread, not once but twice. Finally, I received the correct type of flat bread, which was decent. There was a ton of cheese on very thin bread but not enough pork. The cubed pickles were a weird touch. I think green apples would have been a better option.When we were given the check, the lamb sliders and my friend's complimentary alchoholic beverages (received through Yelp check in) were both on there, so we had to flag down the waitress to get it corrected. The way they organized the bill by listing items as lower priced than the menu, was very confusing. They should have just kept everything the normal price then subtracted the $15 from the total. The service was abysmal throughout our time here. Our waitress was very brusque and didn't seem to know the menu well. She didn't have any patience (I was having a hard time deciding what to order) and would leave then take forever to return. There was a different waitress who was actually more friendly and helpful. I think my poor experience has turned me off from wanting to come back.

I purposely came to Noodlelove because I wanted to see the outside mural created by one of my favorite Instagram Artists, butlikemaybe. However, I ended up really loving my noodle bowl!You order at the counter and your food is placed on a tray when it's ready. The style of the inside of the restaurant is very modern. It was reasonably quiet when we went there, so there was plenty of seating for us. The cashier was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu items. I ordered the Singapore noodles with tofu. It was delicious. Each bite was very flavorful, and the bowl was not too spicy. I also really enjoyed the house hot sauce that they had. Although this place is a little expensive for causal dining, the food is really good, comes out hot, and a decent sized portion. You definitely won't be hungry when you leave. My only complaint is that I wish they would clean up the dining tables and back counter that holds the utensils a little better. I understand that the place is casual, but it wasn't very busy, so someone honestly should of wiped down the areas. I definitely want to return to try the other noodle bowls. I also would like to try some of their in house made sodas. Definitely a great place to grab lunch or dinner in Nolita!

I recently visited a local spot that's been buzzing for its trendy take on sushi—the sushi donut. It's a fun, snackable portion that tantalizes the taste buds without being overly filling. Each donut comes adorned with fresh slices of sashimi, creamy avocado, a sprinkle of fish roe, and a delightful crunch from crispy flakes. Hidden inside was a generous amount of imitation crab, a pleasant surprise that added to the experience. While I savored the novelty and flavors of this dish, my preference leans towards something more substantial like a poke bowl for my next visit. Would I recommend trying it at least once? Absolutely, for the novelty and the taste, but for those with bigger appetites, this might just be a prelude to your main course.

First time at Yokoya on a Saturday late afternoon. It was practically empty when my boyfriend and I got seated. We noticed a limited selection of ramen options but that didn't turn us off. Also, seeing Tsukemen on the menu got me super stoked. I haven't had a dipping ramen since Japan. However, I was very disappointed when I saw the dipping broth because it was a normal thin broth instead of a thick broth. The pork flavor from the broth was not rich and did not stick to the ramen at all when I dipped it. I was better off just pouring all of the broth into my bowl of ramen and eating it like a regular ramen. My boyfriend ordered the Miso tonkotsu ramen which was flavorful but salty. We also got takoyaki balls and a sake to share (no issues there). Just overall not my favorite place to get my ramen fix.

Title: Cozy Charm with a Side of Slow Service

My recent dining experience at this modern and cozy establishment was largely delightful. The ambiance struck the perfect balance between comfort and contemporary, setting the stage for a pleasant evening.

Upon arrival, a brief wait was effortlessly spent at the well-appointed bar, hinting at the restaurant's thoughtful use of space. The menu's variety did not disappoint; each dish ordered by my party was met with enthusiasm and praise. A special nod must be given to the vodka pasta – an AMAZING culinary creation that left a memorable impression.

Portion sizes are incredibly generous. Even the small servings could easily suffice for two, making it a great value for anyone looking to share.

However, it's with some regret that I must withhold a perfect score. Our experience was tainted by a lackluster service that saw us waiting for an unacceptable 20 minutes before our order was taken. While the food certainly made up for part of the disappointment, the service did cast a shadow on an otherwise exemplary dining experience.

Overall Rating: 4/5 stars – Fantastic food in a welcoming setting, if you're prepared to practice a bit of patience.

I like going to this place since it's right near my job and they have a pretty good happy hour. $5 for frozen margs and $7 for regular. They cam add in a flavored juice (I forgot the flavors, there're a lot of them) and unique sugared rums such as cilantro, rosemary and hibiscus. They have a decent taco combo- $11 for 2 tacos and a side or $13 for 3 tacos and a side. The tacos are filling and yummy, my only issue is the meat is never hot, its usually lukewarm going on cold. My biggest issue with this place is they're terrible with timeliness in serving drinks. It only takes 2 seconds to pour a frozen marg as it's already premade, yet for some reason I'm always waiting a minimum of 15 minutes. The other day, 12/20, I waited 30 minutes for a frozen marg. I put a timer on to see how long it would be and had another drink so I didnt complain right away.  When I finally told a manager, she simply said O sorry let me check the printers. The bartender then to 2 seconds to get me a drink. The manager wasn't really that helpful and didn't even try to rectify the inconvenience. That made me pretty annoyed with this place.

Title: A Slice of Tokyo in New York at Izakaya Mew

If you're aiming to capture the essence of an informal Japanese pub without boarding a plane to Tokyo, Izakaya Mew is your ticket in the heart of New York. Emblematic of the traditional after-work watering holes of Japan, Izakaya Mew comes alive at 5:00 pm sharp, and with no reservations accepted, it's a race against time to snag a seat before the 5:45 pm full house mark.

Once seated, the extensive menu at Izakaya Mew is a delightful dilemma, boasting everything from fresh sushi and sashimi to heartwarming ramen and succulent cooked meats and fish. Each dish is a hit, a testament to their dedication to quality. Sipping on their commendable house sake or a chilled Japanese beer straight from the tap only enhances the dining experience.

Efficient service keeps the evening smooth, ensuring that your focus remains on the vibrant flavors and your companions. Izakaya Mew doesn't just offer a meal; it offers the quintessential izakaya experience, ensuring a wonderful evening out. Highly recommended for a taste of Japan's casual pub culture right here in the Big Apple.

Stumbled upon this eatery while wandering the streets, my husband and I opted to sample their slices - a Crab pizza and the renowned Artichoke pizza, a savory experience sliced in half for easy sharing. Personally, the Crab pizza won me over; however, both varieties presented a saltier punch than preferred, overshadowing their otherwise noteworthy taste. Each massive slice is priced at a premium ($6), arguably steeper than the competition. While their unique flavors like Artichoke merit a one-time adventure for curious palates, the combination of high sodium content and steep prices leaves me undecided about a return visit.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at The Jin – Ktown's Hidden Gem

Upon venturing into The Jin, skepticism quickly gave way to delight as each dish exceeded my expectations in the bustling heart of Ktown. The menu, though lacking the anticipated Kimchee Fried Rice for dinner, offered a tantalizing array of options with spot-on portions that left me eagerly anticipating the next bite.

The heartwarming hospitality provided by the owner, coupled with the attentiveness of our waitress, added a layer of warmth to the dining experience. It's noteworthy that The Jin keeps their offerings fresh with periodic menu changes. Among the new introductions was the bulgogi pancake, a savory twist on a Korean staple that stood out alongside the shrimp pancake, both offering a unique take on traditional flavors.

The pan-fried dumplings deserve a special mention for their exceptional crispiness, while the chicken wings - available in both spicy and soy sauce variants - were a hit at our table. The soy sauce wings, in particular, were succulent and packed with robust flavor, earning my highest recommendation.

The Jin is an establishment I fully intend to revisit, eager to explore more of what their ever-evolving menu has to offer.

Title: A Gem in the UWS with Crafty Beers and Cozy Vibes

As a frequent visitor, I'm always eager to return to this laid-back bar in the Upper West Side. Their beer selection is top-notch, boasting an array of crafty options that caters to various palates. While the fries may not stand out, the appetizers like wings, nachos, and tater tots never disappoint.

The dual-level layout, including a playful foosball area downstairs, creates an inviting atmosphere where you can relax and enjoy at your own pace. The service is consistently friendly, and the "order at the bar" system only adds to the casual charm of the place.

This spot is a must-visit for anyone in search of a solid beer experience complemented by tasty bites in a chill setting. It's no wonder it's become my go-to in the UWS, and I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone with a penchant for good beer and a laid-back environment.

This was a really great experience! I had seen videos about this place so when I came to NY, I had to go experience it in person. When my boyfriend and I entered, we were greeted by a host at the register and asked how many people. We had 1 person in front of us. Then a waiter came out from another side and told the gentleman that he would be seated at a booth and then my boyfriend and I were told we'd get a booth next to each other and we could walk to the back to find the booth. Once we found our booth, we hung up our jackets and bags on hooks behind our booth and were told that water was self serve at the water dispenser. We were given a form to fill out of what we wanted for our ramen. I got the recommended toppings which was seaweed sheets, an egg, mushrooms. At the booth, we had a button we pushed which someone came to our individual window and took our order sheets and closed the window. They brought out our egg and toppings on one plate first. Another 5 minutes later we recieved our bowl of ramen in an enclosed container. Taking the lid off, the aroma of ramen was so good! I put my toppings in, peeled my egg and sampled the broth. Everything was super delicious! The broth was delicious and the noodles were the perfect texture I requested. I would definitely come back despite the price for everything was expensive. After we finished eating, we got up, took our jackets and bags and went to the front to pay our tab. We had been given a wooden tab that we had to take to the front with our booth number on it. The experience was super great, I loved being there and the best part was the ramen. It was the best ramen I ever had.

Title: A Fresh Vibe and Flavorful Bowls at Joju Midtown

JoJu's recent addition to Midtown has been a delightful experience. Upon arrival, the modern decor creates a welcoming atmosphere, enhanced by the convenience of order-placing kiosks.

My lunch choice, the JoJu bowl with caramel BBQ pork and sausages, hit all the right notes. Paired with a choice of brown rice, white, or salad, it allows for personal preference. The accompanying spring rolls added a delightful crunch, proving to be a delicious choice.

An absolute must-try are the JoJu fries, tossed with daikon radish, carrots, and an exceptionally flavorful spice blend. To wash it down, the lemon Thai ice tea offers a refreshing balance, thankfully not too heavy on the dairy.

Eager to return, I've set my sights on the lemongrass chicken and the array of sandwich options for my next visit. JoJu is a culinary gem for those in search of modern ambiance and a fusion of flavors.

I thought the food here was good, but not great. We started with the meatballs which were amazing and I definitely recommend. We also ordered the burata which was good, but pretty standard. Additionally we ordered the arugula and artichoke salad, but there really wasn't much flavor. We then shared the lasagna which was good, but a little too much meat inside for me. Lastly, we split the margherita pizza which was just ok. I liked that it was brick oven but there was something really sweet tasting (maybe the sauce?). Overall, it was a good dinner but not sure I would come back.

Came here for lunch and was delighted by the beautiful and elegant fall decorations. Classy and upscale ambiance. Complimentary mini pumpkin bread was brought to our table; it was warm, fragrant, and only mildly-sweet, which I really appreciated. We shared the truffled-Parmesan waffle fries, and since one person in our party was vegan, our waiter offered to set the shaved Parmesan on the side. Our server also shaved generous amount of truffle into the waffle fries basket right in front of us. The fries were crispy and ample; I've had my fair share of soggy or rock-hard fries to know that yes, you can mess up fries. For main course, I ordered the green circle chicken, which came with cotechino and green beans. The Pommery jus was poured on top of the dish in front of me. Overall, the dish was flavorful and satisfying, and I would recommend it to anyone who has a modest appetite.Granted, this is a relatively pricey restaurant, but you come here for the high-quality ingredients and impeccable service. I thought our meal was well worth the price. One thing to note though - they have vegan offerings but seems like that menu is only offered for dinner not lunch. That being said, they are extremely accommodating so they'll make it work.

Seriously incredible food. Surprisingly affordable lunch special considering that it's a cute place in the Village. Definitely loved everything we got and would recommend it--and we eat a lot of Pho and Vermicelli being from Houston!

Nestled in the bustling heart of NYC, Mew is my quintessential go-to for modern Japanese cuisine. The vibe is undeniably cool, with an eclectic ambiance that keeps me coming back for more. Among their stellar offerings, the Mew Special Roll stands out as a personal favorite – a must-try for any sushi aficionado.

True to its vibrant setting, Mew embraces a dynamic dining approach. Guests are encouraged to indulge in an array of small plates, served tapas-style and delivered to the table the moment they're whipped up in the kitchen. The experience is buoyed by a unique service style; there's no dedicated server, creating a casual environment where you simply wave down any of the attentive staff members walking by.

Be aware, though, the popularity of this gem means you're likely to encounter a wait during peak lunch and dinner hours – unless you're an early bird catching the worm at opening time. For those joining the lunch crowd, remember to hit an ATM first, as it's cash only. Mew is a dining experience that’s not to be missed for anyone looking for a taste of Japan in the heart of the city.

Title: Big Expectations, Mixed Impressions

I ventured into this spot with high hopes, mainly enticed by the colossal drumsticks boasted in online photos. My anticipation grew, thinking of the Instagram-worthy shots I'd capture.

We started off with onion rings and a seafood pancake. Although the onion rings were fairly standard, the pancake surprised us with its generous filling of seafood and a delicious accompanying sauce. Despite its smaller size compared to other establishments, it did not disappoint in taste.

Our main event, the half soy half sweet spicy wings, received mixed reviews at our table. While my partner savored them, I couldn't help feeling let down. Contrary to the photos I'd admired, our serving included smaller drumsticks, leading to a slight deduction in my overall rating, despite the kitchen's gesture of serving us extra pieces. The sauce was passable, but it failed to knock my socks off.

I'm intrigued enough to return, with the kimchi fried rice on my radar for the next visit. However, I must admit my discontent upon noticing the seafood pancake's price tag of $15 for a "TINY circle." Value for money, in this case, seemed questionable.

Rating: 3/5 Stars

Jose Andres took a page out of the Eataly playbook for his first NYC venture. This huge market & restaurant space occupies the whole basement / first floor of the new Hudson Yards mall. You can get to it by taking an escalator downstairs in the mall or walk in from the street outside. We didn't know what to expect and were impressed by how vast the space was. It focuses more on the food aspect and less on the market for groceries and kitchen items like pans and cookbooks. We did a few laps before settling on our choices - you can opt for a sit down meal at one of three restaurants, but they were not open yet either due to the newness of the space or time of day. We got tortas, patatas bravas and churros from each of their respective stands. Prices were high-ish but commensurate with NYC food. Service was friendly and pretty quick considering how busy they were (packed). Our one major issue was seating - they simply don't have enough for the demand. I estimate less than one hundred tables in the whole place with lots of lurkers hawking for seats as soon as a party leaves. We ended up standing squeezed in by one of the doors. Anyway, the food was excellent and the whole thing a really cool surprise. Great spot for a date or to spend some time browsing, if you know what you're getting into.

Pros: large slices of pizza, speedy service, conveniently located in Penn station, open until around 1am most days, has beer for purchase- bottled and draft, free refills on soda, very spacious and clean.Cons: the pizzas are actually quite pricey. I paid approximately $5.00 for 1 slice of margarita pizza. The beer was $6.00. I've had better tasting/ hotter pizza at a regular hole in the wall $1.75 a slice pizza joint. Would I return here? Probably. Since it's 1 of the only places that stay open a bit later in penn station.

Upon entering Rubirosa with modest expectations, I found myself in a snug yet inviting space. Fortune favored me with a bar seat, where I opted for a classic pizza paired with a margarita on the rocks. While the pizza didn't take top honors in my book, it was certainly a tasty endeavor. Initially, the $15 price tag for the margarita seemed steep, but the generous pour of tequila justified the cost. Observations of neighboring patrons hinted that the pasta dishes might also be a hit. The bartenders were amiable, contributing to a meal that, overall, was quite enjoyable.

Woah. Jongro was FIRE with a capital F...and IRE! The place was packed on a Saturday evening. BOTH floors (2 and 5). The wait wasn't bad since we did the Yelp waitlist. Highly recommend you add your name there for a reservation. You simply can't snag a reservation without it. We waited at the bar on the 5th floor until our table was ready...only took 5 minutes. They turn tables over here like the late Avcii. What we snagged:-LARGE beef platter. Included all the fixings. ($126) Brisket, skirt steak, ribeye, and marinated flank. The meat was super fresh and cooked by our side table chef. They even refill your sides as the dinner goes on. VERY attentive. -Drinks (mule and some beers) $12ish. -Side of white rice ($1 each) Overall, this place is a very cool experience. Highly recommend for a large gathering as you can share the large platters for 3-4. Price was a little steep, but you don't go every weekend!

I stopped by this pizza spot over the weekend and was pleasantly surprised by the unique offerings. We sampled the prosciutto with mushroom and managed to snag the last slice of prosciutto with fig — a testament to its popularity. The pizza, served in rectangular slices, stood out for not being as oily as your typical NYC fare. While prices per slice ranged from $4 to $8, the quality justified the cost.

The seating arrangement was ideal for a beautiful day, with a few outward-facing seats up front providing excellent people-watching opportunities. Additional seating was available towards the back with a few tables. I thoroughly enjoyed my visit and will definitely make a point to stop by again when I'm in the area.

The owners and staff were quite nice.  But I ordered frog's legs.  It was too sour.  Tons of vinegar I believe but creamy.My squid ink linguine with fresh crab meat was alright but something in the taste is missing.  I cannot tell what.  Maybe more seafood flavor in the white sauce?Tart tatin looked presentable but not exciting.The chocolate mousse was good - but I would like it a little darker chocolate.The choice of food in the lunch menu was disappointing so we did alacarte or the higher lunch fixed menu where the choice is much better.

Food: I had read nothing but good things about this place and sure enough, they were all right. This place was absolutely wonderful and the food was out of this world. We got there right at 8:30 and by the time we sat down and ordered, almost every table was filled. I ordered the special which was ricotta lemon pancakes with a side of bacon. Hands down, without a doubt, the best pancakes I have ever had. The ricotta whipped topping was so light, fluffy, and just the right amount of sweetness which is just how I like my whipped topping. The pancakes were a great size and just the right amount of fluffy. They are a great sharing size if you're someone like me who is never able to finish a full stack of pancakes on her own. Accompanied with the ricotta topping were raspberries that were beautifully placed on the plate. Everything combined into one bite is HEAVEN and I hope you get the chance to taste it. The bacon was cooked perfectly, there was not a piece of fat on that bacon. Friedman's bacon has now become the best bacon I have ever tasted. I could not recommend this place more for breakfast/brunch. This has become my favorite NYC breakfast spot. Service: Our waitress was sweet and helpful for all of my questions. Other: The atmosphere of this place is absolutely charming. It gives a very modern, rustic vibe that I am obsessed with. From the marble tiles to the old fashioned lighting fixtures, I was in love. Even the cute bathroom sign had me. I can't say enough good things about this place. Make sure you get there early, this place fills up quickly.

Upon arrival at Loui Loui, our greeting was delayed by five minutes and we subsequently experienced another 15-minute wait without menus or water. After flagging down the staff, we faced a perplexing question about whether we had eaten, despite our untouched, pristine table. When we finally received menus and decided on our meals, we were asked to move to accommodate a larger party, which added to the initial frustration.

Despite these service hiccups, the food proved redeeming. The mild Louisiana-flavored snow crab leg boiler was delightful, though scant on the corn and potato accompaniments—something to note for future orders. The fried shrimp with fries delighted as well, with a light, crisp breading to commend.

Highlight of the meal was the adult Capri Sun, a Prosecco-infused treat, the name of which escapes me. Despite service setbacks, Loui Loui promises a relaxed ambiance and fresh, tasty seafood offerings. The wait didn't rush the dining experience, and I am keen to return for more food and drink explorations. Loui Loui comes recommended for those willing to overlook some initial service slips for the sake of satisfying a seafood craving.

Not sure because of the restaurant week or just bad choice, the beef was tasteless and so chewy. My friend and I had the same and we both didn't enjoy the steak at all which is disappointing because I was telling my friend how great this restaurant was... I had much better food before but I couldn't prove it. However the service and ambiance are always good. Wish they served better food

Beetle house is really small but it's cute and whimsical. I love all things Tim Burton so I had to stop in especially after seeing Beetlejuice on Broadway. I went on Wednesday around 8pm and it was empty which was good because there was no wait. I heard the weekends get a little loud & crowded so I'm glad I was able to avoid that. There's a prefix menu which is $40 per person for an appetizer and entree which was very reasonable. I ordered the Jumbalaya for the appetizer and the Sweeney beef for the entree. They both were delicious especially the filet mignon. It was seasoned nicely and very tender. I'd go back just to have that again.I had the "blood bag" as my drink. It was fruity, tropical, and not strong at all. I don't know what was in it because the hostess said it was a "secret" but It gave me a little buzz. It didn't seem to have much alcohol in it which was fine, I wasn't there to get drunk. The desserts were visually stunning. I had the chocolate lava cake & raspberry sorbet and both were delectable. Because the menu is pretty limited, there wouldn't be a reason for me to return but my overall experience was wonderful & the food was delicious. Fyi: Not sure what's in the syringe shot but it's nasty. Don't get it! I'd definitely stop in again for a drink if in the neighborhood.Super fun!

SKIP THE KNIFE CUT NOODLES and go straight for the dumplings. My lamb noodle soup with knife cut noodles was so bland. The soup barely had any taste to it and the texture of the noodles were inconsistent. The outer part of the noodles were flimsy, and the middle was more thick and possibly undercooked. Hot chili oil couldn't even save my soup. But try their fried dumplings and don't forget to use their garlic soy sauce with chili oil!

I work around the corner from this place and walk past everyday for the last couple of years. My friend and I decided to pop in after doing our nails. The place was very clean and the decor was recognizable to the Greek theme. Our waiter Manny was very kind and helpful with the food selections. We started off sharing a small Horiatiki, which actually was a great portion size for 2. I ordered the fried calamari and lemon potatoes and my friend had the seafood pasta. Everything was great, very authentic and well prepared. The menu selection was quite large, so I will definitely be back again. We also had the specialty cocktails Jackie'O and the Santorini which were really great.

Title: A Blissful Revisit to Mighty Quinn's - Unbiased Delight

Having worked at this Mighty Quinn's location several years ago, I couldn't resist revisiting to see if the magic was still there - and indeed it was. My go-to meal as an employee was the lean brisket sandwich, and I can confirm it remains a savory masterpiece. The sweet potato casserole is as divine as ever, with the crunch of pecans elevating it to a must-try side dish.

Don't even get me started on the corn fritters; they're the perfect balance of sweet and savory. And the baked beans? Still amazing. A new delight is the addition of mac and cheese to their menu - it may sound unusual, but pair it with those baked beans, and you're in for a surprisingly tasty treat.

In short, the quality at Mighty Quinn's has not wavered. It's a spot where picking anything off the menu will leave you more than satisfied. Returning as a customer, I can honestly say the food is just as I remembered: utterly scrumptious.

Came here with a couple of coworkers after work a Thursday for dinner and drinks. We were seated in the outside section of the rooftop. We were concerned because it was a bit overcast and look like it might rain but they able to pull a covering over the space when it did start raining and just as quickly pulled it back once it stopped. We each had s couple of margaritas which were all good and a frose which was nice on that summer evening. We shared guacamole and chips and each got a taco platter.  All the tacos were good, although it was not much food. I would come here again. It's a cool place, especially in the summer to hang out and have drinks. And the night went on there was a DJ and the music gets really loud. So might not be the right fit if you are trying to have a romantic dinner.

Tiny and filled with delicious varied options of eggs. From the hipster vibe of the staff to the great soundtrack on loop, this was a great meal. It's cozy to be sure and you are gonna wait unless you arrive right when they open. But it is worth it. Perfectly fluffy eggs with a versatile option from mushrooms and cojita with corn to flour tortillas and cilantro with jalapenos.  It has something for everyone. I will admit that the fried chicken sandwich I almost attacked someone over was surrounded by the flakiest biscuit and butter pickles. If no other reason, I'll go back for that.

Title: A Chance Taken, Mixed Results

I recently ventured to a new dining spot with high hopes but was met with a mixed bag of experiences. The restaurant had run out of several recommended items, including their baked chicken with potato salad and kale, leaving me to opt for alternatives like candied yams and cabbage.

The chicken did not disappoint—succulent and well-seasoned, it was a highlight of the meal. The candied yams were satisfactory, though my craving remained unmet. The ribs, unfortunately, seemed to have been boiled and lacked depth until I gave them some oven time at home, transforming them into a savory treat. As for the sides, the mac and cheese was a letdown, lacking in cheesiness and moisture, suggesting it might have been a leftover portion. The cabbage, simply boiled, was unremarkable.

The saving grace was the service. The owner's personal call to discuss substitutions was a thoughtful touch, echoing the courteous service received during my visit.

In the end, I'm awarding three stars for the exceptional chicken, improved ribs (post-oven), and commendable service. While I'm hesitant to return, part of me is curious to see if this experience was merely an off day.

Title: Classic Italian Charm at [Restaurant Name]

My recent dining experience at this traditional Italian gem was nothing short of delightful. There's a sense of authenticity that resonates, perhaps a sentiment echoed by my husband, who's frequented the establishment with friends cherishing childhood memories here.

Venturing beyond the menu, we indulged in an exquisite off-the-menu appetizer - scungilli, a thinly sliced conch bathing in a vivacious spicy tomato sauce, setting an impressive tone for the meal.
