The standout dish was undoubtedly the Veal Rossini. Its tenderness and rich flavors danced on the palate, solidifying its status as a personal favorite. While the veal chop also boasted a pleasing tenderness, it somewhat paled in comparison to the other flavor-packed offerings.

Dessert, a chocolate torte, was pleasant but didn't quite reach the heights of what preceded it. However, the night was rounded off beautifully with a smooth, delicious decaf cappuccino—a perfect end to a truly enjoyable evening.

During my recent visit to the restaurant, the experience with the sushi rolls varied; some featured disappointingly small pieces of fish, while others were generously packed with chunky delights. Unfortunately, the red miso soup fell short of expectations due to a peculiar taste and an off-putting consistency, though it was on par with the standard miso soup served elsewhere. Service was adequate but not exceptional. A notable letdown was the cancellation of our dessert, despite placing the order alongside our appetizers and mains, with the excuse given that the kitchen had closed and wouldn't be reopened. All in all, the establishment earns a solid 3.5 stars, providing reasonable value for the price.

Yum! There's definitely not enough Vietnamese options in NYC, so finding this gem after moving here was a real relief. Great place to eat with friends; try to come on a slower night as the wait can get crazy. Great service and ambience. The broth is rich, noodles and meat were yummy, and the bean sprouts/lime/cilantro toppings were fresh. A bit pricier than what I'm used to paying for pho, but the whole area is pricy so it's nothing too crazy.

We were in the area to watch a broadway show and came across Mentoku. There were some great reviews posted about this place so we decided to check it out. The place was pretty empty except for 1 other table and 1 person at the bar. The service was great, super nice waitress. We got the Karage Fried Chicken to start. The chicken tasted great! Super juicy, good flavor, and great dipping sauce. Good portion size too. For our ramens, we got the Hakata Tonkichi and Yuzu Kosho. The two ramens were vastly different in taste. The Tonkichi, in comparison to the Yuzu Kosho, had no flavor. The Yuzu Kosho's peppery base is truly peppery (and salty). We probably went through a couple cups of water to try to clear our mouths of all the seasoning. The noodles were okay. The Tonkichi was also a great counteracting soup to the Yuzu Kosho. The chashu was great in both ramens. The ramen wasn't spectacular, and overpriced for the quality. I'd come again to try some other dishes, but my expectations would not be as high as our first visit. One note: the place seemed generally clean, didn't smell weird or anything, but there was some sort of fruit fly problem when I went. I'm not sure if we sat near a trashcan, but we were a table near the bar and there were so many small fruit flies that kept coming near our food. I don't think this is normal since I haven't seen it in other reviews.

Came here for dinner with a friend, as I had been wanting to try this place for a while and was in the area for a doctor's appointment. I was mostly disappointed. I got the uni, the market price of which on that day was $21 for small and $28 for large. I decided to go for the large since I love uni, and it wasn't that fresh tasting and had that weird fishy taste to it. I also got the beef, pork, and lotus root shumai and the grilled eggplant with three different kinds of miso, which were both good. My friend got the steak, which she said was excellent, and the fried chicken, which was okay. Overall the food isn't extraordinary and it's really overpriced, because it's a small plates style restaurant. We spent $115 for two people and we didn't even have drinks or dessert and weren't super full from the meal. Service is good. They take reservations but you don't really need one on a weeknight - there were plenty of empty tables.

My default order is always the Ginger Bowl w/Shio Koji Marinated Pork. It's one of their best sellers and I can see why. The ginger scallion sauce is zesty but not salty. The mix-in items blend really well together and provide a good texture. The Shio Koji Marinated Pork is really juicy and tender and I appreciate how the edges are cooked to a crisp. There's plenty of seating around since it's a big space and most people grab their food to go. They move the line pretty quickly so it's not a bad alternative to Chipotle for a more green lunch.

The restaurant is deceivingly large. I thought it would be a tiny place, but they have one large room and a smaller room with a bar. Despite the restaurant being so large, the place was packed when I came with my friend close to 8pm. We were able to get a seat at the counter near their pizza ovens without waiting. You can order one pie with two different toppings as long as the base is the same. We ended up ordering two pies, one Paul's Boutique, and one with half King Salami and half St. Louie.Paul's Boutique - Of course, we couldn't come here without trying the pastrami pizza, especially since they use Katz pastrami. I didn't think I would like the pizza because of the mustard and thousand island dressing, but the flavor was very well balanced. The pastrami wasn't very strong. I thought it would be on the salty side, but it wasn't. The best part for me was the everything bagel crust because it was so crispy. I still have a strong aversion to mustard and 1000 island dressing, so I probably wouldn't order the Paul's Boutique again, but this is definitely something to try at least once.  King Salami + St. Louie - Both pies are tomato sauce based and were very similar in taste. I have a high salt tolerance, but even the King Salami was too salty for me. We were given a small container of peppers to put on our pizzas, and the peppers were much needed to cut through the saltiness. Each half had so many toppings though. Since the place was so busy, it was hard flagging down the waiter for water, to order, to get out check etc. I didn't see him stop working once. The kitchen was also probably backed up with orders, since we waited close to an hour for our pizzas. The waiter was very apologetic though and gave us a gift card at the end of our meal (which I promptly lost...hmm where in the world did I put that gift card ¯\_(ツ)_/¯). I'll have to come back again to try their other creative sounding pizzas.

Title: A Carnivore's Delight That Even Non-Steak Lovers Adore

I'm not usually one for steak, but this NYC steakhouse has become a must-visit on every trip, and for good reason. The consistently impeccable service is matched by the quality of the food. The 16 Oz New York Strip Sirloin is a standout dish—tender and flavorful enough to convert even self-proclaimed meat ambivalents like myself.

The K Rico Chopped Salad, though on the smaller side, offers a refreshing medley of fruits and a delectable avocado dressing that perfectly counters the richness of the meat. Meanwhile, the Jalea Peruana is a generous portion of mixed seafood that delights with its variety.

The sides, particularly the quinoa with figs, brussels sprouts, and plantains, are more than just accompaniments; they're star dishes in their own right. And the desserts? Divine. The Tres Leches is a personal highlight, but you can't go wrong with any choice, as evidenced by our table's selection of the Creme Brûlée and the sumptuous Chocolate Dome.

Whether it's a birthday celebration or just a night out, this steakhouse knows how to make an occasion feel special—right down to the sparkler-topped birthday dessert. I'm eagerly counting down the days until my next New York visit and my inevitable return to this culinary gem.

***This review is based on the "Cousins Maine Lobster" food truck, I've never been to this location.******So the truck comes around a couple times a week around downtown Brooklyn & boy I'm happy they do lol. I've waited when it was a single degree & happy it's warmer now lol. I've had the lobster bisque which is creamy & well seasoned, the lobster grilled cheese is cheesy & with the lobster it's added goodness lol..I've also tried the lobster tots which were also flavorful. I've never been disappointed & curious to go to this location to try some of the other things on the menu that's not on the truck menu.

Mama Sushi is far from ordinary, seamlessly blending Latin flavors with Japanese traditions in a culinary dance that sets it apart in Washington Heights. While the fusion concept may initially raise eyebrows, skeptics are likely to be converted after a taste. Standouts include the "El Montro," "Tre Golpe," and the signature "MamaSushi" rolls, each offering a unique twist on classic sushi. Word to the wise: skip the hassle of parking in the high-traffic area and opt for the train instead, saving yourself a tedious search for a spot. Mama Sushi is a must-try for adventurous foodies seeking an unorthodox sushi experience.

I popped into the restaurant for a quick bite and was pleasantly surprised by their happy hour bargains starting at 8pm, with all bar snacks at half price. The pulled pork sandwich, at a mere $6, was a steal – juicy, flavorful, and generously portioned, although the fat content might not appeal to everyone. Also sampled the Texas twinkies, a delightful combination of jalapeño, bacon, and cream cheese, absolutely worth it at $3 for a pair. Spotted a spicy fried chicken sandwich for my next visit. One critique: the promotion could be better publicized onsite, as there were no visible signs or menus, so prior knowledge is key to enjoying these deals.

lobster macaroni, ny aged steak, mashed potatoes and green beans. i do not recommend the green beans. the flavors weren't that good but the service was great! i enjoyed the lobster macaroni and mashed potatoes. the steak was lame...

A few of my friends (true New Yorkers!) recommended this spot. Try the classic margarita pizza! Superrr thin crust and the ingredients are so fresh. Honestly the pizza looked very average but tasted great!!

Title: A Delightful Delicacy at Oriental Garden

After a gastronomic journey through Chinatown, we found ourselves at Oriental Garden, where we were met with the pinnacle of our food crawl – a splendid Canadian Crab dish seasoned with garlic and Sichuan peppers. While waiting, we indulged in Har Gow; the shrimp dumplings were a delectable teaser, generously filled and wrapped in quality skins.

The crab itself is a culinary adventure – a fun, hands-on experience that requires a bit of dexterity and the right tools to crack and pick through the shell. Be prepared for a messy affair; this is not a meal for your Sunday best, but for attire you won't mind drizzling with a bit of sauce and shell fragments.

Oriental Garden showcases their mastery with seafood, turning our meal into pure delight. Getting down and dirty has never tasted so good. If you're up for interactive dining and a flavorful feast, this crustacean extravaganza is an absolute must-try.

A lot more than just a diner, Sarabeth's serves some great meals, especially for dinner.  My niece hosted a graduation dinner for her fiancé and our extended family.  Reservations for 12 were made with no problem and seating in the large dining room was comfortable.  Note that there are also private dining rooms in the rear.  Free street parking is even available on 27th St after 6pm on a weeknight and all weekend!  When we were waiting for the rest of our group to show up, I noted that the Happy Hour menu was quite extensive and will have to come back for the $1 oysters at the bar (5-7pm).  I'm always in for Buck-a-Shuck!We started with a shared mix of appetizers that everybody was able to try.  Crispy Calamari, Ahi Tuna Tartar, Crab Cakes, Crab Meat Guacamole and Caesar Salad were all done well and each dish looked as nice as they tasted.  Ask for extra bread to soak up some of the sauces.  I opted for the prix fixe dinner which started with the Velvety Cream of Tomato Soup, which really was as velvety as promised.  My Skirt Steak Frites was flavorful, but was more overdone than my medium-rare preference.  My sister's Skuna Bay Salmon fillet was also on the dry side, but my wife's Branzino was awesome!  My son's typical non-committal comment on his Chicken Pot Pie was "Good", which I can agree on.  I drooled at my older sister's Diver Scallops & Pulpo, though.  I swear that octopus tentacle was waving to me.  There would have been some of my niece's Crab Spaghetti leftover, but my son made short work of that.Of course (pun intended), my sister's and my dinners came with dessert.  Hers was the Chocolate Truffle Cake, though really good, was kind of on the small side.  I think they committed a faux pas on my Caramelized Banana Split.  The banana halves were bruléed, but they must have scooped the chocolate ice cream on too early because it was a puddle next to the scoop of vanilla.  My son ordered the Flight of Ice Cream Sandwiches, which was a trio of stuffed cookies with chocolate, vanilla and salted caramel ice cream and looked way better than my banana split.

I recently dined at this local Italian eatery and was pleasantly surprised by the experience. Despite its affordability, the food quality held up, boasting authentic flavors that satisfied my craving for Italian cuisine. Service was impressively swift, with our meals arriving shortly after ordering, a welcomed convenience in the bustling ambiance of a near-full restaurant. Speaking of ambiance, the noise level was perfectly moderated, allowing for easy conversation without the need to raise voices. Overall, a commendable spot for a casual Italian meal that won't disappoint.

This charming Peruvian spot truly delivers on flavor and surprise. The Chicken Sandwich is an absolute winner, with the shredded chicken delighting the taste buds. However, the game-changer is the unexpected hit of sweet plantain tucked into each mouthful, mingling perfectly with the savory chicken. Add to that a perfectly toasted, crunchy bun, and this sandwich takes you on a delightful culinary adventure. Highly recommended for a taste of Peru with a delicious twist!

AN ABSOLUTELY MUST DO 4 & 3/4 STARS. THE CLASSIC CHEESE HERE IS DELICIOUSSSSSS! When you think of Classic New York Pizza by the Slice this is the kind of place that you have etched in your memory bank. They have been here since 1964 & Italian owned. They have won numerous awards & have had lots of newspaper articles written about them over the years. They have pictures of celebrity chefs like Anthony Bourdain & Curtis Stone who've gobbled up some of their famous pizza. The Interior is Old School  all the way from the booths to the brick wall to the vintage Italian family photos. They have a Menu on the wall or you can just glance at the various types of pizzas in the display window. They also have Free Delivery. NY Pizza Suprema is now in The  Ellis Island National Museum of Immigration  & is part of The "History of Pizza" Exhibit. You have to stop by & try a slice. It used to be, you had to have mega bucks & be really rich to have the Good Life, not anymore. The Game has changed. You've been Upgraded. Now You Can Live Like a King on a Limited Budget!

I have to admit I was thrilled to find this 24-hour French bistro when I arrived at my hotel three hours later than I expected due to a cold snap. I was staying at the stylish Giraffe, and they had just put away their complimentary wine and cheese for the night. I didn't feel like Korean, the easy choice for late night eats, so I rifled through the limited number of 'Open Now' options on the Yelp app. This spot was only six blocks away, but it was the longest six-block walk ever because it was so frickin' cold. When I entered, it was Paris in all its dark lighting and boulevard atmosphere.I was halfway expecting to be ignored because it was close to midnight, and I wasn't thirsty, just hungry. But no, while the bar was busy, the huge dining room was rather quiet. The server kindly led me to a prime corner table where I had a view of everything. The menu was pure bistro with the addition of several burgers. I was starving since all I had on my Jet Blue flight was one of those Mediterranean salad shakers like hours ago. Still I kept it under control and ordered three comparatively smaller dishes. First up was the $16 Belgian Endive Salad, which was heartily satisfying for a deceptively simple dish.The crisp endive spears were mixed with roasted beets, walnuts, Roquefort cheese, and cherry tomatoes (photo: bit.ly/2RIyb2O). Just what I wanted. Next was the $17 Grilled Octopus a la Provençal, a lovely appetizer portion of charred octopus drizzled with a tomato-based aioli sitting on a bed of frisée and haricot vert (photo: bit.ly/2Hn6IPD). It provided a true South-of-France feel to my meal. As a side, the $8 Wilted Garlic Spinach was the perfect green touch (photo: bit.ly/2RZXSv7) accompanied by the crusty French bread (photo: bit.ly/2Hqm85G). Sure, I shouldn't have eaten that late and probably should have had a protein bar. But mon dieu, I was in Paris... I mean New York. C'est la vie.FOOD - 5 stars...first-rate French bistro fare any time you want itAMBIANCE - 5 stars...very Parisian...in a grande waySERVICE - 4.5 stars...amazingly attentive fir midnightTOTAL - 5 stars...24/7...zut alors!RELATED - Looking for dining options in New York City? Here's a collection of places I've tried and reviewed: bit.ly/2sGleaS

Walking into this restaurant/bar you notice that all they have is high top tables. No biggie because it's basically a sports view vibe. BUT the tables along the wall are extremely uncomfortable. I had to shuffle around a few times to try to get comfortable. Now let's talk about food.Of course, Jeffrey (you got it) ordered a dozen oysters.I ordered the:Shaved Brussel Sprout Salad:Shaved brussels sprouts, roasted kabocha squash, candied pecans, red onions, pecorino cheese, & sherry vinaigrette.Jeffrey ordered:House Caesar Salad with chicken Croutons shaved parmesanWe also ordered french fries with truffle oil. Eh.My salad was ok. Nothing really to write home about. The squash was delicious. I could have eaten a huge bowl of that.His salad was just a salad. Again not amazing, not spectacular. I gave it three stars only because the food was decent, the server checked back on us (rare in New York), but the seating was really uncomfortable. I would recommend to stand up and eat if they try to seat you at the high tops in the back.

Title: A Grown-Up Diner with a Greek Twist in the Mid-Hudson Valley

Having explored several diners in the Mid-Hudson Valley, I recently stumbled upon a mature, Greek-inspired gem. The diner, reminiscent of a grown-up adolescent, exudes a sophisticated ambiance while still retaining the comfort food charm.

I was enticed by their Businessman's Lunch specials and opted for the Turkey Souvlaki Platter – an unconventional yet delightful choice. It was preceded by a chicken and rice soup that, while tasty, could have benefited from a bit more warmth. The souvlaki itself was satisfyingly nestled in a warm pita, flanked by a fresh Greek salad and uniquely cut, semi-circular thick fries which were both a visual and gastronomic treat.

Further testament to the diner's quality was the veggie burger ordered by one of my vegetarian companions; it was so authentic in appearance and taste that she sought confirmation of its meatlessness. Her satisfaction with the meal was clear as she was the first to clean her plate.

Service here was commendable – prompt and attentive. Though my visits to this part of Manhattan are infrequent, this diner's allure ensures it's on my list for future visits and is worthy of recommendation.

Everyone knows I love to eat. And I was so very excited to be going to AOC East. Partly because it was Valentines' day and partly because I read the menu about a thousand times before going in that maybe it was hard to live up to the hype I created. And partly becasue it was our 15th Valentins' day together.Let's begin. First, when you walk in you notice that its a very small space. You have to basically squeeze through the bar area to get to the other side where the actual restaurant is. When you finally get through the crawl space you are greeted by a gentleman asking if we have a reservation which we did. He begins to take us back to the table alongside the wall. The place is very crowded with the tables being on top of each other so the table was by itself was perfect.We sat for a few minutes and the server comes over with a small chalkboard with the specials written on them. I already knew what I wanted so I didn't need that. Now the food:I started with: Foie Gras Flan & Fricassée de Champignons. Now I love foie gras. This was a different experience. I have never had foie gras like this before. And honestly, I don't think I will ever order this before. The best part about this dish was the fricassée. The mushrooms were just standard mushrooms you buy at any grocery store. But I didn't want to ruin the vibe with negativity being that it was Valentines' day.Jeffrey ordered: (you guessed it)Oysters and french onion soup. Same old same old oysters and the soup tasted like Stove Top stuffing. It was very strange. The cheese was the star of that dish.For my main dish, I ordered the Classic Coq au Vin with Fresh Tagliatelles. This was the absolute best thing on the menu. This was a new experience because of the pasta. But a very delicious one. The chicken was perfect, the sauce amazing and the pasta cooked to a perfect al dente. The only thing that would have made this dish better was it could have been hotter. It was a bit too cold.Jeffrey ordered the special which was a filet mignon with potatoes au gratin and green been with a peppercorn sauce. The steak was cooked to a perfect medium rare and the peppercorn sauce really brought this dish to life.For dessert, we ordered two dishes (meaning I ordered two dishes. Luckily Jeffrey doesn't like sweets):Crème Brulee a la Fleur de Sel which was delicious. The top layer of caramelized sugar was pretty thick and it was delicious.Ile Flottante a soft meringue with crème anglaise and toasted almonds (they called it the floating island) now this dish was a little weird. Very bland with a marshmallow-like consistency meringue. Just weird.I also ordered a cappuccino, which I waited at least 15 minutes for. All in all, I don't know with the thousands of restaurants you can do so much better when choosing a French one. Would I go back? Eh. No.Food was at 3 out of 10 being we only like our main courses. Service lacked something else to be desired. The bill came up to almost $200 including tip. And we do not drink. I cannot even begin to know how much it would of been if we had.But this did not ruin my Valentines' day. My date was also the best part of my experience here and for the night.

Upon visiting this seaside gem, I was greeted by an array of impeccably fresh seafood that paired delightfully well with the stunning vistas. Despite the service being on the leisurely side and the ride there a touch brisk for my liking, the experience was enjoyable through and through. It's a must-visit spot on a sunny day, particularly for those with a hankering for lobster. A fun outing indeed!

nice, quiet, clean restaurant.clean bathroom and nice staff.you can choose two or three proteins.many options, and the additions are essentially limitless.the possible combinations are endless.my only gripe is the scoop of protein is pretty dismal especially when compared to other poke places.

I recently opted for delivery from a local pizza shop I'd often passed by, lured in by its tantalizing aromas—and I was not disappointed. My order, which included a variety of items from cheese slices to a cheese calzone and garlic knots, arrived a whole 30 minutes early, a delightful surprise! The delivery experience was seamless, with a friendly delivery person and neatly packed items.

The garlic knots were a hit, seasoned with fresh garlic and just the right size. The pepperoni roll, while leaving me wanting more than just the end piece, had a perfect pepperoni-to-cheese ratio and was enveloped in soft, flavorful dough. As for the cheese calzone, it may have been on the smaller side for its $5 price tag, but it was by far my favorite, thanks to its hot, bubbly interior and fresh cheeses.

As for the pizza, the cheese slice had a satisfyingly thin and crunchy crust, with just the right balance of sauce and cheese. The slice with jalapeño and bacon was generous with toppings, although I would have preferred fresh jalapeños over jarred. Despite that, the toppings were well worth the additional cost, especially considering the reasonable price of $2 for a whole pie.

In summary, this pizza shop offers great prices for excellent food. Whether you're craving a simple cheese slice or something more indulgent like a calzone or pepperoni roll, it's worth giving this place a try. I know I'll be returning for another round soon!

Title: Authentic Xinjiang Delights at Local Gem

I recently dined at a Xinjiang restaurant that truly impressed with its solid, hearty fare. The meal began on a high note with portion sizes that were generous – a rarity among the myriad of Asian eateries that tend toward smaller servings.

Our server recommended the big plate chicken with bones, promising richer flavor from the dark meat, and it did not disappoint. The dish was ample, easily satisfying three of us as part of our shared meal.

Though I typically shy away from lamb, my companions were enamored with the stewed lamb, praising its succulent taste. A surprising hit for me was the eggplant and potato with garlic and chili, reminiscent of a uniquely Asian potato salad, bursting with flavor. The shredded cabbage offered a pleasant, pickled contrast, while the hot and sour cucumber was exactly as expected – reliably good.

Overall, the experience left us eager to return and explore more of the menu. This restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic and satisfying Xinjiang cuisine.

This restaurant is magical. I was blown away with the food and hospitality. The servers seemed very trained and friendly. For my app I had the burrata and it was incredibly silky, laid on top of an olive salad mix. I ordered the sirloin steak for my entree and it was the only miss for this meal. Not the way it was cooked but just the quality of the steak was very hard to chew on even though the temperature was cooked to medium rare. The server and manager corrected this right away and ask me to order any entree on the menu as a replacement and I went with the seafood risotto. This is all I will be thinking about from here on out- that seafood risotto. I have no idea how it tasted so fresh and bursted with flavor while coming out so fast from the kitchen, probably magic. The fish was perfectly cooked and tossed in the tomato-y risotto. For dessert, even after a week I have been bragging about the raspberry rose tart they've served complimentary for my birthday. They pour rose water over the tart and it just somehow works so well. My colleague had ordered it so not quite sure what it's called. The donuts were just as amazing, dusted with cinnamon sugar and filled with custard. If you come before your reservation, they also have a full bar and bar seating downstairs. This is my new go to.

One of the best Mediterranean restaurants I have been to . I found them while looking on the Crave App. Decided to give it a shot. I had a made a reservation through the app. We were seated right away as the table was ready for us. They brought some complementary breads , while the waiter explained the menu. We went ahead and ordered his recommendations. Food and service was truly on point . I highly recommended it !! Ambiance- 10/10Service - 10/10Happy Hour - YESWiFi - Not Sure Reservation- RecommendedAlso they are  Halal

Whenever I'm in NY this is one of my favorite spots to go to on a night out. It's a great, buzzing atmosphere. The food is always delicious. I love their rock shrimp and crispy chicken bao bun both are absolutely amazing. I also had the wagyu gyozas which were okay but not out of this world. The drinks are great as well.

Had this few weeks ago before the COVID-19 epidemic. Happen to come across this place while I was nearby with a friend. We decided to give it a shot. For appetizers we had the Calamari, it was really good with shredded carrots on top. It was fried to perfection. Wasn't oily or anything. Also the presentation and portion was great for the two of us. For the main course we decided to go with the Margherita pizza with was wood coal I think. Also did one of their specials with was the Spaghetti Scampi which had a lobster tail, jumbo shrimps and mussels. It was really really good !!!Desert was recommended by Eleut(our waiter) and oh boy that was the highlight of the night. It was like lemony based cake. Truly couldn't have a better dinner. Service - 10/10Ambiance- 10/10WiFi - Not Sure Parking - Street

Giardino 54 is a casual, cozy restaurant with a tiny kitchen, serving hearty, no-frills Italian food. Mine was a light lasagna, not heavy like a typical Italian-American one, with the red sauce softened by cream to a dreamy orange color. It tasted the way it looked - a softer, less aggressively in-your-face "I am a lasagna" lasagna. The pasta sheets were nicely al dente, soft but not soaked; some corners had a lightly burnt crisp, and the smoke added a rustic quality to the richness of the vodka sauce.I've come to appreciate restaurants with unobtrusive music and plenty of room for sound to dissipate. This is one of those restaurants, and hence good for date night. Finding a restaurant in Hell's Kitchen that isn't Mexican, Thai, overpriced and/or trash is hard.  This cute, unfussy restaurant transported me to Greenwich village, with its multitude of casual al fresco dining options. I'll be back.

Title: Cozy Noodle Spot with Customizable Delights!

I stopped by for a Thursday lunch at 1:15 pm and encountered a considerable queue, with an estimated 20-30 minute wait time. However, by the time I finished my meal, the line had completely dissipated, so here's a tip: steer clear of peak lunch hours!

Their new junako box ramen is a culinary delight—make no mistake, it's heavy with satisfaction. Not only did it maintain the soup's warmth for an extended period, but the customization options truly catered to my tastes. I reveled in a rich, garlicky broth, and you too can tailor your noodle firmness, broth richness, and spice level to perfection.

Dining in a secluded booth adds to the experience, particularly for solo diners who'd rather not lock eyes with a stranger mid-slurp. Although I missed out on the matcha pudding this time due to a full stomach, it remains on my 'must-try' list for a future visit. A return trip is certainly in the cards!

If you're looking for value and convenience in your pizza experience, look no further. This restaurant offers unbeatable pizza, especially if you opt for the seemingly greasy selections – that's where the magic is. Steer clear of pies that have been sitting out unless you prefer a drier slice. Their cheese and pepperoni pizzas are consistently fresh and a safe bet. However, be mindful that late-night options may be limited, as I found their selection sparse at 11pm on a Saturday. Overall, a solid choice for a pizza craving without breaking the bank.

I recently dined at a restaurant where I chose the lobster ravioli and a bottled tea, setting me back $30. While the meal was enjoyable, the flavors didn't stand out as exceptional, especially given the portion size of merely six ravioli. For the price, I expected something more noteworthy. In future, I'm inclined to explore other dining options that might offer a better value.

Had the opportunity to attend an event here and after telling the front hostess, we were led into the back where there's a giant table with a lot of chairs around it. It was definitely a cramped situation in that you barely had any elbow room.There was bread and butter before the meal began which I didn't get a chance to try.First, the salads came out. I had ordered the Caesar salad and to be honest was a bit disappointed at the presentation of it, being that this place does have a high reputation. It was just pieces of cut up lettuce drenched in Caesar salad dressing with a few small pieces of croutons mixed in.Then after a while, the steaks came out. I had ordered my sirloin steak medium and it was okay. Wasn't the best I had ever had. I did notice that it was burnt to almost a crisp on one side but not on the bottom...not sure if that's how steaks are normally supposed to be served. Broccoli, mashed potatoes and spinach dip were also offered and simply tossed on the plates. It was a bit of an awkward dining experience. Finally, dessert platters came out in that there were five slices of a variety of cheesecakes and tiramisu with a mountain of whipped cream in the middle...the tiramisu was only redeeming choice on that platter. The lemon cheesecake had a weird aftertaste to it.The waiters were courteous and diligently served us during my time here and also cleared away the plates and utensils after each course was served.The bathrooms are small...only two stalls in the women's restroom...not to mention that the floor was sticky too...

As a visitor from Kentucky, I had the pleasure of dining at a unique restaurant that stands out from anything we have back home. The freshness of the food was immediately noticeable and much appreciated. Even though the place was bustling, the service was impressively quick, delivering food that was both fast and served piping hot. This establishment is a fantastic choice for brunch, and such a gem that I left wishing I could take it with me. Highly recommended!

Title: Decent Slice in the Heart of the Bustle

If you're navigating the bustling port authority area and craving a slice, this spot offers a decent option that easily surpasses the likes of 2bro dollar pizza. It's not the kind of pie you'd traverse the city for, but it's satisfactory if you're nearby.

Their pepperoni slice might disappoint if you're averse to a bit more grease, but their mushroom pizza is where they shine. The mushroom toppings are flavorful and robust, with a texture that's spot on. A delightful hint of lemon brings a refreshing brightness to the slice, making for a pleasant and unexpected flavor twist.

Overall, it's an okay place for a quick bite if you're in the area, but it may not be the pizza of your dreams.

Surprising gem right in the Central Park area.Came here with some friends for brunch on a Sunday. We received FANTASTIC service by Josiah. I was a little skeptical in trying this place since it's in such a touristy area. All I expected was ok food with not so ok prices.We had some mimosas (the waiter made sure to go lighter on the OJ which was awesome!  Brunch food was delish. Prices were what you can expect of NY. Service was excellent. They give you cute little fruit spreads. Plenty of attention and great brunch food. We came back with our friends the following day (on a Monday) and found ourselves with the same waiter that remembered us and treated us so kindly.Unexpected good food (for the area). Thanks for having us!

Title: Seafood Delight with a Side of Discomfort

Based on the high praise from my boss, I ventured into this restaurant with expectations as high as my appetite. The culinary highlight was, without a doubt, the Pasta con Lagostini. Seafood aficionados would be remiss to skip this dish, teeming with oceanic bounty and doused in a red sauce that's spiced just right to tickle the palate without overwhelming it.

A delightful surprise was the bread served with tomatoes - a novel twist to the classic table bread that proves the kitchen's creativity isn't confined to the main courses. However, I took a pass on the arancini after scoping out some less-than-stellar reviews, a decision only solidified when I noticed their underwhelming size making the rounds.

My appeal to the management: after traversing the urban jungle, patrons seek reprieve in your dining room. Your chairs, unfortunately, fall short of providing that. A meal enjoyed should extend to where one sits, and in this case, the seating detracted from the overall experience as my comfort was compromised. A change in this department would make for a perfect blend of taste and comfort.

Noticed the sign here for unlimited brunch and thought "why not?". Saturday afternoon and surprisingly not too many people inside this dressed-up restaurant.Unlimited drinks are $25 and do not include the price of the entree. That said, settled on the Croc' Rico Monsieur ($16) - a lightly fried cheese/chicken/bread concoction with a handful of well crisp fries and some greens. Simple and good flavors; needed no additional sauces. As for the drinks, the Rosé Sangria was the best of the bunch; a nice bubbly hit that went well with the meal.Service started off slow, then ramped up thankfully (you want to get your money's worth obviously). A more civilized version of the boozy brunch.

I really enjoyed my meal here at The Tang. Some items can be slightly pricey, but overall, decent portion sizes and you can definitely get extremely filled up with just a few dishes. Service was great-- everyone was pleasant and kept my water cup filled! I ordered the oxtail beef noodle soup. Their broth was delicious. I've noticed a lot of other people ordering their noodle soups too. I'm assuming that those are some of their best seller here.I ordered their pork dumplings in chili oil. There were 2 chili peppers next to that option (indicating spicy levels), so I was expecting it to be a tad spicy. Unfortunately, it wasn't spicy for me at all. It was a mediocre item for me, but other items on their menu were still incredibly delicious.My favorite item from them was the pineapple shrimp fried rice. They served it in a pineapple and it was absolutely delicious. I definitely feel like this item is a must try.I've also had their Chongqing spicy popcorn chicken. It was EXTREMELY crispy. I loved it and it was served with a lot of chili peppers. Their seared beef short ribs were delicious as well. So flavorful. The roasted egg plant also really surprised me-- they topped it with bonito flakes, giving it extra flavors and textures. There are still a bunch of items I really wanted to try. I wanted to try their scallion pancake w/beef tartare, but unfortunately, they told me they were sold out for the day (I'm not sure if this happens frequently for them). Will definitely make another visit back!

Fast casual restaurant with no frills. Dinner was tasty and my Taiwanese dining companion approved of the flavors. I ordered the noodles with the broth, but next time would probably go for the "dry" version: the broth was only a-ok and made eating the dish actually harder. The pot stickers were super yummy!

I had an incredible dining experience during restaurant week at this gem of a restaurant. Each dish, from the salads to pastas, was uniquely delightful, adding a creative twist to classic favorites. The wine list complemented the meal perfectly, featuring a selection that was nothing short of delicious. Coupled with great service, this place is a must-visit. I wholeheartedly recommend giving it a try.

Title: A Dim Sum Delight Worth Returning To

My friend and I found solace from the cold in a dim sum sanctuary that was so divine, we were compelled to return the very next day. This gem offers a plethora of reasonably priced delights in a beautiful setting, attended by the loveliest staff.

We indulged in the steamed shrimp dumplings, matcha bbq pork buns, and shumai, each dish outdoing the last with their robust flavors and generous portions. The shrimp dumplings deserve a special accolade – simply the best!

The main courses, drunken noodle and pad thai, both embellished with shrimp, were executed to perfection, leaving us eager to explore the entire dim sum menu on future visits.

Pro tip: Check in on Yelp while you're there to score some adorable hello kitty custard buns. If you're a dim sum aficionado, this place is a must-visit!

Title: A Flavorful Lunch Rush at [Restaurant Name]

I recently dined at [Restaurant Name], and what a delightful experience it was! Despite its bustling lunch crowd during the week—where the line stretched to the door—this fast-casual gem did not disappoint. The concept is trendy and efficient: choose your preferred meat, sides, and spreads to create a customized feast.

The meat served was not only generous in portion but incredibly juicy, and when paired with tastebud-tingling tahini and hot sauce, it hit all the right notes. The choice of three spreads is quite standard, but the Persian eggplant, babaganoush, and hummus I selected were exceptionally savory, with leftovers to spare thanks to the generous servings.

The fluffy bread provided was a perfect vessel for the spreads, and although the yellow rice was lightly seasoned, it complemented the meal well without overpowering the other flavors.

But the true star of the show? The fried Brussels sprouts. These crispy morsels were an absolute treat, though they carried the guilt of indulgence with their detectable oil content. Nonetheless, they're a must-try.

Overall, [Restaurant Name] is a revelation for the lunch crowd seeking quality food in a hurry. Highly recommend!

I'm a firm believer that the true test of a restaurant's merit lies not in the initial visit, but in the repeated experiences that either dull the initial shine or prove the first impressions right. Nino's 46 is one of those rare finds that not only lived up to my first encounter but actually surpassed it on subsequent visits. The consistency in quality and service is remarkable, and it's worth noting that Kris, the server, has been nothing short of stellar every time. Nino's 46 is a testament to what a dining experience should be – reliably outstanding.

Title: A Spirited Brunch at [Restaurant Name]

I recently had the pleasure of indulging in a bottomless cocktail brunch that tantalized my taste buds and raised my spirits. The star of the meal was undoubtedly the Huevos Revueltos en Salsa Verde – a dish executed to flavorful perfection. In true brunch fashion, I sipped my way through the homemade sangria, a bubbly mimosa, and their traditional margarita. The sangria emerged as the winner with its perfect balance of fruit and wine. Experiencing the joy of leisurely drinking at 11 am truly encapsulated the vacation spirit. A delight for any brunch enthusiast looking for a lively start to their day.

My best friend, her husband, and I recently dined at one of NYC's renowned restaurants during Restaurant Week, drawn in by the allure of Chef Daniel Boulud's culinary reputation. Upon arriving, our party of five was promptly greeted by a friendly host and seated at a great table as per our request.

We kicked off the evening with a delightful bottle of white Muscadet, setting the tone for a sophisticated meal. The starters were universally pleasing, my highlight being the Chicken Pate, which conjured up fond memories of authentic French cuisine I've relished in France.

For entrées, the scallops my best friend chose were tasty but modest in portion, an expected trait in the city's dining scene. Another companion's salmon hit high marks, while the DB Burgers ordered by our husbands fell short, surprisingly outshined by Shake Shack in their eyes, perhaps due to an unappreciated foie gras twist. My roasted duck breast was succulent and thoroughly enjoyed.

Dessert was a shared affair, allowing us to sample a spectrum of sweetness. While the Baked Alaska intrigued us with its presentation, the mango passion fruit proved too dominant. The ice cream, initially deemed a safe choice, emerged as the evening's sleeper hit.

In summary, our dining experience was lovely and the ambiance of the restaurant, combined with the attentive service, made for an enjoyable evening in the heart of NYC.

Tried this place for a holiday team lunch and so glad we did. Friendly service, easily got seats, food came in good time and we were in and out. Got a salad with artic char - basically similar to salmon. It had egg and avocado and generous amount of dressing. The fish was fresh. None of that fishy smell in a salad. Tried the olive oil polenta cake for dessert. Very interesting. It's like a pound cake (but with the thicker polenta taste) with hint of lemon and a kick of flavor from the sprinkled pomengranate. Ordered jasmine tea and you get the entire kettle. Pretty neat. Good lunch location for those who work in the Flatiron area.

Title: A Cheesy Revelation at Delightful Diner!

Review:
WOW is an understatement when it comes to the Baked Cauliflower Mac-n-Cheese at this charming spot! The dish was outrageously delicious, with shell pasta perfectly married to Beecher's Cheddar and accented with thin slices of cauliflower. Every component, including the delicate basil pesto on the salad greens, was spot-on. Priced at $15, its scrumptiousness ensured not even a morsel was left behind – a takeaway was absolutely necessary!

My friend's cup of tomato basil soup followed by the Chicken Lemon Campanelle – a symphony of white wine, parmesan, and spinach – received high praise as well.

The service? Nothing short of wonderful. The staff's "we aim to please" philosophy shone through, making our dining experience incredibly pleasant. The ample seating and cozy booth added to our comfort.

Though too full for dessert, the culinary excellence has me plotting a return visit. If the desserts are anything like the rest of the menu, taste buds are in for a treat!

ZADIE'S is a favorite spot for enjoying an array of fresh northeast coast oysters prepared in many delicious styles!  It's a tiny room with only high top seating (not exactly comfortable) yes, it's casual.  :)On the menu you can find oysters prepared: Pickled, Smoked, Baked, Fried, as well as Fresh & deliciously RAW with all of the accoutrements. We have enjoyed (on more than one occasion):- Oysters ROCKEFELLER - w sea lettuce, soffritto, parmigiana.- Oysters "KILPATRICK" - w prosciutto cotto, brown butter, cured egg yolk, smoked dulse. - CORNMEAL FRIED Oysters - w cucumbers, buttermilk, trout roeThere is section on the menu named "Not Oysters" and there we love:- DEVILED EGGS w bottarga (fish roe). - SMOKED BLUEFISH PATÉ w lovely brown bread.- CLASSIC CAESAR - best caeser evah!- CHICKEN LIVER PATÉ - mit pumpernickelIf you still have room after all of that, you must try their dessert:BOOZY BUTTERSCOTCH PUDDING - w sea salt, hazelnut Brittle.  It's devine! There is an ample selection of wines (bubbly, orange (yes orange), pink, white, chilled red) by the glass or bottle.  Plus chilled beer and ciders.*Select glasses of vino are half price during happy hour: 5-7PM Tuesday - Saturday + all night on Mondays*** Chef's choice: Raw oysters are $1.50 each all night every night! *****Zadie's is partnered w Billion Oyster Project! Triple Yay!!! ***

Came to Rasa a little while ago with a friend. This place was reputed to have good thai food, and in particular I felt like eating some good quality roti, which is why I came here.Not terribly crowded when I arrived. My friend got some other dish which I've already forgotten about. I asked the waitress what was the spiciest dish that they had here, and she told me it was the green curry. I asked her to make it more spicy for my order in particular. I also got the roti. The roti was just fine, honestly nothing to write home about. The curry sauce was alright as well. The green curry was pretty disappointing actually, almost no heat at all. I don't doubt that the waitress communicated the fact that I wanted a spicy dish to the kitchen; i just think they largely ignored this fact. I don't understand how thai restaurants in new york can't even manage one spicy dish. Overall however, the dish wasn't bad.In conclusion, this is probably more of a place for Americans. The flavors that they serve here are notably thai, but lack the strength of what I was looking for.

I came here for lunch on a weekday so the options I'm assuming are limited as they have a separate dinner and lunch menu. Either way, I had a pretty good experience.I got the Seafood Soontofu which I found to be pretty good. It is served boiling hot literally. You get a raw egg in which you just simply crack open into the soup and wait for the boiling soup to cook the egg which was pretty cool to see. You also get a bunch of side dishes as well, which includes a fried fish, with your order which just makes it worthwhile. I was full on the side dishes, fried fish, and soup alone which is a pretty good deal.

Title: High Expectations Meet Mediocre Reality at a Buzzing Italian Eatery

In the realm of highly acclaimed restaurants, it's always a fine line between excellence and disappointment. This particular establishment, with its no-reservation policy, demands patience and persistence. Arriving before 5 PM on a Sunday and facing over an hour's wait as a party of four, the hype was palpable. Yet, the ordeal escalated for pairs to an astonishing three and a half hour wait later in the evening — a testament to the spot's popularity.

Once seated, the anticipation met its first hurdle: a lackluster wine list. Despite the steep average price of $90 for reds, the offerings failed to impress. The cuisine, while generally good, didn't hit the heights of culinary splendor one might expect. The arancini was competent but overshadowed by an incongruous red sauce, while the burrata presentation was careless and the accompanying greens, unidentified. A serving of fried mushrooms rose above the rest with its flavorsome profile, yet the white beans and sausage dish was puzzlingly short on sausage and drenched in an unexpected red sauce.

The mains continued this theme of near misses. The pork shank special was satisfactory but fell short of memorable, and the pappardelle with lamb ragout was notably underwhelming in taste. Even the technically flawless pannacotta seemed to be missing a spark of flavor.

Service was generally efficient, marred only by minor missteps such as an unfortunate wine spill on my attire. In conclusion, while there might be merit in visiting what's billed as a top-tier Italian restaurant in New York, I'd suggest steering clear of Sundays. Perhaps the absence of the chef on this day might explain the stark contrast between reputation and experience. Would I give it another chance? The jury's still out.

Even after 3 years - this place continues to serve good food!  Specializing in seafood - prepared in many ways.This time I tried the special sea bass with truffles sauce and mushroom risotto.I highly recommend this place for people who love seafood.  They really know how to prepare seafood.

Yum.  Came in on Monday at lunch.  Got the mozzerella slice.  So huge.  Loved the crunch of the crust.  Added some red pepper flakes and garlic powder, took it to the next level ($3.50).  Hub got cheese slice ($2.75), the marinara is really good. Quick service AND we found a place to sit.

I visited this restaurant in mid-July and found the food to be decent, but not particularly noteworthy. I chose the quinoa bowl, which lacked a bit in flavor. The service, however, was commendable. Unfortunately, the lack of air conditioning during the scorching summer heat significantly marred the dining experience, as it was uncomfortable to eat while sweating. This seems like a venue that might be better suited for drinks rather than a full meal, especially during the hot season. I'm awarding it three stars with the hope that they will address the air conditioning situation soon.

Title: A Gem for Korean BBQ Lovers

Tucked away from the bustling Korea Way, this refined Korean BBQ establishment presents a modern, spacious ambiance enhanced by mesmerizing LED screens adorning the walls. The menu, brimming with traditional favorites, catered well to our late dinner cravings. We started with a savory mushroom scallion pancake and perfectly steamed dumplings.

The galbi bibimbap was a standout, with its rich flavors harmonizing beautifully with the nuttiness of purple rice—a delightful change from the ordinary. The highlight of our meal was the selection of succulent, marinated meats, expertly grilled right at our table by a server whose attentiveness could not go unnoticed.

Service throughout the meal was professional and discreet, allowing for undisturbed conversation without the usual post-Korean BBQ aromatic attire. The welcoming bar at the front promises potential for a casual drink in a stylish setting. Overall, a commendable choice for an authentic Korean BBQ experience without the typical downsides.

Title: A Disappointing Anniversary Meal at [Restaurant Name]

On an unforeseen return exactly one year later, I found myself ordering the eggplant parm from [Restaurant Name] once again - a decision I'd soon regret. Sadly, this year's experience plummeted, remarkably reminiscent of what one might endure at a desolate roadside diner or a dismal truck stop along US10. The spaghetti had the hallmarks of having languished under heat lamps for far too long, while the centerpiece, a slab of underripe eggplant, was haphazardly cloaked in partially melted cheese, requiring considerable effort to slice through. Though I managed to consume the meal, it left me feeling forlorn and decidedly unimpressed. A regrettable choice, especially on Christmas, [Restaurant Name] has unfortunately declined from a go-to spot to a cautionary tale of inconsistent quality.

Very impressive and consistent all the way! Definitely worth Five stars! I was initially planning date night at Thai Villa but also remembered that this place was in my bookmarks and we stand a better chance of getting a reservation. Ended up to be an excellent decision and we had a fantastic dinner last night. From the reservation process to actually getting seated, the staff was warm and welcoming. They also gave us a good table as requested. First and foremost, the interior design is beautiful! Felt like I'm instantly back in Thailand, plus its homey at the same time. Love the skylight at the center of the restaurant! Upon seeing the menu, I noticed the resemblance to Thai Villa and found out that they're actually sister restaurants and under same owners. Later on I read that Up Thai is also part of this group and so I'm happy that I already got to round up and experienced dining in this wonderful trifecta of the best Thai restaurants here in Manhattan! Don't ever change, guys! But I digress! Now to the food and drinks. We started off with 2 glasses of Prosecco and I love what they carry here. Perfectly chilled too and so refreshing on a warm near summer day. We had the Thai Crepe dumplings and Chicken in Pandan leaves for starters and we loved it. I especially appreciate the latter because having studied a culinary course in Thailand, I learned how to make this and they nailed this dish perfectly! My husband got the Pad Thai with Shrimp and Chicken and I think this in the top 3 Pad Thais ever in the city. The shrimp was especially so fresh and delicious. As for me, despite the many different dishes that I still wanted to order, I went ahead with my go to and favorite Red Beef Curry and I specifically said please make it regular Thai spicy but I think they still held back LOL but I'll easily forgive them for that just because the dish itself was executed so wonderfully! Dessert (we were full but we just couldn't resist) was the chocolate lava cake with Tahitian vanilla ice cream. Yummm! In between our bites, our server Kiki attended to us really well and she is just so nice and friendly. We got to talk about Thailand and our favorite Thai dishes etc and I think that the management should commend her for being so professional and nice. Thanks Kiki! It did contribute to our overall happy dining experience. As for me, I believe that this is just the start and we'll be one of the regulars moving forward. Honestly cannot wait to come back real soon!

Uncle Boon's offers a vibrant array of flavorful dishes perfect for the adventurous palate. During our recent visit, we savored the Khao Soi, which stood out with its perfect blend of coconut creaminess, subtle curry spices, and a generous serving of real chicken nestled between layers of soft and crispy noodles—a must-try for any visitor.

Although the Betel leaf wraps weren't to my liking due to their overpowering bitterness that overshadowed the sweetness of honey, my companion found them enjoyable, demonstrating the diversity in taste preferences.

The highlight alongside the Khao Soi was the tender pork dish, akin to a fine bacon but with a welcome saltiness that paired exceptionally well with Uncle Boon's own Brew, a beer that's good enough to deserve a tasting on its own.

A word to the wise: If you want to avoid the crazy wait times, opt for a summer visit when the city crowd thins out. Overall, Uncle Boon's is a delightful spot for those in search of an eclectic and robust dining experience.

Title: Hearty Breakfast with Room for Improvement

I recently visited this restaurant and sampled the biscuits and gravy skillet priced at $14. Initially, the dish was a delight with its savory taste, but it quickly proved to be overly rich for my preference. A solo endeavor into this skillet is not for the faint of heart or light of appetite. Sharing this with a friend alongside a lighter option would have been a wiser choice. The skillet does, however, offer value with 2 poached eggs and house sausage included, ensuring you won't leave hungry.

Although not the best pick for a lighter brunch, the reasonable pricing and reservation option make a return visit tempting. I'm eager to explore their lighter fare on my next weekend brunch outing.

Unfortunately, my experience at this restaurant left much to be desired, necessitating a stern review. Their "Pollo Asado" was a profound disappointment, lacking in both quantity and quality of chicken, delivering something barely recognizable as the described grilled chicken. What little poultry present resembled inedible parts of the chicken, and the rest of the dish was equally unappealing.

The poor food preparation, skimpy meat servings, and inferior ingredients prompted a complaint to UberEats, who courteously issued a refund for this misrepresented meal. Consequently, I switched to another establishment for a satisfying dining experience.

I cannot recommend this restaurant and urge them to enhance their food quality and honest portrayal of their menu offerings.

Visited this charming spot for brunch with friends and it's a must to book ahead due to its popularity. Although the seating is close-knit, contributing to the lively atmosphere, it maintains a cozy vibe. The noise level is on the higher side, but it's a small price to pay for the delightful food and refreshing mimosas on offer. I am already looking forward to my next visit.

Upon visiting the much-talked-about restaurant on a busy Friday night, I was pleasantly surprised to be seated without delay. However, my experience failed to meet the high expectations set by its reputation. The brisket served to me was unfortunately on the drier side, and the noodles lacked the substance and flavor I had anticipated, being of the thinner variety. Despite this, the broth was a highlight with its rich and robust taste, and the bone marrow provided a delicious savoriness that stood out in the dish. Be advised, an egg does not come standard in the bowl, requiring an additional $2 for those who prefer it with their meal. All things considered, this dining experience was less appetizing than I had hoped for.

Title: Hidden Happy Hour Haven

I recently discovered a delightful spot during happy hour. Despite the deceivingly small facade, the restaurant boasts ample space perfect for groups, complemented by enticing happy hour specials. Although the menu had undergone recent changes, causing the absence of the Cuban sliders I craved, the experience was far from disappointing.

For starters, I tried the guacamole appetizer; while tasty, it left me wishing for a touch more zest. However, the main course more than made up for it—the classic Cuban sandwich was executed flawlessly, satisfying my appetite with its expert preparation. The accompanying yuca fries didn't entirely capture my heart, but they were certainly not a low point.

Adding to the pleasure was a well-crafted margarita from the happy hour selection. While I didn't explore flavored options, it’s on my list for a future visit.

What truly set this dining experience apart was the service. Our server was the epitome of attentiveness, ensuring swift and seamless delivery of our meals.

In summary, if you find yourself in the neighborhood, especially during happy hour, this place is a must-try.

Title: Convenient but Room for Improvement: My Chopt Experience

As a recognized regular by Yelp at Chopt, I've frequented this place primarily for its convenience, especially on days when the weather is less than ideal. While I can appreciate the quick service and the ease of grabbing a salad in the hustle of city life, the excitement about the meals, however, falls a bit flat for me.

Their salads, largely dominated by romaine lettuce, often leave me wishing for something more memorable. That said, the Vietnam destination bowl did catch my fancy, possibly because it resonated with my Vietnamese roots, but sadly, their rotating menu means it's not always available.

I'm on a mission to find 'THE bowl' amidst their offerings, but given the stiff competition from nearby alternatives like SweetGreens and DigInn, Chopt has yet to clinch the top spot for my lunchtime cravings. It's good for a quick bite, but there's potential for so much more if they would shake up their salad game.

Came here during lunch and loved it! Not sure why they only have 3 1/2 stars. The interior is cute and clean. The staff is very polite and the food is great! I did not get a chance to take a photo of the beef soup which was my favorite! The drunken noodle was good but the soup was perfect for the cold day! I can't wait to come back and try their drinks and pad Thai! (Their lunch special also includes a side salad!)

Yummm... hands down the best tacos in NYC, in fact... in my life. Just the other month I was dreaming of Los Tacos in TriBeCa and the next thing I know... BAM!! Here it is, newly opened and located right next to the entrance of Chamber Street station. These tacos are amazing. The meat is so tender and perfectly marinated. The toppings are so fresh and made to perfection. The nachos are warm and thin just like how they make it in Texas. My goto are chicken quesadillas and carne asada quesadillas with everything in corn tortillas and the especial (fried quesadillas) with carne asada. The price is also reasonable. The ambiance is just like any other Los Tacos No. 1, there are no chairs or stools... it's pretty much almost always packed with a long line. However they do move fast. You order with the cashier and the cashier will then issue you a ticket. Then you move forward in the line and give one of the cooks your ticket. The cook will ask if you want everything in it and then make your food right in front of you.

After a long study binge, I decided to partake in another type of binge. A burrito binge.So I looked through my UberEats app, and found Tacombi as one of my options. I put in my order, and waited the 30 minutes to receive my food. I got the Pollo Yucateco Burrito. It was made with quality ingredients, and cooked with care. The Queso Chihuahua served as a delicious dip, and the other three sauces (check pics) added a spicy kick to the whole meal.This was definitely a good choice, I would consider ordering from here again the next time I'm craving a burrito.

Title: A Cozy Ramen Delight at Nakamura

I recently discovered Nakamura on the advice of my Japanese hairdresser. Tucked away in the neighborhood, this casual eatery proved to be a hidden gem for a comforting bowl of ramen. Despite its no-reservation policy, my dining companion and I secured a table on a rainy evening around 6 PM with ease, although the place quickly filled to the brim shortly thereafter.

Nakamura boasts a selection of ramen choices, but the truffle miso ramen caught my attention. As a truffle enthusiast, I was impressed by the vegan option that was far from the often flavor-lacking vegetarian broths I've experienced elsewhere. The combination of various mushrooms and the luxurious truffle essence resulted in a rich and savory broth, perfectly complementing the supple egg noodles.

My friend's shoyu ramen was satisfying but didn't quite hit the same high notes as my choice. The ambiance is straightforward with wooden decor, contributing to the simplistic charm of the venue. Service was friendly although we did have a minor hiccup with unattended water glasses.

The small space can feel crowded as diners wait inside for tables to open up. Despite this, Nakamura is a spot I'd recommend to anyone in the Lower East Side looking for an authentic and flavorful ramen experience.

I had no excuse not to come check out this latest taco dumbo location because it's literally across the street from my work. The only downside is that this place is first come first serve when it comes to seating, so when my friends and I got here every table was taken and we had to hunt to find a place to sit before all our food was ready. I love that you just go to the counter, order, and they bring your food to you. My party and I were luckily able to find some seats in the sand section(which is so cute) and the servers were able to find us pretty quickly. The food is delicious and guilt free. I love that there are vegan, vegetarian, and meat options here. Easily some of the best tacos ever. I got the guac and chips, and the chicken and fish tacos--was not disappointed. I will be back! Also, sign up for their rewards program when they ask you at the register! I already had $5 off my next order ;)

During our dinner visit to this charming spot, we were greeted with an impressive selection of beers and an appetizing menu of bar bites emphasizing Irish fare. The Shepherd's pie, in particular, was noteworthy – easily one of the best renditions I've enjoyed, with its exceptionally light crust standing out. I highly recommend this establishment for a satisfying culinary experience.

Title: Late Night Burger Delight

I stopped by this unassuming gem for a late night bite and was pleasantly surprised by the experience. The medium rare burger I ordered was juicy, packed with flavor, and cooked to perfection. Accompanying curly fries delivered the ideal crispy texture and were seasoned just right – a true comfort food classic. The portions didn't disappoint either, hitting that satisfying spot.

The service was as impressive as the meal – the staff was warm and attentive. Despite its compact size and limited seating, the vibe of this hole-in-the-wall spot added to its charm. Additionally, you get a bang for your buck with the special, which includes a drink, burger, and fries at a very fair price.

In summary, for a great post-night-out meal or just a quick, tasty burger fix, this is the place to go. Count me in for a return visit!

Really lovely place that I stumbled upon. It was not busy when we arrived around 8:30pm.seated right away. Service is fast and the servers are attentive.The menu offers 10piece Omakase for $75, but alternatively you can also choose chefs tasting menu of $25 for 5 price of 45 for 9 pieces. You don't get to choose but the lower price one you don't get wagyu or uni. It's very fair if you are not a huge uni fan, I still got my favorite otoro in the 9 prices. Really quality fish. The sauce of the bang bang shrimp is amazing, came in 4 pieces in jumbo size. Wish they could have more pieces tho. Spider roll is very crunchy, you don't even need to dip in the soy sauce already got enough flavor.

Bomb.com. That pretty much sums up my feelings about this place. Here's what you need to know: 1. Cash ONLY. Come prepared. The only ATM machine around is in front of the burger spot next door.      1a. Loved the price. $14 for a bowl that good? Sure.2. They're open late. I was hungry for ramen at 11pm on a Friday and they sat me at the bar, no questions.3. This spot seems popular. At that late hour, I had a few minutes wait in order to grab my seat.5. Fast service. I felt like I'd only just placed my order before a steaming bowl had appeared in front of me.6. Soooo gooood. I ordered the miso paitan, which includes ground pork and char siu pork. I was in heaven the whole time. I don't live anywhere near here but I'm probably going back sometime soon.     6a. The ramen broth is chicken based and many options don't have      pork, so your friends who don't do pork can join in too!

It was lunch time on a weekend, and I was in the mood for salmon. After looking through my options on UberEats, I found Trufa restaurant and the salmon sandwich that it offered. I decided to give this a try, and waiter the 30 minutes for my food to be delivered.The sandwich came in ciabatta bread, and included avocado and veggies. There was a green salad and some dressing. The sandwich was decent in taste, as was the salad. It left me feeling satisfied.I'll consider this place the next time I'm looking for a good lunch option, and I'll look forward to trying out their other dishes.

Really good fried chicken sandwiches and reasonably priced. The blue ribbon sandwich itself is not that spicy. Highly recommend the firebird to spice your life up a little bit not too spicy. Everything else on the menu is slightly overpriced in my opinion. The service is really great. Nice and chilled out spot and good music

Adrienne's Pizzabar on bustling Stone Street offers a trendy respite amidst the area's energetic nightlife. The modern, wood-accented interior and prominent bar create a chic dining environment. Despite a late arrival on a Friday night, we snagged a table for two at this hot spot. The standout was the rectangular, thin-crust pizza; its crisp yet puffy dough and use of high-quality ingredients left a memorable impression. The Tiramisu, however, fell short with just a single layer of mascarpone failing to deliver the expected richness. Despite this, Adrienne's charm is undeniable, warranting both a return visit and a hearty recommendation.

Title: A Delight for Dumpling Devotees!

My friend and I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant and were thoroughly impressed. True to its laid-back ambiance, it was the perfect setting for a relaxed dinner that left us both satiated and content.

The culinary highlight for me had to be the soup dumplings; I consider myself quite the connoisseur and these were exceptional, easily earning a spot on my top dumpling list. Regrettably, there's no photo to share – they were devoured too quickly!

In addition to the standout dumplings, we relished the Thai Style chicken wings, savory Pork fried rice, and the zesty General Tso. Each dish was fresh and packed with flavor.

Compliments to the staff as well, whose friendliness and attentiveness added to our experience. Paired with a selection of wine and beer, it made for a perfect evening.

Highly recommended for those seeking a great dinner spot, whether after work or on the weekend. Don’t miss out on this place!

Came here  Sunday night with my bf and his cousin. Great selection of craft beers!Atmosphere: Spacious and good for groups. Opens late. Not overly packed. Also has outside seating. What we ordered-Gramacy sliders with cheesy tator tots, - The sliders were very good, but I'd pass on the cheesy tots. I wasn't a fan of the cheese- schofferhofer gefeweizen grapefruit- Buffalo wings- The wings had a nice texture and, the buffalo sauce had a kick to it. -Austineast Cider - light and a little tartyService:Our server wasn't very attentive, it took awhile to bring our drink orders and left after our drink orders without taking our food order.  Also forgot to return out credit card, until we signaled to him that he forgot it when he gave us the receipt to sign.The bartender was very sweet and hospitable, :) Thank you for getting us plates and utensils! Also extra napkins.3.5 stars to be exact. Overall, not bad.

Title: A Late-Night Snack Haven That Truly Delivers!

I stumbled upon this 24/7 eatery eager to see if it could live up to its local buzz, and I wasn't disappointed. Opting for convenience, I grabbed my order to go one afternoon and was quickly impressed.

First off, kudos to them for their Happy Hour—the discounted drinks from 12-6pm are a steal. But let's talk about the real stars: the empanadas and their signature sauces. The GREEN sauce—a creamy cilantro delight—was the perfect complement to the empanadas, making me wish I had snagged a few extra packets. The RED sauce, with its spicy and somewhat sour profile, didn't quite hit the mark for me.

I sampled the much-raved-about VIAGRA empanada, a delightful pocket of seafood stew packed with shrimp, scallops, and crab meat, available in both wheat and corn flour. Wheat was the recommendation and did not disappoint with its chewier texture. At $4.25, it’s a must-try for its unique and satisfying flavor.

The SPICY CHICKEN empanada, solely wrapped in wheat flour, was another home run. Filled with succulent chicken breast cooked in a zesty picante sauce, it was already buzzing with spice without any need for added sauces.

Pro tip: A quick 30 seconds of reheating delivered the perfect taste and texture.

Overall, this place is a gem! Fantastic for a late-night bite or an afternoon pick-me-up, their empanadas with the standout GREEN sauce have won my heart. Can't wait for my next visit!

We came here thanks to the high rating in Yelp and it was worth it. The place is nicer and fancier than other Indian restaurants I've been to, but prices are still the same.The food was really good - we had the potatoes and cauliflower, and the mixed vegetables (both vegan), but the dishes weren't as big as in other places.Bottom line - good!

Title: A Delightful Shellfish Experience at Shaking Crab

My dining companion and I were in the mood for crabs or shellfish, which led us to the bustling Shaking Crab, renowned for its seafood offerings. Warm smiles greeted us upon arrival, and we were promptly seated in the lively setting filled with the happy sounds of diners and tantalizing aromas, all set to a backdrop of enjoyable music.

Our visit coincided with happy hour (daily from 12 to 6 PM, weekends included), and our server was the epitome of friendliness, providing excellent recommendations for first-timers. The Cajun fries that started our meal were superb, pairing nicely with our notably potent drinks—the refreshing Shaking Sweet Tea and the fruity Peaches-n-Shirley.

For the main course, we shared a satisfying bag consisting of a pound of shrimp, a pound of snow crab, along with potatoes and corn. The portion perfectly catered to our lunchtime appetite. Judging by the generous servings around us, it was clear why this option came recommended.

We left with the certainty of a return visit—the Shaking Crab experience was undeniably worth every moment.

I visited this dim sum spot on a weekday around 2 PM and was pleased to find it wasn't crowded. The restaurant boasted a large space, and the waiter provided excellent service. Although we weren't very hungry, we ordered a couple of dim sum dishes and received a free Hello Kitty bun for checking in on Yelp - a delightful bonus.

The Hello Kitty bun was both adorable and scrumptious, filled with a sweet egg custard. The Piggy bun, packed with red bean, paled slightly in comparison due to its dryness, yet it wasn't overly sweet, which was appreciated. Because we were quite full, we opted to take the matcha bun home, and it was surprisingly tasty, even after a delay – it surely would have been even better warm and fresh in the restaurant.

I'm already planning a return visit to explore more of their dim sum menu!

Title: Worth the Wait for Pizza Perfection

Despite the inevitable 45-minute wait or the Herculean task of snagging a reservation, surrendering to patience pays off at this bustling pizzeria. Culinary dedication shines through in every slice, particularly the Tie-Dye pizza—a triumphant trio of vodka, tomato, and pesto sauces harmoniously blanketing fresh mozzarella, sending taste buds into a state of euphoria.

Service doesn’t falter under the demand; the staff's efficiency in ordering and promptness in delivery assuage any impatience. It’s a rare place where the anticipation doesn’t just build appetite, but also appreciation.

In summary, for an outstanding pizza experience that justifies the long wait with culinary excellence and swift service, this restaurant is an unequivocal must-visit. #TieDyePizzaHeaven @traveleen_gurl

Continuing the legacy of its sister spots, this charming gelateria once again impressed with its high-quality gelato, served with a flair for aesthetics. Despite the bustling atmosphere, the staff managed to deliver personalized and attentive service. As a vegan, I'm particularly fond of their sorbet selections – the chocolate sorbet is a delightful surprise, offering a creamy experience sans dairy, a rare find in most gelato establishments. The fruit-flavored sorbets burst with authentic taste, though they do lean towards the sweeter side, making them perfect for sharing. A must-visit for anyone with a penchant for frozen treats.

In this day and age, where people and companies don't care about their customers, it was so refreshing that Jay the manager reached out to us to see if everything was ok. Just by him reaching out shows he and the company cares.  We will all come back and get our lobster rolls here as it is less touristy than the other one.  Are you in the mood for lobster, shrimp or crab???  Then this is the place you want to come to and let me tell you why....The lobster is served Maine style which means it is chilled versus being served warm.  A couple of reason's why you would want to get your lobster roll here is because it is served cold and you don't have to worry about your lobster being overcooked and dry.  It also keeps the texture of the lobster meat in tact. Their rolls are the classic New England style served nice and warm as they are toasted on both sides.  We got a regular lobster roll ($17) and a Jumbo ($23).  So was it worth it?  Well if you look at it like a hot dog, no... However you are eating lobster and how much would you be paying for lobster if you ordered it in a restaurant?  So from that perspective, it is hella worth it as it tasted so good that we had to come back to get two Jumbo Lobster Rolls.  They also serve a variety of drinks, soups and chips.   If you like pickles, it is free.  So good as they cut them fresh each and every day.  Are you looking to share this experience with your friends or Co-Workers?  If so, they also do catering.Mahalo (thank you in Hawaiian) Jay and the crew for satisfying our stomachs with some delicious and juicy lobster rolls.

Wow !
