This is a gem I have fallen in love with this place it has a vegan liquor and a vegan menu It's a cute chic place The play good music Speak easy vibes Girls night Date night Let's go somewhere to pick at something healthy before 11pm because kitchen closes at 11 and have a good drink They have great messages on the wall Cool decoration The menu is a Dominican Spanish style but vegan I had the wrap which was great I forgot to take pictures of my drinks and food because i was deeply into the vibe and i was with my fiancé and sister

We came here for the brunch, and since it was a holiday weekend, the wait was a reasonable half hour. We sat at a sidewalk table. I had bacon and eggs with the meatloaf. I wasn't expecting it, but the meatloaf is not made from ground beef. It was good and beefy, though. I found the bacon to be very substantial, about 3/16 inch thick. It was uncured and chewy, rather than crisp. A side salad came with it, and I found the dressing to be overly vinegary. My wife had the fried chicken, and the serving size is generous. She was not fond of the slightly sweet leaning seasoning, though. It is seasoned with sweet tea.

The Smith is also located across the street from the Lincoln Center. I took my daughter to see the play the great society for her 21st birthday and after the play we decided to go for dessert and drinks. We could not have picked a more fun and great place. Our waiter was exceptionally friendly and helpful. They serve very creative craft cocktails. The dessert menu was excellent and each dessert that we had was very tasty and creatively prepared and presented beautifully. There are a lot of nooks and crannies in The Smith And I should suggest that you go exploring. If you see a peep hole - I encourage you to look through it!

Tucked away as a no-frills, hole-in-the-wall establishment, this spot is a haven for those craving the heartwarming simplicity of a good wonton noodle soup. Their expansive menu promises more Chinese delights, but my experience with the wonton BBQ pork noodle soup alone warrants a recommendation. Priced at a reasonable $8.40, especially for New York, this dish offers value for both its portion and taste.

The soup itself was a comforting remedy against the chill of a rainy day, filled with a generous serving of thickly sliced BBQ pork. Although a couple of pieces leaned towards the chewy side, the overall balance of sweetness and saltiness in the meat was spot-on. The wontons, hefty with a mix of pork and shrimp, were slightly muted in flavor and could benefit from a hint of pepper. However, their plumpness and the quick service—thanks to the precooked wontons prepared right at the front—are commendable.

In summary, for a fast, filling, and wallet-friendly meal, this Chinatown gem does not disappoint.

While the prices at this burger joint may seem steep at first glance—with combo meals ringing up at around $10 and an average burger priced between $7-$8—it's worth noting the generous portion sizes. The takeout-oriented spot offers limited window counter seating and lacks restroom facilities, which might deter some diners. I opted for curly cheese fries and a drink, setting me back just over $9. Although the space and amenities leave something to be desired, the curly cheese fries I savored were tasty, albeit in need of a more liberal dousing of cheese sauce. If you're in the mood for a substantial takeout meal and don't mind paying a premium for it, this could be a satisfying choice.

Great place for tapas...this is one of the 4 locations in the city...best to make reservations. Service and food were great! Nice bar area and depending where you sit, you can see the kitchen.Beverages: Sangria selection of the day: Rosada - rose wine, tequila, cranberry, pomegranate, hibiscus soaked strawberries.  this was good and not too strong...1 glass was enough for each of us.Onto the tapas to share (they recommend 2-3 per person): - Ham and mushroom croquettes - delicious and creamy...I liked the mushroom better- Patatas Bravas - potatoes with salsa (a bit spicy) and garlic allioli- Shrimp with garlic sauce - delicious- 12oz Hangar steak cooked medium rare (if too rare, then flip over on the hot plate to let it cook a little more)- Albondigas - lamb meatballs with sheep's milk cheese...baaa! Make sure to leave room for dessert... was too full, will have to come back again for dessert.If you are celebrating your birthday, they bring out dessert you order with sparkler candle... Restrooms in the back - there are two and unisex. Note: Become a Boqueria insider and receive a pitcher of sangria on your next visit, a treat on your birthday and more..

3.75*I was craving noodles in soup so I went with ramen. It was difficult finding a Japanese place open at 4pm. I practically ran to Karakatta to make it in time for their lunch special that ends at 4. I arrived at 3:55 and I still got the lunch special. When I arrived, a couple was about to leave and a guy was sitting at the bar. The server had her back facing the door and was busy looking at her phone. I walked up to her to tell her one person. She said I scared her. I don't know whether to laugh or be annoyed at her. I was given a choice to sit at the bar right at the door or sit at the bar against the wall. I chose the wall. Apparently to the right after you enter is another row of bar and window seats. I didn't realize this existed as I was going through Yelp. I kinda like that area, very sunny and the light wood makes everything more bright. Another note on the environment is how things seemed kinda old and dirty, not that bad, but enough to notice it, like stains on the wall and mosquitoes. Since I sat at the bar I saw the kitchen and noticed the mosquitoes having fun in there too, but no obvious signs of feastingWhen I was studying the menu and yelp reviews before arriving, I realized this place is known for their spicy ramen and the spicy ginger stamina is a unique one too. I figured sure I'll check it out. I like how the pork belly is charred so there is a smokiness flavor to it. One piece was even between fat and meat. One piece mostly fat. It was ok since it didn't feel oily. The fat part is more salty and savory than the meat part, yum. The broth is chicken based, so it was obviously lighter than pork based. It felt comforting especially with all the ginger and scallions. Someone commented that it's very Chinese style and I agree. It does feel homey. The ginger helped a lot with adding depth to the broth.    My mom would approve of the OD cabbage and other veggies in the bowl. I appreciate it too but got tired of it halfway. I had the standard level 1 spiciness. I felt the heat, and it somewhat irritated my throat but I don't feel like it enhanced my appreciation for the ramen. Also about the noodles. Some people said it was good for not being too soft. I wish it was chewier and "smoother". It was too "stiff" for me. Overall it was a solid bowl of noodles, but I don't "like" it. I guess I was craving more of something like garlic tonkotsu with super smooth noodles. Yes it was my fault for not getting a tonkotsu there, but I figured I should get something that the place is known for.Lunch special karaage. The sauce it came tastes like peanut sweet soy sauce. Nice. The outside is lightly breaded, but I'm not a fan of that. I was awfully burpy an hour after eating it. My burps also smelled like pasta sauce.

Title: A Thai Gem Not To Be Missed

From the moment you step inside, the allure of this dining haven captivates you with its stunning interior and warmly lit ambiance, courtesy of an elegant amber chandelier. Ideal for any occasion, whether a romantic outing, a gathering of friends, or a family dinner, this Thai restaurant sets the mood for a memorable experience.

Visit after visit (four and counting), each dish I've tried has been a culinary delight, showcasing authentic Thai flavors that tantalize the taste buds. The larb gai salad, with its perfect blend of spice and zest, easily tops my favorites list alongside the aromatic chicken with green curry.

The staff's attentiveness adds to the restaurant's charm, ensuring every patron feels valued and satisfied. A word to the wise: on bustling Fridays and Saturdays, the no-reservation policy for dinner means you might wait up to an hour for a table. Weekdays are typically less crowded, allowing for quicker seating.

For those with a penchant for Thai gastronomy, missing out on this exquisite eatery would be a palpable oversight. Indulge your senses and let your culinary journey begin here.

This is one of the restaurants that is close to Lincoln Center. If you have a performance to catch, this eatery is located right across the street. Decided to grab a quick bite before a 2pm show. Most restaurants in the area had 20 mins wait including this restaurant. However, the hostess was nice to get us a table within 5 mins after we explained to her our time constraints. Once we sat down, we were looking for someone who could take our order quickly. We asked what would be cooked fast and decided on getting a burger which came with fries, clam chowder and Brussels sprouts to share.Pretty pricey lunch as it ended up to be $50 after tax and tips. Burger wasn't anything special, the soup was in a small bowl BUT the Brussels sprouts was amazing! Really appreciated everyone understood our urgency and we got out in 40 mins from when we walked in to when we walked out!

First time at Soho Park. It's located in Nolita. Various of shopping store. I was in the mood for American style. I live the interior, it was nice, comfortable and spacious. The customer service was phenomenal. A friend and I had ordered too much food and she gave her honest opinion about ordering too much to finish for two but also told us that if we still have room after, we can definitely order more. The waitress was extremely friendly and kind. She was also constantly checking if everything was fine and made sure she was available if we needed her. The portion was bigger than I thought it would be. The price was very reasonable. I love their Red Onion rings, this is the first time trying Red onion rings. Usually at restaurants they only make it with the regular white onion rings so this was a new experience. It was made with a very thin batter, the onion flavor definitely without a heavy batter over powering it. Overall food was great but the stars really went towards the service!!

Great outdoor space by the water. It has been a long while since I've been here, especially since I live so close but I finally had the smarts to eat brunch here. It's greatly changed since I last ate here for the better!The service was a bit slow but the food was good. We had to wait about 20min for a table at 1:30pm on a Saturday but they take your number and text when your table is ready which is great! On the pricier side but for the location, it's kind of expected. Goat Cheese Soufflé - Easy to share between 2-4 people. Tasted essentially like a savory cheese cake.Burger - Delicious! I would come back just for that. The burger was insanely juicy and huge with lettuce and tomatoes. It came with a large side of fries. The brioche bread it came with was great with the burger. It was sturdy to hold the giant juicy patty but not overwhelm the flavors with bread. The perfect combo in a burger. The burger pushed it to 4 stars for me!Quiche Lorraine - Quiche was super soft and delicate. A good slice for one person or two people to share. It came with a side of lightly dressed salad which I liked as well.Overall, a great lunch. Service was a bit slow but friendly.

I seem to be in the minority regarding my experience here. I was opposed to entering just based on the set up. It resembled one of those order at the counter coffee shops but was actually a restaurant with table service.It was raining and my friend didn't feeling like eating at  one of the many restaurants in the area such as Thai, Japanese or Indian (too bad). While we craved eggs or breakfast (even though it was 1:30), we settled here for its general menu--just hot or cold sandwiches and salads.Anyone who knows me is aware I'm not a sandwich person. This means if I'm having one, it better be good. Sadly my sandwich was anything but.I ordered a mint tea while my friend went with a latte. We decided on the hot sandwiches category. She chose Turkey while my selection was Chicken Po Boy.Service was good and our sandwiches came out in less than 10 minutes.There were 2 sizes/prices for the sandwiches:$8 for a roll and $12 for a mini hero. Luckily I ordered the roll. It was grilled chicken with cheese,lettuce, tomatoes, onion and mayo. The chicken was severely overcooked and I basically choked it down. I even left some behind. It was inedible & just awful. I would have said something if I were alone.My friend actually liked her sandwich. All sandwiches were served with some potato chips. Maybe that was the best part. And the tea. Maybe it was an off day when it came to making my sandwich but the chicken had no taste at all and it seemed like it was yesterday's leftover. BTW, kitchen ventilation must have been poor because I walked out smelling like food all over myself.I'm too fearful to return to give it another try.

Title: Brunch Satisfaction at Cookshop

After several visits to Cookshop, exclusively for brunch, it's clear why this spot has amassed a legion of fans and maintains a strong four-star rating from nearly 2000 reviews. The restaurant thrives on its vibrancy and prime location, just steps from the Highline, making it a weekend hotspot.

Reservations are highly recommended, as I learned from a past experience of being relegated to counter seating. Thankfully, booking through OpenTable three weeks in advance ensured our immediate seating upon arrival this time around.

The frittata was the star of today's meal—a fluffy embodiment of broccoli and feta goodness, paired with a crisp side salad. Alongside, my cold brew iced coffee was the perfect brunch companion. Service was attentive and accommodating, contributing to an overall satisfying experience.

While Cookshop's brunch may not be the best I've ever indulged in, it's undeniably a place to tick off your culinary bucket list—or to engage in some trendy see-and-be-seen business. Certainly a venue I'd return to, perhaps to explore the dinner menu next time. Solid choice, but remember, plan ahead to bypass the brunch rush.

I'm just gonna say the food was good, but I've had better. Our waitress was nice and checked in on my daughter and self as the restaurant got busier. The place was clean but could use a good makeover. The layout of the place is just weird to me. Any way we did enjoyed everything we had and I've learned that their seems to be two ways that shrimp mofongo is prepared, either with a tomato based sauce, or with some sort of garlic based sauce, I prefer the garlic way, and if you care now knowing what I know, you should probably ask first on how do they prepare theirs when eating at Latin restaurants. This place has some really good lunch specials and the price is fair. Although I would only make a return for the lunch and that's if I'm in the area and up to it, because this area has so much more dining options. So if you do make a visit, definitely only go for the lunch, after that the prices are not worth the meal.

The bestie and I decided to celebrate our Galentine's over some delicious carbs!! This gem is located conveniently near the theater district, slightly away from all the madness. The ambiance is dim lit, perfect for date night. However it's huge so great for groups too! They have a huge selection of classic Italian dishes. Service was great, our waitress was super attentive. For starters we ordered the calamari and mozzarella sticks. Both were just deliciously good. The mozz was instagram worthy too!! For dinner we ordered the penne vodka and buffalo chicken pizza. Penne was absolutely amazing. I would've prefer a crispier pie and maybe a drizzle of blue cheese or ranch over it. I will say the portions were great, we left stuffed and with plenty to go!For dessert, we ordered the cheesecake. I wasn't crazy about the raspberry drizzle but the cheesecake itself was good! I'm a fan and will definitely be returning!

Title: A Supreme Finale to Our NYC Pizza Journey

After embarking on a pizza-laden adventure throughout the city, our final stop was conveniently located just steps from our hotel: NY Pizza Suprema. A bustling spot with a crowd to match, we were greeted with an impressive arsenal of pizza varieties, all laid out on trays ready for the taking.

The ample seating was a welcome change from the typical grab-and-go slice eateries that leave you jostling for sidewalk supremacy. However, the prices were a notch above the rest, with slices starting at $4.50 and soaring up to $6.50, a slight sting to the wallet.

But let's talk taste—NY Pizza Suprema served up a pie with a noticeably saucier bite and a crust that championed thinness without compromising on flavor. The cheese? Gooey and divine. Each mouthful was a testament to their pizza prowess, rivaling the famed Joe's Pizza in both lightness and taste.

A minor quibble arose when our slices appeared somewhat less generous compared to our fellow diners', a discrepancy that compelled me to withhold a star. Despite this, NY Pizza Suprema stands tall in the pantheon of New York pizzerias—pricier, yes, but supremely satisfying.

Title: A Letdown in the Quest for Authenticity

As a taco enthusiast, I approached this "authentic" taco joint with high hopes, only to find them somewhat dashed. The length of the queue upon arrival was the first sign of promise, suggesting a feast worth waiting for. However, the reality of the dining experience failed to match the initial anticipation.

The menu’s variety, featuring Fish, Al Pastor, and Carne Asada Tacos, seemed promising. But the letdown was in the execution. All three tacos I sampled were disappointingly room temperature, giving the impression that they had languished on the counter before being served.

The fish taco, lacking in flavor, relied heavily on its Chipotle sauce for any semblance of taste. The Al Pastor missed a key ingredient – the pineapple – a glaring oversight when claiming authenticity. And the carne asada was tough to the point of being inedible, making it the biggest disappointment of the meal.

While I’ve savored stand-out tacos from various eateries across NYC, this place fits more snugly into the "fast food" category, falling short of the authentic experience it touts. It managed to claw its way to a middling 3-star rating, however, thanks to an impressive lineup of beverages that provided some consolation to an otherwise underwhelming meal.

While in NYC met a friend here for dinner- what a great place- it was right around the corner from our hotel so the location is great! We ordered a variety of items- the food was great! If you are a vegetarian you have to try this restaurant! Lots of amazing vegetables to pick from as well as salads and fun drinks! The service was good and the staff was friendly! I will return here when I go back to NYC!

Title: An Unforgettable Epicurean Delight

Last night was an exceptional dining experience at Chef Bouley’s establishment where the combination of splendid company and culinary mastery made for a memorable evening. The food was nothing short of great, a testament to Chef Bouley’s expertise. The service was superb, striking a perfect balance between professionalism and warmth. A special shoutout to Naoufal Echaki and Jasmine, whose attentiveness made us feel both like VIPs and friends. Heartfelt thanks to Chef Bouley and the entire waitstaff for an epic culinary journey that will be cherished for a long time.

Nestled in the heart of Greenwich Village, Olio e Piu presents an enchanting dining experience from the first glance. The building is a delightful spectacle, cloaked in vibrant hues, climbing vines, and blooms, promising an escape from the urban rush. Inside, the restaurant captivates with its sophisticated yet inviting decor—striking the perfect balance between elegance and comfort.

The menu at Olio e Piu is a tour de force of Italian gastronomy. The Bruschetta Ricotta with Truffle Oil greets the palate with a symphony of flavor and texture that is simply divine. The Fettuccine Tartufo follows, setting a new personal benchmark for truffle pasta—undeniably a standout dish. The meal concludes with a Tiramisu that pays homage to its classic roots, yet reveals a mastery that leaves you savoring each bite.

With an appetite for exploration, I am keen to return to Olio e Piu. The pastas beckon, each carrying whispers of culinary excellence that demand to be experienced. This spot is not just a meal; it's a journey through Italian cuisine at its finest.

On one of my study binges, I decided to order from UberEats to save some time. I was in the mood for Indian food, and Chapati House was the first such listing I came upon.I ordered my favorite Indian dish, chicken tiki masala, and waited for my order to arrive.The wait time was reasonable, and I was munching down in no time. My tiki masala was delicious, and it came with a side of white rice and naan. I can tell that the food was freshly prepared, and cooked with care. The naan was warm and soft, and the chicken came with the right balance of spices.As far as Indian food in Manhattan, this is one of many great options. I'll consider them the next time I'm in the mood for Indian food.

Title: A Rainy Day Delight at Rahi

I’ve never been more enchanted by Indian cuisine than during my recent visit to Rahi. After the glitz of the Oscars, a friend ushered me into this culinary haven. The ambiance was welcoming with prompt seating, and we kicked off with a creative twist—a mango lassi cocktail spiked with rum—a delightful start to our feast.

It's rare to find a place where every dish is a palate pleaser, but Rahi did just that. Admittedly lost in the flavors, I didn't catch the names of the dishes my companion chose, but the sauces were unforgettable. The mango sauce, in particular, was so divine we indulged in extra orders of their fragrant garlic naan just to savor every drop.

Service was impeccable, and the food was a journey of flavors deserving of a five-star rating. If you're a connoisseur of Indian cuisine or just looking for comfort on a dreary day, Rahi is a must-visit. My gratitude goes to Rahi for the exceptional meal and to Sam for the introduction. I'll be back soon, and I suggest you make your way there too!

#HatApproved

Really great chicken and shrimp fajitas that come on a sizzling platter with tons of thinly sliced onions and peppers. I also really liked my jalapeño margarita and the chocolate flan brûlée. You can skip the tableside guacamole as it's kind of weak but overall great ambience and easy to make a reservation.

Title: Diverse Ambiance with a Szechuan Twist

Rating: ★★★★☆ (3.75/5)

Last night's dining experience at this multi-faceted restaurant offered a visual feast as well as a culinary one. With its five distinct sections, the establishment caters to various dining preferences. The covered outdoor entrance, welcoming lounge with cozy couches, vibrant bar scene, and notably, the spacious dinner party room, all make a statement. The centerpiece, an illuminated cubic structure reminiscent of an aquarium, adds an atmospheric touch to the main dining area.

Our group of ten indulged in a plethora of Szechuan dishes that elevated the typical Chinese cuisine found on New York City's streets. The flavors were bold and the spices well-executed, satisfying our craving for something exceptional.

However, navigating the expansive menu proved to be a challenge, with an overwhelming array of options beyond familiar American-Chinese classics. Additionally, while the ambiance and food scored high marks, the final bill did take us by surprise. At $450, with drinks seemingly encouraged by the friendly yet persuasive staff, the price point felt steep.

Overall, while the food was delectable and the company delightful, the restaurant's cost might prompt us to explore other cultural culinary adventures next time, perhaps a Brazilian steakhouse. Despite the expense, our farewell celebration for a friend moving out of New York City was memorable. The restaurant earns a solid 3.75 stars, with room for improvement on value.

Overall really great atmosphere and elegantly plated, delicious food! For those who love Baar Baar, GupShup is a fantastic spot to try. From the cleverly named drinks to the unique small plates, you are definitely in for a memorable dining experience.

Very nice location in NYC. I was in the city for work, and we needed to kill some time so decided this was a great spot for coffee and breakfast. I had the diner- 2 eggs your way, fruit cup, toast, and bacon. I added avocado. It was absolutely delicious. I also had a beautiful cappuccino-- the Art was a great start to my morning... a quick reminder to show love and compassion to all. The staff was very kind and accommodating when we had to have a plate boxed up so my colleague could take a call and enjoy later, as well as helping us pay quickly to head off to our meeting. Hope to go back and enjoy other items in the menu!

Came here for a friend's birthday with a large group. We all did the bottomless mimosas drink deal - they also let you get bloody marys if you want and you can alternate between the two. They have seating in the back outside with a cute swing for pictures.  Be sure to BRING CASH though for when you pay and to USE THE BATHROOM BEFOREHAND. They only have one bathroom and given that most of their customers are doing bottomless mimosas, the wait was very long. Food and drinks themselves were fine but nothing stood out. Sometimes the servers forgot our drinks and we had to remind them multiple times which was irritating, especially given the time limit on the bottomless deal, but I assume it was because we had a large group. They also brought our birthday friend a small dessert but then charged us for it at the end without telling us it would cost money! A warning would have been nice, especially since it was pretty small...

Our visit to Raclette was a delightful culinary adventure that I shared with my sisters. Having eagerly anticipated tasting the hyped cheese-centric dishes, we weren't disappointed. The convenience of making reservations was matched by a comfortably uncrowded lunchtime atmosphere. We indulged in generous portions that packed a rich flavor, each bite as sumptuous as we had imagined. The experience was not only fun but also a testament to the restaurant's reputation. Though it's not the kind of fare we would crave daily, Raclette is undoubtedly a must-try for those looking to diversify their palate with an indulgent twist.

Came here for a Sunday brunch with a reservation, around 12:30pm. The space is mostly white, with pockets of greenery all around, and the diners inside that day looked like vegan intellectuals (if such a thing exists). Most tables were already full by this time. We were seated and brought water and menus immediately, and ordered shortly after. The wait time for our food was standard for New York restaurants, about 20 minutes. The waiter who served our food mumbled a bit when dropping off the food, leading to confusing situation, as my husband's ordered dish resembled what I thought mine was supposed to look like. He had ordered the egg in a whole, though mine came with a whole egg, sunny side up, on top, and his appeared to have no trace of an egg, he said it was on the inside. My mad hatter pie, strangely resembling an egg in a hole, also included egg, as well as cranberry beans, cheese, pico de gallo and avocado. It was served with a light side salad. The dish was underwhelming, with little elements of flavor. Similarly, my husband did not like his dish. I had taken him here to show him that, yes, vegan food can be delightful and delicious, and worthy of Michelin stars also. But alas, I came away defeated.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Asian Cuisine Lovers

My family and I have dined at this restaurant several times, and each visit has been a pleasurable experience. The menu boasts a diverse range of Asian dishes, each bursting with flavor and generously portioned at reasonable prices—perfect for accommodating various tastes and appetites in a large group.

Despite being tucked away in a basement, the space is surprisingly spacious, providing ample room for guests. The servers exude friendliness, although they tend to require a gentle nudge for check-ins and refills.

In summary, this restaurant delivers on delectable food and a welcoming atmosphere, making it a reliable choice for a satisfying dining experience.

Amazing amazing Indian! We came here on a Tuesday night, it was busy but not overly crowded, our server Charlie was so great so was the manager Naeem. We had the Guac with fried okra which was so good and a great portion, the jackfruit tacos, the garlic naan, salmon tartar with whipped goat cheese, crispy potatoes, and the masterpiece Himalayan morels. It was truly incredible. The drinks were also awesome, very creative and all really tasty. Would come back every day if I could

Sushi Paradise for Vegans and Vegetarians !!!! I am so glad I bumped into this place - keep visiting often and really like their menu.Everything on the menu is fresh and tasty ! My favorite sushi is the Spicy Mang and am addicted to their Mushroom dumplings.Highly recommend this place.

Had a great dinner sitting at the bar. The bartender was really great, friendly and attentive eveN though they were very busy. Loud and fun environment with good music mixed with holiday music. Many TVs for a good location to watch a game. I hade the Hypocrite burger on a wedge salad. The burger was cooked medium well and was juicy and well seasoned. The salad was amazing with plenty of bacon and perfect amount of blue cheese dressing and chunks. My husband had the Patrick's burger with wonderful Irish bacon and again cooked perfectly. We had the zucchini chips for an appetizer and they were cut thin seasoned well and crispy and terrific. The homemade mozzarella sticks are a must too!

Title: A Spacious Spot for a Fabulous Korean BBQ Feast

I recently visited this restaurant for a friend's birthday celebration and was immediately struck by the ample space it offered. We had a reservation for seven at 9:30 pm on a Friday, and the punctuality of our seating on the second floor impressed us — right on time and at a comfortable, large table.

Our evening started with a variety of appetizers including truffle fries, chicken wings, tuna tartare, Korean steamed eggs, and a delightful chicken and cheese fondue. Moving on to the main event, we ordered the Korean BBQ with a generous portion of beef, accompanied by traditional banchan (side dishes). The service was brisk, the waiter attentive, and the quality of the meat was standout — it was undeniably fresh with excellent marbling.

While I usually opt for all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ, the freshness and quality here made me reconsider the value of quality over quantity. My only critique would be the time it took to cook our BBQ; a hotter grill might be in order to expedite the process. Despite this minor issue, the experience was positive enough to ensure my return. I'm definitely coming back for more of that top-notch Korean BBQ! 

Rating: 4/5 stars.

Title: A Happy Hour Gem Near Times Square

We stumbled upon a hidden treasure just off the beaten path in the outskirts of Times Square, and what a delightful find! Making reservations through Yelp proved easy and efficient, setting the tone for what turned out to be a splendid dining experience.

As budget-conscious diners, we were thrilled with the very reasonable prices. Arriving during the happy hour (4-8 PM during the week) turned out to be a strategic move, with an array of drink specials including 5 or 6 beers and an additional 6 or 7 cocktail options. The red sangria my wife enjoyed and my choice of Shock Top were so refreshing that we couldn't resist ordering seconds.

Sport enthusiasts would appreciate the several large-screen TVs catering to football and soccer fans—a nice touch to the ambiance. Though time was not on our side, we managed to share three small bites: the hot pretzel sticks (very good), shrimp tacos (leaving us wanting more), and Irish meatballs (an interesting dish with room for improvement). 

At around $51 before tip, the value was undeniable. Thank you for a wonderful experience—Sláinte!

Title: Unassuming Spot with Unforgettable Asian Comfort Food

Review:

Don't let the modest facade of this cash-only eatery fool you; it's a haven for Asian comfort food aficionados. From the no-nonsense service to the rapid seating—even just before the inevitable lunch rush—the restaurant is laser-focused on delivering sublime flavors rather than small talk. 

The space snugly accommodates diners with a mix of duo, quartet, and larger communal tables. Once seated, the food arrives with impressive swiftness, which is ideal for those in search of a swift yet satisfying meal. 

The star of the show, their signature Porkchop Over Rice, dazzles with its flavorful, expertly cooked meat and harmonizing pickled vegetables. Even the Salt and Pepper Chicken, which I skeptically eyed due to its varied piece sizes, surprised me with its uniformly crunchy and moist bites that let the pepper's presence shine subtly but surely.

With generous portions at a fair price point, this spot wins you over with taste alone. I'm already planning my next visit, with a mental note to save space for dessert. Highly recommend!

Thankful for their lunch special prices, portions, and delicious food!Banchan is numerous, and comes with free refills so that we never need to order an appetizer. Food was so good that as New Yorkers, we came twice in one week haha. Granted, it was super cold and a spicy, hot broth was exactly what we wanted. Simmered Beef Stew with Rice ($11): so basic but sooo damn delicious. Love the thin slices of fattier beef, the spiciness, and the flavors of the broth. SUCH a comforting brothGamja Tang ($14): spicy pork bone and potato stew. My bf's go to order. It's just a tad too herbally for me, but this stew is loaded with good stuff. They are super generous with the pork bones - each order comes with at least 2-3 ginormous pieces. However, you have to be super patient with this dish, because you'll have to use your time to pick and scrape off the meat off the bones. It's worth it, as the meat is super tender and deliciousKimchi and Pork Stew ($10): one of the stews that is a lot more richer than the other Korean restaurants on the block. A whole lot of kimchi taste, that's for sure! This is something more rich and flavorful, but when I want comfort and cleanish, I go for my beef stew

During my tenure working in Union Square, this gem of a restaurant was my regular haunt, and for good reason. The menu boasts an expansive array of options, ensuring that diners can customize their meals to their heart's content. As an added perk for tech-savvy patrons, they accept LevelUp, making the payment process a breeze. Whether you're a picky eater or just enjoy a wide selection, this place is a must-visit.

I have mixed feelings about this restaurant. Needed last minute dinner reservations. I arrived on time, but my partner was running behind. Fortunately, they sat me early so I had a drink ordered by the time my partner arrived.Food is Nikkei cuisine (Japanese Peruvian). It was restaurant week so they had a very reasonable prix Fixe menu (soup, appetizer, main dish & dessert for $49).The food was good and I would give closer to a 4. Enjoyed the Japanese chicken curry empanada and sushi maki combo of spicy tuna and negihama. The Lucuma  ice cream was something I haven't tried before.So why 3 stars? They brought out the wrong item for entree for partner (they had placed order wrong, but we couldn't change if given we were pressed for time). Then, I had warned them that we were pressed for time, but service dropped off and we had to keep reminding them. We had to ask multiple people for our check.Maybe it was an off night, but the food was better than the service.

Title: A Hit-or-Miss Experience at Vanessa's

Vanessa's has earned its place as a New York City classic, promising a budget-friendly option for those looking to fill up without emptying their wallets. Their dumplings, a menu highlight, vary in quality; some days you'll bite into a succulent, crispy treasure, other days you'll chew on lackluster, rubbery pockets. However, the wontons draped in a fiery oil sauce are a must-try, reliably delicious with portions that defy their modest pricing.

Be prepared for a bustling, crowded atmosphere where the service can mirror the chaos—efficient yet brusque. Despite this, Vanessa's isn't about the frills or fawning servers; it's about straightforward, hearty food that has the potential to impress, as long as you catch them on a good night.

This place is heavily hyped so you know I had to see if the hype was real. For lunch you order at the counter, pay, then wait for your buzzer to go off. No table service so you better know what you want when you walk in! My guest and I ordered the rhapsody platter. You pretty much get a little bit of everything for $38. Wings were ridiculous in a good way. They came right off the bone and had good flavor. Bbq sauce is pretty good as well. Sweet with a touch of heat. The restaurant is pretty spacious and it would be good to come with groups. There are big booths and also tables in the back. They also have bar seating. We sat at a booth and had more than enough room. I enjoyed my time here. The bbq was solid and you are able to be in and out pretty quickly. They also have free wifi if you want to get some work done while you eat. Overall, solid 4 star experience.

Came her for some late night drinks and grub with friends from out of town and I was very much impressed. I've spent quite a bit of time in Japan and throughly enjoy the izakaya scene there but it can be hard to replicate that vibe in NYC. They not only did an excellent job with the food. And I mean truly excellent. The fried short ribs we had were OUTSTANDING, but I got to sample a lot of sushi and other fried treats. All amazing. Their omelette noodles I had, not pictures sadly, was just about the best Japanese food I've had outside of home cooked food in Tokyo. Their drinks and drink selection was also quite good. The nigori I had was excellent and can we talk about the pricing? 7 people for late night food and drinks and it was just over $200 with tip? Wow. Just an overall amazing place that I will be going to again for sure and telling all of my friends.

Title: A Mixed Bag at May Wah

My visit to May Wah back in late 2016 left me with mixed feelings. This eatery specializes in chicken leg rice and pork chop rice—I went with the pork chop to avoid the hassle of bones, but alas, the pork chop bone was equally irksome. An Americanized, boneless option would be a welcome addition for those of us who prefer a simpler experience.

The sauce on the pork chop had an unusual taste, with a faint hint of plastic that was rather off-putting. It wasn't bad enough to stop me from eating, but it did cause some concern. It could have been an atypical day for the restaurant, and despite my reservations, I'm open to giving May Wah another try to see if things have improved.

A minor inconvenience is the restaurant's cash-only policy, which might deter some patrons in an increasingly cashless society. In conclusion, while May Wah has some aspects to work on, I'm curious enough to consider a second visit to see if they've made any changes.

Title: A Sunlit Haven for Tasty Tacos

I recently savored a delightful experience at this restaurant, basking in an open-concept interior bathed in natural sunlight thanks to the expansive windows. The atmosphere was remarkably uncrowded, contributing to the excellent service I received.

The menu standout was undoubtedly the crispy fish taco, which was a perfect harmony of fresh, non-fishy flavor, and an impeccably balanced slaw wrapped in a warm tortilla. The chili relleno taco also impressed, with a perfectly filled chili that offered just the right level of spice.

An additional treat was the variety of unique salsas available to sample, each adding its own zesty twist to our tacos. Whether you're in for a quick bite or a leisurely lunch, this spot is a great choice for taco enthusiasts.

Worked up an appetite after walking around Central Park with a friend and decided to eat at OBAO after doing some research on Yelp. We arrived at around 7pm on a weekday and were seated right away. We ordered a plate of the spare ribs on sugar cane to share and I got the pad see iew, while my friend got the roasted duck noodles. The spare rib on sugar cane came out first and the portions were perfect for 2 people (4 "skewers" in total). The appetizer came with a tasty peanut butter sauce for dipping and the spare ribs were flavored and cooked perfectly. My pad see iew was also delicious - a welcomed surprise to see the mango relish on top. The dish was definitely on the sweeter side but I'm a fan. My friend who ordered the roasted duck noodles couldn't stop raving about her dish so it's safe to say she enjoyed it as well. The service was incredibly friendly and quick. Definitely worth a visit!

I recently visited a quaint Italian deli that may be small in size, with only three seats available, but is incredibly big on flavor. The sandwiches here are nothing short of amazing; I tried the prosciutto with mozzarella and a fig spread that was delightfully delicious. Moreover, the bread was outstanding – fresh, crusty, and the perfect companion to the high-quality ingredients. I highly recommend stopping by for a taste of Italy that will not disappoint.

Title: Disappointing Dining Experience on 42nd Street

I recently dined at a restaurant in the heart of the theater district on 42nd Street, and unfortunately, the experience left much to be desired. The location, while convenient for tourists and theatergoers, seems to be the justification for the inflated prices. The food and atmosphere offered nothing noteworthy—standard fare that did not match the premium cost.

My visit was purely based on proximity and time constraints due to an approaching showtime. In hindsight, a quick meal at a nearby Wendy's would have been a more satisfying and cost-effective alternative. For those looking for an exceptional dining experience, it may be wise to venture beyond the tourist traps. This restaurant, regrettably, is not one I can recommend. Next time, I'll plan ahead and skip the convenience for quality and value.

This restaurant is an excellent choice when you're looking to indulge. We were a party of three and decided to share a variety of sides: the bacon, duo tartar, mashed potatoes, fries, and broccoli, all of which were delightful accompaniments. For my main course, I savored the filet mignon, which was exceptionally tender and juicy. However, the real standout was the bone-in rib eye—a notch above in flavor and a must-try. Throughout our meal, the service was attentive and impressive, adding to the high-end experience. Highly recommended for a special occasion.

I ordered the Crazy sized nachos but wont order as takeout.  It was a bit soggy which was out fault and wont order ahead going forward! Burritos are pretty yummy but it is on 9th ave so you need to feel adventurous to make a trek!It is a small restaurant and only the neighborhood peeps are familiar with the spot but if you want an escape from the port authority garbage food, this might be an option for you!

Title: Double Date Delight at Our Favorite Eatery

Last night, my partner and I revisited our newfound culinary gem, this time with another couple in tow for a double date. The excitement was palpable as we settled into a cozy booth, ready for a feast. We indulged in an array of dishes including Otsukemono, the sumptuous Salmon Donburi, succulent Gyoza, and the star attraction – the Tsukemen.

Our friends were ecstatic, one of them humorously remarked about being left alone in a dark room with the bowls of Tsukemen, which sent us into fits of laughter. We introduced them to the unique 'Hot Stone Sizzle', a fun presentation where a hot stone was placed into the broth, creating an engaging show of sizzles and bubbles – a real sensory delight.

The staff was exceptional, just as on our first visit – friendly, hospitable, and ensured our experience was nothing short of fantastic. The atmosphere remained warm and inviting, allowing us to relax and enjoy the bustling vibe.

We left with our bellies full, our taste buds satisfied, and the promise to return soon. It's clear – this restaurant has quickly become a favorite spot for great food and memorable times.

Service was ok. Took our waitress a while to finally take our drink orders. The food was delicious. Had a burger and it was cooked well. Had the mushroom arancini which was delicious as well as he and the tuna tartare. Mixed drinks were inventive and delightful.

To find this restaurant, it's at the NE corner of 6th and 2nd Avenue.  There's scaffolding right now so I had to look for the name on the scaffolding but almost walked past the entrance.My intention was to try the bbq on the grill; but since I went by myself, I chose the ala carte menu especially when I saw quail.  If you like quail, they do this perfectly.  Well seasoned and evenly cooked  yet so so juicy.  Perfectly cooked mahogany brown.I also ordered the side dish containing the trimmings to wrap my meat in.And I also ordered their lemongrass marinated rolled beef.  That was delicious as well.A perfect dinner.So good I came back 2nd time within the same week!

Sup Crab is a relaxed LES spot to enjoy a seafood boil! The service was great, the food was very good and the music put you at ease.This location was very spacious: small tables on the first floor and larger parties on the second floor. We walked in and got to sit by a booth. The comfy chairs were great for time spent devouring a seafood bag.We ordered: Special Combo ($99), which has Chongqing spicy Popcorn chicken, Fried calamari and Cajun fries, seafood boil with potatoes, corn, sausage, live crawfish, shrimp and choice of snow crab/lobster/ Dungeness crab. We choose lobster.We also ordered fresh crawfish over noodles. Spicy Popcorn Chicken- this was so good! Very crunchy and still juicy bits of chicken with Sichuan peppers. This was the best appetizer. The fried calamari was good and crunchy. I enjoyed the Cajun fries with the dusting of Cajun powder. The seafood boil was so delicious! We ordered Ghost Street spicy and it wasn't very spicy! (Maybe they toned it down for us?)I enjoyed some of the numbing and burning with my juicy lobster. The fresh crawfish was so good! I really enjoyed eating every bite! The shrimps were large and soaked up some of the spiciness. The corn was also good.The crawfish over noodles was very good! I liked not having to peel the chunks of juicy crawfish. The noodles soaked up the crawfish well.This was a fun tasty meal!

Title: A Lively Lunch at Mezetto with Jose the Gem

If you're in the mood for an unexpected twist on your lunch outing, Mezetto is your spot. My co-workers and I popped in on a Thursday, only to find their irresistible offer of bottomless specials every day - a dangerous temptation for our merry bunch.

From the get-go, our server Jose was the life of the party, greeting us with an infectious energy that set the tone for an excellent meal. He expertly walked us through the menu with recommendations that did not disappoint. Standouts included the innovative avocado toast, a drool-worthy burger, and a grilled cheese & tomato soup combo that redefined comfort food with its blend of mozzarella and ricotta, all hugged by perfectly toasted bread. But the true star was the seasoned tomato soup - a Mediterranean twist that delighted our taste buds.

The bottomless sangria seemed to flow in rhythm with our laughter, and by the second glass, we were all thoroughly enjoying the ambiance. Mezetto might be small, but it packs a punch with its cozy charm and ability to make guests feel connected.

Do yourself a favor: visit Mezetto and ask for Jose—he's not just a server, he's a maestro of hospitality. Hats off to Mezetto for a meal we won't forget!

** Restaraunt Week **Made reservations for 5pm on a Friday in early February. Hosts lazily greeted us with a blank  robotic face. Room was close to empty. Only downstairs area was open to dine. Tables/seats are too close to each other. We ordered :Mushroom croquetteGrilled cauliflowerLemon ChickenSalmonWhite & milk chocolate mouseCheesecakeComplimentary bread and oil dips were placed - simply good I must admit. We had ordered the croquettes before realizing they had a restaurant week menu, but the waiter was nice about it and adjusted it to our bill. After all it was also part of the rest. week menu. Both the cauliflower and mushroom apps were delicious! We think the lemon chicken was undercooked. When the concern was raised, the waiter reassured us it was cooked fully through but sometimes roasting chicken and/or other way of cooking poultry doesn't always make the meat white. Unfortunately we had already lost our appetite. The salmon dish was amazingly tasty. The desserts were a great ending. Not too sweet, not too heavy. The cheesecake was on the fluffier side and smooooothe. For the mouse, I highly reccomend taking a scoop of the top white chocolate first. Then only a scoop of the milk chocolate. Finally, both together. You're welcome!The room got packed within 30-45 mins after arriving, yet the ambiance remained the same. Staff increased on the floor but there was no sense of rush or anxious table clearing. Fig & Olive succesfully brings you their tasting experience by combining unique vegetable / fruit flavors and their contrasting colors. Only concern I have is their price point outside of Restaraunt Week and that undercooked lemon chicken. Just can't get over it.Reccomend!

Title: Mixed Experience at Local Café - Disappointing Latte but Superb Gelato!

I recently made two stops at this café, the first visit with high hopes for a morning latte. Unfortunately, the latte fell short of expectations, with an odd nutty taste and underwhelming foam—likely a result of the unexpected soy milk substitution due to an almond milk shortage.

Despite the latte letdown, I returned for a gelato indulgence before work and was not disappointed. The queue was swift, and the variety of unlimited flavors available for the medium cone was impressive, albeit at a somewhat premium price of $7.35. The lychee, mascarpone and fig, and blueberry cheesecake flavors were a harmonious blend, each delectably holding its own.

The non-overpowering sweetness of the cone itself complemented the rich gelato perfectly—a thoughtful touch for a balanced dessert experience. Skipping the macaron didn't detract from the enjoyment.

In summary, while the latte earned a mere three stars, the gelato is undoubtedly a five-star treat. I'm excited to return and sample more gelato creations, this time with my boyfriend in tow—highly recommended for fellow gelato enthusiasts!

Title: A Charming Evening at a West Village Gem

I recently dined at this super cute spot in the West Village with my boyfriend, and it left me eager to return, especially to experience their charming outdoor patio for brunch. The highlight of the night was testing out their much-talked-about "euphorics" cocktail. While it didn't induce a typical alcohol buzz, it offered a unique, subtle lift—think of a mellow energy drink vibe—which was a fascinating twist on a traditional cocktail.

To start, we nibbled on the wild calamari and shrimp dumplings, both decent though not remarkable. However, the hummus served with crackers was notably delicious and should not be overlooked. My main dish, the lobster coconut curry, packed an unexpectedly zesty punch that was pleasantly surprising and added a delightful complexity to the meal. The matcha crepe also made for an enjoyable addition to the evening's spread.

Dessert was the real showstopper with the rhubarb strawberry crumble being an absolute must-try. Anyone with a love for oat bars or strawberry shortcake will find themselves in dessert heaven with this one. Overall, this restaurant offers a lovely atmosphere coupled with some intriguing menu items that are definitely worth exploring.

Title: A Flavor Explosion at a Northern Vietnamese Gem

I recently visited a restaurant that absolutely blew my mind - the experience was nothing short of "BOMB". While I can't vouch for its authenticity, the Northern Vietnamese flair the owner proudly speaks of translates into a delectable menu that will tantalize your taste buds.

The innovative ventilation system caught my eye – it’s not the usual overhead kind you see at Korean BBQ joints. However, be mindful that the aroma of sizzling meats will linger on your clothing.

I still dream about their beef carpaccio; it's a dish I crave even though I'm not a fan of raw meat or fish, let alone onions. But this dish had me captivated – I went from a tentative nibble to devouring the entire plate. A must-try is their 'Beef 7 Ways'. It's a hearty affair, so pacing yourself is key, especially after indulging in an appetizer.

The rice paper wrapping experience is simply ingenious. A tip for newcomers: dip a third of the wrapper in warm water, rotate it until it's soft and slightly sticky, and then stuff it with an array of veggies, fruits, and meats.

For all of you trying it for the first time, you’re in for a culinary treat. Prepare to be envious of your own palate. It's seriously THAT good.

Tucked away in a delightful corner of the city, this restaurant is a feast for the eyes and the palate alike. Its aesthetics are breathtaking, setting the stage for a dining experience that is nothing short of extraordinary. The wait staff is phenomenal, delivering service that's both attentive and unobtrusive, ensuring nothing detracts from the culinary adventure.

As for the food, it's clear that the kitchen excels at their craft. The calamari is expertly prepared, tender and flavorful. The rib spaghetti and meatballs is a hearty, comforting dish that feels like a warm embrace, while the pesto fettuccine is a vibrant dance of fresh flavors on the tongue. Each dish is crafted with care, deserving of the price and likely to leave patrons feeling both satisfied and eager to return.

When you visit—and you must—it's highly recommended to indulge in these specific platters. Prepare for your taste buds to be tantalized and for an overall experience that delivers a resounding 'bang for your buck.'

Title: A Lunch That Sets the Standard

Review:
From the moment we adjusted our reservation through OpenTable for an expanded party, the service was impeccable. Yelp would indeed fall short if it couldn't award this restaurant more than its maximum of five stars.

The dining experience, whether in the main room or the adjacent tavern, remains consistently delightful. We indulged in four entrees, including a succulent monkfish, the crispiest of chicken, and an exceptional stir fry—each dish showcasing the chef's mastery of flavors and knife skills.

What truly elevates the experience is the attentive team of servers and the all-inclusive gratuity model, which simplifies the dining process and focuses on sheer culinary enjoyment. The bread service and the divine rugelach that graced our table at the end of the meal were thoughtful touches that left us savoring every moment.

Despite the brisk pace required by our business lunch, the staff ensured we dined comfortably and exited on time. Although we skipped appetizers and dessert, we're already anticipating our next visit. Our meal ended on a high note back at the office with cold brew lattes and "dough" donuts—a perfect conclusion to an extraordinary dining experience.

This place serves mainly udon and it is quite authentic in terms of flavor and staff.  I ordered the ankake udon which is egg drop noodle and it was piping hot (temperature).  Took a while to cool down since the soup based was thick but once you drink the broth it is mildly sweet and salty in a good way.  The noodle was very chewy but texture was great, not soggy nor al dente.  I also ordered karaage (fried chicken) and it was crispy not greasy at all.  I'd love to come back! Pro tip: you can RSVP on Yelp before you head over since they seem to be constantly full as it's a small but popular restaurant.

Title: A Gem Inspired by "Masters of None" – Thai Villa Review

As an ardent "Masters of None" aficionado, my culinary pilgrimage to Thai Villa in NY did not disappoint. The establishment strikes a delightful balance, weaving warmth and brightness with a casual yet romantic atmosphere. Upon entry, the stunning golden tree centerpiece captivates your attention, setting a memorable and opulent tone for the dining experience.

Time constrained, I indulged in the jasmine tea and pad thai noodles – both exceeded expectations. The tea, blooming like a floral art piece, offered a delicate flavor to savor slowly. Meanwhile, the pad thai's elegant presentation – resembling a cocoon nestled in a leafy embrace – redefined my standard for this classic dish. The flavors were a harmonious blend, transforming a simple meal into a luxurious affair.

While my visit was brief, Thai Villa left a lasting impression. I'm eager for a return to fully immerse in the ambiance and explore further culinary delights. A word of advice to future diners: secure a reservation to guarantee your spot in this bustling hotspot. And don't miss the chance to visit their beautifully appointed restrooms – it's all part of the Thai Villa charm.

This was the best Italian place my daughter and I tried on our trip to New York. It's also the only place we went to twice in the week we stayed in Manhattan. My daughter loved their spaghetti and meatballs. Go early as there's always a line of people waiting outside to get in.

Title: Missed the Mark on Authentic Greek Flavors

I recently visited a local eatery hoping to savor the flavors of Greece but left underwhelmed. Opting for the chicken gyro, I anticipated a taste of the Mediterranean, but the reality fell short. The dish lacked authentic Greek seasoning, and to my disappointment, the promised 'spicy sauce' was merely Frank's RedHot—a far cry from the traditional zest one would expect.

Additionally, the gyro was flanked by a modest portion of fries, which seemed to overshadow the meal with excessive carbohydrates. Given the price point of $13.55, including a Snapple, this meal did not deliver value when considering the tastier and more cost-effective street vendor alternatives available.

On a positive note, the seating arrangement at the restaurant was quite satisfactory, providing a comfortable atmosphere despite the culinary letdown. However, for those in search of a genuine Greek culinary experience, this restaurant may not meet expectations.
I go for the hangry to get the delicious salmon and lobster hand rolls. The iced green tea is very authentic!

I used to come here all the time when I was very young with family but would only eat udon at that age haha. This was my first time back since and now I actually eat sushi haha. I was not disappointed at all.This is a very small restaurant in the basement so be sure to call ahead or be prepared to wait in a line that goes out the door. At first it may appear that the menu is pricey but you will soon understand when your food arrives.All of the fish is crazy fresh & tender with no fishiness at all. Normally I find sushi places load up on rice and give you very little fish. Yama's is the exact opposite. The sushi is stuffed with more fish than rice which I love. I was very impressed.Next time I'm craving sushi in the city and want a sit down dinner, I will return here.

Rating: 3.5/5 Stars

My mom and I, eager for Thai cuisine upon our arrival in Manhattan, were fortunate to find Topaz Thai Authentic just a block from our hotel. Although it's a bit hidden, requiring a climb up some stairs (accessibility questionable), the interior ambiance is inviting, enhanced by dim lighting and tasteful decor.

Once seated at 9:45 PM, we faced a rushed service; the staff announced last call within minutes despite the 11 PM posted closing time. This rush detracted from the experience as we observed others being turned away or limited to takeout after 10 PM.

Now, the cuisine: The Dancing Chicken was exceptional—flavorful and well-balanced with a generous portion suitable for sharing. The Pad See Eew with fried tofu was another hit, nailing the sauce-to-noodle ratio and spice level. However, the Chicken Satay was a letdown, overcooked to a rubbery texture, though somewhat redeemed by the accompanying peanut sauce and cucumber salad.

Had we dined earlier, the rushed service might not have overshadowed the delicious food. Despite the tasty dishes, better time management would enhance the dining experience.

I recently dined at this restaurant and was thoroughly impressed by the flavorful dishes offered at reasonable prices. The staff was amazing and exuded friendliness, adding to the overall pleasant dining experience. I highly recommend giving this place a try—you won't regret it!

I'm pretty much a regular here in summer time. Honestly,  inside doesnt vibe with me, it's just a regular bar. But in summer, you can sit outside while enjoying really good scrambled eggs with mushroom. I can have that dish every month and wont be tired. The toast is a high quality as well. Perfect sourdough that makes your soul happy. They pair the dish with arugula salad and it's just one of the greatest combos ever.

I don't eat Thai food often but I absolutely loved this restaurant. The service was great, the restaurant was full but calm, and my friends and I loved everything they ordered. The servers were very attentive, it's a very cozy spot, good for medium sized groups (4-6 people). We loved the drunken noodles with beef twice and loooved their buns.

Title: A Delightful Surprise at Legacy Records – Cavatelli Love Wins!

After braving the winter journey to New York's Legacy Records, I was baffled by the restaurant's mixed reviews, as my experience was nothing short of wonderful. The menu may have been familiar territory, but the food itself was a revelation.

The Hamachi was a standout starter, with a sublime dressing – citrusy and intriguing with a salty crunch reminiscent of rice puffs. Next, the Mozzarella was an unexpectedly harmonious match with hummus, elevated by a touch of rosemary.

I misjudged the Japanese yam for a warm dish, only to discover it was a salad. Although slightly overpriced, the flavors did not disappoint. However, the star of the evening was undoubtedly the Cavatelli. It was a pasta lover's dream – impeccably cooked, bursting with flavor, and utterly satisfying.

Sharing each plate, my friend and I enjoyed a drink each, and found the bill quite reasonable considering the gratuity was already factored in – all in at about $130.

Finally, a word on the ambiance – the decor was a feast for the eyes. Kudos to Ken Fulk for the stunning combination of green leather and distressed gold at the bar – it added an extra layer of enjoyment to a meal I'd be eager to relive.

In summation, don't let a few negative reviews deter you. Legacy Records is a gem waiting to be rediscovered, offering a gastronomic experience that truly sings, if you're willing to make the journey.

I recently tried out the Japanese cuisine at a local eatery and was left extremely disappointed. Despite the fact that the restaurant isn't Japanese-owned, I was hoping for a higher quality experience. I took advantage of a $5 off promotion via Ritual for my takeout order of Shrimp Tendon but found that it was still not worth the price. The portions were scant, and the presentation left much to be desired as everything was haphazardly packed in plastic.

The quality of the food was subpar— the shrimp tempura was stale, the rice lumpy, and the poached egg was tiny and undercooked, a far cry from how it's traditionally served. Adding to the disappointment was the odd, exotic smell permeating the restaurant as I waited for my order.

All things considered, the experience was far from what one would expect from a restaurant claiming to serve Japanese cuisine. I won't be returning and I cannot recommend it to others seeking authentic or even decent Japanese meals.
My sister and I went here for brunch on a Sunday.  The food was very fresh and presentation was beautiful.  Great service and ambiance.

Title: Unfulfilled Hype at Local Ramen Spot

My recent visit to the much-talked-about ramen restaurant left me with mixed feelings. The noodles were decent, delivering on quality but failing to stand out from the crowd. As for the pork, it was disappointingly thin and lacked substance. Fortunately, the broth partly redeemed the dish with its flavorful embrace.

The solitary dining setup was a highlight, offering a peaceful retreat for a solo diner like myself. However, the experience was marred by a disappointing detail – the ramen egg. Not only was it overcooked, losing the sought-after oozy center, but it also arrived cold and inexplicably still in its shell.

While the place has a certain charm, the overall execution did not live up to the hype, especially considering the price. Despite its uniqueness, I'm left uncertain if a return visit is on the menu.

On my recent visit to the local pizzeria, I sampled the truffled mushroom pizza slice, priced at $6. The crust was a delectable highlight, perfectly baked to a satisfying crunch. However, the overall flavor profile of the slice fell short, striking me as disappointingly bland despite the promising inclusion of truffle—a flavor that usually imparts a rich, earthy depth. While I'm curious to explore other options on their menu, I do hope they consider a more generous hand with seasoning in the future to truly elevate their offerings.

Last night, my friend celebrated his birthday in high style at Gabriel Kreuther, where we were treated to an outstanding dining experience from start to finish. Upon arrival, we were touched by the personal touches, including a hand-signed birthday card and attentive service that expertly balanced attentiveness and discretion. They even stored our chocolate treats from the adjacent shop in their fridge.

The evening was a culinary journey, starting with the signature Alsatian Kougelhopf paired with a cloud-like whipped chive fromage blanc—a dish so delightful we cherished every morsel. Our tasting menu, customized at my request, allowed us to sample a wider array of flavors, with the Rendez-vous cocktail and LANGOUSTINE TARTARE as particular standouts.

The service was seamlessly orchestrated, gracefully transitioning us through each course. The STURGEON & SAUERKRAUT TART was a showstopper, with its smoky, theatrical presentation and tender flavors conjuring cozy winter memories. Although some courses, like the bread service and CITRUS CURED BLUE COBIA, were overshadowed by previous offerings, every dish was executed with precision and artistry.

The grand finale featured not just one but several desserts, including a pear-centric creation and a harmonious blend of chocolate and caramel, culminating in a personalized birthday dacquoise for my companion. The meal concluded with irresistibly petite orange cakes and a taste of Gabriel Kreuther's famed chocolates.

Gabriel Kreuther exemplifies the pinnacle of fine dining sans pretension. It's an absolute gem for special occasions, and I eagerly anticipate returning to savor the seasonal offerings.
Great little lunch spot. Food was great, atmosphere nice. No complaints. Authentic. Stop by grab a bite very quick.

Title: Cozy Weeknight Dinner with Standout Dishes

We visited on a weeknight and were delighted by the prompt seating. The star of our meal was undoubtedly the fried truffle and mushroom perogies, which burst with flavor compared to the other varieties like cheese, sweet potato, and sauerkraut/onions that paled in comparison. I'd recommend steering clear of the boiled perogies due to their lackluster skin.

The potato pancakes, though merely flattened potatoes reminiscent of a breakfast hash, were enjoyable, though their value might be up for debate. The bigos was a clear winner; the dish's sauerkraut was perfectly tangy, complementing the hot dogs and mashed potatoes, and the accompanying fries were a welcome addition.

Service shone at this establishment. They made accommodations for our friend on a knee wheel with grace and efficiency, enhancing our experience. The pace at which our food arrived was also impressive. Overall, a restaurant worth visiting for some select, flavorful dishes and attentive service.

Title: A Gastronomic Delight with a View to Match

My recent dining experience at this establishment was nothing short of fabulous. As part of a large party, we enjoyed a set menu that offered a delectable array of choices. The esotica salad, a crowd-favorite, did not disappoint with its fresh and flavorful profile. For the main course, the scaloppini di pollo was a mouthwatering delight, cooked to perfection.

The drink selection added a playful twist to the meal, with the frozen Bellini standing out as a refreshing complement to the exquisite dishes. The ambiance was further enhanced by the stunning panorama that included the Statue of Liberty, the Colgate Clock, and the Verrazano Bridge – views that elevate any dining experience.

While the restaurant does not currently offer dock and dine options, it would be a welcomed addition, especially for summer visits. The service was impeccable, striking the perfect balance between attentiveness and discretion. 

A glimpse of the calamari served to an adjacent table has already tempted me to return and explore the regular menu. This restaurant certainly promises a repeat visit for any food lover seeking an exceptional meal with an awe-inspiring backdrop.

Title: A Flavorful Experience at Woodpecker by David Burke

Woodpecker by David Burke made for a truly delightful dining experience, albeit with an ample dose of the chef's branding. The appetizers, including the chorizo and octopus, as well as the tuna crudo, were exceptional in taste and presentation. The bacon dish stood out as a memorable highlight, offering a savory satisfaction that left a lasting impression. Lastly, the dessert course of original cake pops was a sweet finale to an overall fantastic meal. Despite the overt presence of the chef's name throughout the venue, the quality of the food spoke for itself—Woodpecker is a must-visit for food enthusiasts looking for culinary creativity and flavor.

If you're in the hunt for a speedy yet scrumptious meal, look no further! This place serves up pizza slices at lightning speed, ensuring you're satisfied and ready to continue your day in no time. Embrace the simplicity, savor the quickness, and most importantly, indulge in the mouthwatering flavors. It's the perfect pitstop for any pizza aficionado on the go!

Chapter II isn't better than chapter I.  Sadly everything taste blah, and the scones were too hard to eat and no flavor.  Will stick to the Westside location. Service was too slow even though it was a weekday morning and barely 4 tables seated.

Title: A Delectable Evening at the Burger Haven

I visited this gem of a restaurant on a bustling Friday evening with my group, and we were fortunate to be seated promptly. The service outshone my expectations – attentive, swift, and quite simply, impeccable.

My choice for the night was the Garfunkel and Tauster burger, an unequivocal showstopper. The meat was succulent to the core, complemented by a generous serving of bacon that elevated each bite to perfection. This wasn't just a burger; it was a carefully crafted experience, leaving a lasting impression with its size and taste. Admittedly, it defeated my appetite halfway through, but it made for a delightful leftover meal the next day.

If I were to nitpick, the fries didn't share the same culinary spotlight as their partner. Although they were satisfactory, they didn't ascend to the extraordinary heights of the burger. Nonetheless, this minor blip hardly swayed my overall exceptionally satisfying dining experience.

Title: Efficient Service and Tasty Eats at Tech-Savvy Spot

My latest visit to this bustling eatery was a delight from the get-go, thanks to their handy kiosk which streamlines the ordering process—high tech meets high convenience! The standout for me was the guac burger, which easily eclipsed its regular counterpart in flavor and satisfaction. 

While the air fries were enjoyable, they lacked that consistent crispiness one might crave—perhaps a minor trade-off of the air frying technique. However, the taco salad was a winner with its spicy seitan chorizo that packed a punch without compromising taste.

Desserts here are a must-try; I opted for a sweet treat to cap off my meal. The cookies, especially the chocolate espresso variety, were divine, with the lemon and classic chocolate chip following closely in deliciousness.

And, for those savvy savers, the promotion of $10 off a $15 purchase via their app is a steal that's too good to overlook. This spot combines tasty bites with smart savings!

Prince Street Pizza in Manhattan stands out as a top contender for the city's best pizza. The bustling spot offers a cozy experience with standing room only, perfect for a quick, delicious bite. Opting for a classic pepperoni slice, I was delighted by the thick, soft dough and the subtly sweet sauce complemented by a generous coating of perfectly stretchy cheese. The pepperoni was the true star—crispy, well-seasoned with a touch of spice, and liberally applied to each slice. This place is generous with toppings, a detail I greatly appreciated. My experience was so satisfying that I'm already planning a return visit to sample more varieties. Prince Street Pizza delivers exceptional pizza, hands down.

I recently dined at a Greek restaurant that transported me straight to the ambiance of Mykonos, despite it being an alternative to my usual midtown spot. Opting for a closer venture to accommodate my friend's location, we dove into a hearty meal on a Monday evening.

The continuity in decor and menu with its sister location created an instantly familiar environment. We shared a spanakopita appetizer, its flaky filo pastry enveloping a generous amount of flavorful spinach filling. For mains, both the pork and chicken skewers did not disappoint, offering up well-seasoned and perfectly grilled bites, complemented by fluffy pita bread and a tangy tzatziki sauce. The standout Greek fries were a crispy delight, crowned with an ample sprinkling of feta cheese and oregano.

Portion sizes were satisfying, and prices reasonable for the quality and quantity of food presented. However, an interaction marred the experience slightly when a request for ketchup was met with a pointed remark that, while likely intended as lighthearted, came across as somewhat dismissive.

Though the cuisine left us delighted, it's worth noting the service lacked the warmth I've experienced at the midtown location. Great food notwithstanding, for future visits, I'll favor the establishment where the service matches the quality of the meal.

Title: A Sweet Spot for Taiwanese Treats

I recently ventured to a bustling Chinatown eatery at prime time on a Saturday night, keen to sample their Taiwanese shaved ice and grass jelly desserts. Despite the crowd, the five of us managed to snag a spot at a communal round table, an experience typical of the neighborhood's popular spots.

My choice for the evening was the mango shaved ice, which was refreshingly delicious, bursting with the essence of ripe mangoes. I also tried the house-made grass jelly deluxe which proved to be an interesting departure from the canned variety I'm accustomed to. This version was thicker and had a glutinous texture that didn't exactly win me over, reminding me to stick with the familiar canned type on future visits.

The taro balls accompanying the desserts were notably chewy and satisfyingly filling. Straying from the sweet side, we ordered fried popcorn chicken that regrettably didn't hit the mark due to its lack of freshness. On a better note, a friend's noodle dish turned out to be pretty scrumptious, piquing my interest in the savory side of the menu.

Despite the miss with the chicken, I'm intrigued enough by the flavors experienced to consider a return trip, with the minced pork rice, pork chop, and another noodle dish in my sights for the next round of tasting.

Overall, a promising spot for those seeking a taste of Taiwan's sweet and savory offerings amidst the vibrant backdrop of Chinatown nightlife.

Title: A Sweet Spot That's Worth the Wait

As repeat visitors to Spot Dessert, my enthusiasm for their sweet offerings remains high, despite the uptick in pricing. The first taste had us hooked with its explosive flavors, and though prices have crept up, the desserts retain their delectable charm. Be warned that this location may test your patience with a 15-20 minute wait, but the reward is worth the delay.

I appreciate their culinary creativity, especially with the seasonal rotations that beckon a return for every new reveal. If you're seeking my personal favorites, I highly recommend indulging in The Harvest for its intricate layers, followed by the comforting crunch of the Golden Toast, and finally the Matcha Lava for that warm, earthy kick.

While your wallet may feel lighter, the experience at Spot Dessert is a richness that justifies the cost, earning a solid $$ on the price scale.

Upon my arrival at Paisley, the surprisingly calm atmosphere contrasted with its elegant decor, featuring regal purple and gold hues. The spacious dining area welcomed us with a well-appointed table by the window. The staff's hospitality was evident from the start, offering to take our coats and umbrellas, which was a thoughtful touch.

Throughout our meal, the service was impeccable, with attentive staff seamlessly bringing out dishes and ensuring our dining experience was pleasant. The menu offered an array of small plates, each at a reasonable $14, accompanied by flavorful garlic naan.

The standout dish for me was the Delhi Chaat, a delightful surprise with its cold lentil dumplings and a harmonious mix of flavors, elevated by the unexpected addition of pomegranate seeds. The Lahori Paneer and Nilgiri Chicken were also commendable, with the latter being succulently cooked. Even the Kerela Beef, which I'm less inclined to order, impressed me with its tenderness.

Paisley undoubtedly made a great impression, and I wholeheartedly recommend it for those seeking to explore an eclectic mix of flavors. It's a gem deserving of a wider audience.

Another location, the 3rd to open quite quickly, with the same excellent slices as at the downtown locations.The Al Pastor is fun, and the plain is really one of the best of the new school slice joints. This is a great addition to an area that can use a good slice joint. They'll be adding their even better square slices soon, so I'll definitely be back.
