All I can say is WOW. I've heard of this company before but I never stepped into any of their locations or had anything on their menu. After this first visit however I'm 100% sold. It's undoubtedly some of the best pizza I've had in the UES.My sister and I walked in around 3 in the afternoon on a Saturday. We had just finished checking out the nearby Guggenheim Museum and were looking for a pizza spot that also had options like spaghetti and calzones for purchase alongside their variety of slices. Our yelp search showed us that Marinara was the closest one so we decided to give it a try.The restaurant itself is kind of a modern "no frills" space with a clean look on the inside inside. It had both indoor and outdoor seating as well as complimentary water for customers. We opted to sit outside since it was a nice day out. We had a decent view of the traffic going up and down Lexington avenue.When it came time to order I went with their pepperoni ($3) and buffalo chicken ($5) slices. The pepperoni option came topped with a hearty amount of it's namesake. The buffalo chicken was also a great slice and the addition of the complimentary sweet hot honey dressing made it amazing. Good quality slices for their costs.Great service and even greater slices. I'd definitely give these guys a try if you're in the UES!

Took the kids here for lunch on a weekday. The place was about half full. We were promptly seated and the kids were given crayons and an activity page with kids menu at the back of it. Wide selection of options available. Kids menu range from $7 onwards which includes the main, side and drink. A scoop of ice cream is an additional $1. We were provided with complimentary bread whilst we waited for our food to come. I got myself a plate of pasta with steak and shrimp which was $20 and also a sirloin kids meal. The food took awhile to arrive but it wasn't anything too crazy. The food we ordered was pretty nice for what it was. The steak was nothing like Wolfgang's or striphouse but I went in knowing it was going to be average so it worked out fine. Service was pretty good. Our server was friendly and attentive. All in all, good experience for what I ate and paid for.

Title: A Flavorful Find Near Times Square

I recently had the pleasure of trying out a restaurant near Times Square, and I must say, it was a delightful experience. I ordered the Tex Mex salad and the pesto mac and cheese, both of which were scrumptious. The pesto mac and cheese, in particular, was a stand-out; it managed to be flavorful without being overly rich—a perfect choice for a busy workday lunch.

The Tex Mex salad had a nice spicy kick, although it arrived with more dressing than I would have liked, despite requesting it light. This was a minor hiccup in an otherwise tasty dish.

Despite the slip with the salad dressing, this place has certainly earned a spot on my list of go-to spots around Times Square, and I'm looking forward to my next order. Highly recommended for a satisfying meal that hits the spot!

Title: A Delightful Surprise During Restaurant Week

I recently had the pleasure of dining here during restaurant week with a friend, and what an experience it was! The menu was innovative, starting with a chilled cucumber soup that, while a bit unconventional, proved to be a refreshing appetizer. Despite its uniqueness, once was enough for me. The main course, however—a corn nut crusted flounder—was a standout. The sweetness of the corn coupled with an unexpected spicy kick brought the flounder to life in a way that truly delighted the palate.

But the pièce de résistance was the chocolate cake dessert. It was a decadent twist on a classic lava cake, both in presentation and taste, outshining its traditional counterpart. The rich chocolate filling was superb and the pairing with salted vanilla ice cream was perfection. I highly recommend saving room for this indulgent treat. All in all, this restaurant provides not just a meal, but a memorable culinary adventure.

I love Korean food so decided to settle here for lunch. This place has a variety of lunch special. One of them was my favorite Squid hot pot Bibimbop. They had a good variety of side dishes. They also served Pumpkin soup. Really liked it.The bibimbop was tasty as well. Would want to come back again for other dishes.

Title: A Long Wait for an Oversauced Disappointment at Nanoosh

After routinely noticing the bustling scene at Nanoosh in the Rockefeller Center's underground during lunchtime, my curiosity finally won out on a day when the queue appeared more forgiving. Familiar with Naya's offerings, a similar eatery in close proximity, I ventured to try something new with hopes of a comparable, if not superior, experience.

My order of Chicken Shawa with half rice, half greens, and a request for extra toppings seemed straightforward enough. However, the swiftness of the ordering process did not carry over to the food preparation. It became clear that the bottleneck was not at the register but at the pick-up point, where I joined a crowd of around 20 diners in the waiting game.

The anticipation faltered upon receiving my meal, which was submerged under an excessive deluge of tzatziki sauce. The overzealous dressing required an unappetizing excavation before I could properly start my meal. In reflection, Nanoosh lacked the transparent and customizable service of Naya, which not only allows customers to supervise their meal assembly but also makes the wait seem shorter. Additionally, Naya's more generous portions and no-extra-charge toppings, paired with a slightly lower price point, left me with the conclusion that my loyalty remains with Naya, while Nanoosh remains a one-time visit not to be repeated.

Title: Delightful Birthday Celebration at a Mediterranean Gem

I recently had the pleasure of celebrating my husband's birthday at a charming restaurant with a group of 11 friends, and it was nothing short of wonderful. With its clean, classic aesthetic and light, Mediterranean-inspired ambiance, the restaurant provided the perfect setting for our celebration.

The highlight was the interactive dining experience provided by the charismatic chef who masterfully held court in the center of the room. Not only did he show us the art of grilling fish Greek style, but he also shared secrets to crafting an authentic Greek salad and other pro tips that were both enlightening and entertaining.

Our diverse dietary needs were seamlessly accommodated with a versatile menu, pleasing everyone from gluten-free guests who raved about the decadent chocolate mousse to those with other restrictions. The freshness and quality of the food were evident, and each dish was a hit.

Capping off the night with the playful touch of the "YMCA" tune as a sparkler-topped treat was brought to my husband, the restaurant truly went above and beyond.

In summary, for anyone seeking great value and a unique dining experience that pairs delicious fare with an educational twist, this restaurant is an absolute must-try.

I had a delightful lunch experience at this eatery where freshness is clearly a priority. The food was absolutely delicious, made with high-quality ingredients that cater to a variety of dietary choices including vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options. The added touch of a complimentary hot drink with their bowls was a lovely perk. Highly recommend for a tasty and inclusive meal.

Been here twice now, once for HH and once for brunch. Both good experiences with service and yummy food. I liked the happy hour classic margarita much better than the breakfast margarita. The mimosa, however, was tasty too. Note: on your house margarita ask for a spicy salt rim.My favorite thing here is the pulled pork tostada. Great flavors. Their house sauces are great and come in cute bottles, just hard to pour as they should add hot sauce lids to these. The brisket taco was my second favorite thing. I ordered on a GF flour tortilla, but found out in second visit from ordering again that the first visit I had gotten it on a tort that had trace amounts of flour even though the server told me about the GF option and that's what I ordered. It's the risk I took in eating out, so not mad, just a little annoyed. I am not celiac, just have a sensitivity. I think they should add a regular corn tortilla to the menu as the gf flour is not that good. However, the tostadas and bowls are great. Will be ordering those from here on out.Great staff and good vibes. Prices are reasonable. My friend that came with me for brunch agreed that the side of bacon. 2 mini strips for $4 was a little much but did taste good.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience

My visit to this charming restaurant was nothing short of excellent. The staff greeted me with warmth and friendliness that added a cozy touch to the meal. Service was prompt as rolls appeared quickly on the table, with the rice served still warm - a clear sign of their attention to freshness.

The yellowtail hand roll was the star of the show; it was undoubtedly one of the best I've ever savored. The balance of flavors left a lasting impression, enough to have me craving more. I'm already looking forward to my next visit, as this place is truly a gem that calls for repeated enjoyment.

I recently visited this charming restaurant, drawn in by its pretty decor and reputation for nice service. True to form, the ambiance was inviting and the staff was attentive. Opting for lunch, I started with the gazpacho, which unfortunately was underwhelming and reminiscent of a cream of tomato soup rather than the robust, zesty flavors one would expect. 

The Chicken Caesar salad was generously portioned but didn't quite hit the mark. While the sheer size was impressive, the chicken was a letdown with its rubbery texture and lack of depth. It seemed to prioritize quantity over quality.

However, it's worth noting that I had dined here previously for dinner and had a much more delightful experience with the duck, which was outstanding and worth recommending. In all, if you find yourself at this restaurant, you may want to consider their dinner offerings over the lunch menu for a more satisfying culinary adventure.

Title: A Five-Star Gem Worth the Wait

Despite the challenge of snagging a reservation, this restaurant more than earns its five stars with exceptional food and a warm, inviting service atmosphere. The burger here has set a new standard for me; it's simply the best. Elevate it to legendary status by adding an egg and bacon - trust me on this one. The 'Four Charles' steak, accompanied by a zesty horseradish dip, was a unique delight, reminiscent of succulent, thick-cut pastrami - a truly unparalleled flavor experience. The corn side dish was another standout, a mouthwatering combination of cream, cheese, and a surprising crunch - easily the best corn I've ever savored. And the spinach? Absolutely divine. If only it weren't such a feat to secure a table, I'd be back in a heartbeat.

Title: Decent Lunch Spot for Groups, Dinner Lacks Value

Rating: 3.75/5

Málà Project undeniably has the vibrant buzz of Midtown, attracting an after-work crowd that fills its space, which comfortably accommodates large groups. My dining experience there, however, was a mix of hits and misses.

While the Turnip with Jellyfish appetizer shone both in taste and value, the centerpiece of the meal – the málà hotpot – left me with mixed feelings. The 'mild' heat level had a perfect tingle, and the overall flavor of the hotpot was enjoyable, yet the portioning was disproportionately skewed. High expectations for a medley of beef tenderloin, pork belly, fish balls, tofu skin, and veggies turned into bemusement as some items like the Chinese cabbage were scarcely present, making the cost per ingredient rather steep.

Our total came to a reasonable $60, but I found the value for dinner didn't quite hit the mark. On the other hand, their lunch offerings appear more wallet-friendly, and I'd recommend giving those a try instead. Would I go back? Perhaps for a casual lunch, but not for a dinner that promises more than it delivers.

We were really looking forward to dinner at Zuma before a Lakers/Knicks game on Jan 22nd.  I have had meals here before and brought clients previously for business luncheon meetings.  This dining experience was the biggest disappointment in recent months because of the poor attitude of a manager hired by this restaurant.  Let's start with the very bad:  We ordered the prawn and black cod dumplings as a starter.  The dumplings arrived, but when we took a bite, the center of the dumplings was cold and the dumpling wrapper was lukewarm.  When we reflected this feedback to the server (so he can tell the kitchen), he took the dish back (which we said we would still pay for) and a manager stopped by thereafter to speak to us.  We did not get his name, but he has grey hair and a unique accent.  He said "I noticed that the dumplings were sent back, is there an issue?"  When we mentioned to him that the dumplings were cold, he became confrontational and added, "we cannot control the food temperature, it could be that the order was brought out and was sitting for a while at your table before you guys took a bite.  We cannot guarantee they would still be hot."  Keep in mind that the picture I took on my phone has a time stamp, between the time that the dumplings arrived and the time we ate it, that was no more than 2 minutes.   We told him that we just wanted to inform the kitchen (so they can get this feedback for future orders) because the dumplings were cold.  The male manager showed even more attitude towards us as if we were trying to get free food (even though we insisted we would pay for the item and just wanted to give feedback to the kitchen and continue with our meal).  He just would not let it go and made us feel very uncomfortable.  My friend repeated to him that we just want to bring this feedback to the kitchen's attention and we were not trying to get anything out of it.  The manager finally left with a smirk on his face and said it was served hot to us.  Our total bill for the dinner was close to $300 (we still left a generous tip as this was no fault of the server), but this terrible individual basically ruined the whole experience over a $18.50 dish (which the manager still left on the bill even though the server took the dish back.  However, I guess we asked him to still charge us so he did).  He never apologized and didn't even acknowledge he would give the feedback to the kitchen.   The person I was with did go speak to another manager, her name was Cinzia, to inform her that the male manager made us feel uncomfortable. She did apologize and offer us free drinks at the bar but he respectfully declined as he didn't want to be a patron of the restaurant going forward.

Beautiful!   The establishment, the staff, the food, the brunch...  I have this place bookmarked.  It's great for all occasions and it's sleek and classy.   The brunch deal is great and the menu is fantastic.  We had a birthday brunch with a sizable party.  Shaterri took care of us and was nothing short of perfect.  She is professional, friendly, hospitable.  She had a way about her that makes her service effortless.  The bartenders were great too!  I have bookmarked this establishment as I will be returning very very soon.   Highly recommended!

Title: Satisfying Eats and Happy Hour Bliss at a NYC Gem

I recently enjoyed a delightful dining experience at a cozy New York City spot, which my friend and I chanced upon while exploring the area on a bustling Saturday night. With no reservations, our wait time was impressively brief, setting the stage for an evening of culinary pleasure.

The highlight of our visit was stumbling upon the Happy Hour specials, which lasted until 8pm—a rare find in the city! We indulged in $6 beers, a steal that only made our meals more enjoyable. My friend savored a scrumptious Beef Stew, the rich flavors and tender meat of which she couldn't praise enough. Meanwhile, I tackled a hearty Steak Sandwich loaded with blue cheese, mushrooms, bacon, and a generous 10-ounce steak. While cooked to my preference, the steak pieces were quite large, making it a challenge to consume as intended. Nevertheless, the flavors were spot on, and I relished every bite I managed to cut with a fork.

The ambiance of the restaurant was the quintessential snug NYC setting, paired with prices that didn't break the bank—an aspect we greatly appreciated. However, our dining experience was slightly marred by the service. Our waitress lacked warmth and attentiveness—she did not check in on us after delivering our meals nor did she engage in any meaningful interaction. A little hospitality goes a long way in making a meal memorable.

Despite this, the overall experience was very pleasant. The restaurant delivered on both taste and value, warranting a solid 4-star review. I would happily return for another round of that delightful Happy Hour and the mouth-watering dishes.

Solid customer service. However the food is bland. Chicken and waffles could've been great had they added a little salt and pepper to the batter or seasoned the chicken. I prefer fluffier waffles, so they were hard for my likes. They were good by any other standards. Fruit was fresh and sweet. We had some fries, which were seasoned with rosemary. Very tasty. Drinks were around $13.50. Typical for NY, but not a waste of money. You'll want two however. For the price point, I think you can do better overall. Cool vibe and has potential to be 5 stars with few changes.

Title: Unique Dining Experience, Ramen Falls Short

I dropped by this ramen spot for the unique service experience, which certainly didn't disappoint. From the moment I was greeted and seated, the staff's attention to detail shone. The bar seating setup and private solo booths with dividers are thoughtful touches that suit individual diners or those seeking solitude.

Their Classic Tonkotsu Ramen comes with a fun twist – customizable options ranging from noodle thickness to broth saltiness, all ordered via a handy table button. At $20 a bowl, expectations were high, yet the execution didn't fully measure up. While the broth was a delightful mix of flavors, especially with the spicy red sauce, the pork slices failed to impress, both in portion size and taste.

The current promotional offer of extra noodles is a plus, but it's not enough to entice me back solely for the ramen. In essence, this place is worth the visit for its service and unique concept, but when it comes to the ramen itself, it may leave true enthusiasts wanting more.

Raku is an amazing restaurant that serves ramen's underrated cousin.... udon!! Dining at raku was such a great experience. I had read many positive reviews and was really looking forward to visiting during my trip to New York. When my boyfriend and I finally tried it out, we were absolutely blown away.AMBIENCE: Small and intimate. The outside of the restaurant doesn't have a sign, so look for the hanging drape in front of their doorway. Inside, the restaurant is dimly lit and very minimalistic, which creates a very special and intimate atmosphere. It felt like we were transported to a nice udon restaurant in Japan! SERVICE: Very friendly and attentive. Our server pointed out the hooks under the table where we could hang our bags since the restaurant itself is small and cozy.FOOD:*** Chicken tatsuta-age 5/5: This fried chicken was AMAZING. It was fried perfectly so that each bite had the most satisfying crunch. The meat inside was extremely tender and juicy. I nearly burned my tongue because I was so excited to eat all of it before my boyfriend did lol. *** Gyunan hot udon 5/5: I ordered the beef udon, and it was delicious! Even though it was a clear broth, it tasted super flavorful and rich. The udon itself had the perfect chewiness, and you can tell it is freshly made. The beef was soft and tender. All the flavors complemented each other and made for a delicious, comforting meal. Chikari hot udon 4/5: The bf ordered this hot udon and it was also very tasty. It had the same broth and udon noods as the gyunan but also included huge portions of mochi and chicken. The mochi was incredibly soft and chewy, and actually tasted so good in combination with the other ingredients. However, it was also very filling and heavy. I would recommend splitting this udon!

I'm way behind on reviews, so I had to pick which one did I want to jump off with.  If you've read any of my previous reviews, you may already know that I'm New York born and raised.  It doesn't make me an expert on all things NY, but I'm pretty confident that I know what I like and can make informed judgments based on that knowledge.  I also know that not everyone appreciates the same things that I do, so I can fully understand the disparate ratings I see on a lot of establishments.With that said, I'm a new HUGE fan of Joe's Pizza.  I've passed it several times over the years, mostly because I don't like standing in line.  What changed for me this time?  My wife; she wanted to see what the big deal was.  Up until that point, I'd never even set foot inside, I'd just snicker at all the suckers lining up on my way past to or coming from Times Square.Anyway, once we got to the part of the line that gets to stand indoors, I got a look around and realized that there was nothing immediately special about the place, except for how busy it always seems to be.  It was your average, run-of-the-mill pizza parlor on a smaller scale.  Everyone knows NY is tight for space, so seating is minimal...a couple of round tops with stools, and slim counter space around the outer edges with more stools for those who want to eat in.  There's some of the same counter space just outside the place.  There is one thing of note that I mentioned previously- the lines.  EVERY time I've walked by this place, there's a line out the door.  But I'm a native NYer and so I'm not one to stand in line when there are at least a half dozen spots in the immediate area that serve up the goods.  But hey, I have an excuse- the wife wanted to know what the big deal was, so we get in line, which moved rather quickly.  These guys were fast, I'll give them that.  It's like a well-oiled machine in there.  Anyway, as I was saying, not a fan of lines, typical know-it-all when it comes to NY staples...yeah.All of which flew out the window with the first bite.  The basics, thin crust, well done, a good ratio of sauce to cheese and a first- pepperoni.  I usually do just cheese because to me that's the benchmark; they get that right the rest usually falls in line.  Again, the wife's influence.  As usual, I'm very glad of her input; it was the best slice of pepperoni pizza I've ever eaten in my 40 years of eating pizza.  We're not gonna get into how old I was when I first had one, I'm telling you- this was the best.  I've eaten pizza all over the city, all five boroughs and both counties on Long Island.  This.  Is.  The.  BEST!  The sauce had really great flavor, without being too sweet or too acidic; the cheese was gooey and melty without being weirdly elastic- and no burn spots!  That's usually how I tell whether or not the cheese is really good (and the pizza man knows what he's doing) - if there's a lot of brown spotting on the cheese, like you'd see at a chain restaurant, I'm reasonably sure it won't taste as well either.  Thin crust- some places like to make it a little thicker, or underdone so that it is a little chewy, some use too much corn meal making for a gritty bite, etc etc - not here.  The crust was perfect.  The sauce, the cheese - the pepperoni was excellent, flavorful and plentiful without overpowering the underlying goodness it is supposed to augment.  And not overly greasy either- which is a bonus, considering the pig that was on top of it.  The garlic knots were equally fantastic- yet another thing that you normally don't find outside of NY.  God, I love those things!As for the rest of the place?  It isn't much to look at, except for the many celebrity photos adorning the walls; if that's your thing you'll have a few geek moments as you recognize a lot of them.  One other thing, it is cash-only, I didn't see any CC machines and didn't ask; I was lucky that I happened to be carrying that day.So, is this the best pizzeria in NYC?    I know that I'll be visiting it every time I go home- there is no other place I feel like I need to go to in order to get my fix.  I know that we visited it twice- once on our way to TS, and again on our way back after a shopping excursion.  First time for everything, it was certainly a first for me to stop at a single spot twice in the same day.  And enjoy it so completely as we did.  So, it is for us; though your mileage may vary, I sincerely hope it doesn't.

Made reservation at Rahi for restaurant week. Thoroughly enjoyed the overall experience. The entrees were served with rice and naan. Pros:Great ambianceService is goodHigh end Indian cuisineCons:Need reservations on weekendRecommendations:Banana leaf chicken (must try!!!)- the flavor of the curry is mind blowing and the chicken is very soft and juicy!Masala cheese omelette- Indian flavor and a lot of cheese and spicesMango lassi

Title: An Unlikely Match Made in Pizza Heaven – Mustard Meets Pastrami!

As a self-proclaimed pizza aficionado, I tend to seek out unique pizza experiences, which is how I stumbled upon a local gem serving up a mustard pizza. The initial reaction – a mix of curiosity and skepticism – quickly turned into intrigue upon discovering that pastrami was a key topping.

Located just two blocks from work, it's surprising that I hadn't noticed this pizzeria before. Upon entering, Rashad's warm greeting made me feel right at home. Expressing my interest in the mustard pizza I had seen online, he recommended trying it with a lighter mustard application. Trusting his judgment, I awaited my order with anticipation.

The verdict? The mustard pizza, complete with pastrami, was an unexpected delight. The bold flavors meshed harmoniously, creating a new favorite for my pizza repertoire. Not to overlook the classics, I sampled the pepperoni pizza too, which was generously topped and equally satisfying, though the mustard variant still stole my heart.

The setting is modest – a cozy space with standing tables only. However, what it lacks in seating, it makes up for in hospitality and the novelty of square pies.

Would I go back? Absolutely. Next week's dinner plans are already set for another square slice of that impressive mustard pizza.

A classic in NYC. Came in here last Friday for dinner and drinks. The wait staff is very kind and attentive. They really let you take your time and are very patient. We got the burger, crab cake, caesar salad, creamed spinach and Brussels sprouts. All were pretty good, nothing that blew us out of the water. You pay for the experience though.

Tucked away in the vibrant Union Square district of NYC, this gem has earned a favored spot on my dining list. With a diverse menu catering to an array of tastes, it's no wonder I've been a regular for nearly a decade. The service here is both quick and cordial—exemplifying the perfect balance of efficiency and hospitality.

One particularly impressive facet is the minimal wait time, a true rarity in such a bustling area. And once you've placed your order, you can expect a prompt arrival of your meal without sacrificing taste; each dish is consistently savory and satisfying.

The value is yet another highlight, with prices set at a reasonable level, ensuring a full stomach without emptying your wallet. My experiences here have been overwhelmingly positive, with very few instances of disappointment. For anyone in Union Square looking for a delightful meal served with a smile, this restaurant should not be missed.

Title: Tacombi – Don’t Let Appearances Fool You

Tacombi is certainly a hidden gem that you might overlook if you're judging solely on aesthetics. With its somewhat dingy exterior, you'd be tempted to pass by – I know I would have, had it not been for my friends' recommendation.

Once inside, the restaurant presents an unconventional dining experience. Instead of individual servers, our group of eight dealt with a communal menu system, which admittedly led to some confusion. The food service style is geared towards sharing, with dishes arriving sporadically as they're prepared. This meant our party was seldom eating in sync, and the staff did misplace some of our taco orders.

However, any misgivings about the service faded once we tasted the tacos. They were, without exaggeration, some of the best I've enjoyed – full of authentic flavor and worth returning for. The disappointment of the evening was the $12 sangria, which was underwhelming at best, tasting more like juice than a wine cocktail.

In sum, while Tacombi might miss the mark on ambiance and service, it hits a home run with its culinary offerings. The tacos are a must-try for any enthusiast.

Title: Quirky Surf and Turf Experience at Burger & Lobster

On a bustling Friday night, my indecisiveness led me to Burger & Lobster, as discovered through a Yelp search. Despite a reservation hiccup, we were pleasantly seated within 15 minutes by a gracious hostess and her assistant.

The restaurant's stylish decor created a lively ambiance, though the conversation volume was amplified by the somewhat overpowering music. The presentation was a notch above, with linen napkins complementing simple wood tables.

Our server promptly arrived, perhaps too quickly, before we had the chance to browse the menu. Upon his return, we decided on a burger and a lobster roll, both accompanied by salad and fries. A request for Cokes returned a surprise—organic cola was on offer, a novel concept for us.

The meal arrived efficiently: the burger was perfectly cooked to medium, and the fries were suitably warm. The ample lobster roll was flavorful with a touch of Japanese mayo, and the fries maintained the warmth. Unfortunately, the salad was lackluster, leaving me to wonder about the dressing's origins.

Service seemed to falter slightly as our server vanished and a busser stepped in for refills. The absence of dessert options led us to seek a sweet finale elsewhere, at a nearby soft serve truck.

Would I revisit Burger & Lobster? It's an "Organic no" from me, a playful nod to the intriguing organic cola that still intrigues my palate.

Title: Unique Flavors at Safari Somalian Cuisine

I recently visited Safari, a cozy Somalian eatery that offers a unique dining experience, albeit with a slightly higher price tag. My dining companion and I indulged in the jumbo steak and mango chicken curry. Although we initially aimed to enjoy mango juices, a shortage led us to try fiimto, a berry and hibiscus concoction that delighted with its sweet profile, outshining the somewhat watery mango juice.

Both entrees were served with rice and bis-baas sauce, a combination I wasn't particularly fond of due to its overpowering spiciness and sourness. The mango chicken curry, however, won me over with its delicious and mild flavor profile. The jumbo steak fell short, unfortunately, not only lacking in beef quantity but also in taste, coming across as excessively salty. In contrast, the mango curry was the highlight of our meal.

Despite the bis-baas and the steak's saltiness, Safari offered a memorable culinary journey with its distinct Somali flavors. The fiimto alone is a refreshing reason to return.

On a hot summer day, nothing beats a scoop of ice cream from Wafles and Dinges with their hardening chocolate sauce poured over the  top.BUT on a cold winter night I had to mix things up and try their hot chocolate (which, as you can see, cane with a very generous amount of marshmallows and whipped cream!)Yes, maybe it was a bit pricey for a standard not chocolate, but still way better than what you'll get at your local starbucks or bodega.Can't want for the warm days to roll back in so I can enjoy my icecream without feeling like a weirdo for eating it in subzero temperatures!

Patron Mexican Grill is always a good time. I came here once in the summer and on New Years Eve. What attracted me to this restaurant were their drinks inside the Patron bottles so that was the first thing I ordered here. My first time, I spent $90+ and my bf spend $90+. That was for two Patron drinks, two appetizers, two entrees and two shots plus tip! The second time we came they were having a deal on margaritas (which are amazing btw) and filled up on those as well as an entree and guac and chips. This restaurant can get super crowded to the point you're basically sitting out the door. They have a bar area, high tables in the front and regular tables towards the back. The high tables can be a bit annoying just because if you're carrying things there is no where to put them and the space is pretty tight. When it's cold out, sitting by the door is also not ideal as people are always going in and out of the restaurant. Overall, I have to say the food is pretty delicious, the drinks are not too strong and the service is fast and personable.

Title: A Square Cut Above the Rest at Prince St. Pizza

With a line stretching 30-40 people deep, Prince St. Pizza sets high expectations – and remarkably, it lives up to every one of them. Upon the strong recommendation of many, I decided to try their fame, and as it turns out, the buzz is well-deserved.

I opted for the hefty square cut pepperoni, which was nothing short of stellar. Sure, it was a tad on the greasy side, but that's a small price to pay for the explosion of flavors and freshness in each bite. The pepperoni was top-notch, indicative of their commitment to fresh ingredients. The mozzarella was a standout, clearly house-made and oozing quality.

In the thriving New York pizza scene, Prince St. Pizza distinguishes itself as more than just a neighborhood favorite – it's a culinary landmark for any pizza connoisseur. Don't let the line discourage you; the wait is a small sacrifice for one of the city's finest slices.

Craving Thai food? Top Thai should definitely be on your top "must try" list here in NYC. Nestled in a  trendy location, it makes for the perfect night out. Happy hour, tasty food and drinks, and SUPERIOR service are what make Top Thai an Elite restaurant. Not to mention they are on the Yelp Top 100 for NYC!Upon arrival we were greeted by the host and he advised us of the wait. He was an extremely proficient host, as he kept checking on us, making sure we were ok, and updated us on the waiting time. We were soon notified a table was open for seating! Inside is a bit on the small side, but it makes for an intimate dinner and servers have easy access to you as well. Once we were seated, our waitress gave us a warm welcome and advised us of their specials and favorite things on the menu. We ordered a beer, the ROSE margarita, and a happy hour mango margarita with Crab Rangoon Won Tons to start. The drinks came out SO fast. I felt so fancy with my Rose Margarita the way it was served, and the taste was SPECTACULAR! Major kudos to the bartender that night. The won tons were a major flavor explosion in your mouth and I highly recommend them as a starter. For dinner, we ordered their Pad Thai w/Steak, and Pad See You w/ chicken...pure perfection. Just an FYI, I am a MAJOR Thai food junkie. I have only a select few places I will try Thai food and I just added top thai to my list! We are originally from Southern Cali, however we frequent NY a couple times a year. I will definitely be bringing my family and friends back here for dinner! Thank you TOP THAI for the superb dining experience.

Visited this gem for the famed pad thai and it absolutely lived up to my expectations! With a prime window seat, my parents and I enjoyed the bustling atmosphere, though there's plenty of additional space to accommodate the lunchtime rush. Opting for the shrimp pad thai, I was delighted by arguably one of the finest renditions of the dish I've experienced. The service was the cherry on top; our waitress couldn't have been more charming. This spot is definitely on my list for future outings with friends. Highly recommended!

A friend ranted and raved about this place but both of us were underwhelmed with this particular meal. Not sure I'd go back.The delivery aspect was quick and no complaints there.Foodwise, we over ordered for two, but got the following:-Three spreads with skordalia (garlic dip), tyrokafteri (spicy feta dip), and taramosalata (salmon roe dip). $19.50-Spanakopita $12-pork skewer $4.50-pippereries gemistes (two grilled stuffed horn peppers with greek cheeses,scallion, and dill) $15-psita lachanika (mixed grilled vegetables , zucchini, eggplant, colored peppers, olive oil and balsmic vinegar) $17-handcut greek fries (sprinkled with feta cheese and seasoned with greek oregano) $9All in all, the only thing I liked was the handcut fries an the tyrokafteri dip. The fries were nicely covered in cheese and were towards the McDonalds soggy side, but better. The spicy cheese dip wasn't that spicy, but was pretty nice with the large amount of warm pita bread they gave us.  The pork skewer wasn't that bad either with the tzatziki sauce.The stuffed peppers were not very stuffed and were bland. They used green peppers, so no flavor in the pepper at all. The worst item in the order. The other two dips were not great.  The salmon roe was far too salty, almost inedible, and we didn't eat more than two bites of the garlic dip. The veggies and spanakopita were nothing special in comparison to other Greek restaurants I've been to. Unfortunately, somewhere between 2 and 3 stars, but maybe the other dishes are better.

I absolutely adore this restaurant! Initially, I hadn't intended to dine on vegan fare, but the inviting ambiance lured me inside. To my amazement, every dish I tried was delicious. The Kale Caesar salad, with its shiitake bacon and maple-wheat croutons, was a standout — truly mind-blowing flavors! I'm eagerly looking forward to returning and exploring more of their menu.

Title: A Must-Visit for Mexican Fare in Hell's Kitchen

Whenever I return to New York City, a visit to Arriba Arriba is non-negotiable. Tucked away in Hell's Kitchen, this gem offers solid Mexican cuisine that won't break the bank. My go-to orders, the chimichanga and enchiladas suizas, have yet to disappoint. A bonus is the complimentary chips and salsa that deliver a satisfying crunch while you browse the menu.

The compact bar area is my preferred seat, where the bartenders exhibit unmatched skill and charm. And whatever you do, don't leave without trying the Mama margarita. Regardless of your preference for frozen or on the rocks, original or flavored, the Mama packs a punch with a blend of taste and potency that's nothing short of perfection. Arriba Arriba remains a staple for both its consistently good food and the buzz from its signature drinks.

This is my second location and it also has great food. Stopped in here for lunch and shared a Fisch with the table, and had my own jamburrito quesarito and a tuna ceviche tostada. I demolished the quesarito as it was really good. The tostada was flavored well but gave me trouble as the toppings kept falling off the shell and onto the plate or table. I'd stick with a taco next time for that reason alone.Each item is about $6.50 each and you need at least 2 for the average person.Service was good, but expect to sit 30-60m for lunch if you're in a hurry.

The house special pho was so flavorful, so much goodness. Definitely a very rich and tasty broth and paired with the marrow and breadstick made it a hearty meal. But, the surprising dish of eggplant blew me away. The glazed, caramelized peanuts made it over the top. Little spicy but worth to try it. The hostess and bartender were awesome and I found out after they were the owners. I only wished the lighting was better for me to take better pictures of the eggplant (overall), but a good place to stop by and try.

I've been here in the morning and evening and both times were crowded but we were seated fairly quickly both times. The space is very small so you will probably be sitting near strangers, but this is to be expected of nyc.I always get the Green Shakshuka which tastes kind of pesto- like and not tomatoey  like normal shakshuka. It was  delicious. My friends also enjoyed their food i believe a waffle and chicken sandwich. They have a lot of vegetarian options and overall great service especially considering how busy they always are. Definitely one of my favorite brunch spots.

I seen this place being offered on Mealpal often.  I used to shy away from this place and go to Sophie's instead.  But today, I decided to give their Mealpal a try.  I am glad I did.  The service was fast and I got my order right away.  The amount of food is spectacular and the baked chicken is cooked perfectly and moist.  The black beans over rice and a carrot as well as potato stick all complimented each other well.  They have me two green sauces by default.  Based off today's order, I would definitely try them again.

Title: A Funky Spot for Tasty Tacos and More

My latest Instagram discovery led us to a taco haven that did not disappoint. Upon arrival, we were promptly seated and just in time to catch happy hour. The Lychee Martini caught my eye and did not let down - a perfect blend of flavor and kick.

The taco tasting began with a decent shrimp taco, followed by a chicken taco that was elevated by its aioli and sriracha mayo. However, the Bulgogi Taco stole the show with its incredibly flavorful meat that was nothing short of a culinary delight.

We also indulged in Tempura shrimp, which was quite tasty, although the abundance of lettuce beneath was a slight letdown, giving the illusion of more shrimp than provided.

The ambiance was as enjoyable as the food, with a small yet vibrant space adorned with fun and funky decor, all complemented by a lively soundtrack. Happy hour here is worth noting, running until 7 pm with some tempting deals.

Service was attentive, prices didn’t break the bank, and both our palates and spirits were left wholly satisfied. This spot is a definite must-try for taco enthusiasts and those looking for a laid-back dining experience with a twist.
This place is full vegan, lovely. I enjoyed the smokey hummus so much. It's not super impressive or anything, but I love they put together all these beets and roots around the plate.

Title: Great Food Marred by Lackluster Service at Black Tap

I recently had a mixed experience at Black Tap. While the food was impressive, the service left much to be desired. My partner ordered through Seamless for a 6:30 pm pickup, including an All-American Burger, a Crispy Chicken Sandwich (both with sweet potato fries), and extra sauces. Unfortunately, upon arrival, he discovered our order had been discarded without any prior communication.

The confusion started as soon as he stepped in and mentioned our online order, which was met with the unsettling response, “Oh, we thought you weren’t coming.” Despite just being slightly late, there was no attempt made by the restaurant to reach out via phone or email, which seems like a basic courtesy.

The result was a needless 30-minute wait for a new order to be prepared, compounded by the absence of an apology or a discount for the inconvenience.

On the upside, our meal, once it arrived, did not disappoint. The All-American Burger with its juicy patty, fresh lettuce, tomato, American cheese, and special sauce was a hit, as was the delectably crisp chicken sandwich accented by tangy coleslaw, cilantro, lime, and spicy mayo. The sweet potato fries were a delightful side and the house-made special sauce was exceptional. The truffle aioli, however, was a regrettable choice for me, not complementing the fries as I had hoped.

In conclusion, Black Tap serves up delicious fare, but the oversight with our online order was a significant drawback. I sincerely hope they refine their communication and handling of pickup orders to match the quality of their food.

My friend and I went to Bob's Steak & Chop House at 1pm on a Sunday for Restaurant Week ($26 for entree + dessert).  The restaurant is part of the Omni Berkshire Place Hotel but you can enter from the street.  The interior is classy and what you would expect for a $$$ steakhouse.  I had made a reservation but it was totally unnecessary!  We were the only people in the restaurant for a majority of our lunch.  A few people came in to drink at the bar, but only one other family came in to the dining room.I got salmon and my friend got filet mignon (6oz).  We both got got the molten chocolate cake for dessert.  Both of our entrees came with a large carrot and mashed potatoes.  The potatoes were delightful!  They had a light garlic flavor that was not overpowering and were seasoned well and whipped to a nice consistency.  The carrot was also cooked well without having a mush consistency.  The filet mignon was cooked to order and was tender, flavored well, and juicy.  The salmon was also cooked well but needed a touch more flavor throughout.  The seasoning was concentrated on top, but was not enough to complete every bite.  The dessert was a standard chocolate cake.  The cake was moist, chocolate was rich, and berries tasted fresh!Service was awesome, although not difficult since we were the only ones in the restaurant.  Every person on the waitstaff was kind and we had multiple check-backs and water refills.  I'm so grateful that Bob's participated in restaurant week so we could take advantage of this deal!  If I am feeling fancy, I would come back to Bob's because the food was good and service was fantastic.  I do recommend Bob's for anyone wanting to check it out for restaurant week!

Title: Mixed Feelings on Mama Mia's

I recently dined at Mama Mia's, where the food largely lived up to its appetizing reputation, yet some aspects left room for improvement. While the mushroom raviolis were a delightful fusion of spinach and goat cheese and come strongly recommended, the cheesy garlic bread missed the mark with its lackluster flavor. My companion found the penne arrabbiata to be enjoyable, though it lacked the spicy kick expected from such a dish.

However, the dining experience was soured by customer service woes. Despite having a reservation for 6:00 PM, we were not seated until nearly 6:45 PM, which seemed to be a common issue among diners that evening due to apparent overbooking. This delay put a strain on our plans, as we were attending a show at 7:30 PM.

In summary, the culinary offerings at Mama Mia's have potential, but the service hiccups cannot be overlooked. I might consider returning, but certainly not when time is of the essence.

Great little Louge location.Bartender JJ was super cool and informative on offerings.Upon Elite Yelp check in you can score 20 tasty good sized wings for $15. That a pretty good deal for a Manhattan location. I originally ordered Teriyaki and Buffalo style but received Teriyaki and BBQ styles. I requested to split the order in half so i would get 10 Teriyaki and 10 Buffalo, but ok got close sorta with two sweet tastes to the play with.All was good and they were very gracious enough to stay open a bit later so I could walk back to them in 5/10 mintues to grab my small bag.  Super thankful and would definitely go back again since food, drinks and service was good.

I can say I had a very nice experience here. I booked it last min for a quick bite and it turns out instayed longer than anticipated.  I walked in about 10 feet towards hostess podium and was greeted so warmly by Chelsea. She has a contagious smile and if you even wanted to go somewhere else, you could not with her warm welcome. She seated us right away at a high table by the front. The place seemed close to capacity already, maybe because of happy hour witlchnis from 330p to 630pm. Happy hour has 1/2 priced oysters, $5 beers, $8 wines and $10 specialty drinks. Well worth the trip. Our server Jelena (pronounced Yelena), was also a warm hearted breath of fresh air. It felt like we where repeat customers although it was our 1st time. They have an extensive drink menu full of delicious beverages.  Picked the tiki drink and the orange Moscow Mule. Both were very nice. Since we were not that hungry but wanted to nibble on a few things, we tried the gambas al ajillo (grilled shrimp in garlic oil). It did not disappoint.  When I ordered the bacon slab, I saw that it came with Brussels sprouts,  my favorite vegetable these days. What a treat that was. The flavor came out so nicely. I almost want to order more of it. It is really good. Although we could not stay, but we did not want to leave because of Jelena and Chelsea. Bazar is very fortunate to have both there. Definitely want to return here again! I felt bad for Jelena. She was handling multiple tables and she did it with a smile and expediency. She is a great server for Bazar!!

Talk about overpriced and not that good food. I came here for dinner(I know, what was I thinking) but the person I came with wanted to eat here. Had to wait about 20-30 mins for a table at 6:30pm on a Saturday night. The service here is good but everything is just ok. My friend got the Mac and cheese with bacon, and honestly it was nothing special but cost about $20. It comes with a marinara sauce that literally tastes like the lunchables pizza sauce. I had the BALT sandwich which is bacon, lettuce, avocado and lettuce sandwich. Barely any lettuce and bacon is hard and tasteless. The only highlight was the avocado. The waffle fries are good but nothing extraordinary. I didn't have an appetite for dessert but probably should've only come here to eat the chocolate fondue. I wouldn't come back here to eat food but maybe dessert. I don't know, probably not though.

Valentine's Day dinner I looked for a great Italian restaurant. I found Paesano on a search based on ratings. I love the atmosphere and authenticity of being a true Italian restaurant. I order the baked ziti with chicken and my wife order cheese ravioli. The baked ziti  was delicious to the point you want more. I also try the ravioli taste like homemade ravioli. The garlic bread is a must try as an appetizer or part of the main entree. The place was super packed that day, but the waiters found us a comfortable table. I highly recommend paesano if you like authentic Italian food.

Packed so Yelp reservation is recommended. They called fast so I got missed once when I was late. We ordered seven dishes plus a kiwi cocktail which was just meh. We liked the chicken karaage, oden Small was plenty for us YUM, gomae blanch spinach was excellent, the yakitori sampler was meh with the pork belly best, salmon aburi nigiri was meh but the sushi mew roll reminded us of Vancouver salmon aburi but son don't like it. The highlight was the creamy kimchee udon noodles!! Nice server.

Black Tap is a lot of fun.  The atmosphere is great (they were playing the Beastie Boys!).  Their burgers a perfect to start your night in Soho. And they're freakshakes....well, come hungry because you have to get one!  These things are absolutely insane.

Needed a spot before a show and Patzeria did the trick, though it took a while to get our food after we ordered and everything arrived at the same time, which was kind of annoying. The Caesar salad, portobello ravioli (believe that was a special) and eggplant parmesan were all great, and more than enough for three people. The parm came with penne, which was awesome. Carrot cake for dessert was decent. I'd say Patzeria is a solid 3.5; would have been a 4 except for the slow service.

The wait for this restaurant was way longer than they promised. The hostess said that we would only wait for fourty minutes, but we ended up having to wait for twice that amount of time. It was around 8:20 PM around that time. Please don't make any false promises. When we were finally seated, they placed us in a tiny booth, that could barely fit five people. The servers were extremely rude to us, and it was so weird that they hurried us out after we finished even though the group before us stayed for two hours. The food was outstanding though, but the service completely ruined the experience. We ordered so much food that melted right in our mouths. I can't say anything bad about the dishes themselves, they all blew my mind.

Delicious Spanish restaurant Some of the dishes reminded of my time in Spain Great friendly staff   Pretty decor Very savory dishes The dishes are great to share as tapas Clean and spacious My favorite dishes of the day were the mixed croquetas and the Shishito peppers I do definitely recommend having the bacalao croquetas as well to make the mixed dish even more excellent. The red wine sangria was fresh and tasty not too strong and not watery. The dessert options were tasty as well. We had the dulce de leche churros and they were a WIN for sure. Everyone at our table raved about them. For 5 people the bill came to $140 which is affordable for Manhattan. I will definitely recommend and will be returning with my husband who is from Spain.

Your little greasy-unhealthy-localized yet yummy-quickly-friendly restaurant!I almost missed this place as the entrance was rather small. The environment wasn't pleasant as it smelt oily - but hey this is a shop for friend chicken and pork belly!Got a minced pork belly over rice with fried chicken. It wasn't authentic-not Taiwanese, but it was tasty! The pork belly wasn't too fatty which I like, and the additional fried chicken (+2) wasn't too salty nor saucy.The rice bowl also comes with some cabbage and pickled vegetables. A little overcooked but the taste was good.The portion was large and the service fast & friendly. No complaint with the expectations of a little fast-food-like place!

I recently visited this local gem and was thoroughly impressed by their Okra Frankie. The spicy aftertaste elevated the dish, giving it a delightful kick that lingered pleasantly on the palate. Additionally, the wrap was a highlight in itself, crafted from a unique blend of five different grains, which added a fantastic depth of flavor and texture. Alongside this, the Chickpea Tempura Cauliflower was a hit – crispy, flavorful, and very satisfying. Without a doubt, I'm eager to return and explore more of their menu!

You can never go wrong with Los Tacos no.1! Authentic tacos, made at the speed of light. I had steak tacos (carne asada) & their horchata is very good as well. If theres a long line, dont worry, it'll go by fast

This is a very small place if you are looking for a table for 5 + you would need to split up. I was intrigued by the giant soup dumpling and the pink coloured dumpling that's what caught my interest to try this place out. The dough is a bit too thick for my liking overall it was a decent place but I think I would not go back as this was more a one time experience for me.

Title: A Gem in Murray Hill - Classic Dining Experience

I had a delightful experience at this classic restaurant tucked away in Murray Hill. The service was impeccable, attentive without being intrusive. As for the meal, the lobster and shrimp linguine was simply excellent – a dish that truly stood out for its flavors and quality. It's surprising that I hadn't discovered this place sooner, especially given the scarcity of exceptional dining options in the area. This timeless restaurant is now firmly on my list of favorites.

Tucked away on a quieter side street between 8th and 9th Avenues, near the bustling theater district, Brazen Tavern offers a tranquil respite with its warm ambience and notably attentive service, thanks to an impeccable Irish waitress whose charm added to the experience.

Unsure about the wine selection at a pub, we were pleasantly surprised when offered a taste of their Rose before committing, which turned out to be a delectable choice.

For the meal, I opted for the Tavern Salad, a reasonably priced base at $10, which became quite the fulfilling dish with the addition of grilled chicken for an extra $7. Though adding protein to other salads may push the price to $25, the generous portions justify the cost.

My friend's veggie burger, served on a Kaiser bun with a side salad swapped for fries, received high praise and left her completely satisfied.

Priced on par with nearby pubs, with mains averaging around $23, Brazen Tavern stands out for its satisfying food and inviting atmosphere. Whether pre or post-theatre, or just in search of a cozy dining spot, this tavern is well worth a return visit.

Title: A Slice of Aussie Brunch Perfection!

I recently indulged in a delightful breakfast/brunch experience at a charming Australian cafe that had been on my radar for quite some time. On a serene Wednesday morning, the ease of finding a table set the tone for a splendid visit. The service was impeccable from the get-go, with a friendly and attentive waiter making sure my dining experience was seamless.

The cafe's cozy interior, with just a handful of tables and additional bar-style seating, created an inviting atmosphere. I kicked things off with a soy flat white, which arrived promptly—smooth and just right. However, the real star of the show was the hotcake I ordered as my main dish. Despite the slight wait for its arrival, every moment was justified once I took the first bite. This pancake was the epitome of breakfast bliss—impossibly fluffy, perfectly thick, and utterly scrumptious. Drizzled with maple syrup, adorned with a generous dollop of mascarpone, and sprinkled with pistachios and berries (though I'd have loved a few more), it left me longing for the recipe.

While there's word on the street about their amazing burgers, it will require a hefty dose of self-persuasion to not cave into the pancake temptation on future visits. If you're on the lookout for an exceptional brunch spot, this little cafe is a gem worth visiting. I'm enthusiastically recommending it and, without a doubt, will be back for those delectable hotcakes.

Title: A Unique Catch-Your-Own Dining Adventure at Zauo

If you're seeking an ordinary dining experience, Zauo isn't the place for you. But for those looking to merge dinner with an aquatic adventure, this is your next stop. Be warned though, it's not for the faint of wallet or heart. Zauo offers a dining experience like no other, asking patrons to literally fish for their meal. It's a unique concept that melds entertainment with dining, but this comes with a price tag that may raise eyebrows.

Despite the potential sticker shock, the experience is well worth it for an extraordinary evening. The restaurant is equipped to handle large groups—just be sure to snag a reservation on the Resy app, especially if you're planning to dine after 6:30 pm.

Upon arrival, staff take great pains to ensure hygiene and fun don't clash. Armed with a poncho, glove, and a lanyard bearing your table number, you're ready to embark on your fishing quest. If luck and skill don't seem to favor you, nets are available, though whether or not that's a culinary cop-out is up for you to decide.

The fish selection is varied between the two floors, ranging from salmon trout to rockfish. Fishing can either be a brisk activity or stretch into a longer endeavor, depending on your prowess with a rod (or net). A successful catch is celebrated with drumming that, while festive, might become a repetitive tune for some.

Once caught, the cooking preparation is in your hands, with four methods available. Our 5 lb salmon trout was split into three delicious styles—soy sauce, fried tempura, and grilled—with the soy sauce preparation taking the top spot. Side note: Additional costs apply for rice and the intriguing fish head soup, which our group skipped.

Beyond the fishing, the menu offers a variety of a la carte dishes; from delicately fried octopus to a savory black cod, all the food screamed freshness. Standouts included the umibozu salad, complete with shell-cracking action, and a particularly fresh uni tempura that may prove too 'oceanic' for some palates.

The setting is accommodating for spectators, with friends able to view the fishing action from a mezzanine level. Cleanliness isn't overlooked either, as we found the restrooms neat and well-maintained.

In conclusion, Zauo offers a memorable and interactive dining experience. It's an ideal spot for a special occasion, especially

Title: A Hearty Japanese Feast at Donburiya

As a fan of Japanese comfort food, dining at Donburiya was a fulfilling experience. Despite the bustling neighborhood, the price point pleasantly stands out, not least because it's a non-tipping establishment. On a brisk Saturday evening, the restaurant welcomed us promptly for an early dinner.

Navigating the menu proved somewhat challenging due to its cluttered layout, comprising both printed items and a handwritten list of specials. This minor hiccup was quickly forgotten as the aroma of our grilled skirt steak appetizer filled the air, drawing envy from neighboring diners who couldn't resist ordering it themselves. The glaze and the accompanying garlic sauce were pure culinary bliss.

It's almost obligatory to sample the donburi at a place bearing its namesake. The Oyako don was a comforting blend of sweetness and savor, with its succulent chicken, tender egg, and vegetables over rice. The Sukiyaki don, enjoyed by the beef aficionados of my group, was equally satisfying with its fried egg garnish providing a perfect counterpart to the simmered meat.

While the dessert failed to leave a lasting impression, the overall meal was a delightful journey through the essence of Japanese home cooking. The minor service misstep of our entrees arriving before the appetizer was easily overlooked given the quality and heartiness of our meal. Donburiya has certainly earned a repeat visit on my calendar.

I only came here because pig beach was closed on Columbus Day, and it was such a horrible choice. Idk how this place is number 1 on yelp. That was probably the only time yelp disappointed me. Lol. But seriously, this bbq was just blah. It wasn't anything special. It was expensive as ever! The portion sizes are meh, and i don't see how people enjoyed it. It was empty for a holiday, and now i know why. I had a single serving of pulled pork, which you can have the meat or they give you bread and say it's a sandwich. The bread is a regular hamburger roll. It came with a side of slaw. I chose the vinegar slaw, and it was just okay. My friend got a chipotle style bowl. (Weird right) it came with white rice, he chose burnt ends, which didn't look appetizing at all. They scoopedIt out of the warmer. (It looked gross) they also allow you to add two of their sides to the bowl. He chose broccoli salad and something else i don't recall. He said it was okay, but it definitely wasn't bbq. Also, they only have a Choice of two sauces, that the employee puts on for you. What! How is this a bbq place? If you've ever been to pig beach, to come here after is like going to McDonald's after chick fil a.. why? Don't. I do not recommend this place to anyone for bbq. You want good bbq, go to Brooklyn and go to pig beach! That slaw they had changed my life lol. Pig beach ladies and gentlemen!

Title: Generous Portions and Fresh Flavor at [Restaurant Name]

I had a delightful experience at [Restaurant Name] where the portion sizes left no room for hunger. Opting for a half size of the crispy boneless chicken with soy garlic sauce proved to be ample for both myself and a friend, marking it as an excellent spot for a hearty early dinner or a late afternoon treat.

The ordering process was a breeze, complemented by a handy buzzer system that allowed us to relax at our table instead of waiting by the register. While there was a slight wait for our food, it was clear that it was because each dish was made fresh to order, which is always a plus in my book.

When the chicken arrived, it was the epitome of perfection in terms of texture—with spot-on crispiness and tenderness that made each bite a joy. While the soy garlic sauce leaned towards the sweeter side, mimicking more of a honey garlic flavor, it was still incredibly tasty and made for some seriously good fried chicken. 

In summary, [Restaurant Name] is a must-visit for those who appreciate generous servings and freshly cooked meals. Just be prepared for a bit of a wait - it's worth it!

My friend wanted to come here for their truffle fries. She frequents often just for the fries and their coconut mojitos. Tried both and was underwhelmed. I didn't think it was amazing as she described. Had the salmon entree and it was good but it's not something I would rave about. It was mediocre food for the price you are paying for the location and ambiance.Service was great up until we asked for the check. It was hard to get the attention of the bartender. He was making drinks, I get it. Asked a waiter if we can get our check and was told we needed to ask the bartender. Tried to get the bartenders attention again. Unsuccessful. Ask some other guy at the bar and thought he was getting it for us but he was just waiting for the bartender to print our check who was busy making drinks. Ask the guy again if we will be getting our check and we need to catch the train. He mocked us and said "can you print the check? They need to catch the 5 train" he had heard us talking about the lines nearby. Ended up missing my Metro North Train (not the 5 train) by 2 minutes. Fine, I missed my train and caught the next one but to mock a customer? Let's give this guy a raise!

Title: A Falafel Fiesta at Nish Nush

As a falafel enthusiast, my cravings were satisfied beyond expectations at Nish Nush. Their Falafel Trio Platter is a delectable journey through classic, roasted pepper, and spinach and mushroom falafels. The roasted pepper variant stood out, tantalizing my taste buds with its subtle heat and a pleasantly firm texture.

The platter also served as a salad sampler which I found delightful for a taste of everything. Kudos for offering both white and whole wheat pita options, catering to the health-conscious diner in me. And let's not forget the ample serving of creamy hummus, the perfect companion for the falafel and pita.

Nish Nush nailed it with variety, flavor, and healthful consideration. It's a must-visit for Mediterranean cuisine aficionados.

Title: A Georgian Culinary Gem in NYC

If you're craving an adventure into new cuisines, look no further! I recently discovered an outstanding Georgian restaurant, thanks to my in-the-know NYC friends. As a first-time Georgian food taster, I was blown away by the savory flavors that greeted me.

Starting with the Adjaruli, a must-try cheese bread appetizer, which is a delightful mix of cheesy goodness that prepares your palate for more. Then the main dish, Chanakhi pork, a masterfully seasoned dish that left my taste buds dancing. The flavor profile was unique and memorable; I can't recommend it enough.

The cozy atmosphere adds to the experience, though it's worth noting that you should book in advance as it can get pretty busy, even on weekday evenings. And for those celebrating a birthday, they have a special surprise that adds to the festive feel.

I'm already planning my next visit to get another taste of that delectable Adjaruli – maybe even one all to myself! Trust me, this place is a culinary treasure.

Title: Cozy Vibes and Tasty Eats at Local Casual Hangout

If you're on the lookout for a laid-back spot for drinks with friends, this place hits the mark. The ambiance exudes comfort with its varied seating options; choose from the bar, tables, or sink into one of their plush booths. Service shines here, with a friendly and attentive team ready to enhance your experience.

Delving into the menu, "Sweet Meat" caught our attention, but it may catch some by surprise. The set includes succulently smoked wings, pulled pork shavings, and another meat that might not be everyone's first pick. While the description might benefit from more detail, the wings were a definite hit.

The Mediterranean plate was a decent offering, though the hummus had a thicker, pastier consistency than preferred. However, the Truffle French fries were a runaway success, not to be missed.

Drink-wise, the Mezcal old fashioned deserves a special mention for its robust flavor.

In summary, this spot is a solid recommendation for those seeking a relaxed atmosphere with friends, good casual fare, and a standout selection of beer and mixed drinks.

Title: Decent Brunch, But Not Exceptional

My experience at this Yelp-discovered spot for a Sunday brunch with my fiancé and dad was fairly average, despite its 4-star rating. Making a reservation turned out to be unnecessary as the place was virtually empty during prime brunch hours, which was surprising. We sampled a range of dishes - chicken liver pâté, deviled eggs, a Mediterranean tuna salad, a bacon egg & cheese sandwich, and a roast beef panini. Each dish was adequate but lacked a memorable punch of flavor that would bring us back for the food alone.

However, the Bees Knees cocktail I had was delightful, and it could tempt me back for a casual drink in the future. In sum, while the meal didn’t quite live up to expectations, the bar might warrant a second glance.

I came here tonight, Feb 8, 2020 after the French Animation Festival and upon entering people were leaving they exclaimed the food is amazing! I went in and asked the hostess if there's any bar space for a couple of drinks. She said of course. The chef was standing next to her conveniently for me,... I had purchased a salad prior to thinking I'd have some time between showings and Q&A's, but I sadly did not.... And I asked if I could eat my outside food at his bar. He was totally cool with it given the circumstances. Thank you soooo much! I've just ordered a Chianti and looked over the menu. I'll definitely be back. I want to try your steak bibimbap! The exterior is a gorgeous entry. Inside is most delightful. Loving the beats! Loud but not obnoxious. It's like when you're on a long drive and all of your favorite edm songs pop up!! Definitely am dancing in my chair right now. The bartender is also awesome. I was lucky to get Tavio. He's super helpful when you're uncertain of what you want to drink but have a general idea of what you like. And he's friendly too if you want to chat. It's a beyond full bar if you want anything classier than wine. Place is spotless and clean. I'm getting lots of good vibes. Lots of tables too. A split level space. Top has additional seating. Bottom, has the kitchen and there's a third floor with bay windows looking at the street. Love the interior design too. Happy eats! I'll be back!

My mom and I recently visited this charming restaurant for breakfast and were immediately taken with the delightful ambience. I indulged in a porchetta panini that was exceptionally moist and tender, bursting with flavor in every bite. Meanwhile, my mom savored the cotechino, with its standout biscuit that allowed the pecorino cheese to shine through. Both dishes left us entirely satisfied, not a crumb left behind. On a spontaneous note, we added a croissant to our order and were rewarded with its superbly buttery, flaky texture. I highly recommend arriving early to experience their breakfast offerings. This spot truly knows how to start the day right!

I came in with super high expectations based on reviews and online recommendations but left disappointed. Okay, maybe disappointed only because I had high expectations but disappointment is disappointment. I came say what it is exactly other than nothing really stood out to me in my bowl of ramen. I ordered the spicy butter miso and a side of karaage. There was a lot of green onions which I didn't care for too much. I found the broth to be thicker than my liking. I wouldn't say it was bad. If a friend made plans to come here I wouldn't object, but I wouldn't be excited either... but maybe a second trip will change my mind, who knows.

The ice cream is better than the milkshakes. I've tried the cookies and cream milkshake in addition to the boozy milkshake. The boozy milkshake is too sugary. The regular milkshake is solid. And the ice cream is just right.I had to dock a point off because the service is never great. You can order ice cream at the counter closer to the ice cream tubs, but sometimes there aren't any employees attending to that area so you have to stand in the longer line anyway

Oh my god my meal at Balvanera was speechless. Came here on a Friday night at 6pm, with a reservation for our company's holiday party. We had ~20 people in our party, so we got a giant table in the middle of the restaurant. We ordered a whole bunch of tapas and meats to share family style, including fried chicken, skirt steak, rib eye, pesto pasta, mushroom tapas, pulpo octopus, beef empanadas, burrata, sea bass, papas fritas (fries), steak tartare, salmon crudo etc. Boy were we in for an unforgettable feast! Also lets not forget the amount of wine we ordered. AMBIANCE:Great vibes, love the latin inspired decor, while it felt like home yet not too pretentious. Atmosphere was dimly lit. Great place to bring friends or date. PROS:Highlights were the meat. Those were prepared exquisitely. I loved the riby eye as it was really fatty, so full of flavor, and tender. The char on top of the steak added a great crunchy texture to the meat. A close second was the skirt steak, and that was really tender as well. The chimichurri that it came paired really well with the steak, but also paired really well with the complimentary bread that we got - what a pleasant surprise! Steaks were seasoned well and presented well. Pairs really well with either the Argentinian Pinot Noir or Cabernet, it really cuts down on the fattiness of the beef really well. The beef was also paired with the potato puree, and those were some of the smoothest potatoes I've had!As for tapas: beef empanadas were some of the best I've had. The octopus was grilled to a perfect tenderness, and paired well with the sauce and puree that it came. It had a great smokey flavor from the grill which gave some parts of it a good crunchy char taste to it. Steak tartare was also some of the best tartare Ive had in a while. I loved the balance of acidity in the dish, and the runny egg on top added more fun to the dish. Salmon crudo was fantastic as you can taste the fish was really fresh and the jalapeno and citrus really cuts down on the fattiness of the fish. The papas fritas were good and crispy too.I didn't get the chance to try the burrata or the seabass, but from my table I heard there were rave reviews as we had a cheese and seafood connoisseur on our table! Service was top notch as the servers were really attentive to our table and made sure we were well fed and our needs taken care of. Thank you! OVERALL:Fantastic experience at Balvanera, great steak and excellent service would make this meal one to remember!
The oysters were so fresh and tasty! The Mac & cheese was also delish! I really like how their bar is set up and thought the layout was funky in a good way

Title: Fresh Flavors with a Side of Disappointment at Ocean Dragon

Last week, after my colleagues raved about it, I decided to try Ocean Dragon's delivery service for dinner. Choosing the General Tso's Chicken and fried rice, I eagerly anticipated the meal. To my delight, the chicken was exceptionally fresh, arguably the best General Tso's I've had from any Chinese restaurant—no dubious cuts of meat here. The fried rice matched the chicken's standard, delivering that perfect balance of flavor and texture.

Unfortunately, the experience wasn't flawless. The egg roll was a letdown; it was bland and forgettable. Also, while the portions won't leave you famished, they lean towards the smaller side. However, for Manhattan, the pricing felt appropriate.

Despite the egg roll's misstep, Ocean Dragon has won me over. I'm already planning my next order.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at Mediterranean Pure Foods

I stopped by Mediterranean Pure Foods for my MealPal lunch and was quite pleased with the experience. The Spicy Lamb Salad caught my eye, and it did not disappoint, except for the missing hummus. This place has a streamlined setup; you simply head to the back and order from an extensive menu.

The side of rice was a delightful surprise, tasting like it was sweetened or perhaps even coconut-infused, which I found moist and delicious. The lamb was good, though it seemed to have been prepared a bit before my 12:45 pm pickup. However, the kofta was a standout, and the freshness of the other salad components was undeniable.

Would I return? Absolutely! Both for MealPal options and to explore more of their offerings.

Title: Reliable Delivery and Comforting Cuisine from 12 Chairs

In the wake of challenging times, 12 Chairs has truly stepped up its game with an impressive delivery service. Despite living a good 4 miles away, my experience was one of prompt service and food that arrived in impeccable condition thanks to their thoughtful packaging.

The culinary journey started with their sweet potato fries, which were nothing short of delightful, and an arugula salad that was fresh and flavorful. My Israeli husband, a tough critic when it comes to authenticity, was thoroughly impressed with the stuffed cabbage, going as far as to describe it as 'amazing.'

Unfortunately, the shakshuka didn't hit the right notes for me; the sauce simply did not align with my palate, which isn't much of a surprise as tomato-based dishes at 12 Chairs generally don't. That said, the overall quality and consistency of their offerings are commendable.

12 Chairs stands out as a dependable choice for those seeking quality meals delivered to their doorstep. Their direct ordering system adds a personal touch that is much appreciated. Without a doubt, we'll be placing another order in the near future.

New York City truly is blessed with a plethora of neighborhood Italian trattorias that shine outside the famed quarters of Little Italy. One such gem is this establishment, which I recently had the pleasure of dining at for lunch. The experience started with a bang, as my friend and I indulged in a house special Octopus Caprese, not listed on the lunch menu but absolutely worth inquiring about. The dish arrived, stunning and ample, commanding the attention of nearby diners as we delighted in its perfectly grilled tentacles, sumptuous burrata, and vibrant cherry tomatoes.

As if the octopus wasn't enough to satisfy our cravings, the Fried Calamari followed suit in excellence, setting a high standard for what an appetizer can be. However, it was the lunch deal that left me utterly impressed: a $10 Spaghetti alle Vongole entree that rivaled any dinner portion. The clams were plentiful, the pasta was perfectly al dente, and the sauce balanced lightness with depth of flavor beautifully. My friend's choice, the Orecchiette Gamberi Burrata, while rich was equally satisfying but its richness does command moderation.

We crowned our meal with a shared Affogato, a simple yet divine dessert that was the perfect endnote to our hearty lunch. This trattoria is a standout for its quality and value among the many Italian dining options in the city.

The main attraction in NoLita, Prince Street Pizza serves Sicilian-style pies. You can't miss this tiny shop because a long queue of hungry patrons is always out the door. While Prince Street Pizza offers a few different types of pizza, the most popular is undoubtedly the pepperoni.
