The crust, tomato sauce, cheese, and meat amount to a delicious pie that will have you clamoring for more. The best part is the shop is not stingy with its thicker-sliced pepperoni. For those seeking something other than a traditional New York slice, Prince Street Pizza will not disappoint.

We are hoping for some restaurants to be open for christmas dinner and this place was one of them.  And a random person told us this is a great place so we went in with confidence.  First they asked us if we had a reservation....well we should have made a reservation on open table.  Yet they managed us into a table.  The service was really slow for sure, as they were probably understaffed.  But they were personable.  The server recommended up the chips and salsa for the table and Arroz con Camarones for me.  Arroz con camarones was bit too salty and shrimp was overcooked with a lot of rice. Guacamole chips and queso was just yummy. Appetizer taco and quesadilla were kiddie size. The meal was not bad but the service and the price could have been better.

I recently dined at a local eatery specializing in what can best be described as perfectly mediocre "Chinese" cuisine. The service was notably swift, and the portions were generous, which could be considered a plus. I opted for the shrimp and noodles, which left me underwhelmed; the flavors were rather forgettable. The highlight, surprisingly, was the occasional charred onion that added a touch of smokiness to the otherwise soggy low mein. Overall, it was an unremarkable experience where the quantity slightly outshone the quality.

Came here for a private event and I was completely blown away!!! TabeTomo is now my new favorite Japanese restaurant! The highlight of our meal was definitely the Chashu Tsukumen, which was the best tsukumen I ever had! The 60-hour pork broth was extremely rich, flavorful, and full of delicious toppings (tender chashu pork, perfectly cooked egg, and a good variety of veggies). The rest of our meal was also amazing, and we finished the night off with delicious hoji-cha creme brulee. Service was also spectacular. We got to chat a bit with the owner, Wendy, who is an absolute gem of a lady! She was very welcoming and was full of smiles all night. She constantly checked up on us to make sure we were enjoying our meal :)Can't wait to return with my family and friends next time! I already miss it!

Went to celebrate a friend's birthday on a Wednesday and hit the happy hour jackpot with exceptional $9 drinks. The highlight was the fresh, meaty oysters, which didn't disappoint. Our indulgence continued with a standout side that stole the show – the lobster Mac and cheese, hearty enough to pass as an entrée and easily one of the best renditions I've savored recently. Our drink of choice, the "Hacienda," was a refreshing blend of grapefruit, basil, lime, and tequila, perfectly balanced without being overly sweet. I'd definitely recommend this spot for a post-work happy hour to unwind with friends.

3.5 stars for food and decor but rounding up to 4 for the excellent service. Tick Tock Diner is attached to the New Yorker Hotel. It has a very convenient midtown location. Most NYC diners are super small but this one is large and spacious. The diner also has a full bar. Food was as expected from a diner. Relatively cheap, good and plentiful. Service was excellent. Don't hesitate to go if you're in the area.

I recently dined at a wonderfully authentic spot where the experience began the moment we were seated, with immediate service and a delightful bread with tomato flan for dipping. The service throughout our meal was impeccable; the staff was both professional and attentive.

The calamari was the star starter, presented beautifully over a bed of tomatoes with a fresh lemon squeeze, evoking a true European essence in both presentation and taste. For the main course, I savored the Fusilli al pesto e ricotta and was impressed by its flavor. My co-worker enjoyed a pasta dish resembling spaghetti, which also received high praises.

I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit, with the lamb already on my must-try list. This place is a definite recommendation for anyone longing for a taste of genuine cuisine coupled with stellar service.

Atmosphere is so nice. I was not expecting it to be so fancy. So so good. Pricy but worth it. I would not order the bone marrow again but would order everything else - soup dumplings, truffle meatballs, and lobster Mac. We did not have a wait. We (2 of us) went at 7 and went to sit at the bar upstairs.

Title: A Gem of a Friday Feast at Pig Heaven

My recent dining experience at Pig Heaven was nothing short of delightful. Conveniently located a short stroll from the 6 train, with pocket-friendly street parking available, the restaurant is welcoming from the outset. Upon early arrival, I was met with warm smiles, particularly from Lisa, the GM, whose menu expertise shined through.

Despite the change in management, the familiar staff continues to preserve the restaurant's longstanding reputation. The chicken sproong—an appetizing blend of spicy chicken and crisp lettuce—was a hit starter. It’s a must-try, much like the acclaimed BBQ ribs that lived up to their fame.

Our service was prompt yet unhurried, striking the perfect balance for a relaxed meal. We ventured to try the fish hot pot, a stellar new addition to the menu. Tailored to a milder spice level upon request, it was served with perfectly cooked rice and was an absolute delight.

The evening was complemented by a reasonably priced bottle of rosé while the attentive staff ensured an ever-full glass of water. The bustling ambience was inclusive, appealing to diners of all ages and backgrounds.

I wholeheartedly recommend Pig Heaven for a memorable dining experience and eagerly anticipate my next visit.

After much anticipation, I recently visited this East Village steakhouse, touted as a local gem. The ambiance certainly impresses, offering an escape straight into an Argentinean retreat. The steaks, while expertly cooked to the perfect temperature, seemed to lack a certain depth of flavor, leaving me reaching for the chimichurri to add zest—which might be by design but isn't quite to my preference. I found the vegetable appetizers somewhat disjointed in presentation, with ingredients that felt randomly assembled on the plate. Overall, it was a decent experience, though not one that stole my heart. The jury's still out on a return visit, as the fare was satisfactory, but didn't ignite a culinary spark for me.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise for an Impromptu Dinner

I recently visited this restaurant on a bustling Saturday evening without a reservation and was delighted that my friends and I were seated promptly. The highlight of my meal was the chicken parm sandwich; a near-perfect rendition of a classic transformed into a sandwich while retaining that essential crunchiness. A tad more sauce could launch it to perfection, though I appreciate the balance to avoid sogginess.

Although the burger didn't quite reach the heights of the Emmy burger from their West Village spot, it stood its own ground, offering up a juicy, flavorful experience without the dreaded grease overload. The loaded fries option, from the two available, was a nice complement to the meal, but the waffle fries arguably could shine solo.

The Sicilian pizza met expectations with its airy, fluffy dough, generously adorned with thick slices of burrata and fresh basil. While enjoyable, a slightly hotter serving temperature would have heightened the experience.

All in all, it's a spot worth revisiting for a relaxed meal, especially when you're looking to dine without the din during peak hours.

I want to give 3.5 stars but I will round up because the congee and the milk tea are the bomb! It's authentic Cantonese breakfast food. We arrived around 11:30am on a Saturday and waited in line for 30-35 minutes. I was surprised that the rice noodle was not the best. We got the pork liver noodles and the beef, shrimp, and chives noodles. They were quite generous with the stuffings and the noodle plates were decently large. The flavoring was good. However, I was a bit disappointed that the noodles were a bit "runny" and "soggy". They added way too much water to their rice flour. The filling was falling out of the thin and goopey noodles, which was hard to pick up with chopsticks. You had to use spoons! I expected the noodles to be much better since this is a noodle roll specialty shop. Fortunately, the meal was saved by the congee and Hong Kong Style milk tea. If you're a fan of seafood, get the Lai Wan congee! It had a generous amount fish and octopus and it was less than $6! It was quite a big bowl and I suggest sharing with another person. It was nice for a cold day. We also ordered some nice crispy fish skins to add to our congee. The milk tea was strong and milky and a good substitute for coffee. It was unsweetened so you can adjust to your liking.Overall it was a pleasant brunch meal and we were stuffed! I will probably come back on a week day when there's less people.

Title: A Hearty Brunch at Maison Pickle

Maison Pickle truly satisfies the craving for southern comfort food with a diverse and tempting menu. Sharing several dishes allowed for a generous tasting experience. The standout was indisputably the fried chicken paired with French toast—a generous serving that could easily satisfy two patrons (refer to uploaded photos for the colossal portion size). Both items were impeccably prepared, offering a delightful blend of sweet and savory.

While the beef French dip was competent, it didn't quite reach the heights of the chicken and French toast. The pork cassoulet, with its savory white beans, was tasty, though the pork itself was notably scarce within the dish. 

The service was attentive and efficient, though it's worth noting that the ambiance during weekend brunch is exceedingly lively, bordering on boisterous. It's a popular spot, so reservations are a must to avoid a lengthy wait. Overall, while not every dish hit the mark, the high points make Maison Pickle a worthwhile destination for those seeking a substantial and flavorsome meal.
Happy Hour Bar Menú 4-6pm everyday !  Charming bar to meet friends after work or that special someone.

I came here for the first time for dinner and ordered the spicy cumin lamb that yelp reviewers raved about. It came in a paper dish filled with noodles and meat that looked quite appetizing. With the first bite, the taste that stood out the most was the strong cumin flavor, then the chili pepper and lamb. The noodles were in-between soft and chewy, and well-seasoned. It would be better if the noodles were thicker to allow more of the texture to show. The lamb was a bit tough to chew, but taste-wise it fits well with the season. There is a good kick to it (I ordered regular spiciness).It was good but I found myself getting tired near the end. This is a heavy dish with lots of oil, and definitely not for someone looking for healthy diet.

Title: A Culinary Delight at Bergdorf Goodman's Top Floor Eatery

Stepping into the top floor restaurant at Bergdorf Goodman, you can expect a delightful dining experience that's illustrated perfectly by their appetizing fare. The duck dumplings, juicy and tantalizing, set the stage for an exciting meal. They certainly know how to whet the appetite.

Unfortunately, the cauliflower steak fell a bit short of expectations. Although the curry sauce was flavorful, the dish itself lacked imagination—something I felt could easily be replicated in my own kitchen. I'd opt for a different entrée on a future visit.

On the other hand, my friend's choice of Lobster Napoleon was the star of the evening—a creamy, rich dish that would make anyone envious.

Capping off the meal with a zesty lemon meringue paired with berry coulis was a stroke of genius. It was the perfect palate cleanser and combined with a pot of tea, it was the quintessential ending to our meal.

Be sure to book your reservations well in advance, particularly around the holidays, as this spot is in high demand. With its bright ambiance, scenic views of Central Park, and a buzz that's lively yet not overwhelming, it sets a lovely scene.

The service matched the quality of the food—attentive without intruding on intimate conversations.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a real treat and justifies its cost. It's an ideal venue for reconnecting with friends or enjoying a romantic date. With its high points far outweighing the slight misstep, I eagerly anticipate my next visit.

Being of partial Taiwanese descent, I am very pleased to see Taiwanese food being represented as it is in 886! Came with my Taiwanese girlfriend on a Saturday night at ~545pm, as she was vouching for the restaurant since her high school senior is the owner of 886 (Eric Sze, owner of the Tang as well). Line wasn't too packed and we were immediately seated. We ordered Taiwanese hotdog, Lou Ba Beng, Beef with Scallions, and the Fried Chicken sandwich. We also ordered one Taiwanese Lychee beer (SOO hard to find outside of Taiwan!). Total bill came about $72 dollars, inclusive of tax and tip - definitely more on the pricier side. AMBIANCE:Trendy, slighly upscale, and definitely caters to a younger crowd. Great date spot, music wasn't too loud (also kudos for playing Jay Chou, Hebe Tian, and Cindy Wang throughout the night)PROS:Taiwanese hotdog sandwich. Holy cow I did not have something that authentically delicious since I last went to Taipei and Taichung's night markets! The hotdog is served in a bun of gluttinous rice, the sausage is slightly sweet and charred (like what you get in Taiwan) and dusty with a healthy dose of what seemed to be like tempura flakes. OMG was that incredibly tasty and delicious! Lou ba beng was incredible too. The soft boil egg was creamy and decadent, the rice was very creamy, and they served it with a healthy portion of braised marinated pork. One of the best Lou ba beng i had in New York City so far! (Maybe Imperial Taiwanese Gourmet still rings true to me, but hey 886 cooks up a great interpretation of a Taiwanese classic). CONS:Fried Chicken sandwich was good - the chicken itself was very juicy, tender, and moist, but I felt the chicken itself lacked a lot of seasoning. Also, the red chilli powder made the sandwich very spicy. They should mention that on their menu that the sandwich was spicy! Beef with onions is usually a very classic dish with big slices of beef with green onion. 886's interpretation of this classic was very odd - its incredibly saucy (usually it isnt) and they shredded their beef which made it more like a 小椒肉丝 dish. OVERALL:Highly recommend! Lou Ba Beng and Taiwanese hotdogs definitely were the highlights of the night. Would love to give this spot a 5 star rating, but the two other dishes were slightly underwhelming. Would definitely want to come back again in the future!

Since 1905 Lombardi Pizza has been serving coal oven thin crust pizza. They are also known as the founders of what is known today as New York style American Pizza. I love older established restaurants and this is one I definitely love! I came here to meet with a friend and we had the Old School Margarita Pizza. It was a simple pizza but the taste was so spot-on what Old School pizza should taste like. The crust was thin, a bit crunchy and a bit chewy. The simple toppings of tomato sauce and mozzarella cheese were fresh and perfect! I have always loved thin crust pizza only because I do not care for the crust. This was the perfect pizza for me! This is definitely place I would love to return to and try out their different toppings. So delicious!!

The tequila oyster shooters are so tasty that my cousin, who had already had several before I arrived, insisted I stop everything I was doing and meet him there for several more.This is literally the sum total of my experience with Cull & Pistol, but I really can't hate. These oyster shooters are damn good, and the people serving them to us were quite nice. Or maybe I think everyone is nice after a bunch of shots of tequila and accompanying oysters. I can't really tell. But I'd come back for more.

Title: "Tableside: A Chic Italian Affair with Homestyle Flavors"

Tableside is not your average Italian eatery; it's a chic establishment where the ambiance is elevated with smooth house music, yet it surprisingly maintains a traditional menu. My litmus test for Italian dining is the meatball appetizer, and Tableside's 'Grandma's Beef Specialty' lived up to its name. The meatballs were a blend of excellent seasoning and texture, simmered in a flavorful gravy.

For my main course, I chose the 'Italian Mothers Love' lasagna, which was nearly flawless. The layers of meat, noodle, and cheese were in perfect harmony, although I found the sauce slightly thinner than my preference. Nonetheless, it was a well-executed dish.

The service was outstanding, punctuated by a visit from a passionate manager or owner, adding a personal touch to the dining experience. It's clear that Tableside prides itself on customer satisfaction, matching it with delectable fare. This combination ensured I left the restaurant with a lasting positive impression.

Title: A Cheesy Haven in NY: An Unforgettable Experience

My anticipation had been building to try the much-raved-about cheese-centric eatery that had flooded my Instagram feed. Upon my visit to New York, making this place our first dinner stop was non-negotiable. The necessity to reserve a table was quickly understood upon arrival; the cozy space was bursting at the seams with fellow diners, and we were almost elbow-to-elbow with our neighbors.

The aroma of cheese wafted through the air long before we reached the doors, setting the stage for the culinary experience that lay ahead. This certainly lived up to the hype - a testament to the foodie community's spot-on recommendation. Conveniently located just a few blocks from the subway stop, the restaurant's placement was another plus.

The pricing didn't leave us with buyer's remorse, which is often a rare pleasure in a city like NY. It was well justified by the quality of the meals and the spectacle of the melted cheese theatrically poured onto our plates. It was an Instagrammer's dream and a feast for the senses.

Our waitress, Marina, was the cherry on top with her warm welcome and attentive service. She expertly navigated us through the menu and our beverage options. As for our main course, my steak and my fiancé's burger were both lavished with a generous coating of raclette cheese - it was indulgent and exactly why we came.

Though the enticing dessert menu beckoned, our appetites were satisfyingly quenched by the cheese-laden entrées. Our experience was undeniably a 5/5 - one for the books and one we'd love to revisit, ideally with loved ones in tow to share in the cheesy extravagance.

Really busy small place by Chinatown, but definitely a great option for a authentic Cantonese without breaking your bank. Lunch on a Saturday was busy but got seated very quickly. It's famous for the casserole, dry/congee/dishes.  most of the dishes are under $10. Got the combo with yellow eel and two other choices from the menu, Portion are generous. You can choose anything from the cooked food menu for The mix roasted meat plate, got the roast duck, BBQ pork and perfectly crispy roasted pork.

Tucked away amidst the trendy facades of the West Village, this bustling eatery exudes an air of nostalgia and warmth, captivating a diverse crowd with its welcoming "come as you are" ambiance. It's a melting pot of New York life, where families, dates, and best friends all mingle, basking in the convivial atmosphere reminiscent of simpler times.

While the atmosphere undoubtedly earns a full five-star rating, the culinary offerings land a modest three stars. The standout dish is the garlic shrimp appetizer—its garlic sauce is truly exceptional and not to be missed. The chicken, sausage, and seafood paella, despite its generous portion, fails to impress on the same level, as does the disappointingly bland garlic soup. The octopus appetizer, although excessively buttery and salty, is a mediocre dish at best.

Despite some culinary misses, the sangria is a redeeming choice, and with the irresistible allure of the ambiance and tantalizing appetizers, this spot still beckons for a relaxed evening out. It's a place I'd happily revisit for the sangria, a round of appetizers, and the sheer comfort of its inviting vibe.

I've been wanting to try the signature Umami burgers with the U on their top buns for a long time now. The TravelZoo voucher I found online was my calling, and I'm so glad I was able to try it. I got to the location around 3:50pm and started ordering. Umami burger, cali burger, and truffle fries. It was a few minutes before happy hour starts at 4pm and the lady there was so nice, she asked if we wanted to wait a few minutes so we can get happy hour price on the fries. Of course we said yes! Then we ordered a full-sized thin fries to make up for the cheaper price of the truffle fries.The thin-cut fries were so good and perfectly crisp. However, the truffle fries were a little on the saltier side because of the cheese. The truffle flavor was strong, but not overpowering. I ordered the cali burger and it was actually pretty good. The patties were nice and juicy and the ingredients were fresh. However, the umami burger was just okay. I definitely think the cali burger should cost more than the umami burger.Also, when they ask you what house sauces you want, go for the jalapeno ranch! It's SO delicious. I also tried the roasted garlic aioli which was just okay, also a little salty for my taste. I have yet to try the other two sauces. I would've asked for one of each had I known that they were going to give me four sauces anyways. Oh well, it gives me a reason to come back!

I had a delightful experience at this restaurant, where the value for money truly impressed me. At roughly $4, the generous portions left me feeling satisfied without denting my wallet. The ample seating ensured a comfortable setting, and the cashier's friendliness enhanced the welcoming ambiance. The standout for me was the rice rolls; they boasted a remarkable texture that I particularly savored, with the shrimp-filled variety demonstrating exceptional quality. Highly recommend for a hearty meal on a budget.

Title: A Disheartening Dumpling Disappointment

I ventured into this dumpling joint with high hopes, sharing a name and a love for the stuffed delights. Alas, the experience was soured from the start by the unwelcoming staff on a Sunday evening. Their rudeness was palpable, dampening my enthusiasm for culinary inquiry.

Eager to at least savor the food, I ordered the chicken and basil steamed dumplings. Unfortunately, these too fell flat – quite literally. The dough was overly thick, dominating the scant filling, and flavor seemed an afterthought. Their policy of charging extra for condiments, like a mere dollop of hot chili oil, only added insult to injury.

In sum, this visit was a letdown, and it's with regret that I must say, I don't intend to return.

Title: A Delightful Engagement Treat at Uncle Boons

After being gifted with a gift card to Uncle Boons for our engagement, we finally managed to avoid the infamous two-hour wait by arriving just five minutes after opening on a Monday, with a reasonable 45-minute wait time. The establishment conveniently offers a text alert when your table is ready.

Starting with the pig ears, they were absolutely addictive—a highlight I might double order next time. While I'm not an octopus fan, my fiancé savored his dish with gusto. The standout of the night, as suggested by our attentive waiter, was the Khao Soi Kaa Kai. The chicken curry was flawless, ensuring a place on our order list for future visits.

Though the vibrant ambiance contributes to higher noise levels, making it less ideal for the hard-of-hearing, Uncle Boons is a gem for a spirited date night. We're already looking forward to our next visit.

Title: High Hopes Dashed by Lackluster Flavors

I headed to this highly praised pizza joint with high expectations, enticed by the unbelievable deal of three hefty slices for $20, especially for New York standards. My choices included the artichoke, lobster, and pepperoni.

The experience, unfortunately, fell flat. Both the artichoke and pepperoni slices failed to make an impression, their flavors as underwhelming as a whisper in a bustling city. The artichoke slice strangely reminded me of a butter-laden concoction, while the sauce on it and the lobster slice was oddly thick, akin to a soup awkwardly ladled onto the crust.

Admittedly, the lobster slice was a notch above its companions, but not nearly compelling enough to warrant a return visit on its own. When it comes to the classic pepperoni, this place is lost in a sea of competitors who easily outshine it.

In a city brimming with pizza offerings, this place misses the mark where it matters most: robust and memorable flavors. Disappointingly, I'll be taking my pizza cravings elsewhere.

Title: Mostly Delightful Birthday Dining

My friends and I recently visited this restaurant for a birthday celebration, and our overall experience was wonderful, save for an initial hiccup. Upon arrival, the hostess's unwelcoming and seemingly bothered demeanor was off-putting and not the best first impression. Fortunately, she was the only downside of our visit.

Our server, Neal, quickly turned our experience around with his friendly and warm nature. His recommendations were spot-on, leading us to enjoy a variety of dishes including succulent spare ribs, flavorful pork belly, tender short ribs, satisfying quesadillas, and an array of tacos—soft shell, shrimp, and pork belly—each dish as delicious as the last and served piping hot.

Further enhancing our evening, Orran Farmer, the assistant general manager, checked on our table with genuine hospitality and thoughtful conversation. His attention to detail made us feel valued and respected.

Despite the initial cold reception, the food's excellence and the team's overall warmth ensure that I'll be returning—hopefully when the hostess is off duty.

This place gets really busy during lunch and I am not sure they can handle the volume. I ordered online for pickup and waited 30 minutes after coming to the place (despite having a pickup tie). I also saw a massive line forming from other people coming to pick up and people who walked in to order. Some people were disgruntled. I am not sure if it was an off day or it is always like this. 0 stars for the timelinesses The food is pretty good- i got the fried chicken sandwich and it is really juciy/tender and pretty filling!!! I would prob recommend coming here during an off-time! Had to give it 4 stars because I would come back to get this.

Don't let the store front fool you. This place has the beat noodles in Hells Kitchen. OMG! I happen to stumble upon this place and I'm so happy I did! I'm sure everything of their menu is delicious, but I enjoyed their Duck Noodle Soup, Beef Nooodle Soup, Steamed Shrimp & Veggie Dumplings and Shrimp Fried Rice. Their ingredients are fresh and you can taste it. The noodle soup is a large portion so be ready to be stuffed! This is a small spot so not good for large parties, but perfect for lunch or a quick meal. I will definitely keep coming back here for more.

I came here on a Tuesday evening around 6:30pm. Our full party wasn't here yet, but there wasn't a wait. We were able to go in right away, but we were squeezed in the corner near the kitchen for 3 people, that should really be for 2 people. It's a pretty small space so it can get packed during busy hours. By the time we left, there were several parties waiting for a table. For food, I got the pad see ewe and tasted the green curry as well. I'd say noticed that both were dishes were on the sweeter side than I expected. The green curry had a slight spicy kick at the end that made it more preferable for me. For the noodles, I didn't particularly enjoy the strong smoky taste it had. But overall, it was an okay meal, but wouldn't necessarily make it my go to for Thai food. P.S. There's a 10% off if you pay with cash.

Title: A Culinary Delight with a Side of Comfort

My recent visit to this bustling eatery on a Friday evening was met with a pleasant surprise—only a 10-minute wait for a table without reservations! The experience kicked off with refreshingly fruity concoctions; the pomegranate soju and a lychee berry cocktail stood true to their menu descriptions, allowing us to savor each ingredient.

The complimentary starters were a delightful touch, with standouts like a corn pancake that was simply divine, along with tasty bites of pumpkin mash and kimchi. For anyone perusing the menu, I highly recommend the seafood pancake - a dish that truly sets itself apart in both flavor and craftsmanship; it’s a must-try even for those less inclined towards seafood.

The spicy gochujang chicken was a notable dish, filled with aromatic spices rather than mind-numbing heat, and served with the perfect complement of sticky rice and rice cakes. Juicy chicken combined with comforting flavors made each bite a pleasure.

We also indulged in the dumpling hot pot, which came loaded with scrumptious homemade dumplings, a variety of veggies, and squid in a light yet mildly spicy broth. A word of advice—don't miss out on those dumplings.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit for another round of impeccable dishes that effortlessly blend taste with comfort.

I recently visited a hidden gem of a restaurant tucked away in an alley, and the intrigue started from the moment I stepped in to find a spacious, dimly-lit dining area bustling with activity. My friend and I had wisely made a reservation for our 9pm Thursday dinner – a must, I quickly realized, in this popular spot.

We dove straight into the heart of the menu, sharing a burger topped with bacon that was nothing short of culinary decadence. While delicious, it's a hearty choice that could test the limits of your appetite. We also savored the duck hash, a dish both rich and irresistibly unique, adding to the satisfying experience.

In summary, this restaurant offers a delightful surprise behind its unassuming alley entrance, serving up dishes that are as indulgent as they are flavorful. A definite must-visit for those looking for a memorable dining experience.

Title: Mixed Feelings about NaNa Thai Street

As a self-professed Thai cuisine enthusiast, I was thrilled to discover NaNa Thai Street had opened near my workplace. The establishment presents itself modestly, a cozy takeout venue with a smattering of tables, and it prides itself on using natural, organic ingredients. Unfortunately, my culinary experience did not fully live up to the excitement.

My main gripe pertains to the balance between cost and quality. The price point teeters on the higher side, which wouldn't be a concern if it were matched by the fare's quality and quantity. The Pad Thai I ordered sadly tipped the scales towards disappointment – it was notably dry and scanty, particularly with a meager offering of only three shrimp.

On a positive note, the dish delivered on promised heat, satisfying my taste for spice. However, the menu's inflexibility was a letdown; the lack of customizable options, like adding a single spring roll, felt like a missed opportunity, especially considering the larger appetizer portions were overwhelming for one person. Interestingly, the express meals come with a complimentary spring roll and appear to be more reasonably priced.

One beacon of hope in the menu's puzzling price landscape is the burrito, which seems to offer a glimmer of value – it's an option I'm willing to return for. Nevertheless, if value is the main criterion, I'm inclined to stick with Thai Villa for future Thai cravings, as it provides more bang for the buck. Overall, NaNa Thai Street walks a fine line, and it might require some menu and pricing adjustments to secure my regular patronage. Rating: 2.5 stars.

Title: A Hidden European Gem

I recently stumbled upon this charming cafe that instantly transported me to the streets of Europe. The moment I stepped in, I was greeted by a chill vibe and a delightful menu brimming with choices. Picking between the likes of Bratwurst, Cheese Steak, Kielbasa, and even a Beyond Meat Burger was no small feat - a testament to their awesome selection.

I opted for the Frittes, which were nothing short of tasty, and the beer options available complemented the meal perfectly. This isn't your posh, upscale restaurant; it's quaint and unpretentious, reminiscent of the quaint spots one might find wandering through Austria, Germany, or Belgium.

For those who appreciate this type of atmosphere, it's an absolute find. I can't help but wish this little cafe was closer to my home. I urge you to glance over their menu and give it a shot if a laid-back European vibe appeals to you. It's an experience I thoroughly enjoyed and look forward to repeating.

Title: A Quaint Surprise at Antique Garage SoHo

Walking into Antique Garage, you might think you've stepped into a chic bygone era rather than a Mediterranean eatery. The name could easily throw you off—it's more reminiscent of a retro boutique than a restaurant. Yet, this SoHo spot offers an ambiance and cuisine that could bring you back for second helpings.

The decor is charmingly eclectic, with mismatched silverware, classic paintings, and twinkling chandeliers, each element contributing to the old-world vibe the name suggests. An antique piano providing live melodies enhances the dining experience, promising even more appeal when the garage-style front windows open in summer.

Onto the cuisine—the menu boasts tempting Mediterranean dishes, though the Manhattan prices might have you tightening the purse strings. Nonetheless, it's a treat worth splurging on, with scrumptious starters like silky hummus served with garlicky pita and feta-filled borek tucked in phyllo dough, not to mention the irresistibly crispy-yet-fluffy bread that graces the table.

Main courses like the grilled lamb meatballs, served with a side of crispy fries and thick tzatziki sauce, satisfy the carnivorous cravings, though they might not steal the show. That honor goes to the adana kebab, bursting with perfectly seasoned lamb that had me envying my girlfriend's plate. We capped the meal with profiteroles, a sweet finale to a satisfying dining experience.

While the service was competent, it didn't particularly stand out. Yet, Antique Garage delivers on food quality and unique atmosphere, even if the bill reflects its upscale location. Generously, I'm rounding up my rating to 4 stars. If you're hunting for a spot with a Mediterranean twist, Antique Garage is worth a stop—just be prepared that this particular 'antique' comes with a price tag.

Tucked away in a cozy nook of the city, my coworkers and I discovered this gem during their 5-8pm happy hour. An oyster aficionado's delight, the $1 offerings were juicy, fresh, and unequivocally worth every penny. To wash down the briny goodness, I sampled their Sauvignon Blanc and Prosecco - both were pleasant, albeit average compared to the standout oysters.

The appetizers, a duo of fries and wings, did tip the scales on the saltier side but nevertheless were savory and whetted our appetites for more. And indeed, there will be a 'more' - thanks to their impressive array of seafood, a return visit is already in the cards.

We were so excited to try this place out but it's nothing but overhyped. The presentation of the food was definitely impressing and unique. I actually really enjoyed my matcha lava cake. I found the green tea icecream complimented the super dense chocolate cake well. My partner found the cookie comp to be very sweet and heavy. He couldn't finish the rest. The  earl milk tea was good. The latte was forgettable and too overpriced. While the desserts were somewhat good, we did not like the music they were playing. The music they put is soo loud that you have to shout to talk amongst each other. Not only was the loudness a problem, but also the inappropriateness of the music. Not nice nor appropriate  especially if younger children are around.

I LOVE this place! I've been eating here all week and just so impressed with how delicious everything is. If you're vegetarian or vegan this place has great options for you. Food is always so good. I personally love the Chili Falafel Burger. It's sooooo good. Their falafel, salads, drinks are all so good. The safe is always friendly and engaging, they love to help you with recommendations. The cooks are happy and awesome. They work really quick here. They accept RITUAL app and can be okay for a bugger group just be mindful it's on stools. Tables don't move.Get your mint drink or shake!

I would give 6 stars if I could, or ten. We looove coming here. The staff is always very warm and welcoming. We haven't had a bad experience here and we come here at least three times per month for the last two years.We have brought our parents visiting and they loved it too. We always have the same dish because we love it, but having tried different stuff it was always great.I go for the grilled salmon with red sauce and my fiancé for the Dalmatian Buzara (seafood pasta with marinara sauce). They make it spicy per request and are flexible to accommodate any changes. My fiancé has tried similar dishes in NY buy says no one compares to  the one here! Hard to beat!And we love the Croatian wines and desserts cart :DFor more years to come!! Save our spot this weekend!

Title: A Timeless Taste of China in C-Town

If you're seeking authentic Chinese cuisine in C-town, look no further than Wo Hop. This no-frills eatery has been a local staple for years, attracting both regulars and tourists alike with its genuine flavors and uncomplicated charm.

The menu boasts an array of delectable options, but I highly recommend indulging in their flat noodles – available with beef, chicken, or shrimp – for a hearty and satisfying experience. The Chinese broccoli is another must-try, offering a fresh and savory complement to any meal. A crowd favorite, the chicken broccoli, does not disappoint with its perfect blend of tenderness and seasoning. For a comforting starter, the wonton soup embodies the warmth and tradition of Chinese cuisine.

While the dumplings may fall just short of extraordinary, they are still a decent choice. Pair your meal with a pot of hot tea to enhance the flavors and embrace the full dining experience.

Word of Wo Hop's culinary delights has spread, transforming it into a hotspot for food enthusiasts and causing wait times to stretch a bit longer than usual. Service, while attentive, can trail behind due to the constant bustling of this popular spot. Despite the rush, the taste and tradition of Wo Hop are worth the wait, making it a landmark dining destination for anyone craving a taste of China.

I regret to report a disheartening experience at the restaurant I visited recently. The ladies' bathroom was marred by an unsettling lack of cleanliness, including vomit on the floor. Service confusion was rampant, with no clear server assigned to our table and food runners struggling to match dishes with diners. Efforts to seek clarity necessitated reaching out to who I presumed was the manager, based on his plaid shirt and tie. Having been a loyal patron of Blarney Rock up the street, it was truly disappointing to have such a non-positive experience during its closure. This visit, unfortunately, warrants a poor review.

I recently dined at this trendy dessert spot for my sister's birthday, eager to capture some Instagram-worthy moments. Conveniently, the restaurant boasts two venues on the same street; we opted for the cozier extension that comfortably accommodates six parties.

Arriving from the NQR station, this smaller outpost is the first you'll encounter. They've streamlined the waiting process with an iPad check-in at the door, though the option to reserve a spot via Yelp beforehand is a thoughtful touch. Our party of five was seated briskly within 20 minutes.

We embarked on a culinary sweet-treat expedition, starting with the standout Golden Toast. Its sublime medley of crisp yet fluffy honey cake, cold vanilla ice cream, fresh strawberries, and whipped cream was unanimously adored - a must-try in my book.

Though I passed on the Matcha Lava, my relatives endorsed it as delightfully rich without cloying sweetness, and a feast for the eyes to boot. The Bubble Tea in Matcha Latte garnered praise for its balance and exceptional boba, while the Taro variant fell short, likened more to cereal milk than the namesake flavor.

Regrettably, the Cookie Camp dazzled only briefly, its saccharine symphony proving too intense. Contrastingly, the Matcha Sunday Special was as satisfying to the palate as it was photogenic.

We concluded with takeout cookies that promised a soft bite. Despite the Taro Bubble Tea misstep, this spot's dessert artistry and inviting ambiance made for a sweet and memorable birthday celebration.

Title: Cozy Spot with Tasty Snacks in K-Town

I've been a fan of this local haunt for a while, primarily frequenting it for drinks, and I was pleased to find that their food holds up as well. The drink selection is quite delectable, though I must note they do lean towards the sweeter side, which may not be to everyone's taste. Be prepared to pay a bit of a premium, but it's justifiable given its central location in K-Town.

Getting a table was never an issue, especially for larger parties, as they seem to consistently have space in the back for groups of four or more. If you're in the mood for a bite, I'd recommend sticking to the bar snacks which are a hit, while the soups were rather mediocre and forgettable.

For sports fans, there are a couple of TVs by the bar. It's acceptable for a casual glance at the game, but if you're in it for the long haul and serious about your sports viewing, you may want to scout out a different venue. All in all, it’s a great place for a laid-back evening with friends over some good drinks and light bites.

Visited a second time, almost a year later (which is a big deal, bc I don't find myself eating at too many of the same restaurants multiple times). After a trip to Japan and trying more omakase spots in NYC, I felt that I needed to update my review just to say that Omakase by Teisui may be one of my top places. They're affordable, yet delivers quality experience and fish. I've been disappointed by a certain Michelin-starred spot in NYC (That I won't name, but you can probably find in my reviews) and I would choose Omakase by Teisui ANY DAY.

Lucked out with a counter seat directly in front of Eyal Shani himself, and I got to watch a true artist at work.  I was mesmerized when he peeledthe skin off beautiful tomatoes with a huge knife, at times not even looking, but knowing exactly how to make the perfect cuts.  Cutting the thinnest slices of fish for carpaccio, angling the cuts of his cucumbers beautifully.  Hats off to this artist.  On to the food.  Our first dish was the 12 foot long pici noodle.  It was delicious, and I found myself wanting to lick the bowl clean to get the last bits of delicious cheese from the sides of the bowl.  My husband asked Eyal what kind of cheese he used because we both loved it so much.  The pizza has a hint of pepper in the sauce that made it unique, and the dough was so freshShared the apple crumb for dessert which was also delicious.  At about 9, the restaurant transformed into a different place.  The bars on the windows came down, the lights dimmed, and it became somewhat like a night club - with cool Israeli music.  Very fun place.I've been to HaSalon in Tel Aviv, and wasn't sure if Eyal would be able to bring the same "living room" feel to New York.  HaSalon NY seems totally trendy, yet still did have some of the living room feel that the name connotes...All of the chairs in the restaurant are different, which I loved.  The servers are extremely fun and personable.  The restaurant is total lively - bustling with noise, music, etc. My one complaint - the price tag.  The pasta was about $32 and was way small for that price.  Dessert was $28, and although very good, seemed way more expensive than dessert everywhere else.  However you are paying for quality.  The heirloom tomatoes he was using looked like beautiful jewels.  I had a great overall experience and will definitely be back! Sent from my iPhone

This place is alwayssssss packed and for good reason. The food is pretty damn good. I've ordered the jujeh chicken kabob -- super juicy and comes piping hot with a side of cherry rice (this is a sweet rice that pairs amazingly with the savory meat). The barg (lamb) kabob is equally succulent and always a crowd pleaser. And for appetizers: get the kashke badenjan (dip the steaming soft bread into this and you're in heaven) or the the crispy samosas.

Title: A Bite of Chi-Town in the Heart of NYC

Nestled along a discreet alley on Canal Street, my solo weekday lunch at this bustling hotspot was as inviting as the warm lighting and wooden accents of its interior. Seated promptly, I dove straight for their much-lauded burger, opting for the single cheeseburger with a twist – adorned with egg and bacon, despite the surprise of two patties.

Forging ahead to the breakdown: The patties were thick, slightly oversalted, detracting from their juiciness. However, the bacon was a standout – its sweet, smoky, and peppery notes were on point. Toasted buns held their ground, creating a stable base for the richness imparted by the runny egg and dijonaise, although the medley of flavors sometimes felt overwhelming. In contrast, the fries provided a delightful crunch, perfectly complemented by the garlic aioli.

Though unable to conquer the generous portions, the meal ended on a high note with a beautifully crafted black camo latte from Sawada Coffee – a recommended alternative to dessert.

While Au Cheval's burger didn't quite top my list and its price tag sparked debate, the overall quality, atmosphere, and exceptional service from my server Celeste tilt the scales favorably for a potential second visit, perhaps with fewer add-ons for a purer taste experience. Worth exploring, especially if Chicago is out of reach.

This place was open late and easy to get a table despite the large crowds after a concert ended. The waitress we had was super friendly and my oreo milkshake was pretty good. The fried chicken I ordered was good but the breast piece was butchered in differently than I'm used to so there was a lot of rib and spine to pick around while trying to eat it. Also I asked if I could upgrade my fries to the special fries on the menu but instead I was brought a sep order. When I asked about it I was told I wasn't going to be charged twice but I was still charged the full price for the separate order or fries. The mozzarella didn't add any flavor and the gravy was not your typical beef or turkey gravy but very sweet. All I could think was that their was applesauce... Good place for cozy food, open late.

I came here for dinner for my birthday with two of my friends. The food was well prepared and the service was great. I enjoyed the artichoke heart and the buffalo croquettes, i didn't really care for the mushroom scallops the dish was a bit bland. We also ordered the tofu, rigatoni and curry stuffed potato. All the entrees were flavorful and satisfying. I would definitely go back, keep in mind the location is popular so a reservation is recommended.

Title: Perfect St. Paddy’s Celebration at Paddy’s!

I had the luck of the Irish on my side when a friend chose Paddy’s for our St. Patrick's Day festivities. You can't miss it with its festive exterior, and once inside, the ambiance doesn’t disappoint — green decorations everywhere and Irish tunes setting the festive mood. 

The place was buzzing but not overcrowded, giving me just the space I needed to enjoy my first Guinness. The bartenders were standout friendly and attentive, contributing to the dive bar’s unique charm. Plus, the owner mingling with the guests was a touch you don’t often see elsewhere. 

Cleanliness was on point too, especially the restrooms, which is always a win in my book. And if you’re looking to mix it up, there are pool tables waiting in the back.

Paddy’s has all the right ingredients for a good time — don’t just walk by, pop in!

Title: A Perfect Spot for Beer and Bites with Friends

I recently visited a fantastic casual restaurant that's ideal for a laid-back outing with friends. The place offers ample outdoor seating for those sunny days and a lively interior complete with ping pong tables and board games, adding a fun twist to your typical dining experience.

Their beer selection is impressive, boasting an array of on-tap options and a vast assortment of bottled beers from across the globe. In celebration of Oktoberfest, they're currently featuring enticing beer and food specials alongside their regular offerings.

The food was a delightful surprise. We indulged in the calamari, which was outstanding - crispy yet light, paired with irresistible sauces. Other dishes, like the fresh avocado quinoa salad and the zesty lemon chicken, were equally delicious and well-executed.

Special kudos go to our server, who was fantastic and went above and beyond. Their patience and knowledge shone when assisting a friend in choosing the perfect beer, complete with free samples ensuring a tailored experience.

Oh, and the complimentary popcorn? Just the cherry on top of a great visit! Whether you're here for the beer, the food, or the laid-back games, this spot is sure to provide a great time.

Dont know in what world that Pig and Khao doesn't get 5 stars. The food is simply amazing. The octopus appetizer, the pork belly, the pork ribs, it just is all so delicious and pairs amazingly with the coconut rice. I have to say, that coconut rice is about the best rice I think I've had in the city. It offsets the savory of many of the dishes and even better if you take it home and fry it up the next day. The drinks were also fabulous and a lot of inventive cocktails. The wait staff was very kind, very attentive and kept our water glasses full. The price might deter a casual diner, but the food is outstanding and more than worth it. Will be returning for sure!

Title: A Mixed Bag with a Highlight on Penne alla Vodka

My recent visit to the restaurant was a culinary roller coaster, starting off on an uneven note with a complimentary bread basket. The bread offered a mixed experience with a disappointingly burnt crust, overshadowed by a decent interior when dipped in the provided balsamic vinegar and olive oil.

The Prosciutto e Melone, intriguing in concept, proved a unique and tasty experience, though its $17 price tag failed to match the value I was hoping for. Moving onto the mains, the Spaghetti & Meatballs fell squarely into the realm of the ordinary, justifying neither excitement nor complaint for its $18 cost.

A clear standout was the Penne alla Vodka. This dish shone with its perfect blend of flavors and a generous scattering of bacon bits, delivering satisfaction worth every cent of its $18 price. On the dessert front, the Profiteroles al Cioccolato were a letdown, with cream puff pastries that were too tough to enjoy.

The much-anticipated Fried Ravioli pastries, remembered for their rich chocolate filling, couldn't recapture their past glory, as the balance had tipped towards bananas over chocolate. Next time, I will request a customization to align with the chocolate-heavy memory.

In conclusion, while some dishes left room for improvement, the Penne alla Vodka stands out as a must-try. It alone warrants a return visit, and for that, the establishment earns my recommendation.

The rice wasn't sushi rice as promised on the menu. The texture was harder like Chinese dinner rice. I get a free beverage for checking in on Yelp, but when I showed it to the lady behind the cash register, she said "can soda only." *roll eyes* For can soda, they only have Coke and Calpico Soda. Lame.Price was $10.95 for a bowl with two proteins; probably the best value in Manhattan. They have warm bowls too. Those actually looks good. Check it out!

Title: A Casual Lunch at Buffalo Wild Wings

I recently dined at Buffalo Wild Wings for the first time, a flashback spot for my girlfriend during her high school years. This suggested a hint of nostalgia and a promising meal ahead. We arrived at 12:30 PM on a Monday to find the vast, sport-filled space nearly empty, which set the stage for what we hoped would be attentive service and a cozy lunch.

Seated promptly at a booth, the restaurant seemed perfect for sports enthusiasts with its myriad of televisions. I chose the Grilled Chicken Buffalitos, accompanied by a side of fries. The dish was flavorful, though portion size left a bit to be desired. Unfortunately, the service didn't match the ambiance, as our lone server seemed overwhelmed, making us flag him down for necessities, which dampened the experience.

In summary, while Buffalo Wild Wings offers a welcoming atmosphere for sports and casual dining, the slightly wanting portion sizes and slower service on this visit suggest ensuring clear communication with your server for a smoother meal.

Title: A Mediterranean Delight at [Restaurant Name]

Last evening, my girlfriends and I indulged in a Mediterranean feast at [Restaurant Name], a decision influenced by a tantalizing photo of their bronzini. The ambiance of the restaurant is cozy and quirky, complete with a bar and a unique bookshelf bathroom door that offers a playful slide to access.

Seated comfortably opposite the bar, I was eager to try the whole fish bronzini, served head to tail, while one friend opted for a filleted version, and another savored the visually stunning black linguini with seafood. The bronzini was a revelation – perfectly cooked, its flavor and freshness pairing harmoniously with a side of scrumptious spinach. It was so impressive that I now fantasize about having bronzini every day!

Service was a highlight, with our waitress Rachel exemplifying professionalism and warmth, ensuring our dining experience was nothing short of delightful. [Restaurant Name] has certainly won our hearts and appetites. We'll be back – maybe next time for that tempting black linguini. Thank you for a memorable evening!

Title: Hidden Gem in Chinatown – A Surprising Find

After a leisurely stroll through Chinatown, my curiosity led me to an unassuming restaurant that piqued my interest. The exterior belies the expansive dining space that awaits upstairs. Accessible by escalator, this establishment opens up to a large, straightforward dining area that encourages a relaxed dining experience.

Service was prompt - I found it easy to summon the various dim sum carts that navigate through the tables. Compared to my previous dining experiences in Flushing, this place certainly held its own. However, there was a slight hiccup with some of the offerings arriving at a less-than-ideal temperature.

One particularly delightful part of the meal was the adorably shaped dim sum resembling little bunnies, which were as tasty as they were charming, almost too cute to consume. It's a spot that seems ready-made for families and groups looking for a place to share a meal. Additionally, the full bar is a nice touch for those who enjoy a drink with their dim sum.

Though not without its flaws, the restaurant has potential, and I find myself inclined to revisit. Next time, I hope to find that all the dishes are as warm as the inviting atmosphere they’re served in.

We came in for brunch around 1:30pm, we were a group of 15 and my friend had already selected the food. We started off with the monkey bread, which was honestly not anything special in my opinion. There was tons of food and the servers were very good about bringing the food out in a timely manner. Some of the outstanding dishes were the salmon with this really delicious everything cream cheese, the tuna tartare, and to my surprise the pancakes were amazing. I'm not a pancake fan and would have never ordered this on my own but everyone was raving about them so I tried them. I've never had pancakes like this before, they came with some cooked apples and strawberries and I would definitely order this again. The server recommended the Hemingway Spritz, if you like grapefruit this is a must have drink. Overall we had a great time and everyone was stuffed.

Happy hour is the ticket here. The cocktails are strong and legit, and at $8 are an incredible value in Midtown. I highly recommend the mojito, which is well balanced, and the Cuba Libre, which is rum with a splash of Coke and lime.The appetizers came out quick and hot. Our favorite was the wings, which were perfectly fried - crispy inside and moist inside - and came in a delicious sauce. We generally thought their sauce game was on point, while the fried options (empanadas and spring rolls) carried less flavor. The oysters also were enormous and a good value at $1.50 each.  Service was quick, friendly, and knowledgeable. The space is bright and welcoming, and while it was boisterous during peak happy hour service, we were still able to have a conversation.We did not have their full entrees, so look to other reviews for more insight into that region of the menu. The Yelp perks here - yucca fries for a check-in and dessert for a review - were the only real misses, and we left most of the tres leches cake on the plate.We'd definitely stop in again on our way into the city on the way to a show. Remember: strong cocktails. Do what you need to do to walk out under your own power.

Title: Fresh Seafood with Room for Improvement at South Street Seaport

I recently visited a charming seafood spot at the revitalized South Street Seaport and had quite a fresh experience. Diving into both the lobster and crab salads, the quality of the seafood didn't disappoint, with both tasting remarkably fresh. While the crisp lettuce matched the seafood in freshness, the salads were a bit too simplistic for my taste, featuring lettuce alone without the accompaniment of other salad staples like tomatoes or carrots. A variety of dressing options would also be a delightful addition.

Remembering my experience from the week prior, I decided to skip the combo seafood salad which includes shrimp alongside the lobster and crab. Although the shrimp was flavorful, it was small and rather tough; a contrast to the more succulent lobster and crab. For seafood lovers like me who prefer to focus on lobster and crab, an option to get a double portion of these without the shrimp would be most welcome.

The chipotle old bay mayo is a standout, adding a flavorful kick that complements the seafood well. The venue itself contributes to a pleasant dining experience with ample outdoor seating by the water. Plus, Chase Sapphire cardholders can enjoy the added perk of relaxing in the exclusive Sapphire Lounge – a benefit that's making me reconsider the card's value, especially with its travel rewards.

Overall, I would recommend this spot to seafood enthusiasts. With a few tweaks to their salad offerings and perhaps a reevaluation of shrimp quality, this eatery could truly shine.

Title: A Cozy Spot with Hits and Misses

My recent dining experience at this restaurant was comfortably satisfactory. While it didn't dazzle, it's a nice choice for a casual meal. We ordered the braised short ribs, which were absolutely delectable, falling off the bone and accompanied by perfectly cooked potatoes. However, the side vegetables left much to be desired, lacking any seasoning and reminiscent of being rinsed in water without much thought.

For those who appreciate heat, the veggie chili packs a punch and is a flavorful option. But be warned, it's not for the faint of palate due to its spiciness.

I also indulged in a glass of sangria for $15, a decision I regret. The taste was mediocre and certainly not a match for its price tag. Next time, I'd skip the sangria and enjoy the more favorable dishes this restaurant has to offer.

As you approach Central Park's Fifth Avenue entrance, you're instantly greeted by the majestic sight of Jean-Marie Appriou's aluminum horse sculptures. Towering at 15 feet, these equine masterpieces have just been installed last week and promise to grace the park until August 30, 2020.

What sets these sculptures apart is their accessibility; they stand directly on the ground, inviting visitors to interact by walking through and around them. Appriou's process, from carving in foam and clay to the final cast in aluminum, imbues these horses with a lively presence that's far from unapproachable. Central Park's already impressive collection of art is enhanced by these new additions, making a walk in the park even more inspiring.

This review is for the poke bowl and service.My date got the steak bowl and thought it was fine. I got the spicy salmon and tuna bowl and it was awful. None of the ingredients seemed fresh at all, and the rice was oddly quite hard as if it were leftover rice. I could barely bring myself to eat anything in the bowl. As for service, we only got the two bowls. My date got his steak bowl and waited to start eating until mine arrived. It took forever so I told him to just go ahead. He almost finished his entire bowl before mine even at arrived. Not sure why it took so long to put together as simple of a poke bowl as what I ordered (see the photo) or why they couldn't coordinate, but it didn't even seem to bother the waitstaff. Maybe I should've tried other items but based on that, probably won't be returning.

Tamarind has long been -- and continues to be -- one of the best Indian restaurants in New York. In a city with well over 100 really good Indian restaurants, Tamarind continues to be one of the very best and certainly one of only a handful that is a high end experience. From the cocktails to the front of house staff to the quality of the ingredients, Tamarind is truly a great fine dining experience. The flavors are varied and rich. While the staples of Indian cuisine can all be found at Tamarind, their unique dishes are the stars of the show. Tamarind's Michelin Star is well deserved. When I eat at Tamarind I always remember Gwyneth Paltrow's quote about Indian food, "when I venture out to eat, I like to go to places with food that I don't know how to make. So my favorites are Japanese and Indian. Indian food has so much layering of flavor, and the dishes go together so harmoniously." The wonderful layering of flavors in every dish is why I keep coming back to Tamarind.

What can I say that they tried, but it needs improvement. Service is good, the staff are all on top of it. However, the food was eh. I thought that the portion size of the seafood bucket was eh. My friend ordered a burger and that was the size of my face, but if they're trying to attract seafood lovers then try harder. I can go elsewhere to get my fix next time. When you walk-in it has cute decor, but you're quite confused as to if it's a diner or something that's supposed to be a ship? The kitchen is kinda out in the open so you can see or hear what the cooks are doing on that side. I was waiting to use the restroom and saw the cooks preparing and they dropped something. I was watching like a hawk to see if they would wash it, reuse it or discard it. They saw me and I think they were debating about it. All I can say is ew...  Not going back it that's what the cooks do in the wide open.

Title: Fresh and Tasty Lunch Find via Ritual App

After exploring new lunch spots via the Ritual food app, I stumbled upon a gem where I indulged in a Prosciutto and Arugula personal pie. True to their made-to-order promise, the pie was exceptionally fresh and simply delectable. The establishment boasted a clean interior and ample seating, visible right from the entrance.

While they didn’t provide takeout menus, pointing me to their online menu instead (a nod to eco-friendliness perhaps), it didn't detract from the experience. The pizza, especially with a sprinkle of red pepper flakes, hit all the right notes – "que rico!" I'm already looking forward to my next visit to taste another creation from their menu.

Title: Joe's Pizza — Worth the Wait?

Having passed by Joe's Pizza numerous times during my recent trips to New York, the persistent long line eventually piqued our curiosity. Surrendering to the hype, my husband and I joined the queue on our final visit, intrigued to discover if the pizza would live up to its reputation.

The line, to our relief, progressed faster than anticipated. We opted for a varied sampling: a caprese, a classic cheese, and a pepperoni slice for good measure. Although the caprese slice fell short on flavor, perhaps a mediocre experience in the grand pizza-scape of NY, the cheese and pepperoni slices performed much better, delivering on taste and satisfaction.

Is Joe's Pizza the crowning jewel of New York pizzerias? Far from it. But it's a solid choice for a quick bite in the city that never sleeps. I'd give it a 3.5 stars if half ratings were an option — perfectly decent but not top of my list.

Title: A Night of Vintage Charm and Mixed Culinary Delights at [Restaurant Name]

I recently dined at [Restaurant Name] with six friends, an establishment known for its Turkish Mediterranean cuisine and boasting two closely situated locales. A tip for future diners: make sure you're headed to the right location, as a mix-up is easily done but, fortunately, easily resolved.

Upon entry, the restaurant transports patrons to the opulence of the early 1900s, with high ceiling chandeliers, antique furnishings, and sumptuous red velvet seating, all immaculately preserved. The ambiance is undeniably the star here.

The menu leans heavily on seafood and grilled meats. While the appetizers may seem steeply priced at $20-$30, they were mostly a worthy indulgence. Highlights included the fresh Sea Bass Ceviche and the Octopus Salad, the latter winning our collective favor with its perfectly seasoned and cooked tentacles.

However, the entrees, such as the Bar Steak with its chewy texture and modest serving, failed to match the appetizers' standard. Even the pricey Baby Lamb Chops, though tender and tasty, could not wholly elevate the meal.

Service was attentive, compensating for mishaps like a leaky vent with complimentary drinks. The experience took an unexpected turn when a broken baluster from the second floor descended onto our table. Thankfully, the staff's response was prompt and concerned, though it was certainly a night to remember for less culinary reasons.

My verdict: [Restaurant Name] offers a strong 3.5-star experience with appetizers that shine against the backdrop of a stunning interior. Entrees and unfortunate events notwithstanding, it's worth a visit for those seeking a taste of the past with a side of good food.

Title: A Worthwhile Fieldtrip to Harlem's Flavor Haven

My recent visit to Fieldtrip was an absolute delight. Aptly named, it offers a culinary adventure right in Harlem, conveniently situated in front of the subway stop, making it hard to miss.

The restaurant beckons with vibrant flavors and colorful dishes that promise a feast for the senses. The beef and shrimp bowls we tried were culinary polar opposites, yet each presented its own array of tantalizing tastes. Although the shrimp bowl left me yearning for a few more succulent pieces, it's a testament to how much I enjoyed the complex flavors.

To complement the meal, the dragonfruit lemonade was a refreshing and interesting choice. The warmth and friendliness of the staff added to the wonderful experience.

While Harlem might not be a regular destination for many, Fieldtrip has certainly earned a spot on the list of reasons to make the journey. Count on us to be back for another flavorful expedition.

Title: Cozy Culinary Close to Our Corner on MLK Day

On the last leg of our 3-day escape from DC, my boyfriend and I popped into this nearby gem for a lunch treat on MLK Day. Welcomed with immediate seating and a team of synchronized servers, the service felt like a well-choreographed dance - attentive without being overwhelming.

I sipped on a refreshing mint tea while my boyfriend sampled a crisp draft beer. As for the food, the upselling skills of our server were both impressive and effective, leading us to indulge a bit more than planned. The chicken wings were a solid starter, but the lobster Mac and cheese was the star – rich and teeming with succulent lobster to the point of opulence, though a few more noodles wouldn't have gone amiss.

My boyfriend's salmon avocado toast arrived with an upgraded side of sausage and a perfectly poached egg, rounding out a satisfying meal. We topped it off with a creamy slice of cheesecake, the perfect sweet note to end on.

The bill was a reasonable $94 considering the quality and quantity. This spot has secured a place on our 'must return' list for future DC visits.

Title: Satisfying Burger Experience with a Side of Southern Charm

I recently visited this gem of a restaurant for a girl's day out with my niece and had a delightful dining experience. My niece opted for the Carolina burger, which was very tasty, though it would benefit from a more generous helping of pulled pork to balance the ratio with the burger patty. Despite this, it was still a hit with her.

As for myself, I chose to customize the Texan burger, swapping out the BBQ sauce for their special sauce and upgrading to truffle mayo - both changes proved to be excellent decisions. The special sauce added a unique twist, while the truffle mayo elevated the entire burger.

The Sweet and Salty dessert shake deserves a special mention, earning an A+ for its indulgent flavors. Visiting at 1pm on a Sunday meant we were seated immediately, no waiting required, which was the cherry on top for our outing. 

Our waiter, Luis, was exceptional. He ensured our experience was nothing less than perfect, even bringing extra ice for our water without being asked. Observing other diners, I noticed the Brussel sprouts, which came highly recommended by my senses. The tantalizing aroma alone was enough to suggest a return visit may be in order. 

Overall, the attentive service and delicious food crafted a memorable girls' day start.

Love this place! One of the top 3 best steakhouses in NYC! Best cream of spinach of all steakhouses! Love the porterhouse here it's their signature steak! All the other ones are subpar. However I prefer keens steakhouse for their prime rib and mutton steak

Title: A Gem for Kimbob Lovers

If simplicity is the key to brilliance, this quaint spot proves the adage with flying colors. Operated by a deft Emo (auntie), who skillfully crafts each kimbob roll with a personal touch, the establishment exudes authenticity in its modest confines. Don't expect to linger – the size is an overt cue that it's a "grab and go" venue, which suits the quick nature of enjoying kimbob, Korea's answer to sushi rolls, only with fully cooked ingredients.

Vegetarian patrons will appreciate the diverse non-meat options available. And for those seeking a warm accompaniment, a complimentary miso soup is on offer to complement your meal's rice content. Speaking of rice, these rolls strike a delightful balance – sparing in their starch, allowing the savory fillings to take center stage, all snugly wrapped in a delicate layer of rice and seaweed.

Watching your kimbob come to life is part of the charm, as Emo's hands weave ingredient into art. The made-to-order approach is not only a spectacle but also a commitment to freshness, ensuring every bite of seaweed remains tender and easy to enjoy.

A word to the wise: this is a cash-only establishment, so come prepared. In sum, for a quick, delicious bite that's light on the rice and heavy on quality, this spot is hard to beat.

My sister-in-law suggested meeting up at Beyond Sushi for dinner. She and her partner have been to the other locations and enjoyed, but they thought this was a good option for us. Aside from great vegetarian food, this location is to Penn Station for me and my SO and is near their subway stop (i.e. it's an easy-to-get-to eatery Midtown during the work week - big plus). There's ample seating inside. We didn't have an issue getting a table for our party of four on a weekday. The interior of the restaurant has a clean and modern look. Also, everyone we interacted with - from the host, to our waiter, to bus staff - were friendly.Below is what we ordered from the menu, which were all hits at our table. - Crispy Confit Potato (appetizer and our favorite item that night)- The Badge Dinner - Chili Mushroom Ramen - Seasonal Roll Dinner - Sunny Side Dinner- Sweet Tree Dinner - Spicy Mango Dinner - Chic Pea Dinner- Mighty Mushroom Dinner Because we were there on a weekday, we made it just in time for the tail-end of happy hour. I took advantage of the deal and had two sakes - Saratoaga Sparkling Sm and Itami Onigoroshi: Demon Slayer. Demon Slayer was my preferred over the two (both were quality though and are ones that I'd have again). Last but not least, they have fantastic vegan ice cream. If you are with a group, I recommend ordering the Ice Cream Trio Sampler. So good and great to share!

Title: A Satisfying Slurp at Totto Ramen Midtown East

My recent work lunch at Totto Ramen's Midtown East location was a delightful experience, notably surpassing their Hell's Kitchen counterpart with its cleaner and more spacious setting. Despite their strict policy on waiting for the full party to arrive before seating us, we managed to beat the rush by arriving at opening time on a Friday afternoon – a wise choice as the place filled up quickly within 20 minutes.

Unlike Hell's Kitchen, where pre-seating orders speed up service, this branch operates on traditional dining etiquette, so patience is required after you're seated. The appetizers – tofu, chicken, and edamame – were typical fare, but the ramen truly stood out. The chicken patina ramen boasted succulent char su and a generous vegetable medley, proving to be a delight. However, the vegetable ramen, from a previous visit, edged out slightly ahead, offering a great option for vegetarians.

Totto Ramen has secured its place as one of my top ramen picks in New York City, on par with famed spots like Ippudo and Jin Ramen. Whether you're a meat-lover or a vegetarian, this spot is worth the visit for a bowl of cozy, delicious ramen.

Title: A Vegetarian Delight That's Worth Every Penny!

Every visit to this gem of a restaurant leaves my taste buds celebrating. Their basic curry with rice is a testament to how flavorful vegetarian cuisine can be, while the potato and cream cheese croquettes offer a decadent, crispy treat. For a mere $14, you're guaranteed a quick, steaming hot, and utterly delicious meal. Perfect for anyone seeking a satisfying eat without the wait. A hearty recommendation to all!

Instagram: @traveleen_gurl

I visited a local restaurant last night during an early moon cake festival celebration, and the experience was notably impressive. The restaurant was three-quarters booked, buzzing with the energy of large groups gathered around each table, designed to comfortably seat ten people.

Dining was a family-style affair with a spread of 11 different dishes gracing each table. The pace at which the plates were cleared—a testament to the appetizing offerings—highlighted the crowd's enjoyment as every dish was devoured within minutes. While the flavors weren't outstanding, warranting a modest 3.5 out of 5, they were certainly pleasing enough to merit mention.

The highlight, however, was the exceptional customer service. Managing such a sizable crowd can be daunting, but the staff handled it with such efficiency and attentiveness that I can't help but give them a full 5 out of 5.

Overall, my experience was delightful, and I would not only recommend this restaurant to others, especially those looking to dine in large groups, but I am also looking forward to my next visit.

Title: Classic Comfort at Pizza Suprema, but with Room for Improvement

Having frequented Pizza Suprema multiple times, it's the sort of establishment that comes up in conversation when you find yourself near Penn Station or MSG and are hankering for a slice. The collective memory of a "really good pizza place" brings you back, and that's exactly what led me to revisit today.

I'm particularly partial to their Sicilian offerings, so I opted for the Pepperoni Fra Diavolo. The slice generally lived up to its reputation; the crust was a standout with its soft top and flawlessly caramelized bottom, though it was somewhat more porous than ideal. Taste-wise, it wasn't quite the showstopper I remembered.

A dip in service warmth was also noticeable this time around, which detracted from the overall experience. Do note that they have a $10 minimum for credit card transactions, which isn't hard to reach with slices priced between $4 and $6. Despite these points, Pizza Suprema still holds its ground as a reliable spot for a satisfying bite.

So imagine going to an All You Can Eat Hot Pot. I call this the adult version of Chinese Buffet because now you pick your own and cook it yourself. Hot pot is when you cook raw food into a simmering soup stock then afterwords you dip it into the array of condiments.They give you a huge plastic bag to put your belongings so there will not be any food aromas lingering. At 99 Favors you can choose from three soup stock.We had the chicken, pig feet, and spicy. I loved the spicy one the best. Some foods we cooked were shrimp, beef, chicken, tripe, cabbage, pumpkin, udon noodles, broccoli, and much more. Our favorite sauces were the homemade sauce, bbq and chili.Service was quick but it slowed after a while. We were there for a long time chatting  and a plus one joined in hours after with no problem.Price: $23.99 ACYE. You can't beat this price for all the options you can choose from.Can't wait to try other hot pot spots.Follow my ig: @eatingwithetienne for more.

Title: A Novel Catch-Your-Own Dinner Experience at Zauo, Chelsea

For my spouse's birthday, I ventured to Zauo in Chelsea, hoping to reel in a unique dining experience. On a quiet Tuesday evening, the three-story restaurant was nearly ours alone, and we were swiftly seated beside the animated fish tank on the first floor.

Zauo cleverly sections off their fish species to avoid any mistaken captures – once a fish is hooked, it's destined for your plate. However, the fish seemed wise to the game, often eluding our bait, turning the fishing more into a charming photo opportunity than an angling challenge. Eventually, we selected a salmon without the thrill of the catch, and our server promptly netted it for us.

The menu allowed us to split our salmon preparation two ways – we enjoyed a savory half tempura, half salt-grilled combo, complemented by a salmon bone miso soup. Our appetizers, Agedashi Go Tofu and Tako Kara-Age, were standouts, delivering an explosion of flavors with every bite.

While the concept was engaging and appetizers impressed, the main courses didn't quite match the hype or justify the cost. They were decent but didn't distinguish themselves from other dining experiences.
