Zauo offers more of a novelty than a gastronomic feast. It's not a meal that'll haunt your tastebuds with longing, but I'd recommend it for those seeking an entertaining outing with friends or family.

There's something to like here at Cookshop, the only problem is that you need to dig past a bunch of disappointing things to get there.Two of my friends and I went on an early Wednesday evening for a catch up dinner. We ordered drinks and a burrata to split between the three of us. When my negroni came, it looked delicious, served with a big block of ice and smelling like a tart blood orange. However sipping on the drink waiting for our appetizer to come, there was practically no alcohol to it, essentially drinking a (very expensive) orange juice. When the burrata came to the table, the ball looked like it had starred in the remake of Honey I Shrunk the Kids. Although tiny, we had high hopes that it would be tasty - cutting through the ball there was little of the creamy spreadable cream you expect in a burrata, all we had was a harder lump of cheese. Especially for the price, I'm not sure what everyone else is so excited about - maybe we just got a bad burrata Placing our entree order, the waiter came back three times as he forgot the cut and cook of one steak and totally forgot what I had ordered. The pork chop, when it came, was hands down the best part of the entire meal, a thick and juicy cut of meat with a succulent glaze and sauce in the plate, topped off with a rhubarb compote, and sage. Sadly, the waiter misunderstood the order and brought a side order of potatoes, delicious though they were, weren't ordered, yet made their way onto the bill. I've heard rave reviews about their brunch service, so maybe this only applies to the dinner service. Overall, the main entrees were delicious, but the service and appetizers left much to be desired.

Cozy and intimate spot for dinner! The place is very narrow so you have to hang up your jacket upon entering. Although the restaurant is small, I think it's the perfect amount of space to have dinner where you can actually talk and not be engulfed by tons of tables around you.To start, we had the 5 bruschette and filet mignon tartare. Both were decent but not extra notable. Personally I prefer my bruschette to have more than just cream and truffle but maybe it's supposed to be kept simple so you can taste the truffle. We also had the option to pay a surcharge for white truffles which we did upon the owner's recommendation, and it was amazing! The white truffle is much more fragrant than black truffle and I would recommend doing so if it's in your budget.The main courses were delicious and I enjoyed them more than the appetizers! I got the Tagliolino Cacio e Pepe which was creamy and fragrant and I finished it in a few bites! My boyfriend got the Oak's Hamburger which was oozing with mouth-watering sauce and covered in truffles! I would order these 2 mains again!All in all, it was a great experience and the service was home-y yet professional!

Title: Disappointing Korean Fried Chicken Experience

Rating: **2/5 Stars**

After being inspired by a Korean movie to satiate a craving for Korean fried chicken, I took to Seamless and stumbled upon this restaurant. Unfortunately, the experience was underwhelming. I ordered a combination of wings and drumsticks with both hot and soy garlic sauces, expecting the flavors to make my palate dance as they have at other establishments. This was not the case. The chicken itself was mediocre compared to other local options, and the hot sauce lacked the punch I anticipated. The soy garlic sauce was passable, but the whole meal would have benefited from extra sauces.

The side dishes also left much to be desired. The macaroni salad was subpar, falling short of even the most basic deli standards. Meanwhile, the Korean-style pickles were a disaster; their juice had leaked out during delivery, which speaks volumes about the lack of care in packaging.

Speaking of delivery, the service was irritating. The delivery person incessantly rang my doorbell, despite it only being a short wait. A more thoughtful approach to both packaging and customer interaction is needed.

Given this experience, I cannot in good faith recommend this restaurant for Korean fried chicken. There are better options, such as Bonchon, that will likely leave you more satisfied. It's a regretful thumbs down from me.

Maya is a great restaurant in midtown. On Sunday, my old coworkers and I met up at Maya for Sunday brunch. I was able to find parking one block away and realized it is close by the 59th street bridge which is also a plus because I live in Queens.On Sunday, there is unlimited drinks and food. So my friend stated we should work our way from the top and work our way down. LolThe drinks were well blessed  . The menu is short but that allows you to share and try more diverse meals. Our waitress was incredible. She was very present and always made sure our glass were full. I had a great time with my great friends and will definitely come back again.

Title: A Gem for Asian Cuisine Aficionados

If you're looking for culinary consistency and delectable flavors, this spot may dip into your wallet a bit, but rest assured, it's worth every penny. My numerous visits have been met with unwavering friendliness and top-notch service, a standard that extends to their prompt delivery.

The soup dumplings here? Best value in the neighborhood. The congee is a comforting constant, flawlessly prepared every time. For those with a hearty appetite, the dumpling platter is a must-try. And if your taste leans towards American Chinese classics, they've got your cravings covered.

The real treat comes on weekend afternoons with their noodle rolls – a divine experience that leaves me thanking the culinary heavens. Whether it's dine-in or delivery, this place never fails to impress.

On the good side, food was delicious. Most importantly that's what you look for in a restaurant. We ordered the beet salad to start (my GF thought it tasted weird but I didn't find anything wrong with it), the fish - which was very tasty and a pasta dish which was also delicious.  Service was very attentive and the location and design of the spot is decent enough to make it cozy'ish"On the bad side: place is new so service was a bit slow though there were only three tables being served. Food took a little too long to come out. One waitress was doing ALL the work... hosting, taking orders, serving, setting tables (a bit of help would have been nice). Overall a good dining experience.Btw - as of dec 2019 it is BYOW

It was okay. The dim sum was the best. All the drinks I had tasted the same. It was heavily priced and the menu had changes. It was weird the staff that was working were eating at the bar with customers. Some of the staff didn't really know the menu.

This was my first time at the 5th Avenue location of Ippudo. I've always had good experiences at the Hell's Kitchen and Astor Place locations. Today we decided to go to the one at 5th Avenue and ordered both of the specials. One was an order of 2 buns with their favorite ramen toppings and the other was a spicy ramen with ground pork, accompanied with white rice and a poached egg that you're supposed to add to the leftover soup at the end of your bowl. Both specials were extremely good, in particular the ramen with the extra rice to add to the leftover spicy broth.

Title: Iconic but Pricey - A Mixed Slice of NYC

I recently visited an esteemed pizzeria, keen to sample their much-hyped fare. We settled on a duo of pies, a straightforward pepperoni, and a customized margherita with added onions and spinach twist. The pizza itself did not disappoint; the sauce was rich and tantalizing, complemented by quality cheese. 

However, the crust fell short, coming off a touch too firm and bland, which detracted from the overall experience. A slightly shorter stint in the oven might have worked wonders. Portion sizes were another caveat; the pies erred on the petite side, challenging the value for money given the lofty $60 tag for the pair. 

Cash-only transactions further set the tone for an old-school vibe. Despite the steep prices, the pizzeria's reputation still commands respect. For those seeking the quintessential, throwback NYC pizza experience, this establishment fits the bill.

Super fun diner!Always come here once every few months. Service can be a bit slow.They have a good selection of diner foods.I've tried their burgers and sandwiches, and I also tried a salad last time I was here.I had the thai salad without papaya- it had a good amount of chicken in it and had just the right amount of dressing.The tater tots are always nice and crispyChicken tenders were pretty good as well.Wanted a whoppers milkshake but unfortunately they were out of whoppers.The cotton candy milkshake was super sweet but to be expected!It was still super good!

Title: A Disappointing Experience Despite the Scenic Locale

My recent visit to a well-rated restaurant was underwhelming, to say the least. Arriving for dinner on a bustling summer weekend, I was surprised to find that the kitchen had run out of key ingredients—no guacamole, tomatoes, or any sauces were available. This was a puzzling oversight for any establishment, especially during peak hours.

It's perplexing why the restaurant would continue serving without these essentials or fail to make a quick trip to the local grocery to restock. The value for money was also disappointing; one would expect more than a single, lackluster taco for $4.95, which unfortunately featured nothing more than dry fish and limp iceberg lettuce.

Although the restaurant's location is quite pleasant, my experience left much to be desired. In this instance, a simple street vendor hot dog would have been a preferable choice.

Despite the buzz surrounding this eatery, my experience fell short of expectations. Visiting during restaurant week, I anticipated a treat but was left underwhelmed. The touted chicken and waffles proved disappointing, with the meat chewy and the waffles lacking in flavor. Accompanying mac and cheese was overly rich, while the side of squash and apples, as well as the biscuit, were unremarkable. The desserts, chocolate and key lime, did little to redeem the meal.

While the meal included wine, it couldn’t compensate for the food's shortcomings. The ambiance, reminiscent of a hole-in-the-wall joint, lacked modern charm, although it was quite popular, filling up quickly so an early arrival is advisable.

Sadly, I couldn’t shake the feeling that a simple meal from KFC or Popeyes would have been more enjoyable, not to mention kinder on the wallet. In the realm of upscale fried chicken spots, this place didn't rise to the occasion.

This is one of my favorite spots in Chinatown. Come here all the time for lunch and never had a bad meal. All the roasted meats are cooked to perfection and have been happy with everything I tried. The roasted duck is by far the best thing on there menu and worth enticing every time.

I attended a Sunday brunch at this venue with a large group of 25, reserved for 1 PM. Unfortunately, the buffet spread was delayed, not fully prepared until 2 PM, even though guests were punctual. On the brighter side, the drinks served had a pleasing kick, and the musical ambiance was an enjoyable blend of Latin tunes and hip-hop beats, which truly livened up the experience. The hookah offered added a nice touch, though at $30 for a session and $20 for refills, the pricing felt a tad steep. Despite the initial wait for food, the overall vibe was great, and I would certainly consider returning for another brunch outing.

If you're a fan of hot pot, this place is a must-try! It's an all-you-can-eat establishment, and for approximately $50 per person, taxes and tips included, you're in for a treat with an extensive selection of hot pot favorites. The all-you-can-drink menu is equally impressive, featuring both alcoholic beverages and nostalgic Asian drinks. The quality of ingredients is top-notch—everything's fresh, and the variety is impressive. A word to the wise, though: be mindful of how much you order, as there's a fee for unfinished food. And don't miss out on their ace ice cream—especially the taro flavor, it's a delightful finish to a hearty meal.

Title: A Brunch to Remember at Bedford & Co.

I recently had the pleasure of brunching at Bedford & Co., thanks to a friend's invitation, and what a delightful discovery it was! The "eggs in purgatory" dish I indulged in proved to be a heavenly choice, accompanied by a side of perfectly crispy fries that were simply irresistible.

But the highlight had to be the Prosecco, which was transformed into a tropical escape with the addition of mango, orange, and guava juices – an absolute treat that sang of summer's approach. This gem of a spot came just in time for the season, and with experiences as good as this, Bedford & Co. has certainly earned a spot on my list of regular haunts. I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

Came here for a company event. The food was great but the service was one star. We shared a bunch of appetizers. My favorite was the smoked eggplant with garlic yogurt, which reminded me baba ganoush. I had the seared greek salmon with cauliflower rice as my main course. It was flavorful. When I asked one of the waiters if the warm hummus (v) with cured "beef" pastirma is vegetarian, the waiter gave me attitude and said "yes it is". Then I asked him what's the sliced meat on top? He was like "that's beef". Then I asked again "so it's not vegeterian". We had vegetarian eaters at the party. I had to make sure that they were not eating meat. The menu was extremely confusing because the beef had a double quote and there's (v) next to warm hummus. But clearly, there was sliced meat on top. So how can it be vegetarian????

My first visit to Keens Steakhouse spurred a mix of anticipation and delight, and I wasn't disappointed. The server who attended to us brought more than just food to the table; his charm and attentiveness added a personal touch to the experience. Each dish served was not only delectable but also generously portioned, ensuring we left satisfyingly full.

The dining room itself was a joy to behold, with decor that encapsulated a classic New York vibe – a treat for both the palate and the eyes. While Keens may not become a regular haunt for us, I see it as a perfect destination to showcase the city's culinary delights to visiting friends and family. It's a place where the essence of New York can be truly savored.

Stopped in last night for a slice. $4.75 gave me a meat lover pizza slice. It was fresh and good. Nothing too different than any other neighborhood pizza joint. They have several different pizza and beer combos that might interest any bar hopper.

I absolutely love eating Szechuan food but it also terrifies me at the same time because of the spice. I was excited to try this place regardless though. We were greeted rather quickly and the waiter offered many suggestions which helped us make a decision, considering how many options we had to choose from. I would definitely skip the milk teas because they were a little pricey, especially since there were no bubbles in it... despite the large bubble tea straw and the flavor didn't taste too authentic. We started off with the scallion pancake and wontons with chili oil for appetizers. The scallion pancakes were very greasy which made it all the more decisions. The sauce that accompanied it was lacking a bit but it was better than nothing. Wontons were great, excellent flavor but a little tricky to eat... super slippery! For our main course, we ordered beef with cabbage, the house special seafood and bok choy. The beef was so good! Really tender and packed with flavor - it was spicy but luckily not too much. There was also a generous portion of both meat and veggies in the dish. I was a little surprised that the seafood was fried but I liked it a lot. I think it was salt and pepper flavor which I love for fish and chicken. Seafood was very fresh and there were large chunks. I just wish the broccoli was cooked a little more, even if it was used mostly for decor. Bok choy was nothing to special but it was a great palette cleanser for all the spices from the other dishes. Presentation was also really nice for the plate. At the end of our meal, we were given a complementary dessert - snow fungus tong sui or "sugar soup." A little to sweet for my taste but it was nice that it was offered to us. Great service and good ambience, overall good experience!

Not a huge fan of artichoke but artichoke pizza was pretty damn good!Heard of Artichoke from my morning radio show where the host, Bert, talked about how Artichoke Pizza was his favorite pizza joint in NY. Ever since then I've had it in the back of my head but never had a chance to try until I randomly stumbled by it near Chelsea market/High line on my recent NY trip.  Usually I have a full blown itinerary of where we're eating to the hour, but after overeating the day before we were just going on a whim on eating whatever, whenever, we felt like it. Normally, that doesn't pan out and we're left disappointed eating randomly chosen food, but this wasn't the case here. I was a bit dumbfounded that there was a police scene right in front of the restaurant doorsteps where there seemed to have been some kind of issue between the staff and the patron and in the midst of it, the staff had actually opened to door for us. But once inside, everything was copacetic.There was seating for dining as well as to go/pick up station in the back.  We chose to just do to go and grabbed slices of pizza but ended up eating inside against the pick up station bar.  I got a slice of the artichoke and while it was a tad salty, it had great cheesy rich flavors.  Sort of reminded me of a quiche or chicken pot pie. yummmmmmm.  Friend got the margherita slice and while it looked great, it was on the dry side that we were tempted on getting another slice of the artichoke but refrained ourselves to pace our eating on that day. Lesson learned from the previous day.While Rubirosa has been our go to spot for pizza, Artichoke is definitely unique and special in its own way that I will look forward to it in the future.

Tucked away atop a bustling food plaza, this gem serves up the best fried chicken in town. It's easy to understand its fame once you've sampled the spicy sauce – a scrumptious blend of flavors that complements the succulent boneless wings to perfection. Each mouthful is a delight, especially when washed down with a cold beer. For a fried feast paired with the perfect brew, look no further than this outstanding spot.

We somehow snagged last minute 2 person reservations for Friday night.For the large pizzas, they allow half and half orders. They are actually very fair cause the whole pizzas cost different prices, but the half and half order is just half of what the whole pizza would cost and not the more expensive whole. All pizza places should do this! Ordered half margherita and half mushroom proscuitto. The proscuitto for some reason was just ham?, which was misleading. The margherita didn't seem to have much basil either. Cheese was fairly thick and stretchy.The crusts were incredibly fluffy and airy and red sauce was also great. The squid ink linguine was divine. Plenty of shrimp, red sauce, and linguine all mixed together. I enjoyed the pasta more than the pizzas. The restaurant itself was TINY. Extremely crowded. Tables all jammed together, no where to move once you're seated. Someone was celebrating a birthday and the desserts were massive. The servers even came around and squirted chocolate sauce into people's mouths. It was really festive and music was incredibly loud. Hard to hear one another and settled for shouting at one another. Not sure if that was a normal occurrence, but would highly not recommend this place for a date.

Sometimes, I can't help but order things that are IGable vs what I actually like. This was the case for The Burgary. I came on a Friday for lunch and we were the only ones in the restaurant. I usually like a simple burger which is easy to eat and not messy. My dummy self saw the "El Chapo" and had to order it. The burger consist of 6 oz. dry aged beef, short rib, pepper jack, chipotle, guac, and jalapeño on tostada. I did want something spicy and the jalapenos did give it a good kick. However, the burger was extremely messy. I hate hate hate soggy buns and with all the toppings, the bun was dunzo. There was just too much going on. The fries on the other hand was extra crispy and well seasoned. At $16 a burger, this place aint cheaps. I wouldn't go out of my way to come here for a burger. I wish they had some lunch specials too.

Happy 6 year anniversary! I have been working in the area for 7+ years and this was the first time I happened to see the restaurant and went in. I'm so happy I found this place because the interior was lovely and the food was good. There's not much authentic Asian cuisine around TriBeCa, and Khe-Yo definitely will hit the spot. It was restaurant week, but my colleague and I decided to order from the original menu. We shared one large (pork curry soup) and one small dish (papaya salad). There was a complementary sticky rice dish with two sauces (super spicy and sweet). My colleague loved the super spicy and I loved the sweet so it worked out. You're supposed to eat with your hands which was interesting. Don't worry they give you wet napkins to clean your hands before you eat it (thank god!). The waitress warned that the papaya salad would be fishy. I never had papaya salad so I wasn't sure what to expect. I wasn't much of a fan though. The pork curry noodle soup was so good. This was exactly what I was craving and it hit the spot! It had a coconut, light, spicy curry with thick noodles- my favorite! I didn't really taste much pork though but I didn't mind since I don't love pork. There were lots of veggies and a slice of lime to flavor your soup. It came in a huge bowl so I was very full after the two dishes. For dessert, they only had coconut gelato, but because my friend was lactose intolerant, they offered mango sorbet. There wasn't anything special about this. All in all, it was a great time and will be back but had to take off one star for the following:- not so amazing papaya salad and mango sorbet- they were slightly rushing us to leave since it was their 6 year anniversary

Prices has gone up since my previous review. The lunch specials are not that great of a deal anymore, but the food is still pretty good. You can get a plate with rice, beans, a side, and your choice of meat for around $11-$12. They give plenty of rice but not that much meat though. Beware of bones. I had the chicharon, which was good but fatty. The green garlic sauce is great, but thick and strong. Extra sauce is 25 cents. There are usually seats available. Self service.

After failing to eat at Congee Village (see my other review), we ended up here at Yee Li. We had previously stopped by at this place to buy BBQ Pork and because it was so delicious, we thought, well, the restaurant can't be too bad! There was a short line, but nothing crazy as compared to what we had just witnessed. We waited for maybe about five minutes before we were seated.In the beginning, it seemed like all would be fine. The one waiter sort of threw our dishes at us as he was setting the table, and we even joked that this would be the start of a great meal because he did that. Up through ordering the food, all was fine. But then, the waiting game began. We waited and waited and waited and the food just wasn't showing up. We finally saw a steamed fish being served and we thought, oh, this must be it! However, it went to a table in the back (I genuinely think they served it to the wrong table because the table that got it did not order it and so they turned to the table next to them and served it to them -- that table sat down way after we had). We continued to wait and had to check in with the waiters several times as to where our food was.Finally, our first dish came -- the Peking Duck. Let me just say that this was a very sad order of Peking Duck. There were four buns and the waiter made each one of them very slowly. He kept looking around at other tables as he was making it and even dropped some cucumber on the ground while making it. As a whole, it was okay. The lobster chips underneath the duck was pretty good. But for $20 for a half portion, I didn't really think it was worth it.Once we finished the duck, it was back to the waiting game again. After another ten minutes or more, the Ying Yang Fried Rice came out. This was probably the highlight of my meal. The shrimp was pretty tender and the flavors were good. It's fairly expensive for a fried rice dish ($16.99) but considering that it was actually tasty, that was actually worth it.More time passes before our next dish comes -- Honey Walnut Shrimp. This is my friend's favorite dish so we have tried it at every place we've been to together. I have to say that this would not rank at the top of my Honey Walnut Shrimp experiences. The mayo was spread out funny on top of the pieces of shrimp and the flavor of the mayo itself was somewhat strange. The shrimp was also way too breaded for my liking. For $22, I would have passed on this.Finally, we finished that and are starting to think we should just cancel our Steamed Flounder. The waiter came back and said "you already got it, didn't you?" We told him no, but if we can cancel it, then we'll just go ahead and cancel it. Of course they weren't going to let us cancel it so they kept telling us it was coming soon, it was coming soon. After another extended period of time, the fish finally came. The fish tasted bitter and the meat was very tough. Definitely not worth waiting for. Unfortunately, the poor service and mediocre food won't be bringing us back, but maybe we'll stick to buying just from the BBQ stand inside the restaurant.

My boyfriend wanted to take me here because I'm an avid fish and Mediterranean lover. I was very excited to try this place because I've heard really good reviews from it (actually just from my boyfriend who is a frequent visitor of this establishment). When we first arrived we were seated right away. They sat us by the windows which was great because I love people watching. Although it was a bit chilly that day so the breeze from the windows did bother me a bit. No worries because the food and service definitely made up for it.The waiter was very attentive and warm and welcoming. We received complimentary bread which was delicious and nibbled on that before our food came. We decided to order the calamari because why not- its a classic dish and I went with the Salmon dish and my boyfriend went with the Swordfish.Both arrived at the same time and it looked HEAVENLY. Omg the salmon looked so juicy and I couldn't wait to smash my face into it. I had a bit of my boyfriend's swordfish which was the first time I've had swordfish and I was surprised that it had a very meaty texture and taste.

I always see a line out the door for the place but never go in. This time there was no line! My friend and I shared the dessert pictured and it was enough for both of us. The cookie was sooo warm and delicious. If it wasn't $11-12 per dessert I'd come more often!

Pretty good ramen. Great service. I may be losing my ability to taste spicy food because I've been eating so much spicy food, so I can't tell you much about how it tasted, but I was definitely satisfied after eating their Oh So Hot Ramen at the maximum spiciness level. Price is around $20 with tip and tax for the one bowl.

I really enjoyed this place because of the food and service. Pho was delicious. This location is in a great spot. I'm going to return here before a rangers game. Ooo the garlic oil stuff in the counter is spicy!

Our recent dining experience at this bustling restaurant on a busy Saturday evening at 7pm was surprisingly pleasant. Despite the crowd, my party of four was seated in about 10 minutes. The highlight of our meal was the seafood jungol, a harmonious blend of fresh seafood including succulent crab, tender squid, and juicy shrimp, all swimming in a rich, well-seasoned soup base that was delightfully palatable without excessive spiciness. Enhancing the experience was the thoughtful provision of a flame to keep our jungol warm throughout the meal. Complementing our entrée, the watermelon soju cocktail was a playful and refreshing choice, striking the perfect balance with ripe watermelon flavor and a gentle hint of alcohol. Overall, this restaurant delivered a memorable meal that I'd readily recommend.

Calling all Pizza lovers. We stopped in for a quick bite for lunch. The Pasta Lovers is a nice big & clean Restaurant with a nice bar. The Bartender which was also our server was extremely helpful & honest. Pizza was perfectly cooked & delicious. I'm looking forward to trying the Pasta in the future visit.

I've been dying to go here! It's a very small restaurant with tight seating. I went with my fiancé, sister and cousin. Luckily we were seated right away because I made a reservation but it was really  tight. We ordered a cheese appetizer, the tuna tartine, the Havana sandwich and the steak for 2 and shared I amongst us 4. We also ordered a bottle of the Riesling. They cut everything into 4 pieces for us which was really nice. It was a perfect amount of food. We ordered the black truffle cheese on top of our raclette steak and it was absolutely delicious. We took a video but I can't upload it. I wish they added a little more black truffle cheese, especially because it's an $4 up charge for that cheese. We ended up paying $54 a person with tip. If you're a cheese lover, I'd definitely recommend going here but make sure you make a reservation!!

While at Chelsea Market we found ourselves in a quandary on what to eat.   So much to see and eat there.  There's a taco place:  Did I come all the way from LA to have tacos?   I guess it would be a thing to compare and contrast.   And the price is right... about $4 per taco.  We ordered 2 carne asada, 1 adobada, and 1 asada quesadilla.   After you order you hand your ticket to one of the guys down the line to complete your order.   You stay and watch and wait for your guy to finish your order.  Then you're challenged to find a spot to eat.  We found a stand up table along the main corridor.  When we were all settled down.  We dug in.  It was all very good.  How does it compare with LA?   I have to say it was up there.  - Lots of flavorful meat.    They don't skimp - only 1 tortillas.   LA, they double up the tortillas and try to fill you up that way.  Yay for only 1 tortilla.  - Avocado sauce.  Come on every tacoThe adobada is OK...it's the Carne Asada is where it's at. I would skip the 'quesadilla' really not worth it. I do recommend Los Tacos #1, even if you're from LA.

Really good food. I'll bring my appetite next time I go. Got to the neighborhood early to see a friend play at the Rockwood. So a little spare time, a little bit hungry and a quick Yelp search, and I found myself at El Sombrero. Standard cafe look, tables, a bar, a huge TV. Nothing fancy. But it's the Lower East Side, you expect funky, and it's Mexican so I suppose the cantina look is intentional. The music was really good. Like, college radio station good. It took me a little while to realize it was all in Spanish. So double bonus value there. A very polite waiter seated me promptly, it was around 6:30, there were only 4 other customers. He answered my questions very helpfully. In about five minutes I had my food. 3 small churrasco tacos (marinated skirt steak).  Delicious and tender, and a generous amount of steak for an appetizer. Tasty sauces, a mild red and a tasty green salsa. (None of that 3-alarm habanero huatchalez sauce like they have at other places.) My only complaint: I was disappointed that I didn't get any chips and salsa. With a soda it came to $15 bucks. Based on tonight's enjoyable snack, I'll be back next time I'm in the neighborhood. You should check them out too, I know Mexican food and El Sombrero has it right. Attention Management: your sign -- the hat -- it's a Fedora. I'm sorry, I hate to complain, but it's not a sombrero. It's a Fedora. The guy who sold you the sign scammed you.

On a brisk afternoon in midtown, I stumbled upon Chirp, a cozy eatery I'd yet to try. The spot, albeit small with a predominance of takeout orders, had a warmth to it. Perusing the menu brimming with Peruvian fare, I settled on the tempting combo deal: a juicy quarter chicken with sweet plantains and pinto beans on the side.

The service was prompt; my name was called shortly, and I was presented with a hearty, flavorful meal. The chicken was succulent, perfectly complemented by the delightful sweetness of the plantains. While the beans were on the saltier side, they might suit others' palates well. Beyond hot dishes, Chirp also offers a selection of sandwiches, salads, and rice bowls.

Eco-conscious and satisfying, my meal was served in paper-based bowls and cups. An excellent, fulfilling dining experience—Chirp is on my list for a repeat visit, and I'd recommend it to those seeking a touch of Peruvian warmth on a cold day.

We enjoyed this restaurant for it's nice decor, great location and pretty good food. While we didn't get the pizza, we did get three appetizers and mains for everyone. The sushito peppers were pretty nicely roasted and came with some glazed tomatoes. We also got the tuna tartare which had a good flavor, but a weird color. Truffle Mac and cheese balls were crunchy and flavorful but broke apart, signaling that the macaroni The fish was fantastic, and expertly fillet'd. Pasta was excellent and tasted homemade! I'm taking off a star because it seemed most dishes had a flaw to it. Also, the service was kind of slow and the place kind of empty, leaving a weird kind of vibe.

Mainly giving this place two stars because the tortillas fall apart too quickly. After 1-2 bites you will need a plate and a fork.  Came here for the endless brunch and tacos.  The al pastor taco is tasty but some pieces were n the dry side.  The chicken schwarma taco doesn't look pretty but is actually tasty.  Also tried the breakfast taco that was mostly ok.Not sure about the standard menu pricing given that I ate 7 tacos which would of been crazy expensive if not for the endless taco deal.

I really loved this place when I visited New York. The line was fairly fast, productivity within in their shop efficient, and the food just out of this world! I've seen many foodies and food blogs recommend this place and it definitely did not disappoint - only $4.50 for a small BBQ pork rice container packed with plenty juicy and fatty meat, cabbage, and rice. So flavorful and satisfying. I grew up eating BBQ pork as it's part of my cultures most favorite foods so I definitely had high standards and expectations going into this experience. I am happy to report that it did not disappoint. I've been searching all over the US for decent ish BBQ pork as the ones in Hong Kong are just so much better...and though the pork is still slightly better in HK the taste, fattiness, and flavor was definitely darn near close at Wah Fung! I wish they had this in LA but will definitely be visiting this place every time I come to NY from now on

Title: A Slice Above the Rest!

From the moment you step into this pizza haven, you're greeted with service that's just as exceptional as the fare they offer. While some might balk at the price of $4.50 per slice, every bite of the chewy, perfectly charred crust assures you that it’s a premium experience worth every penny. Their pepperoni pizza, in particular, is a masterpiece of flavor with its abundance of curly pepperonis and a generous blanket of melted cheese.

The standout feature, however, is the establishment's heartwarming management. My late evening visit, a mere 15 minutes before closing, was met not with rushed indifference but with unexpected generosity, as the manager (or owner) kindly gifted me an extra slice of pizza— a small act that left a lasting impression.

If you've got a pizza craving, this spot doesn't just satisfy it; they elevate it. Wholeheartedly recommended!

During a recent excursion into a new neighborhood in NYC, I stumbled upon a quaint Thai spot with a sterling reputation. Opting for the green chicken curry, I braved the heat and was rewarded with an extraordinarily flavorful experience, complemented by perfectly cooked eggplant and fresh veggies. Additionally, the crab rangoon was a delightful treat, while the complimentary dumplings from a Yelp check-in proved to be a delectable new discovery. The restaurant certainly made a fan out of me, and I'd recommend it to anyone looking to expand their culinary horizons.

The gooey cheese makes for a pretty interesting photo, but from our perspective, the cheese, in this otherwise perfectly reasonable Korean noodle dish, was just an afterthought. It doesn't add anything to the dish at all.Our fried chicken was also cooked well, but nothing to write home about. The restaurant is located on the 2nd floor, overlooking Koreatown- quite a nice view. But the barrel chairs are uncomfortable for old people like me.Otherwise, service was decent and the ambiance inviting. It was just the food that didn't really excite us.

Title: Great Food, Lackluster Service at Local Spot

Review:
I ventured into this restaurant with high hopes, drawn by the promise of authentic, homemade cuisine, and in that regard, it did not disappoint. The dim sum selections were impressive—each dish I tried, I liked, particularly the lobster spring roll and the turnip shortbread. Do yourself a favor and order the soup dumplings; their flavor profile is exceptional.

However, the dining experience was marred by service that was, frankly, subpar. From the moment we were seated, it was a struggle to capture our waiter's attention, and our initial order was delayed as we were overlooked in favor of other guests. Efforts to request a simple ice water were met with apparent disregard, and an order for soup dumplings had to be repeated and was ultimately forgotten.

Despite the delicious food and reasonable prices, the indifference shown by the staff casts a shadow over the overall experience. I can only hope that the service will catch up with the high quality of the dishes—if so, this place would be a true gem.

Title: Flavorful Dining on a Budget with a Side of Patience

Review:

My recent visit to this restaurant was largely a delightful experience. The establishment truly shines with its culinary offerings – each dish was a vibrant parade of flavors, generously portioned to provide not just a meal but a feast. The affordability of these delectable meals was the cherry on top, making it an accessible option for those seeking quality without breaking the bank.

However, the dining experience did hit a snag when it came to service. With only one waitress juggling both floor service and takeout orders, attentiveness suffered, resulting in a slower pace of service than preferred. We found ourselves having to gently prompt her for the check a couple of times.

A hot tip for prospective diners: use Yelp to check in and receive a complimentary appetizer. We opted for the chicken dumplings, which were an absolute treat and kicked off our meal beautifully.

In summary, if you're not in a rush and have the time to savor both the food and the dining experience, this restaurant delivers excellent value. Patience will be rewarded with a satisfying meal that doesn't empty your wallet.

I came here for lunch while doing a business around the area. I just happened to walk pass it because I got hungry right around lunch time. Curious to find out more about this place. It's a place that you order by the counter and wait for your number and then you sit and eat there or take to go. There're quite a lot of tables including high tables. The wait for each order is about 5-10 mins. After getting my order, I sat by the window at a regular small table. I declare that cousins make very good lobster rolls! I finished the pickle and coleslaw too. In addition to that, they sell some macaroni and crab cake in a box to take home and heat up yourself at home. Feeling lazy? That's a box for that! Nice! The service was very good too.

Restaurant Week Summer 2019- Owned and operated by the same company as Park Avenue and Smith & Wollensky - Yet their quality in food differs SO MUCH- We wanted to explore steakhouses/chophouses in the area so we made a reservation online- We noticed a much older crowd in the restaurant- Warm pretzel sticks to start- Got the seared diver scallops, jumbo shrimp cocktail, nueske's bacon, pork chop, roast chicken, filet mignon, coconut cake, chocolate pudding, assorted sorbets- The ONLY thing we enjoyed was the scallops- The bacon was also ok. Everything else could have had more flavor or better texture.- The filet mignon comes out charred. They serve it that way; just a heads up. - I think we were most disappointed with the roasted chicken...how does one get that wrong? - Safe to say I won't be coming back

Be warned : raw chicken, uncooked meat being served! I got a piece of uncooked chicken in my sandwich here today. I really hope I don't get sick... it's a chicken cutlet how hard can it be to make sure it's thoroughly cooked.

My fiancé and I celebrated New Year's Eve at this charming restaurant, indulging in their prix fixe menu at $88 per person. We started with the Montauk scallops, which were a highlight due to their freshness and tender, flavorful taste—I couldn't resist stealing a few more from my partner!

Next, the warm, gooey ham and cheese dish did not disappoint, providing a comforting segue into the main course. I ordered the prime rib, which typically arrives on the rarer side, but I prefer mine more cooked. The server was incredibly accommodating and ensured that my prime rib returned cooked to my liking—perfectly done.

The meal concluded on a high note with a dessert of chocolate cake paired with ice cream and sweet, delicious chestnuts—a combination that was simply irresistible.

Throughout our dinner, the service was impeccable. My water glass remained full without a single prompt, and the staff's attentiveness meant we never had to search for assistance. It was a wonderful dining experience that only heightened our festive celebrations.

Title: A Sushi Lover's Dream at [Restaurant Name]

My experience at [Restaurant Name] was nothing short of extraordinary, with the highlight being their lunch Omakase priced at a reasonable $47. The option to enhance the meal with high-grade Jyunmai Daiginyo sake and lavish additions like extra toro, uni, and ikura sent the experience over the top – an indulgence well worth the cost.

The sushi was a display of culinary artistry, each piece a testament to the chef's meticulous and passionate preparation. The extra-thick toro stood out, masterfully sliced and elegantly draped over the rice – a memorable morsel that left a lasting impression.

As a bonus, booking through Seated afforded me a generous 19% reward gift, further sweetening the already delightful visit. This restaurant is a triple-threat with its exceptional food, value, and rewards. It's an absolute must-visit for any sushi connoisseur.

Title: A Flavorful Bite at Kobeyaki

Having walked by Kobeyaki countless times without a second thought, I finally decided to give it a try on a friend's suggestion. My lunch visit at 1pm beat the rush, but shortly after placing my order, the place was bustling with a hungry crowd.

The wait for my food was brief, about 5-10 minutes, and I had the chance to dive into their spicy tuna burger. While the burger's taste was satisfying, I was a tad disappointed by the patty's slim portion - the tuna was overshadowed by an abundance of bread and cabbage. However, the wasabi mayo on the burger was a fiery delight, even for someone accustomed to spicy foods.

An added bonus was their sauce station, which included tasty options like spicy mayo, wasabi mayo, and teriyaki ketchup. Despite the letdown in the burger's size, the flavors and quality were undeniable. I left with plans to return and explore more of what Kobeyaki has to offer.

This hidden gem was recommended to me by a friend. The ramen was delicious and was just what I was looking for. It had no frills and was a great lunch. It was reasonably priced as well. The inside is intimate and quaint. The service was great as our waitress was very attentive and personable. I would definitely go back on my next trip back to New York.

I recently tried a restaurant with a unique concept where every dish transports diners to a different part of Asia through their bowls. The Seoul and Manila bowls were my picks, both offering a satisfying flavor experience. Generous portion sizes and a hearty serving of protein left me impressed. While some might find the sauces on the stronger, saltier side, I personally enjoyed how they complemented the white rice. Although I've only experienced their takeout, the space itself is cozy enough to seat 25-30 patrons comfortably.

Title: A BLT Like No Other at Smith's

If there was a BLT hall of fame, Smith's would take the crown for serving the most delectable one I've ever encountered in the bustling streets of New York. For a mere $13, you're presented with a bacon-laden masterpiece, a generous portion that justifies every penny. The beer, a steal at $4, is the perfect companion to this lunchtime delight.

The bread is the unsung hero here - perfectly toasted to achieve a crispy texture without the heft, making it an unexpectedly light choice. As for the salad, it's a fresh reprieve from the richness of the sandwich. The spring greens are crisp, and the finely diced veggies are a testament to the attention paid to the small details.

In short, Smith's has crafted a BLT that transcends the ordinary, making it an essential experience for any sandwich aficionado in the city. Yummy indeed, and a sincere thanks to Smith's for elevating a classic!

Title: A Pleasant Surprise!

I stumbled upon a gem of a restaurant and I'm thrilled to share my experience. The ambiance immediately strikes a charming balance, making it perfect for a night out with friends, a peaceful solo meal, or a romantic date. It's also family-friendly, welcoming diners of all ages with open arms. The food was truly delightful, each dish bursting with flavor. Impressed by the overall experience, I am eagerly looking forward to my next visit!

I love coming to this place to lightly study. There are small tables and couches everywhere which makes it such a comfy place to do some reading. The food here is a bit expensive so I've only ever had the coffee ($~3) and espresso drinks ($4-6). I usually get the mocha, dirty chai, or latte. The mocha isn't sweet which I really like. It's a bit hard to flag down the waitress sometimes, especially since it can get crowded and loud during mealtimes and happy hour. There are so many nice couches and little table nooks to hide for a quiet afternoon though. I've also been here for dessert and drinks. Drinks are normal price for new york, around $6-10 for beer/wine. The desserts are great though! My friend and I got a chocolate mousse cake and lemon tart to share. Both came out beautifully decorated and did not disappoint.

Title: My Impressive First Taste of Japanese BBQ at Gyukaku

I recently had my first Japanese BBQ experience at Gyukaku, and it certainly left a great impression. The restaurant's interior stood out with its cozy booth seating, high ceilings, and an inviting view of the street from the second-floor vantage point.

Though they offered a $55 happy hour lunch special suitable for two, my companion and I indulged in the premium lunch set at $75. The set reminded me of Korean BBQ yet stood out with its distinctly seasoned meats, which set it apart from the usual offerings.

A highlight was the salmon appetizer—simply delicious. We wrapped up our meal with a DIY s'mores dessert, which added a playful touch to the dining experience.

Gyukaku provides the perfect ambiance for a romantic date or a leisurely meal with a friend. Would recommend for anyone looking to try Japanese BBQ with an added touch of sophistication.

Modern and super clean! You're greeted with all smiles and friendliness. There's a soft drink fountain! Good selection of veggies (found a friend in one of our veggies plate tho) and noodles (way too many to choose from actually, but more variety to cater to non-Asians). Good selection different types of fish balls (I only wish they have the other kind of fish roe balls :( )Broths were bland as any other places but the trick is to go to the sauce bar, take a bunch of garlic, herbs, some sauces and dump that into your broth, boom, life changing.And they didn't have SACHA SAUCE LIKE WHAT

Ichiran Ramen offers a distinctive dining experience with its alley-like setup and private booths that add an element of novelty. The singular focus on tonkotsu ramen, priced at $18.90, is noteworthy—although on the steeper side, it justifies the cost with quality and the option for customization. Patrons can tweak everything from the richness of the broth to the noodle firmness, ensuring a personalized bowl. Do take advantage of the complimentary extra noodle serving and don't shy away from their signature red sauce; a level 5 spice offers a flavorful enhancement without overwhelming heat. The ramen itself strikes a harmonious balance of simplicity and taste, and the clean broth is a pleasant deviation from the usual post-ramen thirst. In summary, Ichiran serves up a delightful and tailored ramen experience that’s worth a visit.

Review is based on Happy Hour drinks only.Located in the vicinity of Times Square, Social serves as a convenient pit stop for pre-theater bites, happy hour (until 8 p.m.) or a relaxed pub dinner (or lunch/appetizers).I arrived before my friend and got started with a decent cabernet sauvignon. At $6, it was pretty good and I people watched/listened to the good (danceable) music as I drank.It quickly got packed once my friend arrived. She ordered a Pinot Grigio and pours were very generous.Some of the food, although standard pub fare, looked good as it was being served to other patrons. Like most pubs, seating was available at the bar, cocktail tables near the bar or in the back.We didn't stay very long but I enjoyed the atmosphere, music and wine offering a neighborhood like feel to it.Not a bad place to stumble upon.

Great Brunch spot that's nestled in the W VillageI actually made reservations here thinking it was another restaurant, but it was a pleasant mistake. For our brunch, we went with the $44 bottomless brunch (1.5 hrs) option. For NYC, a $44 bottomless brunch is a bit high because most places have them for about $35, but YOLO. I found the restaurant to be pretty cozy with a B&B/country cottage type of vibe. Our server Sarah was pretty awesome by making great recommendations and keeping out glasses full of Bloody Marys. Actually, she recommended the Bloody Mary over the bellini, mimosa, and sangria. She even gave us a 15 min notice that our bottomless drinks were almost over. I had the duck eggs Benedict, which was way better than I expected, and my friend really enjoyed her breakfast burger. The restaurant was pretty popular, but not so popular that one cannot make a reservation a day in advance. I noticed that a few walk-ins were turned away for brunch, so it's best to make reservations just to be safe.

Title: Cozy Weeknight Delight at [Restaurant Name]

Last week, my friends and I decided to visit [Restaurant Name] for a low-key dinner around 7:30 PM. To our pleasure, the place was comfortably bustling without being overcrowded.

I indulged in the 'Plato Julia,' featuring a succulent ribeye steak accompanied by a delightful mix of beans, rice, salad, and avocado. Each element of the dish was expertly seasoned, reminding me of an upscale Chipotle bowl but with a gourmet twist.

The passion fruit margarita was a hit – a perfect balance of fruity flavors with a kick of strength that didn't overpower. It was the ideal complement to the delicious meal.

In short, [Restaurant Name] served up not just a fantastic dining experience, but also the perfect backdrop for an evening with the girls. I'm already looking forward to our next visit.

I recently visited this restaurant for a work dinner and was enchanted by the unique experience of dining in a rotating venue, offering ever-changing vistas that captivated me throughout the evening. It's a brilliant concept that adds a touch of excitement to the meal.

The drinks served here pack a punch, which I thoroughly enjoyed. On to the meal, diners are presented with a three-course selection. My appetizer choice, the Wild Mushroom Ravioli, fell short on robustness, needing an extra sprinkle of salt to enhance the taste, despite the promise of truffle honey.

My main course was the Crispy Skinned Atlantic Salmon, which was well-cooked but, much like the ravioli, was in need of a flavor boost – I found myself reaching for the salt again. Dessert was a chocolate creation that I could only nibble on due to feeling quite full. It was satisfactory, but didn't leave a memorable impression.

While the rotating view is a dazzling touch, the food's lack of flavor means I'm unlikely to return for a full meal. I'd consider coming back for the strong drinks and the novelty of the setting but not for the cuisine. It's a solid 3 out of 5 for me.

We stumbled into the restaurant by chance and were pleasantly surprised. The portions served were generous, and the flavors across all dishes were quite enjoyable. Our only slight disappointment was the scarcity of salted fish, a personal favorite, in the dish that featured it. Overall, a satisfying experience with a small note for salted fish enthusiasts.

Still had a surprisingly long line at 2pm on a Saturday afternoon, but so worth on a chilly day. The broth is so good when it's piping hot. $25 is pretty pricey for a bowl of ramen (esp when it's $7 in Japan!!!!!)

Title: Cozy Trattoria with Room for Service Improvement

Located in the heart of Little Italy, this quaint trattoria truly hits the mark with its authentic Italian cuisine. The veal francaise stood out, tantalizing the palate with its soft, savory flavors. A fresh caprese salad with remarkably fresh cheese makes for a satisfying beginning, while the hot antipasto—boasting a delightful mix of eggplant parmigiana, succulent shrimp, and juicy mussels—was an absolute must-try.

Capping off the meal, the espresso served with a sugar stick provided a perfect, delectable finish. However, it's worth noting that the dining experience was slightly marred by the lackluster service. The staff seemed preoccupied with their conversations, resulting in a need for repeated attempts to capture their attention.

In all, while the food was a delightful homage to Italian cuisine, the service did not quite match up, leaving me to rate this charming spot with 3 out of 5 stars.

I recently visited a unique restaurant for a business lunch, located in a more secluded area opposite the bustling food court in Grand Central. The dining atmosphere was a curious blend of grandeur, with its majestic, tiled arched ceiling, and casualness, reminiscent of a diner with picnic-style tablecloths - an odd, almost conflicting combination.

The service was somewhat attentive, though it felt like they were pushing appetizers on us and neglected to offer soda refills. The menu prices were on the higher side, with main dishes ranging between $30-$50. Three of my colleagues opted for the Bouillabaisse, which was ample and filled with a generous amount of fish, despite the labor-intensive lobster claw. In contrast, my choice, the 'cajun grilled' Grouper, was a letdown. At $35, the portion was notably smaller, and the flavor was sorely lacking – no spice, no salt, just plain bland.

Considering the peculiar ambiance, the steep pricing, and the overall underwhelming food and service, I don't foresee a return visit, especially not for business lunches where impressions are everything.

I was originally planning on ordering something and taking it to go, but I loved the ambiance here so I stayed! It's spacious in terms of nyc standards and there's nice details in terms of the finishing such as comfortable pillows. I had S5- stir fried squid (spicy). I had it as a noodle soup. It was $15 but the seafood was the most expensive. I did see other things on the menu in a $11-13 price range too. I highly recommend this place! The flavor bursts out at you and the spiciness packs a punch. I like the fresh mini red chilis that were used in it. The noodle soup is a great option and I recommend it. The portion size was pretty big and I started feeling full half way through even. There is a generous amount of vegetables and also a wide variety of them. The squid was delicious. I would definitely return here!

Title: Trendy Brunch Haven with a Green Thumb

This brunch spot reels you in with its undeniable charm, featuring neon signs that pop against a lush backdrop of greenery. It’s a hit amongst the locals and beyond, so a bit of patience is required due to the bustling crowd. The avocado toast, topped with perfectly poached eggs and crispy bacon, was a delight, though it comes with a trendy price tag to match the ambiance. While it's on the pricier side, it's worth a visit for a dose of cute, contemporary brunch vibes.

Title: A Rocky Start Saved by Superior Cuisine

My recent dining experience at the restaurant began on an uneven note due to a hiccup with my OpenTable reservation not being recognized, despite the evidence on my phone and plenty of open seats at 6:30 pm on a Sunday. The staff failed to offer an explanation for this oversight, which was slightly disappointing.

However, the food was a redeeming feature and undoubtedly garnered a well-deserved 5-star rating. The lychee martini, with its potent vodka punch and subtle lychee undertone, was delightful, although it took an unexpectedly long 20 minutes to arrive in a not-so-busy setting.

The Vada Pao's starchy nature was a bit overwhelming for my taste; however, the buttery bread was a decadent touch. In contrast, the Chicken Tikka Masala was exceptional - tender, moist chicken smothered in a sauce so divine I yearned to have it as a separate dip for the naan. Speaking of which, the Garlic Naan didn't disappoint, delivering a powerful garlicky experience I cherished.

The Kadai Goat, a serendipitous choice inspired by a New York Times review, proved to be a hit, provided you don't mind meat on the bone. Although service could use a tune-up, earning a fair 3.5 stars, the culinary delights have ensured my return. Next time, I'm there for the food, with hopes for smoother service.

Title: Authentic Italian Vibes at a Bustling NYC Pizzeria

Review:
Whenever I'm in New York, I make a beeline for this pizza haven! A mere 15-minute wait is a small price to pay for what I dare say is some of the city's finest pizza. It's a hotspot, especially around lunch and dinner, so early birds definitely get the worm here.

Stepping inside, you're instantly transported to Italy with its authentic décor. And don't be deceived by the initial view; a spacious seating area awaits beyond the kitchen.

My go-to order never changes: a pepperoni pizza with an extra helping of pepperoni. What sets this place apart is their fresh, perfectly thin pizza with a crust that strikes the ideal balance between crispy and chewy. It's an absolute must-visit for any pizza aficionado in the Big Apple!

Title: A Seafood Feast to Remember

My recent dining experience at this restaurant was nothing short of impressive. True to their promise, the freshness of the seafood was unmissable, and the quality of preparation left us without any reasons to find fault.

The appetizers were a hit, with each dish leaving our plates spotless. I have to give special nods to the Spanish Octopus and the Crab Cake – both were exceptionally delightful. My main course, the special Dover Sole, though on the pricier side and without accompaniments, was de-boned with finesse at the table and was a savory treat.

The seasoning of all dishes, including the succulent Bone in Ribeye, was perfectly balanced and enhanced the natural flavors superbly. Our evening concluded on a sweet note with shared desserts; the Chocolate Cake, Creme Brulee, and Key Lime Tart were simply divine. And the complimentary Creme Brulee via a Yelp check-in was a pleasant bonus.

Even with a busy Friday night crowd, our table of five received efficient service, allowing us to enjoy our meal amidst laughter and good conversation.

In summary, if you're looking for exceptionally fresh seafood and a delightful dining experience, I highly recommend paying this restaurant a visit. It's a decision your palate will thank you for.

This is regarding the Mealpal pickup experience today.  The General Manager of this establishment, Sam, had an attitude toward me when I told her that the Mealpal photo today showed kale instead of the chickpeas she chose to replace it with because they ran out of kale.  I had the chickpeas from here and it tastes heavily of cumin, to which I'm allergic.  Sam acted like she did me a favor and gave me double squash instead.  I would not have chosen this mealpal if I had known that they were going to give me chickpeas.  As you can see from the photo, it shows kale.  Don't act like you are doing me a favor when I paid for the meal.

Cookshop truly stands out as an exceptional brunch destination in the city, effortlessly accommodating diners even during the Sunday morning rush. The staff's professionalism contributes to a well-oiled dining experience. With an extensive menu that caters to various brunch preferences, food lovers will delight in the tasty offerings, from fresh greens and revitalizing juices to hearty egg dishes. It's a top pick for anyone looking to satisfy their adventurous brunch cravings.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Koreatown's K BBQ Spot

If you're on the hunt for flavorful Korean BBQ without the frills in Koreatown, this may be your spot. Priced moderately, the restaurant offers tasty and tender meats that will satisfy your K BBQ cravings. However, if the dining experience is as important to you as the food itself, you might want to look elsewhere.

Service here is brisk and lacks the personal touch. Don't expect any guidance through the menu or an introduction to Korean BBQ if you're a newbie. Our attempt to dive into the cooking process was quickly shut down by staff, indicating that self-cooking isn't really on the menu.

Despite the lack of interaction, the meat's quality almost makes up for the service gaps, and a surprisingly sweet cinnamon drink provided a delightful end to the meal. This place might be worth a visit for the K BBQ itself, but if you're seeking a full Korean culinary journey with attentive service, you'll have to keep looking.

Good but....We came here for restaurant week and the place was hoping. Service was incredible and the drinks strong !We had the artichokes Chaat and octopus app- they were both delicious ...and the entrees just didn't hold a candle to the apps. Mango cod was good but lacking some oomph and the banana leaf chicken was bland compared to the apps and the deal. The dal was probably the best I have ever had. So creamyDesserts were uninspiring ~ I wanted to give Rahi another star but the entrees and dessert were just lacking

Title: A Mixed Bag with Tasty Rewards

My experience at this eatery has been inconsistent, swinging from speedy, satisfactory service to frustrating waits of up to 30 minutes, leaving me puzzled as other patrons seemingly leapfrog the queue. However, one constant remains: the food itself is reliably delicious. The Guac Burger Combo, paired with Sweet Potato Fries, is my go-to — a hearty, messy endeavor that necessitates a fork or a table. These fries outshine their regular counterparts, which I've found to often be served cold. A pro tip: use the app to order ahead and bypass the wait, or dodge the lunch rush by arriving slightly before noon. Despite the service hiccups, the quality of the salads and burgers has me coming back for more.

Title: Exquisite Indian Cuisine and Stellar Service at Ashoka

My dining experience at Ashoka on a serene Tuesday afternoon was unforgettable. Craving Indian flavors, my friend and I decided to dive into the restaurant's lunch special—a sumptuous all-you-can-eat affair for $13.95. Though the 20% Yelp discount doesn't apply here, the value is undeniable.

The ambiance of Ashoka is a blend of elegance and class, complemented by exceptional service that outshines many of its NYC counterparts. We savored an array of dishes, starting with appetizers like chicken tikka and another tasty chicken creation, followed by entrees including the creamy malai kofta and a flavorful chicken saag—though a note on the latter, the chunks of ginger felt somewhat out of place.

Our meal also included a vegetable side, lentils, an abundance of naan, and perfectly cooked rice, each dish leaving a lasting impression of bold and authentic taste. The attentiveness of the staff was unparalleled, with regular check-ins and gracious refills of our water glasses. They even surprised us with complimentary mango lassis, bursting with freshness, and a dessert that sweetly concluded our meal.

Ashoka is a jewel on the Upper East Side, especially for those eager to explore new tastes. The hope remains that their high standards of service will be maintained as their popularity inevitably grows. For an excellent lunch that delivers both in taste and hospitality, Ashoka stands tall as a highly commendable choice.

**Restaurant Review: A Late Valentine's Date**

My partner and I chose this restaurant for a belated Valentine's Day dinner, enticed by its promise of a cute and romantic atmosphere, which it delivered. The charm of the setting was, unfortunately, dimmed by service delays due to our waiter being the sole server on a busy holiday evening.

We opted for 3-course meals, and while the main dishes - my shrimp fettuccine and my partner's steak with yuca fries - were satisfactory, they lacked the anticipated Venezuelan flair, leaning more towards standard American fare. However, the yuca fries were admittedly irresistible.

Where the restaurant shined was in its appetizers, which showcased the Venezuelan influence we were craving. The arepas and tequeños came highly recommended and did not disappoint, though the calamari fell flat.

The wine selection added a nice touch, with my red wine being particularly enjoyable, though my partner's white wine was unremarkable.

In summary, while the experience was a mix of highs and lows, resulting in an average score of 3 stars, I see potential for improvement. With adjustments to the menu to highlight more Venezuelan cuisine and optimized staffing, I would gladly reconsider my rating. We're open to a return visit in the future to see how this establishment evolves.

Title: A Slice Above the Rest in NYC

For years, my quests for the quintessential New York style pizza left me with a taste of disappointment. However, my skepticism was turned upside down by a little gem I stumbled upon during a work trip. Despite my initial reservations, the irresistible garlic aroma wafting from the kitchen early in the morning sparked curiosity.

Come lunchtime, the bustle of devoted patrons and a vibrant array of pizzas, including 'Grandma's' varieties and classic thin-crust rounds, drew me in. The sight of familiar faces securing their "usuals" signaled I was in for a treat. My choice? A square of 'Grandma's Special' boasting spicy sausage, peppers, and onions.

Finally, the slice I was served met all my expectations - a crispy, firm crust supporting a flavorful, perfectly proportioned load of toppings. Gone were the woes of the soggy, underwhelming experiences of the past. Not only did I savor every mouthful, but I found myself eagerly returning the next day for more. It's rare to find a place that surpasses mere satisfaction and achieves pizza perfection, but this, my friends, is that rare find. A snapshot of my two slices on day two is a testament to my newfound loyalty. This isn’t just any pizza place; it’s a must-visit for anyone seeking the true taste of New York.

Title: A Hidden Gem by the Seaport!

Don't let the slightly derelict facade of this neighborhood haunt fool you; nestled by the old seaport fish market lies a culinary delight with a community feel that is second to none. The exterior, with its cracked windows and peculiar door (sans doorknob!), might perplex the uninitiated, but it's all part of the charm – a nod to a bygone era that locals in the know can navigate with ease.

Once inside, you're greeted by the camaraderie of the local bar scene, buzzing and vibrant, particularly during a riveting basketball game. The noise is part of the package, and it adds to the dive's authentic vibe, but if peace is what you seek, there are tables tucked away at the back, offering a quieter enclave for a catch-up with friends.

The food here is a standout. We heeded our friend's recommendations and dove into a feast of Mama's Chinese dishes – from the perfectly Crispy Fried Rice and slightly fiery Drunken Noodles to the standout Drunken Fish Soup and lip-smacking Ginger Fried Chicken Wings. Each dish was meant for sharing, creating a convivial dining experience. Though the menu boasts regular bar fare and seafood options, Mama's specials are not to be missed.

Prices are reasonable, and the service strikes the right balance of attentive and laid-back – there when you need it but giving you space to enjoy your meal. Our server was exceptional, ensuring our comfort without being overly intrusive.

This spot may test your entry skills and challenge your initial impressions, but once you're in, you're treated to a delightful experience. It's a testament to its charm that my friends and I lingered longer than planned, fully immersed in the welcoming atmosphere.

In summary, if you're searching for an authentic local bar with heartwarming food and character in spades, look no further. Just remember to brush up on your vintage entry techniques before you visit!

Despite its unassuming exterior and slightly worn-down interior complete with ripped seats, this restaurant turned out to be a delightful find. The staff exuded warmth and attentiveness, ensuring our food arrived promptly and exactly as ordered. I indulged in a simple yet delicious egg and bacon sandwich on a roll, while my companions eagerly devoured a pastrami omelet and the meatball hero special—both plates wiped clean, a testament to their satisfaction. The cherry on top was the affordability of the meal. This place is a hidden gem for those who prioritize substance over style. Absolute score!

Double Zero - How am I just trying this place?! It exceeded our expectations by far. We ordered through Caviar and it came incredibly quickly and well intact for take out. For 2 we ordered Margarita pizza, Ciao e pepe & Meatballs. It was more than enough food, all good but our favorites being the pizza and pasta. Would order again in a heartbeat.

After hearing a lot of friends talk about this place, I came here on a Friday night for dinner. I sat at the bar where I got a cider with spaghetti and meatballs. Everyone talks about how good their meatballs are. I, on the other hand, thought they were fine. To me, there was nothing special about them. For $22, the portion size was not great. All in all, the place is fine. Nothing really special about it. Note: This review is brought to you by an Italian guy from Bay Ridge, Brooklyn so I am tough critic when it comes to Italian food.

From the moment we walked in, the service at this restaurant was nothing short of attentive. The cleanliness of the establishment was immediately noticeable, setting a pleasant atmosphere for our dining experience.

The star of the show, of course, was the food. We indulged in a barbecue feast that can only be described as a carnivore's dream. The selection included succulent pork belly, perfectly cooked beef fillet, flavorful black pepper beef, aromatic curry chicken, juicy shrimp, tender squid, and hearty short ribs. The inclusion of grilled asparagus and corn added a nice touch of greens and rounded out our meal.

The variety of sauces available was a delight, adding personalized twists to each dish. With such an array of choices, every bite was as unique as it was delicious.

We concluded our meal feeling both satisfied and impressively stuffed. It's safe to say that this dining experience ticked all the boxes for excellent service, hygiene, and outstanding food. I would wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a top-notch BBQ meal.

Title: Buzzing Happy Hour Haven with Room for Improvement

Just popped into this bustling eatery for a happy hour venture and I'm inclined to say it's a snug, yet solid choice, particularly commendable for those who relish brunch and a good bottomless drink special. The ambiance suggests that making a reservation via the Yelp app is a smart move to avoid the close-quarters squeeze.

My taste buds were taken on a joy ride with the Chicken Tinga taco, each bite packed with flavor, and the Baja Fish taco that truly lived up to its hype. Complementing these were the delectable sides – fried plantains, chipotle slaw, and grilled corn dusted with cayenne and adorned with cotija cheese, all of which you can snag at a bargain (3 sides for $9).

They also serve up a deal that's hard to pass: 3 tacos and a Mexican beer for a neat $15, perfect for a laid-back evening with a friend. However, there's room for a few tweaks. The Pork Belly taco fell short, pun intended, with a piece of pork that barely registered amidst the other ingredients. Also, the organic margarita exclusion from the happy hour deal was a bit of a letdown, and the lack of clarity on margarita options could befuddle some.

In summary, if you find yourself downstairs off the street at this spot, you're in for a treat, mostly. Just keep an eye on the menu and your happy hour expectations in check.

I came here for 2019 NYC Summer Restaurant Week, and it was a great first meal to kick off Restaurant Week! First off, the restaurant is impressively large. There's a lower level with private dining rooms and bathrooms, and the upper level is open and expansive. Side note: I also loved the huge entrance door (although it is a bit heavy). I have to say the service was wonderful. We had a main server, but throughout the night, there were so many people helping to refill our glasses, swipe away crumbs, pull out/push our chairs back in after we returned from the restroom, and serve our dishes. They were so attentive and would always check to make sure we were satisfied with our course. I appreciate that when most restaurants advertise themselves as Mediterranean, usually the dishes are heavily Greek. What impressed me about Boulud Sud is that they had Moroccan dishes as well (like tagine!). We started with olive oil and a variety of wine. I ordered a glass of the white wine, the salmon as the starter, cavatelli as my main, and the caffé e latte as my dessert. The salmon was beautiful and tasted quite fresh (the slices were nice and thin). The cavatelli was also delicious (although the lamb dish looked tasty as well)--after this course I started feeling pretty full. The dessert was my favorite; the chocolate marquise was divine! When we received the bill, our server gave us three small treats (I could catch what the name was but I believe white chocolate was an ingredient). I would return!

I am not sure how I've been working per diem in the building right across the street from Omar's for the past two years and did not know they ever existed! My review is for lunchtime take away only...We had a break between patients and two of my coworkers were headed out for lunch, overheard my laments about being hungry and invited me along. They filled me in on how good the food is and that I would not be disappointed. I was stoked to learn the restaurant is a two minute walk from our office. I'm not gonna lie though, the line for lunch had me shook; it was looooongggg but the girls assured me not to worry because the line moves fast and they did not lie.I ordered their lamb adana platter ($12 bucks!) which came with two large pieces of spicy grilled lamb patties, two choices of sides (4 falafel & tabouli for me), a side salad, warm pita, three sauces and a free piece of baklava! The food is bomb! The garlicky sauce they give you is good enough to ask for an extra. There is most definitely no worry that anything has been sitting for too long because I think I saw them replace just the hummus two times over in my twenty minute stay in the restaurant (I'm exaggerating but the turnover is real). The food is super fresh and plentiful. I ate it all because I was starved but you could definitely split the serving into two lunches.I'm definitely going to come back here. The staff is very efficient so don't let the line scare you. Our guy in the front who put together our orders was the best and I wish I got his name. I just know I'll be going back to him every time I visit. Even if you spent 20 minutes to cummute to Omar's, you'll still have time to pick up your food and get back to work before your lunch hour is over. I may even grab a few lunches to take home for dinner one of the days I work in the city, I the future.

I was surprised at how much I liked this place. At first sight EN seems like an elevated "fusion" situation, but the beautiful, modern space and fine dining-esque service do not take away from the star of the restaurant - an authentic and thoughtfully curated menu, executed with an intense level of integrity. Some dishes I really enjoyed: mushroom in soy milk, flounder karaage (comes with a mountain of scallion and delicious dipping sauce), fried chicken (maybe the best I've had in my LIFE, so juicy/soft and unlike regular karaage at all), miso black cod (the texture is like cream), and sizzling wagyu (totally worth it). Great sake list too.Most of the dishes are very shareable in portion, so the prices are not too bad if you come with a group.I could tell this place was legit when I saw two salarymen eating steak sashimi off a whole cow's rib cage - you don't see shit like this everyday.

I was born and raised in New York and the very best pizza is made in New York. In my personal view, what they sell in Chicago or is otherwise labeled Chicago Pizza is not pizza. Once you recognize that what you are eating is simply a different category of food, and not pizza, you can begin to enjoy it. While there are many good Chicago-style pizzas made in Chicago, some of the very best is being made at Emmett's. Each pie is made to order so it is fresh.  The crust is crisp and tasty and cheese and tomato sauce are plentiful. With a cold beer, it is a great meal.

The Restaurant at the Playboy Club  exceeded my expectation. Very classy and upscale venue.  We came here for the Friday Afterwork Event. There was no line to get in because we came on time.
