It was a great diverse crowd everyone will feel comfortable.  I love a great drink afterwork and this venue had great drinks and awesome bartenders with great personalities and they did a magnificent job. I loved my ice cold Prosecco. The DJ played a great mixture of everything. The crowd was having an awesome time and so was everyone in my group.The club had a separate area where you can sit and have dinner but you can order appetizers at the bar. This is absolutely a great spot to go to afterwork. All work and no Play is not good. Enjoy and live life to the fullest.

Title: A Slice Above the Rest – A Must-Visit for Pizza Connoisseurs

As a regular patron of this gem, I can consistently vouch for the delectable experience that is their pizza offerings. Before I dive into the flavors, a few practical tips: bring cash, as cards aren't accepted; don't bother calling ahead since reservations are off the table; and be ready to indulge in a full pie – slices aren't an option here. But believe me, you'll want the whole thing.

The star of the show is, without question, the pizza. Imagine a coal oven delivering the thinnest of crusts, coupled with a homemade sauce that's both rich and robust. The ability to craft your own topping masterpiece only adds to the allure. If you're feeling adventurous, the clam pie is a revelation – it’s the finest I've ever had and is a testament to the culinary prowess here.

While the establishment also operates as a full bar, the pizza is the real pull. It's worth noting, though, that such quality comes at a premium – the prices are on the higher end, but the flavors justify every penny.

My only quibble? The cheese distribution could be more uniform across the pie, ensuring each bite is as heavenly as the last. Despite that, this place remains a top-tier choice for anyone craving an exceptional pizza experience.

Looking for some great, reasonably priced, authentic Szechuan food close to where you work or live is rather difficult in this city. You're usually taking a long trek to Flushing or Chinatown which is really out of the way if you live Uptown Manhattan. Luckily there's a diamond in the rough right by Bryant Park. It's literally tucked away in this city, but I'm here to expose them. Trust me, it's that good.I came here with my gf after work on a weekday. I got there around 6pm and the place was somewhat busy. As the night went on, the restaurant was rather packed. They have a 2nd floor which was for large parties so there's plenty of space. The service is pretty good. Pretty much if you're looking up at them or simply wave them down, they'll come to assist.We ordered one appetizer and two entrees:Sliced Beef & Tripe w Peanuts & Chili - I personally love tripe and spicy food. Naturally I got this for the appetizer. Served cold, this dish is pretty simple, but pretty good. The spicy is not too overpowering and I personally think it's a good warm up for what's ahead.Hot & Spicy Bullfrogs - I never had fried frog legs so this was a first. It pretty much taste like chicken. A very unique dish with that nice kick to it. I'd highly recommended trying some good ole frog legs in your lifetime. If you tried alligator before, why not frogs? Also an FYI, like a chicken wing, there is bones...lots of them (not like a fish though).Chong Qing Whole Fish - The main event, their best seller, and I can see why. Besides the whole the nice sized fried Tilapia which is then nicely sliced in half, it's served with various other garnishes. Off the top of my head, there's bok choy, vermicelli noodles, beancurd, peanuts, potato, taro, and I think I covered everything. We got this less spicy so it was more bearable (secretly would have loved it to be spicier). For $40, this is a hell of a deal.Tired of reading yet? Good, my fingers are tired. Hope I helped you make some important life choices!

This was a tough rating. The staff is really nice and the food was decent, but I left discontent. Ordered guacamole. The portion was really good but kinda lacked some flavor. Maybe needed some salt and lime. Idk but wasn't in love with it. Ordered quesadilla that had black truffle. Omggg so good but so small. It was like size of my hand. I was still hungry and for $37 for sharing guacamole with quesadilla and a soda. Hmm i would rethink that

Honestly one of the best brunch experiences I've ever had! Came in yesterday with a friend and we both loved it here. The decor is super cute and themed well! There's lots of memorabilia and the atmosphere is super cozy as warm. Will say that it's a bit small of a place so definitely keep that in mind. It was also popping for a midday Wednesday which was super fun. We both got different coffees and super enjoyed them! I loved how they have both decaf and non dairy options for picky stomachs like me haha. The food itself was absolutely amazing. I got a shakshouka that was perfectly spiced. The eggs were also cooked to just the right amount of softness, and the Israeli salad that came with it wasn't too oily or salty. They also gave me bread which was crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside, with a delicious cream cheese to accompany it. My friend got the eggs siniya and felt be same way about her food. I had a bite and was super impressed by the quality of the pita ! Her eggs were also cooked to just the way she liked too. The portions were perfect for one person, and the price was decent as well! Servers was super nice too, honestly don't have anything bad to say. If I'm ever in the area again will definitely be stopping by once more :)

The workers here are nice, but they are set up to be slow. They had one worker assembling the noodles and another that was just filling up  sauce for takeout containers.  A little bit unbalanced. Most people were ordering 3-5 orders so that alone will take a minimum of 10 minutes. If 3-4 people are ahead of you then you're going to have a wait. The noodles themselves are only ok. They were more crumbly than elastic. I didn't taste the pork at all so it's really all about the sauce.  I love that rice noodles are popular now but they aren't all built equally.

Title: Disappointing Dining Experience at Local Korean Eatery

My recent visit to a local Korean restaurant proved to be underwhelming despite its clean, minimalist decor and generous portion sizes. The menu promised much, but delivered little in terms of flavor. The shigol bapsang, which we ordered twice, fell short of expectations. Particularly, the bossam was dry, and the accompanying kimchi was overly salty.

Curiosity led me to sample the nakkji bokkeum, which was passable, though it missed an opportunity to impress by not being served in a dolsot for that desirable crispy rice texture. Both the jjigae and banchan were unremarkable, tainted by an overpowering saltiness.

The service, however, was the lowest point of the meal. The negligent handling of hot beverages resulted in my sister nearly scalding her mouth with almost boiling water, presumably fresh from a tea thermos without proper cooling. Our complaint was met with a dismissive laugh from the server, an unacceptable response to a genuine concern.

Given the unsatisfactory flavors and careless service, I cannot recommend this establishment and have no plans to return.

24/7 Korean restaurant in Ktown, with surprisingly cheap breakfast options (~$8-9 as their breakfast specials)!Context: Came in with a friend on Saturday ~10am, and around half the restaurant was full. Atmosphere: Relatively large space for NY, though they offer long benches across 2 walls, and the tables seem a bit close to each other. There isn't much room between you and the next person on the same bench. Service was relatively quick (all our food came out within 20-25 minutes).  Food: Started off with small cold dishes, which offered a good amount of variety (kimchi, seaweed, spicy cucumber). I ordered the Kimchi Jjigae - expect this to be spicy, ant to predominately have kimchi (I was a bit disappointed with the small amount of pork included). I also was not expecting the glass noodles within the soup. But overall, a filling and affordable meal - in total, the cost was ~$12, including tip. Overall: 4 / 5 one of the more affordable places I've been do in NYC for breakfast, and in Koreatown too! Would definitely come back for quick, affordable meal, though I wish portion sizes were a bit larger.

Drinks only reviewGreat drinks, wonderful views and a vibrant atmosphere that takes over the entire floor. Do you really need much more when you're trying to drink with a view? So I'll leave it at that and say you gotta check this place out sometime!

Title: A Ramen Revelation at Shinka Ramen

If you thought you knew good ramen, prepare to be enlightened at Shinka Ramen. Among the variety we tried, the bone marrow ramen emerged as an unparalleled favorite – a sumptuous treat that redefines indulgence. Each slurp was a taste of heaven!

Unexpectedly, we were greeted with a complimentary serving of edamame, a genuinely appreciated gesture that paired perfectly with our meal. The pork, starring both in the ramen and the bao buns, was nothing short of succulent, complementing the rich flavors with its tender goodness.

For anyone rambling through the city with a ramen craving, your search ends at Shinka Ramen. And kudos to the waiter, whose relaxed demeanor and helpful nature only enhanced our exceptional dining experience. Highly recommended!

Title: Tantalizing Pork Belly at a Price at BaoHaus

If your quest is to find scrumptious pork belly, BaoHaus certainly delivers with pieces that are tender and bursting with flavor, proving their culinary prowess. However, be prepared to dig a little deeper into your pockets at this eatery, as the prices tend to be on the higher side.

Be aware that the size of the servings can be deceiving; the pork belly may seem to overflow from the petite buns, but don't let looks fool you—these are more of a tease than a meal. Opting for one leaves you wanting, yet indulging in two can feel overindulgent with their rich fattiness.

The space itself is cozy, to put it kindly. Expect a cramped counter and ordering area, best for a quick grab rather than a leisurely dine-in experience—unless you're okay with leaving with a hint of eau de grease as a memento of your visit.

This is my go to place for tonkatsu in the city. The service is quick and the food is great. I usually get the teishoku because it comes with miso soup  and rice. At first glance it may seem expensive but the prices are actually very reasonable given that tip is already included.

Title: A Feast for the Senses at a Standout Chinese Gem

My dining experience at this restaurant was nothing short of exceptional, thanks to the impeccable service provided by Mavis and Chloe. The dinner was memorable, with an array of savory dishes that impressed both my palate and eyes – as evidenced by the attached photos.

The portion sizes were generous, perfect for sharing, and each dish I tried was a delight. Unlike some other establishments, the cuisine here was authentic Chinese without being overly greasy, striking just the right balance.

The practicalities of the restaurant added to the pleasant experience. The establishment offers a gender-neutral bathroom, accepts reservations – a wise choice considering it gets busy –, and has a happy hour for drinks from 4-6 pm. Additionally, checking in on Yelp rewards you with a complimentary dessert.

Overall, this is a restaurant I cannot recommend enough. It's a place where satisfaction is guaranteed, and you'll likely leave with leftovers to enjoy later. I'm already planning my next visit!

I came here 3 times. The first two times years ago and was really impressed.I came back for my birthday this year and it was frighteningly disappointing.While the asparagus appetizer was delicious, everything else was subpar (not relative to similarly priced restaurants: relative to any good restaurant in NYC...).So when you spend $120+ per person it's not the best experience..

Title: A Grecian Delight in the Heart of Town

If you're pining for a Greek getaway, look no further than this enchanting little spot that may just make you forget you're not actually in Greece. My experience was nothing short of amazing, starting with their SGR Souvlaki Pita. The shrimp version is a must-try—truly a flavor odyssey!

Service? Absolutely delightful. Each visit from the waitstaff brought a genuine smile that could brighten anyone's day—mine included. And for coffee aficionados, the traditional iced coffee is a revelation with its luscious foam and velvety smooth finish.

All said, this gem offers an exemplary blend of scrumptious food and heartwarming service. It's a resounding yes from me—highly recommended!

Recently enjoyed an outstanding Wine Dinner at a local gem of a restaurant, where for $69 per person, we were treated to a culinary ballet of flavors. The deal included a well-curated three-course meal paired with an unlimited selection of wines from notable houses like Pasqua, Seeker, Guenoc, and Antinori. We sampled everything from a crisp prosecco to a robust sauvignon blanc, accompanied by a duo of reds that elevated the experience.

The evening commenced with an amuse-bouche of watermelon, crème, and basil, a bite-sized harbinger of the kitchen's skill. The appetizers were a testament to the chef's prowess: tender yellowfin tuna with creamy avocado, a perfectly seasoned steak tartare, and indulgent sweet corn agnolotti graced with the luxury of white truffles. Main courses of grilled branzino and seared scallops showcased the kitchen’s mastery of seafood, each dish a delicious testament to their dedication to flavor and presentation.

The restaurant's interior was stunning, providing a gorgeous backdrop to the exquisite meal. Service was impeccable, attentive without being intrusive, and the prices were reasonable - especially for wine enthusiasts who could make the most of the unlimited pours.

This dining experience is perfect for a special night out, and with the generous flow of wine, a ride-sharing service like Uber for the journey home is a wise choice. Highly recommended.

This review is for brunch at upland. My friend and I walked in and were able to grab seats at the bar on a Sunday afternoon. The place was really crowded and we would have to wait 2 hours for a table. It's always a good sign when a place is this busy! We ordered the bucatini and fried chicken sandwich to share. Both were delicious! The service was fast and the drinks at the bar was amazing. The bucatini is perfectly al dente and full of parmesan cheese. The fried chicken was so tasty and topped with guacamole and some veggies so it actually tasted pretty healthy (but who am I kidding its served with fries on the side).Highly recommend this place!! The vibe is very upscale and classy. It kind of reminds me of trademark plus nomad kitchen decor. A gem place for a group lunch/dinner or when family visits. Very excited to try their dinner menu next time :)

I really liked coming to this location because it's a good price for Szechuan food. We ordered the Dry Pepper Style Chicken, Cumin Style Lamb, Garlic Style Sauce Chicken, Mapo Tofu, and Dan Dan Noodles. Pros:(+) Spacious location: Good for groups since the location is huge and it was easy to get seating without a reservation(+) Great food for the price: We managed to finish everything and everyone in my group enjoyed the food. Everything was very flavorful although not as spicy as I thought it would be. (+) Plenty of vegetarian options: Both the dan dan noodles and mapo tofu can be made without meat and all of the options had tofuWill definitely be coming back!

Honestly wasn't expecting this place to be that good, but surprisingly it was actually really yummy! Who would've thought to get rotisserie chicken and Latin flare food in the midst of Chinatown? Some good rotisserie chicken too?! Don't knock it til you try it! You'll find some asian influence to their dishes too. I came here for lunch and ordered their ribs & quarter chicken (dark) platter which came with yellow rice, beans and salad for $14.95. Chicken was super juicy and well seasoned. The ribs came in a good big 4 pieces that were really tender and soo tasty, I loved the flavors on it! I'm use to seeing a lot of places serving a mountain full of beans but that wasn't the case here, which is fine because the whole platter itself was already plentiful. Everything on that platter was a nice portion size. Green sauce was great too, not watered down and def get the flavors of fresh herbs. Also ordered side of maduros and the tinga cubano sandwich which came with side of fries. Their fries are SO FCKN P E R F E C T!! The Cuban sandwich ($9.95) was interesting, a little flair and different take on it that I enjoyed as well. Overall, we was really full and I think the price is just right especially for what you get! Not skimped, overpriced, or nothing... n complaints on the food. Definitely recommend and will be back for sure!

Drinks were good and strong!! Service was also really attentive and friendly. The only complaint I have is that upstairs was super warm. The chicken wonton taco was alright...the chicken quesadilla was good and satisfying...I'll definitely hit this place up when I'm in the area.

Love the food here.  Eating inside feels like being at a legit Turkish place, in Turkey, complete with the fluorescent lighting, dark wood decor, etc.  Pretty large menu.  Grilled meat tastes very authentic in all its greasy glory.  All the mezzes (appetizers/side dishes) are on point and fresh.  Also a great deal for weekend lunch prix fixe.  One of the better Turkish places I've been to in the city.Would be perfect if they had some pickles to go with the meats and Turkish ketchup for the lamb Adana like they do in Turkey.

Made a reservation over the phone for New Year's Eve. Instead of trying their handroll sets, my friend and I opted for their omakase meals. I had the mizu while she had the umi with a wagyu handroll a la carte. Super affordable and every piece was decent quality and freshness. My favorite pieces were probably the scallop and king salmon. Their wagyu was lacking a little because it was kind of chewy. It definitely was not A5 grade, but what can we expect for the price? Nonetheless, it was still very fatty. We didn't feel rushed by the chef whatsoever and the meal lasted about 1.5 hours. But I do wish the server was more with filling our glasses of water. Other than that, I'd love to return to try their handroll sets!

Amazing soba! Maybe the best in NYC. I liked the cold soba a bit better than the hot but both were delicious.If you order before 7pm, you can get the early bird dinner set for $33, which includes your choice of entree (sushi, tempura, katsu, and some others I don't recall), a small salad, your choice of hot or cold soba, sashimi, and dessert. The portions are a little small so you probably will want more than that but it still seemed like a good deal and it was all so delicious. Our neighbor got the duck, which looked amazing though also tiny portions. Bonus points for free hot tea with plenty of refills. Also loved the lengthy (but reasonably priced) sake list. Reservations were very easy to make on yelp. Made a Thursday 6:45 reservation just 30 min earlier. Not sure we needed it though as there was plenty of seating.

After a day of exploring Manhattan and Brooklyn, my partner and I found ourselves at a local hot pot restaurant, driven by a craving for something warm and comforting. Despite a brief wait, we were seated in a communal area alongside other diners, which added to the convivial atmosphere.

Opting for the all-you-can-eat hot pot, we selected both the regular and spicy broths, each served in individual mini pots. The hot pot was satisfying, with attentive service complementing the experience. A standout feature was the inclusion of crab in the offering without an extra charge, a generous touch that was much appreciated.

While the broths initially seemed a touch on the bland side, the extensive sauce bar provided ample opportunity for customization and added flavor. To cap off our hearty meal, we indulged in some self-serve ice cream, a sweet note to end on. Overall, it was the ideal feast to round out our bustling day in the city.

Good lunch spot for a quick business lunch, and conveniently located near Times Square. The food is average, with the spring rolls being the highlight of our lunch. By checking in on Yelp you get a free Yucca Fries on the House, which tasted mediocre. We then ordered the Cuban sandwich, which also mediocre. Overall, will likely not return due to the medium to low quality of the food I experienced.

Decided to try out Thy's Noodles as it was being offered via MealPal. I had to wait a couple of minutes which I didn't mind as it meant my noodles were nice and fresh. It came with some chicken mince and vegetables.. and also some chilli oil. The serving size was just right and the level of spice also good. Just don't wear a white top whilst eating it which I obviously did. Hoping these chilli oil stains will come off...

Title: Sweet Celebration at Wafels and Dinges

Last week, to celebrate a birthday, my friends and I chose Wafels and Dinges for a special treat. We indulged in their infamous WMD - a delightful behemoth topped with generous dollops of whipped cream, fresh strawberries, bananas, and a luscious fudge drizzle. The waffles themselves were a perfect balance of warmth and sweetness, harmonizing beautifully with the lavish toppings.

Admittedly, the price point is on the higher side, but for the quality and joy it brought to our birthday celebration, it was a worthwhile expenditure. The ingredients' freshness and flavor truly elevated the experience. If you're looking to treat yourself or someone special, Wafels and Dinges is an excellent choice.

Honestly, some of the slowest service I have ever received. Management had to remake our white sangria twice because it was basically just watered down white wine without any fruit and they even admitted that it was bad so we switched it to a red sangria. They said because of the trouble they would provide a free refill of our pitcher, which never came. Food orders were taken about 45 minutes after we were seated and then another 45 minutes until we saw any dishes arrive at our table. Thankfully the dishes were pretty good (pulpo, hangar steak, and farro salad with steak). The steak in the salad was a bit tough and difficult to slice, given they just gave me a butter knife. I don't think I'll be returning because the service was that bad, even though the food was pretty good.

This cute spot is located in the Columbus Circle mall on the 3rd floor - just an FYI because I was under the impression that it was it's own separate location. I came here for a birthday tea party and it was pretty fun! Most of us did the afternoon tea menu and it came with a few different pastries, scones and mini sandwiches. Of the prix-fixe menu, there were 2 sandwiches (out of 4 types) that had meat in it so it's not bad for vegetarians. However, I wish there were more sandwiches in general to even out with the sweet items on the stand. Definitely a posh little spot to do with your girlfriends!

Recently visited a quaint Indian restaurant conveniently located between Rockefeller Center and Bryant Park, ideal for a culinary detour after some sightseeing. The ambiance was welcoming, and the place was pleasantly uncrowded, creating a relaxed dining experience.

Our group of four sampled the chicken tikka, each tailored to our preferred spice levels—a thoughtful touch for those wary of the heat. Accompaniments included a variety of sides such as perfectly cooked rice, flavorful chickpeas, hearty lentils, and fresh salads. We also indulged in an assortment of naan bread, including plain, whole wheat, and garlic, all of which were delectably soft and warm.

The meal left us satisfied on all fronts, striking a balance between indulgence and comfort. Next visit, I'm looking forward to trying their samosas, hoping they'll be as delightful as the rest of the fare.

A cozy casual spot. This pop-up is located inside "Mama's Eatery" with a sign out front advertising curry. The menu they provide is big, and the Spicy Curry section is on the very back. If you're getting the Seafood Curry Soup, you can choose the size of your noodles.I loved the flavor, big portion for the money, and warmth of my bowl. My friend got the curry chicken with pancakes. While the chicken was really tasty, I felt the flavor was a little more bland and lacking a "wow" factor. The pancakes were a little on the small side too. But it was still a tasty and filling dish.Their hours seem to fluctuate a lot, despite what it says online, they told me they close at 7pm that day.I'm not sure if I'll be back often, but I can see myself going back for the Seafood Curry Noodle Soup on a cold day!

Title: A Converted Skeptic at a NYC Ramen Spot

I ventured into a Ramen joint on 8/19, accompanying my son for his 21st birthday celebration with strong reservations about the cuisine. Ramen never really called out to me, and I was set to maintain my stance. The menu failed to pique my interest, barring one dish that seemed remotely familiar - the fried chicken. I took the plunge and ordered it, only to be taken aback by its spicy, succulent perfection. It was, without exaggeration, phenomenally tender.

Meanwhile, my son and wife delved into their chosen Ramen bowls with gusto. I admit, curiosity got the better of me, and I sampled the broth. It was a revelation - flavorful, rich, and admittedly, quite delicious. It's not easy to concede when one's preconceived notions are shattered, but here I am. This place didn't just meet the mark; it exceeded it. As it turns out, I was wrong, and pleasantly so - this restaurant rocks!

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Harlem Pizza

I recently ventured into Harlem Pizza for the first time and left utterly impressed. The Cheese Me White pizza with an adventurous addition of anchovies was a revelation; it was nothing short of spectacular, easily taking the crown for the best pizza I've enjoyed on the east coast.

In a bid to sample more, I also opted for a veggie-white pizza. While surprisingly topped with bacon, which initially caused some confusion, it turned out to be a serendipitous twist on a classic that I relished every bite of.

The baby arugula salad was another highlight, delivering a fresh and flavorful accompaniment to the stellar pizzas.

A slight disappointment came with the unavailability of Tiramisu, a dessert I was eager to try, but it leaves me with a delicious excuse to return.

Kudos to Harlem Pizza for not only delivering exceptional food but also providing friendly customer service that made the experience even more enjoyable. I'm already looking forward to my next order!

3.75 Stars but rounding up to 4.  So glad we came early on this Saturday night!  My friends and I planned to meet at 5:30pm before heading to a show.  When we arrived, the restaurant had plenty of open tables.  15 minutes later, the place is packed!  This restaurant is really cute and had really great ambiance!  Apparently, it was a little too dark for our neighboring table.  They proceeded to peruse the menu using their very bright cell phone light, which is fine, but people, please...be aware of your surroundings and do NOT keep shining that damn light in everyone's eyes while trying to read the darn menu!!  After about 5 minutes of being in the unwanted spot light, I finally had to ask him to please direct the light elsewhere.  Sheshhhh!!Anyway, I digress...the menu is huge and has something for everyone!  Large portions; reasonable prices (especially for this area!).  Tonight, we opted NOT to dine family style and just order individual dishes.  Coincidentally, we all ordered chicken dishes:~ Pad Thai with chicken (ordered spicy) - stir-fried rice noodles w.tamarin sauce, egg, peanut, scallion and bean sprouts.  Great dish;  fresh ingredients, tasty and had quite a kick to it!  My only complaint is that the chicken was overcooked for my taste.~ Drunken Noodles w.chicken - broad noodles stir-fried w.spicy basil leaves, onion, egg, carrots and Thai broccoli.  Came medium spicy and was delicious.  ~ Pra Ram Rong Song w.chicken - sauteed with peanut curry sauce and coconut milk on Thai broccoli; served w.rice.  Another delicious dish with lots of Thai broccoli.Service and hospitality were great; quick and attentive without being too overbearing.  However, since there were a lot of people waiting for a table by the time we were finished, we did feel like we were being rushed out.
I've really come to enjoy this restaurant as one of my go-to lunch spots. The selection is impressive and always leaves me satisfied with my choice.

I recently revisited Boulud Sud for lunch, having given it a second chance at the encouragement of the general manager, and I'm thrilled to report a flawless dining experience. From the warm smiles at the door to the attentive service throughout our meal, the staff made sure our visit was exceptional, which was a refreshing change from my previous visit.

The cuisine was outstanding. We indulged in champagne and a variety of dips, with the Babaganoush standing out as a particular favorite, testament to the restaurant's expertise in Mediterranean flavors. The Express Lunch deal was excellent value at $26 for a soup and an entrée. The cauliflower soup served as a delicious starter, creamy and smooth to my liking.

For the main course, the Harissa Lamb Burger was a hit, its flavors enhanced by eggplant and saganaki cheese, though the accompanying spiced fries were somewhat ordinary. My friend's Lemon Saffron Linguini was also met with high praise, especially for saffron enthusiasts.

Overall, Boulud Sud has redeemed itself in my eyes, and I am now eager to return, assured of the quality and care that goes into every aspect of their dining experience. A heartfelt thank you to the team for a wonderful lunch.

I recently tried the beef pho soup from this spot through MealPal and it was a satisfying experience. The portion size was generous, not reduced due to the MealPal service, which was a pleasant surprise. They didn’t skimp on the essentials either—all the traditional condiments, bean sprouts, and cilantro were included, ensuring an authentic taste. I’m eagerly anticipating exploring more of their menu offerings in the future.

First of all, this restaurant is sexy af. The lighting, layout, atmosphere. It's like an upscale party with good food. I know it's a steakhouse but wished they offered better appetizer options. Anyways, my friend highly recommended the Kobe beef for $80 as an appetizer (insert eye roll). Anyways, I ordered and we shared it. It was like butter melting in my mouth. It was flavorful, moist and tender. Wish I had gotten it for my entree instead. We split one of the steak dishes made for two people as our entree. It was cooked at our table and he ended with the fancy salt display. We order a side of asparagus to go with it. Overall it was a nice experience, but nothing to rave about. Service should be better, especially at the exorbitant price for every item on the menu.

Overall a good meal, just wish it wasn't so pricey for what it was. I feel like I could get very good cuts of fish for cheaper, however this was still good!We got both the salmon ceviche and the crab ceviche. I definitely think the flavors were very different between the two, and both were good! Octopus - was very good. The octopus was cooked perfectly, and it came with a very flavorful potato as well. Brussel sprouts - these were also good. I don't usually eat brussel sprouts but are never opposed to them. These almost tasted like it had honey mustard slathered on it though. I do think that my enjoyment of this dish declined by 5% after I realized that it tasted like honey mustard though, so I apologize if this deters you from ordering it, or worse ruining the dish for you.

Title: Mixed Experience at The Vessel

I was eager to dine at The Vessel, with high expectations for an evening out. However, my experience was dampened right from the start due to a significant delay. Despite holding a reservation for 5:30pm, a private event pushed our seating to past 6:15pm. A complimentary glass of champagne as an apology was appreciated but didn't quite compensate for the inconvenience.

The menu appeared promising, offering a selection of dishes ranging from starters to desserts. The standout was the Duck 'a la Kumquat', which delivered on tenderness and a delightful citrus twist. The Yellowfin Tuna also impressed with its freshness and the complement of tomatoes. Less remarkable were the Crispy Calamari and Beef Tartare, both of which felt like standard fare. Dessert brought us the Roasted Pineapple Upside-Down Cake, reminiscent of a carrot cake, potentially a hit for those with a penchant for the latter.

Overall, the dining experience at The Vessel was underwhelming. Smaller dish sizes, mediocre flavors, and the initial service hiccup left me feeling there are better culinary experiences to be had nearby.

A simple and classic approach to Italian food that succeeds on all levels. This was a very pleasant meal all the way around. The truffled Mac and cheese balls are a must have for an appetizer. Bursting with flavor. The calamari was one of the best I've ever had. Just a light dusting of breading with an accompanying sauce that was unique and wonderful. All of the pizzas were excellent. You can't go wrong when you make them fresh in an open fire pizza oven.   The pasta dishes were excellent as well. Fresh and well prepared sauces. Pasta was cooked to perfection. Service was prompt and friendly.

Came here for late dinner on a Friday night. Ordered the fish tacos which were delish and fresh- they come with an order of fries: regular or paprika or with a salad. Service was great - atmosphere a bit on the "cold side" aesthetically but still nice enough. My friend that comes here regularly commented that happy hour drinks usually taste watered down. But the atmosphere is always good enough for an after work drink or two if you're around the area.

I recently visited a local restaurant for a weekday lunch with friends. The exterior had an artsy, classic allure that was quite inviting. Upon entering, we were greeted by friendly staff who remained attentive throughout our meal, although service was admittedly slow. The menu selection left us wanting, as the options were rather limited, though what we did order was decently prepared. The standout was the fries—perfectly crispy and generously portioned. Additionally, the drinks menu offered a great variety of choices. In the end, the experience was pleasant but not exceptional, meriting a solid 3-star rating.

**Cash Only**Came here on a Saturday at 11:30am before the lunch hour rush, there were plenty of tables. We ordered the chicken Martabak, Assam Laksa and the Penang char kweo. All were very nice and tasted authentic enough. Didn't realize it was cash only when I went to pay however there is a Citibank just across the street. You have to go down a narrow stairway to access the restaurant so it isn't too accessible for those with mobility challenges. We left around 12:40pm and there were few available tables left.

Pizza will never be the same again. This place has ruined future pizzas to be consumed. Walked from the one trade center to get here and was worth the walk. When I arrived there was a line out the door on a Monday afternoon! My first time there and a usual customer behind me was surprised there was that many people there on a week day. Needless to say it was worth the wait. Ordered the pepperoni pizza which is what they are known for. It was a game changer. I ate here a few days ago and its all I think about. Everything about it is perfection. I wish everyone can have a slice at least once in their life.

My friend and I walked in on a weekday at 5pm and were immediately seated. Our server was very attentive and checked up on us throughout our meal which we really appreciated. Appetizer came out quickly, but our mains came out 40 minutes later which was quite upsetting considering that the restaurant was practically empty. Dishes I ordered:ANTIPASTI +Polipo ($24): Grilled octopus served with beans that is good for sharing. This appetizer was very good and it's something I'll definitely order again. Octopus was flavorful and not too salty. PRIMI PIATTI +Linguine alle Vongole ($29): I was looking forward to this dish, but it turned out to be a disappointing. Pasta was overcooked and it was just flavorless. Generous portions of clams though. Overall for its portions, prices are fair. But the quality wasn't up there. Cesca is nearby so I will give it another try to try their other dishes.

Title: A Hidden Gem Discovered on a Whim

During a shopping trip in an unfamiliar neighborhood, my rumbling stomach led me to a delightful find through my Yelp app. Upon arrival, we were promptly seated at this charming eatery, just moments before the dinner rush.

The warm, freshly-baked bread and olive oil provided a perfect start while we perused the menu. Opting for the prix fixe, I indulged in an exquisite organic burrata with tomato, followed by smoked salmon over spinach – both dishes were remarkable, but the burrata truly stood out. My mom enjoyed a vegan carrot ginger soup and succulent iron skillet shrimp, praising each dish's flavor.

Service was a cut above, with attentive staff ensuring our table remained spotless throughout the meal – a rarity worth noting. A novel touch was the restroom concealed behind a cleverly designed makeshift library shelf, adding to the eatery's charm. Despite its cozy size, the space accommodates both casual drinkers at the bar and those seeking an intimate dining experience.

In summary, this quaint haven offers delectable fare with service that shines, making it an excellent choice for foodies in search of a new culinary adventure.

I LOVE this place! One of my favorite spots in NY so far! The brunch deal was amazing it's only $37 for meal entree and bottomless margs, sangria, or mimosas come on where can you go wrong with this! The manager JOE is amazing!!! He's SO attentive and outgoing I think he must've been the best part of this visit to be honest. The rose sangria is absolutely to die for, it has so much flavor and it's absolutely delicious, and don't forget the guacamole as a starter. Best guacamole hands down, I ordered the chilaquila (I forgot how to spell it) which was really good as well with red salsa because I can't handle spiciness but when I finished my entree I still found myself scraping what was left of the guacamole. Next time I will go I will order endless bowls of guacamole because I don't even know what they put in there that gives it so much flavor in your taste buds! You must go here and try! There is a huge back room for party reservations if you're looking to throw a birthday bash as well, it's secluded and pretty intimate with a bit of Mexican flair!

Title: A Hearty Bowl of Comfort at Tabata Ramen

I recently satisfied my ramen cravings at Tabata Ramen during a NYC visit, and the experience left me yearning for more. From the moment we entered, the efficient seating and hospitable staff set a welcoming tone. Their attentiveness to dietary restrictions was commendable as they adeptly crafted pork-free options for me and catered to my friend's vegetarian preferences, all while diligently avoiding peanuts and sesame due to allergies.

The food was not only aesthetically pleasing but also arrived steamy and flavorful. Generous portions meant I enjoyed a second helping at home, which was just as delightful. The staff maintained their exceptional service throughout, consistently topping up our water and engaging us with genuine friendliness.

While the prices are slightly higher, they reflect NYC standards, and the quality and service justify the cost. Tabata Ramen has earned its spot as a go-to for me, and I'm already planning my next visit.

I recently visited the restaurant for their $13 three rolls lunch special and came away underwhelmed. The selection of a sweet potato roll, shrimp tempura roll, and eel avocado roll, served with a side salad, did seem promising at first. The salad was pleasantly surprising, a notch above the standard fare with the inclusion of grape tomatoes and a tasty ginger dressing.

However, the sushi was a letdown. The rolls were sloppily constructed and prone to falling apart, excessively smothered in sauce that overpowered the taste. I also sampled their fresh lemon soda, which disappointingly tasted more akin to lemon peels mixed with Sprite, rather than a refreshing citrus beverage.

While the portion size was satisfactory, the execution in the kitchen left much to be desired. Unfortunately, the overall experience means I won't be planning a return visit.

Thank goodness this store is here to satisfy my soondubu needs. On a cold 30 degree day shopping at 34th, I was craving warm soup, so BCD was definitely on my mind as a lunch spot to go to. Each time I went (which is like twice), the place is packed. But you don't have to wait for long! They give you a buzzer and I only waited around 5 minutes before it went off and we were seated on the second floor.During lunch special hours (9:30AM-3PM), you can get entrees with a side of tofu soup! I got the Bibimbap Combo with Mixed Tofu Soup ($17.99). You can personalize the spicy level of your tofu soup so I got it Mild! As in every Korean restaurant, you get a mix of side dishes. They didn't have the macaroni side I like the second time I went! :( The bibimbap tasted healthy yet delicious, as I was craving some mixed vegetables! And the tofu soup, which was what I came here for, did not disappoint. I popped the raw egg side dish in there for extra flavor, and it was just bomb mixed with the plentiful seafood, tofu, and beef in there. I love the system here! There are workers everywhere communicating through walkie talkies. They also don't rush you even though we were there for around 2 hours! Everyone is so nice and the food is reasonably priced and yummy! It's no wonder this place is so popular.

The buzz meter for this place registers off the hook. A place that people get excited about to spend expense account money sets a different level of expectations. My friends, there's only one place reality can go from there. First the positives. The place is charming, clean, and very inviting. The service is warm and pleasant - even if they screwed up bringing the apps first rather than with our meals. The menu selections seem well edited, pairing modern mains with a smattering of inspired sides (but sometimes not). My lobster roll came with shoestring fries. But the hangar steak comes with kimchee fried rice - didn't taste it but looked legit! Unfortunately, the food falls a bit short. Basically everything looked good but tasted pretty plain. Corn bread was dense and kind of tasteless. The lobster roll barely registered any lobster flavor. Just generally all tasteless. But then on top of bland food was having the pleasure of paying a premium price. Go if you're a hype follower not a food follower.

Title: A Brunch to Remember at the Heart of NYC

From the moment my party of 10-12 arrived for a birthday brunch, we were met with top-notch service that set the tone for a memorable experience. The vibe is quintessential New York, with vibrant graffiti decor complementing the mood and a music selection that adapts to the patrons, adding an extra layer of dynamic energy.

While we waited for our group to gather, the mimosas were a delightful prelude to the meal. I opted for the SET Steak & Eggs Skillet - a decision that paid off with a deliciously flavored steak paired with sriracha garlic home fries that were cooked to perfection - a delightful crunch outside with the right softness inside. For those less enthused by home fries, waffle fries and tater tots are tempting alternatives.

Our entire group found their dishes to be exceptional, and the atmosphere was ideal for celebrations. We noticed another party indulging in a magnum mimosa, which seemed like a fun challenge. It's also worth mentioning the openness of the restaurant to personalizing the space for occasions like birthdays.

Overall, if you're seeking a spot in NYC with great music, a spirited ambiance, and delectable brunch options, look no further. This establishment is a gem that promises a fantastic dining experience.

We came in this morning, fresh from the airport after a long redeye flight. The reviews looked very promising and I was looking forward to having the avocado toast with poached eggs. We were easily able to get a table. We ordered some coffee and straight into our breakfast dish. I ordered the toast as I wanted and my partner ordered the Sicilian dish which she absolutely loved. Service was also very good and adequate with time. The whole process took about an hour, from the time we walked in to the time we walked out. That shows they are very efficient and fast in getting our food ready. Will definitely come back here again soon.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Southern Fare at Local Eatery

My boyfriend and I recently visited this restaurant with high hopes for a hearty Southern meal, but our experience proved to be a bit of a rollercoaster. The highlight was definitely the warm and comforting cornbread served at the start—it set a promising tone for the meal.

I decided to try the Kool-Aid of the day, which happened to be grape. It was exactly what you'd expect—classic Kool-Aid taste with no surprises there. My boyfriend opted for the smothered pork chop, accompanied by fried okra and mac and cheese. The okra was a letdown, arriving cold and losing its potential to impress. However, the mac and cheese was generously topped with cheese, hinting at what could have been a stellar side dish with a bit more culinary finesse.

As for the pork chop, it was unevenly cooked, with dry spots that were only redeemed by the accompanying sauce. My own dish, the chicken and waffles, was satisfactory at best. The chicken was respectably fried, but lacked the moisture one craves in perfectly cooked poultry. The waffle, on the other hand, was rather uninspiring and suffered from a dry texture.

To sum it up, while there were some good elements, the inconsistency in the quality of food begs for better quality control. This place could be a real gem with just a little more attention to detail.

Headed up this way to go to the AMC Lincoln Square 13 IMAX 3D and didn't know what to eat.  I walked passed this place. And seen it only had 3.5 stars so I was skeptical but I have been to 3.5 star places and found they were much better.  Amd to be honest I haven't really eaten this type of cuisine much.  But I was with a friend and said we should just try it.   I'm glad I did.  I had a few questions about the menu since I didn't recognize some of the food items.  After a few mins asking the patient waiter several questions. I decided to go with the Farro bowl, $13.95.Pick a protein- avacado2 toppings-lentil beans and beer salad Sauce- taziki The Farro is my new favorite grain to eat it was cooked and seasoned very well.  Avacado was nice and creamyLentils were cooked nice and brought a nice texture to the dish. Beets salad were cubed beets that brought a nice sweetness and brilliant color to the bowl. Taziki sauce brought everything together it was fresh with a nice floave of cucumber and lemon. I had some leftover and finished it off in the movies. Much healthier then a bucket of popcorn.  Lol. PS. And wow the movie Alita was amazing in the IMAX 3D.

I am not a huge Mexican food eater but W.O.W their pork taco is to die for! Literally I died and went to heaven and went back in line and got second round! It is so flavorful, and not dry! I highly recommend getting the corn tortilla, add salsa and enjoy! :)

I can't say I've been to other fondue places in the City, but this was a very enjoyable experience. Pretty small and intimate great place for a date night. I thought the prices were reasonable relative to the amount of food you were getting. Loved the spicy, pepper cheese blend we tried and the steak was very tender after getting a bath in our choice of wine. I didn't like the amex-only thing, but we were prepared after yelp (they also call to notify and tell you at the restaurant). If I'm ever in the mood for fondue and cheesiness, I know where I'm going!

My recent visit to this eatery allowed me to sample their innovative kimbap varieties. I opted for the everything kimbap, without bulgogi, and the spicy tuna kimbap as part of a lunch combo set that included a serving of soup and a small portion of tteok bokki. While the kimbap itself did not disappoint—with the everything kimbap being particularly noteworthy for its flavorful filling—the accompanying tteok bokki was a letdown. It was excessively runny and disappointingly sweet, lacking the advertised spiciness. Additionally, despite the presence of hard-boiled eggs in the chafing pan, none found their way into our serving, leading to questions about their purpose there. 

The everything kimbap, at $10.99 per roll, stood out as the star, with its generous and well-balanced ingredients. In comparison, the spicy tuna kimbap was noticeably less impressive. The initial lunch order totaled $22.84, while a subsequent carryout order for four everything kimbaps—still sans bulgogi—came to $47.86. This establishment offers a satisfactory experience for kimbap enthusiasts, with some minor setbacks in the side dish department.

Title: A Summery Slice of Delight Amidst Growing Pains

I recently visited a new eatery with a group, drawn in by the welcoming summer vibes of their expansive outdoor seating. The establishment impressed with their readiness, having our spot prepared just 10 minutes post-reservation call.

The culinary experience was commendable. My Margherita Pizza was a delightful, flavorsome giant that promised value with every bite. The pasta dishes, while smaller, did not compromise on taste. Those opting for pizza can anticipate the joy of leftovers.

However, the service faltered. An oversight in hospitality was felt when the expected complimentary bread was amiss, and parched throats longed for water that wasn't promptly offered. A hiccup with our credit card being momentarily forgotten further marred the service.

Nonetheless, the swift arrival of our food softened these edges, facilitated by a conveniently placed menu outside for pre-seating perusal.

While service hitches suggested a team not yet in its prime, the potential was palpable. It's a place I'd revisit once the teething issues are resolved, as the culinary delights are too good to pass up.

Delicious ramen spot. This is my third time here and it always hits the spot. The ramen here is top quality and all the options are pretty solid. They also have other options for food besides ramen. I enjoy the ambience of the restaurant and it's nice atmosphere to meet with friends. Would recommend as one of the top ramen spots in the UES.

Title: A Brunch Delight at Tribeca's Kitchen

Tribeca's Kitchen offers an unbeatable weekend brunch deal that is perfect for those who enjoy a leisurely start to their day. For less than $20, diners are treated to a hearty entree, a choice of coffee/tea, and a drink, which could be anything from refreshing orange juice to a selection from their alcoholic brunch beverages, or alternatively, a fruit salad.

I had the pleasure of trying the Cabo Benedict - a delightful twist on the classic with corned beef hash and green hollandaise perfectly complementing the poached eggs. The addition of avocado provided a creamy counterpoint to the savory flavors. While I found the hash browns a tad underwhelming, desiring a crisper texture, the side salad was a refreshing interlude.

The service matched the quality of the food, with attentive staff keen on ensuring our coffee cups remained full and ready to accommodate any requests.

In summary, Tribeca's Kitchen is a must-visit for a well-priced and satisfying brunch experience. The food is flavorful, the deals are phenomenal, and the service is top-notch.

During our latest visit to this hidden gem, we were thrilled with the ma po tofu and Singapore mei fun, both packing a delightful spicy punch that exceeded expectations. For those who revel in heat, these dishes are a must-try. We also indulged in the shrimp rolls, which were notably fresh, quick to arrive, and had just the right touch of non-greasiness. One quirky note: the restaurant only accepts cash or Venmo, so come prepared. Overall, another delicious experience!

Set in the vibrant hub of Chinatown, the neighborhood buzzes with energy, drawing a lively crowd to this trendy block dotted with inviting eateries and bars. Despite the overwhelming popularity and the ever-present queue of eager patrons, the food served is agreeably decent, though it may not dazzle the culinary connoisseur. It's a place that's more about the experience and the setting than about groundbreaking flavors. A fun spot to immerse in the local scene and enjoy a meal that satisfies without quite stealing the show.

Blue Fin is located in Times Square, so at a very touristy area which means increased prices for mediocre food. But my friend's work is near here and wanted to treat all of us to sushi. We had a reservation at 5pm on Friday night and were seated immediately. Here is what I ordered: *ROLLED SUSHI*-Truffle Rainbow Roll ($19) -West Side Roll ($17) which consists of eel, spicy tuna, grilled pineapple, and cucumber Sushi was good, but not worth $17-$19. *STARTERS*-Classic Maine Lobster Bisque ($14) Very, very creamy. *DESSERT*-Warm Gala Apple Crostata ($11) This was most underwhelming dessert. Only the ice cream was good. Overall, it was an unimpressive experience. We appreciated the attention from our waitress but she was too attentive. She asked how everything was every 10 minutes or so throughout our meal which interrupted our dinner conversation many times. I also did not appreciate how our host was vacuuming right next to us while we were eating. Honestly if it was something I'd pay for myself, I wouldn't come here: very overpriced for very average food. It's just not worth it.

I like Maison Kayser for their bread, not so much their cakes and pastries.  I prefer Financier Patisserie for their cakes and pastries.  It's a tradition of mine to go to Maison Kayser on Valentine's Day for their heart shaped baguette.  I go to a different location every year (there's so many locations now).  This is probably the best location I've been to.  This location was not that crowded since it's on 3rd Ave and there's a lot of seating compared to other locations.  My sister and I ordered the heart shaped baguettes and coffee.  You can ask the staff for butter and jam.  The staff were very friendly and offered to wrap each baguette and place each one in a separate bag individually which was nice. The baguettes were fresh, crunchy on the outside, and fluffy on the inside.  I would come back to this location.

Title: Buzzing Atmosphere, Unique Appetizers - An Evening at [Restaurant Name]

My recent visit to [Restaurant Name] with friends to catch up over dinner landed us in a bustling scene on a Saturday night at 7:30 PM. It's a must to book ahead, given the crowd. While waiting, we grabbed drinks at the upstairs bar, which seems a prime spot for socializing.

Venturing into the menu, I opted for the grasshopper tacos as a starter. Surprisingly, the taste is akin to sunflower seeds – intriguing for the adventurous eater but perhaps too bold for the faint-hearted, as I ended up polishing off most of them.

As for the main course, the quesadilla was pretty standard and unremarkable, overshadowed by the wait time due to the packed venue. Although the food didn't particularly stand out, the place has a vibe that makes it a solid choice for a round of drinks and a casual hangout.

I recently ventured out of my culinary comfort zone to give Ethiopian cuisine another shot after a previous letdown. I'm glad to report that this experience at [Ethiopian Restaurant Name] was a delightful redemption.

Starting with the appetizers, I savored both the meat and vegetable sambusas, or samosas as they are more commonly known. The beef sambusa was notably well-seasoned, packed with flavorsome beef, while the veggie version, filled with lentils, was decent, albeit in need of a little extra seasoning to truly shine.

For my main course, I decided on the beef awaze tibs, which I can best describe as a harmonious mash-up of stir-fry and stew. Contrary to the menu's "spicy" tag, the dish wasn't the American-hot kind of spicy, but it had an agreeable depth of flavor. The beef was a tad chewy but didn't detract from the overall enjoyment.

The tibs were accompanied by sides of tikel gomen (cabbage dish) and misir wot (spicy lentils), both of which were mild but pleasantly palatable.

Overall, [Ethiopian Restaurant Name] has won me over, and I would definitely consider ordering from here again. A little note for potential diners, this review is based on a delivery order, so the food's quality is commendable given the travel time.

You can have a decent meal at a fair price on the Upper West Side at the Chirping Chicken.  It's really close to the Natural History museum so if you are in the area and need a decent meal you can have that here.  But I give it 3 stars because it's very middle of the road in terms of flavor and quality.  It wasn't really great, but it wasn't bad.  It was just decent, which is totally fine sometimes.  My wife enjoyed it more than I did, but she is a big fan of black beans and rice about anywhere.  Our son had the ribs and they were better than the chicken.  I would eat those.

Great lobster Mac and cheese with a good portion for lunch! This place is fairly priced and has the feel of a New England restaurant. They have several locations but the one near the Whitney and the high line makes for a nice day!
I got the chicken gaucho. The chicken was dried out and they KILLED the salad with onions. Blech. I'll pass. I'm not coming here again.

Pretty good hotpot. Loads and loads of ingredients you can order. Pretty much all and maybe even more options you could find at a normal good hotpot in China. The broth was pretty good but not great -- it was held to be really good though so it was probably just an off day for the broth; unlike for us. Unlike a lot of hotpot places in the US, they actually have the traditional dipping sauce choices you can use to make your dipping sauce which was really great to see. We ordered a lot of veggies but they only brought half of the ones to the table. In the end when we were asking where the other ones were, it turns out they had it in a cart in the back corner where no one could see, so we ended up not eating all of it because we were all already to leave. It's definitely a nice place to go with a few friends, but not as a huge group where you have to meet a spending budget.

Very excited that Friendship Foods BBQ is open in Manhattan! This is their second location; they also have one in Flushing. I visited for an early dinner and tried a bunch of skewers and some other dishes with a friend, and we were pretty happy with the food we got.Favorites:-Garlic oyster ($6.99)-Garlic eggplant ($6.99)-Pork intestine ($5.99 for 3)Also good:-Lamb (with fat) ($4.99 for 3)-Grilled quail ($4.99)-Grilled potato noodle from the specials menu ($2.99 for 5)-Pork belly ($4.99 for 3)-Gizzards ($4.99 for 3)-Grilled pork feet ($2.99)-Xinjiang special lamb ($3.49) - this is apparently their specialty but we actually liked the regular lamb skewers more. The seasoning was delicious but the fatty parts were too stringy.

Title: Overpriced and Over-Spiced: A Disappointing Takeout Experience

I recently decided to try takeout from a local eatery, lured by the promise of convenient delivery after a frustratingly long wait period. While the online ordering process was smooth and delivery was a plus, the food itself left much to be desired, especially considering the steep prices. The chicken and garlic dish, a seemingly simple item on the lunch menu, was priced at an exorbitant $10.00. To add insult to injury, it was excessively spicy, detracting from the overall taste and enjoyment. For those counting their pennies, this establishment, which seems to have aspirations of grandeur, won't be claiming a portion of my earnings anytime soon. In summary, I was not impressed by the balance of cost and quality, and I'll be looking elsewhere for my lunchtime fixes.

Title: A Delightful Deli Experience at 2nd Ave Deli

After multiple curious glances, I finally succumbed to the local buzz and ventured into 2nd Ave Deli. The rave reviews had piqued my interest, particularly for the legendary pastrami sandwich and matzoh ball soup. Opting for the half sandwich and soup special seemed like a winning choice.

From the moment I ordered, the hospitality was palpable; the staff offered sample slices of pastrami, confident in their claim that I'd fall for the flavor. Their confidence wasn’t misplaced. The hot pastrami sandwich was exceptional. As someone who's typically ambivalent about pastrami, I was converted by the tender slices hugged by soft, warm rye bread, the seasoning creating a perfect balance without overwhelming saltiness.

The matzoh ball soup, hailed as "Jewish penicillin," lived up to its comforting reputation. It stood out as one of the most satisfying chicken soups I've had in recent memory, with a delicious broth and the soothing warmth of matzoh balls. The side of challah bread added another layer of enjoyment to the meal.

2nd Ave Deli delivered an experience that was both delightful and delicious, proving that sometimes the crowd really does know best.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at Amy Ruth's

Having previously sampled Amy Ruth's fare at a catered event, which left both me and my sister unimpressed, I approached my first dine-in experience at the eatery with modest expectations. I visited on a busy Sunday afternoon with a party of eight. Despite a slight hiccup with their policy of not seating incomplete parties, we were comfortably seated at a round table after a brief wait, a conducive setting for engaging conversation amongst us.

The array of dishes ordered by my family included smothered turkey wings, chicken wings, whiting fish, and baked catfish, accompanied by sides like collard greens, mashed potatoes, string beans, mac & cheese, yams, and okra. The consensus was that the meals were satisfying, with the sharp cheddar in the mac & cheese standing out particularly.

My sister and I found the gravy on the baked catfish – an unusual addition for the dish – and the lukewarm onions and peppers a bit puzzling. Nonetheless, the rest of the meal was enjoyable. The complimentary cornbread was a delightful touch, and the drink selection, including half & half, hot tea, and Corona, catered to our varied preferences.

Service was commendable; our waitress was attentive, and our meals were served promptly despite our large party size. The staff also efficiently handled post-meal clean-up and offered to-go boxes for leftovers.

The dining experience at Amy Ruth's surpassed our earlier catered encounter, with the restaurant delivering good food and excellent service. It was a reminder that sometimes, a second chance can lead to a pleasant surprise.

So. Damn. Good. The rockaway is to die for!!! It doesn't have any topping but the sauce was so good that I don't even want toppings!!!! 5/5!!Tamarindo was good too. Good amount of mushroom but a little too oily tho cus of the truffle oil. Not as shocking as rockaway but still super good. 5/5We had two pizzas and a beer. The bill came out to be $49. Not toooooo cheap but reasonable!!

Title: Cozy Vibes and Stellar Service at Our Neighborhood Gem

Review:

Stepping into this bustling local haunt on a Monday night, we were greeted by energy befitting a weekend. My friends and I quickly understood why - the place is a classic neighborhood favorite.

Our server, Kiril, managed to shine despite the packed scene. Friendly doesn't quite capture the essence of his service; he was exceptional, making recommendations with genuine enthusiasm and never rushing us. He was particularly knowledgeable about the latest menu additions.

The octopus was a standout, melting in our mouths—definitely a must-try. The eggplant Parmesan was another revelation; its sauce garnered unanimous praise and had us wishing we could pair it with every dish, especially the fried seafood.

Adding to the harmony of flavors, the beet and goat cheese salad was the perfect palate cleanser—crisp and refreshing.

Then came the entrees: The rib eye steak was a juicy delight accompanied by perfectly cooked broccoli rabe and roasted garlic. A good carbonara can be judged by its simplicity and execution, and theirs ticked all the boxes. The mushroom ravioli's creamy sauce had us all nodding in approval, and while the rigatoni with braised beef was delectable, a bit more sauce would have made it impeccable.

Desserts were a grand finale not to be missed. The Nutella Calzone's size is a warning and a challenge, while the ricotta tart with strawberries was astonishingly light and a favorite at our table. The olive cake was decent, airy and delicate, though not a showstopper. The tiramisu, while tasty, didn't quite reach the pedestal we had placed it on beforehand.

In summary, this dining experience was a delightful showcase of Italian cuisine that made for an amazing evening with friends. Reservations are a wise move here, but walk-ins are warmly accommodated. A big shoutout to Kiril for elevating our dining experience; we left with full stomachs and wide smiles.

Title: A Meat Lover's Haven with Stellar Service at YHG

I had the pleasure of dining at YHG on a rainy Saturday afternoon for a casual lunch with friends, and it did not disappoint. With a reservation via Yelp, we took advantage of the bar's weekend lunch-priced drinks, enjoying a well-priced $10 mimosa before being seated.

From the moment we sat down, YHG's service shone. We were promptly presented with water and an assortment of banchan, setting the stage for the feast to come. The food was truly the star of the show; we indulged in the premium and haeundae packages, savoring every bite, particularly the sumptuous wagyu beef. Additional delights like the pork belly kimchi stew and crispy fried mandu elevated the meal further, as the attached photos attest.

Service remained top-notch throughout our visit. When we mentioned a birthday at our table, our waiter surprised us with a birthday treat—a beautifully plated mochi and fruit arrangement, adding a sweet touch to the celebration.

The ambiance at YHG is inviting, making it suitable for intimate dates, or a relaxed meal with friends or family. It’s quite spacious, which is a refreshing change from other, more cramped establishments.

In summary, YHG stands out with its quality meats, excellent service, and inviting atmosphere—a must-visit for anyone looking for a premier dining experience.

On a recommendation we stopped in to have a cool treat on a hot humid day. With refreshing gelato and amazing Sorbetto you can relax, unwind and reboot before facing the busy streets of NY. The raspberry paired with the lime and basil was divine and a perfect stop on our weekend away.

Title: A Night to Remember at a Vibrant Latin Eatery

My dining experience at this restaurant was nothing short of spectacular! From the moment my group of 10 arrived, we were swiftly seated by an attentive staff that made us feel welcomed and cared for. The service was impressively quick, with our delightful waitress ensuring our evening was perfect.

The decor of the place added to the lively atmosphere, enhancing the already festive ambiance. Settled on the second floor amidst the buzz of fellow diners, the venue's Latin music set the tone for a celebratory evening, as we were there for both a birthday and a farewell.

Our choice to share a variety of appetizers was a triumph, each dish more delicious than the last. The standout was undoubtedly the guacamole – a sublime balance of flavor that wasn't overly salty or spicy. It hit the right notes of spice and acidity, leaving everyone craving more.

We indulged in several Margarita Towers, which were both sweet and deceptively strong—a heads-up to future patrons to sip responsibly!

In summary, this restaurant is a gem I'm eager to return to. It left a lasting impression with its upbeat environment, flavorsome food, and exceptional service. Highly recommended for a memorable group gathering!

Title: Unparalleled Unagi at Hachibei - A New York Gem

Finding quality unagi in New York can be quite the culinary quest, but Hachibei stands out as a treasure trove for eel enthusiasts. Hachibei's commitment to freshness transforms each dish into a delightful experience, setting a new standard for this Japanese delicacy in the city.

The menu, while eel-centric, offers pleasing variations. While you can't go wrong with the classic Kabayaki, the showstopper is undoubtedly the Hitsumabushi, which presents grilled eel in three distinct, mouthwatering ways. It's the epitome of unagi preparation, and each bite underscores the unmistakable superiority of fresh, authentically cooked eel over its lackluster, frozen counterparts.

To cap off the meal, dive into Hachibei's dessert offerings—they're simply dope. Whether you're an unagi aficionado or a curious foodie, Hachibei delivers an unparalleled eel experience that's not to be missed.

Title: A Cozy Spot for Ramen Lovers in K-Town

I recently ventured into a new ramen joint in K-Town and the experience was quite delightful. The setup, which included both bar stools and tables, caters to solo diners and groups alike. Opting for the bar stool, I enjoyed the live kitchen view, watching the chefs skillfully blanch noodles and blend sauces.

The menu boasted a variety of tempting ramen options, and I settled on the spicy miso ramen, seizing the opportunity for a free order of chicken wings by checking in. The wings, despite being complimentary, were a highlight; four pieces of well-marinated, succulent chicken with a perfectly crispy exterior.

The ramen itself was served with generous portions of fatty chashu, soft-boiled egg, bamboo, among other classic toppings. While the broth was rich and satisfying, the spice level was mild. A tip for spice enthusiasts: request the chili sauce for an extra kick. At an affordable price, the meal was hearty and left me already planning my next visit to sample more from their menu. A definite must-try spot for ramen aficionados!

Title: Lovely Cuisine and Ambiance Marred by Miscommunication

I was initially captivated by this restaurant's delightful ambiance and the exceptional quality of their food. During my first visit, I craved something light and was thrilled to find the perfect snack-size portion of massaman curry. Eager to return for their lunch special, I made a point to call ahead and was informed it lasted until 4:30 pm.

Unfortunately, my excitement turned to disappointment when I arrived at 4 pm, only to be turned away because the restaurant was closing for an hour. This was particularly frustrating after being told over the phone that I would still have time to enjoy the lunch special. The lack of accurate information provided and the unexpected midday closure not only inconvenienced me but also came across as disrespectful.

Ultimately, I took my appetite to Thai Market instead. While I am still fond of the food and the atmosphere offered by this restaurant, my experience was tarnished by the miscommunication. I hope they can align their customer communication with their actual operating hours. An improvement in transparency would certainly make me consider giving them another chance.

Title: A New Challenger in the Curry Game - Abiko Wins Big

As a devout lover of Thai, Malaysian, and Indian curries, my culinary horizons were recently expanded with my first foray into Japanese curry at Abiko - and what a revelation it was! The curry platter I indulged in was nothing short of astounding. Opting for a basic curry rice plate, I topped it with a chicken cutlet that was the epitome of tender perfection, encased in an immaculate breading. But the true game-changer was the addition of super melty cheese and a sprinkle of green onions and garlic flakes, which I highly recommend. The melty cheese, when mingled with the curry and rice, was the stuff of foodie dreams.

Importantly, the curry itself shone through with its savoriness, not marred by any unwanted MSG aftertaste. A tip for fellow diners: stick to a mild spice level to ensure the delicate, rich flavors of the curry remain unobscured by the heat.

In terms of service, Abiko was top-notch, delivering both speed and friendliness that matched the quality of the food. The pricing - a critical factor for any college student - was reasonable, posing no threat to a budget-conscious wallet. The ambiance of the place, casual and comfortable, offered spacious seating that only enhanced the experience.

To cut it short - I rate both the food and service a solid 5 out of 5. Abiko is a definite must-return and comes highly recommended for anyone looking to expand their curry repertoire or just in search of a delightful meal.

Love this as a go to for lunch! Their line can get long but they keep it moving pretty quick. It gets loud so you often can't hear what the makers are asking and vice versa. The crispy chicken poblano was delish, the dressing has the perfect amount of kick. And I love the idea of the reusable bowl! Can't wait to try more

This place is so great, I want to selfishly keep it a secret, but who am I kidding? In this day and age, it's impossible to keep anything a secret from the public ... ESPECIALLY when its damn good, so here goes another review.Like a cliché, Izakaya Juraku is absolutely one of those hidden gems located on a rather unassuming part of Ludlow Street in the LES. When I think of hot spot Izakayas for an after work happy hour, the LES has never even come close to mind ... until now!I dropped in on a Friday evening after work as part of a group of six people and the place was nearly empty when I arrived at 5:45pm. I had actually made a reservation via Yelp because you never know if a restaurant is crowded, but, honestly, I felt like a slight fool when I walked in since there was barely a soul. However, by 7-7:30pm, the restaurant was PACKED and by the time we left at 8:30pm, the restaurant pretty much indirectly kicked us out because there was a wait forming by the extremely narrow entrance. We drank the 1st half of the night away there for 3 hours, so we completely understood.Like all Izakayas, the menu was many pages and comprised of many different tapa-style dishes. Just about everything is meant to be shared here, except for the bigger dishes, like the noodle and rice dishes. And for those here purely for happy hour, you'll be glad to know that happy hour runs until 8pm, with a set happy hour menu of appetizers and drinks. As a group, we kind of just ordered whatever we thought sounded good - from both the happy hour menu and regular menu. Here's a quick run through of the damage we did here, with some being ordered multiple times. Also, I've added some quick one-liners of the things we really liked ... or were memorable (good or bad):TARO CHIPSBEEF SKEWERSCHICKEN THIGH SKEWERSPORK BELLY AND ONION SKEWERS - Each order comes with 5 skewers so there is plenty to go around. Definitely very tasty, tender and the best of the 3 type of skewers we ordered.FRIED SHISHITO - We ordered 2 of these happy hour dishes and each order was much bigger than we anticipated. If you love shishito, these were great. The ones with the seeds do have a small kick, so be warned.TAKOYAKIGYOZA - Another happy hour menu fave. Simple, delicious and, best of all, there were 5 pieces to every order.AGEDASHI TOFU - The pieces of tofu were big and delicious. Not everyone is a tofu lover, but everyone who did try it, loved it.KARA-AGE - For those not in the know, basically fried chicken with a side of spicy mayo. Who doesn't love them some fried chicken? Enough said.GRILLED SQUIDANBAI MISO BACON - Interesting on paper, but was quite ordinary when it met it's demise in my mouth. The presentation was interesting though as it was served on top of a heated pot, sort of like a small makeshift grill.Besides the food, there were a few drink standouts too, notably the Hokkaido Melon Ale. It was light, refreshing and actually tasted good. It's not on the happy hour menu of drinks, so you will have to dole out a little more for it, but it's worth it!Izakaya Juraku will definitely be somewhere I will be keeping in mind if I needed a get together spot in the LES. The space isn't huge, but if you get here early enough, there are plenty of tables and seats for small and large parties. Our waiter throughout the evening was also excellent and very accommodating. In addition, the noise level was surprisingly reasonable for an Izakaya and not deafening by any means. I don't see a reason why I won't be back at some point.

As I write this. I'm trying to be lenient as we are in unprecedented times but I was not satisfied with my visit to lighthouse today, especially for the prices that they charge. There was supposed to be a limit of 7 people in their small space at a time. They finally abided by it after we reached about 10 people inside for the second or third time. My steamed food was underseasoned, I received the wrong side - an odd tricolored macaroni salad at that - and they would've forgotten my banana pudding had I not reminded them again when I was finally able to grab my order, 30 minutes after ordering. I've been here a number of time so the disorder while ordering and waiting isn't new but the food used to make up for it. Now, that's not the case. Oh, and to add to the disappointment, they were cash only today.

Upon my second visit to this vibrant new Israeli cafe, I found myself enveloped in the same warm and dynamic atmosphere reminiscent of a bustling Tel Aviv eatery. The proprietors, a trio of Israelis, have certainly captured the essence of their homeland. Without hesitation, I ordered the Jaffa hummus and Matzo Ball soup, which have quickly become my go-to favorites. The pita arrives warm, sprinkled generously with sesame seeds, offering the perfect companion to the silky, rich hummus. Meanwhile, the Matzo Ball soup, with its flavor of tradition, feels like a comforting embrace from a grandmother's kitchen—a rarity in this part of town. The cafe's inspiring motto to elevate their offerings by 10 percent daily only promises even greater pleasures ahead. Eagerly anticipating the launch of their evening hours, I look forward to exploring their salad options on my next dinner visit.

I recently dined at a pleasant restaurant with a decent ambiance, but I cannot recommend it for those with food allergies. As someone with a shellfish allergy, I inquired about safe menu options; however, despite the precautions, I still experienced an allergic reaction by the end of my meal. On a positive note, the food quality was good—the pork and beef combo was particularly delicious.
