However, diners should be aware that the kimchi soup is quite spicy, a detail I would have appreciated knowing in advance. Patrons with dietary restrictions should proceed with caution.

Title: A Fun-Filled Noodle Extravaganza at Kung Fu Kitchen!

I recently had the pleasure of attending the "Hand Pulled Noodle Making 101" at Kung Fu Kitchen, and it was an absolute delight! As a first-timer at the restaurant, I'm already excited to return for a full dining experience.

The workshop was brilliantly structured into three comprehensive sections. We started with an awe-inspiring demonstration by a true noodle master who made the complex art of noodle pulling look effortless. Not only did he perform magic with the dough, but he was also fantastic at teaching the technique in a simplified manner for us novices.

Next, we got hands-on, trying our hand at making our very own noodles. The staff was incredibly supportive, providing individual attention and assistance whenever we hit a snag.

The cherry on top was the final section, where we got to savor the fruits of our labor. The noodles were cooked to perfection, and I was particularly impressed by the thoughtful inclusion of a vegetarian broth option.

Overall, the event was both educational and entertaining, offering a deeper appreciation for the intricate art of noodle-making. Kudos to Kung Fu Kitchen for a memorable experience!

Title: A Flavor Revelation at an Unassuming NYC Cart

During a recent visit to the World Trade Center area, my quest for a quick bite led me to a modest food cart near the iconic red cube sculpture. Craving the shish kabob kathi roll which was regrettably sold out, I settled for the chicken kathi roll. This decision proved to be serendipitous, as it turned out to be the best kathi roll I've had to date.

The roll boasted succulent chicken tikka enveloped in a sweet homemade paratha, generously smothered with a tricolor of delectable sauces. At a mere $6, the portion, resembling sizable burritos, offered more than enough to satiate.

Compelled by the tantalizing flavors, I ventured back the next day, only to find the shish kabob kathi roll eluding me once more. Undeterred, I revisited the chicken kathi roll and branched out to the chili chicken & lamb over rice. The repeat performance of the kathi roll did not disappoint, and the chili chicken dish surpassed any I've ever had, easily outshining those from back home in North Carolina.

Moreover, the Indian King cart sets itself apart by accepting credit cards, a convenience not offered by many street vendors.

For anyone in NYC, this cart is a non-negotiable stop. The exceptional eats are a testament to the city's elevated street food game. Trust me, your palate will thank you.

This chain consistently delivers an awesome lobster roll experience that rivals seaside establishments. With its perfectly toasted signature bread cradling fresh, flavorful lobster, each Manhattan location ensures a solid, satisfying bite. It’s no wonder they're a go-to for lobster roll aficionados in the city.

I order from here pretty regularly because they're convenient to my office. I can tell you now, though, that that has ended. I will never order from here again.I put a SIMPLE note in my order of Pork Lo Mein - "no vegetables" - it's so simple. So. So. So. Simple. And this isn't the first time they have messed it up. Arrives and dumplings are perfect, I eat them, and crack open the lo mein - it's basically half veggies. I am 9m pregnant and have Crohn's - this is too much for me but I have no choice. I contacted GrubHub support who reached out to the restaurant.They offered to exchange the food for a new order - but considering it took the full delivery time to begin with and I have meetings, I literally do not have time to wait for this BS to be re-delivered. Then they say in order to refund me, they'd need the food back. The food I have been forced to start eating so I don't pass out from hunger and that they would just throw away anyway.Such a simple request to begin with and then they handled it absolutely poorly from a CS perspective. Giving me a credit or partial refund shouldn't have been that hard - so in the future I just won't bother. There's too many Chinese food options in this city to deal with cheapskates who can't follow simple requests.

We went in late night around 12-ish. It looked like a cool place to grab a quick bite before heading home. They sat us in the back dining room. There were maybe 4 other tables there at the most. We sat there for 15 minutes without anyone coming over to us at all. We just got up and left. I do not see how they expect people to dine there if you cannot get anyone to come to help you out.Not going back.

Title: "Delicious Italian Fare Worth the Wait"

Review:
I'm pleased to rate this gem of an Italian restaurant with a strong 4.5 out of 5, despite a bit of a wait for service. The culinary experience was exceptional. The spaghetti and meatballs were classic and flavorful, the calamari was cooked to perfection, and the tricolor Campbelle added a delightful twist to our meal. The highlight was the cocoa cannoli for dessert – an absolute must-try! Generous portions at reasonable prices made the dining experience even more satisfying. I wholeheartedly recommend this spot for anyone in search of top-notch Italian cuisine. Just be prepared for a slower pace of service – trust me, the wait is worthwhile.

Title: Quirky Spot with a Need for Cleanliness and Space

My recent visit to this establishment offered a mix of impressions. The service was commendable and the drinks hit the mark with reasonable prices. The interior had a unique charm, though it clearly begs for a thorough scrub and decor refresh.

Although I didn't sample the food, the menu suggested typical pub grub that would likely satisfy after a couple of pints. However, the establishment loses points, unfortunately, due to the deplorable condition of the restrooms. These tiny, neglected spaces challenge even the not-so-tall or slightly broader patrons, raising serious accessibility and comfort concerns. The lack of functional soap dispensers was the last straw in an already disappointing scenario.

In sum, while you might pop in for a casual drink, be warned—the bathrooms are a dire adventure on their own. Two stars out of five for the service and drinks, but I'd think twice before returning.

nice little pizza shop in flatiron. cracker thin pies that come in 3 sizes: small, med, and large. I have been a fan of Chef Waldy since I first visited Beacon Restaurant, which is now closed. They served a really fine filet with red wine reduction and wild mushrooms. Definitely one the best steaks I've had. Too bad it has closed. It goes to show you how fickle the restaurant business is. I'm happy that this casual concept is still around. Good and relatively light meal.

Title: A Happy Hour Haven

Review:

My friends and I recently decided to check out the local happy hour scene and stumbled upon a gem that truly knows its way around a cocktail shaker. The drinks here are show-stoppers, and the frozen margarita packs a punch strong enough that one is all you need. Every one of us was impressed with the quality and potency - a rare find these days. Beyond the excellence in mixology, the prices were a steal, making it even sweeter. While we didn't dive into the food menu, the dishes passing by looked appetizing and are on my radar for the next visit. A little tip for the adventurous: the strawberry and guava flavored margaritas are a tropical twist that will not disappoint. This place is definitely on my list for a return visit. Cheers to fantastic happy hours!

Following a friend's recommendation, I ventured to this bustling spot for a Saturday night dinner around 7 pm, prepared for a significant wait — a full hour before we could sit down. Service was brisk upon entry; a attentive waitress promptly took our order and expertly navigated us through the noodle selections, ultimately swaying me towards the crowd-favorite chicken paitan with its promise of a rich broth. The noodle dish was somewhat surprising, featuring miswa-like thin yet pleasingly chewy noodles in a generous pool of savory broth, although the chicken portions were scant. My companion's choice, the spicy ramen, despite forewarnings, fell short on the heat scale.

Thankfully, the restaurant accommodates the plastic-preferent diners, as credit cards are accepted (noteworthy in a city peppered with cash-only spots), but those seeking a digital connection will find themselves out of luck — no WiFi here. The ambiance, however, offered a visual feast with its eclectic, art-splattered walls adding a vibrant flair to the dining experience.

In summation, while the place serves up a decent bowl of ramen, it stands as one option among the culinary mosaic of New York City — great for a visit but with ample competition inviting exploration.

Went to Flex Mussels for Saturday happy hour. Solid seafood dishes and a daily happy hour make this a great spot to grab an early dinner.Quality: Flex Mussels is all about big tasty pots of mussels. With over twenty different flavors, varied in broths and add-ins, there are plenty of interesting and appetizing options. We selected the Bisque Mussels, which came with a tomato, brandy, and cream sauce with big chunks of lobster on top. It was extremely savory, and dipping warm bread into the broth was an incredible way to finish the dish. We also took advantage of happy hour to grab some Happy Hour Oysters, from the east coast, and the Crab Guacamole. Both made for good snacks to complement our main course.Quantity: Despite the lighter seafood options, still a very filling meal.Value: $1.50 for Happy Hour Oysters. $12 for Happy Hour Crab Guacamole. $30 for the Bisque Mussels.Ambiance: Flex Mussels has two locations, but we visited the one on the Upper East Side of Manhattan. The restaurant is split into two, with the bar area at the front and the more formal dining area in the back. Happy hour is restricted to the bar, so we grabbed two seats along the mirrored wall across from the bar to dig in. This area of the restaurant is much more upbeat than the dining room, and made for a good time. They also had some fun global music playing, which enhanced the vibe.Crowd: Extremely popular on Saturday evening. The bar area was packed for happy hour and the regular dining area was full within an hour of opening.Service: Solid service even with a busy crowd.Parking: Tough to find street parking in the area.

I had the Al pastor tacos which were good! I do wish that it would've been pineapple pieces instead of one chunk of pineapple which was kind of weird. Friendly staff, and nice environment. Theres only one small 2 seater table and the rest is standing room only.

First, pay homage to Restaurant Week! This place has a creative menu and great layout. From the fresh ceviche to the incredible pot de creme, it was fantastic.  I had the queso fundido and I found the cheese to be a little thick. But the chef more than redeemed themselves with the incredible tacos and the cod that my friend had. Good work!

During a recent lunch outing, I had the opportunity to try the clam pasta. Presentation-wise, the dish was impressive with a generous portion of clams and pasta. However, the flavor fell a bit short, as the garlic sauce lacked sufficient seasoning, particularly salt. Additionally, while complimentary bread was provided, it was underwhelming on its own. A simple offering of olive oil or a similar dip would greatly enhance the experience.

Title: Mixed Impressions at a Trendy Spot

My recent lunch experience at this restaurant was a mixed bag. We kicked things off with appetizers of edamame and fried shrimp which set a promising start. However, when it came to beverages, the lychee martini fell short on its namesake flavor.

The main courses were a hit-or-miss affair; while the steak packed more heat than expected, the short ribs were satisfying, although the accompanying broth lacked depth. The shared dessert, a matcha cake, was a letdown as it clearly wasn't homemade and disappointingly came from the freezer. A more adventurous choice like green tea or red bean ice cream might have been a better pairing than the mundane vanilla served.

Ambiance-wise, the restaurant needs to fine-tune its acoustics as the blaring music was more of a distraction than an enhancement. Additionally, the slow elevator made accessing the basement level cumbersome, especially for those requiring handicap access. Practicalities like coat and bag storage were overlooked, though a small shelf under the table offered minimal reprieve.

In summary, while the restaurant managed to deliver some culinary highs, the overall experience was dampened by several missteps ranging from flavor profiles to functional amenities.

5/5 I loved this place so much!! If you're in New York and enjoy Broadway, you can pretty much get a show and eat all at the same time at this diner!! The atmosphere was so lively and fun, all the servers alternated performing for the diners and all I can say is it was so worth it to come here!  I had the best time watching with my friends, so much talent and work put into making the guests entertained. From duets to group performances to confetti dropped from the ceilings, this was definitely an experience I enjoyed. The food was alright too! I got the philly cheese steak sandwich, but I also enjoyed the waffle fries that comes with it. Some interesting items on the menu I wish I had tried like the mac and cheese burger. Don't let the long lines scare you, I would def recommend this place!

Underwhelming. Somehow, this feels like Japanese food made by someone's mom who was not a good cook and was improvising ingredients.Takoyaki reminded me of a fried onion ring with chewy octopus. There was no gooey center, the whole ball was fried into a hardened chunk.There was barely any pork belly in the grilled pork belly dish. it was 70-80% just onions and bean sprouts. The pork belly looked more steamed than grilled.The gyoza looked super tiny and probably out of a package.The fried beef tongue lacked tasted and came with a side of broccoli and watercress. Kinda odd paring. Like someone just threw stuff onto a dish from items in the fridge.Miso beef skewer tasted find, but it was placed on top of large pieces of cabbage, not the most appealing look.Service was good, but the food was just unimpressive.

There are a million things that I am so freaking thankful for in my life and one of them is definitely the fact that I live so dang close to Benson's NYC. I've probably been there at least twice a month since I first discovered this gem last year and I have to say it's all because of their Peppercorn Burger.Now, the patty itself is a work of wonder, as it is flavored flawlessly in all its juicy, peppercorn goodness, but coupled with the ciabatta roll, ranch sauce and the most delicious CRISPY ONION RINGS ever and you pretty much have what all my dreams are made of. Seriously.Always thankful for you, Benson's NYC. Never move kthx.

A great hole in the wall serving takeout of traditional cold rolled rice noodles topped with minced pork, dried shrimp, scallions. This authentic and humble dish is done right and if you are in the area looking for a filling snack that is actually "real" chinese food you should definitely stop in.

Title: A Brunch to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

I recently visited [Restaurant Name] for their Sunday brunch and it was an absolute delight. The unlimited food and drink offer for $50 per person is a steal, considering the quality and the variety. Every dish was a delicious journey, complemented perfectly by their refreshing drinks.

The waitstaff, especially our waiter, elevated the experience with their fantastic service — attentive, speedy, and always with a smile. The restaurant's spaciousness, including a welcoming upstairs area, makes it ideal for big groups or special occasions.

Though I would have relished a wider sushi selection, the existing spread didn’t disappoint. [Restaurant Name] has nailed the art of brunch, making it not just a meal, but a celebration.

I recently indulged in an unforgettable dining experience at a local gem renowned for its Middle Eastern flavors. The hummus served was excellent—a smooth, rich, and savory treat. However, the star of the meal was undoubtedly the falafel. As a frequent falafel enthusiast, I can confidently say these are the best I've savored in New York, rivaling those I've enjoyed in my culinary travels. Their Israeli-style falafel is a marvel of textures, boasting an impossibly crispy exterior that gives way to a warm, flavorful, and herbaceous interior. 

Additionally, the house-made mint tea, featuring real mint leaves, provided a refreshing complement to the meal. My only lament is the limited reach of this culinary haven—I'm eager for an expansion, perhaps a location on the east side, to make these delights more accessible.

It was like someone answered our prayers on a savagely cold night. It was 20 degrees outside and Pho was the perfect meal to devour on.Pho noodle soup with coconut curry and fish is a great dish to pick, if you need something filling yet light on the stomach. The soup was piping hot, spicy and delicious, accompanying rice noodles were soft and well cooked while the tender pieces of fish only added to the wonderful texture and taste.Vegetable spring rolls were heavenly; crisped to perfection and filled with medium cooked vegetables. I have found the perfect pho joint in my neighborhood. However I didn't give it 5 Stars coz the place is kind of small and tight, not the best interior. They could do away with a table to two to make it more comfortable for their customers but the food more than makes up for it.

Seamores is a preppy-looking seafood spot just above Little Italy. Their previous long waits deterred me, but on a recent Friday night they were looking a bit empty and my boyfriend and I snagged a patio table on a whim.The menu is broad and crowd-pleasing, with dishes like fish and chips, lobster rolls, fish tacos, and shrimp pasta rounded out with vegetarian and carnivore offerings. The daily specials list notes the seafood offerings for the tacos (seared or crispy), oysters, and "reel deal," their grilled fish meal. You can be as healthy or unhealthy as you want here. We opted for a middle ground, starting with some kind of matcha- and coconut-based cocktail, which was perfectly fine.I was feeling something lighter so I went for the shrimp skewer ($12ish)... my mistake, as it was literally four pieces of shrimp on a smear of sour cream. Great flavor, but laughable value. I ended up mostly munching on the excellent sweet potato fries.My boyfriend fared better with the "reel deal" ($24), made with the fish of the day that our waiter described the most appetizingly. The fish itself was great with a good portion size. We weren't wild about the miso brown butter (a bit sweet), and the sides were all healthy but middle of the road.Service is strong. The interior is bright and Hamptons-chic, and the menus are well-designed. Beer and wine are easy-drinking and beach-friendly, following the theme. Just a sunny little spot. Patio is great for people watching.Very tempting happy hour; I would definitely try them out for that it I was in the area. As it is, it's good quality seafood cooked well for a premium price. Definitely reliable but nothing out of the ordinary for New York.

We finally had a chance to stop by the highly mentioned Emmy Squared. The location accommodates several small groups. Very clean and super friendly staff . My husband tried some odd fries with fish shaving over the top, they were not my favorite perhaps, because I don't like fish very much. We shared a traditional pie no toppings it was actually very good. I am sure you will find something on the menu for everyone. They also offer burgers and fries a couple at the neighboring table ordered it, and they seem to have enjoyed the combo.  The price point is NYC average. Try a square pie.

My dad had gotten a banquet options so instead of choosing individual dishes, it is already sort out for you based on the event and this time it was for birthday event.This location been around for quite a while perhaps more than 28 years, but they did renovations and changed owners/chef and definitely can say its for the better. The authentic Chinese food is absolutely delicious, you may ask them to do less oil/no msg. They'll try to cater to you as much as they can. The waiters/waitress are super friendly. It can get crowded at night or during holidays. ``

I was extremely excited to try this place. Unfortunately I was disappointed . Let's begin with the service. I waited about 15 min for a menu and water. The manager who was older Hispanic male was very unpleasant. Next the food , we ordered carne asada tacos and the taco tower. Tacos were fine. The taco tower not so much. It was missing a touch of something. Very bland . The taco tower did not look like anything that the restaurant advertises. Not to mention the meat within the taco tower was not fully cooked.  Some parts of the tower the meat was pink.  Very disappointed especially traveling two hours to come eat here.  There were no specials such as happy hour. This restaurant didn't seem too customer friendly . More so for the looks and the money. The space and ambiance was nice. Overall some improvements can be made.

Title: A Cozy Retreat for Korean Comfort Food - Gogi 37 Review

During a brisk fall-winter day in NYC, I stumbled upon Gogi 37, a Korean eatery nestled near Times Square. The timing was impeccable – a lull between lunch and dinner meant I had the place almost to myself. Gogi 37's ambiance is immediately welcoming, with a contemporary, uncluttered design that invites diners to relax.

Opting for a seat at the bar, I was met with prompt service. Craving warmth, I went straight for the Kimchi Jjigae, though the mandu and japchae nearly swayed me. Thankfully, the heartening array of ban chan that accompanied my choice convinced me I'd made the right call. The jjigae arrived steaming and satisfying – a robust blend of kimchi, onion, pork, tofu, gochugaru, and glass noodles, alongside a comforting bowl of rice, all for a reasonable $12, especially given the Times Square locale.

While the menu boasted tempting Korean ramyum and a well-crafted lunch box set, my focus remained on the generous, flavorsome jjigae. Although I didn't delve into the Korean BBQ – a decision partly influenced by solo dining – the potential for a communal grill experience in the future wasn't lost on me.

Without hesitation, Gogi 37 earns a spot on my NYC itinerary for a return visit. Its promise of a quick, delectable dolsot bibimbap when time won't allow a K-town detour is too enticing to ignore. For anyone in the area, it's a must-try for a taste of Korean comfort.

Title: A Mexican Gem in NYC

I recently dined at my favorite Mexican spot in NYC and it did not disappoint. Despite its popularity, we were seated immediately. We started with the flavorful corn on the cob and fresh yellowfin tuna appetizers, followed by succulent braised beef tacos, delectable de lechon tacos, and a hearty egg burrito with steak – each dish an absolute delight. The prices were reasonable for the quality received. This restaurant is also perfectly located for a pre-matinee meal. A minor inconvenience is the single bathroom upstairs, which can mean a bit of a wait, but this small detail doesn't detract from the overall exceptional experience. Highly recommend for anyone looking for authentic Mexican cuisine in the city!

I recently visited an absolute gem of a vegetarian spot that left me thoroughly impressed. The highlight was, without a doubt, their veggie burger – quite possibly the best I've ever tasted. It's uncanny how they've managed to capture the essence of a traditional beef burger in a plant-based patty; the flavors are spot-on.

The eatery itself is small and cozy, with just a handful of seats arranged along the walls, which means you might find yourself queueing up upon entry. The space can feel a bit cramped, especially during the dinner rush, as there's minimal room for waiting due to the constant line of hungry diners.

For those looking to try their ever-changing culinary delights, I highly recommend staying updated via their Instagram. The menu rotates often, with special items making frequent appearances. Plus, for the vegan crowd, there's the bonus of being able to veganize any dish that isn't already plant-based. Despite the limited space, the food quality and variety make it worth a visit.

Hey Tony and Doug!Sorry it took me five years to come back!  But I needed a late night slice and I knew just where to go!  Congrats on your expansion!  Loved my healthy spinach and pepperoni!!!  LOL!Till next time!xoxomikey

I recently visited a charming Mexican restaurant in Williamsburg that truly captured my heart. As a Manhattanite not prone to frequent cross-borough adventures, I was pleasantly surprised. This spot boasts a chill, relaxed atmosphere that is ideal for winding down on a Friday night. The affordability of both food and drinks adds to its appeal. If you're in the mood for a round of margaritas, tacos, and scrumptious nachos amidst good company, this is the place to be. Highly recommend for those looking to delve into the Williamsburg food scene.

- Navya J @nyconthetable

Really dont need to write this review because the 2K reviews explains it all. AMAZING. First, Chelsea market is awesome! Loved the crowd and all the vendors there. Came over after a long relaxing time at the Starbucks Reserve. Anyway, as soon as you walk into Chelsea market maybe 20 steps this place is on your left. If you happen to walk past or dont see it just look for a VERY longg line of people. This line moves fassst. So how does it all work? Its daunting at first once you get to the counter. You order the tacos and pay (cash or card!). They give you the receipt and you burrow through the crowd to the waiting area. Now you must "push" past the people who like to eat their tacos right at the counter so you can give your ticket to the taco makers lol. Once you do this just keep your eye on the taco man so you get your food. Once you get your tacos you may have to "push" again to get to add on toppings of your choice - salsa, fresh limes, etc. If ya dont want any of this then your next task is finding somewhere to eat!Please dont sit next door. I saw many ppl asked to move because they didnt buy food from that vendor. Chelsea market has many standing counters to eat at. I found one maybe 2-3 minutes away from Los Tacos looking inside  a fish market? I dont know but I got great views of somebody eating a whole huge lobster while I ate my delicious tacos.So back to the tacos..... I ordered one of each tacos con todo (with all toppings). I appreciated the extra foil/paper wrapped around the tacos because it got a bit messy. Just FYI you can order flour or corn shells. I got corn. My favorite was the pork taco. Very tender. Awesome with the corn shell. The guac was ok nothing special. Chips and salsa yummy! Felt like the chips were a good palette cleaner/mellower (?) between some rather spicy notes from my tacos. Phenomenal tacos!!

Extraordinary in quite a few ways but, as is so much as Hudson Yards, exceptionally average for ultra luxury, in other ways.  It's not so much that one can point a finger at specific issues, but Tavern is not an experience that will last forever in memory.The Tavern begins with entrance into a revolving door off busy, one-way 11th avenue.  The entrance is staffed by a pleasant doorman who smiled and ensured our entry began flawlessly, in spite of the arctic air that pummels you from the Hudson into the concrete vortex of HuYa.  Agreeable and pleasant as well were the front staff, taking coats and seamlessly ushering us to the dining area.  Paul, part of the management team is efficient, thoughtful and conscientious, as are all the team at Tavern.The dining room itself is attractive.  It's a afew steps up from the entry area, with an abrupt turn directly into an architecturally unremarkable, box-like room.  The bar is positioned to the far left, feeling forgotten under the over hang to the 2nd floor (kitchen, with staircase to the 3rd floor private dining club, which has memberships that begin in the purported 5-figures to join).  This is not a destination bar; this watering hole is for those who may some day have to wait a moment before seating.Our server, Jason, was gracious and casual, introducing himself to us by first name.  His knowledge of the menu was extensive.  We began with water and the house-poured champagne by the glass, which my dining companion enjoyed thoroughly, especially as it was served in the finest crystal.  Equally attractive are the cut-glass water glasses, whose heaviness and dark tint make for a sleek table setting.  No salt and pepper were present on the table, however the highlight of the meal, a phenomenal, modern, quirky bread plate of four perfect coaster-size slices of brioche-dough "white bread" toast, with smooth, unsalted butter, quickly appeared and set unrealistically high expectations for the rest of the meal.As our dinner was at a very late hour, we opted to have salad and entrées brought at the same time. My companion enjoyed a Caesar; one of the outstanding recipe ideas was to tempura the anchovies.  For our mains, we enjoyed the short rib and the salmon.  The poached salmon was, according to our server, his favorite dish. I have to say, though I found it enjoyable, between the buttery poached fish and the oiled, roasted brocollini, plus the sauce sprinkled liberally with fish roe, it was all a lot of overwhelming rich muchness.  The texture of the rounds of delicata squash were a bland counterpoint, instead of providing a textural and taste counterpoint to all that heaviness, they were an unseasoned starch.  Would have preferred less oil, less butter, and an acidic counterpoint to balance the dish.Desserts were amiable, unthreatening and basically good.  Choices ranged from ice cream to lemon tart to what we landed on: baba rum and chocolate hazelnut torte.  Baba rum is one of those neglected 1950's desserts that remind me of my granny.  Dates remind me of her, as well.  Put them together in a dessert and it could end up a delightful nostalgic treat, or sticky, dense and rather forgettable.  We've all had chocolate and hazelnut or similar cake.  Lady M does it spectacularly, as does L.A. Burdick in Soho.  Be sure to visit those shops.Phenomenal drip decaf coffee in classic, understated bone china was, like the bread, simple done darn perfectly.  Enjoyed how a substantial portion of milk (options include almond, soy, oat, etc) was served with the perfectly warm java.  Mood music was unobtrusive until the room was empty, then it seemed a like a Pandora playlist for "typical NY hotel bar;" perhaps they'll eventually seek a curated playlist that refers back, tongue-in-cheek to the French Lautrec-ish art in the entryway - playful aural sophistication?There's nothing in other than moneyed appetite with Tavern.  True standouts are the service and the dinner/glassware.  The interior design and food are extremely typical of Hudson Yards, in general, which is to say this is how the rather wealthy of NYC want to mildly exist.  Having been at dinner in Jean Georges and, for a dignitaries event at the bar at the Trump World Tower, the spaces there and here seem like a decor leitmotif to one another (especially the latter - sidebar: strange how worn down that facility has become).  From this one can ascertain that smoked glass, sleek leather, polished wood are unoffensive, modern and, perhaps timeless to the current elites.Perhaps as our meal had only one starter, two mains, two desserts and coffee, plus a glass of house champers, it was a nice surprise that the bill was under $150.  Another plus.TL/dr: Elite class dining at HuYa in an inoffensive, attractive environment.

One of the best lunchees I've had was at this Pio Pio! I always usually get the lunch special but time I decided to try the empanada and boy was I pleased. This was the bwst one  I've ever had, the crust was fflaku but moist and the filling was seasoned well with  spices and veggies that made mY mouuth happy. My son and I were able to split to tomo saltado whOcj was jusT enough becausee we also had the side salad  . The food came out fresh and hott, i always appreciate the flavors of the food at Pio Pio. And judging from the packed house at lunch while leaving it Waac  clear this is a neighborhood gem..

Ouch. What happened here? 6 months ago the pho was flavorful with huge portions of meat and noodles. Now the prices went up and the pho lacks quality and portion size. And cash only? A little disappointed, but the plus is that there is no line during lunch hour. Vietspot seems to be the only pho restaurant nearby so I guess beggers can't be choosers.

I enjoyed this restaurant. Being a Gaga fan should make me biased but the food we all had was hot quick and fresh. I always enjoy giving a server two options and see what they recommend, make sure it's not the most pricey items. We enjoyed the bread as a starter which was tasty with the table EVOO, salt and pepper as seasoning. I would come back if I'm in NYC. Such a cute little cottage like Italian place. I order the meat sauce and pasta, stayed with being easy and I'm glad I did. So cute! Too bad Gaga wasn't around ! Mwah !

Came here on a Wednesday night and there were only two tables throughout the time.Overall it's just not there.There was only one waiter (the restaurant is not small), very untrained also....Shaky tables... Cheap glassware... Uncleaned cutlery...Cocktails - Moroccan Margarita tasted like we'll drink from cheap alcohol. Flying Carpet was better.For the food, I'd say very overpriced for what you are getting. Beets - doesn't taste fresh, flavor was boring.Sardine - I think it was fine but the side veggie was not with good flavor...Meatball - the rice with the sauce was fine together but the meatball was tastelessCheese wrap - nothing specialShrimp - probably the only okay dish but you can get in any tapas place with cheaper price.They gave a free crepe dessert with peanut butter filling and top with ice cream which was actually pretty good I think.Two stars for the try on the interior ambiance.Need more heart on the cuisine, it's a restaurant after all. My company said there's nothing here like Moroccan food.

Title: A Superior Dining Experience at Del Frisco's in Brookfield Plaza

I've frequented Del Frisco's on several occasions, and I'm pleased to report that the Brookfield Plaza location lives up to the chain's reputable standards. Nestled steps away from the World Trade Center, this bustling steakhouse offers a dynamic ambiance, coupled with some of the most exquisite views of Manhattan, New Jersey, and beyond.

Visiting after a poignant trip to the 9/11 Museum, I was instantly uplifted by the restaurant's vibrant energy. Del Frisco's impresses with gluten-sensitive options, ensuring that all guests can indulge comfortably. Our meal commenced with the delectable Ahi Tuna Tacos and the sumptuous Wild Mushroom Flatbreads - both a sheer delight.

The Lemon Dill Salmon and the generously portioned Hand Shaved Prime Steak were our entrees of choice, radiating perfection in temperature, taste, and presentation. Although hearty portions thwarted our efforts to finish the divine Truffled Baked Mac n' Cheese, it made for a delicious takeaway.

Service generally reflects the pulse of a restaurant, and while my server's performance faltered, the management, especially Giovanni, handled the situation with such professionalism that it further solidified my trust in their commitment to exceptional customer service.

In conclusion, Del Frisco's not only promises an epicurean adventure but also sets the gold standard in guest satisfaction. I heartily recommend this restaurant to anyone seeking culinary excellence, and I salute their dedication to rectifying concerns with grace and effectiveness. Cheers to Del Frisco's for consistently delivering a top-tier dining experience!

Jeffrey loves pickle pops that he makes at home. I love dumplings so when we came across the Lucky Pickle Dumpling we figured it was the best of both worlds. When you walk up to the "restaurant" I use that term loosely as it is more like a McDonald's because you order from a tablet hanging on the wall. If you have any type of modifications there's no way to input it to your order. We ordered the number 3. Spicy pork dumplings with pickles and a drink for $15. We also ordered a spicy curry pork dumplings. We didn't know that the number 3 was spicy pork dumplings already. That probably would be helpful information given if we had a live person to order from. But alas that info wasn't given. The dumplings were out of this world. Lots of filling and the gyoza skin was cooked perfectly. The only thing was that it came in about 2 inches of curry broth. That was a little strange to me. But that was overlooked. Jeffrey ordered a pickle flavored soft serve ice cream. It was beautiful. It truly was. And very big for only $5 and some change. But the flavor was just too weird. The best part was the pickle chips but there was only 5 on it. Bottom line: if you like different type of dumplings with fresh ingredients stop by.

Food: 3.5/5Stumbled here due to hunger and vicinity. There was a sign outside that read "happy hour 5-7pm" so we decided to give it a try.Ordered:-Shishito peppers (3.5/5): Some peppers were extremely spicy and some were mild. The salt was provided on the side (which I prefer.) You can't really mess up shishito peppers but 3.5 because they were a bit soggy.-Spicy chicken (1.5/5): Wasn't a fan. I was expecting chicken karaage or something fried but it seemed pan fried and came smothered in spicy sauce. Zero crunch!-Yellowtail cilantro roll (4/5): I'm a big fan of yellowtail and cilantro so this was a win for me. It's served with a spicy (maybe gochujang) sauce on top which I will request for them to omit next time. It took away from the yellowtail and the cilantro as it was overpowering. -Snow crab avocado roll (3/5): Not bad if you like mayonnaise. Honestly not sure what it consisted of as the sauce was overpowering but it was slightly crunchy and topped with roe and a lot of mayo with a hint of sesame oil.-Big eye tuna (4/5): This was tasty but came with (something like) gochujang sauce on the top. It was overpowering but delicious nonetheless. It had these crunchy white rice crackers on the outside which added the perfect texture.-Ikamaru (3/5): Grilled squid was sort of bland. Could use some salt or seasoning. Served with a glazed soy sauce on the side. It was just ok. Bit dry, not very juicy.Service: 4/5Considering we came for happy hour, everyone was super nice and accommodating. They even politely reminded us that happy hour was ending! I very much appreciate last call reminders :)Ambiance: 3.5/5I saw the happy hour sign outside but didn't realize this establishment was in the basement. Long stairs going down. Don't think I saw an elevator but the establishment was clean and modern. Great fast casual place for sushi. Lots of families and friends eating!

On a brisk October Saturday, I decided to see if the buzz surrounding the local eatery was justified. Amidst an array of tantalizing options, I opted for the 'De World's Fair Wafel,' a cozy dish adorned with strawberries, a dollop of whipped cream, and a snowfall of powdered sugar. While the waffle indulgence came with a steep price tag, suggesting it's more of an occasional treat than a regular affair, it was a delightful experience worth the initial splurge.

Title: A Heartfelt Ode to a Delightful Seoul Food Stand in Midtown Manhattan

I stumbled upon a gem in the bustling heart of Midtown Manhattan, a Korean food stand nestled within the Korean food court on 32nd Street (Food Gallery 32), offering a slice of Seoul amidst the urban jungle.

Contrary to initial misconceptions, this was no place for Soul or Solo Food, and certainly not Sole Food, even if Barbie were to make an appearance. What it did offer was a delightful experience of Seoul Food that warmed the heart and comforted the soul with its genuinely good Korean soups.

The standout was the tofu soup, brimming with flavor and comfort, while the Yuk Gae Jang was prepared with a mastery that beckoned for repeat visits. The assortment of soups, undoubtedly, would have pleased any palate.

Admittedly, prices were a notch above average, but not dauntingly so, particularly given its prime Midtown location. This modest cost was a small toll to pay for the authenticity and satisfaction provided by each spoonful.

While it's tragic that this culinary haven has reportedly closed, a part of me holds onto the hope that Yelp’s whispers of its demise are unfounded. If given the opportunity, I'd be first in line, ready to elevate my rating from four stars to a beaming five.

Alas, should it truly be gone, I'll fondly remember this lovely little stand that could have made a Korea out of those, like myself, who relish in the joy of Korean cuisine—undeniably more wholesome, filling, and authentic than even some larger markets, and possibly cheaper, too.

Here's to hoping for a second act for this Seoul Food standout that Manhattan so dearly needs.

Title: A Worthwhile Wait at Joe's Pizza

After noticing the crowd lined up outside Joe's, we were convinced it had to be a local favorite. Indeed, our curiosity paid off. Despite the initial queue, our second attempt welcomed us with a shorter wait, which, to our delight, moved swiftly. Inside, the energy was infectious as we watched the bustling staff craft pizzas with expert speed. I savored a classic margherita that lived up to the hype - fresh, flavorful, and utterly satisfying. Joe's proved to be a delicious testament to the saying "good things come to those who wait."

Title: Cozy Date Night at a Thai Food Gem

I recently visited a local Thai restaurant and was generally pleased with the experience. Opting for the set meal, it began with a Tom Yum soup - flavorful yet modest in size. I'd enjoy a bit more to savor next time. The Eat Thai Salad was a nice touch, especially with tofu dipped in the accompanying sauce, which enhanced the flavors when drizzled over the greens.

On the other hand, my friend's Mango Avocado Salad was a letdown, dominated by mango with no avocado in sight, and the portion was overwhelming. I'd steer clear of that option in the future.

The Chicken Pad Thai was the highlight - a generous portion with a satisfying taste, although it could benefit from more vegetables to elevate the dish.

We spent $37, which felt reasonable for the dinner. Service was efficient, with attentive water refills and polite staff interactions.

I'd recommend this spot for a Thai-food date, particularly noting the abundance of cozy tables for two, and a pleasantly quiet atmosphere around the early evening hours.

Overall, a solid choice for those craving Thai cuisine with a side of tranquility.

This place wasn't bad, but was definitely a bit on the pricey side. We came here to celebrate a friend's dinner with a reservation for 8 people. We were seated at a table that seemed a bit small, but worked overall. Most of the group got a filet or the stripe steak, which was done well, I got the lobster and my husband had to get a medley of sides and appetizers since he doesn't eat red meat. The bacon was delicious, if not salty, but I loved that and the Caesar salad was fine - i didn't like the white anchovies and the soft boiled egg on top was unnecessary, but the salad was good. Someone also ordered the regular salad and I think it was fine. We also got the tuna tartare and the crab cake which was good. My husband got a black truffle risotto dish on special as well as the gnocchi appetizer dish - he didn't like either.Most everyone seemed to enjoy their steaks, but unfortunately my lobster seemed overcooked and a bit tasteless. The sides were also nothing to write home about for me. We got the duck fat potato, asparagus, and mac and cheese. The mac and cheese was pretty good.Then dessert: the cheesecake seemed good, the snickers dessert was okay, the ice cream was meh, but the key lime was very good!As for our server, Brian was really cool and super nice.The only thing that I was surprised about was that he came over to ask if I wanted to join their loyalty program to earn $25 for ever $250 spent and since we had a large bill, we would be earning a nice amount. He never mentioned to $25 fee to enroll so after I paid the bill, I noticed that the charges didn't add up and had to figure it out.I don't know how I feel about that...Overall it was a nice time, but definitely not a place for someone who doesn't eat steak. The prices are what make this place less attractive as I realized one of the martinis ordered to the table was $26. That was more than one of my husband's dishes! Perhaps I'll come back if another friend wants to celebrate, but probably not.

4.5 solid work lunch meeting! They lose a star because the hostess wouldn't seat everyone till we were all present but put a "reserved" sign on the table that was for the 5 of us. I was there a little early and decided to open my laptop and get work done at that bar... no one asked if they could get me anything and it was kind of awkward as it started to get busy. Thankfully she reserved a cozy booth- we fit perfectly. Waitress was slow to come over but we ordered 2 Large salad and Large pizza lunch specials. We tried the spinach salad and Cesar salad, ordered a mushroom/onion pie and pepperoni pie. I have to say everything was delicious and came out quickly. The salads were excellent and so was the pizza. The crust was thin and crunchy and toppings were plentiful. I'd absolutely go back and recommend this spot to friends or colleagues! We didn't feelrushed out at all. They also have an outdoor seating area. Thanks for a great lunch!

The food is mostly tasty but most of the portion sizes versus pricing were all wrong. The labneh, roasted eggplant, and avocado bowl were great. The halloumi tasted great but was only three paper thin slices. The lamb kubeh tasted ok, but very tiny with 3 golf ball sized dumplings for a $19 main course. I guess I expected more from their namesake dish. Overall it was an expensive brunch at $40 (pre tip) a person with only two alcoholic drinks ordered in total. I'm pretty sure I would of left hungry if we didn't order extra pita to eat with the dishes. Also it wasn't very crowded but we always found ourselves having to flag down a server to ask for something.Also note that the online menu on their website says they have a brunch drink special but they stopped doing it without updating the website.

Title: A Dip into Decadence at Maison Pickle

Maison Pickle is a master at the French dip, and it's no wonder most of our party succumbed to their menu's highlight. The dips are generously portioned; my friend and I tackled the deluxe and were almost defeated by just half each. These mammoth sandwiches boast perfectly crusty bread, succulent beef, and an irresistible combination of creamy cheese sauce and crispy fried onions, all tied together with a flavorful jus that elevates every bite into a rich symphony.

Beyond the dips, we indulged in shared plates of fondue fries, garlic baguette, fried artichokes, and mussels - all of which were sterling choices. The fries struck an ideal balance between creamy fondue and crispness, while the artichokes were a delightful mix of crunch and salt.

Service was the cherry on top of our visit; our waiter was not just attentive but also impressively knowledgeable about the menu. And to sweeten the experience, Maison Pickle served a complimentary slice of cake with a sparkler for my friend's birthday - a thoughtful and sparkling touch to a splendid dining experience.

During my recent visit to this quaint eatery, I was genuinely impressed by the authenticity and flavorful punch of the cuisine. The generous portions are a definitive plus for anyone coming in with an appetite. However, the physical comfort within the restaurant leaves much to be desired; the tight quarters barely accommodate movement, and the lack of air conditioning on a sweltering July day was an unfortunate oversight.

Service, it must be noted, falls short of the typical American standard. Patrons should come with the expectation of timely delivered meals, but little in the way of engaging hospitality or thorough responses to inquiries. The staff ensures your food arrives promptly and is delicious—a saving grace for the establishment. If it’s excellent fare you seek and can overlook service shortcomings, this spot might just satisfy your culinary cravings.

Dining at this establishment was an absolute delight, particularly the seafood pasta dishes that deserve a standing ovation. The Clam Linguine was a refreshing experience with its white wine garlic butter sauce complementing the sizeable, succulent clams—an appreciated departure from the all-too-common frozen variety.

As for the Lobster and Shrimp Fettuccine with Drunken Alfredo sauce, it was nothing short of phenomenal. The jumbo shrimp were notably tender and exquisitely seasoned, and the lobster's freshness was undeniable. The Alfredo sauce, rich and creamy, brought the dish together with a depth of flavor that's often missing in its watered-down counterparts.

The attention to detail and commitment to quality ingredients were evident in every bite. Both pasta dishes scored a perfect 10/10, setting a high bar for seafood lovers and pasta aficionados alike.

Restaurant Review: Hell's Kitchen – A Gay Culinary Haven in Hell's Kitchen

In the heart of Hell's Kitchen lies a culinary gem for those yearning for a vibrant, gay-friendly dining experience reminiscent of Chelsea's former hot spots. Enter Hell's Kitchen, the dimly lit, hip Mexican eatery where the atmosphere is as lively as the flavors.

The clientele is as cool and attractive as the spot itself, with an energy that suggests everyone's genuinely enjoying their time. The service only amplifies this feeling, with our particularly charming waiter adding a touch of sweetness to the evening.

As for the food, it's a delightful surprise. The mole chicken enchiladas are nothing short of epic, striking a flawless balance of sweetness. Meanwhile, the chips and salsa are the kind of addictive that has you reaching for more even when you're full. And for those in the mood for a libation, the bar gives off an aura of margarita mastery.

Hell's Kitchen is more than just a restaurant—it's a testament to joyous dining experiences and inclusive vibes. So, if you're searching for an exceptional meal and an equally exceptional time, this is the spot. It's hard to imagine anyone leaving Hell's Kitchen anything but happy. Give it a go and find your new favorite haunt.

I recently enjoyed a classic New York slice at this bustling spot, opting for a pepperoni topping, and it was delicious. This isn't your bargain $1 slice—expect to pay $3.5 for one with toppings—but the flavor is worth the extra cash. The place can get crowded in the evenings with the bar crowd, but it's just as enjoyable during the daytime for a sober treat. Remember to bring cash, as they don't accept cards!

Excellent, delicious pizza and sandwiches. Fantastic imported ingredients, but I kinda wish they went the handmade homemade route, then it'd feel more like I was supporting a local mom and pop shop? When I ordered a "ripiena," they kindly explained that they couldn't make the version that was on the menu because everything was being imported all the way from Italy, but I know of lots of places nearby that make their own porchetta, and that little bit extra helps it not feel like a chain restaurant? Not that I'm against chain restaurants, per se, but if I'm spending $10 for a small sandwich at a chain restaurant, then it feels like it should come with a side dish and soda. Anyhow, that's just me (rambling). I obsessed for two days over the zucchini and onion pizza I had, and the prosciutto arugula burrata pizza was a thing of beauty; and, roman-style (flaky fluffy crunchy chewy) pizza is absolutely my preference over the soggy oily cheesy generic square slices that keep popping up everywhere...

Taladwat is another Thai restaurant addition in Hell's Kitchen except that it is the same owners of my favorite Pure Thai that run this place, so how can they go wrong?!We walked past it, several times and our visiting friend pointed out to give it a try. The ambiance is casual with rows after rows of communal tables to share, we were seated right away and were handed the menu, the concept is pick and mix 2 dishes for $18 and share it family style. I found it a bit chaotic for a big group, as a matter of fact I needed to comeback on a date night to give Taladwat the final verdict!We started nibbling on the "greens leaf basket" but dishes did not take long to arrive one after another, I have few favorites that are worth mentioning, the fried Thai Mackerel with sauce is delicious as well as the kaffir chicken, braised baby back ribs and sautéed shrimps, while I didn't get to try some dishes my friends ordered, everyone seemed to enjoy the food.Over all, it was well worth the visit, good price point and great customer service!

Solid spot for authentic Chinese food in midtown. And trust me, there aren't a lot of those in the area. The manager and waitstaff are incredibly helpful and nice - they walk over and recommend certain dishes if they see you looking at the menu confusingly. It's great that they make that initiative without the guest even asking.Food is delicious. My fiancé and I ordered a few dishes and left stuffed and we probably only ate half of what we ordered.Dan dan Noodles - one of my favorites! The kick is there and it isn't too pasty like a lot of other places. Wonton in spicy chili oil - perfectly wrapped wontons in a subtly spicy oil. Signature smoked tea duck - holy moly smoky goodness. It's very hefty the portion and it is DIVINE. I've honestly never tasted duck like this before. So smoky and full of aroma but not overly salty. Pork belly w leek - Not spicy enough for me but the hint of black bean added a very nice touch. Fiancé loved it. I will be back!

If you're on the hunt for a photogenic dining experience, this charming eatery hits the mark. Perfect for those with a sweet tooth and an eye for aesthetics, the desserts here, though a little pricey at $15 and up, are worth it for the Instagram cache. Come camera-ready to capture the delectable treats and delightful ambience. Highly recommended for a picture-perfect outing.

I was in NYC for a conference and thanks to Yelp stumbled upon this little gem close to Penn Station.The service was great and the food outstanding.  The lunch specials are a good deal and come with rice, naan, dal tadka.  All the accompaniments were terrific. We ordered the Palak Paneer, Chicken Tikka, and Lamb.  We split 2 lunch specials between 3 people and it was more than enough food.  The restaurant is very small and filled up very quickly for lunch. There were many to-go orders being filled while we were there.  That is probably your best bet, unless you get there right before noon like we did.

Title: Unique, Crispy Pizzas with a Twist – Not for Every Palate

I recently visited a local pizzeria known for its unconventional thin-crust pizzas and while it certainly caters to a specific taste, it didn't quite hit the mark for me. We ordered two large pizzas for our party of four, which was an adequate amount – the crust is exceptionally thin, resembling crackers or crisp tortillas.

The restaurant offers a nice option to mix and match pizza halves for those who want variety on a single pie, albeit for an additional cost. Our choices included a formaggio blanco with a delightful addition of caramelized onions & pesto, and a half-and-half pie with chickpotle and curryflower toppings. The formaggio blanco stood out, though the pesto was necessary to counteract potential dryness. The curryflower was surprisingly harmonious in flavor, while the chickpotle lacked the promised chipotle zest, even though the chicken itself was satisfactory.

Despite the tasty offerings, these pizzas didn’t quite satisfy my craving for a more traditional, slightly thicker crust. However, the establishment shines with its happy hour deals – a free pizza with a bottle of wine or two-for-one glasses, making it a potentially attractive spot for a casual drink with a side of pizza experimentation.

I visited this restaurant for an early lunch and was delighted by the turkey burger accompanied by sweet potato fries. The burger, dressed with fresh pico de gallo and creamy tzatziki sauce, was exceptionally tender and juicy. The pricing matched the standard burger joint, yet considering the quality and taste, the value received was quite satisfactory. Overall, a super yummy experience and a meal that truly satisfied.

This place is beautiful with a lot of great artwork and long tables.  Looks like a mess hall of full on partying and drinking.  There's a bar, and bunch of TVs showing soccer.The beer is great.  Sausage is mediocre and service unfortunately is poor.  The waitress took forever to bring our drinks, and took even longer for Gingerale.  Not sure how it took forever to bring the soda when the place was relatively empty during the afternoon!

Because... BRUNCH!! If you're feelin' brunchy, Friedman's will satisfy your craving. It's a bit on the pricey side, but just know that you'll be getting some good quality food! It was my last day in New York and I was craving for a delicious breakfast. I Yelped up brunch spots that were close by, and Friedman's popped up at the top of the list. It's located just a short walk from Madison Square Garden and Penn Station. I arrived right before 8 am which was perfect because it wasn't super crowded. Friedman's shares a space with a bagel shop next door (I believe it's the same owner), but it's a little fancier when compared to its' counterpart. The ambience is wonderful and the setup is very bright and modern. The service was good but nothing too memorable to be honest. What really makes this place stand out obviously is the food. I ordered their French toast with berry compote, a side of bacon, and a fresh squeezed orange juice. Now, normally I wouldn't order orange juice (especially fresh squeezed) because I despise pulp. However, my server sold me on it and I'm so glad that he did. This OJ was so delightful! It definitely tasted freshly squeezed but didn't have a ton of pulp. The French toast was nice and fluffy and the assortment of berries added a nice element of freshness to the dish. That bacon was LIFE! And, it should be for how much they charge for that thang! Trust me folks; it ain't cheap but it's damn good! Thick and crispy just the way that I love it. Yummy yum yum! Loved that bacon to the pieces! I really enjoyed both the breakfast and the ambience. I saw a lot of groups here so it seems like a great space to meet and mingle with friends for brunch. As time went on, it got a lot busier while I was there so I'm sure it gets packed on the weekends. But this was the perfect place for an early weekday lunch. I would totes come back again during a future visit to NY.

I popped into Otto's on the Upper East Side for a quick bite and wasn't disappointed. The chicken and carnitas tacos hit the spot with their flavorful fillings. Prices won't break the bank, and the stamp card is a nice perk for repeat visits. Definitely a reliable spot for satisfying taco cravings.

Title: Pleasant Surprise for a Non-Ramen Lover

I approached my visit to this ramen spot as a skeptic, my palate typically unimpressed by noodle soups, yet open to the guidance of a ramen-enthusiast companion. To kick things off, we sampled the scallop daily special—adequate, but not particularly memorable.

However, the beef bun transformed skepticism into delight. Imagine a French dip sandwich and an impeccable bun amalgamating into a culinary revelation—that was the beef bun. Its savoriness and texture overshadowed the main dish I chose: the spicy noodles. While they were competent, they didn't ascend to the lofty heights set by local acclaim.

Ambiance is admittedly sacrificed for convenience, as one dines amid the bustle of mall passersby. Initially, I leaned towards a modest three-star rating due to this lack of atmosphere and the noodles that fell short of my expectations. Yet, a four-star rating became unquestionable, thanks to the beef buns' triumph, the warm and attentive service, and the delightful surprise of a complimentary lychee slushee shot to end our meal on a sweet note.

First time in NYC and had to try out Italian food in Little Italy. I rely on my fellow Yelp reviewers for the best recommendations. This place did not fail.FoodWe ordered the calamari as an appetizer. It was probably the best I've ever had. Crispy and the marinara sauce was so greasy. I ordered the kiddos a spaghetti and meatball to split. It was huge! I don't think they offer lunch portions there. The meatballs were perfection. We also ordered a fish dish, lasagna and chicken Parmesan and all were delish. You can't really go wrong with anything that you order here. Most of the dishes are large enough to share. ServiceIt was mediocre at best. We were sat immediately in a corner (probably because we had two toddlers with us), but we didn't mind. They took a while to get our order from us. We had to keep reminding the waiter to refill our waters. Then he wouldn't come back. We had to hunt them down to close out the tab. For a place that is expensive for food, I would expect better service. Overall, the four star review is mainly for the food and the quality of food.

Dining at this establishment on a bustling Friday night, one might anticipate a brief 15-minute wait—a small price to pay for the forthcoming culinary delights. The starter courses set an exceptionally high bar; the curry served alongside fresh Roti was a revelation, a harmonious blend of flavors that was truly memorable. The Chicken Satay followed, elevating my expectations with its extraordinary tenderness, surpassing the standard fare of typical NYC Thai eateries.

The pièce de résistance, however, was the Ultimate Curry Laksa. This dish was nothing short of spectacular, with its rich, aromatic broth and perfectly balanced spices. While service tended towards the leisurely side, the exquisite food more than compensated for any lag in pace. Patience here is not just a virtue but a gateway to a remarkable dining experience.

Title: A Noodle Delight That's Easy on the Wallet!

If you're on the hunt for an affordable yet delicious noodle fix, this spot hits the mark. I dove into the cold noodle dish, which, at under $7, was an absolute steal. The dish delivered on its promise—chilled, with the perfect kick of spice, and undeniably refreshing. However, I wasn't a fan of the seitan topping.

My mom opted for the cumin lamb noodle soup and was equally impressed. She raved about the tenderness of the lamb and the unmistakable authenticity of hand-pulled noodles. Tucked in the bowl were little treasures of cabbage, with cilantro and celery adding a delightful crunch to each spoonful.

Later in the evening, despite dining at a pricier establishment, my mom declared her noodle lunch superior. This unassuming noodle haven is clearly a winner for both our palates and wallets!

We came here recommended from a friend who is Vietnamese and tell us Hanoi house has the most likely Vietnamese style pho reminding him of home all the time. Hanoi house is really popular and I believe there is always line but the wait is not too bad. We only waited for 15 minutes and seated at the bar. We ordered Hanoi style beef pho with bone marrow (+$6) and Bun cha ha noi (grilled lemongrass pork). Overall, the food was great but I think we might try other dishes if we come next time since it's too pricey to have pho here compared to China town even it tastes really good.

Came here for a few drinks after a nearby Yelp event. Love the decor, especially the neon. Delicious margaritas, and they have great happy hour deals. I got lost getting to the bathroom and discovered that they have a whole basement area with a separate bar, a dance floor, and some seriously vintage-y vibes. Great place!

{Overall: 4.25, Food: 4.25} Service: 4.5; Atmosphere: 4.5Pretty impressed by this dim sum spot in Midtown. All the dishes are fresh and traditionally made. My favorites were:* Sui mai* Bean curd roll* Hello Kitty Custard Buns - I loved how warm and melted they were inside! If it's your first visit, don't forget to check in for free buns. Service was really expedient and attentive. The space is modern and large.

+ Quick Korean food+ Reasonable prices for the location+ Chicken is crispy, hot, and delicious! Totally recommend!+ Open seating and clean atmosphere.- Soups are premade and sit for the whole day. Suggest to go for lunch and avoid dinner.

I visited this restaurant for a birthday brunch last weekend and it was a delightful experience. Opting for the unlimited brunch proved to be a great value with the quality of food exceeding expectations. Service was top-notch, contributing to an overall fantastic atmosphere. My four-star rating, just shy of perfect, is due to the prolonged wait time despite having a reservation; we were seated almost an hour late. That said, the restaurant's bustling vibe was understandable. The culinary offerings were impressive, with standout dishes and scrumptious margaritas. Plus, the menu caters well to dietary needs with gluten-free and vegan options available. Highly recommend for a tasty and accommodating brunch experience!

This review is long overdued. So my friend and I came here after work (worked in the area) I heard about this place being a really good ass restaurant/ brunch spot so I decided on coming here. It was in October on like a Wednesday so it was your usual slow restaurant day where it's you and like one other table dining in. I placed my order for my drink and my friend who's ID expired was denied a drink I already knew not to expect much from there. The food was ok I enjoyed my French fries of course and my enchilada though it was borderline too damn crispy/burned the soy wings were just OK I had about two passion fruit drinks that definitely was made with about no alcohol in it. I know they are like one of the spots that closes the latest around there If I'm in the LES again late and needed food maybe I'll give it a try again.

The 3rd location of Marinara just opened, still uptown but this time on the west side.It's pretty much the same layout and most of the same great slices and kitchen food, plus a couple new things.Definitely try the MVP Slice and a Pepperoni Pinwheel, a few of my favorite things they make. The mozzarella sticks are also excellent too, as is mostly everything we've tried from the kitchen menu.

Title: Overhyped and Over-sauced

After experiencing the much-talked-about Prince Street Pizza, I'm left scratching my head over its popularity. Our 20-minute wait yielded two plain and one pepperoni square slices that, frankly, didn't live up to the hype. While these greasy slices might serve well as a late-night indulgence, those in search of top-notch pizza might find themselves underwhelmed.

The main offender was the overwhelming amount of salty sauce that dominated the slices, throwing off the balance of flavors. The pepperoni slice did offer a slight improvement, but not enough to warrant the wait or a repeat visit.

Interestingly, shortly after sharing my thoughts online, I received a swift reply from the owner—demonstrating their attentiveness, if nothing else. However, I must note that attentive customer service alone cannot compensate for a mediocre pizza experience.

Come here frequently for selleongtang and sundae. Their kimchi and radish tastes so good! They bring it to you, then cut it for you and add some kimchi/radish sauce. Feel free to ask for more kimchi/radish because it's free. Also their kimchi/radish tastes very fresh, not sour. So if you like fresh kimchi/radish, and not aged kimchi/radish this is the place to get it! If you take out and want more kimchi/radish, it's an additional $5. The sundae tastes really good, and it didn't taste fishy or leave a lingering taste in my mouth. Overall, this is a great place to get some authentic Korean food! Service is also really good! Highly recommend bringing friends and family here!

Title: A Morning Ramen Delight at Ichiran

Who knew a 9:00 am ramen fix could set the tone for an entire day? Discovering Ichiran was serendipity at its finest, as my quest for brunch took a delightful detour. With its doors wide open and a welcoming 'no line' sign, the decision to enter was a no-brainer.

Ichiran's unique dining experience begins with its individual stalls, offering a moment of solitude with your bowl of tonkatsu ramen — an introvert's dream. Don't fret if it's your first visit; the attentive servers will navigate you through the process with ease. 

Opting for a bowl with all the toppings, I was quickly impressed. The pork, thinly sliced and brimming with flavor, arrived promptly, followed by the ramen cradled in a covered rectangular vessel. It was an unveiling of the "best ramen in NY," not an exaggeration by any means. Unlike the usual tonkatsu broth that I find too rich, Ichiran's was exceptionally smooth, a balm for the soul and stomach alike. Perfectly balanced noodles and a flawlessly cooked egg sealed the deal.

The $24 price tag may raise eyebrows, but the culinary experience justifies every cent. And with no tipping? It's just the cherry on top of this gastronomic delight. Ichiran, you have truly mastered the art of ramen.

Quite decent vegan ramen. I wish the service was better, the staff is always in a rush to take orders and serve. My food was spicier than expected, but in a good way. My colleagues liked their food as well, I would come back when I crave ramen.

I stumbled upon this ramen shop when leaving NYU one day and the atmosphere and the vibe of the waiters was actually quite delightful, but unfortunately as other reviews have said, the flavors simply do not leave much to be desired. Our party ordered both the vegetarian ramen as well as regular ramen with meat but it seemed as if both were made with the same bland broth. The noodles were so eggy that it felt like one egg had been cracked open into my mouth with every following bite, and honestly this with the bland broth just made it so I felt like I was eating wet soupy eggs. It may be the neighborhood or it may just be the restaurant, but plenty of ramen restaurants in New York have so much more flavor and "authenticity" in flavor to actual Japanese ramen.

Nestled at the base of Rockefeller Tower, Bouchon Bakery offers a delightful twist on French patisserie favorites. During a simple visit for an Americano, I succumbed to the charms of their immense "Better Butter" PB cookie. It was a tough choice between this and the renowned PB&C variety, but my temporary low-carb regime demanded the indulgence.

The "Better Butter" was a revelation – a guilt-tinged homage to Nutter Butter, except fresher and embedded with whole peanuts and grains. Beneath its toasty exterior lay a velvety peanut butter cream, worth every bite despite the caloric splurge that surely surpassed a package of its commercial counterpart.

For peanut butter aficionados, this bakery is a must-visit. And don't overlook the macarons – their size justifies the price, offering an equally generous serving of decadence.

Terakawa Ramen serves the real deal bowl of noodles in a very small dining room. The ingredients are fresh, the broth is made with care, the portions are good, service is super fast, and prices are fair. CASH ONLY. In general, a bowl, a drink, and a side or appetizer will run $25 ish. There are exactly 11 seats. This is my new favorite place to eat alone! Today I had the tan tan ramen with a Veggie bomb on the side. The bowl was everything I was hoping for. The veggies were a really nice portion for the extra $1.50 (unlike some places that only give you an extra two stalks of chinese broccoli, Terakawa gives you a heaping side bowl of blanched cabbage, onion, carrots, and sprouts). I got my noodles in under 5 minutes.Not advised for people with too many friends, slow eaters, or the claustrophobic. At prime times, you will feel pressured to inhale your food and leave just by the sheer fact that you can feel the hungry waiting patrons stare you down as you eat.

Title: Delightful Dinner with a Dash of Disappointment

My dining experience at this restaurant was largely satisfying, a palate pleaser indeed, marred only slightly by the lack of celebratory acknowledgment for my friend's birthday. The server may not have been the epitome of warmth, but the sommelier compensated with impressive expertise.

The duck was a standout dish, evoking the rich, smoky essence of premium bacon — it's a must-try. Pasta lovers will appreciate the diverse flavor profiles, each dish being a testament to the chef's culinary finesse. Refer to my uploaded photos for a visual taste.

Dessert was a trio of gelato scoops: vanilla, chocolate, and a salted caramel that stole the show. Warning: the salted caramel doesn't shy away from its name, so it's a bold choice for those with a taste for the savory-sweet.

In summary, despite minor service missteps and the absence of birthday fanfare commonly found elsewhere in the city, the restaurant delivers on the promise of a memorable meal.

Omg this place melts my heart! I'm in love with this place. When I lived in NYC I would come here all the time and now I miss it so much. I always get the Fried Chicken Sandwich. It has the crispiest chicken with the most amazing sauce and a fun pop of radish slaw to add crunch! And the loaded tater tots are out of this world! Soooo cheesy. The decor is very bright and modern and inviting, and very clean. Service is great. I hope to come back soon!

Having dined at this sushi establishment once before during an office party, my initial impressions years ago were underwhelming. However, my most recent personal dining experience has entirely reshaped my perception. Arriving early at 6:30 pm, the serene yet opulent dining area was just beginning to come to life.

The service was nothing short of extraordinary; with attentive staff ensuring our experience was unparalleled, it felt as though we were the sole focus of their attention. Commencing with starters, the Octopus Sashimi was a textural delight, its delicate slices enriched by a robust teriyaki sauce that left me practically drooling. The Hamachi tartare was equally impressive, its freshness accented by an array of unique accompaniments served on ice.

Choosing to share the chef's selection of sashimi for our main course was a wise decision, with the succulent cuts of fish proving to be a melt-in-your-mouth encounter. This, paired with two classic yet impeccably executed maki rolls—Spicy Salmon and Yellowtail—was satisfying without leaving us overly full.

Desserts were a standout, particularly a theatrical chocolate mound that was flambeed tableside, creating a mesmerizing show that I regret not capturing on video, as recommended by the waiter. The lighter choice of mochi filled with red bean paste provided a subtle yet delightful end to our meal.

In summary, this sushi spot has redeemed itself, transforming from a forgettable mass catering experience to an exceptional, intimate dining affair that's a must-visit destination. I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit, potentially for the Omakase, and of course, to finally taste the fresh wasabi.

First time in New York so trying to stay away from any big chain restaurants. Thought we'd give this place a try and we were not disappointed. We had the $35 prix fixe menu and it was fantastic. Fresh Caesar salad was delicious and not too much dressing while being very flavourful. I had the mussels and they were amazing. Jose our waiter had suggested this instead of the baked mussels. Wow! It was liking having 2 dozen mussels perfectly cooked in a seafood chowder. Of course he brought more bread so I could sop up all that goodness. He recommended their award winning French Onion soup burger.. I was thinking of having the boeuf bourguignon. No regrets! 8 oz of perfectly cooked medium beef with caramelized onions topped with melted cheese in top of a toasted English muffin. It was rich and decadent (not too salty either). We also had their trout which was also quite good. Ended off with a chocolate mousse which tasted like a chocolate bar. Not silky smooth but enjoyed it. We also had their caramel flan which I liked better. Think of a dim sum egg tart without the crust and covered in caramel. Delish! All in all, an excellent meal and did I mention? Superb service!!!

Very traditional Chinese dimsum place. Huge place and relatively average prices for dimsum. They had most options that I wanted, wished to see more 小笼包 however they had many 点心 so I was satisfied (didn't finish though) Most waiters were Chinese (Canto and Mandarin). The tea served was pretty good.

I recently visited a charming little bakery that caught my eye with its wonderful selection of pastries. Having been there twice, I've had the pleasure of sampling various items. The chicken encased in phyllo dough was a delight, and the sesame seed and honey squares were a perfectly sweet treat. I also tried the beluga lentil salad, which was both nutritious and delectable. All of their salads appeared vibrant and fresh, advocating for a healthy yet tasty experience. This bakery is a great find for anyone looking to indulge in some delicious baked goods while also having the option to choose healthier fare.

Title: A Spacious Spot for a Decent Slice

I visited this pizza joint after an Instagram ad proclaimed it the number one pizza place in New York - an irresistible claim for a pizza enthusiast like myself. Opting for a classic slice, I found the crust hit the mark with its satisfactory crunch and chewiness. However, the toppings and sauce lacked the robust flavor profile that distinguishes the city's top pizzerias. The real highlight was the restaurant's spacious interior, a rare find in the bustling pizza scene, making it an ideal location for a group gathering post-night-out. While it hasn't topped my list of favorites, it's still a decent spot worthy of a visit for those seeking ample seating and a fair slice.

I really really like this place. It also happens to be two blocks from my apartment which makes this new pizza joint even more exciting. I've been here twice and I love the pizza. It's legit New York style thin crust pizza - the likes of which is rarely seen this far north in Manhattan. I hope they get the foot traffic and customers that they deserve.Currently since this pizza place is flying under the radar, it's easy to get a table on any given night. The place is pretty spacious and I haven't had any trouble getting a table. I think they also have a downstairs area - but it was closed when I visited.Each pizza here is made fresh to order and they're "individual" sized. My favorite pie here is their fried pizza. It's actually the only fried pizza I've ever tried and it's truly delicious.
