I'm aware the extra oil is probably not good for my health, but it's too good to pass up.This place is worth the journey up the A/D train to the 125th/St. Nicholas Harlem area.

Believe the hype this places pizza is to die for!!! From tbe fresh creamy mozzarella to the crispy mini pepperonis the delicious crust sweet tangy sauce pure bliss!! Im in Chicago dreaming of this pizza!! Most places that have this type of hype fall short on the hype this place is the real deal best pizza in NYC.Make this place a must stop when in the city.Follow me in Instagram for more food picsChicagofoodking

This place was my wanted go list and finally got to tried but food was just not great. Food(2/5)- I got hungry after got a massage in this area and I gave a shot. I ordered crispy spring rolls, beef pho, Vietnamese coffee. Crispy spring rolls were too salty and sauce tasted little sour for it. In my opinion it would have been better if the sauce was peanut sauce. I requested them to some of hoisan sauce for my crispy spring rolls. Pho was ok but definitely not the best, I had been eat better pho elsewhere in NY. They gave me some of extra Thai peppers if I like to eat spicy. I have to add all of them cuz the broth was a bit oily to me. Vietnamese coffee was good but it was too small size. I'm a huge fan of coffee and honestly this place coffee was not enough to me. Probably I could have more than two cup of coffee in this place if I wasn't full. Service(5/5)- the waitress were so sweet and accommodating. I really appreciated that they were around me and checked I got everything what I need. Even I didn't have to asked them to refill my water. Ambience(5/5)- I like this place, only their interior. This place is cute spot in this area. Very clean but not big place. I would tell you go to this place with small group.

Came here for having a dinner with friends. This place definitely fantastic place and I really like it.The atmosphere of the restaurant  staff was so nice. I would like start from drinks. I ordered bourbon old fashion was so delicious if I have any more room definitely I would kept drinking. As a starter ve got olive oil, four different kind of olives and pickled red and green peppers cauliflowers. Then, I got the special of the day which was black sea bass. Omg! it was so delicious, but the size of the fish was a little small. other than that everything 5 Stars.As a desert, I had baklava. Normally, I am not really big fan of the baklava even I am from Turkey. This place has the best baklava entire of New York! it was not dry and lots of walnuts. Basically I would like to say so delicious. I cant wait to have another experience of this placeThank You MEME MEDITERRANEAN

During my visit to the much talked about eatery, I decided to try the sausage, mushroom, and cheese sandwich, which is listed as #21 on the menu. The restaurant itself seems to be a popular spot, though one gets the sense that its reputation is somewhat buoyed by enthusiastic tourist reviews.

The highlight of the sandwich was undoubtedly the bread—it struck the perfect balance of chewiness and flakiness, and tasted unmistakably fresh. However, the sandwich's filling left something to be desired. The combination of sausage, mushroom, cheese, and a hint of truffle oil could have made for a rich and indulgent experience, but the scanty portions of sausage, cut into thin coins, failed to deliver.

The overall sensation was akin to eating a makeshift pizza sandwich—two quality slices with a layer of gooey truffle-infused cheese in the middle. But the paucity of meat and filling made it clear that the sandwich would greatly benefit from a more generous hand. For a truly satisfying meal, this offering needs to be bolstered with a heartier filling.

We recently dined at this gem of a restaurant for a special lunch date and were thoroughly impressed. The ambiance is enchanting, with high ceilings and a spacious, dimly lit interior that sets the perfect mood for both lunch and dinner. The service we received was exceptional – attentive without being intrusive. As for the food, it was simply delicious, and the drinks complemented our meal wonderfully. My husband and I truly enjoyed our time here and would highly recommend it to others looking for an exquisite dining experience.

Wow, what an incredible gem to add to the East Village! I almost want to keep this place a secret given how awesome it is. Even with a soft open and limited menu (but full craft beer list) it is fantastic. Let's get into it ...Hummus Plate (4/5): Hummus itself is a little thick so I probably won't get this again since there are so many other excellent options. Comes with a TON of pita though and lots of veggies. Quinoa Bowl (3/5): Dressing was luckily on the side because it was WAY too vinegary. The bowl itself had very fresh ingredients and had a nice combo of flavors -- black bean, quinoa, butternut squash, etc. Pretzel (5/5): Such a good pretzel that they make. Warm, doughy, and just so tasty with the side of mustard. Nachos (4/5): Super yummy. Baked on the plate which can be hot so be careful. Lots of cheese and a pretty large portion of food. The sour cream and avocado really bring it together and they're generous with the amount. I did wish the bottom layer got some cheese too as those chips are rather plain. Deviled Eggs (5/5): Wow this is quite possibly the best thing they make. Perfectly spiced egg filling and it comes with toastini and these delectable candied figs. Chili (N/A): When I went here with my father he said it was some of the best chili he's had and not too spicy. I didn't have any so can't add a real rating here. Craft Beer List (5/5): With a constantly rotating menu of local craft beers you really can't go wrong. I've liked pretty much everything they have too. Huge variety of all types of beer -- ales, sours, IPAs, lager, etc.Veggie Burger (5/5): Easily the best veggie burger I've had in NYC. It tastes so meaty and comes in a huge portion. They grill both sides of the top and bottom bun and it brings it together incredibly. Grilled Cheese (4/5): It's a pretty darn good grilled cheese that comes with crunchy homemade looking potato chips (not sure if they're actually made in-house). The pickled onion on the side is incredible too. Service (5/5): I've been here a few times and service is always excellent. They offer phenomenal recommendations on both drinks and food. I appreciate it when someone tells me NOT to order something because it genuinely sucks and to get something else instead. You don't see that often! They always offer free tastes of beer that I'm deciding between too. TL;DR: What an incredible addition to St. Marks/East Village!! A must-try for locals and visitors alike.

Title: Szechuan Sensation at My Favorite Chinese Spot

I've sampled an array of dishes at this local Chinese restaurant, and it's my absolute go-to for a Szechuan cuisine fix. Their Dry Pepper Chicken bursts with flavor, while the Double Cooked Pork is a succulent masterpiece that keeps me coming back for more. Surprisingly, the star of the show is the Cabbage with Dry Chili Peppers – a dish that turns the seemingly mundane into an exceptional culinary delight. If your palate craves the bold and the spicy, this is the place to satiate those desires. Trust me, your taste buds will thank you!

Title: A Gem of Thai Cuisine on the Upper East Side

I can't recommend this Thai gem on the Upper East Side enough—truly one of Manhattan's finest. The food consistently arrives fresh and flavorful, from the zesty papaya salad to the array of mouthwatering curries and noodle dishes. The mock duck here is a revelation, even for devoted carnivores. The prices are just as attractive as the dishes, with generous portions that leave enough for leftovers, and lunch specials that are a steal starting at $9.

The ambiance strikes the perfect balance between chic and welcoming, with intricate lanterns and lush plants—ideal for a romantic date or a casual meal in your favorite athleisure wear. Despite its popularity, which often leads to a brief wait (thank heavens for Yelp's waitlist feature), the service remains impeccable. Staff members are knowledgeable and eager to guide you through the menu to suit your spice preference.

Whether you opt for dine-in, takeout, or delivery, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving exceptional Thai food in a charming setting, all without breaking the bank.

Title: A TriBeCa Gem for a Satisfying Lunch

If you find yourself wandering through TriBeCa in search of a satisfying yet not overly heavy lunch, this spot should be high on your list. It's a reliable favorite of mine, and I can't remember a visit that left me disappointed. Their Hummus & Pita stands out—simple, filling, and consistently delicious. Opt for a platter or indulge in a falafel pita; their pitas arrive toasty warm, while the falafels are expertly fried to a golden crisp.

The staff here add to the experience with their courteous and efficient service, underscoring the reasons why this place has become one of my regular go-to's for a hummus fix in the city. It's a definite recommendation for anyone in the area.

Title: A Diverse Spread at Sahib's Buffet with Room for Improvement

After much anticipation spurred by Yelp reviews, I ventured to Sahib for a lunchtime feast. Priced reasonably at $13, the buffet offers an impressive spread that outshines local competitors, particularly in its generous assortment of both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options.

As a welcoming touch, bhel puri, tandoori chicken, dosas, and naan were served fresh at the table—a commendable approach that added a sense of personal service to the buffet experience. The breadth of choices continued to impress, with chole bhatura, pakoras, saag paneer, corn masala, potato eggplant curry, rajma, butter chicken, chettinad chicken curry, lamb curry, and a duo of rice dishes: vegetarian peas pulav and chicken biryani. For a sweet conclusion, rice pudding provided a comforting dessert.

Despite the variety, the buffet left my palate wanting more—particularly in the vegetarian realm, where the dishes were noticeably bland. On the flip side, the butter chicken and chole bhatura stood out as highlights, bringing the flavors I had hoped to find throughout the meal.

Sahib's buffet earns a solid three stars, excelling in variety and concept but falling short in the execution of some key vegetarian dishes. Should you crave a less spicy Indian buffet with plenty of choices, Sahib will likely meet your needs.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Cantonese Delights at 95 HomeDish

My recent visit to 95 HomeDish proved that while the restaurant excels in creating a convivial atmosphere for group dining with its large round tables and handy lazy Susans, the culinary experience can be somewhat inconsistent.

The shining stars of our 10-dish feast included the savory beef chow fun with gravy, a perfectly seasoned claypot braised fish and tofu, crisp watercress with garlic, and a delightful Singapore mei fun. Each of these selections delivered on the promise of fresh, flavor-packed Cantonese cuisine that left us wanting more.

Unfortunately, not all dishes met our expectations. The sesame chicken was a letdown, tasting as if the meat had suffered a freezer burn and been unceremoniously reheated. Despite its popularity as an American Chinese favorite, this dish did not resonate well, especially with the questionable meat quality.

Similarly, the lobster sticky rice and Yang Chow fried rice missed the mark, failing to deliver the depth of flavor we anticipated.

On the plus side, the restaurant's BYOB policy is a welcome feature, and the acceptance of credit cards adds a layer of convenience.

In summary, while 95 HomeDish offers some compelling reasons to gather and indulge in Cantonese fare, diners should navigate the menu carefully to avoid the pitfalls of their less impressive dishes.

Biting into the authentic slices at this quintessential New York pizzeria is a mouthwatering experience that lives up to the city's reputation for stellar pizza. Don't let a queue deter you; patience is rewarded with a pizza that's bound to rank amongst your all-time top three. It's an absolute must-visit for any pizza aficionado.

Title: "Variety Meets Value at Plaza Deli"

If you're in FiDi looking for a bang-for-your-buck lunch spot, Plaza Deli could be your go-to. This deli prides itself on its vast array of options, from sandwiches and burgers to sushi and fried chicken, not forgetting the salad bar. The variety is impressive; you're hard-pressed to find something that doesn't tickle your fancy here.

The catch, however, is that food is prepared in bulk. A pro tip for those exploring the self-serve hot bar: delve for the treasures that lie beneath. Snagging food from the top layer might leave you with a less-than-warm meal, as I learned.

In conclusion, Plaza Deli isn't going to win any gourmet awards, but it stands out for its use of quality ingredients without breaking the bank. For under $10, it's a solid choice in the area.

Oh. My. GOODNESS. This roll was so freaking remarkable I didn't want it to ever end. It tasted like pure heaven. The lobster itself tasted amazing and then the roll brought it to an unspeakable heavenly level. I tried savoring it as much as I humanly could. I got it with the salad side and that was even good too. My beans were the favorite part of the salad. 100000% recommend everyone try this place. It's worth the money, promise. Service was also good. The staff was very kind & it was quick service! Overall, such a top notch choice.

Title: A Little Slice of Cali-Mex Bliss at Los Mariscos

I recently visited Los Mariscos, drawn in by my nostalgia for California and Texas' customary free chips and craving some authentic Mexican seafood. True to form, the restaurant did not disappoint. The star of my meal was, without a doubt, the fish tacos. At a reasonable $3 each, these tacos were nothing short of divine. The fish was perfectly seasoned and cooked, tucked into freshly made tortillas that I could watch being prepared right before my eyes.

Speaking of freebies, Los Mariscos graciously serves up complimentary chips while you wait—a tradition I've sorely missed since moving to New York City. These aren't your average chips either; they're substantial in size and just as satisfying as the entrees.

The ambiance of the spot is a tale of two settings. The main area, nestled in the bustling Chelsea Market, offers a quick and lively dining experience. But the secret is in the 'back': venture down a narrow hallway, and you're rewarded with a cozy, dimly-lit retreat adorned with coastal Mexican flair. It's a hidden gem perfect for a more relaxed dining environment, and yet another spot to watch the magic happen in the kitchen.

I found no downside to my experience at Los Mariscos. It has quickly become my top choice for Mexican seafood, or when I'm just craving a taste of the West Coast. If you find yourself near the Highline with a hankering for some top-notch Cali-Mex cuisine, Los Mariscos is a must-visit. Their fish tacos are 'the bomb,' and I'm already yearning for my next visit—pandemic permitting.

I've frequented this gem of a restaurant for several years and it has consistently remained a favorite. The value is unparalleled, with the menu being very reasonably priced and the delightful perk of complimentary appetizers, usually a delightful medley of seasonal vegetables. The standout dish for me is their tofu soup, served in a sizzling bowl that promises aromatic delight with every spoonful. Also not to be missed is the small fish appetizer – it's delectably flavorful and worth a try, even if the presentation (complete with head) might give you a moment's pause. It's a must-visit spot for delicious food at a great price.

Title: A Cozy Corner for Classic French Fare

I'm excited to add this gem to my list of regular dinner spots! While modest in size and simplicity, it exudes charm and a bustling, homey atmosphere that won me over. Reservations are a must, as we found out by booking three weeks in advance for our Saturday night dinner at 7:30 PM. The efficiency was impressive, with our table ready right on time, although there's no space for early birds to linger—plan to arrive just in time.

The menu is a delightful nod to traditional French bistros, with well-priced wines to match. We enjoyed a carafe of Sancerre and started with the sumptuous escargot and duck pate. My skate in a tangy lemon caper sauce was sublime, and my husband's hanger steak was hearty and cooked to perfection. Contrary to past reviews, service was friendly and prompt despite the packed house; just be prepared for close quarters and a lively room.

A word of caution for larger groups: it's a tight squeeze, so it's best suited for parties of four or less. Nonetheless, this spot is a must-visit for a slice of France. Highly recommended!

Title: A Gem Along the Highline – A Must-Visit Market in Hudson Yards

If your wanderlust takes you walking above Manhattan's streets along the Highline, make sure to venture into this bustling market tucked away in Hudson Yards. Still sparkling with its newness, the market is a haven for foodies, offering a smorgasbord of eateries and shops that attract both tourists and local New Yorkers.

On a quest for a midday nibble, my boyfriend and I were delighted by the plethora of culinary choices. We settled on a classic French sandwich - jambon, a simple yet delectable combination of cheese and cured ham. At $16, the price might raise an eyebrow, but any skepticism evaporates with the very first taste. I'm no aficionado of cured meats or cheeses, but this sandwich was divine. Delivered in a slender, bite-sized format, the sandwich boasted high-quality ham and cheese, nestled between slices of perfectly toasted bread.

For anyone looking to dabble in diverse ethnic flavors, this spot is an exceptional choice. Its atmosphere, the quality of food, and the variety ensure a memorable gastronomic experience. Whether a light snack or an eclectic meal, this market is a destination that should top your list when you're next exploring the Highline.
Cheap but super tasty roast pig. I usually ordered a Large without the rice and it cost $8.50. The serving is huge. This is a to go place since theres no seat

I never thought I would pay $9 for rice rolls before, but I love rice rolls so it's worth it. This new location replaced Cheers Cut. I'm sad about that, but not too sad because I love rice rolls even more.It's only their soft opening, so they only had two things on the menu. The Joe's Signature (beef, pork, dried shrimp, egg, and bean sprouts) and the Shrimp Party (shrimp, dried shrimp, egg, bean sprouts). My friend and I got one of each to share. I've had the rice rolls at their Flushing location before and I think I actually enjoyed the rice rolls here more. The texture was surprisingly really light. It's nice that you get it fresh instead of having them sit out for a while. They have all the usual sauces: sweet soy sauce, hot chili oil, peanut/sesame sauce etc. I think the only thing I didn't like was the bean sprouts. I've never had bean sprouts in rice rolls before and the texture is weird to me.My favorite place to get rice rolls is still the little cart outside of Hong Kong supermarket on Hester and Elizabeth, but I would definitely come here for lunch often if I can.

Title: Cozy Pub with Room for Improvement

Upon first visiting this local pub, we were greeted by a friendly woman who seemed to be the owner – a warm welcome that set a pleasant tone for our experience. Despite this being our first time here, we found ourselves quickly accommodated with prompt service.

While the atmosphere of the pub was generally accommodating, we were taken aback by an unfortunate bathroom odor upon entry. This did not mar the entirety of our visit but was a notable concern. 

In terms of our meal, we had a few hiccups with the food quality. The fries were disappointingly soggy, and the guacamole accompanying our chips lacked the zest and flavor we had anticipated. Our drinks were adequate, though there was a slight misstep in service when my drink was removed before I had finished, without the server verifying if I was indeed done.

Despite the issues, this pub serves as a decent spot for a quick bite, especially if you're in the neighborhood and looking for a straightforward meal. Next time, I'd be inclined to try a different item from the drink menu, in hopes of finding something to better suit my taste.

It was as good as we had hoped. And we had hoped for greatness. We had planned ahead to little Korea for some lunch.  With some preplanning I had made a reservation at Madangsui.  When we arrived at 2pm it was not that busy.  I'm sure it helped that it was 2pm on a Monday.  We grabbed our seats in a beautiful dining room. As had been my experience at Korean spots, we had quick service.  Immediately after ordering we had our customary 6 small appetizers that you get at such a place. I learned they are called "Banchan" for the group of apps.  They were really good.  The four of us finished them off quite fast.  Soon after our 2 crackling and popping pots of bibimbab.  We have had lunch in many places in Little Korea that were amazing and this was up there. We made quick work of our shared  2 bowls and finished perfectly content.  It was the best refuel for a day of walking Manhattan.    As with most New York we take, we will be back to Little Korea for a bite.   And this place will be one of my top choices.

Title: Delicious Food in a Distracting Atmosphere - 3.5 Stars

My experience at this Lower East Side spot was a perfect embodiment of the classic "but" situation. On the one hand, the culinary offerings are out of this world – an indisputable 5-star delight. The sisig sizzled, the pork adobo satisfied, the crispy pata was a revelation in taste and texture, and even the khao soi and halo-halo left us thoroughly impressed.

However, dining here comes with its caveats. The underground hipster vibe is drowned out by music so loud it turns conversation into a competitive sport. The proximity to neighboring diners transforms your meal into a communal event, whether you like it or not; imagine sharing every chuckle and awkward silence of a stranger's first date.

But what's hard to pardon is the dismissive service we encountered, a surprising lapse considering the restaurant wasn't bustling at the time. It's as if the establishment's buzz has bred a complacency about customer care.

In conclusion, while the food at P&K is unquestionably exceptional, the overall dining experience doesn't quite match up. Next time, I'll opt to savor their culinary masterpieces via delivery for a more enjoyable and personal experience.

Had so much fun here. What a great place. I will say the food is awesome but the bathroom was the worst I've ever seen and would almost scare you to eat here because it's that dirty. 1 Star for being unclean and I mean really unclean

So good! I allied up & felt like I traveled into a Ramen shop in Japan. Small & cute. My hubby and I both ordered the Kuu Chili Ramen. Perfect level of spice! Really good flavors. Fast service. I also tried the strawberry milk. Delicious. My hubby got some sake. Great lunch spot close to the 9/11 memorial and WTC. Cost about $46 total for 2 Ramen & 2 drinks.

The lines are long but worth it. Their grandma slice is absolutely to die for. If you get it fresh out of the oven it's so crunchy and flavorful. Thank god for Price Street Pizza. I tried the white slice/green slice for the first time and it was good but nothing beats their regular slices, and absolutely nothing beats their grandma slice. I bring any and all of my NYC guests here for a true pizza experience.

4 star for the regular dishes.3-3.5 star for the noodles.3 star because overpriced.hmmmmm I'm not a Rice Noodle person so the rice noodle dishes are like meh to me.But other dishes are mostly pretty good besides very overpriced.Cabbage $18 - very enjoyable and addicting flavor but $18 for cabbage is just wow.Organic Cucumber $8 - very freshly made which I appreciated. Mala Duck Tongue $12 - so so doesn't feel like home.Winter Melon $16 - favorite dish, great flavor also addicting, we all couldn't stop eating this one! Stinky Tofu $10 - has a touch of Taiwanese flavor I'm glad for once a Manhattan restaurant is selling it!Pig Trotter $34 - it's pretty good and nice that's boneless, but unlike the Cabbage/Cucumber/Winter Melon that we couldn't stop eating, this was one of the less popular dish on our table.Hometown Lu Fen $22 - I thought it's kind boring overpriced noodle dish but my friend thinks it's quite goodGround Pork Rice Noodle $14 - most boring dish I think each of us had a bite and left the whole bowl there to dry.We had some sake too but a $65/pp meal is considered pretty pricy Chinese restaurant in the village.

Upon entering the restaurant, which I had high hopes for based on its Instagram presence and premium pricing, I was met with a casual diner atmosphere rather than the expected sophistication. The welcome lacked warmth, and the inattentiveness of the staff was noticeable, especially given the sparse occupancy.

However, the highlight of the visit was undoubtedly the Cinnamon Toast Crunch churro milkshake I ordered. Presentation and flavor were spot on – a decadent concoction served in a frosting-rimmed glass, drenched in caramel and topped with an indulgent choco taco and churros, all infused with a strong cinnamon flavor and actual bits of Cinnamon Toast Crunch. Other milkshakes, like the cotton candy and birthday cake varieties at a neighboring table, appeared just as tempting and Instagram-ready.

A pleasant surprise was the happy hour featuring $5 appetizers, where the fried pickles shone, albeit overshadowed by the unforgettable milkshake. Despite a rocky start with service, the beverages alone make this a place worth visiting for those seeking a photogenic and tasty treat.

Came here with a group of friends. A few friends have tried it here before. I got a burger and a few appetizers. I don't see anything special about here unless you really like eating lobster. But there are few different places around. It's a good hangout place. Nice place to try first time and my last time.

If you're passing through Penn Station and craving some authentic NYC pizza, this spot is a must-try. The pizza is surprisingly good for a train station eatery, and it reheats like a charm if you manage to save your slice for home. Highly recommend grabbing a piece for the road.

Returned and tried a few different dishes this time. Jun-Men uses Yelp Waitlist now, which is great. I had the pork bone ramen again, which wasn't as good as I remember but still decent. Sweet potato fries, crispy shrimp and pork buns were also excellent. Standout was probably the shrimp.

I loved the concept of this place and really wanted to love it...but I didn't. Being fast casual, it was super convenient and I stopped in for a quick lunch while working in the area. The pasta was good, cooked well al dente but the sauce was so acidic it was overpowering. The sauce wasn't great at coating the pasta, so it mostly just sat on top. Maybe I'm just jaded having lived in NYC all my life and had great easy amazing italian food.

I recently visited this restaurant for a friend's birthday celebration and had an enjoyable experience. While I would suggest a more diverse music selection to enhance the ambiance, the overall vibe was pleasant. The menu is designed for a family-style dining experience, although I found that the portion sizes seemed more suitable for two people rather than larger groups. Standout dishes included the flavorful lobster rice and a delicious shrimp appetizer. Additionally, the cauliflower dish was exceptionally amazing. Despite the slight mismatch in portion expectations, I would recommend this spot for its tasty offerings.

I got a mozzarella slice for $3.50. The crust is thin and crisp but I probably got a bad slice because it was dry. There was barely any sauce in the pizza. I guess it was okay but I probably would have enjoyed it more if wasn't for the lack of sauce.

This was my favorite lunch spot when I worked in New York City (coming 3+ times per week)! The food is always fresh, delicious, and healthy. Everyone working there is always very friendly and efficient, getting your lunch made quickly. My go to was the salmon bowl with sweet potatoes, broccoli, and the ginger turmeric sauce (let me tell you, that sauce is addicting!) I would suggest ordering off seamless and picking up if you're in the area to avoid waiting in line.

Overall, food here was decent but could be that we ordered wrong.. I thought service could've been better. I was early and asked for a table of two since it's a little hard to get an RSVP. I was told to wait until my friend was here in the most deadpan voice with no smile. I suspect it's because the lady was being taught the ropes and even if I understand, it was awks to see that it happen in front of me as I waited since she didn't look happy. We ordered the Bone Marrow (good but not amazing flavor wise but it did come off the Bone easily), grilled octopus (decent - flavorful but a tad too soft for my personal taste) and the duck breast (Tom Kha Pet - pretty good!! Might be my favorite that I tried) to share and was able to finish most of it although it seemed like we were rushed bc they kept checking in on us. For drinks we both ordered Cruel as a Cucumber (so good!!) and the beer slushy (which wasn't slushy at all!). IG: @phothegram

This place was delicious, a special gem tucked into a quiet street amidst busy midtown east. My brothers and I always come here given the quick 'n easy ramen noodle dishes. With a small menu, you'll conveniently find a dish (containing either pork, chicken or vegetables) without wasting much time to decide. The music was blaring techno music, creating the vibe of a Japanese dance club.The bar and seating areas both clear quickly so you'll never be waiting long to be seated. I ordered spicy cucumbers while my brother ordered a sesame salad, both tasting so fresh. My spicy vegetarian ramen dish then came - boom! A ton of spicy pepper and tasty broth. The place will give you a refill of strictly noodles for $2, too.For a total of two appetizers, two main dishes and soda- our bill came out only to $42. Now that's a steal here in NYC!

Title: A Stellar Evening at E.A.K. Ramen in NY

Last night at E.A.K. Ramen in New York was a five-star experience. The restaurant's interior struck an impressive balance between design and space, setting the tone for the evening. Service was exceptional—attentive, friendly, and courteous without fail.

The highlight, of course, was the E.A.K Ramen itself. A masterful fusion of Tonkotsu and chicken broths created a flavorful base for the dish. The CharSui pork was tender to the point of melting in your mouth, and the flawlessly seasoned and cooked egg added a delicate touch, showcasing the importance of attention to detail.

For fellow noodle soup enthusiasts, this place is not to be missed. Follow my journey for the perfect bowl across the globe on Instagram, Facebook, Yelp, and YouTube at @noodlesoupr and @noodlesoupreview.

This was a unique concept of $26 for unlimited pasta. It comes with free bread and either a salad or vegetables. They change the pasta options every now and then but when I went it was spaghetti with tomato and basil, ravioli, and rigatoni bolognese. Servers come around and serve up all 3 at once, and then you can ask for more of whatever.My friend doesn't eat meat so she couldn't have the bolognese. The restaurant was kind enough to serve her a pesto rigatoni the second time around after they noticed.Another great thing is that they will let you take it to-go if you can't finish your plate! So we got pasta for today and tomorrow.I think this will be a one-time experience for me because it was super heavy on the carbs, but the other dishes in this restaurant looked good!

Title: A True Italian Gem on Mulberry Street

My family and I were absolutely charmed by this delightful restaurant nestled on the quintessential Classic street, Mulberry. Managed by a cadre of the most gracious and hospitable gentlemen, our dining experience was nothing short of perfect.

The sangria we sipped on was exceptional, setting a festive tone for the meal. I indulged in the lobster ravioli, and I must confess, it was a dish I’d travel back for in a heartbeat – absolutely exquisite. My son’s choice of spaghetti and my daughter’s classic lasagna were equally impressive, each dish capturing the essence of traditional Italian cuisine.

For those yearning for authentic Italian fare without the fuss, this spot is a must-visit. We'll definitely be returning for another round of those delectable flavors true to Italy's rich culinary heritage.

Waited way too long after Yelp wait list said my table was ready which I found highly annoying. We sat there for an extra hour waiting, really soured my experience. The host is really great and had a great attitude, the wait staff were far too busy to provide any service. We ordered a range of dishes because we were so excited. The potato foam top with curry udon was amazing. The foam was light and airy, the curry was flavourful and udon was springy. The scallop carparccio was fresh and light, just as expected. We ordered several skewers which we all good but took so long to arrive that I almost fell asleep. On top of that, the Tamago Bacon Skewer (that looks crazy good in their photo) was served at room temperature, slightly warm but mostly cold. It was really gross. They used too much truffle oil that it smelled putrid.

Title: A Disheartening Shift at Sarabeth's UWS

I remember fondly the days when Sarabeth's on the Upper West Side was the quintessence of a New York brunch spot. It was the place to be on Sunday mornings, whether you were starting your day solo with a newspaper or joining friends before an excursion to Central Park. The versatility of Sarabeth's charm was unmatched, serving as a delightful venue for any meal, whether with a significant other, family, or friends. That was the enchantment of Sarabeth's 22 years ago.

Fast forward to the present, and it seems the sheen has dulled on this once-glimmering gem. Sarabeth's reputation still attracts diners, but the essence of what made it special seems to be resting on its laurels. It's not that the food quality has drastically declined—the omelette I ordered was exemplary, and Jayson's ricotta pancakes maintained their renowned deliciousness.

However, dining with Michael, a culinary connoisseur, highlighted the cracks in the Sarabeth's experience. Service was scarce, to put it mildly. The attention from the staff was virtually nonexistent, compelling us to fend for ourselves for basic needs like beverage refills and condiments, not to mention the laborious process of trying to pay.

Michael's request for a lightly cooked omelette was disregarded, and with our server MIA, he was left to accept his meal as is, tainting the overall experience. Pricing, while reasonable on paper, felt unjustified given the lackluster service.

Sarabeth's may still bear the name and location of a New York treasure, but the commitment to excellence that once defined it has waned. It pains me to report that what was once a go-to destination is now just another eatery in the city that could be so much more.

Title: Disappointing Experience Amidst Holiday Hustle

Our quest for a quick lunch during the holiday rush led us to this restaurant after finding Chelsea Market brimming with patrons. Regrettably, the visit was underwhelming. The Cubano sandwich, though passable, did not justify its $15 price tag - one expects a memorable meal at that cost. The fettuccine bolognese was a letdown; it lacked flavor and suffered from overcooked pasta. Service didn't redeem the food either, marked by slowness and a lack of attention to detail. Basic necessities like utensils and water were neglected, leaving us to self-serve for the latter. In summary, this eatery fell short of providing a satisfactory dining experience, both in culinary execution and service.

I hate being cold, but a bowl of hot steaming ramen always warms me up and puts me in a better mood. We went to Nappori on a cold day before seeing a show nearby. We went early, around 5:30, on a Sunday night and had no problem getting a table. I had a hard time picking out which ramen to order, but I'm happy I decided on the tan tan men ramen which was so good. A slightly different take on ramen, the dish had great flavor, but wasn't overly spicy. The cilantro on top was a great addition to the fragrant broth. My husband ordered the samurai ramen which was also fantastic. I would order both dishes again. My only small complaint is that service was super slow. I think there was a miscommunication about who was responsible for a couple of tables which resulted in some spotty service. I'm not sure that we saw the same person come to our table twice, but we got out of the restaurant in a somewhat reasonable amount of time, and the service issues wouldn't stop me from coming back again.

Title: A Dim Sum Delight with a Spicy Kick

I recently dined at this cozy nook of a restaurant and was charmed by their small dim sum plates. The pork dumplings, scallion pancakes, and garlic eggplant were deceptively simple yet bursting with flavor. 

Heeding our waiter's advice, we shared a wok-fried dry pot, ambitiously opting for the "Spicy" level. The heat was a tad overwhelming for my palate, but the mixture of toppings was culinary artistry. Next time, I'll play it safe with "Mild."

The meal ended on a high note with their steamed buns, an unexpectedly delightful dessert, perfectly paired with a side of condensed milk for dipping.

In summary, despite the heat hiccup, the restaurant delivered an authentic and enjoyable experience. The perfect spot for dim sum lovers and those seeking a communal dining adventure.

I was looking forward to trying out Upside after reading about this place in an article in the New York Times. I am a huge fan of charred pepperoni cups after having the famous slices at Grimaldis, (R.I.P.) Prince Street Pizza and Lions, Tigers and Squares. The first thing that caught my attention here were the thickness of the slices. I would be lying if I told you that the slices upon first glance looked remotely appetizing. My slice, as one can tell, was extremely dry. I like a nice and hot grease dripping Sicilian slice. The pepperoni slice offered here lacked flavor, and had an extremely hard crust. I would not recommend this if you have sensitive gums as it may cause abrasions to the roof of your mouth and gums upon finishing it. The dough, on the other hand was airy and lacked flavor. At least the comparable Spicy Spring at PSP has its unique slightly sweetened dough. Worse of all, my slice rung up at an astonishing $5.00. If you're a big fan of hard, flavorless pizza and paper thin pepperoni cups, then by all means, dine here. If not, I'd highly recommend trekking down to Lions, Tigers and Squares Detroit Pizza or better yet, Prince Street Pizza.

Title: A Slice of NYC Steakhouse Royalty

If you're in NYC and craving a carnivorous dining experience, look no further than this longstanding gem, the original of its kind within the franchise and a fierce competitor to the renowned Peter Lugers. Celebrating its 15-year tenure, it's hailed as the pinnacle location among its siblings scattered around Manhattan.

Food (5/5): The star of the show is the Porterhouse steak served medium rare, a masterclass in preparation—juicy, flavorful, and generous enough to conquer the appetites of two. Accompanied by a side of creamed spinach, delights in every bite are guaranteed; however, the German potatoes, though tasty, erred on the side of saltiness. Tip: Save room for their bacon on a potential second visit.

Service (3/5): The experience slightly falters with our main waiter's lack of warmth and minimal engagement, yet it's redeemed by the attentive support staff ensuring a pleasant meal from start to finish.

Space (5/5): The ambiance fits the steakhouse bill perfectly; rich decor paired with subdued lighting sets the stage for an authentic dining adventure. A 6:30 pm arrival on a Saturday might deceive you into thinking reservations aren't necessary, but as the clock strikes 7, the bustling crowd suggests otherwise.

Price ($$$): The cost is on the higher end, but for an occasional indulgence, it's a worthy expense. 

In summary, for a classic New York steakhouse experience with exceptional fare, this storied establishment is a must-visit. Just remember to book ahead if you're planning a dinner during peak hours!
There is a new Szechuan restaurant in town on 38th Street down the block from me, right next to the Australian.  The hot and sour soup, and ma po tofu are first rate.  Need try some other dishes!

If you love old school Hip Hop the way I do, you must visit this spot. The servers were great the hostess was very pleasant and the chicken & waffles were on point (I just wish the waffles were bigger). We ordered a mojito and a blood orange and enjoyed them as well. The music really makes the experience here special.

I recently celebrated my birthday at this fantastic restaurant with a party of seven, and we were all impressed from start to finish. Our waiter, Ferrari, was a standout, making us feel like family by the end of the meal with his exceptional service. The Chicken Parmesan is a must-try; don't judge it by its simplicity—it was delicious. The filet was also cooked to perfection, tender, and bursting with flavor. Do not pass up the chance to try the onion rings with the house steak sauce—it's a combination that's not to be missed. Overall, a great dining experience that I would highly recommend.

Really enjoyed this place when I was trying to find a place to eat with my partner that was affordable, healthy, and delicious tasting Mediterranean food. It's around NYU so it's a great place for students but also anyone who wants a chill ambience and quick food but options to sit down and be served or do take out.

Taco Mahal is a very casual take out place with limited seating and space. We stopped by here late night for quick snack. it was a good experience and the food was very tasty and unique. It Is a Mexican-Indian fusion where the tortilla is roti/naan and the fillings are made of traditional Indian cuisine like Panner tikka, Chicken tikka, chana masala etc. The flavors were absolutely remarkable and it all blended together wonderfully. The mango lassi was delicious in its own right! Over all, Taco Mahal is on point with their mash up of tacos and Indian cuisine. Absolutely delicious and on the affordable side. Would recommend this place to anyone! We will visit again when we're back in village area.

Loved the quality of their food and portions are great, easy to share between the table. We tried the Japanese butter dish, ootoya original unagi, Salmon Ikura Don, and the Buta Bara 3 Assortment. Everything was melt in the mouth and fresh, one of the better Japanese places I've tried. While it's a little pricey, this is a no tip establishment so it came out to be similar to another restaurant with tip. Can't wait to return to try more of their dishes.

Ordered on a coworker's recommendation and was just not at all impressed. The place (from pictures at least) looks pretty cool on the inside, but the food just does not speak for itself. I ordered the pasta pomodoro with a little spice and found it to be bland and overcooked. You cannot convince me that the sauce wasn't prego from a jar. At $13 for a basically two ingredient pasta that I could have made easily (and better) at my apartment, it seems a little like a rip off. Pastas with meat run you around $16. Portion size was fine - filling, but again, being that this isn't exactly an artisanal pasta makes me feel like I'm being robbed in broad daylight. Oddly enough the bread it came with was the best part. I'll also give them props for putting extra cheese on top as I requested.Had a couple of coworkers try my pasta too and they agreed that it was edible, but that's probably the most generous thing that could be said about it. It did arrive warm and on-time. Would not order again.

My three friends and I came on a snowy/sleety Sunday morning. This is an instagrammer's paradise - a stunning tiled, gorgeous bar, and the perfect lighting. Food wise- the food is good. The nachos and the chileatole soup were fantastic. Our other items were okay - the coconut queso quesadilla is truly "cheesy" but overloaded with raw onions, and the Azteca chile relleno left much to be desired. Perhaps the most disappointing part, was the fact that we informed our server about a severe carrot allergy and then finding the server recommended chorizo burrito filled with carrots. Pro-Tips:* You MUST try to the nachos. * Be careful if you have food allergies.* Vegan-friendly (obviously)* Good for Groups

I am so upset that I live in Chicago and can't eat at Mokyo everyday. I have been dreaming about this place since I've been back. I can confidently say  it's one of my favorite restaurants of all time. I found it while doing research for places I want to eat during my trip. After seeing it on foodbabyny's instagram, I decided I must give it a try. To be honest, there was nothing that really made it seem special, I just knew I wanted to try it and I am so glad we did.My husband and I went on a Thursday night around 9PM after coming from Sojo Spa Club. I was extremely famished since the last meal we had was around noon.We expected it to be fairly empty since it was late but still pretty filled but we didn't have to wait. We were welcomed very warmly by a woman I assume is the hostess. We were seated in a room separated from the bar area room. We quickly noticed that the restaurant was much smaller than expected but I didn't feel tight at all.Our server, who I believe was named Bernard (based on the receipt) was incredible. He honestly was a big part of why my husband and I enjoyed the restaurant so much. He welcomed us by asking if we've been there before and let us know a little about the restaurant. He asked if we wanted recommendations, but I had decided weeks before what I would order when we went, so he took our order immediately.We ordered the Beef Tartar, Corn Dumpling, Ceviche, Chicken, Noodle, and Pop Rocks.The Beef Tartar was wonderfully seasoned while still being able to taste the meat. It was nice and chewy with some additional texture that I really enjoyed. My husband really enjoyed the Corn Dumpling and I did too, but I don't think I could eat it all the time since it was very sweet. The Chicken was amazingly crispy and tasty. It was like gourmet popcorn chicken! I can still taste it just thinking about it. The Ceviche was good but I kind of wished there was more to it. It was clean and simple, but it felt like maybe just a little something was missing. Last of the main dishes we had the Noodles which was my favorite tied with the Beef Tartar. The noodles were literally perfectly cooked and chewy and silky. They had a really nice kick of spice that I just cannot get over. I dream about eating it again. For dessert we had the Pop Rocks which were amazing. I honestly didn't like it at first bite but I kept grabbing more and more and realized I was addicted. It was such an interesting mix in my mouth!We also ordered a Makgeolli Mojito and Yuzu Beer which were both delightful. I normally don't like alcohol but I loved the Mojito.The next night, my husband and I went to SakaMai and after being thoroughly disappointed we ended up back at Mokyo since I barely ate. Bernard immediately recognized us and I think he wasn't our main server but he still kept coming by to joke around and make recommendations. We ended up mainly ordering the same things we did the first time but we ordered the Seoul Nights Soju. It was definitely much tastier than regular soju but because I hate the taste of alcohol, I couldn't drink more than 2 shots. My husband loved it though and said he thought it was great quality and very smooth. Bernard ended up bringing us a complimentary dessert of Injeolmi which my husband and I debated on ordering since I was so full. I'm so glad we got to try it though because it was so amazing. It was like a little surprise treat! I wish I could explain what it was like but it was just so different. Maybe like a Ferrero Rocher?If I lived in New York, this would 100% be somewhere I'd visit at least once a week, if not more. Especially since Bernard made visiting the restaurant feel so great! My husband and I both agreed he's one of our favorite servers we've encountered. It seemed like a lot of other patrons recognized and loved him too! I really can't rave about him enough. I honestly feel like he was a big part of why we loved Mokyo so much. I can't wait to go back to eat here again!!

Was looking for a quick XLB fix and was not interested in venturing too far south to get the craving fixed. This joint popped up while I was near grand central and despite my skepticism, I decided to give it a shot. The joint itself has a clean décor and even a nice bar setup for those interested in dinner (I was there for lunch). The service was also good and speedy so definitely thumbs up there.The menu can be broken down to various proteins, noodles, dimsum, etc. Went for the pan fried dumplings, XLBs, Shanghainese noodles, chicken wontons in spicy oil. All of it actually was pretty solid and the quality was solid as well. The food came out speedy and came out in good proportion. The dumplings were good although the meat on the inside did seem a bit skimped on. The flavors were good and they seemed to strike the balance well of "Americanized vs authentic". Definitely recommend checking out especially in area as it will hit the crave.

Upon a recent visit to a bustling local ramen joint, I found myself taking a seat at the bar, a surprisingly unpopular choice amongst patrons despite its practicality, complete with handy hooks for personal belongings. The service, I must say, was commendably efficient, especially considering the team was short-staffed, with the kitchen staff pitching in to deliver dishes.

I dove into a bowl of tonkotsu chashu jiro ramen; the broth was thick and intensely flavored, teeming with pork fat. The noodles were udon-like in their thickness, which proved a bit too hefty for my preference, contributing to an almost bottomless sensation as I made little visible dent in the portion size, ultimately taking leftovers home. The chashu, while not discernibly marinated, got somewhat lost in the powerful soup base. A delightful surprise was the inclusion of a full egg, though it lacked the expected marinated depth.

Fair warning to those with a penchant for additional toppings: your bowl may runneth over. For those who favor a milder taste, be prepared; this broth packs such a punch that you may find yourself reaching for water to temper its robustness. While some may revel in its strong flavor profile, I found it overwhelmingly intense, necessitating dilution for balance.

Title: Overpriced Tacos and Disappointing Enchiladas

My recent visit to this hyped taco spot was underwhelming, to say the least. With tacos priced at a steep $8 each, expectations were high, but unfortunately, they fell flat. Frankly, you're better off hitting up Taco Bell or grabbing an Old El Paso kit from Walmart if you're looking to save money and not miss out on taste.

The chicken enchilada was a letdown; a mushy affair that was in desperate need of texture. The shredded cheese on top was unremarkable, adding little to the dish. Although the green tomatillo sauce provided a glimmer of hope, it was sparse, failing to elevate the overall flavor. In short, this restaurant seems to bank on their prices rather than their flavors, and I can't say it's worth the splurge.

My go to for a soothing delicious Matzah ball soup! Their portion is nice and it comes with a really nice piece of challah bread! I really enjoy it and they are very prompt. I always order takeaway for lunch!

My boyfriend and I recently decided to see what the hype around Ichiran was all about, and I'm glad we did. Unlike our usual spots Totto and Ippudo, we were pleasantly surprised to find no wait and were seated promptly beside each other. The custom ordering process was a breeze with a simple, efficient form detailing noodle firmness and spice level—just a button-press away from attentive service.

The ramen itself was delightful; the broth brimmed with flavor, striking all the right notes for a satisfying meal. While the combo proved to be a bit too generous for my appetite, I have my sights set on the classic with a noodle refill for my next visit. And a major plus—no tipping required, which is a refreshing change from the norm. Ichiran is a must-try for any ramen enthusiast!

I absolutely love it here. Walking up to this place is an experience. The set up is super dope. But that's not even the half. The service is top notch and the Food is even better. Inside is rustic meets Modern with an Caribbean twist. The menu on post on old record covers . Super cute . Anyways ! We ordered pitchers of rum punch mimosa and them sorrel mimosa for the second round . I had the ackee and salt fish on fried plantain boat. My friends had the shrimp and grits. Both were super tasty and beautifully presented.Me and the girls went for brunch on Sunday. It's worth it. The Food was so good. The vibe was so chill the music was right and I really can't wait to come back. Would I come back again ?? Definitely. I wanna try the dinner menu.Should you ?! Hell yea. Have the sorrel mimosa it was my favorite.

I visited Ippudo NY for a lunchtime ramen experience after avoiding the two-hour wait on a previous Friday night attempt. The acclaimed ramen fell short of expectations; the broth was overly robust and bitter, the noodles underdone and starchy, and the toppings disappointingly sparse. The lukewarm serving temperature also diminished the meal's enjoyment. A friend found the lunch set lacking, leaving her unsatisfied.

Despite its reputation and my experience, I suggest giving Ippudo a try for those new to the establishment, as my palate may not align with its well-regarded flavors. Be prepared for communal dining; the setup does not cater well to those preferring private seating with their party, especially during peak times when sharing tables is inevitable due to the restaurant's design favoring solo diners.

Title: Ajisen Ramen: Unbeatable Value in NYC

I've been enamored with Ajisen Ramen since my travels in Asia, so imagine my delight when they opened in NYC! This chain truly offers some of the best-priced ramen around. At a mere $9.50, options like the 3 tenderous rib ramen or the deluxe serving with char-siu and a tenderous rib are a steal. But it's the tenderous rib ramen that I must applaud - its meaty, soft, and juicy quality is unmatched. Tip: For an even better deal, head to their Chinatown location over Midtown. Ajisen is a budget-friendly ramen haven that doesn't skimp on quality.

I would give 3.5star this place if I could.I was going to try at Gopchang story but long line there and went to this place. I've been this place few times since last year. Food(3.5/5)-stopped by for late dinner with friend. We were so hungry and ordered a lot of food for only two people. We ordered beef Combo1. It's included beef brisket, bottom sirloin triangle,marinated beef kalbi with doenjang stew. You can choice any of stew you want if you order beef or pork combo. Also we ordered lunch box. When you eat lunch box they will shack tbefore they will show you. Beef brisket was just ok but their bottom sirloin triangle was amazing. Meat feast, deep and juicy, I thought I find my go to food in this place. Doenjang stew was good with beef brisket a lot inside of stew but it was little salty for me. Lunchbox was nothing special tasted.Service(5/5)- They will very happy to be you're there when you enter to entrance. All the staffs were super friendly. I saw the staffs helped out Caucasian for how to enjoy eating there. I thought they're first time at this place and actually they're right next to my table and they ordered food what we ordered lol. They know how to served food well and make sure everything you get what you need for. Ambience(3/5)- each tables are close and its uncomfortable eat food with friends or difficult talk from noise. This place was really noisy than other restaurant in K-town. I've sats on the second floor and it was nice than one floor but it's only my personal thought or opinion.

This is your standard Chinese takeout spot and they do a good job! Definitely my favorite in the area. Staff is very friendly, but this isn't really a place to stay and eat since there are only 2 tables. I got the pork fried dumplings and thought they were great. I will be back to try other items on the menu.

Stopped by Luu's Baguette for lunch recently, torn between my desire to warm up with a hot bowl of pho and my craving for a good banh mi. The sandwich won out, and I ordered #22 (banh mi cha lua nem nuong- pork roll with BBQ pork), which came out to $9.25 after tax. I thought it was just okay. Fine for the area because there aren't a lot of banh mi options, but not as good as places in Chinatown. The sandwich was kind of light on the fillings, especially considering the price, and I had several bites that were just bread because there wasn't enough meat or vegetables inside, which was a little disappointing. I liked that the service was quick and efficient. The restaurant looks small from the outside, but they have quite a bit of seating inside. Ordering is done at the counter, and they do have a credit card minimum. I don't know that I would come back for another banh mi, but might return to try the pho.

Ordered lunch from here for the first time and I was honestly pleasantly surprised!Got bolognese pasta as well as a tiramisu- i was skeptical for for ordering one hot and one cold dish for takeout and it totally met my expectation!The pasta was flavorful and I can tell it was quality veal meat. The tiramisu's flavor was delicious but it was a bit sad that the dessert tilted to one side during the transportation process so one side has no cake.Would definitely order from them again but would suggest them to change to another container for transportation as paper boxes for pasta is not that good of an idea.

Perfect brunch spot. My gf and I walked in around 1PM on a Sunday without a reservation and were seated at the bar within 10 minutes. I had the breakfast hummus and really enjoyed all of the flavor in it. I like that the egg was marinated (in what, idk but it was delicious) and that I had the option of dipping into the green sauce or the hummus. The falafel was crispy on the outside and perfectly soft on the inside. I would definitely come back and try the platter next time to get a bit of everything (we didn't want to be overstuffed this time around).

Food is really good, the experience could be better. The food was superb. I really could not have asked for more unique, well-executed, rich flavors and textures. We had the abalone tostada, crab infladita, the cobia al pastor, the duck carnitas, followed by the husk meringue w/ corn mousse. Every dish was stellar but the cobia al pastor was something truly unique with almost a sashimi-like smoothness of pork against a semi-sweet pineapple puree that was so delicious. The duck was unbelievably tender and rich, with a nice counterbalance from the radish and onions. The husk meringue was the star and pinnacle of our experience - a hard, sweet shell with a silky texture of corn (salty) and rich creaminess of regular mousse. But outside the food, something felt a little "off". It's hard to pinpoint but I think this place suffers from the "in between" syndrome or "trying to be something for everyone" identity. It was not fine-diney, not casual, sorta sceney (but not terrible), just mixed. The servers were very fast and impersonal and the dining experience did not feel "welcoming".  Very little effort to explain the menu. I think ownership did not go down the "fine dining" route because they wanted this restaurant to be more "affordable" and for the masses. The problem is because the portions are SO small, you end up having to spend a lot of $ to have a worth-while experience. I wish they would have just had this on a tasting menu and made it a high-end restaurant. Instead, despite the excellent food, because the overall experience, we left feeling like we spent too much money (4 dishes, 1 dessert,1 martini, it added up to $250 pre-tip). I think it's a 3.5 but I'll round up because the food was great.

Title: Happy Hour Haven at Barn Joo!

If you're on the hunt for an energetic spot to unwind after work, Barn Joo on 35th street is your go-to destination! Their happy hour is the highlight—with an appetizing selection of oysters, wings, and a variety of drinks that will leave you both satisfied and eager for more.

Although there's a sister location in Union Square, specifically famed for their oyster happy hour, the vibe here on 35th is just as enticing. The Korean-inspired tapas are a culinary delight, and the cocktails are crafted to perfection, ensuring that there's something for every palate.

Just a word to the wise: this place isn't a secret, so expect crowds. Arriving early is key, as they don't seat newcomers close to the end of happy hour, and it's last call for those already enjoying their time.

Service is a standout, with attentive and swift staff making sure your experience is top-notch even during the rush. While I found the table Korean BBQ to be a tad underwhelming considering the portion size and price, it's a minor hiccup in an otherwise stellar dining experience.

To top it all off, reservations and waitlist management through Yelp make planning your visit a breeze. Barn Joo is undoubtedly a prime spot for anyone craving great drinks and tapas in a vibrant atmosphere. Don't miss out on this happy hour hotspot!

If you're on the hunt for a satisfying lunch spot, this place is quite a find. The chicken is the star of the show—succulent and abundant in variety—ensuring you won't tire of the options. While the corn bread missed the mark with a burnt and dry texture, the side dishes redeem the meal. Don't leave without trying the elote corn and Brussels sprouts; they're my favorite picks to accompany the poultry and add a tasty way to balance your meal with veggies.

Love love love wok wok!First because it's kind of hard to find a good southeast asian cuisine in NYC and second because it's hard to find a good priced southeast asian cuisine in NYC.Ordered Hainanese chicken rice and roti prata as well as penang white curry noodle- the taste is unbelievable and the portion is big ! I do think it gives the biggest bowl of rice to go with Hainanese chicken as compared to anywhere else!It's also great with check-in offer, you get a free thai ice tea so remember to get that!The whole meal only costs us $23, which is pretty unbelievable!The only drawback is that they only accepts cash!

During restaurant week, my friend and I visited this spot at an off-peak hour (2 pm), and to our surprise, it was quite empty. The service started off on a slow note - a 15-minute wait just for menus, despite being the only patrons initially. This slowness persisted with inattentive service from our waiter.

The meal, however, had its highs and lows. The appetizers were a delight. My Fritto misto and my friend's tuna tartare were as aesthetically pleasing as they were flavorful. Main courses didn't live up to the starters; both my baked salmon and my friend's Brazino filet suffered from under-seasoning and left much to be desired.

Dessert partially redeemed the experience. My mixed berry trifle and the vanilla crème brûlée ordered by my friend were indulgent and satisfying conclusions to our culinary adventure. Despite the superb starters and desserts, the overall dining experience was undercut by lackluster mains and less-than-stellar service.

I grew up on this stuff!Rice noodles and fish balls! Every time my mom would go to Chinatown, she would bring a huge container and it seemed like it was never enough! The old cart by Hong Kong supermarket by east broadway and Bowery is long gone so I found this cart lady on Centre street. I tried getting some the other day and by 2pm on a Tuesday, she was sold out except for tea eggs.  Well I can make tea eggs myself so I passed. Today, I was determined to make it there early!  So I got there by 10:30am and she still had!  And she wasn't even busy, SCORE!! So I told her my order; 3 mediums along with a large congee for a friend.  I had other things I needed to eat so I settled for a medium and the 2 other ones were for my friends.  I told her that I'll pay her first and that I needed to go shop and I'll be back in 10 mins.  She said, yea yea, you go shop and I'll hold your stuff here.  Perfect! I did my shopping and was back 25 mins later.  She felt bad bcs she said she would have save me my portions and then just packed it later so it would be piping hot when I got back.  She was very kind.  When I got home, it was still piping hot and oh man, I dogged half of that container in minutes!!  Totally brought me back to my childhood.

Terrible place in Manhattan and let me tell you why: Came here with three of my friends around 11 am on a weekday for an early lunch. We sat down and it took 10 minutes for the server to bring us our menus. Okay fine, we can deal with that. We had to ask for drink menus as well. Hm okay, fine. There was a taco Tuesday special on the front of the menu that wasn't clear at all - apparently there's only two options for the 4 taco deal, which wasn't really worth it at all. On the menu it says you can get three tacos for $17, but they didn't even write that it was to be three of the same type of tacos. That's honestly ridiculous. I wanted to get the breakfast burrito, which was listed on the menu under burritos but when I ordered it, I was told that since it's a brunch item it was unavailable. What a terrible menu layout. It's so deceptive and annoying. On top of the annoying menu, the sauce jars are ridiculous. The top of the diablo sauce wasn't allowing sauce to come out and spilled all over my friend's blue shirt and on the wall. The employees clearly saw this happen and didn't even offer tissues. He went to the restroom to try to clean it and they didn't even have tissues in the restrooms. We ended up getting the fish burrito. Not gonna lie, it wasn't terrible, a solid 3/5 because the fresh ingredients were really fresh but man there definitely wasn't enough cod at all. And it was really dry- there was no sauce or anything to cut through the greasiness of the cod. My other friend had a chicken and fish taco, both which were super mediocre for the price. It was so disappointing.

I ordered from here for the first and the food was pretty good. Delivery was less than 40 minutes and the portion sizes are large. I love African food and eat it whenever I can afford to. They are sort of pricey with barely any dishes under $10. We ordered Suya with plantain, egusi with goat and pounded yam and fish pepper soup with pounded yam. They had plenty of meat options which I loved because I normally eat my egusi with stock fish so it was great to try it with goat. Suya tasted like plain steak, wasn't my favorite dish from here but this won't discourage me from ordering again. The fish pepper soup was deliiiccciiiooouusss. One of my favorite dishes. I was expecting a whole fish but won't complain because it was so flavorful and filling. And meal came with a free soda. Win. Win. Win.

Little Park is an absolute gem. From the owner of The Dutch and Locanda Verde comes a consistent, romantic Tribeca option. Appetizers and entrees taste as great as they look.  The wine selection is spot on and the service is second to none. This restaurant is top of the list for special occasions and business dining.

Title: A Cash-Only Gem with Authentic Asian Flavors

I recently dined at a wonderful restaurant that served an impressive array of Malaysian and pan-Asian cuisine. The highlight for me was the scrumptious roti appetizer, which was perfectly crispy and paired with a flavorful chicken and potato curry for dipping. For the main course, the beef fried noodle dish did not disappoint and I appreciated the option to kick up the spice to suit my palate. To combat the heat, the mango smoothie was a refreshing choice, especially on a warm day and offered a sweet relief from the spices.

However, there were a couple of drawbacks. Our experience was slightly marred by a particularly boisterous group in the back, which detracted from the restaurant's otherwise cozy ambiance. Additionally, in a modern world where cashless transactions are norm, I was taken aback that the restaurant was cash-only. Despite these issues, the food was outstanding. If I could, I would have rated this restaurant 5 stars, but due to these inconveniences, I'm settling on 4 stars. Remember to hit the ATM before you go, and hopefully, you'll find a quieter dining experience than I did!

I had a pleasant experience at this conveniently located spot, perfect for grabbing a quick bite. Their vast array of breakfast and lunch options impressed me, and I opted for the BLT. Service was speedy, and I appreciated how my sandwich was freshly prepared before my eyes. Although I chose to take my meal to-go, the available seating is a nice touch for dine-in guests. I look forward to my next visit!

B-Side Pizza is without a doubt one of my absolute favorite pizza spots in the city. Had heard about the place a few times in the past and randomly found ourselves in Hell's Kitchen late one day (Well, late for me) The wait wasn't too long, and after we sat down, I was immediately drawn to the Carbonara pizza, featured in a lot of the reviews. The pizza included Fontina, Mozzarella, and Parmesan cheese along with Pancetta and an egg, and the first bite was almost over-powering my taste buds -- but in a good way. The flavor was unbelievable with a salty, cheesy profile made complete with the Pancetta and egg whisked across the center. The Killer Bee pizza was almost as good, a slightly better version of the pizza at Paulie Gee's in Brooklyn. Finally, the place itself is also cozy and romantic, with top-notch service; a great date night spot.
Came here for lunch. Food took a long while to arrive. Salmon Burger was really good. My friends enjoyed the Egg dishes as well. Favorite was their Sweet Potato Fries, crispy and soft and tasty!

Restaurant Review: Tang Hotpot Delivers on Experience and Flavor

My love for interactive hotpot dining led me to Tang Hotpot, a place that elevates this beloved culinary tradition with its impeccable style and taste. The modern Chinese decor is striking, featuring an Instagram-worthy ambiance with industrial lighting, copper accents, and a stunning mural that captures the essence of communal eating.

As a centerpiece of our meal, the Ying Yang pot, with its pork bone and mildly spicy beef tallow broths, hit all the right notes. The Tang Deluxe platter showcased the freshness and quality of their offerings, with perfectly selected Kobe ribeye, lamb tenderloin, pork shoulder, and a seafood assortment that included succulent scallop, tiger prawn, and sea bass. Additional delights like the crawfish fried rice and the visually intriguing and delectable cuttlefish paste, which turns an enigmatic shade of blue, were unforgettable. The fried pork belly, another addition, was a standout.

Dessert was a beautifully subtle grass jelly, enhanced with nuts, raisins, and mochi — a gentle, sweet conclusion to a robust feast. 

Service was exceptional, with our waiter, James, providing insightful recommendations and maintaining a careful watch to ensure our dining experience was flawless.

Though prices are on the higher side, they reflect the high-quality ingredients and top-notch service. Tang Hotpot is a worthwhile splurge for anyone seeking an excellent hotpot experience.

I recently dined at a restaurant that took me by surprise – in the best way imaginable. As someone who generally leans towards meat-centric meals, I was thoroughly impressed by the vegetarian dishes served here. They managed to escape the typical vegetarian flavor profile, offering a delectable alternative that didn't make me miss meat at all. The service was another highlight; despite our sizable luncheon group, the staff was quick and attentive. A standout dish for me was the meatless sweet and sour pork, which was a delightful paradox, both familiar and innovative. All in all, the meal was exceptionally tasty, and I'd highly recommend this restaurant to vegetarians and meat-eaters alike.

Title: A Cut Above During Restaurant Week

During the bustling Restaurant Week, I found myself at a charming venue, eager to dive into a curated dining experience. The ambiance struck an immediate chord with me—indoors, it was low-lit and classy, while the patio offered a breath of fresh air where I ultimately decided to dine. Service mirrored the setting, with a delightfully sweet waitress, Jenny, and a host team that amiably navigated my seating indecision.

The Restaurant Week menu was my guide for the night. Unfortunately, the Sweet Chili Calamari appetizer veered too far into the saccharine territory, overshadowing any savoriness I had anticipated. The entree, a medium-cooked Filet Mignon, redeemed the meal—exquisitely cooked, it was an effortless joy to cut and savor, although the particulars of garnish and pairing have slipped my mind.

Dessert—a Butter Cake a la Mode—arrived a victor in texture, but again a tad too sweet for my liking; so much so, that the vanilla bean ice cream seemed less sweet in comparison. My mother, with a penchant for sugary treats, inherited the remaining cake.

An honorable mention goes to the complimentary fresh bread and pretzels, a small but appreciated touch. Jenny's Cucumber Gimlet recommendation couldn't have been more spot-on, its complexity so enthralling that the cucumber slices became a part of the meal.

Overall, it was a lovely interlude amidst the city hubbub, and while the sweets may have stumbled, the experience was a solid four out of five. A slight deduction for the overwhelming sweetness, but a visit I'll remember fondly nonetheless.

My dining experience last night was quite a treat. The waiter's suggestion for two appetizers and a shared pot was ambitious, as it turned out to be more than we could manage. The jalapeno chicken captivated with its heat, while the lobster impressed with its freshness. Our main course, the tomato seafood pot, offered a delectable broth that I wished had more shrimp to suit my preference. Dipping the slightly greasy roti in the broth enhanced its flavor, and the veggie rice complemented the pot nicely. A special nod to the service—it was exemplary and truly elevated the meal.

On a quiet Wednesday morning, my visit to FIELDTRIP was nothing short of delightful thanks to Kira's exceptional service. As someone with dietary restrictions, her willingness to accommodate my no-dairy requirement was much appreciated. The veggie bowl was a highlight, showcasing a symphony of flavors where the vegetables truly shone, particularly the perfectly prepared collard greens that still held a delightful al dente texture—a far cry from the overcooked varieties of my Texan childhood.

The bowl's butternut squash was another standout, adding a sweet contrast to the greens. The quinoa bao buns were a hit, especially when paired with the carrot dip, which brought a lovely sweet heat that enhanced everything it touched. Although I avoided the dairy-filled nana bread, it resembled a scallion pancake and seemed quite popular among other diners.

While the fried chicken was flavorful, I missed the promised crispiness, finding it overly drenched in sauce. Between the two rice options, I favored the basmati over the Carolina gold, but I'm already eager to return for the sticky rice and green curry. While Rice-focused dishes are FIELDTRIP's forte, I regretfully missed out on the rice hibiscus soft serve—an oversight I intend to correct on my next visit.

Diving into the latest culinary addition to our neighborhood, I ventured into Goku Ramen, the successor of the erstwhile Kame, whose Dragon Ball Z-inspired lineage has been cleverly preserved right down to the name and décor. Indeed, their homage to the anime is commendable, sparking curiosity about licensing logistics, but that's a mystery for another day.

The heartening inclusion of a vegetarian bowl caught my attention, catering to the meat-free with a rich, umami-packed broth that rivals its meaty counterparts. The bowl boasted a generous mix of veggies, kimchi, and corn, creating a melange of flavors and textures that left my pescatarian palate deeply content.

However, an improvement is needed with their hard-boiled eggs. While the rest of the meal hit the high notes, the blandness of the added egg was a disappointing contrast to the typically flavorful soy sauce-infused offerings at other ramen spots. A simple tweak could elevate the dish immensely.

Adding to the appeal, the takoyaki served as a delectable precursor to the main dish. Bonus points for the wallet-friendly perks: a lunchtime deal halves the price of appetizers with an entree, while savvy diners can benefit from a substantial Yelp check-in discount. Remember to choose wisely between the offers for maximum savings. Despite the egg misstep, Goku Ramen bowls over with value and variety, ensuring a delightful experience for anime fans and foodies alike.

Grrreat greeting at the door. Lovely wait staff behind the bar who wiped down the counter right away and explained how this place works...basically u can order from the menu OR build your own burger. I was in a hurry bec I had tickets to a show, and this place looked clean and upscale and I was craving a burger.  I ordered their signature namesake...The Counter....medium...the waitresses asked me if it was ok for it to be pink in the middle...and it was a true medium. There were mushrooms and shoestring derp fried onions....all on a bioche... the bun was soft, the meat was medium...but sometimes I'd hit something very salty...the little container of aioli sauce was soooooo salty. And the burger in some bites were highly salted. Too bad. I really wanted to like the burger. It looked soooo appetizing. Alas.

The stars are for the amazing meatballs. Some of the best I've ever had, really delicious....as long as I don't think too much about the fact that they're made from veal.The pasta was extremely regular, something you'd make yourself in 10 minutes when you're feeling lazy and have jarred sauce on hand. The salad was salad, lots of iceberg lettuce, lots of raw onion to pick out. The lemon chicken was just disgusting. I hate food waste and feel guilty and time I have to throw food away, but neither my husband nor my son could finish a bite of it. The texture, the taste, the sauce....just terrible.Like most New Yorkers, I've held out hope that one day a nice mobster would invite me to a fabulous dinner at Rao's....
