I can still hold out hope for Tiro A Segno! The $80 was worth it to let me know that I wasn't missing anything, no more known unknowns.

If it isn't a distance away from where I live! I might get this almost every day. The selections are amazing and the flavoring of the food is absolutely delicious. Everything is cooked freshly, starting off with your base then to two sides and then your protein. I believe if you like to add a additional side it'll be extra for it. Staff was friendly, very helpful. They checked to see if it's your first time, kind of guide you how it works. But honestly I looked at the menu on their website first to see what they are offering.There's a great seating area, great for a quick lunch/dinner grab n go type of chain.P.s if you check in on yelp they'll give you a complimentary drink :)

This place is a hidden gem with affordable after dinner sweet bites. They offer a variety of flavors and when you get a cone, they will place your second flavor to look like petals of a flower. For a kids cone, you can try two flavors. So affordable for what you get and the quality of the gelato.

I'm really happy that I tried this ramen spot after walking passed it in Ktown. I've been to plenty of ramen places and my top three favorites are Ippudo, Totto, and now Koku Ramen! I used the yelp check-in to get the Kara Age appetizer for free. They gave a pretty large portion of the appetizer along with a spicy sauce almost like spicy mayo. The chicken had a crispy outer shell with a soft dark meat inside layer. I do like to eat Kara Age with lemon to bring out the flavor of the chicken, so i asked for some and was brought lemon without a problem.For the ramen, I tried the ramen the waiter recommended which turned out to be the more popular one. I'm not a huge spicy fan, so i got it not spicy. It was amazing and had a really good flavor. I appreciated that the broth wasn't over salty either. The pork chahsu pieces inside the ramen were amazing and torched a little bit. Along with that, I loved the unique egg half inside the ramen. The noodles tasted hand made and the bak choy was an interesting twist.Overall, everything was great including the service! They also accept card unlike Toto ramen. Give this place a try because I'll be coming back!!

This place has been on my list for ages, and let me tell you, they do vegan right.Sure, not everything is TOTALLY HEALTHY.. cause that's not what vegan means, but every bite I had was totally scrumptious. It probably helped that I was ravenous post work meeting that I was in town for, but the spicy Thai salad, dressing on the side was objectively fantastic. The sweet, the heat, the crunch, the munch. Into all of it. Also stole a few air popped fries from a colleague - yes. MORE AIR FRIED FRIES PLEASE. It's a little pricey, but I imagine that's par for the course for this area of Manhattan in particular - accessible enough, especially when work was footing the bill. I think it was around $100 for 6 of us, and 3 of us tried the lemonade.

Upon my multiple visits to this standout Korean BBQ gem in Koreatown, Manhattan, I've been consistently impressed. This place isn't just a meal; it's an experience - one that's garnered well-deserved attention, including a nod from Time Out as one of the best Korean BBQ grills in Manhattan.

The restaurant's cleanliness is immediately noticeable, setting the stage for the main act: the freshest, meatiest Pork Belly you could ask for. Served on a perfectly set table grill, this Pork Belly is the epitome of juicy and fresh. Complementing the main dish is an array of banchan, those delightful Korean side dishes, which are varied and come with unlimited refills – a real treat for taste buds seeking authentic flavours.

Pairing the savory meats with a traditional Korean soju amplifies the experience, invoking the essence of dining in Korea itself – an illusion further solidified by their stainless steel chopsticks, which are a sophisticated touch.

The staff, always friendly, enhance the dining experience with their attentiveness and warmth.

A word to the wise: plan for a 45-minute wait due to the restaurant's popularity. But believe me, it's worth every minute. Whether it's your first visit or your fifth, the excellence of this Korean BBQ spot remains unwavering.

This is really a 3.5 star place. The food was very average. The Shabu Shabu was good - very tender beef and loved the cabbage - but would've liked if it came with more different vegetables beyond just cabbage. It needed a little more variety. There was maybe one or two small pieces of tofu and that was it. The pork appetizer was a little overcooked and not as tender as I would've liked. I did really like the sake and they seemed to have a nice list, though most of them were sold out for the night.

Now this is what call southern good! I come from the south, and am quite skeptical when a place not from the south says that they can make true southern comfort food. But baybeeee this place hits the spot! I had the barbecue chicken with collard greens and candied yams. All dishes were absolutely delicious. (They were so good that it honestly reminded me of when I visit my home state). I ordered a slice of red velvet cake to go, which was also absolutely amazing!  I highly recommend his place! Ps. They give you complimentary corn bread.

I recently had the pleasure of trying the new fast-casual spot opened by the Wayla team, conveniently situated right above their original restaurant. The concept is straightforward, allowing diners to build their bowl with a choice of base and an array of proteins and vegetables. I opted for rice crowned with tofu, eggs, and ground chicken, which packed a delightful spicy punch. To balance the heat, I highly recommend the frozen Thai iced tea—it's a refreshing complement to the flavorsome meal. If you're looking for quick yet excellently executed fare, this is a must-visit.

Title: A Satisfying Farewell Meal at Bluebird London

I approached Bluebird London with a usual skepticism towards new restaurants, but my visit, just before NYC's lockdown, left me pleasantly surprised. It became a memorable last dine-out experience.

Post-workout hunger pangs had my friend and I eager to sample what Bluebird had to offer. Greeted by a warm hostess and seated at a desired window table, we navigated the single-use menus with excitement. Our coffee orders, a Flat White and a Cortado, arrived with an impeccable bitterness - a promising start.

Opting for an indulgent meal, we shared a carafe of mimosas, an afternoon tea set, an English breakfast, and a fried chicken sandwich. Each dish was a delight for the senses. The sandwich boasted a perfect crunch and a juicy interior, balanced by a refreshing coleslaw. Notably, it managed to avoid any greasiness. Meanwhile, my friend was impressed by the substantial and flavorful English breakfast, ranking it highly compared to his past experiences.

Our mimosas hit the perfect note, leaving us happily buzzed. The afternoon tea set was an unexpected star, with each sampler bursting with flavor. It was clear that meticulous care had gone into the preparation.

Service at Bluebird London is worth highlighting. It matched the quality of the food, rounding out our visit on a high note. With eager anticipation, I look forward to returning to Bluebird London and highly recommend it to others seeking a balanced, enjoyable dining experience.

Title: "A Unique New Year's Eve Experience at Olive Garden"

My New Year's Eve at Olive Garden for their private event was a mix of challenge and charm. The ticket, priced at a steep $400, grants you access to witness the ball drop—albeit the view is better enjoyed outside the restaurant.

Getting there was no easy feat; Times Square's security barricades meant we had to navigate through strict checkpoints. Only after insisting and showing our tickets did officers allow us to proceed to Olive Garden. The anticipation built as we queued in a lengthy line before finally being escorted inside.

The interior experience was a stark contrast to the initial hassle. Greeted with a wristband, we were entitled to unlimited alcohol throughout the evening. Food-wise, the offerings were standard Olive Garden fare served within a fixed timeframe. Despite the ordinary menu, the perk of having a seated refuge from the cold, complete with access to pristine restrooms, cannot be overstated.

The staff's amiability added warmth to the wintry night, and mingling with fellow attendees from across the globe enriched the event. Overall, while the entry price is quite hefty and the entry process was a bit cumbersome, the convenience and opportunity to experience the ball drop in comfort made for a memorable first-time experience.

I'm astonished it's taken me so long to review this gem, especially given its proximity to my former workplace. With the chef's roots in the famed Din Tai Fung, my eagerness to taste their soup dumplings again was off the charts—something NYC sorely lacks, in my opinion. Their beef noodle soup and fried rice became my go-to delights for regular lunch breaks. And when time permitted, the soup dumplings were a non-negotiable indulgence.

After years away, I revisited this spot on 2/27, just before life took a chaotic turn. It was a reminder of what I had been missing and a prompt to myself to return more frequently. For anyone craving that Din Tai Fung magic, this place holds its own as my top pick for soup dumplings.

On a whim, my party and I stopped by this restaurant, reservations looming just 30 minutes away, and we decided to indulge in a quick appetizer. Our choice was the shrimp appetizer, accompanied by drinks. The portion size took us by surprise – a generous serving that comfortably satisfied three of us. But it wasn't just the quantity that impressed; the quality was equally remarkable. The shrimp was expertly prepared, and the sauce it came with was nothing short of extraordinary.

To complement the food, our drinks were skillfully mixed, striking the right chord of flavor and refreshment. Given that we were in New York City, where prices can soar, the value for money here stood out as reasonable and justifiable.

I seldom dole out recommendations freely, but for this appetizer – and the place that serves it – I make an exception. If you find yourself in the neighborhood, don't hesitate to visit.

As a ramen enthusiast, I believe the broth is the soul of the dish. While dining at Mentoku, I tried the pork tantanmen, which boasted a rich and flavorful broth. Although the depth of flavor was impressive, I found it slightly on the greasier side for my liking. Nonetheless, I was impressed with the generous portion sizes provided with my Mealpal order, a pleasant surprise from Mentoku that I appreciated.

I went on a Saturday evening for roast pork and roast chicken over rice. But roast pork was over. So I only got roast chicken over rice. For $4.25 that was enough food. Chicken was tender and very flavorful. Rice was fragrant. There was a good amount of oil in the food. I would definitely go back for more.

My boyfriend and I were craving ramen and decided to give Minca a try. A few of his friends have recommended Minca and said it's a must try. Although the store itself is pretty small and packed, we were seated within 5 minutes. We ordered the Minca Ramen and the Minca Sio Ramen which includes half pork and half chicken broth. Our order arrived pretty quickly, which was a plus because we were starving! The portion of the ramen was perfect, won't leave you hungry or too full. But my favorite part was the chasiu; it was so tender and melts in your mouth. My mouth is watering as I write that. I will be back to try the other flavors.

How easy you can take a place for granted. We resently had a monsoon here and I was trapped in my building without a life jacket.  My stomach was speaking to me in a foreign tongue and it think it was saying 'feed me!'. So I go down to Delgado right there in our lobby and I see they got Cuban Sandwich on the menu and that's what I get. It was legit, ham, pork swiss cheese, pickle and a touch of garlic mustard on pressed toasted soft bread.What can I say other than Delgado save me from my demons from within.

I recently visited a delightful little spot that instantly charmed me with its super cute ambiance. The highlight of their menu for me was the variety of tinned fish options, complemented perfectly with a luscious crab dip. They served these with an ample supply of bread, dressed parsley, butter, and salt, making sure not to skimp on the essentials, which I greatly appreciated.

The drinks menu was simple yet delicious, aligning well with the overall vibe of the place. The service was pleasant, adding to the cool and relaxed atmosphere. It’s the perfect spot for an afternoon snack, especially on a nice day when you can enjoy an open window breeze. I’m already looking forward to my next visit!

Title: A Charming Evening with a Minor Miss

Our dining experience at the restaurant within this charming old hotel was largely a delight. The rich abundance of hardwood lent a warm, inviting atmosphere, perfect for a cozy dinner. We had a reservation for four, and even with an early arrival, we were promptly seated without hassle. 

The service was commendable – the wait staff was patient, attentive, and ensured we had a quality experience throughout the evening. The salads, an endive and a palm, were fresh, crisp, and tastefully dressed. The pasta dishes, especially the ravioli, angel hair with garlic and olive oil, and the gnocchi with sausage in cream sauce, were the stars of the meal – each dish exuding its own flavorful character.

Unfortunately, the pizza failed to rise to the occasion, tasting akin to a regrettable frozen variety with an overcooked crust. This was the only notable disappointment, as it was clear the kitchen's attention to detail fell short.

A mention must be made about the ladies' restroom upstairs; while aesthetically pleasing with beautiful tiles and sink, it was in slight disrepair with a mismatched toilet seat and questionably positioned toilet paper – a contrast to the otherwise spotless ambiance of the restaurant.

Ending on a high note, the cappuccinos and selection of wines were excellent, complementing the meal beautifully. Moreover, the restaurant's prime location amidst the city's finest shows added to its appeal. Despite the minor setbacks, the experience was one to remember for its character and culinary delights.

We were going to a nearby theater not realizing that the St. Patricks Day Parade would be held a day early this year. Saw the Red Flame Diner and decided to go in, partly to escape the crowds. The diner had a festive atmosphere with lots of parade goers but not overly crowded. We were quickly shown to a spacious booth. We both opted for bagel and lox all the way, nice big toasted bagels with a few slices of lox and all the trimmings for $14.95, a steal for Midtown. Our friendly server even offered free refills on the iced tea. We splurged on a piece of warm cherry pie a la mode for dessert, absolutely delicious with lots of whipped cream and a nice slab of vanilla ice cream, plenty to share. I happen to be a pie maven and theirs seemed ultra fresh and homemade. By that time the parade had passed by and we were able to be on our way. So glad we happened on the Red Flame and plan to return again soon.

Title: Sunday Brunch Buzz at The Hip Spot

My brunch experience at this place, just a short stroll from the 2nd Ave F subway station, was a delightful urban adventure. The Sunday crowd was bustling, yet the wait was a mere 30 minutes before we were cozily seated by the window – a prime spot in the restaurant's cool industrial setting, pulsing with trendy tunes and a stylish clientele.

The menu sampling included shrimp & grits, chicken & waffles, and a side of ricotta pancakes – an ambitious spread to really get a taste of what they offer. The attentive waitstaff ensured prompt service, which was much appreciated amidst the lively atmosphere.

While the vibe effortlessly hit the high note of a perfect 5, the food, though good, didn't quite soar as high, landing at a 3.5. But despite that, the overall brunch experience was solid, earning a well-deserved 4 out of 5. It's a spot I'd recommend for anyone looking for that buzzing social scene with a side of brunch.

One of the few places in the city with decent Mexican fare that does not make this former Texan wrinkle her nose. First of all it's cute in here. Secondly the ingredients are fresh and they balance out well in the dishes they offer. They have decent drink specials and can feed a temporary  vegetarian without leaving anyone hungry. I really enjoyed the ensalada de melon. That cantaloupe, watermelon, jícama action is really refreshing.I also enjoy the outdoor seating. Good for people watching and enjoying the weather although 2nd ave is a busy road in this section.

Life has been rough lately. My parents are rarely able to leave the house now except for doctor appointments. I wanted to treat my parents to something good and something different from their usual Chinese food. Something my mom had always wanted to try was French cuisine but did not have the courage to do so with just my dad due to their language barrier. Today was the perfect chance along with my sister! I made a reservation through their website and they called me to make a confirmation in the afternoon. Very simple!We were not very accustomed to having olive oil for our bread. Very interesting. But I must say, the olive oil was very rich. For the appetizer, we ordered the Escargots and the Ravioli. We were advised that the sauce for the Escargots went well with the bread and it definitely did not disappoint! We loved the combination! Unfortunately, we were given the onion soup instead of the Ravioli dish but it's okay. We are open to trying other things. We actually were not big fans of the soup but I believe it's just an acquired taste. We know for a fact that my sister's godmother would have loved it.(I picked at everyone's food lol)For Entre, my mom had the Tournedos Rossini (filet mignon) cooked medium-well. She LOVED it. The meat was very very tender and still considerably juicy as she got it cooked longer than I would personally prefer. The sauce was good but a bit on the salty side. Still yum.My dad ordered the Magret de Canard (duck). I thought this was a pretty solid dish, my runner up choice! I guess I cannot say too much about it since I only had one bite but I did enjoy it!My sister ordered the Gnocchi Parisian au Gratin (Mac and Cheese). This was, unfortunately, our least favorite dish. She usually LOVES her cheese and would never turn away from Mac and Cheese but for some reason, this particular version was not very enticing. Could not really put our finger on it though...Now my dish (and my favorite) was the Onglet Poele a la Luchonaise (Hanger steak) ordered medium-rare! My sister's first reaction was "Is that really a legitimate French dish if it is not found in NYC or anywhere else?" but hey, when the dish came out, it became her favorite too! It is not as tender as the Filet Mignon but the flavor was much more intense. Simple but delicious.This is a place I would definitely come back to. Was it a fancy fancy French restaurant that we see on TV? No, but it does not make the food any less delightful.I must also say, the service was wonderful. The staff is super attentive but not overwhelming and made me feel very comfortable!It is very interesting that they only accept AMEX, cash, check??? and cryptocurrency but not too overwhelming. I had to make sure to stop by the bank before coming.
And why not day drink when it's humid and there is a table waiting for you Wonderful window service and $7?! Yes!!! Thanks Bettola for the lovely service and excellent drinks!!
If you're indecisive like me, stop in for their happy hour and get a bit of everything! Great spot for some fresh seafood. I will definitely be back

Title: A Sweet Symphony of Flavors at This Artisanal Dessert Haven

Review:
Prepare to be dazzled at this dessert utopia, where indulgence meets innovation. It's not just the Instagram-worthy presentation that'll catch your eye—the flavors here are equally sensational. Yes, the prices reflect the high-end artistry of the treats, but believe me, it's worth every penny for these edible masterpieces. The staff enhances the experience with their excellent service, and it's a delight to behold the variety of confections on other patrons' tables.

I indulged in the lavender sweet potato bubble milk, an exquisite blend that danced on my palate. The regret of the day? Forgetting to take home the stylish reusable cup it came in. My companion's choice, the hot lavender tea, was a soothing concoction needing no embellishments. Accompanying it was the whimsical 'Head in the Clouds' dessert—a delectable stack of strawberry ice cream, whipped cream, fresh berries, and a cloud of cotton candy.

Bottom line: Splurge a little at this spot for a memorable treat—you'll leave on cloud nine!

Came in here lunch and they had a 9.95$ lunch special which came with 1 app, entree and either a soup or salad. This is such a good deal and it's pretty filling as well.I ordered the curry puff (they have me 1 piece), the soup, and pork Pad Sea Ew which was delicious.

I stopped by for a quick lunch at this local spot on a Wednesday afternoon. As someone who has enjoyed their fare during work meetings, I was intrigued to see the place in person. Opting for a pepperoni and mushroom slice, I found the pizza to be passable, albeit a tad dry and more expensive than I would have preferred. While there are superior pizza joints within walking distance, the redeeming quality here was the efficient and amiable staff. It's a convenient option for those times when convenience trumps the quest for the ultimate slice.

Title: "A Gem in the Heart of New York: Barn Joo 35"

During my recent trip to New York, Barn Joo 35 proved to be a delightful discovery, thanks to a friend's recommendation. This Korean eatery enchanted me with its three floors, each boasting its unique yet aesthetically pleasing decor.

The culinary experience was impressive with delectable and hearty Korean dishes. It's worth noting the prices were on the higher end, but the quality and taste justified the cost.

The highlight of Barn Joo 35, however, was the exceptional service. The staff were remarkably attentive, ensuring our dining experience was nothing short of perfect, striking the right balance between being helpful and giving us space.

In conclusion, the combination of great food and stellar service ensures that Barn Joo 35 is on my list for a must-visit when I'm back in the city.

One of the best dim Sum restaurant by tasting. The waitresses are very attentive! The restaurant looks little dated. Very convenient and no far from Time Square. I enjoyed their dim sum. Almost all excellent. I'll be back next time when I'm in New York !

finally got to try this place for a weekend brunch with friend. it was packed when I walked in and the lines only get longer as I was dining with my friend. i ordered the Blueberry pancake while my friend had the tomato soup and egg white omelette. the pancakes were pretty fluffy, came in decent portion, were not too sweet, and blended nicely with the tartness of the blueberry compote. was it the best pancake i've had? probably not, but it sure was a pretty good one. my friend seemed to enjoy her meal as well. despite of being packed, at least we still get to talk without having to scream at each other. so for a quick catch up brunch this place would be a pretty good option. however if you want to stay for long, perhaps you need to find somewhere else since there's always a long line and you need to go as soon as you finish your foodservice was pretty good. i think the staffs are trying their best to be patient despite of the overwhelming amount of customers (and their demand) they have to handle. price wise i'd say it's average and reasonable

This is literally across the Rockefeller Building epi- center . Would be the best and recommended Chinese restaurant  in the area as it is a sit down  style unlike the buffet style few yards up. It is on a second floor and not wheelchair accessible. The place needs an update if they want to gather more customers to come by. We ordered the Peking  duck , fried rice and veggies. Food is okay.  As a customary, free hot  tea , free orange fruit and a hot towel for  hands clean up at the end of the meal. Pricey , we paid extra because of  its prime location.

The Black Ant was pretty busy when we arrived, but it was easy to get a reservation online for our party of 6. Once you walk through the restaurant, you'll see that they also have another section in the back that has skylight windows, pretty darn cute back there.They have happy hour every day from 4-7pm, I would recommend going there then as their prices are pretty high for things like tacos. All food items on their HH menu is $10.Guacamole $10Pretty basic guacamole. The version with black ant salt is $16, not sure that's worth the upgrade.Tacos de Pescado $10 (2 tacos)Sadly these came out cold...the crust was not crispy enough, and the fish inside kind of had a rough texture. Wish it was more tender.Tacos de Pulpo $10 (2 tacos)This was probably the best item on the HH menu - this taco is filled to the brim with octopus, cooked perfectly! Might have been slightly too salty, but that's nitpicking.These were off their regular menu:Croquetas de Chapulin $16Most excited for this before I came as I saw several photos and reviews from others, but this one was the biggest disappointment. It looked nothing like all the other pictures, everything was falling apart, the breading on the outside was not crispy and light, and the grasshoppers on top were not crunchy enough (tasted stale...). Did not taste good...really seemed like the chef didn't know how to make it that day??Crepa $25This was really good, but this was soooooo small for $25. This was literally a mini green crepe with mushrooms and shaved truffle. The crepe had a great texture, but again, way too small.Bunuelo de Pato $25These crispy duck dumplings were like deep fried wontons stuffed with a mushy duck filling. Came with 7 of them. Not sure I'd order this again.Baby Corn Side $8Kinda wish this was a corn on the cob or something, the baby corn lacked flavor. The sauce on the side tasted ok but I think what was black ant salt didn't really do anything for the flavor or texture.Disappointing... especially on the items with insects. It has to add something to the dish, or else why add it / pay the premium for it?

Tucked away just a stone's throw from Central Park, this gem of a restaurant offers an exceptional lunch special that is hard to beat. The Japanese-Thai fusion cuisine served here strikes a delightful balance between flavors and textures, providing a perfect retreat after a leisurely day in the park.

Lunch begins with a comforting bowl of miso soup, followed by a crisp, fresh salad, setting the stage for the main event. The entrée, a masterful blend of Japanese and Thai culinary traditions, is both satisfying and impressively presented, ensuring a memorable dining experience. The quality and value of the lunch special are unparalleled, and the innovative fusion leaves you eager to return for more.

Ordered take out with my co worker, I had really high expectations for this place because of the location and how busy it was.  The food was mediocre, and for the price tag it shouldn't be that (regardless of their "lunch special". ) There was zero quality in their dry pepper chicken combo.  The chicken was all breading and loaded with hot peppers that weren't even edible.  The presentation was nice and appealing to the eye, but for what I pay, I want food - not cheap ingredients and breading.Later that night my co worker and I both got sick.  Maybe an odd coincidence, maybe not.  I won't return to find out.

As a lover of outdoor space such as rooftops and patios, I've had Gallow Green bookmarked forever. Finally came here after Sleep No More (to be reviewed separately) and had a great time. The entrance is beautiful and overall ambience is chill. Most of the guests also came from Sleep No More and there were some very interesting discussions going on. Four stars instead of five because the cocktails, albeit tasty and pretty, are (expectedly) pricey. My friend and I ordered burgers with fries and they were solid, but again (expectedly) on the pricier side. Also, bring bug/mosquito repellent in the summer if you attract mosquitoes like me... Else be prepared for a feast - I mean, be the feast - for those little bloodsuckers.

10/25/19 After the Fantasia concert we were hungry from yelling, singing, dancing and straight acting up. lol Side Bar: Tank and Robin Thicke opened for her. I had no idea Robin could dance. Getting down dancing on his piano. He was great. Fantasia was excellent.Okay, back to TSQ. It was fine. 1a so it wasn't crowded. I had a burger and couldn't finish it. It was huge. Good. My girls had no complaints. Just, the dirty utensils  that were on the table they sat us at. Yuck. The staff didn't make us feel welcome, but again it was late.One other dislike. The restroom is on the second floor. They are not catering to the handicapped and infirmed. That was upsetting to me.Would I eat there again? No.Happy Eats

First things first: I fell in love with the decor, both exterior and interior. Located in the center of the Theatre District, this upscale spot helmed by Michelin-star Chef Hemant Mathur boasts hot pink and turquoise signage with large windows looking into the restaurant, along with beautiful hot pink curtains. Upon entering, there's a lovely waiting area with comfortable seating: Cream colored couch with intricate designs on it and green-blue toned pillows, as well as black and beige plush chairs with colorful pillows. In between were little circular tables with bright yellow flowers in a glass container. The dining area had hot pink plush seats, blue wallpaper with pink flowers, lanterns and towards the back there was booth seating for 4 people. There was also a bar along one side of the restaurant that was prettily lit up in deep purple with gold lights and white, gold and black wallpaper. The entire place was truly visually stunning with an elegant, refined ambiance.  We were given complimentary white, red, orange and green crisps. The crunchy consistency and lightness of the crisps reminded me of Chinese shrimp chips without the shrimp flavor.I was tempted by the Tandoori Colorado Lamb Chops but decided to go with the tried and true choice of Delhi Ka Butter Chicken which came with garlic naan. I also had a Mango Lassi, which was thick, refreshing and sweet. The butter chicken came in a large porcelain white bowl and the sauce was bright orange in color. The chicken was incredibly juicy, succulent, tender and the sauce was wonderfully creamy and flavorful, complementing the meat perfectly. The garlic naan was warm, buttery, nice and fluffy but there wasn't a ton of garlic taste to it. One thing I wasn't a fan of was that rice didn't come with our meals. Basmati rice was an accompaniment and cost $5. I think this should have been included with any entree. My friend ordered the Saar Lamb Kebab which I found to be extremely flavorful but way too spicy for my tastes. I also tried the Saag Paneer which is spinach puree with fresh cheese and I wasn't that impressed. The spinach was too pureed and soggy for my liking, while the cheese was quite bland. Of course, I had to have dessert and selected the Kaju Kulfi, which consisted of Indian cashew ice cream, orange chocolate sauce, and chocolate crackle cookie. It was absolutely delightful. The cashew ice cream had that amazing cashew yumminess and was milky, fresh, velvety smooth and that chocolate sauce was so rich and heavenly. There wasn't much of an orange taste to it though. The crackle cookie was enjoyable - Slightly crispy, while still being moist and filled with chocolate goodness. From the moment we stepped in, the service was top notch throughout. The host allowed us to pick our seats and was understanding about half of our party running late and past the time of the reservation. Everything came out in a timely manner and the waiters made sure to check in on us, without being overbearing. There are a few other dishes I would like to try, but the prices are on the high side so it will be a while before I return.

The decor here surely makes you think of SE asia, malaysia, singapore. But the food doesn't quite meet up with it's forebearers. It's strange they have pad thai here even though its a malaysian place. The pad thai was quite too sweet for me. The hainese chicken was sparse and mostly bones rather than meat and you had to order the rice separately where they usually come together. The rice itself didn't even that usual chicken flavor. A bit pricey for the area as well. I wouldn't really recommend as i've had better.

Title: Festive Flavors and Mezcal Marvels at Maya on Upper East Side

Review:

Maya on the Upper East Side is currently my top destination for that festive Mexican culinary escape within the city. With its lively atmosphere and a touch of privacy in the front lounge, it’s perfect for both social gatherings and intimate conversations.

The space is always buzzing, yet you never feel cramped, thanks to the thoughtful layout providing plenty of space between tables. But what truly sets Maya apart is the impeccable service. The staff's attentiveness, coupled with their expert knowledge of the menu, makes every visit smooth and enjoyable. Birthdays here feel extra special with servers serenading the celebrant with a harmonious rendition of 'Happy Birthday.'

As a self-proclaimed mezcal connoisseur, I am continually impressed by Maya's selection of top-notch mezcal drinks, with mezcalitas that hit all the right notes for me. Not to be overlooked is the divine Tiramisu Martini, a must-try from their dessert menu.

The authentic Mexican flavors shine through in their food offerings. The guacamole is a must-have, served with perfectly thick chips. Whether you opt for the beautifully plated enchiladas or the sizzling mixed fajitas, you're in for a treat. The flan here is pure indulgence and wraps up the meal on a high note.

Maya’s weekend bottomless brunch is a crowd-pleaser, offering unlimited drinks and stellar brunch options up until 4:30 PM for a reasonable price—observing blissful patrons post-brunch as you arrive for dinner is a common sight.

For anyone craving authentic Mexican food, standout mezcal drinks, and a festive dining experience, Maya is undoubtedly the place to be.

I came here the other day for some Tuesday tacos (#tacoTuesday). They were introducing their new street tacos so I figured I'd give them a try. They are available in original (barbacoa), steak, carnitas, chicken and veggie. I wanted to try the veggie, but it wasn't available (that's been happening to me a lot unfortunately). I considered the chicken, but ended up with the barbacoa, "el bistec" and the carnitas. I also got chips and queso (switched it up from chips and guac) and a drink. All the tacos were good, but the barbacoa was my favorite. The steak was a little dry, but the carnitas were juicy and flavorful. The tacos were small, but had a decent amount of meat on them. Their chips are thick and crunch and the queso was good. Overall, I enjoyed the meal. There are better tacos in NYC, but for a fast, casual bite it was convenient and tasted good.

Title: A Hidden Japanese Gem in the Heart of New York

Discovering this delightful eatery was a stroke of luck, courtesy of a quick Yelp search. Seeking a palate change from the city's ubiquitous pizza offerings, my dining companion and I were thrilled to find this authentic Japanese spot. We ventured in on a quiet Monday evening, welcomed by the absence of a bustling crowd, which translated to a prompt serving of our dishes.

Opting for the grilled squid and two varied combo meals, we were impressed by both the quality and value. It's a rarity to encounter such genuine flavors at prices that do not break the bank, especially amidst the hustle of New York.

If your culinary journey has room for an affordable yet genuine Japanese experience, I can't recommend this place enough. It's a must-visit for anyone in the vicinity with a taste for something refreshingly different from the standard city fare.

Really good Sichuan food in midtown. The spicy fish was excellent - robust flavors, perfect spiciness level. I also really enjoyed the the stewed lamb and would recommend. Mapu Tofu was alright, not the best I've ever had, but good all things considered. Favorite was the spicy tripe dish (appetizer, cold). Service was very quick and good. Overall highly recommend this place.

Service at this gem is consistently exceptional, boasting the friendliest waitstaff I've encountered. While the wait time can be lengthy, I highly recommend making use of Yelp's waitlist to secure a spot. The brunch spread is irresistible, with standout dishes like the luscious blueberry pancakes, savory wild mushroom toast, and the perfectly executed nova benny. Despite a concise menu, each offering is a hit, making it a must-visit destination for any NYC itinerary.

I've gotten delivery from spice symphony a couple of times and enjoy the food. Although I'm not normally a fan of Indian food, I've liked the Stir Fried Hakka Noodles and Gobi Manchurian. I'd probably rate my experiences with the delivery a 4/5.However, my boyfriend gave this place a 5/5, an impossibly high rating for him. He had the Chicken Briyani which he thought was amazing even though it had cooled down from the delivery. That bumps the restaurant to a 4.5 between the two of us. Overall, I think the concept is unique for me as I've personally never tried Indo-Chinese food before. I'd be interested in going to the restaurant as the other reviews have shown that it's a pretty classy restaurant (also delivery is always just not as good). This also explains why this is on the pricier side of delivery food.

My boyfriend and I recently dined at this spot renowned for its New York-style pizza, and it didn't disappoint. As someone who's been away from NYC for some time, biting into their authentic pizza brought back a flood of memories and made our trip extraordinarily delightful. Both of us were thoroughly impressed, and it's safe to say that we've found our go-to place for a slice of the Big Apple when the craving hits. Highly recommend for a taste of NYC!

Title: Festive Ambiance, Underwhelming Cuisine

My recent visit to the restaurant offered a mixed bag of experiences. On the plus side, I was immediately taken with the delightful ambiance and excellent service. The establishment truly embraced the holiday spirit with beautiful decorations that added a festive touch.

Unfortunately, the cuisine didn't match up to the atmospheric charm. My pancakes arrived dry, and the croissant I shared was far from the culinary revelation I expected from a hyped establishment like this. Meanwhile, my dining companion had the braised beef hash; while she found it palatable, it wasn't a dish she'd return for - a sentiment that resonated with my overall impression.

Despite the good aspects, the food left us both unimpressed. I respect the place for its halal options, but that alone isn't enough to warrant a repeat visit. Sarabeth's, though aesthetically pleasing, ultimately feels just "okay" on the culinary front.

Title: A Spicy Delight at Han Dynasty

My fiancé and I, having seen the buzz about Han Dynasty on Yelp, decided to try it out for an early weekday lunch. Despite the non-peak hour, the place was bustling, hinting at its popularity. 

After contemplating the menu, we settled on the double-cooked pork belly and the dan dan noodles. The pork belly had a manageable spice level of 4/10, with generous meat portions although fewer vegetables than expected. The savory oil it bathed in added an extra layer of flavor. 

The dan dan noodles exceeded our spice expectations with a rating of 6/10 that felt more like an 8. Despite being light on meat, the noodles were bursting with flavor and had a pleasing firm texture, a welcome variation from the norm. 

Portion sizes were ideal for sharing. I'd certainly recommend Han Dynasty for anyone craving some scrumptious, spicy cuisine.

Title: A Fair 3.5 Stars for Wok Wok's Diverse Offerings

I'm torn between giving Wok Wok a solid 3 or a generous 4 stars due to its average yet affordable fare. The extensive menu, featuring Thai, Indonesian, Malaysian, Vietnamese, and Chinese cuisines, hints at a jack-of-all-trades approach, which usually doesn't excite my palate. 

My choice of Chicken Pad See Ew, scoring a decent 4 out of 5, was satisfactory without being remarkable. My dining companion's Chicken Thai Green Curry, also a 4, raised eyebrows by arriving suspiciously quick, a potential red flag for freshness, although it included a welcome side of rice.

A pleasant surprise was the free Thai Iced Tea we snagged by engaging with their Messenger code—a small but thoughtful touch.

While the service was swift and the price tag welcoming, both our dishes barely hitting the $9 mark, the restaurant's overall ambiance left something to be desired. Wok Wok falls prey to the usual bustling noise levels, and its basement location can be a bit elusive, despite the signage.

In conclusion, Wok Wok may not be my go-to spot given New York City's wealth of superior Thai cuisine options. It delivers a fair experience that is kind to your wallet, but for those in search of culinary excellence, the search continues.

Since I loved this food so much, I came back to order the same meal. However, I had a very different experience. The salad had an extreme amount of dressing - this is saying a lot since I'm the type of person who loves dressing, and especially this particular dressing. However, this tasted like over a cup of watered-down dressing. When I showed one of the servers behind the counter, she agreed that it was a lot but didn't seem concerned, so I asked her for a lid so I could attempt to drain out the dressing. She couldn't find a lid and seemed like she couldn't be bothered by my situation so I asked another server who found me an extra bowl. While both servers agreed that the salad did not look good, neither offered to help remedy the situation.I'm really disappointed in the poor food quality and bad customer service. I won't be returning any time soon and certainly won't be ordering the salad.

Could possibly be the best burger in NYC- it tastes very similar to the burger from 4 Charles. I was pleasantly surprised that the burger actually did live up to the hype. You must get the single cheeseburger (which comes with two patties) with the egg and bacon. The fries were not my favorite but they were good enough since I really only came for the burger anyway. Easy to get a reservation on Resy, but beware they will charge a cancellation fee if you want to cancel a few hours before the day of.

One of my  all tIme favorite restaurants. Went there with a bunch of my Life long friends.  The atmosphere was fun and lively even for a Thursday night.  Not as busy at the bar as I remember. Here is the food rundown. 1) baked clams.  Best ever 2) Spadenni  alla Romano. Skip it3). Raw clams. Pretty good 4) shrimp Fra Diablo.  Get it. So good 5) beef tenderloin. Thursday special. Delicious   But I bit undercooked 6) Escarole. Get it. Delicious 7) chicken parmigiana    Good. Portion was lacking 8) penna alla VodKa. Good 9) bread pudding.  I remember it being better10) cocktails were good. All in all great food.  Service was a bit slow and the chicken parm portion is why I am giving a 4 star.

I came here for a friend's birthday on a Saturday evening in January, and absolutely loved the fireplace! I've been here in the summer, but honestly I prefer it in the winter. The restaurant is larger than I thought it was, and our party of 13 comfortably fit at a long table facing the fireplace. We had great servers who filled our glasses/cleared dishes regularly. I had a Gin Gin Mule (delicious) and the Shrimp Linguini. Although the linguini was so good, it was dripping with olive oil which made it super tricky to eat. The time between ordering and dishes being delivered wasn't too bad, although we waited a while between dishes being cleared and dessert. For our friend's birthday, we got her a chocolate lava cake and ice cream, and the cake was soooo good. Would def recommend coming here esp during winter--I can see it being a cute date night spot as well!

Tucked away as a charming lunch hideaway, this spot boasts a menu of four distinct ramen options alongside a selection of Japanese fare. While the soup's robust and rich flavor is commendable, the ramen disappoints with its sparse toppings. My spicy ramen, at nearly $15, came with a solitary slice of chashu, scant ground pork, and bamboo shoots—a portion not commensurate with its price. The takoyaki appetizer, though a traditional treat, was let down by minimal octopus filling and an overly dominant sauce, with a messy topping of finely shredded squid.

Be prepared to handle cash, as no cards are accepted; although an ATM is provided for convenience. And for those seeking online connectivity, it's worth noting the absence of Wi-Fi, which could be a drawback for tech-savvy diners. Overall, while the flavors have potential, the value proposition may leave you considering other options.

This place was pretty empty although the restaurant was at a good location. The waiters didnt seem to care much. They were nice and didnt give attitude but had no motivation. When ready to order, two waiters just kept talking to each other until they realize we were eyeing them and waved. We chose the pre-fixed salmon dinner set.  Price was worth it for a miso soup, salad, rice, sushi, salmon sushi and the whole salmon with few pieces of broccoli and carrots. Very fulling for $23. However, food was average. Dessert a red bean paste Japanese pancake that you can buy at any Japanese supermarkets. Even after sitting for around two hours there were still very minimum amount of customers. Location is in the heart of St. Marks which is a good location. But food, atmosphere and customer service needs more work. Overall, wont be back.

Title: A Seafood Delight in the Heart of the Big Apple

I recently joined a friend for a girls' night out at a spot she recommended, and I must confess, I was skeptical at first. As a die-hard seafood lover with Southern roots, the idea of a "crab boil" in New York City initially made me want to roll my eyes. However, my preconceptions were quickly shattered.

The crab boil was nothing short of spectacular. Though time has passed since that night and some details have faded, the memory of the succulent crab and the divine sauce remains vivid in my mind. The sauce was so remarkable that after devouring the seafood, we couldn't help but lick the bag and spoon up the remaining sauce—it was that irresistible.

The experience was so enjoyable that I have already penciled in my next visit. Moreover, the warm ambiance and friendly vibes turned a table for two into a merry gathering of four by the end of the evening. In short, the place exceeded all expectations, marrying Southern flavors with New York flair perfectly.

This place is #tdf the chicken parm was omfg amazeballs. The service was equally as amazing as the food which is saying a lot. If you're anywhere near this quaint little spot do yo self a favor and swing by. The pricing is way to low for the quality and quantity of food they have here. The beer and wine selection is small but the items they have are pretty good. The meatballs were unbelievable, easily the best meatballs I've ever had in my life and I've had plenty of meatballs in my time. This place will easily become my go to place for anything parm, chicken, eggplant, whatever. I think it's that damn red sauce it's just way to f'ing delicious. Thank you to the staff and owners for creating the can't miss spot in all of New York.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Comforting Hot Pot in Gramercy

Having spent many evenings in the cozy confines of this quaint Gramercy eatery, it's with fond memories that I reflect on the delicious comfort food they serve up. Admittedly, the place isn't the easiest to spot, and you might find yourself waiting for a seat due to the limited space.

Despite that, the wait is worth it. Their hot pot and noodles are not only affordable but are some of the most satisfying dishes in the area. The star of the show is undoubtedly their Little Hot Pot – a personal-sized cauldron brimming with glass noodles, fresh veggies, succulent meat, and silky tofu skin, all swimming in a mouthwatering broth. It's the kind of dish that warms you from the inside out, perfect for those chilly days or when you're in need of some gastronomic TLC.

Overall, whether you're dining in or taking out, this spot is my top recommendation for anyone craving a hot, soupy treat that promises to fill you up without emptying your wallet.

Title: A Decent Ethiopian Experience in Harlem

I recently visited an Ethiopian restaurant in Harlem in an effort to widen my culinary experiences. The restaurant offered a decent meal that was more than satisfactory for two people. Unlike past outings to similar eateries, I left feeling content without the need for supplemental food, like an extra slice of pizza.

While their wine list isn't extensive, they do feature a selection of Ethiopian wines. The service was notably efficient, with our server displaying commendable patience and helpfulness as we navigated the menu's offerings.

As someone who isn't an aficionado of Ethiopian cuisine, I found this to be a good opportunity to explore and learn. The pricing was fair, aligning with the quality of the food and overall experience. While the dishes didn't quite dazzle, they were enjoyable enough, especially for those already in the Harlem area. If you're nearby and in the mood for Ethiopian fare, this restaurant is worth considering.

I recently tried takeout from Amura and had a mixed experience. The service was prompt with my order ready in just 30 minutes after placing it at noon. Priced at $14.96, the chicken teriyaki bento box came with a salad and miso soup, providing a generous portion of food. However, the overall quality was average; neither the bento box itself, the salad, nor the miso soup stood out as exceptional. The highlight was the sushi included in the bento, which suggested that there might be something special there, though with only four pieces, it left me wanting more. Next time, I think I'll focus on their sushi offerings.

I recently dined at a local eatery where the culinary experience was nothing short of delightful. The wraps on the menu stood out, offering both delectable flavors and affordability that is hard to beat. Adding to the treat, the spinach pies proved to be a must-try – they truly live up to the hype. Despite the bustling crowd, the atmosphere maintained a warm and comforting vibe, making the overall dining experience highly enjoyable. Highly recommend for a satisfying meal!

Title: An Appetizing Experience at a Must-Visit Dinner Destination

If you're looking for an evening culinary adventure, be sure to make a reservation at this dinner-exclusive hotspot that flings open its doors at 6pm sharp. The menu might be appetizer-centric, but it's a whirlwind of flavors waiting to be discovered.

The Fried Chicken, with its unique mochi flour batter, is an absolute triumph and comes highly recommended. Pair that with the Jang-jo-rim – the accompanying buttered rice and mushroom slices make for a delightful, if not essential, choice.

However, the real star is the Oiji Bowl, a concoction of seaweed rice harmoniously blended with the creaminess of uni and shrimp, creating an addiction you'll happily surrender to.

While the Ssam Platter could be tempting, it's a dish you can skip unless you're a fan of fiery pork.

And do leave room for the Honey Butter Chips – a delectable dessert that'll have you savoring the intricate dance of butter, spice, and the sweet chill of ice cream.

The dining experience is further elevated by the stellar customer service. Attentive and efficient, the staff ensures you'll never see the bottom of your water glass or have to navigate a cluttered table.

In short, this eatery is a shining beacon for those who love to indulge in small plates with big flavors, complemented by service that's second to none.

I recently visited a delightful restaurant located conveniently near Museum Mile which offered a wonderful ambience, perfect for lovers of Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisine. The staff were incredibly welcoming and attentive, contributing to the warm atmosphere. The food was nothing short of excellent, boasting authentic flavors and a delectable variety. I highly recommend this establishment to anyone looking for a great dining experience in that area.

Favorite place for pho in Manhattan! Both the Bun Bo Hue and the Madame Pho were extremely tasty and flavorful. The broth of the Bun Bo Hue tasted more balanced, while the Madame Pho broth was a bit too strong on the spices (at least, subjectively) and I couldn't really taste as much of the beefy bone marrow base as I would have liked. Because of that, the pho broth felt a bit flat to me, but it was still loads better than the other pho spots I've tasted in NYC. The meat quality was top-notch, especially the brisket! I'll definitely be returning, or at least ordering for delivery whenever a pho craving hits.

Title: A Flavor-Packed Journey at Xi'an Famous Foods

Living up to its reputation, Xi'an Famous Foods in NYC was a must-visit for us, and it didn't disappoint. Bracing a brief line, we dove into the no-frills self-service format that's all about the eating. The spicy cumin lamb noodles (N2) were my adventure—a generous portion exploding with bold flavors, the hand-pulled noodles perfectly capturing the chili oil and cumin lamb. On the other side of the table, the beef noodle soup offered a milder but equally satisfying warmth. The experience was hearty to the point of indulgent, leaving us in a contented food coma. If authenticity is what you seek in your noodles, Xi'an Famous Foods is your haven.

We stumbled upon this charming restaurant while passing by and were instantly drawn in by its inviting and cozy ambiance. The atmosphere was lovely, and we found ourselves relaxing as soon as we sat down. To our delight, the margaritas and wine selection were fantastic, each sip better than the last. What truly set this place apart was the spectacular service; attentive, personable, and genuinely caring staff made our experience memorable. This "super cute and amazing" spot is a hidden gem that we were lucky to discover. Highly recommend for a delightful dining experience!

Title: A Tale of Two Textures at Crepe Corner

My dining experience at Crepe Corner began on a high note with a delightful made-to-order egg crepe with scallions, airy and light, setting the bar for what I hoped would be an exceptional meal. However, the subsequent choice to "authentically" enhance this dish with fried dough resulted in a heavy-handed affair. Despite adding texture, this inclusion overpowered the crepe's finesse, turning it dense and drastically altering the overall taste experience. A salty, indistinct presence of pork further complicated the dish, overshadowing the crepe rather than complementing it.

While the portions were generous and the pricing reasonable, the combination proved less than harmonious, sacrificing the crepe's initial charm. Indeed, it provided a filling meal but at the cost of sitting uncomfortably heavy afterward.

In recognition of the value, authenticity, and efficient service, I extend a moderate three-star rating to Crepe Corner. Yet, unless pressed by hunger, I'm unlikely to revisit this particular dish.

Oh my yummy! I was craving Cuban food and this place did not disappoint. I ordered the tostones relleno and the empanadas and both were yummy! I tried to take a photo, but it was too dark in there and the photos didn't turn out. Or maybe my eyes just couldn't focus after enjoying the coconut mojito. They had a lively salsa band playing last night (Friday) which made the atmosphere really festive. Great service too!

I ended up meeting a friend here after work, Drinks tried the Banana Jameson not bad light on the Banana taste also tried the Sangria not sure what they game me but it didn't taste like sangria at all it was ahh. Appetizers gave the Rice balls a try not bad decent taste, also tried the Italian eggs rolls they were very good. Food I had the Shrimp Tacos these were decent nice tasting grilled shrimp. Friend had the Western flat bread good with lots of cheese & some short rib pretty good. Decent looking place, nice music playing & a good amount of TV's to catch any sports game.  Service wise they can really use some improvement, when we arrived no one to sit us we had to go looking for someone finally grabbed a bus boy... after being seated our waitress was hard to get the other that helped was better, they brought out the wrong flat bead twice?! So either the person in the back or the guy bringing it out wasn't paying attention I don't know what was going on back there. Checking in gets u a free infusion drink double check your receipt they initially charged us for it.. pretty annoying had to get it removed. Looking at previous reviews for sure all those 5 star very short reviews are from fake accounts this place is ok nothing near a 5 star rating trust me!

Title: A Quiet Saturday Brunch with Hits and Misses

I popped into this spot for a Saturday lunch at 12:30 PM, expecting the usual bustle but found it oddly serene with only two other tables occupied. Surprisingly, they served a brunch menu exclusively, though it was thoughtfully peppered with lunch items, catering to a wider range of tastes.

The expansive dining area gave the impression it could host a lively crowd, making the emptiness all the more noticeable. Service was consolidated in the hands of a multitasking waiter who doubled as a bartender, his jovial demeanor inviting a light-hearted quip about whether he was the solitary chef as well.

A support team of two runners helped maintain the flow, contributing to the overall friendly atmosphere. I chose the nicoise salad, which, while a decent attempt, fell short of authentic. The tuna, however, redeemed the dish with its robust seasoning. My companion opted for the linguini gamberi, which featured a mix of shrimp and arugula—a satisfying if unremarkable choice.

In essence, the food at this establishment is competent without being remarkable. The spacious tables hint at an ability to host larger gatherings, which might bring more life to the environment. While the food won’t transport you to culinary nirvana, it’s a fine option if you're seeking an uncluttered space for a casual meal.

I tried the spicy beef and spicy chicken jerky from here. Quarter pound will give you three slices (approx). Both were really good and flavorful. May be I liked the beef version tiny bit more. I couldn't stop eating and finished the whole thing in a single sitting. This is the absolute best jerky in my life. Even if it said spicy, it was just flavorful without being much spicy.

So amazing and definitely worth coming here. We ordered the following:-beef carpaccio: this was amazing. Such great flavors-homemade ricotta special: the apricot jam that came with this was amazing and the crackers were great. I would definitely recommend this-spinach gnudi: this was a special of the night, but i was hoping that the pasta would be a little bit lighter and less dense -spaghetti with garlic, Parmesan and chilies: this was amazing and my favorite pasta dish-Garganelli with mushroom ragu: the ragu was great but the pasta was a little too al dente -rocky road sundae: this was amazing! I would definitely recommend.Overall, this was an amazing restaurant

Sometimes the simpler things are better. This is an Italian restaurant with all the basics and essentials of Italian cuisine: antipasti, pizza, pasta, some fish and meat. I didn't find anything out of the ordinary but everything was well prepared. I noticed that the menu tries to incorporate some touches of novel cuisine, like the olive oil with capers and lentils. The ñoqui and the pizza were good but the sea bass was excellent. Overall a solid 3 stars, rising 4 stars. I would improve the pizza crust because I like it crunchy, but that is simply my preference.

I've been coming to Pylos for a few years now and I can confidently say they offer the best Greek food in NYC. Not only is the interior beautiful and charming, the food is ALWAYS solid.  Great for date nights, group dinners, and business meetings. I have compiled a list of recommended dished down below along with prices. Recommendations:-Greek salad $19 (Fresh feta, tomatoes, cucumbers, and capers)-Octopus $22 (Grilled to perfection served with balsamic reduction sauce)-Pork Shank $30 (Braised with lemon and herbs)-Beet Salad $14 (Simple but glorious)KEEP IN MIND*No beer or hard liqour. (Red, white, and sparkling wine available)*Street parking available right across the street.

I've visited this restaurant on a few occasions and have been consistently impressed. The ambiance is undeniably classy with plenty of space to relax. Staff members, such as Conner the bartender and hostesses Chelsey and Wendy, are a delight—always friendly and attentive. It's also a great spot for sports enthusiasts, boasting a large TV ideal for game-watching. As for the food, the "Chicken dinner," which pairs grilled chicken with mashed potatoes, is deceptively simple yet downright delicious. Highly recommend for a cozy dine-in experience.

Title: A Spicy Delight at Dalongyi Hot Pot's New York Outpost

As a first-timer to Dalongyi's expansive hot pot empire, I was excited to dive into the sizzling experience at their latest New York location. Joined by a group eager to sample a broad spectrum of offerings, we indulged in a trio of soup bases: the medium spicy, the soothing tomato, and the clear mushroom. Our table was a cornucopia of meats and accompaniments, including succulent fatty beef, tripe, scallops, and enoki mushrooms, among others.

The standout for me was the shrimp paste—paired exquisitely with the medium spicy broth, where the heat was potent yet bearable for those with a penchant for spice. However, if your palate leans away from fiery flavors, the tomato and mushroom broths provide a delectable alternative.

One noticeable void was the absence of a sauce bar—a staple in many hot pot restaurants. Surprisingly, this did not detract from the meal, as the provided garlic, cilantro, and oil complemented the robust Sichuan spices harmoniously, preserving the authentic hot pot ritual with a no-frills approach to seasonings.

The service was commendable, with attentive wait staff ensuring a seamless flow of food and beverages—the soothing coconut milk and soymilk came highly recommended to temper the spicy broth and refresh the palate.

In conclusion, Dalongyi delivers an authentic Sichuan hot pot experience that's worth revisiting. The quality of meats and fair pricing only amplify the appeal. This hot pot haven is a fiery gem that warmly welcomes both the spice enthusiast and those seeking a taste of Sichuan tradition.

After all the shopping and looking at the vessel, stop at this trendy and truly great place. Stopped here for an impromptu drink and stayed for edamame. Very tasty cocktails and very nice menu as well. The staff are helpful and they have great decor. Definitely a fun place! Bring a date!

Many of my friends have recommended Her Name is Han for Korean food but the long wait always prevented me from actually eating at this restaurant.  Luckily, last Friday, my boyfriend and I were able to snag a seat without waiting at 6:00pm!  I know it's an early dinner, but I'm glad we got there early because 30 minutes later I heard the hostess quote another patron an 1.5 hr wait! The decor in this restaurant was on point. It gave off a rustic library midcentury vibe.  There were little details that made the restaurant unique, like the cute porcelain plates with their house logo and the barn-style aprons the servers wore.  The food was delicious.  We ordered the army based soup and braised pork to shared. The army based soup comes with rice and inside there was 3-4 different types of sausage/ham, beans, cheese, ramen and the softest rice cake you'll ever have in your life! The braised pork came with two sauces one was a jam which was actually super tasty with the pork.  It also came with a different type of kimchi than the side dish one we were served. The service was great, we were having our water refilled constantly and the servers named the dishes and what was being served to us (which typically doesn't happen at Korean restaurants so that was nice). Highly recommend this restaurant if you are looking for something in K-Town! Her Name is Han is also under the same hospitality group of other Korean restaurants in the city like Take31 (right next door) and Nonono. Can't wait to try the other restaurants and come back here!

We were invited here by management. Which was fortuitous because I can't say we'd ever be in this area for any other reason. And even if we were I'm almost certain we would've looked past this restaurant as I almost did even though I was standing right in front of it. But don't make the same mistake we would've made!I think we probably disagree with other reviewers. Sure, the dry hot pot is delicious, and the restaurant concept pretty damn novel for NYC. But where we thought the food really shined was in all of the non-dry hot pot dishes. I mean we had a fish noodle soup and a pork noodle dish that were absolutely out of this world. We were shocked. We've paid much more money for much worse food at way more famous places.Anywho, the dry hot pot is also very good, if not one-note (that Szechuan pepper oil taste can only get you so far- wish they'd take some liberties and try some other flavors, even if outside of traditional, authentic tastes). And also, we were totally confused at to what to do because they have this hybrid, DIY concept combined with table service which doesn't work and requires an adjustment (just go to table service and forget the DIY, price/pound, buffet thing- it's confusing and unnecessary).But all is forgiven when I get hot, fresh, exquisite Chinese regional cuisine that greatly exceeds all possible expectations. Don't miss it!

Hands down best burger I've ever had in NYC. And I have had some great ones. There's really not much else to add other than make sure you order the burger with bacon and a fried egg and fries of course. As far as other things go, service was great and so were our drinks - we tied a few different beers and the Old Fashioned. Also, we dined here a few weeks ago on a Sunday and arrived a little before 6:00pm and we didn't have to wait! I don't know if this was an off night or if the early bird special on a Sunday is the play? So, come here, eat until you're about to explode and then go home and lay on the couch. Wait or no wait, this place is worth it.

Come Prima Ristorante is in a modern space that could be in Milan or Rome. Sadly the food does not live up to the slick atmosphere or what one would expect from a high end Italian restaurant in either Italy or New York. The food looks quite good, almost picture perfect. Unfortunately the taste does not match the promise of the looks. The pasta we had was also over cooked. The wine selection is good and the service is spotty. With a little attention to detail and more flavorful food, Come Prima Ristorante could be my go to spot on the UES. I hope they can get there, but they will need to try harder to do it. I wish them luck.

Tucked away in the heart of NYC, this gem of a restaurant offers a delightful throwback to old-school elegance, creating a charmingly upscale scene. While the space buzzes with the typical Friday night crowd, the live music sets a vibrant atmosphere, complemented by an excellent selection of wine and attentive service.

Dress to impress is the unofficial code here, and it's well worth it. A tip for those seeking the crème de la crème of experiences—Tuesday nights are where the magic truly happens. With a top-notch show that's the talk of the town, it's a must-see that you have to witness firsthand.

However, the experience is slightly marred by the less-than-stellar bar staff, who came across as rude and not as prompt as one would expect from such a venue. This minor hiccup necessitated the removal of one star from an otherwise stellar review.

There's not a lot of Korean restaurants nearby, and it was only recently that I came across Momo 97 on Doordash. I ordered from here twice and both experiences were great! I tried their Spicy Pork Bowl, Teriyaki Chicken Bowl, and Scallion Pancake. The bowls are roughly $12 and scallion pancake is $8. They give you plenty of meat and are not stingy about it. Good portions, affordable prices, delicious meat flavors. I will definitely order from here again!

Owned by Morimoto a casual ramen place. The food is pretty good. It can get crowded and if you can lunch is a good time to go. The ramen is good nice broth, good char siu and perfectly cooked soft boiled egg. The appertizers are good too. My favorites are the peking duck tacos, crispy minga and kakuni bao. The one thing I do not recommend is the gyukotsu ramen which is the 7 hour braised beef brisket. The brisket is tough and stringy. The broth and brisket tasted just like a $7 brisket noodle soup in Chinatown but at momosan it will set you back $25 and is not worth it.

I stopped in here for lunch after reading YELP reviews & the fact that it was a 5 minute walk from my conference hotel. I sat at the bar & had a glass of Pinot Grigio and ordered the goat cheese croquettes and charred octopus. The croquettes were 3 small ones with goat cheese & hazelnut inside and topped with guava. So yummy! But oh man, if you dig octopus the Charred Octopus with potato confit & chimichurri was out of this world. Hands down THE best octopus dish I've ever had. The combination of flavors was divine. So glad I stopped in!

Title: A Festive Feast with a Side of Confusion at Local Chinese Favorite

I ventured into familiar territory this Christmas night, having booked a table for nine at a well-loved spot where I've joyfully indulged in many a dim sum brunch. Unlike the bustling daytime ambience, the dinner scene here was noticeably calmer, the stillness punctuated by the savory scents of Chinese banquet classics wafting from the kitchen.

While the food remained a delectable highlight—particularly the deep fried pork chop with Peking sauce, which managed to maintain its crispiness beneath a generous helping of sweet and sour glaze—the service struck a dissonant chord. Despite conversing fluently in Mandarin, there seemed to be an inexplicable disconnect with the wait staff, as if we were lost in translation without moving an inch.

Further adding to the evening's oddities was the early last call for orders at 7:45PM, casting a shadow of doubt on their usual 10PM closing time. It was a puzzling decision on a night when the usual reasons for early closure (such as Christmas) presumably held little sway.

Nonetheless, the flavors of the Peking duck, crispy chicken, and other mouthwatering dishes were undeniable triumphs. The sumptuous spread, from the jumbo shrimp with walnut and mayonnaise to the spicy tang of ma po tofu, mirrored a traditional feast that could easily grace any celebratory table.

In conclusion, despite some service hiccups and odd timing protocols, the dinner was a success thanks to the culinary prowess on display. But for a seamless experience, you might want to clarify dining details ahead of time, especially if you plan to visit on a holiday.
Inase is my usual go to sushi place since it's so close to my apartment. The staff are very friendly and the sushi is solid.

We could not say enough good things about this Italian gem in Manhattan. It was so good we went two nights in a row. First - the food (particularly the pasta) is to die for. Fresh pasta with a variety of sauces obviously prepared with love and attention makes for a delicious and overly indulgent dinner. The wine list is superb and are the salads - I had arugula with Parmesan and my husband had the caprese (not only did we go to nights in a row, we ordered the same things both nights). Now - for the service. It matches the food - impeccable and perfect. The Italian charm and authenticity were not missed on us. Our tables each night were set in cute little corners so we could sit close and talk without having to raise our voices. The setting is romantic without being stuffy. Last - it's still NY so not cheap, but you will get bang for your buck here. Dinner for two will not be over-the-top expensive in the way that you wonder which assets you must sell to pay for your meal. One more thing - I left my credit card there and they had it for me. I always appreciate honesty and integrity. I highly recommend this place. I hope you enjoy it as much as we did.

Great burger place. Not sure why the yelp rating is so low. They have solid burgers that hit the spot. I ordered a cold brew coffee (non alcoholic) as I waited for my friend to arrive. I came around 12PM on a Saturday and the place wasn't crowded at all. Most of the people that were there seemed to be eating brunch.I ordered the California burger with sauce on the side. I should have put the onions on the side as well because they were STRONG.By "no modifications" to the signature burgers, they mean that you can replace things and take things out - but you can't add anything.My friend ordered the WTF which he seemed to really enjoy, it came with fries which I stole quite a few ofOverall, the people here are nice and service is speedy. Bathrooms are pretty clean too - although a bit dark. Sometimes you just really crave a burger and Mel's really hits the spot!

I've been to several other K-BBQ places back in Maryland including an AYCE location called Iron Age, but it had been awhile, so it was time to give this a try again.This location is located on either the second or third floor via an elevator.  We did not check out the karaoke bar further up as our wait was no more than 15 minutes. Was surprised considering the reviews on here.The meal for two was around the $140 mark using the pre-built large beef platter, some soju and a seafood cake.  The 3 meats were basically skirt steak, chuck, and short rib.  All looked like quality meat.  I would agree with others that it would have been nice to have multiple meat sources in a platter, but whatever.  The platter came with a bunch of random sauces (and salt) and sides.  The one I liked the most was the spicy soup. Super good flavor.  The egg dish was sorta meh.  With regard to the bottle of plain soju. Don't do it. Get a flavor, lol.Service was generally good. One guy was super brief, but the others were cool. Overall, the food was good, but I rather have what I had back in Maryland, especially for the price. I don't think its necessarily a bad place to go if you've never had this kind of food before.

Lovely bar and restaurant. We used a Pulsd voucher and our waitress was very attentive. Anytime our glasses got a past halfway empty, she was very prompt on refilling them. The food was tasty and the air conditioning was perfect for a hot summer day.

My son said we ate here years ago and he remembered it being a real treat. It definitely was!!  If you do a Yelp check in you get a free empanada with an order of an entree!  We got a few appetizers to go with our entrees and they were awesome!! One was like a cheese fondue and the the other was like a ceviche. For the entree I got a vegetable casserole that looked like lasagna but was filled with vegetables and so many awesome flavors. One person in our group got the appetizer combo for her meal and it was so much food she couldn't eat it all. It was my birthday so they sang to me and gave me some flan with whipped cream that was amazing!!We didn't have to wait and it was a Friday night. Our waitress was awesome!

Found another awesome Peruvian food joint & I'm so glad I did. Came across this place in the city & it sure hit the spot  The service was amazing as well as the food. Then I learned they have a few more locations in queens that at right by me! I'll be sure to check them out as well the next time I'm craving me some Peruvian!I got the Shrimp & Chicken Pineapple Fried Rice which is Fried rice with chicken & shrimp served in a pineapple & my husband got the Bistek a Lo Pobre which is Steak served on top of fries, sweet plantains, hot dog with a side of rice, beans and fried egg..This one order comes with so much food, you just don't know where to start. But the best part is you get to try a good selection of their food & it all tastes so good! Everything was flavorful & made to perfection! Love their food!.Jose the manger was amazing! He was attentive & friendly which made our experience even more enjoyable!

I came to celebrate my daughter's birthday. She did her research and decided to come here. I must say I was pleasantly surprised. The food was very good. Our server was excellent.  Attentive and friendly. He checked in on us constantly.  And kept the water flowing.  The only hiccup was, it was hot in the restaurant.  The AC could have been on slightly stronger.But the desserts are also to die for.I definitely recommend.

Having just revisited what I confidently declare the purveyor of NYC's best pizza, I remain impressed. The standout was, without a doubt, the Nonna Maria pizza—a choice you simply cannot go wrong with. An unexpected delight was meeting Greg, whose kindness matched the eatery's charm, as he generously shared local visit-worthy spots. A must-visit for any pizza aficionado in the city.

I wanted to give this 4.5 stars, the food was excellent, and the service was friendly, but it wasn't quite at the 5 star, mind blowing, "every detail perfect" level.Seating is a little tight in the space, and the restaurant was exceedingly dim. We had use the votive candles at our table just to read the menu. Muddler Cocktail: vodka, lime juice, prosecco, with muddled basil, mint and strawberries - my kinda cocktail, sweet and fruity without the astringent alcohol bite of a poorly made cocktail, deceptively mild tasting as it creeps up on you through the night.Before your appetizer comes, complimentary bread baskets with 3 spreads to accompany: rosemary, red pepper, and basil(?).
