I usually try not to go overboard with bread, but the warm bread dipped in that spread trio was irresistible, we all overindulged with zero regrets.Grandma's Lamb Specialty: lamb meatballs in a fresh rosemary, lemon and white wine sauce with mushroom polenta crostini - tender and gamey (in a good way) - I was a huge fan of theseGrandma's Beef Specialty: traditional Italian meatballs in a san marzano tomato sauce, topped with fresh ricotta - really, you can't go wrong with any of the meatball appetizers, our table was polarized debating whether the lamb or beef was better.Octopus and the Potato: grilled Portuguese octopus served with potatoes, black gaeta and green castelvetrano olives, celery and red pepper flakes - perfect texture, not a bit soggy or overly chewy (we didn't fight over this since we had an order for every 2 people)Rolling with the Eggplant: sliced eggplant fried in egg batter, rolled and stuffed with seasoned spinach, ricotta and mascarpone cheese topped with melted mozzarella and tomato sauce - it's fried and covered in cheese, so it tastes delicious, but you can pretend it's healthy since it's eggplantItalian Cheesemonger: parmiggiano reggiano, black truffle pecorino, pecorino toscano, creamy dolcelatte gorgonzola, truffle honey and walnutes - I never turn down a cheese plate, and especially not when there's parmiggiano and honey. There is no more perfect pairing than honey and cheese!Truffled Moneybag: ricotta filled beggar's purse shaped pasta, white truffle infused cream sauce - we knew this would be too rich as an entree, so we ordered two for the table. Decadent and rich, we may or may not have cleaned the sauce off the plate with everything we could reach.Wide Road for the Wild Swine: house-made pappardelle with braised wild boar, red wine, juniper berries, fresh herbs - wide ribbons of pasta in wine sauce? yes, please and thank you!Little Ears of Apulia: orecchiette pasta with italian sweet sausage, broccoli rabe, toasted bread crumbs, fennel pollen - despite already having pasta on carbs on pasta, I decided to order a pasta for an entree, and this is everything, all my favorites in one dish. Orecchiette are perfect tiny bowls to hold in sauce and bits of sausage and bread crumbs and I adored this dish so much that I ate way past my waistline's comfort level, thank goodness for loose flowy tops.We ordered desserts but they didn't really register, through no fault of the desserts - we were simply halfway into our carb comas by the time dessert was served. I do vaguely remember a delightfully creamy coffee tiramisu and a refreshing lemon sorbet served in a frozen lemon shell. If you're in the mood for cheese and carbs, you can't go wrong with this intimate little spot, though the next time I visit, I'll prep by wearing a muumuu.

Title: A One-Time Brunch Experience at Jack's Wife Freda

Upon joining the city's brunch scene, I took note of Jack's Wife Freda, a name recurring on numerous "best brunch" lists. The restaurant offers a bustling ambiance typical of NYC's coveted spots, which unfortunately translates into cramped seating and substantial wait times.

The menu is a blend of Middle Eastern classics—think shakshuka and an inventive eggs benedict atop latkes. The side offerings, such as unique cantaloupe juice and duck bacon, add a twist to the experience. However, despite the allure of these dishes, the portion sizes don't quite match up to the price tags.

In conclusion, Jack's Wife Freda is worth a single visit, particularly if you're introducing out-of-towners to New York's brunch culture. Just brace yourself for the wait and a relatively light plate.

Where can I begin with this?!What a lovely place! I gathered here with a few of my friends to play some girlfriends check up night. Everything was great from top to bottom! I apologize for not remembering my waitresses name(we were there on July 9, approx 9pm) but she was the coolest chillest most helpfullest(I know that's not a real word just humor me!), she was everything! Kudos to great service! She convinced me to try the YELP check in bacon wrapped cherry tomato with chipotle aioli and it was absolutely delicious! I don't want to issue spoilers but just try it if you're curious, a pleasant surprise! So let me get to the FOOD!Omg omg omg the chicken and challah was to die for! Chicken was seasoned perfectly and it came with a homemade tomato buffalo sauce actually I don't remember what it really was but it tasted excellent -their version of chicken and waffles, I was stuffed! I also sampled my friends truffled grilled cheese and I want to get that if I visit again! I also tasted the blackened fish with the roast potatoes and that was excellent as well!The vibe of this place is cool, kinda small, I can see that it can become a bit crowded. Had some cool music and spacey vibe, I think there was graffiti on the walls which I completely admire.We were all pretty satisfied with our experience and wouldn't hesitate to come here again Enjoy!

I've walked by this place many times, always wanting to try, and I'm glad I finally did!Its definitely a little pricey, a few $ more than other places. But the food was great. Inside is semi fancy atmosphere. There are a few tables outside along the sidewalk (with heaters when cold) and plenty of seating inside. We went on a Thursday night at 7pm and there was no wait or any issues. One thing I didn't like, was that our waiter didn't read us any of the specials, but read all of the specials to the couple that sat right behind us. Why didn't we get to hear them?They start you off with some bread sticks and bread. We ordered a glass of wine each, tuna tartare app, green salad, SPAGHETTINI NERI AI FRUTTI MARE (black spaghettini with mixed seafood and spicy tomato sauce), and a spaghetti that had lobster and crab meat in it in a pink sauce. I don't see it on the menu now online. They were really nice to split the two apps on two plates for us since they knew we were sharing it. The black spaghetti was delish and had heaping amounts of seafood in it... including perfectly cooked scallops. The lobster pasta was good too but I liked mine more. Also the pasta was homemade and was great!Wine was a good pour too. Will definitely go back.

This was a nice introduction to seafood for my friend that hadn't had very much of it before. We got the white fish, calamari, and seafood sampler. I liked that there were both hot and cold options for a lot of things and a good variety of oysters to choose from. However, I felt that they thought their reputation preceded them and acted a little pretentiously towards me and my friend.

In honest opinion, this place deserves more than 3.5 stars. I did not read any of the other reviews but i am here to speak on my behalf. My family and i came here and i was a little skeptical bc of the ratings but my boyfriends brother wanted Peking duck in nyc so bad. So i had this place marked to go to. I must say that it is indeed a little expensive for some Peking duck, not sure what average price is but it was $60 here. We ordered two. Our ducks came out and we had the chef carve the duck on a side table so there would be no bones or anything. Just skin and meat. It was served with these things that looked like crepe versions of the banh Bao breading, hoisin sauce/dip, scallions and cucumbers. The duck was so delicious, perfect flavoring! Usually when i have had Peking duck, they always just leave the bones so while im eating I have to watch out for the bones too. It was delicious to try but i do not know if I'll be back to pay that price for $60 Peking duck and $10 beers. Our total bill was about $180, so be prepared to spend!

We recently had lunch at this charming old-fashioned soda shop/diner that may seem unassuming at first glance, but is absolutely worth a visit. The highlight was unequivocally the sodas—they're crafted with an authentic blend of soda water and syrup, resulting in the best soda experience imaginable. The food portions were generous with standard diner fare like burgers, complemented by air-fried fries and onion rings that were delightfully less greasy than usual. If you find yourself nearby, do yourself a favor and drop in for an incredibly refreshing soda.
I love Ruby's! The bronte burger and shrimp pasta is a must. I always bring my friends from out of town here.

Title: A Midnight Delight with Noodles Galore!

Review:

Stumbling upon this gem at midnight was a pleasant surprise! The concept is straightforward and satisfying: start with a base of noodles, rice, or veggies, then mix in your chosen proteins and vegetables, and finally top it off with a sauce of your liking.

I opted for egg noodles paired with succulent salmon and fresh bok choy, all brought together with a flavorful Bangkok sauce. The dish was exceptional, bursting with taste in every mouthful. Portion sizes were generous, to say the least – so much so that I regretfully couldn't finish it all, especially with a flight looming the next morning. If only this place existed in Vegas!

The only hiccup came with the pricing. The staff suggested selecting four add-ons, but the cost seemed a bit steep at over $16. By scaling down to two add-ons, the price felt more reasonable at around $12.

Overall, it's a solid 4-star experience. The food is definitely worth a try for any noodle enthusiast, just be mindful of how the add-ons can add up.

Good quality hotpot with yummy sauces. We waited for about 30 mins on a Saturday night for a table for 2 here which wasn't bad for prime time in nyc. We had the original herbal broth and it was very good. We shared a lot of food (see photos) including beef, lamb, seaweed, veggies combo, vermicelli, frozen tofu, fried tofu skin, enoki mushroom, fish tofu, fish paste, and 2 Tsingtaos. The bill came out to be around 100 plus tip. The service was ok because everyone seemed super busy and no one checked in on us that much. Overall, it's pretty good quality food. The sauces are a little limited and they didn't have a lot of different types of sauces to try. The price is a bit pricey for hotpot. Definitely still worth checking it out if you're around the area.

I have always been a proponent of supporting local businesses, but my experiences at this establishment have been consistently disappointing. Initially enticed by their rotisserie chicken, I was put off by a foul odor and an off-putting mustard color. Giving them the benefit of the doubt, I decided to give the restaurant another chance after a hiatus.

On my return visit, I opted for the boneless fried chicken with rice and beans. Unfortunately, the chicken was served raw, as evidenced by the photos I shared. It's disheartening to encounter such carelessness in food preparation. It is essential for any eatery to prioritize food safety and quality, and I hope this feedback prompts immediate improvement. However, until substantial changes are made, I cannot recommend this restaurant.

Title: A Pleasant Evening with Potential for More

My recent dinner at this restaurant, accompanied by my twin and a friend, was a delightful experience that left me looking forward to my next visit. Initially drawn in by the allure of their outdoor space, we settled for an indoor setting that did not disappoint. The ambiance of the restaurant was beautiful, complemented by a staff that exuded professionalism and cordiality.

I opted for the grilled octopus, which, despite being slightly over-charred, managed to impress with its tenderness. Meanwhile, my twin enjoyed the cauliflower dish, and our friend savored the shrimp. Each plate was well-received and contributed to an overall satisfying meal.

Though the outdoor experience remains on my to-do list, this place has convinced me that it's worth a return. The promise of dining under the stars, coupled with the high standards set by this initial visit, has me eagerly anticipating my next outing here.

Wallse is criminally underrated and woefully under-patronized, and don't believe anyone who tells you otherwise.  I have wanted to try Wallse for ages.  Somehow, since it's been on my radar, I've made it to Austria twice and Wallse 0 times.  So when they reopened this fall, I immediately booked a reservation.My friend + I did two 3 course menus; we got: FOIE GRAS TORCHON: I don't care for foie gras so my friend pretty much kept this one to herself, but picture attached for those interested.LOBSTER ROSTI: Impressed with both the quality + size of this dish.  Huge chunks of buttery lobster garnished with mushrooms and leeks served over potato.  I didn't expect to love this dish, and yet it's the one I can't stop thinking about weeks later.SPATZLE: With rabbit and mushrooms.  Exceeded expectations.  HALIBUT: This was the one dish I wasn't totally wild about.  Served with cucumber, dill, and chanterelle mushrooms.  The fish was fresh and well cooked but didn't have the 'wow' factor that the other plates had.  VENISON: Did NOT expect to love this as much as we did.  Served with cabbage and elderberry sauce.  Really, really interesting; our favorite entree.  SALZBURGER NOCKERL: Interesting dessert - served with huckleberries underneath.  I've been to Salzburg myself and had never heard of it; a sweet and light way to end the meal.  SACHERTORTE: I had asked our server about sachertorte and kaiserschmarrn which are my two favorite Austrian desserts.  Unfortunately, they had neither that day, but he did come out with a small amuse bouche size serving of sachertorte out of nowhere!!  Made my day.  WINE/DRINKS: Our sommelier was really, really lovely - Gruner Veltliner is my favorite wine but I don't pretend to be an expert.  She was really patient with us and explained the differences between the different wine regions; we ended up with a Gruner that we both enjoyed.All in all, we were impressed.  My only disappointment was that their schnitzel was veal instead of pork.  I LOVE schnitzel but I don't eat veal, so that was off the table for me.  Otherwise, totally happy with the food, service, & atmosphere, and would be thrilled to go back.

This was fun, and definitely worth the experience! You fill out a waiver before they give you a poncho and "license" to fish, and then you go to the tanks where they give you gloves and a fishing pole. I think they starve the fish a little, so they bit our bait within 2 minutes. The menu to describe it was pretty confusing, but our waitress was very helpful. They also accompany you to fish, so you're not on your own. Basically, each tank contained a fish type, so you choose which tank you want. You won't accidentally catch a $200 fish because you will only fish at the tanks with the fishes you want. Some fishes have different sizes, and they will cost different. But if you accidentally catch a big fish when you intended to get a small one, you have to take it. Then you tell them how you want it cooked, which you can do half-half. We did half grilled and half shabu shabu (the set up costs an extra $5). Each fish also comes with a bowl of rice, so we got some side dishes and pre-cooked dishes as well.  Since it was just salt grilled or boiled, it can be a bit bland for some people but very healthy. I think it tasted good with just a little bit of soy sauce, and the other dishes were also pretty good. I would come here again for the experience, but if you wanted really yummy Japanese food, this may not be the option.

Title: A Bite Before Broadway: A Dive Into Midtown's Hyped Burger Spot

Having heard the buzz surrounding this elusive burger joint in Midtown for ages, I finally ventured to see what the fuss was about before catching "Bat out of Hell" at City Center. Guided by reputation and curiosity, my mom—the toughest of critics—and I found the spot easily nestled next to a hotel lobby, debunking any myths of its hidden nature.

The ambiance screamed dive bar nostalgia with graffiti-clad walls and vintage posters, encapsulating a 'seat yourself' vibe. The menu, scribbled on cardboard, offered simplicity: burgers, fries, grilled cheese, sodas, and beer shakes. Opting for the single patty burgers and fries, we dove in. The burgers were undeniably well-crafted with a juicy beef patty and customizable toppings, yet they didn't quite seize the crown of "best in the city" for me.

However, the fries triumphed; they were a throwback to the golden days of McDonald's but markedly superior. 

While I wouldn't brave hours-long waits, this spot warrants a visit for those in Midtown. It's not about confirming if they serve the best burger—rather, it's about savoring a solid meal in a place with character. Swing by during a quieter time, enjoy a genuine burger, and maybe you'll find your best.

**Restaurant Review: [Restaurant Name]**

**Rating: Food 2/5, Service 3/5**

I recently tried [Restaurant Name] for the first time, having heard mixed reviews from a friend who used to eat there. We were ravenous and went all-in with a generous order of Mala xiang guo, mapo tofu, and kung pao chicken for delivery. The Mala xiang guo came with an ample choice of 8 toppings, and portion-wise, seemed enough for two.

However, our excitement quickly faded with each dish. The Mala xiang guo was overwhelming in its saltiness, overshadowing the flavors even when paired with rice. The mapo tofu strayed far from the authentic taste I’m accustomed to, resembling a watery, oddly sweet hot and sour soup - it was a letdown and a waste of money in my opinion. The kung pao chicken, usually a fail-safe at most Chinese restaurants, also missed the mark, lacking the expected punch of flavor.

This place seems to have a generous hand when it comes to portions but an equally heavy one with salt. Anyone familiar with Chinese cuisine expects a certain level of saltiness, but this was excessive, leaving us reaching for water to quench our thirst.

Service-wise, the packaging was commendable, but the late delivery and lukewarm food were disappointments. We skipped reheating as our hunger couldn't wait.

Overall, my first experience at [Restaurant Name] fell short, and despite the sizable portions, the high salt content and lack of authentic flavors make me hesitant to return. My advice to potential customers would be to specify if you prefer less salt, and maybe steer clear of the mapo tofu.

**Final Thoughts: Generous servings can't save the overly salty and unauthentic tastes of [Restaurant Name]. Would not recommend.**

It's a really sweet little place to grab drinks and appetizers for friends, or a romantic dinner. I came here with my coworkers and had a great time. For a small place it's hard to get around and there are seasoned waiters and some who seem to have two left feet. I come here often and always appreciate the atmosphere and food, but the service depending on who it is can be a hit or miss.

Title: A Love Affair with Late-Night Artichoke Pizza

My late-night cravings are invariably satisfied at this pizzeria, a haven for night owls with a penchant for artichokes. Their classic artichoke pizza is an irresistible nightcap, boasting a fluffy crust enveloped in what can only be described as a sauce of pure enchantment. Despite my best intentions to diversify, the allure of the artichoke slice is unyielding, eclipsing even the tempting seafood option.

The eatery bustles with activity at 3 am, a testament to its culinary magnetism, yet the waits are justified by the generous seating space—a rarity among its nocturnal counterparts. Be warned: the pizza is decadently filling, leaving me in a state of satisfied discomfort. Yet, such is the price of indulgence—a price I'm willing to pay, time and again.

I go to Hunter College nearby and I came across this restaurant since its only one avenue over. I forgot to take a picture of the entree, which was a squid ink pasta and it tasted amazing. The bread and the service was top-notch and the wine was absolutely delicious!!! Will be back :)

We visited Kenka couple times when my husband was in graduated school but weren't here for 3 years since you need to come to wait before they open at 6:00pm to get a table or wait for 1-2 hours in line. Their food was solid for Japanese izakaya with amazingly affordable price. We ordered 12 dishes for group of 6 people and only paid $25 each person. However, their service was horrible and reluctant. We tried to ask for some recommendation but the waiter kept ignoring our questions. It's really ridiculous that there were 6 tables still available but people waited outside at the same time. (We were the first group served so we didn't wait in line.)

Title: A Mixed Bag of Flavors at a Korean Eatery

Rating: 3.5/5

My dining experience at this Korean restaurant was a roller coaster of flavors and surprises. Starting on a surprising note, the banchan, or traditional small side dishes, were not complimentary as is customary, which was a slight letdown.

However, the kitchen redeemed itself with the Korean scotch egg, or what they call the crispy rice egg. Priced at $6, this dish was a revelation, earning a perfect score for its taste and presentation. The egg was wonderfully runny inside, encased in a flawlessly fried shell, and the meat was succulent, paired with a spicy mayo that tied it all together beautifully. This appetizer was hearty enough to share and stood out as the highlight of the meal.

The Korean fried chicken wings, on the other hand, fell short of the benchmark set by popular joints like Barn Joo. Though more deep-fried than I prefer, they were still finger-licking good, costing $9.

The galbijim, or braised short ribs, priced at $20, were tender but drowned in an overly salty sauce that made the broth nearly inedible for me. The generous portion and tasty meat were its saving grace, but I had to resort to the accompanying rice to balance the saltiness.

The soju sampler was a fun touch. For $12, you get four varieties, with both yuzu and lychee standing out as favorites for their sweeter profiles. All were potent and added a sociable element to the meal.

Overall, the restaurant offers a decent experience with some hits and misses. The portions are generous and the prices reasonable, especially considering the location. It's a spot I might revisit for that standout scotch egg and to give other menu items a chance to impress.

This was my second visit to Butter Midtown, both times in private party area. Drinks preparation are phenomenal and bartender does make good recommendations and even adjust cocktails based on your taste and feedback.Reason for 3 stars is mainly food. Nothing out of the ordinary or special given it's one of the celebrity chef restaurant. One of chicken sausage appetizer was rather too dry and bland, surprisingly. Definitely scope to step up.

Title: Sizzling Korean BBQ at Food Gallery 32

During a recent visit to Manhattan's Food Gallery 32, a bustling hub known for a diverse array of Korean eateries, I was drawn to one stall in particular, enticing patrons with the savory aroma of Korean BBQ. This culinary hotspot isn’t vying for the title of best Korean BBQ ever—a claim my charming "Barbie" might whimsically contend for—but it does offer a flavorful and cost-effective experience that stands out, especially in New York City's pricey dining landscape.

The sizzle of the grill and the tender meats provided a satisfying meal, reflective of the overall high standards of the food court. Despite there being no "Kobe-queue" for celebrity signatures, the popularity of this Korean BBQ stall is evident in the eager line of diners. It may not surpass your top BBQ experiences, but it holds its own with affordability and taste.

In conclusion, Food Gallery 32's Korean BBQ is a strong contender in the city's fierce food scene, offering value without compromising flavor. Alongside other great stalls, it makes this food court a must-visit destination for any fan of Korean cuisine.

Tucked away with a splendid view of Bryant Park, especially during the enchanting Christmas Market, this is a gem for anyone looking to savor a fine glass of wine, a well-crafted cocktail, or a crisp beer. My chilly day visit was warmed by the bartender's friendly demeanor and expertise. The cuisine was delightful, with an excellent salad and a particularly flavorful spiced lamb kabob appetizer. Both dishes were sumptuous and left a lasting impression. A highly recommended spot for both the food and atmosphere.

This place is crazy popular. Even during lunch time there is a wait. Understandably so, the food is spectacular.Had the ramen and it was packed with flavor. It had such depth to it. It's a little pricey but for the flavor of the food, I'd say it's quite justified. I want to try other dishes next time.

Nestled in the heart of the city, this charming new eatery oozes warmth and sophistication. Despite its recent opening, it has already established itself with an enticing prix fixe menu, offering two or three delicious French courses. The cuisine consistently impresses, as I can attest after two delightful dinners.

Happy hour here is a gem, featuring a selection of small plates paired perfectly with fine wines. The ambiance is intimate and tastefully decorated, creating an inviting atmosphere for diners. With seating options both at the bar and in a separate area, they accommodate various preferences, though I highly recommend reservations to secure a spot in this quaint venue.

Service is commendable, with the wait staff being both personable and informative, enhancing the dining experience with their knowledge of the fare and wine.

The only slight hiccup is the limited restroom facilities, with just two available leading to occasional queues.

Overall, this restaurant is a culinary haven for French cuisine aficionados and a must-visit for those looking to indulge in a cozy and elegant dining experience.

Title: A Delightful Family Lunch at the Local Gem

Last Saturday, our family lunch outing with four adults and four children turned out to be a delightful experience at this cozy restaurant. Though the dining area is compact, we were fortunate to secure a table for eight at the peak dining hour of 12:30 PM.

The culinary highlight was undoubtedly the tacos, each order bringing two savory bites to the table. We savored an array which included shrimp, cauliflower, beef, and pork, each bursting with flavor. While the guacamole was just passable, the waffles were a hit, completely polished off by the children. The sides did not disappoint either; the black beans and rice were scrumptious, and the plantains disappeared quickly, much to the kids' delight. The quesadillas also received an enthusiastic thumbs-up from the little ones.

As for myself, the salad was just okay, although another in our party found it more to his taste. A standout was the mushroom burger – an absolute treat. However, I did find myself wishing for a mushroom taco option on the menu.

The service was the cherry on top – the entire staff was amiable and welcoming, creating a warm atmosphere. Given the quality of food and the quantity that satisfied both adults and children, the $200 total bill felt like very good value. This little gem of a restaurant has won our hearts, and we are already looking forward to our next visit.
I had a delightful experience at this restaurant, where the relaxing ambiance complements the tasty food and attentive service. It's a place I certainly plan to visit again.

I stopped by at this location during weekdays for lunch couple of times over last few weeks. This location has a bar and plenty of tables you shouldn't have to wait long. Order your meal upfront and they will bring it to you when it's ready. I ordered a frozen margarita with rose salt ($5 during their happy hour!) and couple of tacos. The mini tacos were delicious, the plant based options were an explosion of flavors and the taco salad bowl absolutely on point. Cannot say enough good things about the environment, the food, the drinks. Highly recommend!

Our dining experience was decidedly average. While the drinks impressed with their divine flavors, the food failed to make a memorable impact. Our server was undoubtedly sweet, enhancing our visit, but unfortunately, the lackluster culinary offerings don't tempt us for a return visit.

My recent visit to this Japanese curry gem was a delight! I highly recommend the couple set for a shared dining experience. It offers a taste of their perfectly chewy curry udon and the rich, savory curry rice. The set is complemented by crispy katsu and succulent tempura shrimp, which are fantastic with the curry. Don't forget to top your dish with the provided garlic chips and scallions for an added flavor boost. For the spice enthusiasts, there's an option to dial up the heat, but even the non-spicy version is absolutely satisfying. A must-try spot for curry lovers!

My sister made a reservation to come here last Saturday night. She had bought a Groupon for 4 people and invited me and my boyfriend to join them for dinner. It was an spectacular experience. Everything was perfect.Elena/Helena was our waitress, she was incredible and made sure everything was exceptional for us. We received an appetizer on the house, which was "Homemade Hummus, Tahini, Babaganoush, eggplant salad, red cabbage slaw and beets", my sister and her boyfriend tried and loved every single thing. They also served some pita bread with pesto and pesto cream cheese or pesto butter on the house, not sure which one but was good anyway.We started the night with a bottle of red wine, Cabernet Sauvignon to be exact, which was more than excellent. The Groupon offered two bottles, we received the second with our steaks.We ordered appetizers and salads afterward, which were also included on the Groupon. We had Bbq Crispy Chicken Wings and Moroccan Cigars accompanied with Talia's Salad and Roasted Beet Salad, everything was appetizing and tasteful, definitely inviting us to anxiously wait for what was left.After the appetizers, Helena served our entree choices. The four of us ordered Ribeye Steaks, of course they were incredibly juicy, exquisite, mouthwatering. We were definitely in Heaven. Each Entree came with two sides, as per our Groupon. I ordered the incredible Mashed Potatoes and Sweet Potato Fries and they were both simply perfect. The mash potatoes were made with some garlic taste, it was very flavorful.We went down a bottle and like 1/4 of the second and then ordered dessert, which was also included in the Groupon. We had two desserts, ordered a Tiramisu and Chocolate Cake. Helena informed us the Tiramisu was kosher, in case we wanted to change our option, we acknowledged but decided to keep the order. We made the right decision, the Tiramisu was lovely. We all loved it. After all the food, our waitress Helena brought the bill, which included just the taxes as the Groupon does not cover for them. We stood at the restaurant for about another hour and finished the Wine Bottle. It was a lovely experience as much as it was a lovely evening. In our opinion (unanimous), the price of the Groupon does not even cover 1/4 of the amount of the scrumptious food we were able to consume and enjoy on our visit, plus also getting two bottles of wine, along with an outstanding, splendid service from our waitress and all the staff at the restaurant.Definitely looking forward to come here again and devour another one of those savory, delightful, succulent Ribeye steaks. And definitely would be lucky and would love to have Helena hosting our evening again.

This place was clutch post marathon. After running for about six hours straight in the cold, something hot and meaty hit the spot. It's a pretty tight squeeze for seating but definitely worth it. I would recommend this place to others and come back for more'

What a great little spot! Make sure to reserve a table online otherwise you'll be waiting around. Love the atmosphere of this restaurant. Gives off true French vibes. The bottomless mimosas are great, the food is phenomenal, and the customer service is top notch. Been here a few times and I'll definitely be returning back. I have ordered the Croquet Monsieur and Eggs Scandinavian - neither disappointed. I've even had a friend once order something that wasn't to her liking - without any questions they took it and remade it and had it out within minutes. They make sure you're never waiting around and constantly replenish your drinks. 10/10 for me. Keep in mind: They ONLY take cash. No cards.

Title: A Trendy Spot with Hits and Misses – Japanese Chain Delivers a Mixed Experience

Rating: ★★★★☆

Nestled within a chain that knows how to set a trendy, modern vibe, this Japanese restaurant scores high on ambiance with its cool, minimalist decor, spacious layout, and a quiet atmosphere that all but guarantees a no-wait seating. Whether you cozy up at the bar or spread out at one of the many tables, the place invites you to unwind and relax.

Service here is efficient, garnering a solid 4 out of 5. While it may lack a personal touch, the no-tip policy reflects the straightforward, service-focused approach, which isn't necessarily a downside in my book.

The edamame is a star dish, deserving a full 5 out of 5 for its simple, snappy perfection. The gyu kushi yakitori is another triumph, featuring tantalizingly marinated beef that leaves you craving just one more skewer.

However, not all that glitters is gold. The chawanmushi was a disappointing miss, a struggle to swallow, and is best left unordered. And though the vegetable yakitori was a decent, shareable appetizer, it was little more than a fleeting few bites of standard fare.

A mix-up in my order led me to the sushi sashimi salad, a light and healthy option that unfortunately did little to satisfy my hunger due to its modest portion size. It was a passable dish but paled in comparison to what I've enjoyed elsewhere.

Overall, the dining experience wasn't a letdown, but it's apparent that some dishes shine brighter than others. This seems like an ideal venue for group outings, where you can dive into the extensive menu and find your favorites through collective trial and error. A mixed bag, but in the world of chain dining, it holds its own.

Title: A Cozy Brunch Experience Worth the Wait

I've visited this gem for brunch on a few occasions and each visit has left me satisfied. While they don't accept reservations for brunch and the popularity often leads to a wait, it's a minor inconvenience that's quickly forgotten once you're seated.

The menu may boast typical brunch classics, but each dish is crafted with care - well-seasoned and perfectly cooked. A standout is the chicken sausage that accompanies the Country Breakfast; it's nothing short of amazing. The Oatmeal small plate also deserves praise for its generous portion size, easily standing in for a full meal.

As for the drinks, the mimosas and bellinis come with a generous pour of champagne, and I'd highly recommend indulging in the unlimited option. If you're feeling adventurous, give their specialty brunch cocktails a try. They're a delight and priced just right.

In all, this spot has mastered the brunch experience with great food and drinks, just be prepared for a short wait.

Title: A Consistently Delightful Experience

I frequent various branches of this restaurant, but the spaciousness and calm ambiance of this particular location always stand out. On my latest visit, the hazelnut flavor was a new indulgence for me – an absolutely delightful choice. Beyond the delicious fare, what consistently impresses me is the service. Regardless of location, the staff members are patient, cheerful, and notably attentive. Whether you're winding down after dinner in the city or simply craving an exceptional meal, popping into this restaurant is always a brilliant idea.

I absolutely adore this restaurant! The outdoor seating in the back provides a delightful dining experience. Their margaritas are top-notch, perfectly paired with delicious food offerings. Particularly noteworthy were the fresh oysters appetizer and the succulent grilled octopus – both favorites that I highly recommend.

I popped into this somewhat hidden gem for a weekday lunch, nestled as it is within a shared space with a deli. As a regular, I ordered my go-to army soup to-go. Despite my pre-order call, I experienced a minor frustration with a 10-minute wait before receiving my meal. That said, the wait did little to detract from the enjoyment of the comforting, piping hot soup once back at my office. Priced at under $13, the meal included a generous tub of soup, a side of kimchi, and rice — a value hard to beat. A tip for fellow diners: carry cash for purchases over $20 to snag a 5% discount.

Title: A Dim Return to a Once-Favorite Spot

On a highly anticipated trip back to my favorite city, I made a beeline for what used to be my go-to lunch destination. Expectations were high, with nostalgic excitement for the stylish ambiance hinted at by promised candles—alas, none were to be seen. A similarly disappointing discovery was the apparent abdication of spices in the kitchen.

The menu, seemingly an ode to comfort classics, unfortunately set a stage for letdowns in execution. My BLT, a sandwich where tempeh bacon should shine, was lacking in its promised B. The tempeh's role was to deliver a savory punch, yet it was missing its cue altogether—leaving just the bread, albeit delicious, to carry the show.

My fiancé's choice of the Cajun chicken was a parallel tale of missing zest. The vegetarian meat substitute offered a substantial bite but fell flat with the absence of the characteristic heat and flavor one would expect from Cajun seasoning.

In summary, the once bright culinary light of this establishment seems to have dimmed, leaving behind unlit candles and unspiced fare. Here's hoping for a rekindling of both the ambiance and the kitchen's former prowess.

I came a while ago with my fiance for a quick lunch. We both got the bowl and for myself, I got purple rice and the korean fried rice with the short ribs along with bean sprouts, corn, picked radish as a topping. Portion size is huge and I definitely was not able to finish the bowl. The short ribs were nice and tender and they give you a good amount. My fiance get the bowl with glass noodles which was very good. It did not come with your typical spinach, carrot fillings but nicely flavored with sesame oil! He too got the short ribs with kimchi as one of his toppings. Overall, the food was really good- if I worked nearby, it would be a go-to lunch spot but unfortunately I dont! Service is great, workers are nice and helpful! Will be back if i am in the area again!

I really wanted to be blown away by this place but sadly was not. The interior is very cool, there is a corridor lined with herbs and spices leading to the back dining room, lemons come in cute little dishes, and just about everything in the place is thoughtfully decorated. I came with a group of 6 so we were able to try many things on the menu including the lobster ramen, Javanese oxtail soup, Hiramasa sashimi, fried calamari, whole sautéed shrimp, akuna cod, waygu strip loin and nasi goreng.The most memorable dishes were the lobster ramen and fried calamari. I would definitely recommend getting these. Everything was cooked well and plated beautifully but nothing stood out other than the 2 dishes mentioned above. The cod was also the least favorite and was left mostly untouched by my group and the portions were rather small. Everything was definitely on the heavy side so the nasi goreng was a nice side dish to balance out all the sauces. I think this place has potential so I'm hoping that there will be some new additions to the menu that will offer a comprehensive experience!

Title: The Ultimate Hangover Burger Experience

It's hard to find fresh adjectives to describe a spot so well-loved for its no-nonsense, delicious burgers that serve as the ultimate hangover cure. While there might be a slight inconsistency with the seasoning - some days the burgers are seasoned to perfection, other days just slightly less so - it's almost always a culinary home run.

Be prepared: this is a cash-only establishment, and if you're dropping by during peak hours, expect a wait. But rest assured, the wait is not for nothing; it’s part of the charm and the payoff is a mouthwatering burger experience that lives up to the hype.

Title: A Stellar First Experience at Thai Villa

After four years of anticipation, I am elated to report that Thai Villa exceeds its reputation. Finding this gem a mere stone's throw from my office, I wonder why it took so long. I recently visited with colleagues to explore their famed Secret Menu, available via a Yelp waitlist. 

The restaurant's interior dazzles, with opulent chandeliers cascading light from above—our upper-level seating offering a panoramic spectacle of the venue's grandeur. Although I sidestepped the Secret Menu, the lure was appreciated for it ushered me through Thai Villa's doors.

My selection from the lunch specials did not disappoint: ginger sautéed vegetables with shrimp, enhanced by squid for an additional $4. Accompanied by a salad and hefty, savory dumplings, the meal delighted. A minor letdown was the substitute of peanut sauce over the expected ginger dressing on the salad, but the main course, with its tender veggies and succulent seafood, was superbly flavored with a ginger sauce that was nothing short of divine.

Don't mimic my prolonged hesitation. Either reserve your spot or capitalize on the Secret Menu promotion for a timely seat at this culinary haven. Thai Villa isn't just a meal; it's an encounter with excellence.

Title: A Holiday Haven for Large Groups at HK

Last night, on the eve of Thanksgiving, my group of thirteen and I had the pleasure of dining at HK, a restaurant evidently well-versed in accommodating large parties, especially during festive periods. Unlike other establishments, HK did not constrain us to a set menu, a definite plus considering the varying dietary restrictions among us.

Our server was nothing short of attentive and personable, enhancing our experience and making the recommendation of HK for sizable gatherings an easy one.

As for the fare, the Harvest Guacamole was passable, albeit lacking in excitement and scant on vegetables for dipping. The Grilled Whole-Wheat Flat Bread was met with approving nods, its companion, the red pepper hummus, leaving a pleasant taste in our memories.

The Modern Greek Salad's ample size was commendable, although a few more pieces of feta and olives wouldn't have gone amiss. The Harvest Paella took us by surprise with its delightful symphony of seafood and chorizo, despite being on the saltier side – certainly worth a reorder.

The Salmon emerged as a favorite, uncomplicated yet satisfying in flavor and size. The Branzino, however, fell slightly short when compared to its piscatorial counterpart.

Taking into account the whole dining experience, especially for a large group during a holiday, I would rate HK four stars. The food is a solid three stars on its own, but it's the accommodation and service that truly elevate the overall impression.

I recently dined at a local spot that impressed me with its speedy service and delicious fare. The soy honey wings were the standout dish – absolutely mouthwatering and not to be missed. However, the chicken in the chaufa did leave something to be desired as it was a bit on the dry side. Overall, a great dining experience with just a minor hiccup.

If you're going to come here especially on the weekend for brunch, be sure to make reservations. The wait was about an hour and a half to two hours. We are outside so we could not hear the music. I had the unlimited rum punches which were good and the hamburger. I think the service was pretty fair. It was a fun day even after eating we went back inside to listen to the music. Just don't forget those reservations!

Title: Tasty Brunch with a Side of Slow Service

I recently visited this spot for brunch, snagging a Pulsd deal that offered a solid value of $35 for two people, covering an entrée and a pair of drinks each. My cousin savored the steak rancheros, a hearty plate combining sunny-side-up eggs with a succulent NY strip on a crispy corn tostada, rounded out with Chiltomate, beans, and avocado. I opted for the chilaquiles with steak, a satisfying concoction of eggs (scrambled at my request), crispy tortillas, tangy tomatillo salsa, queso fresco, and avocado. While the steak addition came with a $6 surcharge and was a touch scant for the price, the overall dish did not disappoint.

Our brunch was further zest with margaritas—my spicy version was perfectly complemented by a chili salt rim, and my cousin's watermelon margarita hit the sweet spot. Though the drink selection was limited, our choices did not let us down.

However, the service left something to be desired. Despite the restaurant's empty tables, we experienced quite a wait, particularly when trying to settle the bill, resorting to handle payment at the bar ourselves. Overall, the Pulsd deal was worth it, and the brunch menu had a creative flair, but I might hesitate at full price given the service pace.

So we ordered Rocky's to be delivered to our office. It arrived and looked really good, but we were a little dismayed at how wet the pizza turned out to be. By wet i mean none of the toppings would stay on and you had to eat the pizza with a knife and fork. It was also so greasy that we had to put at least 3-4 paper plates underneath it because it had that much grease under it. All in all the taste was good, but a little bit too runny for me.

As a Mexican-American hailing from California, I've struggled to find a place in New York that captures the essence of true Mexican cuisine – until I stumbled upon this gem! The restaurant takes inspiration from Baja-style cooking and nails it. The moment you step inside, you're transported to Mexico, thanks to the authentic decor and the fact that the staff is all Hispanic, which adds to the authentic atmosphere.

Although the space is on the smaller side, the vibe is upbeat and welcoming. The food is more than decent—it's a delightful taste of home for someone like me. What's more, the friendly and bilingual staff make sure you feel right at home, whether you're fluent in Spanish or not. This spot is a rare find in New York for anyone craving genuine Mexican fare.

Came here yesterday for restaurant week and was satisfied with this Michelin star restaurant. The atmosphere is definitely very elegant and fancy. The food didn't really match my palate as I like stronger flavors and seasoning in my food, but my mother loved it. We both thought the braised short rib was excellent. I would've liked more flavor or sauce with it, but I can tell they made the short rib pretty well. Their duck tartare appetizer was good too - pretty interesting. I'm used to the smooth texture in pate where you spread it on bread, but this was a block of chunks of duck meat which was good too. It was on the more bland side too with a hint of sweetness. The tartellini pasta wasn't anything too impressive. Their small desserts at the end were tasty too. To be honest, I'd give the food here 3 stars. Only gave it 4 because of the price deal for restaurant week. Otherwise, I don't think I would come here for a normal meal due to price and the taste of the food.

We came for dinner on Christmas Day and the entire restaurant is festive and packed. Since we made a reservation it did not take long before they seated us.As we sat on our chairs some nibbles were placed on the table and it did not take long before our server took our order. Since we'd had a big dinner the night before we decided to just order popodums for appetizers and chicken tikka masala and lamb saag, the dishes came relatively fast except mine was wrong, however they replaced pretty much immediately. This is where I noticed that my chicken tikka masala seemed consequently somewhat rushed, dry and really underwhelming.The dishes are served with biryani rice, the lamb saag tasted ok but did not rise to the occasion. I've eaten Indian dishes from around the world (modesty aside) but Benares failed to impress me with their dinner cuisine although customer service maybe good but that would not give me enough reason to comeback!

Tucked away in the bustling heart of Times Square, this hidden gem offers a delightful escape from the typical tourist traps. Upon arrival, our reservation was promptly honored, setting the stage for a pleasant dining experience. While the restaurant boasts an impressive selection of wines by the glass, perfect for pairing with their generously portioned pastas, the culinary execution was good, albeit falling short of outstanding. My spaghetti, though tasty, lacked that harmonious blend of sauce and noodle I’ve savored in more authentic Italian eateries. Nonetheless, the restaurant exudes a romantic charm complemented by truly excellent service. A great choice for those seeking a non-chain dining option amidst the Times Square buzz.

I recently had the pleasure of dining with my family at one of the chain's locations in Manhattan, and I must say, they've maintained their reputation for being incredibly family and child-friendly. As with their other locations, this one did not disappoint in creating a welcoming atmosphere for all ages. The portion sizes were on the smaller side, yet they compensated with a diverse selection of items included in their set meals, ensuring a little something for every palate at the table.

We had a delightful experience at this laid-back spot where we popped in on a whim. I sipped on a glass of red wine that was unexpectedly delightful, pairing well with a cheeseburger wrapped in a warm pita—a truly tasty combination. My friend opted for the lamb, which was even more delectable, though both dishes impressed us greatly. Highly recommend for a casual yet satisfying meal.

Title: Worth the Wait? A Slice of NYC Hype

Recently, after an event, curiosity led me to a local pizza joint that's been the talk of the town. Despite not being particularly hungry, I couldn't resist checking out the buzz for myself. The queue outside was modest – a dozen people awaited their turn – yet the wait for my pizza extended to a substantial 35-40 minutes.

With time to ponder over the menu, I veered from my initial choice of a plain slice, also adding a Margarita to my order, suspecting I might not brave the wait a second time. The plain slice met expectations – crispy, sufficiently greasy, and satisfying. The Margarita, however, was the star; its fresh and vibrant flavors clearly overshadowed its simpler counterpart.

While the pizza lived up to its reputation, the lengthy wait was less desirable. This is, after all, New York City, a haven for pizza aficionados. For those who plan to visit, be advised: seating is sparse, limited to a communal table that accommodates four or five. In sum, if time is on your side, this spot delivers on taste. Bon appetit!

We came for my husband's birthday dinner. He has been here many times in the past and has always had a positive experience. Same with this night. We started with a delicious chef's amuse touch of white bean puree on a crispy toasted baguette. We shared some appetizers - burrata with carrot, maple and chili, beets with stracciatella, hazelnut and cranberry, citrus marinated sardines with ceci fritti, and a basket of focaccia. All were stellar items and would order them all over again. I think the beets though were my absolute favorite.I ordered the honeynut squash mezzeluna with hazelnut and brown butter ($21). This was a mistake on my part. It was okay - but just not at the level that I was hoping for. Portion wise though - it was huge and I did eat the whole plate so it wasn't like it wasn't good. He had the carbonara ($20), and loved it. Perfectly executed classic dish. Prices on our pasta dishes were incredibly reasonable for NYC. Customer service was attentive and friendly. Plus the vibe here was nice and warm. Not stuffy - lots of big groups of people getting together. Great people watching opportunities here. Overall nice evening in Greenwich Village.

Title: Post-Work Relaxation Spot

My colleagues and I frequent this eatery near our office to decompress after work. It boasts a casual vibe, complete with TVs and a variety of games – the arcade and shuffleboard being crowd-pleasers. The menu offers satisfying appetizers; we often share the fries, pretzel, and chips. The drink selection is on par with Manhattan prices, and the cocktail options are worth exploring. Be prepared for a boisterous atmosphere – it's not the spot for quiet conversations. A solid choice for an after-hours hangout.

This is the best restaurant you can go to if you want Indian fusion food. If you want to splurge this is the place!We had the sweetest waitress! I wish I asked her her name!! Thirteen of us were there still we didn't have to wait for long! We had so many dishes from the menu. I was able to capture most of the things on my camera but there were a lot more!!!!!So these are a few that you should most definitely try: 1. Ghost chili chicken kebab: if spicy is your way, you'll be a die hard fan once you've tried this 2. Palak paneer: the freshest palak paneer I've had in my life! The flavor was one to remember 3. Kurkuri bhel: was an amazing snack!! 4. Butter chicken : was delicious  I would order that everytime I'm there!! And other items that we ordered were their okra, kofta, dal makhani, paratwala paneer, garlic and butter naan, chicken tikka masala, gobi manchurian and many more!!!For desserts we had their gulab jamuns!!!! Ah! If you're Indian, you know that the difference between the packaged and the ones we get from a halwai! These were the organic halwai flavored which was really amazing to find in the States! For drinks I had two shots of their tequila and it was the amount I needed for that kick! I would rate this 10/10! So yea, take my word for it! Do try it!

Title: A Solo Diner's Pre-Theater Delight

I recently dined at this gem of a spot before catching a theater show and was thoroughly impressed by the experience. As a solo diner, I was initially concerned about missing out on their tasting menu, but the staff was incredibly accommodating. The tasting menu provided an excellent value and allowed me to sample a variety of the restaurant's offerings. Every dish was a hit, and the quantity was more than enough to satisfy even my hearty appetite.

The restaurant itself is on the smaller side, so it's wise to book in advance if you're not dining alone. I arrived early and enjoyed the calm before it naturally got busier closer to showtime. The service here is the epitome of friendly and efficient, ensuring that I finished my sumptuous meal with time to spare before my show.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a fantastic choice for anyone looking for a quality pre-theater meal that doesn't compromise on taste or value. I left full, happy, and excited to return. A definite win in my book!

Out of all the hot pot places I went to, this one is probably my least favorite. One important thing you should note is this is NOT AYCE. So you are paying 8-10 bucks for a small platter of beef or shrimp. You would think that if we were paying, the portion size would be bigger, but it wasn't. In addition, the place had limited selection of sauces. The food was also just alright. There wasn't too much of a variety to choose from. The beef was on the dry and grainy side. Despite it being AYCE, I could not taste the difference in the quality of the food. I would go somewhere else for better quality and cheaper hot pot. I did not notice anything amazing about this place to want to go again.

Passed by a million times and after it was recommended I decided to try with a friend today. Cute, cozy atmosphere but small. I definitely recommend making a reservation as there was a wait and they were quite busy. Great selection of Mediterranean choices that all sounded so good I almost couldn't decide. Steak and eggs were cooked just right and was the proper portion amount. Also enjoyed the selection of breads and muffins with butter and jam they bring to the table after ordering. Looking forward to going back and trying other menu items and cocktails.

I visited Island for the first time in many years last night. I very much enjoyed it! The decor is preppy meets nautical and the clientele skews older but we felt welcome. Ordered:Caesar Salad ($14)- this salad was made with Boston lettuce instead of the typical romaine. This was a nice touch. The Boston lettuce was softer than romaine. The salad had croutons and a generous amount of fresh Parmesan cheese. The dressing was the real star. It had depth of flavor and the taste of anchovies. Roasted Maple Glazed Norwegian Salmon ($30)- the salmon was a nice sized piece that was cooked to order. It was roasted with a maple mustard glaze. The skin was crispy. The salmon was not dry/overcooked. It came over roasted Brussels sprouts. Seafood Linguini ($28)- the pasta was cooked al dente and served with shrimp, mussels and clams. The sauce was natural, made from the liquid from the mussels and clams, olive oil, garlic and multicolored cherry tomatoes. I really enjoyed this dish! I was a little disappointed that one of the clams arrived shut and therefore couldn't be eaten. Overall, I really enjoyed my dinner at Island. It was a little more expensive than other restaurants I typically dine at, but the service and the quality of the food was very good.

Title: A Hidden Gem Deserving More Stars

I'm genuinely baffled by the modest 3.5-star rating of this establishment. Each dish I've sampled has been nothing short of delectable. The ambiance is exceptional, exuding a charm that elevates the dining experience. Adding to its allure, I've consistently been seated promptly, without the dreaded wait that often accompanies popular dining spots.

The potatoes alone are worth a visit, easily some of the finest I've had anywhere. The burger is a reliable classic, executed with skill. But it was the spicy uovo dish from the brunch menu that made a lasting impression—its name escapes me, but the flavors linger on, a testimony to its deliciousness.

The pasta offerings exhibit the same level of culinary prowess, each one as satisfying as the last. It's a wonder that this restaurant isn't boasting a higher star rating. Perhaps it's only a matter of time before word gets out and the stars align with the quality evident in every bite.

Title: A Vegetarian's Delight at a Bustling Chinese Eatery

As a vegetarian, Chinese cuisine can often present limited options, but thankfully, this restaurant stands out as a delightful exception. During a lunch outing with colleagues, we found ourselves amidst a crowd, signaling the spot's growing popularity.

With a recommendation from a Chinese colleague, who also graciously ordered on our behalf, we navigated the menu with ease, as it is pleasantly available in English, and the staff are conversant in the language too.

Our table was graced with a vegan version of the classic Mapo Tofu, a stir-fried bok choy that was a testament to the magic of simplicity with just the right touch of garlic, alongside other non-vegetarian dishes my peers enjoyed.

Service was marked by the warmth of a notably affable lady who took our orders, and the cleanliness of the venue added to the pleasant dining experience. The complimentary soup was a thoughtful gesture that complemented our meal.

In short, the vegetarian dishes I sampled were utterly scrumptious, especially the bok choy, which left an indelible impression. This is a restaurant I eagerly anticipate returning to.

We came here on January 2nd of 2019. Surprisingly, this place was very busy. There were very little free appetizer provided to us compared to other places that I have been to. The food is ok. Nothing extraordinary. I believe I had better tasting at other Korean places. This one was an OK...

This is an office favorite- and it's easy to see why. Great food, affordable and huge portions with that aioli?!!? I come here for MealPal a bunch, and having vegetarian options are a game changer. The fried tofu is so good, easily one of my most favorite proteins here. The actual purple rice itself is so fresh and delicious, I could eat here every day! The prices on soju are actually very good. I don't normally do boozy work lunches but nice to be able to pick up a bottle on the way home!

I recently dined at a charming spot with a great atmosphere and hip decor that immediately set a welcoming tone. The food was nothing short of delicious, offering generous portions that provided excellent value for the price. The service was a highlight, with a kind and enthusiastic wait staff that truly enhanced the dining experience. Note that the restaurant is nestled in the basement, so watch your step as you head down. Restroom facilities are available for convenience. Overall, a delightful culinary adventure that I'll be eager to repeat.

Despite its compact size, this restaurant delivers outstandingly quick service. The culinary experience is a delight, with both food and drinks leaving a remarkable impression. I indulged in a delectable custom egg sandwich served on a biscuit, enriched with creamy avocado and zesty chipotle aioli, paired with a smooth almond milk latte. The quality of the meal ensures I'll certainly be returning for another taste.

I've been a big fan of Indikitch ever since going to their first location on 23rd Street when they first opened. This Chipotle-esque lunch spot really hits the spot when I'm craving for something that's flavorful and spicy. The food is always fresh and made-to-order.The chicken tikka masala is my go-to and it never disappoints. The basmati rice is fluffy and aromatic, the chicken is tender and the sauce is extremely tangy and flavorful. I like to dip their garlic naan in the sauce. The medley of pickled cabbage and carrots is also a nice palette cleaner. Overall, Indikitch is a solid lunch spot. I'd definitely recommend the chicken tikka masala and their paneer if you're a big fan of cheese. They also offer samosas and mango lassi here!

We were seeing a show on a Thursday evening, and I was happy to find a traditional Thai restaurant nearby. My husband and I dined in, but you could tell that they mostly do take out orders. We saw the delivery guy walk in and out several times throughout our meal with huge orders. The food quality was very good, but it took a long time. Again I attributed this to all of the to go orders they must have been receiving, but even our appetizers took forever. The spring rolls were plentiful and tasty. I appreciated that the tom yum soup with shrimp didn't have an up charge either. Lastly my pad kee mao was delicious and a good portion size. My only suggestion is they focus as much on their dine in customers as take out. We were the only two in the restaurant for most of our meal, and I just expected a little faster service.

Title: Aesthetics Over Flavor at Kips Bay's New Dim Sum Spot

Last night, a quick hop from work brought me and two colleagues to a new dim sum restaurant in Kips Bay. Eager for a nearby spot, we indulged in a variety of dishes, from the quintet-flavored "5 senses" soup dumplings to the playful Hello Kitty and piggy buns, not forgetting the lemon BBQ pork buns and drunken noodles with chicken.

Presentation was top-notch – each dish was a feast for the eyes and could easily dazzle any social media feed. The ingredients radiated quality, especially the charming Hello Kitty buns, which were as delightful on the palate as they were in appearance.

Sadly, the flavors didn't always match the visuals. The drunken noodles lacked heat and tipped unexpectedly towards sweetness, while the lemon BBQ pork buns were missing their citrus note. The soup dumplings were let down by their thick skin, and the piggy buns would have benefited from a longer cooking time for the red bean, which was too dry.

On the brighter side, service was stellar – attentive and swift. Though the experience was a mixed bag, the efforts in cuisine artistry and customer care were evident. Plus, there's a perk for social media-savvy patrons – a complimentary order of Hello Kitty buns with a Yelp check-in.

Final Verdict: Might swing by for another round of Hello Kitty buns and the service, but the kitchen needs to fine-tune flavors to match its Instagram credentials.

All about burgers, but doesn't deliver. When the main specialty of the restaurant is burgers, I was hoping to have a new experience. Sadly I was let down with the "Juicy Lucy". Ordered medium, served well-done. Dry and a bit chewy. They almost managed to have a pleasant flavor, however it was more bland than anything. Service was just lethargic, and even our drinks had to be returned. (I think the iced tea had gone bad or something?)I really hate to give a bad review however this place really let me down. Especially as a burger lover.

Love Love Love this place! .I have been coming to spotdessertbar for yearsss since it opened & I have to say Mango Tango is probably my absolute favorite item I have tried thus far! It's a Summer special: First ever dessert where they plate the whole dessert at the table as you watch! Available until the end of the month (end of August) it's comprised of Champagne mango, coconut sticky rice, buttered toasted bun, coconut ice cream sprinkled with crushed peanuts plated on banana leaves..The authenticity & uniqueness of this dish is mind blowingly delicious! I'm so glad I stepped out of my comfort zone items & tired this! I really do hope everyone gets a chance to try this! Everything was put together right in front & explained why these items go so well together. It's suggested to have a little bit of each item together to have the whole experience & it was one hell of a flavorful experience!Left me wanting more!

I feel as if Korean BBQ is either a hit or a miss but for the most part, this place was a hit. What can I say, it's always fun to order a lot of food and drinks and not feel guilty about it! I'm not 100% sure as to what meats my friend had ordered but they were all great and an adequate amount of each. They do grill it for you which is a plus and there's a lot of condiments that you can mix and match with the meats as well. For drinks we ordered the chum churum (of course), yobo, and a carafe of the melon makgeolli cocktail. Fair warning- the yobo is pretty strong (at least for me). All in all, this is a solid Korean BBQ spot but there are a lot of other options that are worth exploring nearby as well.

Title: Charming Vibes at the Rooftop Bar

I recently revisited this rooftop bar for the second time and was pleased to find it as lively as my initial visit. Despite the crowd, the new additional seating in the bar area was a welcome sight, perfect for patrons like myself who popped in for drinks rather than a meal.

The ambiance remained comfortably chill, creating a laid-back setting that's rare to come by in such popular spots. A highlight for any cocktail enthusiast, the array of options did not disappoint, with a full bar to cater to all preferences. Coupled with the old-school charm of the hotel, the bar has managed to carve out a unique identity.

Although I didn't experience it firsthand, the buzz about the burlesque show suggests it's an enticing feature worth checking out. Not to be overlooked, the elevator attendant's friendliness and humor added a delightful touch to the overall experience. If you're in search of a great time with a nostalgic twist, this rooftop bar is the place to be.

Title: A Satisfying Bite at Prova Pizzabar

During a trek to Coney Island, my companion and I stumbled upon a delightful find - the food hall next to Grand Station Stadium. Amidst the plethora of options, Prova Pizzabar caught our attention, promising a quick pizza and salad fix.

The decision-making was swift, our pizza slices soon crisping up in the oven. Although the caesar salad took a smidge longer to arrive - owing to its fresh preparation - it was worth the wait. Admittedly, my salad was rather crouton-heavy, but the flavors were impeccably balanced.

The meal left us stuffed and content, although the price point did feel slightly steep. In any case, Prova Pizzabar delivered a delicious and filling experience just when we needed it. Perfect for a pre-Coney Island adventure.

Title: Quick Bites and Custom Eats at Joju's Manhattan

Stopping by Joju's in Manhattan offers a refreshing experience for those in search of a quick and customized meal. The restaurant maintains an impressive level of cleanliness, ideal for both pick-up orders and dine-in options. The kiosks positioned right at the front streamline the ordering process, allowing patrons to effortlessly personalize their bowls with a variety of toppings and sauces.

The interior proves accommodating for small groups, with seating comfortably fitting parties of 2 or 4. Joju’s commitment to freshness is evident in every dish, serving up generous portions that boast a hearty foundation of perfectly cooked rice.

On the downside, the entrance does become a bottleneck at peak times, with the flow of incoming customers and those waiting to pick up their orders creating a bit of chaos. Additionally, while prices here are a tad steeper than their Elmhurst counterpart, they remain sensible for the location and the quality offered.

In conclusion, Joju's Manhattan outpost is a solid choice for those looking for a tasty, tailor-made meal in a clean and efficient setting.

One of the people i follow in instagram posted a picture of this place and a little comment that describe of what exactly was it and it really caught my attention. I started googling the place and went through the website and found it amazing the fact that this place once belong to Andy Warhol and also Jean  Michel Basquiat  and what i thought it was  more interesting about it is the concept of making a reservation. We got there and the deco and vibe was super cool, we ordered the bohemian omakese which is like the tasting of the month $100 pp and consisted of several things which i willPost a picture of what we had, we loved everything except the last tasting which was kamameshi however everything else made it for that one thing. Drinks were amaZing i ordered a cucumber one and  two others which i cant remember but everything was how we thought it would be. Service was excellent. If in ny make time and visit this gem
I ordered the gnocchi, and it was amazing!!! This place is kind of expensive, but the food is totally worth it. It didn't take long for the food to come out.

Very cute. Lots of musical stuff on the ceiling and walls. They were able to squeeze us in without a reservation tonight. Unfortunately the food just wasn't up to par with the surrounding restaurants. Ordered prosciutto pizza. Prosciutto felt grocery store bought- thick and not that great. Chicken Parmesan was the saddest thing ever. One thin small cutlet, see pic. And a sad spaghetti next to it that tasted like canned sauce. Maybe we ordered the wrong stuff, the salmon looked good, but what we got, we were disappointed.

When all the other brunch spots along this street were spilling over with people, this place was relatively quiet, until after 11am. The weather was perfect for sitting outside. The food isn't the prettiest, but it tastes good. I ordered the shakshuka ($15), which came with pita bread to dip. I have to say that this place gets mad props for hitting the right bread to sauce ratio. I was able to soak up all the delicious tomato sauce with the bread I was given, and I liked that it was crisp on the outside and warm. The shakshuka had two eggs, which was enough for me, though I think a real shakshuka should have way more eggs. The portion sizes are quite large. The sandwiches are super filling and can be shared with another person, and the French toast came as a mountain of toast and Nutella. You get a hearty meal, the food is decent, and you don't have to wait too long. The only thing is that as more people started coming in, I could tell the waitstaff was starting to get overwhelmed. The guy who had been so good at filling up our water jug stopped coming around, and they took forever to get us our check.

I recently visited a restaurant that had been on my radar for quite some time, and I'm thrilled to say it absolutely lived up to the hype. A word to the wise: reservations are a must, as this popular spot fills up quickly.

The highlights of my meal included the suon kho, priced at $16, which was a revelation of tender, fall-off-the-bone meat, bursting with flavor. Complementing this were the crisp wings for $15 and refreshing summer rolls for $10 – both of which were exceptional.

My dining companions were equally impressed with their meals, so the satisfaction was unanimous. Eagerly looking forward to my next visit, I've got my eye on exploring more of the menu. Additionally, their sister restaurant, known for BBQ, is next on my list.

Title: A Brunch to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

I can't help but extend a heartfelt thank you to [Restaurant Name] for a superb dining experience during their Bottomless Brunch. Thanks to a Pulsd voucher, which the restaurant graciously honored, our morning meal was nothing short of exceptional.

My boyfriend savored the Prosciutto, Honey & Watercress artisan pizza – a delectable combination where sweetness meets the perfect amount of salty goodness. He's already planning his next visit for the Bianca pizza. As for me, a previous Yelp reviewer led me to choose the Chicken & Waffles, a dish I can't commend enough. It's an exquisite balance of sweet, savory, and just a hint of spice – though not too spicy – which paired wonderfully with my unlimited Rosé.

The food quality was notable; the artisan pizza was expertly cooked, avoiding any char, and the meal portions were satisfying without being overly indulgent or greasy. The Amaro Coffee with its touch of liquor was another highlight, thoroughly enjoyed by my boyfriend.

Service was exemplary with courteous servers eager to answer our queries and allowing us to dine at a leisurely pace. This restaurant definitely warrants return visits to explore the rest of their tantalizing menu.

One small note for future patrons, the Pulsd offer includes beer, but the restaurant no longer serves it. Hopefully, this will be updated soon. Nonetheless, the dining experience remains a must-try.

Title: A True Taco Triumph at Los Tacos No. 1

If there's a taco temple in New York City, it must be Los Tacos No. 1. As someone who considers themselves a taco aficionado, I felt compelled to bring my friends to this spot not once, not twice, but thrice during our NYC adventure. Why? Because Los Tacos No. 1 crafts what might just be the pinnacle of taco perfection.

Their adobada and carne asada tacos are the stuff of dreams, boldly flavorful and expertly prepared. Yes, you'll likely encounter a line, but every savory bite proves that the wait is not just worthwhile but necessary for any true taco lover.

I've sampled my fair share of this Mexican staple across the globe, but Los Tacos No. 1 stands out as the best. It's the reason my next trip to the Big Apple can't come soon enough. It's not hyperbole to say that I am, without a doubt, their number one fan.

Despite the puzzling low ratings I had seen online for this neighborhood cafe, my experience was nothing short of delightful. It might be that the service has been a past issue for some, but it certainly didn't deter me from enjoying my visit. The standout was the Chipotle Chicken Panini, which arrived swiftly and was absolutely delicious. Having the option to pair it with chips or a salad is a thoughtful touch. Additionally, the outdoor seating adds to the charm of this great local gem. Its convenient proximity to my home is the cherry on top, ensuring that I'll be returning often to this underrated spot.

Decent place for brunch. Our server was attentive and constantly refilled our waters. The seating is spread out, which is nice since a lot of other brunch places are way too cramped.I liked the spicy kale salad (it's only mildly spicy) and thesmoked salmon tasted as expected and was filling. Broccolini came with way too much sauce, so I'd probably skip that next time. Overall, a nice spot to catch up with friends with the typical brunch food.

The Tsukemen Dipping Broth is Thin!I remember coming to Totto several years ago for their yakitori, which I absolutely loved.  Totto's ramen has won a lot of praise, so I wanted to check it out.  It was hard choosing between the tsukemen and the spicy niboshi--both styles are rare in the US--but ultimately I went with tsukemen.The tsukemen had wasn't bad, but it fell short of my expectations.  The dipping broth was a chicken paitan base with katsuobushi flavors mixed in, but it was rather thin for tsukemen and not puncy.  Chashu were tight coils of pork belly that were prepared ahead, put in the fridge, and then sliced cold, with just a quick blast from an Iwatani torch.  There decent but could've been better.  Noodles were thick and chewy, as they were supposed to.  Plenty of menma but unpickled, egg was fine but left in the pot a bit too long as parts of the yolk were not gelatinous by flaky.Overall, a decent bowl of ramen but not a great one.  Some extra points for the waitstaff, with whom I chatted with in Japanese when she saw me pull out my camera.  Also the chef was kind enough to oblige my request for the spicy niboshi broth ($5).  That too was lacking in flavor.  If they fix their broth, they could be a much better bowl.

Title: Disappointing Dining Experience Despite Stellar Service

My visit to the restaurant started on a high note with exceptional service from a friendly and attentive waitress, earning a solid five-star rating in that department. Unfortunately, the food and drinks failed to match the quality of the service. Both the individual sangria and the pitcher shared with my friend were lackluster, tasting diluted and failing to impress.

I opted for the Tios chicken sandwich, which held the promise of flavorful aioli but was ultimately let down by its dryness. Similarly, my friend's veggie salad, featuring arugula and avocado, was a dismal offering that barely passed as a dish, let alone a satisfying meal.

Considering the prices, I expected much more from my dining experience. Although the service was exemplary, it couldn't compensate for the overall disappointment felt from the mediocre drinks and unsatisfying food. In all honesty, I can't recommend this place and left feeling shortchanged.

Probably the only place to get fresh roasted pig (hangs in the window) with crispy skin. Only $11 per pound and chopped to your liking. The place is too small to really enjoy sitting and keep in mind that there are separate menus for take out and eat-in. One this I don't like is the food is cooked in the basement and sent up on a dumbwaiter so you don't really get to see your food being prepped or prepared, not even a glance. The pork is what gets my high rating!

Cool atmosphere, nice bar, food was average. Decent beer selection. Probably a better spot for drinks and snacks, especially when the weather is nice and you can hang outside. The smoked wings weren't great, not a great flavor on the sauce. The brisket was good, but not a huge portion. Mac N Cheese was good, but pretty average. All in all, most likely a one and done visit.

Great homemade Italian food set in a classic "you can only find in NYC" type of way.
