When you step into the restaurant, it's almost like you travel back in time - the walls are covered with pictures / old newspaper articles with Emilio & co. and famous visitors from back in their day (in one corner alone I saw pics with a young Johnny Depp, younger Bradley Cooper + very young Christopher Walken). Pretty cool.SETTING: we came for a very early dinner to avoid the lines around 5:30pm on a Saturday and were seated promptly in the first room which has a cozy and old-school feel. Little chandeliers hang from the ceilings. Overall the effect is classic. FOOD: for appetizers we ordered the burrata and fried calamari special. The burrata was perfectly creamy on the inside and served with roasted peppers which cut down the creaminess of the burrata. The prosciutto was tasty as well. The fried calamari we could have done without. It was served with the best tomato sauce I've ever had. But if ordering for two I think the burrata was a substantial enoportion. For pasta we ordered the spaghetti with meatballs and ravioli with ricotta cheese. Both were cooked perfectly al dente. The meatballs were the best meatballs I've ever had (yes that's two for two bests here). I can't accurately describe how good it was but just trust me and try it (esp if you like meatballs). The ravioli was also perfect and I really regret I couldn't finish it all (was too stuffed).VERDICT: I don't know how worth it it'd be to wait in line for hours and hours here. At the end of the day it is just classic good Italian food. But if you can manage to get here at a time to avoid the wait, it's well worth the visit ! I will be back for more meatballs and to try their bolognese!

Sunday for brunch 2pm no wait not crowded. It did take a second for me to be acknowledged standing at the door it would have been nice for someone to just greet and say i'd be serviced shortly. I sat at the bar and ate. I ordered brunch food and a mimosa and an arugula salad to-go. Their balsamic dressing is sooo good omg. Everything tasted delicious ! My service was okay (it wasn't bad it just wasn't amazing) I actually received more attention from the head chef as the kitchen was open concept. He was super polite and nice! I would go back here again.

Our family enjoyed the Brussel sprouts and French toast. The French toast comes with three huge pieces of bread, so it's easily shareable. The salmon eggs benedict on the other hand was disappointing because the English muffin wasn't toasted at all. It just crumbled and got soggy under the salmon and hollandaise sauce. I would pass on this dish.I don't think this brunch here was any better than brunches I've had elsewhere.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a vegan sushi spot in NYC, and I was blown away by the experience. The sushi rolls and dumplings were nothing short of excellent, each bite bursting with flavor and creativity. The menu offered an array of tantalizing options, and I found myself wishing for a larger appetite to try more. This restaurant is a gem for anyone seeking delicious plant-based sushi, and I already envy the locals who can indulge in these culinary delights on a regular basis. If you're in the city, do not miss out on this fantastic dining experience.

Do I ever know what the menu says? No. Is that going to stop me from ordering? NOPE! Lupa is undeniably one of the best Roman/Italian restaurants on the lower west side of NYC. I love the ambiance of Lupa while sipping wine and enjoying my meal. The pasta is as fresh as can be, not overcooked, perfectly al dente.

Came here for dinner with a group of my friends. We were seated almost immediately. The staff was so nice & accommodating. Our water cups were always being refilled and the drinks were brought out very quickly. Our waitress gave us great advice on what to order. The food was delicious. Would definitely be back in the near future

Title: A Culinary Jewel Amidst the Concrete Jungle: Au Cheval Diner

Nestled in the bustling terrain of the city, Au Cheval might just challenge your burger benchmarks. It's not just about the hype; it delivers a trifecta of splendid atmosphere, exemplary taste, and attentive service, albeit patience is a virtue you'll need in abundance to relish the experience.

While 4 Charles Prime might share the same burger DNA, it's more a canvas for their rib tip sandwich. Au Cheval, on the other hand, boldly claims the burger crown and with good reason. The flavors are robust, the ingredients high-quality, and every bite justifies the fanfare.

An underground cocktail bar provides solace if the main arena is off-limits, with delectable morsels that shouldn't be overlooked. The vibe? Unwaveringly great, matched only by the culinary delights that await.

However, perfect it's not. Expect your wallet to feel a tad lighter in this "diner" setting – the price point leans toward upscale. And then there's the wait – an endeavor not for the faint-hearted. The no-reservation policy, in a city that never pauses, is a glitch in the system. New Yorkers, known for their hustle, can't afford to lose hours to a waiting game that feels suspiciously like an in-person reservation queue.

If Au Cheval reconsiders this stance, embracing a system more tuned to the New York pace of life, it would elevate from frustratingly good to outstanding. Until such a change, prepare for a tussle with time for a taste of their much-lauded offerings.

Rating: With a fix to the reservation policy, this place could soar to a solid 4 out of 5 stars.

This was good, although not anywhere near best in class in NYC, in my opinion. First visit, I got the prime rib, and my wife got the Kobe burger, both of which were good, but don't stand up to the equivalents at other similarly-priced places (eg Keens). We really liked the chocolate cake for dessert. Good food and huge portions all around, but not one that I'll feel a great need to run back to.

Title: Mixed Feelings on a Convenient Spot

I recently dined at a local Mexican restaurant, lured in by the tantalizing aroma and cool vibe. The location was perfect for a quick meet-up with a friend craving Mexican food near his office. The online reviews had given me a heads-up, but the place still beckoned.

We shared a variety of dishes, including the fried calamari, elote corn, and short rib tacos. The standout was definitely the calamari; crispy and flavorful, it was the highlight of the meal, though I found its $17 price tag a bit steep. The elote, while tasty, didn't live up to its $10 cost, leaving me expecting more from what should have been a standout side dish. The short rib tacos were enjoyable but were let down by a single-layer tortilla that didn't hold up, combined with a rather modest portion size that didn't justify the expense. The accompanying rice had a nice flavor profile, though the beans erred on the side of too salty.

My caipirinha was a win, well-crafted and potent - a saving grace amidst the culinary ups and downs. While some of the sizzling plates at neighboring tables seemed promising, I'm hesitant about a return visit. My friend, more forgiving, might come back, but without a significant draw, I'm likely to pass - unless, of course, the calamari drops a few dollars.

Title: A Charming Post-Brunch Experience

I recently visited a delightful spot which, unfortunately, had closed its kitchen for brunch after 3 pm. However, the cafe area saved the day with its welcoming ambience. We nestled into a very cozy corner, embraced by the tranquil and tastefully French chic decor, and whiled away the time from brunch until dinner with coffee, drinks, and enjoyable conversation.

For my meal, I opted for a simple offering of a cheeseburger, sans salad, paired with coffee. My friend indulged in a hot whisky, which came with a slightly premium price tag of $16. The total bill came to $120, leading to my share being $60 for just a burger and coffee.

Admittedly, the price point seemed steep for what was on our table. Yet, despite the cost, I left without a complaint. The experience—the setting, the company, and the atmosphere—added value that justified the expense. Sometimes, it's not just about the food but the overall encounter, and in this instance, it was worth every penny.

Title: Southern Delights Shine at Sylvia's

If you've heard the buzz around Sylvia's, let me confirm it's all true. This Harlem gem serves up soul food so good you'll savor every bite. Start with their cornbread—it arrives hot from the oven with delightfully crispy edges, setting the stage for the feast ahead.

The star here is unquestionably the fried fare. The breading on the chicken, shrimp, and catfish crackles with each bite, and my top tip is to opt for fried over smothered to truly appreciate the crunch. While the smothered dishes are tasty, they pale in comparison to their fried counterparts.

I indulged in the seafood combo featuring both fried catfish and shrimp, and though the shrimp outshone the catfish with its superior flavor, I was left craving more than the scant three pieces included.

As for the sides, don't miss the mac and cheese—it's the epitome of comfort in a cheesy, heartwarming portion. The candied yams are another highlight, perfectly soft and sweet. The collard greens might not steal the show, but they're a solid accompaniment nonetheless.

Overall, Sylvia's is a Harlem must-visit, especially for fried food aficionados. Remember, when in doubt, go for the mac and cheese!

My recent foray to this spot, prompted by a friend's post, was a pleasant surprise. The ambiance was welcoming with service to match—both friendly and swift. A unique offering caught our eye: alcoholic ramen, which turned out to be an interesting twist on the dining experience.

For our meal, we settled on the tonkatsu and shoyu ramen, accompanied by a Sapporo and the intriguing matcha beer. As a matcha aficionado, I couldn't resist trying the latter, though it veered from expectations. Be warned, this concoction is on the bitter side—the matcha's presence manifested mostly in a bitter aftertaste, and sweetness was notably absent. It wasn't to my taste, though that's purely subjective and doesn't detract from my overall impression.

The ramen, while flavorful, faltered in presentation. Unlike other establishments that serve up visually appealing bowls, here the ingredients were submerged, potentially alluding to a less artisanal origin—though it's purely speculative. It wasn't a dealbreaker, as the taste was satisfactory, but a little attention to presentation could enhance the ramen's appeal significantly.

Was craving rice noodle rolls and happened to see that this place had recently opened close to where I was so I decided to stop by. The line to order was super quick, but we definitely waited for our food for quite some time (at least 10-15 minutes though it felt longer). Each rice roll is made to order so it wasn't a surprise that it would take that long. We got a large order of the shrimp rice roll. The rice noodle part was perfectly soft and chewy at the same time. The shrimp was very fresh and not tough. Next time, I'll definitely consider adding the eggs or corn to my order (honestly, I was confused by all the add-ins bit so I just went plain). Because my sister has a peanut allergy, we got the sweet sauce with sesame which was a nice added touch. However, it seemed that many people actually got it plain (maybe they have it with the soy sauce they also give?). The people working were also friendly. Overall, very delicious and definitely looking forward to going back.

This was a quick, last-minute lunch for my boyfriend and I. We were walking back to our car and decided to stop in, this was one of the first ramen places we saw around us. We were seated immediately and the place was packed for about 2:30pm on a Tuesday! We shared the KoKu ramen and a Thai bubble tea ($15 credit card minimum)! The ramen was delicious ! We got medium spice. This was plenty to fill us both up for about 2.5 hours. The tea was nothing special, we ordered it just to reach the minimum. We got the $10 lunch special price and you must pay at least $15 on a cc. Would come again for a lunch ramen!

I'm still captivated by the charm of this enchanting breakfast spot! It has truly elevated my expectations for what breakfast can be, blending exquisite French cuisine, a delightful atmosphere, and warm hospitality. Despite my initial concern about a possible crowd, the spacious seating was a pleasant surprise, allowing for a choice spot without delay. Service was prompt, with aromatic coffees gracing our table almost immediately—what a refreshing way to kickstart the morning! I find myself longing for a return visit to relive that perfect start to the day.
I was here again recently and had the cobia el pastor, herb guacamole, razor clam tostada, artic char, and the grey sole.  Amazing.  Drinks were perfect also.

Hmm...no. I don't understand the hype of this place: customer service is great but food falls flat. My chicken sandwich took over 15 min to be prepared and when it came out the bun was icy cold. It was also drenched with a spicy mayo that overpowered the flavor of the chicken. I scraped off the mayo and skipped the bun to make the chicken edible. On the plus side, the french fries are super crispy and tasty. And it's conveniently located on the 32nd street food mall, so everyone in your party can grab what they like.

A group of us came for a birthday celebration and we are so glad we did. The ambiance is modern, classy and intimate. The service was great and the food is just amazing. We shared 6-8 plates and opted for all vegan. There are some items that are not vegan but they can make it vegan. For example, the dosa we chose came with avocado, sprouted greens and cashew based yogurt. The lettuce avocado cups were so flavorful too. The pasta bolognese was "meaty" and perfectly flavored. The kimchee stir fried brown rice was also interesting and tasty. We also asked for hot sauce and it was a homemade habanero style sauce which was amazing. They also had rock sea salt on the table in case you wanted to sprinkle it on your foods. For dessert we got the coconut custard with seasonal fruits (gooseberries, pears and pomegranate). I definitely recommend making reservations. Great for date nite or with a group of friends.

I visited this restaurant on a Wednesday evening around 7:30 pm and found the place comfortably open for seating. The interior struck a nice chord for a dinner catch-up with its great atmosphere. Service didn't disappoint, as the staff was attentive, making sure we were well-taken care of with a never-empty water cup.

On to the food, we sampled three dishes, but unfortunately, the quality didn't quite match their steep prices. The Crispy Zucchini, a 3/5, was more bread crumb than vegetable and felt excessively oily, despite a bountiful portion. The Spaghetti and Meatballs also earned a 3/5, with the highlight being the well-textured meatballs, though the pasta was overdone, and the tomato sauce lacked freshness. Lastly, the Penne Shrimp, at 2/5, was a letdown with its overwhelming richness and an unbalanced heavy cheese presence, which rendered it too intense to finish, despite the liberal inclusion of chopped shrimp. While the ambiance and service were spot-on, the value for money on the culinary side fell short.

Venturing out on a rainy Sunday morning, my patience was rewarded at a quaint and cozy brunch spot that didn't keep me waiting for too long. The highlight of my meal was the vibrant Green Shakshuka, which surprised me with its depth of flavor, though it did become challenging to eat without the accompanying toast.

My foray into the House Cured Duck Bacon was an absolute delight. The balance of ingredients in the sandwich made it a standout and my favorite among the dishes. While the Rosewater Waffle concept intrigued me, it fell short on execution with its unfortunate sogginess; a crispier bite would have done wonders. Yet the unique touch of honey syrup added a pleasant note to the experience.

Service was commendable throughout, leaving me with a sense of appreciation. A sincere 'thank you' to the team for a memorable brunch!

Title: A Gem of Freshness and Flavor at an Unbeatable Price!

I must express my adoration for this restaurant right off the bat! The interior captivated me with its prettiness and generous space. But let's dive into the main event - the food. The salmon sashimi was a standout, boasting remarkable freshness that tantalized my taste buds. Not only was the quality top-notch, but the quantity was also generous, especially considering the price.

The other sushi rolls didn't lag behind, each one packing a punch of flavor that kept me reaching for more. Speaking of surprises, the affordability of this place is simply incredible - quality food that won't break the bank!

The beverages were another highlight, with the taro and regular bubble teas being absolutely splendid. Each sip came with the delightful chew of soft, delicious tapioca, pairing perfectly with my meal.

Even the kara-age (fried chicken) didn't disappoint, serving up a decently good experience.

In conclusion, my taste buds are already yearning for a return visit. For anyone looking for fresh, delicious fare at great prices, this is surely a spot you'll want to frequent!

Wow so after fighting a bout of food poisoning for several days after eating at another popular Brazilian steak house (cough cough churrascaria plataforma) I was .. turned off by the concept. I decided to try out Fogo since they were always emailing these amazing deals. The deal in particular was the Fogo Restaurant Month, $39.99 for some basic cuts of meats including the market table. What a deal! I ended up paying $50 per person including tip and tax for a party of 8. I celebrated my graduation here and making reservations was very easy, I used open table. The food itself was definitely better quality compared to Plataforma, although we weren't getting all the cuts of meat, there were still plenty of options. My favorites were the chicken, all of the sirloins and the bacon wrapped steak. Did I mention they also give you unlimited mash potatoes and cheesy bread slides? YES PLEASE. Also, I went over to the cold salad bar and discovered... sugar pepper bacon. What other restaurant serves that? I took a plateful and took it back to my table where it was devoured in seconds. The way you get your food at Fogo, is by flipping your card to either the red or green side. Then the meat cutters will descend upon your table and bless you with a generous portion. This is an AYCE so be prepared to loosen up your pants or just wear stretchy clothes. My server was amazing and kept refilling our waters, and our sides. Fogo definitely changed my mind about Brazilian steak houses and this will be the spot where I recommend all my friends.

I love their cumin lamb noodles. They get the right balance of spice of cumin and pepper and the lamb is always soft and tender. I didn't love their lamb soup since it was a little oily to me. I can't say I enjoyed the entire bowl but a few bites were enjoyable!

The Tang is a great addition to the neighborhood. It's a great place for a casual date in the neighborhood and also for small groups. My favorites are the pineapple fried rice (served in real pineapple), and roasted eggplant. I thought the braised pork knuckle (rice dish) was too fatty (like 80%). Not sure if that's what it's supposed to be, but that was not my personal favorite. Everything else was good. I'm so glad that they finally started the delivery service.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Pizza Lovers near West 4th

Nestled just a stone's throw from the subway, this charming little pizzeria is a delightful find for anyone in the West 4th area with pizza cravings. The eatery boasts a minimalistic charm and a straightforward menu that's as easy on the eyes as the prices are on your wallet. What's particularly impressive is their inclusive selection of slices, catering to vegans and gluten-free preferences alike.

I opted for the tantalizing white slice, which did not disappoint. It struck the perfect balance between hearty flavor and a non-greasy texture, making for a satisfyingly light meal. The outdoor chalkboard with combo offerings is a thoughtful touch, adding to the welcoming ambiance of the place.

Chatting with Sagar, the friendly face behind the counter, I learned they've only been serving for five months—a surprise, given the establishment's apparent ease in delivering quality fare. If you're around West 4th and hunger pangs hit, do yourself a favor and drop by this spot for a slice that's sure to hit the spot. Highly recommended!

Popped in for the bottomless brunch on Sunday which was cool. The DJ was rocking.... mixing new w/old of r&b, hip hop & reggae. With the bottomless deal you choose your entree & get unlimited mimosas for an hour for $30. I went with the salmon. The salmon was a tad over cooked, the veggies & lettuce that accompanied it were both good. BUT the portion was so small. Luckily my friend and I started with guacamole & chips *which was nothing fantastic* because I surely would've still been hungry. The saving grace was the mimosa. Perfect balance of champagne & juice. The service was good, my waitress in addition to others continued to check on us. Next time I'll give happy hour a try!

Upon stepping into this charming little eatery, I immediately felt as though I had been transported to an authentic Italian hole-in-the-wall – rustic and brimming with character.

The meal commenced with a delightful bruschetta combo, allowing for a bit of culinary creativity. The standout spread was the matarocco – a triumph of umami from ripe tomatoes that married beautifully with the crusty bread without creating any sogginess.

The spaghetti alla vongole veraci was a masterclass in simplicity, where lightness in oil paved the way for the freshness of the clams to take center stage, all while the pasta maintained the quintessential al dente bite.

Another highlight was the tagliatelle al ragu bolognese con tartufo. The ragu was a rich tapestry of fine, meaty flavors that complemented the tender pasta, and the truffle added a delicate, aromatic touch without overpowering the senses.

The pizza primavera was a celebration of textures and flavors, with prosciutto laid generously atop, mozzarella stretching perfectly to create an indulgent pull, and the fresh arugula and cherry tomatoes adding a contrasting earthy freshness.

Commendations also go to the bread service; freshly sliced with air pockets that joyfully soaked up the olive oil and balsamic provided at the table. The service was attentive and welcoming throughout, enhancing the overall dining experience.

To top it off, the wine list was notably reasonable, allowing for a delightful pairing without undue expense.

In summary, this eatery strikes a splendid balance between rustic charm and culinary excellence, serving up Italian classics that both comfort and delight.

The dumplings (mandoo) being made at the front of the restaurant and by the window, lured me in. Colorful green and white dough stuffed and manipulated into dumplings intrigued me and I knew I had to try.I love K-town and most restaurants are usually busy and packed with a lot of activity taking place. I was lucky to get a table for lunch at the average sized Mandoo and was in the mood for soup.Aside from their dumplings, they also serve traditional Korean fare. Ramen soup was my selection since I was getting through a cold. The spicy mandoo ramen soup offered vegetarian and non vegetarian options. In addition to ramen noodles, the soup included two mandoo dumplings. The chance to try them. My selection was vegetarian and shortly after placing my order, the soup arrived.At $10, it was a hearty bowl of soup with a robust, spicy broth, fresh wavy noodles, vegetables and dumplings. I really liked it.I might be in the minority, but I was not wowed by the dumplings. The dough was too thick for my liking and the filling wasn't that flavorful. But overall, I enjoyed my soup I would return.

Title: A Burger to Remember at a Hip Haven

Walking into this restaurant, you're immediately enveloped by a vibe that's both relaxed and effortlessly hip. The staff greet you with genuine warmth, setting the stage for an exceptional dining experience.

As for the food – specifically, the burger – it's nothing short of transformative. Juicy, flavorful, and masterfully cooked, it's a contender for the best burger I've ever had. Just thinking about it makes my mouth water. The desire to return daily is a testament to its deliciousness. Pure joy, indeed. If you're in search of a culinary delight served with stellar hospitality, this is your spot.

Michelin 1* Korean fusionThere is only one choice for vegetarians, nice presentation, good flavor but not that memorableGochu was nice and flavorful B&B edamame was THE BEST! The edamame was coated in beyond delicious glaze, spicy but yet not hot, amazing! For dessert they only had Oishii berry composed of 3 special berries, nothing else, no sorbet or glaze, just 3 berries for $9. We passed. The service was on pointMake reservations because we waited 1.5 hr! Solid 4*

During a recent lunch visit to this restaurant, I found the seating process quick and hassle-free. The sparkling water and tea served were quite satisfactory. The Hot & Sour soup caught my attention, especially with the addition of their giant, flavorful noodles – a delightful touch that amplified the taste when coupled with an extra sauce.

Our shared dishes included a Filet mignon with veggies and Xo prawns. The filet mignon was a hit, with its savory meat complemented by fresh broccoli. The Xo prawns, although fried, managed to impress with their size and taste. Combining these with some brown rice resulted in a fulfilling meal without overindulgence.

The ambiance of the restaurant was characterized by a spacious layout and simple decor, which provided a comfortable dining experience. Service was efficient and attentive. While the prices may be considered steep for Chinese cuisine, they aren't exorbitant and the food quality justifies giving this place a try.

WHERE THE WILD THINGS ARE...CHEAP. DELICIOUS. GREAT SERVICE. QUALITY. all those words above... altogether...it's pretty uncommon in Chinatown, but i'm blessed to have this spot; as opposed to the juggernauts of dim sum in this area. there have been times where i had to cough up $50 during Yum-Cha time and let me tell you... it doesn't make me happy. don't wait around at the big-dogs like Jing Fong, Golden Unicorn and Tim Ho Wan. i guarantee you that this is a hidden gem in Chinatown for tea and dim sum. go for the Pineapple BBQ Pork Buns, Shrimp Stuffed Eggplants, Daan Taat (egg tart), Har Gao (Shrimp Dumplings) and Snow Pea Leaf and Shrimp Dumplings. the service is top notch and the ladies aren't shouting in your face and copping attitude like some banquets... but not here! i love that i walk out of here spending only $12. now that's what i call, "tea time". DON'T GET RIPPED OFF!

Title: Sake Aficionado's Paradise with a Price

If your passion for sake knows no bounds, this restaurant is a must-visit destination. The sake selection is beyond extraordinary, a true connoisseur's dream. However, a word to the wise—some of these delectable sakes come with a hefty price tag. But with a judicious choice, one can indulge in a variety of sakes without the fear of an empty wallet.

The food menu may remind you of an izakaya, primarily focused on small, flavorful appetizers perfect for pairing with your drink. Each dish, while in the category of munchies, is crafted to a high standard, enhancing a convivial evening of nibbling and sipping.

While I have a slight preference for their Sakagura East location—owing to its communal bar vibe—if you find yourself near Grand Central, the convenience and allure of this spot are undeniable. Whether it's for the impressive sake or the delightful bites, it's surely worth a visit.

I recently dined at this charming restaurant and opted for the chicken over rice. To my delight, the dish was outstanding, with flavors that simply amazed me. The service matched the quality of the food, ensuring a pleasant experience throughout the meal. I was pleasantly surprised by the portion size, which was generous enough to share with a friend. Overall, this place is a fantastic find that I would highly recommend.

Title: Late-Night Ramen Delight at Ichiran

After a grueling flight that touched down at JFK at 10 PM, I found solace a mere 8-minute walk away from my hotel at Ichiran, open until the late hours. By 11 PM, I was comfortably seated in a unique dining setup — individual stalls designed to minimize distractions and maximize the culinary experience.

Ichiran's efficient ordering system ensures that if you arrive knowing what you want, you'll be relishing your dish without delay. The setup encourages diners to disconnect and immerse themselves in the moment, which is all about the ramen. Staff interactions are minimal, yet service remains top-notch.

Giving in to my cravings, I indulged in the extra noods option. It was absolutely worth it — a heavenly treat after the day's journey and New York's chilly embrace. Ichiran delivered a delightfully satisfying bowl of ramen that's left a lasting impression. I am eagerly looking forward to my next visit!

Imagine waking up in New York City and getting Pizza. And. It just any pizza, New York pizza. It's an amazing experience all on its own. Now imagine our surprise when our friend took us to Joe's Pizza? We were so geeked! Could we afford going to such a legendary place? How were the prices gonna be intense? Did we need suit and tie? Joe's Pizza is a really homey and welcoming Pizza parlor. You come as is, you pay for a slice about the same price as other places, and enjoy the greatness that is New York style pizza! Huge hot pieces, full of flavor, and gives you the true New York pizza experience. The one really cool thing besides the magnificent triangular goodness. We saw the owner himself was  throwing down, making sure everyone got the same original Joe's piece of pizza! You want authentic New York pizza, this is New York pizza!

A friend and I came in on a Friday night with a 6 pm reservation, but it didn't seem too packed yet. To start, we had the agedashi tofu, which I thought was good, but nothing too special. My friend loved it though. For my entree, I went with the assorted sushi and sashimi ($38). This came with 9 pieces of sashimi, 6 pieces of sushi, 3 pieces of a sushi roll, and 2 of those egg things (which I could have done without). It would have been nice if they explained each fish to us but they kind of just left the dishes on our table, and walked away before we even had a chance to ask for anything else. Everything was good though. I really liked the tuna (which is usually my fave), the uni, and the salmon - plus the fact that it was very lightly seared.It's a little pricier than other sushi restaurants of similar quality, but worth it for a once in a while splurge. Maybe next time I'll try their early bird special for $30, which includes sashimi, sushi, soba, and dessert (also avail on Fridays!)

I really enjoyed the delivery from this restaurant. The order came quickly and it tasted fresh. I got the 3 roll lunch special with a shrimp tempura roll, sweet potato roll and California roll. I enjoyed all of them. It also came with miso soup, which tasted great, and was not too salty like other ones I've had. I would recommend this restaurant.

(212) Boiling Point. You get the deal. OHMAHGAWSH. I can't stop thinking about this place since I came here. I was so impressed by the nautical decor. But the foooddd. Oooh gosh. The food was amazing. Apps: Soft Shell Crab: anytime this is in season I get it. Served with Cajun fries. The crab is battered and the meat is ever so tender. 5/5. The Boil: Shrimp and Crawfish. GET ALL THE SEASONINGS MIXED TOGETHER. That is the best combo. All that garlic and lemon and old bay just marries into a trifecta of flavor. The shrimp are the stars but crawfish add a nice kick. The gloves are the same that the hospitals use which I find hilarious. It's quality grade folks. Haha. You get a cute bib. And in order to protect your clothes as you gobble that sauce: use it.

Title: A Peruvian Delight on the Upper West Side

Last Friday night's supper at Pio Pio on the Upper West Side delivered a cozy yet vibrant dining experience that seemed to resonate with all patrons in the warmly lit space. The restaurant's ambiance, with its expansive floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking Amsterdam Avenue, provided a welcoming backdrop to our meal.

Shortly after ordering the Matador Combo, we were amazed at the speed and presentation of the feast that followed. Aromatic roasted chicken paired with a generous portion of yellow rice and beans, sweet plantains, crispy french fries with savory little sausages, and a fresh salad accented with ripe tomatoes and creamy avocado slices adorned our table draped in white linen.

Each bite was enhanced by a spoonful of the unforgettable creamy green sauce, elevating the flavors to new heights. Priced at an unbelievable $39, the Matador Combo was not only a culinary journey through Peru but also an exceptional value. Pio Pio's take on Peruvian cuisine is undoubtedly a gem on the UWS, offering a deliciously satisfying experience without breaking the bank.

I recently visited this restaurant for a company dinner and was initially impressed by the ambiance and the fantastic selection of 90s R&B music. While the atmosphere was inviting, the food and service unfortunately did not match up. The service was notably slow, especially since the venue wasn't crowded, taking an excessive 35 minutes just to place our main course orders.

Surprisingly, they had already run out of steak at 6:30 pm, which prompted me to choose the burger with an added fried egg. While the deviled eggs and mussels were the highlights, the burger itself was a letdown; it arrived charred and over-salted, with the fried egg overdone and unappealing. The saving grace were the fries, which were quite good.

Despite my appetite leading me to eat most of the burger, it was an unsatisfying experience overall. The drinks, particularly the Louisiana, were enjoyable, but when it comes to food, there's considerable room for improvement.

Tang hotpot embodies everything traditional, authentic, and delicious. I came here with my friend around noon on Sunday and we were greeted with warm welcomes the moment we walked through the door. The host was so polite and instantly seated us. I recommend making a reservation ahead of time to make the experience more seamless. We were seated in the back, and this gave me the chance to get a good look at the overall place. The decorations are so dainty and elegant. There are beautiful light fixtures hanging from the ceilings. There is enough privacy between each table so you don't feel crammed. Food: If you're looking for the typical AYCE experience, this is definitely not your place. But if you are looking for quality, well proportioned, and mind blowing hot pot ingredients then this is totally your spot. We got the yuan yang half and half pot, the Sichuan spicy broth was so flavorful. The other half was bone soup, super creamy and perfect for cooking veggies. For dipping, we went with the sesame oil and added everything else in with it (vinegar, garlic, cilantro, green onion). Love the diy style for the dips. For appetizer we tried the deep fried pork belly, a Sichuan specialty. Quite authentic I must say! We ordered the deluxe combo for 2. It came just with about everything on the menu. It includes a veggies platter, seafood, and assorted sliced meats. Everything was top notch quality!!! We added on frozen tofu and tripe - so bomb. We ordered cocktails, the lychee sake was unbelievable. It almost tasted like juice! The pineapple mimosa was fantastic and refreshing. Do not skip out on dessert!!! The black sesame and taro ice creams are the cherry on top to this meal. Nothing too sweet or artificial. They're very generous and provide 2 scoops per cup. Do not forget to try this!! Price: $80 for the platter, enough to feed two, but I would recommend adding on 1 or 2 items just to make sure you walk away completely full. Cocktails are around $10-13. Add on veggies are on the more affordable side. If you're looking to order a serving of premium beeef, it can go all the way up to $65. Amazing team of servers, great ambiance, and the best hot pot I've had in nyc! Must visit!!

I had seen these restaurants around the city and decided to finally give it a try today. It was busy but they have order kiosks which made ordering my food quick. Around the restaurant there are cute, hip sayings on the wall and furniture. In about 5 minutes, I got my order. I chose to dine-in because although it was packed, seating constantly opened up. I ordered: the classic burger and air fry sweet potato fries. I loved the sweet potato fries. That was my first time eating anything air fried and it lives up to the hype of air frying your food. The classic burger was smaller than what I had imagined it to be. However, the beet ketchup was unexpectedly delicious. I loved the pickles. The patty was also delightful. I did mention that the burger was smaller than what I expected it to be (considering the price) but I think there is good reason behind that. I would recommend this to anyone who can be quickly filled up on a vegan diet. Unfortunately, I am not easily filled up so I left the restaurant still kind of hungry. This does not mean I do not recommend you to try it. Definitely try it if you are feeling adventurous.

The food wasn't bad. Highlights were the fish with grilled vegetables, the dumplings, and the beef stroganoff. The fish was cooked perfectly. The sauce for the stroganoff was excellent but it was so buttery, we could only have so much of it. The other appetizers were meh. I think I was mostly put off just by how loud it was and how slow the service was but otherwise the food wasn't bad - just not good enough for me to come back and tolerate the noise and slow service. Maybe cool to come and try once for the live music but definitely don't bring a first date here unless you plan on shouting at each other just to hear each other.

I love this arepa. (See pic!) They included the wrong sauce in our delivery order, but delicious in any case.(But note the photo- the sandwich looks to be HALF the size in actually- vs the website photo...)

Title: A Slip in Standards at Luke's

I've had the pleasure of dining at Luke's on a few occasions, both in NYC and Las Vegas, with delightful experiences to reminisce on. However, my latest visit to their establishment over the weekend left much to be desired.

The newest addition to their menu, the jumbo lobster roll with truffle butter, caught my eye. While the truffle butter was a hit with me, my girlfriend found the aroma less than appealing. The primary letdown, though, was the lobster itself. It lacked the anticipated sweetness and was overwhelmed by an excess of claw meat, which neither of us particularly appreciate for its taste and texture.

On a brighter note, the lobster bisque that came with my combo was a redeeming feature, outshining the lackluster roll. Given my previous experiences, I hope this visit was merely an off day and not an indication of a downward trend.

Title: A Theatrical Treat: Italian Fare Near the Spotlight

Situated in the bustling theater district, this Italian gem offers convenience and classic cuisine for show-goers and foodies alike. The ambiance is quintessentially Italian – cozy and inviting – paired with attentive service that adds to the dining experience.

Begin with their fried mozzarella, a sight so captivating it cries out for a snapshot. While the flavor may be mild, the cheese pull is spectacular. A star attraction is the Hennessey pasta special, a performance in its own right prepared tableside and served from a spinning cheese wheel. It is an indulgent display not to be missed, though a word to the wise: its robust cheese flavor is not for the faint of heart or delicate of stomach.

Overall, this restaurant is a solid pick if you're craving Italian before the curtain call, with prices that won't upstage your night out.

Came here around 12 PM on a Sunday and there was a 30-45 minute wait. The staff was super friendly and accomodating when I asked if we could walk around and explore SoHo they were totally okay with it. When we came back to check on our name, we were crossed off but the hostess sat us right away once we got back. They play party music here and it's a little crowded/tight and small in the restaurant but it's a cute little brunch spot. My friend and I ordered the top two recommended dishes on yelp: Green Shakshuka and Madame Freda. The Green Shakshuka is light and has a little bit of a latin flare to it. It's like a latin fusion with eggs and bread. It was okay, but I definetly liked the Madame Freda more. The Madame Freda was super rich and tasty. I thought it was so interesting that they had duck meat because I'm a huge duck meat fan. I also love arugula which they serve with the Madade Freda, but wish there was more of a dressing on it. This place is very unique and tasty. The staff is super friendly which made the experience really enjoyable. I would recommend this place for a yummy little brunch spot if you're ever in SoHo!

I recently dined at a charming eatery that left an almost entirely positive impression. The highlight of my meal was undoubtedly the seared halloumi with honey, a dish so delightful that I could feast on it exclusively for days. The mushroom special and the combination of labneh with fresh pita also stood out with their excellent flavors.

While I enjoyed the chicken broth accompanying my Beef Kubeh, I found the kubeh itself slightly underwhelming, lacking the depth I had hoped for. That said, the entirety of the meal was still a delightful experience.

Additionally, their baklava was worth a taste, but it was their saffron ice cream that truly deserves a high recommendation. Observing my friend's satisfaction with their plumper lamb Kubeh in beet broth, I am eager to return and explore the other kubeh varieties and broths on offer. This restaurant is certainly on my list for a repeat visit.

Title: A Sweet Indulgence at the Chocolate Shop

I recently savored the delights of the chocolate shop section within a local restaurant and it was an experience that tantalized my taste buds. The shop boasts a charming array of chocolate treats from tins and individually sold chocolates to an assortment of truffles that are simply irresistible.

For those who enjoy customization, the boxes of chocolates offer the option to handpick your favorites or select a pre-packaged assortment, ensuring there's a choice for every preference. The gift boxes are particularly enticing, not only for their variety but also for their affordability—priced between $25-30, they include a quartet of delectable selections suitable for any chocolate aficionado.

What caught my eye, and taste, were the dark chocolate covered caramelized pecans—a spectacular treat that converted even a skeptic like me who usually doesn't indulge in chocolate-covered nuts.

Adding to the charm is a chocolate-churning machine prominently displayed at the front, which offers a glimpse into the chocolate-making process and adds an interactive element to the shopping experience.

For those not in close proximity, the shop's online store is a godsend, delivering the same high-quality products nationwide, making it a convenient option to treat yourself or to brighten someone else's day with a sweet gift.

In short, this chocolate shop is a haven for those who appreciate fine, artisanal chocolates, with offerings that are bound to please both the chocoholic and the occasional indulger alike.

Great place for pitas! We went here on the way to john Lindsay east river park in New York. We stopped by as we were looking for Greek food and we were amazed. The ambience of the place is very soothing. Restrooms were clean and the internal design of the place feels like a replica of Santorini, Greece. We ordered two chicken pitas which were very filling and delicious. It's a great combo of the chicken, fries and the sauce! I would come back again to try the beef pita and the salad!

Title: A Redeeming Dinner Experience

After a lackluster brunch, my boyfriend and I revisited [Restaurant Name] for dinner and found ourselves delightfully surprised. Despite our 8 pm reservation on a Wednesday, the bustling atmosphere meant we waited briefly for a table. The staff appeared slightly overwhelmed, possibly due to understaffing, but maintained their composure amidst the din of the crowded space.

The restaurant's charming decor and vibrant music set an inviting tone, though the volume might be a touch high for easy conversation. Our culinary journey began with a delectable caesar salad and a spicy tuna tartare that both impressed our palates, followed by a decent crab and avocado appetizer.

The main course featured a savory fried octopus and a flavorful fried chicken, though the latter lacked accompaniments - a surprising choice for such a standalone dish. We complemented our meal with mouth-watering sides: the brussel sprouts and the corn, both earning our high praise.

Our celebration was capped off with a birthday cake dessert that, while not extraordinary, was certainly a sweet conclusion to the meal.

Service this visit was noticeably improved, with our previous waiter showing commendable attentiveness and care compared to our initial encounter. While the prices tip towards the higher end, the dinner experience at [Restaurant Name] redeemed itself with delectable cuisine and notably enhanced service, warranting a recommendation for their evening fare.

Had dinner at Ai Fiori on Saturday night. An impressive wine list, a solid and constantly changing tasting menu, and exquisite service highlight an excellent Italian restaurant.Quality: Initially I was concerned seeing a Michelin starred restaurant listed on Travelzoo, assuming it either was an indictment of decrease in quality or that we would be receiving a lesser meal because of the discount. Luckily neither of those proved true. Ai Fiori served up an excellent Seven Course Tasting Menu inspired by the region of Umbria. The meal started off wonderfully with a Crostini Al Tartufo, toasted bread with black truffle and sardines. This was quickly followed by the Coniglio, braised rabbit served on beluga lentils with herb salad. Our pasta course involved a thick Spaghetti With Sausage, served in a light gravy sauce. It was a very strong start, that finally hit a snag with the Pan Seared Halibut. The fish itself was fine, but I just did not fall for the mix of beans, croutons, and pomodoro it was served with. The Pheasant that followed was an improvement, but using two courses on dessert was also disappointing. Nothing wrong with Ice Cream or a Chocolate Cake with Caramelized Banana, just too much sweet to end a meal. I do wonder why they did not offer a full dining menu at the start in case I wanted to add any supplements to our tasting.Quantity: While a few too many desserts, the Seven Course Tasting Menu was still the perfect sized meal.Value: $160 for a Seven Course Tasting Menu, but we had a Travelzoo Voucher to reduce it to $199 for two. Huge range of prices for the voluminous wine list, but we settled on an Italian Piedmont that cost $85.Ambiance: Ai Fiori is located inside The Langham NYC in Midtown Manhattan. After entering the hotel, you take the spiral staircase to the second floor. Here you are met with the lobby and large bar, where we spent a little time before our table was ready. The dining area itself is big with well spaced tables. We sat near the window overlooking the street below. This area was a little brighter than the other half of the restaurant filled with beautiful artwork. If music was playing it was too quiet to be heard.Crowd: Busy, but not packed on Saturday evening. It seemed like the bar area was the more popular section, but the restaurant itself had a good flow.Service: Excellent service. Our waiter was fantastic, but they had enough staff to make sure we were well taken care of even if he stepped away.Parking: Valet parking at the hotel.

Very delicious and traditional northern Chinese food! It's perfect if you're trying to grab a quick bite. You are able to get in and out in 20-30 min.Interiors - reminds me of the vibe of 90s Chinese stores! I like it a lot and it feels very homey. The space is not too large and tables are kinda small.Service - very quick service, every plate came to the table within 10 min.Taste - my favorite is the Mouth Watering Chicken, so delicious!! Not all that spicy but it's got that numbing effect. I also loved the pork pan fried dumplings. It's stuffed with meat and very addicting!This place is way downtown and kinda hidden, if you are nearby, it's worth the search!!

Omg I had high hopes for this place and I am glad that they delivered. We came here at around 12:30pm for lunch. Make sure to come here early because it does book up very fast and then the wait becomes very long. We started by getting the pork belly buns which is what they are known for. They were delicious, super flavorful and the bun was so soft and pillowy. Then I got the garlic chicken ramen and it was amazing, however it is a little different from traditional ramen. It felt like it was a mix between chicken noodle soup and ramen with a ton of garlic! So hearty and delicious especially on a cold day.The service was super attentive and very helpful. This place is definitely on my list to revisit in the near future!

Title: Overhyped and Underwhelming: A Disappointment at Sugarfish

I visited Sugarfish with high expectations, having braced myself for the notorious 2.5 to 3 hour wait, not once but twice, on 1/30/19 and again on 2/1/19. Unfortunately, the experience didn't live up to the hype. Here's my honest take:

Pros:
- Affordability is a plus, with a set menu offering a fair amount of food for $52.
- The seaweed surpassed that of Kazunori, with a more palatable texture.
- The highlight was the scallops – a creamy delight that I could indulge in repeatedly.

Cons:
- The albacore sushi was overwhelmed by an excessively sour sauce, which was quite off-putting.
- Sushi construction was subpar, with rice that fell apart too easily and was inappropriately warm.
- The craftsmanship of sushi was lost here; it was impossible to eat in the traditional 'fish down' fashion without it collapsing.
- An overzealous use of sauce drowned most of the sushi, compromising the balance of flavors.
- Prepare to wait 2.5 to 3 hours, although it's difficult to justify such a long wait for pre-made offerings simply plated upon order.
- Choosing the "Nozawa Trust Me" menu felt like a mistake; à la carte might have been a better option.

Ultimately, Sugarfish didn't measure up, especially for those with a deep appreciation for authentic sushi craftsmanship. It's not a destination I would recommend to fellow sushi connoisseurs. The lack of Asian chefs in the kitchen may have contributed to the seeming authenticity gap. It's simply not a secret I'd want to share with my sushi-loving friends.

**THIS PLACE IS CELIAC FRIENDLY.**I came here around 1pm on a Saturday for brunch with a party of 7, You can't make reservations beforehand for brunch on the weekends. When we went in, it instantly smelled like pure alcohol in the restaurant. It was crowded inside and the lady told us it would be about an hour and 40 minute wait. They take your number to call you or text you when the table is ready, which is convenient.To our luck, we were able to be seated in 30 minutes! We decided to do a wholesome brunch as boozy brunch is $22 extra. We ordered different things on the menu such as the Pancake Burger, Pork Belly Croquette Madame, M&M Pancakes. Everyone enjoyed their dishes, the portions were HUGE.I ordered the pork belly croquette and it was pork belly on a sourdough toast with melted cheese & an egg. This was really good but I could only finish half. I think there was a bit too much cheese, it overpowered the dish. The m&m pancakes come with about 5 pancakes and super instagramable. My friends who ordered the pancake burger were in LOVE with their meal. I tried some and I instantly wished I got it. It was basically a pancake sandwich with bacon, egg, melted cheese, etc in the middle. Of course, there was a syrup sauce as well!!It has great gluten free options on the menu as well. My friend has celiac and she was able to get an avocado toast on gluten free bread as well as the burger on a gluten free bun! Super accommodating. The avocado toast wasn't anything special, not really worth the money. Solid 3/5 but the beef burger was a 5/5! It's $2 extra for gluten free bread but that is pretty standard at restaurants.

From the moment you step into BaoHaus, the tantalizing aromas envelop you, foreshadowing the culinary delight that awaits. With each bao better than the last, it's a challenge to choose a favorite. Skepticism about the hype was quickly replaced with admiration, as every bite delivers a uniquely delectable experience. This eatery is a must-visit for anyone seeking flavors that truly pop. My only wish? That BaoHaus could deliver their heavenly buns across state lines. Kudos to the team for an impeccable dining experience!

Guy-Kaku, at dinner time (around 8PM) was a little bit packed. There was an expected wait time of around 30 minutes, and we were barely able to find a seat at the bar. The happy hour special was pretty good (most of the drinks were between $3-8) and it felt like you were getting your money's worth with both the cocktails and the larger sized beers)Once we were seated at the table, we ordered two sets of barbecue meals (meant for two people each) ... which is when some of the chaos began. A few waiters and waitresses came over one at a time and asked if we already had a waiter. When our food came out, they forgot to give us sauces... despite the fact that each one of us was given an empty sauce dish. The waiter who initially took our order went missing, and we had to ask another one for water (and to my recollection, we never saw our initial waiter again).The food itself was quite expensive. With one beer and my portion of the barbecue, it came out to $46 after tax and tip (in the attached pictures, was a meal meant for four people in total). That being said, the food was quite good. The salad was exceptional, most of the cuts of beef were high quality and good tasting (some weren't, but most were good) but the highlight was the spicy sauce. The spicy sauce made the meal.Despite some mishaps, the meal was solid and I wouldn't mind coming back to try some of the other selections on the menu.

Title: Summer Sensations at Rahi – A Restaurant Week Gem

My second visit to Rahi for the summer edition of Restaurant Week 2019 reaffirmed my love for this culinary haven. Having had an outstanding experience during the winter session, my expectations were high, yet Rahi managed to impress yet again.

The magic of Rahi lies in its mastery over spices and presentation. Each dish I encountered was an impeccable fusion of flavors, elegantly prepared and wonderfully complex. While I savored the pre fixe menu, the real stars were the dishes I hadn’t selected – the artichoke chaat and the mango cod. Both dishes were unassuming on the menu but came alive with rich, intricate flavors on the plate.

Even with the allure of new discoveries, I couldn't resist revisiting the octopus, a dish off the Restaurant Week menu which had won me over previously. And as I reminisced over the soft shell crab from our winter visit, I was filled with anticipation for its return in the upcoming season.

Rahi is not just a restaurant; it's a journey of taste that beckons for multiple explorations. I'm already planning my next visit within the forthcoming weeks - a testament to the allure of their culinary craft.

Rating: 5/5 – Rahi is a standout, crafting an experience that’s both innovative and deeply satisfying. A must-visit for anyone looking to kick off summer with an unforgettable dining encounter.

Title: A Delicious Encounter at a Culinary Gem

I recently ventured to a restaurant with my companion, J, and left thoroughly impressed. Upon the waitress's advice, we savored the dumplings and loc lac – both dishes were exceptional. The dumplings broke the mold of the ordinary, boasting a remarkable blend of tenderness and rich flavors. The loc lac featured succulent beef that truly shone, though the lettuce beneath was merely a garnish without much impact.

We also sampled the Cambodian crepe, which required a generous helping of the provided dressing and spices to truly come alive. Dessert was a tale of two treats: the old school pudding was the star, eclipsing the rather mundane banana crepe.

The restaurant itself is spacious with a warm, wooden interior that exudes upscale comfort, down to the stunning wooden screen and the serene Buddha statue greeting guests at the entrance. We were promptly seated at 7 pm, enjoying a window spot before the evening crowd filled the space. Service, while leisurely, matched the pace of our relaxed meal, punctuated by thoughtful touches like wet naps and advice on enjoying the crepe at its crispiest.

Despite a slightly slow service, the meal was unmarred by haste, allowing ample time for conversation. The staff also scored points for accommodating our request to split the bill on credit cards.

In summary, the experience was rich in flavor and atmosphere. A return visit is definitely in the cards – my gratitude to the staff for a memorable and delectable evening.

Good spot to grab drinks and a quick bite. I think that it's also good for small groups. On my last visit I got the mango flavored frozen margarita and 2 tacos (one grilled chili lime taco and one pulled pork). The tacos were really good and the margarita was nice and strong. I'm usually good with just 2 frozen margaritas. This place usually has a lively crowd, they have great happy hour deals. If you're in Harlem, I would recommend to stop by.

Incredible spot serving up a top-notch product at a good price and with great efficiency. Wife and I split the jumbo lobster roll and were full (and impressed). Super convenient location in the food hall. Will definitely be back.
Excellent bar with good bar food choices. Stopped in for a quick drink and meal in between shopping runs. Had the burger and my daughter had the fried chicken sandwich. Both were great.

Title: A Slice Haven with Generous Toppings!

I had the pleasure of trying out a new spot for pizza slices and I'm already planning my next visit! The variety of slices available is impressive and choosing just a few was a delightful challenge. I settled on the margarita, artichoke, buffalo chicken, and a standout vodka sauce slice.

The vodka sauce slice was my absolute favorite - I couldn't help but devour it and the equally delicious margarita slice in one sitting. The artichoke and buffalo chicken slices were generously topped, making them quite hearty and filling. Even reheated the next day, they retained their flavor perfectly.

While I'm eager to explore more slice options in the future, the vodka sauce slice has earned a permanent spot in my order. The only downsides were the presentation upon delivery, with slices overlapping, and the temperature could have been hotter. Despite that, the taste more than made up for it. Can't wait to go back for more!

Title: A Stellar Korean Feast in Manhattan

Having been recommended by a Korean friend as her favorite spot, my expectations for this Manhattan Korean restaurant were high, and I must say, they did not disappoint. If I were to rate it on the entirety of the experience, it would comfortably sit at a 4.5 out of 5 stars. However, the galbi jjim here is such an exceptional dish that I can't help but bump my rating to a perfect 5 stars.

During a post-work dinner with colleagues, we sampled various items from the menu, and while each dish was flavorful and well-prepared, the galbi jjim stood out as the star of the show. It's rare to find a dish executed with such finesse that you're left planning your next visit before the meal is even over, but here we are. The delectable galbi jjim is a must-try, and it's certainly the beacon that will draw me back in sooner rather than later.

Good Jewish/Eastern European comfort food! High 3 stars.THE WAIT: None on a Monday around 6:45pm. They were still pretty packed!THE SERVICE: Our server was a bit in a rush and I had too many questions. In the process of ordering, three times I asked about an item and he rushed to think I was ordering it when I was still deciding.THE COST: $83.83 before tips for three. Fairly reasonable.DRINKS: * Honey mint ginger iced tea $5 - 4 starsQuite sharp! Had a hint of spice.. I could have used more!THE FOOD:See my pictures for details! Biggest disappointment was my entree, the Ukrainian Meatballs, which were too dry.

Came here for restaurant week with my roommates. Our server was really nice, but the service was really slow because she was the only server for so many tables. I got the garlic mussels and the spicy tuna roll. The dessert was okay, the flavors did not go well together. Overall it was a really good experience. The wine selection was nice and the decor and the restaurant as a whole were beautiful.

The long wait time (4 hours) in Chicago prevented me from my share of this popular burger and when I found out they opened a location in Chelsea, I was set to go.  The stars aligned for an early ish dinner (6pm) with only an hour long wait.  The location is hidden in a seedy alleyway filled with graffiti.  There was an inconspicuous dark blue door and a tiny sign that can easily be missed.  The mood continued inside with very low lighting, almost club like feel to it.  The interiors were beautiful with modern furniture; more like an upscale dining experience with a casual menu.My dining partner and I shared a burger, I know, a sin, but we ordered appetizers at another bar since our wait time was long and we were hungry after watching The Waitress.  We ordered the double cheeseburger (medium rare) with egg and bacon, absolutely delicious and one of the best I've had in a long time. A standout was the chopped salad and also had it with egg.  I would pass on the crispy fries with mornay sauce and the fried egg.  The description of the dish was spot on good, but we simply had too many eggs for dinner and also, it was not as tasty and outstanding as the other dishes. To balance the meal, crispy fries as is would have been suffice.  We ordered root beer with our burger and it's always a win with any burger. I will revisit this joint for sure and hopefully the wait times are shorter.

Beautiful restaurant.  Amazing meal.  We started with calamari that was outstanding!   For dinner i ordered scallops that were cooked to perfection and lamb chops that were delightful.    We were celebrating a birthday and a fizzing champagne was brought out that ended our meal perfectly. Definitely give this restaurant a try.   It is located by the theater district.

Title: A Delightful Surprise at an Unassuming Spot

I recently stopped by a restaurant that a friend discovered on Foursquare, and I was blown away by the experience! The food was nothing short of amazing, leaving no doubt in my mind about returning soon.

I indulged in the fried chicken paired with pancakes—a twist I was initially skeptical about since I'm more accustomed to the classic chicken and waffles combo. However, my taste buds were in for a treat. The chicken was seasoned and fried to perfection, while the pancakes had a unique, donut-like flavor, likely due to the delectable sauce drizzled on top.

Venturing further into comfort food territory, I tried the bacon Mac & cheese - and let me tell you, it was the bomb! At $10, the generous portion felt like a steal.

Washing it all down with one of their refreshing green juices was the perfect way to round off this feast. They've got the flavors and quality nailed down.

Service was a highlight as well. Our waiter, Jonathan, couldn't have been kinder, earning the title of sweetheart hands down.

Lastly, for the tech-savvy and social media enthusiasts, they’ve got you covered with convenient charging outlets and an outdoor seating area that’s too cute not to snap a photo of.

If you're looking for a place that checks the boxes for delicious food, delightful service, and a touch of modern convenience, look no further!

Skip George's and do breakfast like the locals. Huge portions, reasonable prices, outstanding friendly service. This is my go to place for downtown. We had a French Toast Sandwich and Egg/Bacon/Potato platter, Poppy Seed Bagel. Line waxed and waned so be patient and you'll get a seat. They do everything to go as well. Coffee fit for a king.

Found this restaurant on 3rd avenue in NYC after finding out that my actual destination was closed permanently.   The reviews looked good so I gave it a try.   I dined alone both times - once at a table and once at the bar.   The atmosphere is very nice with lovely art hanging on the walls.  The first visit I had the butternut ravioli with a cider cream sauce.   It was amazing.   The second visit I ordered the pasta bolognese which was also very good.   Service was adequate.    On Both occasions the restaurant was not crowded for lunch.   Both lunches were $18-20.00 so perhaps the prices scare people away but it's worth it Update 3/10/20:   Stopped by to grab lunch and they were closed with a note on the door that they would be closed for 2 weeks for repairs.   So call first before you venture over.  Windows were all papered over.

My first dry pot experience was a success! Málá Project is cozy and crowded, so definitely make a reservation if you can to avoid a wait! My friends and I made a 8pm reservation on a Saturday evening, and we were seated after a little wait. The idea of drypot is kind of like a make-your-own stir fry. You choose a whole bunch of items (from protein to vegetables to starch) to put into your dish and then you share it. You also get to choose your spice level for your drypot. For our group of 5, we ordered 2 drypots with 8-10 items each. I absolutely LOVED the dishes -- everything was so fresh and well cooked. The fish was especially warm and flaky, going well with the tender vegetables. Honestly, if I were hungry enough I probably could have eaten a whole one by myself! :)The price was very reasonable for the amount of food that we all had. Service was quick and the staff were really accommodating and friendly for our large group!

Maybe I had SUCH high expectations of Per Se that I'm giving it 4/5 stars. Don't get me wrong, the experience was fantastic, but it's not my favorite Michelin restaurant in NYC. (I think I over hyped it in my head), One thing that gets me a little nutty about Per Se is the fact that they don't have a bar. They have a sitting area where you can sit on a comfy couch and order a glass of wine, while look out at Central Park, but I much prefer a bar.Anyway, I arrived earlier than my guests and they were happy to seat me while I waited, which was really nice of them. I ordered a glass of rose champagne to start, which was spectacular. When my dining guests arrived, they brought with them a nice bottle of 2014 Napa Cab. I wasn't aware you could bring wine to Per Se, but apparently you can for a $150 corking fee. (Now I know).Lunch was $195/pp and consisted of 5 courses. They brought out a preliminary, complimentary course of tuna tartar which was excellent. Then for the first course I had the oysters and pearls, which consisted of a tapioca like consistency, lots of delicious caviar and oysters. This dish was excellent.For course two I ordered the sunchokes, which was a delightful mix of grapes, winter truffles, hazelnuts and a delightful mousse on the side. Delicious. The lubina was next, which is apparently a European sea bass. This was served with parsley, over fork-crushed potatoes over their take on a puttanesca sauce. I thought this dish was okay. It was good, but it wasn't outstanding. For the next course, the substituted quail for the other options as I don't eat pork or beef. The quail was excellent. I think it looked better than the two items listed on the menu! The dish came with two pieces of meat on the bone with a nice crunchy crust to it, and a dash of gravy on the side. This was very tasty. For dessert they started us off with some chocolate cake topped with espresso ice cream, hazelnuts and praline. They also gave us macaroons, chocolate candies and little dough balls covered with sugar. Service was excellent. Food was great.

Very nice experience sitting outside with a very relaxing atmosphere (very different in Little Italy than it is in Times Square). So this is in Little Italy and is pricey but you do feel pampered. It was my birthday so a gentleman came over and played happy birthday to me on his accordion. That was awesome!They start out with a bread basket of awesome bread and breadsticks and we got oil and balsamic vinegar to dip it in. Just try not to get carried away with the bread or you'll be stuffed because the food is very tasty. I got a chicken dish that was stuffed with cheese, mushrooms and vegetables. Very tasty. The others in my party got Gnocchi, cheese ravioli and a linguine and everyone liked their food.

Brunch: A hard 3.5 stars. Rounded up to 4 because I will probably still return. We got comped on two drinks since they messed up my dads drink and took a very long time bringing it. I ordered a burger to be cooked medium and it came rare. However, the burger was delicious and came with French fries. My mom ordered the kale salad with salmon. Instead of kale, they made it with spring mix (which she did not request, it was their mistake). Still, the salad was delicious and it was topped with the best salmon I've had in awhile. Pan-seared salmon with the skin perfectly crispy and the inside soft and flakey. We also ordered spring mix salad with grilled chicken, which was actually SUPPOSED to be spring mix. They added a lot of chicken. Even though its a $20+ salad there is atleast 2 breasts of chicken, definitely keeps you full! However, either the chicken and/or the shallot dressing was very salty because I still have the taste of salt in my mouth.

Tucked away near the Top of the Rock, I stumbled upon Nanoosh, a haven for the health-conscious that’s steadily becoming a staple in the city. The spacious interior promises ample seating, a relief given the city's often crowded dining venues.

Service, albeit not flawless, was acceptable. With the scant number of staff, a bit of patience was required at the counter. The restaurant's design and menu presentation could use a graphic designer's touch, as navigation and order clarity presented minor challenges.

However, any design missteps are easily forgiven once the food arrives. The Powerfood plate was a delight – a harmonious medley of 1/2 basmati rice, power greens, succulent marinated chicken, flavorsome baked falafel, ample hummus, and earthy organic mushrooms, all brought together with Tahini sauce and accompanied by pita bread. While the rice felt a tad dry, reminiscent of the Halal guys' offering, every other component scored high on my satisfaction meter, with both the falafel and mushrooms standing out as exceptional.

Priced reasonably, Nanoosh delivers a satisfyingly hearty and healthy meal. In sum, this establishment earns a solid 8/10 for its commendable culinary experience.

Title: A Gem of Modern Korean Cuisine at Atoboy

My anticipation for Atoboy had been building up for quite some time, and I'm thrilled to report that it did not just meet but soared beyond my expectations. This New York hotspot offers an impressive deal of $46 for three hearty share plates. Despite their deceptively modest size, these dishes left me and my two companions thoroughly satisfied.

Despite being late for our Thursday reservation due to my brother's delayed arrival, the accommodating staff welcomed us with open arms, ensuring a smooth experience even with a tight schedule.

Atoboy boasts a cool, industrial vibe within its compact, corridor-like space. The knowledgeable staff proficiently navigated us through the menu, even tweaking dishes to cater to my brother's pescatarian preference.

Each plate arrived promptly, showcasing culinary artistry both in taste and presentation. The flavors were remarkable, akin to what one would expect from an establishment with a much steeper price tag. Standouts included the pork and prawn, Brussels sprouts, and skate.

Professional and meticulous service added to the impeccable dining experience. I wholeheartedly recommend Atoboy and am eager to return. It stands out as a leading destination for modern Korean cuisine in New York.

Title: Hearty Portions and Delicious Flavors at Local Thai Spot

I decided to opt for Thai cuisine while swamped with meetings and took to GrubHub for convenience. After a stellar recommendation from our CM Jared, I picked the red curry lunch special from a local restaurant on 19th street. The quantity was unexpectedly generous, almost overwhelming for a lunch portion. Flavor-wise, the curry hit the mark with a medium spice level that was mild enough for those tentative about heat, yet still packed a flavor punch. Accompanied by notably large and tender cuts of squid, the meal was impressive. Although it included soup or salad and an appetizer, the main dish alone was more than enough. A minor downside was the flimsy plastic utensils provided, so I suggest requesting chopsticks for a better experience. Would recommend for anyone looking for a hearty and tasty Thai meal delivered right to your desk.

looking for a pretzel from Germany? I mean who isn't, but here's the thing. The pretzels here are literally flown in from Germany and heated to perfection on site.To use a technical term, AmazeballsFor a place that packs a ton of seats into a small-ish space, Katja definitely has an intimate vibe going that I really appreciated. We found a few seats in our natural habitat (read: the bar) and settled in for a relaxing evening after a long day of brunching*. This was the perfect respite after such a day; chill bartenders and snacks to soak up a few of the countless mimosas we had had earlier...you know, while slowly sipping on a liter of German weissbier. To be fair, beer isn't really an alcoholic beverage in Germany, it's more of a staple food. I am, if nothing else, a fan of being culturally sensitive**. We grazed on a couple of pretzels (they are small, order one per person), and a plate of pickles that included some other pickled veggies like carrots - I would absolutely get this again and recommend you try it. Honestly, everything looked good, my only regret that day was coming here kinda full, I won't make that mistake again, promise. to recap; this place is pretty amazing, come for the pretzel, stay for the beer and other delicious foods - I will absolutely be back to try the bratwurst soon. _________*It's a hard life, but someone has to do it. **...and I really really love German beer.

I stopped in here today after seeing this place listed in Eater's top 40 cheap eats in the city. I ordered the Build Your Own Stirfry with spicy cumin lamb, ribbon noodles and extra spicy. The to go container was filled with lamb, noodles and cilantro; very spicy and flavorful. The lamb noodles and the pork fried dumplings (also good) are definitely pricey compared to other places like Xian Famous Foods, however you get a lot of food. The dish was plenty to share! Given Covid, make sure to bring water, napkins and wet wipes to eat outside the place on the counter.

Returning for a second visit to this bustling eatery, it was evident that the place has gained popularity—it was absolutely packed! Despite the crowd, service remained attentive. Each dumpling order arrived with a generous count of eight, making it easy to over-order, but that just means delightful leftovers!

My selections included a varied mix: boiled shrimp dumplings with a delicate, succulent filling, and golden fried pork buns offering a satisfying crunch. A warm bowl of miso soup provided a comforting start, nicely complementing the robust flavors of the roast pork scallion pancake. The pork and chive fried dumplings were a fragrant, crispy treat, while the chicken and basil boiled dumplings rounded out the meal with their freshness and herbal notes.

Each dish was a flavorful testament to the kitchen's prowess. If you're in the mood for an array of dumplings that won't disappoint, this is your go-to spot. Just be ready for a crowd and a happy surplus of leftovers.

Title: Cozy Spot for a Delicious Vegan Ramen

I dropped by this quaint little restaurant on a chilly Thursday evening, drawn by its warm ambiance and the promise of comforting food. Despite its compact size, the place buzzed with activity, and the staff's friendly demeanor made finding a seat in the limited space an enjoyable task. I opted for a spot with a view of the kitchen, where I could witness the magic of my meal being prepared.

My choice for the night was the Vegan ramen, enhanced with extra nori and bok choy. While I pondered the absence of menma on the menu, which would have been a welcome addition, the ramen itself did not disappoint. The broth was exceptional— creamy, milky, and utterly delicious. However, the toppings were a bit scarce for my liking. Next time I'll make a point to request a generous helping of every vegetable topping available. That said, the meal was satisfying, and the experience has me looking forward to my next visit.

Title: Satisfying Korean Fare at a Bustling K-Town Eatery

My recent dining experience at this popular K-Town restaurant left both my friend Jon and me thoroughly content. The menu is a haven for Korean cuisine enthusiasts, and the portions are generous enough to fill you up nicely.

I opted for the short ribs and spicy rice cakes, both of which hit the spot perfectly. The ribs were mouthwateringly tasty, and there was ample to share. The spicy rice cakes lived up to my love for them, providing that kick I crave. Jon's choice of a spicy soup didn't disappoint either; he savored every spoonful.

One of the highlights was the variety of side dishes. They offered a refreshing counterbalance to the main courses' deep, spicy, and savory notes, enhancing the meal's overall flavor profile.

Price-wise, the restaurant is on par with others in the area, with dishes starting at around $9—a fair price for the quality and quantity of food served.

The restaurant itself was buzzing with activity, indicative of its popularity and the authenticity of the food. It's spacious enough to accommodate the crowds without feeling too packed.

In summary, for a genuine Korean food experience with dishes that satisfy your spice cravings and leave you happily full, this spot in K Town is definitely worth a visit.

My neighborhood jaunt to Cervo's was long overdue, and it didn't disappoint. Despite its modest size, the restaurant's well-designed space complements the bustling atmosphere perfectly. The white prawns la plancha were a fresh delight, paired exquisitely with a sauce that livened up the accompanying crusty bread.
