The swordfish conserva, akin to an upscale canned tuna, shone alongside seasonal tomatoes. 

The main courses were equally impressive: the lamb burger, offset by a bed of escarole, balanced its inherent saltiness, while the fried skate wing—a generously sized rendition of schnitzel—was satisfyingly hearty. Cervo's masters the art of simple, yet delectable dishes at prices that don't break the bank. A return visit? Absolutely.

I'll start out by saying I went here for brunch on a Sunday over Labor Day weekend. SUPER cute decor - from the gold accent furniture to the art I would love to steal for my apartment haha! I will say the floral entry way seemed a little basic (actually really basic) like it was trying to be a step and repeat lol. But I'm sure that's the point and gets people to 'gram it and promote them, so hey, great marketing through being basic! I can get behind that. Took forever for someone to greet me when I walked in, like everyone working there was just running around and not even looking at me. I was so confused... like hello?! And then finally someone asked if we had a reservation (we didn't but almost all the tables were open, probably because it was Labor Day) and asked me to wait in the bar area before my friend arrived.Food was subpar. We ordered off of the summer brunch menu. I got the avocado toast which was fine but I don't like when the toast is too toasted, like so toasted you can barely cut it with a knife. My friend wanted to order something off the normal menu (steak and eggs) but still do the summer brunch special pricing; the answer was no, but that's not surprising.I'll be back to try happy hour or dinner sometime because I've seen some intriguing pictures on Instagram, plus the back area decor is just as cute with low teal-ish velvet chairs, etc.

Title: A Tapas Treasure with Unforgettable Beets

I recently had the pleasure of dining here and it was an experience I'm eager to repeat. The array of tapas on offer is a food lover's delight, and I'm already planning my next visit to indulge once more. The highlight, without a doubt, was the beets – their seasoning is simply perfection and I find myself craving their flavor even now.

Another standout was the hummus and pita; it rivaled some of the best I've ever tasted – creamy, rich, and utterly irresistible. The eggplant dish may not have been to my personal taste, but that's the beauty of tapas – there's something for everyone.

Be warned, the restaurant's popularity means it fills up quickly, so do yourself a favor and reserve a table to avoid disappointment. And while I'm still reminiscing about those sensational beets, I caught a glimpse of their brunch menu and the crispy bacon is calling my name. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a top-notch tapas experience!

Every time I have tried the food at Shakespeare I am reminded of the good old pub days back in London. I ordered for the salmon burger on my first visit and it has been my favorite every since. I can say it's the best salmon burger I've had  in the city! My husband ordered for the vegan shepherd pie which was also pretty good! We have also tried their portobello burger which is amazing. I really  want to try their fish & chips as I know it will be top notch! On my second visit, I also had a banana bread beer which was so good!Highly recommend Shakespear for their beer and food!

Title: A Mixed Burger Experience

I've been on a burger exploration at this joint, having savored four different types. My early favorite, the Truffle Burger, has unfortunately fallen from grace due to inconsistent flavors, with its recent rendition failing to leave a mark. On a brighter note, the Sunnyside Burger, topped with a sunnyside egg and bacon, has won me over with its succulence and tastiness, though caution is advised as the delicate yolk may not always survive the assembly process – I’ve witnessed casualties.

The Cali Burger is another solid pick, doubling down on patties without thinning out your wallet. It delivers on flavor, making it a smart and satisfying option. Sadly, the Wagyumami was a letdown – it lacked the moisture I craved, and the kimchi mayo, while a novel touch, couldn't salvage the absence of that rich wagyu essence promised by its name.

You trusted neighborhood staples ha! This spot dishes authentic unpretentious Filipino food. Not overpriced and without fancy plating, the dishes comes in huge potion and resembles home cooking. Service is from zero to none but who cares when the food is so delicious and scrumptious in front of you. Just wave and ask for water as every bite packed spice and heat, in a good way!

Title: A Chinatown Gem for Chinese Cuisine

After sifting through countless options in New York's bustling Chinatown, I took to Yelp and stumbled upon a true culinary treasure. The excitement was palpable, with a queue of eager diners chatting about their long-standing patronage—a testament to its local fame.

The rice, a cornerstone of any Chinese meal, was cooked to perfection, each grain an ambassador of flavor. Their chicken was the star of the show, packing an explosive punch of taste that I can only describe as 'bomb'. The lo mein also stood out, maintaining a delightful texture that skirted the edge of softness, just firm enough to satisfy the palate.

Unable to resist the urge, I found myself ordering extra to savor the experience at home. This place is a must-visit for anyone in search of amazing Chinese food in the heart of New York's Chinatown.

Brunches in this neighborhood don't start until 10am. Thankfully a "breakfast" option got us in the door of Le Bateau Ivre for a meal I would consider brunch. We sat by the window that gave us the best of both worlds: view of the street plus air conditioning in a charming French cafe atmosphere. The dining room wasn't big by any means but it had character.My mom and I both went with the Croquet Madame and a mimosa. The croquet came with a small house salad and rosemary roasted potatoes. I savored every bite of the exquisite ham and cheese on thick French bread.The pricing was just odd. The prices varied from breakfast to brunch. Our mimosas were more for breakfast but the croquet madames were less. In any case, I enjoyed this experience over just doing a generic bottomless and basic at one of the neighboring American joints.

Title: A Hidden Gem on a Wednesday Night

I recently dined at this surprisingly empty venue on a late Wednesday evening with a large group in tow. Initial skepticism due to the lack of patrons was quickly dispelled by the charming decor featuring a sea of tiny round tiles adorning gravity-defying tabletops, walls, and an expansive bench—complete with reasonably comfortable individual cushions.

The Achilles heel of the setting was a rather obtrusive table leg stand that made for awkward seating adjustments and unintentional footsie with my dining companion across from me. Notwithstanding that minor inconvenience, the cuisine was the star of the night. Each dish, from the hearty chicken glass noodles to the meticulously prepared Panko Tilapia, was generous in portion and robust in flavor. Beware of the deceptively fiery Chili Basil Mock Duck, a dish not for the faint-hearted.

Throughout our meal, only a few other diners filtered in, with a stream of delivery orders heading out, which only added to the enigma of the quiet atmosphere. The attentive server was commendable, ensuring our water glasses were never empty and allowing our post-meal conversations to linger without rush.

In conclusion, the food quality, attentive service, and delightful interior outweigh the minor discomfort of the table design. I wholeheartedly endorse this restaurant and encourage others to give it the bustling atmosphere it deserves.

At first glance, one might easily overlook this unassuming eatery, but stepping inside would unveil an opportunity for a delightful and satisfying dining experience without straining the wallet. The compact dimensions of the restaurant suggest avoiding peak times for a more comfortable visit.

Upon entry, the air greets you with an invigorating aroma, a telltale sign of meals prepared fresh as you order. True to its moniker, the establishment boasts hand-pulled noodles that offer an authentic chewiness, testament to their artisanal preparation. Complementing the main dish, the cucumber salad is a standout, delivering a refreshing taste that acts as the perfect palate cleanser. A hidden gem for those seeking a simple yet gratifying meal.

Came for Chinese New Year with 5 friends and we went to town! Ordered 2 rounds of food which included:Steamed Chicken BunsBaked Sweet Pork BunsRoast Pork bunsSteamed Chinese broccoli Shrimp and Mango spring rolls Pork spring rolls Veggie spring rollsScallion Pancakes Baked pork piesSoup dumplings Pork and shrimp shu mai Crabmeat dumplings Curry Beef dumplings Shrimp dumplingsMushroom dumplings Chinese Parsley dumplings (they're actually cilantro)Duck dumplings Beef rice rolls Shrimp rice rollsBlack bean rib tips (they're not spare ribs)Sesame balls w lotus pasteI shit you not and yes we are it ALL! Mostly all was very good and so was service but I really do like it much better with the carts coming around.

Decided to celebrate my boyfriend's birthday at G & G and finally having the holy cannoli! The high ratings by fellow yelpers certainly did not disappoint.We were seated right away as we had reservation for two. Place was a bit dark which gave it a romantic vibe. Tables were a bit too close but we managed. There's a bar on the left when you first walk in and a nice private room in the basement. Service was quick and attentive. Our glasses never ran out of water. Appetizers: crispy octopus was amazing! Very flavorful. Truffled honey bruschetta was delicious. I'm usually not a cheese person but the goat cheese was really good.Bone in NY strip: medium rare was perfect. Good portion. Love that it came with a bit of greens.Prosciutto pizza: nice thin crust. There were six slices which made it a good dish to share. Cocoa cannoli: highlight of the evening! People around us were simply amazed by its size. You literally need a hammer to smash it. Loved how it came with some hot cocoa which you could pour into the little edible chocolate cup. Obviously we were so full at this point and had to pack most of it home. The restaurant was nice to put a candle on it. Happy birthday honey!! Awesome food. Great service. Amazing boyfriend. What more can I ask for. :)PS: don't forget to check in to get 10% off.

If you're a truffle fanatic you're gonna like the new Tokyo shoyu ramen. I came here right when it opened at 5:30pm so thank god i didn't have to wait on line. The broth is clean, light, flavorful and the truffle doesn't hit you like a train. The broth was good and wasn't too salty either. The noodles are al dente and the proportion of chicken was okay. I wish the slice was a little thicker though. The place is very small about 10 seats or so. You can ask them for a cup of water because i needed that after slurping my ramen so fast. My friend got the umami miso soup and the broth was much stronger and oilier.

Title: A Cozy Cafe Serving Up Sandwich Perfection

Recently, I had the pleasure of visiting a charming little cafe I had bookmarked for some time. Stepping inside, the warmth and coziness immediately embraced me, along with the promise of a delightful lunch experience. The seating was ample for the size of the cafe, ensuring a comfortable dining atmosphere.

Without hesitation, I ordered the spicy rizzak—a decision that proved to be a fantastic one. The sandwich was a masterful blend of flavors with sliced turkey, crisp bacon, smooth melted cheddar, and a kick of chipotle mayo that danced wonderfully on my taste buds. It was, to put it simply, delicious.

I appreciated the portion options—a "small" that was quite filling and comparable to a standard sandwich, and a "large" that seemed akin to a substantial sub. Accompanied by potato chips, my meal was satisfying and flavorful.

My experience was so positive that the cafe has secured a spot on my list of go-to eateries. I eagerly anticipate my next visit to navigate the rest of their sandwich menu. If you're in search of an exceptional sandwich, this is the spot you shouldn't miss.

Our ramen spot is Out of business (Ramen Takumi) so stopped by Tenho after reading good Yelp reviews. The room is clean and decorated nicely. The staff is friendly. We both had vegetable ramen. After we orered the food came out in under 5 minutes. I added hot sauce to mine. The noodles were a generous portion. The carrots were undercooked. The corn and broccoli (2 pieces) were good.

Came here for a holiday party and it was awesome! I don't know why the overall rating is only 3 1/2 stars. Everything was fantastic from the decor, atmosphere, service, and everyone we dealt with. We had a party of 14 and everything came out on time and we had plenty of attention at the table.We had family style appetizers a choice of a few entrees and of course desert.  Everything was extremely fresh, nice presentation, great wine selection and on a Wednesday night the place was packed.They put a different spin on most of the dishes. I loved the flash fried cauliflower, the flat breads were warm, soft and flavorful. The falafel balls were the best I've had. Loved the Branzino, it was deboned and all the portions were generous. The deserts were fantastic especially the Silan which is made from shredded Halva. You can't go wrong with anything you order here.I couldn't find anything negative to report on. The servers were very nice, well spoken, interactive and truly cared about you as a customer. Our waiter said he was there for 12 years. I will definitely go back to eat there as it was a great fun night out. I would highly recommend you try them.

During a recent visit to the city, we found ourselves with some time to spare before our trip to the top of the rock and stumbled upon this charming little café. Though we arrived close to closing time, the staff greeted us with smiles and were incredibly accommodating, ensuring our short wait was pleasant and worthwhile.

I indulged in a ham and gruyere baguette alongside a red velvet macaron, both of which were absolutely delightful. The prices were fair, especially considering the cafe's central location and the quality of the food, aligning well with what one would expect from similar establishments.

The café boasted a tempting array of baked goods, refreshing beverages, and substantial meal options that left a lasting impression. This spot is a treasure that I'm eager to return to, and without hesitation, I would recommend it to anyone looking for a quick, satisfying bite in a welcoming atmosphere.

Stopped by on a Saturday, around 1:30pm and there was a little wait, not bad at all. I'd been meaning to try out the pizza bagel for the longesttttttttttt time and finally did! It was delicious - everything I imagined it to be. My boyfriend got the Eggs a la Baz (two latkes, two poached eggs, nova salmon, chive + a fruit cup) which was also good! We also got a toasted whole wheat everything flagel w/ the nova + chive spread - this wasn't all that special, I'd skip next time. This is a cute spot to catch up and have brunch w/ friends or to take out-of-towners to!

I recently visited a local spot for Japanese curry and I must say, it didn't disappoint. Specifically, the curry at this particular location outshines its new branches. It stands a notch above Go Go Curry for me, mainly because of its superior breading – thinner and crispier – and perfectly cooked rice that's less sticky. The sauce here also wins with its more appealing flavor profile.

Another area where this restaurant shines is delivery. Unlike Go Go Curry, where the katsu tends to arrive soggy, the katsu from this place maintains its crunch even after a fifteen to twenty-minute journey. If you're in the mood for Japanese curry that retains its quality from kitchen to doorstep, this is the place to order from.

Title: A Delicious Detour for Hearty Vegetarian Fare

After a considerable trek outside of my usual haunts, I am thrilled to report that the journey to this charming eatery was well worth the distance. Ideal for small gatherings of 3-4 people, the no-reservation policy encourages a spry approach for diners.

Upon entry, I was greeted by a warmly inviting interior, adorned with cute ornaments that set the stage for an enjoyable ambiance. My culinary adventure began with the Deluxe Vegetarian Platter, partnered harmoniously with a vibrant vegetarian borscht soup, brimming with beetroot zest and a refreshing tang.

The platter itself was a celebratory showcase of comfort food: each pierogi, whether it be cheese, mushroom & sauerkraut, or potato, was a delightful parcel of flavor wrapped in pleasingly thick dough. Yet, it was the meatless cabbage roll, drenched in a rich mushroom gravy and tender to the bite, that stole the show, complemented by the unexpectedly comforting and hearty kasha (buckwheat) with onion on the side.

Even the bread served was not your standard fare, offering a sweeter note that was simply irresistible when dipped into the borscht. While the food was a hit, a dash more warmth and patience from the busy service staff would have perfected the experience.

Despite this minor note, I wholeheartedly endorse this restaurant for anyone looking to indulge in a new and hearty vegetarian experience. Rest assured, it won't be my last visit.

Had a delightful lunch experience at this charming neighborhood eatery recommended by a friend who lives nearby. Opted for the falafel sandwich which did not disappoint – it was flavorful and maintained a perfect moistness. The pita bread deserves a special mention, freshly baked and exceptionally fluffy, it was a standout. My friend's green shakshuka appeared equally appetizing. We enjoyed our meals in the pleasant outdoor seating area. All in all, a place worth visiting for a tasty, casual meal.

I approached this dining experience with high expectations, fueled by glowing reviews, only to find myself disappointed. The food was decidedly average, meriting a mere 3 out of 5 - an unexpected score for a restaurant that falls into the four-dollar-sign category. The ambiance did little to elevate the experience, overshadowed by a dark and somewhat dingy atmosphere which seemed at odds with its upscale pricing. Service too, fell short of the mark, leaving room for improvement. While I am open to the possibility of a return visit, there's an equal chance we may opt to search for a steakhouse more befitting of the premium experience and cost.

Got the chance to try out Abiko Curry on a Friday night with my girlfriend and two of her friends. I'd never heard of this spot, but they had been before and swore that it was worth traveling to Koreatown for. Even though it was below 30 degrees out I'm still happy I got to try this place! The dishes, service, and atmosphere all made for a surprisingly satisfying dinner in midtown.We got to the spot around 5:30 in the afternoon. Three of us were there and we were waiting for one more person in our group to arrive. They don't seat you unless your entire party is present so make sure you set a time to arrive. Good thing we did because this place was packed from the moment we arrived. They don't take reservations so I'd suggest coming early to make sure you're not left waiting for a table to become available, especially with a group of 4 or more.When it came time to order I choose the basic curry noodle with a side of chicken cutlet. Honestly a great choice since I looked at the menu beforehand and both these dishes were apparent must try's. I'd suggest getting both and mixing the meat into the noodles since the dishes are both really tasty and guaranteed to leave you satisfied.This spot is basically a long rectangle with seating on both sides of the restaurant. Smaller tables are in the front and their large group tables are in the back. Service was pretty fast since they were busy, but we didn't feel rushed. Just remember to get here early!!!

Stepping into Bowllin', nestled near Washington Square Park, is like finding an oasis of serenity, especially during off-peak hours. The soft hum of Korean tunes sets a pleasant backdrop for a meal that's both customizable and comforting.

Mirroring the concept of the previously reviewed MIGHTY Bowl, Bowllin' elevates the DIY rice bowl experience with a distinctly Korean flair. Whether you're decisive and go for one of their predesigned options or you're feeling creative and want to build your own bowl, the choices are plentiful and satisfying.

As a Korean cuisine enthusiast, I find Bowllin' to be the superior choice between the two eateries. My top pick would be the Bulgogi bowl. It's a harmonious concoction of savory beef, fresh lettuce, zesty kimchi, all crowned with a perfectly cooked sunny side up egg. While their chicken and noodles are respectable contenders, the Bulgogi bowl remains unbeatable.

In the realm of quick and personalized Korean-inspired eats, Bowllin' stands out as a must-try.

Came in with a friend on a rainy Thursday night for dinner. I arrived first and was seated in the back without a reservation or complete party which is always a plus. Once my friend arrived, it was a bit emptier and the waitress offered to move us to a better table. We didn't mind the one we were at but appreciated the courtesy and moved. We ordered a wine and a beer which took longer than I thought it should have to arrive. I settled on the salmon tacos from the small plates, which I wouldn't really consider small. It was plenty of food for me as a dinner! I like the flavor, however, found there was really too much salmon in them or was hard to get a good mix of all the toppings, the salmon overpowered it. It was also definitely dry, but the sauces did make up for it. My friend ordered the steak salad cooked medium, which came out definitely rare. She said the salad was over dressed, and wished the dressing had come on the side. For the most part our waitress was attentive and kind. It was overall a great way to pass the evening with a friend, cozy atmosphere and lots of food options to come back to try.

My visit to this restaurant was an absolute delight, starting with Thomas, our waiter, whose service was impeccable. The cappuccino I had was a delicious and frothy treat, followed by fresh, warm bread with butter that tasted amazing. My boyfriend thoroughly enjoyed his perfectly cooked 14-ounce rib-eye steak, while my salmon entrée was served hot and tasted incredibly fresh. We indulged in a peanut butter brownie sundae for two, which was simply amazing and concluded our meal on a high note. The location is conveniently close to the tree, and the prices are reasonable for the area. This dining experience was fantastic for our first time, and I'm already looking forward to returning.

Always my favorite Italian place around Columbia university. This location is about five mins walk front the engineering building, and they have lunch special. PLEASE NOTE:THIS PLAVE IS CASH ONLY. Theo pasta is homemade and quite chewy, and they put eggs in their dough, so you can see the light yellow color. My favorite dish is casarecca allá norcina. This is a creamy dish wish mushroom and sweet sausage. Probably one of the best creamy sauce that I have ever tasted. In addition, they normally have specials written on the board. This time we tried a lentil soup, which is so good for the hot weather. It has sausage and other vegetables added in. Definitely worth a try if you were luck to have it as soup of the day. Highly recommended you to try it! It wasn't too pricy neither. I didn't discover this place till later of the school year, but I had already eaten there several times.

There are many factors in my life that make me feel blessed, but I have to say that my husband and I had a capital "M" moment tonight when we were truly blessed to be the first guests ever at Omakase Room by Maaser on their opening night. It was such an extraordinary experience, and I look forward to witnessing the incredible success that is undoubtedly on their horizon. I highly suggest you visit the place now, because I have a feeling that it will be very difficult to get a reservation in a few months. From the moment we entered the place, we were greeted with warmth and kindness, and a very minimalist but elegant and calming environment. The music is very soothing and the decor is very tasteful. It's a true omakase room, carefully designed and laid out by the chef himself. The chef and his staff are remarkable. They possess and project a genuine sense of joy in their hearts and have an optimism and love for their craft that permeates the entire experience. I haven't encountered an omakase chef like this in NYC, or perhaps ever. I realize I have yet to talk about the food itself, but I needed to address the ambiance and staff first. The sushi itself was nothing short of amazing. It was so incredibly fresh and well balanced with the perfect seasoning, whether it was seasoned with one of the chef's sauces, with caviar, or with one of seven different finishing salts they have, imported from around the world. We had the 17 piece omakase, and each piece was unique and flavorful and artistically presented. I should add that one of the pieces was a grade A5 Japanese wagyu, which is extremely special, and it was perhaps the single best piece of meat my husband and I ever tasted. I should also note that they are among only a few restaurants in NYC that are actually certified to serve true, authentic Japanese wagyu, and A5 at that. The very best grade. I honestly cannot wait to return to this place soon. We want to get our fix before it blows up with popularity, which is imminent and well deserved!

Made a reservation for 6 and couldn't be seated until everyone arrived. The service was ok, our server was a bit brusque in her manners but that could be due to a lack of awareness.Our food was very good and reasonably priced and the decor is very trendy and cute. The space is tight so be prepared for the noisy atmosphere. Overall a decent experience for thai food.

Fantastic meal and service. Located on the 6th floor of Macy's Herald Square. Amazing views of the Empire State Building, make sure you ask for a seat near the window.We passed on the Prix fixe menu. The meatball app is a must and so is the pizza. I went with the clam pizza which was big enough to share. It was flavorful but a little spicy, ask to go lightly on the red pepper flakes if you are sensitive to spicy foods.The cocktails are pricy at $15.00 each but worth it. You have to definitely get dessert and the gelato was amazing. Highly recommend!

Title: Game Night Joy

I visited this spot with friends to catch a game and had quite an enjoyable experience. The reservation process was seamless thanks to Eddy, who exhibited utmost courtesy both over the phone and upon our arrival. We settled into the lively atmosphere with pitchers of Bud Light and a side of sweet potato fries, which were typical of pub fare. The ambiance was as expected on game night – loud and energetic – contributing to a thrilling vibe that thankfully never tipped into chaos. Despite the somewhat brusque service, likely a side effect of the decibel levels, the place had a welcoming, dive bar charm that proved ideal for relaxing with friends. I'd consider coming back for another high-energy game viewing.

I came across this place surprisingly on Instagram and when I saw they had lobster Mac I knew I had to try it. I came here around 2pm and it wasn't busy, I was able to find a seat as it's not that big and place my order rather quickly. It took about 5 minutes to arrive and it was everything I wanted. The lobster was warm,tender and the Mac was very cheesy,cooked to perfection and seasoned well. Not to mention at a great price, I can't wait to come for another meal!!

Title: A Spicy Delight Worth the Wait

Review:

My experience at this restaurant was nothing short of amazing! Getting there at peak dinner time meant facing a daunting hour and a half wait, but the reward was a table laden with mind-blowing dishes. As a haven for spice enthusiasts, the cuisine pushes the limits of your taste buds, but believe me, it's irresistible - even if, like me, you're not the best with hot food. 

Among the standout dishes, the Stir-fried Pig Intestines were exceptional and a must-try. Prices hover around $15-20 per dish, making it quite reasonable when splitting the cost in a group. Beyond taste, the presentation is immaculate, demanding a spot on your social media.

If patience is one of your virtues, the wait is a small price to pay for a dining experience that will linger in your memory - and on your palate. Highly recommended for a memorable meal!

Historic Italian market converted into a restaurant with a world class brick oven. Fantastic whole branzino roasted with fennel in the oven. Highly recommended if you like fish, and enough for two to share. Pizzas are Neapolitan style, and quite legit, if that's what you like: charred on the bottom but soft and chewy. I really appreciate that they have a marinara pizza (that is, a plain Tomato Pie). Other dishes I've tried are more pedestrian. Service is hit or miss: always efficient, but sometimes lovely, sometimes indifferent.

I recently visited a traditional noodle shop in Chinatown, where the noodles lived up to expectations—good and reasonably priced. The drums noodle with minced pork was satisfying, exactly what I was craving. The service, however, was typical for Chinatown—nothing exceptional. It's time places like this aim to exceed rather than just meet the basic service expectations. A minor letdown was the lack of complimentary water, offering only bottled water or tea for purchase. While understandable from a business perspective, it's a small convenience that could enhance the dining experience. My advice: dine here for the delicious noodles, but consider bringing your own beverage to complement your meal.

I've been to this restaurant several times for lunch in the past and each time was great in every way. How can anyone top this?... by going there for lunch during restaurant week! My party of three ordered the pan seared salmon, roasted chicken breast and the signature cheese burger from their set menu. Our appetizers were the Field Greens Salad with Parmesan Vinaigrette and the New England Clam Chowder. Everything was delicious although the lack of side vegetables for the salmon and missing garnish for the burger was noticed when compared to my previous restaurant week dining last year.

I recently indulged in a pizza from a local joint and was pleasantly surprised by their Half Meatball and Half Pepperoni option for under $20. What's truly commendable is they don't slap on extra fees for choosing two different toppings, unlike some other places. Consistency is key here; my order has always been ready when promised, and the quality never waivers. Plus, they accommodate both cash and card payments without a hitch. Highly recommend for a fuss-free, tasty pizza experience!

This is my second time visiting Woodpecker and I am definitely glad I came back.My original review was one star due to a bad experience on Christmas Day; however, after explaining to management some of the issues we ran into, we were invited back to give Woodpecker a second try.It was a whole new restaurant! The food was great, the service was flawless and ambiance was prefect.My husband and I started our meal with the 'bread & spread' as well as the raw broccoli & miso salad; the butter that comes with the bread is to die for, while the miso dressing on the salad was mouth watering! For our main courses I had the gnocchi while my husband had the hamburger; my dish was great, with the delightful little ricotta dumplings surrounded by butternut squash. My husband said his burger was cooked perfectly, and he loved the fact that it was served on an English muffin (very original).Last but not least we ended our meal with the cinnamon Panna Cotta which was perfect in every way!I cannot forget about the service; our waiter was awesome and ensured we were taken care of throughout our meal.The evening was picture perfect and we will definitely be dining at Woodpecker in the future.

Tried this place before a Broadway show.  We were not disappointed.   We ordered the cheese ravioli, lasagna and shrimp scampi.   All were delicious but the scampi was to die for!   Cannot wait to go back and have it again.   You get garlic bread with your meal which is scrumptious...be prepared for major garlic breathe...lol.

Title: A Delightful Evening at Bettola on the UWS

Last night's impromptu visit to Bettola on the Upper West Side was a testament to the charm this neighborhood holds, particularly in its array of quaint restaurants with inviting outdoor seating. Without a reservation, we were greeted with the option of comfortable indoor or al fresco dining, thanks to the favorable weather and open windows that seamlessly blended the two experiences.

The ambiance of Bettola struck a delightful balance of cute and cozy, further enhanced by the mellow tunes of live music. The menu was a promising spread of Italian staples, with my eye catching the Quattro Stagione pizza. The kitchen's flexibility allowed for a ham-free version, featuring a fresh vegetable medley that graced the perfectly sized and sliced 12-inch pie.

While I savored the thin-crust pizza paired with a crisp Pinot Grigio, the rest of our party enjoyed the Salsiccia pizza and a robust chicken pasta dish. The swift service meant we dined contentedly and still made it to our movie on time.

Bettola delivered on all fronts—prompt service, rustic atmosphere, reasonable prices, and most importantly, delicious food. It's without a doubt that Bettola has earned a return visit from me.

Hate to do this, but I came back last Saturday afternoon with my family because I wanted them to finally try it but I was a little disappointed with the food and they weren't exactly wowed... Just wasn't as amazing as I remembered.There were a total of 5 of us, so I ordered the half chicken ($15) once again as well as the new pineapple chicken ($10.95). This was the perfect amount of food for us, as we finished everything without feeling overly full or still hungry. The orders were assembled within 2 minutes - we were amazed at how it was even quicker than fast food. We brought it upstairs to devour.Now, I don't know if it's the ginger rice or the sauces (I'm leaning more toward the sauces)... They must have a TON of MSG in them. I'm not usually the one to criticize msg in food because I know it's common (and necessary sometimes) but damn did I just put too much sauce on the chicken or something?? Because once again, I felt incredibly groggy for the rest of the day! Last time I thought it was because I overate, but I had a standard portion this time and still felt pretty horrible afterwards. My boyfriend couldn't help himself and bought an additional 2 sauces for 25 cents each (they actually do taste very good), but he also felt pretty crappy from them after our meal. I guess next time, no extra sauces and we gotta be super light w/ the ones they give us... would appreciate less msg in the recipe though!Additionally, I'm aware the chicken is supposed to be room temp but this time the rice was also... room temp. Not sure if the rice is supposed to be that way, but we would've preferred it to be warmer/hot. The flavor was still there though! But between the coldish rice and overly-msg'd sauces, we were a bit disappointed. I also got the thai milk tea but would've preferred it with ice.On a brighter note, the new pineapple chicken was delicious, and loved the presentation. No complaints there! The fried chicken was tasty and the pineapple slices underneath were very fresh. Came with a side of the sweet & sour sauce and ginger rice as well.

I've dined at this restaurant twice, once for their kamayan feast and another time for a regular dinner. To my surprise, the a la carte option surpassed the feast. The kamayan feast boasted an abundance of food, but it sadly lacked flavor and complexity. I prefer not to dwell on that underwhelming experience.

On a brighter note, the restaurant shines during happy hour and their regular dinner service. A recent visit allowed me to sample an array of appetizers and entrees, from quirky spam fries to delectable smoked fish dishes. The standout was undoubtedly the sizzling sisig – a perfectly seasoned, savory delight that wasn't too salty or overdone.

Other notable dishes included the smoked fishes and a delightful honey ham. The spam fries were exactly as one might expect: a fun novelty but nothing more. All things considered, I am keen on returning for their happy hour specials and enticing dinner menu.

Title: A Culinary Gem with Room for Service Improvement

I've dined at this restaurant on two separate occasions and have been consistently impressed by the exceptional cuisine. Each dish boasts a complex tapestry of flavors and textures that excite the palate. Every visit reaffirms my eagerness to return and explore more of their menu.

However, it's noticeable that the staff doesn't seem to share in the enthusiasm for their own fare. Each interaction has been met with a sense of unfamiliarity and a degree of discomfort that suggests a need for more training or experience.

Despite this, the kitchen's culinary prowess makes this a restaurant worth visiting. I remain hopeful that, with time, the front-of-house experience will match the kitchen's evident passion and expertise.

I visited this place a couple years back, maybe like 6 years ago? So having visited again just last week, I'm glad to see that things haven't changed all that much.I ordered a basil fried rice (essentially) and it was about $14. I think that this place is priced just about right given everything, and is a decent choice for thai food if you're coming here to eat with someone. I don't have many comments beyond this!

Returned last Saturday with a couple of friends who had never been here, and even though it was an overall good experience I feel like some of the food was a bit disappointing this time around.Started with the Chicken Satay ($11) which was perfect. Came with 4 skewers, chicken drenched in curry sauce and 4 small pieces of toast - delicious. The additional sauces on the side paired perfectly with the dish. As for entrees:- Khao Soy ($22) - I remembered how much I loved this dish last time, so ordered it again. Unfortunately it was just not the same. Not enough curry broth!! It ended up way too dry for my liking - the noodles were def not soaking in a curry like how they were supposed to.- Moo-Obb Nam Puaung / Grilled Marinated Pork w/ bok choy and Coconut Sticky Rice ($26) - I was super excited for the coconut sticky rice, but there was almost no coconut flavor or sweetness in it. It just tasted like regular sticky rice... meh. The pork was nicely marinated and tasty though, and I loved that it came with some veggies.- Royal Pad Thai ($24) - Had this the very first time I came (a couple of years ago) and thought it'd be the safest dish to go with. The prawns were lovely and indeed it was a good entree. We had over-ordered so we were already stuffed when we all got to this dish, but still thought it was good. Made for great leftovers the next day.Overall, I don't think anything really stood out this time around. Service was great though and because we arrived right around 5pm, we only had to wait about 5 min to get seated under the pretty lights of the main dining area.

Title: A Ramen Revelation in Hell’s Kitchen

If you're hunting for the best ramen in Manhattan, look no further. Nestled in the bustling streets of Hell's Kitchen, this gem is worth the trip from any borough, and it's certainly mine from Washington Heights.

On my latest visit, I ventured into a broth battle: Chicken Ramen vs. Miso Pork Ramen. The winner? The Chicken Ramen, hands down. Its broth was a masterful concoction—rich, almost buttery, yet surprisingly light, overshadowing the heavier miso alternative.

Do not, I repeat, do not skip on the fried chicken appetizer. It's a crispy delight that'll leave you contemplating a second round, but beware the imminent umami overload.

In a neighborhood crowded with noodle contenders, this spot reigns supreme. Whether you're a ramen rookie or a noodle connoisseur, make this your next stop. Trust me, your taste buds will thank you.

I visited Davinci Pizza Restaurant in the Financial District of Manhattan for a lunchtime slice on a busy Monday. The pizza, while decent enough to satisfy a craving, lacked a wow factor; the crust was notably limited and somewhat overly crunchy. Despite that, the Slice of White with ample rich ricotta spots was a highlight and worth ordering again, albeit without urgency.

Portion sizes were standard: $2.75 for a Plain Slice and $3.50 for a Specialty Slice, representing fair value for the area. The ambiance benefitted from the spacious layout and the warmth from the oven on a cool day, though cleanliness was an issue with messy, greasy tables detracting from the experience.

The restaurant managed a steady stream of customers, and service was commendably quick and efficient. Parking is limited to monthly garages, which is typical for the area. Overall, Davinci offers a functional pizza experience for those in FiDi without making a strong impression.

As I came in to write this review (I am way overdue -- it's been a few months since we went), I noticed how much emphasis on brunch and breakfast there was, and so my kind of neutral review may reflect that, since we went for dinner.As a few other folks who gave this place 3 stars mentioned, the place is just "fine." Nothing particularly stood out as amazing, and nothing was particularly off. I'll comment on the space, which others mentioned, too -- it is VERY small. We were a group of four, and were seated at the window seat at the front (next to a larger group of about 7?) and we were very uncomfortable. The seats themselves are uncomfortable, so a heads up for anyone who may have back or sitting issues. I saw that the manager had commented that the place was wheelchair accessible; I can't imagine someone with a wheelchair being able to navigate the space.Don't know that I'd say we had a poor or rude server; he wasn't the warmest, just kind of went through the motions.One thumbs up I'll give is someone in our party had very specific food restrictions, and the chef was able to accommodate her needs, so that's a real plus for anyone with food allergies or dietary specifications.Uploaded some photos of our dishes, but again, wouldn't necessarily rave or complain about any.

I recently visited this gem of a restaurant with an out-of-town colleague and was thoroughly impressed by their value-packed lunch special, priced starting at a modest $12. The variety was commendable: I enjoyed a warming miso soup, a delicious chicken katsu curry with rice, 3 delectable siomays, a fresh salad, and a tasty California roll. My colleagues were pleased with their salmon and chicken teriyaki options as well. The service complemented the food with its efficiency and friendliness. This spot is perfect for a quick lunch meetup, though I'd recommend a reservation for larger groups, especially given that by 12:30 pm on a Thursday, it was already packed to the last table. Definitely on my recommend list!

Title: A New Year's Eve Delight at Piccola Cucina, Soho

I had the pleasure of ringing in the New Year's Eve with lunch at the charming little Italian spot, Piccola Cucina, in Soho. Despite the holiday rush requiring a reservation and a bit of a wait upon arrival (a testament to its popularity), the experience was nothing short of delightful.

The ambiance struck a rare balance between a buzzing energy, with periods of club-like music that had both staff and patrons singing along and quieter moments for conversation—a festive duality for the holiday.

Highlighting their lunchtime appeal was an irresistible special—select dishes for just $11. The ravioli and maccheroni paired perfectly with an impressive selection of wines and non-alcoholic beverages.

The wait staff's friendliness added warmth to the coziness of this Italian gem. The experience was so inviting, I'd recommend Piccola Cucina for any occasion, be it group gatherings, romantic dates, or meals with friends and family. A tip of the hat to this perfect corner of Italy in Soho!

My return visit to this gem for dinner reaffirmed my love for their mouth-watering Mediterranean cuisine. The starters set a high bar with delectable hummus and pita, alongside a spicy feta that didn't skimp on the heat. The main courses truly showcased their culinary prowess, with the grilled Portuguese octopus being a standout, its smoky char pairing perfectly with the tender flesh.

The roasted eggplant was a revelation in simplicity, and the falafel was crisp on the outside, fluffy on the inside. Not to be overshadowed, the cauliflower proved a robust companion, and the lamb kebab was skewered perfection, bursting with savory goodness. This spot remains a must-visit for anyone in search of authentic, flavor-packed Mediterranean fare. I'm already planning my next meal here.

Came to BLACKBARN this past Sunday after a workout with a friend. It was pretty busy and didn't have many tables available so we just sat at the bar -- surprisingly roomy. This place isn't anything too special except for the live music they have on Sunday's.The ambiance was cute, dimly lit with cute decorations lingering from the holidays. The bartender that served us was very friendly, but busy. Everything took its sweet time coming out and it was a little cold upon arrival. Food was, as stated earlier, nothing special. We got the fried chicken and waffles and while decent, was almost too dry to scarf down. Swallowing those waffles felt like eating chalk. The sauce couldn't even save the texture unfortunately. Good thing the side salad had some moisture! The side of sweet potatoes was also extremely burnt to a crisp. How could they even serve that? The cakes with ricotta and honeycomb were also too dry to eat. Super disappointing that I had to wash down each bite with water to avoid dehydration. The thing that saves this restaurant was really the live music  and overall decor. Passing by is sufficient enough.

My recent dining experience at this restaurant was exceptional across the board! The service deserves a standing ovation; our waitress was the epitome of attentiveness and warmth. The vibe of the place struck a perfect balance between cozy and contemporary, creating a welcoming environment for diners.

The menu, though concise, packed a punch with every dish bursting with flavor. The scampi, in particular, was a unanimous hit among my friends and me. It's a dish that shouldn't be missed and clearly showcases the kitchen's prowess.

I wholeheartedly recommend making a reservation to avoid missing out on this culinary gem. I'm already planning my next visit to enjoy more of their mouthwatering offerings.

If you find yourself pondering where to enjoy an authentic and satisfying lunch, look no further. The Farmer's lunch at this spot is an absolute steal at $18 per set. The meal kicks off with a comforting bowl of rustic miso, accompanied by brown rice, tangy pickled radish, and bold kimchi – though, be advised, they might not be keen on offering refills for the latter.

For the main event, you're treated to a selection of entrees paired with a fresh basket of cucumber, lettuce, shiso leaves, and mild pepper. We dove into the Galbi, bulgogi, and spicy pork. The bulgogi was exactly as it should be – exquisitely tender and moist. The spicy pork impressed with a vibrant slice of gochujang, its flavors meticulously bursting in every bite. Yet, it was the Galbi that stole the show, its charred, succulent cubes so full of flavor they overshadow the need for extra seasoning.

Not to be overlooked, the Uni Bibimbap was a textural symphony of nutty, creamy sea urchin and vibrant roe, each element complementing the other to create a perfectly balanced dish.

In conclusion, lunchtime at this establishment is not to be missed. The quality and price point make for an unmatched dining experience.

I recently grabbed a takeaway lunch from a local spot near my office and was thoroughly impressed. The soup was savory, and the chicken basil dish hit the perfect note of spiciness for my palate. Each bite confirmed the freshness and authenticity I'm always searching for in this cuisine. The lunch specials are an excellent perk, making it a regular go-to for me. Although I've yet to dine in, the inviting decor has caught my eye, promising a lovely dine-in experience. I'm eager to return, particularly to sample their pad Thai. Definitely a spot worth visiting when you're in the area!

"If there's a line, there's a reason" - people flock to this place, and if they say "hidden gem", it's really because it's hidden. On the second floor of what looks like an office building. Let me get my one gripe out of the way first...  we signed in and were quoted a seating time of 7:50pm.  We didn't sit down until 8:40. Had I known that, it might have influenced our eating location. Not b/c I care, I was with the kiddos. Ok, that said, the waiting area was slamming, tons of people coming out of the elevator and crammed into the holding pen. And the hostess stand had two (incredibly friendly) hostesses. They have snacks and drinks while you wait which was helpful. Also have a coat check. The decor was fine for the venue and the music was spot-on ( and such). We ended up doing the $87 beef platter with ribeye, skirt and short ribs. Incredible. Also did pork belly and pork short ribs - standout. I would have loved to cook table side, but didn't even have to, our awesome server really did most of the work. The meats looked soooo good raw, quality. The experience comes with all the salty sides / dipping sauces, and lettuce for wrapping and onions for grilling. We started with a cast iron pan, then they swapped out to an open grill. Also ordered two noodle dishes which were fantastic and gigantic portions. Got a small bottle of soju which it turns out wifey didn't like so I drank as much as I could then shared with the friendly table next to us (from Australia).

When @phobarnyc posted a recent photo of their oxtail pho ($15.95) I knew I just had to have it and boy was it good, but you need to get it with the their 25 hrs crazy rich broth (additional $5) #..$21 for a bowl of pho, yes, shocking, but OMG, it was so good. It's not your traditional Vietnamese pho (like phobang or phobest), it's a modern upscale kind of pho. I mean, oxtail isn't traditional is it?..The size is their oxtail (swipe for closeup and the layer of fat around it) was half of the pho (there's also 2 more of the end of the tail pieces. It was so fatty and tender, it literally fell off the bone. You will need good chopstick skills (like myself) to pick up the pieces after it falls off the bone. You can use the spoon too, but what fun is that?..That 25hrs crazy rich broth. It's so beefy, so flavorful, so delicious. I'm not a broth person and I drank about half of the bowl. They load up on the scallion so it made it even better. When I saw the word "rich" I thought it would be thick but it wasn't thick consistency at all. It was your typical pho broth consistency except lots more flavor. You can taste the 25hrs... ..The oxtail is part of their premium selection, they offer classics with more reasonable prices but trust me, get something from their premium selection or at least just get their crazy rich broth... .

Update: One of my favorite is places in the LES. Food is outstanding, delicious unique cocktails, music is great, awesome environment and standout service. It meets all expectations and surpasses them. 5/5

I came here with some friends late afternoon on a Sunday. Had a little bit of a wait but it wasn't too bad - probably waited 20 minutes to be seated for 5 people. We shared an order of the chicken tatsuta-age appetizer. This Japanese fried chicken was so good! It was crispy but not too oily and the chicken was really good. I got the seasonal udon, which was little neck clams in a light and aromatic broth. It was delicious! The clams were fresh and the udon was nice and chewy. It was really refreshing! I also tried my friend's chicken curry udon. It was warm and hearty, great for a rainy day. Chicken was tender and the curry broth wasn't too heavy or salty. Overall, the food was great and I would highly recommend. Service was also very good - servers were attentive and came over to ask how we liked the food. Everything we ordered came out in a timely manner.

Sooo good. We got the Basil Udon with Crispy Duck and Top Thai fried rice with beef. The Basil Udon is soo good. It's so flavorful and they give you so much duck! The duck was tender and delicious. The fried rice was good, but after eating the udon, it didn't have as much flavor. They give you a good amount of meat in this dish too.I definitely want to try their curry, pad Thai and pad see ew.

So, this place is just like your typical bar in the city. Large TV's all throughout, a very long list of beer and even a long list of whiskey, it is pretty loud on a typical week night, good for happy hour and booze one sixpoint beer $8, the bathroom is in the lower level and tbh it could use some upgrade. see my pics! If you are looking to speak loud and lean in close to your company's ear for them to be able to hear you speak, you are in the RIGHT place! But let's be honest, most bars are this way during happy hour. Also, they ask for ID in the entrance!

I recently dined at this establishment and came away with mixed feelings. While the food was passable, it failed to impress, hovering around the realm of average. Unfortunately, the service left much to be desired; both the cashier and waitress came across as rather impolite. It's possible that a Sunday rush and potential understaffing may have contributed to their attitudes, but it nonetheless tarnished the dining experience.

A significant issue was the pacing at which our meals arrived—staggered and slow, leading to an awkward and disjointed dining experience where some of us had finished our meals while others were just beginning. This certainly detracted from the communal joy of eating together. Despite these issues, I believe every customer deserves a consistently high level of service, which was not the case here.

A really lovely meal and atmosphere. My boyfriend took me here for an early Valentine's Day. We always go out the night before because we much prefer a quiet intimate dinner. The service was great as is the service at most upscale Japanese restaurants: unobtrusive, informative, and friendly but not overly so. The meal was good. Nothing truly blew me away but I genuinely enjoyed 90% of our dishes. We ordered the larger tasting menu. It's definitely filling which is a plus as most tasting menus leave me hungry. I wasn't wowed by the meal but I was satisfied. Some standouts include the scallop dish, the tofu amouse bouche, and the rock fish dish (love the texture and the sauce). Overall, I'd go back because I think the menu is a great deal for what you get. They also had a great sake selection. Pretty good meal and also would serve as a good stepping stone into the NYC Japanese food scene.

Da Gennaro was a nice break in Little Italy - beautiful decor, and its freshly made pastas are delicious.My friend and I came by to visit around 3pm on a Saturday, and we ordered the Fettuccine Alfredo ($20) and the Spaghetti Alla Bolognese ($22). While the portions were slightly smaller than I would like for the price and the food's presentation made it seem very homemade (aka just plopped it on the plate), the pasta really came through in the authenticity of the flavors and texture. My friend and I agreed that the fettuccine alfredo was really salty - as if the chef had accidentally put in a tablespoon of salt as opposed to a teaspoon to the dish - but the spaghetti alla bolognese was fantastic. There is both indoor and outdoor seating, and though they advertise "strong air conditioning" indoors, there's basically no difference since the "indoor seating" is simply under a roof with all-open walls/windows. The waiters were at least very friendly with us, but service was just okay. This was considering the fact that we needed to look for someone to wave over whenever we had run out of water for a long time, needed something, or wanted the check, but overall the spaghetti was so fresh and delicious that I would probably go back again.

Title: A Feast of Mediterranean Delights

My experience at this restaurant was a delightful surprise, marked by an overwhelming abundance of food. The horiatiki salad was a refreshing departure from the conventional Greek salad, lacking romaine but still packed with flavor. Yet, it was the octopus that stood out, contending for the title of the best in New York, a sentiment I share wholeheartedly.

The array of spreads accompanied by the exceptional pita bread, overshadowed the standard bread offering. The Mediterranean sea bass I ordered was cooked to perfection, although the accompanying beets and lemon potatoes, while enjoyable, fell short of their potential. A word of advice—opt for the lemon potatoes as a side rather than a separate dish unless you're incredibly hungry, as the portions are generous.

The only drawback was the olive oil, which if of higher quality, could elevate this restaurant to one of my top picks in the city. Though a complimentary dessert was offered, the substantial meal left no room for it.

In summary, the restaurant left a lasting impression, and I am eager to return, perhaps to try the calamari, expecting it to match the high bar set by their octopus. A truly great meal worthy of a revisit.
I am not a vegan or a vegetarian but wanted to try this place. Trued their burger and the midtown melt. Liked the flavor of the food and the service. Overall,Food - 4/5Service - 4/5 Atmosphere - 4/5

Title: Hidden Culinary Delight in K-Town with a Quirky Caveat

I recently visited a culinary gem in K-Town that tantalized my taste buds with its delectable Korean pub fare and inventive drinks. Despite its peculiar refusal to accept Visa payments – a definite inconvenience in NYC – the restaurant offers a delightful dining experience.

The place shines with its range of shared small plates and mouth-watering Korean specialties. The standout was their signature half melon soju drinks; a refreshing and creative concoction served in watermelon or honeydew 'cups' that's as impressive to behold as it is to sip.

The army stew is an absolute must-try, a hearty bowl brimming with diverse flavors from mushrooms to spam and subtly melted cheese, creating a comforting medley perfect for any day, rain or shine. Complementing the stew, the fried dumplings and garlic chive pancake were fried to perfection – crispy without the peril of searing your tongue.

In summary, this spot is a must-visit for anyone seeking authentic Korean pub food with a twist. Just remember to bring a payment alternative to Visa.

Title: A Solid East Village Burger Experience at A-OK

My recent visit to A-OK, prompted by its high Yelp ratings, was a pleasant experience overall. The East Village ambiance met expectations, unpretentious and casual. Contrary to some online feedback, the service was notably commendable with no hitches during my visit.

The menu boasted a decent range of options, and I opted for the EastSider burger priced fairly at $12.50. This bacon cheeseburger came stacked with ham, mushrooms, tomatoes, and onions. While flavorful, I found the toppings a touch too soft for my liking, which made them challenging to bite through and enjoy seamlessly with the burger.

Another misstep was my choice to have the burger cooked medium-rare. The patty lacked cohesion, crumbling more than I would have preferred. Next time, I'd stick to a medium doneness for a firmer bite.

On the upside, the accompanying Corly fries were a highlight, adding a satisfactory crunch to my meal.

In summary, A-OK serves up a decent burger at a good price point, but with a few tweaks to the cooking and topping textures, it could elevate the experience. I'm looking forward to a return visit to explore other burger options on their menu.

Tucked away in a cozy corner, this little gem serves up Korean and Japanese delights, with poké as a standout option. The seats are limited, so expect a full house come lunchtime. Patience is key, as meals are made to order, but a quick phone call ahead can save you the wait. I relished the kalbi bowl from the daily specials—generous in portion and rich in flavor. On another note, while the tonkotsu ramen boasted a tasty broth, it erred on the salty side and faced a packaging misstep for takeout; the paper bowl wasn't quite up to the task, leading the noodles to adhere to the sides, complicating the broth addition. Despite that, it's a solid pick for local workers seeking a good meal, with the added bonus of a warm-hearted owner who adds a personal touch to the dining experience.

We made rsvp for our friends bday dinner, funny thing here u get charged $25 per person for cancellations, we arrived on time & still had to wait almost 30 minutes for the table now I understand u can't rush people still pretty annoying, because of our long wait time they were kind enough to hook us up with some free appetizers. they gave the Mushroom toast very good & the Avocado toast both equally tasty. Drinks, we had some Rose wine the wine was good went well with our meal. On the dishes we tried The Scorched cauliflower this was good with roasted garlic & some capers not bad. the favorite was the House made Spaghetti great taste with the carbonara , mushrooms & onions. The Artichoke toast was delicious great taste with the spinach & black truffle. my least liking dishes were the Celery root this was ok & the Paella this was not a good one for me.  Very small location, dimly lit & it was a bit too warm inside ... would be nice if they had some additional fans or something after eating & drinking u feel like u are going to past out because of the heat not fun. Heat aside we had a good time & enjoyed our meal, I am not vegan but this place is very good & one of the few u can enjoy even if u are not vegan.

Very crowded on a Saturday night. It is very loud, so if your looking for a quiet place don't come here. The waitress was new on the job for approximately 2 weeks. She was attentive at all. She got the drink order wrong, and the food took forever to come. The ribs were average, not seasoned enough. Overall the place is very average, and I wasn't impressed.

I really love this place. It was one of the first restaurants I came to when I first moved to the city and since then I have been many times with family, coworkers and friends. The food is consistently great. The chips and guac are delicious and so are the ahi tuna tacos. My go to meal is the super egg taco with the salsa and queso on the side, it's unbelievable. They also have great margaritas.

Title: A Hidden Gem Just Steps from the Subway

I chanced upon a remarkable street food stand just minutes from exiting the subway, and what a fortunate discovery it was! The food here exceeded all expectations – fresh, flavorful, and absolutely worth the brief wait. While there was a minor hiccup in communication, a friendly local and the affable vendor bridged the gap with some impromptu translation and shared humor over Vietnamese phrases.

I opted for the beef, which was a steal at just $3. Served in a modest plastic to-go container, the portion was deceptively sufficient, allowing each member of our group to savor a mouthful. The dish arrived piping hot, brimming with steam and taste that left us yearning for more. Alas, if not for our ongoing culinary adventure, I would have gladly doubled down on this delightful offering.

I would wholeheartedly recommend this spot to anyone in Chinatown looking for authentic, delectable street fare. Though I'm unsure if this cart is a mainstay or a culinary nomad, it's a must-visit if you find it on the Main Street. Don't miss out on this unassuming culinary delight!

As Thomas Wolfe told us, "you can't go home again." That is unfortunately too true for the truly iconic Four Seasons. Having eaten many times at the old Four Seasons I was really looking forward to a memorable meal. While many of the old touches were there, the magic is totally gone. Like an aging slugger who plays one too many seasons, the Four Seasons should have retired with its epic reputation fully intact.

Title: A Culinary Triumph to Ring in the New Year!

My New Year's Eve dinner at this bustling hotspot kicked off with a minor 15-minute delay on our 10:30 PM reservation, but it was a non-issue considering the vibrant atmosphere. Our exceptionally stylish and attentive waiter shone with 5-star service, making sure we were well taken care of throughout the evening.

The appetizers set the bar high, with chicken yuba dumplings brilliantly crafted from tofu skin that left me in awe of its innovative flair. The spicy crispy shrimp also delivered a memorable punch of flavor. For sushi aficionados and skeptics alike, the sundried tomato and avocado roll is a must-try, surprisingly standing toe-to-toe with the scrumptious crispy tuna rice.

Main courses were nothing short of exquisite. The Moro miso organic chicken paired with forbidden rice transported me to a tropical paradise with every bite, while the grilled branzino, with its crispy exterior and juicy interior, was elevated by a tantalizing ginger ponzu sauce.

While the nonalcoholic beverages were unremarkable, opting for bottled wine or champagne is the way to go. A small caveat—be prepared with your own toilet paper just in case, as the restrooms fall short on stock during busy times. Despite this minor hiccup, I can't recommend this restaurant enough for a dining experience that's sure to impress.

Picked up the black sesame and cream cheese sandwich (black + white), chicken katsu sandwich, corn dog nuggets, and spicy chicken kimbap.The katsu sandwich was the best out of everything! Flavorful and filling, not too heavy. The black and white sandwich would have been better if there was more of the black sesame, but the cream cheese was overpowering it. I wouldn't mind getting it again though because it's different from your normal PB&J.The spicy kimbap and corn dog nuggets were both ok. I don't know if I would get those again.

Title: Mild Mala Experience in FiDi

I ventured into this restaurant with hopes of sating my craving for authentic mala heat, akin to the likes that Mala Project delivers, only to be met with a watered-down version catering to the American palate. The mala peanuts, priced at $5, lacked the fire I anticipated, leaving much to be desired even after finishing the entire dish. It could perhaps appeal to those who typically shy away from spice and are looking to experiment with just a trace of mala flavor.

My main course, the $10 spicy Chicken noodle soup, fell flat when held against the robust and fiery offerings from Xi'an Famous Foods. It was a passable dish but starkly underwhelming for anyone chasing the genuine mala burn.

It's disappointing, especially given the prime FiDi location and the appealing interior of the restaurant. The search for that authentic mala kick in the Financial District continues.

Title: A Taste of Spain at Mercado Little Spain, Hudson Yards

Mercado Little Spain is a dazzling culinary highlight in the burgeoning gastronomic landscape of Hudson Yards. As my girlfriend and I meandered along the High Line on a Saturday morning, our search for a delightful snack led us to this Spanish-inspired market – a true embodiment of the diverse food offerings of this new west side haven.

Upon entering, we were greeted by an array of bars and booths, each presenting a unique ambiance behind their counters. The modern decor seamlessly blended with the individual character of the spots, dedicated to an assortment of Spanish delights including seafood, meats, cheeses, and exquisite wines.

Our choice was a booth offering French-style "jambon" sandwiches, a nostalgic nod to our recent sojourn in France. The Spanish take on this classic did not disappoint; a thin yet flavor-packed creation with high-quality meats and mouthwatering cheese, all sandwiched between perfectly toasted bread that added a satisfying crunch to every bite.

While the price point of $16 felt a bit high for the size of the sandwich, the premium ingredients justified the cost. Mercado Little Spain is more than just a market – it's an experience. Whether you're out for a dine-in meal, a casual snack, or a drink with friends, this market caters to all cravings. It's a must-visit spot for anyone exploring Hudson Yards, offering a slice of Spain amidst the urban sprawl of New York City.

I recently visited a restaurant that certainly left an impression, especially with its seafood and tapas offerings. The clams and mussels were notably jumbo-sized, making them a standout choice for shellfish enthusiasts. The truffle fries are not to be missed; they're a must-order item that perfectly complements any meal.

The spicy chicken tapas was another highlight, delivering a punch of flavor with just the right level of heat to keep things exciting. However, the experience did have a slight hiccup when it came to dessert; the cheesecake, while accompanied by a generous portion of fruits, felt overpriced as the advertised rice wine essence was notably absent from the palate. Overall, the dining experience was a delightful journey of flavors, slightly marred by the expectation vs. reality of the dessert pricing.

I recently visited a restaurant that was conveniently open at 1am when late-night options were scarce. The wait time was minimal, which was appreciated. I found the food to be fairly average; the main dish's sauce skewed too sweet for my taste and didn't seem quite fresh. The dumplings we tried were passable, nothing remarkable. This establishment is suitable for those urgent hunger pangs when immediate sustenance is the priority. On the plus side, the staff was notably friendly, adding a warm touch to the overall experience.

Whenever I find myself in the bustling heart of Manhattan, particularly around Times Square, I make a point to duck into this gem of a spot for lunch. Their special is a steal – under $14 for an ample spread, including two starters and a main course.

I typically kick off my meal with the zestful Tom Yum Shrimp Soup, which boasts a single medium shrimp, mushrooms, and scallions immersed in a piquant broth that awakens the palate. The Vegetable Dumplings, served two per order, are a perfect follow-up, consisting of a soft wrapper enveloping a savory filling.

As for entrees, I'm torn between the sweet and savory pineapple fried rice and the classic pad Thai; each dish bursts with authentic flavors. And though the base price is generous, there’s the option to elevate your meal with additional proteins like chicken, beef, or more shrimp for a modest upcharge.

On days when I feel more indulgent, the prefixed menu for just over $24 is a true delight. It concludes the culinary experience on a high note with fried ice cream—a cold and creamy contrast to the hot and flavorful main courses.

Service here is always on point, with attentive staff ensuring a pleasant dining experience. It's no wonder this place has become a staple for my midday cravings.

I am no vegan! With that being said, I love me a good steak. Initially I was coming for the Saltbae Tomahawk ($275.00) which is a high marbled, mustard marinated, bone in Ribeye. Coming from a Broadway show, we ended up getting to the restaurant pretty late (11pm) so we opted for something quick & light. Although the restaurant closes at 12am, I didn't want to rush thru my food. I'm not a big burger person but I've heard that their signature Nusret Burger was really good and they weren't lying. It's one of the best burgers I've tasted. It was chargrilled with carmelized onions, cheese, juicy, and came with fries. I had the meat sushi as an appetizer which was suprisingly delicious and their signature dessert, the pistachio Baklava with goat milk ice cream will have me definitely paying another visit. The downside to my experience was the seating. I didn't like the location of the table. It was off to the side where it's heavily trafficked and couldn't enjoy my food or conversation because of the amount of people that were walking by. For 2 people, I would have liked the seating to be a little more intimate but yet I was seated in an aisle. Despite the uncomfortability, the food was delicious, the drinks were good, an the ambiance was rich & sexy. I didn't get my steak so I'll definitely be making my way back. With a better seat of course.

Title: A Korean Feast That's Kind on Your Wallet!

My recent visit to this Korean gem left my taste buds dancing and my wallet intact! With an incredibly fair total of about $80 for three diners, the value was as impressive as the food.

The menu selections, from the crispy seafood and scallion pancake to the chewy and spicy seafood tteokbokki, were spot on. The pork belly and spicy pork were particularly addicting, with the perfect balance of flavor and heat. A delightful array of banchan graced our table, with the standout being the small anchovies paired with peanuts.

Despite initial doubts, the portions were generous, leaving us overwhelmingly satisfied. This spot is one to bookmark – amazing food, great prices, and an experience that calls for a return visit.
It was very packed the time I went. Took us half an hour to get a seat. The drinks we got were pretty pricey and did not taste good. It's a great place for aesthetic pictures though.

I am very conflicted as I write this review right now. The overall experience was positive from the service perspective. The host and waiter were attentive and nice. The wine and food came out on time. We started out sharing the Gorgonzola and pear salad. The name and the description of the salad set expectations at a certain level that the salad we ended up getting could barely touch... It was very lackluster. It was also 14 dollars without any protein with it. I've had significantly better salads at to go places like sweet greens and west side market for cheaper prices. Just based on this salad alone, I couldn't give  this place more than a 3 star. The pasta I got was very good though. If we hadn't ordered and tried the salad, I would've given this place a 4-star for the pasta itself. It had a great creamy and garlicky sauce with amazingly cooked shrimps! It came with two huge shrimps but there were cut up smaller pieces of shrimp mixed into the pasta as well. I would definitely come back for this dish... My friend got the eggplant parm dish, which looked good, but I didn't try any of it. She thought it was good, but nothing special.

I recently ordered the Tum Kor Moo Yang with a side of sticky rice through the Caviar app, which had the added bonus of free delivery. The dish was a delightful surprise with the perfect level of spiciness and ample servings of succulent grilled pork neck. The flavors were on point, making for a truly satisfying meal. However, the portion size left me wanting more; the menu's classification of the dish as a "salad" was somewhat misleading, without indicating the size. I would happily order from this place again, but I'd be sure to add an extra side or dish to ensure a hearty meal.

I came here of a Friday afternoon and the place was pretty empty, but the take out section was busy.I have been here twice, and I had a great time both times. I decided to return a second time because I was craving a GOOD steak and this restaurant satisfied that craving for me!!! The steak was tasty, but it could have been cleaned a bit better. The pina colada was refreshing!!!The restaurant and the employees are very welcoming. The restaurant (yes, the place) just makes you feel good. They were preparing for a beach party, later, that night for the 2019 graduates. Love a place that celebrates accomplishments!!!Oh, and I did NOT get my free bread!!! :(* BUT, I would definitely return a third time!

I thought the food was cool. Significant amount of hype around this place and I dont see why. The noodles tasted a little undercooked. Broth was real nice. Egg I discovered at the end buried at the bottom. The pork gyoza dumplings were good. Seats about 20ppl.What I especially didnt like was the bathroom. Bruh if this is where your staff is cleaning their hands, im surprised I didnt get sick!

Title: A Cozy Spot for Italian with a Twist

From the moment we stepped into this charming Italian eatery, we knew we were in for a treat. The pastas and main courses had us relishing every bite, and the desserts were the cherry on top of a delightful dining experience.

I ventured into the exotic with a pasta dish featuring spicy clams, which, to my surprise, conjured up flavors reminiscent of Thai cuisine. Although unexpected, the zesty lime and fried chili accents offered an exciting kick, perhaps a bit too fervent for traditionalists seeking Italian authenticity.

The carbonara, however, stole the show. It was a creamy, comforting masterpiece that I would boldly declare the crown jewel of their pasta offerings.

For the main course, I sampled the branzino. The fish was perfectly cooked with a delectable crispy skin, although the olives nestled at the bottom weren't quite to my taste, dialing my personal rating down to 3.5 stars for this particular dish.

As for the sweet finale, the desserts were flawless. The standout was undoubtedly the olive cake - a surprising delight that left a lasting impression of culinary creativity.

This cute and cozy restaurant didn't just serve us a meal; it provided a delicious escapade that's sure to beckon us back for more.

Very busy here at 1:30pm on a Friday afternoon. Another hankering for their Vegetable Tagine.  This time it wasn't too salty and there were plenty of fresh garnishes so there is crunch with every bite. It usually comes with potatoes, but I think it would be too filling so I always opt out of those.  Perfect for when you feel under the weather. Warms you up and is tasty as well as healthy.

I was very pleased with the service here. Everyone was so friendly and kind. It's such a cozy restaurant with an upstairs seating. I am so sad that it wasn't a five star rating because I wanted to like it. The restaurant offers a lot of options for vegetarians and non vegetarians. I ordered lamb saag, and chicken tandoori. The lamb saag was good but the lamb was not as soft as I would have liked, and the saag was very puréed and creamy (depending on different restaurants some are more puréed and creamier than others and I prefer more of a hearty spinach with more ginger and garlic and less cream). The tandoori chicken had a lot of flavor and had a nice Smokey charred grilled taste. Nonetheless, I was disappointed that it was on the bone. I think this definitely would add more flavor but I like having chunks/Kebob style. Rice is very fluffy. We would have ordered dessert but we were brought the check right away and we weren't asked if we wanted to have dessert or tea. Indian desserts are our favorite.
