I am not going to say I wouldn't return but I wasn't very impressed. My stomach wasn't also in the best shape later that evening (and Indian food is 90% of my diet and this never happens).

Title: A Sushi Gem in NoMad – High Tech Meets Delicious

I recently discovered this fantastic fast food sushi spot tucked away in NoMad. The ambiance is trendy with a hint of cutting-edge, thanks mainly to the convenience of touch screen ordering. For Manhattan, the prices are a steal, which was a pleasant surprise.

The manager, a delightful woman with infectious enthusiasm, enhances the experience. I sampled the Yuzu yellowtail roll for just $4.60, and it was nothing short of brilliant. My appetite still unsatisfied, I ventured back to the counter to indulge in a spicy tuna roll. Fair warning: it packs a punch that lives up to its "spicerama" reputation, but it's definitely worth a try for those who dare.

In short, this place is a great find, and I'm already planning my return trip tomorrow. A little piece of advice: expand to Huntington Village! Your unique concept would surely dominate the dining scene there.

There's only one simple rule you'll need to follow to enjoy some authentic, fresh, delicious tacos at this eatery in NYC. "No Ticket, No Tacos." Essentially you hold onto your ticket order once you pay and the move to the left to give it to one of the cooks to make your order, so you best believe I held on for dear life for mine until it was time to hand it over, periodt!I ordered one of each taco on flour tortillas; carne asada (grilled steak), pollo asado (grilled chicken), adobaba (marinated pork), & nopal (grilled cactus).  After throwing some topping on them joints, they were pretty damn tasty; moreover, adding an ice-cold bottle of Squirt to my order made for a perfect dinner. Be mindful that while there are tables, there are no chairs, and that a line going outside the door has the potential to form, so plan accordingly.

Title: Traditional Touches Shine at Mixed-Fare Eatery

My experience at this establishment left me contemplating between three and four stars—settling on a solid three and a half. The highlight was undoubtedly the service; attentive staff ensured that our bread basket was abundant, tables were promptly cleaned after each course, and our water glasses were diligently topped off. The cutlery was replaced with each new dish, reflecting an impressive attention to detail.

The cuisine, however, was a tale of highs and lows. Seafood options fell short of expectations, despite being elevated by a unique blend of herbs. In contrast, the meat selections were spot-on—both the Kenefes and the meat-stuffed cabbage are highly recommendable and would be my go-to for future visits. The custard-stuffed phyllo was a delightful cap to the meal. While the beet salad was undeniably fresh, it did not leave a lasting impression.

The ambiance of the restaurant was a feast for the eyes, with stunning hanging lamps and elegant arches contributing to a charming dining environment. Although prices are on the higher end, Restaurant Week offered an economical tasting of their traditional dishes, which they craft with finesse. Opting for these signature offerings promises a delightful culinary journey.

Title: Unconventional Service Meets Culinary Delight

My experience at this local eatery came with a few surprises, primarily in the service department which I found to be erratic. Unexpectedly, it’s a BYOB establishment – a detail only revealed once you've taken your seat. Despite this, the gastronomic journey was outstanding. The dumplings are a must-try; I'd return daily if possible, particularly for the soup dumplings and shu mai. The cold noodles adorned with king crab and uni were exceptional, especially when enhanced by the tang of vinegar from the dumpling accompaniment. It transformed into one of the most memorable dishes I've savored recently, boasting high-quality, impeccably textured crab.

The value extends to their tea offerings; the green tea retained its warmth throughout our meal. The orange chicken is a notable standout, elevating the familiar takeout dish with a refined balance of acidity and soy – though it did require a prompt request for its rice companion.

While we had to ask for glasses to enjoy our BYOB beers, the staff was accommodating with ice and service was prompt when needed. In summary, if you can navigate the peculiar service quirks, you're in for a culinary treat.

The space was big enough to hold walk ins although bustling on a quiet street. Really enjoyed their drinks and food: Had a margarita on the rocks with Cuban corn, paella, and croquets. It was a lot of fun. Service was very attentive!

Title: A Refreshing New Take on a Dumpling Delight

Having heard that the esteemed Joe's Shanghai had relocated, my curiosity and palate led me and a companion to explore its latest incarnation, particularly to indulge in their famed soup dumplings.

Upon arrival, the lack of a waiting crowd was a surprise—often a mixed signal for a popular spot—but this was a non-issue post-tasting. The new setting shed the old neon green lights for bright, welcoming illumination, enhancing the dining experience along with a spacious layout that effortlessly accommodated comfort and ease of movement – a significant upgrade from its former crammed quarters.

The culinary journey began with their heralded crab and pork soup dumplings, which lived up to their reputation in flavor, though a small construction flaw in the folds could leave one at peril of spilling the precious broth. Nevertheless, they were delicious enough to warrant a second order. The scallion pancakes were a delight, achieving the perfect balance of crispiness without being overly greasy, and the mini fried dough with condensed milk was a revelation—just mind the heat.

Service was attentive yet unobtrusive; our tea pot was never neglected, and our dishes arrived promptly at the peak of their heat. One note on protocol— the bill included a service charge, making additional tipping unnecessary, a detail I hadn't spotted on the menu but was clearly communicated on the bill.

With a thoughtfully designed restroom arrangement and overall satisfaction on all fronts, it's a hidden gem that dumpling enthusiasts will surely cherish. Would I return? For the dumplings and the newfound comfort, absolutely. Enjoy your visit, and savor those soup dumplings!

Stopped by for dessert and had the pineapple tarte tatin (caramelized pineapple ring with butter puff pastry and complemented by vanilla ice cream).They also provided a complimentary bittersweet chocolate and rosemary truffle.  Had robust chocolate flavor on the shell and a slight hint of rosemary in the ganache.Didn't have another meal in town, otherwise would have tried this place for lunch.  Had been to another Daniel Boulud restaurant and wasn't disappointed.

Nice family run Indian restaurant. Two floors, and we dined at the first floor, where the semi-open kitchen is in the back. All staffs are friendly.We were recommended fish (salmon) curry and lamb with spinach. Both were very delicious. Also ordered the sweet naan with dry fruits and nuts - good as well!

Title: Surprisingly Delightful Visit to Momosan

My recent venture to Momosan, lured by tales of tantalizing ramen, took an unexpected turn due to a broken AC, steering my palate away from steamy bowls to cooler choices. The Mango Matchashu cocktail was a standout start, a masterful blend of sake, mango, and matcha that proved both invigorating and delightful.

The culinary journey continued with two small plates: the tuna zuke don and peking duck taco. The former delivered generous cuts of soy-marinated tuna paired with nori and scallion, nestled atop white rice - each bite resonating with freshness. In contrast, the duck taco, ensconced in a wonton-like shell, boasted tender meat complemented by a crisp slaw and the sweet tang of hoisin sauce, making for a well-rounded and satisfying nosh.

Despite the initial setback, Momosan impressed. The anticipation for a rescheduled ramen rendezvous is high, but in the meantime, their other offerings have certainly etched a mark.

Ahhhh this even hurts me to give 3 stars because things were going so well here. The location is close to an animal shelter that I like to frequent and there are several things to do around the location. I originally found this place on yelp and since I LOVE Thai food it was a must try! Walking in it's a very quant space but they make it work. We were seated fairly quickly and was given our menus. We had several questions due to their being so many pictures but the names of the food weren't attached to each photo. For a starter we order the roti with coconut curry soup, main dishes were the Thailicious seafood spaghetti and the salmon and basil meal. The appetizer was delicious, the roti was a little crispy and had some burn marks but still was able to get the job done. The Thailicious seafood spaghetti was a real small serving and greasy. If you are hungry I would t suggest this meal. The salmon meal (you cannot select the spice level) was delicious and pretty filling. No dessert was ordered. The sad part was towards then end the only waitress seem to get an attitude with me because the bag she put my to-go food in was wet and I asked for another. It's cold outside I would rather have a dry bag in my possession when it's chilly. Well apparently that wasn't of her liking so she walked away without acknowledging me to get another bag and just laid it in the table. For me regardless if it's something you as a business agrees with, if the customer isn't satisfied you want to make sure you do your best to take care of that. Maybe I'm wrong. This just took a four star down to three because I feel being treated Nicky mean a lot to me.

I recently visited a non-traditional spot for brunch and came out quite impressed. Although it started rocky with no coffee offered and the "Sausage Party" dish being unavailable, my Taiwanese sausage breakfast crepe was a game-changer. The combination of egg, bacon, and a distinctive sauce wrapped in a crepe delivered a deliciously unique taste. My companion's burger likewise exceeded expectations. Service was a mixed bag – efficient but lacking warmth. Also, the three-card limit for splitting the bill was a minor annoyance. Despite these hiccups, the exceptional food would definitely bring me back.

My dining experience at the restaurant was a journey of highs and lows. The fried fish tapas stood out as the star of the meal, earning its place as our table's favorite with its excellent preparation. While the beans with clams impressed with their superb taste, the scallops paired with romesco sauce were disappointingly served ice cold—a misstep in an otherwise flavorful selection.

The drink menu brought a wave of creativity that did not go unnoticed. Each concoction was a delightful surprise, showcasing unusual but successful flavor combinations that elevated the dining experience.

However, service fell short when our waiter disappeared for an extended period, leaving us without assistance. This hiccup cut our culinary adventure short as we were compelled to flag down another staff member just to settle our bill and depart, missing the chance to further indulge in the menu.

Patrons should be mindful that while the offerings are delectable, the steep prices do not match the modest tapas portions. Expect to enjoy what you taste but also to leave with a lingering appetite.

Title: Unwavering Excellence at Club A Steakhouse

I've been a regular at Club A Steakhouse for years and it consistently earns an A++ rating in my heart. The symphony of food, service, and ambiance play together to create an unrivaled dining experience, time and time again. On my recent visit, I started with their notable Club A Bacon - a thick, perfectly balanced sweet yet savory slice that sets the tone. Their house salad was refreshing, but I'd suggest skipping the cream of spinach in favor of exploring other sides.

The star of the evening was the 24oz bone-in Ribeye, a medium-rare masterpiece with the perfect amount of fattiness. Paired with a glass of Decoy, it solidified why I never regret choosing the ribeye. The chef's generosity was on full display with complimentary mushroom ravioli and desserts that were the cherry on top of a fantastic meal.

For anyone seeking exceptional steak and a premium dining experience, Club A Steakhouse is my unwavering recommendation.

Amazing happy hours!! This place is a really cold Asian Mexican fusion place. The food was delicious and the vibe is soooo cool here. We had a great time at happy hours where they serve one dollar oysters and half priced margaritas. We ordered paella, grilled salmon on quinoa, and pulled pork fried rice. Everything was really delicious. Will definitely have to come back for more margaritas!!

I recently visited a local noodle shop and was pleasantly surprised by the experience. The establishment offers a no-frills setting, perfect for a quick, hearty meal without breaking the bank. I opted for a noodle soup that cost me just $8 and was rewarded with a generous serving of noodles, accompanied by tender slices of beef. The broth was a highlight - deliciously flavorful without being overwhelmingly salty, and served steaming hot, which was particularly comforting on a chilly day.

While the seating is communal and fairly basic with stools, it's not the ideal spot for lounging over a leisurely meal. However, considering the price and the quality of the food, this wasn't a drawback for me. The meal was satisfying, and I left feeling full and content. I'm looking forward to my next visit, where I plan to delve into other popular dishes on their menu.

Title: A Little Slice of Italy Right in the Heart of NYC

From the moment we walked into this Little Italy gem, we were whisked away to what felt like a quaint trattoria in Italy itself, thanks to the jovial Italian staff who peppered our evening with humor and charm. A bottle of imported Italian red wine was the perfect prelude to our meal; it was delicious and set the stage for the culinary delights to come.

As we settled in, we were served fresh, warm bread with olive oil that was so divine it nearly dissolved on our tongues. The star of the evening, though, was the chicken parmesan. A dish that many would claim to have mastered, but here, it was truly elevated. The chicken was succulent, the breading crisp with a hint of pepper, and it was all smothered in a sweet sauce that was the perfect counterbalance to the generous, gooey cheese atop it. It was hearty without leaving you feeling overstuffed.

All in all, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone looking to indulge in a night of authentic Italian dining in NYC. Highly recommend for an exquisite dinner experience that promises to satisfy your Italian cravings!

I recently dined at an exquisite spot in Chinatown and was thoroughly impressed by their offerings. The Qi Spicy Beef Noodle, a beloved favorite among patrons, certainly lived up to its reputation. The broth was packed with flavor, and the noodles had just the right amount of chew – a delightful combination.

Accompanying the noodle soup, I tried the fried pork dumplings, which were perfectly crispy and flavorful; they definitely warrant a repeat order. However, I couldn't help but notice that the steamed dumplings seemed to be a hit across the dining room, so on my next visit, those will be on my must-try list.

I also indulged in the pork belly baos, which I can confidently dub a 'must-try' item. Light, savory, and satisfying, they rounded out the meal beautifully.

Overall, this restaurant is a gem for anyone seeking a quick and tasty meal amidst the vibrant backdrop of Chinatown. I wholeheartedly recommend a visit.

Whenever I find myself in the neighborhood with a hankering for Italian cuisine, I make a beeline for this gem. The ravioli dishes, especially the black truffle and pomodoro, never disappoint with their rich flavors. The zucchini flowers, a standout among the appetizers, are a personal favorite. I must commend the risotto balls for their scrumptious taste, though vegetarians be wary, as they contain chicken stock. While dining here leans towards the expensive side, the exceptional quality of the food paired with the pleasant ambiance justifies every penny. A must-visit for Italian food aficionados!

Title: Quirky Vibes with Room for Improvement at Tiny's

I ventured into Tiny's solo – a choice reflecting my apparently discerning dining companion's preference for grander establishments. While the ambiance might entice the more whimsical diner with a penchant for freestyle scribbles, the culinary experience slightly missed the mark.

Service was a ray of sunshine, with staff showing genuine warmth that elevated the otherwise average outing. The pricing falls into the typical Manhattan brackets—on the steeper end—so expectations naturally skewed towards the higher side.

Now, the much-anticipated sandwich post-workout was decent, but it didn't quite knock it out of the park. It fell somewhat short in the protein department, particularly after a session of lifting when one's body clamors for chicken-laden sustenance.

Overall, it's a solid 3-star experience for Tiny's. The food might not have fully flexed its muscles, but the service certainly lifted spirits.

This was a wonderful restaurant, more of a Taiwanese fusion place than traditional but still delicious! We joined the waitlist on yelp and arrived when we got the text, which was a very smooth process. We started with the sausage party and the spicy dumplings. The sausage party comes with sticky rice but is surrounded with sausage casing, which was unique. Also I'm a sucker for Taiwanese sausage so no complaints there. The spicy dumplings lived up to their name. We have a high spice tolerance but definitely needed some water after. Well worth it! The three cup chicken was sooo good. The meat was so tender, it fell off the bone. And they got the sauce down, which is not an easy task! Be aware it doesn't come with rice, you have to order it separately. It's also a lot of chicken, feeding both people easily. All the food came super fast, the service was attentive, and the bathroom was ridiculously pretty with toothpicks and mouthwash. Can't get any better!

This is my second time here. Service is good. All day drink specials. Good wings, IPA's and tv's with sports. The vibe is relaxed. Plenty of seating. Close to the seaport and almost every train line by Broadway and Nassau. If you are in the area stop on by.

Title: A Blast of a Time at a Hip Spot

From the moment you step into this spacious venue, you're greeted with an effortlessly cool vibe. The bartenders earn top marks for their friendly demeanor and mixology prowess, serving up some seriously potent concoctions with impressive speed. Take advantage of the wallet-friendly happy hour that rolls until 7pm on weekdays—your wallet will thank you.

Amidst the dim lighting, the party atmosphere is palpable, with plenty of seating for you and your crew to settle in for the night. The menu keeps it simple and satisfying with standout cheeseburgers among the offerings. Entertainment is abundant with a nostalgic nod from arcade machines to an extensive collection of board games, including the ever-popular Cards Against Humanity.

Nestled in a prime location, this spot is ideal for groups looking for a lively evening out. It's a guarantee that after one visit, you'll be planning your next trip back to this fun-filled establishment.

Came here not expecting a whole lot since this is a chain franchise. I was told that it shouldn't be called a chain since it's not like McDonald's or Subways. Anyways, I went for a work dinner so I can't state that I dined where people eat normally. We ate at the wine room (which is a private room reserved ahead). We had around 20+ people at the dinner. Yes, we had our own staff of people helping us our so I can't attest to the service. I can write about the food and drinks. We were given a whole array of appetizers, sides and desserts. Starting with a tray of seafood and I LOVE seafood. I could've eaten the tray all by myself and called that my meal. We also got fried risotto and steak tartar. The risotto was the least favorite dish out of all the appetizers that I had tried. I did order their cocktails from the menu such as the stoli doli, blackberry bourbon sidecar and the bohemian. For the main entree I decided on field greens, butter leaf lettuce, and heirloom tomatoes. I also ordered the filet mignon (which was a bit on the salty side). For the sides that were laid out for the table were the Au Gratin Potatoes, Roasted Wild Mushrooms (this was amazeballs), and the Soy Glazed Brussels Sprouts with Bacon. For dessert I tried the warm apple crostata with cinnamon strudel and housemade vanilla ice cream. All in all this was a great meal.

I recently dined at this spot with four friends and found the experience to be a mixed bag. The pricing is fair, particularly when opting for family-style dishes, which brought our per-person cost to a budget-friendly $15, including tip. Arriving at 6 PM meant we avoided the rush and were seated promptly, but the place filled up quickly.

Our order included chicken fried rice, soup dumplings, smoked tea duck, and chicken and broccoli. The fried rice fell short on flavor and chicken content, while the tea duck was more fat than meat, missing the anticipated crispy skin. However, the soup dumplings stood out, being both sizeable and delicious. The chicken and broccoli was passable but marred by the chicken's tough and peculiar texture.

A small perk of checking in was a complimentary Corona with our entrees. The ambiance of the restaurant was pleasant enough, but the service was unremarkable. In sum, other than the standout dumplings, the meal was just okay, saved mainly by the low prices.

Title: A Missed Opportunity for a Korean Feast

Upon visiting this restaurant, lured by the positive buzz, my experience fell short of expectations. The service was lackluster, with the waitress being inattentive until the tail end of my visit, despite an empty dining room. 

The fried kimchi pancake, touted as a specialty, was a disappointment – overly greasy and unpleasantly soggy. A better choice, though not without faults, was the bulgogi bento box; it was tasty but unbalanced with an excessive serving of rice overshadowing the beef.

On a positive note, the small side dishes offered a pleasing start, and the steamed vegetable dumplings were notably enjoyable. Nonetheless, when it comes to Korean cuisine, I hold a high standard that this establishment did not meet. With only moderate pricing to its advantage, I doubt I'll return for another meal.

I had an outstanding experience at Earls! The staff and owners greeted us with exceptional warmth, enhancing the already cool and well-decorated atmosphere. The menu offers a delightful variety, and each dish we tried didn't disappoint in taste. Their beer cheese is the stuff of legends – a must-try! Further, the selection of organic wine is a thoughtful touch for those who prefer it. This place nails the vibe perfectly. Earls has earned a return visit from me on my next trip!

Oh. My. Gosh. That pepperoni pizza melt into my mouth. A pizza place worth to wait for! From the name said, of course this place is on prince street. Busy busy pizza place. We came around 9ish and waited less than 5 mins (line moves so fast!!) The fresh classic pizza is something that I never forget. Perfect crust topped with pepperoni with pull cheese - I'm hungry right now! Highly recommend!

Yup. Yup. Yup. Believe the hype. First off, adult Capri suns are awesome, try one. This place is tapas style fusion Korean. I'm half Korean - it's not traditional style, but they got the flavor profiles right. I'd recommend coming with a party of 3-4 so you can try more things. We got:-Tuna (4/5 - nothing mind blowing flavor wise, but the fish was fresh and cooked to perfection)-Truffle mac and cheese (5/5 - MUST TRY THIS. The most gooey buttery Mac n cheese I've ever had) -Popcorn chicken (5/5 - crispy, perfectly seasoned - tastes like the yak yum chicken you can order delivered to your door in Korea)-Steak (5/5 - man they know how to cook their proteins to perfection. The feta grits and gochujang sautéed kale really took the steak to another level though - wish there was more of this dish)-Duck confit empanadas (4/5 - filling was good but pastry was a touch dry. The pickle tzaziki or whatever the sauce was, was incredible)-Kimchi paella (2/5 - my least favorite dish, I'd skip it. The rice was a little wet/gluey and the seafood was not so fresh tasting. The bits of kimchi were yummy though. This was definitely the most substantial dish we ordered as the portions are small, so it's a good filler if anything)I came here on the 4th of July holiday weekend so the wait was reasonable - 40 mins at 8pm Saturday, but from what I've read it's usually longer than that. Service is amazing also, and ambiance lively-romantic.

After seeing a matinee, I wanted to try Lido for their bottomless brunch after hearing so much about it. I surely wasn't disappointed. I was greeted by the friendly staff as soon as I walked in and was seated immediately. Already a thumbs up. The restaurant is spacious, bright and very clean. The ambiance is great. I didn't have to ask for water and it was poured within the first two minutes of me sitting. The staff is very patient and will answer any questions you have regarding the menu. Where brunches in NYC can be quite chaotic, Lido is a well-oiled machine. If you partake in the bottomless mimosas option ($16 for two hours...YAY) you absolutely get your money's worth and then some. Your glass never stays empty for longer than a minute. Even if your server isn't around the other staff will refill you without asking. Just the way bottomless brunch should be. One of my pet peeves is when I have to wait around to be refilled after my brunch cocktail has been long gone. Lido does it right! My only complaint is that some of the carafes of mimosas tend to have too much champagne and not enough juice to make it an equal balance. I ordered the grilled chicken panini (loaded with all the fixings). It came with a side salad and I ordered a side of the Rosemary potatoes. They were so yummy! Definitely a must try! Another thing I love about Lido is their outdoor enclosed seating area. Beautiful touch!

Wow! My boyfriend made reservations for Tavola on a Saturday night and my goodness everything was delicious! To start off, we ordered a salad to share and were given complimentary bread with olive oil. Who doesn't love free bread, especially from an Italian restaurant?! I ordered lasagna as my entrée and my boyfriend ordered pork with gnocchi. Honestly, that was one of the best lasagnas I've ever had in my entire life. It literally felt like a grandma made it from scratch with all the love in the world. The flavor of our entrées were on point. Everything was fresh with quality ingredients. Severs do ask if you want freshly grated cheese on your entrée. They do not have a full bar. They only have beer and wine. However, it didn't seem like they had many options to choose from based off of the quick glance I gave up their menu. Overall, very cute and intimate restaurant! I highly recommend it!

Wow, this is a pretty decent place for a meal.  I was not expecting the quality and affordable prices in this part of Manhattan.  This is a Northern Chinese restaurant offering fresh hand-pulled noodles.  Came for an early dinner and the place was pretty empty, but seemed like there were lots of UberEats and Seamless delivery guys coming in and out.Tried their Lanzhou Beef Noodles with hand-pulled noodles and a surprisingly large bowl was brought to my table.  The quality of the broth was quite good.  It looked simple, but it had a decent amount of depth to it.  The noodles themselves were the star.  They were so perfectly "QQ".  I normally like knife-shaved noodles and was disappointed when they initially told me they only offer hand-pulled, but I quickly grew to like these hand-pulled noodles.  They were just the right thickness and chewiness.  There was a nice amount of chili oil floating on top of the soup, but it seemed to be pretty mild and I would have enjoyed the soup more had it been spicier.  The beef was the only weak link for this dish.  The beef was sliced thin, yet somehow was sort of tough.  There were also only three small slices of beef in the soup.Dun Huang offered probably the best Yelp check-in offer I've had to date.  For checking in, they gave me their eggplant salad appetizer for free.  It was a very large portion and could definitely be shared between 2-3 people.  This eggplant salad was better than the noodle soup!  It had such great flavor with a sweet, yet savory, sauce and a ton of garlic on top.  It was a nice refreshing break from the soup.If I'm in Manhattan craving freshly made noodle soup, I'd definitely return.

Gammeeok is located right above Five Senses on the second floor in Koreatown. You must go up a flight of stairs to enter (not accessible friendly), which is a reason why I give this place 3 stars. The interior was clean and modern, and the bibimbap I had was good but not the best I've had. I ordered the seafood bibimbap and there was barely any seafood (mainly just vegetables)! Also, unlike most Korean restaurants, this place did not have banchan (or small dishes that are served before the meal). They only had kimchi.

It was some of the best Chinese noodles I've ever had. They chose a great place to put the restaurant. There's definitely no where else to find this authenticity in that area, would need to go to Chinatown or maybe flushing queens lol Braised lamb noodle: It was best dish of the night. Felt like I could eat it every night of the week. The bite and texture of the noodle was perfect. The lamb was super tender. They were bite sized in the bowl, could have enjoyed a few more pieces but it was fine. And they topped it with a few gigantic pieces of carrot lolChickpea beef noodles:I liked it, glad I ordered it and tried it. The chickpea was mashed like a paste, and it went well with the dish. It was a bit spicy for me but I have low spice tolerance lol. The noodles themselves were also on point Fried pork chop: It was an impressive fry. The outside was crispy, and inside was very juicy and tender. I like the exterior wasn't too much breading, it was kinda perfect like how Japanese does Katsu Soybean pudding:Was just ok, so a bit disappointed. My other half said it was light and not to heavy which was good for after a heavy noodle, semi oil heavy meal. I should would have preferred a dessert with bolder flavors

I had an utterly delightful experience at this restaurant! The seating near the entrance was exceptionally cozy, with comfortable lounge chairs that set a relaxed tone for our meal. Our waitress truly made our visit memorable; her sense of humor, attentiveness, and friendliness were top-notch, adding a personal touch to the service.

The overall atmosphere was quintessential pub vibes – warm, welcoming, and buzzing with energy. I have no complaints whatsoever. A standout recommendation is the "Secret Garden" cocktail; if you're a gin aficionado like I am, it's an absolute must-try. It's a refreshing concoction that perfectly complements the convivial setting.

Absolutely loved this place. Great vibe from Morroco. Lots of cool pictures and culture and staff was very friendly and attentive. We walked from the place we were staying so it was also super convenient (I wouldnt try parking). We got the Turkish coffee and Mogador Brunch items. Everything came out amazing and quite quickly. I loved the eggs Benedict as well. I would happy come here again. A+

I've never been to Vietnam, but I've tried my fair share of Pho joints in Manhattan Chinatown, Brooklyn, Texas, and California.  This place was legit tasty and slightly different than what I'm used to.  There isn't an extra plate of bean sprouts/ basil/ mint, but whatever's meant to be in your bowl is already included - which in this case lots of cilantro.  This might be the "Northern" style difference or otherwise just the chef's preparation.We ordered a large beef combination and first off - the broth is amazing.  Perfectly seasoned and balanced with great clarity.  There is a decent amount of beef and noodles (but I was expecting slightly more for a large).  There's a type of hot sauce on the table I've never seen before (not the typical sriracha) and there isn't any hoisin sauce.  But there is some pickled veg/ sauce (which FYI who's jar should be covered cuz of health dept) that was quite tasty.Worth coming back if I want to spend a little, or fill my next craving for a good noodle soup.

Socarrat proves to be the quintessential spot for straightforward, delectable paella and a variety of tapas. The service is consistently commendable, with attentive managers who go the extra mile to ensure a delightful dining experience. Moreover, their sangrias complement the meal perfectly, and the churros are an absolute treat - do not miss out on them!

Title: Authentic Izakaya Delight at EN Japanese Brasserie

As an aficionado of Tokyo’s vibrant izakaya scene, I was thrilled to discover that EN Japanese Brasserie in New York captures the essence of this cherished dining experience. This gem has become a staple for those craving a taste of Japan without the long-haul flight.

Perching at the food bar offers an immersive journey as you watch the skilled chefs meticulously prepare each dish. The freshness of the sashimi and the perfectly executed cooked fish dishes evoke memories of Japan’s coastal offerings. Not to be outdone, the tempura rivals that of Tokyo's best, with its light, crisp batter enveloping succulent morsels.

But the showstopper is indisputably their house-made warm tofu – an unassuming dish that steals the spotlight with its delicate texture and comforting warmth. Pairing your meal with their expertly crafted cocktails, inspired by the renowned mixologist Gen Yamamoto, enhances the flavors on your palate.

Dessert is not an afterthought here; it's an exploration of intriguing flavors that beautifully round off the meal. The atmosphere strikes the perfect balance between energetic buzz and intimate coziness, making it an exquisite backdrop for this culinary orchestra.

In summary, EN Japanese Brasserie is not merely a meal; it's a multisensory experience that seamlessly blends authentic Japanese flavors with the heart of New York hospitality, resulting in nothing short of a gastronomic celebration.

Title: Sun-Soaked Vibes and Zesty Bites at Playa Betty's

My first foray into Playa Betty's came post-movie excitement with my boyfriend, who had been enticed by his colleagues' rave reviews. The atmosphere immediately swept us up in its lively thrall; brimming with energy and an almost full house, the allure of the sun-kissed outdoor seating was irresistible on such a splendid day.

A commendation is due for the hosts, who exuded friendliness and efficiency in equal measure, swiftly escorting us to our table.

Service was impeccably rendered by Iryna, our server, whose attentiveness and professionalism shone through her handling of the bustling crowd. She effortlessly maintained composure and was remarkably responsive to our needs throughout the evening.

The culinary journey commenced with the standout "rad wings," an appetizer that tantalized our taste buds to unexpected delight. My initial brush with the Playa Betty house margarita was less favorable, its unanticipated spice profile reminiscent of jalapeño left me disenchanted. However, Iryna's swift intervention and suggestion led me to the refreshing Frozen Paloma Margarita—a vastly superior choice.

The main courses swung in with less fanfare: my Hang 10 burrito was underwhelming in its dryness, craving the company of more sauce to complement the fried fillings. Iryna once again proved her mettle, procuring an array of side sauces to salvage the situation. My boyfriend's taco dinner passed without incident but without particular note.

We wrapped up with the churro ice cream sandwich—conceptually a dream, but practically it fell short, with a warmed churro potentially having sealed its fate as a sweet triumph.

In closing, Playa Betty's has secured a spot in my “happy hour” repertoire, with an asterisk to favor the delightful appetizers over its main fare.

Title: A Delightful Lunch at Zavo - Fresh and Fun!

My girlfriends and I recently dined at Zavo for lunch, and it was nothing short of fabulous. Right away, the highlight was their mezze plate; each bite was fresh, flavorful, and utterly delicious. The vibrant atmosphere was enhanced by the best tunes, leading us to sing along joyfully!

But the delights didn't stop at the mezze. For a fantastic value of $26 per person, the lunch set menu offered an appetizer, a main, and a dessert, each more delectable than the last. Plus, if you're looking for an evening outing, Zavo features live music on Thursday to Saturday nights, sure to make the dining experience even more memorable.

For fellow food enthusiasts, keep an eye on @traveleen_gurl on Instagram for more of my food adventures!

Rating: 5/5 – Highly Recommended!

Title: A Festive Lunch at Harry's

Celebrated a work milestone at Harry's and I must say, it's a fantastic spot for a group lunch. We kicked things off with meatballs and stuffed mushrooms, which were crowd-pleasers, but the calamari's breading missed the mark for us – it lacked the expected crunch.

Moving on, sharing pizzas like pepperoni, plain, or sausage is the way to go – they never disappoint. For a lighter but flavorful main, try the Filet of Sole. The Veal Parm, while generous with sauce and cheese, seemed overly fried for my taste.

Desserts were a showcase of indulgence, with the tiramisu and cheesecake standing out as the favorites. And don't leave without trying their iced coffee in a Peroni glass – a refreshing surprise that outshines their regular brew.

Overall, Harry's delivered a celebratory atmosphere with mostly hits on the menu. Would recommend for a casual group dining experience!

Title: A Delightful Explosion of Flavors at a Charming Spot

My recent visit to this restaurant left me thoroughly charmed and satisfied. With monkey chandeliers adding an amusing touch to the decor, the place exudes a unique vibe that complements the fantastic food and friendly service.

The crispy aloo tikki was a delightful crunch in every bite and impressively non-greasy. The paani puri and dahi puri were customizable in a half-and-half order, which was a bonus. Each puri was an explosive bite of flavor, with the mint water offering a refreshing zing and the yogurt-based ones imparting a delicious spicy twist.

The stuffed sia mirch was a standout, with perfectly cooked peppers filled with a tasty surprise, far from the predictable potato mash. The masala Bombay lamb chops, albeit a bit on the pricier side, were absolutely worth it; the sauce was sweet and smooth, and the chops tender to perfection.

Their garlic naan deserves a special mention; it was undoubtedly the best in NYC, being thin, crispy, and flawless.

We also enjoyed a couple of cocktails and savored the Indian draft beer, which was a delightful discovery.

Despite the love for the food, I'm giving 4 stars due to the slower-than-anticipated service. We faced a longer wait for our table, even with a reservation, and the gap between courses felt a tad too long. Nevertheless, the complimentary dessert as an apology for the wait was a sweet touch.

I am already planning my next visit, testament to the flavors and experiences that await at this lively restaurant.

Venturing away from my usual fare, I decided to try the Chicken Tikka Masala at a nearby Indian spot, drawn in by its glowing reviews. Though small, the restaurant maintained a clean aesthetic and even offered a restroom—a gem in the rough around Penn Station.

Service was commendably fast and the meal itself proved flavorful. As expected with Indian dishes, the box was generous with sauce and rice, though the chicken breast was a touch overdone, resulting in less protein than hoped for. While I enjoyed the experience, my stomach's sensitivity to the cuisine might pause future visits. Nonetheless, for those with a hardier constitution, it's worth a repeat order.

I recently enjoyed a fantastic brunch at Cortadito Cuban, perfect for large groups as they offer spacious accommodations in their back room. The standout dish for me was the lobster Benedict—an absolute must-try. The menu is impressively vast, but whatever you do, don't miss out on the guacamole and plantain chip appetizer. For those who enjoy a tipple with their meal, the bottomless tropical mimosa is a treat you wouldn't want to skip.

The service was commendable, adding to the delightful dining experience. However, it's worth noting that the restaurant has only one restroom, which could lead to a lengthy wait. Despite this small hiccup, Cortadito Cuban has won me over, and I am keen to return for another round of their exquisite lobster Benedict.

Title: A Parisian Gelato Gem in the Heart of New York

If you're a gelato aficionado like me, Amorino is a must-visit in New York, even amid the chilly winters. The memory of falling for their gelato in Paris had me scouring the US for an Amorino - and it does not disappoint.

Their flavor variety is impressive, but the hazelnut is a standout - it's the creamy, upscale cousin to Nutella. The unique charm lies in their presentation; opt for a cone, and you'll be treated to a gelato rose, with each "petal" representing a different flavor of your choosing. The optional macaroon on top adds a delightful crunch.

Although the space is cozy, they make the most of it with a few seats and a clean bathroom, perfect for a quick, indulgent break while exploring the city. Make sure to stop by - your taste buds will thank you!

Title: Another Delightful Visit to Capital Grills During Restaurant Week

Our family's latest visit to Capital Grills during Restaurant Week upheld our decade-long tradition of delightful dining experiences. The special menu offered substantial portions and a variety of choices. The starters, a crisp wedge salad with hearty bacon chunks and a Caesar salad adorned with anchovies, set a high note for taste.

The NY Strips served on the bone were a departure from the usual and, while tasty, my husband and son would have preferred them boneless. My filet mignon, ordered medium, was perfectly cooked, yet its lukewarm temperature upon arrival was a slight letdown, narrowly missing the mark of perfection.

The side dishes were quite generous, with mashed potatoes and string beans amply satisfying our table. Dessert was a sweet finish—between the shared Creme Brûlée and takeaway Espresso Cakes, our sweet cravings were more than met.

A cheerful and attentive waiter contributed to a very good overall experience, despite the minor hiccup with the steak temperature. A solid four-star rating feels just right for this dining experience.

I visited Jewel Bako for a birthday celebration and had a wonderful experience!  All of the fish was fresh and had great flavors that you just do not taste in the fish at your average sushi restaurant. This is sushi at a different level. Jewel Bako has earned a Michelin star for the past 14 years running. The service was amazing, they accommodated any request we made.  We were seated next to a really noisy table and asked to move and they let us choose another table. They came frequently to the table and kept everything arranged between courses, it was as if the whole experience was curated down to the arrangement of the table. They knew we were having a birthday celebration and gave us a little dessert treat at the end. Kamatoro:  Jewel Bako offers different types of fatty tuna. The Kamatoro is the fattiest part, which comes from the gill area of the fish. The fattiness gives a rich taste like butter, but it has all kinds of other fishy flavors that come from the tuna. It is something you really need to enjoy and savor.Chutoro Makimono: A roll with chutoro, which is a cut of medium fatty tuna.  The chutoro is less rich in flavor compared to the Kamatoro, but makes a great roll.Assortment of Yellowtail:  Three different types of yellowtail sashimi.  Again just really fresh with excellent deep flavors.Selection of Sushi:  Simply a variety of sushi.  Not really my favorite, if I were to return, I would stick to mostly sashimi rather than sushi and rolls. Grilled black cod:  Cod by itself is not that exciting of a fish, but the char and marinade made it so much more. The fish was cooked perfectly and very juicy on the inside. I was a little disappointed that it was only one small piece though, should be two, also a bit expensive for cod.

Title: A Rustic Haven for Brunch Lovers and Muffin Enthusiasts

From the moment you step into this spacious and rustic eatery, you're welcomed with the irresistible aroma of warm muffins that immediately assures you that no one is put in the corner here. The ambiance is a blend of fun and laid-back, perfectly complementing its friendly and attentive staff, making it an ideal spot for both small and large groups of any age.

The brunch menu offers an array of filling options, and the mimosa pitcher, which my friend and I indulged in, was generously sized—though I did subtract a point for the ice that slightly diluted our bubbly.

As for the main course, the ribs with cornbread and slaw did not disappoint. The meaty ribs came with a delectable sweet BBQ glaze, while the cornbread was satisfyingly thick and fluffy, and the slaw added a spicy kick to the meal. The unlimited warm muffins were the cherry on top—so good that I took some home with my leftovers.

Our experience was so delightful that we made a second visit on the same day for happy hour! For more on my culinary journey and snapshots of this delightful spot, follow me on Instagram @saltandsavor.

I recently dined at a local Jewish deli that offered a commendable variety of traditional dishes. Though the flavors were authentic and reminiscent of classic deli cuisine, the prices were steep, which might deter frequent visits. Unfortunately, the restaurant’s seating arrangement is not conducive to larger groups, making it a challenging spot for parties of more than two. If you're flying solo or dining as a pair, it's a cozy place to enjoy some deli favorites, albeit with a higher price tag.

While the pizza served was satisfactory, it didn't quite rise to the culinary heights one might expect given the steep prices. For those seeking the best pizza New York City has to offer, there are other establishments that may deliver a more memorable experience and better value.

Wow, I had pretty much no expectations going in, but as a huge udon lover, I think this is the best udon I've ever had. I know the Niku udon is very popular, but I went ahead and got the nameko, a soup udon dish with light broth with seaweed and mushrooms. It was the perfect lighter broth for lunchtime, yet still super satisfying. The presumably hand made udon was made to perfection, which just enough bounciness and chewiness. I cannot rave about the soup udon enough!This location is tiny, and every time the door opens in the winter, a gust of freezing air comes into the restaurant. I'll definitely be going back to the larger West Village location soon!Like most NY restaurants, Raku only seats complete parties.

One thing I can say without question, is that NY pizza is the absolute best anywhere, and Joe's tops the list. Born and raised in NY, and living in Florida for most of my life, no one comes close, and only people from NY know this is true.  It's the whole combination that makes it, the thin really chewy doughy crust, with just enough sauce so the cheesy cheese doesn't slide off when you take a bite, that orange color, and crusty enough so you can pick up a slice, folded over, without it drooping.  I ate here twice on a 4 day visit.  First I had to have the classic cheese.  The second visit, I made sure I was hungry, a cheese and also a caprese, which had fresh ripe tomatoes, blobs of fresh mozzarella, and fresh whole basil leaves in addition to their marvelous pizza sauce. That slice, I have to say, was an OMG experience. Each bite was pizza euphoria.  There was a line out the door both visits, but the line moved fast, and got to the front in 5 minutes.  Five guys behind the counter, all working fast and efficiently, making pizza, serving pizza, and cashing you out.  We even got seats in the small and crowded restaurant, because everyone just eats and goes.  So now I am already planning my next trip to NY, because it's all about food in NY!

Came here for a private party and was very impressed!  We were downstairs and there was food and cocktails available.  The excellent bartender made a delicious Wren Old Fashioned.   I was a big fan.The food was great too.  Loved the Buffalo Cauliflower.  The fries were excellent and the sliders were juicy and delicious.  So often, sliders get dried out because they are overcooked.  These were great.The space is cozy and it got a little warm downstairs when it filled up.The upstairs was packed on a Saturday night, with people crammed into the narrow bar area so ingress and egress was difficult and hazardous.  Nobody at the bar seemed to want to let anyone pass.  I'll just assume they were entitled millennials and leave it at that!  Just kidding...kind of. :) Otherwise, a very nice place and a great spot for an event.

Tapas is a fine art that can be hit or miss.  Our experience at Boqueria was more of a miss unfortunately. We came with a large group of 9, so we couldn't order off the regular menu and were forced to get the tasting menu (about 60 bucks a head).  The restaurant is a bit tight but comfortable enough.  Decor is right in line with a Spanish tapas bar.The food here is uneven.  The pan con tomate was good but a tad salty.  Cheese plate and jamon were spot on.  Garlic shrimp had good flavor but the shrimp were tiny and they were sitting in oil (probably on purpose so you could sop up the oil with the bread they brought).  Brussels with chorizo had a sulfuric taste (probably because they were boiled at some point) and you couldn't taste the chorizo.  Meatballs were good but I'm not a fan of lamb and you could definitely taste the lamb (if you like the taste of lamb this is chock full of it).  Sweet potato were crispy but a tad bitter due to some over charring. The skate wing was cooked well but was very fishy so some of our party found it off putting.  The paella was decent - lots of seafood that was coked well but the rice was meh (no saffron - just cooked in whatever sauce they had).  Service was good and polite.  That was probably the best part of our meal.  The food here isn't bad but it could use some tweaks (or we just came on an off night).  Willing to give it another shot down the road.

Despite the slew of negative reviews online, I find myself questioning the harsh criticism directed at this modest pizza joint. Like the adage goes, "you get what you pay for," and that's precisely the case with this establishment. For those in pursuit of top-notch slices, Prince Street might be your destination. There's another competitor a few blocks away that might edge this place out with offerings like shredded Parmesan, something notably absent here.

Nonetheless, the pizza this spot serves up is of respectable quality, especially given its price point. Alongside pizza, they offer an array of economical sides like garlic knots and cheese sticks, which are tasty add-ons to your meal. This isn't the Ritz; it's a straightforward, unpretentious dollar pizza place that delivers exactly what it promises—decent food for a low cost.

In short, don't let the negativity fool you. For a quick, wallet-friendly bite, this place is worth stopping by. I'd recommend dropping in, especially if you're looking for a simple, satisfying experience.

I had a delightful dining experience at this restaurant, charmed by its beautiful and nostalgic interior. The highlight of the meal was the exquisite blinis with caviar, a dish that I would highly recommend. The service was impeccable, thanks to our wonderful server, Olga, who was extremely nice and added to the overall positive experience. I am already looking forward to my next visit. Thank you for a memorable meal!

Recently, my friends and I stumbled upon a gem in the K-town area that's open around the clock, ideal for post-partying cravings. We ordered the beef pho and pepper shrimp. The beef pho isn't your traditional Vietnamese fare; it's a decent bowl with the interesting addition of pok choy. However, it's their pepper shrimp that truly shines. Battered and deep-fried to perfection, the shrimp is mixed with stir-fried peppers and onions, creating a dish that's crisp, flavorful, and wonderfully non-greasy. The pepper is noticeable but not overwhelming, and thankfully, it's not drenched in sauce. For those looking to stray from the typical late-night BBQ joints, this spot is a refreshing change. Their pepper shrimp alone is worth the visit, and I'm eager to return and dive into their other noodle offerings. Highly recommended for post-party dining!

I think this place used to be Ponty Bistro which I also loved a lot! Came to try their lunch as it's not too from my office. Left with satisfaction. Lunch set was around $9, such good deal! If you pick Chicken Tikka Masala or Saag Paneer, you get to choose two other dishes in smaller portions. Like a sampler concept. My favorite was their Chicken Tikka Masala, has little sweetness in it, chicken was a little dry but I feel like it's always like that. Second favorite was Vegetable Korma, never would know how to describe Indian food but it was a memorable flavor. We also had the Cauliflower something also was good. Saag Paneer was my least favorite but again, I think I never love this dish. For lunch if you get to have a Samosa with just adding $1, crazy right! Their Samosa was really good and I love the flavor of the crust thing. Staff (maybe it's the owner?)  Was super friendly and also comp us a free Samosa. Would def come back, glad this new spot added to my work lunch list!

The Ichiran dining experience is truly one-of-a-kind, offering a distinctive way to savor ramen in the privacy of a personal stall. This setup heightened my focus on the flavors presented in front of me. While the broth was undeniably flavorful, I found myself longing for a richer depth, and will opt for stronger dashi next time. The recommended selections on the menu provided a solid foundation from which to customize future visits.

The texture of the noodles struck the perfect balance between firmness and chewiness, marrying well with the savory broth. The chashu, notably tender, was a highlight of the meal. However, the overall pricing felt slightly steep, though one does pay for quality. In summary, Ichiran offers a high-quality ramen experience with the unique benefit of solitary dining.

Solid happy hour menu! The caipirinha's were strong, the snacks tasty (say yes to the yucca fries), and the vibe was great. We had no problems getting a table after work, and our server was really attentive. He also checked for last call on HH, which is always appreciated. So glad I finally got to try it out after passing by all the time!

Title: A Gem in Washington Heights – Where the Margaritas Shine

I've been captivated by this charming spot that's become a staple for me in Washington Heights. With a perfect atmosphere score of 5/5, the restaurant never misses a beat in ambiance, decorating for every holiday and setting the mood with spot-on lighting. The service is impeccable, also earning a 5/5, thanks to servers who truly care and bartenders brimming with personality.

The food, a solid 4/5, is where things get interesting. Billed as Italian, the dishes delightfully surprise with a Latin/Dominican twist that keeps every bite exciting. The value for money is tough to beat, with decent, affordable eats, compelling brunch deals, and a dependable happy hour.

But let's talk about the real MVP here – the margaritas. Whether you desire them frozen or on the rocks, the variety is impressive with flavors like peach, mango, and strawberry. These killer concoctions are not only delicious but also cheap and potent, ensuring your spirits are as lifted as their taste is elevated.

In summary, if you're not after luxury but love a place where heart meets soul (and killer margaritas meet your taste buds), you'll want to make this your next stop in Washington Heights.

Warning: Eating a full meal platter with the rice during lunch will put you in a border food coma / nap. But it may be worth it!This place has a great reputation as a lunchtime favorite for me and my coworkers. Everything here is delicious and authentic.I tell myself each time I'm gonna get one of the sandwiches but get suckered into the spicy chicken platter with rice and small avocado salad. The green sauce is so addicting and goes well with everything. I also like their style of fries - thick cut.People that have had other items such as Cubanos or Soups are huge fans.You'll either be greeted by friendly people behind the cases or their friendly wait staff sitting down. Definitely stop by if you're craving a hearty Cuban meal.

This place is absolutely delicious. Before getting into the food, this place is really nice inside. There are a number of tables for groups of 2 or 4, with additional seating upstairs. I like being able to order from the tablets and customizing all of the food offerings, but the staff is really nice too, if you need them. Caramel Pork Banh Mi: Sweet marinated pork in a freshly toasted baguette, with veggies and cilantro. This sandwich was really tasty, and I had it with spicy mayo included. I liked everything about it. I love that the sandwiches are really packed with fermented carrots; particularly with this sandwich, they really cut the sweetness down a bit. Kimchi Fries With Fried Egg: These were really good. The fries were really crispy, even through all of the spicy mayo. These are really good for sharing, because if you get a banh mi and the fries for yourself, you're going to be pretty stuffed. The kimchi was really fresh and well made. The kimchi went really well with the fries; it was a really great idea to put these things together. The runny egg complimented everything really nicely too. My only suggestion is to put a little less mayo -- more of a personal preference; my girlfriend thought it was perfect. Price: 5/5Quality: 5/5Quantity: 5/5Service: 5/5Atmosphere: 5/5

Title: Convenient Brunch Spot with a Homely Touch

My recent visit to this brunch locale was in celebration of a friend's birthday, and I found it to be a pleasant, if not standout, experience. Its proximity to my apartment made it an ideal choice for convenience. The restaurant offered a lovely, airy ambiance and, despite the Sunday morning crowd, we appreciated the ease of making a reservation and the prompt seating upon our arrival.

The menu selections were satisfactory; I indulged in the pancakes, which were deliciously reminiscent of a home-cooked meal. My companion enjoyed her eggs, although she noted they weren't particularly extraordinary. 

This establishment is worth a recommendation for those in the area seeking a straightforward and friendly brunch venue. However, for those willing to venture into the heart of the east side’s 70s and 80s, other notable brunch options may offer a more unique experience.

Title: An Unagi Lover's Haven – Dive Into Deliciousness

As a dedicated connoisseur of eel delicacies, I stumbled upon a hidden gem tailored for those of us who eagerly ask, "Who's up for that roll with eel on top?" If you've ever faced bewildered glances across the sushi table, fear not; the community of eel aficionados thrives at this eel-exclusive establishment.

Forgive me for not recalling the perfect Forest Gump quote, but this place is all about perfecting the art of eel. Despite previous patrons' concerns about service, my quiet Monday night experience was top-notch. The staff, attentive and considerate, offered a complimentary sake tasting, allowing me to choose the perfect pairing for my meal.

Patience is a virtue when it comes to their eel preparation; a testament to their philosophy of mastery through repetition. The payoff? A tantalizing play of tastes and textures, with every dish crafted to remind us why doing one thing well is an art.

The highlight? The special featuring a divine hot soup served midway, transforming your culinary journey with its warm embrace, ideal for dipping the eel-rice-onion ensemble. It's a unique touch that elevates the dining experience.

In a nutshell, if eel is your thing, make a beeline for this spot. Bring your fellow eel enthusiasts, and savor the flavors before it's too late, as the unassuming facade and lackluster signage might be the only thing standing between this establishment and the throngs of potential admirers it rightfully deserves.

This place is my boyfriend's favorite $1 pizza spot. No matter what time it is people are lining up and dropping their singles here for a slice and a soda. What a great deal for $3 - 2 slices and a can of soda. The pizzas are always fresh out of the oven because of the line, but I never had to wait longer than 15 minutes to get to the front.

Tucked away in a remote spot, this hidden gem is a culinary delight that justifies the trek. The restaurant offers a tranquil dining experience away from the hustle and bustle, likely attributed to its off-the-beaten-path location. The standout soup dumplings tantalize the taste buds, although patrons may find the quantity a tad scanty for the price, with just four pieces served. Equally impressive is the fish blossom, a must-try for any visitor. While the pork dish offered a depth of flavor, it was marred by an excess of fat. However, the ambiance is not to be overlooked – the decor is an attraction in its own right, contributing to a memorable dining experience.

They do one thing and they do it with the skill and precision of a Swiss watchmaker on meth. In this nano-sized food truck there is alchemy at work. I don't know how two people fit in there.. or how they are able to cook in there... however... Rice rolls are pumped out at a dizzying speed.. and for 3$ you get a breakfast that will knock your socks off, clear across the room and into the hamper. Slam freaking dunk!

I had a delightful lunch experience at this well-reviewed restaurant. Despite its popularity, I was pleasantly surprised to find that it wasn't crowded, allowing me to be seated immediately. The highlight of my meal was the chili turmeric chicken paired with jasmine rice — a dish that impressed me with its perfect balance of flavors and spice. Although I typically veer towards red or green curry, which wasn't available, the restaurant's stir fry recommendation did not disappoint and was truly amazing. However, at $15, the portion size was on the smaller side. Nonetheless, the food quality left me satisfied and I'd recommend a visit for anyone looking to enjoy a flavorful meal.

Went during happy hour which is 5-7:30pm.1$ wings and drink specials! Probably the best part of the meal. Unfortunately everything else was weak. Once the service asked if we've been before (the bushwick location, the better location!), he completely brushed us off and walked away saying "its the same". Total turn off b/c it is not exactly the same menu. Our lamb dumplings were under cooked and cold. The tops of it were still hard. The coconut lobster rice is NOT worth 30$. Basically white rice with some coconut flakes and lobster thrown on top- lacking flavor. We were disappointed after visiting the Bushwick location some months ago, where service and food was A1. Maybe it was an off day but total experience was lacking in every way. At one point the maître d' had to give us glasses and water b/c our waiter was no where to be found.

We just had another great dinner at Sinigual but didn't like their new surcharge policy one bit. (Details on that later). It was one of those days so we both opted for large potent drinks - 21 ounce Dueno (one per customer only!) for hubbie and Black Diamond margarita for me. Pricey but well worth it. I had one of my faves for dinner, shrimp diablo with citrus jabanero sauce, green rice and beans. A superb contrast of heat and sweet. Sinigual offers a combo deal of three items for $23, hubbie chose blue corn enchilada, steak taco and chicken taquito for his. Very good as usual. Shared three small creamy scoops of ice cream for dessert, my favorite flavors including coffee and dulce de leche. More yum.The only reason I'm knocking down a star is Sinigual's new policy of tacking on a secret "SURCHARGE" to every diner's bill. When I asked our lovely server what the extra $3.21 charge was for, she explained that it's a new policy by the restaurant to avoid raising prices and that she didn't like it either. Sinigual should tell customers about this beforehand, not take a sneaky approach and just hope people won't notice. This won't stop us from going to Sinigual as we love their food and service, but we're disappointed by management's decision to raise prices this way.

My recent dining experience left much to be desired. The mini-lobster roll, costing an exorbitant $9, was disappointingly more akin to a small piece of bread than a seafood indulgence. Similarly, the "mini-taco" lived up to its name to an extreme, vanishing in a single bite. The calamari and accompanying dip, while the highlight in both portion and flavor, still failed to impress. Ironically, the complimentary crackers emerged as the meal's saving grace. In short, this establishment's offerings were underwhelming, both in size and satisfaction.

I recently tried a spicy fried chicken sandwich through MealPal and had a mixed experience. While the sandwich was satisfying, boasting a generous portion of deliciously fried chicken, the accompanying 'ships', I assume they meant to type 'chips', were disappointingly scarce, at a mere eight pieces. Though these few chips were a letdown, I wouldn't mind ordering the sandwich again. However, I'd suggest the restaurant either skip the chips altogether or offer a more appropriate portion, as such a scant serving comes off as stingy and detracts from the overall meal.

Title: No Frills, Decent Meal at 123 Burger

123 Burger delivers precisely what it promises in its straightforward name. This isn't a place that tries to reinvent the burger; it's where you go for an honest, okay meal without the frills. For a mere $3, you'll receive your food served on a paper plate, with buns that are unmistakably from a pre-packaged batch, which adds to its no-nonsense charm.

The service is unpretentious and direct, aligning with the overall vibe of the place. If you adjust your expectations to the casual, almost fast-food experience, you're unlikely to be disappointed.

In essence, 123 Burger is the go-to spot when you need a quick fix of comfort food without denting your wallet. It's definitely not gourmet, but for the price and the simplicity, it's worth a return visit when the craving hits for a simple burger, shot, or beer.

Title: A Tasty Vegan Indulgence at Rips' New West Village Location

I had the pleasure of visiting the new West Village outpost of Rips, originally from Brooklyn, and was thoroughly impressed by their culinary creations. Their egg and cheese burger, featuring a unique egg patty made from green plantains, was a delightful surprise – not too sweet and perfectly complemented by the satisfyingly carb-heavy smashed tots. What's more, their use of the Beyond Meat patty elevated this to one of the finest vegan burgers I've had to date.

Rips is also famous for their chopped cheese, reminiscent of a Philly cheesesteak minus the onions and peppers. It lived up to the hype, offering robust flavors for a reasonable $12-$14 price range. While the birthday cake milkshake had potential, the cherry syrup was overly sweet and artificial for my taste, though I've heard high praise for their other customizable shake options.

Aside from burgers, the menu boasts vegan hot dogs and, for those interested, beer. The staff's friendliness and the ample portion sizes contributed to a very positive dining experience.

However, the restaurant's size and ventilation do present some drawbacks. The extremely small space seats about ten, with patrons seated right next to the grill. Post-meal, expect to leave carrying the scent of the kitchen with you, which could be inconvenient if you have plans afterward. Due to the intense lingering food odors on clothes and belongings, a 'to-go' order might be advisable.

In summary, Rips delivered a 100% food satisfaction rate, but the ventilation issue led me to dock a star. If you're craving hearty vegan comfort food and don't mind the cozy, aromatic setting, Rips is definitely worth the visit. Just consider dining al fresco or grabbing takeout if you prefer to keep the grease at the grill and not on your gear.

Great service and great food. Damn small portions!For the price point, I was not wanting to spend that much on each entree. It was a good thing that both of us had snacked earlier in the day. We had  the braised pork belly which was phenomenal. Super tender, juicy, and savory with bite. I ordered the lamb entree which I thought was rich. My boyfriend got a small filet of salon which does not include any sides with it! He look so sadly hungry that I offered half of my dish to him. Our waiter did a great job consistently checking in on us. We got in a little before 6 and the place was packed by 7.

Tuesday night, not too many people inside nor outside for after-work drinks. Quickly got myself a seat as the several bartenders behind the bar set me up with a menu and water.Draft list is large with several types of beer ranging from $7-11 depending on ABV%. For food, ordered the Lemon Chicken ($16) - a large sliced chicken breast smothered in a lemon gravy, served alongside roasted vegetables. Chicken is cooked fine, and the vegetables aren't overly drenched in oil. Lemon gravy could be better as the flavor was pretty mild. Overall a decent bar to watch sports or to chill in the area. Most of the week they don't have lunch, which I hope they change.
Stopped by for happy hour while waiting to get on the vessel, this is one of the more affordable happy hours in the area. Fernando was a great bartender, very nice and always checking in on us!

Title: A Flavor-Packed Find in Chelsea Market

My recent culinary adventure in Chelsea Market led me to a bustling, vibrant spot that truly stands out. Despite its simplicity, the tacos here are nothing short of super delicious. The pork taco, in particular, was a revelation—a true powerhouse of flavors that made my taste buds dance.

Expect a crowd, as there's often a line, but don't be deterred. The queue moves swiftly, thanks to the efficient staff. Along with the standout pork, we indulged in chicken tacos that were just as delightful. To accompany the meal, I opted for the Tamarindo—a refreshing tamarind-flavored drink that I absolutely adore.

This energetic establishment is a treasure for taco aficionados, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Chelsea Market has many dining options, but if you crave tacos done right, this is the place to go.

During my pre-trip research for the ultimate NYC pizza experience, Joe's and Prince St. surfaced as top contenders. Choosing Prince St. Pizza was a decision I'll savor until my next visit. Their Spicy Spring slice defies the ordinary—fresh mozzarella and an olive oil-kissed focaccia-like crust form the foundation for a pepperoni revelation. Each slice comes adorned with pepperoni that crisps into delectable cups of flavor, with just enough heat to tantalize without overwhelming.

Days later, I find myself reminiscing about that perfect square of Sicilian bliss and contemplating a kitchen adventure to tide me over. Prince St. Pizza is not just about eating; it's an edible episode of sheer delight I eagerly anticipate reliving. Truly, a must-visit for any pizza aficionado in New York City.

I dropped into this spot for a last-minute dinner, and it was a pleasant surprise. The spicy mang and mighty mushroom rolls were on the table promptly, complemented by a spicy shroom wrap for sharing. Each piece of sushi was already topped with just the right amount of dressing, making additional soy sauce redundant and even overwhelming. The flavors were bold and well-balanced, perfect for vegan sushi enthusiasts. Admittedly, the prices leaned towards the higher end, but that's expected in NYC, where the cost of dining often reflects the steep living expenses. Despite that, the quality justified the cost. Recommended for those looking for a quick, flavorful, plant-based bite.

At first glance, I mistook the restaurant for a typical burger joint, with enticing images of hamburgers, fries, and ice cream adorning the exterior. Once inside, I skimmed through my Yelp app, and the Carrot Dog caught my eye on the menu. It took me a moment to realize I'd stumbled into a vegetarian haven—as a meat-lover, I was initially taken aback.

Despite my carnivorous predilections, the menu was both visually appealing and intriguing, tempting me to reconsider my food choices. Ordering seemed efficient with their kiosk system, and I noticed they offer a variety of items, including cupcakes, Push Pops, cold-pressed juices, and even beer.

The ambiance of the place was inviting with its bright, clean interior and spacious seating, perfect for those who want to dine in or grab a bite on the go.

Though I didn't indulge during my visit, the overall positive impression means I'll definitely be back to give that Carrot Dog a try.

While Joe's Shanghai and Shanghai 21 are both quoting you 40 minutes of wait, Shanghai Heping always has seats available. If you find yourself in Chinatown craving soup dumplings on a busy Saturday, this is your spot to get quickly seated. The soup dumplings with pork and crab and the scallion pancake were both standard affair. Don't get me wrong, both dishes tasted well. However, neither dish knocked it out of the park. Our third dish, the crispy fried noodles with shrimp had an uneven amount of sauce and fried noodle ratio, leaving our not so crispy noodles swimming in the sauce after just a few bites. The shrimp was overcooked and just tasted foul. The final dish, braised duck with scallion in brown sauce took an hour to make. Thankfully we shared each dish, so the timing wasn't much of a problem. I've got to say, the duck was tasty. We were glad someone came to cut the duck for us. Otherwise we would have been totally useless with the bones. The meat was tender and smooth. I would have preferred a heartier vegetable with the duck over the scallion, maybe bok choy, but the scallion was tasty regardless. The brown sauce was a little too overpowering, but I guess that's why it is included in the name of the dish. When the check arrived, they asked us to tell them our tip amount to charge our credit card with it, which we found to be weird. We informed them we would tip after our card is swiped. Later, the person who returned our credit cards waited in front of us while we tipped, which continued to make us feel uncomfortable. There was no reason to be treated with such a lack of trust. I hope they try to give customers space while tipping in the future.

On a dreary, rain-soaked afternoon, I decided to duck into a local eatery for drinks and found myself tempted by the menu into ordering some food as well. Opting for what seemed to be pub staples, I got the wings and fish and chips. The service left something to be desired, as the staff seemed a bit disjointed and not quite on top of their game. Despite this, I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food. The fish and chips were quite satisfying, with a crispy batter that complemented the tender fish within, and the wings soared beyond my expectations, landing firmly in the realm of above average. Overall, it was a decent dining experience, even if the service didn't quite hit the mark.

The newly reopened establishment is where sublime design, exceptional food, and impeccable service converge. The current bae menu breathes new life into Scandinavian classics. The Artichoke char with cauliflower and sandefjord sauce, priced at $34, was a revelation—its taste, flavors, and presentation were nothing short of spectacular. Coupled with seamless service, this restaurant is undoubtedly a true dining gem.

I had the pleasure of dining at what I can confidently declare the best restaurant I have ever visited. Every detail of the decor was stunningly impeccable, contributing to an extraordinary ambiance. The service was unmatched, attentive without being intrusive, ensuring a seamless experience. As for the cuisine, it was a culinary masterpiece—every dish served was an explosion of mouthwatering flavors. In summary, the entire visit was nothing short of amazing. This place is a must-visit for anyone who appreciates fine dining at its best.

Awesome brunch! Really great spot, packed but checked in on YELP waitlist and it was so great! We waited about 10-15minutes for a table, place was packed but service was good around noon on Sunday. We tried the Azuca Hemp coffee (10$) it tasted good but was not worth the hype and didn't notice a difference really... moving on to the food! The best part! We tried the buttermilk biscuits (amazing) they came with butter and this delicious jam, their famous chicken and pancakes (excellent), the BLAT (just ok) the side of fries were excellent though!! My friend also tried the cheese grits- she said they were ok- I don't like grits so wouldn't be a great person to judge. We enjoyed everything.... Highly recommend for brunch!!

I recently dined once again at this remarkable chain restaurant and left utterly content. Whether indulging in the unadulterated joy of their succulent lobster or savoring the lobster roll, delicately nestled within a butter-rich, impeccably crisp potato brioche bun, the experience was divine. Their fries maintained their reputation for consistency, providing the perfect crunchy accompaniment to the meal. Visiting during restaurant week was a delightful bonus, with each of us being treated to half a dozen complimentary oysters, a fresh and flavorful beginning to our seafood feast. This chain remains a steadfast favorite, delivering exceptional quality and satisfaction with unwavering reliability.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Korean Cuisine in Chinatown

I recently stumbled upon a delightful Korean eatery nestled in the heart of Chinatown, where the culinary journey doesn't require a voyage to the famed 32nd Street. The establishment offers a thoughtful lunch and dinner pricing scheme, with a mere $2 difference which leaves one curious about the variance—perhaps portion size?

During a lunchtime rendezvous with a friend, I savored the beef bibimbap, which was an explosion of flavors—a delightful experience for a palate longing for authentic Korean fare.
