My companion chose the army soup, and our meals were accompanied by an assortment of banchan, rice, and a complimentary steamed egg that arrived temptingly hot and surprisingly flavorful for such a simple dish.

Service was notable; the attentive waitress replenished our banchan unprompted—a gesture of hospitality that did not go unappreciated. The inclusion of rice with our meals was also a welcome touch that underscored the value.

Pricewise, the restaurant is a wallet-friendly option, considering the complimentary extras. This gem has earned a spot on my NYC go-to list for when the cravings hit, and the long queues of Koreatown are less appealing.

Whenever I'm in NYC and in need of a satisfying, healthy lunch, this spot is my go-to. They offer a fantastic salad bar that allows for customization or pre-made selections if you're in a rush. What sets this place apart, however, is the a la carte option where you curate your own plate with a protein, grain, and two sides – an offer that changes daily to keep things fresh. Don't miss out on the salmon; it's a choice that never disappoints. Highly recommended for anyone after a nutritious and tasty meal.

Tucked away in the vibrant Union Square vicinity lies this charming gem of a spot. My recent foray during their happy hour left me thoroughly impressed. Boasting delectable tacos and the pulsating beats spun by a live DJ over the weekend, the atmosphere is both stylish and lively.

The crowd is an eclectic mix of fun-seekers, making it an ideal backdrop for a romantic date or a spirited outing with friends. Not only is the food satisfying, but the staff also deserves accolades for their friendliness and efficiency. Price points are on par with the neighborhood's going rate, ensuring you can enjoy the evening without breaking the bank.

This place radiates a fun and chic vibe that's absolutely worth experiencing firsthand. Don't miss out on this delightful spot – it's certainly worth a visit.

Great experience!  Here for a party.  I had the chance to try a few things;Albondigas - This is a dish of Lamb Meatballs with tomato sauce, sheep's milk cheese, garnished with basil on top.  It was served with flatbread on the side which was perfect to sop up the terrific tomato sauce and cheese.  The meatballs were tender morsels, a little gamey flavor to note that it is indeed lamb, a little salty but otherwise a great meaty plate.Croquetas Cremosas - These were advertised as truffle mushroom croquettes.  Mushroom-y, creamy and cheesy, it was perfectly paired, and had me wondering what kind of cheese was n the middle.  This was a very good plate.Escalivada - roasted eggplant, red pepper, and onion on top of a yogurt pool.  I'm not sure I appreciated this dish after having the Albondigas.  Given that the lamb imparted a strong salty flavor on the tongue, this was mild in comparison and seasoned more delicately.  Next time, I'll have this first before the Albondigas, if I do.There was a shrimp with eggs plate garnished with seasoned bread which I don't know the name of that I appreciated due to the fact that I love shrimp with eggs in all forms.  The eggs were perfectly cooked, no browning at all, soft but not runny, complete with small shrimp.  There was a paella with chicken and pork belly, topped with almost well done, sunny side up eggs.  It was a very pretty dish and was almost as good in the tummy.  The rice was very good and well seasoned but just short of the crisp rice that I've come to expect with the best paellas.  The rice was plenty relative to the chicken and pork belly, I'd say the ratio of meat to rice could be a tad better if I really wanted to critique.To finish the meal, the churros, filled and those to be dipped were very good.  For this party, we had the whole back room to ourselves with a view of the kitchen.  The service was great, everything that was required or needed was presented.  Even though I was with family and friends, I couldn't help stealing glances of the kitchen and all the work being done to prepare all the meals.  There something about watching professionals at work that always grabs my attention.  If I ever come back I might be disappointed if I'm not sitting in the same spot.  Haha.

This place is amazing! I've never gone to their dining room for lunch/dinner, but I did go to their tavern area for lunch. Such a good value for the price. It's also a non-tipping restaurant and service is fantastic. I came here for lunch and I got the Citrus Salad which was essentially an artisan salad. It had candied walnuts, salsa verde and kohlrabi. For my main dish I got the grilled sea bass which had potatoes and bacon and garnished with dill. Very well cooked and refreshing. This place lives up to its hype and is honestly a true gem.

Title: Charming Vibe and Stellar Curry at Thai Chella

I recently dined at Thai Chella on a Friday evening and was pleasantly surprised by the ease with which we secured a table without any wait. My choice for the evening was the Yellow Curry, which was absolutely delightful and is a dish I would undoubtedly order again. My friend opted for the Pad Thai, which regrettably turned out to be rather spicy despite a request for a milder heat level.

One thing to note is the absence of a restroom within the restaurant, which could be a slight inconvenience for some guests. Also, for those who enjoy a drink with their meal, Thai Chella does not serve alcohol.

However, the ambiance is where Thai Chella truly shines; the restaurant exudes a cute and inviting vibe that adds to the overall dining experience. After some contemplation between a 4 or 5-star rating, I've settled on a full 5 stars, primarily because of how much I enjoyed the yellow curry. I would happily recommend Thai Chella to my friends for a lovely dining experience.

Loved this restaurant! Went here with a friend and were seated in the back of the restaurant on the first floor. The "Box of Dreams" was delicious - the server took her time to explain all the different fish and everything tasted so good!

Always looking for a good BBQ place in the city, Jax is the latest attempt in Manhattan. Welcoming interior with wood trim and cushioned chairs, mostly empty on a Saturday afternoon.Greeted immediately as I sat down at the bar. Started off with a draft beer ($7) and ordered the Pick 2 combo ($22). Chose the ribs and catfish with a side of baked beans. Food comes out on 10 minutes and certainly looks appetizing. Catfish is small and heavily fried. Not too much meat but a decent flavor. Ribs look hearty, but not.much meat on the bones, and definitely not fall-off-the-bone as you would hope. Baked beans just were not good; tasted.soggy and old. Ended up only eating the catfish and a couple of the ribs.While the service was super friendly, I thought the food left a lot to be desired. Also, happy hour stated $5 drafts, but I got the full 7 (wasn't going to fight the $2). Probably should be stated somewhere if there's a restriction.

I've had Loring Place on my bookmarks for a year and a half now. I was very excited to come here, and I told my parents about it. The moment we had gotten there, the staff was far from friendly. We had to find parking, which isn't too easy to find on a Saturday night, which unfortunately made us a bit late for our reservation. On arrival, after telling the front desk about our reservation the guy at the front desk said "oh you're 20 minutes late, we were calling your reservation for 15 minutes" mind you the restaurant was empty and there wasn't anyone waiting at the time. Lucky for us, they "allowed" us to keep our reservation and we had been able to sit down. And the service made up for the way we were treated upon our arrival. My family and I ordered the cauliflower (which was very good) the broccoli salad, (I wouldn't order again) whole wheat pasta, (a small portion of pasta) the spicy pizza, (the pizza was the best tasting part of the meal) and the sea bass. (Sea bass was a bit fishy) They had also given us a complimentary acorn squash which was nice. The drinks were also good, (I had ordered the 123 resporado) but a bit expensive at $16 each, with glasses of wine around $18. I will compliment the atmosphere though - it's an ideal place for a date, and it's very spacious..just didn't meet my overall expectations regardless of its amazing Yelp rating.

Title: A Gastronomic Gem in New York: Beyond Sushi

Review:

During my recent visit to New York, I had the pleasure of dining in at Beyond Sushi - an experience that left an indelible mark on my culinary journey. Having only sampled their sushi rolls previously, the dine-in encounter was a revelation.

The Fun-guy dumplings are worthy of highlight; they were an absolute triumph of flavors, warranting an 'omgggg soooo good' exclamation from our table. We also ventured into the customized realm with the Sweet Tree sushi roll, opting for soybean paper and a pesto sauce tweak, which proved to be a wise decision and a crowd favorite alongside the delectable Chick Pea sushi roll, also with soybean paper.

Not to be overshadowed, the garlic rosemary bread provided a perfect savory balance, setting the stage for the show-stopping Lemon almond cake. This dessert was a masterclass in sweet indulgence, rounding off the meal perfectly.

Exceptional service enhanced our dining experience further, with our waiter exhibiting remarkable patience and helpfulness as he navigated us through the menu, enriching our choices with his knowledgeable recommendations.

Beyond Sushi has cemented its place not just on my palate but also in my heart, as a top culinary destination in New York. It's a must-visit for anyone seeking a meal that will enliven the senses and satiate the soul.

Can't tell you how much this really hit the spot! After running a bit, I wanted to grab something vegan (making a valiant attempt to go plant based- I'm like batting 50% and even that is too kind ). Opted for the rice rolls-  Nutty Buddy and Spicy Shroom. For both rolls, I opted out of the noodles and asked for more greens. NB: the jalapeño peanut butter was spicier than I thought it would be, but it's totally cool I love spicy things. Not a ponzu sauce fan, but still tried it. It was ok.SS: Loved the shiitake mushrooms and the shiitake truffle sauce that came with it. I would order two of these next time I'm here.

This place was highly reviewed and recommended so had to make a stop here! The environment was amazing! It was so grand and spacious. Though spacious place, but filled with lots of people! This is a very busy hit up spot for dinner. They have a nice waiting area while they setup your table. You can order drinks while you wait. You can make a reservation! Lobster Fried Rice: This was one of the popular dishes. The was cooked perfectly and seasoned well. There were lots of lobster pieces. Crab Stir Fry Noodles: The glass noodles were my favorite! The texture was perfect! Lots of vegetables and meat in the dish!Sizzling Short Ribs: The rubs were so good! I love how there was chow fun noodles and asian pear. The asian pear was a good balance to the flavorful dish! The price was expensive, but honestly it was not bad comparing to how fancy and the quantity and quality of the food we get! Would recommend to come experience it!

As much as I didn't want to love this place, this ended up being one of my favorite restaurants. Each time someone comes into town, this is one of the places I recommend. I've introduced this place to a few of my friends and they all loved it too. I've been lucky with timing each time and only waited about 30 min. for a seat. The reason I come here is for their Toro Ssam Bap with uni added on top. They give you a bowl of nori sheets to make your own hand rolls. The uni is an extra $13 but well worth it. It's a lot of expensive ingredients, but the together the textures are amazing. For appetizers, I also tried the Jeju Chicken Wings and Soon Du Bu. Sometimes at Korean restaurants the soondubu broth is too thin, but this broth was on the richer and more savory side.I've tried the SO Ramyun and Fish Coop. I'm not normally a ramen fan in general, but I'm now a Korean ramyun fan. The SO Ramyun veal broth is very rich and the beef is tender. If you want something on the lighter side the Fish Coop is a good option, but I prefer the SO Ramyun. The bowls are deceptively small. I wouldn't be able to finish a bowl by myself with how rich and filling it is. I would recommend getting the ramyun to share so you can try different items on the menu. The cool thing about this place is that the waiters are also the chefs. They rotate who works in the kitchen and who works on the floor. You can tell they are all chefs with all the tattoos they have.

neighborhood Thai food placed located in Alphabet City / East Village.ordered food for delivery. you can do it by phone (GASP) or Seamless, Grubhub, Eat24, etc. there's always that moment where you question whether you should have ordered Thai as a first-timer...thankfully, i didn't  regret it, at all. the food here was solidly good. prices are a bit higher than you'd normally expect. however, the portions feel large / hefty...translation: the containers are packed full.the Pad Se-Ew with shrimp was satisfying. stir-fried broad noodles, lightly spiced (not spicy at all), some veggies, etc. it has that light soy sauce flavor without being salty. again, big portion--ample amount to share.the Thai Fried Rice with tofu. not greasy fried rice. lightly fried jasmine rice, scallions, eggs, etc. a little bland but perfect if you're in the mood for fried rice without the grease or heat. this isn't just a takeout and delivery place. it's dine-in as well.delivery was fairly quick. drops mic cuz it's time for Thaii outzzz

Title: Delightful Pastelitos at Dominican Cravings

I recently visited Dominican Cravings on a bustling Friday evening. The initial impression was a bit off-putting as I was overlooked by staff engrossed in their own chatter despite a moderately crowded counter. However, the annoyance faded once I sampled their pastelitos. Opting for both beef and ham and cheese varieties, I was pleasantly surprised to find them not only warm and flavorful but also generously stuffed. Based on the quality of these pastelitos, I find myself eager to return and explore more of their menu. Despite a slight hiccup in service, Dominican Cravings made a positive mark on my culinary map.

I've visited this spot multiple times but finally decided to indulge in the famed Margarita Tower—a must for groups of four or more. While the $115 price tag may seem steep, it's absolutely worth it. Opting for the Guava Margarita, which has quickly become my favorite, I was delighted by its strength and flavor. The tower serves generous portions, with each of us comfortably enjoying 3-4 glasses, the buzz dictating our pace. For those on the fence, I highly recommend giving it a go at least once. It's an experience that doesn't disappoint.

We found this place thanks to a list of where to find good Frose we happen to be in the area & decided to give it a try. we came in & were seated right away , they offer some happy hour specials but not for the Paloma Froze, not cool considering they have it featured but oh well we gave it a try anyways, it was decent good taste but not worth the $15-16 dollar price tag for such a small glass. Ended up changing to some beer for happy hour , Dos XX not bad can't go wrong w beer. Tacos are very small, plenty to choose from so I asked for a suggestion & the waitress mentioned the short rib so I tried that one, ahhh it was ok nothing special about it, decent taste to the meat. we also had the California girl now this one was much better great flavor & taste with all the extra on top, lettuce, tomatoes etc.  As for the restaurant decent size with plenty of seating inside & out, fun beachy decor .. service was good & prices are not bad for the happy hour menu, a bit high on regular drinks.

This hidden gem (to me) was quite a charm. My very best friend, whom I treat like a sister brought me here with my brother who is from Manila. We ate Thai food and we ordered the calamari. Very subtle, which you wouldnt think how great the calamari and the sauce they pair it with. It was too amazing, we actually ordered this again as our 'dessert'! TRULY A MEMORY for your senses to experience. The place is packed, expect to have a little bit of wait for a party of 4 or so. I would go back again just because of how they make their sauce. it's truly magic.

Restaurant Week Lunch 2020 $26 for 2 course. Got salmon tartare and 3 chips that taste exactly like onion chip in indonesia as appetizer, big portion. Nice flavour and presentation . Demi strip steak ( additional supplement $12). My friend was shocked when it's coming because it's tiny. But by the end of the  steak we have trouble to finish it. Don't let ur eyes fooled you. The steak nicely done in medium rare. I also order passion fruit margarita that quite potent for lunch :) and key lime pie to share. The meringue slightly too sweet for me but it's because my keto diet regime that made all the food I ate too sweet. Service is good and very efficient. Total cost $85 with tip. Expensive lunch indeed. I definitely come back to this steak joint

I was pleasantly surprised by my experience at Bubby's, as I think it deserves far higher praise than it seems to receive. The highlight is undoubtedly their menu, which features incredibly fluffy biscuits - a pure delight when paired with their delicious jams and butter. Gluten-free diners are in for a treat as well; Bubby's gluten-free pancakes might even surpass their regular ones in taste, which is no small feat. Just a heads-up for the weekend crowd - it gets quite busy, so anticipate a wait. But trust me, it's worth it.

I was very excited to visit this restaurant as it was my first time visiting Manhattan and I had heard from multiple sources that Delmonico's was one of the best steakhouses in the city! My girlfriend and I were celebrating our 2 year anniversary and I thought this restaurant would be the perfect choice for us to celebrate our anniversary at. I called the restaurant in advance to inform them of our anniversary and book a reservation and I was told by the hostess they would notate our special day on the reservation. Unfortunately we were never wished a happy anniversary by the staff, offered no champagne or dessert, or even provided with quality service. Our server rarely visited our table to check on us and took quite some time to come and take our dinner order. When I have visited other steakhouses on special occasions the very least they do is wish you a happy birthday, anniversary, etc. and/or give you a glass of champagne to celebrate, this restaurant did nothing unfortunately. Ok to the food. The steak I ordered was actually quite good! I ordered the Delmonico Steak and it was very large and full of great flavor. The server informed me that they wet age the steak for 28 days and I thought it was one of the best pieces of meat I had eaten. The Delmonico's potatoes we had ordered were extremely tasty and the wedge salad was outstanding! The portions here are quite generous so no need to order a bunch of food if it is just for two people because you won't finish it!  While the food here is incredible the quality of service needs to match that. I am not asking for a parade when I come in the door but at the very least wishing someone a happy birthday or anniversary should be a priority. The prices are very good for what you're getting.

I did the $155 omakaseNo need to repeat how amazing this place is as everyone else already applause applause.HOWEVER, I have to say towards the end of the meal I started to get a little confused about what I was eating as every other course was either truffled, caviared, or foied, etc.First half of the course was a normal style, second half started to go wild. Ingredients are amazing but when one nigiri has 4-5 ingredients I found it a bit difficult to appreciate them.I guess too good is not a good thing as well? Anyways still a unique omakase experience that's not the same with anywhere in the city.I think if I come back I will still do the premium and I might eat the ingredient separately.... And then I might be banned from the restaurant forever.

I had a craving for Japanese yakiniku so I decided to try Yakiniku Futago. An upscaled somewhat pricey bbq establishment with food and service to match. Started with two sushi pieces, the kalbi and the caviar uni wagyu sushi pieces; 2 piece min. The uni wagyu was very fresh, super creamy and rich. The meat just melted in my mouth.The Deep Fried Shrimp and Quail Egg with Shiso served individually on a stick was a very nice and interesting combination. The Grilled Giant Prawns were grilled perfectly and delicious. Finally the Treasure Box which varies by day. On this day, it was chateaubriand. The meat was very soft and rich in umami flavor. It was cooked to perfection but my only gripe was they shouldn't have used scissors to cut such a rich piece of meat.

Jack's Wife Freda, a place that buzzes with hype, offered a brunch experience that shone despite some significant drawbacks. The deafening din of the popular music selection amidst a bustling crowd was a notable discomfort, subtracting from the charm one might expect from such a trendy hotspot.

However, this shortcoming was counterbalanced by the excellent Mediterranean Breakfast that hit all the right notes with its balanced portions and delectable labneh, paired wonderfully with a refreshing mint lemonade. The commitment to sustainability with the offering of paper straws deserves a nod.

Service did not fall victim to the packed space; the staff was efficient, maintaining their cheerful demeanor and even adding a personal touch with parting gifts of postcards and matchbooks.

If you're willing to brave a potentially lengthy wait, Jack's Wife Freda rewards you with great food and service that elevate the overall experience. Just be sure to set expectations for a vibrant, albeit noisy, ambiance.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a charming café known for its exceptional breakfast and lunch offerings. From the moment I was greeted by the amiable cooks, I knew I was in for a treat. Their versatility is commendable, with a menu that spans from mouthwatering tacos to the homely comfort of pollo guisado—I'd confidently recommend any dish they serve.

My go-to choices include the perfectly balanced veggie omelet, succulent roasted chicken accompanied by flavorful yellow rice and steamed veggies, and the classic BLT, which never fails to satisfy, as evidenced by the photo I've shared.

A heads-up for fellow diners: the establishment operates on a card-only basis for orders above $10. While seating is somewhat limited, it contributes to the cozy ambiance of the café. If you're seeking a delightful meal prepared by genuinely pleasant chefs, I cannot recommend this café enough.

Joe's Shanghai - A Disappointing Encounter with Overhyped Dumplings

My efforts to avoid the Joe's Shanghai chain finally faltered one evening post-9 pm movie when dining options were scarce. Granted, we were seated immediately – a single point in their favor. Yet, this fleeting positive was overshadowed by the lackluster experience that unfolded.

The crab meat and pork soup dumplings sounded promising but failed to deliver. The unwieldy thick skins encapsulated a dense and greasy broth that overshadowed the meat, which itself was uninvitingly firm. Any anticipation of a delicate crab flavor was occasionally met with an unpleasantly synthetic fishy taste. Even the pan-fried pork dumplings, while boasting a crispy exterior, were marred by a similarly too-solid meat filling.

Adding insult to injury, the accompanying sauces seemed to betray an aversion to flavor. The black vinegar with ginger lacked punch, and the sweetened soy sauce came across as watered-down. One wonders, were these the dregs of the day's offerings or a standard we were unfortunate enough to encounter?

A commendation is due to the waiting staff for their efficiency and kindness, notably the thoughtful provision of a whole teapot when cups were all we'd requested. However, no amount of polite service can fully compensate for culinary disappointment.

The question lingers – were these the sad remnants at day's end or the norm? Regardless, Joe's Shanghai fell short, turning what was meant to be a meal of necessity into one of regret.

As with many of the Korean places in nyc, this place has the same owner as her name is han.Coming in here, it seems like it serves some more homey dishes that are elevated. Seems like this place specializes in pots.We got the oxtail soup and a mushroom and beef appetizer and a pasta dish. The least favorite was the pasta. It was just some pasta with some pickled veggies in chili oil. Wasn't bad, just didn't hit me like the other dishes.The mushroom and beef was nice, I enjoyed the beef a lot, very well flavored and fatty.The highlight without a doubt was the oxtail soup. First off, these pots come with rice cooked with your choice of mushroom, chicken, or fish (mushroom one is free). So that was a nice touch.Then the actual dish itself was amazing. Had oxtail, tendons, brisket, and ofc the broth.All were so lightly flavored, perfectly cooked, and very wholesome.Then we were asked if we wanted to add some udon...and we were kinda indifferent, but when we found out it came with more broth we instantly signed up! Easily one of my favorite Korean restaurant in the city.

Title: A Flavorful Dive into Ivan Ramen

After watching the Chef's Table episode featuring Ivan Ramen, my curiosity was piqued, and on my recent trip to NYC, I finally visited. Despite its size, I had no trouble securing a reservation at this cozy spot.

I began with an assortment of pickles, particularly enjoying the pickled daikon - a delightful blend of tart vinegar and savory dried shrimp. The fried chicken lived up to its recommendations, boasting succulent meat and a shiso ranch sauce that perfectly complemented each bite.

The main event was the tonkatsu ramen, intriguingly served cold with warm broth on the side for dipping. While the quality of the dish was undeniable, the unorthodox presentation did not win me over, proving somewhat cumbersome and messy to eat.

In all, Ivan Ramen delivered an experience that was both hit and miss, with memorable flavors but mixed feelings about the execution of their unique ramen offering.

Title: A Delightful Birthday Brunch Surprise

My birthday celebration at this restaurant proved to be a delightful surprise, starting with the service. Despite apprehensions stemming from previous scathing reviews, my waiter AJ shattered all doubts by being patient, informative, and highly attentive. He kept our glasses filled, and even when things got hectic, the manager pitched in to ensure a seamless experience. Kudos to AJ for outstanding service!

The food was equally impressive. My Johnny cakes were a revelation paired with perfectly crispy yet succulent chicken wings, and the bacon was crispy without being overdone - a brunch essential that demanded a second helping. The Duck Hash, chosen by my friend, was an adventurous and satisfying twist on a classic.

The vibrant ambience, with neighboring tables equally enjoying their meals, hinted at the quality of other dishes and ensured my intention to return. AJ, see you soon for another culinary adventure!

I'm revising my previous review after a recent visit where I dined in for the first time. Unfortunately, I was disappointed with the food quality. The steamed vegetable dumplings had skins that were unappealingly thick and doughy. Also, the pork soup dumplings' sweetness was overpowering, which detracted from the overall flavor. At $9 for 6 pieces, the pricing felt steep for what was delivered. This experience has led me to lower my rating by a star.

At Tacombi, the size of the place catches you off guard – it's a vast, high-ceilinged area with ample seating. Ordering is straightforward with a slip to specify your choices. The food arrives quickly once the order is in, the highlight being the Corn Esquites, a chowder-like delight topped with cotija cheese and morita mayo – perfect comfort food. The Avocado Tostada is another winner – at $4, it's a steal, with the flavors and textures blending beautifully.

The service, although friendly, can be MIA; with a sparse crowd, we still struggled to flag someone down to pay our bill. On the flip side, certain items didn't impress – skip the pricey guacamole and the lackluster black bean and sweet potato tacos.

Tacombi may not be an NYC essential, but for those seeking a spacious hideout to while away a few hours, it's got you covered.

Title: Hit-and-Miss at a Classy Eatery

After hearing rave reviews about this restaurant, I walked in with high hopes, only to be met with a mixed experience. The decor was impressive, setting the stage for what I assumed would be a memorable meal in a positive sense. The unique entrance and ease of getting seated upon arrival, thanks to our reservation, were both pluses in a classy establishment that held its charm visibly.

The service staff was courteous and responsive, particularly when accommodating our special request to have the meat served on the side for a vegetarian member of our party. The food, when it eventually arrived at our table, was presented beautifully and tasted delightful. Standouts included the tomato soup paired with grilled cheese and the pancakes, scoring an 8/10 and 9/10 respectively.

Unfortunately, the evening's rhythm was thrown off by the poorly executed timing of our dishes. The staggering arrival of food, almost an hour apart from the first to the last item, significantly dampened our family-style sharing experience. Adding insult to injury, the restaurant's internal temperature was uncomfortably cold, forcing us to keep our coats on throughout the meal.

Despite the good tastes, the mac and cheese and pizza fell short of expectations, earning a 6/10 and a less than impressive 4/10. Even the well-executed dishes lost their appeal as they cooled rapidly, which combined with the delay, ruined the mood of our dining experience.

In summary, while the restaurant certainly has the potential for greatness with its ambiance and some well-crafted dishes, the overall experience was marred by logistical shortcomings. A revisit solely depends on whether these kinks are ironed out in the future.

So glad this place is doing take out and delivery during the lock down. Gotta have this delicious food! The pancit is really delicious and they give you a nice portion. I always tell myself to save some but that never works. The tacos are some of my favorites. Its a really nice take on a Filipino fusion. The tasty choices of pork and beef are my go to's and theyre definitely a good meal appetizer. Their lumpia is really delicious and a favorite among our group. Can't wait until theyre open for full service as I want to make sure this gem sticks around LES.

Title: A Festive Feast at Bodega Negra

My experience at Bodega Negra was like a perpetual fiesta! Visiting during Restaurant Week, my quest for authentic Mexican cuisine and a stellar margarita was a total success. Their Happy Hour, running from 5:30-7:30 PM, offers an alluring half-price deal on sangria, margaritas, and select eats, though it's exclusive to the bar area. To take advantage of this, we arrived pre-reservation and indulged in some economically savvy pre-dinner drinks.

The margaritas, though slightly inconsistent (the first was impeccable, the second, overly sweet), were thoroughly enjoyable. When a friend's tardiness pushed our reservation time, the host gracefully accommodated us without a fuss.

As for the food, despite the margarita-induced haze, I recall each bite being scrumptious. The service was exceptional; our waitress navigated through the spirited Friday crowd with friendliness and efficiency.

There's no doubt in my mind—I'll be returning to Bodega Negra for another unforgettable night.

Title: A Tasty Budget Bite at Xing Wong BBQ

After our plans fell through at Wah Fung due to an unexpected closure, my friend introduced me to Xing Wong, tucked away in the heart of Chinatown. A stone's throw from the metro station, this unassuming spot offers a wallet-friendly menu that doesn't skimp on flavor.

Pressed for time, we opted for takeout. I zeroed in on the crispy skin pork – a litmus test for any respected Chinese BBQ joint. Although my meal had to brave a couple of hours before consumption, it remained a testament to Xing Wong's culinary prowess. The skin lost its crispiness, an unfortunate but expected result of its container confinement. However, the pork itself still tasted delightful, a savior during my airport wait.

At a mere $5, you get a generous serving of meat, rice, vegetables, and even a complementary soup, making Xing Wong a standout for budget dining. While I look forward to exploring more of their offerings in person, for anyone in need of a quick, delicious bite, their Chinese BBQ meats with rice are a sure bet. Cash-only policy aside, Xing Wong is a must-try for authentic eats in Chinatown.

I recently dined at a charming French-style bistro that captured my heart. With doors opening at 9 AM, they cater to the early birds looking for a delectable breakfast and continue to serve through lunch and dinner, offering a versatile dining experience.

The Eggs Benedict was a standout, perfectly executed with choices that cater to a variety of preferences, including Canadian bacon, smoked salmon, or spinach. The dish came with a delightful side of potatoes bathed in a robust tomato sauce, dotted with vibrant green and red peppers – a true homage to the finesse of French cuisine.

Their cappuccino was exceptional, rich and aromatic, serving as the ideal companion to the meal. Adding to the authentic atmosphere was the courteous French staff, who enhanced the dining experience with their attentive service.

On days when the weather is kind, they offer al fresco dining, which I found to be a delightful option. This bistro is a gem worth visiting for anyone craving a slice of France.
My new favorite place! Everything is perfect I don't even know what else to say. The vibe was light and airy in the best way. The staff was warm. The music was fun. The food was made with with.

I ventured to White Horse in Downtown Manhattan for a much-needed Happy Hour reprieve after work. The place came highly recommended for its evening specials, and I was keen to try the Cupcake Prosecco from Italy, reasonably priced at $8. While the bar was bustling for a Thursday evening, the service left something to be desired, as it wasn't particularly attentive. The atmosphere was overshadowed by the loud, boisterous music that spilled out even to the entrance. White Horse is your typical dive bar, frequented by the financial district's white-collar crowd looking to unwind from the day's stress.

Sad to report the spinach pie (spanokopita) here isn't so great. The dough was very tough and thick on the outside, not the usual flaky pastry dough -- not sure if that's on purpose though. The chai latte is comparable to Starbuck's-- so if you're into that you'll be happy here as well !

I recently visited one of New York's most talked-about pizza spots, eager to see if the hype lived up to the reality. The pizza slice was indeed impressive in size, possibly one of the largest I've encountered in the city. However, the slice I chose, which was topped with artichokes on a cream base, didn't quite hit the mark for me. The rich cream was a bit overpowering, overshadowing the artichokes that I typically enjoy.

While that particular slice might not have been my cup of tea, the pizzeria does offer a wide selection of toppings, so there's something for everyone. For those curious about this popular establishment, I'd recommend giving it a shot to form your own opinion. Just a note - maybe the experience is different if you're not sober, but I can only speak from a clear-headed standpoint.

Food: 4/5Came for lunch. I know it's an Italian restaurant but unfortunately I didn't try their pasta. I ordered grilled chicken with grilled vegetables. It's cooked in oil and garlic. Very clean and came out fast. I have a lot of food sensitivity and the food here didn't cause any stomach problems for me. My friend ordered the spaghetti and meatballs. Looked appealing but I didn't try any. The bread came out perfectly baked and warm. Our tab was roughly $55 including tip. My chicken was $22.Service: 4/5Good service. Our waiter was friendly and accommodating.Ambiance: 2/5This place is very dark and slightly dingy. It's also pretty small. It's very long and narrow. They have a bar in the front and seating in the back. Our table was dirty upon arrival and had bits of food remains on the table. There was a slight odor lingering.

Best pork bun I have ever had. Got the Shiromaru hakata classic with added naruto (fish cake). Was disappointing that it was 5 small and thin slices for $2 extra, but live and learn. My friend was disappointed that her ramen that was supposed to come with a soft boiled egg was actually only half an egg, not a whole.  Overall, it was good, and not terribly expensive considering you are on NYC, I have had some beamed broths make me sick and I was fine with this. Would go back.

The last place I went before quarantine was The Smith. One of my go to places in the city. I haven't ever had anything on their menu I haven't enjoyed. They are almost always busy, even a short wait sometimes with a reservation, but worth it. You can't go wrong here. I recommend the mac and cheese to start with, and then anything else on the menu as a meal!

Actually 3.5/5. We went there for restaurant week, but we don't find many delicious food ok the restaurant week menu, so we just ordered the steak, tiramisu, and the chocolate cake. All of them are ok - nothing wrong but not very exciting.I like the interior furnishing and the service is really good! But I don't think I will go back again.

One of my mantras is that "food doesn't have to be fancy to be good."  Now, that's not to say that a meal decently plated isn't a feast for the eyes, but it's the flavor that counts.  We eat out quite often, and we've been to some high-end restaurants that were great, and some that were "meh."  And we've been to holes in the wall that had some of the best food we've ever eaten.  I am an unabashed and ardent carnivore, so give me a nice tomahawk steak and a bottle of Italian red, and that's pretty much a perfect meal for me.  But, I will say, our meal here the other night was one of the best I've had in years.  It definitely earned it's Michelin star.  The food wasn't fancy, but the flavors melded so well together, it was a very sensuous experience.  As for the points, very moderate.  There was burrata cheese with raw and cooked apple spirals, complimented by a pecan-mint pesto.  There was shaved broccoli, with quinoa and poached cranberries, with some grated taleggio cheese.  There was cauliflower tempura, and a pan-seared potato gnocchi with butternut squash, chestnuts and truffles.  It was so good I'm still thinking about it tonight!  So, for any of you vegetarians in the area, or traveling to the area, you should give it a try!  They do most of the dishes vegan as well (two separate menus)!

Title: A Culinary Delight Not to Be Missed!

From the moment you step into this culinary haven, you know you've struck gold. The ambiance is nothing short of beautiful, setting the stage for an impressive dining experience. One piece of advice - make reservations and ensure your party arrives together because they adhere to a full-party seating policy.

The menu, which offers subtle changes regularly, promises a delightful surprise with every visit. On the advice of our attentive waiter, we opted for a mix of small and large plates complemented by a trio of side dishes - an abundance which turned out to be both generous and irresistibly tasty.

Starting with small plates like succulent chicken skewers, crispy vegetable spring rolls, flavorful octopus a la plancha, and chilled peekytoe crabs (plus one more that slips my mind but looked as enticing as it tasted!), we were off to an impressive start.

Our large plate selections - the melt-in-your-mouth American Wagyu strip loin, the aromatic coconut crescent duck, the tender yellow chicken, and the perfectly cooked Akuna cod bilindango - were all standouts, with spices that brought each dish to life.

To complement our mains, we ordered nasi goreng, perfectly charred Brussel sprouts, and delightfully crispy corn fritters. Though it sounds like a feast fit for royalty, and it was, we were four diners relishing every mouthful. 

The must-try dish recommendations? The tender and perfectly seasoned octopus a la plancha, the aromatic coconut crescent duck, and alongside a bowl of nasi goreng, the yellow chicken is a real treat.

Ending on a sweet note, we indulged in an assortment of desserts including exotic fruits, silky chocolate ganache, a fragrant kaffir lime pie, and a banana sundae courtesy of the house. If I had to pick favorites, it would be a tie between the banana sundae and the chocolate ganache - both absolutely stellar!

In a nutshell, this place is a taste sensation that will leave your taste buds dancing for joy. I wholeheartedly recommend this gem to anyone looking for a meal that's as memorable as it is delicious.

Title: Authentic Flavors at Dun Huang

My culinary quests have led me twice to Dun Huang, which has a peculiar slogan promising an authentic Chinese experience, but it delivers on that claim with delectable offerings. The standout dish, handmade noodles with beef, arrives adorned with radish and a tantalizing drizzle of chili oil. The light, savory broth harmonizes well with the noodles' perfect texture, which you can tailor to your liking. Accompanying tender beef morsels complete the ensemble.

Venturing into the lamb skewers, while satisfying, wasn't as impressive. Although good, I expected a deeper infusion of chili and cumin flavor, and the price tag—$5 for a single skewer—felt steep for what was offered. Pro tip for fellow diners: the more sensibly priced five-skewer option is the way to go.

Don't miss out on a delightful beginning with the complimentary cucumber appetizer, an epitome of refreshment, especially if you check in on Yelp or Facebook. This small gesture exemplifies the seamless service and the clean, inviting ambiance that defines Dun Huang.

Would I recommend Dun Huang? Absolutely, for anyone seeking a taste of China without the airfare.

This place is amazing and one of the best French restaurants I've been to. It's extremely cozy upon entering (looks like it sits maybe 15-20ish people max?) and they don't take reservations. They also don't have paper menus but rather write it on the wall. This place offers fewer but is extremely focused on each dish making it that I don't think you can go wrong ordering any of them.We ordered the squid and the duck confit and grilled squid which were both amazing. The duck confit was my favorite as it was so tender and just melted in your mouth. It wasn't too salty and was cooked perfectly. The squid was also excellent and the sauce was the perfect complement. Although, I thought this dish was a little less filling and little saltier. Overall I would highly recommend trying this restaurant. It seems like it might be newer but I can see it getting pretty popular. The cozy and dim ambiance makes it great for a date night. The wait is worth it and honestly will probably be less than an hour unless you go at super peak times.

Title: Unagi Excellence With a Price Tag

My latest culinary venture was quite the investment, but the high-quality unagi on offer justified the expenditure. Be warned, the ambience leans towards the peculiar side, with black walls and scant lighting that border on the murky. However, this is a side note to the impeccable service and the exceptional unagi that graced our table.

Diners are treated to a choice between east-coast and west-coast unagi preparations. I savored the Kabayaki, drenched in a sumptuous sauce emulating the texture of sushi toppings, while my boyfriend sampled the Shirayaki, which boasted a subtle crunch. The verdict? East-coast style emerged victorious for our palates.

Accompanying daikon pickles were a standout, introducing a delightful and distinctive punch. However, the clear soup's eel liver insert was less impressive, imparting an unwelcome metallic note to the experience.

A light and invigorating wine gelatin concluded our meal on a high. While I may not be drawn back for an evening affair, the lunch offerings seem enticing enough for a return.

Pontry Bistro was the restaurant that my cousin took me to last month for a nice "Belated Birthday Dinner" experience. This place has been on my radar for some time in regards to brunch (still have to get back there to try their french toast-lol)  and I was glad that we were able to make reservations and try some of their reportedly delicious dinner entrees.Pontry Bistro is in Harlem situated on a corner near West 139th Street. It was a nice August evening when I arrived to meet my cousin who was already comfy at the bar w/ a beer in her hand.. The restaurant is intimate, yet provides enough room for patrons to spread out between the bar and dining table areas. Cool lighting, pretty mirrors and Afrocentric artwork are on some of the walls which I appreciate. The bar area is near the front entrance and we talked w/ the bartender for several minutes before we were seated towards the back area by windows so that we were able to have an outisde view. Our server was patient w/ us as I had questions about cocktails and we both made inquiries about entree options. It was kindly explained to me and I agreed to have the bartender make me a special created concoction that is not on the menu. The cocktail was a mixture of citrus flavors that I like along with some liquor that would not be overpowering in relation to the sweerness of the drink. It really was good, strong and fruity.  My cousin ordered Shrimp Scampi (she absolutely loves shrimp) and I had Penne A La Vodka w Chicken. The entrees were well prepared w/ marinated ingredients that tasted great. Ponty Bistro also gives you huge plated portions so much so that I had to request a to-go bag (which I can say I enjoyed the next day for lunch).  Ponty Bistro's music selection had us snapping our fingers and dancing in our seats as we ate our meal. Everything from Chris Brown's new album to his previous hits to Ric Ross songs and other hip hop music was played...Nothing beats hearing music you enjoy while having good food!This place comes highly recommended and I will be back for french toast!

This was during COVID 19 delivery.  Best packaged delivery I've received!  Arrived in perfect condition and quickly.  I ordered spicy basil chicken, which was pleasantly spicy and full of grilled veggies.  I also ordered Thai spring rolls, which were hot and crispy.  The chicken curry puffs were my favorite!  Seasoned so well, light flaky outer crust, delicious!  The sauces with the spring rolls and curry puffs were both really flavorful.  I also got spicy potatoes, which were good, but they were in a thick sauce and not my favored texture.  I did love their Thai iced tea.  I would definitely try this place again!

I recently ventured to Frenchette on the recommendation of a foodie friend and was thoroughly impressed. Having made reservations a month in advance for my out-of-town friend's birthday, we found the service, food, and ambiance to be nothing short of spectacular. Despite skipping dessert due to full stomachs, the thoughtful staff surprised my friend with a complimentary birthday treat. The entire experience left me eager to return for their brunch offerings or to simply enjoy a casual evening at the bar.

After having our first brunch of the day, we decided to stop for our second. Because why not. We love food. We decided to go to The Smith and what a cute place. It's like a weird diner but not? We waited roughly 30 minutes which wasn't bad considering both inside AND outside were packed. Even while it was 35 degrees out. What even is that.The tables are VERY close together. It's probably socially acceptable to reach over and enjoy your neighbors food as well honestly. Because surprise! You're now a part of every family next to you.I went with the Tomato Soup that came topped with melted cheddar cheese and even more cheese dumped on the bottom with some bread. See, originally I was going to go with the Mac & Cheese because it looked and smelled delicious oh god. But I have this thing where dairy and I aren't friends so I opted to go with something a little.. less cheesy.Husband had the Caramel Apple Compote Waffle. It was pretty tasty, especially with the Mascarpone on the side. My ONLY complaint about it was that it specifically states waffleS. As in, more than one. It was for sure one waffle cut in half. Girl, who you trying to play. Still yummy though.In the end, nice place. I for sure would come back for lunch. Maybe not brunch on the weekend. Also the bar looks super awesome so if you can sit there maybe do that too.

Title: Hidden Gem with Delightful Eats

My recent visit to this charming underground restaurant was an absolute delight. The menu is wonderfully inclusive, offering something for everyone - from hearty burgers to succulent chicken sandwiches, and even satisfying veggie options. I indulged in the buffalo chicken sandwich, which did not disappoint. The freshness of the blue cheese crumbles paired with the zesty buffalo sauce was a match made in heaven. On the side, the fresh-cut waffle fries were a crispy perfection. Overall, the experience was top-notch, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit. It's definitely a spot worth coming back to.

My first slice of New York pizza  was at Joe's. Ordered a slice of pepperoni from here and wow I was amazed at how the dough and cheese tasted. It was something I have to say I have never had before. I fell in love instantly can understand why they have so many people eating here. It's a convenient and easy process to get a slice of pizza. Just come up to the counter and order what slice you want. After I literally was walking and eating the slice of pizza. There isn't a large seating area and pretty much it's standing. But if you want I'd suggest just walking and eating. It seems more nostalgic to me. Be a New Yorker haha when in NYC. I love the thinness of the pizza and if you are super hungry I'd suggest getting more than a slice because you will be craving this all day and night!

Title: A Pleasant First-time Visit with Great Vibes

I recently dined at this restaurant for the first time and found the atmosphere to be comfortably bustling with an excellent music selection that contributed to the casual, relaxed vibes. Despite missing Happy Hour, the $6 hurricanes available all day were a delightful treat.

Opting for the 3-course meal at $35, I started with a Caesar salad, which was a fresh and fitting beginning. The main course, chicken Cajun pasta, was enjoyably spicy and hit all the right notes for someone who appreciates a bit of heat in their dish. To conclude, the brownie was pleasant, though I would have preferred it with nuts for an added crunch.

Service throughout the meal was efficient and courteous. Based on this positive experience, I look forward to returning to this establishment in the future.

I really enjoyed my experience at Caffe Buon Gusto! It's a very small and cozy space, when it's busy it may be verging on uncomfortable tight but I like going to places that feel full! We were seated about five minutes after we arrived, so a little bit past our reservation time. Even though it's small this would be a great place to go for a group dinner I think because it's got long tables that would be perfect for larger groups. They have a pretty extensive menu with lots of homemade pasta options that you can mix and match with sauces, along with a full list of entrées! I had the homemade gnocchi which was absolutely delicious and very fresh and the vodka sauce was also really good my only complaint would be that I wanted more of it!Only reason that I'm giving this place four stars instead of five is that the service is a little iffy. It seemed we had about three different waiters throughout our time and we had to flag them down at times to order things like dessert, but the food made up for that and everyone was super friendly so I can overlook it.Will definitely be returning in the future!

Title: In Search of Cali Tacos at Essex Taqueria

Moving from California, I never thought I'd miss the Mexican cuisine until my taco cravings set in. Eager to satisfy them, I stumbled upon Essex Taqueria, conveniently located just a few blocks from my new abode. As a devout taco enthusiast, I naturally opted for two tacos. Here's where the disappointment subtly crept in – no corn tortillas, a staple for any street taco aficionado like myself. Instead, my tacos came with lettuce, a topping I could do without. The asada and adobada meats were passable but lacked the wow factor I was yearning for.

Service-wise, the pace was leisurely, to put it kindly, and that's with me being the sole diner at the moment. If you're on the lookout for a quick bite, this might not be the place. The horchata was middling, but I will tip my hat to their salsa for its pleasant heat.

In the grand scheme of things, Essex Taqueria doesn't quite hit the mark for me, and I'm left with the quest for that quintessential New York taco spot. Here's hoping the city has more to offer.

Service was exceptional and food was phenomenal.For appetizer, I ordered pulipo and it was easily one of the best seared octopus I've had. The yogurt chives, fennel, and lemon complimented each other very well. For entree, malfade (crab, shrimp, scallop, lemon confit, calabrian chili butter)and torcia (squid ink pasta with seppia and shrimp ragu) was fantastic. Best pasta in town!

Came here with a friend because he tried this place before and told me its to die for. I have pretty high standards when it comes to truffle pizza so I had to check out this place for myself. We ordered the arugula salad as a starter and then the diavola pizza and the truffle pizza that was a part of their specials. I absolutely love truffle pizza but this one was pretty average up to the point that I enjoyed the diavola pizza more. The crust was probably the best part of the two pies. I love brick oven pizza so that part did not disappoint. The salad was also pretty good, super basic and easy to make so you can't mess that up. The rice balls were also good as well. The price was average, and the customer service was well.

Still excellent! Went again this time with the whole family. Wellingtons were on point. Scotch egg, barretta salad and one person got fish and chips. Everyone loved everthing. The waiter was attentive and entertaining. Tried the toffee cake and the bread pudding, putting was maybe the best I've had. My only regret was not ordering a side of the dill potatoes.

More around a 3. something than a solid 4 for me. I was really excited to try this place. Saw them on Shark Tank and then was thrilled to see that my office was moving downtown and virtually two blocks away from this place. Placed an order today for the lunch special: Spicy Mang roll and The Badge dumplings. I also tacked on a Nutty Buddy wrap because if you sign up for an account with their app you get a $5 reward. (bonus points for this!)Of all three items, the best was definitely The Badge dumplings. I would go back exclusively for those. My least favorite was the Nutty Buddy. It looked pretty but it really was very bland, and not great to eat without sauce. The sauce it did come with was a sweet, thick brown sauce which made it taste better but was ultimately too sweet and thick for me. I wound up dipping it in the sauce that came with the Spicy Mang roll. The Spicy Mang roll was just OK for me, definitely more flavor than the Nutty Buddy but still not on par with the dumplings. I also didn't find it to be spicy at all.I read reviews before going and people said that there was so much food and it was so filling, but I ate all three items and then sat there completely unsatisfied. Ever eat a meal and then just.... need something else because it doesn't even feel like you ate? That's how I felt after lunch today. I wound up jetting over to Dunkin for an iced coffee and a bavarian creme donut.The idea is great, and many people seem to love it here, but ultimately, I don't think it was for me, something just felt missing.

Came here for dinner with a friend today on a Friday around 5:30. We ordered a couple things from the menu and it was delicious! Their orange sauce they put on their food is delicious! Their pricing is fairly low and the atmosphere was chill. I would say our waitress could have made more of an effort for our table. My friend and I had to look out for her and get her attention every time. The table next to us had to do the same. (In all fairness she had a bigger party near us, but still annoying because she only came to us once without us flagging her down).

Title: A Flavorful Feast with a Spicy Kick

My recent dining experience at this local spot was a delightful journey through an array of Asian-inspired dishes. Each plate presented a unique combination of flavors that both excited and challenged the palate.

The glass noodle dish was a standout, earning a well-deserved 5/5 for its perfect blend of seasoning. Equally impressive was the BBQ beef, which struck a harmonious balance between savory and sweet tones, clearly meriting another 5/5.

Although the fried rice boasted a vibrant egg topping, its spice level overshadowed the other elements, making it a bit too hot for my taste, thus a 3/5. The broccoli accompanying the rice could have also benefited from a tad more steaming.

The stuffed squid was a revelation, with a spicy yet delicious filling of pork and vegetables, ideal for pairing with rice – a definite 5/5.

I found the clam soup to be overwhelmingly spicy, packed with pepper that dominated its flavor profile. Unfortunately, this made it less enjoyable for me, leading to a score of 2/5.

A watermelon bowl was a common sight at every table, providing a refreshing end to the meal without overpowering sweetness – a solid 4/5.

The service was attentive without being overbearing, ensuring a comfortable dining experience. However, it's worth noting that they do not accept Visa cards, which could be a minor inconvenience.

Overall, this restaurant offers an exquisite mix of dishes that are sure to satisfy those with a penchant for bold flavors. Just be mindful of the spice levels if your taste buds lean towards the milder side.

Most of the places around this area don't have a fancy 'fine dining' look to it. You get this here except without the fine dining price. The place is well decorated with nice red curtains. Definitely a date worthy place. It wasn't too crowded during the evening either. I wasn't hungry for a big meal, so I ordered appetizers. They have a dim sum menu that's available for the evening too. I ordered shrimp dumplings and crab Rangoon. Both were really great quality. My friend ordered their sesame chicken and it was a lot of food. Something else I wanted to mention was that they added lemon to their water. I know it's just water but it made a world of a difference. It was sooo zesty. Wish all restaurants could just do that. Good spot overall. Be sure to check in with the yelp app  so you can score free pork dumplings. I don't eat pork but my friend was sure happy to get them.

First meal in NYC and first meal. I had The Duke (bison burger) that had caramelized onions, garlic aioli and mushrooms. And of course, with a fried egg. Great burger but think it just needed a bit of acid to put it over the top. Side of rings and fries and a Moscow mule Monday special drink ($3?!?) We also had a vegan shake which was awesome. Fantastic coconut flavor and reminded me of the coconut bar/squares that you get at dim sum.

We had an wonderful experience at The Smith! The hostess, the waiter, and the bus boys( sorry don't know the correct term for them these days) were all courteous and professional.We ordered the baked eggs  which was really good. Love the spinach in it. The side of home fries are spicy , so keep that in mind.  The service was fast. Great experience and will  come back again!

This was my second time eating at John's. We were here during a very difficult time, the coronavirus outbreak. The restaurant staff was doing a great job of seating people away from each other.Despite the unusual circumstances, our waiter was in great spirits and provided great service. Our pizza was absolutely amazing. Thin crispy crust with just the right amount of toppings. Our only complaint is that our salad didn't taste very fresh, but I have to wonder if that was because the volume of customers was WAY lower than normal so food wasn't moving very fast. The pizzas are made to order, so that was perfect. Anytime you are staying in the Times Square area, you must try John's. The day before, we ate at the "best pizza place in Brooklyn", and we all agreed the John's was better!!

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Highly Anticipated Dinner

After much anticipation and a tough reservation to secure, my experience at the restaurant was a mixed bag, meriting a 3.5-star rating. While the BBQ Calamari lived up to expectations with its tender texture and flavorful rice pairing, the Sopressini & Smoked Mussels initially stumbled with an overpowering saltiness, saved only by the kitchen's willingness to promptly redo the dish.

The Lasagna, a pricier choice at $64, left me questioning its value, particularly given the scant meat and excess of cheese between its delicate pasta sheets. Accompanying focaccia bread sticks unfortunately did little to redeem the dish, presenting an overwhelming oiliness instead of the expected fresh, crispy exterior.

A delightful surprise came in the form of the Japanese Sweet Potatoes — sumac-coated morsels of mochi-like texture wrapping a sweet, fluffy interior. However, the Nonna's Little Nip cocktail fell flat, with a lack of complexity and a desire for a stronger alcohol presence.

Regrettably, inconsistencies surfaced, like the unavailable chrysanthemum salad that later appeared at a neighboring table. Despite leaving no room for dessert, I noted missed opportunities to try tempting options such as Stuffed Garlic Bread and a special dumpling dish.

In conclusion, while some dishes showed promise, there's ample room for improvement. I'm hopeful for a potential return visit with a larger party to explore more of the menu, perhaps then the restaurant will fully live up to the hype.

Words cannot describe how excited I was when this opened in the neighborhood. Anyone familiar the area knows food options are limited!I ordered the pork gyoza and spicy miso ramen to go. The gyoza was enormous and honestly can be a meal itself; it was delicious but a bit on the oily side. The spicy miso ramen was delicious packed with beef and all sorts of veggies. The miso ramen has the option of spicy vs regular. Menu has a large variety from appetizers and ramen to yaki noodles, rice and bento boxes. They also offer pre-made sushi. Unfortunately, they don't offer lunch specials. Hopefully this is something they're willing to explore. With the hospital nearby, it'd definitely bring in more traffic during lunch hours. The place itself is very small but it is located in the upper east side so realty is limited. 100% returning and trying out the entire menu.

I had a disappointing experience at El Toro while using Meal Pal. The quesadilla I ordered was noticeably lacking in filling, and the beef inside had an odd taste. Furthermore, the guacamole struck me as prepackaged, and the lettuce was unpleasantly browned. Although there are positive reviews out there, it's unclear if the restaurant is compromising on quality for Meal Pal customers. Based on this visit, I'm not inclined to give El Toro another try.

Upon my recent visit to this cozy eatery, I was initially disappointed to discover their lack of a full bar. However, their extensive wine selection offered some solace. I had my mind set on the salmon for a healthier dining option, but fate would have it that the kitchen had run out. Settling instead for the braised short ribs, I was pleasantly surprised when the salmon mysteriously reappeared alongside my dish. Nonetheless, I kept to my second choice and was delighted by the rich sauce that accompanied the ribs. Although the meat was somewhat dry on its own, the sauce transformed it, adding a succulent layer of flavor that also enhanced the accompanying spinach. A garnish of pickled carrots provided a refreshing, tangy contrast to the dish.

The staff's service was the highlight of the evening—attentive, prompt, and cordial, they created an environment where my companion and I could indulge in extended conversation without feeling pressured to vacate our table amidst the bustling atmosphere.

Dessert was offered, with apple pie and a crumble tempting our sweet tooth, yet we abstained, perhaps to be explored on a future occasion. All in all, the dining experience was a satisfying one, and I would recommend this restaurant to those seeking a hearty meal in a welcoming setting.

So I came here for restaurant week. Now I would give just the mean (we had the beef and pork ribs) 5 stars. The meat was super tender and the portion sizes were very generous. But the reason I give it 3 stars For two reasons. First on the food end, i thought the spices were too mild. This place is suppose to be korean food but the flavors were more "Americanized Asian cuisine".  Also the AC was not on and it was about 90 degrees outside. It was really hot and humid despite the fans everywhere. It was hard to sit there and we didn't even have the bbq! If we did I can't imagine sitting and how hot it would have been!

Pretty good noodle place. Ordered the stamina which had whole pieces of garlic in it and some fried chicken. There was a decent amount of chicken, not a lot, but they didn't skimp out. It wasn't super flavorful, but it wasn't bland either. It was very tender. The garlic was actually a nice touch and tasty, but wouldn't recommend if you are going on a date. The udon was cooked to perfection. Pillowy and yummy. The broth wasn't too salty, but pretty flavorful. But there was nothing else in the dish. No vegetables, no garnish or anything else. My friend got a cold soba dish. She seemed to enjoy it a lot. At the end, they gave her hot water to drink a soup afterwards, but it was just hot water and it was kind of weird. But a nice touch? I'm not sure. Definitely doesn't make it a lose a star, just a bit weird. Service was very much on point. Water was always refilled and everyone was very friendly. Overall, the food here is slightly above average, but at the prices they are charging, I feel like there needs to be more in the dishes, whether it be garnish, vegetables, or more meat. This was something I could have easily put together in 10 minutes at home, for $3.

Quick lunch bite around the Midtown East area. SPICY PAITAN with Chicken or Pork Char Siew: Pretty solid ramen with a chicken broth based with spicy sesame oil. The broth was not super spicy or salty but yet still pretty creamy, which really hit the spot for me. The noodles were perfectly cooked with just a bite to it, just the way I like it. I opted for the chicken char siew, which was very moist.All in all, a solid ramen spot. This location accepts credit cards (except Amex) and cash.

Title: A Satisfying Budget-Friendly Bite in Midtown

Located in the bustling heart of midtown, this eatery presents a surprisingly affordable option for those craving a hearty meal. My friends and I were pleasantly satiated by the kebab/salad/rice combo; the flavors were on point, generous in portion, and definitely hit the spot.

The ordering process is straightforward – queue at the counter, order, pay, and collect your food. A bonus is the variety of sauces available in the fridge – a perfect complement to the already flavorful dishes. Once you're done, there's a no-fuss clean-up system where you clear your own gigantic plates to a designated area.

A word of caution: eating kebabs off the sharp metal skewers can be a tricky affair, so watch your fingers! We also had a slightly odd encounter with the cashier who seemed disengaged, leaving us feeling a tad neglected during a question.

But the cherry on top? Free milk tea to wash down the meal. Despite the minor hiccups, it's a spot worth checking out for a quick, satisfying, and wallet-friendly meal.

I recently had the pleasure of experiencing a dinner hosted by my company at a Brazilian Steakhouse, a venue that provided us with a private room complete with a host and attentive staff. For those unfamiliar with this style of dining, it can be quite the sensory overload, but delightfully so in terms of the side dishes and accompaniments, which were nothing short of exceptional. The variety was impressive, ensuring there's something on offer for every palate.

The main draw, however, the parade of meats, was where the experience became a tad intense. As servers circulate with skewers of various meats, diners are asked on the spot if they'd like to try a slice. This rapid-fire decision-making can be daunting and, admittedly, a little nerve-racking for the uninitiated. The pressure to quickly say yes or no meant I opted out of trying several selections.

Despite this, the ambiance of the restaurant was inviting and the overall dining experience was positive. If you're someone who thrives on making quick decisions and enjoys a carnivorous adventure, then this is a setting you'd likely relish. For those who prefer a more leisurely dining experience, the pace of service might prove to be a slight challenge.

Really 3.5 Stars, but rounding up for nostalgia.  It's probably been over 20 years since I've been to a Tad's Steaks.  But when I heard it was closing (on Sunday 1/5/20), I just had to go!The menu ranges from Steaks to pork chops to seafood.  No matter what you order, it will be flame broiled to your preference and served with a potato (baked or mashed), grilled cheese bread and a simple salad (want tomatoes on your salad?  It'll cost ya an extra $1.49).  Prices are pretty low, depending on what you order but with these low prices, comes lower quality of meats.  Still, really not so bad for what it is: cheap eats; cafeteria style.  Warning:  word is out that Tad's will be closing - so expect long lines of people waiting for their last taste of Tad's Steaks. Thanks for the nostalgia!

So happy to see them open an East Village location after visiting the Flushing restaurant. The noodle is where it's at! One of my favorite beef noodle soups, with lots of noodle options. Feeling chewy?? Get the thick. Feelin slurpy?? Get the thin. The choice is yours in addition I've tried their eggplant salad, and shredded potato salad. Both were great, but I recommend adding chili oil to the potato. Portions are smaller at this location so be wary!

I recently went to Gabriel Kreuther for a special occasion.  The restaurant is large, high ceilings, but still feels intimate.  Service is great, and the ambiance of the restaurant is very romantic -- there were a ton of couples dining there.We opted for a prix fixe tasting menu due to our dietary restrictions / not being super hungry, as well as a caviar starter.  There is also a longer form Heritage menu that would have been great had we been more hungry.  The caviar was great and came with a crispy rice cracker I loved this pairing.We had a really heavy fish menu, which I liked.  There were different variations of fish, including crudo and cooked.  I thought each dish was very well-prepared and fresh.  The cooked fish dishes were very nicely prepared, not dry at all.I had a great meal at Gabriel Kreuther and would certainly return.  It is definitely worth going to for a special occasion.  For a more economic option, lunch is more reasonable, somewhat.

Title: A Slurp-worthy Stop at Nakamura

Looking for a quick meal, I stumbled upon Nakamura, a cozy Japanese ramen spot with just 18 seats, which explained the half-an-hour wait. The limited menu didn't disappoint, as their Yuzu Wings were a crispy delight, perfectly halved and infused with a zesty yuzu kick. Paired with a reasonably priced can of Orion Beer for $6, the meal was off to a good start.

The standout, however, was the Tontoro Ramen with its rich pork broth and chewy noodles, a classic done right. For the adventurous palate, the Truffle Miso Ramen packed a punch with its luxurious flavor. Other notable options included the Yuzu Dashi and Torigara, each bringing their own unique twist to the table.

The service? As heartwarming as the broth—attentive and friendly. Nakamura has etched a spot on my go-to list, and next time, I'll be sure to reserve a spot online to bypass the wait.

FOOD: Amazing flavor that is different from the typical spicy Sczheuan fare that dominates the American Chinese restaurant scene. Hand pulled noodles, spicy cumin lamb,  chrysanthemum tea are examples of more unique fare that can be found there that is full of great flavor.SERVICE: Order at the counter and eat if you can find a seat- hard to find at rush hours!EXPERIENCE: most of these locations look similar, it's a simple fast casual dining that does the trick.VALUE: noodles for $10 and spicy lamb burgers for $6. Definitely can be full after one of these for great value.SUMMARY: great Chinese cuisine that is a departure from the norm. An amazing idea from a fellow WashU alum, have been back many times and never disappointed!

I like this place! Authentic Taiwanese street food and dessert that take you back to the old days.Interior - the vibe here is like those shops on the street that have been there for decades. Like family business kinda vibe, so don't expect anything fancy. The place is pretty spacious but you might need to share tables with strangers.Service - good service! Mandarin mainly. They are fast with their food. Nothing to complain hereTaste - the dessert was bomb!! Taro balls were chewy and dense. It was the perfect combo with green beans, grass jelly and shaved ice. I can only imagine how good this would taste during a hot summer day. The popcorn chicken was alright, not as good as I expected for it was overly salty. I'm giving this place a five because I do see myself coming back for the desserts!!

Delicious and affordable meals in a comfortable atmosphere. I highly recommend the Omusoba; I had gotten the original yakisoba (stir-fried udon noodles) before, but the omusoba steps it up by wrapping it in an omelette and topping it with delicious sauces! It also came in a huge portion size so I took half of it home for later. The menu includes tons of ramen and other noodle/rice dishes for about $10-14, which is such a steal in NYC. There are a few great appetizers and drinks as well (I like the takoyaki).

Title: A Surprising Catch in Murray Hill: Cousins Maine Lobster

Finding a standout restaurant in Murray Hill can often seem like a fool's errand, but my recent visit to Cousins Maine Lobster before a movie night might just change the tide. With a somewhat indifferent attitude towards lobster, partly thanks to a less than stellar experience in Boston, I stepped into the spacious and notably vacant Cousins Maine Lobster at 6 PM on a Friday.

The eatery gives a subtle nod to nautical themes without going overboard, and while they flaunt their Food Network-affirmed reputation on the walls, I reserve judgment on what that truly signifies for quality.

The Connecticut Roll, at $17, was a pleasant revelation. Generously packed with large, succulent lobster chunks lightly kissed by lemon and butter, it defied my expectations. The accompanying pickle and coleslaw were somewhat forgettable, yet the roll itself left a lasting impression.

On the side, I opted for the modestly priced tater tots at $4. They arrived golden and crunchy, albeit in need of a dash of salt – a minor DIY adjustment. Next time, I'm eyeing the more adventurous lobster tots.

Beverage options are adequate with soft drinks, beer, and wine but no spirits – and for the home chef, take-home lobster meat and roll kits are an interesting proposition.

At $26.59 for a lobster roll, tater tots, and water, Cousins Maine Lobster is a reliable pick for a swift and savory meal. When in need of a pre-cinema dinner in Murray Hill, this will be my go-to spot. And for those with Murray Hill recommendations – I'm all ears!

The traditional tonkotsu, the chashu is very flavorful and soft it paired with the perfectly cooked noodles that had the right "chewy" consistency. The $25 braised beef rib was so tender the meat fell of the bone, they only serve 20 bowls a night so go early bc we showed up at 5:30 pm but by the time we left the place an hour later it was packed with a waiting line out the door on a Friday night. The tantan had curry spices but not too spicy. Next time i would love to go back to try the yakisoba that's cooked in front of your table or the peiking duck ramen. The appetizers of the Salisbury steak cooked your way on a sizzling platter was also tasty and i must admit the karaage is one of the best I've tasted so far (including places I've been in Japan) bc outside was lightly crunchy but not oily as you would expect from deep frying. They offer a sake taster but I love the refreshing Yamamomo mocktail made with calpico.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Saravana Bhavana

On a quest for South Indian cuisine during a sunny afternoon in the city, we found ourselves at Saravana Bhavana on Lexington Avenue, a street renowned for its Indian restaurant selection. Surprisingly, the restaurant was nearly deserted at lunchtime, which should have been our first clue.

We ordered an array of dishes, including masala dosa, Kerala paratta, and vada, in anticipation of the authentic flavors Saravana Bhavana is known for. Unfortunately, the meal failed to meet our expectations. Each dish lacked the zest and authenticity that define South Indian cuisine, leaving us wholly dissatisfied.

In summary, our experience at Saravana Bhavana was unfortunately dismal, both in ambiance and culinary delight. It's a reminder that popularity back home doesn't always translate to quality abroad.

Title: Happy Hour Hits, Food Misses at Oficina Latina

I dropped by Oficina Latina to check out their much-talked-about happy hour and wasn't disappointed by the drink deals. At $13 for a two-for-one special, the margaritas were a good value and did the trick, though they didn't particularly stand out in the flavor department.

On the food front, I tried the Domino Arepas, hoping for a delightful bite as a self-professed Mexican food enthusiast. Unfortunately, they fell short of expectations; the arepas were unusually pale and thick, missing that punch of flavor I crave. The toppings provided a saving grace, adding some much-needed taste to the dish.

While Oficina Latina is not at the top of my list for a dedicated food outing, it's a viable spot for a casual pre-game session if you happen to be in the neighborhood.
