I recently satisfied my breakfast-for-dinner cravings at this spot, ordering through UberEats. The delivery was prompt, arriving within the standard 30 minutes. The sausage and cheese omelette was the star of my meal — truly scrumptious. The hashbrowns were also a delight, perfectly crispy. Although the biscuit didn't quite agree with me, it was a small component of what was generally a tasty and convenient dining experience.

Title: Underwhelmed and Overcharged

My anticipation for an enjoyable dining experience at this establishment was met with letdown. Rating it a 2 out of 5 might even seem generous, given my disappointment. Upon arrival for our 6pm reservation on a Sunday, we were made to wait despite being punctual. Greeted eventually by a wobbly table which seemed to escape the staff's notice, the evening started on an uneven footing.

Service was slow: a notable gap between the arrival of wine glasses and the wine itself set a sluggish tone. The broiled oysters, at a steep $5.50 each, arrived in a timely fashion, but they were followed by a 20-minute wait for lackluster pasta dishes. Both the angel hair with its sparse clams and the ordinary lasagnettes with ragu failed to justify their $25 price tag.

Our hanger steak, arriving half an hour later, was cooked to perfection but lacked seasoning, as did the accompanying shmaltz potatoes. For a chef with an impressive resume, the offerings fell short. The price point did not match the quality of food or service experienced, culminating in an evening of pronounced disappointment.

Came here with my family after church on Easter Sunday. The atmosphere and decor are incredible! Really loved the signs on the bathrooms! So cute! IT WAS SO COLD IN HERE!!!! That's one of my big complaints. SO cold. Uncomfortably cold. I was wearing my boyfriends big puffy coat the entire meal. My one other complaint before I get into the good stuff would have to be that I asked for lemon for my water 3 times (asked two different waiters too) and never got them. It's fine, not a big deal, but when someone says "YES OF COURSE!" to a request, I figured I'd be getting what I asked for lol. The food; INCREDIBLE! I'm so glad my family and I finally tried this place and now have a place to go for when we want an Armenian meal (but don't want to make it ourselves!) :) We ordered a lot so get ready; Upon sitting down we were given two baskets of pita bread and a sesame, oil, lemony dip that we all loved. I'm not sure what it was called but it was so tasty! And not too filling. Armenian Salad: so good. No complaints at all. Very flavorful and fresh. Mouhammara: It's advertised as spicy but I tried it (and I'm very sensitive to spicy things,) and did not find it too bad at all! To quote my sister who put this dish pretty perfectly- "it tastes like a spicy brownie." Soujuk: very cute!!! So tiny!! Didn't eat this because I don't like soujuk but my entire family raved about it. The quail egg on top threw my mom over the edge. She was trying to figure out where she can buy them so she can try and make this exact same at home. Cheese bereg: we ordered this assuming it was going to be the cheese triangles we make at home with the philo dough. It wasn't- they were more shaped like Perogi's and were crispy and doughy- kind of like a bigger mozzarella stick. Very tasty!!! But not what we wanted - we didn't realize until after but we should have gotten the Subereg which is listed right underneath it on the hot appetizer section. Either way this was fantastic though. Mantee tradition with Meat: my mom had us order these because she had read about them and we all had never had them and they were EXCELLENT! The perfect size to share with a table of 6 people. Very tasty. As far as the entrees go everyone really enjoyed their meal. In my photos you can see what we all ordered. I tried a little bit of everyone's (we all passed around our forks and shared little bites) and everyone's was incredible. I personally shared the chicken and jingle bell peppers with my boyfriend which were both phenomenal. I had leftovers of the chicken for lunch the next day and it was still just as tasty then! Will definitely be coming back here. Although I hope it's a little warmer inside next time!

A solid choice for Japanese izakaya food in the midtown area. Some dishes are definitely better than others but by far my favorite dish here is the soki soba that they serve as a lunch special on a sporadic basis. Soki soba is an Okinawan noodle dish that is difficult to find even in Japan outside of Okinawa. Sometimes I come here specifically to eat this dish!

Title: A Flavor Fusion Fiesta at a Charming Seafood Szechuan Spot!

My recent discovery of a restaurant that marries seafood boil with Szechuan cuisine ticked all the boxes on my culinary love list. But what stole my heart (and taste buds) was an unexpected treasure that surpassed this already magnificent duo.

Ambiance: Upon entering, I was greeted by a bright and inviting space, peppered with adorable decor that promised a cheerful dining experience.

Service: The staff were on their game—attentive, prompt, and considerate, enhancing our meal without hovering.

Value: The prices will have you rubbing your eyes in disbelief, especially given the generous portions of seafood and other dishes on offer.

The Feast: We indulged in the special combo, which boasted a bounty of succulent snow crab legs in their seafood boil—no scrimping here, with a side note of abundant, juicy shrimp too. The ghost street sauce that accompanied the boil was a flavor bomb, hitting the sweet spot between zesty and manageable spice, even for the timid palates.

Appetizers were a treat, with chicken wings so tender they're a must-try, and calamari that did not disappoint. However, the cauliflower with pork belly was a standout for the veggies, offering rich, savory satisfaction that has me already plotting to try the green bean dish next time around.

The Crown Jewel: Let me introduce you to what might have been one of the top 5 bites in NYC—SALTED EGG DUNGENESS CRAB. A dish so good it's borderline spiritual, with me, post-feast, fervently scavenging for every last bit of salted egg and scallion from the crab shell.

Cleanliness: For those who value a spotless restroom, you're in luck—a well-maintained bathroom awaits.

Final Verdict: This place is a knockout, especially if you're a fan or future fan of salted egg yolk. Make a beeline for the salted egg yolk dungeness crab and prepare for a life-affirmingly delicious experience. It's a solid 10/10, and yes, I will be back—no question about it.

I was in the Bryant Park area and I met with some friends at L'Adresse.This place has a very nice ambience, and the service was fantastic. We came on a busy Saturday night before Christmas, but although full we were able to be seated at the bar/kitchen area. This was prefect as the three of us had plenty of room.The food quality was very good. I had the burger and it was great. The other dishes we tried were excellent also  If you find yourself in the Bryant Park area I highly recommend trying L'addresse for elevated bistro dining.

I recently dined at this local gem that Yelp categorizes as a Mediterranean restaurant, but it's more specifically a delightful Israeli spot. The hummus and tahini were absolutely top-notch, perfectly creamy and well-seasoned. I also indulged in one of their dinner bowls, a hearty and delicious stew that was fragrantly spiced and deeply satisfying. The bread served alongside was fresh and great for dipping. Based on this experience, I'm already planning my next visit! Highly recommended for anyone looking for authentic and tasty Israeli cuisine.

I recently dined at The Sea Fire Grill in Manhattan and was blown away by their Restaurant Week offerings, especially the Blackened Montauk Swordfish. The perfectly seasoned swordfish was complemented by fresh garden vegetables and a delightful eggplant caponata, creating a symphony of flavors. If you're a fan of seafood, this is a must-visit spot. The Sea Fire Grill truly delivered a memorable meal worth recommending.

Title: Quick, Fresh, and Satisfying Late-Night Bite at KazuNori

After an evening at the 'Mean Girls' show, my friends and I ventured to KazuNori for a quick meal and it didn't disappoint, even at 10 pm, there was a buzz with a line outside. Thankfully, the line moved swiftly and we were seated within 20 minutes. 

The handrolls, prepared right before your eyes, were fresh and delicious. The simplicity of the flavors truly shone through. I opted for the 5 roll set featuring an enticing mix of crab, lobster, toro, yellowtail, and scallop, though there was a slight hiccup as my order was mixed up and the sequence of the rolls was not as planned. Despite this, the option to order à la carte is a plus for those who prefer a more tailored experience.

A noteworthy detail is that the tip is included in the prices, which simplifies the payment process and allows for a more relaxed dining experience. All in all, KazuNori delivered a quick, satisfying experience perfect for post-show dining.

Title: A Modern Twist on Korean Favorites - A Must-Visit!

From the moment I stepped into this gem of a restaurant, I knew I was in for a treat. It's a modern take on Korean cuisine that absolutely nails the balance between traditional flavors and contemporary presentation.

The standout delight of my visit were the soju flights—a creative and delicious way to sample a variety of flavors. As for the food, the chicken wings were a highlight, boasting a perfect crispy exterior complemented by mouthwatering seasoning. Equally impressive was the chicken fondue, which proved to be a sublime concoction with excellently cooked chicken paired with a fondue that was portioned just right for the dish.

Let's not forget about the pork buns—simply put, they were a revelation. Calling them the perfect bun does not do them justice; they must be experienced.

Every dish I sampled was exceptional, and the attentive, accommodating staff only enhanced the dining experience. There's no question in my mind that I'll be returning for another round of these delectable offerings. This restaurant is unequivocally a must-visit for any food enthusiast looking for a fresh take on Korean cuisine.

I went for a Tribute Society event on a Friday night and it was such a nice time. The event was held in the basement and it was so nicely decorated. The vibes were great and the event was so nicely put together. I had a series of margaritas and they were all the right amount of strong and savory! The bouncer told us the first floor was a good time as well, I will make sure to come back to check it out

While the Upper West Side never hot it's legs as a dining destination minus the newly closed Leonti-  Asset brings some downtown flair uptown.A long bar and some nice touches.Ate:Gratis cheesy focaccia Simply grilled branzino & asparagus $32Ny friend had the chicken The focaccia was a nice surprise in an age of buy your bread. The branzino & chicken while good were no culinary groundbreakers, but if you're looking for a solid spot no suprises, uptown Asset satisfies.

I had a very pleasant dish at North Fork. The food is  good. There is an abundance of seafood options but some good meat options as well. Dishes you may have seen before but with some added flair that makes them their own. I visited with my GF on a Thursday evening. There was lots of warm candlelight and it wasnt too packed, it was perfect for date night. We started off with the elk tartare and the prawns. The prawns were really delicious. They had a nice sear and were well seasoned. The elk tartare was nice. It wasnt too gamey and there were some key limes that gave a nice pop of citrus. Its a rich dish and the portion was a bit too big for me. Its definitely a dish for 2. For an entree I had the sea bass. Everything was cooked perfectly. It was was enjoyable and the carrots were spectacular. Personally I wish the dish had a little more acid. The drink menu was very grown up. Cocktails weren't very sweet and mostly spirit forward. The staff was very friendly and we even got to meet the executive chef Brian who was also friendly and quite talented.

Title: A Culinary Journey Worth Repeating

I can't shake off the memory of their cheeseburger dumplings, a genius creation that lured me from the tranquility of Long Island to the bustling city streets not once, but thrice. The Emmy dumpling collaboration was a July special that left my taste buds in mourning once it concluded. The open kitchen, where the magic happens right before your eyes, only amplifies the culinary spectacle. Although the special is no more, my appetite is whetted, and the rest of the menu beckons for future gastronomic adventures. This place is a must-visit for any dumpling aficionado.

TLDR: High-end Greek eatery off of 5th Avenue. Stick with the course/set menus for the best value. Solid lunch offering for a business meal or just because.For a restaurant that has been around for so long, I only recently got to try Kellari. Had a business lunch and decided last minute to try Kellari. The restaurant is very spacious inside, I thought the seating was quite comfortable. Hostess was a bit cold, maybe it was an off day but felt very unwelcoming. Given the location, the restaurant is filled with a lot of the banking/corporate crowd.We opted for the Mousaka Croquettes to share and both got the three-course menu for $32.95.The croquettes I really enjoyed, it tasted exactly what you'd expect - crispy balls stuffed with all the ingredients of mousaka. It wasn't something you'd see often so I did like it.For the starters, we did the Crispy Basil Salmon and Country Pie. The Crispy Basil Salmon is almost like a spring roll, flash-fried with a meaty salmon filling. Served with a ponzu/lemon sauce with tarama, it's a Greek spread made of fish roe. I liked this, the best way I could describe this dish was it was like a refined version of the Fresh Salmon Rolls from The Cheesecake Factory. A light crispy wrapper with just tender salmon when you bite into it. It can get a bit messy when you eat this so make sure you mind your tie or blouse. The other was the Country Pie. This was their version of a Spanokopita, a Greek spinach/feta puff pastry. They served it with a dill sauce which was tasty. It wasn't as crispy flaky as I prefer but was still good.For entrees, I did the Psari Imeras (Fish of the Day) and we also got the Kotopoulo which is one of their signature dishes. The fish was a sautéed cod with red onion, tomato, small vegetables. My written description sounds bad but I thoroughly enjoyed this. The fish was flaky, the lemon gave it that acidity, the onions didn't overpower everything. All in all, a really great entree. The chicken was a weird one for me. The flavor was there but it was so dry. Like SO dry. I tried a bite of my companion's and all it reminded me of was Thanksgiving. That dry poultry just sitting there as you chew away. The feta/oregano fries were decent. Maybe this is usually really good but I was not feeling this.For dessert, we went with the Yogurt Cake and Baklava. The Yogurt Cake was their version of a cheesecake. It had a similar texture but not as thick, not too sweet.. the berry puree went well with it. The baklava was good, lots of nutty filling but a bit sweet for my taste. Then again though, it is baklava.In short though - I liked Kellari. Price range reminded me of Ammos/Avra, etc. The service I didn't think was terrible, it's standard Midtown staffing IMO. My server was to the point, professional, not particularly chatty but I wasn't looking to talk to him anyway. Things moved a bit slow, especially when we asked for the dessert and more so waiting for the check. I'd like to try it for dinner one day but for lunch, it's a great deal in this area. If I worked around here still - I'd probably eat here quite often. I'd like to check it out for dinner one of these days.

During my recent visit to the restaurant, I had the opportunity to sample their Joe's Signature Rice Roll, a hefty portion that deviates from your typical shrimp-filled dim sum fare. This version was generously packed with an array of ingredients including beef, pork, dried shrimp, egg, and bean sprouts, making for a substantial dish. However, while promising in concept, the roll fell somewhat short in flavor, lacking the complexity one might hope for in such a mix. The provided soy sauce alone was insufficient to elevate the taste, which I found to be on the bland side. Priced slightly above the $10 mark, this dish seems to be in its experimental phase. I am hopeful that with some adjustments, it will reach its full potential.

During our recent visit, we opted for a light fare and settled on the guacamole and chips. It was a delightful choice, with the guacamole presenting a burst of freshness that was both satisfying and ample enough to share among three. The accompanying chips added a lovely, crunchy texture that complemented the dip perfectly. As for the beverages, they were enjoyable albeit we noted that prices outside of happy hour were on the higher side. Overall, a pleasant experience but one to time wisely if looking for drink specials.

The original chef left for four seasons and I can find very little information out there about the new chef Andy Keith. After a meal here it's quite clear that this guy knows how to cook. Monkfish was cooked exactly right and the texture of mostly everything is perfect. At the same time he is really pushing the boundaries in terms of flavors. Everything is spicy and the flavors are heavy to the point of being overwhelming and confusing, especially for seafood. There are other missteps. One of the four gulf shrimps I got was missing its head so the kitchen hid it right underneath the other three. The black kale is fried with stem on and the stem tastes like twig upon chewing. And definitely steer away from the uni toast... both desserts (chocolate pudding and olive oil cake) had great flavors but the temperature and texture are just slightly off. The drink menu is good as always but I was served the wrong drink (got GLOW but received Heima) and also I miss the chenin blancs. My biggest complaint is during restaurant week the restaurant is completely incapable of handling crowds and rushes. I was seated half hour past my reservation time and many tables in the restaurant were waiting short of an hour between courses. The staff is very well trained so I assume everything would have been fine if they simply didn't overbook. Overall disappointing.

So many people told my group and I that we needed to go to Momofuku on our trip to NYC, and it totally lived up to our expectations! We were a little skeptical when we got there and discovered that it was in a mall, but once inside it blew us away!We were seated within 10 minutes on a Wednesday night without reservations. Our service was good! We ordered a bunch of different dishes to share and loved all of them!  My favorites were the pork belly bao and the spicy rice cakes. The pork belly was cooked perfectly, and the rice cakes were the perfect texture and the sauce was so good. We also ordered the seared scallop tataki, fried potatoes (amazing sauce with these!), baby green salad, spicy beef ramen and pork ramen. Momofuku is classy and delicious, and I would 10/10 go back on my next visit to New York!

Finally visited Cafe Buon Gusto @cafebuongusto after watching millions of insta posts, on my Birthday and this couldn't be a better occasion to have an amazing meal here! They got a delicious tiramisu at the end and sang the birthday song for me. Excellent hospitality and such friendly staff! The food is by far the best in Manhattan! I have been to a dozen of Italian restaurants and this is THE best (for the food and hospitality) I got their famous ala vodka sauce pasta- would suggest everyone try to this, as this sauce is their signature! I got mine with capellini pasta but you can get any pasta ranging from gnocchi to linguini. Oh and say yes when they ask you if you want some mozzarella cheese on your pasta, it's delectable. We also got the Linguini pasta with truffle oil sauce, this was not in their menu but my husband really wanted to try this one so they made it for him! . For appetizers we had the Burrata with cherry tomatoes. Finally, the tiramisu that was given complimentary for my birthday

I recently tried the Minced Chicken Noodles from a popular noodle spot, and my experience was somewhat underwhelming. While takeout can often rival dine-in quality, the noodles suffered from sogginess when eaten 30 minutes after pickup, indicating the packaging could be improved for better preservation of texture. Competing noodle joints have addressed this common issue with more thoughtful packaging that keeps ingredients separate, maintaining freshness and consistency from restaurant to home.

Taste-wise, the dish fell flat. The chicken, a leaner substitute for my preferred pork in dan dan noodles, lacked the depth and fat-infused juiciness I crave. Although the noodles were adequately sauced, they desperately needed an elevation in spice, garlic, and overall flavor to bring about the "WOW" factor synonymous with a great spicy, saucy noodle experience. Unfortunately, the dish was forgettable and simply average, failing to meet the high expectations set by the brand's reputation and widespread presence.

One word:  Mojitos!!!!Oh sooooooooo good!  Met up with a friend who moved out here, and his friends, and this place is great!  The mojitos are sooooooo good!  Oh, wait I already said that!  We also had the fricase de pollo....very good!  I wish I was hungrier or I would've ordered lunch.  We just needed drinks and a little snack.If you stop by, ask for Letti!  She was great!  Muchas gracias Floridita!  Hasta luego!

Title: A Pleasant Date Night with Good Vibes

My husband and I chose this spot for our date night, marking our second visit. We kicked things off with some well-crafted drinks – a refreshing Mojito for me and a flavorful Rum Runner for him. Appetizers were a delight with my choice of deviled eggs and his pan con tomate, both of which set the stage for the mains. My wings and potato wedges were satisfactory, but not standout, while my husband's steak and spinach hit the mark with its savory goodness.

The highlight of our evening, however, was the excellent selection of R&B music that created a relaxing and enjoyable ambiance. This spot proved to be a great choice for a chill Sunday evening out, offering a good vibe and decent fare that complimented our date night experience.

I recently dined at a delightful restaurant attached to our hotel, and I must say, it truly exceeded my expectations. The atmosphere was inviting with an awesome music selection that complemented the vibe. The service was top-notch – efficient and friendly, ensuring a great dining experience.

The menu offered an array of tantalizing options, and although we only tried their coffee from the breakfast selection, it was rich and perfectly brewed. I have my sights set on their breakfast offerings for tomorrow.

For dinner, I ordered a crispy chicken Caesar salad, and my boyfriend opted for the burger salad. Both were delicious and beyond satisfying, with generous portions that were well-seasoned and bursting with flavor. The onion rings deserve a special mention; they were colossal and absolutely delectable.

We caught a glimpse of the dessert menu, and it looked fantastic. I'm quite tempted to indulge in their sweet treats later on.

All in all, I can't recommend this place enough. If you're looking for great food with an equally great atmosphere and service, this is the spot to go to.

Title: A 24/7 Gem in the East Village – Veselka

Review:

Veselka stands out as an iconic establishment in the East Village, particularly for night owls with a penchant for breakfast at any hour - thanks to their 24/7 service. My recent visit was a culinary delight; from the expertly crafted sandwiches to the savory beef stroganoff, and the exceptional pierogis, each dish was a testament to the restaurant's commitment to traditional flavors. My girlfriend's choice, the beef stroganoff, deserves a special mention for being utterly sublime.

Another pleasant surprise was the quality of the cole slaw – a simple side that showcased their attention to detail. The bustling atmosphere late at night on a weekday added to the authenticity of the diner-esque experience, complemented by attentive service.

A piece of advice for future patrons: do not leave without trying the pierogis. They're a standout dish that epitomizes the delicious fare Veselka has to offer. A visit here is sure to satisfy, no matter the hour.

If you're in the mood for an unforgettable pork belly experience, then this restaurant is your go-to place. I devoured what could only be described as the best sizzling pork belly in town – crispy, perfectly spiced, and served sizzling hot, straight to the table. And for those who might be squeamish, fear not, as there's not a pig's ear, head, or snout in sight. Just pure, unadulterated pork belly bliss. Highly recommended for a tantalizing treat!

Title: A Mixed Bag at Chikarashi

I recently followed a coworker’s telepathic suggestion and ended up at Chikarashi for a poke fix. Opting for simplicity, I chose the large Goma Shoyu Tuna bowl at $20 and, regrettably, passed up the rare-find Dole Whip.

The bowl was aesthetically pleasing with generous seaweed salad, firm avocado, and somewhat chunky fried garlic that resembled chips more than a topping. Unfortunately, the rice was disappointingly gummy, casting a shadow over the otherwise well-composed dish. The tuna was fresh but scarce, and the miso soup was a welcome comfort on a dreary day.

While the meal didn't rocket Chikarashi to the top of my list, the lure of Dole Whip might just bring me back for another round.

Title: Authentic Flavor, Questionable Value at Dokodemo

As a takoyaki enthusiast, I was eager to try Dokodemo, especially after finding myself in the St Marks area. My experience on a surprisingly quiet Saturday afternoon was a mixed bag.

The takoyaki, while notably smaller than I anticipated, stood out in flavor compared to other New York City offerings. At nearly $10, the portion size left me desiring either a more palatable price of $5.99 or a generous serving of 10 balls instead of 8. A touch of bonito flakes could elevate the authenticity, enhancing the overall experience.

My cousin’s ramen rice order, although delectable, didn't quite live up to its advertised presentation, resulting in a slight disappointment. We also noticed the absence of the sukiyaki omelette, which seems to have been replaced by a burrito - a surprising swap on the menu.

In conclusion, while Dokodemo delivers on taste, the value proposition is less convincing. I'd return to satisfy a takoyaki craving but would likely explore other menu items seeking better value for my dollar.

Title: Modern Vibes, Decent Pho at [Restaurant Name]

My visit to [Restaurant Name] revealed a trendy spot that's cash-only, so remember to hit the nearby Chase ATM before you go. The chic interior is decked out with palm leaves and has an Instagram-worthy aesthetic that adds to the experience.

The ambiance is complemented by electric music and attracts a youthful but family-friendly clientele. However, those with allium allergies should beware: onion and garlic feature prominently in the dishes here.

Their menu includes a variety of pho options, with DIY toppings to personalize your bowl. I sampled the shrimp summer roll, which was fresh and enjoyable, while my partner went for the classic pho. While the dishes were good, I believe the broth lacked depth of flavor, unless you're willing to pay an extra $5 for an upgrade, which I feel shouldn't be necessary.

A nice touch is the crushed ice in the soda – a crowd-pleaser for sure. Overall, [Restaurant Name] left us satisfied, and though it's a cool spot for a group hangout, we prefer another local joint for a more authentic and casual pho experience. Cheers!

Title: Imli's Consistently Culinary Delight

Once again, my latest visit to Imli has cemented its place as a local favorite. This was my fourth visit in just a month, and they've outdone themselves yet again. We indulged in the aloo gobi, chole, and the tandoori chicken, each dish arriving cooked to order with a masterful command of spice. The gravies were a perfect pairing for the fluffy white rice, and the paratha was an essential addition for soaking up the irresistible sauces. Serving sizes were more than satisfactory, promising a delicious encore for lunch the next day.

The staff at Imli deserves a shoutout, with Rex and Anil, in particular, elevating the dining experience with their personable and attentive service, ensuring every visit feels like coming home. Imli truly is a gem that continues to shine brighter with each visit.

Title: A Cozy Hideaway for Students and Visitors

After a lengthy campus tour at Parson's, a student and I were in search of a comforting spot to unwind and stumbled upon this unassuming refuge. Our initial quest for bubble tea led us to a packed corner spot, but fortune favored us as we retreated to this café, which welcomed us with a cozy front window seat ideal for an overcast day's respite.

The café may present a spartan seating arrangement upon entry, but don't be misled—the upstairs area unfolds into a spacious haven that was pleasantly tranquil on a Wednesday afternoon. The vibe is perfectly conducive for studying or simply decompressing post-tour, perhaps due to the minimal patronage during our visit.

This establishment is akin to an upscale convenience store, complete with a multifaceted selection ranging from wholesome buffets and revitalizing smoothies to more substantial fare, the likes of which I couldn't fully explore in one sitting.

I opted for a refreshing kombucha, the student a delectable smoothie, as we both indulged in the quintessential city pastime of people-watching, all while processing our earlier educational excursion. The café's proximity to The New School facilities only adds to its allure for academic patrons.

In essence, this café is a hidden gem that I would have eagerly frequented during my college years. Its variety and ambience are commendable, offering a versatile retreat for both quiet study sessions and casual hangouts.

I recently had the delight of dining at Kura with my boyfriend for a 5:45 PM seating. Despite our slight tardiness, the warm staff welcomed us and swiftly seated us in front of the master chef, Chef Ishizuka himself. Honored to be in his presence, we embarked on an exquisite 16-course Omakase journey. 

To ensure an undistracted experience, I visited the restroom just before the meal began. Decisions started with the drink menu, where we were torn between two sakes. The attentive staff offered tastings of both, leading us to choose the stronger, less fruity option that perfectly complemented the meal.

The Omakase itself was a culinary symphony, with each piece meticulously prepared by Chef Ishizuka. The Otoro stood out in a parade of impeccable, fresh sushi, each bite a testament to his skill. The additional 3-4 appetizer dishes assured that we were more than satisfied.

The entire experience was, without a doubt, a splurge at $200 per person, including tip, tax, and drinks. Still, for a first Omakase in New York, Kura left an indelible mark. I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit to this exceptional establishment and cannot recommend it enough to others seeking a memorable dining experience.

Your average local NYC Irish bar. Relatively cheap drinks and happy hour which is what I like! Never too crowded, service and food are both decent. They have TVs at the bar and the booths at the front offer a view of them. Music is usually a fun recognizable mix. I come by often to ~gossip~ with friends when we need a central location to hang out that's not touristy.

Title: An Unexpected Gem on Cornelia Street

My dining experience in the West Village took an unexpectedly delightful turn when we stumbled upon a quaint Italian restaurant on the now popular Cornelia Street. Despite it being our plan B, the place exuded charm from the moment we entered around 6pm without reservations and were promptly seated by the door. Though slightly breezy, the atmosphere remained cozy.

Our server was knowledgeable and attentive, recommending a bottle of sangiovese. Priced at a reasonable $63, it perfectly complemented our pappardelle pasta dishes. A standout appetizer was the calamari—astonishingly light and crispy, with a just-right batter that clung to the tender seafood and the surprise addition of lemon within, elevating the entire dish.

I wrapped up the meal with an espresso martini that was nothing short of heavenly. The restaurant's interior, with its adorable charm, presents an ideal backdrop for date night. I walked away a convert, grateful for this serendipitous find.

**Review of a Nostalgic Pizza Brunch**

My birthday weekend took a delightful turn with a surprise pizza brunch organized by my husband at this gem of a restaurant which felt like a step back into the Bronx of our childhood. The ambiance was a nostalgic homage to the classic NYC borough bodegas - from the familiar items on sale to the classic pricing, it was like revisiting an old friend.

The staff managed to accommodate our group with a large communal table and provided attentive service, even as our server multitasked as the bartender. The personal-sized pizzas were a hit, perfect for sharing amongst friends. Favorites included the Spicy, Margherita, Breakfast, and Tres Golpe pizzas, while the sight of a bodega sandwich being made added to the authentic vibe.

The highlight was a Nutella pizza topped with bananas and strawberries in honor of my birthday. Absolutely fantastic and made with love. This place nails the New York corner bodega experience and delivers on delightful flavors. Highly recommended for a taste of nostalgia and a great bite. Deadass.

I'm a big fan of this place. Does tend to get very loud as it's a popular place for midtown happy hours after work. The food is delicious and the space is quite unique. It has a nice rustic speakeasy vibe with tons of space!  The Ragtrader is the upstairs part which has a very large dining space with a long bar for drinks. Bo Peep is the downstairs part (basement) which is an awesome speakeasy-like cocktail bar with live music after 7pm on weekdays. Always an excellent service from both host at Ragtrader and down at Bo peep. We decided we wanted to move after happy hour and they accommodated us no problem. Food quality and portions were stellar, and drinks were beautiful, expertly crafted, and delicious. Amazing environment down in bo peep, both before and during the live music. One of my new favorite eclectic cocktail bars in NYC!

Title: Hits and Misses at a Celebratory Soba Night

My dining experience at this restaurant was a mix of anticipation and surprises, tinged with a bit of disappointment. Eager to try the much-acclaimed ikasumi uni ikura soba, my spirits dampened upon learning of its absence from the menu that evening, along with the equally tempting ice tempura dessert.

However, the goma soba—a recommendation from our attentive waitress—proved to be a delightful recovery. The sesame dressing was particularly noteworthy, adding a fragrant and savory element that won over half of my group, overshadowing their jar jar soba selections.

Though we faced a lengthy 2 1/2 hour wait as walk-ins, the staff eased the inconvenience with their friendly and earnest service. Our patience was ultimately rewarded with a shared yuzu cheesecake and matcha creme brûlée—both petite yet exquisitely satisfying, disappearing swiftly amidst our collective approval.

In summary, while the restaurant did falter with availability, they excelled in service and provided a memorable dish that partly made up for the initial letdowns.

Title: A Restaurant Week Gem at Bar Boulud

I took a friend's advice to visit Bar Boulud during Restaurant Week and it was a fantastic decision. As a connoisseur of fine dining on a budget, their Restaurant Week deal stood out with its generous offerings. Unlike the typical restricted options, Bar Boulud let us choose from the entire menu, with only the priciest dishes carrying a fair surcharge.

For a mere $42, I indulged in a perfectly seasoned steak tartare, which allayed any concerns over raw meat, followed by steak frites. While my steak missed the medium-well mark and leaned toward tough, the overall meal was a steal. The dessert, Gatěau Basque, shared amongst friends, was the highlight of the evening - simply amazing.

Adding to the experience was the service. Faced with a delay for our large group's reservation, the staff at Bar Boulud accommodated us without a fuss, bumping our 5 PM slot to 5:30 PM with grace. That level of service truly puts a fine point on an already delightful evening. Highly recommended!

Title: A Spirited Escape Above the City Bustle

My latest visit to this 9th-floor haven was exclusively for drinks, and it was nothing short of delightful—a solid 5/5. The standout was the "State Fair," a refreshing concoction where kumquats truly shined, ensuring my return. "Teton" provided a lovely pick-me-up, although the coconut note wasn't quite to my taste. The "Angel of Music," though aesthetically pleasing, was disappointingly just a sweetened rosé in disguise. 

Service was commendable, and if you're a night owl, remember that while this spot closes at midnight on Saturdays, the 10th-floor sister bar keeps the night going a bit longer.

Reflecting on a summertime dinner, that experience lands at a 4.5/5. The sky-roofed, indoor garden setting was enchanting and perfect for social media snaps, even from our communal table, which felt quite private thanks to cleverly placed greenery and décor. The staff was amiable and on-the-ball, but the cuisine, despite being tasty, did not justify the steep prices.

Would I recommend this place? Absolutely—if you're looking to duck away from the Times Square frenzy into a charming urban retreat, this is your go-to.

10/10 best vegan sushi ever! I tried Beyond Sushi a year ago at Chelsea Market and fell in love. My dad and I shared their sweet tree, la fiesta and spicy mang rolls along with their coconut curry soup and fun-guy dumplings. Everything was incredible. The rolls were paired with delicious sauces, which made each bite an adventure! The spicy mang was easily my favorite. I just visited this location for lunch. I ordered the spicy mang (duh) and the mighty mushroom rolls. They were both absolutely delicious. I loved the umami flavor from the mushrooms and the sweet/spicy flavor from the spicy mang. Both are truly an experience. My friend and I then shared their Chef's Cookie for dessert. It was a skillet cookie filled with peanut butter and caramel and topped with black salt and lemon curd. It. Was. So. Good. Skillet cookies are one of my favorite desserts and this one did not disappoint. It was soft, warm and comforting. I would go back for the cookie alone! I ordered a green machine roll to take home and it was pretty tasty. I've never had almond pesto. Beyond Sushi, you have my heart and I can't wait to come back!

Loved it , my favorite... Im soo into Spaniard food that is not even funny.  Thus little market exceeded my expectation from the food to their sangria to the customer service to the way it setup. I mean what can go wrong even the music was so nice and the vibe was excellent . Yes  it can get a little crazy and packed but i mean you are  enjoying some good food and good ambience in one place and what better place that this new amazing mercadito ...

Title: A Brunch Worth Waiting For

If you're on the hunt for the ultimate brunch spot in the city, look no further. This place has it all: delectable food that will leave you craving more and an ambiance that perfectly encapsulates the spirit of a leisurely weekend morning. Be forewarned, though—the line can stretch long on the weekends, a testament to its popularity and the citywide love for this gem. It's clear once you dine here why everyone is willing to wait. Highly recommend for a brunch experience that truly stands out.

I am giving 4 stars but I've been for work team celebration drinks so I don't know how this place is with the regular service or prices. we had an area for ourselves. The place is incredibly beautiful, the "jungle"/ tropical decoration is super nice and every corner is really well designed. Even toilets were top noch! oMG never seen such a nice "temporary toilet" before. Seems like permanent structure.We had 3 appetizers for share: guacamole with crudités, kind of cheese quesadilla and small bites of tuna with crackers. Presentation of the three were oh so beautiful as well, same for the flavour; it was actually quite good overall... (except for cabagge frudite that was not fresh from my point of view...). Well, quesadillas were bit greasy!Lemonade was tasty and all cocktails were good and quite strong!Check the prices and it is not a cheap place but for the vibes i would pay a drink and sit there and chill.Downside is that it is all open air with few fans so it can actually get very hot... also... you need to eat your food quick otherwise huge flies will come over.. haha

Truly this spot never disappoints. I've eaten here often and it ties as my favorite Thai spot along with Land Thai. Came here with my aunt and sister who were in town visiting for the Lunar New Year. They loved the ambiance and enjoyed the decor. The bathrooms were clean and always stocked with enough of the necessary items and you can tell someone comes  in to clean regularly... something that's super important in busy restaurants but that can sometimes get neglected. I ordered the beef pad Thai. I know it's basic but you'll be surprised how many restaurants mess this up. Sometimes it's too dry, or too bland, or not enough bean sprouts... this one had the perfect texture  of noodles (chewy and satisfying) and the right amount of sauce (not too wet or too dry). My sister got the clay pot. One of my favorites! It had generous portions of scallop, fish, shrimp and all the different meats in there. My aunt got the chicken krapow, which was good but not as good as the otter two dishes. I wish it had more sauce. The green beans were really crisp, which I love. There's few things worse than limp and soggy green beans. 10/10 would recommend this spot and continue to eat here. Also would be a cute date night spot.

Title: Convenient Locale with Room for Culinary Improvement

I recently dined at a conveniently situated restaurant, ideal for the working crowd in the vicinity. Its allure intensifies in winter, offering a tranquil alternative to the bustling Del Fresco Grill. Come summer, the outdoor seating is a gem, providing a perfect vantage point to relish Rockefeller Center's vibrant atmosphere.

Service-wise, the staff was attentive and efficient. My dining experience here has spanned two visits; the first occasion saw me enjoying a fish dish, while on the latter, I opted for a sandwich. While the meals were satisfactory, they didn't particularly wow my palate — a sentiment perhaps remedied by further exploration of their offerings.

I tend to reserve this spot for client meetings rather than personal choice, which speaks volumes of its ambiance over its culinary prowess. During my recent visit, a shared appetizer, a couple of glasses of wine at my client's behest, two mains, a dessert, and coffee culminated in a bill of $154 before tax — a price point that warrants exceptional food, a benchmark that wasn't quite met. My journey with their menu isn't over, but as it stands, this restaurant remains a convenience choice rather than a culinary destination.

I recently dined at a restaurant where the experience was less than satisfactory. Upon early arrival for a reserved dinner, the hostess declined to seat me, citing "resetting the tables," despite the place being nearly empty. This seemed disingenuous, and I was unnecessarily relegated to the bar, only to be seated after my friend overcame traffic delays.

The service from the bartender who doubled as our waitress was amiable. However, the Spaghetti Carbonara, a touted specialty priced at $17, lacked flavor and proper seasoning, leaving much to be desired. The redeeming aspect of the meal was the Tiramisu, which proved to be the sole culinary delight of the evening.

Adding to the disappointment, an early and abrupt closure at 8:30 pm contradicted the 10:30 pm closing time advertised on Yelp, disrupting our dining experience while we were still enjoying our dessert. This disregard for guests' expectations was unfortunate and should be addressed for future patrons.

Title: A Filling Experience Falls Short of High Expectations 

Despite the summer heat, my cravings led me to this highly-recommended ramen spot, and I ventured in with expectations as lofty as the temperatures outside. Unfortunately, the restaurant didn't quite live up to the hype generated by its numerous Yelp reviews. 

On the bright side, the pricing was reasonable, particularly considering the portion sizes. The Mega Paitan ramen left us satisfyingly full, boasting a hearty assembly of char siu, pulled pork, and pork belly. My friend and I also shared a pulled char siu pork mayo don, which impressed with its smoky flavor—a result of being expertly torched right before serving.

However, not everything was perfect. The Mega Paitan leaned toward the saltier end of the spectrum, and the noodles, promised to be al dente, were disappointingly soft for my taste. 

In summary, while it may not be the best ramen joint out there, it's a decent option if you're in the area and looking for a filling meal.

I stopped by "Grill Cheese and More" for lunch and found it to be a solid choice for a quick bite, especially on a quiet Saturday afternoon. The place was tidy, including the single-occupant restroom, which is always a pleasant surprise. I tried the Classic Grilled Cheese and found it slightly on the dry side, although the cheese was generously melted and far from skimpy. The loaded tots were a highlight, well-portioned as a side dish and tasty—though I opted out of the jalapeños, which is down to personal taste. Service was decent, making the overall experience one to repeat if you’re in the area and craving a no-frills meal.

Yes yes yes yes! That's all I can say! Stuffed my face at this awesome establishment. It's initially daunting when you walk in because everything moves at such a quick place but I love that you go in, get your food, stuff your face and gtfo of there. My favorite taco was probably the Tacos al pastor. I found it to be the most flavorful as it has a nice balance of sweet, salt and savory. I am definitely coming back again to get my fill. 10/10!

On my first trip to New York 2 years ago, my boyfriend and I wanted to try Spot Dessert, but it was so crowded with long lines each time we came here, we ended up not trying this place out. When I came again to New York on my own, on my last evening in New York, I decided to stop by here and FINALLY try it.As a single patron, I got seated rather quickly. Coming here was SO WORTH IT. I got the Matcha Lava Cake! Dark chocolate with matcha ganache and green tea ice cream. My taste buds were in Heaven! I love that the lava cake had a slight crispiness to its edges, but the cake was overally still moist and rich and warm and fresh. The matcha ganache oozed out deliciously. So decadent! I loved the mix of rich chocolate with matcha, two of my favorite flavors! Man, if I wasn't watching out for my macros (and I already cheated hard and fast all day), I would have ordered more desserts to try.Customer service was FANTASTIC as well! They were attentive and polite without being overbearing, and ordering and paying was super easy. I really want to come back here with my boyfriend, and ideally a group of friends, in the future!

We were looking for some Korean Fried Chicken and decided to come here. They had a pretty good deal for two people that came with like 7 wings and 4 drumsticks and two beers for $30, and if you toss in a rice it was just enough for us two.We got that with half of them in the spicy sauce and half of them in the soy garlic. At first I liked the soy garlic more but after a while I wanted more flavor and the spicy sauce really hit home for it, especially on the bigger drumsticks.As usual it comes with some delicious pickles. There was only one lady serving everyone when we were there but she was quite prompt running between the tables!

TLDR: New location of Los Tacos No. 1. You will wait, it will cost you a lot but it'll be worth it. Stick with corn tortillas, try the different proteins and use plenty of the house salsa.I had known of Los Tacos for a long time but every time I walked by it in Chelsea Market, I refused to submit myself to that torturous line. However, I recently found out they opened a location near City Hall. Timing worked out for a late lunch and we got here around 2. Place was still a complete sh*t show. The line does move fast though.I think one of the great things is that the menu is simple. Pick if you want corn or flour tortilla, taco or tostada. That's it. We went with a tostada, a taco and quesadilla each. The one thing you notice is the meats are so smoky, it reminded me of the tacos I had in LA. The chicken, the steak the spicy pork - it was all fantastic. Now, this set us back $40 total with a drink.. which is a lot! However, I don't regret going, I thoroughly enjoyed this meal.I would probably skip the Especial next time, it's enjoyable but a bit too heavy/rich. Not to mention, it's also $6 and $8 with a protein. The tacos themselves are not too expensive, you pay a premium as this is a brick/mortar location in Manhattan; not a truck in Queens.If you're near one of these, don't walk - run! You'll satisfy your taco cravings and your taste buds will love you forever.

Title: Cozy Spot with Sociable Service and Great Eats

I recently dined at a charming little spot that instantly won me over with its sociable service and delightful outdoor seating adorned with string lights. Despite the city's reputation, note that the outdoorsy charm wraps up by 9-10pm.

The bratwurst sandwich on a pretzel roll was the star of the meal, served with a tasty mild mustard and sauerkraut, all without breaking the bank. While the potato salad left something to be desired due to its dryness, the brew selection, including a decent hefeweizen, made up for it.

Don't miss the fried zucchini strings as an appetizer; it's a generous serving perfect for sharing, especially with the delectable lemon aioli dip. Overall, this is the go-to spot for anyone looking to enjoy a relaxed meal with a beer in hand, and all while keeping their finances in check—definitely gets my recommendation!

Title: Cozy Ambiance with Prompt Service, Mixed Reviews on the Cuisine

I recently visited this restaurant for a team lunch with colleagues, where we encountered the first sign of their accommodating nature. Despite our group expanding unexpectedly from six to seven, the staff seamlessly managed to fit us in, a commendable feat given the restaurant's rather cozy interior space.

We all opted for the weekday Lunch Thalis, while I also inquired about a yelp check-in offer. The waiter astutely advised saving the offer since the dessert included in my meal was the same as the promotion – a thoughtful suggestion ensuring future savings.

Our meals were served promptly, a pleasant surprise given our number. My choice, the Chicken Tikka Masala thali, featured a delightful entree with a richly flavored tomato and cream gravy that paired wonderfully with the fresh naan. However, the side vegetables – a spinach dish and a potato with green beans concoction – left much to be desired due to their blandness and lack of spices. The yellow daal was passable, yet unremarkable.

Each thali shared the same sides: cauliflower pakora, the aforementioned underwhelming spinach and potato-green beans, yellow daal, rice, yogurt, salad, and kheer (rice pudding). Though the sides were a letdown, the standout was an assortment of tikkas from a colleague's platter, especially the malai tikka, which was notably succulent.

The service throughout our meal was impeccable; attentive without being intrusive. However, the overall quality of the food didn't quite justify the price point; while certain dishes were hits, others were misses. A mixed bag, but with room for improvement.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Dumpling and Noodle Aficionados!

I'm usually one to shy away from dumplings and noodles for dinner, but a friend's recommendation led me to discover this remarkable hole-in-the-wall gem. The interior is deceptively spacious, accommodating plenty of family-sized tables, though it's worth noting they don't provide water—so come prepared!

We started with their delicious $4 potsticker-style fried dumplings (8 pieces) and couldn't resist the complementary chili sauce, a match made in heaven. For my main, the Stir Fried Beef Knife Cut Noodles ($9.50) was an absolute delight. Each noodle dish was charmingly served on a shell-shaped plate, with the knife-cut noodles justifying the extra dollar with their irresistible chewy texture. Despite initial appearances, the generous portions left me satisfyingly full.

Service was efficient, albeit not the warmest—expect to see the bill promptly. But the quality of the food has me eager to return and explore more of their offerings.

After countless snaps and anticipatory cravings, I finally visited the matcha haven I'd been dreaming about. True to its social media allure, the experience did not disappoint. The star of the show was the divinely hot and creamy matcha lava cake, perfectly paired with matcha ice cream—a dream for any matcha enthusiast. Each dish was a visual and gastronomic pleasure, with the aesthetic charm matching the quality of the desserts.

While the harvest pot fell short on its own, a touch of their raspberry sorbet did enhance the experience, albeit not enough to make it a favorite. However, the brick toast, with its lightly sweetened fluffiness and the accompaniment of fruity toppings, was the epitome of light indulgence, especially when savored with their ice cream in the bustling New York scene.

The service was a high point, with warmth and welcome unfaltering even in the busiest times. My previous ventures included a takeaway molten matcha chocolate cookie, which, although not "fresh out of the oven," would likely be a delight if served warm. And I mustn't forget the seasonal Vietnamese coffee sundae from a past visit—enormous and striking the perfect balance between a robust coffee flavor and sweetness. It's a definitive treat for coffee lovers with a sweet tooth.

In summary, this is a must-visit spot for exceptional matcha desserts and a service that makes you feel at home.

Title: Flavor Haven with a Side of Unwelcoming Service at Pig and Khao

I recently dined at Pig and Khao, a culinary gem exuding tantalizing aromas from its open kitchen that tempt you the moment you enter. The food here is nothing short of exquisite, with a medley of dishes that each bring a burst of Southeast Asian flair to your palate. 

Despite my desire to give this place a full five-star rating, the service left much to be desired. We were met with scowls from a particular waitress whose demeanor suggested dining there was an inconvenience to her. However, the culinary delights were more than enough to make us overlook the less-than-stellar service.

On a busy Friday night, our 9pm reservation saw us seated promptly, and we delved into a shared feast. Standout dishes included the Grilled Pork Jowl, which was an interesting and delectable take on the Thai favorite larb - albeit slightly light on pork, the brussels sprouts shone through. The Sizzling Sisig, with its mix of pork head and chili topped with a perfectly cooked egg, was an addictive dish that nearly vanished while I was away.

The Grilled Sirloin was another triumph, enhanced by crispy garlic and a fiery Isaan sauce that left a lingering impression. And let's not forget the Malaysian Fried Chicken - the crunch of the skin and the flavor combination of pineapple chutney and curry leaves made for a memorable bite.

Accompanied by coconut rice, each dish was a testament to the complexity and richness of the cuisine. Despite the service hiccups, the incredible flavors at Pig and Khao are reason enough to return - the food truly speaks for itself.

Title: Quick Service but Underwhelming Pizza

I had high hopes for this restaurant due to the positive reviews, so I decided to give their cheese pie a try. While the delivery was commendably swift and accurate, the experience quickly soured when I found the pizza stuck to the top of the box — not a good first impression.

The pie itself was a decent size but fell flat on flavor. There was a scant amount of tomato sauce and minimal cheese, which was disappointing. Additionally, the pizza wasn't hot by the time it arrived. On a positive note, the crust had a pleasant crunch, although it was unevenly burnt in spots. It wasn't soggy and remained foldable, which I appreciated, and I was thankful for the lack of grease.

Regrettably, the pizza didn't live up to my expectations, and I won't be ordering from here again. My two-star rating acknowledges the prompt delivery and correct order, but unfortunately, that's where my compliments end. It was worth a try, but ultimately a letdown.

I recently enjoyed an excellent lunch at this local spot, particularly impressed with their Taco Tuesday promotion. The daily specials on beverages are an added delight. The steak taco I ordered was very tasty, with straightforward but satisfying toppings. A standout side dish was the yuca fries—perfectly crispy and served with a spicy, flavorful dipping sauce that really enhanced the experience. To top it off, the house-made horchata was outstanding. Highly recommend giving this place a try for a casual and delicious meal.

Ukrainian cuisine proves a delight at this gem of a restaurant where the love for carbs is unabashedly celebrated. Imagine the joy of savoring both mashed potatoes and pasta in one sitting – a dreamy indulgence for carbohydrate aficionados. The menu excites with its creative array of fillings like bacon-egg-cheese, arugula-goat cheese, and a tantalizing 'wilderness' meat option that keeps diners guessing. Choose between boiling or deep-frying; though fair warning, the latter may be a bit on the greasy side, even when paired with delicious caramelized onions. Nonetheless, this spot must be a divine retreat, as the flavors are heavenly orchestrated.

If you ever needed proof that vegan cuisine can convert even the staunchest skeptics, this charming restaurant is it. With its adorable and cozy ambiance, it's the kind of place that justifies the extra dollars you'll spend. Not only did I relish the menu, but my non-vegan partner can't stop raving about their burger – a true testament to the quality of the food. We rounded off our meal with a chocolate dessert that was nothing short of sublime. This spot is a must-visit for anyone looking for unforgettable vegan fare.

I visited the highly talked-about burger spot with high expectations, but was met with disappointment. The ambiance was surprisingly quiet for a Friday before 6pm, with no wait and several open tables, a contrast to the buzz at its smaller sister venue, 4 Charles. 

The service was a highlight, with a very attentive server and a commendable beer menu offering a broad selection. However, the food did not match up. Our cheeseburgers, expected to be a delightful experience comparable to the ones at 4 Charles, fell flat. They lacked the anticipated melt-in-your-mouth quality and were overly salted, as were the fries, to the point where even the aioli couldn't save them.

Overall, the meal left me feeling bloated and unsatisfied, especially considering the price point. For a truly great burger, I'd recommend sticking with 4 Charles.

Tucked just a few blocks from the esteemed Good, Thanks, this Australian cafe is a welcome addition to the neighborhood dining scene. If you're in the mood for a guilt-free delight, the Chop Salad, a steal at $12, offers a satisfying crunch. Those craving comfort food won't be disappointed with the Crispy Chicken Sandwich, arguably one of the best around, accompanied by a generous serving of superb skinny fries for $16. A solid choice for a quick and potentially healthy bite, this spot promises a satisfying dining experience.

Restaurant week dinner 2019 ($42)Appetizer: Mushroom Soup with whipped fresh cream - a larger portion than I expected, I loved that.Main: Loup de Mer (sea bass) Dessert: Tarte Au Pamplemousse (grapefruit tarte + sorbet) - really good, but got too sweet for me - Near Lincoln Center- Classy ambiance- Perfect location for any occasion

My boyfriend and I decided to give this local spot a try for weekend brunch and were seated immediately upon arrival. Despite being mostly vacant, which hints at a livelier dinner scene, the atmosphere was pleasant. We shared a delightful meal that included stuffed French toast, savory baked eggs, and a perfectly crispy side of fried chicken. Each dish was flavorful and satisfying, so much so that we had leftovers to enjoy later. The quality of the brunch has piqued my interest in their dinner offerings, particularly the pork chop and burgers. This place is definitely on my list for a future visit.

Came on a Sunday and there was happy hour at the bar that all cocktails are half off! (We ended up trying 7 of them, yummmmmm) Chicken Tikka- pretty cook, I was expecting little more flavor (I also like heavy taste thought) overall yummy and tender but no wow. Mango Cod- love it! So tasty love the sauce and the cod was fully immersed with the flavor. Duck- a bit disappointed. It was good duck but flavor nothing memorable.

Title: A Burger to Remember at Emily

My visit to Emily was an absolute delight, especially due to their remarkable burger, a juicy masterpiece nestled between the most unique pretzel bun I've tasted. Truly, this might just be the best burger I've encountered in recent memory – a blend of cheddar, caramelized onions, and a mysterious yet captivating secret sauce harmonizing with the succulent dry-aged beef. Embrace the mess; it's a hallmark of a truly great burger.

Complementing the star of the show, the asparagus salad swapped in for curly fries was a breath of fresh greenery, lifted by the tang of ricotta. The broccoli salad stood its ground, too – filling and scrumptious. Kudos to Dominic, our ultra-cool waiter, for accommodating the swap seamlessly.

Emily's ambiance mirrors its fare: vibrant and snug with a rustic charm. Despite its cozy two-floor arrangement, efficient seating by a skilled hostess meant we dodged the wait, though I'd recommend reservations to guarantee a spot in this culinary haven.

DUMPLINGS ARE SO GOOD! We got broccoli beef, Fried rice, General Tso chicken, sesame chicken, and 4D Chow Mein. All of it was good except for the beef dishes. Their beef tasted off. The chow mein, sesame seed chicken and General Tso's chicken were BOMB. I will go back just for the dumplings. Also, the service is pretty slow.

Title: A Cozy Corner Gem in the Heart of NYC

Stumbling upon hidden gems is one of the joys of wandering New York City, and this charming pub near a local bookstore is no exception. With an inviting atmosphere, it's a delightful spot for a satisfying meal. I kicked off my dinner with their chili appetizer—robust, with just the right amount of heat and bursting with flavor.

The Penny Burger was my entrée of choice. It did not disappoint, especially since I could swap out the usual fries for a side of grilled asparagus—though, a note to the kitchen, a few more spears wouldn’t hurt for us asparagus aficionados.

The layout caters to varied preferences, offering 4-top tables, cozy booths for small groups, a communal table, and bar seating, plus a few outdoor tables to enjoy in pleasant weather. Situated on a corner with its "well loved" wooden facade, it's easy to spot this welcoming establishment.

With four large TV screens, I was able to catch some soccer as I dined, which gets an extra thumbs up from me. Service was top-notch, making the entire dining experience wonderful from start to finish. This place is a must-visit for anyone seeking a hearty meal with a side of good sports in NYC.

Allora is the place to go for great Italian! The food and service are impeccable! My husband and I came to Allora Friday night to celebrate our anniversary. We had a reservation at 7:30 p.m. and we were sat immediately upon arriving to the restaurant.We started our meal with a glass of wine which was really fantastic! My husband and I are huge fans of French wines and they had a lot to choose from. For an appetizer we had the caprese salad which had exceptional flavor. For our main courses I had the gnocchi and my husband had the rigatoni; both dishes were full of zest and really hit the spot.We finished up our meal with dessert, I had the cheese cake and my husband had the chocolate soufflé. Both of our dishes were just exquisite and full of rich flavors.The server stayed on top of our table the entire night and was very helpful in helping us choose our dishes.I am very excited to come back to Allora and try some of their other plates! Thanks for a wonderful anniversary dinner!

Title: Mixed Experiences at a Bustling Friday Dinner

My husband and I visited this restaurant hoping for a relaxing Friday dinner, but our expectations were met with some disappointments. The service was painstakingly slow and lacked attention to detail, which was compounded by the excessive noise level that made communication challenging. Although the setting aimed to be more subdued, the volume was still overwhelming, requiring our waitress to make quite the effort to take our order.

The layout of the restaurant was another downside, with tables packed so tightly that maneuvering around them became a nuisance, threatening the safety of our drinks on more than one occasion.

On a positive note, the guacamole appetizer was a tasty start, although the portion size left us wanting more. The swordfish tacos were mediocre and initially served incorrectly as a deep-fried dish, which the staff promptly replaced upon our request. The octopus entrée won praise from my husband, but I found it lackluster. My codfish was notably bland and watery, ultimately ending up on my husband's plate.

We stuck to wine for the evening, so I can't comment on the cocktails. Dessert was the final letdown; the uninspired menu led us to forego what should have been a sweet ending to our meal. Notably, the absence of tres leches cake seemed like a missed staple for a Mexican restaurant.

This place may fit the bill for a lively group outing with drinks, but it fell short for us as a couple seeking a more intimate dining experience.

I fell in love with Éric Kayser on my early Yelp days, I go less now not because I think of them any less from before but because I found so many other good places to go also.I happy to see a chain expand all over New York and now at the Hudson Yards.Kayser is also famous for their bread which I find spectacular, but I was far too tempted by great French style pastries. Pistachios are big in December and January, so I tried the pistachio eclair and pistachio apricot tart. The eclair was excellent with the salty nuts complimenting the delicate pastry and cream filling. The tart was a great combination of flavors with sweet, tart, and savory all playing around in my mouth.There are so many delicious dessert here I never come out empty handed.

This is my go-to Mexican food take out place. I love the nachos here, but they are much better when you eat them in the restaurant. Everything else I have ordered has been great as to take out. I have ordered the al pastor burrito ($8) one of my favorites, milanesa torta ($8) very filling and was able to make 2 meals out of it, chicken nachos ($10) better in the restaurant, and the carnitas platter ($9) my new favorite take out meal. The carnitas platter is delicious and crispy. I recommend getting a side order of 4 tortillas ($1) even though it already comes with 3.

Rating 3 stars for food, and 4 for excellent service.Came here for a weekend brunch in a group of five. I'd previously heard very good things about Perry St, and had been looking forward to eating here. The meal got off to a good start, with my party of five and I being seated at one of the aesthetically pleasing corner booths. The decor here is minimal, modern and elegant, with large windows and a light grey color scheme.After taking some time to decide, the majority of us decided to order the 'Taste of Winter' menu (restaurant week winter 2019), while one of us ordered from the a la carte menu. Our food was brought out in a timely manner, and everything was presented beautifully. For my entree, I had the tuna tartare. The pieces of fish were simply flavored, and fresh. While nothing worth raving about, it wasn't terrible either. For my main dish, I had the lobster (an $8 supplement to the menu). It was prepared simply and grilled in a buttery sauce. You can't really go wrong when ordering lobster, and as such, this one was tasty, but again not something I would recommend or order again if I had the chance. For those of us who had ordered the restaurant week menu, I believe dessert was the best course. Most of my party ordered the molten chocolate lava cake, and it was delicious, from what I had. Instead of the lava cake, I opted for the apple cinnamon cake, which was served prettily with a slice of apple, and sorbet on the side. The cake had pieces of poached apple in cinnamon glaze inside - it was pleasant to eat, but not super memorable.The service here was superb. We had a young looking waiter who was the epitome of professionalism, and all the staff here were indeed very nice.While I didn't have anything that was extremely memorable, I might give this place a try another time based on the ambience and service, and the number of reviews that deem this place excellent.

Signs say $1 pizza, but pizza prices ranged from $2-$4. The pizza was great, albeit a bit too greasy for my taste. Crust was not too thick, or too thin. Just the right amount of sauce! Service was not amazing, but also was not awful. I did not see red peppers anywhere, however only regular black pepper. Note: this place can sit maybe 20 people, but people are in and out in a flash! I would return! If you're looking for a cheap meal, this is it!

Mint Kitchen finds itself amidst the fast casual restaurant surge, offering the familiar protein and veggie combo but at startlingly steep prices. My $18 bowl—topped with a disappointingly meager amount of spinach—hardly hit the mark of satisfaction. The promise of a "falafel-crusted" salmon revealed itself as a mere sprinkling rather than a crust, leaving one to question the value proposition. While the quality of the dish was not in question, the portion size certainly was, especially considering the plethora of nearby alternatives that promise more bang for your buck.

The absence of something as simple as a hot sauce option was a notable misstep, failing to elevate the flavors that needed a kick. Despite the letdown with the food, the interior deserves a nod—with its inviting arrangement of hanging plants and a comfortably cushioned stadium seating area, it’s a charming spot for a coffee and relaxation rather than a meal that doesn't quite live up to its price point.

Title: A Cozy Gem with Exemplary Cuisine

I had the pleasure of dining at this charming restaurant on a quiet weekday evening, where the combination of delicious food, a soothing ambiance, and warm staff left a lasting impression. The recently updated winter 2020 menu boasted a delightful array of dishes, starting with the standout spicy mussels in a delectable coconut broth - the portions were generous, and the dish was served with plenty of bread for the essential dipping.

For the main course, the perfectly cooked fish accompanied by roasted carrots and butternut squash was a harmonious blend of flavors and textures. My partner's duck was equally impressive, cooked to perfection, highlighting the freshness we'd come to appreciate throughout the meal.

It was also a treat to know that the ingredients, along with some of the wine and beer selections, are sourced from the North Fork and Hudson regions, ensuring a commitment to fresh, seasonal produce.

The staff's kindness and welcoming nature added to the exceptional dining experience. I'm already looking forward to my next visit and can't recommend this restaurant enough for those seeking a delightful culinary journey.

If you're in search of the best tacos in NYC, look no further! This spot is renowned for its consistently delicious offerings, with both corn and flour tortillas providing the perfect foundation for their delectable fillings. While every option is mouth-watering, the pork tacos are the real showstopper — routinely selling out during peak hours for good reason. They are, without a doubt, the highlight of the menu. Do yourself a favor and get there early to indulge in what are arguably the city's finest tacos.

Title: A Tasty Visit to Southern Hospitality BBQ with Room for Service Improvement

I recently ventured to Southern Hospitality BBQ for the first time, prompted by a friend's suggestion for a casual meetup. The location immediately impressed me—convenient and inviting. I kicked off the experience with a drink that packed the right punch: both flavorful and spirited.

Although the atmosphere was lively, the service lagged notably. With what appeared to be a shortage of servers, there was a considerable wait for our drinks and later, our food. This delay seemed to be the only blemish on an otherwise enjoyable outing.

When our meal arrived, the crispy chicken tenders proved to be a delectable choice—perfectly cooked and seasoned. We complemented our main dish with a side of tater tots, which were a delightful addition to our Southern feast.

Dessert was the grand finale, with the banana pudding standing out as exceptional—a must-try for any patron. The bread pudding followed closely in terms of taste and comfort, rounding off the meal on a high note.

In summary, with its fantastic food and prime location, Southern Hospitality BBQ has a lot of potential. A boost in staff numbers could vastly improve the dining experience, making it a spot not to be missed.

Title: Convenient but Pricey - A Mixed Bagel Experience

I recently visited a local lunch spot that presents a unique selection of foods. It's a convenient choice for a quick bite, yet the prices leave me hesitant to call it my go-to.

I opted for an everything bagel with bacon, egg, and cheese, setting me back $7. The bagel was a standout, especially with a delightful sprinkle of salt which is atypically thoughtful. The fillings were generous in cheese and egg, while the bacon was standard fare. The toasting service was efficient with a mere 5-minute wait.

The menu is eclectic, offering classic bagel pairings, an array of cream cheese options, alongside a mix of Chinese take-out and traditional lunch items. The smoothie selection also caught my eye for a future visit.

The ambiance strikes a comfortable balance – not overly crowded or noisy, even at a peak time like 12:30pm on a Monday. With open seating and available wifi, it's a solid choice for those looking to dine and work, though I anticipate possible crowds during the school year.

In summary, while the food and atmosphere are commendable, the pricing may deter frequent visits.

Title: Timeless Quality at a Cozy Sushi Haven

I've been a loyal patron of this quaint sushi spot since childhood, and it remains as delightful as ever. Despite its compact size—reservations are a must—the experience is nothing short of grand. Here, sushi rolls are generously sized, ideal for sampling and sharing from the communal platter that graces the table.

While prices are on the higher side, the sushi's freshness and expert preparation justify every penny. The restaurant exudes a charming, hole-in-the-wall ambiance that adds to the allure. Every visit promises great food and a warm atmosphere, making it a cherished destination for sushi lovers.

What a cute tucked away indoor garden oasis!  This restaurant is open late to grab a bite to eat.  We needed some explanations, becasue we didn't know what all the dishes were.  The pasta is fresh and the sauces are lovely.  Our group ordered a combo - pesto gnocchi, chicken tetrazzini and rigatoni a la vodka.  We also ordered a side of sauteed spinach, in an effort to add vegetables.  The food was plenty!  Service was fast and friendly!

Title: A Quintessential Brunch at Le Monde

My love for Le Monde was fully ignited during a late Sunday brunch, an experience so delightful that it demands sharing. For those in search of an inviting outdoor dining experience, look no further than this gem.

Our culinary adventure began with their Challah French Toast, priced at $14, and it was nothing short of perfection. As someone fastidious about their French toast, I was captivated by the light, flavorful slices of challah, crowned with a generous portion of seasonal fruit and kissed with cinnamon and vanilla. Meanwhile, the Shakshuka ($18) was a revelation, marrying lightness with heartiness. The eggs were impeccable, and the use of goat cheese instead of the typical feta was a masterstroke, introducing a delightful creaminess. The star, however, was the merguez – our inaugural indulgence in lamb sausage – which was a savory surprise, harmonizing beautifully with the accompanying charred bread.

In light of this visit, I find the current 3/5 star rating of Le Monde baffling. It's palpable that the establishment has made significant improvements in the past six months, making any older critique less relevant. With confidence, I urge you to ignore the past and allow yourself to be present at Le Monde for what undoubtedly will be a memorable brunch. Go, and let your taste buds be your guide.

Title: Unbeatable Grilled Fish Tacos on E 12th St

If you find yourself craving grilled fish tacos in the heart of the city, look no further. This gem, frequented by NYU and New School students, serves up tacos so satisfying that two are all you need for a hearty meal. The available condiments, featuring spices of varying intensities and distinctive "pink" sliced onions, allow for a personalized and visually appealing dish. Opting out of sour cream doesn't detract from the experience; these tacos are just as delicious and pack a spicy punch I absolutely adore.

Despite its compact size, the establishment offers free WiFi, a unisex bathroom, and complimentary water, enhancing the dining experience. Seating is communal, promoting a convivial atmosphere—not that you'll spend much time seated, given how the tacos demand to be swiftly savored. It's an eating experience so memorable that long after you've left, you'll find yourself yearning for another bite, inevitably drawn back to this lively taco spot on E 12th St.
