My favorite Italian restaurant - the staff is kind, friendly, and professional. The food is  u n r e a l. You can find me here literally once a week.

Title: Hit-or-Miss Experience at Local Asian Eatery

I recently ordered takeaway from this spot when it was fairly quiet, with only a quarter of the tables filled. Despite this, my meal took half an hour to prepare. The hot and sour soup I had eagerly anticipated fell flat, lacking the punch of heat and tang I craved. However, the fried dumplings were quite enjoyable, cooked well with a satisfying flavor. An upside is the establishment's offer of free delivery, a perk not commonly found among its competitors in the area. Overall, a mixed dining experience.

Upon entering, the aroma was utterly captivating – a blend of beef, salt, and cheese that promised a culinary adventure. The menu featured the classics along with premium selections such as Wagyu, and notably, they've extended an interesting promotion offering the veggie burger for free, which was initially for ladies only but now available to all patrons.

I opted for the veggie burger, accompanied by sweet fries and a glass of Cabernet Sauvignon; the bill was quite reasonable at $20. The music created an energetic atmosphere, although I would suggest they add some salad options for a more balanced menu.

There was a delay in service, waiting nearly ten minutes for cutlery is a point that needs addressing. While the veggie burger was enjoyable with a delightful sauce, it didn't quite hit the mark of extraordinary, and the bun was average.

The sweet fries, as anticipated, were delicious. It's worth mentioning that the promotion of the free veggie burger is a welcome surprise and adds to the restaurant's appeal.

Observing SaltBae himself in action was an added bonus, contributing to the global dining experience the place aims to offer. Despite the few hiccups, it's a spot worth visiting, especially for those intrigued by the meat selections and the dynamic ambiance.

Came here on a Sunday for lunch and tried Diving Fish Pot ($35) and Tiger Pepper Beef ($19.50). Diving Fish Pot: A whole fish came in spicy Sichuan broth with peppercorn and veggies like bean sprouts and green onion. The fish fillet was soooo tender that every bite melted in my mouth. I chose mild for the spice level (I like Sichuan restaurants like this spot that allow you to choose spice level!) and it was just the right spiciness for me and I have a pretty low tolerance for spicy food. It also comes with a choice of brown or white rice, so I chose brown rice to eat with the fish. I really liked digging into every part of the fish and my bf and I was able to finish the whole pot. I think the price point for this dish is very reasonable considering the quality of the fish and its portion size. -- I definitely recommend this dish for sharing. Tiger Pepper Beef: Although this dish isn't something very special as you can find it at any Chinese restaurant, I was surprised at how well they did it. The shredded beef was tender and it wasn't too oily. The hot pepper and green onion were also fresh and crunchy. It wasn't really spicy but the hot pepper made the dish pretty flavorful. I also got plum juice and it was very nice to have with the spicy food as it sort of cooled down the spiciness. Additionally, I checked-in on Yelp to get free two spring rolls and they were pretty decent as well! Inside is spacious and very beautiful with Chinese decor. It's hard to find a good Asian restaurant that's not too pricey or touristy in the heart of Timesquare, so I'm super happy to find this place. This could also be a perfect spot for pre or post broadway show meal as it's located in the Theater district. They also take reservation online, which makes it very easy to come even on weekends. They have a lot of items on their menu so I definitely want to come back here again to try some other stuff!

Title: Spacious and Welcoming - A Manhattan Gem for Groups

Last night's group dinner at this Manhattan eatery was a delightful experience. The restaurant's spacious interior is a rare find in the city, comfortably accommodating our party of ten without feeling cramped. Though the decor leans towards the darker side, it adds a cozy ambiance to the vast dining space.

The culinary offerings, though slightly reduced in portion compared to previous visits, still maintained their solid quality. The compact dish sizes did not detract from the overall enjoyment, as each plate was thoughtfully prepared. Regarding the service, it was warm and welcoming, albeit not the quickest. We appreciated the staff's responsiveness when one member's meal was inadvertently omitted, and their prompt action to rectify the mistake was commendable.

In particular, the breakfast menu stands out as a must-try, showcasing the robust flavors of Cuban cuisine. A word of advice for future patrons: this isn't a place for those in a hurry. Instead, it's perfect for those looking to savor their meal and relish the company of friends or family.

In summary, this restaurant is a solid choice for group dining, striking a fine balance between convivial service and quality food. It's certainly worth the visit, especially if you're not pressed for time.

Title: A Lackluster Friday Night at Friday's

I ventured into Friday's for a late-night meal, expecting the usual casual, welcoming vibe. Unfortunately, the staff seemed indifferent to our presence, making it clear they couldn't wait for closing time—still a full two hours away. Opting for the bar where at least the bartender offered a smile, I ordered the bourbon glazed chicken and shrimp with a side of my favorite carbs: mash and fries. Mediocrity was the theme; the chicken overcooked but edible enough to satisfy my hunger, especially when aided by a cotton candy martini. Essentially, you get the bare minimum for your money at this NYC chain past a certain hour. My advice? If you're looking for genuine hospitality and a memorable dining experience, take a short walk elsewhere. This Friday's, despite its clean setting, didn't live up to even modest expectations.

Title: A Delightful Bite at Emily's – Name Bias Totally Justified!

I might be slightly partial given that Emily's and I share a namesake – an undoubtedly cool factor for anyone named Emily or their acquaintances. But setting biases aside, the Emmy burger stands out as heavenly. Imagine a burger with a pillow-soft bun, a patty that’s the epitome of juicy, complemented by the sweetness of caramelized onions and the melt-in-your-mouth cheese. The entire ensemble is a texture enthusiast's dream, right down to the exceptional fries served alongside.

Though the price tag leans towards the steep side for a burger, splitting it with a pal is not only economical but also satisfying thanks to the considerate provision of a hefty knife for easy sharing. The elderflower cocktail added a splash of sophistication to the meal, perfectly pairing with the burger’s rich flavors.

The venue itself boasts a prime location, with the added perks of amiable service, pristine restrooms, and an ambiance that amplifies the dining experience. Whether for the unique charm of dining at a namesake or to indulge in a burger that truly stands out, Emily's is a must-visit.

I came here during restaurant week and I feel in love! I don't like coconut at all but their coconut rice is to die for. Since I had their coconut rice I have decided to try coconut other places, but none of them taste the same as Pig and Khao. It's just soooooo good you have no idea you need to try it. This is the first place that I love to eat Brussels sprouts. If you don't like Brussels Sprouts, try their grilled pork Jowl salad. It's amazing and just so juicy. I finished the whole salad. Since I came here during restaurant week the portions for ribs were smaller. But their salad and pork belly I believe they were the same portion. I wasn't a big fan of their dessert halo-halo. However, I like their Turon. You should make room for dessert !
Yes, loved the coffee, corn beef hash and blintzes were to die for. Our server was kind and very attentive.

This restaurant was decent for taking our group out to dinner.  The prefix course is $60 and you get to choose from a large variety of good French cooking.  We were able to fit about 15 to 20 people comfortably.  Overall I was pleased with the food and presentation.

Title: Trendy Spot for Burgers with Room for Improvement - Black Tap K-Town

Last Friday night, my friends and I, a group of seven, were pleasantly surprised to find no wait at Black Tap in the bustling K-Town for a 7:30pm dinner – a rarity we thought wouldn't last as word spreads about this spot. The hosts greeted us with the same lively energy reflected in the restaurant’s trendy decor, which was irresistibly photogenic.

Drinks priced at an average of $10 were promptly ordered, and our attentive server took the time to explain menu options, steering us towards choices like the Texan Burger. Between us, we sampled a range including the All-American, Bison, Falafel burgers, Crispy Chicken Sandwich, and more. Despite minor hiccups like mixed-up and incorrect orders - understandable for a larger group - the food was generally well-received, save for a slightly dry chicken sandwich.

The night being my birthday, I ambitiously ordered one of their famed milkshakes at 8:30pm. An ensuing mix-up meant it arrived too late for me to enjoy and initially appeared on the bill despite our request to cancel it. Our server’s eye-rolling response to our time crunch soured the experience, though the charge was ultimately removed.

Price-wise, a full meal here can land around $40, a steep price for a casual outing but not out of line for a New York City joint using quality ingredients. It may be best suited for a special occasion rather than a regular haunt.

Would I return? Yes, but likely with a smaller group and more time to indulge in – and properly judge – one of their Instagram-worthy milkshakes.

I've been a fan of Tatsu due to their late night hours at their LA locations. There wasn't much opened in the East Village area after 1am on a Sunday night so we went ahead and hit up Tatsu.  Their most popular item is the wagyu ramen burger. The ramen 'buns' are cooked nicely and still have a crispy exterior but still moist with a good texture once you take those first few bites. The bun is lightly glazed as well and never overpowered so you can still taste the flavor of the beef.The prices do seem slightly inflated compared to their LA spots (it is NY after all) but overall, you cannot complain about having ramen in the wee hours, especially after a drink or two.Enjoy and savor the noodz!

My friends and I were in the area and noticed a new food hall that we haven't seen before. Since we were starving, it seemed like a great decision to enter to see what this place had to offer. We were pretty indecisive but eventually agreed on Thai and the first restaurant we saw was Eat Gai. The ladies at the counter were very friendly and since we weren't sure what to order we just asked for their suggestions. The menu is limited but we ended up ordering a little bit everything just to get a better idea of this restaurant. We ordered the boiled chicken, fried chicken wings, Hainese chicken, sticky rice, ginger rice, and Thai iced Tea. My friend was on diet so she was pretty limited on eating the boiled chicken with gizzards and thought it was tasty. Since she's on a low sodium diet , this dish seemed perfect for her as it was lightly seasoned. I devoured the fried chicken and honestly it was my favorite dish of the night. It was nicely crisp, flavorful, and the pickled veggies added a nice touch. My other friend had the other battered chicken with rice and she enjoyed it very much. I personally prefer the ginger rice over the sticky rice but my friends felt otherwise. The Thai iced tea was slightly sweeter than most iced teas we've tried but we enjoyed the richness it delivered.

Tried the ban an chicken which was delicious. The Hamburg steak could of been better. It was large, juicy, and had a good texture but the sauce had way too much ketchup. It came across as more like a meatloaf.  The agedashi tofu was delicious, and the sauce for the gyoza was nice and tart.I just wish the place had better ventilation from the kitchen. You end up kind of smelling like fried oil. I'd happily order takeout here though to avoid smelling up my clothes. The last thing is that the dishes do seem a bit pricy but when you consider how big it is, it compensates for it.

We went to Darbar recently for their lunch buffet, which runs from 11:30-4 for $15.95. We arrived on the later side, around 3 pm, and were happy to see that the full spread was still available and that they were still refilling the dishes even though there was less than an hour left to the buffet. They had more than 10 different dishes available, including more expensive items like goat and fish, and a basket of naan was delivered to the table once we started eating. Everything we got was delicious, and my favorites were the chicken tikka masala, chana saag, chickpea salad, and onion chutney. They had dessert too, but I was way too full to try any of it. Service was friendly, and they were very accommodating of our child, providing us a high chair and corner table with a lot of space. If you're in Midtown and looking for a lot of food for lunch, this would be a great choice.

I recently dined at a local eatery that offers a fast and affordable dining experience. The flavors on the menu impressed me, showcasing a tasty array of options. However, I must note that the noodles I ordered were overcooked, resulting in a texture that was too soft for my preference. This spot is suitable for a swift lunch or a casual snack when time is of the essence.

I was pleasantly surprised with this place. My friends and I wandered into Gameeook on a Saturday afternoon around 3pm after we had been day drinking all morning. Since it was between lunch and dinner, the place wasn't too busy so we were seated quickly. The menu is pretty simple and doesn't have an overabundance of options, so we promptly decided on what we wanted. For the appetizer, we ordered the kimchi pancake, which by the way, isn't gluten free. There aren't too many gluten free items on the menu, and they don't notate which are and aren't either. But based on the ingredients listed in the description, you can assume which ones are and aren't. It would be nice, however, if they did notate it.While we waited, the server came by with a bowl of kimchi that he cut and divided into a separate plate for us to share. I looked to my two Caucasian friends and admitted that I'm a sucky asian who doesn't know how to use chopsticks. They laughed and the waiter standing nearby overheard, glanced over and immediately brought over a fork. I appreciated the initiative.We then ordered BBQ pork belly, a kimchi tang, and two Dolsots. (My friend is clearly obsessed with kimchi because half of what we ate was kimchi-something). Anyway, the BBQ pork belly was quite a good amount, although a bit pricey in my opinion. It was flavorful, but slightly too oily. The kimchi tang had a mix of cabbage, beef (maybe?), mushrooms, and rice cake. It was slightly spicier than the appetizer kimchi we had. The dolsot came on a sizzling hot plate--great presentation. As aforementioned, I'm a sucky asian, so the waiter figured I probably didn't know what to do with the dolsot. He quickly recommended that I mix everything together and add the sweet/spicy sauce to give it more flavor. Good thing I did because shortly after, everything that wasn't mixed, got stuck to the bottom of the bowl. The waiter saw that we had almost finished the kimchi on our table and offered to bring some more. I love that he was so attentive!We were also looking for recommendations for good boba places to go afterwards and the staff were really helpful in helping us choose a spot.Overall, great customer service, good food, great location! I'd come back here again if in the area.

TL; DR: Jax restaurant consistently underwhelms in value and consistency. Their Southern Chili is hit-or-miss in portion size and presentation, not worth the $10 given its unpredictability in serving, sometimes coming with cheese and other times without. The ribs are a chewy disappointment, and while the Mac & cheese could be a fan favorite, its inconsistent preparation means you never know which version you'll receive. The only redeeming item is the Baked Beans, but they alone can't justify the price when competitors offer superior consistency and execution, especially for delivery. Bottom line: there are better places to spend your dining dollars.

K Kitchen is a hidden new gem for Korean crispy chicken in Hells Kitchen. Tucked away just a few streets from the bustling theatre district, K Kitchen has excellently crisp and well priced crispy kitchen in wings, drumsticks, and crispy chicken burgers (which I had). As opposed to many other crispy chicken places, this authentic restaurant does not hide the chicken flavor among a multitude of sauces or many layers of vegetables and distractions. Lettuce, tomatoes, pickles and spicy mayo, all that's to garnish the generous slab of fried chicken that was crisp and flavorful to the last bite. I paired by burger with the Nine Pin Ginger Cider, which offered a tart cleanse of my palette after each bite. Delicious for anyone who enjoys ginger!The waitress and waiters were extremely kind and the restaurant ambience felt spacious, private and hip. Will definitely return for seconds if I am in the area!

Title: A Taste of Italy in a Charming Cafe

This delightful little cafe is a gem for anyone looking to satisfy their pasta cravings. Despite never having set foot in Italy, I felt transported to a quaint Italian street, thanks to its authentic ambiance. The space may be small, but the opportunity to sit outside and engage in some casual people-watching is a welcome one.

Pairing a good glass of wine with their standout dish, the tagliatelle verdi con ragu, elevates the dining experience. Imagine al dente green tagliatelle laced with truffles and succulent boar meat, presented in a charming pot - it's the epitome of indulgence.

Whether you're stopping by for a quick lunch or settling in for dinner, this cafe doesn't disappoint. I found the service friendly and attentive. Pro tip: capitalize on their lunchtime specials for a truly exceptional deal. Overall, this is an excellent spot that promises a slice of Italy with every visit.

Cute fancy date spot. Husband took me here for restaurant week and the food was great. Enjoyed the mahi mahi wonton tacos the most! Definitely a must order and the drinks were delish. Service was also very fast! Only reason I am giving it four stars is because the restaurant was freezing cold. In the dead of winter, it wasn't pleasant eating and drinking while shivering.

I really wanted to like this place especially because the decor and concept is cool but it is really just like an overpriced shake shack with alcohol. First, you need to order yourself at the counter which gives it a cafeteria/fast food feel. Second, the burger literally tasted just like shake shack. The "thick cut Belgian fries" also were flavorless. For the price it's just not worth it. I think the only thing this place has going for it is the nice outdoor seating during the summer months.

To be honest, the Pizza Norma was a total fail. Way too dry and not a lot of taste. To their credit, the staff noticed that we were not eating it and quickly replaced it with a Stracciatella Pizza to which they added Prosciutto. Both pizzas were comped. Every restaurant has a problem once in a while, it is how they deal with it that sets the best places apart. Since Marta is a Danny Meyers restaurant -- no tipping -- these folks were simply doing what was right, not looking for a better tip. Overall it was an excellent experience.

Food is 3-stars but worth checking out for the cheaper prices & classic cart style dim sum.I only ordered the food on the cart so can't speak to the made to order dishes, all the dumpling & buns were pretty good. The short rib was eh. The peking duck buns were very yummy! It's a busy place on the weekends but with many levels you can get a table. Very noisy & busy but fun place for dim sum

During my visit to a quaint eatery at the Essex Market, I ventured into the world of Arancini, guided by the cashier's recommendation of a sweet variety. Eager to sample a range of flavors, I chose the Mexican, Pizza, and Classic balls. Regretfully, none managed to tickle my palate. The Mexican Arancini fell short, missing the advertised guacamole and sour cream, and was overwhelmed by a perplexing mix of taco seasoning and oregano. Similarly, the Classic was rather bland, yet again dominated by oregano. The Pizza-flavored Arancini also failed to impress, mirroring the same herb-heavy profile as its counterparts. It appears all three distinct flavors were lost in a monotonous oregano haze. While I appreciate the experience of trying something new, I'm afraid my taste buds and Arancini just didn't dance well together. A return visit seems unlikely.

We ordered the half and half soup base with tomato (they also offer mushroom) and honestly I would've just done one pot with tomato, mild spicy. It's incredibly flavorful! The medium spicy, while equally delicious, creeps on you till you no longer want it...I really like how you can order by marking down items on a sheet of paper, however their menu needs a little work. We ended up ordering the wrong things because the check boxes were aligned with the Chinese characters and everything was too close to each other. Nevertheless the quality of meal is good and everything is neatly sliced. I like that they offer cubed meat; it's a nice change up to thinly sliced beef/pork/lamb. Something we ordered by accident was sliced cucumber and have to say that it was by far my favorite dish! It had a nice crunch and was really refreshing. Lastly, they need to install some vents because the smell gets all over your clothes/belongings.

First time in this restaurant, was not disappointed. Ordered a vermicelli dish which came with marinated meat and some greens. Was pretty good and the size was also pretty decent. $9.25 for the dish, not bad value-wise as well. If you do end up here, remember it is **cash only**

I recently attended a venue event at this charming restaurant and was thoroughly impressed. The interior is stunning, creating a perfect backdrop for any gathering. Service was top-notch; staff went above and beyond to ensure our experience was seamless. I highly recommend making a trip to this hidden gem. Even with a pre-fix menu, the food was delectable – a testament to their culinary standards. The bar area deserves a special mention; it's a cozy spot to unwind with a drink, free from any delays or fuss. Do yourself a favor and check out this delightful establishment.

I had a delightful visit to Eataly – a charming marketplace worth exploring for its array of fresh produce, seafood, meats, cheeses, pasta, bread, gelato, cannolis, and the convenience of having three or four restaurants right within the space.

During the Restaurant Fest, I indulged in the $18 2-course pre-fixe menu, starting off with a fresh salad, and perfectly roasted cauliflower and Brussels sprouts. For the main course, the margherita pizza was quite satisfying, with a tasty crust and great texture, although not the best I've ever had. The tagliolini al ragu bianco and agnolotti del plin were nicely prepared, but my preference leaned towards the pizza for its comforting simplicity.

Overall, Eataly impresses with its variety and quality, making it a must-visit for anyone looking for a delightful food experience.

Title: A Delightful French Brunch Oasis Near Washington Square Park

I recently stumbled upon a charming spot ideal for beating the NYC heat with a refreshing drink and delicious brunch. The ambiance strikes a perfect balance, offering a welcoming environment without the pretentiousness of fancier establishments.

The highlight of my visit was the $5 mimosas. Made with fresh-squeezed orange juice, they were the perfect antidote to the city's sweltering weather. After indulging in a couple, my party and I were enticed to try their brunch offerings, and we were not disappointed.

We sampled the Frisée aux Lardons, a classic omelette, and a Salade Niçoise, each dish transporting us to a quaint bistro in France with its authentic flavors and presentation. The attentive service only enhanced our experience, ensuring that each need was met with a smile.

In summary, this gem of a French restaurant is a great find – reasonably priced, high-quality fare, and a stone's throw from Washington Square Park. Perfect for a lazy Saturday brunch or just to quench your thirst with a mimosa (or two).

Overall, classic taco place. Would recommend for families and larger groups. Location: situated in midtown, so it's a nice and convenient place. The restaurant itself is really spacious with lots of seating given its location in midtown. Because of the nice interior, I definitely did not feel rushed eating. Service: service was on the slower side, but still got everything done and were friendly Food: we got chicken tacos, crispy fish tacos, sweet potato taco, al pastor, chips&guac, and the corn (some not pictured). I would say the chicken tacos were better than most. We enjoyed the bean purée that lined the base of the taco. The sweet potato taco was surprisingly delicious and the sauce in it gave it a nice kick. The guac was nice and fresh. Overall, I'd say the tacos weren't anything exceptional. It's a pretty classic taco place (comparable to los tacos but more pricey). Not sure if I'd go again, but the seating and interior was nicer than the classic taco place.

Such amazing service! We got here around 7:30pm without reservations and were seated immediately. The space is a little tight but it's great because we were having a great conversation with the people next to us. They celebrated their 25th anniversary and the waiter brought them some complimentary ice cream and champagne. Our waiter Will was so friendly and funny, always checking up on us. The fried oysters are a must, my friend really liked the duck confit special, I got the lobster just to be fancy and he got the steak which looked awesome. Everything was beautifully plated I felt weird though taking all these food pics for you guys in the dark with flash. We also saw a sugar baby and sugar daddy which made it such a fun night-- this is the place you want to go to dinner!!

Came here on a Friday night to celebrate a friends birthday and I had a great experience overall!Valerie was lightly dimmed (romantic ambience) and music was generally on the loud side, but not too loud that my friends and I had to yell over the music. The restaurant came off with a classy and elegant vibe but also casual enough vibe to just grab a drink at the bar! I tried a Sloe Gin Fizz and it wasn't too strong for my preference. The food was very satisfying! I was contemplating between 2 chicken breast choices and the waiter recommended the Skilled Roasted Roast Chicken. The chicken had a really crispy skin but it was a bit salty. The entree also came with their DELICIOUS Valerie fries that I was extremely satisfied with. Loved the service because the waiter came to check up on my satisfaction of the chicken breast entree he recommended!Everything was good besides the tiny fact that the food took some time to come out. There was an error (on their part) with our reservation. However, they were able to quickly accommodate and set up a table for our large party. It is a bit pricey but definitely a nice place for celebrations!

I think this is a great spot to eat for breakfast, lunch or dinner! They have several stands to eat - sandwiches, salads, Mexican, Asian food and a cafe. They also have different trays of food out. They're reasonably priced for NYC. I pay $11 for a build your own salad. $10 for a sandwich. The quality is fresh and food.They have cafeteria like seating on their second floor. They're centrally located in midtown.

Title: A Seafood Haven in the Heart of NYC – Catch Restaurant Review

I recently visited Catch NYC, after being a fan of the Las Vegas location, and I'm thrilled to report that it exceeded all expectations. Situated discreetly on 9th Avenue, with the dining area on the second floor and a delightful rooftop terrace above, Catch NYC offers a tranquil escape from the bustling city streets.

The hosts greeted us with warmth and efficiency, leading to us being seated immediately – a testament to Catch's service, given that it's often packed. Pro tip: reservations are a must here.

Service throughout the meal was quick, attentive, yet unobtrusive. Now, let's talk about the star of the show – the food. The vegan crispy cauliflower bites with the addictive spicy sauce were a hit, along with the indulgent truffle fries, perfectly sautéed mushrooms, and the fresh avocado rolls, each dish epitomizing culinary perfection.

The grand finale, the Hit Me Cake, was not just a dessert but an experience, captivating the attention of diners nearby as the waiter expertly poured chocolate sauce over the delectable cake, making for an unforgettable end to a superb dining adventure.

I can't recommend Catch NYC enough and am eagerly anticipating many more dinners there. If you're seeking exceptional seafood and more, Catch is a must-visit!

I ordered the spicy cumin lamb noodles and a friend of mine ordered the spicy pork noodles. While I have a high spice tolerance, I was not prepared for how spicy this dish was. On the one hand, I wouldn't want this dish any other way, but on the other, this dish was so spicy and greasy that it made my stomach hurt and made me tear up a little bit as I ate it.  Very delicious meal and I recommend trying it, but because of the spice and how little meat was given, I don't know if I will be coming back. Please note that you can order a non-spicy version of this dish!

We came here with a reservation at 5 to celebrate new jobs. The interior is dark and dim, much like a speakeasy. It's no wonder the reservations were hard to get because there's very few tables.Russ was wonderful and spoke to us about the menu. He didn't pressure is to get anything and informed us of the different options available and suggested different items based on what we asked about. Our table of four ordered the Corpse Reviver, Perfect Manhattan, Rob Roy, and the Lillet Rose Daisy. Then we ordered the 4 Charles prime rib, brussel sprouts, hamburger, and the fries. For dessert, we ordered the chocolate pie and the lemon meringue pie. The Lillet Rose Daisy is really good. It's light and refreshing. The Rob Roy is enjoyable if you like scotch (which I didn't, but my boyfriend does). The brussel sprouts are amazing! Definitely order that as one of your sides. It's well cooked and comes with thick bacon bits. The 4 Charles Prime Rib is huge. It was tender and juicy. I recommend it if you have a party of 4 or larger. The fries taste similar to McDonald's, but they're thicker. The garlic aioli is good with the fries. The Hamburger is nothing special. Russ gave us a complimentary scoop of ice cream because it was our first time here and we were celebrating. He poured hot fudge over the small scoop of ice cream and suggested we eat the chocolate tart and then have a scoop of ice cream. The chocolate tart is delicious and decadent, but it's definitely something to share because it can get a little too sweet. The lemon meringue is very lemony. Our lemon meringue pie had a fishy taste and my friend mentioned it to Russ to see if that was the norm. Russ told the kitchen and later let us know that the kitchen was glad to know about the problem because they needed to talk to their supplier. He took it off our bill. Overall, the service is amazing. Russ is wonderful and was attentive. The food is good, but I'm not sure I would come back, simply because it's so hard to get a decent reservation.
Is it touristy? Yes. Is it worth it? Yes. 2 fresh mozz slices and a Mexican coke, call it a day. Worth the line (don't worry it moves fast).

Back in 2013, my friend told about this craze in 2013, I didn't get the chance to try so here I am now. Here was my experience on a Friday evening.AMBIANCE:Parking: Street parking but it's Manhattan...good luck.Seating: Pretty limited. All inside, stool seating for maybe 10 people.Feels: Manhattan is Manhattan, not the touristy spot but still a busy spot nonetheless. The shop itself is pretty simple, open space with a New York order and go feel with some nice history decor to it. Great place if you're on the go.FOOD:Artichoke Pizza (Recommend)First and foremost, the portion for $5 was pretty stuffing. This was not your everyday NY pizza. The artichokes were well scattered and the cream was quite savory. The thick crust brought good balance to the cheese.CUSTOMER SERVICE: Super! Quick and polite...boom!TL; DR OVERALL:4 Stars. Delicious pizza, fulfilling and pleasant service. If I need something to fill me up or play tourist here, this would be a good spot. Till next time, Basille!Tips:* The got about 2-3 outlet spots if you need to charge your phone or something.

I'm not a big fan of mexican food but I came here with my gf on friday and I must say their food was worth the wait. We ordered two entries Al pastor (pork quesadilla) and enchiladas verdes. Both meals was very flavorful especially that green sauce that was served with the chicken enchiladas. I will be coming back. Furthermore,  I reccomend this place.  Very reasonable price, music level average,  family friendly placeDo not forget to follow me if you are interested in more descriptive food reviews. Thank you :-)

A Matthew Kenney restaurant serving plant-based dishes that vegans, vegetarians, and meat-eaters alike should try.The portion sizes at Matthew Kenney restaurants and vegan-focused restaurants tend to be on the smaller size. I found that to be true at XYST as well, with a few exceptions. The good thing is that XYST is meant to be enjoyed Tapas style, so you'll get to sample more items. FOOD-Halloumi: I don't really like halloumi but my friends raved about the dish here-Za'atar roasted carrots: Delicious. The pistachio yogurt goes so well with the carrots. I'm convinced that roasted carrots are the new Brussels sprouts-Smoked hummus: Comes with pita bread and vegetables. Very good, and I was pleasantly surprised by the serving size!-Cauliflower: This was surprisingly my favorite dish of the night. It's probably the best cauliflower I had in my life, and it was cooked in a way that hid the cauliflower taste and mushy texture-Wild and cultivated mushrooms: Very goodWe tried a few other dishes, but they were less memorable to me. All in all, everything was delicious and absolutely beautifully plated.DESSERT-Lemon merengue pie: A+-Chocolate cake: A+. The ice cream that goes along with the cake is to die for-Sunflower seed baklava: I would pass on this if you're planning on ordering dessertThe two cocktails I tried were also delicious. The ambiance, decor, and service are all excellent.Don't forget to check out Raines Law Room after your meal next door!

Title: Another Delightful Evening at Coppola's

I recently visited Coppola's for what must be the third or fourth time and, once again, the experience lived up to my fond memories. Our selection for the evening included the chicken parm, Caesar salads, and Pasta Fagioli soup—all of which were exceptional. We also tried the margarita pizza, which, while tasty, didn’t quite meet the high bar set on previous visits.

The ambiance at Coppola's added to our enjoyment. After navigating past the lively bar area and descending into the cozy dining space, you can’t help but feel transported into a scene reminiscent of an old-time Italian eatery, where you might imagine a character like Vito Corleone holding court in a quiet corner.

Service was attentive without being intrusive, ensuring our meals were seamlessly enjoyable. Coppola's has solidified its place on my list of favorites, and I'm already anticipating the next visit with great excitement.

Title: A Thai Delight Not to Be Missed

I recently indulged in the culinary offerings of Chu-Ros Thai and was blown away by the experience. As a first-time patron, I was treated to what I can confidently say was the best Thai food I've savored to date. The flavors in each dish were pronounced and authentic - from the fragrant Kaprow to the classic Pad Thai, down to the crispy Crab Rangoon. Not only were the taste and quality top-notch, but the portions were generous, delivering great value for the price.

The takeout menu deserves a special mention for its aesthetically pleasing design and clarity, making the ordering process a breeze. Chu-Ros Thai gets a hearty thumbs up from me, and it's certainly a recommendation I'll be passing on to my local friends. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next culinary adventure with their menu. Till then, Chu-Ros Thai, thanks for an unforgettable meal. See you again soon!

Title: Eclectic Indian Fusion with a Side of Policy Rigidity

As an enthusiast of Indian cuisine, my expectations were moderate when visiting this establishment. I made a reservation for three but was greeted with a rigid seating policy upon arrival – no seating until the full party arrives. I found this somewhat excessive, especially since the restaurant was empty at the time.

Our dining experience started with naan and chicken kebab accompanied by rice. The portions felt rather petite considering the price point, which might raise eyebrows for those seeking a hearty meal. Flavor-wise, the food strays from traditional Indian fare, leaning more towards an eclectic, fusion twist – an interesting detour but perhaps not for purists.

While the ambiance was elevated by the intriguing decor, the exuberance of the music volume could overshadow table conversations. In short, if you're seeking non-standard Indian food in a lively environment, and don't mind waiting for your company to join before taking a seat, this spot could be worth a visit. However, if you prefer a more conventional menu and a quieter atmosphere, this might not be your first choice.

I recently treated my pizza-enthusiast daughter to America's first-ever pizza joint, and it completely lived up to our expectations. The pizza itself boasted a delectable thin, crispy crust, while the toppings were fresh and flawlessly balanced. Service was impeccable, enhancing our dining experience significantly. The restaurant exuded a charming Little Italy vibe, adding to the authenticity of our visit. For anyone with a passion for pizza and finds themselves in New York, this establishment is an absolute must-visit!

Unfortunately I do not remember how I customized my ramen other than the fact that I opted for firm noodles, and ordered marinated pork loin.I found the pork slices to be dry, and the firm noodles soon tasted milky and overcooked. Food was underwhelming, employees were nice, set up is cool (very self-serve). There was a water dispenser to the side of our booth, and interaction with staff is minimal. Along with the ramen, pork slices, I also ordered matcha iced tea, where they give you individually packed sweetener (syrup) and creamer, and the total was about $30-$35 or so. You do not need to tip.

This is my first Caribbean brunch in a restaurant and I wish there was one in Miami. This place sell off for real! My girls and I are all of Caribbean decent so we have a very high bar to go by, but Miss Lily's exceeded my expectations by far! We had a later reservation but we were able to move up our reso with no problem. I got the jerk chicken roti which honestly blew my mind away, not only because it was huge, it was so full of flavor, not too spicy but not weak sauce at all. The roti was rolled like a burrito but is tastes just like it's from a roti shop. My only critique is that the savory could use some sweet, and I eventually asked for the mango chutney that was served with the jerk chicken dish and it was perfect! If it was served with sweet plantain or the mango chutney, it would be super fire! For the bottomless drinks, I got the rum punch which had be feeling so nice. It definitely creeps up on you but keep in mind the bottomless is only good for an hour and you start as a table. So basically, if you decide you want bottomless and everyone else is half hour in, you can only consume your bottomless for half hour, which seems a little unreasonable. Either way, I loved the decor, I loved the music and the food has me salivating reminiscing on its greatness.

Title: Quick, Delicious, and Excellent Value for Money

I recently dined at this hidden gem of a takeout spot and was thoroughly impressed with the value and efficiency on offer. The service was speedy; I was able to walk in, place my order, and head out within an impressive 5-minute window. Despite the size of the place, which is admittedly quite small, the variety of combos was quite extensive. 

The prices are incredibly reasonable, with just $9.95 being enough to generously satisfy two people – a real bargain for the quality of the typical Chinese fare provided. The taste of the food lived up to expectations; it was delicious and hit the spot for a quick meal on the go. 

An added perk that sweetened the deal was the free drink included with the combo, a gesture of hospitality that didn't go unnoticed. The staff were exceedingly nice, adding to the overall positive experience.

My only gripe, and the reason for a 4-star rating, is the interior, which could do with a bit of a refresh. Sure, it's just a to-go restaurant, but a more inviting environment could enhance the customer experience significantly.

One important note for prospective diners: this establishment operates on a cash-only basis! Make sure to stop by an ATM before you go. But if you're looking for quick service, great food, and exceptional value, this is the place to be. Thank you for a pleasant experience!

Title: Perfect for a Business Dinner

My recent dining experience was truly enjoyable. The service received was exceptional, attentive without being intrusive. Our meal was a delight; both the branzino and the ribeye steak were cooked to perfection, boasting rich flavors that are sure to satisfy any palate.

While the atmosphere of the restaurant was rather standard, lacking distinctive character, it provided a suitable backdrop for professional conversations, making it an ideal venue for a business dinner. While perhaps not the quintessential setting for a romantic evening, the quality of the food and the excellence of the service more than compensate.

In conclusion, I would heartily recommend this restaurant to colleagues and professionals looking for a place to dine and discuss. The delectable branzino and ribeye steak are must-tries.

Went here because we had a food coupon we didn't want to waste. Went around 11 in the morning so their breakfast counter was shut. The place is okay with a buffet area and made to order counters that are open at different times. They seem to have little bit of every cuisine. The food counters are okay price wise but the buffet and on the go items are a total rip off ($3 for a cup of yogurt? , no thank you!). Ordered the scrambled eggs with toast, instead got an omelette (too lazy to scramble 'em eggs bro?). The buffet items were heated with steam from the bottom so basically they were barely warm. Some tables weren't clean and the floor definitely needed some cleaning. I'd say breakfast is the only worthwhile time to go here. Avoid otherwise.

Was craving pizza... craving satisfied. We got the prosciutto one. Love the tender but chewy crust and the prosciutto on the pizza was 100. Also had burrata which was super creamy and yummy w the delicata squash and hazelnuts. Not the place to go if you're craving a New York slice but if youre Pasquale jonesin' for the good stuff, it's the joint.

Ordered takeout for lunch. I ordered the roasted salmon with cauliflower and sweet potato sides. Everything was absolutely delicious, the veggies were actually roasted! Nothing I hate more than when they don't roast the veggies properly. It was such a healthy and refreshing lunch. Their entire menu looks delicious and healthy, I will be back for sure to try some other dishes!!

Maybe it was me but I was waiting for a bit before I was asked to order. The staff seemed busy conversations with each other. I will say however, the dumplings were absolutely amazing. I got an order of steamed dumplings as well as fried dumplings and was absolutely amazed at the authenticity in the taste of them.

Title: Cozy Ambiance and Attentive Service for a Private Party

I recently organized a private party at a charming restaurant, which on the whole provided a commendable experience. When scheduling the event, the coordination process was seamless and pleasantly deposit-free. Although a slight hiccup occurred with a change in staff, a confirmation call prior to the event helped to iron out any wrinkles.

Upon arrival, the initial confusion among the staff gave the impression of a simple large table booking rather than a private event. However, the rustic upstairs room allocated for our gathering set a nice atmosphere. There was a minor oversight with the menus, but once I flagged this, the staff promptly replaced them with the special ones we'd arranged.

Service was the highlight of the evening—our sole waiter was exceptional, despite evidently managing multiple responsibilities. The food was another high note, with the branzino and chicken Park receiving particular praise from guests. Dessert was made extra special with the day manager's presentation and a lively round of singing.

For a party of 16, including drinks and built-in gratuity, the bill slightly exceeded $1,000. Considering the quality of service, I felt compelled to tip our waiter additionally. Overall, the experience was good—cozy ambiance, attentive service, and tasty food—though not without room for improvement in organizational communication.

Our main reason for visiting NYC was to visit Mercado Little Spain! We have been fans of Jose Andres, Albert Adria, and Ferran Adria for a long time. We've also been fortunate to dine at The in Miami and most recently Enigma in Barcelona Spain.When I heard about the opening of Mercado Little Spain I badly wanted to attend but scheduling wouldn't allow it. Finally, we were in line to enter the space. The staff welcomed us in with wide smiles and while not every area was open yet our visit was so worth it!Walking around the space we read the menus, watched the chefs cook, and tried to decide how we were going to control ourselves after our big lunch. My one disappointment is there isn't enough seating for the kiosk vibe. We first walked around holding our food looking for space and finally ended up standing and using a countertop.Our first selections were patatas bravas (potatoes with a spicy sauce and aioli), Iberico de Belotta jamon, and a Coca (a type of flat bread). The patatas bravas were good, you can never go wrong with Iberico jamon, and the Coca was surprisingly satisfying! After a long wait, we also enjoyed a Vermut each (blanco) along with the most amazing Paella! The paella was deep in flavor, the meat tender, and the rice well cooked. The only bit missing was a crunch from rice at the bottom of the pan.Before leaving for the night, we purchased somechurros and chocolate to enjoy back at the hotel after we walked off some of the food! They were amazing and addictive!I can't even begin to tell you how badly I want to visit again and try out their newly opened restaurants as well as some of the kiosks we enjoyed!

Rice Noodles Rolls + Congee, two of my absolute favorite food! Note: Cash only!First East Cost location for a Guangzhou, China chain so there is oftentimes a queue outside! STICKY RICE WRAPS ($4.95): Classic dim sum dish! Sticky rice stuffed with mushroom and meat wrapped with lotus leaf! Very hearty for a cold fall night. MARINADED PORK & SHRIMP WITH CHIVES RICE NOODLE ROLL ($6.95): Love the big pieces of shrimp and pork within. This place does not skimp on any of the ingredients. A great rice noodle roll for me is the balance of ingredients with the pillow-soft thin rice noodle. Would recommend!MARINADED PORK & BEEF WITH CHIVES RICE NOODLE ROLL ($6.95): Big pieces of both pork and beef! Definitely a meat lover's choice!LAI WAN STYLE ASSORTED CONGEE ($5.95): Made with white fish fillet, squid, pork skin, topped with ginger slivers, cilantro, crispy vermicelli noodles, and egg slivers. I love the variety of ingredients, but kind of miss the thicker and creamier/cotton-y of other rice porridges I have had. Just to note this is the quick boil version!FRESH BEEF SLICED CONGEE ($5.50): Large beef pieces quick boiled with congee topped with cilantro! The portions here are quite big! I recommend sharing the congee. The service here is very quick and super friendly! Will come back to try other dishes!

Super chic decor, nestled in an unexpected but great central location. Didn't know it was here but am super happy to have found it! The bottomless brunch special is absolutely worth it! The food came quickly, the California bowl was great and the juices for the bottomless mimosas were delicious. Just what I was hoping for out of this spot and will absolutely be back!

During a recent visit to a local spot with my roommate, we were enveloped by the comforting embrace of Chinese cuisine. Our table featured a spread of Garlic Pork Dumplings, Shredded Cabbage, Braised Beef Noodle Soup, and Dan Dan Noodles.

The dumplings, tender with a delightful texture, were topped with crispy garlic chips that harked back to soup dumplings. Meanwhile, the shredded cabbage, tender and generous in portion, carried a subtle heat from chilies that hit the spot for someone who adores Chinese-style cabbage.

A pleasant surprise was the Braised Beef Noodle Soup, a dish recommended over my initial oxtail soup choice. Its broth was rich and spicy, complementing the chewy noodles and sizable portion. A jammy egg accompanied the dish, though it didn't seem to add much—perhaps a better fit for ramen.

The Dan Dan Noodles, however, strayed from tradition with a peanut butter-like sauce, a departure that didn't quite meet our expectations.

Service was attentive and efficient, ensuring a smooth dining experience. Drink pricing was fair, but a note on presentation: serving sake in a stained masu cup used as a pen holder added confusion rather than authenticity.

Despite the minor setbacks, the experience was positive enough to warrant a return for another round of noodles.

Amazing food. Amazing cocktails and drink menu. I don't even live on the east coast anymore, but when I come back to visit NY, this is a must-go-to stop.I think I've had nearly everything on the menu - wings, grilled caesar salad, coconut curry mussels, pickles, oysters - but my fave is the chicken liver bacon sandwich. I literally miss and crave this sandwich all the time.

I came here with a friend for brunch/ lunch to celebrate her birthday. I do think the place has done a good job with ambenice, upscale hipster is the way i would define it. Dark walls, and plants and some design work, as well as a good amount of woodwork on the bar. We sat in the front and Will, our server, was really great, explaining the menu, giving us drink options and getting us the window seat. I just walked in on a Sunday at about 2 and was seated immediately. We had the ginger tamarind drink but they made it into a mimosa for us, which was delicious. We asked for the side of rice (under the market bowls in the menu) which comes as a little box of sticky rice and some eggplant and spicy sauce on the side. Not super interesting. But the fried rice with eggs and sweet sausage was delicious and the market bowl was great too, lots of fresh ingredients, interesting pickles and the portions were large too. We were pretty full and managed to take home some of the fried rice. Total bill was $66 for both of us and the drinks. Overall, great staff, service and fresh good food. I will be back to try the dinner menu.

Title: A Serendipitous Culinary Adventure at Estela

Last night, my friends and I stumbled upon Estela after our original dining plans fell through. At first glance, the restaurant’s unassuming location nearly had us walking by, but what a miss that would have been!

Despite our late arrival past 10pm and the lack of reservations, the staff at Estela welcomed us with open arms and seated us immediately. As tapas novices, we were initially perplexed by the exotic menu, but our savior, Fred, was right on cue. Not only did he demystify the selection, but his warm demeanor and personal engagement added a special touch to our last evening in New York.

The culinary journey was sensational, from the succulent Mussels on toast to the flavorful Lamb ribs and the delicate Ricotta dumplings. Every dish outdid the previous one, leaving our taste buds in sheer bliss.

Fred's recommendation to not skip dessert was the cherry on top — the Sweet potato with Vanilla ice cream and Rum was an unparalleled favorite, edging out the scrumptious Chocolate cake.

In all, Estela was more than just a meal; it was a remarkable experience that capped our trip perfectly. I wish I could award extra stars for the impeccable food and service. We've already planned a return visit next time we're in the city. An absolute must-try!

Recently, I dined at Ugly Kitchen with a small group, hoping to savor flavors that matched its strong reputation within the Filipino culinary scene. Sadly, the experience fell short of expectations given the steep prices. Our 6:30pm reservation on a Thursday found the place quiet, but as the night progressed, the increasing crowd and blaring music disrupted the ambiance.

The extensive menu was promising, and our family-style approach led us to a variety of dishes: Seasoned Frites, Fried Spring Rolls, Ugly Wings, Adobo Ribs, Bistek, several Adobo dishes, and more. The Fried Spring Rolls and Ugly Wings were delightful hits, and the Adobo Ribs stood out, the meat succulent and well-seasoned. However, the Bistek, Chicken Adobo, and Sisig were merely passable, particularly the Sisig, which lacked the captivating flavor I eagerly anticipate.

A significant disappointment was the Fried Isaw, a poor substitute for the unavailable Chicharon Bulaklak, which brought a gamey taste not to our liking. Despite these culinary missteps, the service was a highlight, with prompt delivery and a friendly waitress.

In summation, Ugly Kitchen offers a warm service but requires more zest or innovation in their offerings to justify their prices and to truly distinguish themselves amongst the diverse Filipino eateries I've frequented.

Title: Cozy Comfort at Emmy Squared, East Village

After a revitalizing workout, my friend and I ventured into the bustling East Village for a bite, landing at the popular Emmy Squared on a busy Friday night. Despite the daunting hour-long wait for a table, we managed to snag seats at the bar, a convenient spot offering the full mouthwatering menu.

The cocktail of choice was "With Love From Emily" – a robust yet invigorating concoction that set the tone for an enjoyable meal. Our shared spread included roasted cauliflower, okonomi fries, and the standout Vodka pizza. Service didn't miss a beat; dishes arrived promptly and did not disappoint.

The pizza, with its perfectly crispy crust, was a slice of heaven – highly recommended. While the okonomi fries presented a unique twist, the abundance of sauce slightly overshadowed their crispiness. However, the cauliflower maintained its own, offering another layer of rich flavor to our meal.

Emmy Squared delivered a delightful dining experience with its blend of unique and comforting dishes in a snug setting ideal for friends or a romantic evening. I'm eagerly anticipating visits to their other locations for more culinary discoveries.

I had a great experience at Pig Heaven. When I walked in with my sister I was so excited to try this Sichuan Chinese spot because I heard great things about it. The staff was lovely and the décor of the restaurant was the cutest thing ever! On the wall there was pink pigs with messages written for people saying how much they liked the food. I couldn't help to notice that this is also, a family friendly restaurant as I saw a couple of families eating dinner while I was there eating with my sister. My sister and I tried the soup dumpling which was our first time trying it and it was super flavorful and juicy. The waiter recommended it to us because that's one of their most popular appetizers and I am so glad I went with that option. As entrée we had the Spare ribs and the eggplant and chicken with garlic sauce. Both plates were delicious specially the spare ribs. They do give a generous amount of food which I loved because I took my leftovers home.

Title: Cozy Brunch Haven 

It's hard to believe I only just discovered this gem of a restaurant. My brunch experience here was nothing short of excellent. Despite not having made a reservation on a chilly winter day, we were promptly seated in the inviting dining room. Our server was an absolute delight, enhancing the whole experience with their charm. 

To kick off our meal, we were treated to complimentary sparkling water—a refreshing touch. The Croque Madam with Chicken was a masterful twist on a classic, perfectly executed and simply delicious. Then there was the Nutella Banana French Toast, a divine concoction that transported my taste buds to heaven.

In short, this place is a must-visit for anyone in search of delectable brunch fare served with a smile. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Love tha ambiance of this modern Korean fare.  Reserve thru Yelp so we did not wait.  We sat in the back near the kitchen it is a tad bit more quiet.  We ordered 5 dishes for the two of us.  We had a tempura based roll with an aioli.  Then a soft shell crab deep fried with home made tartar and a hint of truffle oil.  Then we had a bulgogi stone bowl followed by a crispy fried chicken bun and lastly their homemade vegetarian dumplings.  Highlights were the soft shell and the chicken bao. The sauce on and texture of the bao made the dish.  The soft shell crab I would order it again then had a way to keep it crunchy without getting soggy.Sorry for the lack of pics - was really hungry!

I'm being a little forgiving on this review due to only going here because of the name of the place and then only could fit it in for breakfast, which they're probably not known for.The decor was very cool and feels like your dropped into part of Ireland for a moment. I would love to be able to go back and try their lunch/dinner meals. Food a 3, design and decor a 5.

Title: Serenity Found at Midtown East Tea Room

In the bustling heart of Midtown East, we discovered an oasis of tranquility: a charming tea room offering respite from the city's feverish pace. Our visit was initially prompted by the impressive tea assortment, and we delightedly settled on the Jasmine Silver Needle, which generously yielded 4-5 cups per person.

Our culinary journey included dim sum delights like the Scallion Pancake, which was freshly prepared yet slightly marred by excess oil. The Crystal Shrimp Dumplings' thick wrapper overshadowed the delicate shrimp within, but the Soupy Pork Buns emerged as a dim sum favorite with their savory taste. The standout dish was the Braised Dongpo Pork, a delectably tender revelation beautifully complemented by Pu'er tea.

Adding to the experience, the tea room's decor was an enchanting backdrop—adorned with an array of teas and teapots and set to the tune of traditional music. An unexpected dimming of lights at 1PM added a touch of magic, casting the space in a soft, inviting glow.

This peaceful nook is a haven I eagerly look forward to revisiting for another tranquil lunch retreat.

I had a delightful experience at this restaurant, where the Italian cuisine truly shone. Each dish was exceptional, brimming with heart and authentic flavors that transported me to Italy itself. The service matched the high quality of the food, with attentive and courteous staff ensuring a memorable dining experience. This restaurant is a must-visit for anyone looking for genuine, hearty Italian fare. Highly recommended!

Well the space is the same yet so much has changed. It's been a number of years since I last dined here, however I was hoping to return to the same 5 star quality. Unfortunately this evening was a disappointment in more ways than one. We came here as a party of 4 in celebration of a friend's bday. We all has decided on the 4 course tasting & ordered our first bottle of opus for the table. The amuse bounce was really not tasty, bad way to begin a dining experience.  Everyone's apps were tasty, no complaints. The pasta dishes were really small, the men at the table were left a bit underserved. The waiter mixed flat water with sparking in the same glass. The bread was stale.  The main courses at the table had absolutely no wow factor, we all ordered different things & everyone was underwhelmed. Dessert was also just meh...nothing to brag about. For a Michelin rated restaurant there were many mistakes made. I will not return & it's a shame because I held this restaurant in such high regard from years ago.

Title: A Diner with a Show on Broadway

Last night's winding line intrigued us into trying this Broadway gem at 51st, promising a lively late lunch with a twist. Despite the sleet, we took our chances in a 25-minute line for an experience unlike any other: a meal served by Broadway hopefuls.

The waitstaff, all budding musical theatre artists, entertained us with powerful vocals and elaborate performances. They juggled serving duties with an infectious energy, supported by a bustling team behind the scenes. The emcee kept spirits high, weaving humor into the afternoon and encouraging donations to a scholarship fund benefiting the servers' artistic pursuits.

Once inside, we were treated to a 25-minute musical serenade before our comfort food—diner classics like meatloaf and quiche—arrived, well worth the wait. The place roared with laughter, singalongs, and contented diners enjoying hearty dishes and optional drinks.

The ambiance is simple, loud, and lively, not the spot for a quiet dinner or undivided service attention. Yet, it compensates with its unique energy and supportive staff.

While I might not be a regular here, the experience was singularly enjoyable, a one-off that I'm glad to have not missed.

Title: Authentic Szechuan Delights with Generous Servings

I recently discovered a gem for Szechuan cuisine cravings that I had been unable to satisfy elsewhere in the area! The true tests of authenticity for me are the minced pork with cellophane noodles and Chongqing Chicken. This restaurant nailed both dishes, with the noodles being particularly addictive - a must-try for any enthusiast.

Accompanying our meal were perfectly cooked white rice, scallion pancakes that managed to win over my picky toddler, and a very good chicken fried rice. The only letdown was the pork soup dumplings, which unfortunately lacked the signature soup element, but were tasty nonetheless.

Portion sizes were impressively generous, ensuring a satisfying meal with plenty of leftovers. Although the photo I snapped after our feast doesn't do justice to the actual serving sizes, it's proof of the thoroughly enjoyable culinary experience we had.

I recently dined at a gem of a spot that I'll certainly be returning to on my next trip to New York. The Roti Canai proved to be a delightful appetizer, perfectly shareable between two. Yet, it was the Ultimate Curry Laksa that stole my heart. This crave-worthy dish is a symphony of flavors with its aromatic curry and perfectly cooked noodles. The addition of fish balls, tofu, and cucumber elevates it to a must-try noodle soup. I can't recommend this place enough and only wish they had a location closer to me!

Whether for a glass of wine or a classic cocktail or a late night snack or a full meal, Grand Bar is always there to fill the need. Not necessarily the best food or drinks in Soho, but extremely consistent and reliable. Convenience means a lot and being on the second floor of the Soho Grand Hotel makes it extremely convenient. Always reliable.

Absolutely charmed by this delightful dining spot! The service was nothing short of sweet, and it's evident that love goes into every homemade dish. A bonus for wine lovers - it's a BYOB establishment with no corkage fee! The incredible music playing added to a truly enchanting atmosphere. How could anyone not adore this place? Highly recommended.

New Years usually calls for a special dinner, and so my boyfriend said, "a Michelin star restaurant it is!" And instead of visiting a new restaurant, we decided to visit a restaurant we KNEW would serve delicious food (as he's visited before). Uncle Boons it was!We ordered the green mango salad, chicken curry with noodles, and the lobster special. I usually see green papaya salad on Thai menus, so seeing green mango salad instead was an interesting (but seemingly delicious) dish, and sure enough, I was not let down. The mango was perfectly in between not ripe and ripe, flavorsome, and EXTREMELY saucy  the crispy fried squid made the dish all the more better by adding texture and flavor that balanced the sweet and tangy flavor from the mango. The chicken curry with noodles came with both crispy/fried noodles and soup/saucy noodles, elevated the dish even more. In addition to that, I'm a HUGE fan of coconut milk in curry, and this really hit the spot! The dish had the perfect amount of spiciness contrasted with sweet coconut milk. The lobster dish was $38 and, unfortunately, was the only dish that wasn't on par with the rest. It was slightly overcooked, so instead of being juicy tender, it was a tad rubbery. It was a let down, but it definitely didn't ruin our dinner experience. And as a treat to ourselves, we ordered some drinks, but the one we both loved was the Golden Tiger Ya Dong shots. It was sweet and subtly floral. We didn't think the pineapple chasers were needed 11/10 would visit again for the shots alone

I recently dined at a local gem where the hype is absolutely justified – the queue outside is a staple for a reason. The soup dumplings and buns definitely hit the spot, yet it’s the scallion pancake with sliced beef that steals the show for me. It's the dish that keeps me coming back time and again; it’s simply sublime. A friendly tip for fellow food enthusiasts: opt for this location over the one near Port Authority – the quality and experience here are unmatched.

Title: A Burger to Remember

I recently succumbed to a burger craving and thanks to Yelp stumbled upon a gem of a find. This spot ticked all the boxes for an impromptu meal during my vacation. It boasts a charming ambiance with a cozy bar and eclectic art setting the mood perfectly.

The staff was welcoming from the get-go with the bartender offering a warm reception. When it came to choosing a burger from their extensive and tantalizing menu, I opted for the one with maple bacon bourbon sauce, bacon, and Brie cheese, paired with a side of fries.

This burger was nothing short of spectacular: perfectly medium-cooked, tender, and the flavors were a delectable fusion of salty-sweet goodness, all nestled between soft, fresh buns. The fries were the ideal accompaniment, crispy and fresh from the fryer.

My companion’s salad was a basic affair but satisfactory to them. While I'd personally skip the salad, for burger aficionados, this place is a must-visit. Can't shake off that burger craving? Do yourself a favor and head here!

Title: A Delightful Surprise at Elite - New Gem in Williamsburg

As a newcomer to the bustling Williamsburg scene, Elite truly exceeds expectations, particularly in the realm of hospitality. From our first step through the door, the manager's warm greeting and choice seating by the window set a welcoming tone for the evening.

Generosity was on display as we were promptly offered complimentary chips and a delightful duo of frozen and piña colada shots, which were nothing short of spectacular. Although our visit was limited to drinks following an earlier dinner, the tempting variety and affordability of the menu items have certainly left us eager to return for a full dining experience.

Elite's interior sports a chic modern aesthetic complemented perfectly by an upbeat music selection, creating an inviting atmosphere. While we didn’t venture into the downstairs club area, which was quiet at the time, it's easy to imagine it bustling as summer approaches.

The drink selection is impressive as well, catering to a wide range of preferences with creative and delectable options - ensuring a refreshing experience for cocktail enthusiasts.

In conclusion, Elite is a promising spot that I’m looking forward to revisiting soon. Whether you’re in the area for a drink or a meal, Elite promises not to disappoint.

So sad that this place has not been open during COVID, but withdrawal reminded me of the many delicious meals I have had at Amura!  This is my go-to sushi spot on the UES for either take-out or dine-in. Food is reliably fresh with quick deliveries and service. Looove the salmon tartar and all the nigiri. The Truffle Toro Roll is my favorite roll and worth every penny!

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Suprema

If you're ever in NYC craving pizza perfection, make a beeline for Suprema, a gem nestled beside Penn Station. During a recent visit before our train to Baltimore, I had the pleasure of devouring two large slices from their menu—and let me tell you, I instantly regretted not indulging in an entire pie.

We settled on the Sicilian with sausage and an innovative honey ricotta slice. Each boasted a superbly crunchy thin crust without a hint of excess oil or grease. The tomato sauce on the Sicilian delivered a flawless balance of tartness and acidity. But the star of the show was undoubtedly the honey ricotta: impeccably whipped, laden with the right touch of garlic, it was heavenly.

The experience was so outstanding that it overshadowed the usual NYC landmarks in my memory. Suprema's pizza left such an impression that I am genuinely considering another visit to the city just for another taste. A word to the wise: bring cash, as this spot doesn't take cards. Trust me, it's absolutely worth the trip—and every penny.

Title: Still Aboard on the NYC Lobster Boat Experience

Returning to NYC, I couldn't resist revisiting my favorite lobster boat – an experience worth every bit of its charm. Despite the new $10 boarding fee, collected at the dock before receiving a wristband from the welcoming crew, the venture remains a must-do.

Aboard, I indulged in a crisp glass of white wine and savored a generously stuffed lobster roll. Addressing the fee with a manager, I understood it's a nod to inevitable inflation and rising overheads – a fair point in the bustling cityscape, even if it subsidizes those who enjoy the sail sans dining.

And though it's a slight bummer to see passengers not partaking in the boat's culinary offerings, the experience is still valuable. The boat ride alone elsewhere could cost over $25, yet here it includes the potential for delightful fare. In a kind gesture, I was even treated to a complimentary glass of wine.

I wholeheartedly recommend this unique adventure. The lobster roll? Simply delicious.

Dined at this beautiful, spacious restaurant and had a delightful experience. The waitress stood out with her kindness and helpfulness, although I regret not getting her name. Our drinks were strong yet amazing, complementing the great food perfectly. The place was not only big but also spotlessly clean. My friends and I absolutely loved it and would heartily recommend it to others.

Hit Hillstone this week for a friends birthday and boy was it a movie and a half. Everybody knows hillstone / Houston's is the best restaurant group under our sun so were fired up going in. Hospitality was electric when Michelle greeted us and took our drink orders. After sitting down, vibes took a brief dip since our waitress didn't come close to being as friendly and pleasant as Michelle but we overcame quickly by our order tactics. Right off the bat, beers and crisp martinis. One of the best martinis ever, truly. Next up Spinach artichoke dip (not gluten free but yolo), spicy tuna roll, spicy tuna Osaka roll, and another spicy tuna roll for good measure because it was that crazy. Next up, peanut chicken salad. Truly lethal and unbeatable. Fries for the table with those beautiful dips pictured here. And I dug into Dave's burger (sans bun) which was crazy. Along the way we had multiple crisptinis and topped it off with some of the best espresso martinis New York has ever seen. We got a little vanilla bean ice cream scoop action at the end from the waitress which was like a 6 out of 10 on the hospitality scale but I'll take it. ALSO when they kept changing glasses for a clean glass when we were halfway thru martinis that was incredible. Looking forward to many more Hillstone experiences. Bless

I arrived at Black Tap with high expectations, lured in by the viral images of their indulgent milkshakes. Unfortunately, the experience didn't live up to the hype. I opted for the much-raved-about cake shake; while the presentation was Instagram-worthy, the flavor was just satisfactory. Both the shake and the cake perched on top were decent, but neither struck a memorable chord. On a brighter note, the fried pickles ordered by my companion were outstanding – a crispy, tangy delight that salvaged the visit. In the end, Black Tap felt more like a social media sensation than a culinary triumph.
I picked up from here using the Ritual app. I tried their BBQ pork noodles which was ok. The noodle was blah and the pieces of pork was not well cooked. I might try something else someday.

Got the small appetizer with hummus, baba ganoush, toasted eggplant and tzatizki and they were so good along with the Turkish bread. Got the combination platter with lamb kebab and lamb Adana and they were delicious too. A lot of rice but it was tasty

On a Sunday evening, I visited this restaurant, which boasts an old-school charm but unfortunately also features cramped seating. Despite the place not being busy, our request to move to an empty booth was denied due to reservations – though only one group ended up using the booths during our stay.

The menu is on the pricey side, which might reflect the high rent for its location. The food quality was impressive, particularly the jerk corn, which was a delightful highlight. As for the drinks, while tasty, they were made with soju, resulting in a less potent alcoholic experience that didn't seem to match the cost, echoing more of a premium juice than a spirited beverage.

Service was average, with nothing noteworthy to mention. While the culinary offerings were enjoyable – especially the corn that had my taste buds dancing – the combination of the seating situation, drink potency, and price point leaves me uncertain about a return visit.

Title: A Cozy Moroccan Gem near Metropolitan Hospital

I was pleasantly surprised to stumble upon this Moroccan haven amidst my work visits to Metropolitan Hospital. Although I tried visiting their website, it seems to be down; you can still get a glimpse of their offerings on Seamless, albeit at a slightly higher price point.

My visit, which was a while back around March or April, left a lasting impression. The restaurant itself is charming and quaint, with a staff that exudes warmth and hospitality.

My choice was their Couscous, a delightful mix of steamed semolina grain and a medley of vegetables like carrots, sweet potatoes, pumpkin, zucchini, cabbage, and the sweet touch of caramelized onion and raisin. Opting for the Kofta kebab add-on for an extra $4 was a wise decision — the meat was well-spiced and complemented the dish beautifully. As for the hummus and pita, they were satisfactory, though I can't recall if they were part of a special.

The couscous was on the sweeter side, as is typical for Moroccan cuisine, but not overwhelmingly so. The balance of flavors and tender vegetables blended nicely, making for a satisfying meal.

In conclusion, this local spot is a delightful find with its good food and inviting atmosphere. I'd rate it a 3.7 out of 5 — worth a visit if you're in the area.

My boyfriend and I dined here to celebrate his birthday and it was definitely a great choice! Hatsuhana may be a more upscale Japanese restaurant, but its overall presentation evokes comfort and understated elegance. The din of the restaurant is tolerable for conversation, and service is impeccable yet unintrusive. I liked the fact that the two of us were seated in an alcove by the back of the restaurant, making for a more intimate dinner. We had both planned on getting the Box of Dreams, Hatsuhana's star dish. I was tempted but I decided that it was way too much fish for me and I wanted to enjoy everything fresh. We both ordered the Kaisen Chirashi which contained an assortment of fish, including white tuna, salmon, masago, tuna, and clam. I was pleasantly surprised that the chirashi was a 2 tier dish.It was very filling! I loved the amaebi, the salmon, and the uni, but all the fish has that melt-in-your mouth texture that speaks of its freshness and superb quality. The meal was on the pricier side, but the high prices are justified given the quality. I now understand why so many people love to dine her.

I recently dined at Soba Totto and left underwhelmed by the experience. The soba itself was unremarkable, and with the recent change in management, the noticeable reduction in portion sizes was disappointing. Given the abundance of superior Japanese dining options nearby, I'm hesitant to return to Soba Totto unless prompted by strong recommendations from friends.
Your typical late night spot! $6 for tots! the Wolfnight sauce was yummy! But we enjoyed the mix of chipotle with ketchup even more! I will return when I get the tots craving again!

I recently dined at Uncle Boons for dinner and overall, I was pleased with the experience. Securing a 5:30pm reservation was a stroke of luck, as the place primarily accommodates walk-ins and was bustling by the time we departed. Despite the frigid sub-15F weather, diners eagerly queued outside.

The ambiance is cozy, with a small, dimly-lit space that extends from the front area to additional seating along a narrow back corridor. Although the service was a tad slow, our waitress was upfront about the kitchen's pace due to its size, which set our expectations appropriately.

As for the food, highlights include the Kai Luek Keuy (Son in Law Egg), which earned a decent 3/5 for its perfectly runny yolk, though the tamarind sauce was too sweet for my liking. The Plaa Hoi Shenn (Raw Chilled Sea Scallops) and Hoi Tak (Green Curry Snails), both scoring 4/5, were remarkable for their fresh flavors and textural finesse, with the latter's curry sauce making an excellent pairing with the side of roti. The Yum Mamoung (Green Mango Salad) brought a refreshing tartness to our shared plates, also meriting a 4/5.
