However, the Khao Soi Kaa Kai, a vegetarian golden curry, fell a little short at 3/5 due to its somewhat mushy egg noodles and a lack of depth. The standout dish, without a doubt, was the Kao Pat Puu (Crab Fried Rice), a well-executed 5/5 with perfectly fried rice and generous amounts of crab.

Ending on a weaker note, the Squash with Custard and Brulee scored a 2.5/5. While intriguing, the dish wasn't to my taste, particularly due to my aversion to gourds, despite the custard and brulee being adequately sweet.

In conclusion, Uncle Boons delivered a good dining experience with flavorful and intriguing food that largely compensated for the less-than-stellar service. I'd certainly consider returning, provided I could secure another table.

Pretty things never taste good.  we only tried the desserts, and even though they were pretty, we were pretty disappointed. The mango shaped geometric dessert did not taste very mango and just didn't taste very good in general (although it did look pretty realistic). The cotton candy dessert was cake and ice cream topped with cream, berries, and cotton candy. It tasted like normal cake and store bought ice cream, something I can just make at home (it just won't look as pretty). The drink was refreshing, but it just tasted like flavored soda. There was a lot of detail put into the presentation, like the flower in each of the ice cubes and all the fruit in it to make it colorful, but it just wasn't good all together. It wasn't expensive, about $50-60 for 3 things after tax and tip, but it just didn't taste good. I think I can find other places with pretty and yummy food in New York, so I wouldn't come back. The outside of the restaurant is a cafe where they sell desserts and flowers. The inside is the sit down part, which wasn't very busy for a Saturday afternoon. The back also had a chair with flowers for you to take photos, but it wasn't that Instagram worthy of a spot.

horrible horrible horrible!!! customer service, hazardous environment and also nasty food.we ordered beef busut jungol (beef and mushroom soup) which costs about $52 and ended getting less than 100g of FATTY beef brisket and mushroom that they did not even wash or cut properly. my jaw dropped. I asked the waitress (ajumma - whoever worked downstairs on 8/12 around 18:00pm had a nasty attitude, she was the only waitress) if this is what we are really getting for $52 and she literally said "so what do you want me to do?"we told waiter Lee who also had a massive attitude we did not want the food which was basically inedible. He took it without saying anything and slammed the pot on the other table. seriously?also, I have been here a multiple times and my friends always said people (hispanic workers) from the kitchen used the bathroom with customers and they NEVER washed their hands. so disgusting.I hope you do not waste your time and money here and go somewhere else like her name is han or cho dang gol. I am still so upset about waiter and waitress's attitude. never apologized about what happened or for the quality of food. what kind of restaurant is this? (jin jja service gurigo, food gurigo. jang sa e rut ke ha ji map si da!!!!!)

Ramen is amazing here!! Tried the famous Bone marrow ramen and it lives up to it's hype...the bone broth and the tender beef just melts with every bite. The three way wings were really tender and juicy, it's crisp and just delectable.

The food was delicious and the recommendations the bar tender gave me were spot on so 5/5 there but the wait staff was not as good. He was kind, friendly and attentive even on a busy evening  The girl got me butter but no bread even though my first course had arrived and I had to ask for more bread, she didn't check in to see if I wanted more - it was a very busy evening so I understand but something one improve on.The food was 5/5 and I especially enjoy the creativity when it comes to vegetarian cuisine!

Definitely giving this place 5 stars. The workers were very friendly and overall it's a small and cute place that you can a bunch of snacks at. I got the stuffing and two cookies and it came out to $5 which honestly isn't bad.  I ate the stuffing and a Peanut Butter Hozon cookie. The stuffing was interesting to say the least. I don't think I'd get it again but I'm glad I tried it. It was kinda of like a grilled cheese with hot dog and jalapeño in a cup with a Crispy top to it. I do recommend, it's honestly not bad. Originally I wanted the Chicken Katsu sandwich but they were all out. The peanut butter cookie was really good though, if you like them especially. It was soft and chewy and hit the spot. Peach Mart is located on the 5th floor of the Hudson Yards mall.

Cash only!!! Make sure to bring cash!I ordered a meatlovers pizza which had sausage and pepperoni on it. It was so good! The pepperoni had just the right amount of crisp to it and the pizza was so incredibly juicy!! It was huge! The slice itself was $6 which is pretty expensive but it seems worth the hype to at least try once!

Nestled inconspicuously between two Korean eateries, this basement-level restaurant is a hidden gem in the heart of the city. A narrow doorway ushers you into its young and hip atmosphere, which compensates for the lack of cell service.

Upon my early Sunday evening visit, I was delighted by the swift seating despite a full house, a testament to their efficiency. Future patrons take note: arrive early to avoid long wait times.

The culinary experience was exceptional. We indulged in the Kimchi Cream Udon, a creamy fusion delight that reinvents comfort food with a Korean twist. The Tuna Tataki served as a delectable appetizer, though small in size, it didn't skimp on flavor.

A standout was the Mew Special Roll, a spicy salmon and avocado combination, enfolded in seared salmon and crowned with a drizzle of mayo—an absolute must.

Our appetite failed us before we could try the Omu Soba, but it's on the list for next time. This dine-out has easily topped the charts as my favorite meal from my recent NYC trip.

We ended up here because I love pizza and my two daughters are GF. We needed a place with quality GF options (not just a salad) and we came across this spot. It was only a few blocks from our hotel. I admit - I expected mediocre pizza. It was not. My girls said the GF was the best they have ever had and they have tasted a lot. My wife and I had had a regular pizza and it was incredible. It was all so good we returned the next day for lunch. On the second trip I also had a salad, which was simple but very good. The service was great. Everyone was friendly and they were constantly checking in. The beer list is limited, but I'm used the CA where pizza places had 10+ craft beers on tap. I splurged on the $16 pink pepper IPA from Italy. It was very good. Worth $16?  That all relative I guess. I was on vacation and I enjoyed it so no complaints. I wouldn't order it all the time at home. The location is small and cozy, but in a good comfortable way. Definitely go here, especially if you are seeking out GF options.

Double Zero has a creative take on vegan pizza and great space in the East Village. We got the tomato, basil, cashew cheese pizza and the farro-fennel sausage, tomato, cashew cheese pizza. Both were delicious, but the farro-fennel was my favorite because it had more flavor. The wait staff was friendly and we were quickly seated outside. I'm glad they opened a spot in LA because I want to try the rest of the pizzas!

I was not expecting a lot, at 9pm after a long day, but was pleasantly surprised. The food was quick and excellent, with a big portion.Be aware that the restaurant includes service/tips in the bill before signing, which is a bit stealthy.

Risotteria Melotti exudes a charmingly homey vibe which aligns with their story; all the rice comes from the Melotti family farm in Verona, a region known for rice production, and many of the menu offerings are family recipes passed down from Melotti matriarch, Mamma Rosetta.The cozy, rustic ambience is due partly to the small space of the restaurant. Tables are situated pretty close together and there is an open kitchen. Despite the slightly cramped setting, Risotteria Melotti is still a popular choice for groups. I came in as a party of 5, and while we were dining there was another party of 10 that arrived.   We started with a complimentary gluten-free bread basket, which was not my favorite though I respect the restaurant's decision to remain completely celiac-friendly. Also, the olive oil was bomb. I ordered the All'Isolana ($26) which was served in a little shallow pot called a pentolino. I was a little apprehensive about the combination of rosemary, cinnamon, and pork but I did not taste either herb/spice much. The risotto was a tad soupier than I expected, but had the perfect al dente texture. The All'Isolana uses the vialone nano rice variety, which has a higher amylose content than the standard arborio, rendering it much harder to overcook and turn into mush. You can definitely taste the quality of rice. I also had the tiramisu ($12) for dessert, which was advertised as gluten-free. I think the ladyfingers were made with rice flour because they were lighter and crispier than I expected. Solid rendition with an ultra creamy mascarpone filling. Overall, I would definitely return to try out their other risottos (looking at you, Amarone + Mount Veronese)!

Best Chinese food in manhattan.Firstly went with a group of 7, ordered a variety of food.Ok, list my favorite ones here:1. 5/5 Pig feet 猪脚2. 5/5 Crispy pumpkin ball 南瓜球 Dessert3. 4.5/5 Crab tofu 4. 4.5/5 Beijing duck5. 4.5/5 Fried spicy lamb shak? I don't quite remember the name...All other food are delicious as well, but above are recommended!

Came here on a Friday night and the place was pretty packed - something they were not expecting. As a result, it took us about 15 minutes to get seated and service was a bit all over the place. However, I think they tried their best and the food was overall pretty good, definitely sufficient for the drunchies. We ordered a pitcher of margaritas, which didn't come until well after our food because they had accidentally given it to another table. Additional drinks took a while to come as well. The starter nachos weren't so great and also didn't come with any dips (not sure if they just forgot). I asked for salsa but it never ended up coming. I ended up dipping the nachos in my friends' guacamole and rice and beans, which was pretty good. The actual food, I thought, was not bad. Not sure why a lot of the reviews hate on the food, but I quite enjoyed the taste of the sides and my friend said the big burrito was really good. I think we came on a night that was not usual and hence hindered the service. The people who worked there seemed to be trying their best and apologizing so I do think the service would probably be better on a normal day.

I visited this quaint family-run establishment for lunch on a Saturday afternoon. The ambiance of the small space was welcoming and had a homely vibe. We decided to try the lunch special, which featured goat with rice. The dish was decent, offering comforting and hearty flavors.

Additionally, I opted for a chicken salad from the appetizer menu, but unfortunately, it didn't meet my expectations. The combination of a tangy dressing and the oddly flavored chicken didn't meld well together for my taste buds.

Lastly, I found their sambosa to be somewhat overpriced considering the size. While the overall experience was satisfactory, there are areas where the culinary execution and pricing could be improved.

Title: Delightful Italian Flavors with a Touch of Seafood Elegance

Last week, my taste buds were taken on an Italian journey at this charming local restaurant, where the Homemade Crabmeat Ravioli was nothing short of sublime. The accompanying sauce was a rich, creamy delight, perfectly complementing the generous portions of crabmeat and unexpectedly large, juicy shrimps that elevated the dish to a new level.

We kicked off our meal with a serving of bruschetta. Three sizable pieces arrived at a steal for $5.95, making for an appetizer that was as tasty as it was easy to share among friends. As for the surprise celebration, the staff's heartwarming rendition of a birthday song paired with a complimentary slice of mouthwatering tiramisu truly made my friend's half-birthday memorable. The tiramisu was flawlessly soft, dissolving delectably at each bite.

On a return visit, I indulged in the vodka gnocchi, with an added twist of sausage, and it did not disappoint. Each gnocchi was a soft pillow of perfection, rich in flavor and comforting in every sense. Though the food continued to impress, the service experienced a slight dip, lacking the attentiveness of our initial visit, with missed water refills and fewer check-ins.

The ambiance remains alluring with its dimly lit, intimate setting, promising an experience that's perfect for both a casual dinner and special occasions. Despite the hiccup in service, the culinary offerings are so extraordinary that I wholeheartedly recommend a visit for anyone in search of authentic Italian cuisine with a dash of seafood finesse.

This place will provide the standard classic hot pot experience! Great place to do hot pot with friends If it's your birthday, you get to eat for free here! And a monkey will come to serenade you. They also provide bags to put your jackets and belongings in if you would like. Otherwise typically all the clothes you wear to hotpot will leave smelling like hotpot. You can also ask for an apron and they will give you one to use if you don't want anything getting in your clothes!My only qualm with this place is that it seems like their selection of hot pot food is not as extensive as other places. Didn't find spam, potato, variety of fish balls, or a variety of vegetables on the menu (they have some veggies, but not many)
Decent pizza, but waiting in line outside in the cold for close to an hour is just not worth it in my book.   If you order a pie it's pretty $$$...I think there are better options in NYC.

Small crowded place but with tasty xiao long bao! I really like the crab xiao long bao, Dan Dan noodle, Mapo tofu, and Szechuan fried chicken. They're  very efficient and definitely can get you in and out in honestly less than 30 minutes from when you get seated. It's in a prime location on st marks so you're near a lot of great dessert as well!

If you're on the hunt for some good pizza in the Soho/Noho/Nolita part of New York City then head on over to Prince Street Pizza. Their Spicy Square Pepperoni Slice is an absolute rockstar! Fra diavolo sauce, fresh mozzarella and tons of spicy pepperoni curled into tiny little cups makes for delicious bites start to finish.

Grabbed brunch with three friends on a Saturday morning at noon and the whole place was completely empty. Had trouble ordering waffles because their machine was off (?) and another drink was off the menu because it was still frozen (?) so not sure what that's about. The back patio is a gorgeous place to dine, and the umbrellas and decors really make it special. However, I can't say the same about the food....My huevos plate with eggs and salad and potatoes was bland to the max. It's like they didn't season it with anything beside salt and pepper and jalapanos, and they didn't even put much of that either. The eggs were too broken and scrambled so it was hard to eat, and the potatoes were flavorless. The salad was the best thing because it was fresh. My friend's enchilada looked great though, so maybe I ordered the wrong dish.

Title: A Tantalizing Taste of Island Flavors at Concept Eatery

I ventured into the restaurant at 7:45 PM on a Monday night and was pleasantly surprised to be seated immediately. With parking conveniently available on a nearby side street, the first impressions were positive.

This eatery, a vision brought to life by an ambitious restaurateur with several concept restaurants across the island, did not disappoint. The decor was thoughtfully curated, complemented by music that enhanced the dining experience with its authentic vibes.

Upon seating, we were presented with a Scoville guide, along with impressively concise cocktail and entrée menus. The waiter's skills shone through as he adeptly recommended margaritas paired with guacamole. I indulged in a ginger blueberry margarita; its sweetness and thickness from the puree were enjoyable, albeit a tad rich for my palate.

My main course, the shrimp ajillo priced at $26, boasted a generous portion of shrimp. However, the shrimp were slightly overdone. That said, the accompanying garlic sauce was a delight, especially when savored with the modest serving of rice and beans. My companion's beef burrito, a swirl of well-seasoned meat, was a revelation. It's on my must-try list for the next visit.

Dessert was the true showstopper - a tres leches that redefined my dessert standards. Sublime in every sense, with a surprising crunch that added an unexpected and delightful texture.

While I eagerly anticipate a return visit, I must be candid – the food gets 4 stars owing to the overcooked shrimp. Service was commendable, receiving a 4.7-star rating despite a few instances where we had to signal for assistance. A perfect score is awarded for ambiance, rounding off a dining experience that was near impeccable.

In short, it's a definitive return for me, perhaps as soon as this week. A solid 4.5-star experience with room for just a smidge of improvement.
Best milkshake I've ever had! It was really creamy and the chocolate was like hot fudge. That's all I got and it was out of this world good. Great staff too.

I went here for a Saturday brunch and it was empty, so if you're looking for a super lowkey place to talk, this place is perfect.I went with a large group of 6 and the waiter was extremely kind, patient, and fast. We were in and out in 1.5 hours which I thought was pretty impressive. They give you pastry baskets instead of bread baskets before the food - which is a cute touch. The food itself was pretty mediocre and not worth the price in my opinion. Perhaps it was what I ordered but that seemed to be the consensus at the table. I ordered a Challah French Toast which was really egg-y and dry. The syrup had pumpkin in it, for the fall season, but I didn't think the flavors blended well at all. I wouldn't come here again.

Tucked away in a modest corner, this eatery offers a delightful bowl of Golden Fish Ball Hand-Pulled Noodles that certainly satisfies at an affordable $7.50. The steaming hot soup they come in is a treat for the palate, and the skillfully crafted noodles are testament to the authenticity of the craft. However, the cleanliness leaves something to be desired with inexplicably sticky utensils despite their clean appearance. The small size of the restaurant makes it ideal for a quick, no-frills dining experience for those who prioritize flavor and value over ambiance.

I'm not gonna lie, I came here because The Flying Cock was full... BUT I am not upset that it worked out that way because Blue Haven was delicious. It's a sports bar but the food was really good when I hadn't expected it to be. Good portion of Buffalo Wings and the Bacon MAC and Cheese was almost to die for. If I'm in the neighborhood I would without a doubt go back

Had an amazing experience at Sweet Chick. This was my first time eating here with friends. The waitress was friendly, prompt and gave great service. I had the Mac and cheese and cheese burger sliders. I cannot complain the food was tasty . The wait time was over 30 minutes for a Saturday evening, but once seated service was prompt.

Last Saturday night, my friends and I decided to check out this local spot renowned for its lively atmosphere. True to reputation, the vibe was electric, although I found the music overwhelmingly loud, making conversation challenging. On the upside, the service was a breath of fresh air – attentive and personable.

Food-wise, the experience didn't quite hit the high notes. My jerk chicken dish was on the tougher side, and the accompanying mac and cheese didn't leave a memorable impression, especially with the price in mind. However, the Lily's Punch was the evening's standout, a delightful concoction that we all enjoyed. In summary, a fun but not exceptional dining experience.

I've been coming to the restaurant for Italian food as it's close to where I live. The food is different from Americanized Italian food as it's lighter and focuses more on the ingredients than other restaurants that use lots of creams and sauces. This might not be for everyone, but is more of the traditional Italian taste. The chef is happy to bring out more sauce once you've tried the dish and if you still feel unsatisfied. Pros:(+) Service is amazing. After my roommate had a poor experience with the restaurant (just one dish), they wanted to bring us back and try other things on the menu. I felt that this was incredible hospitality and a lot of other restaurants wouldn't care as much about our experience at the restaurant(+) Food was delicious. For appetizers we tried the burrata & prosciutto crudo di parma and the involtini di melanzane. For the entree, I had the speghetti, rosemary, sun-dried tomatoes & chili which was my favorite of the meal. I enjoyed the texture of the noodles and how you could taste the individual ingredients in the sauce. Then for dessert, we ordered the tiramisu and the pera al cioccolato. We loved the tiramisu and the pera al cioccolato was very unique(+) Lots of vegetarian options for pasta which I definitely appreciateCons:(-) I would love to see pictures on the menu since people might not be used to traditional Italian cuisine

Upon initial skepticism regarding the higher-priced banh mis (a nod to Midtown Manhattan's premium), I was pleasantly surprised by the outstanding flavors at this venue. "The Sweet" Joju banh mi, boasting classic Vietnamese ham, pâté, and delectable caramel pork, truly lived up to its name. Each element from the perfectly toasted baguette to the succulent, marinated pork harmonized with the crisp vegetables, creating a symphony of well-balanced flavors in every bite. Complementing the meal was the Thai tea with lemon— a subtly sweet and invigorating choice. I'm now curious to compare this experience to their original Elmhurst spot. Nevertheless, I'm already eager for a repeat visit to explore more of their offerings.

Title: A Brisket To Remember

Once again, this spot has delivered an impeccable dining experience! The star of the show is undeniably the brisket, a dish I find myself gravitating towards time and again. Its flavor profile is robust, with each tender, juicy bite surpassing the last – a carnivore's delight. The sides are decent, but the Mac and Cheese stands out; it might not be the cheesiest you've ever had, but its hearty baked quality ensures it satisfies. If you're in for comfort food that hits the spot, their brisket is a must-try.

Great fast food taco joint in Times Square. Yummy chips and guacamole. Pick your taco meat and tortilla. And go find a table to stand at and enjoy your meal. The pineapple Fanta was really good!  Be prepared for a line.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Blue Smoke During Restaurant Week

My visit to Blue Smoke on a Sunday evening proved to be underwhelming, despite the promises of NYC's Winter Restaurant Week deal. With high expectations for their 3-course $50 offer, my friends and I were met with a strange and disappointing series of events.

Upon arrival for our early dinner, we were oddly told to wait an additional 5-10 minutes, despite the visibly empty restaurant. The persistent suggestion to visit the bar hinted at an unprofessional attempt to increase our spend before even being seated.

Service continued to falter as our waitress seemed to vanish into thin air, leaving us unattended for lengthy periods. This made for a frustrating and dragged out dining experience.

As for the food, though we anticipated mouthwatering BBQ, it failed to impress. The smoked brisket chili was flavorless with no hint of heat; the Kansas City spare ribs were passable but forgettable, and the accompanying Mac & Cheese was notably bland. Only the chocolate layer cake delivered some satisfaction, though it was denser than preferred.

In conclusion, considering the service mishaps and the mediocre fare, Blue Smoke is not a NYC BBQ spot I would recommend. 2 out of 5 stars.

Title: A Staple for Thai Cuisine on the Upper West Side

My go-to spot for Thai cuisine on the Upper West Side, and indeed my favorite across Manhattan, has to be this vibrant establishment. While some may argue that the decor leans towards the extravagant side for the comfort food they serve, it adds to the unique charm of the place.

The ambiance is conducive to social gatherings; however, those seeking a quiet, romantic, or business atmosphere might find the noise levels quite intrusive. Additionally, the restaurant is quite cozy—perhaps too much so—as the seating arrangement feels a bit tight, which can lead to some minor inconveniences like jostling and accidental spillage.

When it comes to the food, the Pad Thai Bolan stands out as a must-try and is superior to their regular Pad Thai. The Krapow Gai Sup (Basil Chicken) is another dish I'd wholeheartedly recommend. While the Hoy Dub (Sword clam) was once a favorite, it's no longer the generous portion it used to be during the restaurant's grand opening. Meanwhile, the Crab Meat Thai Omelet, although tasty, doesn't justify its price tag for the scant amount of crab offered.

All in all, despite a few drawbacks, the culinary experience here keeps me coming back for more.

I recently dined at this local gem where the portions truly impressed me. The bowls came packed with generous amounts of meat and noodles, hearty and satisfying in every way. The appetizers were a hit as well, especially the corn fritters that were a delightful start to the meal. I highly recommend mixing it up between their classic noodle soups and the inventive new ramen dishes. A visit here won't disappoint!

My dining experience at this restaurant was a mix of ups and downs. Our server, Anna, deserves high praise for her welcoming and non-judgmental attitude, given that we don't consume alcohol even during happy hour.

Upon arrival, the hostess initially directed us to a high top near the entrance, which we declined due to the unpleasant cold drafts each time the door opened. Instead, we were seated at a more comfortable table at the back.

Service was swift: the sparkling water I ordered was promptly followed by a dozen oysters for my companion, Jeffrey. The oysters were fresh and nicely complemented by a shallot-rich mignonette sauce. I opted for a bowl of clam chowder and a side salad, while Jeffrey chose a burger.

Unfortunately, the food was a letdown. The clam chowder lacked flavor, requiring an excessive amount of salt, and the blue cheese dressing on the side salad was disappointingly bland. Jeffrey's burger, which was ordered medium-rare, arrived well-done. Despite these culinary missteps, it's worth noting that the french fries were a tasty exception.

While Anna initially impressed us, her service faltered as she failed to check back in on our dining experience. In the end, we left in a hurry, feeling unsatisfied with the meal. My advice: you might want to consider dining elsewhere.

My recent visit to this Montana eatery was nothing short of delightful. The standout of the night was unquestionably the Bison, a dish that authentically captures the local cuisine. The restaurant's ambiance is perfectly suited for a relaxed dinner complemented by an impressive selection of drinks. Highly recommend for a satisfying culinary experience.

Title: Fresh Seafood with a Spicy Kick

My sister and I, in the throes of a seafood craving, initially tried The Boil but were deterred by the lengthy 1-2 hour table wait. Our search for an alternative led us to a nearby spot where we were delighted to be seated immediately.

Opting for the special set designed for 2-4 people, we found the portion size satisfactory, though barely enough for the two of us, hinting that perhaps we have hearty appetites. The freshness of the seafood was the highlight of our meal, a testament to the restaurant's quality sourcing.

However, not everything was smooth sailing. The grease level was notably high, which, while contributing to a rich flavor, also accelerated our sense of fullness. Additionally, the spiciness offered a challenge; despite requesting a mild option, the heat was more intense than expected, posing a problem for my spice-averse sister and leaving me with a lingering fire in my mouth after an encounter with one of the hidden spices.

On a positive note, the spicy popcorn chicken included in the set was a standout—aromatic, crunchy, and flawlessly executed.

In retrospect, despite the few hiccups, the experience was positive enough to warrant a return visit. The allure of flavorsome, fresh seafood and the hope for an improved spice level adjustment will likely bring us back to this establishment.

Very good edition to the midtown east dining scene.  Comfortable and nicely appointed dining room sets the tone for a good time.  The bistecca on the menu is satisfyingly flavorful and the wine list is full of enough excellent and well priced bottles, to find one to go along with it.

Title: A Twist on the Classics at Clancey - Almost Perfect!

I recently dined at Clancey, a spot that prides itself on reinventing classic dishes. As an enthusiast of unique savory breakfasts, I couldn't pass up their Chicken + Challah, a delightful take on the traditional chicken and waffles. It was a spectacular choice, with superbly crispy yet tender chicken, perfectly seasoned. The Challah was a hit too, striking an exquisite balance between sweet and fluffy.

The creativity didn't stop there. Sharing the Yesterday Lo Mein with friends was a highlight – an upscale nod to a takeout favorite, flavorful and thankfully lacking in grease and MSG. The whimsical presentation in a classic Chinese takeout box added to the charm.

However, consistency seems to be Clancey's Achilles' heel. A subsequent visit yielded a less impressive experience, with both chicken and Challah disappointingly burnt. Despite this, the memory of my initial encounter leaves me optimistic, and I'm willing to return in hopes of reliving that culinary excellence. For now, Clancey earns a solid 4 stars with room to soar if they can even out their performance.

Stopped in at Uncle Jacks while we were walking in New York.  It was 5:00 and there were very few patrons yet. We got to pick our spot which I chose by the fan because I was hot from walking the streets. Our waitress, Anastasia, was super and very accommodating to us. I ordered the prime French dip.  It was delicious. Probably the most expensive French dip I've ever had...but it was worth every bite. The August was so dark and rich and the sandwich was perfect. I couldn't finish it all and she packaged it up for me to take with me. My husband ordered the tenderloin and it was cooked exactly how he asked. The potato wedges were hugWe were treated very well from the moment we walked in to the moment we left. Thanks for a great meal

Title: A Familiar Vibe with Average Fare at Thái Son

Upon visiting Thái Son on a busy Saturday afternoon, we found the place reminiscent of its sibling establishment, Nam Son, with identical signage, interior design, and menu offerings. After a slightly longer wait than the estimated five minutes, we were ushered to a somewhat clean table amidst a floor strewn with leftovers and damp tabletops – an initial impression that left something to be desired.

Our meal began with the summer rolls, priced at $5.50 for a pair. Despite their refrigerated past, betraying a lack of freshness, they managed to be flavorful, particularly when dipped in the accompanying savory peanut sauce. The main course of Pho Tái, costing $8.75, arrived in a timely manner. The soup was enjoyable, though the broth was notably light in both texture and taste.

While the food at Thái Son was generally satisfactory, it wasn't particularly memorable. The experience overall was marred by the less-than-immaculate dining area and the need for the waitstaff to replace stained dishware. If you're seeking a standout Vietnamese meal, Thái Son might not be your first choice, but it will do if you're in the area with a craving for pho.

Nestled comfortably close to campus, this eatery offers ample seating that was pleasantly unoccupied during our Saturday brunch visit. Tables are well-spaced, ensuring a sense of privacy and comfort. Service was adequate; it met expectations without offering any particularly memorable touches.

Our taste experience was mixed. The eggs benedict, while generously portioned, was marred by an overly sour hollandaise sauce that was quite unexpected. The accompanying potatoes also fell short, presenting a soft and chewy texture that felt a bit off the mark. Portion sizes were satisfactory, but with the flavors not hitting the right notes, there's definite room for improvement in the culinary department.

It's been a long time since I had dakgalbi, and this place was pretty good! I went on a Monday around 5PM, and there was no wait. The waiter was attentive, and explained the spiciness level to me. He had told me that their level "hot" was similar to the Korean nuclear noodle challenge spiciness, and so I got the medium! As someone who is not very good with spice, even medium felt spicy near the end, but it wasn't too bad!The food took a while to come out, but when it does come out, its all fully cooked so you're able to dig right in- it's not necessarily like the kbbq style where they bring it out to you raw. The food was pretty good and I have no major complaints! Reminds me of dakgalbi I typically had in Korea.

Tucked away on the bustling foodie haven of 20th Street between Park and Broadway, this hidden gem sits modestly between Rezdora and Sugarfish. Initially overshadowed by its more prominent neighbors, it wasn't until a chance encounter on a night out that we decided to give this place a go.

The menu promised an authentic Singaporean experience, so we dove into the chili crab, a house specialty, alongside savory dishes like the tofu special, salty egg prawns, and the staple roti canai. The undisputed highlight of our meal was the salty egg prawns—a delightful yet messy affair that we deemed well worth the culinary chaos.

The tofu dish, while unassuming, captivated us with its simplicity and flavor, and the roti, albeit decent, didn't particularly stand out. The main event, the chili crab, came with a steep market price of $75 (a sting made sharper by a forgotten $10 Yelp discount). The crab was flavorful but labor-intensive, cloaked in a sauce that I relished for its robustness, though my girlfriend found it overly gingery. A notable letdown was the accompanying mon tao buns, which were merely steamed instead of the superior fried variation that this dish calls for.

While the crab might not see a repeat order from us, the restaurant left a positive impression overall. I'm curious to circle back for the black pepper crab. But if there's one piece of advice I'd give to any future patrons: don't miss out on the salty egg prawns.

No frills taco spot - $3.25 - $3.75 (I miss LA's $1.25 taco prices)No chairs - only standing tables Mexican green apple soda is the bomb - $3.50You have the choice of corn or flour soft shell1. order and pay at the register2. take your receipt and scoot over - give your receipt to the cook3. they prepare the tacos in front of youTacos are pretty good here and comparable to what you can find out in LA. It's probably the only place I'd eat at in the immediate times square area. Three tacos will leave you quite content, or full if you have a small stomach.

Today was my first time at this Sugarfish location. I have been to the Flatiron location twice and was super underwhelmed. I wasn't able to make a visit to the LA location when I was visiting, but was craving sushi so my friend and I decided to give this location a try. We were pleasantly surprised with the food here. It is so much better than the Flatiron location. The fish was fresh and the sushi rice was just the perfect temperature. My only critique would be the wait time between when we ordered to when the edamame came out for our "Trust Me" course. My friend frequented many Sugarfish locations in LA so she is familiar with the Sugarfish standard. The timing today did not seem to meet up to the Sugarfish standard for her.

This place is NOTHING like Pig n Khao! There's definitely a more fusion spin to this. The menu includes thai, filipino, and malaysian dishes!! I'd recommended making reservations as the space isn't big and the tables are pretty close to each other. It also get busy rather quick. We came on a wednesday night and there was definitely a wait. We were a table for 5 but we ordered almost everything. We ordered Crudo, Tofu 3 ways, Brussel sprouts, Green curry cauliflower, choeng chee see ew, hainanese duck, lamb rendang, and nasi lemak. Crudo - cold dish. almost like a tar tar with pork belly. I couldn't really take the pork but was good. Tofu 3 ways - included hard tofu, soft tofu, and bean curd. The flavors were spot on, the more I ate the more I salivated LOL Brussel sprouts - IT WAS SO GOOD WE HAD TO ORDER ANOTHER ONE  Green curry cauliflower - only came with 3 small cauliflower but the green curry was pretty spot on as well! Choeng chee see ew - we thought this would be a spin off of a pad see ew maybe, but this is nothing like it!! the noodles are fried but soft on the inside. Very interesting. Its definitely an acquired taste but over all, it was delicious lamb rendang - it wasn't as gamey as expected. also came with slices of roti to eat with the lamb and sauce. nasi lemak - comes with coconut rice with a runny egg and 2 pieces of chicken. the chicken WAS SO DAMN JUICY IM STILL THINKING ABOUT IT. the skin was fried perfectly as well. the sauce it comes with is a heart breaker. SO. GOOD. hainanese duck- i saved the best for last. we were asking for recommendations with our server, and more than 3 employees came to tell us the duck is a must. and trust me, when a black man says a dish is fire - you already know ITS FIRE. we were not disappointed, the duck melted in my mouthhhhhhh. omg. theres a side of crunchy rice, it also comes with some duck fat, which the rest of my table loved but I could have done without it. Even then, it didnt feel heavy to eat at all. the coconut rice is the best ive tasted in new york all my life. we loved it so much we ordered 3 bowls of it. theyre also not skimpy on the rice at all! needless to say, im in love with this place.

During my latest visit to the restaurant, I was once again drawn to the delightful Vegan Quinoa bowl, a dish that had won me over on a previous occasion. This time, I decided to complement my meal with a side of baked sweet potato. Although I anticipated a whole baked potato, I was pleasantly surprised to receive a portion of well-prepared baked fries. Integrating the fries into my quinoa bowl turned out to be a serendipitous twist – the combination was absolutely delicious, elevating the flavors and textures to a new level. The restaurant continues to impress with its innovative approach to vegan cuisine.

Maialino, nestled in Danny Meyer's Union Square Hospitality group, maintains its sophisticated charm as an Italian gem. As long-time patrons since its inception, we've never been let down, with each visit consistently outstanding. The dinners are remarkable, but it's the brunch that truly captures the essence of Maialino's excellence. The service is unparalleled, effortlessly enhancing the dining experience. This place has won our hearts time and again, and we eagerly anticipate our next visit.

I recently visited an exciting Italian restaurant nestled in the Upper West Side, where I made reservations for the outdoor eating area at the back. The ambiance isn't fine dining, but the prompt service, delicious food, and a well-paired wine made for a delightful dinner. The prices didn't break the bank, and the menu had a pleasing variety to choose from. Based on my enjoyable experience during this one visit, I'm happy to rate it at 4 stars.

I recently returned for lunch at this local Thai restaurant and was delighted to find that my experience surpassed the already high expectations set by my previous visits. To my surprise, there was no wait on a Friday afternoon, allowing us to dive straight into the culinary delights.

We started with the curry puffs which were a flavorful beginning, but the true standout were the beef buns—utterly exquisite and a must-try for any visitor. The Chicken pad Thai followed suit with its authentic flavors and was complemented perfectly by the creamy Thai iced tea.

Service was impressively quick, which only enhanced the overall dining experience. With food this good and service to match, it's no wonder this establishment stands out as one of the best Thai options in the area. I'm already looking forward to my next meal here.

Back in they day when I worked on East 43rd St, if a vendor wanted to take me to lunch, this is a place I would recommend.    But those days are long gone (and I've worked in Queens since 2006) so haven't been to this place since dinosaurs roamed the earth.Some seafood loving friends and I came here for dinner and overall, it was a decent experience.    The place is huge and we had a reservation so getting seated was fine.   It did take 20 minutes before our server approached us (although we had plenty of water in the meantime) and he did immediately apologize for the delay in getting to our table.We started with a shellfish sampler and had some oysters, clams and shrimp.  The west coast oysters were very good.  Everything else was fine.For entrees, we all got fish of some kind.  I had a lemon sole, which was pretty good.  I would have liked the meat a little flakier as it was a bit mushy-textured but the flavor was great.   The asparagus and fries I had for sides were fine.Obviously, this isn't a cheap place...even without dessert and only three drinks total among us the bill was well over $300.   But it was a decent experience so I'm going to say this was A-OK.

I recently celebrated a friend's 25th birthday with brunch at Catch, a trendy spot with a rustic seaside ambiance, bathed in natural light – a charming setting despite not being near water. Surprisingly, at 1 PM on a Saturday, the place was nearly empty, a stark contrast to the bustling dinner scene I experienced during a past Restaurant Week.

Our large party was seated centrally, and drinks started flowing, with costly Bellinis at $17 and even an iced coffee priced at $9. We skipped the family-style option in favor of individual dishes. My choice, the Egg White & Pulled Chicken Burrito at $22, was tasty but quite watery and a bit meager in portion, leaving me less than satisfied. The burrito could use a side appetizer to round out the meal.

For a festive touch, we ordered the "Hit Me" Chocolate Cake for the birthday girl—a fun yet messy highlight, with the chocolate and ice cream being particularly scrumptious.

Payment was a breeze thanks to the use of handheld tablets, making bill splitting among the ten of us hassle-free.

In summary, Catch offers a great atmosphere for a group birthday brunch, especially if you're seeking a quieter vibe. While the food did not overly impress, the overall experience was positive, and I am open to returning, perhaps to try the seafood selection next time.

I recently visited a restaurant located right by Penn Station and was thoroughly impressed with my experience. The service was excellent, and the prices were reasonable, with a delightful cooked beef pho costing only $13. The convenience of the location, combined with the quality of the food and service, ensures that I'll definitely be returning. A well-deserved 5 out of 5 stars!

We came here for happy hour, this place has the longest happy hour 4pm until closing. The specials are available at the bar and lounge area. We came in before 6pm and were able to get some seats in the lounge, the bar area was pretty packed. My friend ordered the sangria and I had the classic margarita which was pretty good. I also had the tamarind margarita and that was delicious! Our server was really good, she was friendly and attentive even though she had a lot of tables to cover on her own. Based on her recommendations we ordered the steak nachos and queso fundido con chorizo. Both dishes were really good, the nachos had a good amount of steak. I really liked the queso, although the chorizo made it super oily. This place has an all you can eat and drink brunch for $50. I'm definitely going to come back and check out the brunch.

We passed by BeerZaar walking home from work- it had a pretty nice outdoor seating area, which on a nice day, drew us in.They had a very good happy hour menu- burgers and beer and a pretty good price. The beers all seemed to be pretty local, and while I tend to not like craft beers (personally I drink very light beers like Coors) they had a beer that was delicious and light, as well as others that were a bit more hoppy for my fiancée.The burgers were pretty standard - tasted good, the fries were perfect. The outdoor seating is different from the inside, but from what we could see, it was pretty spacious and clean on the inside as it was on the outside. Though it was around dinner time, there was no wait for either indoor or outdoor seating.All in all, it was a nice dinner. The place was clean, service was fast, and their happy hour specials were very good for a place in this location in manhattan.

Title: A Thai Gem Worthy of Its Name

I've finally discovered why it's called TOP THAI – because it truly is top-notch! Our experience was made even more memorable by Jeff, whose exceptional service elevated our birthday celebration to new heights.

The meal began with a delectable appetizer combo that tantalized our taste buds, expertly setting the stage for the feast to come. The tom yum soup was an exquisite balance of spicy and sour, awakening our appetites with its complexity. Every bite of the skirt steak was a savory sensation, perfectly cooked and seasoned.

But let's talk about the true stars of the evening: the pad thai and duck udon were simply spectacular, each dish bursting with authentic flavors that transported us straight to the streets of Bangkok. And the papaya salad? It was the bold, refreshing crunch that perfectly complemented the rich, hearty entrees.

In summary, TOP THAI didn't just serve food; they delivered an unforgettable dining experience. Count on me to return soon!

Title: A Rainy Night Treat at GFG Bakery

Caught in a downpour and with an empty pantry, my quest for sustenance led me to the welcoming doors of GFG Bakery. As I stepped inside, the modernity of the establishment was immediately apparent, boasting an expansive seating arrangement that stretched beyond the counter and into a large, open area at the back.

My attention was captured by their diverse menu, and I found myself opting for the Chicken Basil Aioli sandwich. This delightful offering consisted of a perfectly heated chicken breast nestled within a large, fresh roll, accompanied by crisp lettuce, ripe tomato, and a tangy blend of Greek yogurt, mayo, lemon, and basil. Paired with a robust cup of coffee, the meal proved to be both comforting and satisfying.

The bakery's commitment to cleanliness was evident, which only added to the overall positive experience. Moreover, their array of Greek desserts, transcending the typical baklava, alongside an extensive coffee menu, ensures that I'll not only recommend GFG Bakery to friends but also eagerly return myself.
The beers are good and cheap which makes this place a steal. The bar food seems "flash fried" which is less appealing but probably what you want if you're drunk on a Saturday night.

Title: A Delightful Pizza Surprise Near the Nightlife

Last night's experience at this unassuming joint, nestled amidst the lively bar scene, was a delightful surprise. The pizza was exceptionally good, capturing the essence of classic flavors. I indulged in a slice of pepperoni and savored the creamy goodness of a white slice, both of which exceeded my expectations for a place so close to a bustling nightlife area.

The service added to the overall enjoyment of our meal. The pizza maker, not only skilled with his craft but also incredibly charming, added a personal touch to the experience, making us feel welcomed and taken care of. His friendly demeanor and sweet nature were as memorable as the pizza itself.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was inviting and warm, making it a perfect spot for a casual dinner with friends or even a late-night bite. I left with a full stomach and a smile, grateful for the good food and the delightful service, especially from the adorable guy who served our pizza (and made it into my photo album).

Overall, it was a lovely evening filled with delicious pizza and great vibes. This place is proof that sometimes the best culinary gems are found where you least expect them. A big shout-out to the cute pizza maker who truly knows how to serve up a slice of joy!

Title: High Hopes Dampened by Mediocre Fare at Antoni's Eatery

As an avid fan of Antoni from Queer Eye, I entered his restaurant full of anticipation, eager to savor the culinary creations. Unfortunately, my dining experience fell short of expectations. The jerk chicken bowl I ordered failed to impress; its flavors clashed and the temperature was lukewarm at best. My side of cauliflower mac and cheese was similarly underwhelming and, troublingly, contained undeclared cashew products, which induced an allergic reaction in my companion. Despite the seriousness of the situation, the restaurant staff's response lacked both concern and accommodation.

On a brighter note, my partner's Thai chicken bowl, while on the heavier side, did offer a more flavorful experience. The one redeeming quality of the restaurant is undoubtedly its atmosphere – the stylish decor and Antoni memorabilia provided a delightful backdrop that fans would appreciate.

Despite the promise of a Queer Eye star's touch, the actual meal left much to be desired. I remain hopeful that other offerings, such as breakfast or coffee, might live up to the establishment's potential. For now, I'd recommend visiting more for the ambiance than for a memorable dining experience.

Title: A Heartwarming Experience at a Local Gem

As the government shutdown reaches an unprecedented 33rd day due to the standoff over border wall funding, it's heartening to witness acts of solidarity within our community. I had the pleasure of dining at a remarkable local establishment that truly embodies the spirit of support during challenging times. This place shines as a beacon of hope, extending a generous offer of free meals to federal employees affected by the shutdown.

The atmosphere was inviting, with an air of camaraderie that can only be felt when people come together for a common good. The staff greeted each patron with a warm smile, reminding us that even in the midst of political turmoil, kindness prevails.

It's not every day you encounter a restaurant that puts people over profits. This act of goodwill certainly made my heart full and my dining experience memorable. In times like these, gestures like these resonate deeply within the community, forging bonds that last far beyond the duration of any shutdown.

As someone from Sichuan, this really lives up to the standard! All dishes were a really good sized portion, four dishes just about enough for three people. 1) Loofah: just the dish to escape a little bit of spiciness. It is light and flavorful. 2) Blood curd: there are plenty of other things in this pot like bean sprouts and spam. The peppers give both of these a slight kick and is perfect pairing with rice too. 3) Eggplant: so so tender. This one was a little bit salty but the taste is there! Usually my go-to and just-order dish at a Sichuan restaurant. 4) Favorite from this meal was definitely the fish. Went well with everything else and at a level of spicy and numbness that doesn't kick in till later. You only want to eat more though! The fish was very tender and you get the option to have boneless or with bone. Pretty busy for a Tuesday lunch time, but most people were seemingly students. Would recommend coming early for dinner especially on the weekends if it's like this on a weekday!

Title: Bustling Birthday Dim Sum Delight

I visited this restaurant for a friend's birthday celebration over the weekend, and the atmosphere was absolutely buzzing. The convenience of tracking our wait time on Yelp was marred slightly by the 30-minute wait and the jam-packed hallway with empty tea pitchers not being the best first impression.

Once seated on the second floor of what I gathered is a multi-level establishment, we were enveloped in the lively din of traditional dim sum service. The staff rolled out trolleys loaded with the usual dim sum classics, though the language barrier required a bit of patience and boldness in our selections.

While the dishes were reliably good, with personal favorites like the turnip cake and sticky rice hitting the spot, the dessert offerings left me yearning for more variety. Beyond the standard jellos and pastries, the inclusion of traditional sweets like tapioca or grass jelly would have enhanced the meal significantly.

A special mention goes to the adorable custard buns shaped like pigs, which, despite their charm, were somewhat lacking in flavor. My advice for fellow diners: bring along someone fluent in Chinese to navigate the menu and ensure you get to try everything on your dim sum wishlist.

New look! More options! Same great taste!Justino's has expanded and I couldn't be anymore happier! My alma mater is in the area, and as a broke college student Justino's was my saving grace. Justino's used to be a tiny storefront with enough space to comfortably fit three supermodels. Now with the expansion you can enjoy your NY style pizza in a dining area the size of a NY style 1 bedroom apartment. So yeah, not that big but it will do. Regardless now we all have a nice space to enjoy that yummy pizza goodness (or pastas or salads) that is Justino's. Trust me it means a lot especially on those brutally cold winter days and sweltering summer afternoons.

I dream about the food here. The aged steaks are among the best I have ever had. The half garlic head that comes with it is creamy and soft (as it should be). Came during truffle season and had to get the special truffle gnocchi - I was not disappointed! First time trying actual sliced white truffles. Also, the lobster mac and cheese was the best I have had. Some places make their lobster mac and you lose the lobster flavor in the cheese but these guys do it right! A bit pricey for a regular night (came out to about 100 apiece) but for aged ribeyes, lobster and truffles I'd say we did pretty good.

Title: A Delightful Lunch Experience at [Restaurant Name]

My dining companion and I recently enjoyed a splendid lunch at [Restaurant Name], where the hospitality shone as brightly as the cuisine. The staff, alongside manager Frank, extended exceptional courtesy, ensuring our comfort throughout the meal.

Our beverage selection included kumquat lemon and passion fruit teas, both reminiscent of the cherished flavors of TenRen's—refreshing and perfectly balanced. The culinary journey was marked by an array of delectable dishes: the mapo tofu and Dan Dan mian were flavorful without being overwhelmingly spicy, while the chicken herbal soup was a personal triumph, brimming with favored ingredients that soothed the soul.

A standout side, the bok choy luxuriated in a savory oyster sauce, complemented by earthy shiitake mushrooms—a must-try recommendation for anyone seeking a vegetable dish with flair.

Be advised, the lunchtime rush does beckon a crowd, hinting at the allure of [Restaurant Name]'s offerings. Despite this, Frank's attentive care ensured our experience remained seamless. Heartfelt thanks to the team for a memorable meal laced with great food and service.

I had a delightful dining experience at this gem of a restaurant, where the culinary offerings were quite impressive. Right from the start, the complimentary chips set a flavorful tone, showing care even in the simplest dish. My main course, the lamb burger, truly stood out with its perfect seasoning and generous serving of fresh veggies — a satisfying and hearty choice. Notably, the establishment adopts a no-tipping policy, which simplifies the payment process and focuses solely on the dining experience. The breathtaking views added a special touch to the meal, making the visit worthwhile for both the palate and the eyes. This restaurant is a must-visit for anyone seeking a combination of tasteful dishes and stunning scenery.

Dining at Tabetomo on a bustling Saturday night proved to be a delightful experience. My friend and I were immediately impressed by the lively atmosphere as we came in around 8 PM. We kicked off the meal with the karaage, which was a satisfyingly hefty portion of 5-7 pieces that set a tasty tone for the evening.

As for the main course, the tonkotsu tsukemen caught my eye, despite my usual hesitance toward dipping ramen. While the broth initially arrived on the cooler side, the staff's innovative use of a hot stone to warm it up was both quick and effective. The soup boasted a powerful garlic punch and could have benefited from a little less salt, yet it remained undeniably delicious.

The no sugar plum sake is a showstopper and must-try. Tabetomo’s policy of serving generous samples, even for a glass order, made the choice a hit. For dessert, the creme brûlée, the sole sweet offering, provided a beautifully light contrast to the meal's savory notes, capping off the meal perfectly.

Service at Tabetomo scored a solid A+, with attentive staff constantly ensuring our dining experience was excellent. The ramen challenge featuring 8 pounds of noodles also adds an element of fun to the overall vibe. I highly recommend Tabetomo for both their food and service. A true gem for ramen aficionados and anyone looking for a great meal.

Decent ramen place in Chelsea. You can eat either at the ramen bar or at the tables. The ramen was fine as were the appetizers. They have beer & wine for sale. Tried 2 kinds of ramen, the fried rice, sweet potato fries, pork buns, chicken wings & crispy shrimp. This was too much food for 3 people & a child. The service was friendly and we had a good meal.

Title: A Solo Ramen Retreat Worthy of the Hype

If you think dining solo can't be delightful, prepare to have your mind changed at this noodly nirvana. The minute I stepped into my private cubby, I realized this wasn't your average ramen joint. The staff shines at personal service, ensuring a splendid experience, minus a bit of a stretch to self-serve water.

Now, let's talk about the main event – the ramen. It's clear that years have been poured into perfecting a broth that exudes complexity in every sip, paired with expertly handcrafted noodles guaranteeing an unmatched symphony of flavor and texture. For the egg aficionados, splurge on the ‘super expensive egg’ – it's the epitome of ramen egg excellence.

While your wallet might feel lighter after this experience, and despite a potentially lengthy wait, this place is a gem that demands to be savored at least once. For the discerning ramen enthusiast, it's an unequivocal must-visit. 100% recommended for anyone looking to indulge in a bowl of pure craftsmanship.

Title: Culinary Excursion into Georgian Delights

I recently visited this restaurant in pursuit of their famed Georgian cheese bread and left with my cravings thoroughly satisfied. Opting for the traditional cheese bread adorned with a perfectly runny egg, it was a joyous palette of flavors that danced in my mouth, confirming its delectable reputation.

Despite being a touch more expensive than what I'm used to in Queens, the location justifies the added cost. Alongside the bread, I tried the garlic and thyme chicken, which, while competent, didn't quite reach the same heights of culinary euphoria.

Arriving on a bustling Friday night, service lagged, no doubt a symptom of their popularity, as the establishment vibrated with patrons. Nevertheless, the kitchen maintained its pace, churning out orders with impressive agility.

My verdict? The food triumphs, making it an easy decision to return. The cheese bread alone is worth the visit, and I look forward to my next indulgence.

Title: Cozy Vibe and Tantalizing Tapas

If you're planning to visit this gem of a spot, be sure to book ahead due to its quaint size. The cozy atmosphere sets the stage for a delightful evening. Dive into their Winter Cocktail menu with standout options like the Figgy Margarita – a solid choice – or The Ginger in China Town, which is a hit for ginger aficionados. However, the L'Antoenita might only appeal to those who favor a stronger, spirit-forward experience.

The tapas are where this place truly shines. The Brussel Sprouts and Sea Scallops are an absolute delight, while the Cajun chicken, despite being good, might not beckon a second order. But don't miss the Steak Tartare and the Charcuterie with duck – both are scrumptious and well worth a try.

An added bonus is their happy hour, available until 7pm every day, offering two drinks for the price of one. This is a steal that certainly merits a return visit.

Final Verdict: Heartily recommended for both the happy hour and the food. Don't miss out on this cozy spot with flavorful small plates.

When looking for a good slice of pizza it takes time, you find a place that has a great crust but the sauce is blah or one that has an amazing sauce but the cheese tastes like it came from the dollar store. Well if you are in the area this place will not disappoint. Starting with the plain slice the dough is the perfect thickness and follows the traditional single handed fold while holding its shape! Pizza was cooked to perfection with a nice crisp crust, the suave has a nice flavor and balance between the dough cheese and sauce. The pepperoni pizza unlike the plan slice the single hand fold happens but the point drops,  the reason for the drop is the amount of these mini pepperoni slices that they put on. Each bite you get that great cheese, sauce, dough mix and this pop of flavor bursts from the pepperoni slices.  Now on to the vodka slice again the fresh ingredients with this vodka sauce that is pleasing to the taste and cooked to perfection. No harsh taste from cheap vodka.3 slices are my limit!!!People seemed to complain about the cost of the slice (plain 3 25, pepperoni 4.50) but pay for quality ingredients. If u want to pay $1.00 per slice go to times square this place has flavor!!!!

I recently had a fabulous Korean BBQ experience at a local gem. Perfect for a party of two, we opted for the 'small' beef combo, which was anything but. It included a plentiful selection of brisket, rib eye, and short rib, along with a delightful assortment of sides like corn, cheese, egg, crisp lettuce, piquant kimchi, and various sauces.

The interactive dining aspect was a highlight, with the waiter expertly cooking our selections at the table's centerpiece grill. The service was swift, ensuring our meats were savory, succulent, and arrived in no time. Coupled with the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff, this place has firmly established itself on my list for a top-notch Korean BBQ craving. Highly recommended!

During a weekday dinner at this oyster bar, despite my shellfish allergy, I found great options. My friend indulged in oysters and a lobster roll while we shared delicious grilled calamari. My fish & chips were tasty. Their happy hour wine deals added value. I'm eager to return.

This place has tasty hotpot and the also have the decor! I think the decor was a bit overdone but the food was overall pretty good. We had lamb skewers for appetizer. I had the Chinese herbal soup as broth and I also tried the mushroom soup broth. They were both very tasty and healthy. We ordered sliced lamb, beef, mixed vegetables, fried tofu, shrimp paste and fish paste. I like everything but the fish paste(the black colored one) tasted not as good. We also ordered pork dumplings and glass noodles. Don't order the pork dumplings because they don't make it in house and they just tasted like cooked frozen gyoza out of a package. Everything else was great and the service was good.

I recently visited a local restaurant with a craving for seafood paella and decided to put their rendition to the test. I was pleased to find that the serving size was generous, comfortably sufficient for two diners. My overall experience was positive, meriting a solid 7 out of 10.

Unfortunately, having a pizzeria in NYC one is automatically held to very high standards especially if you are someone like myself that is from Los Angeles and everyone says the pizza options in LA are trash, but I beg to differ. The pizza was great. I got a slice of mushrooms and honey hot (I never snap photos of my food but, I was very excited). I was satisfied but, I was not blown away. In fact, there are restaurants back home that I would prefer over this spot, but needless to say I would still return and try other slices. Staff is very nice especially the owner/manager. It can get busy but everything moves along fast. Slices may look pricey but they are rather large slices.

Farida is a very cute spot and I would say that it is pretty authentic from the food down to the outfits that the staff wears. We actually ended up dining here during the famous NYC blackout of 2019 (which only happened after our food was served thankfully). But I think it's important to mention that just due to the way the staff reacted to the unfortunate circumstances; they were still very attentive and tried their best to provide great service.Since the restaurant is very small, there is usually a bit of a wait for weekend dinner, but the good thing is that you can get on the wait list with Yelp. I would highly recommend doing so. In terms of food/drinks, I definitely recommend the Compote - very refreshing and reminds me of my childhood when my mom used to make it. We weren't super hungry so we didn't get all that much food but despite that it was surprisingly filling. I had a salmon shashlyk which is essentially just a salmon kebab and also tried some of the chicken. Both were very well cooked and seasoned.

Casa Agave is a sister restaurant to another nearby establishment which uses the same menus (notice no names on them) so if it seems familiar, it probably is.  It's a great place to grab happy hour drinks so swing by for a couple $5 margaritas.  The staff have always been very friendly when I have been in.  On my most recent visit my friend and I each had one of their salads which were actually really good.  They put their own spin on classic salads and include crushed tortillas and normally a spiced up version of traditional dressings.  The salads were a good sized portion and made for a fine meal.  It's a pretty small space and I wouldn't recommend trying to bring a super large group here but you could probably make 5-6 work comfortably.  If its just two, you may find that you're more comfortable at the bar rather than a table.  They have a pretty large selection of empanadas and other more traditional dishes.  I would recommend for a late lunch or happy hour rather than an intimate dinner.  They used to have a salsa bar but the owner/manager told us they did away with that because it wasn't getting used enough. He said we just had to ask for the salsas because they were all still available.  They have several good salsas that range on the heat scale.  Check them out for a great happy hour!

During a recent trip to New York City, a visit to Butter, an establishment run by Iron Chef Alex Guarnaschelli (ICAG), was a non-negotiable for this avid fan. The experience lived up to its expectations, starting strong with a rich and earthy Ricotta and Morel Crostini followed by an unexpectedly zesty Wedge Salad.

The main courses presented a dichotomy in delight; the Salmon with asparagus was satisfactory, yet it was the Veal Milanese that truly stole the show—every bite of the briny, crusty veal chop was a revelation. And let's not overlook the gnocchi mac 'n' cheese; Butter has achieved the pinnacle of pillowy perfection where other gnocchis can only aspire.

In reflection, Butter has secured a return visit, and my admiration for ICAG remains fiercely intact.

The wind blowing down Broadway's halls were fierce, the grumbling in my tummy, more fierce, and it's noon time -- eateries are packed -- I know because I walked into - and out of - three of them already.  No premeditated decisions, and I'm a bit panicky and am too close for comfort to all the sneezing and sniffling. I just came from blocks of textiles and perfumes and the eateries ahead are thinning it seems. Turning left, it was a bright red neon sign that grabbed my attention, I gave no thought other than my last chance -- I rushed in and I collided with a body on a line just a step inside the door. Privately cursing my lack of direction and current state of feeling, I shuffle walked to the counter pondering how little I think of the Poke word - not any of it appeals to me. But po(horseshoe character)'kie being the actual made me very happy, it sounds ancient, and nerds won't irresponsibly flood the streets.I've really never had a Poke(ie) Bowl, fish and rice is nice in theory but I questioned its filling properties. A large Ponzu Salmon bowl before me, I explored with my chopsticks with some prodding, light delicate lifting and moved in closer. I couldn't identify much and thats a good thing, so with an unmighty swoop, I began thusly. The menu reads, Scottish salmon, wasabi ponzu, shiso, kyuri, tibiko, katsuo panko, I'm embarrassed to admit how little I know of this world.The salmon lightly dissolved on my tounge with a beautiful clean far Atlantic finish, yet strong in structure. How the textures and flavors came together was like a symphony in my mouth, but interrupted each time my sticks ran aground on the burried bowl dividers below, like the seperation compartments of 1970s TV dinners, or any meals when shackled.Much to learn young Jedi, much to learn and I must. But in terms of a proper launching point, I deem this days lunch a success.

I have been meaning to get to the Rip's in Brooklyn for quite some time, but it can be a pain to get to certain corners of Brooklyn from other corners of Brooklyn. This new West Village location was just right for my friends and I to meet today, though, and I was really happy to check it out.It's a small spot, but there were three stools right by the front window waiting right there for us when we got there. The guy behind the counter was super friendly and helpful with the menu, and even brought us a sample of the outstanding rice paper bacon. I went with the rips burger and some pasta salad, both of which were awesome. I'm mad I forgot to ask what kind of cheese they use on the burgers, but whatever it was, it was outstanding. I thought the macaroni salad was quite good, but I would have liked a little more seasoning on it. My friends had a breakfast sandwich and the egg and cheese burger, which they both raved about.Solid food, friendly service, and I absolutely love the way they are proudly "vegan for the animals!" I'll definitely be back!

Awesome menu and friendly staff. Staff was also very quick to take my order and make the food. I wanted to taste the potato pancake but the waiter said they were out (first time in 7 years). I ordered two eggs over easy with a side of fries since they were out of the potato pancakes lol. I also had a side of bacon and a cup of coffee. All was made fresh and was tasty.

New favorite lunch spot in LES! I'll keep this super short but sweet because I have no complaints. I've been here twice so far. Their lunch special cannot be beat. You get an appetizer (selection includes half a banh mi sandwich, if you're extra hungry), entree, and drink all for $14. Please note, this is only offered Monday-Thursday. Friday is not included, I came on a Friday and learned the hard way :(.I've tried their five spice brisket lemongrass pho, crispy cod banh mi sandwich. They DO NOT skim on portion. The half banh mi sandwich was basically an entree on its own. They put a huge piece of fish in there. I was surprised because fish is expensive and I'm only paying $14 for this whole meal! The pho and sandwich are so gooood! Must try! You won't regret it.

Title: An Unforgettable Evening at Allora

In the plethora of fine dining options that New York City has to offer, Allora shines exceptionally bright. Our recent visit was a testament to this with its combination of delectable cuisine and exemplary service. The Caesar salad and Steak Diane, expertly prepared tableside by the charismatic Fadil, were not just meals but a demonstration of culinary passion. His engaging stories of travel added a personal touch that elevated the entire experience.

The wait staff's dedication was evident, contributing to a seamless evening. The restaurant's stunning interior and the warm ambiance are simply unmatched, making Allora an establishment we wholeheartedly recommend. This is a rare gem that deserves every one of the five stars we give.

Have delivered now twice #YelpsBigNightIn @YelpNYC made me do it again!!! Have been absolutely impressed with the quality of the food and O M G I was able to order cocktails?! Amazing. The meal for two is a great deal and food was plentiful. So happy to be supporting local restaurants. Husband and I very happy with the packaging and attention to detail! Already looking forward to another Smith delivery this weekend!

Cuisine: 7Service: 8Decor: 8Value: 7Overall: 7If we only had apps and no entree, I would have given the cuisine a 8 or 9. Unfortunately, the Mixed Grill for Four at the end was a disappointment. Next time, I would go back for the Grilled Octopus, Halloumi Fries, Vegetable Mousaka, and try some other new items on the menu.The space is comfortable and beautiful, while the service was friendly and attentive. I will be back and hopefully experience some better entrees.

Artichoke's, you will forever have my heart with that sweet Sicilian slice of yours. The first time was kind of like a love story. I ordered a Sicilian slice around dinner time, couldn't finish the hefty piece, so I put it in the fridge. Went out with some friends, came back not exactly sober, and devoured the entire thing. Even cold, it was a beautiful experience. The crust is so substantial that it retains its buttery crispiness even after hours of refrigeration. Flash forward a year later, I revisit my favorite pizza establishment to get my beloved Sicilian. Again, deliciously crispy (pretty sure my roommate could hear me munching across the room) topped with sweet, tangy tomato sauce, fried basil, and cheese. When it comes to pizza, I really despise crusts that let toppings slide off. The Sicilian crust is consistently one of the best vessels for sauce, holding everything firmly together for a nice, crunchy bite. I love you, Artichoke's. By the way -- it's cash only!

This is one of my go-to take out places. Delivery is always on time and even earlier than estimated. They have a great lunch deal that runs until 3 pm every day, even on weekends. It's any of the classic makana dishes but $3 cheaper, for the exact same thing, so coming for lunch is definitely the best deal. The makana dishes come with a meat or tofu entree, and you can pick your side. Default side is white rice but you can get garlic rice, brown rice or greens for an extra $1. I always get the garlic rice which is flavorful and moist. The dishes all come with roasted corn and a side of Hawaiian macaroni. My go-to meat is the BBQ huli chicken which is very tender and a little sweet. Their bubble tea is not great though. The bubbles are hard and and don't have much flavor. They're also micro bubbles-never seen such small boba before! At first I was surprised at how few boba pearls were in it but after I tasted it, I was glad there wasn't more. The tea itself was pretty standard.

*Sweet potato fries*.Sweet potato fries w/ sour cream & sweet chili.Once I saw this on the brunch menu, I knew I had to try it! Im already a sweet potato lover so I knew this would hit the spot which indeed it did! The sweet potato went so  well with the chili sauce, it's the perfect combo!*Watermelon Mimosa*. I can't believe after all these years, this was the first time I saw watermelon mimosa on the menu! I had to try it & I'm so glad I did because it so damn good & hella refreshing  Great summer drink for sure

I recently visited a charming restaurant that truly embraced the festive spirit during my December visit. The ambiance was delightful, with twinkling Christmas lights and merry tunes enhancing the experience, making the cost justifiable for the environment alone.

While the desserts were somewhat underwhelming, the chocolate martini stood out as a personal favorite and is a must-try for those looking to indulge in a spirited treat. The baked cookie dream, though tempting, would benefit greatly from a more generous scoop of vanilla ice cream. The chocolate hazelnut milkshake was enjoyable, albeit not extraordinary.

Despite the average desserts, the service was commendable. The staff went out of their way to ensure a pleasant dining experience, which did not go unnoticed. Overall, if you're seeking a pleasant atmosphere with diligent service, this spot is certainly worth a visit, just don't set your dessert expectations too high.

Before my friend had to head back to Jersey, we decided to eat near Penn Station and found K Chicken on Yelp. We came as a party of four on Tuesday at around 6pm and were seated immediately. This is what we ordered: -Beel Bulgogi Fries ($10.95)-XL Combo which consists of 16 wings and 8 drumsticks ($33.95)Both were so good! Beef bulgogi fries was a pleasant surprise--none of the ingredients overpowered each other. Chicken was full of flavor too. It wasn't dry but crispy and cooked to near perfection. I would recommend soy garlic and sweet & spicy sauce! Our total came out to be around $48 which was reasonably priced considering the good portions! One con: Just like many Korean chicken places, I wish this place also provided Korean radish as a complimentary side dish. Hence, a 4 star. But other than that, K Chicken is truly a hidden gem!

Refined Italian fare in an elegant atmosphere. Overall: 4.5/5Value: 4.5/5 (lunch)Food: 4/5 Service: 5/5Decor: 5/5 We came for lunch and had their pre fixe ($34 for 2 course, $39 for 3 course). A number of options for each course which was nice, but some of them have supplement charges which can skew the prices on the high side. The food is fantastic and portions are big though. I had the seafood stew and the king salmon along with Nutella panna cotta. The seafood stew was rich and flavorful yet still light, with nice chunks of lobster and calamari and a bit of fresh pasta.
