The king salmon had a nice crispy skin, was a great portion and was nicely accompanied by potato with spinach. The panna cotta was quite rich and creamy. Others in my party had the lemon meringue and tiramisu, and they both liked those as well. A member of our party is gluten free and they were fabulous in accommodating with great bread and gluten free pasta etc. Overall phenomenal food and service, worth a visit for lunch!

Title: A Hip Haven of Flavor Before Hitting the Concert Scene

I’d been eager to check out this much-hyped spot and it didn't disappoint. Opting for a pre-concert dinner, we stumbled into happy hour, where even the $14 drinks couldn't dampen the spirits after my third round. The vibe is undeniably cool, with pulsating club beats set against a backdrop of chic decor.

The tapas stole the show. It’s hard to cover the entire spread, but highlights included the best dumplings I've ever savored, empanada-like fried wonders, mind-blowing tacos, succulent pork belly buns, and soy garlic wings that were downright addictive. The fish and chicken buns were bursting with flavor—truth be told, you can't make a bad choice off this menu.

After a night rounded off with sinfully delicious churros and chocolate lava, I can declare this place a culinary hotspot. Fair warning: expect a packed house, tiny chairs, and a boisterous ambiance. Yet, for food this good, it's a small price to pay. (Pardon any overenthusiasm—I may have been a bottle of Tito’s in when writing this!)

If you love cumin and spicy foods, you'll love this place!Been wanting to check it out as part of my quest to explore the best BYOB places in the city. On a weekday night, was easy to get a table (they also allow reservations via Yelp). Place is clean, decor minimalist, vibe super casual. We ordered the cucumber, big tray chicken, tofu scallion, and lamb rice cakes. Loved each dish. Tofu scallion: serve chilled, mashed soft tofu with scallion; a refreshing dish to whet your appetite, perfect for summertimeCucumber: tastes exactly how it looks, spicy with soy and vinegar and cumin; reminds me a little of the cucumber dish at Xi'anBig tray chicken: wonderfully cooked and tender chicken over a bed of noodles; this is comfort food at its bestLamb rice cakes: probably our favorite dish; the texture of the rice cakes are bomb, super chewy - kind of reminds me of gnocchi; each bite was an explosion of flavor and spicinessBest of all the place is BYOB! No silly corking or bottle fees too. Prices are way affordable. Nestled in EV, I'd definitely recommend this place as a great dinner spot before a night out in the area.

Title: A Gem on Columbus Avenue

I'm always delighted to visit this restaurant, not just for its consistently good food, but also for the inviting and professional staff who make every visit special. The range of drinks and dishes they offer is commendable – no exaggeration – ensuring that even the most indecisive diner finds something appealing on their extensive menu.

Their fair prices and great lunch options have made it a favorite for ordering to my workplace; the quick delivery and accuracy of my orders are always appreciated. And if you find yourself there in the evening, you'll be treated to a particularly nice atmosphere.

In short, this place has become one of my go-to restaurants and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to anyone looking for variety, quality, and a pleasant dining experience in the Columbus Avenue area.

Title: A Delightful Surprise at a Cozy Spot

Last night, on a casual stroll, my companion and I chanced upon this charming restaurant and decided to step in. What a wonderful decision that was! We opted for a seemingly modest combo of tofu soup and marinated pork belly, where the quantity initially seemed deceptive. Much to our delight, the serving was incredibly generous, easily satisfying two hungry souls.

Unlike other Korean establishments that often serve a single bowl of rice with a combo, this place pleasantly surprised us by including two bowls, a thoughtful gesture that didn't go unnoticed. The pork belly was especially enjoyable, and our repeated requests for extra lettuce, which we used for wrapping the succulent meat, were met with unflagging courtesy from the staff.

Every aspect of our meal was pleasing, and the attentive service added to a genuinely happy dining experience. This restaurant has won us over, and we're already planning our next visit!

Title: A Taste of Perfection at OBAO, Hell's Kitchen

It's about time I rave about OBAO, a gem I've frequented countless times. Nestled in Hell's Kitchen, it's a must-visit for any fan of culinary excellence. Booking for six? No problem. Even our slightly delayed arrival was smoothly handled with a warm welcome and prompt seating on their spacious second floor.

The decor is a charming blend of oriental flair with modern touches, and the impressive menu variety is never a cause for concern. Trust me, I've sampled nearly nine dishes, and each one is a hit. My latest indulgence, the bun bo hue, was a flavorful medley of spicy broth, braised pork belly, and rice noodles—a hearty recommendation at $15.

Service here? Unmatched. Friendly staff, servers who know their stuff, and they're always ready to guide you through their extensive menu with personalized suggestions.

OBAO is hands-down a top contender for the best in Hell's Kitchen, perhaps even NYC. For an Asian fusion feast in a stunning setting, this is your go-to. 100% satisfaction guaranteed.

My recent dining experience at this restaurant was exceptional. The atmosphere is inviting, prices reasonable, and the service impressively quick. A highlight was the endless chips and salsa for just 99 cents. A small tip: ask for extra salsa right away as it comes in small portions. The chips arrive warm and fresh, though the salsa could use a bit more kick.

The shrimp tacos were a standout, earning a perfect score for their freshness. The jerk chicken tacos were tasty as well. On the side, the brussels sprouts and chorizo were incredibly delicious – the chorizo's thick, charred pieces were a delightful pairing with the sprouts.

Overall, the food was amazing, and I'm eager to return.

Had an OK experience at Wok Wok - it was my second time visiting in a while. FYI - it is actually located on the basement, so you have to walk down some stairs to get to the entrance. Interior is very spacious and nicely decorated with various cartoons. I arrived around 6pm on a Monday and it was pretty empty besides a few other parties. Service was about less than average - slow and our server forgot our appetizer and I had to remind them before they brought it out. FOOD: My party ordered 3 main entrees and 1 app - all to share family style:- roti scallion pancake- pad thai- Malaysian curry chicken with potato- eggplant chicken salted fish stone rice bowl (my favorite)- 1 free small thai iced tea with a check in on yelpI would say the quality and taste of the food is pretty decent and they had a huge menu selection. Portion sizes tend to be a little on the smaller side, but the food is decently priced! My favorite is definitely the stone bowl rice dish since it came out sizzling hot and created this crunchy layer of rice on the bottom. The meat in the Malaysian curry chicken also was very juicy! Only complaint we had is the fact that my brother found a piece of hard plastic mixed in the food on his plate! (Where did it come from? Who knows - we shared family style and it could have been from any dish) A pretty average dining experience for my visit this time (if not for the plastic in our food), but I can see the appeal to others.

Title: Service Hiccups Dampen Dining Experience

We visited this eatery before a 2PM show, expecting a quick meal. Despite being seated immediately, a lengthy 25-minute wait for chicken put us under time pressure. Our order for honey mustard sauce was met with a spicy bourbon street mustard, an unexpected substitute without prior notice. Upon inquiry, our server admitted the absence of honey mustard but failed to provide alternatives until pressed, resulting in an additional 5-minute delay.

The honey barbecue sauce provided was acceptable yet not what we had hoped for. In a pinch, the ranch dressing served with the fresh-tasting celery sticks had to suffice. The lemon pepper boneless chicken and strips with fries were merely satisfactory; nothing stood out, taste-wise, from the run-of-the-mill offerings.

With time against us, we were forced to take a portion of our meal to go, unsure if the theater would even allow outside food. Overall, while there were no issues with the food's quality, the service missteps significantly impacted our dining experience.

Eateries that have popped up in Brooklyn in recent years typically catch a bad reputation. They're labeled as "hipster" or "artisanal" along with a myriad of other adjectives that have a negative connotation. However, Roberta's Pizza defies all the stereotypes despite being in the heart of Brooklyn during a time where gentrification is at an all time high. Whimsically named pizzas, quality ingredients and an eclectic décor that includes an outdoor bar and their own radio station have created an immensely successful eatery that's pretty much always crowded to the point where the awaiting patrons have to wait at the outside bar until they're seated to enjoy some superb food. The pizzas are expertly crafted; there's a harmonious balance between puffy, chewy, charred-ness and the cook of the toppings. Their appropriately named "Bee Sting" pizza is an absolute must try as the combination of mozzarella, sopressata, chili, tomato sauce and a drizzle of honey stings your palette with hits of sweetness, smokiness, spice and cheesiness. Roberta's is often credited with putting Brooklyn on the map and with one meal there, you can totally see why.

Rahi is one popular place in New York that is serving some pretty tasty flavorful Indian dishes. I recently was looking for a restaurant to try before I left Los Angeles and I came across Rahi on Yelp. I wanted to try something different and this seemed like a good spot. Plenty of wonderful photos on Yelp so it wasn't hard for me to convince my friend to come with me. We came on a weekday during dinner time and the entire restaurant was completely filled. I'm glad my friend had made the reservations before I got to New York. This place smelled so good inside and I really truly wanted to order everything on their menu. We got a ton of things and actually had to take some of it back home. Tried their lamb shank and their banana leaf chicken, as our main dishes. Both the dishes were gigantic and super filling! For the appetizers, we ordered an edamame artichoke chaat which was such a large portion that we literally were full before our main dishes arrived! Each dish was super tasty and I wouldn't mind coming back again to enjoy another nice dinner!

Title: Mixed Experiences at Nino’s 46, But Worth the Trip for Pizza Lovers

My recent visit to Nino's 46 left me with a mix of impressions. The spaghetti and meatballs dish presented a dichotomy of tastes; the pasta itself boasted an appealing chewiness and ideal thickness, yet it was let down by its accompanying sauce – a bland affair reminiscent of flavorless creamy tomato soup. While the addition of ricotta cheese and basil was novel, it unfortunately dominated the dish, creating an imbalance that did not suit my palate. Though the meatballs were seasoned to perfection and generously portioned, they alone could not redeem the overall lack of excitement in the pasta dish. That said, I wouldn’t order this particular plate on a second visit.

On a more positive note, the San Marzano pizza was an absolute standout, earning a spot amongst my top five pizza experiences. From its impeccably thin yet fluffy crust to the expertly melted and evenly distributed cheese, and the perfectly proportioned sauce, the pizza was a culinary delight that I would enthusiastically recommend and eagerly order again.

Service at Nino's 46 was impressive, with our attentive waiter providing exemplary care. Drinks were promptly refilled and our diverse payment requests were accommodated without issue, contributing to the overall satisfaction with the service quality.

The ambiance struck a pleasant balance between edgy and cozy, thanks to the unique graffiti-style art adorning the walls, even if the lighting felt somewhat dim.

In conclusion, while the pasta at Nino's 46 may not have been remarkable, the exceptional pizza and top-notch service make it a worthwhile destination for anyone exploring New York's dining scene.

Tucked away in the heart of downtown lies a charming Italian restaurant that promises a cozy dining experience. The attentive and knowledgeable staff elevates the ambiance, ensuring that each guest feels well cared for. The highlight of the menu is the incredibly fresh pasta, with the zucchini parmigiana standing out as an absolute must-try—truly a revelation for the taste buds. Their Aperol spritz bar is a delightful addition, perfect for those seeking a refreshing cocktail. I wholeheartedly recommend this gem—give it some love, and it's sure to become a favorite!

Honestly more of a 3.5 than a 3..with that said:I got:- steak (platos) with tostones: the steak was pretty dry and lacked flavor (i also didnt get any extra sauce on the side or anything - not sure if its even available). The peppers and onions were a good touch but the tostones were also pretty dry so it made for an incredibly dry meal..also personally wouldve appreciated some rice or something instead- cheeseburger empanada: very good i liked this a lot!! Kinda reminded me of a philly cheesesteak. And price is reasonable at 2.5- chicken empanada: pretty dry, again, not really flavorful

One of my friends had said that this place was just okay, when I asked her for a hotpot recommendation. I'd never tried Mongolian hotpot before, and wanted to see the difference between Mongolian and chinese hotpot, so we ended up coming here for dinner on a Saturday night. We checked in with the Yelp waitlist, and only waited about 10 minutes in person. Staff were nice and efficient, and we ordered using a checkbox paper list. Our items came out quickly. Everything was pretty inexpensive, but the quality of things was not great. Overall, the food was fine but I wouldn't recommend this place to anybody.

Title: Cozy Evening at a K-Town Gem

My friends and I discovered a delightful addition to K-Town's dining scene on a Wednesday night. We walked in at 9:30 pm and were pleased to be seated pretty much instantly. However, we hit a snag upon realizing the KBBQ had a two-item minimum, which was a bit much for our appetites at the time, leading us to pass on it.

Instead, we indulged in an array of dishes, including the succulent Galbi Jjim, a hearty vegetarian Kimchi Jigae, the robust Gopchang Ttukbaegi, and the Michelin-lauded Gyeran Jjim. Each dish delivered bold flavors, though the Gyeran Jjim, which I had eagerly anticipated, fell short of expectations, especially noticeable in the absence of the usual steamed egg banchan. Nonetheless, the banchan selection shone, with the dried anchovies standing out as a highlight.

Service was typical for K-Town – efficient without the frills, complemented by the convenient coat check service to spare our jackets from the lingering aromas of dinner. A nice touch was the offer of a complimentary draft beer for checking in on social media.

In conclusion, a solid dining experience with some memorable dishes and practical amenities that made for a hassle-free evening.

If you are in Hamilton Heights, this would be your go-to Italian restaurant. The restaurant is so clean and spacious, such a good place for brunch, lunch or even dinner! I had the bolognese pasta and let me tell you, nothing was left on my plate. I don't know if I was just famished but the pasta was so good, so fresh and so savory. The sangria was okay but they do have pitchers so it's good to share with a group of friends. I highly recommend going to this place if you are live in upper manhattan.

This is a very cute restaurant. The moment you step in the decor is amazing. They have buddha statues, pretty lamps and romantic lighting. Everyone is friendly. I came here to celebrate both me and my friend's birthday, we were born on the same day! So, when I made my reservations on Opentable I added that we are celebrating our birthday. So the moment we got to our table, they had a cute happy birthday card for us with a note inside. That was so thoughtful! Our waitress even remembered it was both our birthday. That made it super special. We had the chicken dumplings and calamari for appetizers, they were super delicious. I had the pad thai which I asked for super spicy but it was sweet. It was still good though. They surprised us further with an assortment of mochi ice cream with a candle. I liked the thai iced tea mochi the best. Our waitress, Nuch (I hope I got her name right) was friendly and attentive and sweet. We had a very special birthday here. It doesn't end. So after paying our bill and leaving. The staff from the restaurant ran over a block to find us because I left my bag in the restaurant. He ran just to give it to me. That was super sweet. The service here is exceptional and the staff are extremely friendly. I felt really welcomed here. And the food was delicious too. I will definitely come here again. Thank you for making our birthdays special and memorable.

Rebranded from NuNoodle, menu changed slightly and price got higher. I probably like what they have previously better. Nightmarket's menu become more fried food driven and heavy. Beef Noodle Soup remain it's flavor, not amazing but not bad. Crispy Porklet - not bad but feel like it was fried 3 times and the meat was not a lot. Firecracker Tofu Skin - my friend's fav but my least favorite. Feel like I couldn't tell what I was eating besides the fried dough..... Scallion Pancake Burrito - acceptable, missing the classic brown sauce ! Fried Dumpling - this was bad. Only vermicelli inside.... Cheap out ingredient to the max.... One of the few Taiwanese restaurant in the city and would like to see it be authentic more.

I get the hype for this place!! I've always seen Ichiran on social media in Japan and have always wanted to try it. I was excited to see they had two locations and NYC and couldn't wait to try it. You are first greeted by someone who lets you know what sears are available to sit in. I came on a weekday at noon and didn't have to wait for a group of 3. I selected the recommended set with the suggested flavor amounts but with spicy 2 and medium firmness of noodles. The broth was so flavorful but not too overpowering. The spice wasn't too spicy at all but it provided a good kick to the broth. The noodles were absolutely fantastic - the freshness of each noodle is evident with each bite. I was able to get free noodle refills so I decided to get firm noodles - the chewiness of the noodle was honestly so delicious. Definitely will be visiting here every time I go to NYC!

Title: Happy Hour Hits with a Side of Tacos

I popped into this bustling spot on a Tuesday evening, lured by the promise of a budget-friendly Happy Hour. True to form, the margaritas, at just $7 a pop, did not disappoint. Generously sized with a satisfying kick, they were the perfect after-work pick-me-up.

While sipping on my drink, the temptation of tacos proved irresistible. The jerk chicken taco burst with flavor, and the shrimp and crab combo was equally delightful. Despite the service being a touch slow—understandable given the packed house—the staff did their best to keep up.

Be warned, taco lovers: these tasty treats are on the smaller side. A couple of bites and you’re reaching for the next one, which makes it all too easy to rack up a bill, as the "moderate" prices can accumulate quickly.

A word to the wise—skip the chips and salsa. The salsa, merely a dollop of what you’d garnish your tacos with, is underwhelming and not worth the extra expense.

Overall, if you're craving a good margarita and some flavorful, albeit petite, tacos, this is your spot—just keep an eye on your taco tally to avoid a budget blowout.

Tucked away from the urban high rises, my girlfriend and I discovered a quaint brunch spot with a trendy vibe. Expect a wait—ours was 30 minutes despite using the Yelp waitlist and still overstaying the estimated time.

I indulged in the Early Lunch: a delectable skillet of slow-cooked Prime Angus Beef, mingling with chickpeas, avocado, and arugula, crowned with a perfectly over-easy egg, crunchy almonds, and a drizzle of tahini. It arrived with a side of bread accompanied by a flavorful Kalamata olive butter. My partner chose the Farmer's Breakfast, a more modest offering of a mushroom and Mozzarella omelette, paired with a side salad and a dollop of Labneh cheese sprinkled with Za'atar, also served with bread and the same butter.

While the Early Lunch proved satisfying with its rich sauce and tender beef, the Farmer's Breakfast fell short, especially at a $15 price point. The pricing here, even for a simple glass of orange juice, seemed disproportionate to the portions provided.

In summary, the meal was enjoyable with a standout dish in the Early Lunch, but overall, the restaurant's pricing strategy did not align with the value and quantity of food presented.

I've been a regular at this gem of an Italian restaurant on the Upper East Side for years, and it's unquestionably my favorite. Their recent reopening for take-out amidst current restrictions was a cause for celebration. To my delight, the take-out experience matched the excellence of dining in, with every dish maintaining the high quality I've come to love. I'm eagerly anticipating my next take-out order and, even more so, the day I can return to enjoy the ambiance in person.

Title: A Memorable Somalian Feast at Safari in Harlem

Last evening's pre-jazz club dining at Safari was a delightful venture into Somalian cuisine. The necessity of our reservation became apparent upon our 6pm arrival to a bustling setting, quickly accommodated by the efficient staff. 

Opting to start with sabaayad, the unassuming presentation belied its flavorful complexity, paired wonderfully with a spicy green sauce. My hilib ari, the restaurant's roast goat signature, converted my usual reluctance into pure savor, while the mango curry chicken and its vegetarian counterpart received unanimous praise from my husband and brother.

The sweet finale featured hearty Somalian crepes with honey, which satisfied without overwhelming sweetness. Overall, Safari's fusion of excellent food and warm hospitality guarantees our recommendation and a future revisit.

I made my reservations online to eat here a few weeks ago.  It was easy and I received an email the day before to confirm the reservation.  This place has been on my list of things to-do for a while now.  I must say that I was not disappointed.     The restaurant is sleek.  The decor combinations of old and modern, industrial and mediterranean, trendy and classic, all create a sexy stage for exemplary food and extraordinary service.   The vibe is positive throughout.      I ordered the black fettuccine with lobster and crab meat.  I also ordered a serving of Brussels Sprouts for the table.  My son ordered a rib eye steak. My daughter chose the Porterhouse pork chops.   Everything came out perfectly.  Our food was impressive and memorable.  We also ordered cocktails.    We had a server named, James.  He delivered fantastic service.  He was attentive the entire night.      I had high expectations coming in tonight.  They exceeded every expectation I had!
I've never had pizza like Rubirosa supreme! The crust is light, thin and perfectly crispy. All ingredients are fresh and flavorful. You'll savor every bite and get sad when you're done!

Cute establishment and they have happy hours until 8 pm. I enjoyed the Louisiana style wings because of the favor. However, there was some problems. The first batch was semi-cooked, some of the second batches were burned, and the third batch was perfect. I also tried creole poutine, mac and cheese, po boy, and Brussels sprouts.  Staffs were friendly and came to check on us constantly. FYI, we used a 15% discount using Yelp check-up. It was a great deal.

Title: Return Visit Triumphs Despite the Squeeze

Our second visit to this bustling gem reaffirms its must-visit status. While the cozy quarters require a bit of patience, the atmosphere is part of its charm. Be prepared for a wait—this place draws a crowd eager to enjoy the culinary delights awaiting inside. Your perseverance will be rewarded.

The buffalo mozzarella is a standout, offering a rich, creamy experience that's simply divine. And when it comes to pizza, the Rubirosa Supreme is a game changer—its oven-baked perfection makes every minute of the wait worthwhile. This spot remains high on our list, crowding aside, it's an epicurean's delight not to be missed.

On the recommendation of a friend, I ventured into a local Chinese bakery said to rival, if not surpass, Yaya's in the riceball department. True to form, the bakery was a quaint, typical establishment with a cozy interior that placed emphasis more on the food than the seating arrangements. The riceballs, however, were a delightful surprise - an extensive array at remarkably wallet-friendly prices.

I indulged in a Japanese curry chicken riceball, priced at a mere $2, which is a steal compared to Yaya's rates. The seasoning was spot on, hitting all the right notes of flavor complexity. Alongside my riceball, I enjoyed an iced milk tea that struck a perfect balance of sweetness and refreshment. 

Though my appetite was limited, I eyed the other baked goods, which looked equally tempting. Without hesitation, I'd recommend this bakery for anyone seeking tasty riceballs at great prices. Next visit, I'm certainly coming with an appetite to try more.

Title: A Delightful Lunch at [Restaurant Name]

My recent visit to [Restaurant Name] for a Saturday lunch was an absolute pleasure. We were seated immediately, which was a pleasant surprise for a weekend. The restaurant's open windows welcomed a fresh breeze, complementing the lovely summer atmosphere perfectly.

The chicken karaage didn't disappoint—served piping hot, it was an enjoyable start to the meal. However, the star of the show was the Una-tama don. It arrived with a choice of miso soup or salad, but honestly, the don itself demanded all the attention. Topped with a perfectly runny egg, it harmoniously melded with four generous pieces of soft, boneless unagi, resulting in a dish I relished every bite of.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit to sample more from their don selection. [Restaurant Name] has certainly earned a spot on my go-to list.

My recent visit to this gem of a restaurant was an absolute delight, with their pizzas taking center stage. As a group of four, we sampled a range of their offerings including crispy cauliflower, baked ricotta, and pastas, where the whole wheat spaghetti won my preference over the cavatappi.

The stars of our meal were undoubtedly the squash blossom pie and the calzone. The pie could easily hold its own against renowned spots like Razza, and the calzone was a marvel of flavors and textures that left us raving.

A pleasant surprise was the complimentary strawberry salad, which emerged as my top appetizer—so refreshing and perfectly balanced. While the cookies in the cookie box rounded off the meal nicely, next time I might pass on dessert here and explore other local sweet spots.

Overall, this restaurant is a must-visit for pizza aficionados. I'm already looking forward to my next trip back to explore more of their pizza offerings.

After a sweltering day at the Seaport, I ducked into a bustling spot in Little Italy, lured by the promise of a quick bite. The establishment, frequented by tourists, boasted an efficient team that kept the long line moving swiftly. The front of the house was cramped, with the cashier and fountain drink station a bit too cozily positioned, leading to occasional bottlenecks.

The saving grace was the ample seating area, which surprisingly offered respite and a pair of seats on a busy Saturday. The turnover was fast, reflective of pizza's grab-and-go nature, but those with larger parties might find seating a challenge.

As for the main event – the pizza – it scored a middling 2.5 out of 5 in my book. Being a New Yorker comes with lofty pizza expectations, and while this pie was sufficiently cheesy, neither the sauce nor the crust left a notable impression.

In summary, this spot is a convenient option if hunger strikes in Little Italy, but for those on the quest for quintessential New York pizza excellence, you might want to keep looking.

Great spot! We had a filling and tasty lunch here. We started with the cold sesame noodles because we'd never tried them. They were the only thing we didn't love, they left a chalky taste in my mouth, maybe that's what they are supposed to?!The kung pao chicken and garlic shredded pork were exactly what you'd expect. Good sized portion and both the white and brown rice were good. Service was friendly and quick. I was a little disappointed they supplied me a fork in addition to chop sticks without being asked...I can hold my own on chop sticks, thank you!!

Stumbled upon a hidden gem reminiscent of a mini Mykonos in the heart of the city, this super cute spot whisked me back to my Greece travels. The authenticity of each dish impressed, with favorites like succulent Greek meatballs and a standout braised octopus in a rich tomato sauce. While the Greek salad could have been more finely chopped, it's a minor quibble in an otherwise delightful experience. Don't miss out on the creamy hummus paired with warm pita, and be sure to sip on the refreshing Greek lemon soda. Reasonably priced for the high-quality fare, this place is a must-visit for anyone yearning for a taste of Greece without leaving the city. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit.

Ordered a set of 20 and a set of 10 traditional wings - garlic parmesan, chipotle barbecue, and hot. It took about 15 minutes to get our wings. The wings were well-sauced and had plenty of carrots and celery. However, the blue cheese ranch on the side didn't taste good. I wish they provided ranch instead. Garlic parmesan tasted good. Loved the shredded cheese topping on it. Chipotle barbecue was very well-sauced. Tasty and fresh. Hot was not hot enough, it tasted more like a medium. Overall we enjoyed these wings!

I stopped by this charming bakery for a quick sweet treat and was pleased with the experience. The selection of goodies was impressive, with reasonable prices to match. The open bakery design allowed for a peek at the magic happening behind the scenes, adding to the overall appeal.

The staff greeted me with warm smiles and were quite attentive, ensuring my questions were answered with enthusiasm. I opted for the seasonal fruit tostada, priced at $5.50, and it did not disappoint. It struck the right balance with a generous array of fruit atop a crust that complemented without overwhelming.

The seating area provided a cozy spot to enjoy my dessert. The bakery also offers whole cakes and a variety of sweet pastries, tempting me for future visits. Definitely a delightful spot for anyone with a sweet tooth!

I wonder why Taiwanese fare has taken this long to reach mass appeal in New York, but I am here for its boom. Win Son, Ho Foods, and 886 are part of the new generation of Taiwanese eateries appealing to traditionalists and newbs to the cuisine alike. 886 has the most eclectic menu and fun vibe of the bunch, and while Taiwanesse food purists may scoff at their renditions of classic dishes, you can't deny the flavors they deliver.Over my handful of visits here I consistently order the pineapple & shrimp. It's the most basic bitch order on their menu, but it is undeniably tasty, with crispy battered shrimp covered in a light mayo sauce and complemented with sweet pieces of pineapple to counter the other flavors and textures in the dish. I could tell you about the other dishes, but I'm of the mind (at least at this very moment) that everyone has different palates and you should just go with a group and order a variety of dishes based on your predilections. If you're a sake fan be sure to order some Brooklyn Kura. I also love to guzzle down cans of their delicious lychee beer--that stuff tastes like juice.Just don't piss off the host lest you want to feel the wrath of Steff. That's my one asterisk for this place.

After our initial lunch plans fell through, we stumbled upon a Vietnamese gem in Ctown. While the menu boasted an intriguing Vietnamese cheeseburger, we opted for other items. Service was commendably swift, and upon the arrival of our dishes, we were delighted by the ample portions. All in all, if you find yourself in the area, this eatery is a stellar pick.

Cocktails to go and packaged incredibly conveniently (available for pick up and also on Grubhub). The Craftsman has a large variety of cocktails to go (not just canned margaritas like other places are offering). The best part about this is they've packaged the cocktail into plastic bottles as you see in the picture so you don't have to drink it right away. I was also given cups of ice separately so I can use it for when I am ready to drink. In addition, they also sell frose! I went a bit early so wasn't able to try but there are four flavors I'm definitely going back for. The person working there (whom I believe was likely the owner) was also very nice. This is a local business I'm happy to support.

I recently visited Gogi Grill, a standout Korean BBQ fast-casual eatery, and had a fantastic experience. Opting for the hearty bulgogi rice bowl, I was pleased by the generous portion size. The ordering process is intuitive, similar to other bowl-centric places: pick your style (bowl, salad, burrito, or tacos), select a base (choices include white/purple rice, kimchi fried rice, or japchae vermicelli), and choose a protein. While they offer a variety, the bulgogi and galbi are must-tries. You also get to pick four toppings, and I savored the combination of white radish, spinach, bean sprouts, and kimchi, though a few extra topping options wouldn't hurt. Finally, the sauce selection is diverse, ranging from spicy gochujang to a zesty cilantro/lime. If you're in the area, or Hoboken for that matter, Gogi Grill is worth a visit for a flavorful and filling Korean-inspired meal.

Title: A Culinary Journey Worth Every Bite

From the moment we stepped into the restaurant, the level of hospitality set the stage for an unforgettable dining experience. The warmth and attentiveness of the staff in the cozy and welcoming setting immediately put us at ease.

As aficionados of culinary artistry, we were in for a treat with the 16-course omakase. Each course surpassed the last with its freshness and exquisite preparation; it was the kind of meal you'd hope to savor endlessly. Those with particular tastes need not fret—the staff are eager to accommodate, though I recommend embracing the chef's masterful creations for full enjoyment.

The highlights were many, with toro, uni, caviar, and truffle making standout appearances. Of particular note were the crab with caviar, the divine scallop, and the unforgettable ikura/uni/truffle toast. The special Thai basil-spiced tuna with its crispy shallot and spicy dressing left a lasting impression.

The sake selection complemented the feast perfectly, enhancing the overall gastronomic experience. Although our visits may be infrequent due to distance, this gem has certainly secured a spot on our must-return list.

Had a very enjoyable meal here last night. From the outside you can't tell, but the interior is beautifully decorated and extends quite far back. The service here was excellent. When we were seated I asked if there was any outlet to charge my dying phone. The maître d' offered to take my phone and charged it for me behind the bar with their own cord. I thought that was a nice gesture. While perusing the menu I was thrilled to see that they serve dim sum even in the evening hours. My friend was cold and ordered the egg drop soup. It was served in a very large bowl, piping hot and delicious. We ordered dim some as well: Turnip cakes: large portion, absolutely delicious. Nice with the hoisin dipping sauce.This was my favorite dish of the night. We also had shrimp dumplings: this was my second favorite dish. Beautifully steamed shrimp dumplings 4!to a portion. We tried the chicken dumplings as well. 3 per portion. The chicken was ground with some greens. My friend enjoyed this the most. We also tried the  duck buns. We found these to be slightly overcooked and could have used more of the sweet sauce. The buns themselves were soft and fluffy. Then we also ordered an entrée: scallops in house sauce. The waiter informed us that they are usually deep-fried but we could get them stir fried instead. We opted for this. This was our least favorite dish because it was much hotter than expected. There were tons of red pepper flakes. I also would have liked a heads up that this dish is prepared with only asparagus. I do like asparagus but it is something that I don't prefer to order too often. Overall our dishes were fresh and delicious and the service was excellent. I would definitely come back here.

I've been wanting to try Petite Boucherie and finally made it for my birthday dinner. It also happens to be the last day of winter Restaurant Week so we definitely took advantage of the special menu.Here is the review breakdown:Ambiance: the ambiance and decor of the restaurant is very chic and romantic. It looks very much like a Parisian brasserie with dim lighting and candles everywhere. It's a perfect place for a date or an intimate get together with friends. Service: service was great! The servers were attentive without being overbearing. They also gladly exchanged my food because it was cold. Food: everything we ordered was great, from the appetizers to dessert! The only reason they don't have 5 stars is that my entreé came out very cold. It's as if, it sat for a while but they did redeem themselves by exchanging it. I got the escargot for starters and it was very tasty!! The sauce was so rich and delicious! For my main entreé, I got the duck confit and again, aside from coming out cold, it was delicious when replaced. My friend ordered the ravioli with truffle which I loved! For dessert, I got the chocolate souffle that they were nice enough to put a candle on for my birthday.Overall, I would recommend Petite Boucherie. The food was excellent and I was very happy that they didn't treat us like second class citizens even though we were there for Restaurant Week.

Ben's Pizzeria might be best known for its cameo in "Men In Black," but these days, its pizza garners less acclaim. The pies, once lauded, have since settled into the realm of the ordinary - not unpleasant, but far from the pinnacle of New York's pizza scene. The service comes with a side of authentic New York attitude, which may enhance the experience for tourists seeking the full city vibe.

On an impromptu early Sunday morning visit, we were delighted to find this gem without the usual lines and decided to stop for breakfast. The menu offerings were enticing, so we opted for an array of churng funs and jook. Each dish was a pleasant surprise, with the churng funs boasting a soft, fresh texture, and the jook seasoned to savory perfection. This eatery is definitely a great spot for anyone looking for a quick and delicious meal.

This is a cool place with friendly staff and great tacos.  The chile relleno taco is the bomb -- so complex and yummy.  Big open space, just the right amount of effort to be chill and hip and yet friendly.  Highly recommended!

Is small better? Is cozy on a windy March night warmer? Is a third jewel in a crown sparkling?The answer to all these questions are: You better believe it baby!My friend Rochelle and I ate lunch on a freezing day in January at the Spring Street location. We loved its smallness but rustic vibe and delicious Sicilian fare and of course the hanging pots and pans. I've learned that pasta served in a steel pot tastes buonissumo. I've learned great things come in small packages. I've also learned love thy neighbor, especially when you're thisclose and can practically twirl each other's spaghetti!So tonight, we decided to try the Prince Street location, which if you can believe, is smaller than the aforementioned establishment.When we checked in, we were greeted warmly and were given somewhat of a choice of seating. We sat near a window, where in the summer opens up for al fresco dining. We were told the specials as water and lemon were poured in our glasses.There was a special pasta, tagliatelle in a green sauce and veal shank.We had lots of questions about the appetizers: is the Arancini Ball filled with meat rice and cheese? Yes. Is the eggplant prepared Parmesan style? Yes. The fried calamari that was eaten at a nearby table looked great. And of course the bruschetta dressed with bright cherry tomatoes looked mouth watering.There were other delicious pastas on the menu that were quite different than Spring. For instance the Pasta Alla Norma is served with spaghetti versus the tubular pasta. There are pastas served with mushrooms and clams. I actually showed the waiter my photos from Spring and stated he would ask us at the end of our meals which we enjoyed more. Well.. that would be quite hard to answer.So here's what deliciousness we dined on:The house bread, none for me, served in a cute wooden bowl with a saucy spread.For appetizer, we shared the Eggplant Parmesan served in a small skillet. It was lightly breaded and the sauce was vodka style, very different. It was soft and a spoon was necessary.For main courses, I ate Pasta Alla Norma which is eggplant rolls stuffed with tomatoes and ricotta cheese and spaghetti. It was delicious but served al dente. I would have liked it a bit warmer.Rochelle ate Vitello Tonnato which is veal served in a tuna sauce.The 80s soundtrack playing on the speakers were drowned out by the diners talking and eating heartily.The desserts were simple: Tiramisu, Creme Brûlée,Warm Chocolate cake with Vanilla Ice Cream.We shared the Creme Brûlée which was light after a hearty meal.So what's the answer.. is this better than Spring?No,but equally great.Next up: the Thompson Street location.

Title: A Bite of Perfection at One of NY's Finest Pizza Spots

If you're a pizza aficionado in search of a new haunt, look no further. I've stumbled upon what could easily be hailed as one of the best pizza joints in New York. Their 'Bee Sting' pizza is a masterful creation that tantalizes the taste buds with its flawless blend of sweet, salty, and spicy flavors.

The pizza boasts a thin, yet delightfully chewy crust, topped with sublime cheese that stretches with every bite. Don't let the 'personal pizza' tag fool you; the size is just right, leaving you satisfyingly full without the regret of overindulgence.

In a city brimming with pizzerias, this one stands out with its unique offerings. Do yourself a favor and give this place a try. Your palate will thank you.

Title: A Rainy Day Ramen Delight in NYC

On a dreary NYC morning, my spirits were lifted after seeking refuge in a cozy ramen spot in the Upper West Side. Despite the rainstorm, a relatively brisk wait landed us a warm table inside, a much-preferred alternative to the damp outdoor seating.

I indulged in the kuro tonkotsu ramen, a generous portion heartily topped with tender chashu pork, shishito peppers, and a perfectly soft-boiled egg nestled atop delicate thin noodles. The broth was a standout—creamy, rich, and masterfully balancing the hearty ingredients. With a ladle in hand, I eagerly navigated through the inviting bowl, each spoonful a comforting embrace against the rain-soaked city outside.

Service was a highlight—our friendly waitress ensured that our wait for food was minimal even amidst the bustling atmosphere. This place is undeniably a gem for anyone seeking solace with a delicious bowl of ramen on the Upper West Side.

During a bustling holiday Sunday at 1 PM, my party of eight was delighted to be seated within an hour at this stunningly decorated restaurant, a true visual feast for the season. The hostess was exceptionally kind, offering helpful advice and even recommending a nearby coffee spot to enjoy as we waited. 

The ambiance was elevated by the exquisite holiday decor, which stood out as one of the most beautiful settings I've experienced this year. The menu was tempting, leading me to choose the French toast, paired with a shared fig & prosciutto focaccia and a refreshing rosemary's spritz. Although the flavors promised something special, the French toast's disappointing chill dampened the experience. Nevertheless, hunger trumped perfection, and I consumed it despite the temperature mishap.

A highlight of the brunch menu was the inclusion of a complimentary drink—choices of a mimosa, spritz, or sangria which was a pleasant touch. Despite the French toast faux pas, the overall experience was marred only slightly by this culinary hiccup.

Been wanting to try this place for the longest time and finally decided to make a reservation with a friend who was visiting. We tried a variety of dishes to share. We got the 2 items that's off the menu that they have everyday which were the pork buns and the rice cakes. We also tried the scallops, cauliflower, and steak. I think everything was really great quality of food. My favorite would be the pork buns. My friend really liked the steak. Definitely think we could have done with one less dish, which would have been the rice cakes. Good but would not say its very unique. Very flavorful and good though. It is spicy though so keep that in mind if you can't handle spicy foods. Everything was seasoned appropriately and service was great. We spent about $80-$90 per person with drinks though so definitely is a place you would splurge on or a special occasion place.

Title: Stunning Views, Mediocre Drinks, and Mixed Service

My spouse and I visited this restaurant on a bright sunny day, drawn by the allure of drinks and the promise of sweeping views of Central Park. We made a reservation in advance, which I highly recommend. The reservation process was straightforward, and the staff pleasantly fulfilled our request for a window table with the anticipated park view, which was absolutely stunning.

However, the drinks didn't quite live up to the grandeur of the setting. They were merely okay—nothing to write home about. My husband was disappointed when the bar didn't have one of the specialty drinks he was eager to try, and no explanation was given, which was a bit puzzling. Furthermore, the prices were steep, which seems to be more for the location and the view rather than the quality of the beverages.

One perk was the ability to step outside and fully immerse ourselves in the beauty of the surroundings, a feature that I wish was also available on the Central Park side.

Unfortunately, the experience was somewhat marred by the poor attitude of the staff positioned downstairs by the elevators, who were inexplicably rude. While the breath-taking views are a major draw for this establishment, a re-evaluation of customer service and the drink selection might enhance the overall experience significantly.

Reasonably priced pizza in one of NYCs most expensive neighborhoods. This is a tiny, tiny pizza spot but what they lack in restaurant size they deliver in some super tasty pizza. My husband grabbed a slice of pizza and I ordered the Sicilian style with pepperoni, both were delicious. The line forms to the left, as soon as you walk in, to order. Pay for your slice to the right. You can eat in if you wish but there are no tables. They have two ledges on either side of the restaurant. We took our pizza to go. If you're in the area and looking for a quick, reasonably priced meal, Prince St pizza fits the bill.

After a 10 mile run in Central Park, my friends and I needed to fuel up. Half wanted breakfast and the other wanted lunch since it was 11:30am. We walked around and landed here because diner food felt right and we knew there would be variety! It was a packed house but we were seated immediately at the last open booth. Waitress then came quickly to take our order. Now, the food was ok. I got a Chef Special Moussaka with a Manhattan Clam Chowder on the side. Nothing special but hit the spot. I thought it also came with a small Greek Salad, but I was wrong. The waitress was incredibly nice and still brought one out for me as courtesy and didn't charge me! Customer service goes a long way (and an extra star)!

I arrived at the restaurant around 6 PM this Monday evening. During that Monday and yesterday, TabeTomo was having its 1 year anniversary buy one get one free event which is why my friend and I decided to go. Additionally, if you had liked the TabeTomo page they gave you a free draft beer which just goes so well with the ramen and was a nice perk as well. As soon as I entered with my friend, we were seated right away. The hostess who sat us down though had the grumpiest look on her face which lasted from the moment we entered the restaurant till the time we left. I don't think I saw her crack a smile once. Additionally, even though there were three open seats they chose to sit us down right next to a super dusty and dirty window as well an open trash can instead of a cleaner and more comfortable seat that I wanted. After that fiasco though, service improved immensely. Our server was super friendly and helpful. She got our orders in immediately and food was also brought out quickly as well. For appetizers we ordered the egg omelette as well as the fried chicken. The egg omelette was delicious, it was soaked in sauce and came with some minced radishes which really paired well together. The fried chicken was average but I thoroughly enjoyed the egg based tartar sauce it came with. For our actual meal, we got the jiro ramen and dipping ramen to share. Both were great. The flavors were pretty similar but just a bit more robust for the dipping ramen. I also liked how the veggies soaked up more of the flavors in the dipping ramen than for the jiro ramen so if I was to go next time I would probably just stick to the dipping ramen. When we got our check though we noticed they forgot to put the BOGO deal on but thankfully they changed it right away. All in all, apart from some hiccups and the grumpy hostess it was actually a pretty great meal for a cold, rainy day.

Title: A Casual Beer Spot with Hits and Misses

I swung by this local spot on a bustling Saturday afternoon, intrigued by the lively atmosphere. Although the crowd certainly illustrated its popularity, it was apparent that they were short on staff, which meant a bit of a wait for service. Nevertheless, the outdoor seating was the prime real estate here—snagging a table there would be ideal, though they're quickly occupied.

The beer selection is commendable and fairly priced at about $8, aligning with what you'd expect from a similar establishment. But the true culinary highlight was the brussel sprouts. They arrived steaming hot, beautifully paired with onions and pancetta, and were simply delicious.

On the downside, the hummus and pita were a bit of a letdown. The hummus suffered from an unappealing thin and watery consistency and an odd flavor that left us scratching our heads.

To sum it up, this restaurant is a decent choice for anyone looking to enjoy a cold beer and some standout snacks—just do yourself a favor and skip the hummus.

With mealpal, I get to try different places and this is one of the places I want to try because of the cheese pie.If you never had a cheese pie, it's a combination of bread, cheese and raw egg.  The bread is almost like a diamond shape (think of a boat).  In the middle of the bread, the bread is removed and there is melted cheese with a raw egg on top that you mix together.  Afterwards, you pull the bread and dip into the mixture.  It's so good and so heavy that you might have food coma afterwards.I didn't expect something similar to the description above since this is take out lunch.  The food wasn't ready when I arrived so I was able to walk around.  They have Russian decor that makes it home feeling and someone's dining room.  I waited 20 mins for the meal and the hostess apologize profusely and kept me updated.Not that the food was wasn't hot.  The cheese solidified by the time I returned to the office and this isn't my issue.  My disappointment is that the cheese pie was cut up into quarters so I couldn't heat up the cheese bread in the microwave without the cheese melting all over.  Overall not a bad meal but definitely order the cheese pie to eat in.  Hope to try the other items one day.

During a leisurely stroll on the High Line in Chelsea, my curiosity was piqued by a charming eatery, reputed for its stellar brunch offerings. True to the buzz, it didn't disappoint. Opting for the warmth of the interior, thanks to the chilly breeze outside, we were immediately struck by the inviting juxtaposition of its industrial facade and cozy ambiance.

The waitstaff greeted us with friendly smiles and efficiency that meant our orders arrived swiftly. The Bubby's breakfast was a hearty classic, offering a no-frills but satisfying plate of eggs, a choice of breakfast meats, a single slice of toast, and a modest serving of skillet potatoes.

I indulged in the market omelette, a generous concoction stuffed with goat cheese, tomatoes, corn, and a delightful pesto topping. The additional choice of salad, fries, or more of those tasty skillet potatoes completed the meal. Despite the size, my appetite, fueled by our planned day of walking, was up to the task.

The coffee service was impeccable, with hot brews and prompt refills. This spot is evidently a local favorite for brunch, and it's clear why. As a bonus, the best ice-cream from Apple Hills Creamery is served right next door for a sweet follow-up. Admittedly, prices here reflect the trendy location in the meatpacking district and the freshness of the food, but it's a worthwhile treat for any brunch enthusiast.

Wow.  This was the restaurant that I had tried to get into for years and never had any luck.  I had hoped that I hadn't built up my expectations too much in the last 5 years.  We were lucky enough to get counter seats on a Friday night.  When we entered the place looked empty but I soon found out they seat people in 15 min increments so the food could be properly served to everyone.  We opted to go all in.  We went with the wine paring and truffle (black truffle season) addition.  Our first course was a delicious caviar based dish. A good start to the night but nothing would compare to the 2nd course.  The 2nd course was uni on a grilled brioche with a generous portion of the truffle.  I have had all of these ingredients before but nothing I have ever had compares to this bite.  They suggested eating it in 2 bites.  I savored it and made it last 5.  This wasn't just the best dish of the night.  This was the best dish I've ever had in my life.  I could describe each course but instead I will just tell you everything was inventive and delicious.  The progression of the meal was thoughtful and perfect.  I loved the theatrics or watching the kitchen.   It was amazing how smooth it all looked.   Chef Ramirez maintains a very calm kitchen.  Watching him assemble the dishes and meticulously prep the ingredients was one of the highlights.  He was kind enough to spend some time talking to us and tell us a little about himself.This was my 4th 3 Michelin star restaurant.  I believe food wise this was the most complete and adventurous meal I've had.  The service at others is a little more refined and I understand why people would knock Chefs Table for this.  I wouldn't and couldn't.  The food speaks for itself here.

I have been here twice for dinner. They are fairly busy but the tables turn over quickly. I have had some of the appetizers, ramen, and other mains.  I really like how clear the menu is on what is included in the ramen bowls and what kind of broth it is. The food is flavorful and comes out quickly. There is also a video on a loop of how they make the ramen, which I found very interesting. It is a small restaurant with a surprising number of families with young children visiting here.

Title: A Cozy Spot with Hearty Fare in K-Town

My dining experience at this bustling K-Town gem was rather delightful! Arriving at 9 PM to a packed house, our 20-minute wait was a small mercy. The ambiance is charming, adorned with twinkling lights and creative soju bottle decor.

We indulged in the budae jungol, which, while not spicy, was satisfying—especially the unique addition of pasta. The star, however, was the gargantuan watermelon soju. Warning: it's deceptively large, better suited for groups of four than for a pair.

Though not the pinnacle of budae jungol, the dish was commendable. This spot is perfect for those seeking a convivial atmosphere complemented by good food and drink. K-Town visitors, take note!

I recently dined at this charming restaurant and found the experience to be a delightful mix of flavors and leisure. While the food, ranging from the savory escargots and crab cake to the delectable spaghetti and indulgent chocolate cake, was exceptionally delicious, the service tempo was notably unhurried. This slow pace did, however, lend itself to a relaxed atmosphere perfect for a lengthy friends' chat.

We only hit a snag with the initially ordered chicken liver, which didn't meet our expectations. The staff handled this gracefully, with our attentive waitress facilitating an effortless exchange for an additional crab cake - a commendable display of customer service. Overall, despite the slower rhythm of meal service, the restaurant delivered a satisfying culinary experience, ideal for those who aren’t in a rush and enjoy lingering over good food and conversation.

Probably one of the best slice places in Midtown, if not the whole city. Definitely a stop on any NY pizza tour I'd recommend. The pictures of Anthony Bourdain (RIP) amongst others eating there and it being always packed do not lie. That said, it is quite expensive for what it is, be prepared to pay upwards of $15 for a couple slices and a drink. There are cheaper places that have comparable level pizza in my opinion but still can't deny it as a great place.

Do you love-a da Baklava? I do. I love baklava. But good baklava is hard to come by. This shop has such a beautiful variety of baklavas filled with walnuts, pistachios, and chocolate. You serve yourself from these shelves. Almost like a candy store. The pastries and desserts are priced by weight so you can even mix and match if you feel a full sized dessert is too much! I tried the classic and the pistachio filled baklavas. All of which are amazing! They also sell other traditional Greek desserts as well as a full menu of savory items. I will def be back to try those. And of course come back for the baklava!

Alice's Tea House is a delightfully quaint spot perfect for tea enthusiasts and those in search of a cozy nook to enjoy some light fare. The atmosphere is a seamless blend of comfort and whimsy, enhanced by the eclectic and charmingly mismatched teaware.

The scones are a particular highlight, with a delightful range to satisfy different palates. The buttermilk and mixed berry options are personal favorites, both classic and executed to perfection. For the more health-conscious patrons, the vegan apple cinnamon scone is an unexpected joy, indistinguishable from its non-vegan counterparts in its deliciousness.

While the chocolate chip ginger scone is a quality choice, I found the chocolate somewhat dominant, potentially masking the ginger's piquancy. Perhaps a peach ginger iteration might provide a more balanced flavor experience.

The touted pumpkin caramel scone, recommended by our server as a top choice, unfortunately, fell short of expectations. Those with a less intense sweet tooth might find the combination of the sugary scone with gooey caramel topping to be overwhelming.

A word to the early birds: arriving at opening time may come with a short wait, as the kitchen may need a few extra minutes to gear up for the day's service. As a friendly suggestion for the keen, arrive a tad after the doors open for an undisrupted tea experience. Overall, Alice's Tea House is a charming establishment that I'd certainly recommend for a delightful tea and scone indulgence.

Title: A Shift in Authenticity at a Beloved Noodle Spot

I've been a loyal patron of this spot, drawn repeatedly by what I've considered the most authentic Hong Kong-style beef noodles in NYC. My experience has been nothing short of culinary bliss—until my latest visit. Regrettably, the noodles lacked their usual flair. It sparked a suspicion that a new chef might be behind this shift in taste, a change that's diminished the need to venture all the way to Chinatown for that once unmatchable authenticity. On a brighter note, the Hong Kong-style milk tea remains a genuine delight, retaining its originality and charm.

Fantastic food!  Just got in town and stopped for a quick bite. Super fast service and delicious vittles. I had the French onion soup. The soup was hot and done just right. My husband had the wings and curly fries. Everything was great!  Super nice waitress too!

This is my go to brunch or lunch spot. It's great that this is one of few places serve lunch until 4pm. I almost don't want to tell people since I want to keep it myself... Food is always consistent and service is nice. A few outside table is a big bonus for a nice day on this surprisingly quiet street near busy Union Sq Park. The lunch menu is a bit healthier side for my taste. Try the avocado dish or Tuna salad if you want to have something light!

The Fritturella Mista is a must-get for calamari lovers. This is the first place I've been to that serves fried shrimp with the squid, which was a great touch especially for my partner who prefers shrimp much more than squid. It came out freshly fried so it was piping hot and crispy. The pasta dishes were all perfectly cooked and came out fresh and hot as well. I loved the fresh basil and layer of cheese on the fusilli silani, but the sausage was extremely salty. No complaints about the fettuccine alla bolognese. Overall, the only thing that I would have changed was the saltiness of the fusilli silani, but everything else was great.

Title: High Hopes not Fully Met at Trendy Spot

After a pit stop at Boba Guys, my friend and I grabbed a quick lunch at a local eatery previously spotlighted on Chef's Table, which set the bar high for our culinary expectations.

One of the dishes we tried was their Pork Musubi bites, which sadly earned a mere 2 out of 5. Priced at $5 each, the bites were unexpectedly tiny and left our wallets feeling a little emptier than our stomachs. The plum's sweetness in the musubi was a jarring note for my palate, which didn't align with my taste preferences.

On a brighter note, the Gyukotsu scored a solid 4 out of 5. Diving into tsukemen for the first time was quite an experience, with a generous serving of noodles that did not disappoint. The short rib was remarkably tender and enjoyable, paired with a rich, hearty beef broth, though it didn't quite knock my socks off.

Overall, this place didn't live up to the hype for me. While not a complete letdown, it's not at the top of my list for a ramen revisit. There are other joints I'd prefer to explore before considering a return here.

A nice setting in the heart of Midtown. Overall: 4/5Food: 3.8/5Value: 4/5 (lunch) Service: 5/5 Atmosphere: 5/5 We had the pre fixe lunch, with options like the sunchoke soup, duck pâté, Atlantic salmon, and limone dessert. I had high expectations since it's a Michelin 1 star. An absolutely beautiful setting in the Langham Hotel on Fifth Avenue, very luxurious. However the food was a bit mixed. The duck pâté wasn't plated that nicely and was very crumbly - I prefer pâté to be smooth and creamy but this was a very country style one. Did not expect that from the description on the menu. Sunchoke soup was rich, creamy, and delicious though. Salmon was over cooked as was the quinoa base. The lemon tarte dessert was quite small (like a 3x3 inch square) although delectable, but it was accompanied by a grapefruit flavored ice pieces which was quite odd. Overall worth a visit especially for the experience but probably not one of my usual spots.

I came in specifically for the dessert (I saw it on insta) after having dinner at another location, but it looked nothing like it and seemed like they were already prepared and waiting in a fridge. Not sure HOW it was supposed to come out but didn't feel like love was put into making it. Wasn't impressed by the fried chips for the table. Chef came out to check on us. Very nice man. Ambience and bathroom very nice. I might come back again to try another dish, but so many places in NY to try, they normally have to catch me on the first try for me to repeat.

I decided to run out and get a quick bite and Le Sia had recently opened. I went in and was seated immediately. They had been doing some work on the front door and I thought they were closed but they stepped aside and I walked in. The menu is a little confusing and I was encouraged to try the skewers, which turned out to be very tasty. I started with the tiger shrimp [2] with a piece of pineapple in between drizzled with a white sauce. The shrimps are small but tasty. I moved onto the Red willow lamb skewer and then tried the chicken, the shrimp [ a large shrimp on a skewer with the shell-no way to eat this except to peel by hand-messy!!!] The squid was good as well but 4 small pieces. A normal sized person with an appetite would need to have at least 10-15 skewers to feel full. It is just not enough food. The food was good and the skewers are not overpriced but....the staff was helpful in explaining the menu and making suggestions. I will make a return visit in a few weeks to try something which may be more substantial.

Stopped for a midday lunch and some CHOCOLATE! We made a reservation ahead of time thankfully, otherwise we most likely would have waited at least 30 minutes. Our server was friendly but went missing a lot. He left empty plates on our table for a good 10 minutes. There is a good variety of food options, some do incorporate chocolate. I had the southwest veggie burger and I was pretty happy with it. Their aioli was delish, loved their waffle fries. The bun on my burger was soggy so I had to take that off. The burger itself looked kind of like mashed beans and rice together, it definitely benefited from their aioli sauce, otherwise it wasnt too flavorful alone. I also ordered the salted caramel dark chocolate hot coco on the side. That was very rich! Not a huge fan of their mugs because my mug had caramel dripping down the side so there wasnt quite a classy and clean way to sip up the chocolatey goodness. But it was oh soooo good. Overall, I'd come again since prices weren't top bad and the food was pretty good. Perhaps only for dessert since they clearly have that part down.
Rodrigo is the best bartender! Best margs. Best conversation.Love this place! Food is amazing, drinks never disappoint!Fajita Monday's are my fave!

Super small spot but the food is great and worth the wait. Anytime I hear about a halal spot I definitely gotta give it a chance and I'm glad I ended up here. The seating inside is small and a bit cramped, the decorations are super cute and the staff were great and super friendly! I want to say I went with their Pad See Eew, I can't recall the name right now. The noodles were delicious and full of flavor and the chicken was juicy and seasoned well. They also have a great drink menu and do virgins drinks as well. Their mango mojito was perfect!

My friend and I were looking for a spot so we went to Yelp to assist us. We found this spot and decided to try it out. The lower level was small but we were able to get seated fast. The staff wasn't super friendly but we decided to still give it a try. I ordered the lunch special with this Kha Pow(basil chicken dish). It came with a spring roll and I ordered Thai tea. The dish was worth is staying. It was really flavorful and I enjoyed it. The spring roll was also really good. Loved the Thai tea. Actually ordered a second one to go.  I tried to actually go back before I left NYC but unfortunately the rest of the weekend, they did cash only. We had a large group the last night and was super disappointed that they didn't accept cards. I would return to try other items while in town.

Title: Convenient Bite, Hit-or-Miss Dishes

I popped into this spot not as a dining destination, but more as an afterthought to a retail therapy session in nearby shoe stores. To my surprise, the kale salad I ordered, swayed by some decent Yelp snapshots, surpassed my usual pasta-pizza-cookies preference. It was one of the better salads I've tasted, fresh and flavorful. My friend, however, faced disappointment with a rather mediocre pizza that didn't warrant finishing. On the brighter side, the Chardonnay from Wolffer Estate Vineyard was a local delight, elevating the overall experience. If you find yourself shopping in the area and need a quick bite, the salad might be your best bet, but I’d skip the pizza.

Title: A Gastronomic Triumph in NYC: Estiatorio Milos

From the moment we stepped into Estiatorio Milos for our first night in New York City, the experience was impeccable. Having dined at their Las Vegas location with four from our party of six, NYC’s Milos not only matched but exceeded our already high expectations.

Our waitstaff shone with patience and expertise, their demystification of the menu allowed us to indulge effortlessly. The standout starters included the grilled octopus, succulent little neck clams, and an inventive veggie tower—all of which set the bar incredibly high. Each dish was a testament to the culinary prowess of the kitchen.

The shared Greek salad was nothing short of a revelation with tomatoes and feta that could only be described as the freshest of our lifetime. Our main course, a selection of two fish varieties, was met with sighs of contented defeat—we simply couldn't do justice to them after the feast that preceded.

Regrettably, we bypassed dessert, a decision made with heavy hearts and even heavier stomachs. My recommendation? Visit Estiatorio Milos with an appetite so grand that you can explore every corner of their sumptuous menu. For epicureans and casual diners alike, this restaurant is a must-visit when in The Big Apple.

Title: A Hearty Brunch at Maison Pickle

Maison Pickle epitomizes classic American comfort food with its generous, Texas-sized portions. During our brunch visit, we were eager to dive into the iconic Chicken & Challah French Toast duo as well as the standalone French toast. The crispy yet tender chicken was paired perfectly with three thick slices of indulgent, fluffy challah—a struggle to finish even between two! A word of caution for those less enthusiastic about syrup: request it on the side to avoid an overly sweet experience. Despite the syrupy enthusiasm, it stands out as one of the top chicken & waffles renditions available.

Favorites: Chicken & French Toast
- Food: 5/5
- Service & Speed: 5/5 (remarkably quick)
- Price: $$ (value is impressive)
- Ambiance: Laid-back and spacious

Will we be back? Absolutely, and we'd recommend it without hesitation. A solid 5/5 on the return-and-recommend-o-meter.

Cuisine: 7Service: 5Decor: 8Value: 4Overall: 5Honestly, if you are going to charge ridiculous prices for dishes I can order in Flushing for 1/2 or 1/3 of the price, then it better be much, much better. I get the nicer ambience and Manhattan rent thing, but the quality of the food needs to match the environment, and so does the service.Once again, the overall cuisine was quite decent, but $56 for their signature Boneless Pork Trotter w. Abalone should have blown me away ... ... it sadly didn't. On the other hand, the Brown Sugar Glazed Peking Duck was maybe the best in the city, flavorful moist meat, not greasy, with the crispiest of all skins. Though expensive at $36 for a small portion, that was worth the price of admission.Other highlights included the Fatty Beef in Sour Soup and Stir Fried Cabbage w. Soy Sauce. Also, we got the General Tso's Chicken for laughs, but it was actually quite well done. Lastly, all the teas and beverages were delicious, especially the Peach Oolong Tea w. Hand Whipped Cheese Foam ($10).Then there was the Crab Tofu ($26), how do I rate this imposter of a dish. Truth be told, it tasted quite delicious, but it's meant to fool those who have never had this before. The original dish from Shanghai uses a tremendous amount of mitten crab tamale and roe to create a extremely flavorful sauce for the tofu. Uluh uses a little bit of crab essence (likely blue crab, but definitely not the super expensive mitten crabs from China) and mix it with a lot of salted duck egg yolk instead. The markup on this plate is absolutely insane.Lastly, just stay away from all the Shanghainese dim sums. Black Truffle Pork Soup Dumplings (four for $14) lack any truffle flavor, while the Sticky Rice Shumai and Scallion Pancake were absolutely epic fails. I guess that's my fault. Should have known better to order Shanghainese dim sum in a restaurant who's head chefs are Cantonese and Szechuan, regardless of what the waitress recommended.As for the service, we felt like it was often absent. We jokingly said that they had ghost servers, who were friendly when they showed their faces every once in a while. My friend even thought the waitress that took our order was cute, but she only came back to our table once more during the nearly two hour meal.Would I pay such crazy prices for Chinese food again? Yeah, if it's worth it. As for Uluh, I might be back for that amazing Oolong Peach drink and excellent Peking Duck. Otherwise, I'll stick to normal Chinese restaurants where I can get 95% of this stuff for 1/2 of the price or less.

I went to the Greek Kitchen with my boyfriend for dinner on New Year's Day because we were craving some quality Greek food. Let me tell you, we were not disappointed! The ambiance of the resturant was lovely, we sat at a small table for two next to the window. It was secluded and romantic, which was just what we were going for. ( I will post a photo) The portions were HUGE! We started off with some champagne to celebrate the new year, since we didn't get any the night before. It was a Greek champagne, that was sweet and perfect for the two of us. We then ordered the taziki, the middle eastern salad and the kalamarakia for our appetizers. I thought all of them were wonderful, very plentiful and very filling. We enjoyed each of them! But my favorite was definitely the Middle Eastern Salad. The vegetables in the salad were all very fresh, it came with dolmades which were delicious; but the feta cheese had to be my absolute favorite. It may have been the best feta I have ever had. And they didn't cheap out on it either; they gave a large portion of feta cheese on the top of the salad, which was excellent. We were so full after we ordered our appetizers that we decided to split our entree. We ordered the lamb sish kebab, which came with a side salad and our choice of either rice, Greek fries, roasted potatoes or orzo. We chose the orzo. The orzo was the only reason why this review didn't get five stars. It was the only thing I didn't really care for. It was served cold and lacked flavor. But other than that; Greek Kitchen was excellent! The servers were great and on top of their game, and the portions were plentiful and delicious! I would highly recommend The Greek Kitchen to anyone walking by looking for a wonderful meal with great ambiance, great food and great service! I will definitely be returning very soon!

On my 4th time that I have visited New York City!!! And when we got to Koreatown while hopping on the the New York's City Subway from Flushing New York!!! While taking a walk with my family around Koreatown and when it was getting close to lunch time...As we were walking around at New York's Koreantown and looking at what good Korean Restaurant to eat at... Until we came across to New Wonjo Restaurant after discovering this New Wonjo Restaurant so from there we made our final decision and said we will be eating lunch at this place!!!As we walked in for our 1st time to this New Won Jo Korean Restaurant of New York City Korean town!!! When we got in and waiting for the hostess to escort to our table... And the good thing was it wasn't that crowded yet so the hostess took us to our table right away!!!  While looking through the menu and we knew already in what we wanted to order... So from there we ended up ordering some Sushi, and 3 orders of fried rice which was 2 beef fried rice and chicken fried rice!!! Before ordering those yummy items our hostess brought us some kimchis as appetizers which is a famous thing that most Koreans eat!!! Now that, I ate lunch here with my family for our 1st time at this New Won Jo Korean Restaurant of Korean town of New York City!!! All I can say is that this Korean Restaurant was really good especially eating KimChi's, Fried Rice, and some Sushi!!! If your a tourist like me, and if your visting Korean town of New York City and looking around for a good Korean Restaurant to eat at... My suggestion to you yelpers and non yelpers go to the New Wonjo Restaurant it's a really good place to go to!!! While enjoying your vacation at the City that never sleeps which is New York City!!!

My daughter and I visited this restaurant on a Wednesday evening, having discovered it through a Google search. We were delighted by the extensive selection offered. From the moment we sipped our drinks through to our appetizers and entrees, everything was exceptional. The service only added to the excellent experience. Although the prices are on the higher side, the quality and enjoyment justified every dollar. This is definitely a place I plan to return to.

I recently dined at this Thai restaurant and my experience was decent, albeit unremarkable. The Thai spring rolls were passable, though not particularly noteworthy. From the Fire Wok menu, I tried the Roma sauced chicken, which was a curry dish with peanut sauce, peppers, carrots, and rice. The presentation was visually appealing, but the flavors didn't meet my expectations—the peanut sauce, in particular, lacked depth and came across as watery.

The Pad Thai outshone the curry, delivering more on the authentic taste one anticipates from such a classic dish. As for the service, it was attentive, possibly due to the lack of other diners, which also inadvertently led to an uncomfortable feeling of being watched and a subtle push towards the door as closing time neared.

The interior of the restaurant is nicely decorated, and the food presentation is impressive. The cool name adds to the ambiance, but ultimately, the evening failed to impress me. Overall, the restaurant is an alright choice if you're in the mood for Thai, but it might not live up to high expectations.

Title: A Delightful Surprise Beyond the Hype
