I finally secured a reservation at this widely acclaimed spot and was genuinely surprised by the quality of the meal. Opting for chicken due to my dietary preferences, I was presented with a thick, yet astoundingly tender and juicy cut that was unlike any poultry I've ever savored.

The sides didn't play second fiddle, either. The Truffle Mac & Cheese, a daily special, shattered my expectations with its perfectly al dente pasta beneath a golden crust. Meanwhile, the Buttery Mashed Potatoes were elevated by a hint of roasted garlic, introducing a subtle yet transformative flavor that delighted my palate.

Even the Golden Fries, seemingly unassuming, turned out to be incredibly addictive. This dining experience has left me eager to book another visit. The difficulty of snagging a reservation here is not for naught; it truly is an exceptional place that exceeds expectations.

The chu-toro is so delicious that I literally started crying at the table. Every dish and every piece is just perfection. The somm made me feel like an ugly duckling when he asked what sake I have liked in the past and I could recall absolutely nothing... But if you are serious about sushi and sake this place cannot go wrong.

I ordered food by Seamless for to-go. I wasn't hungry when I arrived at NY but I got hungry late night and only could ordered food from deli. I ordered meat sauce spaghetti. Delivery service was quickly and on time. They gave me salad and breads but I didn't try both of them. It's huge big meat sauce spaghetti and I was surprised how they're big then I expected. As everyone know when order spaghetti or pasta anywhere in USA, huge big but it's really biggest I ever tried. Meat sauce spaghetti tasted was ok but definitely not the best. Spaghetti was a bit over cooked and of course I fully understood when I ordered noodles for to-go.I wouldn't recommend this place but i would order other menus again if I don't have to choice any of restaurant at late night.

Title: A Village Gem for Leisurely Brunching

I stumbled upon a fantastic brunch spot in the Village on a busy Sunday afternoon, and what a find it was! The place, which I'm keeping as my little secret for now, serves an extended brunch until 5 PM — a rarity in the city. No reservations for small groups? No problem! I waltzed right in without any wait, a pleasant surprise given the restaurant's multiple locations.

Upon entering, I was greeted by a cozy yet vibrant atmosphere perfect for a laid-back meal. The innovative menu was a breath of fresh air, featuring unique flavor pairings and dishes I've never encountered elsewhere. While there's a nod to classic brunch items, the Mediterranean flair sets this place apart.

For those conscious about portion sizes or looking for vegetarian options, you'll find plenty to choose from without compromising on taste. I left feeling satisfied, not stuffed — a welcome change from the all-too-common post-brunch food coma.

I wholeheartedly recommend this spot for pairs or a late brunch. Solid choice for foodies and brunch enthusiasts alike!

Wow, what happened to this place?  I remember a long time ago coming here and it being excellent.  Now it just feels tired and dated.  It seems a place that's just waiting to be put out of its misery.It was a very weird experience from the moment I walked through the door. I encountered multiple staff members who saw me standing at the door yet never acknowledged me.  Finally I walked up to someone and asked where I should go to be seated for happy hour, and was silently pointed to the back.  So I went back to another room and just sort of plopped myself at the bar with nobody to tell me otherwise.  A few bartenders walked by me and it took maybe 5-7 minutes of sitting awkwardly at the bar before I was acknowledged and given a menu.Came here for the happy hour to get some oysters at a decent price, but turns out the wait for oysters is quite long.  As the guy handed me the menu, he asked "you don't want oysters, do you?  It's at least 45 minute wait for oysters right now". I ended up just ordering a cup of clam chowder since the vibe was so uncomfortable and I didn't want to order real menu items at a place I had a feeling was way past its prime.  The clam chowder arrived and was sort of silently placed in front of me.  There was soup all long the edge and it was just a white soup in a white bowl with a packet of oyster crackers.Unfortunately, looks aside, the soup tasted pretty bad as well.  There wasn't much clam in it. There wasn't really much of anything in it.  It was sort of thick and gloopy from thickener.I also ordered some seltzer.  They charged me $5.25 for the cup of soup and $3.50 for the seltzer.  Definitely not coming back.  Didn't even get a goodbye or a thanks from the bartender.

YUM! Want Italian?? EAT HEREWe had cold antipasta- yum! It's the only picture I remembered to take. I had veal parm and hubs had chicken parm. Both were delicious. We also shared tiramisu and it was good!!

Title: A Satisfying Late Night Stop at [Restaurant Name]

Review:

Ventured into [Restaurant Name] around 8:45 pm on a bustling Thursday night, hungry for some late dining. Surprisingly, we were promptly seated despite a lively crowd. The menu offered great value, with items like chicken dumplings and crab and meat xiao long bao coming in under $10. The highlight was definitely the xiao long bao - plump, savory, and served hot, these dumplings hit the spot with their well-balanced flavors. The special chicken dumplings also impressed with a tasty kick that wasn't overpowering.

However, portions felt a bit meager for my appetite, and the accompanying sauce tipped a tad too far on the sweet side. To top it off, the new diner's treat of a complimentary taro milkshake was a delightful touch, though a notch less sugar would align better with my palate. Despite the minor tweaks needed, [Restaurant Name] served as a gratifying fix for our late-night cravings.

Title: A Stellar Experience That Exceeds Five Stars!

I'm a firm believer in the power of honest Yelp reviews, and it's clear they make an impact! Returning to this gem on 6/26, I was met with the same outstanding freshness and flavor that had initially won me over. The place was bustling, necessitating a reservation, but we were seated much sooner than expected.

Despite the crowd, the service remained commendable. The bocce bread is a non-negotiable starter—it's that good. The fritto misto was delightful, though this time the portion was noticeably smaller. Disappointing, yes, but all was redeemed by the Market Pizza. With its fresh ingredients and generous use of garlic—a personal favorite—the pizza was culinary harmony on a plate.

The evening took an unexpected turn when the owner, having read my previous review, came over to apologize for my last experience, gifting us a complimentary dessert. The lemon cake with gelato, drizzled with what I suspect was a herbal syrup, was exquisite, though a lighter hand with the sea salt would be advisable.

This visit affirmed the value of customer feedback and the lengths some establishments go to ensure satisfaction. I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Keep it up!

Title: A New Year's Feast at Thai72

My friends and I rang in the New Year with a delightful dinner at Thai72 where, to our good fortune, we were promptly seated within five minutes. Opting for a family-style meal to sample a broader range, we chose three popular dishes: Kao Obb Bkk, Shrimp Pad Thai, and Massaman Curry.

The Kao Obb Bkk, served steaming in a clay pot, was a standout with its perfect blend of sweet and tangy sauce, ample chicken, and seafood. While the Shrimp Pad Thai's serving size seemed modest, it was offset by its deliciously chewy, al dente noodles—a unique touch that enhanced the dish.

The Massaman Curry delivered the comforting flavors of tender chicken, onions, and potatoes in a sumptuous coconut curry, proving exceptional even without added spice. The menu's tempting "signature" dishes—like Duck Tamarind and Chilean Sea Bass—promise future culinary adventures.

All in all, Thai72 gifted us with excellent service, scrumptious fare, and a memorable New Year's dinner. It's a gem I'll certainly return to.

Title: A Sweet Delight at Spots

Whenever I find myself back in the city, a visit to Spots is an absolute must. It's where I first indulged in the Golden Toast, an intriguing but divine concoction topped with strawberries, condensed milk ice cream, and whipped cream. Despite the seemingly peculiar mix, it's a flavor match made in heaven. So much so, I've been loyal to it ever since.

Admittedly, the dessert menu is on the pricier side, but portions are generous enough to be split among two or three people, which softens the blow to your wallet. One tip, though – space is at a premium, so I'd suggest using the Yelp Waitlist to snag a seat. Spots might not be the easiest on the pocket, but it's a treat well worth the splurge.

This is probably my favorite place in NYC. Came here to celebrate the end of the semester and man I'm so glad I chose this.We ordered the prix fixe menu for 55 bucks a person. Great price for six dishes. I don't think there's a point in reviewing the food because everything is 5/5 stars. My personal favorite was the toro ssam - get the uni, worth it. My partner liked the warm mushroom dish the most but honestly everything was so good I'm excited to come again and will find any excuse to do so.

Pretty solid place! My gym partner always wanted to try out this place and we decided to go here before our workout. We made a reservation for 1245 PM and we were running a few minutes late. I called Cookshop to let them know we might be 10 minutes late and they informed us that they'll be able to hold our tables for 15 minutes. SWEET! When we arrived, we gave our reservation name and were seated right away. Our server was very friendly and attentive and sweet. I decided to go with the Green and Grains bowl because I figured I'll need the nutrients and didn't want to get anything too heavy prior to the workout. I did also order the Cinnamon bun because I was craving something sweet. My gym partner got the pancakes with a side of scrambled eggs and bacon. I had some of his eggs and they were very fluffy and had the perfect amount of salt. My bowl was also very delicious and nutritious. I also had a bite of my friend's pancakes and it was just as delicious. Had a good amount of fluffiness :)

Having gone to school in LA, I often crave soondubu / soft tofu soup and will come to BCD or Five Senses. I switch off between the two although I like the soup at Five Senses and the variety at BCD. BCD offers a wide range of vegetarian options as well and has soups with unique flavors like curry.Contrary to several other reviews, I've always had great service at BCD with servers replacing my side dishes without me even asking. I like that they have more traditional items here and the broccoli is my favorite (although I don't like broccoli elsewhere). I think that the service may just be better if you go during off-hours.Another positive is that you can get BCD on Postmates so it's pretty easy to enjoy wherever. When you order on Postmates, they pack up the sides for you as well.I wouldn't say that the soondubu is anywhere close to being as good as those in LA, but it's definitely near the top of what you can get in NY.

Tried the "famous" Mac and Cheese burger... completely overrated. Looks way better than it tastes (see attached picture). The mac and cheese itself was not bad, but the burger meat was of highly questionable quality and had an off-putting aftertaste. The apple poppy salad was at least edible.Had a few of the happy hour drinks, which were decent. But definitely skip out on food if you ever come here.

Title: Mixed Feelings About a Tapas Encounter

I had an unusual dining experience at a tapas restaurant recently. The food generally hit the mark – the tiger shrimp and mushroom croquettes were standouts, and the jumbo crab cake didn't disappoint. However, you might want to pass on the truffle hummus, which was less impressive.

The end of our meal took a peculiar turn when our waiter informed us that their card reader was out of order. Oddly enough, we were only made aware of this when asking for the bill. The suggestion to photograph our credit cards as an alternative to cash payment was unsettling. Thankfully, I had enough cash on hand, but the situation felt quite unprofessional and could come off as shady, even if that wasn't their intention.

In summary, while the tapas were satisfying, the payment issue left a sour taste. Clear and upfront communication about such matters is crucial – something this establishment could definitely improve upon.

I enjoy Daniel Boulud restaurants and tried Bar Boulud after going to a movie at Loews AMC the restaurant is more casual than its sister restaurant around the corner Boulud Sud which I've been to, reviewed and enjoyed.They have a shared basement and bathroom which if you are not aware and have gone to the other restaurant will feel worried out from. It's like deja vu. The decor is simple, busy pre theatre as it's across from Lincoln Center. If you've been to most of Boulud other restaurants like Daniel or Boulud Sud you will immediately notice the hostesses are not as friendly.  I came here a few weeks prior without a reservation and was turned away. That's when I went to Boulud Sud with no reservation and they managed to squeeze me in. I would recommend a reservation as if you walk in it appears it's usually at least a 45 minute wait.The food was good and we had a very efficient waiter. I would call it a good experience not great.  I think that you are not made to feel as welcome as I expected because of my other experiences. It was good although for the money you spend i would choose its sister restaurant Boulud Sud.As appetizers we had the tuna tartar and. Main courses were the salmon and Steak Frites dish. Everything was good and I would recommend them for a nice meal. I just would not go out of my way to come to Manhattan to go there.I'm sorry to give them only 3 stars because I was simply expecting more.

Walking into Max Brenner, one can't help but feel they've stepped into a real-life rendition of Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. This destination is a dream come true for any chocolate and dessert aficionado, boasting an impressive array of mouthwatering sweet treats.

During my visit, I indulged in the Baked Cookie Dream – a sublime pizookie featuring a warm, gooey chocolate chunk cookie crowned with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Unlike other pizookies that tend to be excessively sweet, this one struck the perfect balance and melted deliciously on the tongue.

I also sampled the S'mores Concoction, a sweeter experience served in a jar layered with rich chocolate, airy whipped cream, and crunchy rice crisps. While the S'mores Concoction was enjoyable, the Baked Cookie Dream was the undeniable star of the show.

In summary, Max Brenner is a remarkable spot that lives up to the hype with its delectable desserts. I'm already planning my next visit, eager to taste more of their heavenly creations.

One of the most tastiest tonkatsu broth i have ever tasted. They give u a choice of how salty, oily, spice level and the firmness of the noodle. It's 18.90 a bowl without add ons. It comes with 2 pieces of pork and scallion. If u want to add softboiled egg, seaweed, kikurage mushroom, extra meat and scallion it will be additional $5. I think it is so worth the money. Must try. Plus we got lucky we got seated right away

Title: Fresh Ingredients, But Value Falls Short

Upon visiting the restaurant, the quality of the ingredients was immediately evident. The sashimi platter, a highlight, featured exceptionally fresh fish, artfully presented. However, the overall experience didn't meet the expectations set by the price point. Each dish was prepared well, yet none managed to truly dazzle. While the chef's counter might offer a more immersive experience, it was unfortunately unavailable. In summary, good food with excellent ingredients, but the lack of wow factor made the cost hard to justify.

Title: A Delightful Early Dinner with Family at [Restaurant Name]

My family and I, including my 5-year-old niece, recently enjoyed an early dinner at [Restaurant Name] on a Saturday evening. We'd booked a 5 pm reservation, opting for an outdoor table, and were pleased to be seated promptly upon arrival.

The service was exemplary from the outset – our server exuded warmth and maintained a timely flow throughout our meal. It's no exaggeration to say that the biscuits here are a must-try; they are as divine as any you'd find in the South. Airy, light, and delicious with or without the extra indulgence of butter and jam.

The big bowl of Matzo Ball Soup I ordered was precisely what I hoped for – simple, yet wonderfully comforting with its fluffy matzo balls and tender vegetables. My husband's fried chicken was a highlight as well, boasting a satisfying crunch and generous serving.

Our outdoor seating contributed to a relaxed atmosphere, keeping my niece entertained and allowing us to enjoy some people-watching without feeling overwhelmed by noise or crowds. 

Although I didn't get a chance to assess the interior for accessibility features, I look forward to doing so on my next visit. [Restaurant Name] easily won me over with its delightful combination of great food, reasonable prices, ample portions, and cordial service. A recommendation with confidence!

Venturing into the Flatiron District, I stumbled upon a hidden gem: Chikarashi. Discreetly tucked away on 27th Street, this unassuming spot is easy to miss. However, their Japanese-style chirashi bowl, tinged with Hawaiian poke nuances, offers a culinary revelation that is well worth the detour.

Amidst a tempting menu, the Yellowtail enthusiast in me zeroed in on the Hamachi bowl, and it did not disappoint. The freshness of the fish was unmistakable, paired exquisitely with bold flavors and a satisfying kick of chili. Though it packs some heat, those with milder preferences can easily modify the spice level.

Every bite of the perfectly seasoned rice reaffirmed the dish's excellence, balanced by a generous helping of succulent Yellowtail. At $17, the value for such quality and quantity is unquestionable. I would recommend indulging in some extra ponzu sauce or Sichuan aioli to amplify the experience for fellow condiment aficionados.

The pull of the Hamachi bowl is strong – it’s made a lifer out of me. I'm eager for my next visit to Chikarashi, although venturing beyond this newfound favorite might prove challenging.

Went here for dinner with my sister one night. Our reservations were scheduled for 9pm. Our table was ready for us when we arrived. The service was great. Quick and fast. The food was unbelievably tasty. For an appetizer we had the crab cake and raw oysters. We both ordered steaks and shared a loaded baked potato and wedge salad with blue cheese and bacon. We had margaritas and they were strong but GOOD. I will certainly be back soon.

Title: A Gem in Soho: Frenchette

As a Soho local, I've been to Frenchette on multiple occasions. Reservations seem elusive, but the accommodating staff always manages to seat us with a "give us ten minutes" mantra—usually at the bar, which is fine by us. It's a testament to their hospitality.

Being a fan of Keith McNally's dining establishments, I can vouch that Frenchette matches, if not surpasses, expectations. The cuisine, no matter if it's brunch or dinner, is consistently top-notch. Their cocktail and wine offerings are thoughtfully curated and service is nothing short of impeccable.

It's a delight to have such a culinary treasure just steps from my home. Frenchette is a true Soho staple.

I recently had a delightful lunch experience at this establishment, highlighted by their exceptional Mac and cheese. Notably, it's listed as an appetizer but it’s hearty enough to satisfy as a main meal. Additionally, the crispy calamari, while tasty, did have a rather generous squeeze of lemon. The cod sandwich was also enjoyable, paired nicely with a side of well-prepared fries. I would recommend giving this place a try, and don't miss out on the Mac and cheese!

We had a very nice brunch here last weekend. They do offer bottomless which is a plus. The drink options for brunch were great: mimosas (including flavors like mango!), margaritas, and sangria. We stuck with the mimosas and frozen margaritas (it was national margarita day after all!) which were delightful. Our server was also really wonderful and attentive despite having a busy restaurant to serve.To start, we ordered the guacamole medium style. I actually enjoyed the accompanying salsa more than the guac, so I would just order that next time. I ordered the French toast, which I enjoyed. It came with a few pieces of fruit and dulce de leche. The menu mentioned roasted banana which was what initially caught my eye, but I didn't notice any banana in the dish. I will say those who went with the burrito were a little disappointed. The dishes they received were not what they were necessarily expecting. Instead of a burrito, it was more like two breakfast tacos. Overall though, this is a fun place for a group brunch (they have a really nice upstairs area with a skylight!) and would return!

Title: A Cozy Spot for Seollongtang: Gammeeok Review

I recently visited Gammeeok, a gem among Korean restaurants in NYC famed for its seollongtang. Arriving with a party of five at the early dinner time of 5:30 PM, we were pleased to be seated immediately without a wait. Eager to indulge, I chose the seollongtang deluxe. While the soup had a savory depth, it required some extra seasoning to my taste, remaining slightly bland despite the adjustments. The meat portions were on the leaner side and not as impressive as hoped. However, Gammeeok's kimchi truly stood out, freshly cut before our eyes and arguably the best in the US. The attentive visits from the owners added a warm touch to our dining experience. My advice for newcomers: opt for the classic seollongtang to truly appreciate this dish's essence. Overall, the experience was delightful and Gammeeok remains a spot I'd happily recommend.

Title: A Delightful Shabu Shabu Experience at an Affordable Price

I recently dined at a local shabu shabu buffet for lunch and was thoroughly impressed with both the quality and value offered. The lunch deal, available from 11 am to 4 pm, is priced attractively at around $15 per person. The best part? If you arrive before 4 pm and stay beyond that time, you're still billed at the lunchtime rate.

The restaurant's expansive layout comfortably accommodates groups, making it an excellent choice for communal dining. My friend and I opted for the tomato soup base— a flavorful and satisfying choice. We were pleased by the extensive selection of fresh ingredients available. The buffet line-up does vary slightly between lunch and dinner, with dinner offering additional vegetable and fish ball varieties.

The service deserves special mention; the staff was attentive and promptly replenished the vegetables at our table. An added bonus for savvy diners: checking in on Yelp rewarded us with a 50% discount on a protein choice. I took advantage of this deal to enjoy a seafood platter for just $5, rather than the standard $10.

I left satisfied and already planning my next visit. If you're a fan of shabu shabu or looking to try it out, this restaurant should definitely be on your list.

After a long day of hitting the books, I was famished. I was looking for a hearty meal, and came across El Nuevo Caribeno. I went through their many options, and decided to get the beef stew. This came with a generous amount of beef, vegetables, and potatoes, all in a tasty broth. There was a side of white rice and beans, and the portions were enough to make multiple meals. The price was right, considering all this.The food took 30 minutes to get it delivered to my door, and the food was warm and tasty when I unpackaged it.The food sat well with me, and was the perfect meal for a cold rainy day. The next time I'm in the mood for warm beef stew, or for a taste of the Caribbean, I'll consider this place again.

Securing a reservation at this local gem may test your patience, but perseverance pays off. My own triumph led to a delightful 9 PM dinner on a bustling Friday night. While a friend hinted at a dip in quality due to increased tourism and a shift in the menu since the restaurant's opening, I beg to differ. The tourist crowd was thinner compared to other acclaimed French eateries, allowing for an authentic dining experience. The cuisine? It remained nothing short of excellent. Worth the reservation rigmarole, this spot continues to impress with its culinary prowess.

Can only speak for their vermicelli, which is really good!Bun Nem Nuong: grilled pork meatball vermicelli. Not quite a meatball, but these were so juicy and flavorful that the only thing lacking was better grill marks. Vermicelli noodles is abundant, and the sauce is just like every other Viet restaurantCan't remember if what I ordered was the rainbow ice (first time trying these type of drinks!); it was definitely too sweet for me, but really enjoyed all the components in the mix

I've heard about Le Sia for a long time so I was glad to have finally checked it out recently. They're known for their seafood boils and skewers, and both did not disappoint.You choose a type of seafood boil (essentially some combination of shrimp, crawfish, and crab) and an accompanying sauce. I ended up getting the combo shrimp and crawfish boil in the hot & spicy sauce. The seafood was really fresh and the sauce wasn't too spicy at all, although I have quite a high spice tolerance. Next time, I may try the numbing spicy sauce to see how spicy it really is. I also tried a variety of skewers including the pork belly, lamb, and wagyu. The lamb was probably the best, but all were tasty and well cooked.The seafood boils are definitely messy but the apron and gloves help. The restaurant is always packed so expect a wait and crowded seating. However, they recently opened a new location in Midtown which might help, as well as the option to join the waitlist on Yelp.

Tucked away in the bustling heart of Chinatown, Tasty Hand Pulled Noodles delivers an authentic and affordable culinary experience. Despite its modest size, with a handful of tables both upstairs and in the basement, seating was prompt, and the atmosphere was lively, if a bit cramped.

Appetizers commenced with two varieties of dumplings: steamed pork and fried vegetable. The pork dumplings were the standout, juicy and well-seasoned, while the vegetable dumplings were notably fragrant, possibly due to the fennel.

The highlight of this quaint eatery is, without a doubt, the freshly made hand-pulled noodles. Watching the chef expertly work the dough adds a unique charm to the dining experience. I savored them in a hearty pork soup with vegetables, elevated to perfection with the addition of a rich, flavorsome red chili sauce available on each table—a must-try condiment that should not be overlooked.

In summary, Tasty Hand Pulled Noodles is a hidden gem that promises a memorable meal, especially for those who appreciate the art of noodle making and bold flavors.

Hit jackpot when I booked Nougatine for restaurant week and got seated in nice booth in main dining Jean georges instead. ( they are in same restaurant, Nougatine is the bar and Jean Georges is the restaurant ) i came at 5:30pm when they just opened so it kinda nice to have the main dining area still quite while Nougatine bar next door busy and bustling. So glad we ordered Foie Gras brulle that's on regular menu as additional of restaurant week menu . All food are cooked perfectly and delicious. Got nice bottle of white wine from burgundy as well    Service was white glove excellent. All the staffs well trained and know when and where they should come to ur table. As usual for the wine, talked with the sommelier and told him what is the range that we are looking for, and he nailed it. What I learned with fIne dining restaurant, we have to ask sommelier for help since the list is extensive
Average pizza. The pizza wasn't all that good, but at least it was cheap. You can get a good good combo special with two slices and a drink, and it'll hit the spot for pizza.

I came on a Saturday afternoon. Surprisingly it was empty, but opted to stay because I wanted to try to their unique sushi donut. Because my friend and I were the only ones at the store, we got straight to ordering and eating our bowls within a matter of a few minutes.PokeTheir regular bowl cost $11.50. I always love poke because you can choose unlimited toppings. For the toppings that they had, it's pretty standard of most poke spots. But their house bomb sounded interesting. It's a tad bit spicy, but I liked it. The bowl itself is very filing!And got free roasted nori sheets due to my yelp check in! Sushi DonutThank goodness, they had it available. They make it fresh on the spot, so it does take a bit of time to make, which is totally understandable. After a whole bowl of poke, I had less stomach to ingest this donut. Its pretty heavy because it is made of rice. So I decided to split it with my friend. Its honestly not the easiest to split because the whole circumference is filled with different things. But overall, it was delicious. Its almost felt like a more filling onigiri. I would buy this again if I wasn't too hungry, but needed to eat something to prevent being starving later on.

My adventure in finding good Mexican good in NYC has proven to be a hit-or-miss endeavor. Some places miss the mark completely, while other nail it in the head. Sidewalk Tacos fits the latter category.After a long day at school, I was too tired to cook dinner. I decided to order food via my UberEats app. After looking through my many options, I decided to give Sidewalk Tacos a try.I ordered a chicken taco, a beef taco, and a chorizo taco. I waited a reasonable amount of time to get my food delivered, and was ready to devour my meal.I was pleasantly surprised by this place. The tacos were huge, had ample amounts of meat, and were prepped well. The quality of the food was good, and I was satiated and slightly comatose after my meal. It was a good conclusion to my day.This is now my go-to place for good quality tacos. If you are in NYC, and are craving tacos or other Mexican dishes, give this place a shot!

Tucked into a cozy corner, this restaurant delights with its delectable offerings despite the confined quarters. The space may be compact, with limited seating, but they've managed to create a charming atmosphere where the delicious food takes center stage. Their drinks outshine, creating a perfect pairing for the flavorful dishes served. On a peculiar note, service slightly missed the mark when they neglected to inquire about our preference for the accompanying sauce on the fish tacos - thankfully, it was a pleasing addition. All in all, the visit was an enjoyable adventure worth the squeeze.

Last night's venture to Tacombi for a 10 PM dinner revealed a delightful spread of authentic Mexican tacos, closely mirroring the culinary essence of Mexico City. The menu boasted an impressive selection, from the traditional chicken and carnitas to the unique chile relleno and vegetarian-friendly sweet potato and black bean. Each taco was modestly dressed on small corn tortillas, evading the typical Tex-Mex overload of sour cream and cheese.

The standout was undoubtedly the chile relleno taco, which presented a delectable stuffed pepper—crispy from being battered and deep-fried—complemented by shredded cabbage. In contrast, the al pastor taco, while flavorful, suffered from over-dried meat, somewhat redeemed by the accompanying pineapple and salsas.

Regrettably, the sweet potato and black bean and chicken tacos failed to make a memorable impact due to their lackluster taste. However, the carnitas tacos with their succulent, well-seasoned pork, slow-cooked to perfection, were a true delight and came highly recommended.

One important note for night owls: Tacombi ceases alcohol service at 10:30 PM, so those seeking a late-night haunt may want to look elsewhere.

Title: Cozy Midtown Gem with Tantalizing Eats

My partner and I enjoyed a splendid dinner at a charming old school townhouse restaurant in midtown. Despite it being a Monday evening, the place had a lovely buzz, with a lively bar scene on the first floor, yet retained a tranquil dining experience on the second. The service was top-notch; servers were both efficient and accommodating without being intrusive.

The ambiance was the epitome of laidback—ideal for the rainy night that it was. As for the food, it was nothing short of delightful. The steak tartare I ordered was notably delectable, and the red snapper special of the day was a savory masterpiece. My husband raved about the fall-off-the-bone short ribs and the flavorful meatballs.

With generous portions, you certainly get value for your money. It's a spot we'd happily revisit, not only for another round of that scrumptious steak tartare but also to indulge in other culinary delights on the menu.

If you are visiting from elsewhere or if you live in NYC, I think Calle Dao has something to offer to everyone.And yes, there is an old Chinese Cuban community with a unique fusion of the two cuisines you will find in only a few places. The space is large and they are able to accommodate groups as well for small parties.The Yucca fries were a wee bit dry but we got them complimentary so can't complain. You get them on your yelp check in You may be surprised by the mild bitterness in the Tiger Salad. Might be the water cress I think. Super fresh nevertheless.I tried the pulled duck over rice (a fair amount of duck I'd say) which was truly something I had never had before (and combines the two cuisines quite well) and also tried the Chicken over yellow rice which I liked a little better (had a more citrus flavour)The king of the menu however is the Flan. A conglomeration of milky flan, citrus overtones and a marmalade-like citrus drizzle all around it was delicious.Also tried the Tres Leches which is firmer than you'd think but still sweet and succulent through and through If you live in the London terrace building you get a 15%off if you bring your LT card.The service is super friendly and quick.Great place to meet up with friends for.It's a short walk from the CE lines on 23rd and half a block from the high line.

Title: A Delightful Twist on Eggs Benedict at L'ADRESSE

If you're an aficionado of eggs Benedict, L'ADRESSE is your next go-to spot for a delightful twist on this classic. In my latest visit, I indulged in their version, topping it off with some salmon for an extra touch of decadence. To my delight, the base of the Benedict was exceptionally fluffy and light, adding a mysterious yet welcome surprise to the dish. It brought a carby satisfaction without the weightiness, perfectly complementing the velvety eggs and rich sauce.

L'ADRESSE seems to have found the secret to a seemingly healthier yet equally delectable Benedict, and it's a secret worth uncovering. I wholeheartedly recommend giving their Benedict a try. With whispers of praise for their lunch and dinner offerings, I'm already looking forward to my next culinary adventure here. Join me, and let's discover what other treasures L'ADRESSE holds.

Title: Celebratory Delights with a Side of Adventure!

I returned to this gem for my boyfriend's birthday and was reminded why we love it here. The spacious interior offers comfort, though the seating arrangement can pose a slight challenge—elderly guests might find the descent into the booths a bit of an acrobatic feat, as witnessed by my boyfriend's parents.

However, the culinary show is the true star here. Having the chef prepare your meal right before your eyes elevates the dining experience, with engaging explanations and pairing suggestions enhancing the flavors. Each dish was a delight, served in generous portions that promise you won't leave hungry.

Yes, the prices are on the higher side, but the quality and quantity of food, along with the interactive presentation, justify the expense. All in all, another great visit that ensured the birthday celebrations were a hit.

Hmm... I was soo excited about trying this out, but I wasn't as impressed as I hoped I would be. I had the "regs" and the Cap'n crunk nuggets. They were so so. The Cap'n Crunk didn't really taste like the cereal. I chose the crunk sauce that was recommended, pretty sweet, I guess it goes well with it.The "regs" recommenced sauce was their Smokin J's bbq sauce. Ehh it was alright but nothing exciting. You order at the computer and pick up your order when they call your name. No restrooms here.

Title: A Happy Find for a Casual Friday Night

Last Friday night, my friend and I stumbled upon what I can now confidently call my new "happy place." Perched at the bar, margarita in hand and the familiar crunch of chips and smooth guacamole, the ambiance hit the spot with basketball on the screen and beats of hip hop setting the vibe.

The menu didn't disappoint. Along with our guac, we enjoyed a spread of rice, beans, veggies, and deliciously crisp flautas—all presented with an eye for detail on dishware so charming I'm now on a hunt to own a set.

The atmosphere was just the right blend of lively and laid-back, matched by service that was both attentive and swift, perfectly suiting the casual setting. Admittedly, the margarita's sweetness was a bit over the top, but nothing that a mention to the staff next time can't fix. Still, it was a small hiccup in an otherwise delightful dining experience.

This is your typical, casual and classic Chinese restaurant. The food is solid, the service is good, and the location is great as it's right off MacDougal Street. Overall solid Chinese restaurant in NYC. Would I recommend it over other places, not really. It's pretty on par with your classic Chinatown restaurant.We ordered the pork soup dumplings, bok choy, and kung pao chicken. I won't go into too much detail in terms of the taste as it's pretty standard, but the bok choy was a standout winner to me. Cooked very well, crunchy, slightly garlicky and not oily at all! It was great! Solid spot, good for people who live around the West Village and when you're craving solid Chinese food.

Great ambience and good for dinner. I came with a party of 10+ people with a reservation beforehand. I called to reserve. The food was great. Something for everyone! For appetizers our table got the option called mixed appetizers - a bunch of dips with bread (not worth the $25ish bucks it was to be honest). I got the chicken and lamb Adana which were great as entrees. It was definitely a lot of food for one person so next time I'll get one of them.The interior is lovely with dim lighting. The service staff was attentive.

Llamita, nestled on the cusp of the West Village and West SoHo, stands out from the typical Peruvian fare in Miami with a refreshingly modern and understated approach to its cuisine. The ambiance feels as though it was conjured up by a chic Miraflores collective, inspired by the New York antics of luminaries like Franco Noriega and Mario Testino – a cozy retreat that's both small in scale and ambitious in culinary aspiration.

My lunch choice, a succulent roast chicken with a side of arroz chaufa, was a revelation, its smoky essence evoking the sophistication of haute Chinese tea-smoked chicken rather than the ubiquitous lime-cilantro flavors of Latin fast-casual eateries. The chaufa, a complementing side dish, was judiciously seasoned, enhancing the chicken without overshadowing it.

In short, Llamita is that rare gem of a neighborhood spot that could easily become a staple for those fortunate enough to live nearby. It's the sort of place that almost made me regret moving away from the area. While I've since moved on, Llamita is a place that certainly warrants a return visit and a dive into delicious nostalgia.

Hidden brunch gem! Steal of a deal for boozy brunchOverall: 4.5/5Food: 4/5Value: 5/5 Service: 5/5 On Saturdays and Sundays they have a brunch pre fixe special of $19 for 2 drinks (mimosa or Prosecco), coffee/tea/espresso, and a main (burger, chicken and waffles, or omelette). They have $1 oysters as well, beautifully presented. The quality of the brunch food is great as is the presentation and portion - all 3 options of the pre fixe, and the drinks are solid. The service is outstanding, really conscientious of needs and attentive. The space is gorgeous as well, super upscale and modern - think upscale cocktail bar with high top tables and leather bar stools. Love the vibes. Highly highly recommend this place, what a hidden gem and a steal of a deal! Great value for the quality and experience.

Paul's was pretty good. My boyfriend and I stopped in on a weekend afternoon and were seated right away. Cheeseburger deluxe was great; fries in particular were amazing. Definitely the right price, too.

Every few months my besties and I get cravings for filipino food so we are on a mission to find as many good filipino restaurants in this city. Grill 21 was on our list so we organized a meet up with the 3 of us on a Friday evening. Grill 21 opens up at 5pm sharp. The staff seats you right away. This restaurant is small. I saw this mentioned on various reviews but when you get in there you realize OH this really is small. I think there are a total of about 4 tables so if you do not want to wait for a table, be sure to get there at exactly 5pm. Though this place is small, my friends and I were comfortable. I didn't feel smushed and I had plenty of room to enjoy my meal. Our server was super sweet and helpful. My friends ordered combo dishes and I ordered the Pancit Palabok. I've been on a palabok kick recently. I did enjoy it here but I wish it had a bit more sauce. The portion was huge but that's appropriate for the $17 price. The show stopper for me were the Lumpia Shanghai Appetizer. I could have honestly eaten the whole lumpia dish by myself as a meal. I really wish I ordered the garlic rice. It was cooked to perfection here. I had to stop myself from eating all of the rice from my friends. I'll be back for more lumpia, the garlic rice and the delicious San Miguel beer.

Our party of five was hungry and my fellow diners weren't in the mood to Yelp around. They spied the Smith's Bar & Restaurant across the street, and over we strolled to grab a table. Once seated, I was able to determine that this was a three star Yelp spot, so my expectations were mitigated from the get go. The ratings by my fellow Yelper's were already aligned with my take on the ambiance, which is a dark, pub like venue, which might benefit from a very thorough cleaning.Service was prompt and polite, and the food was "OK", basic pub fare which included a burger, a salad, fries, and fish & chips. The food was neither great nor terrible, and our dining experience merited a three-star review on this visit.

Title: A Sip of Japan in NYC: My Juraku Experience

Nestled among the myriad of culinary experiences in NYC, finding a spot that resonates with great food, an extensive beverage selection, and an inviting atmosphere is a rare gem. Juraku is one of those precious finds. Initially drawn in by their impressive Japanese beer selection, which easily eclipsed my previous haunts, I found myself returning not just for their diverse array of brews but for something more intangible.

Juraku exudes a quaint charm with its narrow confines of dark woods and thoughtful Japanese accents. This ambiance is complemented by a beer list that's a beer aficionado's dream, boasting a wide variety that tantalizes the palate. From Yo-Ho's Sorry Umami IPA to the robust Samurai Barley Ale, each visit promises a new discovery.

Admittedly, my first dining experience left me underwhelmed; the izakaya fare didn't quite hit the mark. However, subsequent visits revealed a transformative evolution. Under the watchful eye of Kiyo, the charismatic general manager, Juraku began to shine. His presence, a blend of knowledgeable guidance and genuine warmth, has made all the difference, creating an environment that beckons me back.

The menu now offers not only an ever-expanding beer selection but also a creative mix of other beverages, from beer slushes to innovative cocktails. The food offerings have maturely pivoted—less successful dishes were pruned, making way for an array of tantalizing new additions. The tebasaki, oroshi kara-age, takowasa, and particularly anything with pork belly, have become my go-to dishes, matching and at times surpassing the izakaya standards of Japan.

Juraku's transformation is a testament to its dedication to improvement and responsiveness to patrons' tastes. It has become more than a restaurant; it's a destination I gravitate towards naturally. If you're in NYC and yearning for an authentic slice of Japanese hospitality paired with a remarkable drink and food experience, find your way to Juraku. I'll likely see you there.

White table cloths, older crowd, small intimate feel with delicious traditional Italian fare, Novita is certainly a fancy or special occasion spot. To start - Melanzane Alla Parmigiana (fav app)Breaded eggplant w/ baked tomato, mozz & parmigiano  $16- Asparagi GratinatiAsparagus Gratton with parmigiano and butter $12Entrée- Gramigna Alla Carbonara - Truffle pasta (fav)

Title: A Slice of Heaven at John's Post-Phantom

Nestled just across the theatre showcasing the splendid "Phantom of the Opera," John's Pizzeria has swiftly become my go-to spot in New York, having lured me in three times within my first month here. 

The atmosphere is nothing short of divine, owing to its unique past as a church, complete with an eye-catching dome that bedecks the interior—a stark, yet welcomed contrast to your typical pizza joint. It's undeniably a charming place to decompress with friends, especially post-show.

Now, let's talk food. We started with a Caesar salad that, while not groundbreaking, served as a decent palate-cleanser. The marquee act, however, was the traditional pizza. It's a testament to John's mastery of balance—the tangy tomato sauce melding perfectly with the melt-in-your-mouth cheese, all atop a crust that finds the elusive middle ground between crunchy and chewy. Fair warning: it's irresistibly moreish.

Although I didn't personally sample "My Pear Lady," one of their whimsically named cocktails, it came highly recommended by a companion. 

As for the logistics, do anticipate a crowd during peak hours, but patience pays off as the place sees calmer tides and shorter waits soon after. 

All in all, John's is not just a feast for the stomach but a feast for the eyes as well, making it a delightful haunt for both pizza aficionados and theatre-goers alike.

I recently revisited Cosme after a two-year hiatus and was thrilled to discover it remains a paragon of culinary excellence, if not surpassing my fond memories. The drinks were crafted to perfection, providing a tantalizing prelude to a meal that truly elevated the dining experience. Words can scarcely do justice to the vibrant flavors and artful presentation of each dish, which I have captured in a series of photos to complement this review. Cosme continues to impress with its consistent dedication to quality and innovation.

Hell yeah! Legit New York style pizza for West coast natives like my wife and I. Awesome selections of pizza and huge portion sizes! Since it was my first time visiting New York I had this spot bookmarked to try their delicious slices. They also offer non dairy or vegan slices for those with dietary restrictions. First off, customer service was great. Very friendly and welcoming. Place wasn't too busy when we came in. Side note it is located right across MSG! The pizzas slices I ordered were great. So good everything I pretty much expected from a NY slice! I got the meat lover's and white slice with garlic! my wife for the vegan Margherita and vegan white slice!  So bomb! So good, So big, and so loaded with meat and cheese! I recommend coming by if your are from out of town, I don't think you'll be disappointed! Thanks NY Pizza Suprema!

I came here recently to celebrate a friend's birthday, and we had an overall good experience.  It was an above average meal and atmosphere, but there are certainly more unique, special places to eat in the area.We arrived when the restaurant opened because he had plans to meet up with friends pretty early in the night.  Despite having a reservation, we waited 15 minutes to be seated because it seemed they weren't quite ready to seat guests on time.  The restaurant is located in a very busy area, but it was relatively quiet inside.  It certainly has a Mediterranean feel and has an awesome bar structure as you walk in and a cool tile floor running the expanse of the room.I started the meal with a cocktail called the Jimmie, which was a delicious grapefruit vodka and lemon drink.  Between the two of us, we ordered three of the small bites (the eggplant, potatoes, and tuna crudo), the grilled octopus, crispy potatoes, and a mushroom and goat cheese pizza.  It was a good amount of food and we couldn't have eaten any more.  The standouts of the meal were definitely the octopus and potatoes.  The octopus was some of best that either of us had eaten!  We should have avoided the small bites though and ordered an additional appetizer instead as they weren't anything too special.Overall, I would definitely return here for good Mediterranean/Spanish food, but I wouldn't go so far as to say it's my new favorite restaurant in the area.

Attended an evening event at Manhatta and was an invited guest so I don't have knowledge of menu pricing.You enter the restaurant on Liberty St.  Don't walk toward the building.  Stay on the sidewalk and in the middle of the street is the doorway to Manhatta.  You will be greeting by a host/hostess, who will direct you to the elevator banks.  Press 60 and up you go.When you arrive, one side is the restaurant and the other side is the Bay Room.  Don't forget to check out the Bay Room.  There are several couches to sit and enjoy a pre-meal or post-meal drink.  If you want to try your hand at ping-pong, there is a table.  Beautiful scenic view though the bridges view is in the restaurant dining hall side.  Though some of the tall buildings are too close however still a nice view.The view with the Manhattan Skyline with the bridges can be seen in the main dining room.  You can see the chefs and sous chefs preparing the food.We had a 3 course set meal -- lobster crepe, lamb rack and chocolate mousse.  Everything tasted delicious plus the presentation is simple.  The servers were always making sure your glass is filled whether it's water, non-alcoholic drinks, or alcoholic drinks.If you get a chance, definitely try this place -- good food, good view, and attentive service.

Nestled along the waterfront, this spot is a gem for outdoor dining and imbibing, particularly on a bustling Friday late afternoon. Although it may take a moment to catch the bartender's eye, service is swift once you do. My companion and I opted for beers, reasonably priced at $8 each, considering the prime location. 

However, the Salsa and Chips left much to be desired—a meager portion of bagged tortilla chips with lackluster jarred salsa at $9—a clear misstep in value. Future patrons might do well to pivot towards the flatbreads, which I unfortunately only noticed after the fact, being prepared in an impressive outdoor oven.

The ambiance of dining by the water is the establishment's true draw. With solid drink selections, despite being on the pricey side, the venue successfully capitalizes on its picturesque setting.

Title: A Brunch Delight at Sweet Chick

During a recent New York escapade, my friends and I stumbled upon Sweet Chick after our initial brunch destination was unexpectedly closed. Arriving at 1 PM to a bustling scene, we braced ourselves for a 45-minute wait but were pleasantly surprised to be seated much sooner.

Faced with a plethora of tantalizing choices, I eventually settled on the Eggs Benny paired with a Peach Bellini. The combination of chicken and ham atop a fluffy biscuit, together with impeccable home fries, was truly satisfying. Although the $12 price tag for the Peach Bellini initially raised my eyebrows, the quality of the drink quickly justified the cost, leaving me feeling quite content.

The staff’s friendliness and their attentive service amplified our experience. Sweet Chick left such an impression that a return visit is already on the cards for my next New York trip, with the shrimp & grits and the famed chicken and waffles high on my must-try list.

Max Brenner may not be the destination for a hearty, full meal, but it's a sweet spot for those with a dessert-centric palate or families seeking a kid-friendly atmosphere. While the entrees proved rather unremarkable, the burger stood out as the most satisfying option. Nevertheless, anticipate a dining experience that doesn't quite hit the mark for a memorable meal beyond sweet treats.

Had lunch at Poke Green on Wednesday afternoon. While not the best quality poke in the area, the prices and the portions make it a decent option.Quality: I went with the larger Build Your Own Poke Bowl with 3 Proteins for lunch. And while it was not my favorite in terms of quality, it was substantial and solid. The protein options are pretty standard, I went with tuna and salmon. But they do offer a ton of toppings and sauces. They go overboard a bit on rice, but that ensures you get rice with each bite.Quantity: Substantial, but it is mostly due to the rice portions.Value: $16 for a Build Your Own Poke Bowl with 3 Proteins.Ambiance: Poke Green is located in the FiDi of Manhattan. The shop is arranged weird with a ramp and then stairs immediately inside that lead to a raised counter area. They have a few stools and one couch for seating inside, but it is better as a take-out location. Pop music played quietly over the speakers.Crowd: A small line of folks taking food to go. The speed makes it a great place if you only have a short lunch break.Service: They have the system down extremely well and people are in and out quickly.Parking: Tough to find a spot in the area.

Wayan is a blend of Indonesian food with French cooking techniques. The space is beautiful and the staff is very courteous. The food however, fell a bit short of expectation. The chicken satay was super tender but felt like it was missing something. The baby back ribs were yummy but unevenly fried. Some pieces were drier than others. The oxtail soup was very tasty but the oxtail itself was difficult to eat. The eggplant was not great. The rice felt undercooked. And the seeds in the pandan were crunchy, in a bad way. Overall, I felt as the meal was on track to be something better but was muted when it came to the finished product. I love the fact that they had Bintang beer which I haven't seen in the States. For the price, the food did not deliver. I would not be back.

My partner and I absolutely adore this diner – it's become our go-to spot. The speed of service here never ceases to impress us, with delicious food arriving swiftly every single visit. We've never had to wait for a table, and the staff is consistently welcoming and attentive. It's a reliable choice that never disappoints!

Was a bit skeptical about the chicken based broth and worried about a long wait, but Totto totally won me over. When we arrived at noon for weekday lunch, there was no wait at all, and we were seated and served very quickly. We got the regular chicken paitan and the mega, and they were actually quite different. The mega included different types of meat in addition to char siu (all very tender), a ramen egg, and wavy noodles instead of the straight noods. The broth was super creamy, albeit with a strong chicken flavor, but not too salty. It definitely felt like a heavy meal at the end. The price was very reasonable, but do be aware that if you ask for spicy sauce on the side, it costs $2 extra.We thought the wavy noodles tasted better, so it might be worth asking if you can replace them if you're ordering a dish that comes with straight noodles!

Title: A Solitary Ramen Retreat in the Heart of the Bustle

Nestled surprisingly close to the buzzing Times Square, this ramen shop provides a much-appreciated haven for solo diners. Despite my post-work visit coinciding with dinner time, I was swiftly seated without delay, courtesy of their efficient handling of single patrons amidst a manageable queue.

The thoughtful design of individual barriers was a standout feature, offering a private dining experience that's perfect for those who cherish solitude. The self-serve water station required minimal interaction, ensuring the peace remained undisturbed.

I indulged in the recommended combo on the menu, with a side of rice, reasonably priced at around $27. Considering the location and no-tip policy, it felt justifiable. To my delight, the pork meat slices, usually not my preference, harmonized beautifully with the savory broth and noodles.

Portion sizes were generous; even after a hearty helping of noodles, meat, and toppings, the remaining broth was sufficiently soaked up with the rice, leaving no room for extra noodles.

The meal's end was as seamless as its start, with a simple button press summoning a server to facilitate payment at the front. It's an ideal spot for those seeking a quiet, satisfying meal alone – just be prepared to leave with a pleasantly full stomach.

The crust here is the star of the show - soft, fluffy, crispy. Divine. The dish to get is the pizza as a sandwich, which isn't explicitly available on the menu (they're adding it) but just ask for it! You've gotta get the one with prosciutto. The prosciutto here is a five stars tastes-like-Europe kinda thing. Next time, I'll get the Margarita pizza since we got the Regina and there wasn't as much cheese as I'd like. I love a super cheesy pizza. Peggy was such a kind server, too. I hope you get her!

Was here with a friend for a very early dinner at 4pm.  They sat us down and never returned. We literally had to wave them down and even then the guy we waved down says I'll get your server.  She finally arrived and took our order and drinks.This place is  ayce vegetables, soda, tea, fish balls, dumplings and eggs.  Meat and seafood costs extra.The variety of veg is large but missing the Chinese standard staples of bok Choi and Napa cabbage.Be warned they only give you 90 minutes to dine.I had the pork bone broth but the flavor was lacking.  Good thing they have a large condiment section to make your own dip.They also offer a lunch special for $14.99 before 4pm.

Where after hours club meets Pasta. A place to go for stellar pasta, lively eating experience either solo (no pun intended) or with a small group (not a big place). Great for; Perfectly cooked pasta, fun environment, good music, people watching and simple soaking up of some neighborly NYC lBuon appetito! ------Here again updating to say this place is still amazing. Lunch pre fix was fantastic. Will be back -- again.

Tucked away in the bustling Manhattan scene, this elegant two-story restaurant provided a refined dining atmosphere that was both classy and inviting. My party of four embarked on a culinary journey, albeit with a steep price tag characteristic of its upscale environment.

To whet our appetites, we indulged in an array of starters including shrimp toast, truffle mandoo, sea urchin noodles, shishito peppers, and black calamari. The shrimp toast and truffle mandoo were the table's favorites, delivering on flavor and texture, while the calamari fell short of leaving a mark.

Despite our extensive starter spread, we shared just two main courses on the server's recommendation: a chicken dish and grilled ribeye. Both entrees were expertly cooked and seasoned. Much to our surprise, the chicken stood out with its succulent taste, challenging our preconceived notions of poultry as a mundane choice.

Dessert was a sweet close with Thai tea crème brûlée and mango sticky rice. While they rounded off the meal nicely, they didn't particularly beckon for a second visit.

In conclusion, the dining experience was pleasant, with commendable food, ambiance, and service. However, it lacked that exceptional "wow" factor that propels a good restaurant into the realm of the unforgettable.

Title: A Slice of Old-School Charm in the Heart of Manhattan

From its checkered tablecloths to the bustling, no-reservations atmosphere, this gem of a restaurant is the epitome of old-school charm. I'm completely smitten! The simplicity of paper napkins and casual vibe might deceive you at first glance, but make no mistake—the food here is nothing short of exceptional.

Having moved to NYC not too long ago, I've quickly learned that regardless of the day or hour, this place is the hotspot, packed with diners—and rightfully so. The crowd is testament to the quality and allure of this eatery.

The burger and fries are my go-to, satisfying my cravings with each visit. They've set the bar high, and while I've yet to venture beyond, I'm excited to return and explore more of their mouthwatering offerings.

In summary, if you're a local or just passing through, this restaurant is a must-visit for a taste of genuine New York City charm and culinary delight.

Since these are the "number 1" tacos in the city, I knew I needed to stop by and decide for myself. It was around 9pm. Chelsea Market was getting quieter but Los Tacos was still pretty busy!I ordered 1 Carne Asada Taco (~$4) and Pollo Asado Taco (~$4). Once you order, you walk over to the various workers who will then take your receipt and prepare your order for you. The first question I was asking was "corn tortilla or flour tortilla?" I wanted the flour tortilla. As soon as I said that, the worker said they were out of them. So why give me the option, lol! I had no choice but to go with the corn tortillas. He made the tacos super quick and I found a table before digging in.The tacos were loaded with the meat, onions, cilantro, and guacamole salsa. The tacos have a little kick but if that's not enough for you, they do offer hot sauces and pico de gallo on the side for more flavor.The tacos were tasty but I don't think they're "number 1" in my eyes. That might be because I prefer flour tortillas or because it was an hour before closing so it might not have been as fresh as I wanted. At ~$4 a taco, that's fairly pricy but hey, I guess that's NYC for you. It was good but I want to come back to give it another try.

This eatery is a delightful spot for breakfast enthusiasts, offering a range of hearty platters and enticing specials. Beyond breakfast, the menu expands to include a variety of sandwiches, wraps, and salads, catering to a broad array of tastes. They conveniently offer catering services and delivery, making it an accessible choice for various needs. Pricing is reasonable, especially by NYC standards. With ample seating available, it's also an ideal location for a comfortable and relaxed lunch. Highly recommended for those in search of a versatile dining option.

We enjoyed a delightful outdoor dining experience with a selection of appetizers that tantalized our taste buds. The oysters were briny and fresh, the caprese salad burst with the flavors of ripe tomatoes and creamy mozzarella, and the calamari was perfectly crispy. The main course was equally impressive, featuring a Mexican-inspired salmon that laid atop a savory black bean mash, complemented by a zesty corn salsa. A truly memorable meal.

This place is pretty solid, if you can withstand the outrageous wait times for tables. Everyone coming in is told the wait time is about 2 hours for a table. Probably a good idea to put your name down, do a bunch of errands, then come back. Luckily (kind of), the wait for the bar was about an hour (still crazy of course). This place offers small plates, so it's good to use the following formula to know how many dishes to order: Dishes = # of People * 2.5, then round up. For that reason, I think this place is closer to $$$ than $$. The staff is extremely friendly, which makes up for the really long wait. Our server mentioned that meat dishes take a bit longer than the rest, so we got 2 appetizers, 1 starch, and 2 meat dishes. Korean Popcorn Chicken: Awesome little crunchy nuggets, with a very subtle sauce to them. I liked these a lot, but I would probably swap them on my next visit. These are great! Pork Frita: This item will remain a staple for my Thursday Kitchen visit. This was definitely my favorite; the pork was perfectly crunchy and flavorful. It went really well with the pepper as well. The bacon bits really brought out a lot of the flavor as well. Sometimes, I feel bacon bits can be gimmicky, but these really added value. Lucky Noodles: This was a really good dish too -- a little spicy for my taste though. Through the spicy pain, this dish nailed it; everything detail was packed with flavor. Edamame Dumplings: These were actually delicious, and I was surprised because I expected edamame stuffed inside dough. Instead, they used mashed edamame and packed the dough, with a great truffle sauce to top it off. These are another staple for my Thursday Kitchen visits. Ugly Potato: While I like fingerling potatoes, I thought this dish was overly simplistic to be amongst its peers. Sure, it was good, but compared to the others, they're just fries with a little cheese and a little BBQ sauce. More cheese would be nice!Bread Pudding: This dessert was both light and rich. I like bread pudding in general, but this warm and crunchy bread pudding finished the night off nicely, with a dollop of gelato on top. Delicious.  Capri-Thursday: In general, I thought these were really good. It's really easy to have a couple of these and forget that they have alcohol in them. Akin to juice boxes, these are smooth and sweet! Highly recommended. Price: 4/5Quality: 4/5Quantity: 5/5Service: 5/5Atmosphere: 4/5

Bohemian isn't just secretive to be gimmicky. With their referral only guestbook and plush lounge chair seating they manage to create an ambience that is both low key and undeniably cool. Since the vibes and food are A+, perhaps the speakeasy nature of the place is to keep the crowds away.My friend and I opted to each try the Bohemian Tasting Course, which included all the menu items we wanted. It included a vegetable fondue, uni croquette, washu beef short rib sashimi, pan roasted branzino, sashimi rice bowl or burger, and a scoop of vanilla ice cream for dessert. The savory cheese fondue and uni croquette were definite highlights for me, as was the pan roasted branzino. They allowed me to swap out the beef sashimi for the miso cod, which I very much recommend doing if you're a pescatarian. That miso cod was sublime. The least exciting course for us was the scoop of ice cream, but I believe the dessert changes from day to day.We also tried some cocktails, which were well made and quite strong. A+. Service was friendly and attentive. It was the perfect atmosphere for my friend date!This is a great place to impress a date at with your good taste, or you could even get a small group together and feel like you're dining in someone's fancy living room. I'm so glad this place exists and I can't wait to return.

Sushi is decent here. I ordered spicy tuna roll, spicy salmon roll and the shrimp tempura jumbo roll. The quality definitely wasn't as good. The rolls looked messy and didn't taste as fresh as I would've liked. The jumbo shrimp roll was made with 2 pieces of shrimp tempura but there was a lot of batter surrounding it and it didn't hold together very well. Definitely better to just get some better quality sushi elsewhere.

Came here for the food, stayed for the HOT SAUCE! No but the food was equally wonderful. This pop-up is currently featuring Chef George Mendes and I couldn't have been more excited to come try it out. Ordered the Black Forbidden Rice which was a bowl of golden beets, fresh mango, Portuguese coco-curry sauce, fresh baby spinach and seared tuna. Man what a blast of flavors! I loved the mouth feel of the black rice combined with the smooth texture of the mango. And then you get hit with the crunchy fresh spinach leaves! Obsessed. George Mendes is the chef being featured here until August 28th. Come come come!

Came here the second time. This round we got two appetizers: one NanMan chicken and one sushi bomb. We also got their signature noodles wrapped in omelette, the grilled meat set and the other salmon sushi.The NanMan chicken got good chicken and cabbage. However the egg salad was too sauce and would probably tasted better with more smashed egg.The sushi bomb, which was seasonal, was fantastic. It got a good amount of avocado and the things inside were fresh and flavorful in general.The noodles was Norma so as the grilled meat set. The other salmon sushi wasn't impressive nor bad.A good Izakaya restaurant that's doing food right rather than fancy nor new. Good choices in general if people are looking for decent Japanese food in the midtown area.

Title: Mixed Feelings on Takeout Experience

I recently decided to try takeout from a local restaurant during the current health situation and ended up with quite the mixed bag. I ordered a $6.75 chicken souvlaki pita and decided to splurge on the $7.75 special souvlaki pita, adding bifteki and feta for an extra dollar each. 

What I didn't appreciate was finding out about a 10% off deal for online orders that was only advertised inside, after placing my order with a staff member who could have had a friendlier demeanor. Be warned, this isn't the place for a budget meal.

The preparation was swift, with our order ready in about five minutes, but the portion sizes left something to be desired. These pitas are more snack-sized than meal-worthy, and won't satisfy if you're truly famished. I found the value questionable given the size.

Now, onto the food itself: the special souvlaki pita, enhanced with bifteki and feta, was a treat. It packed flavor and maintained a tender, juicy quality. Even the mildly spiced tyrokafteri was a pleasant surprise for my sensitive palate. Pro-tip: remove the fries from the pita to savor their taste without them overwhelming the more expensive elements.

However, the chicken souvlaki pita didn't hit the same highs. The chicken was dry, and the tzatziki was disappointingly watery. My advice? Go for the special souvlaki.

In conclusion, while there are tasty options available, I'd recommend being aware of the pricing and promotions to ensure you get the most out of your experience.

Title: A Bite of the Big Apple's Best

I finally had the chance to visit the bustling pizza spot that's the talk of the town, and let me tell you—it lives up to the hype. The queue was quite the testament to its popularity, stretching out the door with a wait time between 30 to 45 minutes. But patience is a virtue, especially when it's rewarded with an iconic thin-crust New York-style pizza.

The slice I received was generously sized for the modest price of $3, a true steal in the city. It was on the crispier side, a result of being re-toasted upon ordering, which I found added a delightful crunch to each bite. Though some of my friends found the crust a touch dry, I thought it complemented the texture perfectly.

The pizza sauce was a standout with its bright and zesty flavor profile, striking a superb balance without overwhelming acidity. In a city known for its pizza, this spot has managed to elevate a simple slice to something memorable. Whether it's worth the wait is a question of personal patience, but I'd say go for it—the crunch alone is worth the line.

Very pricey slices. $4 for a pepperoni slice and $3 for a regular cheese slice. Absolutely delicious! There's always a huge line outside the doors of any Joe's Pizza. Great place for a quick bite. Or order for a party!

Came here for a friend's birthday and it's got really nice vibes! Music was a little loud in my opinion, and at times we were having to yell over each other to hear what others were saying.The buffalo cauliflower bites were really good, and made for the perfect appetizer. It was definitely my favorite of the night.I might be a little biased, because I used to live in San Diego. This was my first time eating tacos since moving to NYC, and though both were good, I think I wasn't too excited about the price. But $5 for ONE taco? That's crazy- especially because one taco was just about, if not smaller, than the size of my palm. This might not just be Playa Betty's, and other taco spots in NY but this was one thing that threw me off. The carne asada could have done with a little more sauce in my personal opinion, because towards the end it did get a little dry. However, the al pastor had just the right amount of flavor: the pineapple was a great touch!

Title: Quick, Quality Seafood Fix at Terrace Fish & Chips

I recently visited Terrace Fish & Chips in Manhattan's Financial District for a take-out lunch and was pleasantly surprised by the experience. With a simple yet excellent menu, Terrace Fish & Chips offers high quality seafood and french fries at a reasonable price. The Fried Shrimp, with its subtle sweetness, was a standout, though the Fried Fish did not disappoint either. Crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, the French Fries were a perfect complement to the meal.

For $12, I got a combo of Fried Fish, Fried Shrimp, and French Fries, which proved to be a hearty portion that was more than enough for lunch. The shop itself is small and unassuming, clearly geared towards quick, grab-and-go service, which they excel at without sacrificing food quality. While there were a few seats available, it's not a place to linger.

The crowd was minimal, with a handful of other patrons picking up lunch. The service was efficient—ideal for those in a rush. Be mindful that parking in the area can be a bit of a hassle, but if you're on foot or using public transport, this spot is a great choice for a fast and delicious seafood meal.

I recently dined at Tzarevna and it was an exceptional experience. The venue exudes a cozy and welcoming vibe that makes one feel immediately relaxed. My friend and I delighted in their house-made black bread, which was a standout with its unique combination of molasses, caraway, cocoa, and spices – served warm, it was sheer perfection. We also sampled the classic khatchapuri, which was impressively tender and perfectly soft, exactly to my liking. The service was warm and efficient, adding to the overall charm. I wholeheartedly recommend Tzarevna for a delightful dining experience.

Title: A Taco Haven Worth the Hype

If you're on the hunt for tacos that tantalize the taste buds, look no further. This spot has become a regular haunt for me, thanks to what I consider some of the best tacos around. Why are they so irresistible? Freshness is key here, and it's evident that the staff pour their hearts into their craft.

Take a bite of the Adobada (pork) taco, and you'll understand my loyalty – it's a masterpiece of balance and flavor. But don't stop there; each variety tells its own delicious story, with perfectly marinated meats and standout salsas that truly raise the bar. Whether you wrap those succulent fillings in their supple flour or corn tortillas, you're in for a treat.

A sip of their Horchata may cool you down, but it doesn't quite steal the show – good, yet not the best out there. Plan your visit during the quieter hours to outsmart the crowds drawn by internet raves. And a final note of convenience: they've embraced the plastic, so credit cards are now welcome. This taco place isn't just a trend; it's a taste revelation.
Nice place! The service is very fast, and the food is good. Seafood hot plate is spicy! But the waitress warned me, so no complaints there.

The ambiance in Hall was elegant, classy and intimate. It's a perfect and ideal place for dating. Their food was amazingly delicious and delicate. You can tell how the chef cares about what he cooks from the dishes. My husband's favorite was US Wagyu Beef Burger and Beef Prosciutto. The patty made of Wagyu beef was super juicy and greatly matched with the soft brioche bun. The Beef Prosciutto was fresh, great balanced of meat & fat and it melted in your mouth immediately. My favorite dish was Fig tempura, warm flash of fruit with crispy and thin layer. We enjoyed and felt satisfied with their food. However, there is room to improve for their service. Firstly, it was our first time here and we asked for recommendation but the waiter wasn't patient to introduce. Then when they served our dessert - sake ice cream Monaka, they dropped the top cover to the table by accident but he just walked away without any apology or trying to replace with a new one.

I saw this place on Netflix's Daredevil series, so I had it bookmarked and went to dinner on a Monday. There are actually four restaurants here and all of them serve Indian/Bengali food and all of them are decorated with chili pepper Christmas lights. The people will try to get you to visit their restaurant instead, but Panna II Garden is on the upper right.We were seated quickly. As promised, there were hundreds if not thousands of lights strewn across the walls and ceiling. It's pretty cool. The food is surprisingly cheap, but it's cash only. I got an order of the lamb biryani, samosas, and garlic naan. All of it was pretty mediocre. The garlic naan wasn't garlicky at all. Come for the atmosphere, but don't expect the best Indian food ever.

The Tom yum soup here is AMAZING. Your nose will be dripping from the spice level but you will still want to eat it. The Panang curry is so good too. This restaurant is on the pricier side but well worth your money. Really nice ambiance inside too. Hands down one of the best Thai restaurants in NYC

I recently visited The Mermaid and had quite an enjoyable experience, despite the tight seating arrangement and proximity to the server station, which I must admit detracted slightly from the overall ambiance.

The happy hour offerings are outstanding both in variety and price, particularly the oysters and the mini fish tacos which, despite their size, packed a flavorful punch. Opting to extend our culinary journey beyond the happy hour menu, we were delighted by the octopus dish and the Brussels sprouts dressed with maple and nuts, each earning an enthusiastic A+ from my dining companions and me. The salad featuring frisée greens was another highlight of our meal.

Drinks were equally pleasing with a commendable regular lime margarita during happy hour, seamlessly transitioning to a nice Chardonnay during the main course. The Mermaid isn't just about value, but also about charm, easily seen in its status as a cute local institution.

Service was pleasant and attentive, with our server providing an excellent recommendation for the octopus. An unexpected but welcomed touch was the complimentary dark chocolate pudding served in a demitasse, providing a sweet and comforting conclusion to our meal.
