From the butter and bread with the restaurant's logo at the start to the thoughtful dessert at the end, the experience was a delightful food adventure. Mermaid indeed rules the seas of cuisine, and I’ll surely return for another round of their aquatic delights.

Good Greek spot, came here during lunch on a Monday and appreciated how quiet the place was. Close to Times Square but not in the center of the chaos. Everything was good but nothing really popped. Love the ambience and the fancy decor. Would come back and try the fish next time. We got the 3 spreads- hummus, the caviar one, and eggplant. All 3 was amazing but loved the caviar one the most - it's a bit of an acquired taste. The plates were really small for the price. The flamed cheese was meh but put on a little show. Meatballs were under seasoned. I liked the chopped octopus salad, we shared it among 3 people as a side.

I was invited back by the owner of South of the Clouds after my negative experience with the restaurant via their MealPal offering, and I'm quite glad I did. On a Monday evening at 6:15 pm, only one other table was occupied. When we scanned the QR code on the table for free dessert, we were informed that it was only one dessert/table. I thought this meant the two of us would have to share a single dessert, but we actually both got our own Milky Rice (usu. $6)! I ordered Beef Noodle Soup ($12), and my roommate ordered the Yunnan Chicken Mushroom Noodle Soup ($13). We agreed that they were too peppery, but overall, we liked our dishes. I was pleasantly surprised to find a lot of meat in mine; I just wish the bowl were bigger so that I could pick apart the noodles with more ease. The Milky Rice was sort of like a slightly less viscous soup, and you don't really taste the rice texture. It reminded me of the sweet soups that those large Cantonese Chinese restaurants give for free at the end, except milk flavored.

Title: A Modern Twist on Chinese Classics

I visited this restaurant on a quiet Saturday evening, met by a nearly empty dining room which wasn't too surprising given the lingering effects of the pandemic. Our culinary journey began with their Dry Pot Fish, which emerged as my favorite dish of the evening. The fish paired nicely with a diverse selection of vegetables, although those expecting the fiery punch of ma la flavor may find it absent here.

We also sampled their rendition of Dan Dan noodles, which leaned more toward a soy sauce profile rather than the anticipated mix of hot chili oil and sesame sauce. While enjoyable, purists might be taken aback by its unconventional taste.

The Peking Duck "burger," essentially duck-filled buns, was adequate but fell short of being memorable. Considering the price of $14 for two pieces, its value is questionable.

A pleasant surprise was the Bok Choy with Mushrooms. It was refreshing to find the bok choy not fried, but the mushrooms were a tad overpowered by a barbecue/soy sauce-like glaze.

The overall impressions of the restaurant were mixed. The establishment boasts a clean and modern atmosphere, which is a welcome sight for a Chinese eatery. However, as the meal progressed, the dishes collectively seemed to tip the scales toward the saltier side, and the pricing was a notch above what you might encounter in a Chinatown spot.

Final Score: 3.5/5

*Note: This visit was comped in exchange for an honest review on social media.

The pizza here is pretty good and very cheesy. Considering it's only a buck it's so much better tasting than many joints that charge more. This is one of the cleaner and nicest locations as well and you're in and out in a matter of minutes.

The Boilery is brought to you from the same folks who own Meet Noodles two doors down and though the concepts are totally different, the quality of the food is consistently high. A seafood boil may not be an ideal meal for a first date (unless that's how you roll) but I think it's a really fun way to get down and dirty with your closest friends. There's nothing like wearing bibs and getting sauce all over your face to say "I trust you and this is a safe space." The crab cakes were my favorite appetizer we tried here. The outside was perfectly crisp and the inside was full of what seemed to be pure crab meat. None of the mostly flour nonsense you'd find of crab cakes at many establishments. The grilled oysters came six to an order, and were perfectly plump and pleasantly briny. Did you know that some vegans eat oysters because they lack a central nervous system? Vegans who eat bivalves are called ostrovegans (ostro is latin for oyster). Also, some vegans won't eat certain figs because a wasp has to die inside the fig flower in order for the fruit to grow. Crazy, but I digress. The oysters here were tasty!Now for the main event. A friend and I shared the "Fisherman's Combo," which came with 1 lb. of snow crab and 1 lb. of shrimp. Each order of a seafood boil comes with corn, potatoes and rice cakes, the latter being the most exciting addition for me. A bit disappointingly, there were only 3 pieces of rice cake in my boil, but impressively there was so, so much shrimp. We devoured most of the seafood and ordered some garlic noodles on the side to sop up all the delicious cajun sauce left on the bottom. Needless to say, we nearly had to be rolled out of the restaurant. Like I said, seafood boils are safe spaces for you and your loved ones.

Cute restaurant, a bit pricey. The waitress is very nice. I had an appetizer to share and a main course, and it was very filling - I couldn't finish my main course. The bread they give on the side is also delicious. I recommend the gnocchi to share, because they are VERY heavy, rich and creamy. You can also add additional parmesan. I also recommend the burrata and prosciutto appetiser. Delicious and perfect to share with 1 other person. Cute set up inside, although it smells like nail polish because of the shop next door...

The best Korean friend chicken you can find in the Hells Kitchen area, the chicken is so crispy and cooked to perfection. My absolute favorite dish here was the kimchi fried rice, mouthwatering. If you work around here, stop by after work with your co-workers and enjoy some good food and drinks

Love! Great staff, great food. We were joking around with the host and the waitress. Such lovely ladies. My friend and I were seated almost immediately even though we didn't have reservations. It wasn't super busy when we went. The ambiance can be casual or dressy..so a middle ground would be dressy casual.Our booth was in a corner so we got to chat and crack as many jokes as we wanted. I ordered the burger medium well with fries. I forgot the name of my cocktail. My friend ordered a salmon. We shared fried cauliflower. The cauliflower was so good! The only downside to my experience was our waiter. He was odd and a bit curt but we didnt let that take away from our experience. I'd definitely come back.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Kaikagetsu with my family, and it was an experience to remember. We indulged in the Getsu tasting menu, which was nothing short of phenomenal. The serene ambiance set a perfect backdrop for the excellent service we received throughout our meal.

Each dish was a work of art, both visually and gastronomically. The Assorted Hida beef nigiri sushi delighted us with its variety of raw, seared, and tartar preparations. The Shabu shabu with its rich Miyazaki beef broth was a highlight, as was the fresh and diverse selection of sashimi, featuring bluefin tuna, mackerel, Japanese squid paired with sea urchin, Botan shrimp, and Koho salmon.

The ceremonial flair continued with exquisite plates like the Matsutake mushroom, the succulent Grilled Kumamoto oyster & sea urchin, and a delectable Snow crab cream corn croquette in a tangy tomato sauce. The Salmon roe with daikon radish in green yuzu and the simmered chestnut were refreshing, while the Miyazaki beef rice wrap brought a satisfying richness to the meal. A sweet note was struck with the Japanese fig simmered in red wine and the subtle tofu miso marinade, rounding out an ample and diverse feast.

Every dish was thoughtfully composed and delivered on flavor, making the whole course much more filling than anticipated. I was thoroughly impressed by the quality and care evident in each plate. A night spent at Kaikagetsu is one I'd gladly repeat and highly recommend to anyone looking for a memorable dining experience in NYC.

Delicious Lanzhou noodles! I got the eggplant salad (thanks Yelp check-in) and a bowl of the classic spicy Lanzhou beef noodle soup. I think the beef flank would have been better - the beef in my bowl was sparse and not very flavorful. But everything else (broth, noodles, and sliced radishes) was delicious. Service was also super quick. Would definitely come back here!

I love this place!We are regulars at this establishment. We started going to Fumo at the original location on Amsterdam in Harlem and now occasionally visit this location. I personally like Harlem for its chill atmosphere, but I must say the flavor of food is identical at both locations and always consistent. We eat at Fumo 1-2 times per week and we have never been disappointed. I like the Broadway location to sit by the window and people watch. Food; the spicy calamari is phenomenal!!!! appetizers the Meatballs, eggplant parm, rice balls are so delicious.On the main menu all the pasta is delicious I love rigatoni bolognese, the chicken Marsala is AMAZING!!!! The best is their steak and fries or salad....OMG!!!!Brunch: The avocado toast is what I always get, BUT the chicken and waffles OMG! OMG!! no one has them as good as this place and the grilled cheese with mushrooms it is out of this world the flavors are just perfect. Eggs and steak is so good that my husband always gets a double order.Pizza I cannot rate as we never order it, we get all the other food, but I don't expect it to be bad wit all the other items on the menu being phenomenal.The espresso has perfect crema, and desserts are delicious. Tiramisu tastes homemade, Panna cotta is unbelievable, and my son loves his brownie with vanilla ice cream. You have to try this place.

This is hands down my favorite restaurant in NYC. I probably come here on average twice a week because the food and drinks are just so good. The atmosphere is great at the bar and seated at a table. From the salads to the burgers and ribs a meal here NEVER disappoints.

Tucked away with a mesmerizing view of Central Park, this elegant restaurant is a prime choice for important meetings, celebratory moments, or a special date night. Its decor, reminiscent of DaDong with striking hollow glass tubes suspended from the ceiling, adds to the refined atmosphere.

I attended a brunch here for my sister's engagement and was thoroughly impressed with both the service and the food. The prix fixe menu, reasonably priced at $68 per person, offered a satisfying 3-course meal that left us pleasantly full.

We were welcomed with a delightful assortment of breads, including a scrumptious chocolate croissant and a flavorful cranberry walnut selection, among other artisan choices. The asparagus soup I chose as my starter was incredibly refreshing, setting a high bar for the following course. The strozzapreti, a new addition to their menu, was exceptional – tossed with pine nuts and zested up with a lemony mayo that provided an exquisite kick.

Dessert was a sweetly satisfying pear soup, a perfect finale. The thoughtful touch of chocolate-covered strawberries, served in honor of the engagement, showcased the restaurant's commitment to exceptional service. Altogether, the dining experience was a testament to the restaurant's elegance and charm.

I came here for a late lunch on Christmas eve. It evoked a sense of old time charm for me and with its emphasis on history, it reminded me of classic European establishments (with its emphasis on history), such as Cafe Sacher in Vienna or the New York Cafe in Budapest. I think it is somewhat rare to see that type of dedication to culture and history at restaurants in the States. The service was wonderful. I tried the Ants on a Log for $20, which was roasted bone marrow and snails on crispy sourdough. I felt the sourdough bread was a bit too hard/overcooked but otherwise I enjoyed it. I also had the Signature Steak ($51) which was the boneless rib eye. I thought that although it was a big portion, it was too chewy and had too much fat for me. To be fair though, the waiter had warned me that it contains fat, which was helpful. I think if I were to come back I would try the filet mignon instead. I did not love how the steak did not come with any sauces and I had to separately pay for sauces. I found it difficult to decide and choose between all the options and felt it would have been easier if it just came with 1-2 sauces already. I tried the truffle butter ($12) and the au poivre. If I were to come back, I believe I would try the black truffle ($9). I also had the lobster mac & cheese ($21), which I felt was really delicious. I especially liked trying the baked Alaska as the dessert ($14); it was a great addition to the meal.

Title: A Soup Dumpling Delight Not to Miss in NYC!

My recent visit to this buzzing spot known for its soup dumplings was truly a delight. The star of our table was undoubtedly the pork soup dumplings, their signature offering, which lived up to the hype. Contrary to appearances, the seemingly delicate dough was surprisingly resilient, perfectly containing the generous amount of savory broth within. The flavor-packed dumplings, nestled on a bed of cabbage rather than the typical paper liner, added a fresh and delicious twist that complemented the main act beautifully.

The prices didn't break the bank, and we were met with friendly service. Timing is everything—arriving just before the lunchtime rush ensured a smooth experience before the inevitable crowd. For anyone in New York City, this place is a must-visit for an unforgettable soup dumpling experience.

Title: A Disappointing Melted Miss at "Cheesy Dreams"

Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3.5/5)

My anticipation for "Cheesy Dreams" was high, lured by the prospect of recreating the delectable raclette experiences I've enjoyed overseas. However, this lunch rendezvous fell flat, unable to meet the savory expectations set by its international counterparts.

While the raclette's presentation was a visual spectacle, worthy of social media admiration, the experience peaked at the aesthetic appeal. The flavors, regrettably, were absent. Both my date and I remarked upon the dishes' startling blandness, with not even a hint of the culinary staple - salt - to wake up the flavors. A little seasoning goes a long way, and it seems that a tighter grip on quality control is needed for the food to match its showmanship.

On the brighter side, the charmingly quaint interior of "Cheesy Dreams" provides an inviting atmosphere, and the staff deserves praise for their amiable and helpful disposition.

In summary, while the friendly environment added a touch of comfort, one visit to "Cheesy Dreams" will suffice. The memory of the underwhelming taste overshadows the allure of returning.

I stopped by this charming eatery in the quiet lull of a weekday afternoon and was pleased by the rapid service as my smoothie order was whipped up in no time - a real delight for those in a hurry. Regrettably, I missed the opportunity to capture a photo of this refreshing treat. The interior presented a clean and welcoming atmosphere, boasting a surprisingly generous seating arrangement. Though I didn't partake in the salad bar on this occasion, it caught my eye with an enticing display. What's more, the vast array of sauces and dressings on offer looked promising, suggesting a customizable and flavorful experience for future visits.

I'm currently indulging in the classic poké bowl, and I simply had to share my experience on the spot. From the first bite, the unparalleled freshness of each ingredient is evident. The star of the bowl, the poké tuna, is undeniably fresh, which is essential for a dish like this. Complementing the tuna, the kale is vibrant, free of any wilting leaves. Seasoned sesame seeds add a subtle, perfect flavor that doesn't overpower, while the soybeans, unsalted, allow their natural taste to shine through. The cucumbers are impeccable, fresh and crisp, and the brown rice provides a delightful firmness that holds everything together. Topping off this culinary masterpiece is the caviar roe, adding a luxurious depth to the dish. The combination of these elements is not only thoughtful but executed to perfection, creating a harmonious poké bowl that I highly recommend.

Order/pay at the counter and get a ticket. No ticket, no taco! You hand the ticket to a cook and tell them what kind of tortilla you want (corn or flour). You can also add toppings. The food comes out pretty quickly, so even if there's a long line don't get discouraged. It's worth the short wait.There are counters to eat at but no seats so you have to eat standing up, but it's fine because tacos take like 30 seconds to eat. And trust me, you'll be inhaling these because they're so good.I'd recommend at least 2-3 tacos if you're eating this as a meal, but it's nice that you can get 1 taco for less than $5 if you just want a snack.

First time in Hell's Kitchen, we were told not to stop at the first restaurant we see...and boy do we appreciate that advice!  Further up 9th Ave., we found this place.  It wasn't much to look at from the outside, but once inside, we were treated to a wonderful aroma!  We ordered the lamb/chicken combo (saw the guy eating the same dish next to us), and split it.  The meal was absolutely delicious, service was great, the facility was immaculate; we couldn't ask for a better overall value/experience!

I recently decided to give this take-out spot a whirl, attracted by the appetizing aromas wafting from the kitchen. Unfortunately, the experience fell flat. We ordered massaman curry and bun noodles with roasted chicken. Despite its promising scent, the curry lacked the robust depth you'd expect from such a dish. As for the roasted chicken, it was disappointingly dry and, contrary to its description, seemed anything but freshly roasted. While the take-out experience was underwhelming, the food's potential has left me curious enough to consider dining in at the restaurant next time, in hopes of a more flavorful encounter.

Title: A Brunch to Remember at Calle Dao

I recently embraced the break in NYC weather with a delightful Sunday brunch at Calle Dao, and it was an experience worth sharing. From the moment I entered, the service was impeccable—I was promptly seated even though my friend was circling the block for parking, which is a pleasant deviation from the typical full-party seating policy in the city.

Opting for the bottomless drink option was a no-brainer. For $26, I had a choice from over ten beverages, including margaritas, mojitos, sangrias, and beers—a generous selection compared to the usual mimosa and bellini offerings. Each drink, whether it was the mojito, margarita, peach bellini, or caipirinha, was crafted to perfection without any scrimping on the alcohol.

The real star of the show, however, was the beef & broccoli. It was exceptionally flavorful, served pipping hot, and so substantial I couldn't finish it on my own. Calle Dao is certainly not your average brunch spot—it's a gem that stands out for its great atmosphere, service, drinks, and sumptuous meals. Highly recommended!

I love it when Restaurant Week lives up to the hype. Tuome offered an impressive Winter 2020 menu and overall dining experience. Highlights from the restaurant week menu were definitely the beignets, persimmon appetizer, salad that came with the Pig Out, and refreshing sangria. Everything was really creative and delicious combined - an overall impressive dining experience.Although the restaurant is small and tables are very close together, Tuome still makes for a nice date night. It's no surprise Tuome has a Michelin star.

One of my friend's birthday is on Valentine's Day, so she organized her birthday dinner on Valentine's Day at Codino that my boyfriend & I attended. We had such a lovely time - The food, ambiance and service were great!To set the ambiance, since it was Valentine's Day, the restaurant ceiling was covered in red balloons! With the dim, romantic lighting, and exposed brick walls, the restaurant truly looked magical! The servers were very warm & welcoming and explained the wine list & menu, and we decided to share a couple bottles of wine, some small plates and each order a meal. The cool thing about the menu is all the small plates are $14 and the entrees are $16, which I think is pretty reasonable for NYC. We were a party of 7 and shared the following:Small plates:-Crostini di Pulpo - Octopus dish-Burrata Special - Prosciutto wrapped burrata (my favorite of the small plates!)-Tortino di Granchio e Funghi - Crab & shrimp cakes-Calamari in Umido-Cozze Marinate - Sauteed MusselsEntrees:-Truffle Gnocchi Special -(my favorite of the pastas; we all had a taste of each others who were willing to share lol)-Gnocchi Sorrentina - Tomato sauce-Maccheroni al Tartufo - Truffle Mac & Cheese-Tortelloni d-Aragosta - Lobster Ravioli-Tortelli Prosciutto e Piselli - Tortelli with prosciutto, peas and cream sauce (my dish)-Filet mignon The server also brought out a bunch of birthday treats for my friend on the house, which we all shared and enjoyed! We really had a lovely time and I would recommend the spot to anyone for a birthday, date, or weekend dinner.

Such a cheap place for dumplings !! They are actually good too. Wish the place was bigger as there is no seating. But it is very busy and the line moves fast. Make sure to bring cash! Had the chicken mushroom boiled dumplings which were great!

Good curry and chicken, but was not spicy. 3.5 stars instead of 3.I had this pinned on google maps for quite some time. A coworker had told me that it had super spicy curry and even the medium spice was enough for his spice ladened palate. I ended up getting the basic curry rice and added cream cheese croquettes and chicken cutlet. I ordered it with spice guru heat. I will say the dish itself was generally really good, but I docked stars on price and spice. It ran nearly $20, which isn't terrible but more than similar items for go go curry, which I think is pretty decent for the category. The spice was ok but disappointing. Maybe I was let down from the hype but my feeling is the spice level has been dumbed down for takeout. I'll have to come back and try again later.

During Restaurant Week, we had the pleasure of dining at this gem of a restaurant. The ambiance is classy and welcoming, perfectly complimented by the amazing and friendly staff. Each dish delighted us with its excellence and perfectly balanced spiciness. The mango lassi stood out as incredible, but it was the mango cod that stole my heart. Overall, it was an exceptionally pleasant experience—one that I would highly recommend.

Such an amazing hidden gem! When quarantine wasn't plaguing NYC, whenever I was in the meat packing area around lunch time I would head here. I have ordered so many things from their lunch menu but the personal pizza's for under $15 were so incredibly delicious! Perfectly cooked crust, gooey cheese and their spicy oil is to die for. You won't find a better fresh personal pizza that is pretty authentic to what you would actually get in Italy. Can't wait to get back here!

Average experience.. in from south India and the taste was more for NEwyorkers .. everything tasted less spicy. Chicken dry item was ok .. poondu kozhambu tasted really good but very liquidy (like Sambar or rasam).. loves the veechu parotta.. gulab jamun was outstanding too.. wish it was more authentic :(  good one for a once in a while meal. Service was good and quick .. keep it up guys

Title: Disappointing Experience at a Supposed NYC Pizza Spot

I've been a New Yorker for two decades, and I regret to say that this establishment is nothing short of a tourist trap. On my visit at 2:30 PM on a Saturday, the pizza I received was a letdown; it was a soft, uninspiring personal pan size that lacked the authenticity and value one might expect from a pizzeria in the city. Its quality was comparable to that of a .99 pizza, except it lacked the justification of being a bargain.

When I sent the pizza back, hoping for an improvement, it returned with the same unappealing softness. Clearly, the kitchen missed the mark on delivering what should be a New York staple. Furthermore, the customer service compounded the issue. After asking for a manager and being informed they had left, I sought assistance from my waiter, only to be met with apathy.

In summary, the food was below average and the service was unsatisfactory; this place does not live up to the standards set by its counterparts in NY, NJ, or Philadelphia. Save your time and money – this place is not representative of the pizza culture that these areas are known for.

"This is one of the best salads I've ever had" - exact words that came out of my mother's mouth (she has eaten a lot of salads and does not dish out that sort of praise lightly). She got the Mixed Greens Salad ($14) with Asian Pear, Cucumber, shiitake Mushroom, Edamame,and Toasted Almonds, dressed in Citrus Ginger Vinaigrette. Not surprisingly, she ate every last bite. Yum!I got the Avocado Toast with an egg over medium. It comes on really tasty 7-grain bread with some sort of chili sauce drizzle (but not spicy) and a nice salad on the side. I can easily say that was also one of the best avocado toast dishes I have ever had from a restaurant as well! I'd definitely order it again.We both liked that the salads didn't come drenched in dressing. Our server told us that he could bring us more dressing if we wanted but they were perfect as they were.The atmosphere/vibe is great. Super cute decor. You might want to call ahead of time if you're planning on going for brunch since I know we got super lucky with our table.

Title: Tacuba: A Blend of Stunning Ambiance and Mixed Culinary Impressions

My recent visit to Tacuba left me oscillating between admiration for its atmosphere and mild disappointment with some of the culinary offerings. The restaurant itself is a feast for the eyes: a beautifully appointed space with rustic woods, intricate tile work, and eye-catching industrial lighting fixtures. The ambiance is further elevated by the open windows that invite a warm breeze and sunshine to touch every corner.

The brunch menu appeared promising with innovative choices like ricotta-lime pancakes topped with hibiscus syrup and quinoa-stuffed poblano peppers. Yet, my experience with the appetizer-sized chicken tacos was underwhelming. While the description tantalized with 'adobo marinated chicken', the reality was a sauce that oddly reminded me of canned spaghetti, detracting from the overall flavor.

On a positive note, the guacamole was a triumph—chunky, zesty, and brimming with fresh ingredients, though the portion size was a tad small, leaving us craving more. The margaritas saved the day and were a delightful blend of perfect consistency and mango flavor, though it's worth noting they're pre-made, limiting customization.

In summary, Tacuba is not the pinnacle of Mexican cuisine in the city, but its charm lies in its aesthetics and select menu successes. I would consider giving it another chance, but I'll steer clear of the chicken tacos next time.

Title: Authentic Szechuan Heat at Chow House

As a spicy food aficionado, discovering Chow House nestled in Greenwich Village felt like striking culinary gold, courtesy of a recommendation from my Chinese friend. 

The cold sesame noodles were the perfect opener, flawlessly balanced with a gentle heat that teased the palate. The Mapo Tofu followed, impressing with its generous portion and richly flavored yet mild sauce. The star of the night, however, was the braised fish filet drenched in an exquisite Asian chili sauce. It managed to deliver the heat I crave without sacrificing the delicate texture of the fish, and the vegetables maintained their integrity despite being bathed in chili oil. Paired with rice, this dish was nothing short of a Szechuan symphony.

Adding to the charm, a check-in on Yelp granted us a complimentary glass of wine with our entrée—a delightful bonus. The service shone too, with attentive staff ensuring our water glasses were never empty, an essential touch for spicy fare. 

Chow House is the real deal for anyone in search of bona fide Szechuan cuisine in the city. Highly recommended for a fiery feast that doesn't shy away from flavor.

Title: A Worthwhile Wait for a New Culinary Gem

Recently opened in New York, this no-reservations eatery had me intrigued since the first buzz in the press. Anticipating a queue, my visit was met with a one-hour wait – reasonably offset by a pre-dinner drinks session nearby. This tactic paid off, elevating the dining experience as the flavors seemed amplified post-libation.

Take heed, the menu's pricing can be misleading – the seemingly modest $20 pots are per person for a duo. Yet, the heartiness within justifies the tag. Our pot brimmed with succulent chicken, melt-in-your-mouth cheese, satisfying rice cakes, and hearty potatoes. A minor imbalance, perhaps, was the generous hand with kimchi overshadowing other ingredients.

My verdict? This spot is on my comeback list. Pro tip: swing by an hour before hunger strikes to claim your spot, then explore the vicinity as anticipation builds. The delicious payoff is indeed worth the strategic planning.

This place really disappointed me because I ordered the gluten version. I watched the staff person pull out an old pre-cooked waffle and then heat it up. So it tasted like shoe leather. I asked her why it wasn't from batter, and she mumbled that they make them fresh daily. It was disgusting. I took one bite and went to throw it away. But, there was a homeless person going through the trash. So I even told that person that it didn't taste good, as he wanted it. Hopefully he enjoyed it, although he was already holding an old one that was out of the trash and was about 2/3 already. But, I suspect that that one tasted better, than the gluten free one.As a side note, the regular waffles are delicious and gooey.

Title: Happy Hour Delight Under a Lunar Glow

I recently visited a dining spot that caught my eye for two reasons: its convenient proximity to my subsequent destination and an enchanting lunar ambiance as I'm quite the moon enthusiast. Opting for this branch, I was welcomed by an impressive moon installation looming behind the bar, providing a unique cosmic touch to the setting.

My timing couldn't have been better; I arrived during their daily Happy Hour, which runs from 4 pm to 7 pm – a delightful surprise. The interior exuded warmth, and the dual-level dining option suggested ample space, although I chose a cozy spot by the bar.

The staff were amiable and knowledgeable, adding to the overall positive experience. I indulged in a BEE LINE, a refreshing concoction featuring their house lavender-infused vodka, which did not disappoint.

Happy Hour also allowed me to sample some tempting bites at a value - the tiger roll and soy garlic Korean wings were particularly noteworthy, both tantalizing my taste buds.

The menu teased me with other tantalizing dishes like spicy pork and bulgogi which I plan to return for. An added perk for dining guests is the chance to spin a wheel when you order an entrée, possibly scoring a complimentary item.

Overall, this restaurant has a magnetic charm and offers a delightful Happy Hour experience. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

this is such a pretty restaurant! came here around 5:50pm on a friday night and was seated immediately for a table of 3. i do remember seeing alot of people waiting for seats but i think they needed tables of 4+ so maybe keep that in mind! atmosphere, this place was super cute. they had lanterns hung everywhere and where we sat (upstairs) there was a small bar. i can totally see this as a date night dinner thing haha.service wise, it was phenomenal. the waiters and waitresses were super attentive making sure that we were comfortable and had constantly poured us water.Food wise, it was really good (my friend said it was a lot better than he expected haha). we ordered the calamari (which you must get!), Bun, spare rib on cane skewer, roasted duck noodles and a curry/soup. of course we also got drinks and barely made it before happy hour ended (during happy hour drinks are half off i believe). the sake was good however if i had to choose i would get the lychee flavored alcohol next time (i forgot the name). so for those looking for some good thai food in a bougie atmosphere, i say obao is the place!

Title: A Trendy Twist on Diner Classics at UES Gastro-Diner

Recently, I had the pleasure of visiting a new gastro-diner on the Upper East Side for a pre-New Year's Eve meal. This establishment attempts to elevate the traditional diner experience with a sprinkle of gastronomical pizzazz, though the prices might reflect more of an uptick than the food's creativity warrants.

The interior boasts a sleek and retro vibe, both clean and inviting, with well-maintained restrooms adding to the comfort. Space is at a premium, but the layout accommodates a full bar and ample seating without feeling overcrowded.

Service was prompt and friendly, setting a positive tone for the evening. The menu, large and varied, caters to all-day dining from breakfast through to dinner. Standout dishes included a flavorful Eggplant Parmesan sandwich, a fresh Mexi tuna wrap, and perfectly crispy, non-greasy onion rings. A highlight was the Chicken Lemon Orzo soup, which truly hit the spot. Paired with a Brooklyn Lager and a classic chocolate egg cream, it was a satisfying meal from start to finish.

While slightly on the expensive side for diner fare, this spot presents a refined alternative to the classic diner experience. It's worth a visit for those willing to spend a bit more for an indulgent, casual meal.

Title: Delightful Sushi Experience with a Minor Hiccup

My recent visit to this sushi spot left a favorable impression with its commendable variety in the assorted sushi plate, especially the inclusion of a sumptuous piece of toro. Accommodating my preference, the chefs expertly crafted my spicy tuna roll with rice on the outside, a detail I greatly appreciated. While the tuna roll's filling was regrettably a touch fishy, the rest of the sushi was fresh and devoid of any off-putting taste. The spicy tuna roll itself was a highlight and is on my must-have list for future visits.

My husband opted for the steak entree, which he relished. On sampling, I found the steak to be somewhat underseasoned. Despite this, the overall dining experience was thoroughly enjoyable. I am looking forward to our next visit.

I remember eating at the Oyster Bar many years ago when I used to visit my dad at work, we would periodically come here or another GCT restaurant since his office was right down the block. Since then, Oyster Bar has always been in my periphery - constantly passing it as I made my way to either Metro North or the subway. I was in the area to see a concert at Madison Square Garden and thought it was good opportunity to revisit OB - so we deiced to make our way over and revisit. For being in Grand Central, Oyster Bar is quite large - the aesthetics slightly resemble Grand Central with the curved ceilings and brick but also give off casual seafood restaurant vibes with paper menus and checkerboards tablecloths. When you walk in, there's a lounge directly in front of you with a "saloon" to the right and the main dining room to the right. It was all open space but didn't seem too vast or impersonal. As I said before, the menu is printed on paper - I'm assuming because market prices for seafood change frequently and need to be updated. The menu is huge - lots of apps, mains, sides, seafood prepared all ways, and a number of combo dishes. This is understandable because it's in a major thoroughfare in Manhattan so they need to appeal to a lot of different diners. After being served some rolls and other carbs, we decided to start with the fried calamari. I'll admit I had kind of high expectations but it really wasn't my favorite. I give them props for including rings *and* legs, but the pieces were really small and kind of over-fried. Also, the marinara sauce it was served with was lukewarm to cold. I've had this app at more restaurants than I can count and if I had to rank them this one would be towards the bottom of my list. For my main I had the jumbo shrimp with garlic butter and coconut rice. The shrimp were really large which was great, but I was struggling to find flavor, even with the garlic butter on top of them. The garlic rice was good, just the right portion as was the string beans that came with it. Service was fine, our waiter was knowledgable and the food came out at a good pace. There were some really obnoxious tourists sitting next to us and the wait staff were nothing but professional when interacting with them - well done. Overall, while this is an iconic NYC restaurant, the food fell short for me. The service and aesthetics were good, but not enough for me to give it more than a 2. I would be willing to come back if circumstances found me here, but I'm not running back.

I recently stumbled upon a delightful dining spot while walking to a nearby show, and I'm thrilled to share my experience. The staff were welcoming and contributed to the enjoyable atmosphere of the restaurant. I was impressed with the quality of both the food and drinks; each bite and sip surpassed my expectations. Additionally, the prices were unbeatable for the value received. A diverse menu caters to all preferences, offering delicious options for both meat-lovers and vegetarians alike. This place is a gem that I highly recommend visiting!

Title: A Sunday Dream Brunch at Zodiac

My ideal Sunday now includes brunch at Zodiac, perched atop Neiman Marcus with sweeping views of Hudson Street. Clutching a Bellini with the promise of a Lobster Benedict on the horizon, I find my slice of happiness here.

Price is a pleasant surprise in NYC; however, Zodiac's crowning jewel is its service—warm greetings and unwavering attention from start to finish. The instant arrival of Bellinis set the tone, swiftly followed by their signature popovers—golden, flaky morsels made heavenly with strawberry butter.

The Lobster Benedict, accommodatingly served with scrambled eggs upon request, was a showcase of sumptuousness—generous, succulent lobster harmonized with a subtle hollandaise. It's a dish that tempts a loyal re-order, however much the rest of the menu beckons.

Unassumingly declared as sides, the roasted potatoes were a revelation, possibly conjured from a double cooking in duck fat, achieving a divine crunch with a soft heart. Despite not being a potato aficionado, these alone are worth a revisit.

Zodiac's interior whispers elegance, a soothing palette of sterling, gray-blue, and wood complemented by a stunning bar. The atmosphere is relaxed, you're never hurried—when brunch lagged, the gesture of complimentary Bellinis was appreciated. My next Zodiac quandary? Sampling their afternoon tea or yielding once more to the lobster's call.

Title: A Meatball Oasis with a Twist

I recently ventured into a delightful dining experience at a spot that's reinventing the classic meatball. Far from your typical meat-and-sauce affair, this restaurant offers an impressive selection of meats including chicken, pork, vegan, and seafood options, each crafted into succulent meatballs.

The sauce selection is a culinary mosaic, ranging from rich pesto to tangy yogurt, hearty Parmesan, and sumptuous butter, ensuring each palate finds its perfect pairing. The customization doesn't end there; diners can choose from two pasta varieties to cradle their meatball masterpiece.

For those seeking greener pastures, a range of vegetable sides stand ready to complement your main, or you can opt for a fresh salad. If you're in the mood for handheld satisfaction, "heroes" transform the meatball experience into a sandwich delight.

A well-stocked bar provides the perfect libations to enhance the flavors of your meal, making the dining experience both comprehensive and satisfying.

My time here was unexpectedly fun and undeniably delicious—this is one establishment that's certainly worth a repeat visit.
I had the egg white omelette with spinach and goat cheese and a side salad and it was excellent!  Fast service and great food!

Title: Cozy Vegan Haven with a Dash of Quirk

If you're on the hunt for some delectable vegan comfort food, this cozy nook hits the spot! Their cupcakes, a heavenly blend of moistness with just the right hint of sweetness, are a must-try for anyone with a sweet tooth. The vegan nugget appetizer? Absolutely delightful – crispy, flavorful, and a clear winner.

While they shine with their raw food options, which are both fresh and invigorating, the seating arrangement is a bit of a squeeze, though that's a small price to pay for the place's popularity. However, when it comes to dipping, the place could benefit from including some classic sauces like ranch or mustard.

For those looking for healthier carb options, the lack of multi-grain or whole wheat alternatives for sandwiches is a definite miss. Service can be spotty; refill checks are scarce, and there's an additional charge for extra sauce that feels a tad steep.

The staff's approach to customer service appears to be a roulette, swinging unpredictably between hits and misses. This was particularly noticeable when the stuffed avocado, advertised with mixed greens, made an unexpected pivot to a romaine base without prior notice. Furthermore, their response to ingredient mishaps could use some finesse – rather than rearranging the dish at the table, a simple, straightforward fix would be far more appreciated.

All in all, though the place has its quirks, the food's quality stands out, making it a worthy stop for those seeking plant-based indulgence.

Title: Authentic Chinatown Fare in Midtown East

Finding a slice of Chinatown in Midtown East is a culinary delight, and this unassuming Cantonese restaurant is a gem for those in the know. The ambiance is unpretentious, with a focus squarely on delivering the kind of authentic eats you'd stumble upon in the heart of Chinatown itself.

The draw here is unmistakably the roast meats over rice—succulent options like roast pork, soy sauce chicken, roast duck, and bbq pork sit atop a comforting bed of rice and veggies, all at a wallet-friendly price under $10. It's a substantial plate that doesn't skimp on flavor.

Beyond these best-sellers, the menu boasts a variety of made-to-order dishes. Personal standouts include the savory wonton noodle soup and a hearty beef stew over rice, each a testament to the kitchen's prowess with traditional Cantonese recipes.

Word to the wise: this spot fills up fast come noon. For those with tight schedules, an earlier arrival ensures a quicker seat. Whether you're a lover of Cantonese cuisine or looking for an affordable lunch that doesn't compromise on taste, this restaurant is a must-visit.

Tucked away in the heart of the bustling city, this gem of a restaurant offers a little slice of culinary paradise. With its charming outdoor seating, it's an idyllic spot for both dining al fresco and people-watching. The amazing manager stands out here, not just overseeing the operations but also tending to the patrons with a level of care that is all too rare these days. This attention to detail extends to the service - attentive, yet unobtrusive and always with a personal touch.

The food is nothing short of exceptional. Quality ingredients come together in an inspired menu that offers delightful surprises and satisfies a range of palates. For those, like me, who appreciate a refreshing, non-alcoholic beverage, the fresh juice bar and mocktails are perfect. And for those times when you need a quiet escape, they offer a secret indoor workroom, ideal for anyone looking to combine productivity with great food.

As someone who enjoys a good workout at Barry's Bootcamp just across the street, this restaurant has quickly become a favorite post-exercise haunt. It's so enchanting and convenient that I'm considering moving to the area just to have this culinary experience at my doorstep. I will definitely be returning for many more meals.

Really good place for brunch. The line at Clinton St Baking Co was way too long so we came here, which was a 2 minute walk away. The pancakes here are so golden and delicious and the outside is lightly crisp. They're delicious! I got the smoked salmon eggs benedict and it was pretty good. My friend got the salmon baked eggs, which was a little too salty and heavy for my liking. The portions are good and the food tasted really good overall. Our waitress was really nice and friendly. The food wait time wasn't bad at all. You also get free coffee when you check in on yelp! My cup was never empty.

First time at this location, third time at Carmine's. I actually like this location a lot more than the Time Square one, wherein there's noticeably high proportion of tourists. Here, on the other hand, comprises mainly of large families gatherings. Last night, we spotted at least five birthday celebrations. Fun times. The inside looks a lot nicer and larger than what may appear from the outside.

I recently stopped by for lunch at this establishment and was met with a warm reception from the friendly staff. My craving for a classic led me to try the Margherita Piu Pizza, which unfortunately fell flat in flavor. On a brighter note, the San Gennaro Pizza with its meat and pepper mix was quite flavorful and satisfying. The Kale Salad initially had an overpowering saltiness, prompting a remake; even then, it was rather unremarkable and not quite worth the price given its modest portion size. The Artichoke Salad was passable, though nothing to write home about. In conclusion, the overall pizza experience was just okay – a mixed bag of hits and misses.

Title: A Casual Sea Breeze at The Oyster House

After soaking in the history at the Museum of Jewish Heritage, my friend and I decided to unwind at The Oyster House on Pier A, conveniently catching their weekdaily happy hour. Though we skipped the "oyster hour" deals, the atmosphere at 5PM on a Friday was surprisingly calm — a plus in my book.

The Old Bay Fries I ordered were a hit — perfectly crispy and generously portioned for just $6. As for the margarita, it was expertly mixed and quite the steal at $13, considering the quality. The glimpse I caught of the onion rings at a neighboring table also promised deliciousness.

The decor, with its nautical flair, might tread the line of kitsch but the exquisite views of the water complemented the theme, making for a charming and relaxing experience post-museum outing. It's a place I'd revisit when in the vicinity.

The only snag in the otherwise smooth sailing was the restroom situation. It was more reminiscent of a dockside facility than part of a comfortable eatery, with a scent that was a little too "authentic" for my liking. Despite that, The Oyster House is a solid choice for a laid-back bite with a side of sea breeze.

I've been to this area many times but I never noticed this cute little restaurant. My friend suggested to come here for brunch so we did. I ordered the buttermilk pancakes ($16) and it was a generous portion but I mananaged to finish it cause it was so good. My friend's avocado toast ($16) was pretty big too... she only finished one half of the toast. We got a side of fries ($9) but we couldn't finish it because it was huge and also it required some hardcore jaw work. My other friend got the al pastor sandwich ($19). The pulled pork in the sandwich didn't taste like bbq pulled pork but some interesting seasoning like curry?? My friend was disappointed her cappuccino ($6) was so tiny. Overall decent service, cute place with sufficient sunlight streaming in,food is on the pricier side but it's manhattan and it comes in big portions.

Note: this review is intended for the Burgary located on the 'west' side over off 6th Avenue and 'not' the east side. Yelp did not have the location for the westside. Will write review on the east side location.PURCHASED: fried chicken breast w/ bacon cheese burgerTOTAL: $PROS:+ great price: Excellent price for the food portion given--excellent ratio. I am frugal; that is saying a lot. + creative burger: When restaurants try to create a new type of burger combo some may or may not do well. My opinion is that the Burgary did well. I had the fried chicken breast with bacon in mine. They did a good job. + crispy fries: This spot gets the crispy fries award. CONS:- n/a: I cannot think of anything bad. Though, when looking for them on Google Maps, I had to consult a different method because they were not updated to Google Maps. They have one other restaurant location and that is located on the East Side. IMPRESSION:At the present month, this is by far the best burger I have had in sometime. The price is also excellent. I don't do this often, but I almost went over to the cooks and told them how impressed I was. I told them they made such a delicious burger. Note: When compared to Shake Shack, I would say this is better because of the portions. Though, Shake Shack is still good. Yeah--I'll definitely go back if I am in the neighborhood and need to drop money on some food.

Great Korean BBQ.  Eaten both lunch and dinner here - both times excellent.  Get the lunch tacos with salad or truffle fries.   Recommend the nutty salad if you want to share a salad and do the tacos with truffle fries if 2 are dining.  Will be back.

Yerrrrrm two of my favorite cuisines all in one. Everything about the meal was great. We were in a rush between the two Harry Potter shows (10 min walk from the theatre), and we ordered, ate and paid within a little over an hour after warning our waitress of our time constraint.The lomo saltado was comparable to the ones we had in Peru, as well as the ceviche. The sushi was good too. The California roll used real crab, instead of imitation crab, which was a nice surprise. The only thing we I wasn't a huge fan of was the chocolate tres leches, which was super dense like a brownie. It tasted great - just not what you'd expect for that kind of cake. All in all, the food was so tasty that we are making reservations for our next play in a month.  The inside was very appealing and modern. Note that it's a non-tipping restaurant so the prices may be a little high at first glance. Also, if you CHECK IN ON YELP, you can get a free cocktail with a $30 purchase, which isn't that hard if you order a main dish. I would recommend a pisco sour, which was perfect to go with our dinner and Peru's signature drink.

My husband, friends, and I enjoyed a delightful Saturday afternoon at this spacious restaurant, which was quite peaceful due to it being half empty – a perk for attentive service. We were pleasantly surprised that checking in on Yelp offered us a complimentary homemade gelato, a sweet start!

Our meal began with a few appetizers which had a great deal of buy 2 get 1 free bao – the pork and chicken options did not disappoint. We also indulged in some crispy popcorn chicken with a spicy kick from the mayo, alongside a refreshing garden salad. The ramen was the star for most, with orders of Ma yu ramen and a custom ramen bowl with chashu and ma yu sauce. I played it safe and savored a comforting braised pork rice bowl given my under-the-weather state.

We paired our meal with a selection of jasmine teas – honeydew, passionfruit, and rose without milk or bubbles, which offered a light and aromatic complement to our dishes.

Dessert was a cheerful affair with more of the free gelato. The flavors – pistachio, matcha, and a tropical mango sorbet – were all a hit.

Overall, the experience left us satisfied and eager to return. Yummy indeed!

Title: A Ramen Revelation at Noodle Nirvana

My inaugural foray into the world of ramen at this local spot was nothing short of outstanding. With a generous variety of options, I indulged in the chicken ramen - a decision I'll never regret. The serving size was more than ample, ensuring a hearty experience. Each bite was a burst of rich, savory flavors complemented by a delightful assortment of ingredients within the bowl. Service was both friendly and efficient, enhancing the dining pleasure. Although I couldn't enjoy an accompanying beverage due to being on-call, the food alone was worth the visit. Highly recommended for anyone seeking a delicious ramen rendezvous!

We had a great time at this restaurant. It was a pretty packed Tuesday night for Chinese New Year but we waited about 15 mins for a table for 4 people without reservation. The food was delicious and the service was good. We mostly ordered comfort food such as sautéed eggplants, ribs with chestnuts, and baked fish in spicy sauce. Everything was served on white rice and simply delicious!

I was staying at the New York EDITION hotel and decided to come down for lunch. And I'm so glad I did - the food was wonderful.To start, I had the complimentary sourdough which was AMAZING. I literally wanted to buy a few more to take with me to-go.I opted for the 2-course lunch for which I chose the beef tartare and the sauteed skate, which were both lovely. The beef tartare was fresh and well-seasoned. The skate was cooked to perfection with the top still crispy.I was on a conference call / working on my laptop and the staff were super understanding and helped me rearrange the table to put the food down. The ambiance / decor are a little old-fashioned looking, but overall, would highly recommend this place!

I truly feel it is hard to mass produce greek food. Maybe it is because I am greek and I have high expectations.  I honestly sometimes don't know what these places are thinking serving the food they do. For example, the stuffed peppers (gemista) are as traditional of a greek dish as you can get.  It sucked. It was filled with a cheese mixture that I couldn't even identify. I think the waiter even warned me when I ordered it since it wasn't traditional. Normally, there is a ground meat and rice mixture with different herbs stuffed in a vegetable. Honestly, whether it was traditional or not it was bad. The gyro however was good. It had french fries in it which is in fact traditional. It wasn't anything to write home about but at least they had the ingredients down. We also tried  the tirokafteri and it was way too salty.  Everything here looks the part except for the food. The Interior has a nice greek touch with the colors and decorations. The Service is pleasant as well. The tables were small so coming with a group over 4 people would be difficult. Not my favorite place to get Greek food. Maybe some of the other items on the menu are better! Unfortunately, this experience was not good.

Title: Big Mimosas and Tasty Breakfasts at a Bustling Spot

I recently gave a local restaurant a try for brunch and it certainly earned its four stars, particularly for the generous tumbler of Mimosa that kicked off my meal. Despite its bustling atmosphere, my family and I were seated promptly upstairs and our server was quick to take our order – the start of a delightful dining experience.

The variety on the breakfast and lunch menu catered to all our cravings, from the hearty Lumberjack breakfast that I indulged in, to a range of kid-friendly bites like cheeseburger sliders and chicken fingers. Everything was delicious, with the pancakes deserving a special shoutout. But the standout had to be the $5.50 "Big Gulp" Mimosa, a refreshing and sizable beverage that made the meal even more enjoyable.

With quick service, a welcoming vibe, and a menu that has something for everyone, this restaurant is certainly doing things right. Whether you're in the mood for a classic breakfast or just want to sip on a well-priced, large Mimosa, it's a place worth checking out.

Chill spot in the East Village that looks to provide an authentic Japanese experience. Unfortunately the food wasn't memorable for the right reasons. The Japanese fried chicken was very undercooked. Chicken liver and bacon wrapped scallops were the best things I ordered.

This may seem like a stretch to some, but for some very cheap pizza, it was worth it. Honestly, it was very quick and convenient. The cheese pizza is 99 cents and other pizza with toppings cost more FYI. If you hungry or need a quick snack, check these places out.  Don't forget to put some oregano and red pepper flakes on and fold it and eat up!

After an unsatisfying dining experience elsewhere, I ventured out in search of a palate cleanser and ended up ordering a chicken teriyaki from this establishment. However, the dish was a letdown. It lacked the authentic teriyaki flavor I anticipated, coming across more as plain steamed chicken with a hint of sauce rather than a well-marinated delight. As someone with a background in cooking Asian cuisine, I expected much better.

To accompany the main, I sampled a selection of rolls – spicy tuna, salmon, and eel avocado. Of these, the eel avocado roll was the highlight and the only part of the meal I genuinely enjoyed. Despite this small win, the overall experience was unsatisfactory. Unfortunately, I will not be returning.

I returned to the restaurant on Christmas Day for a quick lunch, where I ordered the 'chicken with peanuts' from the lunch menu—an equivalent to Kung Pao chicken. Although I requested it to be very spicy, it wasn't as spicy as anticipated. Despite that, the overall flavor was satisfying. I enjoyed the dish and would order it again.

Title: A Hearty Feast with Attentive Service at [Restaurant Name]

My recent dining experience at [Restaurant Name] was nothing short of impressive, especially when it came to the generous portion sizes. My mom and I decided on the Penne alla Vodka paired with a Caesar Salad, and the "family style" servings were more than sufficient for the two of us – talk about getting your money's worth!

Upon arrival, we were greeted with a delightful complimentary pizza focaccia, setting a positive tone for the meal ahead. The bread was a tasty surprise that we thoroughly enjoyed. The collaborative spirit among the staff was notable; multiple servers attended to our needs, ensuring that our dining experience was seamless from start to finish.

For those considering a wine pairing, my advice is to splurge on a nicer bottle. While some of the pricier selections fell short of expectations, don't hesitate to ask for a recommendation to enhance your meal.

A shoutout to my fellow vegetarians: [Restaurant Name] has got your back with a special menu just for you. Being able to order with ease and knowing your dietary preferences are recognized makes all the difference.

In conclusion, [Restaurant Name] is a must-visit for anyone craving substantial meals, attentive service, and a vegetarian-friendly atmosphere. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

I love the food here. My coworkers would rave about this place on how delicious the food is. I ended up ordering lunch for delivery one day. Food came quickly and right before the delivery time. I am a big fan of Cuban food so I was curious to see what I would get. Needless to say, I was not disappointed with Sophie's. I ordered the baked chicken lunch special with three sides (chickpea salad, avocado, and rice). I was shocked how big the portions were. Coming from NYC sometimes you don't get your money's worth when ordering take out. The food was great, and I ended up having leftovers for later.  I was very pleased with the delivery, quality of food, and portion sizes.

Delicious! Definitely one of the better udon places in New York. The udon here tasted freshly made, the soup broth is delicious and there is a good amount of variety. I particularly liked the tripe I had, since it had a great amount of flavor and is more unusual to find in udon restaurants.

Title: A Heavenly Indulgence at [Restaurant's Name]*

Review:

Stepping into [Restaurant's Name], we were immediately swept away by the elegant setting of their rooftop dining area, complete with beautiful furniture and sparkling chandeliers that added a touch of sophistication to our early brunch.

Every dish we ordered, which was indeed everything on the menu, surpassed our expectations. The standout, however, was the bacon - it was so delectable that it's almost shameful how much praise I am about to heap on it. The crunch, the flavor, it was breakfast perfection.

In short, [Restaurant's Name] offered an exceptional dining experience where each menu item shone. A true gastronomic delight that's not to be missed!

*Replace [Restaurant's Name] with the actual name of the restaurant.

Just because it's meat, it's not BBQReview for Brisket Plate with Collard Greens side eating at the bar as a single on a weeknight. Walking by Jax looked inviting although the majority of its ~60 seats were empty. It spoke to me saying "come have a frozen margarita and try my meat". I came back later to find less than 15 people eating and one of those was at the bar drinking. Could not get a bead on the quests. Really wanted to call them locals. So I will. Let go with that. The brisket was cooked then felt reheated under a lamp. It go puffy and dark on one side while it was nice and fatty white on the other. Meh. The portion was fine for what I paid, $17.95. There was a strangeC sweet, vinegar water on the top. It's not a BBQ sauce. If you try the brisket, ask for it dry. The collard greens could be soaked longer. A little on the bitter side for me and I love greens. The little corn bread muffin did not for the meal. Maybe even hurt it with is dry, wee, self. It's not needed. So the food, that I tried, is a total no. I would not repeat. Would o come back for something else? I don't have that kind of time. What about the bar feel? If I'm bringing my own party and maybe eat the burger that people Yelp about or the wings, it could be fun. Closing at 11pm on a weekend night will limit how much fun it can get. For me, Jax gets the Ax

Title: Quick and Filling Fish and Chips in Manhattan

I popped into this bustling fish and chips joint on a Thursday afternoon for a quick bite. Despite a continuous flow of patrons, there was no significant wait, making it an ideal spot for a swift lunch. The ordering process was efficient: place your order at the counter, wait a few minutes, and you're on your way with a meal in hand.

I opted for the Fried Flounder Meal, reasonably priced at $11. It included two generous pieces of flounder, a hearty serving of fries, and a drink. If you're seeking value in Manhattan, this certainly fits the bill with its ample portions and perfectly cooked fries. However, the meal fell short on seasoning—the fish and fries were noticeably unadorned, lacking even the basic salt or a wedge of lemon. This left the tartar sauce with the heavy lifting, a savior for the otherwise bland fare.

While the service was commendably quick and the meal was easy on the wallet, the lack of flavor means I wouldn't go out of my way to return. But if you're nearby and in need of a satisfying, speedy meal, this place might just hit the spot.

Title: A Saturday Night Delight at Emmy's

We visited this bustling spot on a Saturday, grateful for reservations amidst the weekend rush. The service was remarkable; our waitress shone with patience as we wavered over the menu. Her explanations led us to a winning duo: the Emmy pizza and a spicy chicken sandwich.

The sandwich packed heat, yet we found ourselves addicted to its tantalizing sauce. On the other hand, the Emmy was a delightful departure from conventional pizza, striking a harmony with banana peppers and ranch. Dipping the deliciously crispy Detroit-style crust into the accompanying sauce was a highlight.

As a self-proclaimed skeptic of Detroit pizza, I'm converted; Emmy's has redefined my palate. It's an emphatic must-visit for any food enthusiast.

This is what cheese dreams are made of! I was so excited to have found this place on Instagram. The raclette gooey cheese plates are the definition of food porn. We ordered the Burger and the Parisienne. I topped my burger with the porcini cheese and the Parisienne with black truffle cheese. I absolutely loved my burger! It was cooked perfectly- juicy meat, buttery bun. It was a mouthful of flavors. The Parisienne was also delicious, however, it is served medium rare. It was too red for my liking but still enjoyed the dish. I would definitely return and sample other dishes.

I have been dying to try this famous shop since I moved here and finally bit the bullet today. I had a fabulous time chatting about my weekend while munching away on two kinds of spaghetti and meatball dishes. This was MORE than enough for us. We shared the chicken meatball parm sauce and classic meatball with red sauce pasta dishes. Extremely tasty but i have to say they were a little cold. The portions are large! We didn't finish either and took enough home for one full sized portion. The parm sauce was rich and creamy while the red sauce was the Italian classic we needed. We stayed for a while after we were finished to let the food baby come to a rest. It was a pleasant dining experience!!

I came here on a Monday, around 5 PM. It was pretty lowkey and chill, just my type of vibe.Even before looking at the menu, I knew that I wanted some good burgers! The burgers were exactly what I wanted; the lettace and the tomato on them were perfect. Did I mention how perfectly cut and thin the tomatoes were? HAHAHA! Oh, and I asked for the burgers to be well done, and that is exactly what I got.This place did not disappoint! :)

The large bao they offer looked to be something worth reckoning, but for the sake of variety we purchased three different flavors of the smaller bao. They were satisfactory but didn't particularly stick out from any other establishment I've purchased them at. We tried the chicken, pork, and vegetarian options. If you check this place out make sure to try the large one!!

Just regular bar food.  I don't see the hype.  The food was okay, the service was good.  It looks like a normal bar.  Nothing really too special about it that stood out?  If you're coming here for Super Bowl, don't expect to hear anything because for some reason, as a bar, they don't know how to turn the volume up.

Title: A Charming Encounter in Chinatown

I recently dined in a delightful spot in Chinatown and was left with a lasting impression. Unlike many local establishments, the staff here were notably communicative in English, which was a refreshing change. Our server, a talkative lady, was particularly attentive, ensuring we were aware of which dishes contained pork and inquiring about our preference for separate checks right at the start.

Although service was friendly, it must be noted that the food timing was unconventional, with entrees appearing before the appetizer and my iced coffee trailing behind as the final act. Despite the wait, our server's humorous reassurances kept us entertained.

What truly sets this restaurant apart are the generous portions at shockingly low prices—a rarity that hasn't yet drawn the crowds it deserves. The food itself was scrumptious, proving that size did not compromise quality.

In summary, despite some timing hiccups, the engaging service and the value for money have ensured my speedy return—perhaps next time, my iced coffee will once again be the grand finale!

Jin Fong is my friends' go to for dimsum in New York and I can see why! I asked multiple friends for recs and this was the spot everyone responded with. It was nice to see they still serve via carts here. I'm used to ordering via menu, but it's nice to do it this way too. Plus the food is served piping hot, and the carts come by often, so there's really nothing I can complain about. I had all my favorites. Everything was good but I thought their chicken feet in particular was delicious; the skin was fluffy and easy to eat off the bone. The water chestnut cake, another one of my favorites, was also good. The serving of tofu pudding was huge and delicious. It's a huge space and there's normally a wait but we came on a freezing Monday so the restaurant was only half full when we arrived around 11.We each paid $22 pp after tax and tip. Not bad at all!

Title: A Delightful Italian Find Amidst the Festivities

Stepping into the bustling atmosphere of San Gennaro's Feast, my friend and I stumbled upon a charming Italian eatery that immediately caught our attention—not for its rustic brick walls, but for the lively pop-up bar outside. The festive sangria in hand, we joined the short wait for a table, a process made pleasantly swift by attentive hostesses.

Once seated, we were greeted by a friendly waiter who expertly navigated our queries. Though the red wine selection was limited, especially if you favor lighter vintages, it was the homemade pasta that truly shone. I savored the unique pistachio pesto pasta, elevated by a sprinkle of roasted Brussel sprout leaves. My companion, typically skeptical of gnocchi, was won over by a brown butter variant paired with succulent braised lamb.

In summary, this restaurant is a solid pick for anyone seeking delicious and innovative Italian dishes in the heart of Little Italy. We're already planning our next visit.

Title: A Fresh Design and Delicious Eats at PB's New Location

Just stepped into the recently opened PB and was immediately impressed by its stunning new design. The space is generous, boasting ample seating to accommodate crowds with an efficient queue system and well-thought-out lighting adding to the ambience.

While I was surprised to find they haven't adopted Apple Pay yet, this was a minor hiccup in an otherwise seamless experience. The staff greeted me with warmth and provided swift service.

The highlight of my visit was the breakfast croissant sandwich—it was a flaky, buttery delight that exceeded expectations. PB has convincingly secured a spot on my list for future visits, whether to savor their food or simply to enjoy a productive afternoon working or unwinding with a good book.

Title: A Satisfying Foray into Steakhouse Delights

My companions and I tested the waters at this steak restaurant, and it didn't disappoint, especially for novices in the steak scene. We shared a steak meant for two and were impressed by the sumptuous taste and texture, particularly the tender center. The salmon was cooked properly, but the true star was the accompanying tomatoes and fennel, which created a refreshing contrast. Surprisingly, the brussels sprouts stole the show with their perfect roast, leaning more towards soft than crispy—just to my liking.

As expected from a reputable steakhouse, the prices were steep but justified by the quality and service received. An unexpected touch of whimsy was added by the beautiful and innovative candle designs that caught our attention. This place warrants a return visit for those who appreciate thoughtful pairings and well-executed classics.

Title: A Cozy Brunch at Ho Foods

My cravings for Taiwanese breakfast led me back to Ho Foods after a couple of years, and I'm thrilled to report it was worth the wait. Despite the popularity of this gem with just 11 seats, our 20-minute wait on a Sunday at 11:30am was a small price for the delectable meal that awaited us.

The sweet soy milk stood out with its perfect consistency and sweetness, setting the tone for a comforting meal. The you tiao, albeit a touch oily, provided a delightful crunch that paired beautifully with the soy milk. We were pleasantly surprised to find the Lu rou fan on the brunch menu, a dish that held true to its reputation with a well-deserved rave—it was outstanding.

Yes, you might find the prices a bit steep, but they're quite reasonable considering the location. Ho Foods left such an impression that I'm already planning my next visit for dinner to try the beef noodle soup. A return trip is unquestionably on the horizon!

My brother in law and I were kind of bar-hopping..but to cocktail lounges, not dive bars. We were at Crimson and Rye before this, and I wish we came here sooner! We got here and the bar was packed - it was a friday night too, so not too surprising. While I was waiting to order, my BIL found a second floor with a more relaxed vibe, where you can actually hear someone speak unlike the bottom floor. And according to the website, it's called the Siren room. It's also intimate, and had a very 1920's feel.We found some standing space and ordered our drinks + oysters!! I ordered the French 75// has Gin, Fresh Lemon, Bubbly, Lemon Twist; Catherine Deneuve and it was DELICIOUS! That was the kind of drink I was looking for - light, bubbly, fruity + refreshing without being obnoxiously sweet. I forgot what my BIL got but he liked it. and we both really enjoyed the oysters! Wished the servers/bartenders were a bit more warm, but it was better than the other place!

Title: A Divine Italian Brunch in the Village

If you're in the mood for an Italian feast that will tantalize your taste buds, this quaint spot in the village should be at the top of your list. My Saturday brunch experience was nothing short of exceptional, especially after savoring their rigatoni with mini meatballs and ricotta cheese—it was, without exaggeration, the finest rigatoni dish I've ever enjoyed.

Adding to the delight was their 3-for-1 drinks deal, where I indulged in three refreshing mimosas for just $15. The service was attentive, the prices surprisingly modest, and the quality of the food simply unmatched. While the indoor lighting was a tad dim for brunch, it did little to detract from the overall ambience and top-notch dining experience.

I wholeheartedly recommend this gem for any meal, and I'm already planning my return trip for more of that heavenly rigatoni. Do yourself a favor and give this Italian place a visit—you won't be disappointed.

Title: High Hopes Met with Mixed Feelings at Trendy Eatery

With high expectations for a reputable dining spot, I was unfortunately left somewhat underwhelmed by my recent visit. It wasn’t all a miss, however, as the shining star of the evening was undoubtedly the service. Our waiter was exceptional—thoughtful enough to steer us away from over-ordering with a friendly chuckle.

The culinary journey began with the Clam Casino. While not disappointing, the miniature clams on my plate did seem a touch forlorn compared to their plump, juicier cousins I've encountered elsewhere.

The biggest letdown was perhaps the Filet Mignon. It was a peculiar take on the classic, sporting a heavily peppered, thick outer crust that hinted at dry-aging—a process that, while innovative, unfortunately resulted in a loss of the meat's intrinsic tenderness. The dish didn't align with my expectations of a succulent and soft filet.

Moving on to the Suckling Pig, the reconstructed presentation was reminiscent of Tuome's technique, yet failed to match up to its standard. Accompanying the meat was an odd choice of fried dough, which took up an excessive portion of the plate and did little to complement the pork.

The Pomme Soufflé was another surprise, and not a particularly pleasant one. Anticipating a cheesy delight, I found myself facing a plate of salty fried potatoes instead.

In summary, while the service was impeccable, the food left me yearning for more—both in terms of quality and meeting my culinary expectations. An adventure, yes, but also a reminder that not all that glitters is gold in the bustling restaurant scene.

Go Dutch or Go Solo!!!I sat at the bar in this swanky joint as the live music played.  The service was friendly and immediate.  Definitely a great brunch place; the menu has a great variety.  I opted for the avocado smash and as a beverage the Ginger Rodgers.   Soooo good!!!After a squeeze of Lemon on the avocado smash to bring out the flavors....it was even better.Definitely a place to try!!

My lunch experience at this bustling restaurant on a busy Friday proved to be delightful. Despite the crowd, service was prompt and attentive, with our server ensuring we always had water at the table and our meals arriving swiftly. We savored the Kung Pao Chicken, which was tasty and met our expectations. However, the shredded chicken and pork were indistinguishable in flavor, leading us to believe they were either chicken or pork, not both as ordered. Nevertheless, the general quality of the dishes was quite good. Pricing was reasonable for the quality and quantity of food received. Overall, service and value were top-notch, and while the food was enjoyable, a bit more distinction between the dishes would have been appreciated.

Service: 5/5
Food: 4/5
Price: 4/5

I ventured into Super Taste, a quaint hole-in-the-wall Chinese eatery tucked away in the bustling streets of Chinatown, searching for an affordable noodle fix. Though dining solo here felt awkward, as seating arrangements had me sharing a table with a stranger, the experience was worth it for the food.

I heeded my friends' praises of Super Taste's baos but decided against them, not wanting to overindulge. Instead, I savored their hand-pulled noodles with beef. Despite my initial dismay at the plastic container (a far cry from San Francisco's eco-conscious presentation), the meal itself was a delightful surprise. The noodles were exceptional — immersed in a rich, savory broth with succulent beef that practically melted in my mouth.

A fiery chili sauce available on the table added the perfect kick, elevating the flavors to new heights, and I found myself devouring the entire serving with relish.

To my amazement, Super Taste accepts credit cards, adding a touch of convenience to the dining experience. This spot is a must-visit for anyone craving quick, delectable, and budget-friendly Chinese noodles. And considering the lingering thought of their raved-about baos, it seems a second visit might be imminent.

I recently visited a vibrant local eatery known for its empanadas, and I must say, the experience was delightful. The atmosphere was lively, and the food absolutely lived up to the buzz. I indulged in a feast of 10 empanadas, each as tantalizing as the last, and at $2 a pop, the value was unbeatable — a perfect pick-me-up for when the budget is tight. To top it off, I enjoyed not one, but two fresh fruit smoothies, which were the perfect accompaniment to the savory treats. Highly recommended for an affordable and satisfying meal.

The food was delicious! We loved everything we got and ate It all. Definitely recommend the wontons. Next time i go back i want to take some wontons home with me! The staff is very nice and speaks decent English as well if you can't speak Chinese. This place gets busy so sometimes there is a wait. Everything was very good so highly recommend! However, they do add tip automatically on the bill so aware because they don't specify It on the bill and just add It!

I have been coming to this little place for like 5 times and finally decided to put the good words to it!It is absolutely one of the best valued soba noodle restaurants in NYC. I came across this place when I was actually going to the restaurant next door and decided to giive this a try.
