It surprised and impressed me in every way!For around $17, you can order a combo of soba noodle and another classic Japanese dish, which is great value since the portion for both is definitely not disappointing and the flavors are authentic. One thing you need to keep in mind is their secret code- you should ask for the big bowl of soba (for exactly the same price!) and gets your cravings fulfilled.Would come back AGAIN AND AGAIN AND AGAIN.

This spot is a clear winner for best Shanghai snack food in the Murray Hill area! The soup dumplings are excellent and the pork rib noodles are fantastic. Don't leave without trying a various of noodles and Bao's!

Came here after a movie date with Pogibear. Like always was craving some Ramen and it was perfect weather for it. Decided to check this place out because they have a vegan option for ramen. We sat down right by the entrance so I was freezing every time someone opens the door. We both ordered the matcha ramen, which came with veggies like mushroom with soy milk base. I initially didn't like how it tasted, but after few more spoonful, the taste grew on me. Never had matcha on ramen before which was very interesting. Ramen is always the best in cold days.

I was Midtown and asked locals where has the best pizza and NY Pizza Suprema was mentioned a few times. It has a great location right by the LIRR and not too far from the Manhattan Center. My first time here I tried the sausage and pepperoni deep dish pizza and it tasted so good, in South FL there's nothing like it. The deep dish pizza was full of flavor, the sauce was homemade and although the center was soft the edges were crispy and I loved that. On my second visit I ordered a regular peppering slice and the cheese was tasty and the pizza was cooked perfectly. The customer service was awesome, even though both visits the place was packed... they managed to assist everyone quickly and efficiently. You can also tell it's family owned which is great. I really enjoyed this pizza and I'm happy that I was able to come here not once but twice in a few days :)!

I've had Artichoke Basille's bookmarked for years. While I'm no stranger to pizza, I've never actually tried an artichoke slice before. After skimming the reviews and pics, I made a decision the next time I was near Union Square to check it out. Lo and behold, that day finally came so I decided to pop in for a slice. Artichoke isn't large - they're set up to to be mostly a takeout spot but have a counter and stools lining the perimeter if you want to sit and eat. It's definitely spacious though, it can accommodate a small crowd plus people eating quite comfortably. Aesthetics are casual pizza shop - nothing too crazy. The menu mostly contains specialty slices for $6 each, as well as pies for $32. You might be put off by the price per slice, but they're huge - long enough that you need two paper plates to accommodate and definitely shareable if need be. While all their offerings sounded delicious, this was my first time so I wanted to try the artichoke. I wasn't disappointed - the slice was topped with plenty of artichoke hearts and lots of creamy sauce. The crust was a little too thick for my liking, but I think it was needed due to the heavy toppings so it didn't bother me.   Service was fast and friendly - note however that this business is cash only. Overall, I had a great first experience at Artichoke's - if all their slices are like their signature one I can understand why this place is so popular. If I ever get a hankering for some artichoke pie you know where I'll be ;-).

Title: Mixed Impressions at High-Priced Tasting Menu

I recently visited a restaurant with high expectations for their renowned tasting menu, now priced at $145 per person for six courses. Unfortunately, the experience didn't quite measure up to the value others have raved about. Both of us received identical courses except for an excessive dessert assortment that tried, albeit unsuccessfully, to make up for the lack of variety in earlier dishes.

The pre-course selection of bread offered various types but none stood out, certainly not against the memorable offerings at Contra or even the loaves I bake at home. The chilled cucumber soup with salmon started well; the salmon provided a savory punch, but the soup alone faltered. The Uni and Madai Sashimi, with its watermelon broth, was my highlight of the evening – a texture delight.

However, the Burrata Ravioli with English Peas was a mixed bag with some peas distractingly undercooked. Our halibut main course yielded mixed results; one perfectly cooked, the other disappointingly overdone. The duck with cherry, rich and well-flavored, particularly impressed my partner, save for some unwanted fennel.

Dessert was a bombardment of sweetness; five varieties including an exceptional toffee ice cream and apricot addition. Post-dessert marshmallows and madeleines were delightful, the former being the best I've ever tasted.

While the dinner had its moments, it pales in comparison to other fine dining experiences like the value at Contra, the immaculate dishes at Gary Danko, or the uniqueness of Momofuku Ko, to name a few. Service was inconsistent, with lengthy waits initially and a too-quick succession of heavy courses. A forgotten coffee offer and absent staff at departure only added to the disappointment.

In retrospect, a regular menu item or a lunch prix fixe might be more satisfying and better paced. Considering all factors, dining at an establishment like Nur seems a more appealing option, with its superior bread, flavorsome sauces, attentive service, and more reasonable pricing.
Came here for our yearly Chinese New Year celebration with Dim Sum. Lots of food in rotation for you to choose from, festive environment, the costumes are an extra treat ;)

This intimate little tapas place feels like a secret bit of New York unassumingly tucked away right off of Grand Street. In fact, we almost walked past it looking for this place. I brought a friend here, and he marveled over how many times he had walked past this location without even noticing it. Service is friendly if a little bit on the slow side, and for a hot summer day, it was a tad warm inside. However, the food more than makes up for these slight hiccups. Japanese Guacamole & Pork Dip: Yuzu-Miso Guacamole - the portion is small, but it's a lovely fusion of guacamole and rich pork, topped with one of my favorite garnishments - chili threads! This perfect for two people to share a few bites.Ponzu Mushroom: 4 types of mushroom, tofu sauce, tempura crispy bits - the hype is real, every bite of this dish an absolute joy, and we had no problems polishing this off.Tako-taco: octopus, chickpea, spicy mayo, nori sauce - now at first glance, this looked very...green, but we gamely bit into this and the combination of the chickpea and octopus (even covered in greens) was a fresh dichotomy of meaty richness countered with the nori sauce and crunch of the "rabbit food"Tuna Tartare: prickly pear sauce, dragon fruit, crostini - pretty and pretty standard for a tartare, the dragon fruit was visually a nice contrast, but the flavors melted into the tartare and didn't enhance it much. Don't get me wrong, it's not a bad dish in any sense, and is a generous size for tapas, but it's just overshadowed by the other dishes here.Chicken Skewers: one of the specials for the night - 6 ridiculously tender skewers topped with a rich warm sauce, I was going to save one for the puppers stuck at home, but alas - we ate it. Rabbit Stew: this was a special for the night, and we were a tad ambitious to order this, but the flavors were rich, heavy, and really - this would be an amazing winter dish, but wasn't the best choice for us to order during a 90 degree summer. I was sad that they were out of the cherry blossom cocktails, but managed to console myself with a tried and true favorite - Yuzu Sake! All in all, this is a lovely little diamond hidden away, and I'll definitely be back with small groups to discover their other dishes here!

I recently had a delightful Japanese BBQ experience at this charming spot. The pricing was quite reasonable for the area, especially the dessert menu, which stood out as an exceptional value. The lunch specials and happy hour offerings provide even more enticing deals. For those seeking top-notch food at excellent prices, an afternoon visit is highly recommended.

Popular spot in the neighborhood for a quick bite. Tried the cheese and the Spinach-cheese pizzas. They were alright. The guy at the front was a little weird though. He was on the phone/earphones. Wasn't really clear who he's talking to. But yeah, pizza was alright. Decent place. Tables and chairs on the left if you need to chill for a bit.

Title: A Cozy Gem for Pre and Post-Show Dining

Located conveniently for theater-goers, this restaurant offers a surprisingly spacious and romantic setting, despite its unassuming entrance. Soft lighting adds to the ambiance, making it a superb pick for post-show dinner. On my visit, the kitchen was recovering from repairs, leading to a somewhat reduced menu, but the service didn’t miss a beat – it was attentive and swift.

My personal highlight was the Cajun chicken sandwich coupled with a side of fries – a perfect comfort dish. The chicken and mashed potatoes were also a solid choice, hearty and satisfying. For those with a sweet tooth, the indulgent hot fudge with walnuts over vanilla ice cream is a decadent treat, but be warned – it’s rich enough to warrant a sharing strategy.

Arriving at 8:15 pm on a Thursday, I was greeted by numerous vacant tables, but don't let that fool you. This spot fills up quickly around showtimes, bustling with an air of excitement and the potential for celebrity sightings. It's best to plan your visit with the ebb and flow of the neighboring entertainment in mind.

I don't know. I was excited to come here, but I really wasn't wowed by the food. I got myself the combo; if you're not getting the bowl, the combo just makes so much more sense economically. I got the 2 buddha baos + 3 spring rolls combo. For $10.95, it's standard Urbanspace pricing. Fine with me.The spring rolls were fine, but the baos kinda disappointed me. I really was disappointed with the tofu. Love the idea of crispy tofu, but I really wish the tofu had some zing or marinade to it because it just tasted bland. Like it was warm when you bit into it and then the tofu tasted like typical salad tofu. So much potential, but ended up disappointed. Oh well. Maybe next time, we'll see....

I recently visited a quaint stall where empanadas and churros are sold side by side, each tempting treat displayed in a transparent shelf cabinet, allowing customers to eye their choices. The variety on offer was impressive—I opted for creamy chicken, ham and cheese, pork saltano, and beef criolla.

Firstly, I appreciated the practical touch of stamped crusts, indicating the different fillings—a clever and charming detail that made distinguishing between them a breeze. The crust itself boasted a nice golden hue, suggesting a flakiness that one would expect from a well-prepared empanada.

However, upon tasting, the visual promise fell short. While the crust looked appealing, it was disappointingly dry and hard, with the edges being particularly tough. The anticipated flakiness was absent, and the thickness of the crust meant that some bites were devoid of any filling at all.

The fillings, unfortunately, did nothing to salvage the experience. They lacked the moisture and vivid flavor needed to counterbalance the crust's dryness, rendering them rather forgettable. To add to the letdown, the empanadas were served at room temperature, which likely contributed to their lackluster texture and taste. The absence of a heating element in the shelf cabinet was evident.

Moreover, when comparing to the larger and less pricey offerings at Empanada Mama's in Manhattan, the value proposition of these empanadas further declines.

In summary, while the stall presents an array of well-stamped and aesthetically inviting empanadas, the actual eating experience doesn't live up to the visual promise due to the dry crust and uninspiring fillings, alongside concerns about freshness and temperature.

**Cafeteria Restaurant Review**

Despite initial hesitations due to mixed reviews, my breakfast experience at Cafeteria has completely turned my perspective around. Unexpectedly, the meal kicked off with an intriguing sparkling water named Llanllyr from Wales, offering a delightfully carbonated start.

Now, onto the crux of the visit – the food. The Lemon Ricotta Pancakes were the stars. Topped with a mascarpone crepe and fresh blueberries, they were irresistible, although I did find myself asking for extra maple syrup. Another gem on the table was the Truffle Eggs, which were elegantly plated atop a thick slice of toasted French bread, accompanied by a delicate mixed green salad. The Maple Smoked Bacon didn't disappoint either, delivering on flavor.

However, not all that glitters is gold. The fresh fruit selection fell short, with strawberries that didn't hit the mark of ripeness. The fresh-squeezed orange juice was refreshing, but unfortunately, the coffee didn't live up to the same standard.

Service-wise, Juan, our waiter, embodied warmth and professionalism, enhancing the dining experience with his sweetness and attentiveness.

With the sumptuous food and excellent service, Cafeteria has earned itself another visit in the near future. Despite minor misses, the overall experience was very enjoyable.

Title: A Brunch Haven That Lives Up to the Hype

I recently visited this gem of a brunch spot on a weekend, and now I get the buzz. With a reservation for three in tow, we were quickly whisked to our table amidst a bustling crowd—a hint to make a reservation because this place is a hit.

The staff greeted us with warmth, and the variety in the menu had something for everyone's palate. I opted for the Smith's Eggs Benedict, and it didn't disappoint—savory and satisfying. Plus, their coffee comes with free refills, a perk for caffeine aficionados like myself.

This affordable and laid-back spot has won me over. I'm already planning my next visit. Word to the wise: snag those weekend reservations; you'll need them!

This gem is amazing for a late night spot that is near central park area. The atmosphere is great and the staff is amazing! Me and the track pack came here after work and had a great time! I got the don katasu and a beer. The katsu was phenomenal and the beer just hit the spot. They stay open til 4am so its great for an after hours spot. Server was really great!

Joe's Pizza in New York City is more than a pizzeria; it's an institution. The Greenwich Village location, purportedly the original, is my go-to spot for what I consider top-tier NYC pizza. Both locals and tourists are drawn to its legendary status, with celebrity endorsements adorning the walls, adding to its charm. Options like pepperoni and plain never disappoint. Here, the routine is simple: step in, order at the counter (cash only), and sprinkle some garlic salt on your slice for an extra flavor kick. Joe's is an essential NYC experience, be it for a quick bite or a pilgrimage for pizza perfection.

Great casual place for dinner! We came here this weekend and we were so impressed! Our waiter was so awesome! He was really energetic, helpful and attentive. They have a ton of great options. I got the bowl with spicy pork meatballs, Parmesan cream sauce and kale. What an amazing combo that our waiter suggested! The pork was so tender and delicious and paired perfectly with the Parmesan cream sauce! The kale was so flavorful and they give you a very good portion. You can also ask for extra focaccia to get all the sauce! Love the meatball shop!

I took advantage of the daily happy hour special (4 - 6 pm): $9.99 for a meat of your choice and three sides. You have a wide array of meats and sides to choose from. There's no table service so you get on line, order, then find any available table. I had no problems finding a table once I had my order in hand. Fast and friendly service so you never have to wait long. The staff is professional and definitely keeps the establishment tidy. Groovy Spanish music was playing in the background while you eat and it adds a nice touch to the dining experience. It was at a very reasonable level so if you're with someone or a group you can hear yourselves converse. The salmon is ordered was so juicy, buttery and flavorful. The sweet plantains were perfectly sweet and crisp. The red beans and rice tasted great. The vegetable medley was decent. It could have used some more seasoning. Overall amazing experience!

Right off the L. But it's not an L, it's a W!Taco Tuesday. What a classic day. Nothing better than lovely weather anddd tacos. Grabbed 2 tacos. One carne Asada and the other carnitas. Because tragically I am allergic to avocado I had to ask for no guac but you can still see how beautiful these are. The meat has that nice grilled taste and is juicy. Really solid choice when you want that taco fix.

Title: A Delightful Evening at Hunan Slurp

I recently visited Hunan Slurp with my two cousins and had a marvelous time. Thanks to Resy, our reservation went smoothly, and we were seated without delay. To our delight, the establishment is BYOB, and while my memory of the corkage fee is hazy, it felt reasonable, hovering around $15.

One of the highlights was the kitchen's open-concept design, allowing us to observe the chef's culinary prowess through a spacious window—a touch that added to our dining experience. Coupled with the warm and informative staff, the atmosphere was inviting and engaging.

We embarked on a shared culinary adventure, sampling numerous dishes. Remarkably, the Cabbage (priced at $18) took the crown—its exceptional taste ensuring I'd return for it alone. Following a close second was the innovative General Tsao's Chicken Reimagined ($22). We also enjoyed the uncomplicated yet tasty Spare Ribs ($12) and the Pepper & Pork Rice Noodle ($16). The only underperformer was the Lotus Meatball ($16), where despite the alluring description, the medley of ingredients like sticky rice, heritage pork, and truffle sauce lacked harmony.

Despite the single misstep, my enthusiasm remains undiminished. Hunan Slurp certainly ranks high on my list for a revisit, and I eagerly anticipate exploring more of what their menu has to offer.

I recently visited a quaint little spot that's perfect for grab-and-go meals. The freshness of the food really stands out, and the portions are generous, giving you great value for your money. I indulged in the bulgogi and galbi, and both dishes were absolutely scrumptious, teeming with authentic flavors. It's safe to say this place has earned its spot as my new go-to lunch destination. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a quick, yet satisfying meal!

Upon visiting this downtown spot to pass the time, I found the service at the bar to be exceptionally welcoming and imbued with an authentic Irish charm that truly suited the place's ambiance. Opting for a tequila sunrise, the drink was expertly mixed and served with a smile. Accompanying the beverage, I tried the wings and jalapeño poppers. Unfortunately, the wings seemed to have suffered from freezer burn, resulting in a rather bland experience. Similarly, the poppers appeared to be a direct trip from freezer to fryer. Despite the lackluster fare, the service at this establishment is its saving grace. With the added benefit of not being crowded, this bar stands out as a hidden gem for those looking to enjoy a drink in good company.

Ok so give them an extra star.......still not sold on the food.....however happy hour late night hours this is the place to be! Music is on point and drinks are strong.....however still the food is nothing to speak on.

I recently dined at a local eatery and came away with mixed feelings. The chicken sandwich, priced at $7.50, was decent though a bit too salty for my taste and heavy on the carrots. The iced coffee, at $4.50, was adequate. However, I was disconcerted by the billing process. Despite my order totaling $12, I was charged $13 without a given receipt or explanation. Future diners, take heed – verify the prices before paying to avoid a similar scenario. Caution and clarity might be in order when patronizing this establishment.

Title: A Cozy Spot for Authentic Malaysian Delights

Finding genuine Malaysian cuisine in the city can be a daunting task, but this charming restaurant is a true gem. The ambiance is cozy, creating a welcoming atmosphere that immediately puts you at ease. The staff are warm and friendly, contributing to the overall delightful dining experience.

The menu offers a variety of mouthwatering dishes at reasonable prices. We savored the char kueh teow, which was perfectly seasoned and wok-fried to smoky perfection. The basil fried rice was fragrant and full of flavor, complementing the excellently prepared salted egg yolk shrimp - a dish that truly shined with its rich, savory notes and crisp texture.

Service was top-notch, with attentive servers who ensured our meal was comfortable and satisfying. Overall, if you're on the hunt for good Malaysian food, this place is a must-visit. It’s got all the essentials: delectable food, inviting setting, and stellar service.

Title: Bottomless Brunch Bliss at Monk McGinns

I've found a brunch gem in Monk McGinns, and my recent visit has cemented it as a regular spot on my dining circuit. With a $39 Pulsd deal, the experience began with a bubbly, perfectly mixed mimosa courtesy of Jacqueline, who understands that it's all about the champagne with just a hint of OJ for color.

Seated at the bar this time, the ambiance was as inviting as ever. The 90 minutes of unlimited drinks were a parade of joy—bellinis, Aperol spritzes, and, of course, those stellar mimosas. The attentive staff made sure our glasses were never empty, generously topping us up before we even had the chance to ask.

But it's not just the drinks; the breakfast burger was a savory delight. Juicy, well-seasoned, and accompanied by a sinful amount of thick-cut bacon, it's the kind of meal that haunts you—in the best way possible—long after the last bite.

In summary, Monk McGinns delivers a brunch worth every penny, deal or no deal. From the drinks to the eats and the service, everything is spot on. I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

Great healthy fast casual spot that isn't just the normal American fanfare. Their bowls, sandwiches, and salads all have an Indian twist on them.Between two people we got the Chana Masala bowl and kale & hearty salad with the coconut ladoo for dessert. The Chana masala bowl was very spicy, but great when combined with the rice and veggies to cool it off a bit. The kale & hearty salad had a great dressing and flavor to it! I thought it would be really mediocre, but it was great.The coconut ladoo was really good! They added chia seed and golden raisins. Great texture and flavors.

Whenever I come to BCD, I always get the same thing: Beef Tofu Soup, mild spicy. It always hits the spot and satisfies my late night cravings. Beef is very tender and the quality of the ingredients they use is excellent. Side dishes are good and service is always fast.  Overall, this place is a solid dining option. I never had a bad experience here. Don't be intimidated with the long lines; it moves rather quickly because the place is spacious! Even if you order just 1 soup with no appetizers/meat, you will be left full and satisfied.

I went to this restaurant on a Sunday around 7 pm by myself and was immediately sat at the bar. The bar has 4 seats, and all the chairs have buckets that you can place a jacket or a bag in. The restaurant was full, so if I did come with someone, it probably would have been a 15-30 minute wait. There is also a bar side to the restaurant, so when walking in, make sure to look at the signs to know which side you're going too. I ordered the Spicy Miso Ramen ($16), which had a nice kick to it, but not too spicy for those that can't take too much heat. The meat was tender, and the broth was flavorful. It comes with a half soft boiled egg, perfectly cooked. The corn adds a subtle sweetness, and the scallions are a must. There is a bunch more on the menu that I want to try so I will definitely be back with some friends.  Great ambiance for a date night, a meal by yourself, or with friends and family.

Title: A Disappointing Culinary Encounter at a Local Vietnamese Spot

Having frequented various Vietnamese establishments, I stepped into this restaurant with a sense of familiarity—unremarkable décor and indifferent cleanliness were as I expected, eliciting neither praise nor complaint. Yet, the true measure of such a place lies in its cuisine, which, regrettably, fell short of embodying the spirit of Vietnamese cooking.

Despite arriving with the kind of hunger that typically makes any meal seem enticing, the dishes we ordered failed to satisfy. The sugarcane shrimp, a dish I usually hold in high esteem, was a particular letdown and left me wary of it tainting my fond memories of better versions. Similarly, the pork chop broken rice was a testament to mediocrity; a basic marinade that even the fish sauce couldn't redeem left me puzzled—how could one err with such a classic?

Adding to the disappointment, my partner's choice of beef chow fun was a foreseeable mistake. The dish's half-eaten remnants spoke volumes of its quality. In a gesture of grace, I refrain from being overly harsh due to my cultural ties, but truthfully, it's a challenge to recommend an eatery where not one dish managed to hit the mark.

In essence, this restaurant failed to live up to the vibrant flavors and soulful preparations characteristic of my people's cuisine. It's a place I cannot in good conscience recommend.

They got my order wrong and I didn't realize until it was too late. I asked for "pork soup dumplings" and what I got was steamed dumplings, not soup dumplings. I should have known because the shape of the dumplings was wrong, but I was tired and hungry.. The steamed dumplings were fine, but they weren't the soup dumplings I was craving. I feel like the person taking my order should have clarified with me. Anyway, the price was fair and the place was clean.

Atmosphere abounds in this splendid genuine Italian restaurant.  You'll need to book but it's worth it.  The walls are covered with the various celebrities who have eaten there which gives a nice ambience.  Tables are close together which adds to the general friendly feeling of the place. My guests all had pasta of one kind or another and enjoyed them enormously.  I had Fegato a la Veneziana which is not easy to find.  Sliced tender calves liver, smothered in onions with a rich red wine and balsamic sauce. Wondrous. A rather pricey house red but good quality Tuscan made with San Giovese. All in all,  a definite return is required.

Pretty decent IHOPLike most IHOPs, you kind of know what to expect when you arrive. It will not be a glamorous dining experience, but you will be fed. I was having an insane desire to have breakfast for dinner and dropped by one early evening. I ordered a steak omelette with a stack of pancakes. I had no idea that the restaurant had all you could eat pancakes, but the omelette was so large that could hardly finish the pancakes. The service was a bit slow. I think that was more of an issue of staffing for the evening because there were only two waitresses. So, I will cut them some slack. No major complaints about this IHOP.

We were working on a Sunday in Murray Hill, and there wasn't a whole lot open when we started getting hungry for lunch. We were in the midst of planning an event and needed a quick bite before our team of volunteers showed up.Fields had just opened and we had never been. We've only been once, but it was a good experience. Fast and easy. We both got salads. Him, a cobb. Me a Caesar with chicken. We'll definitely be back to try it again. It's a good place for a quick bite. It's a step above fast food ... or at least that's what it seems to be. Healthy-ish.

This place was sort of a last minute decision. It wasn't bad. The service was pretty good and there wasn't a wait for the food. The drinks were entirely too expensive for what you get. I got the spaghetti and meatballs and was pretty happy with it for the most part.The environment was nice and the music was good. Overall, it was A-ok, just not a top choice for my next visit.

Nestled beneath Pershing Bridge and a mere stroll across the road from Grand Central Station on 42nd Street lies a delightful old school eatery that sets the scene for a perfect Sunday brunch or lunch outing. The ambience exudes a relaxed charm, inviting patrons to unwind in its cozy embrace.

On my visit, I couldn't resist trying the chicken pot pie, touted by the establishment as the greatest in NYC. While I reserve the title of 'greatest' for those pies encased fully in pastry, not merely capped with it, I must admit this pie did indeed hit the spot. Its hearty filling and flavorful crust combined for a very satisfying meal. Despite my personal pastry preference, this spot is certainly worth a visit for a comforting and relaxed dining experience.

I recently visited an awesome restaurant that delighted me with its tasty food and chill vibe. The decor was spot on, creating a welcoming atmosphere that was matched by the friendliness of the staff. With a myriad of options on the menu, there's something for everyone. While the spicy pork meatballs with spicy sauce left me wanting a bit more punch in flavor, the experience was still positive enough to warrant a return visit. And let me tell you, the Spaghetti & Meatballs entrée was crazy—in the best way possible. Pretty good, indeed! I'm looking forward to my next meal here.

Title: A Cozy Surprise with Satisfying Eats

I recently discovered a gem of a restaurant after wandering with friends in an area sparse with dining options. This cozy spot instantly felt like home with its warm atmosphere and proved to be a terrific place to unwind and dine with companions.

While the menu wasn't brimming with vegetarian options, the choices available were delectable. I indulged in a grilled vegetable panini that was both mouthwatering and generously portioned – an unbeatable value that could have easily made for a second meal.

The only drawback was the dim lighting, which added to the charm but made navigation a bit of a challenge. Regardless, this charming establishment left a mark, and I'm eager to return for another delightful meal.

Title: Late Night Korean BBQ Delights at Samwon

If you find yourself craving Korean barbecue after a night out in Manhattan, Samwon is your go-to spot. Open until the wee hours of 3 a.m., this eatery offers affordable and delectable options that stand up to the glowing reviews.

The prime time to visit is between 11 p.m. and 3 a.m., when the atmosphere buzzes with vibrant, party-goers winding down with some sizzling BBQ. Whether you're wrapping up your night or just getting started, Samwon provides an energetic vibe alongside quality Korean cuisine. Forget the typical late-night fare; Samwon is where the cool crowd gathers to satisfy those nocturnal hunger pangs.

***Review is for dessert only.***Not sure if this is because it was after dinner hours, but this place was awfully overpriced and mediocre for their desserts.I had Veselka bookmarked due to high ratings on Yelp.  Photos also looked good.  Actual experience however paled in comparison.Apple Crumble ($8 for a small square) cake did NOT have whipped cream, as per photos.  It was microwaved and parts were hard.  It definitely wasn't fresh!Blintzes was slightly better, but small for $10.  That's $8 for a blintz + an additional $2 for a tablespoon of raspberry compote.Atmosphere seemed more about ushering people in/out as quick as possible!  Prices were high considering the portion sizes.  Service was fine, but seemed incredibly rushed.

Title: A Brunch Delight at a Chic Christmas Lodge

I recently visited a terrific brunch spot where the dining experience is simplified with a meal ticket system. For just $44, you're treated to a well-rounded meal that includes an appetizer basket, fresh fruit, a hearty entrée, and a beverage choice.

The charm of the establishment did not disappoint, even though we couldn't access the rooftop during the lodge season. Instead, we were cozily nestled inside a space that can only be described as a Christmas lodge come to life.

Service was impressive; our servers were both quick and attentive, ensuring a pleasant dining atmosphere. As for the food, the appetizer basket was filled with delightful mini croissants, scones, and raisin bread. My avocado toast was not only generous in portion but also customizable with egg whites—a healthy plus in my book.

Overall, the experience was nothing short of fantastic. I'm already looking forward to my next visit, with hopes of enjoying the breathtaking rooftop view! Highly recommend!

Title: Cozy Homestyle Japanese Dining at Ootoya

My recent visit to Ootoya on a quiet Thursday evening turned out to be a delightful culinary experience. With reservations made through Yelp, my companions and I were promptly seated upon arrival at 6 pm. Initially, the restaurant was tranquil, but to no surprise, it was bustling with patrons by 7 pm.

The ambiance of Ootoya captures the essence of classic Japanese homestyle dining, and the service is impeccable. Right from the warm greeting by the chefs and waitstaff to the thoughtful provision of warm towels, they ensure a comforting start to the meal.

Our orders included the Katsu Toji set and a Mini Oyako Don with Mini Udon. Each set came with a generous serving of miso soup, rice, and pickled vegetables. The Katsu Toji was a savory delight, and although the Oyako Don was heavily laden with onions, it did not disappoint in flavor.

It's worth noting that Ootoya operates on a no-tipping policy, and while the pricing may be on the higher end, the overall quality of the food and the ambiance justifies the cost. 

I would wholeheartedly recommend Ootoya for a variety of occasions – whether it's a group outing, a romantic date, a professional work meal, or a casual dinner with family and friends. It's a versatile spot that promises a delicious and fulfilling dining experience.

After facing long wait times at other Korean BBQ joints, my friends and I stumbled upon this gem with no wait – likely due to its à la carte menu rather than an all-you-can-eat offering. What a delightful surprise it turned out to be! The quality of the meat here is unparalleled, a standard we wouldn't have found elsewhere. Not only is the quality top-notch, but the portions are generous as well. The meat practically melts in your mouth – a clear sign of the premium experience this restaurant provides. If you're after exceptional Korean BBQ, this place is a must-visit.

Title: A Gem at Quality Bistro – Exceptional Dining Experience

I'm absolutely enamored with Quality Bistro! From start to finish, the experience was flawless. The staff strikes the perfect balance of attentiveness and subtlety, led by our outstanding server, Shannon, who expertly guided our menu choices.

The drink selection impressed us; the Whiskey A L'Orange and Old Fashioned Au Poivre were standouts, and the Chateau De La Chaize Brouilly complemented the meal beautifully. As for the food, the Butter Service Garni shouldn't be missed; it's a delightful and inventive treat. The French Onion soup was rich and satisfying, while the Strip Steak Frites and Lamb Chops were both bursting with flavor, cooked to perfection.

The atmosphere is versatile, catering to a variety of attire and occasions, with a relaxed vibe that encourages interaction among diners. 

In a nutshell, Quality Bistro is nothing short of exceptional. Whether you're a local or just passing through, do yourself a favor and dine here. You won't regret it!

Title: Solid Burgers and Crazy Shakes at a Cool Spot

Rating: ★★★½

Review:
This restaurant certainly has a unique vibe with its two-tiered dining concept. Upstairs, it's all about the shakes, drinks, and bar bites, while downstairs invites you to indulge in their burger offerings. I went for the old-fashioned burger, which was pretty standard but satisfying—a solid choice that came accompanied by a generous portion of fries. The shakes here are a spectacle, oversized concoctions that seem designed for sharing. What truly stood out was the service, which was nothing short of excellent. A great place to visit if you're in the mood for a traditional burger or a fun, shareable treat.

The quintessential New York slice.Probably the best single slice of pizza I've ever had. Perfectly simplistic. I was amazed at how crispy and firm the slice was considering how thin it seemed. Served perfectly hot without burning the roof of my mouth. If you're looking for a classic slice of plain cheese pizza, it won't get better than Joes.Also when you show up at 10:45am and there's a dozen people inside ordering, you know it's legit.

The aptly named SoHo Square lived up to the hype.  The biggest downside though was waiting over an hour for it.  I love pizza and this was absolutely one of the best slices of pizza I have ever had, but I am knocking off a star because I don't know if any pizza is worth an hour plus wait and I believe that there were some logistical fixes that could get the line for their most popular pepperoni pizza square slice moving quicker.  It seemed like there was always about half of a magherita pizza available, so I was a little confused to see them continue to put those in the oven when the pepperoni was flying off the counter like the worldwide supply of pepperoni was about to run out and this was the last chance people would get to eat it.  The other issue was that people were ordering whole pies, so the second a pepperoni pizza came out the oven, it seemed like every third or fourth person would walk away with the whole pie and everyone would have to wait for the next one to come out, which severely slowed down the line, so it would be nice maybe have a cut off point for when people can order whole pies, to keep the line at the walk up counter moving.  These are only humble suggestions from a hungry guy who eagerly awaited his SoHo Square and was overjoyed to have it live up to the hype, but it also would be nice to not have the time to go to a SoulCycle class in between ordering a slice of pizza and receiving it.

I like this restaurant a whole lot. The food three to five stars, but the atmosphere is perfect and the service is lovely. And their bar is excellent. Dined here NYE.  Whereas some restaurants are mob scenes and have limited menus on 12/31, they let you order à la carte at their normal prices.The restaurant is a lovely oasis on 9th Avenue - decorated in classic French bistro style.  Tables are well spaced, unlike in many Manhattan restaurants.I started with a KIR. It was perfect, the epitome of a good kir - plus it had a really delicious lemon peel, which elevated it.Appetizers:  Sweetie got French onion soup and liked it.  I got the TUNA TARTARE. I'm sorry to say that, though NY Yelpers have praised this dish, it was rather boring for me. It was certainly inoffensive. But tuna tartare is a super trite dish in San Diego, and I've had so many playful spins, with so many different oils and flavors. This was definitely fresh, but it was quite bland - just the tuna and avo, plus a few dabs of meh sauce on the plate.  Not what I expect at Marseille, and less good than at almost any place at home.Entrees:  On the advice of our excellent server (a charming man from Morocco whose name I don't recall), I got the trout with lemon sauce and capers. Perfect. Really delicious and a good portion.  Sweetie got the chicken and son got the steak - they were not as enthusiastic as me but they thought their dishes were fine.Wine: I got a perfect glass of Alsatian pinot blanc. Worked perfectly with the trout. Dessert:  I was a little disappointed here. Ordered PROFITEROLES, one of my favorite desserts in the world. The pastry part was too eggy and not really worth eating, though the vanilla ice cream and the chocolate sauce were fine. I wouldn't order this again, and it didn't cap the meal off well. My son enjoyed his strawberry sorbet and vanilla ice cream.Why am I still giving 5 stars if my first and last course were not so great? Dining is not just the courses but also the whole experience.  Service here is both warm and correct, atmosphere is fantastic, price is reasonable. I had some excellent alcohol which put me in a very good mood - and I had one superb dish and two that were fine.  This remains one of my go-to places when visiting NYC - a chic neighborhood place, close enough to Times Square and the Port Authority - but light years away from the craziness!

So I went with my friend after our classes and I reallllllly wanted to give it 5 stars but I'm gonna have to give an honest reviewI got the gnocchi carbonara and my first bite was heavenly. They placed the plate in front of me and I smelled it and almost couldn't take a picture. The sauce tasted amazing, and my friend got the same dish except she added mushrooms on top of it. The mushrooms honestly made it taste even better. My only problem with the gnocchi was that I couldn't tell if it was over or under cooked. I know gnocchi should be soft, and on my first bite it was like a pillow that melts in my mouth, but as I kept eating I realized that it was much mushier than it should've been.The fresh pasta and gnocchi options were amazing so I had to take off a star by the fact that they just couldn't cook it right. The sauce 110% though Also the bread we got beforehand! Omg amazing The service wasn't bad though, no complaints End it was a nice atmosphere for a small place
Decent pub located near bus station.  Bartenders were nice and happy hour specials were ok. The atmosphere is cozy but the menu seemed expensive to me even for the city.

Title: The Perfect Breakfast Stop

I often drop by this deli for their breakfast sandwiches and have always been impressed on multiple fronts. The cleanliness of the place sets a welcoming tone the moment you step in. The sandwiches here are consistently fresh, and they nail the details like adding a high-quality tomato that's never the usual mushy afterthought. The staff is amiable and efficient, ensuring I'm quickly out the door and on my way to work. This spot has easily become a regular part of my morning routine, and I'll definitely keep coming back.

I first stumbled upon this establishment a few weeks ago just walking to catch the express bus across town to the west side. The place looks unassuming from the outside but once you take a look inside it is beautifully decorated with quirky decor and gives you a feeling of being transported back to traditional, authentic restaurant in Mexico. However, that day I stumbled upon this restaurant I actually didn't dine there that day. I took a menu, left to take care of business all the while scanning their plethora of food choices. That and the fact that they have bottomless brunch on the weekends and Taco Tuesday specials on said day caught my attention and I just knew I'd return. My first dine-in experience happened this past Tuesday with my bestie before catching a movie. As soon as we walked in we were greeted by the friendly staff. It wasn't busy whatsoever so we just sat at the bar (faster service lol) plus the bartender was so polite and cute! We ordered $6 frozen strawberry margaritas, which were very tasty. We also ordered the $13 Taco Tuesday special that gives you a pick of any three tacos with a side of rice and beans. Not bad at all. The chicken and steak tacos I ordered were delicious, my favorite being the steak tacos. We were also given some fresh salsa and chips to go along with our meal. I highly recommend this place and I will return for their bottomless brunch.
Came here for restaurant week. The interior of the restaurant was very elegant and impressive. And also the foods were great. The drinks were little higher price than other bars

Title: A Perfect Evening at a USHG Gem

I recently dined at one of Danny Meyer's USHG restaurants for a long-overdue catch-up with a friend and it was a night to remember. As expected from a USHG venue, the experience was nothing short of excellent.

We started with the scallop appetizer which set a high bar with its delightful flavors and perfect sear. The mushroom pizza with stracciatella cheese that followed was equally impressive, beautifully marrying earthy tones with rich, creamy goodness. A must-try during their half-off pizza happy hour!

The standout of the night was the torta caprese dessert. This chocolate cake had a lusciously molten center and was paired with an herbaceous liqueur-flavored gelato that was simply sublime—the perfect birthday treat. And speaking of treats, the staff surprised us with an additional complimentary dessert to celebrate the occasion, a testament to USHG's exemplary service.

In summary, the meal was impeccable, the service exceptional, and the overall dining experience left us both thoroughly satisfied. Without a doubt, I will return to this establishment and would recommend it to anyone looking for an outstanding dining experience.

I went here on a splurge night with my friends.I wasn't sure what to expect because i'm not the biggest fan of sushi, and I'm not the biggest fan of Manhattan.We chose this place, to be blunt because a close friend of mine is a chef, so we all hung back and let him pick the place, and do all of the ordering.Let me be clear. Everything here was phenomenal. Starting with the customer service. The sommelier was extremely helpful in picking out sake for us, and even explaining the sake making process. She even answered lots of our questions about the nuances of its production.We ordered a ton of food, and all of it was delicious. What stands out to me is the grilled octopus, as well as the pork belly. The fried chicken was so good that we ordered another round of it too.I'll definitely be back the next time I want to show off my disposable income and my good taste. lol

Our office had catering from Hummus & Pita and it was delicious. Unfortunately, we had to wait for our meeting to end before getting to the food, so the falafel wasn't as crispy as it was intended, but it was still great! The baba ghanoush was great, and they had these purple olives!

I'm so surprised that this place has so many reviews when the one on the West side is SO MUCH BETTER. The Hells Kitchen location has a wider selection of alcoholic drinks, larger menu, and cheaper happy hour prices. If you look at the menu photo, Rice Dishes are underneath Appetizers, this mistakenly led me to believe that it was a sub-category and that those dishes would be subject to happy hour pricing. I was wrong. The chicken avo don was good and a large portion, however I felt like I was mis-led. At the other location, they serve small bowls of Salmon Avo don for $4 at happy hour. I would honestly recommend those who love this establishment to go check out the West side location. It's so much better in my opinion.

I stopped by this spot for a quick bite before the New Year's Eve festivities in Times Square and was thoroughly impressed with the efficiency of the service. I ordered the vegetable pad thai, which was delightful and reasonably priced at $11. The bustling atmosphere didn't compromise the quality or speed of the meal; I was in and out within 30 minutes. Definitely recommend for a fast and satisfying meal in a pinch!

DEFINITELY ASTORIA LOCATION IS BETTER!!!!It is very dangerous when you are expanding your business and opening extra branches. When you know the original store and the portion sizes, you will always compare the new ones to original one! And you cannot serve anything less what you were serving before, then you get a bad credit!! Whoever reads this they will understand it, if you tried the original one!Definitely a clean restaurant, you can judge it how the restrooms are clean. But be careful, the floor tiles are not chosen carefully, they are slippery when wet!Grilled octopus is a superb, cannot go wrong with that.Cold appetizer plate is ok, could be better. Could have gotten something else instead. I love tarama salata, but the way they prepared is not right. The way you make is whip the red caviars with oil, then add the lemon to whiten it. If it is still salty, add a touch of water.Salad could be better, don't like the steak tomatoes, would be better with plum or roma tomatoes.Saganaki came without the flame!!Love the fried whiting, but with the portion size of the lemon potatoes, i got robbed.Overall ok, won't be back to this location, going back to Astoria.

I have known about this place for a while, never really had the urge to visit.  Silly me.So yes, now I am a fan.  Not only are the servings huge and sharable, they flavors burst out just as expected by the visual presentation.  I haven't had to bag up food in a while.My friend and I had wings (honey sirracha and bbq), chicken quesadillas, and nachos.  I cannot choose a favorite.  The drinks were also noteworthy, as they were ample.  Didn't have to order a second.We also had an attentive host/waiter or whatever they are called these days.  A nice touch when these days the waiters only show up when you need to order or if your glass is empty.It was a bit loud, but what else can be expected on a Saturday afternoon.  The mood was electric - a football game was on but no-one seemed to be too interested.  Just the patrons themselves were all having a good time - what else can be expected when you are enjoying good food and good service on a Saturday afternoon.Cheers Brazen Fox!  I will be back!

Came mid-afternoon for a quick bite.The staff were cleaning up so it was confusing if we could order...but in the end someone came to the counter. The food is decent and well made. We got the Sophia blue sandwich without the blue cheese dressing but it was a yummy combination! The inclusion of green peas actually meshed well with the sandwich. The hamburger was also really tasty which you can get tater tots, onion rings or rosemary fries (sounded pretty interesting) extra charge along with your meal. It has a lot of options, nice clean bathroom, and plenty of seating area to eat.

I've been to this place 2 times, primarily for the giant cannoli that you can smash with a small wooden hammer. I recommend making a reservation in advance. The ambiance is very nice, with outdoor seating when it is nicer out. The Meatballs ($13) are good, but nothing special and I wish they gave you more bread with this appetizer. I did enjoy the Pistachio Pesto ($22), if you love pesto the pistachio adds a nice nutty flavor and texture to the dish. I've had the Inferno Pizza ($23), and would not recommend the pizzas. They get soggy in the middle and have little flavor even though there were so many toppings on it. The Brown Butter Gnocchi ($25) took a couple of bites to decide if I liked it or not. It has an acquired taste, so you will either love it or hate it. The Cannoli is massive and can easily feed 4-8 people for dessert. I believe they change the flavor of the canopy every couple of months. The cannoli itself tastewise is okay; it is not the best cannoli you will have, but it is a fun experience. Overall, I recommend sticking with ordering the pasta or from the grill. If you are here with some friends or a loved one, then the cannoli is an excellent option for dessert.

This place is a really small shop that will always have a line, but it's worth it! The meat was super tender and juicy. I went there multiple times and they can sometimes get inconsistent, but still good regardless. I definitely recommend the crispy and roasted pork. They don't have any seating, but there is a park across the street that's perfect for eating this bowl!

Title: Authentic Gopchang Experience with a Rough Start

I ventured to this restaurant with high expectations for a nostalgic taste of Korea's famed grilled intestines. However, an unwelcoming start with the hostess insisting I wait outside marred the initial impression. Despite this hiccup, once seated, anticipation grew for the gopchang set.

Patience is key here, as the electric grilling plates mean a longer wait for your meal compared to traditional gas stoves, but the result is worth it. The intestines arrived perfectly prepared, devoid of any off-putting odor, a testament to the kitchen's expertise.

We also indulged in the Korean fried rice, a harmony of egg, seaweed, and roe eggs—a solid follow-up to the gopchang.

Take note: payment options are limited; MasterCard holders are in the clear.

The dining experience, solely from the perspective of food, was redemptive and satisfying for any intestine enthusiast. Still, an upgrade in waiting area arrangements could vastly improve first impressions and add a touch of professionalism. Worth a visit for your gopchang cravings, but a note to management: hospitality matters from the moment a patron arrives.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise on a Friday Night

Rating: 4/5

My friends and I had a satisfying experience at this restaurant on a recent Friday night. To our delight, we were seated immediately around 8 PM, which is quite a feat given the usual dinner rush.

We all decided on the chicken paillard paired with salads and shared a side of fries. The chicken was pounded to a very thin cutlet, which I found to be just the right portion size, though one of my friends remarked that it left her wanting a bit more.

The salad was fairly standard, and while I requested the dressing on the side, it came already mixed in. Despite this, it was still enjoyable. The standout of the meal could very well have been the fries - perfectly crispy and served with a delicious aioli sauce.

The service was commendable with attentive and timely assistance throughout our meal. One minor downside was the absence of Angry Orchard cider, but that's a small blip in an otherwise pleasant dining experience.

All things considered, I would recommend this restaurant for anyone in the area looking for a reliably good meal and efficient service.

Came here for lunch with Boo Boo and mi Ma. This place changed owners. There's a noticeable face lift after Yee Li left. There's new floor, new tables, and the fish are in clear water.We shared the soy sauce chicken, roasted duck, Buddha delight casserole, land casserole, roasted pork and Chinese broccoli.I was disappointed they don't serve congee. Almost every time I'm at Ctown I get congee with black fermented egg and I ask that it's topped with ginger oil that is served with the soy sauce chicken. I also brought home the BBQ pork for my work meal prep. That was tasty too. Overall, the cooked dishes needed more seasoning. It's more for the older generation's palate like my mom's. But, the BBQ items like the roast pork, soy sauce chicken and duck were great fresh.

I came here for lunch on a weekday and got the lunch special for 9.99. I was seated right away as I was by myself but immediately after me, a line built up for lunch at around 12:30. The menu is straightforward, with the majority being curry options (curry rice, noodles, etc) and some donburi options. Since it was my first time, I chose the most basic lunch special curry. When my food came, I was surprised by the huge portion of curry rice with a big pork cutlet on top along with a side of pickles and miso soup. The food was piping hot, both in temperature and spice. I chose the extra hot (the second spiciest option) and it had a significant kick to it. I am confident in my spice tolerance and it was definitely at the upper limit of what I can eat without suffering. If you want a real challenge (and pain) definitely try their hottest option. The curry itself is very flavorful and I love the crunchy garlic slices on top. The pork cutlet is very crispy, tender and juicy, a perfect compliment to the curry.The total came out to around $13 with tax and tip, which is pretty reasonable for the amount of food I get. Overall very satisfied with my meal here and will definitely come back!

Title: A Gastronomic Delight Despite the Din

After much anticipation, I finally dined at the local hotspot that had been on my must-visit list. Admittedly, the interior's volume was a notch too high for easy conversation, but what the ambiance lacked in tranquility, the staff made up for with their impeccable service.

The culinary experience was nothing short of phenomenal. Although I arrived with a craving for seared foie gras, the restaurant's foie gras mousse was a delectable surprise, masterfully changing my usual indifference towards the dish. The escargot was a revelation, easily claiming the title of 'best ever', bathed in a perfect symphony of garlic butter and parsley.

Their onion soup was a comfort in a bowl, generously laden with gooey, melted cheese. The starters were so satisfying that our main courses faced an unfair battleground – our appetites were well and truly sated by the appetizers' triumph.

Overall, this bustling eatery is worth a visit for anyone looking for a dynamic dining experience paired with exceptional food.

Two of us dropped in here on a late Tuesday afternoon ahead of flying home.  Lots of choices on the famed NYC Little Italy Mulberry Street, so likely can't go wrong if the place is open.  You drop down some steps to Aunt Jake's, unlike many of the other Mulberry places that are European style with table lining the sidewalks and some proprietors streetside marketing their offerings. There were maybe two or three other tables occupied when we went in, and a few others filled in while we were there. They bring you some nice soft breadsticks to start.  We ordered meatballs to start - 3 nice sized ones come to an order, listed on their appetizer list.  Spaghetti carbonara and ravioli in a short rib and Italian sausage sauce followed.  You can pick your own pasta and pair it with a variety of sauces.  I believe all pasta is handmade - not sure if it's to order, but I will say that our main order took quite some time.  We were not in a hurry, but hopefully the pacing was not typical for our visit - otherwise count on being patient.  But it's worth it, as the carbonara was creamy, salty, and just right.  I am generally not a fan of carbonara with heavy cream, but Aunt Jake's was spot on.  The ravioli was absolutely delicious - the best dish of the two.  The pasta had a bit of a bite to it, and the meat sauce with short rib and Italian sausage was incredible. The server was very polite and friendly, but again, make some time, but it is well worth it for homemade pasta and patiently curated sauces. We were too full to try dessert, but I can only imagine it must be good to be on the menu.  Grab a handful of jolly ranchers on the way out!

Title: A Fast Food Haven for Gluten and Dairy-Free Diners

Review:

I recently visited a fast food gem that blew me away with its incredibly inclusive menu. As someone with gluten and dairy restrictions, finding a satisfying burger can be a tall order, but this place changed the game. They offer gluten-free bread for their tasty melts, and the vegan cheese options mean I don't have to miss out on the full, cheesy experience. But the biggest surprise? Gluten-free tater tots! They were crispy, perfectly seasoned, and absolutely divine. It's not often that fast food restaurants cater so well to dietary needs, but this spot nails it. If you're in search of delicious, guilt-free comfort food, look no further. This is fast food done right for everyone.

My sister and I were able to add ourselves to the waiting list through the app, which was great because we were able to be seated almost immediately. It was PACKED on a Tuesday night, so I'd suggest checking in online regardless of whether it's a weekday or weekend. The restaurant was very loud inside, but decorated nicely and the staff was friendly as well. We ordered steamed pork dumplings to start that were flavorful and the perfect texture (also the sauce was delicious). We also decided on the bulgogi hot stone bowl and the chicken hot stone bowl. Both tasted great! The meat was tender and full of flavor and went so well with the rest of the veggies that come in the bowl. We ended our meal with some cheesecake for dessert. It was a bit more savory than I am typically used to, but it went perfectly with the fruit and ice cream that it is served with! I would definitely come back.

I had a month-long hankering for avocado toast so when a new Aussie cafe opened up in the neighborhood I had to come try it out.  My husband got the chicken sandwich and OJ. The OJ came in a tall thin glass with ice, making it pretty diluted for $6 that seems waaack. Fries were super similar to McDonald's which was exciting, but the sandwich was pretty bland in terms of seasoning -- maybe ordering an unhealthy option at a healthy-ish restaurant is not the way to go? idkI had ordered an egg (+$3) to come with my avocado toast, as did the girl at the table next to ours. Mine arrived without said egg so I asked for the egg to be added and received a side egg, hers showed up with two poached eggs on top :( y u no indulge my egg love sonnyboy, wouldn't come back.

Title: "Joe's: A Slice of Perfection for the On-the-Go Pizza Lover"

If you're a fan of impeccably thin-crust pizza and don't mind a no-seats, authentic grab-and-go vibe, then Joe's is your go-to spot. This long-standing "hole in the wall" has mastered the art of the perfect pizza with an ideal balance of cheese, sauce, and a delightful crust that crunches just right. Perfect for the late-night crowd, Joe's keeps the ovens hot until 4:30 am, making it the quintessential stop for your post-midnight cravings. In summary, Joe's delivers outstanding pizza that's stood the test of time for good reason—it's simply the bomb.

This was my first pizza experience in new York City and I'm very happy with it! Crust was delicious, not overbaked. Pepperoni were delicious little bowls of grease. Highlight was pesta on pizza. Never had that before and enjoyed it immensely! I wonder why they don't add chicken to it.

My go-to dessert spot never disappoints—especially with their "famous" concoction of strawberries, bananas, Nutella, whipped cream, and vanilla ice cream. It's been a consistent highlight through the years, perfectly satisfying my sweet tooth every time.

Title: A Delightful Brunch at The Mermaid Inn – A Family Favorite

Review:

The Mermaid Inn holds a special place in my heart as one of my top restaurant choices in NYC. Much to my delight, the new location in the East Village has lived up to my high expectations—spacious enough even for those of us dining with little ones in tow. The service was nothing short of wonderful, attentive without being intrusive, ensuring we had a delightful experience.

Our brunch visit was a culinary delight. The Po Boy was packed with flavor, a true Southern treat that left me savoring each bite. The salmon benedict, on the other hand, was a perfect balance of rich hollandaise and delicate salmon, poached to perfection. Both dishes were, without a doubt, palate-pleasers.

In conclusion, The Mermaid Inn continues to impress with its combination of mouthwatering cuisine, warm service, and a family-friendly atmosphere. It's the sort of place that always leaves me wondering, "What more could I ask for?" Truly an exceptional dining experience.

Title: Cozy Corner Delight with a Side of Mix-up

My experience at the quaint Corner Thai restaurant, nestled at the intersection of 1st Ave and 14th Street, was a calm one, given the quiet ambiance on a holiday Sunday. Opting for a central table to escape the chilly entrance, we were welcomed by a solitary but attentive server.

The menu boasted daily specials, a feature that sparked joy in the dine-out routine. Appetizers commenced with curry puffs that lived up to their savory reputation – a satisfying start. The deal sweetener was the addition of two spring rolls for a mere dollar and a Thai salad for two, which translated into value.

Entrees unfolded with a slight hiccup; both my boyfriend's basil beef over an upcharged brown rice bed and my selected Pad Thai came with an unrequested chicken cameo. The oversight was peculiar given the sparse crowd. After a polite insistence for what we ordered, the server impressively righted the error in five minutes flat, delivering the wok hei-kissed dishes we craved.

Despite the mix-up, the willingness to swiftly correct the order left a positive impression. Should my travels bring me back to this neighborhood, a return to Corner Thai wouldn't be off the table.

Title: A Sensational Start in the Quest for NYC's Best Burger

In the bustling quest for New York City's premier burger, my journey began at a spot that has set the bar high. From the first bite, it was clear that this burger was a contender. Expertly seasoned, it enhanced the flavors of the melty cheese without dominating the palate, ensuring each mouthful was a delight.

The accompaniment of thin, crispy fries was generous to a fault—a bountiful bowl that complemented the star of the show perfectly. And let's talk value: the Sunday burger special at $10 is a steal compared to the usual $14, with the equally indulgent fries just a $4 add-on. This deal undoubtedly stands out as one of NYC's finest.

To top off the meal, the "Mango Mango" cocktail, a blend of smoky tequila and sweet mango, hit all the right notes, creating a beautifully balanced finish to a meal that will be hard to surpass. If this is only the beginning, I eagerly anticipate what's next in NYC's burger odyssey.

I recently dined at a pretty decent restaurant where the prices struck me as fair. Although the soup dumplings were underwhelming, the spicy salmon roll and eel sushi did not disappoint, both delivering on flavor. Service leaned towards the slower side; however, it appeared they were simply understaffed that evening, which could easily account for the delay. A minor letdown was the limited cocktail menu, especially since a tantalizing raspberry gin concoction was no longer available. Overall, while there's room for improvement, the high points of the meal suggest it's worth giving this place a try.

Title: A Haven for Introverts and Ramen Lovers Alike

From the moment I stepped in and found myself in a private booth, I knew this was a place where my introverted self could revel in solitude with my meal. The intimacy of dining alone with my ramen was an exceptional experience.

I opted for the Recommended Set at $24 without any customization. The ramen that arrived was the best I've ever savored—each slurp was packed with flavor and masterfully prepared. Although next time, I'll be asking for less salt and spice, as it was just a tad overpowering for my taste.

The highlight was the free noodle refill promotion, doubling the joy of my meal without doubling the cost. Generosity seems to be a cornerstone here, and it truly enhances the dining experience.

The presentation was slightly unexpected, with toppings served on the side rather than atop the noodles as commonly seen in photos. Nevertheless, this allowed for a more personalized touch as I could add them to my liking.

Customer service was the icing on the cake—attentive, welcoming, and consistent from start to finish. It's no surprise that this establishment has carved out a spot on my list of favorite go-to eateries.

Title: The Ultimate Burger Haven in NYC - Paul's Triumphs!

I finally discovered the holy grail of burgers right here in the heart of the Big Apple at Paul's! This isn't just a meal; it's a true New York experience wrapped in attitude and the comforting chaos of the city. The ambiance is as authentic as it gets with every sight, smell, and sound sharpening your appetite for the star of the show - the burger.

With a waitress who seems to have mastered the art of mind-reading, placing your order feels like a rite of passage. What you're here for is evident: a heavenly half-pound beef patty with a perfect 80/20 mix, luxuriously cloaked in American cheese, hugged by a flawlessly soft bun, and adorned with crisp applewood smoked bacon. Raw onions add a punch on request, while lettuce and tomato offer a fresh crunch.

Sides aren't an afterthought; the robust cut steak fries demand your attention, especially when dipped in mayo or mustard. Wash it all down with a fountain drink, and you're set for a feast that surprisingly doesn't break the bank - all under $20.

I can say with no hesitation—I FOUND IT!!! Paul's delivers the best burger in NYC. Period.

Was going to try this place the day after its soft opening but everything was sold out by 8pm (restaurant opens from 12pm to 9pm). Decided to try my luck again around 3pm today. Saw a line outside and was told it would be a 20 mins wait for two people. Turned out it was only 5 mins! Definitely go with a small party so you would be seated more quickly.Heard this Chang Fen chain was first opened in 1958 and now has over 50 stores in mainland China (mainly in Guangzhou). Apparently there are some in Toronto and Markham and this is the first flagship in NYC (thanks for opening it in Chinatown rather than Flushing or Brooklyn!). LOVED the congee more than its signature items which were the Chang Fen. We tried the Lai Wan style assorted congee （艇仔粥）and the sliced pork, liver and kidney congee (及弟粥). Both were decent with lots of ingredients and good portion to share. The latter was our favorite. We found the chang fen were okay and rather pricey (more expensive than the congee) except the dough stick rice noodle roll which was great! The dough was crispy. Glad there were also appetizers. The curry fish balls and sticky rice wrap were tasty. The HK style milk tea just brought back all my fond childhood memories. Would definitely go back to try other types of congee and appetizers. Heard the deep fried fish skin was good but it was sold out when we were there.

I normally HATE duck - until I stumbled across this place! It's a hole in the wall Chinese spot that specializes in pork and duck and is cash only. I got the small order of duck, which comes with rice and veggies. Hands down the best duck I've had in a while. Don't be fooled by the outside/NYC hole charm - this place is amazing!

Title: A Solid, if Pricey, Dining Experience

Last night, I dined at a restaurant that presented a mixed bag of impressions. The highlights include a decently cooked selection of dishes, spanning from a ribeye hotpot and tender chicken breast to fresh mixed veggies and succulent baby cuttlefish. Accompanied by a hearty pork bone broth and a side of beef skewers, my meal was satisfying, with the skewers deserving a special mention for their juiciness.

However, the experience did come with a heftier price tag, totaling around $57, which may give one pause. While the food was generally fresh, the lack of a substantial sauce bar—limited to just six powders and two sauces—was felt, somewhat diminishing the flavors that could have been elevated with more condiment options. Additionally, the broth, though comforting, was underwhelming in its seasoning, leaving something to be desired in terms of depth.

Despite the shortcomings, there is enough merit to warrant a return visit. Next time, I'll be exploring a different broth, hopefully, one that packs more punch. This spot seems fitting for those occasions when I'm looking to indulge a bit outside the everyday fare.

Title: A Humble Feast at Nam Son Vietnamese Restaurant

My long-awaited visit to Nam Son Vietnamese Restaurant in Chinatown finally materialized. Nestled on Grand Street between Chrystie and Bowery, Nam Son stands out in an area dominated by Chinese eateries, providing a welcomed Vietnamese culinary oasis.

The restaurant's interior mirrors the familiar layout found in its Baxter Street counterparts—a no-frills, elongated dining space conveniently divided and lined with robust columns of tables. My palate embarked on a journey with the steamed rice crepe with round pork ($9) and a quartet of spring rolls ($6).

The rice crepes, snug beneath a blanket of shredded cucumbers and veggies, were modestly filled with pork and mushrooms. Despite their thickness, they called desperately for the accompanying Vietnamese sauce—a less salty version than what I've encountered elsewhere—to enrich their rather bland existence. Fortunately, an arsenal of tableside condiments stood by to elevate the experience. Accompanied by Vietnamese pork patty slices, the dish didn't dazzle, but it did its job in satisfying my hunger.

The spring rolls, however, were the stars—perfectly sized, each one delicately wrapped, teeming with freshness, and harmonized with mint, lettuce, and that milder Vietnamese sauce.

Prompt and efficient service was the cherry on top of my visit. While the steamed rice crepe didn't steal my heart, the mouthwatering spring rolls and the observed popularity of pho among other diners have piqued my curiosity. Nam Son has secured my return visit; the pho awaits.

Title: A Gastronomic Journey at Urbanspace Pop-Up

If you're a culinary adventurer, the latest pop-up at Urbanspace is a Yelp reviewer's dream come true! This bustling food haven offers an impressive array of vendors that will satisfy your every craving from dawn till dusk.

I indulged my sweet tooth at Ovenly and Mah-Ze-Dahr Bakery, each offering sublime baked goods that were a sheer delight. The savory side of things did not disappoint with Pierogi Boys delivering comfort in every bite and Good Stock serving up rich, soul-warming soups.

Casa Toscana's authentic Italian fare was a highlight, transporting me to the streets of Tuscany, while Mayhem Smokehouse's barbecue had me licking my fingers clean. The Stackery's unique twist on the classic sandwich, along with the elegant sips of Champagne Bollinger ensured a well-rounded experience.

For the snack enthusiasts, Duck Season's offerings were top-notch, and Squish S'mores Bar's gooey creations are not to be missed. Healthy eats were well-represented by Two Tablespoon's fresh and flavorful dishes.

The atmosphere was further enhanced by The Lodge Biergarten By Stout and The Lodge Bar, perfect spots to unwind after a busy day of culinary exploration.

This pop-up is open from 8AM to 10PM and sadly bids farewell on March 1st, 2020. Don't miss the chance to savor this diverse food experience – it's an absolute must-visit for foodies!

Girlfriend and I decided to try the new Hudson Yards yesterday and were not disappointed.  To start, it's on 5th floor with the perfect view of the vessel right outside the window.  We tried to get s window seat but would've had to wait longer so we settled for a seat a little further away.  Not a big deal, they have an outdoor patio you can go outside to take pictures afterward anyway.  The atmosphere and decoration were clean, bright, and modern and the food was delicious.  We had the $32 price fix menu which was a real bargain.  They have a ton of staff but could probably be a tiny bit more organized.  Regardless, a very pleasurable afternoon experience with an amazing view!

Tucked away in the bustling Financial District, this lunch destination is a treasure for those seeking a hearty yet wholesome meal. For a reasonable $13 (tax included), you can indulge in a monstrous poke bowl that promises to satisfy even the most ravenous appetites. The regular-sized bowl has never failed to leave me feeling full.

Generosity seems to be a cornerstone of this establishment—each bowl brims with a plethora of add-ons and sides, ensuring a personalized and flavorful experience with every visit. The visual feast of my loaded poke bowl (see attached picture) speaks volumes of the establishment's commitment to providing value.

Having patronized this spot on several occasions, consistency is another of their strong suits; they never cut corners on quality, particularly with their tuna, which I recommend choosing over chicken for a richer taste. This spot has earned my repeat visits, and it's clear that when it comes to delivering a filling, non-greasy meal in FiDi, they've got the recipe down pat.

Title: A Decade of Delicious Jia Jang Myun

Having frequented this gem for over ten years, I can confidently declare it the ultimate destination for late-night cravings of jia jang myun. The noodles here boast a satisfying chewiness, perfectly paired with the rich, meaty black bean sauce laden with onions. Their half jia jang myun and half seafood soup combo is not only a scrumptious bargain but a testament to the variety they offer. While my adventures through the menu have included items like the General Tso's chicken, I've yet to be disappointed. It’s heartening to witness the bustling atmosphere remain unchanged through the years. This spot remains a top pick for its consistently delightful fare.

Excellent kitchy, whimisical, retro 80s speakeasy that that only be pulled off in a Japanese neighborhood bar! The yakitori is top notch as well as the drinks! I really felt like I was in Japan again but with American salary men having drinks and skewers after a long week.I suggest the beef tongue, pork belly, gizzard and skirt steak skewers!

Ordered the recommended set and it was good.  They also had a promotion going on for a free refill so that was a plus as well.  Also ordered the marinated pork and it had good flavors.  Would prefer it over regular cha siu.  Staff was nice and it wasn't busy so no wait.  Overall a good experience and would consider going back.

Found this spot when I was craving for some Thai and didn't want to go that far in the neighborhood. Gave it a try during their lunch special. The flavors are spot on! And the lunch deals are affordable! I like it so much I'll come even if it's not for lunch. Staff is super friendly and I'm pretty sure they'll start to recognize me soon. It's a little hidden behind the pizza place on the corner. Kinda like a hole in the wall. I hope I'm supporting a small business - it seems like it. Even better if it is... I like to support small businesses. Hopefully I'll get to know the staff and owners more.Go Tos: Drunken noodles: good flavor Spicy fried rice: not that spicy; veggies are not soggy either Papaya salad: they use legit fish sauce !! My friend had one ofWill try more on the menu ;)They close for a little in the afternoon - check the times !

The food was really mediocre and not worth the price you pay. From the appetizer to the soup to the fish entree we ordered, none was satisfactory, since every dish was too saucy/rich in flavor(this might not be the correct description but the idea is that it's not done right) that our tastebuds became fed up with it after two bites. Just look at the attached photo and you will know what I mean. Simply too much sauce. The fish tasted just like tomato sauce. Period. This restaurant is marked as middle eastern but its menu does not really feature many typical middle eastern dishes. I think this is westernized seafood with a bit of middle eastern twist, the result of which is just not spectacular. Although the service and ambiance were good, I would not return for the subpar food.

Title: A Stellar Dining Experience That Hits the Spot

I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant and was blown away by the exceptional service and delightful food.
