Even with a last-minute reservation for six at peak dinner time, the staff was incredibly accommodating, ensuring we were seated promptly at 7 pm. The communication was top-notch as well, with text updates being a lifesaver for anyone with spotty cell service.

The menu offered some tempting appetizers, though the alternative version of the summer roll I tried fell a tad short on flavor compared to the classic. However, the main course more than made up for it. While the rest of my party enjoyed the pho, I ventured into the Bun Bo Hue. It was the perfect level of spicy, providing heat without discomfort. The noodles were cooked to perfection, the broth was free of oiliness, and there was a generous serving of toppings and beef.

Admittedly, prices are a bit steeper than what you'd find in a typical Vietnamese eatery, but the quality of the food and the serene atmosphere make it worth it. It's a refreshing change from the norm, though for those seeking the most authentic pho experience, you might find yourself in Chinatown despite the service trade-off. This restaurant, however, has mastered the balance between authenticity and a touch of Western influence. An easy 5/5 for the overall experience. Would I return? Absolutely.

Title: A True Gem for Pasta Lovers

As an avid foodie with over 500 reviews under my belt, I don't give out my highest rating lightly—yet this Italian haven claims 2 of my coveted 10/10 pandapoints. Visiting New York without indulging in their culinary craft would be unthinkable for me. Whether I'm flying solo or orchestrating a feast for friends, their doors—and menus—are open to all, with prices that won't break the bank.

What sets this eatery apart is the passion that pours into every plate. Managed by a delightful couple, their commitment to quality shines through the sumptuous, al dente strands of their freshly made pasta. The Spaghetti al Pomodoro is a revelation, and I urge you to savor the evening specials—they never disappoint.

But let's talk dolce. Their tiramisu is a masterclass in dessert perfection and a must for any visit. Mark my words, one taste and you'll be counting the days until you can return. A resounding 10/10, this spot is unmissable for anyone in search of authentic Italian bliss.

Fun atmosphere! Noisy, live music and usually pretty crowded! The servers are wearing traditional dirndls and lederhosen and are all very friendly. We ordered the pretzel which is a good size and the weinerschnitzel. It definitely doesn't compare to the food in Munich but still worth a try!

Title: Middle-of-the-Road Ramen in the Lower East Side

I ventured into Ivan Ramen with high expectations, spurred by the captivating backstory featured on Chef's Table. Unfortunately, the experience failed to match the culinary narrative. Starting with the appetizers, the pork buns were unremarkable, overshadowed by superior offerings from other local establishments. The Japanese fried chicken was a highlight, tender and paired well with an inventive shiso ranch dressing.

Moving on to the main event, the vegetarian ramen delivered comfort but fell short of the exemplary standard set by its backstory. The overly soy-heavy broth undermined the otherwise standard assembly of tofu, enoki mushrooms, and tomato. While the cozy satisfaction that comes with a bowl of ramen was present, the dish lacked that exceptional flair I had hoped for.

On a positive note, the restaurant’s ambiance does offer a bit of novelty with a Doraemon figurine playfully adorning the wall, providing a charming backdrop to the dining experience. In summary, Ivan Ramen is a decent choice for a casual meal, but don't expect to be blown away as the Chef's Table episode might suggest.

Title: A Taste of Thailand with a Side of Patience

If you're in the mood for some authentic Thai cuisine in the heart of NYC, look no further. This gem of a restaurant serves up fresh, flavorful dishes that will satisfy your cravings. The prices are in line with standard NYC fare, but don't miss out on the all-day happy hour—the deals are truly a steal. A personal highlight for me was the Lychee Martini, a perfect blend of sweet and strong. The Drunken Noodles also deserve a special mention, tantalizing your taste buds with each bite.

Be prepared for a bit of a wait as the evening wears on, an expected side effect of popularity. One area ripe for improvement is service; it can be a challenge to flag down a waiter when things get busy, which is often in this cozy space. Grabbing the check or asking for extras may test your patience. Despite this hiccup, I keep coming back for the exceptional food and drinks—the flavors are just too good to pass up.

The food is amazing!! The atmosphere is very welcoming. The staff were extremely friendly. We went on a Monday night and was able to have a table. It recently opened so its BYOB for now until they get their liquor license. It will soon open up for brunch. For now, it is open from 6pm-10pm.Chef Jose did come to our table and check how the food was. One of the partners Miguel also checked on us and explained the shaved ice dessert and the chicha morada juice on it as well as the drink. He gave us the drinks to try. Those were amazingly delicious. Seems like a very healthy guiltless dessert. I'm surprised all the sweetness is from the purple corn.This was our first time at any of the Mission Ceviche locations. It was pleasant and makes me curious about the other casual locations as well. Will definitely be coming back and also be bringing friends for a nice sit-down dinner.At first look of the menu, we wanted to order everything, but we narrowed it down to one from each of the 4 categories. The classic catch of the day pollock Ceviche, Octopus Causas, jumbo shrimp skewer and the arroz con mariscos. All were very delicious

I had a mixed experience at the restaurant. On my first visit, I absolutely loved their Yam Fries, which left a lasting impression. However, during a second visit, the Yam Fries failed to live up to the memory—quite a disappointment. As for the dessert, the Pumpkin Cake was satisfactory.

Title: Bustling Spot with Tasty Eats

I decided to drop by this eatery for a Tuesday lunch and was immediately struck by the lively atmosphere – the place was teeming with diners! Despite the crowd, the noise level remained manageable, though seating was a snug affair. Service was commendable; fast to greet, albeit initially rushed, the staff returned quickly for our order after we perused the menu. 

Our refreshingly minty drinks were followed promptly by the main event. The meal was a pleasure to the palate, featuring decently-sized portions, though I wouldn't have minded a little more. The accompanying pita bread was a delightful complement to the hummus and tahini, but an extra piece wouldn't have gone amiss for savoring every last bit.

In conclusion, this establishment earns a solid four stars. It's not quite perfection, but for good food in a decent spot, it's definitely worth a visit.

I've never been so excited to give a review!! This was mind blowing good, authentic, and CHEAP. Two people shared one portion of the 三宝饭 ($7) which included duck , chicken, pork, rice and Napa cabbage, and we were both full. Cash only, super fast service. This place deserves so much more hype!!!

I've been to a couple of Thai places in the city and I've even traveled to Thailand for a month so I have a good sense of what good Thai food is like. This place took me by surprise the moment I walked in. Immediately I felt like I was taken back to the summer I spent in Thailand. They absolutely nailed the ambience and interior. I really appreciate that Thai music is being played sometimes as well even though they do play American music most of the time. It definitely makes the experience feel much more authentic.Now comes the food. I came in with a certain expectation of how the food should taste and since this is a Thai restaurant in America, I set the bar a little lower by default but man was I blown away. Not only were the flavors of the curry and pad kee mow true to its origins, but it was on par or even better than some of the places I've been to in Thailand. The serving sizes were amazing at the given price point and the lunch special is an even better deal. Definitely the best Thai restaurant for quality, experience, and price point. An easy 5 stars from me.Phil's 5-scaleAmbience/Setting - 1/1Food - 3/3Service - 1/1

Title: A Slice Above the Rest at Bleecker Street Pizza

After ducking into Bleecker Street Pizza for a quick bite, I’m pleased to say that it stands out in the bustling NYC pizza scene. We opted for a classic Pepperoni and a tropical Hawaiian – both served by the slice, perfect for a casual dine-and-dash compared to the table-service wait at nearby John’s.

Yelp check-ins are rewarded with a complimentary fountain drink, which paired nicely with our meal – there’s something about a cold Coke with pizza that just feels right. The quality of the ingredients shone through; the cheese was plentiful and the crust hit that ideal balance of crunch and foldability without the charred bitterness you sometimes find elsewhere. With ample seating and well-executed classic NY-style pizza, Bleecker Street Pizza secured its spot as a highlight on my NYC pizza tour.

We stopped in here for the first time today just walking by. We were greeted immediately. Great and fast service!! We ordered an iced latte with almond milk. $11. A little pricey for a small coffee but the coffee is delicious and has great flavor. The roast of the beans is perfect. It was creamy and blended great. No bitterness. Worth it! Will be back to try the yummy donuts they offered! To be continued....

This review is for restaurant week dinner! Do order their Martinez cocktail ($21). It is pretty strong and stiff cocktail. Beautifully done.Started with smoked salmon that comes with a horse radish-y sort of a thing. Paired well with the salmon. Comes with two thin slices of rye bread.Speaking of bread, they give you warm, toasted bread on the house I ordered the lamb Bolognese. The portion was between appetizer and main course I would say. There was hardly any lamb. The sauce was quite good. I'm a tad disappointed with this as a main course. We also ordered the coq au vin which was so good. Tender braised chicken thigh and mushrooms in the wine based saucy base. There was bacon bits too. It was very nicely done.I ordered the chocolate Cake that was so moist and light. Comes with a small scoop of vanilla icecream. Very nicely done. Small dessert size :)The strawberry sundae was good too. It comes with a biscuit of sorts which was soggy however from the ice cream. Will I come back? Yes. It is a jacket required place and although I screwed up and forgot to tell my friend about it they gave him a spare instead of giving us a hard time. Pleasantly surprised for a place of this kind.The decor is fun. Service is great. Everyone seems to be here from a long time which also speaks volumes about the establishments. Next time I am here will be sure to dress up though ;)

This place has a lot of want to, but in the end seems just old and tired. Even the sushi chefs behind the counter - dressed up and lots of decor, but looking tired, with plastic wrap boxes in front of the view. Poor lighting also makes it a poor atmosphere. Friendly and helpful service, but it could not make up for the atmosphere and so so food. I had a below average shrimp tempura appetizer and Japanese style steak (promised as the best steak I've ever had). It was obvious the fryer oil needed to be changed, and the shrimp also came out somewhat soggy. Not the best start. Coming from Austin, the Japanese steak looked similar to (almost identical in appearance to) beef fajitas - right down to the accompanying onions and peppers! It was not, however, beef fajitas, although that might have been better than what I got. There was a distinct lack of flavor that without a doubt put it squarely off the list of best steaks I've ever had. Too bad. This was really close to my hotel (AC Hotel). I should have heeded the average reviews on Yelp. Next time for Japanese I'll try something else.
Best tacos ever!! Hands down, I love these tacos. The corn tortilla is made on site, and it's nice and fluffy! The meat is well seasoned and tender

This steakhouse serves pretty good steak, but for the price, you could find a better value elsewhere. That said, their sides and appetizers were surprisingly tasty and the ambience (especially on the second floor) was elegant. The service was okay, but I feel there was some bias having come for the restaurant week three-course meal; our table didn't receive nearly as friendly and attentive service as the table next to ours. Also, they took our food away when we were clearly still working on it.Club A Bacon: I had a taste of this, and it was really delicious. I was concerned about the size so I didn't order it for myself, but it was actually a substantial piece of bacon. I thought there wasn't as much fat on the slice, which is great considering common store-bought bacon is quite fatty. A very savory appetizer. I would probably order it if I returned. Steak Tartare and Fries: The steak was pretty tasty, with a strong mustard flavor throughout. It had an egg yolk on top, which  primarily made the texture thicker. However, I don't think the yolk added anything to the dish. I like that the fries were most akin to chips, cutting the tart steak nicely. Filet Mignon: While it was a fine steak, there was not much to it. After reading a lot of the reviews stating the steaks came out more well done than ordered, I ordered mine medium-rare, and was surprised to get it actually medium-rare. Nonetheless, it was a pretty good hunk of meat. That said, I would never order it at full price. Mac and Cheese: A pleasant side to go with my steak, I really enjoyed this. It was very cheesy with a crusty cheese topping. Cheesecake: I thought this was pretty good. Personally, I like my cheesecake more crumbly in texture. The texture here was more akin to a very thick gelatin. The flavor was very good and i liked the crust. It was different than usual, seeming to be made of oats rather than graham cracker. Price: 2/5Quality: 4/5Quantity: 4/5Service: 2/5Atmosphere: 5/5

I recently visited a local eatery for an early Friday evening meal and was pleasantly surprised by the experience. I arrived around 5pm to find the place nearly empty, save for another patron awaiting her order. 

My choice for the evening was the bul-go-gi kimbap, a decision I didn't regret. While I was initially disappointed by the lack of sauce variety, expecting something akin to sriracha mayo often served with sushi, the only available option was soy sauce. However, this did not detract from the meal's enjoyment.

The kimbap was expertly prepared by an elder woman who crafted my order with remarkable speed—I spent less than 10 minutes from ordering to receiving my food. 

Despite the sauce confusion, the kimbap itself was scrumptious and satisfyingly hearty. My overall experience was so positive that I'm already planning my next visit.

Title: Happy Hour Haven in Inwood with a Side of Mofongo

If you find yourself in Inwood looking for a lively spot for happy hour, this is the place to be. The happy hour menu might be brief with just four items, but the steak mofongo is a flavorful standout, even if it does swim in its own sauce. For a broader selection, venture into their more extensive appetizer menu that won't break the bank.

The real heroes here are the drinks – expect them to be as potent as they are delicious. The mojito is a revelation, and the passion fruit sangria packs a deceptive punch. A fun and attentive waitstaff adds to the experience, though you might find yourself wishing for a more generous water refresher at times.

As night falls on Fridays, a live DJ sets the scene with music videos casting a glow from the TVs. Although his playlist enthusiasm is evident, it might not be as varied as you'd hope upon a second visit. Nonetheless, this spot offers a dynamic backdrop for unwinding with good company and great drinks.

Title: A Tasty, Yet Mixed Experience

My recent takeout experience from this local eatery was pleasantly average. The highlight was undeniably the cold appetizer platter, which featured favorites like labneh, hummus, and baba ganoush—all of which were delightful. Unfortunately, the other dishes we tried didn't leave as much of an impression, though I suspect the walk before eating may have diminished their appeal.

On the service front, the staff was amiable and efficient, quickly preparing our order—a service level I truly appreciated. Its proximity to my apartment adds a convenience factor that cannot be overlooked, making it a viable option for future impromptu dining needs.

I'm on the fence about reordering, but given the quality of the appetizer platter, there's curiosity to explore their menu further. Here's to hoping their other offerings can match or surpass the starters on my next visit.

First time trying Greek Cuisine and couldn't have picked a  better location(said by Greek Friends).Made a reservation and table was ready right away. It's definitely a place to bring your significant other or date spot. We decided to try few appetizers and then 6-course Chef Tasting . Chef Grundman , really out did himself. I truly loved it . FOOD , I can't begin to tell you how good it was . You just have to try it . Ambiance- 10/10Service - 10/10 WiFi- Not Sure Reservation - recommendedParking - Good Luck

Pros The food was absolutely delish!! I see why people rave about Maison Pickle now. I had the hot honey chicken n toast which came out crispy and piping hot. The bread they use for their thick and fluffy french toast is actually so good!! Additionally, the serving size was huge. After eating less than half, I was super full. Even with a party of 11, our food came out really fast. The staff were super friendly and when one of my friends lost their food when it got taken back to the kitchen to get boxed up, they brought out for her an entirely new entree for her to take home, which was such great customer service! For birthdays, they can bring out a slice of 24 layer cake with giant sparklers. I had the red velvet one which was super yummy. Overall, a great experience!ConsThey only take reservations for 12 or more if you do their prix fixe menu, which I preferred not to because a lot of my friends had various dietary restrictions. I actually had a party of 15 total and we had to make two reservations for 4 and 11 separately and the tables weren't close together at all. Also, even with a reservation for 12pm, we were not seated until 12:40pm.

Joined my coworkers for lunch, location is within walking distance of our office.  Parking is either street side or parking garage.  Restaurant was pretty spacious, server was very nice and kept up with our refills without us having to ask.  The only thing we did not care for was the  heat that came from the ceiling.  We had to request to be moved due to it.  Once we moved we were able to avoid most of the heat from. Food was great and filling.   I ordered the shrimp vermicelli noodles which was really good.  I also tried the bamboo shoots as an appetizer.   It was my first time trying it.  It wasn't bad, and I tasted a hint of ginger but it wasn't anything I would order again, just wasn't my thing.  Overall everyone enjoyed their lunch.  I would return again.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Dumpling Devotees

If you're on a quest for a unique dumpling experience, look no further. This eatery sets itself apart with distinct flavors that eclipse the multitude of cookie-cutter dumpling houses. It's a breath of fresh air for those who seek culinary adventures beyond the trending spots.

Dropping in, I was engulfed by a wave of nostalgia, reminiscent of the cherished New South Wind Restaurant, an icon for 80s kids from Chinatown. The offerings here flirt with perfection, echoing the rare delights from bygone days.

Be mindful, though; while quaint, the seating is sparse, accommodating only a couple of patrons. Larger parties should consider takeout to savor these exceptional dumplings at their leisure. Don't just follow the crowd—this place is a discovery waiting to be cherished.

Title: A Plant-Powered Haven in NYC

I stumbled upon an absolute gem after an exhausting fitness class – a vegan oasis that I can't wait to revisit. First on the plate was the Kale Caesar with shiitake bacon; a tantalizing dish that had me uttering "holy cow" despite its purely plant-based origins. I also indulged in the Chicky Chicky Parm sandwich accompanied by perfectly roasted Brussels sprouts – and I guarded my plate fiercely from any would-be sharers.

The beverage menu didn't disappoint either, featuring a thoughtful selection of beers, wines, and other tempting options I'm eager to explore in future visits. And although I didn't partake this time, the dessert showcase was a visual feast that promised sweet, cruelty-free delights. This spot is a definite must-visit for anyone seeking vegan indulgence in New York City.

Luke's never fails at satisfaction.  Always fresh and meaty no matter which way you roll. Ha! Pun intended.  I love their lobster rolls. The best in the state. Buttery, meaty, seasoned well and always fresh. I opted for the Crab roll and XL lobster roll. To be honest though, couldn't really tell the difference between the regular and the XL which ran me $6 more then the regular roll. There was a lot of meat in it and it was very filling. Always well worth the money. The bread is always light and airy with a buttery crisp to it. The service is always fast and friendly. I have been patronizing Luke's for about 7 years all over the city. I think I've been to every location except the Brooklyn locations. I will continue to go for the quality and the taste. I love Luke's!

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Casual Dining Spot

I recently ventured to a new restaurant I discovered on OpenTable, opting for a Friday night dinner. The highlight of the evening was the service—the waiter exhibited stellar attentiveness and a friendly demeanor throughout our meal.

Unfortunately, the ambiance didn't match up. The interior was lackluster and dominated by an out-of-place, sizeable TV airing news, which detracted significantly from the dining atmosphere.

The menu offerings were average. Our choices for the evening included sushi pizza and a couple of entrees that were palatable, yet unremarkable. The sushi pizza, an interesting fusion concept, was marred by an excessive use of fried potatoes. 

A significant downside to the restaurant was the pervasive smell of food that clung stubbornly to our clothes, necessitating a dry clean for my winter jacket—a disappointing and inconvenient outcome.

On a positive note, dessert shone through, with the cheesecake being the culinary highlight of the night. 

In conclusion, while service was commendable, the overall experience fell short, thanks to the ambiance and lingering odors.

Despite some initial reservations due to negative feedback, I decided to try delivery from this restaurant and ended up pleasantly surprised. The service was prompt, and my orders were consistently accurate across multiple experiences.

My first order, a sushi and sashimi platter (Item 104) in August, was priced at $35.06 after tax, tip, and delivery fee. Although fresh and tasty, I felt that the price didn't entirely match the value, especially as the shrimp didn't meet my expectations, and the accompanying soup was rather unremarkable.

However, the Victoria's Secret Roll in September, costing me $16.76 with all additional fees included, was a different story. It proved to be delicious and well worth the price, making it something I would definitely reorder.

Overall, my experiences with this restaurant have been positive, sidestepping the issues others have seemingly faced, which makes me believe I've been quite fortunate.

Another Restaurant Week success!  I have been meaning to go to this Harlem neighborhood establishment and I am glad I did on one of the coldest nights ever.  The RW prix fixe menu is comforting.  We started with a vegan tomato soup and brussel sprouts and ricotta cheese (not photographed) and they were perfect.  Added a garlic bread and the trio was a great start to a perfect meal of steak and smashed potatoes and chicken marsala.   There are plenty of pasta options which I wanted to try but they were all dairy so I had to stay clear but my non-dairy choices were very satisfying.  My boyfriend's chicken marsala was moist and flavorful.  My medium rare steak was slightly under but was tender and solid nevertheless.  The horseradish sauce on the side was a classic and lovely accompaniment.. Only could have a few bites of the crepes which were laden with caramel sauce.  I did better with the bread pudding which was not too sweet. Definitely will return to this simple elegant cozy place.  I love the old black and white photos of celebrities on the wall, inspiring conversations and memories.

Pick your base: Rice, Noodle (soupy udon) or Creamy Pasta (spaghetti-like). Pick your sides or fixin's (optional). Pick your spice tolerance: Baby, 1, 2, 3, and GURU! I'm currently on Level 2 and it hurts so good! Genuinely spicy, but not spicy just for the sake of being spicy (like those spicy wing joints that make you sign waivers for disgusting food that would otherwise be somewhat tasty if it weren't trying to reach a nuclear spice level). The curry here is superb! Menu isn't that expansive. Just variations of the three main bases, but all beautifully well done. I find myself CRAVING for their curry. Not into curry? There's a very small selection of non-curry bowls on the menu and you can still order sides a la carte. If that's not enough, why come to a restaurant with "curry" in its name?

Title: A Caribbean Culinary Delight at Omar's

From the moment you arrive at Omar's, prepare yourself for a remarkable dining experience that will take you on a flavorful journey through the Caribbean. The wait time is short, promising a swift transition to the gastronomic delights that await.

The food here is simply spectacular, with Omar's passion and expertise in Caribbean cuisine breathing new life into every dish. It's an explosion of flavors from the first bite to the last, each plate more tantalizing than the previous.

As for the drinks, they are nothing short of amazing. Expertly crafted to complement the vibrant food, they complete the dining experience to perfection.

Omar's also hits all the right notes with its ambiance, setting the mood with great music that enhances the Caribbean vibe.

I'm already excited to return to Omar's for more incredible meals and drinks. This place is a must-visit for anyone looking to indulge in authentic Caribbean flavors.

Title: A French Culinary Haven in New York - Le Coucou

Le Coucou stands out as one of New York's finest French dining experiences. A recent weekend lunch highlighted the exceptional quality of their $58 two-course set. The refreshing pâté, infused with foie gras and fruit, awakened the palate, setting the stage for the standout entrée - a chicken meatball with a sumptuous foie gras center. This inventive pairing delivered rich, deep flavors and an exquisite textural contrast, with the foie gras' delicate softness complementing the robust chicken perfectly.

The restaurant's ambiance is no less impressive, exuding elegance and romance, matched by service that excels in warmth and courtesy. An amusing touch is the echoing of the restaurant's namesake, "Le Coucou," subtly playing in the restrooms. From start to finish, Le Coucou provides an impeccable dining experience that goes beyond expectations.

Where do I begin?Mom and I were craving some agedashi tofu and we had walked by this place, saw people eating and were intrigued to try it. I do NOT RECOMMEND this place at all.The hostess who took my order INSISTED they were sold out of Age Tofu. So i ordered the more expensive tempura app. She charged and gave both   neither was very edible after the short 5 blockWalk home. The tempura tasted like old oil. Cold and greasy, we barely managed a few nibbles before having to trash most of the food we received.Also ordered veggie udon $13It wasn't soup....just noodles. Very bizarreShumai tasted *really* fishy. Ate 1 but didn't want to get sick just in case.$43, really bizarre serviand a bag of wasted food later, I wouldn't come back

Great happy hour deals Mon-Saturday til 7pm on food and drinks. $6 glasses of wine and $8 cocktails; best deals in the area! I've been 3 times now and it's super convenient after work. I love the peppers with chipotle mayo ($5 on happy hour menu) and the brussel sprouts ($8 on happy hour menu). They have a good amount of tables and a large bar. Last time, I went with a group of friends and we were treated so well. Adam was a great waiter and helped us decide on what to eat and drink. He was very attentive and constantly running back and forth refilling our drinks. I would highly recommend coming here for happy hour and I will definitely be back!

The service was impeccable. I ordered a lamb souvlaki sandwich with potatoes and tzsiki sauce. It consisted of CUBES of marinated/spiced skewers type lamb cut, NOT the  thin slices off of a lamb spit. I don't like cubes meats. The sandwich was delicious albeit small and it was overpriced. Not sure I would go back again.

Cold Saturday night, was hoping for no wait for a table of two. Unfortunately, still a considerable amount of people at the entrance waiting for their name to be called. Got to the front and was hit with a 15 minute wait - not bad at all considering the circumstances. Buzzer rang 10 minutes later and we got escorted upstairs for table seating.After ordering food, there were a few accompaniments to start off. Got a small whole fried fish, macaroni salad, kimchi, broccoli, and various other dish samples. Fish is a bit oily but better when combining with the other items. For my main course, decided on the Pork Soontofu ($16) - a boiling hot dish of tofu, pork, and veggies swimming in a moderately spicy curry. Tofu took a considerable amount of time to cool off, so best to save your appetizers.Service is up and down - food came out fast but had to ask for refills and the check. Love the fact that it's open 24 hours and the amount of free food given to start. Great for before or after karaoke.

I have to say I am pretty disappointed in Valbella. I went to the old location and I really liked it, so I wanted to bring my husband to the midtown location for him to try. We do a special date night in the city every year around the Holidays, so we really look forward to this night. Walking in, we were greeted by a VERY moody hostess. She seemed like she could care less being there and it set a negative tone for dinner. We started off with a drink and the eggplant appetizer. It was lightly fried and relatively not bad. We ordered another round of drinks with our entrees. My husband just got a titos on the rocks (which is his go-to so he knows what it's supposed to taste like), and they did not make it correctly. It tasted like they added club, and it took so long to get the drink that we decided not to send it back. My husband got the branzino and I got the pappardelle/short rib special. My dinner was amazing - cooked perfect and the homemade pasta was incredible. The branzino was subpar. Very small portion and the side was almost awkward. It was a cold tomato/cucumber/artichoke salad. It didn't pair well with the fish and almost felt like a cheap way to do a side vegetable. The check came and we were pretty surprised how pricey it was given that overall everything was just okay. On our way out, the hostess that was moody was sitting at the high top table on her phone eating dinner. I understand the staff needs to eat too, but it was very unprofessional for a restaurant that is supposed to be higher quality.

Title: A Slice of New York Heaven

As a New Yorker, I've found my pizza sanctuary. It's simply the best pizza I've ever had—the quintessential taste of the city. The lines in Times Square might seem daunting, but they're a testament to the quality and move quickly. The customer service matches the excellence of their pies: prompt, friendly, and always satisfying. If you crave authentic New York pizza, do yourself a favor and visit this gem. Your taste buds will thank you.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Rice Noodle Lovers

Amidst the limited options during this outbreak, a friend clued me in on a spot that's bravely kept its doors open—DM me for the exclusive list. Tucked away in a cozy nook is this unassuming place with an impressively extensive menu. A haven for rice noodle aficionados, my roast duck rice noodle bowl was exceptional, boasting unparalleled texture and an undeniable freshness. My wife's fresh shrimp rice noodle dish echoed my sentiments.

Don't be fooled by the simplicity, though—the dishes require a dash of soy sauce or a hint of hot sauce to truly shine. Still, the generous portions justify the cost. While my choice was delightful, my son, the self-proclaimed 'ramen king,' devoured his ramen with ham bits, signaling another dish done right. Kudos for the thoughtfully packed takeaway and a nod to the owner's eloquent grace and warm hospitality.

I'm compelled to award this establishment a hearty 3 out of 5 stars. Definitely worth a visit for those seeking a standout noodle experience.

Title: A Flavorful Foray into Cambodian Cuisine

My partner and I, along with some friends, ventured to a Cambodian restaurant that, despite its distance, came highly recommended for its authenticity and delicious offerings. On arrival, the warmth of the staff was immediately noticeable, accommodating our preference to sit in the charming outdoor area with no fuss.

Our dining experience began with a bottle of white wine, setting the tone for a relaxed evening filled with good humor and attentive service. The waiter was a delight, eagerly describing menu items and engaging in playful banter.

The appetizers mostly hit the mark, with the papaya salad being an immediate favorite. The Khmer fish cake, nem nuong, and even the disappointing calamari, which lacked the expected crunch, were quickly devoured. It's worth noting that perhaps the calamari was an adventurous but unfitting choice for a Cambodian venue.

Our entrée selections included roast duck, grilled amok, banh chao, and loc lac - each dish revealing the complexity of Cambodian flavors except for the banh chao, which fell flat without its accompanying sauces.

Despite a couple of minor setbacks, the overall experience was so satisfying that a return visit is already in the cards. Next time, we fully anticipate every dish reaching that elusive 11/10 mark!

Title: Cozy Ambiance with Comforting Bites

I recently dined at a lovely spot that accommodated my special request to be seated in the quaint back room by the stone oven, despite their busy schedule with a food tour and private parties. The staff's effort to fulfill my reservation needs through Open Table was commendable, adding a personal touch to the experience.

Opting for a meal suitable for my jet-lagged appetite, I chose the Breakfast Pizza and the Orecchiette with Eggplant to share. While the pizza boasted an impressive crust, its center was unfortunately soggy, perhaps due to an undercooked egg topping which detracted from the overall enjoyment.

The Orecchiette, on the other hand, was a delightful surprise. Every forkful was a harmonious symphony of flavors, with the pesto, eggplant, mozzarella, and pasta creating a culinary masterpiece. The creamy cheese was the pièce de résistance, elevating the dish to a must-try status.

In conclusion, while the pizza was a miss, the pasta alone is enough reason to revisit this charming eatery.

Title: A Broadway Diner's Delight

Tucked conveniently close to the Broadway theaters, this gem of a restaurant understands the pre-show dining rush. Upon entry, the attentive staff promptly inquires about showtimes to ensure timely service. Despite a brief 10-minute wait with reservations, the accommodating team, including the manager, expedited our dining experience without a hitch.

The service was notably friendly and efficient throughout the evening. As for the food, it was simply delicious, with portions that satisfied without overwhelming. The wine list piqued curiosity—each selection featuring unusual but intriguing tasting notes like "birthday cake" or "mango."

Tip: Secure a reservation to guarantee a smooth experience and savor the fine dining this spot offers.

Title: A Fresh Taste of JoJu in Manhattan

As a former Bronx resident now settled in Jersey, my trips to NYC's diverse boroughs are infrequent. However, the opening of JoJu on Manhattan's 555 Fifth Avenue piqued my interest. Stumbling upon their 'SOFT OPENING' sign felt like kismet.

Entering JoJu, I was greeted by a spotless, modern two-story space offering both dine-in and takeout options. Embracing technology, I ordered from the self-service kiosk, opting for the JoJu bowl with an extra egg and a double serving of Vietnamese caramel pork and sausage.

The meal was enjoyable—fresh, crisp veggies alongside flavorful meat; a strong competitor among local offerings, but not earth-shattering. My appetite is already curious about future visits, with items like Crunchy Monster Spring Rolls, Double-fried JoJu Bánh Mì Fries, and savory sandwiches including Lemongrass Chicken and Bulgogi Bomb Me on my radar. I'm also intrigued by the promise of bowls featuring Kakuni Pork Belly and Beef Bulgogi.

Washing it all down with their teas or a Vietnamese cold brew coffee seems like the perfect endnote to the JoJu experience. Count on seeing me there again soon.

Title: A Valentine's Day to Remember at Japanese BBQ

My dining aventure at a Japanese BBQ restaurant on Valentine's Day was nothing short of awesome. The Valentine's special was a steal at $80 for two, including an alcoholic beverage each. My choice was a refreshing mimosa, while my friend enjoyed hot sake.

The meal started with a delightful miso soup and a light, crispy salad dressed to perfection. The standout dish was the Spicy Tuna Volcano—absolutely mind-blowing and worth revisiting for.

The parade of meats, from filet mignon to basil chicken and an array of beef we couldn't keep track of, was succulent and well-seasoned. The accompanying mushrooms were a hit, adding a tasty earthiness to our meal.

Exceptional service amplified our experience, with staff that was impeccably attentive, regularly checking in and expertly managing our grill.

The meal ended on a sweet note with vanilla ice cream drizzled with salted coffee syrup. The restaurant's ambiance and the exciting dining experience made this a place I can't recommend enough.

Boo Boo and I watched youtubers dine here. Okay mostly Boo Boo watches 'day in the life' or 'what I ate during my vacation' vids. We were able to snag a table once the opened for dinner service. I started the matzo ball soup. It was really salty but i still ate it. I didnt drink the soup though.I ordered the special which was a fish over mashed potatoes and the pasta with meat sauce, Boo Boo got the branzino dish which came with a greek style salad.I was kinda underwhelmed because the menu is kinda basic but the price is on the high side, But, we enjoyed our time in NYC.We shouldn't youtubers influence us too much.   If Boo Boo wanted to come back we will come back.

Title: Potential Wrapped in Rice - A Hearty Treat Awaiting Swift Service

I recently had the chance to visit a new local spot during their chaotic Grand Opening weekend, where I sampled their touted "Special Rice Roll." Though I cannot vouch for its authenticity, the roll, generously filled with pork floss, lettuce, and mayo encased in sticky purple rice and seaweed, proved to be an affordable and satisfying option priced between $3-5. It was substantial enough to serve as a swift, hearty snack or a convenient small meal for those on the run.

The current drawback lies in the lengthy wait time for orders, which, in my case, stretched to a 45-minute delay, albeit with fair warning from the courteous cashier. The staff was earnest but overwhelmed, struggling to keep pace with the surging demand.

In sum, the rolls are promising in terms of taste and value. Once operational efficiencies are improved, this establishment is poised to be an excellent go-to for quick and filling eats.

Short review:Mysore Masala dosa was both pricey and not too spicyPlace was super crowded and I had to get the servers attention.Saving grace was the chutneysKheer badam is a good drink for gluttons like meIf I had to summarize this place: Oil oil oil, or rather I should say ghee ghee ghee. I went here during the lunch rush and they operated a bit slow. I ordered a mysore masala dosa which is $2 more than the usual masala dosa. While the dosa glistened red (from said powder as well as ghee,) it lacked the stronger spice flavor I've found from places nearby. There was some potato in there which was good though it wasn't filled as much as some other places also. The texture of the dosa was fine though it was super oily.  In terms of the rest, I found the tomato chutney to be good. The coconut based chutney was unfortunately a bit watery but the other two were alright. The kheer badam drink on the side was sweet with mostly an almond/light saffron/sweetened milk flavor and it was quite delicious.While the portion size was nice, I found the prices a bit high for the quality. The dosa had a bit too much ghee and I think it could have used a lot more spice. The potatoes were good as well as the tomato chutney but if I wanted that, I'd go to another place and get a spiced potato based dish only. If this was in a different neighborhood, I'd give it a higher rating but for this area, there's much better options that are either much more flavored such as Chennai Garden or much more reasonably prices (most other places.) 2.4.

Atmosphere: From the exterior, you can imagine the Pearl Street Diner is a step back in time. It's built into a building (or maybe a building built around it). The inside of the Pearl Street Diner seats only about 20-30 people. There are plenty of booths, tables, and a full-length bar. When I got there, the waitress ushered me to a small table so other parties could use the bigger ones.Coffee:The Pearl Street Diner coffee was brewed hot and fresh and the waitress made sure I had plenty of refills.Food: The Pearl Street Diner menu has everything a stereotypical diner would have. There are plenty of breakfast specials.  I wasn't sure what I was in the mood for, just that I was hungry and tired. I decided to order the blueberry pancakes with whipped cream. The pancakes were good, but it was a small portion and I could have used 3X the amount. I would order them again, but I would probably order something else with them.Service: The waitress at the Pearl Street Diner was friendly and the food came out fast. I couldn't have asked for a better experience.Would I Come Back?I liked the Pearl Street Diner in Manhatten and had a positive experience. If I'm in the area again, I'll go back. It's worth the stop from Battery Park or on your way to the Staten Island Ferry.

Title: A Mixed Dining Experience with Room for Improvement

I made a reservation through RESY expecting a crowd, but to my surprise, the restaurant was nearly empty at 6 PM on a Saturday. Despite the lack of patrons, the decor was strikingly beautiful, setting an elegant stage for the meal ahead.

Our party of four found ourselves on a culinary seesaw with dishes hitting both high and low notes. The Chicken Ramen was a delight, the Morimoto sashimi plate was fresh and delicate, and the Tempura sweet potatoes were a perfect balance of crispy and tender. The Carrot and heirloom tomato dish, along with the rich flavors of the Black cod, Mushroom soup, Avocado roll, and Vegetarian roll, left us appreciating the kitchen’s capabilities.

However, not all dishes reached those heights. The Tofu Miso Soup and an assortment of Pickled veggies fell flat. The fresh-made tofu required three attempts to get right, yet the result was lackluster. Pea shoots, Bok choy, and Chinese broccoli lacked the necessary oomph to impress, while the Roasted pork suffered from being overdone, presenting a burnt exterior.

Our experience was further marred by inconsistent service, as we often found ourselves seeking assistance from staff beyond our assigned server.

In reflection, it was fun to try out the place, but the kitchen's inconsistency and spotty service leave us uncertain about a return visit.

Title: A Delightful Dinner at a Cozy Gem

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this little-known spot after initially discovering it some time ago. It came highly recommended by a friend, and it did not disappoint. My dining companion and I had the ambition to try almost everything on the menu, leaving out only the cucumber dishes.

Each plate that graced our table was a testament to the kitchen's dedication to flavor and craft. Notable standouts included the silky soft tofu with the intriguing depth of century egg and a spicy beef noodle soup that offered just the right amount of kick to warm the soul.

While the prices felt a touch steep relative to the portions, the exquisite quality of the food justified the expense, leaving me feeling wholly fulfilled by the meal's end.

The restaurant operates a policy of seating guests only when the entire party is present. Given its intimate size, I recommend ensuring your group arrives together to avoid a wait, as this charming establishment fills up quickly.

In summary, despite the minor quibble on price and the seating policy, the experience was a positive one. I am already looking forward to my next visit, ready to explore more of their delicious offerings.

Title: Cozy Pizzeria with a Personal Touch

I recently visited a delightful pizzeria boasting a spacious dining area, complete with a television for an entertaining meal experience. The menu impressed me with a wide variety of pizza options to choose from. The staff members were notably friendly and attentive, contributing to the welcoming atmosphere. I opted for a plain slice during my visit and while it was quite tasty, my preference leans towards a slice with a bit more sauce. Nonetheless, this establishment is worth visiting for anyone in search of a convivial ambiance and a substantial pizza selection.

No complaints at all. Service was great, food and sauces were on point, they were attentive and the food tasted amazing and cooked well. I definitely look forward to coming back again. The unlimted meet is always a selling point even though its impossible to continue to eat that much.  But still a great experience.

I love this place - this location and the Williamsburg location equally - food quality is great - Moroccan tea is a must there - service is forest as well - I had Moroccan breakfast with Moroccan tea and both were great -

The ambiance is the place is very intimate, chic and cute ...definitely a city spot. While the food was prepared well and the food presentation was good, I didn't find the food particularly amazing or anything to call home about. The service was good as well but don't know if I would go out of my way for this.

Title: A Cozy Corner of Culinary Delight

I'm compelled to award a well-deserved 4.5 stars to this gem of a restaurant where warmth and charm are served up alongside delectable dishes. On a chilly day, the cozy interior welcomed us into its snug embrace for a late lunch. The décor exudes a thoughtful quaintness, setting the stage for a meal where simplicity shines.

The pesto bruschetta was the opening act—a testament to the kitchen's dedication to freshness, the homemade pesto atop warm, crisp bread was a herald of the goodness to come. Paired with a glass of Nero d'Avola, the wait for the main course was as pleasurable as the anticipation of a second bite.

The arrival of the tagliatelle ragù was a sensory feast, the hint of truffle oil elevating a classic to new heights. Each strand of al dente pasta was cloaked in flawlessly simmered sauce. Equally impressive were the spaghetti and meatballs, where the sheer size of the meatballs was matched only by their flavor, nestled atop a bed of spaghetti with a red sauce that spoke of comfort and care.

The meal was a triumph, consumed with an enthusiasm that left us fortified against the cold outside. This spot is a must-return for me; its magnetic pull undeniable, promising yet another round of simple, yet profoundly satisfying culinary bliss.

Egg Shop is one of the best brunches in all of NYC. Close to Soho, it's a small picturesque cafe that sells ten egg sandwiches, several "cruisers" (egg in a grain bowl), sides, and drinks. Here's why I love it:1) Food: It's out of this world. You really can't go wrong with anything on the menu, but if you like a fried chicken sandwich, order the "hot chix" sandwich. The biscuit, the egg, the chicken, wow!2) Drinks: They have refreshing drinks. I recommend their Bloody Mary or the mimosa. 3) Space: It's small, but gorgeous. There's a bar in the front and tables throughout the cafe. There's a small bathroom in the back.4) Service: It's on point and fast. It's popular so they run a tight ship, but not in a way that causes stress on anyone. We went as a group of four adults and two babies on a Sunday morning and we only had to wait for 10 minutes.

Title: Culinary Delight at Takashi

My dining experiences at Takashi have consistently been delightful, especially with their signature dish, the Niku Uni, and the Kobe Filet Mignon doused in a divine garlic butter sauce that I can’t help but use as a dip for all the other meats. On my most recent visit, the Kobe Kalbi and Ribeye were added to the table, living up to the high standard with their tenderness and flavor.

The portions are modest, which for a party of three, meant sharing an appetizer, indulging in four meat selections – with a double helping of the Filet – and supplementing our meal with three bowls of rice led to a state of contented satiety without overindulgence.

A thoughtful touch was the piece of gum provided at the end, a considerate gesture to counteract the garlic aftermath. Just a heads-up, the immersive experience of grilling your own food does mean a lingering barbecue aroma on your attire. Nonetheless, Takashi remains a top choice for those seeking quality meats and a unique self-cooking experience.

I love Taiwanese style braised food and this was definitely a pleasantly surprise find for me!The menu is customizable and there is a large selection of meats and vegetable toppings. The portion is pretty decent, although I found it a tad pricy. The flavor was a little too light for my liking, but I'd still return to satisfy my taiwanese braised food craving.

Title: Best Bang for Your Buck at Dollah Slice Pizza!

I stumbled upon a gem in the heart of West 4th – Dollah Slice Pizza. This unassuming spot isn't just for those late-night cravings; it's a haven for pizza enthusiasts any time of day. I can confidently say I found the best NYC dollar slice while completely sober – so trust me, the quality is undeniable. Perfect for a quick meal or a post-drinking snack, Dollah Slice delivers on flavor and value. A must-try for anyone in search of an authentic, wallet-friendly New York pizza experience.

One of the best brunch experiences I've had in a while. The interior evokes the charm of old Tel-Aviv cafes, as the owner comes around to everyone's tables. Start your meal with the Moroccan tea - it comes in an ornamental, silver tea kettle and mitt that looked like it was hand sewn by someone's grandmother. The waiters will gladly refill the tea multiple times - but the first pot is the most delicious.The pita bread was incredibly fluffy, and paired nicely with the hummus, drizzled with olive oil and topped with whole chickpeas. Mouthwateringly delicious. The Shookshuka also deserved praise - nicely spiced and served freshly baked challah bread. I finished my meal satiated, but not weighed down, looking forward to my next time back.

We came here for our friend's birthday as he was craving for seafood. Reservation was very easy on opentable.The service was great (thanks to Rachel, Vincent & Angus) and we got a bottle of wine on the house for the birthday celebration!There were 5 of us and we ordered some appetizers to start - salted yolk dungeons crab (highly recommended), scallion pancake (homemade, very flaky), Oxtail tongue & tripe w/ chili sauce & wonton w/ spicy chili oil. All were delicious and not too spicy.Given our group size, Vincent recommended Combo E as you get more seafood choices than Special Group Combo. We were also able to switch out shrimps in Combo E for crawfish. We went with spicy cajun flavoring as none of us enjoy numbing spicy (I know we are at a Sichuan restaurant). We all had a blast digging through our bag and licking every inch of the sauce covering the seafood.We will return again- to try the sup king crab next!

Title: Style Over Substance at New Midtown Dim Sum Palace

My anticipation for the new Dim Sum Palace in midtown was high, drawn in by its glamorous facade and the buzz of its grand opening. However, the experience left much to be desired. Despite the chilly weather, the restaurant welcomed us with an unnecessary blast of air conditioning, which had us dining with our coats draped over our shoulders.

A notable deviation from dim sum tradition was the absence of complimentary jasmine tea, a staple at most establishments. Instead, it was offered starting at a steep $6, prompting a hard pass from us. Moreover, the prices of the dim sum dishes were inflated by $2-$3 compared to average eateries, yet the food failed to justify the premium.

With $33 spent, we left feeling unsatisfied and hungry, the quality of the food disappointing as it tasted stale and lacked freshness. I can only commend the prompt service and attentive waitstaff, which earned Dim Sum Palace its two stars. But for those looking for authentic and value-for-money dim sum, this may not be the spot.

Title: A Charming Italian Retreat in the Theater District

My husband and I had the pleasure of dining early at this delightful Italian spot after a matinee show. The experience was cozy and inviting, particularly on the more spacious upper level, as the downstairs was a bit snug.

For our meal, I savored a fresh mixed salad followed by an impeccably seasoned lemon chicken, while my husband indulged in a succulent lamb dish. The selection of breads served was a delightful prelude to our main courses.

Noteworthy was the wine list, boasting a fine array at just $35 a bottle, which complemented our dishes beautifully. While the pasta special is touted for its value, I find the other entrees - like ours - to be the true stars of the menu.

Service was nothing short of stellar; prompt and gracious throughout our visit. For anyone seeking a warm, budget-friendly Italian eatery amidst the buzz of the theater district, look no further – this restaurant is a gem.

Title: The Ultimate Benedict Brunch at Jane

If you're on the hunt for the best Eggs Benedict in NYC, look no further than Jane. A renowned brunch destination, this spot serves up mouthwatering plates that live up to its reputation. Friendly staff enhance the experience, making you feel welcome as you indulge in your meal.

Be warned, the wait for a table can be quite long, a testament to Jane's popularity. I highly recommend booking in advance through OpenTable to avoid the wait. The variety of Benedict specials is a delight, especially when they feature delectable pulled pork—an absolute must-try.

And let's not forget the mimosas—simply perfect! In summary, Jane is the place to be for a Benedict that will redefine your brunch expectations. Don’t miss out on what could very well be the best Benedict of your life.

I was pleasantly surprised and pleased by Joju, since its fast paced Viet food in a lunch room set up. I tried the beef vegetarian banh mi + kimchi fries along with a viet cofffee. Would i come back? yes, id try the veggie pork sandwhich. Theres options for me, and overall there was flavor and the banh mi was good. its a great place to pick up and go or grab a quick dinner before an event. and who doesnt love viet food? great concept. Here goes a short run down:1. Order your food on the screen - wait for your name to be called2. Theres free water by the counter.3. Ordering a veggie friendly item? Make sure to opt out of the pork sauce4. The Iced viet coffee was okay, but i wouldnt get again - tasted a bit watered down, nothing special about it5. Veggie beef banh mi - very good. packed with flavor - juicy - fresh - toasted just right and very filling. Steep price of about $116. Kimchi fries - overfried, too crunchy, very sharable, good but i wouldnt get again. too much going on here7. Fast service around dinner time.

I celebrated my birthday here last night and had the most amazing time! There were about 18 friends of mine coming at all different times and they were able to give us a huge section in the back. It was great to have a large area to sit. They have great happy hour specials. I love the frozen paloma and it is $8 on happy hour till 8pm. They also have a taco deal on Tuesday! Our server was kind enough to give our entire party a free tequila shot for my birthday and he also gave me a paloma on the house. We were there for hours and never felt rushed. It was a great place for a birthday celebration! I wish I got our server's name because he was awesome the entire night. Side Note: They don't let you do separate checks for a large party and can only take 6 credit cards.

Title: A Perfect Birthday Bash at Eat Thai

I recently organized a friend's birthday dinner at Eat Thai and had a fantastic experience. The staff truly outshined with their accommodating and friendly nature. We had a sizable party of 12, and they seamlessly integrated an extra table with their already ample group dining setup at the back of the restaurant.

The charm of being able to personalize our dining space with decorations and a birthday cake without incurring extra fees added to the evening's delight. Eat Thai's menu boasts a plethora of classic Thai dishes, all of which were bursting with flavor and authenticity. Complementing the food, the all-day happy hour ensured that our glasses were as joyfully filled as our plates.

The combination of delectable cuisine, inviting ambience, and impeccable service rendered Eat Thai a top-notch choice for group celebrations or any occasion meriting a memorable meal.

As others have already mentioned, this place is a fast casual Mexican place that this is very similar in setup and decor to Chipotle. There is a fair amount of seating and it is also very clean. The main thing I had from here was one of their bowls and some sides. Flavor wise, I found it slightly better than Chipotle. The grilled chicken I chose had a nice smokey flavor to it. They also offer a slightly larger menu of toppings than Chipotle with 7 salsas and stuff like corn relish and sauteed squash. The portion sizes are slightly smaller than Chipotle though.
We enjoy stopping in the Keg Room. Drinks are great and food is good. There's something for everyone on the menu.

A friend of mine highly recommended this place. I came here on a rainy day. We liked the restaurant. It's a small but trendy place. It has nice modern decorations.The volcanic tum yum soup definitely wowed me. It's a little bit salty and seasoning is pretty heavy lMy friend and I ordered two kinds of duck. They were pretty good. The portion was big. The food was very filling. I liked the flavors. Duck was roasted to crispy. Our dessert Lychee Sticky rice was excellent. It was my first time to have that and it definitely impressed me. (But we were to full to finish the dessert lol. Service was good. Waiters were pretty attentive. However, the bill was a little bit more expensive than I expected. Overall, I like this place. It's pretty decent Thai food with good service and vibe.

I've lived in the area for many years and finally tried this place a week or so back. I really enjoyed my meal here and will absolutely be back!We started off splitting one of the salads. I don't remember exactly what it was called but it was romaine with dill, feta and I think scallion or something similar. Was really good - lightly dressed and the feta was soft and creamy. Really liked it. I will say that looking around the place their traditional Greek salad looked like it would be even better, despite how much I liked what we got.For the main I had one of the sea bass options (I'm doing really bad remembering the names of things). It seemed like a branzino but I think was called something different. Regardless it was really good. Perfectly prepared and was clearly extremely fresh. My fiancée had the seafood orzo which was also delicious - I loved the sauce. Had a great meal here - only negative is it's a tiny bit overpriced but I still will absolutely be back!

They completely live up to the hype. This is well worth going out of your way for if you're a Seinfeld fan or not, (unlike Toms Restaurant.) I get the lobster bisque which is delicious. Huge chunks of lobster with a slice of baguette to sop up the delicious broth. Grab some and take a short walk up to Central Park for a delicious affordable lunch.Pro tip...  add a couple drops of the spicy sauce from the halal guys cart down the street to give it a nice kick.

My friend and I went to grab dinner at Dos Caminos around 9 PM on a Friday night. The restaurant was pretty full for the time we arrived but we were able to be seated at a large, comfortable booth in the middle of the restaurant. It took around 15 minutes before our waiter came over to pour us some water and take our orders. This was a good representation about how slow service was during the rest of the meal. However the server was very friendly and upbeat throughout the meal. We decided to get a few dishes to share. The amount of food we ordered was a bit too much for the two of us and we could have done well with one  less dish than what we ordered: --Chips and Salsa: Chips were fresh and delicious.  There were three salsas available and they all tasted great. --Queso fundido: Flavor was great! We got it with chorizo but it just seemed like overkill because the queso was already kind of greasy and the chorizo made it even more oily. It came with some quartered tortillas. I didn't really like the tortillas that much and felt that the chips worked much better with the queso. --Short Rib Tinga Chile Rellano: The flavor of the sauce over the Chile rellano was delicious. However, the breading was a bit too spongy than what I would have liked and the short ribs were slightly dry. Also if the Chile was cooked just a little bit longer it would have been even better. It was also a very small amount of food for the price. --Pescado Taco: Adequate fish tacos but nothing too special.I also checked in on Yelp and got a free prickly pear shot. The drink was ok. It was an interesting blend of flavors but not sure if I would have gotten it if it wasn't free. All in all, an average meal slapped with a steep price tag.

Title: A Turnaround to Applaud at Shanghai Delights

Review:
Returning to Shanghai Delights after last year's experience was a rewarding decision. My latest visit, with a considerable party arriving late into the evening, was met with nothing but patience and accommodating service from our waiter – commendable and consistent with the exceptional service I've grown to expect here. This establishment stands out in Chinatown for its young, English-speaking waitstaff, a rarity amongst its competitors.

What truly captivated me this time was the significant enhancement in the quality of the cuisine. The soup dumplings maintained their exquisite reputation, but the black truffle took center stage with its robust flavor and mouthwatering aroma. Markedly improved were the scallion pancakes; gone was the overcooked appearance and overpowering saltiness, replaced by a perfectly golden hue and balanced flavor profile. The Szechuan Style Wontons arrived in a steamy and inviting state, just as I had hoped.

While the Salt & Pepper Squid fell short due to its lack of seasoning, the remainder of our dishes, including the succulent Shanghai Fried Rice and savory Lo Mein, were prepared to perfection. With these positive changes, Shanghai Delights has undoubtedly secured its spot as my go-to destination for Shanghainese cuisine in the heart of the city.

We came on a Friday night at around 7. Our school had a pretty good discount so we each got 2 for $3. I ordered the pesto and jala honey, but they switched our orders and we didn't know we got the each other's order until we ate them which was kind of annoying. So I ended up having the classic and jala honey. They were really good, but the jala honey was my favorite! Panzerotti taste a lot like calzones in texture, with the soft dough and all, but I think they're smaller than calzones. The deal was amazing so I got a jala and pesto to go. I would totally return, but prices are a bit too steep without the discount so that would be the only thing holding me back. 4.5 stars.

Title: Tacovision: Great Eats Marred by Service Woes

Review:

My relationship with Tacovision is bittersweet. On one hand, their fried Brussels sprouts tacos are an absolute delight and the guacamole is rich and satisfying. Couple these with their delicious $7 frozen margaritas during happy hour, and you've got the makings of a fantastic meal.

However, service is where Tacovision falls dramatically short. Time and again, over the course of five visits, the dining experience has been consistently marred by poor service. The waitstaff appears overwhelmed and forgetful, often bringing out dishes haphazardly. Imagine finishing your meal before your appetizers even make an appearance, despite multiple reminders.

While the quality of the food and drinks earns them a respectable three stars, the dining experience leaves much to be desired. Proximity to my office is the only reason I keep coming back. Tacovision, your culinary creations are commendable, but the service needs a serious overhaul to match.

I have been longing to go to the Wolfgang steakhouse for a long time. Now, I got the chance. We had weekend lunch here.  Place is surprisingly quiet while we dined there. We had seafood appetizer, filet and rib eye steak along with their free bread. As we finished our lunch, we absolutely stepped into food coma.  We love food here. Everything is fresh, tasteful and juicy. Service: accommodating. Price: yeah you know it's a four $$$$ restaurant. I can't wait to bring my family here to enjoy a weekday dinner. I bet it would be epic.

I give one star to balance outthis gross misrepresentation.Dear reader, beware, it is a trap!An over-hyped abomination. I'll tell the story as I think it went,it began thirty years in the past.Blondies was born into tough competitionbut its owners were determined to last.They'd make great wings, the best around,hook customers after just one bite.Fried crisp, yet juicy, smothered in sauceNothing fancy but they were done right.Word spread fast, the plan had worked.Blondies became a big success.But slowly they took it all for granted,caring about the food less and less.So here I sit today with my phone and with a heavy heart I must declare.These wings are soggy and sad and plainand served with apathy, beware!!

Holy guacamole this place is the shiiiiiii. Everything we ordered came out hot and delicious. Order the nacho tots, you will not regret it. The butternut squash taco was so good it gave me hope for all vegetables and the nitro shrimp taco was crispy and flavorful and just so great. More like a grab and go kinda place, but there is seating and it has some cool lights inside.

I would give it 3.5 stars, but based on what I ordered it wasn't worth 4 stars. Delivery was pretty quick, and the food was pretty good. The pita falafel sandwich was good but it could've used more hummus. Even with the extra side of tzatziki, it was a little dry. The tabouleh was also good but had the opposite problem. After mixing it, it was still watery at the bottom. There were no problems with the spanakopita, I should've ordered two because I liked it and was still a little hungry. I'll be ordering from here again but I'll also try other places to see how they compare.

A bacon lover's dream! Their menu revolves around bacon. Bacon meals, bacon desserts, and even bacon dressed drinks!  Stopped here on a whim while out and out about with a friend. We stopped in, not knowing that this is the famed bacon place that I've been seeing everywhere on FB and IG. We decided to stop in and have dinner, and I'm happy that we did. The vibe is a fun vibe as they randomly hand out stickers, beer samples, and water based tattoos. (This all happens pending on the day you go). They were also playing some type of trivia game in she back of the restaurant, which looked pretty cool and seemed to have random tables engaging in.For my meal, I opted to have the pulled pork sandwich with bacon and substituted the chips for fries. The sandwich was extremely juicy, well seasoned, and nicely smoked. The fries were seasoned with a sweet and lightly salty barbecue dry seasoning, which was a nice touch. The pineapple coleslaw that it was paired with was nice as well. The coleslaw was slightly spicy due to the jalapeño pieces but sweet at the same time due to the pineapple pieces. My friend opted for the Kentucky fried bacon, which was also quite tasty. It was nice and crispy on the outside, but a bit too fatty on the inside (for my personal liking). It was served in a honey sauce, which gave it a nice overall flavor. Although the Kentucky fried bacon was a bit too fatty for me, my friend thoroughly enjoyed her meal!Though their deserts look delightful, we were so full off of our meal we opted to make a future visit to try them out. (Can't wait to try their bacon infused sundae!)Overall, I really like this place. It's a cool bar type vibe, with tasty food. I highly recommend going here. Kentucky fried bacon: $15Pork pulled sandwich with bacon: $17French fry substitute: $3

This review applies to both locations. I've visited each location twice; my first time at leach location I had the monthly special and one of the dumplings from the regular menu. The monthly specials are always really good, but I do not like the dumplings from the regular menu.... the last two times I've stopped by, I just got an order of the monthly special and then went somewhere nearby for dessert. The sides are ok, but are very pricey. The dumplings are actually pretty pricey too. It's fun to watch them being handmade up at the front, and their house dipping sauce is fantastic, but I can't really recommend anything other than the monthly special. My favorite monthly was the Emmy burger collaboration! I wish all the dumplings were like this.  The buratta meatball dumplings were also really good, and the lunar new year lamb dumplings were amazing. This month there is a French onion soup dimpling and I'd like to try that. So again, the specials are fun, interesting, and delicious, but you're better off going to Chinatown if you want high quality pork or veggie dumplings and you'll get them there for cheaper.

I ate so much here but every bite was delicious. The pirogies are a must have - hands down. I also got the blintzes and the lox bagel. It's a laidback vibe and despite a wait we were seated quite quickly. A perfect NYC brunch.

Came here for dinner with a friend. Ordered a cucumber preserved egg for appetizer, grilled fish on a sizzling plate, thin slice beef in a sour tomato soup. So overall this place is very good. 5 star, you don't come by a Szechuan restaurant in midtown that can bring flavor like this. Been to many others places but this spice is just right. Price is also very reasonable.

Title: A Mixed Experience with Grilled Delights

My dining companion and I ventured into this spot for an early dinner post-theatre and were greeted with warmth and attentiveness by the staff. Our meal commenced with the grilled octapodi, which was ample for two but disappointingly lacked a punch of freshness in its otherwise noticeable grilled essence. 

The dinner salad was a highlight – generous and delicious. Our main course, the Ortikia Sharas, presented a delectable grilled quail, yet the accompanying spinach side fell flat in flavor. The tirokafteri, though, was a fiery addition that delighted our taste buds.

This restaurant offered moderate pricing, particularly for a tourist-heavy location. The ambiance was pleasantly subdued, providing a gentle backdrop to our meal. While not all dishes hit the mark, the standouts and the overall experience merit a recommendation for those in the neighborhood. Check out the photos I've attached for a visual taste!

It's a great spot in NYC, especially since it's more affordable as far as sushi goes. Decently priced for good portions for sets of 3, 4, 5 or 6 handrolls. The seaweed is fresh and crispy. There's something a little different with their rice as well, but I can never quite put my finger on it. I get the 6 handroll set since it's a great value for the variety.1. There can be a wait but the line moves quickly, I haven't waited more than about 30 minutes in the few times I've gone for dinner.2. If you have any allergies or just want to make a substitution, you can do so, but you can only substitute to cheaper fish/sushi based on the guidelines they explain at the counter.3. Sometimes they have a special roll such as uni if you want to pay extra for it.

Title: A Mixed Bag at a High-End Laotian Spot

My culinary journey into Laotian cuisine began with anticipation at this upscale eatery. Despite its presence during restaurant week, the specialty menu was bypassed for the regular offerings, which was a bit of a shock given the pricing. Expect to shell out around $50 per person, but the ambiance transports you – the authentic dishware alone is a cultural immersion.

The meal commenced with complimentary sticky rice served with delectable condiments – a savory and spicy gateway into the cuisine that's eaten with your hands without a mess. The coconut rice was a revelation; deep-fried to a perfect crunch, with an interior that's packed with flavor, paired with refreshing lettuce wraps and a decadent Asian sausage.

Unfortunately, the entrees didn't carry the torch. The chili prawn lacked the heat I craved, and the pork curry noodle missed the mark despite an herbaceous garnish.

My advice? Stick to the appetizers for a more satisfying experience without the sting of the main course prices.

Title: Authentic Hunan Spice at Silky Kitchen

I recently visited Silky Kitchen, a haven for Hunan rice noodle enthusiasts in NYC, and my craving was duly satisfied. Their menu boasts an impressive variety of toppings, ensuring there's something for every palate. I ventured into the hot and sour chicken gizzard (S4), opting for the "regular" spice level, which packed a pleasantly fiery punch, truly authentic to Hunan cuisine.

The quality of rice noodles met my expectations - not the best I've encountered, but they were still quite delectable. The highlight was the rich, flavorful soup accompanying the stewed beef; it was a taste to remember. Patrons have the choice between wet or dry dishes, with the former including broth. I did find a slight mismatch between the toppings and noodles in terms of flavor infusion, though this was less of an issue with the wet stewed beef noodles (S1).

Despite this minor critique, hats off to Silky Kitchen for championing Hunan rice noodles. For those looking to explore the depths of Chinese regional cuisine, this spot will not disappoint - just be prepared for a true taste adventure.

Definitely a good spot I'd love to return to! I came toward the end of the lunch hour so kind of had to rush into ordering FYI (got there around 2:10). I had the chicken dosa which were tasty but FYI very spicy! They use ghost pepper sauce in it and I liked it but it was maybe sliiiightly too spicy for me to finish everything. Good flavor though. My friend had the paneer dosa which were tasty and also used the ghost pepper but didn't seem as spicy. LOVED the naan. I know that naan seems like a pretty basic item but I really can tell the difference between a good one and just an average one. The naan here is absolutely delicious, not dry, and full of flavor. I also got the lime soda but wasn't nuts about the flavor. I had the option of getting it sweet or salty or a combination of both and I went with the combination. If I were to order it again, I would go just sweet.The decor is super pretty and the cocktails on the menu look good. Most Indian restaurants seem to be pretty whatever when it comes to ambiance/trendiness so this one definitely outranks other Indian restaurants for being fun and modern. The service was also great. I would definitely like to return for dinner and to try other items on the menu.

Having heard much chatter about Ippudo, my curiosity got the better of me, so I decided to give it a whirl, armed with high expectations from my all-time favorite spot, Totto Ramen. Ippudo, often lauded, left me pondering the source of its fame. Post a 20-30 minute wait, I was seated and opted for their signature dish. To my palate, it was good but failed to eclipse my experiences at Totto. Even the pork belly wraps didn't quite hit the mark, being somewhat on the smaller side for my liking. While I might consider giving Ippudo another shot in the future, my ramen cravings would likely steer me back to the familiar and beloved Totto Ramen.

Highly recommend Empellón Taqueria if you are looking for some delicious, juicy and tasty tacos in NYC. Empellón is such a fancy yet affordable Mexican restaurant with a catchy menu.I visited on a week day for dinner. Considering I was alone, I seated myself at the bar. I sense Empellón is always busy. Such a cute bar that's filled with artsy decor. They have so many different types of taco selection among many other choices. I ended up ordering two chicken tacos. Best choice ever! The taco was soft just the way I like them. And the chicken was well seasoned, flavored, juicy and had a bit of spicy kick to it. I absolutely loved my meal and surprisingly I did not make a mess. My meal was excellent and had that authentic feel to it.  I'd recommend having a glass of Rose with your meal. Overall the service was excellent. The bartender and manager were friendly and pleasant to be around. Definitely will visit again.

I recently visited a vibrant restaurant during their happy hour and was pleased with the experience. The atmosphere was buzzing with great music, adding to the energetic vibe of the place. Service was prompt, and our waitress exuded warmth and professionalism, ensuring our evening was enjoyable. I tried the yuca fries, which were perfectly prepared and tasty. To accompany my meal, I opted for the Jack Punch, which was a refreshing choice. Overall, it was a satisfying visit, and I'd recommend this spot for anyone looking for a lively ambiance and tasty bites.

Title: Revised Review: Customer Service Worthy of Praise
