Originally, I rated Bap with three stars, as neither the food nor the ambiance particularly impressed me. However, I've decided to revise my review to four stars, not because my opinion of their offerings has changed, but due to the exceptional customer service provided by Jisu J, the manager. Following my initial Yelp critique, Jisu reached out with such professionalism and courtesy that it not only showcased their dedication to customer satisfaction but also earned my respect. This positive interaction has inclined me to consider revisiting Bap to give it another chance. It's a testament to the power of responsive and thoughtful management.

Venturing into this popular tourist hotspot with friends, we were met with the all-too-familiar lengthy wait times, both for a table and our meals. Despite the delays, the restaurant's vibrant decor provided a feast for the eyes, and the delectable milkshakes served as the highlight of our experience, offering a sweet reprieve from the otherwise unremarkable service. It's a venue worth visiting at least once for those seeking to soak in the ambiance and indulge in a frothy treat.

I came here with a group of friends on a Wednesday night. We were a relatively large group of 8 people. The service was top notch. The owner Kenny chatted with us on what he recommended. The decor is modern with dried Chinese spices displayed as a backdrop. For the food: - Live Blue Crab w. Rice Cake: My favorite dish of the night. The rice cake had salty egg yolk mixed in. The flavor was complex and blew me away.- steam egg cup with sea urchin: steam egg was silky and showed finesse- truffle sea scallops: the sea scallops was fresh and delicious, but I didn't like the truffle combination. The truffle destroyed the freshness of the scallops- soup dumplings: The fillings and soup were good, but the skins were too thick- Shanghai truffle wonton: good, but it came to us lukewarm- king crab squid ink shanxi flat noodle: noodles were al dente and I loved the complexity- yang zhou noodle: it was a bit stickier than I would like, but great- Stir-Fried Miyazaki Wagyu Beef: the beef was tender and it just melted- Sautéed Tiger Prawn & Lobster Risotto: rice was complex with bit of sweetness. It was an interesting dish and I liked the innovation. - Tao Jiao Egg Tarts: I thought the tart was too oily- Egg Yolk Sesame Ball: Delicious. Loved the molten yolk filling.

Title: A Bustling Saturday Night at [Restaurant Name]

I visited [Restaurant Name] on a busy Saturday evening and was immediately struck by the vibrant atmosphere; the place was buzzing with energy, and we were fortunate to be seated right away without a wait.

To start, we indulged in an appetizer sampler featuring an assortment of treats: veg spring rolls, fish rolls, dhal vade, and fish cutlets. Each bite offered a delightful taste of the restaurant's capabilities, but the fish cutlets stood out with their exceptional flavor and just-right spice level.

For the main course, the chicken koththu roti hit the spot with its spicy kick — we opted for medium, which packed quite the punch. Despite a 30-minute wait for our food, understandable given the crowd, the meal was worth the patience.

The service was efficient and courteous throughout our visit.

My overall experience was satisfying, and I'm keen to return to [Restaurant Name] to explore more of their menu.

Cane here as a group for dinner and it was my first time coming here.As per traditional shanghainese food, most stuff has sweet tastes but it was not annoyingly sweet.The food is delicious and fresh and I do like the string beans with eggplant and the green fried rice a lot.Maybe because the restaurant doesnt have that much people ordering wine, we had to ask to change two people's wine glasses because they were dirty. Overall it's a pleasant experience.

Jeju Noodle Bar, nestled in the bustling West Village, is a gem I've eagerly anticipated visiting after a trip to Jeju Island. True to the burgeoning hype, it didn't disappoint. Contrary to Korean cuisine's unsung noodle dishes, their spicy ramen was a bowl of rich, robust flavors that defeated even my hearty appetite. Complementing the meal, their steamed buns were an impeccable choice. The soju, a traditional accompaniment, was not only affordable but also a pleasant surprise in the heart of the city. A suggestion for an even better experience? A selection of flavored soju could cater to diverse palates. This spot is a must-visit; I'm certainly going back for more.

Ordered the banh mi online and picked up a bit before I had scheduled to. Ordering online from their website was easy and my order was ready when it was supposed to be. The brisket banh mi was very well balanced with a crunchy baguette and lots of meat. Often times places might make the meat or brisket dry or shredded but Cha Pa's has it sliced and it was juicy. The vegetables also balance out with not too much overpowering of the pickled vegetable. Overall great experience and glad I found it!

Title: An Ode to Xi'an's Culinary Majesty

If the epicurean world were a music chart, Xi'an Famous Foods would top the hits. My recent visit, braving the bitter chill in a daring muscle shirt, proved that the hype around the Spicy Cumin Lamb Hand-Ripped Noodles (N1) is not just noise; it's a life-altering experience.

The ambiance of Xi'an, while snug, buzzes with early 90s rap—an acquired taste, maybe, but it sets a unique tone. There's a slight discord with their tipping policy signage, but that pales in comparison to the culinary symphony they serve.

The staff, particularly one charming server, made the experience more memorable with her warmth and friendliness—tip dispute notwithstanding.

As for the food, it's not just good; it's "tell-your-friends, bring-your-family, shout-it-from-the-rooftops" fantastic. The SCLHRN (N1) still sings its flavorful tune as it did in the basement days of Queens. Though I yearn for that originality, the current serving does not miss a beat.

Despite a few irksome quirks with the playlist and tip confusion, Xi'an Famous Foods earns a solid 5-star rating for its knockout dish and heartwarming service. Go for the N1; it might just make you a believer.

The food here is pretty good, but for the price you pay, it's not much. I got the breakroom fries and for about 9 dollars, you don't get a lot of food. It's also very misleading because when they post pictures on Instagram, they show that the items are full, but when you order it, it barely really fills the whole container. I'm also pretty sure putting those items together isn't that expensive, especially when the Breakroom fries is just bits of things here and there, so it wouldn't hurt to really fill up the container. I've also gotten the Ribeye Cheesesteak Sandwich which is more filling for $10 but it doesn't have a lot of flavor to it. The meat is also on the tougher side, so combining it with their hero which also has a bit of a chew, it is a bit of a workout to eat this sandwich. The onions adds a little sweetness to it, but other than that most of the flavor comes from the cheese sadly. It definitely feels more filling than the fries but it doesn't standout much alone. There are definitely better cheesesteaks that you can get elsewhere. I also feel like they probably do tacos better so ordering a cheesesteak may be bad on my part. Another thing to note was that the girl that was taking my order seemed like she didn't want to assist me. She seemed more into wanting to conversing with someone in the back then helping. The vibe of the workers don't necessarily make me want to come back.
Pretty good slice when you need a pizza fix.  I liked the ample sauce but the cheese was a bit too chewy and the dough was dry.

This review is for the infamous spicy pepperoni pizza! I came here about a month ago and it was worth the wait. Waited about 30 minutes. The line was out the door! It was slightly raining, a little thunder and the line did not waiver one bit. We ordered a whole pizza. There is no pricing discount for a whole pizza versus a slice of pizza. We asked for 8 slices I think it was about $31 for it. I could totally be wrong on that price. I was just hungry and overwhelmed by the smell of this place. There is no seating it's for eating the pizza and going. It is just a small counter lined on the wall. Which is perfect, the pizza taste AMAZING fresh. It still is great after about 40 minutes, but nothing beats fresh pizza. The pepperoni is baked into nice crisp edges. They place a good amount of pepperoni on each square so you will get a pepperoni in every bite. The pepperoni has a nice little spice to it. The bread is thick and fluffy like a focaccia bread. I normally don't like too much bread but this was perfect! I particularly didn't like the corner pieces because that was too much bread, but my sister loved it because of the crispy. So it's a win-win for both of us. The pieces are pretty big. I was only able to eat about 1.5 slices and was stuffed. I'm also kind of a small person so 2 would be a good amount for an average person. As I was waiting for my pizza someone asked if I called ahead for the pizza. So maybe you can call ahead and order a whole pizza? But don't take my word for it. But if you plan to get a whole pizza it doesn't hurt to call ahead and try. Could potentially save you a 40 minute wait!

Food was okay, drinks were good...but our service was wayyyy off! Our waitress Kate was horrible...For a party of 6 on a Friday night, you should already know...we didn't come to play! Waited too long just to order more drinks...Had to flag down another waiter to assist...Kate got my order wrong then tried to convince me to switch plates with my friend since she had what I originally asked for...who does that?!? Place is nice inside, food was ok and on the expensive side, but I wasn't impressed. Nope

I'm not new to the Los tacos1 family so when I saw this Tribeca location open up I was ecstatic. The flavors are consistent across locations. Good flavors, quick and efficient service. Had 3 chicken tacos this visit con todo and enjoyed veery bite. The horrachata is always a win for me. Very refreshing.

Good but food was not rememberable.Dropped in to check out this highly rated spot. It's a couple of blocks from village square pizza and Tompkins square. Run by a nice guy.Ended up getting the pesto knots, an Italian sausage white slice and a meatball parm slice. The Italian sausage slice was the winner but neither slice was something I would go out of my way to get again. The pesto knots were decent but would have used more cheese.

Dropped in to Market Table for a work lunch. Had some great eats (the burger was amazing), but dessert definitely stole the show. The deconstructed Smore with chocolate ice cream is basically a must.Just note, if you're pressed for time, this might not be the best spot. Our apps came relatively quick, but the entrees and especially dessert took a very long time. We did have a few mishaps with orders being brought out incorrectly or an app being forgotten, but the staff was accommodating to fix the issue for our large group. Every plate was clean so guessing everyone enjoyed their lunch as much as I did!

I'm completely smitten with this charming gem of a restaurant! For anyone craving an alternative to New York-style pizza, look no further. Their piadine are a revelation—crisp, warm, and brimming with flavor. Every bite reflects the high-quality ingredients they use; they're satisfying and wholesome, setting a new standard for what I thought was possible in a quick meal.

The menu is wonderfully accommodating. If you're not a fan of cheese, they've got you covered with cheese-free options or the flexibility to customize to your heart’s content. Vegetarians rejoice, as there's an abundance of choices here for you too, featuring garden delights like juicy tomatoes, aromatic arugula, succulent eggplant, vibrant peppers, and sweet, caramelized onions. This place is a must-visit for anyone who values taste and quality.

What a great place. Eat drink and be marry! I really don't have any other way to describe this. It's like Spain in NY. The variety of liquor the have is insane and of the highest quality. They h e a whole menu just for gin and tonic variations. We had 4 of them all where great and reasonably priced. You can order food from other spots to bring over or sit in the shared areas, but some spots will require eating at their location. This bar is so much fun and the bartender, Lee really knows his craft. We were entertained and our pallet was enthused as well!! We sure are coming back!!

Cute spot if you get seating in their garden area! Cool that they have their menu on tablets.My friend and I shared the pesto Vongole dish and a pizza. The pasta was a nice change because you don't usually see pesto paired with clams, shrimp, and general seafood. It was good, but nothing to write home about. The pizza was very very thin. Not what I expected, but still enjoyable to eat. It was nice so it wouldn't weigh you down too much after eating a few slices

First time going to an Olive Garden. Not bad service we got seated on the ground floor right away no wait although it was pretty busy. Bathrooms was a whole two floor travel, good thing for elevators!! Waitress kept checking up on us and was really nice, even offered to take a picture of us! Menu was not as big as I was expecting, I was looking for the rest of it but it was only 1 page of mostly just their popular dishes and they have no salad other than the home salad, which apparently came with my meal of fettuccine alfredo. Salad was actually good and it was served in a big bowl def a two person salad!! Our food did not take too long to come out neither but our mozzarella sticks came out first. Got raspberry lemonade and had free refills, she refilled mine without me having to ask which was thoughtful! I'm not dying to go again but if it's around and I'm looking to eat out I'd come back.

My absolute fav freaking chain restaurant. Holy crap I cannot rave about this place enough. Mr. Luke, wherever you are, God bless you. I love the food here. Some might say I am addicted. I say I have a deep appreciation for delicious and quick seafood. My favorite item has to be the lobster truffle roll. It's just ridiculously good. Mind blowing. My most frequent order is the shrimp roll because 1. It's the second best tasting thing there and 2. I'm broke af and can't afford $20+ lobster rolls all the time lol. I've tried everything at Luke's. All recommended but the winter items just hit different man. Get em while they're still out. Anyway enough of me gushing over this place. The food is amazing, the overall brand is awesome (can't beat sustainability) and Luke's Lobster just makes me all warm and happy.

I really like the decor and ambiance of this restaurant . Hostess was welcoming and the two servers/bartenders were very attentive. They have a fresh guacamole station behind the bar but I came in for a quick work lunch so I didn't have time to sample that. I ordered the wings appetizer and street corn appetizer . Everything came out flavorful, hot and quickly . They have a wall of hot sauces and I don't think I would be exaggerating if I said there was a 100 to try from. I will definitely come back when I have more time to sample their vast tequila bar. Hostess welcoming... service good.... food very good ... and a full bar... I will be back!

Title: Decent Italian Fare in Manhattan

If you find yourself in Manhattan and in need of a satisfactory Italian meal without much fuss, this restaurant might just fit the bill. It's not going to top the list of the best Italian eateries in the city, but it certainly provides a good meal at a fair price. During my visit for lunch, the service was commendable, attentive and swift, which made the experience with a friend and my daughter quite pleasant. The crowd seemed to be predominantly business professionals, which gave the place a bustling, workday vibe. In short, it's a solid choice for a no-frills lunch or dinner if you're nearby.

Title: A Mixed Bag at 21 Shanghai House

My visit to 21 Shanghai House, amidst the myriad of Shanghainese options in Chinatown, was influenced by its favorable Yelp reviews. With a diverse menu and reasonable prices – think $11 for fried noodles and $6 for steamed buns – I anticipated a wallet-friendly, authentic experience.

However, the presence of non-traditional dishes like Kung Pao Chicken gave away the establishment's broader approach, with less focus on authenticity. The Shanghainese Fried Noodles, albeit untraditional with its shrimp, were a seafood lover’s delight but strayed from the classic rendition. The steamed buns were a letdown, with their disproportionately thick skins, yet the flavors on the whole were pleasantly savoury and enjoyable.

Service was a mixed experience. The gentleman, perhaps the owner, was affable and welcoming. In contrast, the waitress came across as overly eager, interrupting our menu perusal with suggestions and checking on payment multifarious times, which imparted a sense of being rushed.

While the food at 21 Shanghai House was tasty, the authenticity and dining experience left room for improvement.

Despite my initial skepticism due to the tourist-driven reputation of Little Italy, my experience at this corner block Italian gem was surprisingly delightful. Enticed by a visitor's craving for authentic Italian cuisine, I indulged in a $42 red sauce seafood platter featuring half a lobster nestled atop perfectly al dente linguini. The sauce, contrary to my usual predilection for garlic oil or creamy sauces, was a revelation—sweet, mild, and flawlessly enhancing the fresh seafood.

The service shone with excellence and friendliness, elevating the meal even further. Alongside the main dish, I sampled the homemade burrata, which, while creamy and fresh, fell short of perfection due to its chilly serving temperature, diminishing the cheese's rich flavor that's best enjoyed at room temperature.

The ambiance struck a chord with authentic Italian charm, boasting lovely views and a decor that transported diners to a past era. This unexpected culinary discovery will undoubtedly become my preferred choice when I next find myself in the neighborhood.

Title: Great Burgers and Deals at 5 Napkin Burger 

I've become a regular at the 5 Napkin Burger near Union Square, drawn in by the laid-back vibe and the perfect spot for post-work gatherings. The burgers don't disappoint; the brunch and truffle options are standouts with their delightfully runny eggs topping perfectly cooked patties – just be prepared for a delicious mess.

Happy hour is a must-try, available on weekdays 4-7PM and a late-night session from 10PM-close. With $1 wings, $3 sliders, and $5 drinks, it's an affordable way to enjoy good food and drinks. The wings and sliders are surprisingly good and become even better with their beer specials.

A pro tip: sign up for their loyalty program. It's a treasure trove of deals like BOGO burger specials and freebies that make every visit a steal. Whether for the solid burgers or the incredible deals, 5 Napkin Burger is well worth the visit.

Highly recommend trying this place if you're a fan of sushi. We got here at 7pm on Tues night and waited 1.5 hours, but the second the actual sushi came around, I knew it was worth it. The warm rice, the sweet and tasty fish, the extreme attention to detail was greatly appreciated. Salmon with sesame seeds was unlike any other I've had. Super top quality fish. The $40 "trust me" omakase is definitely the way to go. Perfect amount of food, it comes with several sashimi dishes and some hand rolls, and gives you a taste of everything. We paired it with two bottles of $11 sake and had a great night. Only weird thing was that the edammame and some of the seafood within the hand rolls was cold. Other than that, everything (including service) was grade A perfect. I think they are a "tip included" establishment which is nice.

Good ol' Danny Meyer's done it again. I'm consistently impressed by how he manages to create an environment that exudes high end hospitality without feeling pretentious. At Manhatta you can actually pick between two different vibes. On one end of the floor is the open-air dining room. Here is where most patrons will come to enjoy a meal. I observed servers attentively waiting on patrons, who were mostly dressed up for what looked to be special occasion celebratory meals.I just came to grab a quick drink and take in the views so I got a cocktail from the bar and walked over to the other end of the floor. This is the part of Manhatta I was pleasantly surpised by. At the other end of the floor you'll find a spacious lounge area, replete with a ping pong table, games, and couches. There are servers casually milling around without hovering, so you can truly relax, enjoy your drink, and take in the views without feeling pressured to end your stay preemptively. I timed my visit to the sunset, and the candy colored sky setting over the buildings on a chill weeknight is just how I needed to end the week. The cocktails here are excellent.

When I told my awesome Indonesian Yelper, James. T., that I never had this type of cuisine before, he helped search one closest to me. I had it bookmarked and promised him that I would give it a try. Since I've tried many other Southeast cuisines. I was very curious to see how Indonesian food would be different from all the rest. I knew before coming here that the place would be tiny, as are most cool eateries in this area. We were lucky to grab some stools by the window. The menu is posted on the wall with colorful photos. Since I don't visit NYC that much, we decided to order all the appetizers on the menu. Might as well, right? For the main entree, I chose the Rendang Sapi (beef) because of the delicious photos posted on Yelp. All the apps came out at once. Even though they were being served in these sturdy cardboard containers, it was beautiful plated. Colorful and appetizing is how I would describe it. We all enjoyed the flavors and were wowed by the dipping sauces and exotic little picked salads on the side. My Rendang Sapi was absolutely delicious. The beef retained its juices and tenderness, reminds me of a beef stew but without the veggies. So happy that it was not dry. Loved all the accompaniments that came with. The curries and spices used seem more mild and tropical to me.On a last note: Service was excellent and the cashier helped answer our questions. They give the cutest plastic utensils. I should have taken them home with me. I want to thank my Yelp friend for helping me find this gem.

Tucked away near the bustling Times Square, the location of this restaurant is undeniably great, a beacon for those eager to dine in the heart of the city. Unfortunately, the dining experience does not match the allure of its setting. While the salad bar stands out as the highlight of the meal, offering a decent variety of fresh options, the rest of the fare is underwhelming.

The main dishes resemble something you might find in the freezer aisle, hastily microwaved rather than carefully prepared. The mozzarella sticks serve as a glaring example of this, evidently pre-frozen and lacking any homemade charm.

Considering the prices—which are on the higher end—it's disappointing that the quality doesn't rise to meet the cost. For those looking for a memorable meal, it may be wise to venture a few blocks further from the dazzle of Times Square, as there are likely far more satisfying options awaiting beyond this culinary cul-de-sac.

Title: A Culinary Triumph at Jeju Noodle Bar

Jeju Noodle Bar has quickly ascended to the ranks of my top dining spots with a menu that boasts an array of delectable Korean-inspired dishes. Securing a reservation can be a Herculean task, and walk-ins may face lengthy waits, but the culinary experience that awaits is a testament to the demand.

My latest foray as part of a quartet allowed an indulgent exploration of their offerings. We commenced with 'before noodles' appetizers that set a high bar for what was to come. The Jeju chicken wings, encased in flaky, crispy skin, dipped in savory Jeju sauce, are a crowd-pleaser. The Tuna Kimbap, elevating a humble classic to gourmet heights, was a delightful surprise.

The highlight of the starters is undeniably the Toro Ssam Bap – a dish that commands attention and is a staple order. Transitioning to main courses, the Gochu Ramyun caught my fancy with its subtle heat and echoes of spicy miso ramen, albeit a milder and less decadent option compared to its counterparts.

The So Ramyun remains a personal favorite, its velvety veal bone broth and raw brisket slices a hearty comfort, particularly during the chillier days. My companions' choices of Wagyu Ramyun and Truffle Bibim Myun did not disappoint either, the former being a luxurious albeit not unrivaled option, and the latter a creamy, truffle-infused wonder akin to an Italian carbonara.

Jeju Noodle Bar, with its contemporary twist on Korean staples and soul-warming ramyun, is an essential destination for food enthusiasts. Its offerings are both comforting and innovative, carving a unique niche that straddles familiar ramen and its own distinctive creations. My advice: book that reservation posthaste to secure your own taste of Jeju's culinary magic.

Title: A Mixed Bag with Stellar Service at Local Chinese Eatery

My recent dining experience was a delightful journey through traditional Chinese flavors with a few unexpected turns. The egg drop soup was a comforting starter, with the perfect consistency and a savory taste that set the stage for the meal to come. Both the crab and pork xiao long bao were exquisite, their delicate wrappers holding a rich, steaming broth that burst with flavor upon the first bite.

The green onion pancake, a last-minute addition to our table, was a surprising hit. Crispy edges gave way to a soft, chewy interior, fragrant with green onion and perfect for dipping in the accompanying sauce.

On a less positive note, the dan dan mien, while adequate, left something to be desired for a palate accustomed to the Sichuan-style, peanut-laden version of the dish. However, it was the pastrami roll that fell flat, puzzlingly reminiscent of bananas and unanimously rejected by our table for not meeting the expectations of its name.

Despite this culinary hiccup, the staff responded with commendable promptness and professionalism, promptly removing the unsatisfactory dish from our bill and bringing more of the much-enjoyed green onion pancakes.

The restaurant itself boasts ample seating, ideal for large groups, and an ambiance that feels authentically Chinese. While not every dish was a winner, the overall quality of the food and the attentive service will bring us back for another round of their hits.

Good food, got the sampler of everything which was a lot of food from dips to meats. The dips were great and I seriously could have been full from it. The different variety of meats were also good, at this point kind it reminds me of Brazilian style restaurant, where there was too much meat in front of you and it was intimidating. I really like the thin crepe-like bread. Perfect for a wrap around the meats and veggies. Overall, good atmosphere, good food and nice place to brings guests for something good.

I adore this place! What an authentic, sumptuous Thai experience. Off-the-charts flavorful is the theme of the food here. My new Thai go-to. From the decor to the pillows to the tin-roofed walls, it's like you've stumbled through a Thai jungle and discovered a little food shack.The two must-gets:- the honey pork sliders WHAT IN THE WORLD thick slabs of honeyed pork sandwiched by a fresh, warm bun and arugula, one of the best bites in New York- the hobo noodles which scream basil in such a flavorful, addictive, refreshing wayThe other dishes - the delicate shrimp steamed dumplings and the pad Thai - were all delicious too, especially the dumplings. But the pork sliders and hobo noodles are so outstanding. Thanks to Keny for serving us excellent food and kindness and solid suggestions. See you again soon!5 stars!!!!!

Jazz brunch in Harlem!Great music, great food, fair prices. Minton's rocks. (It's actually Jazz, not Rock, but "Jazzes" wouldn't convey the same excitement. It would be confusing. So we'll go with "Minton's rocks").Sunday brunch: you have to give your card to reserve the seats, but you Don't pay to get in (they'll bang you $75 bucks if you don't show, though). VERY reasonable prices, I got steak and eggs for $26 bucks. And it was no small steak, it was a good 12 oz. Cooked just right, tender and juicy. The vegetable empanadas were a real treat (make sure to ask for the cilantro/green tomato sauce), and the veggie burger is reportedly excellent.  The prix fixe menu looked equally enjoyable and affordable. My only criticism: Dear Management, what's with the coffee? This is New York City, we take our coffee seriously around here. It's brunch, get the coffee in front of me fast and bring the pot around frequent. The coffee was good and strong, but I was seated 20 minutes before the first cup showed up. Tip #2, when you bring the coffee and the sugar, bring the milk too. It was missing from every coffee service I saw. #3, when somebody asks for milk, bring it. I didn't get any until the 3rd cup. The servers are all nice as pie but I didn't see a lot of hustle. Ok, enough about that. I loved everything on the plate and I didn't have to eat again for a long time. The music! The Dennis Hernandez Trio played fun, exciting, brilliant Cuban jazz. They definitely met the calibre of performance you expect at Minton's. (Fun fact, Minton's was founded in 1938 and played a pivotal role in the development of bebop.) Everybody who's anybody has played there. Here's their Wikipedia page:  en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/…And what a beautiful place. Comfortable seating, very elegant, fun art on the wall behind the stage (see the pictures). You CAN NOT beat the value and the experience at Minton's. Bring your friends, they will hail you as a cool in-the-know New Yorker. DON'T bring a first date: you'll have nowhere to go but down after that. Five out of five stars! I will be back.

While this by Chloe doesn't really differ from the others, it is close to my office, and so I paid it a visit recently. The quinoa taco salad is probably the best thing you can get here, followed by the guac burger. I also love the pesto pasta!Edit: salted caramel CHILL push pop with banana walnut bread was excellent.

Walking in, I already like the decor and layout of the restaurant. Everything seems clean, bright, and new. The bathroom is clean as well.I ordered the rice noodle soup with spicy sauce. All the rice noodles came with the same basic ingredients, including two slices of pork, corn, ham, mushroom etc. You also have the option to add extra protein for an additional $2.99. I chose seafood as my extra. The seafood include imitation crabs, 2 shrimps (with shells) and two mussels. The shrimps and mussels tasted fresh. The flavoring of the soup is good as well and not too salty. In terms of spiciness, it has a good kick to it, especially because the pot enhanced the temperature. The rice noodles were cooked to the right amount of softness. I was afraid it would be too mushy if left in the pot, but that wasn't the case. Overall, I am happy with the food here and would definitely come back to try other things they have on the menu.

I missed their old location by Bryant park, seems they downsized and put forward less quality. so I ordered a honey turkey wrap and a marble cheesecake brownie. the meat was moist and okay, paper thin tomato's and some lettuce, really could used a dressing or a condiment, tasted rather plain for the price it was. the brownie, well tasted slightly dried out, would be nice it was more fudgy. people their working their were nice enough as far as service.

During my recent visit to this cozy little spot with inviting outdoor seating, I had the pleasure of biting into their Hero Signature Burger, and it's a bite I won't forget anytime soon. The burger, a generous, perfectly-cooked 6 oz. patty made from 100% all-natural Canadian Angus beef, was succulent and bursting with flavor. The hero sauce, coupled with the delicate sharpness of thinly sliced onions and the tang of relish, tied together all the flavors in a delightful package, all nestled within a toasted sesame poppy seed bun that added an extra oomph to the texture.

The service here? Spotless and noticeably quick, making it perfect for a satisfying, rushed lunch without compromising the quality of the food. While the fries were fairly standard (though by no means a letdown), the next visit has me fixated on trying a specialty burger and diving fork-first into their poutine.

For an additional $4, making it a meal with fries and a soda is the way to go. I'm already planning my next trip back!

Title: A Cozy Slice of Greece with Exquisite Flavors

From the moment you step inside, the restaurant's ambiance sweeps you away to the Mediterranean with its charming Greek atmosphere, complemented by an equally friendly wait staff. The seating arrangement, albeit tight and not the most comfortable, is a small compromise for the delightful dining experience that awaits.

Our culinary adventure began with a generously-sized salad that was perfect for sharing, followed by an octopus dish that impressed us with its tenderness – the two pieces provided were cooked to perfection. We also enjoyed a selection of skewers, which, while on the smaller side, were packed with flavor and ideal for tasting multiple varieties.

In summary, the authentic taste and presentation of the dishes more than made up for any discomfort caused by the seating. A recommended destination for anyone looking to indulge in exceptional Greek cuisine.

Title: First Time Delight at a Charming Spot

I ventured into this stylish eatery on a bustling Friday evening, enchanted by the decor upon entry. Seizing the chance for a pre-dinner treat, I savored the happy hour, where the cucumber mint smash proved to be a sublime, palate-cleansing cocktail, matched in delight by the vivid mango Habanero. The service at the bar was swift and attentive.

Despite my early arrival for a 6:15 pm reservation, the staff accommodated me with grace, seating me promptly at 6:10 pm. The hospitality was warm, and the energy was high; our server greeted us almost instantly, a testament to the exceptional service.

The salad bar was a cornucopia of fresh and flavorful choices. As for the main attraction – the meats – they were mostly exquisite. The bacon-wrapped filet, picana, garlic sirloin, and lamb were all standout dishes, succulent and well-seasoned. The pork rib fell slightly short on flavor but was tender nonetheless. My only gripe was the elusive beef ribs and a particular server who seemed to overlook our table despite the 'green side up' signal, slightly marring an otherwise impeccable meal.

Determined not to let that hiccup spoil the evening, I left satisfied and eager to return. A solid 4 stars for this promising establishment.

Title: Hidden Gem for Pizza Lovers!

I recently discovered a fantastic pizza spot that I'm kicking myself for not trying sooner! This family-owned gem offers a remarkable experience, blending a cool vibe with scrumptious pizza. Their claim to fame is their super thin crust, though they also serve a satisfyingly thicker option to please all palates.

The dining area is quaint with a small bar, exuding a warm, homey atmosphere complemented by friendly service. Adjacent to the main restaurant, there's a convenient takeout section offering slices, whole pies, or a tempting selection of gelato—perfect for those on the go.

During my visit, the dinner was delightful, with a succinct yet comprehensive menu that seems to offer endless options. This place has definitely won a spot on my go-to list for future cravings. Highly recommend you give it a try!

Title: A Disappointing Visit to a Once-Favorite Spot

I recently visited a restaurant I've been praising for years, particularly for their fantastic wings, expecting to have a relaxing evening with my coworker. Unfortunately, this experience left me regretting my recommendations. Our order included a variety of dishes and drinks, but the magic just wasn't there this time.

The food arrived lukewarm, a stark contrast to the piping hot meals I was accustomed to. The much-anticipated wings, which I've enjoyed for 2-4 years, were a letdown – soggy and seemingly reheated. Even the pizza disappointed with excessive cheese and a limp crust, although I acknowledge not specifying my preference for a crispier base.

The fish tacos were another low point, barely making an impression with their lackluster flavor and airiness; they ended up in the trash soon after I got home. My coworker, whom I'd been trying to impress with this place, politely claimed to enjoy the meal, but their actions—or lack of enthusiasm—spoke otherwise.

To top off the night, the music selection from the DJ was less than stellar, failing to enhance the already dreary atmosphere. This visit has definitely made me reconsider my patronage, and despite the possibility that it was just an off night, I'll be taking a break from this establishment that’s now lost its luster and is, frankly, out of my way.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Authentic Thai Cuisine

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a local Thai spot that came highly recommended on Yelp, and I must say, it lived up to the hype. Even on a bustling Sunday evening, the cozy and often-crowded atmosphere lent itself to an authentic dining experience that suggested advance reservations might be wise.

My boyfriend and I began with the crispy shrimp rolls, each boasting its unique dipping sauce – a touch that truly set them apart as 'slammin'’. The papaya salad followed, fresh and crunchy, though a tad heavy on the dressing for my liking - yet undeniably tasty.

The main event, my seafood pad cha, was a symphony of mussels, scallops, shrimp, and calamari, served steaming hot. Opting for medium spice, it hit just the right note of flavor without overwhelming heat. 

To top it off, a Thai iced tea at a dollar off, just by checking in, was the cherry on top of a delightful dining experience. This place is a must-visit for anyone craving genuine 'home cooked' Thai fare.

Title: A Delightful Japanese Dining Experience

My dining companion and I recently visited this gem of a Japanese restaurant, and we left thoroughly impressed. We initially came with sushi cravings, which were wonderfully satisfied with an array of fresh, skillfully prepared selections. Our eyes couldn't help but wander to the hibachi station where chefs worked their magic, a spectacle that promised another culinary delight for a future visit.

The service was a high point: staff members were both friendly and efficient, striking the perfect balance of attentiveness without being intrusive. An added perk was the comfortable environment, as the restaurant managed to maintain a relaxed atmosphere without the overcrowded feel that plagues many establishments on a Sunday evening. We were seated promptly upon arrival, no waiting time was a pleasant surprise.

In summary, if you're in the mood for authentic Japanese fare with sterling service, this spot shouldn’t be missed.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Fusion Feast

I recently dined at this establishment with a large group which allowed me to sample a wide array of dishes; however, I must admit that my experience fell short of expectations. The Goan sunrise cocktail started the meal on a mediocre note, lacking the punch of flavor I anticipated. The Raw mango culture had a saving grace in its fried bread accompaniment, which I did enjoy.

The main courses presented a rollercoaster of quality. The Rasam ramen and pulled jackfruit tacos were just passable - nothing to write home about. Luckily, the spare ribs, curried lentils, and maitake mushrooms each hit the mark with rich and satisfying flavors.

A standout was the Chicken tikka, which was the culinary highlight of the evening. Side dishes like garlic naan and basmati rice were good, dependable selections, but did not particularly wow.

Desserts proved to be a bit of a letdown. While the dessert pancake was pleasing enough, the bread pudding sadly missed the mark due to an excessively moist texture.

Service inconsistencies further marred the dining experience. Prompt attention seemed to elude us, as we found ourselves waiting longer than preferred for necessities.

Despite the few dishes that I found great, I'm inclined to believe that I would have a more delightful dining experience at other establishments, such as Drunken Munkey. Hence, I'm hesitant to recommend a return visit. A fair assessment, reflecting this mixed experience, would be 3.5 stars.

Title: A Delightful Surprise at Laut Singapura

After escaping the bustling scene at No No No, my friend and I serendipitously stumbled upon Laut Singapura, a gem for Malaysian/Singaporean cuisine that I hadn't anticipated much from. To my delight, the experience earned a resounding five-star review.

From the outset, it was the little details that charmed us – the novel presentation of a hand towel in a miniature bathtub and the attentiveness of the servers who were eager to keep our glasses filled and our dining experience seamless.

The culinary journey began with crispy chicken wings – a revelation in texture and taste, with a perfectly balanced batter that created a symphony of sticky, sweet, and spicy notes that had me licking my fingers in appreciation.

The standout dish, Nasi Lemak, was a cornucopia of flavors and textures. Each component, from the aromatic coconut rice to the crunchy anchovies and peanuts, harmonized to create an unforgettable meal. The beef rendang was notably saucy with the right amount of heat, while the sambal shrimp left me craving more. An unexpected delight was the fried egg, which oozed with a runny yolk that made for the ultimate indulgence.

While the dessert menu didn't entice us, the satisfaction from the meal itself left no room for regret. Laut Singapura went above and beyond, securing a top spot on my list of culinary adventures, and I eagerly anticipate my next visit, perhaps to try their sister restaurant, Laut.

Be careful sitting outside. There was something dripping on us so we quickly moved inside and they were accommodating. It was a much better experience. The lighting is a bit dim so good for romantic dates. The spaghetti lobster was really good but a bit pricey. There is also quite a bit of butter in it. Overall good place to go once in a while

Title: A Hidden Gem in the LES: Floret

I recently dined at Floret, an enchanting restaurant nestled away in the Lower East Side, and the experience was nothing short of delightful. Despite the hustle and bustle of the surrounding streets, Floret offers a tranquil escape with its serene patio and garden, exuding the charm of a bygone era.

On a Wednesday evening, my companion and I were greeted with an irresistibly cozy ambiance that set the stage for a memorable meal. We commenced our culinary journey with the Peekytoe crab cocktail, which was a lovely mixture of tomato sauce, lime, corn, and generous crab chunks. It was pleasing but paled in comparison to the beet tartare that followed. The roasted sweet beets paired with sour cream and trout roe atop a fennel cracker were incredibly refreshing, the fish roe adding a delightful pop of salty crunch to the dish.

The star of the night, however, was the seared scallops entrée. Each scallop, oceanic and perfectly seared, was accompanied by heirloom carrots and citrus fruits, creating a harmony of flavors that were both surprising and familiar. It's daringly unique and easily my new favorite in the city.

Our adventure continued with the Bavette steak, served medium rare with an assortment of tomatoes, roasted eggplant, and stracciatella. As a steak enthusiast, I enjoyed the dish but found myself favoring the scallops even more.

To end our meal on a sweet note, we indulged in the chocolate budino— a layered spectacle of creamy lightness and rich chocolate ganache. It was a revelation in every spoonful.

I wholeheartedly recommend Floret for not only the delectable seared scallops and mesmerizing chocolate budino but also for the overall experience that makes it a must-visit. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Tempted by my colleague's weekly praises and the tantalizing aroma of her vegetarian General Tso's Chicken, I finally visited the bustling, Kosher-friendly hub she couldn't stop talking about. Despite the crowd, predominantly non-Asian, the vibe was welcoming. I zeroed in on the famed dish, reasonably priced at $14.95—and splurged on the $2 brown rice.

The vegetarian General Tso's Chicken was almost magical; I was hard-pressed to find a difference from its meaty counterpart. It was a hearty dish and lived up to its promise of serving 2-4 people. The flavors were so well-crafted that I, a non-vegetarian, was doubting the lack of meat in every bite. However, a pro tip: to fully enjoy its crispy excellence, eat it fresh; while still enjoyable, the leftovers lost their crunch.

I'm already planning my next visit, with the $7.50 lunch special firmly in my sights. This restaurant has won me over, and I'm keen to dive deeper into their menu.

I recently dined at a local restaurant renowned for its Kunming beef noodle soup. While it may not claim the top spot in the village, the beef was notably tender, making the dish stand out among many other establishments. In addition to the soup, I indulged in the mouthwatering chicken. Despite its mini portion, the flavor delivered, leaving me craving more.

The street potato was another dish that satisfied my palate with its good flavor. However, not all that glisters is gold, as the wontons in chili oil proved to be a letdown. The thick skin and flavorless stuffing were disappointing, and the lack of spice was surprising given the dish's name.

Thankfully, the homemade spicy sauce came to the rescue; it was genuinely spicy and enhanced everything I ate. On a curious note, I tried the Mu Gua shui, expecting a papaya-like taste, only to discover it was quite different, but pleasant nonetheless. Overall, the hits outweighed the misses at this establishment, and their spicy sauce might just be their secret weapon.

Title: Gastronomic Delight at a Bustling Hotspot

My recent dining experience at this vibrant eatery left an indelible mark on my palate. The culinary prowess was evident with each dish that emerged from the kitchen. The burgers boasted a perfect sear, juicy in every bite, while the wings were a delightful balance of crispy and saucy. The meatballs were a tender, flavor-packed highlight, and the cheese curds – oh, the cheese curds – were a melt-in-your-mouth revelation. 

Paired with an impressive drinks menu, we found ourselves relishing in the flavors over several rounds of refreshments. Whether you're here to quench your thirst or satisfy a hearty appetite, this spot promises to deliver on all fronts. An absolute must-visit for anyone craving comfort classics executed to perfection.

If it is not obvious by now, my favorite fried chicken is most definitely delicious, perfectly crunchy, light crisp Korean Fried Chicken.I am so delighted to discover Koko in the East Village. They are also on the Upper Westside. We ordered the drums, half spicy & half soy garlic. Both were very, very good and hit the spot, with sides of kimchi and radish to compliment the spice factor and crunchy chicken.Very friendly staff, owner.  Cozy minimal decor with cute chicken posters on the walls, plus good music playing in the background.Koko is known for being the "Best Korean Fried Chicken with Soul" and I agree. Koko also serves Bulgogi Bibimbap, Seafood pancakes, Gun Mandu (Dumplings), Parmesan Fries, Sweet potato fries, Crispy Garlic fries, Soon Tofu Udon, etc amongst other things which we've yet to try. Yes, of course, I will be back. Yum! **  delivery + take-out available *****Open Tuesday - Thursday 12:30 - 10:30, Friday - Saturday 12:30 until  11pm,  Sunday until 10pm, Closed on Mondays ******Various Soju, Beers, and soft drinks available ***

Title: A Bustling Lunch Experience at Mian Kitchen

Nestled in the heart of urbanspace, Mian Kitchen proved to be a hotspot during a busy Wednesday lunch rush. Despite the lengthy queue, the service was impressively swift. The menu offered a tempting array of noodle dishes, bao, rice bowls, and the option to pair with a tea for a perfect combo meal.

I decided to go with the crowd favorite, the Dan Dan noodle bowl. For those who favor a fiery kick, the restaurant accommodates spice adjustments to your liking. Within a mere 5 to 8 minutes, I was presented with a sizable, vibrant bowl of perfectly cooked noodles, mouthwatering minced pork drenched in chili oil, and a perfectly soft boiled egg to top it off.

The dish was mostly a hit, except for the unconventional salad topping - a mix of corn, carrots, and kale. While these fresh components are enjoyable on their own, their overwhelming presence on the Asian-inspired noodle bowl felt misplaced, particularly the corn. Nevertheless, the overall experience was delightful, rooted in the rich flavors and generous portions that Mian Kitchen has to offer.

Cute, tropical-looking, and spacious setting adds to the attraction of this place as the real star is the pho. My first and so far favorite pho is the spicy short rib pho. I really wanted to try that with the crazy rich broth and they were generous enough to accommodate the request. The result was bliss- broth was so rich and smooth. The braised short rib was so easy to eat and so succulent. I also tried the beef balls pho with the standard broth and enjoyed that flavor as well. Depends what intensity and complexity you're in the mood for when looking for a noodle soup. Also shared a platter of three items: fried spring rolls and the chili shrimp (both from the appetizers section) and the grilled lemongrass pork chop over vermicelli noodles. Normally grilled pork with rice is my go-to in Vietnamese restaurants because I never thought the pho was any good (in the NYC area). The kitchen here just completely changed the game simply by being authentic and doing it right. Anyone who knows me knows I appreciate noodle soups but it's almost never my first choice in any cuisine. I do have exceptions and now I can't stop thinking about how mouth-watering the pho here is- best pho in town!

Title: A Delightful Surprise at Antalia in NYC

During a recent trip back to Jersey, we chanced upon Antalia Mediterranean and Turkish restaurant, thanks to a street-corner sign that caught our attention. What a serendipitous find! This gem offers an extensive selection of Mediterranean and Turkish dishes, catering to a wide range of palates.

The food impressed with its deliciousness, showcasing an abundance of fresh, roasted vegetables—tomatoes, green peppers, mixed greens, zucchini, onions, and shredded beets, all of which were a feast both for the eyes and the taste buds. Presentation was top-notch, earning a solid five stars.

Service at Antalia was commendable, our waiter exuded friendliness and politeness, and the overall staff professionalism contributed to the dining experience. The restaurant's cleanliness paired with the perfect ambience made our meal even more enjoyable.

Whether you're in NYC for a visit or just passing through, I wholeheartedly recommend Antalia for a fantastic dining experience that's sure to leave a great impression.

Almond is like a bougie "wait in line for an hour and only be seated when your entire party has arrived" brunch place without actually being bougie. Highlights: Ricotta Pancakes, Hash Our Way, and Fried Rice. It was easy to get a reservation for a prime Saturday brunch time (noon) and we were seated even though one of our friends was running a tad bit late. The restaurant is quite spacious for its location, and if you're a party of 2, you can sit right up against the floor to ceiling windows (so bright!) They have plenty of table arrangements to accommodate large parties, including a big round table!! Quick digression: round tables are THE BEST for big parties and I'm always disappointed to be sat a loooong table whenever I'm in a larger party. It's like, I might as well say goodbye to 75% of my party for the next 1.5 hours because you know I'm only going to be able to talk to people in my immediate surrounding. Anyways, the menu looked incredible, and we decided to order 3 entrees and share amongst the 3 of us. Based on Yelp reviews, we knew we had to get the Ricotta Pancakes with lemon curd and oh boy, they did not disappoint. They were so fluffy with a beautiful char and the lemon curd was light and tart. The Hash Our Way immediately caught our eye on the menu because how can you say no to duck confit?? There were also generous pieces of duck YUM. The Fried Rice was delicious and is reminiscent of a Kimchi Fried Rice, for all you Korean food lovers out there. The grilled baby turnips was a wonderful addition and added to the variety of textures in the dish.I think I found a new go-to brunch place. Not only does the whole reservation system make it very encouraging to return, but the spaciousness and the inviting decor make it a crowd pleaser as well. And of course the food. Next time I would love to try the Brussels Sprouts Hot and Cold, the House made brioche french toast and chorizo omelette. Yes, I'll be back!!

Entering here I didn't really think I wanted any nuggets because that's not something I would actually be craving but I definitely changed my mind after getting home and heating up one of those bad boys. I wasn't expecting a very good well seasoned tender no rib all white meat nugget to wake up my taste buds or for me to write home (yelp) about it. But here we are! It was that good. The lovely lady working the counter helped with my choice and the nuggets were just as good as the hand cut French fries. I choose the plain French fries but next time I'll probably try the old bay or jerk depending how hot it is. Will I come back? Hell yeah Ps I couldn't save any fries for the picture just know the picture does it no justice.

Loved this spot! First they offer this tastyAF pizza at the bar during happy hour. Delicious. Probably could have just ate there all night. My pasta was perfection. Loved my pappardelle and ragu! Oh my god it was delicate yet flavorful. Mmmm. So many tasty apps to share, great wine list and nice service! Will be back for sure!

Came for brunch, solid 3 stars. Food was okay. The crab cakes were very bland, had to put so much salt and pepper on them to be able to eat it. The drinks were good and strong, bottomless for 90 minutes as well! Our waiter checked in on us about once, the rest of the time we were waving him down to get us drinks and refill our waters, which is a pet peeve on mine

Have wanted to come here for a while but didn't want to show up without a reservation.  So this time was able to make a last minute reservation on Yelp. On  a Sunday evening around 6 the colorfully but dimly neon lit, long and narrow dining room is only full in the front section but by 7 pm it was completely filled.  We sat in the back room in a kind of booth seat with hard benches but quite comfortable (you want to avoid the table at the very end which is literally right next to the bathroom).  Other than that, the food - menu is not extensive - was good and pretty much met expectations. A couple of the noodle dishes were rather bland, but the three cup chicken was very tasty, so was the fried rice with Chinese sausage, popcorn shrimp, chili dumplings., and the Chinese spinach was one of the best.  Was curious as to what interesting Taiwanese dessert they might have but they don't offer any at all.  Overall a good restaurant with relatively reasonable prices.  Wouldn't mind returning to try some of the other dishes next time we are in NY.

Title: A Cozy Comeback for Ramen Lovers at Ramen Shack

It's a delight to welcome back Ramen Shack! Venturing in on a peaceful Sunday evening, the spot is inconspicuously nestled within Tomiz/Cafe Zaiya in Midtown, offering a quiet escape. The staff's warmth matched the swiftness of service, with our orders arriving promptly and presented with care.

We indulged in the Quiet Storm and the chicken ramen, both exquisitely prepared, though the intention to sample their coveted tsukemen was dashed by their limited 10 bowls-a-day policy. Alas, timing is key, as our 6:30 p.m. visit was too late to snag this exclusive dish.

While the ramen won us over with its umami-rich broth, charming the taste buds with every spoonful, the whole egg left a bit to be desired - a halved egg might better complement the dish's other elements. 

Ramen Shack has earned my recommendation for anyone seeking a bowl of soul-soothing ramen. Be sure to drop by while you can and perhaps arrive a tad earlier if you're pining for the tsukemen!

I was excited to come here and left underwhelmed. The place is full on a Sunday morning and has a lively vibe, so good thing I made a reservation. Got to a table rather quickly and the service was quite attentive throughout. We tried the fried chicken sandwich and the soba noodles. As somebody who orders a fried chicken sandwich more often than not, this one was just decent. The flavors and textures all blended together and nothing seemed to stand out. It's also quite a messy experience as it's piled high with a slaw that everything falls apart. The soba noodles lacked any flavor at all so you're essentially diving into a heavy carbs with little reward. Luckily the Bloody Mary was delicious and blended full of spice and flavor - that was the real highlight.

Wow! This place is awesome. Been awhile since I had some very good sushi. Note they do not take reservations.  We were table of 4 on a Monday night and the wait was about 30 mins. Food and service was fast and friendly. Got some sake and opted for the $42 trust me omakase. Really good and fresh. Must try!

Title: A Haven for Thin Crust Pizza Lovers

Stumbling upon this cozy spot after hours of exploring the neighborhood was a delightful twist to our day. Not only did it provide a much-needed escape from the relentless rain, but it also proved to be a culinary gem with its exceptional service and mouthwatering thin crust pizza. The crust was the perfect balance of crunchy and light, a true testament to the art of pizza making. Overall, it was a serendipitous find that left us both sheltered and satisfied. Highly recommended for anyone with a penchant for superb pizza.

Fantastic! Went at a time when they weren't busy with my buddy. He had the tofu bibimbap and I had the short rib chulpan. Both can with a pretty nice miso soup and a bunch of banchan. The pickled vegetables, tofu and kimchi were the best of the sides. Loved the chulpan. Short rib was perfect, nice amount of veggies. The rice was a little crunchy on the bottom which I actually liked! Will def come back, want to try the actual bbq!

Title: A Fusion Feast at a Bustling Asian Eatery

If you find yourself craving a medley of Asian flavors, this bustling fusion restaurant is a must-visit. Their soba noodles are exceptional, particularly the tempura soba, reasonably priced at $25, accompanied by a delightful side of tempura that perfectly complements the dish.

But the true stars here are the skewers, an array of choices from chicken to the more luxurious wagyu beef, along with pork and peppers. The limited salmon skewer is a standout, offering a succulent taste of the sea. Service is impressively swift, ensuring a seamless dining experience even on busy nights.

Pair your meal with one of their well-crafted Old Fashioneds, and you're in for a treat. And for a sweet finale, indulge in the Lady M Mille Crepe cakes, a dessert that satisfies with its delicate layers and creamy texture. This place is a culinary gem worth returning to.

I've been ordering delivery from this spot on several occasions and it's consistently delightful. The chicken soup is a standout – arguably one of the finest I've savored. Laden with generous portions of chicken, vegetables, and a perfectly seasoned broth, it's a dish we often indulge in on its own. Alongside the soup, their chicken fingers are a hit – crispy and flavorful. The Mac and cheese is another winner, oozing with creamy, cheesy goodness. The BBQ pork and brisket sandwich is another must-try; it's hearty and satisfying. However, I'd suggest passing on the onion tower, as it tends to be on the greasy side. Overall, I highly recommend opting for delivery from this gem!
The food and service was great. I enjoyed the braised lamb shank, chicken tikka, eggplant and potato curry, and a  nice bottle of Malbec.

I came here, since there is again a lot of hype around this place. I liked it, but again did not see what all the hype was about. I got the calamari black ink pasta. So much calamari, like overwhelming on the ratio. I preferred Supper over this restaurant. Also, I think it's a little bit bigger.

Title: Disappointing Dining Experience at Local Ramen Spot

I regret to inform fellow foodies that my recent visit to this ramen restaurant was less than satisfactory. First and foremost, the cleanliness left much to be desired, with house flies occupying the bar area and compromising the utensils' hygiene.

The spatial arrangement was another sore point, with seating so cramped it hampered movement and made service awkward for the hardworking waitstaff. The Spicy Ginger Stamina Ramen, which should have been the highlight, unfortunately fell flat, with an overly sweet broth that lacked the promised heat, and ingredients like noodles and pork that had a peculiar taste and didn't sit well at all.

The one redeeming feature was the attentiveness of the waiter, who remained diligent in his service, ensuring my water was always filled and providing extra napkins without prompt. However, this did little to compensate for the overall experience, especially when considering the average $20 price tag for a bowl of ramen that ultimately was not commensurate with the quality expected. My advice is to seek out other establishments for a more authentic and enjoyable ramen experience.

I recently celebrated a birthday brunch at Loring Place and the experience was truly enjoyable. The restaurant exudes a modern and chic vibe, with cool decor that adds to the ambience. Accommodating our party of seven, the service was prompt from the get-go, taking our drink orders immediately. 

The drink menu is impressive with innovative cocktails; a friend recommended the celery juice cocktail for a deceptively healthy kick, while the Bloody Mary received praise for its fresh, non-canned flavor. I opted for a Syrah which, despite the steeper price, was delicious.

For starters, the butternut squash fries were a standout, fried to perfection and masking their veggie origin. The brussel sprout pizza, with a goat cheese base, stole the show with its delightful combination of flavors. The tater tots, on the other hand, were a bit oily and more reminiscent of latkes than traditional tots, but forgivable given the challenge of homemade versions.

The main course offered a mix of brunch and lunch options. The burger, although good and flavorful, didn't quite live up to being the "best ever" as claimed, especially for its $24 price tag. The accompanying fries were a hit, boasting a perfect balance of crunch and softness. My wife's tomato eggs were equally satisfying, and the calzone came highly recommended by another diner.

Despite a few minor missteps with some dishes being a tad oily, Loring Place left a great impression. From the eclectic drinks to the quality service, it's a place I'd certainly visit again.

This was my first visit to Arturo's and I LOVED IT!! With its dim lighting and jazz music, this place seemed more like a nice dining spot than a pizza place, which is what I was looking for. They have a good wine selection, a pretty elaborate food menu and they do a half-and-half with the pizzas, which works pretty well with most groups. Even the bread they served was fresh and delicious! We tried the mussels in wine sauce and it went really well with the wine! The pizzas are good - not "out of the world amazing" but really good! I'm sure to visit again!

Title: A Surprisingly Delightful Visit to by Chloe

I recently stumbled upon by Chloe, a spacious and inviting vegan restaurant. Upon entering, I noticed their card-only policy—a minor inconvenience for some but a sign of modern convenience for others. The menu, exclusively plant-based, is concise enough to avoid overwhelm yet varied enough for a considered choice.

In the mood for a light snack rather than a full meal, I gravitated toward the bakery section. Although the selection leaned heavily towards chocolate-based items, which I wasn't in the mood for, I was pleasantly surprised to find a non-chocolate option—the red velvet cupcake.

Priced at around $5, the cupcake was modest in size, making it a perfect snack portion. The lack of excessive sweetness was a welcome departure from the usual cloying nature of similar treats. The portable box it was packaged in added a touch of whimsy to the experience.

While I hope to see more non-chocolate options in the future, it's worth mentioning that by Chloe also caters to canine companions with their puppy biscuits—a thoughtful touch for pet owners.

Overall, by Chloe is a charming spot for those seeking a delectable vegan treat without the guilt.

My go to place for vietnamese pho because of its taste, location, and price.Its a very low key place and it's always busy so dont expect the customer service over the top. However, the turnaround is still not bad so I kept going back.It's pho soup flavor is more flavorful than others that I've try and the portion is decent as well. It's just a bit sad/reality-punching thinking how the portion gets smaller and smaller while the price gets higher and higher over the past few years but well, it's part of life.Would still choose this as my most favorite Vietnamese restaurant with the high prices since other places have increased their prices a lot too.

Nestled beside Lincoln Center, this restaurant provided the perfect prelude and encore to our evening of artistic enjoyment. The culinary artistry on display was as compelling as our cultural outing, with a curated menu complemented by a stellar wine selection. The open dining room, complete with a view into the kitchen, added to our delight, offering transparency and a connection to the chefs at work.

Service was impeccable; the staff was knowledgeable and gracious, embodying the high standards one would expect from a place bearing Chef Boulud's name. While there are other Boulud establishments within arm's reach, this venue stood out for its fine dining experience. The ambiance struck the right balance between elegance and comfort, devoid of any pretentious overtones.

The menu was a well-rounded symphony of options, suitable for a variety of tastes. The portion sizes were perfect, breaking the all-too-common high-end dining trope of leaving diners wanting. My plate of quinoa-stuffed eggplant, adorned with pomegranate seeds, butternut squash, and pepitas, was a harmonious blend of flavors and textures. Although I had a hankering for a side salad, the server's suggestion of broccoli rabe as an accompaniment didn’t quite hit the mark, coming across a tad too salty and soft.

Despite no room for dessert, the overall experience left us satisfied and eager to return. A visit to this establishment ensures a gastronomic delight that complements the rich cultural tapestry of Lincoln Center, promising a well-rounded evening of sensory pleasures.

Title: A Xiao Long Bao Delight at Astor Place

I recently dined at a quaint spot near Astor Place, where the highlight was unquestionably the Xiao Long Bao. These delectable soup dumplings were masterfully prepared, with a rich and savory broth enclosed within. The accompanying pancake also proved to be a delightful treat, boasting a perfect blend of flavors.

However, I was less impressed by the sampler platter, which mainly featured steamed dumplings that didn't quite justify their place on the menu. While the restaurant's ambiance and location were decent, and accessibility wasn't an issue, the venue itself didn't draw a large crowd. The benefit of this, however, was the absence of long lines, ensuring a swift seating experience.

In conclusion, if you find yourself in the vicinity of Astor Place with a craving for Xiao Long Bao, this spot is worth a visit. As for the rest of the menu, I'll leave that to your personal judgment.

Title: Delightful Delivery from UES Gem

I recently decided to try delivery from a local spot in the Upper East Side and was thoroughly impressed. The prices were a refreshing surprise, offering a dinner for two at less than $25, which is quite a steal for the area. Our order included a Margherita pizza and a chicken parm sandwich. 

The pizza was the star of the show – incredibly fresh with a sauce that was nothing short of spectacular. While the chicken parm was enjoyable, it didn’t quite steal the show like the pizza did, and I am tempted to try different dishes in the future.

An added bonus was the delivery service; whether it's an in-house team or not, the delivery guy was exceptionally friendly and fast. This positive experience has certainly piqued my interest to delve deeper into their menu on subsequent orders.

Good. Despite what the other reviews say, sometimes you need to give people in life a chance. This restaurant was good during a quiet Sunday night which originally was a little off putting considering that busy restaurants are a good sign to most people. Since the restaurant wasn't busy, our party of four definitely benefitted from the great service and the kind manager.It was my first time having both hot pot and family style meals at the same time (food overload!) There was triple flash fried chicken, dumplings with chili oil, water simmered beef in hot chili oil, double stir fried pork, then of course the hot pot meals. We had a double broth of both sichuan hot chili flavored and regular chicken broth. We also had many glass noodles to share, tofu, fish balls and the list goes on! To finish this all we ended the meal with a desert soup: egg & black sesame ball soup. The reason I'm giving this place 4 stars is because the restaurant really does care and goes the extra distance to impress, however there may have been some logistical mishaps from previous visits by other Yelpers that shines the wrong light on this restaurant. Things the restaurant should change to improve: not charge for sauce, lower the prices on some entrees and staff more people during peak hours.Would return!

Great food. Quieter than expected, but Coronavirus precautions happening so cannot be a real judge of this restaurant. We got banana walnut bread & lemon ricotta pancakes to start. The bread was very warm & the cinnamon dipping sauce was amazing. The ricotta on the pancakes had lots of orange zest. The Chile empanadas were to die for. I wanted a second plate. The grilled cheese in tomato soup were also very delicious. Loved the presentation. We got bacon on the side since I'm vegetarian. The avocado toast had a nice pepper kick to it & the pizza with crispy eggplant was good as well.Def worth the price and not bad for the city & tapa style.

The ramen here is super filling, it's definitely worth to come here with an appetite especially since you can't take home leftovers. The atmosphere is more loud than Japan since people are more likely to chat here but it's a very similar vibe. There is self serve water stations near you and hooks to hang your jackets. Ramen: It comes with slices of pork and scallions. I usually add an egg since that usually completes the experience for me. If you have an appetite or friends get the premium yakibuta, the meat melts in your mouth and has a lot of flavor. I wouldn't recommend the topping set unless you're really hungry or like all the toppings included. Broth: I like getting medium dashi and light oil. Otherwise I feel the broth is too heavy with the rest of the flavors in the ramen. Original Spicy Red Sauce: The absolute best sauce. It clears your sinuses and amplifies the taste of the ramen.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Flavors, but Some Standouts

My friend and I recently dined here and had quite a varied experience. Although the tuna poke nachos didn't hit the mark for me due to an overly generous saucy topping, and the spicy kalbi bibimbap had an unexpectedly sweet twist that didn't quite work, there were definite highlights. The fried pork gyoza dumplings were a delight, with a crispy exterior giving way to succulent pork inside. The premium sirloin was cooked to perfection, showcasing the quality of the meat. Dessert was the real showstopper – a delightful s'mores concoction that ended the meal on a high note. The spicy tuna volcano was also worthy of a mention; it was a decent dish that added to the meal. Overall, the experience was enjoyable, with some dishes shining brighter than others.

A very dear friend of mine took me here for dinner on a Thursday night, and we had made reservations for 6:30 pm. This place was packed, and that speaks so much about the iconic Keens Steakhouse! There is obvious history associated with this place, and if you are in New York, you "have to" make a trip to Keens!What's amazing about Keens is that it can easily fall into the "tourist" traps/attractions, but it isn't! I was here with a born and raised New Yorker, who shared the same excitement and enthusiasm as me, an Indian born, who thoroughly enjoyed our $60 legendary mutton chop, which was cooked to perfection at the temperature we requested.What should I say about service? It was absolutely top notch! We ordered a fancy bottle of Malbec, the first one, which had gone bad, which our server was kind enough to spot and replace and we thoroughly enjoyed our bottle.Food, ambiance, service - all deserve a perfect 5. Amazingly, after so many years of service, Keens has still managed to maintain a perfect 5, which is something that's quite fascinating! Will definitely come here again!

Title: A Pleasant Surprise at a Bustling by Chloe

I recently dined at one of the by Chloe locations, an expansive and popular spot that's particularly crowded during lunch and festive periods. To anyone who'd rather skip the bustle, I recommend visiting at dinner time, which is quieter and increases your chance of snagging a table to savor your meal in peace.

On the upside, the presentation is commendable, with food meticulously packaged, reflecting its consistent quality. Yet, patience is required as the restaurant seems somewhat disordered, leading to longer wait times, more noticeable when dining in groups.

Despite this minor hiccup, my experience was largely positive. The Quinoa Taco Salad was a burst of flavors, and impressively, amidst the restaurant's chaos, our substantial order was delivered without errors - no back and forth for missing items.

In conclusion, by Chloe served up a delightful meal that mirrored the controlled chaos of a well-loved dining spot - slightly disheveled, but ultimately satisfying.

This was my old stomping ground when I lived on the UES. I've been here for full-blown brunch and dinner and also just snacks and drinks. Great place to hang out with friends night and day; could get a tad too loud for dates later in the week since it's a popular place in the neighborhood but the ambiance is legit. My friend who's still living in the neighborhood wanted to catch up and left the rendezvous details to me. I gladly offered to trek uptown and meet him at the Milton for brunch. Boy do I miss this place! I got the vanilla bourbon French toast and he got the chef's masterpiece. Still as good as I remembered.

My favorite brunch spot in NYC! The menu is set and it's 8 courses that they bring out according to how the table is eating...if you are wanting to take your time and enjoy the environment or sing along with the DJ, they will let you. Our group was having a blast and singing along with almost every song. It was like a party with a great DJ, ambient lighting and they even brought our go go dancers at the end. The food was fabulous and there was not one thing that I didn't like.

Title: Deceptive Frozen Treats and Tasty Eats at a Leisurely Pace

If you're ever in the mood for a post-work wind-down that packs a punch, this spot's frozen pomegranate margaritas are a must-try—delightfully sweet yet surprisingly potent. We kicked off our group dinner with chips paired with outstanding guacamole, a real highlight.

For my main dish, I chose the salmon, which was flavorful and cooked just right. To share, we opted for sides of rice and beans, which, while tasty, were disappointingly scant for our hungry table.

However, if you're not in a rush, the leisurely service won't bother you too much. In the end, the strong drinks and good food somewhat made up for the wait.

Came here for brunch before theatre show. My party selected the bottomless drink option. Our waitress told us the frozen margarita machine was broken and continued to tell us so until we asked one of the managers if it had been fixed. He then said he would go upstairs to  get them because the upstairs machine was working. Our waitress was vague and charged us $10 for a bottle of water because she was difficult to understand. Ultimately the food and drinks were good, the food was served promptly. Would have had a better experience if our waitress was more personable and easier to understand.

$15 CREDIT CARD MINIMUM + FEE!  (Better to have cash!)  My friend and I came to Lan Zhou around 2pm on a Wednesday.  I hadn't really read the reviews about the interior so I was surprised at how spacious it was!  Only a few other parties were in the restaurant at the time.  So imagine coming here on a hot summer's day.  It's in the 90s and I'm assuming you're walking from Grand or Canal Street.  And you're planning to eat some salty foods like dumplings and noodles.  But surprise, surprise, they don't serve water here!  You have to buy bottled water (I want to say $1.50).  As I am water's #1 fan, that alone is a major deterrent.  We ordered the beef brisket stir-fried hand-pull noodle ($9.50) and an order of fried dumplings ($4).  Friends, trust the reviews on Yelp.  If you must come here, come for the dumplings.  While they weren't the most amazing things I've tasted in my life, they were juicy and had great flavor without needing sauce.  And a pretty good deal for the price.  The beef in the noodles was also tender and flavored well.  However, the noodles themselves were flavorless and very oily.  Maybe they are better in soup.Since there's no water refilling, the only service was taking our orders and bringing the check so I can't comment much on that.  Overall, this place is average at best but I docked an additional star for the water thing.  I also think the noodles were overpriced for the quality and portion size.

Upon my recent visit to the new restaurant that has proudly outshone its Pennsy counterpart, I was greeted with an ambiance that provided a refreshing oasis in an area that's generally lacking in trendy dining options.
