The menu was a delightful experience, particularly the Pineapple Margarita, which was an impeccable blend of sweet and tangy, making it a highlight of the evening.

The Short Rib Taco also proved to be a savory treat, falling just short of perfection, while the chicken could benefit from a bit more seasoning to elevate its flavor profile. The guacamole was quite satisfactory, although not the best I've encountered, it was a solid addition to the meal.

Overall, this spot is a welcome addition to the neighborhood, offering a lively atmosphere paired with a selection of enjoyable dishes and beverages. It's definitely a place I'd recommend and look forward to visiting again.

Hands down the best taco spot in NYC. I don't know why it's so good!! Their pick de gallo is bomb. Get all the sauces! They're always packed so be prepared to wait on a line, but it's worth it! I also recommend their horchata!

The food here is delicious. The service is fast. The boss lady is always nice and polite. The location is convenient. What more can you ask for?! I first found out about the cart stand in high school. My friends and I would always quickly stop by (before she packed up for the day) after school for a snack because God knows how horrible American public school food is. But I don't remember visiting her after I graduated (even though I see her almost everyday because I live in the neighborhood). She would always bring back nostalgic memories, but never strong enough for me to stop by again.I'm not sure what it was, but I had a really strong craving for her food today, and finally decided to get a small rice noodles with fishballs. I brought it home to enjoy and a wave of childhood memories rushed through my mind. It felt like home. You really have to try to food to know how homey and delicious it is. The boss lady is always very welcoming and friendly, and she moves FAST. She doesn't waste her time. She doesn't waste your time. In addition to that, everything on the menu is EXTREMELY inexpensive! I had $4 in cash, and I was able to get a meal with just $3! She isn't always there, though, so make sure to get there early on a nice day because you and I both know that neither of us will be out on a bad day.

If you're looking for a reliable spot for comfort food and all-day brunch dishes, look no further! Cafeteria has been one of my go-to spots for all times of the day, whether it's 12 PM or 5 AM, and is my favorite 24/7 restaurant.Can you really say you were at Cafeteria without getting the Mac and Cheese Spring Rolls? Probably not - so definitely get them! I also got the Croissant French Toast during my last visit - would consider getting it again next time, too. Portion size for this one was a bit small, especially compared to the other dishes here!Wait times can get a bit long late at night, but usually it's not too bad during daylight hours.

I'm from the Bay Area where there are a lot of HOT POT/ BBQ places and I'm known to be the hot pot queen! Seeing the good rating and a lot of reviews, I wanted to see what NY hot pot is like. We did not try the BBQ here.The good: I really liked their homemade sauce, it's garlicky sweet. You can add garlic and green onions! The seafood pancake is surprisingly sooooo good, but I stopped myself from ordering a second one because this is a hot pot place I shouldn't be filling on the appetizer. The veggies were good and fresh. The bad: broth is bland, they have very limited meat choices, they only have one kind of beef! And it's not good. It's so loud inside, and they're playing the birthday song almost every 15 mins! It's kinda overboard IMO.For $22 AYCE hot pot, I can't complain much. You get what you pay for.

I'm not much a fan of burgers, so I'll start out with that caveat. I actually ended up not ordering anything, so that I could save my appetite for dinner later, but my friends ordered, and I had a bite out of a burger - it tasted like a typical burger with lots of cheese. My friend also got the spiked milk shake, which he said was too thick and ended up not completely finishing. It's a good restaurant with chill vibes if you just want to catch up with friends in a casual environment.

I was meeting with a friend for dinner, and although this wasn't where we wanted to go initially, I'm so glad we came here! Most tables were full when we got there around 7:30pm on a Friday, but we waited less than 5 minutes for a table of 2.They have a huge menu selection; we decided to split 2 entrees. We got the Chicken Katsu Don (~$15) with the B set (+$1) and the Beef 180g Gozen (~$29) which came with Rice, Pork Miso Soup, and Potato Salad. The B set includes Miso Soup and Cabbage Salad.To start, they brought out the soups and salad. I had the Miso Soup. It was good but nothing special, in my opinion. The Cabbage Salad was just shredded cabbage. They didn't bring the dressing to us until we were almost done, which was a bit disappointing.The actual entrees were delicious. The Chicken Katsu Don was loaded with rice, chicken katsu and egg. It was also mixed in with a sauce and topped with plenty of scallions. Every single bite was great and the portion size was solid. The Beef Gozen was cooked to a perfect medium and yet was super crispy on the outside. My one complaint is that the beef didn't taste seasoned at all. Not even with salt and pepper. We used the sauces to enhance the taste a bit.Overall, both dishes hit the spot! The smaller dishes that came before the entrees were disappointing. Nonetheless, I did enjoy my dinner here and I would definitely come back!

Title: A Series of Disappointments at Taqueria

My experiences at Taqueria have been consistently underwhelming, marked by poor service and lackluster fare. Initially turned away by rudeness so extreme I left pre-order, my subsequent attempt involved my girlfriend being denied service well before closing time. Even when dining in a group, the tacos we shared were unremarkable at best.

Despite the passage of time, my latest visit showed no improvements; prices had inflated, yet the mediocrity remained. Oddly, the restaurant's popularity has grown, which is baffling considering the disconnect between the anglicized menu and the rave reviews touting "authentic Mexican cuisine."

Furthermore, the aftermath of sharing my candid thoughts included receiving an abusive message from what appeared to be a fake account, likely connected to the restaurant. This inappropriate response has compelled me to downgrade my already low rating to a single star. I advise dining elsewhere, as this family business has failed to embody the professionalism and quality one would expect.

These sandwiches are really great. The first time I got it was through ritual and during the dollar dash deal, so I expected it to be really small considering I only paid $1 but it was the juiciest most filling sandwich I've ever had. It was the the Havana sandwich and came with a really great garlic aioli. Amazing. This time I got the Lenwich sandwich on focaccia bread and it was delicious. I try not to finish them because they're so big and filling but they honestly just taste that good. It's nice to have a sandwich that's not frugal with its meat/filling

Absolute disgrace! We came with a large party for dinner and had the worst service. To top it off the food was inedible. I ordered yemenite soup and they sent me tomato veggie! When I questioned it the waiter answered me back saying this is our yemenite. If they do not have it just let the person know!! This is the reason kosher restaurants on the UES don't last! We had several other dishes: the schnitzel lacked flavor, the shish kabob was hard and difficult to chew, the grilled pargiot my friend had to spit out in a napkin. We all got sick from this place. Please save your money and go somewhere where they care about what they serve!!

Health hazard- hygiene alert In the days of corona virus spread.The staff at this place needs awareness. Since it was my bday (during the corona virus spread) I had to cancel all plans but still decided to go to this place (two blocks away from home) for a quick drink. I ordered Pencilin cocktail; mix of whiskey, ginger n honey. The drink was super strong and extremely sweet so asked the bar tender to top it up with ice. He took my glass, used his left  palm to cup around the rim to pour ice. Pls tell me when we have been asked to avoid human touch, will I put my lips on that glass to sip my drink?.When I told the bar tender, he got defensive saying that he regularly washes his hands. Sorry that's no excuse, I'm not comfortable sipping from a potentially infected glass. Anyway I left without finishing the drink and paying for nothing. Seriously people still don't get it. My fault I shdnt step out coz there is clearly no awareness still whatsoever.

I came for dinner and was easily able to make reservations ahead of time. Passion fruit lassi - doesn't have yogurt. Passion fruit was uniqueFive spice cauliflower - fried and battered cauliflower with 5 spices. Extra spicy and surprisingly filling as well.  Banana leaf chicken - curry had strong coconut flavor but it was still delicious. Chicken was juicy and breaks apart easily Roast duck - this was really well done. Succulent and well flavored sauce paired well the naanGarlic naan - fresh and hot. Tastes best immediatelyThey don't serve the typical Indian dishes that you normally see, but instead push towards a more creative style. I actually enjoyed this Indian fusion restaurant albeit really pricey.

Title: A Sweet Start to the Year at Chocolat Restaurant

My first review of the year takes me to Chocolat Restaurant for a memorable Sunday brunch. The Southern-style vibe is a crowd-pleaser, so securing an early reservation is a must to beat the rush.

The service staff did an admirable job, maintaining attentiveness despite the bustling atmosphere. As for the drinks, the red velvet chocolate martini stood out, both in presentation and taste–a must-try for the adventurous palate.

The entrees didn’t disappoint either, striking that delicate balance between satisfying and overindulgent. The perfect portion size left us content without feeling weighed down.

I’m already planning a return visit, with an eye on their happy hour offerings. Chocolat has laid the groundwork for what I hope will be a year filled with delightful dining experiences. Highly recommended for those seeking a touch of Southern comfort with their meal.

Title: A Lunchtime Gem

I've been visiting this restaurant for lunch on several occasions, thanks to Mealpal, and it's quickly become a favorite of mine. The portions strike a perfect balance between satisfying and generous, ensuring you leave full without feeling overstuffed. Each dish I've tried bursts with freshness and flavor, a testament to their commitment to quality ingredients. But the highlight for me has to be their divine sauces – they truly elevate the meal. My go-to dish is the Mediterranean bowl, a harmonious blend of taste and health. Highly recommended for a delightful lunch experience!

I had the pleasure of ordering the Bara Chirachi from this restaurant during quarantine, and I was quite impressed. While the portion size was a tad on the small side, the inclusion of uni was a delightful surprise that added a luxurious touch to the meal. Moreover, the sushi rice was of excellent quality, providing a perfect foundation for the other flavors. Overall, a delicious choice for anyone craving authentic Japanese cuisine.

Tried to call for a reservation as I saw online that the restaurant took reservations, but the lady told me they mostly walk ins and to come as soon as possible to get seated. I came at 6:15 on a Monday night and put my name down for a table of two as I waited for my friend to arrive (only seats full parties). The hostess said I would receive a text message once a table is ready so to stay close. My friend came shortly after but we ended up waiting by the enclosed booth area outside, as there was no waiting area inside, for about 30 minutes for a table. I went back inside to ask how long it would be for a table and she said about 15 minutes or so but I saw there were empty tables inside. She must've seen me eyeing the empty tables because then she said she could actually seat us and brought us to an empty table. That whole situation was a little weird for me and I felt like we would've had to wait much longer if I hadn't asked about the eta. After browsing the menu, I ordered the gochu raymun and the toro ssam bap to share with my friend. The wait staff were courteous and the manager I believe was going around refilling the water for the tables, which I thought was interesting to see. I liked the overall atmosphere of the restaurant and the wait staff were very friendly. The toro ssam bap arrived about 15 minutes after we sat and I enjoyed the freshness and saltiness of the dish. It was $25 for a small dish which I thought was a tad pricey but I enjoyed it! It's a nice sharing dish to start. The gochu raymun tasted okay to me. I liked the chewiness and springiness of the noodles. The broth was rich and creamy but I felt like the overall taste didn't wow me. It was a mix of rich and sour from the kimchi. It was good, but I don't think I'd get it again if I did come back.

Very clean establishment as it looks as if it was just renovated. I happened to come here because I love burrata cheese and was looking for unique pizza joints in New York. I was really impressed to see that this location was open so late (after 1 am) on a weekday and decided to give the Sicilian and burrata slice a try.Not much to say about the service as the associate only popped our two slices in the small oven and then collected my payment. I didn't really hear him explain the prices but I ended up paying about $13 for two slices of pizza (pricey pricey). The burrata was very tasty but the bread part was a bit too stale for me (probably from sitting out for a while so late at night). The other slice was also toasted to a crisp so it ended up like an XXL cracker with pizza toppings. Overall, it's not a bad joint but would not be my pizza of choice for New York. If you're a burrata fan then it may be worthwhile to give it a try.

Title: A Steal for a Slice - Budget-Friendly Pizza Paradise

If you're hunting for an affordable lunch that hits the spot, look no further! We stumbled upon this little gem after a fruitless search for something both appetizing and wallet-friendly, and let me tell you, their $1 cheese pizza slice is a revelation. It's the epitome of value for money.

Despite the bustling crowd, service was impressively swift – the line moved fast and we got our pizza without delay. The place offers limited seating with some stand-up tables, which worked just fine for us as we eagerly dug into our slices.

I upgraded to the pepperoni for an extra $0.75, and it did not disappoint. While the restaurant's cleanliness might not win any awards, you can take solace in the fresh, mouthwatering pizzas that come out of their kitchen. Plus, there's a bit of showmanship involved – you can watch your pizza being made!

In summary, for a quick, tasty, and incredibly cheap bite, this spot is hard to beat. Embrace the no-frills experience and let the pizza speak for itself!

Tucked away in the vibrant streets of Chinatown, I serendipitously discovered a vegetarian gem that effortlessly stands out from its carnivorous neighbors. This establishment caters mostly to the vegan palate, with a few nods to ovo-vegetarians. Don't be fooled by the extensive menu – the generous portions are a delightful challenge to finish, ideal for the voracious but less so if it's your last culinary pit stop of the day.

Upon seating, you're greeted with a pot of tea rather than the customary glass of water, a nod to tradition that's as refreshing as it is surprising. A minor niggle comes with the extra charge for rice, nudging you towards the healthier brown variety.

The clientele is as eclectic as New York itself; a microcosm of the city's diversity where tattooed hippies rub elbows with sophisticated British students, and Canadian yuppies blend with local Chinese vegetarians.

My choice of braised tofu skins arrived drenched in a simple, albeit lackluster brown sauce. Despite its unassuming appearance, the dish delivered on the deep, comforting flavors expected of a braised specialty. While many dishes feature the typical fried offerings draped in cornstarch-thickened sauces, the variety on offer beckons for further exploration. This is a place worth revisiting, if not for the food, then for the experience of New York's cultural mosaic in a plate.

Title: A Bustling Sunday Evening at a Spanish Gem

Last Sunday's dinner service was booming at this charming establishment, but the initial warmth upon entry soon gave way to a cozy ambiance enhanced by the delightful roving musicians.

The culinary offerings were a hit, particularly the appetizers which stole the show. The Pulpo a la Gallega tantalized our taste buds with its garlicky perfection, while the Calamares a la Parilla and the pairing of Spanish Ham & Manchego Cheese provided an exquisite start to our feast. The Paella a la Valenciana was a hearty follow-up, and the meal concluded on a sweet note with a classic Flan. Throughout the evening, sips of refreshing Sangria and the thoughtful touch of complimentary bread and butter rounded out the dining experience.

Each appetizer presented a unique and delectable introduction to Spanish cuisine, setting a high bar for the rest of the meal. A night here is well-spent amidst good food and lively entertainment, perfect for those looking to dive into an authentic Spanish dining adventure.

Tucked away in the heart of Chinatown, this Thai gem stands out for its delightful curry dishes, which pack just the right amount of spice for those looking for an authentic taste. The ambiance is laid-back, perfect for unwinding, while the service is commendably efficient. Despite the hustle of the nearby government buildings, the restaurant remains pleasantly undiscovered, offering a quieter alternative to the popular Vietnamese spots down the street. With its excellent value for money, it's a must-visit for anyone—from office workers to jurors seeking a flavorful escape.

Title: A Thai Birthday Delight

I celebrated my birthday at this Thai gem and my experience was absolutely delightful. Reserving a table for our large group was a breeze, and upon arrival, we were greeted with swift and friendly service. Opting for a family-style meal, we kicked things off with the Sabai sampler platter, which featured tasty rolls and exceptionally flavorful dumplings.

Our main course featured an array of Thai classics – Panang curry, green curry, pad see ew, pad Thai, and kra pow fried rice. Each dish was a hit, but the kra pow fried rice truly stole the show with its unexpected and satisfying kick of spice, paired with perfectly balanced flavors.

Our night at this Thai spot was a culinary success, leaving us eager to return and explore more of their mouthwatering menu. Highly recommended for an authentic and enjoyable dining experience!

Came here on Wednesday night after work to catch up with a friend. Seemed fairly new, but it was pretty crowded even on a weekday night. Doma bossam: this was my most favorite out of all the dishes we got. The pork meat was charred outside and tender inside, and miso aioli on the side added a delicious umami flavor. We made bao sandwich with seasoned kimich and black sesame buns, which made every bite sooo yummy.Korean fried chicken: we ordered this because of all the reviews that raved about it. The skin was crunchy and the meat was juicy. Kimchi aioli sauce was pretty spicy, but it added a nice kick to sweet seasoning of the fried chicken skin.Beef short rib stew: we were sooo full, but wanted something soupy so we ordered this dish. The meat was very tender and rice cake in the soup had CHEESE in it! The soup was loaded with veggies, and I didn't expect to find brussels sprouts as it's not typically used in a Korean stew but it was still delicious and unique. Royal goguma: I don't usually go for a dessert at dinner, but I'm a BIG fan of sweet potatoes so I couldn't pass on this. The mousse cake with Korean sweet potato hit the spot and the sesame ice cream was so flavorful. I liked how it wasn't too sweet either. The restaurant has a really cool atmosphere and staffs were super friendly. I definitely want to come back here next time and try their drinks and other items on their menu!

Had a fantastic time at this three-story bar—perfect spot to catch soccer games on the weekend with their big-screen TVs throughout. The beer selection is reasonably priced, especially for midtown, and the bartenders are welcoming and friendly. While the wings aren't the best I've ever had—those would be the atomic wings from another bar—they're still very tasty and satisfying. Definitely a great place to hang out with friends and enjoy the game.

Title: Classic New York Pizzeria Experience

I visited this well-talked-about pizzeria in the heart of New York, ticking off a tourist must-do. The place served up a good slice, no doubt about it. It boasts the quintessential New York style: fluffy, yet with a perfect crispy edge. The sauce and cheese ratio was impeccable, giving each bite the classic cheesy pull.

What stood out were the toppings; especially the creative white pizza adorned with spinach and pepperoni - both were spot-on in flavor. The crust deserves a mention for its exceptional texture, contributing to an airy, light experience that didn't weigh down the rich toppings.

All in all, while this pizza parlor didn't reinvent the wheel, it delivered a solid, enjoyable pie that lived up to the city's reputation. Definitely worth a visit for any pizza enthusiast exploring New York.

I stopped by for the second time with my sisters. This time we got the regular cheese pie, which I liked even more than the white pie!For dessert we just could not stay away from the Nutella pie which was just as delicious as the first time!  Honestly the dessert is what keeps me coming back for more!  (The lady next to me had a Cannoli and I think I'll have to try that next time!)

I had high hopes for this establishment, but it ultimately fell short of expectations. The entryway was notably confusing, requiring guests to navigate through a gift shop to access the bakery and restaurant. Additionally, the seating arrangements were complicated by varying rules depending on the day of the week.

Cleanliness was a major issue; the premises appeared unkempt with tables cluttered with unwashed dishes, and a restroom that was in dire need of maintenance. The value for money, particularly with the $13 turkey sandwich, was disappointing due to its meager portion size. On a positive note, the dessert was delightful, and the coffee serviceable. Notably, the cookie — recognized as one of Oprah's favorites — was exceptional.

However, despite the bakery's offering, I am inclined to skip a return dining experience; I might consider stopping by solely for the famed cookie takeaway.

This place has great yummy vegetarian options and healthy food choices. Not for those who like to eat a lot of meat.The seating arrangement was very crowded and what upset me was my friends and I had been waiting for a bit for a four person seating yet when it was time for us to be finally seated, they decided to add two chairs to the edge of a table and call it seating... So we had two people sitting at the end of a communal table and then two people trying to share a one person area at the edge... It felt like a health hazard. So I was squished with my friend and tons of people/waitresses walking right behind us... It was really annoying. I had to scoot my seat in a ton in order to provide space. When we had asked to move to a table that was free for four, they said no... Instead they gave it to a group of four that came way after us.My friends and I ordered the green shakshuka, Jack's breakfast, breakfast bowl, and poached eggs with grilled tomato and haloumi.The steak in Jack's breakfast was cooked perfectly but besides that it was okay.The breakfast bowl (the one I chose) was very interesting. Definitely something delicious for people who love to eat healthy (that's not me). It was very light yet filling so I was glad I didn't feel gross after however I was pretty bored after eating it for too long.My friend told me the green shakshuka was very good, kinda tasted like some green salsa.My friend who ordered the poached eggs loved it but said she wished there was another egg or more food to it because she was left feeling hungry.I think this is nice to check out once but I probably won't be coming back because there are plenty of other brunch places I'd like to still try out!

Went to dinner here one night for my mom's birthday. I am picky when it comes to Mediterranean food and this place met all my standards. The decor included a display of the raw fish of the day, which I always appreciate at a Mediterranean/seafood establishment. Our waiter was attentive and prompt. We started with calamari, grilled octopus and spanakopitas, which were all good and I ordered the branzino as my main dish, which was perfect! It was a thin filet, the perfect portion size and melted in my mouth. Overall, great experience!

A vegetarians heaven right here! So many delicious veggie options available... as well as delicious meat options for others! We came in last Wednesday around 7. We made reservations but it didn't seem necessary at that time of the week. We spent a while deciding on our order. We ordered the blended mint lemonade for a drink. It was pricy but very delicious (even though it was freezing outside). The sake margarita also sounded amazing. They do a happy hour as well. I ordered the market veggie plate which came with my choice of 4 market sides. I got the yuca fries (a daily special), Brussels sprouts, eggplant with tahini and the roasted sweet potatoes. All amazing! My friend ordered a hot dog with 2 sides of yuca fries and Brussels sprouts. The sides are much larger when you order them separate from the veggie plate. Regardless, we had plenty of food! I would love to return for brunch as well soon!

You know... I've had Momo long time ago downtown . And I wasn't at first impressed. It's been years since I've had their ramen and I've got to say. I'm impressed.Your not the best thing I've ever had. But u sure as hell surprised me. U brought something to the table for sure.Broth. Had such a nice and light taste. Super clean. Bad ramen shops tend to have this muddy, overly flavored broth. This is nice and clean. It was super refreshing to taste.Noodle were on the weak side. Wish it wasn't like a regular ramen packet noodle.But the pork chasu. Damn. This was blowing my mind. Char. Crunchy. Tasty. Juicy. Thick. My word. It had it all. I would choose this chasu over any other I've ever had.

Detroit style pan pizza in the middle of Manhattan. They do not sell by the slice and only by the personal pan. Each pan is cut into 4 pieces and hefty enough to feed 2. I ordered a mushroom pan for myself and was stuffed after 2 pieces - the leftovers were just as tasty the next day. The pizza itself is similar to a Sicilian square with a crisp, soft, and chewy crust.The pizzeria is small with a few standing tables so it's great for a quick bite or a grab-n-go pie.
Watermelon martini was magnificent & ambience was perfect  on a Sunday evening! The sliders  were tasty

Such a beautiful concept, not only do you get to walk through the collections of restoration hardware but you get to have a drink and a meal. It should be noted the bar area is just for select beer and wine and it is on the third floor. The restaurant is on the top floor and reservations are highly suggested. I didn't eat during this first visit but I did enjoy walking around the floors and getting the RH experience.

Had a reservation for here on a Wednesday night. They had an open front and it felt really cool and breezy. It was not super busy and we were able to be seated right away.Came here with 1 other. We ordered a croquette appetizer and we each ordered a pizza. I forgot the name of mine but it was the one with mushrooms, sausage, and basil. The flavor was good but the bottom of the pizza was super soggy and wet. It was hard to lift the pizza because of this as the toppings kept falling off.Service was good and the food came out super quickly. They also gave us a free panna cotta to share at the end- it tasted like chocolate mint!Everything was decent but probably would not come back again for the $18 pie- could get much better pizza elsewhere.

This place has been under my radar for awhile. I was overall happy with my meal but there could have been a few improvements. Be prepared to wait at least 45minutes because they do not take reservations. I thought the service could have been a little bit better. We were seated by our hostess and she gave us the menus but afterwards no one came to greet us or recommend any items. We sat there for a good 10 minutes. All the waiting staff seemed to be very busy. I am normally okay with mediocre service as long as the food is good but this a Michelin star restaurant and they seem take a lot of pride in it. They need to step up their game. We ordered the 6 course Prix Fixe, which was $55 per person. It was very filling for two people. It was worth a try but next time I would just order ramyun and share an appetizer. Some of the dishes I could skip. -Toro Ssam Bap: It was okay, not bad but not my favorite. Fatty tuna with sesame seasoned rice and seaweed wrap. The menu had scrambled egg listed as an ingredient but I did not taste any eggs in the dish. -Jeju Chicken Wings: Pretty good. Non-offensive. Can't go wrong. Crispy wings with some spicy ranch-like sauce. Came with some picked veggies. -Truffle Roasted Mushrooms: Highly recommended especially if you are a vegetarian!! They cooked the mushrooms perfectly. The oyster and shiitake mushroom texture was soft but with a bounce and not mushy or overcooked, which is hard to do. They were coated with a soy/ balsamic-like savory sauce and topped with fresh truffles. So good! -Prime Ribeye Ssam: Meh. I can go without it. The steak was cooked to a good medium rare but I didn't find anything special about it. The steak was cut to awkward large slices that were hard to bit and eat as a wrap. We ended up just eating the meat and the leafy greens separately. -Gochu Ramyun: The star of the show. Was already too full at this point. You can just jump straight to this and skip everything else. Beautiful rich and spicy sesame pork broth. Nice chewy noodles, pork slices, and pickled lettuce. -Lemon Sorbet: Alright standard dessert. Already had too much in belly and could barely consume more. Conclusion: Ramyun was pretty good! I would save some more room in my tummy next time, skip the nonsense, and just order a ramyun with one appetizer. The Truffle Roasted Mushrooms was a good choice! Would come again and try their other ramyun.

Title: High Expectations Dashed at Overrated Eatery

As a visitor from San Francisco's vibrant dining scene, I anticipated a meal that would hold its own against the culinary competition back home. Unfortunately, this restaurant, with its somewhat pretentious air, fell short of even modest expectations.

The server was a highlight, providing good service amidst the disappointing fare. My main course, the shrimp and jalapeño grits, was a perplexing letdown. The dish presented a sour and vinegary flavor profile, overly generous with what seemed to be paprika. The gritty garnish of arugula was tough, and the shrimp suffered from overcooking and the inconvenience of intact tails. Mysterious sour cubes added confusion rather than taste, and the promise of jalapeños was unfulfilled—save for a lone piece of cauliflower. Served lukewarm, the dish failed on all fronts without a hint of the titular jalapeño.

Commencing the meal with "warm bread and butter" promised a comforting start, yet what arrived was a stale, cold disappointment that foreshadowed the meal to come.

A mediocre well drink did little to enhance the experience, especially given the steep price, and the meal concluded with an apple pie only marginally superior to convenience store offerings, a final letdown in an evening of missed culinary opportunities.

For the $80 spent, I received an experience worth scarcely more than $30. This dinner was a stark reminder that a higher price tag does not necessarily guarantee a high-quality dining experience.

Returned in the winter and had a nice time. The Split man (hot chocolate) with bourbon was awesome, and we were able to cozy up outside by the fire pit. Only thing is that I wish they had food available all day (without having to eat the sit-down restaurant). 3.5 stars.

Title: A Lively Spot with More Buzz than Bite

I recently dined at a bustling venue teeming with aspiring actors serving tables to supplement their incomes. This hotspot, seemingly a magnet for tourists, thrives on a catchy gimmick: high energy performances with a side of entertainment. The ambiance was electric, with singing and spirited action that kept the place hopping.

The service was decent, considering the crowd; however, a minor hiccup occurred when my request for a Coke, relayed through a back waiter, seemed to vanish into thin air. Our choice of Prosecco for the evening was disappointing, excessively sweet and evidently of inferior quality.

The culinary experience fell short of expectations. Their rendition of crispy artichoke hearts missed the mark for me, both in concept and taste. The deconstructed mozzarella Caprese was an unconventional surprise that required a bit of DIY with the provided bread – not your traditional fare, and certainly not to my liking, despite the quality of the cheese itself.

It was apparent that the establishment's Italian offerings lacked genuine Italian influence or ownership. The evening's highlight, however, was a delightful encounter with a well-known actor whom I admire and share mutual friends with – a true fan moment that did add a personal touch to the visit.

The dessert concluded our meal on a sweeter note, bringing some redemption to the table. While I wouldn't return with culinary expectations, the vibrant atmosphere could tempt me back for another round of casual socializing in this theatrical dining scene.

I would echo what others have already proclaimed about this location of Hide-Chan: This spot offers a fantastic flavorful prices at reasonable prices in a comfortable ambience. The competition amongst ramen restaurants is fierce in NYC, but this place stands out. My friend and I met for dinner in the back room of the restaurant. She ordered a spicy garlic ramen with wavy noodles ($15), while I ordered the classic ramen with wavy noodles ($14). We were both highly satisfied with our respective orders. The noodles were perfectly chewy, and my broth was rich, salty, and filling, as I had hoped. The two pieces of pork were tender, while the mushrooms added great flavor and texture. For the location and quality, the prices can't be beat. This is a great spot for a casual social meal, especially since it's not too loud yet the space is darkly lit and comfortable.

My boyfriend and I were hungry while wandering around the financial district and we were not disappointed by Steve's. It was really busy and a little crazy to figure out how it worked or where to go, but definitely worth it! $6 minimum on credit cards (slices are $3) -- don't get caught off guard!

Upon my recent visit to this establishment, I found the cocktail offerings meriting between 3 and 4 stars - a solid selection capable of pleasing the discerning patron. However, the culinary experience was akin to that of Times Square tourist traps; unremarkable and tailored to transient visitors. A notable example was the onion rings, which bore a closer resemblance to miniature donuts, overwhelmed by excessive batter. The Reuben sandwich also fell short of authenticity, featuring grilled cabbage in lieu of traditional sauerkraut. Even upon requesting the latter, we were met with yet another serving of grilled cabbage. On a positive note, the upstairs dining room afforded a spacious and comfortable environment for dining.

Atmosphere: 5Spacious, with high ceilings and multiple floors. They are systematic with their seating, however, it seems there is never a time you can go there without at least a 15 minute wait. They give you a buzzer for your wait which is helpful. He restaurant is dimly lit and have 2 bathrooms.Portion: 5Your tofu pot is adequate but with the extra side dishes on the house, you will definitely be leaving stuffed. There is a lot of tofu in your soup and adequate amount of other ingredients to satisfy your meal. The side dishes are just enough for everyone. I love that you get a full fish on the house!Flavors: 5One of the best tofu soup restaurant chains in my opinion. Their soups and side dishes are always consistently good. Whatever spiciness level I order is just exactly what I expect so no surprises there. There's enough levels to cater to everyone's taste.I always come back to this restaurant. While the wait is awful during rush hour, this restaurant is always my first choice in KTown. Highly recommend it. Even with the wait!!

This is absolutely the most romantic and relaxing restaurant I've been too in New York City. The food was delicious they have a variety selection of food all you can eat and the dessert section as well! Even though you have to purchase a drink it's only $42 for the buffet + the drink which isn't bad for the view your getting! Full rotation takes an hour and half of all of New York! Definitely will be back again (:

Recently, I had the pleasure of dining at a local poke place where I crafted a delightful poke bowl tailored to my tastes. Opting for a health-conscious base of zucchini noodles, I topped it with a succulent trio of shrimp, spicy tuna, and salmon.

The restaurant offers a wide array of toppings at no extra cost, save for the creamy avocado which understandably commands a premium. The joy of my dining experience was further elevated by their policy of unlimited sauce choices, allowing for a perfect customization of flavors.

Each mouthful of my bowl was a testament to the freshness of the ingredients. The proteins were generously portioned, intermingling perfectly with a hearty selection of toppings. The vegetables were crisp and vibrant, while my personal favorites – masago, seaweed salad, and crab salad – brought a delightful complexity to the bowl.

In summary, the poke bowl not only satiated my appetite but did so with a harmonious blend of my preferred flavors and textures. It was a gratifying meal that I’d recommend to anyone looking for a fresh, filling, and customizable dining option.

Great place for a quick bite to eat in Midtown East without having to travel to K-town.  I always get the same thing the Korean Tofu Stew with brown rice $13.95.  For some reason they make this tastier than the traditional soondubu - I think they add some oil or richer broth.  They serve kimchi and a pickled daikon upon arriving.  I will always eat at this spot when I'm craving soondubu after work!

Title: A Sicilian Gem in South Village - Piccola Cucina

If you're on the hunt for the quintessential Sicilian kitchen in South Village, look no further than Piccola Cucina. This humble spot may be small, but as I've come to realize, some of the best things indeed come in small packages (much like my experience at Little Owl).

Upon arrival for my weekly lunch with my friend Rochelle, we were delighted by the restaurant's cozy charm, unique lighting, and inventive wine storage. The daily lunch specials, starting at just $11, are clearly marked with stars on the menu, beckoning diners to indulge without breaking the bank.

While the arancini rice balls were tempting, my pescatarian diet led us to share a fennel salad instead. This was an amazing choice, showcasing a harmonious mix of fennel, red onions, radishes, green olives, capers, and the juiciest oranges.

For our entrees, Rochelle savored the spinach and cheese ravioli with sausage-studded sauce, while I took a fellow patron's advice and ordered the Maccheroni al Ferretto alla Norma Con Ricotta Salata. The pasta, with its vodka-esque tomato sauce, and tender eggplant was nothing short of divine, served in a stylish stainless steel pan that added to the rustic vibe.

The dessert selection did not disappoint, with the cannolis arriving in a delightful trio and the Creme Brûlée offering a surprising twist with blueberries. My Café Americano was perfect - served hot and complemented the sweet ending.

The service at Piccola Cucina? Impeccable. Attentive, gracious, and accommodating define our waiter's approach. And with several locations across Soho, it's convenient too.

In conclusion, for an authentic taste of Sicily at a value you'll cherish, I wholeheartedly recommend starting your culinary journey at Piccola Cucina. Buon appetito!

If you are craving for a samosa chat, go to this place! They have a delicious bowl of chat which is good for two people. I have also tried their biryani and bowls which are okay but samosas are very tasty!

If you're around the neighborhood, Pig Heaven is a solid choice for some Chinese food. The staff here are extremely nice & welcoming. My friend and I had their popcorn shrimp. It is definitely a unique dish-- has a hint of wasabi flavoring. It was surprisingly delicious and I'm usually not a wasabi fan myself. The wasabi flavoring wasn't overbearing. We also tried their shanghai soup buns. It was delicious, but not the best soup buns I've had. (I'm pretty selective about my soup buns, so my expectations for these might be too high. )I've also tried their famous spare ribs. They looked delicious upon arrival to the table-- their glaze was glistening in the light. My favorite dish was their tomato, tofu, and beef soup. I wish they had more of the noodles in there, but I'm not too upset about it. I do wish it was spicier, but the dish itself was delicious regardless.Overall, service was great, food was decent. Dishes were pretty authentic for Chinese food.

I thought it was a good sign that this tony Park Avenue South restaurant shares the same name as my dad's old real estate firm. Yep, he hung out his own shingle and called it Upland Realty. I also happened to be staying across the street at the Hotel Giraffe (review: bit.ly/2HPeVvZ). In fact, the balcony in my room overlooked the restaurant as all sorts of young, trendy people waltzed in and out in varying degrees of drunkenness. Clearly I was meant to dine here, right? So I made a lonely reservation for one on a frigid Thursday evening and give it a try.I didn't know anything about its culinary pedigree. Chef Justin Simillie is a California native who leans quite a bit on fresh vegetables in his menu. Good for me since I wanted to eat healthy on my business trip and nearly OD'ed on the complimentary wine and cheese at the hotel just before I got here. I started with the $19 Little Gem Salad, which was anything but little with avocado, cucumber, and ricotta salata. It was drenched in a walnut vinaigrette and squeezed with an excessive amount of lemon which wasn't even mentioned in the menu (photo: bit.ly/2MQhvAP).For my entree, I went with the $36 Roasted Lamb Shoulder, which was so dominated by lettuce, sprouted lentils, aji dulce, a swoosh of avocado sauce, and a baked sweet potato that I could barely make out the shards of lamb (photo: bit.ly/2TxpwgG). The one dish that met my expectations was the $14 Blistered Shishito Peppers sprinkled with bottarga as it lent much needed zest to my meal (photo: bit.ly/2tetuPX). Yet, the best part came right off the bat, the complementary loaf of Potato Bread with herb butter (photo: bit.ly/2SrjPUc). Now that was worth devouring, the rest not as much.FOOD - 3 stars...pricy dishes with fresh ingredients but faulty executionAMBIANCE - 3.5 stars...busy and buzzy and not overly overwhelming SERVICE - 4 stars...quite attentive and no side-eye for my solitary stateTOTAL - 3 stars...upscale Manhattan dining that just fell shortRELATED - Looking for other dining options in New York City? Here's a collection of places I've tried and reviewed: bit.ly/2sGleaS

During a recent lunch outing with friends, we stumbled upon a gem where we could actually enjoy a meal seated at a table, a rarity in an area dominated by take-out spots and bar seating. The multitasking bartender impressed us with his adept service, handling everything from water to bussing with ease.

The menu delighted us with a variety of options including salads, cottage pie, and grilled chicken, complemented by either a soup of the day or a side salad—I opted for a blue cheese dressing which was quite delightful. Accompanying our meals with a selection of drinks including a Heineken, Guinness, and wine, we found the total bill of $60 to be an amazing value.

Alas, the restrooms were a slight misadventure; an unexpected ramp at the entrance posed a challenge, especially without a warning sign in the men's room. Despite this, the overall experience was positive. This spot is a great find for a relaxed lunch—just tread carefully when visiting the facilities!

Title: An Underground Gem: Decibel

Review:

I absolutely ADORE Decibel. Initially, I thought this place was a well-kept secret, but the nightly crowds suggest otherwise. Hidden below street level, Decibel's unassuming entrance is easy to miss. If there's no line snaking up the stairs – a rare sight – consider yourself lucky and join the queue posthaste.

Inside, Decibel oozes character with its dim lighting and a decor drenched in graffiti – even on the ceiling. The atmosphere is cozy, albeit a bit rough around the edges. The waitstaff, while not all fluent in English, are friendly and exceedingly helpful when navigating the extensive sake menu.

Be mindful that due to the compact nature of the space, Decibel has a strict no-standing policy. If you're not indulging in their offerings, expect to receive your check promptly. It's not your go-to for long, leisurely catch-ups, but for an authentic, bustling experience with exceptional drinks, Decibel is a hit.

During my recent visit to the local eatery, I opted for the chicken green curry, which presented a flavor profile tending towards the sweeter side, likely due to its coconut milk base. The curry was tasty, with just the right amount of spice to keep things interesting. However, the portion of rice provided felt disproportionate, leaving me with more curry than I could pair it with. Service was commendable—staff were warm and the dish arrived promptly despite a bustling crowd. The team managed the space efficiently, ensuring a comfortable dining experience. All in all, the meal was enjoyable, though there's room for improvement in the rice-to-curry ratio.

Stopped by the LES location one summer evening with my boyfriend and we LOVED it! So we decided to go and try the Carmine St. location with my brother and his friend while they were visiting for the holiday's. We each got a frozen margarita upon arriving while we waited for our table. We had a reservation for 645 and arrived at 630 but we were missing one person from our party. The hostess was very kind and asked if we wanted to be seated without him, but they only allot for 90 min per table, so we decided to get a drink at the bar and wait for him so we got to use the full 90 minutes with our entire group! The margarita was strong and very tasty! We got nachos as an appetizer and they were delicious. I have an avocado allergy so they put the guac and salsa (which contains avocado) on the side! I got the cauliflower rice with chorizo and it was delicious.  I personally thought it tasted a bit better at the LES location but I still ate most of this one so I can't complain. Our waitress was nice as well, not super attentive but we did not need her for much. The bathrooms are nice and clean as well. Will definitely be back to any of their locations!

Once a fond memory, my recent experience at Cotenna left much to be desired. High expectations set by swift bookings and excessive text confirmations met with disappointment.

On a positive note, the starters like the Caprino alle Erbe and meatballs had delightful flavors but were regrettably portioned for smaller parties. The restaurant's interior is admittedly striking, creating an alluring date night ambience—providing it's not overcrowded, which it nearly always is.

However, the delights ended there. Service carried a disconcerting air of snobbery; an early arrival was met with annoyance, and our seating by the constantly opening door left us shivering each time a new customer or a gust of cold wind barged in. The closely packed setting was more commotion than comfort, resulting in a loss of enjoyment.

The food, overshadowed by the chilly blasts and poor service, failed to leave an impression. A promised touch of freshly grated pecorino on our pasta never materialized, leaving our dishes and expectations incomplete. The final indignity was the absence of a promised birthday lava cake, disappointingly replaced by the sole offering of tiramisu.

In conclusion, what once might have been a charming gem is now best bypassed in favor of nearby alternatives like Olio e Piú, La Lanterna, or Malaparte, where the experience is sure to align better with the money spent.

Knowing Eric Sze, who owns both the Tang and nearby 886, I had to try out the Tang. I wasn't too impressed with the food at 886, so wanted to venture to see if there were more authentic Chinese noodles at affordable prices. Came here on a Friday night at 8pm with a group of four friends. There was no line so we were immediately seated. We ordered the following items to share: Fried Turnip Cake, braised beef noodle soup, tang's herbal chicken noodle soup, drunk noodles, sizzling noodles, braised pork ears in chili oil. Total bill came about $26.50 per person inclusive of tax and tip. Pretty good deal considering what we got! Disclaimer: I had the input of each of my four Chinese friends - One's from Taiwan, one's from Hunan, one's from Beijing, and myself from Shanghai. We all thought this was a delicious, authentic experience!AMBIANCE:Casual spot. Restaurant space wasn't too huge, but there is a cool outdoor seating portion thats perfect during summers or springs. PROS:Honestly all the noodles we got. My favorite has got to be the tang's herbal chicken soup - You can tell they definitely took hours and hours to boil out such a flavorful and aromatic broth, and the chicken itself was incredibly succulent and flavorful! You can test bits of Chinese herbs in the broth, and it honestly reminded us the chicken noodle soups that our parents used to make when we were younger. Next favorites were the Drunk noodles and the braised beef noodle soup. The drunk noodles had a really nice heat to it, and it paired really well with the thick hand-drawn noodles. I like the amount of cilantro and scallions on it as it really adds a depth of flavorful from the chili oil. The beef on top of it, and also the beef on the braised beef noodle soup, was equally delicious and flavorful, and you can definitely taste the marinade that seeps into the meat. Sizzling noodles were fantastic, and I really like the crunch the peanuts gave on a bed of hot chili oil noodles. Fried turnip cakes were very crispy and airy! I also like the chili pork ears considering its such a staple in sichuan/hunan cuisine.OKAY:Minor complaint for the braised beef noodle soup - I feel like the broth was a little bland and lacking in flavor compared to other Chinese beef noodle soups around the area. I'm thinking nearby Ho Foods makes a killer beef noodle soup. I wish the chefs at the Tang could perhaps cook their soup a little longer in order to develop more beefiness to the broth.OVERALL:We were highly satisfied with our experience at the Tang! Noodles were definitely the star of the night. Highly recommend the Tang over 886. You now got the approval of four happy customers!

I recently visited EJ's, a charming diner-esque eatery tucked away in the Upper East Side, which instantly transports you to the 1950s with its vintage authenticity. My party of four was quickly seated by the window, a coveted spot in any New York restaurant. Expect close quarters and a lively atmosphere here—conversations from neighboring tables may become part of your experience.

Our server proved exceptional, attentive, and well-versed in the menu. I opted for the club sandwich with a side of chicken noodle soup—a standout choice. The soup was a nostalgic nod to a classic, homemade variety that could easily be mistaken for your grandmother's recipe; I savored every last drop. The club sandwich, while standard, was perfectly executed.

For anyone wandering through the Upper East Side with a midday hunger, EJ's is a must-visit for a delightful lunch experience that won't disappoint.

The atmosphere alone upon entering Upland will entice you to dine here.It is a beautifully chic and trendy restaurant featuring New-American cuisine. The walls are illuminated with jarred goodies that give a bright and airy aura to this place.Entrées definitely run on the higher side, but I found this was a nice place to share several plates as a group. To put into perception, between five of us, we shared 3 appetizers, a pizza, a pasta and 2 entreés, and this resulted in plenty of food.The crispy duck wings were a delicious and interesting take on this bird. They are fried perfectly and carry a rich flavor from the duck. The tartare was tasty, but probably not the best I've had. The kale and sausage pizza was savory with each bite and the cacio and pepe was cooked and presented to perfection.For entreés, the angus steak was deliciously tender and juicy, while the cippino was stewed in a decadent broth.The dining experience here is definitely memorable. I would definitely recommend to anyone dining in the Gramercy/Flatiron area.

Title: A New Year's Feast to Remember

My New Year's Eve dinner at this gem of a restaurant was a culinary triumph. We nabbed seats at the bar, a vantage point I'd recommend for the attentive service and convivial atmosphere.

The meal kicked off with a soul-warming soup of the day, followed by an impeccable burrata cheese and tomato salad. The pickled peppers accompanying it were a delightful surprise, sweet and mild enough even for the picky eater. The Ahi tuna tartare stole the show among starters with its perfect harmony of flavors and a zingy ginger dressing.

For the main course, my husband's NY sirloin strip was a standout, seasoned to perfection with a tenderness that simply dissolved in the mouth. However, the true star of the evening was the lobster Mac and cheese. Laden with succulent lobster and perfectly cooked pasta, it was the epitome of comfort food elevated to high art—the very definition of palate pleasure.

Comparatively, a subsequent dinner at Del Frisco's couldn't hold a candle, particularly their take on lobster Mac and cheese. Our experience here set a bar that simply couldn't be matched.

For anyone considering a visit, do yourselves a favor: dine here, opt for the bar seating, and indulge in what could very well be the best lobster Mac and cheese of your life.

Went here based on a recommendation. You buy your meat by the weight and sides by the size. The moist brisket was tasty as was the Mac and cheese and greens.  Online it mentions happy hour and has food options including a sandwich, this isn't correct. There are only drink specials. The bar staff was ok but not overly attentive. I'd stop back if I was in the area.

Last night's dinner at this gem of a pizzeria transported me straight to Southern Italy—no passport needed. Boasting authentic Neapolitan-style pizza, the dough is a dream come true: so soft and chewy, you can (and should) savor it with a fork and knife, just like the Italians do. The ambiance only elevates the experience, with an all-Italian staff creating an atmosphere that's both genuinely local and refreshingly new. No reservations? No problem on a weeknight, though it's clearly no secret spot. Five stars are well deserved for this authentic culinary escape.

Title: Cozy and Authentic Family-Owned Gem

My boyfriend and I recently dined at a charming family-owned restaurant that captivated us from the moment we stepped in. The owners' passion for their establishment shone through in every aspect, making it more than just a meal out—it was a heartwarming experience.

The star of the show was undeniably the pizza, particularly the dough. It was exceptionally fresh, with a delightful soft and chewy texture that demanded to be enjoyed straight out of the oven. Truly, it was pizza perfection.

Despite its small size, the restaurant exuded a cozy, home-like atmosphere that added to the authenticity of our visit. It's a place where every detail seems crafted with love and care, creating an incredible dining experience.

In conclusion, there isn't a single negative thing to note. We are already looking forward to our next visit to this little haven of culinary delight. Highly recommended for anyone craving a slice of home with their pizza!

I've been wanting to check out 886 ever since they opened (shoutout to all the Taiwanese places in NYC, gotta make the rounds and support them). Okay so there was a mix-up with our waitlist seating and our table was given away but it was worth it because we got seated at the bar in front of Eric. He was incredibly chill and definitely went along with all of my humor. The full story: my friend and I arrived around 7pm on a Friday night (oof definitely make reservations). We were told it would be a 40 minute wait for a table for 2, and then when we returned within the grace period, our table had been given away. We were able to sit at the bar in front of what appeared to be a pretty cool bartender, and he turned out to be Chef Eric. We had the most fun night because of our conversations with him. GET THE LO BA BENG! It's Taiwanese for lu rou fan (Taiwanese braised pork with rice). I couldn't stop eating it even though I got full, it was a good portion. The saaaawce issss soooo yummyyyy. The egg that accompanies the rice is soft-boiled and tastes great. Some would say eggcellent.The Taiwanese sausage fried rice was on the sweet side, but still good. Chili crispy tofu was so fun to eat. The appetizer portions were tiny but the entrees were a good size for sharing. I can't wait to come back and try their beef noodle soup. The vibe was so fun and the music was great. Everyone was just hanging out having a great time, and I think this is why we live in New York City. We want to go to a place where people actually connect and get to know each other. We want to support local businesses. We want to be able to get drunk and have some great food if we want to. It's just all around such a good time. I'm coming back and going to challenge you to do the 6 second drink, Chef Eric! Tell Big Richard I said hi!

I've had ROKC bookmarked for a year and been wanting to try it. My boyfriend and I finally stop by last month and it met our expectations! We came on a Friday night around 6pm so there was no wait, however, we did have to sit at the bar. We didn't try any of their drinks this time around but would definitely come back another time for that. They have some really interesting and unique cocktails. Here is what we ordered: -oysters: they have $1.25 happy hour oysters! -uni tofu custard (I forgot the actual name of it but it's the only uni dish for appetizer): this was super tasty, very savory and lots of uni. I was surprised! It is a bit heavy. -Kyoto ramen- very nice and light broth since it's not made with pork. It was savory and very delicious. -Okinawa ramen- this was more of a fusion ramen as there was asparagus in it. Also has only one piece of meat (boyfriend was sad about that LOL) Overall a very solid place for ramen in upper Manhattan. I highly recommend the food and the service was great. Our server was also the bartender and he was very attentive!

This place is surprisingly easy to find if you manage to make the walk out to 10th ave and the venue is pretty big if you include the outside seating, a total A+++The food is pretty good, a bit overpriced howeverThe crowd is a mix of locals and a few visitors, some dates etcWe tried the chips with the spicy pineapple guacamole which was great (chips were definitely on the crispy/heavy side), the shrimp tacos and the ceviche mixto. All were pretty good, nothing spectacular to be honest.I liked that the service was prompt and attentive, but Im not sure if it was exceptional enough for me to travel far out to 10th haha. Just my two centsActually more like 3.5 stars that I rounded to 4, the 0.5 minus comes from the chairs... when I got up I realized I has several splinters stuck in my leg as I was wearing a dress. That was a bummer:(

I recently visited this quaint little spot for my crepe fix and left quite satisfied. I opted for the classic Nutella crepe topped with banana, and it did not disappoint. The flavor was rich and delicious, exactly what you'd expect from a standard good crepe. The level of efficiency from the staff, especially the lady preparing the crepes, ensured a smooth and pleasant experience.

The variety of crepe options is impressive, making it a must-visit for any crepe enthusiast. While the size of the place is on the smaller side and parking can be a bit of a challenge, these are minor inconveniences compared to the quality of the food. The buzz around the restaurant being featured on the Food Network adds an extra layer of coolness to the experience. Overall, this cozy spot is highly recommended for a tasty crepe indulgence.

First time to New York City and visiting Times Square. We absolutely loved our visit to the city and had an incredible week. So many great restaurants, so many incredible sites. I can honestly say that walking into Ruperts deli to grab a snack and a couple of beverages was one of the big highlights of our week. If you grew up like we did watching David Letterman every night and saw just a few of the dozens of times that Rupert was on the show -you might have the same feeling and experience. It was so unscripted, we walked by and saw the sign to the Deli and thought, wonder if he's actually owner of this place or was the whole thing done by an actor for Letterman's script? Sure enough we walked in and it was like meeting a big time movie star in plain clothes, and he looked exactly the same as when he first appeared on the show in 1993. Upon our arrival he offered to help and to pose in photos with us. He could not have been nicer! What an amazing surprise fun stop and experience during our week in the big Apple. Our hearts and prayers go out to Rupert and all the wonderful people in NYC during this difficult time. Be safe, be well, be healthy, be strong!

Sauce Pizzeria has quickly become a favorite due to its unique pizza slices and the delightful side of vodka sauce that accompanies them. Whether using it as a pour-over to enhance the pizza or watching the kids enjoy it like a soup, the experience is consistently enjoyable. Eager to return for dinner, I highly recommend giving Sauce Pizzeria a try to taste the uniqueness for yourself.

I went here tonight for an event, the food was ok. Nothing really stood out, it wasn't bad, but it wasn't great either. It was just eh.I tried the eggplant- it was ok. A little too much sesame oil imo. The scalloped bbq potatos weren't bad, they had decent seasoning.The mutton on the bone I found to be a little bland. Not worth $22.Monstrous Plate Chicken- it wasn't bad. The size of the noodles were about the same as xian's famous foods. But had the texture of standard handpulled noodles. The chicken was juicy and tender. But definitely not worth $22The sautee cabbage was ok. The chicken skewers was fine, same taste as all of the ones i get in flushing for $1. They were nice and juicy and tender.8 jewel rice pudding-this was definitely my favorite dish of all of them. Visually, it is not that appealing, but tastewise it is very good. I normally don't like red bean paste, but it worked really well in this dish. It was sweet but not too sweet. Overall: Not the best, not the worst, there's better nearby. I likely won't be back though.

Came back here right before quarantine hit and restaurants shut down. Restaurants in Chinatown were already shutting down and this was one of the few still open and not crowded. Came here on March 10 with my cousin for dinner. Chinatown was slowly becoming a ghost town; barely anyone was around and the restaurant was half empty.We ordered 4 items- condense milk butter toast, and 3 rice rolls with dipping sauce. Still delish and can't wait to return once everything settles and reopens.

Title: A Thai Gem in NYC

Upon entering the restaurant, I was immediately struck by the stunning decor, which perfectly encapsulated the essence of sophistication and cultural charm. The staff welcomed me with open arms, their courteous and friendly demeanors enhancing the dining experience.

The highlight of my visit was, without a doubt, the drink - the best I've ever savored in New York City, leaving a lasting impression. As for the meal, it was nothing short of AMAZING. The dishes burst with flavor, masterfully seasoned with the ideal level of Thai spiciness I had requested. It was a culinary delight that met every expectation.

I'm eagerly looking forward to returning on my next trip to the city. For those with a penchant for Asian cuisine, I implore you to secure a reservation at this establishment. Rest assured, it's an experience you won't regret.

Food was tasty but not the most authentic I've had, also a bit over priced for the portion/quality it served. The bread is nice, texture and taste wise. A few drink and food options. The desserts were good, my friend really enjoyed their almond pudding (popular choice) and it was very delicious. The Baklava was nice, I liked it but my friend said it was way too sweet for her liking. It's special, worth a try if you like sweet pastries. Better with coffee or tea though consider it is pretty sweet. Nice texture to their food so it's a plus. The price is definitely much higher than the price on the online menu. Nice atmosphere, gets a bit noisier throughout the night but it's alright. Clean and organized place, quite a few tables and no need for reservation but it's an option. Not the most attentive staffs although quite a few walking around, but the service aren't too bad. You just have to raise your hand or call out to then here and there, but no one had particular bad attitude towards the customers. Walking distance (around 6mins) to 6 or E or orange line or (around 12mins) to the 7 line. Overall, it's a nice dinner and I was satisfied but it's definitely not a place I'd recommend or come back again myself.

Note: Credit Cards only.Taco Dumbo took over this restaurant and opened yesterday.  It feels like this restaurant has changed hands ever year.  Hopefully, this will remain here for a while. In case you are curious, there is another location at 19 W. 52 St.  That will remain there for a week or so when I inquired with an employee then it will be consolidated into 1 location here.This location is a bigger space than the old one.  When you enter the door, it's a bit dark to set the chill mood.  Go to the right, the brightly area, to place your order at the registers.  If you dine-in, you will receive a bottle with sand and a number.  The employees will delivery the food to your table. If you request take-out, it takes a while and your food is ready to go.  I wanted something light so I went with the loaded nachos.  It's blue chips, cashew queso, black bean mash, lime crema, pickled chili and onion.  It has a kick (if you can't take spicy).It satisfied my hunger.  Now there is a place to go relax and chill.  Enjoy.

Title: Misadventures on Taco Tuesday

I ventured to this restaurant with high hopes of a festive Taco Tuesday celebration, but the experience fell short. Anticipation waned when we learned that the coveted rooftop was reserved for weekends only, forcing us to settle for the less exciting entrance floor seating.

The ambiance hinted at potential, with an aesthetic that seemed promising but lacked execution and finesse. The drinks, unfortunately, were underwhelming, lacking the robustness one might expect from a place that should have been buzzing with Taco Tuesday revelry.

To compound the letdown, the restroom lacked a basic amenity—a mirror—which left us questioning the establishment's attention to detail.

Ultimately, we decided to continue our evening elsewhere, in search of that vibrant atmosphere we were initially excited for. A disappointing outcome for what should have been a night of tacos and toasts.

Had the lunch specials. The bibambap and kimchi chigae were great! I'd say the same if not better quality than Ktown. The only comment I'd make is that they should have a few more banchan (little side plates)

I am a major tsukemen fan, so I was more than excited when I heard that a restaurant dedicated solely to tsukemen was opening minutes from my place. We finally made it here on a Sunday evening at 6:30pm. A staff member greeted us from behind the bar and asked us where we'd like to sit. They had both tables and bar spots open at this time, but we opted to sit at the bar.TabeTomo's ambience is much nicer than traditional ramen restaurants in Japan, and also in New York. The walls are dark, and there are several chic looking booths at which to sit for parties larger than 2, though overall, the restaurant is small. We were brought menus and water immediately, and decided quickly on what to order. My husband went with the Tonkotsu Chashu Jiro ramen ($18), which was served before my tsukemen. The broth was every bit the quintessential tonkotsu, hearty, fatty, and rich. The noodles were thick and wavy, just like traditional tsukemen noodles, though not traditional by tonkotsu ramen standards. The jiro ramen was also served with several pieces of fatty pork slices. I am not a big pork eater, and could easily give it up for the rest of my life, but I tried the pork here and was compelled to go back for seconds. It was among the best pork in ramen I have ever had, fatty, juicy, and mouth wateringly delicious. My tsukemen was finally served a few minutes after my husband's dish. It contained the same noodles and the same broth, but I had added on the kuro-oni (Japanese black chili powder) for a mildly spicy kick. It was perfection. Have no complaints about the food whatsoever, but I do have a salt tooth, and think this ramen could be too salty for many people. When we left the restaurant, my husband also complained that the noodles were too thick for him, though they were perfect for me.Service was attentive and polite, they kept our water glasses filled up the  entire evening, which they are usually lax to do in other ramen restaurants.Prices are on par with other ramen restaurants in New York, but I thought the $1 for chili powder was a bit much, as well as the additional $4 in pricing for just one soft boiled egg.However, we had a truly delicious and satisfying meal, and would highly recommend for tsukemen and ramen lovers alike.

Title: A Unique Twist on Thai Cuisine at Thai Country Kitchen

I recently had the pleasure of dining at an exceptional restaurant that presents a unique take on Thai food, distinctly different from the ubiquitous Pad Thai-centric menus. Thai Country Kitchen specializes in what they've aptly named "Thai Country Cooking," offering an array of delectable dishes that tantalize the taste buds.

The crab and turmeric dish stood out with its robust flavors, while the soy braised tofu and vegetables were a revelation. As a usual tofu skeptic, I was pleasantly surprised by the extraordinary taste and texture, akin to a soup-like dish that left a lasting impression.

The pricing structure is refreshingly fair; the concept of selecting two entrees for a single price offers great value without feeling overpriced. The communal dining setup encourages a sense of togetherness, complemented by a remarkably attentive wait staff.

For my friend and me, the experience felt like a hearty embrace of Thai comfort food, yet with a novel twist. If you're a fan of Thai cuisine and open to a different dining encounter, Thai Country Kitchen is a must-visit spot that is sure to impress.

Gonzales y Gonzales offers the ideal ambiance for unwinding with drinks and appetizers or celebrating momentous occasions, which I had the pleasure of experiencing during a birthday party last Saturday. While I sampled only from a pre-selected menu, the offerings were flavorful, hinting that their full menu could impress even further. The establishment boasts some distinctive quirks; a mandatory coat check before the evening progresses and vigilant security are indicative of its transformation into a vibrant Latin dance club, complete with live music that promises an energetic night.

One caveat for groups is the two-hour time frame to enjoy unlimited pitchers of beer, margaritas, or sangria under a party package, after which drinks revert to standard pricing. Despite these peculiarities, Gonzales y Gonzales caters to a fun, spirited evening, especially if you're inclined towards dancing and a lively crowd. My overall experience was positive, and I'd recommend it for anyone looking to kick back or kick up their heels.

Upon entering this New York dining establishment, one cannot help but award it a full five stars for its breathtaking interior alone. The high ceilings evoke a sense of grandeur, reminiscent of the building's storied past, rumored to have once been a bank. While the presence of televisions slightly mars the historical charm, it’s easy to overlook when sipping a drink in such an elegant setting.

Situated conveniently close to my workplace, the restaurant is an ideal spot for swift work lunches with its limited but familiar menu. The kitchen staff graciously caters to dietary needs, offering gluten-free adaptations that are both considerate and visually appealing.

Despite its lack of trendiness or modern flair, the venue boasts an impressive wine selection and a full bar, making it a respectable choice for both colleague gatherings and family meals. It's a place that strikes a balance between convenience, quality, and aesthetic appeal, perfect for a midday meal or an evening out.

Place looks nice and friendly. It was. App was decent, drinks fine. What really bothered me about this place is the  practice of adding gratuity in the bill and then try to add the same amount as recommended gratuity not knowing you may be double tipping the bill. Yes we all should review the bill but just passing that off without saying anything is just sneaky. So, check your bill. The gratuity is added automatically then the same amount is suggested in the bottom of the tip section.

Food is really good, high quality ingredients. Prices are a bit high. Came here to get take-out one night for dinner and it was a very easy efficient experience. I ordered the uni mixed fish bowl with rice and the monkfish liver. The uni mixed fish bowl was delicious, fish was of a high quality cut and very fresh, lots of rice on the bottom. The monkfish liver was a bit pricey $10, just a few piece of the liver, good quality but portion size is a bit small. Overall the quality is good, but do prepare to pay a bit.

Tucked away in a snug corner, this charming restaurant exudes a genuinely Japanese ambiance. Attentive and cordial servers ensured our glasses stayed full throughout our culinary journey. As an izakaya, the establishment boasts a menu that's both delectable and wallet-friendly. Our table enjoyed a lavish serving of toro, perfectly seasoned curry rice, crispy fried smelt, irresistible addictive cabbage, and succulent grilled mackerel. While the sake selection impressed, its price leaned toward the steeper side. Overall, a delightful spot worthy of securing a reservation.

Title: A Ramen Haven in the Heart of NY

Review:

From the moment my friends and I stepped into this cozy ramen spot, we knew we'd stumbled upon something special. The staff greeted us with beaming smiles, setting the stage for an unforgettable dining experience.

As a self-proclaimed ramen aficionado, I can confidently declare this my favorite ramen destination to date! The spicy chicken ramen was nothing short of celestial – the noodles were perfectly balanced, and just when you think you've grasped the spice level, the broth comes in with a delightful kick that leaves you longing for more. Despite my limited appetite, I left wishing I could indulge in seconds.

The ambiance was intimate, enhanced by the snug decor that scored a solid 8/10 on my scale. Although I didn't visit the restrooms, there's a small buzz about them being a bit on the tinier side – but let's be honest, it's the incredible ramen that's the main attraction.

Located in a pleasant part of New York, this gem offers great value for money. If you're in the area and your taste buds are craving some top-notch ramen, do yourself a favor and drop by this place.

People, food, atmosphere – it ticks all the boxes with flying colors. My review? An enthusiastic 10/10! Highly recommended for anyone in search of an authentic and satisfying ramen fix.

I came here for lunch with three amazing co-workers yesterday with our sails set to order from the Yelp Waitlist Secret Menu. Basically, you book your table with their through Yelp Waitlist so you can get in-line remotely from the comfort of your couch, office, bed, gym etc, and when you arrive and let your waiter know, they tell you about their secret menu options, exclusive to Waitlist guests. Only two of us ended up ordering from the Secret Menu and we both got the noodle dish. It was about $22, and it was massive (could share for two people in my opinion)! My colleague was tougher than I as he managed to finish the whole thing in one sitting. I myself however, was getting "the sleepies" and had to waive the white flag (white napkin?) with about 3/4 of my plate remaining. I hate wasting food and since it would be plently for dinner, upon request they kindly packed it up to go for me. Oh I forgot to mention the space... umn what?! It is gorgeous inside. As soon as you walk in, you're greeted by this really cool waterfall wall feature (I want that in my living room!) and at the same time, you see just how huge this place really is. It kind of reminded me of Ninja a little bit (in Tribeca) in terms of sheer presence. You forget your right in Manhattan, which on a Wednesday, is very refreshing, even if for just an hour.

Since I was in the Village, I decided to pick up some food.I have my eye on the crab roll.  The crab pieces were in buttered bun with mayo, lemon butter, and seasoning.  Decided to add a bag of chips.  It satisfied my crab craving.  Yum!This location is on the small size compared to other locations.  There are about 6 stools in a squarish U shaped wooden table.  5/10/19: Advised by owner - there are 8 stools with 1 child seat.They have combos if you want a deal.  Enjoy!
Trendy casual atmosphere. I ordered the corn and cheese sizzling plate, and pork stuffed squid. I really enjoyed it! Definitely would come back here!
