I recently dined at a restaurant where the experience was pleasantly smooth from start to finish. I was promptly seated upon arrival, thanks to my online reservation, and the establishment wasn't overcrowded, which was a plus. 

The interior boasted impressive tall ceilings, creating an open and airy atmosphere. A standout feature was the massive pizza ovens that caught my eye—they were not only an aesthetic touch but also promised freshly baked delights. 

Opting for the double pepperoni pizza, I was taken back to Italy with its authentic thin-crust goodness. It was a hit for me. My dining companion enjoyed a steak and potatoes dish, which was described as juicy and well-prepared, tender enough to merit a mention.

The ambiance of the restaurant was welcoming and congenial, matched by its cleanliness and attentive staff. Overall, I had an excellent time here and would recommend it for a great meal in a comfortable setting.

I came across Chick'nCone on Instagram just in time for my latest visit to the city of New York. I was hoping the food taste just as good as it looks and it did. Myself and two friends were not disappointed. We were provided with samples of the top two sauces (Kick'nRanch and Yella BBQ) before we placed our orders. Service was quick as we were there at 11am on a Saturday when they opened. I'm going back to NY next month and plan to go back to try and different sauce.

During my singular visit to this charming eatery in the East Village, I was immediately taken by its cozy ambiance and the intriguingly diverse selection of noodle bowls. Particularly noteworthy is the steak tartare appetizer, a delightful prelude to the main course.

I indulged in the dan dan mixian, a dish that often leaves me underwhelmed elsewhere due to an inexplicable peanut butter taste. Here, however, it was a revelation. The use of fragrant green Sichuan peppercorns provided the authentic numbing sensation I so desire in this dish, making it an aromatic delight. The pork was succulent, and happily, the noodles avoided the common pitfall of greasiness.

On a subsequent update, I must commend the super spicy cold chicken mixian. True to its name, it packed a punch that was both intense and gratifying. This tip-free establishment has earned my enthusiasm, and I eagerly anticipate my next visit when I'm on the hunt for dinner in the area.

Title: Unmet Expectations at a Three-Star Spot in Hoboken

My recent visit to what promised to be a commendable three-star restaurant in Hoboken was unfortunately underwhelming. The establishment itself boasts a pleasant environment, and the location is prime, but the overall experience did not rise to the occasion.

While the burgers we ordered were satisfactory, the service left much to be desired. A mishap with one of our orders, which we reluctantly accepted due to hunger, was just the start. A more personal gripe is that my burger's doneness was never queried, resulting in a medium-well patty instead of my preferred medium-rare.

Compounding the disappointment, we experienced a delay with our drinks, which didn't arrive simultaneously. And to add to our frustration, after our meal, our waitress seemed to vanish into thin air. Despite the restaurant being empty, we endured a 20-minute wait just to get our check, having to request assistance from the hostess twice. 

The food may pass muster, but given the lackluster service, my return to this establishment is not on the horizon. With the plethora of options in the area, I will be exploring elsewhere.

Title: Cozy Brunch Spot with Room for Improvement

My family of five visited this snug NYC brunch spot at a peak time of 12:30pm on a Sunday. Reservations are a must due to the limited seating of 6-7 tables, and be warned: they enforce a strict $25 per person cancellation fee.

Upon arrival, we encountered a space so tight that it bordered on uncomfortable, which was somewhat alleviated after a bit of re-arranging by the host. Service was less than stellar; a 20-minute wait to order and infrequent water refills were part of our experience. The wait for the food, although lengthy at 30-45 minutes, was somewhat understandable given the unique brick oven preparation.

The menu's farm-to-table ethos is commendable, with food origins clearly listed. The brunch entrees were fairly priced between $10-$25, and while the biscuits were disappointingly dry, the blue cheese mac and cheese was the standout dish—rich and flavorful, though best when shared. My brussel sprout salad, however, was unremarkable. The French toast received praise from my parents for its generous portion size.

In summary, while the restaurant had its highs—the delicious mac and cheese, and a great farm-to-table focus—it was marred by the cramped space and less-than-impressive service. Would I return? Possibly, as the concept is promising, but there’s definitely room for improvement.

Title: Underwhelming Experience at a Highly-Rated Pizzeria

After hearing much praise about this local pizzeria, my visit was unfortunately disappointing. Although the thin crust pizza was expected to be a highlight, the chill of the initial serving led to an unsatisfying start. A request to reheat our meal resulted in three of our four slices being served burnt, detracting greatly from the experience, as the bitter taste of charred crust is not what any pizza aficionado looks for.

The vegan pizza option was similarly lackluster, presenting us with a chewy texture that fell short of expectations. As for the classic cheese pizza, it was a letdown, failing to deliver the gooey, comforting sensation that one craves with such a simple and traditional choice.

On a slightly brighter note, the teriyaki slice, topped with chicken, broccoli, and onion, proved to be just okay, but nothing to write home about, especially when compared to the superior offerings at Tony Boloneys in Hoboken.

On the plus side, the prices were reasonable and the service was commendable. However, despite these small consolations, with the pizza itself being such a letdown, I won't be returning.

Title: A Letdown Experience

I approached the restaurant with high expectations, but I was disappointed to say the least. The grilled cheese and tots were passable, but the fried chicken melt was a letdown. Unfortunately, the chicken was overdone to the point of being burnt and left a bitter aftertaste. While I've read favorable reviews, consistency is key, and my experience was underwhelming. The service didn't do much to lift the spirits either—adequate but not particularly memorable. Overall, the service earns a 3/5, the food a 2.5/5, and the ambiance a standard 3/5.

Came here with my boyfriend for the three-course Valentine's day pre fixe menu and absolutely enjoyed my time here. Well organized, clean and very timely for a busy restaurant. This is a business casual restaurant btw| SERVICE |10/10!Open Table labeled a three-course pre fixe menu before 6:30pm but by the time we got to our 6:15pm reservation, they were already serving their four-course pre fixe menu (obviously more expensive). We explained to our waitress the issue and she was able to get a last minute order in for us from the three-course pre fixe menu (win). | FOOD |*Appetizers*Bread (free) - this is provided before any of your food is served and it's delicious and they can re-supply for free; had to stop myself before I'd get myself too full from it.Tuna Tartare - super savory and tendor, comes with bread as well to eat together (highly rec)Paccheri - loved the amount it had to offer and also a bit cheesy, but I love cheese*Entres*Black Linguine with Scallops - noodles a bit on the rough side but has soft scallops to make up for it. I killed it pretty fastLobster Bolognese - Noodles a bit softer compared to the Black Linguine dish, probably also since there's a bit of sauce sitting on it. Lobster was an A++*Desserts*The Apple - only if you're an apple fan. The entire apple tastes like apple creme sitting on a graham crust with a side of vanilla ice creamChoco Dessert (forgot the name) - Super rich chocolate and sweet. Kinda tastes more on the dark chocolate sided with vanilla ice cream, chocolate chips, and cocoa
Enjoyed cozy ambience, tasty food and efficient service. Everything we ordered was delicious. Tuna with mayo was delish.  Cucumber gintini  just perfect. Go check it out for yourself!

On a bustling Sunday afternoon, the wait at this cozy eatery was quite noticeable, a testament to its popularity despite its modest size and predominantly bar-style seating, with only a couple of window seats up for grabs. Dining as a pair, we indulged in takoyaki and a hearty bowl of ramen each. The dishes, teeming with flavor, arrived swiftly, leaving us gratifyingly full. This spot is ideal for grab-and-go or for those patient enough to endure the wait. The allure of their substantial-looking curry has me keen to return. In summary, it's a culinary haven for the ravenous—just remember to go with an empty stomach. Itadakimasu!

I came to try the best thing on the menu the Mac lobster although it was good and had decent amount of lobster it was just okay for me. I would of like for it to have more flavor. The Mac lobster consist of cognac, tarragon, mascarpone.  The amount of cheese added was well portioned it was more of the type of cheese it had that didn't really wow me. The Mac is very creamy and overall it was good. The wait was about 20 minutes they have refreshments and seating. Keep in mind this place is rather small. The staff was very friendly and welcoming. The Mac lobster for a small it was about $11 the portion is for one person if you want a sharing plate get the Med/large.

Title: Healthy, Hearty, and Friendly – A Lunch Spot Gem

I recently had another delightful lunch at this cozy nook that's perfect for anyone seeking both nourishment and taste. On this visit, I indulged in a side of falafel for just $3, and it did not disappoint. The falafel was exceptional, baked to perfection for a healthier twist, without sacrificing any of the moistness you'd worry about in a non-fried version. The serving was generous, providing great value for money.

This restaurant consistently impresses me with its inventive and delicious offerings, stretching from wraps and bowls to burritos. Plus, they serve breakfast all day, which is a definite bonus for late risers with morning meal cravings. First-time customers who use Ritual can enjoy an introductory discount, which is a nice touch.

Though the space is small with limited seating, it's clearly designed with the bustling takeaway crowd in mind. The ambiance is complemented by the warm and welcoming staff, making every visit a pleasant encounter.

For anyone in the area looking for a quick yet satisfying bite that doesn't compromise on health, this is the go-to spot.

What a special place. I moved to NYC expecting to find hidden gems and this one will particularly make the list. To celebrate my brother's birthday, we wanted to find a quaint, quiet, special spot that offered individualized service and true variety. Their menu offers staples from greek salad to breakfast bowls to shakshuka. Apparently their Mediterranean breakfast - two poached eggs, avocado slices and ricotta served wit chopped cucumber and tomato is a special one.  But truthfully - it's their drinks that harness the true power of this place. I ordered their mint tea and it came loaded with fresh leaves, zero sugar and plenty of taste bud "punch" to keep me going the entire meal. This preceded my order of the "Maya's Breakfast bowl," containing scrambled egg whites, red quinoa, kale, spaghetti squash, grilled tomato, radish and avocado. While I'm not a fan of avocado for its high calorie count, its presentation of being finely sliced made it impossible for me to pass up.If you have reservations, get here ON TIME. The restaurant is so popular that you don't want them to give away your table and wait for the next opening. Service is good, not amazing, but it's clear that the waiting staff are willing to standby and help you pick the right dish. A+ food, great location and thus far, one of my favorite breakfast spots in NYC.

French flavor & chef cred with a chef who worked with Jose Andres in a lovely long space. I was here for the soft opening and the smell alone captivated me. Super friendly service at the bar.They specialize in poultry for two, but lots of fish entrees too.Ate:Leeks with smoked onion $13BreadSo perfect and smoky.. will be back for much more.

- Long line during popular hours so join the Yelp waitlist- Take the elevator to the 2nd floor- Got the beef thin skirt, marinated kalbi, seafood noodles, and green tea cold noodles- Their meats are amazing, skip the noodles- The provide free appetizers but mostly it's just different variations of onions - They give you two types of sauces and salt in a little plate - There's also free lettuce that you wrap the meat in - The waiters will cook everything for you so no need to worry about when your dishes are safe to eat- Since they do the cooking, you might feel pressured to finish the dishes right after they've been cooked- Be prepared to spend some money here if you want to fill up

Tucked away in the bustling heart of midtown, this restaurant offers fair value considering its prime location. The interior is charming, providing a lovely backdrop for what is predominantly a typical Greek diner menu. Patrons seem to favor the Greek salads and gyros, which, while popular, are quite commonplace and don't stand out from what you might find in any diner.

The true star of the show, however, is the moussaka. This dish alone is worth a visit, as it is truly outstanding and a testament to the kitchen's potential. Unfortunately, the same praise cannot be extended to the whole fish, which disappoints due to being overcooked and lacking in seasoning. Accompanying sides such as greens, peas, and salad also fail to make an impression, as they are rather bland.

In summary, if you find yourself in midtown and have a hankering for Greek cuisine, this spot might be worth a try—especially for the moussaka. However, if you're venturing out solely for an extraordinary culinary experience, you might want to consider other options.

Title: Serendipitous Discovery at Koku

I stumbled upon Koku when my original dining plans fell through, and what a delightful twist of fate it was! This gem serves up reasonably priced Korean-style ramen that tantalizes the taste buds. I indulged in the Koku ramen alongside a delectable portion of pork cha shu, both of which left me yearning for more.

What truly sets Koku apart, though, is its inviting atmosphere. With solo seating around the bustling kitchen and spacious accommodations for larger groups in the back, there's a perfect spot for every diner. It brought back fond memories of my cherished ramen haunt in Philly.

For those on the hunt for a bargain, don't miss out on the lunch specials – select ramen dishes are offered at the unbeatable price of $9.99. I'm already looking forward to my next visit to sample another of their signature ramen creations.

Authentic Lanzhou noodles is not something you'd expect to find in midtown east.  So I was very excited when I heard that Dun Huang has opened a location right near Grand Central.  I've been there twice now and can confidently say that I will definitely be a repeat customer moving forward.  Their signature item is the Lanzhou Beef Noodles.  It comes in a spicy broth.  Toppings include thinly sliced beef, radish and a healthy dose of cilantro.  You can also customize the thickness of your noodles, from ultra thin to extra wide.  The noodles are hand pulled and it really makes a difference.  It has great texture and goes perfectly with the spicy broth.  It's truly a fantastic bowl of noodles.

I recently visited a local pizzeria around 10pm and was pleasantly surprised by the range of fresh pizzas still available. The BBQ chicken, chicken bacon ranch, buffalo chicken, and Margherita were among the freshest options, though there were others that appeared less appealing. I opted for a slice of the BBQ chicken, which was flavorful and satisfying, though the crust was a bit too generous for my liking. On a separate occasion, I tried their meat calzone for around $6. It met my expectations, providing a decent meal without any particular flair.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience with a Minor Hitch

My recent visit to this restaurant was truly a very nice experience. The ambiance set by the amazing decor immediately set the stage for a comfortable and enjoyable evening. Throughout our visit, the wait staff were notably helpful and friendly, which added to the welcoming atmosphere. However, there was a slight hiccup when my friend's drink order was delayed and required a reminder to two different waiters.

The culinary offerings were impressive overall. The salad bar boasted a pleasing variety, and the meat selection did not disappoint. Although the chicken skewered towards the dry side, the steak was cooked to perfection and was the highlight of my meal. The side dishes, including the creamy mashed potatoes and the delightfully sweet plantains, complemented the proteins well.

Dessert was another high point, with both the tres leches cake and the molten cake being exemplary choices that capped off the meal beautifully. A word to the wise: arrive hungry, as the portions are generous and you'll want to savor every bite. Despite the minor service misstep, this restaurant delivers a satisfying dining experience that is well worth the visit.

Vintage atmosphere and great food. I ordered a vanilla shake and got way more than I bargained for. The animal house tots were a disappointment though. It was heavy and rich in a bad way. The cheese and beans were too overbearing I wish I just went with regular tots. The mac n cheese grilled cheese is delicious though. I didn't get to snag a pic but not messy at all to eat and tasty

Title: A Delightful Taste of Spain at Hudson Yards

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a fantastic Spanish eatery nestled in Hudson Yards, and it’s safe to say that the experience was nothing short of exquisite. With an extensive range of authentic dishes, there’s something to satisfy every palate.

I kicked off my pre-lunch treat with their churros, fresh from the fryer, and at $5 for 6, it was an absolute steal. Crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, these churros were pure bliss.

Next came the chicken croquettas, priced at $12 plus tax. These little morsels of joy, fried to order, were packed with flavor and well worth every penny.

Although the menu brimmed with temptations like Spanish empanadas, Jamon y queso, and patatas bravas, my appetite was fully satiated by the churros and croquettas alone.

For anyone around Hudson Yards, I couldn’t recommend this place more. Those churros are a must-try and, in my opinion, were the highlight of a thoroughly enjoyable visit.

Very very nice Japanese restaurant. I was lucky enough to come here with some friends. They had been here before and said it was delicious. You have to navigate some steps to get to the restaurant, as it is on the 2nd floor. Not sure if there was a lift or anything. Very traditional Japanese feel and vibe here. The decor as well. I was here for lunch during the week so it wasn't too busy. Not sure what else was on the menu but we all ended up ordering the eel. It was bought out raw for us to inspect before cooking which was a nice touch. Served over a bowl of rice as well as a salad and soup. Delicious. Obviously very fresh and you could taste the difference versus not. I will definitely be back when I can.

I had a delightful dining experience at Vapiano in Union Square, just a stone's throw away from the Nutella Cafe. The establishment offers a tantalizing array of pizzas and pastas, with my personal favorite being the rich Pesto and Prosciutto pizza, reasonably priced at $14 for a generously sized pie.

Ordering is a breeze thanks to an efficient buzzer system that alerts you when your food is ready, eliminating the need for the usual tableside wait. Additionally, Vapiano's modern payment approach, where you tap a card to order and pay at the end of your meal, streamlines the entire process, allowing for a hassle-free dining experience.

The ambiance of the place strikes the perfect balance of sophistication and warmth, making it an ideal setting for a casual meal. Given its combination of ease, affordability, and quality, Vapiano is a must-visit spot for anyone looking for a great meal in Union Square.

Above average Italian trattoria located in the Theater District and on a block filled with many restaurants. I was eager to try after more than 1000 Yelp reviews gave it a solid 4 stars.We did not have reservations and since it was around 6:30 p.m., there was a 15-20 wait for a table. Had I known, I would have made a reservation. After 20 minutes, I was seated even though my friend had not arrived yet. That policy is always appreciated. The atmosphere was cozy and nearly every table was occupied. Nino's 46 has quite the fan base. It was very busy and chaotic at times. Once my friend arrived, we placed an order for wine, averaging at $11 per glass. I enjoyed my Rose while my friend was satisfied with her Pinot Grigio.The menu contained several categories such as appetizers, pizza, fresh pasta, mains, sides and select desserts.We had our eye on the pizza. Most on the varieties  included some kind of red meat limiting my selection to the only 2 vegetarian pizza options..My friend and I decided to split the two vegetarian styles--the San Marzano (classic cheese and sauce) and the Green pizza (kale, artichoke, ricotta/white based).The pizza arrived not long afterwards and as a personal pie, was smaller compared to other restaurants.I enjoyed both styles but it wouldn't fall in my category of favorite pizza. The crust was good albeit a bit doughy.  Flavors were good as far as the toppings but the Green pizza flavors did not stand out. They blended together.The noise level of all patrons talking at once in the space was somewhat frustrating. It was very loud.I think I would try Nino's 46 again but not sure if I would rush back.

Hot pitas. Cool labneh yogurt. Spicy schug spread. My bar is high for Mediterranean (I lived abroad) I and Kubeh makes the cut!Great quality pitas, spreads, and classic Israeli dishes like shakahuka. They offer many unique items that you can't usually find at a basic place like mallawach and jachnun (only available on the weekends). I had the chickpea stew for brunch and added eggs. It was so good and so unique. The stew was served on top of rustic bread and the bread soaked up all the flavor. At dinner another time, I had the iraqi vegetable kubeh. A light and refreshing vegetarian soup.The ambiance is really nice. The sweet spot between casual and classy with a modern Mediterranean flair. Bright and spacious layout making it easy to hear the people you're with. I made a reservation for 6 and we got a nice wooden booth to ourselves. Kubeh has friendly service and healthy-ish food that'll leave you feeling full but good. I'll definitely return to try more and get my fix of fresh pita and dips!

MSG pre Queen concert dinner this is the go to place for a quite  before the storm drinks and dinner place. Very relaxing chill vibe and food is always on point. Started with white bean bruschetta with ricotta was very original dish .also had the coconut shrimp special with cucumber and mango salsa so refreshing and vibrant.  I ordered grilled shrimp and scallops with cauliflower quinoa we also ordered a romaine salad trying to be good. To end the dinner we ordered double expresso with a chocolate moose. To die for.  This is a great place to chill and relax and have a good dinner across the street of MSG. NO parking on street unless u want to have a bad day.

Title: Elegance Meets Expectations at a City Dining Gem

I was whisked away for a surprise lunch at a renowned city restaurant known for its opulence and esteemed clientele, predominantly New York business executives. A word to the wise: this establishment demands an upscale dress code. Despite donning a chic sweater, slacks, and boots to contend with the winter chill, I found myself feeling slightly underdressed amidst the well-heeled patrons.

Catering predominantly to pescatarians, the restaurant boasts an array of extraordinarily fresh fish dishes that would delight any seafood aficionado. However, as a vegetarian, the menu left me wanting. The lunch special, while providing a trio of courses—a meze platter, grilled vegetables, and a walnut cake—was merely satisfactory, with nothing standing out as particularly remarkable.

While the presentation and service were impeccable, the offerings, particularly for non-fish eaters like myself, didn't justify the price tag or the necessity for such formal attire. Unless my partner has a hankering for a specific aquatic delicacy that only this spot can satiate, it's unlikely we'll return. For vegetarians and those preferring a more relaxed environment, there may be other venues that better align with your palette and style.

Title: Cozy Dinner Before Ballet

My boyfriend and I stopped in for an early dinner at 5:00pm at a charming little spot before catching ABT's "Sleeping Beauty" at The Met. Reservations seemed unnecessary at that time, though the place filled up soon after we settled in. The humid day steered us to the comfortable indoors where we kicked off the meal with a refreshing carafe of Pinot Blanc, offering just the right amount for two.

In anticipation of the show and not knowing how long food preparation might take, we skipped appetizers and went straight for the main courses. My squid ink pasta was a delightful choice, with a savory boost from the crumbled bread crumbs on top. My boyfriend's salmon was well-received, although I personally wasn't as impressed – a matter of personal taste rather than quality.

The service was amiable, albeit a tad leisurely, but it didn't detract from the relaxed ambiance. We finished our meal in good time, leaving us a leisurely window to seek out dessert before the ballet. Overall, the experience was gratifying, with a note to perhaps explore other dishes on a future visit.

My recent visit to TIE DIE left a savory impression. The highlight was certainly the 'Clam Pie' - though not everyone's favorite, I found it to be quite enjoyable. On the other hand, the 'Fried Rice Ball' was a bit underwhelming, lacking the rich flavors of cheese and prosciutto that one would expect. While it didn't ruin the experience, it was just passable. Overall, TIE DIE serves up delightful dishes with a couple of hits and misses.

During Restaurant Week, my family and I were treated to an exceptional dining experience at one of Chef Jean-George's esteemed establishments. The ambience struck a balance between sophistication and comfort, boasting a vibrant and sensuous design that elevated our meal without an ounce of pretension.

The service was nothing short of exemplary; attentive, swift, and genuinely friendly, complementing the culinary journey ahead. My starter, the kombu cured salmon, was a work of art both in presentation and taste, though admittedly, I was left craving more.

The main course continued to impress with a duck breast prepared to perfection—medium-rare as it should be, with skin that provided the ideal crunch. Accompanied by grilled zucchini and a subtly spiced mole sauce, the dish was a symphony of flavors.

Capping off the meal was the molten chocolate lava cake, a rich and indulgent treat made even more special by the staff's thoughtful timing. Their considerate gesture of pausing service while I stepped away ensured the dessert arrived in pristine condition, demonstrating an exceptional level of service.

This dining experience was a testament to the quality and care that defines Chef Jean-George's culinary empire. It's without question that I'll be returning for another taste of this magnificent fare.

Working down the street, I've been here a bunch for after work drinks, but this was my first dining experience. Met up with a few friends for restaurant week. Started with the wedge and upgraded to the bone in Ribeye. The wedge was refreshing and my steak was cooked perfectly. It was an altered menu, but it was a delicious meal. Nothing bad to say, BP cooks a great steak.

Title: Mixed Feelings During NY Restaurant Week

My boyfriend and I decided to experience this restaurant for NY Restaurant Week on a Friday night and our sentiments about the meal diverged by the end of the evening. He thoroughly enjoyed the meat-dominated selections, grading them a solid 4 out of 5, while my impression settled at a 3 out of 5.

Pros:
- Unique Flavors: While the dishes didn’t personally appeal to my palate, they offered a distinct deviation from the typical Thai restaurant fare, which could be a draw for those seeking culinary adventure.
- Restaurant Week Variety: The event provided an opportunity to sample an array of dishes, which seemed to be a hit as many patrons around us partook in the variety.
- Group-Friendly: The large tented area at the back catered comfortably to a big group, making it a viable option for large gatherings.

Cons:
- Service Pacing: We encountered notably slow service, which might have been due to a large group dining simultaneously. This left us waiting for our meals longer than desired.
- Dish Disappointments: On a personal note, the first course tipped too far on the sour spectrum, the Khao Soi didn't live up to my anticipation, and the vegetable curry struck a sweeter note than my preference.

If you're considering visiting, it may be wise to choose a quieter time to avoid the service delays we faced.

Title: A Flavorful Twist on Curry in Ktown

Nestled amidst the somewhat unremarkable food scene of Ktown, Abiko Curry emerges as a delightful surprise for those craving something different. Their signature dish is Japanese-style curry with a Korean flair, offering a taste that is both unique and authentic.

Although the menu can be a bit perplexing – separating curry rice and "special combo" dishes more by the inclusion of a drink rather than the presence of katsu – the quality of food compensates for any confusion. Be warned, items listed under "pork curry" will not feature katsu, but rather pork pieces within the curry itself. Don't let the small pictures discourage you; instead, focus on the promise of flavor.

The price point, $19 for a katsu curry with rice and a drink, might seem steep, but the excellence of the dish justifies the cost. Patience is key, as you may wait up to 45 minutes for your meal, but the result is one of the finest curries you can find in NYC. With spice levels starting at 1 – which already packs a punch – you'll want to choose your heat wisely.

The curry is rich and aromatic, paired perfectly with a katsu that maintains a crispy coating firmly attached to the meat. While peak times may increase your wait, the end reward is undeniable: for outstanding curry, Abiko Curry is definitely worth your time and taste buds.

This place was truly a disappointment.  The food is bland and so is the service.  Within minutes after we placed our order, the appetizers arrived.  I started my meal with the tofu vegetable soup which tasted like hot tap water with a pinch of salt.  While there were plenty of veggies, they were tasteless and the tofu was entirely too soft. My friend had the scallion pancakes which he seemed to enjoy.  While my appetizer was a fail,  I remained optimistic about the rest of my meal.  We ordered the shrimp with asparagus and the Shanghai bok-choy with shiitake mushrooms and bean curds.  Can you say hospital food!  One would have thought we were on a restricted diet in a hospital.  No salt,  no pepper,  no flavor, just cardboard flavored watery vegetables and 4 shrimps.That didn't stop us.  I guess we are indeed glutens for punishment-- we dared to order dessert.  Fried green tea ice cream and matcha tiramisu. The fried ice cream was ok. The tiramisu was equivalent to a dish sponge!  The decor is not much to speak on so I won't.

I recently visited a charming little Mediterranean gem that may be small in size, seating just 32 patrons, but it's absolutely huge on flavor. The appetizer sampler itself is a culinary adventure, offering a delightful range of tastes perfect for those keen to explore new dishes. For the main course, the shakshouka was a standout—both the beef and the green (spinach) versions were scrumptious and arguably the best I've ever tasted. Add to this the surprise of very reasonable prices, and you've got a winning dining experience. For anyone looking for quality Mediterranean fare that's both kosher and non-dairy, this spot is ideal for brunch or really any meal. It comes highly recommended!

Title: Good Vibes, Tiny Portions

My dining experience at this restaurant was a mix of highs and lows. The atmosphere was elevated by live entertainment featuring a talented singer and violinist, which made our meal more enjoyable. Our waitress, Camila, was a highlight as well—attentive, informative, and always on top of our drink refills. However, the food portions left us wanting more; the tacos served with minuscule sides of rice and beans didn't satisfy, and the unexpected $2 charge for extra chips to accompany the guacamole was a disappointing surprise. While the carnitas tacos, truffle fries, al pastor, and chicken tacos we ordered were tasty, the portions didn't quite hit the mark. The complimentary shot of house tequila for checking into Yelp was a nice touch, but overall, we found ourselves seeking additional food elsewhere post-dinner. Great service and entertainment, but beware of the portion sizes and hidden charges.
Speak easy trendy with great small plates to share. Loved the meatballs and the pastrami style carpaccio.

Their Christmas decoration is on point!! And service was overall great. However, their food was great disappointment. Ravioli was like chewing raw flour (it seemed very old..) It served cold and hard. I can confidently tell that this ravioli was the worst ravioli that I ever had in my life. Their burger was alright. Even though they have beautiful interior, I won't be visiting this place again.

The people here must not like me on three different occasions; they had forgotten my order.  This issue has spanned over two years, and I don't come too often. I understand the place is busy but do not placate me by telling me "5 minutes more," and after 30 minutes acknowledged, they had forgotten the order.  The food is not worth the aggravation of waiting for congee that cooks less than a minute. New Wong and Wu's Wonton King restaurants are better alternatives.

This massive beer hall gets loud and rowdy, but it's one of my favorite group drinking spots because the food's also pretty decent.All hail the massive Oktoberfest pretzel with mustard and beer cheese! The sausage platters are pretty hefty and satisfying as well (I'm partial to the cheese-filled Käse-Wurst, and all the platters come with potato salad, sweet and sour red cabbage, and sauerkraut), but the giant pretzel's where it's at. Easily enough to share with a small classroom of people even if you're stuffing your face. That and a liter of deliciously sweet and refreshing Schöfferhofer grapefruit beer are enough to make me a happy camper.I got the two-liter Das Boot once. All it'll do is hurtle you toward the bathroom every half an hour. If you want the same cute photo-worthy glass mug minus the damage to your bladder, get the little boot.They also have shotskis, which are a fun one-and-done experience, but I'll take the grapefruit beer any day.

Title: Mixed Feelings on the Spicy Spring Experience

I popped by during a weekday afternoon, post-lunch rush, aiming to snag a slice of their famed Spicy Spring pizza. Unfortunately, a 15-20 minute wait ensued due to what appeared to be underestimation in the kitchen; they were low on their star offering, while less popular items languished, seemingly untouched, in the display case.

The efficiency of service could undoubtedly benefit from a reevaluation of their production priorities - perhaps reserving made-to-order for delivery could alleviate the in-store wait times. Additionally, the barely legible chalk menu on the wall could use a refresh for clarity's sake.

Onto the pizza itself: the slice delivered on taste, though I imagine it reaching celestial heights of enjoyment after a night out. However, the grease level was excessive, rendering the experience rather messy. The doughy bread base struggled under the weight of the sauce and cheese, with a sturdier bottom crust needed to prevent it from becoming a soggy carrier for the otherwise delicious fra diavolo sauce, which was flavorful but not as spicy as anticipated.

The pepperoni, living up to their reputation, were a highlight. They crisped up into delightful little cups, albeit ones filled with the aforementioned grease, which I found myself draining before consumption.

In conclusion, while the pepperoni and sauce hit the mark, the overall execution left something to be desired, especially given the lengthy wait time. A good slice, no doubt, but not worth a repeat 20-minute queue.

I had the pleasure of visiting an Italian cafe that exudes tranquility, offering a creamy cappuccino that hit all the right notes. Not only is the ambiance soothing, but the prices are unbeatable—imagine savoring a $6 piadina in arguably the city's finest neighborhood! With the convenience of WiFi, I'm eagerly anticipating days spent working from this gem, indulging in their egg piadinis for breakfast, and savoring the prosciutto and cheese come lunchtime, all while enjoying their rich espressos. A well-deserved 5-star experience!

Title: A Little Slice of Italy with Superb Dining Experience

From the moment my husband and I stepped into the restaurant on a bustling Saturday at 11:40 AM, we were whisked away to what felt like a charming eatery in the heart of Italy. Despite not having a reservation, we were promptly seated, and by the time we left an hour later, it was clear why the place had filled up so quickly – the food and atmosphere are irresistible.

The pasta, particularly the fusilli, was a standout, boasting authentic flavors that had us savoring every bite. I didn't try the omelet myself, but the granola was a delightful surprise, demonstrating the kitchen's prowess beyond traditional Italian fare. The ambiance of the restaurant added to the allure, with a cute and inviting decor that complemented the overall experience.

What truly set this restaurant apart, though, was the service. The staff could easily double as models, but it was their attentive and friendly demeanor that made us feel so well cared for. Their professionalism added an extra layer of enjoyment to our meal.

In a nutshell, this establishment is a gem that I wholeheartedly recommend. For anyone looking to be transported to Italy without leaving their hometown and indulge in incredible cuisine, this is the place to be. We're already planning our next visit!

Title: A Cozy Respite at South of the Clouds – A Soup to Warm Your Soul

As the chill of NYC began to seep into my bones, I found refuge in a delightful spot called South of the Clouds. On a dreary, rain-soaked day, their tomato soup base proved to be the culinary equivalent of a warm hug – perfect for pre-study session fuel.

Don't let the simplicity of the dish fool you; the tiny pepper worked its magic, adding a gradual heat that built up with each spoonful. The soup's slight sourness complemented the spiciness beautifully, creating a balanced and comforting bowl. For the spice aficionados, the option to amp up the heat with extra pepper oil is a welcomed touch.

I left with warmth in my belly and an eagerness to return, eagerly anticipating what other treats the menu holds. South of the Clouds is truly a standout for anyone looking to escape the cold with some good, heart-warming food.

If you:1. Work in the area or find yourself in Tribeca2. Enjoy good quality Indian food, THEN,You should make your way to Benares.Looks are deceiving and from the outside, the place resembled a quick lunch takeaway establishment. Once inside, it was full table service and when we arrived around 1 p.m., it was nearly filled to capacity.There is also an old saying--if the cuisine you're dining at appears to have natives dining there too, it might be an indicator that the food is good. I was pleasantly surprised when I perused their wonderful lunch menu. In fact, I didn't bother to read the other menu presented to us. Many Indian restaurants are known for their delicious buffets, but at Benares, the buffet is brought to you!There were 3 pre-fixe options for lunch (btw, all include dal, rice, naan or paratha and dessert): vegetarian at $11.95, meat at $13.95 or seafood which was $16.95. There was also a Tandoori platter option at $18.95.We chose one vegetarian and one meat platter although I stuck with my vegetarian without trying the meat/chicken. Aside from what was included, there was a choice of two courses. For appetizer, I chose the Paneer Tikka which were two delightful precise squares of deliciousness. Delicate flavors and airy. The meat option appetizer was the Seekh Kabab (chicken) which resembled little sausages. No complaints about this selection.For main, I decided to go with a pureed eggplant dish of which the name escapes me. Coupled with the rice, dal and naan, I felt like I completed a dinner! The non-vegetarian main was a Chicken Tikka which looked amazing. We finished our lunch meal off with a delicious custard like dessert that had some fresh fruit integrated in it.There was so much food that we left some behind (confession--I wanted to take the rice and naan with me!).I really enjoyed my first time introduction to Benares. Service was attentive and prompt while food was delicious and inexpensive. I was too engaged in my meal to observe the atmosphere.What I do know is that I'm returning ASAP. Try it.

Happened to pass this place and they had a sign outside saying everything was half price (happens 30 minutes prior to closing daily).  It's a lot like Wasabi, where it's sort of factory-made sushi prepackaged and ready for grab and go.  Like Wasabi, they also have hot items as well.  Normal pricing is a bit high for the quality, but for half off, it's a value.I went with a to-go box with three salmon nigiri and four slices of salmon roll.  It's usually $6.99, so only cost me $3.50.  Comes with a packet of soy sauce included, but no wasabi.  It must be available somewhere, but I missed it.What stood out to me was the ratio of fish to rice was way off on the nigiri.  There was way too much rice for how thin the slice of salmon was.  The salmon roll was better proportioned.  Nothing special about it, but a nice snack.At full price, I wouldn't come here.  Sushi is supposed to be served at room temp or slightly higher than room temp.  For the price, you can almost go to a normal sushi place.  But at half off for a quick snack? Sure.

I recently dined at Kyma and was impressed with the selection of seafood on offer. The ambiance is inviting with a soft light color interior that enhances the dining experience. The Fried Calamari was a hit, perfectly crispy, and the accompanying tomato dipping sauce added a delightful tang.

The menu offers a variety of dishes, and while the Octopus and Tuna Tartar were merely okay, I must admit that tartar dishes aren't typically my favorite. The Zucchini Chips, on the other hand, were delectable—a simple dish done right.

I had mixed feelings about the Tomato Shrimp; the creamed tomato base didn't match my expectation of fresh tomato, which was somewhat disappointing. However, the Branzino made up for it, serving up both freshness and flavor that captivated my palate. The Cod, though, was unremarkable.

One aspect that did detract from the otherwise pleasant experience was the service; our waiter seemed disengaged throughout our meal. Despite this, the quality of the food at Kyma is undeniable, and seafood lovers will likely find plenty to rave about.

You can't beat the price to quality/flavor ratio. Hand made and sooo good, the green ones are veggie, pink are chicken (not in photo), and spicY beef were soo good as well. Amazing price, filling and satisfying.
Hands down the best BBQ ribs and Chicken & Waffles I've ever had! The drinks are great there as well, you  get a bang for your buck. The soul food and the environment are amazing and correlate.

During a recent visit to Totto Ramen's "Next Door" location, I had the pleasure of sampling their Mega Paitan ramen. Unbeknownst to me, this wasn't the flagship store, but it didn't disappoint. The ramen was a hearty dish, boasting wavy noodles, a variety of pork forms including succulent char siu and hearty pork belly chunks, as well as a mix of garlic, onion, bean sprouts, scallions, cabbage, and a perfectly "half-boiled" egg.

The char siu pork and pork belly were the undeniable highlights of the meal, adding significant flavor and texture. The portion size lived up to its "mega" title, offering a substantial meal for about $5 more than their classic Chicken Paitan, which seemed reasonable for its status as the "best seller".

Service was efficient, though not remarkable. Fortunately, the convenience of paying with credit cards or Apple Pay at the "Next Door" location was appreciated. I'm already planning a trip to the original spot and will keep in mind it's a cash-only establishment.

I liked this place for an easy night out downtown with the friends. Vegan Mexican food doesn't initially sound like it's a hit for everyone, but the food is done well. Vibe is the best thing about this place, it's classy and casual all at the same time. Service is A++. Drinks are tequila based and definitely hit the spot. All of the food is good, and I'd really try splitting appetizers across the table. We drank a lot and paid about $75 each (tip was included with a party of 5). All of the flavors were Mexican reminiscent, and I didn't really crave meat, they seemed to imitate it well, and provide a guilt free feeling. Only real issue is that there was only one bathroom. Try their habanero garlic onion hot sauce! Super spicy.

Beyond sushi is a reliable spot for veggie food, and the service is really good at this location. Recently, I had the Edamame salad, Nutty buddy wrap, Seaweed salad and Sweet tree roll. The nutty buddy is definitely my favorite thing to get (I've tried to recreate it at home but I can never get it just right). They're also on Ritual, so it's easy to order takeout.

Title: Casual Vibes and Tunes at Local Spot

I stopped by this spot on a Wednesday evening with friends and found it to be a decent hangout. The atmosphere was enlivened by a DJ, creating a vibe that was energetic and conducive to a midweek outing. Initially, we were seated in the lounge area, which had a less than pleasant odor—likely from proximity to the restroom—but the staff was accommodating when we requested to move.

Seated by the window, the experience improved. The drinks at this establishment were solid and reasonably priced for the area. As for the food, it was typical bar fare. I opted for the 8th Ave burger, which was unremarkable but satisfied my appetite after a few drinks.

While this place isn't a must-visit destination, it's a good enough choice if you're nearby and in search of a spot for post-work drinks with friends.

Title: A Delightful Surprise for Diverse Tastes

If you're in the mood for an eclectic dining experience, this gem of a spot has you covered with its unique menu that comfortably houses ramen, sandwiches, and beer under one roof. I opted for the Isa Sandwich, a warm, panini-esque delight with a notable punch from the perfectly spiced peppers. My companion's vegetarian preferences were effortlessly accommodated with a steaming, flavorful bowl of ramen. The service was as pleasant as it was efficient, which was a bonus considering the place had a relaxed vibe without being crowded. Don't let the exterior scaffolding deter you; venture in and you'll find this intriguing eatery is worth the hunt.

5/5 for ambiance/atmosphere3/5 for food4/5 for hospitalityreservation required for the weekend brunch buffet$50 for buffet style brunch; prepaid upon reservation - includes unlimited coffee, tea, juices- buffet options are actually quite bland, even the fried chicken which was disappointing- alcoholic drinks are extra, and are quite priceyI'd go back just for the drinks, and the ambiance, but I'd probably skip the food.

I recently visited my usual pizza spot, which typically serves up excellent pies. We decided to order two pizzas – a classic white pizza, which remains my all-time favorite, and a half buffalo chicken, half broccoli chicken. Unfortunately, our experience was marred when we discovered a piece of hair in one of the pizzas. The staff promptly replaced it with two slices of artichoke pizza, but the issue did dampen the overall dining experience.

Moreover, the service left much to be desired. The employee who assisted us came across as brusque and unapproachable. His curt manner made us feel like a nuisance, which is certainly not the feeling one wants when seeking a pleasant meal out. While the food quality was, as usual, satisfactory, the disappointing service might give pause to patrons looking for a welcoming atmosphere along with their pizza.

Celebrating Rosh Hashanah, I ventured into Friedman's on 31st in Manhattan and was greeted with a warm smile from Josh, the host. The ambience at the counter was elevated by Tania's infectious energy (forgive any misspelling). I indulged in a robust coffee alongside a delightful tofu, egg scramble with avocado—deliciously complemented by a tasty potato hash and perfect wheat toast.

Service was impeccable, with Tania ensuring my coffee cup never emptied and Josh checking in for a personal touch. I even made a new Seattle friend, adding to the convivial experience. At $27.22, the value was extraordinary, considering the generous portions, attentive service, and unlimited stellar coffee refills. The menu's variety, including tempting options like Eggs Benedict with Salmon, secures my return visit. Shanah Tovah—Friedman's has truly kicked off my New Year with a bang!

I got the maki roll combo with spicy tuna, spicy salmon, and spicy crunchy crab. The portion size is generous - you get a lot of fish bang for your buck. The restaurant itself has bar seating if you want to watch TV, although the table height is a little awkward. There is table seating, and also chef bar seating. The ambience is sort of sports bar-esque and casual.

My frirnd takes me here for lunch. It's a very adorable little place. The decor is simple and pretty. The food was great. We had the mussel appetizer. It was soft, sweet and melt in your mouth. Interested fettuccine alla bolognese was great. Perfect blend of meat sauce and pasta was definitely al dente.  My friend had pappardelle con salsissia - the sweet sausage was great as well. If I had one complain would be the amount of time it took for dishes to arrive.  We ran out of time and will have to try dessert another time. But definitely will come back.

Title: Long Wait Times Cast a Shadow on a Decent Brunch Experience

My recent brunch experience at this popular spot was a mixed bag. The two-hour wait on a Sunday during peak hours was a significant drawback. However, the delay inadvertently accommodated a friend's late arrival, turning the extended wait into a casual outdoor catch-up session.

Once seated, we were greeted with prompt and efficient service. I opted for the avocado toast with a poached egg which featured fresh ingredients but wasn't exceptional enough to justify such a lengthy wait, especially when compared to other Australian brunch venues I've visited.

In summary, while the food and service were solid, I would only consider returning if the restaurant could guarantee more reasonable wait times.

I'm pretty sure the word of mouth for Momofuku overrides anything I put forward for a review.  The fact is I know about a dozen people that have been. Of them, EVERYONE agrees whole heartedly this is is easily one of the best. So when we were in the Columbus circle area we were happy to shoot up to the 3rd floor and grab a bite.  We got supremely lucky.  2 spots were open right at the bar.  The only 2 spots, but we were glad there wasn't a wait.  Our server ran off the specials and we grabbed the buns and sprouts.   These were to be followed up by spicy beef and Smokey pork.  The buns were so good.  We almost had to flip a coin over the last one.  The sprouts were better than the ones I make, and I'm very proud of mine.Then came the ramen.  The spicy beef I ordered was great, but we actually preferred each other's so I switched to the smoky pork.  WOW.     Yeah, that good.  When we are back in a few months, we will assuredly be at Momofuku.

I came here on a Saturday around noon, and the wait was about 20 minutes. Be aware that they don't let you put your name down on the waitlist unless everyone in your party is there. One thing that was really off-putting was that the hostess was not super friendly. I typically don't think it matters too much, but on the day we went the hostess was super snappy with us when we put our name down, and when our table was ready and we came to get seated. Made the mood a bit sour. Me friends and I all ended up getting the chicken and waffles since they are known for that. It's really nice that they also have a vegetarian chicken and waffles as well. Tried a bite of it and it's pretty good. Very soft and juicy with lots of flavor. I think their chicken and waffle was great. They brought by butters for the waffles (lemon, raspberry, and thyme) a little later which I thought was odd timing (they probably forgot to give to us and then remembered later). The lemon butter was nice though. Also the cup of fruit is really just a cup of berries by the way for anyone that's interested! A bunch of blueberries, blackberries, raspberries, and strawberries only. Overall, I would have given this place a 4 or 5 Star for their food. Was pretty decent. But I just couldn't because the service was so off putting. Normally I don't think that matters too much and food matters more, but not if it ruins the mood of brunch.

Cafe Carlyle offered an evening that was elevated considerably by the stunning talent of Stephanie Block. Her enthralling performance can only be described as a remarkable display of vocal prowess and charisma. Adding to the allure, Stephanie's husband, Sebastian, graced the stage for a duet, providing a delightfully unexpected "double treat" for the audience. While the room's crowded ambiance and the rather unremarkable fare served at the venue could have been a damper, Stephanie's shining presence ensured that these elements faded into the background. If the opportunity arises to witness Stephanie Block's performance, I wholeheartedly recommend seizing it. She is, without a doubt, a captivating force in the world of live entertainment.

I recently had the pleasure of escaping the chilly weather by ducking into this cozy midtown eatery, conveniently situated a stone's throw from the subway. The service was swift and attentive, allowing for a brief yet delightful dining experience. Though it carries a touch of that expected Times Square tourist buzz, the ambiance didn't detract from the meal.

My indecision was rewarded with their Bento Box, an assortment of flavors and textures that truly hit the spot. The warm bowl of ramen was equally satisfying, providing much-needed comfort. A heads up for fellow spice enthusiasts – splurge the extra dollar for the spicy mayo, it's a worthwhile kick to your meal. Highly recommended for a quick, fulfilling bite in the heart of the city.

Came here with friends for a New Year dimsum dInner. Not too crowded and food was hot and fresh. Service was slow and there was a big party upstairs. Shrimp stuffed tofu, baked pork buns, tofu skin wrapped pork, shrimp and chive dumplings, rib tips, duck and chive noodle,mango pudding and a chow fun with gravy was almost all of our order.

Title: A Southern Gem in NYC: Root & Bone Review

I came to Root & Bone on a friend's suggestion and left with my taste buds dancing in delight. This Southern-inspired haven, helmed by Top Chef talents Jeff McInnis and Janine Booth, has truly outdone itself in delivering a slice of the South to the Big Apple.

The service was impeccable, thanks to the fantastic bartender, Emory, who filled us in on the restaurant's backstory while adding a personal touch to our experience. Choosing the family-style "southern favorites" was a wise decision for my coworkers and me; at $35, the value was unbeatable.

We began with airy biscuits and innovative pickled beet deviled eggs, perfectly setting the stage for what was to come. Each side, from the refreshing grilled watermelon and radishes to the tangy buckwheat cheddar waffles and the creamy baked macaroni & cheese, brought comfort in every bite. 

Yet, the true showstopper was the sweet tea brined fried chicken, a dish that alone could pull me back time and time again. The blend of a crispy coating, succulent meat, and a hint of lemony sweetness created an unforgettable harmony, especially when accompanied by their housemade tabasco sauce.

Desserts were the grand finale, with a trio of temptations. While each was excellent, the key lime pie took the crown, tempting me to take an extra one home.

Root & Bone won't just feed you; it will spoil you with its Southern charm and culinary excellence. Do yourself a favor: visit for the fried chicken and key lime pie, and experience one of NYC's finest southern fare offerings.

This was my first time eating dry hotpot and I'm pretty much hooked on it. At this restaurant you order what ingredients you want to add into your "hot pot", it's pretty much like a Mongolian stir fry but with hotpot ingredients. They calculate the price based on the weight of the vegetables and meat. We got ours mild because my friend doesn't like spicy food that much and it had the perfect amount of flavoring, but I wouldn't mind it being a little spicier.I shared an order with a friend and it ended up around $17 a person, which is pricy but worth it if you are only coming occasionally. They do have refills for rice which is nice.

We were exhausted after walking back from Brooklyn we waited for our hop-on/hop-off bus only to find out they had stopped running I was frustrated and needed to charge my phone we walked into this restaurant and I asked the host if it was possible to charge my phone and we sat had a drink and saw on the menu Junior's cheesecake which was one the places we wanted to go to, however, I am glad we stumbled into this place everyone was friendly.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Self-Service Dining

I popped into this charming spot on a quiet Sunday evening to find a peaceful dining atmosphere. With an efficient self-service setup, you place your orders upfront and wait to be summoned by your order number.

The menu's versatility caught my eye, and I opted for the Baked Chicken Schnitzel, substituting the regular potatoes for cauliflower. The result was a plate of perfection—the schnitzel boasted a crispy exterior without the guilt of frying, all thanks to their impressive oven. Quick service, complemented by the staff's warmth, added to the experience.

The interior, right down to the bathroom, exudes an undeniable cuteness, practically begging to be featured on your Instagram feed. And let's not overlook the delightful complimentary tahini truffles, a perk for Yelp check-ins.

In short, this place is a must-visit. I'm already looking forward to my next meal here. Highly recommend!

Title: A Manhattan Marvel: Steaks Redefined

From the moment you step into the heart of Manhattan’s buzzing steakhouse scene, prepare to have your definition of a great steakhouse utterly transformed. Our experience within the Victorian-styled enclave, complete with ambient lighting and an intriguing collection of pipes along the ceiling, was nothing short of exceptional.

The evening began with a refreshing South Side cocktail, a symphony of gin, lime, and mint that primed our palate for the culinary fanfare ahead. The standard appetizer—a simple array of fresh carrots, celery, olives, and pickles—accompanied by freshly baked bread set a high bar for what was to follow.

The shrimp cocktail, boasting five large, sweet, and succulent shrimps draped in a tangy sauce with a hint of lemon, did not disappoint. But the pièce de résistance was undoubtedly the Porterhouse steak intended for three. It arrived as a colossal testament to the art of dry-aging, with flavors that spoke of meticulous care and attention. Each cut, from the beefy sirloin to the tender filet, was a masterclass in texture and taste, seared to a flawless medium-rare.

As for the service, it was as impeccable as the food—attentive and friendly, making us feel well-cared-for despite the bustling atmosphere.

The only caveat to this stellar dining experience was the lengthy waitlist; a table here is a hot commodity planned well in advance. However, that small hiccup aside, this steakhouse simply left no room for criticism. A visit here is a must for any serious carnivore seeking to redefine their steakhouse standards.

I visited with a large party for a friend's birthday after she learned about Raclette on a viral online video on cheese wheels and melted cheese on food. The restaurant is super tiny, and pretty loud inside when it's got a full crowd seated with everyone talking. I am not a huge fan of having too much dairy at a meal but ended up giving this restaurant a try. The waiters/waitresses were really kind and nice and helped to take photos for us.We had a huge problem when they FORGOT to put in my friend's food order and he sat there for 40 minutes without any dish. All of our dishes came out at different times, so he just assumed that he was the last one to get his food. The first time we reminded our waitress of this, she said it was coming out, but IT NEVER DID! I think the waitress also got off the clock and we got a new waiter, which helped us figure out what happened. TURNS OUT THEY NEVER PUT IN MY FRIEND'S ORDER! So they put his entire meal on the house, but we had to wait another 20 minutes while everyone else was already done with their food! We spent like 3 hours eating here!I found this restaurant to be overly expensive for skirt steak and cheese. The taste of the steak is nothing special, just your regular steak. The cheese was alright, nothing special either. I just didn't get the hype and the price. I am sure there are better options out there for cheese.

Every Valentines Day we do a steakhouse. This year, we chose the Capital Grille, Fidi edition. We had easily the best table in the restaurant. It was upstairs, in a private little room, overlooking the rest of the restaurant. Had a round of martinis to start which were excellent. We ordered a bunch of appetizers for the table to share. The lobster Mac and cheese, crab cocktail, oysters and the spicy calamari. All were great but the lobster Mac was the winner of this round. Big pieces of lobster always makes it great. For my entree I had the Bone in Kona which was cooked perfectly and an amazing piece of meat. Add on sides of truffle fries, creamed spinach and mashed potatoes? A perfect meal.

Title: A Memorable Culinary Journey

My experience at this restaurant surpassed all expectations, solidifying its place as a standout in the world of tasting menus. What truly set it apart was the originality of its cuisine and the meticulous presentation. The thoughtful addition of cards detailing each dish's story and ingredients was a delightful touch, offering an engaging element for home cooks eager to pinpoint the sources of exotic flavors.

Selecting favorites feels almost like a disservice to the menu's breadth of excellence, but highlights included the langoustine tartare, winter squash adorned with caviar, sumptuous king crab, aromatic mussels over rice, and the decadent fried scallops with truffles. Each course was a near masterpiece, leaving us longing for more as the evening drew to a close.

The dinner excelled in every aspect — exquisite food, impeccable service, and warm hospitality. An absolute must-visit for anyone in search of a truly remarkable dining experience.

Title: Mixed Feelings on Mofongo Mastery

I recently visited a local restaurant renowned for its chicken and cheese mofongo, a dish I have quite a discerning palate for. The culinary experience was outstanding; the flavors were rich, with generous portions of chicken and cheese, and the consistency was perfectly moist, easily surpassing my expectations. The meticulousness of their packaging deserves commendation, ensuring that the texture of the mofongo remained uncompromised.

Unfortunately, the service left a sour taste. Upon arrival for pickup, my presence was blatantly disregarded, and only after a man entered did the staff spring into action. My eventual acknowledgment came with an unwarranted side of attitude, a stark contrast to the hospitality one would expect. Speaking Spanish did little to ease the interaction.

The food and expediency of service would warrant a full five stars; however, the unpleasant demeanor of the staff is a significant deterrent. The disrespect was palpable, and while the mofongo might beckon, the prospect of enduring similar treatment does not entice a return visit.

We came here as a party of 5 and this place was pretty empty. The service was wonderful. The food however was mediocre at best. Mango Salad: Very different. I personally wouldn't order again. It's spicy with a heavy dose of fish sauce. Chicken Curry Puff: Flavorful. It was good.Tom Yum Soup: It was okay. Not authentic nor the best.Khao Soi: They literally butchered this dish. Everything about this dish was all wrong from the texture of the curry sauce to the type of chicken that's used.Pancake: Pretty flavorful. I could taste the chives.We also ordered a fish to share and it was just average.2.5 stars

This was not a restaurant that was ever on my list of places to eat, but a friend of mine previously worked here, so I came in one night as I had promised to pay her restaurant a visit. It was a Sunday night around 6pm when we came in, and not very busy, with a lot of tables open. We chose to sit at the bar as my friend was bartending that night. She took care of us that night, giving us several dishes to try, all of which were fantastic. Among the dishes we tried were the grilled Brie, grilled Nueske's bacon, the patty melt, and the Don ameche fillet. The grilled Brie, served with toasted bread and honey was a delight to eat, but something that could have been easily cooked at home. The patty melt was one of the standouts, albeit heavy and greasy. It is the dream hangover cure, and suited for people with larger appetites. My husband thought it was great, but only managed to finish half of his. The nueske's bacon is a thick cut bacon, the likes of which I've never had before. It was rich and flavorsome, the kind of bacon Homer Simpson dreams of. I got the Don ameche fillet at the recommendation of my friend, as it is one of the steaks on the smaller side on their menu. It was cooked perfectly to rare, just as I had asked. Service was pleasant and efficient. Ambience is chic and unique for the area. Would recommend for a moderately priced steakhouse.

Title: A Brunch to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

Our initial plans for a birthday dinner had to be scrapped due to a tight schedule for a show, but we seized the opportunity to experience brunch at [Restaurant Name] the following morning. I'd give this place well beyond 5 stars if I could.

Arriving at 11 AM, we were greeted by the tranquility of being the first guests. Our meal commenced with a creatively presented corn muffin paired with ricotta, almonds, honey, and jam. While delightful, a larger size would have been ideal for sharing.

The highlight, however, was the burger - a testament to the chef's skill even with such a classic dish. Each bite of the perfectly cooked patty, enhanced by cheese, arugula, and a delectable sauce, was a delight. Not to be overshadowed were the exceptional potato wedges, elevated by a unique topping, which complemented the burger flawlessly.

The table also enjoyed chard beef served with eggs and garlic bread, though the burger indisputably stole the show. In celebration of the birthday, we indulged in espresso bread pudding, a satisfying conclusion to our meal.

The blood orange Mimosa I ordered was the proverbial cherry on top, providing a refreshing start to the morning.

Kudos to the chefs, whom I personally thanked with a thumbs-up through the window for the delicious meal. The service was excellent, and I regret not catching the name of our wonderful server.

In short, [Restaurant Name] has left us eager to come back for dinner. This gem is a must-visit!

Title: Happy Hour Haven at Barn Joo

I've found my happy hour sanctuary at Barn Joo! Not limited to weekdays, this gem offers its specials during the weekends too. The menu is packed with flavor, especially the potato croquettes – I'd trek across the city just for these little delights. Their wings are another standout, robust in taste and perfectly complemented by their intriguing cocktail selection. Service is quick, with a side of friendliness, making post-errand stops in Union Square even more rewarding. While I've yet to savor a full dinner experience, the happy hour alone is worth a hearty recommendation. Do yourself a favor and drop by Barn Joo – you won't regret it.

Solid pub food, but service is often lacking.  Good beer selection, clean, and lots of TVs to watch sports.  The shrimp tacos with pineapple salsa are actually quite good, as are the burgers and the "pork wings."

My girlfriend told me she wanted fancy Japanese for her birthday dinner. So I went looking up expensive izakayas in NYC. Wrong... She wanted extremely well done sushi. Thus, we ended up at O Ya and were very very happy.The food is fantastic, I think that goes without saying. If you had an concern, the food is amazing. Done. What I was expecting was the great service. Our server was very friendly, attentive and helpful. She helped me find some sake I'd never had before and was a constant source of information as we had lots of questions about our meal. Also, she was nice enough to put together a little to do for my girlfriend's birthday. Through in a very cool Ambience wiht a fantastic soundtrack and we had the perfect evening. (Seriously, it was one good song after another!) It was absolutely lovely.I don't think I can recommend O Ya enough. The food is great, the service is perfect and the sake selection is amazing. Just go already!

I absolutely adore this gem of a pizzeria! Their pizza crust is perfectly crispy, setting the stage for what I can only describe as uniquely savory pepperoni that tantalizes the taste buds. Don't pass up their Margherita slices either – simply delightful. With a cozy bench for four by the door, the setup seems more suited for a quick grab n' go experience. I often grab a slice to enjoy while strolling around. Service is swift, with an average wait time of less than 10 minutes, but be sure to eat your pizza fresh to maintain that signature crunch. The value is unbeatable, with plain slices at just $1 and topped slices at $2 before the late-night price hike post-10pm. If you're nearby, make it a point to stop by – it's an ideal spot for a tasty, budget-friendly snack.

I recently dined at this Thai restaurant and was impressed by the quality of the food. I started with their chive pancakes, which were an absolute delight. The batter was chewy, perfectly fried to a crisp on the outside while maintaining a pleasing squishiness inside.

The highlight of my meal was the drunken noodle with duck. Although the dish didn't boast an abundance of ingredients or vegetables, it packed a punch in terms of flavor. The noodles were flawlessly flat and expertly cooked to avoid any annoying clumping. However, the duck, which was a pricier addition to the dish, only delivered in terms of crispiness at the end pieces. For future visits, I might consider trying a different meat option.

I also had a chance to sample their pad Thai, which I found to be quite decent. Overall, the experience left a good taste in my mouth, and I would recommend this place for anyone craving authentic Thai flavors.

I recently dined at what I can confidently describe as one of the finest Italian restaurants in New York City, and to my delight, it also boasted incredibly affordable prices. The service was exemplary; our waitress, who had a delightful Italian accent, was nothing short of charming. She expertly navigated us through the menu, and her recommendations were spot-on in flavor and satisfaction.

I chose to indulge in the simple pleasure of spaghetti and was thoroughly impressed; it was, without exaggeration, phenomenal. Unfortunately, due to time constraints, I missed out on trying dessert and coffee, a decision I regret. This establishment is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic Italian cuisine without the hefty price tag.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience

I visited this vibrant spot during the city's restaurant week and was pleasantly surprised by the culinary gem I discovered. Having only experienced the club downstairs previously, dining here was a fresh revelation. Despite its popularity, a reservation made two days in advance secured a 9pm seating, and a brief interlude at the bar allowed us to indulge in their delightful Sangra-itas.

The wait was a mere 15 minutes before we were seated, thanks to the efficient and courteous staff. The food was nothing short of excellent, starting with a perfectly prepared tuna tartare and a generously portioned Caesar salad suitable for sharing. The entrees continued to impress with the papardelle toscana and a penne alla vodka that simply shouldn't be missed. Dessert was a decadent affair with Nutella pudding and Oreo zeppole, both of which were sensational.

While the overall experience was outstanding, the bathroom facilities were notably incongruent with the restaurant's high standards, featuring a quirky sink with low water pressure—an area ripe for improvement.

Service and ambiance were top-notch, and the thoughtful touch of honoring my reservation note to include a birthday candle on my girlfriend's dessert was the cherry on top of a memorable evening. Kudos to the staff for making the night extra special!

This restaurant is fantastic - a great wine list and delicious food! The prices are reasonable and a great location to meet up with friends, a date, or out with family. Dress Code is Casual but you would feel more comfortable in a "Smart Casual" setting.Where else can you go and be served fabulous wines by Pascaline Peltier Master Sommelier MOF? She has an awesome wine list with over 2800 bottles to choose from and 20 by the glass options. Chef Diego made one of the best ducks I've had. Check out my photos for more mouthwatering photos. Looking forward to returning again soon!

One of my favorite spots in the City. I haven't been here for a while, but this place never fails me. Andrew, our server, aced it! Pleasant, attentive, and gave a great recommendation for a drink.Appetizer: steak tartar. Yumm!! We had the skirt steak, special of the day. Lucky for me :) it was made to perfection. And since I don't like any sauces on my steak I asked it will be all on the side. It came on a separate plate with the Chimichuri sauce, shallots, carrots and roasted/fried hot peppers. It was delicious on its own. Ginger martini was delicious. I had two, thank you  The drink special was Cognac sangria. It was interesting. You could smell the Cognac but the flavor was dominated by the red wine. Than Andrew recommended a local dark beer. It was a perfect match for the steak. For dessert we had Creme' brûlée which was perfectly crispy on top and rich, silky inside. I love this place. Don't know why I didn't review it before and don't know why I haven't been here for so long. My bad. Hopefully... will be back soon!
Worth waiting in line for! You pay for what you want get a ticket and not even five minutes later you have yourself one of the best tacos !!!!! I got the carne asada tacos and they were amazing.

Last evening, my husband and I dined at this charming restaurant and had a very satisfying experience. For starters, my husband had the beef carpaccio, which he found delightful. The beef was perfectly thin, and the generous sprinkling of Parmesan cheese was a pleasant touch, though he did add a pinch of salt for extra flavor. My choice of salad was a light and delicious mix of endive, artichoke, hearts of palm, Parmesan, all brought together with a lemon and olive oil dressing. For his main, my husband savored the fresh rolled pasta filled with spinach, ricotta, and mozzarella, topped with a rich tomato sauce that he thoroughly enjoyed. Overall, our dinner was a success and we left feeling very content.

Title: High Hopes, But High Prices Overshadowed the Experience

My recent visit to this restaurant was underwhelming and has convinced me it's a one-and-done kind of place. While the braised pork showed promise with its flavors, the meager four pieces served seemed stingy for its $28 price tag. Charging $3 for a simple bowl of rice felt a bit excessive, too.

We had quite a variety with different dishes, but the bill skyrocketed to nearly $500, which is steep considering we had only four adults and two toddlers at our table – and we left feeling unsatisfied and hungry.

The much-touted bass cooked two ways was an adventure in hidden costs. They offered to make miso soup from the bones, a concept I was eager to try until I learned each bowl, bones included, would set us back $3. It didn't help that they brought out six bowls without confirming the quantity and cautioned about the bones – not exactly toddler-friendly.

The sashimi was nothing to write home about, and the crab, regrettably, wasn't worth its price. We paired it with a decent risotto, but it didn't save the overall experience.

In summary, the combination of steep pricing, small portions, and just good-not-great food means that I won't be revisiting. Despite being a fun outing for the children, the cost just doesn't justify a return.

Title: A Dreamy Carbonara in the Heart of New York

As someone with a discerning palate for pasta, finding a dish that can entice me to indulge is rare, but my recent encounter with a bowl of carbonara on a rainy New York evening was nothing short of stellar. With only 48 hours in the city, my craving led me to this beautiful establishment where the ambiance, especially at the bar, was as satisfying as the meal.

Pros:
- The carbonara was the star of the night: a creamy, perfectly seasoned sauce with a beautifully runny egg yolk, a generous peppery kick, and al dente pasta that was neither oily nor heavy. This dish set a new bar for me; I savored every bite and, for once, finished the entire bowl without the usual aftermath of discomfort.
- Speedy service that's typical of New York's brisk pace.
- A varied menu with ample choices to return for, coupled with an impressive selection of wines.

Cons:
