- A brush with rudeness from the hostesses slightly marred the arrival, but the food swiftly overshadowed this hiccup.

In conclusion, this restaurant delivered an unforgettable pasta experience. It's not just a meal; it's the carbonara of my dreams, one that I'll long for until my next New York visit. It's a must-visit spot for any pasta enthusiast, where the hype truly meets reality.

Title: A Delightful Turkish Feast at ABA

My culinary journey through local Turkish eateries brought me to ABA on a bustling Saturday night. Despite the crowd, we were seated with minimal waiting. The meal commenced with perfectly crisp cheese rolls and savory zucchini pancakes, complemented by a flavorful sauce, both appetizers hearty enough to be filling on their own. The highlight of the meal, Sultan's delight, was a tantalizing mix of flavors and textures, so satisfying that I savored the rest as leftovers. Service was efficient and friendly, if not particularly memorable. ABA proved to be a good dining choice—great for a taste of Turkish cuisine that satisfies both as a meal and a next-day treat.

Been to this pub on two occasions now, both times in the early afternoon. Sitting at the bar seems like the way to go. The bartenders both times took great care of my partner and I. There are usually daily drink specials, offering some more affordable choices than many other bars in this part of the city. We made it in time for brunch today and were decided to try the Irish Frittata: egg, potato, peppers, sausage and "Irish bacon" (which to me was basically ham?). The whole thing came smothered in a thickkkk layer of melted cheese; indeed, an indulgent meal to start the day with. The two slices of toast did nothing for me. Nonetheless, for $11.95, it was a filling plate.  I forsee another trip here in the future. The space is large and welcoming. Plus there is the 10% off YELP check-in offer...so why not take advantage of that.
Wow. Didn't expect to be spending that much on my lunch. I only ordered a soup and ended up spending almost $15! Way overpriced!

I came across by CHLOE on Yelp while looking for vegan restaurants in New York City. A friend and I went to the restaurant on a Thursday afternoon and it was quite busy, it seems to be a popular restaurant amongst New York City vegans. The inside is very cute and overall aesthetically pleasing, and there's a good amount of seating. Furthermore, you have the option of ordering at the front counter (via human) or at a kiosk where you pay with a card. After ordering at the kiosk, my friend and I took our seats and waited for our names to be called. I ordered the mac and cheese (comes with shiitake bacon) and the pesto meatball sandwich. My friend ordered the classic burger. Our food was out in less than 15 minutes.As for the food, it's served on a tray, which gave me a cute vegan cafeteria vibe. However, I immediately noticed that the bread of my pesto meatball sandwich was burnt. I didn't want to complain because we were in a rush so I sucked it up and began to dig in. The sandwich was actually pretty good. If it wasn't burnt, I think I would have loved it, but unfortunately, it was very hard to eat. On the other hand, the mac and cheese was tasty, especially the shiitake bacon. It could've used a bit more flavor but I enjoyed it nonetheless. Unfortunately, my friend didn't enjoy her food at all. I didn't get the chance to try the burger but she claimed that it was bland, and she barely touched it. I was sad that we didn't have a great experience because we were very excited for this restaurant but we either came at a bad time or our standards were too high.

Upon my second visit to this establishment, the tonkotsu ramen, my usual dish, jogged my memory of past dining here. As a self-proclaimed ramen aficionado with a penchant for rich flavors akin to Ichiran's, I found their version less impressive, though the soft-boiled egg and chashu were commendable. Despite my personal taste in noodles, there are reasons this place warrants a return: first, their reasonable prices; second, the practical option for small servings; third, an enticing sake selection; and lastly, the consistent, commendable service provided by the attentive bartenders.

While the ramen itself might not beckon me back alone, the overall experience might. It's worth noting that my companions were quite satisfied with their curry ramen—though I'd likely lean towards the Tantan broth for a curry twist. The restaurant strikes a balance that could cater to a range of preferences, including those outside my own.

I love this chain because of the cute interior! Makes me really feel like a señorita! Food is quite decent, chips are amazing and the shrimp quesadilla was really good! It's just the service wasn't the best, we waited the quesadilla for 30 minutes and the waiter just didn't help follow up or apologize for the wait.

Title: A Consistently Delightful Experience at a Local Favorite

My latest visit to this beloved spot confirmed why it's my go-to restaurant; it simply never disappoints. The ease of enjoying a delicious meal here is unmatched, especially with their offerings of hearty burgers and fresh salads.

On this occasion, I opted for the lamb burger, which was nothing short of sensational. My son enjoyed a classic hamburger, while my friend also indulged in a tasty burger. We were pleasantly surprised by the complimentary bread served with a selection of flavorful olive oils – a nice appetizer to kick off the meal.

The atmosphere adds to the dining experience, boasting charming interior decor with pretty walls and delightful little flowers that add a touch of elegance. Having never had a bad meal here, I can confidently recommend it as a staple dining destination in NYC.

For convenience, they offer reservations across the city, ensuring a seamless dining experience. Whether you're a local or just passing through, do yourself a favor and secure a spot at this culinary gem.

Upon arrival at the restaurant, we were warmly greeted by Nancy, who lived up to her reputation for being exceptionally welcoming. Unfortunately, this high note was not maintained throughout our dining experience.

Our waitress displayed a disconcerting lack of hospitality, beginning with her insistence that we hadn't ordered enough food – a point she repeated even after we respectfully declined her suggestion. Despite our initial orders, our party of four felt completely satisfied by the meal's end.

Regarding the cuisine, the mooshu pork stood out with its flavorful filling and was paired nicely with pancakes. However, the eggplant and crispy pork were disappointingly oily, and the latter was tough to chew. The pork soup dumplings were merely passable.

Service further declined as our waitress haphazardly served our meals, reaching across the table without regard for our comfort. It was only after she possibly overheard my comments about her rudeness or anticipated a negative review that her demeanor shifted slightly – too little, too late.

While fairness compels me to commend the mooshu pork, the overall experience was tarnished by the subpar service and greasy dishes. It's a pity that the rest of the staff does not emulate Nancy's cheerful efficiency.

I recently enjoyed a pre-show evening at a fantastic spot near the Neil Simon and August Wilson Theatres, making it an ideal location for a quick bite and drinks before catching a performance. The happy hour here is a real treat, running from 4 to 7 PM with some excellent deals, including $5 vodka shots and $8 flavored martinis, down from the usual $12.

The pomegranate martinis we tried hit the spot—well-balanced and tasty. As for appetizers, the mushrooms julienne was a delightful surprise, a cheesy, saucy dish that mushroom lovers would relish, though hard to pin down in words. The beef dumplings were plentiful and satisfying, accompanied by a dollop of sour cream.

The ambiance of the place is uniquely enchanting, creating a respite from the hustle of New York with a decor that feels like a festive fusion of holiday celebrations. The one drawback was the service; just one server covered the bar area, leading to slower service than desired. We found ourselves actively seeking attention to place orders. 

Despite the service hiccup, the quality of food and drinks, combined with the vibrant, quirky atmosphere, made this a worthwhile visit, especially if you're looking to set the tone for an enjoyable evening at the theatre.

Title: A Go-To Dimsum Delight in Chinatown

Whenever the craving for dimsum hits us in Chinatown, we find ourselves gravitating towards this particular spot. Its location is a breeze - a quick escalator ride leads you into a bustling, capacious dining area. Be warned though, seating gets snug during rush hours. For bigger groups, an early arrival or a quick call ahead is advisable, but prepare for potential language barriers as the staff may be Mandarin-speaking only.

Service is swift; you'll be sipping on your beverage and diving into your meal before you know it. My family has our favorites nailed down - the succulent red pork buns, delectable shrimp shu mai, and perfectly sautéed veggies never disappoint. And for the sweet tooth, the mini egg tarts and durian pastries are a must-try.

Don't fret over the language - the charm of this place is that you can simply point at what tempts you on the roaming food trolleys. And if you're curious, the cart attendants provide concise dish descriptions in English.

In summary, this eatery is a reliable choice for classic dimsum dishes served up in the authentic hustle and bustle of Chinatown.

I came here at my date's suggestion--and I was glad that this was one of the few thai places I looked at that took reservations. It's a nice enough space but small, and the tables are very close together--to the extent that the older men sitting to one side of us basically told my date to quiet down because they couldn't hear their conversation (and he wasn't even that loud). However the service was friendly & attentive enough, and the food was good. I had the 5 star dumplings as a starter (pretty good) and my date had the curry puffs (also good). For a main I ordered the braised pork curry which was delicious--it was a large portion so I didn't even touch the rice that came on the side because I was very focused on inhaling that meat lol. My date enjoyed his pad thai and also the several drinks he had. I only tried the Thai72 mule (basically like a moscow mule, and came in the copper cups that make those so appealing) which was good. We didn't try the dessert, but I think I would if I come back, as well as the non-alcoholic drinks that sound yummy. Overall, definitely worth another visit if I'm in the area.

If it weren't for the owner of Azasu handing me and my boyfriend guitar pick business cards for Ronin Stones, we may have never found the place for years. For an intimate date, take a friend or two to the back room, which is decorated with rock and roll memorabilia, Polaroids of guests, and the lilt of music from old tour videos playing in the background. Danny and I split a few skewers--my favorite being the beef tongue--grilled vegetables and Sapporo. Will return soon to enjoy more of the ambiance and later a larger entree.

Title: A Mixed Bag at [Restaurant Name]

I recently had my first taste of burrata at [Restaurant Name], and it was a revelation – incredibly creamy, the right touch of saltiness, and utterly scrumptious. I was tempted to order a second helping!

Unfortunately, the service was less than stellar. With what appeared to be a single waitress handling the entire dining room, attention to diners was sparse and wait times were lengthy. However, it's worth noting that the kitchen efficiently delivered food at a surprisingly rapid pace.

As for the pizza, while the toppings were flavorful and well-chosen, they were a bit of a double-edged sword. Heavier toppings led to a disappointingly soggy crust, indicating a need for a sturdier base capable of supporting a generous payload without losing its integrity.

In summary, while the food quality, particularly the burrata, made a positive impression, there's room for improvement in service and pizza crust execution.

Title: A Haven for Healthy Lunches in the Heart of Hustle

Review:
Nestled amidst the bustling cityscape, this gem of a restaurant never fails to impress with its consistently fresh and wholesome offerings. A beacon for the health-conscious and vegetarians alike, its convenient location serves as an oasis for busy office workers craving a vibrant, nutrient-packed lunch on a tight schedule. While the early closing time may disappoint the after-work crowd, the midday fare here is so delightful that it's worth rejigging your schedule for. A visit here promises a plate bursting with flavor that will power you through the day.

**Hidden Gem in Harlem: A Vegan Delight!**

Tucked away in Harlem, I've stumbled upon a culinary treasure. The spot exudes charm, with smooth R&B tunes setting the perfect backdrop to its warm, inviting ambiance and family-style dining. The true standout, however, is the exceptional, warm-hearted staff that elevates the experience—undeniably the best service in ages!

Now, let's talk food. Seasoned Vegan challenges the toughest of carnivorous cravings with their mouthwatering lineup. From buttermilk chicken to pernil and oxtail - all plant-based, mind you - this place delivers flavor that satisfies without the post-meal slump. The vegan cheesecake finale? Simply divine! It left such an impression I've since been on a quest to replicate that creamy goodness.

Harlem's best-kept secret? Not for long if they keep dishing out bliss like this!

What a total let down.After years of hearing that this place has the best burger in NYC, my husband and I finally decided to try it. We came on a Monday night and luckily snagged a seat. After we sat, people were getting quoted for an hour wait.The service is brusque here. For the record, I didn't come here thinking I would get fine dining service. But, for an establishment that's been around for awhile, I didn't expect service along the lines of road side diner. No wonder the wait is so long. The waitresses are overwhelmed and disorganized. The food comes out quick, which is a plus. That's about the end of the positives. The burgers were flavorless! For a place that specializes in burgers, you would think that the grill has been seasoned over the years. The fries, however, were nice and crisp. To add insult to injury, the bill we got for 3 burgers, cottage fries, a coke and a glass of wine came out to $90. Are you kidding me?! Wtf?! I questioned the waitress bc there's no way this was correct. She laughed and said she made a mistake. But after reading a few other Yelpers and overhearing the table next to us, it seems that this is a common practice. Make sure you check the bill!Make sure you bring cash...and lots of it!

Paul's Da Burger Joint strikes an authentic diner vibe, tucked away near St. Marks, but the charm fades upon closer inspection. Stepping in on a quiet weeknight, I expected attentive service and the bustling atmosphere of a hidden gem; instead, I found myself in an almost deserted space in dire need of a sprucing up.

Ordered their cheeseburger, which came with a price tag of around $10; reasonable but reflective of the quality. The burger's appearance was rough—unevenly shaped, resembling a clover more than a patty. Though substantial in size, the meat disappointed, overcooked beyond my medium request, lacking in juiciness and the rich flavors one craves from a good burger. It's palatable, sure, but forgettable.

Service could've saved the experience but added to the letdown instead. Despite the sparse crowd, catching the waiter's eye proved difficult, and my plea for pickles echoed by fellow diners went ignored multiple times.

In the dense culinary landscape of East Village, Paul's Da Burger Joint is far from the best burger claim it somehow holds. It's a passable choice for a straightforward meal, but for those seeking the best, the search continues.

This is my second time trying pizza in New York! I was a little shocked by how much the price was; I thought all New York pizzas were $1. But, I just told myself that this pizza must cost $5 for a reason! That was one of the best $5 that I've spent thus far. First off the slices are huge. One slice is so large that they need to use 2 plates to carry it. One plate just simply won't do. The pizza is super thin and crisp! It holds it's own weight and does not sag. Impressive. I ordered the pepperoni pizza and they were very generous with the toppings. It honestly is so good, I want to go back again tomorrow for a second serving. I'm not sure how any other pizza can compare to Artichoke's; the've set the standard pretty high.

With the celebrated chef from Untitled at the Whitney at the helm, and with Dig Inn's track record of creative vegetable dishes, 232 Bleecker's reputation precedes itself. My already high expectations were more than met, with dish after dish delighting my taste buds to no end. I enjoyed textures, aromas, spices, and flavors so magical I thought I had synesthesia and could taste colors. I was fortunate to dine with a friend who shares the same taste in food and lets me make all ordering decisions (pro tip: everyone needs a friend like this in their life) so there wasn't a single dish on our table I had any qualms with. The koginut squash had the tastiest smoky mole sauce to complement the barley in the dish. The einkorn tagliatelle which we ordered as a half portion had a perfect chew, and delicious sauce with fresh and flavorful pieces of crab meat sprinkled throughout. Cauliflower should only ever be cooked charred, and theirs was made even tastier with a deeply nuanced sunflower butter. The best dish by far was the sleeper moses kale lasagna with 5 cheeses. I was floored by the creaminess of the cheese in layers of pasta dough that was cooked to a crisp at the edges. Though you can order any of the pastas as half portions, I'd recommend going with a full portion for the lasagna. That is a dish I will be thinking about and singing the praises of for a long time.Though we lingered at our table for a while, ordering multiple rounds of cocktails and dessert, we never felt rushed by the staff. Standout service paired with standout food remind me why I love living in New York, and I hope 232 Bleecker remains a longstanding pillar of the dining landscape here. Again, don't sleep on that Sleeper Lasagna!

Came here for dinner. Party of 1 so I was seated right away at the bar. For those not down to eat solo, you can make reservations via Resy for parties of 2 or more.Service was efficient (yasss). My order was taken promptly and my water glass was always filled.For starters, I ordered vegetable gyoza but got the pork ones instead. Luckily I was too hungry to complain so I ate it anyways. They were a bit too salty and oily. I'd skip this next time and try another appetizer.For main course, I got the yasai kakiage hot udon. The udon was thinner than I expected. I wish there were a few more pieces of burdock, as well as spinach. Overall, the udon was decent. Not sure I would recommend this particular udon unless you were vegetarian. Portions met my expectations for the price.  I would like to come back again to try their nameko udon.

Tucked away by the concierge desk of the Parker New York hotel, the restaurant exudes a charming 'hole in the wall' vibe. Despite a bustling crowd, the line was swift. Opting for the "works" cheeseburger, it arrived perfectly layered with tomato, onion, mayo, lettuce, pickle, mustard, and ketchup. For a nominal $1.61, the addition of bacon was a worthwhile indulgence. Both the burger and fries impressed with their flavor, making for a scrumptious meal. Highly recommend for a quick and satisfying bite.

Title: Disappointing Happy Hour at The Maze

I recently visited The Maze during happy hour and left underwhelmed. Tucked on the third floor in the heart of K-town, the venue's charming decor, complete with a floral canopy, set high expectations.

The culinary offerings shone brightly; soy garlic wings hit the mark with their perfect balance of crispiness and tenderness, and the herb garlic fries paired excellently with a spicy chipotle mayo - both were delightful. However, the mozzarella sticks were a mixed bag; tasty, but the accompanying chili sauce didn't quite win me over.

The real letdown came from the bar. The so-called 'happy hour' prices felt inflated, with cocktails starting at $11. My lychee-tini was disappointingly dilute, resembling juice more than a cocktail, and the margarita suffered from a stingy pour, hardly justifying its $12 tag. Service was another sore point; a third round of drinks arrived after a 30-minute wait, incomplete and followed by an inaccurate bill.

Despite the tasty food, the lackluster drinks and service marred the experience. I'm afraid I won't be returning to The Maze, a place that otherwise has much to offer.

Yesterday's lunch experience was yet another delightful visit to this local gem. Our group of four was treated to savory burgers and a delectable turkey club, all at a very reasonable price point. The service was commendable — attentive and efficient. I wholeheartedly recommend this spot and eagerly anticipate my next meal here.
First at the waffle place and it was amazing. This is located in Times Square. I wanted more but decided to pace myself. I ordered the Wafel of Mass DeliciousnessPrice $12 and some change

The Grand Central Market at Grand Central Station is just wonderful! So much great food! Pescatore has a really large selection at the Grand Central Market. They have all sorts of fresh seafood. It doesn't smell, which probably means that the seafood is really fresh. They also have some great prepared foods, like lobster salad, crab cakes, all sorts of salads, poached salmon, lobster rolls, even vegetarian items. The lobster puffs (puffed pastry with lobster) looked so good and the same with the crab cakes, but they don't have an oven or microwave to heat food, so I got the lobster salad, which was had mayonnaise and good chunks of mostly claw meat. I also had the salmon roll, which was a good deal. The roll was salmon and a few vegetables inside a rice paper roll. It was meant to be eaten cold. They give you forks and tissues. Excellent

Title: Bustling Bites at Little Spain

Tucked away in Hudson Yards, Little Spain is a vibrant culinary hub brimming with the zest of Spanish tunes and an expansive array of food choices that cater to various taste preferences. The venue houses three distinct restaurants: La Mar delights with seafood, La Lena offers a meat-centric menu, and the Spanish Diner, which closes for food service at 4pm, transitions to a drinks-only spot.

Unfortunately, due to the timing of our visit and long waits at the full-service restaurants, we decided to explore the food counters, which did not disappoint. The tomato and pepper flatbread from Pan Con Tomate was the star of our meal, boasting a delectable crispness adorned with juicy cherry tomatoes and red peppers. The egg and potato tortilla was satisfying, albeit not quite living up to previous experiences, and the ability to customize it was a plus.

We also ventured to try the vegetable paella from the paella station, bypassing the chicken and rabbit option. While flavorful, the paella was notably salty and proved too much for us to finish. As for the patatas bravas, it was a familiar taste, akin to breakfast potatoes, and not a standout dish worth reordering.

A word of caution: the ambiance, although lively, can be quite chaotic. Seating is limited, with a mix of stand-up and sit-down options, and competition for tables is fierce. Diners hover to claim spots, leading to a somewhat rushed dining experience. Ordering from multiple stands means juggling wait times and navigating through crowds, which can be a logistical challenge.

In summary, Little Spain offers an exhilarating taste of Spain for those willing to brave the bustle, but it may be wise to visit at less crowded times or with a strategy in mind for a more relaxed and enjoyable meal.

Tip #1: Sign up for the e-mail newsletter! E-mails are periodically sent with news on specials i.e 10 oz steak for $10!Quality affordable steak is a rarity is Midtown or so I thought! Ikinari is the to-go steak restaurant for lunch for a bargain! Make sure you come early to beat the lunch rush! Come at 11:30AM and you'll be seated right away, horizontal to the person you're with for a party of 2, or across from a stranger if you're alone. The reason being is that the sauces, condiments, and silverwave are lined horizontally. I didn't mind as long as the food came out quickly to break the awkward "hi I don't know you, but you are sitting in front of me" moment.The steak comes out SIZZLING HOT. Be sure to wear the apron provided to prevent grease stains from decorating your shirt. Since the steak continues to cook on the skillet, peel the steak off and place the rice directly on the skillet, and layer the steak on top. That way, the steak stays rare/medium rare. If you leave the steak on the skillet, it will cook to well done. Be careful when you eat! I involuntarily burned my mouth countless number of times. The food is just so delicious and I have no patience for the food to cool down. Also, I continue to forget to bring the mileage card. Supposedly you get a free steak for eating 10lbs. of steak. Don't quote me on the # of lbs. There is an app. May want to check it out if you become a regular customer!

I came to Wildair for my birthday a few weeks ago. It was fun experience with a really well curated menu. A big part of the experience for me was their organic wine options. It was fun to pair with our dishes as they came out.Wildair is bar height seating, and we were lucky enough to sit right in front of the kitchen. I love open kitchens and watch the chefs prep dishes to send out.We ordered the clams, fresh bread,green goddess salad, beef tartare, bacon on toast, fried squid with black mayo, pork Milanese, and my favorite..... the panna cotta with blood orange granita. Honestly, everything was delicious and worth ordering! I especially loved the bacon on toast, squid, and Milanese.But please, don't leave without trying that panna cotta.

Recently, my boyfriend and I visited this spot as a prelude to our actual dinner plans at Take31. Hungry and eager, we ordered the Detroit-style chicken parm pizza, paired with a whiskey cocktail. While the cocktail was enjoyable, it was a tad on the mild side for our taste.

The pizza, however, was a delightful surprise - delivered straight from the oven with a crust that had achieved the ultimate level of crunchiness. Although delicious, I believe a little more seasoning would elevate the pizza from good to great, adding that much-needed depth.

What truly set the experience apart was the exceptional service and the laid-back ambiance of the space. Dining at the bar, we appreciated the relaxed atmosphere, free from any pressure or overcrowding. This place deserves a solid 4.5 stars and a return visit is definitely in the cards for us.

My brunch experience at this locale, courtesy of a pulsd deal, was truly enjoyable. The atmosphere, unmistakably Irish pub-like, was lively and unpretentious. The food impressed with its quality, and the drinks—particularly strong—deserved a toast. A highlight was the 'tipsy teapot,' a delightful concoction that my companions and I shared several times over.

However, the revelry did seem to tip over for some patrons. A few were noticeably inebriated, teetering on their stools, which slightly marred an otherwise fun ambiance. While the spirited atmosphere is part of the charm, the restaurant might consider a more cautious approach to serving alcohol to ensure everyone's comfort and safety.

VERY cool spot in the Theater District for a pre/post-show drink. Met a friend there at about 10:45 and it was a little crowded but not crazy. Piano player was a little loud, but I get it. Sat at the bar and got served as soon as I made eye contact with the bartender. Stiff vodka and water was much appreciated. Not very expensive at all (which is nice for midtown). Would love to go back and try the food.

Title: A Shanghai Sojourn at China Blue

As a Shanghainese native, China Blue took me on a gastronomic journey back home. Celebrating my brother's birthday with a party of six on a Saturday evening, our experience was seamless from start – with an efficient seating courtesy of our reservation – to finish.

China Blue's ambience teleports diners to 1920s-1930s Shanghai, complete with décor that pays homage to the era's Jazz clubs. It's an ideal backdrop for impressing anyone from family to a first date, or for hosting a vivacious group celebration.

We indulged in Shanghai classics like Ningbo kaofu, Yan du xian, and Songshu fish. Each dish transported me to the opulent Shanghainese restaurants of my hometown. The kaofu struck a perfect sweet-savory balance, while the complex, rich flavors of the Yan du xian soup signified hours of careful stewing. The Songshu fish, a generous portion, boasted a delightful crispness complemented by a luscious sweet and sour sauce. The stir-fry string beans were standard fare but satisfying nonetheless.

Priced at around $25 per head, excluding tax and tip, China Blue isn't the thriftiest choice, but the authenticity and calibre of the cuisine justify the spend.

A highlight was the restaurant's thoughtful touch in celebrating my brother's birthday, complete with a complimentary rice pudding and a whimsical 'Happy Birthday' serenade over the sound system.

In sum, China Blue impresses with its authenticity and flavorful offerings. While not the budget option and without the largest portions, it's a culinary gem for foodies and enthusiasts of Chinese cuisine.

Easily put down a 1:30 brunch reservation for four on a Sunday a couple hours in advance. The restaurant was fairly empty when we arrived- it's a good idea to go after 1 PM on a weekend. Absolutely loved the cute nautical theme and relaxed atmosphere. Not chaotic, cramped, or noisy as most brunch places are on the weekends.Smoked Salmon toast and the Lobster Egg Benedict are delicious! Very savory, filling, and amazing texture. The side kale salad that came with the toast also tasted fresh and simple, with yummy sweet potatoes and less dressing. I'd come back to try their salads for lunch next time.Might call this one of my favorite brunch spots in the city now!

Celebrated a friend's birthday with bottomless brunch yesterday. The size of our group landed us a secluded room in the back. I scooted into the corner of the U-shaped booth and started reading the brunch menu. Pitchers of margaritas and mimosas were quickly ordered and brought to the table. The margs (I tried both frozen and on the rocks) were delicious, and strong! The mimosas were luke warm, so I stayed away from them. Chips and guacamole arrived next. Pro-tip: mix the pico de gallo into to avocado for efficient and delicious chipfuls. Honestly, the guac was my favorite part of the meal. Others around me ordered varieties of egg dishes and pancakes, while I was in more of a lunch mood. I went for the chicken mojo sandwich. We waited two long hours for the food to arrive, by which point everyone was sufficiently turnt. Uh oh. My sandwich was the biggest portion out of everyone's dishes. Two grilled chicken breasts, covered with caramelized onion and cheese piled betwixt soft buns. Seasoned fries on the side. Very tasty and filling but nothing to write home about. Definitely a drink-centric ordeal, so be wary of the check if you are not a drinker. The table and room in the back could, in theory, be conducive to conversation, but the volume level of our self selected music was not. Not sure if I got $50 worth of food and drinks but it sure was fun.

When realizing that I would be staying in the Ukrainian Village for my NYC trip, I researched some Ukrainian restaurants in the area and found Veselka immediately. I absolutely love pierogies and I knew that I wanted to see what types were offered here! We came in at around 8pm for a late dinner on a Sunday and we were seated immediately. I had no idea what I wanted, because there are so many great choices! Our waiter (guy with long, silver hair??) was so helpful and told me which dishes he liked and which sides went well with it.I decided to order four different pierogies (fried) - mushroom, potato, arugula+cheese, and meat. The arugula and cheese was by far my favorite pierogi! I also got the beef stroganoff with mashed potatoes, which was also very good. I have to say, it did not seem any different from an American egg noodles + beef dish that I could find anywhere, but it certainly satisfied my hunger and had a great sauce. The mashed potatoes also went very well with it (tip: try putting the mashed potatoes in the leftover sauce).Overall, I think that my meal at Veselka was very good. However, the dishes are a bit pricey for my taste. I would like to come back and order more pierogies!

Title: A Gem for Vegans in the West Village

Review:
I recently visited Delice & Sarrasin in the West Village and left with my palate pleasantly surprised, awarding them a well-deserved four stars for their starters and desserts alone. As someone on the quest for gourmet vegan options, I was delighted by their spectacular plant-based escargot and overjoyed by the macarons and almond milk chocolate cake, which were nothing short of heavenly for a dessert-deprived soul.

The mains, while slightly on the saltier side, were tasty— the Beef Bourguignon and chicken Coq Au Vin, creatively crafted with pea protein, were impressive if not quite indistinguishable from their meaty counterparts. Understandably, real meat has its unique charm, but for those looking to indulge in vegan cuisine, this spot offers a commendable alternative.

The ambiance is made all the more charming by the singing, service-oriented French waiters, which contributed to the venue's romantic vibe, perfect for date night. I'm already looking forward to my next visit to try the vegan Foie Gras and baked Brie. And whether you're vegan or just vegan-curious, Delice & Sarrasin is a must-visit in the quaint charm of the West Village. À bientôt!

Looking for a cheap lunch that won't break the bank? Wah Fung's is here for you. They serve azn BBQ meats over rice with an under $5 price tag. It's a small shop in Chinatown and expect some small lines during lunch hours. There's 2 people chopping the meats, but they are quick and efficient. For the lunch special, you can choose between the BBQ pork or chicken over rice with veggies.I ordered the bbq pork over rice. The portion size was perfect for me. You can upgrade to a large if you feel more hungry and a baller. I was in and out and enjoyed my cheap meal at home. This place is takeout only, but there are lots of parks around if you want to eat it outside. I'll forsure be back if in the area for a quick and cheap lunch!

Went to Blue Ribbon for the first time last night. I did not realize it was a fast casual place and not a full sit down restaurant. We placed our order at the counter and received a pager to inform us when to pick up the order.They have a neat sauce counter where they have wasabi honey, chipotle honey, wildflower honey, hot sauce, ketchup, and BBQ sauce. We picked up the food and dug in. We got 8 pieces of fried chicken, fries, three biscuits, and coleslaw. The coleslaw and biscuits were average. Biscuits could have used more salt and butter. Fries were meh. The fried chicken had a thick coating of breading that easily came off. It was super crunchy and very well seasoned, but it was almost too much breading. I've had better fried chicken that wasn't nearly as pricey, as our full order came out to over $50. It's good but not worth those prices, I'd rather get some sandwiches at Katz, even if fried chicken is my favorite food of all time.

Title: A Delightful Saturday Evening at a Charming Italian Spot

My experience at this restaurant was quite a pleasant surprise. Arriving on a busy Saturday at 7 pm, I was immediately seated outside, which in hindsight was a stroke of luck as a queue soon formed. The complimentary appetizer was a refreshing change from the norm: a delicious bread with white beans, which I thoroughly enjoyed.

For my main dish, I indulged in "The Timely 'Priest Stranglers'", a hearty portion that didn't disappoint, and I even had leftovers to take home. The place exudes a traditional Italian ambiance that adds charm to the dining experience.

While prices are on the higher end, the quality and quantity validate the cost. It's important to note that it's a cash-only establishment, so come prepared. A truly worthwhile visit for anyone looking for authentic Italian fare.

Community Food and Juice, nestled beside Columbia's bustling campus and conveniently located near the 1 train, proved to be an unexpectedly lively spot for a weekday brunch. Despite the midday timing, a throng of patrons filled the space, yet as a duo, we were promptly seated—a testament to their efficient accommodation.

The lunch offerings, straddling the line between breakfast and lunch, did not disappoint. My companion, guided by the server's suggestion, indulged in the formidable biscuit sandwich. Laden with scrumptious layers of scrambled eggs, chicken-apple-rosemary sausage, and cheddar, all sandwiched within a homemade biscuit and accompanied by tomato jam and inventive carrot hash browns, it was a meal requiring cutlery tact.

I opted for the healthier tofu scramble, an asparagus entwined delight crowned with a generous slice of avocado. It was served alongside 7-grain toast and a carrot hash brown. While the tofu's portion was modest and slightly under-seasoned, a dash of on-table hot sauce sufficed to elevate its flavor profile.

In essence, Community Food and Juice serves up commendable breakfast-inspired lunches in a location convenient for locals and campus visitors alike. While it may not beckon diners from afar given New York City's abundant brunch landscape, it stands out as a solid choice for those already in the vicinity.

Title: A Michelin Experience That Hits the Mark

Last night's visit to my second-ever Michelin Star dining destination soared above my elevated expectations. Our party of four faced a 45-minute wait, which we comfortably filled with a nearby bar visit. Despite a bustling crowd and the inevitable defense of our table queue position, we were seated with brisk efficiency.

Our culinary journey commenced with three entrees. The Khao Soi Kaa Kai's Northern-style golden curry, richly enveloping tender chicken leg and egg noodles, was a unanimous hit when paired with jasmine rice. The Kao Pat Puu - a crabmeat fried rice - transformed into a livelier dish with a dash of accompanying green sauce. The standout, however, was the Gaeng Som. Its supple pork jowl, saturated in a light turmeric curry and balanced with Thai herbs and tropical fruits, showcased an unrivaled tenderness and flavor harmony.

Dessert did not recede in quality. A Sticky Rice Banana Pudding catered to the less sweet-toothed among us, while the sumptuous Coconut Ice Cream was my personal indulgence. The sight of bone marrow on neighboring tables piqued my interest, earmarking it as a must-try for my inevitable return.

In sum, an unforgettable evening of sophisticated flavors and culinary craftsmanship that solidifies this establishment's Michelin status.

Nestled in the heart of the East Village, David's Cafe shines as a medium-sized French-American eatery exuding a relaxed charm on St. Marks Place. The interior whispers of a French cafe, adorned with eclectic American bits, all under a soft, inviting glow. The atmosphere is comfortably bustling, perfect for anything from date nights to group gatherings, or simply enjoying a drink.

Their distinct brunch, lunch, and dinner menus offer a delightful variety, but it's their 2016 Burger Bash-winning Burger Queen Deluxe that steals the spotlight. At $17, you're treated to a tantalizing double-patty burger loaded with cheese, fresh toppings, and their signature "special sauce," all hugged between a sesame seed bun and accompanied by a heap of crispy fries. During happy hour, this indulgence even includes a drink.

Each bite of the burger is a symphony of flavors and textures—the cheese melting over the patties, the crisp vegetables, and the sauce tying it all together. It's the epitome of an upscale burger at a value that's hard to beat for a sit-down dining experience. Coupled with their friendly, efficient staff, David's Cafe is a definite must-visit. Grab this burger with both hands, and prepare to be impressed.

Title: An Enchanting Anniversary Dinner Before the Show

From the moment we stepped into the restaurant, we were enveloped in a cozy atmosphere that promised a memorable dining experience. The service was exceptional, adding to the warmth of the ambiance—truly the perfect spot for a pre-show meal.

Opting for the 3-course menu simplified our evening, allowing us to indulge in a culinary journey without the stress of making multiple decisions. Each dish was a nod to classic cuisine, executed with expertise and care, making the simple act of dining feel exquisite.

Our anniversary celebration was made all the more special when the desserts arrived adorned with candles— a delightful touch that showcased the restaurant's attention to personal celebrations. It was an evening of effortless pleasure, and we left feeling pampered and content, ready to enjoy the night ahead.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Happy Hour

If you're heading to this spot for happy hour, come with an appetite for food rather than a thirst for drinks. The $8 wine special left us wanting more, both in taste and portion—a meager half-glass serving that didn't hit the mark. However, the culinary offerings are where this restaurant truly shines. The $1 oysters are a steal, and the pork belly flatbread is a generous slab of deliciousness. The charcuterie and cheese plate is another winner, ample enough for sharing and featuring a fine selection. The space itself is both expansive and inviting, adding to the overall dining experience. In summary, while the drinks may disappoint, the food is undoubtedly a compelling reason to visit. Just maybe pair your meal with something from the regular drink menu or explore nearby options for beverages post-bite.

During a recent visit to the local noodle shop with a friend, we both decided to try the lunch set offerings. I ordered the Miyuk Ramyun, a mushroom-based noodle dish, while my friend opted for the Cha Ramyun, featuring braised brisket. While my dish was satisfactorily prepared with a generous helping of mushrooms, it lacked a distinctive flavor that would prompt a yearning for a second helping. Meanwhile, we both agreed that the accompanying minced pork rice dish suffered from an overabundance of salt, overpowering what could have been an enjoyable side.

Our experience was further marred by the service. The hostess displayed a lack of professionalism and came across as rather rude, falling short of the welcoming atmosphere one anticipates in a dining establishment. While the main courses were decent, the overall experience left us with little desire for a return visit.

Title: A Rainy Day Delight at the Sister Spot to Her Name Is Han

If you're ravenous, you might want to grab a snack before heading over to this culinary sibling of Her Name Is Han, but trust me, the wait is worth it. Venturing in on a dreary day, I was immediately uplifted by the restaurant's bright and pristine ambiance.

The reservation process was smooth, a relief given the weather, and upon arrival, we were swiftly seated. The menu tempted us with various Korean staples, but we settled on the grilled short rib patty and the bulgogi pot, which is an experience in itself as it's cooked right before your eyes – no effort required on your part except for anticipation.

While waiting, it's wise to order some drinks, as the cooking takes time. The quality of the ingredients is evident in every bite, and the journey begins with three tantalizing appetizers that set the tone for the feast to come. A complimentary mushroom rice side further underscores their generosity.

Adding to the customizable experience, diners can opt to enhance their meal with noodles, supplemented with extra broth – a nod to the restaurant's commitment to satisfying their guests' every craving. The venue accommodates both intimate and group dining with equal finesse, though the experience does come with a higher price tag ($$$).

All in all, this spot is a refreshing choice for anyone looking to satiate their love for Korean cuisine in a clean, contemporary setting.

first time here and it was a good experience from the ladies at the door to our waitress. the food was good the atmosphere was pleasant and i just loved the way the bar lit up with all those colored bottles. i had the ribs and they damn near fell off the bone they were so good and cooked well. i had some of my friend calamari and it was cooked well not rubbery at all. i also had the the swamjuice which was very good. 2 glasses of it.

Despite the fact that the cuisine at this establishment has previously met my expectations, my latest experience was marred by service that was nothing short of appalling. Encounters with staff ranged from outright rude to peculiarly indifferent, creating an uncomfortable dining atmosphere that overshadowed the quality of the meals. It pains me to say that unless there are significant improvements in customer service, I find it hard to envision a return visit to a place that seems to have forgotten the importance of hospitality in the restaurant experience.

Stopped by on a Saturday afternoon and they had bar seating available, my server was very nice. I ordered the Volcano Ramen and it was amazing. It was hot and spicy the broth was well flavored. Very deep flavor and seasoned to perfection. My order came pretty quickly and I was out in about 40 mins. Serving size was just right. I'll be back to try the rest of the menu.

I recently dined at this charming establishment on a surprisingly quiet Thursday evening, having anticipated the usual crowd based on previous reviews. The ambiance was delightful, with quaint lights adding a cozy touch.

We opted for a couple of Coronas to accompany our selection of dishes, which included pork dumplings, corn cheese, and a daring spicy pork-stuffed squid. The dumplings were somewhat underwhelming, hinting at a pre-frozen origin followed by a quick fry-up. The corn cheese, on the other hand, was a delightful mix of creamy and sweet – a highlight of the meal.

The main event, a spicy pork-filled grilled squid, however, was an overpowering blaze of heat that obscured the subtleties of the dish's other ingredients. While I appreciate a kick of spice, this was a tad excessive.

In conclusion, the restaurant presents a lovely setting with potential for a lively atmosphere, thanks to its intriguing drink options like watermelon and pineapple soju. While the food was hit-or-miss, it seems that the draw might lean more towards the drinks than the culinary experience.

my fave brunch spot, friendly wait staff, prompt service from what i've experienced, AMAZING food, decent prices for bottomless brunch, and and and their mimosas go a looong way (love that they give them in a wine glass rather than in a flute). can't say enough good things

Tucked away in TriBeCa, this Vietnamese eatery remains a solid choice for those looking to satisfy their cravings. During my latest visit on a brisk autumn day, I opted for the Dumpling and Roast Pork Soup. While it wasn't the finest soup Manhattan has to offer, the savory pork and flavorful broth did not disappoint, even though the dumplings were slightly overdone. Service lagged more than usual which was a letdown. Overall, a decent experience but with room for improvement.

Been meaning to come here for a while -- and kicking myself for not having done so earlier!!! Food was amazinggggWe had:- adjaruli 10/10: this was simply amazing and everything ive been looking for! Cheese was perfect and the bread was fresh and hot from the oven. Definitely going back and trying the rest- khinkali 8/10: this was fine, skin was thicker than i expected. The meat was seasoned to my liking and there was an ample amount of soup inside. Not really something i'd always want to get but wouldn't mind eating- mtsvadi lamb 8/10: was ok, kinda very pricy considering the portion size. The meat was quite juicy, however, and the onions were a very nice touch. We had a reservation and came here on a friday but it was incredibly busy so i highly recommend making a reservation. The space is intimate but in my opinion a little too packed than it should be. We had to get up and tetris our tables a few times so the parties next to us could be seated, which i found a little disruptive.

Brunch is one of my favorite meals and I was so excited to try Michelin Star resturant Nix. I went with a friend for brunch. We made reservations beforehand and were seated almost immediately upon arrival. The décor is so calming and elegant with light walls and beautiful greenery. The menu also looked delicious. I'm a vegetarian and it was so perfect for me. We enjoyed the polenta fries and feta dip to start with. The first were good however I was not expecting the dip that it came with. I wasn't a huge fan, I thought it would be a creamier consistency but it very runny. For my brunch meal I ordered the Egg in the hole and I'm so glad I did! It was delicious and just what I wanted,  I ate the whole thing and was quite full. My friends ordered the patty melt and enjoyed it as well, it was a bit on the heavier side so she took one half home. All together it was great and I will return. Order the Egg in the hole if you like a good egg and cheese sandwich.

Compared to other AYCE sushi restaurants, this one isn't very good. I got 30 pieces total with 6 different toppings, and some of them were awful (salmon, yellowtail, salmon roe), while others were just okay (eel, shrimp, smelt roe). It honestly tasted like they bought everything frozen AND pre-sliced because all the fibers were broken down, and the texture of everything was just like cold fatty jelly...

I had the opportunity to experience the late-night room service, which is available around the clock. Though the service was on the slower side, the wait was a small price to pay for the delectably tempting meals served. In short, despite the delay, the culinary experience was ultimately satisfying and worth it.

Title: A Scenic Dining Experience with Room for Improvement

My recent visit to the revolving restaurant atop the Marriott Hotel during restaurant week was a mixed bag, but the panoramic views provided a memorable backdrop for the evening. First tip: Navigate to the correct elevator to ascend to the 48th floor—this is where your culinary journey with a view begins. Reservation is key, and make sure your entire group is accounted for to be seated; window seats are a hot commodity, and we were fortunate to snag one.

As the cityscape twinkled beneath us, the service remained attentive and efficient. However, as darkness descended, some areas of the restaurant had rather limited visibility, detracting slightly from the 360 experience.

The restaurant week menu had several upcharges which felt restrictive, and the portions seemed on the smaller side. The Salmon Tiraditos was a refreshing appetizer while the supplementary crab cake hit the spot. The Steak frites main course was the highlight with its robust flavors, though the seabass was disappointingly lackluster. Dessert was a Peach & Almond Galette; a promising combination soured by the tartness of the peach.

On a sweet note, the restaurant kindly commemorated my birthday with a small complimentary chocolate cake—a delightful touch.

Pro tip for photo enthusiasts: arrive before sunset to avoid reflections in your snapshots. Remember, the restaurant completes a rotation every hour, an amusing quirk to keep in mind if you step away from your table.

In summary, while the setting is impressive and the staff do their part, the culinary experience doesn't quite match up to the grandeur of the location. A few tweaks could make this a stellar experience through and through.

Came here because I didn't want to spend too much money for just a little bit of food.This was perfect for that. One dollar, one slice of cheese pizza. Just a very simple transaction. Now I don't know if it would've been harder if I ordered toppings as I think they just print out cheese pizzas.One thing to note was that I didn't see any chili flakes or parmesan cheese on the side for you. There was just oregano. Honestly, the quality + speed + cost of a cheese pizza is hard to beat here.

I highly recommend Olio e Piu if you're in the mood for Italian! The cozy decor, delicious food, and friendly staff makes this place 100%! I recently stopped by with a friend to try their summer menu and was really impressed. The highlights for me were the Aperol Spritz and Le Marche (cocktails), Fichi Insalate, and Polipetti alla Griglia.Aperol Spritz - light, refreshing, and perfect for the summer!Le Marche - a bit stronger, cool like a cucumber, and similar to a mojitoFichi Insalate - delicious salad that was subtly sweetPolipetti alla Griglia - soft, crunchy octopus that was packed with flavor!

Rong Cheng House is an affordable and delicious spot in Midtown. Come here for bold flavors that transport you out of Manhattan. The staff is incredibly friendly and when you arrive you feel like you are being welcomed into someone's home. We ordered the dan dan noodles, shrimp dumplings, pea shoots, and half Peking duck special. All of these dishes really hit the spot! I especially loved the dan dan noodles. They were oily in the best possible way. They also were spicy and I loved that kick. This was a great start to the meal and I suggest you order the noodles. I also loved the shrimp dumplings. They were exactly what you'd want from a shrimp dumpling and were much larger than what I usually get at other restaurants for the same price, without sacrificing on flavor.We were recommended the pea shoots which is a dish I've never had before. They were amazing! Buttery and garlicky, but fresh and bright enough to cut through the rest of the indulgent dinner. Finally, the peking duck. I've also never ordered this before but I'm glad we did. Four wraps are prepared tableside and feature veggies, a plum sauce, and the duck. The duck skin was so crispy and fatty. I wish I could just eat a bowl of that duck skin.

We stumbled upon this charming little gem when every other place was bustling and our hunger was nudging us before a show. Its intimacy is palpable with a cozy seating capacity for about 16 guests, offering a personal dining experience. The noodle dishes were delightful, and the dumplings didn’t disappoint, save for one mysterious outlier which was served cold. Despite this minor hiccup, the service was warm and amiable, echoing the friendly spirit of this snug eatery.

Really would give it 3.5. The restaurant is quite small and crowds easy, hard to make it to the door or bathroom without bumping into other patrons or servers (this was 9pm on a Friday). I got the massaman curry which was delicious and came fast. The fried tofu was a little tough but maybe I should've gotten the steamed instead? The prices are good for the portion size, quite filling. Definitely had to take some home. The food came super fast and there was also a complimentary appetizer of puffed chips with a peanut sauce

I came here because I love having cheese on my noodles.So I got the one ramen that had some cheese. The pork was ok, not really fatty, not too firm. The broth was ok. The cheese, what I came for...was also ok. It was all on my pork and wasn't sprinkled throughout my noodles so I only tasted a chunk of cheese on my pork which left much to be desired.If you want cheesy ramen, don't hold out for this spot.

Don't you just love finding a place you'd never heard of before?Yesterday I was in Soho with the bestie checking out an art exhibit, we'd planned to go to happy hour afterwards but after a quick shopping detour we were still undecided. A short google search later (weekend happy hour) we realized Verlaine was nearby...a quick Uber ride later (we're hella lazy) we were getting candy at Economy (we are also millennials with horrible attention spans lol). Once we'd FINALLY gotten into Verlaine it was super cute! A loungey area in the front, a nice bar, and a sleek row/column of tables going to the back of the restaurant. We originally asked for a table and once seated asked to be switched to the lounge area (because again, indecisive). Then proceeded to order; five spiced calamari, crispy wings, hot chips, coconut curry shrimp, extra chips, extra dips, six red sangrias, three lychee martinis, and a gin and tonic. Verlaine is super freaking trendy! Happy hour until 10pm! Drinks are great! It looked to be a great date spot! The food has potential, we were drinking so we needed salty food bites. Our choices didn't do it for us, the sauce that accompanies the wings (might just be plain soy sauce) was the lifesaver for all the food we tried. Everyone who'd ordered food around us seemed to really enjoy their food though. The service, great!!!We'll be back!

Great Malaysian food! Was in Singapore for four years and would like to say this place was authentic!Personally not a fun of the shrimp paste, so things without would suite me. Got the Indian pancake first. The curry was the same I had in Singapore! Soooooo yummy and flavorful!!! I prefer the thinker pancake though, so I would order roti prata next time. The hainanese chicken rice was great! The spicy sauce was not as spicy as the one I had in Singapore, but the overall taste was right. No complaint at all and we packed another order for take-away to enjoy it the next day.The how fun with seafood paste got nice taste, very close to the Singapore ones too.Overall the flavor was outstanding and authentic! Seafood-wise not very fresh but acceptable. Would love to come back!Good service but the service can be long. Cash only.
Beautiful place for a Sunday brunch near Central Park!Hermoso lugar para un brunch de domingo cerca del Central Park!
Best service! Amazing drinks and specials! Creative ramen that you can't get anywhere else!A MUST GO for any ramen lover.

The dry Szechuan pot is very good whether with or without hot spice.You go to the counter and pick your meat and vegetables and they way it.  You can request it to be hot or how spicy you want it prepared.  I liked it either way.The Xia long Bao was alright but the wrapping is too thick for me.  I would like it much more thinner and delicate.The staff is very nice and the place is beautiful.The bathroom too is big and clean equipped with Japanese style buttons.  Nice new addition to the neighborhood.

I finally visited the much-anticipated chic café, drawn in by its adorable decor and summery, open entrance which complemented the airy interior adorned with white and floral touches. Although their late opening at noon had previously deterred me, I was eager to sample their happy hour offerings—though a note of caution, many of their signature drinks disappointingly don’t make the cut.

Upon arrival, the place was tranquil, allowing for instant seating. The menu's bamboo-handled design charmed, and I opted for the rose garden waffle and extended-season lavender glitter latte. Both were delectable, and despite the latte being only lukewarm, it was refreshing on a hot day. The waffle's portion was satisfying without overwhelming.

While the experience itself was delightful, the steep price dampens any urge for repeat visits. My bill tallied up to $37 for just two items, which seems extravagant even with the excellent ambiance. It's a lovely spot for a one-off indulgence, but the cost is a significant drawback for those considering it as a regular haunt.

Hands down the BEST ramen that I've had thus far!!! Did you hear me, fool? The mutha effin' BEST! Theee BEST-EST! Granted, I haven't yet had ramen in Japan. But for American standards, this ramen is the real deal y'all. What the hell have they been serving me up in Cali??? Dear Gaaawd! I will never look at ramen the same ever again!So anywaaaays... you, yes YOU need to come here and get some of this good good. The waits are long but shorter for smaller parties since the seating is communal. Communal seating... yes indeed. Be ready to make some new friends because you'll be up close and personal. Okay, maybe not that close, but still. You'll be sharing a table and eavesdropping... *ahem*... "unintentionally" on other people's convos. Or um... maybe that was just me? Whoopies!Let's get back on track, shall we? The space isn't the largest but people seem to slurp down their bowl of ramen within lightning speed here, so there are always people coming and going. Service is fast and adequate but nothing over the top. I ordered the Akamaru Modern which has a pork broth base with thin noodles and pork belly. It's one of their most popular ramen bowls and I completely understand why. That sh*t is SOOOO damn good!The broth alone deserves 5 stars. Very flavorful without overdoing it and not super salty. The noodles are amazing! They are tougher than your average ramen noodle. I've never experienced this type of consistency before but it was magnificent. It has me wondering if this is the type of noodle that they actually use in Japan. The pork belly was perfect. Not overly fatty, tender, and delicious. Melted in my mouth along with the wonderful aromas of the broth. The entire bowl was exploding with flavor. I added corn and a seasoned soft boiled egg, and it meshed together perfectly. The boiled egg was picture perfect. All of the elements came together in this perfect culmination of deliciousness. I literally slurped every last drop of the broth in that bowl. People were staring, but do you think I have a damn? It was just too good and nothing was going to be left behind. My only complaint: I wish I could have had MORE! But actually, it was a nice filling bowl... I was just being greedy. Oh yeah, and next time I'll definitely be ordering their pork buns! It felt like my nose was gonna fall off after smelling the batch that the couple at the table ordered. I can already tell from the smell that they were delicious! But the bottom line is, you need to experience this phenomenon pronto! It may just change your life forevaaa!

Floret is a hidden gem nestled in a serene alley, boasting an atmosphere of minimalistic elegance. Visiting for a Saturday brunch, we were pleasantly greeted with immediate seating and a comfortably heated outdoor area, a welcome retreat amidst the cloudy day.

The menu, though concise, did not compromise on quality. The soft scrambled eggs were complemented by a standout toast - crunchy and aromatic, paired with subtly flavored quinoa that harmonized with the dish. The chicken sandwich may seem traditional, but the bread elevated it beyond expectations.

For a touch of sweetness, the ricotta toast with fruit was a delightful juxtaposition of creamy and tangy, each bite an exploration of flavor. However, the true star was the French toast, a must-have, brilliantly crunchy on the outside yet pillowy within, accompanied by sweet and lightly roasted pecans that completed the dish with finesse.

In sum, Floret excels with its mastery of bread and offers a refined yet cozy brunch experience. Each dish is thoughtfully crafted, promising a return visit to this quaint culinary nook.

I'm shocked that I've never been here before. The outside is completely underrated compared to their affordable and extensive menu of tons of Mexican dishes. They give nachos and salsa while you wait, which are refillable for free. We ordered the grilled chicken soft tacos and the shrimp soft tacos, which were sooo good. It wasn't super heavy either, so I didn't feel like I was eating a ton. And it was really fresh too. Also, I can't recommend enough their margarita on the rocks. It's sooo delicious, and it's actually pretty strong without an overwhelming alcohol taste. I actually only had one with three tacos and a ton of nachos and still felt woozy leaving. I wish I could get margaritas here all the time (in addition to all of the amazing food). The service is great too. They were pretty quick to get our meal out.

During a recent Friday lunch visit to the restaurant around 11:30am, we were promptly seated in the notably empty dining area. Our initial impression was dimmed by the St. Germain bottles on each table that served lukewarm water—an unwelcome departure from the expected chilled refreshment.

We opted for the waffle & fried chicken and the avocado smash, both of which regrettably failed to impress. The waffle & fried chicken dish, often a brunch delight, was lackluster with its small, dry portions that arrived at a tepid room temperature. The accompanying gravy, while flavorful, ultimately rendered the chicken skin soggy. A future note to self: request gravy on the side. The waffles were disappointing, edging towards chewy rather than the anticipated light and fluffy texture.

The avocado smash fared marginally better, although the toast's staleness undercut the dish's overall appeal.

Despite the underwhelming experience, accolades from fellow brunch-goers about both the weekend service and the drink menu have piqued my interest in a return visit. I remain hopeful that a second chance will reveal the establishment's true potential. Stay tuned for an updated review post-revisit.

Title: A Slice of Perfection at NYC's Original Patsy's

I recently revisited what I consider the best brick pizza NYC has to offer – the original Patsy's. Having been introduced to this gem a few summers back, the thin-crust pizzas irrevocably captured my palate. During this visit, with family in tow, we ventured beyond their signature salads and pizzas, starting with eggplant rollatine and fried calamari. Any skepticism I harbored was promptly dispelled as the dishes arrived. The eggplant was impeccably cooked, striking a flawless balance between sauce and cheese, while the calamari was a golden delight, especially with a touch of lemon.

The main event, the Capricciosa pizza, did not disappoint. Its paper-thin crust held a bounty of tomato sauce, mozzarella, prosciutto, portobello, and black olives. The slight char and resounding crispness were testament to their mastery of the craft.

However, I find myself compelled to withhold a star, rating Patsy's a solid 4 out of 5, as the biting cold inside the restaurant due to a broken heater took a slice out of the otherwise warm experience. Despite the chill, the pizza, as always, was sheer warmth on a plate.
The crepe we ordered was nutella, tiramisu, and strawberries. The strawberries were frozen and far and inbetween. Not impressed in the lease.

I walked by this place on Sunday at 3pm and saw a line. I thought, this must be good. After waiting half an hour, I was seated. I got coffee and the beef rice roll. the beef rice roll was honestly underwhelming.The inside was clean and service was good. Pop by if there's no line. Otherwise, find yourself a dim sum place with rice rolls and a selection of other foods.

Title: A Local Brunch Haven with Minor Quirks

If you're searching for a reliable brunch destination in the neighborhood, this bustling eatery should top your list. With an array of classic brunch selections, including the perfectly ripe avocado toast adorned with poached eggs, a satisfying B.E.L.T, and a balanced pairing of yogurt with granola, there's comfort in their familiar yet polished menu.

Sipping on the robust La Colombe coffee was a highlight, complemented by the friendly and attentive service that made the dining experience feel personal and welcoming. The portion sizes won't leave you hungry, ensuring good value for each dish served.

A word to the wise: the restroom situation is less than ideal, with only one available and inconveniently nestled between the kitchen and dining space, causing a slight dance of disruption with the staff. Additionally, its popularity results in long waits, so either plan your visit with patience in mind or locate a nearby Starbucks for a quicker alternative.

In all, this spot is a testament to the quintessential neighborhood brunch scene—worthy of a visit, with a touch of planning to avoid the wait.

Title: A Succulent Seafood Stop at Luke's Lobster UES

During a recent jaunt to New York, I had the pleasure of dining at Luke's Lobster on the Upper East Side, a stone's throw from the art-rich Museum Mile. This quaint establishment, though small, is bursting with charm and offers a cozy nook to feast on sea treasures.

I was greeted by a hospitable gentleman who took the time to walk me through the tantalizing menu. My choice? Luke's Trio, a delicious trifecta of 1/2 crab, 1/2 lobster, and 1/2 shrimp rolls, paired with a seasonal lobster corn chowder and a beverage. The rolls, though served cold contrary to my usual preference, didn't disappoint. The crab roll emerged as the star, its buttery goodness and fresh lumps of crab delighting my palate. The hearty chowder brimmed with generous chunks of lobster and melt-in-your-mouth potatoes—a true comfort dish.

The only hiccup in my sea-feast was the portion size; the "half" rolls felt more like a teaser to a hungry soul eager for more of that rich, buttery seafood.

Although the portions left me longing, the Trio offered a great value overall. If my wish could be granted by the Luke's Lobster gods, it would be for grander roll sizes to match their grand flavor.

The haunting fear of the unknown will keep me from trying out the newly opened Luke's in my neighborhood—after all, can it really live up to the original? But for now, I'll bask in the memory of that delectable New York lobstah that truly hit the spot.

The restaurant is beautiful and intimate, and service is great. The dishes are small plates, super small plates in my opinion (Do not come here super hungry if you're a big eater). We had the chicken satay's, avocado salad, vegetable spring rolls for appetizers. The chicken satay was definitely my favorite. For main entree we had the Nasi goreng, lobster noodles, pork ribs, the sea bass, and roasted eggplant. My favorite was the pork ribs. It's glazed and falls off the bone good. Honestly for the hype this restaurant had, nothing was extraordinarily tasty or impressive. It's typical Asian fusion dishes but still delicious.

I stopped here for a work dinner, the restaurant has a dining area set lower (watch the stairs as you enter and then step down again into the dining pit) and a long bar to the left-hand side. Coat check at the front, and check-in with the lady closer to the bar.Drink was spilled on the way to the seat, and they very nicely made me another. Bread to start was a multi-grain, whole wheat sourdough (tasty) and a hard baguette (tough). Asked and received a small plate of olive oil (which the table shared).Tried appetizers:- Tuna Tartar w/ cucumber shiso and miso, clean and refreshing- Deviled eggs with creme fraiche and golden trout roe, a nice touch of salty on the creamy center- Grilled tiger prawns - on the dry side, not good for me, too smoky, tooDinner mains:- tagliatelle - wild mushroom, al dente and savory but not overwhelming- long island duck breast was cooked well from a display perspective, but didn't stand out with much flavor- rack of lamb w/ swiss chard, potato puree, onion and reduction - done well and not too gamy, consistency and pink was just right- miso cod - disappointed, the miso flavor tasted simply drizzled on the top of the well-cooked fish, but had no infusion of flavor like you would get at NobuDessert:- gotham chocolate cake - too bitter for me, and I don't like salty ice cream- pear souffle - light and puffy, delicious end to a mealOverall, service was top-notch and the food was a little hit-and-miss. When I come here again, will be sure to try some other dishes.

Upon visiting the much-talked-about Saltbae's steakhouse, one can immediately grasp the reason behind its buzz. The restaurant exudes a cool factor, with the iconic Saltbae persona omnipresent even in his physical absence. With its chic and intentionally dim interior, the space aims to create a specific ambiance; however, an overly loud music volume occasionally disrupted our conversation.

A word of caution to future patrons: be precise when requesting water, as our lack of specification led to an unanticipated charge for premium VOS water bottles.

The #saltbae tomahawk, priced at $275, lived up to its first impressions with succulent initial bites. However, as the meal progressed, the meat became tougher. Sharing this dish might be wise, allowing room for other flavors to complement the rich steak.

Surprisingly, the Nusret burger, with its harmonious blend of cheese and caramelized onion, surpassed the tomahawk in enjoyment. The accompanying fries were underwhelmingly average.

Overall, the experience offers a unique atmosphere and some standout dishes, though it comes with caveats that diners should be mindful of.

Title: "Mixed Feelings on a Pricy Japanese Noodle Spot"

I recently visited a Japanese restaurant that boasted an authentic dining experience. Indeed, the ambiance hit the mark, mirroring a genuine counter-style service reminiscent of Tokyo's busy ramen joints. The efficient service was notable, although it didn't come with the flair of Japanese waitresses one might expect.

The soft-boiled egg I ordered was a highlight, providing a much-needed protein punch. However, the rest of the meal didn't quite live up to expectations, especially considering the hefty $20 price tag for a bowl of ramen before any extras like toppings or drinks.

Speaking of the ramen, it was standard fare—nothing that would lure me away from favorites like Totto or Jin. The noodles lacked that 'wow' factor, and the broth was overwhelmingly salty. I was disappointed to find that beef wasn't an option, which limited the menu for me personally.

The green tea further added to my discontent, arriving lukewarm and in a portion that left me wanting more. As for the seating, despite the touted experience, waiting for a spot—even if it was just ten minutes—didn't feel worth it when sitting in what essentially felt like a cubicle, resulting in an awkward interaction with the server.

Overall, for the price and the hype surrounding the seating concept, I was left underwhelmed and questioning the value. It might cater to someone seeking a novelty seating experience, but for anyone after a standout bowl of ramen, this might not be their best bet.

This place has been on my list for a while and I finally got to try it. I walked in around when it just opened  and I sat at the counter where I could watch the chefs making the ramen. The ramen was okay. I wasn't blown away and I thought it was gonna be so much better. The broth was okay but the noodles were good. They have some sauces and a water pitcher where you can just do it yourself.

Ordered Lucky Famous Burgers through Uber eats for lunch. The pictures on Yelp really sold me, kind of had an In n Out vibe to their lettuce wrapped burgers (protein style). Although this burger was pretty tasty, the lettuce wrap compared to other burger joints wasn't too useful. As soon as I picked this burger up, it basically fell apart and turned into a sloppy lunch. All in all, they do have a good burger. That's all that matters in the end.

There was a period of time when Thai Villa first opened where I went every week for weeks on end without fail. If you know me and know how I don't repeat restaurants because NYC spoils me silly with endlessly delicious eateries, this is a strange aberration in the life of Morlene. Yes, Thai Villa was really just that good. Beautiful decor that makes you feel like you're dining in the palace of Thai royalty, an incredibly fast kitchen, such that you can have your food out within minutes of ordering and be done with lunch/dinner within an hour, and punchy, piquant, aromatic, curries, noodles, and papaya salad galore. Wow, that was a run on sentence. Basically, it was a dream.Fast forward a few years and much of this is still true. The service is still speedy, the space is still beautiful. The food is also quite delicious, but there's something up with that mock  duck. I used to think the gold standard for it could be found  here at Thai Villa, but the crisp, flavorful prices of gluten I used to know here have made way for spongy gross gluten. Okay I know this is only going to matter to the very small percentage of people who come here and order mock duck, but I'm talking to you, fellow mock duck lover, maybe order tofu when you come here.Their lunch special is great value since you get a soup or salad plus appetizer with your entree. But the more interesting dishes are on the dinner menu, including the "royal pad thai" which comes wrapped in egg netting. Check photos on Yelp to see what I'm talking about.Join the virtual queue on Yelp Waitlist to avoid waiting for your table, that service is clutch.

There's always a long line here so your best bet is to come early (like at 6pm) as they don't take reservations. Love the ambiance here and that all staff are Thai, it really makes you feel like you're eating in Thailand. Food is quite good and delicious but the chicken in my Pad Se Ew was a little dry.

Title: Disappointing Dining at Niu Noodle

I recently visited Niu Noodle, nestled in a charming neighborhood brimming with inviting shops and cafes. Despite the area's allure, my dining experience left much to be desired. Upon arrival, the restaurant was eerily quiet, and a request to sit at an ample booth was denied due to an allegedly impending large party that, notably, never arrived during our stay.

The menu at Niu Noodle promised an interesting selection, and the service staff did shine with kindness and attentiveness. Our order was ambitious, including Calamari, Spicy Wontons, Ha Gao Shrimp Dumplings, Pork and Crab Meat Soup Dumplings, Stir-fried Bok Choy, a Ramen dish, and a forgettable item which has since escaped my memory. Of all these, only the Spicy Wontons managed to leave a positive impression. The Calamari suffered from excessive battering, the Shrimp Dumplings were mediocre, the Soup Dumplings arrived lukewarm and flavorless, the Bok Choy was uninspired, and the Ramen, along with the unmemorable dish, was just passable. All this culminated in a hefty $130 bill.

Out of courtesy to a special friend visiting from California, I refrained from voicing my discontent during the meal. Nonetheless, it's clear that despite the pleasant service, the food at Niu Noodle unfortunately doesn't merit a return visit. Luckily, New York City's vast culinary landscape offers countless superior options that I'm eager to explore.

I decided to come here because it was freezing in the city and I needed some soup to warm me up. I ordered the spicy garlic ramen and the fried chicken. I ordered the ramen with wavy and medium thickness noodles.
