The ramen wasn't not the best I had but it was acceptable for nyc ramen.  The only downside of the dish is that the ramen included less than normal noodles compared to other ramen restaurants I have been to in nyc. All in all I will be back if I need a hot soup to warm me up on a cold day.  out of 5 stars

**Title:** Freshness Overloaded, Just a Tad Sour 

**Review:** My wife and I recently visited this little gem in our quest for the ultimate Açaí bowl experience, and I'm pleased to say it delivered on many fronts. Unlike the standard fare at places like Juice Generation, this establishment takes pride in serving up authentic and fresh acai bowls that are a cut above the rest. Each spoonful was a testament to the quality of ingredients used – from the light, succulent berries to the fresh oats, nuts, and a drizzle of honey that tasted nothing short of genuine. Nothing on our plates tasted stale or pre-packaged.

That said, as much as I appreciate the dedication to freshness, the bowls did skew on the sour side. The flavor, although unique, lacked a certain balance that my palate yearned for. 

Overall, I'd rate this spot at a solid 8/10 for its commitment to freshness and quality ingredients, though a little tweak on the flavor profile could make it perfection in a bowl.

Disclaimer: I am not a thai food connoisseur by any means.I haven't eaten much thai food in my life; I usually opt for drunken noodles, curry, thai iced tea, and coconut mango sticky rice. All have been pretty good in my experience. I can list the number of thai places I've been to on my fingers; the best place I've been was Heng in Providence, RI. Uncle Boon's was surprisingly disappointing compared to Heng. When my friend told me that One More Thai was her new favorite thai restaurant, I had to check it out; we ordered the drunken noodles, pineapple fried rice, massaman curry, and the squid in basil sauce (and a lot of green beans) for 4 people. Not only was our meal absolutely delicious and filling, but the service was amazing and we only paid $15 after tax and tip. Dang. I loved everything we got (maybe 4 stars for the squid in basil sauce - the squid was cooked perfectly, but another sauce would've probably been more interesting). The drunken noodles had the perfect hint of heat and was totally addicting. The massaman curry was full of coconut flavor and went down super easily. The pineapple fried rice had a curry kick to it and was ultra tasty. There's a decent amount of meat in all of the dishes. Someone ordered the Thai iced tea and the scent of the tea was intoxicatingly fragrant; I don't remember ever smelling it so strongly. It was a really good one. My friend and I had come from a gelato making class, and the staff was very accommodating about letting us store our gelato in their freezer during our dinner. Even though there was a language barrier, they were unfailingly pleasant and just made it a great experience. I was surprised by how empty it was; it's tough that they're overshadowed by Clinton St. Baking Company's presence next door, but One More Thai is fantastic and satisfying in its own way. I'd definitely come back. I guess it's my favorite Thai place in NYC for now, too! :)

Came here last night with a friend. As soon as we walked in, the bartenders ushered us over to free chairs on the other side of the busy bar. Served us drinks right away and it was the start of a great night! Super friendly people and cute environment! Love the Halloween decor!

Title: A Valentine's Feast to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

My friends and I decided to indulge in the four-course Valentine's Day pre-fixe menu at [Restaurant Name], and it certainly did not disappoint. The Tuna Tartare appetizer was a citrusy dream, delivering both savory and tender perfection - a dish I'd emphatically revisit.

Amongst a trio of shared pastas, the Black Linguine was the star. Its unique combination of green chili heat and sweet scallops won us over, although the lobster bolognese and paccheri were also commendable in their own right.

The Dover Sole entrée was a revelation; its buttery, flaky texture paired with a delectable citrus sauce, and garlicky, fluffy hash could only be described as mesmerizing. Though the spinach side proved too rich for my palate, my companions found it delightful.

Dessert was a showstopper, especially the Orange Vacherin. Its layers of texture - from crumbly meringue to soft fruit salad and granular granita - were a triumph in taste. The raspberry macaron, with its passion fruit mousse and lychee sorbet, was a flavor bomb, albeit a tad challenging to eat.

Our only misstep was the Wild Halibut, which unfortunately was tougher than anticipated, and its sweet bed of sunchoke, wild mushrooms, and spinach left us puzzled.

Service was impeccable, with attentive staff who seamlessly transitioned us from course to course in the formal and upscale ambiance that [Restaurant Name] is clearly known for.

In summary, the food was impressive, the service was top-notch, and the overall experience was one that beckons a return visit.

This is a relatively new restaurant and a hidden gem in LES. Russian food tapas style so be prepared for more limited portion sizes. But don't let that deter you as the flavors are all very well done. Service was also very friendly. We had no issues making reservations via opentable and getting seated early.We sampled a lot of dishes but based on what everyone most enjoyed I would recommend definitely trying:- katchapurri - pelmeni- stroganoff Would probably skip the duck plov. Would describe as more of a duck fried rice kind of dish that we weren't too wild about. Everything else not mentioned, including salads and black bread, were still very enjoyable.

Decent price and quality for a food truck. I ordered the Fish over Rice and  my fiance got the lamb gyro. The rice was excellent while the fish was bland with no flavor and one piece was still super raw and frozen with red area :(.
Although the wait was an hour and a half, food was fantastic. I ordered the beef platter and spicy green tea noodles. It was perfect and satisfying. Service was great, very attentive

Title: A Cozy Japanese Gem in Chelsea: Ootoya Review

Nestled in Chelsea, Ootoya presents an inviting atmosphere with its dim lighting and warm heaters—a perfect retreat for lovers of Japanese cuisine. Unlike its sibling location near 11th Street, this spot boasts the much-coveted set meal options, an offering not checked at Times Square in some time.

Surprisingly spacious, Ootoya efficiently accommodates diners with additional seating near the back, at the bar, and an upstairs area. Wait times are negligible, often no more than 20 minutes, even when bustling. Opting for bar seating can expedite the process.

The menu here has undergone a thoughtful update, with clear labeling that guides patrons through an array of choices, from mixed rice dishes to fish, soup, and the beloved yakitori/bbq fare. My choice of kimchi nabe was delightful, and while ordered a la carte, I paired it with a charmingly presented, smooth egg custard—only $2 extra and not to be missed.

While prices lean towards the higher end, the quality justifies every penny. Each dish is crafted with attention and aesthetically served—my stone bowl entree and the sides in their snug plastic containers were a testament to this. The ceramic jar housing the egg custard, akin to a quaint honey jar, added an extra touch of whimsy.

An added perk for diners: complimentary hot tea upon request. And remember, tipping is not expected here, allowing you to savor the experience with financial ease.

This place is hidden, there's no signs on the street so you follow your map where it takes you and then go up the stairs and there's a hidden cafeteria food court style area and there it is! Pretty good lobster rolls. I think my combo with drink and a side of cole slaw was about $21. The lobster roll was filled with meaty lobster claw meat and tail chunks. Soo good. Topped with a dash of melted butter. I would pass on the coleslaw next time, it tasted more of balsamic and not the traditional cole slaw. Get the chips.Next time I would like to try the crab roll and the clam chowder. Plenty of seating. Restrooms are downstairs you have to take the elevator!

Title: A Worthwhile UES Gem for Brunch Enthusiasts

Despite residing in Midtown East, my journey to this British-style Indian eatery in the Upper East Side is always one I undertake with anticipation, especially for their unique brunch offerings. Though I frequented the restaurant more when I lived closer—about biweekly—it continues to lure me back with its charm.

The restaurant exudes a quaint appeal; it's a small space that radiates warmth, inviting you into its cozy embrace, all complemented by distinctive and cool decor. A standout favorite of mine is the chili cheese toast, an item so scrumptious it leaves me salivating at the mere thought.

On a recent visit with my parents, the universal enjoyment of the cuisine was palpable. Admittedly, the popularity of the place means it's often bustling, which can lead to longer waits since the service is managed by just a couple of hardworking individuals. Patience is required here, but the delectable food is worth the wait.

For anyone not in a hurry and in search of culinary delights not found elsewhere in Manhattan, I wholeheartedly recommend this spot. The flavors linger long after the meal is over.

Instagram: @traveleen_gurl

Title: Prime Rib Triumphs Over Reservation Woes

If you're a fan of succulent prime rib or crave a burger that takes the classic Big Mac to gourmet heights, this restaurant might just be worth the reservation roulette that precedes the meal. Snagging a table felt like winning the lottery, a competition of reflexes against the relentless Resy app, until success landed me a modest 5:15 pm slot on a Monday evening.

Service faltered with an odd mishap of a server prematurely clearing our napkins and utensils, leaving us momentarily stranded when our food arrived. However, the culinary offerings themselves swept away lingering frustration. The prime rib was a standout—tender, flavorful, and perfectly complemented by its accompanying sauces—sans the excess fat and sinew you'd fork out an extra $30 for with the Charles Cut.

As for the burger, it was a revelation. Request some lettuce and tomato for a fresh crunch that elevates the savory blend of flavors to a harmonious crescendo.

Despite a rocky start and speedy service that hinted at a desire to free up tables, the food quality alone may just convince you to jump back into the reservation fray.

Great gnocchi that is light and pillow-y. The portions here are just right- you'll be full but you'll definitely have room for dessert without feeling too bloated. I'd recommend the platter for 2, which comes with pesto, four cheese, and classic red sauce. The four cheese was definitely the favorite. I also loved the butter and sage with spinach gnocchi!!! So delicious and simple, and the perfect light dinner or lunch. My friend got the carbonara, which she enjoyed. The only negative I would say is that most of the dishes are a flat $18. There are many vegetation options on the menu that I think should be cheaper than the meat options since it's basically sauce and gnocchi.

Cozy place for lunch in Soho. Not pretentious at all.  They serve jalapeño cornbread as the "bread basket" which was delicious.  Enjoyed my lobster roll - plenty of yummy lobster pieces, not too mayonnaisey, and lovely thin slices of cucumber and crunchies in the mix.   Opted for a side salad instead of the fries and happy with my choice.  Also indulged in a slice of the Vietnamese coffee pie which was very satisfying.  Damn you for making me cheat on my diet! It's pricey for lunch but it's Soho so why bother complaining.

I stopped by this restaurant for a quick bite and was not disappointed. The lamb sliders I ordered were deliciously flavorful, leaving a lasting impression. Additionally, I indulged in a mezcal cocktail, which quickly became my favorite due to its expert craftsmanship. I managed to snag a table by the window, offering a lovely view that complemented the meal. While the music was on the louder side, it's understandable given the bar atmosphere. This spot would be an excellent choice for a group outing.

Title: A Charming Brunch at Cafe Luxembourg

I recently enjoyed a delightful brunch at Cafe Luxembourg, a charming neighborhood bistro that exudes a cozy ambiance. Despite the bustling atmosphere with every seat taken and a waiting list to boot, the staff managed to be exceedingly attentive—a testament to their efficient service. A tip for future diners: making a reservation is wise for busy times like evenings or holidays.

The bistro's quirky history was a conversation piece, evidenced by the whimsical bumcee displayed in the bathrooms, etched onto their chocolates, and featured on the bill.

The highlight of my visit was the food. The fish and chips were an absolute treat, especially served with brown vinegar and adorned with a quaint paper decor that nostalgically harkened back to traditional English pubs. 

In conclusion, Cafe Luxembourg is well worth a visit for anyone looking to savor good food in a sweet setting. Check out my attached photos to catch a glimpse of the experience. Give it a try; you won't be disappointed.

Got here for lunch on a Saturday just before heading to the broadway show, Book of Mormon. Sooooooo conveniently looked right next door to the theatre! Get out of this restaurant and right into the line heading into the theatre :)I got the virgin mojito - soooooo refreshing!!! Best choice! And the gnocchi with sausage.. BEST gnocchi I've ever heard.. not at all doughy.. just perfect so tasty.. definitely very heavy because of all the cream but yummy nonetheless. The tartufo or tarfuto whatever the dessert is called was soooooo good too.. chocolate gelato with some other things. Super yum!!!Oh and we got 10% off because we had tix to the Broadway.

Title: Perfect Spot for Game Day Grub at Duke’s

If you’re on the hunt for a quintessential sports bar experience, Duke’s might just be your touchdown. Forget about the craft beer and moody vibes—Duke’s is all about straightforward, well-priced beers, lots of screens, and a vibrant, if occasionally raucous, atmosphere.

The wings here are solid, though they won’t redefine your standards. But let me tell you about the tacos—specifically, the crunchy chicken variety. Wrapped in a soft shell and accompanied by a generous helping of chips, salsa, and guacamole, they’re a real game-changer. They offer a delightful break from the typical heavy bar fare, filling you up without weighing you down.

With TVs galore, there’s not a bad seat in the house. No matter where you plop down, you’ll have a prime view of the action. And despite the crowd that flocks here on game days, the staff keeps service snappy and efficient.

Just one pro tip: arrive at least 45 minutes before any big game to snag a prime spot for you and your crew. Duke’s is a winner for anyone eager to immerse themselves in the sports bar scene and indulge in some above-the-bar grub.

The ladies at the register are not friendly. Not personable at all and didnt seem to speak much English. I ended up just getting the chicken wings. The wings were already made and just sitting under a light. The three wings were luke warm and didnt have much flavor. The outer layer was no longer crispy. I love the fact that the wings come with picked veggies and a pretty good sauce on the side. I wish I would of came earlier in the day. Maybe I would of gotten a fresher batch of wings. They didnt have much on the menu in terms of light items/starters. Everything was an entire meal besides the wings. I might come back to give this place another try....ONLY if its early in the day. & just for the wings.

There is usually a wait here. Located on one of the prime busy spot.   Restaurant is small.   Any party ( 5 and more has to wait much longer since they only have 3 roomier booths at the back.   Front tables are small tables.   Tables are very close to each other by the wall. Not much privacy if sat along the wall in the front.   Pro: - fast service.   Actually very fast.   All food was served within minutes. - I had milk tea and coffee combo drink.  Strong enough. -Price is fair.  Portion is fair, not huge- except pork chop rice has two big pieces pork chops.  - stir fried udon noodle is tastyCon: -longer wait. I had party of 5.  - staff does their job.  Not very approachable-salt and pepper chicken wings were sprinkled with hot pepper.  It didn't indicate it was spicy on menu.  - 碗仔翅 ( sour and spicy soup) was weak.  Very watery and nothing like the original.  Conclusion:  rice and noodles are good.  Good milk tea too.  Convenient location.  Can be crowded.  Fair staff service.  Especially like the efficiency of food serving speed.   Yes.  Will return.

Title: A True Slice of Italy with a Personal Touch

My recent dining experience at this gem of an Italian restaurant was nothing short of exceptional. The ambiance is a soothing escape from the hustle and bustle, complete with a charming back garden adorned with heated lamps that made the evening air just perfect.

The staff's attentiveness is commendable, ensuring a seamless meal from start to finish. They accommodate personal taste with ease—an option I took advantage of by adding pear and prosciutto to an already delightful arugula salad. The soup of the day, a hearty minestrone, was a flavorful prelude to the main course.

As for the highlight of the meal, the homemade tagliatelle pasta was a testament to the authentic, quality Italian fare this place prides itself on. Opting out of shrimp, my dish was still a standout and perfectly crafted.

Their extensive food options leave me eager to return and sample more of their offerings. I left with a satisfied palate and gratitude for a meal well served. A definite must-visit for anyone in search of a true Italian culinary experience.

Tucked away just steps from the bustling heart of Times Square, this gem of a restaurant offers a truly lovely atmosphere, perfect for unwinding after a long day. The cocktail selection is impressive, each drink crafted with a meticulous attention to detail. Adding to its charm is the fact that it's open late on Sunday nights, making it an ideal spot for a relaxed evening out. Highly recommended for anyone seeking a delightful dining experience amidst the city's energy.

Title: A Flavor Revelation at Nyonya

Having passed by Nyonya countless times without a second glance, my recent dinner experience there with friends has completely turned the tables. From the very first bite, it was clear that flavor is king at this establishment. The roti served with curry was an exceptional start to our meal; while the roti was good on its own, when paired with the curry, it truly became an unforgettable appetizer.

As a group, we shared a varied selection of dishes including a noodle dish, the succulent Hainanese chicken, a fresh veggie dish, and a remarkable eggplant with salted fish casserole. Each plate was a hit, resonating with authentic, delicious taste that kept us reaching for more.

The restaurant itself boasts plenty of seating, ensuring a comfortable dining experience without the worry of a long wait for a table. I left Nyonya with a satisfied palate and a promise to myself to return. If you're in the neighborhood and have yet to try Nyonya, do yourself a favor and don't walk by – walk in.

After happy hour and apps my colleagues and I were still hungry (story of my life) - so one of them recommended Málà Project since she had been there before and had good things to say. While I'm a novice when it comes to dry pot, I'm open to new experiences so off we went. Like many places in Manhattan, Málà is small. We didn't have reservations, but we only waited about 5 or so minutes for a table. This was a score since most reviews here talk about waiting, and also the fact that we were five people. The decor is simple with exposed brick walls and a minimalist aesthetic. The low lighting made the entire dining area warm and intimate. The menu consisted of starters and then the dry pot section. We decided to start with some apps: the eggplant with roasted garlic and scallion pancakes.  The eggplant was great - it had a very clean flavor and the roasted garlic paired perfectly with it (I'm a sucker for garlic). The scallion pancakes were pretty good - there was nothing really outstanding about them, but they were not greasy which is always a plus. The dry pot is kind of build-your-own; there's a huge selection of items to add (both familiar and adventurous), and you can control your degree of spice. Also depending on the size of the bowl you are allowed to add a certain number of items. We were divided on how spicy we wanted the pot, so we split up and I shared a mildly spicy one with one of my colleagues. We decided to add Chinese bacon, sliced eye of round, chicken breast, prawns, shiitake mushrooms, bok choy, tofu skin, and glass noodles. The flavors were great, and they gave a generous portion which was more than enough for the two of us to share. I have a relatively low spice tolerance, and have to admit the mild degree was testing me - so definitely keep that in mind when choosing how spicy you want it.Service was great - we were attended to promptly and everything came out at a good pace. Overall, I had a great time at Málà Project; being build-your-own dry pot, I feel like I can return here multiple times and always have a different experience. It's definitely worth trying out at least once.

Normally I prefer spicier cruise over Cantonese food, but King's Kitchen is worth a visit to try their famous rice casseroles. Ours includes yellow eel, taro, sausage, and some other delicious bits and pieces. The BBQ meats are also quite goods though very oily, so don't indulge too too much. Service was rather quick despite it being packed for lunch. Overall, I really enjoyed it for switching up my Chinatown routine and would eagerly come back again.

They serve Risotto here and it's great. Can't go wrong with any dish and some are more rich than others. Each dish ranges from 14-23$ish. The higher you go the more protein you snag in the dish. It's a smaller joint, and you must make a reservation and be on time. We sat right by the window on a little ledge area. Kinda cool as I perched over the Risotto eating peasants. What we got:-Started with deep fried risotto balls. VERY fresh and tasty. Had some sexy marinara sauce on the side. -Cacio e Pepe Risotto. VERY rich and creamy with extra breadcrumbs on top. Very good. Highly recommend. -Shrimp Risotto. Shrimp were a little TOO cooked, but it was still a fire dish. What I didn't like was our server. He wasn't the worst I've ever had, but he snagged our wine glasses and said "More wine?" My man, never grab the glass and ask if I want more of anything. You putting your hand on the glass doesn't give me the urge to want more. Also, he dropped some of the Risotto on my friends hair!! My mans got butter finger hands. Got free The best part about this joint is it's 100% gluten free. Our friend is very sensitive to gluten, and this place is a god send. We'll be back to try more dishes and wine.

This is the prettiest coffee I have ever seen in my life!One of the biggest pros of traveling off season is that you can just walk in to any of the trending places without having to wait for a table. As a matter of fact, we were the only people when we we walked in around 4 pm on a Wednesday (then a few people came in).The decor was super adorable (if you like anything girly and pink), dessert was yummy and coffee was delicious (even though I was just staring at it for a good 5 minutes and couldn't make myself ruin such a masterpiece).I thought the price was fair for an overall experience /atmosphere.

Not the same as the old two bridges diner on the corner. Menu seems to have been redacted and no longer include the old breakfast platters. Bacon egg and cheese on a roll which is a new York City breakfast classic came with very thin and overly done bacon. The roll was rubbery and did not hold up well.

Stopped in on a Sunday evening and tried out one of their mini cheesecakes. The taste was good - not too sweet, but I thought the consistency would be fluffier. It could have also been because we had one that was right out of the fridge, so if you do get it, maybe wait for it to get to room temperature? This location is also super busy since it's right in K-Town. Doubt I will be back. At least not to this one. I do love their curry croquettes though!

Oh Fonda, where do I begin?First of all, thank you for accommodating our tardy party.Second of all, bottomless margaritas ARE DANGEROUS and bad for your health..Lol ... but for real, I may sound dramatic but I am serious.Third, I think your restaurant decor and layout is quite darling. The fact that you are housed in a old school New York walk up is charming to me.Now the food:We ordered spicy guacamole and chips to share. This portion was ok but we needed a second order to satisfy the cravings.I ordered the Chilaquiles with scrambled eggs. I enjoyed my scrambled eggs but the chips were too much. After a while I didnt want to eat any more because it was making me full and didnt have much flavor.Sis number 1 had the Revueltos estilo Veracruz which looked like a rainbow. She said it was decent.Mommy had the Torta de Pollo served on a baguette.Sis number 2 had the Breakfast Burrito which looked and tasted good but came out with so much sauce. I would order this next time if I decide to return minus the sauce.Sis 3 and 4 ordered some vegan friendly option which I don't have pictured.Everyone but Mom and I opted into the unlimited margaritas offered during Brunch.  Needless to say each of them had a little too much and the effects were not good to say the least. Personally, I would just say bottomless mimosas and bellinis are a safer option.The Tres Leches was a nice treat to wrap up our brunch.

This venue is right in herald square and they have great happy hour specials. $6 for well drinks, they also have $8 beer and shot deal. This place is very spacious,great decor,  and have ample amount of TVs. The bartender was welcoming. I'll definitely come back for good music and affordable drinks.

Title: A Surprisingly Delightful Beef Cube Salad at a Pho Joint

I ventured off the beaten pho path at this local spot and was pleasantly rewarded with a delectable beef cube salad. Scoring a solid 4 out of 5, the dish boasted perfectly seasoned beef accompanied by crisp romaine and a side of rice, creating a refreshingly tasty snack that I highly recommend for anyone looking for a quick, yet satisfying bite.

Service here was decent, earning a 3 out of 5. Despite my late arrival, the staff was accommodating and nice, ensuring a smooth experience during my brief visit - my friend had kindly ordered ahead for me, and by the time I got there, everything was set.

However, if ambiance weighs heavy on your dining preferences, you might find this place lacking, as it only manages a 2 out of 5. The restaurant's interior is on the older side and leans heavily into a casual, typical Chinatown vibe - not exactly a prime date spot unless your companion is a serious food lover who can overlook the aesthetics.

In summary, while the restaurant might not win any interior design awards, the food and service made up for it. Just maybe save it for a casual meet-up rather than a romantic evening. Oh, and for those wondering about the untouched side of rice - I had plans at Whiskey Tavern and priorities had to be made. No judgment, please.

I recently stopped by this charming spot and had a delightful experience with their grilled cheese. It was scrumptious, featuring perfectly toasted bread and a generous serving of succulent lobster. While it might not constitute a full meal, it's an ideal choice for a lighter appetite or a sumptuous snack. I also tried their shrimp rolls in the past which were equally impressive. If your taste buds are craving seafood with a comforting twist, this is the place to be!

Title: A Refreshing Culinary Experience at a NYC Bar

I had the pleasure of dining at this NYC bar recently and was pleasantly surprised by the quality of both the food and drinks. Starting with the appetizers, each dish was a delightful prelude to the evening’s flavors, setting a high standard that was maintained throughout our visit. The beverages complemented the food perfectly, with a range of options to suit all tastes.

The space accommodated our large group comfortably downstairs, where we were met with an attentive service that is often a rarity in the bustling bar scene of the city. Unlike some bars where food can be an afterthought, here it shone as much as their well-crafted drinks.

The ambiance was inviting, offering ample space without the strain of dim lighting, making it a perfect setting for socializing and enjoying a meal. Overall, this bar stands out in the New York City landscape, serving up an experience that's as satisfying for the palate as it is for the spirit.

Food was decent but the flavor was not as good as the other Cajun seafood places I've been. The sauce was quite light. Service and decor was great. I got the lobster and shrimp combo which was good but flavor was not memorable. It was a big portion, with corn and sausage. Drinks and appetizers during happy hour was a good deal though.

Upon the guidance of Robert Sietsema, I ventured to a bustling Sunday afternoon spot known for its fiery offerings. True to form, the establishment delivered on the heat, especially with the C4 Burning Noodle. While they didn't visually scream 'extra spicy,' the noodles packed an unexpected punch that both surprised and satisfied.

The E2 cumin chicken, unfortunately, fell short of expectations. The dish carried a mere whisper of cumin where a shout was anticipated—a stark contrast to the cumin-laden lamb experienced at Szechwan Absolute in Flushing.

The culinary crescendo was the B10 Spicy and Numbing Pork wonton. These twelve pieces of peppery pleasure, adorned with two pepper icons on the menu, came in a soup that was a slow-burning theatre of mala. While not the most intense mala I've encountered, it was still the standout of the meal, and the remaining broth served as a fantastic enhancement for the remaining burning noodles.

Prices were fair, and food overall was commendable enough to warrant a return trip for other palate adventures. A quick aside: if you're eyeing the lunch specials online, remember they're not available on weekends or holidays—not that you'd want to distract from the truly exceptional items on the regular menu.

This place is so nostalgic. My bf and I both got duck over rice for a total of $12. We aren't fans of very fatty meats - only enough to give that flavor kick. My cuts of duck were primarily fat (which dropped my rating down to a 4), but did have a thick and juicy layer of meat. It was served with fresh rice, cabbage, and a light sauce. You walk in, order right away, pick up your food, pay, and leave. No tables. No chit chat. No servers. I love it.

New restaurants in NYC rarely live up to all the Eater/Infatuation/Times hype but this place definitely did. From the overall ambiance (highly recommend sitting at the bar) to the food, it was a great experience. The duck nigiri is a must try - so unique and good.

I'll say this has definitely earned its one Michelin Star . If you wanna eat out without being too unhealthy or carb heavy: highly recommend The service though - 4/5; might have been the bar like ambiance and we went rather lateThe chefs omakase menu is the way to go for $$ and maximizing dishes and variety cuz otherwise you get one piece of sushi or two pieces of sashimi Now for the dishes 5/5The scallops and sashimi / blue fin were easily in my top 5; close to Nobu DC but not as good as Nobu Dubai in quality ; caviar quality was defi in top 3 in the city We added The dragon roll for the sakeOf being more filling -since we were famished and it was a perfect complement ; Beverages : 5/5Desserts : the orange jelly was unique and delicious if small ; very fresh and in an actual fruit The Japanese red bean cookie were a let down for sure : hard pass next time Overall: worth a shot; great antiinflammatory food ; fun bar ambience; service is good-IshNoise levels LOUD esp at night as they do midnight ramen so just be prepared

Title: Delightful Cuisine with a Bittersweet Service

My friends and I recently visited this restaurant, having booked a table for four through Yelp. Despite our tardiness, the staff was accommodating enough to reinstate our expired reservation, which was a pleasant surprise.

The drink selection was satisfactory – we sipped on a mocha, cappuccino, coffee, and a mimosa, which were all delightful. As for the food, it was nothing short of exceptional. We indulged in the Nova Benny, the savory Wild Mushroom Toast, the flavorful Chicken Chilaquiles, and sumptuously prepared French Toast – each dish left us extremely content.

Sadly, I find myself compelled to give the experience a 4 out of 5, as the service did not match the quality of the food. While initially the service was commendable, towards the end of our meal, the waiter's demeanor shifted. His abruptness and insistence on rushing us detracted from our otherwise wonderful dining experience. It's unfortunate that the service did not maintain the high standard set by the cuisine.

What a classy dinner!  I dined with two friends at Del Posto last week and it was a great evening.The restaurant itself is really big and lovely.  Dimly lit, it made me feel like I was in a movie.  Nearby diners were obviously corporate groups, talking loudly or mergers and lawsuits.Upon arrival, I checked my coat at the entry, and was seated with my friends who had arrived before me.We were given wine and cocktail menus.  We wanted a bottle of wine so the sommelier came to assist.  He opened the book and started discussing some wine in the $500-600 price range.  I'm sure many diners who eat here have an expense account, but this wasn't the case for us.  I told him we aren't looking to spend that at all.  He graciously moved to a page with bottles under $100, and made us feel like we still picked an amazing bottle.The way the wine was presented and served was an art form into itself.  Seasoning glasses by swirling the wine in one then pouring it into the other then pouring a tiny bit into a smaller glass, which I assume was for his own taste to ensure its quality.We opted for the 5-course tasting.  We were first given a small butternut squash and minestrone amuse bouche (assuming they don't call it that at an Italian restaurant, but it was a little starter palate cleanser).  We were then each served with our own plate of mini baguette and a ball of ricotta and butter/cream combo.  It looked like Burrata but tasted like ricotta and butter combined.  Delicious.One by one the courses came out, the wine glasses were filled before we even knew we needed more.  Crumbs were discreetly cleaned from the table.Each dish was tasty and well though out and delicious.

Title: A Delightful Plan B Turns Into A Go-To Burger Spot

After missing out on Chelsea Market by a hair, my friend and I stumbled upon this gem of a restaurant, and it was a fortunate twist of fate. Tucked away and unassuming, the atmosphere was quiet and relaxed around 10 PM on a Thursday night—almost as if we had the place to ourselves.

With no liquor license in sight, the accommodating server at the bar went above and beyond to guide us rookies through the menu's highlights, even tailoring recommendations to our tastes. I opted for the American, while my companion took on the Supreme. To accompany our mains, we shared a generous serving of waffle fries, proven to be more than satisfactory for two.

The burgers struck a balance in size and taste, especially impressive with their grass-fed beef patties that were juicy and well-seasoned. As for the waffle fries, they were a standout, especially when paired with the garlic aioli and, for the daring, the habanero mayo—a combination that got my seal of approval as someone with a high tolerance for heat.

The best part? This isn't the only location to indulge in a quality burger experience. So, whether you're near Chelsea or not, I wholeheartedly recommend dropping by one of their other spots to share a hearty meal and an excellent burger with a friend.

Tucked away in the bustling Garment District, this restaurant is a delightful challenge to find—but the reward for your efforts is more than worth it. The goat dish is a must-try, succulent and seasoned to perfection. In truth, you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. A hidden gem indeed, it's a culinary treasure that promises an exceptional dining experience for those who seek it out. Highly recommended!

Lord have mercy let me tell you!! This spot is IT! We ordered the lobster roll and lobster mac and cheese, I have no words. So good! Amazing! The best! It's small inside but we got a seat still. Customer service was top notch, obviously these people love their job because it showed clearly to us. I wish I lived in NY because I would eat there several times a week. So good!! Must try!

I found myself at Nerai the other night for an educational dinner. I always like to attend these because not only do I learn something but more times than not I get to try a new restaurant. The pics and reviews for Nerai looked great, so I was really looking forward to trying out their fare. Nerai is an upscale Greek restaurant. Walking in, it looks like a typical Manhattan restaurant - narrow and crowded with a sizable bar towards the front. The decor is clean - mostly a light color scheme with touches of contemporary design; it gives off that upscale feel which is very inviting. We were seated in a private room downstairs and even though we were in the basement the color scheme made it feel open and welcome. Because it was an educational dinner, we were only able to choose our entree - but we really got a wide variety of food. We started with pita and three dips - tzatziki, hummus, and spicy feta. The dips were quite tasty - my favorite was the spicy feta since it was the most unique, the other two were good but on par with other Greek places I've been to. They were really generous with the warm pita which was much appreciated. We then moved onto the Greek salad which didn't contain lettuce but rather lots of chunky tomato, cucumber, and onion. It was seasoned well and topped with a huge piece of feta mmmmm. For the main I chose the salmon which sat on top of spinach orzo. The salmon was cooked perfectly - it had just the right amount of crisp on the exterior and cooked medium and tender on the inside. The spinach orzo was a great complement - it was creamy without being too rich or overpowering the fish. For dessert we had chocolate cake which was actually more of a mousse since it didn't contain sponge. It was nothing amazing but a nice finisher to the meal - plus, it came with a small scoop of ice cream which acted as a palate cleanser. Service was good, everyone was friendly and food was served at an appropriate pace. Overall, I was impressed with Nerai - which is rare for me to say because I normally don't get the best of what a restaurant offers when I go to educational dinners. While this isn't the cheapest place, I would definitely be open to coming back for a special occasion - or another educational dinner ;-)

Tried the Green and White and the Deli, was seeking and hoping for that foodgasm in your mouth like when I had EggSlut in the west coast since it's basically a copy of EggSlut. Nope, there was no surprised, just another expensive NY street cart like breakfast sandwich, oh well.The cheese hash brown was not bad but just okay

I came here for brunch with friends sat at noon. It wasn't crowded and the service was prompt. It has a very low key kitchy vibe and super friendly staff. The burgers here are known to be amazing and after trying it I can confirm they are the best! So are the French fries.

Went here for our holiday party, & I must say the service is exceptional.  Waiters are extremely attentive, & the view is phenomenal.  It doesn't matter where you sit, you're bound to have a great view.  The food is very tasty, portion size is moderate so do it expect your average size meat portion as that will disappoint you. Overall taste wise the food is great. Highly recommend for a one time out of the box experience.

I recently had the pleasure of revisiting a classic bar I first discovered 18 years ago, and it remains a gem in the city. The ambiance is invitingly cold and dark, setting the tone for a cozy retreat. Their happy hour begins early, making it an ideal spot to unwind after a day's work. The bartenders, skilled and personable, craft delicious drinks that are sure to please. Gather some friends and head over to this spot for a guaranteed good time – and don't forget to raise a glass for me!

Title: A Tale of Two Tastes at Local Eatery

I recently dined at this establishment and was greeted by an exceptionally friendly and attentive staff, which earns four stars in my book. Their warm smiles and positive attitudes made a great first impression.

The culinary experience, however, was a mix of hits and misses. On a high note, the soup dumplings were a delight, including the regular and spicy pork, as well as the chicken varieties. The sticky rice shumai and spicy pork dumplings did not disappoint either; they were simply delicious. The fried braised egg offered an intriguing and enjoyable twist to the meal.

Unfortunately, the kitchen's heavy hand with salt somewhat marred the dining experience. The drunken chicken and pork meatballs were overwhelmingly salty, to the point where they became challenging to eat towards the end of the meal, leaving me with a salt-induced headache and a desperate need for water. The braised tofu, while not as extreme, still tipped the scales on the saltier side.

In summary, the soup dumplings come highly recommended, and I sincerely hope the restaurant takes this feedback to heart and revisits the seasoning levels in their meatballs and drunken chicken dishes.

Food? Delicious. Service? Absolutely out of this world.Everyone working there was super friendly and welcoming, which is a bit rare for midtown and definitely a breathe of fresh air! They were also quite genuine and knowledgeable about all the dishes.My friend and I ordered the three course and a few sides and wow, you truly can't go wrong with anything here. I personally really liked the Pink Sultan and hummus (duh). The Pink Sultan felt unique to me -it's a yogurt and red beet spread which I haven't really had before and definitely thoroughly enjoyed. They had a great spicier spread to for spicy fans out there, I think it was the ezme. Also, can't forget to give the bread a shout out: 10/10 fresh warm Turkish bread For entrees we chose the falafel dish (classic) and lamb/beef kebabs, which were so so good. We topped of the night with a type of cinnamon flan, baklava, and Turkish tea.I guess the best part not only does everything taste amazing, but is everything is so healthy too!

Title: A Symphony of Flavors at [Restaurant Name]

Review:

From the moment we perused the menu at [Restaurant Name], it was evident that this was going to be an exceptional dining experience. The menu - a canvas of creativity - did not disappoint in the least upon execution.

Each dish that arrived was an exploration of flavors and textures. The Foie Gras Tortellini en Brodo was an exquisite start, with its savory broth harmonizing the rich tortellini against a backdrop of black lentils and crisp apple. The Branzino followed suit, perfectly cooked, and complemented by the subtle sweetness of delicata squash and the tang of sun-dried tomatoes.

The Anatra demanded attention with its perfectly seared duck breast, the heat of Calabrian chili honey accentuating the dish’s depth. The intrigue continued with the Lumache, where short rib met the indulgence of black truffle and a velvety bolognese bianco. Not to be outdone, the Funghi Trifolati was a masterclass in umami, thanks to the anchovy and garlic escorts.

A special mention must go to the special pasta dish— a delightful blend of mushrooms, goat cheese, and cream sauce that convinced us of the chef’s ability to transform the ordinary into the sublime.

Dessert was not an afterthought but a crowning jewel. The Milk Chocolate Tiramisu was a revelation, with its layers of flavor and texture, while the Affogato provided a classic yet potent endnote to the meal.

Returning? Undoubtedly. Recommending? Absolutely. And the tiramisu? Non-negotiable – it’s a must-have. [Restaurant Name] has set a towering standard for what it means to dine out.

Title: A Disappointing Experience at Cozy Soup 'n' Burger

I recently visited Cozy Soup 'n' Burger with some hesitation due to the mixed reviews. Although we were seated immediately in the largely empty restaurant, the service was disappointingly sluggish, and the staff seemed disinterested.

Our order consisted of a burger and a Belgian waffle. The burger was underwhelming, featuring a lackluster bun, a lifeless patty, wilted lettuce, and soggy tomatoes. Each bite confirmed the sad appearance was indicative of the taste. The waffle started off decently but quickly revealed an odd texture and an unexplainable off taste, though the Vermont syrup and fresh butter were its saving graces.

Despite the desire to find a silver lining, I must advise against dining here, particularly when the area offers many other superior and reasonably priced options.

Title: Late-Night Cravings Satisfied at Boka

Boka remains the quintessential spot for fried chicken aficionados in the heart of NYU territory, a beacon of comfort for college memories and late-night munchies. Open until 3am, it's the perfect haunt for post-party refueling, offering a delectable drumsticks and wings combo drenched in a savory soy garlic sauce that never disappoints. The portions are generous, ideal for sharing among a small group, making it not only a personal favorite but also a social staple. Despite its bustling atmosphere at night, the cozy vibe of Boka adds to the experience, ensuring that every visit is both vibrant and satisfying. For newcomers, delve straight into their signature fried chicken and partake in a rite of passage that many have relished before.

Title: Totto Ramen - A Surprising Culinary Delight!

My husband and I, self-proclaimed ramen aficionados, have slurped our way through the city's best. But Totto Ramen has truly toppled our rankings, seizing the top spot with a flourish and nudging the famed Ippudo aside. What's their secret? A humble chicken broth that's deceptively simple yet bursting with flavor. Their Paitan ramen has become our go-to, with its savory broth, succulent char siu, and a divine equilibrium of ingredients. And the noodles? Perfection. I'm known for never finishing my ramen, but at Totto, my bowl ends up polished clean every single time. Take it from a noodle enthusiast - Totto Ramen is a game-changer.

Title: A Gopchang Gem in Ktown, Be Ready for the Wait (and the Noise)!

My culinary journey to this Korean hotspot required a touch of pre-planning due to its bustling nature. On my first attempt, a daunting 2-hour wait sent me packing. However, persistence paid off on the second try; by joining the waitlist well in advance, my seat was ready within five minutes of arrival.

As a gopchang aficionado, I've tasted the spectrum from underwhelming to exquisite, and I'm thrilled to report that this venue's offerings land firmly in the latter category. The restaurant exudes a cool, nighttime vibe that pairs perfectly with a round of drinks.

Be warned, though – the blaring music could turn your dinner conversation into a shouting match. Despite this auditory challenge, this spot has secured its status as my gopchang go-to. Pro tip: Sign up on the waitlist ahead of time and brace yourself for an exuberant, if not loud, dining experience.

Stopped by for a quick bite and I was amazed by the ONE dish I ordered. So this review is based on one dish haha. The chicken drunken noodle came out hot and deliciously flavored! The noodle was soft and yummy, you might run out of noodles before the meat itself. The portion was definitely enough and the greens were nicely cooked and still has a crunch to them. The place was small, not suitable for big family gatherings but perfect for a date or a quick pick me up. The servers were nice and so was the ambience. Def worth a try if you're around the area!

Title: A Hidden Gem Near Bryant Park

My friends and I stumbled upon this surprisingly spacious eatery during a festive visit to the Christmas village at Bryant Park. Its open-concept kitchen lends a modern charm, and contrary to my initial skepticism given its tourist-centric location, the restaurant delivered an exceptional brunch experience.

We grappled with the notorious parking challenges in the area, causing us to forfeit our reservation, but luck was on our side as seating became available shortly after our tardy arrival. Reservations, however, are a must here.

The Raf Coffee stood out, striking the right balance of flavor without being cloying. As for the Shakshuka, it was unparalleled, especially when paired with shrimp. The truffle burger was another palate pleaser that had us returning for a second visit. This restaurant is a testament to the splendors that can be found in the most unexpected places. Highly recommend!

Had a great night here.  The most amazing french onion soup and then perfectly cooked rabbit over pappardelle with mustard sauce.  The branzino over couscous also looked delicious.  The apple tart was light and full of delicate apples with real vanilla ice cream.   High level culinary skills by the kitchen and attentive staff.  Grab a seat outside and enjoy New York at its best.

I remember seeing Manting on Mealpal and walked by it multiple times before but never got around to trying it. The lunch and post-lunch (aka dinner lol) are quite different considering how people usually get a ricebox with four dishes + soup. Post-lunch is when you can get their famous dry pot. In case anyone doesn't know, dry pot is a northern chinese dish that takes the spices in spicy hot pot (approximately the same but everyone's recipe is different) but uses it to stir fry ingredients instead. Anyway, 6pm Friday for 2I remember seeing how some Yelp reviews say that it's better to reserve because it'll get crowded during dinner time. To be honest, I can't find where to reserve lol. It ended up being ok for me anyway. It was like 70% full when I arrived at 6, so I got a table right away. I sat near the door, so it was quite chilly especially when people came in and out. Maybe avoid sitting near the door if you can. Dry pot You order everything on the menu at your table except for the dry pot which you just go up to the counter to order. You'll choose what ingredients you want that's behind the counter. They'll pick it up into a bowl and weigh the vegetables and meat separately. Meats cost slightly more per pound. There were two sections of counters for veggies and one for meats. They don't label the ingredients at the counter, so I was glad I studied the options on the menu before I got up to order. I appreciate how the veggies were submerged in water to preserve freshness. Regardless, all the ingredients could be more fresh. A couple of ingredients ran out. I ended up getting 1.095lb of veggies and 1.465lb of meats.Medium spicy. It came out very flavorful, you can taste the wok hei of it. Medium spicy was not overly spicy, only a little bit on certain bites with higher concentration of spices. It felt quite satay and peanut oil strong actually. Surprisingly it didn't feel too oily, but you can see a puddle of oil at the bottom when you're done eating. We didn't ask but seems like all dry pot comes with white rice. I wonder if they do per head or just 2 for every dry pot ordered. That's nice tbh. You'll definitely want some rice to go with it. Beef Tripe MalatangI didn't know what malatang was beforehand, but according to wikipedia it sounded like the wet version of the dry pot....hotpot without the fire? jk not sure. It came out tasting quite different than the dry pot's flavors. I remember other yelp reviews said that the malatang was more spicy than the dry pot so tone down when choosing the spiciness. I have to disagree. I got mild spicy and quite regret it. The soup became barely spicy. It tastes more like some sort of noodle broth. Either way - not a fan I typically only eat beef tripe as a dim sum, so this was a different take on it. But I felt meh about the ones here. Also the portion of the tripe seemed a bit too small, I remember eating two big pieces and that's it. My friend maybe had one or two too. Guess what there's vermicelli at the bottom! I did not know that until I was pouring the leftovers into a takeout container at the end. This would've been sufficient to order as a whole regular main course. There's actually a bunch of other side veggie ingredients - all of which can be chosen for the dry pot. I hope I got them all but: broccoli, cauliflower, black fungus, seaweed thing, sweet potato, dried tofu, beancurd skin. I actually don't like how it came with so many things - loses focus of the dish. Braised Beef Noodle SoupOk I actually liked this. The noodles were round and very soft/slurpable. It was able to absorb the soup base without becoming mushy. There's a big portion of noodles. It was really cute how the braised beef was cut into small cubes. They were also very tender and soft. I was hoping that the braise marinate can be stronger because the beef was a bit under marinated. Preserved vegetables were added here. I personally don't like eating it directly but the slight sour juices that seemed into the broth/noodles/beef added another layer of flavor which was refreshing. Coconut milkHahah I ordered it in case things got too spicy. Apparently it's coconut milk from Hainan but the flavor reminds me of Vitasoy - I like vitasoy more though lolMy friend and I definitely over ordered by getting 3 dishes. We thought the malatang wouldn't be a full dish. Tbh it would've been fine to just get the dry pot to share. It's quite sufficient. If you were by yourself or it's lunchtime, the noodle soup would be nice. Anyway the price for the amount of food they give is good.

The voluminous menu with colorful photos is wonderful to look at but slightly overwhelming, so I went with my favorite: Beef Pho, specifically, Brisket pho - with the works!  Let me tell you, the whopping bowl of Vietnamese goodness arrived promptly, and it took all the good manners I could muster, not to want to just dive in!!  Glasses fogged before the first spoonful, it did not disappoint: a separate bowl of crunchy, fresh cilantro and basil, and thick, juicy beansprouts ample sprig of greens, along with the plentiful red onion, parsley and other herbs, made this super soup, a treasure trove of delight for your tastebuds, nose and eyes!!  Paper thin shavings of beef with just the right flavor which blends together with all the other yummy things: rice-vermicelli noodles, etc.  I wanted so much to make a serious dent -- but alas, I will be having this for at least 2 other meals!!  Also, the tea on the table is very nice, an old school touch, I really appreciate.-1 star due to the fact that when I plopped my $20 bill down on the bill, it was whisked away (I thought without any change returned).  When I finally flagged a waiter down he said they must be "busy" at the register, but since I'm a busy gal, I almost dashed out without it!  (Bring exact change)!! ;)

This was my first time having duck at a Chinese restaurant. It was phenomenal. The fatty flavor. It was so delicious. It's important to exercise moderation. It gets addictive really quickly. I adore Dan Dan noodles. They were nice enough to serve it without pork and it was great. The thin sliced beef with chilli powder was great. Filling meal that doesn't weigh down on you.It was memorable for sure.

My recent dining experience at this restaurant on a Saturday night shortly after 9:30pm was notable, especially since the establishment was surprisingly uncrowded. We began our meal with the chicken karaage, which was exceptional. The sweet garlic soy sauce elevated the dish to a point where resisting the urge to clean the plate with my tongue was a challenge. Moving on to the Tonkotsu ramen, I opted for additional takana and crushed garlic. While the broth leaned towards the saltier side, it wasn't enough to detract from the enjoyment. The noodles were a highlight, boasting an ideal texture that showcased their dedication to quality. I'm eager to return, not just for the food, but also to explore their sake list.

I bookmarked this restaurant on Yelp a while ago.  I was invited to have dinner at the restaurant a few weeks ago.  For a party of 5, we ordered the following starters: 1. Deep fried Brussel sprouts, 2. Sichuan cold noodles, 3. Shanghai soup dumplings.  1. Deep fried Brussel sprouts - it is rare for this dish to be available at a Chinese restaurant.  And the way they prepare this dish is better than a lot of the brunch places I go to.  The Brussel sprouts are crispy and not soggy and it is well seasoned.  2. Sichuan cold noodles - this dish comes with chewy thick noodles and sesame paste.  It is drizzled with Szechuan style chili oil.  And the balance of sauce and noodles is great.  I do not like cold noodles that are soaked in sauce.  The Sichuan cold noodles here are not too spicy or salty.  3. Shanghai soup dumplings - I was told by my friend that the soup dumplings here is a must try dish.  I like dipping it in the black vinegar sauce with sliced ginger (the traditional way).  Their soup dumplings are pretty good compared to a lot of the dumpling places.For entrees, we ordered the following dishes: 1. Crispy baby shrimp with salted egg sauce, 2. BBQ spare ribs, 3.Steamed fish fillets with diced red peppers, 4. Hotpot beef fillets with mixed veggies.1. Crispy baby shrimp with salted egg sauce - very unique authentic Chinese dish.  This is one of the best entrees we tried that night.  The salted egg sauce evenly coated each deep fried shrimp, giving it a good savory flavor.  2. BBQ spare ribs - per the website, this is the bestseller for 30 years.  Their bbq spare ribs definitely are the best that I have ever tasted.  They are chunky big ribs, as opposed to the skinny bbq ribs you normally would get at Chinese take-outs.  The meat is succulent, with a honey glazed sauce coating each piece.  The edges are slightly charred to give it a slight Smokey flavor.  This is definitely a dish you would need to eat with your hands.  You must order their ribs when you come to this restaurant.3. Steamed fish fillets with diced red peppers - Very delightful dish, the diced red peppers give the steamed fish a new dimension of flavors.  It leaves your tongue with a slight tingling feeling with the spiciness.  4. Hotpot beef fillets with mixed veggies - this is another dish that I think is a must try here.  My friend said this dish reminded him of home.  The soup is a spicy broth. The sliced beef and mixed vegetables are cooked in the boiling broth.  The flavor is comforting (reminds people of authentic home cooking).  The spiciness would warm your body.  The decorations at this place are so cute, the present owner, Nancy Lee, recently renovated the place.  The interior looks chic & sleek and it has pink wall paper.  The walls are filled with carved decorative pigs with messages from different people.  You definitely don't feel that you are sitting in a Chinese restaurant with a long history in NYC.  They play some good music in the restaurant.  It is perfect for gatherings or even dates!   If you are in the mood for dishes prepared with a blend of Cantonese and Sichuan styles and you want to try something authentic, you should definitely come eat here.  The dishes are prepared family style, make sure you do not over-order.   I cannot wait to come back to try their suckling pig and tomato & tofu soup with thinly sliced beef and pickled pepper.  This is way better than affording the big price tags and some upscale Chinese restaurants in the city that serve up the Americanized version of Chinese dishes.  The best part is it is conveniently located on the upper east side, so it is easy to get to.

I recently ventured to try a new rice bowl spot and was pleasantly taken aback by the quality of my first meal. The rice bowl was surprisingly delicious, though I did encounter a minor disappointment when I discovered an additional $1 charge for an egg – a detail that was not clearly indicated on the Seamless app, as the picture included an egg without offering an add-on option.

Moreover, the menu's promise of shredded pork turned out to be ground meat, which didn't align with my expectations based on the description. Despite these initial hiccups, the flavors were spot-on, prompting me to give the restaurant another try.

On my second visit, I ordered directly at the register, opting for the red curry chicken with the extra $1 egg. This time, the dish lived up to its description, proving to be a wholly satisfying experience.

The savory layers of the red curry infused with tender chicken made a lasting impression. I'm eager to return and explore more of their rice bowl offerings. This spot has earned its place on my go-to list for quick and tasty meals.

Considering I'm a verrrrry big fan of hot pot, I'm embarrassed to admit that I had no idea that dry hot pot was a thing until my friend suggested we eat at LaoMa Spicy last week. Thank god she educated me on the wonder that is dry hot pot because hot damn was I missing out! Don't get me wrong, I will always love me some (wet) hot pot, but I have to admit that it is pretty nice not having to cook your own food and poke your gluten ball for the hundredth time to see if it's finally done cooking (9/10 times it is not) because at dry hot... everything is already all cooked AND flavored when it comes to your table. YASSSSS.At LaoMa Spicy, you don't order the dry hot pot at your seats--instead you head up to the counter where you pick and choose exactly what you want in your dry hot pot. There was literally a couple dozen different options, including my (wet) hot pot favorites: fatty beef, fish balls + straw mushrooms. You pick your spice level (fair warning: this place lives up to their name and it is SPICYYY) and are then charged based on the combined weight of your picks and how many bowls of white rice you want on the side. For our group of 6, we split a few appetizers, which were all delicious (but again, super, super spicy and I can usually handle a good amount of spice) and 2 bowls of dry hot pot that weighed about 3 lbs each (each bowl ended up being ~$40). Although the service was a bit slow, it was worth it because everything was soooooo flavorful and fresh and we literally cleaned up every last bit of those huge bowls. I was very pleased with my first dry hot pot experience and I'm already making plans to go again to show others the LaoMa Spicy way.

Title: Almost Perfect Lobster Rolls at Luke's Lobster Times Square

As a seasoned connoisseur of lobster rolls, my loyalty has long been pledged to Luke's. Their rolls have consistently topped my list, and my recent visit to Luke's Times Square location reaffirms their culinary reign, despite one notable drawback.

Service & Atmosphere: The Times Square branch may lack the quintessential New England charm that other Luke's spots boast, yet it compensates with remarkable efficiency. Amid the lunchtime bustle, my mother and I received our order in a mere five minutes.

Portions vs. Cost: It's here that my praise slightly wanes. The standard $17 lobster roll is undeniably petite, and the leap to $23 for a 'jumbo' roll, which barely lives up to its name, feels like a misstep. The expectation of 'jumbo' isn't met, calling for a reconsideration of the pricing strategy.

Food Quality: Putting the price point aside, Luke's culinary craftsmanship remains unparalleled. Each bite of the buttery, toasted roll filled with peppery lobster is a reminder of why their rolls are simply the best.

Return Visit: Despite the pricing hiccup, my excitement for a return visit remains unscathed. Luke's has a knack for creating a lobster roll experience that beckons loyalists and newcomers alike.

In summary, Luke's Lobster Times Square serves up excellence with swift service and unmatched lobster roll quality, although the jumbo pricing could do with a generous side of revaluation. Four out of five stars.

A fantastic dining experience. The food came all at once, and each dish had interesting flavor after flavor. The papaya salad with salted duck egg is a must-order, as were the coconut sticky rice Moo Ping Kati Sod. The meat was tender and flavorful with a strong kick. Of the five dishes we ordered,  I'd say the catfish larb was the weakest, though still good.

Title: A Cozy Dinner Experience from Quantum Leap

Having previously enjoyed brunch at a different Quantum Leap location, I decided to give their dinner delivery a try. My selections for the evening were the Pad Thai and Chicken Nuggets.

The Pad Thai, which I rate at a solid 4 out of 5, was served with an accompanying salad that truly shined with its refreshing flavors. While the noodles themselves were somewhat lacking in zest, the mock chicken pieces added a satisfying element. The highlight, for me, was indeed the tasty salad.

Moving on to the Chicken Nuggets, they earned a respectable 3.5 out of 5. Reminiscent of the veggie nuggets from Enjoy Vegetarian in San Francisco, their texture was spot-on. However, the accompanying dipping sauce presented an odd taste profile that didn't quite hit the mark for me.

Impressively, the food arrived in quality containers that ensured the meal remained enjoyable even after a 15-20 minute wait; the nuggets managed to retain their crispiness, which I appreciated.

Overall, Quantum Leap's delivery service did a commendable job of bringing a wholesome meal to my doorstep. Despite some flavor mismatches, the convenience and quality of the meal were appreciable.

When you walk into Keens you're transported to old times. The decor is super unique and definitely has an old school vibe to it. We took a 9:30 pm reservation as it was their last seating on Sunday and came here for my 30th birthday as a special occasion.  It didn't feel like they were rushing us at all either. The place was vibey even on a Sunday night. We started out with a bottle of wine from Argentine (Sue de Los Andes) which was super delightful. Appetizer we had the crab cakes which were pretty delicious with a nice cream sauce and pickled salad. You can't go wrong with the Porterhouse steak and because I really wanted to try the Main lobster, our waiter offered to have it on the side for an extra $23. I was alittle surprised at how little we got for that price (two claws and a tail). For the sides definitely get the mashed potatoes, mushrooms and green beans! Would definitely recommend to people but I would also probably try a different steakhouse in NYC (because there are so many) before going back myself.

Angels came out the sky and delivered our tuna tartare appetizer...HOLY *****! The rest of the meal: tomato burrata salad and eggs benedict were also fabulous but the real star was the tuna. The service was excellent and our waitress was attentive and personable. I can not recommend enough for a leisurely Sunday brunch. (Angel comment/photo credit Kim D.)

Can it be Ho Yip reincarnated? Might as well be because it it as good as my recently closed favorite Chinese buffet a few streets away!Chen's is a no-nonsense, "grab a quick lunch" type of places, and regulars who work or live in FiDi know it, as it can get crowded.The food is all super tasty! On the buffet, be sure to try the pork chop with pepper, curry chicken, and beef mei fun (the one with wider noodles). All super, super tasty! They also have combos that can be ordered at the service counter. These are awesome as well.If you have read enough reviews of this place, you likely saw they are known for their excellent pricing. It is indeed true--only $6.99 a pound for their buffet (and it gets cheaper as they approach closing time).

We were in NYC for NYE and we came here in 2014 and now in 2019/2020. Each time we come here this place gets better and better. We knew this would be a whole night in itself, the gypsy band was amazing, they even had some performers come from the crowd and sing. We met and sang and danced with other people in the restaurant, the food, as usual, was delish, the infused vodka is great we tried almost every flavor between my husband and I. My husband is Russian and therefore was able to speak with the staff. Our waiter was AMAZING, we recommend this place to everyone who goes to New York. We can't wait to come back the next time we're in town.

I recently dined at this restaurant and had quite a mixed experience. To start on a high note, the squash soup with popcorn was delightful and a clear standout. It's a must-try for anyone visiting. Unfortunately, for those with dietary restrictions, our dining experience was slightly marred by the lack of gluten-free dessert options, which was disappointing. I also tried the pumpkin risotto, which was served al dente — not to my liking, and I wish the menu or server had indicated this preference, as I would have chosen differently. However, the drinks were exceptional, and the bartenders deserve a special mention for their skill and friendly service. Despite the great drinks and soup, I'm left uncertain about returning.

Title: A Feast of Flavors at Xian’s Noodle Haven

If you're seeking the unforgettable experience of authentic hand-ripped noodles, look no further than Xian. The star of the show for me is the N1: spicy cumin lamb noodles—a dish brimming with flavor and zest, sure to satisfy unless cumin isn’t your thing. Their hand-pulled noodles hit the mark consistently with just the right texture.

While I frequent this location for its convenience, be warned that peak hours can lead to busy scenes with potential understaffing. The staff, though, remains friendly. Expect some wait time due to the fresh preparation of noodles, so this may not be your quick lunch spot.

Be mindful that the coveted cumin lamb might be sold out later in the day. Apart from my favorite N1, I've ventured into the N2: beef noodles, NS2: spicy tingly beef soup, and N9: pork noodles—all flavorful, although the beef noodles were slightly lacking in meat quantity.

To wrap up your meal, the tea offered provides a sweet end—quite delightful albeit a tad sugary for some. Overall, Xian is a must-try for noodle lovers—just plan your visit with time on your side.

This is my favorite place in NYC to grab tacos. Some of the best al pastor and chorizo (my tacos of choice) that I have had outside of Mexico. You can't miss this place when your walking down 116th st with the rotisserie of al pastor in the window and the intoxicating smell. You can stop in to pick up or if your lucky you can grab some of the few seating they have lined up against the wall. I've brought multiple of my friends here and every single time they have told me that it lived up to the hype.

Tucked away in the basement of an office complex lies a delightful Japanese gem that transports diners straight to the streets of Japan. First-time visitors should be sure to get precise directions, as the hidden location coupled with spotty phone service might pose a challenge for meet-ups.

The expansive menu offers a variety of traditional Japanese dishes, although some items tend to run out by early afternoon. Service can be hit or miss – during my visit, we struggled to catch the waitstaff's attention for a simple request like a forgotten spoon, inadvertently becoming a spectacle for fellow diners.

Culinary speaking, the meal was exceptionally satisfying. The shrimp tempura over rice and soba noodles delivered both flavor and comfort, while the matcha tiramisu ended the meal on a decadently creamy note. Despite minor setbacks, the restaurant offers a solid dining experience with great food and an authentic atmosphere.

Title: A Juicy Surprise at Thunder Bun

If you're working near 1 New York Plaza and hunger strikes, Thunder Bun is your go-to burger oasis within a stone's throw. Brace yourself for the peak lunch rush from 12pm to 1pm; the lines rival those of theme park attractions. The menu is a parade of American fast-food staples, freshly made to order – it's more than your average burger joint.

My choice, The Thunder Bun, with an accompaniment of waffle fries, was an experience to remember. I wisely opted for takeout, dodging the long wait. The burger, a traditional cheeseburger turned up a notch with an extra slice of cheese, was an oozy masterpiece. It was love at first sight, despite the oil and cheese sweat on the packaging. The steamed potato bun held up valiantly against the onslaught of juicy succulence. It was so tender and flavorful that it disappeared before I even realized, the grease practically ushering it down.

And let's talk about the waffle fries – the perfect crunchy-soft balance to complement the burger. A duo that deserved applause.

Thunder Bun may lean towards the pricier side for a burger in NYC at $6.50, but it stands out in the league of flavor and satisfaction. Don't expect a bland, fast-food experience – this burger gushes with greasy goodness and keeps you coming back for more.

Title: A Tasty Encore at Khe-Yo During Restaurant Week

Rating: ★★★★☆ (3.5/5, rounded up)

Returning to Khe-Yo for Restaurant Week was a decision motivated by their irresistible winter menu. Once again, the restaurant did not disappoint, especially with the starters. The scallops were the star of the show—silky and beautifully marinated in an apple citrus vinaigrette. The yellowfin tuna laab was an innovative twist on the classic, with its ceviche-like zesty flavors and perfectly diced fish. Another standout was the curried shrimp chips, which added a delightful crunch to the appetizer lineup.

Moving on to the main course, the hanger steak served with egg noodles delivered a punch of flavor, albeit reminiscent of an upmarket lo mein, which may not surprise those well-versed in Asian cuisines. Accompaniments like pickled chilies added a welcomed kick, yet it failed to truly captivate my palate. The black bass, though cozy and enjoyable, lacked a memorable factor that would beckon me back for more.

Dessert was where the evening hit a slight snag. Anticipating a novel experience with pomegranate, I was met instead with a choice between toasted coconut gelato and tangerine sorbet due to an unannounced menu change—a small letdown. Nevertheless, the tangerine sorbet was refreshing, if not extraordinary.

Despite a few hiccups, Khe-Yo proves to be a commendable ambassador for Laotian cuisine in the city. While I've encountered more impressive offerings elsewhere, the restaurant's highlights—particularly those appetizers—make it a worthwhile visit. Here's to hoping for more of those exceptional scallops in future menus.

My boyfriend and I, famished after a downtown stroll, decided to finally try Little Poland - a restaurant long on our to-do list. We arrived post-lunch hour to an almost empty diner, which heightened our awareness of the service, an aspect previously critiqued in other reviews.

We shared cheese pierogi and a meatloaf sandwich. The pierogi, unfortunately, were not what I expected. Their sweet and dense filling was initially enjoyable, but as they cooled, the grease made them less appetizing. On the flip side, the meatloaf sandwich, while visually unimpressive with its thick meat slices between dry rye bread, was satisfying. However, it was served with only a pickle that had an off-putting medicinal taste.

Service-wise, we struggled. Our water cups remained unfilled despite several requests, and even getting the check required effort. While Little Poland may have its charm and simplicity, the lack of attentive service was noticeable. When the pierogi craving strikes again, I’ll likely head over to Streecha instead.

Luke's Lobster in Midtown East maintains the chain's reputation for serving up delectable, albeit petite, lobster rolls. The buns are a delightful combination of buttery goodness and perfect toasting, while the lobster meat is fresh and features a generous portion of claw meat, which personally, I find adds a pleasant texture. While it may not be the ultimate lobster roll I've ever had, it certainly stands out in New York City. I recommend upsizing for a heartier experience, but the combo meals are sufficient for a satisfying meal. Even when opting for delivery, this location impresses with prompt and accurate service that often beats the estimated time.

This place far exceeded my expectations. I figured it would be a little whole in the wall- I mean in the garment district there would be a hipster place? But there it was. And they let us sit and talk along time which was good because we hadn't seen each other in a very long time. They make fabulous pancakes and bacon, great salad with shrimp or chicken. And good coffee. Probably everything here is good. They are attached to another place that has breakfast type food- wasn't exactly sure of the relationship here.

The interior to this restaurant is stunning with florals every where. It is very romantic perfect for dates. Perfect for brunch, and coming with your friends, too. I ordered Fettuccine ai Fungi which is gluten free with mushrooms and black truffle. My husband ordered a meat dish (sorry I forgot) but I remember it being delicious! I would go here again.

This is a French bakery chain with locations worldwide, including several in Manhattan. I have had several of their pastries on different occasions and some of their drinks as well. The tea and coffee from here is nothing special and no different than any other chain. Their pastries on the other hand are definitely good quality. The best of the bunch are definitely the various fruit tarts which tasted very fresh. Their chocolate pastries were very rich tasting as well.They also have a very large inventory of breads and sandwiches. This place is actually very similar in selection and quality to Le Pain Quotidien, another bakery chain.

Tucked away in the bustling streets of NYC, this iconic pizzeria is a staple on every tourist's "must-eat" list and a one-time curiosity for locals. My visit was a serendipitous affair, thanks to an out-of-town friend's insistence. Despite its cash-only policy, conveniently, an ATM is hosted inside.

We arrived at 6:30 pm to a 30-40 minute wait, which pleasantly turned out to be just 20-25 minutes—even on a jam-packed Saturday evening. The menu choices were straightforward; we opted for the renowned clam pizza and a standard margherita. Serving a party of five, the large and small pizzas sufficed, especially with dessert plans afoot.

The clam pizza was an aromatic marvel, its garlic scent tempting without overwhelming, and a splash of fresh lemon elevated the flavors further.
