Crisp and thin, the crust was a delightful endnote to each slice. The margherita, reliable in taste, paled slightly when compared to its clam counterpart.

However, one cannot ignore the steep price—$75 for two pizzas and a beer, tipping included. While the allure of the name might justify the cost for some, New York's plethora of pizzerias offer competitive taste at a fraction.

Service was commendable; our server was attentive amidst the chaos, ensuring our glasses remained filled.

Would I return? Perhaps, if only to cater to a visitor's checklist, as this pizzeria's fame and unique offerings warrant at least a single indulgence.

I came here to catch up with a friend around 4:30 pm on a Saturday before Christmas. Odeon exuded an air of simple elegance and some 80s New York flair. I ordered the steak tartare, fried calamari, omelette and the profiterole. The steak tartare was an appetizer that came in an entre size. We actually ran out of crostini but the server was generous enough to replenish it for us. The batter for the fried calamari was served as a breaded mixture and came with two dipping sauces. The omelette, which is also served for dinner, was served with a side of perfectly hot fried skinny fries. I was able to select three ingredients to go inside the omelette, which contained vegetable, meat and cheese options. Dinner ended with the profiterole which is like a cream puff but with ice cream, chocolate and slivered almonds (three were served). The ambience was great, I didn't feel rushed while eating and the Christmas decorations were simply yet festive. Overall I would recommend this place if you're in the tribeca area and you're looking for some classic yet well done dishes.

Our favorite pizza slice we had in NYC! Walk in here and you'll see the walls covered in celebrities who are fans of Joe's. If Leonardo DiCaprio likes Joe's Pizza, I like it too. It was about 10pm and the place was packed. Located only a few blocks from Times Square, I can only assume that it was mostly full of tourists trying this famous pizza. There are several different types of pizzas on display, and you have to be ready to choose quickly when it's your turn, as there's a long line and the staff move fast. We got two slices of cheese pizza and a margherita slice to-go and ate them in our hotel. The slices were super thin, as big as my head, and perfectly crispy on the bottom, with deliciously melted cheese. I miss it already.

Not only is the ambiance and decor pretty cool but the food is good too!  The menu is a mix of California cursive with Italian and Korean influences. The pizzas are really great and perfect to share. All the appetizers we had were fabulous but I had the mixed greens salad and salmon as an entree and the salmon was a bit overcooked and the salad had a touch too much stressing, which I should have asked to have on the side. We all shared the cheesecake and that was easy better and lighter than expected.

Come here for the dumplings and then order all the dumplings. My dad, husband and I came here on a Thursday night after a holiday party, and were immediately seated. We tried two varieties of dumplings: Soup Dumpling with Pork and the Black Truffle Soup Dumpling with Pork. Both were fantastic - thin skin, flavorful broth and a tasty ball of pork. I would recommend the black truffle only if you really like the taste of truffle. For mains we shared the braised boar hock with baby bok choy, and the Shanghai style lo main with beef. Both were excellent. The braised boar hock is pretty fatty and filling, and I'd only recommend to more "open" eaters. Pro Tips:- Come for the dumplings. Order all the dumplings. - Good for groups and walk-ins

Title: A Rocky Start Leading to a Satisfactory Brunch Experience

During our first visit to our son's new neighborhood eatery for brunch, we found ourselves seated in the back room where, unfortunately, we were neglected for 45 minutes despite the visible presence of staff members preoccupied with their phones. This oversight nearly prompted us to leave; however, the manager intervened just in time, reseating us and ensuring prompt service thereafter. The food we eventually received was quite enjoyable, and the gesture of complimentary drinks was appreciated. While we plan to return, we'll be sure to avoid the back room and hope to see improvement in the attentiveness of the service. If not for the initial service lapse, this review might have shone with a higher rating.

Title: A Gluten-Free Gem in Hell's Kitchen

I recently discovered a fantastic spot for gluten-free dining in Hell's Kitchen. The staff here are not only friendly but also exceptionally knowledgeable about gluten-free options, which is a huge relief for anyone with gluten sensitivities.

My meal of choice was the Korean fried chicken drenched in their signature "Hells Sauce," which was the perfect combination of crispy and moist. However, it's worth noting that they top the chicken with nuts, so if that's an issue for you, make sure to mention it to your server. Though a bit disappointing for gluten-free diners, the soy garlic sauce option is not gluten-free, so steer clear of that.

To accompany my meal, I opted for a bottled Doc's hard cider, which was a delightful pairing. Adding to the charm of this establishment was the background music, a quirky mix of '80s pop ballads and lounge cover songs that set a playful mood.

All in all, this place is a must-visit for anyone looking for a worry-free, gluten-free dining experience with a side of nostalgia.

Au Cheval is Enchanté!This restaurant lives up to all the hype and is an amazing experience. Top quality service and food!When you get here it is on a side street on the outskirts of Chinatown and has real NYC character. When you enter the restaurant it gives off a very cool trendy vibe and has a lot big booths great for groups of 4-6. The whole dining room floor is open concept and you can see into the kitchen which is cool. In addition they have a downstairs bar/quick food restaurant called small cheval for those looking for more of a bar/speakeasy type of vibe.I went here for date night and was very happy with the choice. We started the evening by popping a bottle of wine so it can only get better from here.For food we got the:- General Jane's Honey Fried chicken which was an awesome sweet spicy Asian twist on American comfort food of fries chicken- Single Cheeseburger w/ bacon and egg. This burger was cooked to perfection and the egg with bacon on made it beautiful yolky mess! I could eat this burger every day- Crispy Fries - which had an egg on top with 2 side sauces of Mornay Sauce and garlic aioli - the potato's here are top notch and all the employees said we had to get one and they were right which is why I got these and they hit the spot and were a great paid with our main courses. Desert we got the Millie-Fueille which is a light puffy pastry that is super flaky. I have not had anything like this before and it was amazing. I highly suggest ending your meal with this desert.In short:- Delicious Food- Great Service- Cool date spot but note the food can be messy- Good for groups of 4-6- Cool speakeasy type bar in the basement- I will be back here

My latest visit to Becco's—either the third or fourth—reaffirms why this place has become a staple for delightful dining experiences. As always, the service was impeccable right from the moment we walked in, enhancing the whole atmosphere with attentiveness and warmth.

The meal kicked off with an assortment of breads, perfectly complemented by a flavorsome white bean dip. The Caesar salad, notable for its authentic inclusion of anchovies, was a hit at our table, bursting with flavor.

The veal cutlet, a favorite of my husband's, arrived on the bone, cooked to perfection and oozing with succulence. I indulged in the Bronzino special, which was outstanding in its simplicity and taste.

Becco's consistency in delivering quality food and top-notch service easily makes it a highly-recommended destination. Do yourself a favor and make a reservation; this has become a must-visit restaurant for us, and it's clear why.

So delicious! I got their signature spaghetti dish and thought it looked bland, but it tastes anything but that. Very creamy, flavorful, and delicious. The restaurant can get a little hot so keep that in mind -they had all the windows completely open and it was a hot day but I'd assume (hope) that wouldn't be the case on even hotter days.My only qualm I guess is the price -I paid around $30-32 for one pasta dish including tax and tip which is kinda pricey. None the less I'd definitely come back (hopefully often -super yummy pasta).This restaurant isn't upscale but it's a nice casual option for a dinner out or date.

I plan coming to Saltbae Burger since last week, my plan was to go eat over there and hope there's not too much people and get to meet The legendary Salt Bae. Today it happened that exact way. First the service was great. The waiters are respectful and attentive. The food is delicious. I ate the juicy burger and a easy burger. My wife had the Salt Bae Burger. The burger was so juicy like the name and the meat was medium well cooked. The price is reasonable especially for the great food and service.The environment is friendly, make you want to come back. They also have beer and wine. For dessert, they only have shakes. I feel they should add traditional Turkish desserts to the menu. Overall I love this place. Salt bae was respectful and I was able to get a picture.

Adorable decor at this restaurant! The cauliflower hummus salad was really good. They packed on the hummus and the cauliflower was cooked nicely. My boyfriend got the kubeh dish. It's basically like a denser matzah ball soup with a few more spices.

I was won over by the bread and this sun dried tomato and olive oil spread/dip. The bread had a great crispy crust and a tangy, moist, soft center. I would come back just for that!As an appetizer I enjoyed the Arancini Castanesi which were essentially fried rice balls that came with a small portion of arugula and tomatoes. I think the arancini needed the acidity and bite of the tomatoes and arugula to cut through the richness, but overall I'd order again. Unfortunately the middle of mine was cold.Me and my friend split two pastas: the tagliatelle Verdi and the cavatelli. Both were delicious. I loved the truffle and herbs of the tagliatelle. The cavatelli was delicious but also very heavy - choose this one if you're really hungry or you want to bring some home! For desert, we shared the panna cotta. I am actually going to say this was the best panna cotta I've had! Loved the berries and the pistachios. The texture was just right.I'll probably be a regular here after this one visit.

That a badd place to grab a drink but if you're looking for super cheap or an extensive happy hour menu this is not it. Though they do have very good choices for well drinks/liquors they will still run you about 8 to $10 for a mix drink. Even draft beers were about 8 bucks for happy hour. The bartenders were pretty no nonsense type ladies but they were friendly enough to grab a drink and get by. Would I come back maybe, maybe not. They do have real ginger  beer for dark and stormy seas or any other drink of that type.

I love burgers and this has consistently been one of my favorite burger spots. The place is decorated in a really cute retro style. I always like to check out a restaurant's bathroom and this one doesn't disappoint, I especially like all of the Jet magazine covers used to decorate. My go to order here is actually from the kid's menu, it comes with a mini burger, fries and a drink. For me the kid's meal is the perfect size, I really love the fries here. Even though I'm not a dairy person I usually order the black and white milkshake from here. I've been coming here for a while and at one point it seemed that the milkshakes changed and it was not for the better so I started to avoid the shakes. If you're into burgers then this is a great place to check out.

Title: A Ravishing Rendezvous with Restaurant Week

My recent visit during Restaurant Week left me spellbound, offering not just a meal but a culinary journey that has etched itself in my heart. The two-course delight for a mere $26 ensures a choice between an appetizer and entrée, or if whims strike, swapping the latter for a dessert. 

The starter, Polpettini, was indeed a spectacle – pork meatballs that were the epitome of perfection with their crispy exterior and succulent interior, though I confess the accompanying sauce was not to my taste; a minor hiccup in an otherwise impeccable dish.

The star of the midday was indisputably the Cappellacci Di Zucca, butter squash ravioli that danced on the palate with their ethereal lightness and rich buttery flavor. Each bite reaffirmed my decision; these ravioli are worthy of an encore.

Amidst the charming decor and attentive waitstaff, time slipped through our fingers. Realizing our lunch hour drawing to a close, our waiter graciously expedited our entrees with kindness, wrapping up desserts for a sweet send-off.

Anticipation already brews for a return visit – one where time is no constraint, and where the allure of cocktails and a languid dining experience beckons.

During my recent trip to New York, I had the opportunity to dine twice at this bustling spot. My first visit was for Saturday brunch, where I enjoyed the tantalizing 'Holla Pain Yo!' margarita along with customizable guacamole - both delicious, though I found the ingredient portions perfectly measured for my taste with no room for omission. Service was sufficient despite the crowd, though the assertiveness of our server to return later when we hesitated felt somewhat pushy.

My second experience was during happy hour, and the bar staff outshone their table-side counterparts with friendliness and efficiency, reinforcing the high-energy vibe of the ever-popular setting. A word to the wise for the management: attentiveness to restroom supplies is crucial, as a lack of toilet paper can lead to an awkward situation for patrons. Overall, expect lively ambience and flavorful bites if you can navigate the crowds.

The service was great and the ambiance was nice. I wasn't too impressed with the food apart from the jasmine ice cream. Everything else had a strange mixture of flavors. The rice pudding was a bit too citrus-y, the truffle pasta had some sour taste to it too. The sherbet was interesting to say the least. The honey fried chicken was good and they gave us a free dessert for birthday celebration. For the amount of money, I would choose other places over this one although I am sincerely grateful they introduced me to jasmine ice cream.

Definitely not the fanciest venue but I'm a sucker for hole in the wall type place and love the aesthetic. I mean, it's really more so about the food! I've tried their hand pulled noodles with duck and it was awesome the first time and the second time it was good but I was less wow-ed? The duck has been consistently great though. What I now come back for are the pan fried chicken dumplings with chili oil. Sooo goooood!!! It's simple but delicious, I recommend it as an appetizer when you go

Title: Satisfying Szechuan with a Hint of Taipei

My latest culinary escapade brought me to a bustling spot known for its Chinese and Szechuan cuisine with a delightful Taiwanese twist. Before diving into the details, here's a pro tip: join the waitlist on Yelp in advance to avoid the lengthy dinner queues.

The menu is a feast of flavors, and I decided to indulge in various dishes. The cabbage with dried peppers was a standout vegetable dish, offering a bold Szechuan taste that was well-balanced, avoiding the common pitfall of an overly sauced dish. Unfortunately, the wontons in chili oil fell short, coming across as rather ordinary.

Moving on to the heartier fare, the garlic sauce style lamb was generously filled with bamboo, woodear mushrooms, bell peppers, and onions, creating a medley of textures and tastes. The three cup chicken carried the essence of the cuisine well, though it was a tad too salty for my palate.

Despite the restaurant's hectic atmosphere, the service was commendable. However, the dining experience was slightly marred at the end when I discovered a black residue peeling off the teapot’s rim. This mishap not only left a mark on my hands and napkin but also raised concerns about the quality and safety of their serving ware, an area that urgently needs attention.

Overall, the meal was enjoyable with a few minor hitches. Definitely worth a visit for those craving authentic flavors with a twist.

Upon stumbling upon this northern outpost of the Spice restaurant chain, I was pleasantly surprised to see the brand's reliable presence in an unexpected locale. Though some aficionados might quibble over authenticity, Spice holds its own with a sufficiently genuine offering for the area. Consistent with its NYC siblings, the service here was prompt, the food satisfying with generous portions, and the pricing reasonable. Ideal for sating a gin-fueled appetite without disappointment.

Y'all. When I say this is the best ramen place on earth, I mean it. I can never go back to eating cup noodles no more as it would be a disgrace compared to ichiran. I literally shed a tear when I took a bite out of my ramen when it first came out. I kid you not I heard harps and strings playing as I ate (maybe the place had music playing, but still). This place runs off of a no tip base which I found interesting, but makes sense since each bowl of ramen is $24. No lie, it was monies worth tho and I would come back again.

Can't say I was a big fan of this place. For a high end steakhouse, the steak itself fell rather short for me. I had the classic prime rib medium rare- for $65 I expected it to be better. It just tasted like steak cooked medium rare with salt and pepper on top. Also to note- I came with six other people and we all ordered the same steak cooked the same way but some of our meats were either more rare or more medium-well/done- it lacked consistency. Side dishes- had the hash browns which were tasty, the roasted oyster mushrooms which were delicious, the creamed spinach which was also good but not remarkable, and the calamari which was good but average. Dessert- had the coconut cake and chocolate cake. Was also okay but didn't stand out. The staff was very friendly and accommodating and I liked them a lot. But food wise it was so so, the steaks came out on the lukewarm side, and for the price you pay, it could have been better.

Title: An Enchanting Thai Experience Marred Only by a Rice Misstep

Thai Villa isn't just a restaurant; it's a feast for the eyes. The entrance graced by a waterfall cascading over a benevolent Buddha face sets the stage for an exquisite dining experience. Once inside, the real magic unfolds with flavors that whisk you away to the streets of Bangkok.

Our culinary journey was a delight, with the tom yum goong being the highlight. Each spoonful was packed with succulence, featuring six generous shrimp that justified every slurp. The chicken flat broad noodles and basil fried rice carried the authenticity of Thai spices, while the spicy papaya salad added the perfect kick. However, the vegetable mushroom soup and the vegetables with peanut sauce didn't quite hit the same high notes, yet were satisfactory.

Unfortunately, the rice slightly missed the mark, being undercooked and chewy, which slightly marred an otherwise perfect meal. Nonetheless, the swift service on a bustling Wednesday night was commendable, with each dish arriving swiftly and plated with precision.

Sitting in the comfy booth, we found the pricing reasonable for the upscale Manhattan Flatiron area — $100 for an ample and filling meal for three, with drinks included.

Special mention to the creative cocktail - a tamarind old fashioned that impressed my husband. As for the service, it was top-notch. Our attentive waitress ensured our glasses were never empty and the plates cleared promptly.

Would I revisit Thai Villa? Absolutely, but I'd prefer a shorter wait time than the hour we spent on a rainy evening's Yelp waitlist. All in all, Thai Villa promises a beautiful backdrop to delicious food and reliable service.

This is a must for anyone who loves ramen. From the experience down to the food, everything is top notch. The ramen is entirely customizable and you can change the richness of the broth, the hardness of the noodles, salt, spice, and garlic levels. It's been hard for a ramen location to top ramen tatsuya for me but ichiran was undoubtedly the more superior location. The experience is one of a kind in which you are able to eat in booths. The servers open the small slides in the booth to deliver the food and there is a call button to access the waiter whenever you want. This is very unique and should be tried if you're a ramen fan.

Title: A Hearty Brunch with Minor Hiccups

I ventured into this eatery for Saturday brunch, and the French toast was an absolute knockout – both in size and taste. The portions were gargantuan, surely more than a single stomach can handle. The food quality was top-notch, with the thickest syrup I've ever encountered and chicken that was all meat, no unnecessary breading. It's the kind of meal that lulls you into a satisfied slumber.

The service and ambiance didn't lag behind. Despite the rush, a 25-minute wait led us comfortably to the bar area before being seated. The waiter was attentive, ensuring our orders arrived within 20 minutes. The interior was inviting and bright, creating a pleasant dining atmosphere.

However, I encountered a slip-up – a stray hair in my meal. It was promptly addressed by the staff who removed the charge for the inconvenienced dish. My dining companions enjoyed their meal without issue, making this experience an overall win. While I'd recommend this place, I'm deducting a star for the mishap. Four out of five stars.

Title: "A Delightful Post-Passover Carb Indulgence at Pizzeria Sirenetta"

Review:

After a rigorous post-Passover bread fast, my friends and I found sanctuary at Pizzeria Sirenetta on a Sunday. Drawn in by the promise of a rare happy hour that graces the weekend hours, we were eager to dive into the specially priced menu.

We couldn't resist starting with the meatball parm sliders, a delicious though petite treat at $6. Doubling up was a smart move as they were indisputably moreish. Accompanying the sliders, we shared a mini kale salad. Simple, yes, but the parmesan-laden leaves and unique crumbed croutons tossed in an Italian dressing brought a refreshing balance to our table.

The fennel sausage and onion pizza at $12 won unanimous praise - the fennel's character shone through in every bite and the crust had an unexpected crispiness for a Neapolitan-style base. Transitioning to the main courses, the penne arrabbiata delivered a spicy punch that satisfied our cravings for heat, and the cacio e pepe was a creamy dream spun from house-made fettuccine.

Toasting to our carb celebration, I alternated between the pepperoncini martini and the house red wine, both reasonably priced at $8. While they didn't rewrite the cocktail book, they were delightful companions to our feast.

In short, Pizzeria Sirenetta's happy hour provided a fulfilling and affordable toast to tradition. The standout pizza and solid drinks are calling me back for an encore. Solid showing indeed!

Title: A Shrimp Lover's Paradise with Top-Notch Service

From the moment I stepped into this gem, I was absolutely enchanted. It's rare for me to be so overwhelmingly positive in a review, but I just can't hold back the praise for this establishment. They offer mind-blowing happy hour deals, particularly their $1 shrimp cocktail, which easily claims the crown for the best bargain you'll find around.

Beyond the incredible specials, the heart of this place is its service. Exceptional and attentive, they elevate a good dining experience to an unforgettable one. A standout dish is their homemade cavatelli with sausage—a chef-recommended delight that dissolves ecstatically on the tongue.

The beverages are equally impressive, with an espresso martini that's a must-try and a homemade tiramisu that ends the meal on a high note. However, a word of caution on the meatballs—they're a tad pricey at $5 each, and lean more towards bread than meat in composition. But don't let that deter you. Overall, this restaurant is a standout and a must-visit for anyone who appreciates fine food and excellent service.

Title: A Slice of Heaven in Times Square

There's no question that this gem is my go-to spot in the bustling heart of Times Square. The restaurant elevates the classic New York pizza experience, serving up fried pizzas that burst with incredible flavor. The open kitchen ensures each pie is delivered hot and fresh to your table, offering a delectable spectacle for the senses.

Pair your pizza with something from their excellent bar selection, and you're in for a real treat. Admittedly, the seating arrangement is a bit cramped, with tables a tad too close for comfort, making it a bit of a squeeze to navigate the space. Nevertheless, this minor inconvenience isn't enough to deter me. This place is a must-visit for any trip I take to the city, guaranteeing a pizza experience that's truly hard to top.

I recently visited a local pizzeria renowned for its pizza which strikes a perfect balance between a crunchy exterior and a fluffy, chewy interior. However, pizza enthusiasts should note that the slices tend to be heavy on the sauce with a sparing amount of cheese. Among the varieties tested, the pepperoni and white pizzas stood out as favorites.

The pepperoni square was robust in flavor, amply topped with sauce and perfectly curled roni cups, but it could have benefited from more cheese. The white square, on the other hand, was a delightful surprise. Ideal for garlic knot and cheese lovers, it featured crisped mozzarella and thick chunks of ricotta, all enhanced by minced garlic and a unique touch of sweetness from honey – a truly stand-out choice.

The eggplant parm square's intimidating look belied its refreshing taste, with the eggplant and crushed tomatoes offering a zesty twist. Lastly, the vodka square might have been the lightest option but did not compromise on taste with its rich and creamy vodka sauce.

A word to the wise, the store itself is on the smaller side with limited space to dine in, which can be challenging when it's busy. You might consider taking your pizza to go to fully savor these inventive slices in comfort.

Title: A Little Slice of Italian Charm in Chelsea

Last night, a friend introduced me to a delightful Italian spot tucked away in Chelsea, and the experience was nothing short of marvelous—even on a typically quiet Monday, the place was buzzing with energy. Opting for a lighter fare, I chose a salad, which was on the petite side but fresh and flavorful. On the other hand, my friend's pizza was a showstopper, both in appearance and taste, with leftovers to spare. The ambiance alone is worth a return visit; whether you're eyeing a casual dinner date or a cozy catch-up, this eatery hits the spot. Looking forward to another round of authentic Italian cuisine in this charming nook.

Title: A West Village Tapas Treasure

I recently dined in the heart of the West Village, where I discovered a three-level tapas haven that did not disappoint. While the service was satisfactory, the food truly shined, making any minor wait time a worthwhile tradeoff.

The star of the meal was undoubtedly the paella, brimming with a generous assortment of impeccably fresh seafood that far outnumbered the grains of rice. The shrimp, calamari, and clams offered a deeply savory experience that is a must-try for any visitor.

Equally impressive were the melt-in-your-mouth braised short ribs, elegantly perched atop a bed of beet noodles. This dish was a masterclass in flavor and tenderness. Similarly, the braised rabbit paired with a light, creamy foam and fava beans showcased a remarkable balance of texture and taste.

Among the hearty selections, the crispy fingerling potatoes were a reliable choice, though not particularly memorable compared to the other vibrant offerings. The mushroom flatbread, though crisp and delicately infused with truffle, fell into the category of pleasant yet typical.

The chilled roasted eggplant with toasted shallots lacked the punch of its menu companions, coming across as somewhat underwhelming. Dessert was a mixed bag with the key lime dessert being overly dominated by whipped cream despite its decent flavor, while the baklava cheesecake stood out, offering a rich, creamy filling encased in a wonderfully crunchy baklava crust.

While prices may edge towards the higher side, reflecting the neighborhood's standard, the portion sizes and the innovative approach to traditional tapas justifies the cost.

In summary, for an array of creatively executed tapas in the West Village, this restaurant is certainly worth the visit. The inviting space, coupled with a menu that largely impresses, makes for an engaging dining experience.

We came here while waiting to be called for our table at Attaboy. The place was pretty empty when we arrived. Our bartender was super sociable and friendly. She asked us where we were from and what our plans were for the night. We told her about Attaboy, and she told us to be prepared to chug our drinks at any point.We ordered the Everything Nice, Stay Salty and Devon House Punch with tequila. The Everything Nice was so pretty and delicious. The blackberry swirl was a nice touch. I felt bad drinking it. After we finished our first round, we ordered Piña Coladas to top it off. They were good but a little on the bitter side. I understand that the bartender was trying to make her mark by serving us a less sweet version of it but it didn't sit well with me. I wanted it to be sweeter and to make me feel like I was in the Caribbean.The service was amazing, the drinks were good. It's a good place to stop in for a cocktail or two but I wouldn't make a night out of it.

Title: Overhyped and Overpriced

I was underwhelmed by my recent dining experience at a restaurant that’s been receiving a lot of buzz. Despite its reputation, I found the food good yet painfully overpriced, and the portion sizes left something to be desired. My visit wasn't intentional but resulted from an invitation by an acquaintance who swore by the place.

Our meal kicked off with a selection of starters that failed to impress. The ham was unremarkable, especially for its price tag. The most surprising dish was scrambled eggs with snails at a staggering $26. Its novelty couldn’t justify the cost. Meanwhile, the octopus lacked the proper grilling to achieve a pleasant char, a feature disappointingly absent.

Even the side dish of charred carrots, which were inexplicably priced at $15, seemed to carry an expectation of grandeur that they simply couldn’t live up to, unless they came with enchanting tales of their origin.

The main course featured a whole daurade which was undeniably delicious. However, at $76, the bar was set high for excellence.

As if the prices weren’t enough of a drawback, the seating arrangements added to the discontent. Our table, positioned awkwardly in the dense central row, suffered from a chronically wobbly leg which became a nuisance throughout the evening. Multiple attempts by the staff to rectify the situation resulted in an unfortunate spill, adding insult to injury.

Moreover, the traffic of waiters brushing past without apology compounded the less-than-stellar dining experience.

In summary, while certain dishes like the daurade did shine, overall, the restaurant didn’t live up to the widespread acclaim, especially when considering the cost and the less-than-comfortable dining environment.

Title: Aromatic Delights and Juicy Kebabs at West Midtown Gem

I recently dined at a fantastic restaurant in West Midtown, and I must say, their rice alone is worth a visit. It was exceptionally aromatic and savory, so delicious that it could easily stand on its own as a meal. However, that's not to forget the kebabs – the beef kebabs were particularly impressive, being both succulent and juicy. 

Accompanying the meal, the Afghan bread was exactly how I like it: nice and chewy, which complemented the rest of the dishes beautifully. While there's a sister location, Afghan Kebab House II, nearer to my home, I have a preference for the West Midtown spot. I've noticed the sauces at the Upper East Side location tend to be a bit watered down, which is why I choose to make the trip to where I believe the flavors are truly at their best. 

Space is understandably tight, typical for this bustling part of town, but comfortably so and priced reasonably for both the quality and quantity of food you receive. The service deserves a mention as well – courteous without overdoing it, which I appreciate in a dining experience. 

A word on their policy: It's not unreasonable for a restaurant to restrict bathroom use to patrons only, which maintains cleanliness for dining customers. I support this establishment's enforcement of such a policy, even if it means turning away a faux customer here and there. 

All in all, this restaurant is a standout, especially if you're in the mood for some truly delectable kebabs and rice that could steal the show all on its own.

I ordered the Wonton & Fish Ball w. Noodles ($9) and was blown away. Definitely the best wontons I've ever had! The fish balls were good, but nothing special. I want to try the wonton noodle soup with beef tripe or vegetables next time. The customer service was good, and the food arrived so quickly! Instead of water, they served a nice big cup of tea, which was really soothing to drink after the meal.

So good!! I love shanghainese food, and this place does it so well. Food: We basically took half an hour to decide because all the options looked amazing. My friend and I decided to share the soup dumplings, thick noodles, and salt and pepper shrimp. Soup dumplings were so good-- the skin wasn't too thick, which I always appreciate. Salt and pepper shrimp was good and noodles had tons of ingredients as well. Service: The waiter was so kind and patient with our indecisiveness. He also made recommendations and basically helped us decide what to order, which was super helpful.Atmosphere: Pretty big and comfortable sized. For some reason, it got a c on it's cleanliness rating, which scared me at first, but it was honestly fine and clean. Definitely will be coming back here to try some other dishes!

Quite disappointed with this meal after coming across so many recommendations by online platforms for Barn Joo. What I think we need is more Asian food writers commenting on Asian food, not white writers who claim an affinity for Asian food, but will not/have not been to Asian restaurants that might have less comfortable seating or do not have Western ideals of "service".Barn Joo serves Korean tapas featuring traditional Korean dishes with a twist. I appreciate restaurants that attempt to modernize traditional cuisine, but a lot of these "twists" were unnecessary (truffle essence) and/or not well-executed (not-crispy fried chicken). My favorite dish amongst what we ordered was the crunchy tofu, but mostly for the caramelized kim chi on the dish. The breading on the tofu itself was too thick; I craved for the lightness of Japanese agedashi tofu as I struggled to rip apart the tofu skin with my teeth.1. Fried Tiger Roll (tuna, salmon, avocado, kani, chili mayo, eel sauce)2. Crunchy Tofu (fried tofu served with caramelized Kimchi)3. Crispy Chicken Bun4. Galbi-Jjim (braised short ribs, carrots, dates, chestnuts, truffle essence with glass noodles)

Regrettably, my recent visit to the hotpot restaurant in question was disappointing. It's hard to justify their pricing, particularly the $2.99 per person charge for standard condiments. This fee is applied indiscriminately, regardless of usage, which feels quite underhanded.

The restaurant's novelty cans of oils, initially eye-catching, turned out to be unremarkable and didn't enhance the dining experience. Choices for soup bases were limited to just three, with the mushroom variety lacking in flavor and the "mild" spicy option proving excessively hot.

Portion sizes were unsatisfactory, offering a meager selection that did nothing to stand out from the crowd. Claims of "specials" were overstated and you'd be better off visiting hometown hotpot for a similar experience at a fraction of the cost.

Service may also present a barrier for non-Chinese speakers, as most of the staff communicate primarily in Chinese, potentially complicating the ordering process.

In conclusion, this establishment is overshadowed by numerous superior hotpot options available in the city. It's not a destination I can recommend, and diners would be well-advised to seek out alternatives for a more satisfying and value-conscious meal.

This straight outta Japan ramen joint is the real deal! My burnt miso garlic ramen was the best bowl I've had in NYC and I can't wait to go back to try more. The skewers were delicious as well, with the beef being our favorite followed by the bacon wrapped quail eggs - yum! Service was good. The restaurant is wheelchair accessible but gets busy at prime time so can be a bit tight.

Title: A Mixed Dining Experience at the Food Court

Food (2/5): My plate of chicken and rabbit paella was simply passable, not quite living up to my expectations, especially given its $18 price tag and the less-than-generous portion size. Fortunately, the dessert was a redeeming feature. The churros, far from being overly sweet, struck a perfect balance of mild sweetness and satisfying crunch. The dark chocolate dip complemented them with a delightfully subtle bitterness.

Venue (5/5): The venue impresses with its exceptional design, offering a diverse array of choices in the food court setting. It's a pleasant spot that's been maintained with cleanliness and care.

Service (4/5): Service was commendable; having waitstaff on hand to assist with clearing tables is a thoughtful touch, not commonly found in food court environments. The downside was the congested water station and the pricey drinks, which detracted slightly from the overall positive service experience.

In summary, while the main course didn't hit the mark, the fantastic venue and quality service, along with truly delightful churros, made the visit worthwhile.

Title: "Cozy Rosh Hashanah Dinner at UWS Gem"

Last evening, my friends and I were treated to a delightful Rosh Hashanah dinner. The evening commenced with a thoughtful gesture of complimentary apples and honey, which were notably fresh and crisp. Our appetites whetted, we each savored a bowl of house-made matzoh ball soup. The matzoh balls had a pleasing texture, though a touch more seasoning would have perfected the recipe.

For our main course, we indulged in an assortment of shared dishes. The Korean wings were an outright hit, bursting with flavor. The mac and cheese followed suit, delivering rich and satisfying taste. Our experience with the sweet potato fries was equally enjoyable; they were freshly cut and cooked to perfection. The yucca fries stood out with their chunky cut, and while a tad on the dry side, they paired excellently with the accompanying garlic and avocado aiolis.

Service throughout the meal was attentive, contributing to the overall pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. Furthermore, the prices were found to be quite reasonable, especially for the Upper West Side location. This spot comes recommended for those seeking a festive meal in a cozy setting.

I recently visited a restaurant known for its Roman style pizza al taglio. Unlike its Sicilian cousin, this pizza features a rectangular slice with a moderately thin profile. The dough, enriched with olive oil, offers a notable flavor kick and a pleasantly crisp texture. The slices are of fair size; however, at around $6 a pop, they feel a bit overpriced. While the pizza's uniqueness is commendable, my personal taste leans more towards the classic NYC pizza experience. In summary, the pizza here is just okay and might not impress those devoted to traditional New York slices.

During my recent visit to the restaurant, I opted to indulge in their beverage offerings, and I was thoroughly impressed. The Amalfi Gold cocktail was a delightful discovery—its refreshing taste capturing the essence of summer in a glass—while the John Daly proved to be a pleasant and satisfying choice. Although I did not partake in the food, the dishes served around me looked exceptional, tempting me to return for a taste. The ambiance and service were impeccable, contributing to a flawless dining experience. Overall, no complaints—the venue certainly lived up to its reputation.

Came here on a holiday where they had a prix fixe menu in the dining room only, or you can choose to sit at their tavern area and have their tavern menu. We chose to sit in their dining room. The prix fixe menu was $85 for an appetizer, entree, and dessert. Their prix fixe menu had soo many options, and good ones too. My boyfriend started with the lobster risotto and I got east coast oysters and cocktail shrimp, the portions for these starters were so much bigger than we expected! Oysters and shrimp tasted fresh and the lobster risotto had a super strong lobster flavor, the risotto was on the saltier side for me though. For our entrees my boyfriend got the NY strip and tiger prawn which came with truffled Mac n cheese and a spinach salad, his plate was huge! Definitely did not expect the portion of this to be so big, the steak was cooked just right, the glaze or sauce that was on the steak paired very well with it, the Mac n cheese had a very rich and string truffle flavor. I got the scallops which was on top of a mashed potato, scallops tasted fresh. For dessert I got a dark chocolate mousse and my boyfriend got a green tea mascarpone mousse I believe? Both were excellent. Oh you also get some fresh bread with some garlic, butter and olive oil in the beginning which will definitely fill you up if you eat the whole basket.Our server Michael was super attentive and was overall just a pleasant person! This definitely won't be our last time at black barn.

Title: A Spicy Delight at Maison Bangkok

After my go-to spot Up Thai was temporarily out of commission, I found solace in Maison Bangkok via Seamless. Opting for a vegetarian-friendly choice, I ordered their spicy basil fried rice with tofu. True to its name, it packed a punch that delighted my taste buds. The dish was not just spicy, but also rich in flavor, satisfying my craving for something that would make my palate sing. The serving didn't skimp on tofu—a pleasant surprise—though I did find myself wishing that the tofu itself had a bit more seasoning to round out the dish. Overall, Maison Bangkok has certainly made a fan out of me, and I'm looking forward to my next foray into their menu.

Title: Satisfying Dim Sum Dinner with a Few Shortcomings

Last night, we ventured to this spot with a hankering for dim sum, though the dinner menu offered a limited selection. Our appetite was somewhat satiated with dishes like the Glutinous Rice in Lotus Leaf, succulent Skewered Beef, sweet Piglet Bun, classic Steamed BBQ Pork Bun, adventurous Steamed Chicken Feet, and the Steamed Bean Curd Skin Rolls. We couldn't resist adding a Half Roast Duck to the mix, which proved to be a highlight. With its perfect balance of meatiness, fattiness, and crisp skin, the duck was a standout.

Service was lackluster, an aspect I've come to expect at many Chinese dining establishments. Prices were a tad steep for dim sum, but the quality and flavor of the food justified the cost. Despite the service and price, dishes like the glutinous rice, steamed buns, and the unforgettable roast duck made our dinner a pleasurable experience.

I recently visited this restaurant for a date night and was pleasantly reminded of what excellent customer service looks like. Though I can't recall the full name of our waitress, it began with "Vic," she was incredibly helpful in assisting with our menu choices. While the cleanliness wasn't impeccable, particularly in the bathroom, the overall dining experience far outshone these minor issues. A great spot for a special evening out.

My recent dining experience at this restaurant was quite satisfying. The staff were exceptionally friendly, contributing to the warm atmosphere of the meal. As for the food, it was tasty, especially the pierogis which, despite my wish for a larger portion or a smaller price tag, were still enjoyable. I left without any significant complaints and would consider returning.

I absolutely adore the pizza offerings at this bustling eatery. From the classic cheese pizza to the richly topped tomato and mozzarella, and the savory mushroom variety to the exquisite white pizza, each one has been a delightful experience for my taste buds. Despite the crowd, which speaks volumes about the place, the wait is a small price to pay for such heavenly pizza perfection. Highly recommend!

Title: A Yaadman's Take on Miss Lily's Brunch Experience

Review:

As a Jamaican, it's always a bit of a gamble trying a Caribbean spot in the city, but Miss Lily's has been on my radar since a positive experience at their East Village location. This time, my friends and I ventured to a different Miss Lily's for brunch, and while it wasn't the same spot as before, it had its own merits.

The reservation process was smooth and even with a bustling crowd, our service was efficient; we were seated and served promptly. The brunch menu, however, was slightly less varied than what I remember from the East Village venue - notably missing were favorites such as peppered shrimp and stamp and go.

Opting for the Jamaican Breakfast, I found comfort in its familiar taste, though the ackee component was wetter than I prefer, likely canned, which, let's be honest, isn't quite the same as fresh. The ratio skewed more towards ackee than saltfish, and it was overpowered by black pepper, a bit too eager to compensate for the scotch bonnet's punch, I'd guess. The steamed veggies were a pleasant surprise, adding variety to the dish, and the inclusion of sweet plantains and a side of fruits was a delightful bonus.

My friends had mixed reviews on their choices. The oxtail was flavorful but could've been more tender, according to one, while the rice and peas met with approval. The Jerk chicken was deemed okay, albeit dressed in a sweet BBQ sauce that didn't quite hit the mark for authenticity. A Bloody Mary order fell flat - it leaned too much on hot pepper sauce and lacked the rich tomato base one would expect.

Wrapping up, the experience was solid with generous portions and commendable service, highlighted by a particularly attentive hostess who doubled as our photographer, aiming for that perfect group shot. Overall, a good spot for a taste of Jamaica when you're miles from yaad.

Having been lead here and seeing it was next to penn station, I had really low expectation. Came in, and there was no one here, so another not great sign.Ordered a chicken pho and a cooked beef one. The chicken pho had a surprisingly strong flavor, not necessarily rich, but very savory/salty. The beef was pretty standard.Overall, it was a place that scratched an itch. Came with low expectations, and it beat it. Just have that mindset and you'll be content here

Limani dazzles with its ultra-modern aesthetics, boasting an impressive indoor foliage ambiance and a stunning centerpiece: a vast infinity pool-like fountain. This spot is a true jewel with spreads that are absolutely divine, particularly the tzatziki. Their pita bread, with its perfect char, serves as an ideal complement for dipping. For the gluten-sensitive like my sister, the accommodating staff readily provides cucumber alternatives.

The authenticity of their Greek salad cannot be overstated—it's as if it's been plucked straight from Greece. The octopus starter is a standout, surprisingly reminiscent of chicken in its texture and taste, and should not be missed. For the main course, the salmon was delightful, adorned with capers and a zesty lemon wedge.

Our meal concluded with a vibrant fruit platter and a decadent honey cake accompanied by vanilla ice cream—a fitting end to a truly remarkable dining experience at Limani.

Located in the middle of k-town. I came for a friend's birthday and we did the regular order, no kbbq. The food was pretty good, but it was also quite pricey. Here were the foods I tried:- japche - pretty good but nothing amazing about it. I feel like I could've made this at home. In fact, I did make it at home and it was a lot cheaper.- Korean seafood pancake - this was pretty good. You get bits of squid and other seafoods in it.- budae jjigae: consists of half (I believe) of an instant noodle packet, hot dog slices, spam, a few pieces of rice cake. It was spicy, but not dreadfully so. They also serve it with a fire burning under so I would suggest you put out the fire right away or eat the noodle ASAP or else the noodles will overcook. This also comes with a bowl of white rice - My friends also got the house-made fruit sake that I took a sip of. It was really good.What impressed me the most was the banchan. There were so many of them! I loved it! They also refill it for you. I especially loved the sweet fried fish. It was so good. Downside: for some of my friend's orders they asked to take out one ingredient or replace that ingredient for something else, which I understand can be annoying, but the waitress did not keep a poker face whatsoever. Also the place was pricey and I feel like I could've made some of these at home like the japche and budae jjigae; therefore, give this place 3 stars - would come here for special occasions or if someone wanted to eat here, but would not suggest this place myself.

This is a regular ol' diner in the Sutton Place hood. I needed to meet a friend for breakfast who lives on 76 & 1. He came down to the area. It was a decent place to get together. I had poached eggs with tomato and lettuce and coffee. He had an egg white omelette with hash browns and tomatoes.We had a nice corner booth so it was great to just sit and chat. I mean a diner is a diner right? As long as the coffee is good, I'm  ok with a diner!

It's CUBAN!!! Meaning I'm already happy. I've been many times over the years, especially in the summer when I'm free to roam and wander the city and stumble in here for lunch and partake in HH from 11am-7pm...oh that caipirinha!! I LOVE IT!!I've had the steak sandwich, the beef and chicken empanadas, the ropa vieja, the steak and eggs, the yuca fries, maduros, and double all that...LOL! I've never been disappointed coming here. I'm sure i'll actually be back a few times before the new year.

During my recent visits to this restaurant, the service left much to be desired. Initially, the lack of a hostess to greet and guide guests upon entry was confusing, and the unclear seating policy only added to the disorientation. While guests had the choice of ordering at the counter or being served at the table, clearer communication from the staff would have been appreciated.

On a positive note, the lunch special, priced at $12, offers a protein with two sides and is both satisfying and well-portioned. However, upon my return, the service had not improved, and the food, while reasonably priced, failed to make a lasting impression. I retain hope that future visits will show improvements in service and culinary offerings.

I was leaving the Javits Center and walking down to a noodle shop when I passed this little food hall. Since I had never been I decided to give it a try. I chose the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen (Soy Sauce). Service was fast and polite. I took a seat at the communal table and dug in. The Dashi-Chicken Broth was rich with a great depth of flavor, the pork belly fatty and tender, noodles were perfectly al dente with that great chewiness and the egg was cooked 100%. Not my absolute fav bowl I've had but I was very impressed especially after watching the story on Ivan on Chef's Table. I will try other locations as they seem to have better ratings.

I recently stopped by Pizza Italia in Chelsea for a Thursday afternoon lunch and came away with mixed feelings. Their Buffalo Chicken Pizza Slice fared better with its large slices and generous chunks of spicy chicken, offering decent flavor for $4.50. However, the traditional Cheese Pizza Slice, priced at $3.25, was a letdown—bland and burdened with a tough crust.

Despite the large portions, the overall quality didn't compel me to plan a return visit, especially with stronger contenders nearby. The ambiance was bright, thanks to big windows, and the layout was spacious enough, yet the shop missed an opportunity to showcase their pizzas effectively. While service was quick and the staff friendly, the atmosphere was marred by a noisy crowd of nearby students during lunchtime.

If you're looking to grab a quick bite, be aware that parking is a challenge in this area. In a city brimming with pizza options, Pizza Italia doesn't quite rise to the occasion.

We stopped in a bit later in the evening without reservations and they were able to get us in with about. 30 minute wait. It was a busy night but yet they were able to get us seated right away and bring drinks and food in a quick manner. I ordered the lasagna and my gf ordered the pasta fagioli. The food was very good. Plenty of flavor. The staff did a wonderful job of taking care of us despite the fact we were a large group with many requests. They did an expert job of handling our requests for drinks and additional bread. Good job! We will definitely be back.

My first time here I work around the corner from them but never took the time to stop, what a mistake this place seems super cool and the food at least what we ordered was absolutely yummy  definitely coming back here again for some drinks and more yummy food. I got the grilled salmon with warm quinoa

I recently visited a no-frills eatery that delivered an honest and heartwarming dining experience. I tried the #6 spice beef noodle soup, which arrived adorned with a generous dollop of spicy red peppers and oil. The heat had me sweating profusely, but it only enhanced the authenticity of the meal. This place isn't about catering to the finicky tastes of faux foodies; it's all about simple, straightforward, and affordable fare. I left satisfied and eager to explore more of their menu on my next visit. Highly recommended for those who appreciate unpretentious, good food.

Title: A Satisfactory Shanghainese Dining Experience at 456

My visit to 456 for an early dinner revealed a bustling scene uncommon for the hour, which was surprisingly filled with a predominantly non-Asian crowd. This initially raised questions about the authenticity of the Shanghainese fare on offer.

The menu didn’t present any surprises, bearing familiar options akin to its Chinatown competitors. Our meal commenced with the Cold Dish Three Combo, where the flavors of Shanghai Kao Fu, Jelly Fish, and Vegetarian Mock Duck were satisfying, though the portion sizes proved underwhelming, questioning the value of the combo compared to individual orders.

The Crab Meat & Pork Soup Dumplings stood out with their excellent execution, a highlight with their robust and hot broth encased in resilient skins. Equally pleasing were the Fried Tiny Buns with Pork—misleading in name but generous in size and taste, packed with juicy pork and chives.

Regrettably, the Shanghai Noodle with Shrimp fell into the realm of mediocrity, not only in flavor but also in portion, leaving us desiring more.

Service was notably efficient, with swift waiters and a comfortable seating arrangement that accommodated us well before the dinner rush.

While 456 doesn't boast a revolutionary take on Shanghainese cuisine, it does serve up decent dishes that can satisfy cravings without too much fanfare. It's a reasonable choice when in the area and in need of a comforting meal, but manage expectations when it comes to portion sizes.

Title: A Culinary Haven at Pig Heaven

Pig Heaven on the Upper East Side is a gem of a Chinese-American eatery where the food delights and service shines. During a recent lunch with a friend, the experience was notably more polished than your run-of-the-mill Chinese spot, yet retained a comfortable and casual ambience.

The stars of the menu were undoubtedly the succulent BBQ Chinese ribs, which boasted a sweet glaze that complemented the tender pork perfectly. Equally impressive was the tomato and tofu soup with thinly sliced beef stew - a harmonious blend of sweet, sour, and savory that embodied comfort, especially suitable for chilly days. These dishes absolutely demand a repeat order.

Also sampled were the thinly sliced pork with garlic soy dressing, which, despite being a tad on the dry side, was elevated by a savory hoisin sauce. The fried brussel sprouts in a Szechuan black bean sauce offered a punch of flavor, though they erred on the greasy side. Still, their rich taste profile made them a highlight.

Pig Heaven's attentive service added a final touch of satisfaction to our meal. This is a place I'd eagerly recommend, particularly for those BBQ ribs and the heartwarming soup that tastes like home.

Title: A Delightful Evening at a Bustling Hotspot

My partner and I ventured into this restaurant for a date night on a Saturday and it didn't disappoint. Heed my advice - make a reservation! It's a popular spot and even late into the evening, you could find yourself waiting. Fortunately, we were whisked to our seats immediately upon arrival.

Nestled on the energetic first floor near the bar, we began with the edamame. While it was rather standard fare, the presentation gave it a special touch. The main course, Salmon Saikyo Yaki, was a standout. The salmon, marinated to perfection, was paired with traditional accompaniments like miso soup, white rice, house-made pickles, grated radish, and seaweed, each element fresh and flavorful.

Dessert was a sampler whose name escapes me, featuring matcha ice cream, a zesty lemon-flavored cheesecake, and a gelatinous mystery that didn't quite leave the same impression. The ice cream and cheesecake? Divine. The wait for dessert was longer than anticipated, but that was a minor hiccup in an otherwise seamless experience.

Service throughout the evening was nothing short of friendly. If you're looking for a spot that delivers on taste and vibe, this is it—but don't forget to book ahead!

Title: Cozy Pub Vibes with Room for Service Improvement

After an inspiring visit to the MoMA, my companions and I stumbled upon the Bean, drawn by its bustling reputation. The pub welcomed us with its delightful fall decor and an inviting atmosphere, offering a perfect place to unwind. We chose to sit at the bar, where we were promptly handed drink menus and ordered beers to kick back with.

Regrettably, we had to chase down the bartender for food menus, as he was preoccupied with tasks other than attending to our needs. The ambiance was conducive to enjoying the ongoing college football game, setting the stage for a craving for classic pub food. I opted for wings with a side of Brussels sprouts. 

The sprouts, though served lukewarm, were a savory delight with a flawless glaze— a hot serving would have made them impeccable. The wings, while not extraordinary enough to warrant a detour, were satisfactorily flavorful. 

Overall, the Bean holds potential with its appealing setting and commendable fare, meriting a 4.1-star rating for the food and a solid 4.3 for ambiance. However, the service lagged behind at 3.1 stars, leaving room for improvement. A touch more warmth from both the Brussels and the bartender could have lifted this experience into the higher echelons of the four-star realm.

Very small place where if you don't have a seat you are in no mans land. We sat in the back where there was a small corridor and some seating. I like the vibe but if you are claudtrophobic this isnt for you. The wine was fabulous. If you have any questions ask the server since they are all very knowledgable. They even decant it in front of you. Pretty cool. We also ordered some food. The meat and cheese plate was solid. The bread that comes with it is awesome. Its simple toasted bread but it was addictive. The cheeses all had unique flavor. The salami's were also good. I wish they explained what was what but who cares it was all good.I would definitely come back with my wife for a date night. It is that kind of place. Not the best for groups but we still had a solid time.

The hype is real about La Grenouille. It has such a traditional French feel, and you really feel like you've escaped to 1950's Paris.I came here on a second date (major points for him), and was astounded at how formal and elegant everything was. From the flowers to the tables to the wallpaper, the ambiance can't be beat. Upon opening the doors to the restaurant, I walked into a coat check, which was separate from the restaurant itself. When I pulled back the curtain and walked into the restaurant, I was immediately greeted by the Captain, who was so polite and showed me to my table, which he graciously pulled out from the booth so that I could get in.I can't say enough good things about the service here. Honestly, I was a little wary of how they would treat two 25-year olds, but we were treated like movie stars. My only ding is that they weren't as forthcoming with the water refills, but that's about it.The Captain and waiter rotated coming over to our table, and you could see the Captain constantly wandering around the restaurant, making sure everything was perfection. We had no choice but to get the pre-fixe due to the timing of our dinner (7:30 on a Tuesday), but I'm so glad we did. We started with a palette cleanser of a tangy amuse bouche. For my appetizer, I ordered the Saffron Lobster Bisque with grilled scallops and shrimp. My date ordered the smoked salmon blini with caviar, which also came with generous helpings of lobster (not denoted on the menu). Both were excellent.For our mains, my date encouraged me to get the dover sole, as it's the best anywhere. I had never tried it, but, when in Rome, right? I am SO glad I took his advice. There were 2 options for how it would be prepared, and we both opted to go with the version with the mushroom sauce. Honestly, my date spoke French and was able to converse with the wait staff, so I couldn't tell you what the mushroom version was called. The dover sole arrived, and it looked like a mini burrito. I can't even describe what it tasted like, but think incredibly savory and mild. The outer portion tasted like it was wrapped in an egg mixture. I gobbled up every bite.After our main, we were given the choice of salad or cheese plate. I opted for the cheese plate, and my date got the salad. The salad did look pretty sad when it arrived, as there were no garnishes, and it resembled a pile of weeds. My cheese plate came with 4 cheeses, bread crackers, and some fruit and nuts. I would definitely recommend that over the salad.For dessert, he ordered the Affogato Grenouille, which was espresso with amaretto and ice cream, and I chose the chocolate souffle. Both were outstanding. I'm not a huge chocolate person, but I knew I couldn't pass up the chance for a first-class souflee.All in all, this was one of the best meals I've ever had. Every part of it was memorable. As other reviews have stated, you need to mentally be prepared to spend ~$500 for 2 people, including tip, as they have a waiter's tip and a captain's tip. I hope to be back to this amazing establishment soon. Oh, and he did get a 3rd date.

My friend and I visited this gem for a weekday lunch and were pleasantly surprised to find no wait for seating. Our shared spread included shrimp dumplings, shredded roast duck dumplings, Shanghai juicy pork buns, pan-fried tiny buns, Szechuan spicy cucumbers, and scallion pancakes. Each dish was delightful, especially the shrimp dumplings, which were the highlight. While the cucumbers proved too fiery for my palate, they're a winner for those with a penchant for heat. Overall, the meal was hearty and gratifying—an experience worth repeating.

Title: A Crunchy Connoisseur's Delight

If thin, crunchy crust pizza is your penchant, this spot might just top your list. The pizzas boast arguably the thinnest crusts in the city, teetering on too delicate for my taste but still maintaining a pleasant crunch. Of the trio sampled, the standout was the Salsiccia Dolce, which hits new heights of flavor with a switch to hot sausages—a must-try tweak! The Meat Lovers, however, was a slight misfire, tipping the scales toward salty and greasy, while the Classica played it too safe to impress, though it wasn't without its merits.

Landing a table within five minutes at 6PM for our group of six was a stroke of luck, with a line forming shortly after. It's a cozy haven nestled blocks away from the typical tourist trails, making it a prime pick for locals. In a nutshell, if you find yourself meandering through midtown, this pizzeria is a credible candidate for a satisfying slice.

Title: Cozy Vibes and Generous Portions at a Neighborhood Gem

My friends and I decided to try out this spot on a whim on a weekday night, and I'm thrilled we did. Booking online last minute was a breeze, and upon arrival, we were instantly won over by the inviting atmosphere and our upbeat waiter.

Kicking off with drinks that arrived swiftly and packed a punch, we definitely felt we were getting good value. A small hiccup with our starter, the deviled eggs coming out with bacon despite requesting it on the side, was handled gracefully by the staff with a complimentary round of drinks, a gesture we all appreciated.

The main courses did not disappoint. The four cheese mac and cheese was rich and creamy, just as tempting as it sounds. The chicken pot pie was hearty with a great filling-to-crust ratio, although the crust was a tad on the tougher side. It was a pleasant surprise to enjoy it without the usual salt overload.

In summary, between the warm ambiance, attentive service, and delicious comfort food, this restaurant is a place I'd happily recommend and return to.

Yin Ji Chang Fen offers an authentic taste of Guangzhou with its wallet-friendly Chinese brunch options. The rice roll joint’s signature congee and pork liver congee do not disappoint, both delivering on flavor and freshness. Their rice rolls and curry fish balls were standout dishes, paired perfectly with the comforting sweetness of honey lemon tea and the robustness of classic Hong Kong-style milk tea.

Unlike many dim sum places that resort to frozen offerings, Yin Ji Chang Fen serves up dishes that taste unmistakably fresh. It's an excellent spot for anyone craving congee and rice rolls.

On the downside, the restaurant operates on a cash-only basis which can be inconvenient. Additionally, the rice rolls, while delightful, are a bit challenging to share amongst a group - a knife may be necessary for dividing them up. Despite these minor quibbles, Yin Ji Chang Fen is definitely worth a visit for a genuine and tasty brunch experience.

Title: Satisfying Late-Night Bites with a Garlic Twist

Last night's craving led us to this spot for some late-night snacking, and it didn't disappoint. We went for the regular tonkotsu ramen paired with a spicy tuna taco. The taco stole the show for me - its shell was the epitome of crunchiness, and the spicy tuna was mouthwateringly good.

The ramen did its job well, providing comfort in a bowl. However, a heads-up for those less enthusiastic about garlic - the broth was quite heavy on it. For noodle lovers, there's an option to get a noodle refill for a couple of bucks, which is reasonable.

While the location is convenient, it's not a place I'd travel distances for. The menu does have some tantalizing options like bone marrow ramen, but the prices are on the steeper side. Whether I'll return to indulge is a decision for another day. For now, if you're nearby and in need of a tasty late-night stop, this place is worth a go.

Came here on a Wednesday night with a group of 4. Make sure to make a reservation since the restaurant is not huge. The food was great!! We ordered steamed pork buns (not sure they are always on the menu but we got another order at the end since they were so good), tasting of country ham (highly recommend), max's curry potatoes (YUM! I think this was my favorite), and a spicy sausage dish that was a special (too spicy but still good). They tried to convince us that we ordered too many appetizers but I thought it was the perfect amount. Staff was friendly from start to finish and the ambiance inside was fun yet relaxing. All of the cocktails were delicious as well. I would definitely come back!

This was my third visit to this delightful little gem of a restaurant, conveniently located near the subway and Penn Station. Each time I've been here, the service has been impeccable. I have a go-to order: a steak and lobster cooked to a perfect medium rare, complemented by California rolls and a fresh salad. The chef not only prepares a delicious meal but also provides a fun show while cooking. If you prefer a quieter dining experience, I recommend coming early during the week. It gets louder later at night, but regardless of the time, the food consistently hits the mark. I highly recommend visiting for a satisfying culinary experience.

I recently dined at an incredible restaurant where the planning paid off with just a 15-minute wait. The menu, deceptively simple, showcased a mastery of sushi with a six-roll set that escalated in flavor intensity and left me thoroughly impressed. Priced at $29, the value was as delightful as the food. Even their yellowtail, often not a favorite of mine or my fiancé, was transformed into a subtle delight with the addition of scallions. The establishment's dedication to perfecting their craft with high-quality ingredients is evident. This place has won my heart, and I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit to New York to experience it all over again.

We walked in on a Friday night and the wait was about 30 mins for 2. I ordered the $29 burger with roquefort cheese and shoestring fries. The cheese was seriously overpowering and I'm not sure if I ever want another burger with blue cheese in it. I gave it a try but it wasn't for me.Half way through the burger I scraped off the blue cheese and used some ketchup instead. This balanced out the burger more and made it more pleasurable although the patty itself wasn't all that flavorful. The burger felt like the vessel for delivering the blue cheese although the texture of the patty was excellent.There was a lot of shoestring fries. They were quite difficult to eat but were pretty delicious albeit a bit salty. I resorted to using a fork to finish the rest of the fries.Overall, wasn't a huge fan of this burger. I wanted to try it and give it a shot, but I personally don't like blue cheese and this experience only confirmed that even more.
Great place for dim sum! They have adorable custard "pig" buns! It can get super crowded on weekends so be prepare to wait a bit, especially around lunch time.

Title: A Powerhouse Dining Experience at Porter House

I recently dined at Porter House, and although the tab may be hefty, the culinary experience justifies every penny. The atmosphere exudes a quintessential New York City power vibe, with a clientele that leans toward the mature and affluent; think classic steakhouse with an extra dash of exclusivity. The adjoining table's frequenters basked in a flurry of greetings and attention, which, while slightly excessive to an observer, didn’t detract from the warm service we received.

The culinary journey commenced with savory cheddar biscuits and a bread selection - a delectable yet strategic stomach space occupier. The crab cake was a delightful surprise, generously packed with succulent crab, rekindling my affection for the dish. For those craving greens at a steakhouse, their chopped salad is a vibrant medley of veggies that surpasses the usual steakhouse fare.

Side dishes are my steakhouse highlight, with the sautéed mushrooms and broccoli starring; however, the creamed spinach may be too decadent for some. The meal's crescendo was an apple crostata so memorable that it lingered on my mind long after the meal, provoking dreams of expanding waistlines.

For an optimal experience, secure a table by the window with views over Columbus Circle, particularly the cozy two-person booths that promise both privacy and ambience. In essence, Porter House is a dining must for those seeking exceptional food in a setting that's unabashedly New York.

Title: A Mixed Experience at B&E

My dining companion and I ventured into B&E for Restaurant Week, and while the food met our expectations, the service and a unique bathroom surprise were the most memorable aspects of the night.

Firstly, ladies, you're in for a delightful shock in the bathroom – a rarity indeed, and one I'm loath to spoil, so you'll simply have to discover it for yourselves.

On to the cuisine, we indulged in an array of dishes including empanadas, tuna tacos, BBQ short ribs, and Peruvian chicken. We capped off the meal with 'cookies and milk' as well as LES donuts, complemented by 'Pink Panther' and 'ODB' beverages. Alas, despite their quality, these dishes have not left a lasting craving.

The evening's letdowns stemmed from lapses in service. We faced a disappointing oversight by the hostess who neglected us in seating, and a forgotten extra sauce request by our server only acknowledged at dessert time.

The ambiance won points with its speakeasy charm, which would make for the perfect backdrop for a future girls' night out. However, given the culinary cornucopia that NYC has to offer, a return visit to B&E isn't high on my list, save for the company of friends and bathroom curiosities.

Hubby and I found this place when we went to look at the Lexus dealer across the street. We got there right before lunchtime, it was quiet at the time. We were served by a good waiter, Jeffrey. We ordered a slice of pizza for each and also a bowl of lentil soup. The soup was delicious. The pizza was average. We couldn't believe that they make good lentil soup. The lentil soup came with garlic bread, not bad. After sitting there for a few minutes, people started coming in and most of them were tourists. Jeff told us that this pizza place is new. On a cold day like this, the lentil soup warmed us up. I told Hubby, good choice for ordering the soup!

During my New York City adventures, I had the pleasure of dining at a local Poké shop that truly left a lasting impression. Despite not being able to sample other Poké venues in the city, this gem stood out for its remarkable staff, who were the epitome of friendliness. Not only was the service top-notch, but the generous portion sizes also provided excellent value, with prices starting at a reasonable $11.50—a cost that could vary with your choice of fish and any additional proteins.

Admittedly, the shop could have benefited from a cooler environment as the air conditioning wasn't operational, which made for a warmer than ideal dining space. Yet, the serene and hushed atmosphere more than made up for it, offering a perfect retreat to decompress after a busy day of exploring the city. For those looking for a welcoming place to enjoy a delicious and sizable meal without breaking the bank, this spot is definitely worthy of a recommendation.

This was such a fun place to go to! As soon as you fo in- you get a card (think credit card). You take it with you to the count fee- so if you want shrimp in a salad you go to one counter; another counter is for pasta, and another counter is for wine. We had nice casual luncheon sitting at a high top with chargers built into the tables!  We sat and chatted and really enjoyed the food as ell. I'd you check on yep you get a hit chocolate so my teen really enjoyed that .they have big wide windows so you can see everyone outside! I would definitely go back!

Add this Steak place to your list, so impressed with Empire Steak House.  We decided to order the Filet Mignon and the Pappardelle Pasta and share them, also ordered a couple of side dishes.  Our waiter took the time to have the items split in 1/2 and served to us. We were blown away by the size of the portions after being split.  Pic of steak on my plate is my half! Everything was delicious.  I can't say enough about the "Wait" staff and Manager Deca Nikocevic- all were so attentive and knowledgeable of food and wine.  This is an old school style steak place. Big tall booths, crystal chandelier- just a beautiful place.  Nice bar to sit and have a cocktail before dinner too.  We're from L.A. so this may be one of my new places to stop for a cocktail when in town. Potato chips in basket at bar... not pretzels Several birthday celebrations were happening that night and the staff treated each table with sincere enthusiasm.

I recently dined at a local gem where the experience was a delightful surprise. Sitting at the bar, our attentive waiter suggested the braised beef curry from the chef's special menu—a recommendation so persuasive it swept through the bar crowd with enthusiasm. True to his word, the dish was exceptional: the beef was impeccably tender, boasting a melt-in-your-mouth texture and generous portions. Complementing the main course, the crispy catfish salad was a revelation, akin to a flavor-packed crispy slaw. Both the service and food quality left a lasting impression, ensuring my swift return to this culinary haven.

Title: A Delightful Evening at [Restaurant Name]

My friends and I chose [Restaurant Name] for our girls' night out and the experience lived up to our expectations. We shared various dishes, including a kale Caesar salad, a single cheeseburger with bacon, a side of fries, and a prime rib sandwich.

The cheeseburger was satisfying, though not the best I've had. The fries were decent, yet nothing to write home about. However, the prime rib sandwich took center stage; the meat was exceptionally fresh and succulent, complemented perfectly by a side of spicy au jus that gave it a delightful kick.

The ambiance of the restaurant added to our enjoyment, creating a cozy and welcoming environment for our gathering. While not every dish was a standout, the prime rib sandwich was a hit, and I could see myself returning purely to satisfy future cravings for it. Overall, [Restaurant Name] is worth a visit, especially for the prime rib connoisseurs among us.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise Beyond the Stars

I must admit, the three-star rating had me skeptical, but after my recent dining experience, I'm puzzled by the modest score. My initial takeout experience was pleasant, but dining in took it to the next level. The restaurant offers reasonable portions that left both my husband and me full and content.

Service was commendable—our waiter was both amiable and efficient, ensuring a smooth weeknight dinner. I indulged in the spicy seafood champon noodles and was not disappointed. The dish lived up to its name with a generous kick and perfectly cooked noodles, brimming with shrimp, mussels, squid, and a variety of veggies.
