My husband's tonkatsu ramen had a point of contention; he found the pork slices too fatty, though I gladly helped him out and found them to be quite succulent. He, however, had no complaints about the flavorful broth and noodles. We also tried the fried squid legs which were satisfactory; however, the fried chicken caught my eye for a future visit.

The ambience was pleasant, with clean decor and a backdrop of pop music, setting a mood for quiet conversation among the handful of occupied tables. The only hiccup was a bathroom door that failed to shut securely when locked.

In summary, I'd recommend this spot for anyone looking for a quick, tasty meal in the area. It's certainly worth revisiting.

Title: Disappointing Trivia Night at Slattery's

I recently attended Friends trivia night at Slattery's, which unfortunately fell short of a good food and fun experience. Our early arrival allowed us to order before it got busy; I opted for an appetizer combo and an Avocado BLT Sandwich from the rather standard bar menu.

Suspiciously, the appetizer came out too quickly to be freshly made, and while it was edible, it wasn't exceptional. The trivia event, beginning tardily, was marred by noisy participants, making it impossible to hear the questions. Service struggled under the growing crowd, with simple requests like water being repeatedly ignored.

After an hour's wait, my BLT arrived, but my appetite had diminished alongside my patience, and I refused it. The chaotic atmosphere and lackluster offerings at Slattery's have crossed this venue off my list for future nights out. My evening ended in hunger and the regret of not choosing a different spot.

Title: Style Over Substance at Trendy Taco Spot

I recently visited a taco restaurant that seemed to focus more on its Instagram-worthiness than the food quality. The entrance is a feast for the eyes, with neon pink lights and decorative palm plants accompanied by the inviting beats of reggaeton music. This ambiance creates what some might call 'instaheaven.'

Unfortunately, the food didn't live up to the hype. The vegan Impossible taco stood out as a savory delight, and the cauliflower taco impressed with its flavor profile. However, the vegan chorizo taco was diminished by an overwhelming saltiness. The guacamole portion was disappointingly small, overshadowed by a mountain of chips. Toppings felt like an afterthought—disorganized and not complementing the tacos well.

My dining companion's salmon sushi taco was overly dressed with mayo, and the chicken taco lacked any noteworthy qualities. Despite these letdowns, the meal redeemed itself slightly with the coconut soft serve dessert—a delightful concoction that was perfectly balanced, with crunchy coconut and a sweet touch of açaí berry.

In summary, while the vibe is on point, the kitchen needs to realign its priorities. The coconut soft serve is a must-try, but approach the main menu with caution and managed expectations.

Title: A Satisfying Evening at Menya-jiro's Pop-Up

Last night's visit to Menya-jiro was yet another culinary delight. This unique pop-up transforms the Benton Cafe space into a cozy ramen haven come evening. While a tad pricier than one might expect (a dollar or two over the sweet spot), the ramen quality remains unparalleled. 

I indulged in the Kagoshima ramen, and it didn't disappoint—with generous servings of bean sprouts, impeccably cooked noodles, and a soup base so well-balanced one could enjoy every last drop without bracing for a salt overload. The Sakurajima also deserves a nod for those who favor a spicy kick, though besting the broth can be a gratifying challenge on its own. 

While the appetizers beckoned (the takoyaki at the Brooklyn branch is noteworthy), I plan to dive into those on a future visit. Currently, the atmosphere is quiet, ensuring an easily secured seat within its ten-person capacity. Service is as prompt and pleasant as ever, and for those on the move, a to-go option during lunchtime offers a quick, quality fix. 

In essence, Menya-jiro stands as a shining example of pop-up dining done right, offering a savory slice of ramen excellence in downtown Brooklyn.

This place was recommended to us by my husband's cousins, who are big pizza lovers, so I had high hopes. The New York location is also an outpost of a famous pizza place in Naples. After visiting though, I was largely disappointed by this place. We came with a reservation on a Saturday night, and were seated immediately. The restaurant was about half full, and we probably didn't need to make a reservation. We were seated at a table in the back, and given copies of the menu and water immediately. We ordered two things to share, a margherita pizza, and a calzone scarole, both of which were brought out quickly.I was fairly disappointed with the calzone scarole, which I had specifically ordered because it said it had anchovies on it. However, the calzone that we received tasted like it had no anchovies whatsoever on it. Everything else about the calzone was fine, but nothing amazing. The pizza was mostly the same. It was a good pizza; with nothing really to complain about, but nothing great either. The service was friendly, the food came out on time, and everything was done in an efficient manner. Overall, a good choice for pizza if you have no other better options, but not a place I would recommend going out of the way for.

Do you have a friend that likes to do the most? If so, that's probably who I am in your friend group. I wanted my friends and I to get a nice picture in an enchanting atmosphere, so we stopped here before our reservations across the street at Bagatelle. Do I regret it? Absolutely not! Sorry not sorry! Next time, we will stop by and get brunch here. :)

Fig and Olive continues to impress, maintaining its high standards at their Fifth Avenue location, just as they do near The Whitney. The food here is top-notch; the mushroom Croquettes were a standout for their taste. While the roasted cauliflower didn't quite live up to previous memories, it was still enjoyable. Their primavera risotto, a light and flavorful take on the often heavy dish, comes drizzled with a delightful green sauce, adding a pop of color and taste. The atmosphere is as lovely as one would expect, complemented by attentive and accommodating staff. Prices are on the higher side, but the quality and experience validate the expenditure. Overall, Fig and Olive delivers a premium dining experience well worth a visit.

The offerings available for Restaurant Week have gotten less appealing over the years so my co-workers and I were quite excited to find a menu that actually looked decent and worth the price of Restaurant Week.For $26, you get two courses. For the first course, you can choose between the Lobster Bisque, Calamari, and Half Dozen Oysters. For the second course, you have the option of The Original Burger, The Original Lobster Roll, and The Seven Samurai Roll.I'd highly recommend getting one Calamari and one Half Dozen Oysters between you and a friend so you can try both since the Calamari for one person is actually quite a lot (and can feel pretty heavy with the entrees). Both options were really good, though I actually liked the oysters more, but that could have been a personal preference. Unfortunately, no one at our table got the Bisque, so I can't comment on that but the calamari was also well-liked.Everyone (except one) at our table got The Original Lobster Roll. The amount of lobster that they give is actually quite hefty, and the salad and fries on top of it certainly makes it a very filling meal. The Original Burger also looked amazing, and it was ginormous as well. The regular menu actually looked quite reasonably priced as well, so I'm certainly excited to go back and try some other items on the menu sometime.o

Wow, we weren't expecting a long wait/line here when we stopped by since we thought it'd just be fast-casual-food. Well, we were wrong: it was popping on a Friday night. The inside is extremely small; I don't think it's meant to be a sit-down place. The only seating is in a row along the wall, and there aren't real tables. The surfaces you'd be eating on are reminiscent of when you're in a lecture hall with chairs that have the tables attached -- you need to swivel the surface/table into place from the chair. Felt very cramped overall.Here's what I tried:- Megamouth ($9) This tasted like your typical burger with lettuce and general toppings, but of course, with a vegetarian-friendly patty. The patty was underwhelming. While I liked the strong curry/cumin flavor, the texture fell flat since it was one-dimensional and sorta mushy. I'd enjoy it more if there was either a crunchy exterior or more of a "chew" to the patty like seitan or tofu. This is not a big burger by any means - I'd say it's a standard size -- but this is actually their large (the normal Superiority Burger is $6 and smaller). I was still somewhat hungry after eating it, which is an issue at this price point (or my stomach is the issue...).- Burnt Broccoli Salad ($4) A small, light salad that both of my friends got. I personally disliked the dressing and its acidity/flavoring, but both of them enjoyed it, so your mileage may vary.Part of the constant busy-ness seemed to stem from delivering online orders and only one cash register (although with the space constraint, I don't think they could fit another), so I'm just wondering if there's any way to make the process more efficient.  Not sure I'd return if I was craving a burger. The lemon sorbet looked good, though!

Title: Disappointing Dining Experience at NYC Mexican Chain

I recently visited a chain Mexican restaurant in NYC for a late lunch and was met with a profoundly disappointing experience. Despite the restaurant not being busy, the service was abysmal. It took an excessive 25 minutes to receive water and menus, even after requesting assistance from the hostess multiple times, who nonchalantly acknowledged my requests but failed to follow through.

The highlight of my meal was the traditional guacamole with a fresh flavor and accompanying salsa trio. Unfortunately, that was where the satisfaction ended. The chipotle quesadillas I ordered were uninspired, drowned in a BBQ sauce that masked any hint of chipotle. Accompanied by a minuscule portion of guacamole and a smattering of pico de gallo and sour cream, it was a poor dish that required the additional salsas to be palatable.

My friend's veggie tacos were equally underwhelming, described best as average and unexciting. Although the side of rice and beans was well-seasoned with a noticeable cilantro presence, it was not enough to redeem the overall meal.

In a city brimming with culinary options, this experience was a letdown, from the lackluster flavors to the nearly rude service. I regret to say I will not be returning and cannot recommend this establishment to others seeking quality Mexican cuisine in New York City.

My friend loves bibimbap.  Honestly, I didn't know what it was until I tried it with her last year.  Not every time we got to NYC we must find a place to have some.  This time we got a lunch reservation at Madangsui.2pm, our party of 4, walked in and we were immediately seated.  We were given a couple minutes to decide what to order and in the meantime the drinks were served.My boyfriend and I shared the Steak Hot Stone Bibimbap.  My friend and her bf shared the vegetable one.  While we waited for our food, small plates were brought for the table, like appetizers.  We had kimchi, a root vegetable, broccolini and a meat.  We also ordered some dumplings that were perfectly steamed, flavorful and perfect for sharing since there are 6pcs per order.Once the food came out we were in heaven.  Each entree came with a delicious Miso Soup (one of the best I've had).  The Bibimbaps were hot, and very generous in portion.  All ingredients tasted fresh, and full of flavor.  We all were very happy and full, making note to come again during another one of our NYC trips.

Title: A Taco Haven That's Worth the Wait

If your palate yearns for authentic tacos, this spot is a must-visit. Despite a 45-minute wait, the experience my friends and I had was worth every minute. We indulged in carne asada and pollo asado tacos, along with adobada tacos that burst with well-balanced flavors. We didn't stop there; the carne asada and pollo asado quesadillas were equally delightful with perfectly seasoned meats and fresh condiments.

The service was top-notch, and the prices didn’t break the bank. For those looking to sample a bit of everything, I'd recommend three tacos and a quesadilla. Just brace yourself for a wait and cozy seating arrangements. This taco spot is definitely a culinary highlight not to be missed.

My friend and I made a reservation at Olio e Piu for 9:15pm on a Saturday.  The easiest way to make a reserve is to book through their website which uses the SevenRooms platform.  I highly recommend making a reservation regardless of what time you want to eat.  From the time we arrived to the time we left an hour and a half later, the restaurant was still pretty full, which is a testament to how good it is!  The atmosphere is rustic and dark and can get loud at peak times, especially because tables are close to each other.  I ordered the Spaghetti Chitarra Alla Carbonara ($24) and my friend got the Abbondante pizza (mozzarella, pepper, sausage, basil)($22).  The pasta was amazing in both taste and presentation.  The noodles tasted fresh and chewy, and did not depend on the sauce to add moisture.  The sauce also had a rich flavor without tasting heavy!  I'm normally an extremely slow eater but I inhaled this pasta.  It was so delicious.  I was pleasantly surprised as this is the pasta most often showcased on Instagram.  Believe the hype!  The pizza sauce had a fresh tomato flavor, and the crust had a good doughy consistency.  The one thing I will say about the food is that the serving sizes are on the smaller side, so those with big appetites may not be full.Our server Victoria was gracious and made us feel like family.  She gave good recommendations and was the sweetest!  She did multiple check-backs and our water jug was replaced whenever it was empty.  I will admit that Olio e Piu is a tad overpriced, so I went back and forth between 4 and 5 stars.  I also am by no means an expert in authentic Italian food.  However, the food and atmosphere were both so good that I don't mind paying a higher price!

Not the cheapest Vietnamese food you can get on the UES, but we've never been disappointed and they have outdoor seating! Portions are nicely sized, never small. They also have a fun assortment of cocktails to choose from. Things we've gotten before and enjoyed:- Nem - Fried calamari- Assorted steamed dumplings- Pho- Ginger chicken- Bun Xao noodles with shrimp On a nice night, it's a great spot to go to for quick in and out, as they are pretty speedy with getting your food out to you.

Title: A Disappointing Experience at a Midtown Eatery

From the moment we entered the restaurant, the lack of a warm welcome was a red flag. Despite the allure of the beautifully crafted menu with its bold typography and appetizing photographs, the reality fell short, a stark contrast to the less-than-flattering images on Yelp.

Service was lackluster at best, with a particular waiter blatantly ignoring our attempts to catch his attention, even as he attended to others around us. This behavior not only felt dismissive but also raised concerns about discriminatory service practices.

The food did little to redeem the experience. I sampled the Tick Tock Pancake Trio, priced at $13, which proved to be a bland disappointment. Given the myriad of dining options in Midtown, my advice would be to explore elsewhere for a meal that promises both taste and a welcoming atmosphere.

Title: A Hip Spot for Lively Saturday Brunch

I recently visited a vibrant young restaurant, an ideal choice for a Saturday brunch. The atmosphere buzzed with on-point music that catered to the modern diner's taste. Although service did lag a bit due to the small space struggling with the brunch-time rush, the staff remained courteous under pressure.

The manager's cordial demeanor added a personal touch to the experience. While waiting for my companion at the bar, I indulged in a delightful raspberry bellini, which I captured in a photo. The burger, cooked to a perfect medium, did not disappoint either.

For those under 30 looking for a brunch spot that meshes great eats with hip tunes, this is the place to be. Solid 4/5 stars – a commendable choice, although it didn't completely blow me away.

We came here in early evening Friday and were surprised to see a limited menu and small space The waitress at bar was very friendly and gave great recommendations. We got the bada special 2 of us and had chef appetizer ( crab brain?) great sashimi sushi and Maki rolls .  Others tried the edamame ( very different but good), Avocado fries , sushi roles ( sakehana and the love), and shrimp tempura . Wish I had tried the sushi that was in tin foil and cooked on a fire . If I were to do again, I would just ordered their amazing sushi and skip the bada special . Delicious fresh and nice! We were the only non Japanese there

Title: Mixed Feelings at Hou Yi's Hot Pot

I recently visited Hou Yi's Hot Pot, having previously enjoyed the Chinatown location, particularly for their unlimited drinks offering a delightful variety from soy milk to herbal tea and yakult. The anticipation for an all-you-can-eat experience brought my friends and I to indulge in a shared split pot, opting for the tomato beef broth despite the unexpected $3 extra charge not commonly seen elsewhere.

Service was prompt with the food arriving quickly, though the small table size made it a squeeze for all our dishes. The fare was standard hot pot cuisine—nothing noteworthy. However, we did encounter an oversight with some missing items, an issue I've noticed isn't uncommon in AYCE settings.

Mid-meal, we were dismayed to find a burnt rice cake in our tomato broth, rendering half the pot unusable. Surprisingly, swapping out the soup incurred a steep $12 fee, another unusual practice that inflated our bill considerably.

Ambience-wise, the establishment relied on fans over air conditioning, which affected the dining comfort. Comparatively, I find 99 more appealing for its cleaner environment and more courteous service. Given these experiences, I'm hesitant to return to Hou Yi's despite the potential of what could have been a delightful hot pot outing.

Title: A True Taste of Asia with an Atmosphere to Match

I've dined at this gem several times, and its authenticity never fails to amaze me. The decor, adorned with exquisite wall art, transports you to an Asian oasis. Despite the potential wait on weekends, I assure you, it's a small price to pay for the culinary experience that awaits.

The menu is a parade of delights, but some dishes have captured my palate more than others. The Roti Canai is a flaky, buttery starter, perfect for dipping in its accompanying curry. Chicken Poppers are a must-try – they’re the right balance of crisp and juicy. The Chicken Rendang and Nasi Lemak are rich in flavor and will satisfy any craving for traditional fare. Lastly, the Hakka Chilli Crispy Chicken is an explosion of savory and spicy that I find myself coming back for.

Every visit has been consistent with the quality of food, making it a reliable spot for a fantastic meal. My only wish is for an improvement in service, which, if addressed, would elevate the dining experience to perfection.

The decor in this place is beautiful! It's pretty small but we were seated right away on a Friday night. We had the strawberry martinis, and while they were strong, they were way too sweet with a syrup-y taste. Would not recommend. For food we had the basil fried rice which was delicious. I was surprised to see kow soi on the menu, which can be rare to find. However it was not very authentic, it was basically just chicken Penang curry over noodles. Still delicious though!

This is my favorite Thai restaurant in the neighborhood! I've been inside before and hVe also gotten delivery from here through UberEats. I have only had their massaman curry, but I like it so much that I haven't really ventured to try any of their other dishes. The curry is extremely flavorful and I like how the potatoes, many different meat options (including mock duck), avocado, spices and peanuts go really well together in it. It's mildly spicy and also slightly sweet. Their takeout also surprisingly travels pretty well. It was well packed and I received my order quickly. I would definitely recommend this restaurant. Whenever the pandemic winds down and they reopen their restaurant seating, it's worth it to check out the interior. The space has a nice ambiance and there is pretty ample seating.

Thai Son has so many seats and I was able to get seated first while waiting for my friend. I nearly slipped on my way to the seat, and when my friend arrived, she told me she almost fell as well. I also noticed that one of the cups was quite sticky and asked to replace it. While the staff was really friendly and attentive, I found most things sticky from the items on our table (such as the sauce bottles) to the bathroom.The food however, was fantastic. I ordered their #2 pho which is slightly smaller than their #1 and had beef balls. Both bowls included various beef pieces, including tripe. It was so good and the portion size was more than a girl could ask for -- they did not skimp out on the meat at all. It was a bit over $10 and well worth it.

All I'll say is I was perfectly happy to give this place a solid 3.5 stars for pretty tasty, but small, way overpriced food. Service and ambiance were fine... yada, yada, yada.And then they brought that duck carnitas dish and my life as I knew it will never be the same again. Easily one of the top 5 dishes of any category that I've ever had, anywhere, ever... ever. It's just an all-around perfect dish that makes this restaurant so, so worth it.If you go to Cosme and you don't have that dish you are officially stupid.

I quite enjoyed the food we ordered here. Although it's been a while, I remember the Italian chorizo sausage to be quite flavorful. Having sausages in the omelette was a plus too. My friends ordered the egg poutine (?) and spaghetti for brunch. Definitely very filling.

I recently embarked on a culinary quest to explore all of Matthew Kenney's vegetarian venues, kicking off with a delightful brunch at Bar Verde. As someone who leans toward a pescatarian/flexitarian diet, the joy of being able to choose anything from a vegan menu cannot be overstated.

Bar Verde's ample outdoor seating was the perfect setting to savor the summer ambiance. Accompanied by a couple of friends, the service we encountered was nothing short of welcoming.

We sampled the mushroom quesadilla and a serving of nachos. As a mushroom aficionado, the quesadilla particularly impressed me – it was a savory delight that would leave any diner questioning its vegan authenticity. The nachos didn't lag behind, offering a burst of flavors that satisfied everyone at the table.

Bar Verde proved itself to be a gem for anyone in search of mouthwatering Mexican cuisine, vegan or not. This visit has set a high bar for my Matthew Kenney journey in NYC, and I eagerly anticipate the delights that await at his other locations.

Title: Cozy Spot with Hearty Slices – Artichoke

Review:
Artichoke gets a solid 3.5 stars from me for its unique take on pizza. The highlight, the artichoke slice, is a creamy and indulgent affair; one slice for $6 is enough to satisfy, boasting a nicely executed crust. Though rich and flavorful, those with a taste for traditional Brooklyn-style pizza might find it a bit too heavy. Seafood lovers will appreciate the crab slice – also priced at $6 – which is generously topped with crabmeat, making it a worthwhile pick.

The service at Artichoke is commendably quick and efficient. While other options, like the grandma slice, are a dollar cheaper, the standout choices are worth the extra buck. The ambiance is a bit dark, featuring a quirky Christmas story lamp, which adds character to the dimly lit space.

In summary, Artichoke is a decent spot for those looking to try something different from standard pizza fare. Just be prepared for a rich meal in a moody, yet interestingly decorated, setting.

If you're a pizza lover, Prince Street is a must when you visit New York. Lucky for me, prince street is a hop and skip away from my work in SoHo. There was a short but fast moving line during lunch hours on a weekday.You've seen it all over your IG stories and snaps. Is the hype real? YES. Their square shaped pepperoni slice is heavenly. The dough is thicc and the pepperonis are plentiful. The pepperonis are perfectly crisped in the oven. It does have a little kick, but don't forget to add some chili peppers on the side if you want some spicy.One slice isn't enough for a growing man like me, but I can't finish two. It's a little oily, but this pizza is worth the splurge. The pizza is always coming out of the oven, so you can rest assure that you're having a fresh slice.

Title: A Fiery Introduction to Sri Lankan Cuisine at [Restaurant Name]

As a newcomer to Sri Lankan cuisine, I approached [Restaurant Name] with a mix of curiosity and excitement. For fellow spice enthusiasts, this place does not shy away from delivering a true spicy punch - a thrilling experience that hit the mark for me.

We started with the appetizer sampler featuring an assortment, including dhal vade, fish cutlets, and both fish and vegetable spring rolls. All were fried, which made the dish rather heavy, and distinguishing between the fish and vegetable spring rolls proved challenging after a few bites. The dhal vade was somewhat underwhelming on its own but was redeemed by the accompanying flavorful sauces.

The standout of the evening was the pork black curry, paired with unexpectedly thick roti. The curry's robust flavors and heat were beautifully mopped up with the roti, which proved to be a perfect vehicle for such a hearty dish.

Overall, [Restaurant Name] promises an authentic and intensely spicy experience that I'll surely seek out again. I recommend it to anyone looking to immerse themselves in the bold tastes of Sri Lankan cooking.

Mac Attack delivers an unparalleled Macaroni and Cheese experience that outshines all others I've sampled - and I've tried my fair share. The truffle oil variety was a standout, adding a sophisticated twist to a comfort food classic, and it easily clinched the top spot for me. The other two options did not disappoint, each packing its own punch of delectable cheesiness. Highly recommended for any mac 'n' cheese aficionado.

Title: Authentic Flavors with Hits and Misses

My family and I ventured into this eatery with high hopes, eager to dive into their widely talked-about Chinese cuisine. We ordered a selection of dishes, eager to sample a bit of everything. The standout of our meal was undoubtedly the cumin lamb — a dish that I can confidently say was the best I've ever enjoyed. Perfectly tender cuts of lamb were generously coated with an aromatic cumin spice that left a memorable impression on my palate.

The tea egg also received high praise from my mother, who savored the robust tea-infused flavor, although I must admit that it wasn't to my personal taste. On the other hand, the fish fillets in chili oil were satisfactory but failed to impress me with the level of spice and Sichuan peppercorn 'numbness' I had anticipated.

The Couples Delight suffered from a similar fate, lacking the spicy kick I crave in authentic Chinese dishes. As for the Dan Dan noodles, their texture was a slight letdown; I missed the chewiness that usually accompanies the slipperiness of the noodles.

Overall, I'd rate the restaurant at a respectable 3.5 out of 5. While some dishes like the cumin lamb truly shined, others could benefit from a touch more boldness in flavor to truly elevate the dining experience.

Title: A Brunch Favorite in Manhattan

I recently revisited one of my top brunch spots in Manhattan and once again, it did not disappoint. Booking through OpenTable makes the experience seamless, sparing me the usual wait times associated with popular eateries.

The menu boasts standout dishes like the decadently sweet honey pull-away bread and the perfectly balanced challah French toast, each offering a delightful start to the day. For those craving something savory, the buffalo Mac and cheese is a must-try with its bold flavors.

The service here truly enhances the experience, with attentive and friendly waitstaff adding to the restaurant’s welcoming ambiance. The portion sizes are generous, making it ideal for sharing among friends, which also turns this into a budget-friendly option.

If you're on the hunt for a fantastic brunch in Manhattan, this place deserves your attention. Highly recommended for both the food quality and the overall experience.

Title: An Edgy Italian Experience with Room for Service Improvement

Located in the heart of the Financial District lies this Italian eatery that merges a dining experience with a club-like ambiance. Its dark interiors are accentuated with blue lighting and modern decor, complete with stylish curtains that add to its chic vibe. Opting to dine solo, I settled at the bar, which I hoped would invite friendly service. Sadly, the bartender's attention was monopolized by acquaintances, leaving me feeling somewhat neglected throughout my meal.

The menu boasted a variety of Italian classics, and I chose the pasta alla vodka – a New York favorite of mine. While it was good and hit the right spot with its well-sized portion, it didn't quite reach the pinnacle of pasta excellence. However, it did satisfy my craving to a fair extent. The establishment also offers a decent selection of wines, complementing their array of dishes.

In conclusion, while the meal was adequate and the setting had its unique charm, the lapse in attentive service left a slight tarnish on the experience. I'm neutral about returning; it served its purpose for a one-time visit but didn't inspire a repeat encounter.

It was the first really warm day of spring, and a Monday, so we were in good spirits and wanted to continue the good cheer by going out to dinner. As we both enjoyed Madame Vo, we decided to give its new offshoot, Madame Vo BBQ, a try.It was 6pm when we came in, and the restaurant was empty. We were seated immediately, and brought waters and copies of the menu right away. A waiter came to explain the ins and outs of the menu to us, and we ordered 4 things to share, including the nem nuong, bo lui, short rib spring roll, and the banh hoi platter. The nem nuong (Vietnamese pork meatballs, usually on skewers at Vietnamese barbecues) are one of my favorite things to eat. The meatballs that were served here were tasty, and the best part of the meal, but not amazing. The bo lui, rolls of short rib, was surprisingly lackluster. I never thought I'd say it of short rib, as it is one of my favorite cuts of meat, but the short rib here was tough and chewy. Would not recommend getting this at all. The short rib spring roll consisted of more short rib, with bone marrow in what was supposed to be truffle hoisin sauce. However, the elements of truffle and bone marrow were very subtle and completely lost on me. Can't justify the $16 price tag for two pieces of spring rolls that just tasted like regular spring rolls. The worst thing and a complete affront about this place, is that they charged $10 for the banh hoi platter, which would normally come free in any other Vietnamese restaurant. It included the rice paper rolls, lettuce (a scant serving), vermicelli noodles, mint, pineapple, and a medley of apple and carrot slices. Service was friendly and efficient, and ambience was cool, with music that was a little bit too loud. Based on the underwhelming and overpriced food, I would not recommend this place at all, or ever return.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Popular Chain's New Location

I recently visited the new branch of a well-known restaurant hoping for the same quality I've enjoyed at their other locations. Unfortunately, my experience was underwhelming. Despite a wide array of familiar menu items, the service fell short.

Upon arrival at 3pm on a weekend, I was surprised by a 30-minute wait despite several vacant tables, hinting at possible understaffing issues. Without a reservation, which we didn't think we'd need, we were eventually seated but faced disappointingly poor service.

We opted for the happy hour set priced at $60, anticipating a treat. Alas, the food's arrival was painfully slow; even a simple soup and salad took an extra 15-20 minutes to reach our table.

For a better experience, I recommend the midtown east location. And if you decide to give this place a try, I suggest downloading their app to at least accumulate points while you wait.

During my first visit to this restaurant, I was particularly impressed with how knowledgeable our waiter was about gluten-free options, thanks to his personal connection to celiac disease. He recommended the House Rice Noodles, which were not only delicious but also generously portioned—I took more than half home! The pea leaves with garlic were another hit on his suggestion. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

For a bustling Saturday night around 7-8pm, our wait for a table stretched to 30 minutes, hinting at the restaurant's popularity. The atmosphere was overwhelmingly warm, likely exacerbated by the crowd. We opted for the December drink special, a pomegranate margarita, which continued the recent trend of being notably sweet and sour. However, its redeeming quality was the discernible presence of alcohol, paired with an enticingly low price point.

Title: A Hidden Gem with Trendy Vibes

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a unique, tucked-away spot that I've been eagerly anticipating to visit. Nestled upstairs, away from the bustling crowds typical of places like Fuku, this eatery offers a serene reprieve for food enthusiasts.

At first glance, one might mistake it for a convenience store, thanks to its cleverly curated aesthetic. While it's not an actual store you can wander through, the compact space, reminiscent of Bang Bar's cozy dimensions, makes clever use of its area, featuring about 15 steps of well-thought-out interior.

Among the delightful surprises are the various purchasable items peppered throughout, complementing the theme and igniting a collector's spark in me. I can't wait to get my hands on all the branded goodies they offer.

Our culinary adventure began with the omelette kimbap—a traditional and wonderfully authentic snack. Perfect for sharing, it was a testament to the kitchen's dedication to classic fare. Additionally, the delightful packaging added to the overall charm of the experience.

My first visit has left a lasting impression, and I'm already looking forward to delving deeper into their menu offerings. If you're on the hunt for a novel dining encounter with intriguing collectibles and authentic bites, this is a spot you won't want to miss.

I'm so glad I stopped by ! My friend and I ended up getting the dosa and chicken masala curry . The Dosa was fantastic, the potatoes had so much flavor , and it had a nice crisp.The chicken Masala was good, had a strong tomato base, which was interesting. The garlic naan was so good! The flavors and the crisp really made me feel like I was back in my native country.  We also ended up getting this naan bread with lamb filling. Can't wait to come back here!

Saturday afternoon, not many people inside this easy-to-miss restaurant. Large counter to the side where you can order from the simple menu, with both seating indoors and outdoors.Decided on the Pork Okonomiyaki ($10) with additional spice ($0.50 extra), as well as a large format Sapporo ($6ish). Like the fact that they tell you in advance how long it's going to take (approximately 12 minutes). Food arrives on time, piping hot on top of the counter - a layering of veggies, sauces, and pork over a potato like pancake. Surprisingly not too oily and the flavors all worked well together. Disappointed in the spice level - I think they may have forgotten to add any at all - so had to use a bit of the table sriracha.Overall cool Japanese street food spot, especially during the warmer days when you can take advantage of the porch seating.

Title: A Warm Welcome and Solid Italian Fare at Barolo East

If you're navigating through the myriad of Italian dining options in the city and find yourself pondering whether Barolo East deserves a spot on your list, I'd nudge you with a firm "Yes." My recent visit to Barolo East, a late 10pm dinner with a coworker, was met with a surprisingly warm welcome despite our late arrival and the near-empty dining space.

The ambiance of Barolo East was soothing and inviting, contributing positively to our overall experience. The minestrone soup served was comforting, featuring well-cooked vegetables, though a touch more seasoning could have elevated the flavors. The spinach and ricotta ravioli was skillfully crafted; it was satisfying without crossing into the extraordinary.

While none of the dishes I tasted were transcendent, they were all commendably executed. The only other quibble I had was the beer selection—while Peroni is a nod to their Italian roots, a broader selection, possibly including a couple of draught options, would have been appreciated.

In conclusion, Barolo East offers an enjoyable dining experience with a friendly staff and competently prepared Italian classics. It may not have completely blown me away, but I'd certainly return and would recommend giving it a try.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Persian Delights

Don't let the unassuming façade of this eatery fool you; it's a treasure trove of authentic Persian cuisine. The menu might give off a "just another kebab place" vibe, but once you delve into their "stews" section, you'll uncover an array of traditional dishes that are nothing short of remarkable.

The Gormeh Sabzi here is a standout, boasting the perfect tang of preserved lemon that it's known for. The cherry rice is a sweet revelation, complementing any meal you choose. And for a touch of creamy refreshment, the Mast Khiar is on point – rich yet cooling.

This place is legit. Seriously. Make your way there with an appetite ready for satisfaction!

Authentic taco spot in the heart of times square! Imagine that. Literally gives you the feeling of getting tacos from a stand in Mexico. Menu is clear and simply put on the wall- tacos, plates, enchiladas & "mulas" which falls somewhere between the two. Lines can get long here! Like wrapped outside long, but it tends to move quickly. They've set it up so you can order then move to the left to specify toppings and tortillas(& watch it get made) then lastly left once more to add your salsa. This taco spot has standing room only!! So don't expect to be lounging around here after your done eating. This is strictly for enjoying delicious, authentic tacos & bouncing. My favorite taco was the beef. I wish they did fish as well because I'm sure it would be outstanding! Prices are on point too.

Title: A Scenic Feast Overlooking Rockefeller Ice Rink

As the soft strains of background music mingled with the classy ambiance at this picturesque spot, my dining experience was elevated to great heights. Overlooking the bustling Rockefeller ice rink, my friends and I indulged in the Autumn prix-fixe dinner, a splurge at $85 per person that proved to be well worth it for the quality and quantity of food served.

The star of the show was undoubtedly the salmon tartare, presented with an unexpected but delightful pairing of ice cream. The dish was an extraordinary symphony of flavors, both unique and exquisite. As for the main course, I savored the filet mignon, cooked to perfection and accompanied by flavorful mushrooms; though I personally could have done without the bone marrow.

Dessert was a dreamy Chocolate hazelnut tart, reminiscent of an upscale Ferrero Rocher, complemented by the subtly sweet stracciatella ice cream with its delicate custard and egg notes. Service throughout the meal was impeccable—attentive but unintrusive, the epitome of professionalism.

My overall experience was stellar, and I am eager for a chance to return. For anyone visiting, the salmon tartare is a must-try. Thank you for a memorable meal!

Title: A Delightful Sushi Experience Worth Revisiting

I recently dined at this gem of a sushi spot and was thoroughly impressed with both the quality of the food and the service. The sushi was incredibly fresh, expertly prepared, and served promptly - a true testament to the restaurant's dedication to a great dining experience. My sister's chicken katsu was equally delicious and became a communal favorite at our table, evidenced by our collective nibbling!

Having an office nearby is a bonus, as I am already planning to return for more lunchtime indulgences. Additionally, the standout service deserves a mention; our server was the epitome of attentiveness, striking the perfect balance between being available and not intrusive, a rare find in many Japanese eateries we've frequented. Overall, this was a great experience that left me excited for my next visit.

Hands down best burgers ever! So glad I found this cool spot in Chelsea and in walking distance from my office. Came here with coworkers during the week for lunch. We all grabbed spots at the bar !!!! To note this spot is small but there are seats at the  bar and a few around, more like high chairs with a table. Most people ordered their burgers to go so that's another option! Their lunch menu is burgers and they have a variety of side order. I ordered the short ribs burger with fries and was amazing! The taste was great! Perfect sizing not too much fries! Will definently be back at this spot. You can also order a variety of drinks and their coffee and tea smell amazing, they take extra caution in giving you the perfect sip!

I recently popped into this charming little restaurant for a quick lunch and was thoroughly impressed. The Maine lobster roll was scrumptious, generously packed with lobster and tastefully light on the mayo, allowing the seafood's flavor to shine. The lobster bisque accompanied my roll perfectly, rich and delectable. To top it off, the staff's friendliness made the dining experience even more enjoyable. Highly recommended for a delightful meal.

Title: A Feast of Mughlai Flavors

My dining experience at Mughlai was an absolute delight. A friend and I savored an array of dishes, including the Gobhi Manchurian, Veggie Samosas, Mughlai Poori, Lamb Curry, and Chicken Tikka Masala. Each dish brought its own unique burst of flavor, but it was the Lamb Curry that stole the show - tender, aromatic, and perfectly spiced. I highly recommend giving it a try when you visit. Mughlai's culinary prowess has made it a top contender on my list for a flavorful feast.

Title: A Michelin Star Omakase Experience to Remember

Having sampled omakases across the city, the one at Suzuki stands out as a distinguished gem, rightfully earning its Michelin star. Fortune smiled upon us with an impromptu seat at the 9:30 pm slot on a Monday. Future diners, take note to reserve ahead for this in-demand experience.

At $130 per person, the price is well-suited to New York's culinary scene, particularly for the exquisite quality offered. The sushi bar exudes a simple elegance, a fitting backdrop for the renowned Sushi Chef Suzuki's culinary artistry. With an impressive half-century of expertise, Chef Suzuki not only crafted sublime bites but also shared insights into the origins and nuances of our meal—a delightful educational touch.

Each piece of sushi, notably the standout saltwater eel, was a testament to the freshness and skillful preparation, enhanced with intriguing flavors and a precise dab of wasabi. The well-composed assortment included 10 pieces of nigiri, a memorable hand roll, and a comforting bowl of miso soup.

The meal's rhythm allowed for a fulfilling, yet comfortably paced dining experience, leaving me satiated. This omakase is a treasure to be savored on special occasions, worth every cent for the impeccable fare and experience. Highly recommended.

Very very impressed with this place. It wasn't your traditional omakase. Each piece was very unique, looked like a work of art and consistently created the ideal combination of flavors in your mouth. The uni on a cracker with caviar and truffle was one of my favorites, but it's honestly impossible to chose. The staff  and chefs were phenomenal. Made us feel very welcomed and were very attentive. I appreciated that the waiter allowed me to try's few sakes before choosing one. I will defInitely be back

My visit to Fieldtrip in Harlem was thoroughly enjoyable. The staff displayed exceptional kindness, and the presence of the overseeing chef added a personal touch to the dining experience. The menu's diversity, offering both veggie and meat options, caters to a variety of palates. The crab pockets were a delectable treat, and the veggie bowl stood out with its burst of flavors, satiating both hunger and taste. On my next visit, I'm eager to delve into one of the meat-based dishes. While drinks are available, they aren't the highlight, and the pricing leans toward the higher end. Nevertheless, Fieldtrip brings a welcomed diversity to the Harlem food scene, and I'm already planning my return.

I recently had lunch at this Cuban/Latin eatery and was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food. For those looking for an affordable lunch option, they're part of Mealpal, which is a bonus. The meal I got through Mealpal was satisfying and well-portioned (see attached pic). However, I would caution against ordering the fried yucca; it's pre-fried and held in a warm oven, leaving it limp rather than crispy. It's the one item on the menu that might have you questioning its value for money. Overall, a solid choice for a Latin-inspired lunch, just steer clear of the yucca.

I was attending a conference at the New Yorker Hotel around the corner & had a craving for Indian food. I looked at Yelp reviews & went with this place. Glad I did. My food was fabulous. It was pretty busy on a Thursday night at 8:30pm, and it was almost totally full by the time I left at 9:30. They had a $5 glass of wine deal, so you can't argue with a $5 glass of Pinot Grigio in NYC. I ordered the White Coco Chicken Curry medium spicy. It was sooooo good. Came with a bowl of basmati rice. I also ordered garlic naan which came out hot, fresh & garlicky. I downed all 4 pieces. Anyway, good experience here, would definitely stop again.

This might be one of my new favorite places for ramen. I'm not a huge ramen guy but this takes all my praise. I love the broth and I love the thick wavy noodles. Most of all, I love the price and value. $17 for a lunch set - ramen and poke bowl. Thats hard to get anywhere else in the city. We came here Saturday 12:15 pm and waited 10 minutes for 2 people. When we left at 1:30pm there were open tables and no one waiting outside. Wait time wasn't terrible but it was packed when we first came.Expect seating to be crammed and your thigh close to touching another person's thigh. But its NYC so its part of the norm. ENJOY!

Title: A Local Favorite – Cask

As a neighbor to Cask, I've had the pleasure of frequenting it for various meals, and I'm yet to be disappointed. Their breakfast offerings, particularly the smoked salmon sandwich, have become my morning staple. It's a dish that manages to feel indulgent yet healthy, striking a perfect balance with the creamy cheese and light, airy bread.

What eclipses breakfast, for me, is their happy hour—a time of day that Cask truly shines. Their daily specials keep things exciting, but the standouts are unquestionably the oysters and mussels, which I eagerly pair with a crisp white wine for a truly sublime experience.

The ambiance, too, is worth noting, with cozy bar seating and additional space downstairs for those busier nights. And while I've yet to claim the coveted window table, it remains on my Cask bucket list. Here's to hoping I'll be reviewing that view soon!

Title: Disappointment on High at Manhatta

I had eagerly anticipated dining at Manhatta since its grand opening, and an occasion finally presented itself: my parents' 30th wedding anniversary. Unfortunately, our experience didn't match the high expectations set by its reputation and sister establishment, Union Square Cafe.

The highlight of Manhatta is, without doubt, its breathtaking 60th-floor vista, offering an unparalleled view of the city. But a view can only go so far. The service was lackluster, with our waiter appearing disinterested—perhaps an unintended consequence of the restaurant's non-tipping policy. While some guests by the windows received attentive care, our party felt neglected, despite having requested a window table which was not honored.

On to the cuisine, the consensus was that it was disappointingly mediocre, especially given the steep price tag of $500 for four diners. My wagyu bolognese was unremarkable, something I could've easily outdone at home. The chocolate soufflé was the sole standout in an otherwise forgettable three-course meal. My mother's beet salad was satisfactory, but the snails and "bacon and eggs" dish were merely passable. The duck was a letdown, though, on a positive note, my husband did find enjoyment in his steak.

In summary, I desperately wanted to fall in love with Manhatta, but it just wasn't meant to be. For the price and the hype, the restaurant should have delivered an impeccable experience all around. Based on our visit, I cannot in good faith recommend Manhatta, and I don't plan on returning.

I recently stumbled upon a hidden gem in the LES, a ramen spot that may very well be the epitome of 'hole in the wall' greatness. Their tonkotsu ramen was a revelation, boasting what might just be the best char siu my palate has had the pleasure of savoring. The pork was tender, with a smoky grilled flavor that melded seamlessly with the rich broth. And for those seeking an alternative, they offer a superb chicken broth-based ramen as well.

But let’s talk noodles – they were chewy, springy, and stood up to the broth in a way that only the best ramen noodles can. It's the kind of quality that keeps you coming back for more, and that's exactly what I intend to do. Between this spot and Mr Taka, I've found my top destinations for that irresistible bowl of ramen in the Lower East Side. Highly recommended for any ramen aficionado!

I love coming backing to here for their chicken sandwiches because their Chicken Sandwich always hits the spot  They call this the Fire Bird. It's gots pickled peppers, lettuce, tomatoe & spicy chipotle mayo which are my fav burger toppers & I added a sliced of aged cheese because who eats any sandwiches without cheese Also got a side of sweet potato fries cuz they the bestest

I stumbled upon this charming eatery just yesterday, where a kind elderly woman at the host stand warmly inquired if I was looking to dine. Her welcoming spirit led me to peruse the menu, which boasted an array of appetizing starters. Succumbing to my curiosity, I opted for the deviled eggs and quiche. Both dishes were simply delightful, offering robust flavors and a homemade touch that truly hit the spot. Highly recommended for a taste of hearty, comforting fare!

Title: A Delightful Dinner Experience with a Minor Hiccup

Review:

Ventured into the bustling atmosphere of this local gem right after their widely-acclaimed happy hour—it was evident why the place was lively even on a Tuesday night. Intrigued by the vibe, I'm already planning my next visit specifically to catch those happy hour specials.

For starters, the snow crab legs and grilled oysters were impeccable—a testament to their freshness. The kimchi herb butter accompanying the oysters showcased a masterful pairing. Equally notable was the fried feta, which I'd describe as a gourmet twist on the classic fried mozzarella, complete with a generous helping of tzatziki sauce that makes it a must-try for feta aficionados.

The main course had its highs and lows. My wagyu burger, which was supposed to be medium-rare, unfortunately landed on the table well-done, leaning towards the dry side—a minor blip in an otherwise tasty meal. The paprika fries and side salad, however, were seasoned to perfection, with the salad's subtly sweet vinaigrette being a delightful touch. My boyfriend's lobster roll with pesto fries earned his seal of approval, adding another positive note to our dining experience.

Service-wise, our waiter was the epitome of attentiveness, ensuring our meal progressed smoothly with frequent check-ins.

In short, despite a slight misstep with my burger, the culinary journey was enjoyable. This establishment has certainly earned a spot on our return list, promising anticipation for what happy hour might unveil.

No line when I got there around 5:40pm so I would recommend to come before 6pm (at least until the hype dies down) The servers were attentive and came over multiple times to place our orders but we needed a bit more time to check out what to order. Ordered 2 rice noodle rolls (known for their rice noodle here) sticky rice wrap and congee. I didnt like the rice noodle roll much. The plastic chopsticks they have us use is not good with the rice noodle rolls. Hard to grab and the skin broke easily before we were able to our it in our mouth. They should have used wooden chopsticks but that's my opinion. I do like their congee. Wasnt too salty which I like and can add more salt or pepper if needed. There are 2 neutral bathrooms that are across from where they bring out the food. Not the best area to put the bathroom... The bathroom is small. This place is cash only so make sure to bring the moolah. Overall, I'm not a fan of this place. But I do like the congee so maybe i'll have that if I choose to splurge extra money.

Title: Style Over Substance at a Popular Spot

I recently dined at a local hotspot that, despite its popularity, left much to be desired. The restaurant's interior is undeniably striking, with a modern, dramatic aesthetic complete with chandeliers and candles creating a gorgeous ambiance - a promising start for our party of 12.

Unfortunately, the service did not match the surroundings. Our waiter seemed overwhelmed from the outset, initially forgetting our drink orders and requiring a few waves to catch his attention. It took an unacceptable 15-20 minutes just to receive our drinks.

The service fumbled further when it came to coordinating our meal. High-end dining usually means synchronized service, especially for appetizers, but here dishes arrived haphazardly, disrupting the dining experience. Following a disjointed start, our side dishes appeared first, leaving us waiting awkwardly for the main courses, resulting in cold rice by the time the entrées arrived. Bafflingly, they also replaced plates without cause, given they went unused before the entrées were served, an unnecessary gesture reinforced by the impractical size of the plates that crowded our table.

Regarding the cuisine, while the Alaskan cod shone with well-balanced flavors, the rest of the offerings were merely passable and certainly not justifying the premium prices.

In summary, although the setting was visually beautiful, the combination of slow, inattentive service, poorly executed meal pacing, and unremarkable food (with the exception of one dish) makes it hard to recommend this establishment. It's a classic case of style over substance, where the experience doesn’t quite live up to the hype or the cost.

In the mood for tacos? I'm talking delicious, authentic, flavorful tacos #LosTacosNo1 delivers just that. I'm already planning my next visit. My friend and I were craving tacos and this kept coming up as a recommended spot. I was a bit hesitant on how authentic it would be (since it's located in the Chelsea Market). But trust me.... everyone on Yelp giving it a 4/5 star rating is right. The line moves quick. Be ready to order. Credit cards accepted. The staff is fast when it comes to prepping everything (I had to do a double-take). First bite? Amazing. I had the pollo (chicken) taco and the carne asada (steak) quesadilla - con todo (w/ everything). Everything was delicious and made fresh. Definitely needed to order more stuff. But like I said... I'm already thinking of when to return. This spot has the stamp of approval from two Mexican women who know the real deal! :)

Title: A Fresh FiDi Lunch Favorite

I recently ventured into a recommended lunch haven nestled in the heart of FiDi, transitioning from my habitual midtown haunts. The spot, a favorite among locals, boasts a delightful buffet that pays homage to its predecessor, Chen's, both in setup and rotating culinary offerings.

The variety was impressive; I indulged in a sampler that included the crispy Salt Pepper Pork, savory Beef Chow Fun, a gentle touch of Tofu, and the punchy Garlic Chicken. Each dish was a testament to the kitchen's prowess—I savored every bite.

Price-wise, the value is undeniable. With strategic buffet plate architecture, a filling meal can prove quite economical—just $7.99 per pound before the afternoon cut-off, and an even more wallet-friendly $4.99 per pound post 1:45 pm. This place is a definite score for anyone looking for quality and value in the FiDi lunch scene.

I want to love this place and it's worth visiting for bites but be mindful on how you order, you get tricked easily on the portion and it gets very expensive at the end.Mostly is skewer based. The waitress would tell you each order is 3 skewer based, do you want to make it 5 (we have 5 ppl). We did it for most items and strongly regretted it.Tea Smoke Salmon Lettuce Cup - skip, fraud as there's no tea Smoked flavor at all, bland chopped up salmon. We added the portion to 5 but honestly we could have stay with just 3 (1 order) and shared.Seared Tuna on Soba - served cold. Again we added to 5 skewer (3 per order) and each skewer came with 2 pieces of tuna. 1 order we could have had enough food for 5 ppl. Feel like being tricked again for mediocre food. Soba was overcooked too soft ad tasted disgusting.***Octopus probably was the only thing on the menu we really really like. Ok I'd say this one is worth make it 1 skewer PP, it's also smaller.Laksa Crab Soup - $9 a cup, so we made it 5 ($45) what a waste of money and calories Water down coconut soup is not called laksa. No crab to be found but bean sprouts. Rolled my eyes.Pork Belly with bun - tough. In fact my friends were making fun that the best thing they had this meal was the bun, how sad.Daikon Fries - interesting but daikon problably not at its best when being fried.Wine we tried were so so. Cocktails are pre made because of the concept.We spent $80 pp at the end, not worth it. Your smart menu tricked us but we will never return.

Title: A Celebratory Feast to Remember at Per Se

Last evening at Per Se was truly a dining delight, beginning with a heartwarming welcome and an enviable seat overlooking Columbus Circle. Celebrating a significant milestone, the staff, with remarkable attention to detail, ensured an unforgettable experience.

Our server Alex's expertise shone through as he navigated me through the tasting menu, pairing a standout herbal gin & tonic with my selections. Kristy, the sommelier, exhibited a keen sense of taste, impeccably choosing both my white and red wines.

The attentiveness of the staff, especially Haq, added to the elegance of the meal. Standouts included a divine tuna tartare, an exceptional fish dish that easily ranks in my top five, and a sublime matcha ice cream.

A tour of the kitchen to personally express my gratitude rounded off the night, cementing Per Se as the go-to destination for any special occasion worth commemorating.
Solid old school Italian joint. All of the classics present and accounted for on the menu.  Baked clams and eggplant parmigiana are good bets.

My sister went here on a random Saturday since we wanted some food and beverages before heading to an event. Here is the break downEnvironmentThey have plenty of tables but they are a little snug next to each other but it manageable as long as your neighboring guest realize you are sitting next to them. Their bathroom is pretty clean and seems to be well kept. Food:This place is a nice clean spot for simple ramen and simple food. The ramen we got was the Miso ramen. If you get an extra noodle and don't mind a lot of broth then it is great to split for 2 people. It wasn't that flavorful. It was a little too salty for my liking but that is personal preference. My sister enjoy the ramen and getting 1 with extra noodles help feed us both. I would only do that if you really want different items within your ramen, don't mind less broth, and don't mind getting extra items to dress your ramen. We got extra nori and I wish it was on the side so it didn't get soggy but o well. For an appetizer, we got Fried chicken tenders and 1 chicken bun. The chicken was nice a crispy but it seems the lack in flavor. It was just fried chicken and the dipping sauce helped but I still felt like I was just eating plain fried chicken. They do give large chicken tender pieces which is great. The chicken bun was not what I expected. I thought it would be more flavorful but it was just a thin slice for fried chicken that wasn't too flavorful. I think the chicken dishes could have used more seasoning overall. The Hello Kitty sangria was okay. It had a nice kick to it but for what it was worth it was small with a lot of ice. I personally usually got another drink but since I didn't think it was worth it, I stuck with my water.Service:Our server was helpful and informative. She help us decide on what to pick. We did have to keep asking for a refill in water but overall it was a nice basic kind of service.Overall:I personally won't be here right away but its not a bad option for a basic ramen/ noodle dish. I wouldn't come for drinks or happy hour. I would not also get to many appetizers. I would say if you want to share ramen it is definitely doable but the extra ramen comes on the side and not within the meal. If you are sharing just let the server know and they can give you an extra bowl to split it.

I heard from people about how I should try this place and that they have one of the best roast pork in all of New York.  I stopped by there yesterday and luckily for me, the line was short enough.  By the time I got to the front of the line, they almost ran out of the chicken.  I only got 1/4 portion of the roast duck, and ordered separately roast pork.  Lastly, I got a roast pork with rice and vegetable for $6.50 ish.  They did give a ton of cooked cabbage so that was good to see.  Roast pork is pretty good and turnover is very quick.  I do like the sweet glaze sauce that came with the roast pork alone portion.  Again, this The menu is very simple, and the owners do speak English.  They do have a huge following so I am sure there are a ton of diehard fans.

I love tapas and used to be much better. The food is salty side. The waiters/bartender I had, were not friendly at all and have an attitude past 3 times I went. So, I don't feel like giving another chance even though I like the food. It's unfortunate...

Title: A Flavorful Feast at a Lively Japanese BBQ Spot

I absolutely adore this restaurant! The extensive menu is impressive, with each item promising a high-quality experience. We savored a variety of meats for the Japanese BBQ, each enhanced by their delectable marinades. The flavors were so inviting that I found myself contemplating a second order. The atmosphere inside is vibrant and roomy, although I suggest timing your visit to avoid the crowds this popular spot no doubt attracts. I wholeheartedly recommend a visit to this gem for anyone in search of a top-notch dining experience.

Title: Breakfast at Hilton’s Herb N’ Kitchen - A Mixed Bag

Review:

I recently had the chance to sample the breakfast buffet at the Hilton's revamped Herb N’ Kitchen and the experience was quite a double-edged sword. On the one hand, the space has been beautifully transformed with a new sit-down dining area; on the other, the price tag of $38 per person felt steep for the value.

Despite the blow to the wallet, the hotel's new "resort" fee does offer a $10 daily credit to the establishment which can accumulate. Utilizing this, my husband and I decided to dive into the breakfast offerings.

The buffet spread itself was extensive, featuring standard items, made-to-order omelets, alongside unique additions like an oriental section, vegan options, and a central island stacked with an eclectic mix. Gluten-free choices were available, as well as more niche items like "sheep" yogurt – which, to my surprise, tasted pretty much like regular yogurt.

A delightful find was the bread pudding, nestled unassumingly near the vegan bok choy and hot oatmeal; it was a standout. Service was spot-on with attentive waiters serving coffee and tea at our table, although juice options were limited and not particularly medication-friendly.

However, the overall food quality didn't rise to meet the expectations set by the price. It was, in essence, a typical hotel breakfast buffet that filled us up but limited our desire to explore other local dining options.

In summary, while the breakfast at Herb N’ Kitchen offers variety and convenience, it's hard to overlook the mediocre quality and the feeling of being overcharged. It's a decent option if you're keen on convenience and find yourself with accumulated resort credit, but I wouldn’t recommend it for those looking for exceptional culinary experiences or value for money.

After hearing rave reviews about this restaurant's burgers, I was compelled to try them out for myself. I opted for the bacon cheeseburger with a side of loaded fries. Although my meal was acceptable, I was underwhelmed by the burger's lack of flavor. The patty, in particular, was notably under-seasoned, and a pinch of salt and pepper might have made a world of difference. In my opinion, the burger was just alright and not quite worthy of the high praise it had been receiving.

Rubirosa is Raymond's favorite pizza place in NYC; it's mine, too, after Marta (which is a bit fancy for pizza but at least there isn't a wait). Unfortunately, we don't come here often enough because he doesn't like waiting. If you don't mind waiting at least an hour, this is one of the best pizzas in the city. The crust is thin and crispy but firm enough to support toppings - Raymond's pizza pet peeve is when the pizza sags or flops under the weight of the toppings - and even the simplest sauces are elevated to new heights. If you're torn between choices, you can get half and half! + Rubirosa - This is the one we always get; it's meaty and so incredibly satisfying and tasty. It's not fancy - just hearty and comforting. Every bite is delicious. You can't go wrong with this. + Tie dye - This is a vodka sauce pizza with swirls of pesto drizzled on; they're not mixed. I really liked this because I got to try both flavors; even though this was vegetarian, it was totally worth the lack of meat. (It also helped that we got it with the Rubirosa, so our meat need was sated). The vodka sauce is so flavorful and amazing - I wish they could combine the vodka sauce with the meat toppings. When we left Rubirosa, we noticed with amusement that every table had either the Rubirosa, the vodka one, or both. If it's your first time, definitely try one of those.

I recently had the pleasure of trying what might just be some of the best tacos in NYC, if not the greatest I've ever tasted in my life. Located in the heart of Chelsea, this restaurant has perfected the taco. The meat was exceptionally juicy and packed with flavor, leaving every bite to be savored. Each element of the taco contributed to an unforgettable taste experience. I'm already planning my next visit for another round of these delectable delights. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a top-notch taco experience.

Title: Hidden Gem in the Bustling NY Streets

Finding this unassuming culinary treasure was a bit of an urban adventure, as we must have nonchalantly strolled by its entrance a handful of times. But persistence paid off at what turned out to be our favorite New York eatery this trip.

The meal kicked off with their dumplings – a steal at $4 and arguably the best we've ever had. Do yourself a favor and order these without a second thought.

We followed up with beef noodles and a peanut-filled pocket of sorts (the name escapes me), with the latter being an interesting try but not to my taste. Now, the beef noodles – they were the star of the show. A simple dish transformed into a mesmerizing experience. The noodles were perfection, and while the beef didn't quite hit the mark for us, the bok choy married beautifully with the noodles.

In conclusion, don't let this spot remain a secret for you. Go, indulge in those noodles, and join the league of those in the know. Your taste buds will thank you.

Came here on a Saturday night using Yelp waitlist. Ended up working out pretty well and got seated within 10 minutes of checking in with the hostess. Ordered the karaage and tonkotsu tsukemen. Karaage was cooked perfectly and crispy and went well with the ponzu. The ramen was pretty salty. I liked having the noodles separate to dip, but I found that I couldn't eat the ramen broth by itself due. Pretty peculiar but still pretty neat that they offer these heating stones that they put in your tsukemen when your broth cools down during your meal.Also a few things about the restaurant itself-- people waiting can order at the bar which may be a bit annoying if you're dining at the bar, as this isn't the type of place I would expect to have someone reach over my shoulder to grab a beer or set their beer down on the counter while I'm eating ramen. Also, sitting at the bar by the door gets really chilly. If only they had one of those pop-up screen doors or have people wait outside, as there is not much room between the front door and the bar.

Title: A Midtown East Gem: Quality Quick Bites

If you find yourself in Midtown East with a growling stomach, the high-quality food truck I frequent is your go-to solution for a scrumptious meal. With a reputation for consistency, I'm usually torn between a chicken or gyro platter—both excellent choices. Today, my taste buds were treated to a delightful chicken Greek salad, a fresh dish adorned with feta, olives, and a grape leaf, crowned with a succulent chicken thigh.

An essential tip: don't pass up their tzatziki sauce. It's a game-changer, elevating any dish you choose and easily ranking as one of the best I've tasted.

Despite the typically long queue, don't be discouraged. The line is a testament to their reputation and is always worth the wait, thanks to the swift and professional service.

Pricing here reflects the quality—you definitely get your money's worth. For those in search of superior lunch options, this food truck is a standout in the Midtown East culinary scene.

My recent visit to Marseille before catching a show was a mixed bag. The highlight was the food; the tuna tartare and escargot were both delectable, although the tartare could use more chips for balance. The complimentary bread, while flavorful, was tougher than I prefer. Service, unfortunately, lagged despite our time constraints, which was a bit of a letdown. Kudos to our server for accommodating our early payment request. Sampling the seafood burger from my friend's plate, I was impressed and am tempted to return for a full entrée experience. Solid fare, but there's room for improvement with the service pace.

Title: Mixed Feelings at East Side Eatery

I recently dined at a popular local spot on the east side, and my experience left me at a crossroads, leaning towards a 2.5 out of 5 rating. On the positive side, the restaurant commendably informed patrons of an impending price hike due to supplier costs with advance signage. The soup from the lunch special was delightful, boasting a savory flavor profile with ample ingredients.

However, the restaurant's pricing felt steep, particularly the steamed shrimp dumplings at $9 for six, which were merely passable and not exceptional enough to justify the cost. My main course, the chicken with black bean sauce, was visually appealing but unfortunately marred by rubbery pieces of chicken that I simply couldn't consume.

Service was intermittent and uncoordinated, leading to over a twenty-minute wait to process my payment. The duration of my visit was disproportionately spent idle rather than enjoying the meal.

In conclusion, I find it more worthwhile to venture a few blocks farther to Flame for quality dim sum that guarantees value for your money, rather than settle for an underwhelming and overpriced experience here.

UNLIMITED FOOD AND DRINKS!!! Hit this place up on cinco de Mayo because how could we resist? There is a two hour limit of course, food was really good! Minus the chicken chiqulies, the chips were very soggy. Overall the experience was great, except service was super slow. I understand it was busy but I shouldn't be waiting 10 minutes to order another drink. This is a timed brunch and I'm trying to get lit! I only had 4 drinks within two hours, any other spot I would of had 8. Move faster please!

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Kips Bay Eatery

My recent dining experience was a visual feast for the eyes – truly Instagram-worthy presentations across the board. The charcuterie board was a standout delight, with a variety that left no room for criticism. The chicken parm sliders were another hit, cozying up nicely with the surprisingly addictive Macchina Mules, of which I could have merrily indulged in a few more.

However, the journey to Kips Bay may not be one I'll eagerly repeat. While most of the meal impressed, the carbonara did stumble with its overly chunky cuts of ham that disrupted what could have been a smooth, indulgent dish. Moreover, the burrata pizza failed to hit the mark – arriving with a disappointing soggy base that did no favors for the oddly cold burrata on top. Definitely an area in need of some culinary fine-tuning.

I'm giving 4 because they left out a lot of items when I ordered online. They also gave me the wrong dressing. Some of which I paid extra for such as chicken and avocado so I was very disappointed. However, I do think that they have good quality ingredients and although their salads aren't that big, it's still filling. The ingredients were definitely flavored well and I actually really enjoyed the turkey meatball, which was very juicy. I would probably order from them again but just hope that in the future, they make sure to add everything in and give me the right ingredients, especially when I paid extra for it.

I truly enjoyed the food. Service was a little slow!  Atmosphere was ok. Sat outside. Ordered Jagerschitzel ... wow. Spatzle, red cabbage...yum. A very nice gravy!  Also ordered sauerkraut and loved it!  Caraway in it was nice and subtle. I could have ate so much more! The menu offerings were traditional and would have like to try more!  They have German beers. Finished with Black Forest cake. Nice traditional style with sour cherries etc. enjoyed it!I would definitely return.

I wasn't a fan of crawfish before Sup Crab, their crawfish are a lot more plump and savory than any I've ever had. They've made me a fan! I am still dreaming of their crispy scallion pancakes dipped into their delicious sweet and tangy soy sauce. The super-group combo boil is great for a group of 4, each bag has lots of plump shrimps and a large buttery crab (if chosen). The potatoes and corn sucked up all the flavorful boil marinade and made the meal complete. I am definitely looking forward to trying the rest of their boil options!

Title: A Safe Haven for Pho Aficionados

My culinary escapades at Vietnamese eateries usually lead me straight to a comforting bowl of pho, which I firmly believe is a dish that never disappoints. The broth is a reliable source of warmth, while the ingredients unfailingly present themselves as fresh and inviting. The mixed proteins offer a delightful variety, making each pho experience a new pleasure.

In a rare twist of habit, I ventured to try a rice dish during my latest visit. While the rice lacked moisture and required liberal applications of sauce and sips of water to reach an enjoyable state, the accompanying tender meat and its savory sauce redeemed the meal to an extent.

Service, though efficient, teeters on the edge of neglect. The staff is swift when present, yet you may find yourself resorting to exaggerated gestures to recapture their attention amidst their oblivious passes.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a reliable spot for pho lovers. One should set expectations accordingly, come for the reliably good food, and enjoy the flavors that never fail to please, but brace for a dining experience that may lack in attentive service.

Title: L'artusi - A Culinary Gem That Truly Shines

From the moment I stepped into L'artusi, I was eager to see if the buzz was justified. Let me assure you, it exceeded expectations. The cuisine is extraordinary, and the service is impeccable. Our server's wine recommendation was a delightful complement to our meal.

We indulged in both a cow's milk cheese and goat’s milk cheese to start—each offering a firm and tasty introduction to the meal ahead. A cautionary note: save room for the main attraction, the pasta. The handmade pastas here are perhaps the finest I've sampled stateside. The spaghetti, simplistic yet bursting with flavor and perfected by a sprinkle of toasted breadcrumbs, was the highlight. Not to be overshadowed, the pici with lamb ragu was equally impressive, boasting a commendable al dente texture without being too heavy.

Even the branzino fillet, elevated by a crisp skin and nestled on a bed of olives, was a near masterpiece, despite the olives' saltiness slightly overshadowing the fish’s delicate flavor.

Dessert was a tight squeeze but worth the effort. The handmade rhubarb pies won my wife's heart, while the salted chocolate cake with caramel popcorn, although decent, failed to dazzle me.

In summary, L'artusi offers an extraordinary dining experience at reasonable prices, with superior service. This establishment is a must-visit for anyone seeking one of NYC's finest meals.

Absolutely gorgeous interior and delicious food. A friend and I ordered the Papaya Salad, Soft Shell Crab Salad, Pad Thai, and Green Curry. All were truly excellent and bursting with flavor. Would definitely recommend this spot for a date or if you have friends/family visiting town.

Very nice spacious restaurant for a more sophisticated korean bbq experience outside of K-town. The regular dinner and the Restaurant Week menu both looked good. Enjoyed a couple of appetizers which were tasty and generous for sharing.
