The crepes were different and interesting Ke Sal Maricrab and leek wrapped in spinach crepes with a light korean mustard sauceCham Chi Hwetuna sashimi with a soy, lime and sesame vinaigrette over crisp asian pearFor the mains, we had:Un Dae Gu Jo Rimblack cod and daikon radish simmered in a sweet and spicy garlic soy reductionKorean BarbecueKal Bi (beef short rib)Each dish stood out- the beef was juicy and mouthwatering (as expected with kalbi)The preparation of the fish was perfect- light and flavorful- the soupy base it sat in was delicious tooDesserts were also good (subtly sweet, light, and fluffy) even though they're not typical Korean desserts but they sure do hit the spotOmija Dragonpuff pastry layered with omija berry mousse, fresh strawberries and vanilla ice cream with raspberry coulisBanana Sabayonsilky banana infused whipped custard with mixed berries and sesame seed dipping cookiesAm looking to return with a larger party to explore the regular a la carte dinner menu

Title: Great Spot for Chinese Cuisine Aficionados, with a Caveat for Non-Pork Eaters

Last night, my friend and I visited a Chinese restaurant that left quite an impression. She proclaimed the fare as the best Chinese food she's ever indulged in, setting the bar quite high. As for myself, not partaking in pork limited my options, but I found solace in a few non-pork dishes.

The kung pao chicken was decent, though it didn't top my chart of favorites. However, the duck wraps were a delight, brimming with freshness, and the scallion pancakes were a true joy to the palate. The restaurant's ambiance only added to the experience – stylishly adorned, spacious, and welcoming to larger parties.

This establishment is a wonderful choice for those who appreciate variety in Chinese cuisine, particularly if sharing is on the menu. Just a heads up for the non-pork eaters: your choices might be slightly constrained, but still satisfying.

Came for the prix fixe lunch. $50 for 3 courses (including dessert). You can pick any 2 savories for 2 of the courses, which was really great value. Decor was really cool... and the restaurant had a very airy feel due to the high ceilings. Food excellent and generous portions -miso cod was possibly the best cod that I've had. The miso complimented the fish really well. And the sauce was delicious. -ordered the cote de beouff burger, which was a special ($4 upcharge). This thing was amazing... really strong taste (since its dry aged for 60 days) so not for everyone.-chocolate cake dessert was also great. Service was excellentWill definitely return

A very small menu but everything we ordered was on point. Fried chicken and the brussel sprouts were my favorite. Actually the beets salad was also really good. The drinks were average. Loved the high ceiling and chic feeling of the place. Perfect date spot and close to all the fun meat packing night life. Service was great

Title: A Delightful Symphony of Flavors at Amorino Gelato

C'est magnifique! It feels almost ironic to kick off the review of an exquisite Italian gelato spot with a French exclamation, but there's no phrase that captures the essence of my experience better. I indulged in the classic-sized Amorino rose gelato, artfully crafted with three delightful flavors, topped with a delicate macaroon - the epitome of gelato perfection.

The presentation was nothing short of stunning; each petal of gelato was a testament to the craftsmanship of Amorino's artisans. The flavors were equally impressive, a harmonious blend that danced on the palate. However, a word to the wise - this masterpiece is ephemeral. The gelato rose is a fleeting beauty, succumbing to the warmth of your hand rather quickly, so savor it with haste.

In the balance of aesthetics and taste, Amorino ticks all the right boxes. A solid 9/10 for me – I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

My first authentic taste of Japanese cuisine and I was not disappointed.  The ambience right from the start was very cool.  The food was incredible.  Watching the chef prepare the food behind me was really fun.  Never thought I would try live sea urchin but I figured if I was ever going to try Uni it would be at an upscale place like this. I would highly recommend this place.

Popped in here a few weeks ago after happy hour at Stout. Normally we go to BCD Tofu House but wanted to try something new. We had no idea that we had to order while waiting on line, but eventually figured it out when the hostess asked us what we wanted. So we went with the default Gopdol Bipimbab. We didn't wait long at all which is a surprise for a Sat night. I thoroughly enjoyed my meal. But when we finished, my friend said, did you notice there was no beef in our bipimbab? I had not noticed because I had mixed everything in and the beef was minced. But after looking at my photos.....it does look like there was really nothing there. Very little. I hope they were not trying to skimp out. I hope that it was just very finely minced beef. Not sure though.......

Title: Vibrant Spot for Happy Hour

My dining companion and I ventured into this bustling eatery on a weeknight to find it teeming with energy – certainly a hotspot for happy hour if you're local. Be warned: a prime-time arrival means a wait for seating, but once settled, the service impressively kept up with the packed house.

We took on the challenge of a sizeable mango margarita pitcher, a decision that made for a fun yet arduous task to finish. Our attentive waitress steered us clear of the less reliable mahi mahi taco, leading us to tasty alternatives; the steak and pulled pork tacos satisfied, accompanied by a modest portion of rice and beans.

The place offers a solid dining experience, but it's the drinks that'll beckon me back. And a note for next visit – the guacamole is on my must-try list.

Tucked away in the heart of the city lies a charming themed restaurant that's perfect for both dining and drinks. From the moment you step in, the attention to detail is striking, complemented by a semi-open kitchen that adds a touch of culinary theatre.

The menu doesn't disappoint, offering unique selections that cater to a variety of tastes. While the bar area is cozy, it feels a bit cramped due to the raised booth seating directly behind. However, the restaurant compensates with ample table seating on the other side, making it an ideal spot for larger gatherings.

Whether you're in for a meal or a casual drink, this spot weaves a delightful ambiance with good food for a memorable experience.

Came here for lunch and ordered the veggie okonomi-yaki. However, I was given the pork one instead. The okonomi-yaki itself was way soggier than expected. Service is friendly and efficient, but not sure I'd be back again.

I felt like have some pizza and my friend recommended me this place. I thought I found other my favorite place for pizza. Food(3/5)-I ordered mushroom with basil tomatoes sauce pizza for delivery. I like this place pizza but not the best. This place pizza was not too big than other places and enough tomatoes sauce and cheese. I didn't request them to extra tomatoes sauce or extra cheese but I thought it better I didn't requested them to that. If you gonna try this place pizza, don't extra sauce or cheese and please extra with any of vegetables or meat. I wish my pizza had more mushroom. Quite little of mushroom than sauce or basil. I got confused I was ordering just cheese pizza with basil. Dough was thin, not oily and very savory but little tough that it was a bit hard to chew. Service(5/5)-I ordered pizza for delivery a lot and I never seen any places gave me plates when they delivered. This place delivery your pizza with plates. It was amazing delivery service which's I never seen it. They delivered my pizza on time. Sometimes other places delivery late and it was just warm but this place wasn't.

Title: Hidden Gem for Post-Work Libations - A Stone's Throw from Grand Central

I finally visited that inconspicuous bar I've walked past countless times and I'm glad I did, despite some caveats. Nestled in an area surprisingly untouched by the tourist shuffle and a short walk from Grand Central, the ambiance strikes a fine balance between dim lighting and an air of sophistication, making it an appealing escape for locals.

The drink selection is both inventive and steep—expect to fork over $17-19 per cocktail, a price that might make even a seasoned Midtown patron blink. However, the Lychee Martini proved the splurge can be worth it, expertly mixed and thoroughly enjoyable.

It's worth noting that this spot seems to attract a boisterous after-work crowd, so conversation can become a bit of an auditory competition pre-dinner hours. As for dining, I had hoped to sample some sushi, only to be informed the chef was abroad - a disappointment, albeit a curious one.

In essence, this bar fits the bill for those seeking a somewhat refined place for after-work drinks or a late-night rendezvous, provided you don't mind a bit of noise or a dent in your wallet. If you're in the area and looking for a place unlikely to be swarmed by out-of-towners, it's certainly worth a shot. Just maybe save your voice-training exercises for another day.

Title: A Mixed First Impression at BONMi

I recently visited BONMi around noon on a quiet Sunday and was pleased to find ample seating and a calm atmosphere, with the option to enjoy the nearby Lincoln Center outdoor benches. The cleanliness of the place and the friendliness of the staff were immediately noticeable.

Venturing beyond my usual banh mi preferences, I tried the BBQ Belly Banh Mi Sandwich. Unfortunately, it didn't quite hit the mark for me. The overcooked baguette was a letdown, and the combination of ingredients failed to deliver the comforting experience I typically seek in a banh mi. The BBQ flavor on the pork belly may have been an adventurous twist, but it somehow didn't mesh well for my palate.

Despite this, BONMi's 'make your own' option gives me hope for a more satisfying meal on my next visit. I'm looking forward to crafting a banh mi that's more aligned with my tastes.

Where do I begin? We had lunch here last Saturday during our visit to NY.. the restaurant is really cute. You enter on the street level but once you are upstairs, it is alot larger and alot nicer than the entry way would indicate.  There is a nice bar and then there are window booth seats for 3 or 6 as well as tables in the middle. The decor reflects the theme with lobster traps and wood. Both the entry level hostess and the hostess that seated us upstairs were awesome. They were warm and friendly and I was immediately glad that I had come. Our server , Walter was also a breath of fresh air. We decided to each get a burger and then share a 1.5lb grilled lobster. It was alot of food. Too much. The burgers were really good. The bun is a little thick and hard so I didnt eat it. The lobster was delicious! The fries , yummy and even though I intended not to eat them, I did.. womp womp.. I think lobster loaded fries would be a great addition to the menu.

Title: A Disappointing Experience Compared to Its LA Counterpart

Having previously dined at the Los Angeles branch, I entered with high expectations for an equally stunning meal. However, my lunch experience was a stark contrast. Props to the courteous hostess who greeted us warmly upon arrival, but sadly, that's where the highlights ended. Service struggled to keep up, particularly our server who became elusive just when we needed assistance. The food, while eagerly anticipated, was a lackluster shadow of my prior experience - lacking the remarkable flavors and textures that once impressed me. The sudden influx of patrons and the arrival of two large birthday groups seemed to overwhelm the staff, leading to an overall underwhelming visit. Regrettably, this location did not live up to the hype and I have no plans to return.

Love the staff, loved the food, loved the blood orange sangria and especially loved the GAMBAS AL AJILLO and the PAELLA!Unless you want to sit at the bar, please make a reservation! I didn't mind, the staff there were very nice and engaging.We started with JAMÓN IBÉRICO DE BELLOTA Spain's most prized ingredient: 1oz hand-carved, acorn-fed "Dehesa Cordobesa" Ibérico ham, aged for 30 months with a side of a staff recommended cheese.The game-changing moment was when received the GAMBAS AL AJILLO )Shrimp, garlic, brandy, and Guindilla pepper in olive oil) and PAELLA DE MARISCOS (Bomba rice, monkfish, sepia, squid, shrimp, clams, mussels, saffron, salsa verse)! I literally had to stop, smile and say how ridiculously tasteful and prefect these dishes are! And let to me tell you that the blood orange sangria did not disappoint, it was one of the best drinks I have had in a very long time. I wanted to have a drink that contain cava and I lucked with this drink! ( it was not sweet) I wrapped up the lunch with freshly made churros stuffed with Nutella! Literally the best lunch I've had in a long time!!

Pretty good dim sum here. There's almost no wait for a Sunday lunch. It's a super small place and they are known for the carrot buns. We ordered a bunch of dim sums to share and to our surprise everything was pretty good! The shumai and shrimp dumplings are delicious. Chicken feet was just ok. Ribs were good and the carrot cake buns are super cute and yummy!! They aren't too sweet so we really liked them. Definitely would recommend this place on a weekend if you hate to wait for hours for dim sum in china town. Don't forget that they do add a mandatory 15 percent on the bill so you don't have to tip.

Title: A Broadway Bite: Singing Servers Delight in NYC

My recent lunch experience in the heart of NYC turned out to be more than just a meal—it was a delightful show! The wait time was a reasonable 30 minutes for a table of three, a minor delay for what awaited us inside.

The diner's menu offered standard fare, but the real treat was the extraordinary talent of the singing servers. Their renditions of classic show tunes were a joy to listen to, creating an ambiance that's hard to find elsewhere.

I indulged in the Mac n Cheese Bites, which were delicious, though they did leave me with that slightly heavy feeling typical of deep-fried treats. However, any minor discomfort was quickly overshadowed by the entertaining performance.

This place offers the rare combination of dining and entertainment, providing a value-packed experience. If you're in for a meal that comes with an enchanting side of live music, this is the place to be.

Title: A Step Back in Time at Delmonico's

Delmonico's impresses with its cool, old-world charm, offering an atmospheric dining experience that my boyfriend and I enjoyed. The service was adequate, and while the food is commendable, it doesn't quite eclipse the top spot for me when compared to Del Frisco's or 4 Charles Prime Rib.

The filet mignon, though slightly on the dry side, was flavorful. However, the heritage pig bolognese didn't live up to expectations, as it was a bit bland despite the perfectly al dente pasta. On the brighter side, the creamed spinach shone brightly, and the Delmonico's potatoes were nothing short of incredible.

The famed Baked Alaska concluded our meal on a high note, meeting my expectations for this classic dessert. All in all, Delmonico's delivers a solid dining experience. It's a classic venue that's definitely worth a visit for those seeking a taste of history.

Title: A Delectable Dive into Korean Cuisine

My daughter and I were treated to an exceptional Korean dining experience today, with flavors that thoroughly impressed even a self-professed "sushi guy" like myself. The culinary journey commenced with her choice of the chewy and savory Dduck Boki, while I delved into the comforting warmth of Sun Gye Tang and the delightful Shumai shrimp dumplings.

The highlight, however, was the indulgence in the premium Gal Bi. Although the beef selections bore premium price tags – the Gal Bi at $42.50 – the joy it brought to my daughter was priceless. The balance of quality and quantity struck a fine line, with decent pours of Malbec to accompany our dishes.

Service was commendable; attentive waitresses were mindful of our needs, ensuring a smooth dining experience. The restaurant's cozy ambiance fills up quickly by 6pm, signaling its popularity, though an upstairs dining area seems to accommodate overflow.

One minor disturbance was the presence of noisy delivery personnel near the entrance, which at times hampered the dining conversation. Yet, this did not detract significantly from the overall pleasure. I'd encourage Korean cuisine enthusiasts to visit this gem if they're in the area and craving a "bite" of Korea.

I recently ventured into Jungro for a KBBQ experience in Midtown and was not disappointed. Utilizing Yelp's waitlist feature at 6:20 PM made the 20-minute wait upon arrival feel seamless. Our choice was the Beef Set Menu, priced at $83.95, which delivered a variety of non-marinated meats such as kalbi, ribeye, skirt steak, and brisket. Each cut was expertly cooked by our server and paired with traditional accompaniments like kimchi, lettuce wraps, and a tantalizing array of sauces.

We also indulged in the seafood pancake, densely packed with oceanic treasures and complemented by a sweet soy sauce, which was a standout. The quality of the beef was undeniable - the highlight of our meal.

However, it's important to note that the pricing leans towards the expensive side. Despite Yelp's $$ rating, I would consider Jungro more of a $$$ establishment, with our total coming to $122 for two people, excluding drinks. At about $60 per person, Jungro is certainly a splurge, but for those in search of premium KBBQ, it might just be worth it.

I came here in the early afternoon on a weekday, and there was a moderate wait.  There's no seating, only room for the food prep station and register.  You can see the roast duck hanging in the window and the red char siu as you wait in a line that stretches out the door.  Don't be intimidated though because the line moves very quickly.  It's CASH ONLY!My mind is completely blown by how cheap this is for the hefty amount of delicious comfort food you get.  I ordered a small roast duck over rice for $5.50.  The staff works at lightening speed: they put a bed of rice in a tin box, place tasty boiled cabbage on top, slice up the juicy roast duck in front of you and pile it on top of the cabbage, then they top it off with a few ladles of delicious sauce the fatty duck was cooked in.  I don't think I can fully articulate how much I LOVE this hole-in-the-wall.  I'm just so glad I can get my fixing of delicious Chinese comfort food for cheap.  This is probably to most mouth-watering fast food meal you could have for the lowest possible price!

Title: Cozy Ambiance with Room for Culinary Improvement at Local Gem

Walking into the small, bustling space of this down-to-earth restaurant, I was struck by the cozy vibe that only amplified as the evening progressed, although a fresh coat of paint and some updates could elevate the atmosphere further.

Service here is a highlight, with the servers exuding warmth and attentiveness. Unfortunately, the food offered a mixed experience. The main courses, while hearty, lacked the depth of authentic Italian seasoning one might expect. The lasagna cried out for the punch of oregano or dry basil, and while the ink pasta was satisfactory, it too was missing a certain je ne sais quoi of flavor.

The caprese salad did not disappoint, showcasing fresh mozzarella, ripe tomatoes, and vibrant basil. Yet, the bread served alongside was unremarkable, arriving lukewarm and forgettable.

As for the grand finale, the dessert did not just deliver but soared. The pistachio and cappuccino crunch gelato were exceptionally delightful, and my cappuccino was robust and velvety, though a biscotti or a piece of chocolate would have made it perfect.

Mera’s Tip: Don't miss out on indulging in some creamy burrata.

In summary, this restaurant is a beloved spot for good reason, but there is untapped potential in the kitchen that, if addressed, could transform the dining experience from okay to outstanding.

Came with a friend for dim sum because he claims this was better than Jing Fong next door, without the wait. I haven't actually been to Jing Fong but this was really good - prawns were fresh, the skin on the dumplings were reasonably thin. Overall, it wasn't as great as the dim sum in Flushing, Queens, but pretty satisfying nonetheless.

Title: Lunar New Year Feast at Uncle Ted's

To ring in the lunar new year, we opted for a taste of modernity at Uncle Ted's Chinese on bustling Bleecker Street. Kicking off the celebration, a Yelp check-in snagged us 5 free spicy pork dumplings—keep an eye on your bill, though, as ours almost included the giveaway. A minor hiccup resolved, but it cost them a star.

Pre-dinner drinks at the bar were a refreshing start; a cucumber cocktail and a lychee tini set the mood. Conveniently, our by-the-window table awaited us post-sip. The food – a dumpling sampler of shrimp, duck, and pork alongside wanton and corn soup, chicken shumai, and deep-fried calamari – made for a light yet satisfying dinner. Every dish arrived promptly.

The restaurant maintains cleanliness, and the service strikes a balance between speed and maintaining food quality. Our experience, minus the billing oversight, suggests a return visit to Uncle Ted's is on the horizon to delve deeper into their menu.

I've been trying to get to Parm for quite some time. Given the current situation, eating at Parm is obviously out of the question. But I made the trek from Hoboken into the city to pickup Parm to-go.The process (through Yelp) was quick and sanitary. Yelp said my order was ready, and upon arrival I still had to wait a few minutes. But other than that, there are no complaints.Got the fried calamari and, of course, the spicy rotini side dish (only $8!!!). Both were delicious. The spicy rotini was super rich, I'm actually glad we only got the side. Would love to get back soon and try the chicken parm and/or chicken parm sub, amongst other things.

I had heard this place was great and finally stopped by for quick lunch of spinach dumplings and jasmine tea. Unique, flavorful, incredibly delicious. I will definitely be back for more. Spice, spice and spice.

Title: A Festive Brunch to Remember at Horchata

My partner and I ventured into Horchata for a bottomless brunch a few days pre-Christmas, and it was an absolute delight. The ambiance buzzed with energy, complemented by an impeccably curated playlist. The brunch spread was simple yet satisfying, featuring guacamole and chips, an entrée of choice, and unlimited drinks – mimosas, sangrias, or beer.

The guacamole was irresistible, setting the bar high for our mains. I indulged in the Huevos Divorciados, a perfect harmony of eggs and chipotle sauce that left me reveling in the essence of Mexican cuisine. And though I began with a mimosa, the red sangria soon won my preference, while my partner’s white sangria was equally commendable.

Horchata nailed every aspect of a joyous brunch, earning a confident recommendation for anyone craving endless Mexican flavors and vibrant brunch vibes.

This place was good! If I was in the area again, I'd stop by. I've had the Greek Wrap and the Beet Salad. The coffee is pretty good here, too.I came here during lunch and there wasn't a crowd at all. I would definitely stop back to try more of their options.

Title: A Mexican Gem Found – Canyon Road Grill

Living in an area where authentic Mexican eateries are a rarity, my discovery of Canyon Road Grill was a delightful surprise. As a student immersed in busy schedules, convenience is key. Thanks to reliable delivery services, the restaurant's offerings landed at my doorstep after an anticipatory wait.

The star of the meal was undoubtedly the enchiladas verdes. An ample stuffing of chicken and a truly spicy green chili fulfilled my intense cravings. Accompanying the dish were crisp chips in a quaint brown paper bag, paired with mild salsa. While the sides were pleasing, it was the enchiladas that stole the show, surpassing my expectations with flying colors.

For anyone in search of quality Mexican cuisine, Canyon Road Grill is a must-try. It's certainly become my go-to for those days when nothing but a good plate of enchiladas will do.

Title: A Surprising Culinary Adventure at a Hidden Gem

Having never heard of this restaurant before, I was intrigued when a friend suggested it for a group dinner. A quick glance at the food photos online had me eager to try at least four dishes. We made a reservation for a weekday evening—a wise move I'd recommend to anyone planning a visit, particularly on busier nights.

Upon arrival, we grappled slightly with finding space for our bulky winter coats due to the closely arranged seating; some wall hangers would be a thoughtful touch. However, any inconvenience was quickly forgotten as our attentive server promptly took our drink orders and I enjoyed a complimentary shot of Soju thanks to my Yelp check-in.

Our party ordered collectively, which turned out to be a delightful decision. The spread included irresistible Truffle Fries, Crispy Chicken Buns with a scrumptious sauce, Crunchy Tofu, Bulgogi Hotstone, Tuna Mayo, savory Wings with soy garlic, and a Fried Tiger Roll. The Hibiscus Lemonade was a refreshing beverage choice, and the surprise complimentary Soju shots were a hit.

Although every dish was enjoyable, by the time we got to the Japchae with Beef and the Bulgogi Hotstone, I found them less memorable, possibly because they were similar to a dish I had eaten the day before or simply because I was quite full from the other delectable offerings.

In conclusion, the restaurant provides a delightful dining experience with a wide variety of flavors that cater to various tastes, complemented by efficient service. A spot definitely worth visiting, and one I'll suggest for future outings.

My husband and I experienced the height of sophistication at The Plaza, indulging in their Champagne high tea. The convenience of a coat check is always a plus, and The Plaza's system is particularly efficient—a small detail that speaks volumes about the establishment's attention to comfort and service.

Upon arrival, we were seated at a prime table with a sweeping view of the establishment, complete with a nearby bar. The service was impeccable and immediate, with our server exuding warmth and professionalism. Although the decision for our high tea selection was predetermined, the menu still managed to tempt.

The atmosphere was impeccable, a blend of elegance and charm, with well-dressed patrons of all ages enjoying the experience. It was especially delightful to watch children marvel at a tea caddy with cotton candy.

As for our high tea, the Veuve Cliquot champagne set the tone for an afternoon of indulgence. Our teas—an Earl Grey and an English Breakfast—were brewed to perfection, accompanied by an array of opulent savories including medium-rare roast beef with horseradish, a decadent lobster roll, and a sublime foie gras with caviar blini.

The finale, a selection of sweets, was nothing short of stunning, though admittedly overwhelming after the delectable scones with clotted cream, blueberry jam, and lemon curd. The Plaza's high tea wasn't just a meal; it was a masterful display of culinary artistry that left us feeling completely pampered. An unforgettable experience that strikes the perfect balance of delicate and satisfying.

Cozy, warm decor and consistent, excellent service is what makes Crispo one of the few mainstays on this forever evolving neighborhood.  Delicious food with only the freshest of ingredients is what makes Crispo a breath of fresh air and an amazing standout that cannot be disputed. From fresh pasta to a seasonal menu, Crispo will blow the tastebuds of the most discerning of palates. But you can only focus on that because the service is top notch so you can really focus on undisturbed conversations with your lovely company whilst feeding your desires, culinary-wise.The place is beyond spotless and the decor reminds me of romance novels where the protagonist feels moved to take a chance on love after just having sworn it off. Fresh florals, linen napkins, wood panels, old carriagehouse in the rear are all around you.  How can life not seem beautiful when all is well?  This place is great for a date night, catching up with friends or for dinner with the most fastidious of your acquaintances. All of this to say the prices are reasonable, the experience worth it and your body will be happy.  Why not take the chance, love?
I like big buns and I can not lie... BBQ Pork Buns that is! Hidden gem of a eatery, little more pricy than your local bun or ramen join but well worth the money!

During my stay at the Belvedere Hotel, I opted to forego the in-house continental breakfast and ventured to the neighboring eatery for both supper and breakfast. I was thoroughly impressed with the quality of the meals. Their pancakes were particularly outstanding – delicious and perfectly portioned for a big day of exploring.

Service was efficient, providing the two cups of coffee essential for my morning start. One minor quibble was the beverage service. Soft drinks are served in cans, presumably to inflate the bill, but I sidestepped this by requesting water. Interestingly, the first glass arrived with ice, but subsequent refills were warm. I couldn't help but wonder if this was a subtle nudge for not buying a soft drink, but it's a mystery that will stay unsolved as my travels won't bring me back to NYC.

One of my top two favorite omakase spots in the city! I've also been to Sushi Zo, but I prefer Hanare because of the intimate setting (the sushi counter seats around 8 max and looks like a fancy hotel's in-suite bar) and the slightly more inventive menu. Each course was so delicious, but my favorites were:- chutoro- torched otoro (obviously)- scallop with finger lime- uni trio (Santa Barbara, Hokkaido, and one other type from a different place in Japan that literally tasted like a subtle peanut butter... we got to choose our favorite and it was served again in the next course with ikura and osetra caviar)- cold-smoked trout (it was smoked in a serving platter right in front of us and the taste was soo delicious and unique - also points for presentation)- torched wagyu with a MOUNTAIN of shaved trufflesWe ended up also ordering an extra piece of torched wagyu but requested to also have uni in it as well, it was AMAZING.The service was also great, and because each party has their own sushi chef, it was a super interactive and involved experience. I cannot wait to return!

Didn't think I would stumble upon a Detroit style Pizza in NYC, but here we were. This place has some really large slices of pizza. The slices you see behind the counter is actually "2 slices". If you get one slice they'll just give you half of it. Explains why the prices are so high. I ordered a full pepperoni and peppers Detroit style and it was slightly spicy. They cut it into 4 pieces so easy to share. Crispy edges and thicker, firmer crust. Overall, solid pizza place if you're looking for something different but I wouldn't go out of my way.

The portions are huuuugee!! So if you're looking for good value, this is the place to go. The food is very average and I cannot say it was my favorite Cuban meal. I had a meal through mealpal and orders the steak, butter rice, and vegetables. The vegetables and rice were slightly oily, but was quite tasty. The steak, although quite large, was super dry and salty.Overall, it seemed like a good atmosphere for quick sit down or a takeout meal. The restaurant is very big, and has sufficient seating. I would warn slightly that your hair and clothes will smell of the restaurant just by being there for around 10 mins.

I got the impossible truffle burger. Overall it was good - good portion for a good price, and the impossible patty def tastes like real patty! Truffle flavor was a bit light. Very very cheesy. Lettuce was a tiny piece, so was the Tomato. Buns were really good though.

Enjoyed dinner here before attending a show at the MET Opera.We ordered a la carte, and went with the special of the day. It was some kind of seafood soup that came with rice. It was a good light meal.For dessert, we had the grapefruit sorbet. Would highly recommend this tart treat. It wasn't too sweet, but it made for the most refreshing end to the meal. The shaved halva on top made it incredibly tasty.

Title: Boozy Brunch Bliss at a Bustling Weekend Spot

If you're plotting a weekend brunch with your crew, this spot should top your list, especially for those who relish the thought of a boozy brunch. With a quaint outdoor section for sunny days and a cozy interior for year-round dining, the atmosphere is welcoming and vibrant.

The dining concept is designed for groups, providing a set menu that includes a choice of 4 appetizers, between 2 entrees or a brunch paella, capped off with a dessert. For $45 per person, the deal sweetens with unlimited drinks over two hours – a surefire recipe for a merry, albeit indulgent, afternoon.

Our experience was further enhanced by our attentive waitress, whose service was the cherry on top of a delightful visit. 

A heads-up for those with mobility issues: bathroom access requires a descent down a flight of stairs as they're located within the hotel this restaurant is connected to. But for the able-bodied, this minor detail shouldn't detract from the joys of indulging at this hotspot. Prepare to leave satiated to the brim and, quite possibly, in high spirits!

Title: A Brunch Worth Every Penny at [Restaurant Name]

My friends and I decided to indulge in a brunch experience at [Restaurant Name], and it did not disappoint. First things first: make sure to reserve your spot because this place is a hit!

We opted for the unlimited mimosa offer with our brunch entrees, which turned out to be a delightful choice. Although the restaurant was bustling and short-staffed, our server was nothing short of a miracle worker. When we requested a pitcher of mimosa to ease her load, she graciously complied, and our glasses were never empty.

For my main course, I savored the salmon eggs benedict perched atop a cornbread base, crowned with avocado and an intriguing potato accompaniment - a harmonious blend of flavors that was absolutely mouthwatering. To add to our feast, we couldn't resist the fresh guacamole and chips, which was a hit with its generous portion and zesty sauce.

The ambiance was perfect for catching up with friends, and the price, at $48 per person (inclusive of tax, tip, and all our indulgences), felt like a steal for the quality and quantity offered.

In summary, [Restaurant Name] is the go-to spot for a brunch that will leave your taste buds and wallet equally happy. Highly recommended!

I ordered delivery from these guys after having walked past them while attending a UES street fair the other week.  I ordered a pastrami and corned beef sandwich that came with your traditional pickles and even a little side of coleslaw that was on the sweeter, yummier side.  With that, I also got a white fish platter, which came with a bagel and your typical accoutrements and surprisingly cream cheese.The order arrived within the delivery window.All in all the sandwich and whitefish salad are what you expect for typical Deli food. Price was average as well.  No complaints here.

Here's a place that's been here forever from what I gather we randomly decided to stop by since we were in the area. We came in & were able to get a table, drinks we all stuck to beer Stella was my choice, great beer can't go wrong. Music wise not bad, the DJ was playing a decent mix of music which had most people out on the dance floor. Very cool looking place the whole cave thing, they have a decent set up with tables & seating not too bad & some open space for dancing. We got our own drinks, bar wise it was quick & decent prices, we enjoyed our time.

I was so excited to go to Ichiran!  I have been to one of their Japanese locations and loved both the food and the experience.  I'm not sure what happened between that location and Ichiran Midtown; if it weren't for the distinct interior, I would've never known they were related.Ichiran is known for their single-stall, anonymous wait staff style.  I wish they had gone all out at this location and had the ordering process done through a machine, like in Japan.  But overall, I really like this style, especially when eating [messy] ramen.Tonkotsu RamenBroth: Not the most flavorful.  Thin.  Never in my life have I done this before, but I had to dump in some $1.50 vinegar to make the broth have some kind of flavor.Noodles: Sticky and over cooked.Chashu: Served cold, on a plate.  I couldn't quite get over the temperature, tbh.Egg [in shell]: Plain (no marinade) and over cooked.  Came with instructions on how to crack/peel it, which was cute and helpful.I do want to acknowledge that, based on the reviews, many other people like Ichiran Midtown.  Sometimes I wish I weren't so picky, so then I could enjoy amazing food all the time.  I also might have been overly harsh given I'd just had some of the best ramen EVER the night before.  Either way, Ichiran Midtown was a big disappointment for me, and I wish I'd had more time in NY to try another option.

Title: Disappointed by Menu Changes at Koreatown Gem

I was disheartened to find that my once-favorite spot in Koreatown has revamped its menu. On my initial visit, I was charmed by the unique ambiance and the array of traditional dishes not commonly found elsewhere. However, the restaurant has shifted to an individualized set menu, deviating from the communal Korean dining experience I cherished.

The new format serves up fixed side dishes with each set, a stark contrast to the shared sides that would typically grace the table. This change was less appealing to me, as I prefer the traditional assortment of sides to complement the meal.

Despite this, I'm relieved to report that the enticing entrees remain on the menu, though not available à la carte. I must give credit where it's due: their tofu stew is exceptional, surpassing the likes of BCD with its flavorsome and healthier take.

In short, while the changes to the menu have subtracted from the authenticity of the experience, there's still culinary delight to be found in their signature entrees.

I came here on a rainy, cold day in May. And having hot pho was perfect. Almost made up for the fact that it was raining and cold in MAY! I had the summer rolls that was fresh. The vietnamese iced tea which tasted like regular tea with ice. The beef pho was tasty. The broth was delicious. I wouldn't say it's the pho I've had but it comes to a close second and did I mention that's it's only $9! And the portions are huge. The waiter was friendly and professional and the ambience was casual and nice. The bathrooms are kinda messy. And the health grade is still pending but I havent got sick and the food was delicious. So it's worth a try.

Came here for restaurant week lunch special with $26 for two courses, choice of first course: Lobster Gazpacho, Calamari Or half dozen oyster; and second course of the original burger, the original lobster roll or the seven samurai roll. The oysters look pretty fresh and good size. The burger is huge; you better come hungry. The lobster roll are great size with a potato brioche bun pocket full of lobster. The calamari was way too salty which is a bit let down. But overall the meal was delicious and the service is great and fast

Jin Ramen offers a satisfactory ramen fix without skyrocketing to culinary stardom. A visit on a weekday night revealed a quiet atmosphere, accented by rustic decor that was immediately welcoming. The Kakuni Ramen's Filipino-style braised pork belly married well with a perfectly togarashi-dusted poached egg, while the Kuro Tonkatsu Ramen, suggested by our helpful waitress, impressed with its rich black garlic oil-infused broth. Side note: the chicken wings were a juicy hit. Their extensive menu promises something for everyone, and the portions won't leave you wanting. Service is swift, staff congenial, and the prices are fair for NYC standards. Worth a return visit.

Shinka won best ramen at Ramen Fest this year for their bone marrow ramen. People are really into scraping the marrow in their broth. I'm not here to review that ramen though, I'm here to spread the gospel of their vegetarian ramen. It's really good.I know ramen is traditionally made with chicken, beef or pork broth and that vegetarian ramen in itself is a deviation from tradition. But I'm surprised by otherwise celebrated restaurants adding a vegetarian option that you can immediately tell was added as an afterthought to appease the non meat eating crowd. Usually the broth lacks umami and the bowl is filled with a strange vegetable medley that doesn't at all add any flavor. So I'm always doubly impressed by deeply flavorful veggie ramen like I had at Shinka.The broth itself is made with soy milk and sesame oil that adds a nice richness to the broth. The noodles here I'm told are vegan, and they tasted even better than the straight noodles included with the bone marrow ramen. The tofu is marinated in spices that give it an almost char sue like flavor and a bamboo shoot is added as a garnish. The manager/chef told me he really wanted to make a dish that vegetarians and meat eaters alike would enjoy and not miss the meat. I think he did a phenomenal job.I also enjoyed a tuna taco and fried oyster appetizer here, but if I return it will only be for the ramen.

Title: A Thai Delight with Ambiance to Match

I recently dined at a Thai restaurant recommended for its beautiful aesthetics and sumptuous cuisine, and it did not disappoint. Upon arrival, the reservation system proved efficient as we were seated without delay. The lunch special, priced between $13-$18, offered a comprehensive selection, including soup, salad, appetizer, and a customizable entrée with a choice of protein.

The Thai ice tea, served in an adorable jug, lived up to its reputation and was a steal for $5. I chose tofu and veggies with Panang curry for my main course. While the curry packed a bit more heat than I prefer, the flavors were on point, and I'll be sure to ask for a milder version next visit.

Service was impeccable; our attentive waiters kept our glasses full and allowed us to linger in conversation without the slightest hint of being rushed. The restaurant's decor, with its enchanting ceiling and thoughtful decorations, creates a romantic atmosphere that has me planning a return visit for date night. In summary, this dining experience was a harmonious blend of delightful food and enchanting ambiance.

Title: Tacos Triumph at No. 1 — A Chelsea Market Must-Visit

At No. 1, the bustling vibe is part of the charm. The promise of its name is fulfilled in every bite, a high claim, but well-deserved. The line may look daunting, but efficiency is key here; ordering at the cashier and then watching your tacos being expertly assembled by the quick-handed staff means you won’t be waiting long.

The viewing experience is a tantalizing precursor to the main event: the tacos. Watching the cheese being generously slathered on the tortillas whets the appetite for what's to come. The marinated pork taco is a standout, with that clever slice of pineapple adding a tangy twist to each mouthful. 

Don't miss the mini salsa bar; it's an excellent sidekick to your tacos with its options of green and red salsa, limes, and fresh pico de gallo.

In an unexpected twist, the quesadilla, while sharing strong visual similarities with the tacos, surprises with its size and a delightful green avocado sauce that I cannot recommend enough.

A slight misstep is their horchata, which disappointingly lacks richness and the kick of cinnamon, falling short of the heights reached by their food.

Located in the heart of the ever-busy Chelsea market, No. 1 is a stop any New York visitor should make. Just a tip: stick to the tacos, and you'll walk away understanding why this place claims the top spot.

I was excited to check out this spot because of all of the great review. Unfortunately i was highly disappointed and won't be back. As soon as we walked in, the hostess was sitting at the bar and told us to just sit anywhere. Not a very warm welcoming. Our actual server was had a terrible attitude and definitely did not seem like she wanted to be at work. It made for a very awkward experience. When we finally got our food it was a underwhelming. She then told us that i was cash only (which is super inconvenient)The french toast was pretty average and was charged $4 for two pieces of turkey bacon. My husband went for the omelette option with grits, turkey bacon and a biscuit. His biscuit was dry and he didn't eat the grits. The only saving grace to this place was the friendly cook that came out towards the end. He greeted us and noticed my husband didn't eat his grits and offered to take it off of the bill. I don't think i will be returning.

I recently picked up an Italian sandwich on a roll through MealPal at this spot and was quite impressed. The sandwich was delicious, and with MealPal, it was an excellent value. Arriving at 11:30 am helped to beat the lunch rush, making for a quick and easy experience. Highly recommend it for a tasty and affordable bite!

Attended a wedding here this past weekend and it was one of my favorite weddings I've been to.  City winery was filled with lights which gave it a very warm, cozy feel on a freezing night.  The servers were the best wedding servers I've ever seen - they were all totally nice and attentive.  The one imperfection was the food.  For a wedding, the food was relatively very good, but as a restaurant it was just okay.  Had a salad and a steak and they were edible but I definitely wouldn't seek out city winery for its food.  I tried a Riesling wine and it was quite good.  Appetizers were decent (especially the sliders which came on a sweet and very good bun), but again, nothing I'd come out of my way for.

The food was awesome. I got the fried chicken sandwich which comes with coleslaw. I couldn't pick between the two sauces spicy or honey chili so they simply gave me both of them in the side. I loved the spicy sauce it slight tangy, sweet, and spicy all at the same time. I also had the potato salad which was different but delicious. It had bacon and cabbage in it. It's not your typical potato salad but you'll like it. Also they let your sample the sides because it was so hard to choose from. The food was filling and I was able to bring some leftover potato salad home.

Fantastic Cajun seafood that just opened near the heart of Columbia university. Came here on a Thursday night at 630pm with reservation. The restaurant was empty so didn't had to wait to sit down and get seated. My party of three each ordered a fisherman's catch which comes with one lb of snow crab legs and 1 lb of headless shrimp. We also got the fried oysters and a side order of lobster tail and mussels within our boil. I ordered my boil with the mighty sauce at spicy level. Boy were the flavors incredible, but the heat was a little too much for me to handle. Fortunately the server was really accommodating and helpful and gladly took my boil back to add more garlic butter just to tone down the spiciness. What a fantastic service.The sauce was some of the best Cajun sauce I've had around in new York! Suggest a medium or mild spice since their spicy level could be overpowering to some people, but the seafood was fresh and one boil was more than enough for one person. The flavors really blend well and the garlic butter really accentuates a lot of the seafood in my boil. My friends in my party also enjoyed their boil. Also was really helpful when they provided the tools to help us eat the snow crab!Fried oysters and Cajun Fries were crispy outside, fluffy inside. They really nailed the texture when it came to our fried foods. A plus service for being so attentive. Constantly had our waters filled, shells taken away, and was super accommodating to our tastes. Thank you!Overall? I'm just so glad that there's more options to eat around Columbia now!

I recently visited a local restaurant where, unfortunately, my dining experience fell short of expectations. What truly stood out, however, was the owner's response to my dissatisfaction. They not only issued a sincere apology but also refunded my meal as a gesture of goodwill. This wasn't just about the financial aspect; the owner's seriousness in addressing the issue and their commitment to quality improvement made a lasting impression. Their promise to enhance the dining experience in the future has certainly caught my attention. I look forward to revisiting and will update with any new developments. Appreciation is due where it's deserved, and this establishment has shown commendable customer service.

Where in Chinatown can you still find a filling meal for under $5? You can still find one at Fried Dumpling located at tiny Mosco Street near the foot of Mott Street. Yes, there are many dumpling stores in Chinatown and they all vary by style and taste, but they all of varying quality. Fried Dumpling is one of the better ones and specializes in what I believe are Southern Chinese dumplings. It also offers fried buns. In my most recent visit, they were out of the buns so I ordered 10 dumplings for $3. A soda was an extra $1.25. The quality of the dumplings is superb. They're on the small side but contain a neutral filling (not soaked in dark soy sauced meat) wrapped inside a delectably thin, doughy wrapper. When you order the fried variety, the crunchiness contrasts so well with the chewiness of the dough. It's almost like eating high quality ramen but in wrapper form. They fry the dumplings till lightly brown.There's a small seating area with stools inside the restaurant. Finally, a tip in coming here is for you to order their bag of 30 frozen dumplings. It's only $6, and they're easy to prepare at home. You can get the taste of Fried Dumpling at home!

Tucked away near the bustling Washington Square Park, this little gem serves up fast, fresh, and utterly delicious fare that hits the spot every time. The staff here couldn't be more welcoming, and their efficiency ensures you're not waiting long for your meal, even during peak hours. It's wise to have your order ready as you approach the counter – the menu board offers a tantalizing selection that might just have you dithering over your choice!

Seating can be a bit of a premium, but the park offers a delightful alternative for al fresco dining, just a stone's throw away. When it comes to value, the platters here don't disappoint, generously portioned and sure to satisfy both your appetite and your wallet.

What really elevates the experience are the thoughtful touches, such as biodegradable plates and beverages sourced from conscientious companies. It's a small but appreciated nod to sustainability that makes dining here feel as good as it tastes. Whether you're a regular or a first-timer, this spot is definitely one to keep on your radar.

I thought the dim sum here was pretty average, but the restaurant was super spacious, so it was the best choice for big groups.Usually there was a long wait, but since the restaurant was so big, it was worth it, I guess.The dim sum dishes were standard with common dishes like different types of dumplings, har gao, chicken feet, etc.

TLDR: The bar is well-hidden but worth the adventure. The vibe is relaxed, calm and chill. The service is hospitable. The small plates come out fast and--if you're like me--you always want to order more. This bar feels humble--and I like that--but it's clearly superior.

Title: An Unforgettable Slice of New York at Bleecker Street Pizza

My New York culinary quest was dominated by one mission: to savor the legendary New York pizza. Amidst a sea of options, Bleecker Street Pizza emerged as the victor in my personal pizza championship. Their cheese reigned supreme in ooey-gooeyness, stretching with every bite, while the slices struck that enviable balance between too thin and too thick – an especially notable feat when it comes to the crust, which can often make or break the pizza experience.

At $10.50 for three slices, the value was undeniable. But it wasn’t just the pizza that was impressive; the speed and efficiency of the service stood out as well. Unlike other places where flies might dance over the display, here the pizza arrived steaming hot, a clear sign it had just kissed the oven goodbye.

No matter how many times I order from chains like Domino's or Pizza Hut, my taste buds ache for the authenticity and sheer deliciousness of Bleecker Street Pizza. Until next time, I’ll be dreaming of that perfect New York slice.

I was a little nervous eating here based on the mixed reviews and I'll be honest our experience started off a little rocky but that changed quickly. We arrived about 9pm on a Monday and were seated immediately. The only complaint I had is we were waiting for a good 20 minutes for someone to come greet us and take our orders. We actually had to ask one of the staff if a waiter was going to come over. After that the staff was very attentive to us for the rest of the evening. My husband and I have never tried oysters before so we decided to give them a try at a restaurant who boasts to having the best. We ordered the summer loves and the malpeques ( I think that's how it was spelled) the waiter suggested those as they don't have too much of a fishy taste. I'm glad we listened to him because they were delicious. We're now oyster fans lol. I ordered a passionate cosmopolitan before the food arrived and it was great. Definitely packed a punch because k felt tipsy after 2! There was a little mixup at the bar and they ended up making another and let me keep it on the house so I ended the night with 3 drinks and feeling really nice. For the main course I ordered the boneless ribeye frites with the black pepper sauce. IT WAS DELICIOUS!! The steak was cooked perfectly and it paired nicely with the sour cream mashed potatoes I ordered. The staff is friendly and attentive I would definitely return.

I'm in love with Koku! This trendy restaurant has great ramen and Katsu sandwiches! I ordered the katsu do set, which comes with purple sweet potato fries. The pork cutlet is paired with jam, which makes for an interesting salty sweet combo! It's definitely a unique sandwich, fried to perfection. The fries are great as well.My friend ordered the Koku Ramen with pork. I sampled a little and loved the flavors of the soup base. I noticed they have great happy hour deals so I will definitely be back to try those!

Title: A Delightful Brunch with a Dash of Disappointment

My girlfriends and I decided to indulge in a brunch session at this charming eatery nestled in a picturesque neighborhood, and what a mixed bag of experiences it unfolded to be! The ambience of the space instantly won us over, and the service staff was commendably attentive and friendly, ensuring our comfort throughout our stay.

We shared the Black & White Banana Monkey Bread, which was a delightful explosion of flavors, and I highly recommend it for the table. The Sheep's Milk Ricotta and Insalata di Rucola were fresh and beautifully seasoned, while the Scampi and Grits were a testament to the chef's ability to create dishes that are as delicious as they are aesthetically pleasing.

However, not all that glitters is gold. The much-hyped Hazelnut-Crusted French Toast fell flat on its promise—literally. At $22, I expected more than the two pieces of dry and bland toast that arrived at my table. The lack of incorporation of the hazelnuts into the toast itself, instead of being mere decoration, was a letdown, especially given the zest it could have added to the dish. Partially drenched in maple syrup, even then, the toast failed to pique my interest beyond a single piece.

To compound our culinary woes, my friend's Uova Modenese was marred by an overzealous sprinkle of salt in the cotechino hash, rendering it difficult to enjoy. A dish that could have been a savory delight instead became a struggle to consume.

All in all, the restaurant is a lovely spot with potential for a fantastic dining experience if you stick with the winners and steer clear of the few pitfalls.

Tucked away in Hell's Kitchen lies a small but vibrant Mexican eatery that instantly lifts your spirits with its fun, festive atmosphere. On a recent visit, I was charmed by the warm welcome from hostess Celia, who not only greeted me at the door but also introduced me to the friendly bartender. As I sipped on an expertly crafted mezcal margarita, I couldn't help but notice the joyous groups of patrons around me.

The owner's personal attention to each customer added a special touch to the experience, something I had not encountered often in NYC or elsewhere. Celia, whom I affectionately dubbed "Auntie Celia," has a unique flair for making guests feel like family. It's clear that this place isn't just about the food—it's about the community it builds.

I left before trying the food, but the inviting service alone is enough to ensure that I'll return for a full meal. This spot is a gem worth revisiting, both for the drinks and the promise of delicious Mexican cuisine.

Title: Great Spot for Happy Hour and Burgers

I celebrated a friend's birthday at this gem last week and had a fabulous experience. A pro tip: aim for happy hour before 8 PM to enjoy the drink specials—they're a steal! After scouring Yelp reviews, I decided on the Cascalote Burger, which was a triumph. It came out medium rare, just as I prefer, and the fries were the perfect crispy accomplice. The burger's cheese could have been more melted, but that was a minor hiccup in an otherwise savory meal.

The reason I'm docking a star is the pricing. The menu leans towards the pricier side, which caught me off guard — I had higher expectations for a more budget-friendly bill. That said, the quality and taste of the food do provide some justification for the costs. Should I find myself nearby again, this place is definitely on my revisit list.

The new Mediterranean spot at Turnstyle food court is a breath of fresh air for those seeking a healthier dining alternative. With a menu boasting classic Mediterranean dishes including succulent chicken, tender lamb, rice platters, and hearty wraps, each made with fresh ingredients, it's hard not to be tempted. Granted, the prices are a tad steeper compared to typical budget eateries, the trade-off for nutritious and swift service is absolutely worth it. If you're looking to sidestep the heft of a Chipotle burrito or a Wendy's burger, this place is your go-to for a satisfying yet light meal. Highly recommended for a quick, delicious lunch!

I recently tried a slice of artichoke pizza from a local spot, and it was nothing short of incredible – truly bomb.com material! Each bite delivered a delightful mix of flavors, and the crust was particularly outstanding. The generous slice size made the $6 price tag well worth it. Plus, the staff's friendliness added to the experience; they even replaced a slice for free when our friend had a minor mishap. Highly recommended for a tasty and satisfying pizza treat!

I love this soba place! First off, you can choose whatever portion of soba noodles u want, small, medium, or large, with the same price. Most items on their menu are pretty affordable already for what they are, which is around $15-$20, so you know that this is a good deal. My favorite from this place is a combo set where you get a rice dish and soba dish together. I got a chicken and egg don with medium cold soba, and my friend got pork cutlet don with medium cold soba. You can change the soba noodles to udon noodles with any soba menu and you can also choose whether you want cold or hot soba! Even though their main is the soba, I love their chicken and egg don! It's soo yummy. Their soba noodles are also tasty with the soy dipping sauce. The ambiance of this place is causal but not too noisy so you can bring pretty much anyone here!

We wanted to try some Korean BBQ and we were right around the corner from here and we decided to give it a go. We came in around 5:30 on a Sunday and the place had maybe two tables with customers. We were a party of 5 and immediately were seated. Drink orders were taken and then we ordered a few apps and some entrees. I wanted to do the BBQ so I ordered shrimp and bulgogi. The food came out FAST!!! Actually too fast.. appetizers and entrees all together.  Too much too soon. We didn't know what to eat first...pot stickers,  fried shrimp,  scallion pancake or the entrees.  I wish they would have spaced out the food.  The BBQ is not for you to personally cook your food. The server comes around and turns it every few minutes. She was rotating between 3 tables. She was not very friendly. I wish I could have cooked my own. In other restaurants you are given slices of bulgogi and you put them on the fire as you want.  Here it's a glob of bulgogi cooked all at once.  There wasn't even room for it on our plates so she put it on the potstickers plate with the paper! I thought the meat was over marinated.  The shrimp had a weird taste to it... like it was dirty.  Bummer...I was really looking forward to cooking my own food and enjoying this experience.  Instead we were rushed and just didn't enjoy it. The appetizers weren't bad.  Potstickers (both beef and vegetable) were smaller than I'm used to but they tasted good. Yelp check in gets you a free small order.  Scallion pancake was decent. Rap music blasted the whole time which also did not make for a relaxing dining experience. No one came to check on us or ask if we were done or wanted dessert or anything else.  Ironically,  we had to wait and wait to get the check.  After flagging someone down our server finally brought us the bill.  Disappointing all around.  I'm sure there's a lot better... Koreatown being right there and all.

Simply excellent! Excellent service, very authentic food, what more can I ask for! We started with eggplant salad first that can with warm bread and olive oil as well. Then we got the lamb chops and manti which were both excellent! Lamp chops had the super authentic and delicious taste that came with a salad and rice. Manti had the perfect amount of garlic and spice on it. For dessert, we got kunefe, the baklava special and kazandibi. Kazandibi wasn't amazing but we were blown away by especially the baklava special. This will definitely be our regular place to go for Turkish food and are so happy we tried it out! They also deliver on Seamless which we have ordered from. Manti is a must to get!! Highly highly recommend!

I was worried this place would be over hyped since it has been getting a lot of attention but WOW...10000% worth it! The food was delicious! My boyfriend and I both ordered the burgers with bacon and they were amazing. We shared the potato hash as well. We were both in major burger comas after. They switch the menu at 3pm from brunch to dinner so be wary of that depending what you are looking for.The vibes inside were on point! Great decorations, music and staff was very friendly as well. Definitely one of the trendier restaurants I've been to lately. It has a great coffee bar that you can order while you are waiting as well.I agree that it is definitely on the pricey side for a burger in NYC but it was well worth it in my opinion. Would definitely come back but for a special occasion. The only downside is how hard it is to get in. I made a reservation an entire week in advance for a Sunday afternoon. We had no issues at all but if you want to do something around dinner time - it is walk ins only and I heard the wait can be quite long so be prepared for that.

Wow, wow, wow. Probably top 3 best restaurants I have ever been to. The drinks, Devine , the food, outstanding. They start the table off with warmBread paired with your choice of butter, anchovies, and a paste similar to foie gras covered in everything bagel spices. To begin our three course meal we chose escargot and lobster for our appetizers. The best escargot and lobster I have ever had, hands down. The lobster was cooked to perfection in a way I have never seen before and was paired with the most perfectly mashed potatoes I have ever had. For our main course we chose the wagyu and the sea scallops. Both were incredible dishes but I would have to say the wagyu dish was my favorite. The Brussels sprouts and shallot paired perfectly with the filet. Last but not least we ordered the two chocolate desserts, the soufflé being my personal favorite. Everything was served promptly, but didn't interfere with the previous course. The cocktails including the Manhatta and the lemon drink were incredible. Our water glass was never empty. Outstanding. I would give this place 10/5 stars if possible.Oh and let's not forget that breathtaking view! One of the best in the city!

Title: A Tasty Treat With a Side of Savings

I recently dined at a popular spot that's buzzing with patrons eager to dive into their Brunch special – a hearty entree with three drinks for just $28. But what sweetened the deal even further was a tempting Yelp offer of 10% off the entire order.

The menu did not disappoint. I indulged in the Chicken Kale Caesar salad and the Avocado Smash, both of which were as delicious as they were satisfying. However, the coffee selection was somewhat uninspiring, boiling down to standard ground or iced options.

The ambiance was slightly marred by the seating arrangements; the high chairs paired with elevated tables were on the narrow side and, in my experience, unstable. A wobbly seat can take away from the enjoyment of any meal. Additionally, the restroom facilities could benefit from a bit of expansion, as the current setup feels quite cramped.

On the upside, the service shone brightly. The staff was accommodating, allowing me to be seated ahead of my party's full arrival, which added a layer of convenience to the experience.

All said, for fantastic food and excellent service, this place hits the mark, even if some aspects of the physical space could use a touch-up.

I stumbled upon Saigon Market quite by chance while en route to my hotel, and it proved to be a delightful find. The restaurant, a shimmering gem amidst the village, welcomed my colleague and me with immediate seating within its spacious interior.

The highlight of my visit was the veggie dumplings—nostalgically reminiscent of a long-lost Vietnamese spot uptown, Saigon Market nearly matched those cherished flavors. Opting for a light meal, we indulged in appetizers: a personal serving of dumplings for me, beef satay for my colleague, and a shared assortment of veggie, shrimp, and chicken dumplings. A bowl of aromatic sticky rice cooked in coconut milk rounded out our feast.

The service was brisk and unobtrusive, the prices fair. My experience was delightful enough to guarantee a return visit. Highly recommended for anyone craving Vietnamese delicacies in a comfortable setting.

Sup Crab located in Chinatown was simply amazing with a fantastic service. I have to shout out the staff that works there because they were very attentive to our needs. The restaurant really caught my attention because of the nice décor which made the overall look of the restaurant very trendy. When I went it was just a party of two; my friend and I. However, from what I observed, there were a couple of big parties which comes to show this place is great for big parties and birthday celebrations. Now lets talk about food: for appetizer I has the fried Calamari with a delicious chili sauce. This fried calamari was one of the best calamari's I had. Whatever bread they use to fried the calamari with is delicious. My friends had the 6 oysters and she really enjoyed them. For entrée I ordered the fried diced chicken with spicy chili which gave it a spicy kick to it. The portion was more than generous and great for sharing. My friend had the crawfish and shrimp combo with potato and corn. Overall, here you will get your money's worth!

I came here for lunch and got their sushi lunch set (7 pieces with a half roll for $38) and their tuna sampler (3 kinds of tuna nigiri, 2 pieces each, and a maki roll) for $60. The rice was kind of gummy, especially in the rolls, and somewhat bland. The rice could also have been a little warmer. The tuna sampler was a disappointment - the otoro was not even that fatty, in my opinion. The tuna pieces in general also had a strong fishy taste.I did like the hand towel service and that they refilled my buckwheat tea for free though. Otherwise I don't really know why this place has one Michelin star. For the quality of the sushi, I think Sushi Yasaka on the Upper West Side is similar at a slightly lower price. Of course, 15 East has a slightly fancier atmosphere in a more central location but I don't think I'd be coming back when I can go to Sugarfish nearby.

Title: A Birthday Brunch to Remember

My group of 8 chose this spot for a birthday celebration on a Sunday afternoon, and the experience was nothing short of delightful. The staff set the tone with their friendly approach, attentively ensuring our satisfaction throughout the meal.

Kicking off the feast, we ordered two servings of Shrimp Empanadas, which arrived perfectly crispy, accompanied by a delicious (and sneakily spicy!) dipping sauce that tantalized our taste buds.

The star of the show, however, was the Cuban Eggs Benedict. The dish was a marvel of brunch perfection; poached eggs achieved an ideal runniness, complemented by the melt-in-your-mouth tenderness of the pulled pork. Drizzled with a silky hollandaise sauce, each bite was a harmonious blend of flavor and texture. A refreshing salad on the side provided a crisp counterpoint to the rich entrée.

In summary, the dishes shone as brightly as the service, culminating in a very well-rounded and memorable birthday meal. Highly recommended for anyone seeking a superbly balanced brunch!

These Tso Tswag chicken nuggets are the best nuggets ever! Goes perfect with their "crispy af fries".  The restaurant is a small cozy spot, theyre usually playing hip hop and rap throughout the day. They have a clear store front, cool for people-watching. The staff is usually laid back and cool. If you have the chance, go try these nuggets!

Title: A Scintillating Lunch Overlooking the Ice at The Sea Grill

On a bustling Saturday afternoon, December 29th, my companion and I were serendipitously seated without delay at The Sea Grill, even sans reservation. Our table boasted a charming view of the Rockefeller Center skating rink, adding a touch of whimsy to our lunch as we observed skaters ranging from the graceful to the selfie-obsessed, and even witnessed the romance of a successful marriage proposal on the ice.

The culinary journey commenced with complimentary bread, which was nothing short of phenomenal. Opting for the three-course lunch menu at $80 per person, we started with appetizers: a shrimp roll and a vibrant squash salad, each earning high praise for their flavor and presentation.

Then came the moment of truth – the entrées. Heeding our server's recommendation, I indulged in the bay scallops, which lived up to their reputation as a Sea Grill highlight, proving to be fabulously delicious. My friend's lobster roll with chips was equally impressive, confirmed by the delectable bite I managed to steal.

Dessert presented a slightly mixed experience. The Keylime pie itself was acceptable, not extraordinary, but the accompanying Angostura Bitters sauce was a delightful surprise and elevated the final course with its distinctive flavor.

Throughout our meal, the staff at The Sea Grill were commendable, contributing to an overall excellent dining experience that I would readily recommend. From the magical setting to most of the exquisite dishes, The Sea Grill is a gem that warrants a return visit.

Title: A Blossoming Dining Experience at [Restaurant Name]

From the moment my friends and I entered [Restaurant Name] post-church, we were enchanted by its lush interior. Pink and white flowers were in bloom around us, complemented by stunning crystal chandeliers and gold mirrors, all contributing to a tranquil atmosphere that was as soothing as it was elegant.

Despite not having reservations, the staff accommodated us promptly, and we dove into their lunch special – an absolute steal at $12 for an appetizer, entree, and drink. My friend and I shared the grilled salmon rad prink, shrimp pad thai, chicken dumplings, and a house salad. We washed it all down with Thai iced tea and coffee, both delightful in their own right, the iced tea standing out for its creamy sweetness.

While the salad was pretty standard, the peanut dressing added a welcomed zesty kick. The chicken dumplings were a flavorful highlight with great texture. However, the salmon was the star entree; perfectly grilled with a sweet and spicy sauce that was more sweet than spicy, enhancing the flaky fish. The accompanying vegetables were fresh and added a satisfying crunch. The shrimp pad thai, although could have used a few more shrimp, was quite flavorful with well-cooked noodles and plenty of peanuts.

Service was on point – the waitstaff were friendly and attentive, making sure our dining experience was comfortable and enjoyable. I'm already looking forward to my next visit to [Restaurant Name] to explore more of their offerings.

At this point, I've come here at least 738262 times for one reason only - the prosciutto & arugula pizza. It's *always* made to perfection. The prosciutto, which isn't too salty, pairs perfectly with the arugula, cherry tomatoes, buffalo mozzarella and huge chunks of grana padano. SO GOOD. I get this every time I come here - whether with friends or on a date.If I'm in the mood to switch things up, I'll order one of their pastas which, thus far, have been quite tasty. I've gotten the pappardelle bolognese and rigatoni alla norcina but would probably choose the bolognese over the rigatoni (the rigatoni was a little too salty for me). This is also a cute spot for any occasion - brunch with friends (they have a nice seating area in the back with a skylight) or an intimate dinner date. Definitely check this place out!!

We had a great time! Good restaurant with a 360 degree view of downtown NYC and Time Square. They have a prix fixe menu but the choices are pretty solid an delicious. The appetizers were delicious, we had the lobster and pate. The main courses were yummy as well as the desserts. The only complaint we have is the service...our waitress kept forgetting us, which may have been because we were in the corner, but still. Had to wait a while to get the menus, and took forever on the bill...and she almost didn't even bring it to us, telling us thank you and good night before we even paid. I'd say it's worth at least a one time visit, especially if it's your first time in the Big Apple.

Huge portions of solid Thai food in the Murray Hill area. I was craving Khao Soi (northern Thailand noodle dish) and BKK Eatery was the only one in the area that served it. There was a generous portion of shrimp (worth the additional cost to avoid sad strips of white meat chicken) which were all plump and perfectly cooked. My fiancé's order of Pad Thai was also pretty tasty (although super basic).This isn't jaw-dropping cuisine by any means, but definitely a great go-to when a Thai craving hits and you find yourself within the area. The restaurant was pretty empty during Sunday service, but the kitchen seemed to be doing well with deliveries.Service was friendly and efficient.

I recently ventured to this restaurant on a quest to expand my curry experiences, this time aiming to conquer a Korean style curry. Opting for what seemed a safe bet, katsu style chicken curry with a bold choice of level 2 spice, I found myself comparing it to its Japanese counterparts.

The verdict? The chicken's texture was commendably crispy and the rice pleasantly al dente, although the spice leaned more towards sheer heat than complex flavors. As someone who cherishes spice that tantalizes the palate rather than overwhelms it, this was a bit of a letdown, albeit expected.

Despite the aggressive heat, the chicken did not disappoint and single-handedly preserved the restaurant's five-star status in my book. It was non-greasy, delightfully crispy, and packed with flavor.

Curry aficionados should definitely give this place a go. If your spice tolerance is more conservative, consider starting with the milder option. Overall, a solid choice for quality meat in a curry.

Loved the burger...it lives up to the hype. The patties are juicy and flavorful, the sauce is awesome, and the pretzel bun is probably the best I've had! I didn't get the fries (the burger was pretty filling) so I can't speak to them. The wait was about 30 minutes to sit at the bar.

Title: A Fresh Slurp of Tradition at the New Ramen Spot

I recently visited a new ramen restaurant that took the place of a former favorite. The ambiance has shifted to a brighter setting, a contrast to the previous dim atmosphere, with fewer speakers lining the walls. The menu is concise but adequate, offering seven types of ramen priced between $13 and $19, plus extra toppings at fair prices.

I opted for the miso ramen. Sadly, it was missing the egg, but the broth did not disappoint—it was thick, rich, and brimming with flavor. While the pork was somewhat tougher than I prefer, it was commendably lean. For those with dietary restrictions, they offer no pork and vegetarian ramen options.

Although there’s no dessert to finish the meal, the experience was sweetened by the warm and inviting staff. Note: This place is cash-only, so come prepared. Interestingly, they sell specialty pomades targeted at those with thick Asian hair. My friend purchased one for $20, and upon trying it, was pleased with the strong hold and non-crispy feel—no hairspray needed.

In summary, this place is worth a visit for its delicious ramen and the unique addition of hair care products.
