Convenient, no frills meal.  Inexpensive options.  Average taste.If you want some quick Vietnamese food without spending too much, The Pho 5, 6 and 7 are all acceptable eateries positioned near the population centers across Midtown Manhattan.Pho 7 is next to hotel Pod Times Square.Pho 6 is on 51st and Third Avenue next to hotel Pod 51.Pho 5 is on 39th and Third Avenue next to Pod 39.The banh mi is delicious and filling.  If not too hungry, it can easily be shared between 2.  I recommend the combination banh mi that includes cha lua Vietnamese spam, Vietnamese pork salami, and pork liver pate with assorted pickled vegetables.  At $8 it is an incredible value.Sadly, I dislike the rest of the items on the menu.  I have tried the Pho (~$11) which ranks below other Pho restaurants in Manhattan and elsewhere.  It's passable if you really want some noodle soup though.  And the portions are big.  And finally the rice plates (~$10), of which I have included the catfish rice plate below, are similarly lacking taste.  It's very plain.  A scoop of rice, conservative slices of cucumber and tomato, and your protein of choice.  The protein is dry, and your only hope is smothering it in sriracha to save it.As for service, I've had excellent encounters at all three locations.  Staff are attentive, friendly and professional.  The same cannot be said for other restaurants in Manhattan where many servers seemlike they have better things to do than to work hard and make the customer feel welcome.I will continue to eat here on days when other restaurants have closed for the night, or when I do not feel like traveling too far from the hotels for a meal.

I recently visited a local eatery renowned for its gyros and found my experience to be quite pleasant. The gyro I ordered was tasty, although not the best I've ever savored, it was still a solid choice. It came uniquely served in a sliced-open pita rather than the traditional roll, which was an interesting twist. The meat was well-prepared, with just enough seasoning to not overpower the flavors. The tzatziki sauce accompanying the dish deserves a special mention for its creamy and refreshing taste that complemented the gyro beautifully.

The side of fries was fairly standard—nothing to write home about, but a decent accompaniment to the main dish. As for the ambiance, the restaurant was kept clean which always enhances the dining experience. The staff deserves applause; their service was both efficient and imbued with a friendliness that made the meal all the more enjoyable.

In summary, this restaurant is a good pit-stop for anyone craving a gyro with a homey touch in service and environment.

Restaurant Review:

Food: The tacos at this Chelsea Market gem are consistently delightful. Expertly cooked meats are perfectly balanced with fresh veggies, creamy guacamole, and a zesty hint of lime. A must-try for any visitor in the area.

Price: For the bustling New York scene, the tacos are reasonably priced. While not overly large, their affordability makes it easy to indulge in a few without breaking the bank.

Service: Ordering is simple and quick at the counter, followed by a numbered system for taco customization. Despite the inevitable line, the process is efficient and doesn't hinder the overall experience.

Environment: It's a popular spot, often crowded, with limited seating. Most of the time, I end up enjoying my tacos while exploring the vibrant surroundings of Chelsea.

Overall: An excellent choice for a casual and tasty bite. The quality and price point make it worth visiting when you're in the area.

Title: Unremarkable Dumpling Experience

I recently visited a local dumpling shop that failed to leave a strong impression. The menu, lacking in variety, offers few choices which translates to a rather restricted dining experience. I opted for the 50/50 order, sampling both the Mimi Cheng's and the Mighty Veggie dumplings. Between the two, the Mighty Veggie was preferable, though both varieties bordered on the realm of the mundane.

The establishment's touted special sauce, seemingly a point of pride, turned out to be a basic spicy condiment that contributed little to enhance the dumplings' flavor. While there's a chance the other location might elevate the dining experience, my time here was uneventful and, frankly, unimpressive.

Been on my list for a long time - if you come at prime hours, the line is always so long, and I always end up at one of the other excellent establishments around this overlooked corner of the Lower East Side.But I finally ended up here for a quick drink and snack at 5:30 on a Thursday. We each had a bottle of the aromatic Greek wit beer, which I would certainly order again.We shared two appetizers: the spanakopita and the fries with feta and egg. Both portions were very generous given the prices and location. The feta of the spanakopita was a bit more tart than some versions I have had, but overall a good pastry. The fries with feta and egg were very tasty, but this dish felt like something I'd relish a bit more after a few drinks.

Title: Step into Old Shanghai at China Blue in NYC

Nestled in Tribeca, just west of the bustling Chinatown lies China Blue, a gem for those yearning for an authentic slice of Shanghai. As I stepped through its doors, I was immediately transported back to the atmospheric 1920s Peace Hotel-era Shanghai, reminiscent of my days living on the historic Julu Lu.

The ambiance is a tasteful homage to the opulence of a bygone era, with an attention to detail that sets the stage for an immersive dining experience. Unlike the typical Chinatown eateries, China Blue elevates the culinary scene with its authentic and modern Chinese cuisine, striking a perfect balance between nostalgia and contemporary flair.

China Blue isn't just a meal; it's a journey to the heart of Shanghai without the need for a passport. Whether you're a former resident like myself or a curious foodie, China Blue promises a delightful and authentic escape right in the heart of NYC.

This is a really tough review to write, since I'm really not a 'complainer': I ordered a drink which I immediately cancelled; it came after a LONG hiatus, after having ordered a different drink altogether, which also came after a hugely long hiatus. There seem to be too many servers not communicating with each other, as this was on my check at the end. The server was also very impatient, as I was waiting for a friend who hadn't arrived yet, and she was acting as though I should place my entire order immediately.The pizzas seem REALLY inconsistent. The toppings were very haphazard- we ordered our pies based on what we saw next to us. Ours barely had any toppings on them. I'm loathe to try this place again due to the above. Pizzas were ok and almost burnt/crispy. We also had to rearrange the toppings since we were sharing slices. Half of them were falling off the side.At the end, I'd asked for a piece of foil for my leftovers. After affirming twice, it came out in a paper bag with a halved paper plate, causing oil to leak out all over it by the time I got to where I was going.  Ugh.
Ended up stopping in here after my little cousin finish auditioning for LG high school. The menu was just limited not alot of options and the price was a bit pricey.

This place is such a treat! If you're sick of eating American or Italian... You definitely need to give Ethiopian food a try! The owners are so very nice. They have a wine selection from Ethiopia which really intrigued me as I have lived in France. We ordered the sambusa which was OK but don't fill up on appetizers... definitely get one of their meats or vegetables on the fermented bread. If I go back I will be only ordering vegetables because they were so delicious. I also remember liking the minced lamb in the lighter green sauce (in pictures). The food was so flavorful... It makes me want to become a vegetarian because if vegetables can be seasoned that well as well as lentils... Why not switch over?All in all: I give this restaurant a five out of five!!! I definitely will be back... This is a great restaurant for a Sunday afternoon when you just like to eat some nice comfort food and enjoy a quiet and cozy restaurant in Harlem

I have to say this place is an absolute blast. The drinks are strong and delicious, the prices are reasonable, the vibe is fun and free, and the service is on point. I've never been to a place where regulars know each other and will swing by just to chat. It was my first time coming and people were so open and welcoming. It was so diverse and laid back. I had two of the Henny Coladas which is now officially my favorite drink. I didn't grab food when I came, but I'll be sure to come back and do so. We came on a Saturday afternoon, but I also hear the Sunday morning/afternoon crowd is just as fun, if not more fun. I'll definitely be returning and seeing what else this cool spot has to offer.

After some curiosity around the impossible burger, I finally gave it a shot at a local spot renowned for having it on the menu. Unfortunately, my experience was underwhelming. The burger, priced at $13, was notably dry, leaving me to question whether the fault lay in the meatless patty itself or the preparation by Umami's kitchen. Additionally, the cheese on the burger was hardly melted, detracting further from the overall enjoyment. Given the lackluster experience at this price point, I'm disinclined to give it another try.

Walked pass this place several times, and it's usually packed. A sign of a good restaurant..Finally had the chance to experience this restaurant.The beauty of coming on Wednesday night, 9.30 pm is, so easy to get seat, i even could choose the table.They have outside seats, which is nice and relaxing ambience.The only cocktail they have is margarita, and choices of Tequile. However they have maybe 8 flavours of margarita, and 4 frozen margarita.We ordered spicy watermelon and spicy margarita,Watermelon was tasty.Food wise, also was good, its just taking a while to be served, probably cause we ordered salmon. That's fine, not going to complain about everything like some new yorkers.Service was good. Would love to come back..

Stopped by here before catching a bus back to NJFood: I got a Rotisserie Chicken Tinga and Beef Short Rib taco. The order also came with some lime wedges and some sauce. I enjoyed both tacos, though I would say the Beef Short Rib was my preferred one since I felt it had more flavor to it. Service/Environment: The service was pretty friendly and decently quick. The restaurant is located in a food court next to MSG, which makes for a convenient eat if you're going to the venue for any events.Price: The tacos were $4 and $5, which isn't too bad in my opinion.Overall: Pretty tasty tacos! If you stop by this food court, Taco Dumbo is a solid choice.

The highlight of the visit is certainly the duck. Definitely get one for the table. I could finish one with my wife if that's all we ate, but it is best for 3-6 people. The rest of their dishes are nice, but nothing extremely unique special. The BYOB plus the duck makes this restaurant great. We will be back often.

I came here with my girls for their bottomless brunch and I had a great time! They have a great deal of daily 1.5 hour for $23 Mimosa (Peach, Pomegranate, Passion Fruit, and Pineapple) or $27 Sangria (White or Red). The drinks were flowing and the staff was every attentive and made sure to top us off anytime they walked pass our table. The drinks were definitely worth it.     The restaurant was small and intimate and had great open lighting. I personally thought the brunch entree I chose was average, nothing amazing but still good. I had the Mezetto Breakfast, which was very healthy and I appreciated that a lot for a breakfast. It had no meat and the protein were the eggs. We had the croquette and mushroom pizza starters as well, and thought it was delicious. The alveoli on the croquette was very flavorful.      I would definitely come back for the bottomless deal and great atmosphere!

I recently visited a spacious and welcoming ramen shop in the city, distinguishing itself in a crowd of competitors. We arrived early on a Friday evening, noting the crowd swell as we dined.

We began with chicken karaage, which bore more resemblance to crispy popcorn chicken than traditional Japanese fare. Paired with a notably spicy mayo, this was a delightful twist. Shishito peppers followed, meeting expectations for enthusiasts of the dish.

Opting for the miso ramen with pork, I was presented with a choice between loin and belly—opting for the former. The pork was expertly sliced thin, enhancing the already rich soup base. A side of beef tongue proved to be too salty for my taste.

My companion chose the tonkotsu with pork loin and an addition of duck, the latter being a standout feature of his meal with its delicate, thin slices.

While the noodles were on the thinner side and commendably prepared, a firmer texture would have been preferred. Nonetheless, this ramen shop is certainly worth a visit for those in the area.

Title: A Decadent Omakase Dream at Chef Don Pham's Sushi Haven

Review:

From the moment my fiancé and I reserved our counter seats via Resy for an exquisite birthday celebration, we knew we were in for a treat, but Chef Don Pham's omakase experience at his NYC sushi sanctuary surpassed every expectation we had.

Opting for the most indulgent omakase menu at $155 (there are also $85 and $125 options available), we were presented with a parade of luxurious delights. Each piece of sushi was a meticulously crafted masterpiece, far exceeding the standard single slice of fish we've come to expect from traditional omakase.

Chef Pham himself, a virtuoso of the sushi craft, personally served us, turning our evening into a showcase of culinary excellence. The highlights of our meal were nothing short of gastronomic bliss — a towering indulgence of ikura, uni, osetra caviar, and truffles atop a delicate piece of bread; the divine pairing of torched otoro and chutoro, both elevated by the briny pop of osetra caviar; and the pièce de résistance, seared wagyu and foie gras crowned with a revolutionary wagyu fat powder that melted on the tongue.

This establishment is a must-visit for anyone with a penchant for uni, truffles, wagyu, otoro, and caviar. The value for the quality and creativity is unmatched. While the sheer opulence of the ingredients might not be for everyone, for those who revel in such culinary luxuries, booking a seat at Chef Don Pham's omakase table is essential. Prepare to be dazzled by what I can only describe as one of the most memorable dining experiences of a lifetime.

Title: A Spicy Delight and Perfectly Cooked Dishes at [Restaurant Name]

Upon my latest visit to [Restaurant Name], I was once again reminded of why this gem never disappoints. The highlight of my meal, without a doubt, was the Papaya Salad - a dish I insist on having Thai style, with an extra kick of heat. It was, as usual, mouthwateringly spicy and delicious.

The Tamarind Duck was a savory sensation, perfectly cooked and seasoned to delight the palate. As for the Basil Salmon, it was an absolute masterpiece with those crispy basil leaves adding a touch of genius to the flawlessly cooked fish.

Not one to ignore the classics, I also indulged in the Drunken Noodles with shrimp, which struck a fantastic balance of flavor without being overly saucy. The Chicken Pad Thai followed suit, impressing me with its tasty profile.

Starting things off with appetizers, the Chicken Satay was very good, shining especially bright with a peanut sauce that was the ideal complement. And the Chicken Wings? They are a must-try item. Packed with flavor, they're an unmissable treat.

From start to finish, the service was impeccable, making the dining experience at [Restaurant Name] as superb as the food. I left with my cravings satisfied and my taste buds tingling. Can't wait to return!

I recently dined at this wonderful spot that truly impressed me with its delicious offerings. The soup base is exceptional, laying a flavorful foundation for a variety of dishes. Moreover, diners can enjoy the perk of adding extra noodles at no additional cost, which is a pleasant bonus for noodle lovers. A must-try is their appetizer selection; it's clear that the kitchen puts a lot of thought into their starters. An added convenience is the restaurant's 24-hour operation, making it a top choice for satisfying those late-night cravings. Highly recommended!

Sup Crab is a fusion place for Chinese style Cajun seafood and Szechuan food. Their food was delicious with reasonable portion and price. We highly recommend to order the fried eggplant with salted egg yolk sauce which was amazingly great with soft texture inside and salted egg flavored. However, we won't plan to visit again due to dishonest (exaggerated) street sign outside the restaurant and their service. We visited because we saw the street sign showed " Special group combo $99: for 2-4 people". We came as a group with 4 people but when we ordered the waiter told us it is only for group 2 and it showed special combo $99 for 2-3 people on the menu. We thought it was kind of a lie for us but we still tried other Szechuan food dishes. When we ordered, the waiter keep asking us again and again to order their clam which was their best selling item but with "SP price" even we refused directly couple times.

Tucked away in the plaza hotel's bustling food court, this charming little eatery was a delightful find, mere steps from my accommodations. Its popularity was immediately apparent, judging by the formidable queue hinting at a loyal patronage built over time.

I opted for a crab roll, while my companion indulged in the lobster roll, generously laden with extra meat—a decision that proved its merit. The upgrade offered a heftier, meatier experience without the unnecessary bulk of more bread. For seafood enthusiasts seeking robust flavors and hearty portions, this upgrade is a must. An unassuming gem, this spot delivers on both convenience and taste.

Tucked atop the Freehand Hotel lies its charming rooftop bar/restaurant. This spot is a magnet for weekend crowds, offering a vibrant atmosphere that perfectly aligns with the hotel's cool and playful vibe. Don't come expecting an extensive menu – the offerings here lean towards a more curated selection catering to beverage enthusiasts. While the vibe is undeniably fun, it does attract its fair share of tourists. The set-up isn't ideal for large groups as seating can feel cramped, with both the tables and outdoor area on the smaller side. This place is best suited for a casual drop-in rather than a grand dining experience.

This may be the first ever place that charges for food by the weight, and yet doesn't feel like the scale is rigged against you.I went to here on a whim during lunch break at a training in the Museum of the city of New York, not expecting much. The reality is that the food was absolutely delicious. I made myself a nice little plate of jerk chicken, mac & cheese, beef, and some other chicken. I was pleasantly surprised that the bill wasn't high.Shortly after ordering my food, and sitting down to eat it, I noticed the place become packed with local school kids. That made me happy because it showed that there is high turnover there, and the food is replenished regularly. It also made me happy knowing that the locals actually eat here. I would definitely go back here if I'm in the neighborhood.

Very solid fast casual Chinese place. They have a "bowl" option with dry noodles, soup noodles or rice. I had the Chariman mao braised pork belly. A lot of more meat than I expected (very pleasantly surprised) and it was quite good. Not that expensive either, would be a really good lunch option. You can choose your spice level (the spicy level is seriously super spicy, the cashier warned us). There are also a few add on options for the bowl. They also have other options like dumplings, side dishes, and a few dessert options. Quite a bit of seating.

Yes, the restaurant looks as dingy as it gets on the outside, but don't let the exterior fool you because hidden behind those doors is actually a Michelin star restaurant ... but does it deserve that star?I came here recently as part of a group of 4, so we got a chance to try quite a bit of different dishes from their large menu. We got here exactly when they opened at 6pm on a Tuesday, although we had reservations anyway. The restaurant was empty at the time, but as soon as business began, customers started filing in consistently.One thing to definitely keep in mind prior to your meal is that this is not your average NYC Americanized Thai restaurant where you can recognize everything on the menu. In fact, put your reading glasses on because everything is listed in Thai first, followed by a small English description below it.As for the food, we tried to get a little bit of everything or what we thought was the best of everything that sounded good, which included:Tum Thai Kai Kem (Thai Spicy Papaya Salad with Salted Egg)H'orderves Der (Sampler Dish)Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (Deep Fried Chicken Thigh)Por Pia Larb Moo (Deep-fried Spicy Pork Spring Roll)Nue Ping Kati Soti (Grilled Coconut Milk Marinated Beef Skewers)Pad Thai Mun Poo (Spicy Pad Thai with crabmeat and crab paste)Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw Talay (Thai Styled Fried Pad See Ew with Shrimp and Calamari)Vegetarian Fried Rice (Fried rice with assortment of mushrooms and veggies)Grilled Sticky Rice - Der's StyleI won't comment on everything, but a few of them definitely left some lasting memories - some having me daydream for days about it and some vanishing from my mind like a distant memory. First, the H'orderves Der. This was an interesting dish, but mostly because of the little slice sausages, which reminded us of Chinese sausages that you can buy at a market. As for everything else on it, it was just OK. Some of my favorites included the Nue Ping Kati Soti (beef skewers) and Por Pia Larb Moo (pork spring rolls). Honestly, I can't resist a good beef skewer and pork spring roll (like at dim sum) and both were really good and flavorful. The spring rolls were extra crispy and had plenty of seasoned ground pork meat inside. Also, the Vegetarian Fried Rice (with mushrooms and veggies) was tasty too as the rice was perfectly fried and a large serving of flavorful straw mushrooms sat right next to it. However, my favorite was surprisingly the Grilled Stick Rice - Der's Style. Who would have thought that my favorite dish out of everything was rice?! The sticky rice was mounted onto a stick and literally could be eaten like a corn dog. It had a coconut flavor to it, so that was a huge winner for me since I love me some coconut.  As for disappointments, the Pad Thai Mun Poo (spicy pad thai) was a bit on the moist side. It was too soggy for everyone at our table. Also, the papaya salad was just ehhh. There wasn't much to it.Everything here was solid, but nothing really surprised our entire table, in terms of how amazing it was. I will say that the dishes and flavors were much more unique and exotic than what we were used to for Thai food, which was fine as it was geared toward the region of Thailand it originated from. However, the flavors from this region of Thailand didn't wow us like we hoped it would.

I recently dined at this local spot known for its Peruvian chicken. While the breast meat was somewhat dry, which is a common occurrence with chicken, the leg meat did not disappoint and was truly succulent. My dish was served with rice, which was a pleasant companion as it absorbed the chicken's flavors, though I found the texture slightly too soft for my taste. Accompanying the meal was a small salad, which to my surprise, came without dressing. The green sauce provided could potentially double as a salad dressing, but be warned—it's thick and packs a considerable spicy punch that won't suit everyone's palate. As for value, the prices here are a bit steep compared to other places offering Peruvian chicken.

Tucked away just a stone's throw from Madison Square Garden, this charming culinary gem is the perfect pre-show dining destination. Sarah, our delightful server, was the epitome of both friendliness and utility, efficiently navigating us through the menu's bountiful options.

Heeding Sarah's sage advice, we embraced their generous portion sizes, starting with a vibrant little gem salad. At $19, it's an avocado lover's dream, boasting freshness in every forkful. The star of the night, however, was the sausage and kale pizza. For $21, each slice was a heavenly experience, tempting enough to warrant an encore.

Amidst the flavorful fare, the cocktail and wine selection proved formidable, delivering an impressive array of choices for any palate.

With its enchanting interior and exemplary service, this restaurant isn't just a dining experience; it's a must-visit staple for anyone's NYC itinerary.

Have you ever had something touch your tongue and feel like a bomb of flavor just exploded in your mouth??  That's what happened to me today when I ate here for the first time. I found this place walking to another place where I was going to have lunch.  Decided this would be a good adventure and I wasn't wrong.  The service was quick, pleasant but not intrusive.  The got our drinks quickly, took our food order and brought that out fast too.  I had the Gobernordor quesadilla (shrimp and dried chili sauce) and it was fantastic.  Well worth the $8 price tag.  Served on a flour tortilla, its a good size and will be filling if you also get an appetizer, like we did.  We ordered the Corn Esquites and a side of Guacamole (comes with chips...yay!), both of which were incredibly flavorful.  The corn comes with a nice chili mayo sauce to mix up and it provides a nice amount of heat and flavor without being too much.  The chips and guac were fresh and better than most I've had in the area.  I would HIGHLY recommend this place and will likely give it 5 stars after a few more times there.

I had extremely high expectations for this place and this place is alright. The tacos were great, nonetheless but definitely overpriced for what they are. The service was exceptional and there is someone greeting you while you're in line, answering any question you may have. She was really sweet and gave recommendations-- The flour tortilla is quite thin and gets crunchy which means it breaks as well. The line tends to get really long but goes by quick. You need to keep your receipt which has the number or else you can't claim your taco. The corn tortilla holds the taco much better. So fresh tasting as wellI got the adobada (pork) and the nopal (cactus).The cactus is cut up into small chunks, flavored with spices. Granted, it's cactus so it's watery, has the texture of aloe, and has a sour after taste.I wasn't a huge fan of this taco but this is you're going for a non-meat dish. The adobada had plenty flavor and they didn't skimp out on meat. The meat is cut into very small pieces and for me, it was a little dry and salty. It still was bomb and all the toppings put together was delicious. Self serve lime, salsa, and radishes. There is limited seating in the location -- I went against the wall which is a bit uncomfortable since you're facing people waiting in line outside hah. Overall, yummy tacos to get in east coast-- definitely check this place out!

I recently visited a restaurant specializing in poké bowls and was pleasantly satisfied with my dining experience. Patrons can customize their bowls with a variety of bases including white rice, salad, or a combination of the two. I opted for the preset classic bowl, which featured fresh tuna, crisp greens, edamame, a delightful seaweed salad, masago, and a sprinkle of pepper flakes for a slight kick. The bowl was generously topped and the tuna was notably fresh. An added perk of dining here was the complimentary green tea with the purchase of a meal, which was a refreshing accompaniment. Overall, a delightful spot for a fresh and filling meal.

Chill vibe, good mix of older people and not-too-young people. Not a scene. Relaxed, comfortable. Drinkable wine, hard seltzer available. Free chips. Vegan shepherds pie! Good, easy neighborhood spot.

Title: A Baja Blast in the Heart of NYC

I recently had the chance to visit this little gem thanks to a recommendation from a friend, and it truly didn't disappoint. The highlight of my visit was undoubtedly the Baja fish tacos – each one packed with two pieces of perfectly battered fish and just the right amount of toppings. For $3.25 apiece in a city where you typically pay a premium for tacos, I was blown away by the quality and flavor.

I also tried the shrimp taco, which was quite tasty, though the tortilla did struggle to hold its own, ending up a bit soggy and compromised. Despite this minor hiccup, the overall experience was fantastic.

The service was friendly and efficient, with enough seating to accommodate us on a busy day. It's a spot that's hard to beat for those seeking delicious tacos on a budget in NYC. I'll definitely be back for more!

Title: A Fresh Take on Fast-Food Chinese at Asian Taste

Nestled in the heart of Alphabet City, Asian Taste breathes new life into a familiar space with its modern and sparkling clean interior, now serving as a beacon for fast-food Chinese cuisine aficionados. Despite its modest size, the few available seats are a welcome feature for those wanting a quick bite in a bright, contemporary setting with an inviting view into the kitchen where the magic happens.

Asian Taste has smartly priced its menu, offering a range of standard takeout Chinese favorites that don't disappoint. On my visit, the appetizers proved to be a highlight. The shrimp spring roll was notably fresh, boasting a perfect crispy exterior that gave way to succulently flavored shrimp and fresh veggies inside. Equally impressive was the scallion pancake, which was delightfully light and crispy, satisfying my craving for some fried comfort goodness to the fullest.

The commitment to quality here extends beyond the food; Asian Taste serves up its dishes in compostable paper containers, showcasing an environmentally conscious side that's heartening to see in the takeout scene.

Couple the solid food offerings with the friendly and efficient service that hints at a family-run operation, and you've got yourself a go-to spot for a quick Chinese fix, whether you prefer delivery or takeout. And with that, I'm off to dive into my next Asian Taste adventure—those noodz won't eat themselves!

Rating: Solidly Good

I came here for brunch on a Sunday morning.  I ordered the croque madame (ham and cheese sandwich with a runny sunny side up egg on top) and my friend ordered the croque monsieur Hawaiian (ham and cheese sandwich with pineapple).  The sandwiches for brunch all came with salad and French fries.  The croque madame was rather small but the portions of the salad and fries were large.  It looked kind of strange.  The French fries could be crispier but they were hot at least.  The salad was fresh and not overly dressed.  Service was okay, friendly and attentive.  The water glasses were very small and not very practical.  It's pretty pricey but the portions were large at least.  I might come back if I'm ever in the area and there's no other options.

Title: A Gem for Authentic Shanghainese Cuisine

My countless experiences at this gem of a restaurant have prompted me to finally pen down a well-deserved review. As someone raised in a Shanghainese household, I've been on a quest for authentic flavors, and this place has consistently delivered over my numerous visits and takeout orders.

The decor transports you to old Shanghai, with its nostalgic furniture and thoughtful design, enhancing the dining experience. It's not just me; my parents, who have a discerning palate for our native cuisine, praised its authenticity and delectable dishes during their visit.

The menu is a testament to culinary excellence; from the savory soups to the perfectly seasoned green beans and the luscious salted duck egg, every selection is crafted to perfection. There are no missteps here—just pure gastronomic delight.

The spacious interior is regularly animated with private events, a testament to its popularity for special occasions. The service? Consistently delightful, matching the quality of the food.

This establishment isn't just a restaurant for me; it's a piece of cultural pride that I eagerly share with out-of-town guests. My advice: arrive with an appetite, and prepare to be charmed by the flavors of Shanghai.

Love this place! Amazing vegan italian food gave me a chance to enjoy my favorite dishes again like lasagna, gnocchi, and chocolate ganache. The ambiance was also very nice and romantic. Would highly recommend the Caesar salad too - that was the winner of the night for me! The light sauce really brought out the flavors of the soy chicken and the shiitake mushrooms. Best Caesar salad I've had.

More of a 3.5 star but great service bumps it up.Cool, hip, uncrowded place with great service.  Star Wars & The Matrix were playing on the wall via projector when we went. They also have outdoor seating. I was about to go for the dumplings, but $7 for 4 seemed too steep. We tried the tofu guac and it was well-portioned and enough for 3 people. I would be interested to see more food options. The drinks were pretty interesting, but they weren't to our liking. The spicy margarita was too spicy, matcha martini a bit too bitter, and Four F*cks Sake (gin based) also fell short. Overall, it's a hip place to catch up with friends but I hope to see different cocktails and food options.

Title: A Mixed Bag at This Seafood Spot

I visited this seafood restaurant for dinner with friends, eager to try this location based on my experiences with another branch. We dove into a feast of seafood: 2lb of crawfish with fire seasoning, 2lb of shrimp spiced to a tee, and 2lb of mild-flavored clams, all washed down with sparkling water and Coke. 

Unfortunately, it turned out to be a bit of a letdown. As someone who enjoys a good kick of spice, I found myself sidelined by stomach pain, which unfortunately meant I couldn't enjoy the spicy offerings as I normally would. The crawfish didn't seem quite fresh, and the clams were excessively salty, not just to my palate but to my friends' as well. The shrimp, I must admit, were fresh and well-prepared.

The overall taste of our meal leaned heavily on the oily side, which wasn't particularly pleasing. Service-wise, we managed a score of 3.5/5. While we attempted to relocate to a larger table, we were stuck at a snug one presumably meant for two, and with the restaurant not being busy due to a snowy Sunday night, we had to scale back our order. The waitress was amiable, albeit a tad slow. 

As for ambiance, it was commendable at 4/5. The cleanliness of the establishment impressed me, and even the restrooms maintained high standards. The interior didn't offer anything unique compared to other locations, and it was a bit on the smaller side, but it was definitely cleaner.

Note: Remember to bring cash, as no cards are accepted here, much like the other location.

Spring rolls were crunchy and flavorfulGolden puffs tasted mushy inside, not my favorite Pad Thai was ok, not much flavorPenang curry (spicy) was flavorful Oolong Thailand tea was only okMor Thang (Thai custard) was interesting in flavor with crunch on top Service was excellent, attentive, welcoming No wait for a table (without reservations)Place felt intimate Solid 3.5*

After hearing much praise for this Chinese-Indian fusion restaurant, I arrived with high expectations. The concept was intriguing, and I was ready for a culinary adventure. The food was decent; however, it didn't quite differentiate itself from other dining experiences I've had. My anticipation for bold, innovative fusion was met with subtlety, leaving me yearning for a more pronounced blend of the two cuisines. Given the premium prices, I anticipated a meal that would justify the cost with exceptional flair. Unfortunately, the restaurant didn't quite deliver on its promise of an extraordinary fusion affair.

I came with a party of eight people on a Sunday night.Food:I got the braised short ribs ($29) and mango lassi ($5). The braised short ribs were very flavorful and came with mashed potatoes and green beans. It was very very filling. The mango lassi was very refreshing. Service:Very attentive staff and very lovely. There is complementary coat check.Ambience:With the dim lighting during the evening and the bar, it gave a great ambience. Good for a date or hangout with friends! Notes:Make sure to make a reservation if you know you'll be dining here ahead of time! Update: on my second visit recently, I got the lamb biryani (very good) and cucumber and mango salad (refreshing!)

My boyfriend and I visited this restaurant for lunch and were quite pleased with our dining experience. It's not your typical all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ joint; instead, you select specific meats to savor their high quality, particularly the un-marinated options. We opted for the lunch Harundae Set, which featured both marinated and un-marinated short ribs, alongside marinated bulgogi.

The standout for me was the not marinated short ribs—the meat's quality shone through, especially when simply seasoned with salt, though the light marinade provided an enjoyable alternative. Post-main course, do consider adding potato noodles; they absorb the residual meat flavors from the bulgogi pan, adding another layer of deliciousness to the meal.

While the restaurant offers a premium experience with top-notch flavors, it's not the place for those seeking an abundance of food— our lunch set was approximately $60 pre-tax and tip. A worthwhile visit for anyone looking for quality over quantity in their Korean BBQ experience.

Tucked away in a vibrant speakeasy setting, my experience at this burger joint was a delightful surprise. The ambiance was amplified by funky artwork lining the walls and a soundtrack that perfectly complemented the mood. The star of the show, the burger, was notably juicy, living up to the culinary expectation set by the cool surroundings. Accompanied by fries, the meal was reasonably priced with four burgers totaling $46. Despite the compact space, I managed to snag a table for two without a hitch. Even though there was a queue outside, it progressed swiftly. All in all, this place is a must-visit for burger aficionados looking for great food in a unique atmosphere.

I have come here once many years ago and then stopped by today...I noticed they have a new portion of the menu which includes Northern Thai specialties. These dishes seemed quite unique and I liked the addition to the menu.I had the Chiang Mai (noodle soup with chicken). And I simply adored it. The chicken pieces were huge, succulent, and extremely filling. The flavor of the broth was excellent and had a lot of nuance. It was thicker, almost like a curry... and it had hints of coconut milk and red curry. It had a spicy kick without feeling overpowering. I liked the noodles as well; they were medium (not too thin and not too thick). The crunchy or crispy "noodles" on top added a different consistency to it as well.The ambiance is nice as it's not too crowded but there's some chandeliers and other touches that give it a picturesque quality.

I was here within a month of them opening for a semi-early dinner so this review is from a little while ago. The female server here was very nice and she checked whether I have had food from the region before due to the spice level of some of the dishes.To drink, I had their Teh Tarik, or pulled tea which was similar to other places. The tea was a bit stronger here but the prices were higher but what do you expect for this block? Overall, it was fine, and it helped curb the spices from my main.I ordered the Beef Rendang as my main dish. Served on top of a banana leaf with some shredded cucumber, this is a beef dish braised for a long time in a variety of spices as well as a distinct coconut flavor. The dish was very well spiced with a melange of flavors and it packed a good amount of heat. The coconut flavor was not as strong as some other places. The beef itself was very tender and the portion size was fine for the price. It came with some white rice on the side which was fine; most likely jasmine.After looking through their dessert menu, I settled with "Kaya Jam with Sticky Rice" as I hadn't had kaya in a while. Kaya is a very sweet green colored coconut/pandan jam and is commonly put on bread in the morning (known simply as kaya toast.) This was served with two types of sticky rice, a blue one made from butterfly pea flower and the normal white variety. The blue sticky rice has a light floral flavor from the flower used but is really there for color more than flavor. The dish was warm and a comforting end to the meal and was fine for the price (maybe a bit small.)This was a very good Singaporean place and I'll be back to try some more dishes with others (such as the various shellfish/noodle dishes as well as the durian sundae) as I wasn't super hungry the first time. A bit pricey (as expected from the area and it's Michelin background) but worth it. 4.1

Really lovely experience here. The $46 3-course dinner is, despite the price increase after the success of Atomix, still one of the better deals in the city. In my opinion the earlier courses are stronger than the later ones. Service was great. I highly recommend making a reservation in advance through Resy if you plan to visit.Recommended:-Sujeonggwa granita ($9) - sujeonggwa flavored granita with burrata, walnut, and some jujube. Extremely delicious, superb combination of flavors, temperatures and textures. The creamy burrata paired well with the granita, and the candied walnuts were next level. I seriously wanted to order a second one.-Chrysanthemum - chrysanthemum leaves, charred leeks, plum, and shaved cheddar. Chrysanthemum leaves (slightly bitter) and charred leeks topped with shaved cheddar. Delicious.2. Sunchoke - oyster mushroom, black truffle, orange. Really tasty, with the orange adding a brightness to the meaty mushroom.2. Egg (+25 for Hokkaido uni (MP)) - steamed egg with sea urchin, gim, heart of palm, and topped with seaweed and crispy quinoa. The egg is amazing - very silky, and I really liked the pieces of heart of palm inside. The sea urchin is so sweet and delicious; however if you don't want to pay the supplement it would still be great without it in my opinion.OK:1. Yellowtail - kombucha, gim, (watermelon) radish. It's fine.3. Octopus - mango, mojo verde, fermented dubu, and fried fingerling potatoes. Good but nothing amazing.-Special rice ($2) - seaweed rice. Good. Their white rice is also excellent. White rice comes with free refills, as do the banchan (we had white kimchi and kohlrabi kimchi).Not recommended:3. Duck - Napa cabbage, Brecken fern, spring garlic. Meh. The duck tasted good but in a home cooking way, not an elevated way. Also the portion was tiny - it was mostly broth with one slice of duck that had been shredded. I had this the first day it was available on the menu, so this dish may have changed since then.

I really enjoyed this place for the ambience, service, and food. It's really cool to see / hear the history behind it all. We had an amazing waiter that checked on us and made great recommendations. We got a massive amount of meat and there was 0 complaints to it all. I will definitely be back!

I recently visited a local restaurant on a whim for brunch and had quite a pleasant experience. Although I couldn't secure a reservation online on the same day – something I'd suggest doing a few days ahead – my timely arrival at opening meant a comfortable spot at the bar was secured before the crowds rolled in.

The eatery buzzed with energy right from the start, the DJ's tunes creating a vivacious atmosphere that was a bit intense for an early 11 AM start, but still enjoyable. I indulged in the shrimp and grits which were flavorful, although the grits were slightly watery for my taste. My companion's kale salad was a hit, fresh and satisfying.

This restaurant certainly earns a recommendation for those seeking a lively brunch scene. And with a DJ setting the mood in the evenings too, I'm keen on a return visit to experience the nighttime vibe.

Despite its modest appearance, this unassuming little spot is a true gem for gyoza lovers. The dumplings are nothing short of delicious—a must-try for anyone in the area. Don't let size or looks deceive you; it's absolutely worth a stop.

I recently dined at this establishment, purportedly serving Spanish cuisine, and found the experience disappointing. As a fan of authentic Spanish dishes, I regret to say the food here fell short of expectations. The beans on my plate lacked flavor, the rice was undercooked, and the chicken was unpleasantly prepared. Additionally, the soup was overwhelmingly garlicky, which made it difficult to enjoy. Lastly, the empanadas, a classic Spanish delight, were paradoxically both dry and excessively oily. In summary, diners seeking genuine Spanish flavors might want to consider other options.

Nestled in the heart of the bustling New York scene, Harry's stands as a testament to what dining out should truly embody. This establishment isn't just about a meal; it's about the full New York experience—an experience that anyone with a taste for the genuine and the excellent will surely appreciate. From the moment you walk through the doors, you're treated to more than just exemplary service; you're enveloped in the kind of welcoming atmosphere that seems to say, "This is where life happens."

The food is nothing short of superb, boasting flavors and preparations that could very well spoil you for other restaurants. And the service? Impeccable. The staff at Harry's understands that a meal out is an event, treating each customer with the kind of care and attention that elevates a simple dinner to a memorable occasion.

Now, if budget dining is your main interest and you often find yourself frequenting chain restaurants for their low prices, Harry's might not align with your usual preferences. It's a place of passion, quality, and character, traits that inevitably come with a different price tag. In short, for those seeking an alternative to the cookie-cutter dining experience, Harry's is more than a restaurant—it's a destination worthy of every single one of its stars.

Title: Solid Lunch Spot with French Flair

I recently visited a restaurant for a lunch outing with colleagues and found the experience to be fairly average. The establishment offers an array of options, heavily leaning towards French cuisine. I opted for a classic with a twist - a BLT & A (avocado) with fries - that proved to be a satisfying choice. Companions praised the burrata and the burger, highlighting them as worthwhile picks. However, the French onion soup fell short, with its sweetness skewing away from traditional expectations.

Service was efficient, with little wait time for our meals. A standout beverage was the Pomegranate Lemonade, a refreshing and highly recommended accompaniment to any dish. While the restaurant doesn't dazzle, it stands as a decent choice for a no-frills lunch.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience Post-Celebration

Last Saturday evening, post-birthday celebration, my friends and I decided to dine at a popular local spot. Despite a packed house, fortune smiled upon us with an available table. A hot tip for newcomers: check in on Yelp for a round of complimentary drinks, a promotion that nicely kicked off our meal.

I indulged in an Old Fashioned, mixed to perfection—strong and satisfying, just as I prefer. The complimentary chips provided a welcome crunch, pairing well with the tastefully prepared artichoke hearts that we selected as our appetizer.

For my main course, the fillet mignon did not disappoint, expertly cooked to match my preference. Though my salted caramel chocolate tart was on the briny side, I found it decent. Nevertheless, the consensus at the table seemed to favor the apple pie with vanilla ice cream, a choice I'll likely pivot to in future visits.

The service was a highlight, contributing to an overall enjoyable dining experience. I'd readily recommend this restaurant to those looking for a blend of quality food and attentive service.

I visited this restaurant for happy hour with friends on a Friday evening. The experience was mediocre. Unfortunately, the service left a lot to be desired, and the drinks were subpar. On a positive note, the food, particularly the shrimp tacos I ordered, was tasty. However, the menu options were rather limited and failed to impress. Despite the decent cuisine, the overall experience wasn't compelling enough to warrant a return visit.

I stopped by Thai @ Lex around 4:45pm on a Tuesday to satisfy a Thai food craving.  The restaurant is small, and seats 18-20 people.  However, I think they get more business from take-out/delivery.  There was one other person in the restaurant at the time got there, and 2 other parties came in as I was eating.  The decor here is lovely (including the bathroom).I ordered a panang curry with chicken ($13), which comes with a side of rice.  While the curry came with a decent serving of chicken, I thought it was small for $13.  The flavor of the curry was the best thing about it.  It was less peanut-y than other panang curries I've had, but well flavored.  It was also mildly spicy.  The green beans in the curry tasted undercooked (like I was eating them from the ground).Service here was non-existent, which was weird considering the restaurant was not busy.  No check-backs or water refills.  Overall, the food was fine, but not close to being worth the price.  I would recommend Thai @ Lex if it's convenient but not if you're searching for good Thai food.

If you're planning to attend a play and want something convenient, Brasserie Cognac is a great option.  Our family has come here for years and every entree is fantastic.  Definitely inquire about their daily soups and if Pumpkin soup is an option, get it.  Bon appétit!

I recently visited a restaurant renowned for its pizza, and I must say, it did not disappoint. The pizza crust struck the perfect balance between crispy and chewy, catering to my exact preference. I opted for the vodka pizza, which was undeniably yummy, though a smidge more sauce would have elevated the experience even further. The lasagna pizza, however, was a delightful surprise – it was hearty with just the right amount of sauce and meat, hitting all the right notes for a satisfying meal. Additionally, the mural outside added a vibrant touch of NYC flair, enhancing the overall dining experience. Highly recommend for pizza aficionados!

Good fresh hot pizza, quick fast and good, seating area small, need more places to sit. Daily deal is outstanding. Great service and the quickness is breathtaking. The way he moves back there is impressive. Let him sack your pizza and you are in for a treat. We recorded him. Stop by yay.

I really enjoyed this meal. My table ended up sharing a bunch of things:-meatballs: these were some of the best meatballs I've had at a restaurant-Caesar salad: really good dressing and a good portion size. The Parmesan bread that came with it was also really good. -burrata with prosciutto: amazing and the portion was a good size-butternut squash ravioli: this was good, but I probably wouldn't get it again. It was a large portion-Siamese agnolotti: this was amazing and one of my favorite dishes of the night even though I don't usually eat veal-Pici all's toscana: I enjoyed the flavor of this pasta but it was a little too al dente for me -chicken parm: I didn't really enjoy this dish. The chicken was over cooked and it wasn't hot when it arrived at our table.Overall, it was a great meal and I would return.

I have to upgrade my review to 5 stars.Their iced HK milk tea is great! It's nice and strong. it really gives you a kick in the face.  I also tried their rice noodles. It doesnt look the best, but its pan fried so there is a nice thin slightly crispy crust. Yum!  The congee seems to have more thousand year old egg too!

Title: A Splendid Affair at Oceans - Almost Flawless

If I were to rate Oceans based solely on the culinary offerings, a solid four stars would be fitting. However, including the exceptional service and overall experience, this place teeters towards a five-star review.

Let's cut to the chase—Oceans has an unexpected highlight: the upstairs bathrooms equipped with bidets and an interactive screen. Though slightly bewildering at first, the high-tech amenities provide a novel experience that shouldn't be missed.

During our visit, our party of seven was the largest, which landed us in a secluded private room. The exclusivity of the setting amplified the dining experience, although part of me yearned for the buzz of the main dining area.

Our meal commenced with a three-tiered seafood tower, which justified its cost with a fresh and delectable selection, including a standout tuna poke. We then ventured into a realm of sushi rolls and an inventive presentation of sashimi served within the fish carcass—a unique and delightful touch. The sushi was satisfactory, yet overshadowed by the star of the evening: the exceptional langoustines.

In sum, Oceans provides a nearly impeccable dining experience where the food is great and the service is even greater. And remember—when it's time to freshen up, the upstairs is where it's at.

I just discovered my new favorite Italian eatery! The food is phenomenal, and the ambiance strikes the perfect note between cozy and chic with its dim lighting, candlelit tables, and an excellent music selection. Service is nothing short of spectacular, especially thanks to our waiter, Jonah, who went above and beyond—worthy of well over a 20% tip!

The spaghetti and meatballs have set a new standard for me, and that's coming from someone who isn't even a fan of red sauce. Plus, their bruschetta is simply amazing. The prices are quite reasonable for the high-quality experience they provide. I'm already planning my next visit for when I'm back in New York.

Title: A Pizzeria That Even Non-Pizza Lovers Adore!

As someone who's notoriously picky about pizza, I was blown away by this spot – their pies are a rare find that I couldn't fault. Despite only experiencing their takeout due to quarantine restrictions, the quality of the food was exceptional.

The customizable options are fantastic; you can craft your pizza to any size and taste, with both small and large sizes being generously portioned. I'm not particularly small yet found the "small" to be quite ample – I paired it with a walnut apple salad (also surprisingly large) and still couldn't finish my pizza!

For those concerned about dietary choices, fear not – you can opt for vegan or gluten-free crusts, making your meal as healthy or indulgent as you desire.

Verdict: This place is a gem! Once quarantine lifts, I'm looking forward to enjoying the ambiance of their sit-down service. Highly recommended for any pizza skeptic!

The Sunday brunch is the best in town...so I am told. I arrived at the very end and had to waitv45 minutes while the kitchen reset to dinner.The bar is awesome, that much I know. Its fully stocked and the bartenders are pretty damn good.  I sat at the bar for 45 minutes waiting to order a decent burger, as their dinner menu is very, very small.  Steak, fish and burger.  The burger is topped with a big sliced or pork belly as opposed to bacon.  I felt it took away from the burger which was cooked really well.It comes with fries and very small amount of ketchup.  They were really well cooked though and tasted great.I wouldn't recommend them for dinner unless your staying here,  however the bar is pretty awesome so it is a great place to catch a drink with colleagues.
Excellent spot for lunch! I've been a handful of times now and I love the prix fixe options. The value is awesome! Love the tacos and the roasted corn. Delicious! Not to be missed!

I always wanted to try out handmade pasta here and I wasnt disappointed. This is a small cozy restaurant that sorta feels like a big house (atleast on the inside). Our waiter was cheerful and nice. The pasta does take a while to come out but its hand made so obviously its gonna take time. I had the squid ink fettuccine with roasted garlic pecurino which was really good. The only draw back was there was no protein in my pasta. I kinda wanted seafood but they only had clams and I hate clams. So that was the only thing I wish it had. But the pasta was soft and perfectly cooked. The one less star is for the fact that they forgot one of my friend's order because two people in our table ordered the same thing so they assumed they got it twice so they canceled one order. My (hungry) friend waited a long time after that and by the time she got her pasta we were almost done with ours. The waiter was apologetic and they didnt charge us for that one pasta but it still ruined the mood. My friend didnt eat her pasta and took it to go. Other than that it is a pretty nice restaurant that I will go again to.

Title: A Flavorful Brunch at [Restaurant Name] with Room for Improvement

My recent brunch at [Restaurant Name] was largely a delightful experience. Opting for a family-style meal, my friend and I indulged in a spread that included bottomless mimosas, a decision I wholeheartedly recommend. Among our selections, the chili pan mee was the standout dish; its perfect harmony of tang, spice, and sweetness coupled with well-proportioned meat, noodles, and a decadent oozing egg yolk left a memorable impression. The bright notes of the papaya salad were a welcome palate cleanser, providing a refreshing counterpoint to the heavier menu items.

However, not all dishes hit the mark. The hash was underwhelming, and both the garlic fried rice and sugar donuts were merely average. While the mimosas were indeed strong and satisfying, service waned as the brunch progressed, with refills becoming scarce despite a less crowded setting.

Ambiance was a double-edged sword – the energy of the place was dampened by an overwhelming noise level that encroached upon the dining experience, making conversation challenging.

Portion sizes seemed at odds with the family-style concept, leaning more towards individual servings which was a letdown for those expecting to share.

Despite these critiques, the restaurant's culinary highs would entice me to return for another brunch. I’d advise future diners to balance the rich, sometimes greasy dishes with lighter options like the salad. While there's potential for a five-star rating, [Restaurant Name] needs to fine-tune aspects of service and atmosphere. A promising spot worth trying – just don't forget to bring your appetite and perhaps, earplugs.

Tucked away in the bustling heart of the city lies an Italian gem that truly stands out from the rest. From the moment you step in, the beautiful interior and the impeccable service suggest that you're in for a treat, and the kitchen does not disappoint.

Starting our meal with complimentary buttered crackers accompanied by jam and cheese set a high bar. Simple yet executed perfectly, this small gesture showcased their attention to detail and quality, leaving an indelible impression.

We indulged in an array of pasta dishes. The rabbit gnocchi was tender and flavorful, making it a dish I would recommend. The star of the evening, however, was the ravioli pyramide. The harmonious blend of walnut and ricotta was nothing short of divine, earning it the top spot as my favorite pasta dish on the menu.

The spinach gnudi, paired with ground turkey, was the only dish that fell short for me. The combination didn't quite hit the mark, but this small misstep was easily forgiven in light of the other outstanding offerings.

To end the night, we savored the olive oil cake, a dessert that deserves applause. Whether you have a sweet tooth or not, this dessert is a must-have.

In summary, this spot doesn't just serve food; it delivers an experience. Each dish, especially the ravioli pyramide and the unassumingly exquisite olive oil cake, is a testament to their culinary prowess. A visit here is highly recommended for anyone in search of exquisite Italian fare.

During my latest culinary escapade at the riverside gem, I found the Lower East Side Roll to be rather pedestrian; however, the Deep Fried Lobster MAC & Cheese Cubes were nothing short of sublime - a must-try for any gastronome. Take note, al fresco enthusiasts: snagging an outdoor seat requires promptness, as patrons may linger on the boat all day, a policy unbeknownst to us initially. Nonetheless, the establishment shines as a prime spot for delightful drinks accompanied by picturesque views.

I wish I could go back and redo my birthday brunch and pick a different  spot. I had high hopes after hearing great things about this place but was let down dramatically. I arrived late and we attempted to call and let them know however after 10 calls no one ever picked up. Our 2 hour limit on our table had started according to the hostess and when we arrived we were seated.  We were seated in the back which I found dark and away from the lively fun..it was also hot back there. Definitely  not the vibe I was going for. Food- I had the steak and eggs which I did not like. Steak was chewy and eggs tasted weird. I tasted the waffle sandwich which wasn't bad. Definitely the better pick.  Drinks- the unlimited drinks never got me tipsy. Meaning the drinks were weak. The sangria wasn't good neither. They are smart with the bottomless deal because they give you cheap Champagne and juice. it was not worth it .Service/package- this was supposed to be a birthday celebration package prepaid and reserved and my friend stated she paid for a dessert and candle to be brought out because they were told they couldn't bring a cake or birthday things. However, I did see balloons from another party so that was a lie. After we ate, we were given the bill and they never brought any dessert out. The waitress was not attentive and we were kicked off the table and not given much of an option as to where else to go. When the bill was brought the cake should've come as well since they knew they were going to kick us off. Terrible service. I will not be back. Not the place for a birthday celebration. When we emailed about not getting the dessert brought out was told we were late. Regardless of that if we paid for something it should've been brought out even while we were eating. These people are crooks and this is not a place to come to Save yourself the hassle! STAT AWAY!

A Japanese curry restaurant where they don't mess around with their curries. I was looking for a place where there was no wait in Koreatown and this happen to have a few open tables and good food.I got the Couple Set with my girlfriend which came with Herb Chicken Curry Rice, Beef Curry Noodle, Fried Shrimp, Pork Cutlet & 2 Drinks. We got both the Herb Chicken Curry Rice and the Beef Curry Noodle medium spicy (level one) which did not taste like it should be level one spicy as it was already pretty spicy at this level surprisingly. I can't imagine what level 2 regular spicy would be like. And I'm most definitely not ready for their level 4 super spicy. Despite the surprising kick, the spice went really well with the meal. I enjoyed everything I was able to try in this combo set.The service is okay. Just be ready to wave someone down if you need something like refill on drinks, ordering more food, and the check. Otherwise, I look forward to conquering the curry heat that they bring next time.

Wow. Excellent. Loved it. Lamb and rice. Good. Was just going to eat a little and I ate it all in seconds. Fresh and wow. Good good. Nice flavor. Nice spices. Carts are everywhere and now I know why. They are good!

My recent dining experience at this gem of a restaurant surpassed my expectations. We arrived armed with a coupon for a three-course meal accompanied by a wine tasting featuring six glasses. Despite the restaurant being quiet with only a few diners, the intimacy of the atmosphere added to our enjoyment.

From start to finish, the fusion-inspired dishes we ordered were executed with the precision and elegance of traditional Japanese cuisine. The highlight was undoubtedly the best red snapper we've ever tasted – a dish we will not soon forget. Though we hesitated to try their renowned rabbit dish, it's at the top of our list for our next visit.

The service was impeccable, reflecting the high standards I've come to appreciate from my time working with a Japanese company. The staff displayed a respectful and considerate demeanor, bridging any language barriers with their thoughtful actions. A charming touch was the rabbit-shaped napkins, a nod to their famous dish and a testament to their attention to detail.

In short, the restaurant offers an exceptional dining experience that merges delicate fusion flavors with the revered traditions of Japanese hospitality. Highly recommended for anyone seeking an exquisite meal accompanied by attentive service.

On New Year's Eve, my dining experience at the mall's food court was a last resort, with options aplenty yet choosing proved daunting. High prices were a surprise; my sandwich alone surpassed the $20 mark. The menu description left too much to the imagination and the actual meal disappointed, dominated by an unexpected, overwhelming sour pickle flavor that failed to hit the mark for my palate.
Why would you do this to gnocchi?!? Burnt to a crisp! The sauce was good but I would never come back here again. Also a bit pricey for the quality.

We needed a quick after meeting dinner and stumbled upon BXL Cafe. We normally avoid the area as everything is super overpriced and busy, but at BXL, we were pleasantly surprised. We got a table right away even though they were mostly busy. It was a slightly loud but cute ambiance. We were in a hurry so we ordered quickly.The calamari was delicious and perfectly cooked. The raw oyster special (6 oysters and a glass of wine) was a good deal for the area. They oysters were fresh and briny and I needed them that day. The Caesar salad was good.Overall, we had a nice dinner at BXL. Prices were a bit high but that's par for the area. Service was very slow and it was hard to get our server's attention. That was the minus for us. Other than that, a good dinner experience.

Title: A Pricey but Worthy Banh Mi Indulgence in NYC

Despite the sting to my finances, noting the banh mi price has doubled over eight years, my commitment to support small businesses remains unwavering. This spot holds the crown as my favorite banh mi destination in New York City, thanks to its enduringly exquisite flavors – a true culinary delight. For those who seek a fiery kick, I recommend the 'extra spicy' option, which amps up the heat with a generous addition of fresh jalapeño peppers alongside the usual sriracha. Just remember to bring cash, as this is a cash-only establishment.

Came for dinner with a friend on a Sunday night. Service was really great.  The ambience is nice and as everyone knows it's cool to walk through the pawn shop to get to the big restaurant in the back.  Now for the meal.  I wasn't impressed by the wine.  I did do by the glass so not a lot of options per type and it tasted cheap.  My friend and I split the kale and apple salad which was good.  Then she had the carpaccio and I had the grilled cheese bacon and tomato soup dumplings as well as the Thai shrimp.  Those dumplings are to dye for.  They are the main reason to come here.  I seriously dream about them.  The shrimp was just okay.  For dessert I had the cannoli pana cotta which was not like I expected.  It tasted like cannoli whipped cream and had coffee ice cream on the side.  It was ok just wouldn't choose it again when I return.  Overall great place and will return for dumplings service and ambiance.  I do wish to find other amazing items on the menu in the future

We went here for my husband's birthday with our group of friends. They were great at hosting our big party of nine. The restaurant is definitely bigger on the inside which you can't tell from the street view. The menu is broken into the typical menu course for Italian restaurants (Antipasti, sides, First course aka pasta dishes and second course aka entrees. If you had any questions the staff was glad to answer them. We started with the tagliere di salumi e formaggi which was a platter of fresh ham cold cuts, various cheeses and marinated veggies. For the entree I ordered the risotto do mare profumato which is basically a seafood risotto. I loved that the seafood was super tender and soft. The risotto had just enough creaminess that paired well with the baby scallops and calamari rings. For dessert I got the Sicilian cannolis that come with two in one serving. I thought that what was unique was the texture of the cannoli cream. It was supper smooth and light. A great way to end a fantastic meal.

Title: A Fusion of Flavors at [Restaurant Name]

I recently savored the taste of French and Asian fusion pastries at [Restaurant Name], and it was a delightful experience. From the flaky croissants to the moist muffins and the sublime baguettes, each bakery item I tried seemed to top the last. Their cake and puff pastries were the epitome of indulgence, exclaiming "Ohhhh Myyyy!" with every bite.

Accompanying the delectable baked goods, they offer a fine selection of both hot and cold coffee drinks, which provided a perfect complement to the pastries. Seating availability varies by location, but each spot retains the charm of a cozy mini-pastry/coffee house chain. I visited their new addition on the Upper East Side, near 86th and Lexington, and found it quite inviting.

The staff there made the visit even more pleasant; they were both helpful and friendly. Considering the quality, pricing was reasonable, which was a nice surprise.

However, one modern amenity was conspicuously absent – wifi. In an era when digital connectivity is practically a given, especially in a city setting, this oversight was rather puzzling.

Overall, [Restaurant Name] shines with its exquisite pastry selection and quality drinks. If you're not reliant on internet access and are looking for a spot to enjoy a good pastry and coffee, this is a place you might want to check out.

Title: A Delightful Discovery at The Woo

After facing a daunting 30-person queue at Sugarfish, my dining companion and I opted for The Woo, conveniently located just a stone's throw away. This decision proved fortuitous when an hour later, as we were mid-meal, Sugarfish announced the availability of our table.

Our culinary adventure at The Woo commenced with a seafood pancake that, while satisfactory, paled slightly in comparison to the one I savored at Gunbae in Tribeca. The standout of the evening was the Bulgogi beef barbecue, a playful experience where we cooked our own thinly sliced beef along with onions and carrots. The ritual of caramelizing the onions on the grill was particularly enjoyable, and the flavorful salad dressing added a zesty touch to the fresh lettuce and salad. The assortment of kimchi served alongside was a thoughtful touch, although the absence of soup in the meal was noted.

The meal reached its peak with the chicken and vegetable bibimbap, served sizzling in a cast iron bowl. The preparation allowed the rice to achieve an irresistible crispiness, combining texture with the rich flavors for an utterly satisfying dish.

The serendipitous visit to The Woo led to a wonderful and entertaining dining experience that I'll be eager to repeat.

Title: Quaint Bite in the City

On a spontaneous evening out with friends, we found ourselves at this charming little spot. Be warned, the wait can stretch to 45 minutes, yet our patience was rewarded. Despite the snug seating arrangements that brought us up close with neighboring diners, the ambience was undeniably cute and trendy.

The concise menu—a refreshing change from the tome-like offerings elsewhere—meant our choices were simple and the kitchen could swiftly deliver our meals to the table. And swiftly they did, much to the delight of my growling stomach.

The food was pleasant, though it didn't quite send my taste buds into overdrive. However, the highlight was the sensible portion sizes, filling without crossing into food coma territory. The drinks, while adorable and Instagram-worthy, came with the typical city price tag of $14—steep for my wallet but not unexpected.

All in all, a decent dining experience with a focus on balance and style.

Recently, I visited a new grab-and-go style eatery that popped up in the concourse of 30 Rock. Having anticipated a Korean-inspired assembly line akin to Chipotle, the reality was more of a prepackaged selection ordered at the counter, which dampened my initial excitement.

Opting for a lunch box over the snacks-to-go like beef mandu and kimbap visible behind the clear shelf, I was drawn to the presentation—a long, compartmentalized paper box, albeit unnecessarily bagged. The contents included gochujang-marinated chicken, which was tender and subtly sweet, possibly thanks to honey in the marinade. Accompaniments were a mixed bag; the cherry tomatoes were fresh, the kimchi was pleasantly mild, but the raw green bean, solitary mushroom, and dry leafy greens fell short. The black rice was passable, but nothing to write home about.

At $14, the meal didn't provide the satisfaction or value one might expect, leaving me hungry by afternoon. I would have been more content at the $11-12 range, given the overall experience and quantity.

Title: Second Visit, Consistently Amazing

My second visit to this restaurant reaffirmed my love for it! The vast and sparkling clean space immediately sets a welcoming tone. Polite and speedy servers ensure a smooth dining experience, and the culinary offerings are exceptional. I was delighted to discover new dishes have been added to their already impressive menu.

This time, I took advantage of the lunch special—an unbeatable value at just $10. But be warned, it operates on a first-come, first-serve basis, which is fair given the restaurant's popularity.

Despite the bustling atmosphere, the service never falters, speaking volumes about the efficiency of the staff and management. Their ability to maintain such swift service in a packed venue is commendable.

In summary, this restaurant nails it on all fronts: ambiance, service, and culinary delights. I'm already planning my next visit. Highly recommended!

I was happy that now I work in the area and I am about 5 minutes walk from Hill Country Barbecue. I came here today for lunch to get out of the office and enjoy the sun a little bit. The cashier greeted me and handed me an ordering card. I walked up to the Barbecue & Sausage booth and waited for someone to assist me. I told the guy that I want the Butcher's Pick and he looked at me weird. He went to ask someone in the back and guess they have no clue.  Shoot a lot has changed about 3 years ago ::sad face:: I was frustrated and didn't have a back-up lunch spot so I just ordered the Moist Brisket for $14.75 half lb which only came with four slices of white bread. I looked over at the sides menu...OMG so expensive. The guy added a sticker onto my card then put a lot of barbecue sauce in my bag. I missed when the brisket was wrapped in paper. I paid for my order at the cash wrap and asked again about the Butcher's Pick. No one knew about it. I guess they change management and staff. I speed walk back to my office to devour my food. Wow, I am totally disappointed in the brisket. I paid about 16 bucks for bland and dry brisket...SMH!!! I dunked the brisket into barbecue sauce and it still doesn't even make it taste good. It was such a waste of $$$ and I am over you! Go somewhere else, people!

**BRUNCH REVIEW: CajunSea & Oyster**

From the moment my friends and I stepped into CajunSea & Oyster for a Saturday brunch, the experience was impeccable. We were quickly seated and immediately attended to by Peter, our waiter, whose attentive service and enthusiasm made our meal all the more enjoyable.

We kicked things off with a shared plate of Cajun wings & waffles, which was an absolute hit – a harmonious blend of sweet and spicy. Our entrees, the Cajun Shrimp w/Grits, Cajun Shrimp & Sausage w/grits, and a Cajun Shrimp Omelette, did not disappoint either. Each dish arrived hot, beautifully presented, and brimming with bold Cajun flavors that delighted our palates.

Opting for the bottomless mimosas was the cherry on top. With an add-on price of $25 for 2 hours, it was a bargain, especially with Peter ensuring our glasses were never empty.

In short, CajunSea & Oyster nailed it on all fronts – service, ambiance, and culinary excellence. This place is a must-visit for brunch enthusiasts, and I'm already excited for my next visit, dinner!

Came here for brunch today. They make a mean Bloody Mary! However it's the smallest glass and for brunch it's $9 only if you also order an entree. Meh. Counting the fact that it was full of ice to the brim, plus olive garnish and the small glass means the actual Bloody Mary vodka mix accounted for like 3 tablespoons of actual liquid. Anyway... it was delish and spicy just how I like it. The food is mediocre. Their burger is $20 and it's the smallest patty I've ever seen in my life. Comes on a croissant which rubbed me the wrong way. And their sriracha mayo tasted weird. Will come again just to drink, and only if I feel like throwing money down the drain. But great selection of beers on tap-- thumbs up for great variety!

This is arguably the best kosher food in Manhattan. While it's tough to get a table and the place is kinda small, customer service is top notch and anything you eat here will be amazing.Definitely recommend the duck appetizer. It fell off the bone. Also, get the old fashioned with smoke. And get the rissoto balls, and the potatas bravas and the fish tacos. Hell, get everything.The steaks were very very large so I recommend splitting them and going crazy on apps. Also, save room for dessert!!
Bee Sting Pizza is the best thing here! I absolutely love the spicy sweetness flavor of this pizza. Although it is not cheap, great spot to get some fresh personal pie pizza for lunch! Yum!

Pretty standard French brunch option found throughout NYC. I have been to the Bryant Park, Midtown East and UES locations. All offer great options for healthy authentic French fare. I ordered the mesclun salad that came with fall toppings and I chose to add salmon. I have had their muffins, coffee and breads before, which are all bangin. Come here if you're in the area or are anywhere in the city looking for their type of consistent food.

Title: A Festive Feast and Friendly Faces at Local Gem

On a memorable Christmas day, my friends and I decided to explore a new dining spot and our experience was nothing short of delightful. We found ourselves sharing a table with a charming couple, adding a warm twist to our holiday meal.

The menu enticed us with an array of choices, and we indulged in lobster noodle, crab meat fried rice, and a standout dish: sea bass with eggplant in garlic sauce.
