As a rice devotee, every dish was accompanied by this staple, but the sea bass took center stage. This dish balanced a gentle spice with the soothing counterpart of the crab meat fried rice.

To our delight, our tablemates shared a secret – a chef's specialty, the steamed cooba in garlic ginger sauce, a hidden treasure not listed on the menu. It’s a reminder that sometimes, the best dishes are just a friendly tip away.

In conclusion, this restaurant not only served up exquisite food but also facilitated new friendships. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit, and the steamed cooba is at the top of my list.

This place is pretty solid for AYCE hotpot! (We didn't do the BBQ) You get your own single pot which I really like and the selection for meats, veggies, seafood and other random stuff is so extensive and they give you a good amount! I absolutely love how many sauces they have at the sauce bar - you can get one of those 3 dipper sauce plates and just experiment. I got the mala spicy pot and while I did enjoy the flavors (it wasn't too spicy), it was also very oily. After awhile, I was kind of deterred to keep eating because I felt like I was just dipping everything in oil, so if I come back, I'd prob opt for another soup base. They even offer chinese deserts right next to the sauce bar - a cold honeydew puree with sago or warm coconut milk with sweet potatoes. If you check in on yelp you can get free ice cream!If it's your birthday, you can eat for free if you come in a group of 6. Definitely worth it in my opinion! It's a huge restaurant so it can definitely accommodate even 10+ towards the backroom.

Title: A Hearty Pho with Mixed Feelings on Value

During my recent visit, I ventured to try the beef pho dinner to-go, lured in by a tantalizing description hinting at an abundant meal. Although the food earned a solid 4-star rating, where the broth impressed with its rich flavor and the noodles struck a delightful balance between softness and chew, the cost-performance unfortunately detracted from the experience, leaving me unable to justify anything beyond 3 stars for value.

Priced at $24 before taxes and fees, with a modest $2 tip, the total climbed to $32, setting expectations high. However, the promise of a plentiful dish was left unfulfilled. Choosing the larger option led to a curious reduction in the standard beef portions; just two pieces of non-oxtail meat made an appearance, which seemed disproportionate to the extra cost incurred.

Moreover, the broth's quantity scarcely filled the bowl, a puzzling presentation for the premium charged. While the oxtail's fall-apart texture verged more on shredded beef than expected, not quite justifying its inclusion, the bone marrow and cruellers did excel in their preparation and taste.

Ultimately, though sated and satisfied with the quality of the food, I remain skeptical about the meal's overall value. For patrons considering the beef pho dinner, anticipate a good, if not entirely wallet-friendly, dining experience.

Title: A Gem of Asian Fusion Tapas: Perfect for Sharing and Celebrating

I had the pleasure of dining at this quaint Asian Fusion spot for a friend's birthday, and it was nothing short of delightful. With seven of us at the table, we were able to indulge in a wide variety of tapas-sized dishes that were perfect for sharing, giving us a taste of nearly everything on the menu.

Arriving early is essential—this cozy establishment fills up fast, and they don't take reservations. We were smart to show up 20 minutes before they opened and secured a table, but I noticed a lengthy line forming shortly after.

The standout dishes for me included the truffle Mac and cheese, which was a heavenly mix of aromatic truffles and ooey-gooey cheese; the smooth and creamy edamame dumplings; and the eel tacos, which were a unique, flavorful treat paired with a generous serving of guacamole. Every plate was a hit.

Service was impeccable with a capital "I"—a solid 5-star experience. Our attentive servers were constantly checking in, keeping our waters topped up, and swiftly clearing empty plates. They even rushed to the rescue with a tide pen when I had a minor mishap with my sweater. Their attention to detail was remarkable.

There's no shortage of great dining spots in NYC, but for those seeking an exceptional meal with friends, this restaurant is a must-visit. The food is exceptional, the service outstanding, and the experience truly memorable.

Title: A Fairly Average Culinary Experience

I recently dined at this establishment with moderate expectations. While the dishes served were satisfactory, they didn't quite reach the heights of culinary excellence. My top pick of the meal was the Roast Duck and Noodle Soup. The broth was delightfully clean, complementing the fresh noodles and the succulent, well-seasoned duck.

However, the dumplings fell short when compared to my beloved Super Taste, with their overly thick skins. The Fried Buns also didn't impress much, as they were a little too heavy on the breading and light on the filling, making for an unbalanced bite.

The biggest letdown was the Peanut Sauce Noodles. The dish was starkly simplistic, presenting noodles that were underdressed in sauce and garnished with a few scallions. Lacking in toppings or any robust flavoring, it was a dish I felt could have been easily replicated at home.

Overall, the meal was just okay. The restaurant didn't offer anything out of the ordinary or memorable in terms of flavor.

It is a fantastic and one of the most business-centric Michelin 3 establishment that I have had the pleasure of dining. Just note that it is located secretly behind the back of the Brooklyn Fare bodega, not within the hotel, and I'd recommend securing a nearby parking lot a few days before, in case you're driving.In terms of Michelin restaurant, Chef's Table is on par with the big names in NYC with the level of service, quality of the food, and attention to the plating details. Depending on your dining pleasure, you can choose to sit at one of the side tables, or choose to sit at the 'chef's table,' akin to the bar seats, but get a front seat view into the amazing craftwork of Chef Ramirez and his crew. Given that I was celebrating our anniversary, we gladly gave up that coveted spot to enjoy the hustle and bustle, comfortably from afar.Our waiter, Charles, was exemplary in service and would frequent our table and even provide us generous replenishing pours of our wine pairing throughout our 3-hour experience. The overall ambiance has a modern, contemporary, speakeasy vibe. However, because it is located in the back of the Brooklyn Fare, there is only one washroom for the entire restaurant, which can put an uncomfortable break during the dining experience.In terms of the food, I'm sure that the menus change with season variety, but based on the other yelper's photograph, I recognized the crab, sea urchin, langoustine, wagyu, and the frozen souffle and petit fours. Of all of the dishes, I am still thinking and dreaming of the sea urchin with the black truffle resting on top of the softest brioche bun I've ever tasted. All of the fish dishes were shipped directly from Japan and I have to say that the wine pairing was spot on for 95% of the meal, +/- 5% of taste discrepancy and lack of training. The only dishes that I thought were underwhelming were the duck and the custard soup, which were not really memorable and salty, respectively. The desserts were fantastic and magical, but I would have liked there to be more...surprises, like Le Bernadine and Per Se.Overall, this is a restaurant well deserving of a 3 star medal. My biggest disappointment is seeing Chef Ramirez working, but not being able to get a photograph with the legend, but you can't win them all.

I stumbled upon a delightful street cart on Canal and Centre, right across from Starbucks, this past Saturday. What a gem! The medium rice noodles and fish balls were absolutely yummy, bursting with flavor thanks to all the sauces. Quick service, too! And the best part? It only set me back $4.25. An affordable treat that I highly recommend!

Dining at Bouley Test Kitchen for their prix fixe lunch offered a surprisingly opulent experience, defying any sterile "test kitchen" expectations with its rich, salon-like ambiance. Opting for the $55 three-course option - which, to our delight, included a bonus amuse bouche and an extra dish courtesy of the chef – proved sufficient.

The Skate appetizer, while exceedingly tender, was paired with a delightful sauce, whereas the Porcini Flan with crab and truffle dashi intrigued the palate, though it didn't entirely win me over for a repeat order. The complimentary sea bass was the standout dish, earning a special thanks to the chef.

For main courses, the duck served to my son was generous and satisfying, and while my lobster tail was on the smaller side, it impressed with its flavor. Dessert was a unanimous choice; the Pineapple Granite with exotic fruit sorbet and amaretto ice cream ended our meal on a light and refreshing note.

Service lived up to the restaurant's high standards, attentive without being intrusive. While the portions might leave the heartiest of appetites wanting more, the overall experience makes Bouley an ideal spot for a date, striking a fine balance between fullness and satisfaction.

Title: A Charming Evening at a Chic Eatery

Stepping into this restaurant, I was immediately taken by its open, airy atmosphere adorned with vintage bottles and books, creating a quaint and engaging backdrop for an evening meal. Though the prices tip towards the upper end, the quality of the food and the ambiance justify the expense. Make sure to snag a reservation; my dining companion and I were fortunate to find space at the bar around the more accessible hour of 6 pm on a bustling Friday night.

The menu boasts a variety of delectable dishes. The fennel salad was a delightful start, fresh and crunchy with a satisfying bite (4/5). The star of the show, however, was the grilled octopus – an exquisitely tender offering complemented by a comforting side of potatoes, earning it a well-deserved perfect score (5/5). Not to be overshadowed, the lamb skewers impressed with their succulent meat bathed in a delectable sauce, perfect for sopping up with the provided bread (5/5).

To sweeten the conclusion of our meal, we indulged in the churro s'mores. While churros aren't typically my go-to dessert, the combination of chocolate and marshmallow proved to be a delightful pairing (4/5). Overall, the dining experience was a symphony of flavor and charm – highly recommended for those seeking a tasteful and inviting culinary adventure.

Casual bar that's open late and has a fun vibe and $5 margaritas.We wanted to have a later cocktail and while almost everything else was closed in the general area, Mr Biggs was open.  I would guess certain nights this can get crowded but was not when we were there which was perfect.$5 margaritas. Served in plastic cups which, while I'm not a fan, for $5- who can complain. It's a casual spot.  The sweet regular frozen margarita was sweet but good, tasty, not a lot of tequila.  I did not like the flavored one I tried.Server was very friendly and attentive.  Beaming with smiles.

I came here for a birthday dinner for my friend on a Friday night with a group of 7 people.  They were nice enough to seat us even though we were there 30 minutes early.  We ordered the fried eggplant/zucchini chips appetizer, grilled octopus appetizer, Greek salad, lamb shank with noodles, chicken souvlaki with rice, and seafood brochettes (shrimp, scallops, salmon, calamari) over rice.  The portions were generous and the prices were not that bad for the area.  I really enjoyed the grilled octopus and the seafood brochettes the most.  For dessert, we also ordered the walnut cake and they put a candle on it which was nice.  Service was attentive and very fast.  I would come back to try other dishes.

Amorino Gelato is a whole lot of fun.  If you're coming here, you're coming to get their gelato flower (gelato scooped into a cone in a shape of a flower) and really no other reason.  It's a good enough reason to come.The menu has your standard selection of gelato and sorbet.  You order as many flavors as you want and then one of their staff will craft a flower on a cone.  It's pretty impressive and fun to eat.  The gelato here tastes pretty good although they could probably use some larger variety in flavors (lots of versions of chocolate and nut flavors) but maybe that was just what was there the day we went.  Decor is bright and modern.  This location has large glass doors that open up the entire space so people off the street can easily see what's going on and come in.  Staff is really friendly and patient in explaining everything.  Great dessert place, thumbs up.

I've been a patron of this gem for decades, and after a recent visit following a long hiatus, I'm pleased to report that the restaurant continues to delight with delectable fare at affordable prices. Their classic falafel sandwich is a standout, offering both healthful nourishment and flavorful joy, brimming with fresh ingredients. It's a testament to their enduring commitment to quality.

Title: A Culinary Gem on a Dreary Day

My visit to Yin Ji on a cold Sunday afternoon was nothing short of a dining delight. The highlight was the heartwarming congee, priced between $5-$6 – an unbelievable bargain for the hearty portions provided.

My friend and I also indulged in their famous chang fen, choosing the one with marinated pork and shrimp with chives. It's easy to see why they're celebrated for this dish. The meat was impeccably cooked, and the soy sauce added a unique smoky essence that elevated the entire experience. While the noodle's delicate nature led to some structural compromise, this was a minor quibble in an otherwise delightful dish.

Regrettably, we missed the opportunity to try their famed Hong Kong style milk tea, which had already sold out. This gives us the perfect excuse to return. Yin Ji offers exceptional value and delectable cuisine, firmly establishing itself as a must-visit spot for both comfort food aficionados and budget-conscious diners alike.

This is a small hole-in-the-wall that specializes in all day dim sum. All items are freshly steamed as you order so please be patient as freshly steamed dim sum is always worth the wait.The BLANCHED SEASONAL VEGETABLE dish was the star of the day. They were not the usual Chinese broccoli that you find in most places, but were authentic baby YAU CHOI that were very fresh and had a distinct sweetness.BEEF BALLS: These were also my favorite of the day as they did NOT have any after taste of tenderizer or soda powder typically found in most dim sum places.PORK SPARE RIBS WITH RICE: The spare ribs were fall-off-the-bone tender and delicious. Rice was good - actually better than the one we had at THW the previous day.SIU MAI: It was yummy with natural flavors and without any or much MSG. The dumpling was made with mostly lean meat and I like its texture as well as its quality.HAR GOW: They are quite good but nevertheless my least favorite dish of the day. Everything was good, such as the thin, translucent, and slightly chewy skin. But it was probably made with either some fish sauce or shrimp sauce that gave the dumpling a fishy taste that I didn't like.Overall, a nice local dim sum gem that I would definitely revisit the next time I find myself in the street of NYC's Chinatown.

I do love Sugarfish and I gave the other location, near Flatiron, 5 stars. However, this one was a little lower in quality, perhaps because this one is newer.The food tastes the same. It uses the same fresh ingredients. The fish is wonderfully paired with minimal sauces and toppings. Those already paired are to be eaten like that and not dipped in any soy sauce. The rice is warm and it's a nice touch, although keep in mind that it falls apart easily! We both got the regular Trust Me. It's served in 6 different courses. It includes the:-Edamame-Tuna Sashimi-Salmon, Albacore, Yellowtail, Sea Bass, Sea Bream sushi-Toro, Crab HandrollsEverything is simplistic and delicious, but I found these cuts lower in quality than the other location. Look at my pictures, especially the Yellowtail and SeaBass sushi. The fish is jagged, misshapen, and small. Compared to the other location, where the pieces were smoother and more uniform. I still do like Sugarfish, but there are a lot of other different great sushi options in NYC. However, the best thing about Sugarfish is that it's very reasonably priced for sushi in NYC. It was about $40ish (tip already included) for a Trust Me option. Comparison: Spring Street is a little out of the way, while the Flatiron one has a more central location. The service here was not as good, a little more impersonal. Also the bathroom here (in the back) was just not clean while the other location's bathroom was spotless. The plus side here is that it's less busy. The Flatiron location always has a long wait but we were seated here as soon as we walked in! It's definitely a trade-off, but if you are in this area and don't want a long wait time, go here. Still wonderful food. We love every course, especially the handrolls!

Title: Mixed Feelings During Restaurant Week

My Restaurant Week experience at this charming spot was a blend of highs and lows. The staff’s warmth added a lively buzz to our Friday evening, further enhanced by the delightful weather and the pleasant outdoor seating.

The three-course meal kicked off on a high note with a shrimp appetizer that was the star of the night – four well-dressed shrimps with a refreshing apple and mint combination. However, the branzino that followed didn't match up; despite being perfectly cooked, its simplicity left me wanting more, especially since it was paired with just a modest serving of vegetables and a nondescript sauce.

Ending on a dessert that failed to impress, my expectations of a French restaurant's finesse in sweets were not met. Both in taste and presentation, it was average and not something I'd anticipate at a higher-end dining establishment.

In summary, while the ambiance and service were spot-on, the Restaurant Week menu didn't quite deliver the value expected from its price point.
Love this place! The atmosphere is amazing and food is absolutely delicious! The severs are knowledgeable and made our experience a great one! Order the homemade pop tart! It's to die for!!!

Title: Quick Bite, Quality Slice

Don't let the queue deter you; this pizza spot runs like a well-oiled machine, swiftly moving customers from the line to savoring their slice. At $4 a pop, the pizza doesn't just offer value for money—it's downright delicious.

I indulged in the meat combo, which was a carnivore's delight, and nibbled on the equally tasty white cheese variation. The selection caters to vegetarians too, with tempting options like mozzarella basil and spinach. 

The establishment likely won't be your choice for a leisurely sit-down meal since table space is at a premium, but turnover is quick. We snagged a high top outdoors for a casual dining experience—complete with handy tableside seasonings like garlic and chili pepper to tweak your slice to perfection. 

Overall, a stellar choice for a quick and satisfying pizza fix!

Title: A Letdown at a Former Favorite

I recently visited a restaurant that I had often recommended, expecting the usual delightful experience. However, this time was met with disappointment. Arriving at 12 pm for lunch, my excitement quickly faded when the clam chowder was served. Unfortunately, it lacked any discernible flavor and was not served hot, a basic expectation for any soup.

Compelled by the situation, especially since I was hosting a client, I considered asking for a replacement but felt too embarrassed to do so. This hesitancy was a result of my prior endorsements of the place.

Further discontent arose with the Lobster Mac and Cheese. While it had a decent taste, the lukewarm serving temperature was a setback and the cheese, although melted, failed to offer the anticipated stringiness of a well-prepared dish.

These experiences led me to wonder if the restaurant's recent expansion to multiple locations has impacted its ability to maintain consistent quality. Regrettably, this visit tarnished the high regard I once had for this establishment.

I really enjoyed Good Night Sonny. This wasn't the first place on our list for date night, but the place we had chosen did not have oysters, so we went down my list of must try oyster spots and GNS has been on that list for awhile.What an unexpected treat. Now, I got to put it out there that this is really a place for people who drink, and looking to have a bit of food with their libations. It's small and quaint, but gets a very lively crowd that packs them in. That said, for two non-drinkers, we felt quite at home, and enjoyed the atmosphere. It's definitely not the place to go if you want an intimate setting, but it's the perfect place for a couple like us who were looking for a light bite (and oysters) before catching a date night movie.I loved that they offered a nice selection of oysters, which they make accessible during their happy hour oyster special. You get the same oysters at 6 p.m. that you would at 10 p.m. They're a hearty bunch and offer a great balance of east and west coast, and not the usual frumpy offerings. I chose to let our waiter do the choosing, and I must say he chose quite well.The menu is somewhat limited. But, again, it's not the draw. The oysters, the atmosphere and place to hang and chill with friends is what makes Good Night Sonny the kind of place you're never quite ready to say good night to ...

We were able to easily make reservations on Yelp and secure a dinner spot for a group of 6 for Friday night. Ease of last minute reservation was a huge plus!Started off with a cheese and meat plate and also ordered two family pizzas. Each family size pizza can choose up to 3 flavors. Ordered one margarita and one mixed flavor. Each family was about 12 pieces total. The pizzas were solid but definitely on the really pricy side for pizza. They have both indoor and outdoor seating. We opted for indoor seating which is air conditioned, but indoors is also extremely loud since sound seems to echo everywhere. Outdoors is definitely preferred if the weather permits.

Momofuku Noodle Bar didn't disappoint !Lunch on a weekday at 12pm. No wait. Very efficient service.Strtrd sith the classic pork bun (2 pieces). Then tried pork ramen and scallion noodles. Both very good. Large portions $50 total. Definitely a great addition to the Time Warner center.

I recently dined at a noteworthy midtown lunch destination specializing in Vietnamese fare, notable for its banh mi and rice bowls. The establishment boasts a clean, modern interior with plenty of seating. Its self-ordering kiosks are user-friendly, ensuring the line progresses swiftly—I received my meal within five minutes of ordering.

I opted for the JoJu bowl, enhanced with a runny egg and spring rolls. The caramel pork's sweetness flawlessly complemented the Vietnamese sausage's saltiness. The addition of the runny egg was a stroke of genius, elevating the entire dish. The serving size was satisfying without being overwhelming. I left satiated and looking forward to my next visit to explore more of their menu.

Tucked away as a small hole-in-the-wall establishment, this place is a hidden gem for pizza aficionados on a budget. The dollar slice on offer here is a revelation – with just $5 in your pocket, you can indulge in a feast fit for royalty. The pizza boasts a delicious trio of well-balanced cheese, tangy sauce, and perfectly baked bread that come together in each bite to deliver harmony to your taste buds. For a quick, satisfying, and wallet-friendly meal, this spot is a must-visit.

Very nice Greek spot on 14th and 1st. The lunch special of grilled shrimp with a side of potatoes was great. The small greek salad is huge.  I couldn't finish it. Comped bread perfectly crisp. Comped yogurt with cherries delicious. Nice touch. Liked the greek music piped in.Good serviceWould come back when in the area.

Title: A Delight for the Senses at a Vibrant Eatery

I recently enjoyed a wonderful dining experience where both the service and the cuisine stood out. The waitstaff was exceptionally attentive, ensuring that our food arrived swiftly and with great courtesy. 

The meal started with a delightful serving of bread and butter, followed by a selection of tea sandwiches. While each was tasty, the chicken salad sandwiches were a highlight—I’d recommend doubling up on those in place of the salmon for future visits. To accompany the meal, I savored both hot tea and chai, each perfectly brewed and comforting.

The ambiance is truly a feast for the eyes, largely thanks to the bold and vibrant artwork of Ashley Longshore, which gives the space a unique and joyful character.

At around $40, the experience was quite a bargain, considering the quality of food, service, and surroundings. I am eager to return to this gem of a restaurant.

Place was pretty good and for $50 would normally say totally worth it. Fish quality in general  Rey good although certain pieces were colder than I would normally like.  Part of the issue was that I was only one seated for the 5 pm seating and rapidly finessed( out the door at 5:15!). After eating the 12 Pieces I realized that I was still really hungry, so this didn't come close to being a filling meal. I think there are better values in the city. I would rather pay up for the primo experience or pay less and have very good sushi, but not omakase.

Tucked away near Columbia, this buzzing burger/bar joint offers a relaxed setting with sports on the screen, creating a cool, laidback vibe. With no reservations needed, it's a perfect casual haunt for a spontaneous bite. The expanded menu features plenty of bar food favorites, but it's the burgers that truly shine. On recent visits, the widowmaker (a decadent mac n'cheese and bacon combination) and the hot mess (a spicy mix of jalapeño, bacon, and Monterey Jack) along with the sweet potato fries, were particularly satisfying. To top it off, their spiked "siberian husky" milkshake, blending cookie monster ice cream with Kahlua and vodka, was an indulgent treat. A great spot for a weekday dinner, this place comes highly recommended, though expect a livelier scene with college crowds come the weekend.

Title: Cozy Spot for a Weekend Brunch

My visit to this restaurant on a Saturday noon was a pleasant experience. We were greeted with immediate seating, which was a relief considering it was the weekend. The establishment boasts two separate dining rooms, providing ample space that prevented it from feeling overcrowded.

The wait staff was efficient and provided satisfactory service. I opted for the classic bagel with cream cheese, while my husband chose the breakfast sandwich. Both dishes were decent and met our expectations for a simple brunch.

What stood out were the cocktails - they were a creative twist to our midday meal, adding an interesting element to our overall dining experience. 

Would recommend for a no-fuss, enjoyable weekend meal.

Absolutely adore this gem in NYC! With an interior that dazzles, it stands out as one of the city's most beautiful dining spots. The service is top-notch, and the red curry never disappoints with its perfect spice level. Pairing it with a Singha beer has become my ritual here. It's without a doubt one of my all-time favorite New York haunts, and I'm always eager for my next visit. Highly recommended!

Title: A Delightful Culinary Journey at The Tang - Upper West Side

Review:
I am enamored with The Tang's Upper West Side location, which exudes a more upscale and airy atmosphere compared to the familiar intimacy of their East Village spot. A central open kitchen captivates diners, offering a glimpse into the culinary artistry that distinguishes this establishment.

My boyfriend and I embarked on a flavorful adventure, sharing an array of dishes that were nothing short of divine. At $15, Tang's Herbal Chicken Noodle Soup became my comforting favorite, boasting a herbal broth so immaculate and flavorful, capable of curing any ailment or lifting spirits on a dreary day. The chicken thigh melded tenderness with chewy noodles, making this dish a contender against my all-time favorite, their Drunk Noodles.

The Fried Tiger Prawn with Salted Egg Yolk ($18) is an unequivocal must-try. The prawns' crisply seasoned skin, coupled with salted egg yolk and the sweetness of pineapple bits beneath, created a harmonious fusion of flavors. The Braised Pork Knuckle ($12) transported me back to Taiwan with its velvety meat and rich sauce, evoking a comforting sense of nostalgia.

Curiosity led me to the Roasted Beef Bone Marrow ($15), which was an absolute revelation when paired with scallion pancakes and zesty red wine vinegar sauce. This distinct combination is highly recommended for its delightful innovation.

An unexpected perk was the complimentary ice cream for checking in on Yelp. The taro and lychee flavors were exceptional - rich and chewy, reminiscent of gelato, and arguably the best I've ever tasted.

The Tang's well-curated menu, reasonable prices, and beautiful interior design, including an immaculate bathroom, all contribute to a restaurant experience that is truly enjoyable. Additionally, Yelp reservations add convenience to the overall stellar experience. I wholeheartedly recommend The Tang to anyone seeking a taste of exquisite Asian cuisine, and I am eager to return and share this gem with visiting friends.

Title: A Taste of Spain with Premium Prices

I recently dined at a restaurant that offers a true Spanish culinary experience, albeit with a hefty price tag. The food quality was commendable, earning a solid 4 out of 5, particularly for the authenticity and flavor that would remind one of Madrid's finest. The service was exceptional, nearly perfect and close to a 5-star rating.

Despite the high quality, the prices can be startling, with a small serving of squid in rice with squid ink reaching $40, which I feel merits a 3 for value. However, if you do decide to indulge, I recommend not missing the Tocino del Cielo for dessert – best enjoyed inside where you can savor it comfortably.

The menu has highlights such as the Ibulli shrimp, an expensive yet worthy experience, and a notable pan con tomate accompanied by anchovies. The alternative squid dish served on sliced potatoes also stands out, offering more substance than the aforementioned rice dish.

This establishment differentiates itself from the typical tapas joint; from a unique pan con tomate to unconventional squid preparations, each dish presents a twist on the familiar. The black ink rice, despite its price, is as genuine as what you might find in a reputable Spanish restaurant.

In summary, the experience is a mix of authentic flavors and premium pricing. It's definitely worth a visit for the food and service, but be prepared for some sticker shock when the bill arrives.

Last weekend's brunch at this bustling spot was a delightful surprise. Despite the crowd, my friend and I opted for bar seating and were promptly rewarded with exceptional service. We indulged in buffalo wings, perfectly poached eggs with grilled tomato and haloumi, and the savory madame freda. Each dish was a flavorful journey, cooked to perfection. The attentive staff even treated us to complimentary fries. All in all, a highly recommended experience for a satisfying meal and impeccable service.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Roast Kitchen

I recently visited a different location of Roast Kitchen, hoping for a better experience than my previous visits to the chain. Unfortunately, this visit did little to change my opinion. Confusion abounded when, after ordering, I was directed to the opposite end of the restaurant without explanation, only to discover it was the payment area. To add to my dismay, the price for a salad was an astonishing $14. While the taste was satisfactory, the value for money simply wasn't there. Regrettably, this will be my last visit to Roast Kitchen.

Tucked away on the Upper East Side, NR is a gem that transports diners straight to the Meiji era of Japan with its authentic décor and vibrant atmosphere. This period marked Japan's transition into a global powerhouse, and NR embodies that spirit through a perfect fusion of tradition and innovation.

Owned by Shige, an alum of the famed Japanese speakeasy Angel's Share, NR doesn't just promise an experience—it delivers. The cocktail menu here is crafted with the precision and creativity one would expect from such a prestigious lineage, each drink an impeccable blend of flavors that might even eclipse those of its mentor establishment.

As for the food, NR's ramen is nothing short of divine. The broths are rich, the noodles perfectly chewy, and the toppings meticulously chosen to create a slurp-worthy bowl every time. And for night owls or those looking to cap off an evening of fun, the ramen service extends until midnight on weekends, solidifying NR as the ultimate late-night haunt.

In summary, whether you're chasing the ultimate ramen bowl, savoring sophisticated cocktails, or simply looking to revel in a bit of history, NR stands out as a premier destination that satisfies on all fronts.

Love the name of this Indian restaurant in the West Village! I came here with a friend for dinner on a Friday night and even though it's a small place, we were seated immediately. Inside, it is cool and comfortable. I ordered a mango lassi (one of my favorite drinks!) and lamb korma. The mango lassi came in a lovely rounded square shaped glass. It was a lovely bright orange color and quite thick, just the way I like it. The drink was refreshing and sweet.The lamb korma came in a metal bowl and had sliced almonds sprinkled on top. There was plenty of delicious tasting sauce, which had strong flavors of cashew and saffron. The sauce was beautifully smooth. There were plenty of pieces of lamb, which was incredibly tender, juicy and soaked up the sauce really well. This also came with white rice which complemented the dish perfectly.My friend ordered some naan bread, which was served warm and was thin, slightly crispy with butter on top. Very yummy! There was no bathroom to be seen, but we were allowed to use one in the back. However to get to it, we had to walk through the kitchen which was kind of awkward. The service was great. Our waiter was very nice and on top of it. I do think the pricing is a little high, but to be expected given the neighborhood. I would return to share the tandoori sampler which comes with all different types of meat and naan!

*full disclosure: i am not a luxury diner*Came here for a special occasion and had the most amazing meal!! I didn't even know tempura omakase was a thing but -- why wouldnt it be??By my count we had 10 tempuras & an uni one (for an extra charge). They were all astounding but my top three would have to be: shrimp, belt fish, and crab in that order. The shrimp highlighted everything perfect about shrimp in general and was a reminder as to why i fell in love with shrimp to begin with. It was my first time having belt fish and although i don't generally care for fish, this one was just the perfect texture and just bouncy enough. And crab, well, i love crab. I feel that with these kind of "set meals" there are bound to be a dish or two you don't care much for, but i thorougly enjoyed every piece of the meal and was also pleasantly quite full at the end.

The first time I had this gelato was in Italy so I was thrilled to see it in NYC! This is right in theTheater District. The decor is the same as Italy-modern with  wood accents to bring some warmth. Coffee and tea are available as well as pastries. The pastries looked good. There are several coffee variations including affogato. The real star is the gelato! It's creamy but light. I had the small with 3 flavors-vanilla, chocolate and amarena cherry. All were yummy! The amarena had cherries, the vanilla tasted tasted like it was made with vanilla bean and the chocolate was decadent! You can get a cone or cup. I highly recommend the cone because it's shaped like a flower! You can even add a macaroon!The store was clean. There were some tables in the back. You go to the counter and pay. You order your flavors when it's being scooped. The line was long but moved fast. Highly recommend!!

This week I made my second trip ever to tasty hand pulled noodles! This place is located on Doyers street so if you're not familiar with the area it can be a little hard to find since it's a twist and a turn off of a Main Street on a small side street that at times does not have through traffic and is set up with tables along the street and the street may even be painted. Anyway ... this is a no frills kind of place they stick you where they have room for you ... last time I went during a busy Saturday and was seated in the basement this time I sat upstairs... which I much preferred. Their noodles are fresh made to order and some of the best in the Chinatown area I think when going to a place called tasty Handpulled noodles you should in fact GET THE NOODLES you won't be disappointed. I like that you have many thicknesses that you can choose from I prefer the big wide ones. I will definitely come back just for them.

If you're seeking the epitome of comfort food, look no further. This go-to spot serves up a mean bowl of wonton noodle soup partnered with either mouthwatering grilled pork or succulent duck, both of which are super delicious and highly recommended. In addition to their slurp-worthy noodles, the fried rice is a revelation – definitely a must-try. Though they offer dim sum, I'd suggest skipping it as it doesn't quite hit the mark; it's a bit on the mediocre side. Service is passable – nothing to write home about, but the heavenly flavors more than compensate for any lack in that department. Overall, a thumbs up for the food that truly warms the soul!

Hello Yelp friends! Quick update, this business is closed! Nope, not sad about it- just sad that they were a total disappointment especially in the last few weeks of remaining open.... good riddance! 3 stars for the excellent service, great table (upstairs) and attempt at being one of the best burgers in NYC. I'm very sad to report we were not impressed, the burger was mediocre and dry :( very sad to be feeling this way after dying to try it! Maybe it was an off night? Im not sure... the fries are more like chips they are very crunchy and are more pretty/decorative than satisfying. Per waiters recommendation we did try the sheep's  milk ricotta Gnudi to start. This was delicious and very different. Almost like gnocchi but instead filled with ricotta. Sauce was flavorful and the dish is a perfect starter to share. Our glasses of wine were good and the restaurant itself is kind of romantic with pig's everywhere. So cute! As for my heart, it's hurting... I wanted to like this burger so much.
Great Chinese crepes. Excellent for breakfast. Good for a quick snack. Freshly made, with choice of toppings. Also serve hot pot.

Title: A Slice of Home at New York's Finest

If a place could embody the nostalgic flavors of childhood and the essence of New York in a single bite, Pizza Palace is it. As a native New Yorker who grew up under the Miami sun, I've maintained a delicious tradition – a pilgrimage back to my all-time favorite pizza joint with every visit to the Big Apple. 

This isn't your average pizza spot; it's a neighborhood gem crafting the most authentic New York-style pizza that remains unrivaled. The secret? Impeccably balanced sauce atop a perfectly baked crust with just the right amount of chew and char, all smothered in gloriously stretchy cheese.

It's more than just the pizza that keeps me coming back for more – it's the ritual of pairing that heavenly slice with a refreshing kiwi strawberry Snapple that completes the experience. The lengths I've gone to satisfy my cravings, including having my aunt freeze and fly a slice to Miami, is a testament to Pizza Palace's irresistible allure.

With service as warm as the pies they serve, the staff at Pizza Palace aren't just employees; they're like family, making every visit memorable. This isn't just my forever pizza place; it's a slice of home. Love, A Forever Pizza Palace Fan.

During restaurant week, my friend and I had the pleasure of lunching at the Michelin-starred Ai Fiori, a gem tucked away on the second floor of an upscale hotel. Without reservations, we were seated at the spacious and comfortable bar, though the dining area seemed welcoming yet surprisingly not bustling.

The prix-fixe menu offered incredible value—$26 for two courses or $32 for three. I started with the insalata, which, despite being well-composed, tilted too sour for my palate. My friend's poached egg in a tomato-esque soup shared the same tartness but was otherwise satisfying.

The main course saw my selection of a beautifully cooked medium-rare meat with a delectable side of potatoes—simplicity marrying freshness in every bite. In contrast, my friend's shrimp dish triumphed in taste, laid on a bed of peppers and olives, but the portion might leave some desiring more.

To conclude, the creatively presented cake was a delight though the $6 supplement gave me pause, even if it was still a bargain compared to their regular prices.

In summary, Ai Fiori offered a dining experience worth savoring, especially for those looking to indulge in high-end fare at a steal during restaurant week.

Upon my recent visit to this charming little establishment, I was immediately struck by its modest size, which, far from being a limitation, contributed to its cozy and homely ambiance. The old-fashioned decor added a delightful touch of nostalgia to the overall dining experience.

From the moment I walked in, the hostesses greeted me with exceptional warmth, making me feel like a valued guest rather than a mere customer. This level of service was pleasantly surprising and set the tone for a relaxing meal.

As for the meal itself, I opted for the spinach omelet, which was served with a dollop of sour cream. The flavors were well-balanced, and the omelet was cooked to perfection—a delightful blend of wholesome ingredients that left me thoroughly satisfied.

An added bonus to the visit was the extra shot I received for checking in—a small gesture that was much appreciated and one that will surely encourage patrons to return.

Overall, my experience was a positive one. This restaurant offers good food, a friendly atmosphere, and attentive service. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Thai Cuisine - Yuqi's

I stumbled upon Yuqi's in my search for a new go-to lunch delivery spot in Manhattan and it didn't just meet my expectations—it soared above them. Having been underwhelmed by local Thai offerings, Yuqi's was a delightful surprise, and easily tops my list for Thai cuisine in the area.

My first order, the Pork Pad Kra Tiem lunch special with a side of veggie soup, was a revelation. The dish featured a generous portion, a robust and garlicky sauce, and was packed with an array of fresh vegetables. It struck the perfect balance of flavor without being overpowering in sodium.

The traditional fried rice on my second order was just as impressive, accompanied again by a satisfying veggie soup. It's clear that Yuqi's pays attention to taste and quality.

I am already planning my next meal from Yuqi's and looking forward to the experience of dining in. For anyone craving authentic Thai flavors, Yuqi's is a must-try.

Title: Classic Comfort with Stellar Service

My date and I ushered in the new year with a visit to this restaurant on a bustling Saturday evening. Our quest for traditional fare was met with resounding success. The standout of the night has to be the hearty chicken parmigiana, oozing with cheese and served alongside a comforting side of pasta—a dish whose generous proportions justified its price tag. 

The Chilean sea bass, albeit a tad on the smaller side, was an exquisite choice, masterfully cooked to a flaky finish. The sauce draping the dish provided a pleasant tang that beautifully harmonized with the delicate fish and earthy shiitake mushrooms.

Service was seamless, adding to the welcoming clubhouse ambiance that envelops you upon entry. While our table did not indulge in the steaks, I couldn't help but notice the enviable cuts at neighboring tables, suggesting a revisitation might be in order.

In conclusion, the restaurant delivered an impeccable dining experience with flavors that stand testament to their classic culinary approach.

Tucked away near Lincoln Center, this Mexican gem offers a delightful casual dining experience with an affordable touch, rare to find in NYC. Expect to spend around $40 per person, margarita included, which is quite reasonable for the area. 

The interior exudes charm, complemented by excellent service and a cool, inviting atmosphere. Our evening began with skinny margaritas paired with fresh guacamole and chips, a truly delightful start. 

The nachos, cleverly stacked for maximum flavor and presentation, impressed us as much as the taste did. The street taco plates, featuring a mix of succulent steak and pork, were devoured effortlessly by our group, a testament to their deliciousness. 

Overall, this spot stands out as an affordably priced destination for a satisfying Mexican meal in New York City. It's definitely on my list for a repeat visit.

Title: A Chinatown Gem Serving Unforgettable Pad Thai

My experience at this charming spot in Chinatown was exceptional, making it an ideal place for a late dinner or a round of drinks. With an ambiance that exudes coziness, it's a little slice of culinary heaven where I savored what I can confidently say is the best pad thai I've ever had. The crispy pork belly was another delightful dish that left a lasting impression on my palate. Generous portion sizes ensured that we left with a takeaway for the next day—a bonus to an already fantastic meal. The insatiable craving for that pad thai is a testament to the quality of the food, and I eagerly anticipate my next visit. Highly recommended for anyone wanting to indulge in top-tier Asian cuisine.

Restaurant looked cute on the outside and inside. The inside is very modern  and hip. Instagram worthy wall that says crazy rich  broth. The bathroom is where they probably put their best design at because it is beautiful. Check it out. Anyways back to the food. I got the classic pho and was not impressed. There's lots of cheaper pho spots that make pho much better. Maybe it's because I didn't get the pho where the broth is marinated for x amount of hours? The spring rolls were pretty good and let's just say I never got the Thai iced tea I ordered so can't say much about that.

As usual Virgil said not disappoint everything was great from the drinks (fall off the porch is not as strong as it used to be !) to the brisket and mac & cheese and a dessert. The fruit cobbler was amazing and went so great with the ice cream just wish there was a better ice cream to cobbler ratio, I felt cheated of the ice cream!  Our waitress was also very kind she was the Latina who works Friday nights on the downstairs floor. If this Virgil's wasn't so over priced I would come here more often. This is the primary reason why I gave it a 4 star because it's over priced which is understandable because of the location.

This is my go-to spot when I'm craving a comforting bowl of Khao Soi. It's just what the doctor ordered, and will always be a standout dish for me at P&K. However, when we went last weekend we fell in love with the Braised Beef Red Curry. It was so deliciously rich, with tender chunks of beef, and swirls of coconut milk in the curry. We had it with their coconut sticky rice, which was honestly such a treat that I could have had it all on its own, no entree needed. However, when the spiciness of the red curry soaks into the sweetness of the coconut rice, amazing things happen! What a truly divine dish. Go order it. Now. Papaya salad was pretty good. I'd say it was standard - not quite as memorable as the Khao Soi or Red Curry, but still quite tasty. Cocktails were fresh and flavorful, and ambience is great if you're looking for an upbeat, lively night out. It's often busy here, and loud, but that just adds to the fun vibe. Definitely make a reservation if you can.Will be back for sure!

I came here with my boyfriend and we got a 2 flavor pot. One side was the traditional malatang, and the other side was the pork bone broth. We ordered beef tendon, spicy pork ribs, crown daisies, cabbage, king oyster mushrooms, kung fu tripe, marbling beef, and shrimp. All of the veggies are very fresh. Unfortunately, the beef was frozen, which alters the cooking time. We had a couple pieces which were either still frozen inside, or beyond overcooked. The shrimp and beef tendon were the highlights of the meal. The shrimp were so sweet and the beef tendon was delicious.The service is attentive and the space is nice and bright. I would recommend coming here with smaller groups for an intimate experience!

This is one of those trendy restaurants that you come to visit one time for the experience. Has a cool vibe and all, but the wait/crowd and the quality of food isn't something I'd come regularly for. First off, extremely close quarters inside. We came on a Thursday and it seemed super packed, like to capacity. I thought it was just the entrance that was extremely tight, but it extends throughout the dining area. If you extend your elbow too much, you might be getting friendly with the person next to you. Second, service wasn't the swiftest. Our server took 15 minutes to ask for our order and food took another 20+ min (apps) to come out. Now for the food: *Spare rib on sugar cane skewer ($10): was pretty good (small portion), not sure I would get again simply due to the amount of meat your get for the price. *CALAMARI: the softest calamari I have ever had. Definitely the highlight of my meal*Beef panang was ok, not bad, but not the best. Could have used more spices IMO. *Lobster pad thai: the lobster itself added a lot of flavor to the dish. Would get this again.FYI, if you make reservations they don't seat you until your whole party is there and if you are even a few minutes late - they will give away your reservation because that's how packed they are.

Xi'an Famous Foods stands out for its no-frills approach to traditional flavors, offering simple and affordable options that highlight the true taste of Xi'an. While the menu may seem extensive, dishes tend to be variations on a theme. I highly recommend choosing the dry versions of their dishes; the soups tend to dilute the experience, whereas the dry options let the sauce shine. The spicy cumin lamb noodles are a standout – perfectly cooked with a sauce that's rich and satisfying. 

The eatery itself is modest, with minimal seating – best suited for solo diners or small groups up to four, or simply grab your meal to-go. It's the ideal spot for a quick, delicious bite without breaking the bank – expect to spend less than $10 for a meal that's authentically delightful.

Title: Mixed Feelings on a Stormy Mother's Day Feast

My family and I ventured uptown this Mother's Day, braving an unseasonably bitter mix of wind and rain, in search of a comforting meal at a restaurant known for its Szechuan, dim sum, and Shanghainese offerings. Expectations were high, but unfortunately, the food failed to warm our spirits.

The teenagers in our party may argue otherwise with their preference for the Chicken with Dried Orange Peel and Sesame Beef, but I found these dishes disappointingly lacking in their namesake proteins and overpowered by sweetness and excessive sauce.

The culinary highlights were few but notable, including the savory Ning-Style Steamed Gluten (Kao Fu), succulent Braised "Lion Head" Meatballs, and the simple yet perfectly sautéed Snow Pea Shoots. However, the Dried Braised Whole Fish with noodles was a letdown, its sweetness overshadowing the other flavors.

Our meal was further marred by our seating arrangement in a basement-like setting that seemed neglected by the staff. Oddly enough, the oversized lazy Susan at our table seemed to have a mind of its own, possibly due to an uneven floor, which made dish selection an unintended game of speed and dexterity.

The silver lining of our luncheon was a modest 10% discount from a Yelp check-in, a small consolation for an overall mediocre dining experience. My takeaway from this outing is a renewed appreciation for the authentic and less pretentious offerings found in Chinatown. Regrettably, this was a first and final visit for me.

After a long day of sightseeing on the Big Bus, we found ourselves at Applebee's for a much-needed quick bite and respite. Dude opted for a delightful combo of chicken fajita and chicken tortilla soup, while I chose the comforting tomato basil soup paired with chicken cheese penne. Both choices proved to be the perfect pick-me-ups, hitting the spot and recharging us for the rest of the day's adventures. Applebee's truly delivered just what we needed.

Came here for happy hour, okay cute place. Service was quite slow on a sunday. Duck Wing : very tender and good flavor hut sauce a bit too heavyShishito Pepper : very tiny protein and greesyPoutin Fries : not bad

Title: A Culinary Gem with a Service Stumble

I recently visited a restaurant that can only be described as a hidden culinary treasure, perfectly poised between simplicity and complexity. Each dish is an addictive masterpiece, striking a rare balance that leaves you both satisfied and yearning for more. The food isn't just good, it's an experience: every bite is a study in flavor that I already crave to repeat.

However, despite the kitchen's triumph, the dining experience is marred by disappointing service inconsistencies. The staff, often sequestered in what seems to be their private enclave, seemingly forget the art of attentiveness. This lax attitude extends to the awkward absence of a restroom within the restaurant. Patrons are expected to navigate through bustling mall traffic just for a bathroom break, an inconvenience that feels out of step with the luxury pricing of the menu.

Moreover, the expansive private dining room—often empty—suggests a misallocation of valuable space. It's a frustrating sight when such areas could enhance customer comfort and streamline the dining process instead of serving as an employee lounge.

In summary, while the cuisine is undeniably exquisite, the restaurant needs to refine its service and reconsider its use of space to provide an experience that matches the quality of its offerings.

Recently, a new Japanese eatery opened up near the hospital, filling a much-needed gap for this delectable cuisine. Its bright orange facade is eye-catching—a good thing, as it's easy to miss otherwise. The friendly staff welcomed me into a place offering a diverse menu, although, to my surprise, sushi lovers might find the selection less roll-centric than anticipated. Ready-to-go items might be the compromise here.

I indulged in the jumbo shrimp shumai, gyoza, and scallion pancakes—all sizable and scrumptious, with the shumai being a standout hit. A slight critique would be the heavy-handedness with oil; a lighter touch would be appreciated. Considering it's Manhattan, the prices strike a reasonable balance. Overall, a worthy spot for Japanese cuisine aficionados.

Delicious! Such an amazing lunch deal for around $9! I ordered the drunken noodles with spring rolls! The staff was very kind om the phone and when I went to pick up my order. One thing that was weird was the fact that I got only got ONE spring roll. I wonder if it's always like this or or it was a mistake? I would've given five stars, but I feel a bit skimped out. Either way. I'll definitely be ordering again!

From the moment you walk in the front door you are treated like family. We started off at the bar for some Happy Hour drinks, which were strong, great pours and well made. And then wound up staying for dinner. The food was great, as was our server, and the management was on top of everything. I really enjoyed their veggie burger and of course the Brussels sprouts... that's always my test, it seems.The place is cozy and can get a bit crowded, but it is always comfortable, and that's how you're made to feel. If I lived in the city this would be my go-to, regular bar. Such a great vibe. Cheers and thank you!

Title: A Cozy Thai Delight on the Upper West Side – Thai Market

I recently visited Thai Market for a ladies' night dinner and the experience was delightful. Nestled conveniently off the 1 subway line on the Upper West Side, this restaurant captivates with its contemporary decor featuring Thai life, complete with whimsical umbrellas suspended from the ceiling.

Despite a rainy evening causing my friends to arrive late, the welcoming staff ensured a comfortable wait at the bar with tasty spring rolls—a crispy, vegetarian treat to start the night. The menu's newspaper-style format adds a unique touch to the usual array of Thai dishes, including vegetarian options ensuring everyone's needs are met.

For my main course, I indulged in Gai Rad Prik paired with a side of vegetables and white rice. The meal was a revelation—perfectly crispy fried chicken doused in a sublime mix of sweet chili and tamarind sauce, though the accompanying bok choy's soft texture slightly missed the mark for me.

My friends enjoyed their appetizers—fried calamari and Thai dumplings—and spoke highly of their Pad Thai entrees. One even ventured into dessert territory with a Lynchee Creme Brûlée that was as visually appealing as it was appetizing.

The service matched the quality of the food; our server was both patient and prompt, ensuring a smooth dining experience. Clean and artfully decorated, even the bathroom reflected the establishment's attention to detail.

Thai Market is undoubtedly a gem for a date night or a relaxed dinner with friends, offering great food, service, and atmosphere without the cacophony of noise often found in busy eateries. I am eager to return and would highly recommend it to anyone in search of a serene and satisfying Thai meal.

This place was exactly what we needed for our large group. You can call ahead and set a reservation but we just walked in. We were informed by the greeter outside about the extra space they had inside. From the outside it looked like your typical to go pizzeria, when you walk to the back there is way more seats. What also intrigued me was when the greeter mentioned fried Calzone. I told him that is all I need to know I'm going to try it. The food was fantastic, the fried calzone was so good I had to order it twice!! The margarita pizza was great as well. We finalized the food with Nutella pizza which was a hit with the kids. This place is run by true Italians in Little Italy. With many other places to get a bit of Italian food we are glad that we found this gem. Also I wanted to give full props to our waitress who took care of us and not only was she on top of everything to make sure we had but also surprised my mom with a candle and sang to make her day special. there was

Came here with my boyfriend and his mother and really loved the atmosphere!! I love the wood, trees, and lit up moon that really creates a nice environment for a good meal.However, the food was pretty middle of the road. We got a lot of things to split for the table.Bulgogi Hotstone Bowl - eh, this was just okay. Bulgogi is my favorite, I always try to get it when it's on the menu. This was probably the  most "meh" bulgogi I've ever gotten.Truffle fries - good, but nothing exciting. The fries have a "truffle essence" on them that definitely comes through flavor wise. They're not bland, just not great. Pork dumplings with soy garlic - this was probably our fault. There are two options for sauces and we went with the nonspicy one. However, I assumed that it would be a dipping sauce where it was actually cooked on the dumpling. They were good, just not what I was expecting.Chili shrimp with sweet and spicy chili sauce - one of the best things of the night! Perfectly breaded, nice and crispy, with a hint of heat from the sauce.Popcorn chicken with BBQ sriracha sauce - another one of my favorites. Very simple, but the portion is HUGE.Wings with soy garlic - delicious and crispy! Very, very good.Galbi bao buns - the absolute biggest disappointment of the night. Bao buns were *the reason* I was excited to eat here, and I didn't even finish half of one. It tasted like a more dry puck of a burger. 0/10To drink: ginger lemonades. Nice and refreshing!All in all, I really loved the ambiance. (Although I haven't mentioned it, the tables were pretty close to one another. I can see how when it gets busy you can potentially be rubbing elbows with the table behind you.) The food was pretty good, but for the price of everything, I won't think very worth it.

I thought the customer service was excellent, but I came for the wings. The wings were good, but honestly I had better. I ordered two of the BBQ flavor and the Spicy wings to go. I enjoyed the spicy the most. I wouldn't mind buying those again, because they tasted alot like your classic buffalo wings, but with a grilled smoked flavor to them, they were really good. As for the BBQ, they were just ok, I would pass on those, but I really did like thier signature BBQ sauce. It added a nice flavor to the wings. I don't think I will be running back to Mighty Quinn's anytime soon, but I wouldn't say that I would never return. Actually I would give it another try for the meats, but some of the sides look a lil questionable. So I won't count this place out just yet.F.Y.I.- I saw that they are hiring for positions, you should check their website if anyone is interested.

No complaints here. Service was fast and prices are reasonable. I got the curry chicken sandwich and asked for it to be spicy. Chicken was juicy, sauce was flavorful, the veggies tasted fresh, and the bread was crisp on the outside but soft on the inside. Although I think next time I'm going to ask for it to be extra spicy, because I think an extra kick would have been good.

Title: A Flavor Packed Evening Despite the Wait

My friends and I decided to explore a new culinary destination and landed at this bustling spot on a Friday night. True to its popularity, the wait time tested our patience—a little over an hour, thanks to a high-tech, QR code-based waitlist system that's available on-site (though it's unclear if it can be accessed beforehand).

From the exterior, the restaurant appears modest, but stepping inside reveals a spacious interior with an option for private back area seating, a pleasant surprise.

Once seated, we threw caution to the wind and asked our server to surprise us with the house favorites. The resulting feast included: pork trotter, matcha zang zang, soup dumplings, duck, peppercorn chicken, crab tofu, string beans with meat, and steamed dumplings. Most dishes packed a punch of heat, except for the soothing soup dumplings and rich, flavorful duck.

The stars of the night were the melt-in-your-mouth tofu and the exquisitely prepared pork trotter—both dishes earning a resounding 'must-try' from our table.

In summary, if you can brave the wait, this restaurant's extensive and fiery menu is sure to satisfy those with adventurous palates, with a few milder gems for balance.

I recently dined at a restaurant that truly felt like a hidden gem. The food was exceptional, with a cozy atmosphere that invited a return visit. Dinner service was particularly impressive; both the fillet and duck were standout dishes that I highly recommend for their perfect preparation.

Unfortunately, the breakfast experience didn't match up. Despite only ordering an omelette and granola, the service was noticeably slower, taking over an hour for our food to arrive. This was a stark contrast to the dinner service, which certainly set the bar high. 

In spite of the morning hiccup, the delectable dinner has me eager to return. It's a lovely spot that shines best in the evening.

Title: Cozy Spot for a Quick Noodle Fix

My dining experience at this sleek, albeit tiny, eatery near Tompkins Sq Park was a solid 3.5 out of 5. Arriving at 6pm on a Thursday with a friend, we were seated immediately, a welcome start. The minimalist interior boasts three tables, accommodating roughly 7-8 patrons.

The menu was straightforward with a single offering: beef noodle soup. While customizable with various spices and veggies for an extra charge, the core dish lacked the wow factor, especially considering the $15 price tag. Comparable bowls are readily available at nearly half that cost in Chinatown, questioning the value of this upscale rendition.

Service, however, was a high note—attentive and remarkable. The smoked plum juice was an enjoyable discovery, complementing the decent, though unremarkable, bowl of beef noodles.

In summary, despite the higher-than-average price for standard fare, this restaurant is a convenient choice for those in the area with a specific craving for beef noodles.

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Prince St Pizza

As a California native accustomed to exceptional cuisine, my expectations for food are notably high. However, Prince St Pizza has managed to set the bar even higher. During my culinary adventures in the city, I sampled slices from renowned spots like Joe's and Lombardi's, but none held a candle to Prince St Pizza.

I indulged in the pepperoni square, requested extra crispy, and the classic Prince St cheese pizza. To say I was blown away would be an understatement — it was, without hesitation, the best pizza experience of my life. The bold, rich, and robustly saucy flavors catapulted me into a state of bliss reminiscent of Remy from "Ratatouille" during his food-induced reveries.

Be prepared for a wait — I stood in line for a reasonable 20 to 25 minutes. Note that the eatery's cozy size doesn't accommodate indoor dining well. We braved the January chill to enjoy our slices al fresco, but it was a small price to pay for pizza perfection. Prince St Pizza is a must-visit for any pizza connoisseur.

After reading a lot of positive reviews about the Empire Steak House, we were eager to try it out during Restaurant Week. The place itself looks nice inside, but the first good impression was totally deceiving. We weren't offered a coat check which is weird in the middle of winter, but when I couldn't put anywhere my coat, they were able to squeeze it in somewhere. The waiters were negligent, inattentive and not polite. The broccoli soup was very good but the green salad is mediocre and the leafy greens weren't fresh. The bread basket was simply pathetic, apparently old and dry slices of bread were served. After my husband finished his salad with dressing, the waiter took his empty plate putting the dirty fork on the table! What the hell?! Don't they have a clean one to give it for the main dish?? The main for my husband was salmon which was okay, but my filet mignon was simply horrible. It smelled like burnt meat, and although it was entirely covered in a brown sauce, it was obvious from the smell and from the taste (!) that it was completely burnt, which is a total shame considering that this should be their absolute forte. Oh, and the steak knife I got was dirty, there was something like a leftover food on it... No one noticed it until I obviously asked for another one before starting to eat. The mashed potato and the broccolis were okay too (although adding the same side to ALL the main dishes lacks of imagination and  effort). It is also worth mentioning that the glass my water was served in was broken, and all the plates seemed very old and worn-out. After this terrible service and bad food we most definitely won't be returning.

Great little spot. I just walked by and dropped in. I got one of the special sandwiches but the special desert and the superiority burger was the way to go. Man a little pricey, but totally delicious and 100% vegetarian. Win win win.

Title: Innovative Noodles and More at Columbus Circle Gem

Tucked away inside the bustling Shops at Columbus Circle, this spacious and well-lit eatery offers a welcome respite for hungry shoppers and food enthusiasts alike. My mid-week, 7pm arrival was met with no wait, a pleasant surprise for a dinner outing.

The fluid menu, while keeping the dining experience fresh, came with a tinge of disappointment as a favored dish, Chilled Spicy Noodles, was no longer available. Nevertheless, the Toasted Chili Ramen was a delightful alternative, offering a satisfying spicy zing complemented by king mushrooms and fresh veggies.

A standout was the Lobster Honzon Noodles - a dish executed to perfection with exquisitely tender lobster tails that left a lasting impression. For those craving a burst of flavor, the Seared Shrimp Bun did not disappoint, thanks to its generous filling and pleasing taste profile.

While the Pork Belly Bun fell short of expectations, with its unsatisfying cut and imbalance in texture, the Caramelized Shiitake Bun emerged as the star among the buns, earning my highest recommendation.

The Coconut Cheesecake concluded the meal on a high note, its subtlety enhanced by a tangy mango purée, making it a dessert worth ordering.

Service, however, was a mixed bag. Despite the efficiency in clearing dishes, attentiveness waned when it came to ordering and billing - culminating in a billing error that doubled the charge on my friend's credit card.

In sum, while the restaurant hits high marks for its culinary creations, the service component could use some fine-tuning to match the quality of the dining experience.

Title: A Hidden Gem by Bryant Park for a Hearty Lunch

I stumbled upon this quaint eatery via Mealpal and it has quickly become a favorite for lunch. Nestled near Bryant Park, its unassuming charm is matched by the vibrant flavors served. The chicken and pork fiesta bowls are my top picks - a generous heap of well-seasoned meat, rice, beans, fresh salad, and a zesty green sauce that tingles the taste buds without overpowering.

The meat, succulent and marinated to perfection, falls apart with each forkful, reminiscent of the hearty, home-cooked meals one might find in the Dominican Republic. It's a delightful balance of protein and greens, perfect for a midday refuel.

Even with Mealpal, the portions are substantial, ensuring you get great value. I've introduced this spot to my coworkers and it's received unanimous thumbs up. If you find yourself in the area, don't miss out on this unpretentious spot for a truly satisfying lunch.

I found Ikinari through a Yelp search and made a same day reservation for 2 for an early dinner. We took a rideshare service, so we didn't have to worry about parking. We got there at 5pm and were greeted and seated immediately. Process:Take the number from your table to the counter and order your steaks (type and weight). Choose your sides that will come on the hot plate with your steak (corn-default but can be subbed, onions, broccoli, potatoes or green beans). I chose a 10oz ribeye (Rare-as suggested by the restaurant) with corn, onions and added broccoli. My husband chose a 14oz Filet (Rare) with corn and onions. Go back to your table to order your drinks and other sides and dessert.  We ordered 2 sides of Garlic Pepper Rice, due to the other reviews I've read. We agree. Definitely a must. All steaks come on a sizzling (REALLY HOT) platter, so the steaks continue to cook after it's brought to your table. I usually order my steaks Medium Rare, but ordered it Rare. It was perfectly cooked, even after sitting on the platter. When done, just walk up to the cashier to pay. The service was very good too. They were all very attentive. Looking forward to coming back again on our next NYC visit.

I recently visited a local ramen spot and was pleasantly surprised by their extra-large portions. The broth was robust and flavorful, albeit a tad on the salty side, but still enjoyable. The noodles were reminiscent of lo-mein, thick and hearty. A unique touch was the provided hot stone, which not only kept the broth warm but also crisped up the pork beautifully. I'd recommend using it to enhance the dish's texture and warmth. Overall, a satisfying experience for any ramen enthusiast.

If you're in the mood for impeccably fried Japanese delights, look no further than this gem of a restaurant. A regular haunt for my Tonkatsu cravings, I'm consistently impressed by the succulence and perfect golden crust of their fried pork chop. Don't overlook the other fried offerings, either; the Japanese fried chicken and oysters are equally delicious and satisfying.

What adds to the charm is the swift and efficient service. As a solo diner, I appreciate the luxury of being seated without delay. An added bonus is the no-tipping policy, which is a refreshing departure from the norm and eases the dining experience. In summary, for a quick, delectable lunch that hits the spot every time, this place is unrivaled.

Title: Unforgettable Hainan Chicken Delight

If there's a place to indulge in the finest Hainan chicken, this is the one. We opted for takeout and weren't disappointed. The chicken itself was remarkable—tender and flavorful, even without embellishment. But when paired with the sauce, it ascended to perfection. The rice deserves its own praise; infused with chicken oil, it surpassed the typical rice experience with its enhanced taste. A must-visit for Hainan chicken aficionados.
Back for the third time. Love this place. Under the new name. Julia's tea and dim sum house. 7pm on a Monday night and got to meet Julia!Dim sum was fantastic as always!!

Title: Pleasantly Surprised at by Chloe

Walking into by Chloe without preconceptions, I found myself unexpectedly in a vegan haven. As a newcomer to this style of cuisine, trepidation gave way to intrigue when the avocado burger on the menu caught my eye. The decision paid off – the burger was nothing short of outstanding. A hint of spice, perhaps from the chipotle mayo I daringly added, only enhanced the enjoyment.

I eyed the sweet potato fries of my fellow diners with a hint of envy, but post-workout discipline prevailed. The ambiance of the eatery was refreshingly laid-back, with a straightforward approach: order, then await a text to retrieve your meal at the counter. The demographic skewed heavily towards women in gym attire, which added to the casual, health-forward vibe of the place.

All in all, by Chloe delivered a delightful dining experience, subverting expectations and perhaps even converting a few skeptics with its plant-based culinary prowess.

Title: A Brunch to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

I can't believe it took me this long to discover [Restaurant Name]! Embarrassing, I know, but better late than never. Visiting mid-week for brunch turned out to be an absolute delight. Despite a brief wait at the door, we were soon greeted by a charming hostess who wasn't just attentive but sparked engaging conversation both en route to our table and after.

The service only got better when Fatou, our waitress, made her appearance. She was a ray of sunshine, making our meal all the more enjoyable. Her cocktail recommendation, The Razzle, hit the spot with its impeccable mix of fruity flavors and just the right kick for a brunch beverage—the presentation was top-notch, too!

But let's talk about the main event: the Steak & Eggs. I kid you not, my mouth waters just thinking about it. It was a festival of flavors so divine that for the first time, steak sauce was an uninvited guest. The steak was cooked to perfection, the eggs scrambled to cheesy precision, and even the tater tots earned their place on the plate.

It's not just the food and drinks that will bring me back, but the staff's warmth too. Every employee we encountered made a point to engage with us, ensuring our experience was nothing short of spectacular.

In summary, [Restaurant Name] has nailed the brunch game. My only regret? Not coming here sooner!

I'd say it's my top burrito spot! Freshly cooked on the spot and taste pretty fresh. Don't underestimate this food truck! I love how it's in my neighborhood too. There's not enough great authentic Mexican food around!

Title: Mixed Feelings at Mr Bing's Pop-Up

I've been a follower of Mr Bing since their days at Urbanspace Vanderbilt and the Bryant Park Holiday Shop, but my latest experience during their pop-up at my office building left me with mixed emotions. Sadly, my go-to Roast Pork Bing wasn't on the menu, pushing me toward the Bulgogi Beef Bing with a side of Sesame Spinach, steering clear of the vegetarian and non-fried chicken options due to my picky palate.

A plus was the allergen awareness, essential for this nut allergy sufferer, but the revelation that their Chili Paste contained traces of nuts was disconcerting, something I'd not been informed about before.

Watching the staff use pre-made bings instead of the expected made-to-order process was a letdown, compromising the freshness I'd come to associate with Mr Bing. Although the service was swift, it didn't compensate for the quality, with the beef's texture resembling overly dry pulled pork and not worth the $16 price tag. Thankfully, the Sesame Spinach stood out, saving the meal from being a total loss.

In conclusion, while the convenience was appreciated, the shortcuts and the less-than-stellar main left me deciding to return to my other favorite jianbing spots in the future.

Came in for a catch up date with one of my girls after she said the one in Astoria has an amazing tequila selection and also because of #TacoTuesday. From what I was told this location has the same extensive tequila selection. Drinks: no happy hour. Drinks were delicious but considering that no happy hour, the ice to liquid ratio in my La Refrescante was interesting lol -- nevertheless the drinks were good! & I also tried the La MoritaFood: I had the Dorodos De Camaron. For the price I immediately wished the portion was bigger. So while it was good, it's also overpriced. After being told the Astoria location has happy hour on food & drink, I would stop there if in the area.

Food was blah... dessert was blah... they served us lots of alcohol and we all loved the mint/ pesto dip for the bread. They were insanely attentive, but I think it's because we were the only table there. We were all disappointed with our food. First and last time I will have Moroccan food. Unfortunately this is the only Moroccan restaurant in the city. The decor is cute, in the back there are additional rooms to smoke hookah.

Title: Cozy Spot for Pasta and Drinks - La Pecora Bianca

Last Friday night, when Eataly was a no-go with its two-hour wait, my friend and I stumbled upon the charming La Pecora Bianca via Yelp. Even at 6:30pm, the place was bustling, but we managed to snag a couple of snug spots at the wine bar.

Despite the close quarters, our waiter was nothing but attentive and cordial. My choice for the evening was the comforting tagliatelle paired impeccably with The Big Apple, a cider and bourbon cocktail ideal for the winter chill. My friend opted for the campanelle and the tantalizing Forbidden Fruit drink, marrying aperol, prosecco, and grapefruit.
