Both the food and drinks, though tardy in arrival, were worth the wait: hearty, flavorsome, and executed well.

The décor of La Pecora Bianca was a feast for the eyes too, with striking gold and turquoise touches that made it stand out on Yelp as much as the promise of carbs did. While space at the wine bar was a bit tight, the energy was vibrant and didn't detract from the experience; I could only imagine that a daytime visit would showcase the ambiance in an even better light.

Overall, the meal was satisfying, the service commendable, and the atmosphere appealing. Though not extraordinary, the wide-ranging menu has certainly piqued my interest for future dining adventures here.

Have never not had a good meal at K'OOK. I used to come here all the time when I was in college and in the area. Recently, after years, I came back and it's just as good.The crispy egg is always a solid choice, although my friend and I did not order on this particular visit. Instead, we ordered the KimMaRi, which comes with 4 deep fried seaweed rolls with glass noodles wrapped inside. It tasted GREAT, and relatively light for being a deep fried dish. Would definitely recommend. We shared a budaejjigae. It's a pretty small order, I was originally thinking of the large pot ones with the fire underneath. However, it was still delicious and ended up being a pretty good amount of food (along with the appetizer) for my friend and I. They also have happy hour until 8 and serve soju. This is a great cozy restaurant to visit!

Pretty solid but didn't exactly blow my mind away. I opted for the spicy paitan with pork. Maybe I should've done the chicken instead as they're known for their chicken broth but alas! I went on a Friday night at around 6 PM and got seated immediately. The catch is I was by myself and there are always those scattered empty seats at the bar. By the time I left (6:45-7ish), there was a long wait for seats. Basically, on a Friday night, settle for an early dinner if you want to go to any of the three Totto Ramen locations in Midtown. Also, I'm sure this has been mentioned prior, but the two locations in Midtown West are cash only but this location in Midtown East do accept credit (except Amex). Anyways, the spicy paitan with pork was solid but it didn't stand out to me the way, let's say, anything from Ippudo or the duck ramen from Momosan is (IMHO)! I do think that if I opted for the chicken it would've been much better with the broth (which was very good, just not as spicy as I would've liked it to be). On a side note, I don't know if it's garlic in the shakers or something else but stir some in with the ramen and the broth gets even better. The ramen is cooked al dente which is vital because no one wants their ramen falling apart in the broth. All in all I would try Totto again but I don't think I would opt for what I had gotten my first time here- definitely would stick with the chicken next time.

Visited again a few weeks ago. Remember I said get here before you can't? Well Chef Park earned a well deserved Michelin Star this year and I warned you. Our second experience was more intimate as Ellia Park keeps notes and welcomed us back, noting the new seasonal menu and making us feel even more welcome than the first time. The service is only surpassed by the delicate flavors of the delicious food. I expect a second Star in the years to come. Well done Atomix!

I've been here twice and had pretty different thoughts each time. First, the aesthetics here are really beautiful. This place is a perfect date spot. Their menu is quite extensive, so it can be fun to choose some dishes together. Second, my first time coming here I got the royal pad thai which is supposed to be one of their most popular dishes and I really didn't think it was anything special (or worth the 1 hour wait). But the second time around I got their hor mok talay which is Shrimp, Scallops, Squid, Salmon and Crab Meat, Curry Paste, and Heart of Palm served in a Coconut Shell and it was AMAZING. I am rating 4 stars though because the service was a bit slow and the prices are quite steep for the portion size (you're definitely paying for the ambiance). If anything, I now really want to visit Thailand to try more dishes as it's clear from the very extensive menu that there's so much more to thai food than the standard noodles most people think of. If this place was a bit less of a splurge, I would want to come to try the rest of their dishes.

Title: A Tale of Two Visits: Breakfast Triumphs Over Dinner

After an exceptional breakfast experience three months prior, my partner and I ventured back to this bustling spot, grateful for our reservation amidst the crowd. Seated cozily in a quieter corner, we began with the French onion soup that, unfortunately, fell short with under-caramelized onions and an odd addition of small flakes that marred its classic taste.

My partner's roast chicken was satisfactory, but the real star was the generous portion of moules, ample enough to have been shared. Dessert was an essential flourish to our meal; however, the flourless chocolate cake we eagerly anticipated was merely passable, not the delight we had hoped for.

Reflecting on our visit, we couldn't help but feel a tinge of disappointment, having found the magic of our morning meal eluding us at dinner. It seems, at least for now, breakfast reigns supreme at this establishment.

Despite not being connoisseurs of Asian cuisine, the bustling scene at this eatery, with a wait time at 1 PM, suggested we were in for a treat – and indeed it was! After a brief 15-minute wait, we indulged in their Harmony drink sampler which was a refreshing delight. The wings were the showstopper - their crunch was simply irresistible, rendering them utterly mouthwatering. We also sampled the tuna mayo, which was a savory addition to our meal. This gem proved to be a fantastic lunch spot, and we are eagerly anticipating a return visit for dinner. Highly recommend!

Title: A Cozy Gem with Savory Delights - A Night at UWS Eatery

My dining experience at this UWS restaurant was nothing short of delightful. The ambiance is perfect for any occasion, boasting a well-adorned decor that is both stylish and inviting, especially under the romantic glow of candlelight prevalent after dusk. An early arrival before 7 p.m. on a weekday ensured a quieter meal before the evening rush.

The starters set a high bar, with the day's corn soup serving as a warming treat and the French onion soup satisfying despite leaving me craving more cheese. The charred octopus appetizer was tender to the taste, though I wouldn't have minded a bit more char for that extra smokiness.

The beverage selection complemented the meal wonderfully. A glass of Chardonnay paired seamlessly with our dishes, while the sweet mango cocktail provided a refreshing alternative.

Mains were a carnivore's delight; the grilled rib eye was a masterful medium cook, with the red, juicy center pairing sublimely with the perfectly textured fingerling potatoes. The seared branzino was a lighter yet no less delicious choice, accompanied by a creamy parsnip purée and tender poached turnips that could easily rival potatoes as the go-to side.

The meal concluded on a sweet note with a shareable apple tart, enhanced by a luscious dollop of ice cream and drizzled caramel.

The staff's amiability and efficiency were the cherries on top of a stellar dining experience. Gratitude is due to the management for the opportunity to revel in their culinary offerings. I heartily recommend this establishment and look forward to my next visit.

We came here right after seeing Avenue Q, and we were positively starving at this point. After reading the solid reviews, we decided that Dim sum would really hit the spot.We ordered some har gow and duck dumplings to start, followed by pancakes, shumai and some tea. The har gow was delicious, flavorful and packed with shrimp. The shumai were just as tasty, albeit rather small compared to other places. The duck dumplings fell flat, and the middle was cold...clearly an indication of improperly steamed, previously frozen dumplings. I don't expect them to keep making fresh dumplings as people order, but still, don't give me a frozen dumpling. The chinese scallion pancake was crispy and delicious as always, and paired well with the chili sauce. The soup dumplings were also good, although not the best I've had.We were definitely full after our meal, and were happy with our choice.

After roaming through Koreatown and browsing the menus of all the restaurants, we settled on New Wonjo because of the variety on the menu as well as the modern atmosphere! We arrived and let the staff know that we did NOT want kbbq, so they told us to wait for around 10 minutes. After a bit, we saw a party of two come in and get seated immediately... so we asked about why. Apparently, they had space upstairs for people who did not want kbbq, and we were seated immediately after asking about it. Lol.Anyways, I decided to order the dduk mandu guk (rice cake + dumpling soup). We were given banchan (side dishes) immediately after ordering, and the dishes were really great and there were so many for a non-kbbq meal! I really liked their anchovy and japchae. My soup came out pretty quickly, and it was great. The soup was full of flavor and the amount of rice cakes and dumplings was plentiful. I really liked their soup and would definitely come back!

This was a great Irish bar down in the financial district. We decided to stop in there on our way to China town. It is very cozy and has a Irish atmosphere. The bartender was very friendly. He spent some time talking to us finding out where we were from and served our beer quickly with a smile.

Searching for an affordable fusion restaurant that serves fresh sushi alongside an array of Chinese and Thai dishes? Sachi is your go-to destination. The service is commendable, with food arriving promptly, leaving no room for complaints. Sachi embraces simplicity and excellence, providing a straightforward yet delightful dining experience. It's the ideal choice for those seeking a laid-back atmosphere paired with a robust menu.

Ambience : 5/5Food: 5/5Dessert: 5.5/5Service and knowledge of the menu: 3/5, BUTTT it was restaurant week so ill try to be generous hereNote: its from Jean Georges 2 Michelin Star kitchen Let me just start from my favorite menu items and go backwards-- the Pistachio ice cream with fresh peach dessert was positively HEART thawing as was the Molten lava cake  with the coffee crunch ice cream. As the ice cream melted in your mouth, so did any brewing tensions at the table ( the location of the restaurant in the TRUMP hotel had sparked some charged political policy debate on the table) As tensions mounted the desserts arrived and Literally with the melting of the molten lava chocolate ganache, any residual disagreement also flowed away in a sea of decadence. The appetizers were solid . Cucumber gazpacho was notableKUDOS for nonalcoholic drinks and wine and passion fruit/ fresh pineapple juice representation. My big issue with service was that the servers simply did NOT know the ingredients or components of the dishes and while visual presentation was good. I inquired about the cheese board and a special server called the "CAPTAIN" was summoned to the table. The CAPTAIN - while more knowledgeable than most - rattled off 4 cheeses before stating that there were no more. ... the earlier server had said there would be 18 cheeses.. Anyway, Ill be back to try a non restaurant week experience. Ambiance and overall service was decent. The Foodie in me was a little disappointed but ultimately my taste buds couldn't complain.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Curry Lovers

I recently visited this charming eatery and was instantly smitten with its offerings. It's a fantastic destination for those seeking hearty and budget-friendly meals. Their curry particularly stands out; I had the pleasure of savoring the seafood curry noodle soup, which was a delightful mix of rich, robust flavors complementing perfectly al dente noodles. The side of Indian pancake added a unique and tasty touch for dipping into the soup.

I didn't stop there, though – the curry beef over rice also caught my eye. While delicious, I must say the noodle soup stole the show with its more intense curry flavor. Aside from the food, the service was commendable – attentive, swift, and genuinely friendly, ensuring my meal was both enjoyable and efficient. I walked out in a mere 20 minutes, fully satisfied.

I wholeheartedly recommend this spot to all foodies, and I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit to delve deeper into their menu. A true culinary delight!

Title: A Love Letter to Ichiran - New York's Ramen Gem

If there were ever a ramen spot to steal my heart, Ichiran has triumphantly claimed the title. My gastronomic pilgrimage to this NYC haven not once, but twice, in a single weekend (inebriation notwithstanding on round two) is a testament to its allure.

The cornerstone of my affection is none other than the Classic Tonkotsu Ramen – a bowl priced at $19. The brilliance lies in the freshness of ingredients and a broth that defies the ordinary; rich and flavorful without the tyranny of over-salting. Accomplishments I've not seen in ages, I drained every last drop of this liquid gold from my bowl.

A mere $2 invites you to alter the broth's character with a side of vinegar sauce – a worthy experience, turning one bowl into a dual-flavor escapade. Although add-ons are plenty, the transformative power is debatable, save for the premium yakibuta. Borrowing from my boyfriend's bowl, I can confirm it is divine and worth every extra penny.

As for the heat, the level 2x spice played a coy game with my palate, nearly imperceptible. The jump to 5x revealed that Ichiran's spice isn't just about heat; it's a different beast that pricks at your throat uniquely. A balance between the two levels may well be the sweet spot.

In conclusion, Ichiran, you've left me smitten. An expansion to Boston or California would be nothing short of a personal favor to a newfound devotee.

I recently visited a well-known brunch spot in the city, and my experience was just okay. Despite its popularity, the prices seem fair, possibly explaining its fame. I tried the Jack's Breakfast with skirt steak, which was of mediocre quality and a bit tough, but considering it was $24, it felt acceptable. The Peri Peri Chicken Wings had a nice spice and flavor, although some pieces were on the fatty side. The major downside was the long wait to be seated. Overall, an average experience that justifies its reasonable pricing.

Da Rafffaele is a cozy intimate Italian restaurant, planted in Midtown East.the restaurant is softly lit in the evenings. the space is small to medium--with a variety of tables for couples and groups. the space feels cozy without being cramped or crowded. a full bar is tucked in the back with some seating--there's a flat screen TV at the bar. colorful modern art brightens the walls and overall, the interior has that fine dining feel (white linens) without being stuffy and stiff. the food ranges from solidly good to very good to great. the grilled octopus appetizer's flavor and appeal is the accompanying flavors that come with the charred octopus. the portion is small but shareable between two. ~$18. i'd bypass and order the paccheri or head straight to the pasta entrees.the tagliolini with stuffed meatballs is so freaking good. al dente healthy serving of pasta (very shareable). flavorful sauce with savoriness and that touch of tomato acid and sweetness. the meatballs are soft, yet hold firm. the meatballs are stuffed with cheese, pignoli, and more. so good. the filet mignon is just okay to good. parmesan topped filet mignon with a polenta cake and some veggies. in terms of steak, i'd pass on the "carne" and focus on pasta bc that is where the kitchen excels. ~$40. order another pasta or a seafood entree.tiramisu. shareable. sweet. perfectly sweet end to a dinner.stick to wine. there is a full bar. the restaurant has a nice flexibility from being great for a casual date night or a celebratory bday dinner. the restaurant has a local regular residential crowd that frequents it. it's less of a destination restaurant which is nice alternative to tourist trap places which are all flash and no substance. that said, the crowd here leans to an older set...so it's a bit more quiet and less hectic which is refreshing.drops mic cuz i am mastering the PASTAbilitiesi outzzz

The tuna tartare and scallops over a risotto apps were scrumptious.  Two of us followed that with some chips and quac and had a satisying light dinner at the bar in the front of the restaurant.  The lighting is low, but the tiling is colorful.  Nice place for higher end Mexican.  Nice cocktail menu too.

I visited a quaint spot inside the Essex Market around 9pm, where I had the chance to try their chicken rice offerings. Opting for both the regular and fried chicken rice, I found myself favoring the former. The regular chicken rice featured a generous serving of chicken, prepared in the traditional Hainanese manner, paired nicely with warm rice and accompanied by three complementary sauces: soy, mild red hot, and spicy green, each enhancing the dish's flavors.

Despite its appetizingly crisp exterior, the fried chicken rice fell short for me, relying too heavily on its accompanying sauce to make up for what was otherwise a rather dry chicken. However, the meal did come with a complimentary soup—a hot and light accompaniment that did a nice job balancing out the richness of the chicken dishes.

In summary, while the food was satisfactory with some highlights, my recommendation would be to stick with the regular chicken rice for a more enjoyable meal.

This is a popular East Village restaurant that serves Filipino and Asian-inspired fare. There were already several parties waiting at the front door when I came by at the 5pm opening time on a recent weekend night, and the place filled up fast.The menu has about several dozen options that are meant to be shared by an entire party. As I was dining solo, I chose the sizzling sisig, which I knew I could manage on my own. It was a delightful and authentic hot plate full of juicy, tasty pork topped by a runny egg, and it went well with a bowl of coconut rice which, although not as moist as I'm used to, was nevertheless absolutely delicious and, well, coconutty.Having had halo-halo in Hawaii recently, I couldn't pass up the opportunity to try it here, even though I knew that it's a huge bowl that's tough to finish. Here, it the usual macapuno and ube ice cream, but it also had interesting twists like leche flan and pinipig, all of which combined to add nutty flavors and crunchy texture. The shaved ice, meanwhile, was really chunky and wasn't as fine and melt-in-your-mouth as, say, the Hawaiian version that I had. While it was difficult to break apart into edible pieces, the whole melody of ingredients made it an enjoyable dessert.Service was a bit brusque from a female server, while the male African-American servers and staffers were very courteous and professional. Despite the crowds, there's more room than meets the eye: there's additional seating in a cozy, intimate area to the rear of the main dining space.

I recently experienced delivery from this restaurant and was delighted by the speedy service. The pizza impressed me with its perfect crispiness and an ideal balance of sauce to cheese. They even included two small containers of extra sauce, which I found to be flavorful without being overpowering or overly acidic. Eagerly looking forward to my next visit to enjoy their offerings in person.

Title: Cozy Lunch at Parm

I visited Parm for a late lunch and enjoyed a cozy experience. The spacious interior with ample seating made for a comfortable setting, though I would have preferred outdoor seating had it been available later in the day.

The service was friendly, and our meals arrived promptly, which was a plus. With a more concise menu, decisions came easily. The calamari appetizer was a highlight, offering a delightful crunch accompanied by fried peppers, despite the smaller portion size.

My main course, the chicken parm dinner, served up generous portions of chicken topped with hearty mozzarella. The accompanying pasta, however, lacked flavor. Luckily, the chicken's crispy edges made up for the pasta's shortfall.

In sum, Parm is a solid choice for those seeking a straightforward and satisfying meal in a comfortable ambiance.

Stepping into this new upper east side haven truly feels like you're entering a "Magical Indian Wonderland!" The decor is a visual feast – think Hogwarts mingling with Raiders of the Lost Ark, brimming with stunning imports from India and sprinkles of Turkish and European flair. The Indian designer’s touch weaves an eclectic fantasy vibe that had me captivated and snapping photos incessantly.

Upon arrival, the ambiance sets the stage for the perfect romantic date night, enchanting and mysterious. The service complements the scene, with fantastic, friendly, and attentive staff. Even the manager indulged my curiosity about the intricate decor with a smile.

The culinary journey here is best described as "UNIQUE AND INQUISITIVE INDIAN CUISINE WITH A MODERN TWIST." The extensive menu lives up to its billing, offering a cornucopia of flavors. Standout dishes include the Bombay Thali, a vegetable mélange that's a delight for those looking to sample different tastes, and the Club non-veg Thali which managed to impress even my son, a newfound Indian cuisine aficionado.

The shrimp were plump and seasoned to perfection, the samosas – unusually large and packed with flavor – defy the typical, and a chicken dish so tender and well-spiced that you can't help but savor each bite.

Although currently awaiting their liquor license, the establishment's location conveniently opposite a wine store with an excellent selection means you won't miss out on pairing your meal with a great drink.

For anyone in search of a unique dining experience on the upper east side, this beautifully designed Indian restaurant comes highly recommended. Don't miss the chance to indulge in this tasteful slice of India.

Hide-Chan is always a consistent great choice for ramen. You can choose the firmness of your noodles, as well as your spice level. The spicy garlic ramen is very flavorful without being too rich and oily. There are 2 lunch sets, one for $16 that you can get with smaller side dishes and a bowl of ramen and the other for $18 which you can get with a mini rice bowl. The Gyu Don (beef bowl) was a little dry and had a little too much ginger, but still quite tasty.

Title: A Satisfying Curbside Find with a Dash of Patience Needed

I stumbled upon this food truck parked along Park Ave near my office and decided to revisit their fare—or perhaps try it for the first time. My usual Thai food truck haunt had vanished earlier in the year, so I was on the lookout for a new lunchtime staple.

My dish of choice is always the red curry with tofu, and at $9, the price here did not disappoint. Upon tasting, I found the curry pleasantly mild, a welcome change from the often overzealous spice levels elsewhere. The inclusion of zucchini added a nice touch, providing a welcome textural balance to the dish. On taste alone, I would happily give this meal an A+.

However, patience is a requisite for patrons of this truck. The wait time bordered on 15+ minutes, which, while advertised, seems excessive. I appreciate quality food, but efficiency is also key, especially when one is subject to the extremities of weather during peak lunch hours. A little more speed would make this truck an all-rounded success.

Rating: ★★★★☆

Beautiful clean and modern. The space is labyrinthine- we had to walk up two flights of stairs and down another to get to our dining room.  The staff were pleasant, efficient, and accommodating. The banchan were happily replenished. They had a different spin on bulgogi. They used a grill that was convex with a moat around the edge. They put a liquid in, scallions and two raw eggs. As the meat grilled the eggs and scallions cooked in the peripheral well. Once the meat was fully cooked our waitress pushed it into the well.  The result was reminiscent of sukiyaki. It was about the best bull go gi that I've ever had. The mung bean pancake with seafood was excellent. The bibimbap was very good. We really liked this place and would happily go back.

I recently visited this restaurant for a breakfast meet-up with friends and found it to be quite bustling, a testament to its popularity. The vibrant atmosphere makes it a good spot for morning gatherings. However, the service can feel rushed due to its busy nature, and staff seem to be on the lookout for you to vacate the table promptly post-meal. I experienced a minor inconvenience when a waitress, attending to the table next to us, declined my request for a second cup of coffee as it was not her assigned table – a small gesture that could have enhanced the overall service experience. Nonetheless, the restaurant is an okay choice for a casual breakfast rendezvous.

Title: A K-town Hidden Gem for Korean Comfort

After dodging the long waits at popular chicken joints in K-town, we accidentally discovered an unassuming spot that turned out to be a delightful hidden gem. Don't let the shady exterior deter you; the cozy and inviting ambiance downstairs makes you feel right at home. This place is a prime choice for Korean comfort food paired with drinks—perfect for unwinding after a day's work.

Their extended happy hour until 9 pm is a major draw, and we've already returned here for it two weeks in a row. The soju cocktail pitchers, especially the lychee and yogurt, are irresistible, striking the right balance of sweetness without being watered down. A classic like ddukbokki is a solid choice here, and their "ktown flavor" fried chicken with its unique nutty sauce shouldn't be missed.

The only hiccup was the soondae bokkeum, which though tasty, skimped on the soondae, making it less value-worthy. Still, this spot stands out as a great, unpretentious place for a chill evening. I'll certainly be back for more.

Title: A Hidden Gem of Culinary Excellence

My frequent lunch visits to Perry St over the last decade have consistently impressed me with the high-end yet surprisingly affordable dining experience it offers. The modern ambiance provides a delightful backdrop to the culinary mastery of Chef JG. At $38, the lunch menu is a steal, showcasing the same top-tier cuisine that has earned a Michelin star at the flagship location in Columbus Circle.

Service here is without fault; attentive and seamless, complementing the dining experience perfectly. It baffles me to see 3-star reviews when every meal I've had has been nothing short of exquisite.

Brunch brings additional joy with its expanded offerings, including benedicts, pancakes, and duck hash. The French toasts we opted for were, as expected, excellent. And whatever you do, do not miss out on the Molten Lava Chocolate Cake for dessert—it's a delectable must-have that completes the experience on a high note.

Perry St remains an often overlooked treasure that never disappoints, consistently delivering a pleasurable dining experience that is both a pleasure to the palate and the wallet.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Treats at District Social near Javits Center

My quest for a vibrant dining spot near the Javits Center led me to District Social, a hub for craft beer aficionados and culinary curiosities. It's a place one can enjoy both light drinks and decent fare in a moderate to dimly lit setting with a buzz of energetic chatter.

The meal commenced with an array of appetizers. While the calamari fritters intrigued with their tot-like appearance, they fell short in texture, proving a tad too oily and rubbery. In stark contrast, the meatball flatbread was a delight - a harmonious balance of spicy and sweet, topped just right. Unfortunately, the mussels disappointed, their lackluster freshness marred by a sandy aftertaste that failed to impress.

Our main courses saw a mix of hits and misses. The skirt steak was a clear winner, perfectly seasoned and cooked. On the other hand, the lamb skewers left much to be desired, with questionable texture and an underwhelming flavor profile.

To wash it all down, the bottle of Malbec we shared was excellent, though on the pricey side. But then again, a good wine is often worth the splurge.

Service was top-notch; our wait staff shined with friendliness and efficiency. Overall, District Social makes the cut for a round of specialty drinks and lighter dining options. While the culinary experience was a roller coaster, the positives warrant a recommendation, and I'm looking forward to giving this spot another chance on my future NYC visits.

TL;DR pretty decorations, order drinks, order appetizers, don't order the  royal pad Thai, make a  reservation or use yelp waitlist.Thai Villa is a fun restaurant to go to. It is elaborately decorated which makes for a great atmosphere for a date or a birthday/anniversary dinner. It's also great to go just because which is what my friend and I did. We went on a weekday evening, around 7 or so, and it was packed. The wait was 30 minutes for 2 people but I heard some people with larger parties being quoted an hour wait. I would suggest you make reservation for dinner as this is a very popular location. You can also put your name down on the yelp waitlist.The food was good overall. I really liked my cocktail, which was a lychee martini. My friend and I ordered the leaf wrapped chicken, the spicy chicken wings, and the grilled prawn mango salad as appetizers. We really enjoyed all of the appetizers and had high expectations for our main entree. We ordered the Royal Pad Thai to share as our main dish and were disappointed. I had seen in other yelp reviews that the Royal pad Thai was not great but it looked so amazing when we saw the table next to us get their order and we ordered it anyway. It was beautifully plated but the overwhelming flavor was sweetness without very much tang or spice. It was fine, but I wish we had gotten a different entree item. Overall I would make another trip to Thai villa because the atmosphere was great, as was the service, and 3/4 of the food we tried was amazing. I will be sure to try a different main dish next time.

Located inside the Urban Space food hall, you'll find Tomotomo, sister restaurant to TabeTomo. It is a take out restaurant so you'll be able to grab and go if you happen to be craving ramen for lunch. You have the option of getting their tsukemen (dipping ramen where soup and noodles are separate) or ramen. My friend and I opted for the tonkatsu tsukemen as their seafood one was sold out (they only sell 50 bowls a day). The broth was rich and balanced out with a slight touch of vinegar that cut through some of the fat from the pork broth. Noodles were cooked perfectly - I would advise you to start dipping your noodles into the broth right away so that the noodles don't start to harden too much! Perfect amount of broth to noodles but if you have leftover broth (which you deff will) you can always order an extra serving of noodles. Like to add some spice to your food? Definitely get their chili powder ($1) to spice things up! We ordered extra porkbelly, chili powder, and eggs to our noodles! It's definitely worth making your ramen/tsukemen a combo! I'd recommend their pork bun or karaage!While it doesn't have the perks of the hot stone to heat up your soup when it gets cold, Tomotomo is the faster take out version so that you can take it to go and eat in the comfort of your office or home. Will be back soon!

Title: A Birthday Bash to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

I recently attended a birthday dinner at [Restaurant Name], and it was an extraordinary experience from start to finish. Dining with a big group can sometimes be hectic, but the party menu catered to our celebration flawlessly.

Upon arrival, the warmth of the staff was immediately evident. The highlight was the chef personally greeting us and taking our orders—a testament to their unparalleled service. The team's frequent check-ins to ensure our satisfaction earned them an A+ in hospitality.

The restaurant itself boasted an inviting decor and ambiance, setting the stage for what was to be a delightful culinary journey. Kicking things off with complimentary fresh baked bread that you can't stop at just one, we dove into a trio of appetizers: caprese, caesar salad, and grilled artichoke hearts, each as delicious as the last—a rarity in my dining experiences.

For the main course, the lemon sole with almonds was exceptional and stood out as the star dish. Other palate pleasers included salmon, chicken breast with fennel and porcini mushrooms, penne with fresh veggies, and veal—a smorgasbord of flavors and textures to sample and enjoy.

The dessert course was a sweet symphony, with panna cotta, tiramisu, and an array of gelatos. While some gelato flavors were on the tart side, the panna cotta was a personal favorite that I highly recommend.

The wine list and drink selections complemented the meal perfectly, rounding out a dining experience that was nothing short of joyous. My visit to [Restaurant Name] was a memorable one, and I am already looking forward to returning to partake in their regular dinner menu.

Title: A Warm Embrace in a Bowl

Despite my usual aversion to winter, I can't help but yearn for a chill in the air as an excuse to indulge in the delightfully hot noodle soup from this cozy little spot. The soup is a heartwarming concoction, richly flavored and generously topped with a variety of seasonings that elevate each spoonful. An added bonus to the original recipe, the beef was tender and a perfect companion to the noodles.

My typically selective mother found her bowl equally satisfying, a testament to the authentic and well-crafted Chinese cuisine they serve. The clean and well-maintained interior only added to the overall pleasant experience.

While it might not be a destination on its own, it's definitely a gem worth considering if you find yourself in the vicinity and in contemplation of where to dine. If the weather ever cools down, or even if it doesn't, a stop here for a comforting bowl of soup might just be the perfect pick-me-up.

Title: Cozy Spot for Pizza Night!

Last Tuesday evening, my two friends and I hit up this bustling pizza spot, expecting a great evening—and we weren't disappointed. Despite our reservation, we joined the waiting game for a short while, which honestly was no bother given the vibey atmosphere and the live music that filled the air—a rare treat for a weeknight!

The crowd was a melting pot of sorts, with college students, families, tourists, and suited professionals all flocking in for a taste of what we soon discovered to be some heavenly pizza. Space is at a premium here, with both outdoor seating and the interior on the cozy side, so pro tip: book ahead!

The menu boasted a variety to please any palate, but I zeroed in on a large pepperoni and jalapeño pizza—let me tell you, it was a testament to the magic of a coal-oven's touch. I practically inhaled half of it in no time, and my friend, a self-proclaimed pizza purist, dubbed Arturo's a pizza paradise.

Service was the cherry on top, attentive and seamless, adding to an already great dining experience. If you're craving some quality pizza in a lively setting, this place is a solid bet. Just remember to snag a reservation to skip the wait!

Ramen looks good, but very disappointed. Were not informed about the $16 per person minimum charge before we went in.The ramen was very overpriced, didn't have much topping or ramen. The chashu was too fatty.Just disappointed, especially when compared to the quality of other branches like that in Sydney.

Title: A Whimsical Evening at Beauty and Essex

My visit to Beauty and Essex was an eclectic mix of romance and trendiness, starting with the curious entrance through what seemed to be a pawn shop, adding to its funky charm. Stepping inside, the ambiance took a turn for the elegant, with a grand chandelier bridging the two-story dining area and a warm glow from the abundance of candles.

The vibe was cozy and romantic as we nestled into comfortable chairs in an upstairs dining room that provided a welcome sense of privacy, though exiting required a bit of an awkward shuffle past neighboring diners.

The menu was adventurous and fun, with some hits and a miss. The Thai Style Deep Fried Shrimp with its light batter and vibrant slaw was a standout, and the Bulgogi Ribeye Tacos offered a delightful symphony of flavors with just enough heat. The Seared Scallops were a showstopper—large, succulent, and paired with an enchanting mix of flavors that left us craving more.

A hiccup came with the Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup Dumplings, which disappointed in temperature, lacking the comforting warmth one yearns for in such a dish. The memory of the other fish appetizer eludes me, but it was enjoyable nonetheless.

The most significant letdown of the night was the dessert. The Beauty's Wheel, an adorable concept, fell short of expectations, delivering treats that seemed lackluster compared to the stellar main courses.

Despite the dessert disappointment, Beauty and Essex left a lasting impression, and we will certainly return to explore more of their menu—and perhaps order individual desserts next time. As residents of L.A., we're excited to compare our local Beauty and Essex and see how it measures up.

Made a reservation during restaurant week with some of my friends on a Thursday. We got there exactly at 5pm so there was no wait. We ordered the THAI MUSHROOM SALAD,GREEN PAPAYA SALAD, GRILLED PORK JOWL,PORK BELLY ADOBO, KHAO SOI, THREE FLAVOR PRAWNS, BBQ BABY BACK RIBS and the MALAYSIAN FRIED CHICKEN. For dessert we had the TURON and HALO-HALO. Everything was amazing! The pork belly adobo and the three flavor prawns were my favorite. Small venue but the service was top notch.

Stopped by for a quick snack and decided on the duck jian bing. It hit the spot, although there was a tough, chewy piece I struggled with. The menu has piqued my interest, especially the noodle soups and baos, which I'm keen to try on my next visit. Service was a plus—welcoming and efficient. Heads up, the restroom's downstairs, accessed externally. Despite the slight hiccup with the jian bing, I'm looking forward to returning.

Venturing back into Chinatown after many years, I was delighted to find some of my old haunts still thriving. My recent visit to this particular establishment reaffirmed why it's remained a staple. I indulged in a nostalgic feast, sampling a broad array of dishes that showcased their consistent culinary prowess. Every selection from the menu was a hit; it's the kind of place where you could make a choice with a blindfold on and still be assured a delightful meal. A testament to the timeless quality and charm of this neighborhood gem.

I had first stumbled upon this place on the second date with the wonderful lady who is now my wife so this place is still a little nostalgic! I returned recently and it once again impressed me. It is located in the center of Manhattan near Broadway (we came before a show). ATMOSPHERE- 5 STARS Especially for being downtown, the atmosphere is really nice. It is painted to make you feel like you were in the Greek isles. The floor is painted like the stones in the isles and their are bistro lights hanging overtop. It was a nice elegant sitdown for our date. Loved the way they decorated. (I believe their other location was roomier too...although I haven't been).FOOD- being Greek, I am usually a harsh critic of Greek restaurants...I mean who can really compare to yiayias Greek cooking!!! But I was impressed with the food here. It was a bit different than what I was typically used to especially the spanakopita and kolokeffiakefftedes (no idea how you spell that...lol). They were a different take from what I was used to but very good. The meat plate was very tasty as well...LASTLY IM PUTTING THIS IN ALL CAPS BECAUSE IT WAS THAT GOOD...GET THE HORYATIKI SALAD...THE TOMATOES ON THAT SALAD ARE SO GOOD. I HAVENT HAD  TOMATOES THIS GOOD EVER EXCEPT IN GREECE...THEY ARE SO MUCH BETTER THAN ANYTHING HERE...yes it is worth the crazy emphasis...lolOverall this is a great little find and I enjoyed it quite a bit..I have already come back and would come back again.

Title: A Gem for Temaki Lovers

I recently stumbled upon a restaurant that offers an excellent yet budget-friendly temaki sushi experience. Rushing in for a solo lunch, I was seated immediately, and the service was swift and efficient. Each temaki roll was delightful; warm rice paired with crisp nori and fillings that struck the perfect balance of fresh and flavorful. It's a place I'm excited to make my regular spot for a quick sushi fix. However, after an underwhelming experience at KazuNori in LA, I'll be revisiting this spot a few more times to ensure the quality is consistent. But for now, my first impression is a promising one!

Title: A Socialite Haven with a Cozy Ambiance

Last night, I visited a local hotspot that's clearly a favorite among the socialite crowd, bursting with energy and familiar faces. Sadly, I arrived a tad too late to sample their full culinary offerings, as the kitchen had closed. However, a kind server managed to offer us some chips and guacamole, which were quite satisfying given my hunger.

The place boasts an intimate atmosphere, thanks to the dim lighting that sets the perfect tone for a date night or a low-key evening. From what I could tell, the drink prices won't break the bank, which is a pleasant surprise for a bar frequented by the city's popular crowd.

I was there to toast a friend's birthday, and while the setting was convivial for our group, I couldn't help but feel that the ambiance would be just right for a more intimate occasion, perhaps next time a romantic rendezvous.

In conclusion, even without a full meal to judge, the vibe, service, and pricing were on point. I'm tempted to return soon—this time, earlier—to fully experience what their kitchen has to offer.

I recently dined at a Thai restaurant in NYC geared towards a mainstream crowd and left underwhelmed. The cuisine, known for its vibrant flavors, fell surprisingly flat. The lunch special included vegetarian dumplings that lacked texture, coming across as soft and unremarkable. Additionally, the payment options are oddly limited to Mastercard and cash, which may inconvenience some patrons. Overall, the experience was not in line with the bold tastes typically associated with Thai food.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Chinese Pork Delights on the UES

If you're prowling the Upper East Side in search of delectable Chinese cuisine, this cozy spot might just satisfy your cravings. Notably, their ribs are nothing short of exceptional—a must-try, as they pride themselves on their pork specialties.

The decor strikes a quirky yet endearing note, adding to the restaurant's unique character. Coupled with the exceedingly accommodating and attentive waitstaff, you're in for a pleasant dining experience.

It's apparent that this establishment has basked in the limelight of yesteryear, hinted by the myriad of accolades adorning the walls and the predominantly mature clientele it attracts. Despite its faded glory, the place holds its own with a solid menu.

While I tried the namesake Pig Heaven dish and found it to be mediocre, it didn't overshadow the overall enjoyable meal. This local haunt still garners recommendations for anyone seeking tasty Chinese fare in the area. Swing by with your friends and family for a comforting food journey into the past.

Title: A Reliable Go-To for Work Lunches

I've frequented this restaurant for the past five years, primarily for work lunches, and its consistency keeps me coming back. The location is convenient, the service is speedy, which is a blessing for those on a tight schedule. 

The menu variety is a standout feature, with a selection broad enough to satisfy all palates, including the pickiest eaters, and they're well-prepped for larger groups. The size of the restaurant offers the luxury of space, avoiding the cramped dining experience found elsewhere.

My recent choice, the crispy chicken sandwich, was a delight, maintaining the "good" standard I've come to expect here, akin to their salads and burgers I've enjoyed in the past. This place is the definition of casual and laid-back dining.

Bottom line: If you're in need of a quick, unfussy meal, especially in a group, I'd recommend this place without hesitation.

Squid Ink cocktail was interesting but taste normal too. Complimentary Bread Dip looks like they have been sitting out for hours and dried on the outside, not a good way to present. Lobster Pasta - pretty good but not as amazing as everyone was raving about to me.Chicken Meatball daily special - usually not my type of dish but probably was the highlight of the meal!

I selected Somalian food as my first brunch of 2019.Because i wanted to do and try something NEW to me in my life at this New Year start. I was visiting friend lives in Harlem,My friend is new to Harlem and we  are always exploring  and researching  somewhere  from " real Harlem " This place looked like neighborhood favorite.I've never been to Somalia, tasted neither butI believed this was really Somalian iconic food.We  picked most popular dish ( they said) Hilib AriRoasted goat served aside with Somali Basmati rice and BizBaz sauce and Chicken SuqaarTraditional southern Somalia dish, spicy chicken stew with aromatic house spice best served with Bariis or chapatti breadBoth taste really good, I can't pick one dish, and I like to challenge any local flavor and my taste is flexible but  If you are sensitive with animal flavor, you should pick Chicken or Beef. I meant Goat is bit strong  flavor  such as Lamb.They considered  to make our sauce mild,But I wanna try to have more spicy next time!Additionally the server girl was cute and sweet,Some neighbor or regular customers stop by to say happy new year to her.That looked how this place is popular in Harlem. I guess it absolutely is!Anyway, good experience of unknown food in new year !

I recently grabbed takeout from OBAO during the hectic Friday lunch rush in Manhattan's Financial District. Amidst the somewhat chaotic ordering process, the Shrimp Pad Thai proved to be a savory, albeit slightly unbalanced, mix of sweet and spicy flavors. The generous portion of large, succulent shrimp and well-cooked noodles was somewhat overshadowed by an excessive amount of bean sprouts, which I had to remove.

Serving as a hearty lunch, the $12 price tag felt reasonable for the quantity and quality received. OBAO, perched on a corner within a bustling square, struggles with space during peak hours, leading to a confusing set-up for both made-to-order and pre-made dishes that seemed to overwhelm the staff and frustrate guests.

The crowd was dense, and it was baffling to see patrons opt to dine in within the cramped space. Service seemed to lack a coherent system, amplifying the mayhem of the lunchtime wave.

Potential visitors should be aware that parking is a challenge in the area, which might make OBAO a better option for those walking or using public transit. Despite these issues, the standout food might just be worth braving the disorder for some authentic Thai flavors.

Title: A Tasty Twist on Street Food at Underground Turnstyle Market

If your palate yearns for a unique take on fried chicken, look no further than the gem I stumbled upon in the Underground Turnstyle Market. The game-changing Chick'n Cone Meal is a must-try, artfully pairing crispy fried chicken with a handmade waffle cone, accompanied by a refreshing drink and fries on the side. The Yella BBQ sauce, with its zesty mustard tang, complements the chicken perfectly, marrying traditional flavors in an innovative format. The staff's genuine friendliness adds to the experience—offering samples of the popular Kick'n Ranch assures a future visit. Trust me; if you're in the Underground, this spot is well worth the detour.

Restaurant Review:

Nestled above Five Senses, this Korean eatery offers a unique dining experience that begins as you ascend a flight of stairs to the second floor. The warm welcome extends to the offer of hot tea or water, a prelude to the culinary journey ahead.

Presentation takes center stage as a brown ceramic jar arrives at the table, with tongs and scissors unveiling an appetizing serve of fresh kimchi and radish - the sole, yet memorable banchan.

The service is noteworthy, with attentive waiters promptly tending to every request. However, the meal itself is a mixed bag. The Crispy Mandu's filling was scant, leaving the pork and vegetable dumplings wanting. Likewise, the Haemul Pajeon's thickness overshadowed its seafood essence. On a brighter note, the Beef Japchae's glass noodles and vegetables were a satisfying, albeit small, offering.

The soup course saw contrasting fortunes: the Samgye Tang was a standout with its richly flavored chicken broth and ginseng, while the Seolleon Tang's lackluster taste could not be salvaged by seasoning alone.

For the main beef dishes, the LA Galbi's quality was undercut by excess fat, and the Dolsot Bibimbap disappointed with its size and muted flavors.

In sum, while certain dishes excelled, others fell flat, suggesting room for refinement in this establishment's diverse menu.

I visited this restaurant recently and while the food was passable, the service was utterly disappointing. Despite dining at a relatively quiet time around 9pm on a weekday, the attention from our server was nearly non-existent. It was a challenge just to place our orders. Moreover, the server had a peculiar habit of clearing plates and glasses prematurely, disrupting our meal. Such inattentive and intrusive service left a sour taste, and regrettably, I have resolved not to return.

The food was alright. The arepas are fried and didn't seem typical to Venezuelan arepas I've had in the past but it was a good quick stop for some tasty food! It's a very small interior and the presentation isn't amazing but the food was good enough. I would go here again on my own but I probably wouldn't recommend to anyone visiting from out of town as it isn't a special place and there isn't anything extraordinary about it. The juice was great!

This Michelin starred restaurant has takeout sushi and turns into a late night ramen house. It feels like such an oxymoron. We were craving sushi and gave my date search parameters. More formal than Sugar Fish but less fancy than Yasuda.  The sushi special plate, though not omakase, was the perfect level of interest for a weekday dinner.  Three of the pieces were seared.  We started with fried chicken in a basket and silky chawanmushi with shrimp.

On a bustling Saturday night, our party of nine was comfortably seated in the back room. Although eager to kick off our dining experience with a round of wine, we were off to a rocky start with the disappointing discovery of dirty glassware, necessitating a prompt replacement for one guest.

Service was lackadaisical throughout the evening, testing our patience as we awaited our meals. However, the wait was somewhat redeemed by the delectable Mermaid Fish Tacos. They struck an excellent balance between crunchiness and flavor, and the portion size was generous, comprising three fulfilling tacos. Despite the initial setbacks, I departed satiated and with a particular fondness for the fish tacos.

So happy this place opened in the area. Can't speak for the authenticity of this place since I'm not Hispanic. But the steak burrito I had was on point. It was bigger than my stomach, fresh, filling and yummy. I especially like all the sauces they provide for your to grab yourself. I loved that green mild sauce that they had. I poured that sauce on my burrito and devoured that burrito. Service was fast and friendly also. Will definitely be back to try other items on the menu

I recently visited a restaurant with high expectations, having been informed it would outshine popular spots like BonChon and Turntable. Unfortunately, it did not quite live up to that praise. However, it did have its highlights, particularly the Sweet Potato Fries which were incredibly delicious and deserving of an "OMG" reaction. On the downside, the Calamari was a letdown; it was inexpensive, but disappointingly so, with a rubbery texture that was quite embarrassing for a dish with such potential. Overall, the experience was good, though not extraordinary.

Heard of this spot after seeing a Fung Bros video, and I honestly wasn't that impressed. Came with my girlfriend for our anniversary since the two of us were craving some spicy Chinese food. We ordered: skewed beef with cumin, hometown lufen, and pepper and pork. Total bill came about ~$77 inclusive of tax and tip. Quite expensive considering this is Chinese food!AMBIANCE:Definitely the owners are trying to make Hunan cuisine more upscale and refined (explains the rather $$$ bill we got). Decor is modernist and chic, definitely a cool spot to bring a date or a loved one here.PROS:Hometown Lufen was pretty good. The beef that they served was very juicy and the soft boiled egg definitely added a dimension of flavor to the experience. Char shao that came on top of the noodles was very flavorful and sweet that is reminiscient of a lot of classic Cantonese styled barbecue. Good, but not mind-blowing IMO. Skewed beef was very tender and seasoned very aggressively (see CONS). My girlfriend seemed to enjoy her pepper and pork noodle dish. The berkshire pork was definitely the highlight for her.CONS:We told the waitress to get our beef slightly and hometown lufen mild spiciness, since we're not the best in terms of handling food that was too hot. The lufen and the skewed beef were wayyyy too spicy, definitely was more on the hotter side. Way too peppery for our skewed beef! Knocking off another star because for what we got I feel like price wise doesn't justify how much we paid for. Definitely on the pricier side so beware!OVERALL:Mediocre experience. I probably would come back only if they fix some of the issues addressed in this review. Personally, I don't think its worth the hype and the price.

There are different kinds of men in this world, but I'm definitely a Jian Bing Man.Pretty adorable little food stand inside the amazing Koreatown Food Hall located in Koreatown of Manhattan which is known as food Gallery 32, on 32nd St just East of 6th Ave.So many great Korean stands in here with pretty good pricing - especially by Manhattan standards, so come and check them out and see what you think. I've eaten at about half of them now, and will be checking off the others in the coming months.

Title: High Hopes Dashed at Trendy Spot

I approached this trendy eatery with high anticipation, particularly to sample the much-touted fried Pad Thai pancakes featured in a recent Insider article. Imagine my disappointment when they weren't even listed on the menu. Opting instead to order a la carte during restaurant week, my party and I opted for jasmine rice, coconut rice, pork ribs, and Pad Thai.

The dining experience sadly didn't live up to the cool vibe of the place. Our dishes arrived haphazardly – the main course of pork ribs was served lukewarm and solo, followed by the rice and then, perplexingly, the Pad Thai appetizer at the end. To make matters worse, the meat in the Pad Thai was charred, a sharp contrast to the creatively done rolled egg noodles which were the dish's sole redemption. 

Service added an additional sour note to our visit. When requesting the removal of empty plates to make space on our small table, a member of the wait staff responded with an unprofessional grimace.

Regrettably, this restaurant did not live up to the hype. The disjointed serving sequence, underwhelming food temperature, and less than welcoming service painted a picture of disappointment that no amount of ambiance could offset.

I recently visited this restaurant for their happy hour, which impressively runs until 7 PM even on a Saturday – a rarity! I sampled the cucumber gimlet, which my companion praised highly, and I personally fell head over heels for their Tamarind margarita. As for the eats, we indulged in fried yuca, brussel sprouts, and calamari. The brussel sprouts were the standout; I can't recommend them enough. The overall ambiance of the place added to the experience, with cleanliness being a noticeable plus, especially in the restrooms. We were seated at the high tops, so while this review doesn't delve into service, the food and drinks alone were enough to ensure a return visit.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience Near Lincoln Center

My dining experience at the restaurant across the street from Lincoln Center was nothing short of delightful. The comfort emanating from the black and white tiled decor created a relaxed ambiance that allowed us to unwind and savor the evening.

The cocktail menu was impressive, showcasing thoughtful concoctions that were as delicious as they were innovative. A standout appetizer, the fried okra, truly wowed us with its perfect blend of crispiness and flavor.

The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the Saturday short rib special, which was tender, rich, and cooked to perfection. Additionally, the complementary sparkling water on the table was a refreshing and appreciated gesture.

The staff's attentiveness and helpfulness were the cherries on top of an already splendid dining experience. I highly recommend this establishment for anyone looking for a comfortable and satisfying meal in the Lincoln Center vicinity.

I had the chicken kebab this afternoon. It comes with butternut squash and couscous. Everything was so well spiced, which is unfortunate because I found the chicken a tad rubbery. Butternut squash was definitely the highlight. 3 and a half stars.

Great service and attractive breakfast menu. The food is yummy but don't expect something too great. You should come to this place if you are not in a hurry because it seems popular in the area. I came here on Saturday at 8:00 am and this place was busy already. I really liked how this cafe is decorated and their use of lightning.

My friend and I decided to try this restaurant for a quick meal before watching the new Star Wars movie on Friday night. There was a 15 minute wait but eventually we were seated. We ordered the pork bbq, kimchi pancake, and vegetable bibimbap for two.The food took 25 minutes to arrive. First to arrive was pork; before the appetizers. Food was average tasting.Sometime afterwards my stomach ache and I felt the strong dark forces within me. Spending a portion of my time in the restroom spoiled my movie. Never eating there again.

Title: Cozy Spot for a Ramen Fix

After an underwhelming start to our evening, with one local eatery being cash-only and another less than inviting, Yelp came to the rescue, leading us to this understated gem. The restaurant greeted us with an almost empty dining room, allowing us to be seated immediately—a welcome relief from the biting cold outside.

Eager for warmth, we began with a large Hot Sake to share, which hit the spot with its comforting warmth and robust kick. When it came to the main event, I chose the Oki Classic Ramen, a delightful bowl brimming with delicious chicken, perfectly cooked noodles, and a tastefully balanced egg—the broth was remarkable for its rich flavor without even a hint of fishiness. My companion's Volcano Ramen was equally impressive and brought some heat to the table.

The restaurant itself struck a pleasing balance between simplicity and thoughtful touches, including convenient plug and USB ports at each table—a small but appreciated detail that did not go unnoticed. The service was efficient and unobtrusive, and the prices didn't break the bank.

In summary, if you find yourself craving a good bowl of ramen on a chilly night, this spot offers a satisfying experience with all the warmth and none of the fuss.

Title: Burger Bliss at a Cozy Spot

Last evening, my mom and I found our new favorite dining escape after a long day at work. Greeted by the warmth of friendly staff, we were quickly seated amidst the inviting ambiance that promised a relaxing experience.

Kicking things off with a cocktail indulgence, we sipped on a perfectly blended Fuzzy Navel and a classic Old Fashion, both of which were delightful and expertly mixed.

The main event was all about burgers, and they did not disappoint. Mom's Classic Burger embodied the quintessential burger experience – a testament to doing simple things right. My FiDi Burger, however, was the standout; one bite and I was on cloud nine – an extraordinary creation that demands a return visit.

And let’s not forget the fries - the ideal companions to our burgers, boasting that addictive crispy exterior and fluffy interior that keep you reaching for more.

In short, this place is a must-visit for anyone craving a top-notch burger experience in a cozy setting.

I recently visited a cozy, counter-service spot known for its traditional Korean cuisine. Opting for a veggie bibimbap, I found it quite enjoyable with fresh, vibrant ingredients. A sample of the tofu soup from a dining companion's bowl left a lasting impression with its rich flavor and was downright excellent. Our late weekend lunchtime proved to be a peaceful affair, as the restaurant was pleasantly quiet. Recommended for a laid-back meal that promises authentic tastes of Korea.

Came back for dinner and was quite disappointed in the food this time around. Not a fan of their seasoning for the seafood boil, they didn't have that much flavor to it. My group ordered the garlic butter and cajun classic with varying spice levels, but none of them came out that good. I almost asked for salt and pepper to make it taste better. For the price we paid, I totally wouldn't recommend this place. Probably at the bottom of my list of places to eat at in ktown and I'd only recommend getting some dollar oysters and happy hour beers if you're here. The only plus side I would say is the service was good, the waitress was really nice and kept checking back on us to refill napkins and water. The vibe and decor were nice too, there were also lots of seating so very good for groups, they have a floor downstairs if you have a large party. I just wished the food tasted better.

Ivan Ramen had some great appetizers, but the ramen was just okay. Since we came as a large group, we had preset appetizers and then each ordered our own ramen bowl.- Kyuri Pickles: pretty tasty! A little sour in a good way and mildly spicy; it was a refreshing way to start our meal- Japanese Fried Chicken: really yummy! Definitely tasted fried but was still somehow delicate. Also, it came with a tasty white dipping sauce :)- Pork Belly Steamed Buns: super flavorful with a plush bun and a good proportion of meat and sauce- Pickled Daikon XO: a sort of fermented vegetable with chili garlic on top--this was good, but I probably wouldn't buy it- Tofu Coney Island: I'd pass on this one because it was kind of strange; as the name suggests, all of the toppings (like mustard) could have been on a hotdog instead of fried tofuI ordered the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen with enoki mushrooms as an add-on. The noodles were springy, the egg was perfectly cooked, and there was a generous amount of vegetables. However, I wasn't a fan of the broth, which didn't really have a distinct flavor of soy sauce and was mostly just salty tasting. I also tried a bite of my friend's chicken paitan noodles and probably liked them a little more than my ramen. I thought that the flavor profile did not really taste Asian at all, oddly enough, and my friend agreed. Three people in my party ordered the red spicy chili ramen and said it was not very spicy at all, which was kind of disappointing.Ivan Ramen is a cute place to eat (we ate outside in the garden which was kept quite cool by a sort of vortex of three fans), and the waitress who helped us was super nice. If I came here again, though, I'd probably prefer to stick to appetizers--the pork buns and Japanese fried chicken are where it's at!

The place is always packed and filled with people of all ages. The bar is always active and lively. We checked in and the host told us there's a coat check. After dropping off our coats, we waited about 10 mins to be seated even though we had a reservation. We were served water and bread right away. We got a bottle of Chianti and a dozen oysters to start. The oysters and the accompanied condiments were fresh as well. The blackened snapper was delicious. Zesty and flavorful- really pleasing for your taste buds. The Chilean sea bass was so tasty. Cooked perfectly to be soft but flaky. The texture was incredible. The mashed potatoes were great with the fish. For dessert we had the creme brulee and the butter cake. The creme brulee was creamy and had a think sugar crust. The butter cake was great! Incredibly buttery and rich. It's a great restaurant with good food.

Title: Cozy Spot with Potential for a Return Visit

I visited a quaint little restaurant on a Sunday evening that boasted a relaxed and casual atmosphere. With less than 10 tables, the place wasn’t crowded, which added to the laid-back vibe. However, with only a single server manning the floor, service was understandably a tad slow, yet the waiter's pleasant demeanor made up for the wait.

My entrée, a Pad something with mushrooms, where you choose your protein, was decent, though not particularly memorable – a suggestion that I perhaps didn’t pick the best on the menu. On the other hand, my boyfriend’s chicken basil dish was quite flavorful and stood out as the highlight of our meal.

Portion sizes were generous, especially considering the entrees. Despite my own dish being just okay, the overall experience and the taste of the chicken basil give me enough reason to consider giving this restaurant another shot next time I’m in the area.

My friend and I came here specifically for the frog and we weren't disappointed! We shared the following:1. Stinky tofu - this was a very interesting dish. I've had this back in my hometown which is the province adjacent to Hunan and we make it a bit differently. This was a lot crispier (actually borderline hard) and less... stinky...? Regardless, we enjoyed it. 2. Hunan charcuterie - a nice platter of beef stomach, beef tripe, pig ear, and smoked bean curd that's thankfully not drenched in chili oil. But we thought it was just okay.3. Flaming frog - oh the flavor of this dish! I have very high tolerance for spicy food so personally I didn't find this dish too spicy but appreciated that it had a nice kick to it. Lots of garlic though and it's easy to get confused with the frog bits! Also for those of you who's never eaten frogs before, beware that there are lots of little bones to tease out.The sleek and modern decor and the open kitchen definitely elevated our dining experience to the next level.

I've been here a couple times in the past and my experience is always just OK. On my last visit service was pretty slow and we had to end up getting our own utensils and finding someone to close out our bill. The food itself was OK as well. My friend and I both ordered Mojito's which came out nicely. The decor inside is really nice probably my favorite thing about this restaurant as well as the option to dine outside. Other than that it's an OK place to stop and in case you're hungry and come across but nothing I'd go out of the way for.

Great venue to watch a game...if you are an Ohio State fan.  Ok, that's not completely fair, but last week (Jan 1) we picked this bar due to the vast number of TVs and beer options to watch the college football bowl games.  Full disclosure, we came for the Sugar Bowl (UT vs UGA).  When we arrived, Ohio State was playing Washington.  Good game, but after the game (about 8:15pm) the bar started closing.  Now I know it was a "school" night, but the Sugar Bowl is a legit game.  I'm not talking about a mid-season, Pac-12 matchup that no one wants to watch in NYC, but the Sugar Bowl.  Could also be because this particular Ainsworth (there are 3 I believe) is in the FiDi so it gets quiet late anyway.At any rate, we found another place nearby that did stay open.Importantly, this is a good place with TVs everywhere and a full bar.  Give them a try on Saturday or Sunday, but call first if you want to see a late game.

My recent visit to Charlie Bird for a work lunch was a delightful experience. Despite having booked a table, the restaurant offered plenty of seating, and the ambience was conducive to our team conversations. A heads-up for diners: the lunch menu is somewhat limited, so if you're particular about your choices, it's wise to peruse the menu beforehand.

The Cacio E Pepe I ordered was exceptional and well-received by everyone; it was a testament to the quality of the dishes here. We also shared a variety of appetizers, including the Brussel Sprouts, Farro Salad, and French Fries, which were all crowd-pleasers.

While the final bill reflected the upscale nature of our meal—factoring in our selected drinks and the shared starters—it felt justified given the satisfaction of the dining experience. Altogether, Charlie Bird proved to be a great spot for a work outing, offering a serene environment and a meal that left all of our plates empty.

Service was subpar!  Firstly, we were sent up, but the table wasn't ready- so we stood in no-mans-land while waiters shuffled to and fro and ignored us.  We sat down for fifteen minutes and mid- conversation, the same host interrupted to move us because he needed to make room for other parties.  The food was also subpar so I have judged both the service and the food. My fried beef with peanut sauce was chewy, stringy and the sauce was drowning in peanut sauce.  The rice was uncooked.  For an Asian food establishment, I would sure hope the rice would at least be standard and perfect.  The green curry was average.  Same comment about the side of rice and the fact that it was extremely dry and uncooked.I do not see the appeal of this place nor do I understand the long line!  The Thai food is meh at best.  Is this the only Thai place in town?  The prices were high and I simply do not understand, but they need to step up their game with respect to service if they want to charge in excess of $16 per plate.I will not be returning to this place.  RUDE!
My boyfriend took me here for Valentines Day, the food was excellent, and the ambiance was really beautiful. We will for sure come back.

These are really delicious chicken sandwiches. I've had the fried chicken, the buffalo chicken, and the spicy chicken bacon ranch (I believe this one is limited, so get it while you can!!)!! I was going to give four stars at first because while the buffalo chicken was delicious, I don't feel like it traveled well. I was kind of underwhelmed when I got it back to my office. But the spicy chicken ranch that I had the next day more than made up for it! It was amazing kept me so full. I didn't even get a side and this was more than enough for lunch. I will be going back for sides and the Nutella milkshake at some point.

*Mealpal Review*Baodega is a newcomer to MealPal so I decided to try it one day for lunch. The meal was ready when I got there which was a plus. I was actually surprised to see how cool the restaurant was, especially when I saw a glimpse of the outdoor seating area. I took a peek of it and also noticed they have the Chinatown ice cream factory product ready to be served. I ordered the beef mushroom onion with rice. The portion was adequate and the flavors were good. I would have been happier if the ratio between the beef and onions were adjusted so there was less onion and chewing gum to chew afterwards. I would be keen to order something else from here again to try our other flavours. The restaurant has only been opened for 2 months so all the decor and furnishing is new, clean and modern.

Title: A Delight for the Palate, But at a Premium

Last evening's culinary adventure at this restaurant left a bittersweet taste in our mouths. The food was undeniably delightful, but the prices did give us a moment's pause.

Our meal commenced with a luscious prosciutto crudo paired with Stracchino cheese, a harmony of flavors served on crispy baguette slices. While the cheese was creamy and pleasant, a Burrata might have elevated this dish further.

The fried calamari was a showstopper, with its tenderness and a side of robust tomato sauce that impressed our tastebuds. Moving on to the mains, the Rigatoni with Veal Ragu was a flavorful triumph according to my husband, boasting fresh pasta and a perfectly balanced sauce.

I reveled in the cloud-like gnocchi, which, though missing the cheese sauce, was complimented beautifully by the pink sauce alternative. The veal chop, complete with sage butter sauce, was another hit for my husband, but the $62 price tag may make one think twice.

On the drink front, my IL verde was satisfactory, but the strawberry caipiroska stole the show for me. Meanwhile, my husband's old fashioned felt somewhat short-changed in size, and the $20 glass of red wine seemed a steep ask, even by NYC standards.

In conclusion, if you're willing to indulge financially, this restaurant offers a gastronomic experience that is sure to delight. Just be prepared for a hefty bill to match the high-end taste.

I had the chance to visit Jiang Diner with a group of friends on a Wednesday night. We had made a reservation beforehand since we knew we were going to be a large group. I'd definitely suggest doing this since the place is smaller than most restaurants in the area. Regardless, the service and the food made up for what restaurant lacked in space!After arriving we were immediately seated and given menus to look over. The staff recommended that we order a variety of dishes and serve it amongst ourselves since they were pretty hefty portions. We went with several choices, the da pan ji, spicy dried chicken, lamb ribs, beef and lamb dumplings, and shumai. All great dishes, however the spicy chicken tended to be more on the harder side as opposed to tender. I'd suggest getting any dishes you can without the bone as well. Those that come with it come with A LOT of bone inside.Service here was great too. They brought out all our dishes pretty fast after ordering. They were also quick to clear space on our table once we were done with our dishes and also answered any questions we had about the items on our menu.This is a good option for some northwestern Chinese dishes in a casual setting in the LES. I'd come here with a small group who are will to share plates and don't mind trying classic asian dishes with a slight twist.

Stopped by on a late Sunday night because we wanted Thai food and this restaurant had good reviews. The food came out quickly and tasted amazing. We ordered the Thai iced tea which was great and not too sugary. I ordered the chicken pad Thai and asked them to make it spicy which they really did. I wanted to try something new because the menu is very extensive but ended up just getting the usual pad Thai. The menu also has plenty of vegetarian options so there's something for everyone. I will definitely be returning again.

Spectacular is the view.  I love it here in the quietness of the morning and dawning of a day.  Amusing is the scene. With voices, screams, and, laughter of children in the bustling afternoons.Champagne all the way. There sipping by the lake, in their sublime dining room or their outside dock.Romantic lunches and dinners had.  Their "Jumbo Lump Crab Cake" is what I only really, truly, want.CHEERS!
It was great here!!! We jus happened to walk upon this place . We had to wait like two mins for a seat. Then we had ordered the bowls that were beyond delicious . Fresh and hot I loved this place!

I recently decided to try delivery from this local spot for dinner and was impressed by the speedy 30-minute arrival. The meal was packaged neatly, ensuring everything stayed intact during transit. A noteworthy highlight is their green sauce – it's absolutely delectable and has become my new obsession; I find myself drizzling it over everything!

For starters, I sampled the spinach and cheese empanada. Although the cheese presence was underwhelming, the green sauce came to the rescue, elevating the flavors superbly. For the main course, the baked chicken plate with yellow rice and beans did not disappoint. The chicken was succulent and cooked to perfection, accompanied by a flavorful and satisfying rice and beans duo.

However, the garlic yuka side dish fell short of my expectations. Its peculiar taste and tough texture didn't agree with my palate, and I found myself leaving it aside. Next time, I'll opt for a different side, but I’ll definitely be ordering from here again for that green sauce alone!

So ended up here after the shops at Columbus circle didn't offer a decent $$$ option. Outside of per se and masa which is closed on Sundays.Red beet gnocchi , wild mushroom ricotta and lobster marinara stole the show and my heart . Service was consistent and solid. Cozy seating and great ambiance

Justino's serves pizza with every type of topping you can imagine. Walking in can be slightly overwhelming because there are so many specialty pizza toppings to choose from. One specialty slice always fills me up! My favorite it the chicken parm slice, which is loaded with ricotta, chicken cutlet, and marinara. The prices are also pretty decent considering the area.

Kung Fu is legit for all things carbs: dumplings, especially of the soup variety, noodles and noodle soups, and scallion pancakes.Soup dumplings were some of the better ones I've had, including Chinatown Manhattan and Chinatown Flushing.It's too small/cramped/busy to become a frequent visit, and the prices are slightly more Manhattan than Sunset Park, if you know what I mean. But if you work or live in the area, put this on your list.Pro-tip: try to come during off-peak hours, the place is kind of bonkers during the lunch rush, but you can mingle awkwardly outside if you're not fussy.

I recently dined at a local Indian restaurant that truly impressed me with its culinary offerings. The menu presented an exquisite blend of authentic Indian dishes alongside innovative interpretations of classic flavors.

The highlight of my experience was the perfectly executed braised lamb rack paired with sumptuous bone marrow. The flavors were exceptional, with precise seasoning that accentuated the dish's richness without overpowering it. 

The restaurant's ambiance complemented the dining experience, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere that only added to the overall enjoyment.

While the mixed cocktail I had was expertly prepared, I did find myself longing for a broader representation of traditional Indian spirits in their cocktail creations.

This establishment has earned my wholehearted recommendation, and I eagerly anticipate my next visit to explore more of their culinary delights.

Tucked away in a lively corner, this bustling eatery delivers meals with impressive speed. I sampled their egg noodles with baby corn, doused in a robust black pepper garlic sauce.
