While well-executed for aficionados of greasy Chinese cuisine, the dish was a tad too oily and excessively salty for my taste. It's a classic case of 'been there, done that.' Nevertheless, I appreciate their mastery in a certain style and give them a solid three stars for nailing the greasy food game.

Went here to celebrate my bday with some friends. At first we were told we couldn't get a table for an hour but after waiting just a few minutes. We were told it would be sooner and got a table in 10 minutes. I had the passion rose sangria. Which was nice and refreshing. I also ordered the soft crab tapa and had the pork dumplings. The tapas were great. My only issue is we had to wait a long long time to get them and my friend had to leave and was not able to eat her tapas because she had plans. For my entree I got the bulgogi with brown rice and veggies. I liked how it was so healthy. I actually felt good about eating it. This rarely happens when I go out to eat. The portion was just the right size so I didn't have any left overs. For dessert I had the chocolate lava cake which my friend had order in advance secretly since it was my birthday. They did not put a candle or say happy birthday:/ which was a downer. Overall the food was decent and the service was ok.

After a movie across the street, my boyfriend and I decided on a meal at this establishment, reminiscent of the pleasant experience we had at their Murray Hill location. The interior boasted a familiar open kitchen and generous seating; we chose a booth by the window, observing the restaurant fill up quickly during our stay.

He enjoyed the recommended Wagamama ramen, while I opted for the duck salad - a delightful mix of healthy greens, quinoa, and protein, precisely meeting my cravings. I appreciated the convenient elevator access to the restrooms downstairs, a thoughtful touch for those with mobility needs. Additionally, I was impressed with the ample vegan options on the menu.

This place clearly merits a return visit next time we're in the neighborhood.

Isn't Detroit style pizza supposed to have thick, crunchy crust?  I wanted this to to have crunchy crust, but sadly no crunch at all.  The pizza was very chewy/ doughy throughout. The edges looked like the should've been crunchy, but they were just darkened brown from cooking.  I want to feel and hear the crunch -- it just was not there.  My husband and I ordered 1 personal pan pepperoni pizza and we scarfed down two slices each.  I don't think I've ever seen so many 'roni cups stacked on 1 pizza before.  The pepperoni, sauce, and the cheese were great, but the crunch I wanted was missing for me.There were also 3 homeless people sitting on the sidewalk right next to one of the two tables outside the establishment.  The smell was a little less than appetizing.All in all I have had this place bookmarked on Yelp for a while now and was very happy that I was FINALLY able to try it.

Title: A Noodle Haven in the Heart of NYC

If there's one place I never miss during my trips to New York City, it's this noodle sanctuary. The noodles strike a perfect balance — gelatinous in texture, cooked impeccably to avoid any hint of being overly mushy or unbearably firm. 

The customizable spiciness of the sauce is a standout feature. The mild level is gentle for those with a tender palate, while the normal heat provides a robust flavor that complements the noodles without overwhelming them.

Don't even get me started on their tofu — it's a revelation. Softer than silk, it dissolves on the tongue, offering a milder spice that pairs exquisitely with the rest of the meal. This spot is a must-visit for noodle enthusiasts and tofu lovers alike. A true gem!

Love this place! I came here with my family. We were looking for a great lunch spot in the area and were seeking out amazing food (the norm for my family).So glad we stopped here! We got tacos and margaritas. So amazing! I love the ambiance and vibe here, too. This location is very spacious and has a lot of charm.My mom, sister and I all loved our food and entrees. The food was so flavorful and fresh. I'll definitely be back here, again.The restaurant had a lot of seating and although there were lots of people here it didn't seem too crowded.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Grazie

My recent visit to Grazie left me disillusioned, contrasting sharply with the expectations set by previous reviews. The ambiance, particularly upstairs, was stark and uncomfortably quiet, amplifying the need for background music or some form of noise to break the uneasy silence.

Upon being seated, it was immediately apparent that attentiveness to cleanliness was lacking. Both the menus handed to us and the cutlery provided were dirty—my knife to the extent that I had to request a replacement. Notably, even the walls weren't spared from neglect, evidenced by the presence of a fly.

Hoping the food would redeem the experience, I ordered the organic chicken salad, a decision that sadly compounded my disappointment. The chicken was dry and had an unappetizing texture that hinted at it not being freshly prepared. To make matters worse, the pricing did not reflect the quality served.

The dated decor and overall lack of care suggest a dire need for renovation and a menu refresh. Unfortunately, based on this experience, I cannot see myself returning or recommending Grazie. It feels as though the passion and standard once held have significantly waned.

Small restaurant with lovely dimly lit ambiance and chill vibe. There is a communal table as well as a bar area and several 2 seat tables. Bonus that they take reservations and you can request where you sit if you have a preference. The service was impeccable. Our waiter was extremely pleasant and friendly. He took the time to ask if we had any special requests or dietary restrictions. When we told him, he worked with us to specially curate what we ordered, making slight menu modifications that suited our needs. I felt like we had our own private dining experience catered specifically for our needs. The idea of the restaurant is for sharing small plates, but accommodations can be made. Loved it and I will be back.

Title: Aesthetically Pleasing but Overpriced Brunch at Bubby's

I recently visited Bubby's for brunch, enticed by the allure of their much-photographed Pancake Flight. This trio of sizable, fluffy pancakes promised a delightful morning indulgence. The blueberry pancake delivered a burst of flavor, but the banana-walnut version fell short with scarce toppings. The third, adorned with strawberries and Nutella, was sadly nondescript.

Bubby's culinary misstep, however, was overshadowed by the startling $25 price tag - a steep sum for pancakes that failed to dazzle the palate as much as they did the camera lens. Moreover, their payment process left a sour taste, automatically setting a generous 20% tip without clear initial disclosure.

For those seeking a picture-perfect brunch, Bubby's might fulfill that niche. But for value and taste, you're better off exploring other menu options or dining establishments. In summary, decent pancakes, but not at a price that mirrors their worth.

Updated review -- ordered again and I'm getting a better sense of what's good here.  I had the chicken gyro and enjoyed it.  Had regular fries, which were better than the sweet potato fries, but tasted a bit dry.  The desserts were amazing!  I had apple pie and mousse cake and loved both of them.  Got a blueberry muffin which was large and would have been good if it was fresh, but was sadly past its prime.  Quesadilla was okay, but the cheese tasted like cheddar which was a bit odd for a quesadilla.  Delivery was fast and food came hot. Review #1 -- Great delivery - food came quickly, packaged well, and still piping hot.  Food was just average, and not cheap, but portions were large.I had french onion soup - it was good, especially considering it was delivery. Also had the turkey meatloaf.  I wasn't a fan.  It came with gravy instead of tomato sauce.  Also came with a Caesar salad, peas and carrots, and sweet potato.  So much food, but unfortunately nothing was memorable or stood out.Not sure if I'll ever order from here again.  Definitely wont be going to the restaurant.

I arrived at the restaurant just after 4:30pm, beating the evening rush which was a smart move as the place started to fill up by 5:30pm. For those considering a visit, the chawanmushi is a must-try. It's possibly the softest, most flavorful steamed egg custard I've ever had, brimming with a variety of ingredients such as crab, chicken, anago, shrimp, shiitake mushrooms, fish cake, and gingko nuts. It's a delight for the senses.

Moving on to the main course, I sampled the duck udon. The noodles hit just the right balance of softness and chewiness, while the broth was perfectly seasoned. The duck, while tasty, was a tad chewier than I prefer, but it didn't detract much from the overall dish. My experience was such a positive one that I'm already planning my next visit for another helping of their delectable offerings.

A michelin star restaurant with affordable prices, attentive service, and intimate but laid back vibe? all checked.We arrived without reservations on a weekend night and got a perfect corner table. The shrimp and veggie tempura app was perfectly crisp, and the miso soup was as good as any miso soup can be. then we ordered a sashimi for 2, and the sushi for 2 - certainly a lot of food for a couple. The only weird thing was the appearance of the sushi rolls - did not seem like something that a michelin star restaurant would do - still, everything tasted fresh and was superb.The price point wasn't bad for the quality, location, ambience, and service. Would recommend for any sushi lover.Bonus tip: the plum wine is inexpensive and pretty good (if you like plum wine)

Title: Disappointed Return to Las' Lap - Only 2 Stars

I'm heartbroken to rate Las' Lap with only 2 stars. My adoration for this spot blossomed with Chef Kelvin's arrival and his irresistible Arepas. Sadly, those days are gone – the menu has undergone a complete overhaul, stripping away all of Kelvin's magic.

On a recent visit, the once-exciting Las' Lap seemed lackluster. The once standout drinks, while still good, couldn't justify their high price. The compact space, an advantage when not crowded, now just felt empty without the allure of Chef Kelvin's creations.

Our group, eager for a delightful dinner, faced a new, uninspiring menu. Despite what we had hoped based on their Instagram updates, not a trace of Kelvin's signature dishes remained. We settled on the Jerk spring rolls, which didn’t impress our palates, and the Macaroni Pie, which was passable at best. Our dinner dwindled to multiple orders of fries – a stark contrast to the rich flavors we used to crave here.

I'm holding out hope for a revival of Las' Lap's menu. It’s a shame to witness such a gem lose its sparkle.

I recently visited this restaurant and tried their chicken burrito, which was simply delicious. The burrito was generously filled with white rice, corn, sour cream, and shredded chicken, hitting all the right flavor notes. It was also accompanied by a fresh side salad, adding a nice touch to the meal. I was impressed with the prompt service and appreciated the cleanliness of the bathroom. I would definitely recommend this spot to any burrito enthusiasts out there!

Having recently stumbled upon this gem since my job transition, I've quickly become a regular, indulging thrice in a single week. Their breakfast sandwiches, particularly the sausage, egg, and cheese on an everything bagel, are a steal at $3.50. Despite a bustling morning, the service was prompt, suiting those with time constraints. Additionally, their pre-made sandwiches with Brie are a delightful treat. Overall, a commendable choice for a delicious and efficient breakfast experience.

The infamous Pastis is back. One of the biggest restaurant scenes is warmly welcomed back to the MPD. Bustling and friendly and full of Manhattan panache with an updated menu with lots of delicious options.Ate and drank:Rose $7BreadArtichokes and tapenadeSkateI scored an outdoor table on opening night.One of the few places you can get a mini wine- perfect for me . Oh that Balthazar bread and butter.Delicious French fare and Manhattan is back!This has become like a semi toxic relationship with disappointment as standard while I love some items- the skate, the escargot and the duck confit the service can be dismissive at times.Stick to bread and basics here as you may not always get what you want here, except "the scene.'

Some very tasty tacos! Line can get very long but the wait is really not that bad. When we got there, the line was past the spices store and it only took us about 20 minutes to order and get our food so, worth the wait. No tables or seats or anything like that. I opted for the cheese shell tacos which is very good and isn't listed on the menu. I also thought that just for changing the type of shell, the price changed a lot. Would still come back and probably just get one as they are fairly heavy.

Title: A Delightful Find for a Quick and Affordable Feast

I recently visited this hidden gem, an ideal spot for those seeking a rapid yet satisfying meal without breaking the bank. Delving into the skewer combo at a mere $20, I was impressed by the variety it offered, including chicken, chicken skin, gizzards, beef, and pork skewers. The standouts for me were the gizzard and chicken skewers—both exceptionally chewy and flavorful. Adding some vegetable skewers might be a good idea for those looking for a more rounded dining experience.

The yakisoba priced at $9 was also a hit, providing a generous serving size perfect for sharing. The noodles boasted a well-balanced texture, free from the excess oiliness typical of lesser establishments, though I’ve encountered superior versions elsewhere.

Their extensive izakaya menu promises something to tantalize every palate, leaving me eager to sample the cheesy potatoes and okonomiyaki on my inevitable return visit. This spot is convincingly a smart choice for anyone craving authentic tastes at pocket-friendly prices. Highly recommended!

My husband and I had the pleasure of dining at this charming little restaurant for a complimentary dinner, and it was an evening to remember. It was my inaugural foray into the world of claypot cuisine, and the experience did not disappoint.

We decided on a vegetarian claypot for myself and a chicken claypot for my husband, accompanied by a side of quail eggs. The portions were generous, offering great value for the price. The standout feature had to be the bowl brimming with ginger and garlic served on the side; adding it to the claypot elevated the flavors immensely—this is a must-do for anyone visiting.

The staff were exceptionally cordial, not only making us feel welcomed but also providing stellar recommendations that enhanced our dining experience. The freshness of the ingredients shone through, highlighting the quality of the food served here.

In sum, this restaurant is a true gem for claypot lovers, blending great service, affordability, and delectable, fresh food into one delightful package.

The only thing precluding this place from getting a 5th star is the fact that we waited a solid 20 minutes before anyone took our order and I think another 40 minutes to get our food. They initially told us there'd be a 20 minute wait, but they surprised us and it ended up only being 10 mins or so - but then we did wait a bit more at the table, so there's that.We inhaled the warm, crusty, crumbly biscuits. And ordered the chicken and waffles and corned beef hash with 2 eggs over easy. Once they came, we were contented. The waffles - fluffy, draped in butter and syrupy goodness that we added to it. The chicken - crispy, flavorful, with succulent bits of meat cocooned in their browned shell.  We mixed the hash together and each bite contained a flavorful, texturally interesting bite - egg, home fries, corned beef. Honestly one of the best meals I've had- for $40 for the two of us with a nice tip, no less. Worth the wait. It was great. And an establishment.

Title: Unbeatable Lunch Experience at a Western Gem!

Based on a stellar recommendation from my brother, I ventured to this restaurant for their much-acclaimed lunch special. The visit was a unanimous success among my friends and me, with the highlight being their legitimately impressive burger – it's the real deal!

The ambiance transports you to a cozy western lodge, thanks to its extensive use of wood and rustic charm. Whether you snag a booth or settle at the bar, comfort is guaranteed. The atmosphere is also conducive to productivity, as evidenced by many patrons working away on their laptops.

A special shout-out is due to the exceptional service. My server's willingness to crawl under the table to assist me with plugging in my phone was a testament to her dedication. She consistently went above and beyond, enhancing our dining experience.

For those in search of a great lunch offering both value and flavor in a relaxed setting, look no further. This spot has you covered.

Mala Project's sister restaurant opened up in FiDi! They have some of the same menu items but this place serves more home-cooked Chinese meals. I can finally get some real Chinese food without having to go to Chinatown or Flushing.I asked for a few recommendations but for the most part, my favorites were still my basic go-to's. Mouthwatering Chicken - a bit spicy for my taste but I can see why people like it so much from Mala Project due to the chili oil, crunchy peanuts, and chilled chicken.Scallion Pancake - you really can't go wrong or get any more basic than your traditional breakfast pancake! Pan Fried Pork Dumplings - these were literally the best! They tasted just like what you would get at home or in Chinatown. I could make a meal just out of the dumplings themselves! The juicy filling and crispy skin went perfectly with the soy sauce and vinegar mixture!Haw Herbal Tea - I've never seen this anywhere else. Growing up, I remember eating haw snacks but I've never had it in tea form. It was an interesting, citrusy, and tart way to end the meal.

I had a delightful experience dining at this restaurant, where the complimentary bread rolls immediately set a warm and welcoming tone. The sides were satisfying, though I found the corn to be excessively creamy, which may not suit all palates.

Curiosity led me to try the Impossible Burger, despite not being vegetarian, and it was a standout dish. Its plant-based patty was so convincingly meat-like, complemented by the rich flavors of mushrooms, cheese, and truffle, that I was almost tricked into thinking it was real beef.

My boyfriend opted for the Saxon Burger, which was a bit of a letdown. It strayed from the ideal medium-cooked preference, arriving overdone and notably dry.

Service did wane a bit, with our waitress seeming less attentive than we'd have liked, requiring several attempts to catch her attention.

Despite the service hiccup and the Saxon burger's shortcomings, the Impossible Burger's excellence alone is a draw for a return visit.

During a recent trip to New York, I made it a point to visit a much-talked-about local eatery for my first meal in the city. Easily navigating my way there, I arrived at the surprisingly queue-free establishment at 10:30 AM.

Opting for variety, I chose a small plate featuring all three meats - roasted pork, duck, and chicken - for a mere $5. Since the restaurant lacks seating, I enjoyed my meal on a nearby park bench, an experience in itself.

The accompanying BBQ sauce was a standout, enhancing the dish with its subtly sweet notes. The BBQ pork deserves special mention for its tender, well-flavored chunks. It was the highlight, and I admit to savoring it last. The duck, though bony, was tender with delectably crisp skin. The chicken, however, was fairly average and divergent from what I'm accustomed to.

At such a modest price point, this place is nothing short of a hidden gem, especially given the quality of the meats. It's worth noting that this is a cash-only spot, but don't let that deter you from the delicious offerings on hand.

I'm a regular here since I work nextdoor at 30 Hudson Yards and in the dozen or more times I've come here I've fallen in love with the place.  Prices are reasonable for the area as we have very few choices other than very high end restaurants in the nearby mall.  The staff is always very friendly and welcoming.  Food is great.  First I fell in love with their tuna pasta salad - truly delicious.  They have a large grab n go area with sandwiches and salads plus a hot section with soup and sandwiches.  Their breakfast sandwiches are delicious as well as the croque monsieur and croissant with ham and melted cheese.  French onion soup is one of my faves and their warm pressed sandwiches are all solid.  Plenty of tables inside and outside seating when the weather is warmer.  All of their fresh breads are pretty authentic and tasty.  They also have great coffee.  Now while I said their prices are reasonable for the area some may find it a bit pricey as a pressed sandwich will run you around $13 and the soup is like $8 or 9 so it's easily a $25 lunch by the time you're done but personally I don't mind paying when the food and service are so good plus it's literally just a short walk across the park from my office.  All that adds up to me being a big fan and I'm very happy to have them in the neighborhood!!

Dropped in at Printers Alley for a much needed post-work Happy Hour. The place was jam packed and it was a struggle to find seating- a few of the tables were reserved so I'd suggest calling ahead!This is a basic bar with a honky tonk feel. Got a $8 frozen marg ($9 with the charge for flavoring) But was disappointed because the drink was a watery, strawberry slushee at best.We had a good time but had to flag down the waitress every time we  needed a thing. Apps were tasty, but don't expect your typically dine in experience even if you have a waitress dedicated to your table.

Absolutely adore this gem of a restaurant! The dishes are not only delectable but also reasonably priced. The service is commendable, with all staff members being exceptionally friendly and eager to help. I've dined here multiple times with both family and friends, and it's been a hit with everyone. Highly recommend a visit!

Jayleen's is a hole in the wall that serves gyro and falafel on a platter or as a sandwich. The place is tiny and it is literally just one guy behind a counter that prepares the food. The gyro meat is actually very good and is cut straight from a vertical meat spit. It was definitely very juicy. However, their food is really not worth the price. For $12, you get meat with rice and a huge piece of pita bread. You can get an equal amount of food from some street carts for half the price. I guess that is why they give you such a big piece of bread - to make the meal seem more filling.

Heard about this place through a friend, who'd been wanting to come here for a pasta making class for awhile. The pasta making classes here are considerably cheaper than other classes in the city, so we got tickets for one Saturday afternoon and came. We were in the downstairs section of the restaurant, at the bar area. People were in the same room eating when we were doing our class, which I was surprised about, as I thought we'd be in a private room. No one checked our tickets at all when we came in and situated ourselves there, which I was very surprised about also, as anyone from the street could have come in and taken spots. The class was taught by a chef at Aunt Jake's, who was friendly and welcoming, but he had a difficult time individually instructing people due to the size of the group. Instructions were given to the group as a whole, and we did not receive much individual instruction. The class was fun and simple, but in the end, we did not get to eat or take home our own fresh pasta that we had made. The chef said this was due to 'health regulations'. We were instead given sheets of pasta to mold and cut into shapes that we wanted, and instead took these home. After the pasta making section of the class was over, there were a few different kinds of pasta for us to eat, which was share style. It was good, not amazing, but also really nice to have the food included after class. I cooked the pasta two days after class and it turned out really nicely. Would recommend to anyone looking for an affordable and quick cooking class.

Loved it! Our server Sandra was awesome. She stopped by our table the right amount of times which was perfect for us. It was dinner for two, my husband ordered fish and chips and I had the salmon rice and veggies which both were very good. The water brought to our table was great tasting as well. I've been by this place many times wanting to try it out but it alway looks extremely busy but now I think this will be a place I would order from for pick up to take home. I also had a mixed drink that Sandra recommended which I really liked as well. Our bill was $60 which was not expensive at all considering the service, location and amount of food. This restaurant is bi level with an outside patio upstairs which I'll try out next time I'm there. During the summer the door open up on all side of the restaurant too. I also will try their brunch on the weekends as bourbon pancakes sound AMAZING!

Title: Disappointing Brunch Experience

My recent brunch at this establishment left much to be desired. The overall quality of both the food and service failed to meet expectations. I opted for the avocado toast, which despite its steep price arrived as a simple, unremarkable dish with soggy bread and a forgettable salad side. The accompanying potatoes were particularly unpleasant—lacking flavor and distressingly soggy.

My friend's choice, rice and beans, while satisfactory, didn't impress either. It's a basic dish that is hard to get wrong, and though they didn't err in its preparation, it certainly wasn't noteworthy.

Our experience with the staff compounded the lackluster meal. The service was unfriendly, and our waitress seemed uninterested in ensuring we had a pleasant dining experience, neglecting even the basic courtesy of checking in on us.

All in all, whether it was just an off day for their brunch menu or a broader issue at this location, I can't recommend a visit based on this disappointing outing.

I really like this place. It's a quiet, cozy, intimate space where you can get great Italian food for an affordable price. The service was exceptional. Our waiter was very friendly and patient, and went over the specials menu with us, answering any clarifying questions we had and waiting for us to be ready to order (it took me awhile, lol, when there are many good options I go through internal conflict until the inner voices in my head reach a consensus), and he kept our water filled.The pasta is al dente, seasoned perfectly, and of course I added some pepper and parmesan to the dish to add a bit of *umph*, not that the truffle oil needed any additional notes. Let's talk about how I was full but saw the dessert offered on the specials board and decided to go for it even though I knew I didn't need any more food. How the words "chocolate" and "passion fruit mousse" made my heart skip a beat. It did not disappoint. I'm really glad I overindulged that day.I had a nice glass of Chardonnay with my meal and was overall very satisfied with my experience there.I recommend it for dates, family time, or just a place to hang out with friends and have a nice, long conversation.

During a recent visit to New York with friends, we stumbled upon a delightful gem of a restaurant. The cleanliness and organization were immediately noticeable, and the ambiance was enhanced by a cozy blue light, setting a calm and relaxed mood.

The highlight of our dining experience was the omakase, a steal at just $75 compared to the more common $100 offering elsewhere. Each dish was not only visually stunning but also packed with flavor. The bluefin tuna tartar was notably refreshing, and the "four-color island" striped bass entree stood out for its extraordinary tenderness and juiciness.

The staff's warmth and attentiveness added to our experience, as they frequently came by to top off our hot water, a small but appreciated gesture that kept us comfortable on a chilly day. This restaurant is certainly a must-visit, and its combination of excellent food, ambiance, and service makes it a standout.

Title: A Chinatown Gem: May Wah Delivers Taste and Value

If value and flavor are what you seek, May Wah won't disappoint. This gem has been my go-to for years for a quick, satisfying bite that doesn't break the bank. The sit-down section, which might be lesser-known than its bustling takeout counterpart, is a haven where you're promptly seated and served.

The standout for me? The chicken leg over rice. Imagine tender chicken paired with a perfectly seasoned meat sauce, complemented by tangy pickled cabbage—all layered over fluffy rice. The harmonious blend of flavors consistently satisfies my cravings.

Don't miss out on their pickled cabbage soup either; it's a comforting choice on any day. May Wah’s reliability and affordability make it a cornerstone of the Chinatown dining scene. I wholeheartedly recommend it for anyone craving a delightful meal without the hefty price tag.
Mushroom egg scramble, Spicy sausage and caramelized pizza and Bomboloni donuts were all great upon my most recent visit. Service was a little weird though.

Title: Impressive Space and Enjoyable Bites near Grand Central

I recently visited this expansive restaurant with colleagues for post-work drinks and appetizers. We opted for a spot right by the bar, which turned out to be an excellent choice. The menu offerings we sampled, including oysters, shrimps, and fried calamari, were all delightful and unanimously enjoyed by my group. The ambiance of the place added to our great time, providing a pleasant backdrop to our evening. While it may not become my regular haunt, I'd certainly recommend giving it a try if you find yourself in the vicinity of Grand Central Terminal.

The lunch menu at this eatery is exceptional, offering a diverse selection that caters to all tastes. Portion sizes are generous, ensuring a satisfying meal. I highly recommend a visit for a midday dining experience that won't disappoint.

3/5 for the food, the service was very good and the waiter was very attentive. Ahi Tuna - 5/5 very deliciousChicken Katsu Curry - 3/5 - Chicken wasn't as crispy, they put seaweed on top which overpowers the curry taste by quite a bit. Not a fan of the seaweed at allGyu Don - 3/5 - Beef was not cut thin enough or simmered for the right amount. This resulted in some pretty overcooked beef. Again there was seaweed on it, overpowering, which is not a positive thing for meI think that there's a lot of potential for this restaurant here, especially showing that they can do rather well with the Ahi Tuna. If they tighten up on the non sushi dishes, I think I wouldn't mind returning.

This is a great place for a casual dinner or a family outing. The sushi was the highlight of the experience. The lobster rolls were my favorite. I would recommend starting with this. The lavender margarita was better than I expected. The salmon was average.

A warm place but the location, 10th Ave Midtown is a challenge to those whom from the Upper East-Siders.All the plates we've ordered : Tempura fish, Tempura uni, Sashimi Platter, minced shrimp noodles, Kakiage seafood Don, were the freshest at my personally experienced so far. The table service is also the top level and ambiance was warm and vivid.

The Maze is a Korean American fusion bar/lounge. It's not easy to find but they have a standing sign outside - you walk inside to take an elevator to the second floor. I hosted a large party here for the holidays and the staff did a great job to secure us tables in a private area for our group. My girlfriends and I had a few lychee Martintis - it was so good and strong. Food is decent and regular size not party platter size. It's worthwhile to come here during their happy hour specials from 5-8pm. The appetizers are a bit cheaper by $1-3, depending on the entree.My friends and I had a great time and would come back here again.

This was my first time at this location and my last. I ordered a slice of toast with avocado, topped with tomatoes with a side of fruit. Fruit was good because, well, they didn't make it and coffee was decent. My avocado toast on the other hand was HORRIBLE. I was hungry as this was my first meal of the day but I just couldn't finish it. The bread wasn't really toasted for starters and they put so much butter that my bread was starting to get moist. I got the feeling that they didn't have much avocado left because they thinly spread it out instead of adding avocado slices. The pieces of tomatoes almost nonexistent. This whole meal was just terrible.

Title: A Warm Welcome and Tasty Bites at City Gem

I had the pleasure of visiting this charming restaurant in the heart of the city and was immediately struck by the warmth and hospitality of the staff. Sandy and Mauro, who were outside, greeted me with such friendliness that I felt instantly at ease. Inside, Danny the bartender exemplified the kind of welcoming atmosphere that can be hard to come by, offering a warmth that set the tone for a delightful evening.

The restaurant prides itself on its cleanliness, and it shows; both the restrooms and dining area were spotless. The food was a highlight, with flavors that lived up to the glowing reputation that preceded my visit. Additionally, the Happy Hour specials were an absolute hit, providing exceptional value.

One point of concern is the near-treacherous journey to the bathrooms due to the steep stairs. It's a minor flaw in an otherwise enchanting experience, one that won't deter me from returning. In fact, I am eagerly anticipating trying their brunch, which I've heard is quite the weekend treat. Despite the stairway, this restaurant is a definite must-visit, and I can't wait to come back.

I recently visited a restaurant that specializes in Northern-style pho, and I must say, it was a noteworthy experience. The noodles were intriguingly different – larger and less soft than the typical fare found in the States – which added a delightful twist to the dish. This place is confident in its flavors, providing no extra herbs or hoisin sauce on the side, a bold statement that their broth stands strong on its own.

As for the meat options, they keep it simple yet satisfying with just two choices: rare beef or cooked brisket. Both proved to be excellent companions to the noodles and broth. The hot sauce provided is authentic and likely imported from Vietnam, offering a genuine kick that heightens the experience.

And don't overlook the vinegar peppery sauce available in a big jar; it's a game-changer that can transform your entire bowl. This restaurant offers a unique take on pho without compromising on authenticity, serving up a bowl that's both familiar and refreshingly novel.

Title: Decent Taste, Questionable Value

I recently tried the General Tso chicken rice bowl for lunch through the Ritual app, taking advantage of their $5 off promotion for my first order. Upon arrival at the modest takeout shop, I experienced a brief wait of about 5 minutes.

As for the meal itself, the chicken bowl was satisfactory in flavor but lacked a wow factor. A glaring issue was the disproportionate chicken to rice ratio; the bowl contained a scant two tablespoons of chicken, as evident in the accompanying photo.

In conclusion, while the dish was edible enough for a repeat, the regular price of $13 is steep given the quantity of protein provided. It's a meal that could be enjoyed again under a promotional price, but not one I'd recommend at full cost.

Great place to take a date! At first the line was a bit long, but it ended up moving pretty quickly and once you get seated the food starts coming out pretty quickly. I ordered the 5 roll set and it was all delicious! Not the most filling meal ever, but it leaves room if you want to go somewhere nearby like Lady M cakes to grab dessert afterwards.

Title: Comfort Food Bliss at S'MAC

If you're a mac and cheese aficionado, look no further than S'MAC – it never disappoints! During my latest visit, I indulged in the buffalo chicken major munch, which turned out to be a delicious testament to the idea that the eyes are often bigger than the stomach. The portion was generous – perhaps too much so for a single sitting, but who's complaining?

For those with dietary preferences or restrictions, you'll be pleased to find they offer gluten-free options, including elbow pasta and breadcrumbs. Be prepared to pay a little extra for these substitutions ($1.50 for the nosh size and $3 for the major munch size), but given the quality of the meal, it feels justified.

My only gripe? The ordering kiosks. In a bustling city, the charm of human interaction is missed, and the growing line, filled with a mix of puzzled faces trying to navigate the machines, is a testament to that. Despite this hiccup, S'MAC remains a must-visit for a hearty, satisfying meal.

Very cute restaurant with artworks on the wall! There's a machine for you to place an order and pay, and the kitchen will prepare your food accordingly. Pretty cool concept but not sure how it would work if there's a long line. Portions are big for me but I finished most of it because it's delicious!

Cute spot, cozy seating, pink lighting.  There's lots to like about this place. My friend set up a lovely Girls' Night Out here and we enjoyed it  For drinks, I had the mezcal and pineapple which had a nice kick to it. As far as food, we tried the nachos, ceviche and corn.  We loved the nachos.  The coconut ceviche was interesting.  And the corn was good.  I haven't had much exposure to vegan food so for a first timer, this was a very nice intro.  I don't know if I'd order the ceviche again, but definitely get those nachos.  Service was excellent.

Title: The Perfect Happy Hour Spot in Ktown – Baro

Baro has quickly become my preferred choice for happy hour in Ktown. Their offerings are impressive, with $10 soju and $8 wine that pair perfectly with their irresistible truffle fries. What truly stands out is their extended happy hour, going until 6 PM on weekdays and starting at 3 PM on Saturdays, right when the doors open.

The service at Baro is consistently attentive and friendly, ensuring a pleasant experience with every visit. I find their truffle fries to be an absolute delight—the kind of snack that keeps you coming back for more. The drinks are generous in portion, leaving nothing to be desired.

As for the ambiance, Baro nails it with good bar seating and warm lighting, creating an inviting and comfortable atmosphere that's perfect for unwinding after work or kicking off a weekend night out.

In summary, if you're seeking a happy hour haven in Ktown with great deals, fantastic service, and a cozy vibe, Baro should be at the top of your list.

Good salads but they don't mix the bowls well. As I was eating my chicken caesar salad, I was wondering where the chicken was. I found it with most of the parmesan at the bottom of the bowl.About the service, I placed my order through their app but when I arrived to pick it up, they couldn't find it. The transaction didn't go smoothly but the quickly remedied it by preparing my order on the spot.

Shrimp tacos had nice big shrimp but they were overcooked. Tasty and well seasoned, but still. Their carnitas taco was soaked in liquid. Not meaty liquid, like someone accidentally spilled water all over the taco. It was leaking onto the other ones in the container and breaking through the double tortilla. It also tasted like nothing, and the meat was shredded so fine it was stringy, becoming a watery lump in your mouth before disintegrating, like it came out of a pressure cooker. Not a fan.

Title: Authentic Japanese Delight

I was keen on satisfying my craving for authentic Japanese cuisine, and I'm happy to report that this restaurant nailed it. Despite the predictable weekend waitlist, a mere 30-minute patience was well rewarded. The eatery's clean, minimalist ambiance, coupled with top-notch service, set a serene stage for the dining experience.

Opting for bar seating, we were pleasantly surprised by the prompt arrival of our meals. My choice, the grilled mackerel set, was just slightly on the saltier side but executed with perfect doneness. The accompanying rice struck a delightful balance between springy and soft, and the miso soup was generously served, robust in flavor, outshining its counterparts from less authentic establishments.

An introduction to radish in my palate profile suggested potential for a budding preference, although I found myself yearning for a bolder taste. However, true to the subtlety of Japanese cuisine, it remained mild.

The meal's conclusion with a serving of hot green tea was the perfect palate cleanser, wrapping up the culinary journey on a high note.

This is in the running for the, if not the single, best overall dining experience I've ever had. From the waiters polite, but not intrusive attentiveness, to the food, to the wine pairings, to the way they timed things for us to see our show, it was spectacularly well-done.My wife and I came here for our 10th wedding anniversary before going to see a 7p show of Hadestown. Only the dining room takes reservations and only at 5p or later. I gave them a call and asked if that would work and they suggested that we do the three-course prix fixe menu rather than the six-course tasting menu just because they felt like it would lead to a nicer and better-paced dining experience.They were totally right. Between the courses pacing and the wine pairings, the 90-minute meal with 3 courses was just about right for a fun, yummy leisurely, celebratory meal. Beyond that, the were more than happy to let us swap out anything from the tasting menu into the three-course prix fixe menu and were more than happy to do wine pairings for us on the three-course menu. The wine pairings were well-thought-out, somewhat surprising at times, but ally good and they were more than happy to take something back and try again if it really didn't work.As we sat down, they poured us champagne to toast to our anniversary and left us to that for a few minutes before coming back to get the meal started. That was sort of emblematic of the attention to detail for the whole meal.The first thing to come out was an on-the-house appetizer of grilled romano beans with eggplant purée. While not the hit of the night, it was certainly delicious and impressive with how something this simple could be this good. Periodically, they would bring out their dinner buns with whipped goat cheese butter starting with this course. The whipped goat cheese butter was very, very good, but not quite the ambrosia I had hoped for given what it was made with. Still the little bit of tartness from the goat cheese really ups the buttered bread in a way that I'd love to have more of.For our first course I had the beef tartare with pine nuts, rye toast, and pickled mushrooms. My wife had the ruby red shrimp with cauliflower, shell beans, and bacon. While both were good, the beef tartare was pretty spectacular, while I thought the shrimp were merely good. That being said, my wife just didn't want to do raw beef, which I get. So, to each their own.For mains, I had the monkfish with sungold tomatoes, summer squash, and mussels. It was stunning. The fish was perfectly cooked and just a hint of being firm, while still being buttery and moist. My wife got the beef with mashed potatoes, which was also great although I tend to have an easier time finding a good steak than good seafood. Still, I'm super-picky about my beef and this was more than up for the challenge.For desert, we got the cookie plate with milk, the chocolate tart with raspberries, raspberry jam and bourbon ice cream, and if that wasn't enough they brought us a coconut cake covered with coconut meringue on the house for our anniversary. Beyond all that, they sent us home with two small gummies and  two chocolate truffles, which I think they give to everyone who comes regardless.We couldn't finish desert and ended up bringing the gummies, truffles and most of the cookie plate with us for later, but man were they good later. The truffles were almost as good as a Teuscher champagne truffle, which is kind of insane and all the cookies were different and great to try.The winner of the deserts was really the coconut cake, which they should put on the menu. It was dense, moist and spectacular with the meringue offering some interesting texture as well as some appropriate airiness to the complete coconut package.The chocolate tart was also good, and bourbon ice cream is great, but a chocolate tart with raspberries is something I've had done well elsewhere.The desert wine pairings were especially well-done with my wife getting a very interesting sweet mead that was unexpected and incredibly well-paired.

I can't wait to come back. This bustling pizza shop has such a great atmosphere, quick service and delicious food! As a newbie to the area, I'm so happy I found this place. All different types of pizzas available in both personal 9" and large 16" size. Can make your own in either size or go the healthy route and order a salad. Organic crust is available too. The pie was cooked to the perfect crisp. Highly recommend their Goat Cheese and Prosciutto Crostini's-- to die for! There was a nice crowd gathered around the bar, not a ton of seats but plenty of standing room. Didn't get a table outside but it is available. Our waiter was very nice, I look forward to coming back.

The ramen here was pretty bad, and for the area its in, I wouldn't really ever come here.I started off the Thukpa ramen, which I assumed would be the best since it was named after their restaurant. But the broth was bland, the noodles weren't very good and the toppings were just sad.I ended up making my boyfriend switch with me for his dan dan ramen, which was a bit more flavorful, but equally sad in terms of a boring broth, crappy toppings, and noodles that tasted like they were pre-packaged.

I visited this restaurant on a Monday evening and was pleased to find it wasn't too crowded at 6 PM, although it did get busier later on. The waitress stood out with her expert recommendations of the spicy dried pot, Malatang, and various meats.

We opted for the spicy dried pot, fish fillet Malatang, and dried stir chicken with tri-pepper, and were delighted by the ability to handpick fresh vegetables and meats from a vast selection at the counter. The assembling process was part of the fun, with a controlled serving size and a customization of spice levels, before watching our choices being stir-fried into our final dishes.

The highlight for me was the flavorful medium spice dried pot, which packed more heat than anticipated – a pleasant surprise for a spice lover. It came with rice, which was a thoughtful touch. While the dried stir chicken had a good spice, it was a tad too salty. The mild fish fillet Malatang, on the other hand, provided a perfect, soothing counterbalance to the other spicier items, with its flavorful broth that wasn't spicy but still aromatic.

Overall, I'm excited to revisit for another round of the delicious dried pot.

EXCELLENT!  5 stars.For a a modern twist on Indian food, you definitely need to try Rahi.  Here you can find some of the most traditional dishes that are transformed into a delicious modern plate.  One of the best is the Mushroom Khichardi.  For as odd as it is for have mushroom in this dish, it might be better than the original.  Check this place out, you won't regret it.

Title: A KBBQ Haven with Delightful Budaejigae

I recently diverted from my usual order of Korean BBQ at one of my favorite spots and opted for the Budaejigae, a hearty and flavorful army stew. It did not disappoint! The stew was deeply satisfying, and it's hard to imagine this dish being anything but delicious. This restaurant remains a top recommendation for anyone craving authentic Korean BBQ and more. Be warned—its popularity means a wait is likely, so take advantage of the Yelp waitlist feature to save time. The venue is spacious, perfect for group outings, and the consistently good food keeps me coming back.

Amazingly good izakayaThe standouts:Meatballs: 5 stars, super tender and juicyDaikon, carrot, burdock root, and sesame oil: 5 stars, I ordered a 2nd one it was so goodFluke with daikon and ponzu: 5 stars, super fresh and great combo of flavorsAlso got the shishito peppers, and sashimi of tuna, amberjack, and abura tuna. All were super fresh and beautifully prepared.Also loved the squid and beef. Would get the beef again for sure.I would pass on the chicken karage. Not my favWould definitely come back!!

My recent visit to China Blue was an experience I had been eagerly anticipating due to the buzz it’s been generating. The restaurant's decor is a delightful nod to old Shanghai, with an oriental charm that is both quaint and captivating. The menu presented an extensive selection of delectable dishes, and deciding what to order was quite the pleasant predicament.

We opted to indulge in a variety of appetizers, each of which proved to be a testament to authentic Shanghainese flavors. The soup buns, in particular, stood out with their succulence and were a crowd-pleaser. Additionally, the soup we ordered was a heartwarming delight; advertised to serve two, its generous portion could easily satisfy four people.

Moving on to the entrees, each dish was a continuation of the culinary excellence we’d come to expect. It's clear that China Blue isn't just riding on ambient charm—it's cementing its reputation with high-quality, authentic cuisine. For anyone with an appreciation for Shanghainese food, this restaurant is a must-visit destination in the city.

Title: A Taste of Argentina That Delivers

If you find yourself at this gem of a culinary escape, do yourself a favor and indulge in the Argentine Feast. The evening's highlight was undoubtedly the Tabla de Carnes – a meat lover's dream featuring a variety of steaks that were seasoned and cooked to perfection, presented with an artful flair that matched their delectable taste. The grilled tangy peppers served as an ideal complement to the rich flavors of the meat.

Accompanying the feast, the provoleta was a revelation of gooey, melted cheese, boasting a delightful crust where it kissed the pan, while the tomatoes provided a refreshing tangy balance. In addition, the feast included two empanadas, whose thin, crispy crusts encased a savory meat filling – though a baked option would have been preferred over fried.

The feast was further enhanced by a fruity sangria, which acted as the perfect palate cleanser, cutting through the richness of the meal with its refreshing notes. Ending on a sweet note, the flan was exceptional, easily making its way into my personal list of top flan experiences.

The service and ambiance didn't miss a beat, echoing the premium quality of the meal. A visit here is one for the senses and a celebration of Argentine cuisine done right.

Eleven B is a medium-sized Italian eatery, locate d on the corner of Avenue B and 11th Street. Eleven B is a casual Italian-American eatery that serves up comfort eats. cozy dining room. there's an express/takeout entrance next door if you're looking to grab n go. the restaurant gets daily busy on the weekends in the evenings. recently i got dinner via delivery. ordered the meatball parmigiana hero which comes with fries $9. the meatball parm sando is a good-size and shareable between two people. bread was toasted and soaked up the sauce melted mozzarella topping the meatball. the sandwich is filling. the sauce & cheese make up most of the flavor. meatballs could stand to be seasoned more imo, but the sandwich is a solidly good. the fries are not super crispy but are thin cut.the sandwiches at 11B are your best bet. drops mic cuz carbzzz make you sleepyi outzzz

Tucked away in the bustling streets stands a gem of authenticity, an old-style Hong Kong cafe that instantly charms with its simplicity. The extensive menu here is a delight, offering a plethora of choices at surprisingly affordable prices. The breakfast B combo—a hearty assembly of an egg sandwich, a choice between tea or coffee, and a comforting bowl of macaroni soup with spam—is a steal and pays homage to the classic Hong Kong breakfast fare. Not stopping at just the combo, I ventured to sample their congee and noodle dish, both of which upheld the tasty promise.

With its mere 3-4 tables, the cafe exudes a cozy vibe that invites sharing space and stories, as I did with a friendly granny. It's a local haunt where aunties and uncles gather for a morning ritual of good food and relaxation.

The value for money and the quality of the meals here are unmatched. This little cafe has won me over, and I’m already planning my next visit to indulge in another menu offering. For those seeking a traditional taste of Hong Kong without breaking the bank, this is the place to go.

This is more of a 3.5 location to me. A friend chose this place for his birthday, called, and was told that he had a reservation for 12. We get there half an hour early, and we figured we should check in - only to be told they don't take phone reservations. Which is fine - but someone on the staff obviously didn't get that memo. At that point, they told us we would have to wait an hour, so we ambled over to Nitecap for a drink to wait. Luckily, in less than an hour, they managed to squeeze some tables together for us. I'm a fan of strong seasoning, but this is HEAVY. It's delicious, but it's no joke - hydrate well and make sure you get that bomb coconut rice. Our server was an absolute doll and ended up comping quite a few dishes for us, but didn't even say anything - just took them off the receipt!We ordered everything on the menu except the peanuts - everything. next time I'd skip: chicharronwould order with a large group: thai mushroom, octopus paksiw, pork belly adobo, pad cheong see ewcan not resist: corn somtom, coconut rice, sizzling sisig, crispy pataOverall, despite some hiccups, I would definitely come back, but for a select few favorites.

Title: Disappointing Dining Experience at Terminal C

My recent dining experience at Terminal C was regrettable, a reminder of the importance of checking reviews. In the absence of decent cheap, fast options during our layover, we decided to take a chance on a conveniently located spot.

Ordering was modernized through a tablet system, but the wait time for my to-go order was unexpectedly long. Priced at $13, I opted for a meatball sandwich with a side salad. Unfortunately, the meatballs lacked flavor, had an unappealing mushiness, and overall, the sandwich failed to impress, making me yearn for the reliability of a Subway or McDonald's.

The saving grace, albeit minor, was the inclusion of vegetables with a decent balsamic vinaigrette. While I considered revisiting Artichoke for pizza, the pre-made slices on display appeared stale.

My family's collective orders from various establishments within Terminal C echoed my sentiments: the food was merely passable. It’s the sort of place that you'd only resort to out of necessity, not desire.

I had an excellent dining experience at this restaurant with a 5:30 reservation and was seated right away. The Ropa Vieja I ordered was a hit—flavorful with generous portions and just the right amount of seasoning. The service truly stood out; our waiter was attentive, friendly, and ensured our meals arrived promptly. I regret not getting his name to give him the kudos he deserves. This spot has become my go-to for a pre-theater meal, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Visited with three friends and tried a bunch of dishes. Fried artichokes to start were great but not my favorite. We also had a trio of veggies - vegetable tart, roasted seasonal mushrooms, peas & prosciutto - and the mushrooms were amazing. Chicken pepperoni parmigiana was awesome, I liked it more than the one at Quality Italian. Ravioli pesto was the best thing we ate. 101 layer lasagna, Summer spaghetti and Little gem Caesar were all excellent. As for desserts, the Limoncello tart was my fave, though the cannoli was great, too. Service was a bit slow but overall I had a great experience. 4.5 stars.

Every time I dine at El Vez it always a great experience. This place is always busy but are very attentive to their guests. This was my second time there with a friend and had a pleasant server. We ordered small mains and shared so we can leave room for dessert. It was amazing ! We ordered 2 flavors of ice cream and flan! I must say I really enjoyed the flan and would totally recommend it. In the summer I've sat outside too and it's such a great view of the freedom tower.

My poor mother ordered a BBQ Chicken Panini at Cafe 71 and my goodness it smelt just so off. I don't know what the smell was but it was probably because those sandwiches are sitting out all day. It honestly smelled gross and when she bit into it she couldn't even swallow it. I tried to say something but the staff didn't seem to understand me so we just chalked it up to a loss and left ASAP.My Falafel Pita was messy but pretty good though. I think my recommendation would be to stay away from meat products here and just play it safe. All the veggie options looked fresh for the most part. I think the staff is friendly? They did a lot of smiling and nodding but weren't too good at answering questions. So we just kind of smiled and nodded too and then backed away slowly.

As soon as you step into the restaurant, the wood burning oven takes center stage, promising a culinary treat. Kick off your meal with the eggplant Parmesan, a delectable beginning that sets the tone for what's to come. Delve into the pasta selection; each dish is more enticing than the last. And if luck has the tomahawk ribeye on the menu during your visit, take the plunge—it's an indulgence not to be missed!

Great price, delicious, and great service. I paid for the unlimited hot pot, which meant that we were able to put as many meats, vegetables, and noodles into our pot. You can get up to three liquid bases. We chose only two and got the spicy base and the kimchi one. Apparently we are WEAK AF, so the kimchi base was still too spicy for us. We couldn't manage to eat it and actually enjoy it because it was way too difficult. Thankfully they were kind enough to transfer our food into a pot with the original base instead!!Definitely want to come back and try the unlimited bbq. Initially we were considering doing the unlimited hot pot and unlimited bbq, but I'm glad we didn't because it would have been way too much food and too tedious to focus on cooking multiple things at once.

Neighborhood joint serving ramen and sushi. The food is fine, no complaints, it's just very expensive. Mostly likely because I come here during the evening everything is full price. The interior is nice and cozy, and it's right by the corner so you definitely feel the nightlife around. Scanning the menu and specials on the board I feel like the sushi here is way overpriced for your run of the mill sushi joint. The ramen is pretty standard and I just would like a little more oomph to it. Given the competition in this neighborhood for ramen, let alone the block Shokudo is on (right by sake bar hagi 46) I would most likely pass.

Finally got here on a Friday night.  There was a line  but it moved quickly & you can enjoy the celebrity pics while you wait.  I ordered some slices of the Spicy Pepperoni to go.  A Pepperoni lover's dream come true!  The Sicilian crust/SoHo Square was perfect with an abundant amount of Pepperoni & and it seems they always have fresh slices of the Spicy Pepperoni.Saw Customers walking and eating (guess they couldn't wait to get home-that good!) as well right outside the restaurant.  Part of the charm.  Now On my list of must stops when visiting!

I recently dined at a local restaurant that seems popular, although I'm left scratching my head as to why. The food was unremarkable, especially the soba noodles which I found basic and under-topped, particularly given the high dinner prices. While the curry broth was tasty, it didn't compensate for the long wait, the oppressively stuffy and hot interior, or the overall sense that I was paying too much for mediocre fare. In all likelihood, I won't be returning.

This place was right down the street from our hotel.  I was excited when I saw it on the map and couldn't wait to try it.  I was not disappointed.  Went here with my son and girlfriend.  It was pretty busy for 7:30 on a Wednesday night.  We ordered the Uber pretzel for an appetizer.  It was big, and flaky.  I would have liked cheese with it, but the two mustards were not bad.  My son ordered the kasespatzle (which is Mac n cheeseish with bacon and kielbasa).  I dad taxed it, and it was good.  He ate it all!  My girlfriend and I split the Pork Schnitzel with a side of German potato salad and fries.  I would suggest getting one of the schnitzels with gravy instead of plain.  Seems a little dry without it.  Do not get me wrong, we are it all.  Even had the Black Forest cake for dessert.  They were nice enough to split one piece in 3 for us.  It was a good dessert

**Review of The Ramen Roost**

Venturing into The Ramen Roost, I was greeted by their signature dish: a chicken-based ramen that stands out in a sea of pork and beef broths. The bowl arrived brimming with generous chunks of tender chicken - they're certainly not stingy here. The broth itself was a delightful surprise, distinguishable by its creamy, velvety texture that's a delicious departure from the norm. For those seeking a novel twist on classic ramen, this place is a winner. I came in curious and left a convert – this chicken ramen is not just different, it's delightful!

Years ago I spent a lot of nights in Curry row. A young guy could find a tasty Indian dinner and wash it down with mango lassi for a very reasonable price. On 6th street there used to be a great number of Indian restaurants but times clearly have changed.After realizing that all of my usual pots on 6th st have been long closed I came across this spectacle of lights called Panna II. The man at the door assured me that I would have a seat for my party in two minutes, more like 20. Once inside we were sat at a tiny table in the corner across from a group of 20somethings celebrating a birthday. The vibe of this place is fun and loud but the service is incredibly slow. It took 15 minutes just to get a glass of water. Even longer for the waiter to take our order. We ordered lamb curry, chicken tandoori, house biryani,  and naan. Mango lassi to wash it all down of course. The delivery was snail packed and to be honest the food was either terrible or just ok. The chicken tandoori was probably the worst I have ever tasted. The chicken was dry, flavorless, and tough. The house biryani was dry and the meat and seafood were extremely overcooked. The lamb curry had some taste and the lamb was tender but I've had much better. The naan was a joke, more like a warmed up pitas you get at Sam's club.The mango lassi was absolutely delicious and I ordered a few since they came in such small glasses. All in all this is a nice place to get a photo and I would highly suggest eating elsewhere. There are much better options for your palate and the money.

So my New York food adventure continues with lunch at Los Tacos No. 1 at Chelsea market. I decided to roam around Chelsea market and whoever had the longest line I would stand in it. Well lo and behold, I ended up at this taco joint. Maybe I was trying to let my breakfast noddles at Xi'an digest or taking in the amazing atmosphere of the Chelsea market. The line moves pretty quickly and I ended up ordering a carne asada taco. The taco was full of flavor, perfectly cooked steak seasoned to perfection. The tortilla was oh em gee!!!! I got all the toppings minus the onions. The food was delicious, the staff is very sweet and helps you figure out how to order and where to pick up your tacos. Definitely returning to try everythinggggg!!!

During a brief family visit to New York, we couldn't miss out on the iconic thin-crust pizza. Joe's Pizza, conveniently located on our route to Times Square, caught our eye with its daunting yet fast-moving queue. This bustling spot offered a selection of delectably affordable slices ranging from $3-5. Our choices – classic cheese, hearty pepperoni, and a savory white pizza – all hit the mark with their perfect crust, flavorful toppings, and overall deliciousness. Joe's Pizza delivered great value and a memorable dining experience, ensuring our return on the next NYC trip.

During a holiday homecoming, I seized the opportunity to whisk my friends off to Manhattan's culinary treasures, with Korean BBQ topping the list. Our feet led us to the well-regarded Jongro, and it lived up to its reputation. While the menu could have benefited from clearer outlines for newcomers, the selection we made hardly detracted from the overall delight.

Each dish, accompanied by a variety of small plates, was a tantalizing journey through taste. The service? Impeccable and brimming with cheerful attentiveness. Timing is crucial; our earlier dinner at 5 PM meant we skirted around the looming lines that quickly form.

Jongro's unique placement on the second floor adds a dash of Manhattan's quirky charm – be it elevator or stairs, consider it part of the adventure. And in this case, the adventure leads to a feast well worth the ascent. A culinary gem not to be missed!

Title: Cozy Ambiance, Mixed Experiences at Lovely Day

Located in the charming Nolita neighborhood, Lovely Day presents itself as a modest Thai eatery, nestled comfortably as a second choice after the highly sought-after Uncle Boon's. The restaurant's interior exudes a quaint nostalgia with its red vinyl booths, retro wallpaper, and tight seating arrangement reminiscent of a Midwestern basement – though a bit cramped, causing occasional discomfort.

Diners will find a broad menu that unexpectedly includes Western staples such as burgers alongside traditional Thai dishes and daily specials, with ample vegetarian options to choose from. Price points adhere to local norms, making Lovely Day an accessible stop for those in the area.

My experience with the green coconut curry tofu was underwhelming, as the tofu's texture detracted from the overall flavor experience. However, generous portions somewhat balanced the scales. In contrast, the pork belly noodles received a favorable nod from my dining companion. Wine aficionados take note: selections are on the cheaper side but may not impress.

The staff is endearing and diligent, although the seemingly undersized kitchen can lead to longer waits for food during peak hours. Lovely Day is a viable option for those in Nolita, particularly appealing for a low-key night rather than a bustling Friday evening.
Just ordered food from here. And it was awesome I missed it so much. Smith burger and dinner for two. It was easy to get and very orderly. I def recommend ordering out from here you'll enjoy it.

First time trying the place. I went with a friend. She got her food first. I waited, waited, realize people after me got their food.  I realize 20 min is actually long. I asked someone to check. They forgot my food. She goes back to kitchen to look for it. Comes back ask what I ordered.I assume they are making my food. She comes back fairly quick and apologizes for the long wait. I got to eat my food, it's cold!!  They didn't make the food, they must have found my order sitting in the kitchen that they never brought out. So it was cold.Sorry but that's bad service. If you mess up, Don't give cold food. You make fresh food and give hot food. Bad service.

Came here for restaurant week and I'm quite impressed with the quality of the food and service! Ordered the tartare duo even though it was not part of the restaurant week menu (just because we heard it was good), it was flavorful and unique, but can't say I was blown away. I did love their USDA Prime Junior New York Sirloin steak - got it in medium rare and it was perfect! Lobster Bisque - very good flavor and texture, but not much lobster in sight :DOverall not a bad meal for the restaurant week price! Would definitely recomment

This place looked somewhat promising for my pho craving. I ordered the chicken pho. It arrived fast, and in a bowl that took up about a quarter of the table. The chicken was tasty, although I can't speak to how authentic it was. Overall the pho was decent, but considering how expensive it was ($13 without considering tips) I might try a cheaper place before coming back.

Title: A Surprisingly Delightful Discovery

Walking into what I initially thought was a burger joint, I found myself pleasantly surprised by the vegetarian haven that greeted me. The exterior, adorned with classic fast-food imagery such as hamburgers, fries, and ice cream, was somewhat misleading. However, the bright and immaculate interior with its appealing menu quickly caught my attention.

Among the unique offerings was the Carrot Dog - an intriguing vegetarian twist on a classic that piqued my curiosity. Although I identify as a meat lover, the menu's variety and the lure of healthier options were enticing, with items like cold-pressed juices and vegan cupcakes accompanying traditional fare, including beer.

Ordering is streamlined, done via a convenient kiosk that buzzes when your meal is ready - a perfect blend of efficiency for both dine-in and take-out patrons.

While I didn't sample the food on this visit, the Carrot Dog has secured a spot on my 'must-try' list for next time. This spot may just be the place that bridges the gap between hearty comfort and wholesome plant-based dining.

During my recent visit to the local eatery, I opted for the "West Village" sandwich which featured a delightful combination of falafel and baba ganoush, reasonably priced around $6.50 after tax. This vegetarian option offered great value and flavor, contrasting with the meat sandwiches that, albeit generously portioned and meaty, edge towards $9-10 with tax.

I found that the vegetarian choices are not only lighter on the wallet but also satisfying. However, the West Village sandwich was a tad over-dressed with Tahini sauce, slightly overpowering the other fresh ingredients. A word of advice to fellow diners: take a glance at the right wall upon entering. There lies a treasure trove of "signature sandwiches" that could easily be overlooked if you only consult the main menu at the front. A small oversight that could mean missing out on some of the restaurant's best offerings.

Tucked away in the bustling streets of Washington Heights, I stumbled upon a charming hole-in-the-wall Chinese eatery whilst staying at a nearby Air BNB. The decision to give it a try proved to be a delightful one. Opting for their pork lo mein lunch special, I was treated to an exquisite dish that far exceeded expectations. Such an unassuming spot, yet the flavors were bold and memorable. I left with a contented palate and a certainty that I would return to savor their fare again. Highly recommended for a no-frills dining experience with genuinely good food.

Title: An Elevated Dining Experience at RH Rooftop Restaurant

My recent visit to the RH Rooftop Restaurant transcended the usual dining experience with its unique combination of elegance and warmth. The lavish furnishings that graced the venue set the stage for what was to be an exceptional evening.

Michael, the host, was the epitome of customer service excellence. Despite the initial crowd, he managed to secure a reservation for my family, displaying a level of attentiveness that was both rare and commendable.

The ambiance transformed as the night unfolded, with the dark sky serving as a backdrop to the radiant chandeliers. It was a setting that promised a memorable meal, and the food did not disappoint. The 16 oz Charred Rib-Eye was a standout, complemented perfectly by sides of smooth Olive Oil Purée and fresh Broccolini.

However, the RH Burger stole the show. Its quality and flavor propelled it to the ranks of the best burgers I've ever savored. It's not just a meal; it's an indulgence.

Overall, the RH Rooftop Restaurant delivered an unparalleled blend of food, service, and atmosphere. It is certainly a gem I intend to revisit.

This place is so fun to hang out on a cool, Autumn evening after work!The design is very open and airy, with an expansive outdoor patio area and elevated narrow deck that flows effortlessly into the bar ( kudos to the architect!), definitely inviting!I attended for a company event and the management and wait staff were impeccable! Extremely accommodating, attentive, patient and friendly is how I'd describe this great team. The drink menu is AMAZING! I highly recommend the Blood Orange Martini, I found  practically myself two-handing these they were THAT good! The passed hors d'oeuvres were absolutely deeeelish!! Rosemary fries, cheeseburger sliders with really delicious meat, chicken skewers that tasted organic and fried cucumber ball with fresh tzatziki sauce all received rave reviews from our group. I can't wait to come back here! The energy was inviting, lively, and just right for any occasion.

The rating is based on the fact that it is a Taiwanese American restaurant, and therefore, I didn't knock out one more star for not being super authentic.  The flavoring reminded me a lot of Win Son in Brooklyn, where both places take a new spin on household snacks and dishes that all Taiwanese grow up knowing and loving.Dinner dishes that we would recommend are 1) Sausage party and 2) Crispy silken tofu as starters. Skip the oyster omelette, it was drenched in so much sauce that we can barely taste the omelette itself.For entrees, the two of us shared the Water spinach and shrimp paste and Hsinchu Mifen. Both reminded us of home!If you are in a mood for beer, try the mango flavored Taiwan beer. Brunch menu looks interesting, will return for that!

Title: A Quick Bite with Familiar Flavors at Bao by Kaya

Tucked away in the bustling Urbanspace, Bao by Kaya offers a casual spot for a quick and satisfying meal. The bubble tea is decent, not the most authentic but a reliable choice, especially the tea-based options. The service is friendly, and despite a small line, the staff works swiftly to keep things moving.

The seating arrangement spans across the main floor and upstairs, with convenient restroom access downstairs. As for the offerings, Bao by Kaya has a modest selection of gua baos, sides, and beverages. The Apple Sidra here brings back childhood memories and stands out as a uniquely favored soda choice.

I tried the Peking Duck Bao and the Pork Belly Bao; the meat was succulent and perfectly braised. However, the buns didn't quite hit the mark - lacking the firmness and slightly chewy texture of authentic Taiwanese gua baos, they were too soft and became soggy, falling apart quickly. The popcorn chicken, while tasty, did not possess the expected juicy and aromatic qualities of its Taiwanese counterpart.

In summary, Bao by Kaya delivers on flavor but might fall short for purists seeking an authentic experience. It's not a destination I'd go out of my way for, but it's a decent option for a quick, convenient meal if you're in the area.

We went for dinner at this place before all the restaurants shut down. We were greeted as soon as we walked in, and as it was still an early evening on Monday, not yet busy in the inside.  We decided some cocktails after we heard they infuse their own flavor to syrup and alcohol, and that their cocktails are all made from scratch! We had Lavender Mill, and A Pear to Remember. They were both really tasty! They really know how to make creative, strong, and delicious cocktails!We ordered some appetizers: Fried Pickles, Roasted Whole Sardines, and Chicken Pot Pie. They all great, but I was most excited about Roasted Whole Sardines. It looked wonderful, and it tasted as good as it looked! Sardines were so tender and juicy, falls off the bones! Delicious! Pickles were really nice too, and the Pot Pie was packed with flavor, one awesome pot pie! For main, we had Manchego & Prosciutto Burger, and Fennel Seed Crusted Tuna Steak.  The burger bigger than I expected, and it was soooo good! It was like a symphony of all the ingredients, producing a melody of balanced, sophisticated, and totally satisfying flavor. Tuna Steak was HUGE! It looked like a giant piece of thick-cut steak! The bed of eggplants and other ingredients were super tasty, they certainly did not take side stage! All the ingredients were very fresh, filling and satisfying. We also ordered Herb Gruyere Biscuits + Honey Butter, since I was curious about their biscuit. It was warm, soft, heavy, and came with amazing aroma! It was sooo wonderfully buttery, dense yet light and airy.  I LOVED it! Needless to say, we had a great dinner here. All the staffs here were friendly, polite, and courteous. They took a really nice care of us. We enjoyed every bite of every item we had!

Title: Hidden Gem within Jung Lee Furniture - Zoku Sushi's Icelandic Char Bowl

I recently ventured into Zoku Sushi for lunch via Mealpal. Nestled inside the Jung Lee Furniture Store, it’s a hidden sushi spot with a minimalist vibe. No extensive menu or lavish decor here, just a simple setup for pick-up orders, with a few mysterious containers chilling in the fridge.

The star of the show was the Icelandic Char Bowl - a Mealpal option that did not disappoint. The char was remarkably fresh, reminiscent of the pristine waters of its origin. Paired with potent seaweeds, crisp cucumbers, and exquisitely seasoned Japanese rice, the bowl was a harmonious blend of textures and flavors.

While I can't comment on the regular pricing or variety (as there was no visible menu), I can confidently say the Icelandic Char is worth stopping by for. Zoku Sushi may just surprise you with its unassuming presence and delightful offerings.

I'm a huge fan of Philippe chow but this past Saturday when I went I was a bit disappointed. I felt like since we had reservations at 10:30 and my friend was running late they rushed our entire dinner. The place was packed and when we finally sat down we were told we need to order right away without even getting a second to glance at the menu. The waiter only asked my friend if she wanted a drink and when I looked up to tell him my order he was running away already. I felt a bit ignored especially since the place isn't cheap and I was the one bragging to my friend about how good it was. The only reason I gave it 3 stars is because I love the sweet and sour chicken and the crispy beef. I also liked the salt and pepper eggplant. In my opinion , the downtown location is way better. The chicken satay was really good though. I just felt like I've been here before and I loved it, I didn't feel rushed at all but this time I felt like they were pushing us out the door.
