I was told the kitchen closes at 11 pm by the staff in the front and the waiter as soon as we sat down. Sometimes trains get stuck and there's nothing we can do about it. However, next time I would appreciate not feeling so rushed. I don't think I'll ever go back to this location. I'll go to the one downtown. Still has good food though !

Title: Quirky Spot with Tasty Eats

My recent visit to this local eatery was a culinary success in terms of what landed on my plate, though the overall experience was a mixed bag. The restaurant's atmosphere was boisterous to a fault, with staff conversations often overpowering the sporadically fluctuating music volume, creating a somewhat chaotic dining environment.

The service, while efficient in delivering our food, was not without its quirks. Notably, the cashier's stoic demeanor came off as unwelcoming, and a humorous if slightly disconcerting mix-up involved a dish being served to us in error before being whisked away with a casual "my bad."

For first-timers, the "sit and order yourself" setup can be disorienting, resembling a traditional restaurant but lacking clear guidance. This could be improved with more explicit instructions for guests upon entry.

On a brighter note, the food shined. Our selection included chicken, lamb kebab, ratatouille, and lavan—all of which were exceptional. Each dish was fresh, juicy in the best sense, and brimming with flavor. The lamb kebab was notably succulent and well-seasoned. Portion sizes are modest, but the quality justifies the price point. The pita bread deserves a special shoutout for its softness and freshness, earning a perfect score from me.

In summary, while the ambiance and service at this establishment could use some fine-tuning, the high-quality, delicious dishes are definitely worth the visit.

Last Friday evening, my two friends and I decided to dine at a trendy tapas spot, resulting in a one-hour wait for a table at 6:15 pm. To pass the time, we headed to their "Outpost" café around the block, an innovative solution for waiting guests to enjoy a drink. We indulged in their signature light-up "Capri-sun" drinks – the mango/lychee was sweet and delicious, blue lemonade struck a nice balance between sweet and tart, and the cucumber was light and refreshing.

Upon being seated, our waiter advised us to go for two tapas each. We dived into their "Not so Plain-tain" - a stunning dish that earned a perfect score for its brûléed plantains atop a scrumptious mix of cheese and sauces, garnished with nuts. The edamame dumplings were another hit, offering a delightful cheesy, edamame blend. The "Sweet Angry Fries" were spicy and satisfying, although the fries themselves were just fine. The gnocchi held its own with a good spice level, but a point to note, it's not vegetarian as it uses meat broth.

Overall, two tapas per person seemed to be a satisfying quantity. While the food was superb, it could become quite pricey. Vegetarian and vegan options are available, although they lack the heartiness of the meat-containing dishes. It would be a welcome improvement if hearty vegetarian dishes like mac and cheese or kimchi paella could be offered without meat. Nevertheless, it was a great dining experience with an array of flavors and textures to relish.

After hearing so many good things about this bustling Indian quick service spot, I can affirm it lives up to its reputation. It's a godsend in NYC for those craving authentic Indian fare without the wait. I indulged in a meal featuring brown rice, hearty chana masala, succulent saag chicken, and a fresh salad - a generous portion that could easily stretch into another meal. The flavors were spot-on, truly capturing the essence of Indian cuisine. While the chicken dosa is a must-try, take my advice and devour it immediately to relish its crispness; it loses its charm if left to turn into a soggy shadow of itself. And don't even get me started on their samosas – pure delight! For anyone in need of a quick Indian food fix, this is your place.

Stopped in here for an early dinner around 5:30 and there were already people eating. We were seated promptly but as soon as we were seated, more people started showing up. Let me preface it by saying the place is TINY..the size of a shoebox. It's super cozy and you will be very close to other patrons but they make it work. The bread with sun dried tomato and olive oil spread was nice. Sardines Fennel and Orange Salad Very refreshing and tasty! The sardines were warm and plump. Paired with fennel and orange, it was the perfect thing to have prior to carbing up!Our pastas came in the form of a pan. I actually appreciate this concept. Smart thinking from the resto. Less cleaning. More efficient. For the customer it's a nice chance from the boring plate.  All the pastas were cooked as they should be -perfectly AL DENTE. Squid Ink Tagliolini Very saucy and packed with flavor. I am not a big carb person but it needs to be carb worthy and this was definitely carb worthy! Only downside is you might wall away with black teeth from the squid ink. But it's not something a glass of pinot or water can't fix! Wild Boar Ragu Tartufo TagliatelleYou can't go wrong with Truffle herb butter and wild Boar Ragu. The texture was just right and tasty. We thought we would have some left over to bring home but it was inhaled! Staff was super friendly and accommodating. Very Italian. Would def come back again!

My boyfriend and I came here to celebrate our anniversary. We decided on the Signature Tasting Menu which is $235/person. My personal favorites were Foie Gras Mandoo, Tuna Kimbap, Galbi, and Baby Banana. Octopus was my least favorite--I feel like they could've done something to enhance the taste. It was also difficult to cut. Jungsik could've made our anniversary more memorable with personalized dessert/candle; hence 4 stars instead of 5. I did let them know so like any other "high-end" restaurant, I expected something personalized but we were quite disappointed at that aspect.

Again, this is the first place we came to for dinner after arriving to NYC. It has become a tradition, and the only one I like coming to. Friendly greeting, "sit anywhere you like, and I'll follow."Maclain: How you guys doing?  You've been here before, right?  I think I remember seeing you.Me: Well, we come here every time we visit.  We're from California, and the last time was three years ago.Maclain: Well, I guess I didn't see you before!Same great friendly service!  Ordered a great bottle of Sangiovese, and the crab balls and buffallo balls to start.  Both soooooo good!  We also came back for their pesto!  It is so delicious!  Ended the meal with an ooey gooey ice cream sandwich between chocolate chip and snickerdoodle cookies.  They even split it for us.Thanks again!  Might see you guys one more time before we leave!

The TAK Room is Chef Thomas Keller's newest restaurant located inside the new Hudson Yards shopping complex. The restaurant offers a great view of The Vessel and the surrounding skyscrapers. At first we were worried that it might be one of those restaurants that have a nice view, but mediocre food and service because the service was not the best, but once we got our foods Chef Keller did not disappoint. I ordered the chicken pot pie and it was by far the most beautifully presented chicken pot pie I've ever had. It was also the most delicious and was creamy yet not too heavy. The dish looked small and elegant, but it was actually pretty filling and was the perfect fancy comfort food that one could have on a cold winter afternoon. I'm not sure if they'll have the chicken pot pie on their menu once it gets warmer, but this dish alone made me want to go back and try their other items on the menu.

Title: Quick Bites with a Twist at the Dual-Line Diner

Upon entering this intriguing eatery, one immediately notices the dual-line setup: one for crafting sandwiches and another dedicated to assembling lunch bowls. This innovative approach hints at efficiency – likely, the bowl line zips along quicker than its counterpart.

Opting for a seat to enjoy my midday repast, I chose the Cuban sandwich. While the overall flavors hit the mark and the bread was crisply pressed, the pork's dryness slightly marred the experience. Nonetheless, the fresh-looking ingredients of the lunch bowls caught my eye, promising a future visit to explore that option.

For those seeking a swift yet satisfying lunch, this spot is a gem, offering a unique take on fast-casual dining. Next time, the enticing lunch bowl awaits!

Set in the heart of NYC, this restaurant boasts an ambiance that caters perfectly to the hustle and bustle of the quick lunch crowd. The authenticity of the cuisine is commendable, though the main dishes fall short of being truly extraordinary. However, the pastries emerge as the establishment's crowning jewel, rivaling those found in the city's Greek enclaves. Patrons seeking a swift Hellenic experience will find satisfaction here. But be warned: despite the allure of the pastries, the overall experience may not justify the prices, with the entrees leaning toward the overpriced and underwhelming.

First time having Georgian food and I did not know what to expect. I came with a party of 9, and got seated in the back. There is also a cute enclosed makeshift garden in the back, perfect for date night. We started out with a bottle of red Georgian wine, which tasted light and refreshing! We decided to order a bunch of appetizers and entrees and share family style in order to have more variety. Some of the food we ordered - chicken, lamb chops, salmon, charcuterie board Georgian style, garlic chicken, beef and pork dumplings, cheesy bread, and cheese boat! All of the dishes were good, and my favorite has got to be the salmon and cheesy-bread! After that, we topped it off with a delectable Georgian dessert - called the ideali cake. Service was attentive and all the dishes came out one right after another. If you're looking to try something new, give this spot a try!

Please do yourself a huge favor and come grab a sandwich here before it's too late as the pop up store leaves mid-July! Apparently, this sandwich shop is super popular in Florence, Italy and I'm not surprised why! I went around 1pm on a Tuesday and there was already a line outside, but in comparison to other reviewers, 30-45 min wait today sounds like nothing compared to the 1-2 hr wait on the weekends. As you're waiting to order your sandwich, they give you free samples of the bread and meat!! The friendliness of the staff was definitely a huge plus! Apparently, the actual owner flew from Italy to help prepare all the sandwiches! I got La Summer, which was so perfect. The combination of the meat, mozzarella cheese with the tomatoes and the hint of basil was to die for!! I would definitely come back to try the other options before this pop up leaves!!!

Title: Solid Lunch Spot with Room for Improvement

My strategic arrival at the opening time for lunch at this well-hyped eatery, helmed by an Iron Chef, paid off with a quieter dining experience before the rush. Opting for the lunch special, I settled into the anticipation set by glowing reviews. The curry rice and tonkotsu ramen were on the docket for the day.

Regrettably, my high hopes weren't fully realized. The curry rice was competent, yet unremarkable—a dish that would blend into the backdrop of any Japanese dining establishment, with a lean portion of meat. The tonkotsu ramen's flavor profile was pleasing, but it didn't elevate the dish beyond the ordinary, a sentiment compounded by its tepid temperature upon arrival.

Granting the restaurant a solid 4 stars, it falls squarely in the middle of my ramen rankings—an aficionado who's sampled bowls from the U.S. to Japan. While good, a meal here wasn't the culinary revelation I'd anticipated.

Title: Kazu Nori - A Hand Roll Haven

I finally understand the hype about Kazu Nori's hand rolls. At $24 for five made-to-order rolls, including tip, it's an absolute bargain. The unique order-before-seated system is efficient, turning tables quickly — a touch of genius.

Even being tenth in line was no issue; my partner and I were seated within 40 minutes. Immediately upon sitting, our preselected hand rolls were rolled out one by one — talk about fresh! The hand roll set hit the spot perfectly, leaving me satisfyingly full.

Including a refreshing green tea, the total came to just $29. Kazu Nori offers an authentic, speedy, and delightful dining experience without breaking the bank. They've certainly nailed it!

Title: A Snack Lover's Dream at this Japanese Gem

If you're a fan of Japanese snack food, this spot is unmissable. The prices won't break the bank, and the staff exudes friendliness. My crew and I dove into their loaded jagabees and were blown away by the upscale twist on a Frito Pie – think rich, crispy potatoes, brimming with meat, Thai chilis, and scallions. The texture and flavor marriage is an absolute win; you can't skip this.

Sandwich-wise, the pork katsu sando and egg sando are simply sublime. Both were promptly demolished, speaking volumes to their deliciousness. The eatery boasts a cool, hip vibe and there's a fun little surprise game at checkout – I won't spill the beans, but don't forget to inquire!

We left with full bellies and eager plans to return for another round of those irresistible sandos. Highly recommend!

My friends from the west coast was raving about Ichiran and we had added it to our must visit collection. We came into the city to see the tree with our baby and had no intention of waiting in line to get ramen in a tiny booth. However, we happened to park our car right in front of this place and was about to head home when we noticed that there was barely a wait. We did go at an odd in between time around 4:30-5pm and waited about 10 minutes? The staff noticed that we had a baby and suggested we wait inside which was very thoughtful. I expected for my husband and myself to get a booth and each of us take turns holding the baby as we inhaled some ramen in speedy time and head out. We were pleasantly surprised that they even set up a booth for the baby with his own high chair even though we weren't ordering any food for him. This made our experience soooo much better as we were able to totally enjoy our ramen. We got all the recommended options as well as the sides, white rice, and vinegar condiment. The vinegar I added at the end to cut the fat of the broth and mix in the rice which was soooooo good! I liked how the soft boil egg came on the side instead on in the broth and you get a whole one instead of just a half. One thing I did note was the regular ramen already includes the Chashu so if you get the recommended side,  you get extra meat. The service was superb and everyone was SOOO nice, even the gentlman at the cashier. They also have instant ramen you can purchase to eat at home but it's a bit pricy. I think it was $30 for a three pack. Can't wait to visit again!

During my recent visit to Ichiran, I was treated to one of the most delightful bowls of ramen in recent memory. Tailored for solo diners, the unique cubicle seating ensures a comfortable dining experience for those flying solo, but it may not be the best for larger groups. Despite this, our party of six managed to enjoy our meals in a linear arrangement.

I took a dive into the recommended set, which was bursting with tasty add-ons. The warmth of the broth and the excellence of the perfectly cooked noodles truly stood out, achieving a harmonious balance in each spoonful. A cherry on top was the promotional free serving of extra noodles our group received.

While the price tag of $24 a bowl may raise eyebrows, especially compared to the more wallet-friendly tariffs at Ichiran's Japanese locations, the Time Square positioning somewhat justifies the premium.

In summary, if you're yearning for authentic ramen but can't jet off to Japan, Ichiran in Time Square is certainly worth a stop. However, for the globetrotters eyeing the ultimate Ichiran experience, you might want to hold off until you can savor it in its home country.

I recently dined at a local eatery that seems to have garnered quite a buzz for its social dining style, but I must confess, my experience left me underwhelmed. The concept is engaging – picking various tapas from different booths and then gathering around a table to share with friends. On paper, it's a convivial approach to dining out.

Our table ordered a smattering of items: the Paella Valencia ($16.00), a dozen Churros with a chocolate shot for dipping ($14.00 in total), some fancy Jamon, and a Potato Egg Pancake. Each dish was passable, but the price tags felt hefty for what amounted to decent, albeit forgettable fare. The churros were likely the highlight, but again, nothing that stood out amongst competitors.

In comparison to authentic Spanish restaurants found in the city, this place doesn't quite hit the mark. While it may serve as a fun spot to mingle with friends over shared plates, don't come expecting a culinary revelation. On the whole, if you're seeking notable Spanish cuisine, your taste buds—and wallet—might be better served elsewhere.

Came for a late night dinner, I've always wanted to try this place out, had it bookmarked forever.  The restaurant is beautiful, I came during the week so the restaurant wasn't busy at all, upstairs they offer hibachi but decided to just order small bites so was sat downstairs. I ordered an array of dumplings, fried lobster dumplings, soup dumplings,a baked pork bun, scallion pancakes and an order of Oink Oink fried rice  all were delicious but my god!!that rice won me over it was amazingly flavorful. The restaurant does have a full bar, I ordered the strawberry fields cocktail that I absolutely enjoyed. The staff was pleasant and really attentive, the server made really great recommendations which came in handy because I was really indecisive. when you check in you get these adorable hello kitty custard buns for dessert , they were amazing  I loved them. I Will definitely check out the hibachi next visit.

Cool quick viet food option, but my Joju rice bowl (sausage + caramel pork) with mini spring rolls was just mediocre. The portion of meat was very generous. The sausage was okay, but the caramel pork was way too sweet, over powering the rest of the bowl. Though they do heat up the spring rolls when you order, I wouldn't pay extra for them again. They were dry and lacking flavor. I did like the selection of toppings on my bowl though. The store itself has kiosks where you can order without having to interact with anyone, which I thought was pretty cool. This is definitely a plus at lunch rush. However, unlike other places where you can ask for extras, here you can only ask to NOT have something in the bowl. I'm not sure if this would be the same when ordering in person, but just an FYI.

Title: A Delightful Surprise from Local Italian Spot

I recently gave the Italian delivery from my neighborhood a try and it didn't disappoint, especially considering the affordability. The chicken parm hero, priced at a reasonable $9.50, and garlic bread for just $2.50, came without a delivery charge, promptly served hot. The value for money is exceptional, with servings so generous that my additional order of garlic bread (a substantial loaf and teeming with garlic flavor) turned out to be excessive.

The hero itself, while tasty with its savory sauce and perfectly melted mozzarella, had room for improvement due to the chicken being sliced into strips, resulting in a somewhat drier texture and a challenging eating experience. Nevertheless, it was a minor issue in what was otherwise an enjoyable meal.

Overall, impressive portion sizes, on-point flavors, and incredible convenience make this spot a must-try. Despite the chicken hiccup, I'd recommend it and will certainly be ordering again.

On a random Thursday night my friend and I came across this place that from the outside looking in seemed like an average restaurant. We walked in to a very robust atmosphere and were pleasantly surprised that this was not an average place at all! Greeted and sat quickly we choose to have a seat looking into the kitchen. The staff was friendly and the cooks were entertaining to say the least. My friend and I were inquiring on what certain dishes were called and asked for the most loved items on the menu. We drank and laughed at lot that night and I felt very comfortable at this cozy and kinda crowded place. I'm sure I'll be back for more fun. It's a high energy well priced restaurant with super yummy food. For drinks, appetizers and entree the bill for two was $120. Not bad right?! The general manager made his way over to us for a quick chat. He was super friendly. Thx Billy!

Title: A Night of Creative Flavors and Cozy Ambience

I had an exquisite dining experience at this gem of a spot! The ambience alone is enough to earn five stars - perfect for both a romantic outing or a trendy get-together with friends. Despite the bustle of a crowded Saturday night, service was commendably swift; we were seated at 7pm and had drinks by 7:15.

The menu brims with creativity, making choosing a challenge because everything looks tempting. The split pea guacamole was a delightful surprise, with an unexpectedly refreshing twist. Standout dishes included the grilled maitake mushrooms and the charred octopus – both bursting with flavor and cooked to perfection.

The only misstep in an otherwise flawless meal was the cured salmon with yogurt dill sauce, which was overly salty and left an unpleasant aftertaste. This was a rare letdown that slightly tarnished an otherwise perfect dining experience.

But the meal ended on a high note with the phenomenal tres leches cake – an absolute must-try. Despite the minor hiccup with the salmon, I'm eager to return and explore more of the menu. Four stars for now, but this is a place that has the potential to wow with every visit.

Came here for my cousins birthday brunch of 25+ people. They were super accommodating! The bottomless was great and worth it! They gave us a separate area with doors closed so we were able to have a private party. The food was excellent and unique. Would def go back!

I ordered chicken bun from the app ritual. The app told me the food was ready so I went to their place but the food wasn't ready. Most of the time, the app is accurate. So I had to wait for another 15minutes or so.The food is good but not great. The bun was $7.99 but It is worth trying it thou especially if you have the ritual app: they have $5 off of the first purchase so I paid around $3dollar for my lunch. They really have a lot of meat inside the bun (see the picture)The taste of the bun, however, was plain... but I do want to give them credit for the chicken (very juicy and tender: not dry at all) I don't want which is worse: One: they forgot to put the source in b/c they were in a rush of making since I'm there already or Two: the sauce was added in but it still taste like nothing

My friend and I wanted to try a vegan restaurant and after looking at the decor on yelp we decided to come here for lunch. The menu looked very appetizing as they offer several options. My friend and I didn't know what to order and the waitress was extremely helpful. We went with her recommendations and were not let down. I got the green pea + fava falafel and it was delicious. It comes with a side of pita bread, therefore you have the option of making a sandwich which is nice. Additionally, I tried some of my friend's paprika potato wedges and fell in love that I ordered them to go!We sat at the restaurant for hours talking and not once did we feel rushed. The staff is very friendly and offer amazing service. We will definitely be returning as I'm curious to try smoked tofu!
Delicious curry and good lunch deals. Definitely on a heavier side where everything is fried and the spicy curry is very spicy. Yummyyyyyy placeeeee. Definitely worth becoming a regular here!

I recently visited this local restaurant and decided to try their tofu noodles in broth. The dish offered a pleasant surprise, as the tofu turned out to be tofu puffs with a hint of sweetness, which was unexpected but enjoyable. While the assortment of vegetables in the broth complemented the dish well, I found myself yearning for a more generous portion of greens. The noodles themselves were flavorful and definitely the highlight of the meal. Intrigued by the taste, I'm keen on returning to sample one of their stir-fried noodle dishes next time. Overall, it was a satisfying experience with a couple of minor tweaks that could elevate the dish even further.

Despite the growing popularity of Thai food, it is hard to find a spot in Manhattan that really does it right. Thai Villa really does it right. The long lines most evenings attest to the quality of the food. To be clear, Thai Villa is a traditional (American) Thai restaurant. We love Uncle Boon's and while Uncle Boon's is more creative, Thai Villa delivers on what you want, good, fresh, flavorful traditional Thai dishes. The apps, the noodles, the Curry's, the entrees are all wonderful. The service, the decor and the cocktails are great as well. Thai Villa is certainly worth the wait!

Title: Au Cheval NYC – Hyped for the Burgers, but They Didn't Quite Stand Out

I recently visited the New York outpost of the famed Chicago burger spot, Au Cheval, after hearing endless praises about their burgers. The New York vibe was far more relaxed, with reservations easily available and welcoming walk-ins.

Against recommendations, I went for the 'single' hamburger, which comes with two patties, and succumbed to the trend by adding an egg on top. Unfortunately, the burger was messier than I prefer and didn't quite meet my sky-high expectations. Despite its richness, it felt like it was missing a pinch of seasoning – perhaps a bit more salt would make a difference.

However, not all was lost. The side of crispy fries topped with mornay sauce, garlic aioli, and a fried egg was truly exceptional. The garlic aioli was particularly noteworthy – simply bomb.

Service-wise, I can't fault the place – our waitress was delightful and contributed to a pleasant experience. While the burger didn't blow me away as I hoped, and I've certainly had better in New York, the ambiance and sides make Au Cheval worth a visit. Just don't let the hype set your expectations too high.

Great place for dinner with friends! The ambience of the restaurant is discreetly upscale but also casual. Phenomenal service and the dessert was mouthwatering. We had citrus salad and a variety of fresh oysters, for apps. For our main we ordered hot fried chicken, hanger steak with kimchi fried rice, side of asparagus, and my favorite, rack of lamb. All the food was perfectly cooked and the seasoning and sauces complimented the meal nicely. For dessert we tried a little bit of everything. The beignets were divine, my favorite was Meyer Lemon Merengue Pie, and we also tried tres leches cake, warm chocolate tart, and hand pie. Overall would recommend to anyone looking for a filling meal with flavors from all different kitchens and cuisines.

Apparently this is what they call fast food vegan. It was definitely fast food. It was definitely vegan. It just wasn't particularly good at doing either very well, or decently. The food was very fast food. Like gross fast food. The burger was this tiny patty that you'd expect at a step down from McDonald's. It was sloppy and messy. There was more toppings to make it appear to be substantive. But it was mostly bum and some faux fixings. It wasn't what anyone would call a burger, vegan or otherwise. The fries were dingy. The only thing Chloe did right was open up in Rockefeller center, where people would come because it was hip, not because it was good.I got to be honest. I initially gave this place three stars cause I was feeling generous at the time. But, it just wasn't worth that. It's just awful-ish. They get the second star though for being clean, bright and spacious, and semi-friendly.

Title: A Bite of the Big Apple's Best: The Dumpling Delight

If there's a testament to the power of simplicity in a bite-sized package, it's the five hot, scrumptiously fried pork dumplings I savored for just $1.50. But do you need more convincing? Here's the skinny:

Firstly, the place is a magnet for foodies and tour groups alike - whether it's a dedicated culinary journey or not, they all make a pit stop here. And it’s no wonder, seeing that these dumplings are the talk of the town.

Though the pork dumplings steal the spotlight, the menu - albeit compact - caters to varied tastes, including non-meat options that are just as sumptuous.

Fair warning: it's a cash-only counter, and don't expect change. Your cash is your ticket to a customizable feast, adding a uniquely "New York" flavor to the experience. It's quirky, it's fun, and it's absolutely a must-try. Queue up and prepare for an undeniable treat. Yes, you'll agree - it's worth every dime and minute spent in line.

Title: A SoCal Taco Triumph in Chelsea Market

As a seasoned taco connoisseur, I approached this much-hyped taqueria with a healthy dose of skepticism. However, I'm pleased to report that these tacos stand shoulder-to-shoulder with the best Southern California has to offer. Yes, at nearly $4 apiece, they aren't the cheapest around, but once you bite into these generously loaded shells, any price concerns dissipate, justified by their exceptional quality.

The standout, for me, was undoubtedly the meat – it's the most flavorful I've ever had nestled in a tortilla. And if the meat is the ensemble's star, the sauces are its perfect supporting cast – absolutely fire! The adobado tacos rightly reign supreme; as someone who typically favors beef, I was pleasantly surprised to find the pork adobada outshining the carne asada.

A slight misstep is their horchata, which disappointingly echoes a watered-down rendition of the classic drink. But don't let that deter you – the vibrancy of the tacos more than compensates.

Don't be deterred by the sight of the long line; it's a testament to the food's allure and moves faster than anticipated. The taco acquisition might seem chaotic, yet there's a method to the madness that results in a delightfully satisfying dining experience.

All things considered, this spot earns my vote as Chelsea Market's top food destination. Whether you're a taco aficionado or a newcomer to the scene, these tacos are a must-try.

Had dinner with friends on a Friday, October 25th 2019. The place was packed!!!!! Apparently, it is quite authentic Szechuan style - with strong spices. If I did not have a friend who would order for me, I would not have been able to enjoy the Szechuan dish. Our dishes were : Tomato & egg soupClear dumpling Yangzhou fried riceGeneral Tao's chickenBraised beef fillets with napa (My favorite dish of the night !!!!!!!)Sauteed shitake with bok choySteamed whole fish with chopped chili pepper (Quite tasty)The food service was quick, but other service was SLOW ..... We had a very hard time getting the attention of the servers.The menu was sooooo large, and overwhelming ... I could come back but would be at a loss, not knowing what to order.

Title: Comfortable Atmosphere and Tasty Pan-Asian Cuisine

I visited the restaurant on a quiet Sunday evening around 5:30 pm and found it refreshingly uncrowded, allowing for immediate seating. The interior captivates with its artistic homage to various Asian cultures, offering a visual feast to complement the dining experience.

I opted for the Spicy Night Market Noodle with Tofu and Vegetables, a delightful blend of flat and regular noodles amid a garden of veggies. While the dish had a mild heat, it didn't skimp on flavor. Portion sizes were satisfactory, matching the service in its adequacy.

Prices aligned with city dining norms, making it an acceptable spend for the quality and setting provided. Given the overall positive experience, I would certainly return for another flavorful escape.

Title: A Modest Vietnamese Staple: Tu Do - Satisfactory but Not Exceptional

In the pursuit of decent Vietnamese cuisine amidst New York’s limited selection, a cold evening’s craving led us to the doors of Tu Do. Our early Saturday visit around 5:30 PM found the restaurant welcoming, yet sparsely populated.

Opting for simplicity, we shared a banh xeo appetizer and individually selected mains; vermicelli with spring rolls for my husband and a canh chua for myself. The flavors delivered were standard – nothing to lament nor celebrate. Tu Do doesn't rise to the ranks of a Vietnamese culinary must-visit, but it suffices for a nearby, casual dining option.

The service was amicable, and the pricing, delightfully modest. For those in the vicinity with a Vietnamese hankering, Tu Do stands as a passable choice.

Came in for just one round near the end of the night where the only people left were costumed performers from a nearby show doing a Soul Train style funky dance line down the center of the room while me and a friend admired on from one of many tables. Beer bottle cap mosaics on the wall, low ceilings, classic jukebox, and extremely warm, friendly bar tenders gave this place an atmosphere I wouldn't have expected for the area. I'd come back.

Title: A Noodle Lover's Delight at a Charmingly Ambient Eatery

Review:

My dining experience at this restaurant surpassed expectations, with an overall rating that speaks for itself: Ambience 5/5, Food 4.5/5, Service 5/5.

We indulged in an array of dishes, starting with entrees. The Lamb Noodle outshone the rest with its rich flavors, earning the top spot on our list. Dan Dan Noodles followed closely, with a robust taste that didn't disappoint. The Lion Head Meatball Soup, while overshadowed by the other two, was a delightful choice for those in search of a lighter broth that didn't skimp on taste.

The sides also left an impression, particularly the Xiao Long Bao, which were a treat in their trio of soup-filled bundles. The Pork Belly slices on skewers brought the perfect crunch and seasoning to the table, and the Lychee ice drink was the epitome of refreshment, cleansing the palate with every sip.

The ambience could not have been better suited for a romantic date or a casual meetup, with thoughtful lighting, plants, and décor. The service matched the setting, thanks to attentive and respectful staff.

Booking was a breeze via Yelp, and our 8pm Saturday arrival was met with prompt seating. With such an incredible first impression, I'm convinced this will become my go-to noodle haven. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

The decor of the Alice's Tea Cup is very whimsical. It fits the theme perfectly to walk in and feel as if you walked into a chapter of Alice in Wonderland. Growing up, I have always loved the book, any remakes/movie specials, and when you pair this love with my need for TEA, this is the place to be! Yes there are several places to have afternoon tea in the city but I don't think they have the same charm as this Tea Cup!I was here for a bridal shower of a small party of 6 and they were a little slow in cleaning up so we could set up our decorations. We have reserved a time slot for afternoon tea with brunch and they gave us a few tables on the second floor. We shared the second floor with a child's birthday party and regular patrons as well. The place is not too big; cozy vibes all around.The staircase is a little small and the steps may not be the same height so be careful as you ascend. This does add to the charm of the place but may also be a little hazardous if you go rushing into a server holding sandwiches or hot teas! We had a table by the front window so the natural light was great in our photographs! The server was very kind and made suggestions for our teas. We had 3 teapots and the brunch menu: eggs, sausage, scones, and fruit and yogurt. The food was fresh and yummy. Definitely recommend the scones. By the time they brought out the fruit and yogurt I had filled up on the scones and breakfast already. They were nice about letting us take the remaining leftover dishes to go and provided boxes for us to pack them up.  Waitress was very helpful in recommending teas for us to try: there were so man it could easily be overwhelming but we had a good variety!I don't know if they still offer it, but I have seen Groupon deals of theirs pop up in the past. It's a good place to catch up with some girlfriends. It's a place to visit once in a while. I'm not sure if a boyfriend or husband would really be into afternoon tea but it is very family friendly and the food is delicious. I wish I could take a box of scones home!

Met a friend for dinner, arriving just before the 6 PM open. We were the second party to be seated, receiving a table in the far back corner. Glasses of water were poured, $4 Sapporo drafts ordered. The menu covers a lot of territory, with only a few items falling afoul of my shellfish allergy (why must the mac and cheese contain clam juice?). My friend and I picked out a couple dishes and took a couple more recommendations from the waitress. Tuna tataki was the first to arrive. 10 slices of lightly grilled tuna, tender to the touch, soft and delicious. Next, Korean popcorn chicken. Simple, yet elegant. Crispy exterior, fresh chicken within, sweet and spicy sauce all around. First two plates were delightful. A few minutes later, the edamame dumplings arrived. This dish was a little underwhelming, too plain, didn't capture the essence of edamame IMO. Wasn't bad, just not for me. Beer gone, I ordered a mixed drink, served in a see-through plastic pouch like a big ol' Capri-sun. Sweet and tasty, very 'grammable, definitely an intriguing experience. Still, I would've been fine with another Sapporo. Something went wrong with our steak, and it took a long time to hit the table. Worth the wait though! Tasty slices of rare steak, with some sauce for dipping. Another highlight of the meal. Probably could have eaten more, but there is grace in moderation. Next time, I may skip the vegetarian options and stick to the various meats. Those dishes were the highlight for me, and I will gladly return to eat more.

Title: Sky-High Dining Excellence

During our recent East coast family trip, we booked a table at a 60th-floor eatery boasting breathtaking views of NYC and the East River. The reservation, planned well in advance, set the stage for an unforgettable dining experience.

The staff's friendliness and professionalism were immediately evident, enhancing the ambiance with their attentive service. Opting for the three-course lunch prix fixe at $78 per person, my wife and I savored every bite. The menu showcased well-prepared and beautifully presented dishes, with the Waygu entree and Creme brûlée standing out as favorites. The accompanying bread, anchovies, and pate spread were exceptional in their own right.

However, not every dish hit the mark for us; I found the scrambled eggs with veal brain starter excessively salty. Impressively, the wait staff noticed my dissatisfaction due to the largely untouched plate and courteously offered an alternative starter – a thoughtful gesture we hadn't encountered before.

The combination of the stunning locale, exquisite food, and stellar service places this restaurant among the top-tier dining establishments we've had the pleasure of visiting.

Really solid bowl with good flavor and good price.Service people were super nice. I got my food rather quickly as it was made to order.I had never been here before but used a mealpal today to get a Tokyo chicken bowl. It came with grilled chicken, scallions, furikake (dried fish and seaweed) seasoning, mushrooms, cucumber salad and smoked teriyaki sauce over white rice. Overall the bowl was plentiful and tasted really good. I will definitely be back to try other flavor combinations.

Title: A Taste of the South in the Heart of Harlem

My recent dining experience at Sylvia's was nothing short of a Southern comfort odyssey in the bustling energy of Harlem. The ambiance is rich with history; every wall adorned with photographs and news articles that speak volumes of its storied past. Stepping in on a weeknight, I immediately found myself comfortably seated without a wait—a welcome surprise in the city.

Dubbed as the Southern food mecca of the city, Sylvia's lives up to its reputation with a flair for authentic regional cuisine that would be hard to surpass. The professionalism of the staff is evident from the moment the hostess greets you to the attentive service provided by the waiters.

The liver entree, although slightly more breaded than I prefer, was savory to the last bite, complemented beautifully by the standout sides of green beans and black-eyed peas. But it was the complimentary cornbread that truly stole the show—so captivating, it deserves its own fan club.

Sylvia's embodies the soulful essence of Harlem and is a culinary gem that beckons every New Yorker to indulge at least once. In summary, Sylvia's isn't just a restaurant; it's a pilgrimage for the taste buds—one that delivers an authentic slice of Southern hospitality right at our doorstep.

I had heard about this place for so long, and finally had a night to make it there! This place doesn't have any seats but they do have high tables to stand at. My friend and I ordered the mushroom and the sausage/onion. The portions are pretty big; we probably should have taken it to go but ate it all anyway. Next time, ordering only one personal pie and sharing! 2 slices are def enough (it comes with 4).

Title: Delightful Tapas Experience at a Moment's Notice

My visit to this tapas restaurant might have been spontaneous, but the culinary impressions were lasting enough to warrant a review four months on. Securing a table with a mere 30 minutes notice on a Saturday evening was a breeze—indicative of an accessible reservation system.

For a set price of $45, diners are invited to select three thoughtfully presented dishes. While portions lean towards the petite side, the culinary artistry is undeniable from the get-go, as evidenced by the welcoming bowl of addictively satisfying seaweed crackers.

Highlights from the menu included a beef tartare with a refreshingly tropical twist courtesy of pineapple. An unexpectedly harmonious blend of leeks adorned with cheddar and candied walnuts also left a positive mark. However, the standout was the oyster mushrooms paired with sunchokes, elevated by a divine truffle cream that masterfully married textures.

While not every dish reached the peaks of these favorites—the endive wrapped shrimp faltered in comparison and the anchovy's presence in the Galbi dish was notably absent—I was nonetheless enamored by creations like the impeccably tender octopus with mango and mojo verde.

An additional delight was their seaweed rice, a simple yet exquisitely flavorful side for an extra $2 that pairs impeccably with the complimentary pickles provided.

Though typically skeptical of high-priced, small-portion establishments, this experience challenged my preconceptions with its genuinely satisfying flavors and textures. With a menu that's prone to change, the allure of a return visit is strong—an invitation to indulge in both familiar favorites and new culinary explorations.

New York prices, but the service was wonderful and the food was above-average - so it was an overall enjoyable dinner experience for us at Da Claudio.I loved that they had a quite a few specials on the menu (a number of which involved lobster - my favorite!), but I ended up going with the first thing that I had set my eye on, the Black Linguine (squid ink pasta with prawns). It wasn't the best version I've ever had, but overall a satisfying meal, and the prawns were very fresh. My husband ordered the Tagliata (sliced strip steak with herbed potatoes) - the $42 price tag almost was a deal-breaker, but we decided to splurge and let me just say... it was a HUGE meal. Honestly, it was at least double the size of what I would generally expect for a steak dinner - and it was absolutely delicious too. The service was exceptional - prompt drink refills throughout the night, and they instantly brought us a brand new bread basket once we worked our way through the first (what can I say, we were hungry...). To be fair, it was about 9 PM at night, so it was pretty quiet in there, but I still always appreciate awesome service.The location was also super convenient for anyone staying in the Financial District - we were staying at the Moxy Downtown, and this place was literally right across the street. So, it was the perfect option for us on a night where we weren't wanting to venture far, but still wanted to feel like we were going out. All things considered, this place is a nice little Italian restaurant worth visiting.

This is a hidden gem. Great place for lunch or dinner. Place is a bit out dated and needs a bit of renovation. Place been here since the stone ages. Service is great. Food is awesome. Will definitely come here again. Please TLC to the bathrooms. They smell and look not presents.

Title: A Delightful Surprise Amongst a Sea of Options

Choosing a restaurant on a bustling strip lined with countless Italian eateries was daunting, but our decision to dine at this particular gem was met with culinary delight. The pasta dishes were the standout stars of our evening. As I savored each creamy bite of my Fettuccine Alfredo with chicken, and my friend enjoyed the rich, hearty flavor of their penne alla vodka with chicken, we were impressed by the generous portion sizes and the exceptional taste of our meals.

Taking advantage of the summer weather, we dined al fresco, which only enhanced the experience. While we found the service to be adequate, it lacked a certain attentiveness that could have elevated our visit from great to perfect.

Nonetheless, this restaurant is one I'd wholeheartedly recommend to any pasta aficionado. With scrumptious food and charming decor, it earns a well-deserved 5/5 in both categories. The service trails slightly behind at 4/5, but don't let that deter you – this spot is not to be missed.

Overall Ratings:
- Food: 5/5
- Decor: 5/5
- Service: 4/5

We had an excellent meal here last night before going to the theatre.  We arrived a 25 minutes early for our 6:15 reservation and had no trouble being seated, there were plenty of tables available.  By 6:10, the place was jammed.  I started out with a Dia de los Muertos Porter, which was fine; my wife had a red wine and our son a marguerita.  As appetizers we had  trio of ceviches - the tuna and yellowtail were especially noteworthy; the octopus was fine too.  The others shared a guacamole; I don't eat it but the salse that came tieh the chips was rich and fine to eat.  Our main courses were roasted shrimp Toloache (five plump and very tasty shrimp in a nice sauce), carnitas served in a cake-like form, with a hazelnut mole, and queso fundido).  The desserts were so tempting that I found it hard to choose - we ended up with the chocolate cake with hot rocks (pictured below).Service was excellent as well; attentive but not cloying.  There was much to like on the menu, and on another trip to New York I hope to be back to explore further

I used to visit O'Hara's with colleagues during the time when I worked in the FiDi area (literally 2 blocks away). It was always a good time. I popped in recently after so long and it felt like I traveled back to 2008. You can count on O'Hara's for:*Decent eats*Feeling at home, where everyone will get to know your name if you visit often*Good beer/shots/mixed drinks (stay away from the wine. The Rose tasted like a wine cooler)*Great music---the sing-a-long kind*Being extremely crowded*Striking up a conversation with new people*Catching the latest sports score*Befriending the owner, Jimmy*Reliving old memories and making new onesBare bones, minimal atmosphere, unpretentious and fun. Solid.

What a nice surprise! The food here was very delicious and good quality, not salty at all like most Chinese noodle places. The three of us ordered the garlic eggplants, mung bean noodle salad, mo crispy flatbread for appetizers. All were really yummy! I got the braised beef noodles and the beef was very tender and soup well flavored. My sister had the signature noodles which she liked too. My husband had the cold noodles which had a nice kick. Our server William was very friendly and provided great service. We also had both of the desserts. Definitely coming back!

I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a delightful dining experience. The food is simply delicious, full of flavor, and their signature dishes are perfect for a photo op on your social media. The decor adds to the ambiance, ensuring that not only your taste buds but also your eyes have a feast. You'll be greeted by efficient and friendly staff, which makes the experience all the more enjoyable. I absolutely love this place and am confident you will too.

Last night's dining experience at this UES Greek gem was sensational. The tender octopus melted in my mouth, while the succulent lamb chops were cooked to perfection. The lemon potatoes? Simply the tastiest I've ever had. Complementing the exquisite food was the friendly and attentive service, making the evening all the more delightful. Highly recommended for a fantastic Greek feast!

Recently, I had the pleasure of dining at Tribeca's Kitchen, where the brunch options impressed me greatly. The pancakes were delightfully soft and sweet, an indulgence I'd repeat in a heartbeat. Complementing my sweet start, the avocado toast with perfectly runny yolks was a savory delight. Bellinis and mimosas added a festive touch to the meal, and I must admit, I couldn't stop at just one!

For those seeking a healthier alternative, the yogurt with granola and berries is not only a visual treat but also a tasty one. Don't let the diner ambiance fool you; the quality of food here is exceptional. The mango, berry, and banana smoothie was a thick and flavorsome choice that I'd highly recommend for a refreshing kick.

Venturing into the lunch menu, I was particularly taken by the grilled shrimp wrap, which was seasoned to perfection, casting away any initial doubts I had. My companion praised her salmon wrap, rounding off our delightful culinary experience.

In short, if you find yourself in Tribeca, this kitchen is a must-visit for both the delectable diner classics and the tantalizing healthier options.

Came here for a quick lunch with the family. It was a little not as expected, but we really liked the food. I had thought this was going to be a sit down restaurant with menus and order via waiter. Nope. You enter and get in a line and order at a counter via a menu board of fun choices. You then get a buzzer which lets you know your food is ready and go pick it up.When we were there, it was quite crowded and difficult to get a table, but we did after some patience. We were stuck at the corner by the door, so we were treated to constant breezes as customers kept coming inside.We had a burger melt, fried chicken melt, vegetable melt, a plain melt (grilled cheese), and two sets of TOTS! Tots, glorious Tots! Wife had to have them plain, though. These were crunchy and crispy tots fresh made goodness. All of the sandwiches had good bread, and nothing bad at all about the insides.To save a little money, we had curtesy water cups that we filled from the soda fountain. $55 for four, and you get 5% back via Yelp money if you use your registered card.

Title: A Moderately Enjoyable Experience for Girls Night

Rating: ★★★☆☆

I recently visited this Korean BBQ spot for a girls' night out, expecting the same great experience I remembered. Unfortunately, it fell a bit short. Despite having reservations for our party of six, we were left waiting for 15 minutes before being seated.

The food, I'd rate a 3 out of 5. Both the banchan and kalbi were merely average, lacking the wow factor I had anticipated. A previously impressive menu now seemed to have lost its luster, possibly due to a change in the chef or the evening's busyness. I also found the flavors to be overwhelmingly sweet, detracting from the authenticity of the dishes.

Service was equally lackluster, earning another 3 out of 5. It appeared they were understaffed as it took an extra 15 minutes post-serving our meat just to get the charcoal. Simple requests, such as rice refills or essentials like garlic and ssam, had to be made twice. While the service staff was pleasant, it was clear they were too stretched to provide attentive care.

The ambiance scored a 3 as well. It's your typical Korean BBQ setting, adorned with wooden fixtures, but nothing to write home about. A point of caution: should you need to visit the restrooms located downstairs, be wary of the slippery floors.

In a nutshell, while the company was great, the overall experience at this once-favorite spot was dishearteningly average.

Delicious!!! This is for delivery only.I ordered the Steamed Dumplings ($9) and the Beef Panang Curry ($18). Delivery arrived on-time. Order is correct. The steamed dumplings were tasty. They contain a small shrimp. The sauce they came with is more of a thicker consistency soy sauce. It was 5 dumpling for $9. A bit pricey for those I think. I won't order them again. Not worth it in my opinion. The Beef Panang Curry was delicious! I would order it again. There was crunchy green beans and the coconut milk and curry blend tasted SO good. I drank it. There was about a cup of beef total, which isn't bad. The beef was not as tender as I thought it would be and it's sliced thin. Good flavors throughout though. Great portion size too. I couldn't even eat any of the rice that it came with! Love OBAO and I recommend trying it out!!

Located in the heart K-town this bar/restaurant is one of the few places that have happy hour until 8pm for both drinks and food.  Located on the 3rd floor I can see why this spot might be a little tricky to find at first.  When we walked in there were a good amount of people there and plenty of seating at the bar.  Since Halloween was a few days away they decorated the place in Halloween fashion.  I really loved the dim lighting throughout the whole bar which made for a more intimate setting.  Spicy-ish chips were placed in front of us when sat down and were surprisingly pretty good.  We decided to order two drinks to share- "The Latin soleil" and "soapberry odyssey".  Both were pretty good but I really enjoyed the twist between the sweet and spicy kick that the Latin soleil had.  When more friends joined us we ordered some bottled soju along with shots to enjoy.  The menu of this spot is really interesting.  Expect to see Korean/Mexican fusion along with some dishes from each culture.   The service was attentive despite being busy and the decor of this place is my style. Definitely recommend this place!!!

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Highly-Rated Eatery

Having been drawn in by stellar reviews, my expectations were high for this restaurant. Sadly, my dining experience was a mixed bag. The burrata, a pleasant enough start, paired with beets and orange slices, failed to elevate beyond the ordinary. The highlight of the meal was the lamb bolognese; a delectable sauce coating perfectly al dente pasta, I'd easily recommend this dish.

Unfortunately, the pizzas fell short. The meatball pizza was notably disappointing; flavorless with dry meatballs and an uninspired crust. The Killer Bee pizza's adventurous topping combo of sopressata, chili oil, honey, and garlic had potential but was marred by a flavorless, oil-drenched crust that turned soggy, complicating the act of eating it.

In conclusion, while the lamb bolognese was a triumph, the overall experience didn't live up to the hype. I'm unlikely to return, but for those who may visit, the lamb bolognese is the way to go.

This is Pho super sized!  I left extremely stuffed so you will get your money's worth.  The environment is clean and contemporary. The short rib is a must have in your lifetime so don't hesitate to order on your first visit.   Now i know why there is always a line when I pass by.

Tucked away within a stone's throw of Penn Station, this eatery offers a swift and affordable dining experience perfect for the commuter crowd. Although the crabmeat spring roll left something to be desired, appearing over-oily and lackluster, the establishment redeemed itself with its signature combination beef pho. The broth of the pho was notably exceptional, and with the addition of their homemade chili/vinegar sauce, it transformed into a dish of heightened flavor and complexity. Opting for the medium size proved to be sufficiently satiating. Despite the spring roll's misstep, the pho alone makes this spot worth a visit.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this charming neighborhood gem, and I must say, the experience was delightful. The red sangria served here is absolutely fantastic, a perfect start to a memorable meal. Additionally, the complimentary salad pleasantly surprised me with its tangy and spicy French dressing—a treat for the taste buds indeed.

Moving on to the main course, the shrimp with garlic sauce was nothing short of amazing. The flavors were on point, and the dish lived up to every bit of my expectations. The ambiance of the restaurant struck a balance between romantic and fun, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere that complements the dining experience perfectly.

I was also impressed by the generous portion sizes, ensuring that you leave with both your palate and your appetite thoroughly satisfied. This place truly feels like a real neighborhood spot where comfort and quality take the center stage.

My enthusiasm for this dining experience can't be overstated—I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

We stopped by here after Curlfest because we refused to spend money on food trucks at the park for fear of long lines and small portions. Sister's was not too far from the shuttle stop drop off for curl fest so it was very convenient to get to. Before I start off my review I'd like to if this was any other kind of restaurant it would have been a 3 start review BUT you know how the say if the Caribbean women taking your order at the counter is rude than it's going to be a great meal, well that's what this place was like. No one was flat out rude to us but the customer service was not great. The place is small so when we walked in every seat was filled ( more people from curlfest!). No one acknowledged my parties presence until I finally had to go up to a waitress and ask about a potential wait time ( they didn't have one ) We were so hungry we decide to just wait it out because it seems a party would leave in about 10 minutes. Once we sat down the tables were not wiped down, only the plates and cups were taken away. We heard the oxtails were really good so a couple of people in my party were going to order that, I wanted jerk chicken. THEY RAN OUT OF OXTAILS to the disappointment of my party.  We all ordered jerk chicken meals ( it was really spicy for anyone that doesn't like heat ) All in all , I'm not sure if the volume of people coming in took them off guard. But the customer service/ experience was not great but the food is 5 stars. I'm willing to make the trip from NJ to Harlem just to experience the oxtails on a less busy day. I'll keep y'all updated.

Title: Decent Quick Bite at St. Mark's Spot

I recently visited a snug little eatery on St. Mark's, intrigued by its presence outside the usual Chinatown location. With two of their signature rice rolls and a pair of Joe's crepes, three of us found ourselves contentedly sated. The rice rolls, which required a splash of soy sauce and sriracha for added zest, undoubtedly stole the show.

Service was a one-man affair, prompt with the rice rolls but slower on the crepe front. Speaking of which, Joe's crepes were a bit of a struggle to enjoy as the fillings tended to escape with each bite.

The affordability is evident both in the price and the ingredient quality—commendable for a quick bite but not quite the culinary experience that would beckon a return, especially considering the myriad of Asian cuisine options available in the city. A fair 3.5-star experience for those looking for a no-fuss meal.

Title: A Cozy Chelsea Gem for Evening Culinary Delights

My recent dining experience at this Chelsea hotspot was truly satisfying. The restaurant seems to have garnered mixed reviews, particularly for its brunch offerings, but I can't speak to that—I'm here to endorse their delightful evening menu.

The service was commendable; our wait staff was exceptionally warm and attentive, always ready to field queries about the menu. The focus on quality ingredients was evident, and while initial impressions suggested modest portions, the meal sizes turned out to be ideal.

The drink selection catered to all tastes, with both alcoholic and non-alcoholic options. Their lemonade and tea were refreshing, and while the barbera wine didn't top my list, it was pleasantly palatable.

Midweek dining ensured a calm atmosphere, with plenty of seating and no rush or crowd. The linguini & clams, though a tad salty, satisfied with sizeable clams and great pasta texture. However, the standout was the lamb radiatore—perfectly cooked pasta adorned with tender, well-seasoned lamb in a slightly tangy sauce.

Desserts ended the meal on a high note. The olive cake, served with ice cream and berries, offered a brilliant interplay of sour and sweet, although I would've preferred alternative ice cream flavors to suit my non-strawberry preference. The chocolate lava cake, lush and decadent without being overly sweet, was a triumph.

Prices are what you'd expect for Chelsea, justified by the food and service quality. This restaurant has earned my recommendation, and I'm intrigued enough to return for another dinner that promises to be just as delightful.

Title: A Must-Visit for Dry Pot Aficionados

My culinary escapades brought me back to one of my top choices for dry pot, an establishment that, alongside its East Village sibling, draws a fervent dinner crowd—often resulting in up to an hour's wait. Unperturbed by the bustle, I savored the customized dry pot that included lotus root, konjac noodles, succulent slices of eye of round, fish balls, and oyster mushrooms, all seasoned to a perfect mild heat level.

The harmony of flavors within the dry pot was nothing short of remarkable. The eye of round and mushrooms stood out, having absorbed the rich spices and aromas, elevating the dish to new heights. The lotus root and fish balls also made a delectable impression, while the konjac noodles were passable. For anyone in search of top-notch dry pot, consider this place a gastronomic highlight; their mastery of seasoning and ingredient selection is truly commendable.

After a leisurely stroll out of Central Park feeling a bit peckish, we stumbled upon a quaint eatery that immediately caught our attention, thanks to a couple visibly savoring their meal. Deciding to give it a try, we popped in, ordered a pizza, and settled in for what became a splendid dining experience.

The service was impeccable; not once did I spy the bottom of my water glass, a testament to the attentiveness of the staff. As for the main event – the pizza – it was a revelation. It is no exaggeration to declare that this was the best pizza I've had in New York, bar none. What struck me was how it managed to shine without the all-too-common long lines; it's truly a hidden gem.

Their establishment was the epitome of cleanliness, complete with the much-appreciated amenity of a restroom. And the pizza itself? The crust was the perfect symphony of crispness that every pizza aficionado dreams of.

I wholeheartedly recommend giving this place a try; you won't be disappointed.

I came in on a Thursday evening and was seated right away (I had a reservation). It's a decent size restaurant, and there is a bar inside. They offer a pretty wide variety of wine and cocktails.I tried the Babylou's Lumpia, and that was pretty good. This dish comes with two fried spring rolls, but they are larger in size than your typical Filipino lumpia. Also, I didn't read the menu very carefully, but do note that it's vegetarian. So I was expecting meat, but it's full of vegetables (mainly cabbage). It also came very hot, so eat with caution or you'll burn your tongue. (No stars deducted due to anything mentioned about the lumpia, as I didn't read carefully to know it was vegetarian, and I was just starving and that's why I ate the lumpia so quickly!)The Beefsteak Tagalog did not have much flavor on its own, so the calamansi soy sauce was pretty crucial to have with each bite. And the baby potatoes that came with this dish were a little dry. The caramelized onions were delightfully crunchy. The onions and calamansi soy sauce were the highlights of this dish, which should not be the case against steak, but they were. I know the potatoes were the carbs of this dish, but I feel that rice could have been served with the steak. And from the lack of flavor, maybe garlic rice would be better than just plain white rice. Also, when we were served this dish, we were provided with butter knives, which did not help against a thick piece of meat. It was only when we were halfway through the steak that we were offered steak knives.The Kare Kare was the star of the night! The braised oxtail was so tender and fell right off the bone. Even when picking up a piece of the oxtail from the bowl, the meat would fall apart. The peanut-rice sauce was delicious and it had a great meat to vegetable proportion. The peanut sauce is pretty rich, so it was a great balance to eat the oxtail with the rice.To end the night, I tried the Fruity Halo Halo. Such a favorite Filipino dessert of mine! This Halo Halo is a "chilled mixture of fresh tropical fruits with coconut sorbet and coconut juice". So as a dessert, this was delicious and so refreshing. The coconut sorbet was good and the dessert came with pieces of pineapple, blueberries, strawberries, mango, and watermelon. My gripe with this is that halo halo is supposed to be shaved ice. So it was a good dessert, but it just wasn't what I was expecting. Maybe it's halo halo fusion?It's not definite that I will revisit this restaurant. I feel that the pricing is a bit high for what is actually offered. Maybe if it was priced more reasonably, I'd definitely come back to try the other entrees. But for now, I'm not so sure.

Title: Mixed Experience at Friday Night's Dinner Buffet

I recently visited this restaurant for their all-you-can-eat (AYCE) dinner buffet on a Friday night with friends. The fish served in the sushi offerings was of commendable quality for an AYCE setup, though the sushi rolls and nigiri were marred by an excessive amount of rice, which diluted the overall taste.

The fried appetizers mostly hit the mark with savory flavors and crisp textures. A standout was the stir-fried udon, which offered a delightful mix of well-seasoned ingredients and perfectly cooked noodles. Regrettably, the experience was not without its lows—the miso soup was disappointingly over-salted, a flaw shared by the broth of the udon noodle soup. I'd recommend steering clear of the soupy dishes here.

Adding to the disappointments, the takoyaki lacked the traditional punch of flavor one would expect, presenting instead with a forgettable blandness and an unappealing mushy texture.

Considering the price point and the culinary misses, particularly with the soups and takoyaki, my inclination is to opt out of returning for another dinner session at this establishment.

So, Mr. Bobby Flay posted about J.G.'s burger being one of the burgers he often craved. We are talking about a renown chef that's also a grill master raving about the burgers from here. Naturally, I had to give it a try. It was a rainy Tuesday around 12:30 PM. I'd say it was pretty busy, but there were tables available. I was contemplating between whether to get bacon with my cheeseburger or fries or both. I didn't want to be overly gluttonous. So I opted to skip the bacon, and ordered a cheeseburger cooked medium with fries. Food did not take long to come out. I loved seeing that the fries were fried to golden brown perfection. Nothing more infuriating than pale fries that look like they were blanched in oil for 3 seconds. Burger was great in its simplicity. Beefy and juicy with great charred taste. Fries were perfection. Bobby wins again. As for service, staff were 50/50. Half of them were not the friendliest and half of them were. It is what it is.

Title: A Delightful Surprise at a Cozy Neighborhood Spot

I recently enjoyed a dining experience that utterly exceeded my expectations in the best possible way. My sister and I, both unfamiliar with Matzoh Ball soup, decided to satisfy her sudden craving on a whim while in the area. To our delight, the soup was divine—a consommé that was light yet savory, beautifully fragrant, and elevated by a touch of dill. Despite my lack of hunger, I was immediately captivated from the first spoonful.

Curious about the composition of the Matzoh balls, I found myself marveling at their delicious simplicity. They seemed to be a blend of flour and water, yet the flavor they imparted was a mystery I was happy to contemplate over dinner.

The culinary adventure didn't stop there. I ventured further, trying the Noodle Kugel, which reminded me of a not-too-sweet bread pudding with an intriguing hint of tangerine. My sister indulged in the Chocolate Babka, a rich and decadent treat that stood out as one of the most luxurious chocolate desserts we've had.

The entire experience was made even more exceptional by the outstanding service. Our server was one of the friendliest individuals we've encountered, contributing to an amazing dining experience that was as satisfying as it was unexpected. This restaurant is a hidden gem that I can't recommend enough for those looking to have their expectations surpassed.

Title: A Brunch Delight with Unique Twists

I recently enjoyed a delightful brunch at this restaurant and left thoroughly satisfied. The risotto fries were a standout, combining the crispiness of hash browns with a lusciously creamy risotto core – a true revelation for the taste buds. Opting for something light, the chicken lettuce wrap graced my palate with its crisp freshness, complete with a mouth-watering peanut chicken sauce, roasted peanuts, pickled vegetables, and an assortment of greens.

To toast the season, I sipped on "The Grinch," a whimsical holiday concoction blending matcha with festive flavors, perfectly crowned by frothy egg whites adding just the right touch of creaminess. The lobster roll was a luxurious treat, pairing delicate, fresh lobster with a soft bun – sophistication in every bite. While the paella was tasty, it didn't quite hit the heights of others I've tried and seemed a tad overpriced for the portion served.

The sweetness of the banana French toast was a bit overpowering for my taste, but dessert lovers may find it a dream. Service was stretched thin but earnest; our server did his best to attend to us amidst a bustling crowd. All things considered, this place is a solid choice for anyone seeking an inventive and enjoyable brunch experience.

Title: A Lively Spot with Irresistible Charm

My dining experiences at this hidden gem have transformed me from a newcomer to a dedicated patron, eagerly introducing the delightful spot to friends. The ambiance strikes a unique balance between unpretentious and thematic, with its hard, metal folding chairs contributing to its authentic vibe. The open front doors in summer enhance the restaurant's welcoming feel, complemented by the charming taco van that doubles as a quirky photo opportunity.

While the setting is perfect for both a casual date or a group gathering, be prepared for a bustling atmosphere on weekends. Yet, despite the liveliness, service remains efficient with an easy ordering system and direct payment processing—though, currently, Apple Pay isn't an option.

The culinary offerings are as delightful as the ambiance. The crispy fish tacos are a personal favorite, and the vegetarian quesadilla is a mouthwatering choice. My companion's high praise for the corn esquites assures that each dish is crafted with care. In summary, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone looking for good food and a festive environment. Can't wait for my next visit!

Love the Sweet Potato Falafel but found it weird with Asian flavor spicy sauce. Moroccan Carrots not bad but nothing special. Mushroom not bad but nothing special. Pan Roasted Salmon was good but pretty standard. Crispy Kale was kinda a joke for $15

I really like this place. It has become my go-to brunch spot. So far. I've had their chai latte, matcha latte, breakfast tacos and avocado toast. Both the chai and matcha lattes are yummy. I typically get the chai latte. I appreciate that it is well-spiced, andthe little cinnamon pawprints they put on top of the steamed milk are adorable. The breakfast tacos are really good. They come with eggs, salsa and veggies in a tortilla. If you take too long to eat it, the tortillas do get a bit soggy but that's made up for by the fact that the tacos taste amazing. You can get a side of salad (with a delightful tart vinaigrette dressing of some kind) or deep-fried potato cubes. The avocado toast is also quite good. It's served on multigrain toast (which, last time was a bit soft for my liking but was otherwise good), and comes topped with a fried egg. My avocado toast also comes with a salad (although I think you can also substitute the salad here for home fries). The lines here can get crazy on weekends, but the staff is super efficient at making sure that everyone is seated after they order at the register. The system here works well. The ambiance is also great. It's cute, cozy and unpretentious. I also really like that most of the tables have different maps on them. Certain seats at the restaurant can feel a bit cramped when the place is crowded, but I find the coziness to be charming. The staff has always been cheerful, pleasant and helpful for as long as I've been coming here. Note that you're supposed to pick up your own silverware, napkins and water on your way to your table, but the servers bring the food to your table for you, and if you need a refill on you coffee, the servers do that for you too.

Title: A Culinary Gem with Service That Could Improve

I recently revisited one of my absolute favorite spots during a two-week stay in NYC, making sure to indulge not once but twice in their transcendent offerings. The pinnacle of my dining experience was undoubtedly the pulpo, a dish that I've raved about since first tasting it last April. It's so exceptional that their cookbook has found its way into my collection.

The quality of the food here is undeniable – it's a place that consistently impresses with its flavors and dish execution, meriting its status as a top contender in my personal list of culinary delights.

However, it's hard to overlook the less-than-attentive service. Even perched at the bar during a 9 PM dinner, my attempts to flag down staff for additional orders or simple water refills were met with frustrating delays, an issue encountered repeatedly throughout the meal.

Breakfast service did show some signs of hope with a proactive host offering assistance on multiple occasions, yet this didn't entirely make up for the general lack of attention provided by the serving staff.

Even with the service not quite matching the high bar set by the cuisine, this restaurant remains a must-visit in my book. Despite the occasional service hiccups, my enthusiasm for their exceptional food ensures I'll be returning – ready for more of those unforgettable pulpos.

I'm gonna be honest: Veselka is my go to drunk food when I'm in East Village. I've gotten pierogi here several times and each time has been amazing. Highly recommend fried meat, potatoes, and cheese options. The nice thing is they let you mix and match flavors as long as you cook them the same way (fried or boiled).I've never had a super long wait for a table which is super important after a long night out. Veselka's is definitely a staple of New York night life in my eyes, and I hope everyone gives this Ukrainian Diner a try.

Absolutely enamored with this gem in Brookfield! It's a perennial favorite for a reason. Their red velvet is a showstopper, and come autumn, the pumpkin variant simply steals the show. Truly, the cream cheese frosting is a decadent delight worthy of being savored solo. This spot is the perfect indulgent compliment to the surrounding health-conscious lunch options. A must-visit!

Title: A Standout Soba Experience at Ise Japanese Restaurant

In the bustling culinary scene of NYC, Ise Japanese Restaurant carves its niche with exceptional soba offerings. My partner and I secured a 6:30pm reservation via Yelp and were promptly seated in the subdued, conversation-friendly atmosphere of the restaurant.

The meal commenced with a delightful grilled mushroom appetizer that, while enjoyable, felt like a familiar home-cooked experience. The standout dish was the Stamina Soba, a vegetarian marvel of cold soba laden with a plethora of toppings including okura, mushroom, tempura flakes, grated yam, radish, and a quail egg yolk – the dish's symphony of textures and flavors was a revelation.

Equally impressive was the Ikasumi Uni Ikura Soba, which my partner had. The squid ink soba was crowned with fresh sea urchin and salmon roe that offered a luxurious taste of the ocean.

The deep-fried Lobster Koumi Nishu-age presented in two styles – salt & pepper and red sauce – was executed with perfection, its crunchy exterior giving way to succulent lobster within.

Dessert balanced the meal's opulence with simplicity: a raindrop cake akin to the finest gourmet jello and Japanese strawberries with condensed milk – the latter, while fresh, didn't quite excite us enough for a repeat order.

Service was attentive and courteous, dispelling any previous complaints we'd heard. A misstep with a beer-tea mix-up was promptly remedied with a genuine apology and replacement, enhancing our dining experience.

While the decor of Ise doesn't stray from the typical Japanese restaurant aesthetic, it maintains an inviting ambiance for diners.

In summary, Ise surprised us with its unique soba creations and outstanding service. It's definitely on our list for a return visit to delve into their sushi and sashimi offerings. Highly recommended for soba enthusiasts and those seeking a serene dining affair in NYC.

Great for breakfast/brunch! The staff was so sweet and always moving and working. Small space, but it's lovely. Coffee is delicious! And the theme of the restaurant was old yet modern. Service was very quick! The food was also great!

Great decor and service and good food. Wouldn't say they have the most authentic Shanghai food but def creative in a fusion way. We went in a big group and ordered a good variety of food. Good ones that I can remember are the salted stir fry string beans, a shrimp stew on rice, soup dumplings, and the final pumpkin dessert. The fish and braised pork was cooked more in an asian fusion way - very sweet. This place is def suitable for a business or special occasions.
