Overall very average, especially for NY pizza.+big sbarro size slices so 1-2 pieces are definitely enough.  My friend finished 1.5 so it's probably similar to 3 normal slices of pizza +/- napkins, cheese, pepper, etc are available to grab but not on every table-3.95% credit card charge so bring cash!-sodas are also super pricey and the cups are a tiny small.  The saving grace is that they will refill it for you-service was extremely minimal and we had to wait to pay  which I found strange.  Why wouldn't you pay upon receiving your food?  How do they manage this normally?  Maybe it was because we went when they opened and were he only ones there but it was weird.+nice super thin crust with a nice crisp Probably wouldn't come back since there are much better options available

Really solid. First visit, we got the roti, the Thai basil stirfry with shortrib, the fried chicken, and two orders of phat thai (one with chicken, one with prawns). The stirfry and the roti were our favorites, and there's other stuff I'd like to try as well. Not mind-blowing like the original Uncle Boons (or Ugly Baby, for that matter) but really good stuff.

Stopped by this place on a weekday for lunch, having been craving the minced pork over rice for a while. Saw a 4 star review so wanted to give it a try. The place is very tiny but not busy on the weekday during lunch. Ordered the minced pork over rice, come with a piece of tofu, half egg and some cabbage, the portion is small, tbh I was still hungry after that bowl. And a bag of salt & pepper chicken popcorn, they provide the spicy at counter so you can add as much as you want based on your taste. I found the amount of food is quite price for what they are charging. And the minced pork doesn't taste the same as how I remembered in Asia.

I am honestly so impressed & astonished and at how put together and classy this restaurant is after only being open a few months!!! Wild Ink is a beautiful, sexy restaurant that I would 100% recommend for a date night, celebration or even a romantic after work cocktail and their GORGEOUS bar. Beyond how beautiful the inside is, the view of The Vessel out the window is one of a kind and bound to impress your date. Past the aesthetic, the management is so professional, kind, and numerous times throughout the night they came to check on how our experience was. Beyond allllll that let's talk food. Phenomenal! Every single item on our table was properly cooked, flavourful, and delish! We had many apps and shared an entree. We started off with the Hamachi crudo which had such interesting flavour combos. Next we had the Bacon & shrimp shumai and the stuffed buns-- don't you dare come here and skip those buns and load up on that chili sauce! Next up we had the Spanish octopus (another NEED) and the delicious steak. They were both perfectly cooked & seasoned & the steak came with a potato foam, the most interesting side ever! Loved it. Ended the night with the (grilled?) pineapple upside cake which was yums with ginger icecream & a coconut rice pudding. You can tell we were STUFFED!!Cannot wait to return to this amazing spot for my next date night!

During our visit to the restaurant with a group of eight, we encountered a few logistical issues. Despite arriving early, we learned the policy is that seating doesn't occur until the entire party has arrived. Moreover, despite having a reservation for our sizeable group, the staff attempted to accommodate us at a table clearly meant for six, with no room to comfortably fit everyone. The layout of the dining area seems ill-considered for larger parties. Ultimately, we had to split into two separate tables. On a positive note, once seated, the service provided was prompt.

I recently dined at a well-appointed bar that boasted tasteful furnishings and an agreeable, albeit mismatched, musical backdrop. The food, while satisfactory, didn’t justify the steep prices—$20 for a modest serving of six mozzarella sticks struck me as excessive. The drinks were competent, though the absence of a happy hour was a missed opportunity to enhance value. Overall, a decent experience that could improve with more thoughtful pricing and entertainment choices.

Title: Serviceable Quick Lunch, No Frills

I stopped by for a quick grab-and-go lunch and this spot looked promising. Unfortunately, the interior was quite chilly, to the point of discomfort while dining in. That said, the service was speedy, and the make-your-own meal concept was quite engaging, allowing you to customize your dish which is promptly cooked in about 5 minutes.

The food was average at best, lacking distinction with flavors that tended to blend indistinctly, a common trait among large restaurant chains. It's not a culinary adventure, but for a rapid lunch that's relatively easy on the wallet, it gets the job done. A solid 3-star experience for fulfilling the need for speed and convenience without any culinary fanfare.

A Thai-me to remember :) Ordered: (everything was soooo good so I recommend it all) - Pad see ew: my favorite Thai comfort dish and they did it well! - beef dish from the privileged section of the menu: unfortunately don't remember the name of this dish but it was very unique and I highly recommend if you like spicy curries! The beef was tender, the flavor was fragrant and the dish included longan (which is like a lychee) and potato chips for texture - **my favorite dish of the night** moo pork chop: grilled pork lovers unite! The flavor on this pork chop was incredible - so juicy and flavorful (now I want it again). The addition of the coconut sticky rice paired really well with the savory meat Additional pros:- the waitstaff is super kind and helpful. They're great about checking in on you even when the restaurant is busy- complimentary shot glass of soup at the beginning- interior!!!! Nothing like it, it's cozy and beautiful Tip:- long wait so utilize the yelp waitlist!

Came here on a Friday night for dinner and drinks with a group of 7 around 6pm. The restaurant was a little small but they were able to seat us right away. The seating was a little awkward but it didn't affect our flow of conversation. They offered a lot of different Japanese dishes on the menu which was great. We ordered the yakitori party set for the table and I ordered the kimchi udon to try. We also ordered 3 pitchers of beer that came out to be $40, which was a pretty good deal. They also have happy hour deals with beer, wine and chu-hi for $5! The yakitori was okay as it wasn't very flavorful, but I did enjoy my kimchi udon. It was a little oily but the portion was good and it was well seasoned. Service overall was pretty good regardless of the crowd. Definitely a great spot to eat and pregame, but it seems like a very popular place so try to come a little earlier if you're coming with a big group!

Been here few times now, including dinner, brunch and for a quick snack and this place is a solid option for Greek food in les. Decor is awesome, one gets transported in santorini right away. We have tried a couple of things off the menu, and everything was delicious and authentic. Staff is great and tried to accommodate your special requests. Overall a great spot to satisfy those Greek food cravings. FYI...be prepared to wait if coming for dinner on weekends

Really good Thai food, definitely some of the best in NYC and worth the hype and top reviews.Got the minced chicken dish and the more unique pad Thai dish (the one in the netting). The minced dish was so spicy but so good, with string beans, a delicious fried egg, and white rice. It was balanced out really well with the more mild pad Thai with shrimp, big chunks of cilantro, and such freshness in the sauce. The pad Thai I'd definitely get again, and will come back and try other dishes. 5 stars!!!!

If you want a top-notch dining experience, try out Il Mulino's newest location in the Gramercy area. This restaurant fits super well with the other popular spots in the vicinity (i.e. Gramercy Tavern, Sugarfish). Came for Restaurant Week and was not disappointed in slightest. Was greeted by the maître d with a handshake which was a nice touch. He checked in on me and my friend a couple of times which was nice. Ordered the tuna tartare to start, really good taste. Had the Chicken Parmigiana for my entree, unreal, see my photo below for size reference, took up the entire plate had to take half home with me for dinner tonight. For dessert I had the flourless chocolate cake. We added a wine pairing and to be honest, I was blown away by the entire experience. Really delicious place!

Okay wow. I've never had mock duck before and I'm not a vegetarian but this mock duck was out of this world amazing. It was flavorful and had a great texture, it was crispy and fresh, I will strictly be ordering it on all dishes from now on, cannot over hype it. The pad Thai was also very good on its own, the papaya salad was fresh and spicy, I would warn if you can't do spice well most dishes are pretty spicy but I've tried close to 7 different things here and everything is really good.

Pig + Khao presents an inviting option on the Lower East Side for diners with a penchant for pork and the fiery flavors of Southeast Asia, all served up in a decidedly hipster ambiance that mirrors a bustling Bangkok locale sans the frills of fancy decor. The scene is set to a lively hip-hop and R&B soundtrack, and while service is on point in speed and attentiveness, it lacks a touch of warmth. 

Arriving later in the evening may mean missing out on coveted dishes like their fried chicken, and you might feel a subtle nudge towards the door as they close up shop. When it comes to the menu, the whole fried fish is a standout feast paired with a delectable curry, albeit requiring some effort to navigate through the bones. The small plates impress, with the tangy green papaya salad and the savory pad cheong see ew, featuring pork belly and rolled noodles, shining in particular. The coconut rice is a simple yet exceptional side that shouldn't be overlooked. However, the BBQ sauce for the ribs doesn't quite hit the mark, and the pata plate is lackluster. The three flavor prawns are passable, but not exceptional.

Cocktail aficionados won't be disappointed, with the pigroni and Rum and Hyde being particularly noteworthy. For a perfect end to the date night, consider a post-dinner drink at the nearby speakeasy Garfunkle's, which promises to round out the experience with finesse. Pig + Khao is a spot that mostly delights, especially if pork and spice are your dining companions of choice.

WOW this place is amazing! If you want authentic Chinese dumplings and hand-pulled noodles, this place is the place to be! It's SOOO fresh and really cheap too! 8 dumplings is about $4 and noodles are around $6-9. Of course, it's in Chinatown. Also, you can buy 50 frozen dumplings you can take home for $12. If you want veggie dumplings, it'll cost you $20. It's sooooo worth it and I'll definitely come back.

Title: A Meat Lover's Surprise at SEASON!

As a dedicated carnivore, venturing into SEASON, a vegan restaurant, was a step outside my comfort zone - but one that I am now thrilled to have taken. Initially there to support my vegan friends, I was blown away by the mouthwatering flavors that had me forgetting about meat entirely.

From the pizza quesadillas bursting with melty goodness to the decadent Mac and cheese, and the soy fish that had me doing a double-take, every dish was a hit. The hummus? A creamy delight that perfectly embodied the restaurant's namesake, SEASON, with its well-balanced seasoning.

The atmosphere complemented the food with its vibrant and welcoming vibe. The service was personal, making us feel right at home. And the cherry on top: supporting a fantastic black-owned business.

SEASON impressed this meat-lover so much that a return visit isn't just an option - it's a must. Full bellies and big smiles all around, thanks for an unforgettable experience!

During my recent visit to the restaurant, I found the cocktail offerings disappointing, as their sweetness was overwhelming and not justified by the price point. Comparable bars in Manhattan undoubtedly provide a superior experience at similar or even lower costs. The charcuterie board was a letdown, with no room for personalization and a scant variety of cheeses and meats—a couple more of each would have improved the selection considerably. The Shishito Peppers served were unremarkable. On a positive note, the ambiance of the establishment was pleasant, with an energetic and roomy atmosphere.

I love this deli. I work in the area and have tried a number of places for salads. This place is definitely my number one. Places like chopt always skimp on fillings. Lenwich salads are packed with toppings. The meat is quality, veggies fresh, dressings tasty. Prices are right too. Delivery can get expensive but pickup is very reasonable. Their egg breakfast sandwich is no frills but great and only 2.75 (slightly more for fillings)

Got into the city late last night and was starving. Saw this spot pop up on my Yelp and it was a short walk from my hotel. It was the perfect place for me. 4 minute walk, quick service, no wait, and delicious food. I walked right in and got sat right away. Didn't need to see the menu, as my go to is tonkotsu. My bowl arrived within a few minutes. The broth was great! I didn't love the noodles, but they weren't the worst I've ever had. The pork wasn't too flavorful but when I added sauces it was good. On the table is a small dish of sauces. The Fried garlic and onion is awesome and I found myself continuing to add spoonfuls into my soup. Great spot!!

The grilled cheese was ok, though a bit too greasy.  The employees were very pleasant and friendly.  Our food was prepared promptly and accurately.  The soda station was clean and well stocked.  This place is great for a pre-show lunch or dinner, as it is quick and convenient.  However, it does not provide a significant variety of extras to put in to the sandwich.  Also, the web site shows more items which were not available in store.I would come back.The store was clean and well maintained.

Was expecting more after seeing the yelp score.  The food is definitely good, but I didn't think it was better than other restaurants with kebabs.  I had the chicken Adana, which I'd get again; the lentil soup, which I would not get again (purée with no solid lentils, and had a sort of buttery taste that i didn't like), and fries which did not transport home very well.  They had a nice outdoor seating area.  If I'm craving kebabs, and in the area, I'd come back, but I wouldn't go out of my way to return.

During a recent lunch outing with a friend, we decided to stop in at this delightful eatery that boasted a unique menu not found in her hometown. We were promptly seated upon arrival, and the service was warm and attentive throughout our stay. The food, to our pleasant surprise, was quite tasty, surpassing our expectations. A great spot for a satisfying midday meal!

Title: A Cozy Ramen Retreat in the Heart of NYC

As I pen my 1000th review, it seems fitting that it's for a place that made me feel right at home in the bustling city of New York. Ajisen Ramen, a chain that still manages to attract a local crowd, served as a delicious sanctuary just steps from our hotel, warranting not one but two visits.

Our first encounter was a quest for comfort following a thunderstorm, and Ajisen didn't disappoint. Welcomed warmly and ushered into the relief of well-cooled interiors, we embarked on a culinary delight. My choice, the Ajisen Deluxe Ramen, boasted perfectly tender chasu and pork rib in a broth that hit all the right notes – flavorful yet not a salt assault. The Tatsuta Age – crispy fried chicken with a tangy sweet pepper sauce – was an addictive side that I couldn't resist dunking into my ramen.

My dining companion, Daveed, gave the Chicken Katsu Curry his nod of approval, praising its balance and execution. On our second visit, we started with gyoza and Ajisen pork buns. Both were tasty, though a warmer bun would have been preferred. The Tom Yum Chicken Ramen with extra noodles and pork belly was a highlight for me – a spicy, zesty bowl that left me craving another visit. Daveed's Chicken Teriyaki boasted fresh, crisp veggies, although the sauce leaned towards the sweeter side for his palate.

Ajisen Ramen stood out as an unpretentious spot that provided us with not just meals but experiences to remember. Karlene's exceptional service only amplified the comfort and delight of our visits. It's places like this that remind you home isn't just where you live, but where you're welcomed. Till next time, Ajisen, and thank you for being a highlight of NYC!

Title: Middle-of-the-Road Japanese Fare

My recent dining experience at [Restaurant Name] was a classic case of "not great, not terrible." Lured in by a shorter wait time compared to its bustling neighbor, Hagi, this eatery's tranquility should have been the first clue to manage our expectations.

Our culinary journey peaked with the mushroom ramen, a bowl brimming with umami goodness that stood out as the highlight. The Ikura Don was passable but disproportionately rice-heavy, leaving us craving more of what should have been the star ingredient.

The Salmon sashimi mini don raised a red flag with its lackluster hue, suggesting a dip in freshness that was hard to ignore. Our adventurous choice, the Daikon Pork Belly, intrigued us on paper but delivered a puzzling taste and an off-putting fat-to-meat ratio.

The succinct menu, while a nod to simplicity, felt scattered and lacked the cohesion and authenticity one yearns for in a Japanese dining experience. All in all, it seems we might have just made the wrong selections, but it's uncertain if the right ones existed at all. This was a meal that will be remembered more for its convenience than its cuisine.

Title: Cozy Delights at Hak Box

I had the pleasure of dining at Hak Box and while the menu is concise, it's a gem for those who adore authentic, no-frills food. For a mere $11, you can indulge in all three offerings: rice noodle rolls, stuffed tofu, and dumplings. Each dish stands out, but the rice noodle rolls steal the show. These are not your typical cheong fun; they are heartier with a satisfying chew, generously filled with salted pork and dried shrimp, and finished with a fragrant scallion-oil dressing. Hak Box delivers an incredibly savory and substantial experience, capturing the essence of traditional Hakka cuisine.

Loved everything about it. My friend Erika is "the happiest customer" they've ever had. So cheerful and full of joy, so the Manager made sure we got a couple rounds of Prosecco on the house. We had so much food and such great service. Carlos was fantastic and we loved him! My favorite thing was the brown butter asparagus, and then scooping up the remaining brown butter with the bread. Oh yum.  This was my former boss's favorite restaurant when I lived in the city, and I never got to dine here until now. Man, I missed out. I haven't laughed so hard and eaten so well in a long time. What a wonderful evening with girlfriends at a beautiful venue in the village. Thanks to Il Cantinori, I am now missing New York more than ever before.

Title: Super Saiyan Delights at a Cozy NYC Noodle Spot

As autumn painted NYC in hues of orange and gold, my companions and I found ourselves craving a ramen adventure. Our party of eight descended upon this charmingly petite eatery just as the clock neared noon. To our delight, we were seated without delay in a space small in size but ample in hospitality.

The restaurant, an homage to the iconic anime Dragon Ball Z, enveloped us in its unique theme. The walls boasted vibrant tributes, including a striking neon light rendition of Goku, which added a playful flair to the setting.

Our gastronomic quest began with Takoyaki, priced at a reasonable $8. The dish arrived with four exquisitely fried octopus balls adorned with a tantalizing drizzle that teased the taste buds with every bite.

The main act, Spicy Tonkotsu Ramen for $15, proved to be the star of the show. The broth was a testament to flavor, boasting a richness and creaminess that enveloped the senses. The heat was present, yet not overwhelming, creating a perfect balance for those who favor a gentler spice. Accompanied by succulent pork, each spoonful was a testament to ramen craftsmanship.

Our experience was underpinned by swift and efficient service, ensuring that our hearty meal was enjoyed without undue waiting.

In summary, if you're in NYC and find yourself in the grips of a ramen yearning, consider this Dragon Ball Z-inspired nook for a satisfying and speedy dining experience.

Title: Generous Portions at Trading Post - A Mixed Culinary Experience

After completing a 5k race on a balmy summer day, my visit to the Trading Post seemed like the perfect reward. Choosing an outdoor seat allowed for a delightful combination of dining and people-watching, which was an absolute treat.

My cravings for both savory and sweet were on high alert, but I didn't anticipate the generous portion sizes that the Trading Post served up. The heaping potatoes were surprisingly filling – a true testament to the establishment's hearty servings. The scrambled eggs were flavorsome and well-prepared.

However, the french toast didn't quite hit the mark. Anticipating a crispy exterior, I was met with a disappointingly soggy counterpart, which was a letdown amidst the otherwise enjoyable meal. This minor hiccup meant that despite my best efforts, a significant amount of food remained untouched.

On the service front, the staff was both prompt and cordial, ensuring a pleasant experience from a customer care perspective.

In summary, if you find yourself famished and in the mood for ample helpings, Trading Post might just be your go-to. Just be mindful of their overzealous portions and steer clear of the french toast if you prefer a crunch in your bite.

When you travel this far uptown, it's hard to find food that is not too overpriced yet still tastes good. While the food here is pretty overpriced, it tasted good!My friend and I chose this place mainly for the Pork with Kimchi Xiao Long Bao ($10). The dumpling skin here was different, as they were the same thin, translucent, skin you would often see used at dim sum parlors. The kimchi taste sadly wasn't prominent, but you could still taste bits of cabbage. Plus, the dumpling had a spicy kick to it! I'm not a fan of the spoon container the dipping sauce was placed in as it was hard to pour inside the soup dumpling.  We also ordered the Beef Scallion Pancake Wrap ($11). Compared to other places, the dough was thicker but not as fried. My friend compared this to Peking Duck and it's true, especially with the meat, cucumber, and scallion ingredients. Lastly, for our entree we had the Snow Cabbage Pork Noodle Soup. The soup honestly tasted like something a beginner chef like me can make at home, with similar rice noodles I have back home, some cabbage, and some pork. But the soup tasted amazing on a cold winter day so I really enjoyed it! The portion size was a lot smaller than I thought, but everything tasted really homey and comforting. I also liked that the people spoke Canto here! This place was quite the venture from subway stops, so I won't be coming back but I did enjoy my meal that day!

I recently visited this charming restaurant and was thoroughly impressed by its delightful interior design, which added to the cozy ambiance. The establishment offers an excellent happy hour with fantastic prices that are hard to beat. The menu boasts a variety of appealing options, ensuring there's something for everyone. Both the service and food met our expectations, leaving us with no complaints. Overall, this place has quickly become one of my favorites, and I highly recommend it for a satisfying dining experience.

I recently had breakfast at a conveniently located eatery close to my hotel, and I'm pleased to report that my experience was largely positive. Seating was prompt upon arrival, and the service was impressively swift, with our order arriving in no time. The waiter who attended to us was amiable and the cleanliness of the place didn't go unnoticed.

My only gripe was with the cashier, who I believe might be the owner or manager; her demeanor could best be described as ungracious, almost as if our patronage was a burden to her. However, this did not dampen the overall experience too much as the food was quite satisfying. Despite this hiccup, the quality of the meal would prompt me to give this restaurant another visit in the future.

Tucked away on the Concourse level of Rockefeller Center, this contemporary Korean-themed takeaway spot is a delightful find. With a well-curated menu featuring premade dishes, you have the convenience to either grab a quick bite at the available seating or take your meal to go. The standout options I've sampled, the sweet and spicy chicken bowl and the spicy pork bowl, were both flavorful and satisfying, with reasonable price tags of $10 and $14, respectively—quite fair for the upscale location. They also offer a selection of frozen items like dumplings and bulgogi for home cooking enjoyment. The service was speedy and efficient, enhancing the overall experience. I'm looking forward to returning and exploring more of what they have to offer. Definitely a solid lunch choice in the area.

Wow!  All I can say is, how we have not been to this restaurant before is unbelievable!  I'm sooooo happy to have found this amazing establishment and go back for dinner!  We have been missing out!  We had brunch here on Easter weekend and I have to say everything was unbelievably delicious!  I know I have said before but this time I really really really mean it!!  We will be dreaming about that bacon for eternity.  What do they do to it to make it perfection, a bacon masterpiece is what it is.  Light crisp tasty perfection.  The Irish sausage links were outstanding!  When you bite into it there's a snap and nice exterior crunch and then the soft seasoned center...drool.  I had the Canadian eggs Benedict and my husband had the Smoked Salmon Benedict.  He couldn't even speak while eating, just moaning.  This place is soooo good!  You have to go if you haven't been, run there!  Get that bacon!  As for the atmosphere, it soooo big with these grandiose ceilings and Victorian decor but at the same time feels very warm and cozy.  Just love it!  Can't wait to come back!!!!

Title: Unique Artichoke Pizza Experience at [Restaurant Name]

My visit to [Restaurant Name] was highlighted by their distinctive artichoke pizza, which reminded me of dipping breadsticks into a creamy spinach artichoke dip - an innovative take on traditional pizza. Regrettably, the salt level was overpowering during my visit, overshadowing the potential of the artichoke and spinach flavor combination; my partner concurred on this point. Friends have mentioned this isn't the usual case, so it may have been an off day in the kitchen.

On a positive note, the pizza's heartiness is undeniable, with each slice being quite filling. Expect to share or save some for later due to its dense nature.

Service was a high point, with exceptional attention from our server who was both friendly and accommodating. The experience was memorable, and had the pizza been seasoned more carefully, it could have been outstanding.

Rating: Food 3/5, Service 5/5. Would return for a second tasting, hoping for a lighter hand with the salt.

Title: A Hyped Spot with Room for Improvement

After hearing raves about this trendy spot, curiosity got the best of me and I decided to check it out at 9pm, ending up at the bar due to the full house. Commendable right off the bat was the staff's willingness to check in my cumbersome tennis bag.

Kicking things off, the Spicy Rice Cakes ($13) delivered a substantial kick – a tad surprising yet enjoyable. Moving on to the main event, my Smoked Pork Ramen ($18) was a letdown; one lone slice of pork belly hardly justified the price. The noodles, though unique in texture, didn't surpass past experiences. Toppings were scant, with just an egg yolk, a couple of bamboo shoots, and some greens. My girlfriend's Spicy Beef Ramen fared slightly better with two robust pieces of brisket, but still suffered from the same sparse garnish issue.

Despite the buzz, the ramen failed to impress, especially given the more generous and flavorful options available across the city for less. Credit where due, the service shone through as a highlight of the evening. However, for ramen enthusiasts seeking value and abundance, this spot may not hit the mark.

I visited this restaurant for lunch with a friend, drawn in by its high Yelp ratings and the promise of exceptional ramen. The service we received was commendable; however, the miso pork ramen I ordered failed to live up to expectations. It was disappointingly average and, quite frankly, bland. Despite my efforts to enhance the taste with an ample amount of hot garlic topping, the ramen didn't impress. Given the abundance of superior ramen choices in the city, I'm inclined to explore elsewhere rather than return.

I love the ambiance at Trinity Place. Having lunch in a former bank vault turned out to be so coo!l Thankfully, my girlfriend suggested I walk to the bathroom in the back just to take in the entire place. There is actually another vault in the back! I took pictures. But, on to the food...I had the Wagyu cheeseburger, which was as juicy and delicious as you would expect from wagyu beef. Juices were running down my hand, which is the sign of a great burger. I do wish I had a better toasted bun. The sides were home fries and a salad. They were just OK. The hostess was kind enough to step in for the otherwise lackluster service, which I appreciated. I'll definitely go back sometime for drinks and dinner.

Title: An Alfresco Gem at Blockheads - Perfect for Groups

I recently revisited Blockheads for an outdoor lunch with my coworkers, and it's safe to say, this spot is an absolute gem! Tucked away just blocks from my office, it's the ideal chill and affordable destination for larger groups, which is a rarity in the area.

Despite some scaffolding present in the plaza, it didn't dampen our experience away from it. Our group of seven basked in great service under the open sky, accompanied by perfectly cooked meals and deceptively strong drinks.

The Grilled Fish Bowl with Brown Rice drenched in Carrot Ginger sauce caught my taste buds by surprise – fresh ingredients and a sauce that brought it all home. Plus, scoring this delight off the special lunch menu for just over $10 was a steal!

The Frozen Black Flower, a potent blend of frozen margarita and sangria, was the highlight drink. It's size belies its strength, and at $8, it was a total bargain.

All in all, for roughly $20 per person, inclusive of gratuity, my team indulged in a fantastic meal with refreshing drinks in ideal weather. My verdict: Blockheads is a must-visit for an unbeatable lunch experience. Two thumbs up for this establishment!

Delightfully delicious sums up my dining experience! The dishes here are wonderfully cumin-forward, enhancing the flavors without overpowering them. The lamb is the undeniable highlight, stealing the show with its tenderness and taste. Equally noteworthy is the generously served chicken dish, packed with flavor yet pleasantly mild in spice. For an undeniable treat, try the lamb shumai – their tenderness and juiciness are exceptional and deserve a high recommendation. Lastly, the sautéed rice noodles are simply the bomb; an unmissable side that completes a truly satisfying meal.

It was decent. I've never had mind blowing dim sum. I thought the food was alright but nothing stood out to me. I don't think I'll be back again. The selection of foods was limited and I didn't see many noodle or rice dishes. The dessert cart was disappointing. I was looking forward to some really good dim sum but it was just the ordinary. I also thought it was pricey or what it was. Each dish was $4, some worth it some not so much.The peking duck and chicken feet were my favorite. Everything else was meh. I was here on a holiday for lunch but I didn't have to wait to be seated. The place is huge and lots of seating. The tea is great and they charge $1 a person so don't be too surprised when you get the bill.

I recently tried fresh New York Pizza for the first time and was pleasantly surprised. The two slices I had were tasty and left me curious to explore more. Most importantly, it was good value for money. I'm looking forward to coming back for another round!

I recently stumbled upon a gem in East Village, where the ambiance immediately struck a chord with its charming decor and inviting coziness. The culinary experience matched the setting, as both the food and drinks tantalized the taste buds with flavors that were both delightful and generously portioned, ensuring great value for the price. Adding to the charm was the staff's warmth and hospitality, highlighted by the owner who took the time for a pleasant chat, making us feel right at home. This is one spot I'm excited to frequent in the future.

In a neighborhood cluttered with chain pizza options, it's refreshing to find a legitimate slice of New York at this Washington Heights gem. When you call, expect attentive service that ensures your order is taken and prepared with impressive speed—ready in just 10 minutes.

3 Star Pizza may be unassuming but don’t let that fool you; they serve up reliable NY-style pizza with a delectably thin crust and generous, quality cheese topping. The sauce is decent, though not the standout. What truly sets them apart is the level of customer service. The staff here is exceptionally courteous and efficient, which makes the experience all the more pleasant.

If you’re looking for a quick pizza fix that delivers on taste and convenience, 3 Star Pizza is the way to go. Good food combined with their dedication to customer satisfaction earns them an overall solid rating. The pizza itself is a solid three stars, but the extra care from the staff certainly adds to the appeal, tipping them into a four-star experience.

Title: A Fresh Take on Omakase – A Must-Visit Newcomer

Review:

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a newly opened omakase restaurant that has set a new bar for my sushi experiences – and it's only been open for three days! The offerings are mouthwatering, with a 12-piece set for $75 and a 17-piece set for $115. I indulged in the 17-piece and each bite was a testament to quality and freshness.

The ambiance of the restaurant is a testament to the care and craftsmanship that has gone into its creation. Hand-built by the chefs themselves, the décor boasts a clean, minimalist aesthetic with white and wood accents, creating a comfortable and soothing environment to enhance the dining experience.

Service was exceptional, epitomized by the warmth of the chef. Despite the language barrier, his enthusiasm for our culinary joy shone through. With an intimate setting – only four diners at the time – we enjoyed personalized interaction which made the meal all the more special.

The food was undoubtedly the highlight. Standout pieces included the wagyu uni, a hot oil-drizzled tuna, eel, and king salmon. The unique use of cubed ginger as opposed to traditional slices caught my attention, as did the proportion of rice to fish, showcasing a commendable focus on the quality of the seafood.

In conclusion, it's rare to find a place that clearly prioritizes the finer details of dining. I’m eagerly planning my next visit to bring my boyfriend and cousin. If you're looking for an omakase experience that truly stands out, this place is an unmissable gem, especially if you appreciate fine craftsmanship in both ambiance and cuisine.

This place turned out better than I thought. It was three of us. We shared the BBQ combo 1 and spicy pork soup. The meat was tender and tasty. I liked the thinly spliced beef the most. It tasted great with the garlic dipping sauce and lettuce. The waitress was very friendly. She sliced and served the meat.

3 stars. 3.5 for food, 2.5 for service. Came here on Valentines Day with some friends and I think the man at the bar was a bit overwhelmed by the impending rush because he was a bit on the rude side to my group. It was hard to get his attention to order a drink when I first walked in and there was barely anyone sitting down yet. We ordered the escargot, octopus and duck confit to share. Escargot tasted a bit fishy if that is possible.. a hard pass for me. Wasn't a fan of the bread they provided either. The octopus was better but my friend got a piece that was tough and she didn't like. Duck confit was definitely the best dish of the night..  close to a 4.5 dish but the other food brings my rating down.I don't think I would be back after my experience but the steak looked good and I would probably get that instead of my first two dishes if I had to go back.

Title: A Delightful Burger and Drink Experience at The Smith

Upon arrival at The Smith, I was greeted with a thoughtful Purell station—a nod to their social responsibility in these uncertain times. The interior boasted a charming French Bistro ambiance, bustling with energetic staff attending to a full house.

In search of a simple pleasure—a good burger and a refreshing drink—I was not disappointed. The Old Flame cocktail, a savory blend of Rye and Campari, was a delicious start to the meal.

The main star, The Smith's pub burger, was a masterclass in burger perfection. While a gourmet option was available, the standard burger with its fresh, possibly house-made bun, was an unbeatable choice. The juiciness of the perfectly blended meat patty truly made this burger shine.

A slight hiccup with the pickles' off-tasting brine was quickly forgotten after removing them, allowing for an uninterrupted burger bliss. Accompanying the meal were the French Fries—delightfully crispy and addictive, though served in a portion that could easily be shared.

For a French Bistro-meets-gastropub experience near Lincoln Center, The Smith is a worthy destination. With great food and drinks to offer, it's a solid choice for casual yet delectable dining.

Title: Fresh Pasta Haven with Room for Flavor Balance

I recently ventured into a new fast casual eatery in FiDi, intrigued by the promise of fresh pasta that could rival Eataly's offerings. The concept is straightforward and appealing: choose your pasta, pick a sauce, add a protein, and watch as it's prepared for you. 

My meal of choice was the Fettuccine Alfredo with Lemon Pepper Chicken. The portion sizes were generous, justifying the steeper price compared to a typical takeout lunch. I was presented with two hearty pieces of chicken, but unfortunately, the excessive use of thyme overpowered the delicate balance of lemon and pepper, subsequently affecting the whole dish.

That said, the pasta itself was cooked nicely, and the Alfredo sauce struck a good consistency—not too light nor too thick. While my first experience didn't entirely hit the mark due to the heavy-handed seasoning, the quality of the ingredients and the made-to-order experience suggest potential. I'm willing to return and explore more of Maestro's menu, as other reviews have hinted at a more favorable experience.

During my recent visit to the restaurant, I decided to try the Goan fish recommended by our waiter. While the fish was perfectly cooked, boasting a delightful crispy exterior with a tender interior, the accompanying curry sauce didn't quite hit the mark for me due to its coconut shreds, which imparted a curious texture and flavor that I didn't fancy. That being said, it could simply boil down to personal preference.

Service was amiable, though not the swiftest. The venue itself was comfortably spacious. On offer was an attractive pre-fixe menu for $35, encompassing an appealing selection of two appetizers, two entrees, soup, and a dessert — a potential steal I might consider on a return visit when my appetite is up to the task.

The restaurant also offers a daily lunch buffet at $17.95, which seems like a promising option to sample more of their offerings, and I'm tempted to give it a try before drawing any final conclusions about the menu. Overall, I'm open to returning and exploring more of their cuisine to see if my initial choice was merely a misstep.

Came here during restaurant week to take advantage of their dinner deal. We came on a Friday night and every table was filled, so having a reservation is a good idea. When they called to confirm they also asked about special occasions which I thought was a nice touch. The place itself is airy and spacious, with dim lighting that creates a modern, classy feel. From the pre-fixe menu ($42/person) we tried the lobster bisque, baked french onion soup, filet mignon (6 oz) with sides of broccoli and mashed potatoes, and we both opted for the hot chocolate cake ($6 upgrade). My friend felt that the lobster bisque was a little thick. However, we both enjoyed the filet mignon and the hot chocolate cake. We also split a bottle of wine, so in the end our bill was around $100/person. Overall, I can't comment on the regular prices but I think this was a very nice experience and we were very happy that Morton's was participating in the restaurant week deal.

My recent visit to what's dubbed "the first pizzeria in America" did not disappoint. Opting for a weekday lunch with my boyfriend, we faced a brief, ten-minute wait before being seated. Sharing a large margherita pizza—embellished with pepperoni and meatballs—proved a wise choice. The pizza arrived swiftly, boasting a delightfully crispy crust. The quality of the mozzarella and tomato sauce was unmistakable, and the added meats were flavorful. Certainly amongst the best pizza experiences I've had. Be warned, though; it comes at a premium. Our meal, pizza, and two sodas totaled nearly $50. Those willing to splurge, I recommend visiting for an exceptional pizza treat.

I recently dined at this charming Italian eatery and was thoroughly enchanted by the experience. The ambiance is tranquil and inviting, ideal for those seeking a quiet dining atmosphere. With the option for al fresco dining, I can imagine summer evenings here being particularly delightful.

Upon entry, the choice of water—still, sparkling, or otherwise—was a considerate touch. The extensive menu promised something for every palate. We opted for the walnut and arugula salad to start, which was perfectly portioned for two.

Our mains included linguini alle vongole and sea scallops in cream. The linguini featured a generous clam-to-pasta ratio and was bursting with flavor, though a lighter hand on the white wine sauce wouldn't have gone amiss. The scallops were sumptuous, albeit rich, but expertly cooked to avoid any hint of toughness.

A shared cannoli capped off our meal, its size just right for sharing, and paired with coffee that was notably robust—a surefire remedy to any indulgence-induced drowsiness.

All in all, this restaurant is a gem that offers a satisfying Italian feast and is undoubtedly worth a visit.

Title: A Campy, Gay-Friendly Gem with Hearty Entertainment

My visits to this vibrant spot were as delightful as they were memorable. Embracing its campy, touristy vibe with open arms, it's a haven for someone like me who enjoys a good dose of fun with their meal. Despite the ever-present queue, service is swift, ensuring you're seated before you know it.

Breakfast-goers should note the menu's heavy reliance on eggs, not the best for vegans or those with allergies. I returned for dinner and indulged in a burger, which was satisfactory but didn't steal the culinary spotlight.

What truly sets this place apart is the entertainment. The servers double as talented vocalists, serenading diners with Broadway tunes and creating a joyous atmosphere. Although the food may not be the main highlight, it's the whole experience that counts here.

For a night of unabashed gaiety and charming performances, this is the spot. Just remember to show your appreciation with generous tips – the performers deserve it!

Title: A Slice of Heaven at My Favorite Pizza Haven

If you're a pizza aficionado like me, finding the perfect pizza joint is a quest of epic proportions. Well, fellow epicureans, it seems I've stumbled upon a treasure! This delightful pizzeria has quickly become my go-to spot for a hot slice.

Their brick oven pizzas are simply divine. Each pie emerges with a crust that's the epitome of perfection—undeniably crunchy and oh-so-satisfying. Among the variety I've savored, two have captured my heart and taste buds: the earthy Funghi and the sublime Caprina. The latter boasts an intricate meld of honey, figs, and pear, balanced by peppery arugula and the creamy bliss of goat cheese. It's a flavor ballet in each bite.

For starters, do yourself a favor and dive into their calamari—crispy and addicting. For those leaning towards plant-based delicacies, the balsamic sautéed portobello mushrooms are a meaty vegan marvel.

The dessert spectacle is a clever ploy—seeing all the luscious options paraded on a plate would tempt a saint, but I managed restraint. The tiramisu, however, is non-negotiable. Generous in size and rich in espresso and rum aromas, it's the crowning joy of an already indulgent meal. Don't leave without it!

In short, this place nails it every time. For pizza lovers, it's a must-visit. Trust me, your taste buds will thank you.
My favorite dumplings in the city! I come get once a week! So fresh and flavorful. Love their monthly specials and soup so delicious.

Title: Hidden Gem for Ramen Lovers

Tucked away in a bustling multilevel complex, my latest culinary adventure led me upstairs to a welcoming, if surprisingly undercrowded, ramen haven. Immediately greeted and seated on a bustling Saturday night, the experience began on a high note.

Appetite whetted by a duo of succulent Pork Ribs—though at $10, the price did prompt a raised eyebrow—the tender, perfectly marinated morsels set the stage for the evening's main act. The Shinka Tonkotsu, a $15 bowl of ramen goodness, delivered a symphony of flavors. Each slurp from the meaty broth brought forward harmonious notes of sliced pork, scallions, and onions, all playing well with the expertly cooked noodles. Importantly, the spice was kept at bay, letting the balance of the ingredients shine through.

Service was notably snappy, a pleasure on a night out. Though a word to the wise: a trip to the restroom may feel like a trek through a labyrinth.

In summary, this spot is a solid choice for a ramen fix, particularly for those seeking a quieter dining experience.

Title: Perfect Spot for a Casual, Fresh Feast - A Must-Visit!

I recently visited this gem of a restaurant and can't recommend it enough for both friends and family outings. The place radiates a laid-back vibe, which makes it the ideal setting for any casual gathering. But don't let the relaxed atmosphere fool you – the seasonal menu is where this spot truly shines, boasting an array of dishes crafted with the freshest ingredients.

My Easter brunch experience here was exceptional, with a spread that was as delightful as it was memorable. As a fan of the Noho Hospitality Group's eateries, I'm impressed yet again. Their commitment to quality and flavor stands out.

I'm eagerly looking forward to returning soon for dinner. If you appreciate fresh, seasonal fare served in a welcoming environment, this is a must-visit on your dining list!

I've been here multiple times and always enjoyed the variety of noodle dishes and the large portions. This is a solid place to eat in the Korean food court and I'm never disappointed. I most recently ordered the yaki-udon which is placed in the stir fried noodle category. It was served in lots of spicy red sauce and had thinly shredded vegetables and hard boiled eggs on top. Be careful of what spice level you order! I ordered medium spice and definitely needed water with my meal. My friend who loves spicy food ordered the seafood pepper bomb and was overwhelmed by the spice even thought he has a high tolerance. Overall my dish was well put together and served piping hot and I would order it again. I would love to try the other dishes and will definitely come back again!

Well let me start off with Jessie, the very cute bartender here. It's a fun night out for my friends and I and she not only let us taste our drinks she also made several recommendations for us. In the end I loved my drink ! We also got a free spin that included Jell-O shots in a syringe! This is the perfect place to come with friends on a night out. The frozen sangria was  really strong and the Long Island ice tea wowwww we didn't even make it past 2 of them!

I recently visited a restaurant renowned for its dim sum selection and I was not disappointed with the variety on offer. I opted for the seafood and meat dim sum platters which presented a delectable assortment of 10 different dumplings. Each piece was skillfully prepared, bursting with flavor, and the wide range showcased the chef's versatility. My only critique would be that the dumplings were on the smaller side, which meant that they were more of a tease for the appetite than a fulfilling meal. In fact, I found myself seeking out a bowl of pho immediately after my meal to satisfy my lingering hunger. Nonetheless, for those seeking exquisite taste over portion size, this restaurant’s dim sum is a culinary delight worth experiencing.

Too salty for my taste. I agree with several of the other guests as I was surprised that they were Michelin star rated. I will say that the atmosphere, decor and food display were enticing. However, the main point for going was the food and it was disappointing. The place was packed though for a Wednesday night we waited an hour. Thank goodness they had a text system and we were in Soho to pass the time.

I recently ordered delivery from this restaurant and had a mixed experience. The Tiramisu cake was a highlight – it was chilled, creamy, and had a delightful dusting of soft powder on top, served with whipped cream and a cherry, all neatly packed without any spills. On the other hand, the Quattro Formaggi pizza with added prosciutto, at an extra $4 for merely four slices, felt overpriced and left me disappointed. While the pizza itself had good flavor and a nicely foldable crust with fresh, melted cheeses, the cost – $16.95 for a personal pizza – did not feel justified, unlike the Tiramisu which was priced reasonably at $5 and absolutely worth it. For future orders, I'd recommend opting for a pasta dish to get better value for money, and definitely don't skip on their delightful tiramisu.

One of the many "clean eating"fast food  restaurants popping up all pver the city. Basically you get a healthy lean protein and a choice of various sides of vegetables. Pretty much everything is gluten free. A good place if you're watching what you eat.

This is my go-to Vietnamese restaurant whenever I am craving pho in Chinatown. Their food is always served quick! I've never really had bad pho anywhere and especially not here. I usually ask for more lettuce for my spring rolls and the waiters are really generous with that.

Rating: 3.5 stars My friend and I entered the restaurant around 7 PM on a Sunday night. The restaurant was only half full so we were seated right away. The main thing that stood out to me as soon as I walked in though was the smell of the restaurant, it did not smell very fresh inside - slightly like a public bathroom which isn't too appetizing. Service itself was very efficient and quick though. We ordered our food pretty quickly after we were seated and got it in a good amount of time. To share we ordered: --Fried chicken (mixed combo): breading was delicious and flavor was good as well. Chicken was also juicy which I liked. Sauce worked really well. --Fried cauliflower: same breading and flavor as chicken. Cauliflower works surprisingly well as a substitute! --Beef bimbimbop: Pretty average bimbimbop, beef was good though! All in all, a fairly average Korean restaurant but a good meal.

This place is amazing! Every time we come to NYC we always come to joes for a slice(s)This is the classic New York slice! The crust is perfect not too saucy and the cheese is fantastic!Just walk up to the counter and ask for a slice you will not be disappointed! We dream of Joe's and think of Joe's when it comes to pizza, this is legitimately the best slice ever!We did a pizza food tour and this place came out on top!

Title: Form Over Flavor at Pricey Pho Spot

Walking into the restaurant, I was immediately struck by its modern and spacious interior decorated with aesthetically pleasing wood and green accents. However, the ambiance soon lost its charm when I was presented with the overly expensive menu. Hoping for a justification of the prices, I ordered the Classic Beef Pho at $9.95.

Service was commendably quick, but that was where the positives ended. Unfortunately, the broth, which boasted an 8-hour preparation time, was disappointingly mediocre and watery. The noodles deviated from the traditional soft texture, leaning towards a harder, undercooked feel that did not sit well with my palate. Moreover, the beef failed to impress, being too dry for my liking.

In summary, while the establishment makes a great first impression with its design, it falls short where it truly matters—at the table. For the premium price, one would expect a pho that surpasses or at least matches the quality of more affordable alternatives. My advice would be to bypass the fancy setting in favor of the tried-and-true pho found in local Chinatown eateries, where flavor triumphs over aesthetics and your wallet will thank you.

Title: Late-Night Empanada Heaven!

Who knew you could find a game-changing spot serving up an impressive array of empanadas at 4 am? The discovery of this gem was an absolute delight, especially with a full menu that didn't skimp on variety or punch on flavor, and all for the wallet-friendly price of $4 each.

I kept it light with just two choices - the Desayuno Colombiano and the spicy chicken. Let me be clear: these empanadas were phenomenal. I can't stress enough how perfect each one was - bursting with authentic flavor that hits all the right notes.

This spot is a must-visit, and I'm already planning my next trip to make my way through the entire menu. It's a solid 'muy excelente' from me!

Title: Fresh and Customizable Delights at Build-A-Bowl

I finally took the plunge and tried the build-your-own bowl option at this trendy spot, placing my order through Ritual. Opting to splurge a little, my total—drink included—tipped over $20, which feels justified given the high-quality ingredients.

My bowl was a hearty mix of steak and turkey meatballs; both were tender, avoiding the pitfall of dryness, with the steak being commendably thick and tasty. The sides were generally great, though the broccolini came off a tad too salty, and the charred kale could be chopped finer for easier eating. Nevertheless, the roasted cauliflower, lemon ricotta, and mashed avocado were delicious, blending well with the herbed brown rice.

The dressing was another win, especially since I had it on the side to control the amount. A minor hiccup occurred when they ran out of coconut water, but the staff offered a different drink on the house—I'll need to check the bill to make sure they didn't charge me, though.

All in all, the experience has left me eager to return and explore more of the menu's possibilities.

This place is finger licking good! Whenever I'm in the mood for seafood boil this place always hits the spot and I'm never disappointed. They have a pretty big menu of mostly seafood items so if you're allergic to shellfish, this place is not for you. You get to pick what seafood you want and what sauce you want and they cook everything and serve it inside a bag. Honestly the special sauce which is everything is the absolute best. (similar to The boiling crab whole shebang sauce in cali) You can chose your own spice level which is good if you go with friends who loves super spicy and you don't so you get your own bag. I usually go for their shrimp and skip the heavy items like clams and crabs. Their appetizers are also very good. I love their codfish basket and calamari. The service is quick and the staff was friendly. My friend was almost 30 min late and they never once hassled me to order. They did check on me from time to time to make sure I was ok and whether or not I needed a drink.FYI: this place is CASH ONLY and can get really packed with long wait time during prime time dinner time. To avoid the line, come early when they first open.

During an impromptu Friday evening dinner, my husband and I visited this charming eatery, which, despite a smattering of patrons, echoed tranquility. Basking in a modern yet adorable ambiance, we were immediately greeted by attentive staff, promptly providing water and menus.

Our culinary adventure tarried not, as the mango curry and cashew stir fry with tofu promptly graced our table. A slight hiccup with my rice selection was swiftly corrected, showcasing their responsive service. While the tofu in my stir fry could have been more generous, the dish itself was a delectable mélange of vegetables and flavors. My husband's mango curry was a delightful concoction with a hint of spice that appealed to our palates.

The impeccable service, characterized by kindness and diligence, complemented the gastronomic experience; our water glasses never found respite. And for Manhattan, the affordability of our meal was a pleasant surprise.

We wholeheartedly endorse this establishment for a casual dining escapade and eagerly anticipate our return.

Upon entering Lavo, the hostess was unfriendly. Luckily, our waitress, Mika made up for it with her sincere hospitality and warm welcoming. Mika was sweet and Lee was wonderful. I started off with honey roasted peach salad and the baked clams. The peach salad had arugula and stracciatella cheese with Sicilian pistachios. If you're a cheese lover, you will adore the Stracciatella cheese. It was absolutely delightful! The baked clams were lukewarm, savory and satisfying. I ordered the Negroni drink but the bartender seemed pretty overwhelmed so I settled for  a glass of Chardonnay instead. For my entree, I had the red snapper, garlic mashed potatoes and sautéed spinach. The mashed potatoes and sautéed spinach were as expected and the red snapper was flavorful but bony. Overall, I enjoyed my experience and will return again soon.

After recently visiting a highly-rated Thai restaurant in Manhattan, I feel compelled to share my mixed impressions. As a Thai food enthusiast, my expectations were high with the restaurant boasting stellar Yelp reviews. The puns in my head, like being "tongue Thai'd," reflected my excitement to dive into a culinary adventure.

Upon dining with a friend, we ordered various dishes, opting to share and sample more of what the menu offered. The decision paid off; the flavors were authentic, and the portions generous, leaving us both thoroughly satisfied with the food itself.

However, the ambiance left something to be desired. The eatery, a tiny, bustling nook, made for a less-than-relaxing experience. A Tuesday evening visit had us on a waitlist, and once seated, we found ourselves uncomfortably close to neighboring diners. Conversation was a battle against the surrounding noise, rendering any attempt at dialogue nearly futile.

In summary, if your priority is exceptional Thai cuisine and you don't mind tight spaces or high volume, this is the spot. But if ambiance and conversation are part of your dining essentials, you may want to look elsewhere.

Having enjoyed an omakase experience at domodomo previously, I ventured next door with high hopes for their happy hour specials. Unfortunately, the offerings fell short of expectations unless you're particularly fond of oysters. My friends and I shared garlic bibimbap fried rice, fried chicken, scallop risotto, and 4 handrolls. The risotto was disappointingly akin to congee, lacking in texture, although the thinly sliced scallops were passable. The fried chicken was unremarkable and insufficiently crispy, and while the garlic fried rice was satisfactory, it wasn't a standout. It was the handrolls—particularly the tuna and salmon—that came to the rescue, showcasing the restaurant's strength in raw dishes. Though the cooked items were a letdown, these fresh and flavorful handrolls nudged my review up to a generous three stars. In a city rife with superior happy hour choices, domodomo shines for its raw fare but proves underwhelming for its kitchen-cooked dishes.

My favorite place for katsu in NYC. The restaurant is bright and clean, and food comes out very quickly. The unfussy ambience and affordability makes Tonkatsu Matsunoya the perfect place for a quick, casual bite or a catchup with friends.My favorite order is the classic pork loin cutlet (S1) gozen set, which comes with rice, potato salad, cabbage, and their pork soup. Honestly, this one set meal is enough food to share between two people with smaller appetites. The meat is juicy and not too oily, despite the perfectly crisp exterior. I also love their homemade salad dressing for the cabbage and use it very unsparingly! The pork soup is also lowkey the favorite part of the meal - it's flavored lightly with miso and is very hearty. There's plenty of pork, carrots, and konnyaku. Food at Matsunoya is a great deal, especially in the Midtown area.

I had a hankering for thai food today. I decided to try this out today. The food was completely bland and boring, there was no spicyness whatsoever in any of my dishes and not much flavor. I asked for extra spicy for both of them, on a scale of 1-5 with 5 being the most, this was a 0.9. The staff was friendly, but the food was not there. It was very generic tasting. There was not alot of seating there either, which was annoying. Overall, i'm not gonna bother with this place again. For papaya salad, tom yum soup, rice noodles and thai ice tea it came out to be $23.

Came here on a rainy Friday night. It was pretty full inside which was a plus! I imagined it to be small inside but there is also a section in the back, and the bar in the front. The first things we ordered were the Bloody Mary and the Spicy Pomegranate margarita. For $12 they don't skimp on the booze or the cups! The glass was giant size, like a water cup.Food: we had ordered the burrata and the steak. Both were so good! The burrata had a fig reduction dressing, arugula and balsamic. Everything was super tasty. I'd definitely like to come back during the week when they have their specials.

I had been wanting to try E-Mo for a while so I picked some up for dinner one night since I was in the area. I ordered the spicy tuna, beef, and squid rolls. The spicy tuna and beef were good, but the squid was kind of meh. It definitely tastes a lot better than the kimbap over at Woorijip. Each roll is about $8 but they're pretty big/filling. The three rolls were shared amongst two people and it was more than enough. I think one roll per person is enough if you don't want to be too stuffed. Tip - cash only

I come here frequently after a long day in city and I personally always had a great meal here. I recommend the Galbi Tang (short rib soup) and the Seafood Udon. Their sides are okay (some I prefer more than others) but decent. The tables are too close together so you're within 2 feet of another table. Otherwise, I don't have any complaints when I come here!

Title: Mixed Experiences at a Family-Style Eatery

My party of four arrived at the restaurant at 8 PM to find it surprisingly empty, yet it did not translate into swift service. We endured a 15-minute oversight by the host before being acknowledged, followed by a needless 10-minute wait, despite the availability of tables.

Once seated, we found the restaurant uncomfortably warm, with poor air circulation deterring from the ambience. Service, while friendly, continued the trend of delays, as ordering was not immediate.

The food, however, was generously portioned—a family-style baratta and pasta alongside an individual chicken parmigiana provided more than enough for our group, with leftovers to spare. The chicken parm stood out with its tender and spicy profile, while the carbonara's flavor was satisfactory, with well-cooked pasta.

In summary, while the food was decent and ample, the initial service missteps and lack of a comfortable environment were notable detractors from the overall experience.

Title: A Burger Worth the Buzz in the Bustling Heart of NYC

Stepping into this buzzing NYC eatery, it's clear why the burger has earned its stellar reputation. Indeed, the cheeseburger satisfies the deepest of cravings – simple, impeccably sized, and delivering on taste. The patty strikes the perfect balance: tender, juicy, and flawlessly seasoned, without a hint of unpleasant grease. Requested medium-rare, it arrives exactly as such, a testament to the kitchen's precision.

On the flip side, the wallet feels the weight, and the cash-only policy might deter the card-reliant diner. Though the chili commands a premium price, the generous meat content and complete garnish array justify the spend, serving as an excellent companion to the delectable cottage fries.

Service is streamlined, ensuring a minimal wait before you dive into your meal. However, the cramped quarters may not cater to all, as the level of noise often escalates, sometimes forcing you into the midst of others’ chatter.

While the ambiance may fall short, the burger experience alone – mouthwatering and memorable – will lure you back for more.

Not my favorite sushi place for omakase. Yes the price is much more agreeable at $33 for the lunch menu Trust me selection, but the sushi was nothing remarkable. It wasn't a melt in your mouth kinda sushi. The sushi rice also broke apart very easily.... pretty sure that's not what was supposed to happen. Service was great and the waiters were attentive. But I think I'd just prefer to pay more money for better quality sushi.

Solid food, but sparse service and food prep issues spotted.49 Monroe was not an easy place to review. I was torn. On the one hand, the food was flavorful, but on the other hand we ran into service and food preparation issues that couldn't be ignored.We came here as a group of six for a 7:30pm reservation on a Friday evening. To my surprise, the restaurant was still relatively empty with just a few customers at the bar when we arrived. First, the restaurant can be challenging to find because 1) it's located in an obscure location of Chinatown near the FDR Drive and 2) there's not one sign on the outside of the restaurant with their name on it. I might have missed the sign and, if I did, it's because it wasn't visible. The only reason we found the restaurant was because it was the ONLY restaurant on the block. It was definitely off the beaten path that even locals probably don't go to.Once inside, the darkness of the restaurant surrounded us. Lighting could have been a little better, but I guess they are going for a more intimate setting with the younger crowd. I couldn't make out much of the décor, but it had a park slope, hipster feel to it. We were led to a table upstairs that was isolated and literally all by itself. At first, I thought "Perfect!" because we had the small space to ourselves, but then it quickly hit me that service could very well be spotty because in order to reach us the waiters would have to walk up the stairs that only leads to our table and no one else. And my worst fears came true, but more on that later.So, the food. Since we had a small group, we took full advantage of the fact that we had numbers and got in a good spread to share family style. Here's a quick rundown of our order:PATATAS BRAVAS - Really good, addictive mini fried dish potatoes. A solid starter that was really boosted by the spicy mayo included. BURRATA - So simple, but so good. I'd expect nothing less from a good burrata cheese.STEAMED MUSSELS - The mussels were a bit smaller than expected, but flavor wise it was good. If there is any leftover sauce, ask for more bread to soak it up.FRENCH FRIES - It was advertised as truffle fries with shaved parmesan, but neither were on the fries. It was just plain old frites. The frites were fresh, but was nothing more than plain frites.GARLIC SHRIMP - Lots of butter and garlic flavor and delicious.GRILLED VEGETABLE SALAD - The most memorable part about this salad was the pieces of goat cheese that were wrapped in breading like cheese sticks. Mmm mmmmm. If you love cheese, the goat cheese will satisfy those taste buds.ESCARGOT - I have yet to ever try a bad escargot and this was no different. Like the mussels, if you have leftover oils, ask for more bread to soak it up.MEAT PLATTER - Nothing fancy here. A few slices of salami here. A few slices of salami there, plus some grapes and nuts. Not something I would typically order, but our table wanted it.LASAGNA - The order arrived as a medium sized square slice. It was really good and tasty, but I feel the slice could have been a bit bigger.SEAFOOD PAELLA FOR TWO - OK, I've saved the best for last. First, the order was huge and there was a lot of rice. Although it was a paella for 2, it could have easily fed 3. There was lots of flavor in it and it was tasty, but unfortunately the rice was a little under-cooked. A few more minutes on the stove would have helped. In addition, about 1/3 of the way through the dish, we found a long hair and we stopped there. Honestly, it happens, but a quality check wouldn't have hurt, so that was a disappointment.As for the service, as I feared, since we were seated at the isolated table on the 2nd floor, we were basically neglected for a majority of the evening after our appetizers arrives. Surprisingly, all of our appetizers came out blazingly fast and fresh-tasting. Typically, when food arrives quickly, it's a warning sign as to whether it was pre-prepped, but all of the appetizers were good. However, from the moment our last appetizer hit the table to the moment we received the lasagna and paella, it took about 1 hour. Yes, 1 hour between dishes. The restaurant didn't get fully crowded until the end of our meal, so that made it that much more puzzling. We had to inquire multiple times about the fact that we had ordered those 2 dishes and were still waiting. Once again, it was definitely attributed to our location, so I don't know what service was like on the main floor.I didn't go into our dinner with much expectations, but the meal got off to a really good start. However, it was all downhill from there - from the long wait for our entrees to the under-cooked paella with the hair. Would I still give them another try? Maybe. I hate to crucify a restaurant for mistakes like these that might not be representative of the rest of the restaurant, but they are definitely hard to overlook as it seems oversight is not tight enough at an establishment like this.

Title: A Vegan Delight in Chinatown

I recently discovered a gem in Chinatown that caters wonderfully to both vegans and vegetarians - a vegan dim sum spot that truly understands what plant-based diners crave. This place has edged out Buddha Bodai, my previous go-to, with its expansive menu that includes sushi and various entrees beyond the customary dim sum offerings.

The standout dish is undoubtedly their BBQ veg. meat, a plant-based twist on roast pork that manages to surpass the original in both tenderness and taste. My friend and I couldn't resist polishing it off promptly - it's that good.

The beef rice roll deserves an honorable mention; it's a convincing doppelgänger for its meaty counterpart and reinforces the spot as the perfect dining destination for those with dietary restrictions or preferences. Definitely a top recommendation for vegan and open-minded diners alike.

I had a lovely post-workout dinner here with a friend last night. The ambience is amazing - perfect for a date. It was on the emptier side though... maybe because it was a Tuesday evening?We shared a bottle of Cava, the smoked lamb tacos, the dip trio, and chargrilled octopus. Everything was great! The lamb tacos were super flavorful and full of meat. The octopus was yummy although I wasn't a big fan of the beans that came with it. The complimentary bread is warm and tasty. Really loved the bread - it went well with the dip trio.It IS a bit pricey for what you get but I guess that's why it's NYC. They do - however, have fantastic happy hour deals - I would come back just for that. Maybe not for a full meal with full prices though. Attentive service, and great experience overall.

My friend and I visited Supper on a Saturday night with a 5:15pm reservation. We were the first customers to the restaurant and I found the service to be slow in spite of this. We ended up ordering the sautéed broccoli, risotto Milanese and the Timely Priest Stranglers.We were served a nice complimentary bread and bean dish which was very nice and tided us until the main courses were served. Our dishes all arrived at the same time. The broccoli and risotto were nothing special unfortunately but I was very impressed by the Timely Priest Stranglers. I will be back to try more pastas for sure but probably will avoid ordering from other parts of the menu.

Dallas BBQ stands out for its convenient location right across from NYP Hospital and is a staple for my partner, who's invariably lured in by their cheddar-loaded chili and sticky wings. Personally, I'm less impressed; even the salads are overwhelming mounds of iceberg lettuce drenched in ranch.

On a positive note, their new chicken and waffles dish provided a novel experience. The savory waffles, speckled with cheese and green onion, had a distinct Belgian flavor, and the absence of syrup was hardly noticed thanks to the generous glaze on the chicken. I would suggest an improvement, though: swapping the current mix of wing, breast, and small tender for boneless tenders would make for an easier eat.

My boyfriend's choice of crab cakes ended up being more filler than seafood, reminiscent of a journey to the Maryland coast in spirit but not in taste. Maybe seafood at a BBQ joint was a misstep on our part.

If you find solace in hearty BBQ staples, Dallas BBQ could be your haven. Otherwise, if you're just tagging along with aficionados of the place, prepare to "grub and bear it."

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this establishment during Restaurant Week and was thrilled with the experience. At a mere $26, I indulged in a sumptuous meal starting with crispy fried calamari followed by a perfectly cooked 10 oz filet mignon, which was an absolute steal. Opting to elevate the meal even further, I added a succulent lobster tail for an additional $10, and it did not disappoint. The service throughout the meal was exceptional, ensuring a delightful lunch that left a lasting impression. Highly recommended!

My friends and I came here on a rainy Friday afternoon around 2pm. We went to the Color Factory prior but 2 of my friends hadn't eaten breakfast and this was close by. We got seated within 15 minutes without a reservation. Our waitress Karen was very friendly and helpful.I had split The Nozawa Trust Me with my husband. We shared it because we had breakfast and we wanted to make sure there was space for dinner. So it was a light meal for both of us but filled us enough that we didn't need to order more. Actually, they brought an extra serving of Salmon with sesame seeds and albacore to the table by mistake which they ended up giving us on the house, that helped to fill me just right. (Lowkey I felt this was birthday karma since it was my birthday that day :D)My favourite were the:crab hand rollalbacore tunasea breamthe toro hand rollI ordered an unagi outside of the prefixed selection and that was very good too.It was my very first time having nigiri. It was definitely a great experience. And would come back here again if I'm nearby the area.

Title: A Sizzling Lunch Experience at Pepper Lunch NYC

Pepper Lunch, a beloved West Coast chain, has finally graced the East Coast with its presence and I had the pleasure of visiting their NYC location for a Saturday lunch. For those seeking quick yet quality meals during the hustle-bustle workweek, this spot hits the mark.

Upon entering, I appreciated the ample seating arrangements — a wise provision for busy weekdays. I ordered their touted beef pepper rice and found a spot at the front with my numbered stand, a simple system for the staff to locate diners for food delivery.

Service was swift, and the staff were on-hand to guide the uninitiated through the interactive cooking process. The iron plate arrived piping hot, just as the warning suggested, ensuring a quick cook for my meal. For newcomers, be sure to follow the clear instructions for a mixing adventure that's both fun and essential for the dish's preparation.

Utensils and sauces are conveniently self-serve, stationed directly at the tables. The sauces, ranging in flavor from sweet to savory, are key to customizing your dish to taste; I recommend experimenting with each before dousing your meal.

The beef pepper rice, while slightly smaller than expected given the price, was satisfying and flavorful, with the high-quality meat standing out. The rice and sparse vegetables played a supporting role, enhancing the meat when mixed with the right amount of soy sauce.

Overall, Pepper Lunch offers an engaging dining experience where the joy lies in the sizzle and the act of creating a meal to your liking. The sauce selection is the hero, tying all elements together, and while the portions might leave some desiring more, the quality and speed of service provide good value. Definitely a worthwhile dining experience, especially for those seeking a quick, tasty lunch in the area.

The gnocchi is still great, but the service was so poor the second time I came here, that I'd have to deduct a star.Granted it was New Year's Eve, and they were trying to close early; however, this is still not an excuse. While the host/manager here was quite friendly, our waiter was curt and rude and extremely inattentive. He served the apps and the entreés at the same time and left no space on our little table for even dining plates. Of course, they were not prompt on clearing the plates either.Overall, just did not enjoy the vibe the second time around. Our waiter should feel lucky the gratuity was included in the bill. Sadly, I will not be rushing back here anytime soon.

Delicatessen in SoHo fails to live up to its hype, with its main allure seeming to be the crowd of beautiful people sipping on aesthetically pleasing drinks. Despite the promising ambiance, the food disappoints. An attempt at starting off with their truffle spinach and artichoke dip resulted in a battle with an unexpectedly tough crust, necessitating cutlery where chips should have sufficed. The main courses, a classic burger and their 'award-winning' chicken thigh sandwich, were unremarkable, with a fast-food chain arguably doing a better chicken sandwich. Surprisingly, the restaurant was out of sangria by early evening on a weekend, which was a letdown. Service was passable, doing what was necessary but adding no extra charm to elevate the basic dining experience.
