In a neighborhood brimming with culinary options, Delicatessen unfortunately stands out for all the wrong reasons.

Title: A Post-Show Culinary Encore

My friends and I stumbled upon a hidden gem after a show at Juilliard on a bustling Saturday night. Despite being nestled in a tourist hot spot, this restaurant offered an unexpected trifecta: reasonable prices, high-quality fare, and sincere, welcoming service. The vibe struck the perfect chord—cozy, fashionable, and unpretentious.

A spontaneous gesture from the barista—a complimentary banana while we lingered outside—promptly won us over, leading us inside to a tranquil, comfortable setting. We embarked on a gastronomic journey, sampling an array of dishes including a Banh mi sandwich, a hearty farro salad, classic bruschetta, a velvety almond milk decaf latte, a robust black coffee, and a truly gratifying eggplant parmesan.

Each dish proved to be a hit, making it impossible to shine a spotlight on just one. However, the standout for me was the exceptional almond milk latte, closely rivaled by the richly layered eggplant parm. This establishment is a testament to the fact that in the right hands, culinary excellence is not a matter of chance—and I cannot recommend it enough.

Title: Michelin Excellence at Contra

I recently dined at Contra, a gem with a Michelin star under its belt, and the experience lived up to its esteemed reputation. Securing our reservation through Resy ensured a seamless start, with our table ready upon arrival.

Contra's allure stems not only from its off-the-beaten-path location but also from its daily rotating prix-fixe menu, affordably priced at $89— a delightful surprise for the adventurous palate. The option to enhance the meal with a cheese course and wine pairing is a welcome addition.

Service was nothing short of world-class; the staff struck the perfect balance of attentiveness, informative without being overbearing, and ensured impeccable table maintenance course after course.

Every dish was a testament to Contra's Michelin accolade; in particular, the black cod and domestic wagyu sirloin stood out as profound culinary highlights. Expertly executed, these dishes combined perfect cooking technique with nuanced flavors. The desserts impressed with their lightness, steering clear of overwhelming sweetness.

My experience at Contra was exceptional, and it's certainly on my list for a return visit when I'm back in New York.

Two of my friends wanted a good restaurant so in having bookmarked this place on my Yelp list, I thought it was a good place to take them to.  The staff was super friendly but one of the things that killed it for me was that a) my friends were late, and late by a lot and b) it was the day where the temperature dropped to 29F.  The staff was apologetic but what I found out was that they planned on opening the covers (assuming with heating lamps the following week) -- my question is, if you knew that the weather was going to drop, or that it was cold, why wouldn't you want to open it for your patrons on one of the coldest days of the year?  I get that maybe it would be in storage, but it's November and common knowledge that temperatures could drop.  In addition, in having a first-come-first-serve policy, more so should you have heating lamps especially when there is no indoor waiting area possible due to space limitations.  It's hard for me to say because the food was actually really good.  BUT, given the situation above that definitely took it down.  And atmosphere, mood, settings, lighting - those all contribute to the overall experience. The space inside is very small and the acoustics make it really difficult to hear conversations with my friends.  It was also really dark and there was no separate outing so in being seated near the door, I had to eat with my coat on because I was still so cold.  Food-wise we ordered the following things:Beef Fried Rice:PROS- great quantity, easily shareable- not greasy- well seasoned: sometimes the meat can be overly salty but there was just enough flavor in the rice and the meat where it wasn't overwhelmingCONS:- noneChicken Satay Appetizer:PROS:- chicken was not overcooked, juicy- sauces were on pointCONS:- got cold so fastGarlic Fried Rice:PROS:- shareable- not greasyCONS:- not enough garlic: you can taste it but it wasn't as garlicky as I would expect garlic fried rice to be- small bowl as a side, almost like you were ordering extra rice but with garlic oil mixed in.  I don't think this is really worth it.  I've had a friend make me garlic rice from scratch and hers kicked butt with nice browned pieces of garlic in there.Mango Chicken CurryPROS:- definitely shareable quantity: enough to take home (but we also ordered a lot of dishes together to eat family style)- nice balance of the mango, vegetables, and chicken- sauce was very good, just the perfect Thai curry flavorCONS:- noneRoast Duck Udon with BasilPROS: - by far my favorite dish of the night.  Great flavors, duck came out and was super crispy, not fatty- Udon was well cooked, in the flavor of pad see ew but with udon.  It went really well with the duck meat actually.- shareable for sure: we killed this dish though.CONS:- noneOverall, while the food was good, my waiting and then eating experience really kind of sucked.  I was miserable before I got my food and because there were people going in and out and in and out, I was miserable while I was eating.  Would I come back again? Sure, the food WAS good.  But only between the months of May - October.  If it's ridiculously hot outside, I might also bypass June-August.  Unless I order delivery.  That I'm sure would be an adventure in and of itself.  Hopefully any re-visits will let me revise this review but I can't give this more than 3 stars right now sadly.

Enjoyed a nice lunch yesterday at Nick & Stef's Steakhouse which included a Braised Short Rib over Wild Mushroom Risotto as an appetizer on their $26 Restaurant Week menu. At first sight one would think the short rib was the star of the dish but the true gem was the risotto; perfectly cooked, nicely seasoned and just enough bite to the rice.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Ramen and Gelato

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Camellia, a recommendation from a fellow food enthusiast, and boy, was I in for a treat! It's not every day you find a spot that nails both ramen and gelato, but Camellia does just that.

Starting off with the salt and pepper fried chicken, I was immediately impressed. The chicken, reminiscent of popcorn chicken, was delectable and provided great value for the price. Moving on from what I expected to be a ramen experience, I opted for the salmon and rice instead. While the teriyaki sauce was a tad overwhelming for my taste, the dish overall did not disappoint.

The highlight of my visit was arguably the gelato. The hazelnut flavor was predictably outstanding, but the white rabbit stole the show with its unique sweetness. It was the perfect end to a wonderful meal.

Though I didn't get to try the ramen this time, the customizable ramen bowls have me excited for my next visit. The staff deserves a mention too—friendly and accommodating, they added to the already fantastic experience.

In summary, Camellia is a must-try. Whether you're there for the savory or the sweet, you're in for a delicious surprise. I'll definitely be coming back for more!

They have daily happy hour specials $5 from 4-8 making it an awesome deal!! Actually pretty big spot with lots of seating! Lots of indoor seating, and there's also outdoor seating as well to enjoy the weather. The food took a little while to come out, even tho it wasn't much crowded. Service was nice.As someone with no food restrictions, it's alright haha. It's not as good as real cheese or real meat - but still not bad haha Loved the bacon mushroom - it's MAGIC! I think it's way better than actual bacon. I don't know how they got the mushroom so smoky and crispy - magic! The Mac and cheese lacked flavor, was a bit disappointed. The happy hour fries were ok. The fries weren't super crispy. The toppings and sides were also ok

I recently dined at this Thai restaurant and was thoroughly impressed by the cuisine. The pork banh mi was delicious, and the chicken cashew dish became an instant favorite of mine. They offer a good selection of drinks to complement the meal as well. The unique hot air balloon-inspired ambiance adds a charming touch to the dining experience. However, there is room for improvement when it comes to service. Despite that, I would recommend this spot to anyone craving authentic Thai flavors.

On my latest visit to this establishment, which I've frequented before, I opted for my usual choice of popcorn chicken. Unfortunately, the experience fell short of expectations. Due to what appeared to be a backlog of orders, perhaps in a rush to serve patrons before a movie showing, the quality of the chicken suffered significantly. It seemed to be fried in stale oil, evidenced by the darker-than-usual breading, which carried an overpowering oily taste. This resulted in an immediate stomach ache, detracting from my movie-going experience.

While the beverages and theater facilities remained satisfactory, the food on this occasion was a disappointment, signaling that it might not be a focal point for the staff. Based on this experience, I plan to satisfy my appetite elsewhere before enjoying a film here in the future.

The food here was AMAZING! As a Midwesterner, I don't have the chance to experience traditional tapas often, but I'm so glad I was able to stop in here for lunch. We did the lunch special split among three people so we ended up having two apps, 6 tapas and dessert. The croquetas, meatballs, peppers, and patatas bravas were my personal favorites but I doubt you could go wrong with anything on the menu.The only downside was the service- our waitress brought the check before our dessert came out and we sat for about 20 minutes waiting on our churros before having to call someone over and ask if they were coming up. Other than that, an excellent lunch and I'd highly recommend.

Dining at HaSalon is an unequivocal experience that goes far beyond what one may typically anticipate from a restaurant. Dismissing the mixed reviews I encountered online, my visit on a bustling Saturday evening quickly revealed the establishment's appeal. It's paramount to book through RESY, committing fully given the steep $100 per head cancellation fee. Remember, reservations are a must.

Choosing the 9:30 PM seating was a decision well made. Although the price point for red wine starts at $19 a glass, the quality justifies the cost, setting the tone for a spend-ready evening.

Our server, Adam, was the cornerstone of our enjoyable experience. His attentive guidance through the menu, tailored by our food preferences, highlighted his invaluable presence.

Seated at the kitchen counter, we were privy to the chefs' meticulous and almost theatrical plating. The mushroom pasta was pleasing, but it was the tomatoes that truly shone – worth every cent of their seemingly extravagant price. The earthy mushroom steak was another costly but delectable choice. Yet it was the impeccably seasoned scorpion fish that stole the show, a dish I'd eagerly order on a return visit.

The atmosphere took a joyful turn as the exterior grating dropped and diners transformed the space into an impromptu dance floor. The age range of 30 to 60 added a vibrant, inclusive energy. However, those seeking to dance might prefer a table over the kitchen counter to avoid the busy passageway.

Dessert, a chocolate cake, was the only underwhelming part of the meal and in hindsight, additional wine might have been a better indulgence.

Above all, HaSalon envelops you in an environment where the staff, notably an engaging Ethiopian woman behind the counter, exudes passion and joy, further enhancing the dining escapade.

In closing, HaSalon is not just about the food – it's an immersive experience. With a total spend of about $240 for three entrees, dessert, and two glasses of wine, one should arrive ready to invest in an unforgettable evening. It's a place I undoubtedly plan to visit again.

Title: A New Take on Chang Fen at Yin Ji Chang Fen – Not Quite There Yet

As a fan of traditional dim sum-style Chang Fen, I was intrigued to try Yin Ji Chang Fen, a Guangzhou-originated restaurant chain. With its reputation for long lines, I had high expectations for their signature dish. The restaurant's decor, complete with plaques, confirmed its authentic Chinese chain roots.

I ordered the R1 (Marinated Beef & Shrimp with Chives Rice Noodle Roll) and the R8 (Fish Sliced with Chives Rice Noodle Roll), expecting an "elevated" take on the classic dish. However, the initial presentation couldn't mask the two main disappointments. Firstly, the rice crepe lacked the expected supple texture and hardened strangely as I ate, necessitating a spoon due to its loose filling – a stark departure from the traditional, chopstick-friendly experience. Moreover, the proteins within were notably underseasoned, making each bite rather plain.

While the quantity of shrimp in the R1 was generous, the watered-down sweet soy sauce was another letdown, missing the richness usually enjoyed at dim sum spots. On the positive side, service at Yin Ji Chang Fen was quick and attentive. The pricing, though reasonable at $5 to $8 per dish, did not quite align with the quality on offer.

In conclusion, Yin Ji Chang Fen presents a different style of Chang Fen that may appeal to some, particularly a younger crowd seeking a twist on the classic. As for seasoned dim sum enthusiasts, the experience might fall short of expectations. The restaurant offers other options, like congee, which might be worth exploring on a future visit.

Came here for a break from the rain. Got here just after 6pm and the restaurant was half empty. The space of the restaurant is pretty small when one was lugging a stroller and two munchkins in tow. Nevertheless the waitress was happy enough to accommodate us and placed the stroller near their working area. We sat ourselves by the kitchen. The kids enjoyed seeing the chefs making noodles and buns. The service was attentive and we promptly ordered a bowl of pork ramen with extra noodles and chicken karaage bun. The waitress and also chef pointed out the mayo is spicy jalapeño and might be too spicy. They suggested normal mayo which was good thinking! The ramen's broth was tasty especially with the miserable rain outside. It came with the standard egg, shallots, mushrooms and bamboo shoots. The bowl was $17 but I asked for extra noodles for additional $2. The chicken karaage bun was also nice and tasty. Chicken came straight out of the deep fryer and the buns itself was nice and soft. One of the nicer buns I've had. Total bill for the two ended up being $37 with tax and tip. Much better than enduring the rain outside I'd say!

I've been this place serval times and this is just ok food place to me. I am a Korean and this place food was just ok to my taste. Title: Cozy Vibes Over Value at Upper East Side Jewish Deli

I recently visited a classic Jewish deli in the Upper East Side, renowned for its cozy ambiance and friendly service. My friends and I were warmly welcomed on a Saturday morning and were allowed to linger for a leisurely 2.5 hours, which added to the relaxed experience.

However, the indulgence comes at a steep price. Expect to shell out at least $20 for a dish. While the food quality is commendable, you're paying a premium. I ordered the corned beef hash and was disappointed by the modest portion that seemed lost on the plate—a surprising contrast to the hefty price tag.

Ultimately, you're visiting for the atmosphere and excellent service rather than value for money. Keeping in mind the attentive staff, I'd rate the deli at three stars. While it won't be your choice for a hearty meal on a budget, it's a spot to consider for a pleasant hangout with a side of nostalgia.

I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant and was blown away by the quality of the meal. From the cheeses and Jamon to the succulent meats, perfectly charred grilled vegetables, flavorful shrimp, and a divine dessert, every dish was a symphony of flavors, expertly seasoned, and each bite left me in awe. Be warned, though – its popularity means you’ll need a reservation, as it stays bustling well into the evening. Despite the crowd, the attentive staff ensures a delightful dining experience. Highly recommended for a top-notch culinary adventure.

Title: High Expectations Dashed by Lackluster Experience

My anticipation was high upon entering the restaurant, but my initial encounter with staff was disappointing, to put it mildly. The welcome was far from warm; a disheveled gentleman unceremoniously directed us to our table and carelessly tossed menus upon it. His demeanor wasn't cheekily casual, it was outright offensive.

My hope for a recovery was quickly dashed by the sight of my dirty utensils, adorned with remnants of a previous meal. Opting for pizza to avoid using the fork, I found the prosciutto topping to be of average quality, not the Prosciutto di Parma I'd expect from a reputable Italian establishment.

My companions had mixed reviews of their dishes; the filet was deemed good, whereas the chicken Marsala paled in comparison to the excellence found at Fumo in Hamilton Heights.

It's unfortunate when a restaurant rides on the coattails of a bygone reputation. This experience was marred by poor service and mediocrity in both dining ware and cuisine. In this case, the establishment's fame is undeservedly keeping it afloat.

Title: An Average Noodle Affair

I popped into this spot for a late 3pm lunch and was pleased to find that their 12-4pm lunch special was still on offer, allowing for a choice between three ramen variants and four appetizers. The restaurant’s interior boasted an intriguing vibe, adorned with Naruto-style cartoon portraits, catering to a cozy seating arrangement with small tables and bar seats, of which I chose the latter.

The service was brisk and no-nonsense. I opted for the miso ramen paired with gyoza. Observing the chef's routine in the compact kitchen space, the dishes arrived timed to the second. The gyoza, though not particularly hot or crispy, had a pleasantly delicate skin with a satisfactory filling. 

When the miso ramen followed, it presented a firm noodle texture but fell short in delivering the deep umami essence I've savored at other establishments. The bowl's components - menma, perfectly soft-boiled tamago, a single slice of kamaboko, a generous sprinkle of corn, a few steamed bean sprouts, scallions, and two slices of rather dry chashu - were adequate, yet unremarkable.

In summation, this experience was a modest one; both the ramen and gyoza were passable but not exceptional. Despite some patrons' enthusiasm for the spicy Naruto ramen, my quest for a rich, flavorful spicy ramen will likely lead me to explore other venues.

Title: A Night at [Restaurant Name]: Innovative Flavors Meet High Demand

Last Saturday, my friends and I decided to experience the much-talked-about [Restaurant Name]. Expectations were high as we joined the queue right before opening time at 5:20 PM. Despite our punctuality, a missing member of our party meant a waitlist time of about 75 minutes, which is something to keep in mind for future visits.

Upon being seated at a cozy (read: slightly cramped) table for four, our waiter promptly introduced us to the menu. We kicked off with the spicy tuna crispy rice appetizer—where the 'crispy rice' turned out to be more akin to a rice cracker—topped with notably fresh and fiery tuna.

The temakis stole the show with their two-bite wonder and innovative combinations. Specifically, the salmon paired with tomato and onion cream was a delightful surprise, brilliantly complementing with sour cream and chives. In contrast, the scallop temaki was a unanimous letdown due to an overpowering wasabi flavor that masked the subtleties of the X.O sauce.

The spicy dynamite crab was an intriguing experience, with both the seaweed and crab being warmed and spicier than expected. The yellowtail scallion and other classic rolls were highly enjoyable. The service impressed, with a quick roll out of the rolls even amid the restaurant's bustling atmosphere.

One concern was the hygiene of the wooden holders for the rolls. We noticed these were collected and reused between tables without apparent cleaning, raising questions regarding cross-contamination.

Despite the minor gripes, [Restaurant Name] is worth the hype. Attempting a reservation is advisable—and requires either considerable foresight or the willingness to line up early—as the place fills up fast. I'm already planning my next visit and hoping to secure a reservation to bypass the lengthy wait.

My mom and I were here for their afternoon tea. It was a beautiful atmosphere and the staff was especially courteous with storing our luggage while we ate. We both ordered the New Yorker tea. However, I'd recommend try something new and each ordering a different one so you can try each other's! It's an amazing experience that everyone should experience at least once while visiting New York!

I have ordered from EONS for a few times and I thought it was pretty good quality greek for for lunch take out - the portion is good, the foods are fresh, and the delivery is fast.But I was really disappointed today. Ordered create your own bowl with Salmon today and not only didnt they take my special instructions, the salmon literally tastes like cardboard- it was hard, burned, and dry. The farrow and bowl rice are okay so I ate that.Even though the past experiences would deserve a 4-star but a 3-star is needed for today's food. I wish the restaurant could be a little bit more consistent and if they use this kind of quality to serve their returning customers, it's really hard for anyone to come back again.Disappointed. Hope some bad reviews can help restaurant knowing what they did badly on.

Title: Cozy Vibes with Pricy Bites at a Quaint Spot

During a casual evening out to catch the game with a light bite, we stumbled upon this charming little restaurant. The decor immediately sets a warm, inviting tone with its elegant yet understated style, maximizing the modest space with finesse.

Opting for a seat at the bar, we were greeted by Jason, our congenial bartender, who ensured our experience started on the right note. The Iron Skillet Shrimp, priced at $18, caught my eye, though the three-shrimp serving left me questioning the value. The dish itself was a novel mix of flavors, pairing shrimp with chickpeas in an interesting culinary twist. However, the sauce, intended to be a roasted pepper creation, missed the mark for my palate, bearing an unwelcome resemblance to beetroot.

In conclusion, while the atmosphere hit the sweet spot for a relaxed night out, the snack portion could be more generous given the price point. If I find myself back in this neighborhood, I'll likely gravitate towards the more economical $30 prix fixe or the tempting happy hour deals.

Came around 6 as a party of 3 on a Friday and we were seated right away. They have maybe 16 seats, and a bathroom past the kitchen if you ask. We started with the cauliflower fritters/ fried cauliflower and Parmesan fries. The cauliflower was lightly fried and seasoned with a curry powder. The fries were the thin kind, could've been more crunchy but both good options. I had the creme de bacon mazemen and expected to be super heavy but surprisingly it wasn't. Think about a lighter version or Alfredo with thick bacon bits. I really enjoyed this and enjoyed the thick ramen noodles they used. My friends ordered the Russ and roe and steak mazemen. I tried the steak and it was super flavorful. My friends thought their noodles were kinda heavy and the salmon in the Russ and roe to not be super fresh. A good experience and a bit on the pricier side but definitely worth a try.

Title: Unequal Treatment Overshadowed the Meal

I recently dined at a historic restaurant in NYC, drawn by its claim as the country's first sit-down establishment and was met with a disappointing experience both in service and in the culinary department. Dining alone post-NYC Marathon, I anticipated a lovely meal but found my Delmonico steak to be excessively fatty and lacking flavor. To add to the letdown, the atmosphere, while initially promising with its Victorian charm, quickly soured. 

I chose the main parlor for my meal, but a stark contrast in service became apparent between myself and a fellow solo diner, who, by his conversations, seemed to be a high-rolling exec. The staff's preferential treatment towards him was blatant and off-putting. My presence felt nearly invisible as they fawned over him, leaving me to dine without the merest check-in until my plate was clear.

It's unsavory when a restaurant's attentiveness is doled out based on perceived importance. Every patron deserves equal respect and service. Although the fries eventually won me over, it was not enough to salvage the experience. Two stars for this visit – a generous nod to the fries and partly because another section of the restaurant may have offered a more relaxed vibe. Nevertheless, with the myriad options in NYC, I can't recommend a place that doesn't practice hospitality equally.

- We ordered for pick up- The pad thai was average but I really enjoyed the pork pad see ew- One of the few thai places still open that have pork- The pricing is a little higher compared to same dishes at other restaurants in the area

Came here for a brunch event and I was shocked how good the food was for a sports bar!!Their drinks were also really good. Good spot to come for a boozy brunch. Made a very good bloody mary. You can also reserve a beer pong table for free and they'll set it up for you. We tried a little bit of everything!I think my favorite was their pastrami hash benedict or the chicken and waffles. Their French toast was also super yum!The U.E.S. mimosa was good too... blackberry-lavender infused prosecco with orange. I believe they said all of their alcohol syrups and what not are made in house... love that!

We came on a late afternoon and waited around 15 minutes or so. This is a small place (probably fits around 15 patrons) with bar seating only. It was busy when we came so we found service a bit lacking. There was only one waitress. After we were seated, she did not give us a menu so we got up and grabbed one ourselves. We were missing a cup of water and she was prompt about getting us one, but poured us a half-filled cup. She came by after 5 minutes and asked if we were ready... No, I mean we just sat down and weren't served any menus. We had to get the menu ourselves. We usually enjoy ramen joints where you can watch the chefs cook, but here, we found there to be a strong smell of grease. The chef cooking in front of us was friendly. We were served our ramen without spoons and he quickly got spoons for us after we asked. Don't expect the ramen to be authentic, but the dishes are relatively cheap and filling. The soup wasn't very salty, which we like, but the broth lacks depth. I also found the meat a little too lean for my liking. Other than the narutomaki and a few keychains/posters of anime on the wall, there isn't anything special about this ramen joint. It's worth coming if you are looking for a cheap eat, but I wouldn't come back if I had to wait long.

During an early weekend visit to Chelsea Market, I took advantage of the take-out counter at a bustling eatery to dodge the lunch rush. Opting for the clam chowder (~$5) and fish and chips (~$15), I found the self-serve soup deliciously fresh and piping hot, providing a satisfying meal. While I generally pass on fries, they looked standard; my primary delight was the fish – small yet thick cuts, flawlessly cooked. A bit more fish in the balance would have made the dish perfect. A good quick option for those seeking quality seafood without the wait.

GET THE BURGER. Emily is a small restaurant - tight spaces and really popular. Not the greatest child-friendly space, but they were accommodating and no one seemed to mind. We came here on a Sunday afternoon around 4:30pm. We didn't have a reservation, there was no line but the hostess said we'd have to wait for about 30min. OK, we decided to wait. And then we were seated in less than 10min. Not sure why the hostess would even give out an estimate of 30min in the first place. Maybe try to deter people?? Anyways, we split the beets salad, the Emmy burger, and the Colony pizza. Burger was definitely the star - double patty, the onion, cheese and the special sauce all worked in harmony. It was a messy burger but really one of the top burgers I've ever had in my life. It was very well executed with a nice buttery bun, juicy patties, cheese and a sauce that was somewhat spicy and sweet. I couldn't tell exactly what it was but it had almost a Korean flavor to it, but I was blown away. I've had their Detroit-style pizza delivered to me in the past and was a huge fan, but the one we got just had little balance. It had too much acid and bite (tomato, salty pepperoni and salty jalapeno). If the slices had enough cheese I think it would have been OK but there just wasn't enough. I would love to try their other pizzas though. Definitely a place worth traveling and waiting for, but I would pick the burger over the pizza!

Title: A Delightful Brunch Experience

I had a fantastic time during a Saturday brunch at this gem of a restaurant in January. Although there was a brief wait, it proved worthwhile. I opted for the cheeseburger, which was cooked perfectly to my liking and modestly sized, keeping me satisfied for the entire day.

My companions raved about the biscuit with egg and cheese, praising the fluffy eggs and the biscuit's perfect balance of softness and crispness. We also tried the kale salad, which was fresh and well-seasoned without being drenched in dressing, though a tad more squash would have been ideal. The special maple pecan shortbread was simply sublime – a must-try!

The ambiance added to the enjoyment, with a very inviting atmosphere and a staff that was both friendly and on the ball. A glass of their winter sangria was the perfect capstone to our meal. This place is unquestionably worth a visit, and I am eager to return.

They have 700+ restaurants worldwide but none in NJ (so far)..... I'm offended.  This is a fun place to eat and we did not feel rushed at all. In fact, we had a great time.  The ambience is cool and hip.  Our server provided great suggestions and the food is good.  The portion size, however, is quite small.  The meat is thinly sliced, and there are only a few slices, so the price can add up pretty quickly. The marinated beef we ordered were about $26 each and a few were $11 each (for a few slices). The shrimp dish was $8 (for 4 medium sized raw shrimp) and the vegetable dish was $8 (4 thin slices of zucchini, 2 mushrooms, a couple of cherry tomatoes, a thin slice of onion and ~1/4 cup of corn kernels.  As you can see, the value could be better.  We saw signs for happy hour which ends at 6PM but starts again at 9:30PM. The prices are discounted during happy hour and I think most people take advantage of this. Although there were many empty tables around 7:30 pm, the hostess told us there was a 40 minute wait but we were actually seated after 15 minutes.Each table is outfitted with a grill in the center where you cook your own food.  There is a strong fire that flares up when the oil from the meat drips down.  This chars the meat nicely.  To be fair, the marinated beef barbecue is really good.  The beef comes out charred and flavorful.  They also serve cooked food such as ramen.  I did not try it but someone in our party did and he said it was so salty that it was inedible.  Our server didn't know what to do.  He didn't offer to replace it but just kind of shrugged it off.  We asked for hot water so that we could at least dilute the broth which at least made it edible.If you dine here, be sure to download their app for the rewards.  You will be given 100 points at signup, which is enough for an ice cream or a smores dessert.

A lovely Japanese restaurant in west village. Came here with my friend for dinner on the weekend. Contemporary Japanese decor, very delicate. The bar area was pretty cute, they offer different kind of soju/sake/wine/cocktail/beer. Got myself a glass of Orion Lager while waiting for my friend. Japanese beer is always so refreshing. The waitress told me that the chef is from another famous Japanese restaurant Torishin, where me and my friend have been a few times, felt like a level of quality assurance. After we got seated, we were debating between the seasontasting menu (8 courses, $100 per person) or the regular menu. As my friend was worried if she could finish all, we decided to pick from the regular menu.We ordered cod roe, the Japanese eggplant, tuna tartare, white eel with yuzu sauce, wagyu beef and cold udon with cod roe.The dishes were so well made and elegantly presented. Each dish had a unique plate to go with. It kept the original flavor of the ingredient while adding right amount of seasoning to highlight.The place is perfect for a date or close friends catch-up. Love the ambience and the attentive services. The staff came to ask us if we were satisfied with the pace of dish delivery, which was very considerate. The restaurant has been open for only one year, but I can totally see it become a popular spot in west village soon.

Title: A Brunch Gem with Ample Room and Great Options

I had a delightful brunch experience at this spot. Making a reservation online was hassle-free, and to my surprise, the place was comfortably bustling but not overcrowded on a Saturday afternoon. The staff was accommodating and allowed us to be seated before our entire party had arrived.

The ambiance inside was just right, with plenty of natural light creating a welcoming atmosphere without the squeeze of a typical brunch rush. The menu catered to diverse tastes, ensuring that everyone at the table found something to savor. A highlight was the reasonably priced charcuterie board we shared; it was a hit and hinted that the restaurant would be an excellent venue for a cheese and wine evening.

Overall, it's a solid choice for anyone looking to enjoy a leisurely brunch in a relaxed setting.

Title: A Spicy Haven for Flavor Chasers

I've dined at this restaurant multiple times and it's consistently impressive, especially for those who appreciate a well-defined spice level. The noodles here tip the scale on the spicier side compared to the rice dishes, but the heat is always consistent. For adventurous palates, the extra spicy curry delivers a potent punch while still being rich in flavor, albeit a touch thinner than its milder counterparts.

For a truly satisfying meal, skip the standard chicken in favor of a chicken cutlet or other meat add-ons, which significantly enhance the dish with their robust taste. Although rice entrées come with miso soup and kimchi, the generous serving size of the main courses means these sides can be easily overlooked.

Service is swift and attentive, with staff ensuring diners are forewarned about the heat level of spicier options. They remain on their toes with water refills, a much-appreciated gesture as the spice can certainly necessitate it. Overall, a fantastic spot for those who like it hot and flavorful.

I had a wonderful dining experience at this charming little gem of a restaurant. Despite its small, Lilliputian size, the flavors were immense and left a lasting impression. The food was flawlessly executed, striking the perfect balance of modern French cuisine. Each dish served was not only a treat for the palate but also a feast for the eyes with its artistic presentation. Adding to the experience was the courteous service provided by an individual who seemed to be the owner, which gave a personal touch to our visit. I was thoroughly impressed and am already planning my next visit. Highly recommended!

Title: Quaint Spot with Tasty Desserts, Service Could Improve

I popped into this cozy little place on a Sunday night, only to be directed to their sister location a short walk away due to the wait. The second spot accommodated us quickly. I indulged in the delectable 'Dirt Pop' dessert, a delightful concoction of cream, fresh berries, and Oreo crust, with a surprising twist of cake mix at its heart. It didn't disappoint. My friend's chocolate matcha lava cake hit the sweet spot with its exquisite filling, though the slow service meant a longer wait for this treat. The chocolate hazelnut cookies accompanying the ice cream were truly exceptional. While the service was a mix of hit-and-miss, the vibe inside was enjoyable with good music, despite the cramped space. Next time I'd consider a takeout to savor their sweet offerings without the wait.

Title: A Flavorful Experience at [Restaurant Name]

My recent visit to [Restaurant Name] on a late Monday night was a delightful surprise with no wait for our party of three. Upon entering, the enticing aroma immediately whetted our appetites, promising a fulfilling meal ahead.

We unanimously chose the pork belly skewers, a decision bolstered by their reputation. True to the praise, they were succulent and perfectly charred, leaving us wanting more. For our main dish, the shrimp and crawfish mix in medium spicy sauce did wonders for our taste buds. However, for those sensitive to heat, I'd recommend opting for the mild option, as the medium spice proved slightly more challenging for us to handle.

To round out our meal, we introduced lotus root and rice cakes to the mix, both of which we found to be delightful additions that complemented the main course well.

In summary, [Restaurant Name] served as a delicious escape, perfect for anyone looking to indulge in rich flavors and a cozy atmosphere. Just be mindful of the spice levels, and you're in for a treat!

Came here for a birthday dinner celebration and totally enjoyed my time here. As soon as I walked in I was greeted with a smile  and though I was early I waited at the bar while having a drink for the rest to arrive. It was about 22 people at our table and I must say our waiter (can't remember his name but very funny, lots of jokes and he's from greece) was a gem. He handled our table well, attentive to everyone and made sure we were good. Our orders as well didnt take long to come to us bearing in mind our large numbers.I had the pan sauteed salmon with the couscous and radish. The salmon was done medium and tasted really good. The couscous was a different taste for my palette but after many bites I got accustomed. We also ordered garlic fries and omg I could've eaten that alone for dinner lol it tasted good and filling!All in all I had a wonderful time and 2oupd definitely be back!

Do you like tapas? We all like tapas.Did you grow up on Capri Suns? I definitely did and the Instagram video showing their adult versions lured me in. One thing to note, they don't do reservations. First come first serve and be there early. We came by at 9 pm one night and they stopped taking names. The second more successful time, we came at 5:45 when then opened at 6. There was already a line of roughly 25 people in line.Once you get past all that, congrats! The food and drinks are sure to please. The drinks are soju based and are ranked from least sweet to sweetest on the menu. I went with the lychee one which was the sweetest and it honestly tasted like a spiked lychee jelly. And they were not stingy on the soju either!For food, we ordered the pork shoulder, steak, Mac and cheese, and cauliflower. Pork - This was marinated in fish sauce, slow roasted and then either flashed fried or finished in a hot oven. The exterior was nice and crisp while the entire piece was fork tender. It was paired with the most amazing peppers and onions stir fry. Steak - Where do you get cheesy grits, gochujjang stirred fried Brussels sprouts, and medium rare steak? You guessed it. Thursday Kitchen. Somehow this all just paired together perfectly.Mac - This is probably the other reason you're here besides the drinks. Nothing more to say other than it was super cheesy and full of truffle flavor. There were also pieces of clams in there which I glazed over when reading the menu but I really enjoyed it!Cauliflower - This was probably my least favorite. The was florets paired with large white corn kernels and tossed in a spicy sauce. While the other dishes were balanced in flavor, this one was way too spicy. The spice took over everything and I didn't enjoy it very much.When coming here, definitely plan to come early! It took two tries to eat here and it was worth it.

Even before arriving at A La Turka, the very kind host called me to inform me that my 9pm reservation would be too late, as the restaurant closes early on Sundays. The waitstaff and service were excellent. Most notable was our server Levant, who made modifications to the menu and suggestions based on our preferences. We ordered the Mixed Grill and Levant was kind enough to replace one of the lamb skewers with chicken, as it better suited my partner's diet. All the food, the Mixed grill and our hummus appetizer were prepared and presented to perfection. The lamb was tender and cooked at medium, and the chicken was juicy and  flavorful. We also ordered a Montepulciano that complimented our dishes. We have both ordered takeout from A La Turka in the past, but dining in the restaurant was fantastic and we will now be regulars!

Title: Ideal Spot for Happy Hour – Mind the Rush

I've frequented this establishment multiple times and while it's on the pricier side – a common theme in the neighborhood – the experience generally justifies the expense. The ambiance makes it a prime spot for post-work relaxation, with an array of shareable plates that never fail to satisfy. The lamb lollipops are a personal favorite, bursting with flavor in every bite, and the calamari is a hit, with the caveat that timing matters; an off-peak visit resulted in a less than fresh experience, evidenced by the over-quick service and my attached photo.

However, that was a rare miss in the usually spot-on offerings. On a lunchtime outing, my companion's burger arrived, a model of juicy, well-spiced perfection. For the ultimate indulgence, I can't recommend enough topping your nachos with their succulent steak. Despite the occasional hiccup, this place comes with a solid recommendation, especially for those looking to unwind after a day's work.

I absolutely adore this restaurant! My recent Tuesday visit was to grab a quick bite before a movie, and it didn't disappoint. Opting for the beer and burger special, I savored my perfectly cooked medium-rare burger, accompanied by a side of scrumptious fries. I've also enjoyed the Midtown West location, renowned for its inventive bacon-infused drinks and an array of bacon-themed dishes. It's the ideal place to gather with friends for a delightful meal and good conversation. Highly recommended!

Title: A Hit or Miss Experience at a Trendy Spot

I approached this eatery with high hopes, tempted by the promise of contemporary flavors, only to leave with a palate of mixed emotions. The initial interaction was disheartening, as the cashier's unfamiliarity with their own "Tinga" sauce set a tone of culinary disconnect.

A glance at the menu revealed a perplexing pay-per-piece model, leaving one to weigh the value of a single taco at $5-$7, a hefty sum for a sliver of sustenance. My choice, a vegan chorizo taco, arrived in a disappointing fashion – scant and barely above room temperature.

In pursuit of redemption, I ordered the wild harvest grain bowl adorned with impossible taco meat. While served cold—intentionally, I presume—the bowl's composition of local grains, butternut mash, hearty greens, and roasted sweet potatoes offered a comforting, albeit not warming, amalgamation of flavors.

Ultimately, the establishment's allure lies in its potential rather than its consistency. The enticing menu and visually appetizing dishes might draw you in, but temper expectations; the knowledge of the staff and execution of the food can vary. On this particular chilly day, my quest for culinary warmth went unfulfilled, leaving my experience underwhelming.

Title: A Slice Above: NY Pizza Suprema Shines in the Big Apple

Finding a stand-out pizza joint in NYC is no small feat, yet NY Pizza Suprema rises to the challenge with its distinctive and delectable offerings. It's a mystery how this gem had escaped my notice during my time in the city.

Arriving just before closing time, the buzz of the crowded space hinted at the culinary excellence awaiting me. The walls adorned with photos of revered foodies like Anthony Bourdain were a testament to the pizza's reputation. And the proof was in the pie: the Sicilian sausage and baked potato slices were an indulgent delight, the former made even more flavorful with a sprinkle of parmesan, although it was unfortunately served cold due to the imminent closing.

While this minor hiccup prevented a perfect score, it's clear that NY Pizza Suprema is a cut above the rest. My appetite is already gearing up for the next visit to explore more of their tempting menu. A solid 4 out of 5 stars for this pizza haven.

Title: A Lunar New Year Feast to Remember at Chinatown's Dim Sum Delight

I recently seized the opportunity to dine at a renowned Chinatown dim sum spot on the auspicious first day of the Lunar New Year. Anticipating the bustle, our eager party of six arrived at the 9:30 AM opening and were promptly seated in the expansive dining hall, adorned with festive red tablecloths, elegant drapes, and traditional decor that set the celebratory mood.

Amidst the convivial atmosphere, we dived into the art of choosing from an array of carts parading by, laden with an assortment of dishes. Though it's a blur trying to recall each specific offering, the overall impression was that of rich flavors and expertly prepared meats, with desserts that were a sweet punctuation to the savory courses.

The service was commendably efficient. Despite a mild language barrier, the staff were swift to replenish hot water, supply extra napkins, and respond to our requests, ensuring a seamless dining experience.

In conclusion, this restaurant offers a delightful dim sum experience, particularly on a culturally significant day such as the Lunar New Year. Just a tip: arrive early to beat the crowds and fully savor the festivities!

Last weekend in NYC we had such beautiful weather. Winter never felt so good and dinner at Park Avenue Winter was even better! Park Avenue is a restaurant that is very distinctive and fun because their menu and decor changes with every season (Winter, Autumn, Spring and Summer) making it ideal to have the freshest ingredients. Last weekend our server was Francisco and Alex and they were super nice and attentive. We tired all of their recommendations and they were all outstanding!! The food was truly incredible we had their roasted duck super decadent and perfectly cooked the flavors were insanely delicious! For appetizer we tired their pumpkin ravioli and it's definitely a must try!! The octopus was super tender and packed with flavor! But you must leave room for dessert because their dessert are house made super fresh and delicious! Highly recommend their Park Chocolate cube!! Overall, it was an amazing dining experience!

Ginger and Lemongrass is a Vietnamese restaurant in the Lower East Side, the sister of a successful operation in Queens.I went with my boyfriend for a weekend lunch a couple months ago. At noon, we were one of a few parties-- I think they do bigger business at night, though I wouldn't be worried about much of a wait here. The space is surprisingly roomy and has some nice exposed brick and an impressive bar, though the decorations seem a little Ikea (bright yellow metal chairs and fake plants), though there are some personal touches like Cafe Du Monde coffee cans.The menu is a little bit fusion-y, with seaweed tuna rolls and curries sharing space with more traditional pho and banh mi (though note that they don't have the three-pork variation). We kept it classic and got beef pho ($14) and spicy lemongrass soup ($13).Their pho is pretty good: a nice murky broth on the sweeter side, with generous and tender beef, as well as the usual suspects. Hit the spot for my hangover. I thought the lemongrass soup was a bit better with its more distinctive taste.Service was punctual and polite. We also had Vietnamese coffee which was great.A solid pick for Vietnamese in this neck of the woods, and a good middle ground between the no-frills pho shops near Chinatown and the upscale hipster joints in East Village.

I've had the infamous burger at the original in Chicago. So happy a New York location is now open. We were a party of two and tried the brunch menu. We ordered signature items:Single cheeseburger- we added the egg and bacon; and the whole package was amazing. Every party had the burger. You just have to try it - it's juicy and magnificent Foie gras, scrambled eggs & toast - first impression is that it's an overall rich dish. And it's delicious. Get it.Crispy potato hash with duck heart gravy - we were debating on this or the fries; but then the waiter clarified that this dish includes the same mornay sauce, garlic aioli & fried farm egg that the fries are dressed with. This was very good and really filling. The portions are generous and each bite is decadent. I suggest going with a large group to share the dishes and try to balance out the heaviness of each dish.

Title: A Disappointing Korean Dining Experience at a Premium Price

My anticipation for an exceptional Korean meal was met with disappointment during my recent visit to a high-end local restaurant. Despite making a reservation, a 10-15 minute wait to be seated indicated a less-than-organized seating protocol.

The service throughout the meal only compounded the frustration. Staff members appeared rushed, more interested in turning tables than ensuring a quality dining experience. Our orders—a mix of drinks, appetizers, and main courses—arrived haphazardly, with the appetizer and entrées delivered almost simultaneously.

The octopus appetizer, though adequately portioned, lacked flavor. My main course, cured shrimp with Uni over rice, also fell short on taste and the portion size left much to be desired. My husband's fish dish was only passable in comparison to our expectations.

The abrupt presentation of the check while we were still eating felt rude and dismissive. To make matters worse, the absence of dessert offerings after such strongly flavored meals was baffling, especially given the restaurant's price point.

In conclusion, I cannot justify the premium costs for the subpar service and unremarkable cuisine received. For those seeking a more satisfying Korean culinary adventure, I recommend exploring alternatives like Barn Joo, Her Name is Han, or Five Senses, which offer superior experiences at more reasonable prices.

I recently enjoyed a meatless Mediterranean bowl from this restaurant through MealPal and was quite satisfied with the experience. The dish featured four pieces of tasty falafel, a blend of rice and quinoa, creamy hummus, and a medley of fresh mixed vegetables. It was delicious and surprisingly filling. I was impressed by how my order was promptly ready upon my arrival, ensuring the food's freshness. I'm eager to return and sample more of their offerings.

There is always a line when you get here but its totally worth standing on line (which goes pretty quick) for this pizza! They are famous for their pepperoni pizza, but since I'm a vegetarian I get it without the pepperoni and I still think its fantastic! @traveleen_gurl

Title: A Gem of West African Delights

As a Liberian woman with a deep affinity for West African cuisine, I have found myself returning to this restaurant time and again – six visits and counting, to be precise. It's become a humorous test of my dietary resolve, given the sheer deliciousness of their offerings. Each meal here is a feast large enough to last three days, no exaggeration!

My go-to dish is the Dibi lamb paired with atieke, a combination that never disappoints. The portions are generous, and the flavors are authentically West African. It's not just the food that makes this place stand out among the strip of similar restaurants; the ambiance is inviting with its intoxicating aromas and vibrant mix of dialects filling the air. Music videos play in the background, often prompting me to discover new tunes through Shazam.

The sense of home and warmth here is unparalleled. I've introduced the restaurant to family and friends on special occasions like my graduation, and they too have become advocates of its charms. The atieke is always perfectly cooked, and the seasoned onions and tomatoes provided add another layer of taste. Plus, where else can one find the luxury of enjoying a mimosa, ginger beer, and atieke in one sitting at such excellent prices? This restaurant is an undeniable local treasure for anyone seeking the heart and soul of West African cooking.

Was in the area in need of satisfying my hunger pangs and saw this little gem, interestingly enough it's run by a husband and wife duo.As soon as I walked it, the space felt homey, cozy and inviting.  Walked up to the end of the space and was greeted by the husband who was currently having a big lunch and the wife who is tending the kitchen. Since there was only a few patrons, i selected my preferred seating and was greeted quickly with the menu, and specials.  The husband gave me a few suggestions based on my interests on a few items.  I started with the tofu satay, and let me say it was one of the best I've had.  All the different components just felt like a party in my mouth.  For my main entree I went with the pineapple salmon stew dish accompanied by coconut rice and pickled veggies.  It was lighter in spice than anticipated but the flavors were all there.  It was very good and satisfying, even though the portion seemed small, I left with a happy belly.I'd love to go back during the weekend and try either their brunch or dinner menus.

Title: Steady Improvement and Flavorful Dumplings

After an underwhelming initial visit close to their opening, with nearly soupless dumplings and lukewarm offerings, I recently gave this eatery another chance. I'm pleased to report a marked improvement, although it's worth noting the Brooklyn location still holds the crown for the best experience.

Their blue crab and pork soup dumplings are now a standout, bursting with flavor, but could still benefit from a bit more soup inside. The spicy pork truly lives up to its name, delivering a kick that spice lovers will appreciate. The pan-fried bao buns also impressed me with their size and juiciness.

Another favorite was the sweet and spicy pork dumpling jiaozi, despite being a bit heavy on the chili oil, it provided a delightful sweet heat. I ventured into their dry noodles, pairing them with pork ribs, which were satisfactory but could do with more tenderness and moisture.

Sampling a friend's fried chicken filet over garlic rice, I enjoyed the black pepper sauce, though the rice itself could be elevated with more garlic punch and stickier texture.

The restaurant's ambiance is inviting, with a spacious and brightly lit dining area featuring bench-style seating. The convenience of self-service water and condiments is a nice touch, ensuring you can readily customize your meal to taste.

In conclusion, this spot has taken feedback to heart and stepped up their game, especially in the dumpling department. I look forward to their continued growth and potentially reaching the high bar set by their Brooklyn counterpart.

After a strenuous move back to NYC, my ravenous state led me to explore UberEats, where I stumbled upon Hummus Kitchen. Craving Middle Eastern fare, I opted for their chicken shawarma accompanied by hummus and pita bread. The chicken was perfectly seasoned and well-cooked, while the hummus was delightfully smooth, and the pita arrived warm and tender. The meal was exceptionally satisfying. Hummus Kitchen has certainly earned my repeat business with their first-rate impression.

I must've walked past this restaurant over a hundred times since moving to Hell's Kitchen but I've never taken the chance to try it out. My girlfriend and I found ourselves with an Italian caving on one particular Saturday morning and I suggested we try Giardino 54 out. I'm so happy we did because the experience, from food to service, was really excellent.We walked in without a reservation around 12:30 on a Saturday in November. The restaurant only had two other parties inside at the time. Our server greeted us and allowed us to sit anywhere we like given it wasn't packed. The place definitely feels homely due to the wood themed interior design. They also have ample bar seating as well if that's your preference for dining.When it came time to order I went with the frittata carciofi e  "nduja" which is part of their $34 bottomless brunch menu. This also included 90 minutes of classic brunch drinks (mimosas, bloddy mary's, etc.). The dish itself was beautifully prepared and extremely filling. The side arugula salad made for a good start and the main frittata was savory and on the heavier side as well. I'd recommend this dish if you're particularly hungry and find yourself here on any given morning.For dessert we decided to go with a classic Italian panna cotta ($10). What the dish lacked in size it makes up for in flavor. This gelatin based dish was topped with fresh strawberries and blueberries and made for easy sharing. Definitely order for dessert after a filling meal.Overall this was an awesome restaurant if you're looking for more of an intimate place to dine. During the day the large windows allowed for a lot of natural light to come into the space. I can only imagine at night it's just as memorable of an experience. A 10 out of 10 for me!

My first visit to this restaurant left me thoroughly impressed. The decor is captivating, perfectly complementing the vibrant atmosphere and trendy location. Their music selection added a delightful ambience that enhanced the overall dining experience. The staff made a great impression with their warm welcome and unwavering attention to service. I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit.

I recently visited [Restaurant Name] for brunch and was let down by the experience. We arrived before 4 pm with expectations of a full brunch menu, but were informed that only soups, salads, and sandwiches were available. Despite this, we stayed due to hunger and began with the bacon mac and cheese, which was notably cheesy but did not make up for the initial disappointment.

For our main course, we each chose the burger, which, while boasting a thick patty, was otherwise unremarkable. Given the $22 price tag, I had high hopes for a standout burger, but it ended up being quite standard. Overall, the visit was underwhelming and did not live up to the expectations set by both the menu and the price.

Knew it when I saw it from the street this would be a 3 star place. At this point in my yelp career I can just tell.  Like all typical nyc pizza places it had all the pizza in the window with all kinds of styles and toppings. I did some wishful thinking and ordered the square slice thinking that I am at Spumoni Gardens. It looked like spumoni but it sure did not taste like it. Not even in the same ballpark. What was weird that the pizza had a Saltiness to it.    Never really had something like that. This is more of a grab and go type place so if you need a quick bite like I did check it out. I also think it has a bunch of locations in nyc. This is the type of pizza you can set your watch to. You know what you are going to get. 3 stars all the way.

The ramen was pretty good, but the fried rice was what really won me over. Service is fairly quick and we got seating also quickly although the place is small. Price is pretty decent and not too expensive. I'm probably going to get a lot of complaints about this, but I think it's better than Ippudo ramen which is way overpriced for what it's worth. Tip: Cash only!

Title: A Michelin Experience Near the Met

Last evening, my dining companion and I visited a 2-star Michelin restaurant situated conveniently close to our hotel and just a curtain call away from the Met Opera. Expecting high standards, we settled for the 3-course meal given our tight schedule.

Humorously, in hindsight, I'd swap my choices for those of my guest. Venturing into the realm of Nordic cuisine for the first time, we were greeted with dishes that were, in my opinion, heavy-handed in seasoning and pickling. Perhaps an accurate regional representation, but a tad overwhelming for my taste.

I selected foie gras, sea bass, and a chocolate finale, while my guest enjoyed an intriguing egg appetizer, a succulent duck entree, and a citrus dessert. Presentation and flavor were bold and assertive - a visual and sensory assertiveness.

The non-alcoholic grape juice pairings were a delightful surprise, excelling in complementing the meal.

Service and presentation stood out as impossibly flawless. However, the experience stopped just shy of extraordinary, save for the perfectly moist and expertly prepared duck that truly impressed.

In sum, the restaurant crafts dishes with mastery over texture and temperature, yet a lighter hand on flavor might have elevated the meal. I'm eager to return with more time on my hands to indulge in the full tasting menu for a potential revelation.

Title: A Haven for Classic Hong Kong Comfort Food

If your tastebuds are yearning for some authentic Hong Kong street food without breaking the bank, this local gem is your go-to spot. As a regular patron, I can vouch for their House special thick toast—a delightful indulgence of chunky peanut butter and condensed milk atop a pillowy slab of toast. Equally impressive is their unique serving of "HK milk tea (no ice)," ingeniously nestled in a bowl of ice to preserve its robust flavor without the dilution.

Another must-try is their range of tasty chicken wings, with the garlic pepper variant stealing the show. Each wing boasts a flawless combination of a crispy exterior and succulent interior. The coke flavored wings, while subtler in taste, are an interesting twist worth sampling.

Admittedly, the service is brisk, but it's a small trade-off for the consistently swift arrival of scrumptious, piping-hot food. This spot remains a trusty favorite for its delectable offerings and efficient delivery.

What a gem! Got a same day Saturday reservation for 8 people at 9pm. Right from the start everything was great. The hostess is adorable, acts like you've been friends for years, gave me a hug on the way out, haha. We were seated on the couch which was so cool. Decor is cozy, romantic, dimly lit, and the whole place smells incredible. We shared 3 combo platters and a few apps between 8 of us and it was way too much food! The chicken combo platter was my fave. The service was excellent, never ran out of water which is key cause some dishes are spicy. Everything is priced perfectly. Wine is also super affordable, like $30 bottle for the cheapest. For 8 ppl with way too much food and 4 bottles of wine split, the total after tip was $350. The place is cash only FYI. Would highly recommend this place.

Despite the anticipation of a comforting meal during a busy day on set, my experience with this eatery was underwhelming. The veggie burger arrived undercooked, compromising both texture and taste. Accompanying sweet potato "batas" were disappointingly mushy, and the omission of the promised maple syrup further diminished the dish. To add to the letdown, the onion rings were excessively greasy, falling short of the crispiness one would expect. Hunger pangs can make any shortcomings in a meal particularly frustrating, a sentiment only exacerbated by the unjustifiably high prices. Overall, the experience was disheartening, and improvements are necessary to justify the cost and meet expectations.

Had a wonderful experience at Kellari and honestly if my friend hadn't told me about it I wouldn't have known about it! The space is tremendous and I've been in few places this large. In terms of drinks I suggest the wine as they have a great selection and the staff is wonderful with recommendations based on what you're ordering. When you come here you HAVE to get seafood. It's what they specialize in (not to mention sustainable) and it is beyond fresh. The scallops, octopus and salmon we had were all cooked perfectly. If I were to skip anything it would be the potatoes because you really don't need it. This is the perfect place to bring family, colleagues or celebrate when you want authentic Greek cuisine and fresh seafood.

Upon visiting Angeletto based on glowing Yelp reviews, I was met with disappointment. The quaint patio along 2nd Ave offered prime people-watching in Midtown Manhattan, and while the interior exuded an upscale vibe with clean surroundings, the service, though cordial and attentive, could not salvage the meal.

The Bruschetta Platter was excessively dry, requiring a deluge of olive oil and balsamic to be palatable. The Arugula Salad, though fresh, lacked any discernible flavor. The most egregious offense was the Spaghetti alle Vongole, resembling microwaved leftovers with overcooked pasta and rubbery clams, not at all justifying its $25 price tag.

The absurdity peaked with a $20 charge for four glasses of iced tea. After flagging down a manager, the bill was begrudgingly corrected to a more reasonable $5. Such pricing should be transparent on the menu or communicated by the server to prevent customer shock and frustration.

Angeletto, you're not the Tavern on the Green, and your overrated fare and hidden costs are a disservice to your patrons. In a city with culinary wonders around every corner, one expects more, certainly at your prices.

Picked up an arepa for lunch since Ritual offered $5 off my first order here. The pickup process was seamless - I skipped the line & they had my order ready the second I arrived, which I appreciated. I had the Del Corral (shredded chicken, avocado, shredded white cheese) which was just meh - filling but nothing special, the chicken a little too bland. Worth the try but I'd only come back to try the others if I was offered the same type of discount again.

This spot exceeded my expectations. It was beyond delicious! My sister & I tried the beef tripe salad, stewed beef w/ soup noodle, pork & pickled mustard greens w/ soup noodle, dumpling (shrimp chive pork). Everything was delicious, but if I had to rank them based on best to least would be 1) pork & pickled mustard greens w/ soup noodle, 2) beef tripe salad, 3) stewed beef w/ soup noodle, 4) dumpling (wouldn't recommend - it was not that crispy & the filling was alright). Staff was nice and the food came out fast. Plenty of seating too!Super delicious - highly highly recommend! We will be back!

My friend and I came to Sweet Chick around 10:30am on a Saturday.  They don't take reservations so we decided to try and beat the brunch crowd and were successful!  When we left around noon, the restaurant was busy.  The ambiance has a casual, laid-back feel and is a good place to grab food with friends.We ordered the Sweet Chick Waffle ($14) and Chicken and Waffles ($19).  The waffles were both the right texture and were sweet enough to stand alone without needing syrup.  The Sweet Chick Waffle had fruit, ricotta, and honey.  It was fine, but nothing special.  The chicken for the other dish was dry.  I know their thing is southern comfort food but this was more like bougie brunch.Service was great here!  Our waitress was bubbly, did a lot of check-backs, and refilled our waters.  Overall, I'd say this place delivers on your standard, overpriced, American brunch and is a safe choice but by no means a standout.

Came here for drinks and a team dinner and had the most amazing time. We had the chef tasting menu and there was such a great variety of dishes. The one that caught me by the biggest surprise is the edamame dumplings, which had a really strong truffle flavor and packed quite the punch. The glazed alaskan black cod, short rib, and the shrimp and scallop main course were all amazing. Both the cod and short rib were cooked to melt-in-your-mouth perfection. The dessert was a disappointment initially. We had a sorbet that was slightly bitter and not very enjoyable. However, we were later served mochi donuts and ice cream which more than made up for the disappointment. Definitely recommended and would return again for a special occasion!

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience at [Restaurant Name]

I had a fantastic dining experience at this restaurant, starting with the excitement of being the first patrons right at the grand opening hour of 5 PM. The staff's collective greeting for each new guest adds a unique and enjoyable touch to the ambiance, which quickly became lively as the restaurant filled up by 5:38 PM.

Service was nothing short of impeccable. Seated at a community table, we enjoyed the social atmosphere, though I noticed there were options for larger parties as well. Our order of buns arrived within 10 minutes, and the staff even apologized for what they considered a delay — an unnecessary but appreciated gesture.

The food was delectable, particularly the shrimp with its mouth-watering glaze, complemented by egg mash and lettuce — a fusion of flavors worth savoring. Following closely was the Ramen; I chose the Ichiraku with a lighter broth, which was delightful, but I'm eager to try a spicier option next time. The noodles were exceptional in taste and quality. Observing our neighbors, I learned that extra noodles are available upon request — a note for my future visit.

I appreciated the lack of substitutions policy, which allowed me to focus on the dish as the chef intended, but I could still customize my Ramen with a side of tofu for a minimal additional cost. The staff was attentive throughout our meal, clearing even the tiniest of litter like straw wrappers.

I give this establishment a well-deserved 5 stars for their stellar service alone. I'm looking forward to returning and diving into more of their culinary offerings.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Mama Mia's on 9th Avenue

During a recent visit to 9th Avenue's culinary corridor, my companion and I, lured by the enticing aromas of garlic and onion, decided to try Mama Mia before a Broadway show. The restaurant is well-known for its meatballs, but, to be candid, while they had a good form, they unfortunately didn't live up to their reputation as they lacked the herby and garlicky punch I was anticipating.

We also sampled the sausage pizza, which did deliver that quintessential thin-crust, cheesy New York pizza experience. However, our main dish, the chicken parmigiana, was a letdown. Like the meatballs, the chicken was underwhelming and the tomato sauce on both this and the meatballs was overpoweringly acidic, overshadowing the flavors of the dishes.

Regrettably, our dining experience at Mama Mia was underwhelming. Perhaps it was an off night for the kitchen, but the dishes we tried did not tantalize our taste buds as we had hoped.

During restaurant week, I had the pleasure of dining at an upscale eatery that pleasantly surprised me with its casual, inclusive dress code, despite its classy vibe. Metered parking was conveniently available a mere block away.

We kicked things off with a cucumber gimlet; a truly delightful and refreshing choice although a tad too much ice for my liking. A minor hiccup occurred when inquiring about the summer happy hour special – our server seemed uninformed, attributing it to a bar-only promotion.

Our appetites were whetted by a delectable trio of appetizers: a creamy lobster bisque, crispy calamari, and a fresh salad. The main course, a filet mignon ordered medium well, was cooked flawlessly, hitting the mark of meaty excellence.

Dessert didn't disappoint, with the carrot cheesecake taking the crown as my personal favorite. While the restaurant week prices were in effect, the total for three people exceeded $250, suggesting a visit here might be best reserved for special occasions. Despite the price, the quality and experience have secured my intent to return.

Great bar! Always our go to in the city. Never been disappointed when we've come here. The bar is super clean, the bartenders actually care about the drinks they make and always make sure the customer is happy. The fries are a MUST they're fresh, hot, crispy, and so addicting! The dipping sauces go perfectly with them. The slushy changes weekly and they're always delicious, alcohol is definitely present, not like most frozen drinks. I will always come here when I'm in the area and will always recommend this bar to anyone. Kudos to the owner and staff for running an amazing bar!!!

Marinara makes a good slice. I normally get the margherita or the plain cheese slice but tonight I tried something different, and my was I glad I did. I pointed to a Sicilian slice and was pleasantly surprised to find that the crust was stuffed with cheese! The crust was golden and had a nice crunch, it had a layer of tomato sauce and a generous amount of cheese on top, and then there was more cheese stuffed inside the crust. The flavors reminded me of deep dish pizza. If you are a fan of thin crust pizza, I recommend the margherita slice. It has fresh mozzarella, garlicky tomato sauce and basil on top of a crisp crust. I have enjoyed the different types of pizza I've tried at Marinara. If you are nearby and in the mood for pizza, I would check it out.

Joe's Pizza is a New York classic, and their pizza is honestly AMAZING! I got a slice of pepperoni and the thinness of the pizza and crust was perfect for my preference. The zest of the tomato sauce and the flavor of the cheese was just right. Overall, the pizza was not too salty and not too oily.The line is always long at night, but service is quick. You'll be in and out in no time! SO WORTH!!

Title: Elegance and Taste at Nougatine

My recent dining experience at Nougatine at Jean Georges was nothing short of sophisticated and delightful. The venue exudes a classy and elegant ambiance that is perfect for a special night out.

Opting for variety, my husband indulged in the tasting menu priced at $118, while I chose the Restaurant Week 3-course offering for $42. Each dish was a testament to exquisite culinary craftsmanship, not only pleasing to the palate but also generous in portion. We were pleasantly satiated even before desserts were served, leading us to believe that had we both selected the tasting menu, it might have been overwhelming.

Standout dishes included the fresh and impeccably seasoned Sea Trout Sashimi and what I can confidently describe as the best Wild Gulf Flounder with potato ravioli I've ever tasted. A must-try is their Chocolate Lava Cake with ice cream—a decadent, finger-licking treat that left us yearning for more.

However, the experience was slightly marred by a service hiccup. The transition between my husband's courses was unexpectedly long, with over a 30-minute wait after his first entrée and a lack of communication from the staff, hinting at a forgotten order.

Despite this, Nougatine remains a highly recommendable dining spot for its exceptional food and luxurious atmosphere. With a bit more attention to service, it could certainly reach perfection.

Title: A Cozy Gem in Midtown Manhattan

I recently dined at a modest yet charming restaurant located conveniently close to Grand Central Terminal, making it a perfect spot for commuters or those on-the-go in midtown Manhattan. Despite coming across a modest Yelp rating of 3.5 stars, my curiosity prevailed, and I ventured in for a semi-late lunch.

Ambiance-wise, the restaurant boasts a snug atmosphere with roughly 20 neatly arranged wooden tables and a petite bar area. The simplicity of paper held down by clips on the tables might not scream luxurious, yet it has an unfussy, practical charm that could divide opinion.

The menu, while not extensive, presented a decent variety without the usual lure of lunch specials. This wasn't a setback though, as it seemed to promise quality over quantity. As for the service, it was exceptionally attentive and friendly, meriting a high 4 to 5-star rating, even post the lunch rush.

The highlight undoubtedly was the food. The "Kobe meatballs" and "carpaccio arugula salad" came highly recommended and did not disappoint as appetizers. For the main course, the risotto with asparagus was a delightful substitution that didn't sacrifice taste, and the chicken added a satisfying protein punch. Though the Osso Bucco deviated from tradition with a Marsala sauce instead of a classic gravy, the veal shank was tender, and the pasta was cooked to perfect al dente.

Desserts were a delectable affair with the lemon cello flute and a lemon cake, the name of which eludes me, but its flavors remain unforgettable. Adding to the experience was the owner's presence - a genuinely warm and engaging host who added a personal touch by sharing intriguing stories.

Price-wise, expect to shell out more in the range of $$$ to $$$$, with a meal for two hovering around $225 including a couple of drinks, tax, and a generous tip.

In summary, this restaurant offers a pleasing dining experience with commendable service and a menu that delivers on taste, nestled in the bustling heart of Manhattan. A spot worthy of repeat visits.

My college bestie and I had a Galentine's Day weekend in Hell's Kitchen recently. We're both foodies. She's vegan. I'm not (carnivore over here), but I don't mind eating vegan. I'm usually open to trying new things and I've had some enjoyable vegan cuisine. Before we came, I looked up a few vegan spots (on Yelp of course) and sent them to her. She chose this place. I liked the ratings this place I had so I went ahead and made a reservation for brunch. I didn't think the menu was superb for brunch for my liking. I'm more of a hash brown, french toast, chicken and waffles girl.We both chose the pre-fixe menu (unlimited coffee/tea, a small plate, and a large plate) which is $32. That's not too bad. Typically for brunch I'd definitely indulge in booze but I stuck to coffee this time. I had to ask for more coffee (they didn't just bring more). I was impressed with the space (very bright, eclectic colors, modern and cool decor). I appreciated the fresh roses as the centerpieces. From some pics I browsed I didn't realize it was two levels. We were seated upstairs. So back to the food (the main reason for reading a review of a restaurant). I did the avocado toast - I liked it. The P.S. Burger - was ok - was lacking a bit in flavor for my taste buds. I was tempted to ask for hot sauce but I didn't want that side eye. It came with fries. I wanted to do the truffle fries but they were out. If you're not starving, getting a small plate could work but if you're hungry and doing the mimosas (or any alcohol), then absolutely get the pre-fix option. I'm not sure if they offer dessert for brunch. Either way we were too full. The service was good. No real complaints. I can't say I'm ever converting to being a vegan but I'm glad I tried this place out. I would come back again.
