Great restaurant! Difficult to get a reservation. Get the lasagna but far warning there is pork in it! My friend couldn't even eat it so they got the Ragu dish. Everything was well seasoned and service was great. They have a nice but small selection of wines that I throughly enjoyed.  Will be back! Add Don Angie to your list!!!

I celebrated my birthday lunch at this charming spot during a busy workweek and couldn't have been happier with my choice. Despite the bustling atmosphere, the culinary highlight was the vegan impossible beef tacos with cilantro rice – a delight for a first-time vegan taco eater like myself. On a second visit, the street corn proved to be an equally impressive side dish. The decor, eco-friendly to-go bags, and mouth-watering flavors have left a lasting impression on me. For anyone in the area or in search of a delightful lunch venue with a bar, this place is a must-visit. The vegan tacos alone are worth the trip!

Tried to go to takashi but the wait was an hour to an hour and a half so we ended up here. A friend had been before and recommended it. Ordered the soyo kaze tasting menu - definitely the right choice. Highlights for me were the sashimi - really fresh and good selection, the tofu - the pour over sauce was a great accompaniment to the silky tofu and the chicken. I'm not usually a huge chicken fan but with the hot stone, watercress and sauce I was sold.

Tucked away in the 2nd level basement of Nordstrom, this sizable coffee bar offers a delightful escape for shoppers and coffee aficionados alike. With a commendable selection of coffees, baked goods, and around a dozen gelato flavors, it caters to a diverse range of tastes. The adjacent sit-down restaurant adds convenience by offering pre-packaged salads to go. My personal experience with their Caramel Macchiato was nothing short of delightful, with its well-crafted blend and rich flavor, making it a recommended pick for any visitor.

It felt like a gorgeous spring day and I was feeling poke, so I figured, why not try this spot again? This time, I got different things and those things made a major DIFFERENCE. When you come, you've gotta get 1. Their fresh mango, which tastes like it's from Mexico - so soft and sweet and bursting with flavor, and 2. Their avocado, which makes the whole bowl so creamyI also had the tuna and salmon in the Wise Fish sauce with crunchy onions and scallions. There were too many crunchy onions, and the fish still had that slick, wet taste to it that's a little off-putting, but the whole dish is still good, and the rice is really well done.I also had the miso soup, which was a surprisingly good side. It has a great smokey taste that almost feels grilled, and the seaweed is thick and abundant.
This place is a hole in the wall but the pizza is legit! Very big pieces and generous toppings! And I mean, how crazy and yummy is it to have pasta on a slice of pizza? Absolutely loving it!

Calle Dao did not disappoint us! We made 6pm reservations and were seated promptly. We opted for apps instead of full meals. We got oysters, shrimp empanadas, tostones, beef sliders, and their wings. Everything was PHENOMENAL. All our food arrived SO quick but was hot and fresh. Flavors were spot on! Sangria was amazing (sweeter for a red sangria and didn't have that almost bitter dry taste many red sangria have to me). Our waiter was great and his support staff was super attentive. Great great service. Buyer beware - shrimp empanadas are very spicy (which we like).... and you only get 3 tiny ones for $12.... but so delicious! The wings were just killer! But it was all amazing. Can't wait to return! We were in and out in less than an hour which worked well for us.

Stopped in for a quick bite with my wife and parents. While the seating arrangement and ordering process was clumsy, the food was tremendous. For whatever reason the best Taco shops I've had across the country have inordinately complex ordering systems and awkward seating. Tried a carne asada and pollo taco as well as a adobada mula. All three where dynamite. While many taco shops/stands disguise poor quality meat and tortillas with loads of sour cream and pico, this spot did it right with fresh tortillas and exceptional meat. Growing up in Las Vegas I had high exposure to Taco spots and tacos are one of my favorite foods. This was one of the 5 best tacos I've ever had. Definitely the best Mexican food in the month I've been on the eat Coast.

Title: A Fiery Taste of Korea Lands in Ktown – Hong Chun Cheon

Hong Chun Cheon's New York outpost brings the sizzle of Korean cuisine to the heart of Ktown, proving itself a hot spot from the get-go. On a bustling Friday evening, the anticipation was palpable, with a throng of diners eager to indulge in the fiery fare. Despite a lengthy waitlist, the turnover was brisk—patrons simply listed their contact details and awaited the summoning call for an open table.

Tucked away in a somewhat clandestine second-floor locale, the ascent might seem dubious, but the crowd of expectant food lovers is a telltale sign of the culinary treasures that lay beyond the doors. Take note: contrary to misreports, duos must order a minimum of two servings, which, at $20 each, feels reasonable for the experience offered.

The star of the show is undoubtedly their dakgalbi, a delectable spicy stir-fried chicken, boasting a 100% organic label. Featuring a vibrant mix of sweet potatoes, cabbage, and other Korean staples, it caters to varying heat tolerances—my mild preference was accommodated, while my quest for extra spice was graciously met with a side of their hottest sauce.

Served in generous portions, the dish is centered around a pool of sumptuous melted cheese, perfect for meat-dipping. The addition of chewy rice cakes elevated the meal further, and the finale of crispy fried rice crafted from the remaining morsels was a delightful touch, although I found myself craving a simple side of rice to counterbalance the rich, sweet sauce.

Accompanied by a duo of banchan, or side dishes, the meal was a satisfying foray into Korean cuisine. While the sauce's richness might deter me from an immediate return, the leftovers did make for an enjoyable midday snack.

Hong Chun Cheon adds a robust flavor to Ktown's dining scene that is certainly worth exploring—for those who can handle a bit of a culinary wait and the ensuing spice-infused indulgence.

It was my second time back here, and I brought my mom and her friend for her birthday. Overall experience was fine, but a few points that stood out as a sore point was the fact they seated five of us at a small round table, resulting in a cramped dining experience. It was also noted in opentable that the dinner was for a double birthday celebration-- I wasn't expecting free anything but a candle or some type of acknowledgement would have been nice. A lot of restaurants have good food, but it's the overall dining experience and small details that make a place stand out.

Came here to grab my lunch.Tiny little cute Thai restaurant in Chinatown area.Lots of people order to go.They have lunch Special for $9.95 with one appetizer and one main dish.They serve the dish incredible fast. After I order. They serve everything in 5 mins.Everything taste decent. More like home style Thai dish. I recommend here for quick easy lunch.With good price and food!

Title: Authentic Pho with Generous Portions

I've frequented this spot since its inception, and it's my go-to for satisfying a pho craving. While it may not clinch the title for the absolute best pho I've tasted, their offerings are undeniably delectable. The space is compact, yet they compensate with their generous portions. My standard order includes the beef and brisket pho paired with their fresh spring rolls – both consistently good.

A few insider tips for a better experience: bring your own beverage as it's BYOB – pop next door to the deli for a cold drink, and the staff here are happy to provide a glass. Plan your visit accordingly as there are no restroom facilities, and if you're here for lunch, aim to arrive around noon to beat the rush. For those on a tight schedule, settle your bill when you order to avoid a last-minute rush.

In summary, it's a reliable place for a hearty meal, just come prepared and enjoy the fare.

I recently spent a Tuesday evening at La Avenida and can confidently say it's the go-to spot for happy hour. They offer enticing specials on both drinks and food, with the lively ambiance elevated by a live DJ who really knows how to set the mood. While the food, specifically the tacos, didn't quite live up to the high taco standards set by 116th Street's authentic offerings, La Avenida's frozen margaritas were the saving grace of the night. These are not to be missed! So if you're in for a good drink and great vibes, La Avenida has you covered—just maybe eat dinner beforehand if you're a taco aficionado.

In Hawaii we have very few really good Mexican food places to eat at. With that said, when we heard about this place and read the reviews, we had this place on our bucket list for sure. We hoped that the hype was real as we both have  been to Mexico a handful of times and have eaten our way around. So was the hype real?  Ok the answer is yes and no. No meaning that the tacos are a little bigger than the ones in Mexico but hey for $3.95 each it should be. We had the carne asada (grilled steak) and Pollo asado (grilled chicken) tacos and they both was very flavorful and had the nice char. The chips and salsa was one of the best we ever had. Ok first decide what you want and then stand in the line to order. The girl at the register was patient and explained what we need to do after we ordered. Make sure you get a ticket. If you don't, then you can't move down the line. Give the ticket to one of the guys behind the counter. Choose corn or flour tortilla. Then choose what you want inside. Wait for them to give you, your order and make your way to the sauce to add the amount of spice you want. Boom, then eat and get ready to say Oh Em!!!  If you don't like it here then go run back to the boarder to Taco Bell

I recently visited this local spot with high hopes for a scrumptious lunch sandwich, spurred on by numerous positive reviews. The takeaway process itself was seamless; my order was ready promptly, and pick-up was a breeze. However, the meal was a mixed bag.

The sandwich suffered from inconsistent spicing—one bite was mild, the next eye-wateringly spicy, turning each mouthful into a game of culinary roulette. Additionally, the cured meat in their house special banh mi was overpoweringly salty, detracting from the overall flavor.

On a positive note, the grilled pork sandwich was a standout, with a price of $8 representing fair value, although it didn't quite hit the mark set by my expectations. Ordering through a third-party app did limit customizability, which could have mitigated some issues. Despite the letdown, I see potential and wouldn't mind returning, hoping for a more even experience next time.

My latest New York dining adventure for a bestie's birthday bash led me to the lively Buenos Aires restaurant, which boasts a delightful fusion of Peruvian cuisine with an American twist. It's clear from the moment you step inside, where reservations are a must, that this hotspot is a beloved favorite; the place pulses with laughter, and the tantalizing aroma that greets you is enough to kick the appetite into overdrive.

With a boisterous party of 10, we were seamlessly accommodated, and the service couldn't have been more friendly or impressive. The food was the undisputed star of the evening, as we indulged in a feast that surpassed every expectation. The steaks, a particular highlight, were nothing short of perfection—robust in flavor and cooked to absolute precision.

Trust me, the visuals of our spread say it all, but you'll want to experience these flavors for yourself. Hands down, Buenos Aires is a must-visit for anyone looking to indulge in meaty magnificence with an international flair.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Health-Conscious Foodies

Tucked away on Cedar Street, far from its former glitz on Equinox, this unassuming cafe is a breakfast haven in Manhattan. It's a rare find where a hearty omelette, complete with toast and a hot cup of coffee, won't break the bank—even in the upper reaches of the city.

Walking in, I was pleasantly surprised to see a selection of Quest bars—a step above the dubious whey proteins that crowd most smoothie spots. This cafe caters to those of us who are meticulous about our fitness fuel. They even stock Isopure, a top-tier protein powder that underscores their commitment to quality.

Run by a charming Korean couple, this eatery is the no-nonsense health cafe of your dreams, minus the inflated prices. It's the go-to spot for both die-hard health enthusiasts and anyone looking for a good meal without the hype.

I am so sad that the food here was not very good.The drinks I have enjoyed but they aren't the cheapest either.The vibe is really the main draw of this place.Grabbing a few people and sitting in the open window during the summer is really nice. I'm playing hardball here, because I will probably return because I do enjoy the space, the service and the drinks were flavorful and strong BUT-If you are going to have a food-menu; I atleast expect it to be decent or just be a bar that serves drinks.3.2/5

I had a delightful experience at this local eatery, which stood out for offering great value for money – a pleasant surprise in the NYC area, likely due to its proximity to NYU. The shrimp panang curry I ordered was a highlight, striking just the right balance of spiciness. Overall, this spot is a real gem that I thoroughly enjoyed.

Excellent quality ramen spot! It was one of the first cold days of the season and I was craving something to warm me up. Totto offered quick service and delicious food that has the perfect amount of spicy kick to it. The noodles were thick and hearty. Definitely one of my favorite ramen spots in Manhattan!

Milk and Hops is a cool concept, combining hearty ramen meals with a good selection of craft beers. The food menu is straightforward, and while nothing is particularly mind-blowing, I appreciate the mix of ramen and lighter fare that's available.I've had spicy and classic miso ramen here. They aren't going to make your list of best ramen ever, but they definitely hit the spot and go well with beer. My friend let me try some of the jalapeno mac 'n' cheese -- also solid, but not standout.For drinks, there's a great selection of beers on tap, which is a selling point in my opinion. It's a nice change of pace to have a spot on the UES that serves good beers in a bright, modern setting, with a good food menu (rather than a dark, musky bar that has food as an afterthought).There's also a selection of cans for sale at the other end of the shop. You can take these to go, or pick one out to enjoy at the restaurant. Unfortunately, however, each can you open in-house comes with a $2 corking fee.And that's really why I couldn't give this place more stars. The prices are a little steep for a good, not great, experience. Still a good option for the area if you like beer but don't want to drink on an empty stomach. Just don't expect to spend less money than if you were to go to a swankier bar.

I recently visited a casual eatery with a vibrant graffiti art motif that instantly set a relaxed tone. It featured high tables against the walls and windows, and smaller ones scattered around for a cozy dining setup. 

The place operates on a "order at the counter" basis, allowing guests to then choose their preferred spot. The culinary highlight was undoubtedly the crispy goat sandwich, a delightful concoction of gouda goat, avocado, and bacon nestled between perfectly textured multigrain bread that was both crisp and tender. It was so delectable, one could easily be tempted to indulge in a second serving. 

To complement the meal, I had a hot apple cider that was served at an ideal temperature. It was imbued with an expertly balanced spice mix, offering a warm reprieve on a chilly winter day. 

The menu brimmed with enticing options, each seemingly as appealing as the next, compelling enough to warrant future visits just for the pleasure of taste-testing the variety of combinations on offer.

Tucked away in the bustling heart of the New York Stock Exchange district lies a gem of a pizzeria that hits the spot for any New York-style pizza aficionado. The menu featured an impressive selection of toppings from which we chose the pepperoni, honey chicken, buffalo chicken, and sausage pizzas—all of them utterly delicious and satisfying.

Despite its modest size, the place has a straightforward charm with an upstairs seating area that offers a cozy spot to dig in. A word of caution—the restroom could do with some TLC, as the soap dispenser was on its last legs during my visit.

Nevertheless, for a slice of authentic NY style pizza that promises to delight, this pizzeria is a definite go-to. It's a straightforward, no-frills establishment focused on delivering mouthwatering pizza that does not disappoint.

Title: A Seabass to Remember, a Sashimi to Forget

My recent dining experience was a journey of peaks and valleys. The star of the evening was undoubtedly the seabass, prepared masterfully to a point where I can confidently say it ranks as one of the best I've ever savored. It was a display of the Iron Chef's culinary prowess that I hoped to witness throughout the meal.

Unfortunately, the sashimi combo failed to live up to the high bar set by the seabass. In comparison to the renowned standards of Sushi Yasuda, the quality felt lacking, with a disappointing hint that it was not the freshest on offer.

Beverages, however, were a delightful surprise. Both the Morimoto iced tea and the yuzu-flavored mocktail were exceptional, showcasing unique and refreshing blends that excited the palate.

As for other dishes, the miso soup and tuna tartare hovered at the average mark—nothing to write home about, yet not detrimental to the overall experience, thanks to the excellence of the seabass.

Desserts were a mixed bag. The matcha panna cotta stood out with its refined flavor and creamy texture, while the other dessert, featuring a toasted coconut cracker, offered an interesting take typical of Asian-inspired, less sweet desserts.

In summary, while not every dish hit the high notes, the transcendental seabass and the innovative mocktails left a lasting impression that would beckon a return visit.

Title: A Warm Celebration with Cool Service

Our latest visit to celebrate my girlfriend's birthday was a testament to the restaurant's ability to handle a large party with grace. We were seated comfortably at a big table upstairs, and despite the lack of effective air conditioning on a sweltering day, the evening breeze eventually came to our rescue.

Our server was a standout—attentive, patient, and constantly checking in, a rare treat in a bustling eatery. The shared guacamole started us off well, while the mole short ribs I ordered were a hit, and my husband's steak fajitas did not disappoint. A last-minute addition of mac & chorizo turned into a shared delight and underscored the quality of our meal.

The cherry on top? The restaurant's generous check-in offer that gave everyone but the designated driver a complimentary prickly pear shot, making for a spirited end to a night of good food and great company.

I recently visited this restaurant for lunch and was pleased by the flavors on offer. The lunch special, priced at $13, was reasonable although the portion size left me wishing for a bit more on the plate. I opted for the classic dish and splurged an extra $2 for the purple rice, which in hindsight, didn't quite hit the mark for me. My adventurous side led me to choose the strongest level of mala, and while it was deliciously robust, I personally could have handled a bit more heat. One downside is the location – if only it were closer, I would certainly be a regular!

Title: Delightful Thai Fare from Thai72

Last evening, my first encounter with Thai72's cuisine was through a delivery that did not disappoint. The sweet and sour chicken was a flavor-packed delight, while the crepe dumplings presented an intriguing and delightful twist. The pad sew ew offered that perfect balance of savory and sweet that one craves in Thai noodles. Each dish was a hit, and I'd happily reorder them on my next culinary foray. My husband savored his cashew chicken, affirming Thai72's ability to consistently dish out quality Thai food. Our taste buds celebrated, Thai72 has secured itself as our new go-to for Thai cravings.

If the big friendly chocolate lab that we were able to pet outside while waiting for our table didn't automatically make this a 5 star night, the food, staff, decor and drinks took care of it. I'd say "Best Part of the Night" award goes to the dog for sure. But a VERY close second to Buffalo Chicken Mac & Cheese. Holy cow... They used big penne pasta, and lots and lots of cheese. Like, a ton of cheese. The chicken on top was incredible. Everyone at the table was raving about this damn chicken. I am not usually a fan of blue cheese, but the drizzle on top added a ton of flavor. Our table of seven split a large as an appetizer and it was the perfect size - just big enough so everyone had plenty, but didn't fill us up. For my entree, I couldn't decide between half the menu. Really, it was the Potato Crusted Salmon and the Fried Chicken and Toast. Very very different, but both sounded very very good. The salmon won. It was amazing. A very decent sized filet in a bed of really creamy sauce. I loved the crispy crust that covered the salmon and the taste of the cream sauce. I did wish it came with some sort of side like greens or potatoes or literally anything other than just the filet. But still 5 stars because of how good it was. Devoured it along side a glass of sauvignon blanc.  *kisses fingers dramatically* We came here on a Saturday night, as a group of 7, with no reservation. We knew it was a long shot, but we only had to wait about 20 minutes. And like I said, there was a dog there, so no one cared. This place was so trendy, I can't wait to come back and get that fried chicken and toast.

I recently ordered from a local sushi spot via Seamless and it turned out to be a delightful experience. I opted for the "Miso Over You" roll and a "Miami Vice" roll, which, to my pleasant surprise, came with a 15% discount on the $25 order. 

The delivery was swift, and the sushi exceeded my expectations—easily some of the best I've had recently. Both rolls boasted fresh ingredients, with a generous helping of avocado and fish that truly enhanced the flavors. The thoughtful addition of a tin for soy sauce was a nice touch to the overall presentation.

In conclusion, this was a great dining experience from the comfort of my home with sushi that was both delicious and fresh. I look forward to ordering again and would highly recommend it to other sushi enthusiasts.

Had read about this place as a top place to try uptown so when I was thinkIng about a place to meet a friend for dinner this popped into my mind. Made a reservation for 6 pm on a weeknight and I did not need to. My friend was there before me and ordered a beer for me to catch happy hour prices and they held on to mine til I got there so it would still be fresh/cold. I was only ten minutes after her so that wasn't necessary but it was nice. Service was nice and definitely not obtrusive. I ordered the drunken noodles. They were tasty, maybe a little messy to slurp, and were a little clumpier than in would have preferred but I will never not like a spicy bowl of noodles. I'll definitely be back to try more noodles.

Title: A Satisfying Bite at Shanghai Asian Cuisine

Craving soup dumplings, we dodged the longer waits and found ourselves at Shanghai Asian Cuisine – a bustling but cozy spot where a mere 10-minute wait was a pleasant surprise. Seated promptly, we dove straight into their menu, eager for the main attraction.

The scallion pancakes arrived crispy and aromatic, setting the stage for the star: the soup dumplings. We got both the pork and crab meat variety and the classic pork – each bite a burst of rich, savory broth and tender filling – absolutely spot on. To accompany our dumpling delight, we ventured further with an array of dishes: Vegetarian mock duck, Wonton Szechuan style, half wined chicken, along with shredded pork and preserved veg paired with rice cakes, and Shanghai Lo Mein loaded with mixed meat and shrimp. Each dish had its own charm, but the dumplings and pancakes were the clear winners. The wontons, though tasty, left us chasing the heat - a touch more spice would've hit the mark.

Would I return? Absolutely, for that dumpling fix, Shanghai Asian Cuisine in Chinatown is a no-brainer.

Title: Surprisingly Good Thai Fare with Strong Happy Hour Specials

I recently dined at this local Thai spot and was pleasantly surprised by the experience. The food was quite decent—appetizing Thai dishes with the right balance of spice and flavor. They got the meat-to-noodle ratio right, and the sauces complemented rather than overwhelmed the dishes.

During happy hour, the drinks were impressively strong and definitely gave you a bang for your buck. No watered-down cocktails here! Service-wise, things were smooth and speedy, with no hiccups during our visit.

The interior of the restaurant was spacious and modern, offering a comfortable dining environment. It was relatively quiet when we visited on a Tuesday at 5:30 PM, which made for a relaxed meal.

As for value, the pricing was very reasonable. You can grab a cocktail for $5 during happy hour, and noodle dishes are priced between $12-$15. The portions were generous enough to leave us feeling full and satisfied.

Overall, this place is a win, especially considering the scarcity of similar options in the area. Despite some negative reviews I’d seen, my experience was positive, and I’d come back for another round of Thai cuisine and drinks.

I came here for lunch on a Tuesday afternoon since it's close to my work.  My friend and I ordered their lunch specials.  I ordered the chicken curry, 2 veg, and rice for $9.95.  My friend ordered the lamb curry, 2 veg, and rice for $11.95.  I chose spinach (saag) and cauliflower (aloo gobi) for the 2 veg sides.  The lunch was cheap and filling since the portions were large.  However, the food was not flavorful and quite bland.  Indian food should be full of spices and flavorful.  The saag was watery and the cauliflower was dry.  The service was fast and friendly.  There was a lot of dine-in seating.  They also provided a pitcher of water on each table.  It was good to try this place out but with the large selection of Indian restaurants in the Curry Hill area, there are better options for lunch.

Really loved this open air on top lookout to the beautiful skyline of NYC and the brooklyn bridge. The drinks were good. We ordered sangria for our table and two pizzas. They have long tables which is good for big groups. As wells as they have separate areas to order your food and drinks. The atmosphere encourages good conversation as well as the music playing in the background is not too loud. We were there on a friday night and the place was packed but we were still able to find seating for a group of six. Would definitely be back at this spot.

AMAZING!!!!!!!!!!!! We literally had Ray's pizza every single night we were in our NY week vacation.  For being NY, I believe the prices are just right, and I love the fact they have a location near Times Square and another one near my Hilton hotel. Super convenient.  Also, staff was respectful and provided great service.

Talk about an amazing brunch. Stopped in because the founders are Michigan grads (Go Blue!) stayed for the super friendly service and great food.This restaurant is unique in that it's not a typical sit down. You stand in line to order at the counter before being escorted to a table. We went prime time on a Sunday morning and the wait was about 30 minutes.Though we didn't get to indulge ourselves, the sweets section looks absolutely delicious. Our friend was having a hard time deciding on which tea to order and the cashier made her a custom blend of his two favorite teas!Prices are fair for NYC- would definitely recommend.

As New Yorkers are starting to clear the streets and restaurants due to corona virus we did the irresponsible thing and took advantage of an empty restaurant and available table at Au Cheval. We had the entire restaurant to ourselves for most of our dinner. Got the single burger, which has 2 patties, with thick bacon and egg, a half order of fried chicken and side order of fries. So much flavor in my mouth with each bite. They have a very good beer selection as well. GO TRY IT for yourself if you can get a table. You will NOT be disappointed or leave hungry.

This is another hit from  the Quality Branded team (Quality Italian, Quality East and Don Angie are among their other excellent restaurants).Just open in midtown near Quality Italian, this one is as the name obviously implies, their take on a bistro with tons of excellent choices.Start with the Detroit Tarte Flambee ($12), which is like a Detroit style take on a flambee tarte, complete with roni cups, and as the helpful server suggested, a great snack to try as you peruse the large menu.I had dinner with a couple friends who are usually much more fun but were boring tonight and trying to be healthy, which explains the salads and the spring chicken and lamb chops we ordered. Luckily, all that was incredible too, especially the "Rouge & Bleu" ($16), a red beet salad that is a definite top candidate for salad of the year.I was the opposite of them and ordered the incredible French Onion Soup ($16), again one of the best takes on this I've had, with braised short rib and duck fat croutons swimming around. Then the Steak Frites ($45) were perfect too, and on the side, the insanely decadent and must try Truffle Basmati Rice ($16).Due to the aforementioned people that weren't down to eat fun, I just got one dessert, the excellent Black & White Profiterole Sundae ($12), a very good choice for some cookies & cream ice cream covered in chocolate fudge.It's a big menu, so I'm excited to come back to try lots more.

I stumbled along this cute spot while using my mealpal app. The selection looked hearty and healthy. It was seasoned chicken with farro and rice, a shaved brussels sprout salad with diced green apples, hummus, and a yogurt dill sauce for the chicken. It was so good! I would have liked it to come with pita for dipping the hummus but overall excellent dish.

Tucked inside Whole Foods is a cozy sushi bar offering a decent, if unremarkable, dining experience. While their chirashi falls short in portion size, merely a modest serving accompanied by a separate bowl of white rice, the sushi bar redeems itself with its simple rolls. Opting for the dragon roll or the spicy tuna roll is a safe bet for a satisfactory meal.

Title: A Festive Feast to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

Review:

My recent dinner at [Restaurant Name] on Christmas Day was nothing short of exceptional. Despite the last-minute nature of our booking through Resy, we were pleasantly surprised to secure a table for four at 5 PM. The staff graciously welcomed us at 4:50 PM, swiftly seating us and attending to our comfort.

The highlight of the night was our waiter, whose recommendations and service were impeccable. He suggested the Prime Rib Sandwich with Dip, which triumphantly became our favorite. His honesty regarding portion sizes was refreshing, advising us that we could order more later if needed—a gesture that speaks volumes about the restaurant's customer-centric approach.

Every dish we tried was a delight, from the succulent Rib Eye to the perfectly toasted truffle mac and cheese. While the gem salad proved a touch too salty, it was a minor hiccup in an otherwise flawless meal. The dessert—massive lemon meringue pie, paired with indulgent ice cream—was an absolute must-have.

Kudos to the staff for their prompt response in replacing a white wine that missed the mark, even offering complimentary samples to ensure satisfaction.

Overall, [Restaurant Name] delivered a memorable experience filled with culinary excellence. Securing a reservation is highly recommended to indulge in what can only be described as a remarkable dining affair.

Title: Scarpetta: When Reality Lives Up to the Legend

I'm typically skeptical when it comes to restaurant buzz, but Scarpetta deserves all the praise it gets—and then some. Let's start with the bread, specifically the sliced stromboli, packed with meat and cheese that's so good it should come with a cautionary label. And as an aside, the stunning ball chandelier adds a touch of splendor to the already charming ambiance.

But the real star here is the spaghetti. It presents itself modestly on the plate but don't be fooled—there's plenty there, and the sauce is the kind of culinary hug you remember for days. Rich, robust, and it clings to the pasta in a way that would make any Italian grandmother proud. Do yourself a favor and swirl in the provided creme fraiche and tomato reduction for an unforgettable taste sensation.

The braised short ribs, while delicious and fall-apart tender, might leave you wanting just a bit more, but they're an appetizer, so that's just quibbling. The table-side service is exceptional—attentive and gracious without being overbearing.

The fois gras ravioli was creamy and pleasing, though the flavor of fois gras was so subtle it could be easily missed. It's still a dish that satisfies the palate.

Make sure to book in advance—this place is a culinary hotspot for a reason. Oh, and when you go, don't you dare skip the bread or spaghetti. Trust me.
During this pandemic of COVID:19 this place has truly been amazing. They burgers are delicious and huge mouth watering. This is definitely a spot to go  to. It's on the Conner and you can't miss it.

Wow, it has been almost 6 years since my first visit at their 45th Street location. I only came here for their Stewed Pork Burger today. The line was wrapped inside the restaurant and pretty spacious. The cashier was taking the orders and yelling out orders too. I ordered the Stewed Pork Burger and asked whoever was preparing my food to change their gloves since they use a lot of cilantro which I hate. Definitely, a cheap eats spot for lunch! I waited not too long and quickly speed walk back to my office. Must do a photo shoot before consuming lol I love that they toasted the mantou then stuffed with that deliciously, flavorful stewed pork mmmm *mama like* hubby hubba *drools*I haven't tried their noodles yet. Maybe one day lol

I visited this restaurant for a lunchtime treat and was greeted by a queue that extended out the door, signaling its popularity. Once seated, I indulged in their Korean fried chicken, which impressed with its crispiness, further elevated by a harmonious blend of chili and sweet sauce. The slow-cooked pork belly was decent, though slightly on the dry side; however, the accompanying kimchi was nothing short of phenomenal, adding zest and complexity to the dish. The bulgogi hotpot was also a highlight, offering a deliciously rich and savory experience.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Udon Lovers - Raku

If you consider yourself an udon enthusiast, then a visit to Raku is a must. Tucked away on a quaint side street, this hidden gem might challenge you to find it, as there is no sign on the door, but the search is a part of its charm.

Despite its modest size and the inevitability of a wait—about 30 minutes for my companion and me on a bustling Saturday night—the seamless waitlist integration on Yelp is a godsend. Although the waiting space is limited, blending into the lively atmosphere of the place is all part of the experience.

Raku's extensive selection of udon dishes can make choosing a challenge, but you can't go wrong. While the niku udon seems to be a crowd-pleaser, we opted for the chikara and gyunan udons, paired with the chicken tatsuta-age. The speed of service was impressive, with our food arriving swiftly.

The chicken tatsuta-age was a highlight, available in 6 or 10 piece servings, boasting a light and crispy exterior that complemented the succulent chicken within. As for the udon, it's clear that Raku doesn't skimp on meat, and the mochi added a delightful chewiness. However, the star of the show was undoubtedly the noodles: fresh, perfectly chewy, and far from the dreaded sogginess often found elsewhere.

Service was attentive throughout, and the novel touch of a frozen grape to conclude our meal was both refreshing and appreciated. Serving sizes were generous, leaving us satisfyingly full with no room for more.

In summary, Raku has mastered the art of udon, delivering a simple yet beautifully executed dish that beckons for a return visit. It's a genuine showcase of quality over quantity, where every bite speaks volumes about their craft.

My partner and I chose to spend our date night at this charming restaurant, where the serene atmosphere was only enhanced by the limited number of guests. Attentive yet discreet service defined our dining experience, setting a comfortable tone for the evening.

Starting with the grilled octopus over a bed of spinach with Brussel sprouts and potatoes and a balsamic reduction, the dish struck a harmonious balance between sweetness, savory flavors, and a pleasant tang. The bouillabaisse, with its well-seasoned light tomato broth and a hint of spice, was satisfyingly hearty.

However, the sole meunière fell short due to its soggy, slimy skin, marring what could have been a flavorful dish. Fortunately, the evening was redeemed by a creamy and indulgent chocolate mousse.

While service can be leisurely here, the earnest efforts to please are apparent and appreciated. Our experience marked a significant improvement from a previous visit with prolonged dessert service. This meal was indeed a delightful surprise, showcasing the dedication to hospitality that should not be underestimated.

Title: A Gem With Excellent Service But Comes At A Price

I stopped by this eatery on a weeknight post-work and was greeted by a tranquil atmosphere that quickly livened up. The service was notably commendable, albeit the staff did tend to hover a bit too much for my liking—a slight over-attentiveness that led me to dock a star.

Culinary-wise, we indulged in an array of sashimi, grilled fish, succulent pork belly, and a savory salmon with rice dish. Each plate was a testament to the kitchen's prowess, with the sashimi’s freshness stealing the show, particularly the standout tuna varieties.

While I'm eager to return for another round of their diverse menu, it's worth mentioning that this place falls into the pricier end of the spectrum ($$$$). So, if you're planning a visit, consider your budget accordingly.

Went there as a Second option for dinner. Walked passed it a few times and always wanted to try but haven't had a chance until last night. When we walked in we were greeted and taken to a table with 2 guests already dinning. Wasn't too fond to share a table but I lived. We weren't sure where to order since we never been there and the waitresses were too busy chatting. They didn't bother asking if it was our first time there and if it is to please place your order at the counter behind us. We had to figure it out ourselves with a little help from the 2 other guests that was sitting across from us. We decided to feast so when I saw wagyu I knew that was what I wanted. It was just my boyfriend and I and We also got the sirloin, and assorted steak along with all the additional sides and the rice with garlic and pepper. Oh can't forget the takoyaki and sake. The chef Stephen was freaking AWESOME!! He gave us the best cut of what we ordered and he was great explaining the cuts to us. We ordered medium rare for everything but the assorted steak was cooked to well done. The waitress stoped by to check on us and I told her about the overcooked steak. Right away she offered to change it for us and apologized. Everything was amazing! The steak came back cooked perfectly each bite was like butter. I would definitely come back and bring my family next time! Check out the pictures.

We had a wonderful experience at this charming restaurant. The dining room's aesthetics were a delight, with beautiful plants embellishing the windows, creating a welcoming ambiance. The food was delectable; our taste buds danced with joy from the kohlrabi salad and the squash appetizer. Both the chicken and trout mains were flavorful, although I found myself craving a bit more protein on the plate. The portion sizes of the entrees were modest, so do keep that in mind if you arrive with an appetite. Our meal concluded with a delightful dessert that was both indulgent and considerately adapted to meet our dietary needs. This lovely eatery comes highly recommended for a tasty and aesthetically pleasing dining experience.

I got the hand pulled noodle soup with beef today, which was a lot better than the lamb. It was tender and flavorful. I ordered spicy but it was medium, in my opinion. My coworkers enjoyed their dishes as well. I will try their dumplings next time.

This place is a typical bar hangout. Came for a meet up with about 10 friends, they have ping pong and shuffle board and a bunch of TVs to watch spots. The service, was terrible. There is waiters walking around but I had to flag mine down every single time I needed him. Some of our party even just started ordering drinks and starting tabs at the bar because he was so slow. The beer flight I ordered, he didn't even get all the beers correct. Only reason I would come back is for the pretzel and free popcorn.

Title: A Tale of Two Experiences – Culinary Delight, Service Blight

I recently dined at a restaurant that could have easily earned a solid 5-star rating for its food and ambiance. The culinary experience was exceptional with a 2-course prix fixe menu that tantalized my taste buds. The watermelon gazpacho appetizer was an unexpected delight, making even a cold-soup skeptic like me a convert with its refreshing essence of watermelon. The Shakshouka entree followed suit in flavor, though it left me yearning for more with a surprisingly meager egg serving.

However, where taste soared, service unfortunately plummeted. The glacial pace of our waitress significantly dimmed the sparkle of our dining experience. Initial impressions were marred by a belated menu presentation and an inappropriate brunch menu offered during dessert time. A follow-up for our dessert order seemed to be a request too far as we were left abandoned by our server.

It's rare for me to remark on portion size as my appetite is generally modest, but this time the scant serving was noticeable. Despite the exceptional quality of the dishes, the lackluster service and unsatisfying portions clouded my overall satisfaction. Regretfully, I find myself disinclined to return for another round of outstanding cuisine countered by underwhelming hospitality.

WORST service EVER!!!! It wasn't even busy! I ordered Swordfish(tonight's special) and a side of French fries. My fries NEVER came. Fish was good but my waiter was less than average. I guess the girl next to me used to work here because she was getting A+ service. Getting checked on, hugs, kisses, the whole she bang! It took them 20 minute even offer me a dessert menu. I was going to order but I decided to skip it! The only reason I came was because it's close the hotel where I'm staying at! Will NEVER come back! Should have read the Yelp reviews first but I was so hungry after traveling all day!

Title: Mixed Experience with Standout Dishes

I ventured into this establishment for the first time last night and left with mixed feelings. On the upside, the deep-fried fish was a triumph—easily the best I've tasted. The mixed Sundubu jjigae was flavorful, though mild and unfortunately skimped on the shrimp, leaving me to wrestle with the shell. The Tteokbokki was another highlight, complemented by sides of fish cake, an egg, and dumplings, and the kimchi was notably good.

The downside? Service failed to match the quality of the cuisine. An extended wait time of 40 minutes versus the promised 20 set a disappointing tone. Staffing appeared to be thin on the ground, leading to inattentive service that bordered on rudeness. While the pickled radish and bok choy were forgettable and I personally avoid mayo-based salads, those missteps were minor in comparison to the service issues.

Though the food has potential, the dining experience was marred by the lackluster service—an area in desperate need of improvement.

I recently dined at this establishment and opted for the lobster bisque followed by the junior NY sirloin. While the bisque was creamy and enjoyable, it fell short on the lobster content and missed the rich, eggy quality I look for in a bisque. The sirloin, on the other hand, was quite the opposite, boasting an impressive char and surprising generosity in size for a "junior" portion. The steak’s tenderness and fat marbling were spot on. Unfortunately, the sides of green beans and potatoes did not meet the same standard, arriving undercooked and rather lackluster.

I've been trying to make a reservation at Nur for probably a year. Finally my friend was able to snag a reservation for four on Monday at 7:30 PM. The inside of Nur is beautiful and the place was totally packed - which is surprising for a Monday. You can tell this restaurant is loved by many people.I've been wanting to try the eggplant carpaccio for what feels like a million years. It did not disappoint. I loved the date syrup that went over the top. For this dish you definitely need to order one of the breads. We went with the Kubaneh which was absolutely delicious. Don't come to Nur without ordering these two dishes.We also tried the Caesar salad which was very good, but it had probably a tablespoon of za'atar seasoning just plopped on top. We should've mixed it around - it would've been helpful for our waiter to advise. I love that it had more than just Romain lettuce, like baby broccoli and kale.For mains among 4 we shared the octopus and the souvlaki fish. The octopus was very good, but not mind blowing. There was Greek yogurt and tahini, but there was much more yogurt and tahini than octopus. I feel like a dish could've been more balanced. With the souvlaki fish it was tasty but it was all piled in such a way where I couldn't differentiate what I was eating. I think the price point was a little high.I'd be happy to come back and try more of the menu if I'll ever be able to land another reservation. Until next time!

On our visit to the restaurant on a Sunday morning, we were pleasantly surprised to find it less crowded than anticipated. The service was notably attentive and thoughtful, as our waiter kindly brought us a complimentary blueberry muffin to celebrate our anniversary—a delightful touch! The Huevos Rancheros was the highlight of our meal, packed with flavor and generously portioned; it was easily enough for two to share. While the grains and greens bowl was enjoyable and scored a solid 7/10, it would have benefited from a heartier serving of grains. Overall, the experience was positive, and this establishment has definitely earned a return visit from us.

Came here for happy hour yesterday and was very impressed with the ambience from the moment I walked in. The decorations were gorgeous and overall created a great happy hour atmosphere. We sat at the bar and were able to enjoy watching the chefs craft the different rolls and dishes. I ordered the arigato set and chose chicken karaage, edamame, and sake, which was a pretty good deal for only $10. We then ordered some of their $1 oysters.  I'm not usually a huge fan of oysters, but with all the sauce and garnish, these were very palatable for me. I wish there were a couple more food options on the happy hour menu, but overall it was a good time.

The food was good.  The leg of lamb was flavorful and perfectly cooked.  We also had the mussels with frites.  The sauce was delicious!  The calamari was also yummy.  The one gripe I have is that the crowd was super rowdy that night and the waitress dropped my fork onto my dress and stained it.  She did not really do much about it.  Wouldn't you generally comp a drink or a small appetizer or *something* for that blunder?  I thought it was a bit rude.  Nevertheless, the food was good and the decor was innovative.

Title: A Slice of New York Perfection

After visiting the most raved-about pizzeria in New York, I understand the hype. The pizza here sets a high bar, beginning with a sauce that is notably sweet and fresh, steering clear of any unpleasant tanginess. The crust strikes an ideal balance—thin, yet satisfyingly chewy, never crossing into the territory of a cracker.

Where this pizza truly shines, however, is in its impeccable cheese to sauce ratio. Each bite is a testament to the art of pizza simplicity. I'd even argue that the pizza is best enjoyed unadorned; additional toppings seem to compete with the sauce's standout flavor rather than complementing it.

A word to the wise: Time your visit wisely to dodge the long lines. While the pizza is a treat, it's best savored without the preamble of a lengthy wait.

A wonderful French wine bar with great service and ambiance. The staff knows their stuff and they have a broad selection that will satisfy any oenophile. They also have a mystery white and red every night. If you order one of the mystery wines and correctly identify it, you get a bottle. If you are wrong, you pay for the glass of wine. The food menu is limited and just ok.

I regret to inform fellow diners that my recent experience at a restaurant near Madison Square Garden was underwhelming. With the city's vast culinary landscape, it was unfortunate to have hastily chosen such a lackluster establishment due to time constraints.

Although we were promptly seated by a cordial hostess who doubled as our server, the simplicity of the menu was not the minimalist chic one might hope for, but rather uninspired. Our ordered food arrived quickly, yet my burger was so devoid of taste that after a couple of bites, I abandoned it entirely. The saving grace of the meal were the waffle fries, which were decent enough to sustain me for the remainder of the evening.

In hindsight, this venue seems better suited for large groups seeking a place to catch a sports game, with its ample space and quintessential bar food offerings. However, for those in search of a memorable dining experience, it would be wise to look elsewhere amidst the city's abundant options.

I really liked this place the service was great our waitress was super friendly and the drinks were on point. I ordered the whatcha matcha which tasted like a super healthy green smoothie and my friends got the where's Dallas which has yuzu in it? However I don't recommend the oysters it was super fishy... we got the happy hour special west coast oysters and we found a dead baby crab on one of the oysters. I know it's normal for crabs to be on oysters but as a chef you should at least clean it out or rinse it before serving.

The Smith stands as a quintessential emblem of the New York weekend brunch scene, a fact I experienced firsthand during a bustling Sunday visit. Despite its packed halls, the establishment did not falter in delivering sumptuous fare. The Cinnamon Toffee Brioche, a behemoth of sweetness akin to a caramel-drenched cinnamon roll, proved irresistible, nearly devoured in its entirety.

Ever the eggs benedict connoisseur, the Benedict Johnny intrigued with its delectable twist: a cheddar cornbread foundation topped with maple chicken sausage and poached eggs, all crowned with a roasted tomato hollandaise. Accompanying home fries offered a delightful contrast of textures. The Smith may embody the archetype of a "basic brunch" locale, yet it distinguishes itself with superb cuisine and waitstaff adept at providing impeccable service amidst the weekend rush.

This place is delicious and the customer service is pretty good too. There is never a time I have gone here and my food takes more than 5 minutes to come out. It tastes fresh, delicious and the price is pretty good too. The lemonade is fresh and unlike other places, they'll be happy to give you a refill without paying. The cookie has huge chunks of chocolate chips and if you stuffed your face too fast and need a box to go, no worries, they'll be happy to accommodate. The place is pretty big and plenty of seatings, bathrooms are very clean and the perks for spending your money here are not bad. Wish all places had that...will come here whenever I am in New York. On another note, I really hope they open one in DC as I think this place will be loved down here in the hipster hoods.

Madame Vo BBQ recently hosted my boyfriend's birthday dinner, and our anticipation was high given my previous delightful experience. We kicked off our meal with a fresh young coconut - a refreshing, though not unique indulgence, as similar coconuts are available for less in Chinatown.

While I eagerly anticipated the generous portions from my first visit, I noted a slight reduction in quantity, receiving four meatballs instead of six and a visibly smaller beef carpaccio. Despite this, the meal remained ample with plenty of rice wrappers and sides to go around. A highlight was the five-star service, particularly when our server kindly provided complimentary beef tongue after learning about the birthday celebration.

The 45-day dry-aged steak did not disappoint, especially after a keen server intervened to prevent it from overcooking - though my preference leans towards an even rarer preparation. Unfortunately, the oxtail congee fell short of expectations. The flavor profile that once danced with a harmonious mix of honey butter, fish sauce, and soy was now overwhelmed by saltiness, and the usually tender oxtail was unexpectedly tough.

Despite this misstep, the overall experience was positive. Though the congee's inconsistency will make me more cautious in future recommendations, Madame Vo BBQ's appeal endures, and I am open to returning and rediscovering the magic of my initial visit.

I used to work in the area, and would come here during happy hour once in a while.  It hasn't changed a bit.  However, they added flamenco dancing on Monday nights.  I used to love that at ~N on Crosby street, but since that has closed years ago, I'd love to check that out.Stopped in for a reasonable lunch. $14 for a bowl of hearty lentil soup with chunks of ham that really blew me away.  That with the small side of bread an olive oil was a meal by itself.  But wait...it also comes with a nice half sandwich of your choice.  I opted for the chicken, which is served with some nice, fresh, kettle chips.  I needed to take that home for dinner.  Throw in a glass of $5 red sangria that was SPOT on and hit the SPOT and I was out of there for under $20+ tip.This is the kind of NYC place, where you're really transported to another world.  I'm so happy to see it's still here.  I'll be back soon.

Title: Happy Hour Haven with a Cozy Village Vibe

I stopped by this charming eatery during Happy Hour and found myself smitten with its village-like ambiance. The Krankie, a featured cocktail, was a standout – absolutely delicious. The Scotch Egg also impressed with its perfectly runny yolk. While the Sausage Roll was simply passable (though the accompanying sauces were quite tasty), the Beef Wellington provided value at $35, a steal compared to upscale alternatives, despite a slightly heavy-handed sauce.

Regrettably, the Whiskey Cake dessert fell short, arriving tardily, tasting dry, and missing the promised whiskey flavor. On a brighter note, the staff were exceptionally friendly and the restaurant quickly became a bustling hub. Despite the dessert misstep, the experience was overall quite delightful.

Stopped in on a Friday around 8 just for drinks and loved the creative cocktail choices on their menu. We didn't get any food, but the drinks were top notch and the bartender and waiter were very friendly and attentive. It also wasn't crowded yet nor was it too loud so it easy to have conversation.Great spot for a drink, and an easy walk (from across the street) if you're staying at the Courtyard Marriott.

I am one of those people who orders the same thing every time--chicken caesar salad with sweet potato topping and/or boiled egg and light ranch dressing. I've never taken issue with the taste, and with the NYU discount and friendly service, I keep coming back. Plus, free wifi and bathroom don't hurt.Some issues I take with the place:- Up until maybe my last 2 orders, they always get my name wrong. I remember once they put my name as Jackie.- The service could be better. Often times I'm at the checkout counter just waiting for someone to appear.- Tables gotta be cleaned regularly. As we all know, some customers are not great at tidying up after themselves.- The new 2 for $12.99 deal sounds good if you want to have more than one item to eat, but let me tell you, that salad is smol. So smol in fact, that I wish I had just gotten the regular salad for $9.- That crunchy avocado toast would've been good, except the "spicy avocado" is genuinely very spicy. I thought it would've been like a white person level kind of spicy, but wow, I had to take gulps of water in between each bite...

This is a great place for a birthday dinner or a date night. Came here for a friends birthday with a group of girlfriends. The ambience is perfect. We did a pre fixe menu so had a little taste of everything. They had everything from beet salad, eggplant appetizer, charcuterie, pastas, fish, chicken, and a variety of desserts. Overall it was all pretty good quality and nothing lacked flavor.

Title: A Rocky Start with a Stellar Finish

Upon arrival, my initial impressions of the restaurant dipped as I was seated in an unwelcoming back room, where a chilly breeze and less-than-pleased fellow patrons hinted at a disappointing experience ahead. The discomfort seemed to brush against potential undertones of racism, though I can't fault the establishment for the prejudices of others.

However, setting those first encounters aside, the staff immediately stepped up to improve our experience, sealing out the cold and displaying outstanding hospitality that was both friendly and engaging. The dim sum here must be applauded; each piece was crafted to perfection without the all-too-common pitfalls of gummy textures sometimes associated with dark meat chicken. The attention to detail in their dishes truly shone through, and the pricing was unexpectedly reasonable for the area.

Despite the rocky start, the culinary delights firmly anchored my experience in the positive. The photos of our meal speak for themselves, but I'd happily speak for them too—I'd re-order every item we tried in a heartbeat.

While walking by with my Sister. We happen to notice my Aunt and Cousin sitting, so we stopped in to have lunch at this place. Personally, this place is alright and average (I have been to many restaurants in KTown that are worth trying), I felt like the palette was not dancing around. For the appetizer, I had the SHANGHAI DUMPLINGS (Minced pork and vegetable dumplings drizzled with your choice of sauce: GARLIC) which was very good but felt like it could have been more flavorful. For Lunch Entree, I had the MOZZARELLA SEAFOOD DUKBBOKI (Spicy, Soft, and tender rice cakes covered in a spicy sauce, seafood, and mozzarella) which was great but felt like the Mozzarella was a little too overbearing. While eating the dish a piece of clamshell got into my mouth and I accidentally bit into it. I would recommend this place to others. The service is well and the food came out quickly.

I recently had the pleasure of trying the "Red Cooked" Beef Noodle Soup at Ho Foods and it did not disappoint! The broth was flavorful and pleasantly surprising, elevating the dish beyond the usual offerings. The beef was cooked to perfection, tender and melding beautifully with the soup's rich taste. While I opted for thinner noodles, which were quite satisfying, I'm already looking forward to returning to sample the wider noodles. Ho Foods has definitely put their unique stamp on this classic dish, and it's a must-try for noodle lovers!

Super romantic - small and authentic - delicious. Incredibly priced for NYC!!!My wife and I have been here a few times. Once for drinks and apps. Twice for the tasting menu. Both are awesome. I strongly recommend the tasting menu or apps so you can sample as much as possible off the menu. Everything is phenomenal. We like to sit at the bar. Bartenders will keep food and drinks in front of you without being pushy but keeping the perfect pace. Maurizio (the owner) has served us twice. He's a great guy. Wants to know what you like before he picks out what he's going to serve you. Definitely adds to the experience. He will also pick you the absolute perfect wine pairing. Soup - 5 starApps - 5 star meatballs or brussel sprouts with pancetta - wow! Pasta - 5 star - short rib pasta or linguine with clams - insaneEntres - 4 star - lamb shank is insane the rest of the entres are great but not 5 star Desert - 5 star - I don't get desert but I do here. Awesome!!!Prices and service 5+++You and your significant other will leave drunk and very happy.

I recently had the pleasure of trying the Bulgogi Bibim Rice Bowl at a local Korean eatery, and it was a delightful experience. The dish was brimming with authentic flavors and truly lived up to the expectations one would have of Ktown's cuisine. For those in a hurry or seeking a cozy meal without the lengthy wait times, I can't recommend it enough. It's absolutely worth a visit for a quick, flavorful bite.

I recently ordered from this restaurant for the second time, enticed by a promotional deal. Both deliveries arrived on time, with the chicken hot, well-packed, and without any spills. My first order was flawless—the chicken perfectly cooked, deliciously crunchy, and truly lived up to my expectations.

On my second go, I opted for the same choice – the combo with 4 wings and 3 drumsticks doused in extra spicy hell's sauce for $13. There was a bit of inconsistency with the order, as I received 2 wings and 4 drumsticks, plus one unidentifiable piece of chicken. The sizes of the drumsticks varied as well. While the promised heat of the sauce was more of a mild zing, it was still rich in flavor, and the crunchiness of the chicken did not disappoint.

Price-wise, it's reasonable for NYC standards, but the inconsistency in the order and the wing to drumstick ratio make me hesitant to order for a third time. I'm inclined to say that Black Bear in Hoboken still holds the title for my favorite wings.

Title: A Taste of Authentic New Mexico at [Restaurant Name]

I recently had the pleasure of dining at [Restaurant Name], a gem serving authentic New Mexican cuisine, and it was a delightful discovery. This isn't your typical Mexican food; it's a genuine taste of the flavors unique to New Mexico, slightly unfamiliar yet entirely comforting.

Their chicken skins are a signature dish for a reason, crispy perfection that you'll be thinking about for days. We ventured into the appetizer menu, which offers an intriguing array of veggie dishes, but settled on the fry bread with peas, a choice heartily endorsed by our attentive waiter, Joseph.

The main event was a charred cabbage dish, a life-changing seasonal entree that we shared alongside our three appetizers. The cabbage was perfectly charred, lending a smoky depth that complemented its natural sweetness.

The seating at [Restaurant Name] included comfortable couches, contributing to the light and airy ambiance that made the dining experience even more enjoyable. Joseph's enthusiasm about the menu was infectious, and his recommendation for the entree was spot-on.

Though the wine list lacked a familiar Sauvignon blanc, it presented an opportunity to explore the unknown under Joseph's knowledgeable guidance, transforming wine selection into a delightful tasting journey.

In summary, [Restaurant Name] is a must-visit for anyone seeking an authentic taste of New Mexico's culinary heritage, served with a side of top-notch hospitality.

I came here for the Sunday lunch during restaurant week. I do appreciate how they offer restaurant week on Sunday as many other places do not.I had mussels as the appetizer and they were great. They were in a creamy but light buttery sauce and the portion was generous.For the entree, I had the steak frites. Honestly, the steak was not as huge of a portion size as I had seen on yelp or it definitely looked better in the pictures, yet once I started eating it I was pleasantly surprised by how filling it was. The fries were perfect. I liked the béarnaise sauce (sort of tasted like hollandaise) that came with it as well. As a dessert, (not included for lunch's restaurant week), we tried the prickly pear sorbet and the crême brûlée. The crême brûlée was some well except I was a little disappointed there were no fruits on top. The prickly pear sorbet was very rich in flavor. I recommend it for a sweet yet tangy choice. Overall, I think the food was 4 stars but the service was amazing (definitely five stars) and I just loved the ambiance. We were seated on comfortable couches, the mirrors, and blue/green textured wallpaper, made it a charming atmosphere. We stayed and relaxed as we ate our meal for 3 from 12 noon until 3 pm.

I visited Artichoke for the first time around 6:30pm last Friday. When you enter, you'll be greeted with hot, hot air. You might feel like you can't breathe. I don't know if they have AC or not, but that is how my friend and I felt.We ordered one slice of the artichoke pizza and one slice of the crab pizza. The crab pizza was good. It was light and we could definitely taste the crab. However, the artichoke was heavy, too heavy for our liking. I managed to finish my half of the slice, but my friend could not and he is a "foodie." I felt a little sick after the artichoke pizza because of the creamy sauce.

So I was impressed! 88 Lan Zhou definitely has a hole in the wall feeling. It is not  a fancy place and you more than likely will share a table with a couple of other parties but DAYUM the food is good! The price point is excellent too and you can not go wrong with anything you order.I think I love this place due of my love for hand pulled noodles. You can order different noodles styles as well as dumplings. Everything is flavorful, fresh and tasty. The price per dish is less than $10 and in New York that is quite a deal! We ordered a couple of noodle dishes, dumplings and a peanut dumpling dessert. It was all fantastic and we brought some food back to the hotel since the servings were generous.This place is solid for food, just do not expect great service. It is what it is really. Just order your food and eat! ;)
This place is awesome for a little happy hour that's close to grand central. Great appetizers and $1 oysters! Cool atmosphere and good drinks.

I was surprised that I had never been to this restaurant before since it is so centrally located, so I am glad a friend suggested it after he asked if I like Greek food. (Duh... That's like asking if I enjoy ice cream or love unicorns) The interior is spacious and sophisticated with comforting earthy colors.We were served complimentary slices of warm pita bread with olive oil. This was really tasty, soft and toasted to just the right amount.  For my meal, I ordered the combination platter of gyro (ground lamb sirloin), bifteki (ground beef), and souvlaki (marinated cubes of pork). This came with lemon potatoes and a nice sour cream & dill sauce, which made everything taste that much better. There was plenty of each meat. I enjoyed the pork the best since it was marinated which boasted a delightfully intense flavor. It was also extremely tender and charred to perfection. The lamb was also yummy, full of wonderful seasoning. I wasn't a huge fan of the beef though. The potatoes were decent and had a nice consistency. The flavor of lemon was fresh and there were plenty of spices.I also got to try my friend's Greek salad, made of lettuce, feta cheese, and olive oil dressing. It was simple but good. When done with the food, I asked for a dessert menu and our waiter indicated there was none because there were only 2, which he verbally told us about. I decided to order the baklava. A large slice of baklava was served on a square plate with honey drizzled on top, along with smatterings of cinnamon on each corner. It was nicely sticky and chockful of nuts but was a bit too sweet even for me. Service and overall experience were pleasant throughout our time. I would be open to returning, but not for a while because nothing else on the menu really popped out for me that I felt I need to try.

Got their famous highest quality pork tonkatsu- not gonna lie it was pretty dry and overpriced for what you get. Flavors are good but nothing special.Best part is that the beer is cheap $4 a glass and $16 a pitcher. Probably wouldn't go back.Also there was a mouse on the bench on the adjacent table of diners near us. An actual mouse.

Title: Style Over Substance at L Room Café

Having been tantalized by the alluring images of L Room Café on Instagram, my anticipation to visit was high. My friend and I chose a quiet Tuesday afternoon for our experience, finding ourselves the sole patrons for a brief moment. The café exuded a millennial charm with its picture-perfect decor reminiscent of a pop-up museum – all very Instagrammable.

However, the charm waned upon closer inspection. Eager for a sweet treat, I opted for the vanilla ice cream with cotton candy, an enticing combo that promised a feast for both the eyes and the palate. Yet, the reality was a letdown. At $8, the dessert was underwhelming, a basic offering that failed to justify its price tag.

In essence, L Room Café is a classic case of style triumphing over substance. While your camera might feast on the visuals, your taste buds might beg to differ. My advice? Save your money and look past the façade for an eatery where quality matches the aesthetics.

Title: Mixed Experience with Room for Improvement

My visit to this restaurant on a Friday evening started off confusing, with no host to greet us and an antiquated sign-up board serving as the only guide for seating. Though our wait was brief, the lack of attention to the sign-in process left us questioning who was managing service.

My husband and I both ordered the Koku Ramen, requesting the mild variant. Unfortunately, a mix-up resulted in him receiving the hot version, causing an uncomfortable dining experience for him – his dish was visibly redder and resulted in profuse sweating. Despite this, my mild ramen was quite enjoyable, featuring tasty, firm noodles. The pork char siu, however, fell short in tenderness.

The char siu buns were satisfactory but would benefit from juicier, more tender pork. Service faltered again when we had to remind the waiter twice about our missed chicken karage order. Despite this hitch, the chicken karage proved to be the star of the evening – tender, juicy, and flavorful.

The restaurant offers fair prices and a happy hour deal on appetizers until 6pm. The interior is spacious and brightly lit, with a clean layout. A minor inconvenience was encountered with the bathroom running out of paper towels.

We plan to give this spot another chance during lunchtime to take advantage of their tempting $9.99 special. Hopefully, my husband will have a better experience trying the mild ramen then, and we’re optimistic the service will see an improvement.

Rating: 3/5 stars

I've been coming to BCD Tofu House for years and I'm always impressed by the consistency of quality and speed of service. Their tofu soups are delicious and affordable (the kimchi is the best / most flavorful) and they have excellent starters that rotate in and out -- kimchi, pickles, braised beef, mung beans, etc. The little fried fresh is also a great way to whet the appetite.For apps, I highly recommend the jap chae (glass noodles with onions, green onions, and beef) and the seafood scallion pancake. Really awesome stuff!

Sunday Brunch at this spot is a must-try! I suggest making a reservation; I did so for noon and even got seated a bit early by the friendly hostesses. The high table we snagged gave us a front-row view of the amazing jazz band playing from 11-3pm - an experience I highly recommend.

Our server was incredibly sweet and attentive, offering perfect drink recommendations. I started with the Paisley Fields cocktail from the brunch menu - a refreshing blend with a hint of spice for $12. I also tried the Gordon's Cup, another revitalizing choice, and the Ten Thousand Words for $16, which was a delightful bartender's surprise concoction.

For food, I indulged in the Hen of the Woods - a crispy mushroom delight that even a non-vegan would savor. The portion was generous, and it came with a hefty serving of fries. 

Overall, I had a fabulous experience with great atmosphere, staff, food, and drinks. I'll definitely be returning!

Prince Street Pizza still holds its charm, but perhaps the hype has raised expectations a bit too high. Returning to what was once an under-the-radar gem, the experience wasn't the nostalgic delight I had hoped for. The pizza, while decent, lacked that crispy crust and succulence; it teetered towards the dry and bland side, save for the pepperoni-covered half of my slice, which did pack a flavorful punch. The staff's demeanor was neutral - not particularly warm but by no means cold. Although Prince Street remains a good spot for a slice, there are now other pizzerias that have stolen my heart and taste buds.

I recently visited a charming tiki bar that perfectly blended a casual pub vibe with a festive Christmas theme, on the recommendation of my local sisters. The staff was decked out in thematic shirts, adding to the ambiance of the place. The highlight of my experience was savoring their seasonal drinks, especially the 'Blue Christmas' - a delightful concoction of curaçao and vodka, and the 'Reindeer Shot', which tickled my palate with its chocolate peppermint notes. Whether you're looking for a fun group outing or just adore tiki settings, this spot is a must-visit for its unique twist on holiday cheer.

Located in the bustling heart of midtown, this restaurant boasts an intriguing setting with a view that captures the essence of the area. However, it falls into the typical 'clubby' bar category, with an unpredictable atmosphere that swings from being eerily quiet to overwhelmingly crowded. The second floor features a retractable roof, which is a nice touch, but unfortunately, the high walls obstruct what could be a magnificent panoramic of Times Square. As anticipated, the drink prices are on the steep side. I didn't sample the food and my visit was brief, so I can't speak to the overall dining experience.

Visited a local bar with ample space, a rare find in this neighborhood, making it a solid choice for drinks. However, the culinary experience fell short. Tried the Mac and Cheese and guacamole - both passable, but the much-hyped gold wings were a disappointment. They looked great on Instagram, but the taste was underwhelming. My recommendation: stick to the beverage menu. Food isn't the draw here, so I'll likely only return for the drinks.

Title: Exquisite Dining Experience

The acclaim of over 2500 reviews sets the bar high, yet our experience at this esteemed restaurant soared above expectations. Our meal was sublime, each dish a beautiful testament to the chef’s culinary expertise. Though the seasonal tasting menu leaned heavily on seafood, which isn't our favorite, the a la carte three-course menu offered a delightful alternative. Securing a reservation may require some patience, but the exceptional food served is a testament to the demand. A dining pleasure we’d eagerly recommend.

My friends and I came for a quick bite before a show, I had eaten lunch but just needed a little something more to tide me over. I got the seaweed salad and a hot green tea for a very good price, my friend got the Japanese crispy chicken bun and she was it was good and didn't leave a heavy feeling (which in our opinion is the lost important part). Would definitely come back for the reasonable prices and speed of food delivery.

The restaurant impressively maintains its high standards, delivering delicious cuisine that continues to delight. It's a bonus that their offerings remain among the most affordable in the area, providing exceptional value without compromising on quality. Highly recommended for a satisfying meal that won't break the bank.

First U.S. location, this is a fun and interesting restaurant.  The price for the fish change based on market price but we paid under $40 per fish. (Not by weight). If you fish your own dinner, it's slightly cheaper (which is great).  Fishing: They give you a poncho in case you get wet, and once you fish they do some ceremonial shouting, which was interesting. Once you catch a fish you have to take it, you buy, PERIOD. And because it's not by weight but per fish, get the biggest one! :) Salmon was very large and heavy and cost the most I think it was over $100 that day. but would be perfect if you had a large party. Food: You can choose different type of dish you want prepped with your fish, you can even ask for half/half, so you can try 2 different versions. We had 2 whole fish so tried 4 different versions. There is a long list of ways you want your fish cooked. They also have a normal menu. Faculty: It is a new establishment, so things are new and clean. Walking in, you will see a bottom of a huge ship floating in the ceiling, which is actually the second floor. They also have lobster and other seafood in tanks on 2nd floor. Experience: fun experience for all, especially family. It's a different kind of dining experience, everyone should try once for fun.

I had a delightful dining experience recently at a spot that boasts classic flavors and an inviting outdoor seating area. The atmosphere was perfect for a relaxed meal. My friend and I both chose the scramble with goat cheese and broccoli, and the kitchen was very accommodating when we asked to substitute the goat cheese for cheddar. The service was exceptional, adding to the overall positive experience. Highly recommended for anyone looking for great tastes and a comfortable setting.

I recently dined at this charming spot and was instantly smitten by its ambiance, making it an excellent choice for a romantic date night. The standout for me was the clay pot catfish, which was not only bursting with flavor but also generously portioned, allowing me to enjoy it for two meals. It reminded me of the comforting dishes from my childhood. My companion chose the khao soi, a curry dish with crispy noodles. Watching the noodles absorb the rich curry was a delight — the dish was packed with robust flavors. For New York, the prices are reasonable. I'm eager to revisit and savor the khao soi myself. I highly recommend giving this restaurant a try!

This is a fun spot! Very lively and they have comfy seats. I stopped by here for a cocktail and I was not disappointed.
