The prices are steep, typical NYC cocktail prices, but they will load up your drink so you get your money's worth. I would recommend this spot for friends to catch up and chill. The guac and chips were ok, could have had a pinch more flavor

Title: Decent Ramen Experience at Ippudo with Stellar Karaage

Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3.7/5)

My visit to Ippudo left me with mixed feelings. Expecting a sensational bowl of Akamaru ramen, I found it fell short of the exhilarating experiences touted by its fans. The broth was notably rich, and the noodles carried a satisfying chew, which I appreciated. The accompaniments of black mushrooms and scallions added a pleasurable texture and flavor to the mix. However, the chashu failed to impress, lacking that wow factor I've relished in other ramen spots like Ichiran.

On a brighter note, the karaage chicken was a revelation. Contrary to the lukewarm Yelp reviews that had initially made me apprehensive, the chicken was incredibly tender and flawlessly fried, making me grateful I decided to take the plunge.

In sum, while Ippudo is a competent contender in the ramen arena, it wouldn't be my first port of call for a bowl of noodles. Yet, for anyone with a penchant for perfectly prepared karaage, Ippudo is absolutely worth the visit.

3.5 stars for food4.5 stars for serviceWe had the spicy tuna and Yuzu scallop, yucca and cheese croquettes, snapper triadata, duck risotto, pork belly and cheese skewer and the chicken skin skewer. I thought the seafood dishes were all average at best. I did not think the seafood tasted very fresh and the scallop was actually really fishy. I had to cover it up with the taste of lime. The yucca and cheese croquette was pretty good but on the heavy side. The skewers were delicious and felt like they added their own twist to traditional Japanese yakitori. The pork belly with the cheese was amazing and loved the contrasting textures. I will say I was pleasantly surprised by the duck risotto. The duck was cooked nicely but was not too amazed by the flavor. The risotto itself with the quinoa was so creamy and delicious! It was my favorite item of the night, just wish it wasn't a whopping $42. Service was really good and attentive. The food in general was solid but I do not think seafood is their forte. Prices were also a bit on the expensive side.

Came here on my birthday for dinner with my husband, I always like to try something new on special occasions, and the playboy club was highly recommended by someone. Reservations were easy on a Thursday night, I also made a note that I am celebrating a birthday. When we arrived we were greeted by a bouncer at the front door, he was extremely nice!!! Took reservation name, and notified the inside that we were coming in. You walk down a hallway with pictures on the wall of playboy bunnies to the coat check. Then you enter a bar area with is very beautiful, and boom you see all the bunnies! They are all beautiful!!! I was telling my husband that they did an amazing job hiring the staff! Because you definitely need a certain look, I absolutely loved the bunny outfits also, everyone had a smile on their face! The hostess which was a guy immediately said happy birthday, and we were off to be seated. The dining area is smaller than I imagined, but very nice looking. Red velvet wallpaper, fish tank in the middle with the playboy bunny logo on it. The chairs were red velvet, and the silverware was so classy! You definitely felt like you were in a playboy club! Our first waitress which was a bunny came over to take drink orders, we needed some help on what to order, and she recommended one. Shortly after the manager came over, and apologized for the long wait, even though there wasn't one, and said he was taking the drinks off the bill, wasn't necessary because we didn't feel like it was a long wait, nor did we even complain, so it was a nice gesture. Then we got a make waiter, he took our food order, and the original waitress disappeared, confusing but whatever. Then she would come over occasionally to see how everything was, it was a bit frustrating not knowing who was there to help, but there was a large table near us, and about 5 bunnies helping them. I was then told that she's just there to take drink orders, but that was already done by the waiter, I really didn't understand the system, and switching people. The waiter was very attentive! It was his first day, and to be honestly if he didn't mention it, I would have never known. The people to service the table was on top of everything! Constantly cleaning the table, and making sure the water was always filled. Okay now on to the food...for appetizers we had the shrimp, it was just okay...for entree we both had the steak with arugula, and truffle fries. The steak was very tasty, it was butterfly cut, and still cooked perfect, the arugula was delicious! Truffle fries were just like every other restaurant. Okay now on to my overall experience...the Dj was good, the music was good, they played a little bit of everything, the serve was great as I mentioned, I just didn't have a "fun" night, when they brought out my dessert, there was no candle, no bunnies to sing me happy birthday, no special birthday feeling like I've received at other restaurants. I guess you can say the vibe was just all off. Would I go back? Maybe if I was invited by friends, not because I'm in the mood for steak, and definitely not for the vibe. It honestly didn't live up to the experience I had imagined I would have had.

Very fun place; Dan is behind the bar, gave some history of the 75'year old bar. Makes a mean Bloody Mary. Paul greeted us and was friendly and inviting. As we were leaving, Dan offered a Jameson for the road. Excellent hospitality! I will be back!

This place has gotten some mixed reviews so I was a bit skeptical. If you like cheese and you like spicy chicken, this is your jam. We went at 2pm on Friday with 4 people and ordered 3 servings at medium spicy. I love it with extra heat but realistically, medium is more than enough for most people. Also 3 servings for 4 people is also more than enough food unless you have huge eaters. I will say the service is slow but everything is cooked by the time it arrives at your table. All you have to do is wait for the cheese to melt (or not) and enjoy. We added the kimchi rice (2 servings) after to further enjoy the spicy cheesy goodness. Again, it's a lot of food even for 3 people. I highly recommend the sweet potato add on. I'd definitely come back. But the more people you have in the group, the more you'll get to enjoy.

This place is pretty famous and for good reason. My roommates and I came around 8pm on a Sunday with no line. We weren't that hungry just wanted to try the pierogis but our server was so nice and even let us split the check. I got 8 fried pierogies and I even got to choose 1 of each kind - I loved the potato and goat cheese/arugula, definitely something for everyone. I also never had borscht but WOW, super savory, like a tastier chicken soup. Would recommend!

Title: Solid Eats with a Side of Stellar Service

My recent visit to this eatery proved that appearances can be deceiving. Tucked away in an unassuming alleyway that might give the average diner pause, the restaurant delivers a gastronomic experience that's worth braving the sketchy entrance.

The food here is reliable—my "single" burger, which was generously a double, was tasty, yet it didn't quite reach the pinnacle of burger greatness. The accompanying fries were crispy but erred on the side of salty, though the dipping sauce provided a nice touch. Standout elements like a perfectly oozy egg and a savory slice of thick-cut bacon did elevate aspects of the meal.

A small hiccup occurred when my burger arrived with mayo despite my request for its omission. Given the bustle of the place, this oversight was forgivable, and the burger was enjoyable enough that I chose not to send it back.

What truly distinguished my experience was our waitress, whose friendliness and genuine care for customers' dining preferences were heartwarming. Her considerate remarks resonated with us, enhancing the already welcoming atmosphere.

Though my friend labeled the ambiance "hipster," it was undeniably pleasant, contributing to the good vibes. While the price point felt slightly elevated for the fare's quality, the overall experience was positive. I'm in no rush to return, but I'd recommend giving this spot a go for those seeking a one-time venture into a place that balances good food with exceptional hospitality.

Title: A Love Letter to Tableside Guacamole and More

Review:
I’m often asked for my go-to spot when craving the perfect guacamole, and without hesitation, I point to this gem of a restaurant. Highlight of any visit? The tableside guacamole, hands down. It's not just a dish; it's an experience, and one that me and my friends keep coming back for.

What makes it even more of a delight is the fact that this is just the beginning of a consistently fabulous dining experience. The margaritas set the stage for a feast that inevitably leaves us feeling indulgently satisfied—almost to the point of needing a wheelchair to roll us home!

Service here isn’t just good; it’s exceptional — with a warmth that only genuine hospitality can provide, and a manager who never misses a chance to make us feel like the most important diners in the room.

Sure, I hit a small bump when a private event snagged my birthday plans here, but the professionalism with which it was handled (and the fact that they squeezed me in the next day) only reinforced my affection for this place. No grudge held; the experience and food are too good to stay away.

I've passionately recommended this spot for a decade to anyone visiting NYC, and if I could, I’d give it 10 stars! A++ for consistently delivering an unforgettable dining experience.

It was a rainy night and we were craving Indian, so we looked up delivery spots somewhat close by. I am SO glad this came up. Pippali "delivered" on all counts and I cannot wait to order from them again.We got the chicken tikka masala prix fixe, which comes with an appetizer, naan, and basmati rice. And we also got the beetroot dumplings prix fixe. We got the samosas and a chicken-mint dish as our appetizers. The beetroot dumplings are incredible! What! How is that a veggie? Two pillowy delicious morsels of veggies totally wowed me in this sweet and savory sauce that I've never tasted before. This is a surprising must get. Also loved their chicken tikka masala which is also sweet and savory and sumptuous and rich and all the things you want in a masala. The two appetizers didn't wow me as much but the entrees themselves were incredible.And the naan! They're like two massive pancakes but without the butter and maple syrup! So doughy and fluffy and slightly slightly sweet. I even at some of them plain, they are that good. 5 stars!!!!!!

Food: 5/5Not sure why this place only has 3 stars. I've been going to Bocca for years. My go to is the lamb ragu with ribbon pasta. I try to order it every time I'm here because it's the best I've ever had! Their pasta is always perfectly al dente and their sauce is full of flavor!Ive experienced their food to be slightly salty sometimes but I'm extremely salt sensitive. I request my entrees with "no added salt".A few recommendations: cacio e pepe, veal meatballs, grilled octopus and their shishito peppers are my favorite! I also love their vermentino wine!Service: 5/5Everyone here is super attentive and accommodating. Nico the manager is such a dear! He's very nice and always remembers his patrons.Ambiance: 4/5I've been going to Bocca before their renovations. It's very clean and has a cute/warm feel now. Dimly lit and romantic. Great spot for a date or casual dining.

Back again and ordered the Hainanese chicken over rice plus the Hainan chicken laksa. This time they made the soup even spicier for me. Amazing. I love this place. You may not notice it but they do something here that you won't find anywhere else. Ready? They completely debone the chicken. It's details like this that make this place that much better. The secret's getting out though so come ASAP. They're a hole in the wall with no more than 8 seats maximum. Can't wait to come back.

I recently dined at a quaint restaurant with a cozy interior that immediately set a welcoming tone for the meal to come. Despite its limited menu, the establishment made a strong impression. Our waitress was pleasant and attentive, ensuring a smooth dining experience.

The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the rotisserie chicken. It was exceptionally juicy, debunking any prior skepticism I had about dryness often associated with rotisserie preparations. The chicken was not just moist but packed with flavor that tantalized the taste buds. Accompanying the chicken, the rice and beans were perfectly cooked and satisfying. The maduros added a delightful sweetness that complemented the savory notes of the meal beautifully.

All dishes arrived promptly, served hot, and were devoured just as quickly due to their deliciousness. This restaurant is a gem that has earned a spot on my go-to list, and I am eagerly looking forward to my next visit.

Really tasty Thai restaurant, but I'd definitely recommend reserving a table ahead of time. You won't be seated until the whole party is there. We got the Sabai sampler for the appetizer which was decent. I enjoyed the Thai iced tea and green curry with pork, but fair warning that the curry is very spicy so someone with low tolerance for spice would definitely not enjoy it.

Title: A Taste of the Mediterranean Delights

Last night's visit to this bustling Mediterranean gem only solidified its reputation for both excellent food and service. The experience kicked off with a generous $12 sampler of delectable spreads, perfectly complemented by a loaf of warm, freshly baked bread.

Choosing to elevate the octopus appetizer to a main dish was a stroke of genius; it was tender and succulent, rivaling the best I've savored in Greece. The mixed grill entrée did not disappoint either—featuring a quartet of exquisitely prepared meats, accompanied by a unique side of carrots and cabbage, and, of course, the staple rice.

The constant crowd here speaks volumes about the quality and allure of this place. If the stars align for you to nab an outdoor seat, consider yourself fortunate. Highly recommended for a Mediterranean culinary adventure.

Title: Disappointing Greeting but Decent Dining

I visited this restaurant for a pre-theater dinner and was met with a rather unpleasant welcoming. On a rainy day, the process of checking in was smooth, but an interaction with the hostess soured the experience. Despite making an effort to keep the restaurant floor dry by using the umbrella bag dispenser, I was reprimanded by the hostess for not handing over my umbrella to her, which felt highly inappropriate and unprofessional.

Once past the unfortunate incident, the service was satisfactory. The meal itself was enjoyable, with a particularly solid fried calamari appetizer. The steak was cooked to perfection, the trout was delightful, and the cake ended the meal on a high note. While the cuisine was commendable, the initial encounter with the hostess left a lingering impression of discourtesy that one wouldn't expect in what seemed to be an upscale venue.

Title: A Bright New Spot for Pastry Lovers on 23rd Street

Having been a regular at the now-missed Union Square location, my excitement for the opening of the new Paris Baguette branch by 23rd street was palpable, albeit tinged with a hint of nostalgia for the spacious predecessor.

On multiple breakfast visits, the standout has been their pastries and cakes, delightfully lighter in sugar compared to standard American fare, making for a guilt-free indulgence. Their unique selection process adds to the charm — armed with a tray, parchment paper, and tongs, the joy of picking out treats for my team is unmatched, often rounding up 5 to 7 different items.

The staff has been a mixed batch. At times, they meticulously wrap each pastry, a thoughtful touch for my nut-allergic colleague, ensuring no cross-contamination. Yet, I've also experienced less careful packaging on other occasions, leading to the inconvenience of having to request separate handling of the pastries.

A minor hiccup occurred when I was overcharged due to a miscommunication, but swift managerial intervention resolved it efficiently with a refund.

Despite these growing pains in service consistency, Paris Baguette offers a refreshing and lighter breakfast alternative to its heavier neighbors, firmly securing its spot on my eatery map. A welcome addition for those looking to enjoy well-crafted baked goods and dodge the food coma from places like the adjacent Chick-fil-A.

#eatwelltraveloften, and certainly give this new establishment a visit when you're next in the area!

Title: Double Delight at Bocce!

I recently enjoyed back-to-back Friday lunches at Bocce, and I'm already planning my next visit! On the first occasion, my indoor dining experience was welcoming, complete with a charming bar setting. The star of the meal was the superb pepperoni pizza, accompanied by the essential Bocce bread – do yourself a favor and try it. The Purple cocktail I ordered was delightful; however, the Greenmarket cocktail didn't hit the same mark, coming across a tad diluted.

The following week I opted for the patio ambiance and wasn't disappointed. "The Farm" pizza was a culinary triumph, marrying asparagus, mozzarella, and pesto harmoniously, though the unidentified greens on top weren't to my taste. The Derby Cup was the drink of the day, balancing refreshment and flavor impeccably.

Service has been consistently friendly and attentive across visits. Bocce offers a stellar dining experience without the touristy veneer you might expect. It's secured its spot on my lunch rotation with ease.

I recently grabbed a quick slice of pizza from one of the Underground shops after hopping off the subway. Conveniently located, it's a decent spot for a food pit stop. The slice required reheating, which was a slight letdown, but it came out pretty tasty. The standout feature was the pepperoni - it was flavorful and added a nice punch to an otherwise average slice. Nothing extraordinary, but satisfying enough for a quick bite.

Title: A Feast for the Senses at Local Gem

If you're in search of a dining spot that caters to both taste and ambiance, look no further. My friends and I had the pleasure of sharing a sumptuous meal that included red braised pork belly, sautéed string beans, a whole fish with Asian chili, and smoked tea duck. The dishes were accompanied by a generous serving of rice, ensuring a satiating experience for our party of four.

A delightful bonus for us was a complimentary glass of wine, thanks to our Yelp check-in—a touch that further elevated our experience. Of all the delectable dishes, the pork belly and smoked tea duck were standouts, and I can't recommend them enough!

The menu boasts an extensive selection ideal for sharing, making this restaurant an excellent choice for groups. The spacious and orderly interior is welcoming, and the ability to make reservations on Yelp is a practical feature, particularly for weekend outings when securing a table for a larger party can be challenging.

In summary, the combination of delicious food, thoughtful amenities, and ample space makes this establishment a must-visit for those looking to enjoy a meal in good company.

Quite possibly the best place in ktown for fried chicken late at night or after going out to drink. Satisfies the drunchies so well. The chicken was light and airy and not too heavy on the batter which is the best way to do fried chicken. The meat was tender and juicy and lightly salted. The crispiness was extremely on point because of the light batter! Also no matter how late you stay out, this place is always open which is a true blessing. Service was also fast.

I loved Chow House, one of my favorite chinese resaturants in NYC. We came for dinner for party of three was the place was packed but no wait. We started with a wonton soup, it was served in a big bowl but was quickly finished between three people. The wonton soup was very light and soothing, great starter. We then ordered three entrees which were duck fried rice, soy sauce braised pork, and pork with garlic sauce. The duck fried rice has a great smoked duck flavor and was quite flavorful. The soy sauce braised pork was so juicy and succulent. The pork was fatty but not too oily and great with rice. The pork with garlic sauce was quite good but also on the sweater gooey-er side. This is a great restaurant for NYU students and when in the Greenwich village.

Soba-ya earns a solid four stars with its well-rounded menu and tasty, though not exceptional, flavors. Opting for the mini lunch set, I savored a satisfying combination of a mini rice bowl and the option of hot or cold udon or soba. The meal was delightful, and I'm curious about their limited-quantity lunch set or what their dinner offerings might entail. My timing post-opening on a Saturday meant immediate seating, and the portions were notably generous considering the price. Service shone with warmth and hospitality, complementing an inviting interior. While I'm open to exploring other Japanese eateries, I'd happily return to Soba-ya for another meal.

Title: A Night at Ethyl's: A Gimmicky Affair with Pricey Pour

After years of steering clear of Ethyl's on the advice of friends, my curiosity—paired with a spontaneous late-night burger craving—finally led me through its doors. This Upper East Side spot, known for its go-go flair, certainly knows how to create an ambiance with its lush, red crushed velvet interiors reminiscent of the 1960s. 

Upon arrival, the establishment enforces a strict no outside beverages policy, so those thinking of sneaking in a water bottle should think again. Plan on grabbing a table? Be prepared to meet the two-drink minimum per person, a rule that feels a bit pushy when the place is bustling and seating is scarce.

The cocktail prices will make any thrifty gin enthusiast's eyes water, prompting my friend and me, both gin aficionados, to settle for beer—a middle-of-the-road option both in taste and price. The venue did offer a compensatory round, which was a nice touch for the wait we endured.

The dancers add vibrancy to the night, animatedly performing atop the bar and by the entrance. However, for those familiar with the go-go scene, the novelty may quickly fade, as was the case for me.

Now, the letdown: the drinks are exorbitantly overpriced. When ordering a mere four well whiskey shots later in the evening, I was shell-shocked at the $60 charge—a sum that had me almost taking up the suggestion of buying an entire bottle from an equally astonished fellow patron.

On the flip side, the $5 burgers are worth noting—reasonably priced and satisfying. While the second visit with a larger group on a Friday night offered a better experience, it wasn't enough to alleviate the sting from our wallets.

I'm left with mixed feelings about Ethyl's. It's an experience, for sure, and perhaps one of the few places on the UES where you can catch a unique kind of show. But be warned: your bank account might not thank you. Drink at Ethyl's, if you dare, but be prepared for a hefty tab.

This was the perfect spot for Galentine's Day lunch! My friend hosted a galentine's day get together here and the experience was top notch. I have been to Max Brenner's Philly location but this was my first time at the NYC location. It was just as awesome as I would expect! The decor is fun and whimsical and they have a good amount of seating. It is also right off of the 456 and NQRW at Union Square so it is super easy to get to. I had the southwestern caesar salad with chicken. It was so good! I loved the dressing and it was the perfect portion for me. I ordered the chocolate martini and I am SO happy I did. I would seriously come back here just for their chocolate martini. It is to die for! I got the milk chocolate version and would love to go back and try their other chocolate options. If you take nothing else away from this review: GO GET THIS CHOCOLATE MARTINI! We split the European fondue for 2 amongst 6 of us and it was the perfect after lunch treat. I love that they have a little fire so you can roast the marshmallows. It is a great touch. It comes with toffee sauce and your choice of two chocolates. However, if you want all three chocolates and the toffee, you can add a third chocolate for only 4.25 (I think? It is something like that). I would definitely recommend doing that so you can try all their fondues.If you are a chocolate lover, this is restaurant should definitely be on your must try list!

Dining at this establishment is akin to playing a culinary game of chance when it comes to their pizza. On a good day, you'll be served a slice with perfectly balanced toppings on a light and crispy crust, complemented by a tart and sweet sauce. However, on an off day, prepare for a disappointing experience with poorly distributed toppings, a chewy and tough crust, and a sauce that errs on the side of salty and greasy. Inconsistency is the norm here, making it hard to recommend for a reliable pizza experience.

Food: I ordered the vegetable hand-pulled noodle soup. It came with spinach, tofu, fried egg, wood ear mushrooms, and Chinese pickled cabbage. Flavor was not bad and the portion size was really good. Service: Speed was incredibly quick - once we ordered, we were served in 5 minutes.Price: Not bad, $7.75 for a full bowl of noodles, soup, and vegetables, this was a very fulfilling meal. Ambiance: Inside was clean. Otherwise, it felt like any other Chinese restaurant, but more on the modern side.Overall, if you want a quick meal, this is a great place to get a satisfying soup of noodles at an affordable price in Chinatown.

First time trying "fancy" or "bougie" or "high end" hot pot. Experience did not disappoint! I had a reservation at 6pm for two. Restaurant wasn't too packed then, so we were immediately seated at our tables. We got the mother and son soup base $15, and the Tang Deluxe platter $80. We also got extra A Choy, Napa Cabbage, and cuttle fish on top of the Tang Deluxe platter. Pretty crazy to think of getting hot pot during 90F weather, but we didn't sweat and the air conditioning kept it at a perfect temperature for a hot pot feast oh boy. AMBIANCE:Love the decor here! Its clean, modern looking with a slight Tang dynasty twist. There's a giant mural at the back of the restaurant with pictures of Tang dynasty women enjoying hot pot. Lol. Definitely ambiance feels a lot cleaner compared to other hot pot heavy hitters around the Chinatown area. High ceilings and really beautiful restaurant. PROS:Love the soup base! We got the mother and son soup base. The mother (the bigger sized soup) was the spicy broth, and had a really great balance of chilis and healthy amount of numbing szechuan peppercorns. I was afraid the broth was going to be too oily, but it turned out to be not so bad! THe "son" broth was a pork bone based soup thats not spicy. That was probably my favorite of the two cause it packed so much flavor! Delicious! I think there's a decent selection of unbeatable combos. I think the Tang deluxe platter is more or less a platter of their most popular items albeit at a decent price. Other combos exist for a more affordable price. There is no sauce bar, however you order from their menu and its complimentary - unless if you got the truffle oil sauce. Meat was so fresh! The Tang deluxe platter came with the following meats: Miyazaki kobe beef, angus short rib, lamb tenderloin, berkshire pork shoulder, and lamb leg. Kobe beef being their signature dish we were recommended to boil that in the non spicy "son" broth. That definitely was a great suggestion. The beef was really soft, buttery, and the marbling was incredible. So much flavor in just those thinly sliced cuts of meat. Other favorites was the lamb/goat leg, as that meat was really tender and juicy. I also liked how big the slices of the angus short rib came, as their cut of meat was really thick and absorbs the brothiness of the soup base. Berkshier pork shoulder was also delicious too, and wasn't too fatty. Seafood was pretty fresh itself. I loved the variety we get in the deluxe platter. Tiger prawns were big, the scallops were fresh, and we also got an abalone. Definitely really good.Vegetables were prepared really fresh. Loved their enoki and seaweed knots and lotus roots. I mean what can go wrong with vegetables?For the additional items we got, I was a huge fan of the cuttlefish. They cut out giant chunks of the cuttlefish, and it was really fresh and tasty when you put it in the mother pot. CONS:This place is going to be expensive so definitely be prepared for that. Also be prepared for smaller portions. For the deluxe $80 combo that we got I think the portions don't really do justice. We only got two tiny pieces of scallop, and one abalone. Not sure how we are supposed to eat one abalone when the restaurant clearly markets the platter for two people. Same issue with the kobe beef and other cuts of meat - for the kobe we got two thinly sliced meats. We also got the Mung bean jelly in chili oil. Not a huge fan of what they made here, as the mung bean jelly tasted a little raw and chalky in the inside. OVERALL:Quality of meats is on point here! Love the concept that they are striving here at Tang Hotpot. Just be prepared to prepare to pay for a premium, and watch out for smaller portions here.

Title: A Satisfying Feast at Marta

My recent visit to Marta was a delightful experience that tickled my taste buds and left me planning my next visit. The asparagus and risotto croquettes were a perfect way to start the meal, tantalizing our palates with their exquisite flavor. For our main course, the salads were surprisingly generous, and sharing them among the three of us was a wise choice. We also indulged in two of their pizzas, which were simply divine.

The atmosphere of Marta added to the enjoyment of our meal. The spacious setting with high ceilings gave the restaurant an airy feel, even when bustling during the weekend rush. It's a smart move to secure a reservation to avoid disappointment, as this place is clearly a popular spot.

The service at Marta was warm and welcoming. The staff provided excellent recommendations, enhancing our dining experience. It is worth noting that Marta operates on a no-tipping model, which explains the slightly higher prices, but the quality of food and service justifies the cost.

In conclusion, Marta has cemented itself as a must-return venue for me. With its delectable dishes, convivial atmosphere, and attentive service, it offers an all-around excellent dining experience.

Title: "Authentic Ambience, Tasty Food, But Priced for the Expense Account Crowd"

I recently attended a work lunch at this establishment during restaurant week—or as our waiter joked, restaurant month for them. Upon arrival, the entrance featured a unique charm—a string of peppers tethered by a half lemon, which I learned is an Indian talisman to ward off evil spirits. The authenticity was palpable.

The restaurant itself boasts a large, somewhat dated interior reminiscent of a bygone era, yet it maintains a certain charm with its cavernous space and two-story capacity. Service was exemplary, with the staff ensuring our glasses were never empty.

The prix fixe menu offered during restaurant week was a pleasant surprise, including an appetizer, a choice of two entrees, and a small dessert. The crab cake appetizer was tasty, and the tandoori chicken truly delicious, while the naan was absolutely sublime. However, the curry broccoli was nothing to write home about. The nut tart dessert was well-balanced, with a fruit layer that complemented the seed paste.

Despite initial concerns over portion sizes, which appeared small, I left feeling satisfyingly full. The real downside was the pricing. Even during restaurant week, it felt steep, exemplified by an $8 chai tea! A single piece of broccoli being labeled an entree seemed a stretch.

In conclusion, while the place dazzles with its good service and delectable food, it's best suited for a meal on the company's dime.

Easily made a reservation for three on a Friday night. The Kurkum cocktail, Whipped feta and red snapper (special) were my favorites. Also tried the Lamb neck, cauliflower, Octopus and Halva creme brûlée. Drinks were really excellent, I'd come back just for cocktails. I do think Taboon is better, but Balaboosta has a slightly lower price point. Overall solid.

I recently stumbled upon what's quickly become my new go-to spot, and I can't sing its praises enough. Despite not being the newest kid on the block, this gem is new to me, and in just a week, I’ve visited three times, each with different friends who have all been equally charmed.

Open until at least 11pm on weekends, this place is perfect for late-night cravings. Its ambiance is nothing short of magical, offering both indoor and outdoor seating that's equally cozy. Outdoors, you'll find retractable awnings and warm lighting, set against dark brick that creates an inviting atmosphere. Step inside, and you're greeted with visual delights – spacious interiors, high ceilings festooned with interesting lights, architectural wonders, and fresh blooms. Ideal for romantic dates or dinners with friends.

The service has been consistently friendly and attentive across all visits. Now, the main event – the food and drinks. The mezcal old fashioned is a must-try, meticulously crafted. The menu items that stole my heart include a tuna tartare with generous chunks of fresh fish, a tender steak perfectly paired with mushrooms, onions, and sides of creamy mashed potatoes and scrumptious spinach. Other notables: brussels sprouts with a spicy twist, calamari in a delectable sauce, a comforting stuffed chicken special oozing with mozzarella, and a simply divine pasta with a rich, sweet bolognese.

I wholeheartedly recommend this spot for a memorable dinner and drinks experience, whether you're out on a date, with friends, or family.

I thought I wrote a review but I guess I only took photos.I've been here twice. The first time was perhaps a few days after they opened and it was pretty quiet outside of someone there delivering. I went there a second time with one other and it was packed. Both times, the majority of people were speaking Russian.I stuck with a Plov the first time. The meat was very tender and it was a great portion for the price. The rice was excellent. I was not a big fan of the pita, being a bit hard though the other sesame based bread was better.The second time, we shared a tomato/cucumber salad. It reminded me of a mix between a Shepherd Salad though without cheese and an Israeli Salad. The dressing was vinegar based and it was good.She had a Kharcho which was nice and lightly peppery. Very good on a cold day. The meat was quite tender.I had two kebabs. The lamb neck chop was good but paled to the lulya kebab. I've had this form of kebab in a lot of places and this was easily one of the best I have had. It was packed and a little hard to get off of the skewer but otherwise, I'd just get two of them next time, especially as it was cheaper.I wouldn't recommend their od fruit dessert or their kompot but otherwise, the food was excellent. Nice service also though it took a long time to get food the 2nd time.

I really enjoyed the dumplings here. I liked that the fillings were high quality locally sourced meat and vegetables. I liked that the special was a burrata with a pork/beef dumpling pan fried and then smothered in a delicious homemade marinara with basil on top. It was really good and I'd definitely want to come back again.

Made a reservation here on a Tuesday night - and the only available time was after 7pm. We arrived around 6pm, hoping they could seat us early and there were plenty of availability. I got the Kinky Boots drink which was very good, but a little sweet (and expensive) to get more than 1. We got the guacamole, which was on the small size. Good for 1-2 people. The buffalo chicken flatbread was delicious and so was the mac and cheese. The mac and cheese was also very small (especially for the price). The food was good and the ambiance was nice, but the staff was very un-attentive. For the price, they should increase the portions and make sure their staff pays a little more attention to the customers!

Title: Authentic Filipino Flavors Shine During Restaurant Week

My dining experience at this Filipino spot during Restaurant Week was quite enjoyable, offering good value and a chance to savor traditional dishes. The $35 deal for two was a steal, including a shared appetizer, individual entrees, and a dessert, leaving us with ample leftovers.

Service was notably swift, and while reservations were strict, ensuring a slot was worth the effort. The pork sinigang was a standout, with meat so tender it fell off the bone, complemented by a perfectly sour broth. The lumpia Shanghai was competently executed, a satisfactory beginning to our meal.

Our entrees, BBQ chicken with garlic rice and kare kare, were pleasant, though the kare kare's sauce was a tad too thin for my liking, and I've had richer versions elsewhere. However, the oxtail in the kare kare was exceptionally tender.

The real highlight came at dessert with the buko pandan, a delightful treat that more than made up for any minor shortcomings in the prior courses.

In summary, this restaurant offers solid Filipino cuisine that I would recommend for friends visiting NYC. While I have a deep appreciation for homemade Filipino food, which sets my bar quite high, this place holds its own and is certainly worth a return visit.

My husband and I thought the food here was just average. It is a convenient place to eat if you have a broadway show nearby but that's about it. The place was busy and service was punctual. For starters we got the croquettes, which were disappointing. They were just salty with half and half of chunks of ham or mushed ham like spam. We didn't taste any other ingredients that was listed on the menu for this dish. It also seemed to be served on top of thousand island dressing. For pasta we got the gnocchi carbonara, cacio e Pepe, and truffle cream mushroom pasta. The gnocchi was cold on the outside and warm in the inside which made us think it sat for a while. The mushroom pasta barely had any truffle taste in it so I ended up eating it since I'm not a big fan of  truffle. The noodles were also overcooked and bloated. The cacio e pepe was okay. The cheese cup was stale. It seemed pre-made and plated when the pasta is ready. The pasta noodles were al dente but that's about it. They seem popular here for the cacio e pepe dish but we've had better pasta elsewhere.

Tucked conveniently near the red train station and a stone's throw away from the local park, this pizzeria serves as a perfect pit stop for a casual pizza-in-the-park kind of day. Offering an array of choices including pepperoni, margherita, Hawaiian, and the homely grandma slice, the pizzas are generally pleasing without setting new culinary benchmarks. While it may be a neighborhood go-to in the Upper West Side, true pizza aficionados might find superior options with a little exploration beyond this locale. Overall, it's a solid choice for convenience and a decent slice.

I recently visited a local eatery to try their Bold Ramen and came away with a satisfied palate. The ramen boasted a savory broth that hit the right note of flavor without tipping the scales on salt. Both the noodles and the pork were cooked to perfection, and the eggs added a comforting touch to the meal. It's worth noting that the restaurant caters to various dietary needs, offering porkless broth and vegetarian options that appeared equally appetizing. My dining companion opted for the naked noodles, which caught my eye for a future visit. While the experience didn't quite transcend the ordinary, it was a pleasant foray into their noodle offerings.

Title: A Delightful Experience at Starly's Bistro

Review:
Returning to Starly's Bistro for a romantic date night, the experience was just as memorable as our first visit during a birthday celebration. The personal touch of being remembered by the staff, particularly by Starly, was heartwarming.

The evening began with a bottle of CAVA, priced at $35, which exceeded our expectations—chilled to perfection. The grilled pulpo starter was a highlight, showcasing both freshness and expert grilling, resulting in a succulent dish. The garlic shrimp, with its enticing sauce, made for an excellent complement to the bread.

Moving on to the entrées, there was a slight mix-up with the doneness of our steaks—my medium-requested ribeye steak came out medium rare, while my husband's desire for medium was misinterpreted as medium rare. Despite this, the quality and flavors of the meat, particularly with the surf n' turf duet of ribeye and shrimp, left us thoroughly satisfied.

We rounded off the meal with churros, which were delightful, although the dessert menu could benefit from a few more inspired choices to elevate the end of the dining experience.

In essence, Starly's Bistro offers outstanding service, a friendly atmosphere, and top-tier cuisine. While there's room for growth in the dessert department, the restaurant remains a destination we recommend with enthusiasm. Worth every penny for such an enjoyable outing.

Title: A Filling Feast at a Hidden Gem

My dining experience at this local spot was unexpectedly delightful. Though my visit was impulsive, after spotting it near a planned bubble tea excursion, it turned out to be a highlight. The interior boasts a spacious and modern design with striking red hues and wooden elements—a pleasant setting that matched its slowly bustling atmosphere.

The true test came with our order of Sauteed Rice Noodle in Traditional Sauce with Chicken for $15. Skeptical of one dish sufficing for two, I was pleasantly proven wrong by the generous portion. The rice noodles were perfectly chewy, drenched in a robust, spicy sauce that captivated my taste buds. The choice of chicken breast wasn't my favorite, but it was well-complemented by the assorted mini vegetables like mushrooms, squash, and celery, which added a nice crunch to the dish.

This restaurant is a must-try for anyone craving the bold flavors of Xinjiang cuisine. Despite my inability to name the enchanting Chinese song playing in the background, the overall experience has me eager for a return visit—to discover the song’s title and explore more of the menu.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Wings Hotspot

I recently visited the Times Square location known for tantalizing wings and chicken tacos. The honey mustard boneless wings and sweet teriyaki options did not disappoint. However, the overall experience was undermined by inconsistent service. Out of three visits, only once did the service meet expectations, with staff often seeming distracted. An example of this was a simple request for ranch sauce turning into a 15-minute wait, ending with multiple redundant servings from different waiters. The staff's camaraderie is noticeable, but it sometimes detracts from customer focus. The restaurant's cleanliness and spacious setting are commendable. While I believe a handful of waitstaff could step up their game, the food quality is reason enough to give this place a try when craving some good wings. Rating: ★★★☆☆

Title: A Hyped Haven with Hearty Helpings

I've visited this bustling eatery multiple times, and despite the usual wait, my recent excursion with two friends led to an unexpectedly swift seating. The journey to our table was an adventure in itself, a winding path through the kitchen, up stairs, and into a charming nook that could be the restaurant's best feature.

Our choice, "The Cake Boss", had its limitations: it's served large, with a choice between eggplant or prosciutto (we opted for the latter), and a price tag of $35. When it arrived, the pizza was generously topped with prosciutto and a heavy blanket of arugula. However, it missed the mark on the iconic New York foldability.

While the experience wasn't disappointing, it didn't live up to the excitement surrounding it. For those seeking exceptional pizza, there are other venues in the area that might satisfy the palate without the wait.

Despite some negative feedback I stumbled upon, my visit to this beer-centric spot was rather pleasant. One shouldn't anticipate gourmet cuisine at a beer-focused establishment; the fare here is typical bar food. I sampled both a sour beer and an IPA; while IPAs aren't my cup of tea, my companion, an IPA aficionado, approved. The sour beer options were limited, yet understandably so, considering its niche appeal. Nonetheless, I appreciated having a choice that suited my palate. The staff was notably amiable, even indulging our curiosity about the decorations. Overall, a solid place for a casual drink with friends.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Pizza Aficionados

After countless passes by this inconspicuous eatery, a recommendation finally led me to what I can only describe as a pizza revelation. Despite a daunting line suggestive of its popularity, service was brisk, and the wait was short-lived. 

The pizza, particularly the one with fresh tomato and mozzarella, was phenomenal — a masterful blend of classic flavors that could very well redefine your pizza benchmarks. The meat-topped variant, while slightly on the saltier side, was delicious nonetheless.

Admittedly, prices at this spot are steeper compared to others, but the generous slice size justifies the cost. It's a place where the value is measured not just in quantity, but overwhelmingly in quality. The verdict? Absolutely worth every penny for one of the best pizza experiences around.

Title: A Hearty Bite of Chicago in NYC's Chinatown

Upon the quest for an iconic Chicago burger, I found myself navigating the intricate alleyways of Chinatown to a hidden gem that's recently graced NYC with its presence. Arriving on a weekday morning, the hassle of reservations was unnecessary as I easily secured a table in the welcoming, albeit dimly-lit, establishment.

The burger experience here is not for the faint of heart—these patties are robust, embodying the bold spirit of Chicago. Topped with a perfectly cooked egg and crispy bacon, the burger transcended to new heights of morning indulgence, though I must note the bacon's saltiness was a tad pronounced for my taste.

Sharing the burger was a wise decision, given its generous size left me more than satisfied. Beer enthusiasts would appreciate the extensive selection, which offers a perfect pairing for any burger choice. Service was commendable; our server adeptly walked us through the menu, ensuring our burger adventure was both delicious and informative.

In summary, this little alleyway burger haven brings a piece of Chicago's hearty cuisine to the heart of NYC, providing a satisfying, if not belt-loosening, meal that's well worth the search.

Málà Project is one of my favorite restaurants in the city. Hands down. On hectic days, our team orders here to boost our mood and energy. If you're into really spicy food - this place is heaven. If you're not into spicy food the dishes still have amazing flavor. I recommend making your own dry pot - with meat and veggies (things I've loved include: sweet potato, chicken, fish cake, mushrooms, lotus). If you're scared to pick your own dry pot, they offer pre-decided suggestions. My one recc is if you're going to the restaurant - go in a large group so you can try different things and eat family style. The portions are pretty big too, so a clay pot is definitely enough for two.

I came to Raku with a party of 9 because we were not expecting the restaurant to be this small (oops). This place is definitely a hole in the wall for Japanese udon. The outside had no signs except a small menu that indicates the fabric curtains lead into Raku. The restaurant is small and has very limited seating. I would not recommend coming with a party of 9. We joined the Yelp waitlist by splitting the groups 4 and 5 which worked. However, the Yelp waitlist time was very inaccurate. My friends and I arrived at the restaurant at the given time but 4 of us were standing outside for almost an extra half an hour. The waitress then told us that the Yelp waitlist is usually inaccurate, but since the restaurant was so small, we were just standing outside in the cold. I ordered the Kitsune udon which consists of the udon noodles, fried bean curd, and some spinach. The broth was amazing, it was very flavorful but a bit too salty. I would recommend try asking for low sodium broth because I was drinking lots of water due to the saltiness. The udon noodles were very chewy and I liked the consistency a lot. I did find the portions to be a bit small, and I was still hungry afterward. I would recommend trying their other udons if you are hungry. Overall, I do love the food here a lot. The wait was definitely a bit longer than I expected, so I would recommend using Yelp to join the waitlist ahead of time. If I am ever in the area, I would definitely come back.

The lamb and beef combo was decent. I went during a promo, so I'm not sure if the portions is the same size for the regularly priced meal, but it was pretty small. I would not pay $12 for a meal that size, since there wasn't much meat.  It comes with a drink and fresh baked bread. The bread was delicious and made the meal filling. It was a decent sized roll! Service was friendly and chatty. This place is mostly to go, but there are a couple of stool seats.

I am rating it 5 because it is great value and good pizza. Now of course this isn't the best pizza you will ever have, but for $1, you wouldn't expect that. I expected it to be low quality but I was wrong. Good pizza and good size. Good value. If you get pepperoni it will be 1.50 (add .50).Good value, good pizza for the price. Don't expect best pizza ever (5-star tasting).But this place is 5 star because of the value and quick service.

Came here for happy hour with my girls. We ordered both French fries dishes. The two options were herb oil and Cajun powder. The Cajun powder fries reminded me of the red hot chips, it was weirdly good and the herb oil fries were pretty basic. The vegetable dumplings had a weird sauce to it but the dumpling itself was pretty good. We also ordered a bunch of drinks. We had the lychee martini and the first kiss drink. The lychee martini was so good that I had to order more than one. The price was well worth it and our waiter was pretty friendly and attentive.

Nice pizza place, where you can get an authentic NYC slice of pizza. They have places to sit throughout the restaurant, which is a plus in our "on the go" city. Prices are reasonable and service is friendly. I love how they have the caloric values for each food item on their menu, as this definitely aids with my selection! I've been here a few times, and note that they have consistent quality to their food. The garlic knots are a bit more oily that I would like, but other than that it's a pretty standard and solid pizza shop. Cheese slice: $3.00Garlic knots: $2.50

Title: Charming Spot for a Celebration, with a Few Hiccups

I recently visited this adorable cash-only gem to celebrate a friend's birthday. Take note: reservations are a must, as it's a popular spot. We shared two pizzas to start—the Prosciutto di Parma and Margherita—both of which were tasty. The lemon pasta, highly praised in other reviews, was indeed delicious, though not quite 'shout-from-the-rooftops' fabulous.

Unfortunately, the Nutella pizza dessert was a letdown and service was painfully slow. The quaint décor added to the ambiance, but be aware the space is tight, making it ideal for smaller groups. Service could be improved; our waitress was not well-versed in the menu, which resulted in a dining hiccup for one of our party.

In summary, while the main dishes hit the mark, there's room for improvement in both service and dessert offerings.

Title: A Delicious Malaysian Surprise

I recently visited this Malaysian gem, and I must say, it completely exceeded my expectations. Having tried other Nyonya restaurants in Brooklyn with mixed feelings—the 8th Ave location was decent, but the 86th left much to be desired—I wasn't sure what to anticipate. On a workday whim, I gave into my Malaysian craving and was not disappointed.

I typically go for beef with egg sauce over flat noodles—a must-try that never disappoints. This time, however, the curry beef piqued my interest, and I'm thrilled it did. The dish was a delightful explosion of flavors that nostalgically reminded me of Malaysia.

I also sampled the Indian pancake, which was quite tasty, although it was overshadowed by the richness and quantity of the rice, leaving me no choice but to take it to go.

Note that this place is cash only, though there's no need to worry as there are banks conveniently located nearby. The service was on the slower side but satisfactory, and communication was a breeze with many English-speaking staff.

I'm already planning my next visit and would highly recommend this spot to anyone craving authentic Malaysian cuisine.

Title: Celebratory Vibes at Mole in West Village

Finding Mole in the bustling West Village on a Saturday evening without a reservation felt like hitting the jackpot for my friends and me. We were there to toast to a friend's LSAT completion, seeking good margs and Mexican fare. Thankfully, Mole did not disappoint in ambiance; it was electric and perfect for our celebration.

We sneakily caught the tail end of happy hour, indulging in classic margaritas that set the party mood. The guacamole was a hit, creamy and fresh, yet the queso was a miss, arriving more like a solid cheese block than a dip—friendly tip: get the guac.

Hunger satisfied by the chips, we bypassed tempting entrees for chicken tacos. They were satisfactory, though as a Texan, I may hold my taco standards high. While not the culinary highlight of my life, the experience, buoyed by excellent service, made Mole a great choice for our occasion.

Title: A Birthday Treat Worth Savoring at Hot Pot & BBQ Heaven

I had the pleasure of celebrating my birthday at a fabulous hot pot and BBQ joint that truly knows how to spoil its guests. The best part? Your meal is on the house if you visit on your birthday!

The highlight for me was the hot pot and BBQ combo, offering a delightful mix of flavors and textures. They generously offer a "benz pot" — your choice of up to three broths at no extra cost. I opted for the spicy, tomato, and pork bone broths with the spicy one tickling my taste buds most pleasantly. The variety of meats, veggies, and noodles to add to the hot pot and BBQ was impressive, with pumpkin, rice cake, and corn standing out as hot pot stars.

For those who relish customization, the sauce station is your playground; though, the 99 favor sauce ready-mixed was a clear winner in my books. The BBQ experience was made even more enjoyable as the staff tended to the grill, allowing me to relax and enjoy. The steak rib sizzled to perfection, accompanied by tasty sides of asparagus and sweet potato.

An unexpected perk was the tiny scoop of strawberry ice cream, a sweet finale courtesy of a Yelp check-in, which, to my delight, could be combined with the birthday offer. Despite its size, the ice cream was a quality treat, packed with real strawberry pieces.

As I left, feeling satisfied and celebrated, complimentary chewing gums and wet towels were a thoughtful touch to end a fantastic dining experience. Whether it's your special day or you're just in the mood for some good hot pot and BBQ, this place is a gem worth checking out.

What an amazing evening at Felice 56! My husband and I were in the mood for great Italian and Felice 56 did not disappoint!We started our meal with Crocchette di Riso as an appetizer and boy were they delicious! The flavors were perfect and I loved the surprise cheese in the middle.For our main dishes I had the Tonnarelli Cacio e Pepe, while my husband had the Pappardelle al Cacao, Chiantigiana; both dishes were fantastic and   definitely hit the spot! The Cacio e pepe had a bold sauce with amazing Parmigiano-Reggiano that really made the dish perfect. My husband said that the Pappardelle had all the right flavors and the short-ribs were cooked to perfection.We ended our meal with the tiramisu and a scoop of the hazelnut gelato; the tiramisu was so delicate and the gelato was delightful.I also cannot forget about the service which was perfection; everyone was very attentive and went above and beyond to make sure our evening was perfect.I cannot wait to come back to Felice 56 and try some of the other dishes! Thanks for the perfect date night! My husband and I were throughly impressed.

Title: A Gem in the West Village: Authentic Italian Flair

My recent dinner at this charming Italian spot in the West Village was a delightful experience that I'm eager to repeat. The culinary journey began with perfectly crispy croquettes, followed by a delicate balance of flavors in the risotto with parmesan, crushed truffle, and mozzarella. The burrata cheese was a creamy delight, paired harmoniously with delicata squash, kale, raisins, and a gentle kick from calabrian chili.

As for the charred octopus, it was a standout dish, with its tender texture complemented by a bed of olive oil-crushed potato and a flavorful romesco sauce. However, it was the pappardelle with Vermont veal ragu that truly stole the show—each bite of the fresh, homemade pasta was a testament to the chef's dedication to authentic Italian cuisine.

The wine list was comprehensive, enhancing our dining experience with its range of options. The service was exceptional, striking the right balance between attentive and non-intrusive. The ambiance of the restaurant added to the enjoyment of the meal, encapsulating an inviting and warm Italian dining atmosphere.

In summary, this Italian haven in the West Village is a must-visit for anyone in search of top-notch pasta, excellent wine, and an overall wonderful dining experience. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.
Pictured is one of the staple desserts at Nougatine, Warm Chocolate Lava Cakewith Salted Caramel Ice Cream. Definitely recommend ending your meal with this perfect pairing of sweet and salty!

During my visit to a renowned sushi restaurant, I made the unusual choice to try the ramen, only to be met with disappointment due to its mediocrity. Fortunately, the sashimi platter saved the meal—despite the steep price, the quality was impressive. On a potential return, I'll stick to what the restaurant does best: sushi.

Title: A Slice of Authenticity at San Matteo

My relationship with San Matteo's pizza started in 2016, and years later, they continue to impress with their authentic, thin, and crispy pies. The menu caters to all preferences, smartly split between white and tomato sauce-based pizzas. Service here is exemplary; Carmela, in particular, is a gem. Her welcoming presence and unwavering smile contribute significantly to the dining experience.

Desserts are irresistible—I recommend both the Tiramisu and Nutella offerings, the pizza, and the soufflé cake, each a delightful finish to your meal. It’s also worth noting their drinks selection that includes both limoncello and amaro. San Matteo is a must-visit; ask for Carmela for a truly heartwarming welcome.

I had the pleasure of trying Ribs Bao Yum Yum, and I must say, their fried dumplings were a delectable feast! The seasoning on each dish was spot-on, elevating the flavors to delicious heights. However, the ambiance left something to be desired as the space felt cramped, detracting slightly from the overall experience. Despite that, the culinary delights were the stars of the show and are worthy of praise.

Title: Exquisite Cuisine Marred by Excessive Wait Times

My recent visit to this restaurant was a culinary delight with a bittersweet aftertaste. The food, especially the fish, was absolutely incredible – a truly unparalleled experience that tantalized my taste buds with every succulent, melt-in-your-mouth bite of their delectable sushi.

I opted for the $40 dinner deal, which was a perfect portion to leave me sated without feeling overly stuffed. Additionally, the nigiri sake was a sweet, flavorful complement to the meal, enhancing the overall dining experience.

However, the anticipation for such gastronomic pleasure was dampened by the agonizingly long wait. Arriving at 7:30 PM, I was greeted with the harsh reality of being the 42nd patron in line, ultimately not seated until 9:30 PM. For a Tuesday evening, a two-hour wait is simply too steep a price to pay for dinner, no matter how delightful the fare.

Therefore, with a heavy heart, I must give this establishment a 4-star rating. Should they find a remedy for the excessive wait times, it would undoubtedly be a solid 5-star experience.

Had the hot And sweet sausage 10 inch personal pie via MealPal. A bit cold by the time I got back to my desk to enjoy it but it was a decent size portion and enjoyed the thin crust. The cheese was blended and unique.

Title: A Birthday Brunch to Remember at Korean BBQ

For my birthday brunch in 2018, I had the pleasure of experiencing a Korean BBQ spot chosen by my friends. As a newcomer to the restaurant, my arrival was met with a warm welcome and prompt seating.

Service was attentive without being overbearing, allowing us to peruse the extensive BBQ options before prepping our tableside grill. The soju offered was notably potent and paired well with the array of succulent meats that were grilled to perfection right before our eyes.

The pleasure of the meal was heightened by an assortment of savory Korean side dishes. A personal highlight was the hot soup and delectable stir-fried Korean noodles, symbolizing long life and adding depth to the feast. Although on the pricey side, the experience justified the cost.

Celebrating over sizzling grills and sumptuous flavors made for a birthday treat that was both unique and memorable. Definitely a venue worth the splurge for special occasions.

First time trying the place. I went with a friend. She got her food first. I waited, waited, realize people after me got their food.  I realize 20 min is actually long. I asked someone to check. They forgot my food. She goes back to kitchen to look for it. Comes back ask what I ordered.I assume they are making my food. She comes back fairly quick and apologizes for the long wait. I got to eat my food, it's cold!!  They didn't make the food, they must have found my order sitting in the kitchen that they never brought out. So it was cold.Sorry but that's bad service. If you mess up, Don't give cold food. You make fresh food and give hot food. Bad service.

**Review of Sheesha Lounge and Grill**

I recently visited both locations of Sheesha Lounge and Grill - one on Avenue B and the other on E 10th Street. While the place is known for its hookah, particularly the nicotine-free options like the robust lemon and blue mist flavors, I focused on the dining experience.

To start, the Babaghanoush was a flavorful appetizer that set a high bar for the rest of the meal. The chicken kabob, paired with perfectly cooked basmati rice, did not fail to impress with its seasoning and taste. The grilled rib-eye steak, served with fries and a salad, was another standout dish.

The drink selection was hit or miss for me. The blueberry mojito was not to my liking, but the mimosa was a delightful follow-up. However, it's worth noting that the ambiance on weekends can be overwhelming, with a live DJ, belly dancer performances, and Arabic music nights making it a lively yet very loud environment.

Though the place is quite smoky due to the sheesha, which may not be everyone's preference, the lounge's vibrant atmosphere and late-night hours (open till 4 AM daily) make it a popular spot. For food enthusiasts, it's certainly worth a visit for the well-prepared dishes, even if you're not there for the hookah experience.

The interior of the restaurant was elegant and classic. I went there for restaurant week. The hostess didn't make us feel like welcoming. It was 4 of us but they gave a table at the corner where 3 people can seat.. we had to ask to change the table. All the foods were great, nice combination and decoration. And waiting for the dessert! Took us 30-40 mins... no wayAnd their bathroom located basement, so we had to walk far to go to use bathroom

If you're visiting NYC or you just want expensive drinks with a view, Manhatta is the place to be!! Stopped by on a Tuesday late afternoon and ordered cocktails at the bar. We walked to the window and looked out at the amazing view. Wow is all I can say. You can see all of New York through this window! The cocktails  were delicious and this is a non tipping barThey have a lunch special too! Will check out

Title: A Sweet and Savory Experience at [Restaurant Name]

I recently dined at [Restaurant Name] and came away with mixed feelings. The highlight of my meal was undoubtedly the dessert – the Plum Lychee Sorbet paired with Black Sesame Gelato was an exquisite blend of flavors that could easily earn a five-star rating on its own. I could happily indulge in that sorbet every single day.

The Superiority Burger also impressed me with its satisfying taste, making it a strong contender in the plant-based burger scene. Unfortunately, not all dishes met these high standards. The Superiority Wrap fell flat for me and I found myself particularly disappointed with the Burnt Broccoli Salad.

In conclusion, while there were a few misses on the menu, the sorbet and burger alone are worth a visit to [Restaurant Name]. Therefore, I’m giving it a solid four stars out of five. If you're ever in the area and have a penchant for innovative desserts and a good plant-based burger, this might be your spot.

Nestled in the heart of Soho, Cipriani Downtown is a slice of Venice minus the canals. The moment you step in, the ambiance hits with its glamorous clientele and bustling Italian waiters, instantly transporting you to a chic European setting. Unlike the typical Italian-American fare found across New York, Cipriani impresses with authentic Italian cuisine that rivals the culinary experiences of Italy itself. The food and desserts do not disappoint and opting for a night at Cipriani Downtown always feels like the right choice. If you're missing Venice but can't make the trip, a visit here is a delightful compromise.

If you find yourself craving a solid New York slice, this spot hits the mark. With a satisfyingly crispy crust, flavorful sauce, and generous cheese topping, it doesn't disappoint. The variety of pies and toppings is impressive, catering to all tastes. The setting is casual with not much seating, making it ideal for a quick bite or takeout. An added bonus: it's open late, perfect for that late-night, post-party munch. Definitely give it a go when you're in the neighborhood.

With a name like Sidewalk Tacos, the tacos has to be good. I ordered three tacos (lengua, al pastor, and carne asada) and a chicken burrito. The tacos were great but not the best in the area. The chicken burrito was good and had a good ratio of rice to other fillings. They are open during the pandemic for delivery and pickups.

Innovative and tasty food! Made a Resy reservation for 6 people on a Sunday evening and got the fancy booth in the back. Food was amazing. It seemed like it would be really pricey as things were just adding up, but honestly between 6 people, it was a lot of food and we could've done with only 5 dishes. We were a bit irked when the oysters came in the middle of the meal even though our waitress said we would start with the oysters. oh well.- bao: you have to get this. it's delicious! the bun itself is super soft and fluffy- brussel sprouts: great, crispy, and slightly sweet veggie dish- dry aged strip steak: this was my favorite meat dish. it was definitely more on the rare side when we ordered med rare but it was so savory. they poured this sauce on it and had a side of ride and horseradish. it was pretty big- oysters: good, but probably would've tasted better at the beginning of the meal instead of oddly placed in the middle.- pork loin: an "asian" twist on a classic pork loin. I would skip this. it came last so we were pretty full by then- sichuan tteokbokki: had a unique mala taste which I enjoyed! I like these better than regular tteokbokki since you can tell they are slightly fried.momofuku ssam bar was everything I hoped to get out of a momofuku in new york after feeling like vegas was a bit overpriced. next time, we'll try the large ssam plates!

Seafood. The boil is all about satisfying your seafood needs. I came here on a Wednesday night with my niece and a friend to scarf down some of the good stuff. This place is cash only so make sure to fill your pockets up with some of the green stuff before you enter. Our server approached us right away and we ordered our drinks. I fell in love with a Frenchman named Hennessy. He was sweet and strong. It's a good thing I was in a rush because I can tell hes very addicting.  For all of my Hennessy lovers, I'll just let you know I will not give him up but I'm willing to share him, just a little. A friend of mine had the Bayou and said it was good but a little strong. Sounds like my kind of drink. Just be careful because it could sneak up on you. We ordered a pound of shrimp and a pound of snow crab legs each. I like mine spicy so I chose spicy flavoring. I could have got it spicier but the flavors were spot on. So the way this works.1. Pick your protein 2. Pick you flavor- I chose the boil special3. Pick your spice level- there is a level for those who get heartburn. Dry/or mild. The servers will hand you some hospital gloves so you can dissect whatever protein you choose and to keep your hands clean. Your goods will be handed off to you in a plastic bag that only you will know what's inside. As you pick apart everything you can dump all of the evidence in a pail on your table. I know this all sounds like criminal behavior and I must say, it absolutely was for me because I killed those shrimp and crab legs. The flavors were so good and lets not forget the mac and cheese. It had a nice crumble on top with just the right amount of cheesiness. It was baked to perfection. I ate until the "itis" took over my body. So do I reccomend this place. Hell yeah!!! The only downside for me was the cash only option.

Baby Bo's Cantina is a hidden gem. I say that because if you're walking down the block, you just might miss it. Baby Bo's is right across the street from the Kips Bay AMC and a few blocks away from the six train and near local bus stops. Now on to the good stuff. Baby Bo's is a small restaurant but I think that adds to the charm of the place.Baby Bo's Cantina is a nice place to enjoy a taco Tuesday night or just an amazing authentic meal.  Immediately, my friend and I were invited to sit at a table or the bar and we chose the bar. The bartender was amazing and our drinks were so delicious and on point. As we sat and gobbled down our amazing chicken.. pulled pork ... and steak tacos, we admired the traditional art on the walls. The food came out quickly, hot and fresh. Baby Bo's Cantina is definitely a keeper and I plan to return again very soon.

Entering Tenho is an immersion in authenticity, signaled by the grand lantern that beckons you inside to its genuine Japanese ambiance. Service is commendable here—friendly, attentive, and unexpectedly quick, with our Ramen arriving in under five minutes.

We ventured to sample Nozomi's spicy salad, the chef's skewer assortment, and Kogadhi garlic ramen for our meal. The salad was generous yet overwhelmingly spicy, drenched in an excess of sauce. The skewers, however, were the stars of the night—succulent and perfectly grilled, with the beef tongue skewer deserving a special shout-out. This assortment set is highly recommended for its value and quality.

The Kogadhi garlic ramen's broth was rich and creamy, albeit slightly too salty for our taste. The noodles had the ideal chewiness, infused with garlic flavor. Yet, the dish was let down by the scant toppings, leaving us wanting more.

In conclusion, Tenho holds its ground as a worthy ramen destination, with a few areas ripe for refinement.

It's a cute restaurant that look kinda small but actually have a few tables and seats. Friendly servers and decent speed. Definitely a few tables when I was there but wasn't crowded, I got my food pretty fast and it look simple but definitely homemade. Tastes good, lighter on the stomach it's not like those chain restaurants or those really big restaurants in Times Square with heavy pasta. It tastes more like home and a bit like country side for me. Nice texture and cute plates, especially the ones on the wall for decorations. Clean place and not too hard to find. Walkable to subway stations. I'd go back and I do recommend people to check it out! It's not a place I'd frequent but it's a place I'd go back once in a while for sure. I wouldn't mind bringing family or friends along too

Title: Surprisingly Satisfying Asian Cuisine with a Side of Rush

I recently ventured into this restaurant for a lunchtime excursion, despite my usual indifference to Asian cuisine. The experience was pleasantly surprising, as I indulged in a bowl of vegetarian ramen. The dish came brimming with corn, greens, and mushrooms, each spoonful more enjoyable than the last. An accompanying shot of sake delivered a potent kick that lingered after each sip.

However, the meal was somewhat marred by the over-attentive staff. Their constant presence felt intrusive and lent a rushed atmosphere to our dining experience. It was later revealed that an impending closing time was the reason for their urgency. A simple upfront notice about the early closing time would have sufficed, instead of the unwelcomed hovering.

In all, the flavors won me over, but the service could use a touch of finesse.

I had dinner here with a friend the other night when the wait at the Korean place I wanted to eat at was 45 min and I didn't feel like waiting. I knew nothing going in, and was pretty much swayed by the fact that at 7:15 pm they were mostly empty and could seat us immediately, plus this is a BBQ joint and smelled delicious!We sat down and looked at the menu for BBQ . Holy sticker stock - $95 pp?? We almost got up to leave. Then the server explained the menu to us a bit more and we saw options more in our price range, so we decided to stay. Again motivated mostly by hunger and a desire to eat...something...soon! Atmosphere-wise this place FEELS fancy with high ceilings and shiny Asian decor. But inside, one whole wall is a giant digital display of scenes from around the world (I swear I saw Italy and Greece) that changes every few minutes and illuminates the restaurant. Whenever I see digital displays like this I always feel the restaurant is confused as to their identity - is this a fast food joint or a high-end experience? The interior was also kind of smoky, as you might expect in a BBQ joint, but instead of you cooking your own food at your own pace, a server rolls a portable cooking table over to you and cooks all the meat and veg, then transfers that to a hot plate on your table, which keeps the cooked food warm as you eat.My friend and I surveyed the spreads at nearby tables and settled on a seafood pancake (totally average) to start and the marinated beef platter for two, which comes with two kinds of marinated short ribs, steak and mushrooms. You also get the typical lettuce leaves and banchan, plus a pile of spiraled radish which serves as the bed for the cooked meat/veg. But no rice.The banchan was comprised of two kinds of kimchi (cabbage and radish), pickled pink radish, raw strips of radish, sugary dried crawfish, dried small fish with seaweed, another kind of seaweed and some kind of shaved root. All average. And actually very westernized if you ask me - like, the kimchi really had no punch, and 4 of the small dishes were very sweet. One more thing I thought was strange was that about halfway through our meal a person came over to our table and took away our banchan, which were all only half eaten, and replaced them with new dishes of the same items. Not sure why that was necessary and it seemed wasteful. The amount of meat we got was ok for me/my portion, but I know my guy friend was still hungry after, even after eating the pancake. Flavor-wise, it was average again, though the cuts of meat seemed of good quality.They also have a full bar and an extensive sake list with options for individual cups, carafs and bottles. We ordered two carafes of different sake - but what was weird was that one server took our food order and a different one came over AFTER and took our drink order, and our saki never came til I asked for it, which was AFTER we had started to eat. Then, when it was served, the server (a third, different person) was confused as to what we ordered and could not tell us which was which. That was disappointing, though the amount of sake you get in one carafe was quite generous, and the serving vessels and slanty glasses were a nice touch!The last thing that happened was that when I gave them my card to pay, they brought back the receipts but not my card. I signed the receipts and didn't notice my card was not there til the next day when I went to use it and didn't have it (probably as a result of all that saki). When I called the restaurant at first the person I spoke to said no they didn't have my card, but I kept prompting him to check the bar, the register, the bill holders, and then he confirmed yes they had it in the register. That was a little frustrating - albeit my fault for not noticing when I was signing the receipt - but still, I expect staff to be more knowledgable if they are answering the phones.Overall a very average experience.  And they seem like they need to work out quite a few kinks to enhance the customer experience. I probably will not go back as I felt it was very overpriced for the strange service and nothing-special taste.  Plus that weird glaring digital wall. Not my thing! Next time I will just suck up the 45 min wait at the place I had in mind in the first place.

During NYC's bustling Restaurant Week, I had the pleasure of dining at Becco, a gem located on the West side. The accessibility from my job made for an effortless visit to this elegant spot. Entering the vibrant atmosphere crowned by an unexpected skylight was a welcome surprise.

Becco's offerings were a testament to excellent cuisine at reasonable prices. The variety of breads left a strong first impression, followed by a crisply served salad on chilled plates. My choice of the salmon did not disappoint; it was flawlessly cooked and seasoned, ensuring each bite was savored. My companion indulged in the unlimited pasta, which proved to be a delightful and worthwhile option, even without the Restaurant Week discount.

Becco certainly made its mark, and I'm eager to return for another round of their delectable dishes.

We had a delightful dining experience at this restaurant! The service was exceptional—staff members were both genuinely cordial and utterly professional.
