The culinary highlights included a delectable garlic flatbread and a superbly roasted, garlicky broccoli that set the bar high. Additionally, the pasta served with meatballs, though its name eludes me, was scrumptious. A noteworthy dessert twist was their cocoa tiramisu; a chocolatey take on the classic which was absolutely delicious. If I were to nitpick, the pasta did skew on the saltier side, but that was a minor note in an otherwise fantastic meal. Highly recommended for a memorable dinner!

For the price, this cannot be beat. We had a party of 10 people and the bill turned out to be less than $200 dollars. I surely thought it would be closer to $250+. We were all pretty stuffed and satisfied. They had the classics like ha gao, siu mai, lotus leaf sticky rice, etc. Everything tasted pretty good, it reminded me of the dim sum restaurants that I ate at as a kid. One thing that stood out was their piggy buns! Super adorable and filled with egg custard. If you want your bang for your buck, Downtown Yummy is the restaurant to go to.

Went to Dallas BBQ last weekend for a light dinner. Honestly I don't know why! The food has never been great but it was the worst that night. My friend and I ordered a broccoli tempura appetizer to start and what came out was enormous pieces of broccoli with no flavor. I had the Steak and Shrimp and she had an order of honey chicken which looked like a plate of diabetes. I expected better for some reason and didn't get it here. The one bright spot was the waitress who served us. She was very nice as she tried to get us to order additional drinks.  Can't remember her name but she had a very nice personality. :) . Overall , let's just say it will be a very long time before I go back to visit again. I advise ppl who are interested in going to go to locations that have really good business like 42nd st. Food quality depends on the location it seems.

Title: A Long-Awaited Visit to Mama's Too: A Slice Worth the Trek?

As a Bensonhurst native and a pizza aficionado, my standards for a good slice are sky-high. Despite the buzz surrounding Mama's Too, I gave it a year, sparing myself the lines and the journey, until my cravings won out.

With an array of options, restraint was impossible; I indulged in four slices - vodka, sopressata with hot honey, poached pear with gorgonzola, and caramelized onion with mushrooms. The latter two, though innovative, lacked punch, a trend I'm noticing with white pies. Meanwhile, the vodka and hot honey slices hit the spot, their robust flavors aligning more with my penchant for saucier choices.

A highlight at Mama's Too is the hot honey, which you can liberally apply to any slice. It strikes an exquisite balance of heat and sweet, enhancing both savory and sweet notes.

The crust deserves a nod – dense, chewy, akin to Detroit-style pizza – though traditionalists be warned, this isn't your quintessential NY slice. While it may not top my list of all-time favorites, Mama's Too stands out as a scrumptious contender in the city's pizza scene.

Hk cafe in Chinatown. I love hk cafe for breakfast so was excited to try this place. Prices are reasonable for the area... bfast for 4 was just over $20!Dishes are smaller than at hk cafes that I've visited elsewhere (not in ny area) but still filling, especially after the milk tea. Got the satay vemicili which was delicious. Meat had a good satay taste and the soup was nice. We managed to seat immediately but there was a wait when we left (after 10 on a Sunday morning).

I've been here for dinner as well as weekend brunch, and love the vibe. It's in a great location in the heart of meatpacking. They have a brunch deal for bottomless mimosas which I'd definitely recommend - so so fun! Personally, I enjoyed the brunch food more than the dinner. If you're in the area at night, I suggest stopping by for a drink at the bar!- Navya J@nyconthetable

Title: A Must-Try Dish at an Unbeatable Value

If you're a first-timer at this gem of a spot, do yourself a favor and dive straight into their Bun Xuong Nuong. This dish hits all the right notes with its perfectly seasoned boneless pork chop, sliced into succulent strips and served atop cool vermicelli noodles and fresh mint leaves. The accompanying fish sauce is nothing short of divine – a flavor explosion that will make your taste buds dance. For an extra buck, top it off with a fried egg; it's the cherry on top of this already delightful meal. Light yet bursting with flavors, it's consistently a win-win. At such an affordable price, this dish is an absolute steal.

Food: 3.5/5Decided to stop by because they have a cute little outdoor seating area. My friend and I needed to kill time so we decided to give this place a try. We ordered the crispy duck salad, edamame, sauvignon blanc and a rosé.The crispy duck salad was fresh and very refreshing! Perfect for a light snack. The edamame was just average. I don't think I've ever had "bad" edamame? Oh, their wine is only $5 and they have great happy hour deals though!I don't think I've tried enough of their food to give them a fair rating but this would be a great potential happy hour spot.Service: 4/5Considering we sat outside, the service was great. They checked in on us repeatedly and made sure we were ok.Ambiance: 3/5Cute outdoor seating area. The inside is modern and casual but there's only one (messy) restroom for the whole establishment. There's seating for approx 50+ people and one toilet. Bummer.

Great menu and service, probably worth the money, but prepare to splurge. Came here with four people, cost was $275/couple, ie $150/person. Granted, we did get five appetizers, three drinks, and one of the steaks was wagyu ($100), but I felt like it was worth the experience.The food felt fresher and more innovative than Mike's Bistro, and more comparable to Reserve Cut. Appetizers are where they shine, and the service is SUPER fast.Highly recommend the ribs appetizer. They come on the bone and are fantastic. The crispy chicken appetizer is excellent too. So is the beef jerky you get with the 'beef and bourbon' drink. The steaks were excellent, we got the wagyu, fillet (which was small and slightly overcooked), and the jalepeno steak. I'd recommend asking them to cook a bit under where you want it.

One of those times where the yelp score matches the experience. What a great time. We came for brunch on a Sunday and sat in the conservatory area. Apparently you can bring your dog inside in that area which is interesting. The service js very good with multiple people checking on us throughout the meal. The menu is pretty straightforward here. It is pretty much American food done right. We tried the shaved brussel sprouts salad which was not overdressed with perfect texture and fresh ingredients. The wilson burger was on the pricier side ($21) but was the highlight of the meal. So good. It was one of the better burgers I have had in a long time. The french fries were crunchy salty and amazing. I couldn't stop eating. My wife also tried the matcha oats which was ok but very filling.  The manager was also really kind as well. Apparently if you are a first time customer you get an envelope that when you come back for the 2nd time you open with the server. It could be a free drink, free app, or free meal! They got there ish together here. Such a fun experience and definitely warrants the 5 star rating.

This is for delivery only. Ordered via Seamless; a cappuccino with almond milk (for an extra $0.51) and a De Turtle Wafel, gluten free ($10.46). I like that they have soy milk as another dairy free alternative. The Turtle Wafel has dulce de leche, Belgian chocolate fudge and walnuts. It's great they have a gluten free option for no extra charge! Delivery arrived early! However, as other seamless members mentioned, my cappuccino had spilled in transit. See photos. Ugh! Frustrating. I was told the delivery man at least mentioned to be careful with the bag. The bag was wet and torn in the bottom corner. I just threw it away.The cappuccino is hot and has a roasty flavor. No bitterness which is good. No foam... bottom of cup wet. I like that they have their own brand cups. I was provided an extra lid which was clean-ish so I wiped it and used it instead; threw the other away. Overall, the cappuccino is okay, 3/5. Not happy it spilled. Packaging issue. Happy it's hot!The De Turtle Wafel is disappointing. The waffle arrived warm. It's very small for the cost and in a box. Their own brand box. The toppings all came separate. Decent portions I guess? The walnuts were whole and not chopped. The chocolate and dulce de leche seem like your average melted milk chocolate and caramel toppings. Nothing special. The waffle is tough to cut through and is doughy.No utensils provided, no napkins provided.Upsetting! Waste of money. Then a co-worker tells me there's no physical location she knows of, just food trucks or carts? So ummm...I won't be ordering from here again. Too expensive and not worth the hassle! I had to top the waffle myself. Geez oh man. If it were less expensive, maybe.I can't recommend anyone try this. Sorry!!

Great spot for a quick lunch or dinner.Best bowl of ramen in Ktown.  Only $10 for most main entrees.  Koku Ramen is probably the must order and the only one I would recommend.  It comes with all the fixings, egg, pork, veggies, corn, ramen, and the broth.Choose from 3 levels of spicyness.  I usually order the max, and it will help clear our your sinuses.There's seating for groups of 4, but I would not come here if you have a large group.  There's also seating at the bar near the kitchen for the single eaters.

Came here on a Saturday evening and was surprised by my family for my birthday. I came in and noticed this spot is packed, I didn't even realize this restaurant was one of the places I bookmarked and really wanted to go too. So we waited near the bar area with my family having some drinks, until I was brought to the back of restaurant and noticed a table filled with all types of food, I felt like I was in heaven. On the table we had a variety of foods such as a huge roasted pig, lumpias, bone marrow, and different types of curry. I just wish I had starved myself for a week to prepare myself to eat all this delicious food. Big props to my wife and the restaurant to setting this up for my birthday, you guys are awesome. It was definitely a once in a lifetime experience and probably the best experience of my life. Cheers
I tried the lovely earl grey and mint teas which arrives in a cute tea set.  The coconut semifreddo was very original and delicious..

Title: A Decent Bowl of Noodles, But Not Exceptional

Having heard a lot about this restaurant, I walked in with expectations that perhaps were set a bit too high. The beef tendon noodles, priced at $8.50, left me wanting more as the tendon portions were skimpy. The thinly sliced tendons were marinated in an unusual way, infused with a strong clover flavor that reminded me of both a Vietnamese pho and Sichuan dishes. This twist was interesting but not entirely to my liking.

The knife-cut noodles were a hit-and-miss affair – thick and satisfying in some bites, disappointingly soggy in others. I did appreciate the textural variety, but I would tip those who favor consistency towards the traditional hand-pulled noodles instead. The spinach was a nice touch, and the pickled cabbages tucked at the bottom were a highlight.

In summary, it's a hearty meal that may warm your belly on a cold day but doesn't live up to the hype. For those venturing into Chinatown seeking culinary delights, there might be more unique options worth exploring.

This restaurant always comes through for me!!!I have only been here for pick-up and the food has always been fresh and delicious, but they also have a huge seating area with a couple of booths. The beers always look ice cold and they have a full bar. Maybe one day I will sit in and have dinner here. * I am deducting one star because the staff (especially Rossy) needs to fix their attitudes.

If you're looking for a cozy spot to catch a game during the winter months, this place is a must-try. They offer enticing specials on food and drinks that are hard to beat. A personal favorite of mine is their Mac and Cheese. It's not just good, it's stellar - creamy, hearty, and utterly satisfying. I find myself ordering it on repeat. Put simply, it's a dish that comes with a hearty recommendation.

Title: Delightful Eats at Nino's, Minor Seating Issue

My dining experience at Nino's was impressive, with the delicious offerings justifying the bustling queue outside. It's wise to book a reservation, particularly during the busy weekend dinner hours.

The evening wasn't without a hiccup; despite my slight arrival ahead of our booked time to set up birthday decorations, our party was uprooted for another group mere minutes before our reservation – a baffling and unwelcome start.

Nonetheless, the culinary prowess at Nino's salvaged the night. We indulged in an array of small plates - the standout being a pizza adorned with ricotta, prosciutto, and mushrooms, boasting a perfect balance of flavor and texture. I highly recommend it for groups.

My entrée, a hearty pasta bolognese, did not disappoint with its tender meat and spot-on al dente pasta. The side of broccoli rabe with prosciutto was an excellent accompaniment. Nino's also offers a BYOB option with a $25 corkage fee, which is a nice touch.

The menu brims with Italian classics sure to satisfy, served in an intimate setting within the vibrant theater district. Despite the initial seating mix-up, Nino's still shines as a culinary gem worth visiting. 4/5 stars.

I recently dined at Skewers, an authentic Chinese food spot where everything, true to its name, is served on skewers. While I found the dishes a tad on the salty side, they were nonetheless flavorful and enjoyable. A unique culinary experience for those looking to indulge in traditional Chinese skewered delights.

The REAL PARTY ENVIRONMENT; loud music and good vibes... the drinks and food are on point.Come here, surround yourself with some good people and have a blast! Everything you need in one location! Not pictured: shrimp tacos and chicken tacos-  both AMAZING! Planning to return soon :)

Came here on a busy Wednesday after work and the place was packed. We didn't have a reservation so we just hang out at the bar, which was a bit noisy. The back part is the restaurant. The inside is like the vault of a bank, which is pretty cool. I had the lobster BLT sliders and they were delicious. I definitely want to come back and try the full restaurant in the vault.

Title: A Letdown on a Former Favorite at Parm

My latest visit to Parm, once heralded by Serious Eats for having the city's best Chicken Parm, was a disappointing experience. What used to be a thick, juicy chicken patty adorned with perfectly melted Mozzarella and a robust sauce has sadly deteriorated. The chicken is now thinly veiled in breading, lost beneath an acrid tomato sauce, while the over-seeded Italian hoagie roll distracts from the main event. 

Even more disheartening was the cost – the sandwiches, void of any sides, felt overpriced given the quality. While the meatballs appetizer was underwhelmingly dry, the Italian Thin Cut Fries and Mozzarella sticks did delight with their impeccable fry. Nevertheless, these few positives couldn't salvage the overall meal.

On a brighter note, service was attentive and efficient, though the table layout was too cramped for our large party. While the staff deserves credit for accommodating a group of 10 spontaneously, the food's falter makes a return visit to Parm unlikely.

Came here today with my husband after hearing how delicious the foods were from my mother in law. We originally wanted sancocho soup and bola de yuca but it was sold out (must be delicious for it to be sold out b4 3pm). We were super hungry so we ended up ordering to share: 1) chicken pastelitos, 2) chuletas (fried pork chop), 3) pernil, 4) rice with black beans & salad, 5) coffee with milk. We also ordered for takeout 2 cubano sandwich & a dominican cake.Everything was so fresh and very delicious! Our most favorites were the chicken pastelito (super crunchy and savory inside), pernil (so delicious, tender and well seasoned), beans (delicious and savory), oxtail (tender and well seasoned) and the coffees (yum!!). The Cuban sandwich was also soooo delicious, crunchy bread with delicious toppings inside - wow!!The lady serving us was one of the nicest and friendliest people we have encountered.  She was beyond accommodating and welcoming. She really made you feel like you are a guest at someone's home. Customer service was excellent.There was many counter seatings and table seatings. We sat on the table and it was quite comfortable. Decor was simple but you are here for the delicious food!Highly recommended! They ran out of sancocho soup - I hope I can get to try it next time if I am in the area.P.S - they take credit card & they deliver via grubhub & amazon.

Love this restaurant ! Really good hype and atmosphere!Came here for the spring them. Their bread and butter was soooo unique and delicious that I can eat all day! The cocktail was also pretty good, on the strong side actually. We got duck breaks and sea bass among us. Pretty good but not fantastic.Great service throughout.A nice spot to celebrate a little. Worth coming once in a while I guess

Go here!! Found this place on Yelp and came in for lunch. The bar is cool. They have a lunch special where you can get a meal and a glass of beer or wine included. I dont remember all the options but there was a burger on there. I had the cauliflower tacos and really enjoyed them, my mom had the ahi tuna and my grandmother had their burger and fries. We all enjoyed our food. I had the Willie Wonka coctail and it was very tasty. Even had a marshmallow in it! I would come back when in the area and would reccomend to friends.

Was excited to see a Korean bbq spot outside of k town and near where I live, but should've realized why it's not in k town.My boyfriend and I got an order of the galbi and a stew with veggies. The galbi order was pretty small considering how expensive it was. I'm happy to pay more for galbi at nice restaurants, but expect the portions to be decent. The stew was also just alright. A bit watery for my taste. The service was also very inattentive and barely checked on us through the meal or even as we were trying to take care of the check. Maybe we didn't order the right things, but don't think we'll be coming back.

Title: A Sky-High Delight Overlooking the Empire State Building

My recent visit to this rooftop gem was motivated by the allure of breathtaking views of the Empire State Building, and I must say, it did not disappoint. The venue offers a laid-back atmosphere with no strict dress code or cover charge, making it accessible for anyone looking to unwind above the city.

Reservations for seating are available, though walk-ins are also welcome, which adds to the relaxed vibe. Intent on soaking in the ambiance for a couple of hours, I opted for appetizers and drinks. The bar service was efficient, delivering both beverages and food with minimal wait time.

The fried calamari stood out - perfectly crisp and flavorful, deserving a special recommendation. Meanwhile, the DJ kept the mood lively, skillfully blending tracks across pop, hip-hop, Caribbean, and Latin genres.

As expected, the prices match the prime location and stunning views - on the higher side but justified by the quality of the food and experience. The majestic view alone is a compelling reason to visit.

I'm already planning my next visit to this urban perch. Whether it's for the panoramic sights, the diverse music, or the tasty bites, this spot is unequivocally worth a return trip.

Title: Disappointing Delivery from [Restaurant Name]

I was looking forward to trying the Asian Bowl for lunch but ended up deeply disappointed. The delivery was painfully late, arriving about 30 minutes behind schedule. When it finally did arrive, the presentation was a disaster — my meal was sloshed around in the container, a far cry from the neat bowl advertised.

Moreover, the portion size was stingy, particularly the Asian slaw and other veggies, which were barely present. The online photo misleadingly featured a protein which was absent from my order. All in all, the experience was underwhelming, and I regret to inform that I won't be giving [Restaurant Name] another chance.

Came here today for lunch with a friend. We were greeted and sat by the host as soon as we went in (it was early so they weren't that busy). We got the hotpot ($25 per person) with two broths. We did the herbal broth and the kimchi. Both broths were good but the kimchi one was delicious! It's my new favorite. We loaded ours up with: beef, tripe, pumpkin, tofu, fried fish balls, cabbage, enoki mushrooms, lotus root, udon noodles, spinach and quail eggs. Everything was brought out quickly. You can order as much as you want so we ordered everything twice once we finished the first round. We saved the noodles for last. They have a sauce station up by the front with bowls and other condiments. The place is clean and interior is nice. The staff could be a little more attentive but that's really my only issue. We had to hail someone over for everything we needed (like to order food and for more water). No one came over to check on us while we ate to see if we were okay. Everyone was nice otherwise. Overall I would come here again if I was in the area and craving hot pot. Solid broths and prices are great!

This restaurant is the full package. Great food, great environment, and great service!! If you're looking for a nice dinner filled with delicious Thai food I would definitely recommend this restaurant.  Unfortunately they don't take reservations on the weekends but my sister and I arrived at 5:00pm and we only waited 10 minutes, but when we left there was a very long line.  The food was amazing!!! Our eyes were definitely bigger than our stomachs but the mango salad and pad Thai were perfect. The environment is so cozy and so warm and the decor is so unique!! If you're in the city - definitely make a stop here!

Overpriced, okay food and lackluster service pretty much sums this place up. We came here for breakfast as it was on our way to TKTS.Every main breakfast entree on the menu was right around the $20 mark. So my husband and I selected the New Yorker breakfast, which includes orange juice, three eggs, crunchy polenta bites (basically fried cubes of polenta), and either a bagel, challah bread or toast and coffee. All of this for $25, a good deal as compared to going a la carte.After our waitress chatted us up and took our order, she never really came back to check on us or refill our coffees. Only after I think she saw me text my husband to tip 15% did she offer to refill our coffee. By that point we were paying and on our way out the door.We will never come back here for any other mea

Title: Pleasant Surprise at FiDi's Chicken Spot

My visit to this FiDi gem was serendipitous. Mistakenly lured by the promise of the 'best fried chicken,' I encountered a delightful rotisserie haven instead. The 1/4 chicken meal, paired with sumptuous mac and cheese and fresh broccoli, made for a satisfying, light midday repast. Next time, I'd spring for the 1/2 chicken to indulge a bit more, and not skip on the extra bread.

The mango chipotle sauce was a standout, adding a zesty twist to the already flavorful chicken. Talia (or Thalia), our cashier, enhanced our experience with commendable service and charm. Prices were reasonable, adding to the appeal of this accidental find. A return visit is definitely on the horizon.

The service was good and the place was cute. I didn't love my avocado toast, but the other people I ate with enjoyed their food. They had fresh flowers on the table and cute decor. They had a really large French press that was nice and strong coffee. Servers were attentive and the food was out quickly. I would consider it for brunch again.

This is a Szechuan hotpot chain, gotta say I had high expectation before I came. I have been to Chengdu, the capital city of Szechuan province that has top notch hotpot (the other one is Chongqing), if you check on Dazhong Dianping (a Chinese yelp app), this brand was rated pretty high, so me and my friend decided to give it a try. We came on a Saturday evening, waited for approximately 25 mins, not that bad. The place was not that spacious, the waiter suggested us to pick the 3 flavored soup base (tomato, signature spicy,  mushroom). We picked the ingredients from the order, spicy beef, duck blood, shrimp paste, Yan jiao (a fujianese pork dumplings), rose cilantro meatballs, a bunch of veggie. The dumplings seems to be frozen for a long time, pretty stiff... the spicy beef was full of pepper, may not be my thing (I think the waiter should have given a more detailed intro for the first time customers, but they did not say a thing when we placed the order). The only highlight was the dessert rose ice jello (玫瑰冰粉). For a hotpot with $80/ per person, this is definitely not meeting my expectation, although it is better than those "all you can eat" cheap hotpot, but I don't see the differentiator being significant.

Title: A Hidden Gem Unveiled

I had the pleasure of dining at a surprisingly incredible eatery recently and it's safe to say that my initial underestimation of the place was completely unwarranted. Despite a deceptive exterior with rarely a crowd in front, the restaurant's interior extends back, providing a cozy dining space.

Upon entering, I was warmly welcomed by the staff, who efficiently took my order. The system they've got down is impressive – after choosing your protein, you're invited to select from an array of side options, including one rice, two vegetables, one salad, and three dips.

My meal was a delightful mix: I opted for the succulent dark meat chicken, which was tender, flavorful, and skillfully grilled—a true highlight of the meal. Accompanying this were the aromatic rice with carrots and raisins, perfectly prepared broccoli, deliciously sweet carrots, and a refreshing kale salad enhanced by a surprise element of strawberries. 

The trio of dips – baba ghanoush, hummus, and particularly the spinach yogurt – each added an extra dimension of taste, with the spinach yogurt emerging as my personal favorite. The pita bread served was a baker's masterpiece, tantalizingly fresh and still warm from the oven.

Complimentary water was easily accessible, rounding out a dining experience that left me eager to return. In summary, it was an amazing meal offering great value and variety. I eagerly anticipate my next visit to sample more of what they have to offer.

I had an excellent dining experience at this gem of a restaurant. The high-quality ingredients were evident in every dish, offering a perfect blend of variety without overwhelming choices. The fried chicken was a standout, and the uni dish captivated my palate. Although the octopus was merely satisfactory, it still added an intriguing note to the meal. The drink selection complemented the food perfectly, and our knowledgeable server provided commendable guidance. It's a rare pleasure to encounter such well-versed staff. Highly recommend for an all-around delightful meal.

I recently visited one of the upper east side's delectable sushi spots, and though I typically order out, the dine-in experience did not disappoint. The standout dish, the yellowtail jalapeño roll, was impeccably crafted with freshly sliced jalapeños adding just the right kick without being overwhelmed by excessive rice – a true mark of quality for sushi aficionados. Stepping into the restaurant around 9 PM on a Thursday, I was greeted by a cozy yet buzzing atmosphere, indicative of its popularity among locals seeking a casual but satisfying dining experience. Whether you're in for a quick bite or a leisurely meal, this restaurant serves up both ambience and flavor that hits the spot.

Title: A Lunar New Year's Eve Delight at Yunnan Noodle Haven

As the Lunar Year drew to a close, my friend and I stumbled upon a quiet noodle spot gearing up to celebrate the New Year. The crowd was thin, owing to the early closure for the festivities, but the flavors at this establishment were anything but. The star of our meal was undoubtedly the Yunnan Crossing Bridge rice noodles.

One taste of the chicken broth left me stunned; it was an exquisite dance of fresh, savory notes that I still struggle to aptly describe. The broth, simmering for four hours, was a revelation—an epitome of culinary patience and expertise. The delicate yet impactful addition of the broth-soaked crackling added a textural surprise that defied its potential heaviness, achieving a perfect symphony of flavors.

I wholeheartedly recommend this delightful find to anyone with a penchant for noodles. It's an experience that beckons a return visit. Whether for the ambrosial broth or the sheer joy of discovery, this is a place that noodle aficionados should not miss.

wow amazing drinks here that are super trendy and super delicious ! had a very amazing poison ivy which was basically my reason for coming here ! vodka with strawberries yumm also the m$m pancakes were incredible

Title: A Feast for Burger and Lobster Aficionados

If you, like me, have an unwavering affection for the divine duo of burgers and lobster, then there’s a spot you shouldn’t miss. On my recent visit, my boyfriend opted for 'The Beast,' a dish that, frankly, didn’t wow me - it lacked the saucy zest and generous lobster helpings I craved. However, it's worth noting that it might not be everyone's pick.

Delving into my favorites, the standard burger here never fails to impress: it’s top-notch. But the crowning glory of my taste buds has to be their lobster rolls: an absolute delight and a must-try for any seafood lover. This time, I ventured to try their new lobster Mac and cheese. While not the ultimate best I've had, it was a creamy, comforting concoction I thoroughly enjoyed.

Some might balk at the prices, but considering the meal is complemented with a crisp salad and a serving of French fries, it’s a value I'm willing to pay for. In the realm of indulgent surf and turf, this place is a catch!

Title: A Flavorful Experience with Generous Portions

We visited the restaurant for dinner, with a reservation in hand, and were pleasantly seated without delay. A little insider tip: checking into Yelp grants you a complimentary beer – a nice touch!

Our shared feast commenced with Steamed Soup Dumplings which had a slightly thicker skin than I'm used to, but still fell into the 'pretty good' category. The Sliced Beef Tripe was notably thin, tender, and carried a welcome spicy kick. The Pork Belly was a fatty delight - truly indulgent and satisfying for those who appreciate the richer cuts. A personal highlight was the Snow Peas in Garlic – a delicious rendition of my favorite Chinese vegetable.

The restaurant's reputation for spicy dishes was apparent, and while not everyone at our table was a fan of heat, the menu was diverse enough to cater to different tastes. 

In conclusion, the portions were decent, and the service was noteworthy in its efficiency. With so much more to try, a return visit is certainly on the cards!

My first time here. Its on the 2nd floor so you have to get a set of steps to get to the restaurant. I was actually just here with co workers to pick up a large order so I didn't actually eat here. I did get a chance to peek at the set up though. Decent sized space for a restaurant. Seems like it is an old town house. There's a bar right by the entrance and there were plenty of tables. I'm not positive but I want to say there was an outdoor seating area in the back?Our order was all there but they didn't mark down what each dish was which I think should be standard with large orders. The food was good but very spicy. I actually like spicy food so it wasn't an issue for me. I'll be back again.

Is it possible to give this place 6 stars? The pizza is beyond amazing. Neopolitan style. Authentic Italian. They import all of their ingredients from Italy. I am gluten free and dairy free and I am so excited to say that this place has gluten free and vegan cheese options. I have no idea how they make their vegan cheese but it is hands down the best I have ever had and taste and has consistency like real cheese. The gluten free crust is soft and has a great texture (no hard thin crust here!!). This place is so amazing that my husband and I came here every night we were in NYC (3 nights!!). Thank you Ribalta for giving me good pizza for the first time in the 6 years I've been gluten/dairy free.

First time trying a poke bowl &  it certainly won't be my last! So glad I finally decided to check out this place for lunch. They have plenty of options to choose from in terms of the protein, toppings, and dressings. I got a shrimp tempura bowl with red onion, sweet corn, carrots, cilantro, pickled daikon, and wonton crisps smothered in sriracha aioli and wow. So so delicious and a pretty good portion for $13. Aside from the bowls, you can also get poke salads and sushi burritos - saw quite a few people ordering the latter so I'll be trying that soon too.  The restaurant itself is a bit small but they do have a few tables and counters to eat in. There's water free of charge in the seating area. They also have a rewards card - after you buy a certain number of items you get a free one. Staff was nice considering how busy they were. Great spot overall, highly recommend checking it out if you're in the area.

Title: A Delightful Experience During Restaurant Week

My recent visit to this restaurant for Restaurant Week proved to be a fantastic decision. The staff greeted us with unwavering politeness and attentiveness, setting the tone for a lovely dining experience. Elegance permeated the atmosphere, and the thoughtful provision of a coat check was much appreciated in the chilly winter weather.

Each dish arrived as a visual treat and tantalized the taste buds to match, with the chocolate mousse cake standing out as the star of the show. While the portions were modest, the three-course lunch left us satisfactorily full. 

A slight hiccup was the pre-appetizer bread, which was on the dry side, but this was a minor issue in an otherwise impeccable meal. I would highly recommend this restaurant to others, especially during special events like Restaurant Week.

I recently ordered delivery from this restaurant and opted to try the Yum Nam Sod Salad. While the flavors were fresh – a zesty blend of salami, peanuts, red onions, greens, scallions, cilantro, and ginger, all tossed in a chili lime dressing – the portion size was disappointing. Despite the relatively speedy delivery and careful packaging, the salad was shockingly small, especially considering the $13.95 price point. It was far from satisfying and left me feeling like it wasn't a good value for my money. As such, I can't see myself ordering from this establishment again; it simply wasn't filling or worth the cost.

A very satisfactory meal, overall a great vibe. The waiter was quite attentive and our dishes arrived at a timely manner. The interior decor was quaint and suited the restaurant nicely. I noticed while we were heading out that they were Michelin 2018. Anyway, the dishes we ordered for restaurant week's dinner included: softshell crab karage, homemade hot tofu, black angus steak, broiled black cod, green tea mochi, and shiratama anmitsu. Each restaurant week meal came along with miso soup and a salmon roll, which was a great addition to the dinner. I particularly enjoyed the cod, as it was delicately seasoned and extremely tender. I quite enjoyed my meal, as the portions weren't too large either and I hope to some day return to try their grill and other dishes!

Came here for take out for 4 slices and they only got 1 slice right even though it was not busy. Overall good pizza, slightly oily, and wish they got my orders right since we were craving for the missing buffalo chicken- mushroom pepperoni (the only correct one): standard pizza- mushroom pizza: not the best, pretty bland (probably cause not the slice we ordered)- chicken parm: meh (they also gave two of these)

The very very good taco spot from uptown just opened a new location on Delaney Street, right outside the entrance to the Williamsburg Bridge.These are excellent tacos. For $4 each, they have all the different meats you can think of for your taco, which are among the best you'll get in NYC. They have a bunch of other stuff too like nachos, burritos, and rice plates if you want something more substantial.

What a great new addition to Chinatown.  I heard such great things about this restaurant and read the review on the New Yorker, so I was feeling really lucky getting the chance to try their food. I'll be honest though, I had some trouble finding the restaurant at first and walked by it twice before I pulled out my phone and looked at the address.  The restaurant is on the second floor and you can easily miss the door leading into the restaurant.The restaurant is decorated in traditional Chinese style with wood and bamboo accents.  Tables with benches create a nice relaxed atmosphere. But after seating a while, I was wanting seats with backs to lean on.  Also, during the meal I was wishing that they had more ventilation.  When the pots started to boil, and steam was everywhere, it became a bit much to handle.  That in combination with the spicy broth had all of us sweating in no time.  You will for sure come out smelling of hotpot when you leave.    If you are lucky enough to get a table by the windows, you will get decent views.   The restaurant isn't large, and tables were on the small side.  Good thing the wait staff were quite attentive and took away empty dishes quickly.  Most of the staff spoke English and were able to answer questions we had of the menu. They give you paper menus and you order by selecting the items on it. It's so very convenient but the menu could have used more descriptions and pictures.  They'll give you several copies of the menu so that you can reorder and add more items during the meal.I though the food tasted very fresh and tasty.  We ordered the signature spicy broth and tomato-based broth for the half-half hotpot.  We asked for the medium level for the spicy broth.  For the dipping selection we ordered a plethora of vegetables and meats.  My favorite was the pork belly and sliced cucumbers.  There was so much food that I lost count on how many dishes we ordered.  The spicy broth was delicious and had good flavor. We ordered the medium spice level and it had a nice kick.  You can mix your own sauce but honestly you don't need it.  The broth in the hotpot was so good that I ended up abandoning the sauce I made during the meal. I highly recommend getting their watermelon drink.  It was a nice balance to the spicy food we were eating.   Overall, I quite enjoyed my meal and will definitely be back.  And next time I'm ordering the mild spicy!

This new location on 3rd and 43rd is 'da bomb'! The summer roll had the best spicy peanut sauce I've had in years. The jacktuna (jackfruit as tuna) salad was so tasteful I could've eaten two! I can't wait to try more of these dishes. The counter folks were very helpful and let you taste whatever you want. I'm pretty sure all the pasta here is quinoa (gluten free) and delicious. The tables are all high with bar stools (as opposed to regular seating). One of the best vegan places in NYC.

Title: Uncomfortable Experience and Poor Service Overshadow Good Food

I recently dined at a new local restaurant and was met with a series of letdowns. The interior was unbearably hot due to a malfunctioning air conditioning system, making it clear there was a lack of preparation for a summer opening. This discomfort was compounded by the lackluster service that did little to expedite the meal and alleviate the sweltering environment.

The food offerings were a mixed bag. The guacamole was a highlight, delivering on taste and quality. However, not all aspects of the meal were satisfactory. The salsa fell flat for our palate, prompting us to send it back, only to find it surprisingly itemized on the final bill despite not consuming it. As for the main course, the mushroom quesadilla was generously portioned and flavorful, a beacon in the otherwise gloomy dining experience.

Regrettably, the combination of the indoor heat and the underwhelming service overshadowed the few culinary positives. Improvement in basic customer service and a functioning AC are critical for a better dining experience.

I recently dined at Jeju, a place that seems to ride the wave of its Michelin star rather than genuinely deserving it. Unfamiliar with its reputation, I was intrigued to try Korean ramen at my friend's recommendation. Despite its supposed popularity, securing a reservation wasn't possible, leading us to chance a walk-in on a dreary Monday evening, which thankfully didn't require a wait due to the restaurant being surprisingly empty.

The meal kicked off with their Toro Ssam Bap, a dish I found delightful. The concept of wrapping fatty tuna, scrambled egg, and tobiko rice with seaweed was enjoyable, particularly with the unexpected twist of the egg. Yet, the $25 price tag for an appetizer seemed steep, overshadowing its charm.

The main course, So Ramyun, featured a veal broth with brisket, scallions, pickled garlic, and garlic oil. It started promising with the novelty of cooking raw beef in the broth. However, the charm was short-lived as the richness of the broth turned overwhelming, and the noodles themselves were unremarkable.

In summary, Jeju's offerings didn't live up to the hype that one might expect from a Michelin-starred establishment, particularly considering the hefty price. The restaurant's ambiance doesn't compensate for an eating experience that leaves much to be desired. If you're not a fan of heavy broths or high price tags, don't let the Michelin star lead you astray.

Dan and I came here years ago for our 6 month anniversary (now going on 4 years wow!) and it was such a lovely family style dinner. We wines and dined and got calamari to start and the best part was the shrimp francese!!! I've had chicken francese before but never shrimp! Yum!! We also shared penne vodka! We should definitely come back here for our next anniversary:)

Reliably good modern Greek food.  Very good choice for people with dietary restrictions!Everything we had was pretty good.  I did notice the chicken soup tasted different between the two times I visited (lunch vs dinner)?  I particularly loved the caviar spread which is always tasty everywhere I order it.  Octopus was good not bland and overly soft like it is at an unnamed midtown tapas staple.  The dips come with bread but you can optimally add a pretty vegetable crudite plate if you don't want to stuff yourself with pita bread.Service is good.  Spacious new interior with a Tribeca vibe.

I recently visited a restaurant with the hope of enjoying a quick snack, but I was met with a rather disappointing experience. Despite the lack of a queue, I found myself waiting an excessive 20 minutes just to receive an order of fries. The establishment boasts two fryers, each capable of handling two orders at once, yet due to what appeared to be repeated mishaps by the staff, they only managed to produce enough fries for one order at a time.

During my prolonged wait, I observed the kitchen staff repeatedly attempting to fry batches, only to mess them up and start over several times. When I finally received my fries, I found them to be quite ordinary, certainly not justifying the lengthy and unnecessary delay. It seems that either a stroke of bad luck or a consistent operational issue is at play here. In either case, if you're craving fries and time is of the essence, you might want to consider other options.

Title: A Delectable Tease at Miznon - Chelsea Market

On a bustling Christmas Eve day at Chelsea Market, my all-time favorite NYC spot that never ceases to amaze with its ever-changing offerings, my husband and I succumbed to the allure of Miznon for a 'light' lunch. Despite our plan to conserve appetite for a grand dinner, the Falafel Burger available only on Tuesdays and Fridays swiftly sabotaged our restraint. This Miznon marvel, an exquisite amalgamation of freshly fried falafel, juicy tomato, tangy pickles, smooth sour cream, and zesty green chili peppers cradled in warm pita, was a revelation. In a fleeting symphony of flavors, we devoured the divine sandwich, instantly regretful of our decision to share a single portion. Our brief encounter with Miznon's culinary excellence has left an indelible mark, ensuring a swift return to savor more. Highly recommended for a taste of sublime satisfaction—just maybe order your own. Yummmm.

We enjoyed a delightful meal at LOX on Christmas Day, where we were trying to escape Christmas among our people.  We dined at the cafe and then saw a Yiddish play.  It was a memorable experience for our family.The menu in itself was incredible -- creative and inspired gourmet twists on Eastern European Jewish favorites. The food was delicious, presentation attractive and service excellent.The smoked fish and caviar dishes were of the highest quality.  I loved the buttery challah and delicate blini that came as accompaniments along with fresh vegetables and pickles.  My mom was still savoring her memory of how good whitefish salad was a week later, and my dad still dreaming about the delectable mon (poppyseed) pastry.  We tried chocolate babka for dessert as well and it was rich and flaky, a perfect rendition of the classic cake.  Unlike most Jewish delis, service was very good here.  They enthusiastically accommodated all our requests.  The waiter was a cutie.  There is no cocktail menu but they have a full bar.  I ordered a mojito and the chef himself brought out a gorgeous drink artfully arranged on an island of ice, with a generous extra serving that my dad enjoyed. A lovely lunch all in all.

*Mealpal Review*Got this for lunch today via MealPal. The serving size was disappointing especially after I took the dressing out. I rarely finish my food but I managed to do so with this salad, and was still peckish. The salad actually tastes nice. The chicken was nice and soft, goes well with the dressing and kale. Bottom line: would get this again if I was on a diet or if the restaurant decides to up their portions!

Short review: Go for the dons/bowls. The Oyako don is massive and the unagi don is pretty good as wlel.I've gone here a couple times as they have a very different menu to the other local sushi place by work. While I prefer the sushi at Oishi (due to the more plain rolls such as tuna and salmon instead of having cucumber and I find the tuna to be a bit worse here,) I prefer the bowls here as well as the miso soup (as it contains enoki mushrooms and other stuff.) The unagi-don is OK with a good portion while the oyako-don is massive. 3.6 mostly for the oyako don.

Shusssh. The brunch I had today at Quantum Leap could possibly be one of the best I've had all year.  Although I wanted to keep it a secret, I must share.My friend and I were looking to stumble upon a place for brunch in the Greenwich Village area. Sometimes, I'll do homework with a place in mind, but often, it can be a new discovery. Quantum Leap was just that today.From across the street, we nearly passed it up but my friend was drawn to the exterior. Truth be told, I thought it was a health store selling vitamins and juices. Once we perused the menu outside and already decided what we would order, we were eager to try it and very charmed by the quaint atmosphere upon entrance. My friend loves French Toast which was her order, but this was not typical and looked amazing since it was  prepared differently. It included 3 slices of Gluten free bread accompanied by hash browns with raspberry jam on the side and a cocoa powder dusting. She gave it two thumbs up.My selection was the Vegan Choice which was recommended by the waitress. It was full of flavor and very delicious---scrambled tofu, grilled vegetables and hash browns along with one slice of grain bread. All the flavors combined perfectly together and I really liked their version of hash browns.Resembling rice, it was fluffy,  not oily and incorporated lots of onions. My friend had coffee with her brunch and it must have been 5 cups in total because they offered endless refills. I had a hot green tea with one hot water refresh.Staff were prompt & attentive, decor was cozy & immaculate and the food was divine. I highly recommend and cannot wait to return.

Title: A Lackluster Experience at Hometown Buffet

My recent visit to Hometown Buffet left much to be desired, especially when compared to the offerings at 99 Favor. During a lunchtime visit with a group of eight, despite the restaurant being only half-full, we found the service frustratingly slow, particularly when it came to fulfilling our all-you-can-eat meat requests. The servers limited us to one plate of meat at a time, leading to an exasperating dining experience as we constantly had to flag down staff for additional orders.

Many of our requests, like watercress and corn, were repeatedly ignored or forgotten. Although I appreciate a good slice of fatty beef, the cuts served here were excessively fatty, diminishing the overall enjoyment. The rest of the menu was unremarkable – take the dumplings, for example, with their disproportionate skin-to-filling ratio.

A personal misstep was choosing the tomato broth; its charm quickly soured over the course of our two-hour meal. In retrospect, another broth might have improved the situation.

In all, those looking for a satisfying and efficient all-you-can-eat experience might want to look elsewhere. Hometown Buffet has room for improvement in both service and quality.

So my 5 star is for the service, steak, and cocktails. The sides I'd probably give a 4. They held our table for 6 even though our full party was almost 45 minutes late. I was eternally grateful for this. It was also a Saturday night and my boyfriend's birthday. Our server was very attentive and knowledgeable even though it was crazy busy. Our drinks were never empty and we didn't have to wait long for any of our courses. I highly recommend the porterhouse. The serving for 4 fed 5 of us. It was huge and very tasty. The cook was perfect. The steak sauce is better than Peter Luger's for sure. The cocktails were well worth it. Definitely large and in charge. My cosmo was very big and delicious! You have to get the bacon appetizer- again better than Peter Luger's! The sides that came with the steak were okay. Not bad by any means but nothing I'd go back for specifically. I loved everything else so worth the trip.

Title: A Delightful Sunday Brunch Experience

My friends and I decided to indulge in a Sunday brunch at this popular spot at 3 PM and were immediately swept up by the vibrant atmosphere. The music set a lively tone, and the crowd was buzzing with energy, all complemented by the exceptional service.

Initially, there was a minor hiccup when we were offered seating at the bar, which wasn't to my sister's liking. However, her concerns were swiftly addressed by the manager, and by 4:10 PM, we were comfortably nestled in a booth. The quick resolution added to our positive experience.

The brunch menu dazzled us, particularly the Ps burger and the steak and eggs, which I'd classify as must-haves. Both dishes were the epitome of brunch decadence. To top it all, the unlimited drinks kept our spirits high and glasses full.

While this spot is a fantastic venue for a relaxed brunch with friends, be prepared to pay a premium for the experience. Price aside, it's definitely a place I recommend when you're in the mood for a treat.

Title: Homestyle Korean Comfort in the Heart of East Village – K'OOK Delivers

If you're in the East Village and yearning for a taste of traditional Korean fare amid the ever-growing scene of fusion and modernized cuisine, K'OOK is a refreshing oasis. There's an authenticity that resonates from the moment the banchan arrives. Their four complimentary varieties set the stage, with the potato salad being a standout that I'd gladly devour by the bucket. The kimchi, too, carries that signature homemade punch.

The Crispy Rice Egg, K'OOK's take on a Scotch Egg, incorporates kimchi for a flavorful twist. While inventive, it falls a notch short of its traditional counterpart but is nonetheless enjoyable for those seeking something slightly different.

Their Korean Fried Chicken Wings are a reliable choice for your KFC cravings. Competent and satisfying, they do little to differentiate themselves in a crowded field but still leave you content. It's the Hot & Crispy Baby Back Ribs, however, that steal the show. Picture the addictive taste of crispy fried chicken transforming into rib form: juicy, generously portioned, and utterly indulgent.

Traditionalists will appreciate the Dduk BoKi's hearty serving size and traditional elements, complete with a perfectly cooked egg and abundant fish cake. And when it comes to comfort, the Gal Bi Jjim is a dish not to be missed. Sweeter than most, the braised short rib stew has depth, with the meat so tender it falls effortlessly from the bone.

In conclusion, K'OOK serves up homestyle Korean comfort food with a level of authenticity that's becoming rare in the urban trend-chasing gastronomic landscape. It's the perfect spot for those looking to satiate their cravings for genuine Korean flavors in a cozy, unpretentious setting.

Title: Time-Honored Elegance and Culinary Mastery at a Historic Jewel

Review:
Stepping into one of the USA's oldest fine dining establishments, established in 1837, I was immediately struck by the high-quality atmosphere and immaculate facilities. The professionalism and courtesy displayed by the staff enhanced the sophisticated ambiance.

The culinary experience was exceptional. The beet and pear salad with house-made burrata was a highlight; the cheese's creamy interior and firm shape were a testament to the kitchen's attention to detail. It's a dish worth returning for on its own.

The miso bass, tender to the fork and perfectly seared, was served with fresh veggies and complemented by a duo of sauces, creating a harmonious dish. The al dente bolognese appetizer, enriched with delectably tender short rib, did not disappoint either.

However, the chocolate mousse cake stole the show, setting a high bar for all future chocolate mousse expectations with its unrivaled texture and richness.

My high recommendation comes easily for this venerable dining space. I eagerly anticipate my next visit.

After frequently passing by and admiring its authentic vibe, I finally had the chance to try out the local restaurant I'd been curious about. Opting for takeout due to the lack of air conditioning which made the indoor temperature uncomfortable, I ordered a meat-heavy sandwich. While it was generously filled, the flavor didn't quite meet my expectations. Unfortunately, my meal also led to a mild stomach upset. Admittedly, my experience was underwhelming this time around.

Very good!! The veal Parmesan was a perfectly cooked nice piece of real veal - that tasted like veal.  The cheese topping was perfectly balanced and the  cheese tasted as it should. Bonus points come in for real Burratta splotched on the top of the melted cheese. The gravy or sauce, was not overpowering and very tasty. The spaghetti was perfectly cooked - al dente.The portions were spot on. There is no doubt I would come back or recommend it to friends.The appetizer bar is insane and a large group would have a ball here.I'd give Fiorello a 5 star but the price point on the food and wine was a bit high even taking into consideration the location. Not having eaten all day and still hungry from last night's fiasco at Clary's Irish Bar I bounced back and forth in the row of restaurants across from the Lincoln Center. I am certain I made the right call!

Title: A Delightful Brunch Experience!

I had the pleasure of dining at this gem of a restaurant for a Saturday brunch and what a treat it was! Despite not taking reservations, we were seated immediately upon arrival at the bustling hour of 12:30 PM—a rare and welcome surprise for a party of two.

I indulged in the eggs Benedict, which was absolutely divine. Each bite was a harmonious blend of flavors and freshness. My friend opted for a couple of sides, and together we shared a stack of pancakes. The pancakes were a hit—fluffy, warm, and clearly made with care.

I must commend the kitchen for serving dishes that tasted freshly made and didn't give off that dreaded 'pre-made, refrigerated' vibe. The service was attentive without being overbearing, and the atmosphere struck the right balance between cozy and spacious.

This brunch spot has certainly earned a return visit from me. Highly recommended for a satisfying meal that will leave you looking forward to your next visit!

When I walked in it smelled like my grandmothers kitchen. And the chef came out and greeted me with a smile and a shimmy. She had on that grandma auntie head wrap too... I ain't even try the food yet but by the looks of that head wrap, it's gon be FIRE! The bartender was joyful and welcoming. The sangria HAS BLUEBERRIES IN IT !!! Praise him... sorry caught the Holy Ghost real quick. Can't wait to eat ya'll!--------So boom: I had the fish and grits with a salmon cake. Mad delicious, but def not my grandmothers grits. They were good tho. The fish was perfect. But that salmon cake.... praise the lordt. Amazing. The biscuit was terrible. It was cold and did not taste good at all. Service was great. Bae had an omelette with spinach and cheese, he really enjoyed it. He loved the coffee! He also hated his biscuit though. He loved his potatoes too. Overall: I still give it 5 stars- it was clean, smelled great, the music was amazing cuz I'm a 50 year old living in a 26 year old body ... I will be back!

I got the burger and lobster combo which was a smaller version of their burger (still a pretty decent size), full lobster, fries, side salad and a mimosa for $40! What a deal! We also ordered calamari as an appetizer. The lobster was cooked perfectly and the calamari was very good. The burger was about average.

Title: A Satisfactory Work Lunch Experience

I recently visited this establishment for a work lunch and found the atmosphere calm upon arrival, with the crowd picking up later. Service was competent throughout our stay. I opted for a special, which featured shrimp in a zesty sauce paired with rice. It was flavorful and enjoyable, though on reflection, I might lean towards a Cubano sandwich for future visits. Portion sizes were modest, especially when drawing comparisons to the heartier offerings at places like Sophia's Cuban Cuisine. For fine dining, it was almost the perfect lunch portion — however, I must admit a slight preference for the more generous and familiar comforts of Sophia's.

Title: Swift Service, Mixed Dining Experience

I recently placed a delivery order from a local restaurant that warrants a 3.5-star rating. The service left a positive first impression as the order arrived notably fast, which was greatly appreciated. The meal itself, however, was a bit of a mixed bag. 

Starting with the arroz con pollo, it was a mediocre dish; the chicken was served in large chunks that unfortunately translated to a somewhat dry texture. On the other hand, the ropa vieja did not disappoint with its rich and flavorful profile, and the empanadas were a delightful treat as well.

A side of yuca fries had potential but was let down by the fact that they arrived cold. Despite some misses, the portions served were generously sized, making the meal feel like good value for the price paid. 

Overall, while not every dish hit the mark, the excellent ropa vieja, tasty empanadas, and reasonable pricing are points in this restaurant's favor.

Title: Mixed Impressions at American Cut – Not Quite Iron Chef Level

As an ardent fan of Marc Forgione from his Iron Chef days, my excitement for a dining experience at American Cut during restaurant week was met with both hits and misses. The steakhouse boasts a cool, almost underground ambiance, with a distinctively spacious layout, rare for NYC establishments.

The menu tantalized our group, leading to a selection of various dishes. The baked oysters were a creamy overload, masking the natural flavors, while the yellowtail crudo shone as a highlight with its high-quality and flavorful profile. The execution of the tenderloin, however, was inconsistent, ranging from perfectly seasoned to overly salty. Scallops mostly delighted with a perfect sear, save for one pale outlier, coupled with a bland broth.

Surprisingly, the "chicken under a brick" outshone its beefy competitors, claiming the title of best entrée. Sides did not disappoint, with the hash browns providing a satisfying crunch and the cauliflower delivering a perfectly roasted bite, enhanced by a tangy sauce and capers.

Dessert was underwhelming, with the Chocolate Sunday evoking a homemade simplicity that fell short of the establishment's reputation. Additionally, inconsistency emerged again as one ice cream serving contained unwanted ice crystals.

Service was lackluster; instances of servers reaching awkwardly across the table and a casual approach to silverware placement detracted from the upscale dining experience. Moreover, a lack of attention to detail was evident when a dessert was served in the absence of a guest, leading to an unnecessarily melted mess upon her return.

In summary, American Cut unfortunately did not live up to the high expectations set by Chef Forgione's televised success. While the potential shined through in certain aspects, the overall experience was marred by culinary inconsistencies and service mishaps.

Stick with the Sichuan specialities.Tried some new dishes today. They were a little more on the less impressive end. The Gui zhou spicy chicken had okay flavor but wasn't really that spicy.  The kung bao (yes bao, not pao) was decent in flavor, but rather sweet compared to most.

We were in Chinatown and really haven't had sushi since the outbreak.  We decided to try this place out of spur.  Got the party tray A platter which came with 6 rolls for $35.  I think one of them was a California roll while the rest were eel with cucumber, spicy salmon, smoke salmon with creme cheese, salmon with avocado and lastly tempura.  They were all pretty decent and was just average and wish the selections were more diverse than the regular well known rolls.  Good thing is they do taste pretty fresh and presentation was great, but for today, I would give them a solid 3 stars.  I believe there is a Yelp coupon offer which I failed to use.

Had an lovely Indian meal at Pippali. We came here after our visit in Central Park, and decided to have a nice dinner in our last few days in the City. Luckily we found this amazing Indian restaurant around the corner and made our way here. I'm filling in this review late, revisiting my visit and eats from New York City. So glad we found this Indian restaurant, since it's very hard to find a decent Indian restaurant which get their flavours and spices right. We started off with appetisers, we got malai paneer tikka. Which was so delicious and the quantity was right for about three people. Then we got the chicken biryani, which came in this dish covered with roti, which we had to poke in to get to the biryani. So cool! We obviously got dessert, because no meal is complete without dessert! We got gulab jamun, which came with four pieces really good quantity for the price. I loved the ambience here and cost wise is also worth it!

Everything we ordered was very good. We started with the summer rolls filled with flank steak and we really enjoyed the flavor of these. The steak was tender and the rice paper on the outside had a nice texture. We also enjoyed the noodles that came inside. We also got the chicken satay which was great. The chicken was tender and hot when it was served and the sauce had a great peanut flavor. I then got the spicy pho udon soup and really enjoyed it. My husband got the regular pho and also really enjoyed it. The soup portions are huge so you can definitely take half of it home.

Been coming here for yearss! My fav bar of all times with great music and happy hour deals! The food is just as good and the crowd is forever raving. Their kitchen is open nightly until 4 am so you can always grab something to eat. A selection of 14 draft beers, 15 bottled & canned beers, and a full selection of spirits will keep you from going thirsty. my new favorite go to is the huckleberry lemonade!You can never go wrong here! If sports is you thing, Off The Wagon should be your destination. They have 17 flat panel TV's and 1 giant 100" screen where you can watch just about any sporting event both local and out of market.

This place is awesome! The meat buns are wonderful, tasty, and cheap. Two of these should be able to satiate your appetiteThe noodles are fresh and well madeThe cucumber are great. But I feel they are not worth the price for them. I'd skip them next time. The food are freshly made in front of you. They are quick and efficient. There are plenty of space for you to seat and enjoy the food. This is definitely worth it

Amazing baja style fish tacos! (best I've had outside of San Diego)Cool diner-like vibe. (But not cramped)Tables that accommodate 2, 4 and upwards of 20.Quick and friendly service.The only downside is the price...it's a bit pricey.

Thanks to my friend who treated us to Omakase! It was my first Omakase experience so I can't compare to other experiences, but I have to say that it was a wonderful treat. We were all blown away by each plate. Sushi was absolutely delicious and fresh. The high quality of ingredients definitely enhanced the food quality. Chef Toshio Suzuki was very friendly and answered every question we had in detail. Watching him prepare each sushi plate was simply amazing; I personally embrace the art of sushi making and Chef Suzuki's presentation was very artistic which made our dining experience even more memorable. Overall, you will be very full by the end of the course. From small dishes to Chef Suzuki's inspiration sashimi art to absolutely fantastic omakase sushi and handroll to traditional monaka for dessert--I would definitely come back for another amazing Omakase experience. Thank you, Chef Satuski and sous-chef!

Title: A Touch of Culinary Magic at [Restaurant's Name]

Last evening's dining experience at [Restaurant's Name] was a journey of diverse textures and flavors, leaving a notable impression on both my date and me. Our meal commenced with a strikingly good foie gras paired with fig jam, which I can't recommend enough; it was exquisite. The escargot, while decent, lacked a punch – a generous helping of garlic might have elevated it further.

The entrees were a split affair; the crab cakes were satisfactory but lacked distinctiveness. However, the boeuf bourgignon swept us off our feet. It was nothing short of a culinary triumph, enveloping my taste senses in a rich tapestry of flavors that resonated on an emotional level. The plant-based meat was tender and convincing to the palate, and it was just as magnificent when savored the following day.

Dessert brought us the orange creme brulee, where the flavor soared high but the texture fell slightly flat. The top lacked the anticipated shatter of a perfect brulee, and the custard didn't quite achieve the firm set one expects. Despite this, the taste was so remarkable that I would gladly order it again.

In essence, while not every dish was a showstopper, those that shined did so brilliantly. [Restaurant's Name] is a place where flavor triumphs and leaves you yearning for another visit.

I recently had the pleasure of enjoying some of the best Tsukemen in NYC at this gem of a restaurant. The bowl was highlighted by a generous slab of succulent pork, perfectly chewy noodles, and the zesty addition of mustard greens. What really elevated the experience was the broth – an aromatic and rich concoction brimming with shrimp morsels that left my taste buds dancing.

Additionally, the pork musubi was a delightful bite-sized treat, and the complimentary sake paired with it was a thoughtful touch that rounded off the meal beautifully. In short, it's a top-notch dining experience for anyone craving authentic Tsukemen with a few delicious extras.

I went there to meet a friend for a drink and a light bite - it was fine. We were able to sit down and have a quiet area to chat. I had a yelp offer which allowed me to have spring rolls "on the house." My friend ordered a meal and a glass of wine.The restaurant is clean so that's important to me. The waitstaff was pleasant and we were able to get in/out in about an hour (which is all I had to spare that day). It's near Bloomingdales so you can make an afternoon out of it - shopping and dining! Why not? It is a decent Asian place that will not break the bank!

Came here for Christmas Day dinner, it gave a nice classic feel with the lights and old pictures. We made a reservation so we were seated right away, otherwise we heard it was about a 30-45 minute wait. I loved the checkered table cloths and the really old school Italian charm to the restaurant. We ordered classics (chicken parmigiana and spaghetti and meatballs) which were really delicious! There were only 2 of us and being that there food is meant to be family style, the smallest dish will feed 3. We took a bunch home for leftovers but the food truly was delicious. This is a big tourist attraction we noticed being that it's in the Times Square area (Theater District) and is also in the same building as Planet Hollywood. It was a nice dining experience and definitely recommend if you're looking for a classic Italian feel. (The only reason I'm giving 4 stars out of 5 is because our spaghetti and meatballs was supposed to come with 3 meatballs but they only served us 2, just because there was 2 people doesn't meant we shouldn't still receive the full amount it's meant to come with) Didn't make a big deal of it because it was Christmas but be cautious of what your dish comes with!

Title: Great Potential Marred by a Few Hiccups

Last night, February 25th, I dined here for a birthday celebration and my experience was a mixed bag. On one hand, the lamb chops, while delightfully seasoned, arrived disappointingly cold. This, paired with the lackluster service from our server, Antonio—who seemed to embody the essence of slowness and inattentiveness—diminished what could have been a flawless evening.

Despite these setbacks, there were aspects of the night that shone brightly. The host, Cassidy, was a beacon of hospitality, earning a resounding five stars for the warm welcome and attentiveness. The ambiance of the restaurant was also top-notch, contributing to a festive and welcoming dining environment.

The drinks we ordered were commendable, earning a solid four-star rating, complementing the meal nicely even though the main star—the lamb chops—was let down by its temperature.

Even with the service leaving much to be desired, I see the untapped potential of this place. It's a solid four-star restaurant that could easily bump up to five with consistent food temperature and improved waitstaff performance. I liked the restaurant enough to plan a return visit, with hopes next time the entirety of the experience will match the high bar set by the ambiance and host. Fingers crossed for a different server—sorry, Antonio, but you just weren't up to par this time.

Title: A Staple in My Dining Rotation - Rag Trader

I've made the Rag Trader a regular haunt for my dinner plans, and for good reason. The interior design is nothing short of stunning; it never fails to impress my out-of-town guests with its intriguing charm. Although the noise level can notch up upstairs, the overall atmosphere is nothing short of awesome.

The cocktail menu deserves a shoutout, with the Three Piece Suit being a winner in my books every time I order it. Starters here are a delight, especially the fried chicken sliders, which are tantalizing enough to serve as a main course in their own right.

Speaking of mains, the hangar steak flatbread and steak frites are my usual go-tos. The steak is sumptuously flavored and tender for a hangar cut, while the fries never miss the mark - hot and crisp. The accompanying salad is a refreshing sidetrack.

Desserts here are a spectacle, with the flaming sticky toffee pudding stealing the spotlight and invariably ending up on Instagram feeds. Service is generally exemplary, with occasional hiccups when requesting the bill, but that's a minor issue in the grand scheme.

Rag Trader has firmly ousted my previous favorite (sorry, The Smith!) and claimed its spot as a cornerstone of my dining experience. My Amex statements can vouch for that!

During my recent visit to this dining establishment, I opted to try their signature artichoke pizza slice, which I regretfully found underwhelming. The topping was reminiscent of a chunky broccoli and cheese soup rather than a traditional pizza accompaniment, leading to a taste profile that strayed from what I expect from a pizza. Additionally, the slice was overpriced, which added to the disappointment. A smaller, more affordable tasting portion would have been appreciated to gauge my interest before committing to a full slice.

On the positive side, the staff displayed commendable politeness and the restaurant's cleanliness was up to standard. However, should I return, I intend to play it safe with the standard flavors in hopes of a more fulfilling pizza experience.

Title: A Cozy Corner for Lunch Breaks

Nestled just a block away from my office, this charming eatery has become a staple for myself and my colleagues. Its cleanliness and warm ambiance offer a welcoming reprieve from the workday hustle.

Despite the lunchtime rush, the staff remains courteous, ensuring that patrons feel valued without feeling hurried. The lunch specials are a highlight and a frequent choice for me, featuring mouthwatering options like juicy rotisserie chicken, a hearty burger paired with sweet potato fries, and delectable macaroni. Each meal is a testament to the kitchen's consistency, though prices are slightly higher than nearby options.

Portion sizes are generous, justifying the cost and leaving patrons satisfied. Post-work, the place buzzes with professionals unwinding over drinks, making it a vibrant spot for both a midday meal and an evening wind-down.

In summary, this spot is well worth a visit for those seeking quality food and service in a snug and friendly setting.

I love Jose Andres and this is a neat venture.Went on a Sunday. Was a little too crowded to really enjoy the concept. Not a table in sight and it was a little confusing on how to get a seat and/or service.We finally snagged a single seat at the bar (for two of us) and ate standing up after ordering a couple of sandwiches and a pizza.  The sandwiches were very good (though wait to order was long), the pizza was terrible and was donated.I wish I had known how to navigate this before going, as I think I would have enjoyed more.

I recently dined at Han Dynasty and was blown away by the experience, particularly in comparison to their Brooklyn location. The service here is impeccable, a refreshing change that elevated the entire meal. The star of the show was undoubtedly the Dan Dan noodles – a spicy delight that I couldn't get enough of. I could easily devour ten bowls of this perfectly balanced dish. My advice is to visit during off-peak hours to avoid the rush, but even if you do encounter a wait, rest assured, it's worth it. Highly recommended for a standout dining experience.

This pizza is solid. One bite score: 8.4. IT's a bit pricey and the wait can be a bit long if your party is more than 2 people. Wait: We waited about 30 minutes for a table for 3... that never happened. We have to settle for the bar seating. Food: I read in a review to get the pizza well done. They intentionally undercook their pizza because of the volume they make. So ask them to leave it in the oven for a bit longer to make it extra crispy. First couple of slices were total bomb. It definitely got soggy toward the end but still good pizza. I recommend eating it quickly before it gets soggy. Also the sausage pie was definitely more well done than the pepperoni. The pepperoni wasn't very crispy when it came straight out of the oven. Would come back. Good pizza. 5/5. TLDR: 8.4 but get it well done.

Playa bettys was a yelp find. Full disclosure we went for brunch only. They offer bottomless mimosas with OJ or cactus pear. They're a little heavy on the juice but other than that a good deal in NYC. We had the short rib breakfast tacos and a brunch bowl. The food was good, not amazing but still a hearty breakfast to chase mimosas with. Why three stars? The service. It was a busy Sunday and they seemed super under staffed. It took forever to get the mimosas and our waiter would disappear for long periods of time. Would I return when in nyc? Probably not but if you're in the mood for tacos and mimosas, this is your place.

Did my first visit to Coney Island recently. It was quite enjoyable on a Thursday in April, though I doubt I would want to do it on a Saturday in July. After doing the cliche Nathan's hot dog and picture of the Wonder Wheel, we stopped in here to enjoy a cocktail or three and just watch the boardwalk. They've kept mementos of the long history of the space, but it's obviously been kept up to date. The cocktails are fruity and smallish, but at $10 not a bad deal considering the location. The bartender was on top of it and friendly. We didn't eat anything (cheese fries from Nathan's still heavy on the tummy) but really enjoyed the ambience and experience.

Slurp slurp- show me the noods - let's see how many more ramen puns I can add to this review.  With winter temperatures approaching and the wind whipping around the city, leaves you no choice but to find a cozy ramen noodle place and dive into the bowl. I had the Vegetable Ramen with curry base and a large hot sake. Nothing can get you warmer on a windy winter night then hot ramen broth and hot sake- it's the season for hot sake. With winter knocking on your door this place a local take out and sit down simple style restaurant. Small seating area with big flavor and big bowls of Ramen. Veggie Ramen was flavored by the curry broth and soaked up by the noodles. Also tried the fried chicken appetizer, perfectly cooked pieces of chicken- simple dish for the main bowl of noodles.

Had a 9pm reservation for 2 on a Saturday night and it did not disappoint- from the atmosphere to the service, everything was incredible. We were seated downstairs which was intimate, rustic and cozy. The waitress was knowledgeable about the menu and wine (which was perfectly paired with our meal). For our appetizer we ordered the bikini (which was a little panini with ham) and the Brussel sprouts salad.
