We were unsure of what to order for the entree so the waitress recommended we get a full portion of the tagliatelle with Brussels and pancetta (my favorite), half portion of the torchio pasta with sausage (a little spicy kick but it was great) and then the bistecca (incredible skirt steak with truffle oil). The cheesecake was good, but not my favorite since it was warm and not as typically expected.

Title: Convenient and Satisfying - The Hummus and Pita Co.

Located conveniently near our hotel at 40th and Port Authority, The Hummus and Pita Co. is a gem in the bustling heart of Manhattan. Faced with a looming Greyhound trip back to Rochester and a growling stomach, a quick Yelp search led me to this spot for a late-night meal. It did not disappoint.

The ordering process was a breeze, and I was back to my hotel lobby with a steak bowl in hand within 20 minutes. The steak was decent, paired well with their hummus, and the tzatziki added a nice touch. The dolmas, while not homemade, were a tasty side. My travel companion's chicken pita met with silent approval, signaling satisfaction.

Service was a highlight on this dreary Manhattan evening, with the staff being both friendly and informative, adding a bit of warmth to the night's experience.

Overall, The Hummus and Pita Co. offers quick, friendly service, and reasonably priced, satisfying meal options. It's a solid choice for those in need of a fast and fulfilling bite, earning a deserved 4 stars from this traveler.

Located inside the famous Pierre Hotel the restaurant serves up some delicious food. We came for restaurant week and it was a delightful evening. Everything was amazing. The best dishes of the evening was thr Butter Poached Lobster and the Short Ribs. The Short Ribs were so tender that a knife was not needed. The Apple Tart was pretty amazing as well. Perrine always has a prix fixe menu so ita good value for dinner or lunch.

Was excited to check this place out, but it has little new to offer in a city with many great tapas places. Good vibe on the inside with a good wine selection. We ordered the paella as recommended and French fries. The fries were good as most fries are, so if you're looking for a safe option for apps this is for you. The paella was not particularly flavorful. Rather generic and a little bit burnt even. But they give you a lot of it, so it's plenty for two people. We ate most of it despite it being somewhat disappointing. The service was also nothing to rave about, unfortunately.

Finding the perfect thin and crisp slice of pizza in New York City can be an odyssey, fraught with the perils of charred crusts and dough more akin to a cracker. Prince Street Pizza, however, stands as a beacon of hope for pizza aficionados. On separate occasions, I sampled their Sicilian and a regular slice, both of which were nothing short of exemplary.

Brace yourself for the inevitable – the lines can be daunting, and you'll likely be enjoying your slice while standing. But in a city where pizza is synonymous with a quick and satisfying bite, Prince Street is worth the wait. The bustling atmosphere only adds to the authentic experience. If you're in search of that elusive perfect slice, look no further. Prince Street delivers in spades.

3.5 food was above average.  It is located in Chinatown so not hard to find.  It's very beautiful inside and the staff were friendly. We got seated right away.  Their sauce for the seafood boil was pretty good, but I felt that the sauce was only on the outside of the seafood.  Once you get inside, there was really no flavor on the inside of the seafood.  The seafood itself, was kind of bland.  It was cooked perfect, though.  It wasn't overcooked or undercooked.  The crawfish also didn't have any head.

Title: A Line Worth Waiting For: Pizza Perfection Achieved

From the moment I saw the queue stretching out the door, I knew this pizza joint was something special. The tantalizing wait, while daunting at first glance, is an investment that pays off exponentially. Trust me, you'll want to brave it.

The pepperoni slice is a masterpiece—thick, spiced to perfection with a delightful chew and just the right touch of crisp. Pure bliss. Even a simple cheese slice here transcends expectations; the sauce is a sweet revelation, and the cheese? Imagine the freshest, chewiest delight that pulls apart like culinary gold.

I strayed from my usual preference and opted for square slices, a decision that has forever altered my pizza perspective. In summary, this place is a must-visit. Keep patience as your virtue, bring your friends, and indulge in a pizza experience that is truly unforgettable.
Scouted out this spot for a slice following the show at Madison Square garden.  Perfect location, somehow we beat the crowd and grabbed a seat. Good representation of New York Pizza.

I recently dined at this restaurant and was thoroughly impressed with their incredible dry pot, boasting great ingredients and excellent flavor. The udon beef noodles were also a standout dish for me. In addition, they offer fantastic lunch specials that are both delicious and affordable. Highly recommended!

Title: A Disheartening Experience at a Local Ramen Spot

I approached my recent visit to this establishment with enthusiasm, as a self-professed ramen aficionado, but my experience was dismally underwhelming. The service was suspiciously fast, leading me to believe that my meal may have been microwaved, given the dish's inconsistent temperature.

The presentation of the ramen failed to be redeemed by its quality. The chicken, which promised a savory addition, was peculiarly thin, tough, and filled with gristle, rendering it inedible. The broth lacked any depth of flavor, coming off as little more than tepid, slightly meaty water, devoid of the rich seasoning one expects from authentic ramen.

Although the noodles were claimed to be homemade, they missed the mark with their overly thick and unappetizingly doughy texture. Paired with the lackluster broth and the chicken, it was far from the harmonious dish I had hoped for. The baby bok choy, though not offensive on its own, suffered the same fate of being completely unseasoned.

Further disappointment awaited with the bao bun Peking duck that was strangely encased in a fried outer layer, straying far from the traditional steamed buns one might anticipate. The filling, which I presume was duck, was overshadowed by an overabundance of plain white onion, not the advertised leeks, overpowering any other flavors that might have been present.

In sum, my visit was a regrettable fail. This restaurant's interpretations of classic dishes were unrecognizable, and I can only hope for significant improvements in the future.

Title: A Delightful High-End Lunch Topped with Decadent Desserts

I recently dined at a restaurant that, while on the pricier side for a lunch outing, justified every penny with its quality offerings. The star of my meal was undoubtedly the tuna poke bowl, which struck a harmonious balance with its crunch and greens, satisfying without overwhelming the palate.

While the chicken lollipops left something to be desired with their chewy texture, and the steak salad could have benefited from a more generous portion of steak, the other dishes like the mushroom spaghetti and the chicken wrap hit the mark well.

However, the real showstopper was the s'mores dessert – a heavenly concoction of gooey chocolate brownies and slightly toasted marshmallows, complemented by crunchy graham crackers and a perfectly cool scoop of vanilla ice cream. It was an unforgettable treat that completely overshadowed the also tasty cheesecake.

In summary, while not every dish was perfect, the delightful s'mores dessert along with the standout poke bowl made my visit a thoroughly enjoyable experience.

I can't wait to return to this incredible dumpling destination! The delivery from this restaurant was impressively swift, bringing me an array of steamed seafood dumplings, delectably hot and spicy wontons, and perfectly fried pork dumplings right to my door. The portions were generous, offering great value at an affordable price. It's easy to see why this spot could rank among the top 5 dumpling establishments in NYC. Highly recommend for a savory experience!

Good food, but small portions, and no sides come with what you order. We had the salmon and the duck, with a side of brussel sprouts. Everything was tasty, but you won't leave stuffed. Which is good for the waist line I guess. Walked over 20K steps around NYC today, so probably hungrier than normal. Nice staff, cute bar. Dark inside. Not too loud, which is nice.

Omg  the mac & cheese is off the chain 4 stars but they have a serious in house order priority major issue  going on here ......We arrived at 8:05 pm 2/14/19 the place was moderately busy to getting ready to be slammed ....We were a party of four, we sat & my wife made the order took maybe 10 minutes or so using their self serve order system .... Exceeded my expectations for a Chipotle-esque Indian fast-casual joint! I had a strong craving for Indian food and wanted a SPREAD which wouldn't have been possible for under $15pp elsewhere (unless I could convince my carnivorous fiancé to get some vegetarian thali with me). Luckily, this place came recommended by a few of my coworkers, so I decided to give it a try! It was mostly empty for a Friday night at 6pm, since it's moreso for the weekday lunch crowd. The service was friendly and efficient, and the seating area was relatively clean.I ordered two of the "feasts" which came with one main and 4 sides (choice of naan, rice, dal, and salad). I tried both the saag paneer and the chicken tikka masala as my mains and the yellow lentil and classic as my dal choices. We also got an extra order of samosas (3 for $3.40-ish) which made it the perfect serving size for two. All the dishes were very flavorful. By no means was this the *best Indian food ever* but it definitely hit the spot and I was happy I got to have a bunch of different dishes for the price.

Fantastic food, great service, calm ambiance. The quality of the food here is amazing! We got the lobster appetizer, oxtail pot, and mushroom rice. We made a reservation for 8pm on the same day (Wednesday night). They do have a $10 fee if you cancel the reservation, so just beware.The experience was quite fun, having the food being cooked in front of you, and the staff was very attentive (they have timers for the food cooking, so you don't have to do anything except be patient and watch). I'd say that the food was satisfying and great quality, but it was quite expensive for what it was. The lobster chohoe had big pieces of lobster in it, but I personally wasn't too much of a fan of the rest of the salad. The amuse bouche was fine, interesting to an extent but nothing super revolutionary. The oxtail pot was delicious, the broth was savory and the meat tender. My only disappointment was that there seemed to be very few pieces (about 3 for the small pot). I would come back, but not before I visit their sister stores (Her Name is Han, Take 31) first!

Last Saturday, my friends and I had the pleasure of dining at this cozy restaurant. The highlight of my evening was the sea bass, lavishly dressed in glaze garlic sauce, accompanied by perfectly steamed broccoli rabe. Not only was the dish delectable, but the portion was also very generous. The service impressed me, as it was swift, making me feel quite special throughout the meal. The ambiance of the restaurant was just right - bustling yet not overly loud, ideal for a dinner outing or a romantic date. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit to relish another exquisite sea bass. Highly recommended!

If you're in the Bronx around this area, Pelham pkway stop or near the Bronx zoo, you must check out this taco truck. Prices are cheap and worth it, the tacos are amazing and so delicious. You can't pass up a homemade Mexican taco for $2. I personally get the steak taco and chicken taco, they're usually pretty fast, although i have seen a line sometimes, during peak hours.Glad to see they are still open during the pandemic. Support local businesses, they help you and we help them.

I had an extremely disappointing experience at this restaurant. The drinks were weak, and the food was subpar. Additionally, the service was noticeably biased; female patrons received significantly less attention compared to male customers, presumably due to the staff's focus on tip potential. I won't be returning and cannot recommend this establishment.

Unexpected treasure in Hudson Yards! I got lost when I got to this place and went to the actual restaurant, but the real experience is on the bottom floor with the food court. I tried the Pan con Tomate and the Spicy Fried Potatoes. The Pan con Tomate is exactly what it is. Tomato on bread with some salt and oil. It sounds very simple but it was delicious and cheap too! The Spicy Fried Potatoes were pretty expensive and honestly I will try something else next time because they were just okay. My friends also had the churro and ice cream, both of which were hits. I can't wait to come back here and try new things available.

I'm always a bit intimidated by the bustling food scene in our area, and the daunting lines at this establishment had kept me at bay until recently. Seizing the opportunity of a long weekend in February, we arrived at opening and were surprised to find a crowd already gathered. Initially, the packed interior at 11:30 AM seemed overwhelming, but it turned out to be an illusion of slow seating rather than an actual wait.

The ambiance of the restaurant is inviting, and our party of three comfortably settled into a spacious booth. Faced with an extensive menu, we wished for a larger group to sample a wider array of dishes. The meal began with a thoughtful touch—a pot of tea on a heating dish, ensuring a warm sip with every bite. However, a minor hiccup occurred when we had to remind our waiter about the complimentary spicy pickled cabbage, which he had neglected to serve.

Our selection included a shan yao appetizer, mapo tofu, and stew fish filet with chili oil, each dish arriving perfectly executed and bursting with flavors that danced on our palates. Already planning a return visit, the dry chicken has caught my eye for the next culinary exploration. This restaurant is a gem worth braving the crowd for; the food speaks for itself.

This place is a modern take on Korean food and overall the food was delicious. I particularly enjoyed the bone marrow short rib dish as well as the various lettuce wrap items. It's a good place to go if you intend to share food so that the whole table can try out a little bit of everything.

This is a massive operation. These places always fascinate me with how they make all the food and have it ready. They must not like to sleep. We are talking about a lot of food and all of it looks decently fresh. I got a salad where I picked the ingredient in it. This was a full meal and I didn't even finish it. It was also pretty affordable which is great. When I checked out they gave me a card where if I order 4 salads I get the 5th free. Good deal. Anyway, if you need a quick bite and can't decide what to eat you will find something here. This isn't high end food but it does the job.

Title: A Delightful NYC Breakfast and Lunch Gem

I recently revisited this charming little restaurant for the second time, and it was just as fantastic as I remembered. The menu is a delightful mix of fun and creative options, and the portions are generous, ensuring you leave satisfied. I indulged in the "big breakfast," and it was a splendid start to my day. Despite the tight quarters, which are typical for NYC, the atmosphere is cozy and inviting. The service is exceptional, with attentive and friendly staff enhancing the dining experience. I highly recommend this spot for anyone looking for an excellent meal to kickstart their morning or a lovely lunch break in the city.

We came in for a late lunch and it was perfect timing on our part as it does get loud in the restaurant.  Lunch has a $32 Quick Lunch (Monday-Friday) where you choose any Small followed by any Pasta (* $4 supplement). We selected:Small plates1-Dry Aged Beef Carpaccio - egg yolk and truffle shavings 2-Burrata StracciatellaPasta1-Spaghetti Cacio E Pepe2-Rigatoni special with Pork Ragu DessertChocolate lava cake with vanilla ice cream and carmel rice crispy The restaurant definitely had a hip hop vibe but the music wasnt as loud as the others reviewed it in the past.  Staff was patient and attentive. We were  taken care of by our waitress.   All and all it was a great lunch and experience.

The Pisillo sandwich is such a good hearty meaty cheesy veggie filled piece of Italy. From the little spot on a busy NY street down to the worker's smile, you can def see the passion that comes out of this little shop. The sandwich was packed to the brim, very flavorful, and tasted like Italy. The bread was just a tad chewy for me which made it hard for me bite through it but overall still a great sandwich.

Bad bad bad service and mediocre food. When you ask for your drink tall and no fruit and it comes on the rocks with 2 limes and a plate of limes and lemons and the really tall straw doesn't fit the glass. Waiter was constantly not listening and running away before we were able to finish ordering. Caesar salad was good, chicken was dry dry dry, roasted potatoes tasted terrible but mashed potatoes were delicious. Didn't ever properly clean up table. Took way too long to get food, 2 hours for dinner. Was school night & needed to get home. What could have been an average meal turned really really bad. Won't ever go back. Was not my choice of restaurant was my friends.

Down a few steps and through a black door on beautiful West 4th Street in the heart of the West Village you enter Fedora.  You enter another world. This place has character.  The bar that runs along the length of the room takes precedence.  It's a darker space than what you may be used to but luxuriously lit with candles and soft lights.  There's bustle to be sure.  It's a popular spot, but you still feel capable of being alone with the one(s) you're with.  Incredible cocktails.  Extensive wine list.  Delicious bar snacks. One of those deviled eggs is a must, and the shrimp or trout apps will also go nicely with your drinks.  Drinking and eating are both to enjoy here.

I recently enjoyed a delightful dining experience with a friend at this charming restaurant. The dual option of indoor and outdoor seating immediately set a welcoming scene. As a traditionalist, I started with the French onion soup, which was a gooey-cheese dream come true. The main course, a scallop risotto, exceeded all expectations with its perfect preparation. My companion's Mediterranean-inspired salmon over spinach with hummus truly captivated both our palates. We concluded our meal with delicious cookies and well-paired drinks. The value for the quality and quantity of food served was exceptional. I left feeling thoroughly satisfied and am eager to return.

Wife wanted to try this place out today. Went during lunchtime hours, & the place was almost full. We got seated quickly, & given menus. We both went with the original. You get a huge tray filled with 12 different ingredients (that you will add to make your noodle soup), a hot bowl of broth, & a serving of their noodles (i believe all the dishes used the same type of noodle). You are told to add the meat items 1st, & continue till you've added everything in your bowl. Additionally, there are (6) extra toppings you can order at an extra charge. I ordered the pork, & fish balls ($2.99). The way I would describe this place is, that, you're cooking your own food. The noodles, and the broth, by themselves, are bland. After you have everything in the pot, &, let it simmer for awhile, it gets tasty. I would definitely recommend stirring the food, & letting it sit for 10 minutes, before eating. Don't make the mistake i made. This place is open 24/7. Note, the Yelp check-in is no longer valid. Why the restaurant doesn't remove it is beyond me. Also, note, you can get extra noodles at no charge; but broth is $1 more.

Following an exciting day browsing Chinatown's market, my expectations for a hearty family meal were met with disappointment at this local Chinese eatery. Despite our group of nine's ample appetite, the restaurant's service was lackluster at best. Staff members appeared more interested in upselling than accommodating our preferences, insisting on portions and dishes we hadn't agreed to, which was off-putting.

The cuisine itself was a mixed affair. The walnut shrimp and salt and pepper squid (mislabeled on the menu) were standouts, but classics like the Buddha's Delight and various chicken dishes failed to impress, only adding to the lackluster dining experience. Moreover, the absence of eggrolls on the menu was a peculiar omission, and requesting them seemed to baffle the servers, which struck me as an oddity for an establishment of this nature.

Portions sizes also didn't live up to expectations, with "family style" servings falling short compared to what you'd typically receive at other Chinese restaurants. This resulted in us having to order more than anticipated to satisfy our group.

In sum, this restaurant's service and food quality did not live up to the vibrant Chinatown vibe. Given my experience, I cannot endorse this spot for future visits, and should my travels bring me back to NYC, I'll certainly be dining elsewhere.

During NYC Restaurant Week, I had the pleasure of dining at Zavo and my experience was delightful. The ambiance exuded luxury and the customer service was exemplary. The three-course meal, priced at a reasonable $26, offered a generous serving size.

Starting with a large, flavorsome crab cake complete with a complementary sauce and crisp green salad, the appetizer set a high bar. The main course of braised short rib was a highlight; tender, juicy, and irresistible, it left me wishing for a larger portion, particularly when paired with the creamy mashed potatoes which were perfect for savoring the rib’s savory gravy.

Dessert was a journey of contrasts. I ventured out of my comfort zone with the creme brûlée, which impressed with its delicate balance, featuring a thin, crackly top and a creamy interior, offset by fresh fruit – not overly sweet, which I appreciated. Chocolate lovers should note that while the dark chocolate mousse is rich, it may be intense for some. However, the mixed berry trifle was a refreshing finale that I would recommend and look forward to enjoying on my next visit. Zavo is certainly on my list for future dining excursions.

My wife, cousin and I visited The Nugget Spot today (Sunday) around 2:00pm. It was busy. All of the seats and open table spaces were taken. However, we were able to find a nice spot once we ordered our food.My wife and I ordered the Skinny Nugs with Mambo Sauce and Cheese N' Chong with Ranch respectively. My cousin ordered the "Regs" with Smokin' J's BBQ sauce with a side of cajun fries.The first bites of the Cheese N' Chong were delicious, especially with the ranch. I didn't get tired of the flavor. However, the Skinny Nugs got boring after the first nugget. The description of the Skinny Nugs says it is marinated with cajun. I didn't taste any cajun on the nuggets. It tasted plain. The sauce was good though. The "Regs" was good with the BBQ sauce. I think it would have been good without the sauce because it was fried, so it was crunchy on the outside while the meat was juicy on the inside. Lastly, the cajun fries were SO salty. We didn't even finish the fries because it was salty. We actually think they missed the cajun from the Skinny Nugs and put it in the fries on accident lol. Customer service was good! They were very insightful and friendly.

Title: A Touch of Irish Charm in Times Square

I recently visited a charming Irish pub and restaurant nestled in the heart of Times Square, and it did not disappoint. The ambiance was inviting, and the authenticity of the place was palpable from the moment we stepped in.

The food was nothing short of excellent. I opted for the vegetable curry with rice pilaf, a delightful dish that took me on a nostalgic journey back to my childhood. My cousins, visiting from Houston, were equally impressed with their hearty selections of lamb stew and Shepherd's pie, both of which were savory and satisfying.

But the true highlight of our dining experience was our server, Thomas. His service was the epitome of exceptional. Politeness and courteousness were just the baseline of his approach. He truly went that extra mile to ensure our comfort and satisfaction. A testament to his dedication was when I requested an Arnold Palmer, which was not on the menu. Thomas effortlessly agreed to whip one up, serving it up quickly and with a smile.

Overall, the combination of great food and impeccable service made for a delightful dining experience. For anyone looking for a slice of Irish hospitality in the heart of New York City, this pub is a must-visit. A heartfelt thank you to Thomas and the team for a memorable evening!

Snobby vibe fitting.PROS - delicious vegetarian foodCONS - long wait times, cramped seating, pricey for portion, snobby vibe, a menu that would rather be cheeky than clear for customers (shrug emoji), chef*SUPERIORITY BURGER $6Amazing. This burger was inspired by classic Shackburger and it hits. Every note. Sauce. Toppings. Charred patties (bean). Small but satisfyingBURNT BROCCOLI $4Scoop to the bottom for a special creamy surprise. You've never had broccoli like this!MEGAMOUTH $9a bigger version of the regular superiority burgerSLOPPY DAVE $7 ehPRALDON MEARL aka Arnold PalmerNot bad, ask for 90% less ice to not feel gypped -why they chose to jumble up the letters and make it confusing? reread first line of review.WHY I STOPPED GOING*Chef gives samples of gelato to select bystanders (white people). Unfortunately, I've witnessed on multiple occasions. Homage to the Aryan race? The name, menu, chef, vibe and habits certainly make it appear that way. Recommended: Superiority burger, broccoli, iced tea (easy on ice)

Title: A Taco Treat with Room for Improvement

If you're in the mood for affordable and scrumptious tacos, this is a spot to consider. At just $3 each, these tacos come fully loaded and are accompanied by a zesty slice of lime—quite the bargain. The welcoming serving of complimentary salsa and chips is a pleasant way to start your meal.

The taco carnita is a simple yet delectable choice, though the paper plate presentation leaves something to be desired. The flavor is spot on, tempting you for seconds. The enchilada verde with chicken, served with a modest portion of beans and a generous side of rice, was satisfactory but could benefit from a more generous drizzle of green sauce and a bit more heat to elevate its taste. As for the mushroom quesadilla, while it is a decent option, the deep-fried aspect and scant cheese filling make the tacos a more appealing choice.

Drink-wise, the agua de horchata is a sweet treat that complements the meal, but the agua de Jamaica might not be everyone's cup of tea with its unusual cherry and hibiscus blend that could be somewhat off-putting for the uninitiated.

Service is hit or miss. Initially attentive with prompt water and chip service, the staff later mistakenly served us an unordered guacamole and seemed confused when corrected. Additionally, waiting for the check took longer than expected.

Overall, this eatery is recommended for taco enthusiasts, with a note that there's room for improvement in both the broader menu and service.

I recently had the pleasure of sampling a cheese pizza at a New York eatery that left a lasting impression on my taste buds. As a self-proclaimed pizza addict who has tried countless slices in the city, I can confidently say this was the best one yet. The sauce was particularly excellent, enhancing the deliciousness of the cheese in a way I hadn't experienced before. If you're in town and craving pizza, this is a spot you won't want to miss.

Title: A Perfect Post-Wedding Lunch at Ginger and Lemongrass

Review:

I recently celebrated a special post-wedding lunch at Ginger and Lemongrass and it was nothing short of spectacular, thanks to the exceptional service provided by Katerina. Her professional demeanor, coupled with her personal touches - like custom menus and a heartwarming email on my big day - made the experience unforgettable.

Katerina's flexibility shone through as she adeptly adjusted seating arrangements without a hitch, catering to our needs with grace. The staff mirrored her attentiveness, ensuring all guests felt valued and well-cared for throughout our event.

As for the food, it was divine. The pho, enhanced with a generous serving of bone marrow, was a standout for me. The appetizers, particularly the chicken wings and shrimp spring rolls, were crowd-pleasers, and the cocktails complemented the meal beautifully.

Ginger and Lemongrass proves to be an excellent choice for both private events and casual dining. My unequivocal rating would be 5/5 for the fantastic food, service, and overall experience. Highly recommended!

Standard diner. Came here for breakfast with my friend. The pancakes and French toast was solid. I would recommend for a Sunday brunch if you are in the area but nothing more than that. The place is pretty small and not decorated that nicely.

Title: A Cozy New Year's Day Ramen Experience

Despite the holiday bustle, stepping into this ramen spot on New Year's Day was a delight. A group of five, we prepared for a wait but were pleasantly surprised to be seated at the bar in just 15 minutes - a testament to the restaurant's efficiency, even on busy days.

The ordering process was a breeze. The staff accommodated a substitution request swapping pork for chicken with no fuss. We dived into the Minca ramen; the mixed pork and chicken broth was a standout, rich and perfectly balanced, paired with a generous portion of pork. The Spicy basic ramen, though brimming with flavor, could have packed more heat — I'd give it a mild kick, at best.

Noodle texture is key, and here they nailed it — that satisfying chew that ramen aficionados chase. A slight letdown was the tea egg, which, though tasty, was served cold, an unexpected contrast to the warm soup.

The staff deserves a shout-out for managing the small space with grace, ensuring diners felt welcome. Prices were on par for Manhattan, making this a spot I'd readily recommend for anyone craving a solid bowl of ramen.

Title: Cozy Spot for a Quick Ramen Fix

If you're planning to dine at this spot, be sure to hit the ATM first, as it's a cash-only establishment. Amid the numerous choices, I opted for the miso tonkatsu ramen, which proved to be a solid selection. The broth struck a nice balance, being flavorful without the heaviness that sometimes accompanies ramen, although the portion could leave a hearty eater wanting more. 

On a bustling Sunday evening, our party of three was quoted a 5-10 minute wait and, true to their word, we were seated at the bar within that timeframe. While the seating arrangement is functional, the bar area feels underutilized—a tweak here could possibly accommodate more patrons.

In summary, it's a fine choice for anyone looking for a quick ramen bowl but might not be the best fit for larger groups due to the limited space.

This place exudes style and class. From the attentive staff, to the modern art work & decor, as they say first impressions are everything. I am completely impressed. The food & service were 100 percent on point. My fish was presented, and prepared table side, which I found so elegant. The chef came to my table to greet me, and he asked for feedback, I thought that was really amazing. This is a new restaurant in the area, and I feel it will really do well. You can clearly see the passion and attention to detail from all aspects of the dining experience.I recently came back. The food and service was exceptional. I also loved the enhancements to the interior..

Tucked away in the bustling LES/Chinatown area, this budget-friendly Chinese gem serves up some seriously tasty food that won't break the bank. Despite a potential for long lines, my visits on Sunday afternoons only had me waiting a brief 10 minutes. The fast-moving queue is a testament to the efficiency of the place. 

I've indulged in their large BBQ pork and duck combo over rice and veggies on both occasions. The pork was consistently succulent, with just the right amount of fat. The duck, however, was hit-or-miss, with more bone than meat; it's definitely a gamble. 

While there may be spots with higher quality cuts nearby, the value here is unbeatable. Remember to bring cash, and don't count on sitting down—there's no seating available. If you're after great flavors at a low cost, this is your spot.

Absolutely love the burgers from Bareburger. But their impossible burgers are impossibly the best!  I like them more than their beef burgers and trust me you all will! We also got their beer cocktails which were really good! Went perfectly with the burgers and fries. We ordered for the Michelada and Cerveza. The Michelada was strong and well made!  We got the Be My Burger (build your own) impossible burger with brioche bun, avocado, caramelized onions, mushrooms, gouda and chipotle mayo and a side of thickly cut fries

Title: A Gem in Tribeca – Italian Cuisine at Its Finest

I recently dined at what is now one of my top Italian restaurants, nestled in the vibrant heart of Tribeca. The locale offers a delightful urban experience with both indoor and outdoor seating, the latter boasting views of the Freedom Tower. Upon arrival, the attentive host welcomed us without delay, allowing us the luxury of choosing our table in the uncrowded space—though I would advise booking in advance.

The appetizers set a high bar; each selection tantalized the taste buds, with the eggplant dish being a standout. The highlight of the evening was the famous TableSide Truffle Pasta—an absolute must-try that justifies its fame with every forkful. No meal here is complete without indulging in their Creme Brûlée, a flawless finale to a sumptuous dining experience.

With fair pricing for the high-quality fare and an impressive wine list, this establishment delivers on all fronts. The ambiance and service are impeccable, both scoring a perfect 10/10. Parking is limited to the street, which is a small price to pay for such an exceptional meal. This restaurant is a must-visit for any Italian cuisine aficionado.

I checked out the Urbanspace food hall on 52nd and LoLo's chicken sounded like a good healthy lunch. I got the 1/4 roasted chicken with pineapple chutney salsa on quinoa and farro. Everything was seasoned well and tasted fresh. The chilled broccoli side had more flavor than I expected. The chicken was moist and I like the slight spicy kick of the chutney. Not the best roasted chicken I've had but a solid choice for a healthy meal.

To my knowledge, this was my first time experiencing Uruguayan cuisine. Charrua has a nice look and feel to it, with lots of wood and warm tones. Old Uruguayan advertisements and articles adorn the walls. We made a reservation for 7pm on a Friday night but wouldn't have needed it; the place was about half full during most of our time there.The restaurant was out of the first wine we ordered but we ended up with a really nice Uruguayan Tannat (2017) from Traversa. It was a bit acidic but well-balanced, with red fruit and earthy vegetal flavors. Wasn't too tannic although that's certainly the grape's reputation. We started off with a complimentary order of bread with a really nice olive oil dipping sauce infused with delicious flavors from mushrooms and other veggies, which themselves were actually included with the oil. Next up was an appetizer of empanadas (one corn, one beef). I only had the corn one, as I don't eat beef. The dough itself was very well executed: light and crispy, rather than heavy and oily. I did think, though, that the corn filling was too salty and tasted canned. As for entrees: he ordered the fettuccine a la Caruso, which had ham, mushrooms, cream, and Parmesan. I had a bite and thought the fettuccine was cooked well and the mushrooms were very nice.I wanted to try one of the famed chivitas (sandwiches) and opted for the el choripan, which has chorizo sausage, lettuce, tomato, and chimichurri. It was a pretty good sandwich overall: had a soft bun and well-cooked sausage, and the chimichurri was obviously made with a quality olive oil, but it did spill out over the bun and made the whole process rather messy. The sandwich also might have included a few more ingredients to make it a bit more interesting. And finally, the flan was unexceptional but free with the Yelp check-in!I vacillated on this one because I thought it was a solid 3.5. Ultimately I went with a 4 because of the quality of the food/wine and because I was glad to have a chance to sample Uruguayan cuisine.
Great service and menu. The spaghetti and steak was top notch and tasted freshly made. The wine selection is expansive and the dessert menu has great options.

Title: Upscale Korean BBQ Delight - A Cut Above!

Upon entering this high-end establishment, I immediately noticed the contrast with the popular Kang Hodong. The ambiance here is decidedly more upscale, catering to a clientele of well-dressed business professionals. It's clear that this isn’t your average all-you-can-eat joint.

Our choice, the beef set #2 priced at $110, was a carnivore’s dream. The star of the show was the wagyu beef, tender and full-flavored, an expected delight as the cut of the day. Accompanied by brisket, aged rib eye, and fresh cut galbi, it was a robust showcase of quality meats. 

The banchan selection, albeit modest, was enjoyable, featuring kimchi and a particularly tasty potato salad, along with broccoli and onions. However, it was disappointing that the set didn't include rice, a staple I had looked forward to.

The dipping sauces did not disappoint, reminiscent of those at Kang Hodong, especially the zesty one with jalapeño and onions. A mention must be made of the sesame oil and orange Korean salt provided for seasoning - a perfect touch, although belatedly presented.

A slight hiccup occurred when our beers arrived late due to a machine issue, but it was a minor blip in an otherwise delightful meal. 

While I appreciated the quality and atmosphere, I couldn't help but wish the set was a little more comprehensive, perhaps including a few more sides or accompaniments.

Overall, the experience was a hit with my family, and it’s a place we'd recommend for those looking for a more refined Korean BBQ outing.

Food is solid here but pretty expensive. It's $9 a lb and the check in offer does not work. I wanted the 10% off and I spent $18 on lunch here. The fries chicken was good. I really like the avocado salad. They added a lot of oil and cilantro onions. They have a good variety but no oxtails. The cooks are in the back and this place is buffet style. You pay in the front. Rice and beans are good here and I think this place is Korean owned. I see a Korean lady running this place. Wish they would honor the check in offer though.

My recent visit to Uncle Boon's, post their Michelin star acquisition, was nothing short of spectacular. Amidst the sea of Thai restaurants, Uncle Boon's stands out with its impeccable dish execution. To secure a spot without the wait, I recommend arriving 15-30 minutes before opening. The highlight was their green curry, a contender for the best dish I've tasted this year. Pair it with their roti and sticky rice for an unforgettable culinary experience. It's an absolute must when you visit.

This is an excellent new ramen spot in the sad area of Murray Hill that doesn't have a huge number of great options.Try the tonkotsu with kogashi garlic ($16) for sure, and get a few skewers for a very satisfying meal. The Spicy Tomato Ramen ($17) is also delicious and a more unique and fun option if you want something other than tonkotsu.

I ordered a quick dinner here before catching a show. It's in a prime location and central to the theater district. The host was able to take a custom order from me which was a filet of sole with shrimp scampi and steak fries. The fish was seasoned fairly well and I was happy that the shrimp were jumbo sized! My meal was pretty tasty and total came up to about $40 bucks. The lentil soup certainly hit the spot. I was surprised at how good it was! I also had a slice of tiramisu cake which was scrumptious! I've eaten here on numerous occasions for breakfast or lunch but had never done dinner. Now it's nothing fancy but a good choice if you don't desire bodega or deli food in the area. Would recommend.

Tucked away in an unassuming nook, this gem of a restaurant boasts a tiny kitchen that punches well above its weight. With a limited menu, it's clear that quality trumps quantity, as each dish is nothing short of divine. The burger is an absolute standout and not to be missed. And for a sweet finale, the ever-changing selection of gelato and sorbet flavors offers a delightful surprise with every visit. This place has earned a spot on my go-to list for consistently delicious eats.

Last night after work, around 5:30 PM, I swung by Westville for a pick-up order I placed via Grubhub. Opting for their family meal for four, I was pleased with the variety - selecting grilled chicken, chicken cutlet, an upgraded salmon option for a small fee, and a medley of vegetables including broccoli, brussels sprouts, cauliflower, and mushrooms. This hearty offering came with a side of rice and a complimentary mac and cheese that didn't disappoint.

Westville is my go-to for a healthy yet satisfying meal; their market plate is a dream for those who adore their greens. Having visited their East and Hudson locations, I can attest to the consistent quality across the board. For anyone in the financial district looking for well-portioned, nutritious meals, Westville is a must-try.

Overview: 4/5 This was my first time to this Italian restaurant in NYC. It was a great choice for its proximity to the Broadway theaters. The prices were reasonable prices for New York. Ambiance : 4/5This had an old Italy feel to the place They as with ever other restaurant in NY pack them in with 2 and mostly 4 seat tables. Not the best place for large groups. I would highly recommend reservations on weekends and during typical dinner hours (6:30 - 9:00pm)Food/Drink  4/5They had a large wine selection you can order by the glass or bottle. I had a Super Tuscan that was delicious!! We ordered a Kobe meatball appetizer that was OK..I started with mozzarella and tomato salad that was good. I went with my old favorite Chicken Parmigiana. The sauce was a little sweet for my taste and I wished I had a choice of pasta. I'm not a big fan of spaghetti. I finished with a Chocolate Lava cake with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. The dessert was good however no chocolate lava flowed from the center. A tad disappointing.Service : 4/5The waitress was attentive. They were accommodating and sensitive to the needs of a member of our party who has Parkinson's and uses a walker. And they didn't try to rush us out even though the restaurant was packed and folks waiting to be seated.Conclusion :A solid four all around so I would give it a go again if I was in the area. Very, very convenient as a dinner option before or after a show.

Love this place! Have been here a couple times for work lunches or after work Happy Hours with my co-workers. Great atmosphere and great food! The place is set up beautifully and I love the window ceiling in the center. Their wings are my go-to!I took a couple friends here when they visited the city and they really liked the place. They have life size games like UNO so we got to play during dinner. My friends still remember this place

Title: Charming Ambiance at [Restaurant Name], Food Hit-or-Miss

Upon entering [Restaurant Name], I was immediately taken by its enchanting decor and the abundance of natural light, making for a truly inviting atmosphere. The menu was brimming with innovative options, leading us to sample dishes like Dahi paneer, spaghetti squash kofta, mango cod, and lasooni chicken—the latter of which stood out as my personal favorite with its rich flavors.

Despite the creative twist on traditional cuisine, not all the dishes hit the mark for me in terms of taste. We encountered an issue with the kofta being excessively salty, but the restaurant staff was commendable in swiftly rectifying the problem and compensated for the mishap with complimentary chai, a gesture I appreciated.

The culinary miss hasn't dampened my curiosity, though. With my South Indian roots calling, I'm eager to return and explore more of their menu, particularly the Kerala fried chicken and other tantalizing brunch offerings. There's clearly potential in their kitchen, and I'm hopeful that my next visit will be as delightful to the palate as it is to the eyes.

Title: A Mixed Bag at SenYa During Restaurant Week

As a self-confessed food enthusiast, the annual Restaurant Week never fails to ignite my culinary excitement, akin to a gastronomic Christmas. SenYa was this year's choice, a venture motivated by a diverse menu promising bold flavors.

Starting strong, the grilled octopus on my plate was tender, the miso glaze executed to perfection, but the promised kick of gochujang was conspicuously absent. However, this slight letdown was eclipsed by my tablemate's beef tartare—a standout dish with its tender beef harmoniously paired with smoky bone marrow and a savory miso mayo. My octopus paled in comparison.

The main course heightened my dinner envy; the Uni risotto with truffle I had so eagerly anticipated was a disappointment. Lacking the robust sea urchin flavor one expects from Hokkaido's renowned seafood, the dish was mediocre, saved only by the genuine truffle shavings which thankfully bore no resemblance to artificial truffle flavorings. Meanwhile, the chirashi beside me was not only a feast for the eyes but also for the palate, its fresh, succulent fish leaving a lasting impression.

Desserts, unfortunately, did not rise to the occasion. My matcha cheesecake was a dry misstep far from the creamy decadence desired, the red bean ice cream its only saving grace. Across the table, the water cake was more style than substance, relying on maple syrup for flavor.

A special nod to the hot tea, which, with its endless hot water refills, felt like both a bargain and a comforting endnote to the evening.

In summary, SenYa offered a Restaurant Week experience that was a rollercoaster of highs and lows. The meal had bright spots with certain dishes shining through, while others left me craving more in terms of flavor and execution. Nonetheless, SenYa provided a worthwhile excursion into diverse culinary territories.

There are some things I truly love about this place.It happens to be one of the larger places to eat on the block, its light, its a fresh idea and the food has always been very good.I love when they have their butternut squash pocket. Unfortunately I was not a fan of the rice-ball, but I realized that's not really my thing.I appreciate their style in the sense that the menu is always different, but sometimes when you are craving those specific flavors- it's nice to go back to one you remember. I only tend to come in when my favorite one is on the menu.I also wish they were open later- in a hip neighborhood like this and with the easy travel capabilities of this dish, it makes sense it it was a late night meal but alas, you have to wait until tomorrow. 4/5

Title: A Cozy Evening at Saar with Hits and Misses

Upon entering Saar, the ambiance immediately struck us with its fresh and welcoming interiors, complete with eye-catching wallpaper that set a casual tone for our meal. The service matched the environment, as the warm and friendly staff had us seated quickly without the need for a reservation.

Kicking off our culinary experience, the pani puri was a delightful burst of tangy sweetness, paired with a satisfying crunch. The baingan bharta, served with roti chips, was a delicious triumph of flavors—certainly a must-try.

Moving on to the main courses, the paneer lababdar presented a dichotomy with its incredible gravy overshadowing the less-impressive paneer, which lacked the desired softness and had an unappealing store-bought texture. The dal makhni, creamy to the touch, unfortunately fell short in flavor and left us wanting more from this classic dish. However, the breads did not disappoint; the garlic naan was flavorful, and the laccha paratha boasted a delightful crispiness, though the former stole the show for me.

In summary, our Friday night at Saar was pleasant, with a few standout dishes. While there were inconsistencies in the meal, there's potential for a better culinary experience, setting the scene for future visits to explore more of what Saar has to offer.

Title: A Lobster Lover's Dream at Cousins

From the moment we walked into Cousins, we were warmly greeted by Fab, an employee whose knowledge of the company's history and offerings significantly enhanced our visit. His exceptional service made us feel incredibly welcome.

We indulged in a seafood feast starting with a creamy Lobster Bisque, followed by perfectly prepared Lobster Tail & Tots, a flavorful Lobster Taco, and finally, a divine Warm Lobster Roll. Each dish showcased the freshness and culinary expertise Cousins takes pride in.

To sweeten the experience, Fab surprised us with a complimentary sample of their famous Woopie Pie. It was a sinful delight that rounded off the meal beautifully.

Cousins has etched a place in my heart with the best Lobster I've ever had. It's a five-star experience through and through. Highly recommended for anyone seeking outstanding seafood and service.

Came here for my birthday brunch and loved it! The space is great if you're not looking for a rowdy brunch.The hummus and radishes was a great starter! The radishes added a great crunch to the dish. The tater tots were super crispy and the shaved Brussels were refreshing. Brunch dishes were pretty unique ranging from the crispy oyster omelette, baked eggs with mushroom, date pizza, and breakfast hash.

I had dinner at Sangria 46 yesterday. Luckily we were seated right away. My friends and I were very excited for the top us. We love going to a tapas place near where we live. Read me Aileen you will be wanted and were able to order within a few minutes of being seated. Our food also came out very quickly and since we had ordered several tapas it was very hard to fit everything on that table. We had ordered Patatas Bravas which usually comes with a spicy sauce on it. In this restaurant though, they only put the spices and give you a mayonnaise to dip them in. However, the dates wrapped in bacon were amazing and better than ones I have had and other restaurants. We ordered ribs as well and they were OK. I had gotten the white sangria to drink and it was delicious. I was very happy with the efficiency of this restaurant. I would go again but maybe not order the Patatas Bravas.

If I have to name my Top 3 Restaurants in New York City, Don Angie would easily be in that list. Hands down one of the best and most enjoyable dining experience of my life! To start with, this restaurant already holds a special place in our hearts because this is where we held our small post City hall wedding celebration last year and I fondly remember how they made us feel special and gave us that corner table on the right side, upon entering the restaurant. We had the most wonderful meal as we toasted to our newly married bliss. Since then, we were captivated and vowed to come back as often as possible. Coming back however proved to be quite a challenge because they were always full and it was so hard to get a reservation. On our wedding anniversary, we tried to come back but couldn't get a reservation. Fast forward to 3 weeks ago, and just after finishing watching Tootsie on Broadway, I got an alert from Resy that there was an available table and so we immediately grabbed it.It turned out to be the wedding anniversary celebration that we initially hoped for and more. Damien warmly welcomed us and upon finding out from us that we were there for our wedding celebration last year, he personally made sure that we were really taken care of. He asked Kyle to personally look after us and our table and the rest of the evening went by perfectly. We initially were dreaming about their lasagna but we felt celebratory so we indulged in ordering more and trying their other dishes which were all honestly incredible. My husband especially loved the Stuffed Garlic Flatbread and with all those melted cheese, it was a thinner pizza. Delicious! I got to try the prosciutto with melon and wow, what a revelation. We of course ordered the lasagna (and ended up taking this home instead) as we were distracted by the two other pasta dishes which were scene stealers in a way: the Sopresinni with Smoked Mussels and the Buffalo Milk Caramelle. These two dishes were so unbelievably mouthwatering good! All of these paired perfectly with their prosecco too! And lastly, even if we were full, we just couldn't pass up on the dessert we had in mind because, we wanted to bring back the memory of our wedding night, so we had the Honey Zeppole which was made of Sicilian Pistachio and Whipped Robiola. So divine!!I will let the rest of my pictures tell the story. Anyone who appreciates incredible food and fantastic service deserves to experience all that this place has to offer. One for the books! Thanks again Damien and Kyle for taking such great care of us, it was absolutely worth the wait!

Title: A Delightful Kosher Vegetarian Dim Sum Experience

My colleagues and I have frequented this gem for its kosher vegetarian dim sum and continue to be impressed. Arriving between noon and 12:30 pm, we've consistently enjoyed a serene dining atmosphere, unbothered by crowds.

This place sets itself apart by forgoing the traditional dim sum cart service. Instead, a paper menu is provided for you to select your preferred treats. Among the must-try items, the vegetarian beef noodle roll and the innovative vegetarian jellyfish are standout choices. Their congee, particularly the house special and twin mushroom versions, exudes comforting flavors, while the vegetarian shark fin dumplings are intricately crafted to please the palate.

Take note to ask for soy sauce and hot chili oil, as these essential condiments aren't automatically placed on the table. Patience is key here since all dim sum items are steamed or cooked upon order, assuring freshness but requiring a wait.

Beyond the succinct dim sum menu, the restaurant also offers enticing lunch specials for entree dishes – something I am eager to return and experience.

In summary, for a unique and satisfying kosher vegetarian dim sum outing, this establishment is a choice that won't disappoint.

Title: A Delightful Surprise in the City

Last night, my colleagues and I found ourselves hungry in the city after a day of training. Thanks to Yelp, we stumbled upon this gem of a restaurant. Despite walking in without a reservation and facing a daunting hour-long wait, fortune favored us with a last-minute cancellation, allowing us to be seated in a mere 10 minutes.

The charming Irish hostess greeted us warmly, and upon learning of my upcoming trip to Ireland, she eagerly provided a personalized list of must-visit eateries and pubs in her homeland—what an incredibly thoughtful gesture!

Our server, Nick, was the highlight of the evening. His blend of sass and humor, coupled with his attentive service, made our dining experience delightful. His dream of making it big in NYC seemed as promising as his ability to ensure patrons have a fantastic time.

The meal itself was excellent. Each dish we ordered was a hit, leaving us all satisfied and impressed. It's not every day that a dining experience checks all the boxes of great service, food, and atmosphere, but this restaurant managed it with ease. My colleagues and I left with full stomachs and high spirits, already looking forward to our next visit.

Title: Novelty Over Nourishment at Zauo

My recent visit to Zauo was a mixed bag. The novelty of catching our own dinner seemed promising for our group of 10, especially for a unique dining experience with friends from out of town. The concept isn't new—reminiscent of Chinese eateries in NYC or traditional spots in Asia—but it certainly added a fun twist to the evening.

Equipped with fishing licenses (we were given three for the group), we embarked on our piscatorial adventure. We hauled in a Salmon, Rainbow Trout, and a Sea Bass, which could be prepared in a variety of ways; from seared to shabu shabu.

Appetizers were the real catch of the day. The hand rolls were delectable, and both the wasabi and fried octopus tantalized our taste buds. The miso sea bass and tempura stood out among the main courses. We even tried the Salmon Sashimi, which, while a gray area due to restaurant policy, was enjoyable.

However, not all was smooth sailing. The seared Salmon was disappointingly tough, and the soy sauce broth variant managed to be both fishy and gritty. Unfortunately, most dishes were underwhelming, with certain cooking styles not complementing the fish.

If you're after a lighthearted activity, Zauo might be worth a visit, but for those whose priority is the culinary experience, it might be best to drop anchor elsewhere.

Located on the 2nd floor, this appears to be solid spot that only locals come (or Yelpers who wander out of the way would find), as this is definitely away from the usual tourist paths. I only know this from visiting family. As such, expect to hear a lot of Cantonese Chinese--on Saturday you'll see families with their elderly--or simply elderly folks--coming here. Definitely very noisy. The big round banquet tables-- if you are so seated at them are shared, unless you have a large enough party (10 persons).Having said that, the dimsum is really good and the pricing (even though it is higher on weekend), still excellent value. Don't be daunted by the language--carts roll around and ppl walk about with trays to visually hawk the foods. Don't kno? Just ask them to pop the bamboos steamer cover to see what's inside. Point-and-order. They will mark the dish as middle/large/special, or small (I don't recall ever ordering any item as small). There's also a per-person tea charge.Only gripe I had was that they did not have chrysanthemum leaves for tea. Say WHAT? That's the first time I hear a dim-sum style restaurant NOT have that....anyways, if I ignore that, it is decently a 4.Bathrooms--used the men..this is high traffic area so it's decent....They have sensing auto faucet and auto air dryer.

Title: A Taiwanese Delight Not to Be Missed

After reading a glowing New York Times article, my anticipation for this Taiwanese gem was sky-high. Convincing my husband to venture downtown for a noodle rendezvous proved to be a highlight of our winter. Our expectations were not just met; they were exceeded. The meal commenced with an order of tofu that can only be described as sublime, followed by a rice bowl that was so deeply satisfying, I find myself yearning for it at this very moment. The Taiwanese noodles were the star of the show, confirming that this place is the real deal. We've already planned our return for the next chilly evening, eager to relive the warmth and delight of this culinary oasis.

Finally made it to this infamous restaurant. I'd always heard it is delicious, especially the burger. I think overall it was very very good. The atmosphere of this place is the star really, a cozy home-style vibe that is impossible not to love. I really did enjoy my burger (medium rare cooked to perfection)... but everyone else at my table found there burgers to be dry. The fries were also divisive... more of crunchy potato shoe strings than fries, good taste but not easy to eat. Wine was great, careful they don't charge for water (they pull the classic "sparkling or still?" with no mention of tap). Deviled egg was good as well, nothing special really. All in all... I think I'd recommend this place as a solid choice, but I won't go again myself. (P.s. I only realized after we ate and I was researching at home that while the owner stepped down from management duties, he still remains the owner. This dropped an extra star for me, and I definitely won't be back. Google it!)

Highly recommend Makana BBQ & Poke! We had takeout and it was delicious. We had the short rib bbq and a noodle special. Their takeout was well-packaged, the food was really fresh and good portions too! Can't wait to try more on the menu.

Came here for dinner on a double date on a Tuesday night and wow it was busy! Still the service was great and nothing was delayed or messed up. And it wasn't loud so we could hear ourselves and have a decent conversation.Appetizers, we had the beets and bucheron cheese and both were really good. For Main we had the filet Don Ameche and porter house And both good choices. Also grilled octopus (we always order grilled octopus every place we see it on the menu) and all of it was really good. For sides I would recommend the carrots. the sauce it comes in in so good that I was using it as a dipping sauce.It'a a classy dim lit place.

Perfect for a cold night.  Came on a rainy day. The restaurant is a retro early Vietnamese eatery of my younger years. Although if you're more into newer and fancier places, this place might might not be for you. If you're looking for some yummy pho, this is the place! Will have to come back to try some of their other items.

Came here with my friends. We had a reservation which I recommend making especially if you go on a Friday night or weekend. The bbq here is absolutely delicious and their cocktails are really interesting and fun! Great place for groups and/or for dates.

Tucked away without prominent signage, this gem proves to be a sanctuary for Udon lovers, particularly as the chill sets in. The interior, minimalistic yet chic, offers a warm embrace with its cozy atmosphere and limited seating—a mere 12 tables accompanied by stool space near the entrance. Do yourself a favor and utilize their Yelp waitlist to secure your spot.

My hearty bowl of Sansai Udon, complemented by a side of scrumptious shrimp tempura, was a triumph of taste and texture. Each spoonful revealed the undeniable freshness of the ingredients and the depth of the savory broth, making it a fulfilling answer to my cold-weather soup yearnings. The noodles, testament to their authenticity, had me struggling to finish the generous portion.

At $19 total before tip—$13 for the Udon and an extra $6 for the tempura—value met quality head-on. Note that it's a cash-only establishment, although an ATM inside provides convenience. A visit here is a must for anyone craving a noodle fix that feels both gourmet and homely.

Visited Turnstyle for the first time last Thursday and was immediately drawn to their healthy yet appealing food options. Opted for the Spicy Salmon Poke Bowl and shrimp & mushroom shumai - both ready in a mere 5 minutes. The staff's friendly demeanor added to the positive experience.

The reheating tip for the shumai was spot-on, preserving its moisture and highlighting the abundance of shrimp - a real bang for the buck. The poke bowl was a delightful experience; the salmon was remarkably fresh and, despite my high spice tolerance, had just the right kick. The serving size, especially the rice, was more than satisfactory.

I'm eager to return to Turnstyle to explore more of their healthy offerings. Highly recommend for a quick, tasty, and friendly experience.

I think this place deserves a solid 3.5 star (rounded up to 4). We ordered sizzling monekybread with a scoop of coconut ice cream and flakes on the top, drizzled with thai ice tea cream. The desert was def on the sweeter side for me. There's nothing critically wrong with the dessert, it just kinda lacks creativity and imagination. Also the melted ice cream makes the break soggy so I thought I would had enjoyed it more if the ice cream was served on the side...The service was quick and our server was nice.

Another score in the basement at Hudson Yards. This is a great experience and good for practicing my Spanish which I need help with! The colorful decor is so cheerful as well as the wonderful Spanish music playing through the speakers. Everything about Mercado is authentic and makes me want to book a trip to Barcelona and Madrid!

Been here a couple times to visit friends in the neighborhood. Great, convenient location. Items that I've tried on the menu are pretty good quality. Bronte burger and the shrimp spaghetti are good. (I prefer the spaghetti.) The sauce on the sweet potato fries is amazing! Crispy rice was more bland than I expected and almost hurt my tooth chewing! Prices are bit expensive, considering the food quality. However, service was great. Went on a Sunday afternoon and there was no wait!

Title: A Delightful Brunch at a Top-Notch Dim Sum Haven

I recently visited a dim sum restaurant that came highly recommended by my best friend's parents, and it did not disappoint. In fact, some of my friends mentioned it surpassed even the famed offerings of San Francisco.

On a bustling Saturday mid-brunch, we navigated the check-in process by the elevators, snagged a ticket, and joined the communal seating to dive into the feast more quickly. The two-floor setup was spacious, with two dining rooms accommodating the eager crowds.

The dining experience was traditional, with roaming carts bearing plates of tantalizing options. Not only did the carts feature helpful photos for easy selection, but the staff, albeit with limited English, managed to assist us effectively, especially the manager who used Google Translate to clarify some items.

Although there's a compulsory $1 charge for tea regardless of consumption, the restaurant compensates with delightful touches like a chili sauce and hot mustard combo served as a dipping dish—diligently replenished when needed.

We indulged in a variety of dishes, with the Steamed Roast Pork Bun and Pork Siu Mai winning our hearts. Surprisingly, the non-traditional Deep Fried Bacon Rolls with their Pringles and mayo dip became an unexpected favorite. Moreover, the custard-filled pigs were not only delicious but incredibly photogenic.

The staff’s warmth and attentiveness, from refilling water to clearing plates, made the meal all the more enjoyable, never once feeling rushed.

Every bite was a pleasure, ensuring that I will eagerly return to this dim sum gem.

Title: A Symphony of Flavor at Le Coucou

I've just experienced what can only be described as the ultimate lunch indulgence at Le Coucou. With a two-course fixed price menu at $58, I was introduced to a world of refined flavors and innovative dishes. The starters alone, with options like fresh oysters and a delectable warm pike quenelle in champagne sauce with caviar, set the stage for an extraordinary meal. The latter was a standout, possibly the best appetizer I've ever savored.

But the true star at Le Coucou? The sauces. Each dish is graced with a sauce that is nothing short of a masterstroke, boasting subtlety and a nuanced depth that elevates the food to new heights. The saucier here is undoubtedly a culinary virtuoso.

The main course offerings were a parade of sophistication, featuring dishes such as halibut with fermented daikon and an impeccably cooked filet mignonette. My group and I partook in a shared feast, and each dish sang with perfection. The flavors were rich and complex without being overpowering—just pure, unadulterated perfection.

Desserts like an assortment of sorbets and a sumptuous rum baba provided a sweet epilogue to the meal, paired with smooth and hot coffee. The service, from the welcoming hostess to our attentive waiter Nash and the knowledgeable sommelier, matched the caliber of the cuisine—flawless.

To note, dinner shifts to an à la carte format with an extensive wine list where good reds span from $155 to a luxe $4,950. If you're searching for a dining experience that is both gastronomically exciting and impeccably served, Le Coucou is a must-visit.

Title: A Ramen Revelation and more

I recently visited this gem of a spot with fellow food enthusiasts, and I was absolutely taken by the culinary experiences offered. Building my own Ramen bowl was a delight; I opted for carrot noodles in a miso broth, accompanied by tofu, corn, bean sprouts, seaweed, and a perfectly seasoned egg. Even as a typical non-tofu eater, I found the tofu exceptionally savory.

The mango gelato stood out among the varieties I sampled – its creamy texture was a dream, dissolving effortlessly on the tongue. The passion fruit bubble tea was equally impressive, striking the perfect balance of sweet and tart.

The staff's warm hospitality rounded out a truly enjoyable dining adventure. I'll certainly be coming back for more!

When you first walk in you are surrounded by hundreds of red decorative lights that just make the place feel like your in a video, honestly really cool. The food is good, my only issue was there cheese Nan bread that was a disappointment because it's naan bread with American processed cheese, so stick to the regular naan. The meal I had consisted of chicken with curry and brown rice which was very good. I will advise go early because the line forms outside and it can be a wait. Definitely would tell anyone for a unique experience come here, also they only take cash, do not come with cards.

Title: Authentic Regional Cuisine in the Heart of New York

As a native of the region that inspires the menu at this charming spot, I was delighted to discover that their rice noodles and pepper chicken dish rivaled the authenticity of back home. This cozy, modern eatery offers a slice of my homeland right here in New York, serving up delicious food at a reasonable price. With good service to boot, it's an excellent choice for anyone in search of a fast-casual dining experience that doesn't skimp on genuine flavor. Highly recommended for a taste of true regional cuisine.

I came here with my team tonight and had a fantastic evening. But most of the time... it's about who you're with that makes or breaks the experience, not necessarily the venue. The space is beautiful - lots of paintings and decor that truly make it feel Victorian, and we had great service throughout, even though it was pretty busy most of the evening. Lillie's has the location, space, the decor... the foundations of what COULD become a great bar. However, our experience tonight was average at best. Here's why:- As soon as we arrived, they didn't have our reservation in their books even when we exchanged previous communications with the manager. Thankfully, they seated us pretty quickly.- The drinks were hit or miss. The Standard had 0 alcohol and the Lavender Lady had way too much lavender (you literally taste lavender seeds with every sip). They also had so many drinks that were unavailable, even though they were on the menu. - The food? Also hit or miss. For bar food, it was pretty decent but the pretzels were kind of stale and bland. The parmesan fries were on point. Overall, this place is not terrible if you happen to be in the area, but Lillie's is unfortunately not somewhere I would seek out or become a regular at. It's worth a one-time visit just to check out the space. Otherwise, I would explore other bars in the area.

Title: A Culinary Gem: Ai Fiori

Review:
Ai Fiori stands out as my top pick among Michael White's impressive lineup of culinary establishments. While the offerings at Marea might edge out in terms of taste, it's the charm and echoes of L'Impero—a nod to my initial love affair with White’s cuisine—that make Ai Fiori special. The service here is nothing short of impeccable, ensuring every dining experience feels personal and attentive. The pasta dishes are the real stars, demonstrating a mastery of flavor and texture that is hard to surpass. Ai Fiori is more than just a fine dining venue; it’s a versatile treasure that fits seamlessly into any dining occasion, be it a celebratory evening or a casual Tuesday dinner. It's not just a restaurant—it's a consistent delight.

I had a bit of an all-out weekend when my parents were in town. They babysat for free so that meant, hurry up and get resos at places I've wanted to try for quite some time. I was able to score last minute spots at both Llama San and Rezdora, two of the more popular spots in NYC at the moment. One disappointed the other was a standout. Obviously, the restaurants could not be any more different, but I thought Llama San did not match the hype for the price. First the good: 1) we thought the service was very fast, attentive, and in general, very helpful. 2) none of the dishes were outright bad, but I wanted more- either texturally, or flavor profile wise. The negatives: 1) the cocktails were not much to write home about. The latter two drinks we had were in plastic cups- just weird. 2) the scallop ceviche's sauce was so overpowering that I missed the natural sweetness of scallops (could not taste it at all), the hamachi ceviche just tasted a bit one-noted, the duck nigiri- while complex- again I missed the duck, the tofu/shrimp/potato dish had too similar of a flavor profile across the board where it just tasted like mush, the lobster and beef heart was a decent spin on surf and turf but nothing crazy, and the most boring dish of the night the wagyu short rib was the best one but the pieces were too chewy with the edges too charred for my taste. 3) the prices may seem ok but each dish is so small, you end up spending quite a bit. At this total price point, you could go to a more established Michelin-starred restaurant. 4) the downstairs bathroom was downright gross- very dirty which was very off-putting. Had this have been just another restaurant and more reasonable prices, my rating may have been a 4. Relative to hype alone, it was disappointing enough to have been a 2, but I'll round to a 3 because I didn't dislike anything. Just nothing to write home about.

After a delightful show at the nearby Lucille Theatre, we chanced upon this quaint little gem. Despite its compact space, a mere 10-minute wait saw us comfortably seated. Exceptional service was merely the overture to the culinary symphony that awaited.

I savored the scallops—a dish that truly merited a standing ovation. Cooked to perfection, bursting with flavor, and nestled on a bed of beans and mushrooms in an exquisite sauce, it was the pinnacle of fine dining. Fresh vegetables added the perfect crunch.

My husband opted for a burger, which was no less impressive. The beef: top-notch. The fries: a hot, crispy sidekick. This delightful eatery turned a whim into a night to remember. A definite must-return when in lower Manhattan. Simply AMAZING.

Koku Ramen stands out as a late-night sanctuary in the city, welcoming night owls with vibrant K-pop beats and eclectic decor just past midnight on a Tuesday. Though it lacks space, the cozy ambiance and an option to dine at the bar compensate for it. Taking advantage of their weekday happy hour, we indulged in reasonably priced starters—edamame, gyoza, and buns—though the edamame and gyoza were pretty standard fare. Buns, both chicken and pork, lost their distinctiveness under a blanket of spicy sauce.

Beverage-wise, give the Mango Bubble Tea a miss; its cloying sweetness overpowers the palate, despite decent boba pearls. The main event, Koku Ramen, brings a mix of tender chashu pork, bok choy, sprouts, and half an egg in a broth that packs an unexpectedly fiery punch, even at a spice level of 1. While the noodles fell short of the desired texture, the dish overall was a satisfying late-night fix.

Koku Ramen is your go-to for great happy hour specials and the convenience of late-night dining. While it may not top the list of ramen joints, it’s sure to send you to bed on a happy, full stomach.

I recently dined at a local restaurant where I tried the codfish soup. I was pleased to find that they served it with a burner to keep it warm, which was a thoughtful touch. The accompanying banchan, or appetizers, were fairly average, neither disappointing nor particularly impressive. Although the restaurant wasn't busy that afternoon, I found the service to be somewhat slow. Overall, the food quality was acceptable, but there's room for service improvement.

I recently decided to try delivery from a local restaurant renowned for their hand-pulled noodles. Against the restaurant’s own advice, I opted for those noodles instead of the regular ones they recommended. True to their word, the noodles arrived clumped together – a mishap for which I take full responsibility.

However, I encountered an unexpected issue with the beef broth - it had a strong gamey flavor that resembled lamb, which I don't consume. Unfortunately, the taste was so overpowering that it deterred me from enjoying my meal. I believe the menu should have detailed descriptions to avoid such surprises.

Additionally, during delivery, my drink was mishandled, resulting in it bursting open and causing a mess upon arrival. The incident contributed to an overall disappointing experience. In hindsight, dining in might be the better option to truly appreciate what this establishment might have to offer.

Title: A Culinary Gem That Outshines the Rest

If you've ever dined at the esteemed Gramercy Tavern and thought it couldn't get better, prepare to have your standards elevated. Our latest New York dining experience has set a new bar for excellence. We were completely astonished by both the quality and presentation of each dish. The culinary wizardry performed on the humble snow peas left us in awe, while the scallops were so exquisitely prepared, they nearly provoked tears of joy. As for the smoked carrot toast, it's not an exaggeration to say that my wife was overcome with emotion by its sheer deliciousness.

The phrase "over the top" doesn't do justice to the flavors we savored that night. This unnamed haven of gastronomy is now our mandatory stop on every New York visit—but let's keep this our little secret; we wouldn't want to struggle for a reservation. And if you happen to be served by Ben, consider yourself fortunate. His service was unparalleled, further sealing the experience as the best meal we've had in New York. Hands down.

This is a classic American burger place with all the never ending list of burgers and kosher rice pudding. The burgers are sourced from meat from the butcher across the street which shows you the high quality that is put into the food. The service was quick and efficient especially when you're in a New York hurry about moment. Enjoy

Stopped by this cool little cafe earlier today to meet a friend. The host/waitress was super cool and very friendly. My friend and I ended up getting the crepes. The savory ones are gluten free! Cute spot, glad I was able to check it out!

Unfortunately, my dining experience at the restaurant was disappointing. The garlic knots with cheese, which I had delivered, arrived cold and lacked both the promised garlic punch and the expected gooey mozzarella, yielding an unappetizing texture reminiscent of plastic.
