Additionally, while the jalapeño poppers appeared to be from the freezer aisle, they were passable in taste, but their enjoyment was diminished by the accompanying marinara sauce, which was also served cold. Overall, the meal did not meet expectations.

Title: A Last Name Legacy Worth Every Sip

We stumbled upon this gem driven by a quirky coincidence of sharing a last name, but little did we know we'd hit culinary gold. Skeptical at first of the steep pricing for a bowl of pho, my doubts vanished at the first taste of the exquisite broth. It struck a flawless balance, richly aromatic without overpowering spices, and the meat was a tender delight that effortlessly fell off the bone. 

The mango smoothie was another triumph, a refreshing palate cleanser that avoided the common pitfall of excessive sweetness. The wings, however, deserve a special mention – hands down, the finest I've ever savored. They were a harmonious medley of spice, subtle garlic, and fish sauce that I'll crave for days.

Adding to the savory experience was the staff whose courteousness and attentiveness were impeccable, the proverbial cherry on top of an unexpectedly perfect dining experience.

Came here for an early dinner and ate wayyyy too much! Reservations are a must, it was pretty packed even at 6:40pm on a Thursday! The restaurant itself is amazing, I did not expect it to be so trendy. Good music, kind of a Mad Men meets millennial vibe. We ordered way too much food. Started out with the duck hash and chicken wings, then tried the burger. Everything was beyond delicious. FYI a single burger actually has two patties. Even though we were already super full from the apps, we still manage to finish the burgers because it was just too good to waste. Will be returning to try other items on the menu!

After spotting the Vegan Miso Ramen on Instagram, my curiosity led me directly to Mokbar in Chelsea Market. Amidst the bustling ambiance, my dine-in experience was a delight. The dish, as promised by the allure of social media, was delicious, leaving a memorable impression on my palate. It's a certainty - I will be returning for another savory encounter.

Have you tried Indonesian food? I didn't know it was this good. This was our first time trying it.  We couldn't get a table Friday night, so I made sure I made reservation the following night. The server explained how dishes are usually shared family style, and they would come out as they were made. They did come out in increments. And each dish seemed better than the last served. There was not one bad dish. My favorite were the Nase Goreng and the Sea Bass. The former was their take on fried rice, seasoned in a familiar way,  yet nothing I've had before. It had seafood, minced cucumber and cilantro. The Sea Bass was infused with calamansi(my favourite citrus) and steamed wrapped in banana leaves. The baby pork ribs was succulent and smoky; its edges were salty though.  We tried one dessert, banana split cake with ube ice cream, but there was no banana bread in ours. Was it an oversight? It didn't matter, it was still utterly delicious. I just wished they didn't run out of the Pandan Custard. The staff were all just fab, helpful in their recommendations.

Title: A Bite of Budget-Friendly Delight at Vanessa's Dumpling House

Living in Manhattan often means forking out a pretty penny for just about everything, so stumbling upon Vanessa's Dumpling House in the heart of Chinatown is like finding a hidden treasure for a foodie on a budget. Amidst the hustle of my pricey life, this gem offers an escape that doesn't cost an arm and a leg.

Vanessa's is quite the Instagram celebrity, and rightly so. The fried chive and pork dumplings are an absolute steal at $2, proving that affordable can still mean delicious. The spicy beef dumplings, a mere $6.75, hit all the right notes for those who enjoy a kick in their meal. The sesame pancake sandwich, at a humble $3.75, is another standout item that shouldn't be overlooked.

Every dish seems fresh and packed with flavor—the term "bomb AF" comes to mind. Despite the inevitable line due to its popularity, the wait is short, especially on a weekday night (brace yourself for the weekend crowds, though).

The service might come across as "super azn rude," but it's all part of the charm, with a dash of humor to boot. The servers aren't stingy either; when inquiring about the sesame pancake, a sample was promptly offered, a small gesture that wins big points in my book.

Mark my words, Vanessa's Dumpling House is on my list of regular haunts. Great prices, killer eats, and an authentic slice of the city's culinary scene—what's not to love?

I love Rosie's! I've gone to Rosie's many times for HH and I do not plan to stop. My friends and I always have a great time here and HH specials are some of the best in the area. Their tacos are made in house. You can literally see the ladies making them in the middle of the restaurant. Their ingredients are fresh and perfectly executed. Their drinks are also made well and bartenders are always friendly. I've always gotten quick and friendly service here, so I'm not sure what some reviewers are talking about. The guacamole is a must have when you come too! It's fresh, looks beautiful, and is flavorful.I will be back soon for their HH! My mouth is watering looking at these photos.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this charming restaurant with my mom for lunch before a matinee, and it certainly exceeded our expectations. The ambiance is tranquilly subdued, a welcome reprieve from the usual hustle and bustle of the area's dining hotspots. 

The escargots were a standout, bathed in a delectable butter and garlic sauce, achieving that elusive perfect texture that is so often sought after. The complimentary bread was the ideal vehicle to ensure not a drop of that savory goodness went to waste.

Their hamburger, a juicy and savory delight, paired well with the nicoise salad, which was both fresh and satisfyingly hearty. We ended our meal with the creme brulee, and it was exceptional, easily ranking as one of the best I've savored.

Value is often a concern in NYC, but this restaurant offered excellent prices without compromising on quality. Service matched the high standard of the food: friendly and efficient. For those seeking an enjoyable and unhurried French dining experience, I can't recommend this restaurant enough.

I was excited to hear about the extension of Domodomo that allowed walk ins and had happy hour oysters and hand rolls. My friend and I arrived on a Sunday night and were seated immediately at the bar. Our server was very polite and attentive throughout our experience here. Happy hour prices will be implemented all night until March 1st (I believe). Happy hour oysters are 1.50, which I assume are randomly picked during the day. Specific oysters range from 2.25-2.75. Half moons were 2.25. I was extremely excited when I saw they had Kumamoto oysters for 2.75 as well! Oysters were very enjoyable and well worth it. You're allowed to choose two sauces free of charge, so we opted for the cocktail sauce and wasabi lime sorbet. I highly recommend trying the wasabi lime sorbet. Hand rolls are $6, but they also have a 4 for $22 deal. The Uni and Wagyu handroll didn't come with the happy hour deal, but that ones $16 a pop. I highly recommend getting the uni and wagyu handroll though! It literally melts in your mouth. The hand rolls were pretty good. Salmon one was a little lackluster in my opinion. Our table was also given complementary Korean fried chicken since the chefs made extra and I really appreciated this gesture ^_^ the fried chicken was flavored very well and it had a nice crispiness to it. Overall experience was superb and I highly recommend coming here, especially while these happy hour prices are still around!

After frequenting this establishment over the past year, I've been delighted to see a significant improvement in their culinary offerings. The shrimp and grits have exceeded my expectations, and the plantain hash is nothing short of amazing, bringing a unique and delectable twist to the menu.

The ambiance remains as inviting as ever, contributing to the overall dining experience in a positive way. It's clear the vibe here is a huge draw for the crowd.

However, it's worth noting that the brunch experience could benefit from some logistical enhancements. The weekend rush results in long wait times to secure a table, especially given that reservations are not accepted after noon. The lack of a streamlined process turns the occasion into a disorganized affair.

In summary, while the food is a delightful surprise, the weekend brunch setup could use some attention to match the impressive standards set by the kitchen.

My husband and I were on the hunt for an authentic pizzeria during our NYC adventure, and much to our delight, we came across a gem. Opting to trust our instincts rather than consulting Yelp paid off handsomely. The delightful array of pizza slices we sampled did not disappoint, but it was the fresh basil & mozzarella slice that won our hearts. An absolute must-visit for any pizza aficionado.

I'm a sucker for Thai so if you're looking for some great Thai food, with a warm and intimate atmosphere, and service that matches it all - look no further. Cocktails are well crafted, food tasteful and filling. Personal recommendations include the Pad Thai and Pak Mor Puk veggie dumplings. There are definitely more exotic dishes but as a first time visit, I had to get my usual litmus test dish of Pad Thai. Major plus is that they have live wait on Yelp! Definitely will be going back soon and I have a feeling it'll be one of my NYC staples

After all the running around I searched high and low to find somewhere to eat and charge up my phone. Sigh... I wish I was able to look under yelp 1st before ordering. This place looks cute but the food didn't do it for us. My son wasnt happy at all and he would eat just about anything I tell ya.His spicy beef soup was not good. His words not mine. The beef was too chewy he had to spit each one out after chewing forever. On top of that he said it was too salty. I had the cris

Title: Tasty Bites Amidst a Gratuity Gripe

During a leisurely jaunt through Chinatown, a tempting array of dishes on display lured me into this local eatery. The extensive menu, showcased outside with vivid pictures, promised an authentic culinary adventure.

I indulged in soup dumplings and General Tao's chicken, complemented by a fluffy side of rice. The kitchen delivered on its promises, serving up flavors that were on point—satisfying both in taste and presentation. Service matched the quality of the food: attentive, swift, and eager to please.

However, my dining experience was soured slightly when the check arrived with an automatic gratuity tacked on. While I am a proponent of rewarding good service, the compulsory nature of the tip was off-putting. I believe in the principle of tipping as a voluntary gesture reflecting the diner's satisfaction, not as an enforced add-on.

Despite the delectable meal and commendable service, the restaurant's policy on gratuity has marred what could have been a perfect dining experience. This practice alone makes me hesitant to return. They would have comfortably earned five stars, but instead, they've left me with a reminder that sometimes, the aftertaste matters just as much as the meal.

We came here during the evening amidst all the corona virus talks that is spreading like wildfire in NYC. The place could not be any more vibrant and clean. The virus did not deter locals and new customers from coming to this establishment. With that being said, I am a huge fan of soup dumplings which is what gravitated me to coming here. The soup dumpling skin is quite thin but firm, so do not fret about it breaking! The soup was deliciously rich and not too salty. The pork/crab meat was not quite memorable. We also ordered the black truffle soup dumplings thinking it might somewhat resemble what we experienced at Din Tai Fung. The truffle was faint and honestly disappointing for what we paid for. I would avoid this dish if you are expecting Din Tai Fung quality.Give the soup dumplings a try. If that is not your cup of tea, there are over 50 other items on the menu ranging from authentic Shangainese dishes to regular traditional Chinese dishes.

Best steak house in NYC! I've been to all of the top rated steak houses in Manhattan and the other boroughs and American Cut is by far my favorite! The ambiance is old school yet modern, staff is very friendly and greet you the moment you walk in the door. The steak is always cooked to perfection. The star of the menu is the chili lobster, I honestly want to drink the sauce it comes with! Luckily it comes with perfectly toasted Texas toast to dip in. The chili lobster is on the list of one of the best things I've EVER eaten, that's how good it is. My favorite side is the twice baked potato. For dessert I usually get the popcorn sundae which is the perfect combination of sweet and salty

Title: A Local Gem Elevating Veggie Cuisine

Having dined at Loring Place numerous times since its inception, I can attest to its consistently top-notch culinary experience. Chef Dan Kluger, known for his tenure at ABCv, truly excels at this establishment, upping the ante with a vegetable-centric menu that dazzles the palate. While meat and fish are present, it's the vegetables and grains that steal the spotlight, making it an exceptional choice for both brunch and dinner enthusiasts.

Service at Loring Place is nothing short of impeccable, complemented by a vibrant atmosphere that adds to the overall dining experience. The thoughtfully curated cocktail and wine list is the perfect accompaniment to the stellar fare. Loring Place has easily become one of our beloved local favorites, and for good reason.

Title: A Cozy Brunch Spot with Great Drink Deals

I recently visited a no-frills brunch spot with friends on a Saturday. The place offers the convenience of reservations, which is perfect for pre-show dining. They boast an impressive $5 brunch cocktail menu, as well as a $15 boozy brunch option that stands out, especially given the restaurant's prime location.

The ambiance on the second floor was cozy, amplified by a super friendly and welcoming bartender. While I didn't see the third floor, the first floor featured a few tables and another well-stocked bar.

A nice touch was the complimentary mini muffins provided at the start of our meal, although the corn muffins were a tad dry. I opted for the giambotti, priced at $19, accompanied by a 'puffcake'—a daily flavored muffin. Unfortunately, the much-anticipated Oreo puffcake fell short due to its dryness and lack of flavor. Meanwhile, my friends enjoyed their egg benedict dishes, each costing $16.

The restaurant wasn't overcrowded, likely due to the ongoing corona scare, which allowed us to linger and chat post-meal. Despite some misses, the value and location are unbeatable. I'm eager to return, perhaps to experience their happy hour, which runs from 5 to 10 pm with $5 drinks.

Incredible bar tucked away in the Union Square Hyatt hotel! The place looks incredible with the window and glass displays along the walls. The bar is spacious and set up so that it doesn't feel claustrophobic at all even if it's packed. The music level was also perfect for having a good conversation with friends while still listening to great music (amazing playlist too). We came here on a sat night around 11:30pm and it was lively but many tables were open. It had actually been someone's 50th birthday as there were balloons everywhere and a section of people who were clearly celebrating. However, the staff was great in making sure we knew that we were allowed to be there and got us situated quickly. The drinks were absolutely delicious. I got the lazy lover which was full of floral notes, a big winner for me in the cocktail department. The atmosphere was great and my friends and I loved how we could sit and talk for hours without being distracted by large, loud crowds and such. Will for sure be making this a more regular spot for a casual drink!

This restaurant is the bomb dot com! With its fantastic ambience and cordial staff, it's impossible not to fall in love with this place. Every item on the menu is a hit, but the fried chicken deserves a special mention: seasoned to perfection with irresistibly crunchy skin. If you're on the lookout for an exceptional brunch spot, look no further. Do yourself a favor and pay this gem a visit – you won't regret it.

Have you ever had ramen and upon finishing your bowl, you were craving gelato, but you find it a pain to walk a few blocks down trying to squeeze through people on the street? Yeah, me neither.I got to try a few things here at this unique restaurant. Imagine having your favorite gelato shop, a Gong Cha (or some other bubble tea shop you like), and let's say Ivan Ramen all in one. You get Camellia. Some of the appetizers I got to try included the Fried Crispy Pork Belly and the Salt and Pepper Fried Chicken. The Salt and Pepper Fried Chicken was amazing, especially with the dipping sauce that comes with it. The Fried Crispy Pork Belly to be I felt like it was over fried, but it could have suppose to have been like that.The Minced Pork Ramen was very interesting as it is not your typical ramen you find where there's broth. It is a dry ramen soaked in a bean sauce, which provides a very unique experience. Would recommend trying this. It is not spicy, but you can ask for hot oil or chill paste to make it spicy.The best part may have been the gelato. The selections that this unique restaurant provides ranges from Matcha to Mango. They have some unique flavors such as Lychee Rose and Taro. I had the Taro which is very rich in taste and not sweet at all compared to other ice cream shops where there is added sugar to enhance the taste. The best gelato flavor that is a must have upon coming here would be the White Rabbit gelato. They literally took the White Rabbit candy and made it into a gelato flavor. They better trademark that flavor before everyone else starts copying it!Overall, a very wonderful experience. Service was fantastic. The staffs are amazing and friendly as hell. I hope this concept of a ramen/gelato/bubble tea in one conglomerate shop will catch on because boy does it save three different trips to three different shops! #firstworldproblems

We had just finished the Radio City Music Hall tour and were looking for a quite bite and went back to the building across the street which houses Top of the Rock, to the lower level where there are a variety of shops and found Tri Tip Grill.  There was a special on the Cabo Chop Salad with steak for only $9.99 and got that along with the bacon, avocado, chicken sandwich (to go).  We shared the salad and it was flavorful with black beans, jicama, roast beef, medium rare, corn, lettuce, halved cherry tomatoes, and radishes resting on a taco shell.  It was delish.

During a recent visit to a New York City restaurant, we were absolutely delighted by their adobada tacos. Each bite was a culinary revelation — so much so that we couldn't resist ordering a second round, knowing it would be a while before we could savor them again. While the especial asada was decent, it paled in comparison to the adobada tacos. If you find yourself at this establishment, do yourself a favor: go straight for the adobada tacos — you'll thank us later.

Tucked just a few blocks from the neon buzz of Times Square, this no-nonsense pizzeria is the quintessential late-night haunt for the famished partygoer. The pizza here is unapologetically greasy, loaded with cheese, and perfectly engineered to satisfy post-midnight cravings. Following a short walk and an even shorter wait, we indulged in the kind of comforting slice that's best enjoyed after a night of revelry. With our stomachs content and wallets barely lighter, it was the straightforward capstone on our night before we descended into the subway, homeward bound. Quick, easy, and utterly gratifying – exactly what you'd hope for at 2 am.

Title: A Chic and Tasty Seafood Experience Perfect for a Night Out

Last Monday at 7 pm, my nine girlfriends and I descended upon a trendy, seafood-focused eatery for a fun girls' night out. Even though we arrived late for our 6:30 reservation, a brief wait post our courteous call-ahead saw us ascending in an elevator to the restaurant's vibrant second-floor space, which, as it turns out, doubles as a club when the night deepens.

The dining experience here is communal and lively, with dishes served family-style and arriving in a meticulously timed cascade. We may have been overzealous in ordering multiples of everything upfront, leaving us with an abundance of leftovers. A word to the wise: order as you go.

Now, the feast - the Ceviche was the star with its fresh cucumber roll brimming with crab and tangy mango. Do not miss the tableside spectacle of the Catch Roll prepared with a blowtorch, making it not only a taste sensation but also Instagram gold. Skip the basic Spicy Tuna Roll, but definitely dive into the Crispy Rice Roll, a top contender for appetizers.

Richness defines the Scallop Gnocchi, while the Lobster Roll delights more with its buttery bread than the crustacean itself. Portion it out; it's quite filling. Chicken Bao pleasantly surprised me with its soft bun and perfect chicken ratio. The Steak is solid, though not the highlight, and for sides, the smoky Brussel Sprouts and standard-yet-tasty Truffle Fries complemented the meal, but it was the Crispy Shrimp that demanded encore.

For refreshment, the Revitalizer, an unexpected hit, helps balance an indulgent Vegas night with its zesty blend of non-alcoholic ingredients like carrot juice. Be prepared for the wallet impact of trendiness here – it's not for the faint of finance.

While navigating tight quarters to the restrooms might be a mild challenge, the ambience—with its cool brick walls and dim lights—sets the scene for a vivacious outing, albeit amidst a backdrop of business diners.

In conclusion, this place thrums with trendy vibes and serves up some seriously fresh seafood, making for an immersive and enjoyable dining experience.

My prayers have been answered. The best Pho shop in New York just opened a month ago. The Pho Tai (rare beef pho) was so good. The meat was cut perfectly to give you a savory, chewy yet delicate experience. The broth was creamy and flavorful but not overly salty. I also love the philosophy of Just Pho. Do one thing and do it well. My only feedback is that my rice noodles were too short to slurp. Where's the fun in that? Get the noodles a little better (longer, possibly with more springiness) and you'll have the perfect bowl.

Title: A Cozy Spot with Comforting Twists on Classics

Having visited this restaurant multiple times, it's safe to declare it a pretty good find. The salmon dinner strays from the beaten path, offering a creamy concoction dotted with tender salmon pieces that pique the curiosity and delight the palate.

For dessert enthusiasts eager for a sugar fix, the confetti cake could be your slice of heaven, especially if a rich, buttery icing is what your sweet tooth desires. It wasn't quite to my taste, but I can see its appeal for those who enjoy a decadent frosting.

The stars of the menu are the homely touches: the freshly baked bread, crisp pickles, and a creamy, heartwarming Mac n cheese that deserve an encore. These simple yet perfectly executed items are what will likely bring me back to the table soon.

I didn't enjoy my fish tacos from Moonstruck. It was flavorless but steeped in hot sauce which I wasn't aware of so yeah, those full water glasses were my best friend. I hardly use salt but I kept shaking that shaker over my tacos hoping for a change in taste that never came. My friend's tuna melt was delicious so I'm not sure what went on. It was lunch time but Moonstruck wasn't crowded. Staff was quick and the diner was clean. Mon-Thursdays they go till 10 pm and on Fridays and Saturdays midnight. I'm not gonna rule them out just yet so I may have to revisit this review, especially as I've been told their food is "really good". (Not quite) The End. (We'll see).

After a long day, I found the perfect spot to unwind with a glass of exquisite 2016 Chateauneuf-du-Pape at a charming new addition to the neighborhood. This year-old gem, a spinoff from the VSV empire, combines the intimacy of a bustling ambiance with the personal touch of its experienced staff, like Hugo and Carissa, who were more than happy to share their insights.

Nestled among the sparse dining options of Riverside Blvd, this establishment stands out. I savored a grilled shrimp and endive salad, elevated by crumbled blue cheese—a highlight among a carefully curated selection of small plates that promise a gastronomic adventure.

With bar seats fitting my preference and a lively scene, it's no doubt I'll be returning to what feels like an oasis for food enthusiasts in an area thirsting for quality sit-down eateries.

Last Wednesday, after happy hour, my friends and I stumbled upon this gem of a restaurant. The outside menu was inviting enough to draw us in, and we were immediately charmed by the delightful decor and the warm welcome from the staff. Our server impressed us with their professionalism and pleasant demeanor. We each indulged in a ramen bowl, and I must say, everyone at the table was thoroughly impressed with the flavors and quality of the food. It was an unexpectedly delightful dining experience that I would recommend to anyone looking for a cozy spot with excellent cuisine.

Tucked away on Rivington, this charming little spot is easy to overlook, but a definite must-visit for refreshing cucumber/lime/mint-infused water, warm service, and soups with intoxicating broths. The coconut spicy lemongrass soup, a photogenic and satisfying twist on traditional pho, offers a perfect balance of spice and distinct lemongrass zest. To finish, the ube cheesecake, though unphotographed, deserves mention for its creamy, mousse-like consistency, complemented by blueberries. A delightful dining experience for those seeking comfort with a flavorful edge.

Celebrating our 20th wedding anniversary, we sought the illustrious Michelin star elegance that Del Posto in NYC promised, and it did not disappoint. The atmosphere radiates sophistication, balancing old-world charm with modern luxury through its majestic staircase, live piano, and a tasteful color scheme of deep browns, creams, and sumptuous leather seating.

Service at Del Posto is a masterclass in attention to detail. The staff ensures water glasses remain filled and the appropriate glassware is provided for each wine pairing. Their attentiveness is remarkable, extending to even assisting with seating after a visit to the restroom. The dinnerware and glassware, some custom-designed, add to the sense of exclusivity.

Opting for the five-course prix fixe menu with wine pairing, we experienced a symphony of flavors starting with a playful amuse-bouche of soup in a delicate teacup with melon and prosciutto. The freshly baked bagatini bread, paired with an indulgent cream butter, set the tone for the epicurean journey ahead.

The menu was a triumph. Standouts included the 28 Day Aged Beef Ribeye and the sumptuous Crown Shaped Pasta filled with Toma Cheese & Black Truffle Butter, whose rich flavors are still etched in my memory. The wine pairing was thoughtfully curated, although the sommelier's soft-spoken descriptions left us craving a touch more insight into our libations.

Desserts were a spectacle of their own with highlights like the FOCACCINE Veneziane Dolci and the intricately balanced Panna Cotta. Del Posto's playful presentation of chocolates and sweets in a cheese grater with a drawer exemplified the creativity that permeated our dining experience. A personalized touch on the "happy anniversary" zeppoles warmed our hearts.

Del Posto is a testament to the culinary arts, combining gastronomic excellence with impeccable service. We left not only satiated but with an anniversary dinner that will be reminisced for years to come. Del Posto proudly stands as a jewel in the crown of NYC's fine dining scene.

Tucked away in the bustling culinary scene, this restaurant elevates Chinese cuisine to a level of sophistication and delight. Their signature house-marinated chicken truly stands out—a dish that captivated my taste buds with its remarkable tenderness, and a sauce so divine, my friend was compelled to take some home. The eel rice and lotus dumplings, while competently prepared, didn't quite hit the same high notes, though the latter did offer a unique and novel flavor experience worth noting. The abalone tofu was another highlight, masterfully blending rich flavors in a dish that was both comforting and luxurious. As a sweet end to a sumptuous meal, we were treated to complimentary strawberry puddings, a perk of checking in on WeChat—a gesture of hospitality that did not go unnoticed. Overall, this establishment is a must-visit for connoisseurs of Chinese delicacies with a penchant for the extraordinary.

4 stars for food, 3 stars for service, and 2 stars for cleanliness. Averages to 3 but I'm sticking with 2 stars. The kids were literally fake ice-skating across the greasy floors. We took turns commenting on how gross the graffiti bathrooms were. They ran our Discover card, but they don't take Discover. If you can try to see past all that, the food was quite authentic!

I have a mild obsession with eggs in general. The Egg Shop feeds into that obsession & is a lovely option if you're looking for an EGG-cellent brunch! I love the spot because it's really relaxing. The only thing is it's a little overpriced.

During a late-night foray into one of my brother's recommended NYC haunts, our party of five descended upon this gem around 10pm on a Thursday. Seated promptly in a cute Asian-set ambiance, we tackled an array of appetizers including heavenly siomai, tangy kimchi, crispy karage, and delectably spicy gyozas—both house and regular versions.

The main affair featured the Lucky Cat ramen for most, a spicy delight with perfectly thin noodles, while one of us ventured into the land of thick noodles with a hearty pork belly ramen. Both variants impressed with their generous portions and robust flavors.

Service was efficient and unpretentious, ensuring we savored a substantial, satisfying meal. It's easy to see why this place is a favorite; I'm already planning a return visit.

On New Years Eve I was walking down Mulberry just on a stroll to see where my friends and I may get an early dinner before a comedy show when a funny man came out of this restaurant and started speaking to me in Italian! I am fluent in Spanish so I laughed and kept up but he convinced me to come back to this spot at 5pm. It looked much fancier from the outside than the inside but the cheaper prices do match the inside. Regardless of prices, the food was quite good! Maybe not Nonna's but it was flavourful & good!My boyfriend ordered the eggplant parmesan (~18) and it was delicious! I was in the mood for gnocchi (~14)but they didnt have sorrentina on the menu but they made it for me! It was so good and super cheesy, just my style!We also got the stuffed artichoke but I wouldn't really recommend it-- not crispy or flavourful just okayStop by this spot in Little Italy!

Pretty damn good. Not going to lie, I thought this place might have just been just over hyped. I had to wait at least an hour to be sat down. And when I finally sat down and ate - I fell in love with the food. Well first, I think the ambiance is great for a date night. I personally think it's a little too dark for my liking but quite ideal for a date night.Food wise - it's very tapa and sharing style. I think it's a little overpriced for what it is but the food is pretty good so that makes up for it. My favorite though is the truffle mac - it's pretty damn fire if you're into truffle and mac & cheese. Highly recommend you to try that unless you really hate mac & cheese.

An'NamWe were out late walking around and wanted some summer rolls. The only problem was that we were in the heart of Times Square. Not too many options especially since it was late too. In walked An'Nam. It's an unusual restaurant as it's both Japanese and Vietnamese. We came in right before they were closing so we had to take our food to go. We were a bit discouraged at the time because we really wanted to eat there but it turned out for the better.  We ordered two summer rolls. One with shrimp and the other a veggie version. Then I also ordered a small Pho soup. Everything was amazing. The fact that we had to eat elsewhere melted away. Go give this place a shot. If it could please this very picky eater it might just work for you.

Title: A Ramen Revelation in NYC

If you're on the hunt for top-tier ramen in NYC, look no further! The staff at this gem are as friendly as they are professional, ensuring a delightful dining experience from start to finish. But let's talk about what's in the bowl—the ramen is simply unbeatable. The classic noodle bowl is a must-try, bursting with flavor in every slurp. A word to the wise: opt for an extra half portion of noodles to satisfy your hunger, as the standard serving might leave the ravenous wanting more. The interior of the establishment is as neat and inviting as the bowls are comforting. This spot has firmly established itself as a go-to for that perfect ramen fix.
Went here for happy hour and it was delicious. The drinks were really good for the happy hour $8 price and the food was great!! Definitely try the truffle fries and macaroni cheese balls.

Title: A Trip Down Memory Lane at the Dumpling Delight

I revisited a cherished dining spot after several years, drawn back by the irresistible pull of their peanut dumplings. Yielding to the craving, I opted for the chicken-filled variety and was transported back with the first bite, as they were just as delectable as I remembered from over half a decade ago.

Keen to keep it low-carb, I also sampled the BBQ pork shoulder, or moo yang, which, while enjoyable, was not without its faults. The servings were generous, but the pork was a tad cumbersome, lacking the finesse of being thoroughly sliced. Compared to the competition, the accompanying sauce didn't quite hit the mark; it lacked the depth of flavor I've relished at Ayada and Dek Sen.

The service was both accommodating and efficient, though the pace seemed to nudge towards hastiness. Despite this minor hiccup, the restaurant still holds its charm, and should fate guide me back to this neighborhood, their Pad Thai's call will be too tempting to resist.

The waiter is very rude. My friend doesn't really speak English and they make sure to let her know that they don't understand her. The food was good but the pizza was very greasy. Overall, wouldn't go back.

I wanted to try Soup Dumplings so looked for a place that served them in Chinatown. When I got there around 1 pm I had to wait about 10 minutes. I ordered Soup Dumplings with crab meat and pork. There were six of them. I ate the first one and the soup was hot and it was delicious. After a few of them the soup was getting colder. I prefer hot. I also ordered Beef with Tofu from Over Rice sexton. I expected a different dish but it was still good.

Two things to note:1) CDG is not located on 32nd St K-Town.  It's on 35th b/w 5th and 6th.2) they do not offer DIY KBBQ.No reservations accepted on weekends and incomplete parties are not seated.  There are a bunch of bars in the area to grab a drink while you wait, but you run the risk of losing your table because they do not call you when your table is ready.  A couple of our friends were running late, so the host allowed us to leave our name on the list for a table while we went to a bar across the street.  We were asked to give them a call before we came back, which we did; the total wait time for a table when we got back to the restaurant was about 5-10 mins.Service is pretty standard for this area; prompt, responsive, and friendly enough.  The meal starts with individual servings of their famous housemade tofu; nice tofu flavor, slightly underseasoned, possibly to allow the bean curd flavor to shine through.  We ordered two bottles of soju (Chum Churum and Chamisul, $15/375ml), CDG japchae ($18.99), seafood and scallion pancake ($16.99), LA galbi ($38.99), and seafood & tofu jeongol ($42.99).  Everything was delicious, but the pancake really shined.  The pancake was PACKED with vegetables and seafood, and really crispy on the outside.  The LA galbi also impressed with its tenderness and flavor.Two starters, 2 entrees, and 2 soju was enough to satisfy our group of 6.  Inclusive of 20% tip, we each paid a reasonable $32 for a very delicious meal.  The wait for a table on the weekends is inconvenient, and I don't know if I would do it again, but I would come back on a weekday if I didn't have to wait.

Dark, fun little Mexican spot with a great drink menu. We had a great experience the night we went and we will definitely be back. My friend was late arriving to dinner and I was fortunate enough to have the lovely hostess put a reserve sign on a bar seat next to me as I awaited. Since the place was empty at 6:15pm I was surprised she did that. But 10 minutes later the place was packed!!!While I waited I tried more than one of their specialty margaritas ranging from coconut infused to jalapeño spiked and liked each one. And I almost got full on the chips and salsa before we ordered dinner. In the end, the Ceviche was fresh, the tacos were great, and the rice and beans were delicious. We loved every plate and drink. Arrive there early as the seats go fast! But if you have to wait, it's worth it.

Title: A Quick Lunch at Ippudo - Room for Improvement

I gave Ippudo another shot for a weekday lunch, and I was pleased to find no waiting time after a quick phone confirmation. The restaurant wasn't crowded, but there was a lively buzz around the large round table that was occupied.

I opted for the Akamaru Shinaji ramen, priced at $16, and decided to add an egg for an extra $2.50. The service was efficient, with the bowl arriving promptly. Taste-wise, the ramen was just okay. While it's a decent choice if you're in the area, I wouldn't recommend going out of your way or enduring a long wait for this experience. There are definitely competitors out there offering better ramen, particularly in terms of soup base quality and variety of toppings.

It may be silly to write a review solely based on one item on the menu, but the Greek Yogurt was unforgettable. I dined with a friend coming in with a far bigger appetite than I did. She ordered the Branzino which came with a side of YiaYia's Lemon Potatoes, the Horiatiki, and the Fava. All three were delicious, but the Fava stood out to me as an excellent alternative hummus that I haven't seen in other Greek restaurants. Worth a try if you are an adventurous eater, it was delicious.I opted for the Greek Yogurt having eaten a large meal before coming and oh my goodness, it was perfect. The yogurt was decadent and creamy and not overwhelmingly tangy. Chunks of golden apples sat atop a bed of rich honey and chopped walnuts. You really must try it. I have since tried to replicate this at home with moderate success, yet none of the store-bought Greek yogurts could compare to Kiki's. But if a Greek restaurant offers Greek yogurt, you know it'll be amazing.

Title: A Delightful Evening at the Hyped Noodle Spot

I finally visited the much-Instagrammed noodle restaurant that's been all the rage. On a quest for cold noodles to combat the heat, I was thrilled to discover this spot via a search last Friday. The app-based waitlist was a godsend, ensuring we bypassed the chaos experienced at another eatery the week prior. Seated promptly upon arrival, the service was nothing short of efficient.

We began with the 6-piece chicken tatsuta-age, a recommended must-try. Piping hot and dangerously addictive, they reminded us jokingly of a high-end Chick-fil-A, yet they were undeniably scrumptious. For our mains, the ja ja cold udon bowls were a hit. Priced at $14, each serving was a harmonious blend of spicy miso pork, fresh cucumbers, grape tomatoes, and a perfectly poached egg. The dish was a flavorful yet refreshing choice for a muggy evening. As we neared the end, my boyfriend cleverly ordered extra noodles to soak up the remaining savory broth - a satisfying finale to our meal.

Eagerly anticipating our next visit, we're already planning to try the hot udon variations when the weather cools down. This place lived up to the hype, and we left fully contented.

Title: Rotisserie Revelations at Local Gem

Upon my festive visit on Christmas Eve, it became apparent that the star attraction at this bustling eatery is the rotisserie chicken. The popularity of this dish was unmistakable as a snaking line of eager patrons extended out the door, all waiting to take home this culinary delight.

Opting to dine in, I was served a half chicken with remarkable speed. It was nothing short of spectacular — succulent and moist inside, with a skin boasting a glossy, crisp exterior. The accompanying garlic chili sauce was a divine pairing, enhancing the chicken's already robust flavor profile.

While I indulged in some sweet plantains and rice and beans to complement my meal, these sides played a supporting role and didn't outshine the main attraction. As for value, the prices were reasonable for the locale, offering substantial portions that promised a satisfying experience without breaking the bank.

It's worth noting the restaurant’s important role in the community, with a majority of the clientele speaking Spanish; it's a true neighborhood fixture deserving local patronage for its authentic fare and welcoming atmosphere.

Title: A Dinner Delight You Can Trust

I just had dinner at this gem of a restaurant and it absolutely deserves all the praise. The pork chops were the highlight of my meal – cooked to succulent perfection. While the other dish details escape me, the overall experience left such a positive impression that I confidently gave it a strong 4-star rating. Trust me when I say, you need to dine here!

Title: Lackluster Late-Night Curry Experience

I visited this establishment after a late-night curry craving, only to be turned away upon arrival despite their advertised 3 AM closing time. Giving them a second chance at lunch, I opted for the $10 special but was forced to spend $15 to use my debit card, so I added karage (fried chicken) to my order.

Unfortunately, the curry portion was disappointingly small with meat that appeared aged and lacked the crispness and mild brown color characteristic of properly cooked Japanese cuisine. The flavor profile was off, seemingly reheated with a haphazard addition of pepper that failed to deliver the requested spiciness.

The karage was a further letdown – merely warm and excessively oily rather than hot, crispy, and juicy. Service was average at best; the staff selectively attentive, often ignoring me while I waited politely without interrupting the bustling atmosphere of the restaurant. It seemed only certain customers received a warm welcome.

Despite its popularity among tourists and New York City locals drawn by the allure of authentic Japanese curry, the experience falls short. Overpriced add-ons at $1.50 each only added to the disappointment. There are better options out there for those looking for genuine quality and service. Overall, just okay but not worth the hype.

Ive always craved Banhmi but it was only available in Brooklyn until now. I came here three days after their grand opening. There is a big parking lot and it's pretty empty. We were able to get a spot right in front of the restaurant. The restaurant itself is small but very welcoming. The traditional Banhmi and grilled pork rice box was not the best I've had but still very good. The Vermicelli is not as soft as it should be. Overall, I would come back here whenever I crave Banhmi. It's not the best but I'm still very satisfied.

Buzzfeed's Worth It made us do it... so if you stop in, make sure you pick up their Curry Bun!Is it really too much to ask nowadays for restaurants to stop using Golden Curry as their curry fillings / toppings? Well, I'm really pleased that Fay Da's curry filling taste definitely had its own unique flavor, and the pastry bun itself was flakey and hearty. We LOVED our curry buns. Was very tempted to buy more but we didn't want to get too full. Cash only if you don't meet the card minimum. Fay Da was amazing. Will definitely be returning to try their other goodies!

Title: A Flavorful Afternoon at by CHLOE

As a first-time guest at by CHLOE, prompted by my sister's glowing recommendations, our Saturday visit at 3pm proved to be a wise choice to dodge the bustling lunch crowd. The location's spaciousness immediately impressed us, creating an airy and relaxed dining environment.

My order, the guac burger, was a standout – a bean-based patty that thankfully steered clear of the typical mushiness found in some vegetarian options. It was absolutely delicious. My sister's choice, the spicy Thai salad, was equally impressive when I sampled it, bursting with flavor and freshness.

We shared a side of sweet potato fries, which were the perfect complement to our meals. Considering the prime location of the restaurant, the prices were quite reasonable, offering good value for money.

An unexpected delight was the restroom decor – playful and charming with mushroom-themed wallpaper, adding a unique touch to the overall experience.

In summary, by CHLOE has won me over with its tantalizing menu, spacious venue, and delightful quirks. It's a definite must-visit for anyone in search of tasty plant-based fare.

Title: A Gem in the Heart of NYC: Torien Yakitori

My partner and I were fortunate to dine at Torien shortly before New York City's lockdown, and the memory of the experience compels me to write this much-deserved review.

Torien, a newcomer on the scene, may just edge out its sibling Torishin in my affections. The yakitori-centric meal took us on a culinary journey, remarkably starting with an amuse-bouche and weaving through an array of skewered delights such as chicken thigh, shoulder, okra, heart, and even the unexpected – chicken knee and neck skin. Each dish we tasted, including the non-meat options like tofu and gingko nuts, was executed to perfection. However, the knee and neck skin were the stars for me, alongside the tender thigh and delectably smooth tofu.

The intimate counter seating allowed us to watch the chefs masterfully prepare each skewer, adding a sense of culinary theater to our dining experience. Despite a bustling environment, the service flowed seamlessly with no excessive waiting times. Engaging with the chef added a personal touch to the dining experience, enhancing the overall enjoyment.

Not only were the staff exceptionally friendly, but the atmosphere struck the perfect balance between sophistication and coziness. The chicken rice bowl was a delicious finale to our meal, although the choice of indulging in more yakitori was tempting. A word to the wise: for late diners, it's possible some options may run out.

In conclusion, Torien is a must-visit for those seeking an intimate, top-notch yakitori experience. The excellence of both the food and service ensures that I am counting down the days until I can return.

My recent dining experience at this restaurant was nothing short of exceptional! For our celebratory graduation dinner, we indulged in a delightful mix of flavors, including the savory chili ramen, the aromatic curry ramen, the zesty spicy mango roll, and the vibrant fiesta roll. Additionally, the Brussels sprout dumplings and the fungi dumplings were mouthwatering triumphs of taste.

While the wine was satisfactory, the desserts stole the show. The cinnamon roll was a decadent treat, and the cookie accompanied by ice cream was a perfect sweet note to end on. Service was impressively swift, with the food arriving promptly, and the servers were nothing but attentive, going the extra mile to accommodate us by placing a bouquet of flowers in water.

I highly recommend this restaurant for its delectable cuisine and the thoughtful, efficient service that made our special occasion truly memorable.

It was my first time trying Turkish food. I am a very picky eater but I am always willing to trying new foods. My friend and I had a full appetizer spread with bread but the dishes that stood out to me were the Baba Ganoush (made of eggplant) and the pink sultan (a red beets spread). I am not a huge fan of beets but it was prepared different from what I am used to, it was very creamy. The Baba Ganoush had such great flavor and was a great compliment to the bread. The Turkish bread was crunchy on the outside but nice and soft on the inside. It was very addicting, I couldn't get enough of it. I've never liked hummus but my friend is a fan and said it was her favorite of the appetizer spread. For drinks we had Red Sangria which was full of different fruits, I enjoyed it. For our entree we opted for the Salmon in Vine Leaves and Chicken Shish Kebab. The salmon and chicken were flavorful and very juicy. It was suggested by Sergio to eat our dessert with tea which isn't something I am used to. We had baklava which tastes as its ingredients which are pistachios and honey. It was good but was a little too textured for my liking. I also don't like pumpkin so I didn't enjoy the pumpkin dessert as a pumpkin lover would. On the other hand, I fell in love with their Turkish tea and its presentation. Overall I had a good experience at this restaurant. The presentation of every dish shows that they pay attention to detail. The staff was attentive and made me feel welcomed. Hopefully next time I can try their Gyros and some rice pudding!

Title: A Gem for Pizza Lovers!

On a bustling Friday lunchtime, I found myself at a vibrant eatery that was bursting at the seams. With no tables available, the bar became our spot, and what a delightful spot it was! The bartender, not only a whiz with the drinks which were exceptional, lent her culinary savvy to guide us through the menu. At her recommendation, we indulged in the Luca with vodka sauce—a pizza that was expertly tailored to our tastes and simply transcendent.

The ambiance of the place added to the charm, with a setting that was undeniably cool and inviting. But it was the female manager who truly elevated our experience. Navigating food allergies can be a daunting affair, especially with a severe nut allergy like mine and a pistachio pizza on the menu. Her understanding and attentiveness shone through as she reassured me, sharing her personal connection to allergies, which put my concerns at ease.

The care with which she oversaw the preparation of my meal was a testament to the restaurant's commitment to customer safety and satisfaction. In a small kitchen scenario, such conscientious service is a rare and precious comfort.

For anyone in the area, I can't recommend this place enough. It's a sanctuary for both foodies and those with dietary constraints, a reminder that great food and exceptional service can indeed go hand in hand.
The food was delicous. It was packed and we reserved a spot on the waiting list. The menu was a bit overpriced.

The hits and misses kinda balance themselves out.If you've been to Mexico City - Roma / La Condesa in particular - you'll recognize this place. It's the kind of hip, urban place so common there, with an interesting menu, an excellent cocktail list, and all the mezcal varieties that you could possibly want.And yet, once the food comes, you are curiously left wanting.  Some of the stuff is good - very very good in fact (the tamales - oh, those tamales!).  But so much of it is just, well, *meh*. And then when you look at the prices, you realize that you've just paid a small fortune for a resolutely meh experience - something that is the polar opposite of what happens in Mexico City.So yeah, pass on the place.(On a side note, the service is ... interesting.  Very friendly staff, but about half the time they forget to get you whatever you've ordered.  They're very apologetic about it, but it, but then it happens again.  Go figure...)

Title: A Hidden Gem for Seafood Lovers

During a birthday weekend turned impromptu food tour, my friends and I stumbled upon this delightful spot after facing a daunting wait at Shaking Crab. Initially skeptical due to its availability on Yelp and the quiet ambiance upon arrival, this restaurant quickly dispelled our doubts.

Parking was a challenge, but after a few circles around the block, we were rewarded with a great spot. Stepping into the restaurant, I'll admit I was a bit nervous seeing it empty. However, any unease vanished the moment we were greeted by our fantastic server and treated to an array of delicious drinks.

The food here is exceptional - every bite was a testament to freshness and quality, particularly the standout garlic butter sauce that was so divine, I considered stocking up by the gallon. The interior exudes a cozy, chic vibe that immediately makes you feel at home.

Everything about this place screams 'classy' - from the top-notch service to the impeccably fresh seafood. It's safe to say this will be my new go-to restaurant. I'm eager to return and secretly hope it remains as wonderfully low-key as it was on my visit.

Title: A Cozy Gem with Terrific Pasta and Wine Near Broadway

I recently discovered a fantastic restaurant that ticks all the boxes for a perfect dining experience. The pasta here is cooked to cheesy, al dente perfection, paired with an excellent selection of wines that elevate the meal. The cozy atmosphere adds to the charm, making it a comfortable spot for an evening out.

To top it off, the prices are reasonable, providing great value for the quality of food and drink on offer. Its convenient location, just a short walk from the train or subway, makes it an ideal choice for pre-show dining if you're heading to a Broadway performance.

Do yourself a favor and make a reservation to secure a spot at this delightful establishment. The terrific food and inviting ambience are sure to make your evening.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Argentinian Cuisine

I recently had the pleasure of dining at an exceptional Argentinian steak house, which I wholeheartedly recommend. The food was impeccable across the board. Our group opted for several shared dishes, starting with a succulent grilled octopus, a refreshingly light burrata, and savory mushrooms. Each appetizer was a unique and delightful experience.

For the main course, we indulged in a 16oz skirt steak paired with roasted cauliflower. Admittedly, the steak portion was quite generous, and we found ourselves unable to finish it, but the steak's preparation was flawless - succulent, flavorful, and cooked to perfection.

The ambiance of the restaurant struck a fine balance between coziness and sophistication, enhancing the dining experience. To complement the outstanding cuisine, the service was attentive and top-notch.

If you're a fan of Argentinian fare or simply in the mood for a sublime steak, do not overlook this culinary gem.

I loved the indoor patio for our late spring dinner. It allowed us to soak in the last bit of sunlight while having our pre-dinner drinks. I ordered the lamb meatballs for an appetizer (6 for $14) served with a green and delicious yogurt sauce. I also had the scallop entree ($26). The scallops were cooked perfectly but the potatoes and purée that accompanied it was bland and unremarkable. Our service was slow given the limited number of dinners on a Tuesday night.

Title: A Memorable French Culinary Experience at DB Bistro Moderne

My first venture to DB Bistro Moderne during Restaurant Week, prompted by glowing testimonials of their French offerings, was a delight. Scoring the food at a praiseworthy 4 out of 5, we began with the Pate Campagne and Alsatian Tarte Flambee. The pate, presented on a rustic wooden board with a variety of accompaniments and fresh bread, was a standout. The tarte, albeit tasty, didn't quite live up to the hype, presenting itself as an upscale version of a bacon, onion, and cheese flatbread.

The highlight was undeniably the main courses; both the Steak Frites and the Roasted Duck Breast were exemplary in their cookery and artful in presentation, leaving absolutely no room for complaint. Dessert brought us the Butterscotch Pot de Creme and a luscious Black Forest Bombe, and to our surprise and delight, for the birthday celebration, a complimentary serving of Madeleines was a sweet touch.

Service received a solid 4 out of 5. An initial slow start with placing our order was quickly overshadowed by attentive check-ins ensuring our dining experience was nothing short of superb.

In conclusion, DB Bistro Moderne is a gem for those seeking an intimate French dining experience. From the charming red-walled ambiance to the close-quartered tables, it's an ideal backdrop for a first date or a special occasion. I highly endorse a return to this enchanting spot.

Best Chinese food you will EVER taste. Everything is made fresh to order and their crunchy noodles are delicious. The place itself has a very cool appearance . It's a small restaurant in China town that you access by going underground. It's always packed because it's the bomb, obviously. They also have dollars signed by customers layering the wall which looks awesome!As far as the food goes, you can't go wrong. You will NEVER eat Chinese food anywhere else because the quality of the meat used is incomparable!!!!

Title: Cozy Spot Packs a Flavorful Punch – A Happy Hour Delight

Upon first glance, the snug quarters of this bustling eatery may be disarming, but don't let the tight space deter you. Once settled, the staff navigates the cozy room with a seamless dance, allowing guests to move comfortably.

We kicked off with happy hour specials, a decision that proved both economical and delicious. The pork and beef sliders were reminiscent of Cuban sandwiches with a tostone twist – an absolute must-try. The accompanying sauces elevated each dish, from the empanadas to the yucca fries, and even the more adventurous pigs ears and oxtail croquets.

The entrée selection continued to impress, with the spiced goat neck and the glazed salmon on cauliflower rice standing out, both bursting with flavor. The Cuban fried rice and the five-spice skirt steak were equally memorable, ensuring that there's no wrong choice on this menu.

Special shoutout to Justin – his impeccable service and warm personality only enhanced our dining experience. Affordable prices for the quality received makes this spot a gem worth returning to. Just a heads up, the restrooms aren't the highlight here, but that's a minor footnote when the food shines so brightly.
If Joe's pizza were a person I think I'd marry them! Mouth is watering thinking about the plain slice right now.. Limited seating indoor, you can eat it in the small park across the street

I've been wanting to go here since I've seen it reviewed in YouTube videos. I love Soul Food, so getting to check out this iconic place in Harlem was one of the biggest highlights of my trip to NY. We were seated right away. I loved the vibe of the restaurant- it felt very homey. The staff also treats you like you're family, which was very wholesome. Our waitress' name is Tyra, I believe. She was absolutely lovely. I was a little hesitant about the cornbread since I'm not the biggest cornbread fan. Well, now I've converted. Sylvia's has the best cornbread I've ever tried & tastes so good with the butter!! I ordered the Sylvia's Down Home Fried chicken. I appreciate that it was super packed with flavor, but wasn't really greasy at all. I got two sides with it: garlic mashed potatoes and the baked macaroni & cheese. The garlic mashed potatoes had a lot of garlic flavor to it. I personally love garlic, so this was a huge plus to me! However, for those that like the garlic flavor but don't want it to be overpowering? You may not want this side dish then. The macaroni & cheese was divine. The price point is so worth it. You get a lot of food for what you're paying for. The friends I was with were saying they don't think they're able to finish their plate. Uh... I didn't have that problem. My mouth was a vacuum cleaner and I cleaned that plate SO fast. It's so sad I live on the West Coast. I don't know when's the next time I'll be back at Sylvia's, but I hope it'll be sometime in 2020.

I liked this better closer to when it first opened but it's still awesome to grab a quick roll when you're hungry and don't feel like sitting down for a proper meal.  I definitely recommend ordering some of the sauces too - the green cilantro one is my favorite.

Title: Potential Unmet at New Brunch Haven

I ventured into this stylish new brunch spot, eager for the lush Tulum-esque ambiance I'd glimpsed on Instagram, and I wasn't disappointed by the decor or the warm welcome. Regrettably, the initial impressions didn't translate into the dining experience for my party and me.

The prompt seating and pleasant staff set a high bar, but the service faltered soon after. Our appetizers, though visually appealing, were slow to arrive, and the refusal to accommodate egg whites stirred concerns about the freshness of their eggs. Our drinks, while exquisite, were a lonely highlight as we weathered long waits for our entrees. 

When our food did trickle out erratically—cold, underwhelming, and in one case, inedible—it was a letdown. The management's response was commendable, acknowledging the kitchen delays and trying to make amends. Yet, this goodwill was marred when we discovered erroneous charges on our bill, which included items meant as compensatory gestures.

While the restaurant is fresh on the scene and likely ironing out operational kinks, a three-hour brunch with a mix of hits and misses doesn't inspire an immediate return. I might give them another chance for a casual drink when the summer sun beckons, but I'll be holding off on a full meal until I hear of improvements.

Title: A Dim Sum Dilemma at Jing Fong

Jing Fong is a classic choice for a dim sum aficionado like myself, especially on Sundays. It epitomizes the dim sum experience, complete with the thrilling escalator entrance, the palatial dining hall filled with eager patrons, and the customary crowd of the hungry waiting their turn.

The spread here is exceptional; from the perfectly pleated har gao to the succulent siu mai, every item on their menu is worthy of a five-star rating. The shrimp balls are possibly the best in New York City, the pork ribs are mouthwatering, and the fried pork dumplings are a crave-worthy crunch.

However, there's a catch that leaves me both cold and disheartened - quite literally, the temperature of the food. Imagine the disappointment of biting into what should be a steamy shrimp ball, only to find it has cooled down to room temperature. It consistently falls short of the warmth you crave in comfort food.

Despite this setback, Jing Fong will see me again. Its culinary draws are too powerful to ignore. Yet, with each visit, I hold onto the hope that maybe, just maybe, the next bite will be as warm as the environment it's served in.

Best pizza around hands down! They constantly have a line around the block of both locals and tourists trying to get themselves a slice of that goodness. They have pizza by the slice ready to order or by the pie. I shared a pepperoni and cheese pie with the family and we couldn't get enough. The slices are huge, cheesy, and delicious. They have mostly the basics when it comes to pizza toppings, if you want a customized pizza I recommend calling ahead of time to bypass the long lines and wait times. The place is very small so most people just put some garlic powder and pepper flakes on their pizza and bounce. Weirdly enough, I found myself just standing around outside eating my slice amongst other people doing the same, and we all kind of bonded over how great the pizza was. Fun tip, I recommend looking around inside at all the pictures of celebrities that frequent this place, apparently this place was featured in one of the older spiderman movies! If you really want the authentic NY pizza experience, go to Joe's!

Title: A Nostalgic Haven for Grilled Cheese Lovers

Review:

If you're in pursuit of the ultimate adult spin on a childhood classic, look no further than this quaint counter service gem. Specializing exclusively in grilled cheese and soup, with a succinct selection of drinks, this spot boasts a comforting, unpretentious vibe. The menu, brimming with various grilled cheese combos, might make it hard to choose, but you can't go wrong with the original – it's pure nostalgia on a plate. 

I make it a tradition to visit every National Grilled Cheese Day and it's a must-stop with friends when in the area. Even friends from out of town have been charmed by its offerings. But the crowning glory? Their stock of Doc's hard cider. It's a taste of home for me, and its presence on the menu seals the deal – this place is a repeat visit, no questions asked.

Title: A Mixed Take-Out Experience During Challenging Times

As someone who cherishes the dining-in experience, turning to take-out amidst the pandemic felt like a last straw. However, when my usual Thai haunts were closed, I found myself placing an order at this establishment, hoping for the best.

The service was swift; our meal was ready in under the anticipated 20 minutes, and thankfully, it remained warm as we took it back to our hotel. The drunk man noodles, priced at $12, were the highlight - flavorful and satisfying, though I would have preferred a bit more chicken and vegetables intertwined with the noodles. Our special request for a non-spicy dish was met with compliance, which was appreciated.

Regrettably, the $16 shrimp pad thai was a letdown. It was as if the noodles drowned everything else out - sprouts, peanuts, and especially the shrimp, which were limited to a meager five. The sauce lacked depth and richness, resulting in a bland, uninspiring dish that fell short of my expectations for a beloved comfort food.

In summary, the drunken noodles earned a decent 3.5 stars. However, the pad thai's failure to deliver makes it hard to justify a return visit, earning a mere 1 star for its lack of value and taste.

Title: Quick Lunch with Generous Portions, But Service Falls Short

I recently visited a local diner, conveniently situated near my job, for a quick lunch with a friend. The standout feature here is the generous portion sizes. However, the service left something to be desired; it was a slow process to both place our order and receive our check, which ate into our limited lunch hour.

My meal, the chopped steak with cheese paired with a surprisingly large salad, was hearty – although the steak leaned towards the overdone side, detracting from its potential. My friend's bagel with lox and cream cheese was ample and satisfying, with decent quality lox.

Despite the value in terms of food quantity, the lacklustre service was a noticeable drawback. The diner could benefit from more attentive staff to truly make the lunch rush a seamless experience.

Upon being captivated by photos of their vivid blue rice, I knew I needed to experience this culinary curiosity firsthand. The Nasi Kerabu with Fried Chicken caught my eye, and it did not disappoint. While there were slight variations from the menu description, the delightful addition of sweet fried anchovies more than made up for it. The blue rice was faintly sweet, reminiscent of sticky rice, and beautifully complemented the crisp, savory fried chicken. A side of satay sauce added a nice depth of flavor. The salted egg, often a risky endeavor, hit a surprisingly enjoyable note—not too overwhelming in its salinity. Priced at $19, the dish surpassed my expectations with its well-balanced flavors and textures. The Nasi Kerabu is a standout dish that warrants a taste.

Tucked away in a cozy nook of the city lies a quaint hole-in-the-wall eatery that may deceive you with its size but certainly not with its flavors. With just 2-3 tables available, it's clear that the focus here is on the food, not the frills. Opting in through MealPal, I tried their beef noodle soup—a hearty portion that didn't skimp on the essentials. Tender beef mingled with fresh cilantro, a medley of veggies, and just the right amount of chili oil to add a kick, all swimming in a savory broth with delicate rice noodles. It was a satisfying bowl with a profoundly good flavor that promised warmth and comfort with every spoonful. A hidden gem for soup lovers and a reminder that sometimes, the best tastes come from the most unexpected places.

Went for a farewell get together for a departing coworker. Nice place. Good beers for the happy hour, which runs from noon to 7pm. The fries were good, with a mayo and vinegar dipping sauce. The Mac and cheese were cheesy and delicious. This was my first time here since it changed name a year or two ago. Will return for lunch.

Chick'nCone is a delicious concept, and I think it will translate well to other areas as the brand expands.Located in the Underground Market, this place is awesome and relatively affordable. My first Chick'nCone experience was actually in Bryant Park during the summer, and again at the Winter Market there. It's a nice treat and extremely easy to eat on the go. The fries are good, though the real winner here are the awesome cones with a variety of flavors (my preference is the buffalo bleu cheese one). Service here has always been great, and ordering is easy as can be. While there isn't a ton of seating near here, you can still snag a seat if you time it right.I wish Chick'nCone much success in their franchising efforts. The restaurant industry is a tough business, though with this unique and high-quality product (that is very IG-friendly too!), I think they'll make it.Overall: 4.5 stars----Pros:- Excellent chicken, good fries.- Pricing is fair for NYC.- Great service.Cons:- Shame there isn't more seating, though they can't help their location.- Portions could be bigger for the price.

Not sure why the reviews are so low on this place!Came for a casual dinner with my boyfriend and when I say it was quick, I mean it! Without reservations, we were seated, ordered and ate our food within an hour. JG Melon's is definitely no frills and super cheap but the quality is great, better than you pay for. We ordered their bacon cheeseburgers and chips. Meat was juicy and well seasoned, bacon was super crispy, and the burger stayed together through the whole meal. The chips were also good, nice and crispy outside with a super soft center. Pretty decent beer selection and service was attentive without ever feeling rushed.

They have really nice poke bowls to go. It's all build your own. You can get zucchini noodles, white or brown rice as a base. Protein and veggies. Everything is quite fresh and the sauces are really nice! I recommend this place for a quick lunch.

My friends and I love coming here for Hot Pot, because it is great for big groups and allows for people with different dietary restrictions/needs to dine together comfortably. I have gone to the LES location before, but this was my first time trying this East Village location. It's a large establishment with a downstairs basement dining area. This particular time, about 10 of us had a big birthday dinner for one of my friends. For birthdays, 99 Favor offers to store your cake until the end of the meal - when they give you a big birthday celebration song and dance that fills the entire room and includes a mascot! Customers usually start by heading over to the sauce bar to make their own sauce. I like to make mine with a few big spoonfuls of peanut butter, sesame oil, a splash of soy sauce, and maybe some ginger. There's a whole bunch of condiments that you can mix and match for your customized sauce. To eat, my friends and I order almost everything on the menu from an assortment of meats to all the vegetables and even some noodles options. I love that you can really customize your meal with your own broth selection and personal pot to cook the food in front of you. Everything comes out pretty much all at once, and it's amazing how much food can actually fit on those tables. You cook everything in your own pot just the way you like it! The staff are all very attentive and quick with refilling items that you want. It's great and a super fun time!

My recent experience at a Japanese restaurant that prides itself on serving high-quality imported eel was underwhelming. Despite assurances of its superior sourcing—Japanese eel versus the more common Chinese varieties—the restaurant's execution fell flat. The customer service was notably disorganized, with inattentive waitstaff and frustrating delays between courses, diminishing the dining experience of what should have been a refined establishment.

The meal, which amounted to $100 per person, lacked the finesse I expected. Although the eel's quality was apparent, its preparation was inconsistent, with uneven grilling diminishing its potential. The soup bore an unpleasant resemblance to instant dashi, and the edamame was subpar compared to what I could prepare at home.

There were a few highlights: the sansho pepper offered a delightful aroma, the smoked daikon skillfully complemented the eel's flavor, and the plum wine jelly dessert presented a refreshing finale. However, these did not justify the expense, particularly given New York City's wealth of exceptional Japanese restaurants.

Quality ingredients are essential, but they cannot mask fundamental flaws in service and culinary execution. For the price, diners deserve more. I hope the restaurant takes customer feedback to heart and rethinks its approach for a more comprehensive and enjoyable dining experience.

Some things were hit or miss but overall I had a great experience here. Started with a watermelon margarita, which was awesome, and Guac and chips, which were great but a little spicy for me. Standouts were the ceviche, pescado taco, and churros for dessert. Carne Assad was also good. Was less excited about the gordita, shrimp tamale and sautéed kale. Service was excellent.

Recently, my family celebrated my grandmother's 90th birthday at a posh French restaurant known for its opulence and popularity amongst Manhattan's fashion-forward elite. The vast space could easily accommodate our party of ten, alongside other large groups, making it evident that this is a place to see and be seen.

Though the pricing at the restaurant could be considered exorbitant, the service was outstanding, complete with an attentive waitstaff and a convenient coat check that added to the upscale experience.

The menu offerings were a hit or miss. We enjoyed the French onion soup – not the finest ever, but certainly satisfying. The escargot, however, fell short, lacking the punch of garlic and seasoning my aunt craved. My family savored their salads and found the roasted duck quite palatable, though the Peking duck was inconsistent, with parts overcooked and dry. Despite this, the mushroom and duck spring rolls served on the side were a delightful contrast with their perfect crunch.

While my sister's boyfriend relished his branzino, the salmon portions were disappointing to my grandfather and brother, both in size and taste, when considering the cost. Shared desserts were passable, and while my cappuccino missed the mark on frothiness, the accompanying piece of chocolate was a charming touch.

In summary, this restaurant offers a glamorous setting with commendable service but lacks the culinary "wow" factor. While I'm not in a hurry to return, I would be willing to give them another chance, if only to enjoy the ambiance and the attentive staff once more.

Title: A Culinary Fusion Delight at Calle Dao

I recently dined at Calle Dao, a Cuban-Chinese gem, for the second time and felt compelled to share my experience. Arriving early on a Thursday evening, my party and I were seated immediately, just in time to catch the tail end of happy hour.

Calle Dao's inviting dinner menu quickly diverted us from the happy hour offerings. The Cuban fried rice peppered with succulent shrimp and the complimentary yucca fries – a treat for checking in – were standout starters. The lechon bao buns and cashew cauliflower continued the parade of flavor, marrying Cuban zest with Chinese flair seamlessly.

The cocktail offerings, robust Mojito and caipirinha, packed a punch, contrasting the often diluted happy hour concoctions found elsewhere. The matcha tres leches was a sweet, innovative finale to our meal.

Service was a highlight, with our waiter being both helpful and humorous, ensuring we were aware of all deals and guiding our culinary journey with excellent suggestions.

Calle Dao is a definite must-visit. The fusion of Cuban and Chinese cuisine is executed brilliantly, offering a dining experience that I'm eager to return to. Highly recommended for its authentic and flavorful dishes, robust drinks, and top-notch service.

Title: A Fun Birthday Meal with a Few Hiccups

Rating: ★★★★☆

My experience at this eatery was a pleasant one despite a rocky start and a couple of oversights. We arrived a tad late for our reservation, which included a note about celebrating a birthday—unfortunately, our server seemed to be uninformed about the occasion. Service initially left us waiting, but our waiter eventually brought a cheerful vibe to our table.

The stars of the night were the special milkshakes—the bananas foster and the peanut butter chocolate were both delectable and generously portioned. As for the main dishes, "The Fat Cat" and "The Pig" were tasty, although my request for a medium-cooked burger was lost in translation—resulting in a well-done patty. Similarly, my desire for extra onion strings and the specifics on the cheese fries (extra crispy and no salt) were not fulfilled, indicating a miscommunication with the kitchen or a slip in order entry.

Despite these snafus, the food arrived quickly and pricing was incredibly fair. Moreover, the restaurant's location is a winner—perfect for groups and ideally situated for an evening out near RadioCity Music Hall. While there's room for improvement, I'd still recommend this spot for its lively atmosphere and fast service.

I really like this spot for lunch time as almost always I'm able to get a booth. Lunch specials are decently sized and priced. I often get their soba noodles lunch special (and they allow you to choose size at same price pt).

So I've been to the Ippudo Westside location (which I loved, I sat at the bar when I went there.) So I was excited to come to this location. Love the vibes and the very transparent/open kitchen. Like the seating arrangements a lot as well. The staff was all super super nice. There was never a moment my water was close to empty. And of course, the ramen is remarkable. Got the Akamaru New York (vegetarian) with corn added and the spicy ball thing added. Again, so so good. Classic amazing ramen. No complaints at all.
