A more modern and hip take on traditional pho restaurants.  The deco and the atmosphere defies traditional sense of 'dirty' authentic pho restaurant.  Upon walking in, the staff greeted me quickly and informed me that they only take cash, which luckily I had at the time.  I ended up ordering the spicy pho broth. Not the best I have ever had, but not the worst.  Though the menu said there is meatballs, I didn't think I had any on mine.  With more negative things to say than the positive, somehow the atmosphere really made me enjoy my visit. I'd love to visit again to try the crazy rich broth, which I thought was a cute pun as well.

We came here for our anniversary. What a lovely treat. We had a great experience and Harrison our waiter was delightful. I have never been to a non tip (or service included) restaurant and it was honestly really nice. We ordered suppli (which is a rice ball type dish), a savory croissant with meat and cheese, and the BEST dish- butternut squash ravioli with browned butter and sage. One note the portions are quite small so if you're really hungry you're going to need to order multiple courses or plates. They were kind and gave us this awesome cake to split as well. I really liked this place and the ambiance.

Title: Mixed Feelings at MamaSushi

Stopped by MamaSushi for takeout after work yesterday and have to say, my wallet didn't appreciate it as much as my taste buds. The menu is overpriced for the portion sizes offered. I tried the Three Amigos roll and shrimp dumplings, both of which tasted pretty good, but didn't quite fill us up – my friend was left wanting more after her meal, the name of which escapes me.

Despite being called MamaSushi, don't expect a traditional sushi chef experience. And while I can't comment on the drink strength, be cautious of spending too much if you're expecting strong libations. I'm willing to give them another shot over the weekend, but I'm not convinced it'll be worth the price tag, especially given their approach to portion control. Check it out, but consider this a heads-up: your stomach and wallet may need to be prepared.

Phenomenal food here. Everything we ordered was rich with flavor. All the dishes are well portioned - the small plates (tapas) and the rice bowls. Here's what we ordered: - Kara-age fried chicken - Japanese-style fried dark meat chicken, lemon slice, homemade spicy mayo- Garlic Beef Steak - 6oz Angus NY Strip steak, cooke rare, crispy rice patty, savory garlic sauce- Nanban don - crispy white meat chicken tempura glazed with a sweet, rich nanban sauce and homemade tartar sauce, topped with sesame seeds, and a pinch of scallion and ginger, served over rice- Una Tama Don - all natural eel, onions, shiitake mushrooms, scallions, and a soft-cooked cage/free egg, simmered in a rich soy sauce broth, served over rice- Plum Sake - Kagatsuru, Kaga Crane, Mildly Sweet delicate fruitness, slightly tart- Kiku Masamume Kimoto - kiku masamune kimoto style - delicate and balanced, Well- rounded, smoothEverything we ordered was exceptional - slap yo' mama - excellent!  Every bite was SO GOOD. i was full halfway through my rice bowl, but i couldn't waste it. I just ended up eating all the chicken and left the rice. I need this again!  I recommend your try this place. The Kiku Masamume sake is the best!  Gota try that.
In and out bite. This place has been here for YEARSSS. Sirlon steak, baked potatoe and cole slaw. Potato wity buttter DAMNN GOODbread with butter DAMNN GOODcole slaw EWI TOO MUCH MAYOK Bye!

Upon visiting XYST, a Mediterranean-inspired eatery, I was immediately taken by the ambition reflected in its menu. The kitchen deserves praise for not settling for the usual vegan-friendly fare, instead opting to adventure beyond the conventional. Each dish I sampled was undoubtedly tasty, yet none managed to evoke that elusive sense of culinary wonder. The overall dining experience was pleasant, with an inviting ambiance and commendable service from the waitstaff. However, while I left satisfied, a lack of truly memorable highlights means I must withhold that perfect rating. XYST stands solidly at four stars, a very good restaurant that stops just shy of exceptional.

Visiting this world-famous eatery is a must for pizza aficionados. Despite the chaotic atmosphere, which seems to be part of its iconic charm, the pizza truly lives up to its reputation. It's an experience you simply have to try at least once.

It is not warm yet and the word isn't really out and this place is already j packed on Fridays.There are some amazing meats to be eaten at this place. However, I think some of the gems you may not run to are the biggest winners.The spicy potatoes are good. Get the sauces on the side.The churros and chocolate are great. If you are gonna get them, you might as well get a dozen and the chocolate. They are not cheap with the sipping sauce. I wish the churros were bigger but they were great.

As a self-professed connoisseur of Mexican cuisine, I'm thrilled to report that Casa Mexicana rises to the occasion, setting a high bar for authenticity and flavor. Their guacamole, prepared right at your table if you wish, bursts with freshness and can be kicked up a notch at your request. The complimentary and endless chips and salsa are a crunchy, salty prelude to the feast ahead.

Moving on to the main course, the enchiladas and burritos satisfy with generous portions and rich taste. However, it's their chicken specialties, like the succulent Chicken Relleno and the hearty Chicken Norteno, that truly steal the show. And don't even get me started on the churros—stuffed with dulce de leche, they are the epitome of a sweet ending.

The sides, often an afterthought, deserve mention here; the rice and beans surpass the average fare, complementing the spicy, savory mains. The ground beef tacos, a classic choice, will not disappoint. The margaritas? Potent and pleasing—enough said.

While the décor is unassuming, the homely "ma and pa" ambience adds a layer of comfort to the dining experience, bolstered by the delightful option of outdoor seating in warmer months.

In short, Casa Mexicana doesn't just serve food; they master the art of Mexican fare with commendable service and a convivial setting. Forget about the unremarkable interior; here, it's all about a culinary journey worth every bite.

Grand Opening Deal: Buy One Get One 50% Off (Drinks and Food!)Anticipate a long wait as their promotion is going strong! There's only one person making the rice rolls, which is why it isn't as efficient as it could be. Two girls making bubble tea, one cashier, and one more to the assembly line of answering questions and packing orders. Normally, this set up is fine, but for a grand opening, not so much!Braised Pork Rice Roll ($4.25): the rice rolls are PACKED - you guessed it - with rice. I watched as the guy shoveled out a gigantic portion of purple rice before flattening it against the seaweed. Meat/veggies filling isn't too generous compared to the rice ratio, but for my braised pork one  I did get about two and a half thinly sliced pieces. The mayo here was a little too sweet for my liking, but overall, it's okay. I have no praise, but also no negative vibes about the not-a-sushirritoShrimp Pork Rice Roll ($4.25): get this one instead! Shrimp was good, and this roll itself is much creamier and overall, tastes better. Reminiscent of onigiriAlso, be prepared to be STUFFED (from the carbs). You'll suffice on just one order, unless you're a "fantong" (rice bucket).

Title: A Letdown of Love: Our Valentine's Day at [Restaurant Name]

My partner and I chose [Restaurant Name] for a special Valentine's Day dinner, but left disheartened by the experience. The unadvertised Prix Fixe menu for Saturday was exorbitantly priced at $160 and failed to impress. We even witnessed a couple walking out upon glancing at the menu—a bad omen for the evening.

The cocktail selection was underwhelming, with options tipping the scales towards cloyingly sweet. Our first course, a burrata dish, was underwhelming in both presentation and taste, lacking the creativity promised on the menu. The second course, a monkfish dish, reminded me of fish sticks and did not live up to the fine dining setting. Our beef Wellington, a classic third course request, arrived overcooked—well past the requested medium rare. The final letdown was a chocolate soufflé that inexplicably tasted watered down.

Service was hit-and-miss. While generally attentive, we encountered a dismissiveness from the staff, including eye rolls at simple water requests. Plates were cleared too hastily, and long wait times both for the entrees and the bill added to our frustration.

The ambiance was a mixed bag. The single rose on each table and the tapers created a romantic setting, yet the wilting bouquet in the upstairs room detracted from the experience. We also questioned the need for a strict reservation policy, given the multiple empty tables that remained throughout our dinner.

Regrettably, our return to [Restaurant Name] was nothing like our first visit nearly two years ago. For a restaurant of such caliber and cost, we expected a flawless evening but were met with disappointment. It seems a different dining destination would have better suited our celebration.

I recently visited this restaurant for lunch and was charmed by its cute and inviting interior. However, I found the prices to be on the higher side. I opted for the 3 roll maki combo priced at $22, which I felt was quite costly considering the small size of the rolls, particularly the scanty portions of rice and eel. Additionally, the salad that accompanied the combo was dressed in a soy sauce-based dressing that I found overly salty, and I couldn't help but miss the zesty punch of a ginger carrot dressing that I hoped for. Sadly, despite the pleasant atmosphere, I feel compelled to look for my sushi fix elsewhere due to the combination of high prices and less than satisfying portions.

Nestled in the bustling East Village, this chic Chinese hotspot stands out with its culinary prowess. The Peking Duck is commendable, boasting just the right crispness in its delightfully thin skin – a must-try for aficionados. Equally impressive are the crispy shrimp, which pack a subtle punch and come generously portioned, their shells perfectly crisped to a munchable delight.

The chicken and jellyfish salad is a palate-cleansing wonder, accompanied by an array of iced teas, with the lychee ginger variety being particularly noteworthy. However, the rose lychee panna cotta disappoints, its unyielding texture falling short of expectations.

Despite this minor misstep, the promise of exploring further offerings – such as the trotters and an array of vegetarian dishes – ensures a return visit is in the cards. Overall, a venue with some hits and room for dessert improvement, but definitely worth visiting for its standout dishes.

Super cute spot. I ordered and took it to go because my son had an appointment. The menu is pretty simple, they have so many mouth watering options for the nuggets as well as a chicken sandwich but my little boy and I stuck with original nuggets. They were juicy, crispy but a little tough for my 5 year old to eat. He wasn't chewing it properly which ultimately led him to not enjoy it. I however, loved the crunchy nuggets. Some were bite sized, some were big, I mean they were just really good. Customer service was amazing with explaining which nuggets were most preferred and popular. I hear Captain crunch nuggets are a hit so I'll have to try it next time. I didn't wait long for my order at all and I was in and out. I will definitely be back to try an assortment of nuggets.

Came here Friday after work for happy hour. Don't know if they had an event but it was super packed. Cocktails are good, pretty expensive for the area to be a glorified pub and not a hotel or boutique restaurant. Finger food like calamari, shiitake, fries pretty regular. I did have to send my calamari back however for being undercooked/soggy. My sister got the sliders, she loved them. I'm giving this place four stars bc I'm accounting for the crowd and possible strain on the kitchen. The staff was cool, very patient given the high energy evening--cocktails were the win. Definitely a go.

Title: A Burger Haven at Breakroom

If you're a burger aficionado, Breakroom is your go-to spot. Their standout offering, the Breakroom burger, is a culinary behemoth. It's a juicy delight packed with succulent pork belly, a crispy onion ring, and all the classic fixings that create a burger masterpiece. Trust me, it's a messy affair, but every bite is worth a little extra napkin use.

While I find the fish tacos to be a bit lackluster, their other taco options are bursting with flavor, making them a decent choice for those looking for variety. But let's talk sides – Breakroom's fries and tater tots are a golden, crispy triumph that perfectly complement any main dish.

Having frequented Breakroom for years, it's a pleasure to consistently recommend their robust burgers and exceptional fries/tots to all. Be ready for a hands-on experience that will leave you both satisfied and looking forward to your next visit.

Due to Ivan Ramen's episode on Chef's Table, there is much hype around his restaurants, and ramen. I'd been wanting to come here for sometime, but after being quoted with a long wait one evening, we planned ahead and obtained a reservation easily via Opentable. When we came in around 6pm on a Sunday evening, the restaurant was about half or three quarters full, with people also lining up and waiting already. We were seated immediately at the bar stools with our reservation. The staff behind the bar greeted us immediately, giving us water and menus right away. We ordered quickly after being seated, with our fried chicken appetizer being served perhaps 20 minutes after we'd ordered. It was titled 'Japanese fried chicken', but I couldn't really identify anything that tasted obviously Japanese. The menu stated that it included togarashi, which added a nice kick, but really could have been any other pepper. The chicken was served with a ranch sauce and was absolutely delicious- crisp on the outside and moist on the inside. Our noodles were served shortly after. My husband got the Tokyo shoyu ramen. He finished his noodles but then said they were average. On the other hand, I relished every bite of my lamb dan dan noodles. They were spicy and full of flavor, that being said, they were also very, very salty. Was very happy with the food, though my husband was not- would recommend and return.

This was certainly an interesting ramen... especially since I went in with low expectations. It's right on union square, so there's obviously a lot of foot traffic here. Still, there's a fair amount of seating in here, and even some single seating options at the counter, which I availed myself to.The have a number of different ramens, and I saw some of the usual suspects such as tantan and black soy sauce? I opted for shio since it's something I haven't had in a long time. Actually, shio ramen is supposed to be salt ramen, but the thing I was severed was very different. I'll admit I didn't really read the menu closely, but this thing was not what I was expecting, though probably in a good way.First of all, this is a chicken broth soup, which is different from what I usually have. Secondly, there were notes of citrus in this soup. I would guess that it was a result of the roasted tomato in the ramen, but they actually tasted kind of lemony, which is not a bad thing. The pork was well cooked (not too fatty, didn't taste frozen) and the noodles had a good amount of chew, though I felt they could have given a little bit more.Overall, kind of surprised, but in a good way.

After seeing the yelp reviews decided to try this new restaurant close to my work place. They have good lunch specials for a great price $10.99, which comes with a starter and entree. We tried tofu Penang curry and Chicken in basil sauce with veggies with rice for entree and spring roll and house special soup for starters. The soup was super bland and wouldn't recommend that, spring rolls were delicious, basil sauce stir fry was amazing and penang curry was okay. The quantity was good for the lunch special and price that they offer. The place is pretty and cozy. I will definitely try other stuff from their menu soon!!

Not all that glitters is gold. Sometimes it can be more valuable, like platinum or diamonds... but not in this case.The two main draws for Thai Villa is for the stunning interior decoration and the cheapass lunch special. $15 in this part of town? Yes please. Other than that, the only other appeal is the serenity of taking a shit in a pimped out bathroom-- which also falls under interior decoration, but still.On both occasions I've come here, the food was rather ordinary and lackluster. Drunken noodles and pad see Ew were ok. I can't really expect everything but I do value food over atmosphere. Other people don't, so take it at your own face value. The person I came with remarks that the spice isn't very spicy... or spicy at all.I'd recommend coming during evening hours, where presentation matters more. But for me that takes away the appeal of an affordable meal.

I recently had the pleasure of attending the grand opening of [Restaurant Name]'s 6th location and it did not disappoint. The unique interior boasted both style and comfort with its spacious design and superb lighting—a feast for the eyes as much as what was to come for the palate.

My husband and I were greeted with a fun spin-the-wheel game which won us some branded swag and a generous $10 meal credit, starting our experience off on an exciting note. We dived into the menu, selecting the 'Bueno Bowl' which combined a juicy Mojo chicken thigh with brown rice, black beans, fresh guacamole, pico de gallo, and a heavenly maple chipotle sauce. The 'Sesame Bowl' was equally impressive, featuring an herbed chicken breast with an accompaniment of brown rice, roasted broccoli, brussels slaw, crunchy panko, all perfectly dressed in a sesame vinaigrette.

But the highlight had to be the Maple Chipotle Smoked Chicken Wings—pure perfection. They were the kind of dish you reminisce about long after the meal is over. Each bite was a mix of sweet, smoky, and a touch of spicy that had us licking our fingers in public, unashamedly so!

The hospitality matched the quality of the food, with staff making us feel welcomed and valued. Overall, this location lived up to the growing reputation of [Restaurant Name], and I am thrilled to have another go-to spot for delicious, satisfying bowls and unbeatable chicken wings. Highly recommend a visit!

Title: Late Night Surprise at Local Eatery

I ventured into this restaurant close to closing time at 9:20 PM on a quiet Tuesday evening. With a limited selection left, my dining experience wasn't ideal, but the staff's exceptional service deserves applause, nudging my review to a solid 4 stars. 

The kitchen had run out of many items, but the team's thoughtfulness shone through when they substituted the sold-out fries with savory rice cakes, kindly adding a few of the remaining fries at no extra charge. Their hospitality didn't end there; we were treated to a complimentary dessert porridge—a warm gesture that sweetened the deal.

Onto the food, the mapo tofu fell short of expectations; it lacked the characteristic spice, tasting more like plain tofu over rice. However, the Dan Dan noodles were a standout, delivering a perfect punch of spice with chewy noodles and a generous helping of meat. The dumplings in chili oil were satisfactory, although some suffered from a flimsy wrapping—perhaps a side effect of the late hour.

The savory pork rice cakes from the dim sum menu didn't impress; their texture hardened quickly, diminishing the enjoyment. The fries, despite being served less than fresh and described as dry, were surprisingly decent, hinting at the potential delight of a freshly served batch.

The dessert soup was a nostalgic touch, reminiscent of my grandmother's cooking. It's a unique warm dessert soup that's certainly worth a try for its homely essence.

In conclusion, while some dishes didn't hit the mark, the experience was salvaged by remarkable staff and a couple of culinary highlights. Eager to return, I'm curious to sample the full array of what this restaurant has to offer—with hopefully a fully stocked menu on my next visit.

First time here and I'm judging it as an outsider. This is place is not the cleanest, not the most luxurious, or the most sophisticated brunch place. But, it does have loving and caring people that work there. I got greeted with a big genuine smile and a welcome, which is already more than a lot of places in NY. I asked about they Challah Toast and was encouraged to get it. I'm all about trying new things so I did. It was super tasty, thick slices of bread soaked in egg wash similar to a French toast but with a much more thicker slice of bread. The coffee was more acidic than normal, tasty but strong and acidic. This by far, is the biggest side of bacon I have ever seen. Usually it's a slice or two, but at Utopia it's a whole stash of thick crispy bacon!

Alright, so not sure if it was just restaurant week or what, but the meal was incredibly disappointing. The good: - Service - Bacon. Could've been a bit crispier though, but not a big deal.  Now for the not so great.... - Sadly, the steak, which is the reason we even went to begin with. We had 4 people in our group. 3 of us ordered the filet mignon cooked medium rare, and I ordered the ribeye, also medium rare. Food came out quick, and all our steaks were cooked differently. My friend and I got our steaks so incredibly rare we couldn't even cut/chew it. My girlfriend's filet was cooked about medium rare, and our other friend got a medium. Attaching photos of the 3 filets so you can see.. We asked the server to have the rare steak recooked, and when it came back out the second time (within a couple minutes), same thing, still rare. We didn't bother asking to have it cooked again. By the end of the meal, half our steaks were still on our plate because it just wasn't edible.- Steak fries were $7 extra, and they came out soggy and brownish as if they were re-fried or left out for awhile...- My girlfriend got the cheesecake for dessert and there was freezer burn in the middle. Again, based on the good reviews, I was expecting much better. I don't know if it was because it's restaurant week and they were slammed, but it just wasn't a good experience. Throughout the night, we saw a few other tables that also had complaints on their food and spoke to the manager ( I assume that's who it was) at the table. With all the other steakhouses in the city, this isn't one that I'll be back to.

Nestled in a cozy nook of the city is this quaint little eatery that I had the pleasure of visiting on a weekday morning around 11 a.m. To my delight, seating was immediate—no waiting required. The menu, to my wallet's contentment, featured reasonable prices.

The standout star for me was the fried chicken dumplings, a dish that I would recommend to any visitor. Among the noodle selection, the pan-fried hand-peeled noodles really hit the spot, especially when paired with beef, adding a robust touch to the dish. While the pan-fried hand-pulled noodles offered a satisfying texture and flavor, I opted for tofu which unfortunately didn't align with my palate. On my next visit, which is already in the works, the tofu would be something I'll pass on. Overall, a worthwhile spot for a casual and delicious meal.

Title: A Cozy Evening at B Squared

Last night's dinner at B Squared was a delightful experience. With reservations made, our table awaited us in an ambiance that was both fresh and cozy, despite the initial challenge of accessing the high tops which turned out to be surprisingly comfortable. The bar stretching along the side added to the charm of the setting.

The shared black kale salad was a standout, boasting fresh leaves and a perfect balance of citrus vinaigrette and Parmesan sprinkles—a dish so good, it left us wanting more. Our main course, the killer bee pizza, was a hit in flavor with its unique combination of chili oil, honey, and sopressata, although the crust's sogginess in the middle detracted from the overall experience.

Paired with a couple of glasses of wine, B Squared offered a relaxed atmosphere ideal for catching up with a friend. The delicious food and pleasant surroundings made for a good evening, despite the pizza's slight letdown.

I could only speak for their famous spicy cumin lamb noodle dish in soup because that's all I've tried here (I've been twice), but I cannot wait to go back to try other dishes! This location is super clean, bright, and more spacious than their East Village spot. I went with my cousin last week and found a seat right away. It was a little after the lunch rush. When you walk in, you order from the person up front. They give you a ticket and you wait until your number is called. Seats lined the walls and there's even an upstairs area. The spicy cumin lamb noodle in soup was delicious! They gave me the regular spicy option and I took a bit out before mixing because I was nervous it would be too spicy. Their hand-pulled noodles were perfectly chewy and soft. You could tell it was freshly made. The broth was flavorful and packed with spices. It definitely cleared my sinuses. There was a good amount of lamb in the soup too. Next time I'm back, I'll try their ox tail noodle soup or pork and their dumplings! My mouth is watering while writing this review.

Following a return to this establishment after several years, my recent visit proved disappointing, casting a shadow on previous experiences. Opting for the 6-course tasting menu, expectations of a delightful culinary journey were met with the harsh reality of dishes tipping heavily on the saltier side. Most notably, the squab was regretfully inedible, a significant letdown for a course with such potential.

The service also left much to be desired, lacking the personalized attention one would anticipate at such a venue. Despite capturing numerous photos of the night, the taste simply failed to match the visual appeal, making the images a stark reminder of the underwhelming flavors.

The conclusion of the evening came with a steep $900 tab that, in hindsight, would have been more wisely spent at the renowned Le Bernidan. The takeaway is clear: high prices and fancy plating do not necessarily equate to quality dining, especially when the essential personal touch and meticulous flavor balance are absent.

During a work visit to New York, I had the opportunity to dine at this charming family-style restaurant for lunch. Although the lunch menu caters to individual servings, I was pleased to find that they were accommodating enough to substitute eggplant in the chicken Parmesan dish that's typically on the menu. The result was a delightful eggplant Parmesan that did not disappoint.

The standout, however, were the baked clams. They were simply delicious, packed with flavor, and the accompanying sauce was a perfect complement to the fresh bread provided. Portion sizes were generous, to say the least; all of us ended up taking half of our meals home.

This restaurant surely warrants a return visit, and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to anyone looking for a hearty and satisfying meal.

I've never ever had a bad experience here. It's been years and I swear they get better and better. It was pouring raining this time but we risked pneumonia for a po'boy ‍Our server Ricardo was the best, most patient, informed, polite guy I've ever had the pleasure of meeting in a New York restaurant. Give this man a raise! We got a catfish po'boy, grits, red beans n rice, and smothered chicken. Excellent presentation, portion and flavor! As always the ambiance was relaxing and Ricardo let us actually enjoy the meal without disturbing us like some servers do.

My friend and I decided to step in while we were walking around the area looking for some food options. We entered at 8 PM on a Thursday night and the place was fairly empty except for one large party. However, the later into the night we were at the restaurant the more filled it became. Service itself was very quick and efficient. As soon as we were seated we received our menu and had our orders taken. I ordered a thai iced tea and my friend and I split a honey pork slider/peanut chicken slider and bowl of kale tonkatu pork ramen. --THAI ICED TEA: Delicious creamy flavor however slightly too sweet for my taste.--HONEY PORK SLIDER: Absolutely delicious! A must get! --PEANUT CHICKEN SLIDER: Not as satisfying as the honey pork slider, the chicken was a little dry but the peanut sauce it was slathered with was nice and had a nice hint of sweetness. The fried wontons that the sliders came with were also a great addition. The size of the sliders were also pretty large so you are getting a good quantity for your money. --KALE TONKATSU PORK RAMEN: The noodles were really good, well cooked and flavorful. I liked the broth as well. The pork was a little dry - I personally like mine with a little more fat which these cuts didn't have. But the veggies helped to add a lot to the noodles as well. The restaurant itself was a little bit dimmer and a bit run down but in a quaint way. All in all, a pretty good joint definitely would like to go back for those honey pork sliders again!

Title: Mixed Feelings at a NY Eatery with Outdoor Appeal

As someone enticed by a beautiful New York day, I ventured to this restaurant, drawn by the promise of outdoor dining. Unfortunately, the experience didn't quite live up to expectations. The absence of a host meant seating oneself, which was the first sign of the casual service approach.

The service, though well-intentioned, was problematic. My server, freshly hired without proper training, struggled to deliver the expected dining experience. While her efforts were commendable given the circumstances, the other staff was less attentive, exemplified by a male server mistakenly delivering another table's order to me, much to the amusement of the neighboring diners.

Cleanliness was also an issue, with depleted condiment bottles, stained napkins, and a concerning hair in my water. As for the venue, the wooden tables were charming yet wobbly, prompting a seat change.

The menu offered some redemption with satisfactory fish tacos, though they required additional seasoning, and a pleasing salmon dish. Reasonable happy hour prices from 4-7pm may entice locals for a quick drink, but only if they're already in the neighborhood.

The establishment has the bones to be something special, particularly with its seating options. However, it desperately needs attention to detail, staff training, and basic maintenance. Here's to hope and potential – may the management take heed.

Yummy lobster roll but I would say it is a bit overpriced compared to other places, especially for the amount that you get. Overall, Cousin's has the vibe of a fast-food place but the quality of the food is pretty high. It wasn't too crazy here on a Saturday evening around dinner-time but the service was a bit slow. I definitely recommend getting the Connecticut Lobster Roll, it is super buttery and the lobster tastes very fresh.

Title: Manhattan Omakase Experience Without the Hefty Price Tag

Looking for a reasonably priced omakase to impress out-of-towners without emptying your wallet? This spot should be on your list. While the flavors here won't completely astonish you, they certainly won't disappoint either. The sushi is fresh, making it a nice experience to claim you've sampled rather than a feast to satiate a hearty appetite. 

The presentation is visually appealing, adding to the upscale vibe. Expect friendly and attentive service throughout your dining experience. 

It's true, you might find the portions on the smaller side, and the cost slightly steep for what's on offer, but considering Manhattan prices, it's a fair deal. Perfect for a light, sophisticated outing, just don't bank on leaving with a full belly.

Title: A Communal Feast at the New Thai Delight

If you've ever relished the flavors at Pure Thai Cookhouse, there's a new Thai restaurant in town by the same brilliant team that's bound to excite your palate. Embracing the joy of communal dining, it's a place you'll want to visit with a companion or more, as the essence of the meal is in the diversity of small plates that beg to be shared.

The ambiance, with its backless bench seating, channels the no-nonsense vibe of an Asian cafeteria. It's a quirky charm that might not be everyone's cup of tea, especially for those averse to such seating, but it does add to the authentic feel—and perhaps encourages quicker turnover as a side effect.

One highlight of their innovative menu is the 'Pick N Mix' option, ideally suited for a group eager to indulge in a variety of flavors. During my visit with three friends, we dove into eight different dishes. Standouts included the nuanced tastes of chayote squash, vibrant asian greens, and rich mackerel—all of which paired exquisitely with rice. While the crab dish fell short of expectations and didn't justify the extra cost, the overall culinary experience was top-notch.

Be mindful, though, the portions lean towards the smaller side. Rice becomes the trusty sidekick to ensure a satisfyingly full belly at the end of this Thai feast.

So disappointed about the haupia I ordered. My office loves the poke and lunch bowls and I was excited to introduce them to haupia which I make all the time and have had all over Hawaii.  I had it at Makana on St. Nicholas and it was not bad.  Fast forward, I order the haupia from the Makana by my office for lunch bit it was nothing more than vanilla pudding with a little bit of toasted coconut on top.  This is nothing like what haupia is supposed to be like.  Considering you poke bowls are pretty decent, this misrepresentation set me back a little and hope they take it off the menu if they don't want/know to make it correct or learn from St. Nicholas or youtube.  It's not hard and you won't disappoint anyone who has their heart set on having this simple Hawaiian dessert.

High-end, fancy fancy Japanese fusion dining in Chelsea, Manhattan with extraordinary interior design (check out the bathroom). Morimoto's is a great place to celebrate a birthday, date, or any get-together with friends, co-workers, family, etc. The menu is very diverse with a lot of options. Of course, the prices are way up there and maybe not worth it for a lot of their sushi. The desserts were amazing, and probably the best part of the meal. There is plenty of seating in the restaurant, bar, and has multiple floors.I celebrated my 18th birthday here for 6 people, and our bill totaled $459.44 including tax + tips.

I stumbled into this restaurant by mistake, aiming for Dons Bogam Green, but the similarity in names took me here instead. It turned out to be a fortunate mishap as the place impressed me with its elegant atmosphere and an eye-catching wine display, although I didn't indulge in the wine myself.

The banchan set the stage with a tasty assortment from kimchi to Chinese broccoli – all fresh and flavorful. I delved into the Kimchi Jeyuk platter, which was a delightful combination of spicy pork and kimchi that paired flawlessly with rice. The Broiled Eel Bbimbap, however, missed the mark for me with its unexpected sourness, despite the perfection of its crispy rice bottom.

In summary, the restaurant provided a great dining experience at a reasonable price. I appreciated its sophisticated decor and the ambient noise level that allowed for easy conversation. Eager to visit its sister restaurant next!

Title: Convenient Location, Average Brunch Experience

I recently visited a restaurant in the theater district for brunch and came away with mixed feelings. The standout dish, eggs in tomato sauce, was quite satisfying. However, it was disappointingly paired with plain, dry toast – a missed opportunity for a more sophisticated side like a toasted baguette.

Their iced coffee was acceptable after some effort, as it lacked the finer touches such as half & half or simple syrup. I had to settle for granulated sugar, which left the coffee less than smooth. Service was adequate, but the lack of attention to the details in their drink options was notable. 

Overall, the experience was decent; I wouldn't recommend it if you're after a memorable meal, but its proximity to the theaters makes it a convenient choice for a quick bite before a show.

Title: A Truffle Delight at Umami

Today's lunch escapade brought me face-to-face with the alluring Truffle Burger at Umami. Just the wafting aroma of truffles from the takeout bag set high expectations, which the burger met with gusto. Opting for additional shiitake mushrooms and pickles, each bite was a savory adventure heightened by the truffle-infused ketchup, though a word of caution for the faint-hearted – their hot sauce packs some serious heat!

Accompanying my burger was the beet salad, a dish that Umami has perfected. The beets were roasted to absolute perfection, embodying the ideal that sweetgreen's raw attempts never quite grasp. Complementing the rich burger, the pickled onions in the salad brought a refreshing zest that completed a near-flawless lunch experience. Umami has undoubtedly mastered the art of balance and flavor.

Title: A Mild Attempt at Mala for Vegetarians

My pursuit of an authentic Mala experience led me to this Chinese vegetarian eatery after finding my favored Mala Project unexpectedly closed. Excited to sample their offerings, I ordered an array of dishes, hoping to find that characteristic Sichuan spice.

Starting with the Kung Pao Style Mixed Veggies at $15.95, the deep-fried vegetables arrived with a decent yet underwhelming sauce, earning a lukewarm reception, particularly from my vegetarian companion. The sauce came on the side, a thoughtful gesture for takeaway orders.

In a bid for heat, I opted for the Dry Pepper Style Tofu, also priced at $15.95, and requested an extra dose of mala. Despite being billed as the spiciest option on the menu, it fell short of delivering the fiery kick I craved, even with additional chile oil provided.

The Vegetable Fried Rice, costing $9.95, was a more satisfying choice, brimming with a vibrant mix of veggies that included corn and peppers, offering a pleasant taste despite not hitting the mala mark.

Though this spot might appeal to those seeking vegetarian Chinese dishes, meat-eaters in search of the authentic mala heat might find it falls short. While there's a possibility that the 'beyond meat' items could offer some consolation, if it's the real mala thrill you're after, you may want to look elsewhere.

Title: Mixed Feelings on a Fusion Rice Bowl

I recently visited a local eatery and tried their beef rice bowl, which was a reasonable experience but didn’t quite hit the mark for me. At $17, including a $2 tip, the portion size was commendable, and the service was friendly.

The bowl came with white rice, beef, pico de gallo, kimchi, and a green sauce. The rice was on the mushier side, lacking the individual grain texture I prefer. Accompanied by a side salad, it was a nice touch, but not enough to make up for the mushy rice.

The beef, possibly brisket, had a stringy texture that made it easy to tear, yet it was tougher than I’d like. The kimchi was a letdown, tasting more like fresh cabbage with a milder spice level than I expected from traditional kimchi.

On the bright side, the pico de gallo was exceptional, and the green sauce added a welcome spicy kick that I thoroughly enjoyed. While I’ve heard positive reviews about their tacos, based on this experience, I might opt to try another stall next time.

Title: A Surprising Start to Our NY Pizza Tour

As a pizza enthusiast, I flew into New York City with high expectations, eager to embark on a pizza tour and discover the legendary New York-style slice. Our first stop, fresh off the train and plane journey, was a chain pizzeria that, while unassuming, set a high standard for the rest of the crawl.

Despite being a chain, the pizza impressed with its perfectly crispy crust and well-balanced tomato sauce. The cheese ratio was spot-on, complementing without overwhelming, and the slice was generously sized. The shop itself was on the smaller side, but that's typical for New York eateries.

Service was quick and efficient; a plain slice was swiftly reheated, emerging from the oven tasting excellent. This unlisted gem surprisingly outshone many of the 'best of' pizza places we later visited, making it into my personal top picks out of the 15-20 spots we tried.

If you find yourself debating where to grab a quick, yet satisfying bite, this place is worth the stop. At the cost of $2.75 to $3.00, it's a minimal investment for a slice that might just redefine your pizza standards.

This was really great. The views live up to the hype, and the food was better (and funkier) than I had initially expected. We came for dinner and started with the scotch snails and wagyu bolognese for apps, did the wagyu coulotte and venison saddle for our mains, then finished with pumpkin crepe brulee and the toasted marshmallow. We enjoyed everything, but the desserts particularly (and surprisingly) stole the show -- both were outstanding, and the marshmallow is a must re-order if it's still on the menu next visit. Overall, a really nice experience, for a not-outrageous price once you consider hospitality included.

Bomb vegan + vegetarian options! Best fast food Indian food in the city by far. Kati Roll has always felt like such an unhealthy option because the bread is so oily (but otherwise great for drunk food). The alternative are the rotis at Taco Mahal, which taste so fresh and are so well made! The lady at the counter was so helpful and recommended 2-3 roti rolls/person. We were so hungry, so my husband and I ended up getting six total (I think two each would have sufficed if we weren't so hungry). They had two veggies of the day which were vegan (bhaigan/eggplant and chana/chickpeas) and two paneer dishes which were vegetarian (saag/spinach and paneer makhni). Our favorites were the vegan dishes, especially the bhaigan! Love the food, the atmosphere, the reasonably priced food ($4/roti), the service, and the plenty of vegetarian friendly options. Will definitely be back!Update--Went here again and they only had one veggie of the day this time. My recommendations are the following: more vegetarian options, more dal in the dal/rice dish (and not to serve it in plastic), and have cheaper options for samosas ($10 samosas is a crime). Still like the place, but there is definitely room for improvement.

Title: Spirited Brunch Experience at [Restaurant Name]

My husband, his coworkers, and I chose [Restaurant Name] for a 3 pm brunch, and it did not disappoint as a first-time experience. Despite our large group, the staff accommodated us swiftly once we were mostly gathered. The service was commendable, with servers continually refreshing our bottomless mimosas and sangria - a delightful touch.

The place offers tableside hookah, so remember to have cash on hand for that. We opted for the pre-fixe menu, which turned out to be a pleasant surprise with a tasty selection. I went for the wings and pernil, both satisfying choices. A slight hiccup occurred when there was a delay in the kitchen, leading to us being somewhat "lit" before the food arrived.

A word to the wise for slow eaters: keep an eye on your plate. My pernil was whisked away by an overzealous busboy in a moment of distraction, but that was the only minor blemish in an otherwise enjoyable visit.

The ambiance was lively, aided by impeccable music selection, and the restrooms were well-kept with an attendant on duty. Also, note that there's a coat check service at the entrance for a nominal fee of $3 cash.

Overall, it was a scene free of tension, with guests appearing relaxed and content. I'd happily recommend [Restaurant Name] for a buoyant brunch experience with good food and an upbeat vibe.

Title: A Rooftop Delight for Drinks and Dessert

My Thursday night at this rooftop gem was a treat focused solely on drinks and dessert. The spacious outdoor setting provided a stunning view, perfect for a serene night under the stars. The Watermelon Semifreddo was a refreshing masterpiece that delighted my palate. Accompanying this was the "Kyle Knall, Y'all" cocktail — a concoction that was as charming and invigorating as its name suggests. The large daybed added a touch of luxury to the experience, offering a comfy spot to unwind and savor the flavors. This place nailed the sweet ending to my day.

This is my go to stop when I'm in NY! It brings me back to my childhood back in Cali! All I can say is, I'm so glad to have a BCD in the east coast! If you are in need of Korean food in NY, this place is a must go to place! I love how it's open late and how spacious it is! Their spicy tofu soup is to die for, I recommend the beef option! They have combo meals, and although it is a bit pricey, you get a lot of meat! I love the fried Mackerel with the spicy tofu soup!!! Every time I go to NY, I will make sure to make this my pit stop!!! I highly recommend this place!

It was a great diner! Although we started off by visiting this place because it was the outside for Seinfeld, we intended on eating there and it was great! They have all day breakfast but lots of great meals available - diner food of course! Lots of regulars at the restaurant and friendly staff. Reasonable prices and fast service! I would recommend taking pictures outside and definitely stopping in for the food. It's only missing 1 star because the waitress did not bring all the components of the breakfast we ordered - she left out the toast. She assumed that I did not want the toast and she said my plate had enough carbs already. How do you eat your eggs then? What do you dip into that yummy yolk? Next time just let me decide if enough carbs or not

I went to Vic's for an office lunch and was pleasantly surprised.  They easily accommodated our large party of about 10 and the service was quite good.  I thought the pricing was a little high for lunch, but when the food came out I realized the portions were quite large. And the food was really good.  Many of my colleagues ordered the grilled chicken and greens and they all loved it.  I ordered the Calabrian Chili crispy chicken and was impressed.  The presentation was interesting, the salad on top of the chicken was good, and the chicken itself had a really nice crispiness and spiciness to it.  I would definitely return to Vic's.

I took my bf here for his birthday recently. Given he and I love Indian food, I looked everywhere for a very good Indian restaurant to take him this year. Its described uniqueness, positive write ups and reviews made me especially curious of this place. It's expensive and more upscale compared to most common Indian restaurants, so it's perfect for those special occasions. Be prepared for Indian cuisine with a tasty contemporary spin.I appreciated the unique approach to their dishes. For dinner, they offer a few different choices; 3 course with accompaniment, 4 course with accompaniment, or chef's tasting. We opted for the 4 course because we wanted to pick and choose off the menu. You can choose any selection off the menu, and it can be any mix of any items. We shared all our dishes, which included in order --Amuse bouche for each of us - Pumpkin soup and kulcha with cheeseAppetizers - Sweet potato shakarkandi and potato sphere chaatMid courses - Phulka with chili pork and sweet pickle ribsMains - Seared scallops, Ghee roast lamb, Spinach kofta, and Chicken malai tikkaAccompaniments - Kulcha with wild mushroom and kulcha with butter chickenInterestingly, we liked our starter dishes more than our mains. We loved the sweet pickle ribs and the appetizers were pretty great. The phulka is like an Indian taco, delicious but not so easy to share as it's just one portion. I would honestly skip the scallops and the chicken malai next time. They were tasty, but I wasn't super fond of them. The ghee roast lamb is a must. The kulcha was a nice accompaniment. It's like a filled pita pocket. The only annoyance was that our kulcha got cold by the time our second course of mains arrived. We were hoping to enjoy the kulcha with our mains, but we waited too long. As for service, our last main dishes were taking some time to arrive. I noticed the service started to slow down as the restaurant filled up. When we arrived, service was definitely more on point. The restaurant was entirely filled up after an hour of arrival. We had different servers come by our table. The only weird thing I noticed is we didn't get a wet towel for the ribs though the table next to us did. As for ambience, the restaurant space is very nice. The seating arrangement was fine. We got a corner table at the very front, and it seemed like the most private seating area. The noise level can get loud depending where you sit. I noticed a line at the door for a table, so I strongly recommend a reservation before coming here.For a birthday occasion, Indian Accent was a nice choice. We both very much enjoyed the food. It's quite different from your typical Indian restaurant. If you're okay spending a bit more, consider Indian Accent for some unique Indian fine dining.

Title: Satisfying Speed and Authentic Italian Flavors in FiDi

I had a delightful experience at this Italian gem in the Financial District. Notably efficient service paired with attentive customer care made our time-constrained lunch an absolute breeze. Despite our rush, the staff managed to serve us promptly, ensuring we wrapped up within two hours – quite the accomplishment during a bustling lunch hour.

The meal started off on the right foot with a complimentary meat and cheese selection, which was a tasty precursor to the main event. Also, the shishito peppers were a hit at our table; just a word of caution, they pack some heat, so keep water within reach if you're spice-sensitive.

The standout for me was the Veal Chop – an exceptionally prepared dish that was both juicy and tender. It's worth noting that the portions are generous; I savored the rest at home and it was equally delicious the next day. This spot is a must-visit for anyone seeking a quick yet sumptuous Italian meal in FiDi.

My husband wanted to try out PhoBar on a Saturday night around 7pm. We only waited around 10 minutes before getting seats at the noodle bar in the back. As a frequent diner in Chinatown who loves the usual good ol' Viet places (New Tu Do!), I thought it would be a lackluster experience with mediocre pho... backed by a spacious, social media worthy decor and friendly staff - instead of the usual grumpy old waiters who scowl at you. BUT! I was impressed. I had the classic beef pho because that's obviously the first taste test that ANY viet place has to pass. The noodles were good in texture and portion, the beef broth promisingly flavorful! My husband thoroughly enjoyed his short rib pho. I had a bite of the short rib and wow, it was really tender, melty. The pork knuckles were also good, but we'll probably skip it next time to make room for more noodles. The food also came pretty quickly and piping hot, like any broth should be.We're going to go back for the crazy rich broth next time. Hoping people won't instagram the cute decor, noodle lifts, etc etc so there won't be long waits ;) But even if there is, Viet food is only a short walk away in Chinatown!

Came here on a monday lunch time and there was no wait!I got their mini lunch set, but don't be fooled by the name, its not "mini" at all, haha! I left feeling quite full and content. The eel over rice is a MUST- it was so good and was a pretty decent amount. The cold soba was amazing too- perfect for the warmer weather outside. Cute, little place for a quick meal!

Perfect place to stop for a quick bite. We ordered breakfast sandwiches which were reasonably priced and prepared quickly. The lady at the counter was super nice and brought our sandwiches to our table when they were ready. I got a bacon egg and cheese on a plain bagel and it definitely met NYC standards in terms of taste and it hit the spot for sure. The only downside was I didn't see a bathroom available for customers, but then again I didn't ask so maybe there was one behind the counter. Either way, we would consider stopping here again and trying out the lunch or dinner menus!

I recently dined at The Quick, a charming Thai restaurant nestled in the Upper East Side, and was thoroughly impressed. While there was a bit of a wait, the convenience of adding myself to the waitlist via Yelp made the process smooth. A word to the wise: ensure your entire party is present—otherwise, they won’t seat you.

The menu had a delightful array of dishes, but the green curry stood out as the star—it's a must-try! Additionally, vegetarians will find themselves well-catered with ample options. I highly recommend The Quick for a taste of Thai that's worth the wait.

Pretty on par with the fast food hand-pulled/hand-ripped noodle restaurants in NYC.The small restaurant is sort of hidden on a quiet street in the FiDi. I think most people probably come upon it when walking to another destination, but don't underestimate this little noodle shop. Like many hand-pulled noodle shops, the menu will look familiar to those who have frequented similar restaurants - noodle soups, hand-ripped noodles, cold noodles, a few rice dishes and small "burgers" or Chinese meat sandwiches, which look like pitas.I ordered the Spicy Beef Hand-Ripped Noodle, medium spice. The great thing about the restaurant was that they offered different spice levels for the dishes. The order was a reasonable size and what really surprised me was the amount of beef cubes in the dish. I loved that with every bite of noodle, I had a fair amount of beef with it. The beef was very tender, well-seasoned and flavorful. Since it was medium spice, the order had a good kick to it, but it was easily bearable for someone like me who loves medium spicy food. My philosophy has always been that too spicy and it'll take away from the dish, but not enough spice will result in lack of flavor. Like the story of Goldilocks and the Three Bears, the medium spice was jussssst right. The noodle was also very good too and when drowned in the spicy oils with cilantro mixed in it was noodle bliss.I have yet to try anything else from Old Xi'an, but it wouldn't surprise me if everything else was just as tasty.

Title: A Zen Culinary Retreat

I recently visited a gem of a restaurant that truly impressed me with its minimalist decor and serene atmosphere. Despite its modest size, the establishment exudes a warm, cozy ambiance. The staff were notably attentive and amiable, ensuring a pleasant dining experience from start to finish.

The highlight of my meal was the chicken tatsuta-age, which was superb - each piece was large, tender, and encased in a delectably crisp coating. The kani ankake udon I ordered was a revelation; it boasted a rich, slightly thickened broth adorned with real crab, while the noodles were uniquely chewy and flatter than typical udon, suggesting a more authentic take on the dish.

Sampling the curry, gyunan, and niku broths, I found each to be comforting and packed with flavor, indicative of the high-quality ingredients the kitchen uses. A word of caution though; the dishes are served piping hot, so be mindful as your eagerness to indulge could lead to an unintended scald, as it did in my case.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a delightful spot that should not be missed. Do yourself a favor and indulge in the culinary delights they offer - your taste buds will thank you.

For those looking to elevate their noodle experience, this is the place to be. The "So Raymen" is an exceptional choice, featuring a veal broth and brisket that could rival dishes found in Michelin-starred establishments. The broth strikes a perfect balance: creamy, buttery, yet carefully seasoned to avoid overpowering saltiness. Complementing the stellar cuisine is the ambiance, featuring dim lighting that sets the mood just right, and staff attention that ensures a memorable dining experience. Highly recommended.

Title: Delightful Dining Experience at Soba-ya

I recently visited Soba-ya for a weekday lunch and was impressed by the swift seating for my party of five amidst the bustling atmosphere. Opting for the seared tuna lunch set, I was treated to a variety of flavors, including succulent tuna paired with delicately flavored rice and a selection of side vegetables, notably tasty asparagus. The accompanying hot udon was slightly softer than preferred but still nestled in a deliciously simple broth.

The lunch menu, diverse with options, highlighted appealing lunch sets ideal for sampling various dishes. A unique sweet starch added an intriguing touch to the ensemble. While the udon's texture was a tad too soft for my liking, it didn't detract from the overall enjoyment of the meal, which was both scrumptious and satisfying.

The serene decor complimented the pleasant ambiance, and the attentive service from our waitress only enhanced our dining experience. Soba-ya proved to be a delightful choice for a sumptuous lunch, and I would gladly recommend it to anyone looking for a gratifying meal in a welcoming setting.

Title: Disappointing Experience at a Highly-Rated Burger Spot

My expectations were high upon visiting this eatery, buoyed by Gotham social's praise of their burger. Unfortunately, the experience was marred from the outset by the unwelcoming demeanour of our hostess and waiter. Their lack of warmth did little to create a hospitable atmosphere.

My wife's Trial by Fire cocktail delivered a robust kick, a highlight in an otherwise lackluster meal. My barreled whiskey, however, was harsh and excessively sweet, betraying the sherry cask's influence.

The steak tartare offered a generous portion but was underwhelming in flavor, lacking any notable zest. The hush puppies were a miss, so salty they were inedible, even with sauce to temper them.

The main disappointment, the burger, fell well below expectations. The stale bun, charred patty, and scant sauce contributed to a subpar dish that wouldn't hold a candle to a simple 5 Guys burger.

Concluding a meal that hovered around the $100 mark, it's safe to say this was a one-time visit. Heeding Ariana Grande's words, "Thank you, next!" sums up my sentiments perfectly.

Joe & Pat's is the East Village outpost of a classic Staten Island pizzeria, slinging pies in the thoughtfully renovated former Lanza's space.Pizzas start at $24 for a 16-inch, which will feed about two given the thinness of the crust. But it's some fine pizza, as in more than fine-- our margherita pie had fresh, if sparingly applied, mozzarella, tomato sauce with real depth, and a thin, crispy crust.There are also a number of pastas, mains, and appetizers, but c'mon, what are you here for? Service was good. Place is well-decorated, including restored murals, and clean. I'd budget about $20 per person post-tax and -tip for just pizza, no drinks or apps. A worthy contender in the pizza wars.

During a recent visit to the Upper East Side, I had the pleasure of indulging in a slice from Williamsburg Pizza, a gem of an establishment that's recently graced the neighborhood. Though I had heard of its origins in its eponymous borough, I was pleasantly surprised to stumble upon one of its branches.

The interior of the pizzeria is modest and sparkling clean, with a handful of tables inviting a quick dine-in experience. The inviting counter staff recommended trying the Sophia Loren slice, a recommendation I am grateful for. Priced at $4.75, this generous slice boasted roasted tomatoes, creamy mozzarella, a hint of garlic, and a sprinkling of fresh basil. A testament to quality, the pizza needed no red sauce to enhance its flavor—the toppings and the feather-light, crispy crust provided a symphony of taste on their own.

Paired with a La Croix, my entire meal came to an economical $6.00, leaving me both satisfied and eager to return. The mushroom truffle slice has already caught my attention for the next visit, and I'm intrigued to see how the original Brooklyn location stacks up.

Williamsburg Pizza delivered one of the most memorable pizza experiences I've had recently, securing me as a fan. Although based on a singular visit and a single slice, Williamsburg Pizza is on track to earn a full five stars in my book upon further exploration of their menu.

DISHES I RECOMMEND:-Wings (Well seasoned and fried)-Chirashi Don (Fresh diced sashimi pieces over rice)-Sesame and Yuzu Sorbet (Save room for desert!)-Kake Udon (Broth was served hot and udon was cooked perfectly)EXTRA INFO:-Tip is included in the bill.-Free street parking after 7pm Mon-Fri.-Reservations are a must, esp for groups of three or more.

Came here for lunch the other day and it was okay. The place was completely empty when I showed up. I picked brown rice and salad for my base, eel and shrimp for my two proteins, and added seaweed salad, mango, cucumber, dried seaweed, pickled ginger, and ponzu sauce. You can add unlimited toppings. The shrimp and eel tasted kind of frozen and stiff, but the rest of the bowl was okay. You get a free drink or ice cream mochi with a Yelp checkin.
Korean comfort food, good fast and price is right! Reminds me of Hongdae. Nice find in Hell's Kitchen!

After a nice run in Central Park I decided to treat myself to a nice meal since it's right across the street. I started with the Pork Belly Buns, 2 small sized (3 bites I'd say) which were very delicious. A large slab of pork nestled inside a pillowy bao bun. The Ssäm sauce was sweet and slightly spicy and a perfect condiment. For the meal I had the Ginger Scallion Noodles. This is a deceptive sized bowl as it looked to be mostly veg and a small amount of noodles but it was deep and there were oodles of noodles. They were perfectly chewy with a variety of bright pickled vegetables with the tastiest mushrooms I've probably ever eaten. Cute spot, nice service.

Title: A Satisfying Spice Fix at Local Hotspot

I ventured into this eatery with a hankering for something spicy, and it hit the spot! Although it was quiet when I arrived on a Saturday noon, patrons steadily began to fill the space, which boasts cleanliness and an inviting open kitchen. 

I went for the dry pot—a suitable choice for summer, unlike its steamy hotpot cousin. At the counter, I picked my ingredients, charged per pound, and opted for the fiery "hot" spice level—adventurers, take note! The medium spicy lamb, served in a soup with hidden veggies, packed quite the punch, signaling even the "medium" is no mild affair.

The menu's standout was the braided pork belly, dripping with flavor, and the dry stir-fried chicken with tri-pepper, which nailed the crispy-yet-juicy balance. The portion sizes were generous; the flavors, robust and just right on the spice scale.

For those on the go, weekday lunch specials and a cafeteria-style setup are available. Plus, they offer delivery with a minimum $15 spend—a boon for nearby workers like me. This will surely be my go-to lunch spot!

The ramen soup is hot, delicious and plentiful !  Very efficient counter service - in and out! I always add a protein - namely pork belly.   Creamy, spicy broth plus whatever they marinade the pork belly with is terrific.  Noodles always perfect.  Amazing.  A full meal for sure!

I'm wholly smitten with this charming eatery, bestowing a well-deserved 4.5 out of 5 stars. The doors open bright and early, catering to breakfast enthusiasts until 4pm - a generous window for those of us who relish a late start. As someone typically skeptical of cream-based pastas, their shrimp pasta is a delightful surprise, striking a perfect balance with its creamy texture and a zesty hint of garlic, complemented by succulent shrimp that simply burst with flavor. Salads are a hit too, with the shrimp salad being a personal recommendation.

The only slight drawbacks are the wait times which can test your patience, and the seating arrangement that feels a bit too cozy. On one occasion, I inadvertently became acquainted with neighboring diners - a testament to the close quarters. Nonetheless, it’s a minor hiccup in an otherwise delightful dining experience.

It's a challenge to review culinary landmarks such as Sylvia's.  Sylvia's has been in operation for over 50 years and has been an important cultural institution in Harlem where luminaries from politics, sports, and the entertainment industry have dined.  In fact, when my party of three dined here on a recent Friday night, our server even boasted, "If you're lucky, you may even see Leo (DiCaprio) here tonight; he's a big fan of the food."Celebrity sightings aside, I found my overall experience at Sylvia's to be sightly above average to include the ambiance, cuisine, and service.Walking into the dining room, you immediately see the pictures on the wall of the famous folks enjoying the down home Southern Fare for which Sylvia's is famous for.   But I'll note that the main dining area is on the "cozy" side which is to say, it's narrow with the tables tightly spaced together and low ceilings.  Honestly, I found the lighting to be a bit too dark, but there is a small patio for al fresco dining, if so desired.I've been wanting to try Sylvia's for a while, only having tasted their canned goods and award wining hot sauces which can be found in supermarkets across the country.  We ordered three combo plates, since our server suggested we'd be able to try their famous fried chicken as well as the ribs.When the food arrived, I found the serving size to be proportionate for three hungry adults who had spent the afternoon exploring the Harlem neighborhood.  The fried chicken was the better of two proteins.  The skin was nice and crispy and the meat was moist and tender underneath.  My only other observation was that other than salt, I didn't really taste any other spices, save for a few hints of black pepper and garlic - but at least the cook on the chicken was good.I was pretty disappointed in the ribs though.  There wasn't really any type bark on the meat as I separated it from the bone, and there was nary any hint of infused smoke flavor.  Sides were good with the tomato corn stew being fantastic.  Complimentary corn bread was also excellent with hearty ground corn present with each bite.I'll detract a star since I found the service through the night to be a bit uneven.  When we checked in for our 5pm reservation, I got into a "mini-argument" with the host since I had to explain a few times that we weren't walk-ins, but had booked the reservations MONTHS in advance, so please don't seat us in the crappy back table next to the bathrooms.  Also, our waitress had an entire section (about 8-10) tables to herself, so we rarely saw her, but thanks to our food runner/busboy, who made sure our water glasses stayed filled and gave us a few rounds of extra cornbread.Is Sylvia's worth the hype and a visit?  Sure.  It's a nostalgic place with a competent kitchen staff, and it's worth stopping in to take selfie's next to the pics on the wall with famous folks (which I observed a few people doing).  I always visit places that have been in operation for over 10 years, since in "restaurant years" - that's a lifetime.  However, my final thought about Sylvia's can be summed by the old adage: "As is the case with most things in life, the reality of a certain event/place RARELY lives up to the hype."

At first while looking at the menu, nothing particularly popped. However, after my friends and I agreed on a strategy to share a couple dishes here then venture into the food hall for more food, we didn't feel pressured to order an entree each.   We started out with the endive salad.  This was surprisingly simple with a few stalks of endives sprinkled with cheese and pomegranate seeds.  I expected a bit more, but it ended up growing on me and finished my portion. Then we shared the octopus with black ink rice and the seafood stew.   The octopus dish came with 3 small octopi on the top over a bed of this lucious, rich, flavorful stewy rice which had pieces of octopus in it as well.  The rice was delicious.   As for the seafood stew, it included a small piece of fish, shrimp, mussels, and potatoes.  Also enjoyed this dish as well.   Couldn't dine without some sangria, which made the Spanish meal complete.The portions are small, but luckily you're at a food hall, so you can continue to eat after your leave.   It's on the pricey side, so you're better off sharing.  Service was super friendly and attentive.

Title: A Midtown Taco Delight

I recently visited a taco spot in Midtown for a lunch outing with coworkers and was thoroughly impressed. The food was served quickly and arrived fresh to our table. The staff was notably attentive and kind, adding to the pleasant dining experience. I highly recommend the kale and potato tacos, as well as the spicy shrimp tacos – both were delicious. Don't miss out on their corn side, which was equally scrumptious. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Exceeded my expectations with the Ramen and environment. While waiting to be seated you are handed a menus and begin the process of customizing your dish. They seat you in individual stalls (with the option to open them if you're with family or friends). You hand the menu to the staff and within minutes your dish is served. Their broth is packed with flavor and Ramen is made fresh to order. They offer a free second serving of the Ramen noodles if you're wanting seconds.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Flex Mussels

I recently visited Flex Mussels with high expectations, only to leave with mixed impressions. Our culinary adventure began with the daily special, lobster mac and cheese, which unfortunately fell flat. Touted to be a flavorful indulgence, it missed the mark with its lack of true lobster essence and an oddly thin and uninspiring mac and cheese. The scant lobster topping, rather than being succulent, was tough and bland.

Moving on to the main event, we shared a Bisque mussel pot. While the broth was nicely flavored with lobster, brandy, tomato, and cream, it seemed unable to infuse the mussels with the same depth of taste. Although the mussels themselves were well-prepared, the skimpy quantity in an oversized pot was disappointing. The accompanying bread, which should have been a delightful dipper, was unfortunately cold and tough.

Inevitably, comparisons were drawn to a recent meal at Waterzooi in Garden City, which had delivered a superior experience at a better value. Despite Flex Mussels' shortcomings on the culinary front, I must commend the atmosphere. The spot exuded a certain charm, great for a cozy date night, although the framework for dining on mussels requires each person to order their own pot for a satisfying entree portion.

Overall, Flex Mussels has potential but didn't quite live up to the hype during my visit, especially when considering the competition.

Title: A Thai Delight for a Mellow Evening

My recent Wednesday evening visit to this Thai gem was marked by tranquility, as the restaurant welcomed us with plenty of open tables at 6pm. My dining companion and I indulged in a variety of dishes, including fried chive cakes and crispy yellow curry, but the stars of our meal were undoubtedly the chicken skewers and the chicken pad see-ew.

The skewers, infused with an aromatic lemongrass seasoning, were a revelation—tender to the point of melting at first bite. They're a must-try for any visitor. Meanwhile, the chicken pad see-ew provided a comforting familiarity, perfectly moist and well-seasoned, though it followed the expected lines of this classic dish.

Remarkably, there were no low points to our dining experience. With its inviting decor and pleasing appetizer selection, this restaurant has etched itself as a top contender for a laid-back date night. In summary, it's a solid establishment where the pros significantly outshine the mere absence of cons.

Recently visited Burger & Lobster's Times Sq/Bryant Park outpost after being a fan of their Chelsea location. The entrancing walkway, adorned with lobster cages and lights, set a charming tone for the evening. Despite lacking a reservation on a bustling Saturday night, we were seated within a mere thirty minutes.

Service was excellent - our server remained attentive throughout. For starters, we indulged in the East Coast oysters and calamari, both accompanied by delightful dips. Although a bit on the pricey side, the oysters didn't disappoint. The highlight was the Seven Samurai lobster roll; it was divine and, with a side of salad and fries, represented great value at $20.

In essence, for a hearty meal that champions both burgers and lobsters, I wholeheartedly recommend this spot.

El Porron is by far the best restaurant in the area. We were craving some light tapas and drinks on Memorial Day and El Porron did not disappoint.Food:* CALAMARES AL AJILLO (CHIPIRONES) - the best dish that we ate! The sauce was fantastic, we almost ordered a second plate. The squid was tender with slices of garlic throughout the dish. I can't tell you enough how much you HAVE to order this dish.* VIERAS CON TOCINO EN SALSA DE ESPÁRRAGOS - sauce to die for, four scallops with a thin crisp layer on top. The scallops were cooked to perfection. Again, I would highly recommend ordering this dish.* PULPO A LA GALLEGA - this was the lightest dish of the three that we ordered. Light as in less flavor (but still tasted great) and less substance. Cooked to perfection, the olive oil and sea salt combination with the octopus was amazing.Drinks:* CAVA SANGRIA (Small pitcher) - perfect for a hot, humid day. The pitcher allowed us both to have 2.5 glasses, full of apple and orange slices. Delicious!The service was impeccable! We're so happy to find a place close to home that has great service, food, and drinks. Thank you!

Title: A Haven for Pho Enthusiasts with a Pricey Twist

If you're seeking an exceptional pho experience, this spot is a culinary gem that keeps me coming back for more. The highlight for me was their unique twist on the traditional dish with a crispy fried breadstick on the side – an absolute delight. The tendon, served as a hefty 3x2 cube, may seem unusual at first glance, but it's a melt-in-your-mouth treat that's hard to pass up.

Though I'm on the fence about the bone marrow – a supplement not typically in my pho order – other diners swear by its ability to enrich the soup's flavor profile. For those with a penchant for boozy sips, the passion fruit rum slushy is refreshing, albeit light on the alcohol.

Admittedly, the prices can be steep, with a fully loaded bowl climbing to a hefty $28. While I may not be ready to splurge on the most premium pho offering, I'm a big fan of the customizable add-ons, making each visit a personalized pho adventure. Despite the price point, this restaurant's inventive take on a Vietnamese classic is worth the occasional indulgence.

Title: A Culinary Delight at the Chef's Counter

Review:

My dining experience here was a standout in 2018. The opportunity to observe Chef Joe and his team up close from the counter added a layer of entertainment to an already exciting 8-course tasting menu.

The meal commenced with homemade tofu complemented by dashi soy and fresh wasabi – a soft, yet firm appetizer that set the stage delightfully. Following was the seared Miyazaki beef sushi with uni, which, despite its inventive approach, fell a bit short for me texture-wise.

The array of dishes like the kombu cured blackfish, though slightly cumbersome to tackle, was balance out by the sumptuous mini yakitori - the chicken oyster being particularly memorable for its tenderness and flavor. A mushrooms and daikon dish served in a vinegar gelee acted as a light palate cleanser.

The Carabineros prawn was a revelation; its robust flavor encouraged a hands-on approach to savor every last bit. The Miyazaki A5 beef, an upgrade at $25, was like luxurious 'meat butter', though the wow factor of the prawn and beef overshadowed the more delicate Hokkaido scallop.

An Inaniwa udon dish with salmon roe and ume tororo stood out with its refreshing, chewy QQ texture, perfectly contrasting the preceding rich courses. The finale, a strawberry ice cream in a sugar-cone sandwich, ended the meal on a light note - much appreciated after the complex flavors that had danced across my palate.

Set within a small, intimate space, this restaurant is an ideal choice for a peaceful, indulgent date night. Even though not every dish hit the mark, the originality and detail in presentation made this experience one to remember.

I came here since it was very conveniently placed next to the subway and that the wait wasn't that bad (I was seated almost immediately during peak dinner time). The service was pretty quick. I really liked both my chicken appetizers. It's just that...I felt like the Volcano Tonkotsu ramen didn't have much taste to it- it was spicy; however, just not flavorful. And it really wasn't worth the price!! The ramen was so expensive ($18)!! I really wanted to like this place because it had so many positive reviews

Title: Impressive Business Lunch at a Cozy Spot

My experience at this restaurant earns a resounding 4.5 stars! From a well-timed seating to a delectable lunch menu, they hit most of the right notes. Despite the less-than-ideal view from our 2-top table facing a wall, the overall ambience was quite inviting.

The business lunch menu was a welcome surprise, offering a variety of options. My client savored their turkey sandwich while my double patty burger was nothing short of perfection, both of us leaving our plates spotless. Accompanying my burger with a side market green salad, I found it fresh albeit slightly too bitter for my taste, but the fries were a crispy delight.

The attentive service, marked by the thoughtful touch of leaving a carafe of water at our table, was much appreciated. A special mention goes to the warm chocolate chip cookies, courtesy of a known manager to my client, which were the proverbial cherry on top.

I wholeheartedly recommend this establishment and eagerly anticipate my next visit!

Love the concept of fusing two of my favorite cuisines into one: Cuban and Chinese. Came here on a Friday night with a reservation at 730pm, restaurant wasn't too packed and we were immediately shown to our tables. We ordered the following: seafood paella and pork char siu, and we got a order of yucca fries complimentary due to checking in on Yelp. Total bill came around $76 tax and tip included. AMBIANCE:This is where I really loved the cute interior design and the retro theme that they were going for. Think perhaps 1920s China marrying Cuban rum bar. Definitely works well. PROS:Seafood paella was delicious! Love the black squid ink that they used, and they cooked it al dente with a slight crunch to its texture. The seafood was very fresh, and the portion size was good. Paella was seasoned very well, with a good ratio between seafood and rice. I also loved the pork char siu we got, as the pork was incredibly tender and melts in your mouth, and it sat on top of a bed of sweet potato puree. That puree was AWESOME.
