Whoever slow cooked that pork to make it that tender deserves to win either a Michelin star or a James Beard award. Would come back just to eat more of that. Yucca fries were great too. Not too sweet and not that starchy compared to just potato or sweet potato fries. Interesting texture and taste, and very unique. We were also given a complimentary basket of shrimp crackers. Those were light and airy and had a good taste, texture, and crunch to it. CONS:Only complaint would be for the seafood paella, I felt like the paella was drizzling in oil and was slightly greasy. OVERALL:Highly recommend to try out a interesting eclectic mix of flavors, and to experience Cuban-Chinese food in its finest at Calle Dao.

I recently dined at a local eatery known for its authentic offerings and left thoroughly impressed. Opting for the small size of the big plate chicken without bones, my friend and I were delighted by the generous portions. The dish boasted perfectly chewy, hand-cut noodles topped with a chicken that carried just the right amount of spice - though a tad salty, it was certainly worth recommending. Complementing our meal was the steamed lamb shumai, an unexpected twist on the traditional, resembling more of a soup dumpling filled with succulent lamb. Lamb lovers take note: the menu brims with options. To our delight, we concluded our satisfactory meal with leftovers in tow, a testament to the ample serving sizes.
We came here on a Sunday afternoon and the wait was around 40 minutes. But I was astounded of how delicious the food was! It makes sense of why there is a wait for every hour. 9/10

I stopped by this NYC joint for a slice and found it to be pretty decent. The crust does tend to edge toward a cracker-like texture after reheating, but the sauce they use is quite flavorful. They could be a bit more generous with the cheese, though. At $3.00 a slice, there are certainly more satisfying options in the city. However, the cleanliness of the place and the friendliness of the staff add points to the overall experience.

Title: A Trendy Escape Above the Bustle of Times Square

Nestled amidst the hustle and bustle of Times Square, this gem of a spot offers not only a refuge for the weary traveler but also a vibrant scene for locals seeking a chic hangout. Claiming space on both the 7th and 8th floors, the restaurant presents an Instagrammer's paradise with its outdoor areas that boast picturesque views of the urban landscape.

Once inside, the 8th-floor indoor bar doesn’t disappoint either, with its stunning aesthetics prompting patrons to admire as much as they imbibe. The cocktail connoisseur will delight in the meticulously crafted drinks, priced at $19, while the non-alcoholic options, at $12, ensure there’s something for everyone. 

The food menu, though on the pricier side, offers satisfying bites such as crispy fried chicken croquettes, a fresh tuna tartare, and shishito peppers that pack a flavorful punch. And for those looking to indulge, the huge DIY sundae is a decadent treat not to be overlooked.

While Irving on Hudson may claim the city's panoramic views, for an all-around high-end culinary experience in the all-too-often touristy Times Square, this spot stands out as a strong contender. Yes, it's a splurge, but for those in search of quality drinks, food, and an ambience to match, it's money well spent.

Title: Mixed Feelings on Champignon's Brunch

My brunch experience at Champignon was a blend of positives and drawbacks. Although my party of six arrived late, the establishment graciously accommodated us, promptly seating us upon arrival—a commendable gesture of service. However, the hospitality faltered with our waitress, who lacked warmth and patience as we perused the menu.

Culinary speaking, the Egg White Wrap and Egg and Cheddar Croissant my friend and I shared were unremarkable. Both dishes missed the mark on flavor and visual appeal, particularly noticeable as the prices were steep for the offering.

The standout feature was the bottomless mimosa deal—$15 for an hour is a steal in NYC and indisputably Champignon's strongest draw. While the overall dining experience left room for improvement, this brunch special could be a redeeming factor for those with a penchant for endless bubbles.

I came here for weekend brunch with a friend and it was packed. We made a reservation in advance so I highly recommend you do that as well.I got the Benedict Johnny and it was sooo delicious! I don't usually like hollandaise sauce but this roasted tomato hollandaise sauce was so good. The sausage, eggs, and cornbread all went together perfectly.I also got a Bellini cocktail but it wasn't that great. I'd go for a different cocktail. I'd definitely come here again for brunch.

Title: Father's Day Feast at a Family-Friendly BBQ Haven

Review:

My family and I visited this BBQ joint on a bustling Father's Day and were quickly accommodated despite our large party of eight. The staff's friendliness and attentiveness shone through the busy atmosphere. We indulged in generous portions of mouthwatering BBQ, with a variety of options that catered to all tastes, from succulent steaks to healthier choices like salmon and an unexpectedly delightful black bean burger. The children had their own menu, simplifying the ordering process for our little ones.

A pleasant surprise was the complimentary red velvet cake, a sweet ending to our meal. Although I would suggest offering complimentary drinks for kids to enhance the family-friendly vibe, this was a minor detail in an otherwise stellar experience. While some of our steak orders took a bit longer to arrive—a reasonable wait considering the crowd and our extensive order—the quality and taste of the food, including the juicy steaks, crispy shrimp, and massive ribs, made up for it.

Overall, our Father's Day outing was a hit, and this spot in the lower east side has secured its place as a repeat destination for our family.

I've been on a Jamaican food kick lately and I must say this is some of the best that I've had again. Everything from the goat, ox-tails, jerked chicken, rice & peas, and plantains were amazing.Staff was great, drinks were amazing, and I will definitely be back again. Environment was great and just overall vibe was dope. Make sure you stop by for this amazing fare. Only setback was they had run out of goat empanadas.They also have a lounge and DJ on the lower floor. They also serve brunch as well.

I recently tried out this restaurant through Mealpal, not initially aware it was part of a franchise. I opted for the pork chashu ramen and was pleased to see the broth and noodles served separately, ensuring everything stayed fresh for my meal. The pork was delicious, and the inclusion of the half egg added a lovely touch to the dish. Authenticity shone through in the flavors, and the staff were welcoming and friendly. This spot has certainly earned a repeat visit from me.

Title: A Serene Feast at Hao Noodle Chelsea

Upon walking into Hao Noodle Chelsea, after marveling at the West Village establishment, I was equally captivated by this location's tranquil vibe, accentuated by the lush greenery. Securing a reservation for three, we were efficiently seated on arrival by our attentive server, Badka.

Navigating the menu could have been a challenge for my gluten-free companions, but Badka’s diligence in consulting the chef ensured a seamless experience. We indulged in a communal chicken and mushroom noodle soup that boasted a rich, savory depth without succumbing to a sodium overload. Accompanying pea shoots and spinach in ginger were a refreshing complement.

I couldn’t resist the sticky rice shu mai – a personal favorite – which also won approval from a friend. Our dinner concluded with the black sesame balls in red bean soup, a delightful sweet note that left us craving just a few more of those irresistible morsels.

Hao Noodle Chelsea truly fits any occasion, from a casual meet-up to a romantic rendezvous. To avoid disappointment on busier evenings, a reservation is prudent. I am already planning my next visit, with daylight hours in mind, to savor my meal amidst the indoor flora. A heartfelt shoutout to Badka for elevating our dining experience – we'll certainly return.

my fave pizza shop, i mean it's sick that it's a block from my apartment of course but helllaaaa variety, super nice staff, sick toppings (love me some toppings obv) and the pizza itself???   B O M B anytime i bring friends or family it becomes their fave spot too, marinara's till i dieeee oh pro tip: vodka sauce slice, spinach artichoke slice, and eggplant slice allllllll the way

Surprisingly lots of chicken and very few rice cakes. We got two portions for three people. The $19-20 price listed on the menu is for one portion!It was weird that there was a strip of cheese down the middle instead of sitting on top of anything like rice or rice cakes. We still really enjoyed it, and it was enough for the three of us to get full. The only other thing I would've wanted is some green veggies like bok choy to balance out how unhealthy this meal is haha

Really great omakase, very fresh ingredients and attentive service. There are two omakase options here and we chose the 14 piece + handroll option. Every piece was executed with precision and every piece of fish tasted fresh and had flavors that complemented it well and did not overpower the taste of the fish. My favorite pieces were the orange clam, sea eel, medium fatty tuna, the tuna handroll that had shiso in it, scallop with uni and the fluke. One of the courses is chawanmushi and it was one of the best chawanmushis I have ever had. The flavors were subtle but the egg was cooked perfectly and you could taste the dashi. Also a plus that the ginger here is some of the best I have had and I had at least four refills throughout my meal - it was that good!The only reason this gets four stars is because the rice could have been flavored a bit more and not as mushy. Also there could be more uses of different flavors to complement the fish. Would highly recommend omakase here and will definitely be back!

My friend and I loved our hotpot experience here. We started off by choosing a combination of three different broths, which included Dalongyi Sichuan style spicy broth in mild (you can choose the spiciness!), mushroom broth, and tomato broth. As I'm not the best at eating spicy food, I appreciated that their pot serves 3 different types of broth so that I could switch back and fourth between the spicy and non-spicy soup. The Sichuan style spicy broth was pretty spicy for us even though we chose mild spiciness. But it was still full of flavors and I definitely recommend getting this as at least one of your soup bases if you're here. I also really liked the mushroom broth that was smooth and clean in contrast to the spicy broth which created a good balance. Then we got pork slices, beef slices, beef sirloin, and spicy beef ribs, which were all high quality and fresh. I also loved the pretty display of each plate! The house special spicy beef ribs were especially delicious when we cooked them in the spicy broth. We also got veggies, shrimp paste, and glass noodle on the side. Their glass noodle was very chewy and yummy that my friends and I finished it at the end of our meal even though we were so full.  Inside the restaurant is aesthetically pleasing and has a great ambiance that can be suitable for casual meals with friends and family as well as small occasions. They have a lot of tables that are spaced out nicely that I think it can be a good spot for big groups. Staffs are attentive and they even provided us a plastic bag to put in our coats before the meal so they don't smell like hot pot, which was very considerate! Overall, I think this is a great Sichuan style hot pot with a reasonable price point. I would definitely come back here again if I'm around the area!

Tucked away in the lively heart of Midtown, just a stone's throw from the hustle of the train station, hotels, and neighboring bars, sits a gem of a Korean-style pub serving up an array of mouth-watering shareable plates. My palate was delighted by an array of delectable choices, from succulent dumplings and tender pork belly to the innovative bulgogi tacos and fluffy bao buns. A special shout-out is owed to the soft-shell crab - a dish not to be missed.

The bulgogi in particular was a standout, marinated and cooked to such perfection that it prompted an encore in taco form. Accompanying these flavors was an inventive soju cocktail, complete with a flavor-packed popsicle-like ice stick – a detail that both amused and added an extra punch to each sip.

As if the food wasn't reason enough to return, the offer of a free soju shot upon checking in was a welcome bonus. Service was impeccable; the attentive staff ensured our glasses were never empty and our needs fully met. The ambiance was just what you'd hope for a night out in Manhattan - laid-back yet vibrant, setting the stage for a delightful evening. This place is a must-visit for anyone looking to kick off their night with great food, drinks, and service.

Ambiance in Little Italy is amazing. Want to take your lady somewhere romantic and delicious. This is one of the places. So many dope spots on Mulberry and the food choices are great.I had the chicken parm with pasta and it was amazing. Everything was fresh and on point and the ingredients were great. The wife had Fetticini with Chicken and Shrimp and it was some of the best I've ever had.Drinks were good, service was great, and the pricing was on point. I will definitely be back. If the weather is nice, sit outside on the street at one of those tables. The calamari appetizer could've used a little more flavor, but it was cool. Just a little more splash of seasoning will help it.

I absolutely adore this restaurant. I've been here on several occasions and the food is pretty good and the decor is cute! Tuna tartare: so light and fresh. Delicious. Steak tartare: one of my favorites here! Salmon: I'm very picky and they cook it perfectly here. Skin is usually crispy and the fish is cooked slightly under, just the way I want it. Scallop: delicious as well. Gnocchi: it's light but not my favorite Frog legs: delicious! Not greasy. French fries: hit and miss. Sometimes crisp, sometimes a bit soft. Octopus: this is divine! The cook is crisp and the meat is tender. Hummus: their hummus is different from a traditional version. I like it Green beans: nice side Dessert:Creme brûlée: gooood! Soufflé: hit and miss. One time is was so good, the other time a bit dry. Tiramisu: skip.

Was easily able to make a reservation for 7 on a Sunday evening. The restaurant was quiet and would be perfect for a date night. Food is very reasonably priced, as well as the wine. We enjoyed the steak, short ribs, and salmon. Service was great.

Some of the best Georgian food I've had in NYC so far. I came with a group of 8 and they knew how to handle a large party - service was great. I tried:+ Imeruli+ Hachapuri+ Lamb dumplings+ Beef dumplings+ ideali (Walnut cake)Every dish was delicious, with the standouts being the cheeseboat and lamb dumplings. Dessert was also unexpectedly good. I'd say Oda House is better than Old Tbilisi Garden and on par with Cheeseboat in Williamsburg. 4.5 stars!

Out of the fifty-somethng places on my Yelp list, this has been on here the longest. Finally I made the trek down to Chinatown get the fampusn char siu fan! It was as delicious as I thought it was going to be. The char on the pork is making, fatty, but not chewy and over the fluffiest white rice. For 4.25 you can't beat it!

Title: A Slice of Authenticity at Rubirosa, Little Italy

If you're skeptical about Italian fare in Manhattan's Little Italy, let Rubirosa on Mulberry Street change your mind. Its unassuming exterior belies a surprisingly spacious interior with a cozy bar up front and a lighter, more open dining space towards the back, offering an inviting atmosphere that shifts from rustic to airy as you move through.

An unplanned visit after running errands in SoHo proved to be serendipitous, with a manageable 30-40 minute wait for a table, mitigated by a handy text notification service. The menu is a straightforward homage to Italian classics, with their renowned pizzas and pastas front and center. Opting for pizza, we started with the mini rice balls—tasty, if not remarkable, served with a zesty spicy marinara.

The pizza is the heart of Rubirosa. The half-and-half option is a blessing for the indecisive; we chose arugula and tye-dye. The former boasted generous parmesan shavings, and the latter, a harmonious blend of pesto and marinara, both atop a delightfully thin, cracker-like crust that made each bite intriguing.

Service was attentive and efficient, a feat considering the bustling environment. Rubirosa's pizza easily justifies its reputation. I'm eager to return, not only for another pizza fix but to dive into their handmade pastas. Rubirosa is a definite must-visit for an authentic Italian experience in the heart of the city.

I had read about this place online since they get their eels shipped from Japan every Tuesday and Friday.  I came here for dinner on a Tuesday night with a friend.  The place was very Japanese in terms of decor and seating.  We shared the uni gomatofu (sesame tofu) appetizer and the large (1.5 eels).  The eel over rice entrées come with miso soup and pickles.  They were nice enough to provide two miso soups.  The eel was grilled and glazed perfectly.  Their tare sauce was delicious.  Service was very attentive.  They constantly refilled our water and green tea.  It's a bit pricey but the quality was up to par and it's just like the unaju places I've been to in Japan.  I would come back if I'm ever in the mood for unadon.

During happy hour the place can fill up pretty quick so try to get there ASAP. Happy hour is until 6pm. The drinks are a good deal during HH. The tacos are relatively big and filling. It's one taco per order. I didn't really like their crispy fish taco because of the batter they used for the fish. The shrimp taco was okay. The guacamole was good! A good place to stop in for lunch or for a bite/drink after work. A lot of high top seats, bar seating, and a take out counter too. The atmosphere is casual and the employees are all friendly! Not a good place for a large group but to catch up with one or two friends it's a good spot.

I recently visited Manting, a place that touts its dry stir-fried Málà style hot pot. Regrettably, I'd have to categorize their attempt as underwhelming. The pricing didn't leave a particularly strong impression—not too steep, but the food quality didn't live up to expectations either.

One of the main issues seems rooted in the cooking technique. Unlike other establishments that typically blanch ingredients before stir-frying, Manting opts to deep fry, which doesn't do the dishes any favors. This was most apparent with the lotus root, which appeared shriveled and tasted overly fried, taking away from the essence of a hot pot dish.

In short, while the concept is promising, Manting's execution falls short. The food quality beckons for improvement, and a revisit to their cooking method might be imperative to align with the traditional and expected flavors of a Málà hot pot.

Title: A Mixed Experience at AnTalia NYC

My wife and I recently dined at AnTalia NYC, a Turkish restaurant known for its excellent cuisine. We indulged in the cupra dorado and the salmon kebab, both of which were marvels of flavor. The dorado was perfectly cooked and accompanied by fresh mixed greens, while the salmon offered a twist, wrapped in grapevine leaves.

I particularly suggest giving the meze platter a try, as well as pairing your meal with their Turkish red wine, which stands as a testament to the restaurant's quality selection.

However, our visit was not without its issues. The service we received upon arrival was unwelcome; a request for a preferred seating was denied with a somewhat unreasonable explanation, leading to a disappointing start. Despite the restaurant being quiet, the table we chose was "reserved" for a larger party—which, to our observation, never materialized. This inconsistency in seating policy was frustrating, particularly as we noticed others were offered more flexible seating options.

Fortunately, the kindness of another waitress, who noticed our dissatisfaction, salvaged the evening. Her generous offering of a complimentary Turkish custard, which I highly recommend, and her attentive service means I would consider returning—especially for her hospitality.

I give AnTalia NYC three stars, with a caveat: watch out for the service, particularly from the waiter with the ponytail. The food is worth the visit, but the seating policy could use some improvement.

Mar at Mercado Little Spain came with high expectations, considering its pedigree from culinary giants José Andrés and the Adrià brothers. Regrettably, my experience fell short of the anticipated Spanish culinary delight. The ambiance pays homage to the sea, fitting for a spot nestled in a bustling food market, yet the inevitable food court feel persists.

Service was top-notch; my server's wine recommendation was a highlight and managerial presence was attentive and engaging. However, service could not eclipse the underwhelming gastronomy. The bread, admittedly, was impeccable—crispy yet soft—ideal for sauce-dipping.

Classic tapas like Gambas al Ajillo ($20) and Pulpo a la Gallega ($22) were presented, but at a premium far exceeding their Spanish counterparts, without the quality to match. The gambas, a garlic shrimp staple, arrived overcooked and scant, compromised by a slightly burnt sauce. The pulpo, while tender, lacked the culinary finesse expected, and the potatoes beneath seemed underdone and underseasoned.

A hesitant dessert choice, Tocino de Cielo ($9), confirmed my reservations; its texture teetering towards rubbery, with a caramel flavor that missed the mark.

After an $84 tab, I'm left with little desire for a return visit. In search of that elusive Spanish flavor, I'll turn to the rest of Mercado Little Spain's offerings with hopes of a more transportive experience.

I didn't realize until now this is their second location here in NY.  My son had an audition at Third Street Music Settlement two blocks away and we wanted somewhere close by to eat.  We got here at around 11am and while it was busy inside, we were seated right away.  While the menu is not expansive, we all ordered dishes that were just scrumptious.  I got the big breakfast which came with 2 eggs, 2 slices of bacon, hearty hash brown, baked beans, argula, baby tomatoes, mushroom and toasted bread.  Wow for $16, that is a steal.  Everything just worked to perfection and tasted great.  I also got a cup of coffee for 3.50 and if you want a refill, it's 1.50 more.  My son got the banana bread which he finished to the last lick and got some truffle fries.  Those fries were made to perfection.  My wife got the whaley burger with a upcharge for gluten free bun.  This was the first time she had a burger whereby there were beets inside.  She liked it although it wasn't out of this world.  All in all, great food and attentive service.  We would definitely come back.

Title: A Toast to Refined Leisure at Union Square's Culinary Gem

Review:

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a gem within the Union Square Hospitality group, thanks to a generous gift card from my manager. On a serene Monday evening, the bar exuded class without the clamor of a crowd. The bartenders impressed with their vigilant service, ensuring our glasses remained full and our appetites promptly attended to—with the bonus of gratuity included in the pricing.

For $100, two of us savored a delicious meal paired with three artfully crafted drinks. While the menu featured small, sharable plates, the portions were satisfying. The standout for me was the exquisite focaccia with tomatoes and stracciatella—a testament to the sublime simplicity of quality ingredients. The bread, toasted to perfection, showcased a flawless balance of sea salt and olive oil, prompting us to indulge in a second serving.

The fried artichokes were a revelation, their crispiness making them an instant favorite. The special of the day, Branzino, was another triumph—moist, flaky, and crowned with delectably crispy skin. The seafood misto delighted with its light breading and perfect pinch of salt.

Though the bar is known for its wine selection, the cocktails stole the show. The Ciao Mela was a sweet yet potent concoction, while the Sicilian Sweetheart married almond notes with a delightful bitter-citrus twist—easily the best cocktail I've enjoyed in recent memory.

The venue boasts not only this refined bar but also an Italian restaurant, a pizzeria, a hotel bar, and a cafe—all under the same esteemed hospitality umbrella. Whether for clients or a date night, this spot promises an elevated experience. I eagerly anticipate my return for more stracciatella-laden bread and sophisticated sips. A resounding A+++++ for a truly enchanting evening.

During my lunch visit to this unassuming gem, I was pleasantly surprised by the generous portion sizes and the impressive quality of the meal at such an affordable price. At just $8, I received a heaping plate loaded with flavorful rice, fresh veggies, and a substantial serving of delicious ginger chicken that was both boneless and satisfying. What's more, the restaurant offers a thoughtful touch with a large silver tray and a cup for self-service water, which is a nice alternative to purchasing a drink. The clientele, predominantly cabbies and pedicab drivers with an East Indian background, seemed to be regulars – a testament to the authenticity and appeal of the place. It's worth noting that the portion was ample enough to potentially satisfy two appetites. This spot is definitely worth the visit for anyone looking for hearty and tasty fare at a steal.

I tried this poke spot after seeing it on Ritual, as they had a $1 deal for their "spicy tuna nachos". I placed an order and asked for regular tuna, without spicy mayo as well because I'm not a fan of the sauce. When I come into the store, I ask for my order and they tell me that they can't provide me with "regular tuna" instead of "spicy tuna" because the nachos are premade.... Instead, I had to choose with going with either spicy tuna or avocado nachos.The nachos were also straight out of a 99 cent bag (haha!) I'm so glad that I didn't spend actual money on this place.

Took a while to finally get to Au Cheval Diner, but snuck in on a Resy solo reservation on a Monday.  When I was in Chicago in November, the original spot was certainly on my to-do list, but the wait was just way too long so we went to their fast-casual spot, Small Cheval. Still, I felt like I missed out. Enter Au Cheval Diner. A bit difficult to find, tucked in Cortlandt Alley, it's a pretty happening spot. Casual diner feel meets sophisticated menu. Delightful.So, after all the hubbub naturally, I went for the burger. As other reviews have noted, the 'single' features two patties, while the 'double' adds a third. You can a fried egg (apparently what their known for) as well as thick cut bacon. A opted for the single with all the fixings.The burger was cooked well - for the patties being on the slimmer/fast food side, they were still rather juicy. As some other reviews touched on, it was a bit over-salted. That aside, still a delicious (albeit slightly expensive when dressed up) burger - and the peppered thick cut bacon was delightful. Au Cheval aside boosts pretty impressive craft beer list, as well as hand-crafted cocktails. Good times will be had here.Good burger (home of the)? Yes. Best burger ever...less certain. That said, I definitely want to come back for the roast marrow bones and the foie gras scrambled eggs.Welcome to New York, Au Cheval.

During The Infatuation's EEEEEATCON festival in October 2018, I had the pleasure of sampling Roberta's celebrated pizza. While typically not a fan of this pizza style, the Bee Sting truly captivated my taste buds. The harmonious blend of sweet honey, rich tomato sauce, smoky sopressata, and a kick of heat from red pepper and chili oil was a delightful surprise. My advice for future diners: round up some friends, order a selection of pizzas to share, but be certain the Bee Sting is on your table – it's an absolute must-try.

My partner and I had a fabulous date night at this restaurant on a peaceful Monday evening. The atmosphere struck the perfect balance of class and taste, creating a welcoming and upscale vibe. Our dining experience was highlighted by a delectable feast – particularly the roasted mushroom, the perfectly cooked hanger steak, and the sublime olive oil cake, all of which I highly recommend. The sides, especially the creamy potatoes and dreamy whipped cream, were unforgettable accompaniments to our meal. Service was top-notch, with attentive staff ensuring our food arrived promptly. This spot has certainly earned a return visit, whether for a girl's night out or a leisurely brunch.

LOVE this place. Such good vegan food. They have a wide variety of vegan options, any time of day they got you (brunch, lunch, or dinner). They have great drinks and a great atmosphere - I would definitely recommend going during the summer so you can sit outside. Servers are friendly and are happy to accommodate your party. The food is so fresh and flavorful, and portions look small but are very filling!

Title: Disappointing Experience at Buffalo Wild Wings

I visited one of the Buffalo Wild Wings locations in New York and left thoroughly disappointed. The service was rushed and inattentive; our waitress seemed more interested in sprinting away than taking our order. The nachos were a disaster—rated a dismal 0/10 for being cold, dry, and utterly devoid of flavor. My request for extra wet wings was lost in translation, as I received wings that were anything but. Even the beer I ordered upon arrival took an eternity – it only appeared just before my meal was served. Compounding the frustration, all our food was served simultaneously after a 45-minute wait, and to top it off, we were charged for a side of hot sauce. Having given Buffalo Wild Wings multiple chances across New York, I've concluded that this franchise simply doesn't hold up to its Southern counterparts.

I watched Bobby Flay's show, The Flay List,  and knew on my next trip  to NYC that I had to try this place.  We were lucky to walk in and it was moderately crowded.  When we left there was a line formed outside waiting to get In.  Los Tacos No 1 did not disappoint.  It's kind of chaotic but there were employees directing us on what to do.  When you finally get your Tacos , hit the salsa bar and find a table space to eat you'll be  in taco nirvana.    Its a stand up and eat situation and you'll very likely have complete strangers eating tacos face to face a foot across the table from you but don't let that scare you.  There is so much going on and the food so good you won't even care.   Visiting here has to be one of my favorite foodie experiences.  Thanks Bobby Flay for the great taco tip.

3.5 really, but 4 because it's new. When you open their menu, their first page is the chef's bio. If you're anything like me, that would be a major draw as I'm a sucker for storytelling and context. Shinagawa is not just your average neighborhood delivery sushi joint, although I imagine they have to offer Americanized rolls just to stay relevant. They offer more interesting and varied izakaya-style dishes, if you dare to venture out of the norm. One thing I will say is that the restaurant appears to have an identity crisis - does it want to be an upscale izakaya/kaiseki/omakase restaurant or does it want to be a Murray Hill sushi bar with ridiculous rolls and sushi 'pizzas'? Either way, you can have it all.I chose a variety of options in order to form my opinion. The best dishes, in my opinion, were the beef tongue and the eel. Things that your typical Murray Hill patron wouldn't order, but was delightful. The beef tongue tasted remarkably like a tender brisket or a well-braised short rib. The eel was sliced to the right amount of thickness to really complement its oily texture.Honestly the rest of the dishes could use some work. The miso cod - I've just had much better versions in more upscale restaurants where you get a crisp skin and a fork tender flesh, and this wasn't it. I liked the combination of mushroom and I think a plum jam in the Murray Hill roll, but the rolls were ginormous and I hate having to squish it in my mouth. (But I usually never order 'specialty' rolls anyway, so that's just me.) I liked the seaweed in the sunomono, but the sashimi on it was mediocre. The shabu shabu could have used fattier and more consistently thinly sliced meat, in my opinion, but again - I've only had shabu shabu in fancier places where the quality was better.I also got a free dessert from the Yelp check in, which was an elaborate and somewhat messy garden of matcha cream, kabocha, fried dumpling skin and chocolate sauce. This plate of dessert personifies this restaurant - there was too much going on and it was trying too hard. It was tasty but I personally would have preferred just one very good green tea mousse than five different mediocre desserts.In my opinion, if I had to choose a direction for this restaurant, I think focusing on cooked izakaya style dishes would play best to the chef's strengths instead of things like shabu shabu or sushi where the quality of the ingredients play such a huge role. But that's just me, and I have high standards, and I also just came back from a trip to Japan two weeks ago. And also, I guess you gotta make a living in this cut throat neighborhood where the reigning business model is booze and delivery.

TLDR: skip the appetizers aside from the free yucca fries because duh, free, and go for the paella and goat neck, but only if your group can tolerate gamey-ness. Do not order dessert (unless free). I'm gonna have to give up on trying these "fusion" restaurants because adding ONE ingredient from another cuisine (Chinese) into this (Cuban) doesn't make it fusion! Example: seafood paella had Chinese sausage. Bam. Fusion? Uhhh nahhhh. Came on a Sunday night from 5-7pm, where it was relatively quiet - lots of empty tables. Decor is really nice, liked the ambiance, but wasn't great for food pictures (obv). Waiter sweet - offered a free dessert for a review (but ofc didn't have to show him the review) and food came at a decent pace. Sangria ($8 for happy hour): moderately strong, goodOxtail croquettes ($12 for 3): these are about the size of a strawberry. Very crispy exterior, but the oxtail tasted like unseasoned pulled pork to me. The flavors came from the sauce drizzled over the crunchy ball, so the inside was bland. Very average, wouldn't recommend for the price/portion. Definition of bite sized!Yucca fries (free with Yelp Check In): crispy outside, but the inside wasn't as soft as could be. Red sauce was reminiscent of a Korean gochujang sauce, and the other sauce was almost a liquid herby butter type of thing that was quite watered down. Not as good as other Mexican/Cuban placesSpiced Goat Neck ($31): I saw this on the menu and knew immediately that I was going to order this. I love lamb. Yet, I've never had goat. IF you don't like lamb, and you can't stand the gamey-ness, do NOT get this. My friend took one bite, said it wasn't as bad as anticipated, but still couldn't handle the aftertaste/smell. Compared to lamb, the gamey-ness is only moderately noticeable. It's there, but it's nowhere near as strong as could be! It's definitely a large portion - perfect for sharing. Be prepared for lots of fatty content - honestly, it tasted like fatty chunky pieces of braised short rib to me. Super tender and delicious, but also on the salty side. Fusion element: had bok choy. LOL. Prob the sauce too though for this oneBlack Rice Seafood Paella ($32): this was LOADED with seafood, in particular with mussels. Another wet paella, this was a generous portion (meant for sharing!) but I wasn't the biggest fan of the slightly sweeter sauce. Black rice was good, but didn't make the dish stand out or taste different. It's also really hard to mess up a paella, and this was good! But it didn't wow me. Matcha Tres Leches ($12): the stars are docked off for this alone. Barely edible to me. The "cupcake" was hard on the outside. The inside looked to be a very dense muffin situation, but was wet, crumbly, and had that squish squish sound as you cut in. However, it was too wet - the bottom especially was drenched in syrup and the pieces were clumped together. Each bite felt grainy and didn't taste smooth in my mouth. Extremely sweet but nonexistent matcha flavor aside from the dusting at the top.

Title: A Flavor Fiesta at This Must-Visit Restaurant

If you're on the lookout for a dining spot that buzzes with energy and satiates your craving for bold flavors, look no further. Reserving a table is a wise move—this place is popular for a reason, and you'll want to secure your seat amidst the lively ambiance, punctuated by the infectious rhythms of salsa and merengue.

Although I missed the live entertainment during my visit, it hardly dampened the experience. From the outset, the drinks set a high bar, with a strawberry Mojito and cranberry Sangria that were expertly crafted, hinting at the culinary delights to come.

The appetizers didn't just meet expectations—they soared. The chicken empanadas are a revelation, generously filled and seasoned to perfection, a true testament that here, quality isn't sacrificed for quantity.

The main courses continued this theme of delightful excess. My pernil asado was succulent and satisfying, while the ropa vieja was equally impressive. A side of crispy tostones complemented our entrees flawlessly, and despite the tempting dessert menu, our contented appetites left us promising to indulge on a future visit.

In summary, this restaurant is a vibrant testament to the magic of well-executed, flavorful cuisine. It has my wholehearted recommendation for anyone seeking to awaken their palate in a spirited setting.

There are way too many places to go in New York that can give you a true experience and has delicious food than Applebee's. My close friend and I ended up here because she wanted to hurry up and eat, well since there was a wait she was down. They offer breakfast until 12 so we ordered breakfast meals. Mine was a pancake entree and she also order a pancake entree but with a egg scramble dish as well. The process for ordering the food wasn't bad. During the wait that's when you start to see how inappropriate the employees are when customers are right there. They are pointing at people discussing sections, talking about their personal stuff loudly, cracking jokes about some of their customers in Spanish (didnt think they realize there's several people that know Spanish) and drinking soft drinks while right by the customers. I think there needs to be some training put into place for the employees to show them how to conduct themselves during work hours. When the food arrived, everything seemed to be correct. The food was decent, I ordered something simple to make sure it was mess up proof and they sure didn't mess it up so good job! All in all I would not recommend Applebee's because it's a nationwide chain and you should come to New York and explore new options. This location has some hang-ups but with proper training they can get better.

During my recent visit to this casual and spacious eatery, I found it to be a haven for students and those in search of an affordable meal. The tantan ramen caught my attention with its rich and flavorful broth, although the noodles did fall a bit short of my expectations. The pork buns delivered a satisfying and familiar taste that would surely appeal to a wide range of diners. Unfortunately, the karaage was a substantial disappointment; it was possibly the worst I've experienced—remarkably tough, and almost impossible to bite into. Despite this letdown, the restaurant maintains an accessible vibe and a menu that could still be a hit for a quick dining option.

My recent visit to the Spanish Diner at Mercado brought a delightful wave of nostalgia for my time in Spain. The menu selection truly embodied the essence of Spanish cuisine, and I was impressed by the authenticity of flavors in every dish. The food quality was superb and certainly transported me back to the streets of Spain with every bite.

Despite the satisfying taste experience, the pricing leaned towards the expensive side, which is something to be mindful of when visiting. Additionally, our dining was marred slightly by the delay in service; while our waiter was exceptionally courteous, the wait time for our food was longer than anticipated.

Nevertheless, I would still emphatically recommend giving the Spanish Diner a try. Do not miss out on exploring the Mercado itself -- the chocolate con churros on offer are nothing short of heavenly.

Joe's Shanghai has long been a mainstay in the NYC dim sum game, but with the competition heating up, it seems to be lagging behind. The service is efficient, though lacking warmth, and the atmosphere functions like clockwork—no frills, just business. Expect to spend $9.25 for six pork soup dumplings (XLB), and while the portions are fair, they won't be considered a steal.

When it comes to the food, the dumplings here were underwhelming. Despite the thick skins, they tore too easily, and the filling was disappointingly slimy—not to mention they were served tepid, which definitely subtracted from the experience. Considering the abundance of stellar XLB and dim sum options NYC has to offer, Joe's Shanghai doesn't evoke much excitement for a return visit.

Title: Late-Night Comfort at its Finest

I've been a regular at this spot for years, and it's my go-to for post-night-out cravings. The mac and cheese trio sampler is an absolute must-try – it never fails to hit the spot. What I particularly appreciate is the restaurant's late-night availability, providing a perfect, cozy haven after a night at the bars and clubs nearby.

On my last visit, I was seated in the downstairs area, which I found to be exceptionally chic and cute. It's an ideal place for larger groups, offering a space to converse easily without the din of a noisy crowd. Plus, the proximity to the bathrooms (exclusively located downstairs) added a layer of convenience.

In all my years of coming here, the restaurant has consistently delivered quality food and a welcoming atmosphere. It's a rare gem that continues to be a reliable favorite for myself and others looking for that late-night comfort food fix.

So surprised by how great each and every item I ordered was! Typically when I order a small spread to give a few things a try, I can hope to be 50% impressed, but each item here was delicious! Maybe the price made it more delectable than it actually was, but that matters too! Beef noodle soup, pork and chive fried dumplings and kimchi were all above par and I couldn't stop eating any of it. I saw this duck sandwich many people ordered that looked REALLY good as well. Will definitely be back and I'm ecstatic to have found an awesome and budget friendly spot to add to the list. The cooks and cashier were all pretty welcoming and nice as well!!

Title: A Slice of Perfection at Bleecker Street

If you're hunting for the quintessential New York pizza experience, look no further than Bleecker St. Pizza. This gem is ideal for a late-night slice fix, boasting a remarkably swift-moving line, even during its busiest hours. The staff's warmth extends to all, fostering an inviting atmosphere underscored by their charming rapport with the locals.

The pizza itself is a marvel of culinary balance — a masterful blend of crispness and tender chew, topped with a harmoniously proportioned sauce-and-cheese duo. And for someone who typically foregoes crust, I was converted; their crust is irresistibly delicious. With an ample selection of tempting varieties, Bleecker St. Pizza has secured a spot on my must-visit list for future New York jaunts.

This is the second time I lunched here, and this time I was offered the Soba Totto's much coveted Barachirashi lunch special.Since I came in customer number 16 at 11:30am for lunch I was able to grab the Barachirashi for $10, as there's only 20 orders of this available daily! It was well worth the effort and the buzz about this is justified. It was served with hot udon on the side and a big portion of cut sashimi on top of sushi rice.This place is recommended for a quick lunch on the go since they serve real fast; for an office worker with an hour break this place is perfect!

Title: A Turnaround Experience at Marta

Our visit to Marta on a calm Sunday evening at 5pm unexpectedly began with a bit of a hiccup – seating and service were surprisingly slow to come by, despite the restaurant not being busy. However, opting to move to the bar proved to be a game-changer. Bartender Mark was the star of our evening; his personable and professional demeanor, paired with his fun approach to service, salvaged and elevated our dining experience. Mark's spot-on recommendations, coupled with his quick service, reflected his passion for his work and left a lasting impression.

I've been a fan of Marta for years and this visit reaffirmed my affection for the place. For those planning a visit, I highly recommend choosing a seat at the bar for an experience that exceeds expectations. Mark's exceptional service alone is worth the trip.

This place is super close to the South Seaport. Pretty empty when I went at lunch. I used meal pal and for a lobster/shrimp roll. It was well seasoned and tasty. I think the difference is, a place like Luke's lobster scream freshness, made on site before you arrive. This is sorta like a fast food pick up a pre-made lobster roll on the Go-Go!

This location was pretty good. I had a pork bun - one of my favorites in the city, a must-try - and miso paitan, which was decent. No complaints about service. It was lunchtime on a holiday Monday, so my friend and I were seated right away.

I really enjoy this place. I've been here multiple times for just drinks after a night of dancing and this review is for when I came for happy hour. This place gets crowded so definitely get there early! The drinks are food and the food are also high quality. The happy hour Oysters were the highlight and I don't even like oysters! Lol. The mussels were also delicious. Only downside is that the space between tables is very small and there's really no room for personal stuff other than placing them on the ground.

I came in here with two friends on a whim and we weren't expecting to love this place as much as we did. The holiday decorations and friendly bartender created a welcoming environment and we ended up staying for longer than planned. It felt so homey to be surrounded by warm lights, good friends, and delicious food and drinks. I gotta say, the buffalo chicken wrap was so much better than most other wraps I have ever had. The chicken was crispy, but there was still plenty of spicy buffalo sauce. There was a good ratio of lettuce and tomato too. And it was wrapped so expertly that I could pick it up and put it down without fear of it falling apart, defying the laws of wrap physics! The fries were also, like, so good! Salty and fresh out the fryer. We ate every single one. We wanted to try the daily special lobster ravioli, but it was sold out so we pivoted to the penne vodka, which was fairly standard. I had such a lovely time here. It is in a convenient spot, just tucked away down Cliff Street. Pop in for a drink and a meal if you are around South Street Seaport.

I recently visited a quaint restaurant tucked away in a mall, surprisingly spacious and an extension of a London eatery. During the height of New York Fashion Week, they offered a themed afternoon tea - a delightful touch. My friend and I intended for brunch but effortlessly switched to afternoon tea, thanks to accommodating staff. Service was prompt, presenting a bountiful spread quickly.

Contrary to my usual experience, the afternoon tea was satisfyingly filling. The standouts included the savory curry chicken and refreshing cucumber sandwiches, delectable scones, and a notable zucchini mini muffin with lemon cream cheese frosting. The earl green tea was a perfect, herbaceous complement. Overall, a charming spot I'd gladly revisit for its delightful treats and efficient service.

I'd rate the Service & Atmosphere- 5 StarsBut the actually Ramen- 3 StarsThe restaurant is very minimal and our waiter was super accommodating and friendly. I came here with a group of 5+ and many of us made altercations to our order and he didn't skip a beat with them. No mistakes and he even brought extra bowls for us to share. The actual flavor of the broth for the ramen was sub-par. It was kind of bland and didn't taste much like the description. Especially their signature ramen. It was cheesy but did not taste any truffle at all. The best thing I had was the appetizer of the pretzel pork buns. The marinade was great and pretzel bun was a little crisp but soft in the middle. I would come back here for starters but not the ramen.

Came here on a Thursday evening for a pre-holidays friends get-together. It was a large group of twelve people, but the restaurant accommodated us very well. Cocktails at $17 per is par for the course at a place like this. Many are named after Hemingway novels, which was fun. But surprisingly they didn't have a Hemingway daiquiri, go figure. We ordered many appetizers, but the consensus standout seemed to be the truffle fettuccine special. As for mains, most people got steak of some sort, which looked pretty good, although one of the ribeyes looked a little small. I ordered the chicken in crosta, which is kind of like a pounded chicken Milanese except this has an aged parmesan crust and a really buttery sauce that may have had white wine in it. The chicken itself was very tender. Delicious. We also had a dessert sampler platter with tiramisu, cheesecake, berries, etc. The ambiance is very classy, and pricing reflects that, but altogether it was a great meal.

Awesome place. Super authentic and super old school. Most recently got food to-go and was still very happy with it. Delicious pierogi, potato pancakes, and the best blintzes I've ever had. Prices were reasonable for the East Village and the service was friendly. Can't wait to go back for more!

Found this place on Yelp and luckily I did because it is hard to find since it is on a side street downtown. This is a straightforward sandwich shop. They have a long list of sandwiches that you can order. I went with the l'aquila and for $14 you get a huge sandwich.  When you order it you pick which bread to get it on and you know I had to get the sesame bread. So good.  There isn't a ton of customer service here they literally ask you what you want and get it for you. Love it. The sandwich was good but didn't meet the expectations I had honestly.  This is 4.5 stars on yelp... so it should blow my socks off but didn't.  Not sure its 5 stars but 4 star is about right.  Not sure I am dying to come back but if I am in the area I will check it out.

Title: A Weeknight Delight at a Buzzing Venue

My party of five was fortunate to score a last-minute reservation on a lively Wednesday evening at this trendy spot. The ambiance impressed with its excellent décor and an unexpected weeknight buzz.

We kicked off with a Frozen Margarita, which at $13, was the perfect slushy precursor to our meal. The Pollo Toloache, priced at $25, was the star of the dinner—a succulently marinated chicken breast generously doused in sauce and thoughtfully paired with pico de gallo and tasty sides. The chicken remained the focal point, with its moistness shining through each bite.

While the prices are on the higher side, it is par for the course within this location's dining scene. What truly stood out was the restaurant's capacity to accommodate us seamlessly at such short notice—an aspect that will surely draw me back.

I was lucky enough to score lobster tacos today with mealpal.The menu these guys have has been great. Super good combinations of lobster meat, pico de Gallo, and sauce. The cholua sauce was a nice touch but overpowered the delicate flavors in the taco.It usually takes upwards of 5 minutes to get the food, but it's worth it. I do find it interesting that they provide overbuilt bags to carry the food out. Must be built into the regular season cost.

During a day out in New York with my daughter, we turned to Yelp for dining recommendations and stumbled upon this gem. Upon arrival, we were warmly welcomed by Kenny, whose friendliness and guidance on both our beer and food selections were top-notch. We sipped on two delightful local brews while savoring the uniquely scrumptious bacon maple Brussels sprouts and a generously sized pretzel accompanied by an irresistible beer cheese dip. A heads up for future patrons: they operate on a cashless basis, a trend that's becoming increasingly common. This spot is a must-visit for anyone in search of good bites and brews.

I have been coming to Pauls for years,in fact Paul the owner was still working the counter when I first started coming in here.Let me first state that Pauls burgers are Big....They really know how to pack these burgers down and put them inside the round metal lid to simmer.I was always impressed at how many burgers this one guy can always do and do it great...I get a standard burger bacon and cheese and the fries which are awesome as well....I go here by myself most times walking around the east village and love to sit at the counter (only when I come with friends do I utilize their tables.The burgers are not only big burgers but very juicy and always done to your liking..On the downside for me that is,their bathroom's are very small and I'm pretty big so it's a squeeze if I ever need to go in there...

I had an amazing experience at Dynasty Dim Sum. I think this is actually better than dim sum places in chinatown both price and quality wise, even though the atmosphere is less authentic. Upon arrival, I was skeptical about the authenticity of their food because it seemed like one of those upscale Asian restaurants that are way too expensive for serving inauthentic Asian foods. However, I was surprised at the quality of their dim sum and price. My friends and I (4 of us) got 2 crystal shrimp dumplings, vegetable dumplings, pork dumplings, steamed rice roll w shrimp, 2 baked pork bun, braised chicken feet, shumai, and a bowl of rice. I especially loved the crystal shrimp dumplings and vegetable dumplings so I highly recommend them! However, I thought the steamed rice roll with shrimp was very similar to the crystal shrimp dumplings except it was drenched in soy sauce. I thought I would've been fine just ordering the one of them or instead order a steamed rice roll with different filling.We also got free hello kitty buns with egg custard filling by checking in on Yelp and these were sooo yummy and cute. While the service was attentive overall, they forgot our order for the chicken feet. However they made up forit by giving us free piggy bun with red bean filling which were pretty good! It's kind of hard to find the restaurant because the sign is really small and thus difficult to spot from the outside. You have to look for the name Flame Hibachi which is another restaurant joint together with Dynasty Dim Sum and its sign is easier to spot. Our check came out to be $11 per person which was surprisingly cheap for how much we ate and it's definitely cheaper than what we would've paid if we went to a dim sum restaurant in chinatown. I highly recommend this place I think it's truly a hidden gem in Kips Bay!

I popped into the cafe for a quick morning meeting and opted for an iced coffee and banana bread. Despite a minor hiccup with my order being forgotten, leading to a short wait, the taste and quality didn't disappoint. The ample outdoor seating adds charm, especially during pleasant weather. Past experiences with their pain au chocolat leave me eager to explore more of their pastry selections, though I note that lunch choices seem somewhat sparse. I'm certainly inclined to return for a baked treat in the future.

Wow, incredible Toroniku Ramen. Tender  chunks of melt in your mouth Char Sui. Sun Noodles made to perfection, this is a true gem. Follow me on Facebook Twitter Yelp YouTube & Instagram as I travel the world in search of the perfect bowl of noodle soup

As someone who has never liked pork trotters, I probably ate enough here to make up for the past 22 years... I don't know how they do it, but the pork trotters are magical. I was blown away by how they managed to perfect this. This portion size is more than enough for at least 3 people! Definitely looking forward to going back for more of this delicacy Peking duck would also recommend! The crispy duck skin was flavored just right, and made even better when you dip it in some sugar. Truffle xlb was what you'd expect, a xlb. Modern, upbeat and clean interior. Be prepared to wait though! Plan ahead and you scan a QR code at the front to get in-line, but this place is especially poppin at dinner time. We waited an hour but let me say it was worth the wait!! Can't wait to come back and try their other foods.

Title: A Sizzling Cuban Delight in the Meatpacking District

Stepping into La Cubana, one is immediately enveloped in a romantic ambiance, with decor that strikes a balance between simplicity and warmth, creating an inviting atmosphere that has been long overdue in the Meatpacking District.

A live salsa band played the night away, offering a transcendent experience that perfectly set the tone for an evening of Cuban culinary exploration. While the venue scored high on ambiance and entertainment, the sangria at the bar was a bit of a letdown, lacking the punch one would expect from a Cuban establishment.

The culinary journey began with appetizers. The papa rellenas brimmed with rich sofrito seasoning, cooked to perfection, whereas the empanadas de Jaca surprised with their burst of flavor while satisfying my preference for non-spicy fare.

The main course, pargo rojo frito, was a revelation and a generous enough serving for two. Paired with traditional Cuban rice and beans, it underscored what La Cubana gets absolutely right—the authentic taste of Cuba.

Our waiter, Kenji (forgive any misspelling), was the cherry on top—charismatic and attentive, delivering service that matched the quality of the food.

Dessert was a love affair in the form of a guava pastillito—easily the best I've ever had, prompting an emotional response that only heart-eyed emojis could capture adequately.

La Cubana is a gem, ideal for either a romantic date or a lively group celebration. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit with my girlfriends. This restaurant is not just a meal, it's an experience – and one that left me reveling in the joy of discovery.

I recently dined at Canaan, a restaurant where expectations fell far short of satisfaction. Despite the quaint size and adequate service, the cuisine failed to impress. The Sushi/Sashimi combo platter and hand roll were underwhelming in both portion and flavor; the freshness of the fish was not up to par. Although the staff accommodated my son's request for salmon and California rolls, they proved forgettable. The house-made pork ramen also disappointed, bearing an unwelcome resemblance to instant noodles rather than a crafted dish. Regrettably, this Canaan is no promised land for food lovers and should be bypassed by those seeking a memorable dining experience.

Title: A Hidden Gem Unveiled

I recently stumbled upon a delightful dining spot thanks to a MeetUp event, and I must say, it was an experience to remember. Perched at the bar with a front-row view of the small yet bustling kitchen, my friend and I braced ourselves for an evening of culinary surprises—and the restaurant did not disappoint.

The evening began with a symphony of oysters, each variety hailing from New York, offering a tantalizing tour of tastes and textures reminiscent of a summery day at the beach. The deviled eggs, crowned with a sprinkling of bottarga, were a revelation in contrast—salty, creamy, and utterly divine.

While the smoked oysters paired with crackers were enjoyable, the sauce somewhat masked their smokiness, although the accompanying butter was quite exquisite. The Oysters Rockefeller, however, was an indulgent affair with its lavish combination of cheese and spinach, revealing a succulent oyster nestled underneath.

A refreshing interlude came in the form of crisp radishes served with a tobiko aioli—an utterly addictive concoction that left us pondering its potential pairings. The oysters bathed in beef broth presented a visual and gustatory feast, their buttery richness complemented by a savory broth.

Comfort arrived with the Tuscan grilled cheese, featuring a perfect crust and an optimal cheese-to-bread ratio. The classic Caesar salad was another highlight, boasting generous leaves and a hearty topping of cheese and croutons—though a more chopped version would be ideal for a cozy night in.

Dessert was a triumph, with pumpkin pie turnovers and their whisper-inducing crust, balanced by a subtly sweet maple yogurt. The boozy butterscotch pudding was sheer decadence, a dessert that could make anyone contemplate a celebratory dance.

Witnessing Chef Mike Capanile wield his culinary wizardry mere feet away was nothing short of an honor. Observing his passion translate into each dish made the evening memorable and solidified this restaurant as a must-visit on my list. I'll certainly return for the warm ambiance, the outstanding oysters, and the menu brimming with divine creations.

Title: Authentic Mexican Delight in NYC

I recently had the pleasure of dining at what is now my favorite Mexican restaurant since relocating to NYC in August. The cuisine was exceptional, bursting with authentic flavors that are a true testament to Mexican culinary traditions. The drinks complemented the meal perfectly, crafted with a mixologist's touch. Service was prompt and attentive, ensuring a pleasant dining experience from start to finish. While the prices were on the higher side, the quality of food and service provided justifiable value. I am eagerly anticipating my next visit to explore more of their menu offerings. A must-try for anyone craving genuine Mexican fare in the city!

Fun staff, large portions, decent [NY] pricing and tasty fizzy sodas! Great for large parties!Must get: squid ink pasta, pizza [any], burrata, green saladMeh: calamari, veal, tiramisuMissed: fresh fish dishesMy wife and I came here as part of an organized party, and we were incredibly surprised by the intimate yet claustrophobic ambiance of Il Brigante. We had almost 30-40 people in this spot, and catering service was absolutely spot on. The appetizers came out almost instantaneously, nothing appeared to be cool or have that 'just heated up' mouthfeel. Despite the rowdiness of our group, the staff were incredibly attentive, memorized all of our dishes, which were limited due to the party size, but with still a great set of possible variation. I was so shocked that within 10 minutes after we all ordered, the food came out fresh from a kitchen no greater than your private home kitchen as if they were made just for you. Me personally, I loved the burrata and the wide variety of pizzas served as part of the appetizers. The squid ink pasta was a delight to look at, but some of the shell fish had a bit of a foul aftertaste. The veal, while popular among the locals needs better presentation, as it was served under a forest of greens (great for the colon) and I think it soaked up too much of the dressing from the salad and became more soggy.As for the dessert, I liked the way everything was presented en mass, but despite my love affair with tiramisu, I found IL Brigante's version to be a little bit too sweet for my taste.At the end of the day, this place is a 5-star if you're planning for a large event, 4-stars if you count on the food/ambiance along.Food: 4 starsAmbiance: 3 starsService: 3-4 starsPrice: 4 stars

Wonderful place, attentive wait staff and hostess. Food was absolutely delicious. A one (very large) page menu with a variety of options and appetizers.Ambiance was a little off as there was construction being done.Bathrooms we're clean, multiple stalls and not cramped. Delicious and wonderful, good for groups!

I had the pleasure of dining at this establishment and got to savor their really amazing rice rolls. Opted for both the large pork and fried shrimp versions, accompanied by a zesty hot sauce. Each bite was a delightful mix of flavors and textures, perfectly executed. While the rolls themselves were exceptional, a hint more sesame would make them even more tantalizing. Be advised, the wait time can be lengthy; we endured a 45-minute pause post-ordering. For a more seamless experience, I'd recommend visiting during quieter hours. Nonetheless, the wait was well worth it for those delicious rolls!

Disclaimer- Two stars from me for a Michelin star restaurant may seem absurd, but it had nothing to do with the food and everything to do with the service. First, we were running a little late for our reservations (10-15 minutes) and I called to give a heads up and the lady basically told me if I didn't get there soon they would seat someone else. Funny enough, when I rushed over there with my friend there there was a solid 8 empty seats. What's the need to lie to people? Also if we were past 15 minutes late and the table was no longer there I would've understood of course but that was far from the case- I just don't like being lied to. One star off. Second, apparently in the menu the African American waitress with short curly hair advised us that you have to order the food altogether- appetizers entrees etc. This seemed a bit odd but it's there policy, I get it. We decided to get two entrees and the lady asked us if we were sure. "Yes, I'm sure." "Are you really sure?" She must've asked that at least 3-4 times. Not only was it annoying but it got to the point that it was rude. She seemed a little off on several different things too whether if it was forgetting to refill our water (but not forgetting other tables) and asking if we were done eating/drinking when like half of the food was still on our platter. I get it, it's a small cramped place and you want the table for the next person, but what's the point of rushing us? Quite frankly I didn't understand what her deal was but we left under an hour and left her a good tip regardless (because we're not terrible people, she was not a great waitress whatsoever). Another star off.Third, and definitely the "cherry on top" was the manager.  For cocktails, my friend ordered the Naam Manao and Ginger (much better than the latter) and I got the Muay Thai Punch. The Muay Thai Punch...do yourself a favor and don't get this drink. First it was probably a good 3 oz and not the "definitely at least 5 oz" the waitress claimed it was when I asked if I could swap it for something else and then she said she could call the manager. I patiently waited and after a good ten minutes he came out and asked how everything is. I basically told him the truth- I took one sip of the drink and didn't like it. Just that, nothing else. Most restaurants let alone one that's not exactly inexpensive would apologize and take it back, no charge. Actually, every restaurant I've been to has done this. The response I got was "sorry I can't take it back but would you like something else?" Wow, thanks for the sage advice and terrible advice? It was extremely off-putting and concerning that that's their policy. I get it if let's say the meal or drink is half-eaten or half-drunk (for lack of better terms) that it would be "suspicious" but I took the smallest sip of mine and immediately told the waitress instead. Third star off.The sad part about the extremely subpar service was that the food was actually really good, but I guess I have to do takeout instead unless the delivery guy would have the same attitude that's evident in this establishment.***UPDATE- Read the owner's response on my screenshot! If you like being treated with disrespect and bigotry then this is the place for you! Would give it zero stars if I could.

Title: A Szechuan Experience That Sets the Bar in NYC

After my 20th visit in a year, I can confidently say that this restaurant isn't just living up to the hype—it's setting the standard for authentic Szechuan cuisine not just in NYC, but possibly across the United States. If you're ready to graduate from jalapeño-level spice to the unique, mouth-numbing heat integral to Szechuan dishes, cooked predominantly in hot chili oil, then this place is for you.

Be prepared to wait—it's not uncommon to have a 30+ minute wait time, but this culinary experience is worth every minute. Don't fret about the wait, they'll give you a number and call you back in time. The restaurant isn't ideal for very large groups, but it’s perfect for gatherings that allow for family-style dining, which I highly recommend to taste the variety on offer.

Top recommendations include the delicate Pea Leaves with Garlic, the refreshingly tangy Shredded Spicy and Sour Potatoes, and for the adventurous, the Husband and Wife dish made with beef tripe and lung in chili oil. Don't miss out on the Water Cooked Beef or Fish, each a testament to the rich flavors and heat characteristic of the region. For something crisp and visually appealing (perfect for social media), try the Pork and Cucumber Rack, and the Sautéed Lotus Roots for a crunchy side.

Despite the bustling atmosphere, the food arrives quickly, allowing for a symphony of flavors to be enjoyed concurrently. This restaurant is a must-visit for anyone seeking to embark on a genuine Szechuan culinary expedition right in the heart of New York City.

Title: A Satisfying Late Night Dining Experience

I recently visited this restaurant for a late Friday night meal and was pleasantly surprised by my experience. It's a relief to find a place that's open late and isn't overcrowded around 11pm. We were promptly seated upon arrival, and the practical menu printed on the placemat meant we could dive right in without waiting.

We started with the zucchini fried chips, which were a total hit – fried to perfection with just the right amount of coating, served hot and not at all greasy. For the main course, I enjoyed a pasta dish, while my partner's meal included some delectable French fries that I couldn't resist sampling – and they did not disappoint.

The restaurant left a good impression, and I am eager to return and explore more of their offerings on future visits to New York. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a delicious late-night bite!

I celebrated my birthday a few months ago at this gem of a restaurant, attracted by their $49 pre-theater dinner, which exceeded expectations. The service was a highlight, ensuring a special experience from start to finish.

The evening began with warm bread served with a flavorful white bean dip, reminiscent of a local favorite. An additional appetizer, Haloumi me Sika, introduced a well-grilled cheese with figs and a fennel salad, creating a complex blend of sour and nutty tastes, though a hint of bitterness was noted.

From the appetizers, the Soutzoukakia offered tender meatballs with a tomato-forward sauce, whereas the Horiatiki salad shined with freshness, setting itself apart with a unique base. The Spanakopita was a tad too sour and smaller in portion, and the Revithokeftedes resembled falafel, pleasant but not a standout.

The mains were generous, particularly the Paidakia sti Skara, a succulent lamb dish worthy of a la carte status. The famed Lavraki lived up to its reputation, with a tender loup de mer seasoned to perfection. The ora king salmon impressed, especially the spinach rice, but the vegetarian risotto failed to deliver the same excitement and felt more casual than gourmet.

Dessert was a delightful end to the meal. The Kataifi Ekmek and Saragli stood out with their respective pairings of pistachio gelato and tahini parfait. The Greek Yogurt Trio offered interesting variations, though the quince was somewhat bitter.

This restaurant is a standout, possibly the finest Greek dining spot in the city, providing both quantity and quality. Its pre-theater deal is remarkable for the amount and excellence of food provided. With just a tweak to the vegetarian main, this place is near flawless—a resounding 4.8 stars.

Beautiful, Victorian decor . Stopped by for lunch and shared the penne alla vodka and a burger. Food is fine, nothing offensive however nothing to write home about. The establishment is spacious and offers a variety of dishes and drinks. It's a pretty version of a restaurant/ bar. Seems to be a destination good for pre-theater of after work happy hour. Good service provided by the courteous and attentive staff.

Came here before a show for some cajun food. For starters I had the gumbo with hush puppies. The gumbo was good, just wish it was a bit thicker. The hush puppies were delicious though. They were crunchy and tasteful. For dinner we ordered the cajun chicken and sauage pasta. I personally was not a fan. The portions are big and the waiter was so amazing so I tried to love them, but my taste buds won't let me. But the last part of our dinner made me want to come back. Their pecan pie has been the BEST I have ever had.  Not too runny. Not too sweet. Just perfect. The pie made my night.

Spoon Table & Bar is a cute little restaurant that was perfect for a cozy brunch. Definitely make reservations for brunch because the wait can be quite unexpected otherwise. It can be up to an hour or so depending on your party size. I tried the orange zest and cinnamon waffle and biscuits & gravy skillet. The waffle was a tasty morning treat -- not too sweet with just the right subtle hints of orange zest and cinnamon. The biscuits and gravy skillet was a much heavier brunch option -- the gravy was super thick and flavorful. It had hints of spice as well. The biscuit was a bit dry in my opinion. I ordered hot tea which came out to be $4.50. It was simply a tea bag in a cup, but they provided an aesthetic tea pot of hot water. It was a bit overpriced for a tea bag from a generic name brand and pleasant presentation. The restaurant itself was very cozily decorated with warm lighting and quirky decor. Service was very friendly and happy to serve. I would definitely return for brunch again!

The owners of this store take advantage of customers in a very vile manner. Came in yesterday and bought a cool new CBD drink by VYBES in a peach ginger flavor for $7.99 each. I loved it so much & hadn't seen it sold near my hood in Gramercy so I checked Yelp and saw they delivered. Wonderful news, right? However...Called to place the order and they delivered me 3 bottles this evening. When the delivery man hands me the receipt, each bottle says $9.50 plus tax. EXCUSE ME? I know exactly what the owners were doing and it's up-charging a customer just because he feels like it. The delivery man called the store and the owner says it's fine just let her have it for $7.99, I declined to keep or pay for the drinks because I won't give my business to any store that is owned by greedy, dishonest men. You could've made a lottttt of money from me guys. But instead, you thought I was a dummy. I'll order VYBES by the case straight from their website from now on. I was trying to support local businesses for god sakes! Shame on Your Wholesome Foods.

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Prince Street Pizza

It's no secret that I am an ardent fan of Prince Street Pizza, a sentiment I've managed to pass onto my partner as well. Following an energetic night out, we found ourselves craving the unmatched pizza we've come to adore at this beloved spot. Despite the late hour, around 1 am, our gamble paid off; the place was open and bustling with eager patrons.

The line stretched to the glass doors, but the vibrant atmosphere and the wall adorned with photos of celebrities who've visited made the wait enjoyable. When it was our turn, we opted for a margherita-style slice and three pepperonis, all swiftly heated and ready to go. To allow more customers access, we chose to take our meal to go.

Once we settled down to eat, the first bite confirmed why we keep coming back. The cheese on the pizza was indescribably creamy, melding flawlessly with the zesty pepperoni and tangy tomato sauce. The crust was a substantial, bread-like foundation that perfectly supported the generous toppings. Each pepperoni-laden bite was a delight, and the margherita slice was equally exquisite. My friends agreed wholeheartedly, and soon we all succumbed to a blissful food coma.

Prince Street Pizza has truly outdone itself, creating a pizza so irresistible that it leaves us yearning for more outposts to enjoy this culinary masterpiece more than once a year.

After years of buzzing anticipation, my recent visit to this renowned restaurant lived up to the hype. Arriving at 6 PM on a bustling Saturday, my friend and I braced for a 45-minute wait, which seemed a small price to pay for what was to come. With an innovative bar seating arrangement, we eagerly checked off our choices on the provided menu, settling for the 6-piece handroll selection featuring toro, yellowtail, salmon, scallop, crab, and lobster - all for a value-packed $28, gratuity included.

The freshness of the fish was indisputable, and the crispness of the seaweed wrapped around a generous portion of rice made each handroll a delightful indulgence. Of the lineup, the yellowtail and crab shone as the stars, though all were quite delectable. A minor critique would be the liberal application of mayo on the scallop and lobster rolls, which slightly overshadowed the natural flavors of the seafood. A separate takeout experience with just the yellowtail and crab reaffirmed their mastery in seafood freshness and taste. This spot comes highly recommended for any sushi lover seeking quality at a great price.

From the folks who created Artichoke Bastille, this is another winner! A personal size pizza comes in a hefty rectangular box with 4 slices. They offer a good selection of options, but of course I had to go for the pepperoni because of the stacks on stacks of delicious crispy loaded goodness. If you're a fan of Detroit Style pizza with that crispy thick crust, you'll surely get that here. I wish there was a teeny bit more caramelized cheese corners but the tomato sauce and pepperoni did make up for it. For $11, I'd say this place is def worth it!

If you're perusing the menu and your eyes land on the pistachio pesto pasta for $22, consider this your sign to order it. The dish strikes a delightful balance with its nutty pistachio flavor, aromatic herbs, and perfectly chewy texture. Pair it with the side of Brussels sprouts for $10; their crispiness will not disappoint.

As for an indulgent add-on, the bone marrow bruschetta at $12 for two pieces is a non-essential but irresistible choice. While it might jab at the roof of your mouth, the flavor payoff is immense.
