Imagine savoring rich bone marrow without the toil of scraping it out with a tiny spoon – that's the kind of luxury your palate deserves. Trust me, it's worth every bite.
What a beautiful atmosphere with a vibrant and playful setup! Make Believe was one of the hotspots we visited for my friends 30th birthday!  Great service!

Such a cute spot! Came here for breakfast around 9:30am on a Sunday and the service, food and vibe were great. We had coffee, the Della and Eggs and the Filet o' Fish. Would highly recommend both of those entrees. If you're looking for a cozy place with quick service and great food, this is your place!

This is a cute little dive of a hidden gem in Stuy-Town that everyone should know about. It's quite small so I wouldn't recommend someone advertise it as wheelchair accessible but all in all the little place gets the job done.I loved the pork belly and beef platter - brunch special is only $8.95!! Great pieces of tender meat and it comes with this amazing tangy vinegar sauce with a coconut rice! Yummy yummy. Also ordered the egg roll and wasn't impressed with that so I'm gonna skip that next time. Everything else was super delicious!!

My veggie burger was pretty good, although the bun was tough and maybe a bit old. It wasn't the best I've had, it was on the better side of average. The sweet potato fries were very thin and crispy which isn't usually how I like them. I feel like this place is somewhere in between 3 and 4 stars. I probably wouldn't go out of my way to come back.

I would give the food a 3.5. The wine associated with the brunch was a 3. Atmosphere and quaint would be a 4. Customer service was quick but I didnt care for the how they added a bunch of stuff on our bill for tip and tax when we had a groupon. When said and done, we paid an extra $22 buck for two breakfast on top of the groupon. I would not come back for the price on the food. I also didn't like the limited menu. Quality was good but something just rushed about prep on potatoes and amount of food was not what we expected. We added bacon for $6 and it was needed. French toast was good, but for cost just wanted more.

When you can see the chef rolling and stretching your noodles right before your eyes....there is nothing better. I visited NYC on a weekend and had to stop at this restaurant. Small and quaint, friendly staff - they allowed me to go into the kitchen and record the chef, THE THINGS I DO FOR YELP. I ordered the roasted duck noodles --- so full of flavor and the noodles were so chewy and fresh. I ate the entire thing and I kept on my self guided food tour in Chinatown...Great spot, loved my noodles until the last drop.

Check in to use their 10% discount on your entire order! Although I still don't understand why they charged us a 15% service fee and still asked for tips. We were there on a Sunday afternoon. We waited a while to get seated because the restaurant was busy and there was only two staffs on the floor. Food was great! We ordered stir fried noodles (very authentic), Xiao long bao (kinda wished the dough was thinner), sticky rice shu mai, and pumpkin mochi cakes. I'd go back again for other noodle dishes. Their noodles are handmade and very flavourful!

Incredible all-Mac-and-cheese place in East Village. The ambience is very casual but can get loud at times. During the summer they keep the doors open so it can get really hot inside. My favorite Mac and cheese variety was the Cajun one, made with sausage and peppers.

Dining at this establishment was a transcendent experience, one that's sure to leave a lasting impression on any culinary enthusiast's memory. Admittedly, the cost is steep—dinner and a high-end wine pairing each at $355—but for those able to indulge, it's a worthy splurge.

The 12-course meal was nothing short of extraordinary, surpassing even the standards set by prestigious three-star Michelin restaurants in Paris. The standout "Oysters and Pearls" dish was a symphony of flavors that justified its acclaim, enhanced by the exquisite pairing with '06 Dom Perignon.

From the initial amuse bouche, a delectable sashimi cone, to the splendid dessert finale, paired with a '97 D'Yquem, each course was a testament to culinary artistry. The sommelier impressed with expert pairings and the personal touch of including favorites like the 2017 Domaine Saint Prefert Charles Giraud.

Make reservations well ahead, and prepare for a dining experience that is nothing short of a gastronomic odyssey.

I recently indulged in the Connecticut lobster roll at Cousins, and it was nothing short of buttery perfection. At $17, the price may seem steep, but the generous portion of lobster meat spilling out of the roll ensures you're getting your money's worth. Beyond the standard roll with coleslaw and a pickle, the option to add chips and a drink for $4, or upgrade to tots or fries with a drink for $6, is available.

What truly distinguishes Cousins is the extensive menu, which ventures beyond the typical Maine/Connecticut-style lobster rolls. They offer an adventurous variety such as lobster BLTs, quesadillas, tots, tacos, along with non-lobster selections like chowder and fish and chips.

The space itself is inviting, with ample room to easily accommodate our group of ten during a weekday noon rush, and the service was commendable with attentive staff ensuring we had everything we needed.

While a lobster roll from Cousins may not be an everyday lunch choice, it's a delightful splurge when the craving strikes. I enjoy Luke's for a lobster roll fix, but for diverse options and a pleasant dine-in experience, Cousins definitely takes the cake.

Flats Fix is more of a bar than a restaurant. The cocktails and beer selection are excellent. The atmosphere is casual and fun. The food is good, but neither truly Tex-Mex nor traditional Mexican. Having said that, all and all it is a good spot for some tacos, burritos, Margaritas and cerveza. Not worth a special trip, but if you are in the neighborhood. Excellent for groups.

I'm delighted to award this establishment with a 5-star rating. Their service is impeccable, the portions are generous, and the southern Italian cuisine is truly the finest I've had. Highly recommended for an authentic and satisfying dining experience.

I recently visited a cozy Vietnamese eatery tucked away in a snug, narrow space seating about 10 people. The menu offered the typical fare you'd find in such establishments, including Pho with a variety of meat options. While the Pho was decent, it didn't quite hit the mark for me; the flank and brisket lacked tenderness, especially when compared to offerings from Luu Baguette, a mere two blocks away. If you're in the area and seeking Vietnamese cuisine, this spot provides a good meal, but for those in search of the most succulent meats in their Pho, you might want to consider the nearby competition.

We came here (Friday) for Happy Hour after we wrapped on set & enjoyed ourselves at the Bar due to Krista's A+service of fast & friendly. As well as the inexpensive drink & food prices that were right up our alley. If you're looking for a casual, yet trendy & upscale establishment CR&B is the place to be. With the huge bar, there's two dining areas, one by the bar & more of private area on the other side bar/wall.The interior is donned with earth tone "Chocolat" colors & fancy lighting fixtures offering a warm ambience. There's overhead music until the DJ aka Hype Man comes on providing an entertaining atmosphere. Unisex restrooms are in a clean order as with the overall restaurant.Happy Hour is from 2P-8P at the bar only that offers small plates of Fried Chicken/Shrimp, Calamari & Ribs. Cocktail drinks range between $7-$10. Brunch is offers on Saturday & Sundays from 10A-4P. Regular menu consists Chicken, Salads, Steaks, Seafood & handful of Sides. One of the chic/urban eateries in the Harlem restaurant district. I'd return upon my next visit to NYC.

Title: A Flavorful Journey at The Tang

The Tang offers more than just a meal; it's a symphony of authentic Chinese flavors served in an ambiance bathed in natural light with a warm, eclectic charm. The open and transparent setup allows diners to watch as chefs craft their dishes with precision and care.

Service at The Tang is top-notch, with staff members that exude genuine enthusiasm for the culinary journey on which they're embarking their guests. The menu, a treasure trove of meticulously prepared offerings, speaks volumes of the thought invested in each dish.

Appetizers like the succulent Mouth-Watering Boneless Chicken Thigh and Pork Dumplings in Chili Oil tantalize the taste buds without overwhelming them. The Pickled Wood Ear Salad offers a crisp, tangy counterpoint that ignites the palate.

As for the mains, the Drunk Noodles stand out with Momofuku Hozon and chickpea paste adding complexity to the dish, while the Braised Pork Knuckle Over Rice is tender perfection that melds magically with the rice and egg.

In summary, The Tang is a gem that shines bright with its culinary prowess. This isn't just a meal; it's an unforgettable experience—one that beckons for repeated visits to explore the depth of their menu. A resounding endorsement for any aficionado of authentic Chinese cuisine.

Title: A Go-To Spot for Post-Show Bites on the Upper West Side

Whenever my friend and I find ourselves on the Upper West Side, perhaps after a movie or a performance at the W83 Auditorium, we make a point to dine at this local gem. Our culinary adventure often begins with the irresistible scallion pancakes, elevated with a side of chili oil for an extra kick. 

We've delved into a variety of dishes here, from the perfectly seasoned salt and pepper shrimp to the comforting hot pots bursting with fish and cumin flavor. The sautéed snow pea shoots and the simple yet flavorful spinach with garlic never disappoint, showcasing the kitchen's commitment to fresh ingredients.

Admittedly, the wait times can stretch a bit, but the consistently good food makes up for it. Plus, the polite service ensures that even the busiest nights are handled with grace. Overall, it's a place we'll keep coming back to for its reliably tasty fare.

Title: Pricey Eats in a Tourist Hub

Nestled in a bustling tourist area of NYC, this restaurant's prices left my wallet lighter than expected. Despite the steep costs, the dining experience was largely positive, with commendable service from a considerate and attentive server.

Our culinary journey commenced with pimento cheese, which set a pleasant tone. The main courses, though simple, were satisfying; the salads were fresh but lacked complexity, and while the $25 price tag for a basic grilled steak salad could raise eyebrows, the steak itself was a highlight—tender and cooked to perfection. The dressing was well-balanced, avoiding the pitfall of overpowering the greens.

My lavender margarita, though, didn't hit the expected floral notes and came off as your garden-variety margarita—disappointing for someone seeking a twist on the classic. Still, I found it enjoyable enough to sip through to the end.

In summary, the restaurant offers well-prepared food and attentive service, but with prices that demand a bit more innovation and flair to truly justify the cost.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at The Meatball Shop and it completely exceeded my expectations. The meatballs, especially the classic beef and spicy pork, were incredibly tender and well-seasoned. I appreciated the variety of textures, particularly the chewiness that added to the overall eating experience.

Our trio opted for 'The Kitchen Sink' with a delightful parmesan cream and classics, which was a hit. We indulged in the sides – a nutritious selection of quinoa, sweet potato, roasted broccoli, and salad, which complemented the meal beautifully.

Creating our own bowl was also fun; I picked the spicy pork meatballs paired with pesto on a bed of risotto. While the pork had just the right amount of heat, the pesto was somewhat overpowering in its saltiness. However, the chicken meatball and risotto combination was a triumph, with the poultry being surprisingly moist.

In sum, The Meatball Shop is a must-try for its succulent meatballs and hearty sides. Just a small note to watch the salt in the pesto, but definitely don’t miss out on their risotto.

This is one of the trendiest new spots in the LES. I went there around 5 for apps and drinks and I was impressed. Sweet chill wings were crispy, tender and had a great kick. The mushroom and truffle arepas were delicious. The curry bowl although seemingly small was filling, but reminded me more of an Indian curry v a Jamaican curry, still good. And the lobster roll was a lobster salad roll, but also good.  4/5 stars bc my drink was $18. But all in all for two apps, two mains, and a drink it was $83. Not too bad.

An artsy and high quality meal at a premium. The moment you enter this cozy restaurant you feel transported into a peaceful space. The bench tables with upholstered benches on either side are very hip and welcoming at the same time. I could see myself spending an afternoon here reading a book, sipping tea, and munching on their mochi ice cream. Our favorites of the evening were- the vanilla chip mochi ice cream with delightfully thin skin- matcha cheesecake - nice texture, not really sweet, but you can taste the matcha and the slight tart flavor. Not really a kid dessert.- eel in the unagi appetizer- the broth in the chicken ramen- daikon Ume - very strong in flavor and a dish you can't get in a lot of places- the sauce that came with the sushi rolls.Just so-so were- the sushi rolls (ikura was not as full or fresh as we would want and the baked salmon roll kind of fell apart)- the prices! Our bill for a medium amount of food for 3-4 people was $90 before tip.

This is one of the best dining experiences I've had as of yet in nyc. I'd always heard of this place and their pierogies but had never tried either. I was in the area with a friend getting drinks and we both decided to finally try this place out. I was not disappointed as this place hit every notch: 24/7, delicious menu, outstanding service, and a variety of pierogies to try. We ended up trying the short rib and potato varieties. Both were absolutely phenomenal, and the potato pancakes were delicious as well. Everything was super high quality, and the flavors and texture were to die for. I'm absolutely obsessed now and know I will be back, which is dangerous for my waistline but could be worth it. The place was popping off at 1am on a Thursday, normally way past my bedtime, but it just goes to show how popular and good of an establishment that this place is!

Another long day of studying over, and it was a chilly evening in NYC. Soup was definitely a good option, and I found what I was looking for in The Handpulled Noodle. I went with the Build Your Own Soup, which included ding ding noodles, herbal ginger chicken, and a high spicy level.The soup came out as expected. The chicken portions were decent, and the soup was delicious overall. It hit the spot well, and left me satisfied.This is a great option for noddle soup. I would consider them again.

Title: Culinary Bliss at a Gem of a Restaurant

From the moment you step into this culinary haven, your taste buds are in for a delight. The menu is a parade of hits, with the tomato soup dumplings and manchego empanadas leading the charge. The eggplant pizetta is a masterful blend of flavors, and the mashed potatoes are pure comfort food elevated to a new level of deliciousness. Desserts are not an afterthought here - especially the creamy, dreamy pudding whose name escapes me, but it's unforgettably luscious.

Don't miss out on the toasts, whether you go with creamy avocado or fresh ricotta, they're a must-try. Beverages also impress; the cocktails pack a punch, while the mocktails - the Peacock, in particular - are imaginative and refreshing. Connoisseurs of spirits will appreciate the exceptional tequila selection.

Service is where this place really shines. Despite their success, management doesn't rest on its laurels and is wholeheartedly committed to perfection and customer satisfaction. A special shoutout to the attentive manager who made sure our dining experience was comfortable, despite an initial seating snag.

Take my advice and book ahead – this spot is no secret to those in the know. Each visit confirms the kitchen's unwavering consistency. On my to-do list? Their much-talked-about party-style brunch. Can't wait to dive into that experience!

Title: A Delightful Japanese Cuisine Experience at Tonkatsu Matsunoya

My visit to Tonkatsu Matsunoya was a delightful encounter with authentic Japanese flavors in the heart of NYC. The serene ambiance and charming interior set the stage for a comforting dining experience.

The menu, characterized by reasonable prices, offers an array of tempting dishes, making it a challenge to pick just one. Sharing a set with a friend is a wise choice, given the generous portions served. The chicken and pork katsu curry, my particular favorites, stood out with their exquisite taste, easily making Matsunoya my top pick for Japanese curry in the city.

The sets come complete with fresh cabbage, flavorful potato salad, and a choice of soup. While both the miso and meat-based soups are commendable, the lighter miso soup garners my personal preference.

In summary, Tonkatsu Matsunoya is a gem that promises not only a meal but an experience. With its delightful food and tranquil atmosphere, it's a must-visit for anyone seeking quality Japanese cuisine. It's no surprise that I'm already planning my next visit. Highly recommended!

Was super excited to try this place after seeing all the great reviews. However, I was left disappointed. I got the original seafood ramen here that comes with slices of chashu and bamboo shoots. Overall, it's an ok bowl of ramen but everything is just too salty! The soup is very flavorful but heavy. The bamboo shoots are extremely salty and I could barely finish them.

I recently dined at a delightful restaurant that boasts a prime location and an exceptionally welcoming staff. Their popularity is evident, as you might find yourself waiting for a table during busy weekends if you forego making a reservation. A minor inconvenience is that some tables are situated near an exit door, which can be slightly chilly during the winter months. However, any discomfort is quickly forgotten when you try their crab cakes, which are a surprisingly delicious standout on the menu. Overall, a very pleasant experience that's worth a visit—and the wait.

Title: A Taste of Authentic Spain in the Heart of the City

I recently had the pleasure of attending the soft opening of a new Spanish restaurant, and I can't help but rave about the experience. Understanding that the service was still finding its rhythm, which showed in some delays, the staff was nevertheless friendly and well-informed. The real stars of the evening, however, were the food and the atmosphere.

We popped in around 5pm and decided to indulge in some tapas, despite not being overly hungry. The Buñuelos de bacalao were delightful, perfectly crunchy on the outside and sumptuously soft within, paired with a divine honey aioli sauce. The Gambas al ajillo transported me straight back to Barcelona with its authentic flavors and presentation in a charming ceramic pot – the shrimp heads were a delectable touch.

Even the complimentary bread and olives, served while waiting, were a testament to the restaurant's attention to detail and authenticity. While my husband enjoyed a caña, we both agreed it was fairly pricey for the portion served.

The restaurant's décor, featuring a Mediterranean vibe with a vibrant Mariscal painted wall, was inviting and added to the overall experience. Our baby was comfortably accommodated next to our table in his stroller, and high chairs were available upon request.

Glancing at other dishes like the Rossejat, the value for money seemed evident, though we did note the Calamarcitos a la plancha appeared oddly overpriced—a potential menu typo?

Overall, even for a soft opening, the impeccable quality of the food and the charming atmosphere have secured our plans to return for a full meal. This place is a welcomed addition to the city's dining scene, offering a slice of Spain that's both authentic and reasonably priced.

3.5/5. An authentic Sichuan restaurant in the heart of Greenwich Village (so authentic that the corner of the restaurant had random cardboard boxes stacked up haha). The food was delicious, but not amongst the top tier of Sichuan restaurants in Manhattan. However, given the location and portion sizes, I think it's worth a visit. THE FOOD:-Steamed pork soup dumplings: I mean, it was our fault that we ordered soup dumplings at a Sichuan restaurant, but we were craving it. It's not bad, but by no means worth ordering unless you have an insatiable craving-Scallion pancake: BIG miss for me. There were no layers in the pancake, so the all but 2-3 layers were super deeply fried. -Dan Dan Noodle: delicious-Mapo tofu: generous portion, delicious-Sauteed spinach: must get (if in season), delicious-Sauteed green bean: good portion size, I felt like they were overfried-Braised fish with pickled vegetables: yum yum yum. Huge portion size and delicious. I do wish they added more vermicelli/clear noodlesAll in all good food for the area, but not of the likes of Sichuan restaurants in East village.

Came here m as we were going to the movies, which is literally less than 5 minutes away and had a lot of time to spare.. It was a saturday night and as expected, the location was jam packed. We were informed the wait was going to be 45-55+ minutes, we decided to wait it out and have a few drinks at the bar. Let me just start off by saying the drinks here are great. They're not too strong, maybe too light for a heavy drinker  but I thought they were great. There is not much of a large selection of options but margaritas are always good too. They have some beer options but different flavor margaritas is the main option.. (I.e: strawberry, mango,  etc) After about what I believe felt like 20 minutes, we were seated. The way ordering works is you are given a menu and circle what you'd like. The server reviews it with you after to confirm. I ordered tacos and my bf ordered the burrito bowl, fyi the burrito bowl is kind of expensive so watch the prices if you're looking to stay under a budget- everything else is pretty damn cheap. They have a happy hour on certain days of the week. The food was great. The service- for the crowd was decent. I would most likely return as the experience was overall good.

After an enchanting evening at Carnegie Hall, my companions and I sought a late-night dining spot and chanced upon the Applejack Diner. Our party of five was promptly seated, a welcome comfort in bustling New York.

The menu catered to our varied cravings with offerings like French toast (one decadently dressed with Nutella and walnuts), a classic side of eggs and bacon, a plain burger for the purist, and an Italiano pesto panini that hit the spot. The dessert didn't disappoint either—a rich chocolate and Oreo shake.

On a sweltering night, the attentive wait staff was commendable, ensuring our glasses were never empty. While the prices seemed a notch above standard, the convenience and service justified the expense.

Our departure was marred slightly by an unexpected guest—a cockroach found its way onto our server. However, considering its appearance post an outdoor clean-up, we chose understanding over alarm. The situation was quickly handled outdoors, allowing us to reflect on our meal with minimal disruption.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience with Top-Notch Management

I recently dined at a restaurant where the management truly shines. The team went above and beyond for a fellow diner who had issues with her steak preparation, demonstrating genuine customer care by comping her meal without hesitation. It's heartwarming to see such commitment to customer satisfaction.

As for my meal, the scallops were a highlight – cooked to perfection and absolutely delectable. Although the accompanying vegetables were a tad oily for my taste, the overall quality of the food did not disappoint.

A special mention must go to the complimentary chocolate mousse provided at the end of the meal. It was an exquisite touch, the rich and creamy dessert providing a perfectly indulgent finale to a wonderful dining experience.

Title: A Delightful Brunch Experience at the Chelsea Spot

My visit to the Chelsea location for brunch was an absolute treat. Familiar with their dinner service, I was eager to explore the morning offerings and I wasn’t disappointed. Sharing a selection of dishes with my boyfriend, including the Patatas bravas, Croquetas cremosas, Huevos con chorizo, and Nutella-filled churros, we were both enamored by the flavors. Admittedly, the inclusion of the croquetas made for an indulgent fried feast, but it was a decision we didn't regret. The portions were generous, leaving us more than satisfied. Alongside the scrumptious fare, the service was commendable. This spot has certainly nailed brunch.

Title: Plant-Based Pleasure at ByChloe - A Delight for You and Your Pooch!

I recently visited ByChloe, nestled in Manhattan's Seaport district, and it's a true gem for anyone seeking scrumptious vegan eats at a fair price. The alfresco seating is a bonus, welcoming dogs to join the dining experience.

The menu proves that healthy can be heavenly, with dishes so flavorful you'll forget they're good for you. A standout treat was the rainbow sprinkled cookie, a favorite of Brie's mommy, offering that perfect sweet finish. For the canine companions, the freshly baked crunchy dog treats are a gourmet delight.

ByChloe's charm is found city-wide with multiple locations, just call ahead to confirm dog-friendly options. This restaurant is a must-visit for plant-based foodies and their furry friends.

DEALS:- 50% off shochu or sake flights when you check-in on Yelp- $3 and $6 starters + $9 ramen from 9pm to close daily!This place is SO delish! Everything tasted so fresh.1. Beef bone marrow gyukotsu - Award winning and amazing. It's worth the hype. I'm very sad I live in CA and can't come back for this whenever I crave it. Although there was only a teaspoon-sized piece of meat in my bone marrow, the soft, braised beef made up for it! The broth was delicious. My mouth is drooling. I'm sad as I write this in my CA home.2. Spicy tonkatsu - My fiance's because I can't eat spicy. It was pretty bomb. I made him eat the green chili pepper thinking it was a shishito pepper, oops. 3. Spicy tuna tacos - Not the best I've had, but I love how thin and crispy the wonton shell was. I do wish it had more flavor and kick to it.4. Pork bao bun - Thick pork belly slice with lettuce, mayo, and chashu sauce. Pretty basic. Not a fan of super fatty thick pork belly, but if you like it + enjoy bao, then do you boo boo!Service: I think they mistakenly added someone else's order to our check. My fiance didn't check the receipt and obliviously placed his card on the check to pay. Lucky for him, he has me! The total was $77 and I knew it wasn't right. They were kind enough to take it off and gave us two shots of hot sake as a courtesy.Downstairs where the bathrooms are located is a cute little pop-up experience with craft cocktails + desserts! Worth checking out.What a fun experience this place was. Will definitely be spreading the word about an amazing ramen spot in New York.

NR has quickly climbed the ranks to become my go-to cocktail bar on the Upper East Side. Their unique concoction, Mussel+Beer+Cotton Candy, is a must-try—its savory broth and tender mussels create an unforgettable pairing. Though the food menu is concise, primarily limited to four varieties of ramen and a few small bites like the succulent Wellfleet oyster, it's the extensive and imaginative cocktail list that truly shines. 

During my Sunday dinner visit with a friend, we walked in at 6:30 PM without a hitch as the spot doesn't accept reservations. The Transparent Tomato cocktail captivated me with its subtle tomato essence, while my friend's warm Apple cocktail—served in a whimsical teacup—was a delightful twist on spiked cider. Presentation is key here; each drink is an artistic expression served in an array of playful vessels. 

Whether it's the Asian-inspired flavor profiles with ingredients like shiso and wasabi or the striking drinkware, NR offers a sensory adventure. Even the less adventurous eater will appreciate the non-spicy yet rich Kyoto ramen, with its melt-in-your-mouth pork belly.

NR is an alluring destination where the charm of its drinks menu and the quality of its offerings guarantee my return. It's a gem that's poised to fill the void of a downtown cocktail haven, and I'm eager to work my way through their creative menu.

The placed looked very clean but mayb a bit too clean to the point where i smelled bleach all throught my meal. The food was so-so. Not bad but not the best. If you are just hungry and need something to fill u up that would be a place to go.  The mala fish noodle i ordered didnt have enough taste and the mala beef my mom order was too salty. The steam buns were ok, the skin was abit thick but the soup inside tasted good. One note is a 15% tip was already included on the bill, we had a two adult and a toddler(doesnt eat). Not sure if all the resturants are doing this now but im used to adding in the tip on my own and only when there is party of 6 or more tip is automatically included on to the bill.

I had high hopes for this establishment, but my initial visit left much to be desired. After a long day on my feet, I took a seat on an unmarked bench only to be confronted by an employee who rudely insisted the bench wasn't for sitting. As a local, I've seen others seated there without issue, which added to my frustration. Despite the unpleasant encounter, I've returned since and found the staff, including the previously discourteous employee, to be amiable. The desserts here are the highlight; they're so good, they practically sell themselves. The option to join a waitlist via Yelp is a handy touch for quicker service. Despite a rocky start, the sweets are a draw and the improved service warrants a return.

Azuki on 8th Avenue proves to be a rare find in Midtown's dining scene, offering a decent bang for your buck without resorting to the usual fast food fare. Their lunch specials are reasonably priced, with options ranging from $8 to $11. I tried the Chicken Teriyaki Bento Box – a substantial meal that includes white rice, a California roll, shrimp shumai, salad, and miso soup as a starter. While the food is good, it's not outstanding, making Azuki a suitable choice for a quick workday lunch but less ideal for business meetings where you might want to impress.

Title: Cozy Dinner with Meatballs and Personalized Pizza

I recently tried ordering from a local spot via Seamless for the first time and was pleasantly impressed. The meatball appetizer, priced at $6.95 for three sizable pieces, arrived warm, tender, and full of flavor – their marinara sauce had a warm, salty kick to it. They also provided a small container of Parmesan, which, although not the freshest, was a decent addition.

For my main course, I designed a 9" cheese pizza for $9.95. Despite arriving a tad cooler than I would have preferred, the pizza impressed with an aesthetically pleasing custom box. The thin-crust pizza exhibited an excellent fold and crunch, with a perfect ratio of sauce to cheese - very satisfying.

On top of the quality of the food, the packaging was neat, and the delivery punctual, with my entire order arriving correctly. Overall, it was a great experience that left a tantalizing taste in my mouth. Yummmm!

This restaurant is amazing!  It's easy to get to from the 125th subway stop, and there's a bus stop right outside the front door.  We came around brunch time on a Saturday and were seated as a group of 3 without a reservation immediately.  The food came out quickly and the portions were large.  There were ingredients on two of the three dishes that were not listed on the menu - so if you have allergies or food restrictions definitely ask before ordering.

Bar hopping = bar food...my review will be super short because it was a quick bite to soak up the beer. The wings were well done, crispy and saucy!! Fries crisp and golden, the sliders mouth watering!!! Enjoy the attched pics.

I attended a dinner presentation at a local restaurant on a Thursday evening, which kicked off with a reserved private room. Although the space felt slightly cramped, the atmosphere was fitting for mingling before the event.

As the presentation was about to start, we were prompted to select from a prix fixe menu. The spicy tuna roll appetizer proved unremarkable, blending into the crowd of countless similar dishes I've had before. The filet mignon main course arrived without any inquiry into preferred doneness, resulting in an unevenly cooked steak that was over-salted and accompanied by an excessively oily side of kale and onions. Dessert partially redeemed the meal, with a chocolate lava cake of decent flavor, if a bit floury, paired with sublime espresso ice cream.

Service throughout the meal was perfunctory; the servers were not particularly warm or efficient, yet managed to fulfill their basic duties.

In summary, despite an engaging presentation, the culinary experience did not live up to expectations. Both the food and service were middling at best, convincing me that a return visit isn't on the horizon.

Excellent happy hour with a wonderfully engaging bartender who served me a glass of Pinot Grigio and it was great. Cool vibe with fun music and nice patrons. I would definitely return for some of their interesting happy hour items!!

Man that cuban sandwich hit the spot!! It is packed with meat - the pork was so, so tender and juicy that every time I took a bite, the sauce was just oozing out the other end. Love the panini bread, love the sauce (kind of wish they slathered even more on, but a girl can dream). This location is super tiny but I love that it was more of a low key atmosphere. Can't wait to come back to try their other items on the menu.

Title: A Hidden Gem with Upscale Pricing

I stumbled upon a delightful Chinese restaurant right in the bustling heart of midtown west, where the culinary excellence nearly justifies the steep prices. Each dish seemed to surpass the last in terms of flavor and quality. The beef scallion pancakes were a standout – achieving an exquisite balance between meat, scallions, and crispy dough, all complemented by an unconventional but superior peanut-ish sauce. 

The crab and pork soup dumplings were another triumph. Not your everyday find, these dumplings were crafted with a thinner dough, letting their rich, perfectly seasoned filling shine. I still find myself longing for that taste.

Even the spicy noodle soup did not disappoint. Amidst a variety of greens, bean sprouts, and mushrooms, the clear noodles were an ideal pairing for the harmoniously flavored broth.

While the dishes wowed, the prices did raise an eyebrow. If not for the cost, this place would have easily earned five stars. Still, the experience was so memorable that I'm planning my next visit – perhaps for a special occasion when the price feels just right.

Title: Exceptional Service and Delectable Mussels at Cozy Spot

I recently visited this charming restaurant with my sister for what we intended to be a lunch/early dinner, but we were unaware of their intermission at 5 PM to prepare for the dinner crowd. Initially, we were a bit let down by the prospect of only ordering from the happy hour menu, which had a limited selection of mussel pots.

Despite this, we opted to stay for drinks and appetizers, and that's when the experience took a delightful turn. The attentive bartender picked up on our disappointment and went out of his way to check with the kitchen about our preferred dishes. To our delight, they were able to whip up the mussel pots we were craving, specifically the parma mussel pot, which was exceptionally tasty and has now become my favorite.

During our time at the bar, we observed the bartender skilfully crafting a unique drink called the flex shooter. After trying a sample minus the oyster, I found it surprisingly delicious and would wholeheartedly recommend it. The bartender's knowledge of tequila was impressive, and the drinks he made were both expertly crafted and potent.

For those with a sweet tooth, do not miss out on their donuts. The salted caramel is irresistible. Overall, I've always been fond of this place, but the exceptional service during this particular visit has solidified it as a memorable favorite.

In a bid to #SupportBlackBusinesses, I turned to Omar's for a dose of Caribbean cuisine and was not disappointed. Our order arrived promptly through Grubhub, and the aromatic allure of the dishes promised a feast at my boyfriend's place.

We indulged in the plantain and saltfish fritters ($11), a delectable mix of crispy and tender, sweet and savory, with a garlic aioli that truly elevated the experience. Though I typically avoid fried foods, this was a worthy exception.

Next came the curry oxtail special ($20) with rice & peas and salad leaves. The oxtail was rich, flavorful, and so succulent that every bone was cleaned off. The rice and peas were a perfect accompaniment, and I'm already planning to get more on our next order.

The jerk chicken ($18) was a pleasant surprise – juicy and expertly marinated, debunking our initial impression of dryness. Leftovers are eagerly awaited for a weekend treat.

While the mac & cheese ($10) was the comfort food you'd expect, it didn't stand out as much as the other dishes.

Overall, Omar's not only met but exceeded my expectations with its delightful fare. It's a touch pricey but undoubtedly a worthy splurge. Looking forward to our next culinary adventure here!

Title: Exceptional Service and Great Value During Restaurant Week

I finally managed to visit this long-anticipated eatery during restaurant week and it didn't disappoint. My friend and I had a reservation for 6:30 PM and were seated immediately, setting the tone for an evening of impeccable service. The attention to detail was noteworthy, with staff attending to minor splatters on the table and ensuring each course had its own fresh plate.

The restaurant itself boasted an unexpectedly glamorous staff, which added a touch of enchantment to the ambiance. Yet, what truly impressed me was the value offered during restaurant week. It was a pleasant surprise to receive generous portions, like the $19 beef salad appetizer, as part of a three-course meal priced at $42, despite their regular entrees hovering around the $30 mark.

The food was delightful, with appetizers such as beef tartare and beef salad shining in both flavor and freshness. The main courses, shaking beef and Saigon chicken, were executed to perfection, particularly the beef. The sticky rice, although slightly cold and under-seasoned for my preference, was still enjoyable.

Dessert, although satisfactory, didn't quite reach the high bar set by the preceding dishes. It wasn't memorable, but didn't take away from the overall positive experience.

I would heartily recommend this restaurant, especially for a date night, for its exemplary service, the excellent value during restaurant week, and mostly delectable cuisine.

Stepping into this unassuming stall, the first thing you'll notice is the tantalizing aroma of fried goodness that overtakes your senses. This no-frills joint operates on efficiency, so know your order and be ready to move quickly. The star of the show here is undoubtedly the chicken leg over rice, smothered in a savory sauce that you'll want to ask for extra of. The portions are generous, leaving you with what seems like a pound of satisfying comfort food, all for a mere $6. Accompanied by veggies, this meal is a steal. In short, if you're looking for a swift, wallet-friendly feast that will linger in your memories (and maybe on your clothes), this is a must-visit spot.

Title: Cramped Quarters and Missteps at a Would-be West Village Spot

My latest dining experience left much to be desired at a restaurant that could pass for a West Village haunt tucked away in some larger, more forgiving city. The space was reminiscent of a shoebox, overcrowded with patrons and chairs that obstructed every pathway.

Fortune smiled briefly, granting us seats at the bar where we sipped on wine that was merely passable, failing to tip the scales in favor of a return visit. Our foray into the menu began with a cheese board, which promised honey but was unceremoniously served without it. This oversight was a harbinger of the lack of attention to detail we'd encounter throughout.

The establishment's size constraints mean that all cooking is done via an oven behind the bar, resulting in a smoky interior that did little to elevate the ambiance, instead inducing sneezing fits.

In a city sprinkled with stellar wine bars, this place struggles to stand out. With mediocre offerings and a cramped setting, it's one I'll be skipping in future ventures for a glass of wine and a bite.

I came back here for my birthday and I had a good experience again. It was a group of 8 of us with a reservation. We ordered the special appetizer of the night which was Burrata Cheese wrapped in prosciutto with mixed green salad. This was delicious.For my main I ordered the Filetto Di Dentice In Brodetto and it reminded me of home. The sauce for the fish reminded me of how do our steamed fish. It was so good I cleaned the plate. The clams were my favourite part of the dish. Our waitress was very friendly.I was surprised with a tiramisu and this was probably the best tiramisu I've had in a while. I don't remember if tasting so good the first time I came here but it was excellent this time.

Title: Carbohydrate Craftsmanship and Caesar Showstoppers at Bread Perfection

Bread Perfection isn't just a clever name; it's a statement verified by every slice served. Treating diners to a soft, biscuit-like texture, the bread arrives warm, aromatic with garlic and poppy seeds, and ready for a generous swipe of butter—an indulgence hard to resist.

Remarkably, the Hotel Caesar salad managed to eclipse the lauded bread, earning its position as the meal's unexpected protagonist. With a dressing that hits all the right notes, impossibly thin croutons, and an egg that complements without overwhelming, it's a dish that elevates the common Caesar to stardom.

The NY Strip, ordered medium, was tender, well-seasoned, and solidly enjoyable, although it didn't quite reach the memorable heights of its menu companions, possibly overshadowed by the preceding sensations.

Accompanying sides like the overly smooth mashed potatoes and standard asparagus did little to impress. However, the lemon curd tart, crowned with fresh blueberries, provided a zesty and splendid finale to a meal that almost demanded no further indulgence.

Service at Bread Perfection is of noteworthy caliber, attentive to the point where your glass is never found wanting. This establishment is an exemplary choice for those seeking a business dinner or a chic dining experience.

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience

My recent visit to this restaurant was a sheer delight, with lovely food, attentive service, and an ambience that strikes the perfect balance between cozy and sophisticated. The convenience of finding a table via Yelp even on weekends was an added perk, with the venue being pleasantly bustling but not overcrowded.

The culinary highlight of the evening was the truffle pasta, which was exquisite in flavor, and it paired wonderfully with a robust Italian rosso wine. Both were standout choices that I would highly recommend. This place has certainly earned a spot on my list for future dining out.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a local eatery renowned for its ramen, and the experience did not disappoint. Our server recommended the duck ramen bowl, a testament to the chef's dedication as he had perfected the broth after much trial and error. Indeed, this dish, which made a rare appearance on the menu, lived up to the hype. The broth was a sublime blend of soy and roast duck flavors that harmonized in each spoonful.

Although tempted, I resisted the urge to try the brisket ramen after savoring the duck ramen. Despite being a limited offering of just 20 orders per day, the brisket broth failed to impress me as much, coming off as heavier and slightly fatty, which sometimes occurs with brisket cuts. However, my companion found enjoyment in the heartiness of the brisket, while conceding that the duck ramen reigned superior in both flavor and lightness.

The ambient noise levels of the restaurant were surprisingly well-managed considering the bustling full house. The thoughtful design, with shelves under the barstools for personal belongings, added to the overall positive experience. As we departed, a queue had formed, a sure sign of the restaurant's appeal and the anticipation of other diners for a tantalizing meal.

After experiencing this restaurant for the first time in Korea, I was ecstatic to find a location in the States. Their curry is a must-try—rich, flavorful, and customizable in terms of spice level. The medium setting offers a perfect balance of heat and taste without overwhelming the palate. Don't miss out on the cream cheese croquette topping; its creamy goodness blends seamlessly with the curry, creating an incredible flavor profile. Additionally, it's a great spot for vegetarians, with plenty of tasty options. Overall, a delightful and satisfying dining experience.

I recently visited a cozy Tex Mex joint nestled in the west side of Soho, reminiscent of a Blockheads establishment, both in ambiance and fare quality. This mom-and-pop spot shies away from grandeur, offering a straightforward menu where enchilada plates and burritos take center stage. 

The choices are ample - from beef to shrimp, and a vegetarian option ensures there's something for every palate. Each dish we sampled exuded a heartwarming homemade essence, with meats lovingly seasoned, complemented by flavorful rice and beans. 

However, I found the portion sizes modest, particularly the burritos, which were notably smaller and not as budget-friendly as I've encountered elsewhere. 

In short, if you're seeking well-seasoned, homestyle Tex Mex and don't mind smaller servings, this Soho spot is worth a visit.

Title: A Unique Lunch Experience Worth Sharing

I recently had the pleasure of lunching at a fantastic eatery with a coworker, and I must say, the experience was nothing short of exceptional. Right from the moment we stepped into the entrance, the restaurant's unique charm was palpable.

Service was impeccable, with attentive staff ensuring a delightful dining experience. But the true star of the show was, without a doubt, the food. I chose a steak alongside a summer soup — a refreshingly cold concoction — and both dishes were flawlessly executed.

For anyone in search of great taste, excellent service, and a dash of distinctiveness, this place is a must-try. It certainly left a lasting impression on my palate and my day.

We only had about a half an hour to get in and get out so we decided to go to Jebon. The last time we had did there it wears super fast. Our server, Vinny sat us in his section that was pretty close to the door but it was fine cause we wanted to get out very fast. I ordered the shrimp Tom yum soup and shrimp dumplings. Jeffrey ordered the extreme spicy beef ramen with fewer ramen noodles and more broth. My Tom yum was delicious and adorable. It was a very small portion but I actually preferred it because it was quite spicy. Jeffrey's ramen was very beautiful but my Tom yum was 10 times spicier than his. I waited for a few minutes for my dumplings and Jeffrey called him over and asked about them. Vinny said, "oh you haven't gotten them yet?"Not really a big deal except when he brought over my dumplings he didn't bring any sauce with them. The dumplings always come with a vinegar sauce. Long story short: the food is decent. The prices are very low. Quick get in and out.

It's been a minute since I've had Thai food and I decided to give this place a try. I got their popular dish: Ratchaburi Crab & Pork Dry Noodles. The pork was really good and the flavor was similar to the Cha Siu pork you would get in Chinese restaurants. However, their pork was thinly sliced, was not heavily coated in a sweet, sugary marinade, and was not extremely soft/fatty. The noodles were equally delicious with their chewy consistency and soft texture. When you got to the bottom of the bowl, there was a vinegar based sauce. I wish I had known sooner (dry noodles so I assumed no sauce lol), but if you mixed the noodles, pork, and yu choy together, you get a subtly sweet flavor with the savory. I enjoyed this dish a lot as it was light but filling. There wasn't a lot of crab and I could have done without it to be honest. It didn't really add much to the dish. Next time I'll try another one of their noodle dishes!

3.5- but giving 4 star for consistency. I went back to try their Sunday dim sum! It was much better than the first time since the food it brought out to you with carts however the service is just not good- it's very hard to get anyone's attention and they will walk away as you are speaking to them- it's kind of strange and you can't help but laugh because it's very awkward. The food it pretty good and most importantly consistent- pricing is ok and I would recommend for larger parties!

Title: A Gem of Ramen Creativity in the East Village

As a seasoned ramen enthusiast, stumbling upon Camellia Noodle Shop in New York's East Village was like hitting the jackpot. My recent visit on a Monday night with an impressive entourage of 14 found us immediately seated in an atmosphere that was inviting but not overcrowded.

Camellia sets itself apart amidst the fierce ramen competition with its customizable noodle options. Taking the plunge, I indulged in the pork spare ribs ramen embellished with vibrant rainbow noodles—an artistic blend that included matcha, cuttlefish, and carrot flavored strands. At $12 a bowl, the variety in texture and taste was noteworthy, with the matcha noodles stealing the show.

The depth of the broth was unmistakable, simmered for hours to achieve a rich complexity. A perfectly runny egg crowned the dish, while a side exploration into their off-menu beef tenderloin ramen delivered an explosion of juicy satisfaction.

The Taiwanese fried chicken was a delightful surprise, merging heat, tang, and a satisfying bite. Undoubtedly, one of the finest Taiwanese-style popcorn chicken dishes in the city. The culinary journey continued with an exotic array of Asian-inspired gelatos. The White Rabbit candy gelato was particularly memorable, embodying the nostalgic flavors of the iconic Chinese milk toffee candy.

There's room for improvement, however. The pork spare ribs, while tasty, could benefit from additional stewing for a more tender, fall-off-the-bone experience. Additionally, the beef tenderloin ramen seemed noodle-heavy; a better balance of beef, garnishes, and vegetables would elevate the dish.

In conclusion, Camellia is a must-visit for a standout ramen experience in the East Village, with bonus points for their extraordinary gelato selection. I'll certainly return for both the noodles and the unique dessert offerings.

Title: A Delightful Birthday Dinner Experience

I recently celebrated a birthday dinner at this venue and was pleasantly impressed by the prefix menu offerings. The jumbo shrimp cocktail starter set a high bar with its freshness and flavor. My main course, the broiled salmon paired with sautéed green beans, was cooked to perfection, offering a burst of flavors that delighted my palate.

Accompanying the entree was a jumbo lump crab cake, which, while packed with ample crab meat, was slightly heavy on the breadcrumbs for my taste. Unfortunately, I couldn't indulge in the dessert—a tempting bread pudding with pecans, white chocolate morsels, and vanilla ice cream—due to a dairy allergy, but my company assured me it was scrumptious.

Despite the tiny hiccup with the crab cake, the overall dining experience was excellent. I'm eager to return and explore more of their regular dinner menu.

I've been here several times and try to make it a point to go when I'm in town. This location is Pretty convenient in times square, theres upstairs and down so always plenty of seating. I love the sticky wings here, so good! The drinks are also yummy! Try Henny colada.Unfortunately I had a bug in my drink when I came recently and the hostess brought me another, but didnt give any discount or offer apologies. I get accidents happen but that was gross.  After mentioning it she got the manager to give me adiscount which should have been automatic in my opinion.  Bathrooms are usually not the cleanest, but  its NYC I guess. Anyway. 4 stars is for service amongst a couple other things ,but food has always been good.

Heading out with my Yelp crew never disappoints, but dining at Chef Douglas Kim's spot in the West Village truly elevated the experience. The chef's open bar-style kitchen provided a front-row seat to his culinary artistry, complete with a preview of a masterfully prepared fish dish for the next day. This anticipation set the stage for the star of the night: the wagyu ramen.

Served in a velvety veal stock with earthy mushrooms and delicate slices of beef, the ramen proved irresistible. Each spoonful revealed why this bowl could vanish as swiftly as an illusion, an adventure in flavors worth the pursuit. Pairing this dish with a selection from their noteworthy wine list, particularly the Californian pinot noir, complemented the meal flawlessly.

Service here mimicked a well-rehearsed symphony, with staff attending to our needs with seasoned precision. Jeju Noodle Bar casts aside the ordinary with its commitment to culinary prowess, turning a simple ramen meal into a vibrant testament to Korean flair and flavor. This is not your average noodle stop; Jeju demands an adventurous palate ready to embrace the raw and the refined.

I actually got kbbq twice (oop not oops) at diff restaurants within the same week and in terms of meat quality, this place was better. I ordered the small beef combo (for two people) and I left the place 80% full...that being said I wish their meat portions were a bit bigger. If you're with a party of 3, def go for the large combo. We went on Sunday for lunch so there were only a couple of other tables filled. Our waiter was super attentive, asking how well done we wanted our meat, and changed our grill with each meat. Def recommend coming here (and any kbbq place) on their off peaks to get the service you deserve for the $$$ You're dropping here.

I recently visited a charming restaurant that's perfect for both brunch and dinner accompanied by drinks. The ambiance is warm and inviting, with antique furniture, whimsical props, and an array of flowers creating a cozy atmosphere. My arrival on a weekend showed a deceptively quiet scene, but it quickly filled up with patrons eager to enjoy their meals.

Our group of three was able to sample a wide selection with 3 appetizers and 2 main courses, which were generously portioned and left us more than satisfied. Of particular note were the bruschetta and the pappardelle pasta—both must-try items. The rest of the dishes we tried maintained the same high standard of quality. 

The service was attentive and timely, adding to the pleasurable dining experience. This restaurant certainly warrants a return visit, and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for great food in a delightful setting.

During a stroll down Bayard, I stumbled upon Tonii's, a new rice noodle roll joint a stone's throw from the famed Yin Ji. Intrigued, I tried their cilantro cheong fun, which, at $4, seemed fairly priced and with a generous portion. Unlike Yin Ji's, Tonii's offers sit-down service, which adds a cozy touch to the small space.

While the cheong fun here boasts less oil and a healthy speckling of cilantro and scallions, the texture falls short—it lacks Yin Ji's signature silkiness, tending toward an over-steamed, mushy consistency. Pricing is straightforward, with most rolls at a flat rate of $4, a bargain especially for the vegetarian option I sampled.

Tonii's might be a decent stop for a quick bite, but for those in pursuit of the perfect cheong fun texture, it may disappoint, especially when compared to the revered rice noodle rolls from Yin Ji or the Elizabeth St cart.

This was probably one of my favorite New York meals in a while. I *love* Indian food, and while the restaurant itself was small, crowded, and broiling hot...the food (and service) was so incredibly good, I couldn't get enough.I got...+ Samosas (vegan) - they come two to an order, but they're twice as large as any samosas I've seen elsewhere, so #worthit. And they were STUFFED full of potatoes and peas. Nothing quite like the disappointment of biting into something like this, and realizing it's mostly dough or mostly air pockets. Not these. Flavorful, filling, and I was easily won over with the sauce in a heart shape.+ Papadams (vegan) - Goodness, I love me some papadams (I can usually eat 8 by myself no problem... or maybe that's a problem, I don't know). I like their crunch, their distinct flavor, and the dipping sauces. Sahti's didn't disappoint.+ Onion Pakoras (vegan) - these were the best pakoras I've ever had; I like that they had the consistency of a moist fritter. Melt in your mouth, and if I wasn't in polite company I would have claimed a whole order for myself.+ Vegetable Korma (vegetarian) - so this can't be made vegan (something about their almond cashew nut sauce containing yogurt or something?), but this was stupid good. LOADED with veggies like broccoli, carrots, peas, and potatoes... long after I was sweating profusely and my pants had stopped fitting, I kept on eating anyway because I just couldn't get enough.Thanks for everything, Sahti! I can see myself ordering delivery the next time I'm lounging at my hotel nearby after my too late flight. Stay tuned!

Been here twice now and both times I tried something from both their drink menu as well as their food menu and cannot say I was the least bit surprised with how much I enjoyed it all. Their drink menu is fun and extensive with plenty of craft beers, sour ales which I love. I ordered a Hot Toddy at my most recent visit since I am on a mission to try one where ever I go when it's in season, and it was delish. I especially enjoyed their sandwiches and salads which definitely feel hearty bug healthy. I found their Brussels sprouts to be a little salty. Also think they can add a little bit more light to the back room. Service is great, honor reservations which I have learned to value over the years. Since I live nearby I am sure to return and recommend this spot for people who want a nice place near Penn Station!

Title: A Satisfying Twist on South-East Asian Cuisine

I recently ventured into Madame Vo, slightly hesitant due to my usual indifference towards South-East Asian flavors, but I left completely enamored by the experience. The avocado smoothie was a revelation—creamy and refreshing—it's a must-try. Though the Madame Pho was commendable, it surprisingly didn't top my list of favorites. However, Mama Ly's fried rice was a standout, hitting every note of perfection.

The spare pork ribs enveloped in a rich coconut sauce were an excellent addition to the meal, offering a delightful balance of flavors that left me wanting more. To finish, the Vietnamese coffee was notably sweet, but its boldness won me over, much like the rest of the menu items that managed to impress.

Not to be overlooked, the range of smoothies provided a tasty and cool complement to the dishes. The service throughout the meal was exceptionally kind, adding to the warm and inviting atmosphere of the restaurant. Madame Vo is undeniably worth a visit, especially for those looking to be pleasantly surprised by the diverse and delectable offerings of South-East Asian fare.

Went in for brunch and got  the red eye chicken and waffle and it was pretty good. Loved the eggs inside my waffle and chicken was well made. I was expecting the gravy to be a little thicker but overall a very good meal. Husband ordered chicken chilaquiles. He was happy with his choice also.

Title: Unforgettable Omakase Experience at Chefs Garcia and Zagha's

I recently indulged in the dinner omakase at this gem of a restaurant, and the experience was absolutely stellar. Chef Mark Garcia and Chef Evan Zagha are at the top of their game, crafting an array of dishes that delight the palate. The pre-omakase courses set a high bar, particularly the smoked duck which was a standout.

The omakase itself was a parade of sushi nirvana, with each piece of nigiri outshining the last, both in taste and execution. The chefs ensure perfect pacing, allowing for a relaxed yet engaging dining experience, complete with some enjoyable conversation. The well-designed counter space particularly enhances this interaction – snagging a center seat is a must for full immersion.

At $160, the value is exceptional, considering this ranks as one of the most memorable omakase offerings in the city. Whether it's a romantic date night or an outing with friends, this spot is a winner. Eager to try their lunch menu, I plan to return soon. A resounding 5 stars from me!

I recently visited an incredibly unique dining spot that completely redefined the concept of self-service for me. As soon as you pay at the entrance, you're handed a glass – and no two are the same, adding a delightful personal touch to the experience. The setup is reminiscent of a frozen yogurt shop, but for the beverage connoisseur: a wall of taps awaits, inviting you to sample at your leisure.

You're in control here, letting your chosen drink flow for up to 10 seconds, with the price ranging between 69 to 89 cents per ounce. The novelty of pouring your own drink combined with the straightforward pricing makes for a fun and interactive atmosphere. This innovative concept brings a refreshing twist to dining out, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Morimoto had a very modern vibe, and friendly staff. We made a reservation on a Sunday evening for date night, and were seated immediately. We ordered a ton of food, including the spicy king crab, rock shrimp, yellowsnapper jalepeno, sweet shrimp sushi, wagyu beef sushi, california roll, shrimp tempura roll, sea bass, and black cod. It was a lot for two people, but we were there to try all of our favorites! Unfortunately, we were not impressed by the food. For the price point it is, we've had better sushi elsewhere. We did like sea bass, sweet shrimp sushi, and wagyu beef sushi of everything we tried, but not the best I've had.

Best pizza spot in Murray hill along with Norma! Just ordered the shroomtown and pineapple pizza. Got the gorgonzola sauce and lemon basil sauce for dipping and they were both delicious. It also came so quick- in about 20 minutes. Pizza is on delicious thin crust and each ingredient is delightful!

I really wanted to give Strip House 3 stars, because I found the appetizers and service to be meh. However, the review gained a star because the main dishes were absolutely mouth-watering.When I first walked in the restaurant, I was astutely looking for the health grade score, but it wasn't shown anywhere, which was a little worrisome. The two women at the front desk were very nice, but when I told them my name, they disappeared for a minute, and when they returned, neither of them said anything until I asked if I could be seated if the other person in my party wasn't there. They showed me to my table and asked if I wanted my coat checked, which I declined. At 8:15 PM on a Wednesday, Strip House was absolutely packed! Every table was taken. I'm not sure if this is how it usually is or whether it was because it was restaurant week, but it was a great sign, nonetheless.The waiter immediately came over and placed what felt like 50 red books (menus) on the table and walked away quickly. I managed to call after him that I wanted the Restaurant Week menu, and, without saying anything, he just pointed to the multiple menus on the table. Whatever.My friend arrived, and neither of us drank alcohol that night. We ordered our dishes from the RW menu: she got the little gem waldorf salad and strip steak medium well (+$12), while I got the seafood chowder and strip steak medium (+$12). The food came fairly quickly, and when I looked at the salad it was dismal. There were 3 pieces of lettuce and hardly any dressing. It was actually funny. My seafood chowder was very bland and not great. I'm from South Florida, so I know good seafood chowder. I wouldn't order again.It was only after we finished our appetizers that the bus boy came over and asked if we wanted bread, which we accepted. It was annoying that our WAITER never offered us any (eye roll), but that was to be expected. The poppy-seed bread was delish, but the pretzel bread tasted a bit stale.The main dishes- wow!! The strip steak was some of the best I've ever had. In total, there was probably 6 oz of meat, but it was tremendous. It was cooked to perfection, and the seasoning was a thick layer of pepper and other spices. It did not need ANY sauce, and I'm a sauce lover. It came with brussels sprouts that I was practically licking off the plate. It also came with medallion potatoes (2 tiny slices) with a mustard sauce on them. The entire dish was amazing.We ordered 2 sides to split of the truffle creamed spinach and whipped potatoes. Both were spectacular, especially the creamed spinach. You could taste the truffle flavoring, so if you like truffles, this is a must-get. I usually have to salt and/or pepper everything, and nothing on the table needed that. In fact, they don't even have salt and pepper on the table.For dessert, we ordered the 24-layer chocolate cake (+$8). I'm not a huge fan of chocolate in general, and especially chocolate cakes, but I knew this was a must-try. It says that it is meant for 2, but this cake can easily feed a table of 4. My friend and I could hardly finish half of it, and we ate quite a bit. It was very, very good, and I'm glad we ordered it.Throughout the night, our waiter was not present and didn't check on us except once. I'm not sure if it was because we were 2 mid-20s women there for restaurant week and not middle-aged men in suits, but it was unacceptable regardless. When we paid the bill, I also handed him my Landry Select Club member card. Strip House is owned by LSC, and members get points on their card for dining at their restaurants. When I handed him the member card, he finally smiled and became attentive :) Goes to show you don't know who you're serving!

I was hungry and wanted to try something different.  Ordered the traditional Bing.  The food was made fast and quick, but looking at the ingredients they put in the crepe, it's not worth $10 for junk and tasted horrible.Hoisin sauce, chili sauce, scallions, seasame seeds, and cheap Americanized fried noodles that you get from Chinese take out restaurants with your fortune cookie.The packaging and everything else looked fine.  But it was super drenched in hoisin sauce which made it salty as fck.  The traditional crepe was like eating a fried wrap with sauce as the filling.I was so hungry yet I couldn't even finish it.  It was bad and had to Chuck it into the trash.

This was such a treat.  We meandered through most of the Burroughs today rather quickly and decided to have dinner in the meat packing district. This place cake highly recommended and it didn't disappoint. The lobster roll was delicious and the rh burger was ordered but was a bit too med-rare for my guest.  We sent it back twice and the third time it was personally delivered to the table by the chef. At this point it's safe to say the dining portion of dinner was now horribly timed as I plowed through my meal. What was very much appreciated was how the entire situation was handled. I was most impressed with the level of teamwork and attentiveness to our table. The wines were delicious. I just wish places had vodka but it seems i have to maintain my tradition of arriving with my own sippy cup of vodka drank. Will certainly return here. They have one of the most elegant setups for a romantic lunch or dinner.

This is my type of place when I'm going for a quick bite. You can't go wrong with dollar slice in NYC! I love Two Bros don't get me wrong. The only thing with this location is that the pizza topping bottles are sparse and they didn't have crushed red peppers last time I went (which is a much for my plain dollar slices). Also, it could happen anywhere, but my friend and I were approached by a rude man asking for money. He didn't even look homeless either. I'd say this location has more sketchy people than the other Two Bros location I've gone to before, and the quality is slightly lower here, as my slice was a bit cold when served.

Title: A Masterclass in Fine Dining - Gramercy Tavern

If you're seeking the epitome of New York City's fine dining scene, look no further than Gramercy Tavern. The harmony of warm ambiance, impeccable service, and extraordinary cuisine creates a symphony of dining pleasure that's hard to surpass.

Even as a large party with the potential chaos of an infant, the staff at Gramercy Tavern managed the evening flawlessly. From the moment we walked through the doors to our last bite, the experience was seamless. 

Their consistent excellence is the reason we've frequented Gramercy Tavern since its inception and why we will continue to return. Hats off to Danny and the team for sustaining the high standards of fine dining pleasure. Bravo indeed!

Title: Pleasantly Surprised by Oki's Ramen Delivery

I recently ventured into trying Oki's ramen delivery, initially skeptical due to their menu spanning the culinary gap between poke and ramen. To my delight, I found their Volcano Ramen to be a pleasant surprise. The dish came with a generous amount of toppings, offering the flexibility to customize by adding bok choy and skipping the bamboo shoots.

The broth struck a harmonious balance of flavors, although it disappointingly lacked the advertised spicy kick. The noodles boasted a satisfying chewiness, and the chashu featured a perfect mix of tenderness and fat. Unfortunately, the egg fell short of expectations—edging towards overdone, which held my rating back from a perfect score.

Despite the egg's slight misstep, my overall experience with Oki's ramen was overwhelmingly positive. I would not hesitate to satisfy future ramen cravings with another order from Oki.
A small clean bar that features many beers!  Drinks! Food!  Friendly bartenders!  A classic dark bar that plays a variety of late 80's early 90's music. Reasonable drink prices.

I have to say, this restaurant genuinely merits a full 5-star rating. The establishment was spotless, and the staff were nothing but cordial and efficient in their service. Impressively, our food and drinks arrived promptly - with freshness and a delightful crispiness that exceeded expectations. The Nagasaki ramen I chose was absolutely delectable. Our dining experience was enjoyable from start to finish. While the prices reflect Manhattan's standard, the quality and service provided make it well worth it. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Came here for lunch today for the first time as a belated birthday meal with my co worker and had a great time.   Gu is the sushi restaurant this area needs - there seems to be a lot of very high end sushi places and low quality places and Gu is a perfect mid-point restaurant.  They are on open table so it's easy to make a reservation and they have a large selection of lunch specials. I had the yummy sushi special which came with 4 pieces of sushi and the yummy roll and a small salad. It was good and plenty of food. My coworker and I shared the spicy garlic edamame which was delicious and a huge portion.  The restaurant also brought out a complimentary birthday dessert of fried ice cream and sang which was delicious and kind. I will definitely be back and this place will be my new office lunch time go-to. The service was great and it was clean.
Great spot for drinks, food and catching up.  Cool vibe and good looking people. Conveniently located to other cool spots so perfect place to start or end your night.

5/5. TL;DR at the bottom. As a belated birthday present, I took my best friend to Sushi Ishikawa. I chose this place for two reasons: 1. He's never had omakase before and obviously we needed to do something about that and 2. compared with its contemporaries, Sushi Ishikawa stood out for its unique twist on traditional sushi, and my friend has immense appreciation for fine dining that's whimsical and innovative.I had a 5:15pm reservation but we were extremely late due heavy rain and traffic and did not arrive at the restaurant until 5:50pm. The staff was extremely competent and accommodating - explained apologetically that our omakase would have to be executed at a faster pace, and checked on us throughout the tasting to make sure that we didn't feel rushed. My friend and I thought it worked out great and were both very satisfied. We both did the 15-course omakase and had an amazing time sitting at the chef's counter watching our chef prepare each exquisite piece of absolute delicacy with technique and passion. Each piece was a work of art with deluxe ingredients that aren't usually incorporated in traditional omakase such as caviar, truffle, and foie gras, and one was even decorated with gold leaves. We also witnessed fresh wasabi being grated, which was something neither of us had seen before. Our chef was very receptive to our reaction to each course and answered any questions we had. After our last course, as die-hard uni lovers, we simply couldn't resist reordering the night's winner: Canadian uni with black sturgeon caviar on Japanese milk toast, topped with shaved black truffle. Do note that ordering a la carte was very pricey, so choose wisely (like we did :))TL;DR: First omakase experience for my best friend and probably ruined him for any future omakase. Innovative, deluxe, and well worth the price. Service was exceptional as they accommodated our late arrival extremely well.

No disrespect to any of the Ramen places I've been to, but Ichiran now takes the top spot on my Ramen mantel. The concept of eating ramen in an your own booth, and own your own time amplified the experience to the height I did not think possible. Of course the infamous cubicle style seating, and customization of the bowl added the individual experience, but the ramen itself is what I cannot stop raving about. At first glance it seems like your ordinary ramen bowl. Broth, meat, noodle, spice. However; when you mix these ingredients together at Ichiran you get something special. An explosion of flavor with every bite. The combination touches every flavor on the spectrum creating umami. "Pure glorious ramen to warm the soul" - Quote from me forcing myself to not have 2 more bowls PS: the staff was great

A very underrated ramen shop in Midtown right by Grand Central Terminal. Where else can you find a ramen shop fully run by Japanese staff members? This is as authentic as you can get!The service is very good! We were greeted with a big smile and were told to sit wherever we liked to. We chose the table furtherest away from the door. Throughout the experience, that smile never went away and it's great to see that when dining in.My gf and I split an order of Takoyaki. I burned my mouth because I was an idiot and popped an entire one in my mouth immediately when they brought it out. So just as a warning, take small bites and have a iced cold beer or cold water on standby.For ramen, I got the Tonkotsu which contained rich pork broth, Mugifuji pork shoulders, egg, green onion, and bamboo. The Mugifuji pork shoulder stood out to me the most and I tried to make that last as long as possible. The bamboo is one of my favorite ingredients in ramen and the egg was the perfect texture. There was a healthy amount of noodles in the bowl to definitely fill you up. My gf got the Bow Chili which had a decent amount of kick to it. It contained chicken and fish broth, spicy ground chicken, Mugifuji pork belly, egg, green onion, arugula, bean sprout, bamboo, and rayu. If I was feeling spicy, I would have gotten that instead.

I've walked by this gem countless times without a second glance, but I'm thrilled I decided to step in. The service here is exemplary, with staff that make you feel right at home. My Tuscana pizza arrived swiftly, and it was absolutely delicious – so tempting that I nearly devoured the entire thing myself, but I opted to share with my husband, much to his delight. The space has a cozy setup with minimal indoor seating, just a couple of counter seats, but there's a charming outdoor counter with four seats that I'm eager to try next time. This spot is a must-visit; don't make the mistake of passing it by like I did for so long!

Saw this pop up on yelp as I'm visiting NYC for the weekend. So glad I tried it! The hak rolls were pretty filling and the hak dumplings were filled well. Their filling is pretty different from average dumplings I've tried. It has a pretty large sign outside, but the interior was quite small. The decor was cute and simple. Only thing was it was cash only. Fairly priced for what you're getting. Great on the go meal. I would definitely stop by if you get a chance!

Title: Promising Start with Room for Improvement at New Eatery

I recently visited a new restaurant that just opened its doors two weeks ago. While it's clear they're still ironing out some issues, there's undeniable potential here. Opting to sit at the bar, I experienced great service and a delightful "Panda" sake served in an adorable keepsake glass—a step above their house sake, which was generously offered for comparison.

The highlight of my meal was undoubtedly the pork belly buns; a must-try that leaves a memorable impression with its flavors. However, I would advise against their ramen. Although it featured tasty elements, such as the pork, noodles, and egg, the broth's overwhelming soy sauce flavor dominated the dish and the lukewarm temperature was a letdown.

In summary, this spot has the makings of a great dining option—excellent service, charming drinks, and some standout dishes. With a little more attention to consistency and detail, particularly with their ramen, they could truly shine.

I had a Manila bowl and couldn't finish it all! Generous portion for sure. Fast casual place, where they make the bowl in front of you, but not a ton of places to sit especially when busy. Chinese brocoli isn't something I've had before but it's a great balance to the salty notes. lots of flavor, the poached egg is cool how ever they cook it, and the crispy garlic and shallots are  delicious. Why'd I take off a star? something is very salty - not sure if it's the meat itself or the sauces? It's happened twice now. So make sure you've got a glass of water with you.
