**CASH ONLY**I'm always a bit hesitant with pho places that are "instagram" worthy because usually the food suffers. But when one of my friends wanted to try this place out, I decided why not. When we arrived there we were seated right away. It was about 1/3 full so it wasn't as crowded and packed as other pho places. I decided to go with their spicy beef pho and my friend went for the original pho. Along with 2 Vietnamese Iced Coffees.I went to use the bathroom and right when I ordered and when I came back the pho was already there! I expected it to be cold since it was so fast but I was super surprised when the pho was piping hot. Other pho places I've found out that the broth was pretty lukewarm. But PhoBar definitely was not. Overall, it was a really good bowl of pho and I would definitely come back here again despite the hefty price tag. It's so totally worth it and everything was very clean!

Title: A Taco Haven in Chelsea Market

During my whirlwind day in New York, I discovered a true culinary treasure in Chelsea Market that compelled me twice over: a buzzing taco stand known for dishing out the best tacos I've ever savored. Nestled among the vibrant array of eateries and directly across from a burger spot, this gem attracts with a queue that's a testament to its popularity—yet fear not, for the line moves briskly.

The menu may be simple, but the flavors are anything but. The carne asada and chicken tacos burst with authenticity, while the quesadilla—a glorified, cheesy sibling to the taco—delights in its own right. Don't overlook the horchata; it's a creamy complement to the spice-kissed fare. 

While seating is not in the equation, the sheer joy of noshing on these tacos makes standing while eating an afterthought. Coupled with swift service and affable staff, it’s no wonder this place tops my NY food list. A plea to the owners: consider bringing this winning formula to DC, where I have no doubt it would be a resounding success.

Upon my arrival at MáLà Project, I was immediately enveloped by the warm, spicy aroma of chili peppers that brought an unexpected rush of nostalgia, reminiscent of my grandmother's kitchen back in China. The restaurant's ambiance is a cozy blend of tradition and modernity, with its simple wooden furniture set against a rustic brick backdrop, all to the tune of soft Chinese pop music.

The menu strikes a perfect balance between simplicity and variety, allowing diners the freedom to customize their own dry hot pot from selections of meats, vegetables, and carbs. Such versatility means that whether you're dining solo or sharing, satisfaction is guaranteed. Our meal was delivered promptly, boasting the vibrant flavors and freshness that are characteristic of a well-prepared hot pot.

While the Asian-inspired drinks menu appeared promising, the lychee mojito was a letdown, overly sweet and lacking the necessary kick of rum. Nevertheless, MáLà Project offers a quick, cozy dining experience that captures the essence of home, making it a suitable haven during the chill of the upcoming winter nights.

Title: Mediocre Experience at an Overhyped Pizzeria

Review:

I'm hovering around 3.5 stars for this place, as it was a solid "just okay" in my book. Expectations should be kept in check, especially with wait times; I'd suggest that anything over a 30-minute wait isn't worth it. Our order included a Margherita and a vodka sauce pizza. The Margherita came out on top with a nicely balanced tomato sauce that was complemented by some really tasty cheese. The vodka sauce pizza, however, fell flat, lacking in flavor and not worth a repeat order.

When it comes to value, it's hard to complain much given the low price point. Yet, the physical space could be a deal-breaker for some—it's cramped, to the point where you might struggle to find a spot to enjoy your slice. Additionally, the menu was a bit of a puzzle to decipher, and the dispirited staff didn't help to lift the mood of the crowded venue.

In comparison to other spots, I have a clear preference for Suprema Pizza, which outshines this establishment by a fair margin.

Was quite hyped to come here maybe that's also why I was so disappointed. The decor and design gives this place the feel of being trendy. The service is impeccable, attentive hostess and wait staff so no complaints there.The food is a different story... with the accessibility and availability of good authentic Mexican food (that's full of flavor) on the upper east side, I can say with certainty that this place is lacking a WOW factor. Their claim to fame when you read their "story" on the top portion of the menu, is that they focus on producing quality food that is authentic and fresh; so everything is "made to order".I was indecisive on what I should get so I went for the mostly healthy option of a burrito bowl (base + protein + sides and sauce). I chose the arugula and spinach (which turned out to be spinach only and was served more like a dressing for the bottom of the plate than a base); the Baja fish (bland cornmeal crusted pollock which was loaded with salt, lacked flavor and served room temperature not hot as if it were in fact just made); pico de Gallo (fresh ingredients but lacked flavor - tomatoes were over ripe and mushy, no balance or flavor, was definitely lacking something - this of course was loaded on to the plate), fresh corn, black beans (the most appetizing thing in the entire dish) & cotija cheese. All in all not worth the price. Much better fish tacos and good, flavorful, authentic and fresh Mexican in the neighborhood (mexicue, calexico, two lizards, conmigo, just to name a few). Even beyond going to a Mexican restaurant I've had better fish tacos at supply house which is a block away.Icing on the cake, this is Cascabel Taqueria West trying to rebrand itself which I discovered when I received three Bill. Which is even more surprising since Cascabel East pre-construction had some decent Mexican food. All in all spare yourself. The two stars is really just because the service was superb... otherwise it would receive a 0

Stopped by to see what all of the hype is. There was a huge line for it so it must be flipping good. The wait wasn't that bad as ordering food doesn't take too long. There's very limited option, but that's all you really need.I got one Carne Asada taco, one Pollo Asado taco, and one Carne Asada Quesadilla. They had these huge drums with drinks filled and got the Horchata out of curiosity. The quesadilla was essentially just a bigger tacos with cheese so I was disappointed in that. I would have just gotten a variety of quesadillas if I have known that. Besides that, they food is simple, yet amazing to eat. The Horchata is something worth trying as well if you like the taste of cinnamon. Definitely will be dropping by again for my taco cravings in the future.

I recently dined at a charming restaurant with a wonderfully unique decor, making it an ideal spot for a romantic date or a special celebration. We started with the curry puff, which had a delightfully flaky crust; however, the filling was somewhat dry. The chicken satay, while also on the dry side, was saved by a deliciously flavorful sauce. The standout dish was the Panang curry, thoughtfully enhanced with sweet potatoes—a pleasant twist to a classic. It was generously portioned, perfect for sharing. Despite a couple of shortcomings, the cozy ambiance and innovative touches make this restaurant worth visiting.

Title: A Fresh Take on Clean Eating at New Lunch Spot

I recently discovered a gem for lunch-goers keen on clean eating. This fairly new spot offers an array of delicious choices for those looking to maintain a healthy diet without sacrificing taste.

The Verde Veggie bowl, a crowd-pleaser at my office, features perfectly charred avocado and a surprisingly savory combo of kale and beans. Both the salmon and roasted chicken make for excellent protein additions. Set bowls ensure you get a consistent meal, but for the adventurous type, the make-your-own option offers a wide selection. Don't miss out on the Thai chili noodles and the surprisingly tasty vegan mash.

Another highlight is the charred avocado, paired well with their cauliflower, brown rice, and the robust flavors of the Mediterranean chicken and wings. The small venue comes with limited seating, so arrive early to beat the rush. Service is efficient, and prices are reasonable - ranging from $10.75 to $15, variables depending on additions.

Overall, this lunch spot is a delightful surprise, breaking the stereotype that healthy food can't be appetizing. With a good flavor profile and a variety of options, it's become my go-to for a satisfying, health-conscious lunch.

Title: Mixed Experiences at Italian Gem

I recently dined at a charming Italian restaurant during their restaurant week, which also features a comparable year-round lunch Prix fixe menu. For starters, the minestrone soup and tender meatballs served in hearty portions were satisfying. However, the main courses left something to be desired. The Dorade, while cooked well, was underwhelming in size and lacked distinctive flavors. The Gramigna pasta offered intriguing tastes but was marred by an overly oily consistency. All in all, while the restaurant presents a promising range of pasta, seafood, and meat options, the execution on some of the main dishes could benefit from a tweak or two.

This may be one of my favorite Americanized-style Korean place there is. We definitely waited awhile to get a seat here as it's always so crowded! They actually have a cafe that they partner with and turn into a low-key bar at night so that guests waiting for the restaurant can go up the block to this bar to enjoy some of their classic soju drinks that come in plastic bags with a lit-up ice cube. Pretty cool and great quality drinks.The food and aroma of this restaurant is literally to die for. If you love the smell of truffles, this will be your heaven.This is a Korean tapas style restaurant, so definitely come hungry and order a lot. We had the truffle mac and cheese, the kimchi paella, the gnocchi, Korean fried chicken and the steak. I would say every single dish was amazing except probably the Korean fried chicken, but that's only because I've had better in KTown. To call out my 3 favorites would be 1) the truffle mac and cheese for obvious reasons - cheesy, chewy and truffe-ly; 2) Kimchi Paella; 3) Gnocchi. If you can stand the wait, this place is worth it! Definitely check it out!

If you're in for a night of drinks and fun, this spot doesn't disappoint with their outrageous drink deals! It's a haven for those with a sweet tooth for skittle bombs and those looking for wallet-friendly sips; imagine grabbing buckets of domestic brews for just $15 or leveling up to imported for a mere $20 on select days. Deals seem to be a constant here, so your wallet will thank you.

Entrance requires a legit ID as they are strict with carding and scanning at the door, ensuring a mature crowd inside. This spacious venue also features beer pong in the back, perfect for some friendly competition. With a clientele primarily ranging from 21 to 35, the energy is vibrant and youthful. I skipped the food in favor of the drinks this time, but that just gives me another reason to return.

Had a lovely meal here with a large group. We ordered a bunch of things on their menu and shared it family style. The staff was really lovely and helpful with picking the entrees. The server recommended the spare ribs which is their most famous dish. I liked that it wasn't too sweet. Other highlights were the Grand Marnier Shrimp and the Black Bean Scallops. The brussel sprouts were also really tasty. I think this place has Szechuan influences, but I didn't think it was too spicy and I'm not a spice eater.Definely recommend for a try.

Came here kind of not expecting much. Came with a party of 4 and as a walk in.Got the toro ssam bap , fried chicken, soon du boo, so ramyun and fish coop.Everything was delicious here. Toro with some uni is always a luxurious dish and this was no exception.The soon du boo...I thought it was not necessarily focused on the tofu and I really enjoyed it because it ended up tasting like a soup. There was something interesting in it (I forget what) but I enjoyed it a lot more than I normally enjoy this dish.The fried chicken, was so good. Kind of reminded me of karage but the chicken was in the bones. So crunchy and juicy, was done amazingly well. Tastes good without any sauce and the sauce compliments it well.The ramyun (it's really the same as ramen to me) we're delicious. I liked the SO one better as it was much more rich and am glad I shared it with folks. It's too rich for one person, but split 3 ways makes it the perfect amount. Having the veal pieces was a bit interesting, I didn't care too much for the chicken pieces though. The fish one was a nice bonito broth and complemented the other ramyun really well since it's a much lighter broth. Sharing is the way to go for these noodles IMOAll in all came out to be about 34 a person, which is incredibly reasonable for a meal like this. Also, everyone there is a chef! They just rotate roles. That was one of my favorite parts

Ho Foods has been popular among Taiwanese group recently and finally we were here to try with homesick. There is limited choice on the menu, Ho Foods classic "Red Cooked" and sides. The beef noodles soup was pricey ($15.5, we add extra greens $3 and tendon $5) but delicious with high quality ingredients and their broth was cooked perfectly balanced with bone and marrow for 24 hours. Sides were also good especially today's special - tomato and egg, it was soft with butter and sugar. Overall, their food was good and service was adequate. We will visit again to try their breakfast menu.

Tucked away in a charming neighborhood near Central Park, I recently stumbled upon a quaint pizza joint that made for a pleasant surprise. A mere 10-15 minute stroll from the park, the unassuming exterior belied a spacious interior with ample seating hidden beyond the restrooms.

The selection of pizza was modest, offering just 3-4 classic varieties. While this limited choice might not satisfy every palate, the quality of their offerings was solid. Each slice was reheated to perfection in their impressive pizza oven upon ordering. A side of ranch dressing and a range of chilled soft drinks provided a nice touch.

In terms of value, the prices were reasonable for the area. Although this spot doesn't rank at the top of my NYC pizza list due to its limited selection, the cozy atmosphere and good pizza make it worth a visit for those looking for a casual bite in a less hectic part of town.
Um yeah.  You can't go wrong for Italian food.  Wow this place is amazing.  It is a bit cramped space and crowded but the food is why you come here.  Just try everything.  It is well worth it.

As a Dominican native from Miami, FL, finding authentic cuisine away from home can be a challenge, but this gem is the real deal! The queso frito was indulgently cheesy, the mangu perfectly mashed and comforting, and the salami added just the right touch of savory goodness. Their café con leche? Smooth, rich, and brimming with flavor—exactly as it should be. This spot is a must-visit for me on my next trip to New York. A genuine Dominican café that feels like home. Highly recommend!

Panna II is all about the experience! It's fun to be in such an overwhelming atmosphere with friends you enjoy being with and can fun around. The food is okay. It's BYOB so make sure you're good on that front. They bring glasses and open bottles for you. Today, went in and they squeezed my group of 5 in. Service is prompt. Music is upbeat and loud. Birthdays are fun here!

Title: Generous Portions at Kaoru Bowl 

My recent visit to Kaoru bowl was a testament to their motto of quantity meeting value. The "Three Amigos" bowl I ordered was impressively large, living up to the hype with a generous serving of fish. Unfortunately, customization seemed limited; my request to swap spicy tuna for salmon wasn't accommodated, leading to an all-tuna experience. While the quality of fish was generally solid, I encountered a few chewier pieces. Overall, Kaoru offers straightforward, sizable bowls that provide good bang for your buck, though it doesn't quite go beyond the basics.

As a steadfast enthusiast in search of the city's finest Thai cuisine, my recent visit to Noree Thai Bistro was a noteworthy experience. Although it didn't ascend to my top three Thai spots, the restaurant still stands out for serving up satisfactory dishes within a spacious and trendy setting, perfect for laid-back dining encounters.

The pricing was reasonable, especially given the quality of the food on offer. The standout dish of our meal was unquestionably the Lemongrass marinated chicken satay. The aromatic marinade was a delight, and the chicken was exceptionally tender, effortlessly sliding off the skewer — a dish I'd emphatically recommend.

Our main course, the Pad Kee Mao, with its delicate balance of rice noodles, chili garlic sauce, and an assortment of vegetables, was flavorful, though the mild spice level was surprisingly spirited. It was a savory plate that left an impression.

Here's a quick take on Noree Thai Bistro:
- Food: 3.5/5
- Service/Speed: 3.8/5
- Price: $
- Ambiance: Casual and energetic

In sum, if you're in the mood for a relaxed Thai meal that's easy on the wallet and lively in atmosphere, Noree provides a satisfying option. Don't miss out on their chicken satay for a true taste delight!

We have been to Saxon + Parole many times for brunch and dinner. We definitely prefer the brunch. The cocktails in many ways are the stars with excellent food to match. Great spot and always busy so it has a good vibe.

Title: A Satisfying Dim Sum Experience at The New Lunar Year

Celebrating the New Lunar Year at our go-to spot for Dim Sum, we were pleasantly surprised to be seated immediately upon our noon arrival on a busy Saturday— a stark contrast to the usual lines snaking outside. The expansive venue is a beacon for those of us conveniently located near each other, making it a reliable choice for gatherings.

The vast array of fresh Dim Sum didn't disappoint. While we were stationed near the stage, which limited the cart traffic to our area, it was only a minor inconvenience to fetch our selections. Nonetheless, it's a point for the management to consider for improving service coverage.

A slight hiccup was the sticky rice, which fell short in moisture and the anticipated 'surprise' ingredients found within. But that was a small dent in the otherwise flavorful and diverse offerings. The advice for future patrons: arrive with an appetite, as the variety is indeed extensive. Overall, a solid choice for those with a hankering for authentic Dim Sum.

What a great improvement! The food and the service was fantastic! The manager asked us back to give them another chance. Im glad we did. We actually went back last night for dinner and again for lunch this afternoon. Give them a shot! :)

This is not my usual type of place, but I won a gift card to Mandarin Oriental that wouldn't have made a dent in the price of a hotel stay, so I decided to use it for my birthday meal at Asiate. The pre-fixe dinner menu was very limited, more so for my husband who is allergic to shellfish. I had my eye on the quail appetizer, but the sauce on it would've been sweet so we both got the bigeye tuna tartare which looked pretty impressive, but was just okay. A more generous portion of fish than you'd usually get for an appetizer like this, but that fish wasn't well-balanced with other flavors/textures. I got the teeny tiny lamb loin which came with a teeny tiny piece of eggplant and a micro polenta cake (the highlight of the dish). My husband ordered the braised short rib - $10 supplement - which was a larger portion and had a very nice texture. My chocolate cake desert and my husband's creme brulee were great! It was a little silly for them to bring out an extra chocolate cake for my birthday, but I asked for them to pack it up and I was very happy to eat it at home the next day. I will say that the servers are very professional and friendly.

This restaurant was a convenient location while I had a break from jury duty. It was a quiet restaurant that made it nice to sit and read a book. I enjoyed a glass of Chardonnay and one of their salads. The chicken on my salad was a little burnt but I know some people really enjoyed that. The homemade dressing was really good as well as the complimentary bread and butter. I'm not always in the area but would definitely love to try some of their pasta or chicken dishes in the future.

**Title: A Delightful Dining Experience at Joe Allen**

Venturing into Joe Allen on a friend's recommendation turned out to be the highlight of our first night in NYC. Our anticipation was met with a warm welcome from an incredibly nice host who assured us of an imminent table with utmost courtesy. As we sipped on a complimentary glass of champagne from the amazing lady bartender, the anticipation grew.

Settling at our table, which was adorned with whimsical animal plates that the kids adored, the service remained top-notch with the arrival of our friendly waiter. The food journey began with the Burrata and Tuna tartare, each bite an indulgent affair, deliciously whetting our appetite for the main courses. The lamb chops were exceptional, boasting succulence and flavor, while the Branzino alla piastra impressed with its perfect balance of crispy skin and moist flesh, a true testament to culinary expertise.

Meanwhile, the kids devoured the Rigatoni alla Bolognese, with my daughter declaring it a match to her favorite rendition of the dish. This speaks volumes, as any parent knows the challenge of pleasing young palates. We wrapped up our meal with the Pistachio biscotti, a crunchy delight that paired beautifully with our after-dinner coffee.

In a nutshell, Joe Allen not only charmed us with stellar service but also left a lasting impression with their exceptional cuisine. I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a memorable meal in the city. It's a must-visit!

I went to HB Burger for lunch with my colleagues. I tried there southern chicken sandwich. I asked them to switch the fried chicken with grilled. The sandwich came with fries and pickle. My colleagues liked their food too. The price was 17$ which I thought was a bit expensive compared to other places nearby. The service was great.

Title: A Fresh and Delightful Experience at Chelsea Market

I recently had the opportunity to dine at a vibrant spot in Chelsea Market and I must say, it was quite the treat! The establishment prides itself on its fresh fare, with meals prepared right before your eyes, adding an engaging twist to the dining experience.

The menu, transparent and accommodating, clearly marks which dishes are vegan or contain lard. As a diner with specific dietary preferences, I found this particularly helpful. I opted for the chicken taco, and it was nothing short of excellent – a flavorful journey that I highly recommend.

Guests have the pleasure of personalizing their tacos with a variety of toppings, which is a fun touch. Although there isn't traditional seating, the venue offers a standing cart area that allows you to mingle and enjoy the bustling ambiance of the market.

In sum, this spot is a must-try for anyone visiting Chelsea Market, especially for those who appreciate a side of lively atmosphere with their freshly prepared meal.

Title: A Fiery Experience with Mera Mera Soba

I recently visited a restaurant that prides itself on a variety of soba noodle dishes. The Mera Mera dipped soba caught our attention, promising a kick of heat. The portion size is generous, particularly as we opted to share, suspecting it might be more than meets the eye. Indeed, the dish proved to be quite satisfying and more filling than its modest appearance suggested.

The soba noodles were a textural delight, cooked to an ideal firmness that complemented the interactive dipping experience. However, the accompanying hot broth was a double-edged sword. Its spiciness was intense, and the salt level was disappointingly high—a persistent issue even after diluting the broth in an attempt to mitigate the saltiness.

While the intrinsic flavor hinted at the potential for a harmonious blend of heat and savoriness, this balance was overpowered by the excessive salinity and spice. With a more measured hand on these two components, this dish could have been a standout. If you're a fan of bold and fiery flavors and don't mind a saltier profile, this could be up your alley. But for those with a milder palate, proceed with caution.

Title: A Culinary Masterpiece: Modern Indian Cuisine Like No Other

If I had to encapsulate my dining experience at this restaurant in one word, it would be "unreal." From the moment we stepped in to celebrate a special occasion, the chef's tasting menu promised an extraordinary journey, and it delivered beyond expectations.

Each plate was not just a dish but a work of art, presenting flavors that tantalized the taste buds with every bite. The highlight for me was the 'makhan malai' – its taste simply indescribable in its exquisiteness; it's a must-try that I urge everyone to experience.

The 'gola' was a nostalgic twist that transported me back to my childhood, imbuing traditional tastes with modern culinary techniques. As a lifelong connoisseur of Indian cuisine, this restaurant has redefined my appreciation for the art of modern Indian food.

In summary, this establishment is not just worth a visit – it demands it for anyone looking to discover the pinnacle of contemporary Indian gastronomy.

We lucked upon this place a short walk from the World Trade Center memorial as we headed toward Battery Park. I wanted specifically to try these new veggie burgers I have been hearing so much about that look and taste close to real meat, called the "impossible burger" and/or the "beyond burger". Bill's had the "beyond burger" and I must say it was pretty close to the taste of meat, the appearance reminded me of a turkey burger in color. Was it good, I would say yes it was, I enjoyed it. Now that I'm back at home, I'm trying to find it locally! Bill's was busy and pub style feel with full bar and plenty of seating and booths. Lots of families enjoying a beautiful NYC day!

I hate the name of this place.  It's long, hard to remember, and seems to change (When/why did they add the "Real"?  Did someone challenge their authenticity?)  But other than that, this place is pretty fantastic.Located in the Theater District, a stone's throw from Times Sq, RKFLSNR (*insert eye roll*) this small but authentic Chinese restaurant is a popular spot for tourists and locals alike.  We were on the UWS and craving soup dumplings, but didn't want to trek all the way to Chinatown, so this place was the perfect compromise.  We were disappointed to find that the time listed on the Yelp Waitlist feature was incorrect; it said there was no wait, but were told 15-20 minutes when we arrived.The food is delicious, very carb- and meat forward.  We had the pork soup dumplings ($8.95), pan-fried Peking duck buns ($9.25), and house special stir-fry ramen ($14.95).  The soup dumplings were on point and the ramen was really tasty!  Skip the Michelin-recommended Peking duck buns though; it was expensive and was made of more bun than duck.

Whenever I pass through Penn Station, I make it a point to grab a slice at the nearby pizzeria. The service is consistently fast and the pizza epitomizes a good, classic New York slice. It's a reliable spot for a quick and satisfying bite.

Title: Budget-Friendly Burgers with a Side of Surliness

While the service at this local joint may come off as unenthusiastic and the wait for take-out can test your patience, the wallet-friendly prices are hard to fault. The burgers surpass the typical diner fare, and the fries are dependable, though a more generous portion wouldn't hurt. Price-wise, it's a steal compared to nearby competitors without skimping on taste. That said, beware the sneaky credit card surcharge – a detail they're not keen on advertising.

Title: Light Bites and Refreshments at a Bustling Spot

We popped into this bustling eatery for a casual snack and a drink, starting our visit with a stop at the bar. The cucumber Collins caught our eye - a delightful choice, proving to be light and wonderfully refreshing. Once we secured a table, we ventured into the appetizer menu with mixed results.

The crab cakes sadly fell short of expectations, presenting a mushy texture that left us unimpressed and certain we wouldn't reorder. However, the Kobe sliders redeemed our experience with their savory taste, even if their size teased our palate, disappearing almost in a single bite.

An unexpected delight was the complimentary snacks - a thoughtful touch that added value to our visit. The candied walnuts, peanuts, and sour cream & onion chips were a hit at our table.

In summary, while not all menu items hit the mark, the stand-out drink and free snacks made for a pleasant visit.

Small note: Please add a lunch special menu. It'll be hard to maintain this rating especially compared to the old Nepalese place if most lunches are a bit more expensive than the rest of the block. Anyway:This is a new rather fancier Nepalese/Himalayan place found in this area. They open a bit past 12 though the first time I passed, they weren't open yet. It'll serve as a good albeit more expensive replacement to the unfortunately closed Dhaulagiri Kitchen (hope they add similar lunch specials soon.) I ordered the Daal Bhaat Massu (or Masu according to most other places,)  It's listed as: Thali. Typical Himalayan platter with a choice of vegetable, chicken, lamb or goat. This platter is served with mustard green spinach, vegetable & traditional black lentils, salad, achar, papad and rice. The prices range from $12.99 to $15.99 I believe which is a bit more than some of the other places.I got the lamb version which came with dal/lentils, a quite good pea/potato dish, and a very well flavored lamb curry. Along with the main meal, there was rice with peas, papadum (bread,) and a small bit of spiced pickled bitter gourd (wish there was a bit more.) Side note: I am unsure if they give refills of the Thali like other places.The food there was good and I wish I had more time but I arrived there a bit later than I hoped so I had to leave. The staff was nice as well. The person next to me had some momo which came out fast and they looked good as well. I hope this place does well though the prices might be a little high for the general clientele who eat here often. Upper 4 for now (would be rounded down if this place was older.)

I didn't expect the food here to be so good, especially since it was just Italian food in the Village, which there are a ton of and most make relatively mediocre options. But from appetizers to dessert we were quite impressed with the overall quality!We knew the meal was going to be good after our appetizer, the roasted mushrooms, which came with an egg and some shaved ricotta salata on top. The balance with the mushrooms, pancetta and cheese was beautiful, and the flavor was on point, without being too seasoned.Then came the pasta dishes, which were amazing! The spaghetti was super simple, with just olive oil and parmesan crisps, but you could taste the quality in its simplicity, with the garlic folding into oils, and blending in with the pasta.The tagliatelle was my favorite of the two pasta dishes, having a beautiful rich flavor, with a beautiful meat sauce and pasta that was cooked incredibly well. The pasta was slightly chewy, with a beautiful texture and consistency.And dessert surprisingly was quite amazing. We had the olive oil cake, and from the photos it looks like an extremely dried piece of cake. But when you actually get it, its so moist and delicious. I particularly liked the light pieces of salt on the cream, which parred down the sweetness and oil from the raisins, olive oil and cream.

Review #2 - Wednesday Well, with "feels like 17 degrees" outside, we ended up going to the Taste & Grind again. The prices were no less steep, but the service was so much better. That makes all the difference in the world. The food ranged from good to great. We collectively shared the grilled cheese (very buttery but crispy and excellent), the greens salad and garlic knots (excellent), octopus and mushrooms and Yukon potatoes and Brussel sprouts (all very good - though rather small portions for the price), and the fries (greasy and limp again). All in all - a much better experience, with live music (nice, but loud and impeding conversation, bit great ambience) and an attentive and friendly server. -------Review #1 - Monday Two-part restaurant attached to Executive Le Soleil Hotel. The Grind is more of the live music place, and The Taste is all day food and drink options. I went to The Taste for lunch - as it was bitter cold out and I decided to try this place - conveniently off the lobby area of the hotel I am in. Limited menu options -- and pretty steep prices. $18 for a chicken sandwich. They don't really have Happy Hour prices, though they do offer  1/2 price bottles of wine on given days. Food is good, but nothing super special. Fries were a bit limp and greasy, but plentiful. The "crispy" Brussel sprouts were good, but not at all crispy. The fried chicken sandwich was excThere is a tv at the bar, and music playing overhead. Staff is competent, but didn't find them overly welcoming or accommodating. They are they type of folks that seem to be here "to do a job" - which is okay, but it means I would choose (and recommend) other places for food or drink in the future.

My recent visit to this sushi spot was a delightful experience. With no reservations and limited seating around the sushi bar, I appreciated the cozy ambiance. The menu, while small, provided an excellent selection, including a set menu and a la carte options.

As a first-time guest, I was grateful for our attentive waiter who took the time to explain the menu and the proper way to enjoy the rolls. Opting for the 4-hand roll, I found it to be perfectly satisfying in portion. Presented on a simple piece of paper, the rolls are served sequentially, allowing one to savor each creation. The seaweed's crispness, the warmth of the rice, and the freshness of the filling were memorable.

Concluding the meal was seamless with the bill promptly provided, paving the way for an easy payment at the register. This establishment has certainly earned a return visit from me.

I've had a lot of Mediterranean bowls but never one as wholesome as the one from Nanoosh. The rice and quinoa bowls are served with generous amounts of sauces and spreads and the proteins are fresh and organic! I got a baked falafel bowl with avocado sauce, hummus and tatziki on quinoa I

Great spot for seafood. The items are nice and fresh. I love coming for the happy hour (just keep in mind it does get packed during those times). The ambiance is great. It's nice a chill. I love the outdoor seating so take advantage when there is decent weather. The service is usually fast and the staff is very friendly.

Ordered delivery from Dafni late night to my office, and they came very fast surprisingly! I got a Greek salad (added chicken breast +$4) with a side of pita bread! The salad was huge and had an ample amount of feta cheese, which I loved. The grilled chicken was a little bland for my liking, but it was healthy and fresh. Maybe next time I'd opt for chicken shish kebab instead for some more flavor/space. To my surprise, there were also two grape leaves hidden in the salad which were DELICIOUS! The salad was big enough to eat for two meals, and I order from here quite a lot!

Cull & Pistol have been on my must try list for some time. So, I was beyond excited to check them out, especially since I have an uber obsession with oysters. It's become a twice a week habit for me.I was really looking forward to coming here given their reputation for top quality, varied selection at happy hour prices, which is currently $1.50 for any of the ones they offer. What I despise, and find beyond unappealing, is having to sit at a bar or facing forward (as opposed to looking at my dinner companion) and staring at the bar in order to get the happy hour option. Here, that's the only choice.Frankly, 9 out of 10 times, I don't stay at restaurants like that. If it hadn't been for my husband, I would have left. I would prefer to go elsewhere, or or sit at a table and pay the full price, than be subjected to sit awkwardly and uncomfortably, which I was. It was really hard to get past the fact that I was boxed into a six inch space, with the food crammed on this tiny dining area.That said, we got at C&P around 5:15 p.m., and there was no wait. We got seated (at the bar) right away. I ordered a dozen oysters and left it up to the waiter to choose which ones he liked. I appreciated that when they were served, it was done in an orderly fashion so that I could take note of which ones I liked for our next visit.There is no denying the freshness or the quality of the oysters here. But, if I had to pick between getting oysters here or at, say, Crave Fishbar, where you get the same top selection and the same happy hour prices, but served at a table, I'm going to go with the latter.Walking into Cull & Pistol you see that it's a very small place. Very small. But they make the most of the small space and are very inviting.The hubby ordered disco fries, which are basically fries with a can of New England clam chowder poured all over them. He loved them. I didn't get how this creative. It was delicious, but very low rent. We also ordered pistols on horseback. It was different. It came out in a minuscule portion of two small crackers or bites. Jayson said it was very salty and tasted like seaweed. It wasn't particularly filling either. Very small and forgettable. I actually had to look at their site to remember what it was ... I blocked it out.Service wise, it was excellent. They were very attentive and from the backwaiters to the people behind the bar, it was pleasant and delightful.Oysters were delicious. But, the set up and dining situation really ruined the experience for me. And while, it was great to get a reasonably priced meal in Chelsea Market, I'd much rather go around the corner to Jeffrey's, where you don't feel like you're be rushed through in the cheap section. Would I go back? The jury is still out.

Healthy, you can taste the natural ingredients without heavy sauces. Nice ambience. You can tell the chef has a simple, elegant style. I recommend the Sesame crusted seared ahi tuna salad. It was fresh and the sesame made the tuna super crunchy on the outside. I loved the water; mimosa not so much but that might be because I don't like sweet drinks. Xoxox

Title: A Plant-Based Haven for Sushi Lovers

From the moment I stepped into the restaurant, I was greeted with a pleasant surprise – vegan sushi that tantalized the taste buds beyond expectation. The memory of it is so vivid and delightful that I find myself yearning for another taste as I share this experience. Accompanying the sushi, we savored a beautifully crafted beet and "feta" salad, its visual appeal matched only by its flavorsome quality. For dessert, a warm, soft, and utterly scrumptious cookie provided the perfect sweet conclusion to our meal. This place is a gem for vegans and non-vegans alike, and it’s with eager anticipation that I say we will definitely be returning.

I've ordered from this restaurant a few times via MealPal and sampled their Spaghetti Bolognese and Gnocchi. Both dishes were enjoyable but didn't particularly stand out. Portion sizes were modest, which might be a point to consider depending on your appetite. As for the ambiance, the restaurant exudes authenticity and the staff are genuinely welcoming, making it a pleasant dining spot overall.

Great spot for lunch... wonderful cafe with nice backdrop. Stopped in for late lunch on Saturday afternoon and got a nice seat outside by the fountain. We had wonderful service as well... We had the crispy calamari for an appetizer and the light lunch special for $24 where you pick two select items. Had the wrap and soup of the day... Then some iced coffee and the most delicious dessert a coconut pineapple layer cake with coconut sorbet. This was really delicious and I was told all the desserts are made in house and I could definitely tell. I thought the place was a little pricey but clearly you are paying for the atmosphere and location. I really enjoyed it here and I would definitely return.

Visited the new eatery that took over Mew Men's spot, greeted by the lively shouts of cooks and servers. The interior remains familiar with its bench and bar seating. The menu mirrors its predecessor, albeit with a noticeable uptick in prices. I settled on the Spicy Shoyu Ramen, priced at $16, alongside a $7 Sapporo; the beer selection was limited but there were intriguing sake and wine choices, though pricier.

The ramen arrived promptly, a fiery red bowl with a decent kick, tender meat, and a lone pork slice, but the noodle portion was lacking, leaving a surplus of broth. Extras like a hard-boiled egg came at an additional cost, which, in hindsight, I regretfully skipped. In summary, while the ramen was satisfactory, the cost-value balance didn't quite hit the mark. The complimentary green tea at meal's end was a welcomed gesture.

Title: A Spirited Evening at a Trendy Korean Fusion Tapas Bar

I recently visited a lively and stylish restaurant that offers a unique blend of Korean tapas with a modern moon/barn ambiance, making for an intriguing dining experience. The reservation process via Yelp was seamless, and we were promptly seated for our party of three during happy hour.

The cocktail menu, particularly their soju selections, was a highlight, with each of the three out of five that I sampled proving to be exceptional - especially at the happy hour price of $6. Their culinary offerings were just as impressive, featuring farm-to-table ingredients that really shone through in terms of freshness and flavor.

Standout dishes included the Truffle Rice Cake & Cheese, which was a comforting twist on the classic mac-and-cheese, and the Roasted Vegetables topped with maple toasted almonds and chives—a dish that would make anyone crave their greens. The heartiness of the Hotstone Bowl of Bulgogi satisfied our craving for a substantial meal, while the wings, available in Hot & Spicy and Soy-Garlic varieties, were an absolute must-try.

One minor disappointment was the Korean Escargot, which was slightly overdone, creating some concern about the consistency of the menu offerings. This dish might not make it back to our table on a future visit.

Service was efficient, though we did have to flag down our server for the check. Be mindful that the restrooms are located downstairs and are not wheelchair-accessible, which might be a consideration for some guests.

With its fantastic drink selections, delightful food, and vibrant atmosphere, this restaurant is certainly worth a return visit. Just keep in mind their happy hour runs from 4-6pm Monday through Friday, and doors don't open until noon daily.

I ordered delivery from here tonight. Heard they were good. I ordered the buckaroo burger and the vegan carrot cake (no, I'm clearly not vegan). The buckaroo burger had excellent mushrooms and bacon. The cheddar cheese was melted and it arrived warm. The bread was fresh too. The carrot cake was chilled and tasted yummy! I love the icing.  Everything was packaged neatly! No mess. Would've given 5 stars if not for the expensive prices. Can get a delicious burger much cheaper elsewhere. This place is good once in a while for me!

A little background: I've often visited the area in the vicinity of the restaurant for speakeasies and other related nightlife shenanigans. Google suggested that this place would be a good match for me based on my previous restaurant history. On at least two occasions Oiji was full and there was a significant wait if you had no reservation. Cue last visit where a friend of mine asked to join me on my foodie adventures. Oiji immediately popped into my head and I went to work on getting the reservation. If you're using an app like OpenTable you better get your reservations in two weeks ahead of time. This place is popular, but not large, so it fills up fairly quickly. First things first, RSVP. Ok, so once you're in, you're going to L-O-V-E the food. We had the Calamari, Mini-Octopus, Korean Fried Chicken and the Bone Marrow (which pretty much stole the show)! We had some Soju as well but I don't remember the make or flavor. Unfortunately, we didn't have dessert but I think we'll make a point of it next time. They've found a way to combine an awesome atmosphere with great Korean food. I can think of only one other restaurant that can compete. Anyways, the service was very attentive and the menu had a lot of options. I think we'll be back. You should come too!

We were two couples at this lovely intimate seafood/Mediterranean restaurant. It overlooks the river and you can sit outside in the warmer weather. As I peeked out the window, there was Lady Liberty, lit up in all her glory giving me goosebumps.   We had drinks which were delicious and topped to the brim of the glass.  My sangria was deliciously  filled with raspberries and blueberries.  Two if had the whole Bronzino with rice and asparagus.  We shared a Greek salad.  My husband had the flavorful tuna steak and our guest had the lamb chops. Everyone was very happy.   We were bursting at the seams and couldn't do dessert this time.  We will have to come back because the food was great ...portions were huge and prices were more than fair. This was our kind of restaurant.

Title: A Lively Evening at the Local Pizzeria

From the moment we walked into this bustling pizzeria, we knew we were in for a treat. Despite the somewhat cramped quarters and the din of conversation, the vibrant energy was perfect for a night out with friends.

Kicking things off with Frozen Peach Bellinis, we raised our glasses to a night of indulgence. These sweet, strong concoctions were the ideal partner to our impromptu pizza feast and a pleasant twist from the usual beer offerings.

A surprise dish, the Popcorn Cacio e Pepe, graced our table courtesy of our delightful server. The combination of pecorino, olive oil, and black pepper made for a tasty appetizer as we eagerly awaited our main course.

The Dangerfield pizza, with its succulent béchamel sauce, pork-veal meatballs, ricotta, and garlic chips, was a unanimous hit. Its flavors were so enticing that even amidst our group, I found myself wishing I could savor an entire pie solo.

While the Dangerfield stole the show, the Paul's Boutique Dijon pizza was a personal favorite of mine. It was like enjoying breakfast and dinner simultaneously, with its innovative mix of pastrami, smoked red kraut, fontina cheese, 1000 island dressing, and an everything bagel crust.

Though the SR Fried Potatoes were decent, they paled in comparison to the stellar pizzas that dominated our dining experience.

Service here was nothing short of friendly and efficient, adding to the charm of the neighborhood vibe. I'm already looking forward to my next visit where I plan to dive into more unique pizza creations or perhaps even craft my own.

In summary, if you're in search of a lively spot for delicious wood-fired pizza and delightful drinks, this is the place to be. Just remember to bring your sociable spirit, or opt for a quieter night in.

As a regular patron of this restaurant over the years, I can confidently say that the quality of both the food and service has remained consistently high. The starters, especially the gobi manchurian and aloo tilki chat, are very good and set the stage for an enjoyable meal. The main course staples like roti, raita, and aloo mutter never fail to delight with their delicious flavors. However, it's worth noting that rice comes at an additional charge, so keep that in mind when ordering. All in all, the restaurant continues to be a reliable choice for a great dining experience.

I was craving Thai food and being so close to home I figured I check out this new place. I ordered online and picked up at the restaurant. Inside was small but very clean. The female at the register was friendly. I've had drunken noodles at several places, this is the first time I've had it with tomato chunks. It felt so misplaced, I didn't care for it nor was I a fan of the excess onions. I also ordered the jad jaan shrimp, it wasn't spicy but the flavor was decent. I had high expectations for this place. I like the idea of variety foods in the neighborhood but this wasn't exactly up to par. This place wasn't bad, I just wasn't impressed. I may try something else on the menu at a later date.

Soba azuma is an extremely good choice when the weather is super hot! We came here when there was a heat wave (100+ degrees!!). We decided that we wanted something cold, and this is one of the places that appeared. The place was not too crowded around 8 PM on a Saturday, which is really nice! For a party of 3, we waited for around 10 minutes without a reservation. There are a lot of options on the menu. Moreover, you have the option to pick between hot/cold noodles and the size (small, medium, large) all for the same price! The price for each item is also fairly inexpensive for New York standards. I ended up getting a combo with some cold udon and chicken egg rice. The cold udon was really refreshing. The udon was also cooked perfectly, a little chewy but not too hard. The chicken egg rice was amazing. It was flavored just right, not too scary and not too unflavorful. My friends also got something similar and we all loved our food and finished it really fast. This is definitely a place I would come back to and eat here regularly :)

I recently discovered a hidden gem of a restaurant where I had the pleasure of trying their spicy tomato ramen, and it was nothing short of amazing. The creaminess of the broth paired with the perfect level of heat made it a dish I wholeheartedly recommend to fellow tomato aficionados. Additionally, they boast a commendable selection of sake to complement the meal. Definitely a spot worth checking out for those looking for a unique and delicious dining experience.

The Jazz & Blues Preservation hosted the fabulous headline singer Yuko Ito and the premiere songster Nabuko Jazz. A great time that was had by one and all at Renaissance Harlem located on 132nd Street and "Leonard Harper Way" (7th. Ave.) the centerpiece of Harlem's Jazz Age & Renaissance. Wonderful & Tasty food, Marvelous Drinks with Great people and Jazz music to go with... Everybody get on board. Fun for the entire family. Be there or be Square baby.

Title: A Delectable Dive into Thai Delicacies at Top Thai Vintage

Review:

My recent dining experience at Top Thai Vintage in Greenwich was nothing short of delightful. The restaurant exudes charm with its unique décor, whisking you away to another time in Thailand. It's more spacious and inviting than its counterpart, Top Thai Greenwich, which adds to the overall comfort.

During a midweek dinner with K, we indulged in the Premium Platter – a customizable appetizer trio. Our selection included shrimp dumplings reminiscent of Har Gao, albeit with a pleasantly thicker skin. The crispy shrimp rolls were a standout, each featuring a whole straightened shrimp within. The BBQ chicken served with Jeaw sauce had the perfect balance of juiciness and zest.

The Top Thai spring rolls earned themselves a fan in me with their crispy exterior and succulent chicken, bean sprouts, and glass noodle stuffing. A vegetarian variant is available, catering to different dietary preferences.

Beverage-wise, the Thai Iced Tea was a highlight, offering a robust tea flavor sweetened by condensed milk, while the Lychee Iced Tea provided a lighter, subtly sweet alternative.

The Tom Yum Hot Pot impressed with its adjustable spiciness, tender vegetables, and succulent shrimp. Our moderate heat choice was spot on. Equally satisfying was the Khao Soi with its creamy yellow curry and perfectly cooked noodles and chicken.

The Kua Gai Noodle - with its thick, sautéed noodles accompanied by chicken, squid, and egg - was an absolute treat. And K couldn't get enough of the Crispy duck with Basil and Udon noodles, a dish where the crisp skin, thick noodles, and slightly spicy sauce harmoniously came together.

For dessert, the Vanilla Ice Cream and Taro custard were the perfect end to our meal.

In summary, Top Thai Vintage is a must-visit for its delectable offerings like the Thai Iced Tea, Spring rolls, and BBQ Chicken. It's a place I'd eagerly return to – and you should too.

This was a hole in the wall I've been told about from numerous friends. I got the pork steamed dumplings which were ok- I used to live in Chinatown and I've had better, more flavorful dumplings and I also got the pan fried beef noodles which was good but tasted like Lo Mien with beef. The place is cash only so keep that in mind!

My friend and I wanted to grab brunch after doing a workout class around the area. This was only a few blocks away and had good reviews and pictures on Yelp.Upon arrival to the store, I almost felt like I was transported out of NYC. Since I'm not a tourist, I can't vouch for this, but it seems like one of those places that appears on TripAdvisor. It has a tourist trap vibe.Once we were seated, we were inundated by the waitstaff. Literally 3-4 of them came to ask if we were ready to order within 5 minutes of sitting. Others described it as amazing service, but it might be too amazing for my taste. We couldn't sit and enjoy our food or each other's company due to how often they came by. As for the food, the brunch deal was good. It came with tea or coffee, a cocktail and a meal. The food was ok. I don't think I will be going out of my way to come here, but may be a convenient and average option if I find myself around the area again.

Overall, we had a fairly disappointing meal at Salinas.  Immediately, we were at a disadvantage, being led to a table in the bar, rather than the gorgeous room with the retractable roof.  I guess we didn't look "swanky" enough, which in NYC has nothing to do with your dress, but more to do with your hip quotient.  I am too old to look hip in the city.  I apologized to my wife because ten years ago we would be treated like celebrities.The kitchen was closing at 9:30, yes, even in NYC, and the staff was rushing to clean up.  This should never be tolerated.  Servers and staff shouldn't start cleaning up until the last patron has left.  I demanded that in my restaurants. Food was okay, but not memorable.  Our rice dishes were bland, but at least my wife's dish arrived in a traditional Paella pan.  My rice dish was slopped together on a plate.  That being said, the food was okay until the bill arrived:$219.00 for two appetizers, two entrees, bread, two cocktails and two glasses of wine.  That's Michelin star Paris dining prices folks! Yikes!  The room is pretty, perfect for a date, but at those prices there are one hundred better choices in New York.

Get away from the hustle and bustle that is Times Square and just walk a few minutes away to find this great location with amazing food, service, and selection of spirits. The menu is small but they focus on taste and quality. We had Peruvian wings and a great burger. Tv's are available and they even take reservations. Avoid the crowds and check out this place, you'll be glad you did.

I came here for brunch on a Sunday with 9 girls.We had a 1:30 reservation and were seated fairly quickly after arriving. Two stars because the food was good.The guacamole clasico was delicious.The shrimp quesadilla was packed with shrimp and was surprisingly filling, despite looking small.The elote corn was good too!The Boozy Brunch is two hours of unlimited mimosas, Sangria, Bloody Marys/Maria's, or Draft Mexican Beer. The food and our waiter were great, BUT the manager and clean up was extremely disappointing. They say you can switch up your drinks, so as I'm nearing the end of my Bloody Mary, I ask for a beer. The manager serves it to me and goes to take my Bloody Mary, but I ask to finish it before he takes it. Apparently, you can only have one drink in front of you, so he takes my beer away until I can chug my Bloody Mary. It was extremely uncomfortable as he is hovering, waiting for me to down my Bloody Mary... not an easy cocktail to drink fast. I wasn't trying to hoard drinks and if you're trying to limit the drunkenness, don't force someone to chug their drink/don't ask if I want another one.After your two hours, they give you the bill, but HUSTLE you out passive aggressively and don't give you any time to finish the rest of your drinks. A lot of big groups ended at the same tine and it was chaos. Two bathrooms, so the line for the bathroom is insane as everyone is trying to leave, yet wait for their friends and finish their drinks. Bus boys are literally grabbing your cups as you set them down, it was not a great way to end the meal.Not worth the hype.

Title: A Gastronomic Delight at a Reasonable Price

I recently dined at a restaurant that may just have become my new favorite. The decor is delightful, providing an upscale vibe without the hefty price tag. The spacious layout is perfect for large parties.

My meal choice was the Pan-Roasted Chicken, accompanied by Greek Fries and a glass of beautifully presented sangria. The chicken was exquisite, setting a new standard for my future poultry expectations with its tenderness and a sauce that delighted the palate, reminiscent of a delicate gravy. The potato wedges served with it were a wonderful complement.

The Greek Fries were a step above the usual fare, boasting a crispy exterior and a generous seasoning. As for the sangria, it was as pleasing to the taste as it was to the eye, offering a smooth and sweet finish to the meal.

As for the ratings, this place scores impressively across the board:

Price: 4/5 – Affordable for the quality offered.
Quality: 5/5 – Outstanding taste and presentation.
Quantity: 4/5 – Satisfying portions.
Service: 5/5 – Impeccable and attentive.
Atmosphere: 5/5 – Chic and welcoming.

All things considered, this restaurant is a must-visit for a delightful dining experience.
Underwhelming. Strange because the spaghetti was the size of udon--never seen that before. Service was slow. Nothing too special. Probably would not come back?

Last night as a group of three, we dined at a local restaurant, preferring it over its Soho counterpart due to Yelp's promise of no waits. Contrarily, a 30-minute wait greeted us, alongside the inconvenience of a cramped space with outdoor-only standby.

Our dining experience was mixed. The fried chicken was merely adequate, unable to distinguish itself from superior renditions elsewhere. The deep-fried eggplant, while enjoyable, was marred by an excessive oily residue.

The kani ankake udon was a highlight, serving up generous portions of delightfully chewy noodles and a satisfactory amount of crab in a thick, eggy soup, albeit with a steep $20 price tag sans toppings. Disappointment found its way with the niku udon, which, despite its $17 cost, failed to deliver the promised tripe.

In reflection, the restaurant merits a return for certain dishes, though it’s clear improvements are needed to justify the prices and enhance the overall dining experience.

Five stars for 3 star diner, friendly / family owned and run diner with positive energy, solid omelettes and burgers, huge menu selection for breakfast lunch and late night eats, and a wonderful Greek salad I've had in the past.Recent visit my son ordered their lasagna. Me:  Are you sure you want to order lasagna from a diner?? Him, quizzically:  why not?? Well... it was actually good! And huge, served with a generous portion of veggies. He ate half and took the rest home. Years back, my son asked, why would they name themselves 3 star diner and not 4 or 5 star diner? Good question! So I asked: the business is owned by 2 brothers and a sister, thus "3 stars."  The hostess (wife of a brother/ owner) and manager (son of an owner).. One of the owners was working behind the counter.  I strongly support family run businesses and the positive energy and vibe - with smiles, enthusiasm and fun attitudes among the employees They are open and deliver 24 hours.

I came here with a group of about 20 people for a friends birthday. We had a reservation and the space was quite spacious where we were accommodated. The staff were friendly and attentive, always refilled our water without asking.My boyfriend and I shared a seaweed salad as a starter. They offer the salad with a lemon which was a first for me but I did like the sour tang it added. This was also the first time I ever had a seaweed salad that was slightly spicy, it had a bit of a kick to it. Miso soup came with our sushi dx. It was very flavorful with seaweed and tofu but they don't give you much.I was very impressed by the fish to rice ratio for all the pieces of sushi. Also if you order sashimi the slices they give are humongous. Don't order the normal rolls, splurge for the sushi and sashimi because it is definitely worth it. You don't need to add extra wasabi because there is some already placed on all the pieces of sushi.Will definitely return back here to try something else if I'm in the area.

Title: Underwhelming Steakhouse Experience

My inaugural foray into dining out for steak left me yearning for my usual home-cooked Costco cuts. My partner and I braved a rainy day hoping for a cozy meal, but the restaurant's seating arrangement was peculiar, positioning us side by side rather than face-to-face – a slight improvement from their previous stand-and-eat setup.

Given the steep prices, one would expect exceptional service, yet this expectation fell flat. The staff appeared disinterested; one waiter, tasked with directing us to order at the counter, came across as particularly unfriendly. Furthermore, the peculiar inconsistency of one waiter refilling my water but neglecting my partner's bordered on negligence.

Pricewise, the increase to $2.50/oz for a 10oz Ribeye and $2/oz for a 14oz Sirloin since last year was sharply felt. Accompanied by corn, garlic, and onions, the steaks were decent, with a self-service sauces station adding a customizable touch. The Ribeye outshone the Sirloin, which suffered from dryness, although my requested Medium Rare Ribeye skewed closer to Medium Well – juicy and tender, yet unremarkable.

The prospect of returning hinges on budget and their more enticing lunch specials, but should I reconsider, a different location would be my choice to avoid a repeat of the disappointing service.

Came here with a large group last weekend. They would not seat us until our entire group was there. We were seated upstairs at a couple of tables pushed together. The space was kind of tight. The seats were extremely small and it was very noisy. The service was pretty good and we enjoyed our complimentary soju cocktail shots with our Yelp check in. I ordered the beef bulgogi bowl  served over rice The dish was OK. Nothing to write home about. It looked nothing like the colorful photographs online. It was all brown. I had to add all of the gochujang sauce to give it some flavor. I've been to South Korea and I've eaten at some other Korean restaurants in the area. This place is really just average..

Title: A Nugget Lover's Paradise!

I recently visited a spot that's a haven for nugget enthusiasts, offering an assortment of bites that had my taste buds singing praises. From cereal-coated nuggets that add a playful twist to the classic favorite, to hearty traditional nuggets and Mozz Nuggs which are a cheese lover's dream come true, the variety is impressive.

The Old Bay Seasoned Fries were a perfect, spiced accompaniment to the nuggets, and the array of sauces available meant every dip was a new adventure. As for the Nacho Mac, it's a dish I've been dreaming of since my visit—creamy, cheesy, with just the right kick, it's a dish you can't miss.

Honestly, it's a good thing I don't live nearby because this place is dangerously delightful. Whether you're a nugget fanatic or just looking for some indulgent comfort food, this restaurant is a must-visit. Check it out, but be warned, it might just become your new guilty pleasure!

Had the cronut dupe because I couldn't make it to the original one before it sold out but it was disappointing cus it's so greasy. Luckily, they have a coffee/tea menu so I ordered a cup of iced tea and it helped cut down the greasiness and the sweetness but it's a little overpriced. I love their birthday cakes cus it is very sophisticatedly made. The cream is very smooth and milky and the cake is very spongy.

Huge menu , a wonderful variety of options and lots of flavors ! Lychee martinis were delicious ! Great after work drink/dinner spot , good for groups or even a date. The food came out pretty quick and the service was wonderful

Dallas BBQ stands as a culinary landmark in NYC, delivering exactly what you expect from such an esteemed establishment. The must-have menu items include their delectable chicken wings paired with a signature Texas-sized drink, ensuring a satisfying experience. A special shoutout to Elder, the bartender at this location, whose outstanding service elevates the dining experience to new heights. A visit to Dallas BBQ is a decision you won't regret.

Title: Artichoke Basille's Pizza: A Slice of Heaven

If you're in search of a celestial pizza experience, look no further than Artichoke Basille's. After multiple visits, I can attest that their artichoke pizza is simply divine. Picture the most luscious artichoke dip spread generously atop a crispy-yet-soft crust—it's a dreamy combination that haunts you long after the last bite.

The slices are colossal, enough to quell the heartiest of appetites with just one piece. And if it proves too much, they're happy to split it for easy sharing or a takeaway treat. It's a must-visit spot that beckons for a swift return. Artichoke Basille's doesn't just serve pizza; they serve oversized slices of bliss.

My hunny usually puts me on to delicious spots due to his job catering their multiple work events. On numerous occasions he's brought home food from Harry's Italian and each time I fall more in love with the place. Although I haven't had the pleasure to dine at Harry's the takeout from here is spot on. I'm a sucka for Italian food. Hey, what can I say I'm a carb type of girl -- Mamma Mia!For the past couple of years our tradition consists of cooking for each other on Valentine's Day. It's way too expensive to dine out and we really enjoy catering to one another by putting together a delicious spread. One year I decided I wanted to take the time and pressure out of cooking on V-Day and decided to have our day catered so that our night could be extra special. I asked my hunny his thoughts and he was totally on board to get our V-Day meal catered from Harry's. We decided on House Salad which came with a delicious Homemade Balsamic Vinaigrette Dressing, Penne Vodka, Chicken Parmesan, Eggplant Rollatini, and Rosemary Focaccia Bread. Everything was superb. From our hearty meals to the packaging of our V-day dinner, our entire meal was spot on. Each time we have Harry's it tastes better than the last time. It's truly a treat. Harry's went as far as including serveware, plates, and utensils. That's a major plus. I mean who wants to wash dishes anyway? We decided we want to have our 2020 V-day catered by the incredible Harry's once again.

Everything is gluten free! Including the complimentary bread! Feels like true Italian food, without the gluten. Ah, what a breath of fresh air this place was. We ordered the aperol spritz which was high in alcohol and had the perfect amount of sugar (not very much). We followed that with the grilled fig and prosciutto special which was phenomenal. And finally, we had the lemon shrimp risotto. All out-of-this-world fantastic! Generous portions, amazing flavors. A great experience. I will be back.

Came here for lunch and after quickly browsing some reviews, I knew the mixed meze platter would be the perfect sharing plate.  The cheese and meat pastries were delicious that came with the dips.  My favorite dips were the tzatziki and babaganush.  I also shared the octopus salad.  The salad was good but the grilled octopus was a bit over cooked so it was very chewy.  Service was great and the ambiance was lovely

Los Tacos has made a triumphant return and it's as delicious as ever. Picking up our online order was a breeze with their efficient pickup window service. Both the chicken and pork tacos were delectable, leaving no room for disappointment. This place continues to be a can't-miss for taco aficionados.

Title: A Spirited Spot with Unbeatable Appetizers

My recent visit to this bustling hub proved it to be the perfect place for a lively gathering, especially on a buzzing Friday night. Amidst the vibrant crowd, the appetizers stole the show – shareable and utterly delicious. The spring rolls, particularly the Pastrami Ruben and Buffalo Chicken varieties, were a culinary revelation, worthy of the accolade "AMAZING."

While the atmosphere teemed with energy, the standout mimosa complemented our selection beautifully. Given the popularity of the place, I'd advise booking in advance for a sit-down meal.

In brief, for an exuberant outing with top-tier starters and refreshing drinks, give this spot a try. Don't miss out on those spring rolls – you'll be singing praises just as I am. Highly recommended!

The lunch special here is so good. Glad that I came here. I shared the black bean noodle, spicy seafood noodle and fried chicken cutlet with my coworker. It was so much food but I were able to finish pretty much everything. The service was a little slow though.

Ordered Fig and Olive for the first time and was disappointed.Ordered Chicken Paella but was told they could not accommodate my special request so had to change to the Fig and Olive Burger with baked potatoes. First i got surprised because the description of the food clearly stated "fries" and it was just baked potatoes. Secondly, the brioche was hard and not easy to eat. Thirdly, the beef was totally tasteless and burned and it also tasted bitter because the burn. Most importantly, there was also a hair on the potatoes. Thank god i only took a small bite and realized the hair after and didnt just eat it. Could not believe this could still happen at a restaurant that I would say of popularity.Hopefully this was only a one time experience but I would say for a first time comer, it was pretty traumatizing.

Mamoun's Falafel is a small, convenientfast food restaurant. I had come out the Islamic center looking for food and found Mamoun's Falafel vía yelp. The food is excellent and delicious. I just feel for a veggie platter costing 9 dollars they should add more than 3 falafels. I also feel the customer service should be more courteous and in a better mood. If I greet you, say hello back instead of asking what I want. I even said thanks and the guy looked at me like he's deaf. Beside that I love the place because it has amazing food. The  babaganush and hummus was so tasty and fresh. The falafel was cooked on point and tasted delicious. If anyone is around the west 4 district go check it out.

Title: A Cheesy Delight at Shorty's!

Shorty's has won my affection yet again! Their cheese steak sandwich is a delectable masterpiece, and the onion rings are the perfect crispy companions. Staff members, especially the bartender, are the epitome of friendliness, ensuring a swift and pleasant service experience. Prices are reasonable for the top-notch quality you receive, and the adjective "great" falls short of describing the flavorful food.

For sports enthusiasts, Shorty’s is a haven with numerous TVs broadcasting a variety of games. The establishment boasts a roomy atmosphere with ample seating in both the dining and bar areas. If you're looking for a place that combines great food, friendly vibes, and sports galore, Shorty's should definitely be on your radar.

I have been coming to this location several times since this is near my work. I love by CHLOE but this location is a bit off. Their food tastes a bit different from other locations. The staff needs to know the right amount of dressing. I wrote feedback for them but I guess they never checked it. I was happy to find this location and was planning to come here for my lunch but I might not come to this location anymore.

Title: Second Visit Affirms Premium Beats Classic at Local Pho Spot

I recently made my second visit to this Vietnamese restaurant within a fortnight, which says a lot about its pull. Despite not having a particular craving, my go-to choice of a comforting bowl of pho beckoned me back, alongside my boyfriend who was set on reliving the spicy short rib experience.

We started with a Young Papaya Mango Salad, shared between us. It was a refreshing, albeit unremarkable, prelude to our main course. The familiar tang of the Viet Chili dressing was pleasant but not groundbreaking, and it's unlikely we'd order the salad again.

The Saigon Pho I chose, priced at $12.95, was a testament to the comfort of familiarity. It was a decently tasty bowl of pho, although the raw beef had unfortunately overcooked by the time it arrived at the table, leaving something to be desired. The beef balls also fell short of expectations. The broth and noodles, however, maintained their delightful standard.

As for my boyfriend, sticking to the premium spicy short rib proved to be a wise choice. Though he noted it tasted spicier this visit, that could be attributed to not having to share it. The rich flavors and premium quality were consistent with our first visit.

One downside was the service hiccup; they remembered to provide a bowl for the short rib bones but overlooked the essential bean sprouts and basil that are pho staples.

In summary, this place shines with its premium offerings. I now know where my future preferences lie. Solid service and a stellar spicy short rib pho make this spot worth returning to, with a note to self: stick to what they do best.

Was a very packed place but we managed to get a table for two without a reservation. The restaurant is decorated very nicely inside and I was pleasantly surprised. My drink was actually pretty refreshing especially with the hint of coconut in there. Spring rolls were the best I've ever had anywhere and it might have been the rice paper they used but it was sticky enough to keep it all together. I liked the beef pho too-it was undeniably good but I had a request to take out the brisket and just put in more rare steak and the waitress said I'd have to pay $4 more dollars which didn't make much sense to me since I was opting out of something else. I'd come back again but was not pleased that my pho had mostly noodles because I was expected to pay more for some other meat to replace.

Food: 4/5I've heard many different comments about this place from my non Filipino friends so when my Filipino friend asked me to dine with her here, I said yes in a heartbeat. I ordered the salt and pepper squid (1.5/5) at the bar before her arrival. It wasn't the best. I'm convinced it tastes better at a Cantonese restaurant. It wasn't salty or peppery. Tasted more like lightly fried calamari. When my friend arrived, I let the pro do the ordering. She ordered the chicharron bulakalak, the pork sisig, the laing, the beef lengua, and the bone marrow with garlic rice.Two girls with a combined weight of maybe 220lbs and ordering two appetizers with four entrees -I was HYPED. The chicharron (4/5) was delicious. I'm a big fan of Columbian chicharron and found the Filipino version less fatty but equally crunchy. I'm a big fan of texture so this made me very happy. It's served with a shoyu type sauce which added a bit of tang to it. The pork sisig (5/5) was out of this world delicious. Who would have thought anything could be this tasty? It's served sizzling hot and packed with pork belly and a soy saucey type taste. To be honest, I don't even know what else was in it but it was delicious. I think there was an egg in it? The laing (4/5) was very interesting and the spices sort of reminded me of Thai food.  A great vegetarian/taro curry dish. The beef lengua (1.5/5) was my least favorite. It was sort of mushroomy and creamy. I like texture and this wasn't it. It was too soft or maybe even overcooked for my preference. The bone marrow (5/5) was insanely fatty and packed with hearty flavor! Underneath the bone marrow were chunks of beef but that bone marrow made Jane a very happy Jane. Oh garlic rice rules all. Coconut rice needs to step up. I've never had it before but the rice to garlic ratio was perfect!Two girls, too much food, and happy hour until 9pm sounds like a win to me. This is my first time trying Filipino food and I'm very happy/lucky to have tried it with a Filipino foodie friend. I will be back!Did you know Filipinos don't use chopsticks? I'm such an amateur and of course I had to ask for chopsticks...........Service: 5/5The bartender was so sweet and accommodating. She was so welcoming and informative. I wish I got her name but she had a short, bob hair cut. I (like an idiot) asked her for chopsticks and she kindly informed me Filipinos don't use chopsticks. She didn't laugh or make feel dumb. (I felt pretty dumb). She was very nice and attentive.Ambiance: 3/5I was unaware that this place turns into a club at night. I preferred the scene without the DJ because I'm old and loud noise hurts my ears. I went for girls night and wanted to chat with my friend but ended up having to relocate to catch up. Great vibe for a date or to hang out with friends. Happy hour is until 9pm so if music and drinks are your scene, this is the place to go!

Finally, a place that does "elevated" Korean food right! Well-deserved Michelin star. I was a little hesitant to try this place as many fusion or elevated Korean restaurants have not been very good in my experience, but I was proven wrong. Food: We opted for the $55 pp prix fixe menu, which was definitely enough food and well worth the price. My favorite would have to be the truffle mushroom-- the dish was presented with truffle blocks in a box, which the waiter then shaved on to the dish at the table. We asked for the so ramyun, which was a great end to the meal. It was the best seoullungtang broth I've had, the noodles were perfectly cooked, and the picked garlic made sure the dish wasn't too heavy. My favorite aspect about this restaurant is that even though it is a "fancier" take on Korean food, it doesn't change the essence of Korean food. I could still taste the  (mom's taste) factor aka that comfortable feeling of a home-cooked meal, but evolved to a new level of flavors. Service: I loved that the waiters were also the chefs of our meal, meaning that they knew what they were talking about. I also loved how they sat us without making us wait for the full party first-- I really appreciated the small things like that. Tl;dr: Upon finishing the meal, I wanted to come back again.
