Get the prix fixe meal, at least the first time you come here. And if you're Korean, you'll love the experience even more!

Met my friend here for dinner as she is a neighborhood local. Great Japanese cuisine with cool vibes and decor and small intimate feeling. We ordered a bunch of shareplates and I had the kimchi tofu soup which was spicy and came with a fair amount of tofu. The grilled squid was seared and not over cooked. We also tried the dumplings, pork belly skewers and last but not least the takoyaki balls which is always a must. Cooked on all sides to perfection with a nice portion size of squid inside dressed with sauce and drizzled on the plate. Service was great and the friendly greeting us the moment we entered and checking on us though out our meal.

Title: A View Not to Be Missed, But Mind the Time

If you have yet to experience the visual spectacle of this restaurant, it's time you do. The view alone is worth the trip, offering an ambiance that words do a disservice to—you simply need to see it for yourself. Picture opulent chandeliers, serene running water, and atmospheric dim lighting setting the stage for an unforgettable evening.

The venue doubles as a showroom, boasting luxurious Restoration Hardware furnishings perfectly crafted for lounging with a cocktail in hand. The rooftop, accessible even in the chillier months, provides a stunning backdrop to your dining experience.

However, be cautioned: avoid booking your reservation for 8:45. The kitchen's early closing time at 9pm led to a rushed service that marred our otherwise splendid visit. Our waitress hastened us through each course, leaving us longing for a more leisurely paced meal.

Despite this hiccup, the enchanting ambiance is undeniable, meriting a full five-star rating. Next time, I'll ensure to arrive earlier to fully savor this exquisite setting.

I came here for lunch and had their BBQ pork over noodles. It is a lot more spacious than it looks from the outside and the staff seemed friendly. The food was not bad and had an authentic taste. The meat was seasoned well. This place is slightly more expensive by a couple dollars per entree than Vietnamese places in Chinatown, which is not helped by the very average portion sizes. But this is the Times Square area after all.

I recently had the pleasure of trying out the breakfast offerings at a local spot serving up authentic Hong Kong style cha cha tang fare. To my delight, they've also incorporated a taste of Vietnam into their morning menu with a limited selection from their sister restaurant, Sai Gon Dep, featuring savory Vietnamese beef pho and chicken ga. For those looking for a flavorful start to their day, it's definitely worth grabbing takeout from this eatery and enjoying a peaceful meal at nearby Columbus Park.

Title: Cozy Irish Vibes and Tasty Eats

I recently visited an Irish-themed bar restaurant for an early dinner and came away pleasantly satisfied. The highlights of the meal were the deliciously crisp fries and a perfectly poured pint of Guinness straight from the tap. The overall quality of the food was pretty good, making it a solid choice for anyone looking to grab a bite in a laid-back setting. Definitely not a bad spot to unwind and enjoy some classic pub fare.

I recently visited a fantastic pub/restaurant that left quite an impression on me. Their beer selection is outstanding, with the Torch and Crown Almost Famous being an absolute delight for any beer enthusiast. The wings I tried were delicious, perfectly cooked and seasoned. Additionally, the burger shouldn't be missed – it is indeed "really really good." The staff were amiable, and I have to give a shoutout to the bartender who was not only super cool but also incredibly knowledgeable about beer. Highly recommended!

I was having a horrible week and I came here with my girls crew for mother's day to have a diversion and it was worth it. I really enjoyed the food here and the table. Our table was big so we all had a lot of space to move. That was fun. I had the lobster tarlet that was delicious and the portion was filling though not large. The raspberry mimosa tasted tangy like raspberries so I loved it. It was a good Sunday well spent. My only issue was though our waitress was nice, she doesnt check up on the table at all. So we have to call her to get her attention incase we wanted our water filled or pepper or more stuff to order. Maybe it was just a busy day. But I did enjoy my time here and the food and I went home with a happy face.

This review is for the Christmas Eve dinner. Some of the menu items here are on the regular menu. The design and the decor is lovely and provides a good ambiance to set the mood. My partner and I arrived on time for our reservation but were seated well over 30 minutes later. As we waited, we sat at the bar and ordered the Portale (house drink - recommended but not to my liking), and the Don Verde, made of matcha & japanese whiskey with ginger and egg whites (much more preferred!). When we checked in with the manager for our table, he apologized and offered the first round of drinks on the house. When we were finally seated, we were presented the 4-course tasting menu.Antipasti - Capesante: Throughout the entire course, this was my favorite as it was seared perfectly and incredibly flavorful.  Crudo di Ricciola: This was good but not great. It was much saltier and overly citrus, which made it difficult to taste the hamachi. Primi -Lumache: The pasta was al dente and the light black truffle oil highlighted the short ribs. Tasty.Anolini di cavolfiore: Well flavored and balance. I love it when vegetables are done right. Also a highlight of the evening.Secondi - Ippoglosso: I really wanted to enjoy this but the halibut was much tougher and overcooked. This may be a fault of my own but I should have avoided a second truffle dish. I was overwhelmed by the truffle at this point (great for those who relish in this). My partner ordered the Agnello and he enjoyed it very much. Lamb was not for me so I barely tried it. Dolci - by this time, we were incredibly full so we took a bite each of our desserts.Torta di Pere: This maple dessert with pear was unique and I really enjoyed it. Gelati e Sorbetti: This texture was icy and not very creamy - not something I look for in gelato. You would think the blood orange would complement the chocolate and vanilla but due to the texture, I think it missed. Not a fan. Upon paying for our check, we noticed that the initial drinks were not taken off. We noted this to the staff as the original manager was no longer there. There was a light push back, they ultimately took off the initial drinks. The flavors of this restaurant is bold. I would have to come back again for a second try sans christmas rush. Food is above average, service was slow but was overall courteous to us, and drinks are plentiful if you're okay with the Manhattan prices.

My friends and I got their crispy calamari in point judith style as an appetizer. It was covered in pickled jalapeños and garlic which added a slight spiciness to the dish. I'm not good with spicy food but this one was delicious and the dipping sauce on the side balanced out as well. Then we got BBQ bleu burger with extra fried egg and crunchy chicken sandwich. The BBQ bleu burger was so juicy and the buttermilk bleu cheese made it so much more flavorful than other burgers I've had. If you are a fan of cheese, I recommend you getting this burger. The crunchy chicken sandwich was also really delicious. The chicken was very crispy and the meat was huge and so juicy. The salsa verde aioli in the sandwich was definitely a big plus to the overall taste of the sandwich! Both dishes came with sea salt fries which tasted like a way better version of mcd fries -- crispy, not too thin, and just the right saltiness. I know this restaurant focuses on raw food, but I do think their burgers and sandwiches are pretty good.It's very spacious inside and has a lot of seats, a little dark and gets loud since it's a bar restaurant. But overall, a great place for dinner!

Title: A Slice of Heaven on Mulberry Street

After stumbling upon an enthusiastic recommendation from a Korean YouTuber, my wife and I made the trek from Brooklyn to finally experience what I now confidently declare the best thin-crust pizza I've ever had.

Braving the bustling streets of the city on a Wednesday afternoon, we were determined to find a coveted parking spot near this culinary gem. An hour later, our persistence paid off, and we found ourselves stepping into a restaurant that oozed with old-world charm complete with a stunning full bar and ample seating for its prime Mulberry Street location.

Upon our arrival around 1:30 PM, we were welcomed with friendly faces and were promptly seated within ten minutes at a prime table near the kitchen—an unexpected perk that offered us a sneak peek at every delectable dish and pie being served.

The meal commenced with a Caesar salad that set a high bar, easily ranking as one of the best I've ever had. The main event, a large split-order pizza, was equally impressive. Our half Vodka & Sausage and half Rubirosa Supreme—the latter adorned with tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, meatballs, pepperoni, garlic, and fresh basil—was a harmonious blend of delicious, authentic flavors. The vodka sauce was spot-on, and the crispy crust was nothing short of a textural triumph, made even more memorable by its unexpected preparation in a Fish Oven.

Eyes larger than our stomachs, we admired the pastas and homemade zeppoles making their way to other tables, vowing to return to indulge in these as well. The service was impeccable throughout, with our waitress and the manager going above and beyond to ensure a delightful dining experience.

I highly recommend making the visit, and it's safe to say that this won't be the last you see of me and my family—we'll be bringing friends to share in this unparalleled pizza experience.

Thank you,
Greg D & family

Tucked away in the bustling Chelsea Market, BC offers an oasis for German cuisine aficionados. Despite the market's constant energy and the challenge of navigating a large stroller, my anticipation for a savory beef brat compelled me to stop by for a takeout lunch.

BC's menu did not disappoint, featuring an $8 lunch deal with brats served either on a bun or currywurst style. Opting for the former, I appreciated the thoughtful service as my toppings were carefully packed separately to preserve the bun's integrity. Unfortunately, the containers didn't hold up—the spillage from the onion and sauerkraut marred what could have been a perfect handheld meal.

The fries, however, were the highlight—perfectly seasoned and thoroughly enjoyable. Next time, I'd opt to dine in for the full experience, though circumstances this time around necessitated a quick retreat to my car for an air-conditioned, solitary feast. Despite the minor mishap, BC's flavors make it worth a return visit.

Very fun place; Dan is behind the bar, gave some history of the 75'year old bar. Makes a mean Bloody Mary. Paul greeted us and was friendly and inviting. As we were leaving, Dan offered a Jameson for the road. Excellent hospitality! I will be back!

I recently dined at this charming spot before catching a show at Madison Square Garden, and the experience was delightful. Our group of four indulged in a spread that included calamari, burrata, orchiette, spinach fettuccine, and Parma pizza. We rounded off the meal with cannoli and chocolate mousse for dessert. While the orchiette fell short of expectations, every other dish was a hit—full of flavor and perfectly cooked. The ambiance was inviting, and the service was top-notch, making our culinary adventure before the show a memorable one. I would highly recommend this restaurant for anyone looking for great food in the vicinity of The Garden. With just a minor hiccup in one dish, I'm happy to give it a well-deserved 4.5 stars.

I recently visited this restaurant with high expectations during the 2019 summer Restaurant Week, but I left feeling let down. I was eager to sample their offerings, but the experience fell flat. The service was lackluster, which was surprising and set a disappointing tone.

For starters, the bora bora shrimp I ordered was passable, but its texture made it a chore to eat rather than a delight. My boss's chicken ball soup was presented unappetizingly and, according to him, possessed the negative aspects of homemade food without the charm.

My main course, a Japanese karaage chicken sandwich, initially impressed with its presentation but quickly crumbled into a mess with the first bite. It was rather unsatisfying, and I found it challenging to justify finishing it. The accompanying fries were the highlight, but even they weren't enough to redeem the meal. I left the restaurant with an uncomfortable feeling of nausea.

In summary, my lunch here was underwhelming, with the cuisine lacking in both flavor and finesse, which is contrary to the expectation set by their promising menu.

Came here for tapas after work. We had a reservation but had to wait for a short time to be seated. The decor was cute here, and it's attached to a hotel, but also has a separate entrance. Our waitress was super friendly and knowledgeable and the service was top notch. We ordered the $60/pp sampler. They asked if there were any dishes that we wanted to try and incorporated them into the meal. Additionally this option had the famous jamon that we wanted to try. We tried a lot of apps. They were in general solid. Only a few stood out to me. Manchego - I appreciate all the items this game with. Was alright Jamon - was okay. A little fatty. Smooth and mild flavor. Shrimp - was only okay, but I don't like shrimp. My guest enjoyed this. Lamb skewers - I'm not a huge fan of lamb but these were super flavorful. I also appreciated the toppings. Surprise of the night for me. Bacon wrapped dates with blue cheese. I've had this dish many other places, but these were better than most. My favorite dish of the night. Mushroom flatbread - hard pass for next time. Not much originality or flavor. The other star for me was a special for the day. Fried egg over potato straws with ham. It was like super elevated breakfast and it was amazing!! Dessert was another surprise! The mini churros were great! Also the other dessert was some sort of spice cake or something with ice cream. Which had a touch of salt on top which really made it shine! I would come and just order the ice cream . Was worth coming once. Good service; some solid dishes, and a cute atmosphere.

Had a stunning birthday dinner at Manhatta! I started with the Windmill cocktail and my boyfriend had the Manhatta cocktail - both great. We then shared dishes from two pre-fixes:+ Charcoal grilled pork belly+ Squid ink strozzapreti+ Wagyu culotte+ Crescent duck+ Olive oil sabayon cake+ Toasted marshmallow cake They also gave me a black and white birthday cake, which was a nice touch. Sadly they didn't have the famed date cake, but hopefully it will return to the menu one day! Overall impeccable. Be sure to check out the bar and game room that they have, too; it overlooks the water and has a great view of the Statue of Liberty.

We came here on a Sunday evening so there was a lot of available tables. I definitely recommend the hot & crispy baby back ribs! The potato salad banchan was really good so we asked for seconds. It wasn't free though! Their banchan is not free unlike other Korean restaurants I go to. I didn't really like the stone bowl because it had too much kimchi and not enough rice.

Title: A Delightful Discovery at My Go-To Pho Spot

Having visited this gem for the second time, my taste buds were treated to an unexpected revelation - the coconut curry pho. This dish was an absolute game-changer for me, elevating my pho experience to new heights with its rich and aromatic flavors. Initially, I was on the verge of satisfying my curry cravings at a Chinese restaurant, but fate had other plans as I noticed "curry" listed on the pho establishment's menu. Deciding to take a leap of faith, I ordered the coconut curry pho, and let me tell you, it was a decision well made. The dish surpassed my expectations, harmoniously melding the warmth of curry with the comforting essence of pho. Both my partner and I were captivated by the flavor, and it's safe to say that this dish has secured its spot as my all-time favorite. Anticipation for my next visit is already brewing, with the coconut curry pho being the highlight I look forward to indulging in once again.

Delicious for udon. I usually prefer soba, but the udon here is very good. It's not too thick. Soup is tasty and not too salty. Noodles were just the right texture, not too soft.The mini-curry plate is a good sharing plate if you want to try their curry. The curry is good, but still not my favorite as I'm not really a fan of curry.They have Sapporo on draft, so it's a plus. Tasted great with the karage appetizer. The smallest size on draft is the lil guy, which is 16oz. They do have 8oz can also.It's a small place with a few tables, but they do try to accommodate large groups when tables become available.They also have happy hour, but I missed it.

Title: A Gem Worth Booking Ahead!

Review:
I've dined at this restaurant for the second time and it remains consistently fabulous! It’s essential to make a reservation, as the popularity of this place can lead to a wait time of up to two hours – and that's the case any day of the week.

Upon arrival (with a reservation), we were promptly seated at a beautifully set table with a stunning view. The service mirrored the setting - efficient and pleasing.

The meal itself was a delight to both the palate and the wallet. We opted for the Lunch Sakura Course ($39.95), which scored a perfect 10 out of 10. Offering a generous variety of appetizers, BBQ items, and desserts, the value for money here cannot be overstated.

In the drinks department, the Vodka Strawberry Lemonade could have used a stronger vodka kick, earning it a 4 out of 5. The Flavored Sake, however, was a sweet, exquisite treat (10 out of 10), and while the Shochu with Sweet Potato was potent with a strong flavor, it may not be to everyone's taste, thus a 3 out of 5.

Happy hour deals and courses designed for duos or groups add further allure to this bustling eatery. My experience was, simply put, great! Highly recommend snagging a reservation for an enjoyable meal.

Had dinner with friends and everything we had was good, ok my cocktail (Olympia) was weak, but everything else was spot on. They have one of the best bread ever! You must try the Lamb Kebab Terracotta, again it is topped with amazing bread. It's a little delicious surprise and is served as a presentation. Because we were a group, we got to sample a bit of each other's meals and were all in agreement that we made a good choice picking this place. The iron skillet shrimp and octopus are great starters and their hummus is delicious. It is higher in price point so bear that in mind. Nice ambiance, moderate noise, very friendly staff. Enjoyed it. I'd save it for special occasions. We didn't have a reservation but we were lucky that there was an open table and they were able to seat 6 of us. I recommend you make a reservation though, it filled up pretty quickly after we were seated.

Title: High Hopes Dampened by Mediocre Flavors

With much anticipation fueled by stellar reviews, I recently dined at this local Taiwanese spot. Unfortunately, my experience fell short of expectations. While boasting an extensive menu of Taiwanese snacks, the cramped quarters meant awaiting a table, and as a smaller party, we were asked to share our space with strangers.

On the positive side, pricing was quite reasonable—just be prepared to hit the minimum for credit card use.

The salt and pepper chicken had a perfect crispy exterior, yet it was disappointingly bland, missing the advertised basil notes. A spicy option would have been a welcome addition. The pork chop, while appearing appetizingly deep-fried, turned out overly salty and dry. It might pair better as an accompaniment to rice rather than as a standalone dish.

The beef soup was simply adequate; the clear broth harbored a mere 10 pieces of meat, making the portion size less generous than anticipated. I'd suggest trying one of the other soups on offer.

To my dismay, the celebrated minced pork over rice was conspicuously absent from the menu, a letdown for any enthusiast of Taiwanese cuisine. In summary, while the place has potential, the execution of flavors left me underwhelmed.

Buddakan offers a sleek ambiance that's perfect for those looking to indulge in a vibrant dining scene. The menu is best enjoyed family style, allowing you to savor a variety of their standout dishes. Notable favorites include the succulent lobster fried rice, delicately prepared edamame dumplings, refreshingly chilled noodles, and crispy veggie egg rolls. Cap off your meal with a decadent dessert, complemented by a glass or two of bubbly for a truly delightful dining experience.

Came in on a Saturday morning which happened to be the day of the NYC St Patrick day parade so they were quite busy but got a table right away and they seemed to handle the crowd very well. Coffees and waters were filled with regularity and orders taken and delivered quickly.  A couple of blocks from Central Park so you can walk there and then walk around the park and burn off some calories or come in and replenish. Food was good people keep calling this a diner but it seems a little more upscale than that. Pancakes, omelets, eggs any style all turned out fine and had generous portions. Bathroom has a keypad to enter a combination but wait staff quick to give the numbers out or assist those who are keypad entry challenged.

My cousin and I stopped into Rosemary's for pre-dinner drinks before meeting up with my niece and her husband at another Greenwich Village restaurant. Rosemary's was recommended to us as having excellent cocktails. Judging by my Manhattan, the recommendation was on the money. My cousin had a beer while I enjoyed an expertly mixed Manhattan. We also enjoyed an order of marinated olives. We arrived at this delightfully tiny bar just past dusk and sat at a window seat watching the early evening bustle pass by. It was a perfect stop before dinner. I'll keep Rosemary's in mind for drinks when in the Village.

Upon deciding to dine at this establishment, I discovered they lacked any diet soda options, which was a bit disappointing. I opted for the soup, and while it was only satisfactory, they were not shy with the lamb portions. In general, the cuisine was fairly average—neither particularly disappointing nor impressive. For the area, it's a decent choice, but it doesn't stand out from the crowd.

I know it's a brunch place, but I checked it out for la cena, which was an impressive experience. First observations: the menu doesn't feel very Australian! The menu is quite short! And the vibe is cute, romantic, and quiet, although I went for a late dinner, so maybe that's why it was empty. My friend and I shared the beet cashew dip, which I gobbled right up. It comes with vegetables drizzled with oil. I've never had a dip like that before. It's a big portion, too! I got the spicy salmon salad, which was so delicious and filling. The salmon is shredded. The dressing of the salad was a bit too salty for me, but overall, I really enjoyed it. It comes with a huge avocado slice and a good number of cherry tomato slices. My friend got the brussel sprouts pasta, which I tried and agreed with him that it was so unique. They add honey to it! Definite must-have if you're going for carbs. The waitress was sweet and on top of it all. She told us that the menu rotates, so I'm intrigued to return for some Aussie brunch bites!

Title: A Slice of Umami Paradise at [Restaurant Name]

If there's a flavor-packed destination worth a detour, it's [Restaurant Name] – a spot I'm thrilled to declare as my ultimate ramen haven.

My inaugural bowl, the Tabata Ramen, set the bar sky-high. A concoction of velvety coconut broth cradling perfectly cooked noodles, succulent chicken, and flawlessly executed eggs, etched itself in my memory. It's the kind of dish that beckons for a return visit.

And return I did, to experience the Sutamina Ramen, a masterful blend of spice and tenderness, each spoonful a testament to the chef's prowess with pork. Accompanied by a side of their chicken teriyaki, which my boys annihilated with gusto, it was clear that this place is not just a one-hit wonder.

Though a trek for me, every journey to [Restaurant Name] is rewarded with an indulgence in exquisite flavors. For those seeking ramen that resonates with depth and satisfaction, look no further – your search ends here.

I recently dined at a local restaurant known for its Japanese cuisine and had a mixed experience. I started with the Sashimi Platter, priced at $50, which I found to be reasonable in terms of value and quality. However, the selection was disappointing; half of the platter consisted of salmon, which seemed like a rather unbalanced and perhaps lazy choice on the chef's part.

Additionally, I tried the Lobster Soup Dumpling, attracted by its innovative concept and promising flavor. The taste lived up to my expectations, but the execution fell short. The dumpling skin was too thick and wrinkled, detracting from the texture, and there was a noticeable lack of soup within the dumpling. Despite these critiques, I do commend the restaurant for offering such a creative dish on their menu.

I'm not sure what this is and/or what this was. I'm truly puzzled as to what all the hype is about this place - because, it simply was awful. Place was packed with a bunch of "Hipsters" with "Mid-West Accents" that I had to listen to critiquing the food. Incredibly disappointed. Counterman won't talk to you - they rudely direct you to a computer to order your food. Nothing appears to be freshly made - everything is heated up. Again - very disappointed by the entire experience. Won't ever return again.

I recently visited Park Avenue Winter for a birthday brunch and the experience was nothing short of exceptional. Securing a reservation required some foresight, a testament to the venue’s popularity. The decor, an enchanting winter wonderland, set a magical backdrop for the meal.

The pre-fix brunch menu was indulgent, starting with delectable cinnamon monkey rolls. The selection of appetizers - especially the light and creamy local burrata and the unique whipped yogurt with pineapple compote - did not disappoint. The brunch risotto was a standout, rich and satisfying.

The main courses were varied, catering to different tastes. While the breakfast poutine proved too salty for my liking, the crusted branzino and smoked salmon eggs benedict were delightful, lighter alternatives.

A special mention must be made of the attentive service; our waiter ensured our glasses were never empty and surprised us with birthday desserts, complete with candles.

Park Avenue Winter earned a well-deserved 5-star rating. The combination of a beautiful atmosphere, delectable food, and thoughtful service ensure my friends and I will return to experience the changing seasons.

Title: A Hearty Feast for a Bargain at Local Gem

Last Thursday evening, my dining companion and I had the pleasure of visiting this establishment, utilizing a fantastic puls'd deal — what a bargain at only $29! Our meal was a parade of flavors, starting with the crab soup dumplings, which were a delightful beginning. We then indulged in shrimp wrapped in bacon alongside fresh orange slices, potstickers that hit all the right notes, and finally, delectable pork buns adorned with scallions that lived up to their messy reputation, but were entirely worth the extra napkins.

The service only enhanced our experience; our waiter Ian was a sweet and supremely helpful presence throughout the evening. It was a nice touch to have one of the cooks personally serve a dish, giving it that homey feel with heads-up advice on the potentially messy pork buns.

Included in our feast were two well-paired beers, rounding out what was an undeniably satisfying meal. Although we got too excited to snap pictures of our food before diving in, the aftermath was still a sight to behold — a true testament to the deliciousness of the meal.

We’re already eyeing the XL dumpling for our next visit. If it’s anything like the delights we sampled, it's bound to be another culinary triumph.

Kissaki Omakase in the Lower East Side is a gem of a sushi bar, where comfort meets chic design. During a Saturday lunch, the omakase set at $120 per person proved to be a culinary ballet of flavors. The service was impeccable, creating a welcoming environment that felt like an escape from the world outside.

The full omakase experience began with a miso soup that elevated the classic with textured seaweed and scallions, followed by 12 pieces of uniquely crafted nigiri, a hand roll, and dessert. Chef John, alongside another talented chef from Mexico City, presented each sushi piece like an artwork, including an unforgettable unagi topped with Kaluga caviar.

Highlights included a variety of fresh fish such as Saba, Kamasu, Chu Toro, and the extraordinary Ikura with smoked uni that was nothing short of sublime. The overall ambiance of Kissaki Omakase was both disciplined yet playful, adding to the dining experience.

After such an impressive showcase of delicious and inventive sushi, a return visit is definitely in the cards for the 12 piece omakase. Kissaki Omakase is highly recommended for anyone looking for top-notch sushi in a serene setting.

Title: A Modest Lunch Experience

My recent visit to this eatery for a colleague's farewell lunch was a study in mediocrity. The atmosphere benefited from being sparsely populated, and service was competent, yet unremarkable. As for the cuisine, the burrito I ordered was the epitome of ordinary, overshadowed slightly by somewhat more palatable nachos. There seemed to be an air of mild disappointment among other members of my party, with at least two expressing their discontent.

Despite the lackluster meal, its proximity to my workplace leaves the door open for a redux, possibly for a casual drink rather than a full meal. Here's hoping a second visit might elevate my opinion.

Title: A Pizza Worth Dreaming About

I'm not typically on the pizza hype train, but Prince Street Pizza in NYC has officially invaded my cravings. During a recent trip, I sampled multiple pizza joints, and Prince Street stood out with its remarkable square slices that deliver a satisfying fill with just one piece—though I recommend grabbing an extra for a delicious encore.

The crust achieved a delectable trinity: greasy, crunchy, and soft. Pair that with thick, slightly spicy pepperonis bursting with flavor, and cheese that’s nothing short of incredible, and you’ve got a pie that sets a sky-high standard. Whether a weekday evening or Monday afternoon, expect a line, but trust me, it's worth the brief wait.

Prince Street Pizza didn’t just impress me; it set a new benchmark for my pizza expectations. This is one culinary experience I'll revisit every time I find myself in New York City. If you have the chance, don't just walk by; join the line, and prepare to dream about it for months.

I recently visited this gem for the second time with a larger party and once again, it did not disappoint. The variety of dishes we sampled were uniformly delicious, reaffirming my admiration for their menu. Coupled with impeccable service, this establishment has solidified its place as one of my top restaurant choices in New York.

A solid spot for solid Italian food on the East side. There's a small amount of outdoor seating, which my friend and I wanted to take advantage of. The only downside is that there's a downsloping piece of cement that made our table incredibly wobbly and uncomfortably close to the next patrons dining. We ordered the buffalo mozzarella to start and it was incredibly delicious. One of the best that I've had in a long time. Paired with the complimentary bread it was definitely one of the best. For dinner we ordered the penne vodka, which was really good but not the creamiest vodka sauce that I've ever had. Nonetheless it was still pretty tasty (it's hard to mess up penne vodka!). I was a little shocked but the short wine list for an Italian spot but their Cabernet is pretty decent.

We had a delightful dining experience at this restaurant. Our waiter impressed us with exceptional service, and the food surpassed our expectations in both taste and presentation. The ambiance contributed to a splendid atmosphere that enhanced our meal. It's an absolute must-visit when you're in the area for shopping. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit from start to finish.

Second time in a long while. I had the traditional eggs Benedict and it was delicious. I love English muffin better than pancakes for the eggs Benedict. The waiter was super friendly and treated us with some sample juices. Orange juice was excellent and fresh as well. I had a 30 min wait mainly because I didn't make reservations ahead of time and the spots get filled up very quickly. So do make reservations ahead of time on yelp!

Despite enduring popularity and long wait times, my experience at this trendy breakfast spot was mixed. The hour-long queue set high expectations which were somewhat met, but not enough to justify a return visit. I sampled the fish congee, which had the advantage of being boneless, although the fish could have been softer. My request for no scallions was heeded, but my congee came with an overpowering amount of cilantro. The beef and shrimp rice roll was satisfactory, though chive-heavy for my taste. The Hong Kong Milk Tea was notably bitter, but customizable with table-side sugar. The price point was higher than average for dim sum, with a personal tab of $15 pre-tax and tip for congee, a rice roll, and tea. In essence, while the food was decent, the overall experience doesn't compel me to endure another lengthy wait.

I had the privilege to be invited to post-Christmas dinner with friends. The ambiance was cozy and gives the essence of being in Europe. This Spanish restaurant is known for their paella and sangria. Both definitely did not disappoint. Sangria was amazing and a half pitcher, which feeds four people is less than $20. The food portions from what I saw was plentiful and ordering to share would be safe and cost effective. For appetizers, we got the garlic shrimp and chorizo which was authentic and amazing. For entree we got the paella, I personally got the vegetarian paella which was under $20 and it was plentiful. The paella is served on a hot pan and two scoops of that dish I was already full. Service was standard definitely not bad, however, they recommend that tip be in cash and they do not take reservations.

Title: A Must-Visit Taco Haven in the City!

Review:

Absolutely outstanding! This taco spot lives up to its reputation as one of the city's finest. Despite the inevitable wait due to its popularity, it's well worth it. The service is swift, ensuring you get your tasty fix without delay. However, be prepared for the limited seating due to the constant crowds. Yet, that's a small price to pay for some of the best tacos around. A true gem for taco aficionados!

Celebrated my sister's birthday at this spot and what an experience! Kicking things off with champagne in the bathroom added a quirky yet luxurious touch to the evening. The restaurant exudes trendiness and class, creating the perfect atmosphere for a special occasion. The staff was all smiles and incredibly accommodating, adding to the overall positive vibe. And the food? Absolutely delicious. Highly recommend this place for anyone looking to make their celebration extra memorable.

Nestled discretely near my office, I finally seized the opportunity to dine at this upscale gem during restaurant week, where an enticing $26 two-course lunch special awaited. The regal ambiance was further accentuated as our party of 12 enjoyed the luxury of a private room. Cleanliness and opulence extended to the restroom facilities, complete with a full-length mirror.

Service was exceptional, with attentive waiters ensuring our every need was met promptly. The culinary journey began with a New England clam chowder that, while decent, reminded me of an elevated Hale and Hearty offering. My main course, a beautifully seared salmon, was executed with finesse—the texture perfect, moist, yet it curiously stood alone on the plate, missing a companion side dish like pilaf.

While I balked at the $4.25 price tag for soft drinks, overall, the experience was one to be savored, leaving me satisfied with my inaugural visit to this distinguished establishment.

Following a leisurely walk around Central Park, my companion and I decided to visit this local eatery for a much-needed snack. We kicked off our meal with a shareable dip foursome, including a standout charred jalapeño, a smooth guajillo chili salsa, a runny yet satisfying black bean dip, and a house tortilla selection. The poblano queso, although not to my taste due to its grainy texture, may appeal to those who don't mind a feta-like consistency.

The stars of our meal were undoubtedly the tacos. The lobster taco was a delightful surprise, offering a unique and delicious flavor that left us craving more. Meanwhile, the Nashville hot chicken tacos lived up to their name, delivering a flavorful punch that made them unforgettable.

Service was another high point of our visit, with staff that were prompt, attentive, and exuding friendliness. The efficiency with which our food arrived only added to the overall positive dining experience. This spot is a solid choice for a quick, delectable bite that refuels you for the day ahead.

Title: Mixed Bag at Local Eatery

My recent visit to this restaurant left me with a taste of the good, the mediocre, and areas in need of improvement. The star of the show here is undoubtedly the bakery section. Biting into their fresh pastries and bread evokes the very essence of a master baker's skill—crisp, warm, and utterly delicious. 

However, the sparkling reviews stop at the bakery counter. The other food offerings don't justify their hefty price tags. I'd advise skipping the more adventurous soups, which might be too avant-garde for some, and the salads that sadly fail to impress. A word of caution: I've heard whispers of unfortunate experiences with the fish dishes, which may be best avoided.

If you're looking for value, you might find yourself reminiscing about Pret's approach to quality and cost. This establishment would benefit from taking a leaf out of their book.

Despite these culinary missteps, the restaurant shines in cleanliness and customer service. The staff exudes warmth and friendliness, offering smiles that are a welcome relief in our often too-busy lives.

In short: come for the bread and pastries, stay for the service, but consider dining elsewhere for a full meal.

Wolfnights is a local gem just a stone's throw from my place, renowned for its allure as a drunchies haven, yet I find it's a solid choice anytime. I recently indulged in the 'Dire Wolf', a $12+ wrap that initially appeared undersized, but it packed a punch with its fiery, crunchy goodness – absolutely delicious. It left such an impression that I returned the next evening, sampling the 'Brothers Grimm'. While it was enjoyable, the Dire Wolf still reigns supreme in flavor. Open past 11pm on a weekday, Wolfnights has easily become my default spot for late work nights or casual hangouts. Bonus: the swinging seats up front are perfect for some relaxed people-watching. Highly recommend!

Walked by here dozens of times, but never tried it. I was looking forward to coming in since it always appears on yelp as a happy hour spot in the neighborhood.  The website and yelp show their happy hour ending at 7pm on weekdays. I got here at 6:40pm, hoping to grab a seat and some drinks from the HH menu.  Unfortunately, the hostess told me they stop seating for HH at 6:30pm as shown in the sign at the podium.  That's a really strange policy since most places will often extend or let you order from the HH menu even if you're seated right at the end of the hour. Either way, we requested to be seated for drinks and some apps.  I would have been more impressed if the food and service made up for the abbreviated HH. However we were seated at a table where we had to ask for silverware, napkins, etc. piecemeal.  Nothing was set on the table for us, even after we ordered.  Maybe the server was tired or having a bad day, but her lack of care didn't help our poor impression of this place. Drinks and fish and chips were ok -- the fries were the best part of the evening. Those were legit.  Not sure I would come back here though.
Happy hour is a win here.  Good cocktails and appetizers available along with nicely priced oysters during that time

Such a cute brunch spot in the St. Marks area! We were able to make a reservation for 2 for 12:30pm on a Saturday (the reservation was made the day before) and they were able to seat us promptly. David's Cafe is a quaint little space with so much charm! Their simplistic menu along with their brunch cocktail items made it easy to decide what I wanted - The Farmers Omelet (comes with two crispy strips of bacon, large potato home fries seasoned perfectly, and a refreshing mesclun salad). My friend and I also split a carafe of mimosa. Although there's no bottomless option, the carafe definitely hit the spot. The coffee was great too!Service was lightning fast and I thought the prices were reasonable for a NYC bunch.

I just moved to FiDi last month and so I am on a hunt for my new go-to Indian food spot. I ordered from here on Monday - we got garlic naan, paneer tikka masala and samosa chaat. I really liked the samosa chaat, it hit the spot. Only thing is that I asked for no cilantro on top, yet it came with cilantro on top. The garlic naan was really good and I was able to rewarm so it wasn't soggy. The paneer tikka masala was interesting, the gravy didn't taste like normal gravy.. it was more on the tangy tomato paste side, not on the creamy side. I also asked for this to be spicy but it was not. We also did a cost analysis across of couple of places that do deliver by me and this one was the most reasonably priced so that's good. Also this place serves rice complementary with the entree so that's a good perk  that I didn't expect in NYC. I am still going to be on the hunt for my go-to Indian but this place wasn't bad but didn't woo me

Came in the day before leaving nyc for a quick bite to eat. It was kind of chilly so we diddnt have a chance to eat outside. I was actually kind of sad about that. Let me start out by saying that we did recive 5 star service from our wonderfull server. He was extremely helpfully and put up with my roommates friends crap so he was more then the best of the best. We ordered a starter of chips & guac. Some drinks and a few other sides. The guac actually had a little bit of a strange flavor to it and the burger I ordered did lack flavor. This place did happen to have the best taste out of alot of drinks in nyc. If I am ever looking for a great place to have a few drinks on the upper West side on a nice night, I will remember this place and stop by with a ton of friends for drinks on the patio.
not bad, a typical chinese takeout place in flatiron area that provides your traditional american chinese food offering. they also have a 3 dish with rice option for roughly $9.

I've been here twice, once for dinner and once for lunch. The place is tiny and right by Baruch so of course it's generally quite crowded.General notes: A bit pricey for portion size.Tea eggs are good though the "egg" listing as extra is just a plain hard boiled for $1.25 which is ridiculous. Their noodles are alright also.I got the tea egg as well as the eel over rice the first time which was similar to what you can find in Japanese places. The sauce is less sweet than the Japanese counterpart and while I liked it, I found the portions to be a bit tiny for the price. The side seaweed salad was fine. The milk green tea was alright as well. It had some good tea flavor but it was a tad too sweet. The tea eggs were good though I'd prefer if I didn't have to peel them myself.The second time for lunch I got their bam bam noodle which is their take on minced pork over rice as well as their tea eggs again. I asked the waitstaff whether the egg extra listed in toppings is a tea egg and it turned it it was a plain cut hard boiled egg so I didn't bother. I found the dish slightly oily and not too spicy so I added some of their chili oil which was alright. I also added one of the tea eggs from my appetizer for some extra flavor. The dish worked well enough for lunch but I wouldn't go out of my way.Around 3 star or 3.5 star would be more accurate for the quality of food compared to the prices. However, there aren't many good Chinese in the area (though there is definitely more now than there used to be) so this place does well especially with Baruch nearby. Place is alright. 3.4

Title: A Luxurious Belated Valentine’s Day at [Restaurant Name]

Review:
As someone who isn’t a connoisseur of steak, my belated Valentine’s Day dinner at [Restaurant Name] was unexpectedly transformative. The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the authentic imported Japanese wagyu beef. Its rich, delectable fattiness lingers in my memory as a benchmark for culinary excellence.

My boyfriend, a more seasoned meat aficionado, made the perfect call with the wagyu selection, and it's safe to say it went straight to my heart in more ways than one. While we enjoyed a variety of meats, the wagyu stood out as the star of the show.

Service at [Restaurant Name] was impeccable. Our waiter was knowledgeable, guiding us through the preparation process, ensuring we savor the wagyu to its fullest potential. Her attentiveness wasn't limited to the culinary advice—she was also consistently present, filling up our water glasses and making sure we were comfortable throughout the evening.

The ambiance struck the right chord, fostering a close-knit and intimate setting which was much appreciated. It allowed for a private dining experience where conversation could flow easily without the intrusion of noise from other patrons. The thoughtful booth setup truly minimized any potential disruption.

Be mindful that [Restaurant Name] offers a dining experience that comes with a luxury price tag. However, for a special occasion, it's absolutely justified. And do remember, reservations are essential, as this gem is justifiably in high demand.

In summary, [Restaurant Name] offered an unforgettable experience where service, ambiance, and the pinnacle of fine meats combined to create a perfect evening.

I've walked by Andrews so many times, but never took a second to check out the menu until I was invited to have lunch here by a colleague.We got there during prime lunch time and the place was packed with a short line to get seated. We were greeted as soon as we walked in and surprisingly waited no more than 5 minutes for a table. Lots of options on the menu from nachos, salads to cheesesteaks - there really is something for everyone here! I tried the turkey club, which came with a pickle slice and coleslaw on the side. The lettuce was fresh, the bacon was crispy and it was a huge serving so I ended up taking half to go. My colleague got an omelette and enjoyed it. I noticed many tables also got omelettes or a breakfast dish, so looking forward to coming back for breakfast/brunch. Overall quick, attentive service. I recommend this spot if you're looking for a good diner spot in this area!

Came here for early dinner. Pizza before 6pm is 50% off. Awesome!! Gratuity is included in the price. We got 3 pizzas and a bottle of red wine, it came to $99. Attentive and friendly service. The waitress gave our kids paper and crayons for a bit of entertainment. Will definitely be back soon!

Title: Havana Central: A Cuban Jewel in Times Square

Let me say it loud and clear – Havana Central is a gem! It might seem counterintuitive, nestled in the tourist hubbub near Times Square, but don't be misled; this place is no trap. From the moment you spot that charming, neon palm sign, you're in for an experience that's as authentic as it is enchanting.

Stepping inside, the decor captivates with its bright colors, faux trees, and gorgeous stained glass - making the vibe festive and lively. I was greeted by the sounds of a live band, setting the scene for a night of Cuban celebration.

At the bar, the magic continued with bartenders delivering service that was nothing short of stellar. Now, onto the drinks - the mojitos here are a must-try. Every flavor is a hit, but the coconut mojito touched my soul – trust me on this.

As for the food, a check-in on Yelp snagged me a complimentary Cuban empanada. The popular Cubano variation was pure delight, with its crispy exterior yielding to a smoky and savory filling. I skipped the sizable paella for the arroz con camarones, and boy, was that a win! The dish was huge, fragrant, and brilliantly spiced. The saffron rice and juicy shrimp were so good that leftovers doubled as a mouthwatering breakfast.

Havana Central isn't just a restaurant; it's a slice of Cuba right in the heart of New York City. It's a 5-star knockout that's left me dreaming of my next visit. If you find yourself in NYC, do yourself a favor and let Havana Central sweep you off your feet.

Title: A Hot Pot Gem Uncovered During Chinese New Year

My delayed review is a testament to the lasting impression this alternative to the bustling 99 Favor Taste made on me during the Chinese New Year celebrations. Securing a table at this haven was fortuitous and educational, as their staff eagerly introduced us to the hot pot ritual—a delightful, interactive dining experience that warms the soul.

What stood out was the complimentary beverage selection, featuring Asian delights like Yakult-inspired drinks and Yeo's, alongside a self-serve ice cream station for a sweet finale—don't miss out on this! The variety at the hot pot was impressive, though the crab fell short on freshness. However, their diverse offerings ensured this was a minor hiccup.

The ambiance was energized by eclectic murals, adding a unique charm to the space. This place's personality is distinct, embracing its quirks with confidence.

A word of caution: the layout is cozy, which means navigating the tight quarters requires a bit of finesse. And while the selection may vary slightly from what 99 Favor Taste patrons are accustomed to, the quality on most items doesn't disappoint.

In summary, this hot pot spot stands out with its included drinks and desserts, contributing to a memorable and flavorful dining adventure. A must-visit for those craving a steamy culinary escapade with a side of character.

I recently visited a restaurant for their touted high tea experience, specifically opting for the Eloise high tea set upon our server's recommendation for its charm. While the presentation lived up to the 'super cute' expectation with an adorable aesthetic, the taste unfortunately did not follow suit. My friend and I sampled the desserts only to find them overwhelmingly sweet, reminiscent of the fare one might find in a supermarket bakery aisle rather than a specialty dining establishment. In essence, while it scores high on visual appeal, the Eloise high tea left our taste buds underwhelmed.

Tucked beneath a bustling mall lies a slice of Spain reminiscent of Eatily, yet with its own distinct flair. While it may not exude the enchanting glamour one might daydream about, this food court's reality is surprisingly remarkable given its location.

Though it may lack some of the magic and warmth anticipated, when viewed through the lens of its mall setting, it impresses. The array of Spanish cuisine offers a delightful experience that could easily see you returning and happily investing in another round of culinary exploration.

In essence, if you're looking for a taste of Spain without stepping outside the convenience of your shopping spree, this spot is definitely worth a visit.

Title: A Delectable Feast Delivered: Mughlai Special Steals the Show

I recently indulged in the Mughlai Special for dinner, a steal at $15.95, and I must say, it's a feast for both the palate and wallet. The package arrived with a samosa, Chicken Tikka Masala, and a generously proportioned piece of naan bread.

Starting with the naan, it was a fluffy delight, making the perfect companion for scooping up the rich, creamy Chicken Tikka Masala. The samosa was a pleasant surprise, not only scrumptious but also in a double serving. The Tikka Masala itself deserves praise; it was a harmonious blend of creamy, buttery goodness with a tangy twist, brimming with flavors and the right punch of spices.

Beyond the special, I relished the Saag Paneer and Mughlai Chicken Curry. The Saag Paneer was generous with cheese cubes – a cheese lover's dream. Both dishes were satisfying, and the portion sizes were large enough to promise a delicious lunch the following day.

In a nutshell, this restaurant delivers not just food, but also joy and satisfaction. Highly recommended for anyone craving authentic flavors from the comfort of their home.

I recently visited this restaurant for brunch and chose the French toast. Utilizing the Yelp waitlist certainly helped avoid longer waits. While the food was satisfactory, I find myself questioning the value for money. Our seating location detracted from the dining experience, as it was in a high-traffic area with constant disturbances from passersby. Regrettably, this discomfort has dissuaded me from planning a return visit.

Upon the recommendation of a friend and despite a middling 3-star Yelp review, I visited this local favorite, famed from its appearance on the TV show "Friend's Fridge," for a Sunday brunch. The wait for a table of two was manageable, and the option to eat at the bar expedited seating.

The extensive menu tempted with many attractive options, but I settled on the Breakfast Burrito. Priced at $14.50, it proved to be a hearty offering with scrambled eggs, cheddar, onions, peppers, and home fries, all wrapped in a whole wheat tortilla. A side of tangy salsa complemented the dish, enhancing the already flavorful ingredients. The side of home fries was a bonus.

Service was prompt and efficient, contributing to a satisfying dining experience. This establishment is certainly worth a revisit.

Delicious! I'm so glad a great ramen is nearby. My fiancé and I went after I found out I passed an exam as a celebration. It was a Friday night and it was a bit busy but we did not have to wait long. The seating is very close together at this place but we got a table by the wall so we  did not feel cramped at all. We ordered gyoza as an appetizer. I ordered the Tokyo Mule and the Spicy Miso Ramen and my fiancé ordered the Lychee Mojito and Chili Chicken Ramen. Since the pandemic, my fiancé and I ordered takeout from here and it was just as delicious as dining in. They pack everything for you nicely. I highly recommend the pumpkin tempura!
Great casual spot for Thai food. Got their lunch special (~$13) where they allow you to choose 1 appetizer + 1 entree.Tom yum was super flavorful and DELICIOUS!

Title: A Lackluster Lunch at Sky 55 Bar & Grill

I recently visited Sky 55 Bar & Grill for a Tuesday afternoon lunch and came away underwhelmed. The restaurant boasts a prime location in Manhattan's Financial District, situated on the picturesque Elevated Acre. Despite this, the experience was marred by confusing entrance logistics and subpar offerings.

Quality-wise, the Tuna Tartare had the freshness I anticipated but didn't live up to its $21 price point, leaving me questioning the value. The Short Rib Grilled Cheese, though generous in size and served on delightfully thick Texas Toast, suffered a balance issue with an overabundance of caramelized onions overshadowing the otherwise tasteful and tender short rib.

Value felt amiss here, with dishes like the aforementioned Tuna Tartare and $17 Short Rib Grilled Cheese coming in steep for the overall quality.

The ambiance is simple and upscale, with an outdoor patio that's pleasant yet wanting for shade. The view from the window-side tables can be a redeeming feature, offering a nice backdrop for the business lunch crowd that seemed to populate the space.

Service was slower than expected for a weekday lunch spot in such a bustling area, which could be frustrating for those with limited time.

Parking options are virtually non-existent, a notable inconvenience for anyone considering driving to the venue.

All in one, Sky 55 Bar & Grill didn't hit the mark for me with its combination of overpriced food, slow service, and logistical nuisances. There are better places in the Financial District to spend your lunch hour.

Title: A Staple of NYC Dining: Olio e Piú

Olio e Piú remains an unrivaled gem in New York City's culinary scene, firmly holding its place as my top restaurant pick. The consistency of the delectable fare, top-notch service, and the enchanting ambiance, especially on the patio, has never failed to deliver an exceptional dining experience.

On my latest visit, I indulged in my all-time favorite, the Margherita pizza, a testament to simplicity perfected. Its light crust and doughy bite argue a strong case for the city's best. The Clam Linguini, a newcomer to my palate, impressed with its freshness, though a touch more salt or lemon zest might have elevated it further. Nonetheless, it was a delightful addition that's generous enough to be shared between two.

The seafood appetizer, featuring white fish, squid, and notably large shrimp, albeit only two, was a crispy delight and ideal for a small group. Its subtle sophistication and flavors make it an excellent preamble to any meal.

Service was impeccable as always, and a special shoutout to Petar, who ensured our experience was flawless. Olio e Piú continues to be a must-visit before my eventual return to LA, promising a few more memorable meals before departure. Thank you for the culinary excellence that keeps me coming back.

If you want to save a plane ticket to Naples to try authentic Neapolitan pizza, this place is it! I have been to the original store on my last trip to Italy and this sister store is almost the same. Keep in mind that the original pizza has a lot of sauce and is quite watery and must be eaten ASAP or everything just sorta gets soft.  It's definitely something different that you should try if you're into this style.  I will probably stick with the New York slice and treat myself with sorbillo when I get a hankering for it!

Rarely is a fast casual spot amazing enough to warrant five stars from me. But. I've been here multiple times, for MealPal and standard orders, lunch and dinner, and their food is consistently fresh and flavorful.The chicken, beef, and salmon kebabs are perfectly seasoned and cooked, tender, and juicy. The potatoes and zucchini are wonderfully roasted. The beets are great, as are their other salads. For dips, you're golden if you get their spicy hummus, Persian eggplant, cucumber yogurt, or spinach yogurt. Even their bases with the quinoa or vegetable rice are tasty. Their food truly embodies healthy eating that doesn't skimp on the flavor at all. Oh, and you can get a few pieces of roasted garlic with your meal. I mean hello. Winner winner, dark meat chicken dinner.Their hot sauce is also straight fire. No, not the over-the-top spicy kind, but the quality how-did-they-make-this kind. Tangy, chunky, and it perfectly complements the other items. Great fluffy pita as well.I honestly can't think of any negatives since I've never had a bad experience here.

Old fashioned Diner on 57th Street.As any Diner it has a huge menu,from breakfasts to full dinners. My group was hungry and craved for different dishes, so we were all happy.  Chicken Cubano Entree, there is nothing Cubano about it, there is Cilantro as an ingredient and Saffron Rice.  Thin slices of Chicken cooked with seasoning, a pinch of hot pepper, and cilantro. The rice, pale yellow and tasty and Caramelized Onions, Tomatoes over the rice. I liked it.  Pastrami Sandwich  was not bad. The meat was tender and lean. I had a taste.Crab Cakes made with real Crab,not imitation stuffMy niece did like it. Fries, crispy and golden.Hamburger and Fries could not be left out from  our choice of food.The Strawberry Blonde Cheesecake and Chocolate Cake rounded our meal.  We shared Dessert since portions are generous. Both were very good.

I booked this place for a special dinner for my friend's birthday about a month in advance. Reservations were fairly easy to come by on Resy. We came at 6:30pm on a Tuesday night, and the restaurant had several tables full already. We were seated in the main room, and given water and menus immediately (they did not seat me until my friend arrived). We ordered bread ($5), burrata for an appetizer, and three pastas. The bread was presented first, served with olive oil and salt. It was good, but I have had better complimentary bread at other restaurants. The burrata, served with sliced figs and balsamic vinegar, was good, but it was something I could have made at home on my own. Our two pastas that were served next, the tagliatelle, and the torchio, were simply put, not good at all. My friend remarked that the torchio has a better, bouncier texture than the tagliatelle. I thought the taste was better than the tagliatelle also, which was quite bland. No one checked on us after we had started eating to see if everything was good, as is common in most other New York restaurants. There was a long wait in between the pasta and the risotto. The risotto was not good at all - it was flavorless, with some pieces of pancetta thrown in. Then came the time for dessert - we ordered the olive oil cake. I had called Il Buco earlier in the day, requesting to please send out a dessert for my friend's birthday and write happy birthday on it. This request was not complied with, which I was actually quite annoyed about, as I hadn't enjoyed any of the food. The best thing about this restaurant was the ambience. Looking around, you can see that it is truly a scene, and specifically for beautiful people. The decor makes you feel as if you've been transported to a rustic Italian restaurant in the heart of Tuscany. The acoustics of the room are unfortunately not set up in a way that allows you to hear your dining companion well. The service here was very brusque and abrupt. We had one man come out to us at the beginning of the meal, but then as we were caught up in conversation, he waved his hand at us, as if to say "forget about it", and never returned to our table again. The rest of the servers were okay, but seemed harried. I would not recommend this place or return, which is unfortunate because it is famed as one of New York's best.

I recently visited this charming little spot for their weekday lunch special, pricing most pasta dishes at a delightful $11. Opting for the lobster linguine while my mom chose the cavatelli in lamb ragu, we were thrilled with our choices. Both dishes boasted al dente perfection, accompanied by rich, flavorful sauces in portions so generous we struggled to finish – but finish we did, due to their irresistible taste. Despite its compact size (be wise and book ahead), the bustling ambiance is complemented by a remarkably friendly and attentive staff. For pasta lovers seeking a meal that truly delivers value for money, this place is a must-try.

Title: Budget Bites on the Go at New Houston St. Pizza Joint

Just stumbled upon an A-ok dollar pizza shop on Houston, near Allen Street, and this newcomer is small but mighty in its offerings. The place, though lacking seating, compensates with cleanliness and bright lights. An array of pies tempts you, slice by slice, alongside a spread of eats from wings to hot sandwiches.

I opted for the classic plain slice: generously cheesy, decently sauced, atop a thicker, softer crust. My preference leans towards the thinner, crispier variety, with a sauce that packs a more pronounced tomato punch. With the joint's recent opening, there's potential for pizza perfection in the making.

The presence of a cash machine and a fridge filled with soft drinks adds to the convenience. Good for a quick, wallet-friendly bite, this spot caters to the city's relentless pace. Although the crust and sauce might need some tweaking, it's a solid choice for the on-the-go pizza aficionado. Mic drop for the love of pizza - I'm out!

A must try!I have loved The Tang since I first visited the East Village location two years ago and have been back multiple times. This was my first time visiting the Upper West side location, and I had a wonderful dining experience. The menu has really evolved over time. They have always had excellent noodles, but they have really stepped up their game in all other aspects of the menu.FOOD:-Braised beef noodle soup: Excellent beef noodle soup. I think it's really well made, but I would recommend getting the sizzling noodles or drunk noodles if you're only going to get one noodle dish-Seared beef short ribs: Not a must try, but so delicious-Pork knuckle: absolutely delicious pork knuckles over rice. I think this is a must try!-Hot and sour noodles: one of my favorite Chinese dishes of all time. The Tang did it justice-Shredded potato salad: very delicious, crisp potatoes packed with flavor-Sesame tofu: good, but not a must tryThese are just the dishes I had this time, but I have had many other things on the menu. Everything on the menu is worth checking out!The service was friendly and attentive. The food came out super quickly and was super delicious. The restaurant is open, spacious, clean and comfortable. I highly recommend visiting both the UWS and East Village locations.

Cha Chan Tang has been a fixture in Chinatown for over a decade, offering Hong Kong comfort cuisine. The menu isn't particularly healthy, but they serve a wide variety of green and black teas, and mixed aloe vera drinks. We generally visit Cha Chan Tang after dinner with friends for non-alcoholic drinks and to shoot the breeze, because of the restaurant's slightly larger capacity and slightly later hours compared to nearby cafes.Cha Chan Tang can get crowded in the evenings, but seating is generally available during lunch hours.

I would not ever recommend this place to anyone. Save yourself some money and eat at Upland if you really want high end food. The food is definitely not extravagant or delicious. The portions are so so less that even after spending $50 per person you would be left hungry. The server was nice enough to customize my order and get me a vegetarian pesto pasta with rigatoni but the pasta was not Al Dente but was rather difficult to chew and not properly boiled. Even the bread given to us in the beginning was not fresh from the oven. I highly rely on yelp reviews and seeing how highly rated this place is I think the vegetarian options here might not be good. So refrain from visiting if you are a vegetarian. Not a vegetarian friendly place. My friend ordered some meat dish with octopus, shrimp and squid. He said it was ok and not great.

Madame Vo BBQ is the meat-centric spinoff of hit Vietnamese spot Madame Vo, offering a modern interpretation of the classic bo 7 mon, or beef seven ways.I've now been a couple of times in small to large groups, and they have a winner on their hands, judging by the steady crowd level. Come on a weeknight or off-peak if possible. Decor is trendy (floral wallpaper, huge murals, and Be@rbricks), with grills at the center of tables. Noisy space.What's frustrated me about this concept is the $59/person sampler, which you would think would be the best pick, but I've done a-la-carte each time and we've come out full for $30-40 a person. If you're in a group of four, each order should give everyone a chance to taste; I think we did about 2 dishes per person. Maybe the sampler is a truly preposterous amount of meat.My favorites were the carpaccio, raw round-eye garnished with generous fried shallots and soaking in a citrusy vinaigrette, and the meatballs, here a juicy Berkshire pork version. I thought the steak and short rib were also good; tongue and oxtail are worth trying. Bo la lot, ground beef in a betel leaf wrap, has a pretty strong taste.For all of the meats, you'll get rice paper and water to dip it in, as well as various fixings, to make your own summer rolls. Fun interactive experience. Service is solid. Bathrooms are clean. It does get a bit smoky as there's not the hanging vent directly above the grill, but not ridiculous.Recommended for a new side of Vietnamese food.

I attended an event at this restaurant and was thoroughly impressed by the excellent service provided for our large group. Our visit coincided with happy hour, which featured an array of specials at attractive prices. The food, including cauliflower wings, chicken wings, hamburger sliders, and French fries, was served in generous portions, arrived piping hot, and was delicious to boot. The drinks were equally satisfying, rounding off a fantastic dining experience. In summary, this eatery offers great value and is highly recommended for group gatherings.

Restaurant Week success! The food was ahhhmazing! But the lighting stole the show and my heart - I felt like I was under the sea. My only issues is that we had a reservation and still had to wait nearly 45 mins for our table. Better management of reservations is necessary. You're already bombarded with hectic tourism in Times Square; to then after work be bombarded with waiting to sit and dine? And, secondly, the decor I see on Yelp is completely different and set a completely different tone than what I expected with such excitement. Where's the white seating?! ''Twas so elegant and chic. Our waitress was also not very attentive. We had to track down another waiter just for basic needs: utensils, chopsticks, condiments for sushi. Nonetheless, the food was delicious and did not upset. And, HELLO COMPLIMENTARY BREAD!! I'd go back! Order: Appetizers, Steak, and chocolate/caramel dessert. Perfection and beautiful presentation of every dish, which is key.

I was pleasantly surprised by this bustling establishment, especially as commercial spots aren't typically my cup of tea. The spacious interior ensures finding a seat isn't the herculean task it usually is in NYC, especially on weekends. The staff deserve a special mention for their prompt and friendly service.

When it comes to the food, the generous portions are a godsend for fueling up before a long day of city exploration. I indulged in the salted caramel pancakes which were delightful, although a tad denser than my ideal. However, the rich and smooth caramel sauce complemented them beautifully. Overall, this restaurant is a gem that marries great vibes with filling, tasty food. Highly recommended!

Great place. Came here at around 7 on a Tuesday night and it was almost completely packed. Food was delicious - got the spicy pork bulgogi. They give you a bunch of side dishes, like traditional Korean restaurants do. It is a bit pricey. Be prepared to spend almost $30 per person.Only complaints I have would be about some of the side dishes like the seaweed and the rice soup. They just tasted bad lol. And also, the price is a little high for me, so I rate 4/5 stars.

Overpriced, flavorless, and way too greasy.I ordered Little Italy(Asiago, Mozzarella, Pepperoni, Tomato Sauce and Pesto on Levain Pullman)- did not taste any pesto, could not find tomato sauce. Bread was not crispy, the edge was extremely hard and dry not from toast, just dripping with grease in center. I also ordered side of onion rings, there was 6 rings in it. The batter was crispy but way to greasy.Cheese fries was under fried and what seemed like melted cheese did  not taste like cheese. Overall it was disgusting. Threw out more than half.

It was my first time trying DokoDemo so I didn't have many expectations going it. I ordered online and thought they'd pack it to-go for us to takeaway. When I got there, I was greeted by three men who were super friendly and welcoming. I told them we ordered online and he asked if we wanted to eat in or take-out. Given the option, I, of course, chose to eat in.Although we ordered ahead, they haven't started prepping our food yet, which was okay since we weren't in a rush. We ordered the takoyaki and beef yakisoba. It took a while since it was made fresh.The yakisoba was good, but the beef was the star. It was juicy and tender and the yakisoba was very flavorful. The takoyaki was good as well but wasn't spectacular. It oddly came with a pita on the side which I like but was kind of weird. Instead of bonito flakes, it came with some kind of rice krispy, which I don't prefer. Bonito flakes make takoyaki delicious! Sad that it didn't come with any.Overall, the shop was very nice and cozy. The people there were friendly. The food was good, but a bit pricey.

I recently had my second visit to this restaurant with my cousin, arriving during the tail-end of happy hour at 8:30 pm. To our disappointment, the place was unexpectedly out of many items, including sangria, wine, coke, and chicken. With limited options, I opted for a shrimp Caesar salad alongside a whiskey with ginger beer. My cousin mirrored my drink choice but went for the shrimp Rasta pasta.

The jerk shrimp topping both our dishes was the highlight, offering a well-executed spicy kick that we enjoyed. However, the pasta had an unexpected sweetness that didn't quite hit the mark for us, leaving a mixed impression. Despite the letdowns, in recognition of the flavorsome jerk shrimp, I'm willing to give the restaurant another chance, chalking up the mishaps to an off night.

The five of us went to Hanoi Soup Shop for lunch on a Saturday. I should've done my research because the shop was much smaller than I expected and barely fit all of us. There are two restaurants and Hanoi Soup Shop on the left is open for lunch, and the other one on the right is open for dinner. Even though the shop was small, it may have been a good thing because the AC and the fan worked really well and it was actually cool enough inside to consider eating pho on a summer day. The pho was great - I wish there were more greens, like bean sprouts and baby bok choy.My friend and I split a bahn mi, which was also really good. The sandwich contained three thick slices of pork. But beware of the sandwich because very spicy green pepper slices are hidden inside of it. I removed a slice after tasting a hint of it and I thought that was it. However, there was an extra slice further inside of the sandwich, and I took a huge hit and suffered for a good ten minutes - I can handle most of the spicy dishes in New York but I not this. Therefore, for those who can't tolerate spicy food, I recommend asking the staff to remove the peppers when ordering. I'm going to do that when I visit next time.

Tucked into a cozy corner lies a charming burger and shake spot that sticks to the essentials while offering some unique twists. My choice, the Mexicali, boasted a patty rich in flavor, and my order was served up speedily. Each element was balanced just right, including the notably sweet bun that encased the burger - a delightful touch for those with a penchant for a little sugar with their savory. However, be prepared to pay a bit more than expected; my burger cost $9 instead of the anticipated $7.50. A heads-up for card users: there's an additional fee for non-cash payments. Bring cash to get the best value at this humble hangout.

Title: A Late-Night Delight at the Local Ramen Shop

Last week, I found myself craving a bowl of ramen at the eleventh hour and stumbled upon this gem that caters to the night owls among us, closing at 11:30 pm with a final food call at 11. To my delight, the spicy ramen here hits the perfect heat mark – mouthwateringly spicy but not searing, with the soy garlic "basic" ramen revealing itself as anything but basic. Despite its misleading name, it has become my go-to favorite with a rich depth of flavor.

I also ventured to try the spicy miso variety and it did not disappoint. Both bowls boasted a harmonious balance of seasoning, and to my relief, steered clear of being too salty or setting my mouth on fire. The noodles deserve a special mention; the 'thick' option provided a satisfying chew without veering into udon territory – just a touch more substantial than their 'wavy' counterparts.

The hospitality here is the cherry on top. Arriving towards the end of the night, I was half-expecting to be rushed through my meal, but the staff was welcoming, allowing for a relaxed dining experience. In short, this ramen shop is an absolute must-visit for anyone in search of comfort food and a warm welcome, no matter the hour.

Title: Summer Sips and Bites at The Expat's Happy Hour

My visit to The Expat for their summer happy hour was an absolute delight. Arriving on a bustling Friday evening, the place had a vibrant atmosphere that only grew as the night progressed. Perched at the bar from 5:45 pm, we were met with exemplary service; the bartender was nothing short of attentive.

The kumquat spritz, a highlight at a mere $5, was a sensational concoction, both in taste and value. As an added environmentally-conscious touch, I appreciated the use of metal straws over the less favorable paper alternatives. Accompanying our drinks, the $5 calamari appetizer was a neat twist served on skewers. Although it leaned towards the doughy side, lacking that desired crunch, the accompanying sauce was a redeeming feature that elevated the dish.

By the time we left just after 7 pm, the space had filled to the brim, echoing the popularity of The Expat's happy hour. The decor complemented the lively scene, and the menu promised more enticing items that beckon a return visit. Overall, The Expat nailed the happy hour experience, and I'm enthusiastically looking forward to my next outing there.

Westville Hell's Kitchen offers a trendy and spacious setting, perfect for a casual lunch. My friend and I popped in around midday on a Monday and were seated immediately, appreciating the airy half-full dining room. We opted for the grilled salmon plate and marinated chicken breast, both accompanied by two market vegetables. While the sides were underwhelming—with the garlic mashed potatoes needing more garlic punch and the honey dijon on the brussels sprouts not hitting the mark—the main dishes were competently cooked. The chicken was praised for its moistness, but my salmon and broccoli lacked the flavor one might expect from a meal at this price point.

Service was punctual and routine, though lacking a personal touch. Our server's efficiency came across as scripted, and there was a sense of unwelcomeness, highlighted by the removal of our water bottle without offering a refill and a tinge of sarcasm during our interactions.

In summary, Westville Hell's Kitchen is a fair choice if you're nearby and value quality ingredients at a suitable price for the area. Still, an improvement in both service tone and dish flavoring would be necessary to entice a return visit.

**The River's Edge: A Brunch Experience with a View**
