Nestled by the iconic Brooklyn Bridge, The River's Edge offers a delightful farm-to-table brunch experience. Reservations led to being promptly greeted and comfortably seated, a testament to the deceptively spacious venue with its grand windows.

The menu delights with fresh and flavorful options. The scrambled eggs, intertwined with kale and spinach, accompanied by peppery arugula and toast, are elevated by what might just be the best bacon in the area – smoky, crisp, and utterly unforgettable. The French toast transcends expectations, its buttery richness akin to a warm bread pudding and so delectable that syrup becomes superfluous.

The endeavor into the newer-age of brunch dishes presents a cauliflower crusted pizza that holds its own and a grilled chicken sandwich that, while satisfactory, is overshadowed by the accompanying delicious potatoes.

Coffee aficionados will appreciate the 'big ass cup of drip coffee' – robust, smooth, and perfect in its unadulterated form.

While the service was competent, there's room for polish in customer engagement. Overall, The River's Edge warrants a return visit – the view, ambiance, and signature dishes set the stage for a repeat brunch experience.

Title: Disappointing Dining Experience Despite Charming Aesthetics

I find myself constrained to award this restaurant a mere two stars, and that is primarily for two redeeming aspects: the delightful ambiance and a commendable chicken tortilla soup. Regrettably, the rest of the experience fell far short of expectations. Service was characterized by a frustrating sluggishness paired with an unwelcoming demeanor — a combination that can quickly sour any dining experience. 

Compounding the disappointment, the water had a peculiar, almost chemical taste that was off-putting. The guacamole proved bland, requiring an excessive amount of salt and extra lime to coax out some semblance of flavor. A graver letdown was the steak tacos, which arrived cold and so far from expectations that I barely managed a single bite. 

Perhaps most telling of the lack of care in customer service was the server’s indifference upon collecting my nearly untouched plate, neglecting to inquire about the quality of the meal or to address my evident dissatisfaction. In sum, the level of service and culinary execution I experienced does not encourage a return visit.

Title: A Nostalgic Bite in Hell's Kitchen

On a late afternoon stroll through the newly polished streets of Hell's Kitchen, my hunger pangs led me to The Meatball Shop, a far cry from my usual haunts. The once-dubious 9th Avenue now boasts this unassuming eatery, offering respite and a nostalgic backdrop for someone who remembers the avenues’ less savory days.

Perched at the bar, with a craving amplified by weeks of post-surgery sobriety, I relished a swiftly served vodka, followed by the more leisurely enjoyment of a Pimm's Cup. The bartender, brandishing a smile as satisfying as the fare, dished out an array of delicious meatballs which hit the spot, transforming us into contented creatures reveling in simple pleasure.

While The Meatball Shop won't etch a lasting impression in the gastronomic landscape, it served as a comforting solace during a tumultuous week. In the city where memories line the streets, it provided exactly what was needed—a momentary sanctuary and a testament to the healing powers of comfort food and a stiff drink.

good italian spot in midtown east. been around for years now, and with good reason. the food is so good it's hard for us to choose when ordering, i recommend anyone go family style and get things to split that way you get a bit of errythang. some must-orders: the caesar salad, the vodka sauce pizza, the penne vodka, the fusilli pesto, and the fettuccine alfredo. the perfect place to carb load, def check it out

Fast and friendly service with food that reminds me of the late night meals I'd have at street stalls in Taiwan. We got their Shanghai style fried rice, fried pork chop side, and chicken leg over rice for less than $15 total. The food came out very quickly. Their pork chop is great but I think the fried chicken leg stole the show! The skin was incredibly crispy, the meat was tender and not dry at all, and the chicken was seasoned perfectly and tasted authentic. The chicken leg came with rice, braised minced pork, and a generous portion of vegetables. There is a chili sauce at the table which goes very well with the rice. The fried items (pork chop, chicken leg) were crispy but not greasy. The fried rice also wasn't greasy.

Still yet to try the Kobe beef option here. The básic Korean dishes are done pretty decently. I'm a picky Korean and it satisfies the craving without the serious wow factor. My favorite thing here so far has been the bibimnaengmuyn. I really like that dish and it's good to have the option of eating it somewhere in the city.They also do a delicious soju infusion. I really enjoyed the cucumber version. We almost finished it between the two of us which mellowed out our night a little bit.It is spacious and not nearly as crowded as the OG don's Bogam. But a little less personal in character. If you like the big spacious restaurant style of modern NYC this is dressed to impress.

Title: A Flavorful Detour at Wok to Walk, NY

As a pizza enthusiast on a mission, I mistakenly overlooked a gem in New York's culinary scene — Wok to Walk. This Asian fast food spot, first experienced in Amsterdam, drew me back, this time post-pizza feast.

Opting for udon over my usual egg noodles, paired with beef, shrimp, peppers, and a tangy Saigon sauce, it was a reminder of Wok to Walk's allure. The food, slightly pricier than the average Chinese takeout, justifies the cost with freshness and quality apparent in every bite.

The service amplifies the experience — fast and efficient, ensuring you savor their creations without a long wait, a testament to their ten-minute turnaround promise.

If fate allowed, Wok to Walk would be on my dining rotation every fortnight, no question. New York has it, but here's a hopeful plea to bring this flavor-packed, quick-service spot to the hungry crowds of L.A.!

Rating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5 Stars)

Title: Hit and Miss at [Restaurant Name]

While the dining experience at [Restaurant Name] began on a high note with prompt seating, the service quickly plummeted from there. Unfortunately, the staff's lack of attention was unmistakable. Our server failed to inquire about our needs or offer any beverages, straddling the line between non-intrusive and neglectful.

The kitchen's speed in delivering our dishes was commendable, yet this was overshadowed by the absence of follow-up service. A simple request for parmesan cheese went unheeded, and our parched throats longed for drink refills that necessitated flagging down a passing waitstaff.

On the upside, the quality of the food did provide some redemption. However, with a competitive array of eateries nearby, the overall service experience at [Restaurant Name] falls short. Diners might find it worthwhile to explore other venues where the service matches the cuisine's standards.

Title: A Lively Brunch to Warm a Dreary Day

My Sunday brunch experience at this gem was nothing short of delightful. The menu brimmed with tasty options, and the craft mimosas, with the novel option to infuse them with Ciroc, were a highlight. Despite the gloomy December weather, the restaurant's ambiance was vibrant and inviting, thanks to the upbeat music and the warmth of the staff.

The fare was exceptional - the chicken and waffles, steak and huevos, eggs Benedict, and French toast were all executed to perfection. On a whim, we indulged in an extravagant ice cream sundae, complete with sparklers, which was both a visual and a gastronomical treat.

This place hits all the right notes for a fun, dressy brunch where you can unwind and savor good food and good company. Highly recommended for anyone looking to brighten up their weekend.

Had dinner here on Friday night and overall I'd say it was a good experience. We did get something messed up within the order, but the manager came by and fixed it up for us. We ordered a chicken appetizer but somehow we were given a cauliflower appetizer. The nice part was that they just let us have it for free and it was a pretty good dish. Came with 4 others so we ended up ordering about 5 different entrees with rice and naan and it was more than enough for all of us. Food came out relatively fast, was fresh and had a lot of flavor. Not too busy surprisingly on a Friday night though. Overall, good service and good food.

Amazing pizza! The thin crust took some getting used to because my sister and I were expecting deep dish pizza (for a minute we thought we were in Chicago--the flight was long enough that we could have been!). I also LOVED the ambience! The fact that this pizzeria was in a converted 19th-century church fed my inner historian. Service was fast and staff were attentive--we never had an empty water glass!

Title: Relaxed Evening at a Casual Spot

Last night, we dropped into this little gem for a casual post-work dinner with friends and the experience was quite delightful. Securing a table was a breeze, setting the stage for a relaxed evening. The service was commendable, with attentive staff making sure our meal went smoothly.

We sampled a variety of dishes, including steak tacos, a Rubin sandwich, and a nourishing grain bowl amped up with chicken and quinoa. Each dish was satisfying, but the Rubin sandwich stood out as the star - a flavorful twist on a classic that I would happily recommend.

For appetizers, the Korean wings truly stole the show; they were absolutely fantastic - a must-try for anyone with a love for bold flavors. The avocado mash, while decent, didn't quite hit the same high notes.

Overall, the ambiance is exactly what you'd look for in a place to unwind after a day's work: very casual and inviting. Perfect for those evenings when you want to dine out without any fuss.

Tucked away on the bustling St. Marks, this charming eatery delivers a delightful mix of sweet and spice with their honey glazed popcorn chicken—a hit amongst my friends and me. The nori shaky fries offered a pleasant twist on a classic snack. However, the Taiwanese sausage rice fell short of expectations, presenting a straightforward dish that left me craving a touch more culinary innovation. Despite that, the visit was an overall enjoyable experience in the heart of a food lover’s haven.

Title: A Thai Culinary Triumph

If you're looking for the ultimate Thai dining experience, this is the place to be. The value is undeniable with generous portions at a great price. The pick and mix option is a must-try, allowing a personalized taste adventure with two entrees, your choice of rice, and fresh lettuce. Do yourself a favor and indulge in the Ginger Short Rib – it's nothing short of amazing. A visit here is sure to redefine your standards for exceptional Thai cuisine.

Title: Hidden Gem Discovered!

During a day of local exploration, we stumbled upon a true gem of a restaurant thanks to its shining Yelp reputation. Admittedly, first impressions were dubious due to its lackluster facade, but stepping inside, we were swiftly enveloped by the warmth of the staff's friendliness and impeccable service.

The highlight of our visit was undeniably Mama's Curry Chicken - a dish that must not be overlooked. It was a culinary delight, bursting with flavors that had us savoring every bite. Equally noteworthy was the Garlic Shrimp, another tasty choice that complemented our meal.

In conclusion, don't judge this book by its cover, as inside awaits a feast for the senses served with the utmost care.

Right around the corner when you get off the transit. Always a long line here so we waited to be seated to see what was the hype all about. It took about 30 minutes to get a seat and it was an interesting setup. While in line, you fill out a paper to customize your ramen. Once you get seated, you basically just give the paper to your waiter. It's like one of those solo booths where there's a wall to separate each person. Our ramen came in this cute rectangular box, sorta like a bento box without all the sections. I had gotten an egg as well and it came with instructions. The box that the ramen came in had seem big but it's not deep as you think. The portion was a bit small for the price you pay. The broth was a bit on the sweeter side so it was okay. Overall, i'm not sure if this is the best ramen around the area as it may had claim. Would I come back? Maybe only because it opens late at night and if i was coming back from a night of drinking then yes. Otherwise, there's too many options in the city to consider coming back to this one.

I gave this place three stars because the food was good, but so pricey for one lobster roll. I believe I paid 17$ for one lobster roll. With that price, I couldn't imagine eating three with that price. Lol I like that they serve beer.

Title: Hit-and-Miss at the New GFG FiDi Location

I ventured to the new GFG outpost in FiDi with high hopes for Mediterranean delights but was met with a rollercoaster of experiences. Amidst the anticipation, the inconsistency started with multiple cancelled orders through Ritual, which left me bewildered and frustrated. Was it a fluke or a pattern? Eventually, I managed to taste their Turkey Bagel Sandwich and Greek Yogurt Parfait on separate visits.

The pickup encounters were chaotic; the staff seemed overwhelmed and struggled with inventory management – running low on toppings by mid-morning is a red flag. The yogurt lacked its full complement of garnish, and while the bagel sandwich was decent, it did not elevate beyond what you'd find at a standard deli, despite the Mediterranean twist.

Comparatively, GFG's Broadway location shines with better organization and stock levels, making me question why the FiDi spot is faltering. It’s disheartening to think they might resort to serving leftovers due to these issues. GFG FiDi needs to sync their act to match the expectations set by their other locations and the delicious potential their menu promises.

Reservations are very hard to come by but finally managed to snag one for a Wednesday night at 9:30pm. It was delicious! Love that all the plates were made by Korean artists and loved the attention to detail with every dish. Excellent service and delicious food.

Title: A Slice of NYC Heaven Near Times Square

If you're roaming the streets of NYC and craving an authentic slice of pizza to cap off a chilly day of urban exploration, this bustling corner spot near Times Square is a must-visit. The hype is real, given its top-notch reviews, and it surely doesn't disappoint. Brace yourself for a snug space teeming with fellow tourists, but rest assured the line zips along. The reward? A mouthwatering slice of classic New York-style pizza, served piping hot and perfect for a cozy hotel room unwind. Be ready to order fast, grab your 'za, and savor every bite of the city's iconic flavor.

Title: The Dip in NYC Outshines Philly's Best

Move over, Philly cheesesteak; The Dip in New York has redefined the beef and cheese sandwich experience. Nestled on St. Mark's Place, The Dip is the new culinary hotspot for sandwich aficionados. Their French Dip Sandwich isn't just a meal; it's a masterpiece. Picture thinly shaved beef paired with melted gruyere, zesty cherry peppers, all nestled between slices of perfectly crisp garlic bread. Every bite is a harmonious blend of flavors, elevated by the dipping delight of au jus and a punch of horseradish served on the side. This isn't your ordinary sandwich; it's a revelation. And while the French Dip stands out, the rest of the menu holds its own with an array of exceptional choices. So, unless you're in Philly to see the Liberty Bell, The Dip is where you'll want to be for the best beef and cheese sandwich in America.

Having been to the one in Chelsea Market, I was very excited to try out this place and they did not disappoint! I arrived to meet my boyfriend before a show (hey, I love tacos) around 630pm and there was already a line out the door. It was cold (which goes to show the lengths I will go to for amazing meat sandwiched between corn tortilla), but thankfully the line darted forward with surprising litheness. We decided to each try one of each type of meat taco -- the adobada (spelling?), the carne, and the pollo with every garnishment offered and a heathy splash of the spicy salsa.They were all phenomenal!! My favorite was the adobada (pork), the pork melted in my mouth, was sensationally seasoned, and had the accompanying pickled jicama or pineapple, not really sure which one but it was bright yellow and delicious. I could not get these babies in my mouth fast enough and bae felt the same way. The steak and chicken tacos were also magnificent and super filling.Would 10/10 recommend the pork and the steak followed with a close second by the chicken.Only complaint (which really isn't that much of a complaint) is that there is nowhere to sit and there is standing room only -- which makes sense given how popular this place is.It's also supremely affordable -- 6 tacos put us back about 20-25 bucks. Totally worth it, definitely go. The photo is of me barely containing my excitement.

I recently dined at a popular taco spot and found the service to be commendably efficient, even with a queue to contend with. However, the tacos, while enjoyable, didn't live up to the considerable hype surrounding the establishment. In my experience, there are other venues offering superior tacos at more attractive prices.

I consistently enjoy visiting this cozy eatery tucked between a liquor store and another Thai spot. The service shines with friendliness, and the vibe remains casually low-key—not quite the setting for a romantic date, but perfect for a relaxed meal. The menu offers a delightful mix of Vietnamese and Thai cuisine, catering to cravings for anything from savory pho to rich Thai curry.

My multiple trips here have introduced me to a tasty array of dishes, including the pork chop with rice, the flavor-packed shrimp and pork vermicelli, the satisfying mock duck basil, and refreshing summer rolls. Each dish has reliably hit the mark, holding its own against other local Vietnamese restaurants while keeping prices reasonable.

An added perk for diners: it's BYOB, so you can pair your favorite drink with your meal without any corkage fuss.

This is a new, but very different location of Izakaya, the also very good Japanese restaurant on 6th Street.There are similar menu items, but it's a bit more upscale here with nicer plating and a cooler atmosphere. The food is all excellent, especially the Tuna Tartar ($21) and the Fish In The Wine ($36). Try the Saba Mackerel Spring Rolls ($10) too for one of the smaller dishes.The menu is large with tons of stuff to try, so it's definitely worth multiple trips out to Alphabet City for one of the most interesting menus right now.

Excellent squares!  The crust was crispy all around! If you get the one with pepperoni on top, it reminds me of Prince Street. Unlike prince street, this was crispy consistently. The crust was light and airy with many little air pockets so it was like a wafer instead of like a hard cracker. The sauce also had so much flavor. It wasnt just bland tomatoes. Theres a spiced kick to it.  I also ordered their signature burger.  The burger was monstrous too! Just massive of amounts of juicy cheesy meat topped with a pretzel roll.

I went there during restaurant week and I was impressed with the service and the food. Food:For starters, I had an oven-roasted beetroot salad. It is a cold salad and a sweet one. It had a nice balance from the vegetables to the vinaigrette. Sweet in flavors since the beets were roasted. For the main entree, I order the flat iron steak as medium rare and it was cooked to perfection. It was served with bacon cheddar mash potatoes and Kentucky bourbon veal demi-glace. The demi-glace was delicious and went well with the steak. The mash potatoes were on a little salty end for my tasting but overall the meal was delicious. The steak was roughly 8 oz which was plenty. For the dessert, I had a panna cotta that was nice and light. It had a blueberry compote to it that was just the right amount to the panna cotta and a ginger snap cookie. It was like a light cheesecake in my view, sweet and airy. ServiceOur server and everyone there was amazing. Very attentive to detail and we never had our water run dry. My friend and I were coming from another restaurant that couldn't serve our needs and come to a place that viewed us as a valuable customer it was a delight. We did come on a slow day and time.OverallEverything was just to perfection. I would come back, especially for their steaks. Some of the sides were salty for my liking but I usually don't like a lot of salt in my food in general, so this is a personal preference. The steak was cook to perfection and amazing service especially for a busy area in NYC.

Came here with coworkers late on a Thursday night- was surprised to see it was pretty packed at that time. We opted for bar seating and ordered from there.We ordered the crudo tasting to share, and I had the spaghetti alla chitarra.The crudo tasting was awesome, it was well priced and there was a little of everything to sample. In ours, we had the hamasa, fluke, salmon tartare and surf clam. The hamasa had a perfect firm texture with a nice balance of flavor from the chili. The fluke was very light, the delicate flavor contrasted well against the coconut flakes. The salmon tartare was well cut, and quite firm in a good way. There was a nice balance from the citrus and saltiness/crunch from the pork rinds. Super fresh. Finally the surf clam was very different- not too chewy and good heat from the chili. We split the summer lettuces salad, the dressing was light and fresh and I appreciated the array of baby gems. For my meal, the spaghetti was definitely fresh and well made. The pasta was good but the lemon balm/saffron combo may have been a bit overpowering for me. Would go for a different pasta dish next time.

This restaurant has been on my list for awhile now, and I'm so glad I finally got to check it out. Great location and ambience, friendly service, beautiful decor--it feels like dining the living room of an old beautiful mansion. The Spaghetti Chitara alla Carbonara is every bit as delicious as all the hype on Instagram. The presentation of the plate is gorgeous, mixing in the egg is satisfying; I cherished every bite and then wished there was more (portions are on the smaller side). I love my pasta a bit al dente so this was perfect to me. On the pricier side for pasta, but perfect for a night out. Can't wait to go back!

Title: Great Flavors, Service Could Improve

I recently dined at this spacious spot known for its mouth-watering offerings. While the shrimp mofongo and picadera appetizer were truly scrumptious and perfectly portioned for my cousin and me, the service fell short of expectations. After a lengthy 10-minute wait before even placing our order, we found ourselves in the less-than-desirable back corner of the restaurant, needing to vie for our pleasant but preoccupied waitress's attention to avoid further delays.

Even on a bustling Saturday evening, the oversight of new diners being promptly served before us was noticeable. The potential of this establishment is undeniable, with its delectable cuisine and ample room for guests. However, a more streamlined training for the staff to ensure attentiveness is necessary.

A final note for prospective visitors: parking is quite challenging, so for those local, opting for a ride-sharing service like Uber might save you some pre-dinner stress.

I was trying to go for a healthy brunch option at bluebird and I'm pescatarian, and didn't love the options available. I got the omelette but the texture was very smooth, like a crepe consistency almost. The fries were great though. The staff were all very friendly, but service did seem to be a little slow. The place is super cute. I would like to go back and give it another shot, maybe when I'm not trying to eat healthy or for a different meal.

Title: A Gastronomic Delight with a Price to Match

I recently dined at a restaurant that truly impressed me with its culinary offerings, despite the hefty price tag. The standout dish for me was the scallop gnocchi, a delectable masterpiece I devoured in record time—it was so sublime, I would undoubtedly splurge on it again.

While my mojito cocktail left something to be desired and I wouldn't order it a second time, the sushi and shrimp sampled from my girlfriend's plate were impressive, further showcasing the kitchen's prowess.

We capped off our meal with a classic brownie, which was both tasty and amply sized for sharing among three. Overall, the experience was enjoyable enough to warrant a return visit. A word of advice: reservations are essential here unless you're willing to endure the wait.

I read on Food Network's Diners, Drive -Ins and Dives that this was the BEST place to get a New York pizza. We ordered what Guy Fieri had, the sausage and pistachio pizza. For starters we did the arancini di riso (fried rice balls) WOW so hot and crunch with a gooey-cheese center. Spiced to perfection and so flavorful.The lemon salad was made with my favorite lettuce, arugula so there was a bitterness top with pungent Parmesan cheese a perfectly musty Bresaola, an Italian deli meat. Topped with a balsamic vinaigrette. Loved it!Well it's not the best pizza I've ever had but it was definitely different and tasty. The pistachio was ground and made into a pesto then spread on the pizza. The sausage lacked that Italian fennel flavor that I adore. The crust is a medium thickness with a terrific rustic crunch and chewiness provided by the wood burning oven.Okay sorry Don Antonio's but the margarita was the worst I've ever had. It was white in color, liked the citrus flavor commonly enjoyed in this drink and it lacked that sweet-saltiness that I was looking forward to. I'll take the blame, who orders a mexican style drink at an authentic Italian pizzeria?Definitely try this place!

Title: Mixed Feelings on Oriental Delights

I recently decided to try out the local fare at an eatery renowned for its Asian cuisine, and my experience was a rollercoaster of sorts. On the menu for the evening were shumai and General Tso's crispy tofu, ordered via Seamless for delivery.

The shumai earned a solid 'average' rating, with a taste that did not differ from what you'd find at any other establishment serving similar dishes. Moving on to the General Tso's crispy tofu, I encountered my first hiccup: it failed to live up to its spicy promise, leaning more towards a sweet chili sauce vibe that, while potentially a hit with the kids, left my palate yearning for the fiery kick I was anticipating. Additionally, the dish would have greatly benefited from a more generous helping of vegetables to accompany the tofu.

On a positive note, the service was commendable. The delivery was prompt, arriving in 45 minutes as promised, and while the food was merely warm upon arrival, it was evident that care had been taken in the packing process - the General Tso's sauce was neatly separated, preventing any sogginess.

Overall, I'd give the food a 2.5 out of 5, with room for improvement in flavor authenticity and spice execution. The service, however, was efficient and attentive, deserving a 4 out of 5. With a few tweaks to the recipes, this restaurant could certainly elevate its offerings to match the quality of its service.

Based on a glowing recommendation, I visited this pizzeria and it absolutely lived up to the hype. I sampled two large pizzas: a hearty sausage & mushroom and a classic margherita. Both were impeccable, with the sausage & mushroom being notably non-greasy—a rare find in the pizza world. The NY style pizza here is authentic and flavorful, served up at lightning speed, and the slices are more than generous. Situated in a fantastic location, this eatery is a must-visit for pizza aficionados. However, the limited seating and tables that could benefit from a bit more attention might deter some. Additionally, those watching their wallets might find the prices a bit steep. Despite these minor drawbacks, the quality of the food earns this place a well-deserved 5 stars.

Tucked away in the lower east side, "An Choi" is a culinary gem not to be missed. Despite its modest size and bustling atmosphere, especially on weekends when wait times can stretch, the restaurant's food is nothing short of exceptional. The Pho, a hearty and savory delight, is a must-try, especially on chilly days, offering great value and taste that will leave diners satisfied.

For starters, the taro fries and Sriracha wings set the stage for a flavorful journey. Follow up with the shaking beef entree, which boasts generous portions of succulent steak accompanied by white rice and a fresh arugula salad, for a well-rounded meal that justifies the reasonable price point of $15-$20.

While service is consistently commendable, it's worth noting that to-go orders may not receive the same generous portion sizes as dine-in. It's also advisable to skip seating near the back to avoid the heat from the kitchen. Despite these minor considerations, "An Choi" is certainly worth a visit for anyone in the area craving authentic and gratifying Vietnamese cuisine.

I was preparing to give a five star review since the opening of this establishment who had gotten so much publicity however, rather an disappointment to me (and my wife) I gave only 2 star, purely because our server was kind and attentive!First Courses: StriFried Duck Treasure, it was totally tasted like dry woods.  Scored in F-Squid Ink Soup: the soup was okay, but nothing to write home about. Scored in BMains:Kong Pao Chicken, If this place wants to invent a dish, this is it! Scored in CSteamed Skate Wings, was the only winner from the whole set Scored in AHere comes the deep fried red snapper in pine nut source, it was totally a disaster, the soul of this dish is supposed to be the source but I had found any in there. Scored in total FFor such an fancy and pricy place, the style has totally over ride the food. Take any of these dish to Chinatown, they can be beaten with much tastier and few times cheaper at the price!The updateThank you for the management reply. I am not sure if you are aware of the New York Times review? No I am not going to join you again, period.

A very unique dining experience. Ichiran only serves tonkatsu ramen, which is their freshly made ramen in a rich, pork bone broth. The noodles are made fresh everyday and the chef adjusts the recipe to account for humidity and other factors. I ordered the signature ramen, which included charsiu, soft boiled egg, mushrooms and seaweed. The ordering form allows you to customize to your taste: specify the richness of the broth, chewiness of noodles, and the amount of garlic, scallions and chili paste. It's a bit pricey at $24 but well worth it.The most unique part of the restaurant is the seating system. You are seated at individual booths and the waiter delivers your food at your cubicle from the screened-in kitchen. The booths create a personal experience so you can dine and focus solely on the delicious ramen!!

AMAZING HOLE IN THE WALL. Also love that they have a variety of everything. If you check in on Facebook, they give you a free iced Thai tea. And then second visit, you'll get a free appetizer offer. I'm a vegetarian so I got the fried mantou- I always preferred dessert first. This is basically mini donuts/bread with sweet condensed milk. So good!Then I got the roti cheese. If you're West Indian/Caribbean, you'll most likely know what this is. Essentially a quesadilla. Also delicious. Served with an amazing coconut curry sweet sauce. My entree was Thai pineapple fried rice. Service was great and everyone was friendly. definitely check this place out if you're in the mood for some good Asian food.

I recently had my first taste of poké at this delightful lunch spot, and it was an absolute treat. The restaurant boasts a relaxed atmosphere, perfect for unwinding while savoring your meal. What struck me most were the fresh ingredients that packed each bite with bold, intense flavors. Although the serving size was a tad modest, the quality and taste more than made up for it. This place is a must-visit for anyone looking to indulge in a truly satisfying poké experience.

Yuzu is an small, but inviting restaurant with a neighborhood vibe in Harlem. It seems like a place that is frequented by folks who live in the neighborhood. I visited Yuzu on an early Friday evening, and the place was not crowded. The staff was very friendly and helpful, but my waitress seemed a bit distracted with another table. I think the folks at the other table were regulars, and the waitress was familiar with them. Unfortunately, I will say that the food prices are above average for what you get. I take that back. The appetizers were reasonably priced, but the main dishes seemed to be a bit overpriced. Perhaps, Yuzu uses better/higher quality fish compared to other Japanese restaurants in the area. Honestly, I was not wowed with my selections to justify the price. Don't me wrong, the food was good but it was not that good for the price (especially in Harlem). I will say that I was very pleased with my black sesame seed ice cream.

Came here on a Saturday night, the dining room was busy and the bar looked almost full. Tried a few different wines but decided on a Cabernet. Started with shrimp cocktail and then the short rib, which they are known for. Short rib was very good and came with a carrot purée. For dessert I had my favorite- profiteroles with vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce. Food was great. Service was slower, but we were not in a rush.

I recently visited this restaurant for a dimsum lunch and found the experience somewhat underwhelming. Despite the off-peak hour, there was a diverse crowd in attendance. Service was a highlight, with attentive waiters contributing positively to the visit. However, the dimsum itself fell short of expectations, primarily due to the limited variety. While what was offered was fresh and well-prepared, the selection was repetitive and failed to capture my interest—it seemed as though you might have to wait a while for new items to appear. In the end, the prospect of a new dish rolling out was too little too late, prompting us to depart. For dimsum enthusiasts looking for a wide range of options, this might not be the spot.

Nice change from the standard chicken over rice. They have biryani, samosas, and roti rolls. There are $6 lunch specials which seem like a great deal, but I don't work in the area. I had the chicken biryani ($6) which was pretty good and flavorful. It comes with some salad and half an egg. I would skip the white sauce. It's too thick.

Was looking for a new place to eat and family friendly for a get together with friends. Very nice family owned restaurant and great find - service and food were great! Prices are reasonable and location fairly easy to get to in Chelsea.  they have a small bar area in front and a brick oven pizza in the back. Love the decor which made you feel like you're in Italy - from the Pelligrino and the wine bottles. Complimentary baked bread was delicious! Appetizers: Fried Calamari and Caprese (mozzarella & tomatoes)Entrees: Cheese pizza, linguini with clams, pappardelle with mushrooms, chicken marsala Food was delicious and filling. Too stuffed for dessert. will have to remember to leave room for dessert next time.

Title: A Cozy Nook for Fresh Eats in Soho – Westbourne Review

My quest for a healthy dining option recently led me to Westbourne, a stylish yet unpretentious spot nestled in the heart of Soho. Known more for its brunch offerings, my evening visit was a refreshing experience where I savored the 'Over the Rainbowl'—a wholesome blend of falafel, rice, and assorted vegetables. Each component stood out with its freshness, united by a delightful sauce that added just the right touch of flavor.

The ambiance of Westbourne struck a chord with its all-day cafe charm, transitioning seamlessly from a welcoming space for daytime laptop warriors to a dimly-lit evening retreat. The crowd, a mix of solo diners and duos deep in conversation, contributed to a mellow and understated vibe, although I've been tipped that daytime sees a livelier scene.

The fully vegetarian menu, brimming with vegan choices and a caution for the nut-sensitive, does come at a premium—my meal totaled around $18. The place operates on a counter-service model, which was efficient and friendly.

Overall, while Westbourne may not scream 'dining destination,' it's a versatile gem perfect for multiple occasions. I look forward to my next visit, perhaps with a glass of wine in hand to toast to this welcome addition to Soho.

My friend and I came here for lunch on a Sunday and I was blown away by the ambiance of the restaurant, quality of the food, and attentive staffs that overall left an excellent impression on me. For our order, we chose their Yin Yang Pot where we can choose two soup broth from the menu. So we got the Sichuan spicy beef tallow broth with mild spicy level as well as Pork bone broth. The Sichuan spicy broth was so flavorful and aromatic while the Pork bone broth was also very smooth and full of flavors from all the ingredients that went in the soup.Then we got the sesame oil for the dipping sauce, which came in the cutest bottle I've ever seen! You open it and pour in your dipping sauce bowl along with other ingredients like green onion, oyster sauce, cilantro, and garlic that are served altogether. I've never had hotpot with sesame oil like this, but it was perfect to eat with beef I cooked in Sichuan spicy broth because it sort of cooled down the spiciness while making each bite more flavorful. Then we chose the Tang Deluxe combo platter ($80) for two, which was a good mix of beef, seafood, and veggies. The assorted meat, such as Kobe rib eye, Pork shoulder, and Angus beef short rib, was sooo tender and delicious. The seafood and veggies were also fresh and high quality that really felt like the price of the combo platter was worth it. We also got the Deep fried pork belly on the side and it was so delicious with the chili powder that came on the side. Moreover, my friend and I shared two cocktails -- Lychee rose and Pineapple mimosa -- and they were soo yummy and I could barely taste the alcohol while it did get me a bit buzzed. Don't forget to check in on Yelp for a free ice cream, because the flavors are amazing and they get it from the Chinatown Ice Cream Factory which is one of my favorite ice cream spots in the city. We got sesame and taro ice cream, and they were both very rich in flavor. Additionally, I was MESMERIZED by the aesthetic interior and elegant ambiance of the restaurant. Perfect for a special occasion, dining experience with a great atmosphere, or even a weekend brunch since they have a $45 bottomless brunch menu. I think this is an amazing alternative to a typical bottomless brunch for a different type of cuisine. Staffs were also very welcoming, attentive, and friendly. The waiter at our table even came to switch our small plates to new ones as we were mid-way through our hotpot! This spot definitely stands out from many hotpot places in the city. Although it's slightly pricier than other hotpot restaurants, I think the quality of the food and the dining experience certainly make the price point worth it and I would definitely bring anyone here who loves hotpot!

Title: A Saturday Brunch to Remember at Jane's

My experience at Jane's on a gorgeous Saturday afternoon was delightful from start to finish. Having made a reservation for our party of five, we were seated promptly upon arrival. The service was commendable—our server was amiable and attentive, ensuring our glasses were never empty.

While my companions opted for salads and Benedicts, I indulged in the much-acclaimed Vanilla Bean French Toast. This choice did not disappoint. It had been ages since my last French toast adventure, but Jane's rendition might just top the list. The bread was exceptionally fluffy with a satisfying crunch, and the flavors were a harmonious blend that took me to a culinary nirvana.

Observing my fellow diners, satisfaction seemed to be a common theme at our table. This level of contentment is clearly reflected in the restaurant's well-deserved reputation, backed up by a plethora of highly positive reviews.

The ambiance struck a perfect balance between elegance and relaxed summer vibes, adding to the overall excellent brunch experience. Jane's definitely lives up to its high ratings, especially with their French Toast. A visit here is highly recommended for anyone looking to elevate their weekend brunch game.

I had this place bookmarked because I saw an Insider video on FB promoting this neat spot with delicious steaks that made you stand (no seats) so I guess I was just a teensy weensy disappointed to come in here and see chairs!  Well, maybe not, I was actually pretty tired from fooding around New York and definitely appreciated being able to sit down for a bit.  My mister had been wanting steak and quite honestly we're just not the types to really appreciate what makes some $50+ while places like this can serve something super delicious for half that. So basically, it was good. We enjoyed the yelper recommended garlic fried rice and a nice huge slice of ribeye.  Can't wait to come back!

Came last night with friends to kill time before dinner & just some casual drinks, it was a amazing accidental choice! I ordered the Balckwell's Cosmo & my friends had the pear martini. The Blackwell's Cosmo tasted delicious, could compare it to a lemonade. The bartender was such a kind man, taking care of us & checking in often. It was a little quiet last night, but my friends & I did not mind that fact, we enjoyed it, with how noisy NY can be. Definitely coming back here over the summer, to try more drinks and the food here. Strongly recommend visiting Blackwell's if you haven't already.

While I am fully in love with the concept of The Nugget Spot, the execution left a little to be desired.  I came in on a Friday afternoon and it wasn't too busy.  After looking over the menu and looking at the pictures on Yelp, I decided on getting six Buffalo nuggets with the "O.G. Ranch" and six of the "Cap'n Crunk" (Cap'n Crunch Cereal dusted) nuggets with "Crunk Sauce" (caramel) with a side of Nacho Mac & Cheese. I was absolutely in love with buffalo nuggets, and the nacho mac & cheese was nice and cheesy with a nice crunch on top from the tortilla chips; however, The Cap'n Crunk nuggets just weren't tickling my fancy. I totally understand the salty and sweet flavor profile they were going for, but the Cap'n Crunch in the breading made the nuggets way too crunchy and the caramel sauce was overpoweringly sweet. I ultimately ended up peeling off the breading and grabbing some more buffalo sauce on the side to dip them in. I really wanted to like the Cap'n Crunk nuggets but I just wasn't feeling it. Another criticism I have is that the dining area wasn't the cleanest for it be so small. I ended up pulling some napkins and water out of my backpack to wipe down the table, but my suggestion would be for this place to hire someone to make sure the dining area is as clean as possible at all times for customers that want to dine in. The trash can also being placed by where some of the seating is also awkward, but I was able to sit away from it, so it was all good. All in all, I can see my self eating here again, but I know to lean towards ordering a more traditional flavor of nuggets and to getting my food to go.

Title: A Slice of Italian Heaven in New York

If you're seeking an Italian culinary adventure in New York, look no further. My recent visit provided an exceptional dining experience from start to finish. The service was prompt, with the added charm of being greeted by a quintessentially Italian host – it almost felt like stepping into a classic film!

The cuisine is where the restaurant truly shines. Every bite of their pasta exuded freshness, and the sauce was divine – a recipe that would undoubtedly impress even the most discerning Italian grandmothers. The recommended wine pairings were spot on, enhancing the flavors of our pasta dishes beautifully.

We started with a shared salad, which could only be described as the pinnacle of freshness, setting a high bar for the entrees that followed. The ambience struck the perfect balance between romantic and stylish, with dim lighting and tasteful kitchen-themed decor that added to the overall allure.

The seating arrangement encourages conviviality, with family-style tables that might have you dining alongside other guests – an aspect I found quite enjoyable.

When it comes to pricing, expect to pay a premium. Yet, considering the top-notch food, ambience, and service, I found the experience to be worth every penny. A truly superb choice for anyone craving authentic Italian cuisine in the heart of New York.

Like it! Love it! Want some more of it! - Staff are extremely kind, helpful, accommodating and friendly! Kosher - Thank G-d! Hopefully - these guys will be around for many more years to come! Delicious!

If not being dragged by a friend, I probably would never notice and try this gem. This spot is hidden inside of a Pizzeria and who would think of go to a pizza place for Iranian food?I barely have any knowledge about Persian food, nor the geopolitics of the region. But after eating this delicious meal, my mind started spinning. Why does Iranian food look and taste so different from the food of other countries around? Why does Iranian food remind me Indian food among Asian cuisines?  The whole culture and country are so interesting and I want to travel there one day, simply because the food is so delicious! Here is my lunch box with both Kabab and shrimp with vege. Everything on my plate tastes great and so favorable.

Great views, nice atmosphere but that's about it. Looking down from the restaurant, you get a great view of the vessel.The front staff were very friendly but the service of the actual food was horrible. We ordered oysters which they pour liquid nitrogen table side but the guy that brought over the food, it felt like I was at Denny's. He comes over and tells us to move out of the way and dumps the liquid nitrogen and walks off. I was astounded.I ordered the dumplings which they pour broth on and no explanations just pours the broth and leaves. I definitely won't be coming back here.

Title: A Peruvian Feast in the Heart of NYC

During a recent hotel stay on the Upper East Side, I opted for takeout from a Peruvian spot that caught my eye. In a city brimming with culinary options, I craved the distinct flavors of marinated rotisserie chicken, jalea, ceviche, and classic rice 'n beans. The place? Pio Pio 3.

Pio Pio 3 serves up authentic Peruvian cuisine, with a standout rotisserie chicken that you can order by the quarter, half, or whole. They offer flexibility with meat selection and a cost-saving "chef's choice" option. The half-chicken I ordered, all dark meat, was succulent and expertly seasoned. It arrived with perfectly paired rice 'n beans and a side of yuca with an irresistible garlic sauce. The accompanying aji verde sauce was the crown jewel, elevating the dish with its vibrant, tangy kick.

Prices buck the city's expensive trend, giving Pio Pio 3 an edge for the budget-conscious foodie. You can snag a whole chicken for just $10 or opt for complete meals to serve more. Beyond poultry, their menu boasts a variety of appetizers, mains, kid's meals, and tempting tropical juices, Peruvian sodas, sangria, and desserts.

My takeout experience was seamless, punctuated by timely delivery and the bonus of no delivery fees – though a tip is always a kind gesture for good service. If Peruvian food is calling your name, Pio Pio 3 is a must-try. Your tastebuds will thank you.

Title: A Flavorful Introduction to Ethiopian Cuisine at Massawa

My culinary adventure at Massawa marked my first foray into Ethiopian cuisine, an experience that came highly recommended by friends. The restaurant exudes a warm charm during dinner time, thanks to the inviting glow of candles against the backdrop of elegant dark wood decor.

Opting to stay budget-conscious, my companion and I decided on the beef sambusas and shrimp tebsi, both of which promised a taste of Ethiopia's rich flavors. However, even on a quiet weeknight, we were left to wait for over 30 minutes after our water was served before the appetizer graced our table.

When the food did arrive, it was accompanied by injera, a uniquely spongy sourdough flatbread that was a delightful discovery. Its slightly tangy taste complemented the bold spices of the lentils, tomatoes, and shrimp, creating a symphony of flavors in each bite.

While the service staff was amiable and exuded warmth, the overall attentiveness left something to be desired. It's my hope that future visits will see a quicker turnaround from the kitchen and more frequent check-ins from the servers.

In conclusion, Massawa offered a beautiful atmosphere and a tantalizing introduction to Ethiopian dishes, which were as flavorful as they were unique. Despite the slower service, the culinary experience was memorable and one that I would be willing to return for, hoping for a swifter dining experience.

As a food enthusiast, it's a pleasure to share my thoughts on one of my favorite Indian dining spots in New York City. Having visited its counterpart in New Delhi, I can attest that Chef Manish Mehrotra's progressive Indian menu at this NYC restaurant doesn't miss a beat. It's a culinary gem perfect for a special occasion dinner. The impeccable service complements the outstanding food, creating an experience that's both memorable and gratifying. Kudos, @traveleen_gurl, for echoing the high standards of this fabulous eatery.

I was first introduced to Mike's over five years ago after a date at the comedy club across the street. Little did I know I'd a) move to this 'hood and b) this would become one of my go to spots. Sentimental details aside, Mike's makes a really good, cheap pie.It's rare I stray from a medium pie with a topping which will set you back 16 bucks. The pie itself is simple and straightforward with a really excellent crust. I'm one of those weirdos who usually ends up with a crust graveyard on my plate, but Mike's is actually worth eating. It's got a nice crunch and chewiness to it. Some other menu standouts are the garlic knots, minestrone soup, and mozzarella sticks. I was honestly so surprised by how good the minestrone was. It's 4 bucks for a standard side soup serving, but it's filled to the brim with fresh veggies, garlic, and penne. It's perfect if you're not feeling so hot. Although I've tried their calzones and pastas they weren't worth ordering again. Kinda bland and unmemorable to be totally honest.Mike's has been a neighborhood staple for so long the phone number on their box doesn't even have an area code. As long as they're still around it'll be my go to for no frills slices.

Came to Gonzalez y Gonzalez for a quick bite. I ended up getting guacamole and chips, the guacamole could've been better... it was also very little amount. The chips were good. I also had a margarita which I cant complain about, it was nice and strong enough, not a watered down drink. This is a lively restaurant that turns into a full blown party at night, Super fun!

Definitely worth a visit. If you can stomach heavier food earlier in the day, early brunch reservations (pre noon) on the weekend are generally not difficult to come by. When we came around 1030ish I believe on a Saturday, there was hardly anyone else there. The burger is of course a must try. We ordered it with bacon but the bacon is in pretty thick slices so I have to admit, we ultimately ate it separate from the burger. Tasty though - and sweet. The egg is perfectly runny and was the bomb with the burger. Random note- the one patty burger is actually two patties (though on thinner side- not like crazy thick)...and I think the 2 patty is either 3 or more...confusing I know. The coffee bar btw is pretty fun - some unique drinks they serve (both tea and coffee based lattes). Unfortunately they're sweetened, so probably won't get them again, but felt the latte art was pretty impressive. You can also get plain coffee which supposedly has free refills but they are way less attentive vs a diner and so you don't really get many refill opps over the course of your meal. In sum though - we liked it and would recommend! I also have to come back bc I was told the foie gras hash was better than the burger...which as I noted above is pretty good.

Agern is located at the Southwest corner of Grand Central station, unassuming wooden doorway at the top of a few stairs, menu out for display. Scandinavian forging food is what my dining partner said.A $40 pre-fixe lunch ($48 with dessert) was what I went to try with a friend, we were seated promptly and there was plenty of space. Bathroom was up a small narrow set of stairs. Bread was a delicious dark-colored sourdough with bread and a wooden knife to serve. Outside rather hard, but inside was great. We shared two (and one dessert). Beef tartare was cold and fresh, no sour or stale meat flavor. The black bass, squash, yogurt and seeds was also equally good (a mini poke). The main of pork shoulder was fantastic, a melt-in-your mouth goodness and definitely worth it. The mushrooms w/ chestnuts, whey, and dill was unexciting, and a combination of mushrooms that would've cost me less than $5 to make, I use all those mushrooms in my normal cooking - that was not worth the cost. This would've made a better appetizer value, as a main it was entirely disappointing.Dessert - we tried the blood orange, which was cool and refreshing with honey, buttermilk and vanilla. Delicious. Overall the "forager/hunter's" theme was throughout the meal though not in-your-face.Some good (the appetizers, pork shoulder, blood orange), and some disappointing (mushrooms).

Amazing lunch spot!I really like coming to Antico Noe for a quick to-go lunch. The lines aren't too long by 1 PM and go fast since all the sandwiches are pre-made. They have plenty of options and new specials all the time. I've never been to another dedicated panini shop, but these paninis are some of the best that I've ever had. The Caprese, which I usually get, is flavorful and the bread is toasted to perfection. The sandwiches are about the same price range $10 - $13 as lunch anywhere else in Midtown so I would say they're reasonably priced. I wish they had more vegetarian options on rotation since I'm not a huge fan of eggplant in general. They also offer punch cards for 8 visits = 1 free panini. The only downside is that they only give you a stamp per visit instead of per panini purchased.

A bit disappointed with my visit here at Melt Shop. Overall the food is decent and the Fried Chicken melt definitely was one of the better I've tasted and the Chocolate shake was absolutely amazing. However, I thought the portion was quite small especially for the tater tots.I ordered online through Chase pay and they got the food done within the quoted time, it was quite empty when I came in and it was very nice that the food was kept in a warmer to keep from getting cold. Honestly though if their sandwich was a bit bigger for the $9.49 price tag I would definitely be giving them another star or two. Other than the very thick chocolate shake definitely didn't feel like I gotten great value for my money.For what you get though the food is good although the vegan burger tasted pretty mediocre and maybe too much cheese. Definitely could have use more consistency with the food. Since they just opened not long ago I hope to see some improvements in the future and definitely would be happy to come back to give them another try.

Dining with Lori Mendorff Klugman, we were pleasantly surprised by our lunch experience. The Faro and Gem salads were impeccable, setting a delightful tone. Carrying on the momentum, the Carbonara shined; its perfectly al dente pasta, crisped to perfection pancetta, and subtle yet savory cheese, all crowned with a beautifully runny egg yolk, culminated in one of the finest renditions of this dish we've savored stateside.

While the cocktail and wine selections were limited, they were sufficient, blending well with the meal's flavors. However, the gnocchi fell short of our expectations and, regrettably, had to be returned.

Overall, the restaurant offers a commendable two-course lunch for $32, and we'd gladly return, giving the food an 8.5, service an 8, and value an 8.5 out of 10. This establishment comes recommended for anyone seeking a robust lunch special.

During our visit to the restaurant, we experienced a mishap with a hair in our noodle soup, which the staff promptly addressed by providing a new bowl. Unfortunately, the soup's flavor fell short of remarkable. The eel and egg rice was predominantly rice with a scant layer of egg and a few meager, bony eel chunks. The fried chicken, although satisfactory, did not live up to the flavor hype suggested by other reviews. In terms of the gyoza, the skin was of decent quality, yet the pork filling lacked depth of taste. Lastly, the pressed mackerel was agreeable but lacked that standout quality one might hope for. Overall, the dining experience was underwhelming, and with the plethora of options available in NYC, we do not plan a repeat visit.

Wow! I saw this place on Bobby Flay's "the flay list" show and I've been meaning to try if it for some time now but never actually had the time to travel from Jersey to here. I was in the city one night and I really wanted pizza so I scrolled through my yelp bookmarks and came across this restaurant. I ordered take out since my husband wanted to try some and it was raining. I ordered the Colony and the Tina to go. It took about 15-20 minutes for them to make it. As soon as they handed me the box I could immediately smell the aroma, it smelled so good that as I was walking back to the train in the rain I had to stop and take a bite of one. And omg it tasted just as good as it smelled and I had two slices one hot and one cold and they both were tasty. Once I hit home an hour later they were cold but it only took about 10 minutes to heat it up in the oven and it tasted fresh again. I will certainly be coming back here but maybe eat in next time.

I'm continually impressed with Vapiano during my visits to New York. The food is exceptional, flavorful, and satisfies every time. The customer service is top-notch, contributing to the overall dining experience. What I really appreciate is the ability to customize my order to my exact preferences, and the chefs prepare it right before my eyes with remarkable speed. It’s a must-visit spot for any food lover in the city.

The whole entire meal I just kept saying "wow this place is so beautiful." The decor was so well thought out and so beautiful. I came here for lunch with coworkers last week during the day and was surprised by what a great lunch deal they offered. For $15 you could get a soup/salad, app, and a main course. Considering cava and chipotle would cost you about the same, to get waited on in a relaxing environment for the same price is amazing. I got the steamed pork and shrimp dumplings, the massaman curry, and the salad. All was very good though if I go again I'll go for a noodle dish! We also split the sticky rice with custard and coconut ice cream for dessert because I LOVE sticky rice custard and it was as good as, or maybe better, than any I've ever had; certainly the best plated.

Title: A Cozy Spot That Packs a Punch - An Evening at Oiji

After hearing relentless praise from friends, I finally made it to the much-talked-about Oiji with a girlfriend, and the experience did not disappoint. First things first, book your reservations—this place is tiny but mighty.

Seated promptly on arrival, the service was commendable from the get-go. Oiji offers a concise menu, which I appreciate for its focus on quality. Trust me, four dishes, five max, and you'll be set.

Let's dive into the culinary journey:

1. Lobster (4.5/5): This is a must-try. The succulent lobster, paired with savory noodles, delivers a spicy kick that only leaves you wanting more.
   
2. Long Island Duckling (4.5/5): On par with the lobster, this dish delights with its generous portions and the ingenious addition of kimchi rice.

3. Baby Octopus (4.0/5): A personal favorite of mine, thanks to the heavenly combo of garlic and butter. However, it may not be everyone's cup of tea if you're sensitive to bold flavors.

4. Fried Chicken (3.5/5): While it's the talk of the town, this fried chicken didn't skyrocket in my books. It's good but lacks that special edge.

To wrap up, the Honey Butter Chips with vanilla ice cream was the cherry on top. This lone dessert item is their signature for a reason.

In a nutshell, Oiji is a keeper. I'm eagerly anticipating their menu's next rotation for another round of shared plate indulgence.

Honestly I was really between 3 stars and 4 stars, but their meats were good, and they also have games for you to sit and okay while eating.This is an order at the counter / bar then sit and wait for your food type of place. The flavor of their meats were very good. Tried the smoked duck, pastrami, brisket, bacon, half a dozen buffalo wings, Mac n cheese, and pickles. I would skip out on the Mac n cheese and pickles next times. Both items were just mediocre. It's a bbq place, so I guess your expectations for the sides shouldn't be so high. Loved the flavor of the duck!! Some pieces were tough to chew though. Pastrami was good, brisket I felt like it was a bit over cooked. Buffalo wings were quite spicy. Loved the bacon and the subtle maple flavor/ glaze on top of it. We got 1/4 pound of the brisket (2 slices), pastrami (2 slices), and duck (about 4 pieces), and the bacon was the smaller size. It was just enough food to fill two people up. Came out to around $60? I do think this place is worth trying, not sure if I'd go out of my way for it.If you walk in and there aren't seats available, it might be better to come back next time, from the looks of it, people come chill and have drinks for a while before leaving.

PROS:1. Two levels of seating with a bathroom in the back of the first floor. 2. Highly recommend the Joju banh mi, because the pork is flavorful and a fine  balance between savory and sweet. The bread is perfectly crunchy on the outside and really soft on the inside. (The kind of crunchy that doesn't hurt the roof of your mouth!) 3. Lemongrass chicken was okay but I think pork was better. Part of it is because I had some parts that were chewy from cartilage and skin, which I personally do not like   4. They have WiFi it seems, but I wasn't able to connect to it. So not sure if it's publicly accessible.

I've heard about Beyond Sushi from the west coast and I was excited to finally try it in NY. We got the Badge dumplings, spicy mango roll, and the pickle me roll. I loved everything we got and it was a great add on that the rolls each came with a sauce specific to it. The spicy mango roll came with a cayenne sauce and the pickle me had a carrot ginger, they both tied the flavors together. I think Beyond Sushi is a great fast casual vegan sushi spot for the price point and I can't wait til they expand to LA!

2 of us event there around 12:00pmIt was already about 70% fullThere were few option for lunch.Either 2 or 3 items lunch, or you can order single item separately for lunch price.We decide to order lunch Sakura course$39.95Which include the item below for starter:gyu kaku salad x2Miso soup x2White rice x2Japanese fried chicken For BBQ item we got :Bone in kalbi rib eye Yaki shabu beef misoToro beef tare sweet soy Spicy porkChicken breast basil And s'mores for dessert!All the meats were marinaded already,So no sauce needed. But if you like, there were ponzu, sweet soy or spicy sauce on the side for you.The meat quality was ok, with this price, I don't expect high quality of meats. All the marinaded meat were pretty salty, so you can't really taste anything but sauce. Not very juicy and tender either.

Title: A Sunday Feast to Remember at Coco

I recently savored a delightful Sunday dinner at Coco and it was an experience worth sharing. The burrata appetizer and Niçoise salad main course I indulged in were both incredibly tasty. My companion sang praises for his filet mignon, crisply seared on the outside with a succulently soft interior, seasoned to perfection.

Coco's ambiance strikes the perfect balance between romantic and trendy, providing an Instagram-worthy backdrop for our meal. The stellar service complemented the atmosphere; attentive without ever crossing into awkward territory.

The location adds to Coco's appeal, nestled conveniently near Chelsea Market and the Whitney. The cherry on top? A cool 20% discount thanks to a Yelp check-in. This gem has certainly earned a spot on my list for a return visit soon.

Wow, I am so happy I discovered this place. The service is quick and the atmosphere is nice. The menu has so many options- from sandwiches to pho to different teas and Vietnamese coffee. I ordered pho tai and Vietnamese coffee, the pho was so delicious. Everything was great about it, from the lime that is provided on the side, to the richness of the broth. I'm definitely gonna be back to try more on the menu. Such a great find in the neighborhood.

Title: Late-Night Indulgence at a Bustling NYC Spot

I popped into this spot late at night, itching for something indulgent, and I wasn't disappointed. The highlight was certainly the adult cookies and cream shake, spiked with a shot of Kahlua – a decadent treat that blurs the line between dessert and cocktail. Though the shake was teeming with extravagant toppings, the actual milkshake portion seemed to play second fiddle. It was scrumptious, no doubt, but the price tag became hefty after including the liquor.

The Carolina wings were our savory choice – they were satisfactory, with a tangy sauce that added a nice punch. As for the service, it was commendable, especially given our near-midnight cravings.

On previous strolls by the restaurant, it’s often packed, which speaks to their reputation for gourmet burgers. Final thoughts? It's a bit of a splurge, especially when you factor in the booze, but that's the price of culinary adventure in the Big Apple. My rating takes a hit primarily on value, yet the quality and service nearly justify the cost. 3.5/5 stars.

Nope, better pho around the neighborhood. The service is a messy. I saw the manager/owner yell at a staff in front of a customer, it seems like he was training him. The manager/owner proceed to be very rude to a customer. The table I sat at was like a sinking hole. The center of the table was sinking to a point where my pho was tilted one way (see the picture below). I had to scoop my soup to prevent any spillage from happening. The pho was decent which is why I didn't give it a one star. This place is also cash only. I rather go down the block to the other pho spots for cleaner, friendlier and tastier pho. There was definitely no Bang taste in this Pho.

Title: Mixed Bag at Uzebki Cuisine Spot

My experience at this restaurant was a rollercoaster of delicious highs and service lows. On the positive side, the food scored a strong 4 out of 5. For those who follow a halal diet, this place is a big plus. The standout dishes included the prime steak Umka, encased in a flaky puff pastry, and the Beef Faridas Special Shashlyk—both of which were nothing short of amazing. The Lagman soup had decent noodles, but it was just that—decent.

However, the service was a dire 1 out of 5. Despite the staff's friendly demeanor, the service was excruciatingly slow and haphazard, with our orders forgotten and dishes arriving at painfully long intervals. It felt like a classic case of poor management overshadowing the employees' niceness.

Ambience-wise, the setting earned a comfortable 4 out of 5—likely contributing a welcome distraction from the long waits. Seating was average, sitting at a 3 out of 5, adequate but not exceptional in comfort or design.

Unfortunately, the homemade honey cake ended my meal on a disappointing note. It was unexpectedly dense, which made me look for a dessert do-over elsewhere.

In summary, while the food has the potential to draw you in, brace yourself for service that might just test your patience.

4th time coming to this spot and still hits the spot! I forgot you weren't allowed to bring outside drinks in, so they took my bubble tea and put it in their fridge until afterwards to pick up when you leave. A little bummed about that but NBD. Asked for upstairs seating and got seated within 5 minutes. Waitress was very attentive, came by quite often to check on us. The manager Win was very presentable and personable. He chatted with us and even gave us a free appetizer! We got pork & shrimp bun vermicelli noodles entrees and crispy pork belly with Chinese vegetables, kimchi fries and spare ribs with honey tamarind glaze appetizers. The meat on the spare ribs just falls right off the bone, what a great texture! Definitely recommend if you haven't tried it already! Will be back (because 4 times just isn't enough)

Title: A Bachelorette Blast at NYC's Gem

I recently celebrated my bachelorette party at this NYC hotspot, and it was nothing short of fabulous. Our waitress, Chandelier, set the bar high with her outstanding service – attentive, engaging, and full of positive energy.

The entertainment was an absolute riot, keeping us all in high spirits with interactive and playful acts. The bachelorette package added a special touch, crowning me and bringing all the brides-to-be on stage, reminiscent of a birthday but with a bridal twist.

To my pleasant surprise, the food matched up to the high standard of entertainment. The steak entree came in a generous portion and was perfectly cooked. The three-course meal, which included a Caesar salad to start, a choice of entree, and a delightful duo of cannoli and cupcake for dessert, was a perfect fit for a Saturday night celebration.

Drinks weren't just drinks; they were a fun part of the experience with their whimsical theme names. Made for some great toasts! 

The ambiance was perfect for taking memorable photos, which we took full advantage of. 

For anyone looking for an unforgettable night out, especially for a celebration, this is the place to be. Five stars all around!

Visited this spot for their much-talked-about dumplings and wasn't disappointed with their texture—nicely crispy and served piping hot. However, I found myself missing the classic pork and chives variety, which wasn't on the menu. We tried the "reinvented original" dumplings, which, while satisfying, could benefit from a more robust flavor profile. The accompanying sauce was decent, although it lacked complexity. In summary, a good dining experience that has room for some improvement.

Decided to check this place out during a friends brunch event this past weekend and loved it! Super cute place centrally located in the Lower East Side. The inside decorated to play up the West Indian vibes with bright colors. The vibe was fun and everyone was enjoying brunch especially the endlessly flowing rum punch and "pearinis"! Brunch was super affordable, 35$ for unlimited mimosa, Bellini or pearini with your entree. I have to say the shrimp and grits where the best I've had in a restaurant! The grits were creamy and rich. Thick, not watery or soup like. There was a nice cream based sauce that married the shrimp to it as well. The waitresses were very accommodating and super cute! I has stepped out while waiting for my table and they texted me and waited for me to get back! Very nice of them!! Most places would give your table up. I will definitely be going back to check out their dinner menu.

One of the better and more authentic Ramen places I've been in NYC. Their appetizers and the buns are a must try. Soup broth are always flavorful but not too heavy. Service is very nice too!! A nice meal is always guaranteed here.

Title: Lukewarm Experience at Ivan Ramen

As a resident of LA's Little Tokyo with high standards for ramen, my expectations for Ivan were high, but sadly, not met. The service and atmosphere are passable—if you're lucky enough to snag a seat—and service is quick, which earns the first star.

Pricing is on par with what you'd expect these days, $14 for a ramen dish and $4.50 for a bao side. The meal won't break the bank, hence the second star.

However, the culinary experience was underwhelming. The Tokyo Shio ramen's broth wasn't sufficiently heated, and the taste was peculiar. Oddly green and slightly underdone noodles didn't help. The Pastrami Bun, which I had high hopes for, was a letdown compared to offerings from other establishments like Ippudo. This regrettable miss strips away the possibility of the third and fourth stars.

Would I return to Ivan with excitement? The answer is a resounding no. There's no novelty or culinary delight that would draw me back in, thus the fifth star remains unawarded. Ivan Ramen fails to make a mark in a city with an otherwise vibrant and satisfying ramen scene.

This may not be the most authentic of K-Town experiences, but you should've known that from the moment you saw the words "Korean gastropub." And that doesn't mean it isn't a good time. You've got to decide if you want:1. The more affordable, more banchan, more Korean experience.2. A meal that may cost a little more, but will deliver more attractive plates, more items that appeal to an American palate, and in my experience, far, far better service. If you want the former find a different spot, preferably a place that only exists on the second floor of a building around here. If the latter is your style, you're right where you need to be. Just know that if you have Korean friends they will be appalled at the prices, whereas they're pretty standard for a Manhattan dinner out. Don't be ashamed, either; both types of Korean meals have their place. This is an excellent introduction to Korean food for people that aren't as familiar, and even if you are familiar, Barn Joo has a lot of upside. Namely, the food is excellent and well-presented. I have eaten and enjoyed wings, pancakes, traditional Korean truffle fries, galbi, tacos, that mac and cheese-esque thing, bibimbap, japchae, and more. If I were you, I'd wash it all down with shots of soju and beer backs, but that's just because I'm not as into the soju cocktails.

My gf took me to this place while I was visiting NewYork. I had never been a sushi fan but this place completely changed it for me. I visit this place on every NewYork trip now, it's kind of a go-to stop for me and my gf. We've tried almost all types of sushi and spicy man is one of our favorites. I'd definitely recommend it. The dumplings are good too. I wish they had one in Silicon Valley.

The garlic knots were warm, soft and buttery. If you do not like to eat anything green (no parsley flakes) then this is a good option for you. The linguini Alfredo is a large portion (good for 2) but the mushrooms were sour, possibly canned mushrooms.

Title: A Slice Above the Rest in the Big Apple

If you're searching for a top-notch pizza experience in New York, add this spot to your culinary itinerary. As a self-proclaimed pizza aficionado, my New York trips are incomplete without indulging in the holy trinity of pastrami, pizza, and hot dogs, though not simultaneously.

This visit, after a day of pounding the pavement, I ventured into this bar/restaurant for an evening cap. Opting to dine solo at the bar, the full-service staff welcomed me with the genuine NYC charm I've come to relish. Service was prompt, pairing a perfectly chilled beer with what would soon be one of the best pizzas I've encountered in the city.

The pie itself was sublime. A flavorful crust laid the foundation for beautifully balanced sauce and toppings. Each bite reaffirmed my conviction that this establishment is an essential stop for any serious pizza lover. It’s an emphatic must-visit for anyone looking to savor the city's finest slices.

I wanted to like this place, but while I am head over heels in love with the decor [minus the fact they've located the bathroom in the middle of the restaurant], and our server was a cheerful individual with a ready quip or three, we were overall disappointed enough with the food options that we bailed to go eat elsewhere. Frankly? The menu is rather boring.The cocktails are not, I grant you, and we both had a pair before we scarpered, but the food offerings failed to raise any sort of interest from a one of us. Of the half dozen, I specifically remember liking the Sage Advice and the Harvest Collins, and all of us being a bit... I'm not sure I have the words. I ordered a Bleak Marg-Winter because it sounded interesting, but per the waitress' warning, the thing really does taste... Bleak. I don't know how the y managed to do that to what's basically a fancy grapefruit margarita, but it -was- and I am still baffled.So... maybe we were just in a mood? If the food looks good to you, the drinks are decent and the service is good, go enjoy the place properly.

I recently dined at a charming spot ideal for a dinner outing with friends. Venturing into vegetarian sushi for the first time, I was pleasantly surprised by the fare, with the establishment offering a successful and enjoyable experience. Despite the restaurant's specialty in sushi, the standout dish for me was the delightful mushroom dumplings – a must-try for future patrons.

However, the dining experience was marred by persistent flies that buzzed around, suggesting the need for a possible inspection. Additionally, the service lagged, not quite keeping pace with the brisk tempo expected in Manhattan.

While the food itself was commendable, the nuisances encountered ultimately overshadowed the positives. Given these drawbacks, I find myself hesitant to consider a return visit.

Ordered Pappardelle for lunch. It is delicious but also kind of heavy with the cheese and lamb meat as well as the blanket-like pasta!Since I ordered take-out, I would recommend a different container since when heated with hot food, this container tends to leak a lot and it is kind of messy.Overall, great food but would like to try something different next time.

I recently visited a restaurant that's perfectly suited for solo diners or small gatherings of two to four people. The highlight of my meal was the dipping noodles. I opted for both the miso and spicy miso flavors served cold, which turned out to be a delightful choice. The spicy miso, in particular, was a standout, offering a robust kick of heat, especially with the bonus of kimchi for an additional dollar. The concept of personally assembling the noodles by dipping into a bowl of aromatic broth and ingredients significantly enhanced the dining experience. Highly recommended for noodle enthusiasts looking for a customizable and delectable meal.

I was really excited to try this place given the rave reviews, but I have to say I was a bit disappointed with my experience.
