While the $4 sangria during happy hour was great, my entree fell short of my expectations. I ordered the seafood rice (arroz con mariscos) and the seafood was not fresh. The squid came in large chunks, which made it difficult to eat. Also, there was way too much red onion in the rice. The inside of the place is VERY small, which made dining a bit uncomfortable.

Ladies and Gents, Chef Ivan Orkin's world famous Shio Ramen, as seen on season 3 episode 4 of Chef's Table on Netflix. One taste and you'll immediately understand why Chef Orkin is regarded as one of if not the best ramen chefs in the world. His addition of roasted tomatoes into a ramen dish truly creates an umami bomb!

I recently ordered delivery from a local spot and had to share my experience. Opting for the large lamb doner without rice but on homemade Turkish bread, I was not disappointed. The delivery was punctual, and everything arrived piping hot. The bread itself was a lovely combination of soft and firm, though I missed having butter to spread on it. A slight oversight was the absence of utensils and napkins.

The lamb doner stole the show – it was an absolute treat! The meat was tender, the flavors were on point, and it came with a crisp, refreshing salad dotted with red onion, tomatoes, and a spicy hot pepper. At $20.50, the portion size provided great value for money and was satisfyingly filling.

Unfortunately, the Turkish coffee didn't live up to the rest. While it started off well, by the end, I was sipping more grounds than coffee. Not what you'd hope for, especially for $3.50. Next time, I'll be skipping the coffee but will definitely be back for more of that fantastic lamb doner.

Title: A Sichuan Delight in Midtown!

My quest for authentic Sichuan cuisine led me to a gem in Midtown that delivers on taste and value. On a calm Sunday at noon, my companion and I (who will share their own thoughts soon – look out for Pimpan J.'s review!) found ourselves comfortably seated in a casual, yet lively setting. The restaurant, uncluttered at that hour, offered a hands-on experience with a section dedicated to selecting raw ingredients for their signature dry pot.

The cornerstone of our meal was the dry pot, brimming with a choice of 16 ingredients including succulent fatty beef, lean brisket, delicate tofu skin, squid, and indulgent lobster balls. We settled on medium heat, which provided the perfect level of warmth without overpowering the dish. The freshness and variety were evident, and the tailored marinade was nothing short of transformative. 

In addition, the seafood malatang was a seafood lover's dream, generously portioned and paired excellently with rice noodles. The Hong Shao pork deserves special mention for its sweet, delectable sauce that was a match made in heaven with plain rice. 

The beverage selection impressed, from soothing coconut milk to the traditional wang lao ji, which complemented the spiciness with its herbal coolness.

The service shone brightly, courtesy of our attentive server, Ray (from Chengdu, forgive me if that's not your exact name), who expertly guided us through the menu and left no need unmet.

However, it wasn't without minor hitches; the seafood malatang's broth leaned too close to the tanginess of a Thai Tom Yum for my liking, and the fried chicken, though flavorful, was slightly overdone to a dryness not preferred on my palate.

In sum, the experience was delightful: great food, attentive service, and wonderful company. Kudos to Ray for exemplifying great hospitality. I am already anticipating my next Sunday indulgence at this spot. Highly recommended!

Absolutely delicious. May be my new fave Mexican spot in the city. While it is a bit pricey, you can taste the quality of the ingredients. The lobster taco is AMAZING... as is the cauliflower taco. I will definitely be back and will most certainly recommend it to other people.

I recently discovered Mezetto, which quickly became my top brunch destination. The cuisine is delightful, complemented by a generous flow of beverages, amidst a backdrop of convivial chatter and a team of warm, attentive staff. For those seeking tranquility, be warned – Mezetto buzzes with energy, especially during its weekend brunch.

Revelers can indulge in unlimited mimosas with a choice of orange, peach, pomegranate, or passion fruit for $20, or opt for the white and red sangria at $25, both available for 1.5 hours. The Mushroom omelette, priced at $19, was a culinary delight, featuring a generous filling of assorted mushrooms and mozzarella, accompanied by roasted potatoes and salad. The Challah french toast, also $19, was sublime, presenting two hefty slices adorned with fresh apples, dried cranberries, and a drizzle of maple syrup.

For anyone in quest of a lively new brunch haunt, Mezetto is worth the visit.

Title: A Quest for Satisfaction at a Local Malaysian Spot

My culinary journey at this Malaysian eatery began in 2016 and saw a follow-up in late 2018. Craving finer dining within Nyona's vicinity, I was drawn to this establishment that promised an upscale take on Malaysian cuisine.

My initial visit featured the Rendang lamb, a dish imbued with a notable coconut essence that I found quite pleasing. The lamb was of decent quality, yet despite its charm, the $18 price tag seemed disproportionate to the meal's size, leaving me wanting in terms of portion.

Returning in the winter of 2018, I sampled the Ipoh ho fun, which sustained the precedent of agreeable flavors. However, the issue of quantity persisted, as I once again departed with a lingering sense of hunger.

Observing the pattern over these years, it's apparent that the restraint in portion sizes might stem from overhead costs, particularly rental expenses. Nonetheless, this recurring shortfall in satiety is a disappointment that I suspect other patrons share.

In conclusion, while the food quality does not disappoint, the value proposition is undermined by the servings, suggesting an unsolved systemic concern rather than a mere personal expectation of portion sizes. My hope is for a future where the balance between cost and quantity aligns with the culinary excellence on offer.

My fiancé and I recently enjoyed a dinner at Clay Pot in West Village, and it certainly lived up to our expectations set by our East Village experience. Despite arriving on a busy weekday night, we were seated promptly. I chose the clay pot with salmon and eel – a delightful combination that was served with a generous amount of protein. Our meals arrived swiftly, within 15 minutes, and the texture of the crackling rice was a highlight, especially when scraping it off the pot's bottom – oddly satisfying! Both the food and the service were commendable; the staff was friendly and attentive. Clay Pot has proven itself consistently excellent and comes highly recommended for a scrumptious meal in a bustling yet welcoming environment.

I originally had a sit down reservation but plans changed so I got takeout instead to nibble on the bus ride home. Virgil's has a nice open floor plan. There is a cool rustic vibe befitting a bbq place. There is also seating on the 2nd floor.Instead of having to go to the bar to place my order, Virgil's has a  station for that in the back. Service was easy and quick. I got half a pound of brisket and unfortunately, it was the opposite of everything I had hoped it would be. It smelled amazing but was devoid of any flavor. There wasn't a smoke ring in sight. And worst of all it wasn't tender. Shame.

Decent spot for a quick bite. I was really intrigued by the Burrata, Prosciutto, & Pesto burger and while it was cooked perfectly and so juicy, there was so much pesto to the point it was a bit overpowering. I also got the parmesan fries, which are very photogenic but didn't have much cheesy flavor. Plus the cheese was melted in large clumps above the fries and not on the fries in my order. Finally, I found it disappointing that for their fairly high pricepoint (~$20 for just the above two), they do not offer free water and instead ask you to buy a $1 Poland Spring water bottle, and there are no bathrooms. Their food is definitely visually fun, but I felt my experience--potentially on an off night for them--left a bit to be desired.

Tucked away on the Lower East Side, this Italian gem truly hits the mark. The spaghetti limone is the star of the show – its zest and flavor are irresistible, so much so that my attempts to replicate it at home have fallen flat. We indulged in a special pie as well; while tasty, the crust could stand to be heartier for those who favor a thicker base. The fried calamari and arugula salad were satisfactory, though they didn't quite dazzle. For a charming touch, request a table in the delightful garden room at the back – it's a slice of tranquility that complements the dining experience perfectly.

I tried this place for the first time two weeks ago and I've been dreaming about it ever since. I went back today and it was as good as I remembered! Incredible curry, delicious naan, and a great idea. I love making naan "tacos" myself and I was excited to find a place willing to do it for me.

GupShup is one of several new and creative Indian food that is allowing New York to challenge London for title of the best cuisine coming from the Subcontinent diaspora. GupShup Bombay House is a colorful and lively as the food they serve. The food is delicious with classics such as chicken tikka, but new and modern as well with dishes like Rock N Roll Bombay Bhel. The cocktails are outstanding as well, world Class drinks with an Indian flair. We are huge fans of the Bombay Brunch too. Worth making a trip.

I recently had the chance to experience this restaurant located at the Dream Hotel on 16th Street close to the Meatpacking District in New York City.  With an unassuming enterence and a couple of steps down, entering Bodega Negra is a descent into a very cool, well designed space which, rarely for New York, transports you elsewhere.  Interesting that this is a contemporary Mexican restaurant whose roots are from all places, London UK.  There are lots of thoughtful design elements and my favorite is the cloakroom sign (please see image).I had an opportunity to meet the Chef who knows his spices well and set about trying the food and drink.  I particularly enjoyed the Oaxaca Old Fashioned featuring Mezcal and from the food menu my favorites included the guacamole - beautiful consistency (ended up ordering twice), the soft shell crab tacos, yellowtail ceviche and roasted Amish chicken, which was quite succulent.Service was attentive and one of the favorite aspects for us was the music which was loud enough to hear but soft enough to not affect the table conversation.  Bravo Amigos !

Title: Cozy Brunch Spot with Room for Improvement

I recently reunited with an old friend for a Sunday brunch at this bustling eatery and was pleasantly surprised by the short wait time for a table. The seating arrangement is quite tight—you're practically dining with your neighbor—which adds to the frenzied atmosphere of this popular spot.

The hot coffee served was satisfying, but my oatmeal with dried fruit and candied bananas left much to be desired. The topping was delightful, but the oatmeal itself suffered from an unappetizing texture that made it tough to enjoy.

On the flip side, my friend's Abe Lincoln breakfast was a hit, featuring a hearty combination of eggs, grits, sausage, homefries, and thick, buttery pancakes with a choice of topping – the Nutella version was a decadent treat. The maple sausage was a standout for me, and the pancakes stole the show, tempting me to return for a sweet breakfast of fluffy pancakes topped with berries or classic maple syrup.

Next time, I'll stick with the surefire options and aim for an early morning visit to escape the rush. A solid 3.5 stars for this joint, with potential for a higher score if they smooth out the kinks.

I recently dined at a restaurant where I experienced what could possibly be the best hummus I've ever tasted. It was so good that it left me craving for more. On my next visit, I plan to try their enticing bowl of hummus topped with chicken. The food was served promptly, which was a plus.

However, the service didn't quite match the high quality of the food—the server came off as unfriendly and disengaged, lacking a warm smile or conversation. Despite this, the chicken salad I savored was nothing short of divine, truly a heavenly dish. This place is a must-visit for the food alone.

I recently visited a fast-food spot for lunch in the Chinatown area and was thoroughly impressed. The large lunch special, priced at just $6, offers incredible value with a generous portion of meat. The flavors were authentic, and I particularly enjoyed the crispy burnt ends that added a delightful texture to the meal. Arriving at 11 am on a weekday, I was pleased to find no line. This place has quickly become one of my go-to spots for fast, affordable, and delicious food in the area. Highly recommended!

Amazing. I think I still have to wipe the bit of drool. If you looked up "crowd-pleaser" in the dictionary, there might be a picture of the lasagna. It's $64 but it was definitely the star of the meal, particularly when there wasn't a weak link in everything we ordered at all. My one very minor gripe is they turned down all the lights so we were basically eating by candlelight and I could only make out in very murky outlines what exactly I was eating. (1) Stuffed garlic flatbread: Yes. We saw this on almost every table. I'm not partial to garlic and how it makes my mouth feel and smell for the next day but I would gladly eat this. (2) Chrysanthemum salad. This is the salad that anyone who hates salad should order. It's literally several layers of grated cheese with a little bit of chrysanthemum tucked underneath. Really delicious with a slight hint of fibrous, in case you want to feel a tiny bit better about the massive amounts of pasta you're going to eat next. (3) Buffalo milk caramelle. Of all the pastas we tried, this wasn't my absolute favorite, even though the skins of the pasta looked stunning. I liked how the sweetness of the sauce wasn't overpowering though it was one of those dishes where I can eat the whole thing and not be able to explain exactly how it tasted. (4) Lasagna. The best part was the burnt, crispy top edges of each individual rosette. Definitely a must if you're in a group. (5) Charred octopus/Steak. Very tasty but at this point, they were taking up too much valuable stomach room that could be better used for the pasta. (6) Mochi with olive oil ice cream/Tiramisu. My best friend offered this very valuable piece of advice at the start of our meal, "Put down your fork if you're starting to get too full because you need to try the desserts here." The tiramisu looked some type of way with its coiled shape and the general darkness but it might have been the best tiramisu I've had anywhere. Same with the olive oil mochi. I may have needed to be wheel-barrowed out but I couldn't stop eating the desserts. Whatever - you have a separate stomach for that, right? Also, really liked the Bambino's Vino - it's vodka mixed with Lambrusco.

I was disappointed when I came here recently. I say so especially in comparison with the food, ambiance, and service at Spice (Thai restaurant across the street). I had a Tom yum soup ($6.95). I felt it seemed like a portion that would be more fair at $4.50-$5. The majority was all mushrooms and too much cilantro. They skimped with the shrimp and gave 2 at most. I felt the waitress was not particularly helpful or able to recommend anything when asked. I also felt she rushed me slightly and never checked in on me as I wanted to ask for a napkin. My glass of water was never refilled etc.

Title: A Brunch Worth the Wait

I recently had a delightful experience at a bustling city eatery where the weekend brunch truly lived up to the hype. Despite a lengthy 45-minute wait for a table, which led us to take a brief coffee detour at a nearby Starbucks, the overall experience was exceptional.

The restaurant exuded a warm and inviting atmosphere, matched by service that was both friendly and efficient. Our server brought a touch of humor to our table, ensuring a pleasant dining experience while proficiently catering to our needs.

The highlight of the brunch was undoubtedly the steak and eggs, a dish that both my friend and I found to be extraordinarily delicious—I cannot recommend it enough! I also indulged in the restaurant's homemade tea. Although it came with a steeper price tag, it proved to be an exquisitely refreshing complement to the meal.

In summary, if you're in for a superb meal and don't mind the wait, this restaurant is certainly worthy of consideration for your next weekend brunch in the city.

Took my friend from out of town who loves Japanese food here. She was surprised to see the TKG (raw egg and rice) which she said many Japanese restaurants don't have. We added ourselves to the waitlist before arrival, and we still had to wait about 20 mins before being seated, but staff was kind. Service overall was on the slower side but food was decent and we could take our time eating not feeling rushed out by the end of our meal. The quantity will definitely leave you feeling full. Hope to have more chances to try some of their other dishes as well. I'd recommend definitely adding yourself to the waitlist prior to arrival since it's a popular place.

Title: Delightful Discovery at BINGO!BAZAR

I owe a big thank you to the Yelp Community in NYC for guiding me to BINGO!BAZAR, a hidden gem just two blocks from my hotel. This cozy tapas spot exudes warmth from the moment you step in, with its friendly staff adding to the welcoming vibe. Opting for the bar, I was promptly presented with the menus – and a pleasant surprise of 50% off Happy Hour Oysters upon checking in on Yelp.

I sipped on a perfectly chilled Happy Hour Pinot Grigio, finding it crisp and refreshing. For my meal, I chose the Fig and Frico Salad, a balanced blend of frisee, black mission figs, parmesan crisps, and roasted almonds, all harmonized by a generous amount of Serrano Ham and a zesty citrus dressing. I also indulged in the Skirt Steak Bites with a tangy Chimichurri sauce, served with bread that had just the right crunch and softness to mop up all those delicious flavors.

Full and content, I couldn't help but wish my friend Julie F. were here to enjoy this culinary delight with me. BINGO!BAZAR is a must-visit for anyone looking for a friendly atmosphere and mouth-watering tapas.

I had a fantastic evening with friends at this bustling yet surprisingly serene restaurant. The service was delightful, with staff eager to explain each dish thoroughly. We were impressed with the generous portions of the meat dishes, and the tuna's freshness was exceptional. Desserts rounded off our meal beautifully and were a delightful surprise. I'm already looking forward to returning. Thank you for a memorable dining experience!

Title: A Feast for Carnivores at Jongro Korean BBQ

If you're planning a group outing and relish the sizzle of Korean BBQ, Jongro should top your list. My recent visit with two friends was a testament to the restaurant's ability to deliver on the Korean BBQ promise. We indulged in the beef platter, generously portioned for three and reasonably priced at around $120. It could even suffice for a party of four.

The live grilling on an open flame at our table was a spectacle, enhancing the dining experience. The platter featured an array of cuts including skirt, rib eye, and marinated beef, each slice oozing flavor. The standout was the marinated beef—tender, juicy, and seasoned to perfection.

Side dishes and sauces played their supporting roles admirably, with the pasta salad scoring particularly high marks from us. Jongro's popularity is no secret, so brace yourself for a wait up to an hour during peak times. Yet, trust me, the food is well worth the wait. Jongro is a vibrant scene that I wholeheartedly recommend for any Korean BBQ enthusiast.

I came to Han Dynasty for dinner on a recent Friday night, and although we were not able to make reservations ahead of time, the wait time for a party of two was only 10-15 minutes, which is a perfect amount of time to grab a beer at a nearby stand and walk around gawking at all the Dekalb Market has to offer.What I love about Han Dynasty is that they are able to adjust the spice levels on all of their dishes. Although I claim to like a kick to my food, truth is that in reality that kick is more of a light tap. I was able to choose the spice level for all of my dishes and even sides on a scale from 1 to 10 - I'm embarrassed to admit that my comfort level of heat hangs somewhere around level 4.I could not stop gushing about the eggplant for days. Is it strange that my favorite part of the meal was the added extra side? The flavors are amazing. The crispy scallion pancake was tasty, as was the tangy sauce it came with. I could totally see myself indulging in just the scallion pancake and the eggplant with a glass of red wine at the bar - perfect snack.So here's the thing.. the entree was actually my least favorite part of the meal. I went with Scallion style beef, which came with a side of white rice. It's not that there was anything wrong with this entree, but it did fail to impress or even live up to the less glamorous smaller dishes that were bursting with flavor. It was fine, just fine. It did come out with flames dancing underneath the dish, which scored my table plenty of curious looks.I have not had much luck with Chinese food in this area, and Han Dynasty, although a bit pricier than your average Chinese restaurant, is definitely the best out of about four Chinese restaurants I've tried Downtown Brooklyn. Whenever I get a craving for Chinese food in the future, I will now know exactly where to go.

Title: A Satisfying Delight at the New Joju

I eagerly anticipated the opening of a new Joju outlet near my school, sparing me the trek to Elmhurst. Despite a lengthy 1.5-hour queue during their buy-one-get-one event, the mouthwatering banh mi made the wait worthwhile. Though the menu is condensed, appetizing additions like rice bowls and salads have been introduced. 

The venue has been transformed into a sleek and spacious two-story retreat, a perfect evolution from their original locale. Their efficient assembly line service is a game changer, handling the lunchtime crowd with aplomb, and the promise of kiosks hints at even smoother future visits.

I indulged in the lemongrass chicken banh mi and The Sweet (Joju) - the latter stealing the show. A word to the wise: the sandwiches are incredibly hearty, and after savoring both halves, I found no room for dinner, a testament to their generous portions.

I'm already craving another visit - not just for the banh mi but also to relish their legendary kimchi fries. Joju remains a must-go for any banh mi enthusiast.

Title: A Fresh Italian Gem in Downtown: Avena

Avena, the Downtown sibling of its Uptown counterpart, has confidently occupied the space once held by the famed Da Silvano, bringing its own flair to a spot rich in history. Despite the absence of its previous celebrity clientele, Avena stands out with its superb culinary offerings, particularly the pasta dishes, which are a testament to authentic Italian cooking.

The fritto misto is a standout, ensuring that the tradition of excellence continues. For those with a penchant for libations, the interesting cocktail selection and commendable wine list complement the meal perfectly, catering to varied palates. Service is attentive, augmenting the dining experience with a welcoming atmosphere.

Ending on a high note, the pandan ice cream is a delightful surprise, offering a sweet-but-unique treat that encapsulates Avena's ability to infuse traditional Italian dining with a hint of the unexpected. In summary, Avena remains a spot where quality food and good service are still the stars of the show.

Title: Little Alley: A Shanghainese Gem for Vegetable Lovers

In the bustling culinary scene of New York, Shanghainese food lovers have plenty to choose from, but Little Alley stands out for a singular, star-quality dish: the Snow Pea Shoot in Rich Broth. This remarkable plate is a symphony of tender snow pea shoots bathed in an umami-packed broth that's rich with the flavors of fried scallops, pork, shrimp, salted eggs, and century eggs. Every ingredient adds a natural sweetness and depth, making the shoots the star of the show. Simply pair it with a bowl of rice, and culinary bliss is achieved.

While the Marinated Beef Slices—steeped in a spiced soy broth—were tender, they erred on the sweet side for my palate. Despite this minor quibble, Little Alley has secured its spot on my go-to list for that unparalleled vegetable dish alone. This is a must-visit spot for anyone looking for a standout meal in the city's Shanghainese dining landscape.

Title: A Nordic Gem Worthy of its Stars – Aquavit NYC

Having heard of the rarity for non-French, Japanese, or contemporary American cuisines to earn Michelin stars, my anticipation was piqued for Aquavit—a famed Nordic establishment that first opened in 1987. The experience did not disappoint.

Service was the epitome of perfection, striking that delicate balance between attentiveness and unobtrusiveness. The staff floated by our table, effortlessly swapping flatware and refreshing glasses without once interrupting our conversations—a magician’s touch that did not go unnoticed. 

The standout moment came when our engaging server and sommelier recommended a flight of their in-house aquavits—a delightful and unique offering that truly showcased the restaurant's identity (see attached photos for our selection). Their genuine enthusiasm for the cuisine and drinks was infectious, elevating our dining experience without a hint of pretension.

Opting for the Chef's Tasting Menu proved to be a wise decision. The anticipation had been building as we monitored the menu, and each course exceeded expectations, both in presentation (the bird's nest dessert is indeed a talking point) and taste. The standout was the wagyu, possibly the finest I've tasted, outshining many samples from Tokyo and Kyoto.

While Nordic cuisine’s bitter, acidic, and vinegary flavors might challenge some palates, at Aquavit, they were balanced and harmonious within each dish. The kitchen's flexibility to accommodate dislikes, such as my aversion to goat cheese, was highly appreciated and a testament to their customer care.

In my journey through NYC's Michelin landscape, I’ve come to the conclusion that two-star establishments like Aquavit offer the most fulfilling experiences, blending exquisite food with service that’s just right. They are consistently remarkable and worth the detour, outshining their one- and three-star counterparts in value and enjoyment. Aquavit, with its exceptional offerings, has certainly earned its place on my list of must-visit destinations.

This review is only for the 2 amazing cocktails we ordered at this place, one with a scotch base and the other with Vodka. I don't remember the names of either, but they were listed as a daily special at the bar, and both drinks had lime and cayenne pepper in it. They tasted absolutely delicious and had some serious punch in it.

Title: A Culinary Trip to Spain with Caveats: A Review of Mercado

As an avid foodie, I was brimming with excitement to visit Mercado, a space reminiscent of Eataly but with a Spanish twist, promising a plethora of tapas and small bites. While the idea of a Spanish-themed food hall is enticing, my experience was a mixed bag, suitable for a social outing where the variety and ambiance slightly outweigh the culinary offerings.

On a surprisingly quiet Friday evening, our gastronomic journey commenced with patatas bravas and churros—staples of Spanish cuisine. The patatas bravas, priced at $20, were a letdown; they lacked the anticipated crunch, and the pimenton sauce was disappointingly bland, overshadowed by an overpowering aioli. The churros, though a bit on the greasy side, were passable, especially when dipped in the pricey chocolate sauce.

Our hopes for redemption led us to the paella station, featuring a massive pan of premade paella with chicken, rabbit, and a vegetarian option. Unfortunately, my $17 plate was served lukewarm and drenched in oil, missing the cherished socarrat—the crispy treasure that is the hallmark of a well-executed paella.

Eager to end on a high note, we tried an empanada. It was unexpectedly sweet, filled with roast pork reminiscent of Chinese cuisine, encased in puff pastry—an unconventional yet interesting twist.

Despite the initial letdown, we dined at one of Mercado's full-service restaurants, which fortunately provided a decent meal and salvaged the evening.

Overall, Mercado's concept has potential, but the passion and authenticity in its food offerings seemed absent. The offerings felt mass-produced, lacking the soul that defines Spanish cuisine. I'd consider returning with friends for the environment and to explore further but with tempered expectations when it comes to the food.

Title: A Cut Above: Exquisite Dining at the Local Steakhouse

As a self-proclaimed steak aficionado, my latest visit to this beloved steakhouse was nothing short of spectacular. The star of the show, the rib eye, was impeccably cooked to perfection, bursting with rich, savory flavors that left a memorable impression on my palate.

But the culinary delights didn't end there. The chocolate mouse cake was a showstopper, putting a unique twist on the traditional mousse. It masterfully blended a soft texture with an unexpected crunchy center that made each bite a delightful surprise.

Furthermore, the restaurant week menu stood out as a testament to the chef's exceptional skill and creativity, offering a range of dishes that showcased the best of what the establishment has to offer. For those seeking an extraordinary dining experience, look no further—this steakhouse is a gem that consistently exceeds expectations.

Upon my recent visit to the local eatery with my dad, I was initially impressed with the first taste of their much-touted Fed Burger. Unfortunately, as the meal progressed, we both detected an odd fragrance emanating from the beef that diminished our enjoyment, making it more off-putting than enticing. The exact source of the aroma eluded me, but it certainly impacted the overall experience.

Switching gears to the blue ribbon, their fried chicken sandwich fared better on my palate. It was enjoyable, yet when reflecting on comparable offerings, I couldn't help but feel that establishments such as Au Cheval, Shake Shack, and Chick-Fil-A have previously provided more satisfying versions of both the burger and chicken sandwich. In the crowded field of comfort food, this restaurant's renditions, though satisfactory, didn't quite rise to the top of my list.

Haven't tried it but wanted to have their happy hour which says 4-7pm everyday on their website. Came around 6:40pm and now they say they "just" changed it to 4-6pm, really?! What a bummer. Even their menu at the door says 4-7pm. Too bad, lost business

My recent dining experience at this restaurant left much to be desired. Despite the establishment’s accommodation of our timing due to a later football game, the service was lacking from the outset. We endured a 15-minute wait before even being greeted, and our drink orders were overlooked initially.

Once ordered, our food took an excessive amount of time to arrive, with incorrect temperatures on the burgers and mistaken side dishes. Our server's prolonged absence discouraged us from addressing these issues. When my chicken sandwich finally arrived, it appeared to have been microwaved, resulting in a gummy texture, and although the sauce was flavorful, it quickly reduced the bun to a soggy mess. Others in my party found their burgers mediocre and the fries satisfactory, while the kale cauliflower salad was disappointingly basic.

Our server did reappear towards the end of our meal, offering a pitcher for refills, but it was too late to salvage the experience. In summary, this spot may suffice for a casual drink, but I cannot recommend it for a meal.

I recently visited an absolutely adorable date spot that hit all the right notes for a chic dining experience. The food was nothing short of phenomenal, with the highlight being the flavorful Pad Thai and the refreshing Thai iced tea. My husband's Pad See Ew was equally impressive, and the portions were generous and satisfying. Even the side of jasmine rice was freshly made and aromatic.

The restaurant itself boasts lovely decor and a comfortable ambiance, and you'll find the prices to be very reasonable. The staff elevated the experience, being both attentively polite and dressed in stunning uniforms. Plus, the exceptionally clean and pretty restroom is a detail that didn't go unnoticed.

For an unforgettable date night that offers both beauty and fantastic cuisine, this place is a must-visit.

I recently dined at one of the few local restaurants open on Christmas Day. We decided on a hearty breakfast, opting for steak and eggs, French toast, and eggs Benedict. The eggs Benedict was decent, but the highlight was certainly the steak and eggs; the sirloin steak was surprisingly good quality for the price. Unfortunately, the French toast missed the mark, coming out slightly overdone with a charred taste. Service was slower than usual, but that was understandable on a holiday. Overall, it was a standard diner experience with some hits and misses.

I work late hours pretty often and this is a great place to order delivery from for a quick dinner. The delivery has always been prompt every time. Recently, I ordered the chicken shish kebab and loved it! It was so tasty. The kebabs always come with a generous amount of rice and a large piece of bread, so the price for the meal is always worth it to me. I can never finish the whole meal in one sitting, so I keep the leftovers and I'm happy to finish it off the next day for lunch! Next time I would really like to try the baklava and the Turkish coffee.

Recently, our group of 11 reunited for a meal at a local restaurant and were met with exceptional hospitality. Despite our size and staggered arrivals, the accommodating staff promptly seated us at the 'big table' and remained patient throughout the evening.

The diverse menu caters to varying tastes, from sushi and sashimi to an array of delicious yakitori. Although repeatedly reminded of the $45 per person minimum and the automatic 20% gratuity, it was done subtly and didn't mar the experience. The per person cost was fair, especially given the food quality.

Highlights of our feast included the staple salted edamame, which didn't disappoint, and the dry Soju variety, 'Eight Peaks,' upon our server's commendation. The Tako Mini Salad was a refreshing starter, boasting a decent serving of thinly sliced octopus, a favorite of mine. The Gyu Tan (beef tongue yakitori) proved tender and arrived sooner than its quoted 40-minute wait.

Also tempting was the Marinated Galbi skewer, a flavor-packed teaser for what could be a delightful full entrée. The Tamago Mentaiko intrigued with its unique blend of grilled egg and savory cod roe mayo.

Finally, the "Godzilla" roll solidified the restaurant's sushi prowess, combining fried soft shell crab with a medley of flavors and textures that commanded attention.

Overall, the experience was incredibly positive. The staff's attentiveness, coupled with the quality and variety of the offerings, left us all happy and satisfied.

Pretty solid Thai food...depending on what you order. I've ordered a bunch of different dishes from the menu over the last few weeks and some have been great but there are definitely a few misses as well. They do a generally good job with delivery - arrives on time and they've never forgotten anything in the order, even when we've placed as a large group. They tend to respect requested spice levels well. In my personal experience, the good dishes are the noodles and the curries. The massaman is particularly delicious, which is saying something because it's not usually my favorite dish. Green curry is also good (not on par with Thai Villa's in my opinion, but good). Pad Thai is always a big hit.Skip the stir fry dishes; i ordered one a few days ago and it wasn't bad, just a little bit lacking in flavor. It also tasted a little bit like it was made in a dirty pan - like it had a faint taste of burnt oil. Calamari was a little gummy, and the som tum salad was bland as well, although I may order it again at some point and request it spicy to see if it's any better. Prices are good and it's been 25 percent off on seamless for dinner recently although I'm sure that's just because it's newer.Would order again!

I recently visited a crepe spot in the Upper West Side, and I had a pretty standard experience. Opting for a savory crepe filled with basil, tomato, mozzarella, and prosciutto, my expectations were met but not exceeded. The dish was adequate, although the mozzarella was slightly underwhelming as it hadn't fully melted, leaving parts of the cheese cold.

A place to get Japanese skewers, appetizer, ramen, don buri etc etc. They really have lots of food choices.I got potato salad to start and it was goood.Howevehh, i came for the skewer. But uh, it was dryyy. No no no. Pro : Potato salad, seated right away, reasonable priceCon : Not so warm service by my waiter (wish next time I'll just get a nice and polite japanese server), a bit disappointing skewer.The saving points are really their food variety and good price.

I recently dined at Crisp and was thoroughly impressed with their offerings. The Israeli bowl caught my attention with its medley of chopped salad, hearty potatoes, savory eggplant, and perfectly drizzled tahini, all topped with delicious falafel—at no extra charge. The bowl portions are generous, yet I found myself savoring every last bite of this delightful dish, which also includes your choice of hummus or babaganoush and comes with pita bread.

The standout ingredient for me was the eggplant, which added a unique and satisfying flavor to the mix. Alongside my bowl, I couldn't resist the waffle fries, and they did not disappoint as a crispy, crave-worthy side.

While prices at Crisp may be on the higher side, comparable to other eateries in the area, you get what you pay for—quality, taste, and satiety, with taxes already incorporated into the price of the bowls and pita.

I wholeheartedly recommend the Israeli bowl and look forward to exploring more of Crisp's menu on future visits. They've gained a fan in me!

Title: A Lamb Burger Worth Raving About!

I recently tried the lamb burger from a local spot and was thoroughly impressed. Priced at $16, the portion was generous, and the accompanying fries did not disappoint – they arrived perfectly crispy and well-seasoned. The surprise element? The pepperoncinis added a delightful kick to the burger. Delivery was prompt, and the packaging was top-notch, keeping even the shoestring fries crispy all the way from the west village to the flatiron.

While they didn't inquire about my preferred level of doneness, the burger was cooked just to my liking. A quick tip for fellow foodies: there's a $7 discount on your first order via Seamless, making for an unbeatable deal. My experience has left me eager to explore the rest of their creative and affordable menu. A return visit is definitely in the cards.

Title: A Disappointing Experience at Red Lobster - Seek Alternatives!

As an avid food enthusiast, my allegiance lies with local gems like Barbie's Pink Lobster rather than the ubiquitous corporate chains. My recent visit to Red Lobster in the culinary melting pot of NYC was underwhelming, to put it mildly.

The Times Square location, despite its popularity, fails to impress with its below-par seafood offerings. The overpriced menu does not justify the quality of food served, which I begrudgingly sampled and mostly passed on to my unsuspecting family members.

For those seeking authentic flavors in the city, I urge you to venture beyond the mainstream. Opt for the vibrant Chicken Tikka at Biryani Cart, grab a legendary slice at Joe's Pizza, indulge in a Chili Masala Dosa at Ganesh Temple Canteen in Queens, or explore the bold spices in the N1 at any Xi'an establishment.

In a city that celebrates diversity and culinary excellence, Red Lobster is a glaring misstep. My advice: leave the flock behind and embark on a true gastronomic adventure in New York City.

Pretty cool diner with old school decor. Had a funky chicken sandwich with breaded chicken, tomato, avocado and other on ciabatta along win tater tots. Good medium size portion and throughly enjoyed it.

This Vietnamese place is so special to me because it kept its business consistent throughout the years. Of all the years I have been coming here, the food still tastes the same, prices haven't changed and service is just as great.My go to dishes are certainly the spring rolls and chicken pho. The spring rolls come with lettuce, mint and basil for wrapping. The whole wrapping process makes it such a pleasure to eat the rolls. You get your hands dirty and work hard for the rolls, which makes them taste all the better.The chicken pho is like your grandma's homemade chicken noodle soup but Vietnamese style, which means you substitute the egg noodles with long thin rice noodles and add a bunch of bean sprouts to your dish before you dig in. I live for the scallions scattered on top of the soup. The chicken is nicely shredded and quite abundant for a soup that costs you less than 10 bucks. Their chicken curry with rice isn't the tastiest, so I'd skip that dish and go for their rice noodle dishes or phos instead.The service is fast and helpful. We forgot our umbrella at the restaurant and they practically ran after us to give our umbrella back to us. If you find yourself in Chinatown and are looking for an authentic Vietnamese spot, this unassuming restaurant is the right place for you.

I recently visited this restaurant and must award it five stars for its exceptional service. The servers were incredibly hospitable and kind, ensuring a pleasant dining experience. The highlight of the menu, the xiao long bao, lived up to its reputation – these dumplings were truly delectable. For those who prefer to avoid the trip to Chinatown, this establishment is a fantastic alternative. Highly recommend for a taste of authentic, well-crafted dumplings served with a smile.

Bowllin' is just about a minute walk from Washington square park, and as you walk in, you're greeted with a cute interior seating area. The cafe styled interior is actually beautifully designed, and is pretty welcoming. Though the food is Korean, the menu is pretty easy to understand and is thoroughly explained for anybody who is unfamiliar with Korean food.I got my food to go, and customized a bowl (they have a lot of options from poke to bulgogi to "sweet chili chicken" (which I ordered) along with different additives like egg and avocado.The pricing is pretty good for the area, most of the bowls are around $12. The food was decent, however I felt that the sweet chili chicken was quite bland. Though in the bowl the rice was completely covered in the sauce, I did not feel that the sauce or the chicken was spicy at all.

Nice to see when Indian restaurants make an effort with things like ambience and decor. What to get: Try the chicken tikka, the lamb keema, black daal and their cocktails. They have really interesting drinks (one is served in a tiffin) Generally, everything we had tasted decent and was trying to be creative, but only the above items stood out. My parents are from Kerala so I was super excited to see Kerala Beef on the menu, but this is not true to taste and too fusion for me personally. Kerala beef should taste closer to Malaysian beef rendang...more spices and coconut. I highly recommend the chef please change this dish since it's not accurate. Your customers will love the traditional taste I promise. I think it's great to be creative, but also important to stay true to our flavors.Service was great and good vibes. Suggest that more bollywood music be played and that the food not be served all at once. We spotted Anupam Kher there so that was a nice surprise! Seems to be a popular spot with celebrities.

I recently visited a charming restaurant recommended by a casual acquaintance, and I must say, it left a delightful impression. As a fan of the vibrant gay scene, the location felt perfect, akin to finding an oasis in my own backyard. My culinary adventure reached its peak with their avocado toast – an absolute revelation in flavor and freshness. It's a dish that has etched itself into my memory, ensuring that this eatery is on my must-visit list whenever I'm in town. Highly recommended for those looking to enjoy great food in a fabulous setting!

The only good thing about this place is that it opened until 1:30am.Located at restaurant row near Times Square, this place was expensive for what it was. Tasted pretty bad, portion was tiny, and ... idk, this just does not represent how dimsum should be.Even though their service was pretty decent, I would never come back.

When in New York it's a goal to try to hit as many popular food joints as people rave about how great the food is. Apparently Joe's Pizza is Kim Kardashian's must have pizza when in New York, so we decided to try it. However it just didn't live up to the hype.Food: At $4 a slice it's a little pricey thinking about all the other pizza joints in New York's price for a slice of pizza. Unfortunately it wasn't a WOW-AMAZING pizza for us, it was just a regular slice. As you can tell from the photo I didn't like that it was burnt (also burnt on the bottom) so it had that burnt taste. I don't recommend coming because there is usually a long line (we waited about 10 minutes) and the workers were very fast paced and pushy when we asked which pizza was which. Recommendation: Don't come here if you just want a slice of pizza, it didn't live up to my expectation at all. It tasted like the other .99 cent pizza joints (which tasted better actually) than Joe's. The experience wasn't worth us coming to try it.

I ordered the regular poke classic bowl for take out here and I really liked it. I love poke because its has veggies and raw seafood, both of which I love. All the ingredients were fresh and the tuna delicious. It was spicy and I always love spicy and the portion was huge. I will come here again for lunch if I'm around the neighborhood.

3.5 rounded down. Came here for the Kamayan night, which we were seated for at 8:30. I think it's pretty hard to get a reservation for this due to popularity (thanks Buzzfeed) of this kind of meal, since this was the only time we were able to get, even though we made a reservation like 2-3 weeks out.The food is probably new for many people, but the main feature of this style of dining is that you're eating with your hands- something which is a novelty for many people, including myself. Of course you'll be allowed to ask for a fork and stuff like that, but actually the food is not that difficult to eat with your hands, especially since the rice they serve here is more sticky than average. There were quite a few things that we were served here, so I'll do my best to go into each one:1. Lumpia Shanghai: this is essentially a mini spring roll, but it tastes very good and different from other spring rolls I'd had in the past, though I can't quite point out how it was. I'd recommend it though.2. Bone marrow: this dish is.. well if you've had bone marrow, I imagine you know what it tastes like. This was my first time trying this, and I think I got an especially fatty piece, but it was really, really rich, 3. Sausage: The sausage served here is sweet, and goes excellently with the vinegar. I think each person only got one, and I wish they served a few more of these, but 4. Ketchup Banana Ribs: I was a big fan of this dish. I'm not sure I could tell that there was banana in this rib sauce? But it was still great5. Coconut rice: oh man I feel like this was probably the best part of the dinner, even though this was only rice. This was rice that, as mentioned earlier, is more sticky than average, so it stays together quite nicely if you pick it up with your hands. The coconut flavor in the rice is really subtle, but it makes it taste x10 better, to the point where you could really just eat it by itself and it would still taste great.6. Assorted vegetables: we were given a couple of vegetable dishes, such as bok choi and cucumber/tomato salad. Normal vegetables, but paired well with the food. 7. Dessert: we were served halo halo, which I have never been a fan of. I generally don't like ice based desserts, but this one was okay. Mostly edible, so I give them some points for making a good effort.There was another food item which was kind of green looking and looked like spinach to me, but my friend said it was actually a combination of pigs blood and something else. It tasted sour, and I'd really like to find out what it was. Still, the fact that the lighting in this restaurant is somewhat dim made it hard to see what was what. I also got a pina colada (served in a pineapple) which cost $30. I split this with another person, making the drink effectively $15- but it's still way too much money for such a small cocktail beverage. I wouldn't recommend ordering it.The big problem I have is Jeepney's customer service. I emailed them following my dinner multiple times to try and ask what exactly was in one of the things I ate (out of sheer curiousity). Over the course of several weeks, I received... zero responses. Guys, why make a contact us form on your website if you're not even going to respond to it?

Given the current situation finding food and the delivery of food has been difficult. I just want to say thank you for the easy delivery.Wanted to try some falafel today and my mother recommended you guys. You donated food to her job and she loved it. Thank you for that as well.As far as falafel goes its seasoned nicely and taste great. My favorite part is the hummus! Its creamy and hearty like I like and has a fresh taste to it. I love the red cabbage nice and crisp and has a good bite to it. The pickled vegetables with their green pica sauce on top; amazing. The whole plate taste great and I am very happy I gave them a try. The plate was definitely a good experience. I enjoy eating plates of food with lots of color and this did not disappoint. So if you enjoy Mediterranean vegetarian food or just want a break from meat definitely give them a try
This place is very convenient for what it is. We walked right in- 11:00 am on a Saturday without a wait. The corned beef hash was amazing!

OMG!!!! Where to begin!!!!My homegirl and I decided to come here for lunch here on day while in the city. I didn't think I had been there before until I sat down and then I realized I had been one other time years ago.. Anyway let me just say the food here is AMAZING!!!Ambience:This place is nothing special, however you feel at home when you are here. It looks small when you first walk in so you don't think they hav a lot of seating, but what I didn't realize is they have seating in a room on the side and in the back you just cant see it when you walk in. It does get crowded on the weekends especially around noon, so get there before 1p if you don't wan to wait. You can also get there earlier if you are an early riser. Found out they also stay open late on Fri and Sat, which is cool. I also like the fact that it has murals of MJ And Whitney on the wall and the menu also has all types of famous people who have visited like presidents, celebs, athletes etc.Service:Our server was Natasha and she was FANTASTIC. She was honest, funny an sarcastic, I just loved her and you could tell she loved her job. It was funny b/c I was being a bit picky I guess and she kept messing with me about it and every time she passed by I seemed to needed something, to the point where if she walked away and I forgot to ask her for something else I would get up so I wouldn't have to try and get her attention and she would look at me like what you need now, but in a funny way. We laughed and joked with her during our time there. She was just amazing, and although she joked to my friend and told her never to bring me back I told her next time I come in I am gonna make sure to ask for her....lolFood:Well this is a soul food type of place, so if you like soul food you will LOVE this place. i like they fact that some of the names of the entree's are names after celebs and I guess what their favorite meal is there. I had the turkey wing and let me tell you they were huge and so tender. I had it with a side of fried okra and mac-n-cheese. My friend had shrimp an grits with a side of mac-n-cheese and collards, and the meals came with cornbread. The food was just delicious!. I couldn't eat it all and had to take some home. I did taste my friend's shrimp and grits and collards, let me just say those collards were on point, as for the shrimp and grits they weren't as tasty as they looked. I am a southern girl so I am picky about my grits. They do have to be seasoned well, and these were a bit bland and the shrimp also could have been seasoned better. I almost ordered this dish, but am so glad I didn't and she did so I could taste it. Now I know not to order them. But it did look amazingly good, the taste just didn't live up to the expectation.  I also ordered a to go of banana pudding!! OH MY WORD it was soooooooo good!! I was gonna order the peach cobbler b/c it is my fave, but after speaking to Natasha about which to get she said their banana was better, and boy was she right. She actually let us taste a bit of each before I made my decision, which was so nice of her. I had some much of the pudding that I ate on it for  about 3 days... They do you give lots of food for your money!All in all I HIGHLY recommend you try this place if you are in Harlem, even if you're not make the trip it is so worth it ! promise! And ask for Natasha's section.. Tell I sent you ..lol

Had just arrived in NY and wanted to grab a quick bite after checking into my hotel so I found Carve.  I ordered a slice of pizza and asked for it to be crispy.  After a few minutes, my slice was ready, but it was not crispy.  The pizza is overpriced and it was just OK.

Title: A Delightful Evening at Clay Pot's West Village Gem

My dining experience at the new Clay Pot location in the West Village was a treat. As a fan of their St. Mark's venue, I was eager to see what the West Village outpost had in store. Arriving at 5:45 PM on a Wednesday, we were greeted by the inviting aroma from the open kitchen, which was a charming touch, enhancing the anticipation of our meal.

The eatery's interior boasted tasteful decorations, with bold prints adorning the walls and large windows that bathed the space in natural light. Located conveniently near the Houston 1 train station and the scenic Washington Square Park, the setting was perfect for a pre-dinner stroll.

Opting for the classic clay pot with chicken and pork belly, it was a wise choice, made even better by a selection of condiments which allowed customization of flavors to my taste. The meal kicked off with complimentary salted quail eggs that impressed with both taste and presentation.

Service solidified the positive impression, with attentive and knowledgeable staff that served us promptly and courteously. In essence, Clay Pot in the West Village is a must-visit for anyone looking for a satisfying meal in a picturesque neighborhood setting.

Love love love! This restaurant is absolutely stunning. From the service to the drinks to the aesthetic, everything here is a dream. I was staying at the hotel and so my mother and I decided to go up to this restaurant for drinks and dessert. We initially booked a reservation but waited an extra 20 minutes to be seated on the patio. Absolutely worth the wait if you can! Would recommend any of the drinks as we tried a few and you could just taste the quality and care that went into crafting each so can't pick a favorite/ go wrong with any! Also, if you love chocolate, highly recommend the soufflé. You do need to give the kitchen about 25 minutes to prepare it but that time is nothing compared to the end result! Light, fluffy, rich, and delicious. The I  NY edible art was a lovely touch as well. Special thanks to the staff as well because they were fabulous. Really awesome service and nice as they offered to take pictures of us/really were enthusiastic as we talked about our visit to New York. Everything here really exceeded all expectations and we can't wait to come back.

Title: Disappointing Experience Despite High Hopes

I visited this restaurant with high expectations due to its stellar Yelp rating, but was met with disappointment. The service left much to be desired; our waiter was inattentive, neglecting to bring our appetizer and causing us to wait an excessive hour and 15 minutes for our main courses. The roasted chicken and Mac & cheese, priced at $22 and $18 respectively, were not only delayed but also disappointingly portioned, failing to justify their cost.

The only redeeming aspect of the night was a well-crafted drink, which, frankly, isn't a rarity in this vibrant city. Despite this, I can't overlook the overall inadequate experience. My advice: save your money and dine elsewhere. 2/5 stars.

Title: Adequate Greek Fare at Uncle Nick's

Uncle Nick's offers a spacious dining experience with a menu that promises good food, though it stops short of being truly exceptional. As a vegetarian, I found the vegetable kebob with rice to be enjoyable, as was the side of grilled peppers paired with a potato and garlic dish known as skordalia. It seems that the meat selections might be the highlight for many patrons, though my experience alone wouldn't lead me to seek out this establishment again. Yet, its proximity to the theatre district and its uncrowded space make it a convenient, if not entirely remarkable, choice for a quick meal before a show.

Got a slice of the Fresh Mozz ($4). It was as big as my head!Good overall, however it did not knock my socks off. I can see the appeal with the thin and extremely crispy crust. But it's crispy because it's so dry; eating the edge of the crust that had no sauce was a chore.Fresh mozz looked tantalizing until I realized that it was dry and stringy like regular mozzarella; it wasn't soft and melty as it looked to be.Long line, but it moves fast.

My friends and I had a blast here! We came to "glamp" when they had the courtyard decorated with some tent/cabins. We had some spike hot chocolate and probably one of the best cheddar biscuits I have ever had! Our server was also incredibly nice and gave us free ski shots ;) we stayed for about 2 hours just hanging out and glamping, it was such a good time! I will definitely be back next time I'm in NYC! I'm sure there will be a new set up then in the courtyard :)

If you're in the mood for a delightful dining experience, Clay should be at the top of your list. This establishment strikes the perfect balance with its minimal yet chic decor, setting the stage for a culinary adventure. The food is nothing short of tasty, as evidenced by the succulent duck that comes highly recommended by my mother. Meanwhile, the chicken dish deserves applause for its flavorful excellence. Wine aficionados will feel particularly at home here, thanks to a carefully curated selection that kept my sister raving throughout the evening. The attentive waitstaff rounds out Clay's impeccable offering, solidifying it as a prime choice for anyone after a classic dining experience with a modern twist. Whether you're there for the wine, the duck, or the chicken, Clay is a smart pick that won't disappoint.

After a shopping spree at the new Nordstrom, my hunger led me to this gem of a restaurant. The decision to dine here was spot on. Starting with soups and several appetizers proved to be a wise choice. The lobster bisque, albeit served in a modest cup, was packed with flavor and generous pieces of succulent lobster. The highlight among starters was the fried calamari, which stood out with its unique Asian-inspired flair and a kick of heat.

The burrata was another hit, perfectly paired with apples and nuts for a burst of freshness and texture. Moving on to the main course, the halibut fish tacos did not disappoint – they were flavorsome and came with a satisfying amount of fish, making them ideal for sharing, especially after the appetizing beginnings.

This restaurant is definitely a fantastic spot for a meal after shopping, and I am eager to return during the summer to enjoy the outdoor ambiance. Highly recommend it!

Title: A Flavorful Uzbek Feast Post-event at Javits Center

After attending an event at the nearby Javits Center, I ventured into a vibrant Uzbek restaurant at 7pm on a bustling Saturday evening. With foresight, I had a reservation—crucial for weekend dining here.

Unfamiliar with Uzbek cuisine, I leaned on Yelp's wisdom, opting for a Samsa to start, followed by shared plates of Uzbek plov and meat manti. A slight hiccup had the appetizer arriving post-entrées, but it was a non-issue as the manti—with its appetizer-like qualities—was on the table. Both the plov and manti were outstanding, bursting with authentic flavors. The Samsa is not to be missed either.

The one drawback was the restaurant’s inability to buffer the winter chill each time the door swung open, which was frequent given the packed venue. The persistent cold necessitated dining in coats.

In summary, the vibrant flavors made for a memorable meal, but be sure to bundle up in the colder months.

I went here for lunch on a weekend. There wasn't a lot of crowd since we came a little early but the crowd picked up later. The waiter was friendly and the service was quick. I ordered the 3 pepper chicken that came with the wonton soup which was super spicy and the chicken was super crispy. I loved it. My friend couldnt handle the spiciness but I loved it. He got the beef with chili oil which was tasty too but I liked my dish better. We also got the soup pork dumplings as an appetizer and it was good but I've had better elsewhere. In short, this place is worth a try, the food is good and the service is great.

Title: A Slice of Kindness at a Bustling Pizza Haven

As a self-proclaimed pizza aficionado, discovering new pizza joints is my passion. My latest find? A bustling spot I stumbled upon post-appointment, drawn in by the promise of a simple special: two slices and a soda.

The decision did not disappoint. The pizza was nothing short of delicious, with a mouthwatering variety that left me spoilt for choice. Beyond the extensive pizza selection, the menu was brimming with tempting options.

Despite the crowd, the restaurant was well-equipped with ample seating. The staff, including the owners, were the embodiment of hospitality. When I requested a table cleaning, it was attended to promptly.

A heartwarming touch to my visit was witnessing a staff member gifting an extra slice to an elderly man who had come in for a simple meal. The gesture not only touched the gentleman but also resonated deeply with me. It reinforced the beauty in small acts of kindness.

With great food and a great heart, this eatery has definitely earned a return visit from me whenever I'm back in the neighborhood.

Title: A Flavor Fiesta Worth Every Minute of the Wait!

If you ever find yourself yearning for a mouthwatering taco experience, look no further! This gem comes highly recommended, and trust me, the temptation to devour the whole menu is real. I stepped into this bustling establishment with high expectations, spurred by a friend's advice to 'order four.' Note to self: next time, heed her words.

Despite the ever-present queue, the wait is a minor inconvenience compared to the culinary delight that awaits. The menu offers a simple yet crucial choice between corn or flour tortillas. As a corn aficionado, I naturally gravitated towards it and wasn't disappointed.

The tacos, oh the tacos! I opted for both steak and chicken, and the flavors were a dance of perfection on my palate. Sharing a pork quesadilla added another layer of indulgence to the meal, and even the sauce playfully dripping onto my chin couldn't dampen the spirits.

Bottom line: I wholeheartedly recommend a visit. Get ready to fall in love with every bite!

I visited this restaurant with high hopes, only to face disappointment. The mix-up with my order, receiving chicken instead of the shrimp parm I requested, already started things on the wrong foot. Upon returning to correct the mistake, the staff's insistence that it was shrimp – when it clearly wasn't – and their lack of an apology added to the frustration. While the eventual correct sandwich was just mediocre, the generous portion size and the bustling atmosphere of the place suggest it has potential. Despite the off-putting experience, I am willing to give it another try, in hopes that this was a one-off mishap.

Title: A Rainbow of Flavors at [Restaurant Name] - A Must-Visit!

If there's one place you must add to your culinary itinerary, it's [Restaurant Name]. I am beyond impressed – their food left me almost speechless. Imagine a palette of vibrant veggies, sans purple, artistically plated to delight both the eyes and the palate.

The pickled beets are a revelation, a perfect start to the meal. But the star has to be the chicken platter. It's rare to find chicken this juicy and packed with flavor; it's etched into my memory. Accompanied by a crisp salad and unexpectedly repeated, yet delicious, beets, plus whole spicy green roasted peppers, it's a combination that sings.

Don't let the weather deter you – even without the snow, the experience is worth braving any elements. As for family-friendliness, my husband, sister-in-law, son, and I all found it welcoming. In short, [Restaurant Name] is a culinary gem that promises a great experience for everyone.

Really decent pho offered in Chinatown. They take cash only. I would offer it a 3.8. We ordered a Pho, fried spring rolls and a Vermicelli dish with grilled pork.The Pho broth was rich and had a slight hint of citrus. It was a little bit too salty for my taste but overall delicious. The portions were generous. The Vermicelli dish lacked flavour despite the fish sauce. The fish sauce doesn't have the regular punch. They also didn't throw a diversity of veggies (only salad and 2 pieces of cucumber and carrot so small I didn't even taste it). It was very underwhelming. I usually don't like fried spring rolls. Having tried theirs, my opinion remains the same. I would rather have fresh spring rolls. Plus, the fish sauce again lacked the complementary flavour profile to accompany the rolls. The service is always simple and direct, just how I like it. Overall, may or may not come again.

shoyu ramen is bursting with flavors but not overwhelming salty. the egg was cooked to perfection and the pork belly was so fatty. the portion was just right, not feeling like you want to vomit noodles but enough to keep you happy. they have a discount for paying in cash - probably worth bringing cash!

The upside is this place is open till 4am and takes credit cardsIt's super tiny and aged But still has the authenticity of years of business and know they do wellThe place gets filled up off and onLots of people grabbing late night munchies  Since I got there late they only had slices versus full  menu Me and my friend grabbed the classic cheese, the lasagna fully loaded and the chicken tomato slices They range 4-5 bucks each and they heat them up in the coal oven The slices are big and worth the price

I dined at this bustling spot on a weekday evening, arriving at 6:30 PM only to encounter a wait time closing in on an hour. A modern touch was their texting service, allowing us to explore the neighborhood during our wait, a small grace that was appreciated.

The meal commenced with the divinely crispy pig ears, a dish living up to its name. The betel leaf wrap was not only a feast for the eyes but also a burst of bright flavors on the palate. The roasted bone marrow satay did not disappoint either, offering a delectable richness, while the pea shoots were a fresh, green revelation.

A particular standout was the Khao soi, its complex layers of flavors marking the highlight of our meal. To finish, the mango sticky rice was a flawless ending, hitting the sweet spot just right.

I left with delicious memories and an eager anticipation for a return visit, particularly enticed by the prospect of indulging in the coconut sundae. The verdict is clear: this place is a must-try where taste buds are treated to a symphony of flavors.

As a bona fide Buffalonian, I've got high standards for wings, and I'll say it straight—Dan & John's serves up the best wings in NYC, no contest. They nail the Buffalo Wing authenticity that others can't seem to grasp. Whether it's from their brick-and-mortar location or one of their food stands, these wings are consistently superb.

Their hot wings pack a legitimate punch while maintaining deliciousness, particularly when paired with their spot-on blue cheese. On my latest visit, I ventured out and tried the sweet chili and lemon pepper varieties. Typically not a lemon pepper fan, I was won over by their version—crispy, tangy, and undeniably lemon without a hint of artificiality. A dunk in ranch took them over the top. The sweet chili wings were just as impressive, striking a heavenly balance between sweetness and heat, clinging to each wing perfectly.

In brief, Dan & John's has solidified their spot at the top of my wing list in NYC, and my anticipation for the next visit is already sky-high.

My friends and I visited Ippudo 5th Avenue yesterday (Saturday) around 2:00pm. It was busy, but they were able to seat 8 of us within 20 minutes. There is a nice waiting area with limited seating.The place looks clean and minimalistic. Our server was very attentive to our table-taking our drink orders within minutes of us settling into our table. We went around the table putting our orders in. My wife and I ordered the Ichiraku and Karaka Spicy Kasane respectively.As soon as a bowl of ramen was ready, it was brought out. They didn't wait for every bowl to be ready before they brought it out. It makes sense because if the noodles sat, it wouldn't taste as good. Everybody got their bowl within two minutes of each other. However, it took mine five to six minutes to come out. When my friends and wife started eating, I noticed three servers turning around and looking at our table, as if they knew something was wrong. I suspected that our server forgot to put in my order.When my food finally came out, I thoroughly enjoyed it. My wife and I agreed that we had just experienced the best noodles of our lives. The broth was good and the meat was juicy too. The spice level of the Karaka Spicy Kasane was moderate to little.

While checking out Chelsea Market, my son wanted to eat at Creamline. He was a little disappointed that they were out of the cheese sauce for the fries, but he ordered chicken tenders and fries. His brother and I wanted to eat somewhere else, but brother got excited when he saw that they had a certain brand of root beer in their fountain so he ordered a drink. Unfortunately the root beer was out of syrup so that was a bust. The food came out quickly and my son ate it up, he's 17 and was super hungry. After he finished I asked him how many stars he would give it out of five and he said three because it was mediocre. We left and the rest of us ate somewhere else (we wanted seafood), then came back for Fried Oreos for dessert. These were pretty good. The batter tasted kind of like a funnel cake, and the Oreo became soft when it got warm. You get fresh whipped cream to go with it! I would say there are definitely better places to eat in Chelsea Market, but if you have a picky eater who isn't very adventurous, then this is the place for him.

Returning to our favorite Korean BBQ spot with an even larger group was a testament to how much we adore this culinary gem. The universal love for Korean BBQ was palpable among our party, and the experience didn't disappoint. The array of meats and sides coupled with the interactive grilling made for a joyous feast, as evidenced by the numerous photos capturing our collective gastronomic delight. This place consistently delivers happiness straight to your belly, and it's a hit every single time.

We came here for lunch on a Friday and was seated right away. I ordered chicken schnitzel that came with choice of salad, home fries or smashed potato, as well as the option to have either one big side or half and half. I chose the home fries, which came out thinly sliced and deep fried. The fries were good, with a nice crunch reminiscent of potato chips. The chicken schnitzel was fine. It is crunchy on the outside but somewhat dried on the inside, probably due to how thin it is cut. Overall I think the food taste fine, nothing phenomenon or particularly memorable.

**Title: Mediocre Experience with Overpriced Options**

We recently opted for delivery from this restaurant and found the overall experience to be underwhelming. Firstly, the pricing felt steep, particularly with the $3 surcharge for an all white meat chicken preference, which, in my opinion, should be a standard offering.

The meal got off to a rocky start when we discovered they had omitted the rice from both of our chicken dishes. Additionally, staple condiments like soy sauce and accompanying noodles were absent.

Diving into the specifics, the wonton soup had commendable wontons and decent noodles, but the flavor of the broth was disappointingly bland. The hot and sour soup did little to impress as well and lacked the spicy kick one might expect. On a brighter note, the spring rolls were a highlight, arriving crispy and enjoyable.

Unfortunately, the shumai did not live up to expectations. Their oversized portions and tough pork filling detracted from the dining experience, not to mention the high cost. Regarding the sesame chicken, which suspiciously resembled orange chicken due to the presence of orange peels, it was tasty but not what we ordered. The chicken and broccoli dish was satisfactory, but again, the absence of rice was a letdown.

Taking everything into account, including the forgotten items and additional charges, I'm inclined to avoid ordering delivery from here in the future.

Came here on a weeknight for dinner, drinks and some apps.My friend and I both tried two different types of drinks, and didn't like either since they were way too sweet. We may have just unintentionally chosen some of the worse drinks on the menu, but the waitress was pretty clueless when it came to items on the menu, so we just went based off the descriptions. For food we had-- truffle hummus: this was good but the hummus itself wasn't great. It was masked by the flavor of the truffle oil which definitely made it better - chicken skewers: these were good, nothing special though. They were slightly sweeter than I was expecting - basil linguine: I wasn't expecting much out of this simple dish, but it was delicious and packed with flavor! - chocolate lava cake: this was delicious but how could it not be. Portion was on the smaller side but it was so rich that my friend and I couldn't even finish it. Good amount of options and nice ambiance - I'd recommend stopping by

Instagram algorithms kept tempting me with 4K quality pictures of Aunt Jake's pasta dishes. After navigating through the kitchen (only in NY?) we were seated in the backyard. I have eaten lots of pasta in my life. This certainly isn't what Insta promised. The pasta came out not very hot. It was warm but not warm enough that I questioned how long it had been sitting in the kitchen. I had the basic marinara to play it safe. It was okay. The sauce did not taste particularly fresh and wasn't boasting much flavor. The pasta itself was pretty good. Soft but still traditionally al dente. Again I wasn't super impressed. My friend had the bolognese and enjoyed it. We both agreed it was not as amazing food as we had both expected. Somewhat of a letdown. Sorry AJ's.

I haven't had a meal that slapped this hard in a while. My best friend frequents this place and decided to come here for a birthday dinner. They were extremely welcoming about hosting a group of 15 of us. Although the ordering process was complex because of how many of us there were, they still pulled it off with no error. I, and a few of the other guests, arrived here HUNGRY. From the first bite, I could tell this would be a very filling meal. All the meat and vegetable options were exploding with flavor. My favorite option would have to be the special tibs and Awash tibs though. I wasn't as big a fan of the lamb and chicken. Upon request, the waiter was also able to bring out a slice of carrot cake with a candle for the birthday girl, which was a very nice touch to the perfect evening. Not to mention the cake was actually amazing. Probably one of the best carrot cakes I'd ever tasted in my life. Might come back here just to get a slice of my own.By the time we left, I could barely walk out because of how stuffed I was. And to top it all off the price was extremely reasonable. It ended up amounting to about $23 per person (excluding the birthday girl of course). Probably one of the most successful birthday dinners I've been to in a while. Thank you Awash!

They say that the New York City charm of steak houses is a dying breed. Peter Lugers was recently reviewed and scored poorly according to some critics, citing that they had lost their way and fallen off their quality, ambiance, and old school steakhouse charm and only targeting making a buck. Other steak houses require a suit jacket and tie. Would s&w be one of these places destined to fall victim to living on a namesake? Would I like the old school charm like Delmonico's but feign to come back? Luckily I can say no. While appropriate attire is recommended (slacks and a dress shirt) you can easily come here sporting a pair of nice jeans and a polo shirt. The ambiance is light and casual with a flair for location and history. The food, prepared no nonsense served with sides that don't need tweaking, waffle cut fries, Fresh creamed spinach, fried calamari, New England clam chowder (the only way to eat it) along with the regulars, raw oysters, shrimp cocktail, seafood towers and a few other main stays. Quality meats being the proprietor, supplied our bottle of Bordeaux this evening which wasn't too pretentious or expensive ($53.00 for a bottle)Service was constantly checking on us without being too overbearing and was always within ear shot if needed. Everything was prepared perfectly and brought out fresh, quick and hot. Staff were constantly filling glasses and catered to our every need. Sure we went for restaurant week, sure the prefix was $42.00 per person. Factor in the supplemental charges, the add-ons, the bottle of wine I ordered to share with the wife that she decided to have a single glass of,and I drank the rest of that delicious bottle , the bill was around $280.00.
